reviews.comment: Dr. Rasmusson is awesome! He is such a kind and thoughtful person, and is very happy and eager to help when you run into problems. His lectures at the start of class were helpful and made sense. I would definitely recommend him as a professor!!
Really nice guy and keeps the lessons interesting; however, he never checks his emails unless you call him out on it during class. Good professor, but has 0 communication outside of class.

Professor Coombs knows his stuff, is respectful, and a spiritual guy! I never thought I'd enjoy a political class. I learned so much! He makes the work doable and tests are open note. He really needs a TA. His Canvas page is messy and he grades important assignments towards the end of the semester and responds to emails only on the day of class.

Echoing everyone else here: engaging lectures, lots of reading, and tough on essays. However, his criticisms are very constructive and have helped me improve significantly. Pay attention in class, read the material closely and you'll have no problem with your grade while enjoying yourself in the process.

Pretty good teacher, exams and essay are worth most of your grade. Keep in mind midterm and final are NINE SHORT ESSAYS with 2-3 paragraphs each, so around 20-25 paragraphs on pretty difficult topics plus a ton of multiple choice. I like the professor a lot though, great guy who helped me view politics from a different angle.

I loved his class! I was afraid to take Poli 110 (dislike voicing my own opinions, confused easily), and he made it easy to grasp and interesting to learn. His 2 main papers can be on the same subject; therefore, the research progress is natural through the semester. He is funny and perfectly balances secular and scholar learning. 10/10!!

Great lectures. He knows what he's talking about. I think it was one of the most beneficial classes I've taken at BYU. Both liberal and conservative students seemed to enjoy the class. The canvas page is messy and out of order. Make sure you take notes!!

I fear him, respect him, and love him all at the same time. He is super charismatic so you can tell clearly and early on that he loves what he teaches. He is a little scary when it comes to grading, but it all makes sense in the end. Turn your assignments in on time, attend class, follow the rubric and you will be fine. Not a great email responder.

I loved Prof. Coombs and would 100% take his class again. You can tell that he puts a lot of effort into teaching and really cares about his students. He is a harsh grader but harsh does not mean unreasonable. All exams are open note, just make sure to get help on your paper(s) if you're not a confident writer and he will be happy to help.

Attendance isn't mandatory but it is important as you do a lot of class work. He is very receptive to students, I wish every lecturer would teach like him. He grades harshly on papers and easy on the rest. A super great class, very very very easy!

His way of grading is extremely frustrating as it doesn't really pertain to the rubrics. He frequently deducts points for things not included in the grading criteria and adopted a "sorry, not sorry" attitude when I approached him asking for help. Very unclear on how he wants things done and very quick to deduct points for things not mentioned prior
He is nice guy, but an absolutely horrible grader.

If I could take another class with Professor Coombs I would! His lectures are interesting and you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. Plus, he is great at helping and responding to questions. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are in-class projects you should be there for. There are lots of readings and a few tests and quizzes.

He is very energetic in class. I was never bored during the 2.5 hour class. There are pop quizzes so make sure to attend. He is very interactive with the class and has a lot of group work. The biggest thing that I struggled with were the tests but there's only a few of those.

Great guy but difficult grader. He's very passionate and that helped to want to learn more. He grades papers very hard (two). Only a few assignments (quizzes) and he does not let you make up any. Overall, very interesting class learning about politics but hard to excel especially for a 110 level class

Professor Coombs is amazing! Siting in his lectures, you can tell that he really cares about the education of citizens in America. He wants to help you understand complex ideas. He tells you exactly what to read and at what level to read. Be ready for pop quizzes, but as long as you do the readings, you will be more than okay. Plus hes really funny

Professor Coombs is one of my favorite Professors I've ever had. He clarifies the reading assignments with what you need to skim read or closely read. His lectures are AMAZING and he really creates a safe environment to ask questions and discuss all sides of an opinion or situation. If you have any opportunity to take this class, do it.

Professor Coombs is a really great guy! He's always super passion about what he's teaching and cares about what students have to say. Most assignments are graded pretty easy (for BYU anyway). His class always went by quickly. Make sure you turn in everything on time; there are few assignments. Overall, I LOVED this class and this professor.

I learned a lot about our country's government from Professor Coombs. He was easy to talk to. His lectures were great but the pace was kind of quick. There was a bit of homework and papers but he's a fair grader. Highly recommend to take his Poli 110 class.

Brother Coombs was an excellent teacher who clearly values education. The focus of the class is more to become educated and involved in politics, and less about nit picky grading. His class is entertaining and interesting to attend. If you go to class the exams aren't difficult, and if you put real effort into the papers they aren't bad either.

Knows his stuff and genuinely cares about you learning at the level to which it will be useful in your everyday life, is completely respectable of what its like to be a college student, his class can be tough, but not unreasonably so, it is also very interesting and exciting. Plus it gets you out of American heritage

PAPERS! You write two papers that carry a ton of weight. Put in the time for these and you will get an A, because he grades these HARD lol. He is a softer grader on the exams but they're open note, take good notes in class. Reading quizzes every 2 weeks. He is AMAZING though. AMAZING teacher in a very hard class to teach. True colors come out.

Bro Coombs is an awesome teacher. He is very knowledgeable and is very respectful. This is a hard class to teach due to differing opinions about politics from students. He does great, take his class. Argumentative paper on any political topic you want, tests are pretty easy if you go to class- very reasonable class. I learned a ton about politics.

Bro Coombs is great! Lots of reading and information but it was all useful and interesting. Intense essays and tests, but Bro Coombs prepares you well and is accessible outside of class. This class, while difficult, has been so influential in my life!! Study and participate!
Good professor, mostly graded on essays and participation points. I liked that he didn't focus too much on memorization, he is more interested in students understanding the content.

I love Professor Eastley! I took this class looking for a fun GE, and I got it! Highly recommend to other students. There is a lot of reading - I took this class during spring term, but it would probably be more manageable in the fall. Super awesome class!

Professor Eastley is really nice! He made the class fun, and it seemed like he was one of us (in a good way). Although this class was "easy", it was a LOT of reading. Like an unnecessary amount of reading. It often felt like a religion class. Overall, Professor Eastley is great and always willing to talk and work things out.

Lots of reading, but great discussion topics! Class was mostly a discussion, final was a test, then a paper and creative project on a topic of your choice that was covered in the class. Easy to get a good grade, so long as you do the reading and want to think about it a little bit. Overall, amazing professor and amazing class!

I loved Prof Eastley! I took his Engl 201 masterpieces of world literature class, and I really enjoyed it. It is a lot of reading, but the majority of the points in class result in a quick 5 question quiz before class and a little reflection on what you read, as well as a reflection on an in class discussion. I thought this class was so fun!

Loved this class with Dr. Eastley. He is so caring and so insightful. A fair amount of reading with a short write up due for each one, but he is so awesome. Super fair grader and gives really good feedback. All the assignments serve a purpose which I appreciated. Classes are super discussion based because he loves to hear his students thoughts.

Amazing. Amazing. Amazing. Dr. Eastley just really cares. He has such a professional and nuanced view of Women's Literature and the literature of the oppressed, that I as a woman couldn't appreciate enough. He was so patient, involved, and eager to help. He said hi every time he saw me in the hall. Embodies kindness and genuine personal investment.

LOVED this class! Literally a book club. It consisted of reading (+/- 100 pages a week), reading quizzes, short essays, 2 big projects, and discussions in class. If you actually do the readings then it will be the easiest A. I listened to a lot of the books on Youtube but there are some that you'll have to acquire. He is super passionate and nice.

This was my favorite class this semester! I really enjoyed the reading and the quizzes were pretty straight forward if you did it. Classes were mostly discussion and there were always amazing insights. I learned a lot and the projects were so fun and engaging. The spiritual aspects also pushed me forward a lot. 10/10 would recommend.

This was one of my favorite classes at BYU. The reading quizzes are sometimes hard, and the readings are long, but all of the readings had audiobooks. We didn't have any tests, and the two projects were fun to do!

Overall, I really like Prof. Eastley. He was really good at making a lecture interesting. He was personable and funny. There was only one essay and it was easy, but he didn't tell us about the midterm till a week before (it wasn't on the syllabus, talked about in class, in the assignments page, or anything).

Professor Eastley was great! This class honestly felt like a Lord of the Rings book club. The great majority of work in this class is reading, so hopefully you don't mind doing that. I think I averaged 100-150 pages per class period. You don't need to remember details though, which is nice. Would highly recommend!

Prof Eastley was a good teacher. His assignment expectations were pretty fair, and I never got blindsided by any assignments. 

PLEASE READ: Much of the reading has a significant amount of cursing. I can handle a swear here or there, but it was f-bombs every other dialog. Was surprising for a church school. Fair warning, I was caught off guard.

He did a great job of making the class accessible and engaging for students of a variety of experience with Tolkien! Projects were fun and class involved a lot of discussion. Grading is easy as long as you follow the instructions and do the assignments seriously. There is a heavy amount of reading as you read all of Lord of the Rings and more.

Prof. Eastley is AMAZING! This class is such a blast. Perfect for any Tolkien and LOTR fans but also approachable for first-timers. There is a lot of reading but class lectures are so much fun, and there is not much work for this class besides the readings. Tests are graded very easy. Feels like a book club with friends, 100% take this class! 10/10

My absolute favorite professor this semester! His lectures are direct, informational, engaging, funny, thought-provoking, and interesting. Even when COVID forced us online, he managed to cultivate a classroom of discussion and interaction with the text. I learned so much from this class and felt that the ratio of knowledge to work was well balanced

Professor Eastley is awesome! I took English 236 from him hoping to simply fulfill a GE credit but I loved coming to class every week. He is very insightful, provides good feedback, and genuinely seems to enjoy teaching. Would highly recommend this class for any Tolkien or LOTR fans out there. Be prepared to read a little bit every day though.

Prof. Eastley is the best! He made this course feel almost like a book club. The reading at the beginning of the semester was super easy and definitely got longer and harder as we went on, but that's "The Lord of the Rings" for you. There's a very good chance I try to take a class from him again.

Dr Eastley is awesome! He actually made a general class enjoyable. We did everything in class, besides a 10 page paper. Short readings before class. The group projects were fun. Don't take this if you don't like group projects. He grades fairly and tries not to take any points off. Great guy

He's great! And a very reasonable grader, too - he doesn't take off points for stupid stuff. And he's not pretentious at all, unlike most of the English faculty. Lots of group work, but it's all done in class so nobody can slack off. The homework is VERY reasonable. Since most of the work is in-class, you can focus your time on the lit review.

Dr. Eastley doesn't ever make you feel dumb. In fact, he encourages you to come up with good ideas, he gives you the right amount of affirmation, and he instills confidence in  his students. That said, he does qualify your comments, he does give you feedback, help you think more critically, and inspire you to improve. He's really that great.

He's awesome! I would take any class from him. He's clear about his expectations, interesting, and provides lots of in class group projects that let you apply real-time what you learned that day. There are 2 papers, but they're both doable. Only downside is the readings outside of class - there is approx. 30 mins-1hr of reading per class.

Prof. Eastley is super nice and not too hard of a grader, but this class was pretty dang boring. There's a decent bit of work outside of class and it doesn't feel like we actually do anything in class.

There is a lot of reading in this class, but that is to be expected. Short quiz due before every class on reading. Super nice professor who encourages lots of discussion in class and has a real passion for what he teaches. He has great insights and connects reading to life. Three tests, two papers to right. Study well for tests and you'll do fine.

He's easy-going and cares about his students, and allows everyone to freely express their opinions. You take short reading quizzes every day before class, so you can't get by without completing the readings. Tests aren't easy but he does make it clear what to study. There are only two major essays throughout the course and three tests.

Dr. Eastley loves what he teaches and helps students love it too. He is very clear about his expectations for assignments. He is a tough grader when it comes to exams, but there are so many other easily-graded assignments that is makes up for it. There are a 3 days in the semester when you just share a creative writing piece. Also, he's so nice!

HONRS 101: African-Caribbean Literature. He was so energized and passionate about the texts and introduced fascinating background information. The course was intense and Professor Eastley's insights and lectures were gripping, exciting, and enlarging. TAKE FROM EASTLEY.
Great class. Really nice guy.
Professor Eastley is a really good professor to have. The class is hard but he is so helpful that it really isn't bad. Definitely take 292 from him.

I took Professor Eastley for a class combining English 251 and 295. He was able to flawlessly integrate the classes in a way that made the material more interesting. Not only is he an amazing teacher, Professor Eastley is also inspiring spiritually. He sincerely cares about his students and is both fun and innovative. I highly recommend him!

Professor Eastley is great! You will learn from the ground up how to critique and write about literary theory in this class. His methods are simple, but their impact on your learning is amazing. You will have more confidence in your writing and criticism after taking his class. Make sure to complete each reading and be active in class discussions.

He's an awesome professor! You won't regret taking this class! He's really nice and excited about what he's teaching, so you enjoy going to class each day. His class isn't necessarily easy, but his enthusiasm and clarity helps you understand the concepts so well that sometimes it seems like an easy class.

Professor Eastley is great.  His class is structured very well. 3 mid terms (consisting of 20 multiple choice, 2 short essay responses and one long essay response) they really arent that bad as long as you have done the reading. He gives a detailed study guide and everything. Easy grader, and is specific on what he expects. Really Great Professor!

I love Professor Eastley. I was not very excited about taking 292 but he made it so awesome and I just couldn't miss class ever. Heave reading load but the test aren't hard if you pay attention to class and study. Tests are at the Humanities Testing Center so you get to type. He gives you a study guide. Right now I'm taking 380 from him!

This was an awesome class. Eastley's teaching style made it fly by. Probably the best teacher I've had at BYU. There is only one short paper, but the tests are beastly long essay tests, however, there are only 2 midterms and then the final. You won't regret taking this class from him.

Dr. Eastley is extremely smart, but also great at communicating the important points to the students. The reading load is heavy, so not for the faint of heart. But discussions were always amazing. Tests weren't too bad--short answer and essay. I would advise anyone who likes British lit to take this class--it was by far my favorite.
Gifted instructor.  Kind man.

This is the second class I've taken from Eastley, and it did not disappoint. While his classes aren't easy, if you put forth some efforts and stay on top of your readings, it really is a good class. Discussion between peers is a large part of class, and you will have to write papers. Overall, he's a great teacher and nice guy.

GREAT CLASS. would definitely take another class from him. lectures aren't boring - attendance helpful for exams cuz of discussions, etc. not too hard of a graders, but you still have to put in effort. will definitely help if you need it. nice guy. awesome teacher. no complaints about the class.

He picks and chooses his favorites. Thinks he is god of the english literature realm. when grading, he looks for ways to penalize you, not reward you. Pretends to be a "nice guy," but behind the facade lurks something not-so-nice. Unless you are his favorite, you will not be graded fairly.
Very helpful. tests were hard, but go to review sessions and attend class and you will do fine. Hard but i learned a lot.

Awesome. This was my favorite class above all others I have taken so far. The material was fantastic and Prof. Eastley presented it in an interesting way. The quizzes weren't hard, but informative and the tests were just how they should be. Anyone who says he's too hard just didn't try enough. You have to work, but in then end it's worth it.

If you love clarity and enrichment, this is your dream come true!  Professor Eastley sets up the class so you read and take small daily quizzes on blackboard (not bad at all), then, at the beginning of class he will present the writer or poet on powerpoint, then he allows you to have a group discussion, and then a combined class discussion. Perfect

Prof. Eastley does expect a lot of his students, but if you do the work, the tests are very fair. His lectures were wonderful, and he obviously is passionate about literature. I think he is a great professor, but don't think you won't have to work to get a good grade.

If he doesn't like your writing style (for instance using a semicolon rather than a period, and beginning a new sentence) then you won't get an "A". I'm never certain what I take away from lectures... very unclear.

I'm in the same class as the discrimination girl, and I've never felt that way.  He does have high expectations, but I don't think they're to be unexpected considering it's an upper level course.  My only complaint is that his tests are kinda nitpicky.  Other than that, I've learned a lot, and I've enjoyed the material he chose to cover.
No Comments
I thought this class was quite challenging, but informative at the same time. Prof Eastley is one of the more fair teachers I've had at BYU however. His tests are mostly essay based.

I really enjoyed Professor Eastley.  He makes his class challenging, but not impossible.  He tries to make the reading doable and his writing assignments are not overwhelming.  They actually help you learn about the time periods were are studying.  He's a great professor

If you take this class, don't expect an easy A.  Professor Eastley is great and even has a sense of humor, but he requires a lot out of his students.  Be prepared to do a lot of reading and even more writing if you take this class, and be ready for a lot of essays on the tests.

This class was enjoyable, but definitely not the easiest ever. His tests are a lot of memorization and essays, and he asks for very specific answers. His reviews are very helpful, you just better be great at writing essays!

I took his UNIV 101 class. Unlike other teachers I heard about, he stuck strongly to the curriculum. This made lectures a slog, but Prof. Hawkins would lead intermittent fun activities and was a joy when not limited by the basic-ness of the material. There's some some readings / short essays due each class, and he wants 100% attendance every time.

Dr. Hawkins has been the most well-organized professor I have ever taken. His does a great job of keeping his lectures engaging and summarizing the key points to know. 
One warning, however, is that the equations presented in class are not the equations used in homework assignments.

The class was in my opinion a good 9. I think Dr. Hawkins knows the material very well and it's nice to have a professor that is organized and who doesn't jump around i really appreciate it because it helped me stay focused and to see the big picture of the outcomes. He helps you out if you seek him, and doesn't make you feel stupid for not knowing

One of the best teachers I have had. The textbook is so easy to read. He wrote this textbook. The labs are really fun to do and that's your only work besides reading and going to class. I really enjoy his teaching style too. Definitely recommend this class. If you want to learn about computer or electrical engineering you won't regret this class.
Awesome class! awesome teacher! my favorite
Fun in class.  Overall nice guy.  Makes you study but homework and tests are very doable.  He tries to get students involved in class.
Good sense of humor, entertaining lectures. Has a tendancy to gloss over details; overall, though, he is very clear. Watch out for tests - the homework is NOT adequate preperation.
Dr. Hawkins truly cares for his students and is willing to help them out.  Even more than that, he is willing to be friends with us.
Provides lots of useful and fun examples. Very entertaining for an engineering class.
Prof. Jackson is the best.  I never missed the class because I enjoyed hearing the lectures.  If he is still teaching, take his class; it was by far my favorite.

Professor Jackson is amazing! He is very smart and makes the class easy. Even though the tests are easy, you get so much out of the discussions! I learned so much the semester I had him. The guy below said he "slacked off" and didn't cover all the material. It's true we didn't finish completely, but that was because he went into so much depth!

Brother Jackson was a great teacher!  He's funny and we had great discussions!  His assignments and tests are easy yet you still learn alot.  I tried to get him for the second part of Book of Mormon but he wasn't teaching it.

Honestly, I couldn't stand the teacher.  I was expecting Book of Mormon to be my favorite class.  Instead, the teacher managed to slack off so much, we barely got to half of the material. Even so, we had to read all of the pages for the entire semester, including what we didn't cover. Basically, I despised the class. Look for a better teacher.

Each week had different religion professors teaching through videos and reading. I don't understand why BYU needs to make religion classes so hard and unenjoyable. I want to enjoy learning about the gospel instead of worrying about my GPA. I enjoyed the content of this class, but it was harder and more time consuming than it should've been.

I absolutely loved this class, and I felt that Professor Merrill and Anthony cared not only for my grade but made sure I got a full understanding of the concepts being taught. Professor Merrill reached out to me two different times to make sure I felt that I understood everything and to check if I had any questions. Great class & a great teacher!

Aaron is personable and creates a positive atmosphere in the classroom. He facilitates great class discussions, shares meaningful experiences, and is knowledgeable in many areas. The class explores career paths in commercial music. It includes 6 projects, and the class attends several studio tours. If you attend and work hard, you will do well.

Excellent. Warm, friendly personality - the kind of person you just feel uplifted being around. Very respectful. Creates a motivating atmosphere and community among the students. Not the most organized or accessible outside of class, but I wouldn't worry about that if I were you. Also the class is straightforward and not too difficult.

Aaron is the man. I only know him from one class but I'd trust him with anything. He knows what he's talking about, and he's out there to make learning enjoyable. Great class (as long as you're fine to actually write songs and perform them), and Aaron is the guy to take it from.

Aaron is probably the best professor I've ever had at BYU. He's the kind of teacher that makes it very clear through his actions that he cares a lot about each student individually. He also has a ton of experience in the entertainment industry in a variety of different functions. Always has a good story to tell, hilarious guy. Loved the class.

Professor Merrill is incredible! He is a fantastic teacher who really cares for both his students, and their learning. He is passionate about what he does. Music 251 is only available to a select number of students, but as a teacher, I would highly recommend him. Clear teaching, very engaging. Wonderful guy.

Aaron Merrill is one of my favorite professors ever! He made me feel like he was more concerned about my learning rather than just giving me a grade.  You will learn so much from him.  Do the reading in the class because there will be quizzes, but the reading isn't difficult and it's interesting.  Expect work, but expect Aaron to help you lots!
Professor Miller is incredibly knowledgeable and qualified, as well as kind and personable.

BYU is lucky to have Professor Miller! He clearly makes an effort to support each of his students. His assignments are straightforward, meaningful, and not overwhelming. He makes interesting and important connections between diverse subjects during class in such a way that adds inspiration to the course content. Would definitely recommend.

Professor Miller was a highlight of my Masters program at BYU. His ability to explain often complex principles in an easily digestible manner made this course so enjoyable to me. As well, the coursework felt relevant and progressed my understanding of the subjects rather than simply a task to be completed. I'd highly recommend taking his courses.

Aaron is an incredible professor. He knows what he's talking about. His lectures were engaging and applicable to my life. He is super available outside of class and helped me decide if I want to pursue a master's degree. The tests in this class aren't very hard. There are a few bigger assignments, but no busy work. Highly recommend taking form him.

I had such a great experience with prof. miller! he is so genuine and his assignments are pretty easy, and you'll actually learn so much from them + his lectures. I really like his teaching style and how engaging he is! take msb390 from him!
Good guy overall. He was a bit didactic. Most of the discussions seemed like him trying to get everyone to agree with his POV instead of learning. Feels a lot like a philosophy class.
Worst religion class I've taken. Would not recommend.

I mostly enjoyed this class. Tests were online and open book. He gave really good feedback on my assignments. HIs lectures were a little boring. Class discussions could be interesting until they started to drag on. Most assignments were very doable. He did throw a group project at us at the end of the semester that was frustrating. Overall: good.

Professor Miller was a great Book of Mormon professor. He is not part of the religion department, but I learned a lot from him! You need good attendance and good notes in his class. A lot of what is tested on is discussions we had in class. Overall an amazing teacher, I certainly felt the spirit and learned a lot from him.

Honestly he is the most eloquent and well spoken teacher I have ever had the privilege of learning from. He sincerely cares about his students and their insights/understanding of the Book of Mormon. I loved his class.

He was absolutely amazing. He really cares about the students and their understanding of the Book of Mormon. His lectures were amazing and gave a lot of opportunities for student participation. He made difficult gospel concepts easy through clear examples and ideas.

Not anywhere close to being done with this class and it is my favorite. I am a senior. I do not care about school at this point, but I love this class. It is thought provoking, and the only qualitative class at BYU I actually enjoyed. Grades are not the emphasis. He replies to all my emails. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Professor Miller not once returned a single email I had returned to him, and you had to wait forever to get assignments graded. Overall I found the lectures extremely boring and the essays were worse.  Definitely try to get another teacher if possible, but if not he isn't that horrible.

The lectures were the best in the integrated core, but I had a very hard time trying to get help from him. He handed many papers back late, and never responded to my emails, even after I talked to him in class. He is a nice guy, but with his law practice on the side I don't think he has a lot of time to help students.

I CAN'T BELIEVE THESE NICE COMMENTS!!  Grades papers very harshly.  In the integrated core I always got A's on my papers except his class. Very interesting lectures but very unclear on assignments.  Got back papers late.  The bad DEFINITELY outweighed the good.  Take anyone else.  NOT AN EASY A! Don't be fooled by previous comments like I did!
Fantastic teacher. He was one of the most helpful teachers I have ever had. The homework made you think and understand the principles of business ethics. Take this dude over anyone if you can
He is a great guy and a really good ethics teacher.  A former lawyer he really knows his stuff and offers a lot of insight into the world of ethics.  I would recommend him.

Class: interesting group discussions with participation encouraged.  Hmwk: light reading, two group papers, and a couple individual assignments.  Tests: take-home essays for the final.  Teacher: respectful and smart.

GREAT teacher. Really smart and gets you to think about things from all perspectives. Really fair grader, cares about his students. Responds quickly to emails and is very understanding. I learned a lot in his class. Do the reading ON TIME. That is HUGE. Participate too.
Really smart guy.  I really liked BUS M 390.

Brother Schade is the goat! I loved his lectures because they were focused on the most important things. He also answered so many questions I had about the Pearl of Great Price. He's quite the scholar and I learned things that I'd never even dreamt of. He is an endlessly patient person and I could tell he wanted to get to know each student.

He's super knowledgeable on the Bible so his lectures are SO insightful. Good as it gets. The hw load isn't bad at all. He's super understanding and loves to teach. The only knock is that the exams are really tough. But, if you study hard, you'll be fine. But honestly, his teaching ability and knowledge on the subject is totally worth it.

Online reading assignment due before class, make 2 comments then participation quiz. My main beef with this class: lectures, slides content, and test content did not match up. Stuff on tests was often not discussed in class. Tests are online, open scripture, but felt like I was scrambling for answers. Wouldn't take again, take someone else.
Honestly a very caring and smart professor. If you like the Bible, I'd highly suggest his class.

I did enjoy this class however it required knowing a lot of specific information which was difficult for closed-note tests. Brother Schade is a really nice guy and also knows so much. Sometimes it was difficult to know what was bonus info and what I should know.

Professor Schade truly cares about his students. Most of the grade is completion and even though his lectures are prone to meander, the tests are still pretty simple if you take good notes. If you turn in the study guide he adds those points to your test, so it's easy to get above 100.

I loved Dr Schade! He was very caring (called us by name). Lectures were sometimes hard to follow with extraneous detail and picking out which relevant historical details, but take good notes on the study guide & in  personal scriptures. They will be useful for the exams! The homework really wasn't bad and the lectures were uplifting to attend.

Professor Shade is one of the kindest teachers I have ever had. His class was a safe space to feel the spirit, without homework stress. He gives a study guide at the beginning of the semester with everything we need for our exams.  Some of his lectures were repetitive, but I felt like it helped me to prepare for the test.

Dr. Schade as a person is 10/10. Very loving and sincere with a strong testimony. Not my favorite course ever though. I was confused about what I supposed to be learning. Complicated slides. Not sure if anything stuck with me. Test reviews, study guides seemed far from what was on exams. Readings due before each class. Easy class, just confusing

Dr. Schade is great, his lectures are very spiritual and pressure-free. The tests are a bit confusing at times, but the class in and of itself isn't too hard at all. A great teacher for the Pearl of Great Price.

His qualification to teach this class is that he used to travel to the Middle East. He really has a strong testimony, but it's a very boring class. You have to annotate a TON. He has a study guide, but his test questions often don't line up with it, and are very specific about what Greek translations mean, rather than the real content. Not fun.

Prof. Schade was a great teacher and I really enjoyed learning from him. However, the material on the tests is little unclear. Other than that, the grades are really easy to get. Don't take this class if you aren't going to pay attention and really try and understand the material for the tests.

Dr. Schade is the most impactful professor I have ever had. He cares tremendously for each of his students, has an incredible testimony, and teaches with powerful sincerity. If you are looking for a religion class where you will not just learn the facts but feel the spirit and be completely changed as a person, this is the one.

Loved Prof. Schafer! I took this online, on demand. He had recorded lectures which were excellent- Spirit-filled! I took screenshots and made my own Google Docs for study. His grading/expectations are a little ambiguous. Other than that, the class is perfect. I would definitely take from him again.  This class requires doable/rewarding work.

My class was online and I forgot to do an assignment. Before I could reach out to ask for an opportunity to do the assignment, HE emailed ME to tell me he would still let me do it for full points. Grateful for a professor who really cares about his students! Plus the class is mostly watching lectures, reading scriptures, and participation quizzes.

Took his online OT class. The lectures were many and not very engaging, but I imagine the online format didn't help any. Lots of homework, but the assignments were fair and graded mostly on completion. Tests were hard. Overall a decent class, and he was kind to me when I reached out with some issues-- he's a very caring professor & knows his stuff.

Dr. Schade was one of the kindest professors I've ever had. He's wonderful. His Pearl of Great Price class is stellar. Only critique is I felt the tests were a little unclear. I didn't really know what I was supposed to know, and they felt fact heavy. I thought the class would be "what do the scriptures say" but it felt more like a history class.

Love this guy. I took his class on demand. Bi-weekly participation quizzes on LS for "attendance". I never really watched the lectures until before the tests. The tests are on LS and honestly all of the answers are from his lectures so if you cram those a day or two before you'll be fine. Easy religion and I found what he taught interesting.
Tests are very ambiguous to study for, which makes it hard to know what to take out of reading and lecture. Avoid this professor if you can

I appreciated Brother Schade's compassion, and the very passionate way he taught. However, often, I got confused about what he was saying most of the time. The tests are tricky, but he does curve them.

I really don't understand why his rating is so low -- Bro Schade is an amazing teacher. He emphasizes understanding more than memorization and helps you follow along with the entire story and history of the scriptures. He also treats this like an actual religion class -- No quizzes, just based on participation.

Dr. Schade has been a terrific teacher at the Jerusalem Center. He cares about his students and will always give his time to students in need. He is extremely well educated and intelligent and knows the material he is teaching.

Dr. Schade is incredibly knowledgeable about all the historical and language context in the scriptures, which constantly provides new and exciting insights into the meaning. He has the best tests of any religion professor- its none of the nitpicky trip-you-up questions about minor side characters or scripture mastery and more of a testimony session

I loved Brother Schade!! With BYU being so crazy and stressful at times, it is REALLY nice having a class where you don't have to stress about your grade. His lectures were very interesting, and I had many wonderful experiences in his class. His lectures might seem boring if you are not participating :)

I don't know why everyone else is rating him so low. His lectures are intriguing and very spiritual. His homework isn't tough or time-consuming. Tests are long and open book and notes, so if you take good notes during lecture, you'll do fine. Honestly, he's a great professor with fantastic insights. Just put forth good effort and you'll enjoy it.

Dr. Schade is incredibly nice, and his class is an easy A, but his lectures are SO boring! It's honestly not worth the easy A. He takes attendance and incorporates it into the grade. I fell asleep every lecture and/or was on my phone the whole time.
He seems nice, but he makes you hate the scriptures.

Interesting material, but it's hard to know what to study for, especially since there is no study guides for the test. If you miss a class and don't get the notes you're done for. Again, hard to know what to study.   Interesting material though.

His lectures are random and off topic, he mostly bounces around through his slideshows and talks about whatever comes to mind. He knows the scriptures, and he certainly knows Hebrew and Greek (as he likes to prove often) but he doesn't know how to teach.

I love going to his lectures. Granted, they are a little off topic sometimes, but are in depth. He loves getting into the Hebrew and historical settings of the New Testament, which I find interesting. He knows everyone by name and helps us out on the test. I literally got to take my notes and scriptures into the testing center!
We don't really study the scriptures, just a bunch of outside stuff he thinks is cool. Not very helpful.

Bro. Schade is a fantastic human being and I love the way he teaches. Yes, it's true, based on lectures it's hard to determine what will be on the test. However, it's like that because he formats his lectures according to comments given, and really is just a facilitator of discussion. I personally love that style of teaching. TA reviews are helpful
Professor Schade is an interesting teacher. He is passionate about his subject matter, but will sometimes ask obvious questions. He is a good teacher and the assignments aren't bad at all.

It's weird, he seems nice but he's no help. He doesn't do study guides and the TA reviews are vague. We go over a bunch of Hebrew and historic dates instead of the scriptures. Class is long and confusing. I wish it had gone better because the Pearl of Great Price seemed super interesting.

Professor Schade is a nice guy, but his lectures are really boring, and it's hard to take notes in class, because you don't know what to expect on the tests.  The TA reviews before the tests definitely helped.
This class was dry and long. He doesn't give a handbook, reviews, study guides, or anything helpful. Worst class I've taken so far.
Not good. He was not helpful. I took this to study the scriptures and instead we studied a lot of history stuff. Would not recommend to my worst enemy.

I took the FHSS 300 class, and it was really fun. The course was definitely kinda messy, and I had a hard time finding a clear rubric for the assignments. The textbook didn't teach me much but the exam is open book. Professor Skaebelund was very helpful and accommodating when it came to our projects. He is always willing to help!
The homework that he gives you is the research that you have to do.

If you can get past his gravely voice, he's a super nice guy and cares a lot about civic engagement. His class was super interesting, and I would highly recommend it if your interested in the civic engagement minor. The lecturers he brought in were very interesting. Overall, he is a little unorganized but its fine because the class is still easy.

I am a history major. To be very short, skip this class, and Prof. Skabelund in general. Incredibly disorganized, he is not clear at all about his expectations, and his grading is based on stuff that isn't in any instructions or rubric. Reading and writing are crazy unreasonable, and I live in textbooks and essays full time. The class stunk.

The workload for this class is very heavy, with extensive reading assignments, a lot of busy work, and vague instructions on assignments/essays. The grading is very harsh, making the course more challenging than expected. Also, the final includes 2 1500-word essays and a written exam. I wouldn't recommend it unless it's required for your major.

If you don't have to take this class, don't take it. I took it for a GE and was severely disappointed in the heavy work load. Be prepared to read 40+ pages per week. There are 6 required books for this class. There was an essay almost every week and a big research project at the end of the semester. My least favorite class of the semester.

While the class and material is interesting, the professor is easily one of the worst I have ever had. He makes the class so unorganized and much more difficult than it has to be. The group project requires lots of outside time including many things that were not explained on learning suite. The professor is very unprepared, I do not recommend

Super cool class! Interesting lectures & helped me develop new perspectives on WWII. If you work hard and do the reading you can get a good grade in the class. Tests are chill, just make sure you memorize everything on the SG (defs/dates/places). The group project is a little tough, but if you choose dedicated peers to work with you will be fine!

There is a large project worth 20% of your grade that has NO rubric to go with it. Seriously, don't do it unless you are willing to fight for your grade, and still only have it raised by .5%. The tests are fine, you just can't rely on just the study guide. The content is interesting, but there is a lot of reading.

I dropped this class after the first class period. He does not dive into the military history. He basically said, "We will pretty much neglect the tactics, strategies, etc. and just focus on the social history of the War and how we have perceived it." I would not recommend if you are a military history buff and want to learn about the battles, etc.

This was the most interesting class I took. The reading material was extensive and fascinating, and Professor Skabelund was supportive and helpful. I would recommend this to anyone who wants to learn about WWII and is willing to spend time in reading and study.

So much reading due before every class that you could be quizzed on. There are five textbooks you have to buy for the class so be prepared for that. Most of the reading is interesting, but sometimes it's too much. We don't discuss everything we read either so a lot of it feels like a waste of time. His instructions on the big projects are vague
I really liked Professor Skabelund. The class was very interesting and very well structured.

Great guy. His lectures don't cover much of material that is tested. There are two textbooks and 3+ other books you read through the semester that you have to write papers on. He is accessible out of class and wants students to succeed. Most of the material for tests and exams comes from textbooks. TA does the grading, so you're at their mercy.

If you read for an hour before the reading assignment is due, attend lectures, and cram before a test you'll get an A. Teacher recognized me outside of class, so I knew he cared about his students. Lectures were interesting if you enjoy history. He can be disorganized sometimes, but does a good job pulling everything together. Grades fairly.

2.5/5. Skabelund cares about his students and knows a lot about history, but that doesn't translate to a great class. Lectures feel disorganized; sometimes they are very big picture conceptual and sometimes very detailed. His emphasis is Japanese history so that was covered better compared to China/Korea.
Too much (boring!) reading.

History's never been my subject, took this to fulfill a requirement and found myself willing to put in the time toward readings and assignments because I found it interesting and applicable. I spent 1-2 hours leading up to class on readings + a paragraph response, the remainder of assignments were clear and manageable. Highly recommend

I showed up on the first day terrified based on a few of the reviews and history not being my thing, but I took it for a GE and it ended up being my favorite class. Professor Skabelund is a funny guy and way easygoing, I left every class feeling motivated to change the world. Super grateful I kept the class and took a chance

I have taken HIST 343 and 344 from Dr. Skabelund and this class is much easier. Very clear assignments. History majors or people familiar with history classes will find the class easy. History novices will find it approachable. Good GE. 3% points worth of extra credit, so that is really nice. Do your work and EC and you will succeed.

Prof. Skabelund is one of the best teachers I've had at BYU, personality-wise. He is very funny, caring, and charismatic. However, the class is HARD. It's not necessarily a ton of work, but unequal distribution of points and him being a tough grader will take the joy out of what's otherwise a pretty fun class. Choose a topic you love!

Grading is harder than 343. Lots of reading with comp. questions, a group poster that was graded harshly (The class average was 80%, the only people that did well placed in competition). 2 or 3 book dissections. Mt and Final are not bad if you've been paying attention. Very nice person, lots of good info about Japan. Up to 3% EC. Not a hard A.
Amazing professor. He truly seeks to understand students and do the best he can to care for them.

I loved Pro. Skabelund's class!! Be warned, there was a lot of reading. You will use around 8-9 books and read most of them. Skabelund is a very good teacher who gives good lectures and leads amazing discussions. The class does a great job of informing you on the events of WWII and then connecting them to modern-day events. Highly recommend!

Dr. Skabelund's Intro to East Asian History is amazing, and he's a fantastic instructor. He makes the history come alive, and none of the homework feels like busy work. It takes work to stay on top of it, but nothing unreasonablemaybe a couple hrs/week. Instead of essays, the writing assignments are like expanded prewrites with clear instructions.

So so bad. Like its several years later and I still think about how terrible of a teacher he was. His lectures were literally about whatever he wanted. I dont remember learning anything in the lectures that was on the tests, but you still have to go because of pop quizzes. It was absolutely miserable. Do yourself a huge favor dont take him.

B- average in a general class, lost my 4.0 in this class where I put more effort in than the 99% I got in Ochem. Doesn't understand his own course material and tries to make questions hard by using vocab he doesn't know the meaning of. Gives C average on his essays. While a few people did get A's I have no idea how.

I took both HIST 293 & HIST 344 from Dr. Skabelund. They were the most difficult classes I took at BYU, & though I was stressed and almost led to cursing DURING the courses, I managed to get an A in both, & as I look back I realized how much I learned. They were absolutely my favorite classes! He makes you THINK & LEARN!

His grading on essays is unrealistic. There is so much to memorize for his tests. I really would not recommend any of his classes unless you are very interested in the subject matter. He is such a nice, approachable guy. It is a bummer that his classes are so hard.

Professor Skabelund genuinely wants his students to work hard and learn. That being said, all of his classes have a low B average. History 231 was just too much work and then too much memorizing for the tests. His standards for papers are too high. You will not get an A on the papers unless you meet with him. He cannot objectively grade. Shame.

Dr. Skabelund is a good guy, but this class was rough. He does "write to learn"s to make sure you read the textbook, and that 1-3 minutes of writing adds up to 2% of your grade each x 10. Tests had SO much material to memorize which is expected in a history class, but his expectations for essay responses are so high. The final is 2-3 hrs of writing

This class didn't meet my expectations. The reading material was usually interesting and the required movies were great. However, lectures didn't have structure; they were usually redundant and always tied back to Japanese dogs. He offers a lot of extra credit and the assignments and quizzes weren't too difficult so it is easy to get a good grade.

Tests are manageable; some questions are copy-paste from textbook study questions and he gives you terms to memorize. So if you just study you should get an A or B.  Only one actual paper, then just easy homework/reading questions. Pop quizzes on the reading and study questions, but not too bad. There aren't a lot of points so no room for error.

Prof. Skabelund's WWII class is awesome. He has an effective grading system and he offers plenty of extra credit opportunities. He's a very fair teacher. Doing the reading and attending lecture are necessary, but if you are diligent about those then the tests are totally doable. He also provides thorough study guides before the tests.

I really enjoyed this class. I wasn't the biggest fan of the setup of the class and the tests are difficult but there are a lot of opportunities to gain points and he gives out the most extra credit of any professor at BYU. If you enjoy history than this will be a great class for you.

Prof. Skabelund is a nice guy, and this isn't too difficult of a class. Lectures can be pretty boring, but just go over the detailed test reviews that he gives out before the test, and you will do fine. You also have to read three novels throughout the semester, but they're not too bad, and the papers you have to write for them are super easy.

He's a really great Professor and he really likes what he teaches and it shows. There were no hidden questions on the test and he upfront told the class what is expected, etc. There was not a terrible amount of reading. He was always willing to help and gave clear, prompt feedback on papers, etc. Take a class from him, you won't regret it!

He is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He loves what he teaches and tries to make it interesting. Dry wit, but funny :) He's willing to work with you even if that means meeting one-on-one. He opens class up to comments and questions (the more you get involved the more you'll learn). He cares for his students and desires their success.

Skabelund's course is more on memory than history. He balances Europe with Asia and I learned things I've never heard of before. Warning: there are 9 books for this course and you read the equivalent of 7 1/2 of them. This class is a ton of work but it is worth it if WWII and especially memory fascinates you. tests are mostly essay format.

WWII: As one of the previous commenter said about this class, I was really looking forward to this class but ended up hating it. Skabelund is a great guy and really tries hard to engage the class in historical discussion, but the class is set up poorly in my opinion. Way too much reading, pop quizzes, and alot of useless blog posts you have to do

Great teacher, great class. Some real work in reading/writing but he made sure that the subjects were interesting. There is a lot of reading, but about half of it is well chosen historical novels that I really enjoyed and I still have on my bookshelf. You might have to put some effort in, but if you actually like learning this is a great class.

I really did not like his teaching style. I felt his lectures never tied in well with his tests...he mostly talked about modern problems in the world or tried to tie things into the importance of dogs.He didn't test on these things though, it was all on reading, but he still makes you come to his classes and listen to those lectures with quizzes.

I didn't enjoy this class. Lectures were usually. I usually enjoy history but I didn't like the emphasis on Asia.  Its a world history class but it felt like he tied everything back to Asia (and dogs), y so I felt like we missed a lot of important things. I never did the readings but got a B. He is a nice guy though and tries hard to learn names.

There are pop quizzes so you'll go to class, but I wouldn't have gone if not for that. I felt that his lectures were slow and often didn't deal with material covered on the tests. Granted, it was a GE class, so he might be better in a class he enjoys teaching a little more.

He uses a lot of media in his teaching, which is very interesting. It shows lots of different viewpoints. His specialty is Japan, and it shows. There is a lot of reading, but it is not very hard, and is definitely interesting. The quizzes are VERY easy as long as you read and do the online questions. The TA's are helpful and so are the reviews.
Modern Japan is his specialty, and it shows. A good amount of reading is required, but I found it all very interesting. Workload was very manageable, and I always enjoyed our discussions.

Great class. The monographs we read were interesting (and the assignments connected with the readings were cake), but there is a big emphasis on the final paper. Skabelund's always willing to help out, though, so stop by his office hours and you will be fine. A great class if you are a history major looking for an elective or have interest in Japan
For the reading quizzes, it is easy to simply use the questions on the online textbook review.  These are what he draws the attendance quizzes from.
Great teacher, excellent historian. Cares about the subject and his students. Highly recommend the class.

I was really looking forward to this class and ended up hating it. He reads his lectures, the assignments are redundant and unclear, there is up to 70 pages of reading for each class period. It focused heavily on the Japanese side of WWII and talked very little of the war in Europe or the American homefront. I would not recommend one of his classes

Prof. Skabelund is an awesome professor. He brings a unique perspective to history and I never learned so much from one class. There is a lot of reading but the textbook is not so bad and the novels we read are very interesting and applicable to the topic. Be prepared to work hard but in the end you'll learn a lot.

This class was really intense. There was a lot to cover and not very much time. There was a lot of reading. The tests were pretty difficult. Prof. Skabelund is awesome though. He is always willing to help and very excited about what he taught.

Professor Skabelund was awesome! He has restructured his class in a way that makes the class very straightforward (what you put into the class is what you'll get out of it--including you're grade). He taught things that changed my perspective on history and life. Great class and great professor.

This professor has a good structure for his class, his assignments and schedule is clear.  However, his tests are very difficult--reading assignments and attending lectures will not guarantee you an A.  He does not a study guide and gives vague answers on what we need to know.  Assigns LOTS of reading.  His focus on Japan/Asia was neat though.

He has good intentions, but he's still trying to figure out how to run his classes. He was difficult to understand at times, he KEPT changing the syllabus, and the entire semester I was never sure what my grade was. There was also a TON of reading and writing, which was due weekly.

Nice guy but really hard to understand him when he speaks. Lots of reading, boring lectures.  BIG research paper. He grades semi-fairly.  There are weekly readings, postings, and discussions which got really boring.  Nevertheless, I feel like I did learn something about Japanese history, just in a boring drawn-out kinda way.
He class is so boring. And very busy work and hard grader.worse class ever take from BYU so far.

He was a nice guy.  I think that he'll get to be a better teacher in time.  The lectures were pretty boring, but the material was interesting.  I got a B+ in my worst academic semester at BYU (I was engaged, give me some credit).  Allright teacher.

One of the few classes where I've began hating a class and grown to like the class throughout the semester.  His lectures could be horrid sometimes, but at others they could be very impressive.  He'll be a good professor eventually.  I learned about a subject I don't care about, so I was impressed by that.  Grading is hard, however. Very hard.

He was a nice teacher who tried to articulate his thoughts and ideas and tried to get the class involved, even if it didnt always work he wanted to improve.  He had essays as busywork but the readings and the movie viewings were really interesting. The TA's were willing to help you with whatever and I found it an enjoyable class.

Because it was his first semester, I believe he did not know the right direction to go.  However, he seemed intent on improving his teaching.  It seemed as though his grading was fair. My only complaint was the lack of connection between the lectures and the reading but it seems as though he was aware of that and wanted to improve. Not too bad.

I think some of the other ratings were too mean.  He's a really nice guy.   He's more interested in trends in history rather than in dates and names.  The TA's are hard graders, so put effort into your papers.  If you work for it, you'll get a good grade.

I think the other ratings were a bit harsh.  Grading was very harsh.  No tests, weekly essays.  Essays are all based on outside reading so in class discussion seemed irrelevant.  Skabelund himself was fine, enjoyed group discussion.  Not an easy class.

This semester was his first semester teaching, and he wasn't that good, although he did improve a little. There weren't any tests, just lots of papers, required movie viewings, and extra books you had to read. He's nice, and is kind of a pushover. He usually hinted if he was giving a pop quiz.

The absolute worst class I've ever taken at BYU. Avoid it like the plague. He can't teach and his TA's grade like its a masters English class. They will help you if you ask but are pretty set in their grading. Even though they are intimidating, get to know them; it helps. Don't stick around for this class unless you ABSOLUTELY have to. It's a big mistake.

Nice and funny guy. I'd recommend taking this class AFTER anatomy. Class consists of quizzes, exams, and two papers (easy). Slides/textbooks aren't helpful because exams are based on his opinion and what's said in class. Willing to work with us and push things back when needed. Responds quickly to emails. Heard other teachers are easier, though.

This class is a piece of cake, especially if you have taken any anatomy/physiology classes beforehand. Lots of basic knowledge and the things that weren't basic were really interesting. He tells good stories and is an all around funny and personable guy. Its a great class, go take it:)

Aaron is a nice guy. However, this class was rough! Tests and quizzes essentially make up your whole grade. The tests are HARD and seem to be subjective off his opinion rather than objective off facts. Things are often keyed wrong- points are given back haphazardly. Grading and points appeared very disorganized! He also doesn't respond to emails.
Aaron is a great guy but not the greatest teacher. There's lots of busy work, really unclear expectations and poor communication. Also the class I took is different from any of the options up there

What a great teacher. His lectures are super enjoyable and it's really interesting stuff to learn. Highly recommend a class from him. The hardest thing in this class is the tests, you HAVE to show up to class and take notes because you're tested on what HE SAYS bc the slides are basically just bullet points and don't tell you half of what you need

Dr Wells is fine. He is a genuinley nice guy. If you want things to run on time and feel like a college level class, he isn't the right guy for you. He wasn't clear on which tape jobs we needed to know, and I was graded down for following the lab manual vs the lecture (given by his TAs and himself)

I have taken this class and been a TA for this professor and it is SO much work. This is an entry level class and had wayyy to much information for the level of class it was. He rambles quite a bit, but does care for the students and wants them to do well. I only did well bc my TA created good reviews...

I loved Aaron! Sometimes his exams just felt thrown together, but he gives points back a lot because of it. He's a funny guy without trying and I've learned a ton from this class that's been very useful with injuries this year. Good credit to get for my exsc folks with requirements to fill. The lab is also super easy and really fun.

Lol this guy annoyed me so much at first but then he grew on me. Tests are hard because they have random questions we didn't go over, also not written very well so he ends up giving back a lot of points for his mistakes on each test. no textbook. records his lecture if you miss class. such an easy class but my grade didn't reflect that bc of tests.

The material was good, but felt super disorganized. Having never taken anatomy, class was much more difficult to understand. The TA's are terrible. Their reviews are essentially them saying know everything topic by topic. Aaron is super nice though and you can tell he really cares. It can be difficult to extract what's pertinent from his lectures.

Dr. Wells is amazing! His lectures are great and you don't have to worry about getting a good grade in his class because if you study and just pay attention you'll ace the Tests. The pop quizzes are super easy if you review the material. Definitely the highlight of my semester.
great professor harsh grader but enjoyable class
Great professor, great class. Pretty easy and lectures are awesome.

Always a blast to be in his class! Has so many stories involving sports players getting injured. Quizzes are weekly and are pretty easy if you review the material from last class. Any injury he reviews where he tells a story will definitely be on the test. A super interesting class!

Professor Wells was a really good professor.  He has in class quizzes, and you don't know when they will be so you should go to class.  He has an extra credit assignment at the end of the semester which is really easy.  He includes stories and pictures and videos in lecture. Really good class.

Ok, I really didn't like this guy. Maybe it was just because this was his first time teaching a religion class, but the class was a joke. I could have skipped every single class and still have gotten a good grade. His tests are a mess and he talks way to much about his personal life during his "lectures."

Dr. Wells is by far my favorite professor that i've had. His lectures are very interesting and he has had so many life experiences that apply to his class. He is an extremely kind and caring guy who loves to tell jokes and tries to make his class easy and fun, while also helping everyone learn as much as possible. Definitely take a class from him.

I really liked Dr Wells. However, his organization is lacking. He tests on things not covered in class simply because I think he forgets what he has already talked about and what he has not. He is a great person and his lectures are great. But it's hard to get an A on his test as you have to guess out of thin air on a bunch of questions.

I had him for Intermediate Basketball and he was okay.  He seems to really like hearing himself speak, and most days we didn't start playing till 15 after the hour.  His class was almost all 5 on 5, no drills or learning. So if you like 5 on 5 basketball, but need 15 minutes to warm up, take him.

Basic Taping Lab is a great class. Take the evening section if possible though because then you get to practice right after you learn, which is great for really getting the wraps down. The only test is the final, but there are quizzes every week, so make sure you know your stuff. Great class, very applicable to people who are active. Loved it!

Aaron is a fantastic professor, one of the best I've had at BYU! I loved his class. He gives plenty of examples of the things he's talking about and leaves plenty of time to ask questions. Test reviews are during class so you don't have to make extra time for them. Great class, would take again in a heartbeat!

Aaron Wells is a great teacher. it is a basic class but he goes into pretty deep detail. I would recommend taking anatomy first if possible. This class does into pretty specific anatomical structures and it helps to have that background. I would recommend this class to anyone interested in it.

Take anatomy first. I got an A in chemistry but a B+ in this class because I had to teach myself anatomy as I was learning about each injury. I wasn't sure what to study for the exams because we covered so much in class. Some previous knowledge would be extremely helpful.

Aaron is a great teacher. His class isn't easy, but he's very clear on what he expects from you. You need to study good and hard for the tests. He goes over everything that he tests you on, so you don't have to second guess what he's going to ask you. He also makes class fun. Highly recommended.

Amazing professor, if you need to take ACC 310 this is the professor to take it from! Also she shares a thought at the beginning of every class and it was at least as amazing as any of my REL classes.

Prof. Allen is AMAZING! She is highly qualified and presents for the FASB often. She cares so deeply about her students and does an incredible job at helping them learn the material. Her lectures are engaging, informative, and spiritual/inspiring despite just being about accounting lol—and she organizes her course super well! 10/10 recommend!
Dr. Allen is incredibly smart. Teaches in an amazing way and provides real world insight. If you are planning to enter the ACC program I suggest you take it from her.
Taking ACC 310 with Professor Allen is such a breeze — I got 100%

Allen is amazing. All 310 classes are mega hard as its a filter class for the program. You have two midterms and a final that aren't comprehensive. You have two weekly homework assignments that each take and hour + a little. The tests are extremely hard. All the questions are meant to trick you. Do all the extra review stuff and you'll be good.

Prof. Allen was one of the most kind and caring professors I've ever had. The class' exams were hard, but that's not on her. She taught the material well and answered questions and had really good devotionals. I love how she would tell us to prioritize scripture study and wanted us to do well!

One of, if not the best teacher I've had at BYU. She cares about what she teaches but also cares about the students and wants everyone to excel. She shares really good spiritual thoughts every class and teaches the class material so it's easy to understand. 10/10 would recommend.

Prof. Allen has been my favorite professor here at BYU so far. She explains tough concepts very clearly and always relates what we are learning to the real world. She knows what she is talking about and cares about her students' success. Would 10/10 recommend taking a class from her!

LOVE prof allen! Shes super knowledgable and makes lectures interesting. She also gives the best spiritual thoughts ever- truly inspiring and i look up to her so much! She explains hard concepts super well and i would DEF take acc310 from allen

Dr. Allen is such a goated accounting professor. She explains everything super well and also is able to invite the spirit into the classroom. Prof. Allen truly cares for her students. She organized this course clearly - I always knew expectations. Great professor who always stops to make sure everyone understands the concepts. This was managerial accounting in the core. Was a hard class but not as hard as the others this semester (financial, tax, and integrated topics). She's a great professor, highly recommend.

Professor Allen is a great ACC 310 professor! The class is based on 3 tests, 3 projects graded based on completion, and interactive pre-class readings and post-class quizzes. Best professor at BYU, hands down. Professor Allen brought Harvard Business School to Provo, and you'll want to be part of her amazing lectures. Dr. Allen is a beast, she is willing to work with you and walk you through every concepts. She is also a professor that makes accounting fascinating and applying. Listen to her reviews and " tokes" that's where exam coming from and made it to accounting program with no problem thanks to her. Highly recommended~!!

Dr. Allen honestly changed my life. She very clearly explained the accounting concepts and helped us to apply them, but more importantly she made sure we put first things first. Professor Allen is one of my favorite professors I've ever had! She is so eloquent and approachable. The tests are more difficult than the practice exams for sure, but they aren't outrageously hard. I loved how grounded she was/how much she talked about the things that matter most in life.

Definitely the most effort I've had to put into a class, but I know I got a lot out of it. Not a fan of the textbook, pre-class quizzes, extremally difficult exams, and lack of study guides, but Professor Allen was very knowledgeable and lectures were great. Prof. Allen was great! The class material is pretty hard, but she made it understandable. The tests and final are not cumulative which is amazing. Honestly not a very hard class and professor Allen was super cool. Most topics are just a review of ACC 200 with maybe a tiny bit more in depth. Tests are much more difficult than the exam prep resources you're given. Prof Allen was super kind and lectures were good. We focused a lot on real world examples, which I appreciated. However, the exams were ridiculously hard. Wow. Professor Allen is my favorite professor at BYU by FAR! Her teaching style is incredible and even if your grades aren't the best, she gives the best pep talks and reminds her students what matters most. She believes in her students and loves to push them to do their best. Her class was amazing.

Professor Allen is awesome! She is an amazing teacher and really cares about her students success in her class and their personal lives. The textbook she uses is a little convoluted and tough to understand sometimes but she always explains everything really well in class. She is super fair to all her students and is so incredibly intelligent.
Professor Allen is a queen. She cares about her students so much and is willing to go above and beyond to give you the help you need. If you out in the work, you will do well.

Absolutely Incredible. 310 is just a hard class, but you will not regret taking it from Dr. Allen. She is one of a kind. Incredible professor that does everything she possibly can to help you succeed. High Expectations, but very empowering. Absolutely recommend.

Professor Allen is great at explaining difficult concepts and she is more than willing to meet with students outside of class. Professor Allen is wonderful. She teaches well and your success if her priority. Accounting 310 is difficult no matter who you take it from. The tests are hard, but they are a good benchmark to see if you truly have a grasp on the material.

Professor Allen was the absolute best! I loved her! She is a boss lady and she really cares. Shes also way funny and is an amazing teacher!! Acc 310 is insanely hard no matter who you take it from and all of the professors are amazing!

One of my absolute favorite professors. She has a passion for accounting and is really there to help. She made difficult concepts seem much simpler and made learning accounting really fun. Able to tie the gospel into class as well. Her class really helped me to decide if accounting was the path I should take

Prof. Allen is amazing and so inspirational! She is a true mentor and really cares about her students. It was an insanely difficult semester for me, and Prof. Allen was the professor I turned to, because I respect her greatly. She has a real passion for Accounting and teaching.

Dr. Allen is the best! She truly cares about her students and loves her job. She explains very clearly, is always willing to help, and likes to make accounting jokes during class. The lectures were extremely helpful, but the textbook absolutely sucks despite also being pretty helpful. Despite losing interest in Accounting, I still loved this course
Favorite teacher during Fall semester of the Junior Core. Strong, but caring personality. Makes difficult concepts easy to understand. Hecka hard class, but she makes it reasonable.

Professor Allen is a great lecturer. One thing that was frustrating about her class is that the textbook is terrible and you are quizzed on the readings before class get a bad grade on the quiz and then come to class and she makes it was easier to understand. Amazing proffesor, shes clear when she teaches and cares about you learning. The book is not the best, but she teaches everything in class (and 10 times better than the book). Strong independent woman
Professor Allen knows her stuff and wants you to come prepared. She keeps class focused and is easy to understand.

I loved taking physics 105 from professor bennion. He was one of the most kind teachers ever. Professor Bennion was a great professor! I would highly recommend taking from him. Physics is hard in general, but he was always available outside of class to help explain and break down and explain. Prof. Bennion was amazing! I took physics from him last semester. His lectures are good and he explains things clearly. I frequently saw him in the physics help lab answering questions. Loved Dr. Bennion! He's an extremely caring professor and was engaging during class. Awesome and enthusiastic teacher. It is obvious he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The material is difficult but he does a great job conveying it in a way that makes sense. His lectures are engaging and the demonstrations are fun.

This was a relatively easy class compared to other courses and the grading scale is very lenient. Content was very basic and easy to learn by just listening in class and doing the homework. Never had to study and still got an A. He doesn't give the best explanations for things though and many students could explain it better.
I loved Dr. Bennion. His lectures were very enjoyable and you can see the passion he has for physics. This was a difficult class so I found it super helpful to go to the TA lab.

Dr. Bennion's physics 105 class was a lot more fun than I thought it would be. The lectures were very entertaining and moved at a good pace. There were always plenty of practice problems and review material, so even though the tests were sometimes tricky, the questions never came as a surprise.

You can tell from his lectures that Professor Bennion has a deep love for physics, however he's not very clear as a teacher and then he's not the one writing the homework and exam problems and you can tell that it's harder when you get to the exams. I love Dr Bennion!! He is an amazing teacher and makes the class so enjoyable. We had two attempts at each test and really cares that his students understand the material.
he is great

Dr. Bennion is a nice person but I wouldn't take physics from him. His 10 minute devotionals at the start of class were nice; however, he never seemed to finish lectures. Not my favorite subject but Dr. Bennion made it one of my favorite classes! It's just really hard no matter who's teaching it. Class was SUPER fun and he is so incredibly passionate about physics! It was hard to grasp harder concepts but the other professor posts videos for clarification. Tests were not bad if you did the practice tests beforehand!

He would be a very good middle school physics professor, but not at the college level. He's nice but his lectures are long and don't cover the hard concepts well enough.
