This class is just a hard one. For Bennion's first semester, he picked up the ropes pretty quickly. Francis has just been at it for a longer time, but I still was able to get an A. Take it from Dr Francis his class is not set up well

Don't listen to all of the negative reviews...no matter who you take physics from it is a hard class. Physics is hard no matter who you take it from, but Dr. Bennion is awesome. His PhD was focused on teaching itself, so don't listen to the bad reviews. He's an awesome instructor for a hard class like physics and is very easy to meet with after class.

Once you get used to using the physics software it's pretty easy. An 85 is an A- and a 90 is an A. He makes physics religious in interesting ways, which was nice. The class was not that bad. Make sure to study the lectures slides and understand each concept in the exam preparation. You will ready for tests if you do well on the sample exams. Professor Bennion was super nice and energetic but this was his first time teaching this class, if you are going to take physics take Gregory Francis, he writes all of the tests and teaches it better. I had a very bad overall experience in this class. Ridiculous amount of homework. easily one of the best professors I've had at BYU.

- 5 super easy short essays with enjoyable topics you get to choose from a list. Not super time consuming

I loved his lectures! He does have 5 two paragraph papers due throughout the semester and he has a kahoot quiz before every class. I would highly recommend Professor Brown.  He is extremely organized, and although there are some readings, they are SO easy to find. He is very understanding and does not grade too harshly. Honestly one of the worst classes I've ever taken. Professor has a ridiculous amount of political bias and obviously just trying to push an agenda. Beware of that if you take this class, it makes the lectures difficult to sit through.
There is a lot of reading for the class but if you make time to even skim, you will be ok. Pay attention for study guide terms during lectures because while the slides are posted, the verbiage isn't.

Professor Brown was a really good teacher. He tried his best to help out the students, like by including "mercy rules" and things into his grading system to raise grades. I had basic government knowledge from a class I took in HS and I was intimidated to take this class. Stay caught up on the readings and you'll do fine.

He was clear on expectations, class structure, and taught so well. Gave great lectures and explained complex ideas clearly. The class wasn't hard but was still challenging enough to keep me engaged. Professor Brown was great! His class was clear and his criteria was understandable. He is a nice grader and cares deeply about each student. He's super funny and kind.

Professor Brown was amazing. I've always hated history, but I genuinely enjoyed his class. There are quite a few readings, but they are made up for by not having too many homework assignments. As long as you follow the study guide while doing the readings and watching the lectures, the exams aren't that bad.

Could not recommend this class more. Brown is incredibly thoughtful and wants every student to learn. Phenomenal lectures. Only 5 assignments (mini essays, 500 words, easy) for the whole semester. 3 tests. Lectures are packed with info, so pay attention and go to class - the powerpoints WILL NOT CUT IT FOR TEST, you NEED to take notes during lecture. TA's rocked. Test's aren't bad if you take good notes and study. Quizzes you can get by not doing the MANY readings.

Class was brutal but Professor Brown was very helpful. He always took questions and explained concepts in great detail. Class had SO much reading though with tough content. Papers were easy and manageable.

Great guy and professor, really wants to help students learn more about the constitution and politics. Does not help prepare you for tests and the final alone can be worth 34% of your grade so it was really tough.

Professor Brown kept the lectures very interesting but I found there to be way too many readings. I also really struggled on the midterms and final because of the confusing wording. I had a hard time figuring out how to study for these exams as well.

Professor Brown himself is great, but the class is so hard for a 100 level course. Expect to put in a lot of hours every week in order to get a good grade. I did think his lectures were interesting, and I enjoyed the material, but it was just an incredibly hard class with too much reading.

Great class. As long as you do the reading and put effort in this class you will do good. Make sure to look at the review guides as you prepare for the tests. The professor does a great job at teaching and cares for his students. The professor wants everyone to succeed and gives chances to do so.

Mandatory attendance, way too much reading for a 100 level class, and confusing wording on questions where he'd even write questions that were incorrect. Overall if it's your only option to take from him it's not bad but it's way too much reading and work, and confusing wording on tests.
this professor is very good and the lectures are interesting, but you have to remember a lot of material for the tests. the readings are also crucial in order to do good on the test.
Love this class! Its not easy, but you will do well if you go to class and stay on top of things. He is funny and good at teaching!
Professor Brown is a great teacher! His lectures were super engaging, and the tests and other assignments weren't too hard. This class was very informative and interesting!
he is so good!! truly passionate about what he teaches and he makes lectures fun and engaging. the tests are sometimes confusing but the class is really good

Professor Brown is an awesome teacher, even though I got a C in the class. He provided so many chances to get good grades in his class, However the class relies a lot on how well you do the test. The test are all multiple choice but they are very difficult because the questions are worded hard.

Very good professor, highly recommend. Very informative classes with solid explanations of concepts. Explicitly states what you need to do to get an A. Only gripe is that the there is a bit too much reading assigned creating a pretty big workload and he also uses his own website instead of Learning Suite and his website is a bit wonky.

Honestly, this class was so invigorating. I am a business student, but learned so much about the United States and how it operates. I really liked his teaching style. If you don't do the readings, you will be lost. Make sure to fill out the study guide in class during lectures so you know how to do well. Take it if you like reading

This class is so hard! I think Professor Brown tries to make it doable, but there is just a lot of information, a lot of reading, and really hard tests. He does try to help and provides lots of office hours, so if you want to get a good grade, expect to be with the TA's often.

Interesting Class but pretty difficult. Really hard to pay attention during lectures and tests are based heavily off of long boring lectures. extremely informative, lots of info in lectures, but presents it in an engaging way. gives all opportunities for students to succeed on tests. very helpful

Honestly this class sucked and he expected to work/study outside of class way too much
Tough class, requires a lot of reading and outside studying with the TA's.
Professor Brown's lectures were engaging and he provided a fair grading system. The workload is heavy, but manageable with good time management. Unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for exam prep.

Professor Brown is a great teacher, and a good person, but the class itself is really hard. It has so much reading and the tests are really difficult. he's pretty good tbh, but lemme just say I can never hear him idk if this is just a me problem but he speaks SO fast and at the end of every sentence he goes down an octave and talks so low and soft and fast that I literally miss half of what he's saying LOL

I took this class because I am a senior and I wanted the easiest class but dude I LOVED this class. I believe that he is a good man who tries. Be careful- he is rather liberal and not really afraid to hide opinions though he wouldn't disclose his political party.

Professor Brown was incredible. His knowledge was very impressive and his lectures were very straight forward. I loved how organized and transparent he was about grading and assignments. I enjoyed his class a lot. There is a lot of information which makes the class difficult however it is manageable with good time management and attentiveness.

This was one of my favorite classes! Dr. Brown is kind, personable and keeps lectures interesting. There is quite a bit of reading that isn't required but I really recommend as prep for exams. There are 6 short papers (2 pages) but the prompt is clear and they don't take too long. Exams can be tricky but he is very fair in his grading and curving

My favorite professor from this past semester but my least favorite class. Way too much reading for an American Heritage replacement class. However, it did jumpstart my interest in a Political Science Minor. If you feel like you can spend the majority of your time on this class over your degree classes, this is the class for you.

I never did the readings, just attended the lectures and took good notes. I studied for the exams maybe 1 hour each and did fine. It's not a hard class if you put and ounce of effort in. I came in knowing nothing about politics and feel like I have a good grasp on it now. The lectures were fascinating and he kept everything modern and relevant.
This class was very hard but he dropped a lot of quizzes and curved the grade. I did about 12 hours of homework a week for this class.

He is knowledgeable, and he drops quite a bit. However, it really comes down to how good you are at taking tests. I had one bad test, which brought my grade down a ton, even though I studied. The biggest issue I had with his class were the negative comments he made about a certain candidate and a certain party (both in lectures and the book).

The class lasts an hour and 15 minutes, but I never fell asleep once, he is a very interesting lecturer, and gives you the tools to apply what you are learning in order to be a more educated citizen. He has in class quizzes, and about 5 one-page writing assignments, and a few tests, if you pay attention you'll do fine for all of them.

I didn't put a ton of effort into this class. Professor Brown was awesome and I really enjoyed his lectures. There is a Zoom option and I started doing that at the end of the year which was good for my lazy self. He has in-class reading quizzes almost everyday, but he drops a ton and they aren't super hard. I didn't read a ton and did alright.

I loved this class and learned so much! Professor Brown gives organized and amazing lectures! There is a lot of reading but the lectures usually overlap with what we read. You have to write a couple 1.5 page papers but it's very doable. The tests are tricky and can be very specific so you have to really study.

My political science and government knowledge before taking this class was 0, so at first it was challenging. But there are so many TA/office hours and study guides for every exam. As long as you do the readings, attend lecture, and ask questions when you have them you'll be fine! I really grew to enjoy this class and its subject matter.

This class was very time intensive for a GE. You can definitely skim the readings but there sure are a lot of them. The tests are difficult but if you use the study guide and memorize all the terms then they should go well. He does really interesting lectures and they are all recorded which is super convenient for review.

I took this class as a GE credit and loved it. It's one of those classes I think everyone should take because it goes over tons about basic US politics we should all know. There is a lot of reading but you can get by skimming it. Tests are difficult but use the study guide as your holy grail and you should be fine.

I took this class for a Gen Ed and hoped to come out of it a more informed citizen and voter. THIS CLASS DELIVERED! Professor Brown is a great lecturer; he keeps everything relevant and interesting! Never fell asleep, and I always fall asleep in classes. Assignments and exams were very reasonable and helped me learn. In-class quizzes!

Professor Brown is a really engaging and caring professor. You can tell he cares about his students and wants them to do well. He's a great speaker and his lectures are funny and entertaining. He also drops a lot of quizzes and lowest scores. He's a fair grader and there's not a lot of homework at all.

Professor Brown is EXTREMELY intelligent and a great guy. He has a very commanding knowledge of the material, and usually does a good job explaining things in lectures. The class is very VERY reading heavy, but if you know what you are doing you can skim the readings for terms/main ideas and do just fine. Watch out for exams, they can be tough.
He's a pretty good dude. Topics were difficult but he explained things well. In-class quizzes every day, which are not fun but manageable. Lots of reading.

Great course and engaging lectures. There were 15 short quizzes using Kahoot (lol), but your worst 6 get dropped. Plus 5 one-page papers that are basically pass/fail. About 40-50 pages total readings per week, so a little high there (and dense). He announced that something like 80% of students were in the A to B range, so not impossible either.

Avoid this class. Horrible grading system and tests are absurd. 40+ pages of reading a day and the tests are brutal. You will do well in this class if you have a good background in Government. Such a bad choice to fulfill your GE. Interesting topics but he has a clear agenda he is pushing and suffers from false consensus bias.

Adam Brown is very intelligent. However, not everyone is and he forgets that. There is a quiz everyday. The only assignments are enrichment papers. If you do bad on the test there isn't much to help your grade. The tests are extremely difficult, study guides do not help. Listen to what he says because that's all that matters. Don't take this class.

This class is awful. He fails to remember that he is teaching it, and not everyone already knows it. The lectures are really long and boring. There is a significant amount of reading to do before each class, 20-50 pages. He gives a study guide, but it does nothing to prepare you for the test. They are quizzes each class.

Lectures are boring and you don't learn; he doesn't explain anything in detail. I've lost knowledge of the civic process and gotten more confused about topics relating to the political process. Test questions are formed in a way to confuse you. Don't walk, but run away from this class. Class isn't over yet but it's so bad I had to warn you guys.

The class was engaging and I really enjoyed the content but the tests were harder than the study guide prepared you for and were heavily weighted in the end grade. Professor Brown was extremely knowledgable and passionate about the content and was always willing to help which was nice.

Really loved his lectures. Tests are more difficult. You need to study and do readings, but there's a study site with all the textbook vocab on it which diminishes the reading you need to do out of that substantially. Harder than most GEs, but easier than American Heritage. Take notes off the study guide and you'll be fine.

Adam is a really fun professor. The tests are extremely difficult and the study guides didn't help a ton. Studying the Utah textbook will be the best benefit. Also, definitely do the extra credit. I pulled a B+ despite a really poor exam-1 grade. Study way hard for the first test so you can set yourself up for success.

This class wasn't easy but I never felt like it was too much to handle. Lots and lots of readings but very few homework assignments. Professor Brown himself is a super cool guy. He's serious but still cracks jokes and is clearly an informed and intelligent dude without shoving it in your face. Prepare to learn a lot about Utah state politics too.

Brown is an awesome lecturer. He's engaging, and you can tell he's really passionate about his field of study. His tests are hard though and I felt like they kinda came out of nowhere. In-class quizzes every day.

Professor Brown made political science interesting & entertaining. He assigned lots of readings that seemed impossible to get done, but if you skim the readings for vocab words and key concepts that are on the study guide, it doesn't take that long, and you should be prepared enough for the in class quizzes. Also, go to his weekly review sessions!

Professor Brown is awesome. He teaches in an interesting way that keeps everyone engaged, even if you don't find politics interesting. He grades fairly and has opportunities for extra credit. It is definitely not an easy A, but if you do the readings and study you should be fine.

By far the best Political Science class I have taken up to date. It's policy based rather than theory heavy and this opens up the class to tons of fun times. Field trip based and real-life applicable. Professor is amazing. He doesn't teach this often so if you see it do anything you can to take it. Loved the trips around the state.
Lectures are great. Textbook gets a bit dry, but the study website helps.
I never said it would be easy. I only said it would be worth it.

Really makes you think, and open to different opinions. Amazing introductory class, and if you follow the curriculum and just do the time for readings, lecture videos, etc. you'll be fine. The class covers a lot, but he explains concepts really clearly. Easy and fun to learn from.
Lectures were prerecorded because covid. Class was good but would be better with in-person discussion.

It was fully online because of the pandemic, but there were lots of office hours for help and a couple review sessions each week to keep current. Lectures were engaging. Textbooks were all available for free through the library.

Lectures were prerecorded due to the pandemic and class size, but they were much more engaging than other recorded courses I've had this year. I just wish we could have had the course in person to talk about it all. After all, it's politics, not accounting.

I loved this professor and the lectures. The quiz's were difficult and I felt like there was way too much to read before every class but he really did help me learn the material! He is also very good at helping students.

I really enjoyed this class and I took this for a GE. Prof Brown's lectures are really interesting. He does a good job at presenting the material and keeping it interesting even though it is an On-demand class. If you take really good notes and pay attention to the youtube lectures then you'll be set. The papers are short and tests are MC

The lectures are entertaining and the reading is free. There is quite a bit of reading but he gives terms and concepts to study as long as you understand them, you'll be ready for the quizzes. He also gives good feedback on papers and offers a lot of office hours. He also applies a lot of curves to the grades.

Professor Brown assigned way too much reading. I never ended up reading anything after the first few weeks and I did just fine. His lectures go over most of the material from the reading so the books were a little bit unnecessary. His lectures were good and his tests weren't all that hard.

I wanted to write a review due to my frustrations with this course. It is so obvious that this course has been made difficult purely to justify the expense of political science professionals. This material isn't that difficult, but the professor chooses test/quiz questions from obscure details in the text instead of valuable points. So pointless!

I love Professor Brown! He is super engaging and makes complicated workings of government interesting and easy to understand. There's like 25-35 pages of reading before each class but Prof Brown provides a reading guide and it overlaps a lot with lecture so it's really straightforward. Not too much work, and he has weekly Q&A sessions to help out.

This class is truly awful. If you take it from Brown, good luck with the 80+ pages of reading each week. He also makes you watch lecture clips which go well beyond the 1 and 15 minute allotment. If it were possible, I would impeach him. I guess he has taught me that.

I honestly can not believe this guy. He expects his students to read over 80 pages of text a week, while he himself puts forth no effort. All of the class recordings we are assigned to watch were recorded last year. Many of the points he makes are outdated. He expects a lot from his students, but is a lazy professor himself.

I have the more of the same to see. It is clear that this professor does not care about this class or his students. You are assigned approximately 100 pages of reading a week drawn from extremely boring text written by Brown. Brown must think his class is the most important class taught at BYU. It is not, especially when taught by him.

Professor Brown and POLI 110... Has an all inclusive website No need to buy a textbook Study guides that have every term that will be used on the tests Group reviews to ask any and all questions Heavy readings along with lectures. Dedicate 1-2 hours a day Test are multiple choice and easy if you've done the study guide Papers are 250-399 words

Professor Brown is a nice guy, however, his course is so unbelievably difficult. He assigns 30+ pages of reading a day on top of his hour and a half long lectures. He does not give any daily grades to give you a better opportunity to succeed. Your grade depends completely on quizzes, debate papers, and midterms. Highly recommend someone else.

I would not recommend this class. It is very clear the professor puts very little work into the course. He just expects you to spend 8+ hours a week outside of class reading the textbook to teach yourself everything. Take from someone else unless you want to read almost 100 pages of text a week.

Worst GE I have taken. This is the final GE class that I am required to take and I am really regretting taking it from Brown. There are 80+ pages of reading a week of boring text written by Brown. He expects students to spend about 9 hours a week on the readings. This is outrageous compared to every other GE I have taken. Take from someone else.

Dr. Brown really knows his stuff and adds humor to the class. Although he is entertaining, the class is hard and your final grade depends a lot on the papers and the exams. I was glad once I was done with this class! I would say it is better than American Heritage though. Glad I never had to suffer through that one...
The lectures were always super interesting and I learned a ton in this class. There is a LOT of reading assigned, but its totally worth it. One of the best generals that I've taken.

Great professor, difficult internship. He's very enthusiastic and somehow makes dry topics interesting. Maybe it's just the TAs I had, but the grading was INSANELY strict. He cares about his students and seems to be very invested in their success

LOTS of readings. Expect 20-40 pages every night. If you don't keep up, you'll drown. In addition, there are several essays you'll have to write that take a good chunk of time. There are low risk quizzes (he drops the worst half of them). A lot of the grade is the midterm/final and essays, all of which are fairly hard. Be prepared to work

My favorite class at BYU. His lectures are AMAZING, though he does make his political views very clear. I didn't always do the readings (4 question iClicker pop quizzes), but the concepts in the readings are covered very well in class. Papers aren't too bad, tests are hard-ish but fair (he did like a 3-5% curve). Gives fairly easy extra credit.
This guy is awesome. He is a very reasonable professor, which isn't always easy to find among GenEd profes.

Dr. Brown is awesome. My favorite thing about him is that he taught the material in a neutral light, meaning that he did not intermix his own ideas and ideologies into the material. If you'd like an objective view of government and politics, take his class. Awesome lectures. You'll pass the tests if you know the study guide.

Engaging lectures. Lots to learn, but he gives study guides before exams which help to make sure you haven't overlooked anything. (I'm kind of stumped by people complaining that exams were hard to prep for because there were no study guides??? Like maybe pay more attention?) It's a tough class but doable and worth the time.

This class is insanely hard. He talks so fast in lectures and gives no study guides which makes studying for tests virtually impossible without going to TA labs. This was one of the hardest classes I've taken just because I had no idea what to study or read. He gives reading assignments of like 40 pages at a time which is a lot.
Solid teacher for Poli 110. He knows his stuff. Amazing Powerpoints. He statistically analyses tests and drops bad questions. Also lets you know he cares about our well-being, and he really does.
I can't stand political science classes but this one wasn't that bad. I recommend seeing the TAs before every test and go over your debate papers with them too. He curves the class which saved me.

My favorite class taken so far at BYU, and I'm not a political science major by any stretch of the imagination. I took this class to fulfill a general, and it was extremely enriching. The content was logically organized, and I've come away from that class feeling like I learned a ton. Professor Brown is passionate, and his enthusiasm contagious.

Unless you are a political science major this class will probably be miserable for you. Professor Brown talks so fast you can barely hear what he is saying let alone take notes. His tests are ridiculously hard. He doesn't give study guides. He is condescending when answering questions. The class is so unnecessarily hard for a 100 level class.

Great dude, great and interesting lectures, and loads of out of class opportunities to meet with him or other TA's to discuss essays and upcoming tests. Sporadic iClicker quizzes on daily readings, and lots of extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Brown was hands down my favorite this past semester. His class was hard, but he made sure that if we put in the time, we could understand the material. He was funny, caring, and approachable. Although the tests and essays were hard, they always felt fair.

Professor Brown was great. The tests and papers were pretty hard, but if you can make sure you know the material you will be fine. His lectures were amazing, they made a subject I don't really care much about actually interesting. Daily quizzes in class and quite a bit of reading to keep up on.

Brown was a great professor, very funny and relatable. The only downside to the class was the butt ton of reading that applied to both tests and frequent iclicker quizzes, which you can bypass if you're devoted by going to an earlier section and just getting it from there (don't think that's necessarily legal). 3 tests, 3 papers, extra credit.

his class is terrible. He does not teach anything. all he does is put slides up read them off to you and the only assignments are 3 tests and 3 essays. the essays are easy but the tests are very long and very difficult. The worst professor I have had in all of college.

Okay I love this guy! Seriously one of the most caring professors I've ever had. Lectures are interesting and Prof. Brown absolutely knows what he's talking about. However, his tests are unreasonable in my opinion. I completely felt like I knew the material and scored in the 60s on the final. Hoping for a B!

Relates well with students since he is pretty young. Makes the subjects interesting even for someone who doesn't like politics or history. His website has answers to any possible question you might have about his class and is extremely detailed, so take advantage of that. Tests can be difficult, but study in groups and you should do well.

Prof Brown is one of the best! He is very clear about deadlines and assignments, provides a ton of office hours, and is very generous with extra credit. He assigns lots of textbook readings but you can get by if you skim. He's a good guy and a young dad, his lectures are super engaging even if you don't really care about political science. 10/10!!!

Super smart guy that is so respectful of anyone's political views and I have become more sensitive and caring as a result of this class. Incredibly interesting and fun to attend. Whether you care about politics or not, any person who cares about our country should take this class to understand how our government works. Tests aren't bad at all.

Here's the thing. I am not great at political science, but he is hands down the best professor to take the entry level from. You need to work, but an A isn't out of the question. GO TO CLASS and pay attention! that's the best advice I can give. Prof. Brown is excellent and intelligent and your best option. Take the class from him.

Professor brown gives amazing lectures that make Utah politics as interesting as it can get. Tests are long and detailed but if you're good at memorizing a B is definitely attainable. He is very passionate about what he teaches which makes even duller topics not too bad.

My favorite class this semester! Keeping up on the readings is a little hard because they can be boring. But I rarely had trouble paying attention in class, because it's actually really interesting! He's a great teacher. Advice: it's way less work to get to class on time to get iclicker credit than to have to make it up with extra credit

Trust me, the extra credit is worth it. Do yourself a favor and plan to do all of it. Professor Brown gives interesting and funny lectures. The concepts can be hard to understand, but luckily the exams aren't as brutal as they could be. There are reading quizzes in every class. Honestly, do the extra credit and it makes everything easier.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. I'll be real, his classes are hard and you really work for your grade, but there are so many resources and he works extremely hard to help us succeed. He is passionate about his work and although his tests are hard, you'll do just fine if you do the readings. Which there are a lot of. Hard, but worth it. TAKE HIS CLASSES!

Professor Brown doesn't let his biases get in the way of his teaching, which I think is very important for a class like this. He also is active in his field so he has a lot of current research that he brings into his lectures. Overall he was an awesome professor and I wish I could take a class by him again.

This class was great. There's a lot of reading, yes, but there's nothing that he assigns that isn't purposeful and ultimately educational. He's an excellent professor, I would definitely recommend him.

Professor Brown's politics of public land class has been my favorite class so far in the poli-sci major. Field trips to Arches and other places around Provo. It was a first-term class so class periods were long. 3 books assigned throughout the semester, tests are free-response only. He really makes you work for the A but you learn so much.

Professor Brown made this class fascinating. He is really funny and works hard to keep you engaged in class. He is very clear about what he expects, and him and the TAs are always willing to help out. Papers were expected to be short, and tests were straightforward. Put the work in, and you can get a good grade.
Listen: take this class from this man. It is worth it.
Great lectures. Exams and papers are difficult but TAs are a great help. I did a bonus assignment to help bring up my paper score.

Brown is a great teacher and definitely knows his stuff. However, this course is very difficult, especially if you're a first semester freshman & don't know what you're doing. Tests were above my comprehension- failed/low D's on them all. Did well on the papers, which helped. Daily iClicker quizzes and fair amount of extra credit opportunities.

NOT AN ENTRY LEVEL CLASS! Professor Brown is amazing, though. His lectures are so entertaining and you really learn a lot. But he assigns tons of reading and has short iclicker quizzes every class that are based off the reading, the previous lecture, and something in the current news. His tests are extremely long and hard.

This class was way harder than it needed to be. The professor gave heavy reading assignments every night. His grading system was tough, and his lectures felt longwinded. He knows a lot about the topic, and is humorous. He also is understanding. The tests are hard, and you can't miss class.

I really enjoyed POLI110 with Mr. Brown. His lectures are excellent and focused, and he generates great discussion with the class. There is the sizable amount of reading that comes with any poli class, but it's nothing too terrible, and a lot of it is skimable. He's a politics geek and is passionate about the material.

The tests are based evenly on the readings and the in class lectures. Take notes on the discussions and not just the slides because he tests them. I enjoyed this class more than others because he makes you get outside of your perspective and discover that political views are based upon values and nobody has faulty reasoning .

This was my absolute favorite class this semester. Professor Brown is amazing. The class took a solid amount of work, but it was nothing unmanageable. He makes a huge effort to apply the material to the real world and your individual life. Honestly this class was a life changer, would recommend to anyone and everyone.
Adam Brown is the best lecturer I've ever had. He's great at teaching, but his TA's are weak. Don't stress too much about reading, but be familiar with the reading and you'll do fine on the tests.

I would recommend not taking this class. Reading assignments are large--30-50 pages a day. The debate papers are difficult and graded by TAs. Grading criteria isn't clear; you can lose points for almost anything. No useful feedback is provided. Tests are monstrous--100 questions drawing evenly from readings and class. I wish I had taken AmHeritage.

Dr. Brown was easily my favorite professor! If you like passionate professors, then take his class. He's also very approachable.  His class is not easy by any means--expect to work hard for a good grade. There is lots of reading and the material in the reading will be on his midterms and final. He taught extremely interesting topics, as well.

Dr. Brown is great. Fantastic lecturer with a sense of humor but also really thought provoking. There were days I left lecture with my mind absolutely blown. Grade wise it's not an easy class - expect 30-40 pages of reading a week and your grade is based primarily on three tests and three TA graded papers (sometimes subjective).

I really enjoyed Prof. Brown's class!  He was engaging and class discussions were always interesting.  His tests are pretty long and hard, 100 question midterms, 140 question final and kind of hard to study for.  Take good notes, he bases a lot of the tests on lecture materials.  3 short debate papers.   Fairly easy iclicker quizzes.

I enjoyed that Professor Brown was young and more "relatable." He is pretty laid-back and tries to go about this course in such a way that it is a discussion. The things that got me, however, were just how much reading is assigned every week and how tough the tests were. (But there are extra credit opportunities for you to raise your grade.)

Go to class, not only are there iClicker quizzes almost everyday but he goes over so much material that you don't want to miss. It was a very interesting class and he keeps it light with jokes and such. Hard material but if you put a lot of studying and hard work you will be ok.

I took this class as a general and it was one of my favorite classes I have taken at BYU.  His lectures are interesting, and the class is well organized so that you know exactly what is expected from you the first day of class.  Just read the syllabus, go to class, and try to get the reading done, and you will be fine!

Dr. Brown is freakin' great, but his class was sooooo hard. His lectures are incredibly interesting and engaging. Be ready to read A LOT. The exams are really difficult and there are quizzes each class, so make sure you read EVERYTHING in the textbook. I loved this class, even though it nearly killed me.

Good term class. Prof. Brown is very knowledgeable. Read a lot the first couple of weeks, averaged about 70 pages between classes. The tests weren't too bad if you took good notes. His slides are online but they mostly just quotes and pictures without context. Took a field trip to Moab for the day.

Brown is super smart, gives fun lectures, young and energetic, helps a ton(slides, textbook website, office hours, TA , etc). There are 2 midterms (100 multiple choice questions each) and a cumulative final with 140 questions. There are a few one page papers. He is VERY organized, so you always know what to expect. Really great class! Choose Brown!
I took Poli 110 spring term instead of fall or winter, which was a great idea. It moved FAST, but it was nice having only 40 students instead of a couple hundred. Great course.

Lectures are engaging, I learned a lot. Tests are very hard, but doing practice quizzes on the textbook website and going to TA reviews helps a ton. And don't miss class or you'll fall way behind. There aren't many assignments besides exams, just three short papers and two optional ones for bonus credit.

This class is tough. The trick to do well on the tests is to do the online textbook practice tests and go to the TA reviews weekly. To do well on the debate papers, ask a TA to go over it with you as you write it. To do well on the daily in-class quizzes, give yourself an hour or so immediately before each class period to do the extensive readings.

First and foremost, he is SO hot. It's hard not to pay attention because of that... He is super clear about things and explains them well. His tests are crazy hard, but if you use the textbook website's practice questions, they're like the same thing as the tests. He curves a lot too which is great!

Fantastic class! It was difficult, but so are all poli sci classes. It really helps if you've had APUSH. Tests are hard, but if you use the book's quizzing site it is easy, lots of questions are pulled straight from there. Make sure you pass your debate papers through a couple of people, theyre pretty difficult. Lots of reading!

I loved this class! Lectures were interesting and easy to follow. I highly recommend using the book website for studying the book terms. Plus a lot of the questions from the quizzes on the website are on the midterms and final. Attendance is mandatory, but as long as you work hard you'll get an A.

Professor Brown made PoliSci 110 WAY harder than it needed to be. I'm a biology major who took this class as a general requirement, and it is extremely difficult. Despite feeling like I really put in A effort (12+ hrs/week), I ended up with a B in the class. He's funny, but doesn't care about his students individually, and is not flexible at all.

WARNING TO ALL FRESHMAN: This is hardly an intro class, im talking an average of 40 pages of textbook reading before class everytime. exams are brutal! you better be prepared to take notes like crazy too. if you like the challenge go for it. i learned alot but this guy turned me off to political science. this is not high school government class.

WAY TOO MUCH WORK for a 110 class.  I would recommend not taking this class.  He is a nice guy, and knows his stuff.  However he does not teach clearly or make the test questions clear either.  You do as much work as you would for an honors class.  I would defiantly NOT take this class if I could register again.

Knows his subject matter extremely well but doesn't teach 110 effectively- class is much harder than it should be for its level. VERY vague study instructions for challenging exams, quizzes every day, about 15 1 pg writing assignments, LOTS of reading. It's a doable course if you're willing to work with that, and is highly informative.
Great teacher. Class was hard and he made you work but if you study you can get a high grade. Keep up with current events and definitely do all the assigned readings.

Loved the class, but it was hard. Barely passed with a B-. His lectures were awesome, but he made you work. TONS of reading every day-from the book and news-quizzes every class, 2 page papers due friday, 120 question+ exams.. It was HARD. If you take it from him, use the ONLINE BOOK QUIZZES - he uses the same test questions on his exams.

Entered this class with little to no knowledge of politics, knowing it was an "Introduction" class and got blindsided by TONS of reading and hard to follow lectures due to my lack of political knowledge. I'm sure he's great if you are into politics and like studying it, but from someone who was taking this as a general this class was rough.

Professor Brown is a great teacher! I thoroughly enjoyed going to class because he knows how to appeal to his audience. There are a lot of reading and quizzes every class, but it isn't that bad. Definitely take anything from Professor Brown - he is great. He also changes his syllabus throughout the semester to fit our needs.

Professor Brown was awesome! He was extremely enthusiastic about his subject and excelled at explaining difficult concepts.  I did not find this class overly hard...just skim the readings and you should do fine.

Yeah there is alot of reading that goes into it, but if you do it the class isn't too bad. Lectures are well structured and interesting. A guest lecturer came in and I fell asleep but I never did when Brown was teaching. Great  teacher, hard class but it will be hard from whoever your taking it from. Take it from Brown.

I honestly highly enjoyed this class. It was interesting, and Brown was very passionate about politics. There is a lot of reading, but skimming it while keeping possible quiz questions he might ask in mind is easy. USE THE ONLINE BOOK QUIZZES (website on back of textbook)-- it's SO helpful on tests. I got an easy A in this class.

Came in expecting this class to be easy with minimum work, but is anything but.  I have to work my butt off for this class, but I'm still managing to get an A.  Definitely go to class, it's always well explained and I find it really interesting.  The only thing I dislike about this class is the amount of reading required daily.
He is great to learn from in class but his tests are extremely hard!

holy crap do not take this class, impossible.  all the other comments are for his harder class.  this is his first time teachings 110.  this isn't freshmen level.  exams are impossible, he talks a million miles an hour and there's hours of reading every night. i have A's in almost all of my classes except this one is a D.

1st time teaching PLSCI 110. Expectations were WAY too high. This should have been a 4 credit class. Read at least 1-2 chapters a night, plus other assigned articles, iClicker quizzes every class, 2 page paper due every Friday, 3 Exams all had 120 questions on them. Pl Sci interests me but this class was BORING. Recommend taking from someone else.

great and enthusiastic professor. His expectations were a bit overwhelming for me though. I thought some of the key words taught in class were vague-- ie. you could not find concepts in the book or they weren't clearly stated in lecture slides. On the flipside, he is always clear that he is willing to help via office hours and email

Like an earlier commenter said, great professor but he'll make you work. But you'll do fine if you just ask for help. Stop by whenever, even if it's not office hours. I visited him for an hour before each exam asking questions. It's a tough class if you don't ask for help, but he was happy to help me understand things.
A great class. Not easy, but I learned a ton and it was interesting. Brown is good at making complicated material clear. I liked going to the city council meetings.

Best professor ever. The class is well-organized with clear deadlines and such. Each lecture is clear--Brown starts by showing us an outline for the day, then ends by reviewing specific terms we should understand and going over a list of review questions. Lectures are engaging and fun. No complaints; strongly recommended.

Professor Brown may be a new professor, but he is a good one. He kept lectures interesting and he is still connected with students. Take this class if you like politics because Brown will not disappoint.

Great teacher.  I have taken a few classes from him and would recommend him to anyone studying political science.  Knows his state politics (especially gubernatorial elections and powers)and I found class very interesting.  If you do take him, GO TO CLASS EVERYDAY!  His tests revolve heavily around class lectures.
Good teacher but will make you work and read.  So much reading...

This was a very easy class. I got an A- with no effort at all. For a good grade all you have to do is attend EVERY class, take meticulous notes, and cram for about four hours with your notes before each exam. Don't bother with the readings. The only other part of your grade is a fun application paper. Brown is very structured in teaching the class.

I loved Brown's campaign class. He is an engaging teacher, loves politics, and it was clear he really wanted us to learn. His tests were absolutely doable, but you have to pay attention to the "key terms" and "lecture questions." Do that and you'll be fine. He even gives you the essay questions for the test ahead of time!

Decent professor, but worst test writer in the world.  He prides himself on not giving the least shred of help to study for his tests so you have no focus to concentrate on even though you've covered tons of information.  Avoid him if you want a grade that reflects your learning.
Great guy, I am glad BYU picked up someone different than the usual.  He is intelligent and requires you to study.  Good personality and would take all classes from him if possible.

A young professor who will probably improve over time.  Reading was pretty useless, since his lectures were based entirely on what we were supposed to have read.  Tests were overly difficult & study guides were pretty useless; he asked broad questions & looked for minute details.  A little arrogant, but that could change over time.
Adam is the best! He helped me physically, mentally, and spiritually! He is very uplifting and deeply cares about what he does. I definitely recommend him!
Adam Dyer is an easy grader. If you show up you get an A. He always has devotionals at the beginning of class and tries to inspire his students.

He acts like he cares, but it is just a front. When I emailed him for more feedback on my work he got at me, because "I should be coming early or staying after class like other students who have concerns". When I told him that I work before class and have other classes directly after he never responded back. Terrible teacher, ditto grade drop.

I would 0/10 recommend Adam. He will say to listen to your body, but then he will push everyone to "do 110% today!" every single day and if you aren't feeling well or are being gentle with what might become an injury he will call you out for not doing the most and make you do it in front of the class. He also dropped everyone's grade in submission

At first Adam seems great, but if given the choice I would not take his classes again. He is not clear about his grading criteria and does not bring up concerns in meetings, which leads to the assumption that all is going fine in class. All the classes I took from him my grade dropped a whole letter grade than what was reflected on learningsuite.

Adam is great and very personable. Do not believe these other reviews. As a student who has had him for multiple classes - Conditioning, Contemporary 440/341, Aerial Class. If you make sure to participate and show up every day you will get a good grade. If you are struggling you can go up to him to talk about your situation and he is the best!

Take it from someone else if you can. Adam seems encouraging and compliments you a ton but does not reflect that when he submits your final grade. I also do not think this class helped with injury prevention at all. Also, my grade dropped from what it showed on learningsuite when the grades showed on my progress record.
Professor Dynes is great and shows care for the betterment of the student body

Despite what other ratings might say, I thought professor Dynes was an excellent teacher. There's homework for class (super normal) and if you do the readings before class, you're honestly set. The tests are hard, but not impossible. Take the class if you want a non-partisan politics teacher.

Prof. Dynes was hard to take a class from. He was very disorganized and didn't know what the tests would cover until a couple of days before, which made studying difficult. A lot of the TAs didn't know what was going on either. He curved the grades a lot, though, because many in the class struggled. Felt hard for a 100-level class.

The course felt disorganized. Lecture notes did not always match what was on the exams, which were taken in the testing center and were difficult. Weekly homework was completed on an external website and was a consistent requirement. Expectations between notes and exams felt unclear. Attendance was also mandatory. Take a different professor.

His lectures were super hard to understand, he was very scatter brained when he explained things. I think the average grade on the final was a 60%, so his tests were super hard and we were not prepped at all for them. I think he took a little pride in the fact that it was hard to get a good grade in there. Super nice guy, and the TA's were great.
A class to take if you lowkey dont care

Dynes was honestly not a great lecturer in the sense that he is super unorganized and doesn't really have concrete lessons. He goes over time a lot and has to pick it up the next day. He's a tough grader, and he doesn't offer really any extra credit. I recommend doing all the reading and taking thorough notes in lectures, especially for the final.

Prof. Dynes is great. He's pretty funny and is pretty good at keeping the classes interesting. Make sure to go to the lectures and take notes, because all the exams are based on what we do in class, and not on the readings. Overall, really fun class

If you aren't a good student who goes to class even when optional, don't take this class. Dr. Dynes is quirky but fun to learn from. Content is applicable to the world & gospel, helpful for life. Tests are tricky but provides class outlines that simplify studying. Class can get boring, but he knows what he's talking about. Go to TA reviews & study!
This class is just messy, you really aren't explained things in detail.

Professor Dynes is tough. Does not know how to teach material to his students. His teaching style was ineffective, as reflected in the test scores of almost all the students in our class. Don't take this class with him unless you are ready to put in the work outside of the class. A lot of people would ask him questions and he could not answer them

Professor Dynes is a great professor! He gives interesting lectures and is very hands on in helping his students. He makes expectations clear and the workload is manageable if you stay on top of it. Tests can be difficult BUT if you study and go to your reviews you'll be good.

Professor Dynes was very caring and supportive of all the students. There is a lot of reading required for this course, but Professor Dynes does a great job of preparing for the exams. On our research projects he gives great feedback to help improve your question and writing style, with ample opportunities to improve before the final submission.

Professor Dynes truly cares about his job and you can clearly see it. The class I had with him was around 25 people so it was very one-on-one. You will read A LOT in this class and his tests aren't that easy, so you will need to go to the review sessions if you can. He's very accessible outside class. Highly suggest you take the class! Worth it.

Prof. Dynes rocks. Definitely will throw out the lesson plan to meet the needs/questions of the class. I saw some reviews from 2018 that said otherwise; I promise he's great. Super funny, gives good feedback, receives feedback from students well. Interesting class content, too. The class isn't easy, but it's manageable. Lots of reading.

Professor Dynes is one of the nicest professors one can ever meet! While this was UNIV101, the class structure is different than his political science classes. UNIV was very easy - you just needed to write discussions on the readings, participate in class, and do the assignments (activities and reflections).

He is very passionate about politics and American history. He is great at applying and explaining concepts from class to real-world issues. He genuinely cares if we succeed. He is very understanding and open to meeting with us. He's also super funny.

The class material was interesting and Professor Dynes knows a lot about this topic. He was also personally kind and very open to questions and class participation. However, I never felt like I knew how to meet the criteria for writing assignments. His standard for an "A" is much higher than in many classes. Do not take if you value your GPA.

Really a pretty good lecturer, has a lot of knowledge on the subject he teaches, tries to get the class engaged. If you're engaged and study for the exams the class will be easy, but a very large majority of your grade is based on the exams. He does curve them slightly but he will not round up your grade.

His lectures are hard to understand sometimes. He doesn't follow the slides and just rants so it's hard to learn anything. Pay attention though because you will be using the class concepts with your essays. Tests are also harshly graded.

While I found Dynes' lectures very interesting, I didn't feel like they prepared me for the test very well. It was hard to know what to study/ the context in which it'd be brought up on the test. Essays were graded very hard. Sometime's he'd post quizzes and not tell anyone without the ability to retake. Not great, not horrible.

Dynes is a horrible professor. I get that POLI 110 is supposed to be a difficult course, but he makes it impossible. He is never clear about the material. The final is 40% of your grade and it could include any detail from his lengthy and unproductive lectures. Uses 150+ slides a day, so it's not realistic to review the material. Take anybody else.

Took months for grade stuff, added quizzes to the schedule 2 days before they were due. Tons of assignments but were worth nothing compared to the tests. Was impossible to study since there was so many slides. Also submitted grades 2 days late, like c'mon dude you have a Phd from Yale you should be able to figure out how to score a bubble sheet.

Genuinely cannot think of a worse teacher. Prides himself in how hard his class is but his lectures and materials make no sense. This semester he posted grades very late and made plenty of excuses as to why. Just irresponsible and childish. The worst class I have ever taken at BYU
Genuinely cann

I know he tries to be a good prof but he's not executing it right. Spring sem has already started and 50% of our points are not graded yet. Also, the final was 40% of our grade & the midterm 25%, I could fail this class bc of the final & midterm, even when I have gotten 100s on everything else. It's an intro class, it should not be this difficult!!

He wouldn't tell us about reading quizzes before they closed so that's why I got a bad grade BUT overall I really liked this class. He tied everything to the gospel which is important for something like politics. It is a harder class but I'd take this over American Heritage any day. It's just good knowledge to have as a voter.

I really did not like this class. I don't think he explains things well at all and makes everything more difficult than it needs to be. Instead of explaining what a concept is, he will just give an example of the concept. The 2 exams make up 65% of the grade. He also talks about how hard his class is all the time. This is a GE dude, chill out.

He brags about how difficult his class is which really I think is just an indication that he's a bad teacher. If no one can do well in a prof's class, they probably can't teach. 2 exams worth 65% of the grade. He does not lay out content clearly. I know he has good intentions, but this was probably the most difficult GE for absolutely no reason.

Very disappointed with this class and teacher. Far too difficult to be a level 100 class. I feel like he needs to boost his ego by making this class hard. Lectures were 150-200 slides and tests were very difficult to understand and prepare for. Definitely do not recommend.

Honestly, I think BYU just makes its GEs too difficult overall. This class and prof are no exception. Lectures: long and boring, exams and essays too harshly graded to be a 100 level class. These general classes should be to give a broad overview and exposure to a subject, not drop your GPA for something you don't even care about. Don't recommend.

Professor Dynes is honestly the GOAT! I would take his class even if it wasn't required for one of my GE's. The tests were straightforward if you've been coming to class. The lectures weren't long, and it was nice to have all the slides to go back to after class to review. Don't be afraid of other ratings, take the class! The curve helps! A = 91%

I loved Professor Dynes!! He makes himself super accessible and it is very easy to get an A in his class. He teaches the material in an exciting manner, and I looked forward to his class. I do have to admit that while he was willing to go over essays before and after you submitted them, he did not give the best feedback on them.

I would not recommend this class. It was far too difficult for a GE. Lectures were boring and slideshows were usually between 150-200 slides. No feedback is given on the essays. Tests were very subjective and questions were unclear. The grading curve dropped my grade right at the end of the semester. Do yourself a favor and avoid this class.

Professor Dynes is an awesome human! That being said, I would absolutely not reccomend this class. The lectures dragged and were full of so much information that it was overhwelming (he has a powerpoint with 120+ slides for every 50 minute class). He also curves his grades so only the top 25% of the class gets an A or A-

I genuinely really enjoyed Prof. Dynes' class and don't know why his rating is in the 3's. I thought he did a great job with POLI 110 and I learned a lot from him. His TA's are very accessible outside of class and the tests weren't too bad. I'd take from him again for sure!

Hes super awesome, its a great class but you cant just get by doing the minimum. He really cares for his students and connects what he teaches to the gospel. He is super chill and understanding. He makes class interesting.
Don't take this Professor.

Prof Dynes is an incredible human. Very empathetic, and willing to be flexible with your deadlines. The lectures were boring, as he would go over basic things like how to write an essay for half of the class. There are little nuggets of joy with social theory, but most of it is anecdotal and opinion. Felt like a lame high school class.

This class gets hard, mainly with the essays and tests. There is a lot of readings. I kind of felt like he treated us like little kids sometimes, but you can tell he cares and puts a lot of work into his teaching. You can do good if you make use of all your resources (TA's, review slides, etc.)

Great guy, super smart and engaging. Essays graded too harsh by TAs for a GE, I usually get 100s and was struggling to get 93s on them. Need to study a lot for difficult application exams, even opennote they r hard! But they r curved. Weekly readings and inquizitive, 3 exams, 3 essays but he made last one optional, some ex cred available, work forA

I was so nervous to take this class, but I am so grateful I took it from Professor Dynes! He is so kind! Essays were tough at the beginning, but talking to the TAs helped me so much. Instead of feeling like I had to memorize everything, I actually learned the content because of how Professor Dynes builds upon concepts from the very beginning.

I dont recommend this class!! If you can avoid it, you should. It is supposed to be a low level GE, but it will feels like a challenging major class. The papers are horribly graded and confusing. The tests are about his opinions and hard to study for. Didnt learn very much. Not an easy A at all.
Good lectures, a billion TA's but papers and tests take weeks to grade. Feedback was frustrating and not clear. Its hard to get an A.

Professor Dynes is funny and gives good lectures. Theres a lot of reading, but all of the important stuff (on the test) is talked about in his lectures. If you pay attention and take notes, its not hard. The test were online and open note and open internet, but they definitely test your understanding of concepts rather than memorizing stuff.

Prof Dynes really is an awesome guy. Ended up being one of my favorite classes this semester, despite dreading it at the beginning. Makes learning about politics interesting and applicable. He and his TAs are willing to help you with any assignment or topic you don't understand, which was really helpful. Super nice guy, definitely take this class

Prof. Dynes was extremely attentive to his students and clearly cares about how they're doing (made last paper optional). The class is pretty easy (you don't need to read the textbook). Downside is that he tries so hard to make sure questions on his exams have 0 loose ends that it makes the questions convoluted and difficult to understand.

This class was very challenging for me. His rubric for grading essays is extremely specific and the tests were open everything, but he made the questions a bit more challenging because of this. Two midterms and one final, making tests worth 60% of your grade. He did teach very well though.

Professor Dynes is a fine professor. There is a lot of reading for a 100 level class, but I didn't have time to do any of it and still passed haha. He leans liberal on some issues, my parents said he was feeding me the liberal agenda. His lectures are good for freshmen but repetitive if you're actually paying attention. Tests were open everything.

There are three papers and three tests. The essays were graded harshly and the tests were hard! Dynes also lacked respect for his students and we had some very awkward class times due to it. Try a different teacher unless you are a great writer and test taker! It was all pretty ambiguous.

Class isn't hard just kinda boring. Takes notes in class and you'll be just fine though honestly I barely paid attention and still did pretty good. The grading criteria for the papers is kinda vague and I would recommend getting them checked over by the TAs not the writing center. Wasn't sure where I went wrong on what were A essays to me.

Prof Dynes is pretty good. He assigns a good amount of reading, but you can get by fine by skimming. At least for us, he had open note tests, which was very nice. If you study you will do fine grade wise. Some lectures are a bit dry, but I thought some were interesting. I also feel like he does a good job at staying politically neutral.

Prof. Dynes literally talked about the same 5 concepts for the entire semester. I skipped class like five times & still got 96+ on all the tests. Info from the textbook is never on the tests, so reading is really optional. Lectures were generally boring and repetitive. Easy A/GE credit, but you don't learn much. He is a genuinely nice dude though.
This course was Lecture heavy. He cares, and it a good professor. I would 100% take this course from him again. When I took the course the exams were open internet, so that is also a plus.

I am a straight A student and this class is the first time Ive gotten a grade below an A. The grading is subjective and the TAs grade without providing any feedback. Professor Dynes sets up his class in a way where its difficult to get the grade you want.
If you go to class and take notes, you'll pass the class.

I have loved this class. I took it completely online due to COVID-19 restrictions and I watched most of his lectures after the fact, but I learned so much! He made concepts I had never found interesting seem relevant and really interesting. I learned so much from this class!

Prof Dynes was an amazing professor and I would recommend taking a class with him to anyone. He genuinely cares about his students (i.e. cancelled our last essay bc he got a sense that students were too stressed). He does a great job relating to students and teaches in a very beginner-friendly way.

This class started out hard, got easier as it went along. 3 essays to write, 3 tests, and about 15-20 quizzes throughout (on inquisitive which makes them easy and informative). He's unique and funny (sometimes scattered) which make for an engaging class. Takes awhile for grades to be put in, but overall an interesting class with a great instructor.

This class has a million TAs but it takes forever for assignments to be graded. The tests are very difficult and the reviews aren't recorded. High expectations for a GE class. Lectures are very very long and boring. Not a lot of talk about current events. Could have been much better and had a lot of potential but just fell flat b/c of COVID maybe??

Not to fault Prof Dynes, but this class was painful to get thru. Very long lectures covering boring material. Very hard to make it thru a full lecture while actually paying attention. GO TO THE TA EXAM Q&A SESSIONS. If you go to those and take good notes, you should pass no problem. Open notes, open internet tests which was also helpful.

Prof. Dynes is a great teacher and I really enjoyed taking his Poli110 class. The class is very lecture heavy and the only assignments you'll have is 3 essays and a lot of textbook readings w/reading quizzes. By attending class, taking good notes, and with some studying, then you'll get a desirable grade. He wants you to pass the class.

Tests are difficult even if you study. TAs grade essays and don't do a good job. He is not clear on how assignments are graded. It feels like a poi sci major class and not a GE class. Lectures are very very boring. Quizzes are super easy. Readings are interesting. Had a lot of potential to be great but overall not a fun or easy class
just dont take this class cuz you will regret it.

If you write papers as you did back in middle school, you'll get good grades on the essay. What is meant by this is that if you write the thesis like you were taught in WRTG150, you will get a bad score.

Some political science concepts can be difficult to understand, but Professor Dynes does a great job at breaking them down and explaining them. He genuinely cares about his students' success and gives great feedback. His exams are more about understanding and applying concepts than memorizing random facts and I really loved that about his class.

Professor Dynes was a really good professor. He cares about his students and is very accessible. His lectures are interesting and easy to follow along with even if you don't know much about politics. He is very knowledgable and is willing to answer any questions.

Professor Dynes has been one of my favorite professors at BYU. He is empathetic, engaging, and finds unique ways to apply complex topics to everyday scenarios, making the content of the class accessible and enjoyable. He is simply a good person. The reading and lectures are imperative to succeeding in the course, but dont let that dissuade you!

*disclaimer:class taken online during covid* Clear and simple format to lectures, easy reading and simple writing assignments, tests are fair. I think most people who struggle are freshman who havent taken a college level course, but he is really understanding and willing to help. Really applicable to real life, changed the way i see politics.

He is the most caring professor I have. I at first didn't like him because he seemed a bit scattered, but he honestly cares about you and your progress. He is super knowledgeable and is easy to work with. You just have to be patient with him. He treats the class like you are sacrificing your time to be there, instead of him sacrificing his time.

Lectures are boring and it is a waste of time to take this class. Very boring and he teaches us concepts that are beyond introductory course levels. Do not take this class if you want to save your GPA.

Impossible to get good grades with how he has his TAs grade our work. He does not make clear how papers are graded. I also never understood the logic behind TAs grading student essays cuz they are not even an expert in the field yet.

Although it is just a GE course, he teaches us like we are all political sci majors. So I really had no idea what he is talking about. Extremely boring lectures. Not worth it even if you're just taking for credit. Terrible overall. Do not take his class. You will regret taking his class. Probably the worst class.

Tons of readings that were only useful half of the time. The lectures didn't include that much participation from the students and he had a tendency to trail off on tangents and lull you to sleep with his voice. He is a great guy and if you're somewhat engaged as a student you'll pass. But not as enjoyable as it could have been.
Very nuetral and does a nice job of presenting both sides of the subject so you can make your own decisions.

He is so nice! He was so willing to work with me through different challenges and was understanding with my situation. But that does not take away from the fact that his class was SO hard. It did not feel like level 100 class. It is so hard to do well on papers and tests. He curves final grades like crazy but thats because no one does well.

Professor Dynes is clearly good at his work. But if you don't do the readings for class (30 pages per night), or even if you do, get ready to struggle. His 100-level course felt more like a 300. Essay grading is unclear and the tests are ridiculously hard. I left class feeling more confused and discouraged than anything.

I HATE learning about politics, but Dr. Dynes made this class bearable. Was it hard? Yes. Did I want to give up? H%&* yes. That said Dr. Dynes was very understanding with our class and really threw us a bone, I mean I failed an exam (58%) and still got an A- in the class. He did a great job teaching really abstract concepts to our novice class.
One of the worst professors ever. Treats and class meant for general education credits like a 400 level major only course.

Professor Dynes is super smart, and while his lectures can be scattered at times he really emphasizes what you need to know. His reading quizzes can be challenging but he is a fair grader on those and the papers/tests. He also seeks out constructive feedback to try and make the class better which is something many profs don't do. Rewarding class.

Dynes is a nice guy, and comes across as being willing to work with you, but that's not the case. His teaching style is relaxed and unorganized. He's young, overly prideful and shakes off his lack of teaching skills by laughing or rambling until you forget what the question was. I was disappointed. Hopefully he'll get better with experience.

This was my first political science class here at BYU and I learned a lot from this class. He gives a lot of reading and occasionally gives reading quizzes so be prepared. Hes a funny guy and his lectures are very insightful. However, he is quite the tough grader. Also we didnt get our midterms back until the last day of class so...

Dr. Dynes is awesome! Yes, he's a hard grader, but this is college--you're not going to get an A on everything. I've really enjoyed his class and appreciated the emphasis on engagement and participation from students. He's super nice and willing to help students whenever needed, and as long as you are motivated you will do well in the class!

Dr. Dynes is a good guy, but his tests and assignment criteria are very muddy and he's a tough grader. I felt frustrated by all the work I put in only to get mediocre grades. I do like his lectures, he's very smart and likes participation in class. I'm glad I took the class, but he's got lots of improvement to do on his teaching abilities.

Professor Dynes can be erratic at times, but his lectures are very funny. He is very open to criticism and he really seeks to make his class better for his students. This class is good for motivated students. He is also happy to meet with you during office hours, and wants to make his class enjoyable

Professor Dynes is so frustrating to work with, impossible to contact, extremely confusing in his lectures and an incredibly hard grader. He gives you so much work with no guidance on how to succeed. I would have learned better on my own out of the book, but of course you can't miss a class because you get a quiz just about every class period

Okay so Dynes is so bad at explaining concepts. But he also tells you to contact him if you need to figure something out, but he is so bad at responding to you! I had to figure out a time to meet with him about our papers (a mandatory meeting we all had to do) and I sent him four emails with no reply! To the email he provided to us. So annoying.

Prof Dynes is nice, but doesn't seem to know what he's talking about. He doesn't understand what the students are asking so he doesn't answer their questions. He's a tough grader but doesn't give good feedback to help you improve. Good guy, bad bad teacher

Prof Dynes is a nice guy, he knows what he's talking about most of the time, but isn't good at explaining it. He's one of those "knows things but doesn't know how to teach those things" guy. You get loads of reading for homework and have to teach yourself. He's also a way tough grader which is too bad since he doesn't teach you well enough for that

Prof. Dynes is a very tough grader but also caring and really tries to make sure students understand the material. A lot of the reading is technical (and there is a lot of reading!) but he also goes over it in class. He also works hard to get to know students and give them detailed feedback. Good guy! Still a hard class, but worth it I would say!

A wonderful person and super kind. He gives extremely nuanced explanations of somewhat difficult and abstract topics which you might miss if you don't pay close attention to every word he says. Tons of reading, not too many other assignments, but those you do have are time consuming. I learns tons and feel blessed to have gotten to know Prof. Dynes

Professor Dynes is very intelligent (He went to graduate school at Yale) and I really felt like I learned a lot of important things about state and local politics from his class. It was VERY reading intensive, but I took it as a term class, so it was supposed to be more fast-paced. We read many research studies and the final tests your understandng

New professor. Nice guy. He could be more clear when he teaches, but he improved through the semester. He is very fair and willing to bend over backwards to help you succeed. Tests are easy, however he expects a lot on the research paper!

This professor was very easy. You are expected to mark your own attendance, which is something that can be easily forgotten. Most assignments are group works. Easy assignments and participation based, but you need to stay vigilant with submissions, because they're easy to forget haha.

He's super nice and really knows his stuff. Pretty easy, you just work on groups on your own guitar arrangements, and he gives a lecture to everyone. Show up to class and practice on your own and you'll be great.

Adam was great but the TA grading the class was always super late on grading and even gave my last performance less than 100% (which we normally would get) for no written reason. Attendance is worth 11% of the grade and it's self reported. 4 performances in total that you just have to film with your group. Take it if you want to learn the basics.

I loved Professor Keith's knowledge of audio tech--he definitely knows his stuff. He encouraged me so much on my music journey! He always tied in spiritual things and his testimony in just the right way that I needed to hear with every lecture.

Went to class, everyone played on their own for 50 min. (he didn't really teach), and 4 performances as a group of 3-10 ppl. Ask him questions if you want to learn more specifics. Easy 2 credits, especially if you know even a lil bit of guitar. used the textbook maybe 4x.

We had such good discussions, and he was really flexible about talking about what was important ot us. His assignments and grading were very reasonable and weren't too hard. I really think that everyone should be required to take this class because I learned so much!

This is my favorite class I have taken at BYU! He is amazing at promoting discussion, answering questions, and teaching material in a clear way. I learned so much and gained different perspectives from this class. I found the lectures super engaging, which made the exams and the final project doable. GREAT CLASS.

Professor Rogers himself was an awesome professor! Unfortunately, at the end of the semester, the last two big assignments weren't even graded before I received my final transcript score, which I hoped would bring my grade to an A. If you take this class, be prepared to advocate for assignments being graded!

Really great lectures! I wish I had taken this class in person, but I still found the course information really fascinating. I feel like he would have been great to meet in person. Lots of little assignments and a few big ones.

I took his Parenting and Child Guidance class online. He put us in Marco Polo groups to have more organic discussions with classmates. He teaaches concepts in applicable ways using his own kids for examples which felt very personal. I definitely recommend this class for any future parent even if you aren't an SFL major.

I've taken 2 classes from Dr. Rogers and highly recommend. His classes have light work each week, with one big assignment due at the end of the semester that you work on throughout. Sometimes his classes had too much class discussion, and I really just wanted to hear from him, but other than that, his class was easy and engaging!
I highly recommend this class! Dr. Rogers is awesome! The structure was very well organized and the assignment load was as expected. I learned a lot about parenting!

I loved this class. I took it because I needed an elective course and I retained more than I thought I would. There are 3 big papers and i would recommend meeting with a TA if the class is online to go over what is expected, but the class itself was amazing. Dr Rogers does a good job of tying in gospel concepts in a smooth and natural way .
