If you like discussion-based classes - take this!! I appreciated the constant care Dr. Rogers put to each comment made by students. He balanced assignments, lectures, and participation. You will want to listen and pay attention not just to do well on exams but because it is genuinely interesting!!
There is a term project, a few exams, and readings.
Follow the rubrics exactly and have your TA go over your papers and you'll be golden. This was my second class from Dr. Rogers and I love his teaching style

Dr. Rogers was fantastic and the set up of this class is very clear. The workload is totally manageable and his lectures were always really interesting! He has recorded lectures so it felt more personal even though it was online. Totally recommend him and this class. I found his tests to be super easy as well as long as you take good notes!

Mr Rogers was amazing. He taught a controversial subject with grace and openness. The class was very discussion-based, and he directed well. He learned everyone's names despite it being a substantial class full of girls. You are graded mainly through a project you work on throughout the semester, a few in-class quizzes, and tests. TAKE THIS CLASS

Dr. Rogers is awesome!!! It was an online course, but he has it organized in a very clear and manageable way. His lectures are engaging and interesting. Course load is very doable and the same so you can get into a weekly groove with it. He's accessible if needed and super kind. Would def recommend him and his course!

I cannot recommend Adam enough! He is one of the most understanding and empathetic professors I have ever had, which is so important for the subject being taught. He was so willing to work with us on deadlines and other aspects of the class, and he really is very informed on what he teaches. He is always happy to hear a variety of perspectives.

Professor Rogers is the best Professor I've had at BYU. His lectures are engaging and powerful. I've never been so excited to go to class. He's incredibly caring and most classes are discussion based which allows for so much learning. He listens and validates every single person. Please take this class!

Barely did the readings but learned so much from his interactive, insightful lecture. Adam's a pro at citing current research while asking students for their thoughts & opinions. Adam cares for all his students and went above & beyond to support student parents and students with disabilities. Make sure to get feedback on the semester-long project.

Hands down one of the best professors I've ever had at BYU. I wish every class was like this. I got more from the class discussions and interesting lectures than any test or assignment could have given me. Super grateful for Professor Rogers. He takes a lot of time to prepare for his lectures and backs up everything with research. Take his class!!

AMAZING professor. I have taken three classes from him. He is accommodating and respectful towards students. He gives great lectures and tailors his (online, open note) tests to his lectures. He loves discussions and cares more about understanding concepts in class rather than just covering everything. Take a class from him!!

Dr. Rogers is AMAZING. The class was more of a discussion rather than a lecture and he took the time to hear our experiences. We talked about some 'hot topic' things but he navigates it in a very loving and unbiased way. One of my favorite classes I have ever taken. I learned SO much. Tests are open note and he is a very fair grader.

What the other students have mentioned is completely true! The class subject is not the easiest, but he makes it super understandable and the workload is completely doable! He values each comment/question and answers them well! Also, I took his class and statistics at the same time: he is the reason I understood my statistics class!

Best professor I have ever had! Dr. Rogers cares so much about each individual student and if the students are stressed he will push back assignments. One of the few professors that I feel comfortable to actually go to his office hours and helps immensely every time. Take SFL 290 from Dr. Rogers!! The research paper is done throughout the semester

Absolutely the best teacher within the school of family life. He is very considerate about the work load he gives and how his students are doing with his deadlines. He is very respectful in lecture and the grading criteria is clear and doable. It is clear he cares deeply about what he teaches. If possible, take his class!

Professor Rogers cares! Take his class. Don't be afraid he will help you. He wants to see you succeed and he will help you do it every step of the way. It's so easy so feel lost at byu but Professor Rogers helped me feel like I mattered.

Adam is a G, he's seriously so awesome. He's real and knowledgeable and so willing to help everyone out. He assigns textbook readings, but I found no need to do them, especially having taken stat 121 and discussed research in other classes. The research project is done across the course of the semester and you are given all the tools to do it well.

If his class is full, you wait to take SFL290 with Professor Rogers. He is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. He makes such a daunting class completely manageable and dare I say enjoyable. You have a course project completed in different assignments throughout the year+in-class group quizzes an open note test! Just an amazing guy.

Best professor to take for 290. I was terrified of the class because research sounds so boring, but Dr. Rogers makes the content accessible and he remembers what it is like to be a student. The class requires effort, but Dr. Rogers makes it manageable and worthwhile. I wish other professors could take a teaching class from him because he excels.

If I could rate dr. rogers a 10/5 I would. You cannot get a better professor at BYU. He is so understanding. He knows whats it's like to be a student and is so helpful. Everything is broken down and you have a lot of time to work on things. Dr. Rogers is the best! Also he's super knowledgeable and inspiring.

No textbooks and tests are open notes/lecture slides, but they are harder because of that. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll want to go to to take notes because not everything is on the slides and some concepts are difficult to grasp outside of class. Lectures are amazing and Professor Rogers is a great professor though!

I've said it before & I'll say it again, Dr. Rogers is my favorite SFL professor at BYU. He just gets what its like to be a student & respects your autonomy. This was my third class by Dr. Rogers & by far the easiest. I learned a lot & am grateful for a teacher who approaches tough subjects, like gender inequality, fairly & with knowledge & respect

Professor Rogers is amazing! His lectures are very informative and he makes sure everyone understands. As long as you stay on top of your assignments, it's not too difficult. If you are struggling with something, talk to him! He is SO understanding and will do all he can to help catch you back up. Highly recommend him!!

He is an incredible professor and connects with/relates to the students so well. He teaches the material in a very understandable and engaging way. I would honestly say he is one of the best teachers I have ever had!!!

Dr. Rogers is amazing! The material for SFL 290 is kinda dry, but he makes it as interesting, engaging, and applicable as possible. I really enjoyed going to class. He breaks up the empirical paper throughout the semester so it's not bad. He is relatable and cares about you and will help you succeed. Definitely take this class from him!

A super chill dude. Very personable and will make an effort to know your name. I didnt use the textbook once and did just fine. Quizzes are all in class and open neighbor/open note. 4 tests, but easy as long as you study what's on the study guide. Final project is divided into sections with different due dates so you're not super slammed at the end
Dr. Rogers is one of the best professors at BYU. I felt that he truly wanted me to be successful and did all he could to help out. Take this class from him, you won't regret it!

I will never forget that class. I hate stats and research, and I went through some really hard things that semester but I met with professor Rogers outside of class a few times to get feedback and he was the kindest. He is a gem. Take his class and be changed forever! The class requires work but once you finish your project you feel SO proud...

Dr. Rogers is incredibly nice. He cares enough to get to know all of his students' names and he's very passionate about the research that he does. He welcomes questions and feedback, so the lectures are good. I didn't want to take this class, but he really makes it easy to succeed! I would sign up for another one of his classes in a heartbeat!

Dr Rogers is awesome. He is willing to work with you if you reach out. This isn't an easy class by any means but he makes it more interesting. The TA's grade everything which can be frustrating though. It's hard to get consistent scores on things because one TA may say something and then another TA may say another. Rogers is great though!

Dr. Rogers is AMAZING! would take every sfl class from him if I could. He is so willing to work with you and makes it impossible for you to not do well if you put in the effort. He cares about his students and is realistic with the material. Gives you every opportunity possible to get the best grade! One of my favorite professors at BYU by far!!

Dr. Rogers makes this boring class interesting and easy. The final research paper is broken down throughout the semester so by the time it is actually due right before finals, you are already done. There are two midterms and a final. He has only taught this class for 4-5 semester so he genuinely asks how he can make things better. TAKE FROM HIM!

Dr Rogers is FANTASTIC. He knows that the material isn't that exciting or interesting, but he does so much to make it better and more understandable! He's very receptive to how he can improve as a teacher, and is willing to adapt assignments to students' need. Always willing to help and explain concepts. Hands down, take the class from Rogers!
The best!!!! My favorite professor at BYU so far. I second all the other reviews. He genuinely cares about his students and makes dull concepts interesting.

He is a WONDERFULLLLL professor. He understands his students and genuinely wants to help us. Even when he isn't teaching the most exciting concepts, he finds ways to make it interesting. He learns the name of every student in class, which makes learning feel a lot more personal.

Best professor at BYU. He takes times to listen and is always available to help. The class is set up really well -- he gives a study outline for each day of class to help you know what to focus on. Tests are very straight forward. Fun class and fun professor!

Professor Rogers is a real gem. I say he's the best prof to take 290 from. He knows and openly acknowledges that the content may not be very interesting, but he does his best to make it interesting. Assignments are straight forward and the tests, if you study the slides and the study guide, are very doable. Very helpful if you got to office hours.

Dr. Rogers is a lifesaver. I had been dreading this class ever since I signed up to be an SFL major. It is super tough material and honestly very intimidating but Dr. Rogers is superman. He explained the lectures in a way that someone as quantitatively challenged as I could understand. He WANTS you to be successful and learn. Great man &Great prof!

Not an easy class but Dr. Rogers really works with students individually and is humbly open to feedback. He is very knowledgeable and makes a potentially dry subject more interesting through class activities, personal examples/stories, and good PPs. He is kind, inspiring and listens. The research paper is doable with portions due along the way.

If you can take SFL290 from him, I definitely would. Research paper broken into several steps, so you can get individualized feedback. He really takes into account feedback and truly wants to help his students. I was dreading this class, but it actually has turned into one of my favorite classes. Study heavily for tests, they are mostly application

Dr. Rogers is by far one of the best professors at BYU. Dr. Rogers really knows how to teach and facilitate great discussions in class. His expectations for the research paper and tests are very clear, and his class is very organized. He is always willing to help, and I would definitely take this course again from Dr. Rogers. He is awesome!

Prof Rogers is awesome! The research paper is not bad because it's broken into parts that you work on throughout the semester. Exams are not bad and he usually will let you use an index card. He sometimes has in class assignments or quizzes based on readings. If you ever have any questions he is always super good at answering them and helping you.

Dr. Rogers was new this semester but he did a pretty good job. He was teachable and the areas he struggled with he really tried to improve on. Tests were difficult but if you showed up to class and understood the material then they were doable. One major paper which was broken down so it was doable.

I was not looking forward to this class at all, but Dr. Rogers sincerely made me interested in research. His lectures are really helpful so you dont want to miss them. There is a big paper, but you do parts of it along the way and he walks you through it. I have learned so much in this class. If at all possible, take it from him. Seriously!

I wasn't looking forward to this class at first, but this professor made it bearable and he taught the material well. There is a big paper and some tests, but if you stay on top of things, it's not too hard. He was a nice guy and very approachable.

Sanders is THE BEST!! As long as you put effort into the projects you make in this class, you get a 100%. There's an online textbook, but it's free because he just uploads the required reading each week. Super easy course load with only 5 projects (which he gives a lot of time to complete). TAKE 350 FROM HIM!!

Great guy and teacher. Really cares about the students. The class is mainly project based and you spend most of your time on those which is really nice. Very knowledgable and lots of practical learning.

Honestly, he is so underestimated. This is the best teacher for COMMS 350. So, much learning hands-on with camera equipment and it helps that he works in the film industry. More people need to know about him.

Dr. Cavallini is an amazing professor, and I looked forward to her class every day! This was her first semester teaching 342, and it was so good! She told us that she wanted us to enjoy class, and class was really fun, and I learned so much. There were no exams other than the final!
I really enjoyed her lectures! I just didn't love that they are very unforgiving with late work, but the content was enjoyable for me.

You are learning so much material in such a small time but Dr. Cavallini makes it easy to follow and understand. There is not to much reading. Her slides are short but are very good at explain the terms you learned in the reading. She also add interesting videos and stories to make her class lectures funs and applicable. I would for sure recommend.

She was an okay instructor. I learned the materials well from her classes and understood the lessons thoroughly by the end of the semester. However, the majority of the lecture content comes from the textbook or slides. There was not very deep expounding of the slides. All in all, she taught the course was nice.

Adrianne made me feel like a high schooler. It doesn't matter how closely you follow grading criteria, it won't get 100% unless you suck up hard. 

Daily homework, tons of assignments, and in class attendance points all topped off by the fact that she only vaguely seems to know what she's talking about once you ask a clarifying question
I really liked Dr. Cavallini and could really pay attention during her lectures. The tests are based off the lecture slides, so you know what to study.

Dr.Cavallini is AMAZING. The class is very systematic, which made it easy to get an A. Workload is relatively light as most things are graded on completion rather than accuracy. There are 2 papers, both of relatively low effort. 4 tests (including final), all multiple choice, all from exclusively the in-class slides. Lectures are optional.

I really liked her! There was a lot of homework that wasn't hard but took a lot of time out of the week, and there are 4 exams. The lectures were interesting and I feel like I learned a lot, only downside is she moves really fast. There were also a couple of papers that were annoying and took a lot of time to do, but easy to get a good grade.

This class was super fun for me! Definitely stay up on your readings/ inquizitives and you'll be fine. Tests are based on the slides. Study and understand the concepts on those, and you'll be fine on the tests, too. I used notebooklm to study, and it worked out well for me. Dr. Cavallini is the best!!

Dr. Cavallini is an amazing professor! She is so kind and clearly loves her students! This is a very easy class as long as you stay on top of readings and assignments. The course covers a lot of material overall, but she does a great job of covering the important things that will be on the test in class. I would definitely recommend this with her!

This course uses an interactive textbook that has quick quizzes and activities due every Monday and a weekly quiz due on Wednesdays where you earn or lose points based on your answers. The class covers a lot of material, but it's all pretty manageable since you can skim the readings and she goes over the key stuff in class with slides.
Dr. Cavallini was a great professor. She is very kind and wants to help the students. Class felt a little slow at times but not bad. Content isn't to hard. All in all not a bad experience

Professor Cavallini read of slides during her lectures, and they weren't very engaging. It's not a difficult class, I just didn't feel motivated to try because the lectures were so boring. If you like to just study off slides then it's a good fit! I personally didn't feel like we were taught, rather just told.
Very easy class. You technically do not need to go to all the lectures because she has access to all the slides but the exams are easy so long as you utilize the study guides and TAs.
It is a good class. The online textbook is awesome, but the workload every week is kind of insane. The work is very organized, overall a very good class.

Cavallini is a super kind woman. The lectures obvi don't have mandatory attendance but I would treat them like they do. She makes you work and study hard so you pass the class and understand what you're learning. There are textbook assignments weekly and alot of info to cover. stay on top and go to lectures and youll do fine.

Amazing professor! Class isn't technically mandatory since she mostly reads off of the slides but I went anyways. A lot of memorization is required but I found the information fascinating so it was fun. TA reviews before the tests are super helpful since they basically tell you what to study. Would definitely take from Prof. Cavallini again!

Professor Cavallini is really awesome. She loves to have class discussions about the material which make the lectures really engaging. The essays and tests are the bulk of your grade. The TA's do really great reviews and the class feels like a community. Simply material overall. If you have questions or are confused the TA will be your best friend.

The TAs really make or break the class. The professor is really nice. It is pretty much a lecture and an at home quiz after every class with a short paper here and there. The midterms are pretty easy as well.

I loved taking this class from Cavallini! It was a lecture class but she was really creative in finding ways to involve everyone. We did experiments and activities. She explained things clearly and provided many examples. Not many assignments, pretty easy overall, and the TAs tell you exactly what's on the test in the exam reviews.

Really great professor, she's super fun and taught very clearly. I had her for psych 111 and the information needed for exams was very clear. Lecture was pretty repetitive if you did the homework and you have readings and a quiz due with each lecture along with a short paper due each week but the topics are pretty simple and quick.

she's super nice and cute and def take psych 111 from her! very reasonable workload and very clear rubrics. the TAs are also very supportive and helpful. what I kinda didn't like was all the guest lecturers, which had pretty varying lectures. and also slides and study guides are all posted on learning suite which makes this class pretty easy!

Dr. Cavallini was a very organized and sincere teacher. The class was small so we got to know everyone in the class pretty well. We had a lot of assignments though - some were helpful, while others were just busy work.

Dr. Henderson really wants her students to succeed. One of the most caring professors at BYU. Her class also really prepared me for my anatomy class in my DPT program at U of U. I feel ahead of my peers because a lot of the material I am familiar with from her class. In some ways, she teaches the material even better than my PT professors at the U.

Adrienne is a great professor. The structure of her class is good. Her exams are straightforward and are made based on her slides so there are no surprises. There are daily in-class quizzes but they are very easy and only there to ensure attendance and participation. It is a hard class by nature but I can't imagine taking it with anyone but her.

Agatha is amazing! Everyone in the program loves her. She is kind, super passionate about what she teaches, willing to learn with you, understanding, and overall made my experience at BYU so much greater! She is the definition of a wonderful BYU professor!

Agatha is a great teacher and her classes are fun. But she is different when she comes to observe your teaching. She really wants the best for you but she does want you to teach like she does. She's kind of stuck in her ways and her feedback can be contradicting. She really means the best but she has a hard time accepting other teaching styles.

Best professor alert! Agatha is such a good professor and really cares about her classes. She is so willing to talk with you and acts on student concerns. She designs her assignments to be helpful and to give you good practice. She is honestly just a good time. And of course you'll always get lots of free food in her class.

Agatha is the best professor I have ever had at BYU. Nothing but great things to say. She is very understanding, and willing to answer any questions we had. She also brought snacks every class, which was amazing. 10/10 would recommend!

Agatha is the best! She genuinely cares about the success of all of her students. She makes class fun and interactive and works with students if they have any concerns. There are kind of a lot of assignments in this class but she tries to make it the least stressful it can be. She also brought snacks to every class haha.

Dr. Mosenkov definitely wants to help you out however he can. I found the courseload to be just way more than reasonable, though, and unpredictable both on the amount of time assignments/readings would take and on their difficulty. Overall, Dr. Mosenkov's teaching style didn't work very well for me.

Dr. Mosenkov is definitely a great professor; he is extremely caring and is willing to work with you. My only beef is the homework problems' difficulty: some homework problems are really easy and others are obnoxiously hard. Overall, he is great.

Dr. Mosenkov has one of the most organized and thought-out class and assignment structures I have ever seen! He really cares about his students and will go out of his way to help if you express any need whatsoever.

Don't be put off by the amount of work and depth of understanding he wants from you. This class is so jam packed with extra credit that you can easily get an A even bombing two tests. Exemplary teacher always incorporating all of BYU's aims and bringing the gospel to the table. If you're unsure, trust me YOU'LL BE FINE!

Sure he has an accent so it can be hard to understand, sure there is a ton of material, but given the extra credit, and how utterly dedicated he is to your success, its impossible to not get an A. I bombed things and failed an exam and ended up with an A because he is on your side THAT much. Love him. Don't understand the complainers

I was worried at first due to the ratings, but the professor is really good. The class is well-organized and requires a lot of effort. There's a lot of homework, reading, and tough tests. My grade was A-, but with extra credit, it's now an A. I wouldn't recommend it for your first semester. I wish I took this class more seriously.

This class is pretty assignment heavy for a GE class- pre-class and in-class quizzes, weekly homework, LOTS of reading, out of class projects, etc. The content is difficult and the tests can be challenging. Dr. Mosenkov is a very kind and understanding professor. He gives lots of opportunities for extra help and extra credit

Great class and great teacher! The homework involves a good bit of reading, but if you stay on top of things, you'll be alright. The professor and his TAs are more than accessible for any help you could ever want.

This class was quite fun. There were a lot opportunities to observe stars and planets at night with the TAs. Dr. Mosenkov is easy going. There is decent amount of reading and assignments, but the class has been really great!

The class isn't difficult, but it's one of the most frustrating classes I've taken. Questions are poorly worded and sometimes just incorrect. Dates for midterms are nowhere to be found on learning suite or the syllabus. You only know them when he emails you the week before. Not hard, just obnoxious.

If you have an interest in space and our universe, I definitely recommend this course. Professor Mosenkov is a great professor, willing to work with students and does a good job of explaining some of the more complex ideas.

The class was hard, but I could see his desire to improve as a teacher. He's not very experienced with undergrad courses, but I've never seen a professor so eager to actively seek feedback from students, implement that feedback, and generously curve the class grades when it's apparent that the assignment was too hard. Most of the class got A's.

Dr. Mosenkov is a nice person but the class is SO boring and SO hard. The tests had to be majorly curved because no one understood the material at all and the tests were impossible. He's a nice man who loves his students but his lectures were mind-numbing. It was a struggle to stay awake. If you put in the work you can get an A, but it's not fun

This class was horrible. The amount of homework is insane. There is preclass,inclass, and after class quizzes PLUS homework. The quizzes are like 20 questions, short response and so difficult. The test are SOO long and difficult. The readings were insanely long. Learned nothing in class. He is an awkward person to work with isnt well at conversing.

I would agree that lectures are quite boring. However, the class is well organized and he is a genuinely kind person. He sends emails wishing you great weekends and holidays. I see that a lot of others complain that he mumbles but honestly I could understand what he was saying, it was just confusing content. Take for GE only if you like astronomy.

Extremely organized on learning Suite and in general. Gives so many extra credit opportunities, its impossible to get a bad grade. It might seem like a lot of work because he's passionate about your learning, and wants you to go the extra mile, but really the tests are lightwork and if you pay attention to lectures, you will be more than fine.

Unless you are a physics major, don't take this class. It is far too difficult for a level 100. So much reading, lectures are rushed, and an insane amount of quizzes and homework. Tests feel impossible. There's a curve but don't expect it to save you. He cares about students but struggles to explain concepts. Save your GPA if this is a GE for you.

Lectures are a struggle, he speeds through slides and rarely covers the material actually on them. Lots of mumbling and doesn't really answer questions. However, I was able to get an A in his class. He curves all of the tests, and if you have a friend, odds of success for the homework increase. The material is cool though. The TA helps a ton.

He says um after almost every word and he uses a microphone, but don't let that fool you that you will be able to hear him. YOU WONT. He makes you do so much work yet teaches so little. The amount of pre class work you had to do was absolutely crazy. I dropped, because I knew I would've had to "play astronomy teacher" and teach myself. cried...

Professor Mosenkov is a teacher who genuinely cares about his students. The class was often confusing but very informative. Tests are difficult but he always curves them (sometimes a LOT). If you have questions that he didn't answer well in class, he explains things much better during office hours.

DON'T take this class, save yourself a headache. He speaks too quietly even with a microphone; it's hard to understand him. He avoids students' questions & his answers don't make sense, so I was constantly confused leaving class. Tests are confusing & long, there are multiple quizzes due a week & the study guides don't prepare you well for tests.

Spent 13-15 hours a week on this class. Professor reads straight from slides and is very quiet. Expects you to know answers on material not covered. Lectures are organized, OA's and WA's were not. Tests are incredibly difficult (3 midterms and a final). Study guides don't prep. He is nice and an amazing researcher but do not take this class.

Dr. Mosenkov has a thick accent and mumbles. He's the type of professor that is pretty much at BYU to do research and not to be an effective teacher. His grading is very inconsistent and the TAs were very unhelpful. It was my hardest class this semester, which is surprising since it is a GE. Definitely take from anyone else please!

Amazing researcher, kind person, doesn't teach very clearly. This class was designed for you to do the work before and during class, not after, so do the assigned pre-class study to keep up in class. Pre-class and in-class quizzes, labs in the planetarium, assignments to learn the constellations and observe celestial objects, 3 midterms and a final

His entire class is lectures that he half mumbles through. I learned more from reading the slides before class than I did from coming to class. Often very hard to hear, and regularly had a difficult time answering students questions. Would not recommend.
He reads directly from his slides and jumps all over the place. He was never able to answer questions in class and mumbled the entire time. Please take someone else

Dropped out after the first day. He reads everything straight off the slides. Super boring lectures, would not recommend to anyone. He is also very quiet and mumbles sometimes, making it hard to understand him. His slideshows are well put together, but you could go through the slides on your own and save a lot of time. Don't take from him.

Dr. Mosenkov is a great guy, and super accessible. However, lectures are boring, he reads off slides. In class quizzes for attendance every single class, plus a reading quiz before and homework once a week. Pretty manageable. Exams are mostly short answer rote memorization of formulas and numbers, easy to cram for but the multiple choice isn't.

Professor Curry is my favorite! Engaging lectures and helpful exam reviews. Three exams in the testing center were manageable with studying. A couple of writing assignments, but not too hard. Grading was consistent and done quickly. He is a very caring professor who clearly wants students to do well. I hope to take another class from him soon!
You can tell he really cares about his students and what he teaches. This is a great intro class and you get a really good overview of PR and what jobs in can lead to, and it's not that difficult.
Professor Curry is the best!! Loved my Comms 235 class with him. Highly recommend
He is amazing!! I really enjoyed all of his lectures. You could tell he cared about his students. I have never rated a professor before, but I wanted to rate him because he is incredible.

Alex is an excellent professor! He is very kind and wants his students to do well. Be aware that this is a difficult class and requires a lot of time! Make sure to take advantage of the TAs, meet with Alex if you have questions, and take advantage of the extra credit opportunities found at the bottom of some of the learning assignments.

Alex is amazing!! This was a pretty tough class for me since I had never coded before, but he explained things so well and him and the TAs helped one on one which was awesome. You can do corrections on the midterm and all the assignments up to 100% and he gives so much extra credit. You can tell he cares about his students and wants you to succeed!

Professor Jensen, is amazing! I was scared of taking this class but he made it almost easy. The structure of the class is so predictable and reliable. You have a learning assignment at the end of each week, and while they can take awhile, you can do corrections (up to 100%) on all assignments, even the midterm! 100/10 recommend him for this class!!

Alex is one of THE MOST caring professors I have had. Him and his TA's are extremely helpful and beyond willing to help you succeed. I struggled with this class because I struggle with coding. He provided extra credit opportunities and you could redo the homework and midterm for 100% credit back. An absolutely amazing person!!

Alex is the best professor ever! He really cares about the success of his students. This class is not so much a statistics class, but a coding class. You watch the lectures online before class. Class time is more a lab where you work with the TAs on learning assignments! He gave out a ton of extra credit. Midterm and final are projects! USE TAs!

Alex is AMAZING and caring. He offers so much extra credit & opportunities to improve your grade that I only needed a 50% on the final to maintain an A. This class requires practice & consistent effort; don't fall too behind and GO TO OFFICE HOURS for help! Lifechanging class that inspired me to declare a stats minor & believe in a future career.

He is SO NICE! He made stats super fun and not very stressful. There's a lot of long videos to watch outside of class but in class you get to practice what you learned while Alex and the TA's are helping. Lots of help outside class too. The class is super relevant because we used real data and I can use the skills I learned in the workforce.

Alex is the best, truly the best professor I have had. I had no coding/stats background and was nervous about taking this class but Alex helped me so much. He met with me numerious times outside of class to explain and teach me in a way I could understand. He is so helpful and cares for his students, he wants you to succeed and will help you do so.

Alex is my favorite professor at BYU. He is caring, and incredibly knowledgable. I was terrified to take 305, but found that Alex taught it so well that I ended up actually liking coding. It is a very hard class, but Alex and the TAs are so willing to help with anything and are very accessible. I felt it was so rewarding; I learned so much.

This class should've been hard, but Alex makes it so manageable. You'll be learning R to manage data. There are 4 accessible TAs to help with the content and you get tons of coding practice. He plays music during class while you're working and people collaborate. Not my vibe (made it difficult for me to focus), but others seemed to like it.

Best professor I've ever had!! It's kind of a difficult class & requires time outside of class, but he makes sure you understand what's going on before moving to the next concept and is always there to help one-on-one! He's not only a professor, but also a friend!! Please take him if you have the chance!

Alex is a fantastic professor. I did not expect Stat 305 to be a coding class, but with help from Alex, I found that I really loved coding!! He is super helpful and caring while still encouraging you to push yourself past your comfort zone. Our class was all best friends by the end of the semester. We learned while having so much fun!

Alex is very caring. He takes the time to learn each students name. His lectures are very straight and to the point. All of the lectures talked about how what we learn applies to those with Autism which I was surprised about but it wasn't a bad thing. Overall, I would recommend him for this this class, it was an easy class and he is super nice.

Was a pretty typical professor. Trying to fight the positive and negative inflation effect of RMP and give an honest review. Nice guy. He puts off "I was woke in the 90's but now my woke beliefs are conservative and I still think I'm woke" vibes. Class isn't too bad. Honestly no qualms with the class. Attendance not required. I liked the class.

Alex has been by far my favorite professor here at BYU! The fact that he makes you not call him "Professor Jensen" says a lot about who he is. He is caring and truly wants you to succeed. I took this class as well as adolescent development from him and I love the passion he puts into his teaching.
Alex is amazing! He cares SO much for every student. His teaching is unique because he shows up to class not just to lecture but to learn from his students. He really gets to know every student.

Alex is an excellent teacher who really cares about his students and the topics he teaches. His grading seems reasonable until you realize that each of the few assignments in the class will seriously hurt your grade if you fail to notice any number of minor things (A is 95%). Don't expect to ace this class and you'll love it.

Alex is an excellent teacher and keeps class extremely interesting. Here is the struggle- everything is graded by the TA's. Which is understandable except that who grades your papers makes or breaks you because they are very inconsistent between each other. The tests are fair and the major paper really isn't too bad if you work consistently on it

Alex is one of the best professors I've had. The research paper is difficult but he meets with you and tells you everything you should change. Tests are difficult but THE MOST FAIR exams I have ever seen at BYU. They are hard but straight forward questions, not a single one was I wondering when we ever learned about it. He is just the best person.

I LOVE ALEX. He was the best teacher. He engages his students, really cares about our learning process and is a very reasonable grader. He throws out bad test questions. There is one big research project that takes a lot of time and effort and is graded pretty harshly. I love, love, loved coming to class every day. Take this class from Alex!

Alex is a pretty young professor and as such, remembers what it was like to be a student. His assignments are fair and he gives tons of helpful feedback, as well as allowing a note card on the midterm and final. Attendance isn't mandatory but extremely helpful, it's hard to ace a test without it. One of my favorite professors at BYU.

His classes are discussion-based, and he writes the test questions based off of what is discussed, so be sure to attend lecture and participate!  He presents the material very clearly, and is so fun to learn from!  One of my favorite classes at BYU!

Alex is a wonderful instructor. He meets with students individually to review their research paper and gives the opportunity to rewrite it to improve your grade. His tests had a lot of short answer response, but you get an index card, and he asks students for feedback on the tests to improve them. He'll push you, but has realistic expectations.

He is a great teacher who really cares about his students. He is young and a new teacher, so he knows what students want and need. His classes are interesting and he does a lot of fun activities and games. His tests are easy cause you get to take a 3x5 notecard for the multi. choice, but you do need to go to class for the short answer part.

Alex is an awesome professor! Very accommodating to his students. Very fair grader. Class lectures are engaging and full of discussion. He allows a 3x5 notecard on his tests. He writes all test questions right after class so there are no surprises. He also evaluates all test questions and will throw out those that are unfairtoo tricky.
Great teacher, definitely makes learning chemistry very enjoyable.
She explains the concepts very well and makes hard concepts easy to understand. She is a great teacher and keeps the long lectures entertaining. Honestly, she is the best professor I have had so far.

Dr. Larson cares for her students deeply. She takes the time to make sure you fully understand any topics/material. The class is manageable if you show up to class and make an effort to try to learn as much as you can while there (lecture is the best resource). She is clear about what material will be tested, so the tests aren't too bad.

Prof. Larson is an okay lecturer, she posts class notes after class and explains concepts super well, she just sometimes runs out of time to explain a concept thoroughly, and it gets confusing. Also a lot of times the homework was due but she hadn't posted it yet. She's not super responsive to her email.

Everyone says he's hard, and he is, but he's fair. He can seem pretty intense, but he's really kind. If you have questions, he's good at answering in office hours!
Lectures were hard, because there are a lot of math/stat symbols/terms he just brushes over or expects you to know. Class was fast-paced, but that's the nature of the course.

Petersen is a great guy, he would bring chocolate to class. I took 340 and the class is hard as is, however taking it from him made it 10 times harder. A lot of the steps in between solving problems are missed because he assumes you already know. Luckily he does grade tests reasonably. However you will leave this class knowing nothing.

I took STAT 340 (not 330) from him last semester. He really cares about the material and teaching it right, but he also teaches a master's class with very similar material. I wished he had dumbed down the material a lot more for us - I could only figure stuff out by reading from the textbook and working with the TA's. HW assignments are long.

STAT 340 (not 330): Peterson is a great guy, loves what he teaches. I have the feeling nobody knew what he was teaching us half the time or the "why" behind it, he couldn't dumb things down to our level. Hw's were hard but doable, tests were easier (full page of notes for final). Its tough, but ace every hw w the TA's and youll do great.

STAT 340-Hardest class for the major, but taking it from him felt more difficult. He's brilliant, but he has a hard time explaining things on a lower level to undergrads. I learned most of the material from going to the TAs. He's fast and talks through a lot of the processes more than what he shows on paper. He's hard to follow along sometimes.

**stat 340** This class is difficult but that's expected. There's only one homework assignment due each week but they take a long time to complete (get help from TAs). He's pretty nice when grading exams and cares more about correct processes rather than correct answers. His exams are timed which can be a little stressful.

**Stat 340*** not stat 330.

I took Prof Petersen his first time teaching 340. It was Terrible! The homeworks were graded harshly, there are participation exercises in class, and on top of all that the tests were impossible. He curved it HEAVILY at the end. (according to his syllabus grading scale I should have gotten a C-, and I ended up with a B)

This class had a lot of R coding which could be a bit of a slog to work through but really helped me develop my coding experience. The group project took more hours than expected but it became a useful resume tool. Dr. Petersen's teaching style was very open and friendly. I spent a lot of time with the TA for homework help.

Good teacher, I thought he communicated material well and I felt like I left the class knowing quite a bit. Grades were tough though and I definitely felt like I deserved a much higher grade than I received in the class. Group project at the end of the semester, once again, graded pretty tough and lower than what I felt I deserved.

Prof. Petersen knows his stuff but lacks the ability to teach it clearly. He flies way to quickly through the lecture. Several times I had to go online to understand really what was being said. If you don't aren't really familiar with R Markdown and latek coding, make sure you become super familiar or the hw's will become a nightmare for you.

Cool guy, but not the greatest teacher. We spent most of our time working on code but our tests were based off of lectures and quizzes. It is also test heavy. Not enough HW to help your grade. I was kind of confused on the point of the class. It seemed like it should've been easy based on the material but was difficult BC we didn't learn much.

Dr. Petersen is so awesome! He was a mathematics undergraduate and slightly overestimates the amount of math we had taken as first year master's students. He did a great job of making his expectations well known. This course was challenging but that is mostly due to the nature of the material. Study for the tests and you will do fine.

The guy knows what he's talking about but it's hard to follow him since this knowledge is second nature to him; he can get pretty confusing at times. I hard a hard time figuring out what was going on and the textbook certainly didn't help all too much. He certainly does care about his students and is flexible but don't fall behind.

The class wasn't too bad. The thing that got me was the group project since my group wasn't very good, which pulled my grade down. She let the class choose what the grade category percentages would be on the first day of class. There is a quiz with each chapter, but they typically aren't too bad.

Poli 110*  Her lectures are SO boring and hard to lock into because of her teaching style. Attendance is a big part of your grade. Her quizzes were extremely specific, even if you pay attention in class it's difficult to get a great score. She's not flexible and isn't a very approachable person if you need help in life or school things.

Sister McIntire is one of my favorite teachers that I have ever had when it comes to lectures. I always enjoyed going to her class.  The problem was that there are hours upon hours of homework that all the students struggled to understand. She provided no resources and what we talked about in class had absolutely nothing to do with the quizzes.

Heads up: if you're taking this online, she isn't your teacher IRL. She's basically just a glorified TA who barely does her job. She seems to lack reading comprehension (she'll mark you wrong and correct you with the same info you literally said). She's the worst BYU professor I've ever had and I wish I hadn't taken this class.

Don't take if you like teachers who are considerate about your time and your schedule. Only took this one class over summer and still took all of my time. Assigns something every single day. Rarely interacted with students. If you want to protect your sanity, I suggest taking from a different teacher. This professor is the worst I've ever had.

Take Richard Kimball if you don't care for American Heritage. HUGE curve. I think I ended the class with a 45% or something and I just assumed I failed.. I checked my map middle of spring semester, i got the credit and I actually ended with a D+. hallelujah amirite. I got like 35% on every test. Like take him if you truly don't want to take AHTG.
Professor Kimball was really entertaining and taught the course clearly. He was very merciful and gave a big curve on all the exams and final grade.

Kimball was a good lecturer and teacher overall. However, this class in general just sucks. It really all depends on your TA. Don't take other hard classes with this class, and if you can don't work too much if you want to get an A. If you turn in everything, regardless of grade you will pass the class. Also there is a huge curve at the end

Professor Kimball was a little vague & hard to understand in lecture but he knew what he was talking about. I liked the textbook and weekly TA lab. Tests were strange, I wish they would just set up the class curved. American Heritage is great!! I now understand America a lot better & I like how the history is set up to teach the concepts.

Everyone hates on American Heritage, but I actually thought it was a pretty easy and enjoyable class! I never did a single one of the readings, I either went to the review room or had AI summarize them. Kimball's lectures were generally pretty engaging.

NO MORE AHTG SLANDER. This class is SO GOOD. Dr. Kimball is fantastic in every way. Dry humor makes his lectures really super awesome. You interact with your TA way more than the professor. Grade is primarily exam based (but there are a few essays). Lots of readings but they aren't too bad (& they're super interesting). BIIIIIGGG fan of this class!

He explained things very well (and is engaging) and had lots of resources to help condense and cement the concepts into your brain. Going to the review room as often as you possibly can saves your grade! (15 minutes daily) You have to read between every class (sometimes 40 pages). If you work, you can do well!

The content of this class is FASCINATING. I learned so much & loved going to lectures! It was not an easy class though. Attendance isn't taken in class, but if you miss one lecture, it's really hard to catch back up. Spent a TON of time reading, going to TA reviews, and studying for exams. Passable, but NOT easy. (should be a 4 credit class imo)

This class isn't hard, a bit time consuming and the test questions are unreasonable. To second what another student said, it really feels like you are being tested on random facts rather than broad concepts. Like one question was literally identifying who said a specific, unimportant quote in one of the required movies. Essays are harshly graded.
Take American Heritage from Professor Kimball if you have the chance!! I had heard a lot of scary things about the course but Kimball makes it engaging and really manageable.

Kimball made the class entertaining. American Heritage is a hard class but if you go to the review room daily, you will be fine. All the homework is reading, and to do well in the class you have to understand all of it. Kimball gives the least about of reading to do though, so I highly suggest taking him as your professor.

Dr. Kimball has been a great professor. That being said, it I disliked that many test questions felt like I was being tested on fun facts rather than important material. Regardless, there are reasonable curves and this class isn't hard to pass, but it is harder to get an A.
Few better than Dr. Kimble. Thoughtful discussions in class and he is endlessly generous with his time and insights. A true mentor.

If you are taking the history capstone and are interested in sports, Professor Kimball is the guy to take it from. There is always a lot of participation in class and time to listen to not only each other, but advice other students have for you. He loves what he does and makes sure to always leave good feedback to help your success!

Dr Kimball is a nice guy. He's always willing to take questions on lecture and discuss test questions on his office hours. If you're an international student, register for the International only session. TA lab attendance is a must, the quizzes aren't enough to prepare you test. Ask ChatGPT to make practice tests with the content, trust me.

I was scared for this class but it was actually great. Loved what I learned. It requires a lot of work, but it never felt too overwhelming. Pay attention to lectures, both what he says and the slides. Pay attention to the readings. Take good notes. Go to review room!! I did all that and studied and ended with an A. Dr. Kimball is great and fun.

Explains concepts in a way that really makes sense. There's a LOT of reading, three papers (including a semester-long service project), two midterms, and a final. He wants you to succeed. My TA at least was great, and so were the TA labs, so I think he teaches them well. Study early and with a group. Participate in lectures - it makes his day.

Get prepared for lots of reading and taking dense notes during lectures. The TAs and review rooms are the saving grace of this class, if you want a good grade you HAVE to attend those to really understand the material. The exams are test heavy but with lots of studying and understanding what he's looking for they are doable. Def recommend Kimball!!

Professor Kimball was amazing! His lectures were engaging, and he obviously loves American History. I absolutely loved taking this class from him and felt so engaged and connected to the past. The essays were tough, but if you do the readings for them, you will be okay. Focus on understanding major concepts, and you'll be alright!

As a junior, I found Kimball's class to be manageable. If you want to do well in this class though, you really need to do the readings, go to lecture, and take good notes. (Expect about 2-3 hours of reading per week.) We had weekly quizzes on the readings in lab, two required films, and three papers. We also had to do 10 hours of community service.

Listen up everyone! If you're going to take A HTG, take it with this man! I'm an international student and had to learn 90% of this stuff for the first time, but Dr. Kimball made the lectures entertaining and fun and I enjoyed learning because of him. Sure, the readings are alot, but that's why you have review rooms to help you understand them

Professor Kimball made American Heritage bearable. He's super funny and I found it easy to pay attention to him. There is a lot of reading though… like a lot. But as long as you don't procrastinate you should do fine

I think anyone that has anything bad to say about Professor Kimball probably just has an animosity against American Heritage. Professor Kimball was super funny and made lectures super interesting and engaging. This class isn't super demanding assignment-wise, do the readings and go to lecture. The exams are the hard part, get ready to study hard.

A HTG gets a bad rap, but honestly it's overstated. It's not that bad with Dr. Kimball, you can definitely get by only by going to lecture and doing zero readings, it's just that the tests are a little hard and heavily weighted. Anyone claiming this class is right wing propaganda is just plain wrong, quite the opposite. A few essays, weekly quizzes

Dr. Kimball was hilarious and entertaining in a really dry way. There is a mountain of reading, which is really good to do but just attending lecture he basically tells you everything he wants you to know. Doing really well with taking notes in lecture will get you a decent enough grade. Really not too bad of a class.
Insanely test-heavy!!!!!
Exams worth more than 65% of your grade is diabolical. Been here five years, this is easily one of the worst three classes I've ever taken
Loved this class! He is extremely funny and really loves sport history. 10/10 would recommend. You read three books and the tests are reasonable.

I thought this class was super fun and that Prof Kimball was great. He's a pretty nice guy and once you understand his style of humor, you realize he is hilarious. As long as you do the readings and come to class, it isn't that difficult. He isn't a tough grader but there are multiple long readings in this class.

Professor Kimball's AHTG100 is challenging but rewarding. His engaging lectures, TA support, and unstuckstudy AI made the workload manageable. While the grading is strict, staying on top of readings and study sessions can lead to a great grade.

The class is too hard for a GE. While people have complained that AHTG is conservative propaganda, I felt like he was a fair professor who didn't attempt to make excuses for slavery like some might. But, the class is horrible. Hours of reading. The amount of times in test review when they said "this answer is correct but not what he's looking for"

ATHG is a lot of memorization and not necessarily in a fun way. I didn't do a single reading but attended every lecture and took good notes. Go to the TA reviews for the tests and do not procrastinate on studying or the essays and you will be fine. Would definitely take from Kimball though (but maybe not freshman year like I did)!

I absolutely LOVED this course with Professor Kimball! He is ridiculously entertaining but clearly knows his stuff. While there were a ton of readings, they are totally doable if you don't push them off. Go to the TA for extra review and you will be good. Take from Kimball!!

Dr. Kimball is one of my favorite professors overall and really makes the class worth taking. My roommates had Pope, and while they had only complaints for AHTG, I found myself sad when the class was ending. Just stay on top of the readings and go to a TA lab when you don't understand something, and enjoy the lectures, cause Kimball's hilarious.

Professor Kimball is the best. I've never liked history, but I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures. That being said, the class is hard! I went to every TA review, throughly did the readings, studied for hours, and was still not able to get an A. I wouldn't recommend taking this as a freshman, but when you do take it, take it from Kimball and work hard!

The class was not hard--the grading was hard. AH was one of my favorite classes I've taken, and Kimball was an entertaining and phenomenal teacher. Most people's grievances come with how hard things are graded, which is true. But if you really try on your essays and ask for feedback before turning in, go to test reviews, you can get an A.

I took American Heritage my freshman year (unfortunately), But I am so glad I took it from Kimball! All essays only need to be 500 words and his lectures were surprisingly entertaining. TA's can be really hit or miss so taking really good notes is very beneficial in the long run. Overall great class.

Professor Kimball is the one you want to take American Heritage from. I dreaded taking this class and took it my senior year and it wasn't bad at all. Kimball is engaging in his lectures and is a really kind guy. The only thing to note is that TAs make a big difference so hopefully you get a great one!

Kimball is the professor you want for American Heritage. Yes, American Heritage is hard, but only because of the tests. The curve will help. I got 78, 72, and 79 on the exams, and I ended with a B+. There are a lot of readings that are important for tests. Kimball is hilarious. Study groups will save you. Only 3 papers: less than 600 words.

If you take this class from Kimball, it will be one of the best classes you take at BYU. I never understood why AHTG gets such a bad wrap; his lectures were really entertaining and well explained, and I was always aware of the expectations. Sure, it's a lot of work and study, but I honestly enjoyed most of it.

Kimball was funny and lectures were entertaining. If you have to suffer through american heritage, definitely take it from Kimball. Overall the class was interesting and just lots of reading, but the tests were crazy hard. In labs TA's tend to say "this answer is right but there is a better one" so tests were hard to get good at.

Dr. Kimball's lectures are awesome. He's hilarious while also getting the concepts across. The class is curved between all the students in your TA's labs. There is a lot of reading in this class, but actually doing the readings and going to the TA reviews as much as possible will help so much.
Great lectures, always had a good time. Reading is so important and the tests are wordy and hard to understand. But, overall it was a good class.

Our TA told us in the first lab we would be "competing against each other." Took this class as a junior and it made me lose my 4.0 (I'm a pre-med/STEM major). Kimball was nice and his lectures were interesting but there were no study helps for exams and the amount of irrelevant readings was ridiculous. BYU needs to figure this whole AHTG thing out.

Kimball was fine, lectures were ok but the tests were ridiculous. I did really well on all of my quizzes and assignments... they were actually pretty easy but the grade is so heavily based on the impossible exams that it is hard to actually succeed.

best american herritage teacher. the readings are brutal and weekly quiz was impossible. tests werent too bad as long as you pay attention in class. be ready to take good notes in lecture and come every time. only two big papers that were short. he was so funny, lectures were almost always engaging even though its a boring subject.

This is probably one of the best professors I have ever had. Dr. Kimball manages to make his classes intriguing, informative, and make you want to learn more. Whether you're fond of history or not, you will find his lectures interesting. The class is difficult, yes, but the curve is super helpful. He's a great guy and I'm sad to leave his class.

Dr Kimball was a good professor for this subject, but American Heritage is notoriously hard and his tests and assignments are harder than they needed to be. He grades on a curve so there are only so many good grades he'll give out. If you want to do well with him, stay up on the reading and go to the Review Room as often as possible.

Such a good professor! Lectures are interesting, engaging, and fun. The midterms/final are hard, and even harder to prepare for, but take good notes and do the reading and you'll leave the class feeling fulfilled!

Dr. Kimball is awesome. His lectures are very engaging and really focus on valuable content, despite this class material being very broad. The TA reviews are VERY helpful, and studying lots for the test is necessary to succeed, but this class is certainly doable. It is graded on a curve, so only the top 10% or so in your lab get an A.

Professor Kimball is AMAZING! His lectures were entertaining and you can tell he is passionate about what he is teaching. The tests were really hard, but there are TA review rooms that can help. I didn't do a lot of the readings, but if you do the assigned readings you should be fine on the quizzes and tests. I loved this class!

Dr. Kimball made me look forward to every lecture. He made the material entertaining and engaging. American Heritage is not as hard as people say if you attend the T.A. reviews two or three times a week. When combined with a strong understanding of the reading, these can almost guarantee your success in the class.

American Heritage is a very difficult class, but compared to the other professors, you want Kimball! He was very entertaining and you can tell he is passionate about what he does. Missing lectures is hard but they aren't boring. The papers are graded by your TA and none of them were long. If you go to the review room you will do well on the tests.

Phenomenal professor and amazing course! American Heritage is rumored to be difficult, but I promise it is worth the time. I didn't find the content itself particularly difficult, just the work load for those who are unmotivated. Professor Kimball was hilarious in lecture while making sure we get down all of the most important concepts.

Take this class from Dr. Kimball!! I absolutely loved this class and Dr. Kimball's lectures are really good. Prepping for midterms and finals was a little hard but as long as you take advantage of the TA lab you'll do fine! Make sure you do the readings since there are weekly quizzes in lab and you are curved against those with the same TA as you.

I love Kimball with my whole heart!!! Nicest and funniest professor I've ever had, he is so sweet but this class is HARD. Lots of reading and very vague tests and little resources. Pope's class is 100% more difficult, without a doubt take it from Kimball!!!

As an international student, American Heritage is way too hard for a GE. And if I am being honest, neither of the lectures or the TAs were helpful at all. Also, the readings are SO long it usually takes me hours and hours trying to get through & understand it. There are two midterm exams and a final exam, and they are all too hard and unnecessary.

Kimball was pretty interesting but the class itself isn't too bad...every lab you take a 5 point quiz and there are 3 short papers. The tests are definitely difficult and there aren't a lot of resources- no study guides and TA's are usually unavailable or just don't explain concepts well. Overall participate and read the textbook and you'll pass
Run.

Honestly, I have been very afraid of this class and have put it off to my Junior year. It was not as bad as I expected it to be, however, if you do not have a significant amount of time allotted for studying, I would advise taking it a different semester. Tests are tricky and so are the quizzes taken in lab each week.
I mean... it's American Heritage. Terrible class. But Professor Kimball was funny and the lectures weren't complete torture. He was respectful and overall a good guy.

% of grade: Exams-65%, Essays-22%, Weekly Quizzes-13%. Requirements of the 3 essays, 500 words: 10hrs of service, read 12 different articles, read Frederick Douglass. 2 required Textbooks, lots of reading. No study guides for exams, basically expected to know everything. There are TAs & a Review Room to help, but I prefer not to be there 24/7

Love the lectures for this class. They are pretty entertaining and he's a funny guy. The readings can be a bit strenuous with two different textbooks but if you get behind on them it doesn't really matter as long as you do them before quizzes and tests. The tests are pretty difficult but the going to the TA lab definitely helps.

Professor Kimball does an excellent job of making class engaging and funny, especially knowing that no one really wants to take American Heritage.  There is a lot of reading - that won't change based on the professor, and he does put a lot of questions on the tests from the videos he shows.  If you go to TA Review room then you'll be set.

I had a great experience with AHTG, Professor Kimball was great! Hilarious lectures, 5-point quizzes every week in lab. The three essays and the tests comprised most of the grade. Study hard and set aside time for the readings, but if you take advantage of the TA lab throughout the semester as well as before the tests, you should be set.

Obviously AHTG is a hard course at BYU, but he assures you that you will leave with at least a C. The TA access is amazing and helped so much. I think he is the easiest AHTG professor you can get, basically memorize the lectures and go to the TA reviews and you are set. 11/10 would suggest.

Terrible class. Good Person. He is a nice funny guy but this class made me hate learning about American history. I love history and passed the AP US history test but couldn't figure out this class. I never missed a lecture did every bit of reading and studied alone and in study groups, but I never was able to get a test score over 70%.

I LOVED PROFESSOR KIMBALL. I always heard that American Heritage was a BEAST, but I loved it, and I think it was all thanks to Kimball. He was kind, funny, and always had captivating lectures. He is incredibly smart and is able to explain complicated concepts in an understandable way - and he's hilarious. I would take American Heritage again.

I really liked Kimball, his lectures were engaging and organized. He's kind of funny too. But, his tests were unreasonably hard. I thought I did great on everyone but failed everyone. The curve saved my grade. 
Tips: Go to review rooms, study A LOT, do the readings(and understand them) and pray for a good TA. AHTG is hard though so Good Luck!

Professor Kimball was amazing! This was my favorite lecture to attend. The weekly reading quizzes were the class's most difficult part, at least for me. A few of your quiz scores get dropped though. The papers are short but require reading. If you work hard, study, take notes, and use the TAs you'll be just fine! TAKE KIMBALL!

I went in expecting the class to be super hard, but it wasn't too bad. Make sure to keep up with assigned readings and pay attention to lectures. The only homework we had was the readings and a few papers that weren't super long. Only negative was that he would ask some questions on the test about specific details from videos we watched in class.

Dr. Kimball is a great teacher and good at explaining the concepts, although it is a tough class. Weekly quizzes on the readings (LOTS of readings), 3 short essays, and exams are very difficult. The material is interesting but I had to study a lot! TA's are very helpful, and I was grateful for the curve at the end of class.

Professor Kimball gave engaging lectures and I feel like the essays and readings were a reasonable amount of out-of-class work. If you're taking this class, definitely make time to go to the TA reviews, they hold multiple every day in the library.

Kimball was fun, but I felt that his exams were very subjective and unfair. Go to the review room to understand how they want you to think about the concepts. It isn't a very straightforward class. There were random grades assigned to the essays with little to no feedback.

Kimball had good lectures and was hilarious but this class is ridiculous for it to be a GE. The TAs even told us that only 20% of students end up with an A in the class. No matter how hard you study, you never know if you're prepared for the tests. TAs also make or break the class/review rooms, so if you get a bad one, good luck.

Great Professor!
Loved the class

Kimball was a great professor. His lectures were interesting and easy to follow. American Heritage has a bad reputation but with Kimball it was a lot better than I was expecting. He made a difficult class more enjoyable.

I really liked Professor Kimball. He was a great teacher and had very engaging lectures. I know a lot of people hated American Heritage but he made the class enjoyable. I would definitely recommend taking it from him. I also would recommend going to the American Heritage Review Room. It is super beneficial and helps to solidify your understanding.
I personally hated this class but Professor Kimball was very nice. He gave interesting lectures and was easy to follow. American Heritage is annoying no matter what, but that's not his fault.

All AHTG classes are structured similarly, but I don't think you'll find a better professor to take it from than Kimball. He's super funny, has engaging lectures, and has content that feels really important outside of the class.
I only bought the CH textbook and was able to find most of the other readings on course reserve/online for free.

Professor Kimball is the best lecture professor for american heritage. The class wasn't as much of a bear that I thought it would be. Just go to the review room everyday, rewrite your notes, read the articles and just be a good student that wants to learn. Your Ta will make or break the class if you don't go to the review room. It is so helpful!

Would highly recommend this class. AH isn't as hard as people work it up to be, Professor Kimball didn't have me stressing about too much. Just make sure you attend class, read for essays, and do a study review for an exam, then its an easy A. Kimball himself is rather odd in a good way and his lectures were always interesting.

He has some of the lectures I have ever been to, super funny and super engaging. He is super passionate about what he was teaching. The tests were super hard, but they grade on a curve, which can be helpful. It was a super large class, but the recitation labs made it bit better. Overall, really solid professor.

I don't have anything against Professor Kimball. He was great! I just strongly dislike how difficult BYU makes American Heritage. I had two scholarships and nearly lost them both purely because of this class, so I withdrew. Quizzes and tests are so specific. If you don't intensely study every single reading and lecture, you likely won't succeed.
The grading on the essays was a little harsh-but those were graded by TA's. The class was also curved at the end.

Dr. Kimball is a solid choice. Of course the class is hard, but so are all the classes at BYU. Just study and read the textbook. The other professor, Pope gives way more homework but I think Kimballs tests may be slightly easier. Kimball curved the class heavily, so you should be fine. Dont stress, American Heritage is not as hard as ppl say.

Everyone says American Heritage is crazy hard but it isn't too bad with Dr. Kimball! He's a really great lecturer and explains ideas clearly. Not too much homework but doing the all of the readings will go a long way. Weekly quizzes (not too hard). The TA's are super helpful! The review room pretty much guarantees an A. I learned a ton!

This class was extremely hard. Three 600 word essays, 10 hours community service, readings for each class, quizzes each week in lab (not too hard if you do the reading), tests are all multiple choice but very difficult and heavily effect grade. Pay attention in class b/c things he says will be on test. Go to the Review Room. Kimball > Pope.

Reading in this class is spread very unevenly. The tests covered irrelevant material. The content is interesting and important, but the tests are discouraging. No matter how hard you study, you are going to struggle. The quizzes are okay as long as you do the reading, but some TA's make them unnecessarily difficult.

I would take American Heritage again just to be in this class! I loved Kimball and found class super interesting and engaging. Tests are typical to other professors so just take Kimball. Lectures were interesting and he loves to include movie clips to get his point across. Pay attention in lecture, ask questions in lab, study, and you'll do good.

I loved how Dr. Kimball taught this class. I don't like history, but I really liked this class! I learned so much. The tests werent easy, but I managed to get a B each time from skimming notes and what my TA said I should study. And the curve is really nice! Kimball doesn't give a lot of reading too, and honestly that just made the class ��

Kimball was a pretty good professor. The problems with American Heritage all come from AHTG department. Class material is actually, I dare say, interesting. More philosophy than history. But the way the class is structured, graded, and tested is ridiculous. Way too much work, too strict, and unrealistic expectations. But that's not Kimball's fault.

AHTG100 is a tough class, but Dr. Kimball makes it fun. He tries to make jokes which are sometimes a bit awkward, but it makes lecture interesting. He's not great at understanding questions posed to him by students. Very organized and clear in his teaching, and the 5 question weekly quizzes aren't terrible if you read + pay attention in lecture

Professor Kimball is a really good teacher. He keeps class entertaining by applicable examples and stories and kept us laughing all the time. Tests are really hard, but there is a sizable curve at the end of the semester. Doing the readings is pretty important. Go to TA review room!! Makes all the difference.

Though my grade wasn't great it could have been worse. Take this from Kimball because I heard the other professor requires you to write more essays. For the daily reading quizzes take notes of your readings and study them before attending lab. It's a tough class. The material covered is actually really cool and interesting. Be prepared the class.

American Heritage gets a ton of smack talk, but Dr. Kimball was extremely organized, clear, and usually entertaining to listen to. I never felt confused, and if I did there were many resources to help. I enjoyed every one of his lectures. Exams are TOUGH, and nobody gets full credit on essays either. But if you can take AHTG from him, do it.

This was such a hard class mostly I think because you have to read so much, and you don't have very many assignments, so small quizzes and such are heavily weighted in my opinion. Super funny teacher tho! Just read the materials and STUDY GROUPS!

I adored Prof. Kimball. I loved his class, it was so interesting and I looked forward to each lecture. It was very challenging come midterms and finals, and if you want a good grade you'll need to do some hardcore study-grinding. However, it was also my favorite class this semester, and I'd definitely recommend Kimball to anyone taking AHTG 100.

Dont let this class scare you! I did it on top of a heavy course load and did well, just make time to have study groups and GO TO THE REVIEW ROOM AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE! lectures are great, make sure to take notes on his side comments because theyll show up on exams. Its really truly not as bad as everyone says.

If you have to take American Heritage, take it from Dr. Kimball. He has good lectures, and as long as you do ALL the readings and study, you can do fine in this class. Doing the readings and studying for tests is VITAL.
Lectures can be a bit boring but he explains concepts well, has the least amount of HW from the A HTG professors to my knowledge, and looks like Thanos. Definitely take it from Kimball if you can.

Kimball is great but the exams were horrible. I would spend hours going to the review room, attend all lectures, study the readings every week and take notes, go to the lab, and still fail the exam. This class ruined my mental health since I stay up for hours every night studying and putting in so much effort for it not to reflect on my grade..

I loved Professor Kimball as a person but I feel like he was intentionally making the class harder than it needed to be. The content is really interesting and I liked most of the readings but the tests were significantly harder than the quizzes or anything. Definitely do all the readings and show up to class. Also pay close attention to film clips.

This course gets alot of flack, but I would 100% recommend it from Professor Kimball. You have weekly TA labs, so your TA determines alot of your experience too, but Professor Kimball did a great job of being engaging and tackling political and historical content sensitively. His lectures are actually pretty engaging.
This is a very reading-heavy class. Make sure to do the readings and study a lot otherwise you won't get the grade that you want. Professor Kimball is wonderful and very interesting in lecture.

Dr. Kimball was really great at teaching and making lectures interesting. I really recommend him for an overall AHTG course, but the rest of it really depends on your TA.
