The tests are hard and you really have to know your stuff, there's a ton of readings, and the lab quizzes aren't that easy either. This course is just unnecessarily difficult.

I really enjoyed taking AHeritage from Dr. Kimball. The course is super interesting and different form any other USHist class I had taken before. The assignments are straightforward and super important. The weekly quizzes were always harder than I expected and you really need to study for tests. Know the material inside and out! Take Dr. Kimball!

I LOVE prof. Kimball. He is so funny and makes America Heritage enjoyable. I have heard from others that he is better than the other A.H teachers. I actually enjoyed the class because he showed videos and had good lectures and threw in bits of humor. 10/10 recommend taking American Heritage from him!

Dr. Kimball is one of the best History professors I have ever taken. Although you mainly talk to the TAs, he cares about his students. To do well in this class you need to take notes in lecture and need to read the textbook. The review lab in the library is also very helpful. Don't be scared of ATHG, there is so many rescources! Take from Kimball!!

You know exactly what is expected in class, so there are no surprises. His tests and essays are reasonable. You will have to read a good 3 books front to back in his class, but they are really interesting. Dr. Kimball is hilarious, and he loves helping students outside of class. Pretty relaxed, low key style of lecture because of small class size.

I had Kimball for my history of sports class and it has been my favorite class ever at BYU. The lectures were engaging and fascinating. There is a lot of reading, but the readings were actually interesting! Honestly, he's a great professor who really loves the subject matter (also, he's hilarious). 10/10 would recommend this class from him.

If you like dry humor, this is your guy. Absolutely hilarious. I can totally see why its not some people's thing. But for me, I am constantly chuckling in class. Tons of reading but its frontloaded. Intellectually engaging. Would recommend to any upper-level history major.

I cannot recommend taking AH from Dr Kimball anymore! I was terrified to take this class and it was just fine with him. You LITERALLY have about 1/5 of the reading of most AH classes. He makes lectures easy, you have very few assignments, his tests are the easiest. The rest depends on your TA's grading style. TAKE IT FROM KIMBALL, I PROMISE!!

I loved this class. It is not as hard as everyone says if you work for it. Kimball is great. He's funny and the lectures are amazing. It has been one of my favorites. You must come to class and read the textbook. He will test you on anything that he says. There are two short essays. There is some reading, but not a ton. Take this from Kimball.

This class was not as bad as I have heard but everything was vague on grading and the tests were also very vague. You definitely need to read the textbook or there really is no way to do well. Doctor Kimball's lectures also sometimes goes over random things on the test so take good notes. Overall, I would have honestly preferred another professor.

I was nervous to take American Heritage, but it's my favorite class so far. Kimball's lectures are great; he includes movie clips to keep you interested and help you remember concepts. He's funny, too. Make sure you read the textbook or you won't do well on quizzes.

So he did require a lot of reading (about 100 pages a week) for class, but honestly, I got an A by literally just paying attention to the lectures. I wasn't the most excited for this class, but he brought up some interesting questions and was very passionate.

Very knowledgeable and passionate about literature and the humanities. Helps you relate to "classic" literature more than you would otherwise by helping you determine where you stand on controversial issues and world politics.

Lectures with Dr. Kimball were fairly entertaining and insightful, however, the grading criteria was very vague. No study guides or grading rubrics for essays. I felt like I kind of had to guess how to get a good grade most of the time. Questions from Dr. Kimball can be very specific to lecture. If you don't take good notes, don't take this class!

I was terrified to take this class, but I loved it.  Kimball was awesome, I loved his humor and his lectures are extremely straightforward.  If you do your best, your guaranteed at least to pass.  Fair and helpful teacher.  I had a great experience.  I'm glad I took it with Kimball.
Professor Kimball's lectures are very straightforward and easy to understand. If you've ever taken any sort of US History class before, this class is a breeze as long as you do the readings.

Professor Kimball was one of the least interesting professors I have ever had. His lectures were very boring and not clear AT ALL. It was very unclear what we had to learn for the tests, which were basically just memorizing random things he said in class one time. Do not take this class if you aren't willing to literally spend ALL of your time.
The material covered in lecture is not enough,  it must be supplemented by good reading of the textbook.

The lectures were presented well and for the most part I enjoyed going to class.  Everything depends on who your TA is.  They grade the papers and administer the quizzes.  My TA wasn't great but the class was manageable, not as bad as its reputation.

This class was kind of a joke. Class is just dry lecture and discussion. You could almost learn everything we talked about in class from Wikipedia. Some of the books were interesting, but overall there is a ton of unnecessary reading. I enjoy sports, but the structure of the class make it a chore.

Loved Dr. Kimball. His lectures were entertaining and it was easy to take notes. Study the lecture notes and key terms from the book for the tests. The essays sucked though and it was almost always impossible to make an argument within the word limit. Not hard to get an A though because the class is curved in the end (not sure by how much though).
It's a difficult class no matter who you take it from. Kimball's lectures are pretty entertaining. To do well you NEED to do all the readings. He also requires 10 hours of service.

Grading in this class is a little tough, they expect a lot out of their students.  However Dr Kimbal really does care about how his students do.  There are MANY resources available just make sure you use them.  He tries to make them interesting so pay attention and show up and you should do fine. Not a simple course but a good one and he's great!

Kimball is an okay test. His lectures are kind of boring, especially because he tries so hard to be funny. He's not the most clear prof, but the class is okay. It really just depends on which TA you get - you need an easy one to get an A. I probably won't take from him again.

Kimball is very funny and interesting to listen to. The textbook is used extensively, and reading is mandatory for quizzes and tests. The review room is free and proved to be very helpful for me. I've heard that Pope's class had to do way more reading than we did...

Whoever gets Kimball when he teaches this class again is lucky! I had heard horror stories about this class, but Kimball made it as enjoyable and easy to understand as possible. Our class did MUCH better than the other class- he's a good teacher- but study and pay attention and you'll be fine! He generally cares about his students too.

Dr Kimball's lectures are pretty entertaining and good and all that, but sometimes it seems like he is trying too hard to be funny. His powerpoints are worded vaguely which bugged me. His tests are pretty subjective but I heard every American Heritage class is like that. We only had to do two essays and then 10 service hours. Two midterms and final

I dunno why American Heritage gets such a bad rep...Maybe it's just Kimball who made it bearable! His lectures are very clear, just not terribly exciting at times. Do the readings and pay attention and this class is a breeze.

First of all, that picture of Dr. Kimball is hilarious, doesn't really look like him. Second of all, he is a very fun lecturer. He has the voice of Kronk mixed with Jim Gaffigan. This class was really easy, just do the readings and study your notes and you will ace the tests. The TAs are also very helpful in the review room.
I really liked Dr. Kimball! Class is interesting and has variety. The tests were difficult so take advantage of the review room!

Phenomenal professor. The TAs grade everything, not him, but he prepares you very well for the essays, quizzes, and tests. His lectures are consistently engaging, though you won't necessarily care about the material after the course is over. Overall highly recommend him for American Heritage.

Dr. Kimball is a good professor.  Lectures are broken up by his sense of humor.  He is a nice professor, and does a good job explaining things to us.  I didn't like my TA though.  He graded things really harshly.  But the professor is a really great guy, and a decent teacher.

American Heritage gets a really bad rap for being an impossible GE, and I have no idea why. If you do the reading (30 pages of easy textbook reading tops each week) the weekly quizzes are a breeze. Kimball's definitely a funny, entertaining guy and he makes the class interesting. Do your work and it's a fun and pretty easy GE!

He's a HILARIOUS teacher. Such interesting lectures. Reading the book will help when it comes to quizzes (these depend only on your TA, not on him). TA's are really the key to whether or not you have a good grade and that's just luck, but for a professor who only does lectures, he's the BEST. A boring topic but a captivating teacher. TAKE HIM.

I am not a huge history person but I loved this class!! Attend lectures because everything is test material and go to the review room weekly. I had an awesome TA which helped. Read the text book because this is more than just memorizing. Hilarious man who is willing to help!! Definitely  take Kimball for this GE.
Great lectures. Dr. Kimball is funny and interesting and I really felt liked I learned in his class.

Professor Kimball's lectures were very good!  I didn't mind his lectures, but the grading of assignments and the whole set up of American Heritage is horrible.  Because you have to take American Heritage, hope you get Professor Kimball.

Yes this class may be difficult. I heard how bad this class is but people give it a bad rep. If you go in with a good attitude you'll be fine. You have to apply what you learn so its more that just memorizing. Easiest was to study is to connect the lectures with your lab and also with the TA review lab then look at the book.
A ton of work is involved in this class with hardly any pay off. It's impossible to get an A. But with that being said, his lectures are extremely interesting and I learned a lot.

Worst professor ever! If you do the work, you can get a B, but it is absolutely impossible to get an A, as his philosophy is that there is always room for improvement. Even when I went into him and the TA I wouldn't get an A on a paper. Crazy guy.

By far your best bet for a great experience. This class isn't easy, but he definitely makes it enjoyable. Reflective paragragh on reading every class, and a HUGE paper. His grading is VERY fair, just make sure you take each assignment seriously and follow the guidelines he gives you. Great teacher that doesn't destroy your GPA

I thought Dr. Kimball was great. His lectures are funny and entertaining and usually pretty clear. His tests are easy if you prepare well for them. The class is interesting and you can tell he cares about his students and the subject.

Kimball isn't the best professor, but he does try. His lectures are boring and easy to fall asleep in, but he does add dry humour here and there in an attempt to make things more interesting. On the papers, if you write in a view contrary to his, he will not give you a grade higher than 80%. Reading is also required, especially for essays

I thought Dr. Kimball was kinda funny, although most did not. He is a good teacher, but the class is flawed from the start. I was getting As and Bs all year for the class but then got a D on the final. nothing prepares you for that. He didnt teach me anything i didnt learn in high school, but he is the better American Heritage teacher of the two

This class was hard BUT Professor Kimball was very entertaining & he explained things well. Loved his class, Hated his tests! Going to Review sessions with TA's & doing well on reading quizes are important to pass the class. Books not really needed. but packet is a must.

Lectures were fun and interesting. Pay attention to video clips, which will have a couple questions on tests. Make sure you do the reading and you will be fine. TA reviews were helpful. It's really not as bad as everyone says if you do the reading and study.

I. Freakin. Hated. This. Class. I passed... barely. He was probably the best professor, from what I heard. The class is just a killer though, no matter who you take it from. Unless you're a history freak. Lectures made sense, but the midterms were waaay ridiculous and difficult. Not just memorization. Go to the lab, TAs are willing to help. Blah.

This class is hard, no matter who you take it from. Kimball makes lectures fun, interesting, and helpful. He is very willing to help you outside of class. The tests were not extremely difficult, except for the final which was terrible.

i found the lectures really interesting, hard tests though, go to the review room, it really helps!! Luckily i had the best TA though, sadly he this was his last semester so good luck! All the TA's are really helpful in the review room, if you go there every other day for the short overview of the lecture and ask questions you'll be fine :D

This class is terrible, the TA's were useless. BUT! Kimball is  the best American Heritage professor. I actually enjoyed lectures, he was interesting and hilarious. He is a good guy who is really pretty funny.

Professor Kimball keeps the class interesting and ties in some jokes here an there. By talking to other students, I've found that he has less reading assignments than other ahtg professors. You still learn a ton, and the tests are hard. I still would recommend him over the other professors because you learn so much but don't have quite as much hw.

American Heritage is going to be hard no matter who you take it from.  That said, Kimball is a great professor, and his lectures are genuinely interesting.  The only points in the class come from weekly quizzes, a couple essays, and the tests.  Not easy to get an A in.
He's a good teacher and nice, but the class is pretty hard. Easier compared to the other AHTG classes though. Go to the Review Room.

Loved going to class. I felt like the tests weren't what he said they'd be though. He said they would be mostly conceptual but I found that the second test had a lot of random facts that didn't seem important. Overall I liked the class and Dr. Kimball is awesome.

Not as difficult as everyone makes it out to be. I got an A in this class. to do well on those "impossible" tests just study your notes along side your book. Great lectures and really knows his stuff. The tests are relatively fair, but the final was difficult. Use the review room if you suck at history
Kimball is awesome! It is true that the material that you cover and read is not really what the tests are about. The class is brutal, but Kimball makes the lectures fun and entertaining.

Professor Kimball is hilarious and brilliant. He always made class interesting, but lectures are mandatory if you want to do well on the tests. Book reading is pretty much optional..but I found that it helps a lot with the quizzes. I loved Kimball though!

okay here's the deal. You will learn a lot of interesting stuff, stuff that will never be on your tests. I could never figure out how to study for this class. Quizzes are fine, just read. Essays are fine too. Tests are a totally different story. I still got a B, but how I did is still unknown. Buena Suerte my good fellow students.

Professor Kimball is really funny. His lectures are pretty interesting. There are quizzes every week in lab that aren't bad as long as you do the reading. There are three papers that are pretty easy. The tests are impossible, so study hard even though you probably wont do that good. Go to class, do well on the quizzes and papers, and you'll be fine

Dr. Kimball is a really good professor as long as you read the book.  Weekly quizzes in lab and 3 tests which are mostly lecture material.  A couple of papers that aren't too bad but otherwise, a pretty easy class!
This class is pretty simple. Read the book and it will all be well. I never used the review room (except to get papers looked at) and I did really well.

Dr. Kimball is a great teacher! He is interesting and engaging in his lectures. He does several object lessons in class that are really helpful. My advice: go to the American Heritage Review Room on a weekly basis! It is extremely helpful. Go to class and study. Test and quizzes challenge you but aren't impossible. Dr. Kimball is the best choice.
Prof. Kimball is a great lecturer. He has a unique sense of humor that is very fun. His tests are all MC and he teaches from the book. Go to TA lab and you'll be fine.

Powerpoints were not clear. He doesn't put enough details into his powerpoints and he doesn't post powerpoints online so dont miss class. Had to get help from TA's a LOT! Tests were INSANELY HARD! In my opinion the tests were unfair because he plays the "two answers are right, but one is better" game. To be honest, it's my least favorite class...

My favorite professor at BYU so far! Let me point out that I am a very average student, I'm not stupid, but no one would ever call me a genius. He was super clear to me and has fabulous video clips every lecture that really helped me get the point. As long as you go to any review your TA has and put in a decent amount of study time you'll be fine.
Amazing class.  His choice in books was excellent.  Tough tests, but I learned a ton!

Horrible class. If you can think logically, you won't like this class. Tests are ridiculously hard and questions are biased. When reviewing your test all the TAs will tell you, "You should infer that from the textbook." When you read through your textbook, it is nowhere close to what was on the test. Professor is VERY liberal and pushes his agenda
Great teacher, loved him.  Very articulate and was always available for the students.  The tests were really rough.

Kimball is a great teacher, although he is a little intimidating. American Heritage is not as bad as everyone says. Just make sure you listen, take good notes, study hard and read the text. The review room is very helpful. I got an A. Those who complain how hard it is are those who put off reading, don't listen or freak themselves out about tests.

My favorite professor of the semester! Dr. Kimball is really funny, and I found his lectures extremely helpful. I would (and do) tell anyone to take American Heritage from him if they can. He is hilarious, but class was still extremely productive. This class isn't easy, but if you study and keep up on the reading you'll do fine.

horrible...he tried too hard to be funny and failed completely...his teaching style might be relevant for some but it put me to sleep because we accomplished virtually nothing in class. DO NOT take from him. a good TA is pretty much the only hope you have of succeeding

The rumors are true; American Heritage is in no way an "easy" class. You must understand the concepts taught in class, but Professor Kimball teaches them in a way that students can understand. He uses object lessons, and he encourages questions. You must study outside of class to do good. Also, having a good TA can make all the difference.
Dr. Kimball is HILARIOUS!  I loved his class!  He's easy to follow and he makes class interesting :).

Ridiculous.  his lectures were weird, and sometimes a little offensive.  He wasted time trying to be funny and it was really hard comprehending anything that came out of his mouth.  his tests are stupid.  they are so hard.  I only learned from the review sessions.  i just did not think he was very good at teaching...

The lectures were entertaining.  He does a good job of keeping you interested.  The tests are impossible.  But I think you will find that with all the American Heritage classes.  I'd take it from him just so you can survive the lectures.

Dr. Kimball is awesome! He is so funny, and he makes sure to explain everything really well. I enjoyed his class a lot, even though the tests were hard. He makes sure to explain every concept thoroughly and he's very open to questions. Great class, I would definitely recommend him as a teacher.

Kimball's classes are interesting and fun to attend; he makes a lot of jokes. I do have a roommate that hates that, so if you're not into that, don't take him. He makes the information relatable with good examples and media clips. By the nature of the class, the tests are hard but if you take good notes from the book and lecture, you should be fine

It was a relief to have a teacher who was more moderate than conservative. The class was interesting overall. Kimball's lectures were funny. The TA lab was good, depending on your TA. The tests were hard and tricky though. Studying is mandatory.

I took almost every class Dr. Kimball teaches because he made everything interesting, applicable, and yes--enjoyable.  He does not give an easy A, but he does make striving for one as interesting and fun as possible.  He brings out the best in students, and we love him for it.
Class was interesting and he was a nice guy. Moderate politically which was refreshing. Tests were hard but the curve straightened out grades. I would recommend him.

Professor Kimball is very good. His jokes and media clips break up the monotony of lecture. He knows his history. The tests are not bad AS LONG AS YOU STUDY, but have a few subjective questions each. Some lame lazy people complain about the class and how hard it is but they don't study. Weekly quizzes come straight from the readings. Take Kimball.

Kimball is a great professor. He makes the class very interesting and enjoyable...take lots and lots of notes and pay attention, and you'll be good to go! You have to take the class, so take it from Kimball

Dr. Kimball has very interesting lectures and I felt that I learned a lot from the class.  However, his tests are ridiculously subjective. On most questions you have to think, "What does Dr. Kimball want me to think that he's thinking that I'm thinking that he's thinking?".  The verbiage on the tests will trip you up.

I never read the textbook, but attended all the labs and lectures. The quizzes at the labs are easy if you read the textbook. The tests are tricky and I love history, but when the answer choices go up to j that's a bit ridiculous. It's a GE.

This class is pretty difficult. Tests are incredibly hard, but they get a little easier throughout the semester. Grades are based on a curve,so your 58 on a test will probably end up being a B. Read before lecture, and take lots of notes on the lectures and you should be able to pull at least a B.

This is a tough class but not impossible. If you take notes and do all the reading you will be fine. The review room is also available, I didn't need it but it was there to help. Dr Kimball keeps his lectures upbeat, a lot of video clips keep it interesting. Not a real heavy work load just weekly reading and a couple essays. Tests are challenging.
this class is sooooo hard! if you think you're ready for the test, you're not. start studying way ahead of time and make sure to do the readings for the quiz,also a good TA can make a big difference!

Lecture is fun and you learn a lot.  But I'll be honest.  I am not a freshman, and I am on scholarship-I am not an idiot. But this course was the bane of my existence. I studied for hours and got 50% scores on tests...and that was above average. It's a 100 level class!  I think there is a problem with the course.  But the teacher and TAs are great!

I did not miss a single lecture all semester. Funny thing is I didn't learn a thing from him. All he did for his lectures was go through a PowerPoint during which there were a lot of awkward silences. Thinks he is pretty funny, but he's really not if you think about it. Tests are TOUGH with averages around 55-60%. Try someone else.

Bro Kimball is very entertaining and his lectures are interesting and clear. His tests are pretty difficult however...you MUST know the material thoroughly to do well on them. If you can handle a challenge, then Kimball's a good choice.
way hilarious. way smart. and sometimes even inspirint :)
He's very entertaining.  The tests suck and don't truly show your comprehensive understanding of the course but lectures were fun.
Kimball was an awesome professor. Just go to class and take good notes and study and you will do fine in his class.

excellent teacher. lectures were always interesting, tests were very fair. TA was helpful, but I think I would have just as fine with a crappy one. some people think this class is really hard. it's not. if you do the reading and take good notes in lecture, an A is very possible. previous experience with the material helps, ex. ap gov and ap econ

SUPER hard class, study time for tests run about 5 hours. No joke. He's pretty entertaining as a lecturer, but my TA graded really hard on the essays and the average test score was about a 60%. This class is insanely hard. Unrealistically so.

Dr. Kimball is the best professor I have had at BYU. His lectures are interesting, he tries to keep the readings interesting, and he encourages questions and discussion. He is extremely helpful if you go to his office. Sports history was different than I expected, but definitely worth it.

The lectures were fun, but the tests were ridiculous. If year after year students average a score of 60%, it is not a well-written test. Also, my TA was terrible. A good TA can make all the difference!

He is a very interesting teacher and is great to listen to for lecture. The textbook is necessary, especially when studying for tests but he gives you a study guide that really helps if you're willing to put in a little time.
mmm

The class was somewhat of a disappointment for me. Dr. Kimball is very funny, but the class left me unsatisfied in learning. The midterm and final were both 95% based on the textbook; class time was almost a waste. The chapters in the book are too long to read completely, so use a study group before tests. First midterm timed. No long papers.

good teacher, tries to lighten up the class. Plays the devil's advocate a little too much, leaving the impression that somehow socialism and communism are superior ideologies than liberty and capitalism.

Is Professor Kimball a commie? I swear the guy is out to convince his students that the USA isn't the greatest country in the world. This is BYU. We believe in God and Country. Not the propaganda of liberal profesors.
This was an interesting class. The writing assignments were graded a little strictly but that's what the class is for. The readings were great! Never a dull moment in class. Great discussions!

Very tough class, with very tough grading of writing, but that is what the class is about.  This class taken from any professor would easily have been very boring, but the readings that he chooses are very well written, and Professor Kimball is very entertaining. I went to talk to him several times and he was by far the most helpful professor.

Dr. Kimball is an amazing teacher!  He's a way funny guy and his classes are quite entertaining.  If you need to take 200, he's one of the best.  Not the easiest prof that I've ever had, but he definitely wants you to do well and does everything he can to help you.
I hate history but Kimball made this class one of the best experiences i've had at BYU!  I looked forward to every lecture and still apply what I learned in class.  Definitely worth taking!
The tests are hard, but I really always looked forward to coming to that class. He is very knowledgable and passionate about our history. I would definately recommend Dr. Kimball to anyone.

Hist 200 is a sucky class, but Kimball is great. I wouldn't take it from anyone else. He is really willing to help you in any way he can. He knows the class is hard, so he does his very best to help you survive and still get the skills you need. He is way funny and helps make the class less stressful.

Dr. Kimball rocks my world! I loved this class SO much. His lectures are totally interesting, entertaining, and inspiring. I could not wait for lecture every week. He makes you want to learn. I changed my major to history because of him. Take A Htg and take it from Dr. Kimball. Do the reading, take good notes, go to TA reviews, and you'll be fine.

American Heritage sucks, there is no doubt about it but since it's a GE there is no way out of it. However Prof. Kimball made it really enjoyable. His lectures were great, he's so funny and he kept me awake. The tests are hard, and really require a lot of work, it's also really helpful if you get a good TA. I feel like I learned a lot in his class

I enjoyed the class and the lectures.  Do your reading, go to your labs, set up study groups and you'll do fine.  Dr. Kimball is funny, spiritual, helpful, always willing to answer your questions, and able to make hard concepts easy to understand.  Take American Heritage from him and you'll be better off then others. It takes work, but this IS college after all.

The best lecturer I have had. Very funny; utilizes a lot of video clips to explain things; interesting material. I couldn't have hoped for better in professors. The key to getting a good grade in the class is simply being a good student; many do not do well because they are unprepared freshman. It will require effort!

Dr kimball is a smart guy but that is all. his tests ask alot of opinionated questions that dont make sense. his essays are knickpicked to have to include every little detail. im just glad i passed the class and will never have to take it again. i suggest taking the alternative to having to take american heritage with him

Prof. Kimball is a great lecturer! I loved going to class. Be prepared to take a lot of notes. The tests are hard- the multiple choice isn't too bad, but the essays and identification questions are killer. My TA was ok, the class was ok, but Professor Kimball and his lectures were great! I ended up with a B-. Not too bad.

If anyone watches Smallville and has a crush on Lex Luther, take Am. Heritage from Kimball! He not only looks very much like Lex, (especially at the distance which you'll be seeing him from) but he sounds a ton like him as he speaks too! He is way interesting and seems very smart. The tests were way hard, but I passed them, so they're doable.

Kimball was a fun guy. He made the class really interesting, but his tests are tricky. Multiple choice wasn't too bad, but the essays and ID questions require you to state every tiny little detail with exactness about every little thing or you get no points. Labs were ok, my TA wasn't the greatest. I'm pretty happy with my B.
Prof. Kimball is a great lecturer, but this class is very difficult. I always enjoyed the class, but the tests were extremly difficult.  Don't expect an A in this class.

Dr. Kimball was great. The lectures were interesting and worth attending. He is a funny and intelligent guy and is interested in your success. However, the class is difficult and the tests are hard. The final was pretty intense, but not impossible. This was a great class.

Dr. Kimball is funny and smart, and his lectures are very good.  However, American Heritage is just plain hard! The tests are difficult, but grades are on a curve.  Go to labs-it's easy points.  If you're going to take American Heritage I'd highly recommend Dr. Kimball.
Great teacher. Teaches well, funny, and makes class interesting. You do have to work though.
Professor Kimball was probably the best Professor I've had.  He is way awesome...hard class, but well worth it.
Dr. Kimball was as good as I would expect an American Heritage professor to be. The class wasn't amazing, but I really enjoyed it. I wouldn't see any reason to avoid Dr. Kimball in any way.

This a killer class!! The lectures are enjoyable and the labs are easy points, but the tests are tricky and hard! If you are going to take the class be ready for extremely hard tests! Dr. Kimball is a nice guy with a great sense of humor. He makes the lectures fun!

This class sucked.  The first two tests were pretty hard, but the final was ridiculously impossible.  My TA was horrible.  She didn't know how to teach if her life depended on it.  The lectures were ok, but overall... a horrible class.  I learned a lot though.  Don't take this class if you can help it.  Take Poly Sci or something else instead.

This was a great Class! The tests were hard, but luckly they are graded on a curve. Doctor Kimball is  a great teacher and really knows how to teach. Great class. However, if you get a bad TA, transfer to a different section as a bad TA can make the lab experience miserable.

Everybody has to take A Htg, so take it from Dr. Kimball.  Lectures are amazing!  But be warned, tests are hard.  Make sure you understand the concept behind the definitions.  Go to lecture, lab, and stay on top of the reading.  Make sure you understand the general concept of all his major points.

Captivating and inspiring lectures. It's all powerpoint with many movie clips to demonstrate his points. GREAT class...study, go to lab, read the book and you will do fine. His LECTURES are amazing and I found myself leaving inspired as a better, more loyal person! he is also REALLY HILARIOUS! Sold 12 doughnuts to a class of 800...that was funny!
Awesome, awesome professor.  Lectures were great and inspiring.  Very smart and funny. As with most classes, if you study you'll do well.

Dr.Kimball is awesome. i loved his lectures, very entertaining and interesting.i loved learning from him. the class is very reading intensiveand has 4-5 essays and service..study hard and you'll do ok.don't let the ta s scare you..good luck!
Awesome teacher, didn't think I would like this class but I did. Definitely need to study though, to do well.
Kimball is AMAZING!  If you need to take American Heritage... take it from no one else!  He makes the class enjoyable and entertaining, yet so insightful!
He is a really good teacher.  He cares that we all do well in the infamous American Heritage class.  I love going to lecture because of his witty comments and humor.  He knows his stuff.
Professor Kimball really makes boring stuff become interesting, and he relates it to our time with video clips and stuff, and i love that. funny guy too. great class
Professor Kimball makes history come alive, with his dry humor, insightful video clips, and interesting lectures. His class is now one of my favorites!

Prof. Kimball is such a great teacher. He makes the lectures so interesting. This class has been my favorite class, and I think a lot of it has to do with the way he teaches. The tests are hard, but just study a lot and you should be fine. My favorite class of all time!
I really enjoyed this class... he made is so personal and fun.. i would recommend him for any history class!

The subjuct is just a hard subject no matter what, yet Kimball does a good job in presenting the material and does cover everything that he puts on the test.  The class is hard, but kimball is a fair and good teacher.  His classes are very enjoyable, just be ready to study.

Kimball is one of my favorite teachers ever.He has a passion for what he does. I love the video clips he shows, because it really does help everyone understand better. And he is Hilarious!! I love his dry humor!! All of this makes him strikingly attractive, in a very Governmental Agent way (with the shaved head and dark rimmed glasses) Love him!!
Excelent teacher. He knows his topic and makes it interesting. You will have to work in his class, but it is well worth it.  I would highly recomend him for American Heritage or U.S. History

It's a shame that all of you people had to have Kimball for AHtg; large lectures and defined curriculum really are not his thing. I had him for a small history class on something he really loves and he's about the best you'll find at BYU or anywhere else, for that matter.
Awesome teacher. Very Funny and you learn a lot too.  You need to study, but nothing on the test is unexpected.

Killer tests. Amazing lectures!!! Fun teacher, makes history interesting. Mark Patterson was the BEST TA ever! I learned a lot from Prof. Kimball- but he'll be the first to admit its a very demanding class and should be a 400 level.

Great Professor. His lectures are great. The class is hard. The key is to take really good notes in class. I noticed that lectures were key. Also:study in groups. This is key.If you can get together in a small group and discuss the material, it makes it easier. This helped my roommate and I get A's.

The work for this class was ridiculous. He was not a very interesting teacher. He would often poke fun and tease the students. If I am in class, I am there to learn, not be bothered by a dumb teacher. He was definately not a great teacher. His tests were terrible. I do not recommend him at all!!!
Really hard class.  Kimball makes a boring subject kind of fun.  I learned a lot, studied at least 10 hours for each test, and only made a B.  This class is really hard.

He made the lectures fun and interesting so i never wanted to fall asleep. on the downside the test  were very hard i always felt like no matter how  hard i studied it never helped. i didn't think the book was any help at all, just kept you busy.

This class was ridiculous. The lectures were interesting but the busywork assigned was atrocious. The tests were more trivial and the grading procedures were unfair. Avoid this course and take the Econ Poly Sci option. The TA's are horrible for the course

Class was rewarding. It is a very hard class and really helps one dig deep into the Heritage of America. Proffesor Kimball's enthusiasm helps students get excited about the subject. The class is dang hard though no matter who you take it from.
Great lectures, but the tests are killer.  Lots of busy work in labs.
This was a very difficult class, but he made it a fun to take.

While the lectures were interesting and entertaining, I found the book to be poorly written and the tests to be abominably difficult, even after laborious and extensive study. There was a great deal of busywork.
Awesome teacher. He makes the lectures interesting and fun to go to. Great sense of humor.
He's funny and makes what would normally be a boring and stressful class interesting.
He's hot. He's sporty. He's leisurely. He's da bomb!
Good sense of humor, fair grader

She is so easy to work with and insightful about the music she teaches. Very organized but still expects you to be responsible for your playing. Practice is absolutely key. Her lessons were a bright spot in my week. I felt lucky to get to work with her.

Dr. Guymon is very kind and caring towards his students, but had a few hiccups in transitioning from Iowa to BYU. I disagree with the poor ratings, he is very willing to listen to student feedback as long as you are kind about it. Materials was tough and required lots of reading and practice to be prepared, but it's just a different type of class.

Dr Guymon is a caring professor who teaches a difficult subject well. He always makes sure to prepare you for the test, and is open to feedback. If you read before class and attend lectures you'll be fine. Great dude.

Dr. Guymon is a great professor. He loves what he teaches and you can tell he loved being at BYU. He is caring and wants his students to succeed. He is open to feedback and will do everything possible to ensure the best experience for the students. He explains things clearly and prepares you for success

Dr Guymon is a great person who is consistently seeking feedback on how to improve his class. The success of the students is very important to him, and if you read the textbook, you will be prepared for the tests.

Dr. Guymon gets a bad rap sometimes but it is not accurate. His teaching transition from the university of Iowa was rough at times but he is very willing to adjust and work with the class. I felt that I learned well and it was my easiest class this semester

There is no partial credit on code for tests.

All that matters on tests is the final answer, code itself is barely graded. (It's brutal)

Classes were borderline worthless, he doesn't type code, (only handwrites summaries) doesn't show syntax, and doesn't explain the why of code.

Handwriting is awful.

TA hours are the only reason I survived.

Since he'd never coded in python before being assigned to teach this class on it, tbh I was impressed that he made it work. There were some rough patches, but he had frequent office hours, was always willing to work through things with you, directly applied student feedback to improve, and humbly acknowledged mistakes. Can't ask for more than that!

He gives no partial credit on tests, which is crazy for a programming class. He is just lazy and doesn't want to look through your work. Also, he spends most of class talking unrelated topics and then posts 30 minute lecture videos for us to watch in order to cover all the material. The TA's taught the class once and did a better job than him.

This was his first semester teaching at BYU so there were for sure some hiccups, but overall Professor Guymon explains things in an understandable way and the homework load is very manageable. The tests sometimes ask for very specific details that can be frustrating, but overall the class wasn't bad and Professor Guymon teaches it well.

Don't take a class from Dr. Guymon. He takes off points for very minute things that weren't even on the exam keys he posted. He does class demonstrations that he then tests you on, but will not answer questions about them if you happen to miss class or are confused about the concept afterwards. Pop quizzes every other week that you cannot make-up.

Dr. Guymon is new to BYU from Iowa. He gives demonstrations that are cool, but expects you memorize small or minute details from them to quiz or test on. He grades like a middle school professor, and often seemed frustrated when asked about his grading policies, usually referring to his 26 years of experience that shaped them. Avoid him if possible

Dr. C is like the grandpa I don't have. He's so inspirational and kind above anything else. He really wants you to succeed and is so knowledgeable about everything he teaches. He goes out of his way to make learning fun and just loves the people in his classes. I'm excited to take another class from him next semester!
The assignments can seem kind of daunting at first, but Dr. Christenson isn't a harsh grader. Dr. Christenson is funny, caring, and smart.

Easily the most caring professor I've ever had. His was my favorite class from the last semester even though I didn't know what I was getting into. Class includes some essays, a research paper, and 3 tests (I think). If diving into learning headfirst scares you, don't take his class. But if you're hungry to learn something new, take it right now!!!

I enjoyed this class a lot. Dr. Christenson is super knowledgeable and passionate about everything and he encourages discussions which were my favorite part of the class. The papers are tough, I only got 100% on one and it is hard to tell what distinguishes 96 from 100. The 'required' reading is good, but it is ok if you miss it sometimes.

Other than the times he had 1-1 conversations with one student for half of the class, his lectures were passionate and interesting. TOO many essays, though. 3 per each of the 3 exams, 3 throughout the sem, and a 10-page. Exams are fine if you take good notes, but you have to write almost everything he says to get every details. Nice guy, though.

Professor Christenson is an absolute legend. His passion and sincerity for what he teaching is infectious, and he has this unique ability to make history come to life as he teaches. He is also the fastest grader ever - he genuinely had papers graded the day after they were turned in - and he grades pretty generously. One of the most iconic teachers

He is a great professor! He is very lecture heavy but they are very interesting. He is passionate about what he teaches and knows the material well. This entire class is 4 papers, 3 midterms, and a final so you have to make those assignments count. He cares about his students a lot.

I really enjoyed his class. He has an amazing knowledge of the material and this leads to some great in class discussions. He is a very fair grader, although there are a lot of papers. His tests are a bit difficult, but they are take home with open notes and book.

When I signed up for this class I thought I was going to be bored. I was totally wrong. This is one of my favorite classes that I have ever taken. Professor Christenson is so kind and caring! He moved due dates several times because he didn't want us to be overwhelmed. Tests are open note and class was so interesting! Take this class!

Allen is such a champ. He was super forgiving about grading and his lectures are super engaging. You don't have many chances to get good grades, so you've gotta make them count. How good of a writer you are will make or break your grade, but I'd tell anyone to take a class with him

Prof.Christenson is such a lenient grader and is really passionate about his teachings! He is super quirky and fun. His lectures are heavy but are always so interesting and you learn so much in this class. There is a 10 page research paper, but he gives us a month ahead of time to work on it. Definitely wouldn't mind taking another class from him!

If I could take him for all of my courses, I would! He's passionate which keeps the class interesting. All the assigned readings can usually be found online for free so you don't need to buy the packets. There's usually a youtube audiobook for most of the readings too which saves time if you like to multitask. They're life-changing it so read them!

He is my favorite professor at BYU! He is very knowledgeable about all different kinds of arts and his lectures are amazing. Graded by almost all essay assignments but is the most lenient grader I have ever seen. As long as you pay attention in lecture and take good notes, the exams are very straightforward. Overall, a super great, easy, and fun GE

Dr. Christenson is super knowledgeable with art. He is the most lenient grader I've seen. There is quite a bit of writing. Take copious notes on every sentence he breathes. Tests are long--but open note. He's a little quirky, but incredibly friendly.

Prof. Christenson is a great professor! He knows what he's talking about and his lectures are engaging. He writes the tests, so going to class is important. There are a few short papers and a long one at the end. Tests also include a lot of writing. But super fun and interesting class! He's a great professor and an easy grader! Recommend!

Loved this class and professor! His lectures are purely oral so be prepared to write down notes and you are only graded on essays and exams. The exams are a bit lengthy, but they are open note, and book. You don't necessarily have to do the readings, just show up with the book to class because you will read there and then discuss. 10/10

Professor Christenson was such a delight to take this GE from. His lectures were very engaging and you can tell he really loves the subjects he is teaching about. I feel like I learned a lot. Because of COVID all the tests were online and open book which was nice-they would be kind of hard if they weren't. Few assignments which were graded fair

I really enjoyed taking Professor Christenson's class. Humanities is not my best subject, but I felt that he really cared about my experience. His lectures are entertaining and he is so knowledgeable. I loved his class, but if I would have taken it not during covid, I think his tests would have kicked my trash. During covid they were all open note

Prof. Christenson is my favorite professor so far! I took both IHUM 261 and IHUM 262 from him. Both were difficult classes and the exams took me about 2-3 hours each. Read the readings, take good notes in class, and just enjoy his passion for humanities! The class covered all the humanities (ex: arts, music, architecture, literature, etc). TAKE IT!

Dr. Christenson is extremely brilliant and knowledgeable. He is a great, caring and spiritual professor who cares about his students. Attendance is not mandatory, but he provides everything you need for the test in class so you need to go every day. I am a science major and ended up loving this class.

This is my favorite professor at BYU. He is hilarious, and his passion for what he teaches is infectious. I learned so much this semester. He makes the cultures of the past come to life. There are a lot of papers, but the subjects are interesting to write about. You will love this class even if you don't find paintings and architecture interesting.

I've taken several classes from him and his classes are structured the same way. Material is based on lecture (he assigns outside reading but the in-class discussion is what's really important). Although attendance isn't part of your grade, if you don't attend class, you won't get the material! (Getting notes isn't always helpful out of context.)

Professor Christenson's passion for the arts is totally infectious! He helps you look at art and the humanities in a totally different way. He seriously cares about his students and he is the sweetest, funniest person! His life is ridiculously awesome (ask about him being a shaman!). If you can take his class, do it! Esp. Modern Art/Victorian

I love him!! His class is very doable. There are 4 short papers and a 10 page paper. 2 midterms and final. The class is fun and I learned a lot of interesting things. Pretty easy and fair GE. Dr. Christenson is very sweet and nice. He has interesting class discussions too. Make sure to attend class though, as he says specific things for exams.

Dr. Christenson is FANTASTIC. I also took his Maya art class (highly recommend! So interesting) and I loved both classes from him. He's funny and seriously smart. His exams can be difficult, but taking his class is worth it.

Christenson is far and away my favorite professor at BYU. He's funny, quirky, SUPER knowledgeable, and always has a good story to share. This class was what led me to major in IHUM, and it's definitely doable if you're just looking for a GE. As much as I loved the class, I didn't go to half of them and I still got an A. Definitely take this class!!

This is a very doable GE; I was not originally interested in humanities at all  but Professor Christenson made the class interesting. His tests are so long (you have to write 3 essays plus other mc questions) but the reviews prepare you for them very well. There's a 10 page paper at the end, but this class wasn't hard overall; I would take it again

NOT recommended if you fall asleep easily in history classes or if you are not interested in architecture or paintings. The class is not THAT hard,  all memorization as far as tests and quizzes, something that bugged me was that he cared about spelling. I enjoyed it, but the exams took me 3 hours because of the we had to write multiple essays.

His lectures were very in-depth, and all of the exams and papers focused on these lectures. You use the textbooks and other assigned readings for support in your essays, but other than that, everything you have to learn is taught directly to you. Take a lot of notes in his class and pay attention to the powerpoints he puts on learning suite.
I took this course as a GE and actually loved it. Professor Christenson really knows the material and I enjoyed sitting in his lectures. He grades fairly easily and only gave a few assignments.

Christenson is a good professor. You look at paintings and he asks "how does this make you feel?". If you enjoy that, you'll love this class and Dr. Christenson. If you don't like that, this class will be miserable, but at least Dr. Christenson doesn't grade hard at all.
Amazing teacher, extremely knowledgeable. His tests are fair and he is an all around great guy. I would take a class form him again.
Really good, enjoyable teacher. Material is interesting and he tells awesome stories. Tests are straight forward and easy. Never cracked open the textbook.
He is super kind and a bit of a genius. He knows so much, is so interesting. He is really good at helping you, but he gives you a challenge.

IHUM 490R  ARTHC 382. I've taken his IHUM 260 (not that fun) & IHUM 390R (quite fun). His lectures are interesting, supplemented by personal anecdotes from visiting monuments and etc. Very knowledgeable and funny. Not arrogant at all. Papers are reasonable, tests can be a little hard, so STUDY. If you participate, ask questions, it's so worth it!!

Do the readings, but a relatively easy class otherwise. Christenson is incredibly knowledgeable, and the stories he shares in class about himself or an author/painter we're discussing really help give students context. He doesn't really use Learning Suite, but he's good about sticking to the printed syllabus schedule. It's really NOT a bad class!!

Dr. Christensen is THE most interesting man you will ever meet. He knows every little detail of every subject, but never is condescending or rude about it. He's definitely one of my favorite teachers ever. He is the sweetest and fairest man and will help you understand. I don't like humanities but he changed my perspective completely. He's AMAZING.

I loved this class. Every day I came out of it feeling renewed. He knows a lot of fun facts about the artists, writers, and historical figures, and the discussions are always awesome. The tests are relatively easy, and you never learn anything superfluous.

His very name makes me cringe. Undoubtedly the WORST professor I've had at BYU.  Unstructured lectures, makes erroneous statements that differ from assigned reading and then belittles students who question him. Grading is subjective with no explanation for marking down. So full of himself it is obvious that he teaches just to hear himself talk.

Dr Christensen's class provided lots of discussion and lectures that were pertinent and clear.  I thought he was kind of impersonal though and I wasn't very comfortable asking for clarification on assignments, etc.  Not very interested in his undergrad students but does a great job presenting the material in a compelling way.

I wasn't really excited to take this class, but it is now one of my favorites.  Everyone should take a class from Dr. Christenson!  He really loves what he teaches and knows a lot.  He always listens to the students' ideas.  He offers great insights not only about the Humanities, but about life in general.  Take his class if you get the chance!

LOVED this class. i really enjoyed the subject material. Christensen has lots of stories to make it interesting and the discussions are thought provoking. basically he is an awesome professor that has a TON of knowledge and is very interesting to listen to! i would take any of his classes

I had no interest in the subject before attending, nor is this my major. However, it has become among my favorite courses that I've taken at BYU. It all has to do with Dr. Christenson's style. He is an excellent teacher. He is not at all condescending or rude as other comments have suggested. If you want to be enlightened, his is the class to take.

He has been my favorite teacher on campus! His class isn't easy - but he knows so much about his feild. I didn't read the text books - I just skimmed them to write my papers. All Art History Majors should take this class!

This professor takes himself a little too seriously. He is very knowledgeable, and gives very interesting lectures. You have weekly papers that suck, tough midterms, and terrible slide quizzes (which I never passed in spite of studying). It was a good class, but it was very difficult.

The greatest teacher I have had at BYU.  He knew the most interesting information and taught extremeily well - I could remember nearly everything he said.  He made sure you understood the points that would be most prevalent on the tests and was very fair.
Excellent teacher who loves what he teaches about

I don't like this teacher at all. He thinks he knows everything and treats the students like imbiciles. He's disrespectful to the students and often makes mistakes in his syllabus etc. I would not recommend him to anybody.

Professor Christenson will go down as one of my foavorite teachers. He is very genuine, passionate about what he teaches (he gave up dentistry to teach humanities), and fair with the students. He is inspiring. The reading is somewhat necessary if you want to put out some nice essays on the tests and the weekly papers. He made me want to do the work

I basically second the other good things people have said.  His expectations from the students are clear and there's not really tricky stuff on the tests.  It's pretty necessary to go to class. I missed one day and it messed me up a lot for that test.  His lectures are quite interesting and he doesn't grade essays and papers too terribly hard.

Christenson was a genuinely interesting teacher. His lessons were pretty thought provoking and made you want to do the homework. Sometimes it was a little unclear exactly what he wanted, but he was easy to talk to. I highly recommend this teacher. He's nice, he's interesting, and he's fair.

He is a pretty good teacher.  In 425 R there is a weekly one page single spaced paper, two tests and a term paper.  The lectures are interesting, he he is fairly engaging, although sometimes the tests have some questions that he has never gone over or even mentioned.  An A- is not too hard to pull off; an A is tough.  Overall a fun class.

Christenson did  great job. he is an excellent lecturer and I found the subject matter to be very interesting. the TA was so nice, and graded our weekly papers easily, and the tests were pretty predictable. If you thought about it, you could guess what essays would be on them. I recommend this class!
No Comments

He's a funny guy but I have had better hum teachers at BYU.  I don't know about the future, but the TA he has now does a terrible job grading.  There is lots of reading and you write a paper pretty much every week, so that kinda sucked.  It is still a great class and he isn't a bad choice.

Very interesting class.  I loved the interpretations and opinions that he had on all the works we studied.  It's sort of a hard class, requires lots of writing, but he's not too hard of a grader.  If you want to, you can learn a lot and do well.

Not a very compassionate or understanding professor. Reacted harshly when I came to him for help. Mandatory lectures that only spend about 10 minutes talking about the actual material. Little man syndrome.
Love this professor. Go to class study the slides and quizes and you will get a A.

Got A's on every test and quiz but does not accept university excused absences. If you are a student athlete only take if you are not in season or your grade is chopped at least a full letter from attendance. Ironic as he missed a lot of class to go sing.

Lectures can be a bit monotone but he is definitely passionate about what he has to say. The 3 tests that the grade is based are very easy, I missed class quite a bit and did just fine. No textbook, no mandatory attendance, no homework. Just an interesting and easy class!

If you want an easy class without homework - TAKE THIS CLASS.  You are graded on 3 exams, which is fabulous, but also he ONLY grades by his 3 exams.. so study hard. They aren't difficult - just study his slides and you'll be just fine

I LOVE this man. Great teacher. Loves what he teaches and loves WHO he teaches too. I was dying of morning sickness this semester and missed so many lectures and he was SO accommodating! Only grades are 3 tests and if you go to class and take notes, you'll do great on all of them. So attendance isn't mandatory but i STRONGLY recommend prioritizing!

I switched to him because I was struggling with another professor. He goes in depth on topics if you need some extra explanation to understand. I rarely went to class and am set to get an A. Tests are not too difficult and it's useful information to go over.

Taking this class from Parcell was the best choice I made last semester. You don't need the textbook, your grade is based on 3 tests, but the tests were easy. Take the easiest 1/2 of what you talk about in lecture and that is your test. His lectures are not very interactive but were pretty interesting. Best choice for Exercise Phys.

Easy A. Parcell isn't looking to trick you and knows this isn't your only class. There is no homework, your whole grade is based on 2 midterms and the final. The tests only took me about 30 min and were not difficult if you went to class and listened and took notes. Some people barely showed up for class and did ok, but if you want get an A, go!

Eh, wasn't impressed. I often questioned the purpose of this class, you don't cover much that isn't covered already in pdbio 305/362. Lectures were boring, I stopped going to class after the first 2 weeks and got an A. grade based entirely on just 3 tests, but they are very easy. take this class if you are looking for an easy A, not to learn.

3 test grades (including the final) are your score. If you're a good tester, you've got this. Personally not a fan. He's a nice guy but lectures are very dry, he lectures with a powerpoint the entire time, no student interaction.

Dr. Parcell's lectures are decent. He only had two tests and a final for grades which can be both good and bad. Good news is that the tests weren't tough at all. Definitely go to class, his tests cover things he talked about that aren't on the slides. Overall, not a bad class at all. I loved not having busy work.

He is a really good professor, but your grade is dependent on how well you do on the three tests that you have for the semester. He likes to explain things in very great detail, so you can catch up pretty quick if you miss a day or too. He is a funny guy and loves this topic so that is nice.

Dr. Parcell is an EXCELLENT professor.  I highly recommend taking a class from him, especially exercise physiology.  He's clear, interesting, and organized.  The work load is reasonable.  You take quizzes on the reading and 3 exams.
Dr. Parcell is awesome! He makes everything easier to understand and he always answers questions. His tests are based on the lectures so taking notes will definitely help you out.

DOES that make sense??  Yeah this was a fun class that was a more in depth review of pdbio 305 w/o all the digestion and repro sections.  Great teacher. Dry sense of humor but at least has a sense of humor

Great Professor. He really knows what he is talking about and he is pretty funny, kind of a dry humor. 2 mid terms, online quizzes every couple weeks, and a few assignments that are pretty easy. All I did was studied his power points and I did really well in the class. I would take this class from him again!

He's pretty good. He is extremely smart, but prob. needs to dumb it down a bit for the rest of us...minus those byu kids who live for school. The most helpful part is reviews from Dan (grad student). If you go to the reviews, study the powerpoints, & go to class you'll do fine.

Dr. Parcell is awesome. He is such a chill guy and willing to help. This class is easy, and you still learn. You don't have to go to class (lectures generally are not super exciting). I just studied the powerpoints and skimmed the text before exams and got high A's. There are only 3 tests involved (including the final). I would recommend him.

Dr. Parcell is a phenomenal lecturer, he takes time for your questions and he teaches in a way that is interesting and is crystal clear. He brings fascinating insights from studies into his lectures. Hes tests are not bad. You don't need the book. I missed about 1 class a week to go skiing and I was still fine. Study hard before tests and you'll :)

Good teacher. Would not recommend for EXSC 463. There are easier teachers(VERHRS). He uses powerpoint presentations and then puts them up on blackboard. Rare if he puts them up before class it seemed like. He is a graduate student teacher so some concepts are deep and I just lost interest a little. Overall = Okay.

Lectures were monotonous and unexciting at times however he was an extremely helpful prof and his quizzes and tests reflect exclusively what he mentions in lecture, there was really no need to purchase the textbook. It is a good idea to supplement his ppt. slides with what he says in class so definitely attend every lecture!

horrible teacher- quizzes are tough and over a short period of time on the weekend and very easy to forget. If you challenge him on a test or quiz question he becomes overly defensive and somewhat rude. He lacks compassion and his lectures are monotone and boring. No makeup quizzes and they count for a ton of your grade, don't buy the book

I don't know what these other people are talking about.  I loved this class and I thought Dr. Parcell did an EXCELLENT job making concepts and even more difficult topics clear.  He was always willing to help and he had a funny sense of humor.  Very good experience.

Most boring lectures I have ever attended.  He just gets up and mumbles for an hour.  Don't bother buying the book.  The tests are not easy either and he has a major issue with you questioning him on a question.  He gets very defensive and insists that it is your mistake not his becuase his tests are perfect.  Take it from someone else.
alright teacher, but major little man syndrome.  As long as you act like he is great, then you are good.

Professor Brimhall knows what she's doing. She has been a medical Spanish interpreter for years and knew the answer to practically every question thrown her way. However, don't take as a filler class! You can't underestimate the amount of time you will spend on this class. She also required 6 volunteer hours as an interpreter which was hard.

I think she does a really good job with this class. Assignments are structured well to help you learn how to interpret. There is a lot to do out of class, but she doesn't grade super harshly as her main goal is to help you learn to interpret. Class discussions were usually purposeful and she's a very friendly prof.

I liked Allison. The class is good. My one major biff is that there was so much busy work. Nearly every weekday with some Saturdays had something due. Tbh, would have liked more vocab and specialty focus integrated (i.e. learn several new terms per specialty and not just a select few from the transcripts). Overall an okay class.

Since no one in our class is an interpreting major, it's tough because the practices are a VERY time-consuming. I have never had so much busy work. 10-12 hours of homework on a GOOD week. However, very helpful. Don't take as a filler. But, Profe Brimhall is a really sweet lady, and if you want to be come an interpreter, definitely take this class.

This is the worst course I have ever taken at BYU. Professor Kelley is virtually inaccessible to meet with, refuses to accept student accomodations even when mandated by the university, and grades like you personally offended her. The TAs are just as bad. The class either moves at the pace of a snail or far too rapidly for any sane person.

I took this class during Spring Term and definitely recommend it. It was a very easy class with lots of cooking, which made it fun and engaging. The workload was manageable and I enjoyed the class. One tip. I never used the textbook, so I would wait to buy it until you know you'll need it.
She is a great professor. However, don't think you can just float along in this class. There is a lot of reading to be done and the quizzes can be tough at times. But still so much fun and worth it!

I took Allissa's online blended Food Preparation in the Home course. She used canvas for her online assignments. Each week, we had to read a chunk of the textbook, watch some videos, and then take a quiz on the materials before going to the lab. Simple and straightforward, but also challenging in a good way. I learned a lot.
Does not care about her students and does not grade in a timely manner. Take this course from someone else!!

This class was super fun, and easy. Assignments and weekly lab instructions were clear, and easy to follow. Dr. Kelley was very kind and helpful, and easy to talk to. She and the TAs were always ready to help, and grading homework quickly. Exams were also super easy.
I had the class online, so I appreciated how clear rubrics were! As long as you are on schedule, the class  is one you can succeed in. Get ready to learn a lot! ;)

Professor Kelley is so nice! You can tell she really cares about her students and she takes time every class to get to know each person. She was organized and helpful. The class was fun and pretty easy. Definitely take it if you are looking for a friendly environment. Worked in groups of about 4 the whole semester. No cooking experience needed.

The labs were fun each week and there's only one quiz you have to do beforehand. It can be reading heavy, but if you're already familiar with food/cooking, you should be just fine and probably won't need to get the textbook.

Allissa is great but the class was a waste of time. The textbook is useless and the labs are really long. I felt like I was back in high school taking a food class. The TA's were fine but not much of a help either and they graded things way too harshly. Attendance is also completely mandatory with little to no wiggle room if you miss a lab.

Very down-to-earth and reasonable. The class had a predictable schedule that made it easy to plan ahead, and Professor Kelley had clear expectations. I honestly really liked this class. Except for the textbook- it kinda sucked but that's not her fault. The cooking assignments were so fun and low-key easy.

This course is largely put together by the sewing department and Professor Kelley is more of a steward than an instructor. She is super friendly and respectful, she answered a ton of my questions before the course began, and then when my TA didn't answer my email I ended up asking her the question and she was very clear and helpful.

I enjoyed this course! It was definitely a lot of work. The material itself was easy enough to learn, but be ready to sew all the time. Because it was an online class, I didn't ever meet Professor Kelly in person, but she was responsive to email. I learned a lot from this class. If you really want to learn how to sew, take this class.

Because this was an online course, my rating for this professor will probably be very different from those who had her in person, but I had a very difficult time with this class. Some of the resources were outdated or completely wrong, and in her bio she even mentions the wrong class. Only heard from her TAs (which were great).
Took SFL 185 from Prof. Kelley online. At one point I had to restart my entire project and I emailed her about it and she was super nice and gave me an extension which was really helpful!

This class is a ton of work and very time consuming. Professor Kelley is very responsive, and I learned a lot! I agree with some of the other student ratings that the online course needs better organization because the videos and assignment requirements were not always congruous, but Professor Kelley was great to work with when I noticed issues.

Class was super fun and easy to navigate! I was in the online section, and at times it was a little unclear what materials I would need for which week but other than that everything was straightforward. Its easy to get ahead if you want too.
She was awesome! I took this class online and loved it! It is super easy to get ahead! The assignments are chill and lowkey.

Blended class, with reading and a test before class each week, SUPER easy class. Honestly really fun, labs were easy and the food was good, Ta's were fun and played music during class so it was a good environment. Would deff take again and an easy fun credit to do with friends.

This professor is so sweet and this class taught me a lot of cool skills that I am excited to have and continue growing. This class was really hard for me though because it is SUCH a time commitment. Luckily the late policy is very forgiving and the professor and her TAs are very on top of it when it comes to feedback and grading.
This class is a lot of work, but I definitely learned a lot!

I've never met Professor Kelley because I took her online sewing class. The class was fun but very time-consuming and kind of expensive. There was a lot of content to learn very quickly, but I felt like it was explained well, and I learned a lot.

I have never met Professor Kelley as I took her online sewing class. This class was challenging and consumed a lot of time. The projects definitely force you to learn how to sew well fast. When we finished each part of the project, we had to take a video and show that we met each rubric criteria. It was nice to know what was expected of us.

Professor Kelley was an amazing instructor! However, if you are going to take this course, know that it is a huge time commitment. We had three projects, in addition to many smaller samples, unit quizzes, and some discussion posts. You really do learn a lot, but I would recommend taking it in person, as the online lectures were confusing.

I absolutely loved this class. It was my fav all semester. I did the online foods course and I genuinely feel more comfortable with cooking. It was one cooking assignment, reading and quiz each week which was very doable. I took videos of the quizzes and used those to help me study for the exams and I always did super well on them. Highly recommend
I truly loved the course Professor Kelly Taught,  she did an awesome job,  and graded fairly. It is a sewing class, and the rubric is clear and easy to follow.
I loved this class! Professor Kelley was amazing, and the class was very well organized. I highly recommend taking this class if you want to learn how to sew, you learn so many techniques!

This class was so fun! It was blended, so we only met once a week to do the cooking lab. Professor Kelley is very caring and does her best to help students succeed. The TAs in this class were so sweet and helpful! as well. The weekly quizzes are sometimes challenging because of all the reading, but this class was amazing!

Took her online sewing class. Was pretty difficult to follow the videos as many of the steps were said out of order. Grading is harsh for a begging sewing class and it took 15 hours to complete the assignments most weeks.
It's a lot of work but fun!

Professor Kelley is great and understanding! That being said this class is extremely time consuming especially if you take it in the spring or summer. Make sure you don't fall behind because the assignments pile up fast! If you can, I would recommend going to the lab because the TAs are a great help!

Overall, this class wasn't too bad. I actually loved learning, but make sure you have a machine or go to the lab! Some of the lectures were online and hard to understand, but the TAs are very helpful. Don't wait until the last minute to do the assignments, as they take a while and you need a sewing machine.

Took Basics of Clothing construction online with Professor Kelley. We didn't interact a lot, but she seemed like a good professor and provided a lot of resources for additional aid. Difficult class (15+ hours a week) but I learned a lot.

This class is pretty chill. She's a tough grader and the readings are insanely long, but overall it's one of the easier classes I've taken. Just make sure you turn everything in on time and you'll get an A. Tests are just questions from the quizzes and super easy.
Super challenging class even if you think you have sewing experience but it will teach you a lot

Taking this class during spring term is no joke - it goes quick! That being said, Professor Kelley was willing to work with me when I asked for help. The homework/sample assignments take a lot longer than you think they will. Some of the rubrics are a little unclear. The class was cool but time consuming. No complaints about Professor Kelley.

Professor Kelley is amazing, she was so kind to me during this term. I needed a lot of help, and she quickly met with me to discuss options to help me pass her class. With a lot going on in my life at the moment, her kindness was so needed. That being said, her class is no joke, get ready to learn at double speed!

Prof Kelley is great! She is super kind, fun and knowledgeable! The class was so fun but I didn't really learn too many new skills (but I've been cooking my whole life). You do have to attend the weekly labs, missing even one will really mess with your grade. The reading is a lot so I started to skim and did just fine! She is great and I recommend!

Took this online...it was still lots of fun! I enjoyed opportunities to try new recipes. Reading and quiz each week. Cooking assignment each week. Grading can be harsh at times, but as long as you follow the instructions you'll be fine. Fun class! Very doable!

Professor Kelley is so sweet! I took it as a blended course, so there's work online and one 2 hour lab a week. There was quite a bit of work for the online portion. Grading can be harsh at times and she's strict on sticking to the syllabus. Labs were fun and definitely where I learned the most, and you get one make-up for the whole semester.

Amazing class. Yes, lots of homework, but it's because there's a lot to learn about clothing construction. Professor Kelley was very understanding of an injury I had towards the end of the semester, and allowed me to turn in assignments after the due date because of this circumstance so I wouldn't drop out.  I was able to finish strong.

The teacher is great at communicating and sending out weekly emails to remind you what is due that week. She also is quick at responding to emails. TAs are very easy graders so as long as you do the assignments you'll do well. Prepare yourself to do A LOT of sewing. And you do need to study for tests to do well on them.

This course was awesome! Professor Kelley was very helpful whenever I had a question or concern. I took the course fully online. It wasn't incredibly difficult, but it was very time consuming so make sure to stay on top of projects. The instructions for all of the projects were very thorough and clear!

This class is VERY time consuming, but if you have a light course load I'd definitely recommend taking it as I learned so much. The TA's and the open sewing lab are so helpful, they made a huge difference in my experience.
