I did not interact much with Professor Kelley, mostly with her TA. But the class is VERY time-consuming. I would definitely take it again because I learned so much about sewing but be prepared to spend many many hours sewing each week.

This class is very time consuming. I wish I knew that ahead of time. It is a lot of work for a beginners course and taking it online added to the difficulty. I will say I did learn a lot and felt proud of what I made.
Prepare to set aside many hours for this class. I love how much I have learned from this course, but it has been a major time commitment.

This class took up a ton of my time when I thought it would be one of the easier classes on my schedule. I had to spend about 20-25 hours a week watching the videos, doing the readings, working through the samples, and working on the actual project. Some of the videos were really hard to understand and they sometimes didn't line up with the rubric.

I learned a lot in this class but I would say it was really fast pace. There was a lot of homework each week that will take you a while if you do not have experience with sewing. I was a beginner and homework took me anywhere from 2-6 hours a week to complete. The teacher is pretty particular with how you can submitt assignments as well.
Overall I enjoyed this class. The professor is great, the canvas organization was not so great, but still manageable. 9/10 recommend.
Great and super nice! The workload is quite a lot and is very very tedious.

Overall the class was good, i just struggled with the online formatting because it made it difficult to ask questions/get feedback. Also, the lectures/instruction videos weren't always clear/didn't always match the rubric. But professor kelley was really nice and she was very accommodating.

online so I didn't have much interaction with her, but she always sent out motivational emails every week and when I did reach out for help she was very kind and helpful. This specific class was a lot of work and definitely not a class you should take if you want something easy, but you'll learn a lot about sewing and get to make fun projects!
The class is arranged in a way that makes it easy to learn. This class claims to be a beginner class but if you are going in with no prior knowledge the online course could be challenging.

I feel like the course was organized very well. It is a very heavy course and I spent anywhere from 2-10 hours a week on our projects and samples. She is a tough grader, so don't get behind! The videos used are of other teachers though, so I don't feel like we actually interacted with her at all.

While the professor herself was very helpful, replies were slow from both her and TAs so it put me behind if I had questions. That being said, I would NOT recommend taking this class online. The course was very disorganized, had conflicting instructions between the rubric and the guidesheet for patterns, and lacked explanation on so many processes.

I am so happy I took this class because I learned so much. That being said, I would not recommend the online version of this course. its super fast paced with little assistance. That being said, the online TA's are very helpful it just takes time for them to get back to you which often put me behind.

She is so sweet and remembers your name very early on. She actually cares about you. Very clear expectations, and labs are basically always full credit if you show up and don't blow up the kitchen. Take this class if you're bad at cooking.

This class is very difficult for people who have no past sewing experience, but it is doable. There are videos to follow along, but some of them are hard to follow and skip parts of the creation. This class is SO time consuming, so make sure you have tons of time set aside to get assignments done. Overall, I do think I learned a lot from this class

Professor Kelley made an online sewing class really easy to follow along to! Each week you'll had different projects/parts of a project to do but they come with written instructions written and instructional videos which are super helpful! I felt like the grading was totally fair and they offered really great feedback if you don't get 100%. 2 tests

I really enjoyed her 185 sewing class. It was challenging because sewing clothes is new to me. However, they have really helpful step by step videos and pattern slides. The projects took me a lot of time, but grading was not harsh. The only down side was, the tests and quizzes were a little challenging. I would take from her again.

Unclear reading quizzes and does all-or-nothing grading. It was a lot of work for a two-credit, 100-level class. I liked the course itself and love baking and cooking. I just felt like the grading was dumb. I still got an A, but I was worried for a second, haha.

Allissa is so amazing and nice, but I would highly recommend not taking this class unless you already know how to sew. It said it was for beginners but it is not. But I took it as a term class so a semester class would be better. The class was hard and I worked my bum off for a mediocre grade, but she was kind to meet with me to when I asked.

The entire class was videos, so I never even talked to the professor. The videos were hastily made, extremely repetitive, and often didn't show what I needed to see. The professor was really helpful when I emailed her though.

There were never clear enough instructions and they often clashed with the rubric requirements. Everything was made more difficult than it had to be. Definitely don't take this unless you have some knowledge about sewing otherwise you'll be completely lost.
She is a great teacher but the class is formatted online which makes it a lot more difficult. She does a great job with a hard course! Expect a LOT of time spent outside of class.
I had Professor Kelley for an online class and I had a lot of fun! Being a semester term, it was also paced very fast and there was lots of homework each week. She is always open to helping out!

This class was way more difficult than it should have been. The organization was horrible and often the written instructions, video instructions and rubric all showed/asked for different things that rarely lined up. I spent many hours confused and frustrated with this class. This class is not an easy credit or summer class, I regretted taking it.

There was a lot of homework to do in a short period which made it hard. Granted I took this over the spring term, but compared to other spring term classes the workload was heavy. Didn't have a ton of interaction with the professor and mostly got feedback from the TAs who were helpful! The homework takes a lot of time if you haven't sewed before.
nothing against the professor, more against the class. I think there was too much due in too little time, but I guess it was an online class in spring semester, whomp whomp.
This class is an intro to sewing class but she graded so harshly. I put hours into each sample because I have never sewn before, and still got maked down.

I took SFL 185 online and it was a great class that helped me learn a lot that added onto the bit of sewing experience I had. There was a lot of homework that took more time than I liked. The class is set up with clear deadlines and good organization with help available.

I took this class during spring term, so it was a LOT of work in a short time but it was manageable. Overall, all the projects were easy and straight forward, and they had videos that showed how to make each project step by step. There was two midterms but there was a study guide provided that helped a lot.

Allissa was great! I love cooking and this gave me the opportunity to learn more about food and how to cook well. The workload was a lot for spring term but I imagine it would be much easier to take as a semester class. However, I learned a lot and gained a lot of new cooking experiences!

I loved this class. I learned so much that I will be able to use throughout my life. I took the online course and it made it so nice to be able to learn in my own kitchen. Follow the guidelines for the assignments and watch the lecture materials and it's an easy A. The exams come from the quizzes but beware they lock after you see the answers.

Basics in Clothing Construction is a challenging course with a lot of time spent on projects and samples. Such a great course. Because it was online, it could be difficult to figure out what to do and how to do it. Professor Kelley was willing to meet in person to go over questions, which I appreciated.

I took her beginner's sewing class online. There were prerecorded lectures, but whenever I needed help or had questions, she would response promptly and was very understanding and helpful! I learned a lot in the class and although there was a ton of homework, I'm so glad I took it! I have sewn a bit in the past, but I still learned a lot!

I took SFL 110 (food) and 185 (sewing). In both classes, you don't really hear much from her but when you do she's great. 110 was amazing! I had so much fun, TAKE IT! 185 was insane (it is set up to be the same for anyone teaching it) It's way too much work and you're graded harshly. (I knew how to sew but any other way than the BYU way is wrong.)

The class was a lot of work and sometimes the projects were hard to figure out, but I am going to be able to use the skills I learned in this class the rest of my life! The professor was super nice and very helpful, she is easy to work with and made the class more enjoyable.

I think Professor Kelley is a great professor, however, this class was just hard. I took SFL 185R-005 online which I don't recommend unless you have a lot of time on your hands at home and sewing experience. She was great at responding via email and her TAs were wonderful. Her weekly announcements with spiritual thoughts were also appreciated.

Due to the nature of the class, we only really heard from her from useful announcements. But she communicated quickly when you reached out. But the course layout was clear. Sadly the final practical was a little obtuse in how you turned it in but online classes are the way they are.
Allissa is super sweet and understanding.

I took this course online. The lectures were straightforward and so easy to follow. Great class if you want to start sewing or advance your skills. You do have to buy your own material for projects. I put difficulty in the middle because there is a lot of memorizing you have to do! But Professor Kelley is amazing.
This was such a great class and Allissa was such a great teacher.  If you want to improve your sewing skills (experienced or not) I would highly recommend this class.

Taking this class online with Prof. Kelley was pretty good. The grading for each sample you make is very clear on the rubric criteria, but it will really depend on your TA if they think you did it right or not. There's a quiz every week and things due about every wednesday and saturday. Not too bad, but deadlines are pretty strict.

I loved this class - the food we made was amazing and Allissa is super sweet! Pretty chill and fun environment to learn to cook in. At first I was nervous about the readings/videos we had to watch before each lab but it really wasn't too heavy of a workload, though it was more than I expected. I'd recommend both the class & taking it from Allissa!

Prof. Kelley is a really caring and considerate teacher. I loved this class (I really only took it to have an excuse to cook), and I really enjoyed it! If you do the online work before class and take the quiz, the cooking lab will be a breeze (so watch the demonstrations!!). Definitely take this even if you don't know how to cook.

Great teacher. The course was very straightforward. For the blended course, there was textbook reading and videos to watch followed by a short quiz before class each week. Highly recommend taking the course. No prior cooking experience is necessary. Just make sure to turn in assignments on time and not miss class.

Good teacher, no late work accepted so DO NOT MISS ASSIGNMENTS! Lots of reading/videos before class that you NEED to watch/read in order to get through class. If you turn things in and come prepared you'll be fine. My mistake was being late to turn stuff in.

I adored Professor Condie's class! You read a lot of short stories, but they were all interesting and we discussed them in class in a way that really helped me improve my writing. We only wrote 3 short stories throughout the semester, but we workshopped them and Professor Condie gives the most amazing feedback! Would 100% take again.

Professor Condie is the best! She helped me feel so much more confident about my writing and gives super helpful and constructive feedback. She also just cares so much, it was like we were all just learning from each other. Its a very comfortable environment and I genuinely enjoyed being in class.

I love Prof. Condie. She is a really good example of what all writing prof should be like. So kind, accessible, so good at getting grades back on time. Class is straightforward and instructions are clear. Daily writing, but duh, it's a writing class. You write 3 short stories that are workshopped, lead a discussion, daily readings w/ posts on ls.

Ally is so kind and supportive! I was blessed to be among her first students here at BYU. I highly recommend her if you aren't confident in your writing ability and want to try something new. She gives you lots of opportunities to learn and grow.

I LOVE ALLY. Her curriculum, teaching, and feedback took my writing to the next level. Everything we did in class and outside of class was incredibly helpful and allowed me to gain further insight into and passion for creative writing. Our class felt like a family. She is so cool. Not too harsh of a grader, and gives excellent and helpful feedback.
I really loved taking this class from Professor Condie. She is kind and respectful, funny and insightful. I would definitely recommend.

I loved taking a class from Professor Condie! She is an NYT Bestselling author of the Matched series, which is just one of the examples of how qualified she is to teach creative writing. I learned so much! Be aware there is a lot of assigned reading, but they are books and short stories so they are super fun to read. Amazing class!!
take this class!!

What stood out the most to me about this professor is his paragraphs of response to each of my assignments. While I disagreed with a few of his assignments, expectations, and responses, I am certain he does all with good intent. The work is fairly easy but the workload is much more than that of the typical 2-credit class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AS INDEPENDENT STUDY! Gaskill is maybe a good professor in person, but his independent study course was incredibly difficult. He is a very tough grader and nit-picks every minor detail. I wish I did not take this course.

Dr. Gaskill is super funny and very passionate about this topic. Lectures are fast-paced but informational. Be sure to read and answer questions closely and carefully. This class was really informative and also expanded my understanding of the world around me and its many cultures.

Incredible lecturer and educator! He's passionate, funny, insightful, so so knowledgeable. Taking World Religions with him has literally changed my life, I feel much more capable of understanding other people from different religious backgrounds. Beware that at some point he'll probably say something that offends you but you'll get over it.

He has a very dynamic teaching style and energy, which makes it very easy and often enjoyable to sit through his lectures (lots of interesting stories). For me, tests were a bit difficult, so make sure you really study! Also, he was a bit merciless with his syllabus (don't ask questions you shouldn't). The material is very interesting.

This is the best religion class at BYU. Dr. Gaskill is so entertaining, knowledgeable, insightful, and funny. If you want to build your testimony and be a better person, take this class. The quizzes are open note, but very detailed. The exams are simple if you've been in class paying attention. Take notes and come to class and you wont regret it.

He is amazing! Faith-promoting! Mind-blowing insights! Incredibly funny, but incredibly spiritual. I saw another review of him from the same class I was in. The student lied, saying he tries to convert you to other religions and his anti-female. Ridiculous! This was one of the most powerful experiences I've ever had in my life!

Professor Gaskill has been the most impactful professor I have had. This class has deepened my personal faith and widened my perspectives. He helped me better understand that this world is full of people who love God and God loves all His people.

I can't say enough good things about Professor Gaskill. Professor Gaskill is a special man that I truly have nothing but the utmost respect and praise for. He changed the way I perceive others and my own faith. Don't know if I've ever felt the spirit more strong in another religion class while at BYU. Would take it again in a heartbeat!!!!

I saw a review saying that he is derogatory towards women and that he tries to get people to leave the church. Far from it imo. I've never felt remotely offended or talked down to by Alonzo. I find him very caring and considerate. Also, I've never heard him tell people to leave the church. He does suggest we keep an open mind to other religions.

Prof Gaskill is a great teacher, and World Religions is an amazing class! Just be prepared for the pop quizzes, and take notes on the study guide so you don't miss any important info for the exams. He teaches VERY fast, so be ready to pay attention! Exams are pretty straightforward, but you do need to study if you wanna do well.

I would definitely take it again. Use the note-taking guide he provides. Late assignments will tank your grades, and lots of pop quizzes. The midterm and final are straight from the note-taking guides, so study those. Pay attenyion to due dates on assignments!

Alonzo is an absolute GEM! Very passionate about other religions and shares that passion with his students. His lessons are relevant, manageable, and hilarious. He is a whole vibe, honestly. 

Love his sense of humor. Definitely recommend taking this class with him!! There's a wonder why they usually fill up quickly.

This class changed my life. Professor Gaskill is amazing; he is so passionate about what that he teaches. He is super funny and class was really entertaining. I always walked away with some of the most valuable insights on the gospel. My favorite class I've taken at BYU, I hope to take another one from Bro Gaskill in the future, he is incredible!

Alonzo is an absolute GEM! He is such a caring guy who takes the time to listen to students. Tests can be a little tough and there's a lot of information so it's not the simplest of classes.However,quizzes are open book, there are choices with assignments,and he is great at responding to queries. 
He's hilarious and eccentric. Definitely recommend!

Professor Gaskill is awesome and a little wild, but a really accessible guy if you reach out. Class is very lecture-heavy and you have to be really on top of the notes to keep up. He talks really fast and goes through like 5 different topics in a minute. The tests are kind of hard so be sure to study your notes.

You will probably learn more in this religion class than any other at BYU, but this is also almost certainly the hardest religion class at BYU. That said, I seriously may take it again sometime just because Professor Gaskill is incredible and you truly learn so much.

THIS WAS THE BEST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN!! Dr. Gaskill's lectures and testimony are so inspiring! I genuinely learned so much this semester. Exams are based off notes from lectures but he provides a study guide, and there are pop quizzes. But a VERY doable class and I enjoyed doing the homework. You will not regret taking this class!!!
Love this man. If he doesnt go to the celestial kingdom then I dont know who will
Hilarious professor!

Gaskill is genuinely hosting some of the most interesting religious discourses going on at BYU! This class broadened how I looked at world religions and conversed about theology. This was such a great course to get an introduction to the topic and get comfortable with interfaith conversations. Gaskill has a great deal of respect.
Great professor! Amazing lectures that strengthened my testimony and opened my eyes to different and deeper views on religion!
Best professor of world religions. My favorite class I have taken at BYU. So inspiring. I would take this class from Professor Gaskill just for fun. May Guru Gobind Singh bless you.
Great guy! Super funny and interesting lectures. The note-taking guide is ridiculously long, which is what makes the course difficult. All of the test questions are taken from the note-taking guide.

Alonzo Gaskill is a GREAT professor, but if you want to know it's like, here it is: He speaks FAST & he will sometimes get off topic with related stories, but brings it back. He will give you study guides to fill out as he goes, encourages questions, and his tests have Multiple Choice, T or F, and All that Apply. Multiple quizzes so do the reading!

World Religions with Professor Gaskill is by far the best religion class I've taken, and maybe my favorite class at BYU. His lectures are AMAZING and I came out of the class with a genuine appreciation and understanding of religions and cultures all over the world. The tests definitely require preparation but with good notes you can do well.

This class was super fun and engaging, and I learned a lot about other religions. Participation matters and there's pop quizzes, so make sure to attend class each week. The professor gives you a study guide for the exams, but he speaks super quickly and it was hard to keep up. Exams were difficult and there was a lot to memorize.

I actually really liked him as a person and was interested in the subject matter (hence why I took the class). However, the tests were so difficult that I was just frustrated the entire time. I studied for 2 weeks straight for the final and failed it. The pop quizzes killed my grade. I got 0s on all of them after doing the readings. Buckle up.

Dr. Gaskill is incredible! He's passionate about the subject matter and always engaging. Be careful of the pop quizzes though! All things considered, I didn't want this class to end. I learned so much about how to love and respect people who are different than me through this class. 10/10, would take again!!

Dr. Gaskill's class may be overwhelming at first but I think it's fun, enlightening, and so impactful. Dr. Gaskill is respectful, humble man, and educated expansively. His sense of humor never disrespects students and their questions, concerns, or the religions he covers. If you are willing to work hard to grow, you'll get that opportunity.

he is AMAZING.he is so smart& hilarious& says the craziest things.he talks SO fast so it is hard to write down everything he is saying but you can get the notes from other students or just go ask him the questions you.the mid term& final are not that hard BUT you do have to study everything. like i made 400 flash cards just for the midterm :)

Professor Gaskill's World Religions class is a rollercoaster ride - his lectures are fast-paced and full of tangents, but his passion is infectious. Using unstuckstudy ai alongside the textbook helped me ace the exams. Overall, a spiritually rewarding experience.

I really enjoyed this class, and Professor Gaskill is great. But if you are looking for an easy religion credit, maybe choose a different class. But if you are seriously interested in other religions and cultures, absolutely take this class!

Prof gaskill is such a good professor but the tests were ridiculously hard. I prepared for HOURS and made tons of flashcards and did everything I could but I still did horrible on his tests. He tests on the tiniest little details that he barely touches on in class so PAY ATTENTION. Hes a super nice guy though and made class very interesting!

I literally CREATED an account to say, do NOT take this man's class. I have a 3.8 GPA and I got a C in this class... a C in a religion course that I tried my best in (did all extra credits). If you are a total nerd that will be in EVERY SINGLE CLASS STRICTLY NOTING EVERY SINGLE WORD THAT HE SAYS, then memorizing every word, this is your class!

On the surface level, there are pop quizzes so come prepared and the midterm/final require a good amount preparation. On a deeper level, this was the BEST class I've taken at BYU. Gaskill is hilarious, intelligent, and open-minded. His testimony seriously impacted my life. 100% recommend, it's life changing if you allow it to be.

World Religions; Everything on the Final is in class, not the textbook. Provided a note-taking guide with all possible Final questions. Talks fast, likes tangents. Lots of xtra credit available. Pop quizzes are scary. Loves his stuff, made me love it too. Spiritually strengthening fs, love ecumenism.

Professor Gaskill is the most talented lecturer I've ever met. Though his class is on comparative religion I felt the spirit more often than in many other religion classes. Cannot recommend him enough.

I genuinely have never had a better professor. I kind of accidentally ended up in this class but it was the best thing that ever happened to my schedule. There is no one I'd rather take world religions from. He knows his stuff and isn't pretentious about it. Lectures are very fast and a tad overwhelming, but he gives all the exam questions/answers.
This is exactly what you want in a world religions class at BYU. Very inspiring lectures, straightforward, intellectually enlarging.

Almost no homework, and only one paper. The midterm and final is really easy if you follow his detailed note taking guide. Beware, he talks SUPER FAST, but everything he says is so worth listening to. I talk about this class all the time, and I've recommended it to all of my friends.
By far my favorite religion professor at BYU! I usually don't like religion classes but Alonzo is inspiring in every way and I always left his class with the desire to become a better person.

Loved the professor but the class was quite difficult. Readings were simple but assignments were time-consuming, pop-quizzes were annoying, and the exams were impossible. I did every reading and attended every class but got Cs or Ds on the exams. Unless you are a pro at memorization, exams are difficult. But Gaskill is a very engaging lecturer.

The content of this class was super interesting and I'm sure Professor Gaskill is a great person. However, the course-load for this 2 credit class is insane. The journal entries took about 40 pages total on their own and an extensive amount of notes were taken.  Literally any small detail from the textbook or hours of videos could be on the test.

Professor Gaskill is very energetic & hilarious! He was fun to listen to but he talks very fast & it's hard to keep up sometimes. The class itself isn't very hard, but the exams are some of the hardest I've ever taken. They are very lecture specific. I paid attention in every class and studied and still got a C on the exam. Do all the extra credit.

Professor Gaskill gave amazing lectures and besides the tests the course really wasn't too bad, however, his tests were super specific and he doesn't prepare you well for them. Be prepared to study like crazy to do well on the tests and do the extra credit!

This class is much harder than it should be for a two-credit class intended to expose members to religions they are unfamiliar with. If you do not interpret a religion the exact way that he wants you to, he will give you a bad score and send you paragraphs of feedback telling you why you are wrong. I would recommend basically any other professor.

The midterm was very, very unfair.  The study guides gave no help & only covered 1/3 of the questions. Treat it like a 4 credit class to get an A.

I'm currently taking this class on independent study.  If it helps for context, I've gotten A's in econ, finance, chemistry, & molecular biology, & haven't gotten below 98% in any other religion.

The best! I highly recommend taking his class! You get to go to another religion's worship service (or read a 300+ page book) and then write a paper about it. The paper has all the questions/prompts you need to make the paper full-length. The lectures were energetic and insightful. He's respectful of thoughts and perspectives. Take this class!!

He says what comes to mind which some people might take offense by, talks very loudly and super fast. If you don't like this, don't take it from him. However, I thought he was amazing. Highly recommend. There are pop quizzes on the daily devotional reading. Some of the weekly quizzes are worded weird or a little obscure. Learned lots from class.
By far one of my favorite professors! He's very passionate about the topics and can tell really cares about all people. He is absolutely hilarious! I loved this class!

so sO SO good. I wish he taught more classes. Professor Gaskill is passionate about what he does and so good at answering questions. Greatest religion class I have ever (prolly will ever) take. Light homework, but pretty detailed tests. 100/10 recommend

This guy will either offend you or change your life. You choose. He is very blunt but so hilarious and super knowledgeable about religions from his own experience! He talks incredibly fast so be prepared. Weekly-ish study guides are totally doable, just don't forget to read devotional book for pop quizzes cuz those can hurt your grade.

A good man; an incredibly pompous professor. Often seems as if we are studying "the gospel according to Dr. Gaskill." We are halfway through the semester and we've yet to read any sacred texts of the world religions we are studying. Instead, we rely on textbooks written by Gaskill and his colleagues.

I wish that Alonzo taught more classes than he does now. While it may seem overwhelming at first, you soon will see it isn't as bad as it may seem from the get-go. He has the most incredible personality and is one of the smartest professors I have come across. I've recommended him to every student I know, and I wish I could take this class again!

Dr. Gaskill is very funny and passionate about what he teaches. Great professor. Just be sure to write down every single little thing he says in class (even if it seems unimportant, like the year Shinto became the state religion of Japan) because the tests are very specific.

10/10 lectures, he's so funny and explains things in a way that makes sense. His exams are super difficult, after the midterm I had a bit of panic wondering if I should drop the class because I thought I was going to fail. But even with lower scores on the midterm and final, I still passed. This class grew my testimony immensely, take it.

He's amazing but His exams are hard, you probably already knew that, so here's how to succeed in his class:

- do daily readings, pop quizzes matter
- He tests on EVERYTHING in class, including first day material, quotes etc
- He talks fast, use the slides he posts on canvas so you don't waste time writing down slide info

TAKE THIS CLASS

Alonzo is hilarious!!! I looked forward to his lectures every day! He respects others and their beliefs in a way that I want to duplicate. Make sure you do all the readings and you'll do fine on the pop quizzes. Definitely beware of the midterm and final. They are super challenging. The lowest test score I've gotten in my life was on that midterm.

He tests on very minute details and talks really fast, so don't be distracted in class and put a study group together! I didn't do super well on the exams, but I wouldn't trade the intellectually and spiritually enlarging experience this class was. I'd define him as chaotic good (i.e. his personality isn't for everyone), but I enjoyed his class!

Excellent teacher and class. Super interesting material and he was really knowledgeable. He does post slides but take really good notes. One paper, either attend another religious service or read a book. Does give pop quizzes.

Honestly the best religion class I've taken in all 4 years at BYU. Yes, the class is quite difficult, especially the tests, but education is much more than just grades. I feel edified and connected to God in ways that no other religion class or teacher has been able to do. 10/10 recommend, just make sure you memorize everything from his lectures.

Professor Gaskill was one of my absolute FAVORITE teachers this semester. Really makes students think from a different perspective about other religions and how influential they are to our society. Sharing hilarious stories, he truly loves his students and goes into vivid detail to explain religious concepts. Final exam was tricky, so prepare well!

Let me tell you what I did like: nothing. There were some things said during lecture that I found interesting but other than that, this was the worst religion class I have ever taken. Take it from someone who is a good student, don't take REL C 351 from Gaskill. Find another teacher. I could not keep up during lecture and I did not find him funny.

I was excited to take this class, especially after looking at his high reviews. I couldn't have been more let down. I'm a good student and typically do well, and I must say that this class is absurd. Yes the content during lecture is great, but the tests are incredibly difficult and nit picky. You go in never knowing what minute detail you missed.

I absolutely cannot agree with the student ratings that gave Professor Gaskill a 5.0. He talked at hyper-speed, his tests were unfair, and the "Study Guides" were useless because all the exam material came from what he said during lecture. Maybe if he recorded his lectures or even had a study guide... but no. He was the worst professor I've had.

Best professor I've had at BYU. Lectures are good and engaging, he keeps energy high in the classroom. Clearly passionate about his subject and teaches well. Work load was a good amount for the class. 10/10 recommend taking this class.

Alonzo is the man!! I learned more in this class than any other religion class at BYU. He is such an energetic, passionate, and intelligent teacher. I very much looked forward to each lecture, and his last lecture was especially powerful. Tests are very difficult for a religion class, but if you do all of the extra credit you can still get an A.

Gaskil has got to be the most goofy professor I have had and that is why I loved him. He is politically incorrect  but he has a deep appreciation for diversity of thought. He has deep love for what he teaches. The last lecture of the semester was powerful and left me with a desire to be better and holier. Tests harder than other religion classes.

Lectures are amazing, never a dull moment. He knows his stuff and you will learn so much. Tests are hard, and I had to do a lot of studying for them, but if you do well on the study guides, film reports, and the term paper (which really weren't hard), it should be fine. He gives you the slides from class, so just focus on what he talks about.

Ok. Yes. He's funny and knows his stuff. Class is interesting, yes. But, holy smokes, the man couldn't care less about your grade. The exams are extremely specific. Be prepared to write down every word he says. Exams are lecture only and not based on homework. He's intimating when it comes to asking and answering questions in class. Talks too fast.

Professor Gaskill is hands down the best professor at BYU. He makes every single class period so engaging and deeply cares about the course material and his students. He is the funniest guy and as long as you put effort in and show up to class it is pretty easy to get a good grade. Everyone should take this class!!

This was, by far, the best and hardest religion class I have taken at BYU. I am so glad I took it though. The class is engaging, informative, and I have never met a better religion professor. The tests are pretty hard though.
If you want an easy A stay away, but if you want the best religion class on campus I would absolutely take it.

Alonzo is a legend. Massive ADHD energy, but it made the lectures really engaging and fun to listen to! He does talk very fast in lectures, but I was able to keep up. He knows a lot; I learned so much from him and loved his hilarious stories. The tests are a bit hard, a lot of knowing terms in other languages. But completely doable.

I am a senior at BYU. Professor Gaskill is the best professor I have ever had and this class was the most useful class I have ever taken. It is so valuable to learn about cultures and religions of the world and Gaskill is the man to teach it. He has so much valuable experience with these religions and assigns you to learn about them very hands-on.

Easily the best religion professor and REL class I've had at BYU. Plenty of reading, but that's normal for an REL course. If you just do the daily devotional readings and take really close notes, this class is a breeze. His tests are pretty tough, but even I got a B on the midterm and C on the final and still ended up with an A.

His class was very difficult. It was a two-credit class, but there were so many assignments and things to read. His words were very fast and the class was hard to understand because he talked a lot off topic. He made tests entirely from what he taught in his class, and you have to remember all the details of what he said to get good grades.

Good class, I learned a lot. But his tests are ridiculously hard. Like so hard. They weigh heavily on your grade. I took good notes during lecture and put hours into studying for each test and still every time I saw the exam questions I would be so frustrated because they were almost all irrelevant fun facts that were maybe talked about once.

Love Dr. Gaskill with my whole heart. Best energy, most exciting teacher I've ever taken from. Class physically cannot be boring, always a delight to be in that class. Easy grader, difficult tests though, as he expects you to remember very specific details and vocabulary terms of each religion.

Professor Gaskill was a nice guy who taught a great class. The content was interesting and what I learned was transformational. However, I feel like the quiz questions were very specific and not helpful to learn the material. The tests had nothing to do with the readings and all came from lectures, so take notes!! Be ready for a wild ride!

This was one of the best classes I've taken in my four years at BYU. It made me so much more aware of the rest of the world. As far as grades and work goes it is a very easy class. The tests take 20-30 minutes and if you did half the readings then you'll get an A. Attendance is mandatory, you will lose a lot of points for skipping!

I recommend this class to everyone. Not to be dramatic, but this class totally changed my life; it made me a better, more culturally-aware person. Professor Gaskill's test are pretty challenging, but if you take good notes (tricky to do because of how fast he goes) and know all of the vocabulary, you'll do just fine. Seriously, TAKE THIS CLASS.

Hilarious and dynamic teacher. There will never be a boring lecture. Exams are difficult (he really cares about whether you know what the terms mean) but manageable, all multiple choice, but not purposefully tricky. 5-7 page paper due at the end of the semester, read a book or attend another faith's worship

Alonzo is interesting. He is funny but often class can feel like his personal comedy hour. I also found it funny that one of the required textbooks is his personal online Ebook that he draws pop quizzes from throughout the semester. Props to him for getting that additional income but it feels slightly dishonest. He feeds of being controversial.
Very interesting class with an open-minded professor.
Gaskill cares about teaching as a performance, but not about students. Imagine a list of facts from a textbook that you will be tested on at the end of the semester. Now you have his course.

I'm taking this class through Independent Studies and would not recommend it. It is a 2-credit class, but I do more homework than my 3 credit classes. There is a ton of reading. There is a study guide, but the test has numerous questions that are based on obscure facts from the reading. There is no way to know what is on the test. IS: NO!

PLEASE take this class from prof Gaskill. This class really opened my eyes and Gaskill has such a unique perspective on life and religion. You will have to study for tests but overall it was a really good experience. Life changing class.
Professor Gaskill helps give much needed perspective. He breaks through Utah cultural bias to provide a more complete picture of this world and life. I recommend taking World Religions from him.

He's an amazing professor, but I'd recommend waiting to take it in person. Coursework was heavy--lots of reading, he had us BOTH listen to online prerecorded lectures AND join a zoom class. Tests were very detailed/difficult--I'm PDBIO major and I was most stressed about THIS test. 100% recommend taking it from him, but wait until it's in-person!

Dr. Gaskill is literally hilarious! He talks incredibly fast though and it can be hard to take notes. I usually ended up just copying the slides. His TA's don't hold reviews, but when I took the class, we convinced one of the TA's to come to our student review session and were able to get great tips from him. This was my last religion class!

Prof Gaskill's class was my favorite religion class so far! If you do the readingsand ask questions in class, you will take away so much. Gaskill is culturally sensitive and his class really opens you up to a world of new traditions and faiths. I absolutely recommend this professor and think everyone should at least take world religions.

We had to listen to hours of poor audio of recorded lecture from a previous class. Attendance was mandatory for the zoom lectures anyway. There were a few textbooks, multiple of which were written by him, which I find unethical. Homework due on Sunday. I am a good test taker, but his tests were insanely difficult even with a lot of studying.

Professor Gaskill's world religions class was one of the most inspirational and eye-opening classes I have ever taken. It's an easy A, but it's pretty easy as long as you read the textbook and stay on top of things. Either way, I think it's worth it to learn from him. He's passionate about the subject and it shows.
This prof has a VERY good heart. Definitely do the reading and watch out for tricky questions, but he's kind and humble. Grading isn't too hard as long as you're paying attention.

LOVED the content of this class, LOVED prof gaskill's perspective, but be prepared bc the tests are based on the tiniest passing comments he makes in class. nice guy, he just talks SO fast and his tests are on the tiniest details so it's hard to remember. DO NOT take hand written notes, you won't be able to keep up. fascinating discussions though.

The course content was enlightening and intellectually stimulating. Somewhat work heavy for a 2-credit class. Homework reading, assignments, pop quizzes, and short film reports. None of the aforementioned was very difficult. Tests however were fairly difficult and based on minute details from his comments during the lectures. W/o good notes tough.

Alonzo is incredible and this was one of the best classes I've ever taken, but the tests are ridiculous. I'm usually a pretty good test taker but I've gotten my lowest test scores ever in this class. It's still worth taking the class but be sure you study every single little detail he mentions in lecture (which is a lot haha)!!

I know other students found him funny, but I found him disrespectful and pretty melodramatic and loud. He frequently talks over students and refused to slow down when asked multiple times. He also provided a study outline, but the tests were very different and way more detailed. I loved the material but it was way too hard for a 2 credit class.
I highly recommend this class! Best course I've taken at BYU so far.

Dr Gaskill is such a funny guy. Youll learn a lot in his class and will be laughing the whole time. When I first saw him I was a little freaked out by his loudness and boisterous mannerisms, but I adjusted quickly. Heavy workload for a religion class: You have pop quizzes, papers, online assessments, tests, and film reports.

Really cool professor, has a genuine love for the material and for the students. Very knowledgeable. Does speak really fast in class and a lot of what he says is on the test, I'd recommend recording lectures on your phone and listening to them again afterwards. Test felt really tough in the moment but afterwards I didn't do too bad.

As a senior, this was my favorite religion class at BYU. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND taking it from him. We learned about world religions throughout the world, and how they relate to the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

I loved the course and listening to his perspectives. I was put off, however, by how unclear/inconsistent he was about what we needed to know for exams. He also was mostly unwilling to slow down his speech so the class could keep up. This wouldve been fine if he didnt test entirely on what he said in lecture. He needs to be held more accountable.

Professor Gaskill is a great teacher. He is clearly very passionate about religion and knows his stuff. I definitely recommend world religions if you are interested in learning more about different beliefs. I was a little disappointed that there weren't more guest speakers, but his lectures are great nonetheless. The homework and tests are easy :)
I could have gotten an A but, I forgot to do two big assignments. Professor Gaskill is funny and he gives a different perspective on religion and cultures in general.

Brother Gaskill will make you laugh so hard you'll pass out in your chair! Probably THE most entertaining lecturer I have ever experienced. The man's resting voice is like 1000 words/min, he is lightening fast and extremely knowledgeable. I loved learning about other religions and it made we want to know way more than we got to in the class.
He's hilarious and knows so much about the subject. Take this class.

WOW. Mind exploding. Heart expanding. Spiritual but liberal. Wonderful. He will push your conservative limits if you are conservative. I'm not. So I couldn't wait to go to class and feel uplifted by his enthusiasm about Jesus, Allah, Buddha, and good ole' Zarathustra. Also he was at Stanford and is a Stake Pres. No biggie.

Prof Gaskill is amazing. He's hilarious, teaches great content, and makes the tests and assignments not too difficult. The only thing is that the lectures are not very engaging, but they're interesting. He requires a few small papers, and two tests, so not bad. He is one of the best teachers that I've taken.
TAKE THIS CLASS. This is the best class I have ever taken. I learned so much and it changed the way I view other religions. Professor Gaskill is hilarious and lectures are extremely interesting.
He's amazing. Take his class. That's all.

If you're going to take world religions you HAVE to take it from him. Hands down best professor and class I've had at BYU. It's so much more than just learning facts about other religions and it should be required for everyone. Alonzo is hilarious and really helps you to find a love for other religions.

Dr. Gaskill is THE BEST professor. He is my favorite professor at BYU hands down! His lectures are so interesting and entertaining. I actually enjoyed going to his class. There is one big term paper, but it wasn't difficult. There are daily readings, but they are really short. Overall a great experience. Take this class from him!!

I loved Brother Gaskill and this class! He is an incredibly engaging lecturer, and he really helps you gain an appreciation for world religions. I had high expectations for this class, and it definitely exceeded my hopes! You get to attend another denomination for a project, which is really cool. Tests and papers are not too hard, just take notes.

TAKE WORLD RELIGIONS FROM GASKILL. He is hilarious and his lectures are super engaging. He helps you have a passion for learning about other religions too. He talks incredibly fast, but provides a ton of insight on the material. There's only one big paper due, and it's not too bad.

This class and proffesor has been the best class I have ever taken at BYU. I learend so much and have changed drastically becsue of what I learned. Proffesor Gaskill is so funny and so inspiring at the same time. The tests and quizzes are not hard at all if you study and read even a little bit. The content is enjoyable if you open your heart.

He makes you do more work than in your typical religion class, but it's all super interesting content. He's a good teacher and super inspiring in his view of other religions, and I would definitely take a class from him again.

Alonzo is a hilarious teacher that has a refreshingly realistic view on life and on all religions, he's also a convert. He works to make his classes fun yet informative. He does tease and poke fun, so if you can't take a joke then this class may not be for you. One of my absolute favorite professors.

Dr. Gaskill is very straightforward and blunt with students, its just the way he is! He is one of the most personable, kind professors I have ever had. His lectures were incredibly entertaining, and his tests were hard. This subject is one that I feel every BYU student needs to learn more about- other religions. Definitely take this class!

Probably one of my favorite professors and classes I've taken. He's absolutely bonkers and talks super fast, but I genuinely loved the new perspectives he brought to issues and the passion he has for the subject. Never a dull moment, all the lectures are so entertaining, you leave the class with a new respect for other religions, super spiritual

Professor Gaskill is about as quality as it gets. He is hilarious, and gives the best lectures! He knows more about religion than anyone I've ever met, and he has such great insights. Take this class from him, you will not regret it!

Professor Gaskill is the faster speaker I've ever had as a teacher. He's also one of the funniest. This guy's wit is impressive. Honestly, he has more energy than a 15-year-old boy with ADHD. He's such an amazing teacher! He has so much knowledge about different religions and it was amazing to take this class from him.

This was one of my favorite classes at BYU. Alonzo is so funny and helps you understand other religions. This is also one of the easier religion classes at BYU. Make sure you are prepared for the pop quizzes though because those can really jack up your grade. Definitely take this class!

By far the best religion class I have taken. Professor Gaskill knows the content he is teaching, doesn't have a biased religious view, and has a great sense of humor. It might have a bit more HW than normal religion classes, but 10/10 would take again. Just do the reading and don't skip class and you'll be fine.

Missing 2+ class periods deducts about .8% of your final grade per absence. His lectures are really engaging, entertaining, and informative (even though he speaks fast and can be sarcastic). So, don't miss class! Go to the TA reviews! Ours had access to the test and was helpful narrowing down what to study. He is one of my all time fave professors.

Not bad, his class was exhausting for me though. My brain had a hard time keeping up let alone my pencil for taking notes. As far as tests go, go to the TA reviews. GO TO THE TA REVIEWS. It's impossible for you to know whats on the test unless you go, and you'll end up studying a million things you will never need to know.

So this professor is kind of a stickler about his grading system and following the syllabus rules. This seemed to take away from the course; however, the class wasn't as hard as I originally thought. He's definitely very open-minded and a lot of that rubbed off on me. Extremely energetic and talks very fast. Take it if you go to school to learn.
This was the best class I have ever taken, not only did I learn a ton, but the teacher is amazing. He is a child in an old man's body, and you will never be bored in that class.
If you let it, this class will change your life. I wish it could last forever.
He knows his stuff

I love Dr. Gaskill! He has the most hilarious stories! Lectures are mandatory but you won't want to miss them anyway. Lots of small (easy) assignments. As long as you follow the calendar on LS for assignments it's easy to get everything done quickly. I think this is one of the best classes I've had and I think I'm a better person because of it.

I loved this class. Professor Gaskill LOVES the material and really opens your eyes to the truth in all world religions. He talks a million miles an hour but allows for questions. The readings are mandatory but they allow the class to have a good discussion about the different religions. The tests aren't bad if you go to the reviews! Take the class

Very striking professor. He has a sublime understanding of life and of God. Not only is he enlivening but also comedic, prepare to laugh. He has some priceless life experiences and I die every time he reenacts them. Such is a hoot, love the man.

This has been my absolute favorite class! Professor Gaskill is such a knowledgable guy & is very open to questions. His lectures made me excited to go to class because you never know what crazy story you might hear. He is hilarious, but you will also learn so much. If you have any interest in the world/people/religions around you, TAKE THIS CLASS!

I was expecting this class to be tough, but it was a super easy A. Lots of little easy A assignments to help your grade. Pop quizzes over daily readings (short paragraph each day). Tests are specific, but if you add to & study from the class google doc and go to the TA review, you can ace them. Really great professor, and super interesting class!

I definitely enjoyed World Religions with Professor Gaskill. Some of his classes were a drag though because he just lectures the whole time, but he throws in stories and jokes that usually keep you into it. Textbook is required for quizzes, and additional daily reading for pop quizzes. You're grade depends on you being consistent with assignments.

Professor Gaskill might come off a little abrasive at first, but his heart is pure and he will inspire you if you let him. Yes, the tests are hard (particularly the final), but he gives so much extra credit and easy A assignments that you'll be fine. Believe me, I  got a C- on the final and still got an A in the class.
I had higher expectations, but it's not too hard. Some lectures were interesting, sometimes I was bored. Tests were sorta hard, overall okay, some good info.

really great guy who knows his stuff. very intelligent. TONS of material covered over the 12 religions and theres not a lot of help of what specific things to know for the test. you pretty much just have to know everything going into a test.

Professor Gaskill is an amazing professor! He provides a well-rounded perspective to religion. His syllabus is clear and he makes his requirements simple. You have to attend class but his lectures are very engaging and his tests are straightforward. He will warn that he likes to poke fun, but I absolutely loved the class and woud highly recommend!

I loved this class so much! Alonzo strikes me as kind of ADHD but it just makes his lectures funnier. He has an obvious and heartfelt testimony and really strives to live and understand other religions. I learned so much and feel closer to God and enormously more prepared for my mission now!

Professor Gaskill is up there with my favorite professors at BYU. He came highly recommended by some friends and I thought World Religions sounded like a cool class anyway so I signed up. His lectures are fantastic, his enthusiasm is through the roof, and he is down right hilarious. It doesn't hurt that world religions is a great class already.

I really wanted to like Brother Gaskill, I did. His lectures were semi-interesting, and he did explain things very well. But, I felt like half of the time he was just talking about the LDS church and how the culture is all messed up instead of focusing on other religions. If you can take it from someone else, do it. If not, it won't be the worst.
I really liked this class from Dr. Gaskill. He knows his stuff and will open your mind to new perspectives and views on the world. Take him!

I would take this class again and again. I've always had an interest in world religions, but now I am eager to study them much more. The lectures were amazing. He provided a great comparison with LDS beliefs, and he has a deep belief in the light we can gain from these other faiths. I would highly recommend this class!

Very good teacher, able to help better understand religion through the eyes of another faith. Very intelligent and talks very fast to cover a lot of info. Test are based off of class, not book. Quizzes are book not class. Very good teacher and I thoroughly enjoyed every class and looked forward to it each time. Definitely recommend.

I have taken just about every religion class at BYU and this was my favorite, hands down. Brother Gaskill is so passionate about what he is teaching, and has the coolest way of presenting it. Class is NEVER boring and you leave it with a better knowledge of other religions and a stronger testimony of your own (at least I did). Take this class!

His class is interesting, but it is really tough and a lot of work compared to a lot of other religion class. It would be a fun class to audit, but he makes the class unnecessarily difficult compared to other religion classes I have taken

Brother Gaskill is a great lecturer. Nevertheless his grading is very tough. He claims he doesn't like memorization but his tests are pure memorization and very unlike how this class is supposed to be.  Went into the final with an A and came out of it with a B+. His midterm and final are just questions that are way too specific and irrelevant.

Brother Gaskill is an interesting teacher. He is very knowledgeable on the subject matter which is a good and a bad thing. It is his tangents that you want to pay attention to, they are golden. His perspective on life and the Gospel is exceptional; he makes you want to be a better student and person. Highly recommend his class!

Professor Gaskill is by far the best teacher I've ever had at BYU. Not only his he hilarious but he is so knowledgeable in World Religions that you are left wanting more after every class. He teaches in such a way that is entertaining and simple to understand. Best class I've ever had the pleasure to sit through. Read and do hmk and you'll be fine.

I LOVED Gaskill's world religions class. Favorite teacher and favorite class. He is hilarious and bring a perspective that is a breath of fresh air. He challenges you to open your mind and think differently than we normally have. I really think that his class should be required. It is harder but we are at college to learn not just to jump hoops.

Enjoyable class - excessive policies.  This class changed my point of view in a positive manner, but the stress I felt in trying to live up to all the class policies at times took away from the enjoyment and learning in the class.

Gaskill is my favorite professor at BYU. He's hilarious and snarky (usually in a good way). I learned SO much. However, if you're hoping for an easy religion class, look elsewhere. This class is harder than it needs to be (IMHO) because essentially anything that comes out of his mouth can be on the test, and he speaks at hyperspeed.

He's a funny guy. Don't take his sarcasm too seriously. He's pretty out of touch though. He said that students shouldn't care about getting an A in his class. That being said, his class isn't very hard to get an A in. It's a really interesting topic, but his pop quizzes and movie reviews really make it all lose meaning. They suck.

Freaking hilarious. Easily the most enjoyable (and sarcastic) teacher I've ever had. There's a lot of material, but if you pay attention and take good notes, you should be alright. You have to attend class since he only uses the lectures for his tests. He also speaks incredibly fast, so if you zone out a lot, it might not be the best class.

ABSOLUTELY HILARIOUS. Clearest syllabus, grading criteria, and schedule of any class I've taken. The reading totally applies and the lectures build on that perfectly. Tests are somewhat hard - all from the lectures (use the class Google Doc) and memorize details, not just the basics. Almost everything we wrote off as too specific was on the test.

I loved this class. Gaskill really knows what he is talking about. He cares about it and he is very clear and what you need to do to get a good grade in this class. There are pop quizzes and they're extremely easy if you just do the quick reading very day. Tests can be a little hard, but he doesn't try to trick you. Stay on top of content. Take it!
Amazing, inspirational teacher. I would take this class 100x more. Alonzo makes you laugh out loud and learn more than you could ever imagine--all in the same lecture!

World Religions taught by Professor Gaskill was my favorite class so far at BYU. Professor Gaskill is engaging and funny. The class was informative and eye-opening. Take his class if at all possible! The tests can be difficult so be sure to stay on top of the content.

Professor Gaskill is a great teacher, who honestly loves his work and is inspiring. His class is eye-opening and made me appreciate other religions more than I would have ever known. If you want to know more about God and much more, take this class.

This is one of my favorite classes I have ever taken at BYU. Professor Gaskell is a great teacher. His lectures are really funny and well done. This class really opened up my mind to other religions and people. I took so much out of it! His tests are hard, but as long as you take good notes and pay attention you will do well. Loved it!

I think professor Gaskill is one of the best professors I have had in my experience at BYU.  He can easily come across as rash and coarse, but I really enjoyed how raw and uncensored his personality is.  He is not afraid to speak his mind on any topic and to address things as they actually are instead of trying to shelter or shield students.

Gaskill's lectures are fun, interesting, and informative.    HOWEVER, his tests are extremely hard.  Tests are usually 30 questions on about 6 different religions.  He doesn't give you a study guide, so you're left to memorize every aspect of every religion.  You'll get tested on the smallest details and it's really frustrating.

He was an extremely fun teacher. His class should be a required one. It was the best religious course I've taken at BYU. He opens your eyes and makes you want to be different. I celebrate Ramadan now every year! He is willing to call out anyone and embarrass them but not in a degrading way. You will get a lot more liberal view in this class.

I loved this class!  The professor is great.  He is sarcastic and energetic and knows so much! His lectures were never boring.  I never wanted to miss.  It requires a bit of work, but definitely doable.  His tests are a little tough, you need to study.  But I would for sure take his class again if I had the chance.

Professor Gaskill was a great teacher. He can move a bit quickly sometimes, so you have to pay good attention in class, but the subject is interesting enough that it isn't a problem. He also has a lot of good stories. The test is on material covered in class, so make sure to show up. If you are looking to strengthen your testimony, take this class!

Alonzo is fetching awesome. His sass is something to be admired. He helps to understand and remember the material with hilarious stories. Be prepared for an abundance of sarcasm and witty banter. He requires some work but it's definitely the most rewarding religion class I've ever taken.

This was probably the best class I've ever taken.  I loved World Religions and Professor Gaskill's teaching.  The man is absolutely hilarious.  Even with the endless humor, his lectures are still amazingly informative and teach so much about so many interesting things.  I feel like a better person having taken the class.  Highly recommend!!!

I loved this class from Professor Gaskill. I highly recommend the class and him to everyone I know. Sure, the tests aren't easy, but you can still probably get away with less work in his religion class than you do than others and still get an A. This class changed my perspective for the better, and his lectures are anything but boring.

This class is difficult. Makes study guidesquizzes so that if you miss 2 points, you get 100%, miss 3-5 points and get 50%, miss more and get a 0. Each study guide takes forever and you still have to really work even though it's open book. Talks super fast and doesn't give a study guide, so you have no idea what to study for tests. But-FUN LECTURE

Be prepared with your daily devotional readings because those pop quizzes are a surprise! He is hilarious and very clear and a great teacher! One of the best I've had at BYU.  The tests are fair and make sure you take notes on his lectures from what he talks about and not only what is on the powerpoint.  You will love this class. Study for the fina

Great lecturer. He is hilarious and very knowledgeable. Make sure you go over the daily readings right before class. Sometimes he will spring a pop quiz in the middle of class. I just wrote a brief sentence summary of each day at the top of my notes. Worked wonders. The study guides and tests are a little rough because of their slight ambiguity.

Professor Gaskill is a blunt, but funny. I enjoyed him as a professor and learned a lot. His tests are impossible though. Unless you memorize every detail from the textbook and class, you won't get a good grade on the test.

Gaskill is a great teacher, but he definitely talks extremely fast! The online quizzes are all based upon the book, but his tests are all based upon his lectures.  His exams are definitely tough with a "Mark all that apply" section.

Brother Gaskill was the professor of the last religion class I had to take while at BYU, and I have to say, I saved the BEST for the LAST! His lectures were very interesting. If  I ever needed to make up work, he was VERY understanding. If you do your part, you should do just fine in his class! Thanks for all the laughter and great insights!

Professor Gaskill is a great guy but a TERRIBLE teacher, He talks way too fast and his lectures are scattered and confusing. It is impossible to take notes and his slides have basically no useful information which makes studying stressful. You will also spend 3+ hours on the study guides which are very hard and the wording can be confusing.

If you don't appreciate sarcasm, don't take this class--but if you do, go for it! I've really enjoyed Professor Gaskill's class, he has some great insights and his lectures are entertaining. Just make sure to do the reading VERY thoroughly and to show up to class, or else you'll find yourself failing.
Quizzes were kind of tough, but he is my favorite Professor I've ever had.  Class was super interesting and I left the class laughing every time

His quizzes are hard, but open book. His tests are based on the lecture (nothing from the book), but his slides are poorly done, they hardly have any information on them. He does not post his slides online you have to go to an office to look at them which is inconvenient. It is an interesting class, but he is not a good professor.

The lectures are super interesting and overall the class isn't too difficult. Weekly quizzes aren't hard if you do the reading. One paper that almost everyone gets 100% on. But the final can be tricky and is a large part of your grade--study with a group!

Best religion professor that I've had! He is very blunt and you laugh a ton during his lectures! Weekly quizzes took maximum 5 mins if you did the reading. 4 vids that you need to watch and write a paper about. Choose a religious service to attend and write a 3-4 pg paper. Loved the class! Take it from Gaskill!

His lectures are really fast-paced, making it difficult to take good notes. But his lectures are very interesting, and Gaskill is super funny. Be warned, you have a weekly quiz you have to take in the testing center based on readings. Each one took me about 15 minutes. BE SURE TO DO THE READINGS. The final was pretty tough. Great class, though.

I absolutely adore this man. People who are offended by him are seriously getting offended way too easily. He's just blunt and says it like it is, which, especially for this particular class, I loved. He's so interesting, clear, and absolutely hilarious. His quizzes can be a bit tough, but everything else is graded SO easily that it evens out.

Professor Gaskill is a great professor. I learned loads from his class and I felt that I had a much better working knowledge of significant world religions after attending the lectures and reading in the packet and manual. Some find offense in his comments but often it is because they are looking for it anyway.
Best Professor I have ever had! Super interesting and hilarious. He made the class fun but still educational.  Super outspoken which I love.

I know I'm an outlier, but I'm not a huge fan of Brother Gaskill. He's very rude and very offensive and doesn't take into account students' feelings.  His test are hard and are every week so do the reading paying attention to even the minor details. The material is very interesting so if you take the course, take it somewhere else.
Best professor at BYU, IMO

He is my FAVORITE professor at BYU. He is SO smart and has written many books. As a convert, he has a really open mind toward other religions. I have taken every class I can from him and it has strengthened my testimony immensely. Also, he is HILARIOUS. I always looked forward to class. It's not hard to get an A if you show up and do the readings.

The class material is very interesting but brother Gaskill was not my favorite professor. His quizzes are almost impossible to do well on unless you read the book with a fine tooth comb. His final is comprehensive and covers only his lectures which were given at mach speed. I found his class interesting but his tests frustrating.
overall the class is rewarding and full of important info.... Great class...

Tests are INCREDIBLY ambiguous. many times he says, yeah thats right, but i wanted you to put this answere....  having said that, the lectures are the greatest! theres a 30 page (15 page single spaced) page due in the middle of the semester. not sure if good lectures are worth the paper. it requires around 40 total hours from start to finish.
Awesome professor, enjoyable class.  If you can't take the sarcasm find someone else, but everyone else is going to laugh and have a blast learning.

Absolute best religion professor on campus. Was Greek Orthodox until his 20s, so he brings a great contrast to the normal Uber-Mormon professors. Taking his classes makes you eager to defend and learn about other denominations. Tell your zealot Mormon friends to take him and they'll be much better because of it! Also, he's HILARIOUS.

I will take any and every class he teaches.  Incredibly knowledgeable.  Over-the-top animated and funny with his teaching, but also incredibly intellectual.  Favorite teacher I've had during my entire college experience.  Obviously loves what he does.  Tests are challenging but more than worth it.  TAKE HIM!

Gaskill is AMAZING. Easily my favorite professor to date. Very animated, honest, and interesting. I learned so much from his class and it was easy to get a good grade if you do the reading for each class.

Bro. Gaskill is the best.  He is very entertaining (uses Piano as footstool) and if you skim the reading looking at bold and interesting points, the quizes are cake.  Tests are much easier and it is hard not to get an A on them.  Great class!
BEST. PROFESSOR. EVER.

I LOVED this class. I thought it was SO interesting & enlightening, and Professor Gaskill is HILARIOUS. He has a Masters in Theology from Notre Dame. He's one of those religion professors who isn't afraid of the truth, which I appreciate. I would take any class from him! 2 midterms & a final, he drops your lowest test score. 1 3-page paper.

Great professor and a really easy class. If you do the reading beforehand and highlight important parts the quizzes will be a breeze. After the first quiz it is pretty easy to guess what will be on the quizzes. That is all you use the textbook for. Tests are completely based on lectures and are extremely easy. An A in this class is easy.

One of the best teachers at BYU. Helps you to have an open mind and understand things with clarity. Very funny and straightforward and honest. His quizzes were sometimes difficult but he does give hints that are really helpful. Class is mandatory but he's very entertaining so its worth it. HIGHLY recommend him for this class.

Brother Gaskill is the best teacher at BYU.  His quizzes may seem hard, but if you have done the readings before class, he will give you hints that make the answer obvious unless you didn't even look at the reading.  His tests are easier than the quizzes, and he gives good study guides for it.  He is an entertaining professor! Highly recommended!
Brother Gaskill is awesome! He not only changed the way I looked at other religions but also the world in general. Great class!
Best Religion Teacher at BYU Period.
great

Gaskill was the funniest teacher.  i really enjoyed being in his lectures.  he does talk really fast, but he puts his power points online so its ok.  tests are tricky but not so bad if you study hard. not an easy class but worth every minute.

Alonzo is pretty cool. Imo he could be an auctioneer. Even though he talks fast, he weighs the test, which is a big help. If it's hard to keep up with his lecture speed chewing something like starbursts or gum helps. Alonzo imo balances mercy and justice pretty fairly when it comes to test grades. Just do the readings and show up for class..

This is by far a HISTORY class, so if you don't like history don't take it. Annotate the readings, show up to class and pay attention. If like me you're easily distracted, find something to eat (like starburst). The tests aren't too hard as long as you study. The paper is strait forward as well.

Excellent Class, Excellent Teacher!  I looked forward to class everyday. Classes are exciting and interesting. This was my favorite class i've taken at BYU and would recommend it to anyone.  The class isn't easy, but I am definitely not a great student and I still got an A-.  If you do the work you'll be fine.

I had Bro Gaskill for World Religions and I looked forward to his lectures every time. He shared his knowledge very well and every lecture had multiple hilarious moments. He has quizzes about once a week-ish but just make sure you read carefully and you'll be fine. His midterms are almost easier than his quizzes. Also he speaks REALLY fast.
The tests aren't even fair! Much of the material contained on the tests is never covered in class. But to each their own.

I loved this class! I learned so much about Christianity but surprisingly I also learned a lot about my own beliefs. Gaskill is full on energy and hilarious. I was never bored and loved every minute of his class. His tests aren't easy but, in my opinion, they are fair. Once I actually put forth the effort to study for his tests I did really well.

Excellent lectures. BUT chaotic and no flow. Seemed like just random topics on Christianity. Tested us on material before it was presented in class. Unless you're a theologian, you won't do well in this class grade-wise.  It's nice to hear a fresh perspective, but not worth the potential grade hit.

Great prof!! I honestly enjoyed his classes and looked forward to them every time. Has a great sense of humor and makes fun of everything (and everyone) so if you get offended easily this isnt the class for you. Not too much reading, but lots of test questions come from the books. I'm taking him again ASAP

I love Gaskill's humor and intellect, and always enjoyed lecture. It did seem like we spent more time on curiosities and minutiae than on doctrine; Gaskill's religion courses have a decidedly secular feel. Also, there's a 10-15 page, exhaustively-researched term paper, which seemed excessive for a 2-credit course. Great teacher, decent course.

Loved this class. He is the most fair, helpful teachers I have ever taken. I got sick and missed one of the quizzes(very hard btw) but he let me come and take it later due to my sickness. WHO DOES THAT? Just go to class and pass the quizzes and you are set. Very interesting lectures!

Best teacher I've had in my 2 years at BYU. If you have a brain, you'll be alright in the class. Take a lot of notes. He is sometimes hard to follow, but if you pay attention for the whole time and take notes, you'll be happy when tests come around. He is a riot-soo funny. You leave that class with an extra tad of happiness in your life. Enjoy!
Best teacher I've ever had for a Religion class.  You do have to work, but all of the work helps in the understanding of other Religions. I hope to be able to take more classes from him!

Gaskill is my favorite teacher at BYU. AMAZING. knows so much and is SOOOOOOO FUNNY!!! I wish i could take him again. World religions is interesting, and he just is the cherry on top! Take it from him. a bit of reading and assignments, one paper, and tests. I didn't do so great, but i don't care! it was totally worth it! trust me.

Great professor -- absolutely enjoyable to listen to, eminently knowledgeable, and will really take the time to answer questions in class and out. DO NOT take his class if you're not interested in Religion and just want an easy credit. He will make you work for it.

Brother Gaskill is awesome! He makes lectures so interesting with his tangents and it's hilarious to see him lecture us while standing on top of a piano. He's open for any discussion. He's fair. You have to write a 10-15 page term paper but you have 9 weeks to do it and it's not that hard. Exams are doable if you study.  I highly recommend him!

Um, greatest class ever. Seriously. He is so hilarious, brilliant, and entertaining. I looked forward to his class every single day. You learn SO much in this class and it's just.. ah! Awesome. Please take it, you won't regret it! Do the readings, and as long as you follow the criteria on the paper exactly, you'll get an A. LOVED. THIS. CLASS!!!!!!
Very interesting class.  He's crazy!!  But really he's way smart and down-to-earth and he knows what he's talking about.  Grading is pretty easy.

It was a very interesting class.  The reading material wasn't bad at all.  And there are only 3 small papers that are fairly easy.  His tests aren't terrible as long as you've done the reading.  Many questions are almost word for word from the text.  I would highly recommend this class to anyone.

He's very enthusiastic?he talks about as fast as the guy on a radio commercial who reads all the legal info?but he's paradoxically really easy to understand.
