He's very engaging and pretty hilarious (although sometimes brutally honest), and quite intelligent and knowledgeable. His tests are a bit hard, but they're curved. Prob my favorite professor.

Christian history- I didn't fall so deeply in love with Gaskill as most of these kids do who have never thought independently, but he was fair-minded. He may assail comments for debate's sake, so speak carefully. Not a brutal class -- 3 very short papers, and he counts 2/3 of the reasonably hard tests. He's written some interesting related stuff.
Awesome and amusing teacher! The class is really interesting and I gained a ton of insight from his lectures.
Hilarious!  And the work is more than doable.
Amazing professor. He is engaging and intelligent and brings a facinating perspective to his class and his writing. One of the best.
Hands down the most amazing professor I have ever had.  He brings un-biased and fantastically clear views to the sometimes choking atmosphere of BYU. A plus plus plus plus plus plus.
Funniest professor ever.  You won't regret taking him.  I only took this class because he was the professor.  Totally worth it.  He made boring (to me) material interesting.

He is absolutely hilarious and animated. He talks a mile a minute and is dripping with sarcasm; if you're sensitive, get a different teacher. He is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. The class is pretty easy, as long as you read and pay attention in class. Tests are good, the paper was easy. This is a great spring/summer class.

Oh, where do we start with Alonzo? Greek Orthodox, definitely a third degree master mason, resident of Payson, passionate hater of texting and kisser of relics. Extremely entertaining, but beware of his groupies. They try to take over the class with their flowery language. They draw close to him with their lips, but their hearts are far from him.

I only took this class because Alonzo had been a sub for my World Religions class (which I also recommend) and he was hilarious.  I was not excited at all about the class, but he made it interesting and fun.  Two tests but if you use the study guide for Gonzalez it's manageable.  One paper that is very easy.  Take this class!

Although he made me laugh, I think I learned more about my own beliefs and feelings than anything...and I learned a ton in this class. Should be required course. It is a 3 credit hour class,and worth everyone of them. I would so take him again
Bro. Gaskill is funny and extremely knowledgeable. Be prepared to take notes fast!  His tests and grading are quite fair.  The required paper is a lot of work but fulfilling.

Gaskill is the bomb.  Not your average religion professor, not by a long shot.  He's Greek Orthodox by birth. The class really encourages critical thinking about religion.  He's a nice guy and terrifically humorous.  You will never, ever sleep in his class.  But, if that's not your thing, don't take him.

Honestly, it's one of the best courses I've ever taken at BYU. The material was interesting and Prof. Gaskill was hilarious. He is sarcastic, so don't take this class if you're offended easily, but he warns you about that. I learned so much about Christian History. I'd recommend him to anyone.
He is a 'lion hearted' Professor. Plus he will teach tones of really cool stuff that no one else will!!!
Gaskill is the man. Great religion prof., very intelligent, and will keep you interested and laughing. By far the best religion prof. at BYU.

Alonzo is very interesting and very intense. I can see how his personality would bug people if they weren't into that sort of thing, and he makes a lot of political comments, which is kind of awkward. His class was alright, I only audited it so I have no complaints. He's an entertaining teacher, if nothing else.

A GREAT professor if you're looking to learn.  Getting an A is only difficult if you're lazy or have a learning disability.  I like him so much I'm reading one of the books he authored.  Great guy, entertaining, and very smart.
He speaks really fast!  The tests are hard, but he curves things up really really generously.  The paper takes a LOT of time, but isn't difficult.

Bro. Gaskill is awesome! I waited all week to come to this class and it seriously changed my perspective on the world. He is really funny and his class will push you. The quizzes and tests are difficult but its definitely worth the work. I recommend this class to everyone.

His lectures are super interesting and he's way funny and intellent. The paper isn't too bad, you just have to follow EXACTLY what he says and you'll do fine. Tests are way hard. We were tested a lot on what we learned in class so be sure to take good notes. Attendance is mandatory, so signing up late for the class might end up hurting your grade.

Entertaining, not very spiritual-oriented. Very academic approach to the Doctrine. Tests are RIDICULOUSLY hard, don't take from him unless you have a 4.0 and are willing to get a lower GPA for the sake of being entertained. Basically, go for an easier class. You can't even write everything he says because he writes so fast. Fascinating topics thoug

He is a great professor, I've loved his lectures ? he is high energy and talks extremely fast.  This is one class you will never fall asleep in.  His tests, however, are ridiculous.  Most of the things that are on them are not covered in the class so they are very difficult to pass.  The paper is easy.

Hilarious, high-energy, rapid-fire lectures. Not for the thin-skinned; he is brazenly sarcastic. He studiously avoids the subtle "Here are all the reasons why Mormons are better than everybody else" mentality that one or two BYU professors (not to mention students) have. Tests were tricky but reasonable if you studied well.
THE BEST RELIGION PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! Seriously, his classes really helped me understand other religions a lot and he is hilarious!

WOW! AWESOME! Very brilliant, but understandable. Suuuuuuuuper funny. Some of his test questions are a little ridiculous though, but he was negotiable with a low class score once, so I thought he was very understanding. Interesting person to meet.

Awesome classes, but don't have anything to do with the tests. Tests have very little to do with learning. Really easy term paper conditional on following one sentence in a 6 page explanation about how you are to write the paper. Your grade will not be reflective of your effort.

He is BY FAR the GREATEST RELIGION PROFESSOR EVER!! He had the class rolling every day.  He's freaking hillarious and I learned so much from his class. His quizzes are extremely difficult and impossible to pass, but the test are easy.

By far the best course/best professor I have ever had. I've learned so much that I will take this course again soon. He is extremely intelligent (graduated from Notre Dame and Stanford), makes class very fun, and very enlightening. I would highly recommend this course!
Alonzo is hilarious and his grading is extremely fair.  I would recommend any of his classes, especially this one.
amazing class.  i really enjoyed the banter, and how he challenged us to look at things in a different way.  one of the most influencing teachers i have had.

He is an amazing Teacher!  Yes, the paper due at the end of the semester was difficult, but since he tells you about it on the first day of class, it's really your fault if you don't get it done.  If you use the study guides for the tests and actually study, you WILL pass them. He doesn't do trick questions at all.  I loved that class!
This is a great class. Brother Gaskill is hilarious, and also really kind when you deal with him on a personal level.

Loved it! So interesting, really good discussion. He talks really fast, so be friends with people in the class if you miss something. Don't take this class if you're easily offended. I thought he was hilarious. But lots of people get offended by him. Don't expect excellent grade. Start early on the huge paper, otherwise, it WILL cause stress.

Started out really enjoying and liking him. But he would get so off track so easily that it was annoying. He made a lot of students not want to attend class and thought that he said things that he shouldn't be saying even though it was funny. He would openly debate with students in class and waste class time. So we were tested on material that we d
Gaskill is hilarious and entertaining, opened my eyes to other religions, he made it so interesting buthis tests are frustrating and tricky, hard to do well on, overall great class

Great teacher, make sure to not wear the 'sensitive sweater' to class because he can get rather sarcastic; very energetic, lots of fun stories, helps you think outside of the box as far as the LDS faith is concerned.  Read very carefully for the quizzes (They are a BEAR!) and go to class every day

Brother Gaskill was a great professor because he actually challenged us on our thinking, which I've had very few religion professors do. It's a 3 credit class and you have to earn your grade (quite a bit of reading) but I found it to be a very valuable class that I'm glad I took. Strongly recommended, but not if you're lazy.
He's really funny, sarcastic and keeps class interesting. Don't procrastinate the paper. Take notes in lecture and you'll do well on the exams (there are three, all on Blackboard).

I can't even stress how much I recommend this class AND taking it from Gaskill.  I learned more in this class than any other class ever and Gaskill is SOOO smart AND entertaining.  I laughed so hard my stomach hurt every class but still learned a ton.  Take really good notes and pay attention to any specific details in reading like numbers

Bro. Gaskill is my HERO!! I have never loved a teacher more! He is so intelligent and I learned so much.Yeah, BOM has a long paper, but it was an easy grade and this is college, you have to write! World religions is awesome too! He is so energetic, so funny, and so humble!!! I love his classes and I love his work. I can't say enough about him!!!!!!

Very entertaining, somewhat eccentric, teaching style.  His tests do not cover the material learned very well.  3 MC tests with 25 or so questions.  If you have the chance, take a class from this guy.

Well I had him for World Rel. and loved him! But this class was brutal.  He only has four assign, 3 of which are confusing multiple answer tests and the other is a beastly single spaced commentary paper on a section of the D&C.  His lectures are full of energy but sometimes you have to question if he is teaching the gospel of Gaskill or of Christ.

Such and AMAZING teacher!  He really gets you excited to learn and wants you to do well in the class.  He definitely knows his information and is very excited to  teach it.  He does talk very fast, is quite sarcastic, and some could take him to be offensive, but  he does it in good humor.  If you are going to take this class take it from Bro. Gaski
Great Teacher just follow the guidlines for his beast paper, go to class, and attend a study group before tests.  You will Get an A

Bro Gaskill was my absolute favorite professor this semester! He talks super fast but class was always fun! Make sure to study the reading before the quiz to do well. Also study alot for the tests. I wasn't ever prepared well enough for the quizzes, so be sure to read!! Overall, I would highly recommend this class with Gaskill to anyone!

This class is seriously amazing.  I definately reccomend it, especially if you are pre-mish. I have learned so so much. The quizes are not too bad if you do the reading. I have never had a professor who cared so much about me and spent so much time helping me outside of class. Lectures are interesting and engaging. Take this class!!

I loved taking Dr. Gonda's anatomy class. She gave great lectures, was very helpful to our needs and gives great feedback. Go to office hours with her, and she'll help a ton! The course is challenging but you can turn to her and the TA's for help, and it'll make sense.

Dr. Gonda was a really kind and caring professor who had fun, engaging lectures. The only grades that come from the lecture are the tests, but if you do the practice questions and read the "textbook" (just lecture slides with a few paragraphs of extra text to go with them), you can do really well.

Gonda was the best college professor I have ever had. I have never met someone who genuinely cares about the students so much, she is so kind and so smart. She is so willing to meet with you and help you out, she taught so of the most difficult things and made them feel easy. Cell 220 is a hard class and its test heavy but her exams are easy!

Dr. Gonda is an amazing professor & she really does care for her students & their success. BUT, her class was extremely hard. I put in WAY too much time because her exams were TOO hard and I was spending many hours studying and going to TA reviews. Her tests were tricky & what seemed easy for her wasn't. I recommend going with another professor.

Dr. Gonda is one of the most involved professors I have ever had. Although the class was difficult, she was willing to work with all the students. She made a difficult course very interesting and fun. I would definitely take from her again.

Dr Gonda is my favorite professor I've ever had! Expectations are clear and she is so genuine in class. She wants everyone to do well and will help you succeed if you want to! She wants to answer your questions about things and seems to actually love what she's teaching. She does an excellent job explaning tough concepts.  Absolutely take from her!
Cell 220 is one of the hardest classes I've taken. Professor Gonda is great. For being a hard class, she makes it easier. Learn to study and study hard.

Dr. Gonda is my favorite professor I've had here at BYU!! She cares so much about the success and genuine learning of the students in her class and will work her schedule around to meet with you if you can't make it to office hours. Cell 220 is a hard class but she will walk you through everything if you just ask. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER!!

Dr. Gonda is my favorite professor on campus! She cares SO MUCH on your grade and how you are performing. I HIGHLY recommend Dr. Gonda. CELL 220 in itself is veryyyy difficult but Dr. Gonda made the suffering a little less severe hahaha.

Gonda is one of the very best professors I've had. She took the time to review things in her office hours. The lectures have a lot of content so we didn't always finish but she would go back and finish the slides in next lecture. She made sure to explain things well, review, and orient us when teaching new material. Practice exams were very helpful

I seriously loved taking this class from Dr Gonda. She's an incredible teacher and really cares that her students succeed. It's a super tough class and requires a lot of studying but Dr. Gonda is always willing to help with study tips and go over tests and questions. If you take this class definitely take advantage of the TA's and office hours.

Dr. Gonda was awesome. I took this class from her in the spring semester was brutal. Anatomy is going to be tough no matter what, but having a good professor helps. She is super understanding and wants all of her students to succeed. She was very personable and accessible outside of class. Make sure to put enough time into lecture and lab

Dr.Gonda was great! Man this class was brutal but I really appeciated how Dr.Gonda was very understanding and gave lots of resources to help us suceed. Definitely take advantage of the online tools. Also dont neglect lecture, I put all my effort into lab and did great but lecture snuck up on me. Interesting class but def lives up to the reputation.

This class is a lot of memorizations, but it's run by a super kind and caring professor. Going to lectures help but you can ace the tests with just the PowerPoint slides and the textbook. Also take the practice exams offered, they help! You definitely want to be present for labs.

She was good. Im not passionate about this kind of history and I just took it for credit. Just show up, keep your video on, and participate once in class. Theres no reason to do the readings and the class is pretty boring. She makes annoying sounds into the mic sometimes. The open note tests arent too bad but you need to have a solid study guide

Look. Like others have said, she knows a lot about history but she is just a terrible presenter, especially online. She'll chew gum during her lectures in the microphone and the classes go on and on and on. She forces you to be at class and attendance is heavy on your grade. If there's another option, take it.
Look, she's passionate about history, but her classes jump all over the place and she doesn't present the material very well; it's really hard to pay attention, especially online.

She did well on trying to get student participation and on hearing the different standpoints of students, but the class gave me more of a seminary vibe than a college level religion course (especially for RMs). There are readings and student questions due every class period. It felt more like 2.5 credits to me. She did fine, but I have had better.

I enjoyed having Professor Taylor for Book of Mormon 121. The reading is not bad at all and I loved the student questions. Her tests are pretty difficult, but if you know the study guides well then you will be fine. Be prepared to attend to all your lectures because you will not do well if you skip frequently.

She is really enthusiastic about studying the Book of Mormon. I really felt that she reached out to her students and tried to engage everyone in class discussions. She loves to hear feed back from students and particularly likes to hear different opinions. I liked pairing off into small groups and discussing different opinions.

Profesora George is someone who genuinely cares about her students! She works to help everyone succeed no matter their level of spanish. Attendance is important, and the course work itself is pretty standard across all 321 classes but I would say that I had a really good experience in comparison to some other teachers that my friends had.
Ella es tan amable y nos entiende! Es de españa entonces es super divertida! Nos trae comida de vez en cuando.

She is such a caring teacher and engaging. There was a good amount of reading but it was manageable. I would take her class again and I would recommend her to anyone taking Spanish 321. She also spoke very eloquently and clearly. Her discussions are the reading and lessons were helpful. Her lectures were also relevant to the material for the class.
absolute queen. I would recommend this class

Love Profe. George! The class is a little heavy on reading sometimes but you can reasonably get through it. If you have a good base of spanish already you will be fine. If you're not as confident with your spanish I'd reccomend starting with something easier, you have to be at a higher intermediate level for this class.
Great professor who teaches the class well. Consistent homework assignments, but nothing extreme, just be prepared to do them and you'll get a good grade.

Professor George is very caring and easy to work with. She has a good sense of humour and is easy-going. She gives you a project that is to be done with a classmate. Most of the lecture time is spent talking to a classmate, doing fun activities, and, of course, the lecture itself. She is undoubtedly my favorite professor at BYU.

Profesora George is AWESOME! She is super friendly, Spanish, and wants you to succeed. It's not a difficult class; you maybe have a poem or two to read each week. Make sure you show up because she takes attendance. Tests are easy, review is useful and there's only one group project worth like 30% of your grade and it's pretty straightforward.

My QUEEN I love her. She is so understanding and funny and made everyone feel comfortable at their level of spanish. I was nervous coming into Spanish 321 but it ended up being one of my fav classes of the semester. Assignments are straightforward and consistent. I couldn't recommend her more!!

Prof George wants everyone to learn and also do well in her class. She is super lenient, so if you have an issue or need, just talk to her! It's honestly up to the student whether you want to learn, but her enthusiasm definitely encourages participation. Take her class!! She literally puts all of the test material on the study guides!!!

Profesora George is amazing! She is super caring, respectful, accommodating, and patient.The class is super easy and all of the assignments are really given by the department on canvas. Seriously though, Profesora George is just an awesome sweet person who made us all feel loved and welcomed in class. Would definitely recommend taking 321 from her.

Professor George was great! This class is a breeze but Professor George made it especially easy. Assignments are due before class then a discussion in class. Assignments are easy; 30-60 minutes per week. There are 2 midterms and a final which are easy and take less than an hour. I wish I could take all my Spanish classes from Professor George!

She is amazing! If you are taking SPAN 321, take it from her! She is the best professor I have had at BYU hands down. She is super personable and makes sure that all her students feel comfortable in class. The work load is easy and are almost guaranteed an A.

Professor George is so awesome! She is super understanding about assignments and teaches you well. If you are really interested in spanish you will learn in this class. She also knows that a lot of people are taking it just to get the challenge exam credits but makes it fun anyway. I would love to take all of my spanish classes from her.

Profesora George is amazing! There are a decent amount of assignments, but none of them are too hard and I didn't find it to be too time consuming. She is really funny, and passionate about making sure you understand, questions are always welcome. Her goal is to help everyone get an A. Class was very enjoyable and informative!

If I could rate him higher than 5, I would. He's genuinely so good at teaching writing improvement. There was one assignment that took me several hours over the weekend, but he does a great job pacing the course and helping students succeed! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!! He also organizes groups to help with peer review, and they became my good class friends!

The grading is pretty harsh in this class, but he lets you rewrite your work to improve your score. Although, only half of the assignments met this criteria, as the rest were not graded by the end of the semester. He wants you to succeed!

Dr. Frost truly cares about his students and wants all to succeed. He is a tough grader but gives you the opportunity to rewrite and submit your papers as many times as needed. He is willing to give you feedback and help as much as you need.

Disappointing class. Papers graded very harshly, which is OK, but the thing that frustrated me was that I didn't know how to improve. I would follow the rubric as best I knew how, but then I would still get some of the worst scores I've received in my 3 years at BYU. Also, I didn't feel like I learned much about how to actually write better.

Dr. Frost is great! He grades harshly, but you can rewrite your papers until you get the grade you want. However, only 1/3 papers were graded before the semester ended, so that didn't end up helping. Don't feel like I learned much honestly. It's "writing and presenting" but you spend 1 day on presenting. He is a stellar professor though! Easy A.

Dr. Frost is excellent. I took away so many useful skills for my writing and presenting from this class. His papers are not simple, but he gives you class time to work on them as well as one-on-one consultations. You won't regret taking this class from him.
Guys, I love Dr. Frost so much. He boosted my confidence as a writer and helped me get on track to get my public scholarship posted! The papers were a ton of work but well worth it.

Dr. Frost is an excellent professor and he does a great job of working with each student individually to help them improve their work. The assignments in this class are all purposeful and not too challenging, but they do promote growth and good quality work. This class makes publication seem possible and within reach.

Professor Frost is AMAZING! He is a real human and is willing to work with studnets. I'm convinced that I would not have made it through this class if I had had a different professor. That is not to say that he is lenient with students, or gives out easy As, but he understands that we all struggle and senior cap stones are hard to write!

Professor Frost is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so patient and so accessible. If you need time to meet, or have a question about a topic/homework, just email him! He is very responsive! Also, the topics he teaches are so interesting. You can tell he has a lot of passion and knowledge for his subject!
The readings are often difficult to understand, but he goes over them in class. The weekly writing assignments arent too hard, but to get a good grade you should take them seriously.

Professor Frost is awesome. I really loved his class and I learned a ton. He was really good about helping students interact in class. He really cares about students and the material. Pretty much every Saturday there is a short essay due that covers readings but they are pretty easy. There is a midterm and a final that aren't too hard.

I really enjoyed Dr. Frost's class, and he did a great job presenting information from multiple perspectives. Attendance is required, and make sure you tune in. He is quick to respond to emails, and his advice is always helpful. The topics are quite controversial and he does a good job moderating multiple perspectives. Would recommend this class.

Class was average, though there was lots of reading, you HAVE to go to the lectures if you're not understand or you won't pass the class. Has a small paper due just about every week and a term paper, but only two tests throughout the course. Good class just to get that credit over and done with.

Favorite professor in BYU so far! He was so nice and knowledgeable, I learned so much from him! Loved answering questions! There were about 10 writing assignments through the semester, two quizzes a week, one big essay, and two exams (midterm and final.) Takes a while to get your grades back, though. Besides that, awesome! 100% recommend!

Solid professor, super nice and intelligent. There are short weekly essays and the TA's can be tough on them, but the workload isn't too bad. Participation quizzes and in class writings for attendance (doesn't mark zoom attendance, but you need to go to class for the in class writings). Tests aren't too bad but include essays. 1 miderm, 1 final
Loved his class! Professor Frost is very accessible and knowledgeable. He actively encourages his students and wants them to succeed. Fair, understanding grading. Would definitely recommend!
Stellar professor, make sure you really read the cases. Interesting material, but a little dry at times so find some way to pay attention.

You can tell he really cares about his students but this class is overall hard. Lots of work with weekly mini essays and quizzes. Quizzes are super easy as they are open notes but the midterm and final is really hard. If you take this class be prepared to spend a lot of time doing assignments and a final project that is like 12 pages long.

I originally dreaded this class, I was just taking it to complete the GE. However, I ended up really enjoying it. Dr. Frost has great lectures and is good to his students. Once I forgot to turn in an assignment and he was very understanding and gave me full credit even though it was late. Tests are fair but the class requires a lot of reading.

Really enjoyed this class! Learned a ton about healthy dating/marriages & not just from a religious standpoint. Bro Frost was kind and approached sensitive issues with an open mind. The readings were fabulous and actually helped me in my current relationship. Lots of reading, quizzes each week, short essays due each week, but not hard at all

Dr. Frost was a great professor. This class has an intense amount of reading, and if you struggle with reading ancient philosophy it isn't easy to get through. That being said, Dr. Frost made it easy to understand the material in his lectures and was incredibly helpful when he was asked questions. The tests aren't bad, just be ready to write essays

Dr. Frost is great at explaining things! I thought POLI201 would be like American Heritage, so I took it. It was so hard, though, because of all the writing. Most of the final grade was based on essays. Worth it, though, because it is interesting. I took this online during the pandemic, so I had a ton of free time. Hard for a STEM major like me.

Dr. Frost is an amazing professor who provides a lot of amazing insights into the philosophies of the Western World. Philosophy itself is not easy, but Dr. Frost's lectures and discussions help make the readings more bearable. Tests are easy if you do the readings. Pop quizzes are possible, but, again, if you do the readings they're possible!

I LOVE Dr. Frost, he is so kind and understanding. The philosophy paper was challenging to write, but each of the TAs I talked to were helpful and (to me at least) clear in their grading/expectations. You are graded on open-note quizzes, 10 short SRs, a paper, some in-class writing assignments, and midterm/final. Challenging, but very doable.

Dr. Frost was an absolutely amazing professor and I always looked forward to his classes. His lectures are extremely insightful and Dr. Frost is an extremely intelligent person. He's really nice and asks a lot of questions, prompting lots of discussion and participation in class. Tests are not hard but they require studying. I highly recommend him!

A 5 is not high enough for Professor Frost, but is too high for most TAs. Amazing lectures, clear on class requirements, made content interesting. In-class writing assignments for attendance. Tests weren't bad (MC + essays). Awesome class environment. TA graded papers were inconsistent, but gave feedback when asked, and my scores improved.

Frost was a very nice professor, pretty clear in lectures. The slides are accessible and he is always willing to clear things up for you. Aside from that, the TAs are a bit of a nightmare, the reading lengths are sometimes inordinate, and for a GE, too much work. Unless you LOVE philosophy, I would suggest a different class for this requirement.

Essays are graded by TAs, which is what the majority of the grade is based upon. Multiple choice on tests is easy and straightforward, and he gives a pretty detailed study guide, This might be a great class for people who are interested in political philosophy, but I realized how much I hate philosophy early on. Liked Dr. Frost but hated the class.

Here's my problem. I got a 97% in my upper-division philosophy class, where all my papers were graded by someone who has a Ph.D. in philosophy from Princeton. I got a 90% in professor Frost's general-ed philosophy class, where all the papers were graded by a TA who wasn't even studying philosophy. I put more effort into professor Frost's class.

His TAs are problematic. I checked my term paper with one of them, who said it just needed a couple of revisions (which I made). I turned it in and got a B-. The rest of the semester I was getting As on the papers, so it didn't seem like reliable grading to me. Plus, he docked me 3 points for reasons not found on the rubric.
Doctor Frost is an amazing professor! The class content is insightful in both a political and religious sense. Doctor Frost is possibly the best professor I have had all year.

600 word weekly "summary and response" essays were a joke. Your grade in the class almost solely depends on these essays and the TA's grade very subjectively. No feed back is given. Grading is random. They probably throw a dart on a board for grades. My 'A' papers were as good as my 'C' papers. Most weeks only 3 people in about 200 got a 10/10.

Honestly, he is nice, but you don't have enough time to have personal relationship with him because the class size is massive. His lecture is hard to understand, especially very unclear what to study for the test. Indeed, it was one of the worst class ever. I trusted the previous feedbacks before I took this class, and I regret my decision.

Dr. Frost has been my favorite professor at BYU. He is incredibly smart, and leads great discussions in class. This class has made me change my minor to political philosophy. I highly recommend that you take this class. There is a lot of reading, but it is totally worth it. My understanding of the world is much more enhanced now.

I loved this class! Professor Frost is so kind and I really enjoyed his lectures. There is reading and a reading quiz due before every class. Every week there is a short paper due, and only 2 tests. Definitely would recommend.

Professor Frost is honestly one of the easiest professors I have taken any college classes from. He is a easy professor not because the material is easy, but because he is incredibly generous, and very very straight forward. HE IS NOT a professor that plays games. he is also a really good lecturer.

I took this class solely for the GE credit but it ended up being my favorite class! Dr. Frost is the nicest guy in the world and really knows what he is talking about. This class basically got me through my first semester at BYU!

Reading quizzes due every class that are easy. Sometimes does in class writings so go to lecture. Weekly essays that are easy. Tests are 20 MC and 2 short answer that I felt were easy. One paper. Lectures were really good and interesting and he seems to really care about the students. Would definitely recommend taking from him

I loved this class! Every class is a lecture/discussion. you MUST take notes. I took detailed notes from every class and I felt that the tests (MP and 2 short answer) were easy. Weekly writeups (ask him if u need help! I felt they were pretty easy), midterm, non-comprehensive final, one essay. At least skim the readings, sometimes pop quizzes

This class was super easy. You have to do a quiz before each class that's easy. The midterm and final are basically exactly like the test. There are 3 papers in this class and they all go off of each other. The grading is so easy. If you put any effort into it and complete it you will get a 95. There are in class assignments so you do have to show

Dr Frost is one of my favorite professors of all time. Why? Because he cares about his students. You can tell by the way he engages everyone and listens to what they have to say! He is always willing to help. He makes interesting topics that can be easily pictured as dull. The work is not extremely heavy and everything is very fair!

Great at teaching confusing concepts and getting the students involved in discussion. Tests were pretty hard but if you do all the readings and go to class you'll be fine. Attendance is not mandatory but there are occasional pop quizzes and in class assignments. He is really good at teaching the info without inserting his opinion.
Very respectful, very caring guy. Gives solid lectures and doesn't make his class too hard. Is very willing to work with the students. Highly recommend taking a class from him
She is a wonderful professor! I loved taking her class and she really cares about her students and she loves encouraging students to take initiative and to learn more about their families!!!

I have taken plenty of religion classes at BYU and this one was the least clear/worst structured. Requirements for projects were unclear, and the grading was harsh for a intro family history class. On top of that the TA was rude and would interrupt class. My husband took the same class with a different professor and he enjoyed it much more.

Honestly I was ok in the class until the professor essentially told us not to study for the final and said it would be super easy. Home to final — it's way harder than she painted it to be. The TA held no review and it was all free response. I just felt lied to. After the exam she said “if your blood is boiling keep in mind the essay portion is 2x”

Amazing class! Dr. Harris is a true expert in her field. It has been one of my favorite classes to learn about family history for a non-family history major/minor. One major biography project that you have lots of time for. Required research log that you must fill out. Two hours every week, but she makes it very doable. Best religion cred!

Dr. Harris is fantastic at guiding students—she teaches you how to research, organize, and discover things you never knew about your family. The class is really just a well-guided 30-hour family history project with no busywork. She's brilliant, connects you with experts, and the TAs are great. Easily one of the most rewarding classes.
Professor Harris was amazing I learned a lot, and enjoyed learning from her.

Dr. Harris teaches life skills in 217. It's not just for a class or for a test because it's mostly about you and your family. I felt like what we do in this class really makes a difference in our relationships and in the community. It's not just about doing a good job in family history but it's also about using family history skills to do good.
Everything you could hope for in a professor.  Helpful, interesting, incredibly knowledgeable.  Awesome experience.
Dr. Harris really cares about her students and wants you to succeed. She is always available to help you and is good at providing feedback that is meaningful and personal. I highly recommend her!

This was the best class I have ever taken and Professor Harris is amazing. She was always available and her lectures were very interesting. You could turn in any assignment late and she was very flexible with extensions. I learned so much in this class and had a lot of fun. I have never felt so loved and individually cared for by a professor 10/10.

I felt like it was unclear what exactly she expected the students to have learned by the end of the class. She seemed to have in her mind exactly how each concept and facet of history fit together, but when she explains it she explained it in a shotgun approach while expecting you to put each of those pieces together by yourself.

I'm a CS major, and I thought I wanted to minor in Family History, but changed my mind. Dr. Harris is very nice. She is accommodating, and is very clear with her instructions on assignments. If you enjoy family history, this is the professor to take it from. Make sure to attend class and don't procrastinate. So many papers and research projects!

The only work in the class is a semester-long project, but it was what made me decide to go into genealogy. Dr. Harris is really passionate about her subject. She doesn't believe in tests, so there's only one exam and it's really easy. When I forgot to turn something in, she let me turn it in two months late for full credit. It's a great class.

This class has a lot of assignments but they're not busy work. They help you learn the material. 50 hrs of genealogical research which includes writing the project summary for the research. Grading can be a little hard and there isn't a ton of feedback. Awesome teacher-Loved going to the lectures. Stay on top of things and take notes in class.

Whatever the class, you have got to take something from Dr. Harris while you're at BYU. One of THE BEST resources and experiences you can have. She is very knowledgeable. No, her classes aren't easy, but the work will pay off big time. Super great to work with. I missed the final because I got the dates mixed up and she let me make it up!
I didn't care for the class, but she was clear about what she wanted and she tried to accommodate to all learning styles.  I just didn't like the subject, I guess.

Very helpful!  The classes are challenging, but she is very clear about what she requires.  She isn't out to trick you.  I learned the best methodology from her.  She has really helped me to improve the quality of my research.
She tries to tailor the class to accomodate every learning style. I felt that she made the material very relatable.
She is excellent! Slackers hate her, but if you do your best she will do whatever she can to help you learn and understand.

She is awesome! She won't baby you, which is probably why some students have rated her low, but if you do you best she will do anything to make sure you learn the material. She really cares about her students and the subject She is honestly the best professor I have ever had at BYU and most of my friends in the Family History Program agree with me.
No Comments

I really enjoyed this class. The most difficult thing in the class is the format - different than just lecturing. She tries to make it a good class for all learning styles. Readings are crucial to class, however if you miss a reading then someone who did the reading had posted about it on a class blog. Not a bad class at all - I enjoyed it a lot.

She was an okay teacher. nothing great,but she wasnt horrible eaither.  the lectures can be usefull but boaring.  All you do is take notes. If you have never done any family history reasearch before it wil be hard to follow, but if you have done some before you will be bored.  its a no win situation.  She doesnt grade very fairly
I had an illness and she was completely understanding.  This isn't a hard class.  Go to class!!  Do the assignments and reading and you'll be fine.  Just make sure you can put in the time.

Umm...lame! Went to class the first few times, never went back. Totally unhelpful! I wanted to take this class because I wanted to learn to love family history, I tried really hard to enjoy it, but couldn't. The assignments and project and completely time consuming. Try another teacher.

I was really hoping this class would help me with my family history but it was SO FRUSTRATING!  The tests were not too hard but lectures put me to sleep and were terribly confusing.  Amy is a nice person but she does a bad job explaining how to do things.  There is also a 30 hour project so BEWARE! Take this class from another teacher!
I loved this class! Dr. Tanner seems so genuine. The homework takes about an hour to complete. The exams are easy if you go over the study guide beforehand.

Dr. Tanner really cares and wants all her students to do well. Class can sometimes be boring but going to the TA hours is very helpful. There is a lot of homework but none of it is too difficult. Dr. Tanner is very sweet and kind and wants to help everyone pass.
I love Dr. Tanner! Really great, helpful with students who aren't as familiar with difficult math concepts, really just a delight.

Dr. Tanner is sweet and does care about her students. However, she is very picky on exams and you have to be very specific. Assignments are all on paper so you have to be at class to get the homework. The homework is graded on participation which is nice. She does take a long time to grade. Lectures are very boring and seem like a lot of busy work.

Prof Tanner was an awesome lady, and really knew what she was teaching. She cares about her students understanding and learning of the curriculum, therefore she offers test corrections for every test within the class. Homework and attendance are the main portions of the grade, both of which are super easy. Would recommend!

The way she taught the information was very clear, organized, and interesting. The homework assignments are quick and easy. The exams are very manageable. You will do a lot of group work in class. Attendance and participation are part of your grade. Dr. Tanner is very caring and great at answering questions and concerns.

She's super sweet! Tests are closed book but take home. you can make back half points on problems you got wrong. Class was somewhat boring and some things were surprisingly hard but overall good class

Dr. Tanner is very organized and prepared for class. But her lessons are so long and boring. I don't know anyone that enjoyed this class. She also plays favorites and will grade your exams harshly if you don't actively comment in class. She is very professional but also kind of treats the class like kids (seating chart, dumb activities).

I loved this class! Dr. Tanner is very organized and good at checking in with each student to see where they're at in understanding the concepts. You'll have a page or two of homework after each class but they're not hard and help a lot in your learning. She's amazing at what she does, take this class from her!

This class was very boring for me. It is an easy A, so don't be scared to take it from her. She is very kind, and she does well at presenting the material clearly. She gives amazing feedback to help you improve. You have 2 assignments once a week, about 3 exams, and 2 observation assignments. Very low stress class. Attendance is important.

I really loved this class. She does a great job teaching by encouraging work with a group and student participation during class. The homework is pretty easy and helps solidify learning and the structure of the class is consistent and easy to follow.

I loved this class! There some difficult concepts but Professor Tanner reassured us it is normal to not understand the concept completely. Everything is printed out which I loved, all notes are to be done in a notebook. Homework is handed out and expected to be done next class, fairly easy usually 1-2 pages. She is very specific for midterm.

I honestly think Dr. Tanner is the best professor I've had so far at BYU. I took her class during spring term and loved it! The class itself was very interesting, but my favorite thing was that you could tell Dr. Tanner knew what she was teaching; she's a veteran teacher. The hw wasn't hard, and the tests were take-home. Take this class from her!!!

Awesome class -- I hope to take it earlier. She is caring, amiable, and always want to help you out. HWs are graded by completion, and the exams are take-home. Proof studies and the final reflection are generously graded. No need to read the textbook -- as long as you're familiar with the slides and HWs, you can get a decent grade.

She is very understanding of absences and is willing to work with you. She knows how to teach very well. The homework was a pretty balanced load throughout the semester, with 3 take home tests and a couple book response write ups. Quick at responding to emails.

Dr. Tanner is so knowledgeable. I learned so much from her. You talk a lot in groups about homework and teaching strategies. You also get to interview kids in school to learn their thinking styles which is fun. The three tests including the final were all take home tests which was nice.

This class was really helpful in understanding how to teach kids math. Classes were fun and engaging and we even got to interview kids a couple times which was super cute. Homework wasn't difficult but I learned a lot from it!

Prof Tanner is great! The class was exactly like 305, even though I had a different teacher. She is very kind and will work through problems as much as you need. Also you can do test corrections which is GREAT. I wish I could take another class from her, because it was such a good class!

3rd easiest math class at BYU (Math 191 and 391 are easier). Nice lecturer and online activities. This is actually not quite a math class, but a history class with philosophical thinking skills. Lots of readings, though. Take it if you need to fulfill a math credit and want to explore things deeply.

Great course! It wasn't an easy A (don't underestimate the biography project) but there was no busywork and I learned a ton, and honestly it was fun. She gives a lot of opportunities to engage with the mathematics the way people did historically, which is fun. No memorizing names or dates, no exams. And you give yourself your final grade.

Professor tanner makes an online class actually entertaining and enjoyable. We had interactive activities, frequent and interesting readings and a pretty cool biography midterm assignment. Philosophy of mathematics is a fairly easy class if you put in the time and the way professor tanner has this class organized it's easy to keep track of HW.

I really liked having Dr. Tanner as my professor. She is very caring and wants all of her students to succeed in the class. It's a decent amount of work: about 2 pages of homework a night & the exams can be a little bit tricky, but not too bad. She did move on to new material pretty quickly, so just beware of that if you don't understand. Love her!

Took Spring term. She's a really nice person, but I wasn't a fan of how the class was structured since I'm a pure math major. Participation is graded, which was really silly to me (prob not so much if you're a MathEd major). In short, lots of reading, you have in class group worksheets, you have to give a couple presentations, but no exams.
She was a good teacher, and I loved the class. However, she wasn't always the best at explaining things to people who didnt understand.

I really enjoyed Dr. Tanner's class. She was a fantastic teacher. She explained things in depth and made sure everyone understood. She gave us problem packets to help us work through the lecture materials to make sure we understood the concepts.

Great class. She takes things slow and makes sure everyone is on the same page. The four tests are take home, so very low stress and you can spend as much time as you need. Each class you have two sheets of homework due, but it's graded on completion. You learn a lot about how kids think about math. Prof. Tanner is super kind and fun

Dr. Tanner models the type of teaching she wants you to learn. Read the books she gives (they're both interesting and useful). The activities in class are both fun and help you to think about the concepts. She lets you choose your final grade, but you do the work anyway because it is helpful. Go to the MEA activities early.

Dr. Tanner is an amazing teacher! She does a great job at teaching challenging concepts and fills the time really well. I loved how I learned even though I didn't love what I learned. She helped prepare me to be a better math teacher.

Sister Tanner is an awesome teacher. She is very clear with instructions, very organized, and is very helpful. She assigns homework each day, but you can go over it as a group the class before you turn it in. There's a lot of information given in this class so you have to attend and pay attention, but it's a good class!

Dr. Tanner is incredibly helpful. She really helps you know the material. If you attend class every time and really participate in the group work, you will do well! She gives very thorough reviews of the material before the tests, and she even lets you retake tests so you can get some points back. She really cares and is willing to work with you!
Angel. Literally perfect. Her HW is solely graded off if you did it and her tests are easy.

Amy is great at explaining difficult concepts through interactive learning. She is also very open if you need help with anything. This class is easy, just do the work. Each homework assignment is worth 5% of your grade so missing more than one will really hurt you.

The best math ed teacher! 2 hour long classes but the time went by so fast because we were so engaged in learning. Lots of hands-on activities to use in future classrooms. She explains things very well. I learned as much about teaching from watching how she did it as I did from what I learned in the class. I loved this class - thanks to Dr. Tanner!

The curriculum is well designed! He or the TA always gave clear feedback on the homework, and he was very responsive outside of class. There are a lot of readings and biweekly 50 question quizzes (keep up) but they are very concept-based and really help you learn and internalize the material. He genuinely cares about you and wants you to learn!

He never really taught anything. Most of the semester, you're kinda on your own. There is an absurd amount of work, multiple long quizzes a week, labs, etc., and none of it is clearly explained. The Stata software is frustrating and difficult, and again, very poorly taught, so you're on your own. Don't take this teacher if you can avoid it.

Burt is a great professor, and his class was easy-going. My only gripe is that we were rarely tested on the Book of Mormon outside of reflections, so when the final came up, I felt unprepared, even after studying the study guide. If cramming is your style, then this is a great class, but I know some people struggle to learn without a challenge.

I originally did not want to take the book of mormon class but ended up having to, he made the class enjoyable and spoke about the book of mormon in a very educated and refreshing way. Fantastic teacher, I learned so much.
He didn't want this to be an overwhelming class but instead a class where we got to learn for the joy of it on a whole new level. He was fun and very understanding with everyone.

As long as I showed up, this class was never a stress for me. Prof. Burt definitely puts his whole heart into the class, and it never fails to put a smile on my face! He explores the Book of Mormon and its themes in a really unique, deep way that gets me thinking for myself.

Brother Burt has a passion for the Book of Mormon that is contagious. His lectures are very engaging and bring a different perspective to gospel principles. He is very understanding when it comes to your grade and will go the extra mile to help you achieve the outcome that you deserve.

Professor Burt is a very knowledgeable professor. He cares deeply about the content he covers. He discusses different viewpoints from philosophers as well as different faith that relate to themes in the Book of Mormon all centered on Christ. He has inspired me and has helped me learn of Christ. I would recommend Professor Burt, 10/10.

Lectures didn't feel like they helped me all that much, but Professor Cluff wants to help his students succeed. My main complaints are about the course itself, which is shared across all of the professors teaching it. The course-wide grading rubric will smell your fear, so go to the TA Help Lab and get to know the TAs, and you'll be just fine.

Professor Cluff explained the material clearly, kept the class engaging, and always made time to help when concepts felt confusing. His teaching style made the course feel manageable and even enjoyable, and it was obvious he genuinely wanted students to understand and succeed. I really appreciated the effort he put into every lesson.

I loved having Professor Cluff! It was a small class with example based lectures and lots of opportunities for class participation and discussion that helped with understanding how to think through complex blocks of code. The class had online videos available and attendance was not mandatory. And Professor Cluff is kind and willing to work with you
He was so kind, and caring. I enjoyed his class, and we learned a lot.

He was a bit unorganized in his lectures. The course is somewhat easy (coming from someone who had absolutely zero experience with python). You can pretty much pass the class with the textbook and Google alone. Easy class for an A, Burt maybe pick another professor to actually learn the material.

Andrew Cluff is the worst professor I have ever had at BYU. His lectures are a complete waste of time and dont help you for the checkpoints or assignments. The syllabus describes the class as an intro course for students to gain exposure. Not the case at all. He also did not follow the syllabus at all. Not accommodating at all. Hes just terrible

BYU Singers has easily been one of the best aspects of my adult life. Dr. Crane is a bit hard to read at first and doesn't come across as very approachable, but he's simply the perfect leader for BYU Singers. He's extremely invested in the choir's wellbeing and manages to create an impressively good balance between seriousness and lightheartedness

Dr. Crane is one of the best, most competent directors in the choral world. He also takes time to truly connect with his students and is a very safe professor if you don't fit the BYU mould. He is so caring and compassionate; he's truly one of those professors who will change your life. 10/10 BYU could not have a more qualified person for the job.
musical and directional genius. really cares about his students. passion for singing, conducting, choral and vocal excellence and diet coke.

Amazing, I loved singing in the choir with him. Totally stand-up guy, super caring, hard-working, honest, determined, and really good at what he does. You can tell he really cares, both about the students and the music. Best class ever.

Dr. Crane has changed my life and the lives of all of my peers. He is dedicated to excellence and helps us achieve it through carefully prepared lesson plans as well as going with things in the moment. This man is brilliant and dedicated and ready to help you unlock your full potential.

Dr. Crane is definitely my favorite professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about each of his student's happiness and success. He notices when someone is gone. Every person matters. You can tell that he loves what he does and that he loves us. We have fun in class and we don't waste time. He is not only our conductor but also our friend.

Dr. R. Andrew Crane is the best man on the campus of the BYU. He is incredibly dedicated to his duties and works incredibly hard. As a conductor, he is precise and easy to follow, inspiring passion. The Crane is a master of his art and imparts an astounding amount of his hard earned doctoral knowledge to us lowly students on the daily. Funny af too
Dr. Crane is easily one of the best conductors that I have ever had the fortune to work with; he is among the most professional and driven professors at which I have studied under.

Dr. Fry embodies what BYU expects of a professor, IMO. He intellectually challenges his students, while also leaving room for spiritual inspiration. Thermo is a hard class, Dr. Fry makes the class so manageable. He teaches very clearly, is willing to listen, is compassionate. His class is set-up for success. One of the best ChEn professors.
Andrew Fry is a very good teacher. Course materials are very organized and neat, the curriculum was clear and presented very effectively.
Dr. Fry is honestly on of the most down to earth and relatable professors I've ever had. Thermo is a HARD class, but he taught it in a very clear and manageable way.
Dry Fry is a stud! Probably my favorite teacher ever. Do pre exams and be cautious on exams to not make arithmetic errors because you dont get partial credit until test corrections.
Best teacher at BYU hands-down.

Dr. Fry is a great teacher. Thermo is a hard subject and Dr. Fry does a great job teaching it clearly. The homework can be challenging but Dr. Fry is always available to help. There are several tests that are open textbook. He tells great stories before lecturing and is willing to help any way he can.

Dr. Fry is one of the best professors at BYU! He teaches a hard class but does it very well. He explains things clearly and is super easy to talk to outside of class. In fact a group of students went rock climbing with him after the final XD . Also he is super funny and has the best stories!

Thermo is a hard class, Dr. Fry makes the class so manageable. He teaches very clearly, is willing to listen, is compassionate. His class is set-up for success. One of the best ChEn professors.
