Dry Fry is a stud! Probably my favorite teacher ever. Do pre exams and be cautious on exams to not make arithmetic errors because you dont get partial credit until test corrections.
Best teacher at BYU hands-down.

Dr. Fry is a great teacher. Thermo is a hard subject and Dr. Fry does a great job teaching it clearly. The homework can be challenging but Dr. Fry is always available to help. There are several tests that are open textbook. He tells great stories before lecturing and is willing to help any way he can.

Dr. Fry is one of the best professors at BYU! He teaches a hard class but does it very well. He explains things clearly and is super easy to talk to outside of class. In fact a group of students went rock climbing with him after the final XD . Also he is super funny and has the best stories!

Professor Hedges' class is how every religion class should be. Attendance made up 75% of our grade and the rest was a few small and quick reading assignments. His goal was to have a place where we could come and not stress about what we'd be graded on, rather enjoy the material being taught. Got to enjoy a semester-long story of church history!

Professor Hedges is an amazing religion professor. This is the first religion class I've taken where there were no difficult quizzes based on the lecture and where I felt like I could just sit back and enjoy. Professor Hedges knows each of his students by name and remembers you. He is wonderful and I wish I could take his class again.

This was my last religion class in college, and it was hands down my favorite class of all time. Hedge's goal is to help students genuinely remember this content. To do this, he makes 83% of your grade attendance-based. The remaining points are several easy readings and responses, and a final that is 25 true-false questions. Amazing teacher and man

This class is so easy. There's only a few easy assignments throughout the semester. Although his lectures are boring and he's a bit disorganized. He talks quiet and writes a few barely legible things on the board so it's hard to pay attention. But he's super flexible is such a nice guy. He's super smart and will help you understand church history.

Talks, looks, and acts like President Eyring. Amazing lectures that feel very conversational, but take meticulous notes or the tests will sink you. Do the readings and the quizzes are super easy. Talk to him about grades if you have problems. One of my favorite religion professors so far. I can't say enough good about him and his class.

Prof. Hedges is so kind and an amazing lecturer. Class really helped my testimony. However, do not(!) take it for credit. Every test question was worded very carefully to mess you up. And even if you can get past that, if you miss random things said in class, you won't do well on the tests. Tests weighted heavily. Ridiculously difficult class.

Fabulous professor. He is the best history teacher I have ever had. He presents the information clearly and in story format. He makes study guides for the tests. He expects you to remember what is reasonable. You'll learn a lot, but you'll enjoy learning it. Do go to class, it's really important and it's really interesting!

He is a nice guy with a good heart, however, if you don't take notes on every single word he says, you will do poorly on the exams. The readings are LONG. His exams are the most ridiculous things I have ever taken. It's basically all on random facts that he briefly mentions. If you want it to feel like a religion class, don't take it from Hedges.

He is a great guy and my testimony grew a lot through this class, but holy crap do you need to take another religion class. His tests are MONSTROUSLY difficult. He acts like this is a 3 credit class instead of a religion class. Expecting you to write down everything he says on in the lecture because you never know what will be on the test. ITS BAD!

I loved this class. The material was really interesting and Professor Hedges was willing to work with the class on deadlines of assignments. The tests were a lot of memorization but I did pretty good with a little of effort

Take this professor! He is very kind and works with you on things. The quizzes are easy if you do the reading, and the reading isn't bad. Pay attention in class and take good notes, and you'll have no problem with the exam! His lectures are VERY interesting and easy to pay attention to! Take Professor Hedges!

I loved having Professor Hedges!! He just sits and lectures with no slides but is extremely interesting. I feel like that helps with notes because we just write what we hear. He is friendly, humble, and clearly knows his stuff. He also has a great perspective.

Dr. Hedges clearly knows a lot about the subject, but is very clear in separating his personal opinions and views from the Church's position. There's out of class reading to do, and his lectures go along to perfectly cover all the material you need to know.

There is not another religion professor that teaches like Dr. Hedges. He doesn't rely on PowerPoints, but instead tells the story of church history in a narrative form, one that is easy to take notes on. Aside from the tests, most of the points in the class come from just completing the assignments. The tests are multiple choice and are easy.

Easy class. No busy work/pointless assignments. Just 2 papers and 2 exams the whole year. I love the content of the course and I engaged with what is taught. The professor has an apostle-like voice and sometimes I can get sleepy. But, overall, an easy, yet informative class.

I love professor Hedges! This was by far my favorite religion class that I have taken in my 3 years at BYU. His class is taught like a history class. There isn't much homework. The tests were kind of hard, and his study guides weren't as helpful as they could have been. Overall I really liked the class and found it super interesting

Professor Hedges is a nice guy. but for the love of God take a different Religion class. This class was easy to follow reading and lecture wise, his tests are insanely hard, requiring you to memorize unbelievable amounts of information, and you'll get tripped on tricky wording intentionally. It's a religion class, it shound't be this difficult.

Don't get me wrong, he is a great lecturer and really works to help you build your testimony, but his tests are wack. The tests are supposedly based on what's taught in class, but there are so many things we NEVER talk about that show up on the test! Audit the class if you want to build your testimony, but if you're doing this for a grade, DON'T GO

Tests are ridiculous for a religion class, especially the final. All memorization of dates and names and the questions are purposefully worded to mess you up. Don't take this class if you are looking for an easy religion class to boost your GPA, it will do the opposite. Lectures are all on the chalkboard, with half the material being irrelevant.

I never leave reviews for professors, but this is my favorite religion professor I have ever taken a class from. He cares much more about building testimonies and learning than he does about grading harshly. Take this class!

Brother Hedges is a great man. I respect him so much. His class felt more like a history class than a religion class, which I found super interesting. I loved going to his class, even though I feel like I could've gotten notes from someone else. Class includes weekly reading quizzes, a couple of papers, and three tests. Pretty easy, and I loved it.

This is one of my favorite classes I have ever taken at BYU and it is certainly because of him. He is such a kind and gentle soul that works so well with you. Seriously if you just talk to him, he sees the difference between enforcing arbitrary rules about grades and working to your individual situation. He teaches with the Spirit.

Sorry but his class is incredibly boring. No visuals, just writing on the chalkboard every so often. Tests were ridiculously hard and pointless. How is memorizing a bunch of random names helping me increase my faith in the Savior and in the Restoration? I studied hard and still got screwed by this class. If you can't memorize well, don't take.

Prof. Hedges has been one of my FAVORITE religion teachers at BYU. He cares more about the Spirit being in class than he does about testing hard - if you go to class and write down notes, you will pass the test with flying colors. He made pioneer history seem so interesting, and had very little work in his class, making you really learn the lessons

This has been my favorite class taken at BYU!! Take his pioneers class if you can!!! Its so interesting you you learn so much. Brother Hedges is AWESOME and cares a lot about his students (he gives you all the resources to do well). I laughed at whoever said his tests were super hard- your tested exactly on the class lecture

Dr. Hedges is an expert at what he does. Take his class! I was skeptical about taking a class about church history, it sounded boring. He delved into important topics like polygamy and took the time to answer everyone's questions. The only weekly homework is reading the one chapter in the free textbook.
I absolutely LOVED this class, but the difficulty of the tests was a little crazy... Too tricky of questions for a religion class in my opinion. But Dr. Hedges is incredible.

The workload is fairly light. He gives one three-point quiz per week on the reading, and an easy term paper (you get 100% if you meet the page requirement). THe quizes and the midterm/final are easy if you fill out the study guide he gives you. All of his lectures were super funny and interesting. TAKE THE CLASS FROM HIM!
Brother Hedges is amazing. I was excited to take this class in general, but he made it my favorite class I've taken at BYU. The textbook can just be found for free on the church website.

I loved taking a church history class from a professor with such clear and realistic expectations. Getting a good grade wasn't a matter of guesswork. It was a matter of putting in a consistent 2 or 3 hours a week on reading and studying for tests. The term paper was also a good assignment, and not too hard. I highly recommend Dr. Hedges.

He has been my fav religion prof. so far. Very knowledgable about many aspects of Church history. You need to go to class everyday if you want an A, as the exams are almost explicitly from his lectures. 2 midterms (20% ea.), final (30%), 2 papers (9% ea., pretty sure he always gives 100% if you do it), reading (10%, self reported), class eval (2%).

This is the perfect religion class! I learned a lot, but it wasn't very much work. Almost no readings (besides continuing your personal reading of the Book of Mormon) and very fair tests. He loves the Book of Mormon and has many interesting academic and spiritual insights. He really cares about his students and how they're doing in the class.

Professor Hedges is a VERY GOOD instructor. Yes, it's important to attend class (duh! this isn't an online class). Theres nothing on the test that isnt covered in class. Homework is minimal and can be done at an easy pace. If you don't understand something, Prof. Hedges will do anything to help. Anyone with a negative review simply didnt try.

This turned out to be the hardest history class I have ever taken. You have to become an expert on the D&C to pass his ridiculous tests. If you miss even one class, you are in big trouble. Make sure you take the class with a friend who takes good notes. I definitely recommend taking it from Dorius or Brooks, it will save you so much time and effort
Good lectures, caring instructors, inspiring papers, and INFERNAL TESTS.

I have absolutely loved Prof. Hedges' class. He has an astounding knowledge of the scriptures and is awesome at explaining difficult concepts. His lectures are awesome. The class is very easy to pass as long as you take good notes. He cares much more about your spiritual growth than a syllabus and it shows.

Okay--I honestly hate taking religion courses because I feel they are subjective, graded way too heavy for 2 credit hour, blazay blazay. BUT--Professor Hedges is literally the ONLY religion professor I have loved. Not only does he care bout his students, but he gives you the facts, opinions, and lets you know which is which. Take him, and only him.

Brother Hedges is possibly the best religion teacher I've had so far. He is real, honest, spiritual, and knows so much! He is so nice and will meet with you to discuss any of your questions. You need to pay attention in class, since that's where he gets all his test questions. His tests are straightforward.

Brother Hedges is one of the most kind and genuine people I have ever met. His lectures are so interesting, and he never uses powerpoint so you do have to go to class. If you pay attention you will do well. He answers tough questions honestly and is super smart. I wish I wasn't graduating so I could take another class from him!

I loved Professor Hedges. He is by far the best lecturer I've come across at BYU. He  just stands in front of the class and tells the information as if he's telling a story. He always makes sure you know the information though. He's good at answering difficult questions and really cares about each of his students! TAKE THIS CLASS!

Honestly my favorite class ever! I wish I wasn't graduating so that I could take another class from him! Quizzes each week, but do the reading and you will be fine. Tests are easy, just study your notes from lecture. Research paper does take some time, but he is a super easy grader. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

I love Brother Hedges! This is honestly my favorite religion class I've taken. He has weekly reading quizzes but as long as you did the reading and come to class you'll be fine.  His tests are heavily lecture based so you need to come to class.  He does require a term paper but he's a pretty lenient grader.  Definitely would take him again!

This guy is absolutely fantastic. I took his Joseph Smith class and Pioneer class and I considered it an honor and a privilege to attend. Seriously the guy is easily my favorite religion professor ever. He knows church history extremely well and his lectures were super interesting, and I loved the class! Do yourself a favor and take his classes!!!!

I didn't do as well as I hoped, but even still I have no reservation saying this class was like a 6/5 content wise. It was so amazing to learn from one of the lead historians on the JS papers. Super humble teacher that can answer just about any question openly and honestly about JS. Really helped my testimony of JS grow. Hard but totally worth it!

This was my third Church History class at BYU, and thanks to Bro. Hedges, it was my favorite. Such a knowledgeable, engaging lecturer, one of the nicest guys you'll meet, and extremely helpful. Very skilled at handling tough topics in Church History. The class is very manageable & stress-free. If you need a religion credit, take this class.

Willing to discuss hard and sensitive topics. Creates atmosphere where you can ask any question, and he really encourages questions so we can get better understanding.  He really helped strengthen my testimony of Joseph Smith and the restoration. Easy grader. Class has lots of interesting material. Has a deep understanding of early church history.

Best teacher at BYU! Offers a lot of extra credit. Extremely personable. Looks like President Eyring :)  He himself says his class is designed to be easy. If history interests you then this is the class for you. He loves history and his lectures naturally draw you into the topic. Extremely easy grader. Highly recommend

As someone who is not a fan of BYU religion courses, I absolutely loved brother Hedges' class. He cares about the students and the material. My favorite thing about brother Hedges was his transperency about church histroy, something that I find very refreshing. I will definitely be taking classes from him again.

By far best teacher at BYU. So sweet and caring. He got really sick and was out for a couple weeks, and you could tell how hard it was for him to be away from class. He loves what he teaches and makes it simple to understand. Go to class and do the reading, you have a weekly quiz in class of 3 questions, normally multiple choice. Overall easy class

Wow I have never been in a class where I was clinging on to every word the professor was saying It was awesome to just bask in the amazingness of the lectures you have daily quizzes based on the reading but he tells you what you need to look for in the reading in order to do well He teaches you and then he tests you on what he teaches, a rare trait

Brother Hedges is by far the best professor I have had at BYU. He knows the history of the Church forwards and backwards and is willing to discuss the tougher subjects in class or after during his office hours. His tests are fact based and come straight from lecture so make sure to take detailed notes. He really wants everyone to succeed.

Brother Hedges is an amazing teacher! I loved this class so much and would take it again in a heartbeat. I'm going to take more classes from Bro Hedges including the next class Rel 342. It is an easy class but you learn so much and will feel such a stronger understanding and appreciation for the early saints.  Highly recommend Bro Hedges

One of the best religion professors I have had. He is clear in his lecturers and is easy to follow. His teachings are all based on primary sources and proven facts. Go to class, pay attention, take good notes and you will learn incredible amount and wont want to stop learning. Tests reflect exactly what he teaches in class.  HIGHLY recommended!

I learned so much from Hedges. His lectures are very interesting and he knows a lot about church history. Go to class and review the study guide and you'll ace the tests. There are a few readings, but you have the entire semester to do them. He is very laid back and only requires one easy 5 page paper.
Brother Hedges wants the students to succeed. He really cares about the topic and is SO knowledgable about it. The class was easy and interesting... the best of both worlds!

I took REL C 342 my first semester at BYU and I LOVE Professor Hedges! He doesn't use powerpoints or anything, so you are responsible for coming to class and taking notes, but he's so funny and knowledgeable. Will definitely be looking for classes to take from him in the future.

Great lecturer, he just starts talking without notes or slides!  There's a lot of reading, but it's all extra nice-to-know stuff, so go to class EVERY TIME and take notes or you'll fail the exams. However, I had taken D&C already so this class was easy. Takes lots of time on controversial stuff in Church History. Enlightening, easy class.

One of the best religion professors out there! This was my favorite religion course I've taken thus far! You will enjoy every second of this class and you will do well! As long as you listen and take notes you'll be golden. Professor Hedges is super helpful too!

Best religion professor at BYU. He's so helpful, and spends a lot of time discussing the more "controversial" parts of Joseph Smith's history. Extremely knowledgeable and Christ-like, he's awesome. The exams are a little difficult, but if you use his office hours, getting an A or A- isn't too tough.

Great guy really nice teacher and the class was not bad but man his tests were hard especially his final. I will admit I was not the most prepared but geeze his final was one of the hardest test I have taken at BYU. This class made me hate religion classes at BYU a lot of knowledge & no spiritual growth. I would find another teacher if I were you.

I really liked him as a teacher!  He tried really hard to answer our questions with actual facts.  My testimony was really strengthened.  I was rarely bored and loved coming to class.  It's a class you can't skip because what you read is not what is on the test.  He was quick to respond to emailed questions.
If you want a class with lighthearted lectures and difficult tests that cover topics not discussed in class then take this class

AWESOME! teaches the bom class like you actually learned something on your mission, ie, doesn't insult your intelligent by teaching seminary lessons. he shows insights into bom scholars' research and points where critics get hung up on details in the bom, particularly very difficult problems to resolve. Fun to take if you're a bible geek. nicest gu

Hedges is awesome, and this is not coming from one of those weird Peter Priesthood types. He makes Church History interesting and doesn't sugar coat it. He tells it how it was. One paper, and a map quiz. Reading is not mandatory, and you the tests consist of names and dates. An hour with flash cards and you got an A. Sister Black who . . .

Bro Hedges is amazing.  He has so much knowledge stored in his head and when he shares it with us it is so simple to understand.  I took the first half of B.O.M and got an average of 96 on the tests with barely any study b/c i retain everything he teaches.

Great class. i like the way that Bro. Hedges distinguishes between commonly held opinion and true doctrine. He is careful to say only what is true. If he gives an opinion he specifically prefaces it. I really enjoyed this class. I would be more than willing to take any class from him. One of the best religion classes, and the tests are easy.

Bro Hedges is a great teacher.  He did a good job of bringing in the spirit, included the class in the discussion, and taught very interesting points on the BoM without any busy work. The best teacher ever! He cares so much about his students and the gospel and he doesn't present his opinion as the only right answer. He is extremely humble and extremely knowledgeable. Awesome Professor! His class provided exactly what I wanted: A nice spiritual uplift, virtually no homework, and an easy A.  He is remarkably humble and knowledgeable. Encourages class discussion and invites the Spirit very well!  Take one of his classes if you can!

Best teacher I have had at BYU. I took BoM (2nd half) from him last Winter; just finished up Ch. History with him. BOTH classes were absolutely fantastic. Absolutely fabulous teacher! I can't say enough good things about him. He knows so much, knows how to transmit that knowledge, and keeps it incredibly interesting no matter what he is talking about. Grades and tests are extremely fair. Will definitely take more classes from him!

Hedges is da' bomb! I'm teliing you, if you are thinking A-Dog (Andy) for a class think no more and add the man! You will not be dissapointed! Best teacher I've ever had, that's for sure! One of the only teachers that you may have that will know your name and who you are and interested in talking with you about whatever after class! Great Man Andy!

Ok, so Hedges has been the best proffer I've ever got here at the Y! Absolutely fab! Take any class that you want from this man and you should learn loads and have blast while you're at it! Everyone I know has loved his classes! Honestly, best teacher at Brigham Young right here! Tests are not hard as long as you go to class and take some notes.

Great professor! I found his lectures to be very interesting and engaging. He doesn't try to trick you or anything on th tests, which I always like. Amazing man! I took him based off of people's comments on the website and it was well worth it! It was seriously my favorite class. He is totally lenient and awesome. I'm taking Church History Part 2 from him in the fall.

AMAZING TEACHER!!! Looked forward to his classes every week! Why isn't he teaching more??? He is such a laid back guy yet maintains a certain reverence towards the subject that it feels like home whenever in his class. I'm taking his Church History class in the fall and am stoked! I loved Brother Hedges!This is how every religion class should be!He teaches very well! Way awesome teacher! I loved every second of it. My only complaint is that he doesn't teach more classes!

Great teacher! The tests and assignments were fair. He's a great lecturer, so I really enjoyed listening to him tell church history stories. I could remember what we had talked about so that I only referenced notes for dates, etc.

Hedges is great. This is the most interesting class on the church I have taken. He's a way nice guy. Course is easy, 2 two-page papers and a map quiz and 2 midterms and a final. Reading is optional. The best religion teacher at BYU by far.  The nicest guy there is and he is extremely helpful.  He understands that other classes take up a lot of time so it is a class you can get an easy A in if you just show up and take notes.  Great Class!

This is the second class I've taken from Bro. Hedges, and I was not disappointed. He teaches by the spirit and is always willing to answer questions. He understands you have other classes and does not demand alot of your time. While he doesn't require class attendance, his tests come straight from lectures. So don't miss class and take good notes.

Brother Hedges is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He always brings the spirit into the class and has such interesting insights. I really hope to take more classes from him. My testimony grew so much while in his class. If you go to class and take good notes, you'll do fine. I loved his teaching style! Thanks for everything :)

Bro. Hedges is AMAZING! I'm planning on taking many more classes from him. He lead spiritually and intellectually engaging class discussions. Dr. Hedges was a really good professor who brought the spirit into the room. Although, his tests were a little on the difficult side. This class was awesome!! Bro. Hedges is a great teacher who just wants his students to grow spiritually and understand the BoM better. There are 2 short papers that you get full credit for if you do them, and then a midterm and a final. It is a very stress-free class and I would highly recommend it to anyone.
Brother Hedges is the best! He is such an incredibly kind and humble man and he knows a lot! Take good notes in lectures and tests are easy!

Professor Hedges is an amazing professor!!!  He teaches strait from the Book of Mormon and backs the book with facts rather than opinions.  His tests are a little tricky, but not terribly difficult.  I found his class very enlightening and spiritual.

Bro. Hedges is really an awesome teacher. He isn't afraid to get down to some really hard issues, and he is always willing to help you with anything. Professor Hedges is awesome! He really cares about the students; he even learned all of our names. He's really interesting to listen to and creates a comfortable environment in the class. Tests are pretty easy, based almost entirely on lecture. Great guy!

This is a guy who cares about his students! There are papers to write but it is a given 100% so long as you do them. The tests take some studying becuase of the amount of material but a class I would recommend! He is a great professor
He's awesome!

Incredible teacher!  He bends over backwards to help his students.  He is soft and kind, and he is humble and respectful to his students.  If he does not know the answer, he admits it. awesome professor...I took 3 different classes from him and learned a ton.

Outstanding teacher!!  I can be critical with religion professors but he's the best I've had so far. Class was OK...Only take this class if you are good at memorizing facts! the tests were 90% matching and true/false about dates, people, and section numbers. Also a 5 page paper, but that was easy. i wrote it day before it was due and got 100%

Hedges is my favorite religion professor EVER. Took him for the second half of D&C and Church History 341, and loved both classes. CH 341 was one of the best courses I have ever taken. Bro. Hedges is an awesome teacher. His lectures were interesting... take lots of notes because he tests on what is said in class.  He is really helpful in preparing for test. Great class, I recommend it!

Brother Hedges is awesome!  Very kind and helpful.  Paper was 5 pages, but graded extremely generously.  Final was hard, but other tests were much easier.  Lectures were very interesting.  Loved this Prof.  Highly recommended.
Tests involve memorizing facts from lecture.  Lectures are good.

Bro. Hedges is probably one of the best teachers.  You learn a lot while the class not being ridiculously hard.  As long as you go to class (and you'll want to-it's that good) and take notes, you'll do fine! just make sure you go to class...it will make or break your grade

I loved Hedges and his class.  His class is great if you attend. I really enjoyed this class. Very knowledgable of subject matter. excellent instructor. assignments are fairly graded and not too hard. knows what a 2hr class should be.

Hedges really is great. Lectures are so interesting! He is willing to take interesting/important tangents. We had 1 quiz, 2 tests + final, and 1 5pg paper. Great teacher; learned a lot!  His class is very reasonable, if you simply go to class and take good notes.  Grade is made up of three tests, a final, and a term paper.  I would definitely recommend him.

AMAZING class, I learned a ton. And Prof. Hedges is great. He's very helpful, very chill, and he knows his stuff. I'm taking another class from him next semester. He's way good, and the class is really interesting. Easy tests, just pay attn in class and take detailed notes.

Easiest class i have ever taken.  He is smart and super laid back.  He gives you everything you need to know for the tests.  He is a very nice guy and is flexible.  Tests are easy (took me 15 min).  A nonstressful interesting and fun class.  Guaranteed A!

One of the smartest religion teachers out there.  His class was way interesting, and it did not require loads of work like other religion classes.  He keeps things interesting and the tests go right along with lecture.

One of the easiest classes I have taken. If you are a history major, you will be pleasantly surprised to learn that the research paper does not even require a thesis. Bro. Hedges is the best religion teacher I've ever had. He is always willing to answer any question and makes it easy to ask any question without you feeling uncomfortable. Bro Hedges was great.  His class was really easy and fun.  Very friendly and interesting.

Bro. Hedges is fantastic for all the reasons everyone else said.  One day I spoke in class (for the first time a few weeks into the semester) and he called on me by name! Great class! You don't have to buy a textbook, you just bring your Book of Mormon. He is very instresting and I learned a lot just by going to lectures. Go to class and you will do good on the tests, and you will learn a lot about D and C

Perfect religion class - easy, but you still learn a lot. He's definitely not one of those religion teachers who's out to prove that religion is a serious subject. I loved this teacher, I am planning on taking his other class.  His lectures are very interesting, his test study guides are basically the test, and he knows a ton.  Very helpful and friendly, low stress class.  I HIGHLY recommend!!!!!

Wonderful lectures. Made sure we all understood that this was a 'no stress' class. Finally a religion teacher who realizes its only 2 credit hours!
I loved this Class! He is an amazing teacher. The test arent too hard as long as you go to class and pay attention. I really enjoyed this class, and would take another class from him.

Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about Mormon history--lots of cool stories and anecdotes. Encouraged students to think about the subject, not just regurgitate answers. I plan on taking hime again.

He's an amzing teacher!

A pretty easy online class. I stopped watching the recorded lectures about halfway through the semester because I realized you really only need to know the textbook reading. His lectures just cover the online portion, but the tests are much harder than expected.

Lectures weren't required and often confused me more than benefited me. Professor Holmes is talkative to a point where he talks more than he needs to and often leaves students unsure on the content of the unit we are on. One of the worst class experiences I've had. Class time feels pointless, and no late work is accepted. Grading is heavy on exams, and if you mess up once, the final determines everything. Class was ok. It was all conducted online, so it was nice to be away from the pressure of in-class, but it was just kinda boring. You don't NEED to go to class, but it does motivate you to learn the topic. The tests are not bad, but you have to put time into studying. I did not learn a lot tho, just skimmed the topics.

He loves to talk, so much so that it is hard to determine what is actually important. His tests are difficult to understand. Overall he doesn't actually help you learn.

Dr. Holmes is great. I took FIN 200 online, so most of the learning was on my own. It's very important to do the reading for the quizzes, and he also posts lectures, which are very engaging and very helpful. Great class, even if you're not studying finance!

As apathetic to teaching as you can get. Didn't show up to class more than 50% of the time and relied on “online lectures.” Test material totally outside scope of lessons. Not sure how he is still employed.

FIN201 is a pretty standard class, but Professor Holmes does a good job lecturing. He is funny and shows that he actually cares about his students. Nice and not boring but DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM. I'm sure the rumors that you have to cheat to get through this class are true. It feels like everyone cheats through Holmes Fin201 class. You feel you almost half to given he is such a poor lecturer and the minimal TA support. Pretty much nothing mattered except the exams and the final. If you don't do well on any one of the exams you absolutely have to do amazing on the final to get an A

Best professor. Finance just sucks so its not easy, but he's tenured and gives you every chance to prove you know the stuff on his tests. Final test is a fatty tho and it's not easy. Because he is a tenured employee, Holmes has become relaxed and lazy. His jokes in class aren't really conducive to the BYU honor code. Lectures are sub par and don't really provide much value. Holmes class was set up in a pretty ineffective way, with quizzes on the weekly chapter due Monday morning before even getting to have lectures on the chapter material, which made it hard for you to effectively learn the topic. Just kinda like an average class. Professor Holmes seemed cool, his lectures were nice but I pretty much taught myself everything like I've done in every other class. Professor Holmes didn't do a thing this semester. He posted lectures from a year ago and would send weekly emails. Actually the worst class I've taken at BYU. Sarcastic and unclear. I didn't feel prepared at all for the tests, which were super heavily graded. I even studied for hours and almost failed the final. Get ready to just watch his recorded lectures from last year. it was suppose to be in person and he used covid as an excuse not to do anything. Was a little frustrated that he used COVID as an excuse to not really teach this semester. Used recorded lectures from a previous semester. Lectures were good and he made material that sounded extremely difficult in the textbook quite simple which I appreciated. Grade is 80% tests.

Professor Holmes is the most boring person on the planet. His lectures are drier than the Sahara Desert. Hardest class I've ever taken. And Holmes does nothing to prepare you for the tough exams. I relied on the book and did what I could to do well in class. Holmes has made me rethink wanting to major in finance. He's a very boring lecturer, and he's not easy to get help from. I was alone in this class and struggled.

Professor Holmes is a super nice guy and a great teacher. He prepares you well for the exams and gives you the resources you need to succeed. If you take the time to watch the lectures, do the practice problems, and watch the reviews, youll do fine.

This class was tough and disorganized. The lectures were often fuzzy (finger covering the microphone). The lack of communication and organization was disappointing compared to other classes in the business school with 800+ students. I feel I taught myself everything. Take it in person if you can.

He's a solid teacher, but nothing special. I can't say I'd recommend him nor turn anyone away from him. The material is complex, but most people can get it down with good study. The course itself though is so expansive that by the time you've finished one of the 13 chapters you feel like you've taken an entire class. All of the tests are very hard.

The final is everything but you wouldn't know that from Dr. Holmes because he never even told us how many questions it would have. He is truly the most boring human on the planet earth. His lectures are 1 hour 1/2 of him reading off a PowerPoint in a monotone voice. And you can't even speed up the videos. Take it in person or with someone else!!!!!
This class wasn't too bad. There's not a lot of coursework throughout the semester but the exams are important. The TAs are super helpful so I would recommend going to the lab often.

FIN 201 with Holmes was much more challenging than I expected it to be. For the first test, I studied solely using the textbook & its practice problems and totally bombed the exam. I later found that the TA Exam Reviews and Holmes' exam reviews are SO helpful. WATCH THESE BEFORE THE TESTS. Be sure to watch all of Holmes' lectures as well.

I took Professor Holmes' FIN201 class fully on demand because of covid, which was tough by itself, but the class material on top of that was even more difficult. We had to learn everything on our own, and Andrew would pre record lectures every week, which was somewhat engaging. Also, I DO NOT recommend taking FIN201 and ACC200 at the same time!!
He is not easy to work with. Brick wall. No leniency.

Professor Holmes did a great job explaining the concepts needed to know for the tests. He provided tons of previous exam questions and test review videos so you know exactly what to expect on the exams. If you study the exam prep questions and have a good understanding of them, this class won't be a problem.

This class was really frustrating for me, especially the weekly quizzes. They're due before the lecture, so your have to spend a lot of time in the textbook shooting in the dark on some very complex topics. They're due Monday at 10AM so my Sunday evenings were consumed by 3 or so hours of this. Tests are difficult and make up most your grade.

Every time he says "finance" I want to hurt myself Signed up for this class specifically because it was NOT an online class, then he decided to make it one anyway after the semester started Half the videos have a very distracting background and the course materials are not organized. Does not respond to emails. Relies on textbook to actually teach

He's awesome! You read and quiz before your first class of the week, then spend the two class periods going over the material- I was not a fan. It makes the homework seem useless (I would stumble through it, not understanding what I did until class). He thoroughly goes over concepts in class and works through problems. Pretty funny guy

Holmes is amazing. Anyone who is willing to put in work can get an A. The secret to success here is taking the practice tests AND understanding them comprehensively. If you bomb any tests, the final will supersede the midterms. Holmes gives you a formula sheet for the most important equations, so there's less pressure than taking it from Brau.

Ok. In all of my time in school, Professor Holmes's Finance class was my absolute least favorite class I have ever done. I eventually had to petition to drop the class because I was getting panic attacks every time I went to class. I nearly dropped out of school JUST because of that class. It is awful. Take it from another professor.

I did not have a good experience in this class. Although I am not a business student (I am doing the minor), I have been able to succeed in all other business classes except this one. Class lectures were very hard to follow, bungeelink quizzes were very difficult, and I did not feel prepared for the tests. I would NOT recommend this professor.

Dr. Holmes is a good guy but lectures are extremely confusing. I did fine in Accounting and Marketing at BYU but this class from him was a whole new level of intense. Tests weigh a ton and he does not do a good job of slowing the pace down according to students' needs. Sometimes cracks a good joke but overall class was boring and hard to follow.
Hard course. Tests count for 75% of your grade. Final average was a C. I studied countless hours. Take course, but don't expect this to be an easy A.
He was a decent teacher but DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS IF YOU HAVEN'T TAKEN ACCOUNTING. not worth it. also heard brau is easier.

I had the pleasure of learning from Dr. Holmes through the Kaplan-Schweser CFA exam preparation material (for years 1 and two). He has a gift for making technical material understandable and relateable. I would recommend his teaching without hesitation to anyone.

A lot of people prefer Brother Brough's Fin201 class (taught in the winter). This class is very tough, but doable if you learn the material as you go, study the practice tests and know the ways he could try and trick you, and go to the TA lab with any questions you have. The tests are the hardest part of the class, prepare well for them.

Dr Holmes really tries his best to be a good professor. The tests are heavily weighted, so get ready. But if you're sincerely looking to learn about practical finance (like credit cards, investing, insurance, loans, taxes, etc) just take SFL 260. I learned more practical info in 1 week than in the entire semester of this class.

Professor Holmes is a great teacher! Finance is a fairly difficult business prereq but if you study it won't be awful. He uses BungeeLink each class to do participation quizzes. Good class all around!

Don't be deceived by all the people who appear to get A's on this site-- the class was pretty difficult and mostly graded on tests, with like a 1.5-2.0 percent curve at the end. Taking ACC 310 at the same time as this made life easier. Tests are essentially practice test problems only they change the numbers. PRACTICE EXAMS are your key to success.

Prof Holmes is a fun teacher I guess but I didn't like how the class was set up. You must read and take a quiz before going over material in class. Attendance is needed to answer in-class questions for your participation grade. He does let you use a formula sheet on tests. I think Brau does not, so +1 there.

Holmes definitely grew on me to become one of the best professors I have had in my 3 semesters at BYU. He knows his stuff & has a witty sense of humor. I loved how he occasionally took a break from lecture to give a "thought of the day" & took the time each class to let a few kids talk about their weekends. this class is not hard if you PRACTICE!

Holmes is OK but is definitely not as good of a teacher as the other professors I've had from the business school. This class is much easier than Acc 200 or Econ 110, but be careful because over 75% of your grade is based on exams. Doing the practice problems at the end of each MyEducator chapter is the best way to prepare for the exams.
Good guy. Class wasnt bad. Midterm and final are huge
Prof Holmes is a great and very funny guy. All of his lectures are a review of the textbook reading, which can make the lectures boring at times, but overall an enjoyable class.

Dr. Holmes does a great job preparing his students for exam content. He tells you in class what type of problems most students miss and why, so that you don't miss them on the exam. The practice exams are key to understanding the material for the tests, which he also tells you. He trys to make class entertaining. I thoroughly enjoyed the experience

Professor Holmes has such an engaging, fantastic way of teaching finance. This is a difficult class in terms of content, but he teaches very clearly and sets you up for success. Really make sure you do and understand the practice exam questions on MyEducator; that helped me out a ton. Great experience overall, he's the man!

Dr. Holmes' teaching style is clear, succinct, and engaging. The course material is much easier than ACC and ECON. As long as you study hard for the exams, you'll get an A. Weekly quizzes, with attendance taken through online questions during class. Great option for FIN 201

I loved professor Holmes. Finance can be kind of boring, but he is so personable and funny that I actually really enjoyed the lectures. Not a lot of homework, and he prepares you very well for the tests. If you're willing to work hard it's perfectly possible to get an A.

I loved his good humor, and I liked how personable he was. He sincerely cares for and loves his students. A tough class, but he puts it in simple terms. You go out of order from the textbook, but it makes more sense the way he does it. Really liked his personal finance section at the end. He clearly does all he can to help students do well.

I've had Holmes-fall and Brau-winter in this class. Holmes: more boring, teaches fine, gives awesome practice tests, way more prepared for test. Brau: hilarious, feel spiritually uplifted every day, study really hard, horrifying shock when you see your test grade. If you want a good grade, take Holmes. If you want a funner professor, take Brau.
Professor Holmes is hilarious and gives great lectures! This course requires that you do a lot of practice problems and you read thoroughly, but the hard work pays off.

Best thing about Dr. Holmes is that he doesn't make you memorize financial ratios like the other teachers do! This a huge saver on grades! Also, he has 2 ways of grading--either the "normal" way, or your final exam can count as a big portion of your grade. You get whichever gives you a higher grade! Also, take ACC 200 before this class will help.

He explains how to resolve a problem, he will go step by step, and in the end he will say something like "and that is how you don't do this"... Then you need to go back and reset your mind for the correct explanation (same with his text book, lots of fluff). Easy tests though, I got 100%
The tests are hard and he does do curves. Lectures are often hard to focus in and he goes through the materials quickly. Take lots of notes.

Professor Holmes is an amazing finance professor. I fell in love with finance taking this class from him. He is so funny and super engaging in his lecture. I will take this class from him over and over again. Also he was so willing to work with me when I traveled to Africa for a family emergency. Never a dull moment in class! Knows his stuff.

Dr. Holmes is a really nice guy, he knows so much about finance you will learn lots from him. His tests will melt your head if you over think. I feel like he tries to trip you up. I could imagine him and his TA's writing tests in that way and then joking about it. TA's are very helpful it's a shame the lab is only open for 2 hours a day.

I messed up and took this class as a Freshman so it was probably the hardest class I've taken up to this point and the worst grade I've ever gotten by far. But Dr. Holmes is great. He is very funny and caring about his students but sometimes what he says in class about Finance seems confusing and sort of all over the place.

Great professor. Super reasonable and understanding if you talk to him, and his tests are very fair. You get a formula sheet on every exam, one quiz due every week, and he's a pretty funny guy. Definitely would recommend taking the class from him.

Holmes class is easy. I read everything, took notes and took the practice quizzes multiple times and only missed one question on all of the exams. I felt like I could have learned it myself though. Whenever I listened to him in class, I got even more confused.
Great teacher. His tests are pretty straightforward, and he lets you know what is going to be on them Just study well fo rthe midterms and you'll be fine.

Holmes was awesome! He's a super funny/smart guy. I found the class to be the usual--you read the book, take notes, come to class, prepare for the midterms, study for the final, and get an A. Read, and practice the Qs at the end of the book. Final wasn't bad--I studied for around 2x the time I spent studying for the midterms and scored similarly.

Professor Holmes is an entertainer and a great teacher. He talks really quick sometimes. He gives students the benefit of the doubt. Four midterms and an accumulative final was  a little much, but it'll all pay off and come full circle by the final.

I loved Prof. Holmes. Although I didn't end up with an A, I thought he was a very good teacher. He teaches for the test but also for the overall understanding. He knows what he's talking about and seems to like to help students out. Don't be afraid to take his class

Doctor Holmes teaches you well, if you've read the textbook before hand. If not, you're gonna be lost. The midterms are fairly simple if you do the practice tests and you understand finance. The final is not as hard as people say, you just need to study well for the midterms, and review those notes.  No essays, just numbers and formulas.

Dr. Holmes is a great professor!  The class was not time consuming and I probably spent and an hour and a half to two hours every week on reading through the book and doing the quiz.  Reading the book is essential (at least for me) in doing well in this class.  It prepped me for the lectures and tests.  Do the practice tests and its an easy A.

He is the Dr. Perry Cox of BYU. He cares about his students success but is very proud of his skills. He has a right to be though because he is a financial genius! He is a good teacher if you test well. Interesting class. I wouldnt take him again
Good class, just don't like the way he pronounces FINANCE.

Class moves fast which I appreciated - no room for bullcrap just some good humor. You really need to master the content. Practice tests and quizzes will help you for tests. Final is a beast (comprehensive). I got a 92 on all tests (I do well with math - TVM) but a C on the final (didn't finish in time). All text and no long videos like ACC200 :D

Professor Holmes is a great professor and his lectures are really interesting! It is definitely a harder class so get ready to put some good hours into studying. His grading criteria is very clear and he really wants each of his students to do well.

Definitely the funniest professor I've had in my college career so far. Also one of my hardest classes to date, but you can get a good grade if you put in the work. A huge learning curve and he sometimes may talk finance over your head, but if you do the reading before you go to class, the lectures will help solidify everything.

Taking Fin201 I was worried about the difficulty. Professor Holmes made it as clear as possible and also very interesting. He was also willing to work with students who were struggling. The tests were difficult, but if you do the practice tests in MyEducator you'll be prepared. Take finance from Dr. Holmes if you can.

I left this class with a passion for Finance! The class uses a program called MyEducator, an online program that has all of the reading, videos, quizzes ect. If you do the practice tests multiple times, the tests are really not hard. I would recommend sitting in the front couple of rows and visiting the TA's for help occasionally.

Professor holmes is awesome and funny but he is very deep in subject and talks perhaps in a vernacular that is beyond the kind any professor should use in a Finance 201 class. Great class. Learned a lot. Got a b-
Dr. Holmes is a great teacher. Great sense of humor. The course is useful and set up well. It will definitely take me a few weeks to forget about that terrible final. Praying for a curve...
Dr. Holmes is hilarious and interactive in class. The tests are difficult and so is the final. You can take the quizzes as many times as you like which is nice. The grading policy is very forgiving.

Professor Holmes is a very good teacher. He's a great lecturer. He's made me seriously consider majoring in Finance. He tells you exactly what undergrads usually trip up on during the exams. The average on the tests was normally pretty good (Mid-High B), but there were also a select few (of 800 people) that got a 16 percent. Don't be them.

Incredible professor. Really knows and loves the material. Really good at keeping class fun, interesting, and interactive (despite the huge class size). A little difficult but there are a ton of course-help materials available to help.

Enthusiastic professor. He knows his stuff but has a hard time teaching clearly. He uses awful analogies that often times are just confusing. Not the worst finance professor, but I would try someone else. Tests are rough but he is merciful when it comes to grading. Not the easy A.

After helping over 5 professors for Fin 201 as a TA, I truly believe he is the best for Fin 201 at least for me. He teaches and tests you on intuitions rather than memorizations. Even though his exams are a bit harder,  in Winter '15 his class did better than Dr. Brau's class on the exams (averages) throughout semester. Formula sheet provided also.

Dr. Holmes is a master lecturer. He constantly reviews the material he previously taught so that it can be applied rather than just memorized. He makes Finance 201 about as easy as it could be and is table to take questions from a classroom of 600 hundred students and still be on schedule! The practice tests are EXCELLENT prep for the real tests.

I truly only did well in this class because I have a background in accounting. He is funny and the few assignments are easy. Lectures are chill. Tests are a bit tough. I feel like he often used vocab I didn't recognize. Good class. LOVE TOSHI!

I enjoyed his class. He go off tangent in finance topic, but to me they were interesting enough. He has practice exams which are hard but helpful. To me his teaching was clear and the amount of work I put in was normal. Too bad that he cannot have Toshi for this class, but I still think you should take this class from him if you care learning.

Dr. Holmes is great. He teaches the intuition behind finance. The practice exams are very difficult, but if you can do everything on the practice exam you will be successful on the test. If you don't excel at memorization take Finance from him, he gives you  a formula sheet, but requires you know the intuition. I would take Finance from him again.

I loved his lectures. This was my retake and I took once from Dr. Brau. Dr. Holmes explains materials better and he gives you the formula sheet with the exams as well. He actually taught intuition behind principles instead of just teaching formulas like Dr. Brau did. If you want to learn the materials rather than just get an A, he is the man!

He is funny and perhaps a finance god. I think he explains concepts very clearly and lectures are organized enough. His exams are tough, but he gives you a formula sheet. Practice exams are harder, but prepared me well for the exams. I heard that his tests are harder than Brau, but his test averages are higher. so that tells a lot about Dr. Holmes!

There's quizzes every week, they are easy if we do the readings, we can do them unlimited times . It's important to come to class because we answer TOP HAT questions.  He is fun and it's easy to stay awake.  The midterms are HARD! But just as any other finance exam.

I heard that he will be teaching for the winter, so decided to put some comments. Honestly, his exams are hard, but it is possible to get an A with curve he sets. TAs are helpful... I should not tell the specific name, but if TOSHI will be your TA for the semester, he emails a lot, but he is the TA and super smart. You will be lucky if he is there.

Holmes is VERY smart and passionate about the subject he teaches. He talks very fast and is sometimes hard to understand, but you can tell he really cares about his students and wants them to do well. Class is really hard and requires a lot of studying, but if you are diligent, an A is definitely possible, even if you haven't taken ACC200!

Professor Holmes is awesome. Really funny, very clear in teaching, cares about the welfare and learning of the students. Monday TA sessions were just review by TAs. One TA was not very good at teaching but all the other TA's were great. Do the software, skim the readings, and pay attention in Wednesday lectures. Do the service and career prep hw.

Great teacher even though we had a little bit of confusion due to new style of materials. The exam is a little more difficult that you have experienced, but I think it is a great prep for other college classes. Many people complained his speeds etc. but it is intro class and great way to get expose to the business world, I think.

He speaks fast, but that is normal for finance professors. His lecture is clear and some TAs are very helpful (at least this year). Wanna do well? On top of the schedule and go and meet with TAs often for help. TA reviews could be helpful for the exam study. Exam is harder side, but at the end he curves the class at the end of semester as needed.
Great teacher.

Good guy and decent teacher. Keeps things interesting with real world stories. You have to do the reading to stay afloat. Hard class but very useful. Tests are quite hard but not in a way that you can't do well on them, you just have to know the material really really well. Overall a very good class and you learn a lot.

Talks way too fast. Tests are suppose to be "trick" type questions... probably to test your knowledge, doesn't work on everyone that busts their butt off Holmes. I just didn't really like this class at all. He's funny and very smart. Most important part is that I learned... but never wanna take finance classes b/c of this class.

Agree with most of the comments here. The professor is quite funny and interesting but his tests are way too difficult. I thought I did prepare carefully for it but got a bad grade. The wordings of the tests are very confusing and ambiguous. Even though I completed the Acct 310, this class is still a bit  out of my reach.
Way too hard. Speaks way too fast in class for you to understand. And his tests are harder than ANY I have taken at BYU. Take it from Brau if you can.

Great guy.  By far the funniest teacher I've ever had.  Makes class more than bearable despite complex financial subjects.  You can tell he loves the subjects he's teaching.  More than willing to meet with you after class to help.  Weekly quizzes are easy points, but tests are difficult.  Must know material inside and out to do well on test Q's.

Run! This class was extremely difficult.  You could study forever for the tests and think you had it down pat but then come out with a terrible grade.  Good guy, and funny but man are his tests awful. Anyone who says any different is either a genius, or has no life.

I like Professor Holmes as a person and he does fairly well teaching...when he slows down his teaching "speed". His weekly quizzes are not too bad, but his test are intense. If you have not completely mastered the chapters then you will get a low B or a C. Pretty much the only people that have taken ACCT 210 get A's on the test.

way too hard of a class for a minor class...he pretty much used the same material from the 301 class. tests were ridiculous and the quizzes were due monday morning at 8 am...worst time ever. would not recommend this class to anyone

Maybe the 'for majors only' version of this class is a lot harder but I didn't think the one for business minors was too difficult. Tests seemed pretty much like the weekly homework quizzes we took and he points out in class the common mistakes made.  Grade is composed of reading quizzes, 1 weekly homework quiz, and 3 tests.

Most comments above are from people that are going to have a hard time in the real business world this is a business class that's why the tests aren't exactly the same but it's never anything you don't have the ability to solve with some problems solving ability. If you can't problem solve don't go into business. Great Teacher personable reasonable

He is all right tries to teach in an interesting manner. The packet is too cute, and is too focused on tricking students (like his tests).Tests measure how well you read the question and remember the ways he will try to trip you up. The material is really disorganized and much is covered in other classes or on  wikipedia.

I enjoyed this course and Professor Holmes and learned a great deal over the course of the semester.  The tests weren't exceptionally difficult, but they did not accurately measure what was actually taught in the course.  Professor Holmes is a great man though - the course just needs a little more structure and organization.

I like Andy Holmes, and I really enjoyed this class. He's entertaining and a really good teacher. Yeah, his tests are hard, but if you study and do your homework you'll be fine. He's super reasonable. I would definitely take a class from him again.

Terrible teacher not b/c he is bad at lecturing but he is terribly disorganized and unfocused. Most of the practice tests have mistakes on them that Holmes doesn't explain. You'll walk into the tests thinking you have a clue what you're up against, but you'll soon realize how much Holmes hasn't prepared you. Terrible.

The other comments are spot on.  He is a personable and interesting professor with lots of good information.  He expects you to know everything he teaches right away and the tests are very difficult.  Overall, this was a hard but very useful class.  And yeah, you definitely need the book.

The best teacher at BYU. The tests are hard. If you do not know how to do a multi-step problem, tests will make you suffer. It is a good check if you will do well in Finance or not. This is college and BYU. If are not doing well, it does not mean you are not learning. Don't go and don't whine in his office. Just do the work and homework, you'll be

He's an entertaining guy and cares about his students. However, his tests are ridiculous. You may study for hours for the test, feel like you are prepared, and then run into questions you've never seen before. I usually walked out of tests feeling like I must not have learned anything in class even though I put the work into it.

I really enjoyed this class.  Holmes has really practical lectures.  It takes a lot of practice to get the material down, so be prepared to study hard.  I'd recommend taking ACC 210 before you take this class.  The tests can be monsters.
He is a great teacher and he really cares about his students. If you study the notes and the book the class is easy.
Holmes is a funny guy but his class his tests are always a surprise from what you learn in class. When I took the test, I felt like I learned nothing in class.  The test questions are ambiguous.

The class wasn't too bad.  The material taught is pretty simplified and could be a lot harder.  Holmes is a good guy and does his best to teach effectively.  Test questions can be a little vague and unpredictable but getting an A is manageable.

Holmes presents the most important data that is used today in the financial world. He doesn't bore the class with useless financial equations. Tests are hard, but fair. All in all, a great professor....He keeps things humorous and light

I really enjoyed the class!  The test were hard, but it was very helpful to do the optional homework assignments.  The class is graded on a curve so it doesn't matter how you did on the test; it matters how the whole class did on the exam.  The class is entertaining and you will learn a lot.

He teaches well.  Anything useful you'll learn in Acc 210 is covered in this class.  Much more applicable than any accounting class.  Lecture attendance non mandatory, but be sure to go to personal finance days.  Tests are on par with other Marriott School classes.

He is an awesome guy and also funny. But regarding his teaching style, I did not learn a thing from him. For some reason, our test were extremely harder than the prior semester. So when he gives you the practice test, make sure you study everything else. Labs are extremely disorganized. You never know what he will ask you on a test.
The class is very entertaining.  He has a personal finance week and a home buying seminar.  You learn a lot of useful stuff.  Tests aren't easy, but you can do well.
Work hard and the class is easy. You must study HARD for the tests. Lectures are interesting. He's a funny dude and really like his students
Way easier than accounting 210.  I really enjoyed this class and this professor -- Holmes genuinely cares about students.

He is a great professor. You MUST attend the labs or else you will not get a good grade.  Also, his final is much harder than his other two tests so be prepared.  He makes lectures more entertaining than most professors so it's probably not a bad thing to go to class every day.
Good class - engaging professor, but lectures are not a must. If you read the chapters and review the slides he posts on blackboard, you don't need to go to class. Labs are VERY important.
The best "Man" at the BYU. Prepare well for the final, it was a lot harder than the two midterms. Midterms are just piece of cakes. Recently, I noticed his ugly grandchild story is kinda true.

Dr. Holmes is very knowledgable about finance, but this means he moves very quickly through the material.  He's nice and funny, but the class is extrememly difficult and tests are designed to trick you.  Good luck with this one.
Great teacher - almost makes me want to change my emphasis to finance. Notecard allowed on the final so that's good - tests are difficult, though. Study and work hard and you'll get a good grade.
He is an awesome and very funny teacher! He made a hard class fun. The test are kind of tough.  The only thing I didn't like about the test was that there were too many trick answers.

A challenging, but fair class.  The teacher is very specific about what you will see on the tests.  And allows you to contest any test questions you think were poorly written.  Also, don't go to labs and goof off with friends.  Ask questions, do you assignments and you'll get a decent grade.  The final was A LOT harder than the two midterms!!

Makes a difficult class fun, there are still times when you'll get lost in all the mumbo jumbo of finance, just make sure to ask questions for clarity in your labs.  you will have to put forth your effort in this class if you want a good grade.
This professor is awesome.  Funny, interesting, makes you love finance.
The Class is awesome, but the tests are freaking hard!

The teacher is funny and makes class interesting.  Tests are a little difficult but not impossible if you put a little time and effort into it. Overall a great class that doesn't require too much effort.
Awesome teacher, tests are difficult, the concepts are not hard to understand if you pay attention in class.  He's every bit from the south as he says he is.

It is a very easy class. He is kinda goofy and we have a stupid joke contest every day. Also, his granfather failed his finance tests and therefore married a very ugly woman because he wouldn't make it on the cover of GQ. The class is really easy

Worst class I've had at BYU. The book is bad and the teacher teaches stuff differently in class anyway. You must have a magic memory for remembering acronyms because he never uses actual words. Grade is based on 2 midterms (25 questions ea.) and a final!!

I actually liked Professor Johns way more than I thought I would. He had very interesting lectures with a lot of information. The tests were fairly easy, but you have to study a lot. He is super easy to contact outside of class, and gives really clear answers.

Dr Johns was a great lecturer and I love feeling like I genuinely learned a lot in his class. There was a lot of reading in this class but it was still doable. Quizzes aren't impossible but you won't be able to get away with not doing the reading if you want a good grade. But overall this class was great and I recommend!

I took his HIST 221 course. I enjoyed the material, but did not like the way the class was run. You are almost completely graded on your midterm, a semester long paper, and the final. He got really behind in lecture, but still expected you to know everything from the readings. This made all the information a bit jumbled, as he was so far behind.
He moved up the due date for an assignment by a week for no apparent reason. He also acted very inconsiderate to his students through the whole semester in general.

We never had discussions, we just listened to him talk. You do have to read though, because he expects you to quote from the books (or at least paraphrase) on tests. Gradebook has 10-12 pg paper, midterm, final, and "participation." Sometimes we'd be a couple minutes over and he'd go, "Any questions? No? OK, see ya." Doesn't post lecture slides.

Your grade for this class is based on 5 quizzes, 1 midterm, & 1 final. No easy homework points to cushion your grade so if you're a bad test taker, good luck. Sometimes quizzes include material that hasn't been assigned yet. Extra credit by attending campus forums! Liked him as a person, did not like the class. Very jumbled up and stress inducing.

Dr. Johns is one of my favorite professors at BYU. His lectures are fascinating, and the readings are actually interesting. He makes himself very available to students who want some help. Very clear expectations on tests and assignments (he only does a mid-term, a final, and a research paper, no extra fluffy assignments). Fantastic professor.

HIST490. Prof Johns is a good prof. I was frustrated that nothing was on Learning Suite. He printed off the syllabus and grading material at the beginning of the semester and that was it. So get a folder or something and DO NOT lose them. Every time you have to turn something in, you have to print it off and deliver it personally to his office.

To give credit: amazing lectures- SO engaging & fun. However his class was terrible. INSANE reading each week w/ quizzes about obscure details.  For exams he expects you to know EVERY detail from the textbook, even if he skipped over it in class. Take this class if you like breaking down mentally during midterm/finals week.

Dr. Johns is an amazing professor! Would definitely recommend him if you want to actually learn something rather than just trying to get out of American Heritage.  His lectures are very interesting, and he is clear with expectations from the beginning.  One of my favorite classes to date.

If you miss a day of Dr. John's class, you're out of luck. He had a lot of good info to share but he got super behind in the material he had to cover so we had to cover it on our own with the textbook. He also assigns a lot of reading (one week had a 30+ pg textbook chap, a 20 pg reader ch, and a 145 pg book) and you have to do all to pass quizzes.

Not sure where all the hate on past reviews are coming from. I absolutely love this class - Dr. J always comes prepared for lectures and has been very quick to respond to emails and grade midterms. He gives plenty of opportunity for extra credit if you are worried about the few graded assignments (midterm, final paper, and final exam).

VERY VAGUE IN WHAT HE WANTED AND BASED GRADES ON VERY FEW THINGS. THOUGHT THIS WOULD BE A GOOD CLASS INSTEAD OF AMERICAN HERITAGE, IT'S NOT. YOU HAD TO WORK TO GET IN HIS HEAD FOR WHAT HE WANTED IN PAPERS AND QUIZZES. READINGS TOOK FOREVER, AND THE LECTURES WERE VERY BORING. I SPENT THE MOST TIME ON THIS CLASS AND GAINED THE LEAST FROM IT.

DON'T DO IT. This class was horribly overbearing, three times as much work as any other class. The professor requires huge amounts of reading. I had to basically memorize the readings to pass the quizzes. The lectures have no opportunity to participate in learning. He is vague in explaining the assignments.

Doesn't make his PPTs available online or allow laptops in class. His lectures were alright, but he is a tough grader. Doesn't give out As! Told me I had the 4th highest grade in the class and the 2nd highest grade on the final so my B+ was a good grade. Took the class expecting a better alternative for AMHTG but it was a mistake.

Dr. Johns does not explain what he wants from his students at all. He's very vague, and on tests he grades to the curve to make sure he gets a certain number of As Bs and Cs, not actually according to how you expound on material. Avoid if possible. He says it's a discussion based class, but just lectures and has no respect for undergrad students.

This guy although I respect him as a a professor, his lectures were great, he is by far the worst professor I have ever had in 4 years of schooling. He is not out to help the student. He is not on the same team as the student hoping they pass. He is ridiculous with deadlines, even if the error was his fault he will take it our on student. Bad clas
This class was pretty terrible. Grading was all over the place with very little feedback.

Great guy, but this class was amazingly difficult.  Everything is based on the midterm, semester paper, and final.  That's not abnormal, but the surprising lack of feedback was.  I would definitely suggest looking at other options before taking this class.

Very knowledgeable about the subject matter, and grading is very straight-forward -- all based on the reading, a few quizzes, lecture, and exams. There is a ton of reading assigned each week, so that will take some extra dedication.

I have taken every single class that he offers.  He is my favorite teacher at BYU.  He is difficult, but once you figure out what he wants he is not difficult.  Just do the reading and support any claim you make on a test with examples from the reading.  If you don't mind reading this is one of the best teachers you can take.

This class was difficult. Lectures were hard to stay awake in. Professor was very nice and gave lots of extra credit. Tests were all dependent on readings, and there was a LOT of reading in this class.

Reading humanly impossible. (300+ pages/week). Tests ridiculous. Grading harsh. 40% of grade was midterm/final, 30% paper, 30% random in-class quizzes. Unless you already know everything about US history, do not take. He was super prideful, unapproachable, and unsympathetic in his attitude. He seems to be there just to show you how smart he is.

Dr. Johns is very knowledgeable but that does not equate to being an effective teacher. He gave zero feedback on our assignments and seemed to talk at the students rather than with them. Grading felt arbitrary. Discussion was minimal.

Amazing lectures! I learned an incredible amount about the Vietnam War and its present legacies. The amount of assigned reading is humanly impossible to complete - and I still got an A. Use the study guide and indexes to prepare for the tests. Memorize the document authors' themes and cite in the test - he loves that.

Great teacher, hard grader.  Specialist in Vietnam-era politics.  He bases his tests and papers around tough essay topics and doesn't give a lot of feedback on the reasoning behind his grades.  I learned a lot, though.

I think I gained a much greater understanding of the cold war and why the nuclear arms race was so great for America in his class. If not for nukes, the US wouldn't have beat the Russians in hockey in the American Olympics in 1942. Johns is a great teacher, and a greater American. Plus, he's hot.

I was very interested in this class.  The information was really interesting.  The only problem is the grading is ridiculous.  He gives you a couple essays and IDs on each test.  The ID grading is ridiculous!  I swear I put good detailed answers... still a B! My lowest grade ever!  Avoid unless your GPA doesn't matter!!!  Also atleast 250+ pgs/week
Wasn't organized enough for me. Too much reading. He is fun to listen to, but the tests are killer. There was a paper and some pop quizzes. Doesn't seem too interested in what he is teaching.
Very Hard!!! Way too much reading and impossible tests.  However, a very nice, helpful guy (NOT HOT!!).
Very interesting class, very funny guy.
A great teacher!  Makes the class fun, even if the tests are hard and there is a lot of reading.  I'd definitely take another class from him.

Was very intense!! Tests are all written and wants a lot of detail. Knows the subject very well and will expect you to as well.  Tons of reading!!! (Sometimes 300+ pages a week!)  Good for learning, not for GPA!!

Deep learning for Engineers is a fairly new Tech Elective class, and Dr Ning had it incredibly well made. The topics, coursework, and resources were fantastic. This class was truly worth the money spent, and I would happily pay for it again. It is very code heavy, which is expected for a graduate level Deep Learning class.

Dr. Ning-a-Ding is a wonderful professor. I'm sure he would have been even better with a subject he was passionate about, but he still made sure we learned and had a good experience. His goal was definitely to require the least amount of work for us. Tests weren't hard, but there was multiple choice/true false that was for some reason kinda tricky.

Great professor who taught the basics but still learned a lot. The class itself has simple concepts, and Dr. Ning is able to solidify those concepts without killing your grade. While he's not very passionate about this subject, he still helps you to see the application of it. Tests were also extremely doable.

Dr. Ning was a fantastic professor. Very kind and respectful of students, even when they would ask rhetorical questions. Lectures were very concise and clear. The material was hard, but his tests were very reasonable. One homework assignment per week that was hard but not busy. I learned a lot from him. Highly recommend!

Sometimes I felt I was more there for him, I think he could have made things to learn and build off of verses very complex's ideas! 

Grades fair!
I did like the class!
Good for a credit!

If you do all your assignments, you can easily get a good grade in the class. His lectures don't really related the assignments in class, so don't get stress out about writing down every single little thing he says. Cancelled class a lot, which is nice because class doesn't related to the grade you will received.

Interesting lectures, lots of readings. I think it was maybe an off semester for him, cancelled class a lot and took a very long time for grading. Only had 6% of the class graded by finals, which was stressful because you don't know where you stand. Essay based exams. Only 2-3 assignements in the entire course, so get extra credit when you can.

One of the most bizarre classes ever. Professor Reed is kind and understanding, but his lectures and assignments were very abstract and random. It took him forever to grade the assignments and I had no idea where I stood in the class until way after finals. He was lenient with my late work and an easy grader if you completed the assignments.

I actually took another course. Professor Reed is amazing. He clearly strives to bring inspiring ideas and perspectives to class. The workload was fair and not overwhelming.
