I also liked how he made an effort to provide opportunities to engage with the material outside of just assignments, including through service projects and interfaith dialogue.

The entire class is based on essays which are subjectively graded, and the professor doesn't provide any feedback on the grade you received. He doesn't give 100 on the midterm or the final. Highest score on the midterm was 95 and final was 92. Lectures are scattered and not worth the time attending unless there is an in class assignment.

He is not the best lecturer, but the class is lecture heavy. The max score on the final was 95%, he expects a lot from students. He also does not grade for long periods of time, so you will not know how you are doing until finals are over. I don't recommend this unless you already know a lot about world religions. Not entry level class.

Do the extra credit & you'll get a good grade. If you want to learn about what religions believe and their history, not your class. If you want to learn how religions fit into the world (what is religion, why we have it, etc.) this is your class. Lots of cool opportunities (like doing a podcast, or having lunch with/ rabbi's and pastors).

This class is full of great lectures and discussions. You will learn not necessarily learn facts about religions but more about how they fit together in the world. Do the extra credit assignments! Your grade is based on a few things so the extra credit will help cushion your grade. This class will change your perspective and understanding.

If you want to participate in thought provoking discussions, go to class. If you don't, you can still get an A. Papers were easy and the final only took me a few hours. One of the best religion classes I had - no crazy tests, very gospel centered and respectful, and I actually enjoyed going to class and I was never stressed about my grade. 10/10

Dr. Reed is very kind and fun. However, lectures were unstructured, unfocused, and disorganized. Rather than discussing the customs, beliefs, and practices of world religions, Dr. Reed would delve into convoluted tangents about various philosophical subjects. I also felt that grading was very, very subjective.

The class was very reading and writing heavy, with 20+ pages to read per lecture and essays due every couple weeks. The exams are free-response, and the questions are hard to understand. Your grade is based entirely on  papers and exams. If you love reading and writing, this might be the class for you, otherwise, I wouldn't recommend it

This was putting me to sleep. It is so much reading with little to no structure during the class. He had no PowerPoints and a weak lesson plan - I have been confused with what to take notes on/ what is important to know. You have a lot of readings before class and then during class, you mainly just talk about the readings.

I took the blended course, and I wish I had taken it all in-person because I enjoyed his class so much, although I didn't love the online portion. He was great at teaching world religions in such a way that was inclusive, interesting, and respectful. I learned about how to approach people of faith and he taught the information in an inspiring way.

Dr. Reed is great! Understanding and aware of his students with interesting lectures.

Spring class entailed 200 word after class writing, simple assignments about each religion you discuss, 4-5 page paper, and a midterm and final. Lectures are heavily discussion based which occasionally made them hit or miss depending on other students comments.

Dr. Reed is an amazing professor who is clearly passionate about what he teaches. I took this class as a blended course which has a lot of work due at the end of each week, but I found it amazing that I was able to learn all that I could in one semester. You get what you put into it, but I can't recommend this class or Dr. Reed enough.

I took his class hybrid so I only saw him once a week. Lectures were good and he was clear on all the topics. He was also really good at relating the lessons to us and explain them in ways we can understand. The assignment load was great, I didn't feel overloaded and the assignments we had were straightforward.

Good lecturer - he is extremely knowledgeable. His final was an essay that was difficult but better than a final.

YOU GET OUT WHAT YOU PUT IN - that's cheesy but it's especially true for this class. If you actually want to learn, do the readings!

World Religion Class I will say inspired me deeply to do more as an individual to learn and understand those around me. Often going through faith crisis, this class helped my testimony grow & learn the importance of always seeking for good & truth. There are many extra credit opportunities and Professor Reed is very fair in working with students.

I think this was an off-semester from what I've read in the past. The course was extremely disorganized! I took it because I read that he didn't have tests, but only papers. Well,  that's the opposite now. Tests, which multiple choice was harder than expected, and one paper. Lots of busy work which can be educational. Canvas was not his friend.

He was a very fun professor to take from. He knows his stuff and has some really powerful lectures. The content of the lectures is not on the test though. It all comes from the textbook. It's a bit challenging for a religion class, but it's not too bad for the Global Awareness GE requirement.

This was such a cool class to take for a religion credit! Professor Reed was a good professor. He gave us lots of opportunities for extra credit that related to respecting other religions - I went to a few and they were really neat. Lots of reading but I found it interesting so it wasn't too bad. A few papers as well but grading was very fair.

The lectures were always very dry. It may just be the subject, but I felt like Professor Reed went above and beyond with pretentious mannerisms. I have no doubt that he knows what he's talking about... but *I* don't know what he is talking about. Maybe there's too much content for 1 semester in the class, especially for a 2-credit elective.

Dr. Reed is incredibly knowledgeable on the subject of world religions and does a great job of teaching about each religion, but more than anything he really inspires his students to learn from the good in other religions and encourages inter-faith cooperation. The class was graded off of very few assignments, but he is an easy grader.

Offers Extra credit but you are not likely to need it. Only graded on a few short papers and the take-home essays tests. Class is conducted like its philosophy, daily readings used in the papers. No busy work and no attendance required. Worth it for a low-effort relaxing lecture period. Readings and lecture topics are even intriguing at times.

LOVED Dr. Reed! Genuinely cares for his student's success. He is super smart and his lectures are more like class discussions which made them way more interesting. Only a few papers make up your entire grade but he is a really easy grader so don't worry about it. Offers lots of extra credit opportunities. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

I really enjoyed his class! Super interesting lectures and readings. I liked that we only had one midterm. We watched a lot of videos about other religions, which was super interesting. Would definitely recommend!

Dr. Reed's class was graded strictly on papers and he doesn't grade them too harshly. There are no dumb multiple-choice tests. He really wants you to understand and think. My perspective on the world and religion changed for the better due to his class. He also offers some extra credit opportunities that are actually really cool. He's a great guy.

For me, Professor Reed's class was way more difficult than it should have been being a two-credit religion class. I spent hours reading and taking quizzes on obscure passages of the Quran each day. He takes his class very seriously so it's just a heavy reading load, but if you can skim and/or have a photographic memory you'll thrive in here.

This class is graded off of about 4 papers. The topics are a little complex, but it isn't hard to get a good grade if you do the readings that the papers are on. He offers extra credit for attending some devotionals and other meetings. Papers do have to be turned in hard copy, so make sure you have a printer or prepare beforehand.

Lots of reading but you can get by skimming. You usually discuss in class but tests are writing about topics related to the readings. I loved the assignment to read 100 p. of another religious text but don't procrastinate. Also, don't be afraid to listen to it, still a great experience and a little easier to undertake.

He was an alright professor and the way he structured his class wasnt too bad. But he was NOT accessible outside class at all. I was sick for a month basically not knowing whether I had a serious health condition. I emailed him several times asking about assignments, incomplete contracts, etc. He straight up ignored me for over a month.

Professor Reed is hands down the best best professor I've ever had at BYU. His World Religion class is very masterfully taught and he explains difficult concepts in a clear and straightforward way. I definitely recommend Professor Reed to any student at BYU, he has an approach and way of thinking that benefit students regardless of their major.

I really enjoyed World Religions with Dr. Reed. There is a lot of reading, and the individual reading quizzes are harder than they should be, but when I talked to him about that, he met with me and was really helpful. There are a couple papers, but they're pretty easy. This class is really interesting and is definitely a good religion class option.

Dr. Reed teaches through thought-provoking questions. The structure of the class is straight-forward. If you want to learn something, you have to do the daily readings and really consider his questions, but the class is quite easy. 3 short papers, and one 5-page paper. No homework for like the last 3 weeks of class. 2 take-home tests. Solid choice.

Dr. Reed is awesome. One of my all time favorite religion classes. He really likes to challenge the class and have real conversations with you. He often invites you to push back against his ideas. Get ready to answer the question "What do YOU think?" Grade is heavy on papers, so watch out for that if essays aren't your thing.

A LOT OF EXTRA CREDITS! Professor Reed cares about his student and their grades. He gives tons of extra credit. Lots of reading! I took this class to learn more about religions, but his teaching is more philosophical, making it less enjoyable.

Dr. Reed is an amazing professor, but he conducts his religion class as if it were a philosophy class. The discussions are great and all, but they start to get pretty confusing when just about every day in class is a discussion, and very minimal formal instruction is given. Also tons of reading. Good class, but a lot of work for a 2 credit course.

I loved this class. Literally just do your readings and you will be successful. You need to be able to think analytically, but duh, welcome to BYU & college! He asks questions that really make you think & I learned so much about other religions that has helped me be more understanding & tolerant. Coming to class is helpful to deepen understanding.

This was an online class where the only part Professor Reed seemed to play was to record a short video of himself talking at the end of every unit. Not very helpful. I listened to it on double speed. He's probably great in a different, more interactive setting.
An extremely average professor. Not that great of a class. All things just okay.

This class was great! Professor Reed provided really interesting discussions. There were a lot of readings, but skimming wasn't a problem because we covered them well in class. I would definitely recommend this class! I learned a lot and enjoyed the discussions.

Man I hated this class. This is a philosophy class full of jargon. Logged on to every lecture trying to figure out what was important to take notes on and eventually stopped going to class. He just talks about nothing. The assignments and 2 tests are essays that you only really need the readings for. Take this class from a different professor!

I loved World Religions with Dr. Reed! I would usually just skim the readings before class because they were LONG, and then actually read carefully to write the short (1pg) paper. I loved going to class because he showed really interesting videos, talked about how we can be inspired by different religions, and allowed for discussion. Great class!

Don't take this class if you don't want to use your brain, but if you do then you're going to learn so much. He gives you so many new perspectives, and he is willing to discuss anything. Everything you'll turn in is writing based, including midterm & final. Write well and you'll have no problem. This class made me think hard and I liked it.

I really struggled in this class because there are so many readings that were intellectually challenging. I was confused all the time. Dr. Reed is very knowledgeable, but you have to really be interested in learning how other people think about religion to understand lectures. You have to think hard in this class. Kind of like American Heritage...

100% lecture- he just stands there and never stops talking. There are a TON of readings, but not a lot of homework (I guess that's nice). If your paper isn't perfect you are docked 1-2 points, but that brings you down to an 85% or 90% just for one stylistic choice he doesn't agree with. Two months in and only 2/10 assignments are graded.

This guy just stands in front of the class for 2 hours trying to tell you everything he knows rather than trying to help you understand things about religions. Insane amount of reading assigned. This is more of a philosophy class than a survey of world religions. I spent every lecture hating myself.

I really liked Dr. Reed. I had to take his class online because of Covid, but i think it would have been even better in person. I appreciated the amount of useful information the class gave me. Helped inform me to make up my own mind. I also appreciated Dr. Reed's commentary and how open he was to meeting with us.

He takes attendance & the lectures are interesting, but I find them completely unnecessary. Lots of papers, but it's easy to get full credit on them. Tons of readings, & if you don't do them on schedule (like me), you'll end up spending more time on the papers & tests catching up. However, it's an easy class even with minimal effort. Tons of EC.

Dr. Reed's class is hands down the best religion course I've taken at BYU. If you're willing to put in the work and do the reading, the lectures will make sense and help you think about religion in a whole new light. He has a great perspective on different world religions and has no bias whatsoever. He's a great guy and looks out for his students!

Insane amount of reading each week! Be prepared to learn absolutely nothing about world religions. Grades are based on 5-6 one page papers, a take home midterm that's 3-4 pages (single spaced) and a written final. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. Even though there are only a few assignments, can still take 2-3 months before he enters grades

Prof Reed really pushed me to think about other religions in different way. I learned something new every lecture (I could've gotten even more out of it if I actually did the reading though), and he really knows how to spark important discussions. Yes, there are essays, but that's it! All he looks for is that you have opinions and can defend them.

World religions is entirely essay based and the essays are very unnecessary. Definetly not an easy A. Doesn't focus on what other religions teach, but rather on pluralism and how to be mormon and still consider others. The lectures are a waste of time and there are 8 essays. The midterm and final are 6 essay questions.

This class should be taken by every student at BYU. Extremely eye-opening. Class is small so it is mainly a discussion, not just a lecture. Lots of readings to prepare for the lectures. Midterm and final are take home. Have to read 100 pages of another religion's text and visit another service. One-page papers once a week. Attendance taken on paper

Professor Reed is a great guy. He values every opinion, and lets the class discuss hard topics. The thing is, I personally didn't gain anything from the topics we discussed in class. I learned more when I just did the mountains of reading instead of attending class. He has you write a papers based on opinion, and the tests are essays.

This is not a world religion class; it's a philosophy of philosophy of world religions class. Literally the only day I learned anything about a religion was when we had a substitute. Do not take unless you prefer comparing obscure philosophers and theologian's viewpoints on secularism to actually learning about culture and spiritual beliefs.

This is not a world religion class like it said this is a philosophy class with religion emphasis. Super boring and a TON of reading. Lots of reading so if you want to get anything out of this then cooperate if not you can coast by easily.

Dr. Reed is an absolute scholar on church history. His lectures were very educational and inspirational. I wish he taught Book of Mormon and New Testament courses! His exams were free response, but he had high expectations of us students. The readings were long, but definitely applied to the lectures and the exams. Awesome professor!

Professor Reed is the best religion teacher at BYU. His class is not hard, but he will push you to question why you and those around you believe in your religion. Easy, enjoyable, thought-provoking environment that always left me wishing class was longer. Definitely take this. 10/10 would recommend.

Professor Reed is amazing! I definitely recommend him. Lots of reading, but it was all interesting. All quizzes and tests were short answer, but graded fairly. Didn't get upset about any student disagreeing with his ideas, which happens in too many religion classes. I loved learning from him, he was an amazing lecturer.

He taught very interesting, academic lectures, but there were tons of papers for this class - more than I anticipated. Every assignment is essay-based. I put a ton of work into this Foundations of the Restorations class. His lectures were interesting though, and he loves to answer tough questions about the gospel and church history.
I absolutely loved this class. It was refreshing to have a class where we actually got to discuss what we read and to explore the topics rather than just sit and listen to a professor drone on.

Professor Reed is extremely smart and knows the history behind the Restoration. He expects you to know a ton as well. If you don't have a firm background knowledge of historical events, you feel like you are behind. He teaches it as a history professor, not a religion professor. Its a hard religion class that requires a lot of writing.

This class is more focused on projects than tests so make sure to take your time and do well on the final project. Because Dr. Reed doesn't like the testing center, tests are on Learning Suite which is nice. He doesn't teach to the tests, he just lectures and goes where it takes him, so go over and know all the study guides to do well on quizzes.

Dr. Reed was a fantastic lecturer and we had the BEST class discussions. I loved that he tackled the hard questions and concepts head on and let us add our input and thoughts. Dr. Reed was really open and good at allowing people to talk academically about religion. There are 2 long projects and the midterm/final are 6 short answer q's (so long!).

Professor Reed is amazing and helps you step outside the BYU bubble and understand the major world religions from believer's point of view. It is a lot of work, and the quizzes which make up a third of your grade have tricky questions about one line from the reading. You also have a major paper due but it's doable

This was by far the most tedious religion class I've ever taken, and not worth the 2 credits at all. Dr. Reed is a good lecturer, but tried to do too much with the course. The several large papers, the term project, and VERY thorough quizzes and exams made fore a massive headache that distracted from all my other classes.

INCREDIBLE class and professor. My perspectives on EVERYTHING were changed - I grew in my own religion while learning about others. Fair grading. Tests and most quizzes were written so it's easy to get some points even if you don't know exact answer. Helpful study guides for every unit. Fascinating readings and discussions, Prof knows his stuff.

Professor Reed is awesome. He really cares about his students and understands you have a life. The projects and assignments were fun and interesting. I learned lots and have a much broader view of religion.

I went into his office hours and he talked with me for 45 minutes about random religion topics. He cares a lot about his students. Beware his reading and quizzes, THEY ARE HARD. There's 30-50 pages due every class time and his quizzes are conceptual and essay based, usually not multiple choice. LISTEN DURING LECTURE AND TAKE NOTES.

Dr Reed is really cool, though he travels a lot- I took him during summer term and he was gone for three weeks and had online lectures. The reading quizzes are fairly easy, but for the midterm and final he has you explain concepts for each religion. If you go to each lecture and take good notes, and THOROUGHLY read each reading, you have a chance.

Warning: Dr. Reed likes testing through essay writing (and multiple choice sometimes); if you're not confident in writing essays, beware. I managed all right. The content was extremely interesting. The lectures were great. As a person, Dr. Reed is awesome, and very willing to work with students. He's definitely passionate about what he teaches.

Dr. Reed is one of the best professors I've had. A lot of reading, but his tests are definitely doable and a lot of the questions are off of the study guide. He really helps you think. I didn't have much of a testimony, something I've struggled with my entire life but Dr. Reed has been one of the few people to help grow my testimony. Extra credit.

This class was hard but it was worth it.  Lots of reading, but awesome lectures and Dr. Reed really gets everyone involved and makes you think a lot.  ALL tests are online but they are closed note.  If you want to learn about other religions take this class.  If you want to sleep through a religion course please don't.

I took World Religions spring term.  Because it was so compacted there was a ton of reading to do, but it tapers off after midterms.  Dr. Reed really teaches you how God views other religions and how he has played a role with them.  Your religious worldview will change  quite a bit and how you define religion will change even more.  Great class.

Dr. Reed is the best religion teacher I have had at BYU. He does a great job of helping students reach beyond their own cultural understandings to love and respect people of other faiths. At the same time, he helps class members develop their understanding of their own faith. Deeply enriching class. I couldn't recommend it more highly.

Honestly Dr. Reed is one of my favorite Religion Professors here at BYU. He is very knowledgable in his field of study, and really makes you think for yourself - if you allow it. He takes class attendance, but you don't want to miss class. Also, make sure you do your reading and review his study guides before test. Seriously - take this professor.

Reason I say this class is so hard is because he doesn't know the subject. He seems like someone that wants to debate and philosophically discuss things but doesn't understand it. Uses very specific vocabulary all the time but uses them incorrectly and doesn't understand background. Tests are often wrong, impossible to work with him on it.

I never got the feeling that Dr. Reed enjoys teaching about religion. In fact I never got the feeling that he had a testimony or felt the spirit in his class. I think he just loves knowing about the history and facts. This class was spiritually destructive to me, he was not good at resolving conflicting ideas and just does not teach by the spirit.

Dr. Reed is a chill dude. His World Religions class is really great in the sense that I feel it will really benefit me in the future as I interact with people of different cultures. That being said, there is a TON of reading. And the tests can be pretty tough. Not a lot of opportunities to increase your grade.

You must take this class from him! He knows so much and explains things so clearly! There's a lot of reading, but he goes over it in class and explains it all. Don't miss class. The lectures are the majority of the test, but the tests and quizzes are easy.  You can use your scriptures so just write your notes in there. Best teacher ever!

Dr. Reed is a fantastic lecturer, I learned so much from this class.  There's a lot of assigned reading, but in reality if you just read the assigned scriptures and some of the other stuff, you'll be fine.  The tests are pretty specific, so you'll have to study for them, but I highly recommend taking this class from Dr. Reed.
He is a great teacher! I took his evening section of Foundations of the Restoration and we had the BEST discussions. I would take this class over and over again if I could.

Personally, I loved Dr. Reed! I also really enjoyed learning about all of the different religions - SO interesting! Yeah sure, there are a few quizzes and you've gotta memorize a bit for tests but looking back on the class it honestly wasn't the hardest. Pretty chill. And Dr. Reed is totally willing to work with you on your grade. He's awesome.

Loved this class. I think it should be required for everyone. Prof. Reed is amazing! Seriously, his humor is hard to figure out at first, but then the class becomes super chill. Expect to read a lot. Like that is how you pass this class, by reading what he assigns. You also get participation but it's mostly attendance. He really knows his stuff.

Unfortunately, I wish I didn't take this class because I don't need it for my major or for generals. Dr. Reed is very knowledgeable, but I wasn't intrigued during his lectures. Lots of quizzes, but he does offer a lot of extra credit. There are only two tests: a midterm and a final. Also, he requires you to write an investigation paper.

Tests are very lengthy and there is a lot of writing required. He also expects you to memorize a lot of information about every religion for the each test and there is a very comprehensive quiz on each religion on the first day of discussing it.

Not particularly accommodating with regard to absences, even university excused ones, and participation counts for a significant part of your grade. Gives pop quizzes, which you can't make up for ANY reason. Lectures seemed a bit scattered. That said, good class if you've never interacted with people of other religions. Meh at best if you have.
Interesting subject matter. Highly interactive and and engaging teacher. Assignments and tests completed with ease.

Burt is a great professor, and his class was easy-going. My only gripe is that we were rarely tested on the Book of Mormon outside of reflections, so when the final came up, I felt unprepared, even after studying the study guide. If cramming is your style, then this is a great class, but I know some people struggle to learn without a challenge.

I originally did not want to take the book of mormon class but ended up having to, he made the class enjoyable and spoke about the book of mormon in a very educated and refreshing way. Fantastic teacher, I learned so much.
He didn't want this to be an overwhelming class but instead a class where we got to learn for the joy of it on a whole new level. He was fun and very understanding with everyone.

As long as I showed up, this class was never a stress for me. Prof. Burt definitely puts his whole heart into the class, and it never fails to put a smile on my face! He explores the Book of Mormon and its themes in a really unique, deep way that gets me thinking for myself.

Brother Burt has a passion for the Book of Mormon that is contagious. His lectures are very engaging and bring a different perspective to gospel principles. He is very understanding when it comes to your grade and will go the extra mile to help you achieve the outcome that you deserve.

Professor Burt is a very knowledgeable professor. He cares deeply about the content he covers. He discusses different viewpoints from philosophers as well as different faith that relate to themes in the Book of Mormon all centered on Christ. He has inspired me and has helped me learn of Christ. I would recommend Professor Burt, 10/10.

He's a really good guy, super humble and willing to accept feedback. His lectures felt like they were AI-generated - good information, but usually vague and difficult to follow without any focus or rigor. He's passionate but seems to lack applicable knowledge. Class activities usually feel like busywork, but a few are genuinely helpful.

by far the worst class I have taken. the material seemed a bit redundant and there was an insane amount of homework. Dr South seemed to not know what he was talking about half the time and for a 100 level introductory course into the program it was way harder than it should have been. do a study abroad for this course if you can

South's class is just an insane amount of busy work that doesn't feel like it applies to sustainable infrastructure in the slightest. His use of AI gets really annoying, it feels like his slides and assignments have all just been generated with no revisions.

He is a great person and truly cares about the students and wants them to succeed. He is always willing to take and answer questions and give feedback back. He is a little unorganized in his course material but he gets things worked out. He brings up the gospel often and it's inspiring to see his faith. Can distract from the course. Great guy.

My least favorite professor at BYU this far. His classes are extremely unorganized and it is very clear he has no idea what is going on. Expectations are very unclear. The course isn't too hard but due to his lack of preparation and clear expectations it makes it hard to learn the material.

This class could be helpful if you're interested in architecture or environmental extremism. However, the course often felt unorganized, and it was hard to know what to expect during lectures. The assignments were unclear and often seemed prepared at the last minute.

South was in charge of developing a new version of the 311 this last semester, so I understand why it was difficult for lots of students. But, the TA was very helpful and if you actually utilize that resource, pay attention during class, and ask questions/emails, then you can easily get an A. He was open to feedback on the class which was helpful.

311 with South. Assigned huge tasks with poor grading standards. Plan sets were sloppy and unprofessional. He had a general idea of what to teach but lacked proper preparation. This didn't seem like his top priority—I wouldn't be surprised if he was dealing with personal issues. Didn't feel at all valuable to my education. Total joke of a class.

CFM 311
Don't take a class from this guy, lots of homework that appears randomly so if you are looking to plan ahead for them forget about it. The homework was a big project due every single week, not even that the homework was not clear at all. The class is not engaging and confusing. Please do yourself a favor and don't take a class from him.
Complicated and confusing. It felt like he rarely came to class himself. Things were explained poorly. Homework was on unclear or uncovered topics

Dr. Bradford does a great job of teaching MFT theories & the lectures are very discussion based. The assignments are applicable & help you really engaged with the theories. You watch therapy sessions and write about them and write a couple short papers that are helpful in preparing to become an MFT! I definitely recommend for aspiring MFTs

I really liked Dr. Bradford. Shes an entertaining lecturer and I felt like she did a good job walking us through each theory. Lots of class participation. It's hard cause it's a 400 level class not cause Dr. Bradford intentionally makes it hard. She is really good at recognizing the needs of the class.

This professor was nice and interesting to listen to. I enjoyed lectures when we actually learned things. Most of the class time was spent on "debates" that each group had to do in front of the HUGE class. The assigned reading was ridiculous and the pop quizzes in class everyday were so hard, sometimes it didn't matter if you read. Tests were hard.

Make sure to do the reading for each and every class- pop quizzes are somewhat tricky even if you have read. I worked really hard all semester and thought I had barely pulled off an A (a 93). After finals, Dr. B changed her grading scale so a 95 was needed to get an A. Test questions often worded unclearly. Good class but take it from someone else.

Make sure to read before class so you can do well on in-class quizzes and take notes on lectures. The tests may have extraneous information that was not covered in depth, so really take studying into your own hands. Follow the rubric exactly for the papers, she has tough guidelines for her TAs when it comes to grading.

I loved Dr. Bradford's class!! Lectures were very interesting, but sometimes rushed because we had little class time. You HAVE to do the reading because she does pop iClicker quizzes. Tests are more application based. TAs are VERY helpful in clarifying material & for getting help on essays! If you put the work in, it is truly doable. TAKE HER CLASS

Professor Bradford is a great and engaging teacher, but there wasn't enough time in lecture to cover everything. Many questions on the tests came from the reading, and there was a lot of reading, which made it hard to know what to focus on while studying. The TA's were great, make sure to meet with them about your papers.

Attendance not mandatory because class time was not spent on lectures and was a waste of time. Bradford is passionate, but only teaches a fraction of what is needed for tests - the rest must be learned from textbook. Not the worse prof ever, but there are definitely better options for the same class.

Very straightforward person and it makes for good lectures. Iclickers are used every class and some pop quizzes. Really clear tests that are not bad at all. Plan your time well with the papers because they have a lot of power.

Professor Bradford is really smart and knows what she is talking about. Papers are definitely not an "easy A". Ours were 6-7 pages and there are 2 of them and you need to have good formatting. Make sure to meet with a TA to go over your paper because that helps. They are doable. Her tests were somewhat difficult but the study guide helped a lot.

Once you get used to her directness, she's a really great professor! Her directions aren't always clear but she's aware of that and is realistic about her expectations. I thought it was cool that she shares examples of different types of therapy, so you can see what the book talks about.

This class was helpful for preparing me for MFT but I didn't feel passionate about the engagement in class. It was an easy A because (as a senior) I had heard this material in SFL 336, made easy tests. The professor is a very experienced clinician but class times were for me just copying down powerpoint slides instead of expounding thoughts.

Dr. Bradford is awesome! She makes class fun and interesting. I feel like I learned how to be a better mother and caregiver. The class was good - the study guides are extensive so plan to study a lot for the tests.  However, papers are an easy A so just do well on those and you'll be fine.

Dr. Bradford is seriously the best. She is hilarious, caring, and competent. She is a good example of a working woman with a family. She gives incredibly helpful study guides and allows for student participation. I loved this woman. The essays are fairly tough, so make sure you attend all TA help sessions for them. All in all, a great class. :)
She is amazing! She cares so much for her students. All of the assignments are interesting and not just busy work. I would 100% recommend taking her class!

Classes were a good mix of informative and engaging. She cares a lot about writing and her students. You end up writing a significant amount by the end of the semester but the workload is broken up into manageable chunks. I'd recommend her class!

Prof. Jones is the most human professor in the CS department. She's caring and friendly and her due dates are reasonable. The actual class isn't too bad, I thought lecture wasn't very helpful, so I only attended labs and still got an A. The homework is manageable and you can get extensions to due dates. Don't use AI to write code or you're cooked.

Professor Jones is awesome! She explained things super well and broke each example problem down into steps that were easy to follow. I ended up not going to class a lot towards the end of the semester which was fine because she posts lecture and lab help videos online. If you go to class she often gives homework and project hints.

I highly recommend taking CS110 from Professor Jones. She was a great lecturer and always attentive. Attendance is optional but strongly recommended. The class itself is well-structured and not very difficult. Strongly recommended taking CS 110 before CS 111/IS 303 if you haven't programmed in years or haven't programmed before.

Absolutely loved CS 110 with Professor Jones! I think the class is structured really great, and with Professor Jones as your lecturer it gets better. She's very caring, always willing to answer a student's question about what we're doing the moment comes up (which isn't bothersome because everyone else has the same question just no one is asking!)

I loved Professor Jones she was so caring and sweet! There are a ton of resources to help if you're lost and TA hours are super helpful if you get stuck on a homework or project. I thought it was a great beginner coding environment because of all that.

She was good! my one complaint is that it's sometimes difficult to get help. At least for myself, I took the class completely online and wasn't able to attend any TA hours or anything in person. The TAs were slow to help and Professor Jones often just deferred to them. But when it really counted, she was helpful.

I took this class online and it consisted of watching lecture videos, watching a lab video, and then doing homework. The bulk of the grades are projects after each unit and they can take some time, but aren't super difficult. Dr. Jones was a good online teacher and I you still can go into TA office hours whenever you want.

She is just so nice. Lectures explained everything clearly, homework and assignments were clearly organized. Useful programming help pages were linked to every assignment. Lab section was over zoom for the online students, but I was able to figure the assignments out on my own usually. She's very understanding and easy to contact.

For those of you not ready to take on CS 111, I think Professor Jones is a great option for CS 110. She did a great job introducing the fundamental concepts of coding and showing in person examples of how the code works in class. The majority of this class is coursework and the tests are weighted less than in most other classes.

I took her for CS 110 and it was a very streamlined experience. 2 homework assignments with 2 labs a week with the occasional project. It is a great intro to computer science class that isn't too difficult if you pay attention and ask questions. There is a help lab available and you get to use applicable skills fairly quickly.

Dr. Jones was good. I was in-person and it was nice to go, but not necessary. She also always had a video posted of each lecture and lab, walking you through. You get a few assignments every week, it starts out super basic then ramps up a little bit, but I don't think I would ever say it was hard. Easy GPA booster class.

Professor Jones obviously cares about her students and is willing to work with you on assignments. Not only does she encourage questions about assignments in class but she is easy to access outside of class. She can often be found in the CS lab helping students. Although attendance is not mandatory, she sometimes did homework questions in class.

I took the online class. Everything was set up well, but there are lots of small assignments, and sometimes you had to use multiple websites to make sure you were keeping up with everything. I feel like it gave me a good grasp of coding. Attending an in person lab section was super helpful for completing the homework.
The online section is super easy if you have any prior coding experience or are well-acquainted with computers. She is really helpful when things don't make sense.

Professor Jones is extremely kind and shows a lot of care for her students. I wish I could give a 4.5 rating. The class was made as easy as possible given the amount of content that is covered, and she is extremely helpful and reasonable. the only reason I didn't give a five was because some of the lectures were a little boring and confusing.

I loved her! She really loves art and history and I learned a lot from this class. She will help you if you email her. I would add a warning that she is a tough grader but she does give the exam questions before. Also go to the TA review because they will give you topics you should cover. This is a very doable class if you work hard.

She is an amazing teacher!! I loved her class. The tests are graded tough but she gives you the essay questions beforehand, so you can prepare as much as you want! You don't need to pay attention in class if you lock in before the tests. I would 100% take her class again.

The writing is disproportionately weighted in your grade, and the grading criteria are all over the place. You will give the same amount of effort for similar assignments/tests and will get drastically different results. The lectures were pretty boring and a chore to sit through. You are given a very detailed study guide for the tests.

There are in class assignments that will drop your grade if you aren't there. She lays out what the exams will be like. Give yourself adequate time to prep for them - they require you to memorize everything. She is open to giving you help, and she will give you feedback on the exams. Test are taken in the testing lab. She understands this is a GE.

If you are looking for an easy GE, this is a solid choice. The paper nearly killed me at the end of the semester, but it helps that we only did one! The exams are easy to pass since she gives great feedback and detailed guides! Attendance does matter though, because she has weekly in-class assignments! She is super nice if you need help!

Angela was a joy to be taught from. She knows a lot about art history, teaches in an engaging, clear way, and really makes it possible for anyone to succeed. It's still a college-level class with an academic research paper, group presentations, and exams that really assess your understanding, but she makes it all doable and meaningful. Loved it!

Angela is an excellent professor, and I highly recommend her to anyone looking to take ARTHC 202. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about art history, so I always found her lectures fascinating and engaging. There are a number of big assignments in the class (e.g. group presentation and research paper), but she has very clear expectations.

I really enjoyed Angela's class. She knows her content incredibly well, but she also knows that not everybody is an art lover. She teaches the material clearly and provides more tools for success than any professor I've had before. I'd highly recommend this class to anyone and promise that you'll be able to learn a lot and do well.

She is the best! I was nervous is take this class because I'm not a art/history person, but she makes it engaging and enjoyable. I felt very 'scholarly' after taking this class and could hold a conversation about art. That being said, do NOT procrastinate studying or the assignments. Tests are all essay and kind of intense, but she prepares you!

Do yourself a favor and take this class from a different professor. She provides the essay prompts beforehand but there are 7 of them to prepare for and she nit picks on the details. Her expectations are only semi-clear and her feedback only gives you some idea of what you could have done better.

Incredibly passionate about her subject material but also realizes that she's teaching a GE. You know exactly how to prepare for tests and weekly assignments are VERY manageable. She's very understanding and will work with you individually if there is a need. She's a lovely person and even brought cookies! Anyone would enjoy this class!

She's SO sweet, super quick to respond to emails, definitely cares about you and your success in her class. You'll learn a ton from her! She provides study guides and very clear expectations for the exams. There's one term paper with very open-ended topics, so you can write about almost anything. I can't recommend Prof. Wescott enough!
Lectures are optional but very helpful. Tests are clear and the answers are given in class. Expectations are clear. I learned a ton and enjoyed the class!

Such a great teacher! Most of the lectures were really interesting and I feel like I learned a lot about both art and history. She gives you all of the potential essay questions on the exam beforehand so if you prepare well, the tests are extremely straightforward (and graded fairly). Take this class for your generals!

She was very clear and knowledgeable. She knew her material and was more than willing to help her students out. In other ARTHC classes, I have fallen asleep because they are so dry. I didn't fall asleep once in her class. You know exactly what is on the tests and she grades very fairly. Take this class!

Sadly, this class was a huge waste of time. Wescott just talks and talks for 50 minutes and can't get the class envolved. The occasional homework was easy, but I felt like I wasn't learning anything by doing it. I can honestly say I did not learn a single thing from this class.
Sis. Wescott taught me so much about art! She felt rushed by the curriculum, but taught effectively. Hers was one of my favorite classes.
She made the class interesting. If you take good notes and prepare for the tests, it's a pretty easy A. You'll know exactly what's on the test a week or so before.

Very helpful, and fun to be in class with. The classes were long sometimes, but that's just what happens in a three-hour class. She gives you a break in the middle though.Tests are easy as long as you prepare properly. She'll give you all the help/information you need. Great class!

Angela is awesome! She is very helpful during her office hours and always willing to work with you.  Lectures were 2.5 hours so obviously dragged on, but I like to think it was the subject matter and not the teacher.  Just study what she tells you and you'll do fine

Lots of work outside of class for group presentations. She has a convoluted attendance policy involving written arguments advocating for your participation grade. She facilitates great discussion but often lets the class get into the weeds. She is a very lenient grader and her test for ethics were fairly easy.

This felt like a high school class. Each day, students grade themselves on how well they participated (did you comment in class, refrain from doing homework, etc). This is later used to write two essays about what grade you feel you deserve. The textbook was very informative but the lectures were just class discussions that were not very helpful.

She is a good professor. There are small weekly readings of a book, one big group project, a handful of small papers and two tests. You will be graded on participation during class, so don't skip it. It's really not a hard class, just participate and talk to the TA's about the papers if you're struggling. Fair grading.

As a premed, non philosophy major, this class was tough. Definitely don't take this class if you're premed looking for MMI practice; there are much easier ways to get that. The exam study guides are like 200 questions and she only gives them out the week before the exam. Everything is graded very hard, but she is very willing to work with students.

I really liked Dr. Faulconer because she was willing to make adjustments when needed. The class really is just read, discuss, and write. When we asked her to push stuff back, she would as much as she could. Super loving.

Dr. Faulconer is a good professor. Tests are straightforward and the material is easy. I found in class dicussions to usually be dull. I would've enjoyed looser debates that weren't totally based on textbook readings. She is very kind. 

My major gripe is that the thematic essays are graded somewhat arbitrarily and at the mercy of the TA.

LOVE HER. favorite class this semester. I would seriously recommend everyone take it. Granted I'm a Phil major so I am biased. This class is totally discussion based, not lecture heavy. Readings are short and super interesting. She grades hard but the criteria is clear and pretty fair. Papers aren't too difficult once you get the requirements.

Assigns papers that are difficult for non philosophy majors and grades them harshly. You also are only allowed three absences the whole semester. The midterm and final are worth 40% of your grade. She tries to answer questions the class has but I would not recommend this class unless you are willing to participate heavily for an ideal grade.

Class is very interesting and the professor makes it enjoyable to go to. She is tough on grading but pushes you to be better. She really knows her stuff and respect others opinions and views. Very understanding to life situations that arise
Terrible. This class fulfills the Bio major requirement but has nothing to do with biology. Ridiculous class structure and VERY strict grading. RUN!

This class is heavily graded on participation. Weekly reading with a prep assignment, handful of short essays, one group project, one midterm, and a final. The class structure follows a pretty set routine. Harsh grader, but could be worse. I would say I definitely don't enjoy philosophy, but this class really isn't too bad.

It seems a lot of the reviews are made by people who don't expect what a philosophy class is like. In short, you read a philosophy essay (usually an influential one), you discuss it for about a week in class, then (usually) write a 2-page paper on a related topic. Faulconer does this well, distilling the complex topics into their basic arguments

Very boring class. In-class participation was so emphasized that I often felt we learned nothing from the discussions. She grades harshly, none of this semesters projects or essays scored 100%. It feels like shes justifying her role as a teacher by grading harshly. Nonetheless, shes a nice person and knows a lot about philosophy. Dont expect an A.

Love her! Class was discussion-based and was always really interesting. She is very respectful of everyone's opinions. Somewhat harsh grader but not too bad. Participation is HUGE. As long as you are there every day, stay engaged, and offer comments, you'll be great with those points. Tests aren't too bad and she gives a great study guide.

The lectures are interesting, and pretty participation heavy. There are quite a few readings that you have to do before class in order to participate, and a portion of your grade IS based off of participation. There are also a few essays, but they are pretty short, and the exams aren't super difficult. I absolutely recommend the class for a general

If you are looking for something to fulfill your Letters general, I would not recommend this class. This class is full of busywork, and the material is so dry. It may seem like an easy class, but it's rather difficult for being a general. If you like being forced to give comments and write things about material you don't understand, take this class
Dr. Faulconer is very intelligent and always gives great lectures. PHIL 110 can be taken as a general credit, so I highly recommend signing up even if you aren't a philosophy major!

Great Professor who really values what we think. Attendance is crucial but the discussions were always interesting so you wouldn't want to skip anyways. Very understanding and willing to work with you. She always left really good feedback on papers and wants you to succeed. I recommend this class to everyone even if they aren't in the major. 10/10!

Dr. Faulconer is very intelligent and a tough grader. That being said, Bioethics was the best class I've taken at BYU. Your grade relies on intelligent participation and excellent writing. You need to know your stuff (that means read: over and over again). She is kind and willing to help you. She even invited us to her house for dinner.

The test midterm was verbatim the study guide.  Took me 10 minutes and I got 100%.  She grades your writing semi-tough, but it's still an easy A if you participate in class.  It's really just a fun class.  If it's not interesting to you then you won't do well, but if you like it then you'll do great.

I had doubts about signing up for a Philosophy class, but it was actually somewhat interesting and she is funny and involves the class. Lots of participation so get ready to speak up! As long as you know what she wants for the graded responses, you'll be fine. Midterm and a final and some pop quizzes. Take it from her!

A fantastic professor.  She's kind of new, but she's very helpful and very interested in doing a great job. She's a very nice person.  Class discussions were fun and insightful, and she was very willing to change things up based on where the discussion was heading.  I'd highly recommend her classes.

Class is entirely busy work. I was putting in a ridiculous amount of time doing unnecessary  work. Readings were ridiculously hard. She changes her expectations all the time. You have to do group meetings every week and honestly they became pointless after a while. If you want to have the workload of a 400 level class then take this class.

great class! she memorized all of our names on the first day. be meticulous and follow grading criteria for full points. she values creativity most. helpful TAs. and there are extra credit opportunities. W for international students

She was such a good teacher! She's phenomenal at teaching course concepts. The homework load honestly isn't a lot. If you just do the work, you're going to get an A in the class. Usually, homework and assignments are due before class, but she leaves assignments open for that whole week. Attendance is graded.

Professor Imbler was kind, but a bit pessimistic. Her lectures were long, and if you had a different opinion from hers, she would get very defensive. Some of her emails were also very passive-aggressive, and it wasn't a safe environment to foster learning. She also would give you an activity and then sit on her phone in the back or at the front.

I love Ann Dee! I had a great time in her class. She can be difficult to get a hold of outside of class because she rarely checks her email, but she's very present when you're with her. A lot of the class is self-graded, so be honest and you'll do fine.

THE BEST. She said "We writers... we talk and talk about how great writing is, and we never do it." LOL! So in this class you have to write an hour a day for homework and I LOVED IT! Nothing will improve your writing more than actually writing and Ann Dee knows that and leans into it. Take this class.

She is the best teacher! I love her so much! This class is a ton of workshops on each other's stories and writing your own stories. It's really fun, and you really become friends with everyone. It's very casual and easy, but you really learn a lot! I'd take her for any class I can, especially this one!

She is one of the best writing professors I've taken! I loved her approach to workshopping, the freedom we had in the independent research project and I appreciated how she pivoted based on feedback to teach us more publishing-industry-specific details. She requires 1 hour of writing or 500 words per day, which encourages a valuable writing habit.

Way too much homework (you have to write for 1 hour every day in addition to readings) but this class did more for me than any other creative writing class. She doesn't have a lot of confidence in herself which is odd, because she's awesome. I loved all the guest speakers but I wanted to hear more from Ann Dee. One of the best classes at at BYU.

This class involves a ton of reading, but for the most part they are novels and fiction. So it isn't too bad. She divides the class into small writing groups and that is really the focus of the class. I improved my writing and enjoyed my group, but try to take it with a friend so you do have someone you know in your group.

Gives a hard class, but it is more than worth it. She grades tough but allows revisions on all papers which allows for growth opportunities. She doesn't grade all the small assignments, but make sure to do them because they help so much. Revise every paper. Come prepared to class. Definitely would take again, I benefitted from this class so much.

Professor Low is really kind and supportive. I used to struggle with writing, but her class made it feel way less intimidating. I'd definitely recommend her to anyone who doesn't love writing or wants to get better at it. Her grading is very clear and fair, and you can miss up to two classes before it counts against you.

Professor Low is one of my favorite professors I have ever had at BYU. Although the hours of the class are extensive, she makes the time pass quickly by making class legitimately fun. The assignments are not tough, yet they really help you improve as a writer. She is very understanding and wants to help everyone. TAKE WRITING 150 FROM PROF LOW!
Lots of papers but it's a writing class so it should be expected. Interesting class, you are able to write about what interests you. Gives good feedback

She did a fantastic job, you have to do a lot of papers but it did not feel to bad. The professor does a great job of helping if you ask any questions and makes everything clear if you are confused. Highly recommend taking WRTG 150 with her.

Professor Low teaches in a very application-based way and encourages us to look through the lens of rhetoric and apply this concept to our assignments. Very considerate and cares about her students and their ability to succeed. Good amount of reading and lets students chose topics they are interested in to write papers on.

She is a super fun and nice professor! She even brings food to class sometimes and is pretty nice with grading except i am pretty sure it is impossible to get 100% on your papers. But other than that super enjoyable and still wasn't too hard to get an a or a-.

Absolutely loved her class! Her classes were so interesting and I learned a lot. She also really helped the class with time management to help us get the big papers completed on time and with confidence in our writing!

Anna Low definitely been one of my top favorite Professors at BYU! She super positive/caring and does fun activities. She's super willing to help you out if you need it and is always there for you. You are expected to work in the class but its not overwhelming at all. The papers you write in class she will help you along the entire process.

So understanding and caring about any struggles I had, and she always had the best comments when students presented or turned in papers. I thought it was super cool that she memorized and remembered the names of all the students in my class. We got to write on any topics we were interested in, and she was always respectful towards our beliefs

I like the class and the source material. I really appreciate that we can choose our topics for writing, as long as they fit the criteria. However, as far as grading goes, she is either really picky, or I can't get a read on what she wants. I feel a little like I need to read the professor's mind to get an A in her class.

My favorite teacher this past Winter 2021 online semester. Very few assignments but are worth a lot of points and teach the necessary skills. I became a much better listener, writer and researcher. Loved the Prof and the way she has the class structured. Easy grade if you work hard to write well but not too bad. Wish I could take again!!

Anna Low is my one of my favorite professors at BYU! You can tell that she truly cares about her students well-being and their success. It is a writing class, so be prepared for a lot of writing but she is willing to help in any way possible. She gives amazing feedback! I would recommend her.

Prof Low expects a lot for a writing course, but she does set you up for success. The assignments are tedious, but they really help to make you a better writer. The class was straightforward and laid out clearly. There were 3 major papers, and various small assignments due throughout the week. If you work hard on the 3 papers, you will get an A.

Anna is a great teacher; she got her masters from Harvard. She can be a tough grader but is willing to work with you. You can tell she loves and cares for her students. The difference between the 1 and 2 credit sections was an extra hour in class/week.

I enjoyed the class. We had lots of good opportunities to practice reading, writing, and speaking Spanish. She cares a lot about the students and addresses individual needs well.

Because she isn't a native speaker she genuinely listened to all of our "what if" questions & instead of dismissing them as stupid (like some native teacher do)  she would research questions right there. She was more like the guide and we were all learned together.  As long as you can defend your answer, she's good about giving points back on tests

She's pretty strict and a tough grader, especially on essays. She seems to want things done a very specific way. She's good at giving points back on tests though.
This class has lots of assignments, but be sure to stay on top of it and you'll be okay.
The class was enjoyable. I liked having exposure to many different Spanish songs. However, the curriculum was scattered and I thought that class time was used inefficiently.

What I liked the most about her was that she would research questions right on the spot to make sure she was giving us the most correct explanation to an answer. It showed me how I can look up my own questions and how to use given examples to find the generic usage of a word. What I dislike were all the errors that were on tests and quizzes.

It was a fun class just to relax & have a chance to practice some Spanish. For some reason, I had been under the impression the class was for a grade, but in the end it was just a pass/fail course, which was slightly disappointing, but probably appropriate since the class doesn't require much. If you are looking for a fun 1 credit class, take it!

This class is still being developed. There was no course syllabus and the grade is completely dependent on attendance. It is fun and there is a good music to learn, but I wouldn't go out of my way to take it again.
She is great! Very helpful when you ask. She has an amazing vocabulary and speaks so that you can understand and is super nice!

This was one of my favorite classes! Anne is an amazing person and an amazing professor. She really cares, has a lot of experience, and knows what she is doing!

She grades tough too, but gives solid feedback to help you improve for the next time, and she'll always help you if you reach out to her. She's amazing at applying what she teaches. Take for sure!!

Anne's lectures are the best! She tells amazing stories and you learn SO much in her class. The work load is doable, especially if you get stuff done during the class time she gives you to work with your group. The workload can seem overwhelming, but it gets done.

Take Anne's class! She makes you work for your grade, but she is willing to fix your grade to reflect your improvement in her class. She'll make you laugh in every class and she is very knowledgable in child development. I can actually see the application of her class in real world situations. She really makes you think for yourself.

TAKE THIS CLASS FROM ANNE. Fabulous class and SO rewarding. Anne is one of the best teachers I've had. Anne knows her stuff and makes content accessible and interesting. The class is overwhelming at first, but you get the hang of it. One class a week is lecture, the other is groupwork, so attendance is graded. If you put in the work you'll get an A

Anne is a funny lady, but has an intense personality, so don't be offended if she says something that seems rude. She really is a nice person! This class requires a lot of work and can be frustrating at times because the requirements for the group work change every unit and the powerpoints are graded pretty hard. But Anne is there for you!

Anne is an incredible teacher with so much knowledge of child development! She made class lectures fun and interesting. The class requires a LOT of group work and consistent assignments, but deadlines and expectations are always 100% clear. All assignments are useful for future teaching. Tests are easy and open book. Take this class!

Anne is a great lady but a terrible teacher for college students. She left us feeling confused and stressed every lesson & her grading was completely unfair. If this class is any indicator of the quality of BYU's ElEd program then there are nothing but dark clouds in its future. She teaches how to be a good teacher but doesn't apply those teachings

TAKE A CLASS FROM THIS LADY. She is awesome. I actually looked forward and enjoyed going to a 3 hour night class. Great and funny instructor. Class mostly designed around group work and fairly easy. Tests are open book/open note and come straight from the text. Assignments are actually helpful. Build your toolkit as you go, not the night before!

She is the BEST teacher for Child Development. I really liked the way that this course was set up. She is very accommodating and understanding of her students and always has the best intentions. Her tests are open book but can be tricky. However, this class is very organized and interesting.

I loved this course. Other sections of the same class use a sociology book (for a parenting class??), but Ann uses an actual parenting book. Long reading assignments, but interesting for the most part. If I had any problems, it was with the TA who loved taking off points; Ann was full of energy, made the class fun, and a fair teacher.
I LOVED this class! It was fun and interesting and extremely informative. Dr. Ure was great; she made sure that we understood the material well and her midterm wasn't too hard if you studied for it.
No Comments

This class was fun but more work than I expected. The mid-term is hard but you are allowed to argue your essay parts. The final is take home and then in oral-real easy. The teacher is excited but some times a little hard to follow. You have weekly assignments that are time consuming. Overall, it was an alright class.

Prof. Mella is super nice, and very relaxed about due dates (as compared to others who teach this class). A lot of the time I didn't feel it was necessary to be in class, but she was always helpful when I had specific questions. Have her edit your compositions and you'll get As on them. A lot of homework (regardless of who you take it from).

Hna. Mella is funny. A bit unorganized. Very kind. You can turn in things whenever. Homework everyday but it's not hard. 4 100-question tests + final. Can be hard but not very. Compositions, Spanish event write-ups, quizzes, presentation - all very, very easy. If you're looking for an easy A from a funny teacher, she's your woman.

SUPER easy. I did not go on a mission, and my spanish was bad but I needed this class for my major. She is super understanding and so willing to help. Easy class if I can pass but honestly she's funny and always tells interesting stories. I recommend her.

I HIGHLY recommend this class for RM's looking to get some Spanish credits. Class time is kinda a waste of time but the class is SUPER easy. If you learn anything (you probably will), it will be from the text book but definitely not from the teacher. Again, if you speak Spanish and just need credits, highly recommend.
Boring lectures. Weird reading assignments. Willing to help.

I felt like 90% of the students could speak Spanish better than she could. She would correct things on your papers that weren't wrong originally, but the corrections were sometimes inaccurate. Still a super easy class though. She basically just reviewed the common grammar most people have heard 20 times already. and was very dull. Often inaccurate.
Lectures are a little slow and boring but there are no surprises in this class. She's consistent.
Great Teacher!  She gets a HUGE smile on her face every time someone asks a question.  She loves to teach and loves to help others learn.

Hna Mella, nice lady, SUPER easy class.  If you just got off the mish and are looking for an easy A this is the one.  She is kind of annoying and talks about nothing a lot of the time, but she will give you the answers to the tests. Not a great class, but an easy A.

Easy A, just study the vocab she goes over before the test. She gives the answers to the quizzes. Take her if you are in it for the 16 credits, and dont have much time to dedicate to the class. She is good though

Hermana Mella was a great teacher. Im not a super smart person but was still able to pull off an A in her class. She has been around for a long time as a professor so she know what it takes for her students to learn the required criteria. I definitely would recommend taking her. Great teacher
bo.  I hated the class.  Horrible teacher.  She does not look to help anyone.  Doesn't do well answering questions, and does not explain anything.  Don't take her class.

Mella was not a good teacher. easy as that.  She goes off on random tangents about politics in the middle of lectures and does not explain anything well.  Pretty much you have to read it from the book.  She will drive you crazy.  If you are looking to get a B, very easy.  To excel and really understand the material, do NOT take it from Mella.

Mella is a very easy teacher. I hardly studied for tests and browsed the web during most of class, and I still got a B+ in the class. She has 4 essays and like 6 tests, plus some homework that she doesn't even grade, you just show it to her and she marks you down. If you want an easy grade, take it. If you want to learn spanish, don't do Mella.

If you are a returned missionary looking to get credit for the spanish you learned and aren't planning on majoring/minoring in spanish, this is the way to go. Easy to get an A, just not much a teacher- you won't learn hardly anything, especially if you already have a pretty good grasp on spanish.

Prof. Mella has been one of my favorite teacher here at BYU. She teaches a class designed for returned missionaries and she does a great job at it.  I found her very funny and anyone who doesnt like the class just expects the teacher to teach every things and is to lazy to work on thier own to learn.  She was a great teacher
boring and long winding in tangents. good hearted but doesn't push the class to learn anything. If you are bored easily don't sign up for her class. you will go insane

She is an EXTREMELY boring teacher... Most of the time she talks in English anyway and she rambles on about crap that is totally irrelevant to the class.  She is a push over though for the most part.  She reads STRAIGHT from the text book so I don't think that you have to attend class if you are self motivated.  I hated the class personally.

The worst class I have taken at BYU. Prof Mella is a nice woman, but if you're actually hoping to improve your Spanish, look somewhere else. She's very scatterbrained and goes off on random, pointless tangents every two mins, and she speaks mostly in English, with some Spanglish. I only go to class when there's something to turn in.

Good, kind-hearted lady, terrible professor. When I approached her about the grading of several essays, I asked her why what I had written was wrong. She only replied that her Chilean husband said it sounded wrong, and that I could verify on Google, but she didn't know what the Real Academia said. She left abruptly without answering anything else.

I signed up for her class 2 differant symesters because it is always the only one that is not full, but after one day each time I dropped it for fear of loosing my sanity. When asked a question she just goes on and on in english about nothing and changes the subject and 30 minuets later the class is over and she has said nothing.

She has an extremely easy class with an easy grading scale.  Also her tests aren't very hard.  She's not very clear when answering questions though.  A great class if you just want the test for the 16 credits, but if you actually want to learn a lot you might want to try another teacher.

She is a great spanish teacher.  She is very knowledgable and definitly knows her spanish very well.  I would recommend taking spanish from her.  Shes always willing to answer quesions and is a very nice lady.  Shes laid back and fun just like a spanish class should be.  Its my favorite class!!

She is a great spanish teacher.  She is very knowledgable and definitly knows her spanish very well.  I would recommend taking spanish from her.  Shes always willing to answer quesions and is a very nice lady.  Shes laid back and fun just like a spanish class should be.  Its my favorite class!!

What more can I say? Everyone else has already said it. I would advise to try and take the class from ANYONE else who is teaching it. She asks for respect and then does not give it in return to past or present students or even to other faculty members. NO ONE know grammar better than she does - according to herself....

DON'T TAKE THIS FROM HER. Yes, she's easy, but the class is ridiculous. She talks to herself the entire period and eventually gets somewhere with a point. There are much better teachers than Prof. Mella, esp. since they actually teach grammar than ramble incessantly about nothing. She takes 50 minutes to give the translations for 8 vocab words. Does anyone really want to sit through this? She just repeats what the textbook says and never gets anywhere in her lectures. You can get an A by going to 3 lectures, at best. That's what I did. And I regretted it because she just wasted an entire semester of mine.
Hna. Mella is a nice lady and helpful within her limited sphere of understanding, but not that great of a teacher.  Take 321 or 322 for her if you want and an A without the work.

You mean people actually want to learn this stuff? I thought this was the most slack class I have ever taken, such a nice break from the sciences.  I didn't open my book once, hardly went to lecture (when i say hardly, i mean like 6 times the whole year). I didnt even know what the tests were going to be on but i just went and took them. Great!

Easiest class i have ever taken.  I can't believe this is considered higher education.  Never had to do the homework, attendance not necessary but i went anyway to play Party Poker on my laptop.  You get the tests ahead of time and the final was open book and notes.  If you want to cheat yourself out of an education this is the class to take.

I just didn't like this class at all.  If you're not majoring or minoring in Spanish don't take it.  It won't help you with your language.  It's just maticulous grammar.  No fun.  Hermana Mella is a very sweet person, not the best teacher but she's totally willing to help you and she's very easy going.  Give her respect.

Hma. Mella is very nice and easy going. She does know her grammer well, however on her tests there are always several errors in spelling or ortografía, things that we would be docked for in compositions. The class is very laid back. Tests are online before in class exam and final was on blackboard. I heard this may change, may be well to find out.
I felt like I learned just as much if not more by reading the text book on my own rather than going to class.  Everything was very lax: due dates, attendance, test taking . . .

She may be the worst teacher I've ever had. She might know what she's talking about but she can't explain it. She usually speaks in English. She tells boring stories that have little to do with what we're learning. It's definetly an easy A.  Midterm and final are open book and on blackboard.  But if you want to learn something, take Daryl Hague.

Although boring, a very easy class.  Many times only 2 out of the 25 students would be awake but she continues on.  She is a nice lady.  An easy A if you speak the language.  Bring something to do during class to pass the time.

This class is painful.  It is an easy A, but your Spanish will not improve at because of this class or this professor.  She didn't prepare for class.  We wasted the first ten minutes of each class with the bienvenido, 20-30 minutes on pointless cultural presentations.  And then she does a few minutes of boring grammar that we learned in the MTC.

Boring, with a narrow view of Spanish language.  She is nice, but class is a total waste of time.  The book is terrible.  Class is very easy, but you won't learn much.  Take her if you want an easy A.

Mella goes off on tangents but she knows her grammar better than anyone at the university.  If you can be patient through her anecdotes, you will learn a lot.  She is very helpful and wants her students to learn. During my Praxis exam, many of her sideline stories actally helped me get the right answers.  Easy A class!

HORRIBLE!  I stopped going to class.  It was better to take an E and repeat with a better teacher than sitting through the class.  You will start poking your eyes out if you sit through this class.  Drop Now.

The class really is a joke, very easy, no work, but you don't learn anything new.  Mella knows her grammer probably better than most if not all the other professors, but spends most the time telling stories in English.
Easy class for RM's.  Didn't have to do much.  Easy professor for this class.
She talks in english.  Nuff said

Easy A class, really nice woman. I learned a lot from the book, but nothing from class. As much as I love Mella as a person, I recommend someone like Labrum or Chaparro if you're more interested in learning the material.

One of the worst classes ever! Drop this class. It isn't even worth sitting through just for the A.  You won't learn a thing and you will be kicking yourself for taking it.  Leave now while you still have a chance!

This class is a joke! Mella is totally disorganized and you don't learn a thing. She basically reads to you from the textbook. She certainly does know her grammar, but that just means she is very unforgiving if you make a mistake. Run from this class!
