Brother Sweat is an awesome lecturer, he tries to help you on the tests by showing what the learning points are of his lecture so you can decipher what to study. Hard part is he doesn't always make clear the answers to his learning points. His lectures are involving but often runs out of time leaving you to fill in the cracks. Still very insightfu

I LOVED this class with Brother Sweat! His lectures are entertaining and I learned something interesting in each class period. The assignments are sometimes long, but I learned a lot about Church history and really enjoyed the reading. I would recommend taking this class from Brother Sweat!

BEST RELIGION TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD. Brother Sweat is so loving and sweet and funny! He loves the gospel and he loves his students. Not only did I learn a lot about the Restoration of the gospel, my testimony was strengthened a ton.  He is just solid. So kind and so funny. Tests are easy if you study. Just the best. Please take this class.

I took D&C First Half from Bro. Sweat with some friends last semester and we HAD to take second half from him! Class consists of short reading insight papers that are due before each class, but they are quick and easy. One (easy) 3-page paper, and two exams with an in-class review of everything needed before you take it. MUST TAKE FROM HIM!!

Professor Sweat is fantastic! He's seriously been the greatest! He knows a TON about church history, and he isn't afraid to answer the hard questions about church history. He doesn't shy away from it, he's honest and straight forward. He really loves the gospel, and it shows in his teaching. Take it from Sweat!
Do the work and you will do great! He tells you everything that will be on the test! He is great!

Honestly my favorite professor that I have had at BYU. Tests are easy and extremely fair. I learned a lot from him, and loved the way he explained the D&C. There are assignments due every class period, but it is way easy. Take the class, you will not regret it!

Here's the thing about religion professors at BYU: some are more like seminary easy-going, spiritual teachers and others want you to memorize every general authority quote and church history date in the book.  Brother Sweat falls in the first category - which is the kind I like.  He will teach you, and bonus - don't have to memorize any dates!!!

Great religion teacher. It's not ridiculously difficult. The point is really to help you become a more Christ like individual. Do the insight submissions, and do put some time into your papers and you'll do great! So spiritually uplifting. And he's funny too.

Top-notch professor.  Great at teaching, funny lectures, and overall fun class.  Loads of work for a religion class, but its worth it.  The tests are easy, so this really is one of those classes that your grade is based on the time you put into it.

Great at lectures. Very good at translating dialogue and emotions into something more relatable to students. Makes sense of difficult doctrine, gave me new perspectives on certain things, and makes sure you know when he's sharing his own thoughts vs doctrine. Also ready to admit he doesn't know something. Reading & response due before each class.

Dr. Sweat changed my life. I'm leaving on a mission soon. He attends global religious conferences and demonstrates fantastic, well-rounded (as in from the perspective of other religions too) understanding of the Godhead and our own religion. And history (need a teacher like this for the D&C! He doesn't skirt around anything, yet very tactful). YES.

Sweat definitely knows his stuff and gives a lot of good context to the D&C. He encouraged questions and talked thoroughly about difficult issues in a way that was honest, insightful and clear. This class is more time consuming than many religion classes though. Written assignments due before every class and four papers. Only 2 easy tests though.

Great man. Knows the Gospel, knows how to teach, and loves it. Good at answering even obscure questions, although he could cite his sources more--but overall he's brilliant. Just don't be an idiot like most college students and expect an A from zero effort.

Great man, and I feel like he is super spiritual, knows a lot, but will quickly admit if he doesn't know something rather than theorize or give his own opinion.  Tests were very fair and I loved the class.
Brother Sweat is my favorite teacher I have ever had at BYU. This is the perfect balance for a religion class. The assignments and reading are easy and so worth your time. Very spiritual too.

He taught a lot of worthwhile things in this class and you can learn quite a lot. He has a few written assignments that you will have to invest some time into. He sometimes said things where I wish he had cited a source.

Brother Sweat is one of the best professors that I have ever had. He cares about his students learning important things and he always explains himself clearly. He's very mindful of his students' needs and does his best to cater to them. Great professor and person.

He tells you everything you need to study for on the Midterm and Final. Very Organized class and assignments due dates are clearly marked on the syllabus.Do all the assignments and study exactly what he tells you on the tests and you'll get an A ! Funny professor and great spirit.
My favorite religion teacher thus far.  Funny guy.  Tests aren't very hard but there is some busywork.
Great professor! Very insightful, very knowledgeable, humorous, chill, and keeps the class entertaining. Definitely recommend.

Bro. Sweat is awesome! I have taken all of my religion credits already and Bro. Sweat is by far my favorite of all the religion professors I've had. I've learned so much from him about the D & C. There are a few big assignments but as long as you do them correctly, you'll get an A. He tells you exactly what to study for tests. Awesome guy!

love LOVE him and his teachings!!! Tons of knowledge, great spirit! There's quite a load of homework but you learn so much. Doesn't accept late homework. Attend the lectures, you'll be spiritually uplifted and you'll do well on the tests too. He made the D&C so interesting and so precious! I was always looking forward to the next lecture.

awesome guy. good lectures although he lets the crazy students distract him and he goes off on tangents. easy tests - he tells you exactly what will be on the test in the review. there is a ton of busy work. a reading journal for every class and 2-3 essay every month plus miscellaneous work. but all those points help you get an easy A
Good teacher, but lots of unnecessary busy work for a religion class.  2 papers throughout the semester which are annoying.
Brother Sweat is the bomb.
Best religious class I've taken at BYU. He's so insightful and I went to every class because it was so good. There are 2 assignments every week but they are really easy. A few papers also.

I've had some amazing religion professors at BYU, but Brother Sweat has topped my list by far. His stories about church history blow me away. I've never learned so much in one religion class. His sense of humor makes the lecture hall seem to actually rumble from laughter. I'm signing up for the second half from him without a doubt.
This is exactly what a BYU religion class should be like…easy, but inspiring and uplifting.  He is hilarious and his classes were like a punch in the face with the Spirit.  Awesome!

Professor Sweat is a young, intelligent, energetic, professor. He has incredible knowledge of the gospel and a strong testimony. Lectures were great, homework was reasonable, and tests were fairly easy if you studied. I recommend him to everyone who needs to take a DC class.

Phenomenal teacher and person. Loved every minute of this class. So smart, genuine and engaging. Taught me to love D&C, and helped me develop skills to get more out of the scriptures in the future. This class can bless and change your life.
Sweat is the clearest religion professor at BYU. Super easy! I registered for his second half of D&C, that's how much I enjoyed his class. He sets you up to get 100% on everything, just go to class.

Professor Sweat is hands down the best professor I have ever had. This class was life-changing for me. I learned a tremendous amount spiritually and temporally. He challenges you to know specifics on the test but you feel the spirit and learn so much in his class. He is hilarious, caring, and very intelligent. Take his class!

Brother Sweat is a great person. He cares about the student's growth, while helping him/her to obtain the necessary knowledge and apply it to their life. Class is fun, and I learned a ton of new things, even though I thought that I was already familiar with the content. Brother Sweat is a must-have professor.

Bro. Sweat is hilarious, but in the right way for a religion professor. This class emphasizes finding applicable principles in the Doctrine & Covenants rather than just knowing facts, and it's been great. This is what religion classes SHOULD be like. You get graded for your applications, not memorizations. Definitely recommend.
Brother Sweat is the best religion professor I have ever come across. He actually cares about his students testimonies. He only makes you learn useful stuff for the tests.

Brother Sweat cares a lot about the success of the students in becoming closer to the Lord. I really don't like having to take  BYU religion classes, but this class is great.  Instead of being useless like in a lot of BYU religion classes are very good to make you critically think about your testimony, and help you relate principles to your life.

AMAZING teacher!!!! I never take the time to write ratings for a teacher on here...but I need all to know what a wonderful teacher he is. He truly cares about his students and the spirit is strong in his class. He's super personable and will help you in any way he can.He reviews test questions prior to tests.Pay attention and you'll easily get an A

Brother Sweat's an AMAZING teacher that I will definitely take more classes from in the future. He made his 5-7 TH D&C class not only bearable, but enjoyable with his amazing sense of humor, testimony and knowledge of the gospel. There was no question that I'd feel the spirit in his class and that he really cares about his students.

Bro. sweat is very uplifting, entertaining, thoughtful and brings me to repentence or tears each week (in a good way, of course). The class is structured well and not with an overwhelming workload -- weekly readings, journal entries, 2 mid terms, 1 final, 1 research paper, 3 few "go and do" activities, and a class participation grade. Love him!:)

Professor Bowden means it when he says he cares about you passing. He has a powerful testimony and will remind you of your worth. And for the record, most of the low rating on here are because they were freshmen and EVERYTHING was hard. I took this class as a late sophomore and loved it. Just LIVE in the TA lab. Do ALL of the listed practice exams.
Awesome guy

The Mechanical Engineering Seminar class is unnecessary. I would suggest just going to the first couple classes unenrolled, this is where they explain the graduation plan and how to apply for the major, but after that its just fluff. Bowden is a nice guy, the class just doesn't do much.
The MeEn Seminar is a pretty easy class, gets a little boring toward the end. Definitely go do the tours for the Project and Prototyping Labs. Take advantage of the outside of class credit options.

Dr. Bowden carried me to an A. You have to spend several hours on homework each week, but that is the only way you're going to learn the material, by practicing problems. I got a D on 1 of the 2 midterms and still finished with an A. As long as you are committed to work hard, you can get the grade you want.

ME101 is not a good indicator of how good of a professor someone is, however, I did really enjoy the class. It is pass fail and teaches you a lot about the ME program. I really enjoyed Professor Bowden however, not much engineering was actually taught.

ME 101 is hard, there's no way to get around it. Despite this, I liked Bowden's very organized plan. He responds to all the students' questions and works with us to get us to understand the material. He is strict with deadlines, but he's also very clear about those deadlines. around 4 hours outside of class per week for me, sometimes more in ME 101
Took Professor Bowden for Material science. He gave good lectures and cares about the students.

Just as a background I got an A in the class. He is the worst professor on campus I have had so far. He doesnt give you all the info you need to do assignments and expects students to perform at a masters level. Do not take classes from him if you dont have to.

He shared teaching this class with 2 other teachers. His test questions were among the hardest and most intense. He didn't give as many lectures, his slides did not help with studying, but his content/lecturing was interesting. He was always available to help.

The class was easy. The content is simple. I love biomedical engineering, but what you learn here isnt practical or useful unless you want to do research only. He acts very nice, tells you things will not be hard, and then you feel like you aced the test and semester project only to find no one in the class received an A. Not one student.

This leadership class is a stroke different from his other classes, but he teaches it very well. The class consists of tons of group work, but as long as you communicate with your classmates, it's reasonable. Professor Bowden cares deeply about this class and is willing to help outside of class as well.

Bowden makes this class unnecessarily difficult, the tests are way harder than they need to be and he didn't curve any of them. The lectors are engaging, but it doesn't make up for the daily frustration I had with the class. If there's an option to take this class from a different professor your grade will thank you.

He takes a lot of pride on being a harsh grader. For a group project my group followed the rubric but we were still given the lowest grade with no feedback. I don't recommend Dr. Bowden since he basically expects you to read his mind to perform well. If you are unsure about biomechanics I'd recommend auditing the class instead.

His lecture for this class was amazing the first two weeks. But it was just down hill from there. The class itself was useless to an engineering career and Dr. Bowden is an extremely hard grader. He will find something to set the average for his class at B. The content was interesting but not useful at all.

Dr. Bowden is a nice person, but that's about all the good things I'd have to say. Assignment outlines are unclear and only give the standard for a "B" and he refuses to further elaborate. Tests are ridiculously difficult and include questions on topics not covered in class. He feels extremely prideful in his grading and refusal of flexibility.

His lectures are awesome, but that's about all I liked about his class. He told us at the beginning of the semester that his wouldn't be the class that we would be stressed about this semester. That was a huge lie. He doesn't give a rubric for the larger assignments, and basically expects you to read his mind. Take a different professor.

Anton Bowden is someone that's very sure of himself. He is not very open to feedback, especially on his heavily subjective tests. You will not find the answers to problems in his slides. You need to have a good vision of how his mind works to do well on tests. Students spent hours out of class working on pointless labs. Organization was terrible.

You can tell that he cares about his students and how they're doing in the class, but he is very confident in his teaching and testing abilities (so he's not really open to criticism). For the final exam, the class average was literally 69.5%. I would not recommend taking this class, especially if you are not a mechanical engineering major.

I learned a lot in this class, and you can tell Dr. Bowden really knows what he is talking about, but he didn't work super hard to actually help us do well, and the tests were really difficult. There were times when I was convinced he wanted us to fail the class. If you take Leadership in a Global Context, don't take from him.

Professor Bowden is amazing! His class is admittedly difficult (but no matter who you take this class from it will be so) but he is probably the most caring professor I have ever had. He sincerely wants his students to succeed and diligently works for them. Attend lectures and stay on top of your assignments and you'll do great!

This class will consume your life. Professor Bowden knows his stuff, but this semester was probably just tougher overall not being able to meet up with TAs and classmates in person. Homework took me soooo much time to do, but tests are typically easier than the HW. Dont expect to get homework corrections for about a month after you turn them in.

Bowden is a solid choice for an ME EN 101 teacher. You can tell he cares a lot about his students. For me, the tests were pretty manageable. They were way simpler than the homework. Just make sure you have a really good conceptual understanding going into them. Make use of the TA lab when you don't understand something.
He is an awesome teacher, really cares about his students. His tests are tricky. The class isn't too bad.

Dr. Bowden is a great guy. I enjoyed his lectures and learned much about leadership from him. However, he is unclear at times with his instructions. The tests are very hard and he expects you to go above and beyond to get an A. It is hard to get an A in his class but probably won't fail. An A requires 95%. Highest grade in class was 96. Average 86.
Tons of homework, helps if you can talk to him outside of class

I loved the lectures and labs! Dr. Bowden is a very nice guy. I feel like I learned a ton about leadership; however, I felt like the class was filled with busywork. There are a lot of assignments to do outside of class, including meeting with an assigned group weekly. Oh, and you need a 95 to get an A. Don't take this class from him.
He works problems pin the board all period, and the board can get hard to see. He knows what he is doing as he teaches, but seemed to go through the lecture rather quickly.

This class is the second time the department has taught the class, so the structure was awful. The Prof. Bowden is nice and lively, but he doesn't necessarily teach the material, but rather starts doing problems on the board. If you already know Statics, this class will be an easy review, if you don't, you will live in the TA lab to get a grade.

Dr. Bowden is very personable and a really great guy. I had the opportunity to do a Study Abroad with him and I loved to see how he lived outside of being a professor. Talking to him was always uplifting and helpful for the class and for my life. I highly Recommend him!

Dr. Bowden was awesome! He always responded to emails within the hour, and was very forgiving and easygoing. The papers and tests aren't graded too strict and it is fairly easy to get a good grade. The study guides for the tests were also very helpful. He made lectures interesting and I learned a ton from the class
Dr. Bowden is a good teacher. He explains what you need to know and tests are reasonable. He is passionate about the subject matter.

Great teacher.  Very friendly and helpful when you go talk to him.  Not an easy grader, makes you work for your grade, but definitely worth it.  You will learn the material if you work.  Recommend him

I didn't like this class. Dr. Bowden is an interesting fellow. He can be nice at times but on the other hand he can be purposefully vague and ambiguous which I didn't like at all. Also, he didn't live up to his word on grading things in time.

I took ME250 and ENGT231 from him. He is a great teacher who obviously cares a great deal about his students and his subject matter. His classes aren't easy, but you will definitely learn the material if you do your assignments. The time commitment for his classes are just average for a college class.
In taking ME 250 from Dr. Bowden, I felt that he really cared that the student learn the subject matter.  His class isn't an "easy A", but is very informative.  I enjoyed him as a professor.

Dr. Bowden is still one of my favorite professors.  I was checking on other profs and when I saw his rating I had to see why and add my two cents.  He is an awesome professor.  I really didn't care for the subject much, but the class was interesting and informative.  I wouldn't take it from any other professor.
Good professor, tests are pretty easy if you study. He sometimes refers to himself in the third person which is pretty weird.  You have to write a ten page report which sucks but it isn't too bad.

Worst professor I have ever had for any class. Ever. Lectures, homework, and tests are on separate, unrelated material. Homework is not only long, but doesn't help at all with tests. I got a great score on all test preparation "games" only to find out they have nothing to do with test material. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM.

I didn't interact with professor Dean much, but whenever I did she was helpful and kind. Your grade in this class mainly relies on your exam grades and there is no extra credit, so be aware of that. Memorize food sources for the vitamins/minerals there are so many questions on this and it's very specific!!!!!!!!!

The homework and everything was easy, but it didn't translate whatsoever to the tests. I spent so much time reading and studying compared to all my other classes like marketing and information systems. Still got the worst grade I will ever get. Get ready to memorize the textbook and then get tested on something completely different.

Her study guides do not cover everything that will be on the test. This is because her tests are super specific and questions could be on literally any sentence from the textbook rather than testing main ideas. I would recommend not taking this class from this professor.

Don't take this class it's not enjoyable and it's just a lot of busy work for a hard class. Sends out study guides with the words "(May not cover everything you need to know)" which is very unhelpful and stupid.  I study for these tests for hours and still don't know what it will be on it, because it is the most random things as others have said.

Didn't enjoy this class. The worst thing about it is the tests. You get tested on the most random things. I study everything for hours and still don't know what's on the test. Would not recommend taking this, the tests are awful.

Her difficulty is definitely higher than 3. There is no extra credit at all. So you need to literally do great on everything. Tests were hard. Make sure you know everything from the lecture vids and the textbook. Like even the small details. I took this course during the summer and it definitely took a lot of my summer time to get an A in this clas

The most unorganized class I have ever taken at BYU. She did not give a single lecture the entire class so I had so read the textbook and try to remember every sentence because you have no idea what will be tested.

Took this class online and it was phenomenal. Great lay out, information was easy to understand, not too much work required. I really didn't try very hard, studied for each test for maybe 2 hours in advance, got an average of 85-90%. Obviously it helps if you're interested in the material. Seriously a very easy online class that's actually useful.

This was a faily easy class, and it is one I think everyone should take. I learned the basics of nutrition and now feel more educated in making future health decisions. Prof Dean is very sweet and knowledgable about nutrition. The class is pretty easy, but can sometimes be a lot of work (mainly reading and quizzes).

Besides consistently messing up important facts Dean is alright. Students needed to correct her on the information frequently. Does use iClicker, doesn't do attendance though. The exams are long and heavy. Exam reviews are done in class with the help of TAs. Study guides are provided and are relatively helpful.
Professor dean is really nice but this class was super boring. It also wasn't made clear that attendance was mandatory at the beginning of the semester. There is a lot of homework.

Doctor Dean is such a sweet lil peach. Her class was pretty easy, especially if you have basic knowledge of nutrition. A lot of people don't show up to class but she rewards her students that do show up to class with boosted grades and prizes. She curved everyone's grade in my class that showed up the day before thanksgiving break. Take April Dean!

I mean the class was interesting, but the teaching could have been better. Professor Dean is nice but she is very vague when teaching. Kind of gives a general overview but the tests are very specific. I ended up teaching myself a lot of the material.

Professor Dean really was not a good teacher. The lectures were so boring and it was hard to be engaged. I feel like she didn't know half of the information she was teaching. I would not recommend taking a class from her. It was awful.

Ok she did not make any insensitive comments. Many are mad bc the class wasn't an easy A. All tests are made by the department and not the teacher. You have 3 projects which are easy and a quiz every week that you can find on quizlet. Make sure to fill out the study guides and memorize those. Has review q's after lecture that are sometimes on test.
I love this class. Ignore every bad thing said about her; she is a fantastic teacher. went to class every class period and loved the lectures.

Prof Dean is like an old relief society president who went online and got a fake degree. She forgets everything, has to ask her class for answers, and teaches you something wrong at least once a lecture. During the anorexia and other eating disorders lecture, she made lots of insensitive comments and jokes. Also makes the TA answer all questions.

The only thing I didn't like about this class was the amount of reading. I'm a slow reader and I take notes while reading so on the weeks where she assigns more than one chapter, it was miserable. Reading takes me 2-3 hours and then she assigns a quiz online each week. I would much rather take this class than biology for the biological science GE.

The actual lecture is hard to pay attention in and they are kinda all over the place. Some things on the reviews aren't even talked about in class. The tests are pretty hard, a lot of the concepts talked about in the lecture aren't even on the test. Tests are worth a lot, but are kinda hard to pass.
Lots of memorization. Hard to pay attention. Boring lectures

Prof. Dean taught a lot of applicable material that I have applied in my life. She is so smart and so funny. Her stories are awesome. Easiest class I've taken. I think the reason others say the lecture was boring is because it's an hour and 15 mins at the end of the day, but there was a lot of interesting material. I would take her again!

The class was easy. Her lectures were boring to be blunt. Attendance isn't necessary but at the end of each class she goes over questions that can sometime be on the test. She posts slides but they missing things that were in class. Towards the end of class I stopped going and just read the textbook and I was fine.

In NDFS 100 from professor Dean I was shocked by her lack of perfessionalism. She was consistently stumbling on her words or correcting herself which portrayed to the students that she was not confident in the subjects taught in this course. To add to her lack of professionalism I never once received a response to the multiple emails I sent.

Prof. Dean is awesome! She is so caring and extremely intelligent. She has a lot of out of the classroom experience which makes her lectures more interesting. It is easy to tell that she cares about the success of her students. This is a very easy class. If you show up and take notes, then the tests are a breeze. Easy quizzes. Take prof. Dean!

Professor Dean is a very intelligent teacher! Occasionally she assumes the class is educated on certain aspects of nutrition that haven't been discussed but is more than willing to clarify and answer questions! There is a quiz every week that is open book and every few weeks there is an easy assignment. Tests aren't too difficult if you study!

Professor Dean is the sweetest lady, but not a very good professor. I just read the textbook and only went to class during review days because the lectures were not helpful. There are a couple assignments that are very specific with what you need to do, but they are easy. Don't take this class if you are a nutrition major.
She's a really sweet and nice lady, but her teaching could've used a little more enthusiasm and interest.

Not a great professor.  She is a nice lady, but doesn't know how to teach or control a classroom.  She would start the lecture and no one would even know because we were all already talking and tuning her out.  I stopped going to class because I could get more done on my own during that time.  Just go to the in class reviews which are graded.

I was not a huge fan of Professor Dean. She's very sweet, but she doesn't know how to control a classroom. And I was constantly bored. all. class. That being said, I made some good friends because we were all bored together. I know some people who really liked this professor, so that's something, but I probably wouldn't take another class from her.

Very nice but scattered in her teaching style. Mumbled and took a long time to say not very much. I stopped going to class because I could cover the same amount of material in the book in 20 minutes instead of 1 1/2 hrs in class. I just went to in class reviews, which are graded, and studied on my own.

Taking this class I was basically teaching myself. Prof Dean did not explain concepts clearly and the tests were rough. The tests require a LOT of memorization. If you sit any farther back than the 3rd row you will barely be able to hear the teacher. I took this class as a G.E. and MAN I wish I had taken biology. This class is definitely a science.

Her class is pretty easy if you show up, listen and fill out the study guides as you go.  She's really nice and cares about her students.  Really sweet lady, she's fun to listen to and get to know.  Can be a little boring if you take her later in the day, but overall I really like her.

Dr. Dean is my favorite professor so far at BYU.  She was very helpful and incredibly clear in explain difficult concepts.  She makes the material relevant to real life.  This class has so much valuable information and it feels important to know.  If you're thinking about taking NDFS 100, take it from her!  Not too difficult.
two credits hours for three hours workload. she is reading ppt slide only and you have to in class because TA will give you stupid questions to put on quizzes. sucks.

Dr. Dean is fantastic.  She's one of the few professors I have had at BYU that learned my name.  Her grading is fair and her tests are not too bad.  She prepares you well for assignments.  I loved taking this class from her and would completely recommend her to anyone.

She is a great teacher. Class was once a week for two hours, it was a little boring but not bad. Assignments and quizzes aren't too hard, but the tests were a lot harder than I expected. Study hard for the test and you should get a good grade!

Dr. Dean was pretty rad. I enjoyed this class, and it was a once a week night class. She kept us interested, and she's really nice. 3 exams, 3 assignments, 13 quizzes (3 dropped), and thats it. Not too difficult, but you still had to put in some work. I would reccomend Dean to anyone, I think she's a great professor.
GREAT teacher. GREAT class. Not too easy and not too hard. Lots of good information. Highly recommended!

I took NDFS 100 (basic nutrition)as well as 310 Sports nutrition from her. I Have learned a lot from her classes that I have applied to everyday life! She gives you outlines that clearly show what will be on the test.  Take these classes from her! If you need sports nutrition 310 I especially recommend April Dean.

Nutrition for 3 hours on a Thursday night is brutal no matter who you take it from, but I congratulate her for keeping us awake and interested that long every week. The class is tough (don't take it if you want an easy A), but you learn a ton of applicable information that will be useful in the future.

Best NDFS 100 teacher at BYU.  The NDFS dept is anal about reviews, etc., but Dr. Dean always gave us extra review for the tests and always hooked us up.  I would definitely recommend taking her night class.
Ari is a really great professor. He does his best to relate to the students and wants to help them succeed. This was his first time teaching the class, but he did well. Funny and friendly.

Professor Coleman is really engaging and willing to help students with concepts and assignments. He sometimes gets off track during lectures but he is super responsive to questions and teaches you what you need to know.

Professor Coleman is very knowledgeable in the field of Philosophy and I think often forgets that we are not. I didn't find the ideas relatable or interesting and there are only lectures so it is hard to stay engaged. You're supposed to be confused by the readings, which I didn't like. This class wasn't interesting and felt hard for no reason.
Enjoys what he does

I was very intimidated by this class, but it's manageable. Aside from a 500-word weekly paper, open note quizzes, and a 2,000-word final paper, keeping up with the material is enough to get an A. Coleman is respected, kind, and funny, and I loved how he consistently tied everything back to the gospel. I highly recommend taking philosophy with him
Super easy class, and good readings. 10/10 would recommend. It will definitely make you smarter.

While I really enjoy talking to him outside of class, and I think that he is a really smart guy, he makes things overly confusing. I feel like in class he should be clarifying what we read the night before, but instead he is obfuscating it further. If you want to be very confused by philosophy, take this class. Consider other PHIL 110 teachers.

He is a really great professor and is very insightful. You have to go to the class. Make sure you pick a topic you care about for your final paper. He drops the lowest 5 quizzes/absences which made my grade go up a whole letter. Overall take from him.
Professor Coleman is a very fun guy. You will most likely get an A if you show up to class and turn in everything on time. He drops the lowest three quiz grades, which is a lifesaver!

This dude is an absolute genius and phenomenal professor! The topic of philosophy already opens the mind and invites people to think more deeply but Professor Coleman invites you to think even deeper. I loved his ideas and questions and his lectures were the perfect balance of lecture and conversation. Plus he's hilarious

Professor Coleman is the best teacher I have had this semester. His biggest goal in teaching is to get to know what you have learned and how, with his help, you can expand on that knowledge. He will help you out anytime you need something, and he is super easy to have a conversation with. I 100% recommend taking this class.
one of the most interesting and applicable classes I have ever taken

Professor Coleman is the best!! If you're taking PHIL 110, take it from him. Every week there's a reading and an essay. He grades the essays based off of improvement, not skill. He takes attendance via 10 easy pop quizzes. He drops the 3 lowest quizzes. Classes are discussion based, not lectures. Super interesting class and a very easy A!!!

Professor Coleman is amazing! He is great at explaining difficult concepts and has a discussion based teaching model. Writing assignments are graded on how your writing has improved over the length of the course. Naturally, this course had a lot of reading. There are a handful of pop quizzes that are used to measure attendance and can't be made up.
Lectures were kind of confusing and didn't go along with the tests we had. Teacher was funny, but sometimes kind of rude. Teacher and TA didn't respond to emails very promptly.

Professor Cuadra has probably been my favorite religion teacher since I have been at BYU. He is very caring and understanding and he is a really cool and loving teacher. He desires to help you understand the doctrine and that is something that I valued alot in his class.

Professor Cuadra is absolutely amazing, and I can't recommend him enough. His lectures are PHENOMENAL, and I left them with a newfound love and understanding of the Book of Mormon. Keep up with journals and take notes/pay attention in lectures, and you will be set. I wish he taught other courses, because he is one of the best professors I've had!

He is the best religion professor at BYU. The way that he teaches is so inspired and he is willing to change his lesson plans to fit the needs of the students. He offers extra credit on the exams which is always helpful. He does a project at the end of the semester instead of a final exam. I would take this class 100 times if I could.

I am so grateful to take my last religion class with Dr. Caudra. His class was inspiring and one of the most Christ-centered experiences of my life. He is passionate and willing to step away from his lesson plan to personalize his teaching to the needs of his students. Class always went by so quickly, and I grew to love the Book of Mormon SO MUCH!

He taught me Jesus. He asks that question in class often and it really changes the way you look at the scriptures. He is passionate and a great professor. He provided important hints in class in preparation for the exams. Super kind. I only wish he would teach other courses.

I have never felt more uplifted in a religion class at BYU. The grading expectations were clear, and there were opportunities for extra credit. He was approachable and kind. I laughed and cried in class—it was a great balance of spirituality and academics. I would gladly take more classes from him in the future.

I have never felt more uplifted in a religion class at BYU. The grading expectations were clear, and there were opportunities for extra credit. He was approachable and kind. I laughed and cried in class—it was a great balance of spirituality and academics. I would gladly take more classes from him in the future. 10/10

Not very personable, I didn´t feel like a priority to him. I came to him with spiritual questions that were important to me (I expressed their importance clearly), but he was watching a video while we were talking. He was funny and engaging in class. The lectures were great and uplifting, but my experiences with him outside class got in the way.
Ariel -the goat- Cuadra.  That basically sums it up. He's hilarious and genuinely cares about his students. He does have some difficult assignments but they are worth it.

Professor Cuadra is a fantastic teacher and a great man. He really cares about each of his students and pushes hard for us to succeed. The coursework was mostly weekly readings/write-ups. the lectures were really fun. notes are a must. If there's any hesitation on whether to take this class or not, TAKE IT and you won't be sorry

He strikes a great balance between intellectual and testimony-building conversations about the Book of Mormon. I love how he shares experience as a global church member. I was always reminded that the Book of Mormon is for everyone around the world, not just people in the US. No final exam is awesome too.

I LOVE Brother Cuadra. He genuinely loves his students and literally stopped his lecture last class to ask if we were doing ok because we were all so tired with finals. He is funny, has amazing gospel insights, and is Chilean so he brings a lot of unique global and language perspectives. Read the syllabus! and learn to find Jesus :)

I absolutely loved this professor. If you want to come to know Jesus better, take his class. He is incredibly caring and thoughtful in every lesson, knows each student by name, and always takes time to answer questions. I have never had a more genuine, Christlike teacher. He truly teaches in the Savior's way.

Bro Cuadra is the absolute best. When he teaches he is so engaging and he is so funny. But he's really good at taking thing seriously too. I feel the Spirit so much in his class. I would encourage anyone to take his class. This is the second one I have had with him.
Great professor, for some reason I can't submit my review
10/10 would take again, he cares and really gives it his all in his lectures.
This professor was one of my favorites. He cares so deeply for his students and I left the class feeling renewed and humbled. It was a great experience for me.
Christ-like

Hno Cuadra is one of the best religion professors I ever had! I looked forward to his class every day and always left with my mind blown. He teaches the BOM and church doctrine so well and his lectures were a great mixture of hilarious and spiritually uplifting. Attendance is mandatory but it's so worth it.

I learned a lot about Christ from the Book of Mormon in this class. My faith grew, and I had fun while learning. The tests were fair, and the workload isn't heavy, but attendance is important. It's a great class if you want a good balance of spirituality and fresh insights from the scriptures.

Bro. Cuadra is by far my favorite professor! He is hilarious, he genuinely cares for & gets to know his students, and his testimony & knowledge of the gospel is incredible. He made me see things in a new way every single class & I always got so much out of it. He wants you to succeed - exams and projects were very fair. 10000/10! I love his class!!

Brother Cuadra is an excellent professor! Every class There's new perspectives and insights every class. The tests are very fair, and if you're in class and take good notes they are easy to pass. I'd give this class 10/10!

He really gets to know his students and genuinely loves them. It is important you are in class because his tests are very based on what he said in class, take good notes. However, his lectures were extremely insightful and inspirational and to add to it he is hilarious, you won't want to miss. He is my favorite professor on campus easily.

Bro Cuadra was one of the best professors you can have for this class. His lectures are amazing and he's super funny. Just know that attendance is mandatory.

TAKE HIS CLASS TRUST! It is not too heavy and you learn a lot! Attendance is important but Bro. Cuadra makes it worth it! He was a bit intimidating at first, but is actually the kindest, most caring professor!
Brother Cuadra taught me how to connect with Christ on a more meaningful and personal level. While it isn't a heavy homework course, consistency in completing assignments is important.

Brother Cuadra was an amazing professor!He's a very hilarious person and likes to crack jokes a lot. I do admit, his lectures are sometimes very fast and can be a little confusing when you're taking notes. If you keep up on your journal you'll be fine. You can turn in make up work till the end of the semester with very low penalty. The course is very reading-heavy, and attendance for zoom calls with small groups are mandatory. She's super nice!

Before this last week, I would have rated her higher, but Dr. Tice and I had multiple discussions after she changed the syllabus and now she is making our class take a final without any study guide/resources after we were told to expect an open-book test. With the changes, I won't get a good grade on the final and I won't get into law school.

Nice lady, but similar to the other comments on here her quizzes/tests are super ambiguous. She'll list 4 correct answers and it becomes a game of guessing her mind rather than something we have learned. It feels like we are being tricked. Again, this might not be her fault and is a department issue but the class was much harder than anticipated.

The class is straightforward and has lots of potential, but Professor Tice's grading is extremely difficult. Her weekly quizzes are VERY hard/ambiguous. Our entire discussion group has agreed that she writes her questions to trick students. When you talk to the TAs they refuse to help. If you care about your grade avoid it. Please fix the quizzes!

Dr. Tice is a great professor. Her lectures were awesome. Lectures were all online but it was necessary to watch them as each class period was an online group discussion about the lecture. Grade is based heavily on attendance, but I thoroughly enjoyed watching and attending this class.

Dr Tice is one of the most genuine professors I've ever had! She constantly seeks feedback on how to improve the class and is very willing to help students who are struggling or falling behind. The zoom setup was great and the quizzes and tests aren't too bad as long as you do the reading.

Professor Tice is fantastic. She's willing to work with students, expects a lot of us but formats class in a manner that provides ease of passing and excellence if you try. Group exams, open textbook exams, information relevant to life.

Dr. Tice is a wonderful teacher who really cares for her students. She teaches in a very straightforward way and her tests are easy, but you still learn a lot. Group projects were fun; hopefully, you get a good group.

I loved this class! It was a very easy A. The class is focused on helping you learn the information through discussion instead of tricky exams and heavy homework. I learned a lot from this class, so I appreciate it a lot. Do note that there is a lot of reading, but if you spread it out over the week, it's doable. I highly recommend Dr. Tice!!!!

This class was almost entirely participation (points for commenting, group tests, etc), but the weekly quizzes were impossible. We had to read the chapter and take a closed book test that was ridiculously difficult every week. Overall these quizzes were maybe 20% of your grade and all multiple choice, so easy pass, but not necessarily an easy A

Dr. Tice wants all of her students to get an A. She is amazing and super caring. There is a lot of reading and the reading quizzes are tough, but a super small part of your grade. Tests were taken as small groups with optional TA help. Lecture was super cool as well and done on your own time.
She's a great professor, makes the material easy to understand.
Dr. Tice puts a focus on the learning, rather than just memorizing material which I really respect. She cares about her students a lot, and designs the class in a way for you to succeed.

This class was great! There was a fair amount of reading each week, and a quiz on the reading, but you were able to use notes on the quizzes and the quizzes weren't worth very many points anyways. The tests were open note, book, group and TA. She recorded her lectures and we just had to watch them and meet with our groups twice a week to discuss

Because of covid I took the class online. She would pre-record lectures and then there were discussion groups. Dr. Tice is great, but the TA does a lot of the grading and leads the discussion groups and so there is little interaction with the professor.

I loved Dr. Tice's class and I was surprised to hear that some people had a hard time with her. I really enjoyed her class and I always found her to be a really sweet professor! The class is pretty lecture heavy but she says herself that she wants all her students to get A's. The tests are open book and the TA's help a lot. Take the class!

I don't know why some people say she is rude because Dr. Tice was one of the sweetest profs I have ever had! She really wants all of her students to succeed and was always willing to answer questions. Tests can be a little tricky, but they are open book/notes and you can ask your TA 5 questions. Overall, the class was a true gem.

I would take the class again for the material, not, however, for the teacher. Dr. Tice has been rather blunt and offensive via email which ruined her general "niceness" during class periods for me. Even the class setup itself was not what I prefer, whether her "evidence" supports these open-book quizzes/exams or not. Take someone else!

Professor Tice fought for her students to have open-book tests to increase learning. She is a true advocate for students personally, and as a larger body. I respect her as a scientist, as well as as a person, and she brings up a lot of good points in class. She's a lovely woman.
Dianne Tice has a great lecture class, however, she is generally a rude professor. She verbally attacked me several times through emails and was just aloof as a teacher. Really disappointed.

She is kind and I enjoyed the class material. That being said, there is a LOT of reading. Although I actually enjoyed reading this textbook, it took hours for me to do so. I took really good notes but still had a hard time on reading quizzes. Open book tests but still difficult, somehow I'd only get 90% despite finding all the answers in the book.

Dr. Tice is REALLY NICE and caring and knows psychology well. But this class was super lecture heavy and I don't feel like I learned much from it long term. It is a simple class and had the potential to be really easy, but I found the quizzes to be really difficult and randomly specific. It could be an easy class for you, but it wasn't for me.

Dr. Tice is an incredible person. She genuinely cares for every student, even though its a big lecture class. The class is an easy A as well. There is a lot of reading and the quizzes are tricky, but the tests are open note.
Dr. Tice is an amazing woman but I DID NOT LEARN ANYTHING the class is ridiculously easy but also completely dreadful and boring. So if you need an easy elective take her.
Best class I have taken at BYU. Dr Tice is amazing and the class is fascinating.

Tests are SUPER EASY! Focus more on the quizzes and the readings! I highly recommend studying 2-3 quizlets online about the material, and then reading and taking the quizzes! I learned a lot from her. Shes incredibly smart, and everything she does is research-based! Also, her iclicker questions are super interesting!

Piece of cake easy A class. I'd be surprised if anyone got less than 98% on the tests. Dr. Tice is very kind and encourages her students to keep learning, but her lectures are boring, esp if you take the 1.5-hour-long class. Hardest thing is the quizzes on the readings, but they shouldn't kill your grade if you do the readings.

I enjoyed this class. I learned a lot, and it truly wasn't very difficult. Tests are open everything, and you meet with a group each week to go over the material taught in lectures. The quizzes were a bit rough/annoying at times but overall this class was pretty easy and enjoyable. Attendance is mandatory, but Professor Tice is a great professor!

This a pretty easy class. The midterms and final are all open book, open TA as long as you try to answer the questions yourself first. There are weekly quizzes that are not open book, a final paper, and digital dialogue requirements. Attendance is taken every day. Dr. Tice is such a caring, devoted teacher. Take this class, you won't regret it!

Prof. Tice is amazing! She is so thoughtful/caring., wants to help her students in any way she can, she emailed me and made sure I knew how to write the paper because I was still a Freshman and not familiar with APA format. You do have Digital Dialogues and group discussions for participation points. I learned so much in this class though, 10/10!

Professor Tice is the absolute best. She strives to have her students succeed. Every test is open book, neighbor, TA, etc. and the reasoning behind it is awesome! There are quite a few quizzes online, but theyre super easy. Lectures are very interesting too. There are too many good things to say about her, best professor Ive ever had!

Pretty solid choice. She knows her stuff and is very organized and clear. She tries really hard to make social psych an easy class and does a good job of it. Tests are open note and online, including the final. Weekly chapter quiz from the textbook. It's a lot of reading, but you get a full page of notes. One easy paper. Pretty easy.

This class was extremely easy. Theres was a weekly learning statement and reading quiz and that was it. All the midterms are open everything. The lectures are fairly interesting and she says that her goal is for you to get an A. The only downside is the 2 hours of participant studies but those are required for every psych111 class

One of my favorite professors in BYU. Everything she does is research based... tests, quizzes, assignments, you name it. She is really smart and she has an answer for everything, once again, based on research. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER. Your gpa and life will become better!!!
Dr. Tice is amazing! This class helped me so much not just to understand material but also in life. You need to take this class regardless of what you want to do. Definitely take from her!

Dr. Tice is definitely the best professor to take this class from. No essays. One closed book quiz a week. All other tests are open book/note/neighbor/TA/professor. Lectures are engaging and informative. One "learning statement" due a week which is just a paragraph about what you learned that week. EASY MONEY

Easiest class you'll ever take. All tests (midterm & final) are online and she encourages taking them with your classmates. I never bought the book and did just fine w/o it. Going to lecture is not necessary, but you'll want to because the material is really interesting and you'll just want to spend your whole day with Tice. She is an angel.
The best teacher at BYU. Open to the world and very nice. Does not judge you and gives you new perspective. I learnt a lot. I loved this class even if I think social psych is kinda common sense.

Dr. Tice is seriously the best! Easiest class ever, but you still learn a lot because she is such a great and interesting lecturer. Hardest part of the class was getting myself to show up since class isn't mandatory. All of her tests are online, open note, open TAs... easiest A but not a waste of my time either!

Dr. Tice is the best. Easiest class I've ever taken. Hardest part of the class was getting myself to show up so I didn't feel bad for missing her interesting lectures. Online, open note tests, weekly learning statements that I did during class every Friday. Easiest A and worth going to

Best teacher! She cares about the students and will take any feedback seriously. Tests and exams are open book (but not always easy) and you can ask questions with Tice and TA during their hours while the test is running. Super nice and genuinely wants you to learn, great and easy to understand during lectures! Good power points too

Professor Tice has a super easy class. Daily iclicker quizzes. Every week you have to say a couple sentences on what you learned. Tests and exams are open book and open note and they last a week. Super easy! Best professor to take PSYCH 11 from.

Dr. Tice is truly an expert when it comes to social psychology and had a lot to offer to the class. There were no quizzes or papers, just weekly learning statements and three take home, open book, open neighbor, open professor tests. Just stay on top of the reading and take good notes and you'll be fine.

Easiest class i have ever taken. Great teacher and has a great testimony. The class is very interesting but i don't go much because you do not need to. You only have to write a sentence or two a week about what you like from the class. All exams are open everything including the TAs. The answers can all be googled too. I have a 100% in the class.

Seriously, take this class. Dr. Tice is the most caring, kind professor you'll ever meet. All you have for class is a 1 paragraph paper a week about what you learned. The tests are open book/notes/friend/EVERYTHING. You don't even have to go to lecture, but you should because she is that great.

Took this course online, VERY heavy on the reading each week. The exams were super easy considering they are open-note and open-book. Weekly quizzes, but you can take those twice to get 100% on them. A few projects throughout, and the criteria are clear, and TAs are super helpful for looking things over before you submit them. Fun class to take!

AMAZING LECTURES - so inspiring, and it's obvious that she's passionate and knowledgeable about the coursework. She utilizes a variety of media types to enhance the lessons and always mentions how to apply new information to your own life. Lots of projects/papers instead of multiple choice exams- I loved it, but not everyone did. Would take again!

I took an online human development class through Sarah Coyne, but it was Professor Frasers lectures that were used in the modules. I absolutely loved her lectures! She was very open minded and insightful in human development.

I liked the course content but didn't love the way it was taught. I felt like there were too many opinions thrown out during lectures and that made it hard. However, the class is super fun and interesting and the homework is honestly pretty easy to get started and do.

This class was interesting but I honestly felt like it was a lot of busy work and I didn't learn a ton. Weekly discussions, quizzes, and video activities. There are also 6 big papers/projects throughout the semester that take some time to do. One final exam that is open note but proctored, however it literally took me 3+ hours so be prepared.

I loved this class! I learned a lot; she is such a great, knowledgeable teacher.
All of her tests are open note (they would be very difficult if not, but are pretty easy with that) and so the biggest thing (I felt) was the papers, some of which I felt were graded kind of weirdly (and occasionally incorrectly imo) but the TAs grade, and she's great.

Such an amazing teacher, the lectures were interesting and thought provoking, and even in such a big lecture hall she did a great job about letting people participate and ask questions. Lectures were useful and important for midterms, all open note tests, readings, and exams, 4 papers and help available from Ta's, great teaching and so amazing!!!

Her lectures are AMAZING and I learned a lot. One quiz from the textbook every week. 3 open note exams, not hard but also not easy. 4 papers total but 3 were due the last 2 weeks. However, you can everything done as quick you want. Finish all the quizzes and papers early. TA's can be really tough graders on papers, but just go talk to them for help

I loved having Dr. Fraser because she is so caring and knowledgeable! Sometimes the reading for this class could be intense, but the expectations were always clearly laid out every week. I learned a lot from this course, and I loved having Dr. Fraser as a professor. She also gives a lot of helpful life tips which were great.

Really nice lady, lots of busy work. Quizzes every week and a chapter of reading a week. 4 papers due throughout the semester, but they get progressively easier. Really interesting concepts taught, and she used her kids as examples for development concepts. Glad I took from her!
She is based on learning, not testing. Chapter reading due every Saturday, but all work helps in class. no busy work. content heavy, but she gives aids on testing.

If I could take all of my family life classes from her, I would. Amazing! She's kind, relatable, and has interesting lectures. There isn't too much homework. You do need the textbook because there are weekly quizzes. I took her for spring semester, and it was still good. She is also a big advocate for students and their wellbeing. Take her class!

This class was well-rounded with assignments... tests, papers, & reading quizzes quite often but all of them were doable, especially if you go to the TAs (they are the ones that grade everything. the teacher was great but I will say the lectures did get boring &  long sometimes. overall a good class &  not too difficult to get an A.

This class was super easy with projects every few weeks instead of exams and had us use Marco Polo to interact with others. Very entertaining and inspirational to learn about, even if you aren't doing anything specific with human development this class is useful

Dr. Fraser has been one of my favorite professors. Every class was so interesting and she always found a way to tie what we learned into the gospel. They're about a chapter a week of textbook reading. There were 4 papers that were not very fun, but   the Task really help with understanding the rubric and formulating your essay. Love this class!!
I couldn't recommend Dr. Fraser more. She is amazing!

Loved this class. Professor is very prepared for lectures. Final is not cumulative and can use notes and textbook on exams. Essays were the most difficult part of the class, but overall not a hard 200 level class.

Dr. Fraser is really good at getting students to think about things in different ways. The papers in this class are pretty difficult, but the rest of the work is really easy. Tests are open book & open note. I didn't pay much attention to the lectures and still did really well.

It's not what I thought this class would be. 4 Papers, 3 exams, and 16 chapter readings (about one a week). Extra credit opportunities. The papers are hard, and TA's are tough. A lot of reading. But it is a really interesting class directly connected to church doctrine. The professor is very kind and willing to work things out with students.

Take this class from her but ONLY the online one. It is super easy online, just have to watch the lecture videos and do a weekly quiz that is open book open note. She doesn't believe in tests so you have a project every 3ish weeks. Super easy A and an interesting class for sure.

Dr. Fraser is amazing! She is such a good teacher and her class is super interesting and fun. There is a chapter quiz on the text book each week but they're pretty easy. Definitely recommend taking from her, deadlines for assignments are the best out of all the other professors! Also the TA's are super helpful!

This is a capstone class, so there is a group project where you do research and present it at the Fulton Conference. Dr. Fraser was an amazing professor. She was so knowledgable and loved what she was teaching us about. Class involved lots of group discussion about moral aspects. I loved this class and highly recommend you take it from Ashley!

I LOVED Professor Fraser!! She was so sweet, and the class was so interesting! There is a weekly assignment, but it is pretty easy. (just use control f and the search bottom to find the answers from the textbook) There are 4 papers, but the TAs are super helpful, making the papers very doable. She is probably my favorite professor!

Literally my favorite professor. Tests are open book, open note and she cancels class on weeks that papers are due so you have extra time. She is so accessible and her lectures are phenomenal. Lots of extra credit is offered too

Read the rubrics and then go to the TAs for the papers. If you don't, you will not get good grades. The course material and the TAs are over all the sections, hurting what would otherwise be a half-decent class. The lectures were mildly interesting but not the best. It's great that she has a diverse perspective, but the class was so-so.

Professor Fraser was great! She handled all topics with respect and would bring in a gospel perspective which I thought was really cool. I think I could've gotten an A without going to class, but I still went because it was interesting. The reading was also interesting and relevant, and the papers had very specific rubrics.

Lectures were super engaging despite there being hundreds of students! Weekly readings and quizzes, but not too hard. The tests are open book, but are not super easy. There are also several papers to write. Prof. Fraser teaches really well and did a good job including the gospel in her lessons. I learned a lot of interesting things in her class!

This class was really interesting, and you can tell Prof. Fraser really cares about what she does. She always tries to bring the gospel into whatever we're talking about. All the tests are open book, but sometimes it's hard to find the answers. I definitely would recommend this class to all majors because you learn a lot and it's not too difficult.

I love her so much! Textbook is online, we had readings every week and a reading quiz every week ( got to use the book). We have three exams and all open note and open book and you can start the test and go back to it anytime. 4 papers, TAs expect a lot, but if you go to them you should be good. TAKE FROM FRASER!!!!!

Dr. Fraser is amazing. I took SFL 210 from her and found her lectures very engaging. Her tests are open note and open lecture slides. There are a few papers with clear grading criteria that I found to be manageable. A fair amount of reading and weekly quizzes online but they are consistent and very manageable.

Prof Fraser was great but the course is organized in an interesting way, the lectures aren't necessary because she repeats information from the textbook reading and the tests are all open book so it is hard to motivate yourself to go to the lectures when you can just go to the textbook during the test. The essays are rough so spend time on them!

such amazing and engaging lectures. She does such a good job at teaching the concepts and making them interesting and relatable. Exams are multiple choice, online, and open note/book. There are 4 long and relatively difficult papers which is the only downside to the course. They took a lot of work to complete. But I still definitely recommend

* Lots of papers to write
* Participation matters
* Open notes on assignments and exams
* Take notes on everything (sometimes on exams she will ask about something she said in a lecture)

I LOVED this class. Dr. Fraser is extremely understanding and helpful. She gives open book, open note tests that you can take an indefinite amount of time on. Definitely, an easy class that I think anyone who plans on being a parent should take. It is so helpful and enlightening. I highly, highly recommend.

professor fraser is great! just make sure you have a good ta. grading for papers was inconsistent since the ta didn't seem to understand proper apa mechanics and good structure. other than that, a pretty easy class that applies to a lot.

Professor Fraser is such a fun teacher to have. Her lectures are very engaging and she's really fun to listen to. You do use the online textbook and are responsible for reading and taking a chapter quiz each week, but her exams are open note. Would 100% take her again.

Dr. Fraser is the best professor I have ever had! She is so modern and intelectual. Also, she is not like other professors that expect us to be perfect, she understands the LDS world and lots of things outside of it too!

Dr. Fraser is an AMAZING prof! She is fun, personal, and considerate.

Just the right amount of participation with very engaging lectures. Weekly readings/quiz were super straightforward and managable. A couple papers with fun topics and generous grading. Finals were open note, online and open for a week.

Class was fun and interesting-- Take it!

One of the best professors I've ever had. Tests are open note and the three papers are very straightforward. Cares about her students so much and gives the most incredible lectures. Felt the spirit more in her class than in my BOM class. Take this class from her!!!

BEST TEACHER EVER! I was a little wary at first because she seemed like she would be difficult, but she is the most understanding, caring, flexible teacher ever. She actually cares about your learning over busy work. She also takes questions seriously and researches your question for next time if she didn't know the answer. Never had that before.

My favorite professor! Learned so much and loved it. Has fun polls to interact with class. Weekly readings with quiz that are open note and book. Textbook online. Take advantage of search bar on textbook for quizzes and tests. Lectures for whole class period and open to questions. 4 papers that are difficult but doable. Tests all open note/book.

1st sem. teaching SFL210 and it went great! Prof. Fraser is so caring and sensitive to the nuances and complications of Hum. Dev. and she was a great teacher. Online textbook, open note open book tests and quizzes, that was great. 4 papers that are the same for every SFL 210 prof, but they were interesting enough. Prof. Fraser is a great choice!

BEST TEACHER!! She really cares about her students success! ALL EXAMS ARE OPEN BOOK AND NOTES! literally amazing! They are also online and you have TWO weeks to complete the exam. I feel like I am walking away a better person, better future parent and spouse! You learn so much cool stuff! The papers are long but the TA's grade easy and are helpful

She genuinely cares for her students! Although her tests are pretty lecture based/heavy, there are chances for extra credit, and she really wants her students to succeed. 1000% would take a class from her again.
The class itself was fine and the content was interesting, but IF YOU CAN TAKE IT FROM A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR

She is the most understanding person. Her empathy makes Human Development so much more applicable. Papers are fairly easy, just make sure to analyze thoroughly. Strongly recommend you come to every class because that is where the bulk of your understanding of the topics will come from. Open book tests!!!

Dr. Fraser is one of the best professors I've ever had. She care a lot about her students and is passionate about what she teaches. There are a couple papers in this class, but they have clear outlines and grading criteria. You need to read a chapter from the textbook and take a quiz on it every week, but they're open book/note just like the exams

Professor LeBaron Black is the sweetest. She genuinely cares about everyone and remembered my name. The in-class discussions she leads are meaningful, and I leave her class feeling uplifted every time.

The class was helpful but I took it during spring semester and it was a lot of busy work and assignments.  You have to read the textbook to do well on the quizes, but the quizes and tests are open note (google docs) and open textbook.

I really wish that I did not take this class online during spring semester. I think I did not learn as much as I would have in person. There is a lot of busy work. The way she has her Canvas set up is kind of confusing. I think I could have gotten a A in this class if it was in person. It being online made me slack a lot.
I was frustrated with how obsessed this teacher was with her own research, podcasts,etc. This class was very easy to do online. Honestly it felt like a lot of busy work.
Professor LeBaron is awesome! She is always willing to help when you need it!

Dr. LB is always very responsive, kind, and willing to help! She always sends out reminders of what is due that week, and has lots of resources to help you succeed. The videos and concepts are amazing! There are a lot of pretty tough exams, but they are open-book open-note. Loved this class!
Its an amazing class because it is so applicable!

Dr. LeBaron Black is passionate about family finance and offers amazing tips that can lead to future financial success. I took this online, and the material is mostly conveyed clearly, but there are a few difficulties with understanding the math. Despite that, this class is extremely useful for understanding finances and how to manage them wisely.
She was kind and cared for her students.
I took this class online and it was still an amazing class. She truly cares for her students and wants you to succeed. She is very willing to help.
She was helpful in accommodating different students needs and will help you if you put in the work. This class is mostly run by TA's, they are really great too.
Professor LeBaron Black is a very kind professor and her online class was very engaging and interesting. I do not recommend taking it over spring semester but it was good none the less.

I took this class in the spring online and it was good. Class isnt super hard just a lot of homework and tests are really long. As long as you do good on the homework and know the equations for the test its not hard to get an A or A-. Teacher is nice.

It makes me sad that Prof Black has bad ratings. I reached out to her many times during this course and she always responded quickly and was forgiving. As for the class itself, the information is INVALUABLE. You will be grateful for the rest of your life that you took it. Just don't take it over the Spring, the pace and workload is unreal.

Professor LeBaron was fantastic! I took SFL 260 remotely and found it very applicable. I wish I'd learned this in high school. My only interaction was her weekly videos, but she teaches clearly and is passionate. The class is easy to follow, tests are open-note, and the assignments help you grow financially. Great class!

The tests are basically all written responses, and my TA was a harsh grader. However, Dr LB allowed us to get half points back on all our tests, which was a game-changer! Dr LB seriously cares for her students. I also took “her” online family finance class, but she just manages it and it is run by TAs. NOT a bad teacher like people say.

I loved SFL 260 and loved taking it from Dr. Black! She is such an understanding and sweet professor! She reached out to me personally and helped me figure accommodations out. This class is SO doable if you put in the time and effort! And it will literally change your life-I now feel so much more confident on buying a car and a house!

Dr. LB is genuinely one of the most caring and loving professors I have ever had. She puts a lot of effort into making her class inspiring, spiritual, and manageable for her students. You will have to put in work to truly learn and excel in her class, but it is so worth it. I would take another class from her in a heartbeat.

Dr. Lebron-Black is kind and caring. If you need help and reach out, she will try to help. Just be responsible and reach out on time, and give them time. This class is well structured, and if you do the practice math, you will pass the exams. Just make sure to do the practice and math reviews. Once you know the structure, you know what to expect.

Extremely applicable class! Covers relevant topics and is not overly challenging. Rubrics are clear, the textbook is easy to follow, lectures are engaging, and exams are open note. The workload is somewhat high but similar to other online courses. The professor is kind and helpful!

I love Dr. LeBaron Black. She is such an amazing teacher. She prepares her classes very well and teaches with passion. She truly cares about her students. She is kind, respectful, and just a genuinely good person. I respect her a lot. She is very supportive and caring toward her students, and she is always joyful. Take her classes for sure!!!

Dr. LB is more concerned about students learning, than about complicating the class with busy-work or overly challenging assignments. If you need anything, she is a safe space. She creates engaging lectures that also make it enjoyable to learn from the other students in the class as well. I learned a lot that will help me in my future career.

I did an MFHD class from dr lebaron-black and it is one of the best classes I took at BYU. Ashley is so passionate and educated and designed the class so we learned from teaching and engaging in the materials ourselves. I would 10/10 recommend her she is happy to meet outside of class to talk or mentor about anything. She rocks!
Excellently curated course. Tough subjects presented respectfully. This class had a positive impact on me and facilitated critical thinking.
I love Dr. LB! She is so kind but also very clear about her expectations and fair in her grading! She also has great class structure, discussions and lectures!

Dr LB is incredible. She addresses hard topics masterfully, providing contrasting views, teaching us to think critically, speaking respectfully, while also not shying away from difficult but growing conversations. While the class has a fair amount of reading, it is very doable and the readings are interesting. One of my favorite classes I've taken!

I took this class in-person, so I can say truly that Dr. L B is one of the nicest people. She is great at teaching in a way that is easily understandable. You need to know the content very well for the exams, the written questions are hard. Don't listen to the negativity!

This class is super applicable to life! I would definitely recommend to anyone who has no clue about anything money. I took it while I was getting married and still did great. There are so many extra credit opportunities, ways to get your grade up, and detailed rubrics, so I'm sure the people who rated her poorly did not take advantage of that;)

Really unfair professor, won't help when needed and really hard to reach. I don't really know what online instructors do, she had no influence in my learning. I was less than one percent away from a different letter grade and she refused to round it.
Class is not insanely difficult if you have some financial background, very weird and strict grading though. Not the best, not the worst.

My mother taught me that if I don't have anything nice to say, I shouldn't say anything, so I won't. I could say a lot of things. Having such a rude professor is not fun. One of the best professors I have ever had!! His lectures are never boring and he keeps you engaged for the entire class period. He is funny but also super clear when presenting material. The tests can be hard but if you study they shouldnt be too bad. If you are debating if its worth it to come to the Salt Lake Center, it is. Love this guy.

In all fairness, his CHEM 105 class is easier than others. He doesn't use short answers and the exam questions are very doable. However, he is one of the best teacher of complex topics, even if he doesn't deal with every concept in the book. He teaches clearly and succinctly. His engaging and assisting style of teaching also greatly helps learning.

I LOVE THIS MAN. He is an amazing lecturer (even on zoom he was engaging), a funny guy, and naturally included spiritual tidbits and chemistry fun facts as he taught. I never liked chemistry growing up but his class made me like it! I didnt think the tests were as hard as other reviews said, but Im a pretty good test taker. Take a class from him!

Gillespie made a difficult subject interesting. He's fun and great at answering questions and explaining topics. He worked out many examples. Homework due every night but didn't take very long. The tests were reasonably difficult. If you worked the problems and reviewed the material, they were definitely doable. I found I didn't need the textbook.
Amazing teacher! Wants his students to succeed and will always answer questions! HIGHLY RECOMMEND
Hes the GOAT of teaching Chemistry!

Professor Gillespie is a great teacher. He was always willing to stay late and help with any questions we had. Beware, tests are given every other week, and they can be pretty heavy. His expectations are clear, and I really enjoyed his teaching style.
