By far the best teacher that I've had in my life. I did well on each test because I did all of the work that he assigned to us. Do your work and you will be FINE! I can't express how much I recommend this teacher to anyone who is scared of taking Chem 105. He made it SO doable. He stays after class to teach. BEST CHEM TEACHER THERE IS!

Professor Gillespie is a homie. He does an awesome job explaining concepts and helping you understand how to do problems. Idk why so many people said his tests are ridiculous, because they're really not. You just gotta attend class and study. Use his worksheets and smartworks to get an idea of how tests will be. BEST CHEM TEACHER @ BYU BY FAR.
I usually don't take the time to do leave ratings, but Professor Gillespie is the best teacher I've had at BYU. He explain things well and gives you every resource you could possibly need to succeed.
He's good, his class is just late.. I had a tough time having the energy for it. His class and exams are totally reasonable.

Professor Gillespie is the best! Chem 105 is a tough course but he teaches hard concepts very effectively. His course is very organized so you can get into a rhythm. He makes the course very memorable because he is so passionate about it. Only complaint- The final was weighted VERY heavily and he didn't prepare us as well for it as he could have.

Better than normal, but undeserving of a the 4.8 avg his account holds. He's a good teacher but the tests are more difficult than they should be, and are meant to trick intelligent students in order to level out the bell curve. I hope you've taken AP chemistry.

His lectures are the best! He teaches really simply and nicely and is really funny. BUT HIS TESTS ARE ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE!! He will teach something and have really simple examples to show the class. THE TESTS ARE CRAZY HARD. EVERYTHING IS COMPLICATED AND YOU WILL FAIL NO MATTER WHAT. YOU CAN STUDY FOR 8 HOURS AND GET A C! Exams are 75% of the grade

Mr. Gillespie is a fantastic teacher. He is the biggest nerd, just LOVES chemistry, and interacts super well with all the students in a way that will make your experience in Chem 105 memorable. His biweekly tests are tough, but he pushes you to really learn the material in a fun and interactive way. A serious recommendation for the Chemistry GE!!

I loved online summer term with Professor Gillespie! He teaches high school too, and is kind of hilarious. He is real. He would teach in a shirt and tie and shorts :) (We only saw because he stood up to grab his kid.) We had Fridays off, the tests were never open during the introduction of new material, and the tests were each week. Study ppts only

Professor G is the best! He explains really tough concepts in a way that really makes sense. He moves at a good pace. He prepares you well for his tests and will never test you on something he didn't teach. Chem 105 is a tough class but if you do the work and go to class you can definitely get an A.

Prof Gillespie is a gem. I was dreading taking chemistry, but I actually enjoyed this class. He really understands how to connect to students, and how to teach well. Also he's hilarious. Totally worth it to take the train up to SLC! You'll also get some extra homework time in-- which you'll need!

Professor Gillespie is a great teacher. He is very knowledgeable and is willing to work with the class to ensure that the topics are being taught clearly. Do the daily quizzes and worksheets and you will be fine.

Awesome lectures. He is truly passionate about chemistry but doesnt teach it in a mad scientist way that makes the content go right over your head. Hes goofy which helped keep students awake since it was a night class. Tests are fair and his homework assignments are very manageable with a good amount of drops.

Professor Gillespie is the man. Taking chem 105 from him was the best decision I made throughout my entire college career. He takes time at the end of each class to go around answering questions and personally making sure everyone understands. Plus, he always starts his lectures off with awesome spiritual thoughts. Take chem 105 from him. Period.

Bro. Gillespie is a great teacher. He loves Chemistry and that comes across in his teaching. He really wants students to understand and goes out of his way to make sure students understand IF they ask for help.
BEST CHEM CLASS AVAILABLE THROUGH BYU !!! best class ever. You will actually learn chemistry and get a good grade. He is the man!

Professor Gillespie is the best professor I've had at BYU so far!! He is so good at keeping you involved and making sure you understand the concepts before he moves on. It was also my favorite class of the semester because he makes it a fun environment. If you have the chance, definitely take CHEM105 from him!
BYU should give him a Chem 106 section to teach.

One of my absolute favorite professors. He makes chemistry fun and the 2.5 hour long lectures go by so fast!! Couldn't imagine taking it from anyone else- plus he is really concerned with our individual understanding and makes the class spiritual as well, which is cool for a chemistry teacher to do!! LOVE LOVE LOVE
He is a really good teacher, very chill. There is homework assigned pretty much everyday but it is really easy. There aren't really any surprises on the tests or anything like that.
Really great professor, makes lectures fun and interesting. Plenty of homework, but stay on top of the material and you'll be fine.
This class has been my favorite this semester. Bro. Gillespie is fun and engaging and teaches the material in a way that benefits everyone. He helps students all he can and never disappoints.

I loved this class! Definitely the most work i've done for any class, but that is due to the subject.  He is amazing at taking difficult concepts and explaining them in simple and clear terms. Does fun in class demonstrations occasionally.  There are online assignments and worksheets that you need to do almost daily. Does helpful test reviews.

Professor Gillespie is an awesome teacher. He does a really good job at explaining material, and giving feedback when you don't understand concepts or need help. His tests are fairly difficult, but they are passable. Reading is a huge part to understanding the material that he teaches. Very hands on, interactive class too.

Professor Gillespie's class is great! He's such an amazing teacher, and really breaks down difficult concepts in a simplistic way that helps so much. If you do your work and understand his lectures you should do well in his class. The tests are hard, but compared to other chem 105 courses this class is a great option. Love Brother Gillespie!
Brother Gillespie is a great guy. His class was a normal level of difficulty but he gives you all the right tools and help to be successful. Explains very clearly but goes fast.

Brother Gillespie is such a great teacher. His presentations for each chapter are clear and concise, he gives "quizzes " every class but they are so helpful and really helps you understand the challenging concepts of this course. I highly recommend this class!

Does everything he can to help you out. Explains the concepts clearly and then will help you one on one after the class if you still don't get it. The homework he gives is actually useful and studying those and the study guides he gives make the tests manageable.

After failing chemistry 105, I thought this class wasn't my thing. Gillespie taught the concepts in a way I understood and it clicked. He would explain a concept, then go over a problem, and then an in class quiz that you work on with others. It's a great method to retain and understand chemistry. If you show up and participate, you'll do great.

Bro. Gillespie explains tough topics in a clear and understanding fashion.  The class is still hard but with his hep it is defiantly doable.  But if you want to pass the class you have to try, if you want to get a good grade you have to put in A LOT of effort!

After taking this class the semester before I thought there was no chance of doing well. After taking the class from Brother Gillespie, I changed my mind completely. He helps everyone understand the concepts and teaches them very clearly, I would recommend him to anyone taking a chemistry class!

Awesome teacher!  Exam 3 was hard, but still possible to get an A on it.  He is super helpful.  He gives worksheets with steps on how to complete the problems and his tests are very similar to his worksheets.  Definitely take him!

Definitely the best professor I've had at BYU. You won't have another teacher take as much time to make sure everyone really understands what he's going over. His tests are fair and are actually based on what he teaches and the practice worksheets which is refreshing from a BYU class.

He made Chem 105 SO DOABLE. You hear so many horror stories about how awful it is, but I did not think this class was that bad. You have homework to do everyday but it's not impossible and it helps keep you on top of the material. His test reviews are helpful. Very approachable and willing to work with you.

Chem 105 is super hard but i honestly think he's the best professor to take it from. He's really funny and really knows his stuff. He only teaches the things that will be on tests and doesn't add pointless fluff. The homework he gives isn't difficult but the tests are. Although I didn't do well on all the tests, I still feel like i learned from him

Bro Gillespie is about as good as you can get for a Chem 105 teacher. He's funny, helpful, and really goes the extra mile to help you understand the material. His tests blow and you have homework assignments every night, but pay attention during class and it's not too bad.
Gillespie is the man. Super fun class. Don't be a baby; it's just chem 105. Little kid science. You'll hate it more from any other professor.

Okay, so I only had him for four classes because he was a sub for our actual professor, but he really impressed me. He's a talented teacher, down-to-earth, sincerely cares about students, passionate, and made the time to learn what he didn't know so he could teach us with clarity and fullness. He actually wants us to learn the material. So helpful.

Great professor! He is  great at explaining and making the class fun. The environment of the class was like a big family. Always had lectures at beginning of class and then learning community at the end of class. He stayed late answering all our questions and helping in any way that he could. Homework is a must to pass and understand concepts.

He is a very likable person. His manner of teaching, however, is hard to follow. Tests have little relation to assignments. HW is due five days of the week. He expects time spent watching videos and reading during the week. I would say at least 2-3 hours of work per day. Tests are curved, multiple choice A-H. Drops many HW assignments.

As a part time student working at slc, I didn't have many choices but to take the only session offered at salt lake center. However, I can't say how lucky I am that Gillespie is teaching here. He explains the hardest concepts crystal clear; easy to follow; super funny and extremely approachable. His class is fantastic, best science teacher ever!

Never taken chemistry before but Gillespie made it possible to get an A.  Yes the lectures are long and yes the tests aren't easy but he sets you up with everything you need to pass the tests. Great teacher and VERY satisfied with taking it up in SLC. His average grade says a C+, not true, CHOOSE GILLESPIE!

Bro. Gillespie is AWESOME! I wouldn't take Chem 105 from anyone else! His lectures are thorough and helpful and entertaining--also very clear. He gives plenty of homework that's pretty easy but they are stepping stones to get an A because they help you prepare for the tests SO MUCH! Take this course from Gillespie and you won't regret it!!!

He was a nice guy but tests were pretty ridiculous. His lectures are fun  but hard to follow. He drops a lot of the assignments which is nice however there are tons of them. He is a great lecturer but not the best teacher. Chem 105 is a really hard class and I would take it on campus next time because 2 days a week isn't enough to understand.

Originally scared about college chemistry, took this class, studied a ton and got an A.  Now i'm in 106 down in provo and shave an A.  Gillespie made it possible.  Amazing teacher, and class set up.  Smaller class, more time with the professor.

Professor Gillespie really made chemistry fun and interesting. I enjoyed going to class and he gives you the tools to succeed. Test are very tricky and are majority of your grade. I would recommend him to anyone.

Professor Gillespie is ~25 years old, which make him extremely approachable. He is the best Science professor I have ever had. I hate Chemistry, and he made it tolerable. I never read the book, just came to class, and got an A by reading his powerpoints and doing micro exams. He gives all the tools to succeed. Tests are tricky.
Very enthusiastic as a professor. There is a lot of homework, more than is useful especially the Micro Exams but will prepare you for tests
So interesting that I actually changed my major to chemical engineering. HIghly recommended. Best explanations of hard concepts that I've heard from any professor. He's really funny, too.

GREATEST TEACHER... EVER.  I have never had someone teach with such clarity-- I didn't even have to read the book and I ended up with an A!  The hw he gives out is just enough to learn-- no busy work.  He drops hw scores and mini-exam scores.  If you want to understand chemistry AND get an A, TAKE IT FROM HIM!  He CARES!

Proffessor gilespie really cares about his students. His tests are hard but doable. He really prepares well for his classes.  If you take chem 105 you have to take it with gilespie. He likes todo one on ones to help you as much as possible.

Super fun and enjoyable to work with! Very willing to help and answer questions! Tests are hard, but everything is covered in class so if you pay attention and do all the homework you'll do well in the class.

Has a large book for pearl of great price. Has a lot of readings for a religion class and cares more about making you memorize trivia and doing large amounts of busy work than actually growing your testimony. This is the first bad religion teacher I've had and I'm a senior. Very disappointing

Dr Shannon is an amazing religion professor. He really knows his stuff, knows his students by name, tackles every question asked, keeps lectures fascinating, and clearly has a firm belief in God. He teaches both easy and hard doctrines with skill and care. 10/10

I wouldn't recommend taking this class for 3 reasons:

1. His classroom discussions are based 80% on what the students want to discuss. He often failed to adequately cover the learning outcomes we needed to know for the test.

2. His exams are like trivia. 

3. Its December and I have ungraded quizzes from September.

If you are looking for an easy religion class, don't take this one. Dr. Shannon knows his stuff but there is a 4-5 page reading guide you need to fill out before every class (as your read 5-15 chapters in the Old Testament....) Takes him forever to grade things and he tests you on obscure details.

He understands the OT and so lectures were always super interesting.  You have a study guide to fill out before class on the reading prep which can get up to 8 pages of questions to answer, so they get pretty lengthy.  But you better do them because 70% of the test questions come from these reading guides. exams felt more like random fact questions
Don't take Prof. Shannon. Tests are unclear and he teaches questionable doctrine.

He's such a great professor! Knows his stuff, and really listens when you ask questions. Fill out the reading guide while you do the readings, the quizzes and test come from those! The tests aren't very hard, he tells you what to study.

I studied the Book of Mormon every single day for 2 years and struggled on these tests. I love his lectures, he's really smart and has great insights. The only problem is those quizzes and tests are more of random facts rather than actual doctrine. Even the open book tests I struggled on while using ChatGPT, the scriptures and Gospel Library.

I loved the lectures! He's an Old Testament scholar so he focused on parts of the Book of Mormon that connect with the OT. I enjoyed the random facts, and that I always felt the Spirit really powerfully. The tests were more like trivia than important gospel principles, but the rest of the assignments were simple. A quirky guy but great class!

Dr. Shannons a great guy but I would not recommend his class. He was horrible about getting grades in on time. He never grade 1/3 of our quizes and kept making empty promise about how they would be done by next week so you never really knew where your grade was at. The tests were unnecessarily hard and more on random facts from the Book of Mormon.

I took him for REL A 275, but the tests were not on teaching OR doctrines of the book. He said the cumulative portion of the final was only from previous midterms, but he added extra questions over that area as well. The study guides weren't helpful and it was almost impossible to do well in this class. Do not recommend.

RELA275 Long study guides with pretty useless questions (# of Seripham wings, how many sisters did Nephi have, why was Jacobugath destroyed, ect) for every class. His pop quizzes only once happened on a Monday most were on Wednesdays, and many of them were missed anyway. I will say I learned a lot about the historical context of the Book of Mormon.

There are incredibly long study guides for every class, about 30-50 questions you're expected to know on the reading, and you *might* have a quiz each class. The only study guide you get for tests is the hundreds of questions from the study guides of every day. For the final, he said "you should know everything we've talked about." Not worth it.
0/10 would not recommend

Professor Shannon meant well but he wasn't my favorite when it came to teaching style. He assigned tons of readings, expected you to answer 50+ questions for every lecture, and never responds to emails. We never discuss the readings in class, but the midterms are all on the readings. I would personally skip on this class.
His class doesn't overburden you, but it just wasn't quite what I was hoping it to be. His teaching style just isn't my favorite.
Dr. Shannon rocks!! Take his classes!

Pop quizzes but you get 8/10 just for being there, the questions are usually obvious from the reading. The reading is just in the scriptures for the OT class at least. His lectures are just so great. Part of the class is students asking questions which was great bc the OT can be weird. He helps the OT sound really beautiful actually.

Ive never heard a professor talk so fast. But I LOVE this guy. Not the typical cheesy EFY BYU professor. He knows his stuff. OT class was challenging but I actually learned a ton which I feel like I dont normally in religion classes. He just has great lectures and barely any homework. Lowkey such an awkward guy but it really works for him.

Dr.Shannon was my favorite professor during my time at BYU, the way he teaches is phenomenal! It's really easy to get an A, he gives you a list of questions and with them the exact verse of scripture that they are found in. You will not regret taking his class, his class is spectacular. Dr.Shannon and the content he presents are as cool as it gets.

Lectures were phenomenal. Decent amount of reading, but he compiles all the required readings into one book, which was super clutch. The only thing that was tough was that no electronics are allowed. Do the readings and you'll pass the tests, but the lectures are phenomenal. Dr Shannon is brilliant and has great insights. Would take again.

Dr. Shannon is great! Lectures were inspiring and insightful, do pay attention and take good notes because lecture material does appear on the exams. 2-3 questions quizzes once a week, nothing crazy. He does talk very fast when he gets excited about something, but he is aware of this and will slow down if you ask him to.

Very knowledgeable professor -- he speaks so fast that some words blend together lol. Expectations for class and assignments are clear and homework is doable. The tests are okay because you can use your notes on some of them. However, I just took my final and there are assignments from almost 2 months ago still not graded... really annoying.

Dr. Shannon is such an amazing professor. For this class, there was a lot of reading. He gives very helpful feedback and is always willing to meet with you to answer questions and explain things you don't understand. I left every class feeling uplifted.

This professor is by far one of the best men I've ever met! He is so king and loving and is so willing to explain anything and everything! He luckily put together a book that has all of the readings, guides, questions, this is super helpful and beneficial! There is a quiz a week, but do your readings and don't worry! His testimony alone is worth it

They didn't have the class option but I took Rel A 392 R and it was the best religion class that I ever took, hands down. I took the class because I wanted to increase the depth of my knowledge. And he literally changed the way I approach religion and how I understand ALL of the scriptures, and this class has legitimately changed my life. TAKE HIM!

Not your typical EFY professor - focuses on the doctrine and understanding what the scriptures are saying. Knows 6+ languages. Still extremely caring and accessible. Its really not that much reading compared to a 3 credit class. Just do the reading before each lecture and you'll be fine. It took me about 30 minutes to do the reading.

Professor Shannon was such an awesome professor. I learned a ton in his class and he always led amazing discussions. I really liked how he didn't just teach from a powerpoint, but rather allowed class to go in the direction of questions people had. He definitely knows his stuff! He is one of my favorite professors and I would definitely recommend!

Dr Shannon is incredible! His 392R Survey of the Old Testament class was amazing. He shared incredible insights, and worked each lecture around questions that students had. His excitement is contagious! There are a few easy quizzes based on Bible readings. Great class!!!

I don't think I've ever had a more religious experience than this class while on BYU campus. He smashed most of my preconceived notions about the New Testament and replaced them with knowledge that increased my understanding of the gospel.

I loved this class. Professor Shannon gives amazing lectures that touch on both the intellectual and spiritual. The homework he assigns gives you everything you need to get a good grade on his tests (questions are pulled directly from the homework) and he holds a really helpful review session before the final. I'd definitely recommend Him.
This man is THE GOAT. I learned so much intellectually and spiritually. Super easy. Can't recommend this class enough.

Dr. Shannon is great! He knows a lot about the Old Testament and is super passionate about it. He's not always super clear about assignment deadlines and he can get a little sidetracked sometimes, but he cares about his students and wants to help!

Love Dr. Shannon! This ain't your gooey EFY kinda religion class, but that's exactly why I loved it. He has a really great academic yet spiritual approach that made his lectures so interesting. Participation is important but if you do the quizzes, they're pretty much the tests. Really knows ancient scripture and brings a great spirit to class.

Professor Shannon has a clear love for scripture, and that comes through very clearly in his lectures. There's a lot of stuff that only gets mentioned in lectures, so attending and good note-taking are important, but the lectures are excellent.

no electronics in class
Tons of reading. but really its maybe 2 hours between class.
Hes really really good at teaching concepts in class. if you do homework and take notes everything will work out
my only complaint is the lack of stuy guide for the midterms and finals. he just kinda says its about everything which sucks

This was such a bad class. He starts off every class by discussing questions from the reading which takes up half of the time and goes on random rants which don't have anything to do with the material. The readings are long and so boring and don't teach you anything. He never actually answers any of his learning outcomes and is hard to understand

I love this man! Such an amazing class! There were some classes where the spirit was so strong you could almost reach out and touch it. Prof. Shannon answered many of my questions that other religion professors hadnt been able to answer for me. It is a 300 level class, so be expected to do a decent amount reading, but its pretty reasonable.

Fantastic professor. 10/10 would recommend. Very inspiring lectures and engaging intellectually. So long as you do your written responses, read the assigned scriptures, take the reading quizzes, and pay attention in class then you'll do fine. He cares greatly about individual students and values all opinions & questions.

Great class with amazing lectures where I learned a lot. However, it did often seem very geared towards students majoring in some type of religious studies and became hard to keep up with all the readings. A couple papers are due throughout the semester but very easy. Tests and final paper are the opposite. Tests are on obscure things and timed.

Dr. Shannon is lowkey my fave religion professor at BYU, definitely more academic than EFY speaker. if you're looking for the next hank smith or john bytheway, dr. shannon might not be your cup of tea. but if you're looking to gain deep scriptural and doctrinal knowledge while being spiritually uplifted and subtly entertained, Dr. Shannon's the guy

Prof. Shannon seems like a really nice guy. I took him online so I think he misinterpreted a lot of my questions, but he was earnest in trying to answer them. He was very accessible outside of class. His tests/quizzes were open book and were pretty easy for me, but not for people who aren't speedreaders.

Worst class I have ever taken. The lectures were boring and long. Least spiritually edifying religion class I have taken. The quizzes and tests were terrible. You had 5 minutes for every quiz 5-7 questions long and 65 minutes for 76 questions on the final. If you have any amount of test anxiety, try thinking about having 51.3 seconds/question.

Doctor Shannon is what I want from every religion professor at BYU. His discussions were thoughtful and spiritual. There is quite a bit of reading, but if you pay attention and do said readings, you should be able to easily get an A. He is also always available and ready to help with questions. Highly recommend.

Boring is the best word to describe him. Maybe he is different in person but in my online class he could not keep my attention. The only participation was volunteering to read. He is not a goofball, I never heard him make a joke or even laugh. It was like he was showing off his knowledge and saying "Look how holy I am" Class difficulty was average

Oh my heck, this was my favorite religion class I've taken at BYU thus far. Brother Shannon shares all of his knowledge about the scriptures (Pearl of Great Price for this class), gives amazing resources, and the reading is reasonable (about an hour per class period). He always asks thought-provoking questions and bears testimony. You'll love it.
The papers he assigns are pretty easy. Exams are multiple-choice and short answer, which is kind of annoying but not too difficult. He is a very knowledgable guy and I enjoyed his class a lot.

Professor Shannon is honestly one of the best religion professors at BYU; his class isn't as demanding as many religion classes are, but he still puts in a lot of good effort into his classes and is AWESOME at answering questions about his subject material! I've never been a huge fan of religion classes, but this one felt just right to me!

Kind of a goofy guy but it makes the class interesting haha. In all reality, though he's a solid choice. Does a great job bringing the spirit. Make sure you do all the readings and fill out the reading guides.

Professor Shannon is really kind and gives great lectures. There is a quiz every week so make sure you do the readings and show up to class. Other than that the work load isn't too bad and all tests (other than the final) are open book open note.

Amazing in class discussions, he's able to pull from other writings and stuff to bring up things I've never heard in class. Really respectful and acknowledging of different perspectives. I've never had as much acknowledgement and defense of women in any religion class. Really strong spirit in this class, I'd take him again in a heartbeat.

LOVED the class! Amazing teacher. He is very knowledgeable about the subject matter. Conveys the material so it is easy to understand. Invites student participation in the lectures. Do the homework and you will do great on the exams. Enjoyed his teaching style. I would definitely take another class from this professor.

Dr. Shannon is a unique, but great, religion professor. His PoGP class has changed how I view the scriptures. There is definitely more of a focus on academia as opposed to spirituality, but he still has his deep moments. It may just be the class, but class discussion seemed dominated by students trying to 1-up each other, so be careful.

Dr. Shannon is a solid professor. Grading criteria couldn't be clearer, and test material comes directly from defined class topics and reading questions. It's an easy A with an hour of work a week. But it's also a really cool class. I've learned a lot from the Pearl of Great Price. Dr. Shannon loves discussion so it's not boring.

Professor Shannon gives some of the best lectures I have ever had in a religion class at BYU. He takes the stories from the scriptures and applies them to our lives in way you would have never thought of. He also really cares about his students and does his best to ensure your success.

Dr. Shannon is one of a kind and very knowledgeable, but his teaching style and my leaning style did not mesh well. There was more out of class work than most religion classes, and it wasn't very spiritual. There is one (generally) 3-4 page reading guide per class, so for me it was just find the answer and memorize.
Loved this class, learned a lot! I didn't fill out the reading guides, I think that was why I didn't do stellar. Hes a great teacher. Lots of assignments, lots of reading.

Bro. Shannon is awesome! I have really enjoyed his classes and tbh I was a little worried at first that I wouldn't. His teaching style is different but I came to really like it! He is funny and very intelligent. He is willing to answer any questions and leads most of his discussions based on student comments.

Dr. Shannon is so much fun. He's kind of an odd ball, but in the best ways. He is funny, engaging, and clearly very invested in the gospel as well as the material of this course. This class is easy if you pay attention, take notes, and do the reading guides he provides. Exams are open note and there are even a few extra credit opportunities!

Dr. Shannon is amazing! He teaches the doctrine very clearly. He doesn't usually tell you what will and won't be on the test, but he gives a study guide where all the questions tell what will be on the test. He teaches very thoroughly, and if anyone ever has questions, he takes time to answer those questions then continue with the lesson.

Dr. Shannon is an amazing teacher! Every day you come to class, he makes you feel inspired by the time that you leave. Readings are useful to know the material beforehand. Occasional quizzes in class, but if you do the reading, you can ace them easily. Midterms come with reading guides and if you go over it, it'll be no problem passing the class.

I really enjoyed his lectures and think he's great but this was ridiculously hard for a religion class. Felt like I had everything down and would receive low grades on exams. In class quizzes were near impossible. I've never made less than an A- in any other religion class.

Favorite religion class by far! He made me excited to do the reading assignments and attend class. I always had to share with my friends what I had learned that day from his class. You know what to expect on his tests, so it is easy to study for. You will not regret taking Pearl of Great Price from him!

Dr. Shannon puts great effort into his lectures and is passionate about the scriptures. He encourages questions and doesnt shy away from controversial or difficult topics. There are daily reading assignments, weekly quizzes and papers, and three tests. An inspirational and uplifting class.

Dr. Shannon is an amazing teacher. He explains the Pearl of Great Price really well and always encourages questions, and discussion. He's very passionate about the scriptures and considerate of everyone's comments. Weekly Quiz. Few tests. He's a great teacher. I recommend him highly.

2-3 hours/week for an A . Kind of felt like we were just surveying random parts of the Bible for most of the class, but at least he's spiritual about it. Study guides are given for quizzes and tests, but can sometimes be a bit confusing and long.

I LOVED this class. My favorite religion class at BYU- and this was my last one! Brother Shannon is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about this material. He manages to make every single class meaningful. Gives pop quizzes every other class or so, and expands on homework material- you need to attend to do well on tests but they weren't hard.

He is SO EXCITED about what he teaches and it's contagious! He brings in artifacts and ancient texts to get students to understand the history of the scriptures they're learning. He takes time to learn all the students' names and is always looking for ways to give extra credit. I can't give enough praise to Dr. Shannon.

Let me clarify that the four I gave him for difficulty is only relative to other religion classes. This is one where you need to work to get an A. I luckily got an A-, the average grade was a B. If you remove the outliers with awful grades then the average would still be hovering around a B+. He is a funny and passionate teacher, it just isn't easy

This was my favorite religion class I have ever taken. Dr. Shannon is very intelligent and gives amazing, spiritually uplifting lectures. The weekly quizzes are easy. The tests can be kind of hard, just make sure you study. Only one paper, which he grades pretty liberally. Take pearl of great price from Dr. Shannon! It is life changing!

I loved Dr. Shannon. His tests are semi-difficultBUT all of the questions come from his study guides. Lectures were very interesting and he knows SO much about the New Testament. Quizzes once a week, but he gives you a list of questions that the quizzes will come from. There are 4-5  papers that are worth a lot of your grade, but he grades fairly!

He isn't the worst religion professor ever, but I won't be seen in any of his classes. That was the only class I couldn't get and A. Weird lectures that have no real flow to follow. He does try and he is very lenient with his students.

Though he's not a full-time staff member, he's one of the best teachers I had.  Be expected to read and fill out reading guides during the entire semester, but if you do that and pay attention in class you will do fin on the quizzes and tests.  There's one long paper due, but it's not that difficult.  Would definitely take another class by him.

He is an okay professor for the Book of mormon. Weekly quizzes can sometimes trick you. He sometimes will get on a topic and somehow relate it to something that no normal person would make a connection with.
He is positive and lenient with any situation that you bring to him. Good man.

Brother Shannon's class looks tough and time consuming on the syllabus, but once the semester starts it is a cinch. He is extremely lenient on the quizzes and tests. He does give long reading guides, but they are pretty easy to fill out. His class is very spiritual, and you learn so much. Sometimes he allows for late work. He will work with you.

Reading guides for every section thoroughly discussed in class. Test questions are taken directly from them, a review session is held in class the day before the test, and sample essay questions, and topics to know are posted early. 2 midterms and a final, 3 two-page papers, final 7-page paper, quizzes in class (from reading guides). Great guy!

I really did not enjoy this class. Brother Shannon doesn't teach you information about the text, he just preaches about Christ and how He saves us all. It's like a 2 hour long sacrament meeting talk. His tests are really hard, as in 100% short answer. Don't take him, there are way better Book of Mormon teachers.
Hard class, but what did you expect? He knows EVERYTHING. He tells you straight up what he expects from you, but be prepared for a lot of memorization and studying.

His lectures are very interesting and his knowledge for the scriptures incredible. Class mostly based off reading charts papers and ATTENDANCE! But his final for the first half of the Book of Mormon was ridiculous. You had to know EVERY DETAIL. Like names of fathers and stuff..Beware, you have to put up a fight for test curves..I know we did

Bro. Shannon has so much knowledge about the scriptures. Everyday you walk into class knowing that you're going to walk out uplifted, informed and generally better off than you were before you came. I wish I could take every religion class from him.

I LOVED THIS CLASS.  I was always SO uplifted every day, and there's no busywork, which is awesome.  Basically, your grade is determined by daily attendance, a weekly 1-2 page paper, honestly reading for half an hour out of the scriptures daily, the midterm, and the final.  He's super funny, and always willing to help you! TAKE IT. :)

Interesting during lecture, but his lessons rarely correspond with the information on tests. If you do the work it is not too difficult to do well in this class.The weekly assignments buffer your test grades.

Bro. Shannon is really hard. He is a great lecturer, his classes are very interesting but you'd best know the Book of Mormon really well or you'll be lost when it comes to tests. And I mean you had better know details. He knows how to teach a class but he doesn't know how to write a test. No-one got a good grade on the final because it was so bad.

Professor Shannon is an awesome teacher! I've learned so much from his class! He really cares about his students understanding the material. He does require weekly assignments but they weren't bad and they really made me think about what the message was in the text. i would highly recommend taking a class from him.
Very hard, but alright at teaching
Everyone who takes Dr. Allen's class loves him. He is such a cool professor. His teaching style is really engaging and he loves students
BJ helped me want to go into sales. I had never wanted to in the past, but he helped me see that sales is not at all what I thought it was. Plus, he is a really fun professor
Bj's class changed my life. He gave a spiritual thought at the beginning of class one day that changed the way I see church and my relationship with God. I am forever grateful for that
10/10. Would recommend!

Best professor ever!! I took his class two years ago and his class convinced me to go into sales. I knew his class was useful when I took it, but it wasn't until I worked in sales after school that I realized how useful it was. It helped me so much. A must if you want to work in sales!
He is the most enthusiastic teacher I had in the business school. And you can tell that he really loves his students with the work he does with the Sales Society. He even helped me get an internship.
I learned so much from this class that helped me in my job. Fantastic professor!

Honestly this class was a waste of time. BJ seems like he does not enjoy teaching in the slightest, and he says there is no final yet you take a test on the last day of class and then your "final" is writing a four page essay.... Not very helpful for life or sales in general. I would take a different sales class if I were you and save yourself time

This is the best class that I took in the business school. It is so useful for real life, and I felt like everything I learned could be applied in my job. And the professor is super cool and loved his students.
I felt that this class could be taught within 1 credit hour rather than 3 credits. He is an amazing individual who loves his class, it just felt like a waste to me.

I created this professor just so I could tell you how awesome he is! He gives the most amazing spiritual thoughts and really cares about the class and your sales skills! 10/10 would recommend. Super fun

She definitely cares about the subject but the class was just so unorganized that it was hard to follow. She was constantly switching due dates and having quizzes about topics and readings that we hadn't read or covered yet

I took Bonyata twice and I just love her. She is super caring and the classes I took from her were really easy but you actually learn things from the assignments. I highly recommend taking her for any Spanish class!

Take 330 from Prof. Bonyata!  The class is super manageable with a couple short readings every week and just a few papers.  Class was really meaningful and she facilitates discussion that makes you really think in a good way.  She doesn't grade too very hard, and she takes a class period to review before each exam which prepares you really well.

She is awesome. She is very caring, will work with you, and will respond to questions very quickly. The tests are a breeze if you review the PowerPoints she posts. But if you don't do well with individual and group projects, be prepared because she loves them!

I'm not quite done with this semester, but Hna Bonyata has been the best. She really cares about the topic and her students. She is willing to meet you one on one for extra help and wants her students to succeed. Super amiable. Would take from her again!!

Sra. Bonyata is a great professor. She is very passionate about what she teaches and wants to share that with her students. While you do need to be in class and participate to get a good grade, the class itself isn't too hard if you pay attention. She also responds well to emails and is very accessible if you have questions.

It was her second time teaching the class, so there wasn't any structure, and there are no rubrics at all. Hardly anything goes into your grades, so you have to do well on every assignment. The tests are completely free response and essays. And there are so many presentations, the students basically teach the entire class.

The professor was nice and tried to be excited about the content, but she was not a great presenter of information. She spent half the class talking about things that weren't on the study guide and barely talked about what was on it. I ended up teaching myself the majority of the test content. We also had to create 50 min group presentations.

This class is very easy and I don't feel like she honestly expects much of the students. There is very little homework and tests are mostly matching or east multiple choice. The class is not very exciting and you have to pay attention because she will randomly call on people, but the material isn't hard. Overall she's a solid choice.

Awesome lady but this class was pretty boring over Zoom. I know she didnt enjoyed it either. Its an easy A and the last month of class is extra chill. Im sure it would have been a blast in person though!

Hermana Bonyata makes SPAN330 a very enjoyable experience. She has a lot of fun while teaching, and I can't help to think how awesome the class would've been in person without covid. The course, however, was slightly more difficult than I had anticipated especially with the added complications of online learning. Overall great experience.

This semester was probably rough for her but she really wasn't my favorite spanish professor. She seemed to grade off her mood so sometimes I would randomly get a good score on a crappy paper or get a bad score on something I felt I did good on. She also takes forever to put the grades into learning suite. However, shes a sweet soul. Good lady.

Lectures are a waste, but required to attend and participate. Mostly spent reading the hw assigned beforehand and watching random videos. Disorganized syllabus. Rubrics for papers and projects don't exist. Subjective grader. Test questions mostly ask for opinions. Not accommodating to students in need. Luckily most assignments are easy though.
I thought I was going to hate Spanish Literature, but I absolutely loved it. She made class so fun and interactive. If you need to take this class take it with Hermana Bonyata!!!

She must be one of my favorite Spanish teachers in 4 years! She changed me into a happy, excited person when I was sick and grumpy! She links the gospel to the class content and is so kind and smart! Her Spanish is amazing. My advice: make sure to study thoroughly the longest reading she assigns as you'll have to write an analysis paper about it.

Prof. Bonyata is a caring, kind person who gets to know her students. She isn't a native Spanish speaker, but she knows her material well. The class is graded on a combination of tests, essays, and quizzes, so you really do need to do all the reading and understand it well, but it isn't an overwhelming amount. Lots of classroom discussions.

Profesora Bonyata is the best. I felt like her course was right on the level it should be for a 300 level spanish class. The literature we read was easy to read, the movies we watched in class were interesting and the class overall was really fun. 100% would take the course from her again.

Excellent professor. She is emotionally invested in her work and takes time to get to know her students individually. She was pretty scattered but genuinely kind. Tests are passable, but you cannot get by by skipping the readings. Several lessons were inspirational and spiritual. Best gospel application Ive seen in a Spanish class. Group projects.
I loved her. She was a very caring professor. She also expects you to participate a lot.

I really loved this professor. I haven't ever had a teacher that made me laugh so much. She gives out study guides for the tests which is nice. The course is designed so that you start out with the hard stuff and then it just gets easier from there. Some reading but it wasn't too bad. However, there are quite a few assignments...

Hermana Bonyata is an excellent teacher who loves her students. She really cares that they all learn and grow. She expects everyone to participate, but doesn't push too hard for those introverts. She gives great feedback and teaches the nuances of poetry simply. There are several papers, but they aren't too hard, and she helps along the way.
Sister Bonyota is an exceptional caring teacher... love her !

Hermana Bonyata is fantastic. I'm sorry for the people that didn't like her because I had a blast in her class, as did everyone else in my class. She was really great about making her classes relatable and having real (and incredibly fun) discussions. She's not difficult, keeps students interested and engaged and has a ton of fun. Highly suggest.

I'm not a native Spanish speaker nor Spanish-speaking return missionary and she was so helpful in meeting my needs. There are two exams and a final, four papers 2-5 pages long, and quizzes for each reading assignment. There is also a poetry reading assignment and a short play you do in front of the class, very easy. Excellent professor, reccommend.

I enjoyed the class. Prof. Bonyata is extremely peppy excited to teach. Sometimes I felt like papers and test answers were graded too much on her opinion... Be prepared to go to the Spanish writing center--even after doing that she will pick out errors. Overall  straightforward, and relatively enjoyable. Participation in class is important to her.
Sister Bonyata is a homie. She is fun and her class is not overly difficult. You will get an A in the class if you just pay attention and write cohesively in Spanish. A fantastic choice for 339.

She is not hispanic, for those looking for more exposure. She often didn't respond to my emails. LS had tons of outdated information. Her grading on papers and activities was rubric-less. It was mostly subjective, you have to be able to guess her opinion and match it. We were literally graded on a play performance, in a literature class.
One of the more worthwhile Spanish classes you can take. She is prepared and has a schedule which she actually follows. Lots of participation and an engaging lecturer.
Prof Bonyata is really cool. You sing a lot though, which is unnecessary. She is pretty liberal which is fine, just different than the typical BYU feel. She's fair and helps you review for tests.

Loved this class! The workload was very light, but I still felt like I learned everything I needed to. I understand poetry a lot better now. The stories and plays gave us a lot to think about, and she lead some deep discussions. So glad I took this from her.
HERMANA BONYATA IS THE REALEST. she makes learning fun and is willing to help whenever you need it. smart, funny and overall wonderful. just want to be her bff and take every class from her.

Prof. Bonyata gave a really enjoyable class.  The activities during class were very helpful.  I was never too stressed out with homework or completing the projects for class and I still learned a lot from her.  I would definitely recommend her every time.

Hermana Bonyata is amazing! We had so many real-life discussions about what we read for homework and she really helps you to apply what you're learning. She plans the schedule so that the class gets easier as the semester goes, so it's a total breeze during finals.
She is one of the best professors I've had. Information is presented well, and expectations are clear. The short stories and poems we read were very interesting and thought-provoking.

She seems to know what she is talking about, but you don't really get too engaged in the material. She shows videos, which spice up the class and she also sings, which can be fun or just awkward. Her tests are not long, but therefore can cause you to lower your grade quick with small mistakes.

I absolutely loved taking Hna Bonyata's class. I feel like she was very clear and I always knew what was expected of me. I loved the Poetry section and I felt like she was always really good at engaging us and helping us learn about literature. Her tests are hard but she gives you study helps. If you're taking Spa 339, definitely take it from her.

She did a great job of putting all the aspects of what we were learning into perspective so we could each understand it. She is one of the easiest graders I know and is very helpful when needed. She made literature enjoyable, which has not been done by any of my past teachers.

Very easygoing teacher. Sometimes you think she may be going on a tangent, but she is really trying to make the material applicable in "hip" ways. I mean, when you watch "Stranger Than Fiction" in class you know she's cool. Quizzes and tests are online and wicked easy; however, do take care to use proper grammar on essays. Highly recommended.

Hermana Bonyata really wants her students to enjoy the course and does a great job of putting together relatable lectures that will interest the class. I didn't understand much about how she graded things and why she talked about some of the things she did, not of all which seemed to really reflect a gospel standpoint, but it was an enjoyable class

Great teacher.  Had her for  the intro to lit class.  I hate literature, but her class was the most enjoyable and fun class I took this semester, I looked forward to it each day.  She is very reasonable, work load is manageable.  Tests are not difficult with the study guide.  If you take 339, take it from her.

She is such a nice lady that cares about the students and doesn't judge their spanish. Uses songs and movies to better clarify. Three total tests, each take about 2 hours to take. Essay format and recognizing the work of the author. Memorize the study guide for tests and you'll be fine.  Easy, but not easy enough for an A. Must attend for points.
Not crazy about her. Class was ok and kind of interesting. She can be unclear sometimes and sometimes go off on counterproductive tangents. Some parts of the class were fun.

Wonderful class, Señora Bonyata is one of the best professors I've ever taken a class from. She explains wonderfully, and truly cares for her students. She is a very compassionate woman and I've learned many things from her. She encouraged us to discuss topics that we were reading as well as debate some. She always maintained control and topics nev

Hermana Bonyata is a very fun, down-to-earth person. She enjoys having fun with her students, offers multiple opportunities for extra credit, and makes each class enjoyable. We read stories and go in depth to real-life application of it to ourselves. I highly enjoyed her class and would definitely take another class from her.

She's really nice, but unless you want a really unorganized class to lower your GPA, don't take it from her.  Had to guess what she wanted on tests, due dates are never clear, and she doesn't respond to emails.  Again, nice lady but don't take it from her if you can avoid it!
Really good teacher. Her curriculum is easy to understand but not the easiest. Do the homework and study for the tests and you can get an A.

Profesora Bonyata was always very kind and understanding, even to us students who found it difficult to speak Spanish with all of those confident RM's ;) Tests aren't hard if you just study the study guides and attend class. She made studying Spanish Literature fun and entertaining.

I was anti-lit for a long time as I have found it to be disturbing.  Worse still, in Spanish so that I don't know all of the words.  Nevertheless, Professor Bonyata's enthusiasm and course setup was so effective, that I really ended up appreciating the class.  She is very nice, fun and makes it all life applicable.  I took SPAN 339 from her too.

Profesora Bonyata is really into poetry and "expressing" one's self but personally I hated the class. Her test where ridiculous and she expects a lot out of her students. She is a nice person but I would not recommend taking the class from her if you can avoid it.

Prof Bonyata is really nice and personable and encourages class participation. She moves pretty fast through lectures and it is easy to miss things. Fortunately the material is not very difficult. The tests are easy if you do the reading and pay attention. I didn't expect to like this class but she made it interesting and I ended up enjoying it.

Avoid her. I went to every class, did all the homework and still failed. I studied the study guides for the test but she made her tests from the powerpoint.  Why have a freaking study guide if it doesn't help for the test?  Don't take a class from her. She is very slow to respond to emails and she isn't helpful. BTW,I have a 3.7 GPA overall.
She is a sweetheart!

Great teacher. Makes class interesting by relating the lit to every day life. Tests are straight forward. If you know the study guide, which comes straight from the ppts posted online, you'll get an A. Daily HW which helps you keep up with the short readings. One project, either essay or ppt presentation. Would recommend to anyone!

I enjoyed this class, especially compared to other literature professors I've had.  She makes it interesting and tries to make the material something we can relate to.  She does fun things like showing movie clips to demonstrate a theme.  The tests are hard (a lot of little, seemingly insignificant details), but she is very willing to help.

This class had the most ridiculous grading ever. There was no consistency. The same exact answer that one person wrote on their test was marked wrong on another persons. Will have pop quizes just to hurt your grade... nit picky details...she loves the material which is great but this class will lower your GPA

Hermana Bonyata is great because she enjoys the material.  I remember one time when she was reading a love poem like she was the one receiving it.  She is pretty animated.  I recommend the class because it is possible to get a good grade and the literature that is learned is really great.

She is a super nice lady who believes in leaving early.  She always gave us time in-class to work on our big assignments so I rarely did any work outside of class.  But it was pretty disorganized and sometimes her rubrics weren't very clear.  I wonder if people struggling w/ grading was b/c of the TA because I feel like she grades super easy.

She is terrible at using learning suite and is constantly adjusting deadlines. She is a hard grader and gives no feedback. We had class presentations and not a single group got 100%. I have spent so much time on this class between the 10 hours of volunteering, online textbook, IRIS module, and so many busy work assignments. So frustrating!

(CPSE 402) Believe the reviews for Professor Smith. The most disorganized, frustrating class I've had at BYU. I spent all my time jumping through hoops and hoping I met invisible rubric standards. She changed her mind frequently and didn't know how to use LS. Lectures weren't planned and were rarely useful. Take this class from someone else.

Very disorganized and she didn't take ownership of the class(CPSE 402). Feedback rare and unhelpful when there. She would put in 0s before grading anything, making it hard to see progress. She tried to guilt trip the class into doing extra work that wouldn't count for our grade, & was upset when no one came to a class she'd canceled the week before

She seems disorganized and lacks clarity in her teaching, frequently changing rubrics after assignments are submitted, which makes meeting expectations hard. Her grading is harsh, and feedback is unhelpful/not given. I have not gained anything from the class due to poor communication and awareness of discrepancies in course material.

I've taken a couple of classes from Barb and she hasn't been the best professor, but I actually enjoyed her class this semester. She is a tough grader and her study guides are not helpful, but I could tell that she was trying to improve and trying to show that she cared about us and the class. She did provide us with good opportunities to learn.

This professor is a very kind lady but most lecture time is field trips or watching videos, so instruction comes from the textbook. Exam study guides are extremely vague, and assignment descriptions often are as well. She is a tough grader. I was often frustrated and it was difficult to receive the grade that I did.

Not a good class at all. Very unclear rubrics that do not match up well with the instructions. She seemed nice but I never met her with it being online. So much group work which is difficult for an online class. Overall, this was closer to a 3-4 hour credit class than a 2 credit hour with the amount of work given each week.

The online version of this class was needlessly difficult not in terms of understanding the material but in the amount of work. The last weekly module was about an hour to an hour and half longer than the other weeks and was due on Thursday instead of Saturday. Lots of small projects so get ready for that. Maybe the in person class is better?

Can't rate Professor Smith specifically because I took the class online and we didn't interact much with the her. She's nice, just didn't really get to know her. The class is a lot. No tests, but there are a lot of assignments and group work to complete. It's manageable but you'll definitely have to put in the time.

This was hands down the worst professor and class I have ever taken at BYU. The class was full of SO MUCH busy work. It says it is a 2.0 credit hour class, but from Barbara, it is 4.0. She is so accommodating (no help)and she and her TA were impossible to get in contact with (which is ridiculous online) Not to mention like 10 group projects total.

I've had Barbara as a professor for three classes now. She is difficult to work with, assigns so much busy work, is not accommodating, and does not seem to know the content that she is teaching. It's relatively easy to pass the class, but she does not like to give 100s on things (without giving feedback/reasoning for why).

I loved and hated this class. It was difficult to know the exact information we were supposed to learn. The definitions and concepts seemed to always be changing and I had a hard time keeping up. I loved it though because it furthur deepened my love of teaching and working with exceptional children.

This class was so much work for a 2 credit class in my opinion. You teach yourself from the textbook and attend class for attendance. You take a quiz on the chapter you read every week, there is a lot of material and you have no idea what to pay attention for the quiz. Luckily you can retake the quiz.

This class is terribly unorganized and seems like she is constantly trying to find ways to dock points with no feedback. Lots of readings with specific quizzes, 10 volunteer hours required (hard to get in spring semester), and lectures are basically a review of readings. For a class focused on accommodations, she wasn't very willing to accommodate.

Not an awful professor but she was very unorganized from the beginning and although she adjusted due dates some days had a unnecessary heavy workload. Participation is super important and she will emphasize it quite often. Tough grader and will never give you feedback on anything. If possible take from another professor.

Learning Suite wasn't ever accurate, so definitely important to go to class! I personally didn't mind her quirks, but it was frustrating to not have clear expectations. She seemed like she wanted to improve as a teacher and moved due dates when we mentioned the workload was heavy. Not a bad class but might have been easier with a different teacher.

Overreaching, uneducated, unhelpful, disorganized, everything wrong with the current state of higher education. Teacher needs a reality check on how little the students respect her.

BYU, please read these reviews and get rid of teachers who have no respect for the upcoming generation.

Professor Smith knows her stuff, but is not very approachable. She is willing to work with you, but doesn't give you that much help. This class involved volunteer hours, which was really cool. Field trips were also really cool, but the lectures were pointless. Her tests were kind of random. I wouldn't take her agani except for the volunteer hours.

Professor Smith definitely requires participation and attendance. Volunteer hours are required which is a lot of work, but it is also super awesome -- probably the best part of the class. Her lectures didn't feel very helpful, but she knows her stuff for sure.

I really liked this class. She is a tough grader. It's an intro class and more than half got below a B (maybe 2 A's). She loves sped and knows so much. Her tests are very specific and challenging. You will read the whole text book the first 1/2 of the semester. The field experience is life-changing. Attendance and participate affect your grade!

This class was way too difficult for only 2 credits. There are weekly reading quizzes that ask for the most specific details but are closed book/note. Half of the time the assignments aren't even on the schedule and then she takes off points for the smallest things. On top of that, so much time was wasted in lectures. Take from someone else PLEASE

This was the most disorganized class I've ever taken. The weekly reading quizzes are near impossible asking for specific details when they're closed note. She takes off points for the smallest things and doesn't make it clear why you lost points. Felt like a lot of time was wasted in lectures. A ton of work for only a 2 credit class.

Honestly ridiculous. I paid $1000 for a class where the teacher talked about church half of the time and had to learn everything myself by reading the textbook. Honestly, it was so disorganized and the assignments are graded with expectations that are unclear. I would do anything you can to take this class from a different professor.
Barb is a very nice lady. Most disorganized class ever, it was ridiculous haha

Dr. Smith is nice, but this class is SO disorganized! And the grading criteria is very unclear. She'd have assignments due that weren't even on the schedule, so it was very easy to miss assignments and get docked lots of points. Her quizzes were also extremely specific and unnecessarily difficult. If its possible, take from a different professor.

Professor Smith is a nice enough person, but her class was ridiculous. She had no clear grading criteria and it was nearly impossible to get an A (her cutoff was 95% and she docked points for the most random things). The class was disorganized (no units or tests, just whatever random thing she wanted to talk about) and lectures were pointless

Prof. Smith is a good professor and is very flexible when it comes to grading. Sometimes that can make it difficult to know when an assignment is due. Her class is fairly easy if you pay attention in class and turn in assignments. There is a lot of reading but it is manageable.

Barbara Smith is the worst professor I have ever had. She taught the same material over and over again: direct/explicit instruction. Which is ONE teaching method. Even though as teachers we need to know a wide variety of teaching methods to accommodate for each student's learning style. She is also rude to you when you suggest other lessons.

She is a very nice lady, but as a teacher, I can honestly say I have never been more frustrated with a professor. Her teaching style is that she really doesn't have one and she just talks at you and it is hard to retain information that you actually need to know. Honestly, if I wasn't set in my decision to be in SPED, I would not be in this major.

Sister Smith is a nice lady when you do what she wants. She does not take attendance, but if you do not go to her class, you'll get on her bad side and she'll grade you unfairly. The class is pretty interesting though.

Nice woman but a little bit scatterbrained. Super easy class as long as you do the readings and turn the assignments in on time. Lectures can be very boring sometimes but it's such an easy grade that it's not that big of a deal.
The class organization was a mess. Sister Smith has good intentions but when you get on her bad side you'll stay there for ever.
Sweetest woman ever. She is so loving and spiritual and wants to help everyone. She is also very understanding about deadlines and grades leniently as long as you do what is asked. No tests! Easy A!
The class was a great start into the Special Education program.  Sister Smith is great!
She means well, but probably should participate in some professional development workshops.

A pretty typical Physical Science class. Honestly what matters more than the professor is your TA and really understanding the textbook. Professor Bickmore does a good job answering questions but the rest of his lectures are unimportant if you do the homework and other assignments.

I enjoyed taking physical science from Professor Bickmore. There are chapter assignments and weekly articles but nothing unreasonable. On most assignments excluding tests you have multiple attempts to get the right answer which helps greatly with learning. He explains the concepts well enough, so as long as you read the textbook you'll do fine.

Mr Bickmore knows all the lectures but in my opinion he is not the best at explaining them.  He is like any average college teacher: cares about the lecture but not too much about how students are doing. Bring your i clicker always to class and make sure you take photos to all the ppt slides.

Dr. Bickmore is a good guy and has great intentions, but his lectures are quite dry. It feels like he just begins lecturing before the students even realize what's going on, and then he just breezes through things quickly. The class overall isn't too hard, but there is a lot of reading. 4 midterms and a final. I took it Spring term and survived!

I will be honest. Avoid taking this professor. With all love and respect, his lectures are dry, boring, and confusing. He's a great person with a great heart, but his teaching style makes the class even harder. The readings are long and hard, the only way to get an A is by going to the TA lab. Don't suggest doing it in the spring, too fast and hard

I really enjoyed this class. It is difficult and you do have to work to get a good grade. You can bring a notecard to the tests and that is helpful. I felt like he taught the concepts in a way that made a lot of sense and I understood the chemistry concepts from his teaching better than I did when I took a chemistry class.
The course is hard. He makes it very possible to pass if you attend every lecture and you do your part by reading and doing the before class questions.

Brother Bickmore is a pretty good teacher. Kind of goofy and gets on tangents; not extremely clear. Reading is mandatory even tho it probably isn't necessary. Overall, alright teacher but not my first choice.

Dr. Bickmore knows his stuff, and I did learn a lot from his class. There are no outside assignments and he has chances for xtra credit, but his assessment methods were a bit sub-par. Despite what others say, though, the course is survivable.

I did learn a lot in this class, but none from Prof Bickmore.  I had an extremely hard time understanding him and I hardly ever went to class.  I studied a lot with a TA who knew her stuff and got a decent grade.

This class is very difficult for a two credit class. He ends it 2/3 of the way of the semester which is nice. There are quizzes for the reading on blackboard that have a-m choices. Copy the quiz questions because he recycles them for tests. Two finals: one lecture one lab. Lab is identifying rocks, lecture is a 150 question test! Im glad to be done

This class is hard and requires a lot of extra time. Dr.Bickmore is very unhelpful and it feels like he is trying to trick his students. His quizzes and tests have multiple choice options that make the test impossible by having 20 different options. I would highly recommended not taking any classes from him.

The last comment was pretty accurate.  Prof Bickmore is a nice guy but he isnt always clear, his quizzes are tough even though theyre even open book. Also... theres a ton of text book reading. Definitely write down quiz questions (as your taking it) & study from them later.  You can manage an A, just gotta study hardcore & remmeber what youve read

The hardest part about this class was the quizzes. But the test is based on the quizzes, so make sure to copy the quiz questions to study. I thought this was going to be a horrible class, but it just takes effort. It's not an easy A, but it's managable. He does try his best to teach what we need to know though.

The hardest part about this class was the quizzes. But the test is based on the quizzes, so make sure to copy the quiz questions to study. I thought this was going to be a horrible class, but it just takes effort. It's not an easy A, but it's managable. Use his period sheets. Read them before class. He does try his best though.
Iclicker determines attendence. you have to participate in 75% of questions. Everything is online. Tests are semi difficult because the answers are somtimes a-j to choose from

Very frustrating because he is not clear when he explains things. He is a very nice teacher and he is willing to work with you to help you but is just not clear. A quiz every week on blackboard. The test is on blackboard with unlimited time. On tests and quizzes have a, b, c, d, a and a, a b and c but not d...it's so confusing!

This class was the worst I have taken at BYU. It was worse than Am Heritage. He blames his poor teaching skills on the fact that he is ADHD, tries as hard as he can to trick you on his huge tests, and relishes in his multiple choice questions that include options A thru R. Terrible experience, learned nothing but lessons in how to be a bad teacher.

This class was the worst class I have ever taken. Tests were ridiculously hard and he admittedly prides himself in trying to throw you off by putting letters a-m and making up words on tests. He is extremely immature and loves rocks a little too much. The lab was ok as long as you get lucky and get a good TA. Lectures were so boring

This was my absolutely best class this semester.  If you are interested in really learning about geology then this is the class to take.  The tests were difficult, but this is what made the class valuable.  I learned more about effective teaching from watching Dr. Bickmore teach.  He is fair, cares, and listens to his students. Real quality.

This guy should not be allowed to teach- his exams are really hard and the workload is unreasonable for a 2 credit class. He knows that everyone hates him and hates the class, but he doesn't change anything. I feel sorry for anyone who has to take this class.
Worst teacher I have ever had. He writes multiple choice questions with letters A-T, and he thinks that it helps you learn. AVOID him if at all possible.

Horrible teacher. He thinks he's funny and tries to be "cool" so people will like him... doesn't work. He shouldn't be allowed to use blackboard - he never posts when a quiz/exam opens or closes, and the exams are ridiculously hard, quizzes are even harer sometimes. One of the worst classes I have ever taken.

This class is ridiculous. His lectures are worthless, his quizzes and exams are written poorly - probably one of the worst teachers I've ever had. He prides himself on writing quiz/exam questions that trick you (he openly admits this). He should not be teaching. Yet another example of how a smart person IS NOT necessarily qualified to be a teacher.

booorrring class. I didn't go to class at all and pulled of a good grade. I just did the reading, learned his concept maps, knew the answers to the review questions both in the book and on his review sheets. Really do the reading, it helps a lot. Don't waste your time going to class, all notes are online anyway.

This professor borders on the ridiculous.  His language resembles that of a badly brought up twelve-year-old: childish, even crude.  The concept maps were helpful to me, but many of my classmates complained a lot about them.  Lectures are nearly useless--he can't explain things well at all.  I learned almost everything from the textbook.

Very good professor, but vague in letting you know what to study for test. I studied very hard and got Bs on all the tests. A study guide would be helpful, but the review sheets work ALMOST as well. The mini-lesson is fun. Make sure you study for the rock final, too. My TA's default answer was "I don't know," so labs were sort of useless.
This class is really boring. The lectures are not helpful at all. The book teaches you what you need to know for tests. The labs were fine.

If you can avoid him I suggest it.  Loves doing concept maps, but tests are really hard.  Lab isn't too bad, but lecture is really boring and shows pictures but doesn't explain the process of disaster very well.

This professor is the biggest bonehead ever.  He is completely unhelpful to the students because he is too busy being a stand up comedian in class.  His assignments are stupid, and he is kind of unfair; the information he tests you on is not even on chapters he tells you to study.  All I can say is I am sorry to all that has to take his class!

Aviod him at all costs.  Going to class is a watse of time. The book is your only help and it's not good at all.  Tries way too hard to be funny.  No study guides.  Teaches like we are the ones in elementary school, not the teachers.  Good luck with him.

Wow.  Horrible class.  Worst I've had at BYU.  Changed the syllabus 4 times during the semester.  Doesn't teach concepts clearly.  I might as well have taught this course to myself.  He doesn't focus enough time on what you are being tested on & doing projects on.  If you are elem ed take regular physical science then do the lab seperately.  J

Pretty much, no one has a clue what Prof. Bickmore is talking about.  He goes off on tangents, and his jokes are really lame.  If you want a class that you are going to dread going to, then take Physical Science 110 B.
good overall
I thought he was really nice, but he tried too hard to be funny, rather than helpful.  His tests were ridiculous and completely unreasonable, and his grading system is very poor.

Prof. Bickmore just didn't do it for me. He was extremely nice, but really just tried to be funny.  His lectures were mostly pictures, which helped none. His tests had nothing to do with the lectures. I wish he went over the material more. He does know his stuff, you just have to get it out of him.

I read everything and I thought the tests were reasonable.  I thought the book was pretty good.  Don't waste your money buying the experiments for kids book - you don't use it at all.  I thought this class was more interesting than 110A.  You can choose your attitude about this class though...

A lot of people in our class liked him, but I found Dr. Bickmore nice but annoying and somewhat immature. His lecture material never had much to do with his tests, and he spent the whole lecture just trying to be funny and entertaining. So I guess if you like that, get him, but I really didn't learn much and continually dreaded this class.

He is a great teacher. Lectures are always interesting and he tries to keep it lively. Labs can be boring. Start studying for the rock final early and make sure to go in and study the rocks. The tests are kind of hard and very long. There isn't a study guide, but make sure to do the book work.

The class is very easy. Just read occasionally and go to lecture and lab and everything will be fine. Dr. Bickmore isn't always fair though. I got earned an A in the class but got bumped down to a B- because I was late to the elementary school. Be careful who you work with on the group project because they have a say in your grade.
This class was very easy.  Geology is kind of boring, but Dr. Bickmore did his best to make it interesting.  The tests were easy as long as you went to class.
The tests were easy if you studied the study guide.  Labs were really boring.  Class was really boring.  Dr. Bickmore is nice though.
this was probably the easiet class i have every taken.  The tests were so stinking easy I felt like I was cheating the system.

If you like licking rocks, take this class. Its not super hard, and he makes it kind of interesting sometimes. Then again, sometimes its boring and you go to sleep. Lab is ridiculous and unnecessary, but you have to go cuz its a big chunk of your grade. Study and you'll do fine.
Tests were hard. Lectures okay. He is kind of wierd. Labs were easy. Lots of busy work.
