Class wasn't difficult but when I became ill and needed to talk to him about homework he treated me like he had better things to do then help me.
he is a funny guy... test are kinda hard but all you have to do is put in your time.. but labs are ridiculously easy.. just show up and turn in your work adn that parts done
tests are hard, but the labs aren't.  I would have done better if I had put more effort in to the class, but he is helpful if you go talk to him.
He had fun assignments that made learning about geology worth while.  He made the study of really boring rocks, kinda fun.
Class can be a bit too easy at times. He is very helpful, if you have any trouble in the course just go talk to him. Very nice.

Prof. Bounous was a solid voice teacher but he tended to get distracted and use up time in the short lessons. If you pay attention to the weekly reflections on performances, you'll pass. However, if you aren't exactly sure why you are taking these lessons (like for an audition or for certain songs), it might be a waste of your time.

This man has a lot of experience and you can tell he loves his job. His tips and guidance are helpful and taking his class helped me to improve my range and taught me how to practice productively. He does sometimes go off on unrelated tangents. Watch out for those and do your best to redirect them.

Great guy, really knows his stuff and knows how to help you improve as a singer. Of course the amount of improvement that occurs depends on your out of class practice. Only downside is that he can spend a lot of the 30 min class time talking instead of having you sing and analyzing.  Worth of the class depends on time spent outside practicing.

I had a really, really difficult semester and Dr. Bounous was very understanding and helpful and cared about how things were going with me. I don't know if I would have survived the semester without his help.

Dr. Bounous is a lot of fun. He really helped develop my voice this semester. He's also great with Italian lyrics because he served in Italy. My only issue with him is that he talk A LOT. Sometimes he'd take up half the lesson with small talk, leaving 10 minutes to warm up and 5 to actually sing a song for him. Overall recommend him
Brother Bounous is very knowledgeable, talented, and encouraging.  He listens to your singing preferences and interests and helps you reach your goals.  And he looks like Geoffrey Rush.  :)

I took Barry as my voice teacher in 1995-96. I very much enjoyed having him. I believe he taught me in a way that other voice teachers did not to free my voice and present myself. He seemed to be more interested in me than in himself or in the music itself. I very much enjoyed working with him and still learn from some of my tapes of the lessons.

Very forgiving and helpful voice teacher.  Enthusiastic about helping everyone to achieve their best performance.  Spends a lot of time trying to find ways to explain technique in a way that will help the student.  I have worked with this teacher for more than 4 years and my confidence, and ability has increased dramatically in this time.

Nice guy. he DOES talk alot, but hey, i'm only a minor and voice isnt my focus. I was nervous to have to sing in front of him, but he's really easy going and not very critical (but he IS helpful) it turned into a really stress-relieving class.

Not a bad teacher. Knows the male voice really well and works well with others. The only problem is that he talks way too much. If you take from him, be assertive and don't let him go on and on because he will if you don't stop him. Out of my 30 min weekly lesson I sang for maybe 10-15.

A nice guy, but tends to spend most of the rehearsal talking.  Of the 30 minutes, I would maybe sing for 15.  He does a good job of telling you what you need to do to improve your voice, but he isn't really clear on HOW to do it.  He was, however, very helpful in selecting music in preparing for the School of Music auditions.
kinda long-winded sometimes, but he definitely gives helpful criticism...i'd take the class from him again.

I'm not a music major, so I feel like he didn't care. I would sing something TERRIBLY, and he would just say "pretty good, pretty good." It got really annoying, he didn't push me at all. He has a lot of good insights, but he can't just say something, he has to go into this long explanation, so the most I ever sang was 10 min of  the 30-min lesson.

This was a private lesson-type class, 30 min./week.  He's good at identifying what you need to improve and giving you precise suggestions on how to achieve it.  Nice guy, but he does like to talk and express himself, which can be a drawback if you only have 30 min./week.
did okay with him, didn't make a ton of progress, but he does have some good stuff to share
Pretty good class.  It was tough to get the 2 hours of practice a week he wants, though.  And if you're scared of singing in front of people, it may not be for you, we did that a lot.

One of my least favorite teachers.  Would grade assignments labeled as "rough drafts" as if it was our final submission, and would take points off for stuff that was just his own opinion.  Whenever I emailed him I never got a response back.  Wish I coulda taken it from someone else, but he was and probably still will be the only option

CHEM 391 was an entirely different experience than CHEM 381M. The technical writing course is co-taught and is so different. Lecture is important, but your paper is most important. Good feedback is given by professors and peers. Don't be afraid of taking 391 from him!

This class was rough. He wasn't my favorite lecturer because of all the vocabulary he used. There was a TON of material that we had to know in ridiculous detail to do well on homework and exams, which made it feel like I couldn't humanly do well. Grading is harsh. If I don't pass, I'll probably try the nonmajor section with a different professor.

Dr. Willardson is a great professor! When teaching the biochemistry majors, he explains things very clearly, and I learned more from his class than any other class this semester. His tests are challenging, but he makes sure that the class is curved so that an average grade is a B. He's nice, and going to his classes is very engaging and enjoyable!

Dr. Willardson was insulting, he mocked me for my appearance on more than one occasion and he made everyone feel stupid constantly. When asked how to prepare for exams, his response would be "know the material" and each exam was ludicrously difficult. Take 481 from ANYONE but him.

This class covers A TON of material, and he would not give you any hints as to what to expect on the test, so his class was pretty tough. Because it covers so much, he was not an expert on every subject. If you think you're smarter than him, he gets frustrated. Advice: Stay up to date on the topic you're discussing. Test time will come fast.

I agree that he is generally unapproachable.  He can be quite rude and unhelpful.  Sometimes he is very helpful, but generally not.  He tries to make the class easier to navigate but doesn't do a very good job.  Not very organized either.  He's a nice enough guy, though.
One of the most rude and unapproachful professors I have ever met. He's the kind of professor that you never want to ask a question to during class.
I dont agree with the other post on here. He was really nice to me. It is supposed to be a hard class. I think he was fair and helpful and knew what he was talking about. I

Dr. Willardson is extremely unhelpful.  When approached he is openly rude.  Most notably he has a juvenile temper that flares up at the most inconsequential things.  Sad to see professors with such an attitude.. especially at BYU.

This is for math 213. Dr. Paulsen taught very clearly. When exams came around, there were no surprises. Everything on the exam had been covered in class. There is a lot of homework, but it really reinforces the material and is good preparation. Dr. Paulsen was accessible outside of class, and was willing to stay late to answer questions.

Dr. Paulsen cares about her students and is very passionate about math. She moves quickly during lectures, but if you take good notes and study for the tests, you'll do well. The homework each week is easy to get 100% on since you get unlimited attempts, so you just have to focus on the tests. She curved them all, so that helped too.

I felt I just don't learn the way she teaches. Like you're writing the entire class. I don't hear a thing when I'm writing. The way the class is structured is you just go over example problems for the homework, which isn't a bad way to do things. I just felt if we had a packet of the example questions a guy like me could listen and learn.

She cares so much. I struggle with math; I always have. Of course, I struggled in her class. The difference was that she took an extra hour after every class to keep teaching me until I understood the material. This was the first class that I actually felt like I was following along and able to understand what was happening. She is wonderful!

Becky was the best math professor I have ever had!! I am not someone who is good at math by nature and was really nervous to take her class because I had not taken math in a long time, but she was so accessible outside of class times, loved when students asked questions, and gave us so many opportunities to practice.
Becky is a very good teacher and knows her stuff. She cares a lot about her students and teaches very well. I would 100% take from her.

She's an awesome teacher; take her class if you can. Lectures are dense, and she moves fast, so pay attention. The final was hard, so she curved it, added a ton of points to all the grades, and dropped the grading scale by 1% so everyone could keep their grade. This single-handedly saved nearly 100 A/A-s in the class. Awesome teacher, learned a ton

I don't know where these 5's are coming from. She is easily one of the worst teachers I've ever had. She does not care for her students. She doesn't leave pauses in her lectures for questions. It's a rush job every time, she goes over the most important parts of the lecture 5 minutes after class is over. Her TA's are equally as bad. Save yourself.

Becky was amazing and really cares about you succeeding. She is willing to meet with you if you need help! The tests are hard and in the testing center, but if you suck at math, she is the one to pick because she works with you!

I took MATH 110  
   At first I was a bit nervous taking the class from her because she had made a few mistakes in her math but it turned out alright. 
   If you actually do the homework like you are supposed to and try to learn it instead of just getting through it, you will succeed.

Becky is so accommodating! I had an accident, and she gave me so many extensions on homework, exams, and the final. She is willing to work with you and go over any problems you have. No extra credit, however, your grade gets curved a little bit at the end depending on how well you do on the final. Lectures are clear and covered the weekly homework.

I love Mrs. Becky! Genuinely such a caring and enthusiastic teacher, which matters a lot to me since I've never liked math at all. She made each lecture bearable and although there was a bit of homework, was lenient on handing out extensions that made them due whenever the next exam was. I could tell she loved her job, and her students!

She is a great professor, all the assignments gave you unlimited attempts on every question so you get 100 on all of them which was great and the exams were exactly what you would expect based on the study guides she gave us. She is very nice and had straightforward lectures.

I went on rate my professor to know which teacher to take for math 110. everyone suggested professor Paulsen. I'm so glad I chose her class. I am not good at math. however it was a pre- requisite for PSYCH. She would meet with me twice a week to have one on one math tutoring to help me be successful and pass the exams! no one I would recommend more

She's actually a boss. Also, this is for Math 110. There's 2 labs every week where participation matters but you just do a super easy worksheet and then you can work on your homework. Tests are pretty easy.

THIS IS FOR MATH110 not 112. Professor Paulsen is a great teacher! She cares a lot about her students and will go out of her way to help you succeed! Class isn't too hard, it's not brain-dead easy or anything you still need to attend, study, and give it your best but in the end it's very reasonable to get an A!

If you need calc, don't hesitate to take from Becky. This class was a ton of fun, especially for a math class. She's personable and caring, but also a great teacher. Easy to get help outside of class. Very understanding. Learned so much from her. You won't regret choosing Becky.

Becky is the best math teacher I've ever had! I only got to take Calc 1 from her because her teaching schedule didn't line up with when I was taking my other math classes. If you have the chance, take a class from Becky! You will not regret it!

Dr Crosby is amazing! Not only is he a genuinely good guy who wants to help his students, but he gives incredible feedback. This class has two majorly stressful assignments due in the middle of the semester, but once you get past those, the class calms down a ton! This class seriously helped me become a better orator!

Professor Crosby was one of my favorite professors at BYU. He taught an amazing class, and cared about his students. He was even willing to help me review my personal statement for medical school outside of class. He is awesome and take him if you can!

Professor Crosby is amazing.  I took UNIV 101 with him, and his lectures were always relevant, and geared toward preparing us for university level work.  He made a special emphasis on presentation, which was excellent and made class engaging.  I still remember the things I learned in his class, which help to this day.  Great professor, 10/10!
My sensei 🙏

Ben Crosby is a fantastic professor. He is passionate about the source material and explains it in a way that is easy to understand. His expectations and communications are incredibly clear and concise, and he is very reasonable about expecting your best work, but not ever overdoing it. He cares so much about his students and knows how to teach.

Dr. Crosby does an incredible job helping you practice skills. He gives great feedback and KNOWS what he is talking about. Taking this class will help you so much in your efforts to become a better communicator and public speaker.

Prof Crosby's class was great! Tests were never too difficult, papers were set up well and fairly graded. a few group projects, but he did what he could to make sure your grade doesn't suffer if your group wasn't helpful. He's passionate about what he teaches, teaches it clearly with lots of examples and practice.

I really liked Professor Crosby's class. It was super interesting and he always gave us good feedback. Most of the classwork was group projects but we were graded for our individual effort, which was nice. It was sometimes hard to get in touch with him outside of class and he was a little disorganized but he was super helpful when he did respond.

I sincerely enjoyed this class! He seems intimidating but is willing to help you learn. You feel some pressure to do and perform well and as long as you really pay attention in class you should be fine. His tests and assignments felt easy enough and nothing surprised me in questions asked. You just have to try hard in this class.
Professor Crosby cares for his students. This class helped me get out of my comfort zone and become a better public speaker. I would say if you want to excel in this class ask for his help.

Clear passion for subject but this class seemed off his radar most of the semester. Syllabus is clear, unlike the fact that you have the same group for papers/projects the whole semester for better or worse. Long reading assignments, as expected. Also wouldn't acknowledge me on campus, which was weird, especially as he values delivery so much.

Great professor, this class on public speaking took me out of my comfort zone but I've never learned so much about how to present well! My improvement was night and day after his instruction, and it's helped me in more ways than I ever thought. Manageable homework load, mostly graded on some presentations. Definitely recommend!

I am normally not a fan of english or writing classes and was just looking to get a GE out of the way, but Professor Crosby made the class interesting and I honestly enjoyed attending lectures. There were only a few short papers and one group project. The two tests had very clear study guides. Would definitely take again!

I expected this class to just be a boring, general-requirement class, but Prof. Crosby made this class such a joy. I loved the lectures he led, and he made it a great environment for class discussions. He spoke and taught with such respect and knowledge that it became so enjoyable to learn.

Easy A. This class had both a manageable workload and a lot of interesting material. You get to debate in class and work often in a group. You write 2 group papers, and there is a final group project. Tests are open-book, open-note, and open-peer. Professor Crosby cares more that you are learning the material than about your grade in the class.

Professor Crosby is a nice guy. This was supposed to be a persuasive writing class but he kinda turned it into a debate class- we had to give a group debate in front of the class. I learned a lot about debate and verbal persuasion, but honestly not too much about persuasive writing. For a GE credit it wasn't bad, just not what I expected.

He does an incredible job of knowing that this isn't your main class of the semester and the workload was incredibly manageable which was a huge relief. Coursework is blessedly light without feeling like I was missing out on the actual learning experience. He's entertaining to be in class with and feels very real and chill and knowledgeable.

Dr. Crosby cares about his students and created an enjoyable/easy gen ed class. He blends debate and writing which is neat. What prevents me from giving him a 5 is that I didn't feel like my writing improved--we did not turn in a graded, written assignment until near the end of the course. I hope that changes. (This was his 1st year at BYU)

I had this professor for ENGL 322, Fundamentals of Rhetoric. He is awesome!! Very passionate about his subject and is even more caring about his students. Tests are open-book, open-group, and open-Google. Group projects are graded individually, so if you're stuck with a lame group you can still get an A on your part.

Dr. Gibbs is a pretty good professor, but a lot of the content you are tested on is all based on his own research/opinions/experiences, which I don't love. But the content is really great and will help you see different perspectives!

He loves his students so much! Readings aren't very long, gives detailed reviews before the midterm & final (literally tells you explicitly what is on the test and what he's looking for). Lectures are very engaging, he tries to help everyone have a chance to participate. Not a sociology major but loved this class; I'd recommend Gibbs to anyone.
Professor is alright, makes you learn ideals that don't align with BYU at all. TAs right now are REALLY bad, slow grading and a bunch of nonsense taken off.

I'll be honest... I started off hating this class. But once I got used to it, it was very interesting and enjoyable. There is a little bit of busy work that takes time, but overall, I have come to love this class. TAKE SOC 111 online from him! It's a great class.
Is unable to admit mistakes and take responsibility. Whole class hinges on essay. There is textbook reading which is remarkably unnecessary and there is no need to do it.

Guys! If you are taking SOL 111 take it from Professor Gibbs. He is so engaging and his lectures are awesome. I am not super into sociology, however his class changed the way I see the world. Work load is totally manageable and the tests were easy. He incorporated fun guest speakers and did a great job of relating the class back to the gospel!

Nothing to say about the teacher or any of the lectures because I never watched a single video all year. You will have to record 2, 1-3 minute response videos every week though which is really annoying and doesn't add any value to the class. All you have to do for an A is listen to the review video, and read the study guide the day before the test.

Dr. Gibbs is incredibly well-connected and can give you the resources and ability to succeed at BYU. Building a relationship with him can be incredibly valuable, and he makes it easy to do so! The organization of this class is pretty basic, but the lectures and readings truly provide you with the opportunity to start looking at things differently.

Kind of a tacky course setup, to be honest. It is clearly intended to cater towards newer students, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. Material is very very easy, just review the study guide for exams. There are many Marco Polo assignments (basically video recorded discussion posts), I was not a fan of those. Just a lot of busywork but easy.

Class is pretty easy and straightforward. Be prepared for a lot of busywork. Make sure to study the study guide thoroughly and know the terms discussed in the guide. If you do that, you will get a guaranteed A.

Dr. Gibbs, even in the context of amazing BYU professors, really stands out. He has a passion, excitement, charisma that is really unmatched. Class was intellectually and emotionally stimulating and often very funny (Gibbs could moonlight as a standup comedian for sure). Far and away the best lecturer I've had in school.

Singlehandedly the best UNIV 101 professor at BYU. Very inspired guy that genuinely cares about ALL his students and their futures. He made my very first semester at college way less stressful. He knows the resources we need to be successful in all our classes and our futures. HIGHLY RECOMMEND IF YOU WANT LESS STRESS! HE EVEN HAS A YURT! :D

Ben is one of the most amazing people I know! His class is very insightful. He not only knows how to teach what he teaches, but he is passionate about it and helps you find purpose in what your doing.

Ben is my all time favorite professor. I can't say how much his ideas shaped me and my love for sociology. Beyond that, he's the only professor I've ever had that went out of his way to say hi and chat with me when he saw me, which he does for all his students. I just loved loved this class and couldn't recommend taking a class from Ben more.

I don't care who you are, what your major is , or what you have in mind for you classes. You have to take a class by Ben Gibbs. It will be a truly amazing experience. He will make you laugh, and he will teach you so many things. Such an amazing professor.

Changed my life. His lectures are so honest, so pure, and so genuine. He explores the world in a way to truly give you a new more compassionate perspective. Sometimes instructions are not clear, but nothing could make me not recommend this class, or tell you to not take a class from professor Gibbs. I recommend this class so so much!

Prof. Gibbs is a really funny and caring professor. However, this was the first time in years he taught Soc of Education and it was SUPER unorganized. He changed assignments and due dates constantly. Also, we did a research-based group project for most of the semester. So if you don't like group-work this isn't the class for you.

This class was absolutely amazing. Ben is so inspiring and gives the most amazing lectures. He genuinely cares for each student. This class was difficult and has a lot of reading and big papers, but it was so worth it and there was never any busy work. I got so much out of this class and from Ben, and more than just about sociology.

Ben is an amazing scholar and a great teacher! I decided to take his class after he was a substitute in another SOC class I took. You can tell right away that he knows what he's talking about; he's done a lot of research. His class is hard, you have to read about 3 books and some extra readings, but it pays off in the knowledge you gain.

Gibbs is both a good person and a good professor, which is such a winning combination. There's a lot of class participation and not a lot of lecturing. But even if you're the shy type (which I am), Gibbs makes participating easy and debate among classmates enjoyable and friendly. He clearly cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Professor Gibbs is an incredible man.  He has so much love in his heart for the people around him, and that's what makes him such a powerful sociology professor.  He has taught me how to see others in a kinder, more caring light, and inspired me to do something about it.  Truly inspirational class, I would highly recommend.  SOC112 forever!!
He is an amazing person and shows it through his lectures. Really cares about the material and his students. Wish I took all my classes frmo him.

Ben is a great professor, especially for this class. He handles all social problems in a way that doesn't offend but speaks the truth about the issues. He is very easy to get in touch with or talk to face to face. He is willing to adjust the course if he is given any feedback. Daily homework is some easy reading and a quiz before each class. EASY A
SUUPPER AWESOME!! Ben Gibbs is hillarious. love the subject material, loved discussion.

Gibbs is a very passionate teacher with a great sense of humor and tender heart. He will go out of his way if necessary to help you. Class requires that you read 4 books and comprehend well (2 page summaries and a huge final paper). Don't procrastinate submitting your reading dialogues. Missing them will slowly eat away at your chances of an A.

Great teacher really cares about the things he teaches! This has been my favorite class so far! He really brings a deeper meaning to the class and always ready and willing to help students out. Do the reading it's worth it and will make sense at the end of the class. I think just being in this class makes you a better person!
Professor Gibbs clearly cares about his students and is willing to help you be successful in his class.

This class was challenging, but enjoyable and well worth my time. Professor Gibbs respects all viewpoints and is clearly passionate about what he teaches. I would recommend any of his classes as he is one of my very favorite professors. But, prepare to work hard; you are in college after all.

I took this class for fun and it was not fun at all. Really wish I hadn't taken it. He treats us like grad students- the reading load and work load are insane. His power points are not clear and if you miss class you will have no idea what's going on. Really harsh grader on papers, and tests are impossible to study for.

Favorite class and favorite professor ever. Hands down. Ben isn't like other soc professors; he makes you care about what you're studying because you know HE cares a lot. Lectures are great and although some assignments/papers were tough and stretched you, it's a capstone class so that's expected. He's ALWAYS willing to help/talk outside of class.

I had hear good things about Gibbs and they are all true. The capstone project is HARD so make sure you put a ton of effort into it. He's occasionally confusing with assignments. But he's an amazing lecturer that makes you think about the world. The class changed my life.

Ben Gibbs is a great professor. He is super passionate and interested in inequality in society. This class is very interesting and has many topics, so you don't get bored. Ben helps you out if you need it. Also, he's very attractive. Overall, one of my favorite sociology classes ever.

Ben is a great teacher and person. He really cares about the issues in the class subject matter and wants all students to be conversant with the ineqaulity literature. 422 was one of the most insightful classes of my college career. That said this was one of the most difficult class I've had in  the major. There is a ton of reading and writing

Great, funny, interactive lectures that still get the material across.  Updates his tests depending on what he covered in class.  Gives out specific study guides based on the slides.  Lets you know the exam essays ahead of time.  Do the reading every time and participate in the Discussion Board, and you should be fine.
This class is so much reading! He is a nice guy, but isn't very interested in helping you out. Says a lot to just look in the book. Wouldn't recommend this teacher

Kind of a high and mighty guy. Assigns way too much reading which is pretty obvious material that he just goes over in class anyways. If you want less idol worship and less reading, get a different teacher.

Interesting class for sure, but WAY TOO MUCH reading. Anticipate 8+ hours of reading/wk. He is nice, but useless in his office hours. Does not care about students at all. He makes you feel like you wasted his time coming to see him, so don't expect a lot of useful help from him. Other than that he's interactive and interesting as a professor.

Awesome discussions. Great insights. Loved when we talked about the "big" issue. You will walk out of class every day a changed person. Last day of class he brought us all "hugs" which are really small juice bottles. He loves sociology and his students--I definitively recommend him. Sign up! DO NOT hesitate!!!
Fun class and one I've learned the most in.

Ben is exactly what a professor should be. Engaged, funny, helpful, and passionate. You will learn so much about how to look at the world in a completely different way, a way of compassion. Sociology helps you see things as they are. Take as many classes as you can from him. You won't regret it!

Ben is the best professor I've had in college. He's passionate about his work, and he's passionate about helping his students become the best they can be -regardless of their major. We read a lot and had great discussions. He and his T.A.s are extremely helpful; be sure to do the study guides for the tests and read; you'll do great. AWESOME class!

I loved his class. He is a great lecturer and has realistic expectations for his students. There is a large group project, but it's fun. The 3 tests were moderately hard, but I thought his class was really interesting and he prepares you well for all assignments/tests. Very approachable. Passionate about the subject and about helping students.

You learn some very good things in this class. I enjoyed the class but there is quite a heavy workload and the papers and tests are graded quite harshly. He makes you earn your grade. I did enjoy the class and feel you discuss very important issues. He is a great teacher with a good sense of humor but he is still quite hard.

Ben is one of the best professors I've had. He will help you out in anything, he is so comprehensive with his students. His lectures are so well prepared and makes them interesting,For test hi gives out a study sheet with around 50 questions or so, you go to the review and will get them answered and the test comes out of them. hot guy!

Ben is one of the best professors I have had at BYU! He is truly interested in the subject and he is more than willing to work with students! If you complete the assignments and follow the study guides your grade should be fine.

Great teacher.  He is passionate about his work and he really cares about his students.  He's also pretty young, so I feel like he understands the studnets better.  That and he never shares or enforces his opinions.

He is a really fun guy and he is really helpful. The tests are not easy and you do have to do all the readings or you will  bomb the quizzes. The projects and essays were all easy and I actually had fun with a photo project that he does. All in all, he is a great guy and a great teacher. He almost got me to like Sociology... almost.
Great professor, awesome class.

Best new professor at BYU. Will do anything for his students, including mentoring them in other projects outside of class. His tests can be iffy, but his class is an awesome experience that I would recommend to anyone.

Ben is the man. Cares as much about his students as any professor I've ever met. Class was always interesting. His tests are sometimes kooky but everything works out in the end. Great, Great professor!

Feedback from Dr. Hill was misleading at worst and cryptic at best, and spaced in such a way that by the time you get the feedback you need, you don't have time to submit the assignments before the deadline. I had to redo all my sources and ended up submitting half of the assignments late. Thankfully, the TAs are very merciful with extensions.

Hill is perfect for students who have never written a literature review before; otherwise, he is pretty frustrating. The assignments were mostly useful, except for the annotated references. Most assignments contribute to the paper, such as drafts, annotating articles, and understanding APA. Almost everything was graded by the TAs, very easy class.

The whole class is working on one massive paper, but it's spread into chunks throughout the semester so it's totally manageable. Definately a lot of work just reading through papers and synthesizing info, but it's super interesting and I feel like I learned a lot in this class on how to write. Barely interacted with the prof but the TAs were great

This class was very helpful in learning how to write psych papers. Dr. Hill makes sure the assignments all contribute to writing your final paper and goes through the format and planning with you via phone consults so it isn't too difficult. Taking this class online is a good choice because most of it is just writing. Would take this class again!

If you're familiar with APA style already or you like to just do your work independently, I would never recommend this class. I'm sure if you're unfamiliar with the process or you like asking questions, he's a great professor, but for me, it was way too much hand-holding and busy work. Would never take a class from him ever again.

I would totally recommend this class online. Every assignment was helping to write your final literary analysis. The TAs were super helpful and accessible, and Professor Hill was so kind and helpful in writing our papers. Some things were unclear, but the professor and TAs were really understanding

This class was online so I never met with him, but the phone call assigments were so helpful! He basically structures your paper with you so it doesn't feel nearly as intimidating. Also, it is broken up into so many chunks that you are consistently recieving feedback so you cant procrastinate and it is a much smoother writing process.
Graded very heavily on a few things. Expect a major time commitment for only a few assignments.

Dr. Hill was a great choice for this course. He is very caring and willing to help out whenever possible. He did 2 phone consultations to help plan out your paper. The workload is reasonable and the course is organized well. The paper was daunting but planned out in a way that keeps you on track. He is a great choice!

Dr. Hill is very willing to help you when you're confused. He has a couple phone consultations during the semester. I got two assignments mixed up and he was super understanding and was willing to switch some stuff around for me. Some of the criteria was a little unclear, so don't be afraid to email him with follow up questions.

A lot of assignments that feel like busy work throughout the semester, but they end up helping for the final paper. No tests. Just keep up with the homework and you will get an A. There are 2-3 assignments a week, but most require minimal effort.

There's one big paper that you're working on throughout the whole semester, but the professor talks you through it. He has two phone consultations, and he'll answer any questions and he's super nice. There's also a presentation at the end, but thankfully, he made it so that we could just film a video of us presenting, so it was super easy.

Professor Hill was a sweet guy, but completely out of touch with the psych department. Dr. Hill didn't follow the canvas structure causing confusion about the general writing of the main lit review. He graded the lit reviews off an imaginary rubric he didn't post, and it didn't align with the canvas rubric. Take this class from any other professor.

Waste of time. Time consuming assignments due every day all for a paper that takes you a day to write. Dr. Hill's expectations are completely separate from the online course material. If actual peer-reviewed psychology papers were graded according to the class rubric, they would get no better than a C. Class has nothing to do with the real world.

This class was very easy. I got 100% on almost every assignment, and it's mostly busywork. The class makes the lit review seem not too overwhelming. Only thing is, the online course doesn't really match what Professor Hill wants on the final paper, so make sure to ask him lots of questions and go to the FHSS writing lab they are soooo helpful.

This class was super useful. I took it online which was super great for me, but I heard from people taking his in person class that he was super nice and helpful. I really enjoyed having it online and I interacted a lot more with the TA's than Dr. Hill. However, when I did talk to him about my paper, he was always very helpful and sweet.

I LOVE DR HILL!! Sweetest man you will ever meet in your entire life!! All the bad ratings on this make me wanna cry because he is the best professor you will ever have. He will meet with you over the phone as many times as you need to make sure you get a good grade. Highly recommend Dr Hill for PSY307

This is a class that I recommend taking online than in person. You aren't learning anything new but rather learning how to grow your critical thinking skills. Dr. Hill and his TA are the best and defiantly are available to talk anytime! You work on your literature review all semester, this is a stress-free class, and you get to choose your topic.

In its online form, this is a well-organized class. Prof Hill has a few phone calls with each student to check-in. Assignments help you along the writing process for drafting a full-sized lit review. I loved the emphasis on ministering to the one. Prioritize Hill's criteria over the online material because he'll be the one grading your paper!
This was a great class, I learned so much! I interacted mostly with the TA's. I really liked the online format for this class, it was well organized and straight forward to follow.

Professor Hill was great! Since it was an online class and we mostly spoke with the TAs, there was little time to talk to him, but he had a phone consultation at the beginning of the semester and he was so kind. He really wants you to do well in the class.

As scary as I thought this class would be, it was quite manageable. He even has phone consultations throughout the semester to make sure every student is doing alright. We have one major assignment that you work on for most of the semester little bits at a time and there's lots of guidance. I'm glad I took this course from this professor(:

I love Dr. Hill and will likely go back to him for advice and a good conversation many times throughout my life. Very clear grading expectations, checks in with students over the phone 2-3 times in the semester, makes it easy to complete the 8 page research paper that is really the whole class. Take this class from Dr. Hill!!
Wonderful man. Super kind, and always willing to help out. His class has a good amount of writing in it however it is separated out so you can easily write an 8 page paper.

Dr. Hill is a great guy who will help you if you need help! I had concerns and he was always willing to help me. Although some of the APA styles weren't very clear, I had questions and received clarification from him. I also used quite a bit of outside sources to get help. But If you are willing to ask for help he will help you.

Dr. Hill was amazing for me this semester! I had a bunch of issues this semester, and I still got a B in his class despite them all. He really worked for me and helped me earn a decent grade. Kind. I gave him a 4 because he is only available at late night, like 9. Also, he didn't design the course, but it was honestly horrible. Lots of busy work.

His class is the least amount of work than the other professors to take writing from (just one 15 page paper), yet you will still learn how to be a better writer. Dr. Hill is one of the most loving, kindest people I have ever met. Just study the power points, and the quizzes will be a piece of cake. It's easy to get an A!

Hill gets paid to make you teach yourself APA style, write a ton, and give presentations. Literally teaches nonsense for twenty minutes each class and the rest of the time is student presentations and quizzes that cover the useless material he lectures on. Such a waste of time, but attendance is taken and quizzes are in class..

Quizzes are on the schedule, but never given on scheduled days..... lectures are never useful, only sometimes about writing topics and pointers. Your lit review (the big paper that is the center of the class) deserves attention in class, but never gets it. Brother Hill only babbles about random philosophical things and has students present...
take from someone else, literally anyone else..

Have to be in class for quizzes and attendance (we are in college, hello?). Won't teach you APA 7 even though that's the new thing. Stuck on APA 6, the future is now old man. Nice guy most of the time, but class is useless. 15-20 page paper is the center of the class, but you are on your own with that monster, Dr. Hill will be of no help to you.

Worthless lectures, unrelated to your massive literature review that takes up your life. Lectures don't cover quiz content or help you write your paper. TAs were unhelpful. Ol' Benny Hill doesn't even teach half the time, he has the TAs stumble through teaching and has endless student presentations. Want an A? Gotta teach yourself EVERYTHING.

Although he may not be the best one to take personality from, he is the best for writing! Few assignments and very manageable to get an A. He is also very loving and approachable. I've never felt so cared for by a professor! His writing class is also the least amount of work. Please take!

Professor Hill is possibly the worst professor that I've taken at BYU. His class, layout, teaching style, and content is so disorganized. He's a nice guy, but there is so much reading and videos. The quizzes are the worst part. There are TEN of them throughout the semester, ALL at the TESTING CENTER. Lectures barely line up with quiz content.

Does not give clear expectations for assignments or quizzes, no clue what we are actually supposed to be studying, lecture is philosophical rather than scientific or about the course material. LOTS of out-of-class reading, and that's where the majority of the test material comes from. Heavily recommend against.

Hill is a very sweet man. However, his grading criteria is suspect and unclear. For the final project, the highest grade was a 78%, worth 20% of the grade. Which might be fair if the rubrics were clear, they are not. In fact, he changed the rubric as we were working on it. His class is not about personality either, rather it is pseudo-science.

Dr. Hill is a good person. However, if you hate having to read the professors mind for assignments and quizzes, he is not the professor for you. He is extremely disorganized and his quizzes are really subjective in terms of what he asks. You have to think about what Dr. Hill thinks is the right answer. There is not an objectively correct answer.

I really like Dr. Hill as a person, and that's why I signed up for this class with him. But not much relevance to personality whatsoever, plus there are weekly quizzes in the testing center with questions about minor and irrelevant things. I gave this class as high a rating as I did because I loved how meaningful class discussions were.

I loved this class from Dr. Hill! He is super helpful and I went to him a lot with help on my literature review. He spaces out the due dates so it is very doable to write the paper. He is super sweet and really cares about the students. You have to give a couple of presentations but they are super easy. Highly recommend taking the class from him!

Takes attendance, mostly doesnt until presentations (last couple wks), basically only 10 quizzes, presentation, and a final. 10 quizzes are easy if u read over the slides before taking them. The final is just the quizzes compiled (they give you the answer key) so I memorized and got 100. Easy but talks about random crap NOTHING to do w/ personality

Dr. Hill is a sweet man who will do everything he can to help you get the grade you want. He gives great feedback on your paper. His lectures are disorganized and don't cover everything necessary to do well on the quizzes, but if you go through his class slides online you'll do fine. The APA manual will be your best friend.

Dr. Hill is great, he's definitely willing to help students outside of class time. Although I must say that some of his class periods didn't seem too productive, it was a pretty easy class. He also graded the term paper pretty easily.

Professor doesn't focus on Personality at all. The class is almost entirely focused on religion and abnormal psych. He is poor at communicating his expectations to the students. Some of the quiz questions were borderline ludicrous--for example, he asked what the breed of dog was in a video that he was going to show in class but didn't have time for

The class was listed as Personality, yet that is not what the actual class material covered. It felt more like a review of Psych210 and whatever Dr. Hill found that he needed the class to know more about through his personal lease and opinion. High 300 level class but run like a middle school class. Tells you how to take notes though I'm a senior..

I had taken a different class from Dr. Hill so I was excited, but it became the class I disliked the most. The material often didn't correlate with the class, and it felt more like he had found a soap box for things he thought were interesting, whether or not they were relevant or useful to students or what the course was supposed to be.

Not my favorite class, but awesome professor. Very pleasant and available to talk to. The essay is the big semester project, kinda stressful, but Dr. Hill is helpful. Class time often seemed redundant and a lot of the quiz material didn't seem applicable at all. Quizzes were hard, but he's changing that. Easy to get help when it's needed.

Dr. Hill is by far the best professor I had at BYU! Psych 307 was pretty tough and culminated in a 15+ page research paper but Dr. Hill gave good feedback throughout and was very fair in grading. As a person, he's truly amazing. I've never felt more supported and cared about by a professor on an individual level. So glad I took 307 from Dr. Hill.
Huge group project, but it wasn't too bad. Didn't have clear grading criteria on this. He's a really great guy and a good professor. Lots of deep thinking and deep topics.

Easily one of the greatest teachers I have ever had. I had a lot of health issues this semester and not only was he extremely understanding but went out of his way to make sure I got the help with the class that I needed. The class is completely doable, and he really cares about the personal progress of the students even beyond the class.

For 307 you simply can't go wrong with Dr. Hill. Quiz every week that is not hard, final written directly from quizzes, and of course the 15 page lit review due at the end. Dr. Hill is easily one of the most caring and reasonable professors I have ever had. He really wants to make sure that you succeed and learn how to write well in psychology.

I loved Dr. Hill! He was easily the most available and helpful professor I've ever had! He made sure I totally understood what was expected, answered all my questions, and seriously taught me so much essential information! I would not have taken this class from anyone else! I wouldn't have been able to do it without him!

Dr hill is probably my favorite teacher I have had at BYU. He helped me feel much more confident in my writing and research ability, while giving me clear and humbling feedback which taught me how far I really need to go. He is not easy. And you will have to put in a lot of work. But he gives clear instruction.

He really knows his stuff. I am so glad I took this class. It seems overwhelming but once you realize you should really follow his timelines for the research paper it's not bad at all. By the time it's due, you realize you've written almost the whole paper bit by bit. He's the nicest professor at BYU and the most caring one, too. I love Dr. Hill!!!

You have one major homework assignment all semester. It's a 15 Page research paper. No big deal, super easy. Then there are a few quizzes toward the beginning all taken exactly from his slides. If you pay attention, you'll pass no problem. The final exam is the exact same questions from the quizzes. Dr. Hill is always there for you and AMAZING

Dr. Hill was a good lecturer, but a bad tester. His tests were more concerned with if you memorized the exact wording of quotes used in class or in YouTubes required for the class. Overall, it was not a very difficult course. You need to get a 95 to get an A in the class, which further reflects the inadequacy of his grading. Good guy, bad tests.

Good guy. My main beef with the class really is about the organization; Dr. Hill never used the assigned textbook before class. He hadn't taught a big class,  about 100 students, and fumbled with clarity and consistency.  At the beginning was rough with students opposing his contradictions in class. He tests off off slides and what he says.

Love love love Dr. Hill. I've never met another professor who is as willing to help students succeed. He gets excited about every student's paper, and is super accessible to talk to. My favorite class of the semester.

Dr. Hill is incredible! So sweet, and 110% dedicated to helping you succeed. There's one major paper you write all semester long, and meeting with him is so helpful. He gives great feedback, and what you learn in his class makes the rest of the major SO much easier, it saved my butt in 309 and 310. Recommend him x1000!

Dr. Hill is my favorite. I've taken 307 and 342 pers. from him and am sad that I am unable to take his 3rd class. He is the epitome of what a great therapist should be. He genuinely loves and is interested in his students. Homework load is reasonable and the quizzes aren't bad if you look over the slides. I highly recommend him. He's the best.

Professor Hill is super awesome. He has a great sense of humor and is a great teacher. The course is very reasonable because Professor Hill gives great feedback and you always know what he wants from you. Great class, would take it from him again.

Easily my favorite teacher!!!! HE is amazing, and will help you get an A. Honestly, I believe he wants everyone to get an A. He has 3 Tas, and if you ask for his help, he wont say, "contact the TA's" he will ask when he can meet with you so he can help you be successful!! easy quizzes as long as you follow the Digital Dialogue! Easy A. GREAT GUY!!!

Dr. Hill is amazing. He is always willing to meet with you outside of class and help you as much as he can. He is super sweet and funny. His class has been one of my favorites at BYU. He wants you to memorize some definitions, but its not that hard. There are review sessions for his quizzes, so you will always be prepared for the quizzes.

Dr. Hill is fantastic. He is amazing and very willing to meet with students outside of class, which helps your grade a ton. He is concerned about each student. Learns every student's name. Lectures are interesting. He will do everything he can to help you get an A. I highly recommend taking writing from Dr. Hill.
Best teacher I've had at BYU. I don't like writing but this ended up being one of my favorite classes just because prof Hill is so sweet and funny, and just all around a great human being.

Dr. Hill is an incredible professor.  He's got an awesome sense of humor, fantastic T.A.'s, and the sweetest personality you can imagine.  He's very patient and dedicates so much of his time to help you with your assignments.  If you know the study guides, you'll ace the midterms.  I highly recommend taking this class from him!

Dr. Ogles made the class so manageable. He seemed to genuinely care about his students, and he made a point to learn everyone's names and check in on every student as often as possible. There were a lot of quizzes, but they were open note, and the homework was pretty doable.

Dr.Ogles is a wonderful professor. As intimidating as stats might be, he made it a breeze. He clearly outlines what the course and workload will look like and sets you up for success. Homework and labs are collabroative and open note/ resource. Lecture quizzes are also open note/ resource and you can even ask the TAs to help you with the question.

Dr. Ogles is an amazing professor. I wasn't sure what I wanted to do after undergrad, but this class gave me insight into PhD vs Master's, as well as the various helping professions. It was all very insightful and practical for the future. Some hard work is needed to succeed in the course, but it is worth it because of its practical nature.

He was the best. I would go to most lectures but mostly pull up late and just pop an AirPod in and grind out the class work, he would come up to me and ask what I was listening to. The class is very manageable and all online do-able but going in person is super worth it.
He is so funny and makes coming to class a joy! I would highly recommend Dr. Ogles!! He is so helpful in answering questions and creating understanding. Super easy to relate to and so sweet!
I took his class last fall. He definitely knows his stuff, and he sets up the class so that you can have actual experience putting techniques into action. Easily my favorite psychology class.

Dr. Ogles knew my name and taught one of the most enjoyable courses in the psych major. However he gave no leeway when I was unable to take an exam due to a legitimate personal emergency. When I asked if I could take the exam a different time he responded by saying it was my fault for not preparing. He thought I was lying and my grade suffered

I took Dr. Ogles class almost 2 years ago, and I can still say this was not only the best class I took in the psych major, but also the most useful. This class is clearly a passion project for Dr. Ogles are you can clearly tell that he really loves teaching this class. Its a great class to test out therapy/counseling as a profession.

As long as you do the readings and watch the lectures, the coursework is super easy. Dr. Ogles is amazing, and there were so many fun moments in class. Personally, I found stats to be fun, especially the labs, because you are able to choose your own variables from a survey. Don't stress; take this class from Dr. Ogles; you won't regret it!

I can't recommend Professor Ogles enough. We never had a dull day in class. While it may seem like a lot of work at first, once you get used to it, it really isn't bad. Professor Ogles mostly uses Canvas to teach and then class is more like a review or time to do the assignments. He made stats 308 a great experience for me! I would recommend him!

Such a caring professor, really makes an effort to know students' names and make sure everyone is grasping the subject. Honestly, whole class COULD be done online, but make an effort to go to class, it's so much easier with his reviews and having him and the TA's there to help you out.

Dr. Ogles is so funny and seeks to develop close connections with his students. He is caring and extremely knowledgeable. There is a chapter quiz every week and a case study that you work on throughout the semester, and there is not a huge lit review like most psych classes have. There are guest speakers throughout the semester which is cool

Another just fantastic professor who really made me fall in love with clinical psych. He gives you as much hands on practice with the profession as possible and genuinely cares about your success not just in this class but in your career. His tests are a little tough but if you study with the study guides you should be okay. Go to TA reviews!

This was a great class! Everything was online in Canvas, so you didn't even have to show up to class if you didn't want to. If you did go to class, Dr. Ogles and the TAs were there to help with homework and answer any questions you had on the quizzes or labs. He made stats easy for people who had never taken stats before in their lives (aka me).

Dr. Ogles is a really great professor! We used Dr. Hardy's Canvas platform, so showing up to class wasn't necessary, but it was so nice to know that going to class to get extra help was always an option. This class is organized in a super approachable way, and made stats not as difficult or intimidating as we dove in. Would definitely recommend!
Class gives you a great insight into different potential helping professions. There are a lot of assignments, but they are all pretty helpful.

Very nice guy and the class was not hard (definitely does not need to be four credits). He uses the same Canvas as Dr. Hardy. You don't need to go to class but it is nice to go and get personal help from him since he only lectures half the time and the other half we do work in class. Not a lot of reading or homework. A good option for sure!!!

his rating is great for a reason. i love guest lectures it gives a lot of perspective. the TAs are helpful. tests and quizzes aren't too hard but there is regular reading quizzes. assignments aren't bad. three midterms and a final though.

I can't emphasize enough how helpful this class is. There are a lot of guest lecturers that come in from  different fields, and it was amazing talking to them about careers in psychology. I recommend the class and Dr. Ogles for all all psych majors. He's an amazing teacher!! Also, a ton of extra credit is offered

Dr. Ogles is a great guy. He generously offered to meet with all of us, which was helpful for me. I really enjoyed the guest lectures as well. My only complaint was that there was a lot of subjective experience incorporated, and I feel like I wanted more studies and research involved.

Dr. Ogles is great! This class is really beneficial to learn about different helping professions, all the assignments are purposeful so no busy work! Dr Ogles really cares about each student and wants to help you succeed in not only the class but your future, he is a great resource, and very knowledgeable! I highly recommend him

Doctor Ogles gives good dad/grandpa energy and you can really tell that he cares about his students. Everything is on canvas and lectures by Sam Hardy are there too so you technically don't have to go to class, but I did bc I liked asking questions. For every lecture there is a long quiz, but the quizzes really do help you for the exams.

The class is designed very well. It is very good for learning and retention. Teaches concepts well. There's also a lot of assignments so the grade you get is what you deserve. They drop one of each type of assignment too. He's also just a great person and will help you out. I have only good things to say about this class. It makes stats not scary.

Prof Ogles is very kind and understanding. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Lectures are long and sometimes un-engaging, but Prof Ogles does well to explain topics. Class is operated through canvas and class could be taken entirely online if you wanted. Class is graded on bi-weekly HW and quizzes, collaborative labs & 3 tests

He was my favorite prof this semester. there were a few tests during the class, but the study guides followed pretty close to the test. You have motivational interviewing assignments that were my favorite part of the class. You get to practice therapy skills on your roommates and actually apply what you learn. Very inspirational class.

I really loved taking clinical psychology from Dr Ogles. We practiced therapeutic techniques in "real plays" and he had lots of therapists come into classes to talk about their work. I was able to realize that doing therapy was not for me in this class rather than in the middle of grad school, which was great.

By far best class/professor I've had at BYU. He encourages diversity of approach and opinion. Makes you think, but also enjoy exploring psych. Grade is weighted fairly. Tests are fair but there's quite a bit of short-answer questions. He cares about his students personally and wants you to succeed. I loved it so much I never missed it, even at 8AM!
Dr. Ogles is the man. This class is easy but also super informative. Would take again in a heartbeat

Dr. Ogles is a wonderful professor- he truly cares about his students. Classes are thought-provoking and interesting. The class isn't too hard- just take a lot of time with the written assignments because he grades those very carefully. Tests are good- just follow the study guide he provides for you. Awesome guy, awesome class.
Dr. Ogles was amazing! Out of all the classes I have taken at BYU, his was my favorite. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed.
My fault for getting a B+ this class is informative and easy, I just didn't study for the final at all. Love Professor Schooley though he is really dope.

Amazing introduction to cybersecurity. You'll probably know if it's the field for you after taking this class. Attendance was optional, though I strongly recommend attending class. Dr. Schooley is kind, accessible outside of class, spiritual, and extremely knowledgeable.
Best professor ever
Was my capstone coach. GOAT

Dr. Schooley is great. He is very willing work with you and has a fantastic teaching philosophy. He also is very knowledgeable and has a lot of industry experience he draws upon. Being the first rendition of the class, it had a few bumps, but the class was interesting and I am confident it will continue to improve.

Professor Schooley was amazing. The class consisted of a short reading before each class, and the labs were pretty straightforward and you were able to do them right after class during lab. There were no exams which was really nice, most of your grade was based on labs and projects, but the projects allowed for a lot of creativity and flexibility.

This is exactly what a songwriting class should be. It's largely a workshop and performance based class, with group feedback and minimal assignments. At the end of the class you get to record a demo in the RB studio with a TA. The tests/assignments/readings are easy. At the end of the semester there is an exposition for selected students to perform

BEST CLASS YOU COULD TAKE AT BYU!!! You dont have to know much about music to take this class, i promise. Everyone is at a different level! Great way to make friends and get an easy grade for elective credit!! Ben is such a great teacher and he is very kind. Has a great passion for songwriting!
he is himmy.

There is a lot of homework for this class but it is very good review and prep for exams. His lectures are great make sure to ask questions, he does a good job explaining any questions you might have; there are no bad questions with him.

Prof Webb is a great math teacher. He's always willing to answer questions & stay a few minutes after class to clarify problems. However, the bookwork problems were much harder than the problems we did in class. Be sure to go to the TA class because you can get all of your homework done there & ask questions. Don't be afraid to ask dumb questions!

The lectures cover the basics of the topics, yet the tests and homework are much more difficult than the material he teaches in lectures. Test averages through the year were C's. Your TA will drastically affect your success in this class since they do all the follow up on subjects.

Great class, took the envelope with 213 and 215. Dr. Webb does great with explaining how the concepts are applicable. You can get through this class fairly easily as long as you do the hw, and go to the lectures. Practice tests help prepare a ton for the actual so do them.

Diff Eq is a very difficult class, I will say up front. To succeed, you will need to give this class a lot of attention. Dr. Webb taught through examples, a saving grace when I reviewed my notes while doing the homework. However, these tests were insanely difficult. It's possible to prepare for these, but it will take serious time outside of class.

I average a B in most math classes and did not pass this one. Prof Webb is one of the best lecturers, but he has the hardest tests I've ever taken in my life. The class would have been much better if we had less content. It was way too much, too fast. He's a great professor, but you must work UNBELIEVABLY hard to succeed.
His lectures are super helpful.

Dr. Webb is an amazing professor. He's kinda goofy but is easy to relate to. Even as someone who is not taking another math class if I can help it. He writes the entirety of his lectures on the board so we could follow along. There is so much homework, but if you stay ahead it can only help you. Difficult class, but he does a great job.

great lecturer and great guy. His class is unnecessarily difficult. Teaches and tests on more concepts than other teachers. Expects you to remember random things he went over maybe once. Has vocab portions on his test. Lots of classmates (including me) got the worst grade they had ever gotten on tests. Expect a 4-5 credit workload.

Dr Webb is the best math professor I've had at BYU. By far. He is very respectful to all students and is always willing to talk about questions people have. It's clear that he honestly cares about how we learn. That said, the lectures and HW aren't always the best preparation for the exams. But just put a study group together and it'll be fine.

Best teacher I have had at BYU. He is accommodating and understanding to all of his students. Diff EQ is a hard class, but if you go to his lectures he teaches you everything for the homework and tests. He is not confusing and doesn't go on tangents. Practice exams prepare you well for tests, and he is a very nice grader on tests.

Its a typical math class where the tests are harder than the homework, which is harder than the classwork. The difficulty of the new DiffEq concepts were reasonable/manageable, but he made it unnecessarily hard with strangely complex algebra and calculus. His philosophy: be a human calculator and remember everything you did/didnt learn in the past.

Dr. Webb is a great teacher. Calc was a hard subject, but Dr. Webb did a great job teaching it. He was always available to office hours and T.A.'s are a great resource for this class. There are assignments due everyday Monday through Saturday so lots of homework, but manageable. Test were pretty hard, but he prepared his students well.

Professor Webb is intelligent yet humble. He's kind when students have questions, and he's quick to make sure you don't feel bad about new and difficult concepts. His lectures were clear, organized, and engaging. There's homework practically everyday, but it prepares you well for the tests. He's an incredibly skilled teacher and I highly recommend.

Prof Webb was really good at taking complex concepts and making them much easier to understand. His lectures used a lot of helpful examples and he always related things to real-life scenarios in STEM. He lets you to go to the math lab for the homework and quizzes which was super helpful. The tests are hard but if you study, it'll be much easier.

Dr. Webb is an incredible professor! The workload wasn't too bad either. We had written and online homework due before each class. Do not miss any lectures. Tests are both multiple choice and written, but the written counts for more. TAs are ridiculously helpful and kind, as is Dr. Webb, so utilize your resources. I would highly recommend Dr. Webb

I loved Dr. Webb as a Calculus teacher. I think he taught the material very well but if you miss class even once, you could be in trouble. You need to get the textbox. I couldn't see a good reason why not to take Math112 from Dr. Webb.

Dr. Webb is an incredible teacher. He was able to take difficult, complex concepts and make them simple. There was a good amount of homework regularly, but that's to be expected in any math class. I always felt prepared for the tests, between in-class reviews, math lab reviews, and my own study. I would 100% recommend this class.
Its a hard class in general, but Dr. Webb is amazing. He is super understanding and aware that it doesnt come easy to most people. Definitely would recommend Dr. Webb if you need to take Math112.

This was the third time I had Dr. Webb. Calc 1, Lin Algebra, and this class. Diff Eq is tough, but that's not his fault. If he's an option for 334, then take him. He's usually organized and likely more clear an instructor than other professors. Homework can get long and confusing, but just keep truckin! Use your resources and you'll make it.

pros: organized, efficient, willing to help one-on-one and outside of class. cons: streamlined lectures, doesn't always have time to answer everyone's questions in class. overall: better than average when it comes to math classes. The homework wasn't too hard, the class was organized and I knew what to expect.

His lectures are just him copying the textbook onto the board, and explaining what it means. It works fine. The homework can take forever, and he doesn't always check the problems before we do them, and so sometimes he had to change it, or take out problems, because he asked us problems beyond our reach. The tests weren't too bad. He's decent.

I am a senior this year, and out the dozens of professors that I've had during my 7 semesters so far, Dr. Webb has been the best organized. This is really helpful for taking good notes during lectures and orienting myself in the class and measuring my progress.

Dr. Webb was the only professor that I didn't really like this semester. There's a lot of stuff to cover which is tough, but I wish he had put more emphasis on doing examples in class. A couple times, I figured out that I had been doing a kind of problems differently than he intended, because he hadn't gone over it clearly enough in class.

Dr. Webb is a good teacher, he tries to make the lectures apply to the homework, and tries to prepare you for the tests. The tests are not easy at all, but they aren't tricky either, they are just like the homework: difficult but doable.

I understand he was trying his best, but he did not make the class accessible at all for non-math majors or attempt to relate any concepts in class to the real world or show any practical applications of them. The utter pointlessness of the course for 80% of the students made it hard to sit through his super dry lectures or put any real effort in.

I had Dr. Webb for networks, which was fun, since that's really the focus of his research. He's a good lecturer, and the focus of the class was quite practical, developing knowledge of base concepts, rigorous proof abilities, and programming implementation. The project was fun. Dr. Webb is a friendly person and a good professor.

My 2nd time having him. Hasn't changed. Organized, not boring, easy to take notes from - he talks slow and pauses for students to think. For him, it's about the math and not the logistical stuff. For the Honors section, you have a lab once a week and a few extra book problems. Otherwise, it's the same as everyone else (tests, online hw). Good guy.
Great professor! There's a lot of material so he has to move quickly, but he broke things down. Lectures were entertaining and he really kept us engaged. Wish he had more office hours. Good man.
Dr. Webb is the classiest professor on campus. Great lectures and his practice test are very helpful. Best math professor hands down.

This is the 7th math teacher I have had at BYU, and Professor Webb is by far the best. He is very clear and thorough in his lectures. He also does "quizzes" once a week that really is just a little extra homework that reviews material from the week before. Honestly it helped me a ton! If I had to take another math class, I'd take it from him.

Dr. Webb is probably the best math professor I've ever had. Differential Equations definitely isn't an easy course, but he takes the concepts and breaks them down in an easy-to-understand way. He also applies concepts from previous math classes.

Calc wasn't something easy for me but Dr. Webb helped. I dropped this class the  first time with another prof. but got an A with Dr. Webb. That being said tests are by the department so his class isn't really easier he just did a pretty decent job teaching. Even if you took calc in highschool this will still probably challenge you at some point.

Somewhat quirky, but very cool and nice guy. Could Calculus have been easier with another professor? Probably not. So he is the guy to take it from. He will stay after class and answer questions as long as he can. Go talk to him during office hours too. Not necessary to go to each class. I kept up by watching YouTube videos beforehand. Take him!

Awesome teacher! He has a way of taking confusing topics and make them simple and easy to understand. He's always looking to improve as well, he asked our class halfway through what he could do to improve and HE DID IT. Very caring and willing to spend time with you one on one to make sure you're successful. With him and Math Lab it was very doable

The material is hard, but he breaks it down so I can feel confident on starting the homework. He definitely prepares you for the tests through his lectures and hw. Doing these two things & going to the math lab will bring you to success in his class.

Doctor Webb is amazing at explaining concepts. He has a really good balance of writing proofs on the board and doing example problems. He's always super nice when you have concerns. One thing I really loved about his class was that he always started with a prayer, which really set a good tone for the rest of the hour. He's awesome! Take his class!
His lectures are calming. He's just got a knack for math and is really good at putting notes on the board.

The honors section had same exams non-honors, just deeper learning with labs and homework that helped us get better grades.  Great teacher, checks for student understanding. He answers questions if you ask,  helpful especially in office hours. Wants his students to succeed. I liked the applications to linear algebra that he shared.

Math 313, is by itself a very hard class. I don't think I would have been able to pass it without the help of Professor Webb. He really tries to focus on what you have learned and expand it to the material you are currently learning. Also, he has consistent out of class hours for additional help. I highly recommend this professor.

Prof. Webb is a really awesome guy.  He teaches material in an engaging and accessible way, and encourages the class's intention and involvement.  He's great with answering questions.  He talks about the practical applications of what we're learning, especially with linear algebra being his primary field of research.  Would recommend for any class!

Dr. Webb is the best, really cares about his students and wants you to succeed. Explains the material very well and clearly. Has incredibly elegant handwriting. He really tries to make the class its best and continually improve his teaching. Has "discuss with your neighbors" questions every class, really help engage you and shake up the lecture.

Dr Webb is the best math teacher I have had by far. His lectures, deemed slow by some, cover all of what you need to know to learn the topics. His homework and tests were totally manageable. We covered more material in this class than any other professor in the same class and the average was great. Fantastic. Would recommend to anyone.

Dr. Webb is awesome. His lectures are very well put together. He is very good at explaining difficult concepts and does his best to make sure everyone is on the same page. He is a super nice guy. class average was 84.22%.

Professor Webb was pretty good. To me, it seemed like he went a little too slow, and we didn't always learn enough to prepare us for the homework. But you do eventually learn every concept, and he makes sure you know it well. And he's a really nice guy.

He's a really good teacher, things are very clear. The only thing I disliked was he spent a lot of time on the basics and building up to a concept, and less time explaining things related to the homework. On the whole, though, he's one of the better math professors at BYU, and the math lab TAs fill in the gaps for what he doesn't cover.

I had the hardest time keeping my eyes open in this class! Prof Webb is the driest teacher I have ever had. He explains extremely basic topics in class and then the homework is way advanced. I would fall asleep for 10 min and wake up to him doing the same problem on the board. Avoids questions and said "Someone hands you an integral" 800 times...
ben is very helpful. not really easy to understand, but his tests are very easy, he grades his homework really fairly. like sometimes i did absolute crap and i hada 90. totally in love with him.

This is a unnecessarily hard course, the book is awful.  Ben's a doctorate student, but is fairly good at teaching 112. Ben is a nice guy who will help you whenever he can (he's cool about late hw etc.) The HW is hard and he grades it hard, but the tests are very reasonable.  The final is a beast.
One of the best Math 112 teachers on campus.

This class is a bit of a disappointment for those looking for an engaging, interesting class. 90% of the material is about insulin's involvement in the pathways and the lectures are so long as they are recorded and honestly not engaging at all. Very boring overall, I really wish he did more with this class, felt neglected. You'll never see him

He is the best professor I've ever had. Honestly, his class is hard, but the way he has the class set up is 100% for your benefit and success. He wants you to succeed & you can feel it! This isn't the type of class where you can memorize the idea of a topic and be fine; he requires you to really understand and think critically in his tests.

His email: With the end of semester comes many, many emails from students asking for mercy. Please, don't send any more! One very important thought: I've already installed mercy into the class by way of the midterm retake average. I gave you some mercy with the retakes (and dropping a quiz). Now it's time for just a little justice.

I do not normally write these, but he was in class a total  of 9 times the whole semester. His TA's ran his course, I was appalled. I have never seen a professor so dismissive of his students. He provides a video to watch before class, then in class you do a worksheet with your group. If you miss class you get a zero, no makeups.
