Best Class ive taken.  You watch the lectures on your own time, but you only end up spending about 50 min in class instead of the 2 hours.  Most vids are 40 min or less.  Very beneficial grading system.  Exams are fair, but you need to know your stuff.  You learn a ton but it's not completely overwhelming.  No homework or textbooks.

I love Professor Bikman! His class structure is straightforward to understand and do well on the tests. Everything he says in his recorded lecture is fair game on the tests. But, they lectures are recorded so watch them twice, take notes, make flash cards, and you are set. I also love bikman's personality and he cares for his students. 10/10

I LOVE BIKMAN. He is one of the smartest people I have ever had the pleasure of listening to. You watch pre-recorded lectures before class which is SO beneficial for learning. The workload was totally reasonable, especially for a 4 credit class. I 100% recommend him and this class, lowkey am trying to take another class with him.

I took Cell 305 from Bikmaan two semesters ago and am still benefitting from the things I learned in his class. I loved the flipped class style so I could actually process his lectures and learn the material. His lectures are amazing and he's such a cool guy. You do the assignments in a group in class which can be nice.

Professor Bikman is one of my favorite professors at BYU. He is great at explaining complex things, and he is so interesting to listen to. There is a lot of group work, but all inside of class. Exams are hard, but everything is off of his slides. GO TO TA REVIEWS!!

Professor Bikman is one of my favorite professors at BYU. I was scared going into physiology because it is a very difficult class but professor Bikman laid everything out and "simplified" his lectures. lectures are recorded and you can rewatch as many times as you want, super helpful for exams. Group work is a majority of your grade

Professor Bikman is one of those professors who you just want to listen to and learn from. He knows what he is talking about and you truly feel like you're learning true, accurate, and valuable information. His classroom style is flipped, which I usually don't like, but I ended up loving it for this class/it was super effective. Take his class!

Opinionated & AWESOME. Author of "Why We Get Sick" & an expert on insulin sensitivity & diabetes (lots of peer-reviewed journals, podcasts, and informative YT videos). CELL305 focuses on clinical cases (so useful), NO math, & working in a group. Very generous w/ opportunities to raise your grade. Only teaches CELL305 in the fall, but worth the wait

Great class! The flipped classroom format helped me understand the material, and group assignments were fun. Bikman is an interesting professor who's passionate about adipose physiology and diabetes, as he's a renowned researcher. This class covers a lot, and I could've done better with more effort, but he's the professor to take!

Flipped classroom. I LOVED IT. Take this class from him. You will learn so much. It is a hard topic so you will have to put in the work but he is a great teacher and will prepare you. Watch letctures at home and you can re watch them. Homework in class and the TAs help so much. Group work in class which was so helpful. GREAT CLASS!

Dr. Bikman is great! Lectures are clear and easy to follow. He has a great ability to simplify complicated topics. There are a lot of things to know for Endocrinology, but overall, pretty easy class. There is a big paper and a group project, but very little homework otherwise. Enjoyable class, interesting subject, and wonderful professor.

Dr. Bikman is my fav professor, very influential. Class is clinical case study based. My best piece of advice: go to his office hours every week, and he will make sure you understand. Tests are based on powerpoints. Lots of group work, which can be a good thing. Resist the urge to take detailed notes, focus on understanding the concepts first.

Bikman is a great teacher and very passionate about the subject. He has a very strong personality and is very opinionated so he tends to be a little disrespectful at times. His tests are easy, everything comes straight out of the powerpoints and is case study based. He has one lecture per test that he really cares about and only tests on that.

I found it really easy to pay attention to the recorded lectures because Dr. Bikman is so engaging. Even though the lectures were pre-recorded, he still managed to make it interesting and his personality shone through the whole time. The class was fun and taught me so much about the body.

Loved this class! If you are considering taking it at all, just do it! He totally changes your view of the human body and how it works. It is so eye opening. His lectures are fantastic, and if you study, this class is very doable.

Bikman is AMAZING!! I loved his class! His tests are hard for sure, but fair in my opinion. He really focuses on the most important material and leaves the rest out. I loved the format of his class. And he is absolutely hilarious! So sarcastic! You will love this class. Do not take it from anyone else!!!

This class was life-changing. Bikman is passionate, knowledgeable, and engaging. Everything he says is backed by empirical research, even if it goes against what people have accepted in the past. I'll be healthier because of this class, but more importantly, my future patients will be as well. It's also a lot less than 4 credits of work. Do it.

Dr. Bikman is awesome and this class is amazing! I have learned SO MUCH. He has an off-color sense of humor, so just know that. I tend to get offended easily and I haven't been personally offended by things he says, but I know some people are. He is an amazing professor.

Dr. Bikman is honestly one of the most influential professors I've ever had. He has made me question everything I've ever learned in college so far. He is super smart and knows his stuff. Be sure to know his Powerpoints so you can do well.

Bikman is the greatest! His lectures are incredible and he always presents the latest data on whatever he is presenting in class. He presents some pretty controversial stuff so data helps! Go to office hours and build a relationship with him, he is always willing to answer any questions and explain things again and again.

Bikman is an excellent and knowledgeable teacher. Very smart and willing to help all who put in the work for it. This was a challenging class that takes time and dedication. This class is mandatory for nursing majors but also very important for those in PDBio or planning to go to Med school. Highly recommended. There is no other teacher like him.

Bikman is knowledgeable of what he teaches and does indeed practice what he preaches. lectures are interesting & you learn a lot. If you are good at memorization & case study tests, this class is for you. If you are a nursing student, this class is for you. If you are not a nursing student, understand that this class will be 10X harder for you.

Very inspiring/knowledgeable professor! 5 tests and a final with some other little assignments here and there. Slideshows are huge and you gotta memorize every little detail in them for the tests, but all the info is very clinically relevant. Class is a pretty easy B+/A-, a little more work for an A. Would definitely take again

Dr. Bikman's class is straight up fun if you're a premed. Tests are extremely straightforward and assignments are fairly lenient. He totally likes to have fun in class and has a great sense of humor. He's super down to earth and is sure to make this class as interesting as possible! One of my fav professors!

Dr. Bikman is awesome!! He really cares about Pathophysiology and wants his students to learn and succeed. He takes pride in his Powerpoints. The subject was fascinating and I would definitely take the class again. The tests can be hard but if you study hard you will do great!

Awesome class, awesome professor. Go to office hours with questions. DRILL the power point presentations. If you know the power points class is an easy A/A-. Nutrition majors hate him (they do not like the data that Dr. Bikman presents in class--there's some new controversial stuff in the world of research). My advice: take it and see for yourself.

Plan on memorizing his slideshow.  He is very generous with grades at the end of the semester, but the slide shows were massive and the tests are extremely difficult.  I would not take it from him again.

Bikman is a professor who is clearly very passionate about what he teaches, and in that way his class is very entertaining and interesting. However, his lectures are typically 100+ slides, and he doesn't give any kind of study guide for tests and reviews are question-based only. Tests are tough and require a lot of study, so start preparing early

Best class and professor I've ever had at BYU. Very applicable content. He will actually permanently change the way you think about lifestyle and disease. It is a challenging class that is worthwhile. You won't regret it.   Also, he practices everything he preaches!!
Looked forward to his class. He keeps class interesting and is super funny! Take this class even if you don't need it for your major!!
Best teacher ever!
This is a hard class, but he does a good job at teaching it!
I loved this class!  The lectures were fun and I enjoyed going to class.  Definitely review old tests with Dr. Bikman or the TAs to prepare for the final.

This is a challenging class and Dr. Bikman does a fantastic job.  He clearly cares about the students and does everything he can to help them learn.  The lectures are two hours, which is long in any class, but he does a good job keeping it interesting.  Without questions, it's the most useful class I've ever had.
Easy class. His powerpoint have everything you need to know. Probably don't have to attend lectures to do well. Pretty good lectures, but his powerpoints are the size of cyber elephants.

Fantastic teacher! Loves his students and presents material very clearly. Yes, tests are hard, but if you pay attention and go through the slides you'll do fine. No extra reading, simple homework due each week with a group. Really inspired me for life in addition to teaching patho. If you have a chance to take with him, you won't regret it.
Simply wonderful class.

He has been my favorite professor at BYU (and I've been here 7 semesters). He is hilarious and teaches clearly. His lectures are based on the latest research, you will learn a lot of interesting stuff! And you won't even need the textbook.

Dr. Bikman is great.  Two things especially:  1) His PowerPoints are the best I have every seen.  All of the information is right there, with very clear formatting.  Great study tools!   2) His passion & investment in the students are remarkable, and makes going to class enjoyable and not a burden.  Learned a ton, well worth the work and time.

Dr. Bikman was probably the best professor I have ever had. He really cares about the students and is very passionate about his field. My life has been permanently changed after taking this class. I loved learning about insulin resistance and obesity especially!

Bikman's the man. Very cool, very funny, very passionate about his field. I learned a ton from this class. Some might not love his humor, but in my opinion his personality makes him so much more relatable and his class more enjoyable. Very aware of individual students and willing to accommodate office hour needs. Shares meaningful life insights too

One of the best classes and professors at BYU.  He goes above and beyond to help students really learn the material and he wants us to apply it in our lives.  I felt like I learned more useful info than I did in my other pdbio classes combined.  Oh and the class and professor is super entertaining and hilarious! A good grade is totally obtainable!

Favorite class by far!  Dr. Bikman teaches REALLY well!  He makes pathophysiology so fun to learn and his humor is absolutely hilarious!  Tests are hard, but if you buckle down and study thoroughly, you can do well.  He offers opportunities to raise your grade, such as extra credit and exam retakes.  Hoping to take weight-lifting from him!

He's funny, laid-back, and cares about students' learning and success--very approachable. The material is hard, but he is accommodating with grading. He's very passionate and informed about his subject--he backs up all his lectures with current research and accepts student feedback. I loved his somewhat off-color humor/attitude, but some might not.

Bikman is a wonderful up-and-coming professor and researcher. The class covered everything you would expect in a pathophys class, and in addition had a special focus on Bikman's research area - insulin resistance, diabetes, obesity, etc. This makes it particularly useful for premed, nursing, and dietetics students interested in prevention. Take it!
He is a good lecturer and very enthusiastic. It's a very interesting class. He seems to care about the students, but his TA is always angry. I think she just hates everyone.

Best. Class. Ever. It was hard. It was worth it. Bikman is inspiring and so fun to learn from. Everything is on the slides. I suggest making your own study guides from day one-it makes the final studying easier. Also, GO REVIEW EXAMS. Again, best class ever.

Bikman's class will change your life. He has you do a lifestyle project where you make one positive lifestyle change and document it for a month. This was the greatest element of the class. I am on my way to living an infinitely better life than I was before. His tests are hard, but realistic to clinical/ healthcare settings. Greatest class ever!

After reading some of the previous comments, I thought I would set the record straight. I took 365 from Judd and was his TA one semester. I've been Bikman's TA for three. The bottom line: they're BOTH great teachers. I wonder how many of the reviewers who insist Dr. Judd is the less desirable option have even attended his class? Probably none...

This was my favorite class I took at BYU. It is a tough class, but Professor Bikman's passion for the subject makes it really fun to learn. He is very personable and new everyone in the class by name. If you are interested in a career in healthcare this is the best class you could take at BYU.

Dr. Bikman is amazing! It's a 4-credit 300 level class, so of course it will be challenging, but Dr. Bikman makes it easy to handle! Do the extra credit opportunities, attend lecture, take notes on the slides (I used my computer, but I guess printing works too), and know the slides for the test and you will get an A!
Fun class!
Awesome class.  Great professor.
Bikman was very cool and interested in the students.  His perspective on insulin resistance was very neat.
Great professor.  He was interested in the students and his enthusiasm for particular topics was infectious.

I found this to be a hard class. It was Professor Bikman's first semester teaching, so I am sure this contributed to the difficulty level. He was a really great teacher and very helpful. He is genuinely concerned about each of his students and he wants you to do well. Definitely better than the other Pathophys teacher. I would recommend him.
Bikman is ok.  I did not enjoy his teaching style, and the class is HARD. There is tons of information and if you get behind, it is hard to catch up.

Bikman is one of the best teachers I have ever had. I would definitely suggest taking him over Judd. He is willing to give extra credit and work with the student to help them exceed. Class was interesting and fun. Tests were reasonable, not extremely difficult. Definitely take this class from Bikman!!
I love Bikman. I would definitely take him over Judd. He is really fair and gives you lots of extra credit opportunities. Bikman is the man.

Had him for physical science 100. Course material itself is difficult, but his lectures are entertaining and he's a funny guy. definitely knows what he is talking about too. Class was genuinely enjoyable. You have a reading and lesson in-between each class but besides that there is isn't extra homework besides a really easy lab "article essay"

Dr. Boizelle was one of my favorite teachers! I took Phy S 100 from him and it was a very well organized class. His teaching style is super interesting and you could tell he knew a lot about the things he taught. He brought an interesting spiritual perspective to lectures and he was great at answering any questions that students had.

Professor Boizelle is a kind person who is passionate about his material. He knows a LOT about the subject and classes are usually used as a Q&A session that may be only tangentially related to the source material. Reviews and readings were effective in preparing for the tests, but self-motivation is necessary. Good class but would not do again.
Dr. Boizelle is awesome! He cares about what he's teaching and he makes lectures engaging and interesting.

Professor Boizelle is awesome! His lectures are interesting, he knows his stuff, cares about students, loves answering questions, and will admit if he isn't certain about a topic. If plan to take this class as a GE be aware that it's not just star gazing and UFOs, it's real science, take it if you are interested in learning about the Universe.

Dr. Boizelle is the nicest guy, and his lecture slides are top notch. Although homework is difficult sometimes, that's to be expected for this class, and the problems are very well thought out. Also he is extremely lenient with due dates.

Dr Boizelle is incredible. He's a newer professor with a lot of responsibilities here at BYU so it takes a while for things to get graded, but he's a very clear lecturer with very organized slides, and accessible for help outside of class. He's funny, kind, and one of my favorite professors. The content of the work is hard, but not too heavy.

Dr. Boizelle didn't understand what was difficult for his students, but he got better at it in the end. I did fine on the tests, but my roommate failed them. The tests were very application-based and you had to know how to infer things you didn't learn. The tests were heavily curved. Go to the reviews and use the study guide.

Dr. Boizelle is a very fair grader, but definitely expects you to give his assignments a decent effort. A lot of students, like myself, signed up for this class expecting star gazing and UFO debates, but the real content is much more challenging. Yes, it's an intro class, but it's still a GE for physical science. Expect real science!

Professor Boizelle is super passionate about for astronomy. He is really funny and overall a great guy but I feel that he would be better suited for a higher level course. For tests I referred back to the slides and the homework. This class is difficult but not impossible. I wouldn't recommend to fulfill a GE.

This is a very tough class for a GE. I would spend 4-6 hours studying for the exams only to end up with a 75-80% which was about average for the class. Don't take this class unless you are super interested in astronomy.

Professor Boizelle is very charismatic and that makes his class a little more bearable. However, if you don't have a science background I do not recommend this class. It's meant to be an intro class however the content is much more advanced. If you don't go to the lecture and really study the textbook midterms won't be easy.

IF YOU LOVE ASTRONOMY YOU WILL LOVE TAKING THIS CLASS FROM BOIZELLE! If you are new to this subject this class will definitely challenge you, but you will learn a lot. Boizelle knows so much about astronomy and loves sharing it. As long as you show up to the lectures and do all the assignments you'll be fine.

This class was extremely hard. There were few times I actually understood what we were talking about. He is available for office hours and is helpful there but if you don't know what's going on it's just like sitting in another lecture. Speaking of lectures they are very long, it would take two classes to get through a lecture he'd scheduled for 1.

This class is difficult if you don't have a science background. The nice thing is midterms aren't waited heavily so if you do the other assignments you can still get a decent grade. I would definitely go to his office hours or TA hours to get extra help. Boizelle is a super nice guy and I really enjoyed going to the planetarium for part of class.

Professor Boizelle is a good guy, you can tell he loves what he does. However DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DONT ALREADY HAVE A SCIENCE BACKGROUND. I took this class for a general and it seriously killed my GPA. His tests we extremely hard, mostly because the concepts he taught were way too advanced for a introduction class.

He is a great guy but He is used to teaching upper-level classes and really struggled to explain simple things in a way that made sense to most people. The class is definitely doable but if you are worried you might struggle with the concepts I would recommend taking it from another professor who has had more experience teaching the class

This was NOT the easy Astronomy class about stars I was hoping it would be. Boizelle is a super cool guy and passionate about the work but I felt like he didn't know how to teach a class this simple. He constantly jumps into really difficult concepts and doesn't explain them very well. The midterms and tests are ridiculously difficult.

VERY HARD CLASS. Right off the bat, I have to say that Dr. Boizelle is a super cool dude. Nice, funny, and honestly the kind of guy I would be friends with off-campus if I was a teacher haha. Still, Astronomy is a bad class to take as a freshman cause it's really hard. Boizelle teaches really well, but the content and tests way too hard

I love Dr. Boizelle - he's super passionate about his work and knows what he's talking about. He gives plenty of time to do the homework, and if you pay attention in class, its not hard. Attendance isn't a part of your grade but you do need to be there so you don't fall behind on lecture material. Labs in planetarium were very cool.

I don't normally like flipped classrooms (watch a lecture video and then come to class for support instead of learning everything in the classroom), but I loved this one. Frandsen is the best professor I have ever had. He knows the content, he cares about answering questions clearly and kindly, and he showed that learning matters more than grades.

This class was set up by Professor Frandsen and run by TAs. He really cared about our experience and encouraged testing ideas, even if we were wrong. You work in groups of four, and half the grade is participation. No busywork, 95% of people got A's, and it was genuinely enjoyable. I'd totally recommend it!
Dr Frandsen is the best physics professor at BYU maybe even the world

The best professor I have taken from. I literally said in my teacher evaluations that they should give him a raise or something. Very caring and approachable. He goes out of his way to make sure each student in the class has a good experience and feels like everything is fair.

Physics is not my thing and I struggled with the course content, but Dr. Frandsen was literally the best. He is kind, intelligent, and available to his students. Never spoke down to anyone, encouraged and answered questions, very clear expectations, good vibes. Fostered a compassionate and focused learning environment. He is a gem. Love him.

amazing professor, he made me truly enjoy physics, The homework is super helpful for the tests, the lectures were interesting, and he usually adds a huge curve for the test as long as you do test corrections. He is awesome, can't say that enough. I wish all professors were as caring as he is

I wish all of my classes were taught by him. He has you watch his pre-recorded lecture before class and then you show up to do practice problems. This method ensures everyone is taught the same amount of material. His tests are straightforward and not tricky. He also curves the exams often which boosts your grade. He teaches very clearly as well!

Frandsen is one of the better physics teachers. Sometimes his lectures could be a bit confusing or vague, but it is hard material. I would definitely do prep outside of class to understand the topics. He does exam corrections and curves, they saved me!! He was easy to approach about questions, and his class is organized and well thought out.
Loved his physics class
Dr. Frandsen is the best.

Dr. Frandsen is hands down, the best professor I have had. He truly cares about his students and does everything he can to make a difficult course not only survivable, but enjoyable. You can feel his enthusiasm for the subject. If every professor were like unto him, the world would be a better place.

I love Dr. Frandsen, he is such a nice guy and truly cares about his students. He is there to teach and make sure you learn unlike other physics professors. His tests are challenging, but that is expected just make sure you have a conceptual understanding of the material and use the homework to help you prepare for the tests. Again, he is awesome!

Physics is the worst, but Frandsen is the best! He really wants to help his students do well and listens to them when trying to improve the class. Tests are hard because they are only 20 questions, but he prepares you well for each of them. Go to TA reviews and do HW problems to study. He also curves all 3 tests and the final.

Frandsen is a homie. Physics is hard no matter what, but he makes the topics interesting and really tries to help. He curves the tests hard, and let you argue points for partial credit. He makes getting a good grade reasonable if you try. I hated 105. Frandsen made 106 seem fun.

Dr. Frandsen was everything I wish my chemistry teachers were. I straight up failed the first test, worst score Ive ever gotten in my life. He not only curved my test, he offered partial credit for questions I was close on as well. He was fantastic for boosting my self esteem and my next test score was worlds better. Couldnt recommend him enough.

Professor Frandsen is the best! I was nervous going into 106 but he gives the best lectures and is super straightforward. His tests are usual college tests, but if you go to his lectures and review the slides you'll ace them. His practice problems are super great and overall he is a hilarious guy. Would recommend taking it from him for sure!!

He is a very good teacher. He really cares about the experience that we had in class. He asked for feedback about what we did and didn't like about class and he actually listened to what we wanted. He is very fair and clear on his grading. If you go to him about questions that you didn't think were fair, he will consider it. You can get points back
Great professor. Simplifies difficult concepts and really wants his class to succeed. Doesn't overcomplicate things. Loved this class.

Dr. Frandsen is new, but is clearly a cut above your typical hard science professor. He really knows his stuff, teaches it so simply, makes himself available to meet outside of class, and is very compassionate. Impressively intelligent, as well as super humble.

Walked in the first day and he told us it was his first semester every teaching, that made more than a couple of us nervous for sure. Turned out to be my favorite science professor so far. Super clear with material covered, everything that he tests we go over in class, really good at explaining concepts. And he is the best dressed man on campus.

First semester teaching, it wasn't too bad. I suck at physics, but this course doesn't require too much time. The tests are hard, but if you really know the slides front and back, and how to do the homeworks, you're golden. His lectures are a bit boring, but I also think physics is a dry subject. Great guy

Professor Frandsen is an incredible teacher. His lectures are clear and interesting, his homework is straightforward and fairly easy, and he has extremely helpful office hours. Tests are worth a lot of your grade with only 20 questions each, but as long as you know how to do all the homework and iClicker problems you'll be just fine.

Dr. Frandsen is fair. Physics is a subject that doesn't come easily to me, but his lectures were thorough and prepared me well for his tests. Tests weren't surprising and were similar in difficulty to the homework. Overall, Dr. Frandsen is a nice guy and cares about his students' success. If you're taking Physics 106, take it from my boy Benjamin.

His class is very fair with about 2/3 of your grade being determined by tests. The other portion comes from iclicker, homework, and reading. He curves the tests and they are all very reasonable. He prepares you well for them. If you pay attention in lecture and do the rest of the assignments, you should do well.

Dr Frandsen is awesome. Brand new, but seems super experienced at teaching. Very funny and approachable, makes physics seem interesting. Anyone who can do that is clearly amazing. He curves the tests, offers participation/effort points that are easy money and is extremely helpful in office hours. Tough course, but take it from him if you can.

This was his first semester teaching, but it feels like he's been doing this for years. He teaches very well and is willing to work with you. Bi-weekly reading assignments (30 minutes each), weekly homework assignments that aren't too bad for the most part, and three curved midterms with a cumulative final. If you have the chance, take it from him!

Dr. Frandsen is young, friendly, approachable, funny, clear, and very caring. The only assignments are 30 minute readings, weekly online homeworks, and 3 midterms and a final (which are admittedly tough, but he curves). His slides are great, use them for studying and homework. He uses a free online textbook. I'm very impressed with him.

Dr. Frandsen is a new professor in the physics department but wow hes so great. He teaches in a very understandable way and is very friendly. His tests are hard, but physics is just hard in general. Hes very willing to adapt and help. Definitely would recommend his physics class. Hes so great.

Professor Frandsen is great! His lectures are much more interesting than the other physics professors I've had, and he teaches concepts very clearly. He's accommodating and friendly, very communicative with the class so we always know what's going on, curves tests, and gives very little homework and reading. Take physics from him if you can!
My fault for getting a B+ this class is informative and easy, I just didn't study for the final at all. Love Professor Schooley though he is really dope.

Amazing introduction to cybersecurity. You'll probably know if it's the field for you after taking this class. Attendance was optional, though I strongly recommend attending class. Dr. Schooley is kind, accessible outside of class, spiritual, and extremely knowledgeable.
Best professor ever
Was my capstone coach. GOAT

Dr. Schooley is great. He is very willing work with you and has a fantastic teaching philosophy. He also is very knowledgeable and has a lot of industry experience he draws upon. Being the first rendition of the class, it had a few bumps, but the class was interesting and I am confident it will continue to improve.

Professor Schooley was amazing. The class consisted of a short reading before each class, and the labs were pretty straightforward and you were able to do them right after class during lab. There were no exams which was really nice, most of your grade was based on labs and projects, but the projects allowed for a lot of creativity and flexibility.
I think this was his only semester teaching statics. He did a great job and taught clearly. Obviously it is a big class that covers difficult concepts.

Approached Dr. Terry multiple times for grade adjustments due to confusing and inconsistent instructions, but was denied every time. Instead, he gave the whole class free points only if you read an email and completed a random assignment within 10 hours, no in-class announcement. Pushes "same for everyone" instead of helping students in need.

Actually took ME EN 101 (Statics) from Dr. Terry but there wasn't an option for that. Dr. Terry is a phenomenal professor who cares, and provides every opportunity for the students to be successful. He is also very approachable and willing to help. Statics can be a tough class, but Dr. Terry explained the concepts clearly.

I really enjoyed Dr. Terry as a professor. The class was hard but he wants the students to succeed. If you have an issue speak with him or the TAs and they can almost certainly help. Course was great!

His first semester with Mechatronics, so it is understandable that he couldn't be an end all be all with programming questions, but he sure tried to help debug or troubleshoot whatever your semester robot had with you. He's a fun professor that tries to help you in whatever way he can. I would recommend him for future mechatronics classes.

I was worried about taking his class, since he was brand new to BYU, but honestly I think system dynamics from Dr. Terry ended up being my favorite class (so far at least) since I started college. Dr. Terry wants you to do well, and will bend over backwards to help you if you're struggling.

He's newer to teaching at BYU, but he did a great job teaching Dynamic Systems. It's a pretty difficult course with a lot of complicated concepts, and it did feel a little rushed at the end when we shoved thermal and fluid systems in just a few weeks, but the exams aren't too difficult.

Beth was very kind and understanding of her students and had a great sense of humor. The class was a bit disorganized, and there were some repeat assignments that got mixed up. The first hour of class was usually not class-related, and it went by pretty slowly. Phonics instruction also wasn't super clear, but I learned something at least.

I love Beth! She is such a fun teacher and loves what she teaches! The class itself is rather easy, just reading a lot of children's books and writing about them! You work a lot with your table group which I really enjoyed! I highly recommend this class from Beth!

I truthfully don't understand how Beth's rating isn't a 5.0. I admire her as a teacher, but especially as a human. I didn't feel like she was my professor, I felt like she was my friend. You have to read children's books and do small assignments on them, but the books are short and on YouTube. PLEASE take this class from her!

Beth is an incredible person, and she taught us well how to have that Christlike love for our future students. I took her Children's Lit class as well, loved both. She's wildly intelligent. She has high expectations for everyone, but if you're irresponsibly lazy in class, she won't say anything. I love how she lifts/cares for everyone around her.

Loved Beth! I read all the reviews on here before taking her class and was a little nervous, but she is so caring and open-minded. The class is definitely one of my favorites, even though I don't even like to read. All the books we read in this class helped me discover a new talent. Class is not hard to follow, just show up & do everything on LS.

Borup is the best. Super easy class. First semester she taught K6 writing and I enjoyed it. Each class was more of a discussion. She also made one day online, so we only met once a week for about 1 hour. She and her TA grade super easy. I loved all the topics we talked about. Not a lot of homework, just a fun, educational class. Incredibly easy.
Beth was awesome. I had no idea how much I actually learned from her class until finals came around, and suddenly studying was so much easier and way less daunting. I learned how to learn

Beth is chill af. I had a B most of the semester due to turning in assignments late. But near the end I shot Beth an email explaining that I was worried about my grade and within a week I was back up at an A. Guys, there's no way you shouldn't get an A as long as you show up and do the work. If you're struggling just talk to her.

Beth is super chill. Mid semester I thought I was going to get a B because of a couple assignments I turned in late. But I just shot Beth an email and we figured out how to get me back up to an A. If you're ever struggling in her class just let her know, she'll help you out.

Beth is an AMAZING professor! She genuinely cares about every one of her students and will do anything to help you! I loved her lectures and learned so much. Would definitely take a class from her again!

I thought the class was so practically helpful. My reading got a lot better and faster. It was cool to think about reading at such a high level because I do so much reading for school and see how the strategies can be implemented. Beth was so kind and personable. She cares a lot about her students. She made class fun.

Beth is one of the kindest professors and tries her hardest to make sure her students are grasping the information. She is personable and kind and I was always excited to go to class because of her. Assignments are not too difficult or time consuming, just make sure you go to class as attendance is mandatory!

She is a great professor. She's very caring and likes to know how you're doing inside and outside of class. She loves to talk and can give you some pretty good advice. This was her first semester teaching Writing, and I think she handled the transition well.

Beth is very caring and has this dry sense of humor that kept things interesting. I'm gonna be honest though, this class dragged out and everything I learned over the semester I could have learned in a quick article. The assignments weren't always very clear but the grading is very lenient and I didn't do very much work outside of class time.

Beth was really nice. Her class is interesting, and actually felt useful. I loved her so much, but sometimes class days were really boring or confusing. Besides that, her assignments are easy and she is super easy to contact!
Beth is an amazing professor, I highly recommend taking her class if you get the chance!

I am shocked that Professor Borup's ratings are so low! Her class was great! It was a pretty easy class just a lot of reading since I took the Children's Literature class. There were a few chapter books we had to read, but she didn't require you to finish the chapter books. Just gain an understanding and opinion of the book.

Beth is a nice person, but I did not feel that she prepared me to teach literacy in my own classroom. Unfortunately I did not pull much from her literacy classes and she often excused us from assignments, which was nice in some ways but really ended up being a disservice in the long run. I would recommend taking literacy courses from someone else.
She was very kind and thoughtful. You do have to read a lot so make sure you get a library card!
Beth is a wonderful person. I would not recommend her class. It is disorganized and then surprisingly strict with grading. The assignments are not worthwhile.

Beth's children's literature class was super easy. The assignments don't take too long and there was not a midterm or final. Sometimes she has in-class assignments worth about 15 points that she hands out, so make sure you attend class.

I had a great time in this class! I think that Beth is a great professor and genuinely cares about each of her students and what she is teaching. She is one of the kindest/honest professors I have had at BYU. I learned a lot about different types of literature for the classroom, and I am excited to implement it in my future classroom.

Professor Borup has improved a lot since last semester! This is my second semester with her and she has definitely taken her criticism to heart! She is really funny and kind and a very easy grader! She is a bit scatterbrained but she takes her teaching seriously and I have learned a lot from her this semester!

Don't listen to anyone. Beth is cooky, but she knows what she is talking about. It is easy to get her off-topic, but she is so knowledgeable and chill with what you talk about in class, that you can ask questions about things that you want to know and she will help you learn about them. Lots of good applications from her class. Easy, quality class.

I took STDEV 109. Professor Borup is scatterbrained to say the least. She's kind and cares about her students, but she never knows her own deadlines and or schedule. The class is easy and mostly based on attendance, and the things you learn are helpful. Easy A if you need it for your GPA. Don't bother buying the textbook if you take it.

She is a really nice person but not a great teacher. She will go on tangents in the middle of class about random things in her life and there is no incentive to pay attention. The class is super easy and she is an easy grader but I learned absolutely nothing in this class. The essay was the only hard part but only because it was tedious.

Super easy A, but is that always a good thing? I enjoy an easy A as much as the next person, but I really do not feel prepared to teach literacy to my future elementary students and that's the point of this class. I love the low stress of this class and Beth is super understanding, but I didn't learn anything.

I know her reviews are all over the place.  If you pay attention to any of them- pay attention to this one!!  Beth is a wonderful person.  You don't learn much in her class, but it is super easy!  This class will NOT be a source of stress in your life. Just go to class and put forth a normal amount of effort and it will be just fine.

Beth was a great choice for this class. She knows what it's like to be a student, so she doesn't assign very much. Her lectures were a bit random and all over the place, but she definitely cares and is knowledgeable about her subject. There were a few papers and online modules, but nothing to worry about. Beth is pretty funny too!

Beth was so kind and always tried to work with you whenever you needed it. Her lectures were a bit all over the place and some days I felt I didn't learn a ton by being there, but she is fun and truly cares about her students/class. Attendance is mandatory, a few papers that weren't too bad, and an easy final we took together!
This class made me question going into the field of education. The overall tone of this course was often gloomy the topics were negative and left me thinking that I should change my major.

Scatterbrained is the best word to describe Beth. She's just all over the place. If you go to class, you'll pass. You'll go down a grade if you miss class though. I never even read the chapters and still got full credit on assignments. You basically talk about the same topic every "lecture." The TA's grade the few, short papers very easily.

I don't really know what to say about Beth. I did every reading assignment without actually doing the readings, and that's about all you do in the class. She is kind of disorganized and is not clear on what she expects. Pretty much just show up, do your assignments and you'll pass just fine. I just did homework for other classes during her class.

I love how interactive her lessons are. It is such an easy class and it's not lecture heavy at all. Lots of small group discussions but they are great. The readings for the class is so interesting and has helped me learn so much! Easy A! They grade so easy

Beth is simply the best. She allows you to turn in projects as many times as you need to and will give you meaningful feedback. She has been in the classroom recently and has a lot of knowledge and love for teaching, and literacy specifically. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed.
Beth is so sweet! However, I feel like I didn't learn much from this class. While it was an easy A, it didn't do much to prepare me for the El Ed major.

I love Beth as a person, but I struggled in this class. It was confusing and a little inconsistent. 2 (small) papers, some digital responses, and ATTENDANCE (mandatory!) are the main pillars of your grade. One of the easiest "A"s ever. However, Beth is honestly the kindest, most personable, and caring person ever and I would take this just for her.

Don't take this from Dr. Borup. She's extremely inconsistent in her grading, her instructions and rubrics for papers are extremely vague, and most of the time she talks about things unrelated to class. I'm not sure I learned a single thing in this class besides the things I learned from doing my own research for the inquiry project.

I really loved this class! Dr. Borup is not like most of the professors at BYU in the sense where she recognizes that busy work is not conducive to learning. She would give us "work days" to complete our assignments so I was not stressed from this class at all! She is very understanding and willing to work with students!
Professor Borup is great! She is kind and helpful. You have to put in the work and actually read, since this is a reading class. If you do the work it's fine!

Beth likes to spend time talking in class, and doesn't focus on the material. She gave us a final that had information on it that we never covered in class and wasn't on her study guide. Not too much work, but not too much learning.

I really really loved Beth, but I didn't get much from her class. She is super chatty and everyone in class had a great time listening to her stories, but that's just about as much as you get from the class. There aren't very many assignments. It's a low stress class. But participation is like 15% of your grade so you have to go to class.

Professor Borup is super nice and I have nothing against her as a person but she should not be a college professor.  The criteria for her assignments were never clearly defined and then she would dock you tons of points for them.  I emailed her with questions about my grade and she switched everything to an A so she wouldn't have to deal with it.

Professor Borup is one of the sweetest people you will ever meet. She's very passionate about teaching literacy, and she cares about her students. This was a blended class, and the online assignments were pretty long. If  you do the work and don't like your grade, you can re-submit it for a better score. She really wants you to succeed.

Class is very easy, but a bit of busy work. Beth is extremely nice but also extremely talkative and so half the time you spend listening to stories. You won't really learn a lot except for the article you read. As far as preparing you to be a better teacher...doesn't really help a lick. you can take it, but it won't do much for your intellect.
Beth is great. She gets how the TELL courses are...TELL courses, and she adjusts the classwork so that it actually makes sense. Bring your appetite to class, PS.
She is fabulous! I had her for TELL 400 as well, and she is my favorite TELL instructor up to this point.

Love Liz!!! There is a lot of reading but it's mostly novels so it's not hard to get through. She's great about answering questions in class and lectures are really fun and interesting. Warnings: ask questions in class because she takes a while to respond to emails, she takes a while to grade so be patient.

Worst teacher I have had. The reading load for each class was unrealistic and she seemed to forget that it is a 200 level class. Told a lot of personal stories that were irrelevant. Uses this really annoying, whiney voice a lot. Takes forever to grade assignments/tests. The free response part of tests are graded on how much she likes you. Horrible.

I really enjoy her as a person, but I think that there was so much content in her class that I ended up not learning as much. I feel like this class was sort of treated like a "weed out the weak" class.

I learned a lot from Liz and her class, but it was difficult. You'll do quite a bit of writing, and you can't scrape by without doing the reading. She is also very strict on late work and tends to be disrespectful sometimes in her interactions with students. However, I really enjoyed the lectures and my writing skills definitely improved.

I was excited about this class but Professor Christianson was not my favorite. She assigned a TON of reading for every class and the homework assignments were unnecessarily long. The tests were also very difficult and it took forever to get grades back. I did enjoy most of the reading for this class and she brought us donuts one time which was nice

Liz is a great person with good character. I enjoyed her as an individual, but found her class to be very challenging. The readings was a lot at times, but could easily be accomplished by dividing it up. Her exams were extremely challenging and dense. She spends a lot of time telling stories rather than focusing on the discourse.
Liz was a great person but she gave way too much homework and gave really hard quizzes. I would not take Liz for writing 150. She is a very skilled Professor fit for higher level writing classes.

I would take her again in a heartbeat! She was engaging and entertaining in lectures, and shared personal experiences. She taught new concepts that I thoroughly enjoyed, and cares about the students. We get an assignment in each class, so attendance is important. Tons of reading - but she helps us understand what we read.

Liz is the sweetest person ever. There is lots of reading due every class (20-30 pages), but it is manageable because that is usually the only homework. Exams are ok. Just pay attention in class and keep up with the readings and you'll be fine.

Liz is a nice lady. She tells great stories and is just a good person. But I didn't love her class. Learning and test answers come from really dense reading while lectures are light and easy to understand. There isn't a lot of feedback on assignments and tests are pretty hard. There is no way you can do well without studying throughout the semester

We read a ton in this class about an hour before each class period, and these readings were vital to understanding the class. She was kind and made class discussions enjoyable. However, it wasn't always clear what was expected of me and it wasn't clear what we were expected to do for each assignment.

I loved taking this class from Liz! She is an amazing lady. I learned so much from this class, I think it was the best possible option for my CIV1 GE. Her lectures are amazing and interesting. There is a lot of reading for this class, but I found most of it incredibly entertaining. I would take this class again.

Liz is super nice. However she is the WORST at providing help. She wants you to learn "to trust the learning process." Every time I have asked for direction on an assignment, she never gives you a clear answer. Her midterm was unnecessarily difficult. The average was a D. If you are a freshman required to take this course. DO NOT TAKE IT FROM LIZ!!

I took it Spring term and she was super helpful and caring about the schedule and tried really hard to make the course load less overwhelming. But definitely get ready to write. This class covers a lot of different writing genres. Liz was amazing though, and her stories are awesome!

Liz cares about her students. By the end of the semester, her class felt like family. She loves it when people participate in class; be prepared for in-class group work and discussions. There's a lot of reading and writing in her class. Sometimes her essay prompts are "squishy," so if you're confused, ask questions before you start writing.

This class was hard. My lecture was focused on detective fiction. It's hard to figure out what she wants on papers, & wants things very specific. That being said, I loved Liz as a teacher. She has a strong testimony, brought us treats at least 3 times, and made the class interesting. It was hard, but I am glad I took her class.

This class is tough but Liz is a good teacher who cares about her students being more than just students. She often talked about ethics and being good citizens. She gets off topic but her side notes are not boring. Tests are long (100+ questions) and some questions are very specific. You have two creative essays to write and she wants perfection.

Wonderful class. I took masterpieces of world lit for GE credit, so we learned more about the civilizations and cultures of the masterpieces we read instead of the actual literature, but the tests reflected info from both. I did awful on the tests because I thought I could retain everything we read, but dang there was a lot of pages that we read.

Liz is funny and has good lectures, but not much else going for her. She does not work well with student who have complications with due dates, even if brought up beforehand. She is often rude, sarcastic, and unprofessional in her email responses and does not apologize for making offense. Her essay prompt are unclear but she expects perfection.

Liz is really funny and I genuinely enjoyed her lectures. However, at the beginning of the semester she said that she enjoyed general classes bc it didn't just include English majors yet she still expected perfect writing. I was looking forward to an English class that would focus on ideas rather than writer's craft but I never got it. Disappointed

She was absolutely amazing.  She is one of the best BYU professors I've ever had.  She pushes you to work hard and it's a lot of reading, but it's a fabulous class and I have benefited greatly from it.  She's also the sweetest person and loves class discussion and encourages it.

Liz is so funny in lectures, she's really easy to listen to and pay attention during class. Attendance is required. There's 5 papers over the whole semester, TAKE ADVANTAGE OF HER OFFICE HOURS. If you go in a couple, or several times to meet with her, she'll help you get an A on all your papers. Would definitely take another class from her!

This was my favorite class that I have taken at BYU thus far. Even when the material was confusing Liz made it incredibly fun and exciting to learn about. Liz genuinely cares about her students doing well and understanding the concepts in the readings. Definitely take this class from her!

Liz is really great, and overall her class was a good experience - I learned so much. Getting a good grade is not the easiest, and the homework load is rough. I would not recommend taking other classes with a heavy reading load while taking this class - but she does give substantial credit for just doing the reading. Tests are unpredictable.

Liz made lectures interesting and she was pretty funny, but I found myself getting offended on multiple occasions. She doesn't hold back in criticism, even if it makes you feel like really bad. Her emails to me when she didn't agree with my paper were sometimes hurtful. She's a hard grader. Not an easy A at all, even though she will say it is.

Liz is great & hilarious & makes the class interesting. However, the class has a lot of homework (busy work) & if you fall behind on one task it negatively affects you for the rest of the project/paper, I lost a lot of points for this. She's a tough grader & sometimes expectations aren't clear. Overall Liz is great & the class is better than others

I LOVE Liz! She is an amazing teacher.  Her class is very engaging and although literary theory is not my thing I always enjoyed her lectures.  You always have a lot of reading every class period.  As long as you keep up with it you should be okay though.  Not too many papers, and the tests are a lot but reasonable.  Sometimes she brings food!
Liz is a great professor and super funny. Took her Short Story class over Spring term and it was a laid back class but I still learned a lot. Definitely recommend her.

Liz is seriously the best! The class is tough, and very reading-heavy, but she makes it fun and manageable. The tests really aren't that difficult if you go to class and put the time in to study. Be aware that she expects all of her students to check Learning Suite daily to make sure they know what is due when. She won't remind you in class before.

I absolutely adore Liz. She's hilarious, she's sweet, she's super helpful. The class definitely had a lot of reading, but she assigns one student to every reading to make an outline, so that helps. Two papers, three tests, not bad with the study guide. Seriously, take this from her. I would take every English class from her if I could!
Liz is awesome!

She's fantastic! I feel that she really cares about her students.  The class isn't super easy, you have to make an effort, but you learn so much. And it is all very valuable knowledge. Especially for an English Major.  I would take from her again for sure!

Awesome professor who kept lectures light and easy to sit through. There is no better 311 teacher than Liz. Her grading is fair and she pushes you to become a better writer. She also brings in treats. Thanks Liz!

Liz is an incredible teacher, but demands a lot from her students. It is a lot of writing with not enough time to do it as well as you might like, but you will learn a lot. She is quite sassy and fun to work with; I would definitely recommend Liz, just be prepared to make this class your number one priority.

She knows how to teach and is very good at explaining things. She's very clear and has good speaking skills. She is nice and approachable--she's willing to work with you if need be. That being said, her English 251 class is a beast with tons of homework every night. Her tests were pretty difficult, but not if you do all homework and go to class.

Absolutely adore her. She really cares about her students' welfare, and she's really good at relaying information. Didn't enjoy the class due to the subject, but I learned a lot because of Liz. I really recommend taking this difficult class from Liz...she'll make it a little bit easier for you.

Best teacher to teach English and how to write well. Learned a lot, but unfortunately is extremely hard to get a hold of outside of class for help. Wouldn't recommend taking her for spring term because she doesn't take the time crunch into consideration for the 10-page research paper. Overall class grades suffered because of it.

Do you want to actually learn how to write and have fun doing so? This class fulfills it's purpose and Liz, yes "Liz", is an amazing teacher. She's always prepared to teach and cares a lot about her students to help them understand the core concepts of the class and help them succeed. One of THE GREATEST teachers I've had at BYU. No kidding. DO IT.

I was hesitant to take this class because it was honors, however Liz was so great. She is very approachable and willing to make time to help outside of class if you need it. Assignments and projects are outlined pretty clearly. Came to love this class and the small class size was WONDERFUL.
I do not know why other students gave that low rating. If you focus on Dr.Lamb's lecture and write it down in lecture note and practice micro exam, you will get a good grade.

This class was so awful. I ended with an A but only because of Khan Academy and self study. You cannot get ahold of her, quizzes and exams are very difficult, and there is little room for improvement.

I met with her for the first time and she proceeded to tell me to drop the class and take it in person, but that wasn't an option for me. Takes a while to get back to you in email which is difficult for it being an online class. The only nice thing is she is willing to work with you if you need to go back and relearn and will extend deadlines.

I mean I got a B+ by attending the first day of class and the final. I didn't even watch any of the recordings. She doesn't curve anything, and barely sends out emails. Chat gpt and the practice tests were my teachers.

Professor Olsen was amazing,
She was very clear on her expectation and her lessons were very interesting. There is around 3 assignments per week that are 10% of the grade, and are docked if late. Tests are 50% of the grade, and the final is 30% of the grade. To do well on the tests take good notes in class and definitely do the practice tests.

Professor Olsen is a very good teacher. I felt a little less prepared for the midterm than I wanted to be, so I'm hoping she gets better for the final. Her lessons are very good though, she's quicl to answer any question you might have. And her lectures don't leave much to question. She's a great teacher.

I think the other reviews were a little too kind and optimistic. The TAs are phenomenal, but the videos that she uses are from 2006. She does not make her own videos and relies heavily on the TAs. She is willing to meet but takes at least a few days to respond, which is not helpful. And unlike other Chem 105 classes, she really does not curve.

She is a nice professor, the 3 hour class at the SLC center didn't work well for me. She is very flexible with assignments, so if you have good time management skills, it's manageable; however, if not, I would recommend going to Provo. I found the class more challenging than it needed to be, but she is always willing to help with personal needs.

Okay I would not take her unless you totally have to. The lectures are very long and hard to stay engaged and so it is difficult. If you miss a class she always offers an online lecture but again, can be very long. I felt that the material itself was very easy, but she often explained concepts a lot harder than they actually were.

This professor was accessible even though it was an online class. She came in clutch and had mercy on me. Raised my grade from a D plus to C plus. The tests were awful. I turned in every assignment and watched every lecture. Tests are the majority of your grade. The lectures were someone else's videos. This is just a difficult class in general.

Professor Olsen is a very amazing and fair professor. The lectures and videos are long, but they do prepare you for the tests. Monday-Friday there was at least one TA available in the morning that would help you with any question you had. The class was also very organzied.

Dr. Olsen is a fabulous teacher. She does show that she cares about her students and selected awesome TAs to help us with anything we needed. 
CHEM 105 is a beast of a class and they make sure you are aware of that. If you are not self motivated, do NOT take the online version. It can be very easy to get behind and your grade will suffer.

I actually took Chem 105 online from her and when compared to other Chem teachers, she is a must. While the material was pretty hard, there was a lot of help available and each test had extra points added to it to make up for commonly missed questions. I highly recommend her.

Best teacher I have had in collge. She is great at explaining, and I rarely had to cram or study a ton before tests because assignments prepared me enough, and she was amazing at answering emails and any questions. I recommend taking at Salt lake Center because classes are smaller and once a week.

I honestly am not sure why some of the ratings on here give Sister Olsen a bad rap. Her lectures are pretty intense, but she was always double checking to see if we had questions in case we didn't understand something. She helped those who felt behind, and when I wrote down every single thing from lecture I didn't have to read the textbook.

Sister Olsen is awesome! She really cares and gives as many opportunities possible for her students to pass including: dropping the five lowest grades, sometimes extending deadlines, and responding quickly to emails. It was a lot of work, but i'd defintely take the class again.

Wanted her students to do well in class. There were three assignments on Mastering Chemistry due every week, but if you ever had a question, you could email her and she would help you find the right answer. Really nice and very willing to take extra time to make sure we understood the concepts.

The only way you'll get an A in this class is if you're just a naturally smart kid and never got a B in you're life. If you're not, then don't plan on an A. The only thing i would add to the rest of the bad reviews, is she Hopes you understand the material, not helps you understand the material. I feel bad, but don't take her. Save your GPA.

Professor Olsen flies through her lectures expecting you to know the concepts already. When asked a question in class she does everything but answers it directly. There's weekly labs that aren't actually relevant to what you need to know for the class. I basically had to go home and teach myself every day, she was that awful.

Dr. Olsen really knows her stuff. Her class is way too hard for a 101 class though. The tests are pretty hard. She does give extra credit and wants you to succeed. Just be prepared to study a lot. The first two exams are easier than the last two. Beware. Each exam is harder than the next. Just study a lot and go to the help lab and you'll be fine.

I'm awful at Chemistry so this class was tough. Olsen  is available for office hours and encourages you to ask for help. Her lectures were confusing though so be prepared to do a lot of learning on your own. You don't have to read the book, but it helps you pass the class.

Professor Olsen was just alright. The material isn't difficult, especially if you've taken chem in high school, but she's not great at explaining concepts. It felt like she was rushing through the material to fit the information into the class, instead of focusing on if we understood it. She's nice and cares about her students, but isn't great.

Professor Olsen is very interested in her students, but I had a hard time with lectures. I felt like she was often confusing. The labs didn't really help me learn the material, and I felt unprepared for most of the tests. I loved how organized MasteringChemistry is, that saved my grade.

Doctor Olsen is the nicest person.. that being said I thought her explanations of concepts were far more confusing than they needed to be.  She was always willing to help, just didn't make a ton of sense all the time

She really knows her stuff and I always thought that lectures were clear and understandable. She always helps us work through several example problems in class, and she often does fun demonstrations of the chemistry we are learning about. By far one of the better people to take the class from.

What an intelligent, yet down-to-earth teacher! This Sister really cares about students. She was kind enough to help even though I was going to audit the course. I wish she was teaching all other Chemistry classes. I wouldn't even think about other professors. I'd be in her class, hands down! The Chem department needs more of her! Speaks clearly!

Professor Olsen explains things very clearly, and will adjust lesson speed to class comprehension. Is very clear about what information is needed for tests, and sets you up extremely well for subsequent chemistry courses. Thank heavens for no iclicker quizzes, but her lectures are hand written on the board so attendance is wise.

Prof Olsen is alright. There's an online homework assignment for each lecture. I thought they were pretty easy overall, very manageable, and they helped me prepare for tests very well. The Labs are super annoying and useless. I never went to the TA reviews, but I did outside studying for the tests. The tests get harder as the class goes on.

Dr. Griffen is the best! He knows so much and there can be a lot of info in lecture, but if you pay attention are willing to think critically the tests are manageable. Exams are open note so he mostly tests application. The homework assignments build into a research proposal which was interesting.

His tests are difficult. Short answer (as in, couple words sometimes) that require recall rather than recognition. Lectures are well organized, and the study guides he gives are more useful than they may seem (seem vague, actually pretty spot on if you look through his slides).

Burnt out senior signing off here, and I have nothing but good things to say about Dr. Griffen. Yes the tests are difficult, yes there is a lot of content, but if you can make an argument that stands on its own you will do just fine. Not at all a copy and paste professor, will expect you to think. Wish he ran the whole biology department.

He's really passionate about what he teaches, and his lectures were really engaging! His tests were pretty hard and almost ALL short answer. Take good notes on lectures and fille out the study guide early and you should be good! I liked this class a lot even though the tests were tricky.

I took Dr. Griffen for ecology and half of animal diversity. Ecology was great and really interesting. The half of my animal diversity class that he taught was great! He appreciates animals and instills that in you too. In the other half of the class, it was a different professor and I didn't learn or enjoy it nearly as much.

Doctor Griffen is truly inspirational and his lectures are fascinating and hilarious, however it is a lot of information covered in a very short period of time. You should stay up to date on the readings and prepare accordingly for exams. Start filling out your study guide early on so that you have time to review it before the exam.

Took the first half of Bio 220 with him and looked at the textbook maybe once. Just go to the library if you need it. I'd highly recommend filling out the study guide as you go and then memorizing it. Tests are pretty much all short answer, but aren't horrible if you study the lecture material. Faster teaching style, but fun and interesting.

He rarely follows the textbook material during his lectures, and his exams are graded a little too arbitrarily. He also assigns a lot of busywork type assignments, but his lectures are very engaging and interesting, and overall if you come to every lecture and use the study guides for exams, you'll do just fine.

I enjoyed Dr. Griffen as a lecturer, but it was a frustrating class. Reading quizzes due before every class and few homework assignments saved my grade because the tests killed me. They were open book, but online in the testing center, and even though I went to reviews, brought in notes and the textbook I still couldn't get above an 80.

Dr. Griffen is always a fun and inspiring professor. He is super engaging in his lectures, and gives amazing feedback on assignments and tests. I learn so much each time I take a class from him. He is a tough grader, but all exams are open note open book, so all you need to do is take good notes and keep up with the class.

I loved taking marine biology from Dr. Griffen! His lectures do have a lot of information but the tests are open notes so it isn't too overwhelming. He really cares about his students and utilizes many teaching strategies to maximize his student's learning. There is no busy work in his class, everything is necessary and builds on itself.

Dr. Griffen is actually my favorite professor ever! He cares very much about students and their success. The class isn't easy, but as long as you show up and try your best, he will help in any way he can. Super accessible outside of class and very knowledgeable about the topic. Could answer any student questions. So kind and genuine!

I loved having Dr. Griffen as a professor! He taught the invertebrate section in Dr. Belk's BIO220. He is a tough grader on the exams, but his lectures are super interesting and he answers everyone's questions. He explains topics super well, and references the readings. He is super knowledgeable and loved having in class discussions.

The subject matter is a lot and pretty complex. Prof. Griffen isn't bad, but he goes through the topics very fast. Tests are very difficult and specific, the study guides aren't super helpful. Grading on tests is super tough. Not a bad professor, but not great either.

Best professor I have ever had. If I could take every class from him I would. He uses case studies and outside research for the basis of his lectures, and even though some of the material can be difficult, he explains topics very well. Exams were open book and open note, giving students the chance to apply ecological principles to situations. 11/10

This was an alright class. Tons of readings and the exams were pretty difficult. Dr. Griffen is a great person and his lectures were pretty engaging, however, he expects you to think and know things as if you are an ecologist with years of experience. If the class as a whole does poorly on an exam, he does offer question redo's which was nice.

Dr Griffen was great for the capstone course. Very reasonable expectations and made the course about learning and practicing real world skills (not memorization). Most of the class was a group project, which went about like any other group project.

Dr. Griffen is an awesome professor, he is very knowledgeable and engaging. The textbook for this course is very helpful if you do the readings. Class assignments are graded lightly and are very forgiving (you get unlimited attempts on the reading quizzes) He replies quickly to emails and is willing to work with his students.

My favorite prof. Super engaging in class, and makes a huge effort to teach in several different styles so everyone gets it. There are required readings and short quizzes before class to introduce you to the material and he goes more in depth with examples and practice exam q's in class. Overall an awesome guy, super approachable, kind, and funny.

With COVID we've been doing online classes, and that honestly sucks. But Dr. Griffen is incredibly understanding and recognizes how hard online learning is. He is very accommodating in tests in exchange for simple participation and is an incredible professor who really knows his stuff.

Dr. Griffen is such an inspiring and fair professor. He was always quick to respond to emails and very willing to help students. The textbook used for this class was my favorite textbook I've ever had - very easy to read. He doesn't give busywork - every assignment is meaningful and interesting. I loved this class. One of my favorite professors!

Good guy. Great teacher. Great scientist. He knows a lot about how real world science works but it is different from BYU's expectations. I.e. he expects you to be able to do math, BYU (according to major requirements) does not. If you do what BYU wants, you will be unprepared for his classes and do poorly. Tests are crazy messed up. Odd situation.

The class was okay, but the tests were insane. I filled out his entire study guide and went through every single powerpoint slide. (It was probably like 300). I still did bad on his exams. It is a lot of material. Even though the grading is extremely hard, the content of the class is still interesting.

I had Dr. Griffen for Bio 220 and enjoyed it, but Bio 350 was totally different story. His test questions are ridiculously hard. Choose free-response tests over multiple choice if he ever gives you a choice. He won't show the tests to TAs, so they can't help you much. Reading quizzes actually affect your grade so make sure to read the textbook.

I really like Professor Griffen as a person, however not so much as a teacher. He was good at keeping class interesting, however when it came to tests it was hard to know what he was looking for at times. Some questions were just plainly poorly written. Very strict on late work, and you have to read the book before each class to do well.

Bio 220 was pretty great, but it was frustrating being in Bio350. Lots of busy work. His way or the highway on homework that felt open ended. Very strict late work policy. He is big on grad school, but gives no way to make up work when you go for interviews. Iclicker quizzes on obsolete reading points & doesn't drop any. Bad at test writing.

I took Dr. Griffin for Bio 220 and it was hard but not terrible. Ecology has been a nightmare. Easy material. Tons of busy work (weekly homework, writings, class discussions, etc.). Tests are extremely difficult and Im a 4.0 student. They are poorly written (lots of mistakes, very guess what Im thinking). 94 for an A. Avoid at all costs.

He can be really unkind and belittling. He gives lots of opportunities to participate in class but isn't afraid to tell you what he thinks of your comments or questions, highlighting your ignorance or telling you he thinks your opinion is dumb. The material isn't difficult, and he teaches pretty well. He's unwelcoming in office hours. Tough tests.

He loves his subject, but he kind of treats you like you are dumb. I used to ask lots of questions, but he just treated me like an idiot in class. He has a hard time with anyone having a different perspective than his. I took him for both bio 220 and bio 350.. he was ruder in bio 350. His tests are "guess what I am thinking".

Bio 220 was a manageable class. I took it when he had just started at BYU, but I found him very approachable and nice. Tests were long and were only free-response, but they weren't too bad. Everything came from his lecture slides. Taking Bio 350 from him right now and it's a whole other story. Only multiple choice tests and much harder.

I really enjoyed Griffen's lectures. Tons of information with every class. It was really difficult to prepare for tests because he wasn't specific about what we needed to know. Some topics were general many were crazy specific.

Professor Griffen absolutely loves what he teaches, and lectures are fun and involved. However, he believes that you should really prepare on your own for the test, and the TA is not allowed to see the test before hand, so the reviews are basically just going over the slides. The tests were open answer, and our only grades pretty much.

I took math 302 from professor Barker and he was great! Definitely difficult content however professor Barker was helpful and mindful of making sure we understood, so kind and very funny! Lots of homework, one for each lecture and it was mandatory. Tests were hard but sample exams were similar.

I just might not do well in classes that are only meant to be lectures with basically no group work, especially with math. I don't learn well on my own, but hot dang, this guy moved at light speed through the material. Probably gonna take the class again cause i don't understand anything after having taken it
Amazing professor, had him for math 302 and was great at teaching and responding and adapting to feedback
This guy makes no sense. Class is disorganized across multiple platforms /textbooks. Luckily content is super easy so teaching yourself is within reason.

It was Dr. Barker's first time teaching MATH213, so there was an adjustment for the first few days. I also took it during spring term, so the class was fast-paced, but manageable. I appreciated the way he responded to student questions and concerns in class--with respect. It really felt like he was genuinely invested in helping students succeed.

Math 290 is hard no matter what. Dr Barker was a fairly good professor overall. He was not a superb lecturer, but definitely more than adequate. We had Dr. Anderson sub for us a few times, and he was amazing. Dr. Barker is more quiet and soft spoken, but he's very kind, and is good with precision in his explanations. His grading is more than fair.

Professor Barker was one of the best professors I have ever had! He creates a super safe classroom environment where it is easy to relax and focus on learning instead of worrying about what others think. He truly cares about his student and takes time to carefully analyze and thoroughly discuss questions. His class is lots of work but worth it.
