Professor Barker TRULY wants all his students to succeed. This class is difficult, not cause of him, but cause of the info that is covered. But he has the best heart and is so fun. I say attendance isn't mandatory only cause you do HW in class, lectures were uploaded. Tests were easier than HW, but still hard. If you need to take 290, take from him

good guy, good teacher, terrible class. Please don't take this as a criticism of Dr. Barker, but as a a criticism of the applied math major's class structure. This class was not ready to be taught. Overall it wasn't too difficult of a class, homework was relatively easy and quick and the tests weren't too bad either. I didn't learn much though.

Very sweet person. Incredible difficulty explaining hard concepts and answering on the spot questions. Lectures are not very helpful, nor are office hours. If you take from him, it's probably best to use the TA or math lab.
Very nice guy. Hard time teaching you something that you don't already have an understanding of, difficulty answering on the spot questions. Tests aren't nearly as bad as the homework.

It was clear that he was still figuring out the class when he taught it to us, but he's a good teacher. The midterm projects were where I learned the most, but they were sometimes difficult, confusing, and very time-consuming.

Dr. Barker is the best. He genuinely cares about his students and is very kind one-on-one. The material in Math 290 can be a bit dry, but as far as Dr. Barker is concerned, he is always willing to help and does his best to answer any questions and to make everyone feel comfortable in class. I would definitely recommend taking from him!

Dr. Barker was great, he is very approachable and is good at explaining different proofing techniques. I really enjoyed him as a professor and it made 290 a little more bearable. But if your not a huge fan of proofs and you don't have to take 290 don't. HW takes FOR-EV-ER.

The content of this class was extremely challenging. Professor Barker is a nice professor and the TA grading the homework is very lenient, but there is absolutely no extra credit offered (he made that clear), and the essay portions of tests require absolute memorization of proofs. Homework takes about 1-3 hours per assignment, due every class.

Math 290 isn't an easy class. But, Dr. Barker was good at explaining the concepts in an accessible way. One nice thing was that Dr. Barker didn't just lecture during class, he really got us involved with group activities. He also had us practice writing proofs together and gave us opportunities in class to participate. Great professor!

Dr. Barker is a great guy, he has a hard time understanding questions on the spot but it doesn't get too much in the way of the lectures. Go to office hour if you don't understand something in lecture. Math 290 is a really hard class because it introduces you to higher level math, but he helps make it manageable. Tests are MUCH easier than HW.
He is helpful and caring to others. There was some frustration when we had to take a large reading test that the state required, but he helped us through it.

I took CPSE 203! Professor Blake Hansen is an incredible teacher. He Cares a lot about his students and will answer any questions whenever questions are asked. He is very funny and loves what he teaches. This class was all about experience and he wants his students to succeed. I would 100% take another class from Professor Blake Hansen !!

I took CPSE 410 from Professor Hansen and he's a super nice guy, but not a great professor. Every class felt exactly the same, and it got boring really fast. The assignments were super confusing, and he wasn't good at answering questions or explaining things. He basically gave us all the answers for the final though, so that was nice.

I honestly didn't learn anything from Blake's class. His lectures were always kind of random and off topic. He was always adding random quizzes and never did what he said he would. He was hard to communicate with and he didn't grade almost anything until finals were over. He's a very smart man but he is lazy and doesn't know how to teach.

Professor Hansen's heart is the right place, but his class was a mess. He thew out half the assignments and the ones that were still there didn't make much sense. I don't think he cared about the class very much. That being said, it was also pretty easy to get a good grade.
Pretty easy class, and I loved Dr. Jones! There was kind of a lot of reading and writing, but it was all pretty easy.
He's an excellent professor who cares about students. Tests are really straightforward, easy.
Not too much work and very easy. Follow the rubrics and you will do well. Not the most exciting class by nature of the content but Jones is a good option. Very understanding and kind!

I have never ever once wanted to make one of these but Dr.Jones is SO amazing I just felt like I had to come on to brag about him. He does a great job at making a typically hard class manageable, and you can tell he really cares about his students and their success. I always felt comfortable coming to him for help or with questions!

Dr. Jones is the best! Not only was he very helpful in class, he was always up to meet / help outside of class as well. He is so supportive and truly cares about the success of his students. Would 100% recommend him as a professor. Also, his research sounds so cool, so look in to that too!

Attendance is taken with short, easy quizzes at the start of each class, and the class itself was pretty straightforward. There are kind of a lot of assignments, but they're not too bad. Class average is an A, so definitely not a super hard class. The professor is also super caring and is understanding when you have to miss class.

I always roll my eyes when I see reviews saying "they care so much!!!" but I'm serious when I say he does care. There was a quiz on the reading every class and if he saw enough confused looks on a question he would give us the answer. He also provided candy during the final. Prof Jones taught the material in a way that related to life.
Take 310 from Dr. Jones- you won't regret it! You learn so much and there aren't unnecessary assignments

I know the class has been restructured since I took the class, but if you do the readings you will be okay. He plays lots of funny clips and the content is genuinely interesting. The year starts off slow, but picks up into more interesting topics. Does cover the brain and its functions, but that isn't the main focus of class.
Professor Jones is awesome! He really cares about his students and wants to help. The class is easy as long as you stay on top of your work. Definitely take psych 310 from him!

Professor Jones is awesome! I would highly recommend taking a psychology class from him. His lectures are super interesting, and he gives you just the right amount of assignments. If you are willing to put some work in, you will do just fine. Tests can be a little tricky since they are application based but study and it is awesome!

Take Psych 111 from Prof. Jones. His class is super easy. You could easily take this class without going to lectures, I did though because he was interesting and told stories and showed tv clips to help us understand concepts. There's an easy 5 question quiz online with every class, and a few papers throughout the year. Nothing too tough though.

Super nice guy, he had the class set up so you could pretty much succeed with just doing the readings from the free online textbook and papers/quizzes. I went to lectures in part to review material and in part just to hear his awesome stories and examples. You need to make sure to do things on time, but he gives you plenty of heads up.

Dr. Jones is awesome. I loved his class, I felt as though learning about psychology was a pleasure to do and not something I had to do. He had very fun lectures and the class structure was very good. I didn't too amazing in the class, but that was a lack of effort on my part. Awesome class!

Really nice guy. I rarely went to the lectures, but when I did they were very engaging. He posts all his slides and the TA reviews are really good. The tests cover a lot of material but if you watch the TA reviews and make flash cards you'll be chillin.

Dr. Jones was my favorite professor this year. Some people don't like him because they think he tells too many stories that aren't relevant, but this is exactly why I liked him so much. Dr. Jones is kind, loving, smart, and engaging. He has so many inspirational stories to tell that teach us about psych, and his little twin daughters are so cute!

I love Dr. Jones because he was so caring and thoughtful, but he was a little dry sometimes in class. I also noticed that in some of my other psychology/sfl classes we were taught the same concepts but differently than he taught so that was interesting. He made it interesting and was very humble and the sweetest person I have ever met.

I looooved this class! The content might not have been super interesting but Dr. Jones did a great job of explaining the concepts in interesting ways. The group project was really fun and there's one big paper, but he broke it up into small assignments throughout the semester so it wasn't hard at all. I would recommend this class to anyone!

Dr. Jones was fantastic. His lectures were entertaining, enlightening, and informational. I always enjoyed going to class. My one complaint is that the tests always caught me off guard as they were more difficult than I expected, so you may have t study a bit more. TA reviews are super helpful.

THIS professor is SO SO good! He tells the funniest stories that relate to the content he is teaching and it helped me remember everything. His tests were so fair and I would say pretty easy. You just have an online reading and 5 question quiz every day you have class. If you put in the effort you will get a good grade.

I love Dr. Jones! There is no textbook, only online readings that are free. It's required to read them before class but it is so much better than an actual textbook. He is super engaging and clear in his lectures and cracks a lot of jokes and shows videos to help us grasp concepts. Great guy and great professor!

Attendance is not mandatory but I highly recommend that you go. There are a few topics on each day that are not included in the reading but he goes over it during lectures. You have access to lecture slides but they're only the student version so not everything is on there. Its a fairly easy class just attend the lectures

The lectures were engaging, and it was clear that Dr. Jones cared about all of us. He incorporated lots of videos and stories that demonstrated the topics. He provides a lot of help and is very clear on the assignments. I enjoyed the class and learned a lot from it. I recommend it for the general science credit.

Dr. Jones is so nice and caring & he is very genuine. I really loved this class and it made me love psychology even more. The workload is totally doable. He makes lectures so interesting and tells the coolest stories. He also shows a lot of clips from The Office and other funny shows to help you learn the material better. Take Psych 111 from him!!

Dr. Jones is a great guy! This class could be hard for me to focus on because of the online format in the morning, but I still feel like I learned a lot. He's very passionate about the subject and cares for the students.
Great class; Professor Jones does his best to teach psychology while encouraging students to use it to improve their own lives. He also has great TAs. Highly recommend.

I liked the structure of class & appreciated the free online textbook. I liked learning about psychology, however, the lectures were very surface level, the tests had material we never went over, we didn't know what to focus in the reading, etc. I had an 89.6 but Prof. Jones wouldn't bump me up. I lost unnecessary points on projects too from the TA

LONG online reading assignments to say there's "no textbook" Test questions are based heavily on trivial information from the readings. Lectures do NOT prepare you for anything in the daily/weekly quizzes, or for midterms/finals. Fairly easy grader as far as papers and projects go - that's the only perk though. policy not to bump grades.

Professor Jones cares not only that you learn principles of psychology, but that they take a meaningful place in your life. Every week I found myself relating random life events to something we discussed in lecture; I would self-evaluate myself and adjust my behaviors. The tests were pretty hard, but not impossible. I highly recommend for anyone.
Dr. Jones is a very kind man and is very understanding. His lectures are always very thought out and he is does a great job of teaching the material in a way that is easy to understand.

This was easily one of my favorite classes I've taken! Dr. Jones is the best and I think everyone should take Psych from him whether they need to or not. Lectures are engaging and prepare you perfectly for tests. No textbook, just super helpful online reading! Take note of the daily quiz questions because they are very similar to test questions.

He is super chill and nice, and he tried to make his lectures engaging. Homework is not that hard, but the tests are not written well and can be challenging. You have to read one article per class, then have a quiz about the reading. Weekly connection papers are basically graded by completion and are only one page, with one goal-tracking project.

Reading quizzes during every class. Lots of reading, but it's interesting. Tests are mostly MC, but there are some essay questions. He really cares about his students and wants to help in anyway he can.

I love Dr. Jones! He gave amazing lectures and I was always excited to come to class. I'm not big on psychology, but he made me LOVE it! There is reading before every class that's online and then he gives you a quiz at the start of each class to see if you read, but I LOVED the articles and reading them, so it didn't even feel like homework. Study!

Prof. Jones is by far the most fair professor I have ever had. He trusts his students and treats them like adults. He tries not to make things too difficult, but watch out for the tests, just in case. There isn't a textbook for this class (which is amazing); instead, he asks you to read articles written by actual researchers in the field.
Honestly one of the best classes I've taken at BYU , this class helped me to want to change my major to Psychology. He is super funny and really caring. Definitely take this class from Him.

Blake Jones has by far been my favorite teacher at BYU so far! He has some crazy stories that really help you to learn and remember the things you learned in class. All of the class work and homework is super easy, you do have to read and show up to class though. Tests are easy if you study the definitions. I loved this class, take it from him!!

I LOVE Dr. Jones! I learned so much from him in this class, he teaches in a way that's totally engaging and makes you want to learn. You have an article to read online before each class and then take a quiz on what you read at the beginning which you're graded on, so make sure to do all you reading and show up for class! Tests are straightforward!
I loved this class so much! Dr. Jones is amazing. He taught in a way that was engaging, humorous, and that helped me grow intellectually and spiritually too

Wow, Dr. Jones is the best. Very understanding and will work with you for whatever you need. Exams and other assignments are super straightforward. He doesnt require you to have a textbook but has enjoyable reading assignments with quizzes for each lecture. He is super helpful and engaging. I would take him again in a second.

I love Professor Jones! You can tell he is an all around good person and he makes lectures fun and interesting! He has one assigned article to read before each class and you don't even have to pay for a textbook. There is a short quiz at the beginning of each class about the reading, 2 midterms and 1 final exam. Take Psych from him!

He is an awesome professor, funny and caring he really tries to give the students their best chance to succeed. It's an easy A as long as you do the readings and go over the lecture slideshows before taking the test you should do well. The readings are all online so no buying a book.

Dr. Jones is definitely who you want to take 310 from. In comparison to the other professors, his work load is much more doable. He is super accessible and willing to meet with students for any questions. You have textbook readings and quizzes in class every day, but the readings aren't very long and the textbook reads pretty easy.
I don't have too much of an opinion. Super nice guy, but not interesting to listen to. I will say, though, that the semester project with him is WAY easier than with other 310 professors.
Proffesor Jones was really awesome. He's a very nice guy and I learned a lot in his class.

Dr. Jones is one of the best professors I have had so far at BYU. Class is easy, there is a study guide for all the tests. Just memorize the terms and you'll do fine. There are iClicker quizzes every class and class reflections every week that count for a good part of your grade, so you will not be able to skip and get an A. Show up and your good

Prof. Jones is pretty funny, and he makes the subject matter very interesting and relatable. His lectures and test material come straight from the before class readings, so taking notes on the them would be a good idea.
Dr. Jones was amazing!! If you are going to take psychology, take it from him!! He will help you do well!! Seriously such a nice guy that genuinely cares about his students!
Dr. Jones is the best. He is super caring and passionate about what he teaches. He wants his students to succeed and is just a genuine, kind person.

He is an AMAZING Professor. Kind, compassionate, and makes a huge effort to make his lectures fun and entertaining by providing funny videos. The tests are pretty specific but he gives you a study guide beforehand that covers everything in the test. Clicker quizzes every class but he is super lenient grading them. Hard not to like him honestly.

This teacher is amazing! He spends a lot of time talking about why the concept works, and not really how the concept works so you can apply it to all different problems. He cares a lot about his students and he's a super sweet person. He tells funny stories in class. Overall he is an amazing teacher and you should def take CALC 1 from him.

FANTASTIC choice for calc 1. Just enough homework to make you learn it well enough to succeed on the tests. I usually skipped the lab sessions with the TAs unless I had a question with the homework, then that was a good time to better learn and understand. Tests were ALL written, never multiple choice. THIS IS A GOOD THING trust 💯

Overall Professor Peterson is an amazing teacher and person. His goal to have the students understand the math concepts not just plug and chug numbers. This was not my first time taking Calculus One, and with that being said it was difficult to score an 'A' in this class. Grades will come down to the mid-terms (entirely free response) and the final

I LOVED having Dr. Peterson! He cares so much about the well being of his students. For MATH 112, he teaches it differently than the other professors. I understood more of the concepts and material he taught. He found it more important that we knew what we were doing and why, rather than getting the right answers, which is amazing! Take his class!

If you are taking this for your major but aren't planning on pursing math any further, take a different professor. You can use a scientific calculator (not graphing) on the midterms, but you can't on the final. Homework is worth like 20% of your grade, the rest is tests. He knows a lot, but doesn't teach simply or prepare you well for the tests.

Dr. Peterson is fantastic at directing class time to understanding how math works. If you are a plug-and-chug kind of math-goer, you may not like math 112 from him. I loved how accessible he and the TAs were outside of class, and how prepared I felt for each test because of the HW and Written HW.

Professor Peterson is a fairly good teacher. He's very personable but the lectures are dry and sleep-inducing (I don't suggest taking his class in the morning). Do know that he expects explanations during the tests on how you found your answer (on the first test he didn't explain this) and tests take up the biggest portion of your grade.

Dr. Peterson is the best!! He makes difficult concepts much easier to understand, and he always walks the class through his thought process when working on difficult problems. There is a fair amount of homework, but never overwhelming. The TAs are very accessible, and the recitation/lab hours are super helpful for going over concepts.

Great teacher but what he taught had little to do with elementary education. Taught concepts I didn't go over in high school. Only section that requires an actual math textbook ($170!). Exams & final were difficult but do-able. Graded daily homework. Def. take him if you're shooting for middle school, if not, find another teacher.
Very helpful.  Doctor Peterson is probably the best professor that I have ever had.  He makes going to class enjoyable, and he is a super nice guy.
Dr. Peterson is great. He is the only 112 teacher that allows a calculator on tests! I would HIGHLY recommend Dr.Peterson as a teacher. Very clear lectures.

It had been 5 years since I had taken Calculus, so I was nervous going in, but Dr Peterson was an absolutely amazing professor. Make sure you go to class, go to lab, and do your homework

He created tests from scratch and based everything from the HW.  READ: If you do your homework and understand it, you will pass the test.  Very helpful

Dr. Peterson is quite helpful. He teaches for practicality and understands we'll apply the math in real life situations. He allows graphing calculators on tests. Extremely helpful.  The tests were extremely similar to the homework, so if you could do all of the homework problems you could do everything on the test.  All homework was helpful, but nightly so you have to stay on top of things

If you can take MthEd 305 or 306 from Dr. Peterson, do it!  Homework and tests are challenging, but definitely doable.  The class is very well organized. I had him for both MathEd117 and 218. I plan on taking every class possible from him. He pushes you and helps you to really understand concepts rather than just procedures. Blake Peterson is an awesome guy!  He is so accomodating and an overall great teacher.  I have learned so much from him and he has really helped me understand how to become an excellent mathematics teacher.  I love going to his class  and feel that the work load is definitely doable.  Take from him if you have the chance.  He's great!

She also shortened all the readings and took us on field trips. I recommend taking univ from her because she doesn't expect as much from you as some professors do.

I really enjoyed this class. I'm interested in User Experience Design, so it was topically relevant to me. We had lots of fun in-class activities and even got to use an eye-tracker to test website usage. Dr. Anderson always learns everyone's names and cares about her students.

The class consists mostly of common sense readings and lots of video clips. Everyone gets A's on assignments so in the end your participation grade determines the curve, which is mostly based on attendance. The class does not feel like a graduate-level course and I would not take Dr. Anderson unless you have to.
Great class. Loved learning about project management and system design. Set up a great foundation for the rest of the program. She is awesome.
She's a nice lady. The course wasn't so nice.

Professor Anderson is top-notch.  She really knows her subject because she has both industry experience and excellent academic credentials to back up her perspective.  When you go to class, be alert and take it seriously; you will learn a lot.

Wow, I can't believe some people are saying she is a bad professor... trust me, I've had bad professors, and she definitely isn't one of them! She's a good teacher, and she gets to know all of her students' names. And for the bonus point, she watches things like the Colbert Report, so you tell me, how cool is she? (spoiler alert: Very Cool)
Class was fun.  She learned all of our names.
I thought she was a decent teacher. I also thought it was funny because anytime something went wrong she always through one of her colleagues under the bus. Helpful and Pleasant

I think Prof. Anderson is a great teacher, she's really down to earth, made class fun and enjoyable. She's super knowledgable, really she's just interesting to talk to and pretty funny. I liked the class, it thought a lot of helpful stuff, but mainly if you're looking at who to take for ISYS 201, I would definitely recommend Anderson

I found the class material to be interesting and really not that hard, but the way its taught in class makes it confusing. There seemed to be a large disconnect between class, assignments, and the final test, as if each were being done by a different teacher.

Poor experience. Wasted time with videos and games in class, only to send you home with a beastly assignment that no one knew how to do. She consistently taught us how to do stuff for the first time literally minutes before handing out the test. There were a few guys who were vocal and she just assumed everyone else knew what they were doing too.

She is awesome! very fair and funny.  Tons of sweet videos in class.  You do need to do all your reading before class for your grade. Once you get past that, you'll enjoy your life in the MISM. Fo real.

She is very helpful and does well at explaining the things you  need to know.  The class is a big class and they need to have a curve so expect to work to get an "A".  You may consider taking it spring/summer, I hear it's much easier.  All in all it was a good and not terribly difficult class.

Anderson is a good teacher.  A lot of the problems in the class reflect more the ISYS department's decisions on how the class should be run(such as some stupid test questions and some out-dated information), not the teacher.  However, as a teacher, she did a good job of preparing her students for the tests and homework.  I'd try and get her.

Hmm...nice lady.  an annoying class but what do you expect.  she knows everyones name which is cool (its a huge class)  take it from her if you can.  pray for a good TA (he grades everything) the final was a beast.  i barely read at all...skimmed before class for the quizzes...memorized the vocab for the final and got an A.  so there ya go.
I thought Prof Anderson was an awesome teacher. She is more than accommodating and honestly tries to get to know all of her students.  I would recommend her!

Easy class if you have a computer background.  One of the few teachers i've had who knows your name the first day.  Students tend to get higher grades in her classes, or so i understand
Compared to the other ISys 201 teachers, Prof. Anderson explains the topics the best. Her classes end up scoring higher on tests and projects than other sections.

Dr. Anderson is one of those people that you get along with or you don't.  She does prepare you well for the exams but she did say a lot of things that were useless.  The class is very unorganized. Her class was easy, and the material was interesting.  Unfortunately she doesn't actually understand computers.  If you come into the class understanding computers well, then you'll just have to tune her out, because alot of her material is outdated, simplistic, or just plain wrong.  Unfortunately, from what I hear she's better than the others.

If you are taking this class, she is definitely the teacher to get.  She is nice and wants her students to do well.  The test can be a little tough though, but the tests are the same for every ISYS 201 class, and she prepares you the best.

The class isn't scattered brain... she is!!  The class is easy if you pay attention in lecture...but she does tend to add info that you'll never be tested on or only see if your major in IS.  As a finance major, I could have cared less...

Dr. Anderson is great!  I loved her class and the way she taught.  She definitly prepares you for the tests well.  She cares about getting to know her students and is extremely helpful.  Class goes fast, even though it is an hour and a half, lecture plus some type of activity.  Definitly reccommended.
She is the best teacher. She will prepare you for the tests better than the other teachers. Go to her reviews for the test and if you memorized what she teaches.... You will do fine. She is great
Great class, she is the BEST 201 teacher by far. Nothing cooler than a women who knows computers.
The class is kind of scatter-brained, but Dr. Anderson is good. She is smarter than the other 201 professors, and seems to care more about the students. I am glad I took it from her.
Dr. Anderson is awesome!  I would highly recommend taking her classes.

I really enjoyed COMD133 with Professor Brinton. She has a fun sense of humor and incorporates relevant videos to help facilitate learning. Going to class is important because she doesnt post the lecture slides. Theres also only a few things that go into the grade book so you need to attend to take the quizzes. The class is definitely doable!

Your grade is based almost entirely on pop quizzes and tests. There is sometimes advance warning on the pop quizzes, but the questions are all random, specific facts from the slides. Tests are tricky (a lot of A, B, C, A&B, A&C, all of the above types), so go to the TA reviews. Also she talks very quickly and it's hard to tell what to write down.

She is so funny and has great lectures! I enjoyed coming to class. She has "pop" quizzes but told us about them the class before. One or two of the lectures were a bit disorganized, but the TAs can help make things clearer.

Dr. Brinton is an amazing professor who really cares for her students. She is the funniest and cutest lady ever! The only issue I had with the class was the exams... there is only a midterm and a final, but the wording on the exams is VERY tricky. I'd recommend going to office hours and all of the reviews!

She is a great teacher and really cares about what she teaches. The problem is, she won't post her slides so the whole class all you are trying to do is frantically write them down and you don't get to learn much from what she explains. Your 2 tests are 75% of your grade and the 5 pop quizzes are the other 25%

She's the best! Such an interesting course and her passion and wit makes it that much more fun! The course material can be tricky but she takes the time and is always willing to see you after class. Exams are totally fair. They are based only on what was on her slides from class so I'd recommend regular attendance. Love her!

Dr. Brinton is so nice and you can really tell that she cares about what she does! Her excitement about communication disorders is contagious and there's not a class that I went to that she didn't make me smile. The class is easy, just make sure you study for the Midterm and Final because those are what pretty much make up your grade.

Go to class and take good notes and that will save you haha! Dr. Brinton is so fun and awesome, but the exams and quizzes are hard. Also I only looked at the textbook twice; everything you need to know is from her lectures.

Dr. Brinton is a fantastic professor. She is very passionate about what she teaches. She explains things quite well but does not post the slides so going to class is a must. I did not use the textbook and was fine. Just make sure to take good notes in class if you don't get the book. Making a study group will definitely be helpful!
THERE IS NO HOMEWORK! Only studying for tests which is VERY important because grades are primary based off the test. I learned a lot in that class and the material is easy to understand.

Dr. Brinton's lectures are hilarious and entertaining, however she makes sure you learn the material. She warns you when there's a pop quiz. The TA reviews are helpful for the midterm and final. What I liked about this class is that the difficulty of the quizzes and tests made me actually learn the material, which will help later on with the major.

Great teacher. Her quizzes can be a little difficult but once you figure out how to study for her class they aren't that hard. She cares about her students and has a deep love for the field and it shines through in her teaching. A fantastic teacher; would take another class with her in the future in a heartbeat.

The class was great covered a lot of stuff and gave a great overview of the major. Go to her office hours so she knows you! She offered a review for me because she knew me. Go to TA reviews. And tests determine your grade by far. Overall a good class.

Dr. Brinton is hilarious. I loved her intro to ComD class. Grades are based on a few announced quizzes in class, one paper and two tests. Doesn't post slides online so attendance and notetaking are mandatory.

Professor Brinton is an amazing professor. She is very inspirational and passionate about her field. She gives pop quizzes, but tells you when they are, so they are not really 'pop'. She also only grades on a few assignments, so as long as you do well on them, the course is great. I would highly recommend Professor Brinton to anyone!

If you think you might want to major in ComD, Dr. Brinton will help you find your passion for it. She loves what she does, and she knows what she is talking about. 133 is an intro course so she is really just touches on the basics, and doesn't expect you to know a bunch of complex stuff. There are 6  pop quizzes, but she tells you when they will be

Dr. Brinton is hilarious! The class is purely lecture based, but she makes them very entertaining and engaging. She doesn't post her ppts online, so you need to take good notes. I did bad on first exam, started going to Dr.G office hours and did much better after. Make sure you sit by TA for in class extra credit. Don't take if you cant go to Dr.G and the TAs.

This class is extremely difficult. Our first exam average was 62%, higher than last semester's 58%. When asked about the low scores, he just said “study harder.” I felt confident with the material, but his tests are ridiculously tricky and cover concepts we never learned. Save yourself, your GPA, and your sanity and DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!

I like Dr. Gassaway. He is understanding, very smart, adaptable, and even humble. This was his first time teaching this course. Inevitably, the course is not yet perfect. The expectations were vague: obscure questions, specific answers expected. You need to work with TAs to get good grades. Read the book! Even if you can get by with little reading.

His first semester ever teaching a class, of course there were issues to be fixed. He listened to feedback and I feel confident he'll keep adapting the course. His 1st test was impossible but the rest were reasonable. 
His class made all other classes look that followed easy because of the depth. Go to as many office hours as you can

Its not an easy class but that's because its BIO CHEM. Work with him and he'll help you out. He's very helpful. Take the class seriously because the content is hard just like O CHEM. All his work does prep you for any field in science.
His class is probably the toughest I have taken at BYU. However, as I am studying for standardized tests, I find myself appreciating how deep I had to dive into the subject.
Good man. Just not a good professor. He had ample opportunities to make up for big mistakes on his part for our class but didn't follow through.

Yes, this class was a beast and Professor Gassaway's exams were some of the most challenging I've ever taken at BYU, but it's possible to succeed. After each midterm, significant extra credit was offered in-class and TA's and the professor were very helpful in preparing for the exams. If you take this class, be ready to spend a lot of time studying

Before this class, I had a 4.0 GPA. This was the most difficult course I have ever taken. The tests are ridiculously hard, and he doesn't cover everything in lecture, so you have no idea what will be on the tests. Homework is impossible without TA help and it doesn't really apply to the content. Lectures are disorganized and have no flow to them.

Dr. Gassaway is a very nice and intelligent person. However, this was his first semester teaching and it didn't go amazing. Hhis lectures were a lot of talking. My biggest issue with the class is his expectations were not clear at all. I think as he teaches more he can iron this out, but it was very frustrating.

The class average was 86, which is pretty high for a chem class. He gave a lot of extra credit for exams. It was a bit confusing to know what material was needed for the first exam, but for the next exams, he was clear. I put in ab 2 hours each week and then an extra 4 hours on the week of an exam, and was the 98th percentile. Just go over slides.

There are some positive ratings for this professor. If you value your gpa, a social life, or the potential to go to med school, ignore them and DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! However, if you'd like to give up your social life and live and breathe biochemistry for a semester, and have a mental breakdown every exam then by all means, it's your life.

Take it from a student who earned an A in this class, do not take it from Dr. Gassaway. Chem 481 is difficult but he makes it impossible to be successful because of his lack of preparation on what he's teaching. The tests have unclear questions with multiple answers and the homework is completely unrelated. Do not take from this from Gassaway!

Worked harder in this class than I did in any other class I've had but still couldn't figure out how to do well. Tests are VERY difficult and seem to require additional knowledge outside what we learned in class and what is found in powerpoints and HW. However, he is a new professor, and I could see him changing some things for the better.

Worst class I've taken at BYU by far. His lectures and slides are impossible to follow + full of irrelevant tangents about his research. He's extremely vague about test content, doesn't make practice exams, and TAs give conflicting advice because they don't know whats going on. DO NOT take from him if you want to actually learn and get a good grade

Would not recommend taking this class. Homework's were close to impossible without going to office hours for help. Tests were confusing and often had multiple correct answers with only one marked as correct. Lectures were confusing. More difficult than Ochem solely because it was not clear what you should know. Nice guy, poor lecturer.

It was extremely confusing to know what to study for throughout the whole class. There is so much information and the guidance is minimal at best. Good guy, but man the tests are rough. Preparing and taking those exams made me appreciate the little things in life.

The tests are SO hard. He is the most incoherent professor I have ever had. The test questions and slides are so convoluted. Even the TAs were confused. Take this class from literally any other professor

I wish I can give him a 4.5 but there's no such that choice. 0.5 off just because Dr. G's exam is EXTREMELY HARD (or maybe i wasn't study that hard since the class average is 86...). Other than that, he is a smart person (if you know his experience, ok he got into his phd progam at yale while also did the folk dance team in byu) and class  are fun!

Super nice guy, tough tests. Homework due every week, if you work with the ta's on it it's straightforward. iClicker for class participation (drops some though). Tests are long, and pretty difficult, but he does a mini in-class test retake where you can retake the 15 most missed multiple choice question for 15 extra credit points. Nice guy.

I finally felt the chemistry — in Dr. G's classroom. His lectures are exothermic: they give energy instead of draining it. He's a true catalyst, lowering the activation energy for learning. Zero negative ions in this class — all positive vibes. On the fence? That's your titration endpoint. Take it. He's the gold standard — Au-some, even.

My 4th year in STEM & I am dead serious when I say he is the worst professor I have ever had at BYU & I have had some bad professors! He was very smart though & knows a lot! The only saving grace for this class is the exams aren't weighted super heavy. Lectures are very confusing & would often be an information overload. You have to teach yourself.

Throughout the semester, there was no clear path to success. Besides that, it is an amazing opportunity to learn from his knowledge and expertise, as well as from the promptings of the spirit.

I took his 2-hour Eternal Families Class. He's honestly great. He's quirky and will keep you entertained. There are some papers you have to write, but they are not bad. His tests are in the testing center, but again, not bad. Honestly, the dude was probably one of my favorite professors.

Great Professor, he comes well prepared for all lectures with interesting, relevant content. Participation is required, come to class expecting to be actively engaged. If his class works for your schedule then consider taking him as your professor.
He was great very passionate about the subject. Had really good discussions I never got bored in his class.

Professor is awesome! You can really tell he has a passion for what he teaches, and he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. The class itself was pretty manageable, but don't sleep on the exams—they can be a little more challenging than you might think, but not too bad. Definitely put in the time to go over the study guide and slides.

This class was a seminary class. Not only was it super easy, but it was boring and I didn't learn anything. He teaches mostly his own opinion/soapbox which is very frustrating and then he tests you on what was said in class. He is a very nice guy and he loves the Gospel. He will give you all the attention you need which is also nice.

Brother Porter is awesome! The first day of class i thought he would be one of my favorite professors this semester, that's the truth with some cheese on it. Great in class lectures, grading is specific and if you follow directions you should get an A for sure!

Brother Porter is totally centered on Jesus Christ.  It is obvious.  He loves the gospel, and you can tell it is totally genuine.  He sees and treats his students as equals, even though he's obviously knows a TON about the gospel.  It's like he sees us as people who are headed for where he is, and that he wants to do all he can to help us get there

Brother Porter is awesome. He loves teaching and is very passionate about what he teaches. Being a religion class, it strengthened my testimony. I loved his classes and he is defiantly one of my favorite teachers I have had.
Take REL C 200 with him. You will not regret it! Just an all around great man.  I wish he was teaching another class I need  next semester I would sign up in a heartbeat

This was Brother Porter's first time teaching at BYU, and he killed it! He is exactly what you want out of a religion professor; extremely enthusiastic, passionate, and kind. Lectures are enhancing, and not just plain regurgitation of the same ol stuff. Took this the semester before my wedding and it was invaluable as a resource. Highly recommend!!

Profe Rodgers is the best Spanish teacher at BYU. Makes content that would be so boring interesting with his love for it. My second class I have taken from him. Wish I could take all of them from him!
He is an awesome teacher and only wants you to succeed. If you go to class and do the assignments you will get an A. The test is a little hard but it's open note and open internet

dr rogers is AMAZING!! you can tell he really loves what he teaches. tests are open note and take home, which honestly helped me to better understand the material. there is a big paper at the end of the semester but it's open all semester long, so don't procrastinate it
I wish every Spanish class was taught by him! Hes super funny and his tests are super fair. He is understanding and very caring on top of super knowledgeable.

Dr. Rogers es el mejor! He's funny, kind, and super understanding. He is insanely chill and relaxed: attendance isn't super necessary, he provides a free pdf of the textbook, and all the tests are open note. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM DR. ROGERS 10/10.

Dr Rogers is so passionate about what he teaches and he's so good at it! I was intimidated by SPAN 325 bc I had never taken a linguistics course before but he made it super fun. He does a lot of practice in class so you know the material and his tests are open book and open note. He's super awesome and funny!! Take a class from him if you can!!

Profe Rogers is great! His class can seem really daunting at first (sooo many new terms and ideas) but he does a really great job at explaining and giving opportunities for practice. His tests are open book and he reviews before each one. Final project is a research report. It's a challenging class but if you show up you'll do fine! Great teacher!

Took both 325 and 423 from him. Take his classes. His Spanish is fast, but very understandable. He has you do most of the work in class and has very few grades compared to other classes, but the classes are well organized and fun. For projects, just do your best--he sees efforts made and will give you good grades if you try!!

Prof Rogers is the best. He's a linguist so he really knows his stuff. Definitely take this class if you served in Chile, he talks a lot about Chile and it's super fun. Attendance is not required but his class is fun and chill so it doesn't feel like a burden to go. You can find the pdf of the textbook online so don't buy it. Take this class!!

Prof Rogers is seriously the best!! He is such an engaging teacher, is incredibly inclusive, loves what he does, and is super reasonable about all assignments, due dates, and tests. Highly Recommend!!!
He's a great teacher very clear with his class. Funny and nice to all the students! all around great teacher.

This was one of the best classes I have ever taken, I have heard horror stories of friends who have taken 321 Language classes from other teachers. However my experience was amazing with Professor Rogers. I 100% Would recommend taking this class from him

He really does care for students. There aren't a lot of assignments, so the points from them are important for your grade. He's really funny, and he knows the material, and is able to convey it really well.

Is hilarious and passionate about teaching language. He is very caring and easy to work with. There are readings and quizzes in textbooks as well as occasional essays. The rest of the class is just enjoyable participation.
Relaxed and super fun.

I cannot recommend Prof. Rogers enough! The class was very enjoyable and he is so knowledgeable and passionate about Spanish and language learning. It never felt stressful and he is very understanding and wants you to do well. He's not a harsh grader and there isn't much homework outside of class besides 2 papers, midterm, and final.

Literally the chillest professor to grace this campus. There are only 2 maybe 3 papers, 1 midterm, and 1 final that makes up your grade, but he's a very easy grader. He'll accept late work for full credit if you talk to him. Assignments in class are fun because he's super funny. Take this course from him if you love yourself and spanish!
Fantastic teacher! Super chill grader and interesting lectures.

There are only ten graded assignments, but you're set to get an A on at least four of them. The tests are take home and open notes, and you get a week to do them. He adapts lectures to make sure you get good practice, and his lectures were always interesting. 11/10
Easy class! Just come to class, listen to Brandon lecture, and fill out an attendance quiz. Would recommend to everyone!

I only took the lecture hall. The grade is all attendance. No homework. Brandon was funny. He had great lectures planned out, was good at explaining things like print publishing and E-Book contracts in a way that I could understand, and he covered for is sick days with good guests.
Guys, it's Brandon Sanderson. I don't feel like I need to say anything more than that.

Brandon is such good teacher! He really loves what he does. I loved learning about writing from someone who has actually been there and can offer real advice. He is a genuinely kind person and always made a point to talk to his students before class.
Best class I've ever taken, no joke. I loved getting deeper into the nitty gritty of how to write well than any other creative writing class I've taken at BYU so far has done!
Super fun lecture series! The class is once a week, and I always looked forward to it. Would recommend for any aspiring writer!

Make no mistake, this class is meant for people serious about writing books. But it's super interesting, entertaining, and he knows his stuff!! Supremely easy, attendance is the only grade. Also super approachable and friendly.
You aren't graded on anything except attendance, and even that is loose. It's basically a lecture series. I mean, come on! It's *Brandon Sanderson*. You should take his class and read his books.

BRANDON SANDERSON IS EPIC!!! I filled so many pages of notes because he just stood up there and spouted wisdom. He is so kind, inspiring, and overall amazing. 110% recommend! Although... I'm pretty sure most people take this class purely because it's freaking Brandon Sanderson, so idk why you're checking Rate my Professor in the first place

If you're on the fence, just take the class! The only thing graded is an attendance quiz each week, and that takes ten seconds. The rest of the class is Brandon giving advice and sometimes bringing in guests. Even if you aren't a writer, I highly recommend taking the class if you are able to. He's funny and his lectures are amazing.

It's a semester long lecture series. There are no assignments or anything, just an attendance quiz every week on LS where you just type in what you liked about lecture that day. Brandon is hilarious and you can tell he wants to help his students succeed as writers and pass on his knowledge of how to make it in a super saturated career path.

Why are you even looking at reviews? As Dan Wells would say: It's Brandon FREAKING Sanderson. Enough said. This class is amazing and I will be taking it again and again. Just don't forget to submit the attendance quizzes. I set a reminder on my phone. All you have to do is show up, learn amazing wisdom from BrandoSando, and submit a 30 sec quiz.

It's just graded by attendance - there's an attendance quiz to be completed during class. It's just one lecture a week with THE BRANDON SANDERSON sharing about his writing process and his advice. I loved this class, and I'm not planning on being an author. Highly recommend.

Y'all, it's literally Brandon Sanderson! This class was super easy and also super good. Every week you listen to him talk to you about how to write and then do an attendance quiz that takes like 5 minutes maximum, so if you show up to class every week and do the quiz, you're guaranteed an A. I loved this class! :)

It's just graded by the weekly attendance quiz. It's only open for a short period of time during class and 30 minutes after, so don't forget to fill it out! This is a great class to hear from an actual published author. Most other writing classes are fine, but this is a chance to learn more about the industry if you want to write books.

Its literally Brandon Sanderson. What more can you ask for? Class is entirely attendance based so if you do you will get an A no problem. He is super knowledgeable and dedicates quite a few classes to just answering questions. A must take for an aspiring author.

Great class. Attendance is mandatory. Each quiz is a 2 question quiz on LearningSuite, where you answer what you enjoyed from the lecture and what questions, if any, that you had. Truly a great, easy one-credit class. I took it for the easy A, wound up learning how to better write, actually.

Literally, it's Brandon Sanderson. He's super engaging and teaches a lot of amazing pointers for people who want to write books. All you have to do is show up. That's it. No homework, just a quiz each week with one question: if you attended the lecture. Best class I've ever taken.

Your only grade is attendance, and you get one free pass on that. Easily my favorite class at BYU thus far--who wouldn't want to attend a lecture by a favorite author for credit? Brandon is super knowledgeable, and I love the structure of the class. He does a really good job of explaining the different parts of writing and the business of writing.
The class is solely graded on attendance and is really good! His lectures are engaging and I left each class with a desire to sit down and write.
Professor Sanderson is a really great guy, he is a prolific writer and that should be enough to take his class, but if that doesn't convince you, all you have to do is show up to get credit.

If you can take this class, DO IT. Brandon is an incredible writer and speaker, with excellent insight and hilarious stories. A super easy 1 credit class. Only attendance is required and you get one freebie. One of the best writing classes I've ever taken. I looked forward to it every week.

Great professor. He shares what he knows, and gets great subs when he's out. Chances are you're taking the class because he's an amazing author. Otherwise, it's an easy, entertaining one credit class.

Sanderson is naturally hilarious and knows his career extremely well. Organizes the course based on plot, setting, characters, and publishing. Sometimes he plays the multi-millionaire card and goes to Hawaii for a bit, but he gets really good subs. No homework, just show up and fill out a slip that the TA passes out. You won't regret taking this.

I have no complaints about this class. It was insanely fun and very helpful towards my (long-term) goal of becoming a published author. Only got an A- because I missed two classes and didn't have time to do a make-up. He is also willing to spend a few minutes after class answering questions you have.

Amazing! He is a New York best selling author and known around the world for his writing. He will make you never want to stop writing. Lectures are inspiring. Don't miss the chance to learn from one of the best in the industry.

Took his 1-credit lecture on creative writing.  You don't need to be a writer to take this part, though he'll probably make you want to write something.  Absolutely no homework, 1-2 absences in the semester are allowed to pass the class.  Great advice for writing and practical things like getting published.  Points you toward some good resources.

I finally felt the chemistry — in Dr. G's classroom. His lectures are exothermic: they give energy instead of draining it. He's a true catalyst, lowering the activation energy for learning. Zero negative ions in this class — all positive vibes. On the fence? That's your titration endpoint. Take it. He's the gold standard — Au-some, even.

My 4th year in STEM & I am dead serious when I say he is the worst professor I have ever had at BYU & I have had some bad professors! He was very smart though & knows a lot! The only saving grace for this class is the exams aren't weighted super heavy. Lectures are very confusing & would often be an information overload. You have to teach yourself.

Throughout the semester, there was no clear path to success. Homework assignments seemed disconnected from what was taught in class, making it unclear how to study or what to prioritize when preparing for exams. Exams were discouraging, with averages often a D. Lack of clear expectations made this course more frustrating than it needed to be.
His exams can sometimes be unfair, but you can get an A if you work for it. I feel super prepared for the biochem section on the MCAT thanks to him. He knows his stuff and he's always avalible.

Hardest class I've taken.Go to EVERY TA you can to check your homework, and every Dr.G office hour you can. Ask Dr.G about everything even if you think you know it. I did bad on first exam, started going to Dr.G office hours and did much better after. Make sure you sit by TA for in class extra credit. Don't take if you cant go to Dr.G and the TAs.

This class is extremely difficult. Our first exam average was 62%, higher than last semester's 58%. When asked about the low scores, he just said “study harder.” I felt confident with the material, but his tests are ridiculously tricky and cover concepts we never learned. Save yourself, your GPA, and your sanity and DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!

I like Dr. Gassaway. He is understanding, very smart, adaptable, and even humble. This was his first time teaching this course. Inevitably, the course is not yet perfect. The expectations were vague: obscure questions, specific answers expected. You need to work with TAs to get good grades. Read the book! Even if you can get by with little reading.

His first semester ever teaching a class, of course there were issues to be fixed. He listened to feedback and I feel confident he'll keep adapting the course. His 1st test was impossible but the rest were reasonable. 
His class made all other classes look that followed easy because of the depth. Go to as many office hours as you can

Its not an easy class but that's because its BIO CHEM. Work with him and he'll help you out. He's very helpful. Take the class seriously because the content is hard just like O CHEM. All his work does prep you for any field in science.
His class is probably the toughest I have taken at BYU. However, as I am studying for standardized tests, I find myself appreciating how deep I had to dive into the subject.
Good man. Just not a good professor. He had ample opportunities to make up for big mistakes on his part for our class but didn't follow through.

Yes, this class was a beast and Professor Gassaway's exams were some of the most challenging I've ever taken at BYU, but it's possible to succeed. After each midterm, significant extra credit was offered in-class and TA's and the professor were very helpful in preparing for the exams. If you take this class, be ready to spend a lot of time studying

Before this class, I had a 4.0 GPA. This was the most difficult course I have ever taken. The tests are ridiculously hard, and he doesn't cover everything in lecture, so you have no idea what will be on the tests. Homework is impossible without TA help and it doesn't really apply to the content. Lectures are disorganized and have no flow to them.

Dr. Gassaway is a very nice and intelligent person. However, this was his first semester teaching and it didn't go amazing. Hhis lectures were a lot of talking. My biggest issue with the class is his expectations were not clear at all. I think as he teaches more he can iron this out, but it was very frustrating.

The class average was 86, which is pretty high for a chem class. He gave a lot of extra credit for exams. It was a bit confusing to know what material was needed for the first exam, but for the next exams, he was clear. I put in ab 2 hours each week and then an extra 4 hours on the week of an exam, and was the 98th percentile. Just go over slides.

There are some positive ratings for this professor. If you value your gpa, a social life, or the potential to go to med school, ignore them and DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! However, if you'd like to give up your social life and live and breathe biochemistry for a semester, and have a mental breakdown every exam then by all means, it's your life.

Take it from a student who earned an A in this class, do not take it from Dr. Gassaway. Chem 481 is difficult but he makes it impossible to be successful because of his lack of preparation on what he's teaching. The tests have unclear questions with multiple answers and the homework is completely unrelated. Do not take from this from Gassaway!

Worked harder in this class than I did in any other class I've had but still couldn't figure out how to do well. Tests are VERY difficult and seem to require additional knowledge outside what we learned in class and what is found in powerpoints and HW. However, he is a new professor, and I could see him changing some things for the better.

Worst class I've taken at BYU by far. His lectures and slides are impossible to follow + full of irrelevant tangents about his research. He's extremely vague about test content, doesn't make practice exams, and TAs give conflicting advice because they don't know whats going on. DO NOT take from him if you want to actually learn and get a good grade

Would not recommend taking this class. Homework's were close to impossible without going to office hours for help. Tests were confusing and often had multiple correct answers with only one marked as correct. Lectures were confusing. More difficult than Ochem solely because it was not clear what you should know. Nice guy, poor lecturer.

It was extremely confusing to know what to study for throughout the whole class. There is so much information and the guidance is minimal at best. Good guy, but man the tests are rough. Preparing and taking those exams made me appreciate the little things in life.

The tests are SO hard. He is the most incoherent professor I have ever had. The test questions and slides are so convoluted. Even the TAs were confused. Take this class from literally any other professor

I wish I can give him a 4.5 but there's no such that choice. 0.5 off just because Dr. G's exam is EXTREMELY HARD (or maybe i wasn't study that hard since the class average is 86...). Other than that, he is a smart person (if you know his experience, ok he got into his phd progam at yale while also did the folk dance team in byu) and class  are fun!

Super nice guy, tough tests. Homework due every week, if you work with the ta's on it it's straightforward. iClicker for class participation (drops some though). Tests are long, and pretty difficult, but he does a mini in-class test retake where you can retake the 15 most missed multiple choice question for 15 extra credit points. Nice guy.

Professor Christensen is the best professor at BYU, in the jr. core, and at teaching Acc 406. He also helped me get a financial need scholarship and will forever be my hero. It may sound like I am biased because of this, but there is not a single student that I've EVER spoken to that doesn't think he is the best professor for this class.
He's the best, there really is nothing else to say.

Like others have said, he's the best professor I have ever had. He knows so so much and everything he does is incredibly helpful to the students. Honestly I don't have a single complaint about this class. Anything I could possibly take from him I will be taking!

The best professor I have ever had. Absolute stud and is a great teacher. Helps you understand what you need to know for the exam. The class requires work to get a good grade but if you work hard in class you will do great.

Professor Christensen is probably the best teacher I have ever had. He is incredible at teaching things and helping everyone understand. You can tell he truly cares about you and is an amazing example.

Christensen is the best! I loved his class. Compared to what others have said, this class was surprisingly challenging for me, but Christensen was great at explaining concepts and always willing to answer any questions. Talking through concepts with my team was what I found most helpful for my success.

Pro. C. is the best professor I have had at BYU. I would run through a wall for this man. He loves his students and teaches them with skill and enthusiasm. I wish I could have him as a professor over and over again. The absolute best there is. I am not only a better accountant because of him, but a better person.
He is the GOAT. Enough said.
All I can say is he is the greatest professor I have interacted with. His class is fair and amazing.

Professors don't come any better than Professor Christensen. He truly cares for his students and does everything he can to support them and their learning. He is accessible outside of class if you need anything. He does a great job at explaining difficult concepts and facilitating conversation in class. Cannot recommend him enough.

Professor Christensen is an incredible professor. He makes auditing so engaging and fun to learn about. Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had, you can tell he cares so much about the students and is willing to help as much as needed with the learning process.

Likely the most authentic and caring professor I've had. He makes class fly by and is a fantastic teacher. He is willing to drop everything and help any student at any time. He pushes for excellence but has great empathy for everyone's situation. His experience and expertise keep the class fascinating. We are lucky to have him at BYU.

This class is pretty tough, but Dr. Campbell gave us a ton of resources to learn and review course material. The study guides are comprehensive and clearly communicate what concepts are the most important for the tests. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is helpful, especially because he mentions which concepts will be on the tests.

Dr. Campbell is a great professor. I missed a few homeworks, he noticed and offered to help me catch up on all of the material during his office hours. He cares about his students and is encouraging. But, the tests are hard. I would recommend doing the practice exam problems from the course packet, as they are fairly similar to the exam problems.

The class material is hard, but Dr. Campbell does the best he can do with it. He told us at the beginning of the class that if we turn in all HW and try our best on the exams we will not fail the class. It's true. If you turn in all assignments, then the class is weighted so that if you get an average of 85 of the exams you will get an A.

The concepts taught are incredibly difficult to understand, and take lots of time and repetition to truly learn, so progress feels very slow. Prof. Campbell provides a plethora of resources to accommodate this, but some feel redundant. He has decent lecture slides and great demonstrations.

Electricity and magnetism is a difficult subject, and it feels like Dr Campbell is a bad professor at first, but you eventually realize that he is really good at preparing you for the tests. The tests can be hard, but they are definitely doable.

Campbell was an exceptionally caring and devoted professor. He really wants you to understand the content of this class and is very accommodating. HW due dates were extended, he gave us hints on test question and emailed us with direct responses to our questions.

Expect to put in a LOT of hours inro this class. Tests aren't weighted very high, so HW is a lot of your grade. Overall Campbell isn't bad at teaching, but always forgets to put in his hearing aids and can never hear what's going on.

Literally the best teacher I ever had. Nearly died, and got a 49% on the first test, but once you figure out all you need is his practice tests, it gets way better. Don't get lost in the super deep derivations of certain equations. Just try to understand and basically ignore it for the tests. The practice exams are basically the same as the tests.

Professor Campbell is the sweetest man!! However, his lectures can be a bit dense and confusing. Learned a lot more from the textbook and working in study groups. This is a HARD class, frustrating, confusing, and I shed many tears. But it will be okay, you can get through it. Just remember, electricity is spicy air and magnets are magic.

A bit unfortunate that a 94% is an A. Dr. Campbell cares for his students, but his lectures are not very helpful. Find an outside resource to really solidify the material. You can take a booklet into the testing center with you, that is the only thing that got me through this course. HW is a large portion of the grade, so exam scores matter less.

Professor Campbell is very caring and gives many tips to help students succeed in the class. His lectures are not always the best, and responses to students are sometimes a little confusing or lacking. He does provide lecture slides, which he compiles into one slideshow before each exam. He is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject.

PHSCS220 is a very difficult course and I don't feel he teaches it very well. Lots of learning comes from the textbook and not in class. He gives very good spiritual devotionals and gives cool in class models to represent the different laws of physics we learn but I still find myself very confused and often consult the textbook for understanding.

Professor Campbell is great. This class is insanely hard, but he does well with the challenge of teaching this class. I was struggling through the class, but the TA section proved itself very helpful. I also love how we got our tests back and the amount of feedback. This was helpful in my preparation for the final. Overall, great professor.

The class was difficult but Dr. Campbell did a good job of making sure we had everything we needed to do well in the class.  On the last day he was really sick and had to leave the room a few times because of it, it really stood out to me how much he genuinely cared about us and what we were learned that he tried so hard to be there and help us

This class was very hard, but Professor Cambell understands the material and teaches it very well. I put so much effort into this class and received a good grade. Definitely would take another class from this professor. The homework study sections and practice exams are what prepared me for the exams.

I was amazed by how much effort Dr. Campbell puts into his classes. He communicates clearly about the course structure and provides ample resources for preparing for tests and for reviewing content. He was also incredibly respectful to all students and all questions.
Physics 220 is a hard class but Dr. Campbell does everything he can to help you succeed. Super nice guy and goes out of his way to meet with you and help you if you are struggling.

Campbell is a super nice guy, but I felt he wasn't a very effective teacher.  I felt he focused on every little detail instead of starting with the important main ideas in simple terms.  He posts his lecture slides on LS, which is all you need for HW so that was helpful.  All said and done, he definitely cares for your success and understanding.

Honestly not great but not awful. Don't necessarily need to read the textbooks much to do well. Definitely read & utilize the lecture notes => will save your life on HW and Exams (all open book/notes). HW & Exams were definitely tricky but not too ridiculous. Lectures not entirely helpful, so sometimes did HW during class. Definitely caring though.

I saw Prof Campbell maybe once. You will only interact with the TAs really. The setup of the class is unique. Experimental design rests with the lab group and is exploratory in nature. The lab group changed every week so you work with different people each week. Pretty easy to get an A but you also have to put in the work. Makeup labs at the end.

This review is for Physics 108 the lab portion. This professor did not show any interest in this class. He was rude in his emails and overall did not do anything to help the students. This class was a huge waste of time.

Dr. Campbell is one of the kindest human beings I've ever met. He really loves his students and wants us all to succeed. The only challenge with his class is that the lectures are almost as confusing and boring as the textbook. The recitation sections were the only reason I did well in this class. You really have to work with other students.

Dr. Campbell took difficult material (Physics E&M) and made it a good experience. I think I'll end up with an A or A- even though physics is really hard for me. His tests are wonderfully written - you're tested on class material and won't miss points because of algebra mistakes or bad unit conversion. Recitation sections are absolutely necessary.

Dr. Campbell has a big heart, loves the subject and his students. The lectures can be kind of confusing, but as long as you read material and start on homework before the lecture, he loves answering questions! Big emphasis on study groups so you get to know the other people in the class pretty well.

I absolutely loved Prof. Campbell. I took 220 from him during Covid (Fall 2020) and he always did his best to help us understand the difficult concepts during a very crazy time in the world. He is a very caring man and he will help you answer the questions and concerns you have. Try your best (I'm not great at physics) and take it fr him!

My favorite physics professor so far! The class is difficult, but taking it from Dr. Campbell makes it reasonable. The grading weight is spread out well among different types of assignments, so a bad test score won't destroy your grade. He structures the course to provide a lot of different types of learning opportunities.

Genuine and Spiritual, always started class with a prayer. Homework is challenging but very instructive, lectures are mostly for the topic introduction. Low weighted tests and final so don't stress. Provides practice tests. BUY THE COURSE PACKET. Worth every penny. TAs are very helpful for homework but labs kinda lack intuition.

Similar to many others, I was nervous about taking the majors section, but it was well worth it. Get into a good study group and participate, work hard, organize and plan well, and go to lectures, and you should do just fine. Dr. Campbell really cares and wants you to succeed. Love his spiritual/inspirational thoughts every class! Would recommend.

I was initially nervous about taking the major/minor section of PHSCS 123, but after hearing about the other sections, I can honestly say that this class will set you up for success compared to the non-major/minor section. If you're on the fence about it, take this class. 6-7 open-note/take-home midterms, interesting material, and great professor.
Class is mostly just reading through previously read lecture notes. Not super helpful for learning, but a good guy. Always willing to answer questions.

Dr. Campbell is very caring and spiritual. He is willing to get to know his students and help us with every question. This class is a tough class itself. It was hard for me to understand what he taught all the time. It will take a lot of hard work to get good grade.

Dr. Campbell was amazing. Each class was started with a spiritual thought and a prayer. The Live Q/A sessions were great opportunities for Dr. Campbell to address any questions you had. He really wants to ensure that you understand what is being taught. That being said, reading your textbook is IMPORTANT. Challenging class, but it was enjoyable.

Dr. Campbell is one of the nicest profs that I have ever had. He really cares about his students and has said multiple time that he wants all his students to succeed. Reading the textbook and taking notes will help you out a TON! He is very accessible by email outside of class. Get ready to work hard, and you will get the most out of this class.

Make sure you use the practice test problem packet! He gives a ton of practice problems from each chapter, that are exactly like the ones on the test. Even when I was behind in class. I would just do those and feel super ready for the tests.

I barely got an A, it wasn't easy but this class is soooo interesting, and Dr. Campbell is the kindest man. I ended up TAing for him after. He really wants students to succeed. You have to understand the concepts and it takes a lot of work, but very reasonable.

If you need to be taught by example, find a different teacher. You are basically self-taught, and there is little chance you will be prepared for the exams. Even though it is open everything except others and the internet, you still won't find what on earth the question is asking.

Fantastic professor. If you are taking this class you really need to make sure you take the time to understand integrating conceptually as you will be using them throughout the year. TA's are always available in the lab to help out. Homework isn't bad and prepares you well for the tests and you get to take the course packet in to the tests.

Lab is fairly straightforward. Pre-lab reading and quiz every week, and a lab summary write up and notebook check each week after lab. Lab's aren't too bad, but generally take the full 3 hours. No tests, but there is one research paper during the semester. Show up and do everything and you can get an A.

This is a physics class, meaning it requires work, I would recommend having taking multivariable calculus before hand as you understand the math better but Dr. Campbell is a kind, caring, honest professor who teaches very well. He is very passionate about what he teaches and you can tell. He talks a little quiet so I would sit close to the front.

Dr. Campbell is the nicest, most caring professor I've ever had. With the pandemic and transition to online learning, he made everything accessible, dropped the final, and worked so hard to make everything available. This class was the hardest I've ever taken at BYU, but he is probably the sweetest professor ever. He has a true heart of gold.

Dr. Campbell is great! The class is hard. Nothing about electricity & magnetism are intuitive to me, but he makes the class doable. It requires a lot of studying, but he is very helpful and willing to work with you. The class is structured to help you succeed. I didn't like the class, but I'm glad that I took it from him. He makes it suck less:)

This class is challenging, but Prof. Campbell makes it doable. His lectures have lots of fun demos but can be a bit abstract with harder concepts. Find a good study group for the homework and you will figure it out. He really cares about his students and about how we are doing in class and wants to challenge us to help us learn.

Very do-able class. Show up, do the labs and do the post-lab quiz and summary. There is also a paper on anything you can relate to physics, but other than that easy class. Only warning is that because it is so easy, an A is a 97, A- is a 93, B+ is a 90 and so forth. However, an A is very do-able.

Dr. Campbell has been my best professor at BYU so far. I highly recommend taking any class that you can from him if you're a Physics major. You don't get grades for going to his lectures, but they are worth going to. He likes to delve deep into the material, so if you're not a Physics major then maybe he'll be a bit difficult for your taste.

Dr. Campbell is an amazing human being. He's actually one of the most caring people I've met in my life, and he really respects and loves his students. All of his tests are take-home and open book, but they're still pretty tricky and there's 7 of them plus the final. Definitely not an easy professor, but he helps you learn the content very well.
