Professor Campbell is great! I love how he opens each class with a spiritual thought and a prayer. Professor Campbell is a real gentleman and all of us students respect him. I thoroughly enjoyed each of his lectures and learned a lot.

Dr. Campbell is awesome!  It really surprised me to see low ratings on him- he is not the easiest of professors, but his power points are crystal clear, and openly accessible while in the class.  He does a very good job of preparing you to know what information is going to be on the tests too.  He is very helpful at office hours too if you drop by.
Physics 107 is the easiest course on earth and I really loved it.  Just make sure to write the lab summaries well.

Coming into this class, I already knew a few things about the material, specifically the circuits section with resistors.  I found the class very interesting, and enjoyed his slides and explanations. He did demos almost every week, which were quite fun.  You can bring a summaries book into the tests and final, make sure you take advantage of it!

Dr. Campbell isn't the best lecturer I've had, but he knows the material inside and out and does his best to help you understand it. All the exams were take home tests, he was extremely respectful toward students and their questions, and he is genuinely interested in your performance. Tests and assignments are frequent but fair.

I highly recommend Dr. Campbell for Physics 220.  You can take an extremely helpful course packet into the exams with you.  He is very respectful of students and soft-spoken.  He is very Ivy-league smart and never uses filler words when he talks.  The course material is very difficult, so make sure you take it from Dr. Campbell. Extra credit!

Choose him if you really want to understand the proof, calculus behind the concepts you learn. He seems to skim through a lot very quickly in class so plan on doing the reading as well as the homework to stay on top of understanding stuff. He's friendly and very willing to help you on a one-to-one basis. Hard class. The grading curve is lovely.
Literally CANNOT take physics and put it in simpler terms. Doesn't have the vocabulary to do it. I was lost the whole time but the TA's helped me and the class was easy enough that I still got an A

About as useless as the rest of the physics department. Occasionally he'd reveal a useful formula in class, or say something you had to know for tests(which were fair, in my opinion...which was a minority opinion). He hints that he has to teach the way he does. Incredibly awkward person. Smart, but awkward, and a poor teacher overall.

Typical physics class.  Do the homework and go to class and you'll do ok.  He is always willing to help and talk to him after the tests and he will try to help you understand.  Not the greatest teacher but he loves what he does and that makes his lectures interesting.  The material in class isn't the level of detail needed for the test, luckily.

Don't take this class from him if you can help it!!! He doesn't teach anything...just clicks through his power points. The only people who did very well in this class had prior experience with the concepts in other classes. You have i-clicker quizzes, that's about all lecture is good for. He's a nice guy but he can't teach.
Nice guy, extremely fair grading....has iclicker quizzes daily on whether you did your reading.  Lectures are worthless besides the points from the quizzes.  Pretty mediocre teacher.
Will work with you until you understand what the point is. Well prepared material. If he doesn't know something he will tell you he doesn't know rather than give a bad answer.
He wants you to enjoy the subject as much as hae does.

I like physics, but this branch of it is a bit more abstract than I'm used to.  Professor Campbell had good demonstrations and was very nice, but I often lost track of where he was going with his explanations.

He teaches the class in a strait forward and organized way. The test format is a bit unusual but once you figure it out it actually makes things easier. If you go to the TA lab and do all of the homework then the class is not too hard.
Cold as ice.  Totally distant and seemingly apathetic.  TA's taught class.
He could have definitely been more organized and goal-oriented towards teaching me something.
Intelligent professor, but teaches at too high a level for undergrads
Personally quite likeable but has an incredibly weird format for testing and homework that is almost incomprehensable.  Hard to understand. Needlessly complicates some things.
No Comments

Obviously a new teacher. Seems to lack thorough knowledge of subject as he gets defensive quickly. Just do it his way and get through. Maybe UVSC will get an opening someday and he can go there. (University of Phoenix perhaps?)

Brand new.  As a teacher he means well, but is almost incomprehensible.  He speaks math, and gets a little frustrated when you don't get it right away.  A nice guy, though.  Plan to spend lots of your own time trying to understand the material.

I decided to become an econ major after taking his class. Super awesome professor, his lectures make a lot of sense and he teaches very clearly. Read the textbook, attend every lecture, and go to the TA lab often, and you'll do great.
Great teacher! I ended up extending my graduation to add a minor in Econ I loved it so much. I really feel like he is the best Econ 110 teacher! Hard class but he did a really good job teaching it.

TAKE FROM PLATT!! Put in the time! He and his TA's really care about students and they are actually good at helping students understand material. He clearly tells you what to do to succeed in his class, his spiritual thoughts usually deserve a mic drop, and he is also HILARIOUS! I'd share my Prof. Platt quote book, but RMP won't let me. :(

He is the GOAT! He gives you all of the material you need and gives you so many opportunities to lift your grade. But you HAVE to know what you're doing, it can be easy to fall behind. Visit the TAs. Don't think it will be easy because hes nice

This class is honestly pretty difficult but if you put in the time you should do ok. Go to the TA lab and his office hours, he explains things really well. My biggest piece of advice would be to do all the quizzes until you get 100% because you understand the material not because you guessed. Dr. Platt does a great job!

This class is ridiculously hard. Good luck reading 19 chapters to a textbook written for Economics PHDs (it costs $400 btw) then pass the comprehensive final that's 33% of your grade. I studied for 8 hours and got a D on my final. Brennan did a decent job teaching, but the lectures were rushed. You barely have enough time to comprehend anything.
Make sure to read textbook before class. Honestly a very difficult class, although if you put in the work you'll do ok.

Lectures were interesting and easy to understand. There are weekly quizzes but you get infinite attempts and some are dropped. The lowest midterm is also dropped. Professor Platt is a really great guy and I loved how he incorporated real-life examples and gospel principles into his lectures. This class made me love economics!

He's like a father figure. If you do the work and study (his practice quizzes are extremely similar to the exam ones), then you will enjoy his class and learn things about the world. He also connects what we're learning to our lives and encourages us. You can tell he cares; he's a super nice guy from afar, and when you talk to him up close.

If you have to take ECON 110, take it with Professor Platt. He is honestly such a legend. He teaches very well and if you just take the practice quizzes a ton of times you will do really well on the tests. Grading is very clear and he drops 4 days of attendance, 3 quizzes, 1 midterm, and one of your writing about economics assignments. :)

FANTASTIC PROFESSOR!! Econ 110 is just really, really hard. The lectures were fantastic and related to the gospel and to real-life applications of economics. Tests are curved, questions that are too hard can be dropped as well. Homework has unlimited retakes. If you have to enter the pit of despair that is Econ 110 take it from him.

I felt like I was pretty confident in the material but my test scores were not reflecting that. He does drop your lowest scores in each category which is really nice. The course is just difficult material. He really incorporates the gospel and real-world application of the Econ concept into every single lecture. Go to the TA lab!

He was awesome! I had an error in my grading and I emailed him and he responded almost immediately and got it fixed for me. He incorporates the gospel into the class and it adds a really interesting perspective to economics. Homework was easy, and he provides practice problems that mirror the test for each chapter, which makes it easy to study.
tough class.

Very good professor, I was taking it for a gen ed. You're expected to come to every lecture and there are plenty of opportunities to earn points from homework and participation in class, and the lowest grades for each section (not including the final) are dropped. He is passionate about the work and makes himself as available as possible

The material is difficult and there is just so much to learn and understand. It's very logical(walking through problems with TAs help a ton. Lectures can get boring, but he is a great guy who cares about his students. He drops lowest quizzes, essay scores, the lowest Midterm and you can get points back on the other midterms with corrections.

Platt did a great job explaining tricky concepts. The course material itself is difficult, but by attending every lecture and putting in the hours, it is doable. Platt cares deeply and was willing to address any questions in class. Overall, the class is organized, but it's very test-heavy.

Professor Platt is a great teacher. Econ 110 is a complicated course and it was the class that took up the majority of my time. I think Platt did a great job teaching. This class is going to be difficult no matter what professor you have I feel. So, if you need to take Econ 110, I would definitely recommend Professor Platt!

I love Professor Platt. He cares so much about the students and teaching economics. That being said, econ is a very difficult subject. You must read the textbook, go to class, and meet with TA's to do well in the class. Best part is that everything on the test in from the infinite question bank, so you know exactly what to expect.

Professor Platt has a great understanding of the material and teaches in a very clear way. There are lots of study materials and practice quizzes for the tests. If you can do well on the practice quizzes, you are ready for the tests. This class takes next to no work outside of class other than studying.
Awesome professor, the most difficult aspect of the class was how much harder quiz and test questions were compared to the ones reviewed during lecture.

Professor Platt is a good guy and an understandable teacher, but ECON 110 is simply brutal and the grading is tough. The final exam (worth one-third of your grade) averaged around 70%, and even with several 90%+ mid-term exam scores, I finished with a B. You have to be exceptional––not just above average––to get an A.

Dr Platt lays out this class very well and has great lectures. The exams are brutal, especially the final, which is worth a lot. But put in the work and you can get a good grade. Always do the practice quizzes multiple times. I never once read the textbook.

Econ is a challenging subject, but Platt makes it as good as it can be. His lectures are clear and helpful, though attendance is mandatory. Homework is manageable, but exams require significant studying and effort, and the final is worth a large portion of the grade. He prepares students well for the exams, but the course is still tough overall.
He is a good professor, but the class was hard to be engaged with and the exams are extremely difficult. Never studied more for exams than in this class.

This class is very challenging. He is a great lecturer, but the class size is huge so you can't get one-on-one time in class. You will have to study a lot, do a ton of homework, and be prepared for the three midterms. The TA lab is helpful, and the study tools are also useful, so use them. If you're not willing to work, don't do this class.
Great guy. I had a good experience when I went to office hours. If you read the textbook you will have an easier time in the class.

This is a very difficult subject taught by a very understanding professor. He does a great job at teaching everything necessary so no one is surprised once they get to the exam. It is very demanding of your time, just make sure you do the redoable quizzes as much as you can and you'll be ready to go for every test.
This guy loves trick questions more than anything in the world. So frustrating

Taking this class is like watching your NFL team. You're gonna be disappointed and frustrated until you decide to stop watching and hope for a magical comeback in the post-season for your final exam. 
He is a nice enough guy, but listening to his lectures and trying to pull it together for the exams over and over gets really old.

I think Platt is the best option for ECON 110. He goes over practice problems all the time to help you on the exam, which is life saving. He explains things very well in lectures. His exams are basically the same as his biweekly-ish practice quizzes.

Frequently has very low averages on his exams and, despite claiming to curve at the start of the semester, he does not really curve. For example, the average grade on the second midterm was a 65%. The teacher decided to oh so generously drop certain questions raising the average to a 70%. I didn't miss the questions he dropped and so got screwed.

I was freaked out by this class when I read the ratings, however it was actually really chill if you DO WHAT HE SAYS (he gives great advice on how to succeed) and listen in class. A lot of the people that complain that this is the hardest class ever were likely the many I saw not paying attention in class. If you are a STEM major don't even worry.

He is so passionate about Econ 382! I took it from him after he had a 3 year break and he was still phenomenal. I would highly recommend anyone to take it from him. One weekly homework assignment and the exams had plenty of practice problems.
He teaches Econ 110 the best! He is the reason I am now an Econ major. Teaches to a basic understanding. The TA lab was necessary to do well on homeworks but you get unlimited attempts on it.

I loved Dr. Platt's class! The course itself was kind of hard sometimes but he did a great job of preparing us through lectures and the textbook. He had a lot of grace built into the course. The lowest midterm grade was dropped as well as the lowest quizzes, essays, and absences. The course layout was pretty straight forward. Take it from Platt!

Expect to invest an absurd amount of time just to stay afloat. An A is possible, but only if you treat it like a full-time job. My business professor even used this class as the prime example of a demotivating organization—setting the bar so high that students either sacrifice everything or accept failure. I failed every test and still passed yay!

Dr. Platt is the best Professor for econ 110.  Overall, his class structure is the most manageable and fair. He has weekly quizzes (HW) that resemble the test questions exactly. He also has the best spiritual thoughts. Achieving an A in his class is very manageable. Be ready to learn understanding rather than memorize. Take econ 110 from him.

HARD class. However the course is super interesting and he is an amazing lecturer. From my understanding most of the teachers grade the same way, but the final is worth a lot. If you have to take this class, try to take it from him.

Great class! Definitely a complicated subject but Dr. Platt explains the topics very well and is always open to questions. He is very patient, funny, and kind and delivered very interesting lectures. An A is very attainable if you put in the time.

His lectures where interesting and entertaining, but his tests were extremely difficult and together acount for 70 percent of your grade. This class is a very difficult class. The class average on the final was 67 percent this year. The teacher drops some low scores, but even with that mercy, good luck getting an A in this class.

ECON is tough, but Platt is the best teacher to take it from! GO TO TA LABS they will save your life and help explain concepts in more depth. Some of your lowest scores will be dropped, which will help your grade, and it will be curved at the end of the semester.

Overall Platt made Econ survivable. If there's one thing I would change is for him to stop making politically incorrect statements in class about the election or COVID, etc. He says things that could get him fired if someone were to bring it up to the department.

Econ 110 is an unavoidably hard class, but Dr. Platt makes it very survivable, and I loved how he would blend some religion into his lectures! It is structured well, with dropped grades and lots of opportunities to practice (which is the best way to learn the concepts). I highly recommend the TA lab. The TAs were super friendly and SO helpful!

If you've never taken an economics class before, this class will be hard. He is forgiving with the items he drops (lowest midterm, lowest essay, and lowest three quizzes), but this class is still a beast. He's a pretty good lecturer but due to my lack of experience, it was very hard.

Great professor who has set up the class so you can learn and be ready for exams. Quizzes allow unlimted attempts which is how I prepared for exams--you don't need to understand the lectures, just learn the quizzes and you'll learn the class just fine. Just participate in class (Y-poll), do the quizzes on time, and learn the quizzes. It was work.

Dr. Platt is great. Econ 110 is a hard class, but he does a good job teaching it. The quizzes you take every week are old test questions, so when studying for the test, take the practice quizzes over and over again. Take Econ 110 from Dr. Platt!!!

Take Econ 110 from Platt. He is a good teacher and drops your lowest test and essay score. I waited to take this class from him and I'm glad I did. Tests are exactly like the practices, but you need to study, or you will not do well. Lectures are good. There is a textbook, but I really only learned from lectures cuz I don't read well.

This class is not easy. Professor Platt did the best he could with what he had, but see the TA's often if you struggle. He's a great teacher, but there is so much depth to the subject that makes this class hard.

Hardest class I've ever taken. Very fast paced, covers A LOT of material. He is engaging and caring: drops lowest scores and allows for extra points on the midterm. Homework has lots of applications not covered in class. There are also a few discussions and short papers, but very easy. GO TO THE TA LABS- even though they aren't allowed to help much

This class was HARD!!! I had to work my butt off to get an A. My recommendation is go to the TA lab and don't leave until you can do every single homework assignment and get each question correct first try and then you will be ready for the exams. I didn't read the textbook I just hammered practice problems. Great professor! Good luck!

ECON110 is a challenging course, but Professor Platt makes it manageable. Attend class, use the textbook, and form study groups. Apps like Unstuck study can also help with prep. With effort, you can succeed in this course.

This is definitely the easiest ECON 110 class at BYU. Only showed up to class for the i-clicker, I don't remember a single thing professor platt said and I walked away with a B. I probably spent less than an hour a week on this class. I'm sure I would've performed better if I put in any amount oof effort.

The class is made harder than econ has any right to be. If you've taken AP Macroeconomics, that's probably the first 2/3rds of this class. You will need to extensively study for the tests. Overall, though, he teaches the concept better than the other ECON110 professors. Take it from him.

I really like Prof Platt. You can tell he's great guy, but ECON110 is really hard. The TA lab hours are terrible, which makes it really hard when you are confused. He went over tons of stuff, but one semester later I remember nothing about what we talked about. It got dumped out on the test and forgotten. Really hard class but Platt does great.
Make a study group for this class!! There are iClicker questions during lectures.
Great guy, great lectures. Lots of quizzes, tests matter the most for sure. Not as hard as most people make it out to be.
ECON 110 is very difficult, lots of memorization of different terms, different rules and when to apply or not apply them. Requires a lot of time and effort out of class.

Tough class but great organization, I loved how the quiz and test questions were similar! I didn't love how some of the exam questions were a little subjective, but Professor Platt took responsibility for some of the bad questions and gave us points back which I really respected. It's a lot of work but he makes the path to success clear!

This is a hard class, but Professor Platt did an amazing job teaching it! His lectures were clear and understandable, and recorded so you could rewatch and learn at your own pace. He genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. He's very clear on what material is on tests and gave practice problems from previous tests to study.

Platt does a fantastic job explaining really difficult concepts. This class can be hard because most of the information is new and different. I would highly recommend reading the textbook- it explains things in a clear way and you have a better understanding going into the lecture. I got one of the highest grades in the class and it's what helped.

DO NOT GET BEHIND. As tempting as it is to skip the readings for new material those days while you're studying for the midterms, do not do it. I got so behind in terms of textbook readings that I was lost during lectures and had to go back and rewatch every lecture from the beginning of Midterm 2 material to the end. Learn from my mistakes.

This is a hard class, there's no way around it (and I've survived the accounting junior core). But, if you're willing to put in the effort- read the textbook, go to class, take good notes, and study HARD for the tests, you'll do well! Platt gives you tons of resources to help you succeed- tons of TA hours, recorded lectures, and practice quizzes.

Lived the teacher he really cared for his students.  He is very understanding about situations yet sets a clear grading criteria.  The tests are defiantly hard but TA labs are always open and his test are based on what you practice to make tests easier.

Doctor Platt is amazing! If you have to take Econ 110, take it from him! You can tell that he really cares about his students and he really wants them to learn the material as well as do well in the class! He does a great job of inviting the spirit as he teaches and the quizzes are super helpful test prep! He drops one of the midterm scores too!!

Super hard class, but Platt's a good professor. Knows his stuff and is willing to answer questions in and outside of class. Tests and the final are a huge portion of your grade. His practice tests are exactly the type of questions you'll see on exams. Textbook is VERY helpful. Appreciate him bringing the gospel into lectures. Study hard for an A.

Thing is I am a bio major so this class was extra difficult but honestly the professor is great. He has all test questions on practice quizzes but it takes a long time to get all possible questions from the quizzes. I never read the textbook and did alright. Thing is the Professor is great, economics sucks.
Difficult class no matter who you take it from, but I would definitely recommend Platt. He gives plenty of practice material that are very similar to the exams. Be prepared to grind hard for the A.

Accounting Major. Probably one of the hardest class have taken in BYU. Platt makes me want to get Econ minor. He is stupid smart but the quizzes and tests are tough. Definitely read textbooks before attending . The pace was slow literally you can finished all the content yourself in 20 mins
You'll spend a lot of time in the TA lab asking questions. If you need help, the YouTube channel JacobClifford is really good. Lectures are dense, but if you like business, it's a tolerable class.

His practice quizzes prepare you so well for the tests. There are 3 tests and he drops 1. A 92 is an A and he curves the class. The content is really tricky but he is good at explaining things. I had to put in a ton of time but with his test prep material he makes getting an A straightforward. Loved this class.

ECON110 is known for being difficult, but I think that Platt is the best of the econ teachers. You are able to drop a couple of quizzes and one midterm. There is an econ lab that is really helpful, but the biggest thing is to study the practice quiz questions to prepare for midterms and the final.
Dr. Platt was a wonderful professor! Though the material was incredibly difficult, he taught it efficiently and comprehensively.

Super tough professor. If you don't show up to class, good luck. His slides are kinda vague, and he only goes over how to solve the problems in class. You can tell he loves teaching though. And he lets you retake the bi-weekly quizzes as many times as you want, so grades really just depend on the three midterms and the final.

Professor Platt is very knowledgeable about economics but not the best teacher. The class average on one of our exams was 60%. If the whole class is getting that bad of a grade, that definitely says something about the professor and their teaching style. The class was so unnecessarily difficult for a general class. Don't take from him.
Great teacher. Really knows what he's talking about and answered questions well.

Dr. Platt is a great professor, and very passionate about economics. The TAs were amazing, almost all of them were really helpful and really reliable. However, it is no joke that this class is tough. I spent 20+ hours a week in the TA lab and still didn't get a great grade. But economics is generally hard, so Platt is the best you can take it from.

My brother literally died this semester and he said my options were to just do it or drop the class. He's a nice guy and he wants you to understand the material, but all my other teachers offered ways to help and he didn't. It was frustrating because I worked so hard but couldn't keep up. It was an extremely difficult and test-heavy class.

PRACTICE the material, maybe 2ish hrs per chapter. He's taught 110 for years and a bunch of days, quizzes, and even a midterm is dropped; he knows this is hard and tries to bridge that. Take notes, practice outside class, and DON'T SKIP his lectures. 110 is rough, but you should take Platt if you want to survive and actually learn something!

I went to every class, went to the TA lab frequently, did the test make-ups, and did my aboslute best. Econ just isn't for me. I don't have my final grade yet but I'll probably end up with a C. I feel like Econ clicks or it doesn't. I enjoyed the material, I just didn't test it well. This class has so much material to learn it's exhausting.

Platt has an awesome rule where you can drop one of your midterms which is a lifesaver in ECON 110. He also has iClicker participation, pass/fail essays, and homework assignments that help to buffer your grade. Not the most engaging lecturer but explains concepts in an easy way to understand. ECON isn't fun but he's a great option for a professor.

Professor Platt was honestly a good teacher but the content material was difficult. You have to attend class every day to get the material from class because he doesn't post it. The grade for this class is very test heavy so if that's not your strength I wouldn't recommend him.

Econ110 gets a pretty tough rep, but if you stay on top of things you'll do fine. Lectures can be long, but Platt does a great job teaching the material. There are practice quizzes for each chapter that are almost identical to each exam. If you practice those a few times, you'll be set for each exam. You can drop a lot of grades and TAs help a lot.

Professor Platt's class is one of the most difficult I've ever taken. He was a good lecturer, though it was hard to ask questions because the class was massive. I appreciate that he responds to emails within half an hour and coordinates with students to make tests fair, along with curving the final grade.

Dr. Platt was an incredible teacher who made a traditionally difficult subject easily understandable. I would recommend going to every class and attending recitations. Dr. Platt is happy to help, as are the TA's. The tests were difficult but doable if you work hard and understand the concepts before you go in. Overall, very worthwhile.

Professor Platt is an awesome teacher! Economics was not necessarily my jam, but Professor Platt helped me get through the semester in a way that allowed me to pass. Professor Platt is a 10/10 professor and person!

The tests were very similar to the homework quizzes for each chapter. He allows students to take as many practice quizzes you want to study for the tests.  I felt that his lecture notes did not help a ton on the tests but the textbook itself and the homework quizzes. IClickers required for attendance. Very large curve at the end of the year.

Amazing lectures and very accessible. He grades on a generous curve, so you will definitely at least pass the class if you put in the work. If you are a senior who is anxious to graduate and want that C in Econ 110, take Dr. Platt's class. If you want an A, the TAs and most students agree that Dr. Pope is the way to go.

For whatever reason this class breaks everyone's necks, but he's the best econ prof at BYU. Just get it over with him, he's a solid dude who cares and explains everything very clearly. He's got a very low tolerance for student crap, which I appreciate. Take econ from him.

Dr. Platt is a solid guy and he is in my opinion the best professor to take Econ 110 from. The most important and hardest part of the class is the tests. The three midterms and the final together are 75% of your grade and you need to do well on them. Hit the practice quizzes hard to prep for the tests and you'll be fine.

Professor Platt is an amazing teacher. Econ 110 is a hard class, but by no means impossible. Pay attention in class and go see the TA's whenever you can. For the exams the best way you can prepare is by doing the practice quizzes he posts.

Honestly, I hated this class. It was incredibly difficult and I never understood what was happening. However, this is not a rating of ECON 110, this is a rating of Professor Platt. 

Brennan Platt is clearly good at what he does, and is incredibly knowledgable on these topics. He's also a very nice person, and gives lots of chances to do better.

Here's what you really want to know!
 
- Attendance required (you can miss up to 4 days)
- Don't BUY ANY OF THE BOOKS 
  Book: "Dead Economists" is at the BYU Library.
- If you have an iPad or touch computer download the PowerPoint notes for your class notes instead of buying the packet. 
-You'll write 4 short essays (1 gets dropped)

ECON 110 is hard, but Dr. Platt is really good at conveying the information, giving up plenty of practice opportunities, and staying focused and productive during lecture. He allows you to retake quizzes as much as you want and drops a midterm, so you have multiple opportunities to do well. The class is tough, but Dr. Platt is amazing!

Platt gives you a fair chance at getting an A by giving you multiple quizzes per week (each can retaken until you get 10/10) that have real past exam questions. If you study these hard, you will do well on exams. If the questions still dont make sense, TA labs are usually helpful. His lectures are usually enjoyable. Better than Kearl fo sho.

The lectures are extremely confusing and rather useless. Unfortunately, they're mandatory. If you want to skip, know your grade will plummet from the loss of I-Clicker points. To actually understand econ, go to the TA lab. They can teach 75 mins worth of confusing lecture in 5 mins. Also, don't buy the book. It's straight useless.

ECON 110 is going to be a hard class no matter who you take it from. But I am definitely glad I took it from Professor Platt. He is very knowledgeable & could clearly explain most things. However, the TA lab and recitations are what saved me. Weekly quizzes help to actually learn the chapters which you need for the tough exams. Lowest grade drops.

Professor Platt has mandatory lectures. His lectures alone do not prepare you for the quizzes but there are resources like the TA lab and recitations that are really helpful in preparing for quizzes and test, which are really the same as the quizzes. Going to the TAs is more helpful that going to Platts lectures.

Econ is a difficult class. Our exams had a 65% average, BUT there was a generous curve applied at the end of the semester (took me from a B- to a B+). He uses previous exam questions for the homework, so you know what to expect, 5 essays, but I got 100% every time. Attend TA recitations, take good notes on his examples in class, and you'll survive.

Platt is a good guy and is pretty good at explaining difficult concepts. It always made sense in class. However, the assignments were very difficult. Biweekly quizzes were repeatable, but very tricky. And he writes his own exams, which are extremely difficult and tricky. Class average before the curve was 74%, which I can only attribute to Platt.

Pretty solid professor. I liked him a lot. And he's really passionate about it. Like all smiley during the class. I've never seen anyone soooo hyped about econ. The class is honestly not crazy hard. Just go over the notes before the tests and really hit the practice quizzes hard. The tests are basically copies of the quizzes. He also curves :).

I did not put forth too much effort into this class, but Professor Platt did a great job. The concepts are useful from a broader perspective, but it is crucial to get into the details of graphs, calculations and such, which can be a huge time commitment. From what I have heard, he is the professor to take this class from at BYU anyways.

TAKE PLATT!! ECON 110 is HARD, but he makes this class so much better. He's fun and cares about his students. Your grade is mostly the midterms and final, which are very difficult, but if you make sure you have time to study you should be fine. He provides practice problems for every chapter that are either on the midterm/final or very similar.

Platt is so good. As far as 382 goes, he's the best professor to take it from. He loves microeconomic theory and even though I don't super enjoy it, he made the class interesting and very well organized. It's a hard class, so be prepared to dedicate a lot of time to understanding the material and doing homework, but Platt makes it doable.

Professor Platt is awesome. He is very clear with his grading, and his course follows a very set schedule. He is reliable and his tests are straight forward. If you do his practice exams, you won't see anything you can't do. He is an interesting lecturer and uses interesting examples in class.

Platt is just one humble man teaching Econ. His dry humor is also very entertaining. He is very clear when explaining and is willing to listen to the students, something many professors don't do nowadays. In Econ453, be prepared to learn a lot models and theory. However, the math isn't too hard. The HW is a completion grade. Study for the tests!

Brennan Platt is a really solid guy! He teaches and demonstrates the problems very clearly. He gives lots of test helps with practice tests and TA review sessions. The class is a tough one but you have everything you need to succeed. Just approach the class the way he tells you to and be willing to work hard and you'll be fine.

The homework and course material are not too difficult, but the tests are quite tricky and are very different from the practice problems and even some of the practice tests from previous years. I felt like I understood the concepts well and studied hard, but the class did not prepare me well for the tests.

Dr. Platt is an organized, brilliant, and caring professor. Each lecture was clear and thoughtful. The class wasnt bad as long as you understood each game presented. Homework was tricky, but Platt helped us work through it. Lectures are essential to success, not the book so much. Great advice on grad school. A must take for PhD preparations.

I had always heard horror stories about the class, so I waited until my last semester to take it so my GPA wouldn't suffer too much. I'm just happy to have taken the class from Platt. He explains things pretty clearly and gives lots of study resources for the test. Another plus: you are allowed to use the front and back of a paper as a cheat sheet!

For me ECON110 was not as hard as everyone said it was. The homework load was very manageable and it wasn't the hardest class on my schedule. Dr. Platt does a very good job at making the material engaging and the slides are pretty comprehensive of what you need to know. Plenty of exam practice material too and overall very interesting course.

Guys, hear me out. Professor Platt is INCREDIBLE! Econ 110 is an extremely challenging class, but he explained things so well and made me want to study economics even more. As long as you put in the work, you will be rewarded. I will definitely be taking more classes from him. (Also, he loves movies and does fun impersonations all the time haha).

Without a doubt the worst class I have ever taken. Professor Platt sucks at explaining things. I failed the first two tests because he struggles with wording tests in a way that is understandable. I would not recommend this class to anyone unless they want their GPA to tank.
I have never had a worse professor at BYU. He is uncaring and disrespectful. Does not care about students. I recommend never taking a class from him.

Don't take ECON 110 from anyone else. I utilized every office hour the week of each midterm and he always walked me through all the questions I had. The best thing is that he gives you all the past midterms and finals to work through so you know exactly what will be on the test. If you can do those practice midterms then you'll get an A for sure.
Great Professor. There was quite a bit of reading, but it wasn't too bad. As long as you thoroughly do the homework and work on the practice tests, you will do great.

Platt is fantastic. I took this class just because he was teaching it. Great material - he taught you everything step by step. Hard homework, easy tests which made all the hard work with it. Such a humble yet brilliant guy and well respected! Every lecture is purposeful and the homework guided to prove specific points. Love the guy and class.

Professor Platt did great with the online lectures. Not very many assignments in his class. One pretty easy assignment per lecture, and one small 500 word paper every two weeks. He is an amazing teacher and explains things clearly. Pay attention during lectures, do all the reading, study using his past exams and you should be good!

The actual workload is not too bad for Econ 110 with Platt, but it all comes down to midterms and the final. Study, study, and study even more for the exams. There are a few essays, but they are graded super leniently and don't count for much of the grade. Dr. Platt is really good at sharing real life applications of Econ!

Took this over zoom and it was an absolute mess. Did most of my learning on my own since the lectures were chaotic. 100% recommend getting the lecture notes, that's the only way to keep up with his online lectures. Down to earth guy though and did his best with handling online and curving for lower grades this year.

Take it from platt!!!! He lets you have a sheet of notes on every test. The class is difficult no matter who you take it from but Platt makes it so enjoyable. People who take it from Kearl regret not taking it from Platt

Great professor! The class is notoriously difficult but definitely possible. I got an A by studying like crazy for each test. If you work through every single practice test he gives you, you can succeed in this class. Average test grades are always 65%ish but I got an A on each. Study the past tests over and over and over again! You can do it!

Dr. Platt was a really nice guy, but I was super lost the whole semester. Economics is crazy difficult to understand and it felt like he was teaching it in a way that he understood, which left me with so much confusion. I can almost guarantee I would have done better if this class was in person because it just felt like there was a huge disconnect.

Econ is pretty tough to understand, but Dr. Platt is really good. He has very clear expectations and a really organized system. Despite the HUGE class size, he does a good job addressing people's confusion.

Brother Platt did a good job with teaching ECON 110 this semester over zoom, but that does not change the fact that Economics is a really tough subject, especially an introductory course. He is a good guy and teaches well, but the subject is fairly difficult. Would not recommend taking over Zoom if possible. My toughest class this semester.
The material is tough, but he really makes the stuff easier to understand.

Professor Platt is a good choice for econ 110. He takes concepts that are somewhat challenging to understand and simplifies them. The exams aren't all that bad if you put the time in to study for them. He provides many past exams to study off of so you know exactly what to expect. There are a lot of papers, but they aren't hard or time consuming.

Don't take this class unless you have to. His lectures are hard to understand, boring. He doesn't teach always according to schedule so sometimes you have homework when you didn't even learn the topic yet. He drops bad grades, but that doesn't help anything when most of your grades are bad grades. Don't take his class.

Waste of time. You have lots of reading. Lectures are 95% what you already read in the textbook, 5% info not in the textbook or notes packet and guaranteed to be on the test. Tests are so hard/poorly written that even the TAs can't explain some problems. Platt claims it's about learning and not memorization, but he sits on a throne of lies.

Looking for an organized class with clear grading criteria, resources to be successful, and someone who really knows how to explain difficult concepts? Platt is your guy. He is inspiring, very clear, good at answering questions, and up front about the work load. One of my top econ professors.

Disclaimer: this is when covid hit. All of my other classes are online but they seemed to manage to make the content more enjoyable and bite sized, however instead of explaining concepts in a more simple way he elaborates by talking more making concepts more confusing. Homework he assigns is also unnecessarily lengthy and complex.
Professor Platt made 382 so interesting! Great lectures and manageable hw load. Make sure you find a study group early on.

He's a good person, but not a good professor. He's more concerned with research than teaching. He uses Mindtap and it is extremely not user-friendly. The exams are very difficult and some questions the TA's aren't even able to answer. Not as bad as Kearl, but very difficult. Pretty vague slides. No EC. No tech. Miniscule curve. Lots of reading.

I cried as soon as this class was over. Not sure if they were happy tears, or sad tears because I just got destroyed on the final. I studied so hard for each exam, going through each practice exam more than once and focusing on what I didn't know. Still got killed. He's a great professor, though. I learned SO much in this class. Very useful stuff.
This guy gives you all the resources and explains things lucidly. If you can't ace it then you should switch your major to elementary education or marketing.
This man is a total legend. So glad I took Econ 110 from him.

Dr. Platt is awesome. He knows what he's talking about, and teaches with patience. He gives multiple examples for every kind of principle, and uploads all his past test for the students to study. But it's not an easy class. The tests count for 80% of your grade, so if you mess up there, there's little to no chance of recovery. Study hard for tests.

This class wasn't nearly as bad as its reputation. Go to class & take good notes--especially when he emphasizes a point. Draw his graphs! The 'practice exams' are actual exams from previous semesters & are way helpful. Nail the midterms if possible bc the final can be rough. Drop by the TA lab with your questions and you'll be fine.

Professor Platt is pretty awesome. I love that he is willing to help his students. BUT ECON is SUPER HARD! All three tests worth 80 percents of the grade. He often made error in his tests... If you keep doing previous exams, it will help you with his tests. He teaches super basic stuff but hard concepts are tested on the exam!

Worst class I have ever taken at BYU. Tests are so hard nearly impossible to do well on. Half of the class was asleep during lectures so boring. Professor Platt is really bad at explaining the difficult concepts and often made errors while teaching and on exams which added to the confusion of the class. Id take this from someone else if you can.

Prof. Platt is a great teacher and the class is exciting. The homework is doable and enjoyable but the tests are unreasonably hard. Getting an A in this class would be impossible without 12+ hours a week of studying. I could explain the concepts accurately behind all 70 questions on the final but they were all worded to trick you.

He is really bad at explaining challenging concepts. He just tells you all the basic principles but expects you to master them and answer tons of nasty questions on test. Would never take any class from him again.

Dr. Platt is a great professor and his class is very straight-forward. Getting an A in this class requires more than memorization. Learn the theory behind the material and you'll get a good grade. From what I hear about the other ECON professors, Platt is the best to take this class from.
He's a nice guy, but it's just all about exams. Let me tell you, the first midterm avg score is only 7X%, the second midterm is 6X%. No curve, no extra credit. Think 100 times before you take it.

I liked Dr. Platt a lot. The class definitely could have been worse. But, it was lots of work and it never really got easier. I got A's on the first two midterms and a C on the final, which was 40% of my grade. Best of luck.

I learned more from Professor Platt's class than any other class I've ever taken. He's just a fantastic teacher and I switched my major to Econ because I enjoyed it so much. That being said, it was a very difficult class. 80% of the grade is based off of three tests, so study for those. Definitely recommend his class for anyone.

Dr. Platt is easily one of the best professors at BYU. He is very fair and you always know exactly what to expect from him. He was able to take complex concepts and explain them in a way where it was difficult to misunderstand. His tests are tough, but if you take all of the available practice tests, you can get an A. Take this class for Platt!

ECON 110 is a very tough class, but Prof. Platt is the man to take it from. Takes complex concepts and breaks them down to help students understand it. Strict when it comes to his policies, but it's good to know what to expect. Would take again!

He's a really good proffessor. I learned a lot and really enjoyed his lectures, but the class was rough. Be aware that most of the grade is on the tests. Which are quite difficult. A really demanding class overall. That being said if I were to continue in economics I would certainly seek to take other classes from him.

Econ110 is a challenging class no matter who you take it from, but Dr. Platt does a good job. Honestly I think I learned more from the textbook than I did from his lectures but they were still interesting. Tests make up a big portion of your grade and are very hard. He gives you lots of practice tests that help you prepare.

Doctor Platt lacks English grammar proficiency, especially on his tests. Besides, his questions are very ambiguous. If I hadn't studied Econ in school, I wouldn't have gotten an A. In general, he does a poor job explaining really hard concepts.

I like Dr. Platt pretty well, and he's pretty good at explaining the material, although it moves super fast so it's hard to remember everything. There's a huge disconnect between the homework/class material and tests. They're super hard and feel like he's trying to trick you with things you've never seen before and a-j answer options.

Very good at teaching, clear expectations, and tons of opportunities to succeed. Tests are a heavy portion of the grade, but he provides the previous five years of exams for your preparation, which helps a ton. TAs are helpful and grade things on time. Lowest hw, assignments, and attendance are dropped. Cares about his students and loves economics.

Dr. Platt's passion for economics is infectious! And while it was a challenging class (and I definitely won't major in it) I really enjoyed his lectures and came away from the class with a deeper understanding of how the economy works. Workload is manageable and there are a lot of resources to help you succeed (TA's, practice tests, etc)

I am so glad that I took ECON 110 from Professor Platt. I was worried going into this class, but it was okay. Platt explains tough economic concepts so well, which makes the class possible. TA's are available to help with questions. If you put the work in, this class is definitely possible to get your desired grade.

You're on this page because you're dreading Econ and want a good professor to make the class bearable, right?You need to take from Platt! He is so passionate about economics and that doesn't mean he's hard! He teaches in a way that is personable and easy to understand so you WANT to learn more. I'm certainly no econ scholar but I enjoyed his class!

Avoid this class if you can. Stupid hard. There is a degree of mercy built into the system, but the class is so hard and the exams are unforgiving and they make up most of your grade. You can tell he really loves talking about economics and that he cares about students, but I had to get retaught everything by TA's. I've never been so frustrated
Dr Platt is a really good teacher. You can tell he really wants his students to understand what hes teaching. ALSO, HE LOOKS LIKE MICHAEL SCOTT SO...

110 is SO hard, but Dr. Platt explains it as simply as possible. Super organized with clear instructions and expectations. Very PRECISE with vocab. definitions (esp. tests). Ties in spirituality without sounding "churchy." Posts previous years' tests with answer keys to prepare for current exams. Most useful/practical class I've taken so far.

I changed my major to second because of this class. Professor Platt makes Econ apply to pretty much anything. The work is manageable even when taking more than one class in spring term. He drops your lowest grade out of the essays, your lowest three for Aplia assignments, and five attendance days. The three tests total 80% of your grade.

Hendoes a great job at teaching a subject that is challenging for many students.  He's very up front about the tests and grading and gives you the information and resources you need to succeed.  I took the class because I needed to but it's probably been one of the most useful class I've had. An excellent option if you need to take Econ.
Economics is just economics, it's going to be hard no matter who you take it from. Platt was okay, but I feel he could've done better at explaining context and conceptual topics.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IN THE SPRING TERM. Seriously. The Average grade for spring term in this class is 76%. There is far too much material needing to be covered it far too little time. Professor Platt is an awesome teacher, and if you take the class, take it from him. I spent 40 hours per week, and still only B+. I had a 4.0 before this.
I loved taking Econ 110 from Platt. It's tough material, but he makes it interesting. Expect to work for the grade you want, but I would take another class from him again.

Probably the best ECON 110 professor at BYU. I've taken (and withdrawn from) Kearl's class, and Platt's lectures, textbook, and course organization are significantly better. He's extremely respectful of students and his lecturing style couldn't be clearer. Tests are hard, but it's like that in any of the ECON 110 classes.

Great Professor! He turned economics, a subject I've always been afraid of, into something interesting, and even enjoyable. Crystal clear and informative lectures. His tests were among the hardest I've ever taken, so get ready to invest some time in study and in trips to the Econ lab. But if you do an A is for sure in reach. I totally recommend!

No matter who you take it from, Econ 110 is going to be brutal.  That being said, I really think that Platt is a good choice.  His lectures are interesting, he is funny, it is possible to get an ok grade, but the tests are pretty rough.  You aren't going to find an Econ teacher that gives easy test though so I say definitely take it from Platt.

I just took the final - 4 hours. Good lectures, but tests are disgustingly difficult. 35+ hours in the library just studying for the final. His past tests (he gives them to you for practice tests) were no where near as difficult as this year's tests. He's cracking down on grades and tests this year.

Dr. Platt is amazing! I mean, Econ 110 is a hard class but he made the class super fun and fairly easy to understand. His tests are difficult but if you work hard, there's still a chance to receive an A in this class.  Again, if you are thinking about taking this class, TAKE IT FROM HIM! HE'S THE BEST!
Great professor! Explain concepts vary clearly and lectures are fun to attend. Very long homework. His posted all the past exams, so you have plenty resources available to prepare yourself.
Very good teacher for a tough subject. He cared about the class and was willing to answer questions. If you want to understand the material take this course from Dr. Platt!

The class is challenging, but definitely doable. He's a great lecturer, very good at explaining tough concepts. Practice tests are super helpful. You don't need to be afraid of taking this class from Platt.

Just took the final today...took me 3 and a half hours. Tests are no joke. He gives you a bunch of old tests for practice, but I felt like the actual tests were harder. He is a great teacher, with a lot of interesting insights and thoughts! I'd recommend this course. Just study study!

Professor Platt is absolutely awesome! He has been one of my favorite teachers. He teaches clearly, completely, and makes it interesting. Even though he only offers spring and summer, he makes the workload manageable and you can get a good grade if you work hard. In my opinion, he's the best Econ 110 Prof you're going to find!

Excellent professor. He explained concepts of economics very well. He is always willing to talk to you after class. He is passionate about his work, which is important. You do have to attend class and pay attention and do the assignments otherwise you could easily fall behind. The assignments in the class were pretty straightforward. Great class.

Dr. Platt is likely one of my favorite professors thus far in my experience at BYU.  He is excellent at explaining the difficult concepts, and despite the difficulty of the material, getting a good grade in his class is definitely doable. I highly recommend Dr. Platt and his econ110 class.

Do not take 382 from Platt. I cruised through 380 and got an A, but 382 from Platt was the worst class I've taken in the econ program. His homeworks are insane, the TA's are not qualified to help you, and the tests are heavily focused on "theory" which you were too busy to learn since you were trying to finish the insane problems in the homeworks.
Professor Platt was great. He is always upbeat and explains things very clearly with graphs and slides. Great class. The tests are very difficult but doable.

Platt was one of the best teachers. His class was hard, but in a very organized, thought-provoking way. If you have trouble, go to his office hours, he really does want to help. Everything he does is planned and he articulates concepts really well. There is a bit of a curve starting out, just learn his style and you'll love it. He's the best!

He allows up to five absences. Book/online access code that costs about $100, maybe a little more, is required.  That said, the tests aren't as hard as people make them out to be.  Attend class, copy down graphs, study for a few hours before each test, and go through the class slides that he posts online and you will do well; an A is very doable

he is the best Econ 110 teacher at Provo, he has all his slide printed so you know what to focus on. He is so organized, and he is not arrogant like other Econ 110 professors, He also provides the last 3 years of midterms he has administered, if you practice those and are understanding the material on them and getting the right answers, Ul do good.
I would not recommend taking a class from Professor Platt. His lectures are boring. I was tempted to zone out many times. Although he is a nice guy, I think his tests are quite unfair.

Platt was an excellent professor! When I started the class, I was thinking about switching from an Econ major to just a minor because my other classes had burned me out. This class made me love the subject again though! Great prof; passionate, easy to understand, helpful and super personable. Got to know all the students. Take his class if you can!
Professor Platt was great. He is very organized in his lectures, which helps students understand the material. It is a tough and demanding class, but very doable. I would definitely recommend Platt.

Great class. Platt loves to teach and does a great job. He's wonderful at explaining the concepts. He's not quite as sarcastic as Kearl or Lefgren, but he has a fun seance of humor. Tests have a math and intuition focus and very mild. An A is 92 percent. I don't know a single student who disliked the class. I would take 382 from him (or Lefgren).

The class material is moderately hard overall but totally possible to get a good grade.  He is not the best lecturer in the world and focuses way more on spitting out as much information as possible before class is over than making sure it makes sense.
He is a good professor.  He did a good job at explaining concepts.  The tests were tough, but not impossible.  The class was fair though and he is organized and clear.  Take econ from Platt.

Last poster must have been sleeping the whole time, because Platt is an incredibly well-organizaed, clear, and helpful professor, and the tests aren't bad.  Expectations are straightforward and he posts the actual midterm and final tests from the last 3 years to help you prepare.  Funny guy; entertaining lectures too. always smiling, pretty young.

HARDEST Econ 110 professor! People complain about Kearl but they still get B's in his class. This class seems easy at first but is INSANE once you get to the later material. Assignments on Aplia are okay, but the exams are way harder than the other professors. I got a B+ and I put in about 9 hours a week. Exams are 60% of your grade so STUDY HARD!!

All homework is online. He's enthusiastic about economics. The textbook (also online) is very clear and was more help to me than lectures.  He posts the midterms and finals from the two previous years as practice tests and they are big helps.  Weekly 500 word essay, about two homework assignments per week.  Very helpful during office hours
HIghest recommendations.

Highly highly recommended.Extremely well organized,extremely passionate about economics.Clear lectures,great examples,always willing to help students.Stay on top of homeworks and essays,GO TO THE CLASS,tests aren't too bad.Talk to him personally,TA lab sucks.If you plan on having a really good understanding of Economics,Dr.PLATT IS THE MAN.!!

Great teacher. Aplia makes it very easy to understand, but his lectures are extremely clear and helpful. I never used the TAs or study groups, but between Aplia and lectures, I felt I understood everything. Weekly papers/responses, but not too bad. Take econ from him!

I took this class as a pre-req for getting into the business program and it was tough (as are all econ classes).  Going to lectures is a must because Platt gives good examples and application problems for the concepts. Stay on top of the assignments and get help from the lab the day you need it.
Great teacher! If you have to take Econ 110 take it from Dr. Platt! I took it from Dr. Kearl last semester and hated it; this class was so much easier to understand. I actually enjoy economics now!

Platt is a very good teacher, his lectures are worth it (you can hardly afford to miss a day). He lets you know what his expectations are up front, as well as what you can expect on the tests. Homework and tests are pretty difficult, but that's because the material itself is tough.

Excellent professor! Lectures were very clear and he is INCREDIBLY well organized. The material itself is difficult, so don't blame him for that. Homeworks are pretty intense, but he gives you plenty of time. Don't procrastinate! Go to TA labs (I recommend for every homework)! Have a study buddy! Tests are challenging but do-able.
Very nice teacher. His class made you strech but was to too bad!

Dr. Platt is one of the best teachers that I've had in the Econ program. He knows his stuff (lectures are great), and will not move on until the concepts are clear.The homework is insane, but attending TA hours will cut down that time significantly. He lets you know exactly what will be on the test, which is a change from many other Econ professors

Of course it's a hard class. All Econ 110 classes are hard at BYU, but I've heard worse about other teachers of the Econ. Professor Platt is very passionate about the subject yet doesn't go off on tangents and is very organized. I would recommend this class.
Smart teacher, knows his subject very well. Useful class.

His class will bore you to tears. Its so boring, and doesn't make you want to learn or come to class. Platt is rediclous, and a goof ball. His test are beasts, and his TA's are even worse. I strongly recommend not taking the class from him.
Very good prof.  He uses powerpoint as most do for his lectures and supplements with overheads and graphs.  The weekly essays aren't too bad either.
Uses overheads and powerpoint for lectures.  He is very good at explaining the graphs he draws on the overhead.

This is Dr Platt's first time teaching econ 110. He is a theorist and I felt he was trying to convert everyone in the class to a theorist point of view. Pretty forgiving but beastly tests. Homework load was not too bad. Econ is just a beastly course at BYU. Plan on TONZ of hours and utilize the TA's if you want a decent grade.

Whew, 382 was a doozy from Platt. His TA's were good and I spent alot of time in the lab. He is also pretty good at making himself available to talk to his students. Apparently he is more of a theorist so this may not be the best teacher to take, unless you plan on doing an Econ PH.D. Tough class. Long tests. Teacher is a cool guy though.

Dr. Platt really loves the topic, and I think he presents it well. It's evident that he is new, but there's no way around that one. The only problem I really noticed with him was that his tests were ridiculously long! Get a good TA and plan on many hours in the ECON lab (and testing center) and you'll do fine.

Prof. Platt likes to teach. He's a theorist, so I think he likes to make the class more intense than it needs to be. Given that he's new, I can allow some slack, but the material wasn't taught too clearly. I love micro, especially the topics in 382, I wish I understood them better than I do now.

Professor Platt is the wrong guy to take Econ 382 from. He knows the material very well, and is very smart, but he likes to show  it. his hw's are ridiculous and doesn't really care about his students learning, he just cares about getting through the material.
He was an okay professor. He graded your testimony more than anything. Found ways to deduct my grades even when I did the full work. Try to take it from a different professor if you are taking REL.

I took REL 250C from him. He is really good. It is easy to get an A from him, you just have to show up and do the outlines to pass. It is not a lot of work, and the homework is easy. He gives you "hope cards" for little things, if you want to skip a test or don't go to class once, you can use them and you'll be fine.

To be honest I was not a big fan of they way he teaches. You wont be able to check your phone all year, even if you want to know what time it is. He turns off the lights sometimes just to see if he can catch people using their phones.  I didn't like the way he taught and wouldn't take him again! I think he ask too much for a religion class!

Brother Schmidt is a brilliant guy. If you are interested in the history, translation and background of the New Testament, this is the class for you. Personally, I didn't feel the Spirit enough in class and we didn't go into doctrines as much as I would have liked. He is definitely a good guy and makes class easy if you put a little work in.

2 papers 2 tests. only read the docs you plan on writing about for your papers. Do the essay portion of the tests and be sure to cite some of the docs. I never read a single page in the text and only read 16 of the 100s of docs but I attended every class and scored high on the tests. Also just burn a copy of the DVD from someone dont buy one.

Best professor in the EXSC department hands down. If you need a sign to take a class from him, look no further. He is always willing to work with you if something comes up during the semester. Make sure to go to class if you want to do well on tests. Truly this guy just loves to teach and he cares more about students than anything else. 100/10

Dr. Feland is the BEST! I have taken multiple classes from him and he is by far my favorite professor at BYU. You can tell he truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed. Attendance is not technically mandatory, but he says a of things during lecture that aren't necessarily written in the slides but is important to know.

I was scared to take a neuro class but this is one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. He teaches the material in such an easy way that helps everyone to learn and engage with the class. He's always willing to help and work with you and makes everything so fun and manageable. 11/10 recommend.

Dr. Feland is my favorite professor at BYU. He cares so much about his students and will let you make up almost everything as long as you ask. He is super willing to work with you and is a super fun and engaging lecturer. You'll be on the tables everyday learning things practically and he'll review things as you go to help solidify your knowledge.

I loved Doctor Feland, and he teaches very well. His class is a bit disorganized, but not in a way that makes it difficult to know what expectations are. His exams are all based heavily on his powerpoint slides, so study those and you'll do well. He does a great job of catering to the needs of the class; he pushed exam dates around a couple times.

440 is tough, but Feland makes it so much more manageable. He can be a bit disorganized but if he messes up he always makes it up. If you study your O and I's then you've got it made. He is very clearly passionate about what he teaches and does a good job at making it clinically relevant.

Take 440 from Feland! This class will be HARD no matter who you take it from, but I promise you'll enjoy it with Feland. Stay on top of the OIAI's, if you fall behind on those the quizzes/class will be brutal. There was only one assignment outside of class besides preparing for the quizzes. Great spiritual thoughts! And he cares about his students!

Dr. Feland is the kindest and most engaging professor! Take 440 from him if you can, he's super flexible with your schedule and cares about you personally. He really cares about the material and has great hands on demonstrations every class to help you learn and to keep you engaged and having fun. I cannot say enough good things about Dr. Feland!

You have a quiz every class period that requires a lot of memorization. Though you have to put in time for the quizzes he is a super great guy. He is nice, caring, and lets you retake a quiz if you miss one. He is super understanding and wants us to succeed and help us know what he is teaching. Highly recommend this class!

I took 460 and 470 from Feland, he is the BEST. He's super passionate, and his lectures are very engaging. His tests are pretty hard, but based off his slides. His class can be disorganized and chaotic, but he's responsive to emails. Also, he takes the time to learn every student's name and really cares about his students.

Feland is a great professor and person. I took 460 and 470 from him. He really cares about his students and enjoys what he's is teaching. If you attend class and pay attention, his classes aren't too difficult.

Might be my favorite class I've ever taken. Dr. Feland is very chill, very smart, and explains things well. Everything is really relevant and interesting. Tests are taken from lecture and from the slides, so they're pretty easy to study for. He is very kind and spiritual as well. Sad I can't take another class from him. Would recommend to everyone.

Dr. Feland is amazing. Super kind, caring, and really wants you to succeed in his class. Lectures were really good and very insightful, but tests were difficult. Memorize the power point slides because they're 95% of the test. Take Feland's class if you want a laid back, educational, and fun class.

Dr Feland is awesome! Super engaging lectures, lots of useful and applicable concepts are covered.  Exams are  very specific and difficult until you realize that 95% of the questions come directly from his power point slides, so if you memorize those verbatim then youll do fine.

Most days he gives a brief introduction different anatomy and how to do different exercises safely and then you do those exercises for the rest of the class. He is a physical therapist and knows his stuff. Loved the class since I'm a beginner, I feel more confident in what I'm doing at the gym now and what not do to.

This class is a tough one, but Feland gives you everything you need to succeed. He puts the textbook readings online so you don't need to buy one. There were a lot of powerpoints for this course that he used for lectures and which had a lot of information. But he creates the tests on these powerpoints, so they are useful. Overall, great professor.

Feland does a great job of engaging students in the learning process. Lectures are very hands on doing different tests on each other. He does a short quiz about once a week at the beginning of class. He's great at answering questions. Tests are straightforward, but can include pretty specific details. All info is in the slides, though. He's great!

100% would recommend Dr. Feland. He's very clear on what you need to know for tests, and doesn't try to trick you.  Class is super hands on, and feels like things I will actually use in my future career. No busywork, put in the time and effort and you will do well. He also knows the material increbilely well. Lectures are pretty funny as well.

There are like 5 exams. He's not the most engaging lecturer but he does well enough. Great guy, and he's super willing to help. Make sure to study throughout the semester because it's not material you can cram easily. Overall, it's worth taking his class. Great experience.

LOVED HIM!! Will definitely take more classes from him in the future. He explains things well and makes it interesting. He chose to explain in depth certain aspects and skip others. Study the homework and powerpoints well and you're set for the tests.

Dr. Feland is awesome. The class is very straightforward. Not a lot of homework, just some in class quizzes. He doesnt believe in trying to trick students on his exams so everything you need to know comes straight from the lecture slides and lab classes.

Dr Feland is awesome! This class is way easier than EXSC 440! This was the second time I had Feland for a professor and I am going to take 470 with him because he is such a great teacher! He teaches the class very simply and doesn't try to trick you on the tests. The information is very straight forward.

Feland is a really great professor, and i took 440 from him which was a lot more memorization but his 470 is really interesting and he is super passionate about what he is teaching about. He is always super caring and will send out an email about the quizzes and tries to make the class as applicable as possible! TAKE 470 from Feland. Best decision!

Feland is a great lecturer and a nice dude. My only complaint is that the class is VERY heavily based on origins, insertions, actions & innervations of just about every muscle in the body. The exams are very focused on these (like 70%). Other profs only test on the lecture material which is easy, so you'd be better off taking 440 from one of them.

Feland is a good teacher, his slides are good and really tries to explain stuff. BUT, this class is based almost ENTIRELY on origins an insertions for every muscle in the body. You have to memorize O&I, action and innervation for large groups of muscles for weekly quizzes and then that's basically what the entire exam is. Its very overwhelming.

Dr. Feland is the best, probably my favorite teacher at BYU. His tests require a lot of memorization but are really straightforward, and all the material is clinically relevant. he is lenient with grading and wants to help you out. Any class you can take from him, take it.

Feland is awesome. Super funny, clear lectures, very applicable. I really enjoyed coming to class each day. The only downside is that he requires a 94% for an A. But, all things considered his tests were all MC and very clear and straightforward, so if you know his slides you'll be good. Definitely take from Feland!

Any class you can take from feland do it! He is way cool and you learn a ton. Grade is based solely on quizzes and tests but he gives study objectives that are all you need to know. Probably my favorite professor I have had at BYU

Nice guy, but hard tests. Insane amount of memorization which is why you take the final in groups of 4. Even had to rush through the last half to finish on time. Cumulative daily quizzes of O, I, action, and innervation of 6-8 new muscles each time so you're always studying. No breaks. If you're not pre-PT, someone else might be easier.

Feland is the man. accessible and helpful. His classes require a lot of memorization and studying, but it is clear what will be on the tests just put in the time. quizzes at the beginning of every class but then you could  just leave look at the slides and be fine. Don't bother buying a textbook. Take it from him!
This has been my favorite class at BYU, Dr. Feland is the BOMB! He's an awesome professor, does not try to trick you on the tests and is always there to answer questions

Awesome teacher. Seriously he's hilarious and his lectures are awesome. Lots of work there's no denying that.. The work is interesting and 100% useful though. No busy work nonsense. I enjoyed every assignment. I would NOT take this class from anyone other than Feland. He's the man. I got an A.

Class is pretty straightforward but not a cake walk like people on here make it out to be. The average on the final was 77% (After he gave it a 2% raise). Why the low helpfulness score? He refused to round my grade up .05% so I could be in the next category - that's right not .5%, .05%! Kinda lost respect for the guy

Dr. Feland is very concerned with the success of his students. He is also very straightforward with what he expects and pretty much tells you what's going to be on the test. There is a ton of memorization though, that's why he can be so clear on what's going to be on the tests. Never miss class or lab, and go to extra labs before the test.

One of my favorite professors! Super easy class if you go to class, take notes, and are interested in the subject matter. He tells you exactly what to know for tests. I really liked his style of teaching, relaxed and fair.
He is a great teacher! He knows his material and tells you exactly what you need to know!

Class is only easy if you study because he is straight forward in telling you what you need to know for exams.  If you are not good at memorizing then this class will be really hard.   He makes it as entertaining as anatomy could possibly be.  Great class

He is a good teacher. He knows the material well. Has a great personality for teaching. The class is all memorization of course, I recommend getting a study-buddy the first day, Feland recommends it as well. I really enjoyed this class. Oh, and there are 4 cadavers for this course.

Feland is one of the best teachers ever!! The class is just as everyone said, easy.  All you have to do is study the notes and you're set.  Just make sure that you pay attention, he tells you just what's on the test. Take any class you can!!
Gets to the point and tells you before hand what he wants you to know and what he expects from you.  Pretty funny and entertaining.
Great entertaining teacher. Gives those he likes better grades. Group project grading was unfair, two did all the work and everyone got the same grade and he wasn't very open to suggestions.
He is super fun and super easy. Just follow the study guide and study your notes thoroughly before the test.
He's a good teacher and puts humor in his classes.

This class was A LOT of fun. He had a make a video presentation that he wanted to be funny. The tests are easy if you really study the study guide he gives you and review your notes, but make sure you pay attention to detail. He really funny, class is definately not boring.

Feland is an excellent teacher for any class, this one is no exception.  I've taken almost every class he teaches.  The material is very difficult, but he makes it do-able.  This is a great class if you are going into physical therapy.
The class is super-duper easy.  Just don't leave your shadow hours to the very end.  Feland is absolutely hilarious...!
He's very laid back and easy going. He is very helpful and easy to talk to.  Take him if you can.
I really liked taking this class from Feland.  He gives you lots of lab time to memerize. He's a very reasonable grader.  You'll be glad you took it from him.
I took the 460 night class, and it was awesome.  He makes it fun, and interesting, and doesn't make it too hard.  I would recommend him for any class that he teaches.
