Best professor in the EXSC department hands down. If you need a sign to take a class from him, look no further. He is always willing to work with you if something comes up during the semester. Make sure to go to class if you want to do well on tests. Truly this guy just loves to teach and he cares more about students than anything else. 100/10

Dr. Feland is the BEST! I have taken multiple classes from him and he is by far my favorite professor at BYU. You can tell he truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed. Attendance is not technically mandatory, but he says a of things during lecture that aren't necessarily written in the slides but is important to know.

I was scared to take a neuro class but this is one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. He teaches the material in such an easy way that helps everyone to learn and engage with the class. He's always willing to help and work with you and makes everything so fun and manageable. 11/10 recommend.

Dr. Feland is my favorite professor at BYU. He cares so much about his students and will let you make up almost everything as long as you ask. He is super willing to work with you and is a super fun and engaging lecturer. You'll be on the tables everyday learning things practically and he'll review things as you go to help solidify your knowledge.

I loved Doctor Feland, and he teaches very well. His class is a bit disorganized, but not in a way that makes it difficult to know what expectations are. His exams are all based heavily on his powerpoint slides, so study those and you'll do well. He does a great job of catering to the needs of the class; he pushed exam dates around a couple times.

440 is tough, but Feland makes it so much more manageable. He can be a bit disorganized but if he messes up he always makes it up. If you study your O and I's then you've got it made. He is very clearly passionate about what he teaches and does a good job at making it clinically relevant.

Take 440 from Feland! This class will be HARD no matter who you take it from, but I promise you'll enjoy it with Feland. Stay on top of the OIAI's, if you fall behind on those the quizzes/class will be brutal. There was only one assignment outside of class besides preparing for the quizzes. Great spiritual thoughts! And he cares about his students!

Dr. Feland is the kindest and most engaging professor! Take 440 from him if you can, he's super flexible with your schedule and cares about you personally. He really cares about the material and has great hands on demonstrations every class to help you learn and to keep you engaged and having fun. I cannot say enough good things about Dr. Feland!

You have a quiz every class period that requires a lot of memorization. Though you have to put in time for the quizzes he is a super great guy. He is nice, caring, and lets you retake a quiz if you miss one. He is super understanding and wants us to succeed and help us know what he is teaching. Highly recommend this class!

I took 460 and 470 from Feland, he is the BEST. He's super passionate, and his lectures are very engaging. His tests are pretty hard, but based off his slides. His class can be disorganized and chaotic, but he's responsive to emails. Also, he takes the time to learn every student's name and really cares about his students.

Feland is a great professor and person. I took 460 and 470 from him. He really cares about his students and enjoys what he's is teaching. If you attend class and pay attention, his classes aren't too difficult.

Might be my favorite class I've ever taken. Dr. Feland is very chill, very smart, and explains things well. Everything is really relevant and interesting. Tests are taken from lecture and from the slides, so they're pretty easy to study for. He is very kind and spiritual as well. Sad I can't take another class from him. Would recommend to everyone.

Dr. Feland is amazing. Super kind, caring, and really wants you to succeed in his class. Lectures were really good and very insightful, but tests were difficult. Memorize the power point slides because they're 95% of the test. Take Feland's class if you want a laid back, educational, and fun class.

Dr Feland is awesome! Super engaging lectures, lots of useful and applicable concepts are covered.  Exams are  very specific and difficult until you realize that 95% of the questions come directly from his power point slides, so if you memorize those verbatim then youll do fine.

Most days he gives a brief introduction different anatomy and how to do different exercises safely and then you do those exercises for the rest of the class. He is a physical therapist and knows his stuff. Loved the class since I'm a beginner, I feel more confident in what I'm doing at the gym now and what not do to.

This class is a tough one, but Feland gives you everything you need to succeed. He puts the textbook readings online so you don't need to buy one. There were a lot of powerpoints for this course that he used for lectures and which had a lot of information. But he creates the tests on these powerpoints, so they are useful. Overall, great professor.

Feland does a great job of engaging students in the learning process. Lectures are very hands on doing different tests on each other. He does a short quiz about once a week at the beginning of class. He's great at answering questions. Tests are straightforward, but can include pretty specific details. All info is in the slides, though. He's great!

100% would recommend Dr. Feland. He's very clear on what you need to know for tests, and doesn't try to trick you.  Class is super hands on, and feels like things I will actually use in my future career. No busywork, put in the time and effort and you will do well. He also knows the material increbilely well. Lectures are pretty funny as well.

There are like 5 exams. He's not the most engaging lecturer but he does well enough. Great guy, and he's super willing to help. Make sure to study throughout the semester because it's not material you can cram easily. Overall, it's worth taking his class. Great experience.

LOVED HIM!! Will definitely take more classes from him in the future. He explains things well and makes it interesting. He chose to explain in depth certain aspects and skip others. Study the homework and powerpoints well and you're set for the tests.

Dr. Feland is awesome. The class is very straightforward. Not a lot of homework, just some in class quizzes. He doesnt believe in trying to trick students on his exams so everything you need to know comes straight from the lecture slides and lab classes.

Dr Feland is awesome! This class is way easier than EXSC 440! This was the second time I had Feland for a professor and I am going to take 470 with him because he is such a great teacher! He teaches the class very simply and doesn't try to trick you on the tests. The information is very straight forward.

Feland is a really great professor, and i took 440 from him which was a lot more memorization but his 470 is really interesting and he is super passionate about what he is teaching about. He is always super caring and will send out an email about the quizzes and tries to make the class as applicable as possible! TAKE 470 from Feland. Best decision!

Feland is a great lecturer and a nice dude. My only complaint is that the class is VERY heavily based on origins, insertions, actions & innervations of just about every muscle in the body. The exams are very focused on these (like 70%). Other profs only test on the lecture material which is easy, so you'd be better off taking 440 from one of them.

Feland is a good teacher, his slides are good and really tries to explain stuff. BUT, this class is based almost ENTIRELY on origins an insertions for every muscle in the body. You have to memorize O&I, action and innervation for large groups of muscles for weekly quizzes and then that's basically what the entire exam is. Its very overwhelming.

Dr. Feland is the best, probably my favorite teacher at BYU. His tests require a lot of memorization but are really straightforward, and all the material is clinically relevant. he is lenient with grading and wants to help you out. Any class you can take from him, take it.

Feland is awesome. Super funny, clear lectures, very applicable. I really enjoyed coming to class each day. The only downside is that he requires a 94% for an A. But, all things considered his tests were all MC and very clear and straightforward, so if you know his slides you'll be good. Definitely take from Feland!

Any class you can take from feland do it! He is way cool and you learn a ton. Grade is based solely on quizzes and tests but he gives study objectives that are all you need to know. Probably my favorite professor I have had at BYU

Nice guy, but hard tests. Insane amount of memorization which is why you take the final in groups of 4. Even had to rush through the last half to finish on time. Cumulative daily quizzes of O, I, action, and innervation of 6-8 new muscles each time so you're always studying. No breaks. If you're not pre-PT, someone else might be easier.

Feland is the man. accessible and helpful. His classes require a lot of memorization and studying, but it is clear what will be on the tests just put in the time. quizzes at the beginning of every class but then you could  just leave look at the slides and be fine. Don't bother buying a textbook. Take it from him!
This has been my favorite class at BYU, Dr. Feland is the BOMB! He's an awesome professor, does not try to trick you on the tests and is always there to answer questions

Awesome teacher. Seriously he's hilarious and his lectures are awesome. Lots of work there's no denying that.. The work is interesting and 100% useful though. No busy work nonsense. I enjoyed every assignment. I would NOT take this class from anyone other than Feland. He's the man. I got an A.

Class is pretty straightforward but not a cake walk like people on here make it out to be. The average on the final was 77% (After he gave it a 2% raise). Why the low helpfulness score? Dr. Feland is very concerned with the success of his students. He is also very straightforward with what he expects and pretty much tells you what's going to be on the test. There is a ton of memorization though, that's why he can be so clear on what's going to be on the tests. Never miss class or lab, and go to extra labs before the test.

One of my favorite professors! Super easy class if you go to class, take notes, and are interested in the subject matter. He tells you exactly what to know for tests. I really liked his style of teaching, relaxed and fair.
He is a great teacher! He knows his material and tells you exactly what you need to know!

Class is only easy if you study because he is straight forward in telling you what you need to know for exams.  If you are not good at memorizing then this class will be really hard.   He makes it as entertaining as anatomy could possibly be.  Great class

He is a good teacher. He knows the material well. Has a great personality for teaching. The class is all memorization of course, I recommend getting a study-buddy the first day, Feland recommends it as well. I really enjoyed this class. Oh, and there are 4 cadavers for this course.

Feland is one of the best teachers ever!! The class is just as everyone said, easy.  All you have to do is study the notes and you're set.  Just make sure that you pay attention, he tells you just what's on the test. Take any class you can!!
Gets to the point and tells you before hand what he wants you to know and what he expects from you.  Pretty funny and entertaining.

Dr. Wells is the best! Do music with him, you will not regret it!

Dr. Wells is the best professor I have had during my time at BYU! Singing in the Men's Chorus is 100% the best part of my day, and he holds the choir to high standards, but the payoff, along with his jokes, makes taking any class from him worth it.
If you love singing and want an uplifting (and entertaining) class, audition for Men's Chorus. Doctor Wells is an amazing conductor.
Most amazing professor ever.
One of my favorite people ever.

Dr. Wells is the best.

Dr. Wells is such a good guy. Not only is he an incredible choral conductor, but he very clearly loves his students and cares about our success both in and outside of his class. TAKE MENS CHORUS ITS AMAZING AND YOU WONT REGRET IT. Just be sure to confirm the calendar of events with your semester beforehand to avoid conflicts.

Im in mens chorus and this is the best choir director I have ever had.

Dr. Wells is awesome! I couldn't have asked for a better choir director for this year. His jokes are great, he chooses awesome music, and he makes Men's Chorus enjoyable. Anyone looking for a great class and a great director should take Men's Chorus with Dr. Wells.

Dr. Wells did a great job during his first year as director of the Men's Chorus at BYU. He definitely has a different style than Sister Hall, but I thought he did an excellent job taking on the role of choir director during COVID. Very well done.

Dr. Wells is a fantastic director. Men's Chorus isn't the same without Sister Hall, but he's filled her shoes remarkably well, even in the midst of the COVID pandemic, and I'm sure he'll settle in even better given time. He's so awesome! All that you need to do is show up and ask questions. Hands down my favorite theory teacher ever!

He's really kind and funny but moves super quickly. He's really good at explaining the material, though, so if you just pay attention in class, then it's not a hard class. Miss class? He responds to emails super quickly with topics you can research yourself if you want!

Dr. Y is great, he cares that you do well in his class. He teaches music theory very efficiently, his videos are great and I still use them. Dr. Y is a solid choice if you're going to take music theory at BYU!!!

Dr. Yorgason is a very kind, soft-spoken man who is invested in your success. He had such a calming presence that was great to be welcomed by early in the morning. You learn so much and he was very easy to learn from.

Dr. Yorgason teaches so clearly! I still use his videos as a reference for all things theory-related because he explains things concisely and clearly. He is friendly and easygoing and always ready to help. Reasonable amounts of homework and tests are doable.

Professor Yorgason is great! He's a good teacher and really knows what he's talking about. There is quite a bit of homework that takes a while, but it's important that you do it because it's the best way to learn the Theory and do well on the test. Yorgason has an archaic understanding of what music education should be. Hes very particular about theory and gets caught up on the stupidest arguments about no longer relevant music. Not too hard to approach.

Dr. Y is super great. He cares about his students and makes learning theory accessible. He caters his classes towards what the students need help with and he really appreciates questions. His class is very straightforward and if you show up most of the time you will do well. I 100% recommend taking theory from him.

Super excellent teacher! He teaches clearly, and makes concepts east to understand. He has a great sense of humor and is really understanding if you need to miss class. You also get a chance to take skill tests up to 2 times and online quizzes unlimited times. SUPER GOOD PROF! WOULD RECOMMEND1

He puts everything you need to know about music theory in your hands and then encourages you to do something with it.  Completely reasonable.  The class is very well structured.  It is an effective educational experience.  And, his is jokes are all original because he's teaching people not lessons.  He cares about music and theory and his students.

LOVED his class! Very easy to understand the material when he teaches. Homework nearly every time but none of it is unreasonable. He wants you to succeed and is nice outside of class too. This is my third theory course from him and he's my favorite!

Dr. Y is an awesome theory teacher. He's great at explaining concepts and answering questions. It's obvious that he loves music theory and he spreads that enjoyment to his students. His classes are both informative and fun. I've taken three theory courses from him so far.
He is a great teacher and will take from him again

Dr. Y is super awesome. Out of any Theory Core professor I've had so far, he's been the best at explaining things clearly. For anyone who feels like they're miles behind their peers when it comes to theory, Dr. Y is a great choice. He cares about each of his students and will go out of his way to help you succeed. Definitely recommend. Funny too.

I know many IT students complain about Bret Swan being disorganized. This is because he changes his course/assignments every single sem to adjust with current IT market compared to teachers who teach same stuff and graded same assignment for past 7 years. no comment

@IT355: Very Unorganized Professor i have ever seen.He does not know students have other classes as well in the same semester  @IT350: I doubt having him as a teacher for database class.He is seriously so much unorganized on his homeworks,assignments and projects at all-scary work load sometimes and no work sometimes--

This class was horrible! All major projects are graded during finals week, including the ones due months prior. Grades are always a surprise, but then again so are the assignments. If you don't care about learning and love disorganization at its best, this is the class/professor for you.

Earlier comments talked about IT 101 being "in transition".  As of last semester, it's figured out.  I really enjoyed the class.  Dr. Swan can be kind of disorganized, but get to know him, talk to him after class, etc, and he can be a great source of help and guidance for your whole education career.

Half the class was taught by other professors. The lectures were horribly boring. The Labs were either ridiculously easy and could be done in 10 minutes or they were overly hard requiring the use of software for which Dr. Swan would provide 3 hours of tutorials, instead of just showing us a simple example. No tests, no quizzes. Easy A.

My interest in the material was overshadowed by how bad this class was organized.  It felt like there was no accountability.  We often waited weeks before getting grades back on projects or assignments.  The instructor seemed to not know about the material.  The TA seemed like he knew more.  Set your expectations low for this one.

This class was incredibly boring. If you're there to get an idea of what IT is you'll get that in the first week and wonder why you're still there. The weekly labs are more busy work than anything, you just have to fill them out to get credit. No quizzes, no tests. There was no class structure. You only need to go to class for a few in class labs.

Kinda funny teacher, mostly boring. Course is poorly designed and at times worthlessly easy and other times incredibly hard.  Not what a freshman seminar class should be. Stay away from this teacher if you can help it.
Very, very unorganized. Canceled class on a regular basis. Instructions for projects very unclear, but he is willing to help and add further direction when approached. Easy A

I can't believe this class is a 2 credit hour class that meets 4 hours a week to watch the discovery channel.  The TA handled all the labs, all of the homework, and I'm sure most of the tests.  The material isn't difficult, but because of Swan, the class has serious flaws.

He was trying to redo the class while I was in it but most of the assignments where just bussy work and you really don't retain any of it. He never really taught much eather Great class but just needs a little work. Take it if you are willing to work by yourself and learn by yourself.

IT 101.... I felt Like i was in high school still.  Its not a hard class if you want an easy A, but if you want to actually learn something..... not the best professor.  3/4 the way through the semester he decided to cancel the final because he felt he gave us to much homework earlier on.  You are thrown in with all ranges of computer proficiency.

Assignments were often off topic or about something we hadn't learned. Didn't give feedback or grades for anything until after the semester was over.  Assigned a 20 hour final project with only 4 class days left, then failed several of us for not following some made up project criteria that was not in the written project criteria.

Really cares about the topic and his students. Knows how to apply what you're learning to real life, makes tests and assignments more business format, which is awesome. Could do project instead of final. Class itself had some bad labs, but the TA was helpful and the lectures were interesting. Bro. Swan's a great guy, I recommend him!
Awesome class!

Everything in the class is heavily weighted, falling behind can tank your grade. It's easy to lose a lot of points if you misread questions or struggle with exams. Overall, he is a good teacher and the discussions are engaging, but the course is strict and unforgiving with homework and grades.

You will read a TON of plays in this class (shocker) but I really enjoyed all of them. You can also watch recordings of the plays BYU Library Drama Online Database. Attendance isn't mandatory, but classes are fun and discussion-based. 2-3 pretty easy 2-page papers. Tests weren't bad.

Prof McInelly is my favorite professor I have had in college thus far! His class structure was completely discussion based and helped me not only understand Shakespeare, but also gain knowledge on how to delve deeply into literature. His class environment is comfortable and it's on your honor whether you read the books and attend the class!

I highly recommend Dr. McInelly as he has great knowledge of the texts you read, interesting discussions, and an overall good class environment. While he is a very hard grade, an A is definitely possible. Make sure to do the readings thoroughly and go to office hours to have him read through your papers-- he provides great feedback!

Hes a tough grader, never gives anyone 100%. He will take points off even if he believes you have the best paper ever made. This class we read 7 shakespeare plays. He has 3 easy papers and a midterm and a final. The midterm and final grades are pretty much 80% of your grade. hes a really nice guy and I enjoyed his lectures and the class!

Really nice guy. Attendance was not mandatory, but he made things interesting when I did go. He grades tough on writing; says he doesn't believe in giving 100%, which he stood by all year (highest grade I ever saw from anyone was a 57/60). An A- is totally realistic, but an A is very difficult. 

Also I took English 232 but its not an option

I really like him as a teacher. He's nice and seems to genuinely care about your opinions, but I didn't love how so few things determined my grade. Your term paper at the end of the semester is almost half your grade. And you can have an A until the end, and then drop to an A- because he is a hard grader on writing. Gcod class though overall.

Dr. McInelly is a knowledgeable professor who cares about his students and their understanding of the material. He selected challenging texts and helped us to understand both historical background and literary analysis. My biggest criticism was that there were EIGHT total assignments, so it was difficult to improve my grade. Overall, I recommend.
Experienced teacher and relevant lectures. Lots of chances for revision and feedback on papers before submission.
Nicest professor ever. There is a lot of reading in short amounts of time but the books are always good.

By far one of my favorite professors! Listens to students and is willing to be flexible on assignments. Idk why he's gotten bad ratings. He's an easy grader, super fun, and plays movies in class sometimes! There's a lot of reading but they're good books so it's not bad. The class is discussion based but you don't have to talk to get points.

Prof McInelly is a SOLID choice. I would def recommend him. There is a lot of class discussion and peer review, but not anything that could make anxious people like myself, well... anxious. Relevant lectures and kind person

There wasn't loads of outside work other than the papers you need to write which is expected for a writing class. I had a crazy semester and wasn't able to make it to all the classes. He was not very understanding about my absences which lead to my grade dropping a lot! He is a good professor, I just felt a lack of caring for his students.

Professor McInelly is one of my favorite teachers at BYU! He is really good at listening to his students and answering questions. There is quite a bit of reading, but nothing unusual for an English class. He gives great feedback on essays and he is willing to meet with you whenever it works best for the both of you. I HIGHLY recommend him!

Loved this course, I learned a lot about British literary history and also felt like my writing improved. Well-organized, clear, and interesting. Profess McInelly is very willing to meet with you and discuss papers, questions, concerns.

Professor McInelly is fair and structured.  I took an Independent Study course and it was well run.  He responded quickly to emails and was clear in his expectations.  My advice is to do all the homework, be diligent in comprehending the readings and you will do well.  If you are stuck, contact him.  He will work with you.

I loved Prof McInelly! His class was so fun and he was very easy to understand. He listened to our feedback on the course evaluations and immediately changed what we had critiqued. He is genuinely just being a great teacher, not trying to show off his intellect or make students work their tales off to please him. He made me look forward to class.

Professor McInelly gave me a great capstone course for the English major! It was low key, actually the most relaxed, probably, of any of my other English classes. He expects you to read and participate, of course. I loved that I felt respected as a literary critic in McInelly's class. The discussions and reading material were really interesting!

Brett is an awesome teacher. He takes time to help his students and truly seems to care about your grades.  He is super helpful and just an awesome guy.  I would definitely take another class from him.

I loved Professor McInelly. You definitely had to work hard to get a good grade in this class, but if you just did what you were told to do, it was pretty simple. He's a great teacher and very, very understanding. He has amazing teaching strategies.

This class was amazing! I had so much fun in it.  If you take it winter semester you'll get to celebrate his birthday with him which was a lot of fun :) If you go to student teacher conferences he'll really like you. Definitely worth taking this class from him.

This class really helped me grow as a student - especially as an English major. Improved my writing immensely, and helped me gain appreciation for the written word. Really, I've always loved to read, but this was on an entirely different level It pushed and streched me, and it takes a good teacher to organize and teach a class that does that.

I really like Dr. McInelly. This class however, was EXTREMELY tedious. This sounds odd, but I wonder if English majors ought to take this after a year in the program, it might be more helpful later on. There is a guest lecture every week, which is fine, but when you're a freshmen you don't usually know what you want to do yet anyway. Take it later.

He seems like a really nice guy, but he only taught the class twice this semester.  The rest was filled up with guest speakers.  I learned a bit, but none of it was really helpful.  Ditto to the counseling office thing- you really could learn everything there in just a few minutes.  But an easy A, nonetheless.

Professor McInelly is pretty cool, but I don't really know for sure because he didn't actually teach the class. There was a guest speaker every week, and I hated going. I spent an entire semester sitting through lectures that really taught me nothing. Everything I learned that semester would have taken me 20 minutes in the counseling center.

Dr. McInelly is fabulous--he is absolutely one of the best professors I have ever taken a class from. He is interesting, knows his subject well, and very intelligent.  He is very willing to help his students succeed--I met with him multiple times outside of class to go over papers.  It's not a super-easy class, but it's worth the effort!
eh. I didn't care for this class at all.
Intro too the English major. He usually had a guest speaker, but he still seemed really nice and fun. I would like to take another class from him.

This was absolutely one of the best classes I've ever taken.  Dr. McInelly is incredible--he knows his stuff, is a great teacher, and is more than willing to help his students outside of class.  I would HIGHLY recommend taking this class from him.
His lectures were a regurgitation of the reading and he often showed videos of the stuff we'd read. I was really disappointed.

AMAZING professor! I am shocked at the negative reviews! I have had MANY professors at BYU and Dr. McInelly is by far one of the top five. He is a conscientious mentor and knowledgable in the subject. If you take the time to complete the course work (which is NOT too much) he is willing to help you individually as much as you need. Ignore the negs

McInelly is a great teacher.  The topics and questions he discusses in class are the prompts for test questions.  Listen carefully in class and get to know him out of class.  He is very personable and helpful.  Probably the most fare teacher I have ever had at BYU.  You get what you earn.  I have had him three times, I think he is great.
In McInelly's defense, this was his first time teaching a larger section. I hear that McInelly is more personable and fun on a micro-level.

Not very fun. Same thing everyday. If your idea of knowing exactly what to study for a test is getting 3 answers to the test, than yes, he tells you exactly what to study. However, I didn't find that mode very helpful.

Professor McInelly made you work hard to get a good grade, but isnt that what college is all about?  I think some people are biased but they should blame themselves not the teacher or TA.  If you keep up with reading and pay attention you will succeed.  He tells you exactly what to study for.
I smell a rat in these earlier comments!  Good professor, friendly and helpful.  Prepared for class.  I'd recommend Professor McInelly's class to anyone.

Lame class. Lame teacher. Boring lectures that are not helpful for tests. McInelly can't hold an engaging class discussion for his life. Analysis of literature is shallow. He doesn't ever apply literary theory & he's very closed minded to interpretation/approach. This class is not worth your time!!!

McInelly's lectures are boring Powerpoint presentations. Class discussions are repeatedly interrupted by off-the-wall comments by fatuous students, and he usually agrees with these dopey comments. His grading standards are different than his T.A.'s, so it is hard to know exactly what he wants.

Being very objective, I hated this class. Lectures weren't engaging, tests were harder than necessary. He comes across as somewhat pretentious and really doesn't seem that itelligent. He needs to lose the powerpoint lectures and show that he can do more than regurgitate the Norton chapter headings.

Mediocre at best. He has exceptionally high standards, and few students meet his expectations. He is willing to meet with students, and is nice, but isn't practical in his class or teaching. His lectures are poor, and fail to interest.
I've had better...
He's a really nice guy who loves his students. Class is always fun. Although the assignments are a lot of work, he always gives helpful feedback for improving your writing.
He's definitely hot!  That always makes class worth going to.  I never have trouble paying attention because my eyes are always glued to his beautiful face...he's a pretty good teacher, too.
Dr.  McInelly is the best!!  His class discussions are so much fun, and you will look forward to the class every day.
Amazing teacher - I have and would reccommend him to anyone wanting to improve their English writing, comprehension, and analytical skills.
Fun teacher, good discussions.

Makes the grading system a competition, which is fun for 10 people but dissuades 90% of the class from caring. What was most frustrating is he moved so fast but class often ended early and the last 2 weeks we did nothing. Content is so helpful (SQL and Excel) but its clear he just cares about having a captive audience to talk about his life

The mandatory days are the least relevant aka talking about his life. He spends 4 whole class periods talking about his life then claims he physically can't slow down on the actually important content. Unfortunately, he shows little interest in teaching the skills we actually need like SQL and Excel, but I would recommended going to those classes

He mostly talked about his own life stories and experiences, which had nothing to do with course material. Attendance was mandatory, but not super helpful to understanding the material. He was nice, but doesn't really work with you, tests are hard and he's proud of it, he tells you not to plan on finishing the tests.

Lots of lecture that didn't pertain to material, lots of life stories. Changed attendance to not mandatory halfway through. Timed in person tests that he prides on being difficult. Not much homework, all lectures can be replaced with videos from Canvas. No book. Similar to IS201 with SQL. Show up to first day of new units, can skip the rest.

Teaches great skills with Excel and SQL. Attendance was required starting out, but then he changed it midway through. He does go really fast through things in class, so have to watch videos after. Tests aren't too bad. SQL is pretty similar to stuff in IS201. Shares great life stories, though, I highly recommend going for those.

Super valuable skills, if you watch the online videos you will do well in the class. He made attendance optional during the semester and, apart from his spiritual thoughts, I didn't get anything out of class in person. Online vids are straight forward and teach you the material, TAs will help you succeed.

Professor is a very goofy guy! He enjoys teaching however was not the best at teaching challenging skills. TA's were not helpful the entire semester. Required attendance until halfway through the semester. Unfortunately, 412 is a required course to take and there are no other options. I was lost the majority of the semester.

He teaches hard skills you need for an internship/job. At the end of the summer he sends a survey to former students asking how the curriculum could be changed to help them more in internships, so he changes the curriculum every year. Will dock you 2% for every absence after the first 2 (data shows that missing more than 2 drops your grade heavily)

Don't see the point of this class being an in-person class. He moves really quickly and if you miss him, you just need to go home and watch the videos that he posted to learn it. Still don't understand why he gives a test out that nobody can finish in time. It's an in-class test on your laptop, and the given time is ridiculously short.
The most useful class I have taken at BYU! It can be challenging but he gives you all the resources he needs. He is an amazing professor and you can tell he cares about his students!

The best class I've taken at BYU. Professor Hathaway teaches purely from lectures and practice problems, so there is no required textbook. He offers videos online to watch for further assistance if it's needed. This class teaches you hard skills to add to your resume. The concepts are extremely challenging and will push you!

Professor Hathaway truly cares for his student's success. This was his first semester teaching @BYU (he previously taught at John Hopkins), so he made sure to adjust his course plans as the semester went on to accommodate our needs. His grading is based on your performance against your peers, so the lowest grade you can get is a B-. Would recommend

Very knowledgeable professor and a great sense of humor, however lectures were rarely focused on the topic. Everything I learned was outside of class with the textbook, slides, or TA's. Lots of extra credit opportunities. If you're willing to put in the work/already know mmbio go for it.

Took this course in the spring, and it started manageable, but it quickly ramps up with a midterm every other week. Pickett allows retakes up to 100 if you get above 70 the first time, which took a lot of pressure off for me. There are a decent amount of extra cred points, so take advantage of those. His spiritual thoughts are great as well!

Dr. Pickett is a really good guy. I loved how he would let you retake the exams if you got a 70% or over on the first one. I would warn against taking it in the spring if it is only two days a week. Too much information jammed into two 2 1/2 hour sessions a week. Also hard to go back and study because the slides had a lot of information gaps.

After seeing some of Pickett's previous reviews, I can say he has definitely changed. Tests were super straightforward, and he allowed retakes. He gives a ton of extra credit, and he's a super solid dude. Memorize his slides, and you'll be golden on every test. Take from him fs.

The closed note test thing kinda sucked, and I think the tests should've been revised because of that. But besides that, Dr. Pickett is honestly great. He explains things very simply and gives good application. He's super nice and down to earth. I TA test reviews were also really good, he basically gave the test questions. Use the TA's!!!

Attendance is not usually required, and there are several easy extra credit opportunities. Dr. Pickett is kind and understanding. Although exams are now closed note, the TAs and professor clearly explain what to study. Lectures can feel chaotic but are engaging, and he is very open to questions and re-explains concepts well. Amazing teacher

I can see why students struggled in his class but he is amazing. He lets you retake exams if you fail and has plenty of opportunities for extra credit, like PLENTY! The exam reviews from the TAs are pretty comprehensive as well. The workload is not super bad either. Kind of sad seeing his rating go super down when he doesn't deserve it at all

He's a nice guy, but his teaching style is too fast and smart to understand. I got my grade entirely off of my own studying and ChatGPT teaching me the concepts, not off his teaching. He does have tons of extra credit though. Focus on the starred learning objectives for the free response test questions.

I really love biology and I thought I would like this class. This is not supposed to be an easy class and I understand that. But this class was made way harder by taking it from Pickett. My friends in Poole's class have had a way better experience and have actually learned things. It is nice that he curves the grades at the end of the semester.

Honestly, if you need to take this class, don't take it from him. 

His lectures are hard to follow, the content is all jumbled up in his slides, and his expectations change throughout the semester. There was one class period he "addressed" some student complaints only to justify why he was right in the way that he was doing things.

The class is set up terribly. There needs to be recordings of the lectures. No one is paying attention and can learn as fast as he teaches. The content isn't super difficult to learn but there is no way to learn it. There aren't any videos or helps online and you can't learn the content needed for the exams just by looking at the slides.

I had a really hard time learning in his class. I wish he simplified some things. TA reviews are helpful. I think that this class could be improved in a lot of ways: how material is presented, how the class is structured, making the quizes worded like exams. I do like how he said he will curve the class so the highest person gets 100%.

The class is fair, it's a little harder than I would have thought. Sometimes I had a hard time knowing if he was joking or being serious. I wouldn't recommend this class but I also wouldn't advocate against this class. I think for me his teaching style was just diffrent. My friend really liked him as a teacher but his teaching style is different.

He's ok. I do understand why this class can be frustrating. I tried to email the TA's for help and I only got 1 response back. That was a little frustrating. I like Pickett he seems like a nice guy and the class forced me to make friends to study, which was nice. Again great guy a little frustrating of a course, had hard time with exam questions.

Honestly, I never paid attention in class, but I studied the TA reviews and the learning objectives sufficiently before exams, and the lowest grade I got was an 89.5%. The class is balanced out with other assignments too. Lectures are dense, but the material isn't hard. Pickett offers MC question retakes and extra credit; he is a fair professor.
The material was difficult, and he just blew through it. Study guides were released last minute, and exams determine your whole grade. It was so painful. But at least there was extra credit.

Dr. Pickett is a lovely professor. I understand the frustration of many of the recent ratings, but he is fair. He's also willing to work with students. The class is large, so it's often easier to go to office hours for specific questions. The concepts are new to me, but I've been able to learn them and enjoy the background info he gives on topics.
This course was so bad it makes me want to get on here and write 3 ratings about how bad it was. The professor, at heart, is a good guy. The course, at heart, is meant to drag you down.

If you do anything in this life, don't take this class. Man, this year was tough, no matter how much time you put into this class, it'll never be enough for an A. I didn't have any fun this year cause I was studying for this class. I can't tell you how much this class consumed me and made things impossible. Idk if ill ever recover from this class.

It was difficult to know what to expect on the tests; they were not difficult but there was a disconnect between the huge amount of content in lectures compared to the exams. There are retakes and lots of extra credit opportunities, so it is doable! Pickett is willing to help, but the TAs and their reviews are what saved me.

He gives so many opportunities to get extra credit points, as well as test retake. If you ask questions and come to class prepared you'll do fine. He's an awesome dude, and cares about his students. I think some of the other reviewers are just sour because you have to put extra effort into the class and learn the concept not just memorize.

I'm gonna be honest here, he's a chill guy but this class is worse than losing my first wife. This class is horrid, bro made the test closed note which is fine but the class is not set up for closed note exams. The TA's are not ballers like they should be. Do not take this class if you wanna be happy and get ragebaited by this class.

He is a great guy but my experience was that this class was made to be harder than it should have been. It was hard to identify what was important information from the slides and lectures, and how to apply it for the tests and quizzes. Really nice guy though and will work with you if you need it.

The class is poorly designed. Dr. Pickett is a nice person, but the class structure isn't designed for the success of his students. Between the way he lectures, the slides provided, and difficulty of the tests (and lack of study material to help) makes the class frustrating.

If I were to bump into Dr. Pickett on the street and talk to him, I'd think he's a great guy. Unfortunately, he's not a good professor. Lecture slides are full of overcomplicated diagrams. He attempts to help students understand with analogies, relating Batman to biology. Then the tests have nothing to do with Batman, but the overcomplicated slides

He provides LOTS of cool extra credit opportunities, sometimes they are spontaneous but it still works! He is very transparent on how/what we are graded on as well so nothing is ever a surprise. He also allows us to retake exams and keeps the highest score which has saved my butt this semester and also has helped me learn what I got wrong!

Students he had in the past pressured him to get rid of open note exams (because they apparently didn't learn anything from them. Kind of dumb ruining it for everyone else). He allows us to retake exams after reviewing what we got wrong, which is a reasonable alternative. He also loves his comic relief! These 1 star reviews are so irrelevant.

The tests were designed to be open note, so they are super difficult now that we can't use notes. His slides are often super messy, and filled with confusing diagrams that he quickly skips over. Taking this class is like drinking water from a firehose. He spends too much time in lecture trying to be funny and asking questions no one can answer.

This class was switched from an open note test to closed note this semester but he didn't change the tests so they are very hard. I never learned anything in his lectures, he's a terrible professor, and just takes more time to tell jokes and stories than actually to teach well. The slides are also a bunch of very confusing diagrams that dont help.

He is a really nice guy, but honestly I think he spends too much time joking and bantering with people and it is distracting to learning. He also goes through the slides really quickly and it's hard to understand. You'll have to spend a lot of time studying by yourself to understand this. Also, class is no longer open note, but he allows retakes.

Dr. Pickett is a very kind person. He loves his dad jokes to start off class. Overall, I think the class is missing something. Looking just over the slides is a little rough sometimes, and it doesn't always make sense. I think this class is slightly more difficult than it should be when compared to the other 240 classes, but I do think he is fair.

These students conspiring together to give him a bad review are putting no effort into this class. He is an amazing professor who provides a reasonable compromise for getting rid of open note exams. He allows us to retake a parallel version of the same exam, AFTER meeting with a TA about the questions we got wrong. That is reasonable.

All these people saying Dr. Pickett is a bad professor are probably just not committed to the class.  Dr. Pickett is a fantastic professor if you put in a good level of effort. It's not an easy class and was never meant to be, but Pickett helps a lot if you talk to him outside of class. His lectures are great too. Take this from Pickett.

He's not horrible. He's fair I like how he lets us take the exams twice. Helps to balance out the hard tests by knowing kinda more what he is wanting you to focus on after you take exam 1. Overall I think he is fair, but still not the best option imo
Not too bad. I'd appreciate more guidance on the tests but it's doable with a retake. Really good guy too.

I now have anxiety, this class and its tests constantly make me stressed. I never know what to study and I always get a poor grade. Tests feel inconsistent with the material taught in class. Despite putting in the effort, I leave the class feeling more confused. This course hasn't changed since he made the switch to closed-note tests.
this professor is bad. I studied a couple nights ago for a test for 7 straight hours - no joke- just got the worst test score I have ever gotten. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM PICKETT
Worst class I have ever taken
I've actually been able to get pretty good grades on the tests so far, but that is not due to his class. I love his jokes but I can see why it might distract from others learning.

I saw other people in my lab making a rate my professor so I guess I'll join with previous complaints. This class is just a flat-out failure. My academic advisor said this class should be easy with my huge workload this semester. She was wrong!

I'm kind of fed up with Professor Pickett. His class is honestly a joke. It's impossible to learn anything in his class. He is a super nice person, I'll give him that... But in terms of teaching, he may be the hardest professor I have ever had, and I have taken a ton chem classes, like ochem (I thought would have the hardest ). DO NOT TAKE!!!!

This is for sure one of the hardest bio classes I have ever taken...It's just because you never know what to expect on the exams- no study guide, slides are vague, and he constantly makes jokes that distract from learning. The only people who really do well in his class are the people who already know the material from another class.

BE WARNED: The high ratings are from when his tests were open note. This semester, all tests are closed note, but he is using the exact same exams as before. They are unfairly difficult and not designed to be taken from memory.
His lectures are a waste of time. Slides are a confusing word salad and he just makes jokes instead of teaching. AVOID!

He is a great lecturer! Exams are everything and they happen to be open note! I never studied for this class except for 3 hours before each test and did well. I highly recommend because he teaches the content well and has easy applications.
Wonderful and super smart guy. He's  clear on what will be on the exams and they're  open note. Sometimes it was difficult to understand the concepts but overall really liked the class.

This is your best shot at an A for mmBio 240. All midterms and final are open note (unlike other professors) and there is A LOT of content to cover. He has each lecture on a powerpoint available for you to open on the first day and all through the semester so you can skip class if something comes up. Also he is very caring and kind.

Dr. Pickett is friendly and does try to make his students laugh, but sometimes spends too long in lectures doing this instead of teaching the content. However, his exams are self-proctored, open note, and not very hard in general. Attend class and study for exams and you'll be fine.

The only reason people gave him good reviews is because his tests are open notes. I'm not sure how he was hired as a professor because he literally cannot teach. His way of teaching is asking us questions that no one knows the answer to other than the 10 people in the front row who answer them. He really is a nice guy but just sucks at teaching.

Dr. Pickett is great! He makes class fun and enjoyable. This class doesn't have any exams, so participation is important. It is focused on research, fixing phage annotations, and writing manuscripts. The work is pretty easy, and it gets you published which looks really good to professional schools. Great Class!!
Dr. Pickett is awesome! He's hilarious, and he makes lectures fun. His tests are difficult, but they are all open-note, which is really nice.

I took Dr. Pickett's class during COVID, and he was able to make lecture interesting and engaging. I felt like his exams were very doable and if you put honest effort in, you will succeed. I would consider him to be a very skilled caucasian. Take this class from him if you can.

Dr. Pickett is very knowledgeable and his class is set up for you to succeed. Exams are open-note, so just take good notes over the learning objectives for each lecture and you'll be good to go! Dr. Pickett gets easily distracted and tries to be funny, which was often frustrating to me and made it hard to focus. Attendance quizzes each class.

Recipe for success in this class is paying attention in lectures and understanding the big concepts he teaches. Tests are open note and stupid easy. I recommend taking the exams with a double monitor and using control F on all the slides. He also offers 2% or more extra credit that takes a few hours or so. Easy class to get an A in for sure.

Professor Pickett teaches very quickly and can get distracted. But, I thought he was hilarious. His tests were pretty easy. They were open note and you could use his powerpoints to find answers. Most of your grade depends on the tests, but there are lots of extra credit options. Only have to write one essay. I would definitely recommend him for 240

Dr. Pickett knows a lot about biology! He wants to create a fun environment in his classroom. There are daily participation quizzes, so get to class and try to pay attention. His lectures can be a tad bit confusing and boring, so you'll have to hit Khan Academy for some topics. Tests are open note just still study for them and you'll be fine.

Not too bad of a class. Pickett likes analogies, which can be helpful. All exams are open note (use the learning objectives!!) and quizzes at the end of every class, but they're easy if you're paying attention. He can get distracted telling unrelated jokes that sometimes take away your focus, but other than that a good option for 240.

the only reason you should take from him is that his tests are open note and most the answers are on the slides. other than that you don't really learn anything in class because he gets distracted by not funny jokes. i just didn't enjoy his teaching style and i noticed most of my classmates rolled their eyes a lot too.

Ugh. He tries so hard to be funny and never finishes a lecture because of it. Spends time on easy stuff and just breezes through the hard stuff. I had Johnson for the first week of the semester and I could already tell he was way better. Uses lecture slides, no textbook, canvas, attendance quizzes, stupid discussion boards each week for no reason.

Grades are very test based. That being said, exams are totally open note and based off the slides. If you have really good notes, and focus on his 'learning outcomes,' you'll ace every test. His tests aren't tricky, but there's a lot of material, so good note taking will save you. Highly recommend! He's a great teacher, and it's a fun class.

Dr. Pickett's tests are all based of the lecture slides, so you don't need the textbook for this class. All his tests are open note online and they are open for several days. He has attention quizzes every class so you do have to attend class, but he tries to be engaging and funny. He's nice, helpful, and available outside of class. Take from him!

Dr. Pickett was a funny guy, but sometimes I felt like his lectures weren't engaging or on topic. However, the exams were all open note/book, so they were not horrible. Difficult, but durable with the notes. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Overall, would recommend the class, I enjoyed it!
Dr. Pickett is a great teacher. MMBIO is hard but he does a good job of making it bearable. Lectures are good but I had trouble focusing sometimes- he did too. All in all, a good professor

The tests for this class are open note so complete memorization isn't required. No homework except a short term paper, though if I took this class again, I would look at the slides before class for stuff to sink in because I ended up cramming a bit for the exams. The lectures weren't too bad but sometimes hard to follow due to the material's depth.

Dr. P is a great option for 240. All the tests are open note, but they are tricky and timed. There are some essay/diagram questions that can be graded harshly depending on the TA. Overall, the material is super interesting and it is a fun class. I would recommend reading the slides before coming to the lecture. Quizzes every lecture.

Favorite professor at BYU so far
Open note tests
Closed note attention quizzes after each lecture 
One easy essay due towards the end of the semester
So many extra credit opportunities

Professor Pickett has been one of my favorite Professors at BYU. He makes it very clear what is expected of us and his tests are open note. Since the tests are open note attendence and annoating his power points is crutial. Overall, super nice, funny, and fair professor.

Great guy. He wants you to understand and succeed. He helps you learn and is willing to review any material. Lots of Dad jokes. Be ready for those. Tests are super fair and are open book/notes. Take 240 from him. It is worth it. Trust me on this one....

It felt like he really cared about us as students in our education and success. His exams were open note, but you have to know the slides pretty well to be able to find the info you're looking for. He makes mmbio fun.

Professor Pickett was awesome. Each class you have a post-lecture quiz but he never tried to trick us. Once a week there was a "pop quiz" but it was always at the beginning of class on Fridays. The exams were open note and open lecture slides, so sometimes they would be quite tricky. All of the information you'll ever need is in his slides.

This course isn't designed well by the department, but Professor Pickett does a decent job -- better than others I've heard of. He only covers things briefly, if you're able to understand the way things are explained the first time, you'll be okay. Tests are difficult so study with a group outside of class! No homework, which honestly makes it hard

I would have much preferred taking this class in the fall. Absolutely WAY too fast for spring term. So much material is covered in a short amount of time it's impossible to understand it all. He is such a nice funny professor though! Very approachable. Closed note quizzes at the end of class and open note tests. LOTS of extra credit opportunities.

Won't take much of your time. It'll just stress you out. 90% of your grade comes from open note tests and closed note quizzes. He just reads the slides and I walked out of class frustrated almost every day. Bc tests are open note, they're timed/hard so watch out. There is generous extra cred and the TAs revived my learning experience in this class.

The content of this class was not my jam. I was always so confused. I felt like Dr. Pickett wasted time and skipped over more difficult topics. The lecture goes fast and by the next day I had forgotten everything. Quizzes at the end of every class that were sometimes on topics barely discussed. Luckily, tests were open note which saved me.

I really enjoyed Dr. Pickett, he's really funny, he starts class off with dad jokes! However there were some students that took advantage of his fun side to kinda waste time in class. His tests are open note, open lecture slide; but it does allow some of the questions to be a little harder. He allows many options for extra credit (I didn't do them)

Tests are open note so I was just super comfortable with the slides and got high A's on all of them. Offers lots of extra credit and curves the class so I knew I was getting an A basically. Not super interesting lectures but that's really just the material. Super nice guy and super nice grader. Wouldn't get an A without his nice grading.

Just like the other ones say, the slides are the key to this class. I dont understand a lot of the material, but I'm doing fine. Dr pickett is a fun guy and he makes lecture exciting. I actually want to go to this class

He's a great guy, but he isn't the best at explaining difficult concepts. You don't need the textbook and he posts his slides on canvas. Each lecture has learning objectives for things you need to know for the test, but it's pretty much just all the info on the slides. There's a quiz at the end of every class and tests are open note, open slides.

Wasn’t a super difficult class, exams were all open note and you could copy and paste from the slides directly. Didn’t really understand the content and did well. Caveat is that the lectures are very boring and not interesting.

The class wasn't hard, but I honestly don't think I really learned anything. I would go to class confused, and then leave confused. He doesn't really explain anything, just reads off the PowerPoint slides. Exams are open note which was a life saver, I would get a B on them without understanding. Exams are over 65% of your grade so do well on those.

Everything you need to know for exams and quizzes is outlined really clearly in the Learning Objectives (tests were timed, but open-note). Go to class, fill out and review the Learning Objectives, take the quizzes, and you'll do fine. He's also super approachable, willing to answer any questions, and offers a decent amount of extra credit.

Dr Pickett is super understanding and really there to help students. Hes open to suggestions and really gives lots of opportunities to better your grade and prepare for tests. We were allowed to use notes for tests cause of corona so they were pretty easy but without notes they would have been really tough. Lots of material covered in short time!

I went to class a total of 5 times during the semester. The class was very easy because it covered much of the material I learned in CHEM 381, just less in depth. I would have liked to go to lecture more but was unfortunately not able. He was a good lecturer from what I saw though, and very kind and considerate.
Dr. Poole is great, he's really passionate about the subject which makes lectures interesting. Use the TA exam reviews and you'll do fine. Don't buy the textbook, you don't need it.

He's hilarious. The lectures are actually entertaining. Sometimes he's a little hard to follow though. He's tests are straight forward enough. The third one is definitely the hardest. But I would take his class again. Also his class is never actually 2 hours long.
Dr. Poole was great! He teaches clear and there's not much homework. He also gives lots of extra credit
Great teacher, I'd recommend finding a great study group. I personally didn't and didn't do super well in the class, but it's definitely possible.
Great Professor, very funny guy. I'd recommend a good study group for this class. I didn't have one and struggled a bit because of that, but I'd recommend this class to anyone.

Dr. Poole is the goat. His lectures are pretty entertaining. He is a funny and a kind of awkward guy. His tests aren't bad. The final was the easiest test of them all. He bases them off of the learning objectives so they are pretty easy to study for. He uploads videos of the lectures to Learning Suite. An A is very doable

I LOVED Dr. Poole. He made molecular biology engaging for me, he's super energetic and explains things so well, as well as records lectures. His tests aren't unpredictable, and homework is completion based. I would absolutely recommend Dr. Poole for anyone needing to take MMBIO 240.
Actually took him for Univ 101, best prof ever for that class. He's so kind and felt like he was really there for us, he made sure the workload was never too much/too annoying.

You don't have to go to lectures or read the textbook to do well in the class, but I recommend going to class because Professor Poole has the best lectures. You can tell he loves what he teaches about!

Dr. Poole is the best! This was one of my favorite classes by far, he made all of his lectures super engaging and easy to follow and explained difficult infection pathways clearly. He's very clear on what's on the final and what you're expected to know. He's also really funny. I wouldn't recommend skipping class because there's some vital stuff.

Dr. Poole is so epic. He is funny and entertaining. He has like no homework and all his slides have "Learning Objectives" and he only tests you on those. There is a super chill group project and that's pretty much it. Wish my Cell Bio class was like this.

Dr Poole is the only teacher you need to take for molecular biology. This is his bread and butter and he teaches it so well. Incredibly easy class because he covers the material so clearly. He's also absolutely hilarious. I heard so many nonchalant one-liners during the semester and his demonstrations are both entertaining and helpful.

This teacher is amazing. He offers literally every possible resource to help you succeed. He records every lecture so you can go back and watch it. He does completion homework to boost your grade. His tests are the nicest things ever and he offers literally so much extra credit. Your grade and learning is ENTIRELY up to you, which is awesome.

Dr. Poole is a funny guy who loves disease. It felt like MMBIO221 but easier. Two midterms and a final make up 60% of your grade, but he also gives some extra credit. One paper on a pathogen of your choosing, but overall, this class was very good, and I understand a lot more about disease.

He is so passionate about biology that makes you love his class. He gives time during lectures to ask questions and records them in case you miss them. Attendance is not required. He is easy to reach outside class during his office hours to go over content or answer questions, and offers extra credit. You should definitely take this class from him!

Super funny and passionate about biology. Pay attention to what he says in lectures and not just what's written on the slides, because he explains it better than the slides. Tests are straightforward and based on the learning objectives, so if you make sure you understand those, you'll be set. He provides a free pdf textbook but I never needed it.

Dr. Poole cares so much about his students. He tries his best to give everyone the best help possible and takes into consideration their personal circumstances. He's also very responsive when you have questions for him. My grade needed to be fixed, so I emailed him at 11pm and he responded within 6 minutes with the grade corrected.

Dr. Poole is awesome at explaining the concepts and his lectures are SO entertaining. He makes the learning objectives for each lecture clear and the test is based off them. The tests are most of your grade and you do need to study for them, but all the material is taught in class and nothing surprising. I can't recommend him enough!

Attend lectures and pay attention, you will do just fine in his class. He also has all of his lectures recorded, but it's better to come in person because if you have questions, he makes plenty of time for students to ask and clarify anything they don't understand. His tests are based on what he teaches and are acurate to what is discused in class.

Many students find Dr. Poole to be an engaging lecturer. He spends a large portion of class answering questions which can be annoying if you already understand the content/don't learn that way. Fortunately every lecture was recorded which was nice. All MC tests, not too bad, questions fairly based on objectives.

Professor Poole's lectures can be engaging, but the material is quite challenging. Rely on his sample tests and tools like Unstuck study alongside the textbook to succeed. Mandatory attendance helps, and the grading is reasonable if you put in the work.

Prof Poole is awesome. the material isn't always fun or entertaining but Poole has an amazing sense of humor that makes lectures enjoyable. there were 3 midterms and 3 papers and that was really all we got graded on. if you have to take 240, take it from Poole and no one else!

Pretty good class overall. A few "mini papers" that helped prepare for the exams, exams, and a group project. Daily quizzes to do before class that add up. Lectures were sometimes kind of confusing the first time through, but he usually records them for you to go back and watch. Reasonable amount of work. Know the practice exams inside and out.

Tests are worth a big portion of your grade but he gives you old tests from past years to study and basically uses the same questions. Didn't put in a ton of time and still managed an A. Take 240 from him!

Favorite professor at BYU. He cares about you understanding material & makes his lectures engaging. Never full 2 hours to go through material, doesn't feel rushed & allows as many questions as needed. Tests are very fair, he posts old tests up to review to prepare for upcoming tests. Extremely workable & will do whatever he can to help you succeed!

Dr. Poole was a really fun professor, but he was not super helpful outside of class. His tests are all reused from previous years, despite the textbook no longer being required. Questions were often confusing and about things that we never discussed in class. Really engaging and interesting lectures though!

Dr Poole is so unintentionally funny and it makes his lectures super engaging. The concepts are hard, but that's just how molecular biology is. No homework, but exams/papers are worth a ton of points. His learning objectives tell you what you need to know for the exam, and his sample exams follow pretty closely with the real exams so those help.

Dr. Poole is awesome. His test reviews are cool, cause he doesn't prep anything but can answer questions thrown at him. That being said, come prepared with questions! He takes the time DURING class to make sure everyone understands the concepts instead of rushing through like other teachers do. He has "mini papers" that are just regular papers.

Dr. Poole is a great professor. His tests go exactly with his slides and he wants students to succeed. Lectures can be hard to follow, but the general concepts are what he tests on. The class is VERY test-heavy but doable. Molecular biology is tough, but Poole made it enjoyable!

Dr. Poole is the MAN! 261 is straightforward. I hardly put any time in until it was time to take exams, and I headed into the final with a 100 (due in large part to the massive amount of extra credit he offers). The TA reviews were helpful and he provides practice exams for the midterms that helped a ton too. Super kind and an entertaining lecturer

Material was not hard at all, watching a few quick YouTube videos was enough to clear up any confusion I had. However, his lectures were often very confusing and very fast paced. LOTS of extra credit on exams, often curved up 4% on each one. Very, very caring guy but his lectures were just all over the place and hard to keep up with.

Super passionate and engaging during lectures! He makes it easy to succeed as long as you take notes and do good studying. 3 exams plus final, all in testing center multiple choice. 4 minipapers, one is a video. Records lectures to watch later. Has great practice tests!

Super chill class; no homework and no textbook or readings. You need to do well on the minipapers (there are 4) and exams (3) to do well in the class. He gives practice exams to study with that help a lot. There is a decent amount of memorization but you also have to be able to understand how the processes work to do well in the class.

Dr. Poole is really nice and you can tell that he puts in a lot of work to try and make his lectures engaging. However, his class is entirely lecture dependent, but his lectures are very confusing. His slides are reused so they don't make a lot of sense. Exams are heavily weighted. When studying for his exams, be prepared to teach yourself.

Dr. Poole is my most favorite professor I've ever had here at BYU. He is brilliant & hilarious and makes really challenging topics easy to learn. He uses a lot of demonstrations in class to teach challenging concepts. These concepts are taught mainly in the lectures and aren't on the slides so it's important to attend class. 10/10 would take again!
I am a senior at BYU. I took multiple of his classes. He was my favorite professor. If you have the opportunity to take him, do it! It is thanks to him that I learned how I studied. Great professor!

Prof Poole is such a fun professor and so intelligent! The class itself is pretty difficult though, which I didn't expect. Go to the TA help labs to study for the tests. Do well on the essays because it will help pad your grade. Don't make my mistake and think you can get away with studying just definitions of stuff, know the processes too.

Best and easiest class I've taken at BYU. Dr. Poole and Dr. Lane Fischer co-teach it (Poole teaches about different genetic disorders, Fischer teaches counseling skills). It's a fascinating class and the counseling skills are super helpful even if you don't become a genetic counselor. Absolute 15/10 class. I will recommend it to literally everyone

One of my favorite professors of all time. I've taken both molecular bio and infections&immunity from him and he is by far the best option for both. He's a very simple teacher, just know the slides and youre good! Also, im not one to care for teachers being funny but the dude has the driest humor and its hilarious. I tell all my friends to take him

Take this class from Dr. Poole. He is super funny and so knowledgeable. If you go to class, take good notes, and study well for the tests you'll do great. The tests are worth a lot of credit, but with little homework, there is a lot of room to study.  The textbook isn't needed.

I rented the textbook, and never read it. It may be useful if it's challenging for you. His exams are based on the objectives covered in lecture. He is super engaging and makes protein synthesis interesting and fun (a hard task). The minipapers are challenging to write but great tools for studying. I recommend studying the practice test/optional hw

I loved Professor Poole's class! It was so much fun and made me love learning about diseases! He teaches very clearly and his textbook is very easy to read. Homework is just reading a short textbook chapter and then doing an open-note quiz for each class. Super easy. His tests weren't too bad either, just require a lot of memorization.

The textbook is mandatory for quizzes and will provide lots of details necessary for the tests. He is an amazing instructor who makes lectures both entertaining and educational. This is my favorite class that I have taken at BYU.
He knows how to make learning about viruses fun. It's pretty straight forward, all exam questions will be on the slides and TA reviews were a big help. Really not to bad if you study.
Loved Doctor Poole. His tests require a good handle on the topics but they aren't too bad, very fair to what was taught in lectures. Review his practice tests before class and use the TAs!

Taught memorization and then tested on application. No study guide or clear testing guidelines or expectations.

Very smart man though.

The best professor for MMBIO 240. There are some really hard concepts but he taught things clearly! His key objectives/optional h.w. were a little disorganized, but one TA saved us with his test reviews. Tests cover a bit and are 75% of your grade so study in advance. Don't put off the mini papers and study the midterms before taking the final.

Dr. Poole is awesome! I loved lecture every week. He loves what he teaches and makes lecture interactive and hilarious. Tests are completely based off his lectures, which is nice because you don't have to read the textbook, but you must go to class. Your grade is based completely off of tests and minipapers. Use the practice tests to study!

While attendance wasn't required, all of the exam material comes from the lecture learning objectives. If you come to class and take good notes and study based on the learning objectives you will do well in the course. He doesn't use or require the textbook. But most importantly, he is such a fun and caring professor. He loves the stuff he teaches.

Really wants students to do well, very approachable, good test prep materials. Teaches difficult concepts well, and very interactive in class. Super good at answering questions and keeping students engaged. GO TO CLASS because he expounds on the limited info on his slides.

Dr. Poole is hilarious and explains everything really well. Sometimes it's hard to understand his slides because they're pretty sporadic but I got away with not studying until 1-2 days before the tests and they were all fairly easy A's. Pray that you have a good ta and memorize their test reviews, and you'll easily get an A.
This was an easy A as long as you read the learning objectives and follow along in the class. I enjoyed the class and Dr. Poole is such a gifted teacher!
Learned a lot about immunology and virology. Dr. Poole was very chill and its an easy A if you put in the work

Take this class from Dr. Poole! His tests are incredibly straightforward and literally come straight from the slides. His lectures are entertaining and informative. He takes a ton of questions that are kind of off-topic, so it can feel like he is wasting time. But that is the only downside. The class is easy but teaches everything you need to know.

Don't even hesitate if you have the chance to take his class. He's super funny, super understanding, and super knowledgeable. He explains things super well and answers all the questions people have. Very reasonable tests. The class isn't easy, but an A is totally doable. Just do the homework assignments, come to class, and study for exams.

Dr. Poole is phenomenal. Breaks down complex ideas and concepts and makes them understandable for any level of understanding. Would highly recommend him as he has been very accomodating with COVID and thorough.

Doctor Poole knows his subject really well but I feel he doesn't deliver it well. He posts his slides, but there isn't very much information on them so you can't really find answers to questions on them. He didn't give a lot of context on topics that we covered. He would just jump into a complicated process without explaining what we are learning.

Dr. Poole was a good professor for MMBIO 240. I had no idea what was going on the entire semester and I still passed. He changed his exams this past semester to be open book, note, internet, etc. Participation is not mandatory and the book is not needed at all. A few mini papers which aren't bad and surprisingly a decent amount of extra credit.
Dr. Poole was so FUNNY! His class would soar by so quickly! The tests were pretty simple and for us it was open notes. I never had to worry about my grade in this class and every lecture was a JOY!

Dr. Poole is a solid choice, his lectures are amazing and he is a very caring person. This class has a lot of material and the grading is heavily dependent on the tests, but there is no busy work or stupid assignments, you just have to study and understand the material and you will be fine! Dr. Poole is a great choice for MMBIO 240!!

Dr. Pool was great. He always spent time answering students' questions. This class was about 75% exams, 16% essays, and the rest were easy pre-class quizzes. If you aren't a strong test taker or writer, this class may not be for you. Tests are open-note, but they are semi-difficult. You have to work for your grade. Lots of extra credit.

The whole class was kind of meh. Super dry humor, but made class more interesting. He switched the exams halfway through the semester, which I felt made a disconnect between his lesson plans and content on the exams. But overall not a hard class to deal with. Don't bother going to lectures, all exams are open notes. Heavy weighted though

I can't say this enough times, but Dr. Poole is the BEST. He really cares that his students understand hard concepts, and has thought of cool ways to break them down/explain them. He is more than willing to answer questions in and outside of class and never makes you feel stupid for asking. He loves his job and his field, and will help you love bio
