He likes the class to be discussion-based, which is great until there are specific students who like to ask a question every 5 minutes. Felt like we didn't finish the material for the day very often. He is great though, very knowledgeable and passionate. HW due after every class period, usually took me about 10-15 mins. Tests are not too bad.

Professor Poole was the best! He was super funny and taught really well. I understood the concepts and I didn't even have to read the textbook! He was super chill and cared about our learning more than assignments. Most of the assignments were to help us better understand material. He was one of the best teachers I've had and super easy.

Dr. Poole is very amazing and his lectures are very interesting. He does let anyone ask questions so some people may not like all the questions but just be respectful. You must study for this class, ask the TAs for help on confusing topics. Get a good study group and you should be great.

I can't say enough about Dr. Poole; he is an absolutely fabulous teacher. He is hilarious, straightforward, and very lecture-dependent. Know what's on his slides and what he says during class and you'll be fine. He hardly ever even references the textbook.

Dr. Poole is an amazing professor! He is what got me hooked on molecular biology. I can understand the subject and type of learning required may not be everyone's cup of tea, but Dr. Poole make it way easier with dad jokes, demonstrations, and straightforward multiple choice tests. He clearly knows a lot and cares about his students.
Dr Poole is my favorite professor. Hes a great teacher and is passionate about it. This class isnt too hard if you study well and go to lectures, you dont need the textbook at all.

Take this class from Dr. Poole! He is hilarious, and his tests are based on what is on his slides. Make sure to go to the TAs to get your minipapers checked before you turn them in, because they can be tricky. There is an extra credit paper at the end of the semester which can make up missed points and boost your grade up to 4%.

Fantastic teacher that actually makes learning enjoyable. I would take all of my course from him if I could. Your grade is pretty much just the tests, but that's fine as long as you pay attention in class. You definitely will need to study, but Dr. Poole makes it worth it.

Dr. Poole has engaging lectures. The tests are challenging but not impossibly hard if you study and go to TA reviews and such. My only complaint is that in mmbio 261 the TA's don't have office hours to go over hw before submitting and dr. poole's demeanor when you visit him in his office with questions can make you feel like you're asking dumb Q's.

Dr. Poole was a great Professor for this class. 3 tests and a final that are pretty straightforward. He wont try and trick you and make them difficult. Homework is optional. 3 mini papers that you basically get most of the points for if you just get it done. His lectures are funny and very helpful in simplifying things.

Dr. Poole is an entertaining professor who loves what he does. He is great at answering questions and a well-rounded professor. His TA's are extremely unmotivated, but I would recommend this class to anyone who loved biology.

Dr. Poole is the best, and is the funniest biology professor I have had. He genuinely cares about his students and makes molecular biology easy to understand. If you have the chance definitely take it from Poole. His tests are straightforward and he provides past tests to help study from.

Dr. Poole likes to involve his students in learning and makes the material pretty easy to understand. Tests weren't bad, but ask him to post an old test to help you study, that's the best study guide. He has an online book that has homework questions. He wrote most of the book so it matches lecture and is very helpful.

Professor Poole is an amazing professor! He really loves what he teaches and does a lot of really funny demonstrations to help the class understand difficult concepts. The textbook is not required, you know everything you need for the test by attending lectures. There are only 3 tests, 3 papers, and the final and that's your grade.

Prof. Poole is one of the most amazing professors at BYU. His lectures make even the hardest subjects easy to understand. He cares about his students, answers questions clearly in class, and is absolutely hilarious. He made this class enjoyable, helped me love the subject, and helped me learn a lot. He is also very accessible outside of class.

He is a fantastic teacher. He goes the extra mile to teach concepts in class in really easy ways. Whenever other bio teachers subbed in for him nothing made sense, but he was great. A lot of memorization for tests but they're not hard. He let the class do an extra credit paper when people did poorly on one of the tests. He cares about his students.

Dr. Poole made me love molecular. He never writes on the board but gives you his slides- personally that worked for me. Lets you ask ALL questions in class. He is HILARIOUS. Has 4 tests and a few research papers.

It's pretty clear what's expected of you. There are online homeworks on the reading every week (I went to the TA lab for most of them), three midterms, and three mini papers. He even lets you retake a midterm. This class was difficult for me, but if you put in the work it's very doable.

Dr Poole is so funny! His tests aren't too hard and he makes molecular biology entertaining (which is not an easy task). He has the most forgiving grading scheme on the planet (you can retake 1 midterm). You will have to write 3 short papers, but they help you study if you do it right. He's great, I loved his class, even though biology is the worst

NOT an easy A class! graded on HW assignments, a research paper, 2 exams and a final. 1 extra credit paper. Average on midterms was a mid C for both. 25% of class dropped after first exam. Hard to study for exams. Only study material is his class slides which are very vague; topic bullet points which he then talks about. Need to take notes!!

Dr. Poole is a good guy that loves the subject but the class is not super organized. The exams were fair but the homeworks were really challenging at the beginning of the semester. He made changes through the semester but it was still not my favorite class.

I LOVE Dr. Poole. I am passionate about this topic, and having a professor who is passionate and has a great command of the class was great! He makes great visuals in class. I recommend printing out his slides and using them to make additional notes so you can write down his visuals and other helpful things. Very straight forward testing & grading.

I didn't really care for this class. He's super funny and sometimes his let's are really funny and participation heavy wish is nice, but I found myself heavily relying on the TA review. There's also 3 mini papers you'll have to write. They aren't so mini.

FUNNY. A great lecturer w/fun demonstrations. Grade is mostly about tests, but know the learning objectives well & you'll be fine. 3 tests+final, 3 mini papers, online HW due before class(read the textbook for these. otherwise you'll fail them). Take good notes about things NOT on slides, & see TAs/him for any clarification. TAKE IT FROM HIM!

Dr. Poole is really funny, but they way he ran his class it was near impossible for me to succeed. The readings and lectures cover hundreds of different concepts, but the exam will focus on a tiny fraction of those concepts that are super detailed. So the only way to pass is to know everything and more. Almost entire grade based on exam scores.

Dr. Poole knows what he is talking about and presents the material in an engaging way. For the Honors 220 class that he teaches he had a great chemistry with Dr. Cutchins. Sometimes the grading was a bit unclear and usually it took a while for them to grade tests and papers. Makes you think and exposes you to a lot of diverse opinions.

He's the best teacher and if you don't take MMBIO 240 from him you are doing it wrong!! Gave very entertaining lectures and was super personable. He knows what he's talking about and really good at helping his class to understand. As long as you memorize everything on his powerpoints and his lectures, you'll ace the class.
Dr. Poole is great! He is a really good teacher. Make sure you ask questions in class when you don't understand something. His TAs are kind of useless unfortunately.

Dr. Poole is an amazing professor who obviously knows his stuff. MMBIO 261 is all memorization and if you pay attention in class and memorize his Powerpoint slides, you will do fine. He is funny and engaging and tries his best to make the material interesting.

Dr. Poole is awesome! He is one of my favorite professors at BYU. His tests can be difficult but he gives you extra credit and a chance to redo one of his midterms, so it is very possible to get an A in his class. He is also hilarious. Make sure to go to lectures. Most test questions come from his lectures and his P.P.s can be hard to follow.

Dr. Poole is an amazing teacher. He simplifies difficult concepts and relates material together. Gives great rants about vitamin C, essential oils, and vaccination. Loves his subject which makes the material easier to learn. Daily readings, a few essays. Everything was straightforward. Great class with great professors. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

Dr. Poole is hilarious. I laughed a lot. His powerpoint slides were basically just topics he wanted to teach us about and a list of exactly what he was going to ask on the test, so I would recommend looking at those, and going to class to listen to the answers. I never used the textbook, taking notes in class was sufficient.

I seriously love Dr. Poole. He is the absolute best. His classes are easy if you go to class and study. I enjoyed 240 more than 261, but that is just personal preference. He is super caring and funny. He doesn't quite appreciate the greatness of the Prequels, but loves Star Wars, and that makes him cool. Everyone needs to take one class from him.

Dr. Poole really changed my perspective about Biology. Hands down to the best Professor ever! Three midterms and a final. Also, a paper due the end of the semester. Take this class from him. You won't regret.

Great guy! He is very down to earth and willing to help students succeed if they put in the effort. Class is difficult and the material can be confusing, but he is willing to work with the students for the grade they deserve.

Dr. Poole is the best! My grade went up 5% just from his extra credit. Don't get the textbook, you'll be tested off of specific material from the slides and problems he does in class. Attendance is essential. The TAs gave helpful reviews and that's where I learned most of the info that was on the exams. I wouldn't take this class from anyone else.

This class was team taught by Dr. Poole and Dr. Cutchins (from the English department). He's brilliant and has a great sense of humor. Being a general education class, he kept the biology portion at a pretty basic level, but it was very interesting and tied into the humanities portion surprisingly well. I really enjoyed his class.
The book didn't help much, but the tests were mostly lecture based. Go to class and you'll be fine, just don't forget to submit the homework.

Dr. Poole is the best! He is very straight forward on his tests and tells you exactly what you need to study. You DON'T need to buy the text book, everything you need will be on his slides. He gives lots of opportunities for extra credit. Hands down the best 240 teacher!!

Dr. Poole is the best, take any class you can from him. I found him very funny, he has a nerdy/dry sense of humor. Straightforward class with 2 midterms, final, weekly homeworks, and a paper that is graded very leniently. Definitely need to study for his tests but there are no surprises, just put in the time.

Poole's great. HILARIOUS guy too. Not an easy A but if you put in the studying you can definitely get one. Don't buy the textbook. Tests (4) are based on his slides. Would make a point of going to class and taking notes. Slides are vague. Does give out like 4% points worth of extra credit. One easy paper. Homework easily graded. Highly recommend!

Dr. Poole is my favorite MMBio professor of all time!!!!! Seriously take at least one class from him. 261 was an amazing class, and even though I had to take a not ideal time for MMbio 240, I would never have taken 240 from anyone else. He makes it so interesting, and his easy to follow PowerPoints keep it clear. Not to mention he is HILARIOUS!

Dr. Poole was AWESOME!! Seriously one of my favorite biology teachers that I have taken so far! He is very fair with grading and genuinely cares that his students are learning! He always answers everyone's questions in class! Super nice guy that loves what he does! If you are going to take MMBIO 240, take it from HIM!!

Dr. Poole is a good teacher if you are ready to hit the ground running to learn mmbio. There is no required textbook for the class so it's hard to learn and you are expected to know a lot before class. If you are willing to put in the work to learn, he's great, otherwise, if you don't know anything like me, you will struggle.

Dr. Poole is easily the best professor I've had so far at BYU. He's very engaging, he has hilarious demonstrations, and he always answers every question. Literally the best. Word of warning though: most of his TA's don't like to answer your questions, explain things to you, or interact with you in any way. Just talk to Dr. P if you need anything

Taking Poole's 240 class actually was the reason I switched my major to Microbiology. Tests and homework was very reasonable. He is a funny and very intelligent man. Some of the things he taught were difficult concepts and he taught them with ease and simplicity. I liked forward to every lecture. Would take again and again!

I LOVED Dr. Poole. Don't get the textbookjust follow along on the slideshow and write down anything he says that isn't on the slides. Requires a fair bit of study and memorization, but that's just 240 for ya. Solid extra credit options. He's also hilarious. Definitely the best choice for this class.

Dr. Poole is probably one of the best professors a BYU. Take any class you can from him. His grading criteria is clear. The class is very interesting and he answers almost all questions. Tests are based off of the slides, but content clarification comes form lectures. Make sure you take good notes. The final is the easiest of the tests. Ex credit.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He is hilarious, makes class interesting, and I've literally never seen him skip anyone's question. He answers all questions that the class asks. He explains things well. Don't buy the textbook.

Easy weekly quizzes due before class. 3 tests and a final. Final is comprehensive, but by far the easiest. Tests focus on small details in the slides. MEMORIZE THE SLIDES. One paper due near the end-- long but fairly easy. Funny, dry guy. Great at giving examples.

MMBIO isn't a super interesting class but professor poole tries to make it better. Unlike most science teachers he isn't trying to fail you or make you life hard. I feel like I got the same grade on every test no matter how much I studied so I wasn't sure what change.. In the end though he really is on your side and you will do alright in the class

Dr. Poole was great! My only thing against the class was that the third midterm was crazy hard in comparison to the first two. This was annoying because you think you know how to study for his test, then all of a sudden you have a randomly crazy hard test. That said, Each midterm progressively gets trickier. However, the final was not bad at all.

Dr. Poole is one of the best microbiology teachers on campus. Very funny guy.  He is very straightforward about what is on tests, so in that sense its not difficult. He responds quickly to emails if you have questions.  I wouldn't buy the textbook. I will take him again.

By far one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He is so intelligent and teaches difficult concepts so well, often with visual and object demonstrations. Tests are straight forward and he really has the student's best interest in mind. Take MMBIO from him if you can, you won't regret it. I, myself, will be looking for other classes he teaches.

Dr. Poole is by far the best professor to take mmbio240 from. His tests are straightforward, and he gives you a detailed list of what to study for each chapter. He does a great job of trying to keep things interesting. Sets aside a lot of time for questions and additional discussion as well, and can answer just about any question you throw at him.
Dr. Poole is a fun teacher to take. His tests are all based off of his lectures and powerpoint so don't buy the textbook.

Dr. Poole is fantastic. He is a great lecturer and really cares about his students. He wants you to know the material and succeed and is willing to adapt. His tests come from his lecture slides, so know those and you're set.

Dr. Poole is a great choice for this class. Here's what you can expect: - Homework (5 questions) twice a week - 2 midterms and a final - 1 simple paper You likely won't use the textbook. He tests you on his slides AND the things he says during lecture, so you have to pay attention. Download his slides before, follow along and write extra info down.

I didn't really need the textbook because he teaches everything in class.  With that being said, I took him for both mmbio 240 and mmbio 261. You want to pay attention in class because some things you won't find on the slides despite him saying everything comes from the slides. Not a hard class, just listen and he offers extra credit.  TAKE HIM
This guy is awesome.  He is a good teacher, and only tests you on what he teaches you.  If you are willing to study, getting an A shouldn't be a problem!

Dr. Poole is just great. He understands what he is teaching and can explain it in a clear, simple manner. However, he spits out a lot of information in one lecture, so pay attention and record the lectures. I would definitely take his class again.

Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll want to go anyway. Super amazing and often hilarious classes. I loved 240 and 261 from him. I think everyone should take them both. Such a knowledgeable, funny guy. It's easy to be engaged and excited about the material. I feel like now I'm done with his classes I'm done with the best the college has to offer!

Dr. Poole teaches very clearly and is very willing to answer questions in lecture. He seems to prefer questions. He enjoys teaching the subject. The material does get pretty detailed so be prepared. You will definitely want to do the homework, both for the grade and how much the questions reflect the tests.

You cannot possibly go wrong with Dr. Poole. He teaches you everything you need to know and nothing else. The exams are extremely fair and rarely have any curve balls. The final exam is also extremely easy. Clear expectations, hilarious, and very informative. Take MmBio 240 from him!!! You won't even open the textbook, just buy the online code!
Dr. Poole is the man. I'd take all my bio classes from him if possible, because 1) he explains things so well and 2) he sounds like Patrick from Spongebob. Enough said.

Only teaches this class winter semester. Offers extra credit on each test. He makes MMBio interesting and spices up lectures with humor. I don't like biology at all but I liked this class. If you know the slides and go to a TA review the tests will not be hard. Definitely the best MMBio teacher at BYU.

I took MMBIO 240 previously at BYU, and the structure of the class was so inconsistent and the homework system so flawed that it made the class impossible. I retook the class years later from Poole. Night and day different. His lectures are engaging, his grading is clear and fair, and he offers help where he can. certainly a good choice.

Dr. Poole has really fun lectures and makes them interesting and hilarious. He really makes you love viruses and bacteria more than you should. However, it is a hard class and you need to put in effort, not because Dr. Poole is a hard teacher, but just because of the nature of the class.

The Powerpoints are no joke. If you know them and the homework questions you will get an A.  There is one paper but it isn't bad. The class material is really dry so he tries to spice it up. Best/easiest MMBIO 240 at BYU

Dr. Poole is one of my top 3 professors I've taken a class from. He's super smart but doesn't treat you condescendingly. He's funny and makes lectures interesting. If class is slow it's because people are asking questions for the sake of asking a question. Dr. Poole gives reasonable work and his tests are fair.

Dr. Poole is a genuinely funny man. He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter, and his TA's actually know what they're talking about, for the most part. The objectives do a great job of setting the expectations for the lectures and tests, and the content of the class was very interesting.
He is an awesome professor. He makes a hard concept simple. I recommend anyone to take molecular biology from him.

Dr. Poole is the best professor! Just go to class and take notes... do the homework (it's not hard) and study for the tests and you'll get an easy A. The final is super easy as are all of the other tests. He's hilarious and sooo easy to listen to.

Honestly I feel like Dr Poole would be a better high school professor. In my opinion he doesn't respect our time in class. People seem to like his jokes, but they lower his credibility in my opinion. The homework is pretty simple and the tests seem okay.

Dr. Poole is the man.  Totally fair, teaches you what is necessary, tells you what you don't need to know.  Review the slides, take good notes of what he says in class. KNOW the homework before the test and you are golden. Dr. Poole is great!
Some tests are manageable, but others are so over-the-top hard that there is no real way of knowing what you will be tested on. The TAs almost never gave reviews, so you're on your own.

I was scared of this class but it is actually super manageable. If you listen and take notes in class on the stuff that he says that's NOT on the slides, and then later combine that with the slides into the objectives, you're golden for exams. Dr. Poole also comes up with a lot of demonstrations that help explain and reinforce difficult concepts.

Dr. Poole is very dry and a little boring, but his class is really interesting and the tests arent very hard. He has objectives after each lecture that he makes the tests out of. So if you understand on the objectives the you will do  just fine on the tests. I would recommend his class to anyone.

Dr. Poole is amazing! He is super funny and makes learning the material so much fun, yes, fun! He is a pretty easy grader, but you will have to work for your grade. Test have everything to do with what you learned in class, not tricks, just learn the material!

This professor is hilarious! His class is manageable as well. There is not too much material to cover, so he takes the time to really discuss the "ins and outs" of molecular biology. Based on discussions that I had with students that took different professors for MMBIO240, I learned that Brian Poole is by far the funniest, easiest, and best around
Wonderful teacher; VERY easy grader. However, due to certain issues he freaks out over tiny things, like reminding him about an error in the gradebook.
Dr. Poole is the best teacher for MmBio 240. He makes it interesting and teaches it very clearly and the test is a good representation of material covered.

Dr. Poole is just the best! His exams are totally reasonable. It's just like everyone else is saying-study the slides and objectives and pay attention to the little things he says in lecture, study hard, and you'll do great! Very straightforward. :) He is very helpful if you have questions. Keeps class entertaining and teaches things well!

Loved this class, informative and great! Study the slides and understand any concept he talks about in class. I never bought a book, but you will need to get ahold of one just to do the quizes. He's funny in a dry humor sort of way but a relaxed and nice professor. Study hard for all the exams and you will be fine!

Dr. Poole is awesome. He is a little quirky, but kept class entertaining and his tests were very reasonable, you knew exactly what to expect. As some advice, don't buy the textbook. Just use one at the Life Science learning center to do the quizzes and save yourself over 100 bucks. Oh ya, and lots of extra credit! Take Dr. Poole!!

He has a dry sense of humor and is a very likable guy. The book was way too detailed to be worth the time. Tests weren't too bad--the final was not cumulative! I just watched youtube during the student presentations. You basically just need to read the abstracts of those papers before the tests. I slept through my own group's presentation.

Take MMBIO 240 from him! He explains difficult concepts in a way that is easy to understand. He keeps class interesting with his nerdy but funny personality. He is also REALLY easy to work with. Don't be afraid to talk to him for any reason. Awesome teacher.

Dr. Poole is great.  He did his best to make learning the info as easy as possible.  The tests were very fair.  He teaches very clearly and his lectures are entertaining.  I'm way glad I took MMbio from Poole.  Highly recommended.

Dr. Poole is literally the best. He is one of the most approachable teachers you have ever met. He was more than willing to help and answer all questions, take personal time to talk with students, and is just a stand up guy in general. The tests were tough, you had to study hard, but he gives you all the information you need. Enjoyable lectures.

Dr. Poole is one of the best professors at BYU. He is very intelligent and very funny.  His class is very do-able and he makes sure the class understands concepts before he moves on.  Lots of demonstrations. Hard exams but straightforward, just need to study hard.  He genuinely cares about his students.
Great professor!  His explanations make perfect sense and his tests are straight forward.

Dr Poole is the best choice for MMBio240. He is a great guy that is excellent at explaining difficult topics and he gives you absolutely everything you need to ace the test. If you fill out the objectives, and attend reviews, he tells you absolutely everything you need to know for tests and doesn't try to trick you at all. He wants you to do well.

Great professor! Has a sense of dry humor that he slips here and there to make things interesting. Filling out the objective sheets are critical - if you know what's on them, you should do fine on the test. Also has demonstrations that really help with understanding the concepts. Always wants the class to do well.

Dr. Poole (aka Chance Daily) is awesome.  His tests are pretty hard, but he really wants the class to do well.  Also he is hilarious.  If you focus on learning the objectives that he posts every week, you'll do fine.

He's dry as the desert, but still cracks jokes related to the subject matter. I tutor students from his MMBio 240 classes. There are plenty of resources for you. I love Dr. Poole & his classes! He is a great teacher & a great man.

Dr. Poole is rad, I liked class progressively more each time I came. Expect quizzes every mon/wed. Tests are really clear if you know how to set up an experiment. Ask questions about things you find interesting that are somewhat relative to the topic, he loves it when the class actively participates. and he brings in object lessons regularly.

Class was pretty difficult.  He does post slides before class.  I suggest printing those off and writing notes on them during lecture.  Test could be a little ridiculous.  Yes, he compensates grades depending on how the class did, but it just gets frustrating studying for them.  Dr. Poole is a nice guy, but his class is harder than it has to be.

Great professor! First time teaching the class, did a great job. First test was easy, the second one was hard, but gave everyone 15 points(yes 15)to makeup for it. He is quite nerdy, but loves the subject. His voice can get dull, but you get used to it. Tests are 15 MC and written (short ans,essay) Homework is 5ish questions from reading, open book

Professor Boyer is great. He is kind and wants all of his students to suceed. He is genuine and knows what he is talking about. You know exactly what to expect on exams and quizzes. Straight forward class if you put in the work.

Excellent professor. This Boyer module of this course is very math-heavy, but I felt like it clarified a lot of things about asset pricing theory. He has a way of explaining things very clearly through the mathematics. This class is a must if you want to get a PhD in finance. Dr. Boyer will blow your mind.

Prof Boyer is a very genuine guy, and a great teacher. This class can sometimes feel mundane and repetitive, but the tests are fair and based off the homework and assignments done. Definitely a challenging course, and an understanding of statistics is necessary.

FIN 410 isn't an easy class but I really liked professor Boyer. I feel like his tests and quizzes are fair and that the homework represents what I was tested on. Boyer was definitely one of the most caring professors I've had at BYU, which is saying something.

Dr. Boyer is an excellent fit for this course. He cares about the students in his classroom. He's patient, willing to answer all questions, and goes at a pace that everyone can follow. His exams are the most straightforward that I've seen so far, out of the junior core curriculum. The TA's are helpful too.

FIN 410 is like learning Mandarin Chinese for most students the first time around. I know it was for me, but once the material started to click I really enjoyed this class. Regardless of the subject material, you can't not love Dr. Boyer. One of the most humble, compassionate and genuine people I have ever known.

An excellent man and teacher. Not always the most riveting lectures but always willing to do what it takes to make complex material clear. Among the best professors I've had. Don't bother buying the large text book but his course notes are vital.

In all of Professor Boyers interactions he was kind. His class is statistics heavy. He simulates the real world as much as possible using real data, having you solve homework and test problems using excel. His class has 3 test, in-class quizzes, homework, and 2 trading assignments. There are no surprises on his test. I highly recommend taking him!

Professor Boyer is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. Apart from being incredibly intelligent, he is incredibly kind. You know from the way he teaches and interacts with students that he also is a great father and husband. Having Dr. Boyer as a professor is an inspiration and a breathe of fresh air. I would highly recommend taking him!

Professor Boyer is one of the smartest people you will come across when it comes to Finance. He really cares about his students and will take time to help you one on one. The way he teaches 410, however, is difficult to most. Most students don't think the way he does, which makes this class from Boyer more difficult. Tests are tough.

Boyer is the man. Take investments from him. He is really easy to go and talk with and is more than willing to help out. The tests are very straightforward. Just do the practice problems and you'll do well. Highly recommend this professor.

Boyer was my favorite professor in the finance jr. core. Take 410 from him if you can! At first I thought he would be boring and not helpful, little did I know. He teaches 410 in the best way ever. Do all homework and you will be prepared for the test. He is an amazing professor and person as well. So much respect for this man.

Professor Boyer is a great person. He knew everyone's name the second week of class and is recognized nationwide for his expertise in financial securities. Although I loved him as a person, I absolutely hated him as a professor. There were some class periods where I seriously couldn't tell if he was teaching us or  just talking to the whiteboard.
He does a great job of teaching an extremely difficult class. It's hard to follow the material, but he always tries his hardest to help you understand. Tough class but he's a great guy and way smart.
GREAT GUY,  CAN BE BORING AT TIMES BUT VERY INTERESTING AND SO WILLING TO HELP ANYONE THAT ASKS FOR IT

He's a hard professor to pay attention to. He reads from the powerpoints and works example problems. It would be a lot more helpful if he let the students try to work the problem and then walked us through it. He's a nice guy and is available if you need help, but his lectures aren't very engaging. Overall it was a fair course though.
Nice guy, poor teacher. His lectures are boring and he rarely looks up from his powerpoint slides. He fails to provide real world examples and does not interact well with his students.

This is a really interesting class, and Boyer is a really great guy and very knowledgeable. Unfortunately he doesn't convey that knowledge very well to the students.  He just goes off PPT slides for an hour and a half each class period.
His tests are easy bc they're all numbers.

This class was pretty killer as far as material is concerned. However, I feel like Boyer is one of the most organized and knowledgeable professors I have had. He made himself available for students at all times. He helps us understand the intuition of all problems. I recommend him highly. TA labs are a must for the homework (unless you're a genius)

Dr. Boyer's class is hard but manageable if you stay on top of it. His tests are fair and very similar to his practice tests. He doesn't try and trick you, but will test your knowledge and skill. The required text book is useless, don't waste your money. If you take time to do all the really long homework you'll do fine.

By far he is my favorite professor. His class is challenging be nature, but he is so willing to work with you. You just need to reach out to him. I really enjoyed every class I attended. He is still young, but I would say he is a rising star in Marriott School. I think he is  the best.
Professor Boyer is awesome. He's a young, really cool guy. His jokes in class seriously had me laughing every day.

Dr. Boyer is an excellent teacher.  The material is challenging at times, but he has a sincere desire to make sure everyone knows what is going on.  The practice tests were EXTREMELY helpful as review for the real tests.  Dr. Boyer does a great job with this class, and I would definitely recommend taking 410 from him.

I give mad props to Dr. Boyer. He is an excellent teacher. He wants you to learn the material, he always has his door open to stop by with questions. Plus, I think he's just a cool guy. If you take Investments, take it from him.

Dr. Boyer is a good teacher. The subject matter is challenging no matter who you take the class from. Anytime I had any questions or problems his door was always open.  The class is really good and extremely applicable to the real world. I would enjoy taking another class taught by him.

Really nice guy and willing to help you anytime in his office and will let you make up quizzes if you have to miss class, but his class is very boring.  It is almost impossible to focus.  I thought the class was pretty difficult because it was hard to pay attention. If you can do that, you should be good.
He was a totally cool guy.  If you came to class, the quizzes were super easy.  And then the exams were just exactly like the quizzes!

Time consuming. He's quite young and still figuring out how to teach. His study guides are identical to the tests, but he changes the tests every time since he's still learning the best ways to give them. Definately not the most fun class, I'd take a different professor if there is one. Hes a cool guy and he's willing to spend tons of time helping.

Brian is epic! He is very good at caring deeply about students' projects and has insightful suggestions! This class is super chill and what you put in is what you get out. There is a lot of freedom and that is good and bad depending on what you do with it. I loved the opportunities for experimentation with new techniques!!

Professor Christensen will help you explore art and learn as much as you allow. He will help you as you communicate. 
However, he didn't grade most projects until after the semester ended. I couldn't do anything about my grade then. If you want an A, you should communicate that with him. 
He gets distracted easily and had some hour-long demos lol.
He is such a cool teacher! I loved his class so much.

He is so funny! Brian knows so much and gives good feedback when you ask for it. A little disorganized but what art class isn't? You're grade is determined by your projects, and you only have 5-6 so just spend your work days wisely. He is willing to do almost anything to bring your vision to life, and will teach you really cool techniques.

Brother Christensen/Brian is a great teacher in my opinion. He is knowledgeable, chill, and will always make time to help you out. I give him 4 stars, not 5, because he is quite disorganized. This doesn't bother me though but it might be difficult for you. He won't always explain assignments/due dates clearly, so make sure to always ask!
Would not recommend.

To earn a good grade, be prepared to agree with Croxall's perspective, interests, and material.
+HOMEWORK

Professor Croxall is probably one of my favorite professors on BYU campus. He cares so deeply about the materials that he teaches, and makes an effort to help every student succeed. He may seem kind of snarky at first, but he is one of the most genuine people I've ever met.

Dr. Croxall seems intimidating at first, but he's actually so compassionate and respectful towards his students. (Though he's not afraid to tell you if your comments are dumb.) His grading seems scary, but the balance between hard assignments and easy points ends up working in your favor. Also, the class content is so relevant and fun.

This was my favorite class I've ever taken at BYU, and Professor Croxall is definitely the reason. The class will be small, guaranteed, but that made it really fun. I gained a lot from discussions and projects, even though I felt bad with computers . Professor Croxall takes student feedback and gives clear feedback really well.

Hard to get a read on Professor Croxall--he seems to be really passionate about teaching and his source material, but he was also a little belittling at times. I guess I'd probably take it again because I learned a lot and he definitely gave opportunities to get a good grade.

Such a good teacher! Like, he's really really good at teaching, and he cares about what you learn more than what he's able to cover. Puts a really fresh spin on things, though it helps that he teaches pretty unique things. Very honest, and appreciates honesty. Group projects aren't bad. He makes you memorize people's names but it's nice actually.

this was the most enjoyable Gen Art credit I think I could've taken. As long as you did the HW reading and your Inquizitives, you'll ace the tests. The class is very engaging and you can tell he knows his stuff. people who didn't get a good grade in this class most likely just didn't give it the time needed. Class always gets out early
Professor barker is the best take his class he knows all the topics very well

I enjoyed Prof Harker's class. He is passionate about music. The lectures can be dry, but the material is explained well, his review sessions are extremely helpful (in some cases he tells you the answers) and the homework is straightfoward. I went to his 3hr class- we were often done after half that. The review sessions were less than an hour.

Dr. Harker is awesome. The homework is really straightforward and he tells you exactly what will be on the test. Don't skip class because everything on the test is from the lectures and his slides aren't that easy to navigate. There's one group project. Also his lectures are NOT boring! They are very interesting and I think he's hilarious.

As far as the knowledge he has got it and knows a lot about music.  However, I would only recommend his section if you do not have any other sections available to you.  The biggest issue is his lectures are rather dull, which is a shame because the topic is interesting, but the lectures lack engagement and passion which turn me off when I go.

I wish I could say something good about Professor Harker, but I can't. I could have gotten an A without ever coming to class and just doing the reading and assignments. The classes were redundant and unnecessary. He has a sleepy, slow, boring lecture voice. The class is easy, but I don't recommend it.

This class is a breeze, especially if you have a background in music. I did all the homework within the first week or two of class, so it doesn't take long to do. The tests are so easy, probably the most tricky thing is remembering the forms that all the pieces are in. But if you have the chance to take it from Dr. Harker, please do!

Readings/textbook aren't necessary but lectures and homework are. Must take notes on lectures to do well on tests as prof. doesn't post slides. Made music interesting, no background needed. Drops lowest test. Must attend 4 concerts and write reports. Can tell prof. really loves music, he made class great even while dealing with injuries.

He was great! Lectures were long but he made them feel easy-breezy. There was a lot of material, based only on the lectures -- I was nervous about the exams but none of them were cumulative, even the final. Passionate about music history, made me excited about it too :) Great excuse to go to music performances, too.  *Textbook was online.

Dr. Harker was amazing! I've heard this class is notoriously difficult, but Dr. Harker made it so straightforward and fair. He prepared us very well for tests and there was never anything on a test we did not learn in class. There are 5 tests each 10% and if you studied, it was easy to get an A on every test.

I loved this class! Attendance technically isn't mandatory, most of the content on the tests was stuff that was discussed in class, so missing probably isn't a good idea. Don't be intimidated by the length of the class, he hardly ever released us after more than an hour and a half. I felt so great after every class, I'd definitely take it again.

Passionate about Jazz. Slides are wonderful. Lectures are interesting and super useful. Go to class, you will WANT to go to class because he is kind, caring, and engaging. 10/10 I wish I could have him for every music history class.

This is the best music history professor you will ever have. His lectures are engaging, he wants each student to excel in this course. He makes himself available for help and does not sugar coat the history of music. His tests are hard but he sets you up to do well in them. (I am not a great test taker) 
TAKE HIM FOR MUSIC HISTORY!!!!!!

Not a hard class if you are familiar with music and composers. He drops 2 assignments and 1 exam. You have to go to 4 classical music concerts and write a report but it isn't hard if you go to the music building and look at their schedule of free concerts. Class is only 1x per week though, it gets long but never goes the full 2 hrs and 50 minutes.

He is the best professor I could ask for for a music history course, funny lectures and the workload and tests are fair for what the class is. He is forthright with what the test looks like. Be sure to read the textbook, it will help. I am taking him again for 301, fantastic professor!

I was pleasantly surprised by how much I learned from Music 101 and how I began to care more about classical music. Dr. Harker emphasizes slowing down and appreciating art while learning about its background. It is an adjustment at first, but his class will change your life.

It's straightforward. Lectures are posted online, attendance not for grade, but I recommend attending class. His lectures are thorough. Tests are difficult if you don't watch or attend lectures. Expect to study if you want a good grade. Your grade is made up of only quizzes and tests. Don't worry. It's not bad if you stay on top of it.

He is really nice but this class was definitely my hardest this semester. The tests were pretty difficult and I didn't feel prepared for them. Reading the textbook isn't necessary, but because the lectures were confusing, I would recommend reading it.

Professor Harker is very kind, but this class is objectively boring unless you're super into old music. Every class is roughly 2 hours long of you just sitting in a room listening to music blare at you. I struggled staying awake most of the time. It's not super hard if you can memorize all the facts about each song and composer, but it's boring.

my husband and I who were both in the class planned to go on a vacation (before we even go into school) and the in person test happened to be when we were gone. I asked if we could take it before or after we get back, and his advice was to reschedule our entire family vacation. or not to go on vacation during school. not very emphatic or helpful.

He thinks his class is very important. He doesn't share his slides, he doesn't have recordings of lectures, and he doesn't make study guides. Exams are poorly written and reference obscure details. Lectures are boring. We have to use a paid service for homework. He loves what he teaches though.
Lots of lectures. Must attend four concerts outside of class. Exams are reasonable and he drops your lowest one, but if you don't study, you will definitely struggle.

MUS 302 is somewhat hefty, but this professor is seriously underrated. Very clear with expectations, very helpful in lectures, and cares a lot about the material. Homework load really isn't that bad. Exams (3) somewhat hefty but once again you go in knowing exactly what will be on the test. Is a caring and a fair lecturer/grader.

I loved taking History of Jazz from Dr. Harker. He really knows His stuff and gives super clear examples of different styles and genres. I also felt he was super respectful of the culture and history of jazz music, and barely talked about white versions of jazz. Lectures are super important, can't miss them if you want to do well.

I loved taking Music 302 with Dr. Harker. His lectures were really informative. However, I would say that it's really hard to get a good grade without coming to class. That is your best bet for acing the tests. I had to study quite a bit for his tests. But I feel like I learned a lot and have a better appreciation for the music and composers now

I have no music background and class was easy. Must attend 4 concerts and write reports. Tests are online in testing center and pretty easy, have to study but straight forward questions. 1 assignment per week and its like a game, you can answer as many times as needed to get 100%. Lowest midterm dropped. Prof. is very passionate and knowledgeable.

He's a great Professor, he is really passionate about music and is a great teacher. He knows his stuff and helps you understand. He is actually really funny in his own way and I thoroughly enjoy attending class. You really only have one assignment a week and you will always get 100% on them plus four concert reports. The tests are pretty easy too.

Professor Harker was amazing! Watch all his lectures, take good notes, and you will do well on tests. I have a music background, play 5 instruments, and have taken AP music theory in high school so it was a BREEZE, but I believe even someone without a music background can pass this! Make sure you have a good ear for listenings of the music though!

Professor Harker is really great. I took from him online so I would watch his lectures at 1.5 speed lol. He has 4 tests and a research paper. I dont love the writing but I learned a lot from the lectures and tests. He puts everything you need to know in the syllabus very clearly. He is so nice, always emails the class and holds weekly office hours

I had Dr. Harker's music 101 class on demand, which meant I never actually got to talk to him in real time. However, his lectures were very interesting and he made it very clear how to get an easy A on the tests and in the class. He would literally reply to my emails within minutes of sending them, and he was always so helpful and kind.

I really enjoyed learning about the music things in class. I started out not so great for my grade, and didn't do well on the first two tests. However, I reached out to Professor Harker and he gave me a better idea of how to go about the class, which really helped me. I ended with an A. Good gen-ed class.

I thought this class was going to be really hard but prof harker does a good job at preparing you for the tests. although his lectures can be really boring, you need them to do well on the exams (textbook info isnt on the exam) make sure to know the listenings VERY well! there are listening sections on the exams. pretty easy, just put in the work

Easily the most difficult class I've taken and as a 101??? Really? He talks so slow, I put his lectures on 1.25 speed since I was taking his class online on-demand. Because the tests weigh so much in your grade you have to take them seriously and study REALLY hard if you want an A (I re-watched lectures at 1.5 speed in order to get a 90%).

This class is way too hard for a general 101 class. Expectations of memorizing exact 20 word definitions, being able to identify a specific piece of music from many time periods, and very tough merciless tests. Lectures are dull, hard not to sleep through. Don't take it with this professor if you want an easy art credit.

His lectures are so dull and are not available online so you have to pay attention to all the boring parts if you want to do well. the fact you cant even review your notes online is silly. Thinks his class is very important

Taking M302 and M303 was my least favorite part of being a music major at BYU. While Dr. Harker seems like a great guy, his teaching style is pretty bad. His tests aren't actually hard, he just does a horrible job of preparing the students. It's a brutal class for 2 credits, and it sucks because it's required. The more recent reviews are right.
Zero test prep and mocks people who ask questions about what to expect on the test. Good luck.

Caffeine up before his classes because they're like Ben Stein narrating CSPAN. Doesn't tell you what to expect on the tests - obviously wants you to become a freaking expert on his life's work. Asking what you're going to be tested on seems insulting to him. Acts like his is the only class you probably have.

Dr. Harker really knows his stuff. However his class was rather dull and didn't include lots of student participation, despite a class size of 30-40. The exams were all in-class. He required lots of memorization of concepts, solely to regurgitate them on the exams. I forgot them all just days after the exam.

Dr. Harker uses powerpoints and lectures that he does not put online, so you have to come to class if you want the information on the test. I didn't do the textbook readings and I was fine, but you have to bring the Anthology (from Bookstore) to class every day. He is open to help outside of class, but really makes you work for a good grade.

I took Music 101 for the general credit and I was really impressed with how much I actually learned. I came to understand and appreciate music so much better. The class has a lot of listening and some readings each week. You also have to go to 4 concerts outside of class and write short reports on them (makes for good dates!).
Love his lectures but the tests are hard...

Very knowledgeable, but expects too much of a Music 101 class. This class isn't for music majors, it is a GE and shouldn't be treated like it is for Music majors. Tests are hard and it was very hard to know what we were going to be tested on. If you can do well on the test you will get an A, chances are you won't though. No curving either.

I've taken History of jazz and 303 from Dr. Harker. I love the way he approaches educating his students, leaving much to discovery but also directing us towards advanced thinking. I actually remember what I have learned in his lectures. His tests aren't made to fool you and he lets you know what you need to study. Tests are based off of lectures.

Harker's class requires a lot of reading and listening, both to his lectures and the music you'll be tested on. He doesn't post his powerpoints so you have to go to class. Study groups saved me with this class. The tests are all in-class, which is nice.

I'm not very musically inclined but I did recognize that Professor Harker was a great instructor. I would have failed if it weren't for his lectures; he explained concepts from the book in a way that I could understand. The homework load was reasonable. Three tests plus a final, but they weren't too bad. Just listen to the required songs often!!

He is pretty good and i think he teaches the subject well. It is just SO boring. I would reccomend finding another teacher for this class. I think some people in the class really liked him though, so you might like him as a professor. Tests are also pretty hard too, you have to study A LOT.

Bro. Harker knows what he is talking about but assumes everyone else does too, even if you're not a music major. He doesn't offer any test prep at all or tell you really what you will be tested on unless you ask him. Lectures can be boring. Tests are harder than they should be. Interesting subject, so take the class, just from a different teacher.

Brother Harker was a professor that truly cared about his students. He knew everyone in the class's name by the first day of class, and really seemed involved in the class. He was always happy, and very knowledgable about the class content. Great professor.

If you're looking to take MUSIC101 for the GE requirement, take it from Harker. I took the once-a-week class that was 2 1/2 hours, but he always let us out early and gave us a break. That being said, don't skip class or you'll miss really well-done lectures. He knows his stuff and explains things really well. I thoroughly enjoyed the class.

I took Professor Harker as an evening class once a week.  Hardest part about the class is staying awake during the lectures.  He basically goes over what the tests will be on in class.  Much less work than other Music 101 teachers, max one hour per week.  Pay attention, take good notes, memorize the songs, and you'll get an 'A'.

Professor Harker is really a man I look up to.  He gave me an appreciation that I wasn't expecting for musicians over the last few centuries and for their achievements.  I thoroughly enjoyed this class.  I had to study about 3 hours for each midterm, and about 5 or 6 for the final, but I did well.  I would definitely recommend him.

This course was so much fun! I learned a ton of interesting stuff about music and genuinely enjoyed class. Grades: weekly online quizzes (open book), tests, and concert reports. He let us do 2 extra reports and skip the final--it was awesome! Not too hard at all. Attend class bc you get your info from lecture, not the book. Would def recommend!

This class was so detail specific. The listening quizzes and tests were so difficult for me. They are so hard to study for and he was unclear about what would be on them. I learned a lot, but it was a lot harder than it needed to be. The textbook has a lot of extraneous info. so it is hard to read.
Listening and written tests were extremely difficult to prepare for. Expectations were not clear. Knowing jazz helps, but won't guarantee you a good grade.

So, he's not a regular religion teacher, but Dr. Harker's class was really wonderful in helping me to understand and apply the teachings in the second half of the Book of Mormon. If he's on the religion list: TAKE HIM!

I'll be honest, I am not a student with any musical talent but this class seemed easy to me. It's obvious that Prof Harker likes what he is teaching and he answers questions very helpfully. Tests are not that hard as long as you do your part and study. Attend every class and take good notes and you'll get a good grade on this class.

Pretty boring class but relatively easy and straightforward. Take good notes and study a little and you can get an A without a problem. Professor Harker seemed disinterested in the material most of the time and the lectures were not engaging. Take from someone else if you actually want to learn something.

I thought Dr. Harker did a great job teaching this class even though he normally doesn't teach it. Test questions are such that "either you know it or you don't". So if you're not interested in putting time into this humanities course, you'll have a hard time on the tests.
Terrible professor. Talks way too much and doesn't test us on what we cover in class. He says "we have to learn it on our own through readings".....then why are you here? Don't take it from him.

Super boring class. Bro. Harker just lectures the whole time in a super monotone voice. Unless you LOVE history, this class will be super boring. Tests are also pretty hard, you have to study alot. Nice guy, but boring and alot of boring reading.

Dr. Harker is a great teacher. He kept us interested in his lectures and involved students in most of the discussion. BUT, The tests were hard and he doesn't prepare students for what will be included. It's a toss up, you never know what details he wants you to know. Anyway, I would say take it from Howard. His class is more fun (and easier).
Very straightforward class.  Take good notes because the tests come mostly from the lecture.  Very helpful.

Very organized and straightforward. Go to every class and take notes, this is where 80% of the test comes from. Read the text outlines online instead of pouring over a boring textbook. I've had many classes from him. He is helpful and willing to work with you.  Tests aren't hard if you study for them and READ THE ANTHOLOGY! Loved the class.

Take excellent notes!!!!! This is probably the hardest part. I had this class evenings on wednesday and always started dozing off halfway through. However, I made it out with an A because of my notes. The test questions follow the lectures/book very closely so review those beforehand and you'll be fine. Plus he drops 1/10 tests including the final.

If you're even slightly uninterested in Jazz, do not take this class.  The material is really boring, and he focuses on a very select set of musicians.  I wouldn't recommend taking this class.  All of the tests are extremely hard.

Really boring class, tests are hard and he doesn't care about students understanding. The worst teacher I could ever have during my 4 years at BYU. Too much irrelevant information. Take this class with Dr. Hinckley!!!!

Pretty boring lectures for how interesting the subject matter could be. He definitely knows his stuff but just isn't the greatest teacher. Listening and written parts to each of the 4 tests. The listening is pretty tricky but you can do well on the written parts without too much studying. I like Jazz so that helped out.

The class consists of 4 2-part tests, a journal for 4 concerts, in-class writing exercises, and 4 listening charts. He's a great teacher who is very informative and loves the subject. I enjoyed the class, but the tests were difficult, asking for a lot of details from the textbook. A hard class, but definitely worth it if you love jazz.

Very good teacher. listens to every person's questions and makes sure they understand. Good at explaining abstract concepts. No extra credit, but he drops the lowest test score (including the final).  Only homework outside of studying for tests is 4 concert reports, which you get credit for just doing them. TAKE GOOD NOTES, and study before tests.

I  think Harker is a really nice professor. The tests were tough but his lectures are very helpful and if you take good notes you will get a good grade. I liked the class a lot. I would recomend this teacher. He is very nice and really wants to help the students.

History of jazz is sweet class especially if youre into music at all. You need to know the bold words and people in the book for every test. Get with familiar with the songs and know the form. You have 4 tests with 2 parts to each and 3 listening charts. Thats it. Harker is a good teacher and loves jazz.

Take his history of jazz class!  His classes are very informational and interesting.  He is a total music geek and it is obvious he's very passionate about it.  He does look for specifics in his tests, however, and you pretty much have to memorize the book chapters to do well on the test.  It's not too hard, though.  Loved it!

I thought Harker did an excellent job and is a good professor. You do really have to study, and the listening exams are tough. But I came into the class with no jazz knowledge and not a lot of interest in jazz, and left loving it! Not easy, but this class is worth it!

I took the Jazz History class from Bro Harker. His lectures were interesting but you have to know a lot of little details in all the songs besides the title and artist. The tests were hard but he does give a review sheet. There is a lot of reading you have keep up with to get a good grade. there are no other assignments to help boost your grade.

Very clear in both his expectations and his teaching style.  Tests have a lot on the music, so it's a good idea to go to class because he spends so much time on the music.  For a music history class, which are notoriously difficult, it's not too bad.  I would have definitely have gotten an A if I had gone to class each time.

He was an awful professor. He didn't know the material about which he was lecturing, he spelled words and composer's names wrong on the tests and was an awful professor. I don't recommend taking any classes from him! He refused to give perfect scores on exams as well, saying that no one should be getting perfects.

Compared to Music 301 and 302, this class was a walk in the park!  He spends a lot of time on the stuff you actually need to know. Sometimes his lectures can drag, but if you pay attention and do the reading, it isn't that difficult. I enjoyed this class.

Harker is a great teacher.  He knows what he is talking about.  If you take good notes and read the text you will do well; however, if you do not you will do very poorly. I have come out of his courses much more informed and with a better understanding of both music 303 and 304.  Anybody who thinks otherwise is just lazy.

I loved this class.  If you have a love for jazz, it is super fun.  Really interesting lectures.  You do need to study hard for tests, but he tells you exactally what you need to know.  As long as you read and highlight all the bolded words in the book and learn them, you will be fine.  the listening part is easy if you put a few minutes into it

I don't know what everyone else is talking about, I found this class to be fairly easy with a minimal amount of work. I found the lectures to be interesting and easy to understand. I think the big thing is if you like jazz or not. If you don't get very excited by it, don't expect a high grade.

This class is VERY difficult.  To Dr. Harker's credit, I learned a lot about Jazz music and the knowledge has stuck with me.  I received a "B" grade, which is the lowest grade I have ever received at BYU (I am a senior).  Overall, I think the B was worth it because he gave such great lectures.

Not as easy as you might have heard but Bro Harker is a nice guy and does care for the students. If you have a concern he will listen to you. I actually enjoyed the listening portion of the tests. You can listen to it all week long to get it down as you study for your other classes.

DO NOT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE TAKE THIS CLASS FROM THIS INSTRUCTOR! HE'S A **** WHO GIVES NO PREPATORY INFORMATION TO THE TEST! U GET MOUNDS OF INFO & NO WAY TO ORGANIZE IT TO KNOW WHAT YOU'LL BE TESTED ON!!!  MUSIC IS MY MAJOR, I KNOW A LOT ABOUT IT, & I'LL PROBABLY BE GET A D! ****!

This class was difficult because for the tests, you have to identify few-second clips of songs that may be up to ten minutes long. Many of the songs sound alike. The actual music history was interesting, but reading assignments were long. Test material seems irrelevant to the point of the class.
Horrible teacher. Tests require you to pick out 10 seconds of a 30 minute song on the first try.  He won't play it again.  Take this from a different teacher.
Why is it that the test average on a music test is 62.5?  10% of music 101 gets A's?  I was counting on an easy A, but instead I got a block of torture.  Why not just stick your head in a blender?

THE GOAT. He is the best teacher, and gives great advice outside of the base content of the class. Couldn't recommend him more, but get ready for some independent study if you want an A. Not much class time in 274 for how hard some of the later content it if you have no time value of money experience.

HE IS A LEGEND. I absolutely love taking classes from him and you can't go wrong. He does teach some difficult classes and this one is no exception. He does his best to make sure we understand what is going on. He is also super caring, he took an entire class to get to know us. Pay attention and do lots of practice problems and you'll do fine.
He is the best, not to mention you get SOA exam fm credit for it. Exams are everything, definitely do practice problems every week so you are ready
This class is incredibly difficult. Professor Hartman makes the material easier to understand, but this class is hard. I would suggest not taking this class, unless you want to be an actuary.

Dr. Hartman is an excellent professor who cares a lot about the material and is always happy to help. The class is certainly hard, but he works hard to make it understandable for everyone. I would totally take classes from him again!

I have taken multiple classes from Dr. Hartman and he is, by far, the best professor I've had. He cares about you, takes time to answer questions in and outside of class, and has lots of energy. The content is challenging, but Dr. Hartman makes it easy to understand. Plus, he is super willing to help you with your job/internship search.

Brian Hartman is probably the best professor on this planet. He is a very down to earth guy and explains things exceptionally well. If you don't understand what is going on in class lectures ask him and one on one you will learn so much more! Just expect to have to practice a lot, the class is difficult but for good reason!

By far the best professor at BYU. Super engaging and thinks like a student. He isn't caught up in the terminological side of things so it is easy to ask questions and understand the answer. Fantastic preparation for exam FM. Be prepared to make this your most important class of the semester. Studying is a must.

Love this guy. Class was HARD and I studied my butt off to barely pass. Homework takes a LONG time, but it's a because it's meant to prepare you for the standardized test. Professor goes a little too fast sometimes and likes to explain concepts and math verbally, so I was lost every single class. Great guy though, love him a lot, just a hard class.
Best professor i have ever had. Take this class join the actuarial program you will love it.

Very rigorous class but very fascinating. The class is fast paced, but Dr. Hartman does a great job at teaching all the necessary material to pass exam FM as well as teaching why certain math works the way it does. Don't plan on memorization to save you. Repetition and understanding the concepts is key.

Class was hard but I pulled off an A. Was curved but the average was still a B. The class was super hard but he gave you all resources to pass and I loved it. Great intro for actuary science. Test were page of notes and had two versions, you took both and kept higher score. I did not pass Exam FM on first try. I suggest study a lot out of class.

Dr. Hartman is hands down my favorite professor at BYU. He really cares about each of his students and wants them all to succeed. He teaches a very difficult class but he is always willing to put in the work to help you understand the difficult material. Dr. Hartman is teaching for all the right reasons, and it shows in his work.

Dr. Hartman cares about his students being successful in class, in the major, and in future career. He is super chill-very easy to talk to. The tests are tricky but definitely not impossible. Yes, some people fail them, but he curves a lothe is just recreating the conditions for the FM exam. I loved his class!! Get infinite actuary too to help!

Hartman's class is tough, and it can be overwhelming if you're not in love with the subject matter. But he is an excellent advisor and professor and he works to create an awesome environment for his students.

Dr Hartman is one of my favorite professors at BYU! The course material is difficult, but he does really well at helping every student succeed in his class and in SOA Exam FM. I wish I could have him teach all of my classes because of how caring and helpful he has been.

Dr Hartman has been my favorite professor at BYU. He cares so much about each of his students and is dedicated to help you succeed. 274 requires a lot of effort to succeed, but is very doable with the online resources and TA's. You won't regret taking a class from Dr Hartman!

Brian is a champ. This class is definitely tough, but I have never had a teacher in my life who has cared so much for his students. He wants everyone to do great and he is amazing at teaching difficult concepts. 10/10 would recommend if you are an Actuarial Science major or not. This class is tough and you need to work, but it's def worth it.

Doctor Hartman is a great professor. Stat 274 is the prep course for the SOA exam FM. He's really caring about his students and is very encouraging, even though the material is quite difficult. Because its a prep course for exam FM, almost the entirety of your grade will be reflected by your test scores.

I'm not exaggerating when I say Dr Hartman is the best professor at BYU. He wants you to succeed- in this class, in your major, in your career. He is always willing to talk, give advice, help find an internship, etc. 274 is tough but will help you determine if Actuarial Science is the thing for you. It is heavily curved. Go to the TA's a lot!

I loved Dr. Hartman! It is definitely a hard class, but he is a great teacher and works his hardest to make sure that everyone does as well as they can. He also has some of the best TAs at BYU. They are so smart and crazy helpful for the homework and preparing for tests. Dr. Hartman wants to know everybody personally and he is just a great dude.

Dr. Hartman is one of the most genuine people I've ever. He really wants to help you be the best that you can be--even if it's not in actuarial science. 274 is really hard and requires a lot of work. I wouldn't use it as the only thing to prepare for FM but you could if you wanted (I used The Infinite Actuary and it helped a lot).

Dr. Hartman is hilarious and engaging. He is always willing to help with subject material, specific problems, and picking future classes. The class is hard, but it prepared me well for the FM exam. Be prepared to put in a lot of time to learn and do tons of practice problems. His tests are difficult, but gives 2nd chances and grades on a curve.

Dr. Hartman is wonderful! The class itself is extremely hard, but Dr. Hartman teaches it in a way that will allow you to understand it and then apply it in homework. This class is for Actuarial Science majors (prospective majors), so it isn't the typical class. Be prepared to work hard, and don't be afraid to ask for help.

Dr. Hartman loves the material and cares about students. The class mostly consists of preparing for exams, which are difficult for most and tedious for all. Without any background in financial mathematics, it was difficult to understand the notation from class slides. I would suggest study material other than the optional textbook.

Best professor I had at BYU. If you are an actuarial science major and put in the time, this class will be enjoyable and valuable. Get to know Dr. Hartman and you'll see that he is highly invested in your learning and future career.

We don't have to buy books and we don't have to read it. He is a fun person to talk to, very approachable and friendly.  Sometimes his tests are tough, not going to lie, but I think he just want to better prepare us for the FM exam. He is a good teacher and someone who really want you to succeed not just in classrooms but also in life.

Tricky material and it was his first time teaching here at BYU. Things were somewhat unorganized, but not atrociously so. Tests were difficult for most, and easy for few. He's a nice guy, and is there to help at least.
He understands the subject better than any other professor teaching it! Easy in class quizzes, lots of homework, good organized notes.

Heat Transfer is tough no matter what, but Iverson makes it worth it. He's incredibly kind, approachable, and genuinely cares about his students. His tests are hard and homework is detailed, but the structure helps you learn. He truly embodies Christlike love in how he teaches. One of the first professors I liked enough I felt the need to rate.

Dr. Iverson is a great guy who genuinely wants you to succeed. That being said, the class is rough, the homework is graded very specifically (SAFER method), and the in-class tests are extremely difficult. Although he curves the tests, it will take SO much time to understand and do well. So just be prepared.

Listen up. Straight A's until this guy. This was my last semester of a 5 year program. Never had such a terrible experience with a professor's teaching style before now, and Ive had some rough patches. He barely grazes the subjects in class. He uses a standard note sheet each lecture you can use to copy, but it won't help you on the hw. Overworked.

Dr. Iverson has been teaching this class for a while and has developed an excellent method to help us understand heat transfer. There are in-class quizzes but are easy and self-graded. All of his lectures have been recorded and uploaded so you don't really need to attend class. HW is nothing harder than we've done before.
Very difficult to work with. Someone to avoid if you can.

Very nice guy. The main problem is that he doesn't explain any details in anything. Part of the reason for that is that his lecture is only 25 minutes long. Also, the 25 minutes allotted to in-class time is used up by stupid questions that students ask, and Dr. Iverson will spend too much time on those questions. He writes g when he means q.

Dr. Jensen is the epitome of a good professor. He knows what he's doing, he knows how to explain it, and he is very good and understanding the root of a question and helping students figure out what they're missing (something that a lot of technical professors often struggle with). He cares, iterates, and finds what works for a class.

The professor really tries to adjust the course to fit his student's needs. I overheard that in a TA meeting he asked how they could best help struggling students. He's a caring professor and is willing to help you with your projects. His course is project and lab heavy with take home exams so it's a class that shouldn't add too much stress.

Dr. Jensen is the best professor I've had thus far at BYU. I was very impressed with how respectful he was towards all the students and he was always seeking out feedback on how the course could be improved and how he could better as a professor. The course was paced really well. Fantastic professor and well-taught course.

Great professor. Class was very well organized and I learned a lot. He frequently seeks feedback on how to improve the course and makes changes accordingly. Very kind and caring and teaches clearly and effectively, and slips his quirky sense of humor in here and there. Would highly recommend.

Doctor Jensen's 273 class was very clear about what was expected. He always gave rubrics so you knew exactly what to do and is one of the most reasonable professors I have ever had. His class was interesting and as a result, is one of those few professors that make you glad that you came to BYU. Glad I took this class from him!

Dr. Jensen is a nice guy, but not a great professor. Even for an intro class, the material he taught was so basic it felt like we never learned any useful skills. The grades were highly weighted on a few things, while other big projects were worth only a little. The tests are easy. He wrote the textbook, that's why he makes students keep using it.

This was my favorite ME class in my 4 years in the program. Pace of material is perfect. Grade your own homework with given solutions, so you always know what's going on. Tests were reasonable. Teacher was great, respectful, understanding. He even lessened HW assignments during the group project. WOULD RECOMMEND the class and especially the teacher

Advanced Machine Design. I liked this class. I feel like I have gained a greater understanding of how to design things and use tools available, whether mathematical models or FEA software, to analyze systems. Great teacher, very passionate about the design process.

Dr. Jensen is a smart guy, yet he knows how to teach new, difficult material clearly and directly. He's definitely one of the kindest professors in the department. Reasonable grader, light homework load, and fair tests.

If you have no prior programming experience, this is a very hard class. Jensen is a very nice guy and knows his stuff. Sometimes the class lectures get off track and follow the students' questions for way too long, but overall, he's a good teacher.

Jensen is a great teacher. Very helpful and his classes are fun. Yes, programming is hard but he does a good job of teaching the material. Labs are hard as well but the TA's are great. Exams are fair, I felt prepared for each one but they were not easy. I would take him again.

Programming is really hard to teach in an ideal context; Mechanical Engineering is far from that ideal context. That said, Dr. Jensen did as good a job at it as I could imagine. This class was trivial for those who already knew how to program, but was very difficult for those who didn't have the knack for programming. Focused on Excel, Matlab, C++.
Great teacher.  He is very helpful and gets the students involved in class.  Tests are very fair.

Dr. Jensen is a very intelligent teacher.  He knows what he is talking about and puts forth effort learning everyone's name in the class.  He has his office hours and is willing to help when needed as well as has good TA's.  The labs are difficult and you will spend more time then they give you, but that is what is expected. The tests are very good

Yes people, he is a nice guy. We are at BYU.  The point of this is to help other student know what to expect. Thus said, Jensen should not be teaching this subject. He obviously has never taught before in his life. The labs are painful. If you take this class, you might as well download C++ from the internet and stay at home for the labs...
