The lab was confusing at times, but is basically a free 100, so that boosts your grade a lot. Dr. Mazzeo is super smart, and definitely knows his stuff, but sometimes he explained concepts in a way that made them seem more complicated then they actually were. Overall though, he was decent and dropped a lot of assignments/quizzes.

This isn't too hard of a class, but when combined with 240 (an electrical engineering class) 301 is harder because it's geared toward the ecen students and students with some prior knowledge. Because of that, Professor Mazzeo isn't the best at teaching the fundamental concepts but he's great at teaching the variants.

He is very student focused and wants everybody to succeed. His lectures are well intentioned, but aren't explained simply enough to help us with solving our homework problems. The exams are super difficult, so it pays to really study the homework problems and do very well in the equally difficult lab portion of the class.

10/10 Like the other UNIV classes, you have your set of assignments and shenanigans that you need to complete, but prof Mazzeo really cares about his students. He has cool stories and presents well. Additionally, he takes the time to read what you write about, giving genuine feedback and pulling from the online discussions for class discussions.

It's a harder class with hard homework, but Dr. Mazzeo did a great job. I would definitely take a class from him again. Very good at understanding and answering questions. Explained advanced concepts well.

Very caring and invested in student success. Does not belittle students for asking questions, and will even pause a lecture to re-teach if he notices multiple students struggling. Respectful of those experiencing faith challenges (some professors at BYU are awkward about these). Quizzes and exams didn't always clearly follow homework assignments.

He's a good lecturer and can answer almost any question you throw at him. Overall good, but not much else to say outside of that. Will help you understand stuff to an okay degree. Nice guy, kinda funny.

Dr. Mazzeo is a great professor who really tries to create the spiritual learning environment that BYU is supposed to have. Sometimes the lectures are hard to understand but you can generally figure it out during homework. The ChemE majors (301) always seemed lost but everyone else seemed to follow fine. Talk to him and ask questions after class!

Go to his office hours. He will teach you. He doesn't judge people and doesn't talk down to them. He's very reasonable. His slides are key to success in his class to use them to study, do the homework, and study an hour or two for the quizzes.

Dr. Mazzeo is nice and very passionate about electronics but kind of hard to learn from. He is very knowledgeable and intelligent and has a hard time dumbing things down for people who have no previous experience with electronics. Lectures were pretty confusing, I made it through this class largely thanks to hours and hours in the TA lab.

ECEN 301 is a very difficult class if you haven't had much exposure to the concepts (as I hadn't), but Dr. Mazzeo is pretty good at explaining things in a relatively simple way and then expanding on that, and he is very caring about students and their feelings. But be prepared: the semester-long Arduino project is cool but VERY time-consuming.

One of the least professional professors I have had to deal with. Didn't show up on time for meetings and ran them long, lied about material on exams, disagreed with other professors over course material, stated "will respond within 100 hours" almost 2 months later and no response, Assignments graded late once no opportunity to make corrections.

Great professor and knows a lot, but 55% of your grade depends on the six hours you spend on your midterm and final. I went from a solid B to a D because I didn't do so well on the final. It would have been nice if more of the grade had been on the 100+ hours that you spend on the homework and reading.

He's willing to slow down to make sure the entire class understands. If you look at the old tests you will be very prepared for his tests. There are quizzes every Friday that really help you confirm your understanding of the material

Mazzeo is super smart, went to MIT and got a 4.0. He told us that he would stay up until 3am doing homework and expects us to do the same. He demands a lot. I didn't feel like he was great at explaining the material and felt very frustrated in his class (I still got an A). The quizzes are all similar to previous years quizzes. Study those.

The class is tough.  Test mean was at ~65% with std deviation of ~18.  He is very fair though, and really wants students to succeed.  The material is just hard, and he says he cannot, in good conscience let engineers enter the industry without understanding these concepts.  Aside from granting undeserved grades, he does everything he can to help.

One of the best professors I have ever had.  He is perfectly clear in all of his teaching and is always very prepared.  He challenges the class, and if you put real time and effort into his assignments you will do well.  He puts real thought and effort into the class and really cares about the students.

Good at explaining things in class, but the tests are IMPOSSIBLE.  He went to MIT and Cambridge and expects his students are at his level.  Homework and tests have nothing in common.  He doesn't care about comments about his tests, even though the average is horrible he still things the class should be better.

Simple to understand, but always left me thinking about new things. He isn't afraid to bring up hard topics like divorce, LGBTQ in the church, inactivity, etc. He always speaks so respectfully of every demographic. Do the few assignments well, it will be very thought provoking and perspective changing. Can't say enough good about him.
Fantastic professor, I thoroughly enjoyed his class despite not being very excited to have to take it at the start of the term. Brian is the best, and would take any class from him again.

One of the easiest religion classes I've taken. The lectures were super engaging and fun. He cares about his students and addressed hard topics, like divorce and church history questions, in a way that was respectful and informative. There are attendance quizzes, but they are quick to do and the tests were also easy as long as you went to class!

Such an amazing class. Doctrinally centered and aimed to improve our lives and connection with Christ. Brother Mead is so funny and also a great and caring teacher. Projects were simple and also very uplifting and not just busy work. Homework and tests had extremely clear and reasonable expectations. Homework weighted much higher than tests.

I LOVED this class, it's the best religion class I've taken at BYU. He really cares for his students, and he makes a 200 person lecture work as a discussion based class. There are weekly assignments, but they don't take more that 30 minutes. Honestly, assignments had a clear purpose, he doesn't believe in busy work. Exams were piece of cake too!

Brian Mead deeply cares for the students. He is funny, engaging, and loving. There were quite a few assignments; most of them felt like busywork. Attendance is part of your grade so you must attend to get the quiz code, but the lectures were interesting and fun.
I loved his eternal families class. Also, if you have him you should pop by his office hours. Even if you don't need help in the class, he's super fun to chat with.

I loved this class, and always looked forward to the lectures. I made sure to take notes and write down what I was learning from the spirit throughout. The projects aren't too hard, and I found that I was able to make connections with others through them and learn a lot that I can apply in my own life.

Brother Mead was great. This class had more work than other religion courses I've taken, but none of it was terribly hard. I loved a lot of his thoughts and he is very loving of all, regardless of your background. Tests are online and not hard. Attendance quizzes make up a bulk of your grade.

I like the guy, but if you don't have a lot of time to dedicate to religion classes, don't take it from him. Attendance is mandatory, he only drops one of the quizzes and nothing else. If you can't make it to every class, your grade drops a lot, and he doesn't seem really flexible with that. Tests are easy, projects are nice, only attendance sucks.

10/10 so glad I had him. hes by far the best religion professor. hes super caring and super chill. there's like three projects in the semester but they're super easy. His tests are so chill. the work he assigns is actually meaningful and doesn't just feel like busy work. hes super fun and caring. take from him hes the best.

Brian Mead is easily one of my favorite religion professors I have taken a class from. He is so inspirational, and his lectures are so engaging. He teaches difficult concepts in a way that just made sense. The class was also really easy to get a good grade in, while still being interesting. Take eternal families from him!!

Didn't learn much because he didn't really go into controversial lds topics-- answered hard questions without really answering them. Frequently had students turn to person next to them and read quotes on board out loud; in a class of 100+ people, this was overwhelming. Despite my gripes, tests were VERY easy, even the final. Attendance mandatory
Great teacher, class is very well organized. Attendance is mandatory and there is a weekly quiz, but it's super easy.

Can't say enough good things about Bro Mead. The most genuine, willing-to-help person I've ever met. Attendance is required but the lectures were always really engaging and uplifting so it never felt like a waste of time to be there. Course work was decently time consuming but not difficult. I'd HIGHLY RECOMMEND his office hours, even just to chat

Professor Mead is engaging and is passionate about what he teaches. There is a lot of reading, which is annoying, but the assignments are easy. The tests are online, and pretty straightforward. There are 3 projects due throughout the semester, and those probably take the most time. Overall, easy class, just lots of reading.

Exams are all online and are pretty much common sense. There are quizzes every week, and those questions are used in the exams. There are 3 projects that don't take too much time. He is great to work with students on concerns with grades or content. Definitely recommend him for eternal families!

Professor Mead is one of my favorite BYU professors. This class was amazing and made me want to take all of his religion classes. It is homework heavy, but if you do the work right when it is assigned and stay on top of projects it is very doable.

Brother Mead is by far the best religion professor here! He cared about your spiritual growth and teaches so well! I would have gotten 100 but I missed a couple days due to work and also spaced a midterm! I would recommend his class to everyone! He gets to know his students and is really just a wonderful human being! Take this class!
Lectures were engaging and inspiring and the homework was very managable. You can tell that Proffessor Mead really cares for and respects each student.

I took this class from Professor Mead because I took one of his classes a couple years ago and loved it. This was not the same and his teaching style has changed a bit. There is way too much work assigned for a religion class. Won't be taking another class from him.
Lectures were really engaging and the class was really easy. If you do all the work, you're chilling. He's a really good teacher who cares about his students' success.

Super easy A, just do the work. The median grade for the class on all of the exams was 100%. Just go to class and do the work, and you will do great. Lecture is mostly entertaining and is a good way to start the day.

He is the best. I would definitley take another class for him. It is one of the lighter and easier religion classes I have taken. It is doable and a fair amount of work. He handled difficult topics pretty well.
He's a great professor and guy. The class is not difficult, but it requires a substantial amount of work for a religion class. Easy to get an A and the lectures are very spirit-filled.

So so so much homework. 3+ assignments each week, 3 projects, 3 midterms, on top of the 3 assignments each week. If you have questions about anything, you're better to just beg God for the answer rather than emailing him. Does not work with students.

Lazy professor. WILL NOT ANSWER EMAILS. He makes it clear to not email him. Does not give grace at all. TESTS ARE PROCTORED. He is the type of professor to say his hands are tied and can't do anything. He takes over a month to grade anything. Does not care about students.

He is an AMAZING professor. All you need to do is show up and turn your assignments in on time and you will get an A. The grading is not harsh at all. Tests are at home not proctored. Could not recommend the class enough.

Im not big on byu religion classes, but I wish I could say enough good about the guy and his class. You WILL get an A don't worry. When he says the average score for his tests is a 100% he's not joking. Show up for the attendance code, or know someone and you will be fine. No homework, and class time can be used to study for his class or others.

Phenomenal! This class was the perfect mix of spiritually strengthening and challenging. I believe Religion classes are meant to spiritually strengthen students while not adding to the college stress or workload excessively. This class perfectly met my expectations. Professor Mead gave such good lectures and was such a good Disciple of Christ.
W Professor W class structure

He is super funny, and teaches so well. He makes sure that everyone can get an A and the workload is very light. We a 5 question post assignment after class every period and I small essay due at the end of every week. Tests were pretty simple and definitely don't need to study ever.

This was one of the easiest religion classes I've taken at BYU. He seriously wants everyone to get an A in his class. There are attendance quizzes, 3 projects, and then 2 midterms plus the final. Make sure that you don't put off doing the projects because they can be very time consuming. Great class overall!

Professor Mead is very kind, and he's good at teaching Eternal Families. This class is remarkably easy, which might not be for everyone, but it can be good for those who are stressed. The projects are really engaging and you can learn a lot from it. Professor Mead is also happy to meet up with people outside of class to answer deeper questions.
Do you want an easy A in a religion course? This is the class for you. Do you want to delve deep into the family and prepare to have one yourself? This is not the class for you.

You see, this class was SO easy. I appreciated the easy A, but I was left lacking. The lectures and homework were very surface level. The lectures were very compact and filled with so many unnecessary quotes, it always felt like we were rushing to get through the material. This was not the quality I expected or wanted from a BYU religion course.
Awesome guy. Passionate about the topic
y'all know the scene in mean girls when regina is writing in the burn book? yeah that's all I have to say about this professor
started praying daily for peace because this professor made me crash out like no other

AVOID PROFESSOR AT ALL COST!!!!! SO LAZY WITH GRADING!!!! HE MAKES SUBMITTING PROJECTS UNREASONABLY HARD. WITH THESE PROJECTS YOU HAVE TO PROVIDE MULTIPLE LINKS, IF LINKS DO NOT WORK, HE WILL FAIL YOU, NO GRACE IS GIVEN!!!!!!!!!!!!
one of the easiest religion classes I have taken, will definitely take from Mead again

This class was life changing. I learned lots and the format of the class is amazing and straight forward. He really cares, his assignments are geared towards real life application. He loves the Savior and it shows in the way he teaches. The tests are closed note but not hard. Low stress. My testimony grew. No essays, projects are fun and worth it.
I loved being apart of Mr. Mead's class. You can tell her really cares about all of his students, I never wanted to miss a single lecture.

This class is a really good class, set up so you can learn but not hard at all. You have like three decent sized projects and 3 tests that are easy. The projects are a lot more time consuming. You have to be in class to get a password for an attendance assignment. Class stays pretty surface level.

Easiest class I ever took, I usually was just doing other homework during lecture. He's nice but the class doesn't get too deep. Seminary vibes. The hardest part is the 3 projects, for 2 you record yourself presenting the project.
Take his classes, he's the best educator I've ever had.

Took Eternal Family over Summer. Brother Mead is great. He's a little quirky and sometimes he'll tease students, but great guy, easy class. Ended up having a transformative experience in the class just because I put in the work and did the assignments. Grateful I took this class from him.

I took his class this semester, and it was great! The way he teaches the eternal family class is good, and there is not a lot of work outside the class. He just has you do an attendance assignment, a case study, and 3 bigger projects each semester.

Loved this class. Brian Mead is the perfect teacher for the job. He has great energy, very bubbly, and knows this is a beginner class. If you're a member, all of this stuff is pretty common knowledge. Unlike BOM class. No tests, no final, just some papers and fun projects.

Every week we had an attendance quiz where we had to write about the family proclamation, we did this twice a week with 5 written questions and two multiple choice. Then on top this, we had a case study ranging in 3-7 short essay questions. All while doing weekly readings. Homework remained the same during midterms, essays, and 3 large projects.

I loved my eternal family class with Brother Mead! I felt inspired every day in his class and feel like I am much more prepared for my future family and can make better decisions in my everyday life. He had 3 midterms and a final that were all the same amount of your grade and very reasonable. I highly recommend taking a class from him!

Professor Mead's class was low stress and I loved it. Each class is the same format: presentation/lecture, so it is predictable. There is an attendance check every day, so you do have to go to class. Homework is very easy. He has spiritually motivating/well-thought ideas. He is a very kind person and strives to build friendships with his students.

Brother Mead is the best! He makes class very enjoyable. It was probably the least stressful religion class I have ever taken. I took his class summer term, and it is extremely manageable, even in the shortened term. He genuinely cares for all his students and is extremely Christlike.

I loved Dr. Mead's class! The class was light-hearted, despite some of the tricky topics. He always did a great job at approaching things with a loving, eternal perspective. I had this class at 8am and looked forward to going to lectures. Assignments were super easy. No final exam if you do all the quizzes! I heavily recommend Dr. Mead for RELC200.

Super interesting readings, and a very relatable professor! He really makes an effort to connect and care for his classes. Few and simple assignments, which really let you focus on learning and growing! When I took, you could sub avg quiz grade for the final, which was clutch

Mead is a good guy. The class has no midterm and final if you do your homework. You have two reading homework assignments each week that are self graded. Each class he gives out a participation code for you to get credit of your participation and a quiz of what you learned. Each week you have to do a 4-6 paragraph fake scenario short essay. Not bad

I used to hate reading student reviews that said "best class/professor I've ever had", but now I get it. Professor Mead is hilarious, kind, and intelligent. His pre-class readings about the eternal family changed my life. Class is structured to be easy enough to actually learn and feel the Spirit instead of stress about grades.
He was absolutely amazing and super understanding of what people are going through. No final if you just go to class and take the post-class quizzes. Very engaging. Take this with Brother Mead!!

Good teacher overall. Personality can be a bit much at times, but he is genuine. If your attendance quizzes are good enough you dont take the final so thumbs up from me. Also the class is large so its not personal which I liked.

Loved Prof. Mead. He was super kind, he has really interesting lectures and slides, and he was caring. He always started off class with friendly discussions and was really funny. I didn't learn a ton in his class because some things were obvious... but there were some little things I learned and loved learning about. I'd definitely take him again!

Dr. Mead is cool and does a good job with the content. This class, however, is super obvious, and I can honestly say I learned nothing. I expected eternal families from a psychology PhD to include more studies and psychology instead of the same lines from the Family Proclamation. Class is super easy though.

Simply a great class and great professor. Approached a variety of topics with love and understanding, and did an incredible job of covering the surface level of EVERYTHING when it comes to the eternal family. I'd easily recommend to anybody considering :)

Brother Mead is great- he approaches tough church topics with love and care. This class was pretty easy- show up, take the quizzes, do the weekly assignments and you'll be good. You can even opt-out of the final exam if you've come to class throughout the semester which is huge!
Brother Mead is super kind and caring, and this courseload is LIGHT. Ideal religion class. Well planned, thoughtful lectures, although just personally I got a little tired of his jokes at times.

Brother Mead is the most amazing professor I have ever had at BYU. Even in his huge classes, he really ministers to the one. I learned so much. There's always mandatory reading before class, and a post-class quiz with a password you get in class, so you have to be in lecture. You'll want to be there anyway tho bc he's amazing. 11/10
Great professor and learned a lot. Pretty easy class.

If you have the opportunity, take Brother Mead's class. He provides the perfect combination of 1) a strong learning environment where students gain a stronger testimony 2) and I never had to worry about my grade (the assignments are not hard and grading criteria is very clear).
He is the sweetest professor and cares so so much about his students.

Absolutely incredible professor. BYU is truly lucky to have him! Has a super cool background in psych and shows how we can apply teachings to our lives. Is so so open minded and accepting, too. Very inclusive and empathetic. Easy class too-- you get an A if you do easy readings and come to class and do one weekly assignment on time. Love this guy!

He makes the class so enjoyable for everyone. His lectures are super engaging. There are post-class quizzes after every class, but they are super easy if you attended. 3 big projects during the semester that are super uplifting. Do whatever you can to take this class from him.

Brother Mead was very good about adding his thoughts to the discussion boards. Excellent communication and posts great weekly announcements. He wants you to succeed and posts contact information with every announcement so that you know you could reach out to him with questions or if an emergency arises. Great class!

Prof Mead has super interesting lectures that you don't need to take notes on which is amazing. The class was so so easy and unstressful, assignments felt applicable to real life usually. Just stay on top of the post-class quiz and get everything done and it's an easy A

Quizzes after every lecture, very easy if you attended the lecture, hard if you skipped. At the end of this class the combined scores of all these quizzes counted for our final which was super nice. You could also opt to take a real final if your quiz scores were not good

Right now, I don't think that you can beat Professor Mead for RELC200. He is an engaging lecturer and he clearly strives to be sensitive to a diverse range of important issues. The class is also one of the most organized classes I have taken, his straightforward class expectations removed any stress for me. His assigned projects were awesome.

This class was probably the easiest religion class I've taken at BYU. If you want an easy A, take this class from this professor. Attendance is not required, but I'd recommend going to get 100% on your daily quiz. You can substitute your average daily quiz grade or take the final. No midterm. Not the most inspiring lectures, but easy.

Such an awesome professor. There are a reasonable amount of readings and daily quizzes. This semester you could use your average quiz score instead of taking the final exam which I thought was awesome as the quizzes were really easy if you attended and paid attention in class. I highly recommend taking this class from him.
I love Professor Mead! I think his background in psychology was really cool for this class and the topics we talk about. He's a great guy and you can tell he cares about the students.

Brother Mead was fantastic. He is compassionate and empathetic in how he approaches the course material, which is so necessary for an Eternal Families professor. There were quizzes every day after class, but if you did the reading you did well on them. There are also a few big projects, but all of them were fun and testimony-strengthening.

Incredible professor. Really cares about his students and takes the time to get to know them. Does a great job of teaching difficult and polarized topics with love and understanding. Readings before every class, one assignment due every saturday, and three big assignments during the semester. Professor Mead is one of my favorite professors ever.

He makes sure his expectations are clear and even gives suggestions of how much time you should spend on each homework assignment (it's not a lot). Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you go to every class you'll get an A, a stronger testimony, and some laughs! He goes out of his way to make life as easy as possible for his students.

I cannot recommend taking eternal families from him more. He is very understanding of the situations of the students and makes learning as early as possible. Have a super simple quiz at the end of each class, but most of the content is common sense if you read the reading. The reading before each class only took about 15 to 30 minutes.

Brother Mead cares about you. He wants to teach this class to help us all understand the topics talked about, and you can see that in his lectures. He did a fantastic job at explaining sensitive topics, knowing many struggle with them. He also makes it easy for you to succeed if you come to class and do the readings. Take it from him!!

Professor Mead is so caring and he really wants his students to succeed. He structures his class so that if you are in class, you don't have a final, and the hw is easy. There are readings before each class but you don't actually have to do them to understand. He is engaging and his lectures are interesting - my favorite religion professor so far!

Brother Mead is incredible!! Def one of my fav professors I've had at BYU. He works tirelessly so that the class is as uplifting and interactive as possible. He's extremely flexible, willing to meet when best for students, and his motive is truly for everyone to grow spiritually. The workload is perfect, requiring effort, but isn't overwhelming.

The most caring professor and really does teach by the spirit. I was going through a rough semester and he was very respectful and understanding. Overall he is easy and will strengthen your testimony .

I wish I could select every good attribute about Brother Mead because he is the best religion teacher EVER! I loved every second of his class! He is one who truly cares about testimony growth instead of busy work. There were readings for each class, a weekly self review, two projects and the easiest midterm and final ever. Take his class!
Great teacher. You learn a lot of difficult topics in this class and he addresses them all so well. Restoration Project is hard but not to bad if you work on it all semester.

Super easy class! You do 2 simple projects throughout the semester and have a midterm and a final. Brother Mead cares about his students and purposefully designs the class to be as student-friendly as possible. Great class, great professor!
A good class and the lectures were good. There was a fair amount of work to do for the class but if you do the work you will do well.

Brother Mead's class was awesome! You can tell he really cares about the topic of eternal families. The assignments are super easy and he helps you prepare for the midterm and final throughout the semester. He also makes the topics applicable to real-life situations.

Brother Mead really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He is very clear about expectations and super understanding. Some questions on the tests were dumb, but it was easy enough overall if you study the specific questions he has for each class. There was a significant amount of work outside of class, but probably pretty average.

Brother Mead is so amazing. His lectures were always inspiring. There is a lot of reading to be done before class which is the only thing I did not vibe with. He allows you to write short essays throughout the semester instead of taking the midterm and final and it's so worth it. He is not a harsh grader and really his intent is to help you.

Brian mead is one of the best professors I have ever had! His lectures are top-notch and spirit-driven. He tries to make the class as simple as possible. Very few projects and tests. He almost always has some alternative for anyone. Super approachable and just a down-to-earth guy! I am absolutely taking another one of his classes!!!

Great class! Brother Mead cares about each student and wants us to succeed. The class is set up where we do have a lot of reading, but the tests are relatively easy if you go to class and he gives lots of extra credit. I learned a lot from his class and recommend him as a professor that isn't difficult, yet you still learn from.

He is the best! He not only made me love the religion class, but he taught it in a way that was so easy to understand. It would be hard not to get an A in the class with how he has things set up. He is so kind and caring, and very accessible outside of class. Loved him!

The lectures are amazing and super clear. Cares about students. He is super fair and understanding. Easy grader, just do the assignments and you will be fine. You have the option of writing short essays or a multiple-choice exam for the midterm and final. I did the essays and it was easy. All in all an easy class but I feel like I learned a lot.

Brother Mead was amazing! I was worried about the final project when he announced it at the beginning of the semester, but it was surprisingly easy. I always felt the spirit during lectures, and you can tell Brother Mead loves each of his students and truly wants them to succeed. I definitely recommend taking eternal families from him!
He was wonderful! I loved his eternal families class. Very easy out of class assignments that never took me more than 30 minutes to complete. I would take any other class with him when able

I thought Prof Mead did a really good job teaching this class. I think the curriculum was pretty basic stuff, nothing too interesting but Prof Mead made it as interesting as possible. There is an attendance/what you learned quiz after every class, two big projects, and weekly assignments. No papers! Tests are not very hard.
Dr. Mead is a really great professor. I loved taking this class from him!
Really good professor! Down to earth and you can tell he wants you to succeed!

He talks to a lot of his student which is nice, but somehow it's also kind of hard to actually talk to him... I don't know how both of those things are possible, but that's what I've found. There is a lot of talking to your neighbor. Good class, fairly chill and doesn't stick out as being super memorable (good or bad) compared to my other classes.
He give great lectures and makes every topic engaging. Readings for homework can be kind of long, but if you go to class and do the homework, you'll get an A.

Favorite professor at BYU. There was readings before class that were easy if you listen at 2x speed. He remembered a lot about students personal lives - my wife and I took Eternal Families together and he got to know us really well. I learned a lot this class about the church and how to raise a better family. One of the easiest and best classes!

Love Brother Mead. Just *do* the assignments and you're golden. The way a religion class should be. Super awesome lectures and class, with some reading- might seem like a lot to others, but I just would read it on the way to class or on a Sunday and I was fine. Overall, great class. Would definitely take from Brother Mead again.

I cannot say enough good things about this class and about Brother Mead! The class content is great and is definitely in my top classes I've taken at BYU. You get what you put in for sure, but this class makes it easy to care. Brother Mead is super caring, very flexible, and you can tell he genuinely wants you to succeed! Take this class!!

Reading assignments twice a week which you can get done in less than 30 minutes listening to them using speechify.

2 projects the entire semester, interviewing couples and a final project.

He loves meeting with his students and is passionate.

Very amazing professor, take him if you can!

He's a great guy, but it's not worth it. Readings are longer than necessary, you have to do multiple projects that are pointless, and class is required but a waste of time. Most of it is super basic and he treats it like a seminary class, always wanting people to talk to neighbors. Didn't learn anything new. Waste of time. Sad that it's required.
Amazing professor, class is not difficult, just make sure you do the daily quiz thing. I learned so much more about eternal families.
This class is awesome!!! The hw is very easy and takes little time. It was also interesting and fun. I would fs take from him again

I enjoyed this class. Brother Mead is a professor who doesn't care much about memorizing small details but just wants you to understand the doctrine. He was open to discussions and discussed tough topics well. Tests were not difficult, and there was little work throughout the semester. Highly recommend!

Professor Mead is an incredible teacher who is really good at addressing doctrinal issues. He is very fair about his grading and the class's difficulty level is perfect for a 2 credit hour religion class. Would highly reccomend.

I love the feeling and atmosphere in Brother Mead's class. I feel respected no matter what opinion or questions I have. I was upset with his TAs though, because they would never explain why when they docked points here and there, and it wasn't clear.

Brian Mead's Eternal Families class is phenomenal. He's always cheerful and dynamic in lectures, also super reasonable and understanding when it comes to grades. His priority is certainly to teach an uplifting religion class at BYU, and he excels at it. Tests and assignments are very reasonable, and you just have to show up to get an A.

There is a lot of reading for this class, but it is so worth it! Brother Mead is absolutely amazing at explaining hard topics and helping students reach their full potential! I would definitely take this class again! There are two tests that took me 8 hours to complete and a couple projects. Other than that, it is attendance and reading!

Eternal Family is a very easy A. It is structured in a way that, although you should go to class, you don't need to. The tests are very easy and there are not many assignments. There is one easy assignment due after each class that takes 5-10 minutes and a weekly assignment that takes 10-20 minutes. Professor Mead is super caring and understanding.

He is such a great professor. He was very understanding and caring of the students. He talks about the family and views it from all sides which is very good. His lectures are very entertaining and the workload is pretty light. Take his class you won't regret it.

TAKE RELIGION WITH BRIAN MEAD!!! He is seriously one of the best professors I have ever had. His lessons are so interesting and he cares so much about his students. Every lecture is always so entertaining and its an easy A.  I would take him again and again.

I cannot say enough great things about Professor Mead. If you are struggling with your testimony, THIS IS THE CLASS TO TAKE! Professor Mead is not afraid to tackle church history topics. He is so caring and strives to create a relationship with each student. If you are looking to take 225, take it from him!!

He's good at teaching some of the more controversial topics. Attendance is graded, but self-reported. Post-class assignments that take 5-10 minutes, and an end-of-week assignment that takes about 30 minutes. End of semester project. For finals, it's a multiple choice question test or case-study option. Easy class, just didn't click w/ him.

Very good professor, the class setup and discussion is exactly what you want out of a REL course. However, and this may just be a personal preference, almost every 5 min, during every lecture, he has you discuss what he's lecturing about with the people next to you. Which is fine, just felt like a waste of time to me, but great if you're into it.

Brother Mead is by far my favorite religion professor I have had at BYU. I left his class every day so grateful I had attended. I was honestly hesitant to take this class, but he totally changed my perspective. His class was fairly easy and if you do the weekly reflections and participate you are very likely to get an A.

Brother Mead is a stud. He's a fantastic teacher and teaches the more sensitive subjects very well and with respect. I had no issues with him. He taught clearly, I felt the Spirit, and I didn't feel like this class was a huge burden. He knows a two credit hour religion class shouldn't be causing you any stress and he makes that clear.

Professor Mead is amazing!! I loved taking a class from him and signed up for another class with him! His lectures are amazing and you'll really learn a lot and feel the spirit. The readings are required for class, but it's not hard at all. He also lets you use notes on all of the quizzes! I would recommend everybody to take a course from him!

Brother Mead is an amazing man. His class is everything a religion class should be - inspiring and informative, with clear tests and assignments that actually deepen your learning, a classroom extremely open to discussion on difficult topics, and honest conversations about controversial events in church history through a lens of faith and reason.

Bro. Mead is 100% the BEST professor I've had at BYU. He is kind, funny, accessible, and very versed in the Gospel. You'll feel the Spirit, laugh, & make friends in every class. No busy work, every assignment actually helped me grow. Talks through difficult topics in Christ-centered way. Very open to questions/feedback. Gets to know you personally.
Brother Mead is so caring! He tries to get to know all his student's personally. He was always willing to help out with anything. He was very good at getting you to understand his lectures. Very Easy

Bro Mead has been my favorite religion teacher that I have had. His lectures were always uplifting and interesting. He took time to listen to and respond to questions. His tests were very reasonable and quite easy. It was easy to see that he cared about his students and wanted them to not only be successful in his class, but learn life lessons too.

I had Brother Mead for Foundations of the Restoration and absolutely loved him. Did a great job explaining all of the sensitive topics in Church history, and was extremely welcoming of all students and opinions. He also did a great job in encouraging us to ask questions about the material/gospel. Great job in grading as well. LGBT+ friendly as well

Brother Mead was an absolute blessing. He clearly cared about his students, was always willing to work through problems or questions, and taught us to seek further understanding on our own. I would highly recommend him and loved him, as well as this class, so much. He was incredible!

Brother Mead is so great.  He makes an effort to learn each students name and get to know them personally.  I took Foundations of the Restoration my first semester at BYU and I loved it.  I signed up for Eternal Families with him almost a year later and he remembered small details about me that I don't even remember telling him.  He truly cares.

Rarely do I have a class where I never look at the clock. Prof Mead was the exception. His lectures are awesome you can tell that he has a deep passion for what he does and the content that he teaches. He is extremely fair with grading. But come to class!! A lot of the things he emphasis are only found in class lectures.

I am currently writing this as I am still in his class. He is amazing. He cares so much about his students. He wants to know you individually. He is such a good teacher. He goes over a review of the week every lecture which is very helpful for test. His assignments are very very easy.

Prof. Mead was AMAZING. He was incredibly kind and really seemed to care about his students. He was able to explain hard and complicated gospel topics in a simple and respectful way. I learned SO MUCH from this class, and I want to take it again when I am married. Mead is an amazing professor, and knows his stuff about families and the gospel.

Brian Mead was a great professor. Taught difficult church concepts well and was open for questions that he either answered or was willing to answer after class. The majority of your grade is based on weekly check-ins. His tests are pretty easy and are all online. Finished with over 100% in the class.
Loved this class about Eternal Families. There is 1 assignment each week plus 2 easy reading quizzes. Plus a midterm and final that he curves. Mead is caring and smart.

Professor Mead is a great teacher. You can tell that he really cares about people and is very understanding of people's different difficult circumstances. The stuff that he has to teach can sometimes be sensitive subjects but he does a great job of teaching them.
I LOVED this class! I learned so much and he is so respectful. He will work with you if you need help, but his TA was not the best at getting back at emails. Definietly recommend this class.
Great professor

If you are interested in family and marriage, I highly recommend this class from Mead. He is super knowledgable about the church and its views. There are pre-lecture readings with a quiz online. The readings are normally talks or devotional and are pretty easy. There also are analysis essay at the end of week, 30 mins max.

Professor Mead is super caring. My only issue was that he never responded to emails, including time sensitive ones regarding an assignment. If he did respond, it took a while. He's not super accessible outside of class, unless you have his phone number. There was a lot of reading, but his lectures were pretty good.

Brother Mead is incredible. He's caring for the students and presents the topics in a way that promotes faith while not discounting those with questions. Provides ample time for in class discussion and will always take time to answer questions and listen to thoughts. Spectacular teacher and human being.

A student opened up about some personal struggles in class. The professor encouraged the student to tell the story and then reported them. The student is now facing expulsion. He is not a safe person to talk to.

Professor Mead is amazing. He is so kind, caring, and inspirational. I took this class summer term, and there was a lot of reading assigned. That being said, his expectations and grading criteria are clear. If your looking for amazing spiritual discussions and uplift, this is the class to take! Attending this class was the highlight of my day!

Brother Mead is an incredible professor. If you're taking Eternal Families, take it from him. Brother Mead teaches church doctrine as it stands now, not 50 years ago. He encourages discussion and wants his students to know how to seek answers and inspiration. He isn't afraid of having difficult discussions. This class is a testimony builder.

His class lectures are amazing very insightful and was very knowledgeable! The readings, final project, and weekly analysis projects sometimes take a bit of time, yet if you study hard for tests you'll be fine. Be sure to do all the extra credit that he gives out and do the final project as soon as possible.

I loved this professor! He made class fun while also teaching us all the things we needed to know. He seemed to really care about his students. either. There was a decent amount of reading to do, but I took it in the summer, so there would probably be less in a slower-paced semester. Would definitely take a class from him again!
Lots and lots of reading. Way more reading then I ever expected from a 2 credit class or a religion class. The only reason I wouldn't take him again is because of all the reading.

Definitely my favorite religion professor! He really cares about all of his students and it shows in the way he organizes the class and lectures. He covers difficult topics in a respectful manner and gets to know his students. He wants everyone to succeed in his class and is very understanding when life things come up.
My man Mead's background of working in departments in the Church means he has great insight into what Church leaders actually think.

If you want to understand the LGBTQ+ community better, please take him. He has background working for the church and explains things in the most amazing ways. He was really caring and explained everything very clearly and doctrinally based.

I liked Professor Mead. He was kind, and tried to make his lectures interesting and interactive. However, his grading system is out of wack. This was my last religion class, and the only one that I did not receive an A. I did ever single assignment and only missed once the whole semester. Only take this class if you are fine not getting an A!!!

There is a lot of writing papers, although the class is super easy to pass. Just do a bit of research into the assignment and then write about it. Definitely would recommend it again for this class. Great professor, he will give you bonus credit as well!

I liked him a lot for my religion class but beware, there are a lot of assignments. Two tests, a paper, and lots of reading each week at a minimum. He really does have great lectures and is passionate about the gospel, though. If you want a really in-depth class and don't mind the workload, go with him for sure. He cares about his students a lot.

He's fine. He is/was a seminary teacher. I think his wife's wealthy, or he comes from money, because they take awesome 5-* vacations. In either case, he tends to treat students like high-school students and wants to be "your friend."

Standard Religion class, read, apply, report. Not as interesting as I had hoped for the Articles of Faith. 7 Week course makes things a little frantic, but not unmanageable. Professor is good, gives feedback even if a little generic
Brother Mead is a great instructor and cares very much about his students learning to live Christ-centered lives. I would recommend him to anyone wondering which section to take.

Great online teacher. First few weeks there is a good amount of homework, but after that there is once a week posting in a group plus comments, an almost 600 word reflection, a small participation quiz and that is about it. Really personable and tries to post comments specific for you. Wants to get to know you. Recommended and will take again.

Brother Mead is an amazing online professor. Typically, you never hear from your online professors, but he provided feedback frequently and inspired me to learn as much as possible. He truly shows how much he cares about his students. Always offering extra help and going above and beyond to show you how much he cares about the topic, as well.

Great class for any type of student. Not a ton of work and is an easy A as long as you participate, but I also learned a lot and enjoyed the class. I love how the class is structured. Brother Mead was a great teacher. Would take this class again.

Not a bad class. A lot of reading, typical religion class; read write share discus reflect. Assignments are the same each week just with a different article of faith. Great way to grow your testimony of the restoration of the Gospel.

The class itself is not too complicated. Bro. Mead gives clear expectations, is available if you need him, grades papers timely, and has nice little additional inspirational things to post weekly. I highly recommend Bro. Mead. If you show up, and put a little effort into completing the assignments, you'll do well!

Brother Mead is a great online teacher. He leaves comments on almost every single assignment and responds back extremely quickly. The class was packed into the 7 week break so there was quite a bit to do, but the easiest religion (and funnest!) I've ever taken. TAKE IT!

I went to class a total of 5 times during the semester. The class was very easy because it covered much of the material I learned in CHEM 381, just less in depth. I would have liked to go to lecture more but was unfortunately not able. He was a good lecturer from what I saw though, and very kind and considerate.
Dr. Poole is great, he's really passionate about the subject which makes lectures interesting. Use the TA exam reviews and you'll do fine. Don't buy the textbook, you don't need it.

He's hilarious. The lectures are actually entertaining. Sometimes he's a little hard to follow though. He's tests are straight forward enough. The third one is definitely the hardest. But I would take his class again. Also his class is never actually 2 hours long.
Dr. Poole was great! He teaches clear and there's not much homework. He also gives lots of extra credit
Great teacher, I'd recommend finding a great study group. I personally didn't and didn't do super well in the class, but it's definitely possible.
Great Professor, very funny guy. I'd recommend a good study group for this class. I didn't have one and struggled a bit because of that, but I'd recommend this class to anyone.

Dr. Poole is the goat. His lectures are pretty entertaining. He is a funny and a kind of awkward guy. His tests aren't bad. The final was the easiest test of them all. He bases them off of the learning objectives so they are pretty easy to study for. He uploads videos of the lectures to Learning Suite. An A is very doable

I LOVED Dr. Poole. He made molecular biology engaging for me, he's super energetic and explains things so well, as well as records lectures. His tests aren't unpredictable, and homework is completion based. I would absolutely recommend Dr. Poole for anyone needing to take MMBIO 240.
Actually took him for Univ 101, best prof ever for that class. He's so kind and felt like he was really there for us, he made sure the workload was never too much/too annoying.

You don't have to go to lectures or read the textbook to do well in the class, but I recommend going to class because Professor Poole has the best lectures. You can tell he loves what he teaches about!

Dr. Poole is the best! This was one of my favorite classes by far, he made all of his lectures super engaging and easy to follow and explained difficult infection pathways clearly. He's very clear on what's on the final and what you're expected to know. He's also really funny. I wouldn't recommend skipping class because there's some vital stuff.

Dr. Poole is so epic. He is funny and entertaining. He has like no homework and all his slides have "Learning Objectives" and he only tests you on those. There is a super chill group project and that's pretty much it. Wish my Cell Bio class was like this.

Dr Poole is the only teacher you need to take for molecular biology. This is his bread and butter and he teaches it so well. Incredibly easy class because he covers the material so clearly. He's also absolutely hilarious. I heard so many nonchalant one-liners during the semester and his demonstrations are both entertaining and helpful.

This teacher is amazing. He offers literally every possible resource to help you succeed. He records every lecture so you can go back and watch it. He does completion homework to boost your grade. His tests are the nicest things ever and he offers literally so much extra credit. Your grade and learning is ENTIRELY up to you, which is awesome.

Dr. Poole is a funny guy who loves disease. It felt like MMBIO221 but easier. Two midterms and a final make up 60% of your grade, but he also gives some extra credit. One paper on a pathogen of your choosing, but overall, this class was very good, and I understand a lot more about disease.

He is so passionate about biology that makes you love his class. He gives time during lectures to ask questions and records them in case you miss them. Attendance is not required. He is easy to reach outside class during his office hours to go over content or answer questions, and offers extra credit. You should definitely take this class from him!

Super funny and passionate about biology. Pay attention to what he says in lectures and not just what's written on the slides, because he explains it better than the slides. Tests are straightforward and based on the learning objectives, so if you make sure you understand those, you'll be set. He provides a free pdf textbook but I never needed it.

Dr. Poole cares so much about his students. He tries his best to give everyone the best help possible and takes into consideration their personal circumstances. He's also very responsive when you have questions for him. My grade needed to be fixed, so I emailed him at 11pm and he responded within 6 minutes with the grade corrected.

Dr. Poole is awesome at explaining the concepts and his lectures are SO entertaining. He makes the learning objectives for each lecture clear and the test is based off them. The tests are most of your grade and you do need to study for them, but all the material is taught in class and nothing surprising. I can't recommend him enough!

Attend lectures and pay attention, you will do just fine in his class. He also has all of his lectures recorded, but it's better to come in person because if you have questions, he makes plenty of time for students to ask and clarify anything they don't understand. His tests are based on what he teaches and are acurate to what is discused in class.

Many students find Dr. Poole to be an engaging lecturer. He spends a large portion of class answering questions which can be annoying if you already understand the content/don't learn that way. Fortunately every lecture was recorded which was nice. All MC tests, not too bad, questions fairly based on objectives.

Professor Poole's lectures can be engaging, but the material is quite challenging. Rely on his sample tests and tools like Unstuck study alongside the textbook to succeed. Mandatory attendance helps, and the grading is reasonable if you put in the work.

Prof Poole is awesome. the material isn't always fun or entertaining but Poole has an amazing sense of humor that makes lectures enjoyable. there were 3 midterms and 3 papers and that was really all we got graded on. if you have to take 240, take it from Poole and no one else!

Pretty good class overall. A few "mini papers" that helped prepare for the exams, exams, and a group project. Daily quizzes to do before class that add up. Lectures were sometimes kind of confusing the first time through, but he usually records them for you to go back and watch. Reasonable amount of work. Know the practice exams inside and out.

Tests are worth a big portion of your grade but he gives you old tests from past years to study and basically uses the same questions. Didn't put in a ton of time and still managed an A. Take 240 from him!

Favorite professor at BYU. He cares about you understanding material & makes his lectures engaging. Never full 2 hours to go through material, doesn't feel rushed & allows as many questions as needed. Tests are very fair, he posts old tests up to review to prepare for upcoming tests. Extremely workable & will do whatever he can to help you succeed!

Dr. Poole was a really fun professor, but he was not super helpful outside of class. His tests are all reused from previous years, despite the textbook no longer being required. Questions were often confusing and about things that we never discussed in class. Really engaging and interesting lectures though!

Dr Poole is so unintentionally funny and it makes his lectures super engaging. The concepts are hard, but that's just how molecular biology is. No homework, but exams/papers are worth a ton of points. His learning objectives tell you what you need to know for the exam, and his sample exams follow pretty closely with the real exams so those help.

Dr. Poole is awesome. His test reviews are cool, cause he doesn't prep anything but can answer questions thrown at him. That being said, come prepared with questions! He takes the time DURING class to make sure everyone understands the concepts instead of rushing through like other teachers do. He has "mini papers" that are just regular papers.

Dr. Poole is a great professor. His tests go exactly with his slides and he wants students to succeed. Lectures can be hard to follow, but the general concepts are what he tests on. The class is VERY test-heavy but doable. Molecular biology is tough, but Poole made it enjoyable!

Dr. Poole is the MAN! 261 is straightforward. I hardly put any time in until it was time to take exams, and I headed into the final with a 100 (due in large part to the massive amount of extra credit he offers). The TA reviews were helpful and he provides practice exams for the midterms that helped a ton too. Super kind and an entertaining lecturer

Material was not hard at all, watching a few quick YouTube videos was enough to clear up any confusion I had. However, his lectures were often very confusing and very fast paced. LOTS of extra credit on exams, often curved up 4% on each one. Very, very caring guy but his lectures were just all over the place and hard to keep up with.

Super passionate and engaging during lectures! He makes it easy to succeed as long as you take notes and do good studying. 3 exams plus final, all in testing center multiple choice. 4 minipapers, one is a video. Records lectures to watch later. Has great practice tests!

Super chill class; no homework and no textbook or readings. You need to do well on the minipapers (there are 4) and exams (3) to do well in the class. He gives practice exams to study with that help a lot. There is a decent amount of memorization but you also have to be able to understand how the processes work to do well in the class.

Dr. Poole is really nice and you can tell that he puts in a lot of work to try and make his lectures engaging. However, his class is entirely lecture dependent, but his lectures are very confusing. His slides are reused so they don't make a lot of sense. Exams are heavily weighted. When studying for his exams, be prepared to teach yourself.

Dr. Poole is my most favorite professor I've ever had here at BYU. He is brilliant & hilarious and makes really challenging topics easy to learn. He uses a lot of demonstrations in class to teach challenging concepts. These concepts are taught mainly in the lectures and aren't on the slides so it's important to attend class. 10/10 would take again!
I am a senior at BYU. I took multiple of his classes. He was my favorite professor. If you have the opportunity to take him, do it! It is thanks to him that I learned how I studied. Great professor!

Prof Poole is such a fun professor and so intelligent! The class itself is pretty difficult though, which I didn't expect. Go to the TA help labs to study for the tests. Do well on the essays because it will help pad your grade. Don't make my mistake and think you can get away with studying just definitions of stuff, know the processes too.

Best and easiest class I've taken at BYU. Dr. Poole and Dr. Lane Fischer co-teach it (Poole teaches about different genetic disorders, Fischer teaches counseling skills). It's a fascinating class and the counseling skills are super helpful even if you don't become a genetic counselor. Absolute 15/10 class. I will recommend it to literally everyone

One of my favorite professors of all time. I've taken both molecular bio and infections&immunity from him and he is by far the best option for both. He's a very simple teacher, just know the slides and youre good! Also, im not one to care for teachers being funny but the dude has the driest humor and its hilarious. I tell all my friends to take him

Take this class from Dr. Poole. He is super funny and so knowledgeable. If you go to class, take good notes, and study well for the tests you'll do great. The tests are worth a lot of credit, but with little homework, there is a lot of room to study.  The textbook isn't needed.

I rented the textbook, and never read it. It may be useful if it's challenging for you. His exams are based on the objectives covered in lecture. He is super engaging and makes protein synthesis interesting and fun (a hard task). The minipapers are challenging to write but great tools for studying. I recommend studying the practice test/optional hw

I loved Professor Poole's class! It was so much fun and made me love learning about diseases! He teaches very clearly and his textbook is very easy to read. Homework is just reading a short textbook chapter and then doing an open-note quiz for each class. Super easy. His tests weren't too bad either, just require a lot of memorization.

The textbook is mandatory for quizzes and will provide lots of details necessary for the tests. He is an amazing instructor who makes lectures both entertaining and educational. This is my favorite class that I have taken at BYU.
He knows how to make learning about viruses fun. It's pretty straight forward, all exam questions will be on the slides and TA reviews were a big help. Really not to bad if you study.
Loved Doctor Poole. His tests require a good handle on the topics but they aren't too bad, very fair to what was taught in lectures. Review his practice tests before class and use the TAs!

Taught memorization and then tested on application. No study guide or clear testing guidelines or expectations.

Very smart man though.

The best professor for MMBIO 240. There are some really hard concepts but he taught things clearly! His key objectives/optional h.w. were a little disorganized, but one TA saved us with his test reviews. Tests cover a bit and are 75% of your grade so study in advance. Don't put off the mini papers and study the midterms before taking the final.

Dr. Poole is awesome! I loved lecture every week. He loves what he teaches and makes lecture interactive and hilarious. Tests are completely based off his lectures, which is nice because you don't have to read the textbook, but you must go to class. Your grade is based completely off of tests and minipapers. Use the practice tests to study!

While attendance wasn't required, all of the exam material comes from the lecture learning objectives. If you come to class and take good notes and study based on the learning objectives you will do well in the course. He doesn't use or require the textbook. But most importantly, he is such a fun and caring professor. He loves the stuff he teaches.

Really wants students to do well, very approachable, good test prep materials. Teaches difficult concepts well, and very interactive in class. Super good at answering questions and keeping students engaged. GO TO CLASS because he expounds on the limited info on his slides.

Dr. Poole is hilarious and explains everything really well. Sometimes it's hard to understand his slides because they're pretty sporadic but I got away with not studying until 1-2 days before the tests and they were all fairly easy A's. Pray that you have a good ta and memorize their test reviews, and you'll easily get an A.
This was an easy A as long as you read the learning objectives and follow along in the class. I enjoyed the class and Dr. Poole is such a gifted teacher!
Learned a lot about immunology and virology. Dr. Poole was very chill and its an easy A if you put in the work

Take this class from Dr. Poole! His tests are incredibly straightforward and literally come straight from the slides. His lectures are entertaining and informative. He takes a ton of questions that are kind of off-topic, so it can feel like he is wasting time. But that is the only downside. The class is easy but teaches everything you need to know.

Don't even hesitate if you have the chance to take his class. He's super funny, super understanding, and super knowledgeable. He explains things super well and answers all the questions people have. Very reasonable tests. The class isn't easy, but an A is totally doable. Just do the homework assignments, come to class, and study for exams.

Dr. Poole is phenomenal. Breaks down complex ideas and concepts and makes them understandable for any level of understanding. Would highly recommend him as he has been very accomodating with COVID and thorough.

Doctor Poole knows his subject really well but I feel he doesn't deliver it well. He posts his slides, but there isn't very much information on them so you can't really find answers to questions on them. He didn't give a lot of context on topics that we covered. He would just jump into a complicated process without explaining what we are learning.

Dr. Poole was a good professor for MMBIO 240. I had no idea what was going on the entire semester and I still passed. He changed his exams this past semester to be open book, note, internet, etc. Participation is not mandatory and the book is not needed at all. A few mini papers which aren't bad and surprisingly a decent amount of extra credit.
Dr. Poole was so FUNNY! His class would soar by so quickly! The tests were pretty simple and for us it was open notes. I never had to worry about my grade in this class and every lecture was a JOY!

Dr. Poole is a solid choice, his lectures are amazing and he is a very caring person. This class has a lot of material and the grading is heavily dependent on the tests, but there is no busy work or stupid assignments, you just have to study and understand the material and you will be fine! Dr. Poole is a great choice for MMBIO 240!!

Dr. Pool was great. He always spent time answering students' questions. This class was about 75% exams, 16% essays, and the rest were easy pre-class quizzes. If you aren't a strong test taker or writer, this class may not be for you. Tests are open-note, but they are semi-difficult. You have to work for your grade. Lots of extra credit.

The whole class was kind of meh. Super dry humor, but made class more interesting. He switched the exams halfway through the semester, which I felt made a disconnect between his lesson plans and content on the exams. But overall not a hard class to deal with. Don't bother going to lectures, all exams are open notes. Heavy weighted though

I can't say this enough times, but Dr. Poole is the BEST. He really cares that his students understand hard concepts, and has thought of cool ways to break them down/explain them. He is more than willing to answer questions in and outside of class and never makes you feel stupid for asking. He loves his job and his field, and will help you love bio

He likes the class to be discussion-based, which is great until there are specific students who like to ask a question every 5 minutes. Felt like we didn't finish the material for the day very often. He is great though, very knowledgeable and passionate. HW due after every class period, usually took me about 10-15 mins. Tests are not too bad.

Professor Poole was the best! He was super funny and taught really well. I understood the concepts and I didn't even have to read the textbook! He was super chill and cared about our learning more than assignments. Most of the assignments were to help us better understand material. He was one of the best teachers I've had and super easy.

Dr. Poole is very amazing and his lectures are very interesting. He does let anyone ask questions so some people may not like all the questions but just be respectful. You must study for this class, ask the TAs for help on confusing topics. Get a good study group and you should be great.

I can't say enough about Dr. Poole; he is an absolutely fabulous teacher. He is hilarious, straightforward, and very lecture-dependent. Know what's on his slides and what he says during class and you'll be fine. He hardly ever even references the textbook.

Dr. Poole is an amazing professor! He is what got me hooked on molecular biology. I can understand the subject and type of learning required may not be everyone's cup of tea, but Dr. Poole make it way easier with dad jokes, demonstrations, and straightforward multiple choice tests. He clearly knows a lot and cares about his students.
Dr Poole is my favorite professor. Hes a great teacher and is passionate about it. This class isnt too hard if you study well and go to lectures, you dont need the textbook at all.

Take this class from Dr. Poole! He is hilarious, and his tests are based on what is on his slides. Make sure to go to the TAs to get your minipapers checked before you turn them in, because they can be tricky. There is an extra credit paper at the end of the semester which can make up missed points and boost your grade up to 4%.

Fantastic teacher that actually makes learning enjoyable. I would take all of my course from him if I could. Your grade is pretty much just the tests, but that's fine as long as you pay attention in class. You definitely will need to study, but Dr. Poole makes it worth it.

Dr. Poole has engaging lectures. The tests are challenging but not impossibly hard if you study and go to TA reviews and such. My only complaint is that in mmbio 261 the TA's don't have office hours to go over hw before submitting and dr. poole's demeanor when you visit him in his office with questions can make you feel like you're asking dumb Q's.

Dr. Poole was a great Professor for this class. 3 tests and a final that are pretty straightforward. He wont try and trick you and make them difficult. Homework is optional. 3 mini papers that you basically get most of the points for if you just get it done. His lectures are funny and very helpful in simplifying things.

Dr. Poole is an entertaining professor who loves what he does. He is great at answering questions and a well-rounded professor. His TA's are extremely unmotivated, but I would recommend this class to anyone who loved biology.

Dr. Poole is the best, and is the funniest biology professor I have had. He genuinely cares about his students and makes molecular biology easy to understand. If you have the chance definitely take it from Poole. His tests are straightforward and he provides past tests to help study from.

Dr. Poole likes to involve his students in learning and makes the material pretty easy to understand. Tests weren't bad, but ask him to post an old test to help you study, that's the best study guide. He has an online book that has homework questions. He wrote most of the book so it matches lecture and is very helpful.

Professor Poole is an amazing professor! He really loves what he teaches and does a lot of really funny demonstrations to help the class understand difficult concepts. The textbook is not required, you know everything you need for the test by attending lectures. There are only 3 tests, 3 papers, and the final and that's your grade.

Prof. Poole is one of the most amazing professors at BYU. His lectures make even the hardest subjects easy to understand. He cares about his students, answers questions clearly in class, and is absolutely hilarious. He made this class enjoyable, helped me love the subject, and helped me learn a lot. He is also very accessible outside of class.

He is a fantastic teacher. He goes the extra mile to teach concepts in class in really easy ways. Whenever other bio teachers subbed in for him nothing made sense, but he was great. A lot of memorization for tests but they're not hard. He let the class do an extra credit paper when people did poorly on one of the tests. He cares about his students.

Dr. Poole made me love molecular. He never writes on the board but gives you his slides- personally that worked for me. Lets you ask ALL questions in class. He is HILARIOUS. Has 4 tests and a few research papers.

It's pretty clear what's expected of you. There are online homeworks on the reading every week (I went to the TA lab for most of them), three midterms, and three mini papers. He even lets you retake a midterm. This class was difficult for me, but if you put in the work it's very doable.

Dr Poole is so funny! His tests aren't too hard and he makes molecular biology entertaining (which is not an easy task). He has the most forgiving grading scheme on the planet (you can retake 1 midterm). You will have to write 3 short papers, but they help you study if you do it right. He's great, I loved his class, even though biology is the worst

NOT an easy A class! graded on HW assignments, a research paper, 2 exams and a final. 1 extra credit paper. Average on midterms was a mid C for both. 25% of class dropped after first exam. Hard to study for exams. Only study material is his class slides which are very vague; topic bullet points which he then talks about. Need to take notes!!

Dr. Poole is a good guy that loves the subject but the class is not super organized. The exams were fair but the homeworks were really challenging at the beginning of the semester. He made changes through the semester but it was still not my favorite class.

I LOVE Dr. Poole. I am passionate about this topic, and having a professor who is passionate and has a great command of the class was great! He makes great visuals in class. I recommend printing out his slides and using them to make additional notes so you can write down his visuals and other helpful things. Very straight forward testing & grading.

I didn't really care for this class. He's super funny and sometimes his let's are really funny and participation heavy wish is nice, but I found myself heavily relying on the TA review. There's also 3 mini papers you'll have to write. They aren't so mini.

FUNNY. A great lecturer w/fun demonstrations. Grade is mostly about tests, but know the learning objectives well & you'll be fine. 3 tests+final, 3 mini papers, online HW due before class(read the textbook for these. otherwise you'll fail them). Take good notes about things NOT on slides, & see TAs/him for any clarification. TAKE IT FROM HIM!

Dr. Poole is really funny, but they way he ran his class it was near impossible for me to succeed. The readings and lectures cover hundreds of different concepts, but the exam will focus on a tiny fraction of those concepts that are super detailed. So the only way to pass is to know everything and more. Almost entire grade based on exam scores.

Dr. Poole knows what he is talking about and presents the material in an engaging way. For the Honors 220 class that he teaches he had a great chemistry with Dr. Cutchins. Sometimes the grading was a bit unclear and usually it took a while for them to grade tests and papers. Makes you think and exposes you to a lot of diverse opinions.

He's the best teacher and if you don't take MMBIO 240 from him you are doing it wrong!! Gave very entertaining lectures and was super personable. He knows what he's talking about and really good at helping his class to understand. As long as you memorize everything on his powerpoints and his lectures, you'll ace the class.
Dr. Poole is great! He is a really good teacher. Make sure you ask questions in class when you don't understand something. His TAs are kind of useless unfortunately.

Dr. Poole is an amazing professor who obviously knows his stuff. MMBIO 261 is all memorization and if you pay attention in class and memorize his Powerpoint slides, you will do fine. He is funny and engaging and tries his best to make the material interesting.

Dr. Poole is awesome! He is one of my favorite professors at BYU. His tests can be difficult but he gives you extra credit and a chance to redo one of his midterms, so it is very possible to get an A in his class. He is also hilarious. Make sure to go to lectures. Most test questions come from his lectures and his P.P.s can be hard to follow.

Dr. Poole is an amazing teacher. He simplifies difficult concepts and relates material together. Gives great rants about vitamin C, essential oils, and vaccination. Loves his subject which makes the material easier to learn. Daily readings, a few essays. Everything was straightforward. Great class with great professors. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

Dr. Poole is hilarious. I laughed a lot. His powerpoint slides were basically just topics he wanted to teach us about and a list of exactly what he was going to ask on the test, so I would recommend looking at those, and going to class to listen to the answers. I never used the textbook, taking notes in class was sufficient.

I seriously love Dr. Poole. He is the absolute best. His classes are easy if you go to class and study. I enjoyed 240 more than 261, but that is just personal preference. He is super caring and funny. He doesn't quite appreciate the greatness of the Prequels, but loves Star Wars, and that makes him cool. Everyone needs to take one class from him.

Dr. Poole really changed my perspective about Biology. Hands down to the best Professor ever! Three midterms and a final. Also, a paper due the end of the semester. Take this class from him. You won't regret.

Great guy! He is very down to earth and willing to help students succeed if they put in the effort. Class is difficult and the material can be confusing, but he is willing to work with the students for the grade they deserve.

Dr. Poole is the best! My grade went up 5% just from his extra credit. Don't get the textbook, you'll be tested off of specific material from the slides and problems he does in class. Attendance is essential. The TAs gave helpful reviews and that's where I learned most of the info that was on the exams. I wouldn't take this class from anyone else.

This class was team taught by Dr. Poole and Dr. Cutchins (from the English department). He's brilliant and has a great sense of humor. Being a general education class, he kept the biology portion at a pretty basic level, but it was very interesting and tied into the humanities portion surprisingly well. I really enjoyed his class.
