The book didn't help much, but the tests were mostly lecture based. Go to class and you'll be fine, just don't forget to submit the homework.

Dr. Poole is the best! He is very straight forward on his tests and tells you exactly what you need to study. You DON'T need to buy the text book, everything you need will be on his slides. He gives lots of opportunities for extra credit. Hands down the best 240 teacher!!

Dr. Poole is the best, take any class you can from him. I found him very funny, he has a nerdy/dry sense of humor. Straightforward class with 2 midterms, final, weekly homeworks, and a paper that is graded very leniently. Definitely need to study for his tests but there are no surprises, just put in the time.

Poole's great. HILARIOUS guy too. Not an easy A but if you put in the studying you can definitely get one. Don't buy the textbook. Tests (4) are based on his slides. Would make a point of going to class and taking notes. Slides are vague. Does give out like 4% points worth of extra credit. One easy paper. Homework easily graded. Highly recommend!

Dr. Poole is my favorite MMBio professor of all time!!!!! Seriously take at least one class from him. 261 was an amazing class, and even though I had to take a not ideal time for MMbio 240, I would never have taken 240 from anyone else. He makes it so interesting, and his easy to follow PowerPoints keep it clear. Not to mention he is HILARIOUS!

Dr. Poole was AWESOME!! Seriously one of my favorite biology teachers that I have taken so far! He is very fair with grading and genuinely cares that his students are learning! He always answers everyone's questions in class! Super nice guy that loves what he does! If you are going to take MMBIO 240, take it from HIM!!

Dr. Poole is a good teacher if you are ready to hit the ground running to learn mmbio. There is no required textbook for the class so it's hard to learn and you are expected to know a lot before class. If you are willing to put in the work to learn, he's great, otherwise, if you don't know anything like me, you will struggle.

Dr. Poole is easily the best professor I've had so far at BYU. He's very engaging, he has hilarious demonstrations, and he always answers every question. Literally the best. Word of warning though: most of his TA's don't like to answer your questions, explain things to you, or interact with you in any way. Just talk to Dr. P if you need anything

Taking Poole's 240 class actually was the reason I switched my major to Microbiology. Tests and homework was very reasonable. He is a funny and very intelligent man. Some of the things he taught were difficult concepts and he taught them with ease and simplicity. I liked forward to every lecture. Would take again and again!

I LOVED Dr. Poole. Don't get the textbookjust follow along on the slideshow and write down anything he says that isn't on the slides. Requires a fair bit of study and memorization, but that's just 240 for ya. Solid extra credit options. He's also hilarious. Definitely the best choice for this class.

Dr. Poole is probably one of the best professors a BYU. Take any class you can from him. His grading criteria is clear. The class is very interesting and he answers almost all questions. Tests are based off of the slides, but content clarification comes form lectures. Make sure you take good notes. The final is the easiest of the tests. Ex credit.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He is hilarious, makes class interesting, and I've literally never seen him skip anyone's question. He answers all questions that the class asks. He explains things well. Don't buy the textbook.

Easy weekly quizzes due before class. 3 tests and a final. Final is comprehensive, but by far the easiest. Tests focus on small details in the slides. MEMORIZE THE SLIDES. One paper due near the end-- long but fairly easy. Funny, dry guy. Great at giving examples.

MMBIO isn't a super interesting class but professor poole tries to make it better. Unlike most science teachers he isn't trying to fail you or make you life hard. I feel like I got the same grade on every test no matter how much I studied so I wasn't sure what change.. In the end though he really is on your side and you will do alright in the class

Dr. Poole was great! My only thing against the class was that the third midterm was crazy hard in comparison to the first two. This was annoying because you think you know how to study for his test, then all of a sudden you have a randomly crazy hard test. That said, Each midterm progressively gets trickier. However, the final was not bad at all.

Dr. Poole is one of the best microbiology teachers on campus. Very funny guy.  He is very straightforward about what is on tests, so in that sense its not difficult. He responds quickly to emails if you have questions.  I wouldn't buy the textbook. I will take him again.

By far one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He is so intelligent and teaches difficult concepts so well, often with visual and object demonstrations. Tests are straight forward and he really has the student's best interest in mind. Take MMBIO from him if you can, you won't regret it. I, myself, will be looking for other classes he teaches.

Dr. Poole is by far the best professor to take mmbio240 from. His tests are straightforward, and he gives you a detailed list of what to study for each chapter. He does a great job of trying to keep things interesting. Sets aside a lot of time for questions and additional discussion as well, and can answer just about any question you throw at him.
Dr. Poole is a fun teacher to take. His tests are all based off of his lectures and powerpoint so don't buy the textbook.

Dr. Poole is fantastic. He is a great lecturer and really cares about his students. He wants you to know the material and succeed and is willing to adapt. His tests come from his lecture slides, so know those and you're set.

Dr. Poole is a great choice for this class. Here's what you can expect: - Homework (5 questions) twice a week - 2 midterms and a final - 1 simple paper You likely won't use the textbook. He tests you on his slides AND the things he says during lecture, so you have to pay attention. Download his slides before, follow along and write extra info down.

I didn't really need the textbook because he teaches everything in class.  With that being said, I took him for both mmbio 240 and mmbio 261. You want to pay attention in class because some things you won't find on the slides despite him saying everything comes from the slides. Not a hard class, just listen and he offers extra credit.  TAKE HIM
This guy is awesome.  He is a good teacher, and only tests you on what he teaches you.  If you are willing to study, getting an A shouldn't be a problem!

Dr. Poole is just great. He understands what he is teaching and can explain it in a clear, simple manner. However, he spits out a lot of information in one lecture, so pay attention and record the lectures. I would definitely take his class again.

Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll want to go anyway. Super amazing and often hilarious classes. I loved 240 and 261 from him. I think everyone should take them both. Such a knowledgeable, funny guy. It's easy to be engaged and excited about the material. I feel like now I'm done with his classes I'm done with the best the college has to offer!

Dr. Poole teaches very clearly and is very willing to answer questions in lecture. He seems to prefer questions. He enjoys teaching the subject. The material does get pretty detailed so be prepared. You will definitely want to do the homework, both for the grade and how much the questions reflect the tests.

You cannot possibly go wrong with Dr. Poole. He teaches you everything you need to know and nothing else. The exams are extremely fair and rarely have any curve balls. The final exam is also extremely easy. Clear expectations, hilarious, and very informative. Take MmBio 240 from him!!! You won't even open the textbook, just buy the online code!
Dr. Poole is the man. I'd take all my bio classes from him if possible, because 1) he explains things so well and 2) he sounds like Patrick from Spongebob. Enough said.

Only teaches this class winter semester. Offers extra credit on each test. He makes MMBio interesting and spices up lectures with humor. I don't like biology at all but I liked this class. If you know the slides and go to a TA review the tests will not be hard. Definitely the best MMBio teacher at BYU.

I took MMBIO 240 previously at BYU, and the structure of the class was so inconsistent and the homework system so flawed that it made the class impossible. I retook the class years later from Poole. Night and day different. His lectures are engaging, his grading is clear and fair, and he offers help where he can. certainly a good choice.

Dr. Poole has really fun lectures and makes them interesting and hilarious. He really makes you love viruses and bacteria more than you should. However, it is a hard class and you need to put in effort, not because Dr. Poole is a hard teacher, but just because of the nature of the class.

The Powerpoints are no joke. If you know them and the homework questions you will get an A.  There is one paper but it isn't bad. The class material is really dry so he tries to spice it up. Best/easiest MMBIO 240 at BYU

Dr. Poole is one of my top 3 professors I've taken a class from. He's super smart but doesn't treat you condescendingly. He's funny and makes lectures interesting. If class is slow it's because people are asking questions for the sake of asking a question. Dr. Poole gives reasonable work and his tests are fair.

Dr. Poole is a genuinely funny man. He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter, and his TA's actually know what they're talking about, for the most part. The objectives do a great job of setting the expectations for the lectures and tests, and the content of the class was very interesting.
He is an awesome professor. He makes a hard concept simple. I recommend anyone to take molecular biology from him.

Dr. Poole is the best professor! Just go to class and take notes... do the homework (it's not hard) and study for the tests and you'll get an easy A. The final is super easy as are all of the other tests. He's hilarious and sooo easy to listen to.

Honestly I feel like Dr Poole would be a better high school professor. In my opinion he doesn't respect our time in class. People seem to like his jokes, but they lower his credibility in my opinion. The homework is pretty simple and the tests seem okay.

Dr. Poole is the man.  Totally fair, teaches you what is necessary, tells you what you don't need to know.  Review the slides, take good notes of what he says in class. KNOW the homework before the test and you are golden. Dr. Poole is great!
Some tests are manageable, but others are so over-the-top hard that there is no real way of knowing what you will be tested on. The TAs almost never gave reviews, so you're on your own.

I was scared of this class but it is actually super manageable. If you listen and take notes in class on the stuff that he says that's NOT on the slides, and then later combine that with the slides into the objectives, you're golden for exams. Dr. Poole also comes up with a lot of demonstrations that help explain and reinforce difficult concepts.

Dr. Poole is very dry and a little boring, but his class is really interesting and the tests arent very hard. He has objectives after each lecture that he makes the tests out of. So if you understand on the objectives the you will do  just fine on the tests. I would recommend his class to anyone.

Dr. Poole is amazing! He is super funny and makes learning the material so much fun, yes, fun! He is a pretty easy grader, but you will have to work for your grade. Test have everything to do with what you learned in class, not tricks, just learn the material!

This professor is hilarious! His class is manageable as well. There is not too much material to cover, so he takes the time to really discuss the "ins and outs" of molecular biology. Based on discussions that I had with students that took different professors for MMBIO240, I learned that Brian Poole is by far the funniest, easiest, and best around
Wonderful teacher; VERY easy grader. However, due to certain issues he freaks out over tiny things, like reminding him about an error in the gradebook.
Dr. Poole is the best teacher for MmBio 240. He makes it interesting and teaches it very clearly and the test is a good representation of material covered.

Dr. Poole is just the best! His exams are totally reasonable. It's just like everyone else is saying-study the slides and objectives and pay attention to the little things he says in lecture, study hard, and you'll do great! Very straightforward. :) He is very helpful if you have questions. Keeps class entertaining and teaches things well!

Loved this class, informative and great! Study the slides and understand any concept he talks about in class. I never bought a book, but you will need to get ahold of one just to do the quizes. He's funny in a dry humor sort of way but a relaxed and nice professor. Study hard for all the exams and you will be fine!

Dr. Poole is awesome. He is a little quirky, but kept class entertaining and his tests were very reasonable, you knew exactly what to expect. As some advice, don't buy the textbook. Just use one at the Life Science learning center to do the quizzes and save yourself over 100 bucks. Oh ya, and lots of extra credit! Take Dr. Poole!!

He has a dry sense of humor and is a very likable guy. The book was way too detailed to be worth the time. Tests weren't too bad--the final was not cumulative! I just watched youtube during the student presentations. You basically just need to read the abstracts of those papers before the tests. I slept through my own group's presentation.

Take MMBIO 240 from him! He explains difficult concepts in a way that is easy to understand. He keeps class interesting with his nerdy but funny personality. He is also REALLY easy to work with. Don't be afraid to talk to him for any reason. Awesome teacher.

Dr. Poole is great.  He did his best to make learning the info as easy as possible.  The tests were very fair.  He teaches very clearly and his lectures are entertaining.  I'm way glad I took MMbio from Poole.  Highly recommended.

Dr. Poole is literally the best. He is one of the most approachable teachers you have ever met. He was more than willing to help and answer all questions, take personal time to talk with students, and is just a stand up guy in general. The tests were tough, you had to study hard, but he gives you all the information you need. Enjoyable lectures.

Dr. Poole is one of the best professors at BYU. He is very intelligent and very funny.  His class is very do-able and he makes sure the class understands concepts before he moves on.  Lots of demonstrations. Hard exams but straightforward, just need to study hard.  He genuinely cares about his students.
Great professor!  His explanations make perfect sense and his tests are straight forward.

Dr Poole is the best choice for MMBio240. He is a great guy that is excellent at explaining difficult topics and he gives you absolutely everything you need to ace the test. If you fill out the objectives, and attend reviews, he tells you absolutely everything you need to know for tests and doesn't try to trick you at all. He wants you to do well.

Great professor! Has a sense of dry humor that he slips here and there to make things interesting. Filling out the objective sheets are critical - if you know what's on them, you should do fine on the test. Also has demonstrations that really help with understanding the concepts. Always wants the class to do well.

Dr. Poole (aka Chance Daily) is awesome.  His tests are pretty hard, but he really wants the class to do well.  Also he is hilarious.  If you focus on learning the objectives that he posts every week, you'll do fine.

He's dry as the desert, but still cracks jokes related to the subject matter. I tutor students from his MMBio 240 classes. There are plenty of resources for you. I love Dr. Poole & his classes! He is a great teacher & a great man.

Dr. Poole is rad, I liked class progressively more each time I came. Expect quizzes every mon/wed. Tests are really clear if you know how to set up an experiment. Ask questions about things you find interesting that are somewhat relative to the topic, he loves it when the class actively participates. and he brings in object lessons regularly.

Class was pretty difficult.  He does post slides before class.  I suggest printing those off and writing notes on them during lecture.  Test could be a little ridiculous.  Yes, he compensates grades depending on how the class did, but it just gets frustrating studying for them.  Dr. Poole is a nice guy, but his class is harder than it has to be.

Great professor! First time teaching the class, did a great job. First test was easy, the second one was hard, but gave everyone 15 points(yes 15)to makeup for it. He is quite nerdy, but loves the subject. His voice can get dull, but you get used to it. Tests are 15 MC and written (short ans,essay) Homework is 5ish questions from reading, open book

Dr. Price really knows literature and how to make it relevant/engaging for students! The one hard thing in the class is that he asks a lot of writing (in Spanish ofc), but he doesn't grade it hard; he just wants you to write to get the experience and practice. Class lectures are super fun and he is super passionate about teaching and the subject.

He is very passionate about the material, which is a huge game changer because most days I came into class without any desire to talk about it. He is super funny and keeps things light. He believes in writing, so prepare to write often. Do not procrastinate your Anthology project!

He was absolutely amazing and made the literature so much fun. We would dive into the stories and he was a very fair grader on all the assignments. The anthology is a BEAST of an assignment, so don't procrastinate it like I did, but he wants you to succeed. He also makes the BEST TACOS

Best decision I ever made was taking Spanish literature from Professor Price. I used to hate reading in Spanish. Thanks to his passionate, interesting, and incredibly well-informed lectures, I now LOVE the subject. His assignments are thoughtful and help you grow your passion for critical thinking and cultural appreciation. Not crazy hard at all.

Super entertaining lectures! Very passionate about what he teaches. A lot of writing in spanish. Sometimes expectations are unclear, and he doesn't give feedback on your writing or grade promptly so it feels a bit like busy work. The semester project is a beast, but he's willing to help with it. Tests aren't hard (he made us tacos for the final)!

Prof Price is really easy to listen to. The guy knows his stuff and is clearly passionate about it. For the most part, I'm not interested in span lit, but he makes it interesting and makes it make sense. Doing well in this class is extremely easy. There's a few small papers and one bigger project and that's pretty much it. Highly recommend.
Great professor very fun and learned a lot!

Dr. Price is awesome and is clearly passionate about what he teaches. He doesn't require a ton of homework, and it's really easy to do well on as long as you do it not at the last second. Probably the best person you could take 355 from, and I'm planning on taking another class from him. He cares about his students too. He's great.

Dr. Price is so funny! The class is definitely more humanities based. You will have to do a lot of writing in this class. There were four big projects worth only ten points each that made up 70% of your grade. Some short like a page but others like 6 pages. If you can write in Spanish you'll get an A. He's so passionate it makes the class fun.

I took Span 330 from him and I really enjoyed his class. He teaches really well and keeps the lectures very entertaining. He had 2 small books he made us read but it wasn't that bad. If you pay attention in class and do the readings, you'll be completely fine!

He's a teacher who really cares about his subject. He assigns A LOT of reading, but it is mostly interesting and fun information. His lectures are super entertaining, and he is awesome to talk with. If you're really interested in the subject and want a hilarious professor, he's your man.

Very much has favorites. If you LOVE literature and if he likes your ideas, you'll love this class, and quickly become one of his favorites. If you're not the academic type, avoid this class. He is a fairly merciful grader though.

Amazing professor and is a reasonable grader. I received some tough feedback on an assignment this semester but he was 100% willing to work with me to get it to a good point. Cares about his students and is extremely in tune with the class needs. Willing to change things up if needed. Could not recommend him enough-take him if you can! A+++++++++++

So he assigned something like 7 texbooks to read and tons of movies and albums to "consume". I didnt read any textbook, i watched the movies and touched on the songs. The lectures are good, and overall I feel like the class was really fun and a blessing. We had a lot of papers to write but he also said he regretted giving us so much homework.

I took Spanish 461 from Dr. Price and now recommend it to all of my Spanish-speaking friends. Dr. Price's knowledge and passion for Mexican-American lit is contagious, and I looked forward to every class period. The reading was never too much and the books were all captivating. Dr. Price is very opened minded. Favorite class I've taken at BYU.

THERE IS SO MUCH READING. You have been warned. He is a very "woke" professor and he is super fun. But tons of reading with not a ton of knowledge about what we need to know and what we are just reading because it is interesting. If you are a slow reader don't take this from him.

Professor Price was disorganized from the beginning of the semester. It was hard to know what he expected on assignments because his instructions where either unclear or nonexistent. There were not a lot of assignments, but the ones we did have were heavily graded. Studying will not help your grade, assignments are subject to the teacher.

He is by far my favorite professor. Do not believe anything negative people say about him, he is AMAZING!! He is so hilarious he will have you crying every class period, and has such a deep passion for Latin American Culture. He knows it so well, and does a great job teaching it and making you have passion for it as well. Highly Recommend!!

He's well read in Latin American studies, but he was so dogmatic (while he encouraged "cognative dissonance"). He took time to talk with me outside of class because his lectures bothered me so I respected that, but his aim seemed to be to attack European culture and history rather than focus on facts or teach an unbiased history of Latin America.

Dr. Price is funny, but unclear. I found his class frustrating because he waited until a couple of days before the due date to post assignment information. He is a slow grader, and his essay (12% of grade) rubric says 8/10 is a superior, so it's a HUGE hit for just a few errors. I don't feel like I learned much, and the tests cover obscure topics.

Dr. Price was fantastic! His lectures are hilarious and insightful. The projects and movies were beneficial to the learning experience. If you are planning on taking 355, this is the best professor to take it from. My most entertaining professor here at BYU thus far, by far.

Professor Price is the funniest professor I've had. His lectures keep you on your toes and are always interesting. He gets off on tangents frequently but they usually apply somehow to what the subject is. Some students claim he is edgy and makes you watch terrible things but I saw nothing wrong with what he said or had us watch. Would recommend!

Super enthusiastic about this subject, and it catches. It was a fun and interesting class, awesome material and fun on-the-side projects. The movies were worth watching and open your eyes to a lot of other cultures. Most grading is easy, I had almost 100% the whole semester BUT he totally got me on the final and ended up with an A-. STUDY FOR FINAL

Dr. Price is the best! He loves this subject so much and wants his students to as well. There was plenty of reading and watching movies, but it's interesting and when it comes to grading it was mostly on participation. Can definitely get an A and you'll have a ton of fun doing it, and learn so much about Latin America. Loved the required movies.

Price is an awesome guy, some may not like his humor but I love it. There is a lot of reading in this class, I recommend creating a Google Doc with friends to share the load. The movies we watched were worth it. This class was a lot of fun and honestly the papers are not bad. He will help you and loves feedback. One of the most entretenido classes.

Profe Price is a nice guy but this course was terrible. Homework took 9 hours a week, even though we met as a class three times a week. He expects you to read the whole book plus a bunch of extra reading assignments he gives links to online AND a bunch of videos and movies that last anywhere from 1 hour to 3 hours.  Take from someone else!

Dr. Price is solid. He loves his subject and is knowledgeable about it. His classes are interesting, informative, and even funny sometimes. He is very clear about what will be on the tests, so if you are willing to put in the effort to prepare you will do well. The one tough thing about this class is there is a ton of reading homework.

Dr. Price was a good professor. He's very passionate about what he teaches and wants to give this to his students so they see the world through new eyes. Sometimes his movie choices are inappropriate, & he does give a lot of homework, but if you do it and go to class every day you'll get a good grade in the class. Overall, I liked the class a lot.

I thought the topic of the class was extremely interesting. The professor ruined the course though. He gave  way too many assignments for this class to be worth it. Get ready for tests, readings, a long research paper, many long movies, and assignments to attend different events and activities. If you have lots of extra time then take this class.

Brian Price was easily my favorite Spanish professor I've had at BYU and was one of my favorite professors from BYU overall. He is a very good lecturer and has a real passion for the subject matter. I genuinely enjoyed the class. His tests and papers are graded very fairly and he wants you to succeed. Also a funny/entertaining guy

I took univ 101 from Professor Roberts; it was truly a joy to be in class with him when I was I think Professor Roberts is a fantastic teacher and person, and it truly shocks me how much he touched my life in the short semester I had with him.

Professor Roberts was remarkably kind. He loves what he teaches, as dry as it may be at times. This class is very heavy reading, but the study guides will save you. He is one of few teachers that has political bias and actually grades impartially. He is focused on helping students achieve and think deeply.
Professor Roberts gives great lectures. He is very clear about expectations, and is more than willing to go over tests with you to help you improve for the next one.

Dr. Roberts makes you work for a grade, but works with you for that grade. There's a lot of work, but it has a point. Tests are hard, but he grades fair and gives great feedback. If you're engaged in the homework and lectures, you can thrive in the class, and he will magnify all aspects of your education.

Lots of reading, but that's really the only homework. You report your reading every day in class. No reading quizzes. 3 tests with 10 multiple-choice questions, 15 quote identifications, and 1 essay (which isn't hard if you prepare). He grades the 2 essays pretty hard, but gives great feedback. Meet with him outside class for help on the essays.

Professor Roberts is great! The class is interesting and thought provoking and I always left class wishing we had more time to continue our discussions. Roberts is so smart, very articulate and and all around great guy! Highly reccomend!

I took this class last semester but I still refer to the material often--it's so wide-ranging and relevant. Dr. Roberts is an articulate, caring teacher, very respectful of his students' thoughts.  There was a great class atmosphere, fascinating analysis of ideas, and generous encouragement.  I had a great experience.

I never write reviews, but I had to write this one to spare some poor soul. Roberts is nice, but his class is the most miserable class every.  His tests are ridiculously hard and don't test on what you learn in class, forcing you to memorize. Lectures are boring and HW is rough. I do not feel like he added to my education in ANY way.

Dr. Roberts is the best teacher I've had at BYU so far. The reading material he selects is fascinating and he leads great discussions in class. His points are clear, so you know exactly what to expect on the test. Dr. Roberts really cares about his students and his class was my favorite!

Professor Roberts has been my favorite professor at BYU. I love everything about his 293 class - the reading assignments are great and pretty much the only hw, tests are take-home and reasonable, class discussion is stimulating, and the environment is super fun! Professor Roberts cares for each of his students and his class is REALLY GOOD.

I loved his teaching style! He was very clear with his expectations. He gives you just the right amount of work. He tries to incorporate class activities and discussion into his lectures. He's brilliant and not condescending at all. I recommend him 100%!

Great teacher and not intimidating at all, which is great. If you're interested in learning, you will with this guy. He has great points, but doesn't feel the need to prove his intelligence like I think some professors do, so what you learn is good stuff you can remember. Tests are easy if you learn the review sheet. He's also very funny.

Brian Roberts is a very relaxed professor. I enjoyed the class because it was engaging, but not elitist. He knows what he's talking about, and if you are willing to be an active learner, you'll have a good time in class. He allows for class participation while keeping the discussion from straying from intelligent analysis.

I loved this class-and I was dreading it. Power points were well organized and helpful. Class discussions were thought-provoking and informative. I will definitely try to take another class from Prof. Roberts.

His class discussions sometimes go over my head. It feels like a few students carry the discussion, and he assumes the rest of us know what he's talking about. Still, he's a funny guy, and if you do the reading you'll be okay. Very well-organized class, and he knows what he's talking about!

I was hoping for an easy Eng class and it was, but it was also fun and interesting--I could have gotten away with less thought and effort but Prof. Roberts, and the literature, made me want to put more into it and I ended up getting a lot out of it.

This was a fantastic class. I'm not a huge fan of American literature, but he starts great conversations and I got a ton out of the reading because of them. Tests are a lot of IDs, matching, and two easy short essays. Definitely take this class, it's worth your time.

I have been putting off this class for awhile now, but Brian really made this class interesting and I enjoyed it more than I thought I would. Doing all the reading helps alot with tests, and class discussions are fun. I would definitely take a class from him again.

This class is so entertaining! He plays video clips to help demonstrate different processes that are described. The textbook is really interesting but if you come to class, pay attention to the study guides, and go to the review sessions, you'll do great! Lots of critical thinking in writing but the TAs are helpful if you're stuck.
Hes fine. He doesn't really make sense but it is a cool topic. The tests were hard honestly and he is a really tough grader. If you try(I didn't) Im sure you'll be fine.

If you dislike APA style like me, you will have to bear with the essay assignments. Felt like the grading for the papers got very nitpicky, but I cannot deny that he knows his stuff and he's excellent about breaking down complex social dynamics into simple terms and expressions. Be diligent with the reading and you'll be okay!

Professor Willoughby is a good professor! I always enjoyed lectures, and I appreciated that he always gave examples and explanations for terms. There is a lot of reading in the textbook, so be prepared for that. Listen to his in class hints. There are a bunch of papers, so it was a bit of a trial by fire. However, the TA reviews are very helpful.

I always loved going to Professor Willoughby's lectures! He is super knowledgeable & passionate about what he teaches! The assignments weren't too bad, but it seemed the essays/quizzes were always due in the same week. The TA's grade the papers & sometimes it seems a little unfair, but you can have them look at it before you turn it in.
this class is amazingggg. only 4 assignments the whole semester. quizzes are not hard. you will learn so much and he is a great teacher!!! i would 1000000% recommend this class

The TA's grade the essays SO harshly...have them edit it for you so you know what they are looking for. He gives EC but his lectures were quite boring It is interesting material but there's no participation from class. Take him but go to the TAs any chance you have for essays and tests. Tests were pretty easy if you went to the TAs review.

His lectures are pretty entertaining, especially with his fun movie clips, but they are directed more toward single students rather than married students so the class felt less relevant for me. Overall I enjoyed the class and the things I learned, but the essays were difficult---took a lot of brain power and the requirements were not very clear.

Super fun class! Would be better named "Relationship Development" rather marriage prep. Fun lectures with a lot of interesting topics. I think that the TA graded a little too harshly on some of my papers, I believe she is the only one that even looks at them. The whole grade is 4 papers, 7 random attendance days, and a midterm and final.

I had a lot of fun in this class. The Content is interesting, and the tests were pretty true to the class lectures. There were "reading quizzes" to make sure you had done the readings, but these helped me to do well on the exams.

Entertaining lectures, offers extra credit if you visit him during office hours. Maybe it was just his TAs, but I felt like my papers were graded more harshly than they deserved :( 
I've heard rumors that he's a contraversial figure in the SFL but he was good as a teacher based on my experience. 
Tests are at the testing center which I dispise.

Not marriage prep, more like dating 101. Not engaging lectures. He has class "discussions" but he is always looking for the "right" answer. He does not give back points for unfair TA grading. 7 random attendance checks (easy to make up). Four papers (avg 5 pages). One midterm, one final. Two books that I never read (only slightly covered on exams).
Professor Willoughby is the best and I learned so much from this class. I was always engaged and inspired. The tests and finals were very manageable. Highly recommend!

I loved Dr. Willoughby!! His lectures were engaging, and he always used great examples to illustrate concepts. There are 4 papers, 5 reading quizzes, a midterm and final - do the reading, study, meet with TAs, and attend class and you'll do great! I learned so many interesting and helpful things in this class for my current and future families.

Dr Willoughby was an amazing professor. He makes everything super applicable to your own life. He uses examples that explain concepts. His lectures are very entertaining and engaging. However, your entire grade is based on a few quizzes (can't be turned in late), a few papers (can be turned in late with points taken away), and the midterm and final

The TA's grade harsher than a graduate level course. Class is for my major and completely turned me off from SFL. Professor is willing to talk but won't take into account changes. Went in to talk and he agreed with me but still took away points and refused to admit the TA was incorrect and harsh in the grade. Tests don't reflect class, difficult!

Professor Willoughby was fine, honestly an overall solid choice for this class. However, I would not recommend having any kind of emergency or issue in his class. I had a major migraine and physically couldnt take a quiz and he refused to let me take it a day late. Good at teaching, not at helping out students.

For a class on hard topics that most of us have experienced, he teaches with zero empathy or sensitivity. He is a tough grader because he is so vague in the rubric, but so specific in what he is looking for. There are 2 tests, a 10-page lit review with assignments leading up to it, and a movie paper. I would not take a class from him again.

Avoid this prof! He has arbitrary grading standards on the papers - there are very specific things he grades on that aren't even in the rubric. For how straightforward the content is, it's ridiculously challenging to get an A in the class. The study guides are intentionally vague and he tests on random minute details from research articles.

Prof Willoughby is a solid choice for SFL 160. He is personable and tells good stories to explain concepts. There are 4 big papers, 5 reading quizzes, and a midterm and final. The TA's are going to be your best friends in this class.

I absolutely loved this class & looked forward to it every week. Grading was tough and he's very straight forward when you have conversations with him. Papers can be a bit unclear but if you attend the paper reviews and stay close to the TAs, you will be totally fine. As long as you study and apply yourself, you will succeed (imagine that).

This professor is probably my favorite professor at BYU. If you are interested in SFL or physiology, definitely take a class by him!! His lectures were really entertaining and I felt like he made the concepts really easy to grasp.

I loved the lectures- he has examples that get you involved. I will say don't take this class if you don't like reflecting on your family situation because that's literally all your assignments. Your grade is mainly said assignments (4 papers) and reading quizzes so not much room for error.

I LOVE Dr. Willoughby! This whole class is about how to handle stress - so he focuses a lot on making sure we are as least stressed as possible. We basically had 1 paper, a midterm, and a final - so very few assignments. As long as you pay attention in class and do the readings before the exam, you'll be fine! Literally one of my fav profs at BYU.

Amazing lectures, powerful and life-changing lessons. You're only graded on like 5 things throughout the entire semester but he will consult you every step of the way if you take the initiative and go to office hours. His lectures are always creative and refreshing. I highly recommend!

Prof. Willoughby is the best! His lectures were really interesting while still being concise in teaching you what you actually need to know for the tests. The workload really isn't bad if you plan ahead for the papers and reading. If you put in the work, you can easily get a decent grade. The TA is also great.

I love Dr. Willoughby! I took his SFL160 class also. He is very clear and kind. His lectures are inspirational and help you to feel like you know him. I learned so much from this class! He grades you on only about 5 things, so that makes it hard to feel confident in passing the class. He's extremely accessible and helps those that ask for it.

Prof Willoughby is a nice guy and the topics of this class were interesting. There's a 10 page paper due at the end of the semester and two exams that are relatively tough. Mediocre class, but overall, not too bad. If you have to take it, he is an okay option. You for sure have to work hard for an A, as there are are only 5 assignments.

I really liked him up until I accidentally noted the final as being on a different day than it was. He handled the situation with 0 understanding or care. We are living in unique times right now. He has 0 regard for circumstances and is very much a believer in the law is law and 0 exceptions or mercy when honest mistakes are made.

Seems like a really nice guy and made lectures fun with music videos related to class content. Used good activities to help you understand. Very tough grader and gives super unhelpful and vague comments. It wasn't clear what he wanted and gave little direction for the final paper.

Dr. Willoughby is amazing! I took his class in the spring and he did such a great organizing the material and making guidelines clear. The textbook reading is on the test, so you need it. I thought his assignment made you work for a good grade, but it was definitely doable. He brings insight that other teachers can't. His study guides are helpful!

He teaches in a way that is easy to understand and the material is very interesting. It's a tough class though. The tests are super specific which makes them hard to study for and there is a 10 page research paper that you turn in at the end. He's a tough grader so you have to put a lot of time and effort into it, but it is doable.

Professor Willoughby is my favorite professor I have ever had. He teaches in a way that really keeps you interested and makes you want to learn more. There are constant examples and connections given in class about the subjects to make learning more personal and understandable. I looked forward to going to class. Plus, not ridiculously hard class.

Overall I loved this class because its fun and interesting and I really loved prof. W. He is a great guy who really knows what he is talking about. But the assignments are long and extremely stressful and the TA's are very tough graders. I don't think I got an A on a single essay. And the last essay was 9 pages, and it took forever.

His lectures were entertaining and he keeps things interesting but his class is only graded based on a few assignments and quizzes. With only a midterm and final. Not a lot of room to miss points. His assignments are graded way to hard. Don't take this class if you're just looking for an easy A.

I've taken 5 classes from him (SFL 160, SFL 335, SFL 403R twice, and MFHD 513), it's safe to say that he is a great professor and that his classes are worth taking! He has taught me so much about real world things and has been instrumental in preparing me for grad school. He's an aloof kind of guy, but is a great resource.

This professor is extremely difficult and very unforgiving. He will go out of his way to make things more difficult. It seems like he struggled a lot as a student so his way to give back is to make students struggle to succeed which is not the way to go. He will not give you any extra help. He key words are " read my syllabus" its in my syllabus.

Dr. Willoughby is incredible!!!!! I learned so much from this class that I will use the rest of my life, and I'm so glad I took it. I think this should be a required class for all BYU students, it's that important and awesome. Test were pretty easy, papers are easy if you give yourself time and use the TAs. Amazing lectures with movie clips! 10/10

His lectures were pretty good, and he often showed movie clips! There are a couple easy reading quizzes, but the thing to look out for is all the papers. 5 in total. Some were not that bad to do, but two of them, in particular, killed me, especially the last one which is 7 pages of torture! If you don't mind writing, I highly recommend this class.

I've heard horror stories about this class, but it is honestly really good and the things we learn are useful! He gives us clear grading and feedback for the final lit review (have to turn parts in during semester). Even though subjects can be hard, we focus on how to be resilient and it's been positive to learn these things. I love his lectures!
Good teacher and interesting material. I thought his class was tough for a 100 level course, but it is doable. I still use what I learned in his class in my other SFL classes.

Dr. Willoughby is a great professor. I took the class over summer so it was 2.5 hours long, so his classes kind of dragged on. His lectures aren't very exciting, but very informative. The papers are a large majority of your grade. Attend the review sessions and you will do great on the exams.

Prof. Willoughby gives amazing lectures and really teaches the concepts thoroughly. I would recommend his SFL 160 class to anyone regardless of their field of study because he is that good. Sometimes his TA's grade a little bit harshly, but he teaches with passion and in an entertaining, capturing, and applicable way.
If you don't like writing papers, don't take this class.

There are lots of papers/assignments, but they really help you understand the material. Make sure you pay attention in the lectures- it's where most of the test information is best understood. Lots of fun stories and examples with videos, movies and such.

I took both SFL 160 and SFL 335 from him. His classes have always been my favorite. He is an amazing lecturer. I have never been bored in his class and honestly his 160 class was the reason I switched to SFL major. All of his assignments make sense. There are no bogus assignments, they all have purpose and help you understand the material.

He'a brilliant. He'a taught the course at least 12 times. Group activities during class are way fun. Very straightforward in personality and teaching style; it's easy to learn a lot from him. A midterm, a final, 1 10pg paper, 1 5pg paper. Very helpful when you need him. I appreciated his mastery of the content and understanding of the BYU student.

Three different TAs that grade differently. Some TAs were more lenient than others. Professor doesn't care about his students. Only cares about getting through lecture material. Seems approachable, but actually isn't. 7 page paper due at the end of the semester. 4 papers total.

I loved taking this class and learned so many useful things. His papers were harder, but you can revise them at the end for some credit back. Study guides help with the midterm and final. Overall, I really enjoyed the class and would recommend taking this class. I learned things that I use in my daily life with my friends and family.

Dr. Willoughby is pretty great. He can be very funny and his class is actually super interesting. The papers are hard! You NEED to go to a TA to have them check your paper. The grading criteria is very finicky.

Willoughby is an amazing professor. His lectures were fascinating and I never wanted to miss. There is some reading, but it never felt like a lot. There are 5 writing assignments, but he is very clear about what he wants. This was my favorite School of Family Life class!

4 quizzes on readings, 5 papers, 1 midterm, extra credit for reworks. Workload was easy, except when writing a paper. Last paper is 7 pages, others 3-5. The TA's grade the papers and they were harsher than needed. I got away with a B in the class (TA's screwed my grade over). Lectures were pretty boring but we watched movie clips each class.
I loved going to class every day. He made this class so interesting with lots of movie clips and examples.

So the class was great and Willoughby is a fantastic professor! Learned some great stuff. Papers were long and I dreaded doing them. The only complaint I have is that the TAs graded my papers more difficult depending who got it (one TA was generous and I got As, the other gave me Cs).  Book is essential for quizzes and readings were long.
I really enjoyed this class and Professor Willoughby! The lectures were interesting, and kept the class engaged. Five assignments and two tests. It wasn't bad at all!
Absolutely loved Dr. WIlloughby and this class!

Great teacher to the whole class, not willing to be very helpful one-on-one when needing extra help. Felt like he didn't care/ want to make time to help me out when I am having a hard time this semester.

Every day after I left class I thought to myself "I love my major." A tad more liberal than most professors--refreshing perspective--and, even if you are very conservative, he will not offend. Essays are a lot of work but really, he's incredible.

He is very good at helping apply the material he is teaching. The essays are difficult but he and his TA are very helpful with explaining requirements and reviewing your essays so use the office hours! The text  book is very helpful and there is always test questions that come from just the book so do all the reading. It's hard but worth it!
Professor made the class interesting and informative

Dr. Willoughby is an awesome teacher.  He is extremely helpful and even helps those interested in research.  If you want a free an A you will not get it but you can earn it!  His teaching style is entertaining and the class is never boring.  Come to lectures if you want an A even though he does not require you to be there.

Lectures are fun and interesting but when it comes to the writing assignments- super work-intensive and harshly graded. Spent 5 hours on one assignment just to get a B. Do not take this class if you're not going into the family sciences.

My favorite professor by far! His lectures are interesting and interactive and he doesn't read directly from the PowerPoint slides (which I loved!).  He is very willing to give help and feedback and he is specific and clear about what he is looking for in his assignments. I loved this class and highly recommend it!

I LOVED this class! Dr. Willoughby is very knowledgeable in this field, and does a great job explaining concepts and getting the class involved with discussion and activities. He makes the information very relevant to everyone. The 10-page research paper is intimidating, but very doable. Take this class!

I enjoyed this class, but  not the TA I had. He was rude every time I asked him something, so I wasn't a fan of him. Anyways, I worked really hard on papers and tests and kept getting B's. So it's not the easiest class ever, but it is fun. Willoughby is a great teacher and uses a lot of examples, but papers and test are almost possible to get an A.

Great class, only one midterm and one final, easy and short textbook readings, and really interesting overall!  Great class whether you are taking it for your major or for a general.  Not too difficult or time consuming, and the TAs are great.

He is a really great professor. He knows his stuff and he explains things really clearly. He encourages discussion in class which helps with comprehension. The class is hard--two tests and a couple papers. The papers are long, but they are worth it. He's always willing to help and he gives constructive feedback. Take his class if you're interested!
Great teacher. Helped a lot and allowed me to understand the concepts. Overall a wonderful class. Highly recommend.

I LOVED this class. I found the lectures very interesting and thought Dr. Willoughby teaches in a way that makes the topics fun and easy to understant. Yes you have to study and do a few assignments, but I took this as a freshman and got 100% on the Final exam. Enough said. If you're interested in learning about the family, this class is for you :)

For your own sake, take this class from another teacher.  I transferred into this class from a class with a different professor and was extremely disappointed.  I honestly haven't learned a thing in this class and it is very difficult busy work.  Professor Willoughby is a nice guy, but he is not a good teacher.  He just reads his slides verbatim.

His class was very interesting and I liked the way he taught!  The papers were long and difficult and the tests were a lot of memorizing.  Overall a good class, but if you are looking for an easy one I would say pass.

My FAVORITE class taken at BYU (and I am a Senior). Class discussions were always interesting, Dr. Wiloughby is highly interactive and fun. He does everything in his power to clarify questions about the test or research paper. Each class he reminds about deadlines.  Very flexible with emergencies. I would recommend this class to all majors!

He is a really good professor. Parts of the subject were really boring, but he did a good job teaching them. He uses a lot of movie clips to demonstrate different theories. Tests were hard and their were a few papers, but if you keep up with the reading and start your paper before the day it is due, you'll be fine.
Nice guy, great lectures, makes material enjoyable, but he is tough! Tests are really hard, and paper is almost impossible to do well on. Expects graduate level work for an undergrad. class.

Took 335 and 460 with him. Awful! I tried going to his office for help with a paper but it was useless, he failed me. Start papers the day class starts, ask for help, do all the readings, and go to every lecture! Or better yet, take a different professor.

At the beginning of the semester, he's so good looking and teaches an incredible lecture, but at the end you might just hate him. The hardest part is playing the guessing game on papers because no one has any idea what he's actually looking for.  Frequent visits to his office are a must if you want to do well.

He is a good teacher! He used clips from movies to make the class more interesting. However, we had to write several long papers that were slightly tedious. I would still very strongly suggest him as a teacher.

He's fairly young and recently got his PhD, but he's done well for his first year as a BYU professor. Since he taught a 460 class, he demands near-graduate level writing and thought. He tends to make assignments sound simple, but they challenge you. Going to him for help outside of class is highly recommended for clarity.

Good Teacher! You can tell he knows his stuff. Uses a lot of media and pop culture to reinforce topics and help students apply it. Fair amount of papers but they're spread out. Tests are pretty tough-overall makes sure you do the reading! Good class, def. recommended.
BWW is my diva. He is a freaking comedian and is friends with all his students. If you have the chance to take his class, do.

This class is an awesome way to take care of your art ge credit. The main information needed for tests can be gotten from the slides he posted, but it is a lot easier if you just show up to class, even though attendance is not graded. There was no busy work, 4 exams, 4 concert reports, and then ocassional open note quizes. Overall was fun, easy.

I had Woodbury for Introduction to Jazz, which is a Jazz history class. The resources needed to succeed are incredibly accessible, and if you show up to class and take notes you shouldn't have any trouble on tests. This class doesn't really have any busy work, and focuses primarily on learning through lecture and lecture slides.

Great class! Definitely felt more like a history class (rather than music theory) but it wasn't too hard. I went to class and studied for about 2 hours before each exam and easily passed. Prof Woodbury cares about his class and loves teaching. Would suggest!
An excellent musician. Can seem hard to please or live up to expectations. Knows what he's doing and is there to help you.

I loved this class! It was one of the easiest on my schedule this semester. Professor Woodbury is so funny and he does a great job teaching. The information is really straightforward, and there is almost no homework. You just have to study for the exams, but there's only 4 and the last one isn't comprehensive. This class was so interesting.

I have loved this class! It's really is not that difficult. Professor Woodbury does a great job and helping you appreciate Jazz from both a historical and musical viewpoint. The tests definitely take studying, but even if you put in an hour of going over the study guide or a quizlet, you'll do fine. And the final is not comprehensive!

He is an amazing teacher! He explains everything so clearly and welcomes questions. He provides a very clear study guide so there's no question about what's on the tests. We always go over the study guide in class, so it is very straightforward. The class before each exam is a review, so he'll fill you in on any part of the study guide you missed.

Prof. Woodbury is very nice, makes funny jokes, and is always willing to answer any questions. He posts all his lecture slides on Learning Suite. Tests are in the Testing Center, make sure you have wired headphones. Don't buy the textbook. Tests can be hard, make sure to write down what he says during lectures, not just the info on the slides.

His lecture slides aren't really helpful for exams. Pay more attention to what he says and write notes according to his study guides. You have to remember an excessive amount of facts for each exam which is annoying if you're only taking this class for an arts credit. Bottom line, don't take this class thinking you won't have to study.

Woodbury is clearly passionate about jazz, but he's not the greatest at teaching. I love learning the actual content so that is a plus?
Everything in the class is pretty chill but the unit tests are ROUGH. You learn a lot in class and it is tough to memorize every bit. There is no study guide. This is more of a history class than an art class imo.
Professor Woodfield shouldn't be teaching anymore. He appears uninterested in being there, has little patience, and often explains things in an unnecessarily complicated way.
He is a very smart guy and definitely knows his chemistry. I couldn't learn with the way he taught.

It should be recognized that CHEM 105 is a difficult class and would be hard no matter what, but Professor Woodfield did not help. He genuinely cared for his students and wanted to help, but he was rather intimidating and did not seem approachable. He does not use slides and makes lectures overly complicated. I would not recommend for CHEM 105.

Don't take this class from him if you want to actually learn anything. He showed up to class one time and told us he realized accidentally gave us the wrong formula THREE WEEKS PRIOR, but wouldn't adjust our grades or curve anything. Basically the entire class failed weeks worth of assignments because of him, and he refused to do anything about it.

Do NOT take chem 105 or any lower level chemistry class from Dr. Woodfield. I had to teach myself everything. His lectures are all over the place, often teaching upper level things that you don't need to know, and skipping lessons that are essential. You're better off waiting a semester until you can get a good professor than taking chem from him.

Worst class ever. Very poorly structured. Should be at least a 5 credit class for the workload. The answer key of the online homework is often wrong and they don't bother even correcting it. Don't waste your time reading the textbook. TA is your best help. The only thing you get from this class is pure frustration and confusion. Good luck.

Take with Woodfield if he is your last option. I got an A so it's definitely doable, but he makes it hard because he doesn't use the slides like the other professors. The other professors also will drop your lowest test score while he didn't for us. He's funny but makes it so everyone feels uncomfortable to ask questions.
holy, worst class i have ever taken in my life. he would talk about topics that had nothing to do with what we were going to be tested on and he was not very nice.

This class is just hard. Despite what others might say, Prof Woodfield does want his students to succeed in the class. I felt very prepared for exams, which were very similar to hw and practice exams. He is sarcastic and he does not teach from slides. Use the provided resources. He is very knowledgeable and is clearly passionate about the class.

If you are reading this, don't look any further. Switch professors if possible. If you want to keep a good GPA, DO NOT take this guy. Trust me I know you think you're smart, but he wants you to fail. Not joking, he takes pride in being a very difficult teacher.

All it took was showing up to every lecture, sitting towards the front, taking notes with a pencil and paper on basically everything while marking things I didn't understand when initially explained, and genuinely taking time to study and I got a high A. He's an incredible professor who explains things well and deeply if you actually pay attention.

Hardest class I've taken, it did weed me out of premed realized I didnt care enough to be a doctor, so it did its job.  Honestly most of what people say about him isn't fully true.  He's sarcastic and may come across rude but if you're not a baby you'll find it funny. Lectures were tough, no PowerPoints, tests were hard but fair same with the grade

Takes his class seriously and appeals specifically to conceptual and auditory learners. If you like lectures, stories, and sarcasm, you'll definitely be entertained. Wouldn't recommend for visual learners. He teaches by explanation, algebraic examples, and uses a chalk board exclusively. Also requires more teaching materials than other options.

His lectures are all over the place. He doesn't prepare his lectures for class, he just starts ranting. The TA's were good and I learned a lot from them. He gets so frustrated when people ask him questions. A lot of homework and hard tests.

Save your gpa. DO NOT TAKE WOODFIELD!!! He's very knowledgeable but cannot tech to save his life. He's useless about 99% of the time. His grading scale is very unforgiving. Sucks he's tenured- he doesn't care about his students anymore. 
If I could go back, I'd go to class for the iclicker quizzes and then walk out and teach myself these concepts

This was one of the worst classes I've taken at BYU. Coursework was rarely covered in lectures, leaving you on your own for homework and labs. Dr. Woodfield requires you to buy his software for a good grade, which feels wrong. He travels often, canceling class or having others teach. Tests had low averages (50s-60s), proving how unprepared you are.

Dr. Woodfield knows his stuff, but he's not good at teaching it. Lectures were disorganized and easy topics were made complex - I would walk into lecture prepared and feeling good then walk out completely lost and would have to unlearn a lot of the stuff he said. Also didn't like that he required us to pay for an expensive software that he owned.

Lectures are not helpful. Too much money, if Beyond Labz, his own creation, is going to be required for the class, I shouldn't have to buy my own activation code. Stop taking advantage of poor college students, get money from Beyond Labz by selling it to other schools or governments, don't rob those of us that are already struggling.
Please do not take from him

Not a bad guy, very intelligent, but holy cow he is not a useful lecturer. Only was able to get a good grade because I had a TA who was going into her 5th semester as a Chem 105 TA. Lectures were so confusing. Tests were also very challenging, you kinda took them with the purpose of not ruining your grade, but that was more of the curriculum.

He was no questions asked, the worst professor I had in my 5 years at BYU. He is a terrible teacher. Every interaction with students he has is rude. He speaks down to them, and never answers questions. He does not help students in any way. He has no business teaching at BYU.

Chem 105 is a tough class, but with the right study tools like Unstuckstudy, you can succeed. The lectures can be confusing, so rely on TAs and the textbook. Overall, it's a challenging but rewarding course.

He always told us "we should know how to do this" and no matter what "this" was, I never knew how to do it. He didn't really teach us what we needed to know. I learned way more basic lab skill in chem 227 than in this supposedly introductory lab class. I was severely disappointed when the tests had questions about things we were not taught.

I know this class is a "weeder" but it did not have to be this hard. The test averages were very low (in the 50s), and the tests often covered material that was never talked about in class or recitation. And all grades are curved so that only a small percentage of the class is able to get an A. Don't take this class.

I worked as a TA for this professor and two others (Asplund and Hansen). Woodfield is easily the worst. His lectures are horrible; he spends very little time covering class content. Doesn't care about students at all, frequently mentions his tenure and lack of empathy for struggling students. Take from someone else or don't take the class.

Prof. Woodfield started off the first day by introducing himself and telling us, "If you have questions about this class, read the textbook or ask your TA. I will not answer your questions for this is not real chemistry. Talk to me when you want to talk about actual chemistry." Passing grade was a 43% showing the "prowess" of his teaching style. :(

Chem 105 is a difficult course to begin with but the class is unnecessarily difficult. Dr. Woodfield is very intelligent but a terrible instructor. He doesn't use slides and his lectures are basically him talking about what he wants to for an hour. Rely on the TA's review but don't count on learning anything.

Dr. Woodfield is extremely smart, sometimes too smart. Because of this, his lectures can be confusing because he moves quickly and assumes we know a lot more than we do. I didn't read the textbook, but friends that did understood lectures better so I would recommend it. Study groups and recitation are a necessity in this class.

Chem 105 is a hard class regardless of the professor. If you have to take it, make sure you talk to your TA's and go to TA reviews because the way Dr. Woodfield explains things during lectures is confusing- but it's going to be like that no matter who your professor is. Take from Dr. Woodfield because he has good TA's and he is super fun.

Prof Woodfield cares about his students but is a very intense person. He obviously knows his stuff really well but sometimes that makes it difficult to learn from him. Having a strong background in chemistry is recommended, if you didn't take high school chem get ready to work. The hw is how I learned all the content (and the TA's)

If you are a visual learner DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. He uses no slide shows and blabs the whole time. He's not helpful to your learning, you'll only learn stuff from Smartworks. You have to buy a lot of materials in his class compared to other classes(at least $200 worth). If you don't have a good chemistry background from high school it's very hard.

Professor Woodfield is a great guy. He really knows his stuff and is a chemistry genius. However, he doesn't really know how to teach intro level Chem. What he taught during lecture didn't really seem to match up with what was on the test or on the homework. I had to learn a lot off of the internet. I am retaking the class from a different teacher.

chem 105 is a difficult class but he made it WAY more difficult than it needed to be. His lectures had hardly anything to do with what he was actually going to test us on. He's a genius man but because of that he doesn't know how to teach simply at ALL. He only derives equations and talks about his PhD.

Woodfield first came off as arrogant, but eventually mellowed into a very sage-like professor. Lots of wisdom and it was clear he really understood the material of the lab. Dr. W. was very forgiving and graceful when it came to late assignments, and his TA's were quick to provide solutions to problems. Overall great professor and class.

Chem 113 is a lab class (NOTE - WAYYY more work than 2 credits. I'd call it like 3.5. Take fewer credits this semester to accommodate that.). Good but difficult. If you do not read the lab thoroughly and come prepared, it's gonna be rough. Dr. Woodfield does a good job of explaining the labs before you do them. There is a lot of pre-lab homework.

Dr. Woodfield was a GREAT professor. I loved him, he's pretty funny. Woodfield talks about super fascinating and profound things in his lectures, but they don't always focus on the MEAT of what we're supposed to learn. And CHEM105 is VERY DIFFICULT if you've never taken chemistry before. So a lot of people relied heavily on the TA's.

Dr. Woodfield comes off really hardnosed and strict at the beginning but he warms up throughout the semester. Explains concepts in great depth but sometimes too much depth because I would leave understanding the topic less sometimes. If you do the reading before lecture it really helps you follow along with what he's doing on the board.

Chem is a hard class with any teacher, you should treat it as a 5 credit hour course. The thing that makes Woodfield worse is how he grades, after the semester is over he lines everyone up and places letter grade lines in gaps, meaning all that matters is that the rest of the class does worse than you, pitting you against your classmates

If chemistry comes easily to you, Woodfield is fine. He spends a lot of time on the concepts and the history rather than teaching you the practical application for the tests. If that is not your learning style, take from another professor who will teach you application. Regardless, Chem 105 is hard from any professor so be willing to work hard.

He was the worst professor I've ever had. His lectures did not match up with material on the test, and he does not curve grades based on student performance. He goes off on random tangents during lecture, then complains that he doesn't have enough time to lecture and won't take any questions. I had to learn the content from my TA and teach myself.

Dr. Woodfield was great! He can sometimes get a little off-topic during lectures, but you can really tell that he cares about chemistry and cares about his students' learning. Tests are worth most of your grade, so study study study. I recommend doing the readings and problem sets BEFORE the topic is covered in lecture.

I really enjoyed Professor Woodfield's lectures. If you can't handle sarcasm you might not like him. He really cares about his students and the material. The class itself is intensive, but if you do your readings and understand the problem sets, you will be more than fine. I would not take Chem 105 again but Prof. Woodfield is great.

Honestly Woodfield was not a bad professor at all. People give him a hard time but the class isn't that bad if you put in the work. His lectures are not that useful but they are interesting, and as long as you do the reading and homework you will do fine.

I would listen to this rate my professor reading, I am trying to help you. Professor Woodfield is very kind and caring and genuinely TRYS to care for his students. While he is one of the nicer professors for chemistry, his lectures are very hard to follow and the tests do not always line up exactly with what he teaches.

This class is meant to be an entry level Chemistry class, isnt taught that way. If you havent taken chemistry in high school, youll be very lost. Even if you have, its rough. The lectures rarely cover relevant material and the TA saved my life. Do not take chemistry from Woodfield if you want to be taught the material.

Professor Woodfield knows what he's talking about. He's intelligent and knows the subject of chemistry well. But, he teaches at that high level, and for a bunch of freshman in college, his lectures are often very difficult to understand. Easy concepts are not clear. Get a study group, talk to the TA, and watch Kahn academy and professor Dave.

He loves chemistry deeply, but often spent half the class or more talking about unimportant things(covid19). It was hard to ask questions in class without feeling ridiculed. I didnt go to his office hours, but I like his take on religion reconciled with science. The textbook taught me the class. Do all the assignments and study with others.
Professor Woodfield teaches very well. Chem 105 is a really hard class, but if you pay attention in class and listen to what he says, you'll survive.
He knows what he's talking about for sure, but goes super fast and it is easy to get lost.

This class is so. much. work. If you have the time to put in the effort you will do well, if you can teach yourself. The lectures are less than helpful so you better hope you get a good TA. if you can take from another professor do it. The tests for all the chem classes are the same, and Woodfield starts class by saying most people will not do well

I only survived this class by watching professor dave and the ochem tutor on youtube. Woodfield doesnt teach material and often gets carried away in specifics that arent necessary for midterms. There are 3 midterms and a final, and way to many additional assignments. This class is doable but you need to be willing to work hard to pass.

Professor Woodfields Chem 105 class was absolutely impossible. His lectures are so hard to understand, that in hindsight, I wouldnt even go. His tests were extremely difficult, and he clearly does not care much about his students. The only way that I was able to survive and learn anything was from my TA. Take Chem 105 from a different teacher.

If you take Chem 105 from Dr. Woodfield, it is CRUCIAL that you read the textbook and do the homework. When you study for tests, do the problems at the end of every chapter. If you want a good grade you have to work for it. Lectures are often off-topic, so make sure you are doing the readings to keep up with the material. Also, GO TO CLASS!

Dr. Woodfield is very smart and knows what he is talking about, but he doesn't really care if you know what he is talking about. Most of the learning was done outside of the lectures, and you really have to be motivated to actually learn the material. Would not take if you want to actually learn from a professor!

DO NOT TAKE FROM WOODFIELD IF YOU VALUE YOUR GPA OR MENTAL HEALTH! Chem 105 is a hard class no matter what, but Woodfield makes it unnecessarily difficult. Does not care about how students are doing in the class. Lectures have nothing to do with the exams, stated multiple times he doesn't like teaching and doesn't care if you do poorly.

AMAZING lectures. Brutal exams. Don't be scared of this class, but get ready to work for your grade. All Chem 105 classes are brutal, but this guy is really, really hard. TAs are fantastic. Honestly, your TA matters more than your professor because you interact with them more. Woodfield was a little flaky, but passionate and entertaining.

Professor Woodfield is clearly very passionate about chemistry but multiple times has stated that he doesn't enjoying teaching very much. He seems to only be teaching to get his research paid for. He doesn't care about his students and only ever wants us to talk to the TAs and not him. TAs and textbook are most important resource for this class.

Woodfield really cares about chemistry but lectures were confusing and the tests had nothing to do with lectures. Each test was extremely hard no matter how hard I studied. In the end, I had to teach myself topics from the textbook and YouTube lectures saved me. I would not recommend him for Chem 105.

Dr. Woodfield is extremely knowledgeable about chemistry, but he can feel disconnected from students and the class expectations often feel unrealistic. For an introductory lab, the level of precision, accuracy, and speed we were required to have was very high compared to how little we were actually taught about lab techniques. TAs are very helpful.

Do not take this class with this professor! I loved AP Chemistry and my advance classes, but this professor ruined my desires to ever learn more. The lectures are random and confusing, the amount of daily homework is insane, and you are basically teaching yourself in this class. Find anyone else as your teacher.

Lectures usually involve 15-20 minutes of tangents and after that still are not clear. If you love reading and learning from textbooks and smartwork, take the class from him. If lectures help, Professor Sevy gives amazing lectures. I watch Professor Sevy's lectures with my roommate and it's like day from night.

Doesn't care about students or teaching, clearly just there for research. Doesn't know how to explain concepts in a way students understand, ridiculous amount of homework, the TAs were so-so, ended up needing tutoring to even barely understand what was going on.

Hybrid class due to Covid. Doesn't teach in lectures, rants are irrelevant. Grades tests pretty harshly. CHEM105 is going to suck no matter what, but he doesn't help the situation. Learned more from Khan academy and things like that than I did from the class. Tests were weighted heavily for the grade, so if you do poorly on a test, you're screwed.

I almost dropped out of the BYU Chemistry department because of this class. It was way harder than necessary. Even though it was a two credit class, Dr. Woodfield's work load made it feel like at least four credits. He focuses more on lab results than education. He was very sarcastic and didn't answer questions in a helpful way. Worst class ever.

I loved him as a person, but as a professor it just didn't work for me. I felt like lectures never covered everything I was supposed to know and made the assignments so difficult because you really had to teach yourself everything. Cool guy, hard class.

I didn't take chemistry in high school, took this my first semester and it was my hardest class. Dr. Woodfield moved much too fast for me; I often left lecture more confused. You have recitation homework, in person labs, virtual labs, smartworks, 3 midterms and a final. I felt like I learned more from the TAs on how to actually do the homework.

Dr. Woodfield's lectures are all over the place, learned almost nothing from them. Some of the content is really hard to grasp, but the difficulty of this class is due mostly to the ridiculous amount of homework, some of which is unique to Woodfield. I've heard Hansen, Wood, Smith, or Sevy are better choices. Woodfield is smart but disorganized.

Dr. Woodfield is an awesome professor. He knows what he's talking about and makes sure you know as well. Make sure you read the labs before coming to class. Labs are important but STUDY HARD for the tests because that's what makes or breaks your grade. You will enjoy this class from Dr. W.

Woodfield does a great job of teaching hard concepts. He's really intense and he knows it. I learned a lot, but he wasn't very accessible outside of class and I mostly relied on TAs for help. It's also impossible to predict your final grade because of the curve he uses. Put in lots of work, and you should be ok.

I'll be honest, Dr. Woodfield scared me at first, but by the end of the year I got to the point where I couldn't wait to go to class. Dr. Woodfield is an extremely talented and passionate lecturer, just make sure to pay attention in class. Biggest advice is to not be afraid of him and to just put in the work to learn at a deeper level. Fun class!
