Very lab specific. All graded by spreadsheet. Even if you understand the concept 100% and something goes wrong in the lab you're screwed. Woodfield just talks 30 mins before you start a new lab. It's really all TAs. Not very helpful outside of class. Worth more than the two credits BYU allots it

Lectures weren't well put together. He would jump from subject to subject, not helping us to connect the dots. The course was standardized among all 105 profs, and he refused to teach to what we needed for the test. He would ramble on about what he found interesting. Then the day the test opened would say "learn this, this, and this on your own"
He is intense and a bit scary at first, but if you just go to class and pay attention he gives away half the test in the lecture. He is a pretty awesome guy.

Dr. Woodfield is a very intense man. He is a really smart guy and obviously cares a lot for his students. His tangents during his lectures, although not always chemistry related, were always meaningful. This class takes a lot of personal study and practice; there is not way around good discipline. Dr. Woodfield makes the journey more enjoyable.

Dr. Woodfield was a great teacher! Other people complain about how he talked about his life for half the class, but it made class enjoyable and he still taught the material adequately. He focused a lot on getting the students to learn how to work hard and take more initiative in their learning. This made the class hard, but meaningful.

Pretty difficult class, very picky grading. The class was enjoyable though, we did some really cool experiments. TA was more important than the teacher just because he was gone all the time, so make sure you get a good TA. Don't underestimate the weight of the tests - they are more important than you think.

Foreward: Woodfield is nice, funny and cares lots about chemistry. However Woodfield is consistently gone and when he was here he spent half the time discussing his personal life. He doesn't follow the textbook and his lectures were often disorganized and difficult to follow. This is a hard class no matter what but he doesn't make it any easier.

Chem 113 can be frustrating because your grade is lab-heavy (obviously). There are also lab quizzes and practice questions and a midterm and final. Some labs are just really hard to do well on no matter how well you understand it. Chem 113 was the hardest class I enjoyed. Your TA can affect you a lot. Make sure you buy the Qual Analysis book.

Dr. Woodfield has a unique style. He expects you to teach yourself just as much as he teaches you. His exams are hard. I enjoyed Chem 112 but it was tough. Written and online homework every week. 3 days of lecture a week, and they arent super fast paced. Youll learn a lot.

This is a really difficult class and Brother Woodfield helped alleviate some of the stress. He has a very kind and calming demeanor and is genuine in his desire to help his students succeed. He is understanding when it comes to the challenges of this class and has a lot of empathy.

woodfield focuses on the CONCEPTS not regurgitation. you need to learn how to learn yourself if you want to do well in this class. do the readings before class. he is a great guy and genuinely cares. he pretends his class is harder than it is. go to class and recitation. you will be fine.

Dr. Woodfield is a chalkboard and lecture only professor so that isn't you, take from another professor. He had weekly reviews that were helpful, but tests were still hard. Be ready to work for a good grade. I learned a lot on my own after class through the daily homework.

His lectures are really confusing. He teaches tons of stuff that "you don't need to know" and mixes in the stuff you do need to know... In the end he gets everything you need across, you just get really confused in the process. If you have to take this class from him go to TA reviews and get friends with other professors to study with.
He is a great teacher and wants you to succeed!

I came into Dr. Woodfield's class a little worried about how difficult it would be. It turned out great! A lot of students got worried about how you can't control some aspects of your grade in 113 because it is a lab class and sometimes things go wrong. Dr. Woodfield was understanding and has tests to balance it out. Great professsor!

Doctor Woodfield is very passionate about chemistry which can be intimidating, but makes him hilarious and inspirational. He's great at explaining the concepts in a way that is useful. You will need to rely on the TA's for help with everything and the tests are very difficult, but he curves heavily.

Dr woodfield is very cut and dry with the grading in this class. the exams actually arent very heavily weighted. but grades you get on the labs will make or break you. He uses excel spreadsheets to grade most of them, so its very formulaic. even if you are within 2 points of a higher letter grade at the end of the semester he wont give it to you.

Woodfield is a chalkboard only guy, so if you like powerpoints and such, you will be disappointed. He does not use online material, so your best bet of learning outside class is going to TA help sessions (which are really good) because the only material for the class is the textbook and he has a love hate relationship with it.

It's chemistry.  Obviously the course will be very difficult, but Professor Woodfield makes an effort to help the students learn and understand the material.  If you go to him with concerns he will be very respectful and do everything he can to help you.

He is a very intelligent man, and he lets you know this, as others have mentioned. He does truly love Chemistry, which is great to see. He tries to scare students by saying his tests would be alot harder than the HW, but the questions on tests and HW are nearly identical in most cases.

Dr. Woodfield is a funny sarcastic man who keeps lectures interesting. His grading method is awesome. He puts everyones grade percentages on a sheet and draws lines where there are score gaps to determine grades. The homework isn't too bad 2 worksheets a week and 1 online assignment. Took me about 3-4 hrs a week. But a good TA is essential.

Dr. Woodfield is very tough but fair. He clearly explains difficult concepts and makes sure you know how everything connects together. Although he may seem intimidating, he will respect and help you if you're willing to put in the work. This course is difficult, but manageable if you have a good teacher. I'd highly recommend Dr. Woodfield!

Either you will love his class or hate it. He constantly relates things back to each other and he makes you think about the problems for every angle. He can be intimidating and seem standoff-ish but if you push past that, he is a such a funny caring professor. I HIGHLY recommend taking it from him. Our class had the advantage over the other section

Such a great teacher! Very willing to help. Read the book before class, do the homework early, don't work in groups to do homework, and study hard for the tests. Expect to put in at least 20 hours a week. But Dr. Woodfield is definitely my favorite professor! This was the only class I could completely stay awake in. Highly recommended!

Very passionate and he knows chemistry very well.  It might take a little while to get used to his style, and you need to get the homework done early and study hard for the tests, but all in all a great professor.  He truly loves teaching chemistry!

BEST professor I have ever had at BYU. He is super funny, passionate and interesting. He makes chemistry personal and applicable. Walked out of every class feeling good and excited about chemistry. His enthusiasm is contagious. :)

Extremely hard class. Expect to do at least 10 hours of homework a week if you want to get at least a B. I got an A-, but i studied my buns off. Lectures are interesting, he says you don't have to read the book... but you do or else you won't understand the concepts fully. make sure you have a friend who is good at chemistry who will help you.

This is a hard class and after talking to TA's from other classes, he teaches a few concepts that aren't taught in other classes but are discussed in Chem 106. If you're looking for an easy A he isn't for you but if you want to learn THE MOST then take Dr. Woodfield.  Ignore the comments where people say he's evil. excellent at relating concepts.

Woodfield has a great sense of humor and goes on tangents all the time. The class can be really challenging if you don't do the homework right, especially since its worth 20% of your grade. The final was mostly questions from midterms so review those! If you are looking into a chem related major, take it from him; its hard but well worth it.

Great class! It was a very challenging class. It was not particularly fun, because it pushed me beyond my limits. But now i understand, very well, the concepts. Dr. Woodfield is a very funny guy. He liked to give us pep talks or tell us to go teach our dates about the chemistry we just learned at the upcoming football game. I definitely recommend.

This is one of the few classes I have taken that actually stretched me and pushed my understanding and epistemology.  Hard class.  Great class.  Professor Woodfield explains everything in math. His pep talks are the best.
Well...I didn't like the separation of ions aspect of things at the end of semester...
He was probably the hardest professor I ever had, but luckily he explained concepts pretty well.  His homework is hard, though.

I really enjoyed Dr. Woodfield. he went deep into his subject. He made sure students really understood what they were doing when they answered a problem by making sure all of the assumptions were challenged. Warning: the class is heavily calculus based. That said, he improved understanding of basic chem & prepared me for future classes. Great teach

Dr Woodfield was out of town for about a third of the lectures so we had to listen to grad students. Our first midterm had a B- average and he was outraged that we did so well. The remaining tests were significantly harder. He shoved a semester's worth of labs into the last 2 weeks of class because he forgot! Take someone else for Chem 105/106!
Easily the best professor I have ever had. Very passionate about chemistry. Very helpful. The assignments and tests are very fair even though they can be challenging sometimes.

Hmm. He is extremely passionate about chemistry, and it rubs off on you. Tests are hard, not definitely doable if you work hard. I think that's his point for making them hard. Virtual Chemlab is sort of useless, not entirely, but mosttly. Decent lecturer. If you want to really learn the material, take it from him. Tough bite, though.

Dr. Woodfield is known to be tough and I know that other students strongly dislike him but I really like how he teaches. He uses conceptual patterns to teach and can't use many examples because of time. You often have to learn a few new concepts for the homework but nothing unreasonable. I never read a page of the book. I would recommend him.

Dr. Woodfield spends 10-20 minutes of every 50 minute class talking about himself and how amazing he is. He focuses heavily on his own work (Virtual Chem Lab), which is pretty useless. He is condescending when students ask questions. He frequently gives misinformation in class, and the tests are heavy on non-chemistry topics. Avoid him if possible.

Mr. Woodfield enjoyed teaching but he would teach things quickly sometimes and leave the students in the dark on wha he was actually talking about. I recommend reading the book even though about a third of what you read is not improtant for the class and pay attention in the class as much as possible.

Overall i liked this class.He is very passionate about chem isnt afraid to show it.Class is very hard though.4 hours of homework a week if you dont really care, 7 if you actually want to learn.Take notes from the beginning of the homework each week if you want a good grade in the class.Get equations from the book for each chapter. Time=good grade!

Expect to have atleast 6 hours of homework a week online. Go to TA recitation sections for help on working out actual problems. Actually read the book and stay on schedule, even though he says the book is wrong. He likes to give homework questions on concepts he hasn't even covered in class. Pay CLOSE attention during class, he tests on lecture.

Not knowing anything about Chemistry made his class one of the toughest classes I've ever taken.  He expects people to know what he's teaching or to figure it out on their own.He LOVES chemistry and is willing to talk to you but if you don't love Chemistry and don't work hard you will struggle with him.  I did like his personality though.

Hardest class I've taken in my life! Woodfield is passionate about chem, and expects you to be too (ie devoting any extra time to it). Doesn't always get the right answers when he's explaining hw. Intimidating. However, he's surprisingly helpful if you go see him in person.
He likes to go off on random tangents, homework help sessions are useless with him but his TA is great!

He was the hardest professor I have ever taken, not because I don't know the subject matter but because I got nothing out of this class. He doesn't help and his lectures are mostly out of book. His exams are silly because they aren't related to class materials or book.

Worst professor I have ever had! First day of class he tells you not to pay attention to the things said on ratemyprofessor.com. You really should listen. He gets off topic and doesn't use the book. He wastes tons of class time and then expects to you learn the material all on your own...which is kinda hard since he doesn't use th book.

Woodfield is difficult and challenges his students. You never really use the text in class, and he hates Atkins (the author). If you ever ask him a question in class be sure to think through it first because he is rather condescending.

Horrible experience. He doesn't follow any structure at all for his classes, and it's very difficult to weed out the meaningless information from the  information that actually pertains to the course. I would have failed for sure if I hadn't been also enrolled in Chem 113.

Prof. Woodfield is not that good of a teacher because he goes way over everyone's heads just be prepared for that. The good thing about this class is that the final grade is relative or curved. Therefore even if it means going to another professor's lectures, this professor does have a handy grading scale for such a tough subject.

I really enjoyed this class.  Dr. Woodfield is extremely smart and a little intimidating.  He has the tendency to teach stuff way over your head and then he accelerates so that you definitely won't understand. The course, however, is well-designed and prepares you well for the tests, which are hard and MATHY.  Tough class but I learned TONS.

Professor Woodfield was great at explaining things in a way that kept class interesting. His demo's were really helpful although the best one by far was the superfluid Helium that he did in class. If you actually do the problems in the book the class is amazingly easy, and made even easier by his explanations of the chapters in class.
Hard, but good. Thermodynamics is tough, but that's thermodynamics. Good teacher. It's a weeding class, so yeah, it's hard, but 112 is a breeze if you get through 111.

Most frankly, Woodfield is extremely arrogant. He is a very intelligent man, but this seems to have gone to his head. His tests are long and difficult and for some reason he has a personal vendetta against multiple choice questions. I was happy when the class was over.

Professor Woodfield has an obvious love of chemistry. I appreciated his enthusiasm. Unfortunately I felt the class organization, grading, and test material was entirely enigmatic. It felt he was intentionally trying to trick us by withholding information, being vague about tests, and being unpredictable. The average on his "easy" final was a D...

Great professor. We covered the same topics I had studied last year in AP chem, but we went into so much more detail, and I learned a ton more. He focuses more on understanding why certain equations are used and where they came from rather than just memorizing them and taking them at face value. I loved the class.

Very hard course. Plan as if the class is a 4.5 credit class, homework is nothing like the examples in the textbook or the ones in class. Lectures are very interesting. Exams are difficult. If you want an A study 20+ hours a week. Make sure you have a very flexible schedule so you can have time for help with Dr. Woodfield, TA's are helpful.
Great teacher. Really cares in how much you learn. Not so much the grade you earn.

Woodfield is a hard teacher, and I think he likes that reputation.  He is interested in helping you learn, his tests aren't easy (they are all free response, but that means partial credit!)  If you like Virtual Chemlab, you'll love this class (He wrote the thing and isn't afraid to use it).

Very good professor. Teaches concepts very clearly and very in depth.  Only weakness is how much he loves VChem, which is understandable I guess cause he wrote it.   The students who say he is unapproachable outside of class are probably right, but he does such a thorough job in class that no one needs to ask him for help .
dr. woodfield rocks! his tests are exactly what he teaches in class, so if you go, you will be fine in the class
Great Teacher.  His class is really hard but you learn so much.  He teaches you to learn the material and understand it rather than memorize it.  It's definitely worth the effort to take his class.

He's great. You would think that being a science teacher that he is that he'd be boring but he has a good sense of humor and he makes chemistry fun. Some people think that he's vain because he mentions VCL quite a bit in class but VCL really is useful and fun. I definitely recommend taking chem 111 & 112 from him.

At the beginning of the year he warned us about this website. But, I have found it all to be true. He is vain. He answers questions in a demeaning way.  His class attendance is terrible.  Often turned teaching over to his nervous TAs. His truancy was very unprofessional. His teaching is unique, not bad.  His tests have a sinister side to them.
Hard but really interesting.

Woodfield is very effective at teaching.  You never know what will be on his tests and they are very difficult.  The homework didn't follow the text at the beginning of the semester, which meant receiving lots of help from TAs.  He was out of town for Chem Lab so much he couldn't be too helpful but he was helpful when approached.

This was a hard class, but i learned a lot. The tests are killer, but it all turns out okay since he grades on a relative curve. he is a great guy who wants his students to LEARN rather than PERFORM. there is no surface learning in this class.

He's very vain.  I've never had a professor that talked about himself as much as Dr. Woodfield.  I'm sure he's smart, but he could have talked more about the material and less about how important his research is.  He seemed to think he was to important to help students, and would send us to the TA even if they didn't know what they were doing.

Dr. Woodfield's class is a lot of fun because he is so enthusiastic about what he teaches. His love for the subject helped me learn more than I would have. The class is pretty hard but not impossible if you stay on top of the reading and homework. Woodfield is a GREAT guy and is quite willing to help students that approach him.

MR. WOODFIELD IS THE WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD.  I once went to his office asking for help.  I asked if I could talk to him.  He said, while dusting a plant, "only if its just a second."  Who does that.  He is a jerk and his class is so confusing.  DO NOT TAKE CHEMISTRY FROM WOODFIELD.  It would be easier on yourself to bite off your arm.

Moves fast and forgets that sometimes people don't have the chemistry background for the terms he uses, but overall a good teacher for the course. Explained concepts in such a way that my understanding of the material was far better than before (2 high school classes of it). Good tests (after curve), enjoyed ChemLab, a few too many trips.

Woodfield knows what he is teaching but goes way to fast and doesn't take time to explain the details. Do your homework and read the book and go to the help sessions and you should do fine. Tests are hard  but the curves help out a lot. Don't talk in the class he does get mad! He will occasionaly cancel class due to trips he makes.
Brian stands as the crappiest teacher I have ever had.

The guy is a jerk.  "Who's the only one that can measure heat capacities in the world???" Who cares?  He tests you on things that he swears he went over in lecture but proboably never did.  He's never wiling to help out.  The worst teacher I've had at BYU.

Woodfield is great. He really knows his stuff, which makes him make the course a little more challenging that it probably *needs* to be. But I wouldn't take it with anyone else. His tests are harder than the book, but you will be fine if you take lecture notes. Plus he hardcore curves some of them.
He thinks he is the smartest man alive.  Just ask him about Virtual Chem Lab.
hard teacher, but helps a lot with help sessions and required homework.

He's a smart ass. He says he's always available but he's not. When you ask him for help he gives you a sassy comment and brushes you off. His tests are all written, though it is reasonable. He doesn't grade you according to test scores or homework. He compares you to the rest of the class.
No Comments

Dr. Woodfield is a great guy. His lectures are entertaining and helpful. TAKE GOOD CLASS NOTES. However Dr. Wood is so busy all the time that getting help from him is hard. If you ask him for help during office hours he tries to get you out as quickly as he can. He's not real patient.

His teaching was good, but he covered stuff not in the textbook. When you try to get help from him, he isn't very willing to sit down and walk through problems. He just tries to get you out of his office asap. if you don't need help he's a decent teacher. Boreo-goates is better.

This class is 99% memorization. It's definitely way harder than it needs to be. Don't take this if you're not planning on spending 8+ hours a week. If you want an easy art GE, take ARTED 326. I took both, and I'm shocked they're the same GE and have the same credits. She rarely comes to class, especially for the last lab.

Easy GE class for an art credit, definitely recommend. I felt like the TAs did mostly everything.  I loved the labs and being able to put flower arrangements together, but lectures felt like a waste of time. The ID test was the hardest part of this class. I didn't take the tests as seriously as I should have. (you will need to study).

Super easy ge class for the spring! She talks more about business than about floral design, and makes designs as she talks, without explaining the methods she's using. I didn't use the textbook and did fine, just use the study guide to take good notes. TAs honestly do most of the work and provide lots of ways to remember flower ID.

Brianna Hall is the best professor I've had at BYU. She's super knowledgeable about the floral industry. The TAs are really helpful for exams and ID quizzes. Tests aren't bad if you put in effort and there's no busy work. She is so kind and Christlike and truly cares about her students. I'm sad I'm not in her class anymore. Definitely take her!!

This class is super fun I highly recommend! Brianna is so sweet and was a great teacher. My one complaint is the three lecture exams are SO hard and kept me from getting an A in the class. There is a ton of content and I felt like a lot of the questions were super tricky. Be prepared for a lot of studying if you're going to take this class.

Honestly this class was a little harder than I thought. She's not really organized and doesn't allow you to have access to her slides. It's also confusing what's gonna be on her tests because she picks the most tiny details that I couldn't remember if we even talked about. She does drop a test which is nice, but idk if I would take again

floral design was the cutest and such a fun GE. it was one of the easiest GEs i have taken and Brianna Hall was super nice and very planned out schedule wise. the only hard part of the class was the identification quizzes but honestly they weren't too bad. attendance isn't mandatory for lecture but it is for the lab portion.

Brianna is so sweet. She really cares about her students. Lectures aren't required, you can do the reading instead if you want. Tests are 100 questions and kind of hard, but the lowest score is dropped. Labs are super fun, but be prepared for the floral ID quizzes, requires a lot of studying, but not too bad if you study. Would highly recommend:)

If you never have any issues or extenuating circumstances, the professor seems super nice and caring. The second you have an issue, her nice person persona disappears. The TAs, for some reason, all only have free time at the exact same time 1 day a week, so it's difficult to make up work without accruing a ton of late points.

This class was a great option for a GE! There are three exams and two floral ID quizzes that were a little tough, but one exam gets dropped. Each week there's a lab where you make a floral arrangement and it's so fun! The TAs were super helpful and lectures were fun.

Brianna is the best! So kind! But this class is hard. The exams are difficult and the ID exam is graded harshly with focus on capitalization and spelling. Don't take this class for fun. Its not just learning about flowers and arrangements, its learning how to start a floral business, so if thats what you're looking for great. Not what I expected.

Labs are easy and arrangements are so much fun to take home. The only complaints I have are the difficulty of the exams, they are a large portion of the grade and even when following the study guide there were parts of the exam you wouldn't know unless you read every inch of the textbook. She does drop the lowest exam score though!

The lectures were boring. The tests are designed to trick you. The two flower ID tests are fine, but the 3 exams were dishonest. They ask niche questions that aren't necessarily in lecture (they might be buried in the textbook). The flower labs are fun but you might as well learn yourself or ask someone you know who does weddings (common in provo)

Don't let the reviews scare you! This class is not bad for an art credit. Tests are tough and require you to study but they were easier than my other classes. There are 2 ID quizzes where you have to identify different flowers. These are tough but doable if you study! Attendance isn't required for lectures but they are fun!

LOVED this class! You do best if you read the textbook chapters, but she gives very clear reviews/content which is helpful. I learned a ton; labs are really fun. She is super caring and puts time networking with students wanting to move farther into floral design. She is AMAZING! I enjoyed the workload. In my top 3 classes, and I'm a senior.

Professor is super nice. However the class is unnecessarily difficult. It often feels like she is trying to trick you. The identification tests seem more like they are set up to trick you than to help you learn the materials. If you don't already know a good amount about floral design it will be an unnecessarily hard class.

It's a fun class that's probably easier than a lot of other art GE's, but I wasn't a huge fan of the way that tests were run. It required a lot of rote memorization. It's not hard if you're good at memorizing. It was a lot of fun to do the flower labs and bring your arrangements home though!

This class was a crash course in plant biology, floral history, and business. TONS of reading. Two major (but easy) identification quizzes. Three midterms, 100Q's each all multiple choice. The midterms felt like memorizing lots of random trivia, but she'll give a lot of answers in class if you pay attention. The labs are super fun and very doable.

Brianna cares about her students and is passionate about what she's teaching. I loved the flower ID exams because I felt like they applied directly to real life. The textbook exams were kind of annoying though... felt more like I was being tested on if I could remember exactly how something was phrased in the book/lecture rather than concepts.

This is a fantastic class to take if you need a break from the stress of other classes. I learned so much in this class and feel like I will be able to call back on it throughout my life. Brianna is a great professor who cares about her students and their learning and success. The lab especially is lots of fun and a great way to spoil others.

This class was awesome and Brianna is so sweet. The tests were kind of annoying, and the ID quizzes were also frustrating. BUT, it was one of the most fun classes I have taken. Lots of TA help, and the labs are really fun!

Professor is super nice & knowledgable. Wants to help you succeed. Sometimes participation points- syllabus will say which days. Tons of memorization of flower names. Floral labs are once a week and super fun, plus you get to take home the stuff you make. Tests are the study guide. More work than I thought but def worth taking.

This class was more work than I thought but the labs were SO FUN! You'll get free stuff :)Have to memorize lots of flower names. Open note reading quizzes due before each class. Get the online version of the textbook and command F for the answers to the study guide rather than reading the whole chapter. Everything on the test is on the study guide.

Loved this class! Reading and study guide help prepare for tests. Lectures are not mandatory but labs are. You get to bring home flowers and learn a great skill. TA's are great. You have to memorize flowers (look, common name, scientific name) but not too hard. Great class to take if you want to have fun. Lectures were fascinating.

Professor Hall is really kind. Her class is harder than anticipated, but she gives you all of the resources to be successful. There is reading each week, it always seems like a lot but there are lots of pictures. She does in class quizzes, drops 1, if you go look at your quizzes they are the exact questions from her exam. Always willing to help.

Brianna is a decently nice person, but this class was a joke. A ridiculous amount of reading and memorization. She was willing to answer questions, but it seemed like it always bothered her. She criticized our whole class after the first exam for getting a lower average than normal despite her giving us a study guide. Easier than other art GEs but.

Brianna is really great, but her class is a lot tougher than expected. Be prepared to memorize 80+ flowers with their common names, scientific names, inflorescence, and name origins. The tests are pretty easy but the ID quizzes require a ton of studying. And there are reading quizzes every class period, so don't show up unprepared.

This class is the best! The labs are fun and Brianna is a great professor. I would highly recommend taking this class. Brianna is very caring and gives great feedback. There are in-class lecture quizzes so you need to read and study the textbook chapter. You have to put in work just like you would any other class but this class is worth it!

I LOVED this class. I've never had a more caring professor. Brianna is really passionate about floral design and you can tell she has tons of experience. If you have any questions she is more than willing to tell you what she knows. If you ever need anything just talk to her and she is so kind and understanding. My favorite class at BYU!

This class was really great. She is passionate about floral design. I took it in the Spring which seems to be easier than a full length semester. She is so sweet and caring. Not a breeze, but way easier than any other Art GE.
Brianna is awesome! Great teacher for a great class.
He was amazing. Lots of reading but we had deep discussions every time that helped me grow and become better and see the world in a new light.
I cried so much. Grades hard.

I loved taking Brice's class!  There is reading for every class that can be really long but it's manageable. He makes expectations for all assignments and tests very clear so there are no surprises. He is super fun and clearly cares about his students. He has really good insights on the texts and made class super interesting!

Brice has the best lectures and i learned so much. There was a lot of reading but he actually taught us how to read effectively, and especially how to write analytically. Super helpful class if you want to become a better writer and he makes you think so deeply about literature. Show up and be engaged and you will do fine.

So absurdly kind and supportive of his students.  He cares about wellness and wants everyone to feel calm and accepted in his class, but he doesn't talk down to anyone.  Brice expects his students to work hard and some of the assignments are definitely graduate level stuff.  If you're planning on doing grad school, this is great prep.

Brice is PHENOMENAL. I have yet to take a course from a professor that compares to the lectures Brice teaches. He ensures an energetic and caring environment wherein students feel comfortable to share and discuss. The course was difficult, but I find that Shakespeare normally is. If you want to become a better writer, take a course from Brice.

This was my favorite class I have taken at BYU. It was hard! And I did not read/study as much as I should have but Brice is the best teacher here. Every lecture was engaging and fun and made me LOCK IN. He is wonderful and so intelligent and you will 10000% come out of this GE with applicable skills that can be applied to any major. 100% Recommend.
Classes are very engaging! Really created a desire to learn the material! Many things learned in this class that I will apply to social, academic, and spiritual life!

Brice was one of the best professors I have ever had! His lectures are so engaging and I feel like I learned so much from him. He really cares about his students and truly wants everyone to be successful. He was always willing to work with me when I needed anything. He is a tough grader, but I learned a lot from his feedback. I loved his class!

I adore Dr. Peterson. His grading was tough, but he was so good at teaching and providing help for students who needed it. His lectures were always super entertaining, it was the one class I never missed. Dr. Peterson helped me so much to become a better reader and writer. I'm actively looking for more ways I can take his classes in the future.

I really enjoyed the lectures given by Professor Peterson. There was a lot of reading, but it was doable. What got me were the tests. They were way too difficult for a 200 level English class and made my grade drop drastically. He wasn't willing to let me redo anything or help me in any way and told me to withdraw from the class instead of helping.

Brice is honestly the best. While he can be a surprisingly tough grader, I feel I became a better reader and writer (and citizen of the world) because of his class. He has a way of making complex and confusing topics clear. While he grades like a tyrant on papers, the midterm and final were pretty easy and he provided a lot of study help.

Loved this class so much! Brice is a great professor that's very understanding and makes class engaging. There is a reading due for each class, and pretty much every class is a discussion on that reading, but it's always interesting. Essays weren't graded too harshly as long as you spent good time on them.

Gender/race tangents led the class discussions. We learned Shakespeare on a social justice level and not much else. Brice is accessible, but it felt like you wouldn't get a good grade unless you argued for his beliefs in your papers (it felt like he was working against you if you disagreed with him). Seriously - take a different GE.

I have taken Brice's classes several times and love his lectures. He truly makes things relatable to his students. He does have few assignments that are weighted very heavily which makes grades challenging. However, he is always available to help students outside of class to discuss papers before and after they're due--take advantage of this!

Brice is the best professor I've had! He sees and expects the best in his students. He grades tough but gives detailed feedback on how you can improve. His classes are engaging, participation-based, and student-driven. If you have the opportunity to take a class from Brice, do it! You'll come out of it a much better student, writer, and individual.

Dr. Peterson is /amazing/ and I cannot stress that enough. He's easily one of my favorite professors in all of undergrad. The only downside is that he is and EXTREMELY tough grader; I'd argue he expects students to write at a graduate level. Other than that, he's a phenomenal and engaging lecturer and is very accessible outside of class. 4.5 stars!

Brice has been one of my favorite teachers and this class was definitely my favorite class I've ever taken at BYU. He is a tough grader for papers but he does it in a way that will help you improve your writing. He created such a safe, kind space in the classroom which was vital because we discussed some very hard and controversial topics.
The content of the class may seem intimidating, but it makes you such a better writer.

Brice is one of my favorite professors, and his Women in Shakespeare class is one of the best classes I have ever taken. I'm not exaggerating. My classmates and I still talk about how much we loved it months later. The EEBO project especially is so much fun! Ask him for help on your papers!!! He's understanding and his classes are safe places.

Don't let the difficulty rating fool you: Brice Peterson is one of my favorite professors at BYU. He is an incredibly tough grader, but he wants you to succeed. He gives the best feedback, loves meeting with students, and wants you to succeed. My writing has improved more during his class than it has the other 2 1/2 years I've been at BYU.

I took ENGL 303 with Brice and loved it so much that I took ENGL 384R with him, too. His engaging teaching style, knowledge, and accessibility make him an excellent professor. Classes were discussion based, and he was easy to reach outside of class. Grades are based on a few major assignments, but he will work with you so you can succeed.

I actually did the readings in ENGLISH 303 instead of skimming sparknotes because Brice assigned digestible, relevant material, and the environment he created made me to want to bring something intelligent to class discussions. Papers had tight rubrics but loose prompts, tricky to figure out at first, but eventually became a huge help

Brice is an amazing professor who provides thoughtful lectures and creates a community of learning. Topics were approached with sensitivity and fostered genuine learning. He is a tough grader for papers, but is always willing to work with students to improve. His feedback helped my writing more than any other class. I would highly recommend.

Dr. Peterson has very clear expectations for the class and for assignments. He is very transparent on all procedures and meets with students often (we only need to email and set an appointment). I loved studying women in Shakespeare's plays. The papers and projects all stack together nicely to prepare you for final projects. Class was always fun!

Professor Peterson is an incredible teacher. He expects high quality work, but he is willing to help his students achieve this. I've never had more feedback and help from a teacher. His class discussions are fun and educational.

I took Brice Peterson's Women in Shakespeare class and it was absolutely one of my favorite classes. In lecture you can feel how passionate Brice is about the subject and it made the class feel engaging and almost family-like. The discussions were awesome and although the class was tough and reading heavy, it was worth it. Gave great feedback too!

Brice (as he prefers to be called) is unabashedly my favorite professor. He genuinely cares for his students and his course subject, every lecture felt like a valued discussion. He's a tough grader, but I came out of each assignment with a clearer understanding of how to write better. I'm taking another class of his this fall. 15/10 professor.

Brice is very nice and willing to help on assignments but I would never take his class again. There are too few assignments and they HEAVILY affect your grade. Also, his lectures are often side-tracked or overrun by the students' comments. This isn't necessarily negative if you prefer discussion over lectures, but just something to keep in mind.

It was awesome in lecture! Class was mostly discussion-based & always interesting. Brice made sure that people were heard and that we analyzed the work from many different angles. However, he is a really tough grader, & there's not very many assignments. I LOVED his lectures, but the grades were too much. If that changes, I'd take his class again.

SO MANY ESSAYS. Also, Im an introvert. If you sign up for his class, make sure youre ready to participate A TON (he WILL call on you). But overall, he is an amazing professors. Youd have to do all the essays no matter which WRTG 150 class you go into so Ill for sure recommend him.

Dr. Peterson is one of my fav profs! This class had a lot of papers but he gives GREAT feedback that helps improve future papers. I LEARNED HOW TO BE SUCH A BETTER WRITER BECAUSE OF HIM which's helped me in other classes (and I'm a non-English major). The exams were super easy - almost the whole class got A's. Lots of discussions so do the reading!

I loved this class and Bridger. I would seriously recommend taking it, because it forces you to do beneficial reading and learning that is important, but that you probably wouldn't take time to do on your own. I learned a lot that has helped me with my Freshman year, and the class discussions are very enlightening.

Talbot was a great teacher. He had so much applicable experience and expertise who made the class interesting and engaging. I was always impressed by home he valued every comment or opinion in class, even when I was annoyed by a student or felt they were being rude. Such a great class, and a must take for freshman!

I took this class for the credit and easy A and was not disappointed. Professor Talbot is so lenient and accessible outside of class. I learned more about campus and myself. There are occasional papers that are due but they're very chill and he grades so easily. 10/10 would recommend.

This man taught my Univ 101 class, and it was relatively easy. The papers can get annoying, but they were graded leniently. He tried to make the class fun, but due to the nature of the class it was not an easy task.

Great class--I would highly recommend taking 388 from Frandsen. That said, it is obviously a really hard class so be sure to budget your time accordingly. Tests were not tricky; there is just a lot of content you need to know to succeed on them.

Dr. Frandsen is one of the best teachers in the econ program. Lectures are digestible and insanely interesting. Don't take this class if you don't have enough time. Problem sets were long and confusing. Tests were segmented into a written and a coding portion (coding was take-home), both extremely time-consuming. Lots of content--should be 4 credit

This class is very challenging but it is also incredibly rewarding. Dr. Frandsen is very knowledgeable on this topic so he is able to make difficult concepts digestible to my pea-sized brain. The tests are tough but they are fair and they are very reflective of his practice tests. The projects are straightforward and you only need to skim the book.
His class is taught but is also incredibly rewarding. He is very knowledgable and he cares very much about his students. He is amazing

This is the guy to take 388 from. His class made me a better economist in terms of critical thinking. The tests were very much like the problem sets and practice tests. Knows the subject matter in and out and teaches it well. Make sure to read before every class.

Dr. Frandsen's class struggled with pacing and has a heavy theory focus (handwritten proofs). Coding felt secondary to the unnecessarily long book assignments. Econometrics-focused ML crammed at the end made the research project tough. Great guy, but better ML options at BYU exist unless you really want to do an econ PHD.

Python should be a prereq. The course is theory-heavy with little ML application. Most assignments took 5+ hours, it felt like a harder Econ 398. I learned a lot, but unless you're PhD-bound, consider auditing or taking another ML class. Frandsen is chill but unwilling to ease the load. Daily quizzes focused on obscure details from long readings.
Brigham's class was amazing and made sure to clearly explain all of the concepts. The class is very interesting and requires a lot of effort but it is very rewarding in the end.
If someone told me Brigham Frandsen was one of the three Nephites, I wouldn't question it at all.

Should probably be teaching at MIT. I say this in the kindest way possible, but I think BYU students are on an intellectual plane several rungs lower than Brigham Frandsen. He does his very best to turn our slack-jawed stares and hollow expressions into some modicum of understanding, but at the end of the day, he really is a man among children.

Beware of this class if you're not confident in your econometrics math skills!! I did fine in 388 and 488, but this class was a monster and way exceeded the level of difficulty of any other class I've taken. If I had a better handling of the math, I'm sure I would have had a great experience in this class.

Everyone in Econ should take 484. It's by far the most useful class in the major. Don't worry about python, he teaches you most of the things you'll ever need to use for the class in Python. If you pay attention, you should get a 100 on the take home computational midterm and final. The written portion is difficult but not worth that much.

Professor Frandsen is awesome. Taking clear notes in lectures is a must. Occasional pop-quizzes, I would skim the chapter for 1-2 hours before each class and did well. He explains everything you need to know in class so don't miss. Memorize the proofs and derivations. It is a little math heavy but take great notes and study them and you'll do well!

I like Dr. Frandsen, but he's an econometrician. The lectures are good, homework is not too hard. The group research project was fun as well. Expected an easy A, but the final was take home, open book/note/google, the hardest final I've ever taken, and me and all my buddies bombed it. Great content though if you want to learn machine learning.

484 is crazy statistical theory meets python coding. Never spent more time on homework than in this class- unbelievable amount of math + coding. That said, I also took 388 from him and Dr. Frandsen is a gem: extremely clear, organized, caring, beyond smart. Great class, but be prepared to put in time especially if you have no coding background.

Dr. Frandsen is a great 588 professor. There is a massive curve, so most people get an A (at least the top third of the class). Some of the proofs are hard, but he only tests you on the easy ones. The problem sets are also very hard and take forever, so everyone just went to the TA and he did them for us. The tests were easy, just 1 long problem.

Dr. Frandsen is an incredible 388 professor, especially if you are planning to pursue a phD. He is pretty mysterious about what is on exams, but it is essentially just 1 long problem that will walk you through everything you've learned. I found that you could just look at the schedule for the lecture to do well on the quizzes instead of reading.

A caring guy who teaches with sharp clarity. His lectures contain everything you will need to know for the tests. Writing down everything he writes on the whiteboard during the semester is all you will have to know to do well on tests. Not the book. The homework's difficult, but most test material isn't from hw. Class attendance mandatory to excel.

If you aren't double majoring in Math and Econ, or aren't planning on getting a PHD, then don't take this class from him. His teaching style is geared towards those type of individuals (aka not me). So, his lectures are great, but then once you get to the homework and tests you have no clue what you're doing. Grading is super nit-picky and unclear!

Dr. Frandsen is brilliant and a very clear teacher. That said, his criticisms on this page are valid-- He weights the final and final project as over 50% of your grade so you have no idea where you are at most of the year. He doesn't do a good job of teaching STATA programming and leaves you on your own. He is very mysterious about test content.

You won't have any clue as to what your grade is until after the semester ends. His grading is stuffed heavily to the last week--research projects are due then and the final is worth a huge percentage of your grade. Not a great of a professor. A lot of people like him, but I would avoid him in any future classes.

Dr. Frandsen is easily the worst econ professor at BYU that I have ever talked to. His grading requirements are random and there is no way to know what he will take points off for. Students who rate the exact same answers may get different grades. If you happen to learn in the way that he teaches you get something. If not, none of it makes sense

Frandsen is a great lecturer--very clear. That's the main reason to take 388 from him. Probably the best of the 388 teachers. Problem sets are hard, just pray you get a helpful TA. Get your data for your project as early as possible.

Econometrics is a difficult subject, but Dr. Frandsen really makes it interesting, and his lectures are engaging. (I didn't understand 378 very well at all, but that wasn't a problem - he basically reteaches it with more intuition.) The main points from the readings will be quizzed in class. Go to him for help with your project - he wants to help.

Frandsen really knows his stuff and he'll help you a lot if you ask.  I only wish the class was more applied and less theoretical and we were able to spend more time and slow down instead of covering so many topics.

He's a great professor. The class is difficult. If you're on the fence about taking it, don't. It's all of the nasty mathematical derivations that you mostly skip over in 388 and 488. A lot of linear algebra. A must if you're planning on doing a Ph.D. Otherwise, I'd recommend taking a different 400-level class. He teaches it as well as possible.

DO NOT take from Frandsen. The tests were very difficult and although he said there would be a curve at the end of the semester there wasn't (probably the hardest class in the major and not curved??). Super picky grader and will mark you off for dumb things. Long paper/project isn't bad, also dont buy the book.

Dr. Frandsen Is an amazing teacher! His tests and homework are hard. Its almost like you have to guess what he wants you to do. But It gives you a great opportunity to stretch.  During the semester he was hurt so we had other professors sub in for him and by far he is the better teacher.  He curves the class so dont worry if your grade is low.

388 is just downright hard, no matter who you take it from.  Frandsen is good at giving examples to talk you through difficult principles though.  His tests are hard, but once again, that's just the game of econometrics.  Commonly referred to as the best 388 professor.

Prof. Frandsen is an amazing lecturer. He somehow manages to take a difficult concept to teach and breaks it down in a way that is very easy to understand. Tests are hard, but he makes the class manageable.

Prof. Frandsen is an awesome teacher.  He is very intelligent, but he is also very clear in the way that he teaches the material.  The tests are difficult and the class takes a lot of work and effort.  I didn't understand Econ378 at all, but I was able to understand this material lots better because of the way that he teaches. Great class.
Incredible teacher.  Extremely clear and organized.  Literally couldn't have done this class without him. Absolutely changed my view of the major. Highly recommend him!

Great Professor! He teaches a lot of material but breaks it down so that you can understand it. Since there is so much material it is great that he reviews everything in class multiple times and the tests are fair.

Frandsen is a fantastic professor! This class is hard no matter who you take it from, but he knows his stuff and is always willing to help. Attend class, go to the reviews and work with the TAs and you will do just fine. I would take another class from him!

Profe Morales is caring and appreciative of students. She is easy to talk to and wants the best for all of her students. If she notices a student that is struggling, she will ask them how she can help them perform better. high love + high expectations

i love profesora morales. she is so kind and so sweet. the beginning of the semester goes a little slow in terms of homework, but then about halfway in, it picks up a lot. there's 4 essays and several little readings with easy quizzes. definitely would take a class from her again if possible

Sweetest woman ever, but I didn't learn much from her class. I felt like she was just teaching things in lectures to fill the time, not because it was actually important to know. We wrote a lot of papers, which she graded very harshly. Honestly, I learned more from the professors at the writing lab who reviewed my papers than I did from her.
I was really scared by this class at first, but she's a great, caring professor

She's awesome. Yes, she calls on you in class and attendance matters, but other than that this class was 3 very simple essays and various mindless spanish grammar LS quizzes which you can fly through. Wants you to do well. Everytime I messed up understanding something, she would let me know and give me time to redo it so I got full points. 10/10

She really cares about helping her students learn better grammar. She is a tough grader for the essays, which are weighed the heaviest. She seems intimidating at first, but is actually really nice and understanding. Be ready to pay attention and participate because she calls on people.

Professor Morales was wonderful. She genuinely wants to help her students learn Spanish. She was great at getting students to participate and was available outside of class to help as well. She cares for her students and wants to see them succeed. The class wasn't too difficult, just expect a light reading before each class.
Class was so fun, so easy too - you could literally just come and sit on your mat and just work on your breathing. You only get to miss 5 classes so be careful with that.

Grades are based on a multiple-choice 30 questions online final exam with notes. A super sweet teacher who is just happy you came to class. You can literally take a nap on your yoga mat and she doesn't care. You get 5 absences a semester or you automatically fail so beware! Definitely would take it again. Super easy class.
Brittany is so sweet and made this class a dream!! Highly recommend!!

Brittany is the SWEETEST! She just wants her students to show up and get whatever they want out of yoga. I loved coming to class because it gave my mind a boost for the day! Watch the # of absences you have (you only get 5 for the semester). Final is crazy easy!!! LOVE HER

Brittany is the best. She knows what she is doing and helps you to achieve whatever you want to get out of yoga. She also doesn't take yoga too seriously and makes it fun! Take yoga from Brittany! You will gain so much from her and yoga and you won't regret it. She is my favorite teacher I have ever had. Just show up to class and you will pass.

Professor is very responsive via email! If you need help just ask. Total there were 7 exams(final included), 12 quizzes(listening/reading), 6 discussions, online lectures, and a music project. All exams used respondus and requires camera, but the quizzes do not. I took the minimester and it was good. About 3 days between due dates, fast paced.

This class was so fun because Dr. May fully immerses you in the elementary classroom experience. Her lectures are amazingly cohesive and organized, and I learned so much from this class that I know I'll use in the future.

She is a professor that definitely cares about her students and teaches for the right reason. She doesn't teach to prepare you for exams, but she teaches in such a way that makes learning fun, interesting, and quite an enjoyable experience where you are learning for the sake of learning. I HIGHLY recommend her!

I really liked the course, but I could tell this was her first year teaching this course at BYU. She was very accommodating when I needed to miss class, and didn't beat me over the head when I happened to be lazy and miss class (8am happens).  I really didn't like the saturday observations, but I could see where they would be useful.

Professor is very responsive via email! If you need help just ask. Total there were 7 exams(final included), 12 quizzes(listening/reading), 6 discussions, online lectures, and a music project. All exams used respondus and requires camera, but the quizzes do not. I took the minimester and it was good. About 3 days between due dates, fast paced.

This class was so fun because Dr. May fully immerses you in the elementary classroom experience. Her lectures are amazingly cohesive and organized, and I learned so much from this class that I know I'll use in the future.

She is a professor that definitely cares about her students and teaches for the right reason. She doesn't teach to prepare you for exams, but she teaches in such a way that makes learning fun, interesting, and quite an enjoyable experience where you are learning for the sake of learning. I HIGHLY recommend her!

I really liked the course, but I could tell this was her first year teaching this course at BYU. She was very accommodating when I needed to miss class, and didn't beat me over the head when I happened to be lazy and miss class (8am happens).  I really didn't like the saturday observations, but I could see where they would be useful.

Professor Eldredge was amazing! She might be my favorite professor at BYU. She explained things very well and knew the content. She is wonderful at teaching, and it is also very clear that she loves her job and her students. Her spiritual thoughts were frequent, personal, and inspirational.

A fabulous teacher, especially for a hard class. The first exam was the hardest for me, but her teaching style is good and she tries to help us do well. Start preparing for the exams early. Exams are very different than how ACC 200 exams looked.

Took Eldredge for ACC 404 and ACC 540. She was amazing. First year teaching, but I think she did a great job. She is incredibly nice and explains difficult concepts well. You don't feel scared asking questions in her class.

Prof Eldredge is the GOAT. I took ACC 404 from her and she is the best teacher at teaching financial accounting I've had thus far. She explains tough concepts very well and somehow has an answer to every question every student had. She learns everyone's names and truly cares about everyone. Phenomenal teacher!

Amazing person who really cares about her students and presents the course in an approachable way. Very responsive and very good at helping you answer questions. BE WARNED - even if you excel at 200, 310 is still SUPER hard. It is super demanding and time consuming but manageable if you put the effort in. DONT underestimate the first exam it tricks

Professor Eldredge is a main reason why I chose to study accounting at BYU. She is an incredible professor and is so encouraging to students. She is knowledgeable and relatable to each of the students. Although tests are hard in 310, she does a great job at preparing you and helping you study. She uplifts students and builds confidence!

What a chill ahh professor. She always comes to class excited, which in turn makes you excited, and she explains things really well, always pausing to see if anyone has questions. 3 tests that are challenging, but she provides lots of material to prepare. pre class lessons and post class quizzes, but that's it, so its on you to learn and prepare.

I got an A in ACC 200 & was able to understand the concepts really well, but in this class I leave every class extremely confused. Professor Eldredge teaches in a way that convolutes the concepts I used to understand, & I'm really nervous for how the rest of the semester is going to go. Take ACC 310 from someone else.

Obviously Accounting 310 is a difficult class, but Professor Eldredge does a great job of teaching the class and supporting students. The 3 tests will be the biggest contributors to your overall grade, so study more for them than I did :)

Professor Eldredge has been my favorite accounting professor! Although this is a very difficult course, Professor Eldredge taught the content incredibly well. She made classes fun, and she was very relatable. She is an adjunct professor, so her real-world experience made for an educational class. I would highly recommend her.

Pro Eldridge is great, she lectures well and does a good job addressing questions. The class content itself is what makes the class hard. The 310 class is really test heavy for all professors, but it's all graded on a curve among all the teachers.

Professor Eldredge explains the material really well.  Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll want to come to class every time to understand the material.  The material is what makes this class hard, not the professor.  Highly recommend taking it from her!!
I really like Professor Argyle. Don't be afraid of him!

Easily one of the best teachers I've ever had! Loved his class! My favorite out of the 3 (401, 410, & 453). Not an easy course by any means, you have to work for it, but it teaches you to be financially literate and Argyle is the best. Tests can be tricky, avg. was usually around 80. Easy quiz each week. Group homework assignment each week also

Brooke is very nice but makes this a tough class. I never felt confident I would get the grade I wanted. There is no extra credit, it takes 94% to get an A (instead of the standard 93% I've seen in every other class), and even on papers where the feedback was something like "Great paper!" with no other comments I'd only get a 95%.

Brooke is a lovely person and obviously very knowledgeable, but WOW is she a tough grader. I followed the rubric exactly, but she still found ways to dock points from my papers. She also focused mainly on grammar lessons rather than actually teaching style, so a lot of the time I was relearning things I learned in 9th grade.

Brooke was mostly really great, but there were a few times when she seemed to lack knowledge in some of the deeper nuances of the topic and so the class ended up being more about grammar than style. There were times when it was mind-numbingly easy. She could also be abrupt and hard to read, but ultimately she was accommodating and nice.

Helped me become such a better writer! She teaches grammar lessons which are so helpful! Daily quizzes that aren't too difficult. She's so organized and really cares about making sure you do good in the class. She's really chill too. You do a literature review, resume, magazine spread, and proposal. I learned how to create a great resume!

Brooke was so awesome. This was my first class at BYU and she was super organized and helpful. Youre graded on 3 papers, daily reading quizzes, participation, and a final. She gives you tons of help if you just ask and she grades exactly how she says she will. Class was so fun every day, really discussion heavy. I highly recommend!

I love Brooke. She is super sweet and understanding. We met twice a week over Zoom and should would go over the schedule like every class so we were on top of everything. There are four main assignments-- literature review, resume, magazine spread, and a proposal. No exams. She teaches grammar lessons which were awesome!

Professor Downs (she prefers to go by Brooke) is a great individual. She is very open to different perspectives in class and will help you out any way she can. Now - regarding the class. You are assigned reading between every class and take bell quizzes each day on the reading. She grades 1) Quizzes 2) Participation 3) and three papers. A94%

I love Brooke! Her American Lit class is great. She is a really fair grader and as long as you do the readings before class (which aren't overwhelming at all) then you will do really good in her class! No tests or final, just 3 essays (about 3-4 pages each). There is a quiz on the reading each class period but they are really easy if you just read.

I really enjoyed this class. I read many things that I would not have otherwise been exposed to , and she gears the questions and discussions so you can talk about things that are interesting to you. She understands that the class is a GE, so she does not grade the papers too harshly, which make up most of the points. Amazing overall.

We read a lot of plays throughout the semester. We had a reading quiz every class day (you could skip 3), and you have to participate at least once a week to get a 100% in participation. There were three papers throughout the semester and she was a bit picky about grading, but overall it was fair.
Brooke was funny and enjoyable. I liked her class and hope to take more from her in the future.

Professor Downs is very passionate about the material and does a good job balancing lecture, discussion, and group work. She's not too tough of a grader either. There is a lot of writing in her course but why would you take creative writing if you don't enjoy it?

She doesn't give full credit on big assignments, so expect to fight for every point. Also, watch out for "extra" rules on papers she grades that are not specified in the rubric. She can be very cynical in dealing with students and uses poor examples from previous students as laughable examples in class :( Try to take this class from someone else!!

Prof Downs is way chill. Her Eng 202 class consists of several books. She takes a quiz at the beginning of each class. You can miss like 3 of them without needing to justify your absence/tardiness. Grading is based on quizzes, participation (class is like a book club), and then 3 essays. No final/midterm!!

This is my second class I've taken from Brooke, for good reason. She knows her stuff.  She really cares about her students; she reached out to me to make sure I was okay after I missed a couple classes and helped me to keep pushing through the semester.  She's a fair but generous grader when it comes to papers.

English 315 was great! Assignments are spaced out well & the hardest one is at the beginning.  Brooke is an excellent teacher and provides time to give you feedback. If you read (5-10 pages per class), come to class, and ask questions you will do well. There is no final and reading guides for all quizzes. I would recommend this class to everyone!

Brooke is a great teacher. Expect lots of feedback from her on your essays! Daily readings with really easy quizzes every class. Final exam is a group project that was very easy and very fun! I would absolutely take another class from her!
Brooke is a fabulous teacher. She's incredibly funny and obviously has a passion for what she teaches. I would recommend her to everyone. Honestly, one of the teachers I've had at BYU.

Brooke is extremely funny. She has a very dry sense of humor, she will say something hilarious and everyone will laugh except her... which makes it even funnier. There are lots of writing assignments but they aren't difficult and they are very fun! I would recommend this class to anyone who enjoys creative writing.

Avoid at all costs. Brooke just straight up does not know how to teach. She was so confusing about project instructions that people would come to class and literally everyone had done a different project. I feel like this class was detrimental for my portfolio and it sucks that I now have to apply to the program using projects from this class.

This class was so frustrating. I was super excited to take it and soon lost all my motivation. Brooke is very nice but she shouldn't be a teacher. She was all over the place and didn't know what she was talking about. She didn't even bring a laptop to class and would make a student screen share the slides. We hardly ever got class time for projects

She cares a lot about design and is so sweet but she cannot teach. She doesn't give good feedback on anything. Questions are met with tangents and repeated nonsense. Lectures are unhelpful as she reads from slides she didn't make and it's clear that she hasn't looked at any of the assignment descriptions and she constantly changes the requirements.
THE GOAT, test have a lot of material though

You can tell that Prof. Britt has a love for teaching and has amazing credentials. His stories are fun to listen to but he can often get off track. His TA was my saving grace with his office hours and study guides, giving you exact topics to study instead of the vague "read the textbook" answer.
King. Lots of lectures but he's hilarious and very passionate. Read the textbook and go to reviews and you'll be fine.

Professor Britt is a really nice guy. He really cares about his students and loves his job so much. He does occasionally get off topic, but it's never too bad, there's just so much information in the first place, which can make it difficult if you're not interested in the class. Just go to the TA reviews, pay attention in class, and it'll be easy!

Lectures are confused and scattered. Professor doesn't know what's on his own slides. Genuinely funny and friendly but sort of checked out. The textbook isn't helpful, but go to TA test review and do the study guide and you'll get an A.

Easy general to get out of physical science and the content was interesting, but the lectures were horrible -- he is so disorganized and I honestly didn't learn anything from class but there are in class quizzes so you can't skip. Go to the TA reviews because they help so much!! There is a big term paper but you get all semester to work on it.

He is funny and entertaining, but lectures are kind of unbearable. He isn't very organized or clear about what is important to know because he goes off on so many tangents. You have to attend class because of in-class quizzes. Everything I learned from this course was either from the textbook or the TA reviews. The TA reviews will save your life!!

He's hilarious. He loves getting to know his students. And he's SO knowledgable and literally famous in the paleontology world. There are pop quizzes which are pretty hard if you're not really into the content, and there's particularly one paper that is soooo time consuming it's wild. But I would say overall, it's a reasonable class and he's great.

This professor does not care about his students. There are no exceptions for ANYTHING. He speaks to me and my peers rudely and doesn't think about his students on a personal level. Never taking a class with him again.

Professor Britt is funny, engaging, and passionate about the stuff he teaches. Gives decent extra credit. The course is definitely more difficult than a lot of people assume going into it, but manageable especially if you actually put time into it. Britt has a tendency to get off topic during lectures which can make it difficult for note taking.

This class is extremely easy if you put in minimum effort. The exams have in class review sections where Professor Britt reads straight from the exam for what we need to know and the TAs host review sessions with all the information needed. The lectures are very engaging and Britt is funny, interesting, and enthusiastic with the topic. Would rec!
He is a good guy and all, but he is the kind of professor who is not clear in the exam reviews, unclear on what is important for the content of the class, and does not explain things well
Instructions are vague, essay instructions are very strict DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

LOVED HIM!! Hilarious, caring, and also focused on his students learning. This class can be difficult and a lot of work at times but Dr. Britt makes an already fun topic so much better. If your interested, this is a great general to take!

Britt's GEO100 class is fun but challenging. Lots of quizzes and essays, but he makes it engaging. Definitely not an easy A, but worth it to learn about dinosaurs. unstuck study was super helpful for preparing for exams.

I absolutely loved Professor Britt! I enjoyed going to his lectures, and he is so engaging and hilarious! There are two papers you have to write, but if you go by the rubric and get feedback from the writing center it's not bad! To study for the tests, fill out his study guides. He always tests from that material! Such a fun general!

This guy focusses more on making his students laugh than teaching, maybe he should consider being a comedian instead. The amount of work for a GE class is INSANE. DO NOT take this class if you want an easy A for the physical science GE. HE CAN'T teach, never stays on topic. He is by far the worst professor I've had. Very nice guy, awful teacher.

Professor Britt is the best! As long as you're proactive and put real effort into the assignments, you will be fascinated and enthralled by the world of dinosaurs that he lets you into! Absolutely take this class if you like having fun!
Super funny and engaging lectures. Surprising amount of papers/essays for a GE class, but the material is interesting enough that I didn't find that to be a problem.
Dr. Britt is a super fun teacher, but this class was way too time consuming for a GE. There's a ton of homework, and two 5 page term papers. It's not an easy blow off GE.

Britt was fantastic. He's super fun and makes the class relatively easy. A couple papers and tests will take some time to complete/study for. Almost every class has a quiz worth a few points, but they'll just be the main ideas from the lecture, and the questions are essentially what are on the tests. I would recommend 100%.

Britt is a solid dude. Dinosaurs (geology 100) IS NOT A BLOW OFF CLASS! It is fun but it's not easy. There are a lot of quizzes and essays. However, the class is very interesting and I would take it again. There are no field trips; the course description is outdated. But worth it to not take physical science.

I took Dinosaurs from Dr. Britt and it was really interesting. He is really funny but be warned of his TAs. There are quizzes almost every day based on the lectures so make sure to pay attention. He really knows his stuff, but has lots of slides that are unimportant for what you need to study. Find a friend in this class and it will help you a lot.

I LOVED THIS CLASS! I took this class hoping to have fun and learn something new while knocking out some GE credits. This class was harder than I expected, with two 5-page papers and in-class quizzes almost every class. However, Professor Britt was very understanding and his whole goal was for us to have a good time and learn how to enjoy science.

This class was really interesting! Professor Britt brought in fossils for us to see and touch. It was however a very time consuming GE and you really need to study for the tests. You need to go to each lecture because there are in class quizzes. This class was just a lot of work but Professor Britt is pretty reasonable and gives extra credit.

Professor Britt is so fun! He is passionate about what he teaches. It is a great class, but sometimes got away from me. I did great on the first exam and then not so great on the second. He showed mercy to the whole class and let us all retake it. He wants you to succeed. I would definitely take a class from him again because it was so much fun.
Professor Britt is awesome! This class was really hard but I learned so much. If you want an easy GE do not take this class! This is a great class if you want to challenge yourself and learn a lot!

Hilarious guy, I loved lectures. As a non-science major, I took this class hoping for an easy time and to learn fun things about dinos. I learned lots of cool dinosaur stuff, but it was honestly a lot harder than I had expected. You are expected to know LOTS of info. If you want to take the class and are hoping to get by without studying, good luck

I LOVED PROFESSOR BRITT!!!! He literally looks like he stepped out of the movie Jurassic Park. He is so funny and is so brilliant. Make sure you study for the tests and focus on memorization but other than that it was such a breeze!! He really wants his students to succeed and gives out cool fossils!

He's really funny but it gets old real quick. The class had easy pre-lecture quizzes, two 5-page research papers, 3 exams, and an attendance quiz. The class is not as fun as you'd think but it's still interesting.

An amazing professor! Very hilarious and passionate about his field of work and you can tell in lectures. There are assigned readings and pre-lecture quizzes before every lecture. The TAs are helpful with providing decent study guides and hold review sessions. Britt is very willing to answer questions and gives a lot of extra credit.

In a 100 class called Dinosaurs! I thought it would be just right for me wanting to get a GE 
If you don't love dinosaurs don't take
You are required to turn in a draft of 2 5 page term papers but don't get any feedback on them
The final paper is graded getting into the nitty gritty
Nice person but lectures were unorganized, quick and jargon filled

I will give credit to Professor Britt- he knows his stuff. However, the expectations for a GE and a 100 class were unreal. Two 5-page papers, 2-3 chapters of reading a week, inaccurate study guide, disorganized and irrelevant lectures. It was not organized learning. Difficult exams.

For a 100 level class, this was ridiculously hard. There were 2-3 chapters to read per week, disorganized lectures, 2 long research papers on topics not covered in lectures, in-class quizzes, and study guides did not prepare for tests. Some questions on tests were nowhere to be found on the study guide. Find another physical science class.

I love Dr. Britt! I had such a good time in his class and learned so much. There are readings and quizzes before class and quizzes after most lectures, but they can help your grade in the long run. There are also two term papers that for me were a bit stressful. He is hilarious and really so passionate about his field!! I don't regret this GE.

Professor Britt is fantastic! His passion for what he teaches really comes through in lecture and in conversation with him. Exams were somewhat specific, but overall I really enjoyed the class. Highly recommend!

Prof. Britt was awesome! His lectures are straight comedy. The lectures are a little crazy and hard to fully grasp. He goes pretty fast through the slides, so take time to review them after class.
