He gives you a ton of extra credit opportunities, so take advantage of those and you'll be okay. Super cool class that teaches more than just dinosaurs.

Possibly the worst class I've ever taken at BYU. The course is to fill a GE, but all the lectures are very science jargon heavy so I didn't understand what he was talking most of the time. Goes against the textbook sometimes. and goes on lots of side tangents. Tests are unnecessarily hard and specific, even with the study guides he makes.
Professor Britt is a good professor for people who do not care about science. If you are not interested in science, take it. If you are, this class is not particularly challenging.

Fun class and probably one of the best Professors on campus. He brings in the spirit and gives us dinosaur skulls to touch. My only criticism would be mandatory lectures (because quizzes were given after class) and 5 page papers. It just seemed a bit too difficult for a class about dinosaurs. I learned lots, but I'm done with this class.

Professor Britt was so helpful! I got covid partway through the semester, and he was the most flexible and helpful of all of my professors. Additionally, when I was concussed he was the most compassionate to my needs. The class takes effort - make sure you do your readings and work hard on the papers, but an A is totally possible if you work. 10/10

Professor Britt is legit so funny. He makes lectures fun and I never felt super bored in class. He asks how we are doing and cares about the students. There is reading weekly or biweekly in the textbook for quizzes. There are also two term papers in this class which is not fun, but there was a whole list of topics we got to choose from .

I swear he invented dinosaurs, he knows everything and is so passionate about teaching this course! His lectures are entertaining, and there are in class quizzes but they're low points. It can be hard to tell what is actually on the test, so I started taking notes right on the study guide as we went through and it helped a lot. Pretty easy class!

I liked Prof. Britt. He was caring and funny. However, I did have a few qualms with the class. The lectures at times felt all over the place, and the exams were strangely hard, even with a lot of study beforehand. It wasn't impossible, though, and this was still a solid class. Super interesting stuff, and Prof. Britt is very passionate about it.

Professor Britt really knows his stuff and is very funny. His lectures were fun and he often brought in casts of fossils to show to the class. His study guides are HUGE, but if you understand the main ideas of the chapters and lessons you can base your studying on those. Overall, it was a fun class and he was a great professor.

This class is the balance of easy material with just enough studying and memorization to make for an ideal GenEd class. Professor will meet with you outside of class (we still keep in touch a year later) and is enthusiastic about what he teaches. A bit scatter brained at times but it hilarious and caring. Study the reviews and you'll do great!

Dr. Britt was my favorite professor this semester! His lectures were super entertaining and he provided lots of useful study tools. The material was fun and I understood it well from his teaching. He also offers extra credit which is available all semester. Overall- amazing class!

Professor Brooks' class teaches students to become effective learners in courses unrelated to their major. So, reading your textbook, quizzing yourself, participating in class will help you attain the most out of his classes. Additionally, do the extra credit reading! It made a massive difference in how I approached his and other classes.

Pretty entertaining, but he went on lots of tangents during lectures that made them difficult to follow. Pretty easy, I paid next to no attention during lecture, spent very little time on this class, and still got a solid A. Lots of extra credit opportunities if you need them. MC questions weren't worded well and he sometimes contradicts the book

Britt is a nice guy, but his class is extremely confusing. I don't think I fully understood one lecture I was in, and it was 3 times a week. Also, the tests are extremely difficult. The study guide rarely covers all the little details he tests on. Very nice guy, but I would never recommend this class.

Super nice professor who really cares about getting to know his students. BUT I have never been more confused than in this class. I was lost the whole semester. His lectures were extremely confusing, and there were 3 a week. His tests were so hard, there is so much memorization on random topics that don't seem important, but are on the tests.

I LOVE Prof Britt. I honestly have 0 interest in geology, but he made it interesting and entertaining, which is super impressive. Funny lectures, tells you all the "cool stuff, man" and is super knowledgeable. Not an easy A, but he gives you all the resources you need to be successful. Reading quizzes, two papers, three exams. Enjoyed the class

I love this man. He is probably one of the best teachers I have ever had in my life. I actually love dinosaurs because of this man. Even though this class was online with hundreds of kids, some how by the end of it, he knew me personally. I only made a hand full of comments in class, but he remembered all of them!

I loved this class, take it if you like dinosaurs. He knows EVERYTHING about them Sometimes is disorganized, you never know what you should know from lecture, but he basically goes over the test in the review, and there are so many extra credit opportunities that you'll be fine if you do them. Lots of cool field trips, and one very easy paper.

Brooks is a fantastic professor! I'm convinced he knows as much about dinosaurs as anyone alive. Because he's passionate about them, he expects you to learn you stuff, so the tests are pretty hard, but if you can see past the grade you'll realize you're learning a ton. I loved his class (do the extra credit and you'll get a magic +5% at the end)!

I liked prof Brooks but not his tests. It required knowing really small details and sometimes asked about stuff we hadn't learned yet. There is lots of busy work but there is also LOTS of extra credit, so you don't have to do well on tests. He disagrees with a lot of stuff the textbook says so you cant fully rely on that which can be confusing.

This professor knows his stuff. Sometimes it was hard to follow lectures, but the grading criteria is very clear. Go to the TA reviews and you'll do GOOD. The TA is your go-to for getting an A. This professor is so funny and I enjoyed his comments. Dinosaurs aren't my thing, but I would choose this class again over other courses for my GE credit.

I don't particularly like geology (I took it cause I like chem less), but 95% of the time, I forgot that in Prof Britt's class! He is the funniest professor I've had. There are a couple of things that you should be aware of: He goes through ppts at light speed, I swear, so count on never catching everything. Also, the textbook was a beast :/

Loved this class and Professor Britt! He gives you multiple extra credit opportunities, mostly coming from reading a really great book that you can take quizzes on. Hes hilarious, makes the class easy, but you can honestly do really well just by going to test reviews, doing the study guide and going over his posted slides

Oh my heck I freaking love this guy. He has the best sense of humor! As long as you attend class and do the readings, you will do just fine. His study guides are very helpful, and I always did well on the tests (even got 100% once!). We had a pizza party at the end. The group projects are a bit annoying, but it is so worth it to be in his class.
Definitely wasnt my favorite teacher. I thought the lectures were boring and dry. Stopped going to class after thanksgiving, but did okay on the tests.

I really liked Prof Britt. Loved the class. Engaging lectures (a lot of info to cover and pretty complicated when you have to remember and differentiate all the Latin) but totally would take this class again, one of my favorites.
He is an absolute unit. Best professor I've ever had.

Dr. Britt is a man whose calling in life is to study dinosaurs. This makes for a very engaging experience because he just wants to share his love of dinosaurs with the class. Sometimes this does mean that the more administrative/organizational aspects of teaching a class fall by the wayside, but overall it is a very interesting and enjoyable class.

You get to go on awesome field trips (Thanksgiving Pt, Spanish Fork Canyon, etc.). Dr. Britt is hysterical and one of those teachers that appreciates sarcasm. Take notes in class, but usually class and the textbook teach the same things. There's a couple of papers, but not anything horrible. Tests are easy.

Dr Britt (BBB is his nickname) is AMAZING. He is absolutely hilarious, he prepares slides, test study guides, exam study guides, a class party, field trips and is very flexible with working with you on what you struggle in class. There are lots of group work in this class, so its a good way to make friends. He has lots of experience. Amazing man!
Best professor I've ever had! Such a spiritual learning experience...I would take this class all over again!

I have LOVED my experience in class with Dr. Britt. Not only is this guy hilarious, he really does a great job of explaining concepts and preparing you for the exam. The workload is the usual readings and some essays. I would certainly take a class from him again. It's been my favorite GE course!
Hilarious. He can make a Geology lecture funny enough to suffer through. A lot of writing, but probably better than other Geology classes. Good class for non science people.

Dr. Britt is absolutely fantastic. I have seen on here that people don't like his teaching style, but it is phenomenal. Any dislike of the class should be attributed to a fault of the student, in my opinion. Was a great class! Dr. Britt earned my respect, and he is a great man!

The lectures could get a little boring but his humor made it better! His tests are multiple choice. USE THE STUDY GUIDE and fill it out during lectures, he'll make it available if you ask. 6 question quizzes every class, the field trips are super fun! Not a hard grader.

PROFESSOR BRITT IS THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. This guy is freaking hilarious. Like honestly. SO FUNNY. I really loved this class. I mean, when else are you going to be able to learn about dinosaurs? Probably never. This class is a lot of work (papers, quizzes, group projects), but it is 100% worth it. Take it!!!

Geology 103 really isn't the most interesting of subjects for those who are taking it as a GE but Professor Brooks certainly makes it enjoyable. He's pretty much the king of dad jokes but although he likes to joke around, he really knows his stuff. Lots of reading and two main papers but you can get extra credit if you're falling behind.

Professor Britt is hilarious and found a way to make geology appealing to those not majoring in it. Lots of reading and a few field trips but he was highly flexible and willing to do what he could to help student succeed.

Dr. Britt is great. He has so much love for geology and he is so nice. Took this class for my GEs, but was super fun. love the field trips and the labs. Study for the midterms though. Before taking the midterms he gives a review session in class, DONT MISSED THAT!

If you're taking this class for a GE credit, it's not the most interesting of topics. However, Professor Brooks makes lectures endurable with his wit and jokes. The class itself is not too challenging if you pay attention and do your reading. There are also opportunities to raise your grade such as book quizzes, extra credit, and short reports.

He is my favorite professor at BYU. He deeply cares about paleontology and this class has urged me to pursue it. He is very hilarious and his lectures are straight up funny. If you get to know him, he is like a father figure. He will try his best to solve all your problems, even if they don't involve anything related to the class. He is awesome!

The class was pretty challenging, but it's doable. Just gotta study for once. His lectures are jumbled at times but he's really passionate about what he does. Though this class was challenging, I would take it again because of Dr. Britt.

He is very witty--always cracking jokes & saying funny things--often ridiculous things, but still hilarious. His love for dinosaurs & geology help class a lot. Lectures are important because the textbook is slightly out of date & because he doesn't put everything on the slides. Field trips! If you love dinosaurs, you'll love this class! Busy work.

Britt definitely has a love for Geology. But he should spend more time explaining concepts  rather than talking about how "mind boggling" all of it is. Get ready to memorize the textbook because you won't learn much from his lectures alone. In fact, he doesn't take attendance so I suggest skipping class and using that time to read the textbook.

Lectures were always dry, unengaging and most always off topic. Field trips were fun, but I could not stand going to lecture. You'd be surprised how somebody could take a topic like dinosaurs and suck all the fun out of it.

Meh. This class shouldn't be called "Dinosaurs," but maybe "Geologic Principles of Prehistoric Life." Not much about actual dinosaurs. Tons of busy work, too much group work with huge groups, and tests are in-between hard and easy. Class time drags on. Better than other general science classes, but not by much. But the field trips are way fun!

Prof. Britt is an engaging and interactive teacher who loves student participation and making geology jokes. Take heavy notes from the textbook and on his power points, and make sure you go to class because his lectures really solidify the information.

An engaging professor who captures your interest in the dynamic processes of our Earth. Do not be alarmed by his relentless efforts to sway students to the Geology department, just demonstrates his love for the field. Really appreciates participation, and if he calls you out for being a country music fan or cat-lover, just means he respects you. ;)

Overrated. People just like a professor who's funny, not talented. Lectures are disorganized, all your learning comes from the book, poor teacher, hardly ever in office hours, and is often demeaning to students. The class isn't bad if you're a good student. Need to know what you learn in the book well. Material was cool, but wouldn't recommend him.

I really like this class. Content can be a little dull but Dr. Britt is awesome. I would hire him as my father-in-law. Really helpful and kind. Chapter reading with quizzes every chapter.  Papers graded  by TAs are not too bad. Would suggest getting TA help on labs. Can be tricky. Overall good experience.

Honestly, Brooks is a great guy but this class is not worth the trouble. Classes are long and tests are extremely specific. Many questions come from picture captions and graphs in the textbook. Lectures and textbook are also extremely vague and scattered. He can be self righteous, so if you have a hard time with that be aware. Field trips are fun.

Do NOT take this class.  I grew up loving dinosaurs but this class was horrible.  It is honestly a pointless class and is harder than a 100 level class should be.  There are two 5 page papers plus a bunch of one-page papers.  It sounds like an easy, fun class but it's not.  You better be good at using Learningsuite to see when things are due!

Professor Britt is a great teacher and the tests aren't bad if you know the material well. However, there is a lot to know.  He also tends to put a lot of irrelevant information on the power points so you have to sort out what's important and what's not. He also does 2 or 3 online quizzes a week that are open textbook but still kind of tough.

Dr. Britt is an amazing, kind, smart professor! He made this class amazing! He loves paleontology and because of him, this class was AMAZING. He's a renowned Paleontologist. I have loved dinosaurs my whole life. I loved learning about dinosaurs and this has been my favorite class ever at BYU. AWESOME field trips, you get to hunt for bones!! wow!

I loved Dr. Britt! Yeah... maybe his jokes were dry but at least he isn't boring! He really knew his stuff and is extremely helpful. Just get your work done and you'll be fine! Go to the review sessions - they are SUCH a big help!

Professor Britt is a great teacher! He is great at teaching the subject and he knows what he's talking about. He also has a great personality that keeps everyone in class interested. I would highly recommend him to any student that wants to take his class.

The only good thing about Dr. Britt is that he knows his stuff and you will learn from him. Unfortunately he gets his jollies from ridiculing others and anyone he disagrees with is a "moron". He might respect you if you are a pretty girl, but otherwise don't count on him taking you seriously.

Dr. Britt is awesome. I've only had 1 or 2 professors who are more personable and helpful, but also hilarious. The man is a crack up. Just be ready from him to razz you if you pipe up. This class was ok, but his tests are KILLER. They destroyed me and I studied 30+ hours per exam. It didn't help that our TA wasn't very good.

Dr. Britt is my favorite professor! He knows his stuff and is involved and interested in the subject. I definitely want to take another class from him, even if I just audit. He will answer any questions you have and makes the topic fun and interesting. The field trips are informative and the assignments are not hard.

Dr Britt is amazing. He has a remarkable passion for his subject which combined with his very entertaining personality makes class a joy. There were some problems with the class but these were really all the TA's fault and Dr Britt made sure that, even though it was frustrating during the semester, grades turned out fine in the end.

Less about dinosaurs and more about general geology than I would have liked. Still, it's a fun class to take in the summer! Being a freshman class it has a lot of busywork, but that also means it isn't too complicated. Just make sure you have time for it in your schedule, some of the projects can take a long time.

This class was my least favorite and I wouldn't suggest it. If you do decide to take it, here's what to expect: weekly quizzes online, 2 midterms and a final, extremely boring textbook, 2 term papers, and a lot of boredom. I would only suggest taking this class if you really like geology. He knows his stuff really well, go to the test reviews!

Dr. Britt is so passionate about the subject but that was the only thing that made it interesting for me. The readings are extremely challenging if you're not a science person and the work load is pretty heavy. Don't just think this class will be an A because it's a 100 level class, be prepared to work your butt off!!!

This class is fairly easy, just time consuming.  The lectures are quite dry but Dr. Britt asks if you are understanding. The field trips are the best part but the class overall is pretty dry and time consuming.
AMAZING! Love this man! if you do the reading and study, your work will pay off! he is hilarious, learns all the students names, and cares about your life, not just your grade! love this man!

awful. he is only concerned with publishing and does not care very much about the class and his students. the TA does all the work and all the real teaching. ridiculous. he does not think-at all-about how the class may be for students or how he could teach info better. just expects the students to read his mind. why is he a professor at all?

His class was so hard to follow, his lectures were very disorganized and you had no clue how to study for tests. Also he accused me of plagiarism even though I cited my sources in my term paper. Writing his research papers took way too long for the grade you get on them. You would definitely need to absolutely love geology to do well in this class.

If you enjoy spending hours upon hours writing papers, taking quizzes, going on field trips, completing assignments, and taking ridiculously hard and comprehensive tests, all for a 3.0 credit class, then go ahead and take this. I spent more time working for this class than any of my others, and it was the only class I received a lower grade in. ugh

This class changed my perspective of the world.  Dr. Britt really knows his stuff.  His lectures are disorganized, and studying for tests is tricky because there's so much material to cover, but Dr. Britt has a great sense of humor and true passion for what he teaches.  The research papers are a pain, but doable.  It takes some effort to do well.
Dr. Britt was one funny guy. Dinosaurs was really interesting and fun and I learned a lot from him. He knows a lot about the subject and is very passionate about dinosaurs.

I had Dr. Britt's "life of the past" class during Fall 2006.  He is an expert in his field, and there are few people in this world who can claim to have dug up more dinosaurs than him.  His class was extremely interesting, and changed the way that I look at life. 2 1/2 years later, I still love the topic.  I recommend his class to everyone!!!!

I think Dr. Britt is great professor.  I really enjoyed his dry, off the wall humor.  It definitely made me want to come to class every time just because he's so passionate about the subject.  Everything I learned was way interesting, but it was way hard to get all the reading done and understand what he's talking about. Lectures were disorganized.

Dr. Britt is a very nice guy and is very excited about his subject.  He wants everyone to understand and is very helpful.  5 assignments the entire semester, but 25 quizes online (identical to the practice website ones.)  Once you know that they're easy.  Nice guy.  Makes things interesting.  Very funny.  Highly reccomend.

Dr. Britt is a professional in his field.  He knows what he's talking about and his excitement for the subject is evident.  The tests are reasonable and he provides study guides/sessions.  If you don't leave college knowing that dinosaurs didn't fly or swim, you didn't learn anything.

Britt is a great professor and tries really hard to connect with his students.  He gives a study guide and make sure you know everything on it.  He gives tons of extra credit and if you are willing to work hard you can get an A!

I didn't actually go to class that often, except for labs.  I found his lectures boring and unhelpful.  The class isn't that hard, but he words his tests funny and I consistently scored in the 70s-80s even though I aced assignments.  Study EVERYTHING for tests!

I absolutely loved him. His jokes were dry, but i thought they were great. The tests were challenging, but if you do the practice quizzes online, then you are set. He knows so much, and you learn a lot...especially on the field trips!

I guess you either like him...or you don't.  He thinks he is very funny in his lectures (which he rushes through very disorderly) and expects a lot of 'busy work' to be done.  He doesn't seem to go by the textbook, but he still expects you to know what's in the textbook.  He likes to put students on the spot, too, about off-subject stuff.

I took this course online and I found it to be very informative and helpful. All the material he puts on his tests are in the practice quizes, so study with those. The class is boring, but you get extra credit for coming. Easy A if you keep up with the deadlines.
Dr. Britt was one of my favorite teachers.  I really learned a lot in this class.  His jokes were terrible, but they made class more fun.

This guy knows his stuff.  He is teaching the basic course, but focuses mainly on sedimentary rocks because he is a paleotologist.  He makes the class ineteresting and is a good teacher and a great guy.  I recommend him for anyone serious about geology.  Peace!
He's one of those guys who laughs at his own jokes, rushes through the lectures while you struggle to take notes. Too much information is expected to be memorized. Impossible tests.
Harsh grader.

Don't take this for fun. Lots of reading/study guides, don't miss a single day or your grade will suffer, teacher and TAs are bad at responding, worked my tail off but missed one class period and turned a few things in late and the teacher would not work with me. Little grace is given; study guides and reviews were unhelpful. Take mind/body health.

Amazing professor who truly cares and connects with students. However, the course is very demanding. The material is manageable, but there's a lot of it. I fell behind quickly. My advice: stay on top of readings and pace yourself every day to keep up. But don't be afraid to take it because I learned so much!
Super nice guy! He showed us new lifts every few days and let us roam free. Great if you've never lifted weights before!

This professor is great. He learned every students name in my class after the first week and would come ask me about my day every class. The homework isn't bad, maybe two hours a week (but you only go to class one hour a week so it evens out) and the tests aren't bad if you watch the reviews and learn the content. I am going to miss this class.

Honestly this may have been the most useful and fascinating class I've taken in college, and I'm a senior. Dr. Bailey really cares about his students. If you have any background in physiology (particularly cortisol) that'll save you study time. Just go to class, study the quizzes in preparation for the tests, and you'll be just fine.

Dr. Bailey is a kind professor and he does care about his students. This course was new and he did a fairly good job at teaching the new material. The criteria for projects and assignments was extremely vague which made it hard to complete assignments accurately. Tests are weighted heavily so study the guide well and know your stuff.
Go to class and you are fine. Study the slides and quizes for the exams and you will get a A. Great guy great class!

Bruce is a fun guy to learn lifting from, and you can tell he knows his stuff! He doesn't take up too much of your workout time but still makes sure you know proper form and such. He is also very easy to work with and will show exercises/lifts multiple times if needed. Super chill guy. Would definitely recommend taking Swell classes from him!

This is the WORST professor I have ever had! I wouldn't EVER take a class from this dude. He claims that this class is easy, but I literally do more work in it than in my four-credit physiology class. I only go to class for attendance points. The TA's was just as bad too!!!! This is by far the worst class I have taken at BYU.

He teaches for five or ten minutes per every two hours of class. He will help teach you movements, but mostly the class is super autonomous. He gives you a sheet with a full body workout that is awesome, but it is up to you to try hard in class. He has an exam that requires you to review some slides with gym safety and anatomy, but it is easy.

This class was only an hour a week. We had one quiz due and he gave us a blank study guide to fill out. The TAs provide amazing exam Zoom reviews. If you study the review slides you will get near-perfect scores on exams. This course wants you to succeed and the few assignments we had were easy

Professor Bailey is one of the most kind teachers I've ever had. Lectures are slow and homework is ok. The main reason I gave the difficulty a 4/5 was the tests. They make up a huge portion of your grade and are TOUGH! There are huge and incredible specific open note questions on all of his tests which wrecked my grade. Overall not the worst class.

Despite other poor reviews, I didn't think that the class was hard or too demanding. If you do the readings and study a little bit you will be fine. I bought the book required for the class and didn't open it once at all. Professor Bailey is willing to help and really wants the best for his students. Overall, I actually enjoyed it.

Easy A. Dr. Bailey assigns lots of homework, but if you follow the directions exactly, you'll get an A on all assignments. STUDY TA REVIEW SLIDES for exams. They're really easy. My main advice would be to show up to class and read directions carefully for each assignment, and you'll do fine. Extra credit is also offered.
He's a nice guy and helpful if you need more instruction on how to do lifts properly.

Honestly, not my favorite class or professor. I am a senior and this stress management class was my most stressful class this semester... Tell me how that makes sense. I will say, Dr. Bailey definitely knows his stuff. I have heard from other people that the in person class is not as bad. So much busy work, but tests basically make up your grade.

Professor Bailey has been one of my favorite professors I've had at BYU! All the principles are extremely applicable and the class load isn't bad at all. Here's the breakdown. Lecture each tuesday. Quiz tuesday night. discussion group each saturday. 4 assignments, 2 midterms and a final. If you're considering taking this class, DO IT!!

I liked the outline of this class. There are 4 assignments, they're all very manageable and applicable, just put the time in. The test reviews are gold, and the tests are pretty straightforward if you've studied enough. Great info!

Dr. Bailey is a nice guy, and stress management is not a hard class. I just don't think his lectures are very good. He often mumbled to himself and just repeated exactly what was said in the readings. My advice, take the class because it has really interesting and important content but just do the readings and that's all you need.
Extremely boring class and the exams are difficult. Don't let the title of the class fool you into thinking this is an easy A.

I took weight training from him, and despite being a super nice guy, he wasn't the most helpful teacher. He would demonstrate each move once, give some tips, and then never touch on it again. I really wanted to learn more about technique and proper form, but he spent most of class working out on his own rather than giving corrections.
Professor Bailey is super chill, and pretty much embodies stress management :) Going to class isn't essential to pass this class.
He is very nice and veryyy laid back. Super chill, nice and genuine. I didn't love his teaching style, but I think if you put in the work you can make it a good experience.
I absolutely loved his lectures. They are so applicable. I would recommend everyone take this class! He knows what he's talking about.

This course is content heavy; you have to read and know a lot. Textbook is a "self help" book but is important for explaining certain relaxation techniques/principles you need to know for the test. There are written questions on the midterm & final. The TA review sessions are absolutely worth it.

Honestly a good class. You don't need the textbook at all; all the info to study is in the Canvas readings. Interesting material so reading isn't bad; use the study guide. Bigger assignments are easy to get A's on. Quizzes & tests are closed note/book but decently straightforward. Do well on the study guides and first test to set the tone.

Dr. Bailey is so kind but I really struggled with his teaching style. Youre required to read the material beforehand, but its literally just his lecture typed out. It was definitely repetitive. But the class overall wasnt hard!

Honestly IDK why he has such bad ratings because he is awesome! Textbook would have been helpful, but I made it by just fine without it. He is clear about assignments. GO TO TA REVIEWS for the tests! Very clear about what to study. Bailey is clear about what is expected and it's pretty basic. A lot of in class participation points! AWESOME TEACHER!

Professor Bailey is mediocre at best. His quizzes are ridiculous. A lot of the questions were made to have you try and see what the professor thinks is the right answer and not what the text says is right. The quizzes are also closed book and note and asks on details which is WAY annoying. Bailey makes me wanna sleep in class.

I was so hesitant to take Dr. Bailey due to the horrible reviews, but he really cares about his students and wants you to succeed. His lectures are engaging and is the least stressful class. He gives a studyguide for each section which is helpful. Go to the exam reviews, they are gold!
Interesting material but the tests seemed to be unreasonably difficult. I never felt very prepared for the questions that were asked. Had a hard time knowing what to study and look for.

Professor Bailey is really great and nice. The first test was a little hard, but if you study the quizzes you will do a lot better (I learned that for the second test going forward). He really cares about his students, and the assignments and quizzes aren't very hard. Gives you credit for being in class. Would recommend.

His Stress Management class is awful. I don't care if he is a nice person or whatever it is that people say. This class has so much busy work, he is awful at wording questions and what he expects you to know for the quizzes and tests is ridiculous. This class requires way too much time and causes more stress than helping you to deal with it!

Listen, this isn't going to be an easy A. There is a lot of work involved. But Professor Bailey is a really good teacher. He cares about you and the content he teaches is really useful and immediately applicable. You have to do all the readings, there are a lot of quizzes, but it's not hard material, just a lot of work. I would take it again!

Are you an Exercise and Wellness major? Honestly just take another class. Such a kind guy but this class is hard to take seriously and graded too difficulty. Unfortunately a SUPER hard class to follow. Great guy but not the greatest lecturer.
Hard to follow. Boring lectures.

SUPER genuine, good guy. Assignments posted in advance and easy if you didn't procrastinate. Out of all my classes, this is material I've applied most to my day to day life. Despite lecturing from slides- it is really interesting stuff if you want to learn! Loved the relaxation techniques, and even enjoyed the textbook! Need to read it for quizzes

Professor Bailey was awesome!! He is so nice and really cares about his students. I took this as a freshman and, while it was pretty difficult, I enjoyed it. It is not an easy A but isn't too bad. Probably would have been easier if I'd had the same background as other students. You will love this professor!

This guys name is literally Bruce Wayne Bailey. He is a cool guy and was super helpful and fun. The class was painfully easy, one test, open book, and you can retake it. There is no reason not to take him.

Not worth it. He's a terrible lecturer, hardly coherent. His presentation of the material is very biased and skewed. Tests are UNREASONABLY DIFFICULT and study guides are pointless. You have to be a mind reader or be able to memorize the book and then decipher his test questions to get an "A" on his test. More like Stress You Out 101.

I would advise against taking this class. The tests are harder than necessary, there are a lot of little assignments that I felt were graded unfairly, and the TAs are terrible. There was never a TA in my class, and the reviews she gave were sub par at best. If you're a PH major, take HLTH383. Same exact content, easier professors and curriculum.

Dr. Bailey's class is hard, but so worth it! I learned a lot, and have even used things from class since I took the course. It is a lot of work for 2 credits, so be prepared to study. Dr. Bailey is also extremely helpful and understanding.

Way too much for 2 credits. the irony is that in the stress management class I was extremely stressed out. The professor and the TA did not communicate well. He would say one thing and she would grade based on an entirely different criteria. the tests were hard even though he gives you a GoogleDoc study guide all filled out. harder than I expected.

AWFUL. Most useless class I've ever taken. 1) Bailey is boring and said outright he doesn't even care about the topic much anyways. 2)The amount of busywork you will do for this class is inappropriate for it being 2 credits. 3) his tests are poorly done. 4)After the 1st week of class less that 1/3 of the class comes - he reads right off the slides.

I actually really liked Dr. Bailey. Yes his class was hard and a LOT of work for a 2 credit class, but he did lots of discussions. There were online quizzes and the tests made up a lot of the grade so study hard! But he is a good lecturer.

Hard class to deal with! Study guides are not helpful. Too many quizzes only worth 1 point compared to 3 extreme tests worth 55% of grade.  Questions on tests not covered in class causing low test grades. Agree way too much for a 2 credit class and be prepared to be "stressed out" with this stress management class.

Prideful, rambles, never makes his point, talks in circles, excessive work for a two credit class, if you don't pass the tests you fail the class so 4 months of completing assignments is worthless! Tests count too much of the total grade.

Mr Bailey is a nice guy but he is not a very good teacher at all. Very dry and very boring. Grades assignments very tough and Tests are hard considering it is a two credit stress management class. If you are looking for a time consuming two credit class this is the one for you.
Wonderful instructor.  He really knows the ins and outs of exercising, and is a real friendly guy, too.

The class is really easy, it's just really tedious.  Dr. Bailey really wants the class to be hard, but the subject matter just isn't.  He's sort of a jerk, but it was an easy class so it was worth it. 3 Tests and 1 final (a study guide for each test), all of them are comprehensive.  I'd recommend it for an easy class but again, it's BORING.

This class is not difficult. If you do have trouble, he is more than willing to help you out. You have to put some time in to do some assignments but they are all useful to help you learn the material. As long as you go to class, pay attention, do assignments, and do the reading, you will be just fine.

I dont care what anyone else has said, he was a really good teacher, his classes on relaxation were tons of fun! the quizzes were easy as long as you did the reading, tests had quiz questions in them so study those, pay attention in lecture and what he says to know in the book. Ch 2 only one hard to following his lecture on. Overall good teacher!

His class wasn't as bad as people claim it is. there wasn't a text book, and he is very approachable. we did have a quiz every week, but if you did the reading it was easy to get 100%. i studied with him one on one several times before a test and he was always willing to review the tests with you. good guy, dont hesitate to take it from him.

I very much agree with what has been said.  The tests are very very ambiguous, and he is terrible at explaining the material.  It is key to learn how he thinks in order to do well on the (almost) weekly quizzes.  This class is way too much work for a 2 credit class- it should definitely be 3.

I agree with the comments already mentioned. The test and a paper is what you are graded on. The paper wasn't bad since it had to do with the Bio Feedback lab.The test he didn't not prepare you for. He made study guides but they really didn't help. He tries but I'm sorry I really didn't learn much other than what you have already read.

I think he did a fine job, I didn't have to work that hard and got a good grade.  He posts all of the notes and presentations on BB for your study use.  I'm sure if your looking to dissect any teacher you could have ample opportunity to scrutinize them.  Take this class.

I agree!! I had a hard time following what he was saying. He spent an entire hour trying to teach us the physiological stress response correctly and didn't know how to say the names of the hormones involved. Tests questions are very ambiguous. Learn how the man thinks & you'll ace the test. If you think logically, you'll fail. Nice man,bad teacher.

This man tries hard...he really does, but I had a hard time understanding what the heck he was teaching. I knew the material better than he did and he's the one with the PhD. It was the most stressful class I had...and it was stress management for crying out loud! His tests were awful and class was a drag. Not too much work, but killer tests.

Professor Hansen is great! He is perfectly suited for teaching coding to all of us as beginners, and as long as you do the assignments, you'll have no problem whatsoever in doing well in the class. All assignments come with a test to ensure you've gotten 100%. Attendance is not mandatory but I recommend it to better understand! And he's HILARIOUS!

Professor Hansen is an excellent teacher. He clearly articulates the principles of coding for beginners (which I definitely am). He makes an introductory course appealing and entertaining. Plus, he's hilarious and has a quick wit!

I learned a lot of useful things about SEO in this class. Bruce really knows his stuff, and he's a great guy. We each choose an individual project to work on at the beginning of the semester, so you have to be good at getting things done on your own since there are no real deadlines, but overall I would definitely recommend taking this class!

Bruce is knowledgeable, friendly, and wants to help you however he can. Class is only offered at 8am which can be a challenge if you aren't a morning person. If you don't listen to every word with scrutiny, you might miss something that appears on a quiz/exam. The grading was tougher than it needed to be. Decent class, but not the best experience.

Bruce is the CEO of Sebo Marketing, a local internet marketing agency. As such, he really knows what he is talking about!! Take this class to learn all about SEO, Google AdWords, Google Analytics, and other essentials of Internet Marketing. This was his first semester teaching and he did phenomenal. I would take any class that he teaches.

Bruce is amazing, would take a class from him again in a heartbeat. If you take his class make sure to take advantage of how much knowledge and experience he has by asking questions and taking what he has to say seriously.

Bruce does an excellent job at disseminating a lifetime worth of knowledge in just one semester- the class is incredibly useful and his advice should be taken seriously. He is reasonable, interesting, and knows what he is talking about. Lots of reading, but the books are good!

Loved this class! It's super easy but valuable if you want to go into software engineering. There are lots of readings but don't skip them! They're good reads and they'll prepare you for working in industry. Bruce is super lax on grading as he cares more about the lessons you're learning on the group project rather than actually finishing.
Easy grader. Most students get an A, as long as you show up to class. Class was surprisingly interesting and useful. Very good for job preparation.

Prof. Webster gives students a lot of free rein in the course. There's a ton of extra credit. How much you learn from the course, depends on how much effort you're willing to put in towards the projects

A respected veteran of the field (just look up his wiki page). Wry sense of humor & lots of dry wit. Very understanding, super chill. Probably the most important CS class you'll ever take. Validates all the struggles of software engineers. Entire class is a fun group project - no stress. Attendance is actually enjoyable! I'd rate 10/5 if I could.

Prof. Webster is fantastic! This class was very practical and easily has been the most useful in terms of preparing me for work in the industry. Seriously, if you're considering taking this course, just do it. You won't regret it.

Doc Webster is the best! 428 helps you really understand some of the key problems that plague the industry, and helped shape my paradigm. The group project was fun, and we were able to get a lot accomplished. You must pass the final, but if you do your reading, it will be a breeze. Please take this class, and learn from Websters endless knowledge!

This class is super awesome, Mr. Webster is super awesome. This class was very manageable, even on the easy side I'd say. Only one midterm, no final, and a semester long project that you don't even have to finish. I always enjoyed lecture and you learn a lot of cool things. Would recommend to everyone! Easy useful CS elective.

Professor Webster is awesome. Most applicable class I have taken. He is also super understanding. There were a few times I had something come up, and I was late submitting an assignment, and he let me turn them in late. Best CS class I have taken. Really fun.

Dr. Webster is the coolest CS professor in the department. CS 428 is pretty easy and it has tons of useful information that is really applicable to a software engineering career. He has tons of experience is the real world (which is really nice in a school full of pompous academics). Defiantly take his class, you'll never regret it.

428 is the dream CS elective. Bro. Webster basically just shares stories about his time in the software industry and relates it to the books you read. Choose your own project with a team, turn in periodic deliverables, and you don't have to finish the project by the end of the semester. If you need another elective, CS 428 is fantastic.

He's an adjunct professor, and only teaches one class, so he's very accessible. He has decades of experience in Software Consulting, and he knows a lot about why projects fail. A lot of the class focuses on how to run a successful software project. A big portion of the grade is required reading, but none of the reading assignments are time wasters.

He cares about what he teaches. Labs can be educational and enjoyable when you are in a good group. Labs rarely went the whole time. There was an online portion too. He sometimes had a hard time explaining things or just said that everything was important. Tests were challenging. There was obvious drama between TAs and they weren't always prepared.

The class was mostly online lectures and then instructional lab/application by the EAL manager. Overall an informative class that dives deep into the analysis aspect of environmental science. I was impressed with how much I learned.
I loved my soil science lab!!! Dr. Hopkins and his TAs are the best. Labs are super easy and never took up the whole 3 hours. They made it very easy to learn and participate in a lab during COVID.

This class is realllly basic. It's 1 credit, so it shouldn't be a lot of work, but it was a bit juvenile. The class kind of feels like an afterthought for the professors and TAs. All labs are partner labs. Easy class, but don't expect to learn much.

I feel like he doesn't really know how to teach this material very well. I mean, he knows it, and he loves it, but he isn't very good at making others excited to learn about it or understand it. His lab notebook assignment is a joke, he wants you to write in it every class, but doesn't want anything repeated from the lab workbook...

Dr. Hopkins is an excellent professor and a really great person. He usually knows most of his students by name and is very willing to provide support. He is passionate about the subjects he teaches and his classroom is a great environment to be in. All you really need to do is show up to class, pay attention, and do your work.

For a one credit class, his soils lab has a lot more work than it should. There are weekly quizzes, a large worksheet due before each lab, a semester-long project, and a lab notebook. However, he tells us exactly what will be on the final. I think I would've learned more if the class have covered less material.
Hopkins is a great guy and I enjoyed his soil lab. Pretty easy class as long as you show up and put in the work. There is a semester long paper which was a little rough but overall a very easy class.

Dr. Hopkins is a great professor. I learned many insightful things in his class. You do need to show up to every class to get the daily credit, however he lets you make up missed days. There is a lot of reading because of course you have to read the whole first half of the book of Mormon. His exams are practical and fairly easy.

Dr. Hopkins didn't follow the pattern that many religion professors follow. The pattern that they want to give as few A's as possible in order to keep grades down and their department happy. He cares about your testimony of the Book of Mormon and his whole goal is to help develop your testimony into something stronger, Great class!
I never knew turfgrass was so phenomenal before I took this class. Now my life is turfgrass. Dr. Hopkins is a turf genius. I wish that I was a turf plant.... Great professor!

I love Dr. Hopkins, he is one of my favorite PWS professors on campus. I've taken most of his classes, he makes you work for your grade, but only because he wants you to learn, no busy work to be seen anywhere, everything has a purpose and that purpose is knowledge! I highly recommend him
Fantastic class. I learned, was inspired, and without excessive work for a religion class.
Best prof I've had!

Brother Hopkins is a nice guy. Getting a scientific perspective on the Book of Mormon was interesting, however I feel that many assumptions were drawn that I don't feel had enough reasonable evidence to accept. Some test questions are opinion based, and I felt these had no right answer, so it was playing the "guess what's in my head game".

Pro. Hopkins is rad. A really down to earth guy who's pretty into dirt (excuse me... Soil). This was just the 1 credit lab class, so it was pretty chill. It was sometimes a lot of work for 1 credit (ESA assignment at the end of the semester took a while), but still totally doable. The labs and people were really fun!

Nice guy, but incredibly disorganized. Makes you buy a subscription for TopHat, even though iClickers are just as effective. Tests aren't too hard, but the weekly textbook quizzes are NIGHTMARES. Don't even buy the book because most of the pages are on LS & for the weekly quizzes just copy/paste the questions into Google and it'll have the answer!

I'm rating for PWS282 & PWS283  PROS: - Relatively good at teaching. - Cares about his students. - Tries hard to help us understand.  CONS: - He's pretty disorganized. - There is quite a bit of homework. - Need to memorize a lot.
I hated the idea of taking SOIL SCIENCE, but absolutely loved it.
Love his fresh style. Very applied. I learned a ton.
Without Dr Hopkins I would not have passed 282.  I learned more from his lab than I have the actual soils class

Class was very hard.  No turf class listed as a pre-req, but if you hadn't taken his turf class before this class several parts of the class were beyond what was taught.  I had to go to other professors for help because I couldn't figure it out and Hopkins was unavailable. No textbook, made it very difficult to do any extra studying.

Dr. Hopkins is UNORGANIZED. I agree with most of the posts below. He just gave you a textbook and expected you to learn the subject on your own. His "lectures" were discussions, he did not prepare at all and was stalling for time.

Half of your grade is attendance, which wouldn't be so bad if the lectures weren't completely pointless. Half the time lectures are guest lectures who drone on and on about things you will never be tested on. The 5-6 tests are difficult and unclear and the course is POORLY organized. I would not recommend this class.

This class was pointless. The tests do not reflect what you learn and are ridiculously hard. The lectures teach you nothing. he is very nice but the classes are pointless and you get points for being there. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! its not worth the double credits. You have lots of stupid tests you have to take every day before class. DO NOT TAKE

PWS 150 was one of my least favorite classes at BYU. The lectures did not aid my understanding of the subject matter, the TA's were unapproachable and Dr. Hopkins made excuses up until finals week for why they did not have our material graded. Overall, it was a disorganized general that required as many hours of busy work a week as a part time job

I did not like him at all. His lectures consisted of either reading straight off the powerpoints (which are online) or of going off on tangents. Tests are in class, and most of the answers are given out during the test... It's pretty much a joke. Field trips are scheduled short notice. I wouldn't take a class from him again.

Just don't take this class. Dr. Hopkins is a nice guy, but this class was disorganized (to put it lightly, it was boojy, fer real doe). Blackboard never worked for some reason, lectures were often pointless and consisted of him going on tangents. Group projects were pointless and not helpful. Content was interesting, but just take Bio 100.

I personally couldn't stand his teaching style.  He preferred to have discussions about the morals of certain environmental issues instead of teaching some of the hard material in the book that we were quizzed on before class.  I never would have gone to class if not for the iClicker quizzes every day.  I personally don't recommend this class.

Lots of reading/reading comprehension quizes. Lectures are usually interesting, but can get boring. Tests are all based on the study guides. Grades papers and other assignments very easy. Good for a general ed requirement.
Lots of busy work targeted towards freshman and sophomores. Excellent lecturer, and more than fair at grading and assignments.  Easy approachable.

Dr. Hopkins was a great teacher. I am not interested in science at all but he had some very interesting class periods. The study guides are almost exactly what is on the test so filling that out is extremely important. I would definitely recommend this class for a general!

Prof Hopkins is awesome! He's real down to earth and makes class interesting even if you aren't a science major. The textbook was easy to read and not dull. The TAs were helpful and are in charge of grading. There are I-clicker quizzes, so be prepared. The tests went along with everything Hopkins and the TAs provided. Great class, very applicable.

Hopkins is a really nice guy and his lectures are entertaining.  You have to read the book though.  Very interesting and enjoyable class...and I am usually one to struggle with science.  I took this class for a general and felt it was very applicable for real life.

Dr. Hopkins is a good professor, but I didn't like the structure of this class. The TAs were in charge of all of the grading, and everything felt unorganized. Class was often pointless, but I went because there were clicker quizzes. It wasn't too difficult, though. I probably didn't enjoy it mostly because I'm not a science person.

'Living with Plants' is an awesome class, everyone should take it!  Dr. Hopkins really made the class fun and gave us practical plant knowledge.  We did a lot of activities (walks outside, scavenger hunts, growing pea plants...).  Didn't require too much reading and the grading was fair, a lot of extra credit opportunities.  Highly recommended!

Take his class! I loved it so much and learned lots about advertising. The second half of this class is just group projects, but the class is small enough that they are fun. He is caring and wants to help you out. My advertising skills grew a lot from his teaching. It was one of my only classes where I got to know the professor and he was great!

Bryce is a good teacher and its obvious he cares about his students. If you take this class know there's a lot of group projects especially towards the end (that's advertising though). Overall, the class was good, and I learned the foundational concepts, but I didn't feel like there was a lot of depth to his class.

Bryce is very kind and passionate about Advertising. There is a lot of group work especially in the second half of the semester. Overall, you should just take the class, it stretches your brain a bit but it's a great experience.

Bryce was a great professor to have at the end of my undergrad time in advertising. You can tell he cares deeply about his students and has a strong testimony. The capstone project is intense, but super fun. He gave us a ton of time in class to work on it. I learned a lot about presenting as well and feel super prepped for industry work. :)
Bryce is the GOAT! Gives lots of feedback towards creative projects but its all out of love and makes you better. Loved his class!

I loved Professor Isaacson's class. He really easily helped us to learn about advertising in an engaging way, not to mention he is so helpful for students applying to the advertising program. Only hard part was that sometimes I felt time constraints on group projects, but they were so fun that I don't really care too much.

Get ready for group projects... They are beneficial to the creative process, but they seem non-stop. While I won't go into advertising, this class was interesting, and I won't look at ads the same again

Professor Isaacson has done an incredible job teaching me how to think like an advertising student. He is open to feedback and honestly seeks to improve. The class was intense, but it helped me feel more prepared for the rest of the program. Would absolutely take again, he is a great mentor for any project.

Good guy.Not a great ad teacher. Doesn't understand the program culture. Doesn't take feedback and unwilling to work with students on deadlines. He should talk with the other professors to learn how to actually teach in this program. I wanted my capstone project to be meaningful but everyone was thrown off by his rigidity. Waste of my last semester

Bryce made my capstone class miserable. Rigid, condescending, and completely out of touch with his students. Everything felt forced and performative. No flexibility, no inspiration — just control. I left the class drained and frustrated. Take literally anyone else if you want to actually enjoy learning.

Brother Korth is very kind and passionate about what he teaches, but the lectures aren't very engaging. They're mostly lecture-heavy with little discussion or interaction. There are a lot of required readings, which can be interesting, but expect to spend a significant amount of time on them. Exams are relatively easy, though.

Brother Korth is a very nice guy. He genuniely cares about the class and the subject he teaches. The lectures are very basic, apparently a lot of people don't agree with The Family. I wish he stood more on doctrine and firm ground when teaching instead of teaching loosly around them.

-Long midterms each with a ~600 word essay due along side them, I'd say that's unfair for religion.
-Lecture is mostly listening to him ramble about whatever while waiting for the attendance phrase.
-He is a nice guy just didn't learn much other than I shouldn't be gay.

The class isn't that hard, I was just struggling with depression at the time. He was decently understanding, but I still feel like he cared more about lecturing then students. I remember one student asked a really honest and earnest question one class, something like "Why do we need to be baptized" and he just ignored it, continuing his lecture.

Classes were awesome and my favorite part about this course, but there was a butt-ton of readings (graded on completion) that never really helped you understand class or course material better. Other than that he's an amazing professor that teaches tough concepts very well. Do the work and pay attention and it's a pretty easy A
Love Brian, took it 2022, a lot of slides, informational, super supportive professor. Don't be harsh on him, he is nicccceee

For a 2 credit religion class, this class was ridiculously too much. I believe that he is under the assumption that he is teaching a 4 credit class. He requires reading before each class, the tests are around 80 questions long with questions that is like "guess what I'm thinking". The course project is 3 to 4 spaces single-space so get ready.

I loved Brother Korth. He is very welcoming and kind. He shares personal experiences that he has had and how they have helped him to grow closer to Christ. Assignments are easy readings that are also enjoyable. Take a class from him and you won't regret it.

I took 2 classes from Bro. Korth (one each semester) as a Freshman at BYU. I was put into a pilot class (UNIV 101) with him by chance but I grew to love him and his teaching style so I took another class. He turned into my favorite Professor and became a father figure to me while I was away from home. Highly recommend him and this class :)

Took this as an online class. The lectures in the class are not by Brother Korth. The lectures are boring, long and just entail someone reading words off of the slides. The class is easy enough but just like every other religion class at BYU, is boring, repetitive and ultimately not that great of a class.

I had a good experience with Brither Korth. I liked how the class felt overall with the tests and the project. With the tests, it would get confusing about what I should have done to prepare, but if you do the review he gives out, you will do great. He does have a lot of information (like really full slides)

Dr. Korth is a wonderful professor. Lots of reading before class each week, but the lectures were inspirational and he tried to have student input as much as possible. Tests were reasonable and semi open note, and the final was a 3-4 page essay that was also reasonable. I learned a lot and would absolutely take his class again!

Dr. Korth is very good at treading lightly to not offend anyone. However he takes this a little too far and doesn't really say or teach anything in lectures. I was really hoping to learn and feel the spirit in this class, sadly I didn't learn much. Readings were too often not focused on scriptures, apostles, or conference messages.

Loved Korth, but he does end class late, has too many things to do before class, tests are very long, and he has big papers due the same day as all the tests. His class was frustrating because he gives you credit for doing all the work but it's on your honor, so after I worked my butt off to get an A, students who did nothing also got an A:/

I thought Professor Korth was an good professor, I had to take his class for the credit and thought it wasn't bad. He is very nice and responds fairly quickly, be ready to read and good luck on the tests, I feel like there is too much reading and random things on the tests. I did his class summer term, but it wasn't very crazy hard.
I love professor Korth ! He is the best professor I have had so far! He is caring and super love person. He is understanding and willing to help for your success! Very highly recommended

Week-long units feel a little rushed, but Bro. Korth makes the effort to consider multiple viewpoints while discussing doctrine. Teaches truth with compassion, very sensitive and caring. Tests were clear - utilize the study guides. if you're a member, not much new knowledge, just sound reaffirmation of core doctrine. Loved the Heavenly Mother unit.

I loved this class so much! I recommend it to EVERYONE!!!! I learned so much and he grades so easy. I felt like I could learn without being stressed about my grade. There is a textbook but it's free and barely used.

I was very unimpressed with this professor and this class. It was entirely run by the TA and full of typos, weird questions, poorly written materials, and unclear assignment instructions. It was easy enough to get an A, but I spent more time guessing about what they were looking for than actually learning anything.

The class was not very hard. The tests are all basically "guess what the professor is thinking"/wants you to think. The lecture material was pretty meh. It was a fairly easy A, but not an enjoyable experience.
Lectures are alright, but assignments and tests are pretty easy.

I LOVED this class! At BYU you always are tested on how well you know your religion facts, in this class the tests are all about learning the overall principles and how you should improve, seriously the BEST religion class. Brother Korth is SO sensitive to his students and you can tell how much he cares for all of us.

Brother Korth is great and will teach you a lot about different viewpoints and how to be a better disciple of the lord. But he is very strict about attendance and will only allow 1 or 2 absences before he'll start cutting into your grade. There are also a lot of reading and writing assignments that can pile up pretty quick.

Brother Korth is my favorite professor so far! His class was so amazing. There were a few assignments and papers, but I found them very engaging. His class was very relaxing, you just show up and feel the spirit. Tests are super easy. He is respectful to his students, and makes sure to only teach doctrine. Be sure to take Eternal Families from him!

Not the most entertaining, but very uplifting. Very sensitive towards LGBTQ+, divorce, mental health, and disability topics. Tests were clear and easy, final was just a paper you could write in advance. A few papers required, but if you do them they're pretty much guaranteed an A.

Attendance is weighted heavily. It was an easy A. The tests are ridiculously easy, especially with the study guide. A couple of course projects make it more difficult/time-consuming. He often got sidetracked talking about LGBTQ issues, but he just wants everyone to be clear on the doctrine. The LGBTQ people in our class appreciated it a ton.

Korth is a sweet man. His lectures sometimes felt repetitive and I can't say I LEARNED anything as much as I just had already-known truths compounded by this class. I really appreciated the sensitivity around LGBTQ+ topics. I'm queer and always felt safe in his lectures. He doesn't teach false doctrines, he just teaches with compassion.

I had this class from Brother Korth in Spring 2020. I reached out to him for clarification on something he was teaching that was false. I was not argumentative or combative, but he never responded, even after I followed up. He is the kind of professor who seems to tackle hard topics within the church, but it's all fake.

Brother Korth is amazing! As a gay student this is a hard class to take because the topic is sensitive, and while I was offended right off the bat with another professor, I switched to Bro Korth and never got offended a single time! The tests are super easy and the assignments require work but he doesnt grade harshly. Overall, I highly recommend!!

Brother Korth is AMAZING!! This is seriously a life-changing class! Completely changed my perspective on dating and marriage. Perfect balance of spiritual and academic. Very intersting class discussions and handles controversial topics perfectly!! Lots of extra credit opportunities. Highly, highly recommend taking this course from him-LOVED IT!
Really wasn't a fan of this class when it was on-demand. Felt like 4 credits of work for a 2 credit class, Bro. Korth was fine but him and his TAs were hard to get ahold of. Good class content.

Bro Korth is a nice guy and this class was really easy. However, if I'm being honest I found it to be a bit boring. I'm not sure how much of that was content or his teaching. He did give some good reading sources however so I feel like a learned a lot from assigned readings. I didn't like the course projects but he graded them easy so that was nice

Very nice guy and has a big heart for everyone. As are most religion classes, it is what you put into it. The course was VERY interesting to me honestly and gives a lot of appreciation for the family. Lots of reading and a few other projects on the side but a manageable load.

Doctor Korth is a great teacher. He is passionate about the content and he is willing to help. However, his lectures can put you to sleep. If I had to do the course over, I would take it from Doctor Korth. The workload is very manageable and the midterms are based on lecture material so it is easy to prepare for those.

Readings were never too long, a few projects that seemed overwhelming at first but were manageable, and tests followed the study guide well (closed note). (Lots of extra credit) Brother Korth is a great guy who cares about his students and works hard to make his class wonderful!
Super fun professor. It is nearly impossible to fail this class. This would be a great class to take when you have a full schedule because it isn't very time consuming.

Brother Korth is the nicest guy, he genuinely cares about your grades and understanding of the material. The class is overall super easy but you learn a ton! I wish he taught more classes I would for sure take a class from him again! There's a lot of reading but I didn't do a single one and ended with 103 in his class.

Professor Korth is AMAZING because he truly cares about his students lives and not just their grades. He understands college is stressful and tries to ensure that his class is a spiritual sanctuary where we can grow our testimony and feel the spirit. His broad perspective on families really helps. Do yourself a favor and take his class!!

I think this may have just been the course rather than the professor specifically, but it was an extremely easy course and you get what you put into it. There was almost no stress involved and prof. korth is a fun guy.
Brother Korth is incredible!!! I loved all of his lectures and stories. Such an inspirational professor! He's also so flexible and easily approachable. I can't recommend this class from him enough!

Easy A. He posts the lecture slides online, so read over those before you take the tests and you'll do fine. I got 103% in the class. He's also a very nice person. There's a fair amount of reading, but it's easy and you don't really have to remember what you read because the things you will be tested over are in the lecture slides. Loved the class.

Brother Korth is absolutely incredible!! The assignments in the class are super easy, and help you in your personal development. He does not give busy work. There was a lot of reading to do, but it was all relevant and worth it for the class. Take this class if you have the chance, you won't regret it!

This is THE BEST religion class I have taken at BYU. His class requires effort in the assignments, but they really help you learn, and the exams are super easy. I got a 101% in this class with my eyes closed and failed the last religion class I took. Brother Korth is so caring and passionate about the gospel. He really strengthened my testimony.

I seriously loved this class. It was spiritual, eye opening, and life changing- not to mention the professor was the KINDEST person ever. The midterms were (really) easy, and the projects were time consuming but WORTH IT because it added to the learning experience(his rubrics were super detailed so you always know what he expects). TAKE THIS CLASS!

Lectures at the beginning were pretty dry but they got better with the semester. Also didn't like how his slides contain paragraphs of info with all the colors of the rainbow. BUT the class was very manageable and easy. I got 102% without even doing all of the extra credit. There are several projects but they are very straight-forward. Good choice!

Wonderful guy, real down to earth and willing to share personal experiences. He is very loving and passionate about this class. If you put in the effort to do the readings for the week you'll get a lot out of it. He assigns more projects than I would have liked for a 2 credit, but it's manageable. Gives clear instructions and outlines for all test

I loved Brother Korth! He is very personal, relatable, and kind. The midterms are extremely easy to complete, he provides extra credit, and he is sensitive to specific topics relating to family and marital issues, gender identity, and sexual orientation. It feels like a safe space. Assignments are straight forward, and he always answers questions.

Brother Korth is a great lecturer. He does a great job at covering controversial topics! There is quite a bit of homework for a 2 credit class, but it is not that hard. 2 exams, 4 projects, and the final is a writing project. He grades super easily!
I loved Brother Korth. He is fantastic! TAKE ETERNAL FAM FROM HIM.

Brother Korth is the best! You will have an amazing spiritual learning experience because you won't be so worried about your grade. Just do the readings and participate in class and you'll be fine. Tests were very easy.
Take. This. Class. It's exactly what you want from a religion class. This guy is so sweet.

Overall a very loving and caring teacher. I took this class over zoom and I could tell he wanted the students of his class to understand the importance of each doctrine he taught. 10/10 would love to have him again.

Super nice guy, but not a great lecturer. I mean, he is a great choice for an easy religion class. You should go to every class, but he posts a study guide before each midterm along with his slides. His slides have everything you need to know on them. Probably one of the easiest classes I have ever taken at BYU.

Bro Korth really is a kind man. He cares about his students and loves feedback and is very humble. But do know that he loves reading off of slides all day every day which gets real monotonous, and he goes NUTS with the highlighting on his slides! He has a podunk Idaho feel and isn't the most engaging or creative, but he is a sweet teddy bear.

He's an amazing man. He makes his lectures personal and he wants to answer any questions students may have. There is a lot of reading, but it is well worth it. A few projects and a book of your choice to read during the semester. As long as you don't procrastinate its pretty easy. I loved this class! Bro Korth is such a nice guy!
good feedback given.

He knows his stuff and is good at connecting with students on an emotional level. No need to buy the packet unless your a paper-reader person. Just look up the talks online. Very slide and lecture heavy, kinda made it hard to stay interested in the lesson. This is a good choice if you're looking for an A for a small amount of effort.

Professor Korth is one of the most genuine people you'll ever meet. He really does seem to care about each of his students personally. His class relied heavily on powerpoints and it has a high school seminary vibe to it, but I appreciated that he took time before, during, and after class to answer any questions that I had. Awesome guy, easy class.

Byran Korth is a good man and I enjoyed learning from him, but the lectures weren't terribly engaging. He just read off of his powerpoint and rarely asked for participation. I wish he would have shared more about his life and whatnot. But the class is beyond easy. Tests are 105% average probably.

Dr. Korth is the very best!!! His classes felt like your favorite seminary class from high school. He's super nice, really respectful, and an easy grader. Start the final projects early in the semester, because they do take a little bit of time. Best religion class I've ever taken by far, I'd highly recommend!

Bro Korth is awesome. He cares a ton about what he teaches and you can tell that by the way he talks about everything. It gets a little lecture heavy without student involvement so its hard to stay completely focused. He provides close study guides for his tests which aren't too difficult. If you want an A in this class, it is there for the taking.

Two online midterms (don't worry about taking notes in class, he posts all his slides so I reviewed those for maybe an hour and got 100 on both). Course project which requires a bit of work. Final that is a paper which was nice. Lots of reading but most were conference talks so I did 2x speed. He asks that you come to class but you self grade that

Brother Korth was really nice and I really loved the discussions we would have in class. He really cares about his students and handles sensitive topics well. However, he has A LOT of assignments of varying sizes. If you are okay with that then this is a great class to take! If you are looking for an easy religion class this one is not for you.

I really loved this class from Professor Korth. There is a bit of reading, but if you do the reading and come to class and finish the assignments you will do well. The tests are both really easy. There are extra credit opportunities if you need them. He does a really good job of covering controversial topics and helps you to feel the Spirit.

Prof Korth is excellent at his job. He makes his class interesting and thought provoking, but does NOT make it unnecessarily hard like some others. I would highly recommend you take this class from him. It is pretty easy and does not require a ton of time to do well. Tests are online and pretty easy too.

Brother Korth is absolutely amazing! I have loved his class. You have a few big assignments, 2 tests, and a final that is a paper. You do PSE's after every unit where you grade yourself. This class does have a lot of readings but they are enjoyable. Make sure to come to class. The class was easy to enjoy since I didn't have to worry over my grade

Not my favorite religion professor, mostly because he just read off the slides and there wasn't a lot of class discussion. But I did learn A LOT from him and he was really good at being sensitive about difficult topics. He cares about the students, assignments are graded easily, and there is the perfect amount of homework for a religion class.

Finally a religion professor who remembers that this class is only two credits, not 5. This is my last year at BYU and Korth is the best religion teacher I have had so far. Interesting lectures and the right amount of homework to keep you interested and accountable without killing you.

Hey, it's a religion professor who teaches a 2 credit class like an actual 2 credit class! Professor Korth is an awesome lecturer who gives just the right amount of homework. Expect a couple of hours of reading a week, plus the occasional writing assignment, but this class won't attack your schedule like the Kraken that some other Rel classes are.

I took Korth for Eternal Families and he was great. Really easy grader, offers lots of extra credit, and is happy to help outside of class. I also really liked his take on the doctrines covered in the course. Nearly half the grade is comprised of attendance, so you definitely need to go to class.

Great professor, I learned a lot in his class. The class was not hard at all, the grading criteria is clear. Most of the homework is reading scriptures and reading or listening to talks which I could do while doing other things. Very respectful as we discussed tough topics. Would take from him again.

I love Brother Korth!! I truly looked forward to coming to his lectures and was sad at the end when it was over. The midterms are really easy if you do the readings and pay attention during the lectures. He is so respectful and truly cares individually about each of his students. I always felt the Spirit in his class. TAKE IT FROM BROTHER KORTH!!!

Prof Korth earnestly believes in the material in The Eternal Family class, but he creates space for you to vocalize your struggles privately or in discussion.
