He takes feedback well and looks for student input. The class is easy and well-laid out. He's relatively fair in his assessment of difficult social issues and doesn't really push an agenda.

Extremely easy to get an A in his class. There are a lot of projects and papers, but they are basically completion grades. His tests are the easiest I have seen at BYU. On the other hand, his lectures are boring and his teaching style is ineffective. I didn't gain anything spiritually or academically from this class, but at least it was an easy A.
Solid choice for a religion class if you want a non difficult professor that you actually learn stuff from in a simple, not exaggerated way.

Brother Korth is simply inspiring. He genuinely cares about EVERY single student. I loved his lectures as he shies away from no topic. His faith is super strong and this class answered SOOOO many questions that are usually considered taboo in mormon culture.
Great teacher. He gives great lectures and provide everything you need to know for every the final.

Dr. Korth is just a real stand-up guy. He is genuine, caring, and knowledgeable about the family and the doctrines surrounding it. Very easy class if you are willing to do the reading and participate because 50% of your grade is self-evaluation. He trusts students to be honest and invited them to share in class often.

Brother Korth is so kind. His class is slide heavy so prepare yourself for that. He uses a lot of quotes from Gen. Authorities during lecture. You don't really need to take notes because all the information you need to study is on the slides. So study his slides and you'll pass. He has several big assignments that aren't too difficult.
If you want to go to seminary again, take Brother Korth.
He's the bomb. Really chill dude. Doesn't teach apostasy like a lot of Professors do.

Brother Korth is a nice guy. However, his class is extremely disorganized. He assigns topic-based readings, then does not lecture on that topic and instead gives the same lecture over again, expecting his students to keep up with the schedule that he ignores. His lectures go downhill and difficult topics are opinion-based. Not the class I wanted.
Brother Korth gave the testimony-strengthening lectures. He was relatable and personable. Found/shared wonderful talks and quotes.

Brother Korth is so genuine and truly cares about his students. He'll answer any questions and leaves room for discussions if you want. This class was super easy during summer. Everything's online. He assigns a lot of readings that aren't really necessary but you get credit for just doing them and going to class
His teaching style is more lecture-y so just be aware that it may be boring at times. He also loves to assign lots of reading for credit and likes his assignments to be single spaced papers.
I LOVE THIS CLASS. no work but i always feel like i'm still learning. I can ask anything i want in that class and we will discuss it. very open very easy yet very spiritual

Brother Korth is such a good teacher. He really cares about his students and wants to help them. Each class is begun with a song, prayer, and spiritual thought. His tests are mainly doctrine based rather than based on memorization. If you think you already know a lot about eternal families you'll be surprised by how much you'll learn in his class.

Brother Korth is great. His lessons are organized and available on learning suite. All tests and projects are submitted online and participation is self evaluated. Show and be engaged and you should be fine.

It's an easy A. Go to class, do the readings, and you'll be more than fine. Lectures can get pretty boring, but go for the points. Tests are online so they're convenient and easy. Not the best religion professor I've had, but a straightforward and easy class.
Not impressed, Very boring lectures. Never fully answered his students questions. He goes off rants often.

Dr. Korth was very caring and helpful, and he really wanted all of us to succeed. My one complaint is that he told us the test should be easy if we followed the review and it was not that easy. You can boost up your grade simply by doing the readings and showing up to class, though. I learned a lot from him!

Brother Korth is such a kind and caring man.  He wants you to succeed as a student and as a person.  Class is a super easy A.  I don't feel like I left class feeling insanely inspired or that I was incredibly more well versed in church doctrine, but I did have an uplifting spiritual experience.  I would take a religion class from him again.

You have quizzes after every topic. They ask if you were present for the topic, otherwise attendance isn't really essential. Bro Korth was nice and wants his students to succeed. Assignments were easy as long as you do them before the last second. I thought lectures became increasingly repetitive throughout the semester. He offers extra credit.

Dr. Korth is very caring and makes it very easy to get a good grade.  He frequently gets behind schedule with his lectures, and he is sometimes overly apologetic with sensitive subjects, but overall, he's a great professor.

Dr. Korth is an excellent professor and is genuine in his teaching.  He is passionate about ECE and does a great job of teaching it to students.  Sometimes he gets a little stuck on topics and it is a little repetitive.  It isn't terrible but it makes it a little difficult to stay completely engaged at those points.  He listen to students.

Honestly the best and easiest class to take at BYU. Every assignment is handed to you on the first day of class, so if you want to finish the course in the first couple days of the semester, you can. Brother Korth is a great teacher and makes topics that may not necessarily relate directly to you understandable and interesting.

Brother Korth is really funny and enjoyable. There are some awkward topics, but he made them as non-awkward as possible. There is very little homework and the tests are all open note, which adds to the class's appeal. If you turn in everything on time and make an effort, you should get an A.

He would get sidetracked during lectures, and then to make sure we stayed on track would just skip material. So when we got to the tests there were things we never discussed. There are so many busy work assignments that teach you nothing. The TAs and the professors are never on the same page.

Him and Jerry Johnson co-taught this class, they were entertaining during lectures but I feel like most lecture information was not really that helpful on exams. If you go to TAs to get points back on lab assignments, and study the guides before exams, you'll be fine. The textbook is helpful but not required. TAs are a great resource in this class

Byron Adams was a great professor and I really enjoyed his class. I enjoyed his lectures because him and Jerry would try to make boring lectures a little more interesting. I did not enjoy how the class felt pretty disorganized. Some of the bigger assignments didn't give very many instructions it oftentimes felt unclear. The textbook is not needed

Weekly group study session required, textbook is pretty irrelevant, schedule is a little messy up to the first exam but cleans up after that. Test review material will save your grade. Good class super funny, if you're here to learn then you will learn a lot, but if your just here to pass the class it would be easy to retain nothing.

I hated this class. It had so much potential but it was so poorly organized. Exam dates were moved last minute. Textbook readings are irrelevant and we were always behind in lectures. The only way to suceed is to memorize the TA exam review slides, like word for word. They say the class isn't about memorization but it totally is. I learned nothing.

If you took BIO130 from him and want another of his classes, this is not the one. There is almost no new material, though it is interesting stuff. There are 5 small papers and one major one. WATCH OUT FOR THE FREE RESPONSE SECTION ON TESTS. Not that it's hard, but that it's fairly long. Overall a pretty decent class, I recommend

This was just a fun class.  I don't know why other people complain about the workload; it was way easier and less of a time commitment than the other 2 credit STEM classes I have taken.  Just memorize his slides and especially the TA reviews and the exams won't be hard.

Ate an entire (9.25 oz) bag of Dorito's in class on Halloween as part of a "gamer" costume. Class was great, labs were somewhat off-track from the lectures, overall a great class. Whenever I asked a question outside of class, he would always answer and then provide extra information and background on the topic I asked about. Fantastic professor!
I loved Prof Adams and Johnson (they teach together for this class). They are SO qualified and care so much for their students. Would absolutely suggest taking Bio 130 from them!
I felt cared for, included and respected in his class.
This class was dual taught by Dr. Adams and Jerry Johnson. Solid overall, their lectures were engaging and usually easy to follow.

I took anatomy and found it super interesting and fun!  It is extremely memorization-heavy, so you have to be willing to devote the necessary time to preparing for lab quizzes and lab and lecture exams.  My grades on the exams were very clearly correlated to how much time I spent preparing for it.

This class was with Byron Adams and Jerry Johnson team teaching. Byron was gone unexpectedly for most of the semester doing research in Antarctica but when he was there he was often the comic relief. He is so passionate about biology and stewardship and the gospel of Jesus Christ. The class took effort but it was so worth it.

Prof. Adams was amazing! He was lots of fun, and explained topics very thoroughly and clearly. Lectures are pretty heavy, but they upload the slides to learning suite in case you missed something. Would love to take another class from him.

WOULD RECOMMEND. He was so funny and a great teacher. Really made class entertaining and fun, without detracting from the educational part. If you do all the work, go to class, and study, you'll do great.

This is the closest any class has come to breaking my 4.0 lol. It was a little hard to know what/how to study for tests, and they're sometimes graded somewhat arbitrarily by TAs. That said, the course material is really interesting and he gives engaging lectures. Idk what I came away from the class really knowing, but Byron is a great guy, love him

He teaches his class like it's a standup comedy show. He gets sidetracked very easily, and his lectures can be hard to follow. All of his tests are largely memorizing lists, so GO TO THE TA REVIEWS. They pretty much tell you everything you need to know. Grading on tests and papers is very harsh, so study and put in a lot of effort on papers.

He and Jerry are so funny! Their lectures were fun to go to. It was difficult material, most of the people who did well are people who took AP Bio in high school, and they relied almost entirely on previous knowledge. For people like me who didn't, we had to basically teach ourselves the material. TAs are accessible and helpful, go to test prep.

Took this class with Byron and Jerry. They are some of my favorite teachers I have ever had. It felt more like stand up comedy than class. That being said they sometimes get behind on lectures but of you study on your own time you got this easy.

Byron and Jerry taught BIO 130 together. I rarely read the textbook - just for diagrams and questions. Pay attention to any posters and homework they assign, stay on top of the book and and go to review sessions and this class is easy! They do tend to wander during lectures, but attend so you understand the major points better.

BYRON AND JERRY JOHNSON ARE SO FUNNY! They teach the class in a way that does not confound religion and science, which is something I am very careful of avoiding myself at BYU. They are funny and they had phenomenal TAs. Go to TA hours and you'll be fine. Tests are difficult, but they prepare you well for them. Bio 130 was fun because of them.

So funny. I took this class with him and Jerry Johnson. I have so many pictures of them in weird and random costumes just teaching biology. Could use a LOT more organization though. Plus, a lot of reading. The only reason I got an A was because of the curve...

His lectures were great, but organization is not good. Half of the "study guides" weren't on the tests, and some of his assignments either made me feel like I was in middle school or weren't clearly explained. The worst thing was that they clearly explained the curve they'd put on the class, then they never applied it

Bio 130 with Byron and Jerry was my favorite class I've ever taken! They're so funny and teach meaningful topics that I found very interesting. The lectures are entertaining and they go over possible exam questions and let you know what to do to get prepared for tests. One essay, weekly lab homework, group studying, and some other assignments.

Byron team taught this class with Jerry Johnson. Super funny and really knew his stuff. Lecture was always very fun and interesting. Definitely would recommend his class to anyone, especially those that want to learn or have a short attention span (like myself).

Just expect to treat this like a 3-credit class. Byron is great but gets easily sidetracked. Go to the TA reviews, work on the study guides with your (required) study groups and you'll do fine. He brought snacks for everyone to the final, so I feel like that tells you what you need to know. Sometimes the TAs grade differently which is frustrating.

This class was way too much work for a 2 credit class (more than my 4 credit 400 level classes). He is a tough grader and looks for any opportunity to take off points - it's not enough to just meet rubric criteria. Tests are very long and difficult and you have to know the material in great detail (tests are mostly fill-in-the-blank and essays).

Byron is a really fun teacher, but not really the best for helping you understand material. He and Jerry Johnson taught together. Most of learning is done in lab with TAs. You have to write a paper on Your Inner Fish, which kinda felt like a dumb assignment. Tests aren't too bad if you put in the work. There are some good extra credit opportunities

Dr. Adam's class was really awesome! He did a really great job making the lectures full of interesting information. The class had lots of tests that were heavily based on the examples given in the lecture sides. He required that we meet with study groups outside of class (1.5-2hrs/wk). This is a really interesting class but you need to study.

Buckle up kids, this is one of the hardest two-credit classes you will ever take. The lectures were great, but there is just SO MUCH content. Get ready to memorize... Adams did a great job blending science and religion. Lots of papers. Exams aren't too bad, but you NEED to study. There's a textbook but you dont have to use it IMO. Class is curved.

I took this class and the higher level evolution class at the same time, so it was a lot of repeat material for me, but Dr. Adams is really funny and kept the lecture entertaining. There was a fair amount of writing and some of the criteria could be a bit muddy depending on the TA grading it. Overall, a pretty solid class.

Hes funny in a dad kind of way, and reconciles faith and science extremely well. The class wasnt a breeze but he provided the means to be successful. I took AP Bio so I didnt need to read the textbook, but doing so could only benefit. Highly recommend Professor Adams. :)

Byron and Jerry Johnson team taught Bio 130. Both Byron and Jerry are hilarious and they explain things super well. They answer questions with ease and really know their stuff! The tests were hard, but not unreasonable if you attend TA reviews. You really don't need the textbook. Overall, they're some of the best professors in the life sciences.

Him and Jerry were fun & silly. The class itself was ok, but honestly I learned nothing real. They taught like 25 different concepts per lecture & went over really big things in biology for like 5 min and went over things we really didn't have to know for 25 min. TBH I felt like I was wasting my time. Study groups didn't really help & were annoying

Half the class is super cool, the other half is DRY but Byron does 12/10 job at making it enjoyable. I was laughing every class. He made everything apply to our lives to make us better people- not the normal BYU church way (did that too) but in real ways. Not to be poetic but it isnt a class, it's an experience. A lot of papers but worth it.

Professor Adams is a funny guy. He is easy-going and likes to answer students' questions, even if they stray from the topic he's teaching. The TAs for this class were most helpful in explaining how they were going to grade assignments, which made a big difference for me. Byron teaches, but the grades come from the TAs.
This class was unorganized. Lectures and study guides do not prepare you for the exams. Adams and Johnson were at least entertaining but often wasted time. My lab TA was not that great.

Adams is hilarious. He gets sidetracked often, so be aware and ready for some random stories. He does care though, and is easy to talk to. This is a hard class. Unless you're sure you LOVE science, maybe stick with BIO 100. A lot of the teaching comes from TAs and make sure to study and take their advice.

Some people might love Adams style of teaching, which is joke heavy, constantly sidetracked, and running behind schedule, but it wasn't for me. For an hour and a half of lecture, only about half was useful information (most of which could be learned just as well from the textbook). TA's do the bulk of the teaching in lab.

Hilarious professor, but tests can be a little hard. Tests consist of MC and essays, but if you memorize the slides, you'll do fine. Papers aren't too hard, but a grasp of principles taught in class help to get 10/10's on them

This class was too funny and I never knew what I actually had to study for the tests. Whenever an exam came along, I never used my lecture notes to study and I felt like I was studying for an entirely different class. I like classes that help me to pass the tests, not ones that revolve around jokes and being funny.

Dr Adams is SO RAD- he's extremely smart but really humble and teaches in a fun, accessible way. He takes an interesting subject and makes it fascinating, and the class isn't too much work at all. I never read out of the textbook, just went to TA reviews and reviewed his slides. TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Adams is a great teacher. He is super funny and makes lectures interesting. The class is hard but if you go to labs, office hours and put the time in with studying you will be fine. I really enjoyed his class.

Dr. Adams is hilarious. He makes Biology fun and loves to connect with his students. He's passionate about nematodes and evolution. The class isn't too bad if you do your reading and pay attention in class. Look at the study guides to know what you need to remember. If you fill them out and study them in groups, you'll do fine.

Professor Adams is funny but so much that is distracts from the class.  He will also openly mock whoever opposes his views on evolution so beware of that.  He has a true passion for his field of study but his field of study is not Bio 130 so I imagine his higher level classes are more effective, but in Bio 130 I learned very little.

Dr. Adams is an entertaining lecturer, very smart, clearly cares about students. I loved taking 420 from him. Be prepared to put in some effort-- this class was just as much work as many of the 3-credit classes I've had (seven 2-page essays, final paper, 2 fairly tough midterms + final) and the best grade in my class pre-curve was 92%.

My class was co-taught with Jerald Johnson. They were hilarious. I never used the book. Everything on the test is from lecture. TA reviews help. They offer extra credit for going on a date with someone you teach your poster project to. I really enjoyed this class. You do have to read Your Inner Fish by Neil Shubin and write a paper on it.

I took this class when it was team taught by Dr. Adams and Dr. Johnson. It's not an inherently easy class but they definitely make it possible! Be willing to study and take good notes during lecture and you will be fine. They also had great ties between biology and LDS religion that helped me learn how to better reconcile the two. Take this class!

This was by far my favorite class this semester. Dr. Adams Co-taught with Dr. Johnson and they were quite the pair! They made lectures so interesting and taught the material very well. They genuinely cared about their students concerns, opinions, and success. This class takes a lot out of you, but there are plenty of resources to help you succeed!

He co-taught this class with Dr. Johnson when I took it. They explained all the important material really well and had a great balance of serious teaching and more funny things to keep our focus. It's one of the most entertaining classes I've taken. They also took time to comment on the topics from a gospel standpoint which kept things clear.

This class is very difficult but Bryon is the best! I want to switch majors just so I can take more courses from him. He is easy to get along with, and he wants nothing more than to see his students succeed. He also gives the best pep talks before exams. I would recommend the class; it wont be easy, but I learned so much and had fun doing it!

Professor Adams has a great sense of humor and, for the most part, did a awesome job with his lectures. I loved being in class everyday, Professor Adams is the reason I switched to Bio. Realize this isn't an easy class, I spent a ton of time in the Bio Lab getting help from TA's. Would definitely recommend,  but be ready to work.

He is awesome. Would almost switch to a bio major to take more of his classes. Hilarious, and stuff he taught me has helped me out in several other classes. Kind of tough, but manageable, and he loves the subject. Really wants you to love biology as much as he does.

GOT AN A---barely. Did well on the tests. Got an A-, A, and A on the tests. Final was easier than the midterms. I worked hard and did every reading. I never missed class, but was late one time. This class you will do well if you just work hard. I got an A despite not doing well on the paper we write. I got a B on that I think. GOOD LUCK GUYS! take!

Professor Adams is a people person, which is why he gets some positive reviews. But as a teacher, he is horrendous. The readings for class rarely corresponded to the lecture content. He provides lists of material that could be on the test, but these are very inaccurate. I survived because I spent hours upon hours studying the textbook.
Difficult. Don't take unless you have the time to put into the class.

He's a good lecturer.  He's terrible at writing tests; the questions are always really subjective and unclear, which makes it difficult to get an A even if you know everything.  Labs are excruciatingly boring and pointless (3 hrs, miss two and fail).  Often assigns lengthy readings that have material you never need.

I loved this class! He's a way cool dude (he talks like that too) and you learn a lot. Overall it was a blast and not too difficult. I found that doing the reading helped. He also gave these awesome motivational pep talks before tests. I think he's the best for Bio 130.

He'll keep you laughing the entire lecture and you're still learning a ton! Bio 130 is a more hands-on approach to biology, and I definitely recommend it to anyone who has an interest in majoring in biology. Take this class from Byron! It's my favorite class and made me love biology! He is also really approachable and makes the class interactive!

Best professor for this class hands down. He makes the class interesting and knows so much.  You have to read the txtbk for in-class quizzes. He really wants to make sure you understand the material. Best class I've ever taken at BYU.

First time teaching the class.  Tried too hard to be funny in the beginning of the year, but after his mid-semester review Adams completely changed for the better.  The class is very difficult for a 2-credit class, but he gives many extra credit opportunities (around 8-10%) and you'll come out of the class with a new interest in biology.

Prof. Adams is a good teacher. Don't expect to not do work, and especially DO THE READING. It makes everything else in class make sense. Also, the TA's are there for help, so use them. The tests aren't bad, just don't expect to not have to study.

Dr. Adams is an incredible teacher. If you are willing to put in the work and make an effort yourself then you'll do well. He keeps class entertaining and relates the material in ways that help it make sense and goes above the bare minimum. Both review sessions and study guides are helpful. I love this class and wouldn't take it from anyone else!

Take this class if you are interested in learning a lot. If you came to college not to learn then go ahead and take someone else. His tests are a little hard but MORE THAN FAIR. His TA students hold weekly reviews for anyone interested. (Go to these). And he reviews the information for a full day before the test, telling you what you need to study.

He reviews everything you need to know for the test in class with you. All these haters clearly dont want to think. They dont want to work. You will learn more from adams than any other professor. Take it from him and you will not be sorry. I didnt know any bio before taking this class and loved it. I would only take this class from him.

Tough Teacher. Basic Material. Take from other teacher unless you plan to go on to molecular and want to learn a lot now. I honestly hated the class, but learned material in prior biology classes. Wants you to apply, which is great, but doesn't teach what to apply. Don't take. He's funny, but you'll you'll be sorry.Class is Easy A from other Profs.

Dr. Adams expects you to THINK.  His TA's hold weekly review sessions where you can go ask them ANYTHING about the material and those review sessions seriously saved my grade. Basically free one on one tutoring.  The previous comments are harsh because they can't apply what they've learned.  I really enjoyed this class, but I had to work for it.

Wow, lots of harsh stuff here. I loved this class and DR. Adams. If you are willing to put in the work (go to class, do the reading, go to review sessions) you will do well and learn a ton. He does not spoon feed you and that bothers a lot of people. Dont let those below me deter you, Dr. Adams is an awesome teacher and this is an awesome class.

This is a joke. He is seriously the worst teacher in the world. His lectures are completely pointless and you don't learn anything from him. He cares more about being funny and being nice to the students than actually teaching them biology. Worst teacher I've ever had. Avoid at all cost.

Terrible teacher. You learn absolutely nothing from him. His greatest concern is that students like him, not that they actually learn anything. More of a stand up comedian than a professor. You feel like you learn nothing from the lectures, then he expects you to know an inordinate amount of info for his exams. Avoid if possible!

This is honestly the worst teacher I've ever had... Interestingly he's also possibly the funniest.. Its his first time teaching the class... hopefully his last. He teaches nothing.lectures are pointless. you have to memorize the book and think his way to do good at all. Luckily basic class So I previously learned most material.

Awesome class, awesome professor. He explains the material with enthusiasm and applies it to modern day terms to solidify the concepts. The tests are easy if you do the reading and follow the review sheets. HIGHLY RECOMMEND

Adams is a funny guy, good instructor, and genuinely nice too. Unfortunately he has no idea what is reasonable. Every day we read 50-100 pages from the text, tests are extremely difficult and you have no idea what to study. I have a harder time and spend more time for this class than I did for CHEM105 or MMBIO361. Avoid if at all possible!
Awesome. Honestly how could you improve molecular biology more than handing out sweet prizes for correct answers during class?

Dr. Adams is pretty fun. He likes to give out sauce packets for good answers which is always a laugh. And he tends to put up random but hilarious pictures on his slides. But his class is really disorganized. The packet is a nightmare. I had a really hard time knowing what I was supposed to learn. oh and the textbook is difficult.
he's a great person.  His tests are really hard if you don't think how he wants you to.  The book is worthless.  Study his packet and class slides to do well.

You have to study a ton to keep up. taking it during the summer was a mistake. But byron is one of my favorite teachers. Funny, which made it easier to stay awake. Learned a lot! but tests (im not so good at) and his were fairly difficult, but not impossible.
You have to take this class from him! He is hilarious.
One of the best teachers I've ever had. He is hilarious!

He has a fun personality that made this science class unique. The take home quizzes were impossible w/out TA reviews. Daily reading quizzes aren't bad if you actually did the reading. You should attend regularly, but I don't think missing a couple would kill. Tests were hard but possible. I scored well, but studied my tail off for this class.
The professor was really fun. Quizzes were practically impossible without TA help.  Tests were pretty hard.

His "surfer-dude" personality is kind of a turnoff and comes off as not very genuine; it feels like an act he puts on to impress students.  He is extremely intelligent (sometimes impatient with slower students) and has impressive credentials (which actually leads you to believe even more so that his classroom behavior is a farce).

Great class but it seemed that Dr. Adams was just trying to impress the students. He has a unique personality that seems cool at first but then gets old. If you keep up on the readings and go to the TA sessions you should do really well. Tests are fair in my opinion not the easiest. Take your time and read each question carefully!

Dr. Adams offers a refreshing change of pace. He is very entertaining, and also brilliant. So, while class may seem all fun and games, dont let yourself get behind or underestimate the difficulty of his tests. Exams are hard, and you will need to befriend a TA in order to get an A in this class. Also, you will need to read a LOT. Choose Adams.

Dr. Adams was hilarious and definitely made the class fun and interesting to attend. Tests are hard, lots of (dry) reading required for in-class quizzes, and you WILL NOT do well in the class without attending TA review sessions.  Adams is very helpful and courteous in response to questions.  I definitely recommend taking from Dr. Adams
This class was hard.  It requires a lot of outside work.  Byron is a cool guy, but sometimes his analogies don't really work.  It's important to go to the review sessions with the TAs to do well.
Byron is a funny guy, but the class is hard and often its hard to follow what is going on. The tests are pretty hard but fair. Study a lot and go to the TA reviews!

Loved this class. Dr. Adams is the man.  He is so funny.  Just make sure you go to the TA help sessions and read before you come to class for the quizes.  Takes a little work to get a good grade, but I love the guy.  I never thought Molecular Biology could be so interesting.
He's an awesome teacher.  Makes the topic interesting and lectures are always fun to come to.  His test are hard but fair and everyone can do well in his class.  Group study totally recommended!!! :D
Awesome teacher!

this dude is a total bro.!! i put this class off forever cuz everyone told me how hard bridgewater was.  I asked every bio student who the easiest bio 240 teacher was and no one even knew who adams was except for one grad student.  when i asked him about adams he started laughing because he is so easy compared to the other teachers.  The funny thin

Great Class.  I learned a ton.  Don't take it from anyone else.  I would recommend him to anyone.  He's lectures are way entertaining and he is way hilarious.  The class isn't very easy but if you go to the TA reviews religiously you'll do fine.  Byron is the man!

adams is great.i didn't want to take the class because i'm not too interested in the subject, but adams made it an enjoyable class.he's funny and makes it easy to pay attention.i learned a lot and recommend taking him for this class.DON'T TAKE ANYONE ELSE FOR BIO240.tests are tough, but there are lots of free points in the class to make up for it

Great Teacher - Great class.  Probably the only teacher at BYU who can incorporate Rage Against the Machine in his power point lecture and get away with it.  He LOVES what he teaches and that helped me want to study.  His tests contain A LOT of true and false questions which to me was very annoying.
Great class.  The man is hilarious.  Some of the examples were a little off the wall but overall a great experience.
great guy. lots of fun, but tough tests. Dont take the class from anyone else. I would pay money for the kind of comedy he produces in class.
Byron makes lectures on an otherwise tedious courese very interesting.

Byron is an awesome professor!  He is very enthusiastic about the most boring subject and makes it fun.  He always has random jokes and has fun with the students.  His tests are medium hard, but if you study you got the A.  I totally recommend him.
No Comments

Byron rocks.  As a person, but not as a professor.  He's very funny and enthusiastic about an otherwise boring class, which is great.  His 'surfer-dude' attitude entertains, but isn't the best for teaching a complicated class.

Dr. Simmons is very smart in mathematics but is very naive in teaching. This course was entitled Statistics using Excel, except the class was in a classroom and Dr. Simmons wrote everything on the board by hand- we hardly used excel. Additionally, he had unrealistic expectations on the amount of material he wanted us to cover in a very short time.

I took this class during a summer term as a freshman right after studying calculus for a full year in high school. While this class isn't a calculus class, math was very fresh in my mind still. I worked hard in this class and felt like the practice tests and reviews truly prepared me for the exams. He rounded up my grade for me which was super nice
Dr Simmons was a great Professor. Any Calculus class is difficult, but he explains the concepts very well. Lots of homework, but it prepares you for the tests.

Simmons is a pretty good math teacher. There is a lot of homework, but the online homework tells you if you got the right answer or not, and the book gives you the paper homework answers so it's easy to get full credit. Because the homework is set up like this, the class is pretty easy to understand. If you've taken calc before, you should get an A

Simmons is probably the best math teacher I've ever had, which is saying a lot. He is absolutely hilarious, always engaging, extremely clear in lecture, and always wanting to help. I would definitely take a class form him again!
Professor Simmons was great. He taught clearly and was helpful. I always felt like I understood the concepts and that if there was any questions, I would get a helpful answer.

Great Teacher!  I didn't expect much first day of class, but I was wrong.  He answer every question even when we're short on time. If something seems unclear, he'll deviate from his notes and go over it in more detail to help us understand.  Tough course, but he really tries to help us understand.  Also, great sense of humor. Dry jokes. Awesome.

The class starts off really easy and then gets harder throughout the semester. Go to class and pay attention to the lecture. I never took any notes, and I was fine. If anything doesn't make sense, or you get stuck on the homework, go to his office hours; he loves helping students and can explain abstract concepts very clearly. Very fair grader.

I loved Simmon's class. Be careful and thorough on proofs and memorize the list of things he gives you as "given." His lectures are pretty much straight from the book -- I highly recommend reading the section before class and following along with the book during class.
I liked Skyler as a teacher.  He was funny and pretty good at explaining things.  The tests seemed abnormally brutal though.  Very nit-picky on proofs.

Brother Simmons' lectures are engaging. He cares about his students and he wants to help them understand the material. Don't be afraid to ask questions, do the homework, and the subject isn't too terrible.
Hilarious guy, explains concepts well, very generous with office hours.

I don't like being rude, but Skippy is the worst professor I've ever had. He has a terrible time explaining things, and is so utterly boring. His class is miserable. The topic is time consuming, but would be with any teacher. At least take the class from someone interesting. Worst teacher I've had at BYU so far. Would not take again. Avoid him. BOO
Skippy is awesome! Very funny, enthusiastic, and explains things super clearly. Very helpful during office hours. Made differential equations doable.

Such an easy class with a great teacher. He has a funny sense of humor that made us laugh even at 8am in the morning! He teaches the stuff through examples. You take the final every week and if you pass then you dont have to come to class! Easy class! Awesome teacher! The only easy pre-req for Marriott School
Straightforward class. I took Calc in high school and passed the exam the second week of class. Once you pass the exam you're done, so it was nice to have some free time.
I had to take this class to get into the Business program. Similar "final" exams were offered once a week. All you have to do is pass it once. Take it every week and you'll be fine.

This class wasn't that bad. Go to all of the reviews that he has for the tests and learn how to do all the problems and it is an easy pass. I never took calc in high school and I did have to study quite a bit, but I managed to get through it okay. Go to his office hours, he is always willing to help.

This class you just have to pass the final test to pass the class. The Test are nothing like what we do in class. In class I understood it but it was as if the tests were in greek. I ended up being one question away from passing the test and I completely failed the class.

Math 341 during the Summer is really intense - expect it to be at least a part-time job. However, Dr. Bott is a legend! Spiritual thoughts through the roof, knows sooo much math too. Lectures incredible - he explains well and makes math truly exciting! He cares about both math and you. I would 100% recommend. Get ready to let epsilon! :)

MATH 341 at double-speed in the summer is intense. By necessity, there is so much homework. But CJ makes the class very engaging and doable. He gives amazing lectures, answers emails quickly, and gives deep, helpful spiritual thoughts. He demands a lot of rigor, but he will help you actually learn analysis. I couldn't recommend a professor more

C.J. was absolutely amazing as my MATH 314 professor. Always gave his all and you could tell he genuinely cares for all his students. Definitely would take this class again with him even though calc 3 can be pretty hard with the material.

CJ is incredible. His 341 course is extremely rigorous. He has some reading, but most of it is covered in class. His weekly tests are usually easy, and his lectures are really interesting. He is funny and he/his TA's are accessible outside of class and always open to questions. The grades are weighted well, so if you mess up on one assignment you can always catch up on another.

First--show up to class, the lectures really help, but everything we cover is in the reading so I guess you can decide if you want to come, attendance isn't taken. Amazing professor--cares about his students and wants to see them succeed, progress, and become better. Would definitely take another class from him. One of the best people here at BYU.

I was not excited to take this class, but Cacey made it amazing. He is hilarious and a good professor. He reviews material in class at least 2x which makes it easy to remember what he wants you to know, and the quizzes every week are easy as long as you read.

I really enjoyed my time with Dr. Farnsworth, his knowledge on family history research is amazing and he was always willing to help students when they asked. The lectures were full of useful information and tips for personal research. The class is focused around researching one family group so your grade relies heavily upon this project.
Great lecturer. He gives study guides, which are really useful. The entire grade is based on one paper, two midterms, and a final, which I'm not a fan of, but the tests themselves weren't super hard.

I cannot even describe how amazing Cacey is, he is one of my favorite professors I have had. He is extremely helpful and wants his students to do well. There is one big project due at the end of the semester, but the assignments during the semester are different parts of the final and he gives great feedback. I would definitely recommend Cacey!

Such a good teacher! We focused on one project the whole semester. Yes you had to put in quite a few hours but you learn a lot. The final in its self was very due-able! I probably emailed a million times during the semester and he was very quick to respond and help. His TA was just as helpful too! Youre set for success if you take the class.

You have a semester long family history project (this is college not Institute so stop whining about having HW). It takes some time but if you do the checkup assignments along the way then by final time it will be nearly done already. Need help? Ask! He changed how he did things halfway through the semester to be more helpful which was awesome.
Professor McCoy is awesome!! He was very involved and truly loves his job! He stayed active and really talked with students

Dr McCoy is interesting. I think we would get along well outside of school but when he was my teacher he was just difficult. He graded very harshly with unclear criteria. He purposefully misunderstands or misconstrues what students are trying to say but its for the sake of "making us better." I needed lots of help to pass. Not a good experience

Professor McCoy is one who inspires you to be better and to do better. I failed my first assignment, but I took advantage of every opportunity and improved exponentially. There is a process in place, trust the process. McCoy knows what he's doing and he wants to help you succeed, let him help you.

Dr. McCoy is one of the most arrogant people I have ever met. He will wave his PhD in your face every chance he gets. His class was interesting but I have a sour taste in my mouth from my experiences with him in and out of class. He must be right and intentionally or unintentionally likes to make students feel lesser.

Dr. McCoy has very high expectations for his students, but its because he knows what their potential is. This class was heavy on the reading and the research for the final paper, but Dr. McCoy is always there to help and is a very attentive listener. His office is always open for help, and you will need help because the course is very difficult.
If you work hard you will get a good grade! He will hook you up if he sees you are trying and want to be there! Best teacher!

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. You were expected to read 50 pages per class from the textbook, as well as 30-60 pages in articles, as well as reading 3 books throughout the semester. two of the books were necessary to read for tests, 1 book had a casual 15 page essay due. His essays were graded VERY harshly, and his lectures were harsh.

Professor McCoy is one of the best professors at BYU. He ensures that you as a student are treated as a professional and take responsibility for the work you do. McCoy is very accessible and is willing to work with you and be flexible if you reach out to him and put in the effort.

Dr. McCoy is both professional and personable. He goes out of his way to help students to succeed, but EXPECTS YOU TO LISTEN AND FOLLOW DIRECTIONS. Don't overthink the HW. Come ready to play if you want to offer an opposite view of his. Read the books he gives you, follow his instructions EXACTLY on how to complete assignments, and you'll be fine.

This man should be a legend. He is single-handedly trying to fix problems with how BYU students are perceived after graduation due to their education. He requires a lot of participation, which is great for a class on something as raw as history. He isn't afraid to push back and make you defend your position. He is one of the most capable teachers.

Dr. McCoy may seem intimidating at first, but he really is approachable once you get to know him. He may seem tough on grading papers, but if you meet with him and follow his guidelines, you will succeed and become a better writer. He really expands perspective about racial issues and teaches history in a non-canonical way.

Dr. McCoy gives a great perspective on history that is different from most teachers at BYU. He is very real and makes you think about what you are saying. Class discussions were very interesting, but the way he grades was hard. It is impossible to get a good grade in his class, but you do come out of it learning a lot.

Professor McCoy provides a necessary look into history that is neglected at BYU. He is tough and he demands excellence but he also makes it possible to attain by being available to meet with students. If you want to go to graduate school, he is a good professor to prepare you.

I learned so much from Professor McCoy. I would take this class again and again. I learned so much, and it wasnt just about history it was about the world today. There are a lot of writing assignments, but his office is always open if you need help. If you arent afraid to have your way of thinking challenged, this class is for you.

Dr. McCoy is amazing. He really cares for his students. He is a breath of fresh air at BYU, and he has expanded my mind. He does grade differently than other professors at BYU, but after you speak to him, it will be a lot easier! He's a true gem.

This class is a lot harder than you think it will be and I've never written or stressed about so many papers in my life. He doesn't post grades online or anything. Participation is part of your grade. Be ready to have to talk in class. You basically have to go to his office hours to get a good grade. This class is much harder than a typical GE.

You don't feel like you are learning from a professor but from a friend. I absolutely loved his class. But, do not take his class if you have to get a good grade. He grades like you are in grad school and the class usually requires a TON of work. You'll get frustrated and wish you hadn't taken his class but ultimately, you'll learn a lot from him.
This man is scary but he will teach you to write well. So, intimidating but completely worth the effort. He is willing to work with students more than any other professor I had.

Prof. McCoy is extremely tough but he makes up for it by being available to meet with students to discuss papers and make improvements. He is often unclear about grading (or inconsistent) but this will never reflect negatively on you or your grade. If you put in the work you will get a good grade and have an eye-opening experience with history.

Not a good teacher at all. For a GE his class is incredibly hard and I would never take a class from him again. The grading criteria was extremely unclear, very self righteous. He changed the syllabus so many times during the course and couldn't not even vocalize what his expectations were until he was grading. Always pointing out faults in others.

Incredibly difficult for a GE course. Expectations for work were often unclear while grading was intense. Prof. McCoy knows his history and does a good job lecturing and providing times to meet with students, but the work necessary to succeed in this course is more than usually required for a 200 level course.

Dr. Andersen is a wonderful person, but was unfortunately very unhelpful. In our 1-1 meeting, she told me I was doing well in the course and that I shouldn't be concerned. I then earned over 2.5% HIGHER in the class than the standard grade distribution for an A and was instead given an A- based on an extremely harsh curve in the class.

She was unhelpful with assignments and really hard with grading. Her lectures were long and unhelpful. She is definitely very smart, and I enjoyed talking with her one on one. But as far as a professor, I wouldn't take a class from her again.

I have nothing but good things to say about Dr. Andersen. She is a relatively new professor, but it's like she's been teaching for years. Just come to class, be an engaged learner, turn in your assignments on time (there's light HW, a few papers, etc.) and you'll be fine. Please please please take Living Prophets from her. You won't regret it!

This was my favorite class this semester. Dr. Andersen cared so much about her students and I learned so much from her. Her class is easy as long as you read the talks and do the assignments. You 100% recommend taking Living Prophets from her.
Dr. Andersen is one of the best professors I've ever had. She really cares about her students. She was the first professor I've had that knew my name. Take this class!

Really great professor and asks for everyone to participate. I enjoyed and looked forward to coming to every class. Homework load was light, and she really does care for each student. She takes the time to learn your names, and definitely is very strong in the gospel.

She is an awesome teacher, and her class is super chill. Show up, stay on top of the assignments, you will pass, and you will have a good experience learning important useful things. She will ask everyone to participate, and she has a lot to say. She keeps it spiritual, and works really well with the students. Take her class for credit.

Mevrouw Congrove is difficult. There is no syllabus and the grading is just based off if she likes you or not. While she does laugh at your jokes, the class is too much just sit there and watch. I feel like she tries to play "professor" too much by forcing so many assignments and slides with no rubric.

This class is pretty difficult. The vast majority of your grade comes from the exams and essays. The exams are quite hard and require extensive knowledge (practically memorization) of the poems and short stories; the essays are easier but are harshly graded. There are required readings for every class, but they help your Dutch vocabulary a lot.

Mevrouw Congrove is the best! Her classes are really not as difficult as people think. Make sure to review well for the exams. There is also one paper that you write at the end of the semester, but she gives feedback and allows you to make corrections before turning it in. If you study and pay attention in class it's easy.

This is definitely a serious class. This class included reading and analyzing a packet of old-current Dutch literary texts. The tests are pretty difficult and involve memorizing the stories and poems. You have 4 presentations to give on authors. Professor Congrove is very kind and funny, but be prepared to study for this class.

She is extremely nice. You will learn. It was difficult that she assigns homework and either grade it so late that by the time you received it, it did not matter anymore, or that most of the homework she assigned never ended as a grade. Her class is straight outside of the box and creative. My Dutch improved a lot thanks to her technics.

Prof Owens treats her students like human beings and I respect her so much! She's so kind and makes the class enjoyable. Her class is more lecture heavy in the beginning and then mostly only toward the end. This is very helpful with other classes/finals. Choose her as a professor for COMMS 319!

Professor Owens is awesome! Seriously, if you have the chance, take 319 from her. You do have to attend class as attendance is a big part of your grade. But she is super helpful in making sure you understand the content.
Some of the labs in the class are confusing. Doctor Peterson herself is phenomenal, and the lectures are generally interesting.

Professor Peterson did well teaching this class. It was a good introduction for anyone considering the Electrical and Computer Engineering or Cybersecurity program at BYU. It was a simple class as an overview of the program, so for myself, an Electrical Engineering major, the class was simply just a requirement for the program.

I get this was just a seminar course, but it was rough. I came out with no additional knowledge about the program and oftentimes left class more confused. It's not worth your time to attend class. She takes no control over lectures and most time is spent answering dumb questions from the syllabus.
Professor Peterson was pretty average. Seeing as 191 is a seminar class, it's not a very difficult class. Professor Peterson kept me interested during the weekly lectures.

I enjoyed this class. There are some challenging topics, and many of us had a rough experience in one of the prereqs and were slow at first, but she worked to make sure we got caught up and could succeed. The exams were straightforward. The only major class issue was out of her control: constant hardware failures for the lab equipment.

She starts every class with a spiritual connection to what we are learning in class. She is very kind and easy to work with.
EcEn 191 is a pass fail class with a variety of paths to take in order to get enough points in the class.

ECEn 483 (also listed as ME 431) is a very difficult class. This was her first time teaching an undergrad class, and I think only the second class she's taught. She was hands down one of the best professors I've ever taken a class from. She was very interested in helping us learn the material and was often late in the lab with us solving HW issues.
Professor Newell's etiquette class was one of my favorites this semester and I'd recommend that everyone take it. She is caring and funny, and the class is light work with high life relevance.
One of the easiest A's at BYU. Also, one of the most respected and caring professors here. Just take it

Professor Newell was the best professor I have every had! I took her "Professional Etiquette" course and learned so much. Her resume makes her qualified to teach it. MOST impactful class I took at BYU! Super easy course - virtually no time spent outside of class. She was great at getting everyone involved and was invested in our success.

She is so nice and so qualified to teach this professional etiquette class. Lectures were so interesting and useful in everyday life, and it is graded easy, I got 100% on every assignment and review quiz. There are also a lot of extra credit options. In the lectures there are always funny videos and class participation.

Professor Newell is goated. This is easily one of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU, and it was super easy. She likes students to interact with each other, so be ready to do that. Great class, made me want to be a better person.

Professor Newell's class was awesome! She and her co-professor (Sterling May) taught fantastically, and all the lectures and homework really helped me in terms of finding out what I wanted from Grad School and looking at where would be best. I have recommended this class to tons of my friends and would recommend it to anyone looking at grad school.

I took this class by accident but ended up loving it! Professor Newell is one of the neatest people and I learned so many valuable lessons from this class. She designs the class in a way so students cannot easily fail.

It was a really easy class but I feel like I learned a lot. It's a nice two credit filler course and Dr. Newell is an amazing teacher with incredible stories. You can really tell that she cares about what she teaches.
Professor Newell is really great! She has had some cool experiences globally and tells interesting stories. She is a very gentle and sincere person with a lot of heart.

If you are considering taking this class, DO IT. Professor Newell is the most amazing professor and inspires the class everyday. It is not difficult at all and the homework assignments are all rewarding. This class changed my life, and I am sure it will change yours.
Dr. Newell shares a solid combination of the concept addressed through the student development classes at BYU. I would definitely recommend taking if you have never taken a student development class.
Do not take it. Most annoying and frustrating class. the dumbest assignments and dumbest final too. Promotes yes culture and other dumb nonsense. don't take it, waste your time elsewhere.

If you are thinking about taking a class from Sister Newell, DO IT! She is amazing, caring, insightful, kind, and inspiring. What she teaches is very applicable. This class is not meant to be hard. If you show up to class and do the tiny out of class assignments (literally no more than 15 min/week), you will get an A.

This is one of the best classes at BYU. Professor Newell is the sweetest teacher you'll ever have, and the class content is phenomenal. You learn all about professional etiquette, and the stuff I learned this semester actually helped me get an internship for next summer! She is truly invested in your future. Highly recommend this class.

Candilyn was probably the best professor who I've taken my entire time at BYU.  She is incredibly genuine, full of wonderful stories from her life, and gives plenty of opportunities for learning.  Her professional etiquette class was probably the most spiritual class I've been privileged to be a part of.

Sister Newell is a total sweetheart and has a ton of good experience to share. She is a very authentic, good soul and she sincerely believes what she teaches. She cries a lot as she shares stories. Her husband was an ambassador and mission president in Sweden, so it's basically pretty legit.
Such an amazing teacher! I my writing really improved with his class, he gives great feedback and wants his students to succeed.

I couldn't say anything bad about Dr. Sederholm if I tried. He is so funny and caring and really excellent with his students. Kind of reminds me of Remus Lupin but if he was played by Benedict Cumberbatch.

This class was writing heavy at the end, 8-10 page paper on Edgar Allan Poe.  I wish we started writing sooner to remove later stress. First part was focused on reading one or two short Poe stories and discussing them in class, as well as a chapter from Craft of Research, an excellent book on how to write. Classtime was slightly boring, but okay.

REVIEW IS ACTAULLY FOR HONORS 290R. 
Loved loved loved this class. Very discussion based, thought provoking, and interesting. Midterm was 25%, and final was another 25% of overall grade. Excluding that, there were maybe 9 other assignments? Must do them all for an A, but to me it was worth it bc of how fun it was. You don't need to do the readings

The class is mainly discussions which are always good. He knows a lot and his lectures are always entertaining. He cares about the students and the material he is presenting. Would 100% take another class from him.

Dr. Sederholm is awesome. Incredibly personable and willing to help you stretch as a writer. Class discussions were always interesting and enlightening. Highly recommend if you want a professor that really cares about you and your education.

Professor Sederholm is one of my all-time favorite profs at BYU. He's SUPER knowledgeable & hilarious to boot. I've never had such a good experience in class. However, there are only a few grades (papers), and he's a tougher grader. But he definitely helps you write better & will always meet with you to workshop papers. 490R Horror seminar forever!

I don't think I've ever felt more respected and included in a class, and not as a student, but as a sentient human being. He makes everyone feel like their opinion matters and outside of class will talk to you for an hour in the hall about pop culture, movies, etc. He is a touch grader, but I learned more about writing in his class than any other.

Very arrogant. Thinks he is better than most professors; he said that to me. Gives little meaningful feedback on papers, and there are a lot of them. He is funny and interesting, but I would not take him again.

If you are OK with getting a C in your transcript then go ahead and take his class! I am a straight-A student and got a decent grade in his class, but it took blood, sweat and tears. Be prepared to work your tail off and still be frustrated at the final grade.

Truly a great teacher, a little hard on papers (avg. BC grades), great discussions if class is medium-small (which happens in upper level classes). So hilarious--goes on tangents *sometimes*. This particular class may become another very soon, so it'll change. So worth it if you want to learn how to THINK and write well.

I love Dr. Sederholm! One of my favorite professors at BYU. His class discussions are very interesting and you learn a lot. He grades tough on the writing but it's always fair and ultimately makes you a better writer. I would definitely recommend taking a class from him if you have the chance.

He is an excellent, truly interesting professor. It was a small class, and we'd sometimes get distracted from the subject matter, we had so much fun talking about interesting things. If you usually get A's on your college papers, expect a B on these papers. They were very, very hard papers for me personally, but I can't say they weren't fair.

Love Dr. Sederholm! He has great insights to everything. He is very caring and learns everyones names. He is always there to help and wants you to succeed. Seriously he is one of the best professors I've ever had, and have taken many classes with him and never regretted any. He's awesome.

Adored this class. Professor Sederholm is hilarious, the readings were incredibly interesting (though LONG, and and you had to be "into that kind of stuff"), papers weren't bad. Very good feedback on the actual essays. I've never had a teacher really READ my papers like him. Some didn't like his grading-mostly people used to being exceptional.

Professor Sederholm is FANTASTIC! I graduated more than 2 years ago and haven't been in his class for 4 years but still remember how much I enjoyed his lectures. Honestly, you can't go wrong with any of his classes- I took both Humanities 261 and 262 and loved both. Thank you for two great classes Dr Sederholm!!

Sederholm is an outstanding professor--his classes were discussion based, and always very interesting. I would recommend his classes because Sederholm stretches the way you think. The class wasn't too time consuming--I would recommend doing the readings though. 4 papers (very difficult to get A's on), a midterm, and a final. I got an A-.

He is a very nice guy, and it was a pretty easy class. Unfortunately, like most professors, he doesn't really read the papers. 4 papers required for class, and that's everything. Gives out B's by default. I suggest going and talking to him after the first paper so he knows you care and can award your grade accordingly.

Professor Sederholm is a wonderful teacher. Being a Humanities professor, he offers a completely different reading of the Book of Mormon, focusing more on themes than on details. It is very possible to achieve an A, as long as you pay attention to the themes mentioned in class. Love him!

Hands down the best teacher at BYU.  He's hilarious.  You'll find yourself quoting him to all your friends.  He not only made the subject interesting, but he taught it so that I can actually remember it two years later.  Worth every minute!

I LOVE THIS MAN. He is by far one of my top three favorite professors at BYU. His class lectures are awesome and he's a hoot. Essays were graded hard, but I've definitely improved my writing skills through his class. Take any class he teaches because he rocks.

While this class is not an easy A it is definitely worth it. Professor Sederholm makes the course extremely interesting and brings in relevent connections.  Best professor in the Humanities College and probably at BYU as well.
Here's to you Sederholm, fulfilling your lifelong dream.

Dr. Sederholm is hilarious! He cares about the student and endeavors to make them better writers. He has cookie days, sometimes brings action figures to class, says the most hilarious things, and he learned all of his students names. The class is mainly discussion over what you read. The tests are hard, but if you take good notes you should do well

Brother Sederholm is an awesome teacher for your BoM class. The format he uses is mostly discussion based, i.e. he comes to class and leads a discussion on a few chapters in the book of mormon. Assignments were few; there were only two papers a midterm and a final.

Super entertaining. He gives a fresh perspective to the Book of Mormon which is totally relate-able for students. The class is mostly discussion with a few papers. Grading is completely fair. A B paper gets a B. Finally.
Awesome

Dr. Sederholm is awesome. He is one of the funniest guys I have ever met. I don't really like Humanities, but I thought this class was good. He isn't an easy teacher, but not difficult. Just go to class, take good notes, and study hard for the tests. Writing is a big part of the class, so plan on spending time on that.
Sederholm makes his classes enjoyable.  I had no interest in the class however he helped make it very interesting!  He's a really funny and cool guy and he'll help you out whenever you need it.
By far one of my favorite professors at BYU.  Not an east class, but I learned so much, and appreciated the challenge and knew he really read all of my papers carefully and made me a better writer.

his class is basically discussion, with not much outside work. there is one paper. He helps you if you ask. For tests, its three essay questions (three times throughout the semester, including the final) If you listen in class, you will be fine. He isnt trying to trick ppl. he is SO nice and caring. TAKE FROM HIM!! He truely cares about students.

Dr Sederholm did a great job alternating between facilitated class discussion and lecturing.  The reading assignments were really manageable and his flexibility towards the syllabus was appreciated.  Great sense of humor.  Took actual interest in my writing and gave useful suggestions.

Sederholms class is very fun. He likes to discuss things a lot though.  So when you are in this class, there isn't much work, just talking about what you are reading and analyzing what it all means. he is very fun and a great teacher.
Sederholm is awesome! I have learned so much in this class and it feels like he knows everything! Its so great!

Sederholm was a BLAST! I took Hum 262 from him and simply LOVED the class. This semester I am taking Hum 261 and Book of Mormon (Rel 122) from him. He is a hilarious teacher and genuinely cares about his students. Just a note: he likes cookies and asks you to bring them to class.

I've taken Hum 261, 262, 350, and 420R and I plan on taking BoM from Dr. Sederholm.  That's how awesome I think he is.  Papers can be hard but he'll coach you through and you'll improve as a writer.  He cares that you learn, not memorize, and gets excited when it comes to his specialty, Gothic literature.  Don't miss lectures because he's hilarious
I've taken Hum 261, 262, 350, and 420R and I'm planning to take Rel A 122 from Dr. Sederholm.  That's how awesome I think he is.  He

Sederholm is seriously a great professor.  He is passionate about what he teaches, concerned for the welfare of his students, and aloof enough to keep you laughing at him despite the difficulty of his class.  Be prepared to re-evaluate how much you think you know, but if you work hard at your writing and analysis, you can do well in the class.

I loved Prof. Sederholm. He is hilarious. He really cares about his students and helps them in any way he can. He does grade somewhat hard on the essays and tests, but he is very fair. You always know what to expect on the tests because he tells you what to study. He gives plenty of essay options. Go to class though, because it is all discussion.

I love Pro. Sederholm. I have taken him for both 261 and 262, and loved it. Before his class I was a biology major and I have decided to change to Humanities.  He is a great professor, funny, helpful, and very intelligent. He addresses several topics considered taboo and discusses them very pc. Take this guy, he is great!
The papers are difficult but extremely valuable in working towards being a better writer.  The class is interesting and Dr. Sederholm is funny and very helpful.

The subject matter was somewhat difficult, but it was a good class.  Prof. Sederholm gives good feedback on papers.  You have to work hard to do well, and your writing skills will improve.  He's a funny guy too.

Dr. Sederholm is definitely one of my favorite professors at BYU. He's absolutely hilarious! We died laughing at least once every lecture. His papers and tests are tough, but he really forces you to reevaluate your writing and overall learning.

He is really one of the best professors I've ever had. I learned more in his class about life than any other class I've ever taken. He cares so much about his students, and he's just real with everyone. Totally his own person-super smart-but not out to prove himself to anybody. But, he's a TOUGH grader.  That's my only complaint. Otherwise, AMAZING

He likes to teach you to think.  He has an odd, but still funny sense of humor and has interesting discussions in class.  There's lots of required reading, which you might get away without doing, but then the test will have a question specifically about the one you didn't read... Very easy to get a B in this class, fairly tough to get an A.

great class, learned a TON, papers kind of tricky, sederholm's tough but fair in his grading.  he genuinely cares about his students. lots of reading, loved it when he would go off on a tangent about movies or something. kept us from falling asleep.  he also spent the first few minutes of class asking us how we were doing in the class and in life.

In both of classes be prepared to write 5 one to two page papers that are not too hard. There is also a final paper which is 3-5 pages. The tests are essay and as long as you go to class and write notes you'll have now problem, i didn't read much for either class and i was fine as long as i always paid attention in class. Sederholm is hilarious!

AWESOME guy. I got very sick for almost a month and he actually called me on the phone to make sure I got everything turned in. His tests are easy, his papers are hard, the journals help your grade a lot. Highly recommend - his lectures are the best. He is so funny and you learn so much about life in this class!

Sederholm is a super teacher. He is on stage most of the time--tells lots of jokes and stories, and in person he is extremely kind and helpful.  His papers are killer; very hard to get A's. But if you go talk to him it helps a TON. The tests are fine. Make sure you share your comments in class. That's what he tests on.
He is so funny and I learned and improved a lot on my writing.  He is a hard grader, but if you can get past that plaease take him.  I loved, loved his lectures!

He has a very good way of making class interesting, but is difficult.  He wants perfect writing, and is unable to effectively teach those who seek writing help.  Overall, he is a great guy to have a class from.  I never wanted to skip.

Sederholm is hilarious. I would take this class again just to go to his lectures. We get off topic a lot but we still learned a great deal about the topics. This was a great class. You have to be able to write well to do well in this class.
Lots of fun! Sederholm is a riot and I don't think we get through a whole class without laughing. :) Excellent teacher, but you have to work hard in his exams and papers.

When I took this it was online. It was very straightforward, nothing special. Just go through the lesson and do the labs. I would recommend getting a little ahead. The final project was a little rough and you need the TA's. They get busy so try to go in sooner rather than later.

The TAs are extremely helpful and ensure you get full credit on the homework. The final project is pretty cool, just be prepared to dedicate a solid 10-15+ hours to it. Overall a fantastic 1.5 credit class. I was glad I had some coding experience in other languages as I think it would have been a difficult adjustment learning online from scratch.
Professor Pendleton is SO helpful. She even called me to help me submit some of my assignments past the due date. She wants all of her students to succeed and really cares for us. BEST teacher ever!

I took this as a sprummer class & was more work than I thought necessary for 1 online class. I only heard from Pendleton in exam review videos which were helpful. The daily reading/quizzes can take 20min-1.5 hours. The material wasn't hard, but tests are 85% of the grade so you need 90s for an A. Daily labs for Qs, 2% bonus for practice quizzes

Professor Pendleton cares about her students and truly works with them to help them succeed. She sends weekly emails every Monday to detail what will be covered and due that week, responds to questions quickly and in very helpful ways, and explains concepts from the very beginning. If statistics is a challenging concept for you, take it from her!!

There is little to no interaction with Professor Pendleton. She is quick to answer emails, but is not always very helpful. The major pro of this class is the flexibility. You can watch the lectures and do homework as far in advance as you would like. One con is the tests are weighted super heavily.

The class was online so there wasn't much interaction with Dr. Pendleton, but the videos she showed were useful and the TA's were very helpful. If you haven't taken a coding class before then you will probably spend a lot of time on this class then a normal 1.5 credit class,but if you go to the TA's you can get a lot of help and the grading is fair

Carly Pendleton is a good lecturer, though we really only saw her face on the exam review videos. Her test prep documents, like glossaries, practice tests, and 100-slide review packets were helpful! You get to use formula sheet/table sheet on every test. The tests are all comprehensive. Challenging. I feel I am well-prepared for a research job.

This is an online class, so there was little interaction with Professor Pendleton. The course itself was pretty straightforward and there are lots of resources to help you succeed, if you need them. Learning is done by reading the book, taking graded quizzes, and watching review videos if needed. Definitely do-able, but you need to put in the work.

I took the online STAT 121 course. There are three 1 hour lectures per week (MWF) that require 2 quizzes after each. There are four tests throughout the semester. I personally think that the class is too harsh on the grading, and weighed heavily on the tests. I got a B on one test and A's on the other 3 and still couldn't get an A in the class.

Not much interaction with her since it's an online class, but honestly it's not that bad if you go to TA hours. They are the most helpful thing for this course! Reading the textbook and watching the videos helps a little, but GO TO TA HOURS! They grade the homework and are very helpful for the projects.

Pretty standard as far as online classes go. I probably could have gotten a better grade if I I had taken a face to face class, but it was worth it to have to spend minimal time on a GE. Her video test reviews were helpful, but other than that, you're mostly on your own.

While a useful class, the course should not be an entirely online format. TAs were not very accessible and would cancel office hours during critical points of the semester. Unless you already have extensive knowledge in R, this class will be terribly time consuming for only being 1.5 credits.

The online version of Stat 121 is such a good choice. Don't be worried to take this online class. Carly Pendleton organized this class so well. The concepts aren't extremely difficult, but the online instructors explain it so well. Great study guides. Lots of TA help if you want it. Definitely take this class.

AWFUL! She does not teach at all. You are give 6 videos and a textbook and expected to teach yourself 100%. Terrible and would not recommend. Good luck passing this course without spending hours more than you should dedicate to a 1.5 credit class. Worst class I've taken at BYU.

I took both Stat 121 and 123 with Carly Pendleton, both of which were online. Even though the class is online, she is very accessible and always responded to my emails. She is very helpful in her responses and teaches her online videos very clearly. Overall a great professor.

I took this class during the "sprummer" term online. It was surprisingly difficult for me at first, which was weird because I am a math person. The class is straight forward with three lessons per week. It was hard for me because they have multiple professors who teach the recored lessons. Carly is awesome when she does reviews though!

Professor Pendleton is a great choice for taking the intro to stats class. She explains everything very clearly. The class is fairly easy, especially if you just listen in class. Because the class is big, it is harder to interact with her one on one, but she is willing to help any who have need of help.
I had limited interaction with Sister Pendleton because this was an online class but she was helpful and responsive when I would send her an occasional email.
She is a good professor. Uses lots of PowerPoint, but she explains it pretty well. She was decent.

Intro level stats class, you can read the lecture slide included in the packet outside of class, but if you attend you can earn i-clicker extra credit. Attend the review sessions for the exams, do the weekly quizzes and you'll be fine.

Dr. Pendleton is not amazing, but is not terrible. she is about average.  I took her for her first year, so I am understanding.  She relies heavily on PPTs, and it was not hard to get distracted. She is very willing to help outside class and will walk you through everything.  I took AP stats in HS and still had to study, so be aware!
She was an awesome teacher. Class is super mandatory, but there is no required outside reading. You only have to read if you didn't understand something in class. She explains it super well.

I only used the textbook a handful of times. DON'T GET THE LECTURE NOTES- they are available digitally; a waste. In-class quizzes get you participation bonus points (2% to final grade). She wasn't too good- just read from the lecture slides we have anyways- only went for BP. Recitations may go over homework (yay) or just material not understood.
