Sis Pendleton is an okay prof. It's her first year so I cut her some slack, but I really struggled in her class. Some of the time she didn't even know what she was talking about, and the class had to correct her frequently. She also talks in a very monotone voice which makes it easy to fall asleep! I recommend taking stats from a different prof.

Don't know your grade all semester until transcripts submitted. Class is only a 2 min write up for attendance, she reads part of the book doesn't give her thoughts, peer review rest of class. Only gives feedback during 15 mins of review, doesn't take it home to think about more. Good details of grading expectations NOT given. Condescending tone.

Carol is very quirky and sarcastic, which may be off-putting to some people. But if you take the time to get to know her, she is so kind and really cares about your success in the publishing industry. And this is probably the easiest creative writing class you'll ever take. Just show up, participate, and write!

I've taken from Carol several times and not only is she one of my favorite teachers but she's become a good friend. Amazing writer, gives good, kind feedback. Sarcastic, funny, and laid back. Class requirements basically just the minimum to improving and becoming a better writer.

I admire Carol as a writer, but I was very frustrated with her class. She rarely explained assignments to my satisfaction and emailed me about every other week about perceived problems (mostly the fact that I had to leave a few minutes once every couple weeks for my job).

Carol is the best! She weeds out people at the beginning and seems kind of intense, but she really cares about her students and really cares about helping you write the best you can. If you want to be a better writer, take this class! She also knows TONS of people in the publishing world, so it's a great way to network!
Taught me everything I needed to know about writing. She's awesome. Tough, but still awesome.

I was excited to take from her, but I was disappointed. She's sarcastic and sassy when you have sincere questions. The work load is ridiculous. You had to read 12 different books in one semester! Her feedback is good when it's what she enjoys reading, if not too bad. To her, "this is the only class that matters so who cares if you fail the others?"

Carol is an incredible writer and I learned a lot from her. But her feedback drove me crazy. I was lucky to get more than one word on my blog posts. She also got super annoyed at us because we were a quieter class? Refuses to accept late work. You have to get critiqued by the class  4 times and post daily on a blog, so the workload isn't too bad.

The best class ever and the best teacher ever. She doesn't like fantasy or sci-fi so I was a little worried when took because thats all I wrote, but she converted me to literary fiction. Take her you won't regret it.

Carol is absolutely F A N T A S T I C. She is intelligent and she really cares about her students. She knows how to write. Her class was one of the best I have had on campus. I wish I could have a class from her every semester. She truly will do what she can to help you and to listen to you.

Carol is the greatest!! She's so helpful and informative. The class makes you write, but that's the whole point if you want to be a writer. My writing will forever be influenced by the writing gospel of Carol Lynch Williams. Carol not only is a wonderful teacher, but she also became a great friend.

Very fun and informative class. Carol's a published writer, herself, and that was very helpful for our constant class critiques. I really looked forward to class every week for the workshopping! Make sure to do your seldom homework, though... it ends up determining your grade in the end!

Don't let the bad reviews stop you from taking her class! Professor Clark is super kind and the class is super easy -- plus it's been two years and she has a different TA! You basically get 100% on everything as long as you turn it in on time. I liked her and would recommend her for Comms 304!

Professor Clark has good intentions & is kind, however, her TA & grading style ruined it for me. Our entire grade was based on a group project that we worked on throughout the semester. Despite our hard work we received a C with the only feedback being that the citations were incorrect. Lots of work, unclear rubric, & TA grades everything harshly.

Don't take this class. Not only did we spend  all semester on rudimentary COMMS101 principles, but the grading on the final was extremely unfair. The content of our essay was less important than citations having the proper indentation and the TA grades everything. Basically impossible to get an A despite the content being elementary.

Seems to be really kind but is such a frustrating professor. Her canvas courses are extremely disorganized, and there is a ridiculous amount of work. Grading is weirdly harsh considering there is super little direction for the assignment and rubric. Very heavy work load. She is so disorganized, would not recommend. Avoid if you can.

Exams are easy (open note, open book, essay format). She is good at reiterating what you need to know and gives you a handout with all the big ideas and required knowledge. Homework I would say can be a heavier load, but if you're good at skimming it won't take you very long. She is pretty disorganized, but very kind.

The class was easy but it was disorganized and there was a lot of homework. There was a time I got points taken off for "not writing enough" when I wrote exactly what the rubric required; when I emailed the TA about it, I got no response back, and then the rubric requirement changed after to fit the "not writing enough." I thought that was unfair.

A lot of unnecessary busy work. We had at least 3 heavy assignments per week that I felt never truly benefited me. I felt like I was just doing the assignments so I could check them off and move on to other work.

I like Prof. Clark as a person but this class was a little disorganized. It's hybrid so we meet once a week and the online portion is extremely work-heavy. Basically just go to class and do the projects, the final is open-book and homework throughout the semester preps you for it pretty well. She's not a tough grader but her TA was kinda vindictive
Incredible director and person! Could not recommend more to anyone interested to try out for Vocal Point and appreciate the caliber that this man has brought our group to.

Undoubtedly one of the best professors I've had at BYU. I didn't expect to love the class, but Dr. Deccio made class fun, approachable, and inspirational. Gets to know his students by name and actively learns about their lives. Doesn't overload you with content either, all of the assignments and projects felt relevant and never excessive.

Amazing Professor. 460 was tough, but he made it worth it. He writes everything on the board so it's easy to follow along with notes. 2 midterms and a final. Every week there is a homework or lab due. Labs build on each other and homework is relevant. attendance is not mandatory but it's critical for understanding the concepts and I'd recommend

Deccio is an amazing guy who wants you to really understand the concepts of the class. He also makes lectures fun and has some good one liners if you pay attention. Don't procrastinate, especially on the labs as those are the real time consumer. The lectures I think are very helpful and key to understanding the content.

This class was a little harder than I expected but not impossible. I came here to say what others are already saying - he is a gifted and caring teacher and you will learn a lot of really valuable things in this class. This was my favorite CS experience at BYU as a whole.

Great lectures, efficient teaching, cool projects. One of my favorite professors so far. He really knows his stuff! I wish I could take more classes from him. He makes challenging concepts feel more approachable and is an excellent teacher.

Dr. Deccio is one of the gems of the CS department. Labs build on each other and he managed to make Internet protocols interesting in lecture. He's also a great choice for 324 and is very available outside of class. Definitely take a class from him if you can.
Best Professor

Honestly, probably my favorite teacher. The pinnacle of BYU professors, especially in the CS department. He is a kind person and really cares about his students. He lectures well and adjusts his assignments to teach you what you need to know without being any more difficult than they need to be. His exams are easy if you do the assignments.

My favorite CS professor at BYU. Fantastic professor and just great guy in general. Labs can be tricky but if you get a study group and get TA help early they are completely doable. I would highly recommend taking CS324 from him, he's a really clear teacher and really cares about each student.

Professor Deccio is amazing! He does a fantastic job teaching difficult material. Some of the labs were a little challenging but very doable with the time given and TA help. I learned a ton from both the labs and his lectures. He really cares about is students and their success. I would absolutely take another class from him!

I have never written a review on this site, but I'm doing it for the first time for Dr. Deccio. His class was just that good. Honestly the greatest professor I've probably had in my entire college experience so far.

Definitely my favorite CS prof and tied for 2nd favorite overall at BYU. The class is very technical and complex but he is a phenomenal teacher and person, very caring and thoughtful, and I loved this class. Assignments are well-structured, very clear, and often genuinely fun. Midterms all multiple choice & most lenient late policy I've ever had.

Dr. Deccio is the best professor I've ever had. He takes what could be very dry topics and makes them accessible and interesting. The class is definitely tough, but he is very fair in his policies and always supportive of the students. This is the only review I've ever written on this site, and Dr. Deccio definitely deserves it.

Dr Deccio was an amazing professor! The material in 324 is a bit boring and quite hard at times. My biggest frustrations with the class were with the material not with the professor. He is super nice and makes an effort to memorize everyone's names as fast as he can and remembers little facts about all his students. Really nice professor!

I LOVED Dr. Deccio. I would absolutely take his class again. His class was so incredibly hard, and I thought a lot of the material didn't match up well. The homework, tests, and lectures were great together, but the labs didn't seem to relate. I loved his classes though, and he made the tough material interesting.

Favorite prof I've had at BYU. Systems programming can be tough but Deccio does everything he can to help students succeed. VERY generous late policy which is nice for students like me that are always behind :) Lectures are helpful, and the homework is designed in a way that actually helps you learn the material.

This was the best CS class I have ever taken. Dr. Deccio is the most caring and helpful professor I have ever had. The content is tricky, but the TAs/professor are helpful and Dr. Deccio is merciful. I was actually excited to do my homework in this class. Tests were all multiple choice and we could bring in a page of notes.

What a guy. He created a network simulator. It's a tough class for sure, but WOW you really learn a ton about how networks work. He's done research in this area, so he's super knowledgeable, but he is good at making concepts digestible. This is my second class from him, and I'd take a third if I had time in school left.

Deccio is a solid option for 324. His lectures for the most part are pretty straight forward, and he provides a lot of example code. The labs are VERY time consuming. one took me 30 hours and I still ended up with a 0 on it. Exams are not terrible, if you study, and pay attention in class you can get by, if not you will likely end up with a C.

Dr Deccio explains concepts really well, and he provides plenty of example code to learn from. Class time is well spent. The homework is actually useful, not busy work. Overall the class is difficult but very doable.

I LOVE deccio. Seriously such a good professor. He always does little thoughts at the beginning of class that are probably the best part of the lecture. Very good at explaining confusing topics and I felt very prepared for every test. Labs are a little challenging because you have to read through his code, but there is a generous late policy.

You will learn a ton in class, both about life lessons and computer science. Professor Deccio actually teaches the material instead of assuming you already know it like some other professors. One of the teachers I have learned the most from.

Dr. Decio is not a very good teacher and his lectures are hard to understand. The way he teaches CS 324 makes the class unnecessarily hard and I know for a fact that many of my friends did not pass. His tests are especially bad with lots of gotcha questions and many students complained.
Explains the concepts well. Respectful and fair grader.

Dr. Deccio cares a lot about his students. He took the time to learn everyone's name and he had every students interest in mind. His lectures were a little scattered sometimes, but I feel like I was able to learn the material I needed to. The labs were difficult but very doable.

This class is super rough. However, Dr. Deccio did a fantastic job making what should be very dry/unapproachable material be accessible. My biggest problems were with the class and C itself, not with Dr. Deccio. Very accessible, addresses students' questions directly on Slack/LearningSuite. Amazing professor for a dreadful class.

I felt professor Deccio was very approachable and helpful. He made the class interesting and made some good jokes. I would take him again. The first day he seemed a little quieter than other teachers, but after that he was the best teacher ever! Cool guy! He had devotionals in class that were very pertinent to our lives, not just computer science.
He thinks he can receive inspiration for others and he is very unkind and mean. It was not a good class. The class was awkward. You won't remain anonymous.
Casey was great. This class helped me cope with the stress of college life simply because it was so uplifting. Take it, you won't be sorry.

BEST. CLASS. EVER. Honestly changed my entire outlook on life, the professor is amazingly talented and will come to class the first day knowing your name and where you're from. He doesn't care about grades, only learning. Learning through Service :) I would take this every semester if I could.
This class is one that will impact you for life--not just till next semester. The principles are extremely important and so important. Casey does a great job with them helping you grasp them as well.

I loved this class! It really inspired me to want to live a service-filled life, and the professor really cares about all of his students. The class is filled with the best people and the material that is covered in the class is very inspiring and fulfilling. DEFINITELY take this class before leaving BYU!You will make life long friends and love it!
Excellent class, Excellent teacher. If any class should be required at BYU, this is it!

I absolutely loved this class. In fact, this is my second time taking it. Casey is an incredible professor who really cares about the students and their insights. Class is based mostly on discussion about the assigned articles and other topics focused on service. He does a great job at getting students to view service from new perspectives

Casey is amazing. He cares about each student and knows their names. He really practices what he teaches and it would be tough to leave this class not completely changed or inspired. This class has completely changed my entire outlook on service and I think it has really helped me learn to serve better.Take this class! Take it 2 or 3 or 4 times!!

Casey is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He is so caring and such a great leader. You really can learn so much from just attending class. I'm taking another class from him next semester and I'm so excited. Take a class from him!

Casey Peterson is awesome! He truly cares about the individual and he wants only the success of every student. Service and Learning will teach you lifelong service. Go into the class for the right reasons, and you will get so much out of it.
Casey is my hero. His class is freaking amazing and every person who goes to BYU should have to take it to graduate.

Peterson is the best. Seriously probably my favorite class I've taken at BYU. So easy and enjoyable. Just go to class, not only is that what your grade is based on, but it's a great class anyway. Take this class from Peterson!

Before I took this class I thought service was helping people. However after this course I realized that service is organized and, if done with those who are being served in mind, can be high impact and scalable. I can honestly say that one year later I am still exercising principles I learned in this course. Bottom line: Register NOW

Fantastic! This class caused me to reevaluate and really attempt to define my philosophy of service. The readings for class were a mix of gospel and intellectual articles. Class discussions were fantastic, thought provoking, and always enjoyable. Casey leads well and is so kind. He had already memorized everyone's name the very first day of class.

Casey does a great job cementing the importance of service into students' minds. A range of philosophies about service added depth to my understanding of service. The workload is appropriate for a one credit class. If you complete the assignments you will get a good grade, but even more importantly the assignments increase your desires to serve.
Professor Peterson is awesome.  His classes were easily understood and well explained.  The best part was that all of the material was applicable in real life.  I highly recommend him.

She's the best! Really cares about you learning and retaining important info. The class got easier as the semester went on. The workload was a lot for most of the semester. It is structured similarly to financial in the Core. Fun class!

Budd knows how to teach. This class is hard but Budd is very good at explaining difficult concepts. Just don't ask questions in class because she is scary. If you have questions talk to your group. There is also a pretty big curve at the end so don't worry about getting 70-80 percent on tests.

Professor Budd is super caring! She has health condition but she still keep on going and try to help us to succeed. She explains things well and is passionate about her job .Intermediate Accounting is hard so make sure you go to class. She is sometimes direct but spiritually inspiring. I think she did her best.

Professor Budd explains things well and is passionate about accounting. Out of all the Junior Core classes, this one was by far the most engaging and time well spent in the classroom. The class is difficult and exams are pretty hard so make sure you go to class. She can be passive aggressive sometimes though.

A lot of people in my class disliked Professor Budd and I don't get why. She creates a fun class atmosphere and is very cheery. She sometimes struggles to answer questions and explain challenging concepts. Overall, just don't take what she says too personally and you'll be fine.
*I took ACC 409 from her.

Prof Budd is my least favorite professor I've ever had. She is passive aggressive, judgemental, and even made a girl in my class cry. I took two classes from her, and I hope I never have to see her again. Seriously diminished my experience in the junior core.

Professor Budd is awesome! Financial Accounting is a tricky class, but she explains the concepts very well and makes the class so much fun. I always looked forward to class and learning new material, she is a great teacher and very kind!

everyone says she's so amazing, but she was the worst professor in the jr core imo. she never answered my questions, would never explain anything personally, and i just had the worst time in class cause I was so lost. had to go to other professors to ask for help.

Overall, the class was very insightful. However, Prof Budd oftentimes had trouble answering our questions and teaching in a way that was easily understood by all students. There are things covered in class that aren't in the reading, so go to class! The class is very rigorous, but the curve helps a ton. Do well on tests and you'll be okay.

This class wasn't that hard imo, it just builds off of the hard work done in ACC 200. Some of the homeworks were a bit long, but overall it was very doable. She isn't the top tier at having fun lectures, but despite that she made class time valuable, as she taught concepts very clearly, solidifying them, and engaged you with those around you

Professor Budd is an amazing professor. Please believe everything about the course. It is incredibly difficult at times, but she does her best to make sure that students understand the material and actually cares about the success of each student. The class is difficult, but Professor Budd makes the class more bearable.

She wouldn't answer a single question I asked, but she would answer everyone else's questions. None of the answers she gave were that good though either. She definitely chooses people she likes better than others too and it's obvious

While I did well in the class, it was NOT because of her. She was nearly useless in the classroom.

I liked prof Budd! I hated the textbook and the layout of the class. It was way more unorganized than acc 200 and for $200 the textbook sucked. Just be prepared to do a lot of studying for the test and you'll do great! There's also a curve on the class that was really helpful. Professor Budd is a great person and you can tell she loves her students
She is so dang awesome. I would take every accounting class ever from her.

Prof Budd really cares about her students, and she makes that very clear. The reading and quiz are always due 2 days before class, so come prepared, and her teaching will help things click for you. Always shares a spiritual thought at the start of class and is so approachable. This class was hard, but she teaches it well.

Prof Budd is amazing! She knows what she's talking about, teaches in understandable ways, cares about her students, and is willing to answer questions. The class itself can be intensive and the tests are key, but study hard and you'll be fine. If you are ever worried, just reach out and she'll be more than happy to help. She wants you to succeed.

She is an incredible teacher who is extremely invested in her students. She gives you her cell number to text with questions you have at any time! ACC404 is probably the hardest class in the Jr. Core, not because she makes it that way, but because of the complexity of the topics covered (consolidations, derivatives, deferred taxes, etc.) good luck!

Prof Budd is honestly the best in the jr core. She teaches in a way that everyone feels welcome and valued. She is extremely good at explaining the hard material in ways we can understand it. 403 is your typical accounting class, and it got super hard during the last few units. 100% recommend prof budd (too bad you can't choose in the jr core)

Professor Budd is great. ACC 404 has a lot of complicated material, but if there's anyone who could get you to understand it, she probably could. Focus on being able to do problems, not memorizing, and you'll do alright.

Professor Budd is great at keeping a good balance between teaching and caring for her students. She is very animated and it is easy to like whatever topic she is teaching about. You know she loves accounting!
Prof. Budd is great. She is super energetic and does her best to make a difficult subject understandable.

Acc 200 is a difficult class, but Professor Budd is amazing!  I thought it was incredible to see how she taught how principals of accounting truly are applicable to all of our lives- business major or not!  Plus, I felt like she was a pretty talented teacher.  I was able to understand hard concepts when she taught!  She is great!!!!!

This is the best professor at BYU I've had! I loved every single lecture I went to. I never felt like skipping class. I highly recommend taking ACC 200 from her! You will go to class only like once a week and the rest of your time will be spent watching a super helpful software. I loved the class, but it's not for everyone.

Professor Budd is one of the best professors I have ever had at BYU. She's helpful, caring, clear, concise, and very entertaining. I loved taking ACC 200 from her and she's even almost convinced me to change my major to accounting.
She is a good teacher that really knows the material. This class is no joke though, expect a TON of work!!!!!!!
Cassy is an awesome professor, she explains tough topics in probably some of the most easy to understand language

I took this spring term and Professor Budd was amazing. She makes herself very accessible and is super approachable- even held a yoga session in her backyard for our class! The tests are really tough. I recommend watching every minute of software and doing every practice problem. I started doing really well when I went to the lab to do homework.

I took this class during the Spring, which was hard, but doable. Proff Budd is amazing and super helpful! She explains well.  I would consider myself a non-accounting brain student. I spent many hours watching the software, which was very well done. You will love Norm! I bombed the final, tests are hard. But if you use your resources it works out.

Very impressed with the class.  Grading is very logical and clear cut.  Pretty technical and difficult subject, but the online textbook with Norm is phenomenal.  Homework takes a while and requires a lot of attention, but practice makes perfect.  Tests are tricky (MC) - attention to details is essential!  Learned a ton - Sis. Budd is really good.

Prof Budd is awesome. Her lessons definitely clarify the software and if you still have questions, she is totally there for you during office hours. My best advice is to listen when they say to use the accounting lab. It wasn't until I started watching the software and doing homework in the lab that I really understood the material. Stay current!
tough class but very worth it for any major. stay on top of things cause they go by real fast

Gifted orator. Can come across as stern in class, but outside of class she is very bubbly, friendly, and helpful. ACC 310's study questions and tests are much harder than ACC 200. Put in the time, ask lots of questions, and see Prof. Budd for help. Study for tests individually and also in groups. Quizzes in ACC 310 are really hard!

Professor Budd does a great job at providing clear guidelines for daily course work. Her lectures are clear and consist of good examples with plenty of case studies that are fun and interesting. Complete your work on time because there is no late work accepted without being docked points. She is very helpful if you go to her office.

This class is tough, but that is because there is a lot of detail that you are required to know and understand for accounting. Prof. Budd does a GREAT job explaining things and is very approachable. The tests are hard and there is a lot of homework, get as many points on homework and quizzes as possible and don't fall behind and you should do well.

Prof. Budd is an amazing teacher. The class is not easy by any means. It is meant to be a tough class. She clarifies everything and she is super willing to work with you. Her class is interesting and she makes the topics fun. I loved the class.

This class is NOT EASY. Because so many students think they want to go into accounting, this class is used to weed out students who aren't meant for the junior core. However, professor Budd is as good of a professor as you can get. She's great, and I have no complaints about her whatsoever.

Incredible teacher. Explained concepts more clearly than text reading. three online mini quizzes each week allows you to always have accounting concepts fresh on your mind. She is very outgoing and engaging.

Professor Budd is quality. The class was very demanding and difficult but not impossible. The textbook was one of the worst I have ever had and yet was very expensive. All that aside however, professor Budd was very helpful and effective.

Professor Budd was the only teacher for ACC 310 when I took it. It's a hard class; she makes up for it with her awesome-ness. She makes herself very available to help us and makes it very clear that she wants us to be happy and do the best we can. You'll work a lot, but she makes going to class fun!

Prof. Budd is awesome! She trully cares about her students. The class is intended to b challenging and requires you to take time out of everyday to study for your class. But if you like Accounting this class is for you!

Not good at time management.  She'd rush the last half of the powerpoints which usually were the harder part of each subject we were learning, leaving you to learn it on your own.  She'd spend too much time answering unnecessary questions.
Professor Budd helped me create an extremely enjoyable learning experience. I highly recommend her for diligent students.

What a great professor! She really cares about her students and is always checking to see if we understand what is going on or have any questions. She really does want everyone to succeed. Budd can be kind of intimidating to go talk to, but she's nice and helpful. The class is really organized, which helps in doing well!
Professor Budd rocks! The class itself is extremely hard and time consuming but Professor Budd does a lot to help students. A+++++

Most challenging class I have taken so far. The textbook is mediocre and the material seemed unorganized, but that's the department's problem. Prof Budd is awesome. She has a fun and engaging personality and does all she can to help students understand. Don't worry if you do poorly on the tests, I don't think anyone gets below a C in the end.
Actually cares if her students are doing well and learning the material. Keeps things fun and brings a big-picture perspective to the material. Awesome teacher!

This class will be hard no matter who you take it from..all the teachers will teach the same material. Budd is extremely helpul, and teaches as clearly as she can. She makes things interesting and I really enjoyed the class. Material is hard, tests are harder

Professor Budd is an exceptional teacher. She is very patient with students, much more patient than I would be with dumb questions. She explains difficult concepts very clearly and tries to make the class interesting. Highly recommended
I felt she explained abstract concepts quite clearly and used real-world examples to clarify principles.

I avoided Professor Budd for audit mainly because of negative comments on this site about her but now regret it.  I had Financial Accounting from her.  The subject matter is very difficult, but Prof Budd did a great job at teaching difficult concepts with clarity.  She also seemed to truly care about helping her students succeed. Highly recommended
She did a great job at teaching a very tough subject. She worked well with her students. She is willing to help however she can.

Professor Budd is one of my favorite teachers at BYU. The class was hard, but if you are going to do accounting at BYU, you have to take it and I would very much suggest you take it from her if you can get into her section. I also had her for Audit (fall semester), and would say the same thing for that class.

Explained concepts in a way that students understood.  Always made herself available to help any students who had questions.  Really cared about her students and their education, both in and out of class.  Highly recommend this professor.

Great class! Hard, but fair with Prof Budd. Great job at explaining hard concepts, and willing to help you whenever you need it. She does tell a lot of personal stories, but I found them all helpful. They all aided in teaching her point, or strengthening testimonies. You would not like them if you don't want to learn or don't want a testimony...

This class is shouldn't be tough but was. I thought the material was never taught clearly. Class time was a joke, you listen to Budd's personal stories and kids' dumb questions. It wasn't clearly outlined. I disliked constantly doing homework without a lecture. The effectiveness of the teacher was close to a independent study course. not fulfilling

Audit is hard, Cassy is a GREAT teacher, her sense of humor helps, she shows sincere concern, she will try to explain until you get it, always fun class. Don't let the bad comments persuade you to skip such a great teacher!

She was hard because the class was hard.  But if you show that you are paying attention and interested she is very helpful.  She wants every student to do well and will help you on an individually if you need it.

Do not take her class!! VERY condescending. NO People skills , even less tact. And she always talks about how much harder it is being a girl, and how she has to work harder and feels people wont take her seriously because she is a woman. GIVE ME A BRAEK!
Very good at explaining difficult concepts.  She also has a genuine concern for her students and that they truly understand the material.  A very good professor.

Just not very fun. I swore I was having flashbacks to the Jr Core, which sucked. We had quizzes and homework to turn in, in the last semester of the Macc. I don't doubt her intentions, but it was by far my worst class of last semester. I know there aren't many options, but try to avoid her if you can.
Condescending. Will dock your grade if she happens to think you're are unethical, regardless of whether or not that is true.

I took audit from Professor Budd. I find it hard to believe that people found professor Budd condescending. She is one of the most caring teachers I've ever met. She is really good at explaining audit concepts as well. She really cares about her students (which you hear a lot and doesn't really persuade me to take a teacher). She's awesome.

I don't know what all the negative comments are about her.  I wasn't a fan of the subject matter, but I think she is genuinely interested in helping the students to understand it.  She wants to sit down and review the assignments together to help students understand on a one-on-one basis.  I wasn't a fan of the class, but did appreciate Prof Budd.
Don't take from her!! She gives quizes before she teaches the material.  Lost her temper several times with the class.  Overall just a negative experience...
A wonderful teacher.  She is kind (most of the time) and does her best to uplift her students in many ways, much more than just academically.  Highly recommended.
Condescending

Don't take from her!  She gives assigned readings, asks for homework, then goes over homework and quizes and then the cycle begins again!  No teaching involved.  She is smug and rude in her communication with students.  The book weighs 500 lbs and is poorly written.  I hope and pray that Norm will make another set of CD's cause this lady is a joke.

She really cares and really goes out of her way to try to explain stuff so everyone gets it, which is not something that always happens in accounting. She's also pretty darn funny for a middle aged woman, and her class is FAR more enjoyable than the other junior core classes.
She is a fun teacher and really friendly with all the students. She makes auditing as interesting as it can be in a classroom setting and she has a lot of experience with auditing.

SOOOO hard. I managed a B+ but thought I was earning a C-. It's really time consuming, there are in class quizes alot and online homework stuff. The exams are pretty rough too. She's smart and clear and wants to help and I really respect her, but the class consumed my life. Our whole class was in over our heads.
Very engaging Prof.

Honestly not a bad class! I hated it at first, but as the class went on the topics were interesting and it wasn't hard to get a good grade. The TAs are so so helpful and respond so quickly to any concerns. They will also check your essay and make sure it fits the rubric. Study guides provided for both the midterm and final which was awesome.
The TA test reviews are super helpful!! The material is really boring, even though the subject is interesting. Pretty easy to get an A though!

This professor genuinely wants her students to succeed and truly understand the material. Very understanding about extensions because of medical or family problems. There's a lot of subject matter covered, but she posts so many study guides and live review sessions that the tests weren't bad at all. Absolutely loved the TAs in this course as well

I was surprised by how much I enjoyed this class. I loved the content and learned so much. A few papers, each with a very clear rubric. Follow the rubric and it's easy to get a 100%. A few extra credit opportunities. 2 closed-note exams, with a detailed study guide provided. Some small 10-minute assignments each week. Very manageable!

Class was relatively interesting for a GE, you could normally finish the week's assignments in a few hours. Check out the textbook from the library, but you can get by without doing the readings. Most of the grading is by TAs and reach out early if you want help with assignments. 4 papers that kinda sneak up on you, closed book midterm and final.

I really enjoyed taking this class from Lundell! It was very straight forward, and the assignments and readings were very easy. There are 5 big papers you write throughout the semester- if you send it to your TA they will tell you things to fix, and then you'll get a good grade. Attend the TA reviews- helpful for quizzes and exams!!! easy class !!

Because it's an online class, you will never interact with her in person. However, she is very accessible and responsive to emails and is more than happy to meet with you if needed. The course is very straight forward and easy if you just follow the rubrics and outlines. They focus more on formatting than actual content, but that makes it easy.

A very good class. I am always hesitant to take online classes since they can teach you nothing sometimes, but I actually felt like I learned a ton in this class. It was very clear what was expected and what you needed to do each week. Loved this clas.

She was an ok teacher, rarely heard from her but she desperately needs to upgrade the instructions for most of her assignments. They're outdated and extremely confusing in most parts. Other than that the content was okay but lots of assignments and papers throughout the semester.

The amount of reading Lundell gives is out of control and is repetitive, she could condense the amount of reading- mid-week discussion/comments, reflection paper (she says one or the other, but it's both many weeks), and a weekly quiz. then 3 paper, mid-term, and a final. This is a three-credit class with about a five-credit workload. AVOID CLASS!

There was no substantial interaction with the professor, just with TAs. I reviewed the midterm with my TA and she said multiple questions would probably be removed since they were confusing. Make sure to always check the rubric for your papers, and DEFINITELY write your paper a couple days early so you can submit it to the TA for review.

The Professor was nice but this class was really difficult. Go to all the exam study sessions with the TA's. They give you everything that will be on the test. But also study the study guides. If you put in the work, you can get an A.

This class is definitely an easy A if you just follow the instructions and work with the TAs. The TAs provide super helpful reviews for the exams and will give you feedback on all your papers before you submit them! Dr. Lundell is very merciful and will make sure you succeed if you ask for help. I would 100% recommend this class to anyone!

This class should have been considered an independent study, not on-demand. The professor never introduced herself to us, and never taught us. I taught myself this material. This class also had so much reading and essays. This class was hard and it was harder because there was not a professor teaching.

This is my favorite class I have ever taken at BYU. Dr. Lundell is very caring and super willing to help you! The TAs are also super helpful and will read over your papers before submission so you can make corrections. They also host really helpful exam reviews. 4 papers but they're interesting topics and help you apply the concepts from class.

There's a lot of reading, but otherwise a really great SFL class! The TA's are great & will give you feedback on your paper if you send it to them early. Dr. Lundell & the TA's really set you up for success with this class.

I never really met Professor Lundell, but her TA's were INCREDIBLE! They were very approachable and would give really good feedback. If you write your paper like a day before, the TA's will go over it with you. The review sessions are also SUPER helpful. I really enjoyed this class!

Took this class as a freshman, non-SFL major. Easy A as long as you stay on top of your assignments. Read the rubrics for the papers! So many people miss easy points by forgetting something small like formatting, but all the information you need is readily available. ATTEND TA REVIEWS. They will help you SO much.

This class is extremely doable. Midterm and Final reviews and TA help for papers. There are 5 papers, but they are not particularly difficult to write, and the TAs will tell you what is expected and how the paper will be graded. If you do the reading, the quizzes aren't bad and they don't impact your grade too much. Great class, and not very hard!

I never actually saw or talked with her but her class was an easy A. Took online summer 2020 and she just had us read the lectures, respond to a discussion board, take an easy quiz for each lesson, and write 5 papers. As long as you do the reading its an easy A. Wrote lots of papers the day of and always got an A. TAs are super helpful for tests

The TAs grade so meticulously that its impossible to get a good grade. Assignments and lectures are thought provoking and interesting, so its a shame that papers and tests are so hard. She tests on very specific information from the readings, and there are at least 30 pages of reading from the textbook every night.
You will never get an A on a paper. The tests are easy, but the assignments will wreck you. Beware: THIS CLASS IS HARD.

The material is SUPER interesting and really applicable, but if you can take it from someone else, DO IT. The papers have nothing to do with the material and you often feel like you're writing about nothing. The TA's also grade harshly and an A is 94%. Basically impossible to get an A.

Do you want extremely broad rubrics and then get graded on extreme specifics? If so, this is your class! The grading is unclear, weekly 6 pages papers, and the TA's are unhelpful. The material has some interesting facts but does not make up for the number of papers there are. I'm a junior at BYU and this is the first negative review I have wrote.

No video lectures, all reading, so be prepared to read, read and read. Quizzes are tested off if you did the reading (very specific questions), exams are based on your knowledge of the material. Every point really counts towards the final grade, so make each count. Spent about 5 hours a week, besides studying for the exams. TA's are a huge help.
Definitely recommend this class to fill a general. Super interesting, useful information, set up well, great and understanding professor!

I took this class online during spring term and it was a breeze! Very little work, but when there is an assignment, DO IT, because 15 points is a lot when there is like nothing toward the final grade. Just a midterm and final, 100 points each. Two writing assignments. I wrote both the day off and got great scores!

Professor Pavia is super nice but I wouldn't recommend taking her class in the spring. It felt like her course was not really set up for spring. I personally did not like the way that she graded, she is trying out some new way of grading rather than how it is traditionally. It felt confusing and unnecessary. She also just has a lot of homework.
She's awesome and knows her stuff. Lots of reading but she did a good job of making it applicable and using the principles to actually improve our writing.

I had to drop the class on the first day because I had some trips planned (during the summer term) and she was unwilling to accommodate me. I understand it's summer term and I signed up for classes but even my anatomy professor during spring term was more lenient. Labor-based contract, guaranteed a B but have to do 12+ additional hours to get an A

Professor Pavia is a very caring and nice person. She did take time to meet with me outside of class. Her instructions were sometimes confusing and it felt like she explained the assignments in a more complicated way than they really were. I would say pay attention to the study terms, learn to apply them, and you'll be fine.

She is passionate about her field of study. Her lectures tend to be vague and confusing. She expected you to know and learn most of the concepts on your own, with a few slides in class to review what you read. She only had 3 major papers, which made each paper vital to your grade. she was not very good at getting back with emails or grading papers.

Proffesor Pavia is very interesting. She teaches you so much and you learn so much more than you ever thought you would. In some moments she is very specific but she also will work with you and emails back very fast for a professor. It was not a super easy class but super worth it because I learned a lot and feel like I am a WAY better writer now.

Decent English professor. She didn't explain everything well but the assignments were straight forward and very practical. The two final group projects can be a pain in you are in a less motivated group but still manageable. There is a twelve page paper but if you do plenty of research it's actually a really enlarging assignment.

I took Accelerated Portuguese with her (101 and 102 in the same semester) and she's a good teacher.  Her first language is Brazilian Portuguese and so you can trust her ability in the language.  However, she's super busy and doesn't have time to prepare a good class some of the time, however read the book and you'll be fine.  She grades easy too.

Suzy is a very kind person and knowledgeable about editing. However, she grades in a very harsh and completely arbitrary way that seems to expect students to read her mind and copy her editing style exactly. Despite being a very experienced editor, I left this class feeling worse about my editing skills and very discouraged as an editor.

Suzy is a wonderful teacher. She picks assignments and projects that will give you real experience with what you are learning. She is always available to give you feedback or check something before you submit it. There is a lot of reading and assignments, but it's all worth it. She's super accommodating if you have a need, and she's so sweet!
Suzy is awesome 10/10

Suzy is one of my absolute favorite professors. I have taken two classes from her, and am taking two more next semester. She is kind, caring, and so smart. She is so willing to help, and she truly wants her students to succeed. There is quite a bit of homework, but the majority of it was very helpful and educational. 10/10 would recommend.

430 is a really cool class with Suzy. You work with the same group all semester so she has you come up with a team charter and it makes group work so much better. She's a really fair grader with this class and there's no busy work, because you're putting all your effort into your book. She's really helpful when you're not sure how to edit something
Her class wasn't difficult but there was a lot of busy work and some of her lectures weren't very helpful.

I think Suzy is an excellent professor. She's so clear, organized, and intelligent. She's good at explaining difficult concepts, and is always prepared to spend as long as you need to help you understand. Not a super hard class, but you'll learn so much. There are a lot of assignments, but they're all fairly easy and are essential to your learning.

Shocked to see she doesn't have a higher score. She makes herself available and is so willing to help. Great lecturer and very knowledgeable. She cares deeply about her students and what she studies. I highly recommend taking her terrorism class, it is worthwhile and is something you can be proud of when you graduate.

Prof. Beesley is obviously very passionate about this class and the material she teaches. I did very few of the readings and still managed to get an A-. DO NOT procrastinate on the analysis paper!! The tests were somewhat difficult, but if you study, you'll do just fine. They're more about applying the concepts rather than just pure memorization.
I would give her a 6 if I could. Wonderful class.

I really like Professor Beesley. She does a good job of explaining course material, and I found it all very interesting. However, considering that POLI 170 is a probably just a GE credit for most people who take it, I would say that the workload is a little heavy. I enjoyed the class, but I am relieved to be finished with it. :)

Professor Beesley is great at breaking down difficult concepts in international politics. She helped me see things from a different perspective on multiple issues. Class-wise, grading on writing assignments is quite strict. There's an 8-page analysis paper and lots of reading. TA's were not helpful.

Ok so the class wasn't too bad, but let me tell you. The TAs absolutely suck in this class. Professor Beesley's taught the material well, but her TA's were the worst. No TA reviews, they took forever to grade assignments (like months on end), were not very helpful at all. I wish she had better Taste

She is super great at teaching and is very clear about what you need to do to pass the class. She is also really good at making the class interactive which is impressive with a class of like 120. I'll definitely be taking another class from her

This class was probably one of the best ones that I've taken in Poli Sci, and Dr. Beesley is the reason why. I think some students have a hard time in her classes because she will ALWAYS play the devil's advocate with your comments. This isn't meant to discourage you, but to make you truly think through your argument, which is awesome.

The best person to teach the terrorism class; she definitely will fight you a little bit on comments, but she does a really good job of solidifying your understanding of the theories you read in class. I learned so much from the class, and I loved the open-ended paper you write (can be coauthored). Good professor overall.

Funny professor. She uses inquisitive (flashcards where you can get a 100% grade every time if you do it for long enough). PLEASE start the final paper early. Readings ain't bad, but long. Not a work-heavy class, but the analysis paper is 8 pages long and due at the end of the semester.

Professor Beesley gave amazing lectures that were super interesting. I did not know anything about the topic before and I have considered majoring in this topic because of her class. There is a midterm and final exam, never any quizzes. Reading assignments are due each class. The long readings make the tests a lot easier if you do them.

Professor Beesley is extremely knowledgeable. However, she expects every person in her class to understand political science at her level, which, if you are not a political science major (like me!) makes it difficult and time-consuming to do well in her class. She was also extremely condescending many times I attempted to participate in class.
She is a great professor! She is so knowledgable and so humble. I really enjoyed her lectures because she saw things from both perspectives and was very thoughtful and always there to help.

The readings were long and heavy to someone without a background in Econ, but I learned more content from this class than any poli sci class at BYU. Dr Beasley is a great lecturer and gave clear study guides for the test. I came in with very little Econ backround but put plenty of time into the readings and got a fairly easy A

I LOVED professor beesley. She is super funny, caring, and very educated in her field. She is a great professor for POLI 170 and I hope to take more classes from her in the future. You need to buy the online program for homework, but you could probably get away with not doing the readings. The lectures are pretty similar.

I took POLI 170 with Professor Beesly and loved it. It's a lot of homework for a 100-level class, but the readings are interesting and her lectures are always engaging and make good connections to the readings and current events. The 7-page paper was tough and the TA's grade hard, but the midterm and final were pretty easy as long as you studied.

I love professor Beesley, she is amazing!! I went into the class knowing literally nothing about international relations, and now I am an IR major. I could listen to her talk about IR for hours, she gave amazing lectures. High expectations for a 100 class though, and TA's grade very harshly. Go to TA office hours as much as possible!!!

Prof. Beesley is easily one of my favorite Professors at BYU by a long shot. Very knowledgable while also being approachable. Her lectures were humorous yet informative, and her tests were very straightforward and easily passable if you do the readings and pay attention in class. Wish I could give her a 6.

Prof. Beesley is an articulate, knowledgeable woman with comprehensive and reasonable ideals about the world. Her classroom was open and involved frequent discussion, despite having a lecture everyday. I admire her very much.

Dr. Beesley is one of the most brilliant professors I've had. Her knowledge and passion for IR is inspiring. Each class is engaging, exciting, and insightful. Definitely one of the BEST IR professors at BYU

Professor Beesley is amazing. She is extremely knowledgeable and cares about her students. There are tons of readings for the class but you can skim to get the info for daily assignments. 5 KC lectures, monthly digital dialogue and final paper are required. There is one mid-term and a final, the mid-term wasn't that bad though.

LOVE Prof. Beesley! She's so kind, and pretty funny. Very accommodating, & will negotiate readings/exam parameters. She REALLY knows her stuff, I respect her so much. TONS of readings, but you can skim the txtbk if you do it alongside the InQuizitive assignments. Definitely do the other readings all the way tho. Very interactive, & I learned A LOT.

I really enjoyed Dr. Beesley's class. I felt like it was well organized and she really knew her stuff. It was a lot of work- a few papers + a poster, long readings, a few tests, but they were all really useful. She doesn't post her slides so you have to go to class to pass. I would absolutely take another class again.

Very interesting class, but Prof Beesley's lecture and slides were seriously disorganized. Everything I learned came from the textbook. You have to have a genuine love of the subject & a fair amount of prior political knowledge to succeed. TAs grade harshly. Daily LS quiz, midterm & final, 8-page paper, 5 KC lectures, participation grade.

This was my first poli sci class, but it helped me make the decision to major in poli sci. The lectures were super interesting and weren't the same as the reading (go to class). We had tons of fun playing games to understand the concepts. Major parts of our grade were our Major Paper, the 4 discussion board, 2 tests, and 5 Kennedy Center Lectures.

Dr. Beesley is an amazing professor. She's tough but explains things very well. Attendance is not only mandatory for points but because it helps a ton with comprehension. I tried super hard and still didn't get an A, however it was an amazing class and I'm so glad that I took it.

Tough class. Dr. Beesley does seem to care about her students, but theres little room for error if you want a good grade. Readings take hours, and the quizzes that go along with them are often ambiguous and tricky. The tests are thankfully relatively easy, but you need to put in a lot of work if you want good grades on the other assignments.

Professor Beesley is so smart and a great teacher! Class seemed liked way too much work for a 3 credit class, but was definitely worth it! Started off the semester knowing almost nothing about international politics and at the end could hold a good conversation with people about world events and political theories. Not an easy A, but passable.

Professor Beesely is a very smart professor, and well respected. For a 100 level class, there is lots of reading and homework that is graded VERY harshly by TA's, without clear criteria. I worked harder in this class than my 200 level classes and was pretty frustrated by the unclear criteria.

Decent class. There's a whole ton of outside readings that get obnoxious after a while, at least for Politics 170. This isn't my best subject, so I found it difficult. If you're going for the required global awareness credit, maybe consider taking a different class.

Beesley is a smart cookie, you can tell she knows this subject very well. However, her slides are very disorganized and EVERYTHING is graded harshly. There are readings (around 40 pg) with quizzes due every class, 300 word post due every month, a 8 pg paper, 5 outside lectures w/ 1 pg write-up, 1 midterm and final (written and multiple choice).

Understand, first off, that I am biased... because I love the study of world politics. This class was FASCINATING, and I think that anyone with a healthy curiosity about world would enjoy this class. Professor Beesley is wicked smart and gives excellent lectures.

This has been my least favorite class at BYU. Beesley requires lecture attendance but all you really need is the book. Her lectures are scattered, full of tangents, and the slides are practically unreadable. As many students have said below, her grading criteria is awful. I felt like I was playing "guess what's in my head" all semester.

I loved Professor Beesley. She literally knows the answer to every question you will ask her. Some people think shes a tough grader but I have loved having her and love her lectures. She makes them fascinating and engaging. She never makes you feel dumb or that your question is stupid, she tries to answer every question that there is.
Prof. Beesley grades SUPER hard with unclear grading criteria, so the homework is difficult, but she has very good lectures and is willing to speak with you outside of class.

Unclear grading criteria. Quiz questions are there to trip you up and confuse you. You can respond to her prompts exactly as they're asked and she'll still dock you because she wants a specific answer. Nothing is clear. Don't take it from Beesley.
Unbelievably awful for grading, not fair and ridiculously harsh. I cant believe how many good reviews she has. TAKE IF FROM ANYONE BUT HER. She is the reason I changed my major.

Great class! Readings can be dense (lots of economics) but she explains them well in class. Clear study guides so you can study effectively. Makes you do write ups on the readings but those help you remember them. I was struggling and she met with me outside of class, very willing to help you succeed.
Honestly my favorite class and loved her teaching style. She's super nice, reasonable, and interesting.

Professor Beesley is very knowledgable and is a great lecturer. I felt like the workload was reasonable, with only 1 paper, 1 midterm, 1 final, a few outside lectures, and daily reading assignments. I learned a lot without having to work myself to death.

This class is tough, buy you will learn a lot. There is a quiz before every class, and if you put the time into understanding the concepts tested in these quizzes you'll do well on the tests. It can be a lot of reading too, but doing it is worth it. Beesley is funny and makes the lectures interesting. If you put effort in, it will be worth it.

Professor Beesley is a nice lady who's pretty understanding. Her tests are pretty hard and she grades the papers extremely tough. Her lectures are long and if you actually want to get an A then you have to put at least two hours of work in every night. There's a lot of reading and daily assignments too.

Professor Beesley is an amazing teacher! She really understands the subject and is willing to work with you on the homework. There is a quiz on every section of reading so make sure to do those! The tests are fairly easy (some multiple choice questions and a couple of essays). Get started on the Analysis paper early on. I loved this class!

I love Prof Beesley. She was organized, accessible, and accommodating, and lectures were always interesting but also easy to follow. Exams were straight-forward. Some of the daily assignments are confusing and I didn't feel super prepared for the paper at the end of the semester, but I loved the class, learned a lot, and she was a big part of that!

Really struggled with this class. It was really tough yet incredibly interesting. There is a big paper that seemed really rushed at the end of the semester and the daily assignments were rough and graded really harshly. I came out of the tests really feeling like I understood things and had done well but my grade did not really reflect that.

As long as you stay on top of the reading and daily assignments, this class isn't too difficult. The paper due at the end of the semester is pretty challenging, but TAs are helpful with writing and editing it, and as long as you've done the work, you can get a good grade. The exams require lots of writing, but the multiple choice section isn't bad.

The best teacher I have had at BYU. Professor Beesley is smart and educated. She has a sense of humor. She is kind and understanding. She is supportive and will help you. She is hard - she expects you to work, but she won't leave you to fend for yourself if you ask for help! I hated politics and I took this class from her and now I like it.

I took this class just because it sounded interesting, but it's becoming my favorite class of the *whole* semester! Prof. Beesley is smart, organized, and flexible. She is honestly such a good teacher! There's a lot of reading and quizzes, but if you work hard, you can get a good grade!

Beesley was awesome! A lot of reading, but that's normal for a political science class. TAs were inaccessible, but Beesley was very willing to discuss my paper in office hours.  Really intelligent professor, really interesting class! Would definitely take again.
good lectures, do the reading and then listen to the lectures and you will do fine. The 8 page paper is tough but she is supportive and helps you out, if you seek Prof Beesley out.

Dr. Beesley means well, I don't think her intention is to fail students but she is extremely off the mark. The course  was so unorganized. I finished with a B+ but that was only because a lot of hard, hard work. Her TAs do all of the grading, they're always late and her questions on homeworks and tests make no sense whatsoever.

The class was challenging but so worth it. I was always impressed by how responsive Dr. Beesley was to her students- she really cares about them. You get the grade you work for, it's not going to be handed to you, but an A is totally possible. The readings took about 2 hours for each class period but I learned so much, making the final pretty easy.

Just got out of a final that took 4.5 hours of my life. She doesn't help you get prepared. Try and avoid her class at all costs. Very hard to work with. I love the subject but she just makes it harder.

Dr. Beesley means well, but this class is very disorganized and based on readings that are often difficult to access and long. I was often confused on what she expected out of assignments, particularly with the 8 page analysis paper due at the end of the semester. Overall, I would recommend taking this course from someone else.

I don't mind the readings. The confusing part is knowing what she wants us to read. She has a syllabus that we can pull up to see what she wants us to read. but sometimes the readings don't pull up on the internet. Her slides are not helpful. Very disorganized. Its a very lecture based class. She doesn't take roll. Overall you don't learn...

Prof. Beesley is such a helpful teacher! I've taken her for both POLI 170 and 450 (her capstone research seminar) and I've been so impressed with how she works to help guarantee student success. Her lectures are very interesting, and you can tell that she really knows what she is talking about. On top of all that, she has a great sense of humor!

Professor Beesley is an amazing teacher. I learned a lot in this class. The down side is that there is A LOT to read. Besides the book, she assigns articles to read and answer questions about for every class. There's a 5 page paper at the end of the semester, but she's willing to help you out with it.

Never tested on memorization of content. Just reading guides and personal reflections. This class was educational without being overbearing. Dr. Lay is very kind and I highly recommend taking a class from her. she is so reasonable.

Professor Langford is amazing! She is passionate about the material she teaches. She encourages students to think through new situations and apply concepts to real-world teaching. The workload isn't bad and mainly consists of discussions and conversations about the material. I learned a lot from the course and enjoyed the class.

I took ELED 310 from here not TELL 450. This was the most boring class I have ever taken. It is 3 hours which needs to be changed as well, but she talks about the same thing every time and makes no sense. She is really kind and an easy grader but I retained nothing from this class. Take from another teacher if you want to get anything out of it.

(EL ED 310)
Nice person, just not very organized. Classes were long and she often just read off of the slides. She NEVER responded to emails. If I missed a class, I emailed her to see what I could do to make up for it, and never heard anything back. Lost quite a few points from that. If she had responded and worked with me, I would've gotten an A.

I took ElEd 310 from her. While she is nice, I don't think she should teach this class. The class itself is way too long, and she usually just talks the whole time. It's so boring, and half the time she pauses for weird amounts of time. Never seems like she knows what she's teaching about beforehand. The exit tickets are pointless and way too hard.

I took SC ED 353 from her, it just wasn't an option to select on here. Very sweet and caring. You could tell how much she loves education and has a lot of good ideas about how to create a multicultural classroom. Class is easy and all about thinking and growing, not grades. I had a hard time understanding her Canvas page and she was scatterbrained.

Professor Lay is a sweetheart. She is a little scatter-brained and her lectures aren't super engaging, but the class revolves around reading and group projects. It was manageable and a small class. I learned a lot from her application to our classroom sections of projects.

Dr Lay is a kind person and was helpful when I asked for it, but that's where my praise for her stops. Her instructions are unclear, she never completes her thoughts so you never know what she's talking about, and it's basically all group projects and reading. She doesn't even really teach. Take it from someone else if you wanna get something out.

There wasn't a lot of homework and the workload was easy. You do a lot of work in groups and there is a lot of discussion in this class. I feel like I learned a lot but the classes were 3 hours long which got really tiring after a while.
There is a lot of reading, but the reading that you do is useful. So many of the things that I have learned in this class I have found to be applicable in my future teaching.

Incredibly chill! She has like three major projects & quizzes that are super easy (and you can retake) plus there's no final exam. Professor Lay just wants her students to understand the concepts of the material and how it connects with real-world classrooms.10/10 would take a class from her again! Attendance isn't mandatory but it's a small class.

I really appreciated being in the class and always felt appreciated. Professor Lay is really knowledgeable about the current issues that ESL face in schools. I really learned a lot about advocating for students. Professor Lay was really understanding and was quite flexible with assignments and projects. I would recommend taking a class from her.

Professor Lay is knowledgeable, caring, and willing to work with her students. It is clear that she was recently in the classroom and remembers what it is like to work with real students and in a real classroom. She is young and in touch with the current social climate. I had her Spring term and it was wonderful. I would recommend her to EVERYONE!

Sister Lay is very nice and sweet, but very vague with instructions. She isn't very helpful either. This class was basically students learning concepts from the book and then teaching the class. One huge final project that's pretty fun. I would say stay away.
i love dr rose. she really cares about your learning and is so willing to help you!

This class was SO helpful in preparing for the OPI. I have literally never felt more fluent in French (even on my mission). Dr. Rose is SO nice and helpful, but there are NO opportunities for extra credit & she grades SUPER tough (and doesn't give notes for how to improve). Study the vocab - pop quizzes are worth the most percentage.

Professor Rose is incredible! She is so focused on helping each individual student and she is accommodating with difficult circumstances. Her goal was to help all of us learn the realities of teaching. She is so Christlike and really values individual opinions.

I genuinely enjoyed learning French with Dr. Rose. She explains the tricky grammar in a way that helps me understand, which is good, because this class is like grammar boot camp! Be prepared for a lot of discussion with a partner during class, mostly going through grammar problems together. I liked the writing aspect of the course!

Incredibly understanding, willing to help, and just an overall great human being. Her feedback is always so constructive, even if you do something totally wrong, because you can tell she genuinely cares about you.

Professor Rose is the kindest teacher I've ever met. She grades a little harder, gives amazing feedback on assignments, gives a bit of homework, and shows genuine care for the students. She demands good work. She helped me build confidence in my teaching abilities; I definitely recommend. Take her classes!

I loved Brother Conrad as a teacher. His lectures are hilarious, and he tries really hard to connect with the students. A lot of the assignments were unconventional (like go on a solid food fast for 3 days, or go on a media cleanse for 3 days), but he believes all the assignments have a point that he's trying to get across.

Brother Conrad's assignments were very unconventional. We had to do a three day digital fast, a 48 hour no-talking fast or juice fast, an interview with an atheist, and to attend a religious service of a different faith (among many other odd assignments). In theory it sounds fun, but I always had to plan my week around complex assignments.

Bro. Conrad is an incredible professor! This is a low-stress, interesting, and fun GE class to take, and I've recommended it to all my friends. I had so many interesting assignments from this course, so only take it if you're up for some adventure in your life. Overall he's a super dynamic and caring guy and you won't regret taking this class!

Brother Conrad is an amazing professor. He does a great job teaching us about various philosophies and how we can both understand the world around us and come unto Christ by doing so. He teaches in a very unbiased manner and encourages participation so that more perspectives will be taken into account. He's a great person and a great professor.
His class is very discussion-based.

Conrad acts as more of a guide to the class, letting students structure the class early on in the semester. This style might be a bit jarring if you wanted something more structured, and it does mean that the quality of your class depends a lot on your classmates. Strong emphasis on teaching rather than busywork, all assignments felt purposeful.

I learned so much in this class and it was very manageable. We had short assignments from the reading due before every class and some application assignments. The first few assignments were hard, but once you figure out how to do them it's very easy. Brother Conrad is amazing! He's so passionate, caring, and classes were never boring.

Brother Conrad is more than an incredible academic who makes you challenge your beliefs and ideas as philosophy should. He is an inspirational and heart-touching human being. His class flow was very organized and engaging, grading was transparent, and his lessons were invaluable. I would take this class again with Brother Conrad; we had a blast!

I don't ever write to rate my professor but felt I needed to for this class. PHIL 110 is awesome (and it's because of Conrad). Show up, and participate, and you will be just fine. He doesn't expect you to know everything. It's a small enough class that you get to know your other classmates - which is cool.

I loved this class enough to return as a TA! Lectures are more like class discussions, and they are always thought provoking and deep. Brother Conrad is incredibly passionate and full of energy when it comes to lecturing about philosophy. I will be taking more philosophy classes in the future because of this class!

Brother Conrad is great and the class is an easy A. Lectures are a little long because of how late they are but he is great. He is a seminary teacher so it is that kind of class feel. There are a decent amount of assignments but they are pretty easy.

This class taught me so much about how to think. Bro Conrad makes it a very chill class if you do the reading and assignments. We would have group discussions often about our opinions about the reading, while he would challenge us to think deeper or in a different way. He inspired me to read more into some of the philosophies we studied in class.

Oh, "Master Conrad," where do I begin? My favorite Professor at BYU, his class will serve to be a refreshing respite from your other courses. A warm, welcoming environment conducive to learning is all you can expect from his class. There is reading, yes, but it is very minimal and very interesting. 

I seriously cannot recommend Conrad enough.

Brother Conrad is awesome. I've learned and changed more in this class than in most of my BYU classes, partly because of quality class discussions and because the readings and assignments are so reflective. You get what you put into it. Easy A, interesting classes, fair grader, very accessible outside of class.

I am so glad I took this class with Brother Conrad. He was such an Inspiring, Caring, and Relaxed Teacher. He has a passion for Philosophy, so I knew I was in good hands. He always came to class ready to teach. Homework was easy, and class was fun! He cared about each student and their needs. All I can say is, take this class with him!!

Brother Conrad was inspiring, funny, and so down to earth. There were lots of assignments but no midterm. The final exam was a class party, we all brought food and presented a project on our life philosophy (it also could have been a paper if you chose). If you do the reading and participate you will be inspired. I learned so much. would take again

I liked this class a lot even though I'm not into philosophy! Don't freak out when your first few assignments get bad grades. You'll do a lot better on the rest of them, trust me. This class is an easy A if you do your work and go to class. I did find the lectures a little boring, but that might be since class was in the evening and I was tired.

Brother Conrad gets to know all of his students by name. I learned a lot in this class from our discussions. There are written assignments due before each class, but no midterms. The more prepared you are to share your thoughts or ask questions about the text, the more this class is a really rewarding experience.

I'm a senior and Professor Conrad is the best professor I've ever had. His teaching method is very unorthodox, so much fun. The lectures are great, homework is easy. No real final exam, just a final project. Would 100% recommend as an easy GA.

Conrad is an amazing professor, if you have to (or want to) take philosophy, hes the professor you want. The class itself isnt difficult, you just have to write different responses to the readings and do a few application assignments. Conrad creates an engaging and open discussion about the readings in class and really makes it fun.

This class was a very easy A. Class was all discussion based and are graded on participation. Conrad really understands the phil and loves it, was cool to see so many people come together with all their opinions.

Easy A, interesting discussions. If you want an objective intro to philosophy, I don't recommend this class at all. Allows critical thinking but only to a certain point. If you want mostly Christian philosophy and to hear people (including Conrad) bear their testimonies, you'll love it. Felt like seminary. Conrad is great, very energetic.

This class was really eye opening! I thoroughly enjoyed the selection of philosophers that we read from. Sometimes the reading is challenging, but it is always discussed in class. There's lot of room for creative thinking and personal responses. Professor Conrad really wants the students to engage with the ideas presented.

Brother Conrad is seriously the best. There are quite a few assignments and the TA grades them so grading was pretty tough at first but you get the hang of it and the final was pretty easy. This class was on zoom this term and we had a lot of really interesting discussions and brother Conrad is big on hearing your opinion/thinking outside the box.

Brother Conrad is a great instructor. This class really strengthened my testimony of Jesus Christ through the lens of philosophy, which surprised me. Best option for fulfilling your Letters GE, hands down. You'll just fill out responses to readings and then come to class and discuss. Easy yet incredibly enlightening. I loved this class.

If you are looking for an easy A this is the class. Other than that I would not recommend this class, professor Conrad is easily the worst professor I have ever had at BYU. Assignments are very unstructured, and he is very unclear, it is mostly just busy work.
