Dr Verhaaren is a wizard. Especially in higher level classes, he is super open to helping students. Love the lectures, and the readings and assignments were super interesting!

Dr. Verhaaren is a super funny lecturer who did a ood job explaining tough physics concepts to a mix of majors. The textbook was fascinating and the research paper was manageable. Weekly science and history practice problems were chill. I highly recommend this class for Phys Sci GE.

Dr. Verhaaren's class was very fair. The tests were clearly based on homework problems or in-class examples. The homework allows you multiple attempts to get some credit which is helpful. The only issue with the class is an A is a 95. Dr. Verhaaren's teaching got better as the semester went on. Sometimes I felt like he was simplifying too much.

105 gets mixed reviews bc so many people have to take it, but Verhaaren is super fair. Lots of exams but that helps more than it hurts. Make sure you understand concepts, not just math. Pay attention to the slides he has at the end, people tend to pack up early but that stuff is on the exams. Good professor, the class is just hard.

Good exam format (7 midterms and a final). There's not a lot of homework/practice problems available. Lectures are often more conceptual than based on problem solving, and when there are example problems they are very difficulty and poorly explained. That being said, he cares a lot and is willing to do anything to help you succeed.

Dr Verhaaren does a fantastic job of breaking down concepts and explaining things at a level that beginner physics students can understand. I personally do not like physics, but I thought lectures were engaging and helpful. There are lots of exams (7+cumulative final) but honestly I liked this format better because each exam covers fewer concepts.

Professor Verhaaren is a really nice guy, but as the semester progressed his lecturing really went downhill. In the first few weeks things were really clear but from then on he made tough concepts more complicated with convoluted math and poor explanations. He has potential, but I had a hard time learning anything from his lectures this semester.

While he is a good professor he often is distracted from the lecture by student questions, he introduces difficult concepts in his lectures (difficult example problems), and attendance is mandatory (iClicker quizzes). Exams are very important and fair (7 total + final) and switch throughout semester (online non-proctored, testing center, in-class).

He does a very good job of explaining the concepts in a way that can be understood. The course is also very organized and he is on the side of the students. There are a lot of tests and it can be stressful but I feel like that it is done for the benefits of the students.

The subject is hard for those who aren't doing anything with physics, but he was an amazing teacher. I was terrified to take this class, but the way he sets it up helps you learn and not get too overwhelmed. I highly recommend.

Dr. Asplund is a very smart professor and has a lot to offer, but his class was just disorganized. There was no clear expectation of what we were supposed to know, just a list of terms that everyone Googled on their own. You'll learn a lot of random things, but it's not too hard to get an A as long as you attend every class.

Professor Asplund's approach to teaching composition is more collaborative than prescriptive; this means you won't learn quite as much, perhaps, but you'll learn more of what you're curious about. You will need to analyze and compose unusual music--but what is college for, if not broadening horizons? No final, but assignments require solid effort.

Dr. Asplund may not be the best lecturer, but he's an understanding and flexible professor. You get assigned a group which you have to write four compositions for. Getting together to practice these before performing in class was always a struggle.

Dr. Asplund is completely brilliant and kind, but I really didn't like his class. The homework took me hours. Almost every class was competition based board work(who can write this the fastest) and he wouldn't check our work, leaving lots of us stressed and confused. Lots of unnecessary tangents. Don't take unless you are solid on music theory.

Sixteenth century counterpoint is an obscure topic and Dr. Asplund doesn't try to make it relevant . He likes it to exist as something obscure for you. The class is difficult with compositions due every class period. He doesn't give great lectures but expects you to learn everything from the reading. Sometimes he doesn't even remember the rules.

Dr. Asplund is a brilliant guy, but he should not teach this class.  Expectations for passing off teoria homework were near impossible.  Tests were quite difficult. Homework did nothing to prepare you for tests (the two were disconnected)  The only redemption to expect from the class was his frequent use of extra credit. Don't take from him.

I love Dr. Asplund! He's so brilliant and funny.  Assignments are easy, just do them.  His style is like no other; creepers, chainmail, and suit jackets with colored skinny jeans but honestly he rocks it all.  The class is easy, just pay attention and make sure it makes sense to you for the next class because most likely there will be a quiz.

Dr. Asplund was great! He is incredibly brilliant and you learn a lot in his classes. He expects you to be prepared and work hard, but the class is pretty easy if you have a little bit of background in theory like I did.

Dr. Asplund is NOT the best music theory teacher at BYU! I completely understand theory, but listening to him teach it made me confused!  I think he is rather easy with homework, grading, tests, etc, but I didn't learn as much from him as I did from other teachers!
Professor Asplund is amazing.  Thoughtful, great shoes, articulate, generous, and inspiring.  He rocked my world.
He's a poor instructor. His lectures in class are directionless and wonder over various topics. He will take time outside of class to help you, but that will be the only place you'll learn.

Asplund is way into composition but he has you practice the concepts in class all the time so the two composition assignments aren't too hard and are lots of fun.  Straight lectures aren't his strength but those don't happen too often.  Not too much homework, 7 worksheets and no final. I'm taking him again for 296.

Composition class with Asplund was really fun.  Be prepared to write atonal/weird stuff, because the class is all about expanding your mind with compositional techniques.  No homework (other than composing pieces and performing them), no exams.  Easy grading.  Cool teacher.  Knows his 20th century stuff and is really funny once you get to know him.

Asplund is the BOMB for 20th Century Theory! He is so FUN and extremely funny! His grading is really fair and I like how its not all boring book work. His lectures are fun to listen to! He's my hero! (and hes a fan of school of rock... what more do you need)
He's cool.
He is a very funny teacher and excellent for 20th. century stuff
He loves it when you ask questions and is usually very clear and helpful. He's also absolutely hilarious, in an awkward goofy kind of way ;) I'm taking an 8am class just to have him!

I wholeheartedly reccomend taking 20th Century Theory with him!--it's his field to a T; it was the best class in all my theory core, and the most fun too.  We focused a lot on composing pieces in the styles we learned and people did CRAZY things on performance days.  Just a blast.  A very stylish teacher--he's definitely Seattle hip.

His class was not difficult, but it often was derailed by excessive tangents on little questions . His Learning Suite was NEVER organized, in spite of him continually saying he would. We spent an entire class period each semester going over his midcourse ratings, and he rarely made any changes. He was unaccommodating to say the least.

Fantastic professor. He is pretty strict with his class policies but he makes them very clear from day one, he is slow to grade, and assigns a ton of readings so be prepared to spend several hours a week doing those. Other than that, he's a super fun professor to have and is willing to help as much as you need as long as you reach out.

I was confused because I took CPSE 300 "from Christian Sabey" but he never had a video of himself, so I'm rating the class more than him. 
This class is manageable, but it feels like a lot of busy work. Some weeks there is a lot to do, other weeks it's not too bad. You mostly just work through a module of videos and readings. + lots of group work.

I got Professor Sabey as my UNIV professor, he was super kind and understanding. He was always willing to answer questions for me as someone going into the education program and put in a lot of effort to make everyone feel included. Hes a slow grader so you won't be up to date on how you're doing in the class but hes been very receptive to feedback

This was my favorite class that I have taken at BYU so far. He is really passionate about the subject and I really learned a lot. The test were a bit tricky but if you study, you will be fine. There are quizzes every class period and the lectures were very engaging. I recommend this class for every education major.

I loved Prof. Sabey's class. He is really passionate about ABA and teaches really well. He also does review games frequently which are really helpful. He's super slow at grading though so you never really know how you're doing in the class. His tests are also pretty specific and he grades harshly on the short answer questions. He is awesome though!

He's a nice guy and he tries hard. His examples can be confusing. His test questions are ambiguous and won't argue with you. He is right no matter what. If you read the easy-to-read text book then you should be fine.
Christian is a really great teacher. The class is hard but you learn a ton!!

I've taken a few classes from Christian, If you are in the Sped program you will have to. He is a great guy and he REALLY cares. His biggest flaw is organization, sometimes it gets a little much, BUT if you are open about your concerns and you talk to him, he is one of the most understanding professors. Be excited to take classes from Christian.

Christian is so great!! He is caring and wants his students to succeed. He really takes your feedback and tries to be a better professor. He respects his students and cares about how they are doing in the class. The class is fair. I wouldn't say easy A. but Christian makes up for it in how helpful he is!

Dr. vom Lehn is one of the best professors at BYU. Incredibly caring, available for his students, and really great at teaching difficult topics. This class was also definitely among the most difficult classes I took and was very calculus heavy, but Dr. vom Lehn is committed to helping everyone succeed. Come prepared with your best Econ joke!

I love Dr. vom Lehn! He is very knowledgeable, and is an amazing pedagogue. His classes are structured so clearly, and if you put in the work, it's very easy to succeed. The class itself is pretty math heavy, but it's doable. It's also always connected to real-world scenarios, which is so awesome.

Vom Lehn is a beast. Great teacher, and very passionate on topics that few could teach passionately. You won't regret taking a class from him, but you might regret not taking a class from him. Just pay attention in class, attend office hours, study for the exams, and you'll pass.

I hated macro when I signed up for this class, but thanks to Dr. Vom Lehn, I now tolerate it. He is a wonderful person, and this class was the best-organized in terms of assignments, tests, and support, that I have seen in my five years at BYU. If I had tried harder, I would have gotten an A-. I highly recommend Dr. Vom Lehn.

Econ 581 was a ton of work, with each problem set taking many hours to complete and some of the most difficult exams I've seen. That said, Dr. Vom Lehn is a great lecturer and wants students to succeed. He is incredibly supportive: 581 students can come into his office hours at any time, and most students get an A or an A- in the class.

Professor vom Lehn is super great. I signed up to take this class from him because I'd taken another class and liked it, and growth ended up being one of my favorites. Use his lecture study guides, and definitely study well for his exams, and the class is very manageable. His office hours are also super valuable.

Vom Lehn is the GOAT and the best economics professor you will ever have. I strongly recommend taking at least one class from him. He is very organized, and his review guides make his class very passable if you put in the work. Also, he puts up with all my shenanigans in class (SO if you're reading this right now).

Absolute legend. Every Econ student at BYU should take his growth class. Intuition and math behind models are effectively explained. Tons of online resources. Very engaging course material. Fascinating lectures. Take one of his classes!!!

Dr. vom Lehn is the GOAT. He is fantastic at teaching difficult concepts simply, and he is completely transparent about class expectations. He is also reachable outside of class time to go over difficult concepts. Take from him!

381 is tough, but vom Lehn is a stud. Obviously passionate about macroeconomics, and he lectures well, but you have to pay attention because he says things that seem like they are in passing that are on his study guide. His study guides/chapter reviews are life savers, and you should fill them out as you go along. Work for it and you'll get an A.

One of the best Econ professors at BYU. Material is hard but he gives really good lectures that are focused on student understanding. Accessible outside of class, hw & study guide is EXCELLENT preparation for tests. Class is super curved so you can still do well even if you bomb the tests. Tests are application focused, not many proofs.

Professor vom lehn is great. Just a really good guy, funny, understanding. In all his classes (I've taken 2), I've found them difficult, and I had to grind to study for the tests, but he really does give you all the tools you need. Just LISTEN carefully when he talks mentions structure and use the review sheets for tests.

Professor Vom Lehn really is an awesome professor. I'm not an economics major, so econ classes tend to be harder for me because I'm not a mathy person, but although there is some math in this class, if I put in the effort, class was doable. Problem sets were hard, but he posts the answers and practice tests after to help you prepare for tests.

Econ 581 was a difficult class that required a lot of time outside of class, but it is doable. Dr. Vom Lehn makes himself extremely accessible outside of class, and he really cares about you and your life. Our TA was also awesome, so that made it easier as well. Would recommend!

He provides so many resources that it feels super manageable. But you definitely need to do all the readings and attend class etc. Why nations fail was a great book. We used the other textbook once for a hw assignment but never again. If you practice the homework and practice exams and really study the lectures/review notes you'll ace the exams.

Vom Lehn is an incredible Professor. His class isn't easy, you have to do consistent work to get an A: Homework, Reading, etc. But, he gives you all the tools you need to succeed if you put the work in. Every midterm has 3 practice midterms with answers, every lecture has posted lecture notes, slides, and a review sheet. Great teacher, great class.

Come on! If you're taking this class, does it really matter what the RMP score is? This class is ridiculously hard. Professor vom Lehn is cool and gives you help to succeed, but you are going to feel like an idiot no matter what. It may have been easier if I had a better math background before.
HARD class, but he's a good professor. Pretty standard homework load comparable to 380/381. Don't get the textbook, you don't need it (you do need Why Nations Fail).

Prof vom Lehn is an amazing instructor! I loved the organization of his class, and he taught the course very clearly. He genuinely cares to his students (knows ALL his students by name). Perhaps, he is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. To the point that I enjoyed the course and did not care much on my grade.

The content is geared for a research career and is all models but lacks teaching the intuition behind the models. Very few in the class could apply the concepts learned into the real world. Comes from an Ivy league PhD and thinks he knows all of the answers unless it is politically charged.

Dr vom Lehn is amazing. 381 was my favorite Econ class ever. He teaches so clearly and provides you with the equations you need on the tests; you just have to just grasp the concepts. His lectures are fascinating and I'm sad that I'm not pursuing a graduate degree and won't be taking 581 from him. Take this class from him- you will love it!

Dr. vom Lehn is awesome. The class was probably the most difficult Econ class I've taken at BYU but felt that Dr. vL did a great job teaching and made himself available outside of class. He is just a genuinely good guy and really cares about student success. Very fair grader. Highly recommended.

Dr. vom Lehn is AWESOME! His class is organized really well, his lectures are interesting, and he makes sure that everyone is doing okay. The class is SUPER difficult, but he provides resources for you to do well and the TA was easily accessible. Take from him! You won't regret it!

This class was made to be way harder than any Econ class I've ever taken. Very math-heavy and his tests are impossible! The first midterm the class average was a D! And it doesn't get better after that.

Dr. Vom Lehn was my favorite Econ professor by far. He teaches you so much about how the world works. I usually never write comments; however, this man deserves to be praised. He cares about you as a student and he is more than fair on tests. Would take again any semester.

This is one of the few economics professors that legitimately care about you as an individual and want to help you succeed. He'll do whatever he can to help you pass, it's not an easy class but it's definitely doable. Tests are tough but don't stray too far from the HW.

Dr. vom Lehn is perhaps the greatest mix of intelligence and kindness I have observed especially in a university professor. Though the material can be challenging, he gives you all that you need to succeed and learn effectively. If you are on the border and you don't know if you should take a class from him, do it.

Dr. vom Lehn is the clearest econ professor. He lets you know exactly what to expect and how to prepare for his exams. No surprises. His tests really make you think and stretch beyond the problem sets (that were too easy compared to the test IMO), but it really separates those who just memorize and those who understand the theory.

I loved taking Macro from him. The subject matter is difficult but he makes it about as easy as it could ever be. More than any other professor, he makes the grading criteria straightforward and the expectations of what is required every day are very clear. If you work hard, you'll do well. Loved the class and would 100% take from him again.

Professor vom Lehn is a fantastic professor. He is super smart, knows the material extremely well, is very prepared for lectures and good at answering questions, and is always current on the data. He does a great job of structuring the class and providing helpful resources. He is also very caring and invested in the students' success.

Prof. vom Lehn does a great job at structuring the class and explaining the content in a way that makes it easy to understand. He is a funny guy and makes the class entertaining and fun. He is also really willing to meet outside of class and help with whatever you need, whether it's relevant to the class or not.

He really is a fantastic professor and he knows Macroeconomics better than pretty much anyone. The problems sets are ridiculously hard. The tests are ridiculously hard. It's all easy to him because he's extremely intelligent, but I think he doesn't realize just how difficult it is for most students to understand the concepts.

Professor Vom Lehn is a good professor who knows the material super well. However, this was the first year he taught Econ 432, and the class structure reflected the newness. Most of the students, including myself, that struggled agreed that there was a disconnect between the professor's understanding of what was reasonable and what we thought was.

Solid professor. Gives you study guides and posts notes before class. Super willing to help you out. He always started lectures with inspirational quotes (which I really appreciated). Tests could be tricky, but still doable. Part of your grade is participation based, so don't skip class. Lots of algebra (know the proofs for tests!).

Vom Lehn is a good professor. In my opinion, his content is sometimes  hard to understand the first time through in lecture, and there's a lot of material. He provides a ton of material to review before tests--past exams, review sheets, homework solutions--so plan ahead. He makes the class doable, but you do have to put in the work.

With vom Lehn, I enjoyed Macroeconomics much more than I thought I would. Clearly he is an extraordinarily intelligent and gifted person. He memorizes all student names before first class even starts to show he does care about you. Tests are okay, and he does give a generous curve. Helpful office hours. He's great at answering questions of any kind

Had a tough time in this class because he didn't make many of the models very interesting and his handwriting is very bad. However, reading house of debt is awesome and he's plenty helpful outside of class.

Prof. vom Lehn is very responsive to student needs. His lectures are generally easy to follow and he uses a mix of math, theory, examples, current events, graphs, etc. to appeal to a broad group of learning styles. He gives you every resource you need to succeed

Prof. vom Lehn is honestly my favorite professor I have had so far. You can tell he really cares about his students and wants to see you succeed. The material can be pretty mathy, but other than that it is relatively straight-forward. He gives many opportunities for understanding. Take from vom Lehn!
Truly the best and most fair professor I have ever had. Tests are not too terribly bad, but he prepares you super well and gives a ton of information

Dr. Vom Lehn is an amazing teacher, he explains clearly every concept. He is very accesible outside class and gives very good feedback. Take good notes, and solve some extra exercises from the book to be ready for tests.

Take this class from Vom Lehn!! He is so helpful and there for his students. He is always willing to put in time to meet with you and review concepts. He allows you to replace your lower midterm grade with a higher one. The tests are just like the practice tests. No need to buy the textbook.

Professor Vom lehn was amazing! He cares a lot about student understanding the material and also our input on the class structure.  There is not too much homework but you'll probably need a Ta or group to get it done. Tests are great /very reasonable and aligned with the class material. Go to the Ta reviews and you will do great.
Probably my favorite teacher I have had here at BYU. He teaches clearly and his tests are straightforward. He has a huge interest in the students and wants everyone to succeed.

A good teacher who does care about his students.  However, he isn't very gripping and I occasionally found the class boring. Class participation was low (I think this was largely because he didn't seek it), which made the class monotonous.

Professor vom Lehn is one of the best professors I have had. His class and lectures are very structured and organized making it easy to follow along and know what to expect. He has great lecture notes, takes student feedback and actually incorporates it to become better. You can tell he really cares about your success as a person and in your career

Vom Lehn was one of my favorite econ professors.  His lectures are organized and interesting.  You are expected to work, but an A is very attainable if you put in some effort.  His tests are very fair and reasonable.  Pretty much, I really enjoyed his class and you should definitely take any class taught by him.

Dr. Vom Lehn is such a champ. He's very accessible and down-to-earth and is super interested in helping students. He goes kind of fast on lectures, but he explains clearly and you can always go in and talk to him if it doesn't make sense. He prepares you well for tests, and the class isn't too hard.

Wonderful professor. Not at all boring and dry like many other of the econ professors at BYU. First test is very calc based. Second one is more like traditional econ you would find at other universities. He is witty, interesting, and even smarter than he lets on. Really fair grader, and actually cares about students.

Such a good professor. Only reason it's not easy is because there is literally no way to make the material easier to understand. I respect this guy a ton and enjoyed his class. He's brilliant and can actually share whats in his head. He's there to help and goes out of his way to help students have a good experience. He's always trying to improve.
I took his class when he first came to teach at BYU. Very nice professor and he is willing to reach out to students. His tests were tough though...

Great class! I learned SO MUCH about Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign. The projects are very time consuming and take a lot of work, but Christina gives great feedback and helps a ton along the way. Best of all, I got a job because of the skills I learned in this class! Would recommend, would take again.

First, this is a graphic design class not a software learning class though you do watch videos on the software. You are expected to be both creative and good at InDesign, Photoshop, and Illustrator. She owns up to the fact that this class takes a LOT of time but doesn't change it. Her expectations are well beyond a beginner graphic design class.

Lots of good discussion about design principles. She moves fast, and I wish we had spent more time on the programs because so many times I was on my own confused. HOWEVER, she and the TA are really good at helping outside of class. And if you're lost in class Christina is happy to answer questions. I learned a lot and I'm excited to learn more.

It is nearly impossible to get a 100% on assignments in this class since a 100  absolutely flawless. Grading is very subjectiveit's her way or the highway. Expect to spend hours in a computer lab on campus, it's the only way you can access the required programs without paying for them. Must have access to BYU server to get any class content. -_-

She's great! She moves really fast when teaching the Adobe programs, but always stays after class to answer questions and help you with projects. She grades fairly, but strictly, so make sure you double check the assignment requirements before turning in. No exams, just a few easy quizzes and our big design projects. (It's secretly a design class)

She's prompt to answer emails, encourages you to call, and is helpful in her office hours. She moves fast in the class tutorials and the whole class is rarely up to speed with her, but you can figure out how to work the programs by googling it. She expects you to teach yourself, so if you have that expectation going into it then you'll be fine.

She knows her stuff but moves very very fast. She spends a lot more time on design theory than she does actually teaching how to use software programs, so it's hard to actually apply what she teaches. However, she does her best to help the students when they need it (which is a lot).

She's a super great lady. This is not at all my forte, but meeting with her during office hours really improved my work. Class was essential to learn, but even if you miss she's willing to help as much as she can.
Willing to work with students; if you need help, she is more than ready to assist you. She's fun, artsy, and really knows her subject! Wonderful teacher!

I don't think that there was a day that Prof. Johnson left class on time--she ALWAYS stayed after to help students with their projects! She gave very clear examples and would explain things again whenever a student asked during class. I highly recommend her!

I loved this class! Prof. Johnson was VERY clear in explaining concepts to us and giving examples. She was always willing to give extra attention to subjects as long as the students spoke up and asked her to explain. I don't know if she ever left class on time after it ended--she stayed after class every day to help her students on their projects!

Very good at what she does design-wise, but not good at teaching. Way too hard at critiquing projects, and guidelines as to what the TA will grade and what the teacher will grade are way too arbitrary and ambivalent. Hard.

Endless, boring lectures. I took it with a friend and she was my saving grace. Had tons of questions on every single assignment and got to the final and had no clue what I was doing still. Fairly easy grader. I feel like I would learn the skills better during an internship or something.

She's a great connection to have because she works for Lucid Press. Her grading criteria were unclear and sometimes the assignment itself was unclear. Lectures had good content but were super boring. You learn a lot of stuff at the surface level. Expect lots of projects.
This is a great class for any major! If you are looking for a class to grow leadership skills this is a great one! The class is a mix of lecture and role play so though it is long, it is not too bad

This is my favorite class I've taken at BYU. Prof Beck continually asked for ways to improve her class and connect with students throughout the semester. You truly get what you put in to the class. I would prioritize doing the extra credit and observing a mediation in person! I wish I had done it earlier in the semester!

Professor Beck is very proactive in seeking and implementing feedback from her students and is willing to work with students outside of class if they have questions or concerns. Her background is in law, but she was adaptable and helped students get what they wanted out of the class based on their career goals or goals in taking the class.

Prof. Beck is a professional mediator and shares real life experiences and tips during lecture. The textbooks are genuinely interesting and applicable to life. I learned a lot about conflict resolution in this class. The last hour of class is for role-plays where we get to practice mediating conflicts which are fun and memorable.

Dr Beck is one of the best lecturers I have ever had. She is always mixing up her teaching with videos, activities, role plays, opportunities to share, to get up and move, and to stay engaged. She's funny and thoughtful, and very intelligent, attentive, and engaging.

Probably my favorite class and professor. I didn't even know what mediation was going in, but the content was so useful, assignments were clear and interesting, and class discussion and role plays were so fun. 3 hour mandatory attendance and I still looked forward to it, SO IMPRESSIVE. She does an amazing job and is engaging and respectable. 10/10

Probably my favorite class I've taken and the best professor. She is funny, engaging, and skilled. I didn't even know what mediation was going in, but the content is so useful, the assignments are clear and interesting, and class discussion and role plays are fun. Mandatory 3 hour attendance and I still looked forward to it, SO impressive. 10/10

Professor Beck makes class super interesting and engaging. There is quite a bit of reading but I felt like everything was interesting. She also did lots of role plays that made class more fun to be in.
Thoughtful teacher and definitely experienced in the subject. She asked for feedback often and tailored the class to our needs.

Guys this was the best class with the best professor, it changed my life. The course is awesome because it helps you become a great communicator and negotiator and will help with anything you do. Prof. Beck is caring, understanding, professional, and funny. She does her best to get to know everyone. The class is very well structured, 10/10.

Really kind prof! This class is a heavily "come and participate" style class, so if you travel a lot/ don't enjoy a 2.5 hour long night class I don't recommend taking it. The 2 books we read for class are amazing & I learned not only how to mediate but how to resolve conflict. A good class if you are interested in a career in conflict resolution.

Awful lectures, unclear grading criteria, and pointless homework assignments. This is probably the worst class I have taken at BYU and I don't think the subject matter was not the problem. This class could have been a really valuable and enjoyable experience if it was taught by someone else. No connections are ever made to pscyh either.

Class time is wasted. You are graded on only a few things. Assignments are just busy work. Lectures are unorganized and exactly the same information we read before classes and are quized on before the lecture. But if you skip you fail. She is a sweet lady but seems like she does not know what to teach or what to do with lecture time.

Prof. Beck is friendly and does a good job of engaging the class. You cannot miss more than one class if you want an A. Quizzes on the reading at the beginning of each class with a paper and a final exam. Lots of practice mediations, so you get some actual experience with what mediation is like. Interesting class with a good professor.
This was a great class!
Take this class!

This is a wonderful class if you are not an art major (or if you are too, maybe)! Dr. Hale really knows her stuff and has really engaging and interesting lectures.  The grades are mainly just attendance, 3 exams (1 essay per exam), and 2 papers.  The class is very doable and a great experience.

She was a great instructor. Taught very well and was clear with what we had to do in exams. However, her TAs will make or break the class for you. Took two classes from her, and the second time, the TA was horrible and ruined her reputation. Grading was very unclear. Professor Christine is amazing, but her TAs can ruin the class

Prof Hale is awesome! She really cares about each of the students and makes the class fun. The midterms can take a bit of time to prepare for but are graded kindly. An A is easily achievable if you show up to class and study a few hours for the tests. Her lectures can get a little political sometimes but it didn't really bother me.

As long as you tune in to class and do the papers, you'll be fine. The Zoom sessions are super long, and you really do have to pay attention and participate because she throws in random pop quizzes. There are about five papers to write, two of them are timed, and well, the topics aren't very interesting so it can be a struggle.

Prof. Hale is kind and this class is reading heavy, not work heavy. The tests are in essay format and have clear study guides. I struggled with this class personally because it's 2.5 hours over zoom and I wasn't always sure what to take notes on. It also took weeks to get a response on emails sent to her or the TA. Grades took months to be put in.

Christine is SO NICE! You can tell how much she cares about art. She always invited classroom dialogue regarding the different pieces, and also talked about some that might be hard to accept. She knows her stuff! She made the class so engaging and really helped me develop a love for art and know how to appreciate it better. Take ARTHC from her!

Took this summer term, and it was a long class, 3 hours 2 times a week. But she made class time fun and I learned a lot about art and history. She's super sweet and there's just a few papers throughout the term that you had to get through.

I had no interest in art coming into this class, but I now unexpectedly love the art world because she made it come alive. The class is very, very easy, but in this case, there's not a trade-off between it being easy and learning a lot. She is also super funny and kind, and I respect her so much as a person and a professor.

I love how much she knows and how she makes art and history come to life!! She was one of my absolute favorite professors at BYU and I will be so sad to leave her class. The way her class is set up, the grading, the assignments and exams are SO doable. She is fair, kind, non-judgemental and very engaging. She is also so full of energy!!!

If you're taking this class for a GE, I would highly recommend taking it from Professor Hale! She is the nicest person and super sweet. This class is very easy if you show up, participate, and do the assignments (there's not that many assignments). You do get graded for participation but just a couple of comments per class will do it!

Wow this class was insanely easy. Take her for your GEs! 2 simple essays, 2 midterms and one final. Exams are responding to prompts she gives you beforehand. Class is less focused on memorizing things and more focused on application. I am not a huge fan of art but genuinely enjoyed learning from Dr. Hale. Classes felt a bit long though.

This class is hilariously easy. Like I put maybe 20% the effort into this class then I did for the other civilizations GE I did the same semester. That doesn't mean I didn't learn just as much. I loved this class because I felt like I could actually enjoy the lectures instead of feeling like I needed to memorize little details.

Highly recommend taking this class. Prof Hale is a very caring individual who is an expert in her field. If you want to do well in her class make sure to show up and participate in lectures, and to do your best on the assignments. There are three exams in the class, but she will help you prepare for them in class. Great class, even better prof!
Met online once a week. Attendance required. Kind professor and interesting lectures. Learned a lot about art and changed the way I think of it. Would take again for sure.

For a GE this class was great. The biggest bummer is the it was 2.5 hours once a week. Which was hard for me to get everything I needed to out of the class. There are 3 tests, a couple of small papers, one long paper and pop quizzes. You also need to participate in class. Professor Hale is a sweetheart and I would totally recommend her class.

Hands down, Christine is my favorite professor. Ever. She is sooo kind, so caring and is an amazing teacher. I enjoyed her lectures so much and always looked forward to them. I learned so much and really felt like I understood the concepts she taught. I wasn't a huge art fan, but she knew how to make art fun to learn! 100% take from Christine!

Prof. Hale is so kind and fun! Her class was super easy, yet you still learn a LOT of cool stuff! I never knew I had an interest in art history until this class! I also got my textbook late and managed to get through the class without using it much, so dw if you don't get it. Take advantage of the TA reviews, they're so helpful for the exams!

Prof. Hale is a saint. I always enjoyed class and learned so much. She knows a ton about art and really knows how to share her love of art with her students. Three tests in essay format and one long term paper. 4-5 pop quizzes in class just to keep track of attendance. As long as you study you'll get an A on the test. Her class is full for a reason
Professor Hale is incredible. If you are attending BYU, you simply need to take her art history classes.

Prof. Hale is one of the best profs I know. She has a way of making her lectures so interesting and engaging. She is a very merciful grader. The only downside is her classes are so full and the waitlist is so crazy. Art can actually be interesting. Thank you Prof Hale.

Christine is great, I wish I had taken her for my first Civ credit as well because I hated IHUM 201! Her class is interesting, easy, fun, and actually made going to art museums and seeing design and architecture more interesting. I didn't like I'd like it much, but I loved it!

This was the easiest general I've taken. Prof Hale was super nice and good with grading. Lectures felt pretty long especially during spring term but no complaints. A couple papers and some written midterms and there were pop quizzes in class but they're easy if you take notes during class.
Professor Hale is the best! Easy class, but you learn a lot. Wish I could take her course over again.

One of my favorite classes ever! If you pay attention and participate in the discussions, it's easy to write good papers and get an A. Not a crazy difficult class but you still learn and retain a lot. She's a great lecturer and makes it easy to connect with the art. I really liked her questions - really helped me think and remember things.
Prof. Hale is one of the nicest people ever. The class was pretty easy as long as you kept up with the material. She is super caring and kind and passionate about art.

Professor Hale is a GEM! Everyone needs to take a class from her. It was easy (3 tests, 2 papers, and 3 group quizzes), she was SO kind, and she really makes you appreciate art history. I took her for 202 and will for sure take her 201 class.

Best professor ever. She loves art and her lectures are amazing. There is NO homework. Only 2 midterms and a final that were open book and she gives you a week to do it. She understands that most people in the class are here to get a GE and knows you have other classes going on. Seriously the most caring professor, a hidden gem at BYU. TAKE HER!

TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER TO FULFILL CIV 1 G.E. REQUIREMENT! It is such an easy class, but you learn so much! I ended with 101%! There are two compare & contrast midterm essays, a long term paper on one specific piece of art, and a final essay. Those are really the only 4 things on your grade, but she's a nice grader! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Sister Hale is so amazing. TAKE HER. She responds to all your emails and is so nice to all of her students. Her class is not too difficult and it is super fascinating to learn of all the different types of art in the world.

Honestly this was my easiest class at BYU, and I knew nothing about art before I took this class. I left loving art and really enjoying the class. Professor Hale is always willing to help her students. If you are afraid of art and want an easy class where you will learn a lot, this is if you. There are three exams, a paper, and a one page write up.

She is amazing. One of the few BYU professors who understands what college is about. The class is super easy but the her lectures are amazing. I despised anything to do with art before taking her course but I thought the class was fascinating and am now very interested in the subject matter.

Christine is a great teacher. There aren't a lot of assignments in her class, but they are easy and she grades very liberally. You really feel her love of art history in every lecture. There are 3 pop quizzes, but they were easy and we took them as a class. If you need an art general, this is the one to take.

Christine is AMAZING! My favorite classes. Her lectures are long because they're only once a week, but honestly, she makes up for it by adding cool stories and keeping you engaged. VERY few assignments which is nice because as long as you follow the prompts on the papers and midterms, you should do well. Pay attention in class. Enjoyable course.

I LOVE PROFESSOR HALE!! The only assignments all semester are 3 term papers, a mid term paper and a final paper, all of which are graded kindly (I got a 98 on all of them and didn't even try that hard). She is also SO KIND and makes the lectures very interesting! Easiest A but also learned so much!! TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER!!!

This class seems hard on paper because there are so few assignments, but she is the easiest grader of all time. I never touched the book. Just go to class and get the main ideas down, and the tests are way easy. She is super nice and willing to work with anyone who needs it, and her lectures are really interesting too!

Amazing class! I took it online. There were 3 exams and 1 paper. The exams are essay format. She is a really nice grader. Must attend the live lectures and participate to receive full credit. Easy A. Didn't use the textbook at all. Take this class!

Christine is an extremely nice person and it was a fun spring term with her. I took her class online during COVID and it was an easy A. As long you half pay attention in class, youll get 100% on the take home tests (might change with in person classes). Theres one 5 page paper during the semester that isnt too difficult. NO HOMEWORK!

Christine was so nice and this class was very interesting. Her lectures were super interesting and well-paced. Although we had class for 3 hours, I never really felt like class was boring. I loved it when Christine would tell a personal story in relation to a piece of art. 2 midterms, a final, and 2 papers. A great GE option!

I took ARTHC 201 and almost always read the textbook before class. It's not totally necessary, but it helped a lot with understanding what was being discussed in class. This is definitely an easy class and should be taken if you want to get some effortless generals knocked out. Christine is great!

You could tell that Hale cared a whole lot about what she taught. She was super engaging and relevant in her lectures. The class was super easy yet rewarding. If you need that civ credit i 100% recommend taking 201 or 202 from here.
Although this class is graded by very few things, it was very manageable! She made class interesting and the class didn't demand a lot of busy work which I really appreciated.

On paper, this class looks scary (2 midterms, two papers, and a final) but Christine was a great teacher! I have been dreading taking this class for my GE, but I was lucky to get Christine for 202. She is really knowledgeable, but isn't obnoxious about art history. Her lectures are very reasonable, and she'll help prepare you for the exams well.

She's amazing. I was NOT excited for this class or this subject but she makes the history and art so interesting and applicable (yes-- she makes ancient art applicable to your life lol). She doesn't take herself or the art too seriously and is so open-minded. She made a 2-hour evening class fly by. Come to class and tests are not bad. Take her!

Prof. Hale is a good teacher. She is passionate about art history. There are not many assignments but if you come to class, the midterms are not difficult. She is an easy grader, but there are not many assignments on your grade. You don't have to show up to class, but I highly recommend going because it will be an easy A if you go.

She is awesome! Her goal is to help students gain the tools to appreciate art. She teaches from a list of works, and you have to go to class to get the info on them. I didn't touch the textbook, if you take good notes in lecture you'll be fine. Tests are essays based on prompts given beforehand. Quizzes are easy. Minimal memorization needed.

Christine is honestly one of the best professors I've had at BYU. She is extremely engaging and passionate about art. Even though I'm done with art GEs, I'm a little sad I won't be taking more classes in the subject. She grades generously and fairly, her criteria and expectations are more than clear. Highly recommend.

Let me start off with say how much I HATE the humanities, especially art. BUT Christine was an amazing professor. She doesnt take herself too seriously or the works of art that we looked at. She made me appreciate art. Tests are simple, essays with a prompt. You have to memorize the artist, painting name, and date then understand basic concepts.

Professor Hale is awesome! She's one of the few teachers I've had that is open to other opinions. She doesn't care much about specifics, but more about understanding ideas and concepts. I never touched the book. She gives a few pop quizzes, but they're super easy and usually with a group. Tests are one essay with prompts provided before hand.

Christine is seriously awesome. She really loves what she teaches but she sometimes gets her facts wrong so it's important to follow along in the textbook. There were two midterms with art ID and an essay, a 5-6 page paper, and a non-comprehesive final. Participation is a big part of your grade so be sure to speak up a couple of times each class.

Christine is a great professor! I enjoy art history, but you will like this class even if you are just taking it to check off your GE credit. She makes the lectures easy to understand and exciting. There is a lot of participating and discussing in class so the time flies by. The tests and essays are not graded hard either.

If you need a good art/world civ class to take, this is fantastic! I am not a history or art guy at all, but Christine is extremely entertaining and is a great teacher. She explains things very well and she absolutely knows what she is talking about. She forms her tests in ways that make you learn the history and context of the art. Great class!

Professor Hale is seriously the best. I came into Art History class thinking that I wasn't going to enjoy it at all, but ended up loving the subject. Her class is super straightforward, just do the readings so you're ready for in class quizzes and you're good to go. She doesn't make you memorize a ton of pieces of art like other professors.
This is a tough course, and she has high expectations of her students. She is fun, though, and as long as you play by her rules she will be your best friend.

I was disappointed in this class. I expected a more college like class especially for the upper division. Many times myself, and others, felt like she was still teaching Jr High. If you want to really learn something about family meal managment, pick another class. It's easy but there is lots of busy work. Also the class wasn't cery well structured

She is so awesome. I really enjoyed her class, she really loves what she does and you can tell. She is very helpful and is also very understanding and really works to help her students succeed. Her tests are cake and she doesnt assign too much busy work so I highly recommend her.

Cool guy, he genuinely cares so much about you and wants you to enjoy what you are learning. Books were great, didn't have to put a lot of brain power into reading them cause there were simple comprehension quizzes and discussions, then write about the books for final. I did have to remind him to post the tests though, he is pretty unorganized.

He is an awesome teacher! I really loved each lecture and how flexible he was with what he taught. He was never afraid to drop what he was teaching and switch to something different to help us better understand what we were learning. He's super willing to work with you to help you succeed! If you do the reading and show up to class you'll do great!

Professor Blythe is awesome! I ended the course feeling more like friends than just teacher-student. I learned a lot from this class, past the topic only. It's stretched me into trying new things I probably wouldn't have before. His class has a lot to offer but you get what you put in. Super kind, understanding, works with you. Go in open-minded.

Class was confusing, and the content was quite boring and weird. I feel I didn't gain much from taking the class other than learning about angels and demons which I personally think won't take me anywhere.

Professor Blythe is passionate and wants you to become a better reader. However, this class was harder because of his disorganization and lack of structure. You didn't know what to expect going into class that day. You might enjoy the class if you like angels and demons (his chosen topic), but I personally would have taken something else.

He is genuinely my favorite professor! Some may say he's weird, but he is the best guy out there. He is so kind and forgiving! He cares for his students so deeply, he once brought us chips and cheese to eat during a lecture! he is truly the best! He is very passionate about teaching, and is always open to debate!

If you are interested in angels, demons, selling your soul, folklore, and the devil, you might like this class. I have no interest, so I did not enjoy the class. I appreciate the fact he has an odd interest, but I personally didn't enjoy the content.

Chris is a wonderful professor and quickly became one of my favorite professors at BYU! I actually took two courses at once from him, and he was delightful in both of them, so much so that I'm currently taking another course from him! He is very knowledgeable about folklore, and will get you excited about everything if you just enjoy the ride.

Professor Blythe continues to be my favorite professor at BYU! He is kind and understands that learning comes more from class discussion and participation than tons of useless homework. There were only four major assignments and daily reading quizzes that weren't too bad. He is the best. This is my third class with him, & I can't wait to take more

Dr. Blythe is the best teacher I've ever had! He's a charismatic professor that teaches really, really interesting topics that relate to my faith and grow my knowledge of the larger world around me. He's helped me in my own personal and academic adventures, growing my skills as a writer, researcher, folklorist, and more. I cannot thank him enough!

Dr. Blythe teaches in a really fun way. He's very calm and easy to talk to, and tackles a lot of complicated material in a super professional way. He had the authors of most of the books we read come visit which was so amazing. At times his assignments were tricky, but he's totally willing to clarify. It's a lot of reading, but at least it's cool.

Best professor EVER!! Super fun, kind, and caring. He will try to learn everyone's names and something about them. He's not the most organized, but he grades very generously and his classes are a good time. I want to be like him when I grow up. Take his class!!

Professor Blythe is AMAZING! If you have the chance to take a course from him, you absolutely should. I took ENGL 640R from him. He cares more about your growth as a learner than about grades, and I think this is one of the classes where I grew the most because of that. He is also very open and honest, always willing to talk with students. 10/10

Prof Blythe was a great teacher, making this class easy and fun. The readings weren't too difficult (if a little boring), and there were very few assignments. The few assignments were not hard and he gave lots of help. I found his lectures very confusing and disorganized, but there weren't any tests so it didn't impact me at all.

The key to passing a Blythe class is finding out what fascinates him and then basing your essays on that. If you put in any effort—show up, do the readings, participate in class discussions, meet the very basic essay requirements—he'll pass you. I literally got 100% on every single assignment.

I liked his stories, his passion, and how he allowed us to explore our own interests. I wish it was more structured and organized. I did the reading (unlike most of the class) and found it mostly unnecessary. The vibes of the room were weird and the discussions always felt awkward. Could've been bc of my class and not him.

Professor Blythe is the best professor I have ever had. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. On the first few days of classes, Professor Blythe clearly laid out his assignments/schedule for the entire semester. The books and concepts taught were incredible! I would one hundred percent retake this class!

What a fantastic waste of my time. Class discussions almost never lined up with assigned readings for that day. Blythe has virtually no accountability or expectations built into his class but then gets upset when people are on their phones/laptops. If it seemed like he tried, students would take it more seriously. He is not a serious professor.

He's an ok teacher, but this class stressed me out. Not super organized. Daily reading quiz and lots of reading. I liked most readings, but sometimes it felt like a lot. Grades are from writing a short story, creating an outline for an anthology, daily quizzes, participation, and 4 papers. I didn't like the grading on papers, but to each their own.

I didn't really care for him as a teacher. He's not the most organized, but he's fairly fast with returning grades. There was an almost, if not, daily quiz on readings. You have several big projects for this class, ultimately turning in a folklore project to Special Collections. He seems really nice, but I find him a little personally invasive.

Excellent professor with a great understanding of his art and how to become an effective student of literature. The classes are discussion-based so come prepared with your reading done. There are a lot of short papers that are really easy and clear to do. Professor Blythe is very kind and understanding and will help you succeed.

I loved Professor Blythe! His class was interesting and I loved the books we read. Of course there is a lot of reading, but that's the class you signed up for. There are about ten 500 word essays throughout the semester. The classes themselves are mostly discussion based and you will be expected to participate.

I was super scared to take this LDS literature class because i don't love english classes but i loved this one!! You need to do your reading before every class and he does give quizzes. The readings take a couple of hours so be prepared. I genuinely loved writing the papers and participating in the discussions!! 10/10
Just a quality guy. One of the only professors that's taught where I wanted to go out and learn more about things I learned in class.

He has a vast knowledge of sources that you can possibly use on research projects. He is also well acquainted with whats presently going on in academia, which was essential for my project. Excellent instructor

Be prepared to read a lot. And always read, you never know when he is going to ask about it or quiz you on it. Its a little frustrating when you read and he doesn't ask about it though. Just read always to be safe
If one is preparing to go to grad school, this is the class that teaches you how to be a scholar. Very intimidating, and a tonne of information.

This class was titled Mormon History, and he presented the history in very non-biased way, which is unusually difficult to do from any stand point. Any question a student asked was answered with an unusual ease. He opened my eyes to how the Mormons represent a fascinating, fringe aspect of antebellum American culture. Great and demanding class.

Dr. Chris Blythe knows his stuff. If you have interest in ACADEMIC  Religious Studies you must take his classes. He clearly and interestingly presents the material in class. He is absolutely hilarious in a way that somehow adds to the lecture or point he is trying to make. Read the books he assigns and be actively interested, and you'll get an A.

Professor Cutri is a kind person, but his classes lack clarity and structure. Expectations and grading often feel vague, and feedback tends to be broad without actionable direction. Classes can feel disorganized, and communication is inconsistent. Best for very self-directed students.
Chris does a great job inspiring you to make something impactful. He focuses less on rigid school deadlines and requirements, and more about pushing you to your personal fullest potential.
GOATTTTT!!! I can concur about him being the opposite of Jeff Sheets lol. For that reason alone, take Chris.

Totally disregard the bad reviews. Chris is the best professor at BYU hands down. I've never had a more caring and relatable professor. He's definitely not political, at least from my experience. I feel like he gets on everyone's level. He's literally the opposite of Jeff... which is why you should stick with Chris throughout the entire program.
Chris is pretty openly political, doesn't give amazing feedback (he gives it on a group level, as opposed to just your group), but has a good heart and wants the best for his students.

Chris Cutri IS AMAZING! If you are an Ad major, please please please take a class from him!!!!! He is so good at what is does and is such a smart guy. I took him for 309 and he really got me excited for my future in advertising!
He's a great teacher! He is really passionate about this class and he knows his stuff. Most of the Homework is in class and the final is a class presentation to a client. Really good class!

Super good teacher and has amazing content and lectures. Brings forward some pretty interesting things to think about and really pushes for critical thinking. This class has been super good for me to take! The only thing I have a problem with is, the final test. He doesn't talk about facts in class but expects you to know them on the final.

Nothing good about this teacher, at all. He shouldn't be teaching. I did not learn anything from his class, everything he teaches is available online. He's pretty much an aging hipster, and he takes offense to others who do not share his views. His most damning feature however, is that he doesn't seem to care about his curriculum, nor his students.
Honestly, it's not a difficult class. He's a great guy that will work with other people. Cares about his students!
I never really knew what he was talking about or why he graded the way he did.. but he was an okay professor. Incredibly kind to the core and really knows his stuff.

very interesting guy. Easiest class ever automatic A if you just go and do the homework. I really enjoyed some parts and others I felt totally lost. He is a total hipster and really cool guy and I enjoyed his insights. He is very artsy and you know how artsy people are sometimes. Overall the class was kinda a waste but its easy and he is a cool guy

He's ok. You have do the reading  bc he has a quiz almost every day. His tests arent too bad. DO NOT procrastinate your final project, start as early as possible. His expectations seemed kind of unclear tho..

This was my most favorite class all semester - most of us were actually wishing the class wasn't over at the end of the semester.  He's an interesting and funny guy, and he wants to push you creatively.  He's very willing to help and accepted feedback for his method of teaching.

A quirky guy- but he knows his stuff. Wished that he did attendance because the whole class was just one big project. Seems to spend more time with his creatives, but probably because he knows more about what they're doing. A nice guy whose not into hard deadlines and lets the class determine the flow.

I think Chris is one of the most underrated professors in the communications department.  Honestly, I've learned more about the advertising industry, being creative in general, working with other creative professionals, and production than any one else, and there are some good professors out there.  Sure, he's an interesting guy, but so helpful.

He might have listened to the feedback, because I had him Winter '09 and I didn't see nearly as much favoritism or emphasis on foreign films as everyone complained about. The classes were actually pretty interesting, he didn't spend the whole time lecturing so we had some great discussions. No tests, just projects, so don't worry about taking notes

I have no idea why people say he is boring or unhelpful. Maybe they're looking for a free A? He is interesting and insightful and will change your perspective on life. Do the reading, participate in class and you'll do great. One of my favorite classes this semester.

I'm not sure what everyone else is talking about. I certainly wasn't one of Professor Cutri's favorites, but he went out of his way to help me on assignments. I added the class late and he helped me catch up. I really liked that he has real world experience with what he teaches. And he is a genuinely interesting person.

I agree with the other posts-you have to fit a certain category to become one of his favorites. The class is fairly easy, but I also learned everything from the book, not Cutri. Take someone else if you really want to learn about the real world of advertising.

Great class, TERRIBLE TEACHER! If you are a jock or tall, forget about it! Not helpful, doesn't work with you on anything and you learn nothing! I would have rather taken Am Hert twice! What does that tell you?

Worthless!!! He is horrible. I'm all about participation, but who in the heck wants to spend the weekend watching films from Iran? Sucking up to get a good grade is pathetic! It should be based on your work and not how much of a "foreign film watcher" you are! Class could have been cool but hated the guy! Two Thumbs Way Down!!!

Chris is a good guy, but it is true that you need to think like a nerd to understand him.  Talk to him, express interest and make sure he learns your name.  I originally got a B+ in this class but after talking to him and showing some discrepancies, he bumped it to an A.  Helpful Hint:  Watch highly touted foreign films and ask him about them.

Chris is a fun teacher to have form comms330 because that is his specialty.  I wouldn't take a lecture-type class from him. If you want to get into creative track, he is a good one to choose because everyone thinks McKinley's class is the only way in.  If you are self motivated and if he is impressed with your ads, then you have a good shot.

Worst teacher ever!!! Cutri is totally scatterbrained and changes dates without telling you until it is due, then he won't except late work, well unless of course you are "one of his buddies." He seriously is a wolf in sheep's clothing. He seems all laid back but when you need his help he is horrible! Basically TALK TO THE HAND is what you'll get!

Cutri is a terrible teacher! Unless you are an "artsy" person you will get a crappy grade! He says class participation will boost your grade. Not true! If you want to get an A- like half the class, come to class shut up, do the assignments and don't express your "non artsy" opinion! If you don't like films from Iran or where ever, DON'T TAKE HIM!!!

Good teacher, gave tons of practical advice and application. Very easy to get along with. Assignments and projects were hands-on and in-depth enough to give us a good taste of the advertising world. I thought the class was fun and gave us good experience.
I'm still not sure what I was graded on.  He is a really nice guy, but I kind of felt like I got shafted out of an A.

Most disorganized teacher I have ever had at BYU. Due dates changed ALL the time. Tests were hard. I would reccommend taking it from someone else because I would never put myself through that again. I had to retake it because you have to get at least a B to get into the major. i retook it w/ another teacher & got a A and leaned tons more.

He's a nice guy, but his class was so disorganized and all over the place. He changed due dates and forgot things all the time. He would give you a study guide and then the tests would look nothing like it. I didn't really learn anything new in it and felt it was a waste of time.

I loved this class.  Chris does a great job in making the material easy to understand.  The end of semester project where you are given a real client and asked to create an ad campaign was also tons of fun.  I would reccomend this class to anyone.

Nice guy, not a stellar teacher. A bit scatterbrained, & not dependable or clear -which makes the class harder than it should be. Study guide for tests, but things are left off. Multiple choice questions are misleading so challenge them if you have facts. Lecture is pointless because he just reads info from the slides that is straight from the book
Chris is a good guy and it is a good class, if you want to apply to the creative track take McKinlay, if not then I would stick with Chris.
Helps you to think differently in your ads, but very scattered and abstract in his grading.  I wish I took McKinley.

Definitely a nice guy, but the course was disappointing. Lectures were hour long slideshows giving basic details on concepts. Learning came from doing the homework. 70% of the grade was from exams. The final was very long for the given time limit, and no specific review materials were given. Other exams were fine.

He is the best ME professor I've known in the ME program. He always cares about his students and puts his best effort to help students understand the class. Thermodynamics is definitely not an easy class, but you can go through this with Dr. Dillon!

Great professor! Homework was due once a week and was very manageable. Reading quizzes did not take too much time. Tests were not too difficult. Lectures were also easy to understand and super interesting. He is easy to talk to if you have questions.

I've been telling everyone in ME I know to take the class from Dillon or not to take it at all. Definitely the hardest class I've had at BYU so far (possibly comparable to CHEM105?), but Dr Dillon cares about you succeeding. You'll leave this class with an intuitive understanding of some pretty tough subjects, and that'll pay off a ton later.

Dr. Dillon is the move for thermo. His lectures are super clear and helpful. The homework actually helps you prepare well for his tests which are hard but reasonable. He cares a lot about his students and is a fun teacher.

Dr. Dillon is one of my favorite ME professors so far. He cares so much about his students and takes time to share how great we are doing. His spiritual thoughts are next level. His lectures are clear and he breaks down complex topics really well. If you invest time into doing the homeworks well, you will do great on the exams.

Dr. Dillon is one of my favorite professors at BYU. The class is extremely well organized and expectations are very clear. Tests are very fair. The content is difficult but he teaches it as clearly and simply as possible and tests only on content that he covered in class. I wish I could take a class from him every semester.

I thought the class was good not great, tests are difficult. He spends the first 10 minutes of every class doing a spiritual thought which for me was not ideal. He seems to not see things from the students perspective very well (he made the final double the length of the midterm without any time increase and didn't care when we objected).

Dr. Dillon is one of my favorite professors. He helped me realize I could talk to professors when I was confused. His lectures were great and he is passionate about thermodynamics. He also understands the student life, and is very caring, and offers encouragement. Reading quizzes each lecture are helpful. Start the weekly homework early.

Amazing, def best professor for 202! Online readings and reading quizzes to do before most classes, but the quizzes were open book so not too difficult as long as you actually read. 4 papers but 1 is dropped so you only have to do 3, and 3 exams total (including the final which was non-comprehensive and weighted the same as the other two tests).

Dr. Flood is the best professor to take 361 from, and one of my favorite professors in general. He is super expert in the topics that he teaches, and his lectures are so engaging and informative. You have to write a 5-7 page semester paper, but he is always available outside of class and willing to give personalized, specific feedback and guidance.

You can tell Dr Flood truly cares about you and what he teaches. We read a ton of different works from tons of eras, genres, and literary movements. After talking with friends in other sections, Dr Flood is def the best 340 professor. Curriculum is organized perfectly and everyone felt welcome and safe to share thoughts and interpretations.

Dr Flood is awesome! You really get out of this class what you put into it. He doesn't care how good your French is, he just wants you to participate. There is a lot of literary analysis evidently so be ready to dig deep and read between the lines. I missed a homework assignment and he very willingly reopened it for me! He is the best!

Dr Flood is very passionate about the topic and does a great job teaching the literature. There is a lot of reading that you have to complete to really succeed, but if you skim or miss one here or there you should be fine. There is a semester long paper that is pretty difficult though so be prepared for that.

Gave out entirely arbitrary grades on writing assignments and was unclear/hypocritical in regards to attendance/participation--all of which accounted for a freakishly high % of your grade. More intrigued about himself, his own theories, and position than concerned about student success. Your grade is in his hands--be prepared if you take his course

His course is relatively entertaining if you like to read and analyze. His tests aren't difficult if you pay attention in class, he prepares you well before them. The hardest part of the class is the Thesis paper. I can't stress that enough, be DILIGENT with that paper. It can raise you up a letter grade or destroy your letter grade.

Dr. Flood is awesome. He was a pretty nice grader. We had a decent amount of homework, but not too bad (almost all the reading is online, so you save your money). The class was really fun and interesting. 10/10 would recommend taking his class.

Professor Flood was a great professor and he really cares about what he teaches. He is willing to work with students and he gives great feedback on assignments. There is a lot of reading for his class so allow yourself time to get that done before class.

Very good professor who is passionate about what he teaches. Reasonable and willing to work with students. Lots of assigned readings but most of class time is spent analyzing assigned works so no more than a quick skin is really needed. Tests can be a bit tough with some very specific questions, has all lectures posted though for study

Professor Flood was informative and kind, definitely enjoyed being in his class. The workload was a bit heavy, but that is probably normal for a language class at BYU. I really enjoyed being in his class, and he made sure that we got chances to participate as well as learn from the lectures.
Professor Flood is great because he is extremely knowledgeable and gives fascinating lectures. He is good at leading interesting discussions. He is a fair grader and gives good feedback.

He's a really nice guy. I don't love studying literature in English, let alone French. He made it as simple and understandable as possible. Meet with him if you have any issues and he will happily help!

Prof. Flood does an awesome job of making each piece of literature we read interesting. He has a great sense of humor. His class is structured very well, so if one puts in the work and does the required 3-5 total pages of reading before each class period, and A is very doable. Keep on top of the various semester long assignments.

This class was genuinely enjoyable, and while there was a fair amount of reading, the class discussions were greatwe actually talked about the readings and their importance, and there were no surprises later on the exams (and only 2 papers!) Dr. Flood loves what he teaches and it shows. Im already taking another class from him next semester.

I really like him as a person, he is super sweet and cares about the students, and gave some pretty solid extra credit opportunities as well. Readings are huge though and can be hard. I just wouldn't take him again because I know you could take the same class with someone else and not jeopardize your grade as much. Grades papers super hard.

Dr. Flood is demanding, but I learned a ton and he is super passionate about what he teaches. He taught a lesson about Easter traditions in France and it was hands down the best lecture I've had at BYU. French 202 was my favorite class. That being said, if you don't enjoy reading, papers or speaking French in class you might have a hard time.

If you're a French Major and  have all the time for this class, go for it. I talked to several good students in the class and they agreed on one thing: he doesn't realize that we have other classes too. He was kindof rude and disrespectful to me, he thinks you need to earn his help. If you're struggling and need help, not helpful at all.

Fairest teacher I've ever had. If you do something wrong (such as on papers) he is very fair with letting you resubmit. It is very possible to get an A in this class, and I think you will get exactly the grade you worked for. I learned more in this class than the rest of my french classes combined.
Energetic about French literature, expects you to be as well. Learned a lot about how french culture came to be. If you actually can speak french he grades harder than if you cannot.
Flood is a great teacher, very funny, Though language classes are very hard and this class required tons of work i loved it. I learned a ton about french and i speak way better now then i did before.

Though I went in with no real interest in French literature, the teacher really tries to help his students appreciate the materials studied and understand the significance of it. This was a fun class, and the professor is very interesting and helpful.
Rude teacher, tried to intimidate the class and to dominate and make people feel uncomfortable. Contradicted his own french speaking. Wasn't respectful with student's comments.
No Comments
M. Flood is an amazing professor. He really cares about his students on an individual basis and it shows. I highly recommend taking a class from him if at all possible.

Pro Haney is a very nice individual who cares about his students but his lectures were impossible to follow along with and get anything out of. They are messy and all over the place with constant tangents of unrelated material. The tests were hard to prepare for, not related to lectures and the TA grades unnecessarily hard.

This class was very simply run with reading assignments due anywhere between 1-3 weeks apart, a few essays, and a few tests. Reading was technically required before each lecture, but I didn't listen a whole lot and still got an A. If ancient history is your thing, you'll love it a lot more than I did. If not, it's still an easy GE.

He goes on tangents sometimes but when he talks about themes or reads sections in class, it'll be on the exam. The lectures are not super entertaining but if you're able to understand large themes in the text & look at the study guides, you'll be fine. Super nice guy, just not a fun class if you're not into greek mythology or philosophy.

This class was super fun! He makes learning about Greek and Roman history and myths very interesting. Any papers that you have to write are usually on topics of your choosing. He provides study guides for exams
The lectures can be extremely boring and it is hard to know if what he is saying is important or not.

Professor Haney is a really nice guy, and if he taught a more interesting subject I would totally take a class from him. This class itself however, seemed a lot harder then it needed to be for a GE.
