The tests in particular are needlessly difficult, including multiple essays. I liked the professor, but was glad to be done with the class.

Great guy, good class structure and organization. His assignments and grading are fair. The only issue with the class for me was that it was incredibly boring. The subject is just straight up lame. I do not care about greek or roman literature.

TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HANEY!!!!! He very clearly states the grading criteria. There are no surprises on that front unless you were not listening. Lots of reading, but the stories are actually super interesting. Come to class having read the chapters - great discussions about them in class. He's hilarious!! Makes lots of jokes but also dives deep.

This class is so hard... but so are all humanity classes. His tests are unbelievably hard, no multiple choice, so get ready to study. So much reading you couldn't even finish it. The tests were weighted so heavily that if you did bad, you were out of luck. The class is so, so hard, but the professor is a nice guy. He will try to help you succeed.
He was a very caring and funny teacher. If you memorize the terms and everything on the study review you will do great!

I'm taking this class right now and it's so difficult. Professor Haney really is a sweet guy, but there is so much reading and he is a tough grader. The midterms are SO hard and require you to have random facts memorized from reading, most of my classmates got a C or below. I would not recommend this class unless you have a perfect memory...

This man was so sweet I really liked him. You have to read a lot but if you do it you will be ok. Go to class! There are several papers but he is willing to work with you. Tests are hard but if you look at the study guide you will be fine.

I loved this mythology class! Dr. Haney is kind, passionate, and engaging during lectures/discussions. The chosen texts are interesting, and class discussions were fun. He showed genuine interest in our opinions and interpretations of the texts. He was also flexible when schedules needed to be shifted or assignments needed to be altered. 10/10!

He was an awesome professor, though because of certain conditions he missed/cancelled class a good handful of times. A lot of reading, but even though I didn't always fully understand the concepts the lectures pretty much explained everything you need to know. pay attention, take notes and you'll be just fine.

don't get me wrong professor haney was a sweet guy, but he taught like it was a class for ancient literature majors. He expected us to understand the material so the lectures were just him talking about what he loved. The tests are insane, and hard to study for. The amount of reading assigned was crazy. Don't take from him just for a general class.

Honestly all you have to do is go to class, write 2 or 3 short essays, and study the exam review doc intently and you will do great! Other than that there is like 0 homework. Our whole class wanted the test to be online rather than in the testing center and he let us do that. I barely read any of the books. Study groups help for tests.

I would compare the difficulty of this class to American Heritage. The text is complex and I feel like the lectures are only the professor talking. I was lost as to how to prepare for the tests which are extremely difficult for a general class & required lots of memorization. He's a great person, but don't take this if you just need the credit!

This is one of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU. Professor Haney is so great and lectures are really interesting. The amount of reading you're asked to do is honestly kind of ridiculous, but I mostly skimmed and read cliffnotes and felt like I was on track enough. Tests are kinda specific but overall this was fun.

Easily my favorite professor of all time. Great teacher, our discussions in class were super interesting. He's fun to talk to and gets to know his students. We wrote a few essays in this class and he was very loose about the format. He also helped me a lot with some stuff going on in my personal life and was so so kind. 11/10 would recommend!!

The lectures and discussions that I had in this class were some of the most fun and interesting that I have had in any of the classes I've taken so far. The only thing I didn't like about the class was the tests. He gives a study guide, which really helps, but the tests are pretty long and you have to memorize a lot of specifics. Great class though

Professor Haney's passion for what he teaches is infectious, and I found his lectures and the materials he has you read very intellectually stimulating and worth while. I did spend a lot of time reading and studying for the tests, but the material is generally very interesting and straightforward. So glad I took this class!

This class had three tests which were totally manageable if you studied and three two page papers on a subject of your choice making it a pretty straightforward class for grading. There was also an opportunity for extra credit. Professor Haney and I had a disagreement on participation grades, but we were able to iron it out amicably.

I will die on this hill. Professor Haney is great. I see a lot of people here trashing him, but I feel like that is unwarranted. I see a lot of people talking about how hard the class is, but he literally gives a study guide on the things he will test you on. So, you'll pass if you fill out the guide even just SparkNotes the readings.

He had no plan going into lectures and often got sidetracked. Often taught like we all cared about the material as much as he did. Did not even use a powerpoint so it was almost impossible to distinguish between class material and tangents. Very vague on grading and very heavy on reading. If your taking for the GE just avoid him and save yourself.

IHUM 201 had an insane amount of reading, an average of 60-70 pages of reading per class period. It's very difficult to distinguish which parts of the lectures/reading are essential. We read tons about the heroes and fools of history, and I left realizing that I'm the biggest fool for taking this class. Find a more relatable class with less reading

Terrible class. Boring lectures that have nothing to do with the tests. Everyone flunked the tests in my class so he had to curve them. He abstractly gave participation points and graded the papers with no feedback. Classic humanities teacher who thinks his class is important when everyone is just there for the GE.

I didn't sign up to take this class with professor Haney. I decided to stick with it for the GE, but it was not fun. The lectures are dry as can be. The grading on papers is extremely vague; no specific feedback. He just reviews the readings or gives long history dumps. This class needs some serious re-thinking. Use Audible for all the readings!

Lectures are hard to follow. Tests are hard. Seeing as this is a general credit, I'd highly recommend getting an easier professor. He makes this class difficult for no real reason. It is not worth it. Nice guy though

I love Dr. Haney as a person and professor. This course had only a few, pretty simple assignments. His tests were pretty difficult and memorization-heavy and they dictate most of your grade since there are few grades overall. I learned quite a bit from his lectures and he's really kind. If you're a freshman, though, maybe find someone easier.
He teachers well, talks a lot, grades like you are a graduate student of ancient literature...

Love Prof Haney as a guy, but for a 100 level GE this is structured and graded like a Masters program. Although I may have learned more content than most classes, after putting in over 20 hours a week for three credits, the TA's are unable to help create paths of success for any assignments(all of which lack rubrics and specific instruction).

I really liked this class and Prof. Haney. He knew what he was talking about and you could tell he loved it, and that made it really interesting. The discussions in class were very intellectually stimulating and I looked forward to it. To pass, make sure you write down the parts of stories he talks about in class, that's what you'll be tested on.

This guy is very nice, but very difficult. The way that he runs the class feels like we are actually majoring in Ancient Literature. He loves what he teaches and expects you to love it as well. If you have a tough time reading and writing a lot like I do, its a tough class that will take a lot of work and headache.

Professor Haney is so passionate about what he teaches! He expects a lot from you however. There is a good amount of reading before every class period, and his lectures are a mix between lessons and discussion. You have four 2-3 page papers throughout the class. I was excited for this class and I really enjoyed learning from him!

This class was insane. The amount of hours it took for me to study for those tests was crazy, way too much for a GE. Tests are way too specific. I put in more time to studying for this class than any other class I took. Good luck if you take it from him! You're gonna need it.

Professor Haney is one of my favorite professors at BYU. His class is a discussion on the readings and videos assigned, and it is clear he values the opinions and ideas of each one of his students. Very caring and respectful as well. I was sick and he allowed me to make up an essay a few weeks late. Several papers due with attendance recorded.

I loved Professor Haney's class! He is super nice and you can tell he really loves to teach what he does. There is a lot of reading involved, but you spend class discussing the stories so it isn't boring. Super great class! Would recommend it to everyone.

I really like Professor Haney, but this class will not be to everyone's taste. He talks A LOT in lectures. There is a lot of reading and comprehension is necessary to do well. If you are interested in mythology then it is an amazing class, if not then this will probably be a long and boring semester. Participation affects grade

I took this class as on on-demand course. The quizzes were really easy and open note. There were 3 papers based on the major texts in the class. The papers aren't bad only 3 pages with clear prompts and TA sessions to help get you on the right track. This class also had lots of extra credit. The professor was very on top of grading.

Haney is BY FAR my favorite professor. He's the reason I am pursuing a degree in the Humanities. Only 3 exams in total and the papers don't take much time at all. He is also a VERY generous grader. You do not have to complete all the assigned readings, just do spark notes, and you'll be just fine! I cannot recommend him enough.

This was probably the second most boring subject through all my generals(right behind American heritage), and yet professor Haney is a fantastic professor that makes the class interesting. He cares about each of his students and gives extremely helpful, personal feedback for each student.

The only reason I give him a good rating is because he is a super nice guy. He genuinely cares about his students. Other than that, he didn't have much to work with. The humanities are boring except for some fun stories. Since most will have to take this class for GE, he is a safe bet. Although not my favorite, I have fond memories of this class.

Every lecture I attended helped me better understand what I needed to do or study for the class. He will send out weekly summaries of what is due that week which always helps if you are forgetful like me. There are quizzes over the readings and some questions form the quizzes will appear on the test. Overall, he did a great job.

Professor Haney is such a sweet, genuine guy. He really cares about his students and is so excited for lecture each day. His tests are lots of memorization, but the study guide prepares you well for it. He loves getting to know his students personally. Assignments did get redundant and the lectures got dry- but I would take it from him again.

Really interesting course. He knows so much. There is a LOT of information packed into the curriculum. This is one of those classes where you're really getting your money's worth. Fair amount of work. It was very manageable, you just had to be willing to sit down with a big stack of flash cards for the tests. He REALLY cares about his students.

This class wasn't the worst but I definitely did not look forward to it. Prof. Haney is very knowledgeable and a good teacher but is very boring. His lectures are jammed with a TON of information. He grades test and assignments very hard and are all written.

I really enjoyed this class. His lectures can be a bit mundane, but his knowledge of the humanities is amazing. Very straightforward grading criteria: no homework outside of readings, 2 essays, and 3 non-cumulative midterms. Very reasonable course, extremely nice professor, and a great learning experience. Would definitely recommend Prof. Haney.

Professor Haney was wonderful. He is full of knowledge and so excited to share it with his students. He definitely want his students to succeed, as he is willing to meet outside of class, gives great feedback, clearly states what he expects, and creates study guides that help prepare for the test perfectly. I'm so glad I took this class with him.

You're probably confused scrolling through the antithetical comments, so hopefully my perspective may add something. Dr. Haney is very kind. This class is for you if you are engaged by literature and are self-motivated. This class is not for you if you are easily bored by lectures and are likely to check out at the back of the room.

Not my favorite class. Really only 1 or 2 students in the class were fully engaged, rest were checked out. Very tough grader, readings not realistic to do for already busy students. Wouldn't recommend for someone that's not gifted for these type of classes.

Good professor but only 5 grades for the whole semester, although he says that varies each semester. 2 papers and 3 exams. A lot of information to know for the exams, the study guides are helpful but you have to have all the information yourself to fill them in and the essay questions are graded critically. Definitely not an easy GE option.

Wow. This class was so difficult. His study guides are SUPER vague and are not super helpful. He is a tough grader and expects you to know SO much! His tests are all memorization and regurgitation. The essays are hard too. Rubrics are not specific and then he destroys you. Not to mention it is SUPER BORING. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!

Professor Haney is one of the kindest and most understanding people. He is INCREDIBLY knowledgeable about the humanities. Tests require some studying/memorization. But if you study, you are guaranteed a decent grade. Professor Haney is a generous grader on both tests and papers. Overall, not too difficult or overwhelming. I loved this class!

Professor Haney has a contagious love for humanities. Very clear in his expectations and willing to meet with you outside of class. Put in the work, do the reading, participate in class, and you'll do just fine. Honestly, highly recommend him!

Professor Haney is a great person. Very approachable and kind. However, the class was one of the hardest I have ever sat through. This class is LECTURE HEAVY. I usually do really well paying attention in class but no matter what I never could focus during the whole class. Tests are insanely hard and come from very obscure places. find another class

Prof. Haney is a nice guy who is very knowledgeable about the IHUM 202 material. His lectures are jam packed with material. He is very willing to answer questions. His tests require you to know a lot of class material, and they are all written.

Haney is well-meaning and kind. The class requires quite a bit of work, but it is possible! The midterm and final made up 50% of your grade, but luckily there was a study guide of topics, dates, art, and lit to memorize. The lectures are hard to take notes on and can be overwhelming, but they are essential to your success. Study group suggested

Great guy, interesting lectures, tests memorization heavy, gives very comprehensive study guide. Would recommend taking this class if you want an interesting, averagely hard class where you learn a lot.

This class changed my life and that is only because of prof haney! I am not a humanities person-- at all-- however his passion and knowledge (seriously he is a walking encyclopedia) made it enjoyable. He is SO helpful and really cares about his students. Pay attention in class and really study the study guides he gives and you will do fine!

Professor Haney is a very caring and kind professor that tries to get to know the students. He is willing to meet outside of class. His lectures are good, since it's a history class there's a lot of information shared, but he certainly is very knowledgeable and helps you learn. Not very much reading until towards the end of the semester.

Prof. Haney is a very humble and likable guy who tried to learn all of the students' names. He had 3 exams which you really had to study hard for and take good notes in class. He also had 7 small papers and 1 big term paper. If you follow his feedback and get help from the TA, you'll do alright on these, but you have to work hard. I learned a lot!

Haney isn't bad- he obviously knows and loves what he's doing and wants to help, but the papers were kind of unclear as to what he was looking for and there were a looot of papers (one every other week and 3 others on top of that), not hard just a lot. Too much for a GE IMO. He also tends to rant rather than lecture so you never know what to know.

Grade based on attendance, two papers, and 3 tests (all easy). No busy work besides readings, which I probably only read half of. Class became much more enjoyable when I actually participated in the discussions. He is great-super nice, understanding, and passionate about hum. Study guides tell you everything on the tests and you can rewrite papers.

Helped me fall in love with the arts. He also touched on gospel principles often in class -- if you're paying attention. He shows how God's hand was in literature and artwork across the ages in Western Civilization. Focus during lectures, the tests will be based on lectures and what is in the study guide. Such a fun guy, you'll love him.

Professor Haney was an incredible professor. He made me want to learn more about Humanities. There were a few papers (2) and assessments (3) but the study guides and rubrics make it easy. Make sure to take good notes in class. Also, if you have a question or concern don't be afraid to talk to him. He's willing to help out and wants you to succeed.

Prof Haney is the BEST! He makes humanities easy and fun! The syllabus is very fair and outlined extremely well. He is very easy to reach outside of class and willing to work individually with students and the class as a whole if things needed to be cleared up or adjusted. Lectures are fun, readings easy, and study guides are great!

Don't take IHUM 201 from him if you want to learn about art--it was basically a Greek and Roman lit class. You read straight from the books during class. He is a great guy but not what I expected for Humanities. Tests can be tough as are not multiple choice.
Great professor that cares about his students. His lectures are entertaining and you will learn a lot. Study the guides he gives you before tests and you should do fine. Definitely recommended.

Highly recommended. He's passionate about his subject, and he really wants to give you the opportunity to make a personal connection with the content and learn it in full. The class discussions are interesting, and you actually learn something from them. To do well on assignments, express an interest in the content.

I went into this class sort of dragging my heels--I really thought it was going to be difficult and I wasn't interested in it at first.  Professor Haney completely changed my mentality.  In-class discussions were amazing, and he was so helpful when it came to projects and written tests.  There's lots of reading, but it's worth it.  GREAT CLASS!

Prof. Haney is a really great teacher who has a lot of knowledge about the subjects and has a real passion for his students and what they learn.  I like that he gets to know everyone's name. Very personable and lectures were almost always good.  I'd recommend the class to anyone.  Lots of reading, but most of it is pretty enjoyable

He is by far the best English teacher I have ever had! He is so cool! He was very willing to work with you. He structured the course on what the class needed not what the syllabus said.  I would recommend him to anyone! :D

He absolutely loves the subject, and it shows. Very flexible according to the needs of the class. Discussions were very fun. The only problem I had was that sometimes he would go on about ancient mythology/history assuming that we already knew as much as he did about it. Overall a very fun class and a very fun teacher.

I thought he was an amazing lecturer and made the lectures interesting which is good, considering I absolutely hate history classes and had to take this to fulfill one of my generals. He was unnecessarily tough on grading though, which was frustrating because very few of us were actually history majors.

This was his first time teaching the course so I felt the instructions on the projects were a bit vague but Dr. Jones is THE NICEST man. He was easy to work with and really caring. His class wasn't too hard- just take lots of notes during class and do the readings and you will have no problem.

I took this class instead of taking American Heritage and would absolutely recommend it to anyone with the same idea. This class was so interesting and Professor Jones is very engaging with his lectures. The tests are all written, but they weren't too bad if you know your stuff. Weekly quizzes aren't bad either. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

I cant say enough good things about Professor Jones. He teaches American History from all angles and truly dives into the material. His lectures are fascinating and he creates stimulating discussion. He cares about students, even after the class had ended I needed help with a University issue and he made time to meet with me. Take this class!

Dr. Jones is passionate and wants you to be passionate about history. He focuses on the minority and makes you think about history in a new way. He has a unique teaching style and makes you work for a good grade. There is one midterm, the final, a research project, and some quizzes. Lots of reading and interesting lectures. I loved his class.

I took this class for a GE and really don't like history, but I loved this class. His lectures are really interesting. There's a lot of reading, but his quizzes are pretty easy. Besides the quizzes, there's the midterm, a research project, and the final, and that's it. He really wants to help students succeed.

Prof. Jones is one of the best professors I have ever had. He places an emphasis on the minorities who are often more overlooked in American History and he talks a lot about what it was like for slaves. He does not gloss over things, but tells it for what it is. He is incredibly helpful and accommodating, and he really knows what he's teaching.

This was the first American History class I've actually enjoyed. Professor Jones is hilarious and he makes class fun. Tests are difficult but if you study hard you'll be fine. The project takes a ton of time but it can be fun if you choose something you like to do. I would really recommend this class!

He made the Doctrine and Covenants exciting. He specializes in Pre-Civil War American History and knows early church history SO well. My testimony grew SO much thanks to this class! Prof. Jones made all of the weird stuff in the D&C make sense and helped to humanize the people of the early church. Great lectures, tough tests, and memorization.

He knows a lot about American History and definitely brings a good discussion. However, every other Monday you have to take a five question quiz on a 50 page chapter. I found these slightly difficult because it was a lot of information to read and hard to remember everything. His tests are writing in class tests. I thought he graded fair.

Prof Jones is obviously an expert on many topics dealing with international relations and conflict.  The texts were engaging and he is always prepared for class.  It a shame that the university is letting him go.
This class was just okay for me. The lectures get pretty boring and it seems like he just plays roulette to decide on who gets what grade.

Do not take this class from Jones. His grading is incredibly arbitrary (even for a political science class) and he loves to play favorites with his students. Make sure you participate a ton and kiss up to him and you will have a chance at a good grade. Don't bother reading the text, but do go to class (despite how boring and pointless it seems).
Fun teacher but his tests involve too many "guess what I'm thinking" questions.

He is a nice guy who is a pretty good teacher.  He has very obvious biases, but I learned a lot.  Tests are too tough if you go to class and study in advance.  I would recommend this class for a Political Science elective.
He has a bias, but remains a good professor. lots of reading, but he covers what is needed in class. good class, not that hard.

Euro Security is interesting.  The readings are for learning; he tests your knowledge of security concepts and policies. He's not going to spoon feed you.  Be analytical and clear in the 5 papers and in exams.  Use him, he'll help up.  He's Welsh, so expect the European bias, but he is married to an American. Go to Class, it helps (mostly)!!!

Prof. Jones is a new at this job so he's still learning how to be a professor.  I really didn't learn much in this class--the material had been covered by many of my other Pl Sc electives.  Most of the time he's friendly, but  he can be downright mean when he's having a bad day.  He assigns TONS of readings but doesn't test you on them.

I never do reviews but I HAVE to hype Chris up! He is one of the best instructors I've ever had. He is very intelligent and eloquent but does not let that get in the way of him being kind and empathetic. He is very willing to work with you and make accommodations if you have any challenges. This course is well-organized and changed my life.

Guest speakers almost every week, but it is a 2 hour class and would often drag on a bit. Slightly unorganized. There is a LOT of reading, and you have to keep a reading journal. However, an overall interesting and easy A.

This course needs review. The way TAs grade in this course is unhelpful and often painful. It is set up so only a couple of students can get an A, and it is the most important class you can take in Political Science if you are looking to TA for future classes. Political Science professors will look at the grade you get in this class.

Honestly, I feel like this class was unnecessarily difficult. There was an huge amount of reading and your whole grade is based off a case assignment project and 2 exams, all of which were graded very harshly. That being said, Professor Krewson himself is great :)
He requires attendance for every class unlike most professors that allow you to have up to three absences. Does not post his slides. Very unclear expectations. Tests are very difficult.

Nice guy, but honestly the worst professor I've had in college. Does not care a bit about the success of his students. In lecture, all he cares about is pushing through the slides. His assignments are ambiguous and if you appeal anything he likely will never help you. If he's reading this, I genuinely hope he improves his teaching. Do not take.

Professor Krewson was a super nice and helpful guy! It's just a hard class. The grading was pretty harsh and took forever to get back. Quizzes sometimes asked the most obscure questions from the readings. Rubrics for assignments tended to be vague, so writing the essays was often difficult. Overall, though, I survived.

Krewson is a pretty good teacher-it's just the class in general that's rough. The grading is pretty harsh, but he does his best to explain the assignments and walk people through their questions. His office hours are really helpful-it's easier to get feedback when it's just one on one. I had to take this class, and I'm glad I took it from Krewson.

Make sure first week you get to know your TA because they are EVERYTHING. I had a hard time with mine, and I wish I had switched when I had the chance. Krewson is the best professor to take for this class. He was very bad cop first term good cop second, so doing stats and R studio second term felt easy by comparison.

The class is hard. Lots of reading and stats. Krewson teaches you to use R Studio which makes it harder than other professors that just use Excel (assuming you are more familiar with Excel than R). I still have assignments from early October that are not graded; but that's not Krewson's fault. More of TAs. Made it tough to apply feedback/grow.

Professor Krewson is amazing. He is super kind, responsive, and willing to help. He also tries to keep things relevant. POLI 200 is like a bootcamp, it is intense and a rite of passage. You also honestly have to advocate for yourself to get feedback and the grading is extremely slow, which is hard. I feel very lucky for my TA and Krewson though.

Not a huge fan. Rubrics for every essay and assignment were far too specific, which made it difficult to understand. The amount of "it must haves" was unusual, making it feel like I wasn't the one in charge of my own papers. Krewson is a kind man and offers good help, but the grading was far too strict, felt like working in a small box.

Well designed course. Every class, there's readings and a discussion board based on what you thought was interesting from the reading. No other assignments until after the midterm - then you write a Supreme Court opinion! Go to his office hours, he's very helpful. His tests are excessively tricky in my opinion so study. Would def recommend him!

Dr. Krewson is super nice and generally a chill guy. There was a ton of reading. And he is not the easiest grader, but you will learn a lot about the supreme court/ US court system so it's really good if you're wanting to go to law school or thinking about it.

Krewson is obviously very passionate about the classes he teaches. If you don't like to show up to class, this class is not for you because there are no excused absences. He made way for interesting class debates, which was more enriching than just discussing SCOTUS opinions, but his midterm and final can be pretty intense if you aren't prepared.

Professor Krewson is a really nice guy. It is obvious he cares about his students. I felt like this class really prepared me for law school. With that being said, if you are looking for an easy A poli sci elective, I would not take it. He is a tough grader, I did not get a 100 on a single assignment. No TAs, he grades everything himself. Great guy!

He's a really nice and genuine guy who seems to really enjoy what he's doing. There is a paper due every week, attendance is part of your grade, and the midterm and final are pretty intense. Prepare to memorize a lot of Supreme Court cases for tests. Readings are really important; you can't really skip them. Not bad, just intense sometimes.

Dr. Krewson is awesome. I ran into him outside of class and he took time out of his day to stop and talk despite being on his way out the door. He clearly cares about his students and is passionate about what he studies. I found the tests to be actually kind of difficult but there wasn't anything on them that we didn't go over at some point.

Really interesting readings and an awesome capstone project: we wrote SCOTUS opinions to an ongoing case. First half of the class is the basics of SCOTUS and the federal judiciary, second half is models for predicting judicial decisionmaking. Tests weren't too bad; just know the slides (he posts them). Super enthusiastic and wholesome guy.

Dr. Krewson got thrown in the deep end with my class, as it was his first time teaching the class, and our group was the biggest crew of bellyachers and whiners on campus. He handled the complaints and protesting well, and made sure to be available during office hours. It also didn't help that his TAs kept undermining him, but he handled it well.

POLI 200 is a hard class. But, Professor Krewson is probably the best teacher you can have for it. While the class is still difficult, he does his part to make it more manageable. He's very responsive if you need help and he's a nice guy.

Just be aware--for the first half of the semester you'll be writing a 5-page paper about every week.

Its hard to leave him a bad review because he is such a nice guy, but this class was very boring. I was so excited because the topic interests me, but the powerpoints put at least 5 people to sleep each class. The papers and tests aren't terrible, and he is flexible and willing to work with students with due dates. I learned a ton (in between naps)

Krewson honestly has so many good things he wants to share, and while I thought his tests were not written super well, this class is totally passable. The readings are genuinely interesting, and he's so passionate about the subject that it makes it all the more interesting. You'll never meet anyone else who loves the Supreme Court more.

While the class is certainly difficult, he is willing to go through everything with you. He is very respectful of students' inputs and opinions, and willing to change content and exams based on what students say. Fun and personable professor who is trying his best. Learned so much and am excited to take another class from him.

Professor Krewson is among BYU's best. He really knows his stuff, loves what he teaches, and relates to students very well. His class is challenging but reasonably so, and he is very accessible. Tests required you to study but never had any surprises. Reading was manageable and genuinely interesting. Great guy.
I really enjoyed this class. It was a great combination of work to lecture and every lecture I felt I learned a lot. 10/10 would recommend.

Alright here's the deal... this class had the potential to be awesome. Krewson is obsessed with data, especially his own research. The readings for class hit over 80 pages for each class hour. We had 2 papers due within a week of each other totaling 25ish pages and there were 2 tests. Took forever to grade. Class was death by powerpoint.
I withdrew from this class about a month into the semester because I would read the text book, come to class, and have the text book regurgitated to me.

Okay class but he just taught out of the textbook (no slides) and I feel like I didn't learn anything. The material isn't that hard to get a hold of but we had on average 80 pages to read before every class. Also, I never really felt like he actually answered anyone's questions

Dr. Smith is amazing. He cares deeply about music and wants to create beauty and a spiritual experience for everyone involved. He made music meaningful for me again! If you are on the fence about auditioning for the symphony, I highly recommend doing it. Be brave; you will not regret it!

Dr. Smith is an OUTSTANDING conductor, professor, and disciple. I was in the Symphony Orchestra and was wowed by the constant focus on the Savior and our personal refinement, as people and as musicians. He puts his whole soul in the music. AWESOME class!

Dr. Smith is an amazing conductor! Absolutely loved being a part of his orchestra. He leads with care and wants to help us produce amazing music. Right before concerts can understandably be a little more stressful, but the reward for working hard and listening pays off. Always looked forward to rehearsals with him!

Dr. Smith is so talented at conducting and describing music! Lots of rehearsal time/1.5hrs a week of practice (for strings) for only a 1 credit class. Assignments inlcude listening to the pieces, attending 1 sectional per concert, personal practice, and sometimes a recorded playing test. Music was challenging for me but this was my favorite class!

I love dad
-Gabriel
If you love music you will love this class. You have to listen to the music, practice, and go to class, but I loved the class. The music is hard tho, so you actually have to put in time to learn it.
I love Dr. Smith. You can tell he really loves his job and cares for the students. He does fun music and answers emails really fast. Highly recommend taking this class if you love music!

Dr. Smith is fun to work with. He is passionate about music and knows how to apply the music past the classroom. He will not tolerate phones and talking, so if you aren't able to be respectful, don't take this class. You are required to listen to the music, practice 1 hr every week, have two sectionals per concert.
This is a great class. Don't feel scared if you aren't a music major, you'll do well if you put in some practice. For a music instructor, he has a calm demeanor and was very inspiring.
Excellent musician and conductor. Will get stressed and frustrated if you don't prepare-- he can tell.

He's very passionate about music, and it's only polite to express appreciation for the passion. So don't goof around in class, and he will like you! He likes everyone. He's so nice and patient. He does kind of make a big deal out of the strings being important and everyone else not so much, which makes me kind of upset as a horn player. But oh well

Dr. Smith is an amazing person.  I don't think it is possible for him to get mad and he expects the bests from everybody.  The amount of patience he has in incredible and he respects all of his students.  Playing under him is a great experience.

Dr. Smith is a phenomenal conductor. He's one of the kindest people I've met and I would take another class from him in a heartbeat. (I took symphony orchestra). There was not a day of class that he was rude to us or that e took his anger out on us, and we were even stuck in a pit with him for 3+ hours every day. Dr. Smith is AWESOME.

He is such a good teacher. I don't think it is possible for this guy to lose his temper b/c he was always very chill in class and very respectful towards everyone. Loved learning conducting from him. I'd recommend anyone to take a class from him b/c he was one of the nicest teachers I've ever had at B.Y.U.
What a great guy! Band was awesome with this Dr. Smith. Likes to laugh, compliments a lot--one of my favorite professors.
This is a great class.  It's a little frustrating at first, but as you get into it, the class gets really fun.  Prof. Smith really knows what he is doing, and you learn a lot.

Fun class. It is hard if you have any conducting experience prior to this class, you will feel like you are conducting in a straight jacket. Just go with an open mind, and have fun. Bro. Smith is a lot of fun, and makes the class interesting, most of the time.
Take notes on his powerpoints in class. Read the textbook. It covers the things on the test. He has a strict appearance. He is, but he is really awesome
Hard, but entertaining. unfortunately it took me several years to discover that if one actually speaks to him, one may get ANYTHING clarified,

We went hiking every week. The thing is that i couldnt enjoy the hike because you have to take notes while he is speaking. It wasnt fun at all. Tests come from the book. So read it and memorize concepts.

Nice knowledgeable guy. Lots of people fell asleep during his lectures b/c lights off for powerpoint with no class involvement. Listen to lectures and you will do fine on the quizzes.  Tests are another story.  straight from the book, which he doesn't use. studying for the tests seems pointless until you see the test. I got 75-80 on tests.

He'll out hike any student any day.  He lives what he teaches, and is one of the best teachers I've ever known.  If you take his class, expect to learn a lot.  If you don't it's probably because you didn't put anything into it.  That's your fault not his.

He is a good professor.  The exams are a little tough. They tend to be process of elimination multiple choice rather then multiple choice where the answer jumps out at you.  You have to read the book, because he will test out of the book alot
Way cool teacher, loved the class

Great professor. Its a fairly easy class. You show up listen take some notes, take the blackboard quiz and then study for the tests. The tests do not come from the lecture but from the book, which you don't find out until test time. They are a little difficult, I usually got a B or a C without that much studying prob. like 2 hours.
Wrong.  His lectures are always horrible.  I would like to see him take one of his own exams.  He would probably be very confused by the wording.

At first the class seems like its going to be horrible, but then you listen to a few lectures and go to the labs and its pretty easy. Most of the lecture is not on the test but you need to go in order to take blackboard quizzes. Test or Midterms are mostly from the book and are fairly difficult, But he throws out about 5 questions each time.

He comes across as a tuff guy in the beginning but he's really a nice guy. He lectures every day and you MUST take notes everyday. He really makes a difficult class, not necissarily esay, but very bearable. I love his class.

Brother Clarke is one of the most amazing individuals I've ever met. Once a geologist for dirty oil companies, he has since 'retired' so that he could be a teacher at BYU, UVSC, and a local high school.  His classes were always interesting and his dry/witty sense of humour makes it über-entertaining.  I would sign up a class by him in a heartbe

I had this teacher for three years in high school and a semster at BYU, and I think he's great. Some students just don't seem to click with his teaching style; he may seem intimidating at first, but he's really a softy. He loves his students and is very willing to help. He is also really funny. No "Excalibur" in college to wake sleeping students...
The class was so boring I thought I was going to die. Plus he didn't explain anything so the labs were really hard. He's a nice guy but . . .
Mr. Clark's bark is worse than his bite. He really is a sweetheart. He is one of the most brilliant men I know, and I learned a lot in his class.

His lectures were very boring and powerpoint slides were taken from other teachers. Daily quizzes on blackboard are annoying but not tough. He curves EVERYTHING: daily quizzes, tests (no matter the average), even came close to curving the whole class. Listening to him talk is funny at first but obnoxious by the time you're finished.

Professor Callahan is one of my most favorite professors at BYU. I've taken multiple classes from him and I've learned so much from each one. The work load is easy but from the activities and class discussions you will truly understand and learn how to apply to content. HE IS AWESOME!

Super awesome guy, you can tell he cares about you and wants you to succeed. Just show up to class and do all the assignments with a little bit of effort and you'll learn a lot and get an A. 10/10 class, 10/10 professor.
Callahan was awesome and so kind and knowledgeable. Unfortunately comms 101 is pretty boring material and my class sucked at participating but he did his best to make it interesting. Stud.

Super awesome dude. Put in some effort and you'll get an A. Super nice and you could tell he really cared about each and every one of us. He learned everyone's name and I really appreciated that. 10/10 professor.

Professor Callahan is SPECTACULAR!!!! The Comms 101 class is well organized, and you are set up to win with the assignments, along with the midterm and final. Lectures are amazing and helpful. Its clear that he is passionate about what he teaches and that every lecture is original while still being able to teach the content efficiently.

He's awesome! I loved his lectures, they were very entertaining. We had a huge class but it felt small because he was good at relating to all of us. And don't be scared by the final project, it's not hard at all. The two tests (midterm and final) aren't too bad, the TA gave us a really good review in class. Highly recommend professor callahan!

Professor Callahan was an awesome teacher! My favorite thing is that all the coursework and lectures were very relevant to what you need to know - he doesn't waste your time with extra stuff! Classwork was very easy and lectures were entertaining! Tests are straightforward! Take this class from him!!!!!!! I 10/10 recommend.

Professor Callahan was sweet and funny. You can tell that he cares a lot about his students and is passionate about communications. The course content was very boring but he did his best to make the class engaging, so it wasn't painful to attend. As long as you do the assignments on time and make an effort for the papers the class is an easy A.

Callahan is one of the funniest professors I've ever had! His lectures were engaging, course work was easy and content was continually appealing to a wide variety of students. I cannot recommend him enough. Comms 101 was easily one of my favorite classes, and the two tests are really easy. Everything else relies on projects, which are laid out.

One of my favorite professors ever! The class was easy, engaging and insightful. He has look deeper into things  and see real world applications instead of just reading from the textbook. There are a couple projects and a group presentations but those were fine.

I cannot recommend Professor Callahan enough!

Prof. Callahan was so great!! He cares so much about his students, and many of us would stay after class just to talk to him. His content is genuinely so interesting and I feel like I learned more in this class than a lot of my classes in college. He's also HILARIOUS! He never fails to make his students smile. The work load is very manageable.

Callahan's class was MY FAVORITE! His lectures were entertaining and he does a great job of connecting with his students. The class is focused on using the content to "Create" and less on memorization. No exams, all super easy assignments that are as hard as you want to push yourself. Basically, you get an A if you do the assignment. SUPER FUN GUY!

The best professor! He's funny and cares about all his students. The class seemed very disorganized which I was worried about but it's nothing to stress about because even though it seems disorganized, what he takes for a grade is clear. The projects are awesome because you can do anything that interests you. Do NOT take from a different professor!

Prof Callahan was very passionate about this class and his lectures were engaging. He wanted students to dive deeper and be creative instead of just reading a textbook and taking quizzes, which showed in the class material. There were several open-ended projects (graded very easily) and 1 group presentation. Attendance not mandatory, no tests.

PROFESSOR CALLAHAN IS INCREDIBLE. PERIOD. He is so personable and is there to help you with anything that you need. I love that he stretches our creativity and allows us that freedom to tap into that part of education. He allows you to be creative and do whatever you feel is connecting to the class for the homework assignments. He cares so much!!!!

Dr Callahan was GREAT. He's so funny and sweet. Super easy class and teaches material in a not tedious way. Sometimes I felt the class could've been a bit harder but overall such a great class and if you need help outside of class he would've definitely help. he invited us all over for a bbq at the end of the term. awesome guy!
I love this man. He was so fun and made the class engaging.
Pro Callahan is so fun and truly cares about his students. Gave a great introduction into the journalism field and I really enjoyed completing the assignments!

Clark Callahan is the GEM of the Communications Department. He is focused on career readiness and his classes are easy and applicable. If you get the chance, you should absolutely take classes from him.

I adore him! He made every single student in the class feel like he truly cared that they were there. He had everyones names memorized within the first week even though we were wearing masks and he would acknowledge everyone! Not super work heavy and a very easy grader. Easily got an A just got showing up and doug the assignments on time!

Callahan is easily my favorite professor I have taken at BYU. I felt like he wanted me to succeed not only at BYU but in my future career and life. He is so genuine and fun. He starts every class with a dad joke and had us over for a BBQ. Take any class you can from him. YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT

Prof. Callahan is one of the nicest people ever! I loved him! He really made the class fun and easy. He wants you to succeed, so hell do whatever he can to help with that. He even likes having students come over to his house for a bbq

Clark is genuinely one of the best professors I know. Such a caring and kind person, he really wants all his students to succeed. He can be goofy but also knows a lot about Communications and overall is just the best ever. Take his classes. Or even better go on any study abroads that he goes on.

Professor Clark was phenomenal. He was hilarious and made lectures interesting! He could get off topic at times so it was important that students participate and keep him on task. I have never had a professor care more about his students than Clark. He graded fairly and the workload was very manageable! Class was fun when the students participated!

Prof. Callahan loves his students. He wants to do everything he can to help them through his class. Listen to him in his lectures and do the reading (just highlight the bold parts) and you will get an A. Hands down, best teacher I've ever had.
He is awesome! Will work with you and makes you feel welcomed. I would recommend you take comms 238 from him!

Really cool guy, easy class if you just show up and do a bit of reading/homework. A must-have class if you're interested in any communications major. Take it and you'll see what you can do with it. He's the best, take him if you can.
Comms 101 with him was way easy. Only a few essay assignments and the tests were pretty straightforward if you went to class and listened. Expect reading from the textbook every week.

Absolutely Amazing!!! Greatest professor I have had at BYU. He was helpful beyond belief and always helped you make sure you got a solid "A" MUST TAKE THIS CLASS! its entertaining and informative!  You wont regret it!!!

COMMS101 was a super easy and enjoyable class, and Professor Callahan is great. He's really clear about what you need to do to get an A, and as long as you try (do the readings, spend time on the papers) you will do well in the class. He's a funny guy and really cares about his students.

I absolutely recommend you take a class from him. Such a helpful (and easy) professor. Lectures were engaging. Easy grader. I quote: "If your essay has a solid thesis statement, you will get at least a B." Grades on general concepts, not meaningless specifics. He will answer any question you have and you know exactly what to expect. Great teacher.

Professor Callahan is seriously the best. He is so helpful with tests and quizzes, midterms weren't bad at all, just wants you to be honest in your reading and he will help you get a good grade. Shows lots of videos in class, lots of real-world application. Highly recommend.

I was expecting the class to be really time consuming and stressful, but COMMS 101 turned out to be one of my easiest classes and caused very little stress. Professor Callahan is very aware that students really desireneed an A--or at least a good grade--to be admitted into the Communications department, so he does his best to help you succeed.

Callahan is great!  I loved him and his class.  It was an easy A as long as you tried.  I literally didn't study for the midterm and got 100%, & only studied for 45 minutes for the final and got a high A.  There are 4 projects dealing with typography, color, etc. that you have to do throughout the semester & a final one, but they aren't difficult.

Callahan is a stud. Had no interest in this class before, but he made it very enjoyable to attend. That being said, the class is cake as long as you go on days when there are quizzes. I was missing a few quizzes at the end of the semester and he met with me and we were able to work out a fair agreement. Take ANY class from him.

Callahan is the man. For real. Loved everything about the class. The assignments are interesting, and the lectures are engaging. You want to go to class. For real. Callahan cares about his students and really understands the pressures they face as college students. He's always working to help you out.

Well-versed in the material, and teaches in a way relatable, engaging style that makes me look forward to each class. He has a huge amount of knowledge of theory and communications history. Plus, he genuinely cares about each student and their growth. What an amazing teacher!
Dr. Callahan is like the BEST! He's smart, nice, and funny! His class is totes great and really interesting. I highly recommend him as a professor! My fave professor and class of the semester! :)
Great teacher. Brilliant writer. Valuable class.
Callahan is the man. He does things the right way. Wish all were like him.

This was a fantastic class. Yes, it was at 9am during spring term, but I wanted to come to class every day. We had interesting discussions and he applied the topics to the world and made them relevant. Not to mention, he cared about all of us in the class.
Take every class you can from this man! Best professor at BYU.

Brother Callahan is the best! He truly wants to help you succeed. Class is not boring he is always talking about new technology and how it's affect our society. Really interesting. I'm taking more classes from him!
Very very good class
This class is only hard in the sense that you think it will be way easy and then all of a sudden you realize youre getting an A- just bc you barely read the text.

Callahan is the best! I loved going to his class. He gets to know his students personally and truly cares about how they are doing. He wants everyone to get an A and will help you out! Very approachable and a great professor! Definitely take his class!

Dr. Callahan is one of the best professors at BYU. He teaches only what is applicable and useful to you. he is fair in his grading and truly cares about his students and his interests.I have done well in all of my classes with him. He assigns presentations that make you think outside the box and prepare you for future presentations.

Callahan is by far the best professor in the COMMS dept. He cares about the students learning-not memorizing. He is understanding and knowledgeable about the topic and he applies everything to real life. Take him-you won't regret it.

Professor Callahan is a must take if you are a comms major at BYU. He cares about you learning and growing not if you memorize. He cares about his students and is very approachable. Great professor and great class.
Great teacher. Very fun and personable. He doesn't try to trick you. He is very fair.
Clark Callahan is a great professor, very clear about his expectations and doesn't try to trick you. He wants his students to succeed and helps them in whatever ways he can.

He is a mother! Seriously! His grading is very fair, the reading is always on Blackboard (no books needed), and he is really concerned about you learning, not memorizing. His classes are fun, and he is open to suggestions and questions. He even schedules a day in the semester to review your grades with you, so you can make up for lost points.
Callahan is a great guy. He has really interesting insights. A fair class.
One of the best teachers in the communications department.  He is fun and smart.  He always helped me and made sure everyone got a reasonable grade

Callahan is the best teacher you could ask for.  He informs you of all information that you'd need to know for the midterm and final exam.  He made class very interesting and created inside jokes with the class.  He'll help you after you leave his class in applying to the program as well.  MOST HELPFUL AND FUN TEACHER I'VE HAD AT BYU!!!

One of my favorite teachers by far. Class was always entertaining, everything you learn is relevant, the tests were easy and he learned everyone's names and joked with us all the time. Even when he got off topic, it related to the class somehow. Actually makes you love going to class. ABSOLUTELY recommend Callahan!!

Great professor.  Always helpful and encouraging to his students.  Is approachable with any problem or question, etc. Class was a bit small, but he made it interesting.  Would highly recommend taking from him.  Great guy and professor.

Favorite teacher I have had at BYU. She finds your learning style, and the teaches that way. She cares about your improvement and gives very clear advice about how to improve. She is demanding as a teacher, but she is also very nice. I would highly recommend taking viola lessons from her, if you have the opportunity.
Clear, demanding, and intense. She really cares about you as a person and does not see you as just another student. She is flexible, but expects for you to be giving the class no less than your all.

Sis. Bigelow is great!! She helps with everything and most of the time she is really kind. I recommend her for any class because she is easy to work with. Sometimes I felt like she didn't try to get to know me well, but overall, she's a good teacher.

He is a really awesome professor! I took his KOR315 class (Sino-Korean workshop) and loved it! The expectations for his class are very specific, which is nice, and you learn the level 8, 7, and 6 Chinese characters (tot. 300). He really knows his stuff and makes it easy to remember all the characters

I didn't know any Hanja before this class and now I know several hundred. There is a lot of homework and the textbooks were used, but aside form that it's not too bad. Professor Parker knows what he is talking about and he cares about the students.

Dr. Parker is a funny guy who is passionate about Korea and knows a ton. He has worked with Korea and the language his whole life since his mission. I took the Sino-Korean class from him (Hanja) and really liked it. I knew like 4 characters before the class but now I know several hundred. I am going to take another class from him.

He allows you a whole 8.5x11 sheet of notes on Exams; every exam is online with basically no time limit, and his test review slides contain the answers to any question you'll see on the exam. I literally didn't study anything but his review slides and got an A on every test. Also, an A is a 92%. Took it summer semester, so could be different.

I took 106 during the summer semester, and it was by far the easiest option. Exams were all online with basically no time limit; you were allowed a whole 8.5x11 sheet of notes, and his exam review slides contained every answer to the test questions. I literally didn't study anything else and got an A on every test.

I think he's improved since the last reviews. He uses mnemonics and his slides' visuals quite well, so I understood concepts well, though sometimes he rushed the slides. TA hours are every weekday and plentiful, he stays after class to answer questions, I loved the practice questions (wish there were more!), and the online homework was great
Clint, where do I even begin? This is by far THE BEST and most doable option for physics 106. Use all of the resources he gives you for the exam and you will get an A without having to stress.

Professor Goldman is easily the best option for physics. Don't listen to the other reviews. Very approachable guy. 3 tests + a final. All the exams are online and you get a note sheet and equation sheet.
Terrible class. This guys office hours consisted of the 10 minutes after class, because he had a high-school class he had to hurry and go teach. Seriously. Poor lecturer. Bad tests.
I rarely write reviews. Nice guy. I'm not going to say much more. Read the rest of the reviews.

The slides aren't his and it shows. A kind guy but he's a high school physics teacher and it seems he isn't as capable as teaching a college level class. Won't share the slides till after class even though he gives no time to write them down during class

I asked him for help because so many concepts weren't clear and he said that his time was tight, and that I should just use youtube and read the textbook. He is not accessible outside of the two hours once a week during class. Instead of working through problems in front of you, he just rapidly talks through what he'd do mathematically. Not helpful

This class will set you up for failure. It's taught as if you've learned all of the concepts previously and come to lecture for a light review. I believe Mr. Goldman knows his stuff, but it's another thing to be able to teach it. His slides, exams, and homework come from another professor and he has a hard time being able to explain it.

This seems to be a side gig of him. He doesn't make his own slides, homework, or tests. He is frequently confused by problems that students ask him and he doesn't know how to explain things clearly. The only time he spends on this class is his time in lecture--he does not have office hours and has no TA. You're not set up to succeed in this class.

Don't do it if you actually want to learn the material! Once a week is tempting, but he is not available outside of those 2 hours at all, there is no TA, and he won't record lectures so people come to class, so you can't review things that he talked about--if you don't pick it up immediately in class, you really have no hope of getting it.

I felt like Clint really knew his stuff, I think the class is just difficult. It's once a week in salt lake so you don't have as much exposure as you would in a mon, wed, fri class. Sometimes he explains things as if you've already had physics before. He's a really nice guy, just be specific with him when you need something clarified.

Physics is hard but if you were take from anyone, take from Professor Goldman. There are 6 tests and a final that aren't too bad (I am not a math person btw). They are online and you get to have a note sheet with you (game changer). There are weekly homework assignments that are also online. If you go to class and do the work you will do great.

Dr. Guymon is the most caring person ever. He will do everything to help you succeed and is willing to communicate. He listens and is willing to apply your feedback. He is fair, kind, and just a great example of what a BYU teacher should be. By this point, you know ChemE classes are hard, that won't change. He makes it 100% reasonable.

This is a lab class, so much more hands-on and self-directed with very little lecturing. He was always there though and willing to help when needed. He knows his students by name. He is super inspirational and loves teaching/being here at BYU.
Clint is super helpful and cares about students' progress. He will do all he can to accommodate needs.
Great course, Clint knows his stuff!! There were some super heavy readings, but he is considering writing his own textbook to fix that.

Dr. Guymon is the best. Never met a professor that cares as much about us students as he does. He might not be the best lecturer of all time, but he is always willing to improve and listening to our feedback and actively changing to help us succeed. He is exactly what I would hope every college professor is like.

Dr Guymon really wants to help you succeed, but the department did him dirty with this course. He's still trying to find the perfect curriculum, so the lectures tend to be less than helpful. The pre-class doesn't directly help, so get ready to do your own research on syntax and use AI to help you understand.
Watch out for the exams

Guymon cares for his students. His exams were 2-3 problems that were semi based on the homework but frequently required applications never seen before. Dr. Guymon is probably the most caring professor I have ever had. He is so willing to help! Lecture sometimes felt a little long and HW sometimes was a little disconnected from class, but he was always open to feedback and changed to meet our needs! There is a lot of reading in this class. Dr. Guymon is new, but he truly cares about us! He shows so much love and care for the class, and loves teaching. I had no coding knowledge, the class was hard, but doable. Dr. Whipple uses a discussion-based teaching style and organizes the course around philosophy readings. Dr Whipple is a great professor who is very passionate about what he does. It was great to learn more about local plans and I really enjoyed his lectures! He is very helpful and it's easy to see that he cares about his students. Very fair in his grading and the pop quizzes didn't actually end up affecting our grades ;)

Dr. Whipple is awful, he treats students like they are all ignorant and asks the most simplistic questions in class. It felt like a junior high class and the lectures were extremely boring and repetitive. On the other hand, he requires huge reading assignments to be completed beforehand and often has detailed pop quizzes on the readings.

This man made the history of banking regulation the most interesting 3 weeks of the semester. I actually took Colby for 453 and 409, both awesome classes. Just an all around great dude. If he ever left I'm pretty sure the finance students would actually riot. If I ever did college again I'd just take everything I could from him.

I actually took MBA 609 from Colby, but it wouldn't let me select that course number. Colby is freaking awesome and one of my favorite professors ever. I would highly recommend any class you can take from him.

I absolutely loved this class. One of the best professors I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. He made every concept so applicable to real life and he really cares about connecting with each student on a meaningful level. Cannot recommend Colby enough.

Colby might be the best professor at BYU. He genuinely cares about each one of his students, makes the class fun, and does an amazing job explaining macrotrends. The class itself is quite easy if you show up and just study for the at home tests (I didn't). If Colby could teach all the finance classes, I would gladly accept.

Colby does a good job of keeping lectures engaging and relevant. He focuses more on helping students learn rather than teaching content. The exams come from lectures, so you have to understand what's talked about in class. He also integrates Christ into class.

The most REAL professor I've had. Says things how they are with love and passion. He's doesn't normally teach 410 but  only two tests with no homework. So gotta get good test scores. There is weekly readings but nothing is reported. Id highly recommend Colby. Attendance is not required but id highly recommend going to ever class!

I actually took FIN409 with him, but didn't see the class listed. Colby is awesome. Everything you could ask for. Spiritually uplifting, engaging lectures, minimal out of class work, easy grader. Super good guy, would recommend his classes to anyone.

Great professor and amazing testimony. I we\as spiritually uplifted by his spiritual thought every day. Reading textbook is required bc of quizzes but his lectures are the most important thing. Record them and re-listen to them. Take good notes! I would recommend him to anybody for this class. An A is attainable with good studying!
Absolute beast. Favorite class of the entire Finance program

Loved him for this class! I feel like he really cared about the practical knowledge and understanding that we needed on the topic. Didn't teach the heavy math part, mostly focused on the concepts. His spiritual thoughts at the beginning of class were the most uplifting part of my week! Highly recommend taking any class from him!!

I actually took FIN410 with Colby. The most amazing, spiritual powerhouse, hilarious and intelligent man! You can feel his love each and every day in class. I loved taking this class from him because he just wanted us to learn stuff. If you don't take a class with him, you are doing yourself a GREAT disservice. Colby is one of the greatest at BYU!!

I love professor Wright, he is the best professor I've had a BYU. The material is fascinating and he teaches in a way that makes you excited to learn more the next class. He is hilarious and teaches with stories and jokes and overall makes class incredibly entertaining. It is test heavy, but they are very doable. Definitely take this class with him

This class is very difficult, but fair. Dr. Wright's lectures are very important to understand if you want to do well in the class. Dr. Wright did a good job of connecting the overarching class themes to practical application. This is a 400-level class for sure, even if it is more 10,000 ft. view than other Junior Core classes.

Colby was probably my favorite professor I've ever had. He is the kind of person that I just wanted to hang out with and talk to. He's super scholarly which I respected him for and has so much depth that makes his lectures more than just the bare bones of a curriculum that you might get with another professor. He's grrrrrreat!

The best professor I've had at BYU. I've taken two classes from him, and he never fails to make a subject as vanilla as finance entertaining. His lectures draw you in, and I've learned more about real-world application here than anywhere else. His class really prepares you, and isn't too difficult (although its not a pushover class either)

Colby is very nice and knowledgeable. However, it wasn't the best class I have ever taken. I feel like I would forget 80% of what I learned in the next few weeks. I also believe the experience would have been so much better if it wasn't online.

Colby is the best professor I have ever had. He teaches the material in a way that is so interesting. He genuinely cares for his students. I can guarantee you will laugh in every lecture and leave feeling uplifted everyday.

Colby is such a bro. This was one of the easiest classes Ive taken at BYU. There are some easy assignments that dont require too much time and a midterm and a final. If you record his lectures and listen to them before the tests you will be fine. One of the most entertaining and least time consuming classes Ive taken.

You'll enjoy going to Colby's class which is nice. The economic indicator presentations were way too long from the class members, so hopefully those get adjusted. Not extremely hard if you put effort in to the course, but its an easy class to not put effort in to for some reason. I will remember Colby's antics more than the class material.

Colby is by far my favorite professor at BYU. His lectures are hilarious and he teaches the material so well. He really cares about his students and makes it very obvious. The material isn't easy, but definitely doable if you work hard.

Colby is my favorite professor at BYU. His lectures are super entertaining and he knows how to keep the class hooked. On top of that he is such a genuine person. He is super considerate and gives great spiritual thoughts and personal anecdotes. Class is farily easy too, especially comapred to Fin 401.

What is there to say? He is candid, genuine, and the most honest person in the state of Utah. He won't sugar coat anything for you like some other BYU professors, and you should appreciate that. Take 453 from Colby, no question.

Colbys lectures were engaging, energizing, and creative! His class had 2-3 papers (last was optional), 3 test, and reading quizzes. Colby communicates clearly what to expect for individual assignments, test, his class, and the finance program; I appreciated that. He is a great guy and loves his students dont miss the opportunity to take his class

Colby is brilliant. Loves his class, loves the students, loves the material. Natural born teacher. Probably the best professor I've ever had. Material isn't terribly tough, pay attention in lectures and pay attention while you read. Truly inspirational professor. 3 papers, lots of online quizzes of escalating difficulty, three tests.

Professor Wright is one of the professors who make school worth it. The class is pretty hard but if you study and ask questions, you can do it. Dr. Wright's tests are fair and clear, but they are very lecture-based, so take good notes and pay attention. He'll take you out to pizza if the Cubs win.

Colby is an amazing professor. He tells stories during class that will keep you hooked. He's genuinely interested in your success so go visit him during office hours if you want one-on-one help. Fin 453 has a lot of reading and you have to pay attention in class. Tests are from readings and lectures, and he doesn't use powerpoints.

The only professor who received a standing ovation from our class at the end of the semester.  Colby is the man.  Colby cares so much and it shows in his lectures.  He is amazing.  Definitely take every class you can from him.

Colby is an amazing professor. He is a very tough grader and you need to listen to his  lectures word for word because random things pop up on his exams that you would never think would. He is caring and hilarious. He's not the easiest to get in contact with due to him having a lot of responsibility in the Finance program.
No powerpoints were used which was amazing.  The professor is very clear and holds his students in the highest regard.  He compares his students to those attending Harvard, Stanford, and Yale.

Professor Wright was the best teacher I have had at any level in my educational career. The class subject matter was already interesting to me, but he kept me on the edge of my seat the entire semester. Great lecturer, great person, very funny, and he brought in life and gospel lessons to the class when appropriate.

A professor who sincerely cares not only about students passing, but about student's lives. Fantastic class, excellent professor.  You will not regret knowing Professor Wright. Spiritual, motivational, inspiring, and very smart!

Best professor not just in the Marriott School, but at BYU. This class would be extremely boring if he didn't teach it. He is very funny, and is very good at explaining the material. Highly recommend taking his class
Simply incredible.  This class could have been really boring, but Dr. Wright made it the best class I had last semester.

Best professor I have had at BYU. He really opens your mind to new ideas. He explains everything very well to help you understand. Tests are very fair. Lectures are very interesting! I highly recommend taking a class from Dr. Wright!

Dr. Wright is the best teacher I have ever had. I wish I could continue taking classes from him because he is so good at explaining and helping you remember - and he doesn't kill you with boring slides. He is incredibly smart and extremely humble. He was born for this. I would recommend any class he teaches.

Dr. Wright is the best professor and lecturer I have ever had. He cares so much about his students and gives so much clarity to what could be a confusing topic. Take EVERY AND ANY class offered by him! If you read and go to class, you can get an A. He is very personable, which makes the class even more enjoyable. He is the man!

I've never wanted to avoid a class more than this one. Her demeanor and comments made many of us feel uncomfortable. The lectures felt excruciating, boring, and repetitive. She was really sweet, and always listened to everyone's views. Her class is fairly easy with only a few readings each week. There were a few assignments that weren't clear, but if asked about it she would explain deeper! Just become her friend, and this class will be a blast.

Professor Cole talks to you like a child. If your opinion is different then hers, you are most likely wrong because she is convinced only hers can be right.The work is very confusing and mostly busy work. You have reading checks too that have nothing to do with the class or coursework.

There aren't a ton of class discussions more presentations. But I loved Collin's insights and all the artists he brought as guests. You do wait to know your grade until the very end but if you're honest and work hard it's fine. I was willing to give myself grades other than A's in the self assessments when I felt I deserved it and I ended with an A

Collin tends to go off on tangents a lot, and isn't very organized on Learning Suite. Be prepared to see most of your grades posted on the last day possible (the grade submission deadline after the semester ends). Your grade is based off self-evaluations but I wish we could have known our official grades within a reasonable time of submitting them.

He is the nicest guy, and does everything he can to work with you. You'll struggle unless you ask questions in class. Hands-on lectures with code demonstrations, but it can be hard to hear due to talking. Practice concepts before class to not get lost. Novice professor who's learning to teach, but he's really knowledgable. Do quizzes and homework right after learning it - so much easier! He stayed after class to help. Very willing to help!
The projects are hard but he does a good Julie helping and is willing to work with you
Helpful if you see him 1 on 1 but not the best at explaining things to large groups in lecture. Very nice and dedicated professor

Professor Flake was always able to answer my questions when something wasn't quite working in my code. I fi brought it to him we would work together to figure it out. The content is also taught by showing how to do the concepts talked about, which was very beneficial for me.

Prof. Flake did an amazing job as his first semester of teaching. He cares about the students learning and comprehension. I wish we would've taken the steps to understand navigation in each of the sites first before diving into using them. Other than that, he and the TA's do a great job with this class.

He's a really good guy and super accommodating and understanding. It was his first semester teaching so it took him time to get used to lectures but he improved a lot and he also knows information systems really well. Overall: dawg.

I took Professor Flake in his first-semester teaching. He was inexperienced in teaching at first as expected but improved greatly with time. He is a very caring guy that knows his stuff. IS 201 is a hard skills class but he was always willing to help and answer your specific questions. TAs are also super helpful. Overall good class.

I had him his first semester teaching. He was very accommodating the class was super intuitive and if I had questions I could reach him in or out of class.  His class follows the textbook closely which is super nice if you miss anything you can pick it up later without falling behind. Often the online textbook was more helpful than the lectures.

It was Professor Flake's first time teaching which made it a little hard to follow along with him during the lectures. He is very willing to help his students and there are a few extra credit opportunites. MyEducator had helpful videos to help you understand concepts that weren't explained as well in class.
