However, all that knowledge comes at a price. This is by far the hardest religion class I've ever taken at BYU, and as a person I find him a bit arrogant and condescending.

unable to answer any questions about D&C doctrine. EXTREMELY condescending, not approachable at all. Don't comment in class, or you'll be personally attacked. Paper is a joke. Every class he tries to literally go through 100+ slides, only ever gets to half of them. Disorganized. Pointless. Devoid of all light. You name it. avoid like the plague.

He's such a nice man and is always accommodating when you go to him. His classes seemed long because we never got through all the material and often times, his comments or discussion seemed rather unrelated to the first half of D&C. He's very knowledgeable on the material he teaches but I think his excitement for said material causes him to tangent
Good professor. Well organized class. Very knowledgeable about D&C and Church history. Cares about his students. I recommend him.
He will work with you very well.

Bro Manscill was my favorite religion teacher, his test were very fair as well as the grading of them. After the tests were done he would go through comonly missed problems and ended up giving credit to everyone for the most commonly missed ones. GO TO THE TA REVIEW the TA literally gave the answers that were on the test, go and take good notes.

I really loved this class.  Bro Manscill knows a ton about the D&C and he loves teaching it.  You just need to listen in class, take notes, and go to the TA reviews to do well in the class.  It is a little harder than your average religion class, but he is very interesting to listen to.  I recommend this class.

This was the hardest Religion class I hav taken at BYU, 1/4th of test questions were his interpretation on scriptures. He cares about his students but tries to teach too much in the class he doesn't get through half of his slide and expects you to study them to get a good grade. My advise do not take from Bro. Manscil his class is no good!

This was the worst religion teacher I have ever taken, his test are ridiculously hard! He doesn't teach about 1/4th of the test and if you don't go to the review session you will miss those questions. you have to write a 3 page paper, and give a class project. He expects way too much for a religion class! be smarter then I was and don't take him.

Bro. Manscill knows a TON about D&C. Exams were closed scripture and extremely hard with specific detail (like matching verses, names of sections, people present, dates, places). More of a history exam than anything else. Pop reading quizzes in class. Go to the TA test reviews. Take good notes in class since powerpoints are useless for exams.
I hear he has a new TA that has revamped the tests and even does reviews.  Basically tells you all the answers for the tests.  He TA'd in the summer and was super helpful.
Did not enjoy this class at all, would never suggest it to anyone. He is condescending and class was not fun to go to.

His class is super boring. It was hard taking it in the morning because I couldn't stay awake. You focus more on worthless facts during the class then actually feeling the spirit and you are tested on a lot of little details that you have to memorize from his slides. Didn't like the class very much.
Nice guy, strong testimony, TERRIBLE tests and quizzes. Dont take this guy.

Great professor. He really cares about your grade and your success. Tests are fairly difficult, but he allows you to use notes/scriptures on them. If you use them, you'll do fine. If not you'll fail. But he won't allow you to fail. One of the best professors here.

Bro. Manscill is the best religion teacher I have had so far. He is so funny and really kind. He makes it a point to get to know everyone in the class (he made a video the first day with us all saying our names and where we were from into the camera...ha) Class was easy and really interesting.

Those who want to be edified, don't take this class. He encourages shady discussion, disagrees with modern revelation, and tries to get you to buy like 4 extra books. My guard always goes up in this class, because I just don't believe him. I don't feel like I'm learning much except a few random facts, and lectures too quickly to take good notes.

Nice guy, though he sometimes comes off as arrogant.  Terrible at lecturing.  Doesn't complete his sentences and mixes up names/pronouns, which makes him very confusing.  Also, several times I've heard him teach things that were totally wrong.  Quizzes are very difficult, though he's lenient on the answers.  Tests are hard, also.  Don't take him.

He is a great guy but a not such a great professor. He would have us read, and quiz us but what he decided was the right answer was not usually what the readings had told us the right answer. I took him for OT and he always had to be corrected on his information, I don't feel he knows the Old Testament as well as he should to teach it.

Manscill is very knowledgeable, but he is also very out of touch with the needs and wants of his students. If you take this class, keep in mind that it is about HIM and HIS knowledge, not about what you learn. Very frustrating professor--and impossible tests that he HAD to curve or else everyone would have failed. If you have a choice, do not take.

do not take him.  He had so much information he would rush every time we had class.  you dont really know what he will put on the tests.  He is boring and his powepoints have so much info on them its ridiculose

this class was ok.  His powepoint slides were over the top and every class period I felt like he was rushing through to get all the information.  ok guy, bad class if you can take it from someone else
Quizzes are ridiculous. Lectures are really boring, trite, and not very uplifting. Test was fine. Not that nice of a guy.
Don't take him. Boring.
All of his questions are from out in "left field." Nice person, but I would suggest someone else as your teacher.
He's a good guy, knows his stuff. But he is a poor lecturer. He doesn't finish thoughts and is often confusing. I don't recommend this professor.

What are people talking about in those nagative previous comments? He deserves better feedback. He is very amiable and is willing to help students. The only problem is being able to catch him- very busy. He is very intelligent and you'll do well if you dig into the D&C. Recommend- take Church History at the same time, you'll be better off.
Not a bad class! I thought it would be a miserable class because of the comments I've read. But Dr. Manscill did not reflect what I've read.
i actually really enjoyed this class...i'm suprised at so many negative comments...i felt it was well taught and uplifting...i learned a lot and did well in the class...

I wish i had enjoyed this class more. i was really excited about it but was terribly let down.  i felt that doctrine was pushed aside to learn about marginally interesting and arbitrary facts about the apostles.  i wish i had felt uplifted at all during lectures. Manscill wont be recommended by me.

I didn't enjoy this class at all. I agree completely with most of the comments here. He's a good guy, but a little full of himself and his tests are ridiculous. You're not free to ask an intellectually honest question because of the teacher's personality. I had a really hard time sitting through class and being uplifted.

I expected D&C class to help me develop helpful study habits and interest. Turns out, I'm just required to memorize his own pseudo-doctrine, guess on tests (he never talked about half the material), and put up with his ego-centric nature. Nothing in this class has actually been applicable or insightful. I strongly recommend: DO NOT TAKE MANSCILL!!!
Pretty easy going guy who is more than willing to work with you and a fairly easy class for D&C. I recommend him.

Take as many classes from Dr C as possible. Not too hard, just follow the instructions... and if you enjoy dry humor you will love him. He tries really hard to make you understand the material and he really cares about his students.
Must attend every class! He's a good teacher but he's very strict on his grading. He won't give you any free points! If you really want to learn the material, I think he's good.
Clear instruction, if you put in the hours he tells you to, you can learn it and get an A.  But it really does take 12 hours of study to prepare for a test.

This class was OK. Dr. Tree didn't require a lot. I don't think I learned a lot, but Dr. Tree really cares if we do well on his exams. His exams are pretty easy/ If you pay attention at all you'll do just fine.
Dr. Tree is an amazing professor. The class was a lot of work, but there are a ton of resources to help. Overall I loved the class. 10/10

Dr. Tree is a good teacher.  He really wants to drill only a few concepts into the student's minds. ... At least in 321.  If you couldn't easily explain how to do every single HW problem, you're going to get rocked.  It's that simple.  If you know your stuff, the tests aren't that bad.  If you're understanding is lacking, you'll fail exams.
Great teacher, care's about his students. I would take this class again and more classes from him. He is a fun teacher and keeps you interested.
Awesome Professor!  I loved thermodynamics from him and hope to take him for more classes.  He is very fair with tests and homework and very clear in his teaching
Dr tree is an awesome teacher.  He knows the material extremely well.  The homework assignments are due once a week and takes some time.  Study the homework and class notes to do well on the tests.

I'd take a bullet for Dr. Tree. The class was superbly taught, he had fair grading procedures, and was extremely helpful in person. Homework load is generally moderate depending on how well you understand the material. Exams are thorough but fair. Don't take Thermo from anyone else!

Great class! Great Prof. He probably more invested in helping students learn than any other professor, but you have to put forth the effort.  I liked him so much I took his fluids class (ME 312), internal combustion engines class (ME 425), and his intermediate thermo class (ME 521).  IC Engines was awesome.

Took Thermodynamics from him.  Loved the class, and his teaching style.  It's challenging, but you will learn a lot.  He is a reasonable teacher who is really interested in the success of each student.  I would highly recommend him.

Great teacher, really cares about his students.  Make sure you go to class and pay attention, he does a bunch of quizzes but always lets you know ahead of time what you should know.  Homework is pretty resonable and if you do it all you will do well in the class.
I took Internal Combustions from him and I really enjoyed the class. At times the homework wasn't clear as far as what to do, but he always clarified it and helped as much as possible.
Great teacher

This class on Internal combustion engines was great.  I appreciated Dr. Tree being a friend to everyone in the class.  I felt like I could ask even dumb answers and get a detailed response.  His true love is Diesel engines.  He even was willing to give advice on grad schools, programs, etc.
Great teacher. Gives resonible tests and the right amout of homework.
Clear teaching style. Recommend.
Finally an ME teacher that cares!!  Was very concerned about his students and gave individual attention.  Made class fun too.

Professor Hatch had great lectures, and I felt like I learned a lot in the class. Deadlines for assignments would change on occasion when he had to travel for work (he's adjunct faculty), which was a little frustrating, but it would always be in our favor - gave us more time to complete an assignment. I would take his class again.

Professor Hatch had great lectures, and I felt like I learned a lot in the class. Deadlines for assignments would change on occasion when he had to travel for work (he's adjunct faculty), which was a little frustrating, but it would always be in our favor - gave us more time to complete an assignment. I would take his class again.
Disengaging, self interpreted, and heavy lectures. Professor uses personal knowledge and theories instead of doctrine. Take religion from literally anyone else.

I was intimidated on the first day, but I'm so glad I stuck with this class! I didn't realize how much I didn't know about the Restoration until he made it come alive. He knew everyone by name and trusted us enough to grade our own tests. One of my favorite professors at BYU

He is super knowledgeable about the foundation of the restoration. He is funny and engaging in lectures. He doesn't post slides often, so it's important to go to class and take notes because you can use them on exams. The exams are open-note on Learning Suite, and sometimes you will grade them yourself and then submit the score.

Brother Belnap pretty much teaches straight from his own knowledge and references the scriptures. No slides and everything you need to know on tests come from him in his lectures and a few readings (Not required but should do if you want a good grade). Doesn't reply to emails and neither does the TA so ask other students for help.

Very lecture-heavy and hard to stay engaged. He often kept us past class time, which made me late to my next class. What was frustrating is that he sometimes showed up late himself and could come off as rude. I wouldn't take another class from him.

Everything is basically self graded, attendance, midterms, final exam, etc. Everything is online and open note. Didn't love his lecture style, but found the midterms manageable nevertheless. He is so understanding and willing to work with his students.

He was frequently late to class, but I thought his lectures were phenomenal. At least for the BOM, he's one of the easier professors. HOWEVER, you MUST take notes on EVERYTHING HE SAYS if you want to get a good grade on the tests. I'm not talking about just general ideas, I mean literally everything. ALSO, write down every scripture read in class.

He has a very obnoxious voice in my opinion and attendance is necessary so there's no escaping it. It's a super easy A but I hated going to class. You grade your own tests and have to write about a 500 word report each week. He was also late to class over half the time, so most class periods, we had to stay long

He made the grading criteria very clear and straightforward. There was a good amount of reading, but nothing too difficult, and his lectures made it all very interesting. For a religion class, the focus tended to be more on learning the material than feeling the Spirit, but I still felt the Spirit on multiple occasions. Highly recommend.

I have very mixed feelings about this professor. As far as the false doctrine, I didn't notice anything and wasn't bothered by this. I was bothered by how self-important he was. Incredibly disrespectful of student's time - starting and ending late. But he's clear about all requirements and is an engaging lecturerer. So very mixed feelings.

It's obvious that he loves the scriptures, but I think that's the extent of his teaching prowess. Lectures were interesting, but not always related to the exams. His expectations are not clear at all and he also has students grade their own tests? He has a one hour video of feedback and you input the grades. Brother, what am I even paying you for?
Really great lecturer, super engaging, all of our exams were online, self-graded, and the final project was super fun and easy. Highly recommend taking New Testament from him.

Lectures were engaging and interesting. He likes teaching complex ideas and isn't afraid to discuss sensitive topics. Very knowledgeable. Make sure to take really good notes from the lectures! Anything talked about at any point during any lecture could be on the exam, and he doesn't give study guides.
Take any class from this guy. He taught and interesting class and was super easy. I think his religion class has been my easiest at BYU. He is very nice and had some super amazing insights to share.

This professor was ultimately my least favorite teacher by far. He was disrespectful of our time, showing up late and ending over time. He lectured like we were religion geniuses and expected us to fill in the blank for everything he said -- literally. Very disorganized and didn't lecture on the reading assignments but whatever he felt like.

He really knows his stuff and proves it in his lectures. He really dives deep into doctrine of Christ and makes us think deeply. His exams were pretty tough but if you paid attention in his lectures and take good notes you'll be fine. All his quizzes and exams are open book/open note so make sure you take good ones!!

He's a really great professor, you just have to do the reading and go to class to do well. Tests are self graded but take a few hours to complete and are kind of difficult. He's really nice but isn't super accommodating for students when it comes to confusion about assignments. Like just not flexible about a lot.

Attending class is a must, for the UNIV 101 class he gave us a ton of work to do outside along with a huge scavenger hunt across campus which took a long time, but is inspirational and you learn a LOT

took Christ and Everlasting Gospel from him. Lectures were engaging, but his approach was very scholarly, so it was hard for me to feel very spiritually uplifted. A lot of his points seemed to be about things that were "fringe doctrines" at best, mostly speculation and theories. Not terrible but there are definitely better religion teachers.
Professor Belnap makes the lectures engaging, but his scholarly approach can get a bit specific. The workload is light, and unstuck study was great for exam prep.

Some things I learned about Brother Belnap:
 
1. He isn't going to coddle you.
2. He might entertain you.
3. His class is not a testimony meeting.
4. He will do a deep dive on any number of religious topics.
5. He knows more than you do.
6. Er ist von Frau Schnee, Babsi und Wolfgang anerkannt.

The evening class was two hours long on a Tuesday night. If you can focus for that long that late, this is an easy class. His discussions wander far and his midterm and final questions are so specific and unanswerable. At least he leaves both the question and your grade up to your own interpretation.

There are some fundamental things wrong with Bro Belnap's teaching techniques. He is a BIG lecture guy and rarely involves his students. The exam are just obscure questions about the random opinions he shared in class. We just felt like he didn't care about us. It was an EASY class, but I didn't grow in my faith literally at all.

Brother Belnap really knows his stuff he cares a lot about his students. If you show up and take (diligent) notes, you'll be fine. His clerical skills are so frustrating though-you have to watch hour long videos to grade your own exams and his approach is very much that HIS interpretation is always right, no matter what. 5 minutes late very often.

Don't get me wrong, I liked Professor Belnap. He does have a very doable A. Everything is self graded (attendance, midterm, final). He does throw in some random assignments here and there thoughout the semester. Please know, class is a long, non-interactive lecture. He doesn't get to know students very well and disregards any comments made in class

Christ and His Everlasting Gospel has so much information and doctrine to learn in such a short amount of time, and Brother Belnap goes about it wonderfully. He is very engaging and willing to answer any questions the students have (which are many). There are 2 weekly assignments (simple) and a few quizzes that are fine as long as you go to class.

This class is pretty easy, but Brother Belnap is pretty arrogant when it comes to lectures. The few times people raised their hand in class, he essentially just disregarded the comments and questions. Class was easy and mostly self graded, but him and his TA hardly respond. I wanted to get more out of this class but he's just not very good.

It's been a while since I've taken a religion class I truly liked, but this class was that for me. I would say his interpretations probably aren't confirmed doctrine, but he connects everything to doctrine and principles that we believe in. He's an engaging lecturer for the full hour and definitely gets excited over teaching, which is fun to see.

Brother Belnap is my favorite professor I have had at BYU! He is super caring about all of his students, but you need to show up to class. The only way to get the material is listening to his lectures. There were a few exams that were **self-graded** and related directly to what he lectured on. 100% take a class from Brother Belnap!!! (I am!)
Great lectures, especially on the cultural background of the Book of Mormon. Not very many actual assignments except for the final project and some weekly online "group discussions". Would recommend.

He is super nice and his lectures are fun! He goes a little into more of what he thinks doctrine is but it is still fun. Super easy to get an A. The one thing that bothered me is he makes you grade your own exams. Even the final. So just be prepared for an hour and a half video of him telling you how to grade yourself

Brother Belnap is a great guy, but his class definitely felt like "The Gospel According to Brother Belnap." I loved Bro. Belnap's lectures, but he can move fast and tests are exclusively based on the things he says in lectures so if you can't keep up, you won't do well.

Professor Belnap is an awesome guy, super inspiring lectures and teaches the BoM in a really interesting new way. Learned everyone's names in probably the first week and a half. Also an easy professor to take 275 from, the workload was really light.

Prof. Belnap is a great guy. Good class. Good structure. Engaging lectures. Nothing against him. He's just a bit too enthusiastically loud for me. I just felt anxious most of the time because of the noise and raised voice. But as I said, great guy and a great class. Just don't take Prof. Belnap if you want a more laid-back, quieter professor.
Brother Belnap knows what he's talking about. He is hilarious. His lectures are sometimes boring... but if you pay attention you'll get a lot out of it and see the Book of Mormon in a new way.
Seriously slay take this class with him, just take notes

Professor Belnap takes a very scholarly and literary approach to the Book of Mormon, but in doing so, he teaches the teachings within the Book of Mormon as "the gospel according to Dan Belnap", and that is not very helpful. He's a great professor, and very passionate about what he teaches, but it's not the best approach to teaching about scripture.

I took this class from BYU Independent Study and it took Professor Belnap months at a time to grade any of my assignments. He was not super nice when giving feedback on the assignments. I did learn a lot in this class, but if I could do it over, I would take it from someone else.

Professor Belnap is an amazing professor with a very scholarly approach to the scriptures. He knows his stuff and loooooves to share it with you! He is hysterical and literally WILL NOT put you to sleep. He is very kind with grading and will allow you to submit corrections over and over. If you don't get an A, it's kind of your own fault.

Brother Belnap is passionate about what he teaches. He likes to think that he teaches in unorthodox ways (although I didn't think so), and he likes to tell jokes, so the class is usually pretty fun. The midterm and final seem like way too much work for the type of class that he teaches, and he didn't even bother to grade them, so that was a shame.

Loved the class. The ones that rate my man low just don't like to think, and are the most likely to say that the gospel is very simple when it's not. Ya, class is hard, it's the Pearl of Great Price, intelligence (wink) comes at a price. He tells you that his class will be very academic before the add-drop deadline so you can switch if you want.

He wasn't very respectful of classmates when they were confused or asked questions. He doesn't have many assignments so you either ace them or fail. Get ready for long- short answer exams! 
I didn't gain any spiritual experiences from this class. I recommend taking it from someone else.

Pearl of Great Price from Professor Belnap was the worst religion class I have taken at BYU by far. He doen't use slides or study guides for the tests so you just have to write down everything he says. The class seemed more about literary analysis of the Pearl of Great Price text and Brother Belnap's opnions on things than actual doctrine

Hands down favorite religion professor at BYU. His lectures are incredible--never boring, always enlightening, entertaining. Some assignments, the midterm and final are a little hard-hitting and heavy intellectually, but it is so worth it. (essay response, open book/take home midterm & final; --take notes during lecture and you're totally set!)

Don't take this professor if you have academic accommodations, he was very rude when I asked to use mine due to my disabilities. His lectures also feel very scattered and often don't connect at all to the course material.

The content of his lectures was interesting but the organization of this class did NOT work for me. Preclass readings due Sun and Tues night were like 35% of the grade which is ridiculous. Test content based solely on lectures so you have to get to class and take thorough notes. only 3 other assignments. Not hard but you need stamina for his class
Super easy. Midterm was self graded, and so was the final. Weekly discussion boards, but thats it.
Very focused on academic side of the scriptures. Everting in lecture is his opinions. Doesnt take the time to grade midterms. Pretty much the bad side of the BYU religion department

This dude sounds like Mr. Bigweld from Robots which is my favorite part of all his lectures. He makes learning about Christ SO interesting and really views the gospel from a deep philosophical view. I really loved this class. He really cares about his students and will work with you if you need extra help. Do the discussion posts and u r good.

If you're dying to learn about the ontological and epistemological issues of the Book of Mormon, then this class is for you. If not, then you will probably hate it. I will say though, it is an easy class. Take notes on every word he says and you will do good on the exam. There are not a ton of assignments and you get to grade your own exam

How to get an A: 1. don't do readings. 100+ pages each, he tells you the 3 things that will be on the quiz. Ctrl F those topics before the quiz, I averaged 9/10. I never read. 2. Write down EVERY SCRIPTURE he says and his interpretation of it. 100% of test questions come from this. 3. 3 papers. Can resubmit until 100% Loved him! Will take again!

The papers/quizzes involve INSANE amounts of readings and research! One small quiz might involve 100+ pages of outside material! Tests are only based on what he talks about in class, WHICH ARE JUST THEORIES! Nothing he says is actual doctrine, just what he thinks! He literally told us he wants the class to be hard and hopes we didn't ace the final!

Took for Evlasting Gospel. TAKE NOTES OR DIE ON EXAMS. Exams were take home, open note, open book. No class discussion. Great lectures, but no powerpoints. If you can recreate his thinking on assignments, you will get an "A." Some of his conclusions seemed convoluted or on the outskirts of doctrine. However, has total mastery of scriptures.

Brother Belnap was my favorite religion professor Ive had at BYU & Christ & the Everlasting Gospel was my favorite religion course. I loved coming to class everyday (not like me at all) & he had a perfect balance with intellectually & spiritually stimulating lessons without making the course difficult. 10/10 would recommend

Loved it! Belnap is so passionate of what he teaches which makes coming to class so much fun. Although he does as a lot of questions during lectures and expects responses, he will never call a student out on giving the wrong answer, he accepts every answer. He teaches exactly what's on his tests so attendance is key but the tests aren't difficult

Belnap is kind of a character. He takes some getting used to, but he is a smart guy and has engaging lectures. In his class, it's important to take lots of notes and mark down references. However, he gives a lot chances for a student to get a good grade, as long as they are willing to keep trying.

I didn't really like Bro. Belnap's teaching style at first, but I loved this class! He gave so many great insights to the scriptures that I had never heard before. Be sure to be in class to take good notes because your midterm and final will depend on it. Only two assignments but daily readings and digital dialogue.

Bro. Belnap is an awesome professor! The biggest advice I would give to someone who takes his class is to take thorough notes. There are only two exams and then two other assignments. All are doable, but you have to put in the work. He expects you to do the readings from the scriptures and the Digital Dialogue questions before every class.

Dr. Belnap is THE Professor for REL 250. He taught many of the LDS Apostles. He knows what he is teaching and LOVEs his job. He will go the extra mile to make sure you understand what the scripture is really saying regarding the lesson. He gives clear feed back and unlimited time to resubmit your assignment for a better grade. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

Brother Belnap is so knowledgeable and is very willing to share that knowledge. Readings due daily. Only 2 papers and a take home midterm and final that are open note. Only lectures, no Powerpoint. You will learn so much about the Savior and the scriptures in this class. I left each class feeling inspired. Great class!!

Personally, I was not a fan of Brother Belnap's teaching style-- he has a "guessing game" style of teaching, and it makes it difficult to guess the right answer, then I got confused and felt like I wasn't learning anything. However, some people really enjoy that style and are able to learn a lot from it. However, it did not work for me.

I have taken two courses from Bro. Belnap. It has been amazing. He has a class that focuses much more on comprehension than memorization. The midterms are actually fun take home exams that are open book and note. Just take good notes in class and enjoy the ride. You can easily get an A if you just revise your essays and take time to do the test. :)

There are 3 quizzes, 2 take-home tests, and 3 short papers. He does not use PowerPoint. So, you have to type down everything he says in lecture to do well on the tests. If you try your best, you can get an A in this class. Dr. Belnap is so smart. He is very theatrical so his lectures are really fun/engaging. He teaches doctrine well. Great teacher!

I was excited about class initially, but honestly every class period goes like this: "Okay, here's Point A that you all understand...(1 hour of random tangents later)... and congratulations, now you've arrived at the conclusion I want you to at Point B. I have proved I'm a genius, your mind is blown."

There were lots of readings, but they were good and relevant. You have to work hard and really study up even though the midterm is open book, but he's a great guy with a good sense of humor and you'll learn a lot and enjoy yourself.

So enjoyable, I looked forward to his class everyday. He gives you a really beneficial and new perspective on the scriptures and helps you understand them in a new light. He's super funny and understanding. He's really accommodating, especially if you have mental issues as long as you tell him up front.

He is THE best!!! Classes are really fun and spiritual. Although attendance isnt required make sure you have class notes. A couple homework quizzes and couple of papers you can resubmit as many times you want

You basically write all of his personal observations of a few BOM chapters word for word and then get tested on it. I recommend recording the lectures, because he provides nothing to refer back to. Doesn't use slides or write on the board. The 3 external reading assignments are long and convoluted for how little points they are. I don't recommend.

Very unique but inspirational man. Very intellegent, but not the most organized. Learned a lot from his class, just make sure to take a lot of good notes for the midterm and final. Great class that wasn't too overwhelming for a religious class.

Brother Belnap approaches the Book of Mormon in highly academic lectures. His lectures were mind-blowing me, and I wouldn't miss a day of class. His class consists of three essays, a final and midterm. You grade yourself on the final and midterm, and the essays can be resubmitted until you get an A. Overall very interesting and engaging class.

Very interesting Book of Mormon class. I learned a lot of insight on seeing the Book of Mormon from a Nephite perspective. Not my most spiritual and testimony building class, but I learned a lot about Nephite religion and the Book of Mormon. If you pay attention in class and take good notes the tests are a piece of cake.

I hated this class. Bro. Belnap went off on tangents about cosmos/chaos, his tests were ridiculous, and he had a weird obsession with Korihor. We spent 5 weeks just discussing Alma 30. If you're looking for a deep 400-level theology class, take this. If you're looking for a spiritually strengthening 100-level BOM class, don't take it from Belnap.

He gives really good lectures, I loved them. He explains what's going on in the text in a way you won't have heard before. The problem is the papers. Why do we write papers that have nothing to do with the class itself? And then his grading is very subjective, based mostly on his opinion. He does let you resubmit them as much as you want though.

If you learn a lot by listening to lectures, you will do really well in class. Absolutely no busywork, just a few papers and two tests. Dr. Belnap is one of the professors that wants you to learn how to think about something as opposed to just telling you what to think. I loved learning about Isaiah with him!

He rambles on in class in every which way.  Some of the stuff is good but you don't really internalize any of it, especially with Isaiah.  The papers you write just need to fit with his opinions or you will get a bad grade.  Impossible to tell the difference between rants and his actual lectures.  Dont take if you want to be happy with your life

Do not take his class online. Every homework question is subjective in that it is impossible to figure out whether you explained enough. It's very difficult to guess what he's asking for and he'll dock points when you can't figure out what he was thinking when he wrote the question. He has no clear cut way for you to achieve an A.

He has been my favorite religion professor.  If you are looking for someone with deep knowledge of the scriptures, look no further, especially if you want to learn the mind blowing doctrines.  He lectures the entire time, but it is fantastic information.  On the final paper, just follow the rubric and you will do fine.

I'll be honest, Brother Belnap has been my least favorite religion professor at BYU by far. His class is just him talking and he repeats his lectures a lot. Most of the time I feel like he is just trying to pass the time because he continuously looks up at the clock. Everything we are graded on is papers where we regurgitate his personal views.

Bro. Belnap is fantastic. He stretched my brain and made me think in ways I didn't know I could. However, I would never take this class from him again. The scriptural analysis in this class is 90% scholarly minutia and 10% relevant and applicable doctrine. Unless you're planning a career in seminary and institute teaching, take someone else.

Classes are almost entirely listening to him lecture, but that's because he's got lots of stuff to share and I didn't really mind it. I even recommended sitting in on the class to my boss at the university. A lot of his test questions are lecture based, but he lets you use notes. Your grade is a research paper, three quizzes, midterm, and final.

One of the best religion professors in BYU. His approach to scriptures are unique and inspirational. The take home exam and midterms are also pretty easy if you listen in class. He is also not a harsh grader on paper. He understands scriptures like no one else and you can always feel the Spirit. I would definitely take another class from him.

Best religion professor I have had yet and I have had many. If you are looking for the easy blow off BOM class, this is not it. Fantastic lectures and extremely informative. One paper that you work on throughout the semester, so it is not that bad. Two written take home tests that are open note and open book. Grades like a college professor.

Professor Belnap has a lot of amazing insights into the Pearl of Great Price and his class was super interesting/engaging. There are only a few assignments, which means each one is worth a lot of points, but they are spread out so that they are totally doable.

The best religion lecturer I have ever had.  Absolutely incredible classes.  If you really want to understand the Pearl of Great Price, he is the professor for you.  Not much homework, just one paper that he grades very strictly.  If you are looking for an incredible teacher and doctrine to amaze your friends and enjoy writing, look no further.

Love Belnap! Only problem for me was the style of the midterm/final. They are essay format. I spent easily twice the amount of time finishing the midterm for Pearl of Great Price than any other of my classes. I regret nothing, and highly recommend taking this class.

Fantastic professor, really knows his stuff, he expects real academic work in terms of the paper and the tests, but sets the class up in a way that it really is in your control how well you do. The spiritual nourishment meets academic enlightenment of his classes is the best. Take good notes and all will be well.

Brother Belnap really cares about the individual student. He is academic, as well as spiritual, leading to a religion class that actually grows your testimony and your ability to defend the church, instead of just making it a "feel good" environment. He really takes his job seriously, and is committed to helping us understand.

Brother Belnap gives good assignments, you will not face busywork. Lectures are interesting and not afraid to follow implications of the text, while still maintaining purpose and thematic unity. If you have interest in a religion class that's academic and fulfilling, then take it from him. It's what religion classes ought to be at BYU.

Prof Belnap's class is extremely subjective. He preaches his own doctrine, not following the assigned reading and jumps around in the scriptures to prove his points. He makes some interesting conjectures, that he later assumes as fact, especially about the social structure of the societies presented. Homework load is pretty light.

Belnap's class was unlike any other class I took. There weren't many assignments, which meant not too much busy work. However, his lectures were amazing. His understanding of the Book of Mormon is so deep, and he could relate even the smallest details to life today. There is a paper, so make sure you know what he wants and you'll do fine.

Really difficult class b/c I didn't like the teaching style (sit and write every word he says) and b/c there are literally 9 grades in the class. Take-home open-note open-book midterm&final (not bad). Three reading quizzes and student evaluation (easy). Thesis, outline,&paper really difficult and graded hard. I wouldn't take him again.

If you have the opportunity to take a class from Professor Belnap, take it. He is knowledgeable, decisive, and most importantly, kind. If you have concerns about not just the class but your ability to follow through it to the end, talk to him. His insights into texts, back with credentials, is fascinating and it was a privilege to participate

Rarely involves the class in lectures.  More interested on how correct you sight sources, write bibliography, and grammar than the content in your paper.  Harsher than most my BYU English professors. He is very knowledgeable about the Book of Mormon but seems to care more to prove he knows a lot rather than teach.  Not a super spiritual  class.

I learned so much about the Book of Mormon from Brother Belnap. He focuses on the context of the scriptures, especially socio-economic-political implications. He requires a research paper, but gives plenty of resources and asks for an outline first, so it's not too bad. What you learn is definitely worth the work too.

Dr. Belnap is the greatest professor I have ever had at BYU. His insights into religious history and concepts is second to none. Every hour of class was captivating. His teaching has shaped the way I read the scriptures more than anyone else. I highly recommend any class he teaches.

It is well worth it to take a class from Brother Belnap!  His lectures are really interesting and he helps you see the scriptures in a new way.  He talks super fast so sometimes it is hard to keep up with him, but overall an excellent professor!  I felt like a tiny sponge trying to soak up a pail of knowledge!!!
He's a great teacher! it's insane how much he knows about the Book of Mormon. But overall a great class!

This was a very hard intense class, but he was a very interesting lecturer. Take really thorough notes in class and that will help you on the tests. Makes you read some questionable articles for reading.

He doesn't ask any questions or involve students at all in the lectures so it's hard to stay focused. He gives lots of his theories on the BOM as if they were facts (and I don't find them convincing). Came late to class almost EVERY class period. Very knowledgeable but doesn't seem interested in students. Not a spiritual religion class.

Huge paper that took a lot of time, but sooo worth it for his amazing lectures. Guaranteed mind blowing experiences for every class period. Take home tests were really long, but if you have the right note taking strategy they're not that bad. I learned more from this class than all religion course put together.

Prof. Belnap is FANTASTIC. I'm not academically inclined and I'm just getting through school so I can get a job, but Belnap was truly inspirational and helped me grow. Easily my favorite professor at BYU. Go to class and take notes or you'll fail the take home midterm and final. No meaningless busy work, just go to class to have your mind blown.

Harder than my Econ 110 class.  Very good lecturer. Paper requirements are stringent. Take home tests are really hard.  I did learn a lot about the Book of Mormon. This is more of a history class than a spiritual class. Really makes you think in a new paradigm about the Book of Mormon. Quizzes are hard. Grades really hard.

Dr. Belnap is absolutely terrific. His primary flaw is that his tests require you to reproduce pretty much exactly what he said in class, but the things he teaches are new, exciting, and profound. I learned new ways of looking at gospel principles that were deeply edifying. He is an academic and a scholar--a rare find in the religion department.
Fantastic lecturer! Class was super interesting, which was good cause you have to take really good notes. I procrastinated the paper until a couple days before but it was super easy with ebsco.

Go to class everyday, write down every word that comes out of his mouth, read the entire part of the Book of Mormon that is expected (part of final), and expect to write a tedious paper. The midterm and final is take home, open note, and you grade it. He is funny and entertaining, but somewhat prideful. Got an A, worth taking!

Expect to take very detailed notes to do well. He really dives into the scriptures and is interesting, but the class is based on a very limited amount of points. If you don't do very well on one assignment, it will be hard to raise your grade. A little difficult, but worth the experience.

Belnap is awesome! He really knows what he's talking about and has a lot of really good insight to the scriptures. His class does involve a lot more work than most religion classes, but so worth it. Attendence is a MUST. His midterm and final are directly from his lectures. Note taking is also a must. Write down everything he says.
He is a great teacher and actually teaches what is written in text you are studying.  I felt like I was learning something instead of just going to Sunday school.

he is a very challenging teacher who expects a lot.  need to put too much work in for just a religion class.  his lectures are interesting and his tests are straight from them so you basically need to write down everything he says. have to do a big research paper that takes a lot of time

He's pretty decent. I either really liked him, or didn't depending on the day. Tests are take home and long, but fairly easy. Final paper is kind of ridiculous with the sources you need for it. Not my favorite religion teacher, but it was alright.

Fascinating and challenging. Take very detailed notes. He mentions examples in the text and scripture references. Write them down. Write everything down. Also, complete the reading before the final. This was the most challenging and fascinating religion class I have taken in my 4 years. Take detailed notes and you'll do great.

Class was so bomb, because of Belnap. No expectations for class, but he made it my favorite. He makes you see the scriptures in a whole new way. Hilarious, smart, sarcastic, spiritual. Bonus points for reading. Super fair/easy grader (you grade your own tests). Take detailed notes, you'll want to anyway because lectures are so good. Take home tests

Professor Belnap knows this subject very well. Take very detailed notes of his class. I found the class to be very educational, I learned SO much and came away with a better perspective. He doesn't give his ideas as doctrine but lets you know what's his and what's doctrine. His tests are based on lectures, so if you don't take notes expect to fail.

Fabulous professor who really cares about his students and is extremely knowledgeable about the Pearl of Great Price. The paper was really tough but he ended up grading everyone very fairly at the end. I would recommend this class.

Brother Belnap had some really cool insight. Tests are take home open book, so be sure to take good notes. There is one research paper that takes a while to do and there are quizzes that require you to do extra reading outside of the Book of Mormon. The final is another take home test (bring your syllabus to class the last day). Good class though.

I'd advise you take another professor. The grading is quite difficult; an A isn't impossible but it's improbable. The midterm and final are based solely on his lectures and his pet theories, so TAKE VERY DETAILED NOTES. Read the scriptures before the final exam, because that is part of your grade (he doesn't tell you that beforehand)
Amazing teacher. He is funny, yet can conduct class with a solemnity rare to experience. He brought many insights into the Book of Mormon that I had never before pondered.
Some people love Brother Belnap and some people hate him. He is my favorite religion teacher at BYU. Take him and never regret it. If it isn't a good fit though, find someone you enjoy.

I loved taking religion with Brother Belnap! He is easy to listen to and funny. Write down EVERYTHING he says and you will be fine. Tests are take home open note and open book. Research paper as well, but it's really not bad, I promise! I learned A LOT!! I loved going to the class. I would definitely recommend it! TAKE THE CLASS! You learn SO much!

I love Brother Belnap. He makes me feel the spirit and it makes my day. His essay isn't bad, he's very helpful, quizzes on readings are easy just memorization.  The midterm was open note however, it was still tough. Take great notes!!! His insights are incredible and leave me in awe. Great guy, great professor.
His way or the highway.

He was a great teacher.  ATTENDANCE IS MUST!!! Everything on his tests will be from in-class, and he almost takes everything verbatim, but they are such obscure details (that are actually really interesting & insightful to the scriptures) you can only get it from class.  He helps you make connections that you would never make on your own. He Rocks!

Great professor, but his class is impossible. I appreciated his enthusiasm, insights, and academic approach, but unless you basically remember verbatim all of his off-the-wall personal theories, you will do poorly. For a religion class, we barely touched the scriptures and used no textbook, which makes it hard to study. GO TO CLASS.

Bro. Belnap is a great guy.  He's funny and makes everything really entertaining.  He's a little bit power hungry though.  He doesn't like to be wrong and he will not be wrong.  You have to take notes on everything he says because that's the whole test.  Overall, good guy, good class.

Take super good notes on everything he says and take the paper seriously, and its not too hard. His tests come right from lecture.  PGP was best religion class at BYU and I would take any class I could form him. Fast paced, but VERY good teacher,
His class is amazing!! He doesn't make the class easy but it is extremely interesting. I loved his class
If you're looking for an easy A, this isn't the class for you.  Hard work.

Had a returned missionary Book of Mormon class - he had the best insights of any religion professor I ever had at BYU, hands down.  He can be a little power-trippy and intense, though.  Overall I really enjoyed his lectures.

He is pretty intense. He will make you think that his class is really hard. You HAVE to come to class and take notes of almost everything he says. If you do that then you will do well cause his exams are easy. The essay is important but is also pretty easy. I didn't think that I liked it at first but in hind-site it was a great class.

This class was WAY too hard for a religion class. I wouldn't recommend it. Sure you might learn a lot of different things, but having to worry about getting an A in a religion class when you have other classes to worry about isn't fun. He grades pretty harshly on essays and makes it a point to not give 100% on anything. You can only miss 18 points.

Dr. Belnap is amazing. He said the class would be hard and he was right. Fun class though, you learn so much about the New Testament. Dr. Belnap's explanations are fantastic, he does a great job. The class is fun. I recommend Dr. Belnap for New Testament.

Loved the class, but it was tough. Its totally based on writing. The essay is all of your grade, and the midterm and final are essay format. Easy to get a b+ or higher, but come to class and take good notes. He is a great professor

First things first, Professor Belnap is a great guy. He is not unreasonable, and will help anyone. With that said: This was one of the most frustrating classes that I have taken in a while: If you do not take down every word he says, you will not do well. You cannot keep up by reading the scriptures, you must be in class. His tests are infuriating

Wonderful teacher.  This was a class that I never missed because I wanted to hear what he was teaching!  Easy tests and paper is graded tough but you have plenty of time to work on it and he is very willing to help.  Professor Belnap is very knowledgeable and I HIGHLY RECOMMEND his classes.

I guess I'm an anomally.  I didn't like Belnaps teaching style.  He was 15 minutes late every day.  Looked for obscure things to teach. reacted defensively to questions. Also he was hard to follow.  For instance he would announce that he was going to teach three things and then me and everyone I was sitting by would only get 2 of them. TANGENTS!

Bro. Belnap is great. Extremely knowledgeable- a lot of his ideas go over my head but he is always willing to talk to you and explain. I see some people complaining about my paper, and I would be too had I not met with him at the very beginning about my thesis. Once he guided me to a good one, I had a pretty easy time writing the paper.

I would not take this class again simply because of the paper. It is WAY too technical, especially for a religion class. Other than the paper, if you just go to class and take notes on every single thing he says, you will do well. He teaches the scriptures with a scholarly approach rather than a religious

His lectures are interesting. With the paper it is a lot of work at times.  His tests are a bit pointless, just regurgitation of your notes.  He takes a very scholarly, exegetical approach to the scriptures.  If you don't care to know what the word exegetical means, don't take the class.

Great teacher. Easy class if you just pay attention. Tests are take home and easy if you pay attention in class. You grade your own tests. One paper to write three times. He is a tough grader on the papers but it will end up ok if you go talk to him about how to make it better. 3 quizzes to take on other readings but the quizzes arent hard :)

I never once left Professor Belnap's class without having felt the spirit really strongly. His class leaves you with a true testimony of who you are, and what your relationship with God can and should be. He's very knowledgeable, but he's more than willing to share what he knows,and cite all sources. Loved the class.... TAKE IT!

He is the most annoying teacher ever. On the paper if you don't write exactly what he would write, then it's a bad paper. He loves his voice and his opinions. I learned a lot, and his class is easy enough, I was just bothered by the fact that his opinion is docrtine and that everything he does from the way he talks is annoying
Prof. Belnap is awesome.  He is immensely intelligent and has a unique view of the scriptures.  1 paper, 3 quizzes, a midterm and a final. That's all.  Go to class and you'll be fine.
i love this class is my favorite!. if you are looking for a professor who really teaches and explains everything,then go with Dan Belnap

Just the right amount of hardness. He stretches your mind the perfect amount without you going crazy. Blows your mind away with how he knows so much! Great guy. Recommend him to anyone who wants to actually learn something.
This man brought the scriptures to life, very funny and cares about his students.

Bro. Belnap is the most amazing professor ever. He takes common knowledge and ties into the gospel. His knowledge on the facsimilles was amazing. Anyone who takes his class and doesn't like it obviously wants a professor that will tell them to read their scriptures, say their prayers and they will go to heaven!!!!! Or your still at EFY
If you just take notes in class you will have the answers for the test.  Very enjoyable class.  I looked forward to it. You learn a lot as well.
Among the finest religion professors I have ever had.  I was so grateful to have his course because it made BYU religion credit worthwhile.

The best teacher I've ever had, hands down.  Attendance is not mandatory, but if you don't go, you won't do well on the tests.  2 tests -a midterm and final.  3 quizzes throughout the semester on sets of readings from the NT.  One final paper - 5 pgs long.  (I actually enjoyed writing it, and I usually hate writing papers.)  TAKE THIS CLASS!
Really great professor. Readings for the reading quizzes were REALLY long essays or chapters from books and the questions were hard. Go to class or you'll have a lot of trouble with the exams.
best teacher i have ever had for ancient scriptures he reaaaally knows his stuff. very impressive

I loved Brother Belnap's class. I was a little hesitant the first week or two, but i quickly got over that. He has this ability to draw you into his lectures, and leave you walking away astonished with what you've learned. Make sure you read all of the assigned chapters, and take goodnotes. This was my favorite class, and i hope to have him again.

Belnap is tight. His class is amazing and you will learn more from him than any other religion professor at BYU. His class is VERY fairly graded and any one who gets a bad grade DIDN'T GO TO CLASS. Take good notes and its a piece of cake!

I took 211 and 212 from him. Lectures are interesting and insightful. Tests are based solely on lecture, but do your reading (it's just scriptures). The assignments aren't too bad, but take some work. He started doing outside readings for quizzes.Those kinda sucked, but didn't hurt the grade too much.You have to pay attention in class, but  takeit!

Bro. Belnap is my favorite religion professor thus far. I have taken REL 122 and 211 from him. His class is not easy, but not so hard to where I felt consumed by it. It was enough to stretch me. His lectures are full of information about the scriptures that I have never realized before. Take a class from Bro. Belnap!

Mostly rigid class schedule. He is kind of in-your-face, but doesn't ever say anything abrasive so it's easy to handle. Likes to talk about the Book of Mormon more literally, historically and doctrinally, as opposed to spiritually. He went out of his way to apologize to me about something that didn't even offend me. I learned so much.

Belnap is a wonderful teacher. His lectures are amazing and you learn well beyond the basic scope of the New Testament. The assignments and tests are fairly easy and they aren't much to worry about. Anyone that says the tests are hard just didn't go to class...that simple. I say this because he gives the answers to his exams during lecture.

Bro. Belnap is incredible. You have to take good notes, but the lectures are so amazing that taking good notes isn't a problem. There's only one 6-page paper that is completely open-ended and he grades it very leniently. Also, both the tests are take home and if you go to class and take notes you'll do fine. I learned sooo much in this class.

I loved the class. Bro Belnap is an engaging teacher who delves into deep doctorine. it is definately not like seminary. He skips alot of the usual stuff and spends time on more obscure but very important info. Attend class and take good notes and you'll do well.

Bro. B. Was a good professor but my beef with him is the way that his tests are not common knowledge type things. You can only do well if you know exactly what he said in class and can put that on the test. YOu have to answer according to what he told you in class.  Also disapointed that he never gave sources for where he got his insights.

Bro. Belnap is great!  One research paper, two take home tests that you grade yourself.  YOU HAVE TO GO TO CLASS to get a good grade!  If you don't go to class, you will do poorly. Brother Belnap is great though and is really helpful!

You have to work a bit for your grade, but I learned so much and did well in the class. GO TO CLASS (and take notes) and you will be well on your way. I LOVED Brother Belnap - he gave so many insights. I learned so much about the Old Testament and he was very good at explaining concepts that were a little difficult to understand.

The class was good, but very doctrinal. The lectures were very confusing sometimes. You really need to focus and pay attention. Attendance is mandatory!!! The midterm and final are takehome, but you can't answer them unless you took good notes in class. There is also a 5 pg paper due towards the end of class. Start on it early!

Brother Belnap is an incredible lecturer.  So many new insights about politics and culture of BOM that you never think about.  LIke someone else said, on the first day, he sounds way intense, but it's not too hard.
Great teacher with great insights.

I had Bro. Belnap for the Pearl of Great Price, and the class was amazing.  By far one of the best teachers I have ever had.  He taught really well, but you must go to class or you will have a very hard time with the tests (midterm & final).
Bro Belnap is awesome! I was really scared the first day of class because he made the class seem really intense... But I never thought I could learn so much from the New Testament!! I got an A.

Great teacher! One of the best professors I have had at BYU. I learned a lot in this class.  Take detailed notes, and you will do fine. 1 paper, 2 tests, not really that hard, just take a lot of time.  Great class!
this class was awesome.  Brother Belnap knows his stuff.  There is a 5 page research paper and the tests are essay, but the class is worth it.
GO TO CLASS! the tests are based  on the lecture alone. Also pick a challenging topic for the paper and he will grade a lot easier because you are working harder.

Very good lecturer, doesn't assign busy work. 1 5-page paper, 1 midterm and the final.  Midterm and paper require a lot of work but thats it, beside your old testament reading, which you don't really get tested on.  Keep very good lecture notes.
His lectures are amazingly good.  I never once got bored in his class. Not too hard either. Highly recommended.

Bro. Belnap is an amazing and powerful teacher! I learned so much from his class- best class I have taken at BYU. Make sure to take detailed notes, not only for the tests, but for your benefit later on in life. You will learn so much from his knowledge and testimony of the scriptures.
I learned a lot on his class.  He taught some major reoccuring themes and taught about the importance of the prespective of the authors.  HOw it affects what they put in and wrote.
Great lectures!  Come to class, take detailed notes.  All his tests are open note and open book and based off of his lectures.  His assignments are a cinch, just do them.

Bro. Belnap is a great teacher. Likes to digress, but lectures are interesting. Learned a lot from this class. Gives NO busywork (unlike some professors, who thats their whole life). If you take good notes and pay attention in class, and can write a 5+ page research paper over the semester, you'll do great.

Bro. Belnap is an awesome teacher. Although we only made it through Jacob in an entire semester, I can say that I know a heck of a lot about 1 Nephi-Jacob. Take very detailed notes, his tests are based solely off of class discussions so you need to be in class as well. Grades very fair. Tests are easy if you take notes. Overall was a great teacher
This class was amaizing, I loved it.

Interesting lectures.  Brother Belnap tries to bring you into the box he is in.  A little bit condescending and self-righteous, but what religion professor isn't?  Overall, good lecturer and interesting class.

belnap is a nut.  he goes on for entire lectures about something he could have discussed in one or two sentences and have relatively little bearing for his tests. way interesting stuff but goes on a little too long....his tests are way easy as long as you take good notes cuz they are open note/open scripture.  if you want an ecentric guy take him.
This was the best religion classes I have taken here at BYU, I was interested in going to class.  It is not a suday school class like some classes here.
This was a terrible class.  He teaches a bunch of crazy things based off of his own definitions of words and expects you to regurgitate it back to him on his tests (which were actually quite easy).
Real good.

Bro. Belnap is an amazing teacher! Not only did I learn more about the Book of Mormon than any Seminary class, but I learned how to effectively continue to study it! The paper isn't too long, just pick an interesting topic. And be sure to attend class so you can do well on the midterm and final! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND TAKING HIS CLASS!

Book of Mormon class..Very interesting lectures.  Take REALLY detailed notes, though, because his tests are usually open book, open note and VERY detailed.  They're usually just essays with no multiple choice and are based on class lectures.  5-page research report as well.  Good class, not a big homework load.  Highly recommend him!
Loved him. I didn't fall asleep once. He's way interesting and the stuff he relates to the Book of Mormon is incredible. I highly recommend him.
He's hard and his tests are very detailed.  Good lectures, but hard
An excellent teacher

hmm, i don't know about the other classes, but he seems like he doesn't like what he's doing... somehow, he makes you feel like he's doing it just because he needs the money, but doesn't have the spiritual touch that you could be feel in other classes. Also, he grades things a weird way, and takes too long in manor details that you won't need...

Excellent teacher.  This has been my favorite Religion class thus far.  He teaches the context of the scriptures very well, and relates them to the Jewish culture surrounding them.  Lots of interesting information.  Recommended!
Don't take a class from this man! He teaches what he wants and does not care what you think. Class seems more like a history lesson rather than something spiritual.

My favorite religion professor thus far.  He teaches lots of useful material (without notes!) and not just what you can learn by picking up the NT manual.  He has extensive knowledge of the language and history of the Bible.  Lectures are intriguing.  Take good notes.  You'll use them on the open book/note tests.
Fabulous lectures. Reasonable assignments. He really knows about Jewish and Greek culture (among others), which makes the class particularly interesting.

AMAZING! This guy knows about NT history and culture. He is funny, spiritual, and easy. He talks, we listen, don't skip class. He doesn't leave room for class discussion, but he has much better things to say than what a classmate would. There isn't a whole lot of work. Just a paper, but the man is strict on grammer and format. I recommend!

He is an amazing teacher who really knows his stuff.  His assignments were pretty easy because he is, as he himslef says, lazy.  He doesn't want to have to grade much so there is much that you have to do.  Tha means you need to be sure you do everything well.  A very good teacher.  I highly recommend.

He knows his stuff. Seems like he has the whole semester of lectures memorized word for word in his head. Smart guy. Class was pretty easy and the lectures were facinating, although sometimes he was hard to follow. Take good notes and you'll do well in the class.

Such an amazing class. The professor is brilliant with Hebrew and ancient traditions. You learn a lot of in-depth information about the New Testament. Take good notes because the final is straight from the notes in class.
Don't fall asleep. It's hard to write essays about something you weren't awake for. (i mean don't fall asleep every day)

Must attend lectures, the tests are straight from stuff he says in class.  Is an Ancient Languages guy, so talks about hebrew and stuff.  Talks alot about the political and social things of the Book of Mormon.  Interesting.  Don't do honors, only difference is paper is 10 instead of 5 pages.

Term paper on topic of choice and final are the only grades.  Grades like an English teacher, so don't take him if you haven't spoken English for 2 years.  Very clear teacher with cool insights on religion.  The class was fairly easy and enjoyable.
Knowledgable and enthusiastic.  Offers a different perspective on some subjects and teaches some pretty deep doctrine.  Gave good feedback on the research paper.

okay teacher, enthusastic, kind of quirky, good insights, deep doctrine, sometimes too 'deep' and seemingly off the wall or exagerated, but overall good, Research Paper on topic of choice, which i enjoyed, -go to lectures or you'll fail  the test!

I took Professor Bryce for Music Theory 1, as well as for private lessons. He's funny, intelligent, and just a genuinely good person. He really knows his music theory and is really big on why music is effective. I'm taking his class again next semester!
Love Professor Bryce! Everything that comes out of his mouth is either funny or helpful. Great feedback, and you can tell he cares. He explained how to teach the tuba and taught us how to play well.

Organic chemistry is challenging, but Dr. Ess's lectures were very helpful for exam preparation. Attending class is essential to do well, and his office hours are a great resource. Be ready to invest significant time into the course, but if you do, you will do well. There was also a generous curve at the end of the semester, which was nice.

It's organic chemistry so obviously this was a hard class. Dr. Ess usually told you exactly what would be on the exam and is very helpful in his office hours. Dr. Ess cares a lot about his students. He doesn't do the two exams for your entire grade thing anymore and he did curve one of our exams by 8 percentage points. Overall super solid option.

Dr. Ess dosent let anyone take pictures or record lectures, which is frustrating because a majority of test content comes from what is on the board. Only 2 exams and a final. There are also randomly assigned study group that you have to meet with 3 hr/week for a part of your final grade. Old school style of teaching. Expect to spend 15+ hours.

Dr. Ess isn't that bad. You have to be prepared to LOCK IN. He only does hadnwritten lectures on the chalk board- no slides, no recordings. You are not allowed to take pictures of the board either so make sure you get it all. He also tests on super small details that he mentions in class which is kind of hard. Pre class assignments are worth a lot.

For me, his lectures always felt disorganized and if you don't take exceptional notes in class you will not do well. He assigned us all study groups and my partners never went to class. He was very slow to respond when I contacted him about my study group and the issue was never fully resolved. Not great.

This class was amazing! I gained a much deeper understanding of organic chemistry. Dr. Ess wants to help you learn the material, and the lectures and homework were clearly structured for this purpose. He is extremely helpful during office hours! However there was very little posted on learningsuite so be sure to pay attention in class for due dates

He was awesome! Very explicit on his expectations. Half of his exams come from what he writes on the board in class. The other half come from practice problems he assigns us from the book. Prepares you very well for the test. Attendance is not mandatory, but he doesn't have any lectures online so to get a good grade you need to show up.

For a graduate class, it was pretty reasonable. Lectures were good, but expectations for grading, exams, and homework were somewhat unclear. Not too organized, but he was very accommodating with extensions. Let us schedule the midterm as a class. The exams were reasonable and reflected what he had taught in lecture despite the random HW assignments

Very few graded assignments.
Dr Ess is amazing! I recommend him to anyone that wants to learn about organic chemistry.
Keeps lectures focused
Tailors tests to what is discussed in class.
Tests understanding of concepts and reasoning, not random facts.

He wants everyone to succeed, and doesn't put up with nonsense.
Dr Dan forever!!!

Wish I could take another course from Dr. Ess! Lectures were great and Friday quizzes pushed me to learn the material before exam time. Use all office hours; take lecture notes; drill tons of textbook problems before exams; work with TAs. Required 10+ outside class hours/week to keep up. Watch for hyperconjugation and mechanism examples in class.

Dr Ess has been the best professor I've ever had. Organic Chemistry is an extremely hard course however Dr Ess is an extremely good teacher. He has limited office hours but I would HIGHLY recommend going to those. Please take his class!

Professor Ess often missed his scheduled office hours. Even more often, the office hours were scheduled at the same time as TA recitation periods. The course was poorly organized. There were some very time intensive, vaguely graded assignments which did not provide preparation for the exams. The midterm was only available Halloween weekend.

Great class and Inspiring Professor. Yes, almost your entire grade is dependent on the midterm and final, but it is structured like a masters class. It's your responsibility to learn, and do the homework (do it! The tests are super similar to the homework, and that is the best away to learn!). Dr. Ess really knows his stuff and cares!

Dr. Ess's class was like a ghost town; I guess people heard about the midterm and final being all of your grade. The smaller class size really helped me. His enthusiasm is contagious; he's fantastic at explaining concepts! I loved the lack of busy work but def stressed over the tests. OChem is just hard, but I learned a ton & am ready for Biochem!

Not sure why he has such a low rating on this website. I felt like this class was very independently driven. If you want a good score on the test, it is very clear as to what you have to do. I honestly prefer his system of one midterm and one final- both are very straightforward. Highly recommend to others!

Loved class! Great for students who like to ask questions. He has some very rewarding office hours, and if your interested will go more in depth than in class. Only 1 midterm, and no graded HW. If you keep up with the HW (Exams are very similar to HW) you will be fine. If you don't... good luck. Would love to take another class from Ess!

The only two grades during the whole semester were the one midterm and the final. That sounds super threatening, but I promise you it wasn't that bad. I feel like he prepared us well enough for the tests. He also spent a lot more time on pre-biochem topics than other professors do which is really nice.

Professor Ess seems like a good guy... DONT TAKE OCHEM FROM HIM. Your grade in the class is solely based on 2 exams in the class. You don't have a textbook, and his lectures are almost entirely just him talking. You also have a mandatory study group, which, like what? I dropped this class and took it from a different professor, way better.

He is a really really nice guy and a pretty good lecturer but his class sucks. The material is really hard but the resources he gives aren't very helpful. 90% of your grade consists of 1 midterm and a final. Everything hinges on his lectures- the readings don't matter at all. Be wary of this class.

He is very intelligent and amazing in his field; however, I don't believe he is as great at teaching the material. He didn't give us a textbook and there were two things in the grade book, one midterm and one final. The tests are like 15+ pages and all free-response. He doesn't have any good hw or quizzes to help you practice. Horrible

DAN IS THE MAN. He assigns you into study groups that are actually the best thing ever. the TAs and Ess himself are SO easy to contact and they give great feedback. Ess' tests are made new every semester based off exactly what he teaches you. study hard, but no surprises at all. super fair, awesome class. super hard duh bc it's ochem but ILOVEDIT.

O chem with Dr Ess is different than other professors. There are no power points, its all on the chalk board, and the only two grades in the class were our tests. That being said, I dont think Ive ever learned more in a class than with him. Hes always super helpful in office hours and cares about his students really learning the material.

Doesn't use a textbook or lecture slides, instead teaches the principles in class using practice problems. His teaching is incredibly effective since he focuses on the principles behind the rules. Entire grade is based on a free response midterm and final. Requires students to meet with a study group made up of peers for 3 hours a week.

Dr. Ess is a super smart guy and can sometimes take it a little fast, so if you dont understand right away, write it down and ask him in office hours later. There was a ton of work outside class too, so if you have a big course load, consider taking this a different semester. I spent about 8-10 hours a week to keep up.

Dr. Ess is very reasonable, considering that ochem is a difficult subject. He curves tests and is clear on what you'll be tested on during lecture. The key to success is taking good notes and having a solid study group where everyone's willing to put in the time to master the material. He's also accessible outside of class and willing to help!!

Dr. Ess was a great professor for a very difficult class. Your entire grade is based off the midterm and the final so that's a little stressful and also makes your learning during the course completely self-driven. Use office hours and make sure you really understand the concepts and you'll do fine. Very rewarding and not a memorization class.

Dr. Ess is a great teacher. He teaches the concepts well, and provides many opportunities to learn. You are required to work in a group, but that helps a ton. O Chem was not as bad as some people claim, but it still requires a ton of work. Your whole grade relies on a midterm and a final. The tests are completely free response.

Nice guy, very smart. Makes class somewhere it's ok to give wrong answers. Your whole grade is almost completely based on a midterm and a final that are both free-response. Exams are a bit rough, but they get curved. You're assigned to work in study groups he chooses, which is the other bit of your grade. GO TO CLASS - that's how he writes exams!

Dr Ess is the BEST! He's so straightforward with tests, gives great feedback, inspirational, and is SO willing to work with you--he's a professor that genuinely wants you to succeed. OChem is a HARD class but he makes it doable, memorable, and enjoyable. Wish I could have taken all my chem classes from him.

Dr. Ess was a great OChem professor. I loved the format of the class and his emphasis on personal learning development. The team setting was also very helpful. He did an amazing job at explaining difficult chemistry concepts in class and he fostered the environment of learning. OChem was my favorite class because of him.

Dr. Ess really knows his stuff. It is a hard class but that is to be expected for Ochem. He teaches you everything you need to know in lectures. Doing the textbook readings before lecture is very helpful. One downside is Dr. Ess is not super accessible/approachable for help and his test keys are really specific.

I LOVE THIS MAN. He is so awesome. Some reviews say he is really stuck up and shouldn't be a teacher, but he was very accommodating and my favorite chem professor at BYU. Teaches they why behind every mechanism, and answers questions really well. I looked forward to going to class every day. Take from him!

So much respect for this man. He is incredibly knowledgeable-- he can answer almost any question you throw at him. He sometimes calls on random people to answer questions, but creates a classroom with a comfortable environment so it's no judgement if you get it wrong. His tests are basically his lectures, so take good notes! I learned so much!

Dr Ess was a very knowledgeable professor and a good man. However, the structure of the class made it very difficult to succeed. Tests were over 80% of the grade, and they were free response. The rest of the grade was composed of computer modeling assignments and how you worked with an assigned team. I would highly recommend somebody else.
