This class was HARD, because he expects students to know the "WHY" behind what he teaches, and not just the surface level knowledge that gets you by in most classes. His tests are extremely difficult, but they are curved, and he curves your overall grade too. I got an A in CHEM 352 in large part because this class prepared me so well for it.

All Ochem professors are difficult at BYU, but not all of them are reasonable. Dr. Ess is very reasonable, curves his tests, and wants students to succeed. Most of your grade is based on exams. I never read the textbooks, and he has no class slides. Attending class is crucial to get class notes, because that is what you're tested on. Great guy!
Dr. Ess is one of the best lecturers that I have ever had. He explains the concepts clearly and concisely. Pay attention to what he writes on the board because it will show up on the test.

I learned a lot in Dr. Ess's class, but he was SO inaccessible. He had like 5 hours of office hours for 200+ students, and they were always packed. Also, you need to answer test questions exactly like he would to do well, and he's not very flexible. If you have to take from him, you'll manage, but be prepared to work very hard.

Dr. Ess is an awesome professor. His lectures are very important to attend because most, if not all of what is on the test, is from lecture. Honestly if you listen in class and put in the time to do the HW problems he gives you, you'll be fine. Test's are hard, but it's OChem, it's a hard subject. He genuinely cares about students success, IMO

LOVE Dan! Lectures are THE most important part of the class, & he lectures really well. Pretty much never opened my textbook after the first week of class, other than to look at charts, bc he tests almost exclusively off of what he says in class, + off the homework problems he assigns (but hw isn't graded). Grade  4 tests, a paper, & the final

His teaching style is really effective and straightforward. If you pay attention and do what he tells you, you'll learn a ton. The hard part is, while homework isn't graded, it's absolutely essential if you want to do well on tests. Do the homework for your own good.

Has no filter. Can be super rude but the guy is a chemistry genius. He just makes you feel stupid to show how smart he is. Your whole grade is 4 tests and a final and one paper. No homework but the grading criteria is ambiguous on tests. His tests are based solely on what he says in class (or so he says).
The guy probably shouldn't have a job that requires him to interact with students. Very arrogant and rude.

Sure, he knows his stuff about chemistry, but he's rude, uninviting, and stuck up. His tests are extremely unclear- you need to put down 4 or 5 answers before you get the one he's looking for. Even if your other answers are correct, you won't get points for them. It seems like he's trying to put himself on a pedestal by making students feel dumb.

He is a good lecturer and his tests are super lecture heavy. Doesn't really seem to care about the students as much. Not accommodating when I had a mid semester injury and wasn't supposed to be taking tests even with multiple doctor's notes. Be prepared for your life to focus on his class.

He is smart and a good lecturer but that is the only good about the class. The structure of the class is very poor. Requires you to go to lecture or it will hurt your grade. At times he can seem very stuck up and demeaning to the students. I would take it from someone else if you could. If you're world doesn't revolve around ochem, find someone els

Dr. Ess is an amazing lecturer, one of the best I've had. However, his class structure is not conducive to learning. This semester you were only graded on three tests, nothing else. Thus, most of the class did nothing for the class except for a few days prior to a test. Homework and quizzes could have helped us all learn a lot more.

Great professor. very professional and teaches very well. It was a difficult class but he makes it doable. I enjoyed it and did fairly well. I feel like it can be hard to do really well but most everybody get a decent grade. Reading is necessary at times but the class is based mostly on lecture.

Dr. Ess knows a ton about O-Chem. If you really put in the work and go to class and go talk to him after class or  during office hours, you will be able to understand O-chem. When I say understand, it will make sense like another language or way of thinking and not just a bunch of scattered pieces of information.
He's a very fair grader, but it's a tough class. The reading is really necessary to understand the lectures. He does a great job making a tough class relevant to his students.

Dr. Ess was the best Chemistry professor I've had so far at BYU and I've had some really good Chemistry professors. He is extremely knowledgable, and therefore clear when he teaches. His grading is fair, and he does a good job at letting you know exactly whats on the tests. If you do the homework you should be fine.

Dr. Ess is a great teacher. He teaches the material clearly, if you pay attention in class you get a lot out of going. Doesn't use the boom much. There is a lot of HW, takes a lot of time, but it really prepares you for the tests. I loved Dr. Ess, favorite chem teacher so far.

TEST ADVICE: The tests felt like reading a foreign language. He uses confusing words such as "canonical" and "invoke." I got C's on the first two tests because I simply didn't understand the questions. When you answer the questions, answer them in at least 3 different ways, because 1 of those will probably be what the TA is looking for.

HARD class, but teaches OCHEM with clarity. Test's on the other hand... VERY unclear. You can make your answer look like it came straight out of the textbook, but your'll loose points anyway. Study like you've never studied before. Your'll learn a lot, but I definitely don't feel like my scores reflected my actual knowledge of the material.

Ess is a fantastic professor. Obviously 351 is a very challenging class, but if you put it the work you can succeed. Ess is a great lecturer and made Ochem enjoyable. His inclusion of MO theory and other sections might make him seem more difficult, but he really prepares you well for the MCAT.

Spectacular lecturer- the best I've ever had. Test grading protocol is nebulous at best- it's difficult to try to guess what information you ought to provide when it isn't asked for (lose points for not including a drawing he didn't ask for). Misleading disparity between quiz and test answer content (same question, same answer, lose points on test)

Dr. Ess is a fantastic choice for an organic chemistry professor. I can't imagine it being taught more clearly and thoroughly. You will come away from the class not only with a knowledge of OChem, but a true understanding of it. OChem is ALWAYS hard, he knows this and does all he can to help you succeed. If you put the effort in, it will pay off.

Dr. Ess really cares about his students and wants them all to do well.  Unfortunately, it's a hard class and there are boatloads of us, so you need to seek him out. If you go to his office and ask him the questions, he'll more than help you through the material.  It's rough, but if you keep up your end of the bargain, Dr. Ess will keep up his.

Dr. Ess was a good lecturer and explained the difficult concepts well. The class is massively curved so its tough to know where you stand although the averages on the tests was as low as 50 percent. The tests were long and could be a bit poorly worded. The key is to memorize the review slldes! I didn't bother with book problems after the first test
I also went into his office and was accused of not going through the exam key before hand, but oh well. Maybe not the most approachable but he's good at explaining the concepts.

I actually enjoyed taking the class from Ess. He went fast but was fun and competent. I felt like he explained the reasoning for the mechanisms really well. Hard class. Read the book. Memorize mechanisms. Tests were a bit sketchy but I had him for his first semester of teaching so that may have changed.

Great teacher.I had this class from Wood too and i understood it so much better w/ Ess.He explains with MO theory in detail so u know whats happening in the rxn, not just memorizing.this is by far the best way to teach o chem if u want to really understand it. i'm not one of those genious byu students and he helped me to get the difficult concepts

Professor Ess is a really good.Someone else complained that he uses MO theory but that was what made him great.He explained things in more detail than other o chem teachers(I took it from Wood too)using MO theory and that helped me to understand it.I knew what was going on instead of just memorizing.i'm not an A student and he made it manageable.

He is a good teacher, however you MUST read the book before attending lecture.  Otherwise, you won't have any idea what he is talking about.  Seriously. He will say if you choose between lectures and the book to study, go to lectures.  No.  Read the book, cause you'll have to read the book anyhow!  Just do both, you'll be fine.  It's not so hard

Dr. Ess is really hard. That being said, he's personable and fair. The thing about his class is that you HAVE to read the textbook before coming to class - if you do his lectures are clear and really helpful, if not you'll be totally lost.

Dr. Ess is friendly and personable, but often unclear. His lectures proceed at lightspeed, he ADORES molecular orbital theory, he does not set a grading scale, and there is no way to know your class standing at any point during the semester, even if you ask. Exams range from 1.5 to 5 hours in length. O-chem is hard; Ess doesn't make it any easier.
Dan makes this the easiest class ever. Lectures can be super boring but tests are open note/slides which was awesome. Definitely recommend taking him!

Dan is awesome! He is super clear on what you will be graded on and does his best to help out each of the students. His lectures are dense and you should pay attention in class for the quizzes. His tests are super nice: open note and online. He's super understanding and cares about his students.

Dr. Graham is simply ideal for Phil 201 and 202. He explains everything very thoroughly and is clear in what he wants you to do. If you pay attention in class and do the weekly quizzes, the 3 essays and tests are a breeze.

I really enjoyed this class. As long as you go, pay attention to the slides, and take the in-class quizzes each week you'll get an A. I found the material super interesting and all the tests are take-home and open-note! Would take again!

Dan is a really great guy. He tries to make the class fun but it is just such a boring class. He lectures the entire time and reads straight from the slides. Assignments are extremely easy. Tests are take home. Weekly quizzes in class - if you read the powerpoints, they are extremely easy. Overall, he wants to make the class easy.

One of the sweetest people I've ever met. He really cares about his students. Lots of reading and a short reflection due before most classes. He really loves what he teaches, and while it can be confusing, he's always willing to meet and help students. Other than the reflections, the main assignments are two presentations and a 10ish page paper.
“Prof Paul” is the best! He is so kind and caring, excellent at explaining weird Italian grammar/word concepts, and he grades very mercifully. I learned so much and did not feel stressed at all.

Super nice guy, although I don't feel like my Italian really improved much. Exams can be long  but they're like the homework, which I  felt was a bit time consuming , but its basically impossible to not get an A and Prof Paul is a really kind person.

Prof Paul was AMAZING! While it felt like there was always many assignments to do, I rarely spent more than an hour or two outside of class on them, pretty easy. The frequent quizzes and exams could be frustrating, but the subject wasn't too challenging, so it was not too bad. He challenged our language, and strove to answer our questions.

I've taken 321 and 340 from prof paul and he is by far one of my most favorite people on campus. He *actually* cares about his students and their wellbeing, and he teaches for understanding and appreciation. He's very adaptable and communicative. I have thoroughly enjoyed his classes and I can't recommend them enough

Professor Paul is a great teacher who really cares about his students. He is almost always available to help you if you need help outside of class. He is for sure on your side, all while trying to make sure that you get the most out of the course. I 100% recommend this class to anyone interested in Italian.

Dr. Paul is by far one of my favorite professors at BYU! He is so caring and truly such a great professor! If you are deciding between taking a class from him or someone else choose him!!! You will not regret it!

One of the best professors ever! Super caring and understanding which is reflected in his policies. Gives a TON of extra credit. Entrance exam is the final. He is seriously the best. There is HW for every class but it maybe takes 20-30 minutes and it is just for completion.

Super caring professor who understands students super well. He's patient and kind and helpful. There's homework every class which can be tedious but he's a great guy and because all the test and quizzes are online, it's pretty easy to get an A.
Great professor. Clear grading criteria and he is willing to work with you when figuring out grades or assignments. Very reasonable.

Professor Paul is a really great professor! If you do your best on all of the assignments and come to class, you will get an A. My one word of advice: don't buy the English grammar for students of Italian book. It was unnecessary. I never read one chapter of it. But do get the other books.
Prof Paul is awesome! Very helpful and accommodating. The class is pretty reasonable as far as work, eight one-page essays during the semester plus a page or so of homework every day.

An amazing professor. I had him for the graduate equivalent- STRAT560. This was my favorite class of the semester. He is really good at getting the content across and is good at not assigning "busy work". He is very kind, encouraging, and cares about his students lives. My classmates and I talk constantly about how awesome he is.

I don't know yet what I got in his class, but Professor Thomson is great. He's super caring, willing to answer questions, and makes an honest effort to make his class enjoyable and relevant. The cases can get long at times, but the quizzes and test (just one test!!) are not bad and the final project is very doable. Would definitely recommend!

I think Dan is a good person, and I have no quarrel with his character. Unfortunately, he is not qualified to teach. His case studies are extremely hard to get good grades on, and his quizzes and midterm are also pretty hard. He flies past material in class and doesn't prepare you for it at all. That being said, his final project is not too bad.

Every week there's a case study and every other week there's a chapter quiz. The final is a large group project. Overall its a pretty easy class. Make sure to put in lots of effort on the weekly case studies. Participation really matters and you're graded on it even though the class has 60+ people.

His class was initially unorganized, but improved throughout the semester. His grading got harder as the semester progressed, but the final project wasn't too difficult. He's a really easygoing guy and his tests and lectures were fine.

Dan Thomson was new when I had him. He was pretty disorganized, and the lectures were frankly pretty boring. He is an adjunct, so take that into consideration. He was a nice guy, and he'll probably get better in future semesters, since he didn't have a lot of time to prepare.

JUST TAKE CS 474 FROM HIM! I learned a lot, and his lectures are always fun! Also, COME TO CLASS! His lectures are CRUCIAL to understand the readings. This was the best class for me so far, so HAVE FUN!

The older ratings on RMP for CS 474 from Dr. Ventura scared me a bit it looked like the ratings got better over time so I decided to take my chances. I am very glad I did. The projects can be challenging but you are building cool things. If you are interested and put in the effort, you can accomplish it. Take this class if you want to learn AI.

His lectures were clear; I never left confused. During lectures, he's always open to answering questions and is concise in his answers. He knows his stuff. I typically spent 4-8 hours on weekly labs. The final project requires you to log 30 hours, so get started early. Hands down, the coolest class I've ever taken! Def gonna TA for this class

Dr. Ventura does a great job teaching this course--the lectures are fantastic. The labs can be a bit clunky, but I have definitely learned a TON about PyTorch and deep learning, and Dr. Ventura makes the class super enjoyable. He has definitely worked out the kinks from pervious reviews that said it was disorganized. 10/10 would recommend!

I really liked Dr. Ventura. He is super familiar teaching the course material and so it often felt pretty clear what we were learning about. The class is hard but the fact is CS 312 is a hard class in general and you have to take it from someone, might as well take it from someone who's experienced and teaches it well.

Good lecturer, not very accessible outside of class. Bad experiences with TAs. No late work allowed (1 minute late is a 0). Tests were not difficult, interesting material and it was presented in a good way.

no late homework tolerance at all which is kinda unreasonable, projects are rough but doable but expect them to take a ton of time, and doesn't use learning suite except for submitting assignments, insisting on using his own website. At least his is slightly better than other cs professors that do this.

The class was pretty time intensive but the lectures and labs where helpful. Good TA's options to help you get through the labs. No tests, just labs. I usually had to spend about 10 hours a week to get labs to work. You could probably get half credit on labs with 5 hours. Actually legit, image recognition, face generation, text generation.
Dr Ventura is so good at explaining difficult concepts and his classes are super organized. CS 312 isn't an easy class, but I learned more from this class than any other in my CS undergrad.

Dr. Ventura assigns enormous labs and has a 0 late work policy. I explained to him my extenuating circumstances and he rejected my request for an extension on a lab. Not cool. He is also obviously more focused on his research than on his teaching. Do yourself a favor and take this difficult class from a professor that actually cares about you.
Completely inflexible and subjective with grading. I was extremely disappointed with the lack of effort put into teaching and accommodating students.

He's a cool guy but it's so difficult to catch him outside of class. He doesn't have official office hours and if you want to set something up he takes so long to respond back it almost seems like he's trying to avoid meeting with students after class. I'd just make sure to triple read the syllabus so you know what to expect

I took Ventura for CS312 so I was looking forward to this class. However honestly it feels like his first time teaching this class. So poorly organized, it feels like he doesn't completely understand the material. Labs are much harder than anything he goes over in lecture so I'd consider this class self taught tbh. No late work is accepted either.

This class didn't seem too difficult. but man he's a tough grader. There were times I would literally do my homework and check it with the TAs and still lost many points. I would study for hours, and lost LOADS of points on trivial things on exams. The labs are a pain because not only do you have to get the lab working, but then write a report.

Dr. Ventura seems like a nice guy but he is a merciless grader. Tests were poorly written and graded very subjectively. I felt I understood everything on the final yet somehow only got a 78%. Nothing feels worse than scoring low on material that you thoroughly understand. His lectures are avg but he struggles to sufficiently explain complex topics.

He's a great teacher. There's no ambiguity of what's expected of you. If you read, pay attention in lectures, and turn in homework on time you will succeed. He explains each of the algorithms covered in the class really well. He's very good at relating what we are learning to real-world application.
Good at lectures, but merciless in grading, and over trivial things. Late assignments are a 0. Unless you're just taking a couple classes, save yourself the stress and go with another professor.

Lectures are slow and boring. But if you can last through them, they're quite helpful. Personally I missed about half of them and did fine in the class. Projects are tricky so start early and get TA help. This class can be interesting if you take the time to do the readings and watch Youtube videos about the topics.

Professor Ventura is a good professor. His lectures aren't mandatory, but it's almost essential to attend all of them in order to get all the material you need for the projects and exams. He doesn't accept any late work.

Prof Ventura is a sweet spirit. I personally didn't like the book and found his lectures to be more helpful in understanding the content. His humor is very genuine and childlike, fun to attend class. The labs weren't too bad and once you get the hang of the homework that isn't too bad either

Dr. Ventura is a poor lecturer and you'd do much better in his class if you just skipped it all together and just watched youtube videos or attended another professors lectures. He seems really focused on his research and doesn't care much about his students or classes. He doesn't accept any late work and the labs are very poorly written.

I am a Bioinformatics major so I was worried about taking this class without the same CS background as other students. Dr Ventura did a great job at explaining things clearly, making me feel like I could understand everything. He is easily the best CS professor I have had at BYU. It's a lot of work, but a good class

Dr. Ventura is passionate, skilled, and approachable. He was fair and clear with his requirements. His lectures were extremely helpful, and he was always willing to spend time to thoroughly answer questions both in and outside of class. He made lectures interesting and fun. Exams were challenging but satisfying - fair and properly representative.

It's tough to rate Ventura. He has an engaging, passionate style. Can be inspiring. But as I interacted with him more, I felt he ultimately does this because it's his job, not because he cares. If questioned, it's my-way-or-the-highway. He even defensively refused to speak with me once, seeming very insecure. This made learning tough for me.

Dr. Ventura made the class very interesting and was capable of explaining concepts and algorithms clearly. Lectures felt important and interesting, and Dr. Ventura even managed to work some humor into the class.

He is very entertaining and just an all around good teacher. Algorithm design in inherently boring, but he did a great job of applying it to real world applications. The labs are difficult but aren't that long, so as long as you go to class and do the homework (due every lecture) you can definitely do well.

Honestly, he was a good guy.  He has a positive attitude and nice.  The only thing that bugged me about him was when he said that grades do not matter.  If grades don't matter, then just give me an A.

I came into this class expected Dr. Ventura to be a hard teacher, but in reality the class was very doable. He teaches clearly and in a way to help everyone understand. The class has 6 projects (5 individual, 1 group) and hw due each class period. It's a valuable class and I enjoyed it!

I have a 3.91 gpa even after taking this crazy class. This is the lowest grade I have ever receive, yet with the work I put in and with my grade compared to the other students, I should have received a higher grade. The class average was 69% in this class. He is a very nice guy, but doesn't teach. Tests are aweful. I had to live with the TAs.

Dr. Ventura is an amazing lecturer, but grading procedures are designed to make students fail on the homework and tests, not make them succeed. His TAs will generally deduct the maximum points possible for mistakes. Successful students tend to get their answers on the Internet.

I would like to say that Professor Ventura isn't a hard teacher. His classes may be difficult but that's because of the nature of the subject. He's a great teacher that tries to simplify the best he can and is very fair with grading and class policies. I recommend him to all students and recommend they take advantage of TA and office hours.
Dr. Ventura fed us some muffins during the final exam, and the muffins were amazing. He is an awesome teacher of a subject that is very difficult to understand.

I really came to love theory after taking 252 from him. He explains things quite well, and manages to make the subject matter fascinating. I will be taking from him again. That isn't to say that he isn't tough. His test are just that, but if you put in the time to do the hw, you will learn the material. Highly recommended professor.
Prof. Ventura is great, he makes class interesting and enjoys teaching the subject. It is a difficult class and not one I wanted to take but he made it worth while.

Hard class, but I enjoyed every second.  He's a very fun teacher and makes what could be a boring subject VERY interesting.  DO THE HOMEWORK WITH THE TA'S!  I started the semester trying to do it on my own.  After the first test, I switched.  they are brutal with points and you need to learn how they think so that you do the tests right.

he's a really fun professor.  i went in a couple times and surprised him in his office with questions.  he didn't seem to mind.  DO YOUR HOMEWORK WITH THE TA'S!  THEY WILL BE BRUTAL AND TAKE OFF LOTS OF POINTS!  very tricky class, but very interesting and fun.
He is an awesome teacher. I hated the material but because of how he taught I loved it after. The only thing is, his tests are very tricky....

One of the best teachers I've had in a CS class. Very easy to understand! He really allows the class to learn at their own pace. He enjoys the material and actually cares for the individual students. I never wanted to miss class.

I highly recommend this blended class to anyone who wants to learn how to cook, already knows how to cook, and those in between! The class is SO much fun! The textbook readings are long, but if you skim, you'll be fine. The lecture videos are 10 minutes or less, which is so nice. Try to get to know Dana during lab, she is the coolest.

I love Dana! She is so fun and this class is a blast! If you have room in your schedule, definitely take it! She has a passion for teaching and does a great job connecting with her students and helping you to learn new skills. She wants to see you succeed.
Dana is fantastic! Her class is well organized and the expectations are clear. She's fun to talk to, and when you understand her sarcasm, it's even better.

I enjoyed cooking in Dana's class. She was intimidating at first but then I just saw her as a very structured teacher. She cares about her students and is super good at cooking. I didn't read the textbook and got by just fine.
Dana Hunter is one of my favorite professors! She is very fun and down to earth. Just beware of assignment deadlines, as she is not very lenient about late work.

Never regretted anything more than taking a class with this professor. I initially took this for an elective credit as most people do for this class. However, once the semester started, it was obvious Professor Hunter took the class way too serious. She had no empathy for a family death that impeded on my class participation and was overall rude.

I've had Professor Hunter in the past and her classes are truly awesome. She does her best to connect with students and in class time is great. I think this semester she may have tried to up the difficulty level.I don't think a lot of her quizzes/tests were well worded or tested what she was trying to test. However, I'm sure the class will improve.

Takes your grade from 20 points to 15 with one mistake, is quite critical when you ask for help, and does not give you resources to succeed on exams. She is passionate about food, but I would not take this class again.

Dana is one of the sweetest profs out there! She is super helpful if you have special circumstances, and I was excited to go to class each week. The recipe packet is invaluable, and i use it on a weekly basis to this day... each recipe is built to be pretty easy to put together and made with ingredients that are easily accessible. Take this class!

I loved this class!! I looked forward to it every week. Pick a good group because you'll be with them all semester. Mine was awesome :) I learned a bunch and I will totally be taking more classes from her when I can in the future.

This class was what I looked forward to attending each week, not having to stress about loads of homework or assignments; I could show up and cook for 1.5 hrs. Cooking in a small group was enjoyable, you get to know each other and expand your skills and knowledge in the kitchen. She's willing to help you get back on the right track if you get lost.

Super awesome class!! You cook once a week and the class is pretty easy. The exams are a breeze because they are just composed of quiz questions that you have already seen. The quizzes are open book/open note and the textbook is like literally the coolest book ever. Awesome class!

Look her up under Dana Adcock for more reviews. This lady is amazing! I already felt comfortable in the kitchen and felt like I knew a lot, but I still learned so much! This class is really just a fun class where you make food and Dana makes it awesome. She has very clear expectations too which is helpful.

Professor Becerra has a lot of readings each week and the tests focus on memorizing 3 or 4 bullet points about a topic that can be tricky. I've attended other religion classes that are a lot more spiritually uplifting instead of just focused on memorization. Overall a good professor and not too hard to get an A. His classes are small.

Hands down favorite religion class I have taken. He encourages a lot of group discussion and is a super knowledgeable guy. He is also super funny and made the 2 hour class feel like an hour. Take good notes in class and you'll be fine. Take this class!
I did not enjoy this class and I found it very hard to get an A. He didn't care to learn your name even though there was only like 20 people in the class. Overall wouldn't recommend

Dr. Becerra is awesome. His approach to theology is inclusive and his class is history-heavy, which I really like. He makes it clear that he's not grading you on your testimony. His TA graders are pretty picky though so make sure to really read through what they want before you submit an assignment.

I loved Brother Becerra! I was worried this class would be super doctrine-heavy, but it was a good mix of doctrine and spiritual opinion/theory-based discussion. There is a lot of reading and a short writing assignment every week, but it's doable. Take good notes in class and review the weekly quizzes to do well on exams.
Love him, would not recommend his class. Tries to make simple things very doctrinally confusing.

Brother Becerra is super great and his classes are really uplifting and informative. There's a ton of reading every week though. This is the last religion class I needed and I've never had one that required so many different readings every week. Exams aren't too hard but there is a lot of "select all except" or "select all that apply" questions.

Although the class took a lot of time and work, Prof Becerra cared about his students, and wanted us to grow as people, which I appreciate. If you are wanting an easy religion credit, this might not be the one for you. If you want to truly build your testimony and put in a good amount of effort to the class, you'd love it!

Professor Becerra seems like a good guy but his class was not it. I rarely felt the spirit throughout the semester. He assigns tons of readings and a lot of them aren't uplifting at all. He's a very picky grader. You will get docked on almost any writing assignment/paper if you don't include your word count...kind of ridiculous.
Daniel was great. He was super caring and a great guy. Lectures were easy to follow and tests/quizzes were super easy

Daniel is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. You can tell he truly cares about his students, and he is so understanding of God's love and how to show it. I learned so much about the history and context of the New Testament and I really enjoyed it. The class is the perfect amount of work for a religion class.

Such a great class! You do the readings, weekly journal assignments, and class quiz. The quizzes and powerpoints tell you everything you need to know to pass the exams. Super fun, engaging teacher, focuses on facts and points out what things are theory/can't be proven.

Dr. Becerra is super friendly and very open to different views. Sometimes it was hard to keep track of assignments on learning suite because he adds them as the class goes. If you aren't very interested in New Testament historical context, then you probably don't want to take this class.

I also took his 211 class and loved it so much I took this one too! I really appreciate his open-mindedness (especially for a religion class) and his willingness to include marginalized communities and how they apply to what we are learning. He brings in all perspectives, not just old white men. He also really knows his stuff!

Dr. Becerra is a great professor. We had a lot of reading for every class, but it was all needed, I felt. He is very inclusive, if that is something you are looking for. Very knowledgable on the context of the New Testament. Tests were very easy.

According to all known laws of aviation, there is no way a bee should be able to fly. Its wings are too small to get its fat little body off the ground. The bee, of course, flies anyway because bees don't care what humans think is impossible.

Daniel is an excellent professor and I loved his class. He is kind, funny, respectful, and his lectures are very informative and engaging. He kept class very straightforward and organized and I really appreciated that. He is always willing to help you if you're struggling to keep up with assignments or have additional questions.

Great professor, makes the lectures feel very meaningful and he genuinely cares about the students. He is also able to approach issues in a way that feels meaningful rather than brushing them under the rug. However, there is a lot of reading assigned, although you can get away with skimming it most of the time.

Dr. Becerra is a great religion professor, albeit with an ego. None of the assignments are difficult, and it doesn't take too much studying to do well on his test. He focuses a lot more on the historical and academic perspective of scriptures instead of the doctrinal perspective, which I appreciated, but others did not. Highly recommend.

Prof Becerra was great. He helped me see the gospels from a broader perspective of Christianity and the world than most BYU rel classes. Some students didn't like readings not from LDS sources, but I thought that was the best part of the class. Professor Becerra is extremely inclusive and welcomes all perspectives which is really important to me.

I'm sure Professor Becerra is a great guy, but I did not like the way he structured his class. He has us reading a ton of controversial opinions, and I honestly don't feel like it helped me with my testimony at all. I did not enjoy doing the readings, unlike my other religion classes, and a lot of the readings just felt like a joke.
I'm sure he's a great guy, but this class was so boring. He just didn't make it very engaging.
This guy rules. Genuinely one of my favorite professors ever. Super down to earth and communicates clearly. Also goes into great detail and offers super interesting insights. 10/10 would take again.

Brother Becerra was awesome! Enough work to learn but not enough to make it stressful at all. All you have to do it take good notes from the lectures, take 2 open note quizzes each week, and one easy writing assignment. Tests are straightforward, pretty much all of the answers are straight off of the quizzes. Good guy, super kind. Take it!

Be prepared for more doctrine and less of the spiritual side of the B.O.M. Becerra's semester project is intimidating but it's totally doable, do the writing assignments, and the readings, take good notes on his power slides/make quizlets of the quiz questions, and be prepared for some frustrating discussions w/him in class and you'll do great.

Professor Becerra's class was amazing. We touched on a bunch of interesting topics that you typically don't in a class. I wasn't always super engaged, but the class was not that hard. The tests were online, but were hard. He pulls questions from the quizzes, so study them for an easy A.

Took this as my last religion class, to be fair I was looking for an easy class that I could breeze through. This class would be good for freshmen with lots of motivation. After 1 absence, every other one is a percentage off your final grade- two quizzes and 1 paragraph a week, tests are proctored. He lectures like a high school history teacher

Becerra is definitely my favorite teacher at BYU! He is so smart and truly knows what he is talking about. The quizzes are extremely easy if you take notes during class. The tests are so. easy. There's a decent amount of reading but I think he is trying to lower that. He really makes learning about the BOM entertaining!

Professor Becerra is awesome. You have a quiz before each lecture, and then about a paragraph of writing for each week. Sounds like a lot, but its super easy. Only 1 midterm and 1 final worth half of your grade, but they are very easy and questions are EXACTLY (90%) or extremely similar to quizzes. (seriously, study quizzes!). Super easy class!!!!!

This guy sucks!!! Most questions were answered with idk. We didnt read the Book of Mormon, he glazed over the whole thing the 1st 2 lectures. All he cares talking about is including LGBTQ+ into everything, taking it too far in regards to church standards. If you dont want to learn about the BOM take this class. I have 0 respect for this man.

I loved Dr. Becerra's class so much that I also chose to take REL A 121 from him. Both classes were on-demand and followed the same structure: reading then lecture then quiz with DD assignments at the end of the lecture. He expects more work than other religion professors, but I like the historical view of the gospel rather than only spiritual.

Dr. Becerra's lectures were AMAZING. He tied real life into the BOM beautifully. That being said, the amount of readings there were was insane. The prof. himself was super cool and the environment was spiritually enriching. He knew a ton. But the workload felt like 3 credits. Lectures are more important than readings for quizzes, take good notes!

Good class. Not overly spiritual, the assignments are pretty easy but he can be kind of unforgiving. I was a couple hundred under the word count for our final paper and it was pass or fail, worth 10% of our grade. He gave me a zero on that assignment and only gave my 50% after I asked for mercy. Overall it was an ok class.
This guy is incredibly smart and teaches very well. He answered questions really well, and was super prepared for each class. I liked this class a lot!

I really recommend Professor Becerra! His lectures are interesting and interactive, and he has a lot of knowledge on the subjects. One thing I would say is that it is pretty important to attend class everyday because some of the quiz questions are on things that he says, rather than what he wrote in the power point, but the quizzes aren't too bad

I felt like this was a pretty easy class overall. Just memorize all the quiz answers for midterms and finals! The class is very relaxed and I love how Professor Becerra makes everyone feel comfortable and included. I did feel like the lectures didn't match all the quiz questions, but most of the time he puts the lecture slides on learning suite!

This class is absolutely amazing! I was hesitant at first because this class is more academic than my previous religion classes, but I have learned so much. He knows how to teach with the Spirit, paves the way for a lot of great discussion, and provides great differing points of view. The tests are super easy if you study the learning objectives.

Prof. Becerra is awesome!! He made this class so enjoyable and uplifting. Tests aren't hard and they're basically taken straight from the quizzes. There's a bit of reading to do, but it's honestly not bad. Lectures are awesome. If you're going to take RELA121, take it from him!

Dr. Becerra is amazing! He got better throughout the semester and was open to feedback. I appreciate how he always tried to grow & adapt to the needs of students. There is a good amount of reading, about an hour a week. The class doesn't require much work. He is clear about what will be on the test, so only a little studying is needed. Pretty easy!

He is such a kind, inclusive professor, and such a genuinely good person from what I saw. I took him spring semester, so the class was more condensed, but it was a bit of work. However, the work wasn't very difficult, you just had to put in the time.

I absolutely loved Professor Becerra! He was very open to feedback and made sure that all students felt welcome and had the opportunity to succeed. I learned a lot from this class. There were discussions that were significant to the learning environment. A lot of readings were required for the class but it was totally worth it!

Daniel is so great!! I wish I had him in person so that I could get to know him better. Daniel does a great job of emphasizing equality and acceptance among his students, which is very refreshing for a religion professor. His tests are derived almost entirely from the weekly quizzes, so if you study the quiz questions, the tests are super easy!

Daniel is a great teacher. he cares about balance in his students lives, so he's not gonna let you forget you have the class but its not gonna kill you at all. i wish all religion professors modeled after him. ive taken 2 classes from him and they have been the best 2 religion classes i have taken here at BYU. take from him, you wont regret it.
Awesome professor. Decent work load but manageable, and inspiring. Hes happy to help and answer questions. Highly recommend taking a class from professor Becerra!

I wanted to rate Professor Becerra because of how hard he tried with the covid situation and giving on-demand lectures. He certainly tried his best and he really is a good professor (not that I think many other people would say he's a bad one). Definitely hope to take an in person class with him down the line!

Daniel is a really great teacher for The Book of Mormon. He has studied theology and has a great interest in the scriptures, and you can really tell that from the lectures. The class was entirely online, but I only had to watch two lectures every week. The reading can be a handful, so try to space it out where you can and you will be just fine.

I love Brother Becerra, he's incredibly thoughtful and always brings interesting and new perspectives to gospel topics I've heard about my whole life. He definitely has an academic take on the scriptures but is also heavy on testimony and the spirit. His class was one of the most inclusive I've been in at BYU! Can't recommend enough.

Professor Becerra is super cool and you can tell he is smart and has some real knowledge about the New Testament. Overall cool class and I learned some cool things, he focuses more on intellectual than spiritual learning. He makes it way too difficult with his quizzes and tests. Still managed to get an A and he's a great guy, but it was TOUGH.

Please take your class from Brother Becerra! He has a strict attendance policy, but I had health issues this semester and he excused all of my absences. His lectures are very straightforward. As long as you take notes and pay attention, you'll do great. He has daily quizzes, and the midterm and final have almost the same questions.

Bro. Becerra is a really caring, nice guy. He has a lot of passion for the gospel and really helps you to work through complexities within it. Homework is really manageable, and all the answers to the quizzes are on the powerpoints in class, so just take notes and you'll be fine.

Professor Becerra is honestly one of the best professors that I've had at BYU. His lessons are so spiritual, yet grounded. He has a lot of passion for what he teaches. His quizzes and exams are pretty straight forward. If he mentions that it is on the quiz, it is gonna be on the quiz. If you have questions, you can email him for clarification

I really hate religion classes at BYU; that being said, Dr. Becerra is an awesome choice. I feel like my understanding of the new testament has really helped me grow. He's very clear on expectations and grades fairly. Tests weren't too bad either.

The grading criteria isn't very known. He tests you on stuff that you have to have heard in class and just remembered in order to know the answers. This makes it hard, he didn't have any reviews so it's hard to know what to study for the tests. He did bring the spirit and I learned a lot, but it's hard to be tested on things you don't remember.

I am in loveeee with Bro. Becerra. He is absolutely amazing. His class wasnt overly demanding, but I still learned so much. I loved the way he taught and he was always very clear about what would be expected of you throughout the course. I have a completely new understanding of the New Testament.

I absolutely loved this class. Outside class work was just readings for the lectures, short quizzes on the lectures, and a short response to one of the readings once a week. He really took the time to learn everyone's names, listened to comments during class, and encouraged discussion. Note: we only played Kahoot once.
The class is great and Dr. Becerra is very insightful. His first year teaching at BYU he is already doing a great job. The class is not an easy A though, so be ready to put in the work to pass it.

This is the best religion class at BYU and its mad easy. Daniel is hilarious and his lectures are incredible. He brings in a ton of different perspectives that make the Savior more universal. Seriously-- this class will be such a blessing.

I really loved this class. He is laid back but in a way that he still has control over the lecture and students. He gives great lectures that give a different perspective to gospel topics emphasizing the importance of minorities and women. Quizzes are taken after every class that are the exact test questions so going to class is super important.

Great professor, who genuinely cares for his students. There are readings and quizzes for every lecture, but they are 100% manageable. He is so willing to work with you if you can't make it to class for any reason. He was great at leading discussions as well, loved his class.

HONESTLY, such a great teacher. His lessons are so clear and he's such a good guy, I'd take his class any day. He has a great, welcoming class environment. I LEARNED A LOT and felt the spirit. I always felt welcome and always felt like I was learning. He's way organized to and CLEAR!

What a great guy. He loves the material and the students. Very willing to work with students on grades and open to teaching suggestions. Teaches in the savior's way by involving students and teaching doctrine. Strong spirit in his class room with the right amount of humor. Bro Becerra is the best.

Professor Becerra is a great guy. You can tell that he's new and still learning the ropes, but he cares a lot about the material and students. I really appreciated how willing he was to work with me. He also gives fun "Kahoot" quizzes that are ungraded, but questions from these quizzes appear on the midterm and final (study guide provided).

Dr Milton is AMAZING. His lectures are so engaging and he's really good at encouraging good class discussions. He's also very accessible outside of class and is so willing to help you out and to give good feedback. I could tell he genuinely cared about me and all of his students. Genuinely one of my favorite professors I have had at BYU!

Professor Milton is SUCH a good teacher. Super engaging lectures and relevant material. Gives great feedback on policy memos. Reasonable grader. Really helps you prepare for final exam and gives opportunity for you to get a good grade (if you participate often and show that you care). Great career advice and always willing to chat. Also very funny.

I took Art260 from Daniel. He remembers everyone by name and is very caring. He is knowledgeable about photography and well-qualified to be teaching the class. I highly recommend taking a class from him!

Daniel Everett is a phenomenal professor. His courses are well outlined, consistently structured and very engaging. He tells you exactly what he expects, while giving you ample room to explore new media and ideas and is constructive with his feedback. 10/10 would recommend

Daniel is an awesome teacher! He gives great feedback and is helpful during the brainstorming process without taking over. He really opened my mind as to what art can be, it's more than just good and bad art. He is a very specific grader and I think he expected a lot of us, but he wasn't a harsh grader. He really cares for his students growth.

Can't believe this guy was not on here. AMAZING instructor. He's Peter Everett's younger brother and is super cool. He is constructive, but not critical on you and your projects and very open minded. I really learned how to think differently in this course and my work improved a great deal. I most definitely recommend him.

If I could rate him higher than 5, I would. He's genuinely so good at teaching writing improvement. There was one assignment that took me several hours over the weekend, but he does a great job pacing the course and helping students succeed! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!! He also organizes groups to help with peer review, and they became my good class friends!

The grading is pretty harsh in this class, but he lets you rewrite your work to improve your score. Although, only half of the assignments met this criteria, as the rest were not graded by the end of the semester. He wants you to succeed!

Dr. Frost truly cares about his students and wants all to succeed. He is a tough grader but gives you the opportunity to rewrite and submit your papers as many times as needed. He is willing to give you feedback and help as much as you need.

Disappointing class. Papers graded very harshly, which is OK, but the thing that frustrated me was that I didn't know how to improve. I would follow the rubric as best I knew how, but then I would still get some of the worst scores I've received in my 3 years at BYU. Also, I didn't feel like I learned much about how to actually write better.

Dr. Frost is great! He grades harshly, but you can rewrite your papers until you get the grade you want. However, only 1/3 papers were graded before the semester ended, so that didn't end up helping. Don't feel like I learned much honestly. It's "writing and presenting" but you spend 1 day on presenting. He is a stellar professor though! Easy A.

Dr. Frost is excellent. I took away so many useful skills for my writing and presenting from this class. His papers are not simple, but he gives you class time to work on them as well as one-on-one consultations. You won't regret taking this class from him.
Guys, I love Dr. Frost so much. He boosted my confidence as a writer and helped me get on track to get my public scholarship posted! The papers were a ton of work but well worth it.

Dr. Frost is an excellent professor and he does a great job of working with each student individually to help them improve their work. The assignments in this class are all purposeful and not too challenging, but they do promote growth and good quality work. This class makes publication seem possible and within reach.

Professor Frost is AMAZING! He is a real human and is willing to work with studnets. I'm convinced that I would not have made it through this class if I had had a different professor. That is not to say that he is lenient with students, or gives out easy As, but he understands that we all struggle and senior cap stones are hard to write!

Professor Frost is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so patient and so accessible. If you need time to meet, or have a question about a topic/homework, just email him! He is very responsive! Also, the topics he teaches are so interesting. You can tell he has a lot of passion and knowledge for his subject!
The readings are often difficult to understand, but he goes over them in class. The weekly writing assignments arent too hard, but to get a good grade you should take them seriously.

Professor Frost is awesome. I really loved his class and I learned a ton. He was really good about helping students interact in class. He really cares about students and the material. Pretty much every Saturday there is a short essay due that covers readings but they are pretty easy. There is a midterm and a final that aren't too hard.

I really enjoyed Dr. Frost's class, and he did a great job presenting information from multiple perspectives. Attendance is required, and make sure you tune in. He is quick to respond to emails, and his advice is always helpful. The topics are quite controversial and he does a good job moderating multiple perspectives. Would recommend this class.

Class was average, though there was lots of reading, you HAVE to go to the lectures if you're not understand or you won't pass the class. Has a small paper due just about every week and a term paper, but only two tests throughout the course. Good class just to get that credit over and done with.

Favorite professor in BYU so far! He was so nice and knowledgeable, I learned so much from him! Loved answering questions! There were about 10 writing assignments through the semester, two quizzes a week, one big essay, and two exams (midterm and final.) Takes a while to get your grades back, though. Besides that, awesome! 100% recommend!

Solid professor, super nice and intelligent. There are short weekly essays and the TA's can be tough on them, but the workload isn't too bad. Participation quizzes and in class writings for attendance (doesn't mark zoom attendance, but you need to go to class for the in class writings). Tests aren't too bad but include essays. 1 miderm, 1 final
Loved his class! Professor Frost is very accessible and knowledgeable. He actively encourages his students and wants them to succeed. Fair, understanding grading. Would definitely recommend!
Stellar professor, make sure you really read the cases. Interesting material, but a little dry at times so find some way to pay attention.

You can tell he really cares about his students but this class is overall hard. Lots of work with weekly mini essays and quizzes. Quizzes are super easy as they are open notes but the midterm and final is really hard. If you take this class be prepared to spend a lot of time doing assignments and a final project that is like 12 pages long.

I originally dreaded this class, I was just taking it to complete the GE. However, I ended up really enjoying it. Dr. Frost has great lectures and is good to his students. Once I forgot to turn in an assignment and he was very understanding and gave me full credit even though it was late. Tests are fair but the class requires a lot of reading.

Really enjoyed this class! Learned a ton about healthy dating/marriages & not just from a religious standpoint. Bro Frost was kind and approached sensitive issues with an open mind. The readings were fabulous and actually helped me in my current relationship. Lots of reading, quizzes each week, short essays due each week, but not hard at all

Dr. Frost was a great professor. This class has an intense amount of reading, and if you struggle with reading ancient philosophy it isn't easy to get through. That being said, Dr. Frost made it easy to understand the material in his lectures and was incredibly helpful when he was asked questions. The tests aren't bad, just be ready to write essays

Dr. Frost is great at explaining things! I thought POLI201 would be like American Heritage, so I took it. It was so hard, though, because of all the writing. Most of the final grade was based on essays. Worth it, though, because it is interesting. I took this online during the pandemic, so I had a ton of free time. Hard for a STEM major like me.

Dr. Frost is an amazing professor who provides a lot of amazing insights into the philosophies of the Western World. Philosophy itself is not easy, but Dr. Frost's lectures and discussions help make the readings more bearable. Tests are easy if you do the readings. Pop quizzes are possible, but, again, if you do the readings they're possible!

I LOVE Dr. Frost, he is so kind and understanding. The philosophy paper was challenging to write, but each of the TAs I talked to were helpful and (to me at least) clear in their grading/expectations. You are graded on open-note quizzes, 10 short SRs, a paper, some in-class writing assignments, and midterm/final. Challenging, but very doable.

Dr. Frost was an absolutely amazing professor and I always looked forward to his classes. His lectures are extremely insightful and Dr. Frost is an extremely intelligent person. He's really nice and asks a lot of questions, prompting lots of discussion and participation in class. Tests are not hard but they require studying. I highly recommend him!

A 5 is not high enough for Professor Frost, but is too high for most TAs. Amazing lectures, clear on class requirements, made content interesting. In-class writing assignments for attendance. Tests weren't bad (MC + essays). Awesome class environment. TA graded papers were inconsistent, but gave feedback when asked, and my scores improved.

Frost was a very nice professor, pretty clear in lectures. The slides are accessible and he is always willing to clear things up for you. Aside from that, the TAs are a bit of a nightmare, the reading lengths are sometimes inordinate, and for a GE, too much work. Unless you LOVE philosophy, I would suggest a different class for this requirement.

Essays are graded by TAs, which is what the majority of the grade is based upon. Multiple choice on tests is easy and straightforward, and he gives a pretty detailed study guide, This might be a great class for people who are interested in political philosophy, but I realized how much I hate philosophy early on. Liked Dr. Frost but hated the class.

Here's my problem. I got a 97% in my upper-division philosophy class, where all my papers were graded by someone who has a Ph.D. in philosophy from Princeton. I got a 90% in professor Frost's general-ed philosophy class, where all the papers were graded by a TA who wasn't even studying philosophy. I put more effort into professor Frost's class.

His TAs are problematic. I checked my term paper with one of them, who said it just needed a couple of revisions (which I made). I turned it in and got a B-. The rest of the semester I was getting As on the papers, so it didn't seem like reliable grading to me. Plus, he docked me 3 points for reasons not found on the rubric.
Doctor Frost is an amazing professor! The class content is insightful in both a political and religious sense. Doctor Frost is possibly the best professor I have had all year.

600 word weekly "summary and response" essays were a joke. Your grade in the class almost solely depends on these essays and the TA's grade very subjectively. No feed back is given. Grading is random. They probably throw a dart on a board for grades. My 'A' papers were as good as my 'C' papers. Most weeks only 3 people in about 200 got a 10/10.

Honestly, he is nice, but you don't have enough time to have personal relationship with him because the class size is massive. His lecture is hard to understand, especially very unclear what to study for the test. Indeed, it was one of the worst class ever. I trusted the previous feedbacks before I took this class, and I regret my decision.

Dr. Frost has been my favorite professor at BYU. He is incredibly smart, and leads great discussions in class. This class has made me change my minor to political philosophy. I highly recommend that you take this class. There is a lot of reading, but it is totally worth it. My understanding of the world is much more enhanced now.

I loved this class! Professor Frost is so kind and I really enjoyed his lectures. There is reading and a reading quiz due before every class. Every week there is a short paper due, and only 2 tests. Definitely would recommend.

Professor Frost is honestly one of the easiest professors I have taken any college classes from. He is a easy professor not because the material is easy, but because he is incredibly generous, and very very straight forward. HE IS NOT a professor that plays games. he is also a really good lecturer.

I took this class solely for the GE credit but it ended up being my favorite class! Dr. Frost is the nicest guy in the world and really knows what he is talking about. This class basically got me through my first semester at BYU!

Reading quizzes due every class that are easy. Sometimes does in class writings so go to lecture. Weekly essays that are easy. Tests are 20 MC and 2 short answer that I felt were easy. One paper. Lectures were really good and interesting and he seems to really care about the students. Would definitely recommend taking from him

I loved this class! Every class is a lecture/discussion. you MUST take notes. I took detailed notes from every class and I felt that the tests (MP and 2 short answer) were easy. Weekly writeups (ask him if u need help! I felt they were pretty easy), midterm, non-comprehensive final, one essay. At least skim the readings, sometimes pop quizzes

This class was super easy. You have to do a quiz before each class that's easy. The midterm and final are basically exactly like the test. There are 3 papers in this class and they all go off of each other. The grading is so easy. If you put any effort into it and complete it you will get a 95. There are in class assignments so you do have to show

Dr Frost is one of my favorite professors of all time. Why? Because he cares about his students. You can tell by the way he engages everyone and listens to what they have to say! He is always willing to help. He makes interesting topics that can be easily pictured as dull. The work is not extremely heavy and everything is very fair!

Great at teaching confusing concepts and getting the students involved in discussion. Tests were pretty hard but if you do all the readings and go to class you'll be fine. Attendance is not mandatory but there are occasional pop quizzes and in class assignments. He is really good at teaching the info without inserting his opinion.
Very respectful, very caring guy. Gives solid lectures and doesn't make his class too hard. Is very willing to work with the students. Highly recommend taking a class from him
Hard class, good professor. Tells bad dad jokes and has pop quizzes, but is accessible outside of class and is generally very caring and kind.
He is genuinely a great professor. Statics is a hard class, but he taught it very well. He also was great at tying in spiritual lessons and funny stories.

Statics is a difficult class, def a weeder, but Maynes is a fantastic professor. He is always willing to take time to answer students' questions. He wants you to succeed and will help you! 
There are pop quizzes every week, so plan to always come to class.

I took his statics class, and it was extremely difficult, yet Maynes was an excellent professor for it. He taught concepts very clearly, but also made the class engaging and fun. Still, its such a hard class- the tests were so fast paced and I spent so much time time on the homework. He expects the same high caliber of work as his teaching.

The best professor I had in my freshman year. Gave me a lot of inspiration on becoming a real engineer. I am always looking forward to each of his lectures haha.....You can surely get an A in this class if you put full effort in the HW, and studying the exam.

He is really good at teaching principles of statics. He loves it and that love is contagious.
He really cares about each student, and takes tons of time to help anyone who comes to office hours.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER

Y'all, do yourself a favor and take statics with Dr Maynes!! It's so easy to pay attention in class because GUYS HE'S SO FUNNY! If you pay attention during lecture, do the homework, & use the TA lab then you'll get a really good understanding of the material, trust :)
Very skilled and experienced professor with a great sense of humor and a fair system of grading.

I always looked forward to going to Dr. Maynes's class. Lectures are entertaining and grading is fair, especially since he lets your final score replace your quiz score or a midterm. As long as you start the HW early it's not terrible and the tests are about as difficult as the HW.

So far, my time with Prof Maynes has been quite the struggle. There has been a lack of clear expectations, communication and deadlines. He seems to be a wonderful person, he makes lectures fun. However, his time management, expecially in quizzes is horrible. He also does not really show us how to do any questions related to the hw in class.

Most upfront and clear professor I've had. If a student answered a question wrong he would let them know, and there was never any "figure it out yourself" when we asked him. Has a "rule of justice" or "rule of mercy" where he can curve your grade at the end, or you can fight him on every little assignment for the points you want.
Dr Maynes is an awesome teacher. He drops some quizes and the final can erase a grade for another test. He teaches clear and really wants to help you succeed.

1. Textbook is confusing to read. i.e. "Refer to diagram 11.3 and plug in equation 6.11." Also gives very limited explanations of concepts. 2. No powerpoints or out of class notes. If you miss class, the textbook is your only help, which isn't much. 3. Homework starts with very complex problems rather than simple ones leading to harder ones.

Dr. Maynes is a legitimately caring man who has a firm grasp on the concepts he teaches and a gift to communicate them to his students. TA lab is critical for the homework, expect 8-12 hours a week. He does quizzes on random days to check for attendance and review principles. If you have to take 101, take it from him!

Dr Maynes is amazing, one of the best professors I've had for sure. He's funny, very helpful, very experienced, he cares about you, and he will always be available for help. Great class, go to the ta lab to do he, the homework takes 8-12 hours per week but that's normal for the class.

Dr. Maynes memorized EVERYONE'S name. He really seemed to care. Teaching was pretty good, although I frequently got lost. Quizzes and tests were hard AND timed, but Dr. Maynes curved the class, gave extra credit, and showed "mercy" with the final grade. He made a lot of jokes and has a good sense of humor. I really liked him! The class is HARD!!!

DO YOUR HW ON TIME! If you do the homework and understand it enough to explain it to another student, you will get an A. If you wait last minute to do assignments, then get ready to settle for a low grade. Maynes learns the name of his students and wants each individual to succeed. Do your part and you'll do great.

Really great professor. Definitely knows his stuff. It definitely was a tough class and took a big time commitment. Homework was due once a week with usually 7 or 8 problems and each would take about an hour. So like 8+ hours of homework a week. He wanted you to come to his office hours which ended up being really helpful. Tests were tough, timed.

Dr. Maynes is extremely clear, helpful, and predictable. Tests are fair and predictable - virtually every test he gives has average 78-80%, standard devation 10%. Lectures are interesting, engaging, and clear, with frequent review. Answers questions insightfully. Always clear what you need to know. Between him and his TAs it is easy to get help.

Took both advanced fluid mechanics and convection heat transfer from him. Great teacher, helped students understand the material but kept the coursework expectations reasonable. Good balance in the courses. Now I think he's the chair of the ME department.

Dr. Maynes is easily one of the most talented teachers i have ever had. He is amazingly clear and can explain difficult concepts and make them approachable and easy to understand. His tests are beasts though. They are fair in material but very difficult to finish in time. Pop quizzes every week, frequently on things he went over in class.

Maynes is a great teacher. Incredibly well organized and extremely helpful. His exams are hard. The 50 min time limit is tough if you are not a quick thinker. Easily one of my favorite classes. There is a decent homework load but it is all designed to get you through the exams.
Maynes is great, he knows his stuff and is REALLY WILLING TO HELP YOU!
he is a great techer, i also had him for 512 and it was great as well. he is very meticulis in his teaching, and gives assignments that will make you tthink and learn not buisy work at all.
One of my favorite teachers.  He talks fast and writes fast but explains the material well.  Tests are fair.  Very willing to help students out.

Thermodynamics for me was an awesome class. I learned a ton. Maynes explains the material very well and is a nice guy. His tests are very difficult though. They are 50 minute in class exams. If you are a quick thinker you will do very well in the class. If not, like me, you may struggle. It was still my favorite class that semester.

Dr Milton is AMAZING. His lectures are so engaging and he's really good at encouraging good class discussions. He's also very accessible outside of class and is so willing to help you out and to give good feedback. I could tell he genuinely cared about me and all of his students. Genuinely one of my favorite professors I have had at BYU!

Professor Milton is SUCH a good teacher. Super engaging lectures and relevant material. Gives great feedback on policy memos. Reasonable grader. Really helps you prepare for final exam and gives opportunity for you to get a good grade (if you participate often and show that you care). Great career advice and always willing to chat. Also very funny.

Dr. Smalley is very kind and put in effort to make this class fun and accessible, but I struggled with his teaching style. Class structure required SO MUCH TIME  This class made me question whether I wanted to be in EE (there are cool topics later on in the major for any others that just don't enjoy the circuit analysis/design from 240).

The worst class I've taken at BYU. Lectures were entertaining at the expense of learning. Mixing 240 and 301 students was a bad idea. Homework didn't match up with lectures or the tests. Final was brutal. Prof not accessible outside of class. TAs often skipped their hours. Nobody seemed to know what was going on. 10/10 would not recommend.

Dr. Smalley is one of the most entertaining lecturers I've had, though is humor usually takes the place of good explanations. He gets a "Very Easy" rating because it is very easy to keep close to 100% in the class (or more with extra credit) up until the final. But beware the final, it evens that distribution right back to a B-average bell curve.

Professor Smalley is a very nice guy. I think he would be great to work in his research lab, however, he seems to not care very much about this class. The class was horribly unorganized at the beginning and is mostly run by TAs. The "Scrolls" he gives often contain content that was not covered in class or was not explained very well.

Dr. Smalley is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. The way he structures his class is interesting and might not work for everyone, but it allows for a lot of flexibility.

Previous reviews have mentioned that if you do the Dragon Scroll at the end of the semester, you will receive an automatic A in the class. This is no longer the case.

240 is already an extremely difficult class, and I really wanted more from Dr. Smalley. He did not show up to nearly enough classes, and the "path of risk/pain" approach seemed stable at first but didn't work out in the long run for me and many others. Retaking this class with different prof. He is good for a lot of students, but not for me.

EC EN 240 is always going to be difficult, but it was pretty annoying to have Dr. Smalley regularly finish up his lectures and leave 50 minutes into a 110 minute class block. The extra time not spent in class was nice, but I'd rather the lectures be paced better so that whole huge topics aren't gone over in 5 minutes.

Those who gripe about the coursework aren't rating the Professor. Dr. Smalley is one of the best at BYU. He's fresher out of school than most professors so he gets it. The class (ecen240) is HARD. He makes it so much more bearable. People gripe about not needed the information again, but its a FUNDAMENTALS of CIRCUIT THEORY class. For EE and CE.

Great teacher. He keeps class fun (Kung Fu theme!) and the homework/tests (in "scrolls") is really effective and flexible. It felt so great to complete a scroll, feeling that I had mastered a subject. It was also really nice when I didn't have time to do a scroll to know I could still get credit for it on the midterm.

Can't say enough bad things about Smalley. The scrolls are a complete joke. If you do them all and try to get a good grade on all of them, plan on spending a minimum of 25 hours a week. Also, he won't tell you this, but if you do the dragon scroll at the end of the semester, you get an automatic A regardless of your previous grade.

This was by far my least favorite class at BYU! This class forces you to spend 20+ hours a week on concepts that you will likely never use again. Don't take it from him if you want a social life. ALSO, if you do the dragon scroll (at the end of the semester) you get an automatic A in the class. He keeps that part a secret. Shhhh. Don't tell.

Dr. Smalley is a good teacher for a select few. I did not learn the material at all. It is not mandatory to learn in his class for a good grade as long as you put in work. You will spend over 20 hours a week on this class.

Dr. Smalley is probably the most inspirational professor I ever had. His way of teaching circuit theory makes it so memorable. I can see how 40 years down the road, I can still recall the mnemonics that Dr. Smalley taught us when analyzing circuits. Highly recommend!

The worst part of this class was the 8am time. Attendance is needed for in class quizzes, but you really only need to read the scrolls and take the scroll tests. Try to avoid relying on the midterms if at all possible. First midterm is easy, but the second one killed my grade and I spent the rest of the semester making up for it. Time consuming.

Captian Smalley takes the dullest subject (EM Radiation and Propagation) and turns it into everyone's favorite class. I spent the entire term bragging about how awesome this class is to my CPE and EE friends who mistakenly didn't take 462. You'll learn how to defeat a Klingon starship in class. I suggest you watch some Star Trek as a pre-req.

This class structure was very different from any class I have ever taken. It is all about mastery. There are 40 "scroll" tests which you take. There are many chances to take them with minimal deductions. Or you can not take them and just take midterms instead. It took a lot of work, but it was worth it.

So he's a really good teacher and you will learn a lot but you will study a lot. You can either take 40 quizzes (each 30-45 min) or the 4 midterms. The midterms are really really hard and the quizzes take a lot of time to take/retake. Overall I spent probably an average of 15-20 hrs/wk in this class - no kidding. But he's very nice and fun.

Doctor Smalley is great! He wants the students to achieve mastery, and prove it with his incredibly hard final made up of MIT problems. The rest of the class is amazing, and he helps you want to learn the subject matter. Use the TA's and stay on top of the scrolls. In-class quizzes make attendance pretty necessary.

Grand Master Smalley is, in truth, much more than meets the eye. Each day, class is as hilarious as an episode of the Muppet Show, and the class even eventually will have its very own Statler and Waldorf heckling from "the balcony" at his campy jokes. Believe it or not, what would be dry and dull math and science is suddenly Star Trek on steroids!

He is the best professor at BYU!!!  He is so helpful and really cares about his students.  He is very theatrical and loves to make the class interesting.  Would definitely recommend him as a professor to anyone!

Dr. Zappala is a really cool guy, and he is such a nice professor. I enjoyed my time in this class, and really learned a lot in each of the computer science departments, and I feel confident that I can succeed in the program. He's got a nice calm voice, and is really flexible with assignments and helping his students succeed. Great guy all around!

It's a new course, so extra assignments were added partway through the year whenever he felt like it. I didn't particularly like the course (felt kinda pointless) but the professor himself seemed nice. It's a seminar class so each week we had different CS faculty come in to talk about their expertise.

Definitely a great guy and you can tell he cares about his students. This was his first time teaching this course so kinda just added extra homework whenever he felt like it. Cool to see the different aspects of computer science but also just felt like a waste of time. While not my favorite class, I would take another course by him.
Super nice guy, class was easy if you do the work and go to TA labs for help.

CS110 is a simple class if you make it one. Dr. Zappala made it really enjoyable as well. I never felt that there was something I couldn't do. There are so many resources available for help. I'm not a computer guy, I'm just doing a stats minor and needed this class. Don't be afraid of it, especially with Dr. Zappala. Very good class Great Professor

Almost all your grade is assignments and projects, which aren't very difficult. Finished the semester with almost 100 percent. Make sure to go to the labs. They are honestly more important than lectures. Zappala is a great, caring man. I enjoyed his lectures.
