Dr Zappala was wonderful! The class itself is a bit hard, but you will absolutely learn and understand how python works! The TAs for this class are amazing! I would 100% recommend taking it from him.

While attendance isn't mandatory, going to both lab and lecture will set you up for success. I took this class the semester after it was first piloted, so while there were still things that needed to be fixed, Professor Zappala and the TAs asked for and acted on feedback. Overall, Professor Zappala was great - take this class, and take it from him!

I adore Dr. Zappala. He is so kind and gives little devotionals frequently. He is very smart and very willing to help. This class was new and we were all struggling, so he made us this guide that was very very helpful. I loved CS110 and Dr. Zappala is a great person to take it from.

Professor Zappala is a great teacher who cares about his students, but CS110 needs some serious changes. I had never coded before and expected it to be a class where I could learn the basics at a decent pace. In reality, this class moves incredibly quickly through the material, and you are assigned 8+ hours worth of labs each week. So overwhelming.
Dr. Zappala is a real gem! Super kind and caring. Goes an extra mile to help his students. Very respectful. Great teacher.

A really good man and professor. I feel that a lot was taught by him and very fast and that he probably needed a bit more organization, but he is a solid angle, very caring and understanding. Accommodating and fair.

Web Dev. Learn JS, HTML, CSS, Vue, and Mongo. He makes tutorials for each class project which are easy to follow (mostly copy and paste...) but if you fail to understand the concepts, you'll struggle on your "creative projects" -- making a website on your own. Midterms are harder than expected.... average is like a low C on them.

Great teacher, really cares about helping his students. Very willing to help during office hours/after class. Passionate about web programming and good lectures, as far as CS lectures go. Learned a TON in the class but at the end it got pretty difficult. Definitely doable, just put in the work and you'll learn so much.

Zappala is great. He's caring, wants to help, and does his best for the students. It was partially due to how supportive he is that I was disappointed with CS260. It was supposed to be a 200-level course on par with 240, but he move so slowly that I learned very little I couldn't have gotten online. An easy A, if that's what you're looking for.

I'd give Prof. Zappala a 7/5 on helpfulness if I could! He's extremely respectful to students! He's also a great lecturer and usually gives extra credit. I'd recommend taking any class he offers. He's involved in the research community as well and shares updates on networking research. I don't love the material but Prof Zappala made it worth it.

Prof. Zappala was awesome! He listens to students and is one of the most flexible professors I've had. He's a great lecturer and I feel like this class is one of the most applicable to industry work. Make sure you get a good group for the project at the end.

I really liked Zappala's lectures, and his style of slides, and open everything tests. I had to work for the A, but it was very doable and I learned a ton. Group project at the end of the semester took a bunch of time, but with the materials he gives you, you wind up with a really impressive result.

Zappala is a very cool guy.  He has a very laid back demeanor and is very accepting of all students.  The projects here are like any other BYU CS class.  Didn't get much out of lectures.  Most learning occurs on your own.  Tests were open book, and final was open internet!  However, they asked vague questions and expected specific answers.

Dr. Zappala was a great teacher, really enjoyed this class.  Tests are open-everything except your neighbor (like, open internet, open-book).  Projects can be a bit tough, but our doable.  The first two are in CC++, the rest are in Python.  Plus, there is no textbook.

Zapalla's 360 class was very good, he gives good lectures and introduces you to both Python and Javascript which I was surprised aren't taught earlier in the program. Some of the early projects are a little more tedious then helpful, but the big group project is a wonderful opportunity to do something real. Oh, and open notes internet tests rock!

This class was tough, but Dr Zapalla is very generous with late work and he definitely wants you to succeed.  However, as with any CS class, you have to stay on top of the projects because if you get behind, you're screwed.
Super easy class. Open note tests. Projects can be demanding, but they are not too big. Really makes you want to do programming for more than just school and work.
Great class, you actually learn to do something useful. Lots of help with the projects, no homework. Open computer in class exams.

Dr. Z really knows his stuff and he wants to help you learn, not just jump through hoops. The labs are tough, but Dr. Z is always willing to answer questions after class, via email, or on the Google Group. You can tell Dr. Z puts a lot of effort into making the labs a meaningful learning experience. Worst grade I've ever gotten, but great class.
Awesome professor. Teaches concepts clearly. Also, open note tests!!
So hot...
Best CS teacher I've had.  He's always willing to stick around after class to help out.  I never went in during his office hours so I can't say much about that.

Dr. Zappala rocks! He is clear, very helpful, and obviously interested in making sure that all his students succeed in the class. Many assignments are hard, but I enjoyed them all and learned a TON. No busywork in this class. I really wish Dr. Zappala taught more classes! My favorite CS professor so far (and I've taken a lot of CS classes).

The class was fascinating, and the material was presented very well. The labs for this class were my favorite out of any CS class so far. He is a great teacher, and networking is his research focus as well, so he really knows his stuff. He is also not afraid to say he doesn't know something, and go off to come up with a better answer later.

Really cool class, and Dr.Zappala is very smart, helpful, and respectful of students. The labs were very fun and not so hard. Exams are not hard at all. This class has a normal load for a 3 credit class. Do not take it with any other professor. Dr.Zappala rules.
good professor to teach and inspire students to learn. Very easy to cope with and be ready for some steep learning curve if you haven't done anything with Python before.

His tests and grading are fair (he did have a very generous late policy) but the labs are murder.  Labs 2&3 are the worst, if you can make it through those then the class is an "easy" A. If you can't, then it's an easy D+, because they're weighted pretty heavily. The lectures were helpful for the tests, but not so much for the labs.
Clear and Sharp. You should expect a lot of hard labs along the way.
First semester taught so there were disadvantages. Projects were very confusing. Had to withdraw...

Projects were very unclear and took a long time.  Most of my time was spent figuring out what he wanted.  Tests are similar, unclear and hard.  He is a very smart man, and willing to help, but I didn't feel like he felt this class was that big a priority.

Great class and should only get better as the class material is refined. Dr. Zappala was very helpful and a great teacher. He was willing to let me take the final early because I was heading out of town. Very interested in making sure the students do well.

He seems to have relaxed his late policy a bit; in fact, he had the most reasonable policies of any CS teacher I've had.  He also gives partial credit, and bends over backwards to make sure you learn the stuff.  Tests were somewhat beastly, but mostly due to the volume of information.  I recommend him highly.

Kind of dropped the ball on this class, but Dr. Damron was very understanding. He gave me extensions. Class had a mix of relevant and irrelevant content, but it could have been the fact that I was more focused on my internship then the course. Came back to leave a review after he was review-bombed; great guy and didn't deserve the bad reviews.

Clearly some student didn't like him and review bombed him. When I took the class every week focuses on something new.(managing a project, being a team player, etc.) It helped me grow professionally and get an offer for my dream job post grad. Students who rate it badly are just wanting a vacation instead of an academic internship.

You won't find a better professor. Danny is very student-oriented and works hard to give you a good grade. His internship course is impossible to fail unless you just don't care. Grading criteria is clear, resubmissions are allowed as long as the OG submission was on time. The class is all about teaching you future skills, very applicable long-term
Great professor, very involved with the students and kind. Take him if you can!

This class was the worst class I have taken at BYU. It honestly felt so pointless. The assignments just felt like we were doing the same thing over and over again without learning anything. I would avoid this class at all costs. Very disorganized!

I felt that the grading criteria was extremely unclear and would change on a whim. Very strict late work policy. Seems to understand the material well, but I didn't feel that it was conveyed well. Little meaningful participation. Long waits for grades and feedback was average at best. Would not recommend.

Does not properly go over slides during lectures and usually does not finish slides, so you will get tested on things that you never heard. I never studied but did well on tests mostly but the essays were the worst parts.

Dr. Ray is very nice, but his class is so difficult. I took this class as a GE, and it required more work than any of the STEM major classes I was taking. His lectures covered so much information, and there was no way to know what was going to be on the exam. He is also a really tough grader and requires a ton of work outside of class.

I actually took 241, but it wasn't an option on RMP. Dr. Ray is a really cool guy, but his class is a struggle. There is always WAY more information crammed into a single lecture than there should be, which just ends up meaning that none of it really gets absorbed. He is also a fairly picky grader and doesn't always set very clear expectations.

I have never written a rating on Rate My Professor before, so please know this is important. Professor Ray always went over on lecture time, covered 17 lectures worth of information each class, and graded so harshly. I don't think he believes in giving 10/10. He was rough. Would not recommend.

He just pulls slides up and covers them way to fast, the homework is miles long and is difficult to do. it isn't an engaging class, just show up while he talks and go home and figure it out. the Test are just random things from the giant scope of material he covered on slides. So there is no way to study effectively for the class

Very good instructor and very enthusiastic about history. Expectations for assignments were clear, and PowerPoints given in class were always made available afterwards. All before class assignments were completion grades based on the textbook reading. Set learning objectives to make exam expectations clear and the final was not cumulative.

Awesome professor, awesome class. I learned so much about Islam and about African history, and it was always clear that he genuinely cared about helping students to understand the material. Goes above and beyond to make himself accessible and answer questions. Can't recommend this class enough.

Every class day you have a tough "busy work" type assignment due. Each class period is a lecture that is hard to follow. He talks fast and there is a lot of information. you have 3 writing assignments, 3 tests, and 1 group project. The good thing is that he responds great to emails and is quite understanding. attendance is mandatory.

The lectures were pretty boring and the big semester group project was a pain. It felt like busy work. Almost every assignment felt like busy work to be honest. There is a textbook for this class but the tests are based off of the lectures, so there's no point in reading the book. I hardly read it and did fine on the tests. Not a great class.

Strengths: Most responsive to emails I've ever seen. Structures the class towards understanding changing academic views of Islam in Africa, very modern approach.
Difficulties: One-sided lectures, just him talking for the most part. Lots of writing, (maybe too much) but was good practice, because he gives lots of feedback.

Lectures were pretty boring and hard to follow. Him and his TA's were tough graders and I felt like took off too many points for small things. You don't need to read the textbook, tests are pretty much just off of lectures and class activities. There's also a pretty lame group project worth a chunk of your grade.
Grading criteria could be hard but he was easy to talk to and gave interesting lectures. Group project was a pain. Lots of time spent on this class. Tons of information to remember. Three papers.

There's a lot of material to cover, but Professor Ray sticks to a manageable schedule. He knows what he's talking about. He emphasizes understanding over memorization. He refers students to TAs for questions and test prep. The big semester project is a group project. 10am was the perfect time for this class.

Professor Ray's are very interesting. Several times he shared some of his insights on some tough topics (patriarchy throughout history and in the church, evolution, etc.) which I thought were really cool. All that being said this class is not easy. The tests are really hard to study for and every lecture is full of so much information.

Don't take this class from him! Every single day is lecture after lecture and it gets incredibly boring. He expects you to love history even though it's just a general so the tests are super hard because there's so much information and you don't know what will be on it. He grades way too harshly, it's infuriating. Stay away!!

The extra credit is what saved me in this class. He is a tough grader and likes to put his tangents from the lectures on the tests. To be fair, HIST 201 has a ton of information, so it's a lot to memorize.

This class is HARD. At the start of the class he explained that he designed it to be an intro level class-that was not the case. We had quizzes due almost every class, multiple papers with unclear expectations and criteria, the TAs were awful and gave contradicting critiques, and you're graded very harsh. The lectures are great, but that's about it

Mr. Ray is a tough grader- nothing is perfect enough for an A. There were three essays and the prompts are very vague. Lecture heavy: random tangents he goes on will be on the exams. After taking an exam for this class, I looked at the notes and I'm pretty sure if it was an open note test I still would have done bad.

Honestly terrible. He does not explain assignments and his criteria are always unclear. The exams are online, but none of the material covered in class or the textbook is in the exam. You'll have to write multiple essays that require odd formatting and part of your final will be a group poster project.

Extremely difficult tests. Too much personal involvement in a class I'm required to take. Essays are too long, group project is too difficult, and too much homework. Only take if you enjoy crazy amounts of homework and stupidly difficult exams.
He is a tough grader but you get lots of good feedback from him. You will also get good historical background from him.

Even though the material we covered was interesting, and I walked out of class with an understanding of the topic, the tests were unnecessarily difficult. Test questions could be the tiniest of details and not what you studied. (he doesn't provide a study guide) Wouldn't have passed if it weren't for my TA. There is a group project and a final.

I liked Dr. Ray's lectures a lot. The reading was long and boring and the tests were hard to prepare for. We did three essays and the grades were kind of a crapshoot. I never knew what I would get and the feedback wasn't that helpful. Very lecture heavy, take good notes, and review the slides. The group project at the end sucked. A lot.

He's a nice guy as a person, but the class is pretty tough for a GE. Essays and tests are graded pretty harshly. Expect to read 1-2 chapters from the textbook every week as well as complete reading assignments that can take between 1-2 hours. There's a whole lot of content crammed into one semester. Nice guy, tough class.

This was one of my favorite classes at BYU so far. I'm not a big history person, but Daren Ray makes it so easy to be interested. The tests are pretty hard, but as long as you go to class and take good notes, you will get at least 80%.

I actually really enjoyed this class. It is very lecture heavy but the homework is literally impossible to not get 100% on (inquisitive). He teaches really well but my only gripe is that the tests are pretty hard, we're tested on a  small things that only come up for a couple minutes in lectures. Essays are straightforward, and there's extra credit
Professor Ray is a good guy but his grades and criteria could be a little confusing. He used Top hat for participation and it was awfully confusing.

Save your GPA and your mental health. Don't take this class unless you're willing to give up your social life and have a couple of good cry sessions. Don't say I didn't warn you. 

Good person, not good teacher. Way. Too. Much.

I would highly not recommend taking class from Professor Ray. He has a fun personality. HOWEVER, this class was ridiculously difficult. I spent HOURS every week doing homework and put a lot of effort into this class. He grades everything so harshly. The tests are super hard. It was frustrating. I loved history before taking this class. Not anymore.

Basically, if you actually enjoy history, you might actually enjoy his class. If you don't, then don't risk your gpa. He has heavy lectures, and you're tested on what he says, not on what is on the slides or what the textbook says. He will only give full credit if you go above and beyond the expectations. Pretty strict grader on the three papers.

Dr. Ray is a good lecturer and seems like a great guy. As a human I would like to know him better, however his class was pretty hard for me and not very enjoyable. The tests were hard, the essays were graded pretty strictly, and participation points are confusing. If you're doing this for a general, maybe find an easier class. I wish I had hahaha.
Professor Ray knows his stuff. He moves fast and goes through a TON of material. Keeps you engaged. Focus on geography/map questions & timelines for tests!

Not good if you don't like history. Expects you to go above and beyond for every assignment. He will only give you full credit if you exceed expectations, will only give you partial if you "just meet" them. Is very boring during lecture. He's not very understanding of difficult situations. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU LOVE HISTORY.

Great Prof. Most of his test content comes from his lecture so go to class. Participation and attendance count. 3 pretty easy papers(2 pages max). One group project that seems more difficult than it is. Form a study group and use his study guide. Hardly an extra credit offered.

The class is pretty straightforward in what is expected; the readings are long and there are weekly reading assignments with questions. The tests are very much graded off of what is discussed in lectures (although it parallels the book mostly). There is a large group project worth as much as the final and he gives 2% EC for student ratings.

At first I really didn't like the class because I felt like he didn't cater the class towards his students, but something switched in the way he structured the class and taught. Now I really respect him, and can easily recommend him. He is a genius and teaches more info than you need to know sometimes. If you like history you will love this class.

If history isn't your thing, this class isn't for you. His tests are very hard. He will tell you that his goal is an average grade of a C on tests. Even if you know the general idea of what you are learning, that is not enough. His tests cover very specific/random facts and places. If you choose to take his class, GO TO TA REVIEWS!

Prof. Ray really knows his history. It was a very educational class in which I learned a lot about ancient civ. and how they connect and relate to each other. I would say that the review sessions are very important for doing well on the tests. Also, practice doing ID questions before the exam. This and knowing geography will help you succeed.

Professor Ray is an average professor. His lectures can be interesting but they tend to drag on. Its important to do well on homework and credit/no credit assignments to balance out the harder exams and group projects.

Prof Ray is an ok professor. His lectures are rather long and can sometimes be boring. The most important thing is to get 100 on homework/participation/attendance grades so you can afford to lose points on exams and papers and still keep your grade up. It is hard to pinpoint what writing will receive a good grade, which is frustrating.
Very difficult professor. Grading was very harsh. Lectures were quite long. Would not recommend taking the course from him at all.

Professor Ray is passionate but his tests are hard. His lectures are extremely boring and hard to follow. This class has a lot of work and reading that needs to be done before every class period. Overall not horrible but I wouldn't take it again.

Though Professor Ray is good at explaining topics in his lectures, he is non-accommodating and assigns a lot of work for a 201 class. It's doable if you're willing to put in the work and time, but he's a stickler with rules and is not understanding if you're in a difficult situation. It's worth it to take this class from a different professor.

Dr. Ray is a solid choice. He's super passionate about history and the lectures are fairly interesting and go right along with the reading. The tests are a little tougher, but the homework is weighted enough that as long as you do all the work and go to class, you can get an A even if your test grades are pretty mediocre.

Professor Ray is very passionate about history but just not my style of professor. Tests were really hard even when I studied a lot for them. There were readings due every class which were long but not unbearable. Aside from 3 exams, there was one big group project and 2 mini essays which werent too bad. Overall was my least favorite class.

I had some extenuating circumstances that caused me to withdraw my first run of this class. Professor Gates was incredibly accommodating and caring, which I am extremely grateful for. Easy class, wonderful professor, helpful TA. Philosophy focused of course, but I still enjoyed it.

Dr. Gates has been a great teacher. He tries to make the lecture interesting and create discussion in the classroom. It is a pretty easy class although you need to study many concepts from the lectures from the midterm and memorize them word by word. He is also generous in grading as long as you follow the rubrics.

I took Phil213 as a substitute for CS404 in Spring 2026 and we only had 7 students in the class, so lectures were very flexible and there was always time to ask questions. Lots of reading, but he gave us most readings online or textbooks could be found on the library course reserve. I used flashcards to study and aced the exams.
Dr. Gates managed to keep lectures interesting even when most of the class was checked out mentally. The class often felt more like philosophy than CS.

I strongly recommend any other teacher for PHIL. He is truly kind, but his requirements for projects/assignments were unclear and in class every student had to work together to get him to explain things better. His TA graded pretty poorly so it was possible to negotiate more points. His test questions would draw from niche class discussions.

He is a really cool professor, really into his stuff. Most of the assignments are easy if you pay attention or do the reading. The exams are a lot harder than the rest of the class. would take it again; he makes the material super interesting.

Professor Gates is highly intelligent and his lectures are super interesting. However, his class management style is fairly disorganized and hard-to-follow. You'll enjoy his class but be prepared to be very proactive in making sure you're on top of ever-changing due dates and surprise assignments.
Awesome guy! I love his lectures and he's fun to talk to. His classes are exactly as difficult as they should be!
Fantastic professor. You can tell her really cares about his students. His lectures were very interesting. Overall, a fantastic class.

The ethics weren't thoroughly explored, his understanding of computer science was poor, and we didn't really talk about applying it to business. The whole class felt shallow and not well prepared. 

He got really distracted during lectures and would ramble a lot.

It's not hard, but the midterm and final are each worth 25% of your final grade.

Dr. Gates is a fantastic lecturer; the presentations and flow of class is really easy to follow and the grading criteria is clear. He cares about his students success and organizes assignments in a way that is both fun and intellectually stimulating.

Prof. Gates teaches in a straight-forward way, with helpful lectures and clear expectations. The readings can be dense, but using resources like unstuck AI for study prep makes the course manageable. Overall, a rewarding class with an approachable instructor.

Before I say anything negative, I want to say Dr.Gates taught me a lot. I learned really quickly with his way of teaching. However, I think he puts too much weight on tests(50% of your grade), and there are only 2 tests per semester. The tests are hard too. You cannot just memorize everything on the study guide. Trust me, its not enough!

I loved this class. He teaches in a way that for me, was hard to follow at first, but you have the PowerPoints and readings all available for you and if you make sure to study those you'll do great on the tests and papers. He was really funny, relaxed, and overall a great professor.

I took this class for a GE credit but it was so confusing to me most of the time. Professor Gates would talk about all kinds of random things during lectures and it was hard to follow. The power points were not up to date, learning suite was not updated to our accurate schedule. He's a funny person and very nice but hard to follow in long lectures.

Professor Gates is amazing. He knows a ton, loves what he does, and takes care of his students. Couldn't recommend more.

Do the readings, use his powerpoints to study for the tests, and you'll have an A.

There were some readings but if you skimmed them you were fine. Lots of lectures but the important stuff is clearly defined. Some memorizing different moral systems. Maybe 2 pop quizzes all semester (which showed up on LS so they werent even pop quizzes).

Very nice, lectures are good. Lots of difficult reading with difficult reading quizzes (some of them are pop quizzes). But he goes over the all the concepts that you need to know in class. Would give him a 5 but he was pretty disorganizes (accidentally made a quiz only 5 minutes long, didn't post instructions for assignments at times, etc.).

The class wasn't too tough, but pretty disorganized. You teach yourself most of the stuff because he likes to talk about ethics in certain movies or other real-life cases without addressing the topics in-depth. Slow grading. Also, he was always late to class and usually didn't have a lesson plan.

Professor Gates was amazing! I loved all the topics he managed to squeeze into this class as we got to focus on ethics and thoughts on morality. The main focus of the class was a group project that applied a ethical analysis of modern-day technology. There were only a couple of quizzes and a couple of essays which were all real short!

A couple pop quizes. daily readings but only really required for the pop quizzes. One group project but it was relatively easy. Lots of fun. very relatable professor who tells you exactly what he wants you to know for the test, which I respect.

He knows his stuff, and he's an easygoing, approachable guy. There were 4 short easy papers, graded generously, and a "group" project with a ppt presentation and a paper. The midterm and final were free-response heavy, and pretty hard. The info you need is given in class/on the review, you just really need to know it. I learned a lot, good content.

Good guy and solid lectures with lots of class participation, but was pretty disorganized. Very slow grading. I didn't do as well as I hoped but that was on me as I didn't study for the midterm as much as I should've (but there weren't really any opportunities to correct that). He was consistently 5-10 minutes late to class which I guess is fine

I really enjoyed this class because of the professor. I learned a lot and it was very clear what was going to be on the exams. The quizzes and writing assignments were easy if you went to class. Readings were due every class. It was a very good experience overall.
He's a great professor! Very approachable, respectful, and kind. The readings can be long, but nothing crazy, and there are a handful of papers to write. I'd recommend taking a class from him.

Dr. Gates is a funny and laid back person, the kind you'd want to invite to a game night. He is a philosophy professor, not a CS one, though he has a passable technical knowledge. Class is straightforward and interesting enough. You only use the textbook for a few chapters for the last half of the class.

The first half went well; problems occurred in the 2nd half as the materials focused more on application than theory (Plato's works are not covered). The reading load is okay, but Terry's book is a parody of Kant's moral philosophy, and the business guide is useless. A pretty chill guy who goes off on tangents but doesn't explain concepts clearly.

So much reading!!! Ahhhhhh. The class was hardly posted on Learning Suite and it was so hard to figure out what was expected for assignments and tests. Besides that, Prof Gates is an awesome dude and I really enjoyed his teaching content. Nothing bad to say about him personally, just the organization of the class. I wish things were clearer on LS.

I took this class during summer... It was okay, but I was a little disappointed because I learned more from the TA reviews than I did in class. His tests were pretty fair and the writing assignments weren't too bad, but the TAs also graded them.
Great down to earth guy. His tests are a lot of memorization, but not application.

Took him during a summer term. I went through something really horrible to begin the term, so I flunked the first half. I went to talk to him about how I could approach the second portion of the term to get a decent grade. In short, he spent two hours per week with me in office hours to help me get a B+. What more can you ask out of a professor?

I really liked Professor Gate's ethics class! For the most part your only homework is reading before class. Definitely need to study for the two exams but the TA is awesome and has really good review sessions. Definitely would take this class again!

Professor Gates its a really chill guy, papers aren't super interesting but they are graded very easily. Discussions can be pretty interesting. Wasn't my favorite class because I like CS not writing and philosophy, but the course wasn't bad and I'm glad I had Professor Gates as my teacher.

Professor Gates is awesome! I learned a lot in his class, and you can tell he really cares about what he's teaching. Make sure to really study for his tests, because they are very free-response heavy. There's also a big group project at the end of the semester, but it honestly isn't a lot of work. Definitely recommend taking this class!

He's a nice teacher but lectures are sometimes slow and dry. I missed about a third of them and it didn't hurt my grade at all (his attendance policy isn't clear). The midterm and final are easy if you do the review guide and review slides, and attend a review session. They pretty much hand you the answers for the tests in them. Group project is ok

Great teacher, enjoyed the class. Interesting topics and discussion, related life to the things we were learning. The reading wasn't always clear, but he explains it in class very well. His tests are very fair, provides a study guide for the exams that are a good representation of it. A few quizzes and writing assignments that are graded easily.

I really enjoyed the lectures for this class. Everything we discussed was fascinating and we had good discussions. He is really fair and willing to work with you if you have any problem. The study guides, readings, and lectures are good representations of the exams. Overall he's a great professor and I enjoyed taking class from him.

He is a super nice guy. Can get behind on grading at times but he is a very lenient grader. Always enjoys reading our papers and usually gives them 100%. He has us spend about $35 for the semester on a couple books but nothing terrible. The second book we use is an easy read and not too boring.

Prof Gates is a good choice for your letters GE. Several papers that he grades easily (basically completion), but they are fun topics anyway so not hard to bang out. He's engaging and funny and makes effort to know his students personally. The tests are a little hard and require some memorization, but he does a good job of telling you what to study

Dr. Gates is an amazing person and prof. He really makes ethics applicable to each person and helps to show how it is something applicable to our lives. I feel like I will remember a lot of what I have learned for the rest of my life. There are several short papers and a group project. But, if you do the work it's easy to do well.

Professor Gates is a great teacher. His lectures are always enjoyable, with lots of real life examples and fun videos. There is opportunity for questions and discussion. He gives reasonable amount of time for assignments, and they aren't difficult. There were a couple of pop quizzes/online quizzes, but they are straightforward and he gives heads up

Dr. Gates is a good teacher, but as of right now he is also the only option for CS 404. If you have taken PHIL 213 from him before, this class is EXACTLY the same but with an additional group project. Lectures are okay, he can sometimes get on a tangent. Penalties for not attending are not exactly clear. Still a fine class, tests aren't cakewalks.

The class was rigorous in readings, while it wasn't a huge amount of reading the difficulty of the reading ranged from quick to understand to some material that required a lot of thinking to get through. The class was funny but I still always learned something whenever I was at class. I would take another class with him given the chance to do so.

I feel so lucky that I got to be taught by Professor Gates! He is a fantastically engaging speaker, and I thoroughly enjoyed his classes. Prof Gates made learning so exciting; I still reference things he taught us/things that happened in his class. I would highly recommend taking this class!

Dr. Gates is a real gem! I enjoyed showing up to hear his thoughts and also my peers. The readings are lengthy, but he discusses them in class. He is a chill grader and gives very detailed study guides for the tests. He loves seeing students in office hours to talk about material. Genuine with great stories. Def take your Letters GE from him.

Professor Gates is clear about the grading criteria, and ready to help you succeed in the class. Great lectures about ethics and it is obvious this guy knows his stuff. He is also entertaining, never really had boring lectures and we watched videos during class often which made it more entertaining. Would totally recommend this class to anyone.

Professor Gates is great. He really tries to connect with his students and is really clear when he explains concepts during his lecture. There was a group project which, like everyone else in the world, I am not a fan of, but it was relatively painless and I didn't have to rely on my group that much.

I took PHIL200 Honors (and a religion class) with Prof. Gates, back in 2005. Was going through this randomly and wanted to say how great an instructor he was. I ran into him once while working at my job during school and he was very genuine and caring, we had a good conversation. Definitely take a course from him, I'm sure he's still just as good!

DARIN GATES IS AMAZING! I came into his class from the first day loving it, and I can't but smile in his classes. He understands special circumstances, and HE WILL HELP YOU SUCCEED! He always went the extra mile with his students! He cared to make a personal connections with me, and I'll always tell anyone who asks how much I love professor Gates!!

Professor Gates is intriguing and an easy grader. There is a lot of readings, but they are such good readings! Also, even if you don't do the readings, they are discussed thoroughly during class so you can get a solid understanding. He is a little scatter brained but that didn't interfere with my grade. 10/10 would recommend to a friend.

Dr. Gates has fun teaching style. I enjoyed his intro to ethics class and the way he made it fun and applicable to college students. We got to read "Bonds That Make Us Free" by Terry Warner. This book was a life changer. Inspiring class. Great concepts. Good teacher.

Darin Gates is focused, talks on his feet for his intro classes, but this is a great way to discover what he finds priority in the power points to do well on tests, and his acceptance of just straight logical-talk essays and work in his class is great. Its a lot of learning, and little of having to dig into a subjective teacher's psyche.
Dr. Gates is a great teacher--the material is interesting and feels relevant to what we'll face as computer scientists. There is a lot of reading, but the class if very manageable.

Professor Gates was the best Philosophy teacher! He truly cares about his students and wants you to learn. There a couple one page papers you have to write, but you get credit if you put the effort in. One midterm, one final, a couple pop quizzes. He takes attendance, not for credit, but he likes to get to know his students. Take it from Gates!!

Professor Gates, really cares about you learning the material. His tests are open response, but not overly difficult. He covers everything well in class and has good power-points. The final paper is  4 pages double spaces and you can choose your topic. I feel like I am a better person after taking his class and would recommend the class to anyone.

I love Prof. Gates as a person. I don't love this subject. I took PHIL 213 as a GE requirement and I have no interest in the class whatsoever. That being said, prof. Gates is really funny. He takes the time to learn everyone's name and he really cares about his students. I just didn't like the class.

One of my favorite philosophy teachers ever at BYU! I was so happy to have him more than once. He's very nice, leads good class discussions and is organized. He expects you to learn and do your best. There is a good deal of reading and some homework, but it's not an overload.

This was by far the best class I've taken while attending BYU. He's very, very intelligent and well versed. While the exams were difficult, he was very courteous about helping his students improve. You MUST take this class.

I loved taking this class from Dr. Gates. He is a terrific conversational kind of lecturer.  He facilitates great classroom discussion and his lectures allow for engaging input while remaining focused on the topic.  Great class. Great Professor.

I had a great experience in Ethics with Professor Gates. He's one of the best lecturers Ive had at BYU and really willing to help outside of class. One of those classes that I feel like I'll always look back on the content. He's a real expert in business ethics, so even if your not into philosophy try it out, and this stuff is useful no matter what

Prof Gates is a great guy! Goes on tangents a bit, the tangents are usually fun to listen too. He goes major into the philosophy of it all and I wish there was more connection to business. Not my fav class, but good guy.

Professor Gates is really smart on the subject of philosophy & ethics. This was his first semester teaching the Business Ethics class, so lectures felt pretty philosophy-heavy, but he got better at applying the principles to specific business cases as the semester went along. I think he'll only get better at teaching this class with time.

Dr. Gates is one of my favorite professors in the Philosophy Department. He is very caring and approachable. I was sick for a few weeks of the semester, and he made accommodations for me to retake quizzes, homework, etc.  He encourages you to voice your opinion, but as far as tests go, they are pretty much straight out of the book. Loved Gates!

He is very disorganized, the readings and powerpoints are scattered all over LS.  He only used the PPs on occasion.  There is a lot of reading but they are managable. Rarely if ever replied to emails and only actually returned one paper w/ feedback out of the five papers, but they were pretty easy. Took forever to grade tests. Doesn't round up!

There is some really great material in this class. Some of the lectures are really interesting and some a bit more dull. The reading analysis are pretty easy. Prepare for the final paper early. I wish I had time to go in and talk it over with Professor Gates before it was due. The tests are really easy if you memorize the study guide.
Super nice guy. Sometimes he's a little unclear and sometimes he seems to drift off topic, but he's responsive to students and encourages participation.

Professor Gates is a super nice guy and really cares about all his students and their success. Although some concepts were hard to grasp, lectures were interesting and I really enjoyed his class. He is also an easy grader. He does tend to go off topic fairly easily though, just ask questions about the concepts and he will get right back on track.

Dr. Gates is an awesome professor! He's willing to help and makes the classroom a great learning environment. There is quite a bit of reading, but that should be expected. He is always clear concerning assignments and provides study guides for tests. I would definitely recommend this class if Dr. Gates is teaching it!

I found this class to be rather difficult, but it was also my first semester back in school after taking a break for three years to get away from school. Luckily, Professor Gates is very kind and will work with you if you need him to do so.

Professor Gates is an excellent professor. He cares about his students and their learning of the material.  His tests are meant as learning experiences and really help to better internalize the material. Tests are very fair, especially since he provides a study guide and even goes through it during class time. Great experience, highly recommend

Don't take this class if you aren't intrested in the subject. The readings are super hard and all he does is repeat them with no explanation. The whole class feels directionless and he gives the hardest tests and like everyone fails.

Take him if you need this GE and don't care, or if you are sincerely interested. Great teacher and class. I NEVER did the readings except for summaries, and I skimmed readings for quizzes (which are open book). The study guide is fabulous. If you are interested in the material, I'm sure the readings will make the class even better. 50% effort = A

Professor Gates is sincerely interested in and respectful to students. He is thoughtful about ethical and moral issues and well-versed in philosophy. He also connected the course content to the LDS gospel in a way that I really appreciated. I really enjoyed reading Bonds That Make Us Free and some of the essays on abortion and same-sex marriage.

Professor Gates is wonderful, genuinely cares about the students, and does what he can to help the students fully understand the concepts discussed in class and in the readings. The course is very interesting and covers many areas of ethics. If you do the readings, attend class, and fill out/study the study guides, you'll do well in the class.

Professor Gates is a very good professor. He genuinely cares for the students and helps them whenever he can. He respects other people's opinions even if they don't agree with his own. Philosophy 150 was a very good and insightful class. I would recommend Professor Gates.
I loved this class so much! Professor Gates is a great professor that is very helpful. The class is challenging but a lot is learned. Definitely recommended if you want to become a better writer.

Professor Gates is extremely nice and flexible but lectures are uninteresting. Lectures consisted of a lot of philosophical hypotheticals that didn't seem relevant or pertinent to real life situation or current events.

Professor Gates is a wonderful teacher with a remarkable sense of fairness and genuine respect for each of his students. Class discussions were always interesting and he took the time to explain concepts repeatedly as needed.

Dr. Gates is awesome. He is very personable and easy to approach! I was not at all looking forward to this GE, but choose this class because it looked easy. I actually really enjoyed it!  Very interesting discussions about moral dilemmas. His study guides prepare you perfectly for the tests!  Insightful and not too big of a workload. Take it!

I enjoyed every minute in Prof. Gates' class. He's incredibly helpful, clear, humble, and helped us apply the principles of ethics that we were learning in class to our own lives. The time flew by, and I wish I could take another class from him.

Professor Gates may be the best professor I have had at BYU. He is generally interested in his subject and well-versed in it. Class is super interesting since he doesn't just unload his knowledge on you--he encourages different views through class participation. He is kind, humble, and understanding. Wish I could take another class from him.
Prof. Gates is an incredible teacher.  He is very precise and engaged in his subject that he teaches.  He also was very very helpful and personal.  I highly recommend this teacher!

I took this class with no love for ethics--it just fit in my schedule. However, Dr. Gates does a GREAT job of making the material interesting. Classes aren't lectures, they're discussions. This course was shockingly engaging and I loved talking about the material. The tests are a little hard, but very doable. I highly recommend this class.
This was pretty easy. You have to write only five papers, which is quite sparse for a writing class. He is kind of a comma and grammar Nazi though. I would take it from him again.

Gates knows his stuff and loves the subject. He occasionally  takes attendance. He goes over the reading, so there really isn't a need to read or even purchase the books. Even if you hate Philosophy, you'll enjoy his class. Tests are just like the SG's, so study hard and actually do the work!

Gives a lot of reading, but he talks extensively about them in class, so you dont really need to read them.  There are 6 1-page summaries over 6 readings, so those are really the only ones you need to read.  Study for the tests and you should be good :)

Professor Gates is my favorite professor so far and his class will be the only one I'm sorry to leave. Very smart guy, knows his stuff and explains it very well, very engaging and makes the subject interesting, I highly recommend him! I will take any class of his I can. Very nice and easy to talk to and pretty lenient on assignments and readings.

Professor Gates is a great guy. Very lenient on late assignments and absences. Gives very clear and concise study guides for each exam and class time is interesting and useful. Probably the easiest general required class that I took at BYU. Gave about 50% effort, got an A-. Highly recommended!
Great professor. Really cares about students. I very rarely went to class but kept up on assignments and studied hard for tests and got an A-. Gates is awesome.

Great guy, difficult class. There is a LOT of reading that you need to do before each class or else lectures will be completely over your head. If you approach him one-on-one he is SUPER helpful. He hands out a study guide for each exam. Try as hard as you can to memorize everything from it and regurgitate it back for the exams.

This was a good class. Other rating describe the professor well. Sometimes kind of side tracked but very nice. Willing to help if has time but it seemed like he never had much time. If you do all the readings everything makes much more sense. There is a fair amount to read though. I enjoyed the class when i understood.

Read from textbook in class. Grading standards are subjective and vague. Very slow to return graded material. I didn't know what my grade was till the end of the semester. There are better teachers in the Philosophy Department.

Professor Gates is a very insightful professor.  He makes his opinions known, but also acknowledges other opinions and admires well-constructed arguments, no matter what they are arguing for.  He made this class interesting and fun when it had the potential to be very dull!

Gates is an average teacher, nothing special. He likes the sound of his own voice and is not good about replying to e-mails and grading on time. He goes off on irrelevant tangents all the time which makes for a frustrating learning environment. If you really want to learn, pick a different professor.

Dr. Gates is a very good teacher. It is true he has tangents, but he some how, nearly, always applies the tangent to the subject. Most of the class is graded on papers you write. He is a strict grader, but this forces you to learn how to write better. I definitely have become a better writer in many ways. I recommend Dr. Gates!

Very nice professor, can be easily distracted at times but his tangents can also be very interesting.  The class was slow at the beginning but got much better by the end of the semester.  The assignments are reasonable, and I learned a lot about being able to argue my point and he helped me to improve my college writing a great deal.

institutes great discussion. knowing the study guide is imperative to the tests. very accomodating to student's needs. a page summary was required every class for the assigned reading, but he basically gives a 100% if you did it. we barely used our textbooks.

A good teacher, but sometimes absent minded. Looks like Matt Damon. I enjoyed this class and learned a lot! Interesting lectures but sometimes hard to follow. Only saw our total grades once--not posted on Blackboard.  16 1-page reading summaries (basically pass/fail), 2 2-3 page papers, 2 midterms, and the final. For tests, study the review sheets!

Prof. Gates is a great guy.  He tends to go off on some tangent, but not as much as most of the other philosophy professors I've had.  As long as you memorize the study guides he gives you'll know everything you need to know for his tests.

This professor is fantastic. I have some health problems, and he has been very accommodating with my physical limitations. Very thorough exploration of the subject material, not just a superficial skimming.

This guy is the most useless teacher I have encountered. I bought the textbook, placed it on my shelf, and today I retrieved it to look up the ISBN. Not once have we used the book. If you want to learn about the humanities, play "The Longest Journey" by funcom. You learn far more from this than you would from this class.

Professor Gates is a really cool guy. His teaching style is a bit spacy and the lectures are sometimes hard to get information out of. He does provide reviews for his tests which have basically everything you need to know. Just memorize the information on those and you'll be fine. I recommend this class though, and I don't care much for philosophy.

Great Great Teacher. One of my favorites at BYU. Very nice guy with great insights. A little spacy at times, but what Philosophy professor isn't? Class was always engaging and interesting.  Take a class from him if you get the chance

I was upset that I had to take English again for my major despite having passed the AP English test, but I loved this class.  It was so fun to debate morality issues and I loved writing the papers.  He just isn't the most accurate with his grammar knowledge.  Big comma splice freak.

Professor Gates is a good guy.  He seems really laid back but he knows his stuff.  The first test of the semester is KILLER but the subsequent test and final are MUCH easier.  It can be a difficult topic to comprehend and he doesn't do a GREAT job at explaining it sometimes, but he will explain it better if you ask him to.
Gates is sick. This is a way good class. Teaches you how to think. I would not buy the grammar book though. Expensive and i used it once for two minutes. Gates For President '08

Professor Gates has a very affable personality, and his demeanor towards his students is great.  He answers pretty much every question you have about the readings, so the only real task you are responsible for is putting forth your time in studying your notes.  If you do that, you should have no problem getting a good grade.

Tests were memorization from the lectures. Write down what he says in review and memorize it - I learned this after a 74% on a test I felt prepared for. He was really disorganized - lost several of my assignments, didn't pay much attention grading tests. Nice guy, knowledgeable, but not very helpful to students.

This class was interesting, but the tests require memorization of basically everything discussed in class. If you memorize well, go for it, but if not ... beware. It's all verbatim listing of philosophical arguments, etc. Prof. Gates is wonderful, though. And easy on the eye, which is refreshing.

One of the best professors I've had. He was a little unorganized, but that seemed due to faculty transition. He was more interested in everyone learning, rather than tests. A lot of writing, but it's not hard if you go to class. I'd take his class again anytime.

I really enjoyed this class. The readings (few that I did) were really interesting and brought up strong arguements. I learned to find other foundations for my opinions besides moral and religious beliefs.

Prof Gates is a really nice guy.  He remains pretty opinionated and kind of teaches his opinions as the best choice, but listens to others.  A lot of readings that you dont really need to do, but are interesting.  The papers are pretty easy.  He is pretty disorganaized in his lectures. Attendance is not manditory to do well in this class.

I'm not even joking about the easiness factor, this class was pretty pleasant with the workload.  Pretty disorganized teacher, but a good guy still the same.  Material was fairly confusing, but if you want a good grade and one of the more neutral Philosophy professors at BYU, I reccommend him.

Okay...the bad news, he's a little random and spacey at times.  The good news, he puts everything on blackboard, helps as much as he can, gives you everything you need to know for tests, is fair, entertaining, and the man's extremely attractive--always wears blue to compliment the eyes.  Don't take if prone to distraction; otherwise enjoy.
Professor Gates is a very good teacher and a great guy. You get out of the class what you put in. If you do the readings and come to class you will get a lot out of it.

Was the most unorganized teacher I've ever had.  He only knew the answers to the questions he was prepared to talk about.  Other than that, you were on your own.  He was a nice guy, very funny, but I'd never take a class from him again!

this class was a total waste of my time. he gave us a lot of reading to do which we were never tested over and usually never even discussed. also, attendence does not count for any of your grade, so why go and listen to a discussion that does nowhere? he is a great guy, but a very disorganized and ineffectual teacher. take a real phil class.
Don't take this class. Take a real philosophy class and take a real first-year writing class. It was so boring and I learned nothing. Great, nice guy but bad class.
The summaries due at the end of each reading are lame.  And the reading is a lot.  If you like philosopy, you'll like the class.

Don't expect him to come to class prepared with an organized, coherent lecture.  Also, don't expect to see any of your grades until the final exam--he waits until the last minute to do his grading.  This class is pretty easy because he doesn't expect much, but it is hard in the sense that you have no idea what to expect on the exam or for homework.
Interesting man. Fun class.
great

Favorite Teacher at BYU. Focused on learning, not cramming and regergitating for tests. Makes you read and try to understand. Explains hard concepts well. Learns every student's name. Willing to be reasonable about strange circumstances that affect your class performance. such a nice guy
Good guy, interesting lectures.  Very straight forward class

Brother Gates, while somewhat unorganized and computer illiterate, is a good guy and has a great interest in the gospel and helping students learn. No paper to write, though 1 page summaries are due after each reading. Tests are reasonable and he does try to get review material out before each test.

SUCH A GOOD GUY!! He's just getting into teaching religion, so he's a little unorganized... but makes up for it. He gives VERY comprehensive reviews for tests-- just do the readings and you'll be fine. Also- he always makes you feel like your opinion/pov matters.
good teacher but some of his test questions are pretty random.  they're all free response, so its kind of difficult
Good man.

Not the most challenging professor, but he is entertaining and he understands and explains the material extremely well.  He takes a sincere interest in students and often goes beyond the call of duty to assist them.

Positives: Good discussions, explains concepts well, considerate of students, makes class interesting. Fair amount of work, but pretty easy to get an A. Downsides: If you want a hard-core "academic," he's probably not your man. Habitually late f

Dr. Gates is an excellent teacher.  The idiot who says he is borring is dead wrong.  His class is always intriquing and meaningful---if you come to class, listen, and do the reading.  He is able to explain very difficult material in a clear manner.

I'm not sure what philosophy classes these other students have taken before but it takes much more than a Nice, Cool, guy to be able to teach philosophy in a meaningful way. His class was boring and unchallenging...but an easy A.

Dr. Gates is an excellent teacher who cares whether you succeed or not.  He is flexible and understanding of college workloads.  While he is well educated and intelligent, he is very good at making you feel like your comments are valued.
No Comments
great guy greeat class very personable and helpful. was in a depeche mode like keyboardy rock band in his younger years. very cool teacher
Professor Gates is a highly interactive teacher.  He's personable and allows for great discussions.  You will come away feeling like you've learned so much!

Clearly cares about his students, which I respect, but talks as if his class is more important in the lives of students than it is. Lots of writing assignments, but lab assignments are really fun. I learned a lot, but I didn't love how the information was presented. Textbook is free and online. Uses Max rather than Learning Suite. Very accessible
Honestly his personality is the worst part of his teaching, and he went on tangents about unimportant things like not using the word "can't."

Dr. Ragozzine is great. however, this class took up way too many hours of my week. every class you have to report on what you learned in previous classes and if you attended. weekly assignments which took me 4+ hours each. TA's are great and give extensions for everything basically so that's an advantage. tests are open note and open book though.

Professor Ragozzine is so much fun and witty in his lectures. He allows for a lot of help from other students and TAs for assignments and its wonderful. He also allows for extensions to be given even if you just need extra time on an assignment. Overall one of the best professors that I've ever had.

You can easily do well in this class. The professor gives out 5 extra credit points for every exam and they are all open note and book. He is an easy grader and doesn't hesitate to give out extensions. The assignments do require concept application in new situations we haven't specifically discussed but there are plenty of TA's willing to help.

Idk how this class has great reviews. Very passionate- not good teacher. Jumps in without covering basic physics principles. Tests SO long (final was 6 hours). Wordy- his instructions are 4+ pages. TAs are so behind on grading that idk what I'll end w (just finished the final and they're still grading my midterm). Just take physical science instead

He is very intelligent and kind. He just isn't a teacher. Classes were lecture heavy. Homework was long and involves topics that were not discussed. BUT the assignments are graded easily. The tests are open-book.
just awesome

I took this class to fulfill a GE credit but Dr Ragozzine is a really good teacher, so I enjoyed the class. You could do well on tests and assignments by attending class and listening to him teach/lecture. He uses a lot of examples in class to help students understand. Big assignments are due every week, but the tests are open-note. Take his class!

Legit, changed my life.  He makes it clear our academic success is his number one priority. Difficult when it comes to putting your mind to work but the results are priceless. So grateful I took this class my first semester. He is homie and so kind, he always connected lectures to the gospel and is a master teacher.

This is the HARDEST and the BEST class I have ever taken at BYU. Dr. Ragozzine is an amazing professor because he gave me the guidance I needed to figure things out on my own. And because I figured out such complicated things on my own with the concepts he taught me in lecture, I have gained so much confidence in my ability to do hard things.

This professor clearly knows a lot about astronomy, however his lectures and homework assignments are designed for people with a previous understanding of physics and astronomical concepts. His tests and homework assignments are ridiculously long, and he words them extremely poorly.

If I was not taking any other class, or if I was an astronomy major I might think differently. But this class was much harder than any of my junior or senior core classes. I wish I could say I learned something, but to be super blunt the amount of work he gives and expects gave me no choice. All that I learned went straight into short term memory.

Don't take this class unless you have a solid background in physics and are willing to spend beyond 7 hours a week working. It took 3 months for my first exam to be graded, there's so much homework, and the slides don't have all the information needed for tests. He's wonderful, caring person, but a confusing professor. Avoid this class for the GE.

All tests and the final are online and open note but the average in the class this semester was a 72. If you pay attention is class you will do a lot better, it is just a bit difficult to follow at times which makes it easy to space out.

Doctor Ragozzine went above & beyond my expectations. I look forward to his class because he himself is AWESOME. He's great at presenting his lectures. He brings a wonderful positive presence while lecturing. He answers students' questions in a manner that never makes them feel stupid. He is ALWAYS knowledgeable when asked questions.He made it fun.

Does not teach well, you pretty much have to teach yourself. Gives a lot of busy work for homework (he says it is to help you, but you learn nothing from it). There are fun aspects of the class, like learning the constellations, but overall I think he needs to work on the setup of his class and teach in a way that will help the majority of students

SUCH an amazing professor. He really emphasize learning over grades. He gives you TONS of chance to practice for tests and has really small in class quizzes that aren't graded, but that still let you practice accessing test-like questions on a regular basis.

I learned nothing in this class it was way to difficult for a ge and not worth the time. Dr. Ragozzine was very nice and was lenient with assignments, but I dont think he understood how to teach the material in a way where we could actually understand what he was trying to teach.

At the beginning it was a little overwhelming because there are a LOT of assignments in this class. However, he's really flexible about turning things in. Overall, it was a good class and it really isn't that hard to get an A if you do your assignments. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. Probably one of the most caring and kind professors I know

He is amazing! 227 involves helping write a scientific paper! The tests are scary, and homework is intimidating, but if you try, you'll for sure get an A. I definitely was nowhere near the best in the class, yet I still ended up getting over 100 due to his extra credit opportunities. He makes it a very spiritually focused class as well!
Super helpful and flexible with assignment due dates.

This class was really hard. There was lots of busy work and the tests were incredibly difficult. There is also a lot of spiritual thoughts and a religious paper. Dr. Ragozzine obviously cares about his students and is a a good lecturer, but I did not enjoy the class.

I've been at BYU for 8 semesters and Professor Ragozzine is by far the greatest professor I have ever had. His teaching style is phenomenal, effective, and entertaining. He genuinely cares about each of his students. He expects a lot but isn't a difficult grader. The tests made me feel proud because I walked out saying "wow, I did that." LOVE HIM

This class is a joke. It's an unbelievable amount of work for a GE class. If you hate euphemisms, don't sign up for this class. Every assignment has a different title: HW is not HW, test is not a test, etc. The assignments usually have 15 things to go along with it, and if you would enjoy time to do hw from any other class, don't sign up for this.

Amazing class and an amazing professor. Readings for each class day, but you'll only be quizzed once a week on one of those readings and the quiz is open textbook so they're all super easy. Very engaging class. Hardest part of the class was the homework due at the end of each week, but if you put an hour or so into it you'll be fine.

Dr. Ragozzine is a super caring professor. He makes an effort to get to know each student. The class is difficult, but he is willing to meet with you. The homework can be long and difficult, so make sure to take advantage of office hours both with Dr. Ragozzine and the TAs. There is quite a bit of extra credit available.

Definitely one of my favorite professors I've had. Takes the time to know his students, and help them succeed personally. The class format is really easy to understand but very different from other professors. We did a lot of varied types of work, including working on an active research project. Super interesting class, great lectures.

Nice guy and pretty engaging in class. Grading wise you will get 10% on one assignment then 100% on the next assignment, though that is because the TA grading isn't super consistent throughout the semester. Over all i would recommend him. However, he often posts last minute assignments that take 5hrs to complete, which kind of drove my crazy.

He definitely makes you think more than other physics professors. Most of his problem sets don't have clear-cut answers for you to just give. It doesn't feel like it while you're taking the class, but there's a fairly decent amount of extra credit available, too. He understands the student's lives, so he's very caring and accommodating.

Good class, but lots of homework. Problem sets are often an all-day endeavor if you wait until the day before they're due. The book is needed for some homework problems and the weekly quizzes, but other than that I didn't use it much. Lectures are interesting and engaging.
I loved this class and this professor. I would definitely recommend this class if you are interested in astronomy. The class isn't easy, but it is definitely fair.

Dr. Ragozzine is a great lecturer! He explains concepts very well -- even with no astronomy background you could understand. You definitely need to understand the topics to do the homework, but if you want to succeed, he makes it possible, as long as you actually are trying.

Dr. Ragozzine is an incredible professor. He sincerely cares about his students and gives many opportunities to succeed in his class, including tons of Office Hours, TA help, partial and extra credit on exams, etc. He teaches in a way that you can't simply regurgitate information, but you learn the concepts on a deeper level and learn to apply them

Dr. Ragozzine is an AMAZING professor! He has a knack for explaining difficult concepts in ways that make sense, and I really enjoyed going to lectures. Some of the material is a bit tough, but he's a generous grader. If you put in some effort, you'll do fine. Take classes from Dr. Ragozzine!

Professor Ragozzine was disorganized and assigned way too much work for a 3 credit class. There are many projects that will take weeks to complete, so start them far in advance. He gives problem sets almost every week that take over 4 hours to complete and are graded on effort and accuracy. A lot of work and time dedicated to a difficult class.

Dr. Ragozzine is probably one of the smartest professors you'll ever have. I enjoyed his lectures and how hard he worked to integrate modern developments in astronomy into the class. He's a little disorganized, but he explains things very clearly, which was nice considering this sophomore-level class used a senior-level textbook.

He's a nice guy, but honestly the class was extremely unorganized and unclear. He explains things in very unnecessarily complicated ways, even the TAs in the reviews admitted he didn't teach us the right stuff. His instructions would be 10 pages long when they could be a paragraph. I was so excited for astronomy, but i'd suggest a different teacher

I really enjoyed this class. It was a lot of work, but I don't mind the subject matter so it didn't bother me too much.  Professor Ragozzine was really interested in helping out his students and making sure he was on the right track. Take this class, he cares about you and cares about Astronomy. He really is a sweet man and the Planetarium is cool.

This is Dr. Ragozzine's first year teaching a 100 level astronomy class, so often it was close to the due date when he released assignments, but this will most likely be better because now he already has all his material prepared. There are lots of opportunities to get extra credit in this class.

Dr. Ragozzine is an amazing professor. He's very passionate and very knowledgeable. His lectures were some of the best that I've ever had. He is very engaging and explains things very clearly. His class is rigorous, but you have everything you need to succeed if you put in the effort, and you'll be better for it in the end.

So Dr. Ragozzine is a really nice guy. You can tell he really cares about his students and what he's teaching, however, he is also kind of new to teaching.  He writes test and homework questions that only make sense to him, post assignments only a couple days before they are due, and does not explain difficult concepts very well.

Professor Ragozzine is very passionate about what he teaches. He is willing to help students and answer questions, however, he gives a TON of busy work and projects that require a lot of outside class on-campus work. The assignments are usually simple enough but take hours to complete and are confusing.

It's nice to watch films in class but when people are always falling asleep, you're better off watching them at home. He doesn't use Learning Suite — big L if you don't own a printer — and his teaching either repeats the readings or is entirely off-topic. For exams, you kinda have to know EVERYTHING about the films — he doesn't exactly prepare you.

Professor Larsen was such an engaging, substantive, and fun instructor. There was a short written assignment every week for the first 2/3 of the semester and two exams, all of which I found super manageable and helpful. Since being in the class, I feel like my understanding and appreciation of film has significantly greater depth.

Darl is a phenomenal professor. The laid back vibe of this class made me eager to actually learn the information I wanted to learn. He expects the best and gives points for the things you do know. Just an incredible class from an incredible teacher.

Darl is really awesome and funny too. I took history of animation from him and found the class relaxing actually. The exams are lecture-based, so only a bit of the readings apply. You also get to watch a lot of old cartoons all the way to the modern-day. I recommend that you watch all the additional viewings he sends.

Let me be clear: Darl is the best professor Ive ever had, and one of the best people Ive ever gotten the chance to know. In every class, hell leave you to achieve what you want to. Hell give you all the ressources to succeed, but he wont make you, he wont tell you even what success means. Dont take his classes for granted, youll want more.

Darl is a great professor. But he expects quality. He's not going to treat you like a child or hold you by the hand. You'll do a lot of your own learning, and get supplemental comments from him. Watch out for the "fun page" on his exams, and be sure to read and watch the movies, even if he doesn't take attendance.

I had Darl for History of American Animation and it was my FAVORITE class I had ever taken! He is so funny, smart, articulate: I looked forward to coming to class because it was a blast.  Half of the class you watch cartoon clips which are awesome.  Easy A as long as you listen and take notes.   Just an all around fun class.

Darl is the best professor in the ENTIRE WORLD! He is so knowledgeable of all the concepts he teaches in class. The films are both insightful and entertaining. It is hard to be bored in his class not only because there is so much to learn, but he has such a laid back attitude and simply put: he's hilarious. I definitely have a teacher crush on him!
Darl is a great teacher. I love his dry humor and the ease whith which he can articulate concepts and ideas. His class is always interesting and I would definitely take another class from him.

Professor Young is a great teacher for anybody looking to get into writing. She covers a range of different kinds of writing as well as some of the most technical things like how to go about being published. There is a lot of reading to do for this class but good writers are prolific readers.

This class was disappointing. Professor Young used contract grading this semester, and I hope she doesn't continue it. You can put in a lot of effort, but if your assignment is not perfect, you get a zero or maybe half credit. She also moves on to new assignments before the last ones are due. I wouldn't recommend this professor.

Professor Young is great! She gives you clear instructions and good feedback. If you do the work, show up to class, and follow her instructions (on Learning Suite, very clearly written), you'll succeed. She responds quickly to emails and is super willing to meet with you if you need. Great choice for this GE!

Sister Young's class was informative and a great introductory/review of creative writing skills. She gives great feedback and is very accommodating. Class attendance is necessary and so is participation with your peers.
She understands the use of AI in our day and age. Honestly, she's a fair grader for an abstract subject such as writing. Highly recommended and suggested.
Professor Young is an amazing writing instructor. Her critiques are valuable, and she's devoted to helping students improve. Unstuck AI was a game-changer for preparing for her class.

Prof. Young is an amazing creative writing teacher! She gives honest feedback and truly wants each student to improve, which I definitely did thanks to her. She assigns a fair amount of readings, but they're super beneficial and worth the time if you really want to improve your writing. Nice to work with; I highly recommend her.

An incredible professor and an incredible writer. She provides harsh (but very helpful and very clear) feedback, and it is obvious that she wants each student to improve. Lectures are engaging and fun. Lots of homework, but it is often enjoyable and her instructions are clear. She does her best to help students learn to love the writing process.

Prof Young is amazing! She is extremely clear in her grading and grades strictly by her rubric, so grading doesn't feel subjective at all. She is super willing to help out and wants everyone to do well in her class. She puts a lot of work into organizing her content in the best way possible and it pays off. I would def take her again!

Professor Young was awesome. She clearly defined what it would take in her class to get a good grade and was very fair. She warns you in advance when you need to start working on things and is gracious in how she orders the class around breaks and such.

Professor Young is an amazing professor who understands that most of her WRTG 316 students do not want to write. That's one reason why some STEM majors even choose to go into STEM. So she totally understands. I really enjoyed the class. I will recommend, for the instructions unit, design instructions that she won't have materials to test. Trust.

Professor Young's class will challenge your writing and force you to grow as a writer. You'll have to devote a significant amount of time to reading and writing for her class, but it is worth it. She is a phenomenal instructor.

Professor Young is a really good teacher! She is a tough grader but has very specific rubrics. She gives you lots of resources to succeed in her class. All of the assignments are helpful in the workforce. You need to put in the work, especially in the big literature review assignment, but it's very doable. I would take it from her again!

She does a great job at explaining the concepts of writing various genres. She's a discovery writer, so some of the concepts she teaches lean more towards that, though as a planner myself, I still found it helpful.
