She also critiques precisely and intensely, but it's very helpful for improving your work.

Prof. Young is pretty nit-picky and will dock you points for little things. At times she can be a little bit condescending when teaching or answering students' questions. That being said she makes the class manageable and although the class will keep you busy, it's never too much to handle.

Darlene Young is an excellent professor. She is very smart and efficient, and she gives good feedback on projects. She is also respectful and kind. 

The Creative Writing class is made up of three sections: Poetry, Fiction, and Personal Essay. I learned so much every class period and the readings are at most two hours for every class period.

Professor Young is a great teacher. I took this class as an elective and was worried that it would be more intense than I wanted, not being an English major. But I am glad I took this class! I learned a lot about how to better express my ideas and through each of the writing assignments. Her grading criteria is very clear.

Professor Young is not only a great teacher, but more importantly for a Creative Writing class, an exceptional writer. I struggle listening to feedback from my peers or professors that are unable to write well; that was not the case here. Professor Young has a strong understanding of what makes a good story, and I accepted all of her feedback well.

Writing 316 is not an easy class, but is very much required. Dr. Young hands down has to be the best professor to take this from. There is lots to do, but it is organized in a manageable way. Dr. Young is always ready to help if you fall behind. 100% Recommend

She was an INCREDIBLE teacher! I appreciated all of her insights and teachings. She was very focused on helping us know everything she has gone through to be a published writer. I became a better writer throughout this class. She gives a lot of feedback--heavier on the critque side than on reinforcement. I would take this class again!

Dr. Young really cares about her students. I can attest to this with a quick experience. Two absences are allowed, and I had already used both before learning of a medical school interview that would take place during class. I talked with Dr. Young, and she was very helpful in allowing me to miss another class period so that I could interview.

Amazing professor! She helped me a lot when it came to my writing and how to use grammar. She seemed to care about each of us and wanted us to succeed. She has quizzes and assignments that are do before the class time (could change each semester) so make sure you are aware when assignments are due.

Professor Young made WRTG 316 my favorite non-CS class. There are so many cool projects you get to work on. Make sure you keep track of all the little assignments and due dates so you don't lose any points. Take this class from her!!!

Mrs. Young is amazing! It is so easy to learn with her. She is great at explaining things so learning feels very natural. She is very considerate of the reading material and makes sure it is easily accessible--everything can be found online. We had a few quizzes but she went over what was on them so it wasn't a surprise. Participation matters.

She is a very kind, understanding and intelligent professor. You will definitely learn how to become a better writer in this class! There are no big exams-just a couple little quizzes that are easy. The biggest things is making sure you do the readings before each class (there are about 3 ish), and doing the writing (3 different units).

Professor Young's Creative Writing unit was one of the most enjoyable courses I've taken as an English major. I feel as though I've really improved as a writer, and I'm happy that there was more than just fiction in the genres we chose to study. If I weren't a senior, I'd honestly consider switching tracks due to the class.

Professor Young's feedback on assignments can sometimes be brutal. She usually gives you full credit for assignments as long as you follow certain guidelines (double-spaced, serif font, etc.), which she'll tell you at the bottom of the assignment description, but will almost always give you plenty of feedback, some of which can be tough.

Professor Young is amazing. She pushes you to hone your writing skills, and explore new things. The readings are due every class period, but there isn't a lot of reading to do, and it is ALWAYS very helpful for writing things in general. If you don't like getting critiqued on your work, don't take her as she plus your classmates critique your work.

Professor Young is a great Creative Writing professor. She always gave lots of great feedback on all of my projects and pushed me to be a better writer. I would definitely recommend her course to anyone.

I loved Sister Young's class! She's really good at exposing students to good literature, good examples of what we would be writing. And she's great at breaking down what a good piece of writing is. I'm a pretty terrible writer, my poetry is non-existant, but I still loved her class. Do yourself a favor and take it with her!

Sister Young is awesome. She is super caring and is always accessible outside of class. She pushes you to try new things in your writing, and makes things worth enough points to where you can try new things and not have to worry about it affecting your grade! Her feedback is also super helpful. I would recommend her to anyone taking this class.

Sister Young is super nice, always willing to help, and easy to talk to after or outside of class. Her class is easy to get an A in as long as you actually do the small assignments. She purposefully makes them worth more than the few big assignments so that you can experiment and learn without the pressure.

This is for WRTG 316 but I didn't have that option. Not going to lie, the lectures are a little dry when she needs to cover the BYU-required curriculum. However, she does plan the course so that you can succeed. You will need the textbook for a few reading quizzes, but those are not hard. If you want you can show her before submitting it.
Best professor I had all semester! Genuinely helpful and so much fun. Can't recommend her enough.

Sister Young is an incredible lady! She cared so much about her students and she knows a lot about LDS literature. Her midterm was a little tricky, but she gives study guides that are really helpful. If you are looking for a letters GE, I would highly recommend this one! Would take it from her again.

Professor Young is the sweetest lady ever! I felt like I learned a lot and I wasn't constantly worried about assignments like in other classes. She gives really good feedback because she takes the time to get to know you and to get to know your writing. I would recommend her to anyone.

I can't recommend Sister Young highly enough! She is accomodating of circumstances and needs, she is more than willing to give feedback (which is both consturctive and encouraging), and she has designed the course to set you up for success. There is a lot of writing practice and reading, but most assignments are participation based. She is great!

Professor Young was a great mentor! Her feedback on assignments was always clear and helpful, and she helped introduce me to various genres. I actually like poetry now! Her class does require effort, though. There's always an assignment to be done and there's a lot of (helpful) readings. It takes time, but your writing will improve!

Prof. Young's class is demanding, but very rewarding. Her lectures, homework, and in-class activities are engaging and hands-on. Through them you learnt to be a much better writer, because she is a true mentor.

Sister Young was amazing. She really cares about her students and helping them grow and develop as writers. There is work to be put in, but that is to be expected if you want to learn and grow. That being said, it was manageable and never too much.
One of the most caring and wonderful professors I have ever had. If you are thinking about becoming a writer please take her class! She will help so much and she genuinely cares.

This class was a lot of fun. I learned a lot about creative writing and we got to do fun exercises that helped a lot. There were a decent amount of readings, but they are all creative writing, and fun. There were also a lot of smaller writing assignments. Just stay caught up on homework and you're golden.

I loved Professor Young! She really helped my writing and had interesting lectures. She's very good about critiquing your papers honestly, but respectfully, and I always agreed with her feedback. She's not a pushover, and this isn't an easy A, but I would say your grade is more based on effort and improvement rather than ability to write.

Dr. Young is a phenomenal professor. She allows the student to put forth the effort and let them decide how much they want to grow throughout the semester. She stretches your writing and allows you to improve all the time. I would say if you are looking for an easy A this is not the class. You will have to work for it.

Dr. Young was one of my favorite writing professors! She really helped my writing improve --but she makes you work for that improvement. Be prepared for some critiques on your writing, but also for compliments too! She really emphasizes attendance, so if you don't come to class, expect to fail. I loved her so much, and she's very caring.
Very thoughtful and provides interesting insights. Always willing to help.
She cares about us and treats us like friends. She is great at teaching the subject and at giving constructive feedback. My wrigint improved more than I thought possible because of her.

She knows the subject and has real world experience in the field. Class was usually pretty interesting. The attendance policy is a little extreme, but I believe that's more the fault of the English program than the teacher. I also didn't think that the packet we were supposed to buy contained anything we couldn't have done without.

This was a great elective that forced me to drastically improve as a writer. She definitely spends extra time on poetry, as it is her expertise, but those skills transferred directly to my ability to write fiction, so don't dismiss it.
Darlene is such a sweet teacher and the class is a blast. There's a lot of work, but it's all creative.

Darlene is a great professor that I think really taught me how to think differently about writing. However, if you're wanting an easy A this is not your class. There are plenty of assignments given in this class but they were for the benefit of the student.

Darlene is a super great professor who is clear in her teaching and grading, you basically grade yourself on the major papers! As long as you do the homework you will pass, and learn a lot about writing as well. Great class and worth the time! Fun assignments too.

This class was great. I learned a lot about writing--different techniques, what to do, what not to do. I felt like I produced really great and meaningful content in this class. In order to get better you have to practice, so there's quite a bit of writing and reading that goes along with this class. The good news is if you do it you'll get an A.
Darlene is a good teacher. She is still new to the college method of teaching but at the rate she is going she will be a great professor in no time. Highly recommended.

Great class for both new or practiced writers. Assignments/readings favor discovery writers, so if you like to outline, might not be for you, unless you're interested in learning different techniques. Good place to practice--graded on effort, not quality (thank heavens). Lectures are well prepared and interesting. Darlene is a star.

Sister Young is amazing. Yes, she gives you homework that pushes you. BUT if you do it the best that you can she will give you full points. She encourages creativity and therefore will not dock points on content as long as you try. She is very accessible outside of class. I emailed her for help once and she replied in less than ten minutes.
Sister Young is awesome! I loved this class and I highly recommend taking it from her!
A little bit heavy on connecting course to Mormonism and very heavy on writing assignments, but overall wonderful
Sister Young is so good at walking you through the writing process from beginning to end. Learned so much!
Sister Young is an amazing professor. I would highly recommend taking her class if you want to truly grow as a writer. I learned so much!

Darlene is a wonderful professor who cares about the subject that she is teaching as well as the students she is teaching the subject to. There is a lot of reading, but it is not too difficult if you are willing to set aside a chunk of time. It is enjoyable reading material, so that helps. I would recommend this class!

She was one of my favorite professors. Really engaging, she really tried to tailor her lessons to help us grow and develop. She really cared also about our mental and physical wellbeing and tried to elevate the heavy readings required for the course. Readings can be sometimes overwhelming at times along with the assignments but still a great class

Great professor. She really cares about her students and their success. Sometimes it felt like there were too many assignments due at a time, but even so the readings were engaging and inspirational. It makes sense that the class is participation heavy, but it's unfortunate that there have to be so many grades to "force" work. Took the fun out.

I loved this class. All the teachers in the English department want to teach English 218 so the ones who get there want to stay. Darlene's class makes you a better writer and she's genuinely interested in your work and improvement. There are a few short group projects and a weekly 1 page response that goes with her assigned reading. TAKE THIS CLASS

There is a lot of work in this class but the nice part is that as long as you do it all you'll get an A but most of it is fun to do anyways so it's not a big deal. Most of the work is given full credit as long as you completed it by the deadline and fulfilled the basic requirements which she is always very clear on.
Excellent class, I've really come to love writing after taking it.
A fair bit of work: something is due almost every period. Gives good and detailed feedback most of the time. Open with the class. Readings are hit and miss, but they do the job.

Darlene is a super great teacher. I was having a really difficult semester and she was so understanding when I came to her with my concerns. The assignments are all interesting and incredibly helpful. She gives great feedback, especially since this will not the last draft of some projects for some writers.

Professor Young is great; she really cares about helping you improve your ability to write! She's really good at returning emails and will give you as much feedback as you can handle. Class can be a little dry, but the readings are usually interesting/instructive. There's a bit of group work and a lot of peer review, but nothing too painful.

I honestly loved this class. I laughed, I cried (in a good way), and overall had a great experience and learned a lot. She took time to get to know us, and although there was fair amount of readin/writing, she gave a lot of detailed feedback on our assignments that was SUPER helpful.

The workload seemed to be a bit much at times, but the grading is super lenient, so you get full credit on pretty much everything if you turn it on time, and getting an A isn't super hard. If you're willing to work for it a little bit you can really learn a lot.

She taught me so much about sensory writing, and opened up my mind to lots of different ways of thinking about writing. She explained real-world experiences about publishing and writing. I got a lot out of her class! Take her class!

The class is centered around writing (Our tests were writing assignments), and the difficulty really depends on how much work you want to put in. Darlene Young makes sure to give you all the tools you need to succeed, and effort alone gets you a good grade. There are a lot of writing assignments, and a few partner assignments, but I enjoyed them.

I seriously loved this class. Sis. Young does a great job of making this class fun and enjoyable but also super informative. She obviously knows her stuff and is always willing to give super helpful feedback--even after you aren't her student anymore. I felt like my writing abilities improved substantially, and I always wanted to come to class.
Professor Young does a great job of giving every student a chance to receive clear feedback and improve as a writer. It is evident that she cares about her students' success.

Sister Young is a nice and caring professor. I was not as much fan of the heavy number of readings from Mormon authors and would have preferred to have more variety, but otherwise, I feel like Sister Young is a great person and a truly involved professor

Professor Young is genuine and passionate about writing. Classes were interesting and I learned a lot. She is picky about grammar and you will read a lot. The readings as good. This class has a lot of assignments, but if you do them, she will reward you. She takes a lot of time giving feedback on papers which is very helpful.

Prof Young cares about her students. She's encouraging and willing to work with you. You have to do the work to get an A, but it's not challenging if you want to become a better writer. There are group projects and attending class matters. She kind of looks down on fiction writing, but only because she loves poetry and thinks it's underrated.

This is a fun class, and Darlene is very good at teaching how to write well. She estbalishes good grammar rules after the poetry unit, and is willing to work with you, if you ask her for help via email or after class. Will push you to come up with new and fresh content so avoid common fairy tale tropes.

This class does require quite a bit of reading and homework, but it is doable and is so worth it! Even after 4 months you feel like a way better writer. Take this class with Sister Young, and you won't regret it!
Great at presenting projects, super flexible, easy/fun readings, and is willing to give extra credit if you work for it.

Prof. Young is a phenomenal teacher. She views learning as something to be enjoyed and will work with you to give you the grade you want as long as you put in the effort and turn in assignments on time. She is also extremely helpful and willing to meet outside of class and give you extra feedback to help improve your writing.

You have to push yourself to try new things, but you get good feedback and if you do your best and meet her grading criteria, you are graded generously. If you do what she asks, you will not have a problem getting an A. If you are intimidated by creative writing, Darlene is good at helping you feel comfortable experimenting with low stakes.

I really liked taking ENG218 from Sister Young! She gives great feedback. There is quite a bit of homework so it's more time consuming than an average 200 level class. Lots of reading and writing assignments, but nothing boring. You don't have to be a great writer to take the class, either, but your writing skills will definitely improve!

Sister Young knows what she's talking about and is quick to give feedback or extra help. She is real with you about what you can do to improve while still encouraging you to write how you want to write. She conveys the rules and tricks of writing in a simple way that makes it less overwhelming. You'll be a better writer because of this class.

This was a challenging course, but it taught me so much. There is a lot of reading, but everything assigned is interesting. The grading in this class is based on progress and completion. It is not based on how good of a writer you are, and from experience I can say that your writing will be better afterwards no matter how much experience you have.

Outstanding job of instructing on the material. Great examples, outstanding feedback. If you want to get better she is outstanding. If you are trying to just get by, I would find someone better. She makes you want to be your best, and then helps you understand how to get there.

Professor Young takes into account that people come to class with different skill levels, so most of the assignments are graded solely on following all the instructions and not on talent. The final assignments are graded a bit more harshly on overall quality and improvement, but the other assignments balance this so an A is very possible.
Great class, would recommend heavily for people who want to write one day

I really enjoyed taking a class from Sister Young. She has really good insights with our assignments and writing in general. Taking this class has taught me a lot more about different ways to approach writing and given me great tips for how to become a better writer.
Sister Young avoids bias when it comes to style in writing, which is super nice and allows me to write as I please.
Mrs. Young helped me get really comfortable as a writer, and even though she gives a lot of feedback and expects a lot of revision, thats a good thing!

Sister Young is fantastic! She knows what she is doing for sure. I grew so much as a writer through taking her class! Sure, the class is hard, but it was so much fun and I loved every minute of it! She loves us as students and even invited us to come to Thanksgiving dinner with her family if we had no where to go. She's just an awesome woman!

Creative writing is not an easy class by any means. Sister Young expects students to work hard, but gives them the tools necessary to succeed. This class has pushed me more than I've ever been pushed as a writer, but it has also helped me improve more than I expected.
Tons of reading, some papers, no tests. Attendance graded heavily.

It's a writing class, so naturally there was a lot of writing to be done. This also went hand in hand with the amount of readings. However, it was all interesting content, so it wasn't drudgery at all.

Sister Young is a wonderful professor who really cares about helping her students learn and grow. If you show up to class, do all the assignments, and complete the reading, you will get an A. She gives you plenty of opportunities to fix mistakes in papers, and to improve your final product, but there are quite a few assignments and readings.

This class was awesome. I've never been a writer and now all I can do is write! Sister Young is inspiring, and she gives you the tools and help you need to become a better writer. She has great lectures. There are a lot of readings, but they are helpful in your assignments. Take the class!

I am not a big writer, and this class helped me a lot. Sister Young is very engaged in her teaching as well as giving us feedback in our writing. I am thankful I took this class from her because she really takes the time with each student. Also, she answers to emails very quickly and the classes are way fun!

Sister Young is great! She cares about students having a good experience in addition to progressing. She went out of her way to help us. She's published a lot of material and really knows her stuff. She also ties the gospel into her lessons. And, as a side note, sometimes she brings doughnuts randomly to class. Do the homework and you'll be fine.

I felt like some of the feedback I got on my papers was a little frustrating because it was more about personal preference than actual craft. But this class is great for forcing you to write. It's a lot of work, but easy to get an A because most assignments are graded based on correct completion, not quality of writing. It's a safe space to write.

Prof. Young is amazing. There is a lot of writing, which is a good thing, since you signed up for a writing class. You're learning along the way, so she doesn't grade off of content, but off of improvement. She provides great feedback that has helped me become a better writer. Take her if you can!

Sister Young is one of the hardest professors I had but she is the best one too. She challenges her students. I loved her class and her genuine desire to help students become better writers shows in the work loud she gives, which is a fair amount. Do fear because she also provides a lot of help for her students. She will not give up on a student.

I am so glad that I took 218R from Darlene Young. I have never learned so much about writing!  I would take it from her again in a heartbeat. She really cares about her students and she is willing to work with you if you are willing to work with her. She cares so much! She even invited us to her house for Thanksgiving if we needed a place to go. :)
You are given a chance to learn great writing skills.  There is a lot of reading and writing of papers.  It is a very time consuming class BUT a really good one.

Prof. Young is a brilliant writer and, more importantly, a remarkable teacher. Her lectures, the reading and the assignments are all worthwhile. You will leave her class a better writer. She must spend a ridiculous amount of time grading, because she always gives a ton of specific, insightful commentary on your work. Take a class from Prof. Young!
I loved this class! Sister Young was an amazing teacher and you can tell that she values her students. She wants you to do well and you can feel it. She is an exceptional human being.

She's great. I took 218R from her and she actually seemed to genuinely to care about us growing as writers. Great feedback, willing to meet, discuss, and revise writing. Loved the writing assignments, not too many but I actually feel like I'm a better writer without being overly stressed with crazy deadlines. Take her class!!!

Brad was great, very knowledgeable in his field and very willing to help students out! He had set time periods we could meet with him on campus and ask about anything, the class, the industry or advice. The course was offered over two weeks with 4 meetings of about 4 hours which sounds like a lot, but it goes by quick and you learn a great deal!

If you are interested in an intelligence career, this class is a must-take. Not only do you gain valuable information and skills, you also gain a friend in Brad. The guy camps out at the WILK to meet with students all day to help students with questions, internship apps, and resumes. TAKE THIS CLASS!

An absolute gem of a man. Gives up considerable time to meet with you as long as you want, and is willing to help in any way possible. Has informative lectures and brings animal crackers to split the long lectures. Super helpful class that anyone, regardless of major or career interest, could benefit from taking. One of the best classes I've taken!

Professor Bruton is an engaging teacher and incredible guy. He's really funny and you can tell he cares about the students and wants them to succeed. The advice he gives regarding open source information collection is really fascinating and he gives great advice on applying for 3 letter agencies. Would highly recommend.
Super interesting subject, very interesting professor with a great history. Had some biases but definitely worth the educational experience. Very genuine teacher, much respect for him.

I'm grateful to have taken this class because it has changed my career. I went in to the class expecting to learn, but I didn't know that the skills I would learn in there would translate to a career. I'm so grateful that I took the class. It was the best class I could have possibly taken.

Brad is just a genius when it comes to this class. He has done it his whole life and teaches the course very well. You can really tell he cares about his students and spends hours outside of class accessible to you for career advice and class help.
Great gentleman, great experience taking this class from him and learning from all of his experience. Genuinely cares about his students and is invested in their success.

This is the second time Ive taken this class from Professor Bruton and Im just as happy as I was the first time I took it. He is the most accessible professor Ive had at BYU, and will do anything and everything to help you succeed both in class, and outside of class. He has a wealth of knowledge and is amazingly helpful. Take the class!

I absolutely loved this class. Prof Bruton gives unmatched insight into the intelligence field; if you're interested in that as a career path, take this class. Resume advice? Bam. He's got you. When and how to apply to three letter agencies? Boom. Whatever you need. If you put in thought/effort on the assignments, it's not difficult to get an A.

This class will provide very useful information and skills for any student that does research papers, and is absolutely necessary if you are a Poli Sci major or have any interest in the CIA, DIA, DHS, or any other intelligence agency whether working for the government or through a private company's intelligence department. Wonderful professor.

Absolutely must take if youre interested in intelligence/national security. Brad will be your mentor and best friend as you seek a career in intelligence- MEET HIM OUTSIDE OF CLASS. He is available during the 2 weeks to meet students- BRAD IS THE BEST!! This class got me my dream internship, even though OSINT isnt my thing. BUSY 2 weeks.
Brad is very relaxed and does an excellent job with the course. He teaches practical skills and is an excellent source for anyone interested in a career in Open Source or Intel in general.

Absolutely necessary if you want to have anything to do with the intelligence community. Take advantage of the opportunity to meet with him outside class, it works wonders. Class itself is a bit long with 3.5 hour sessions, but you'll be glad you did it. Brad's a great guy, and the class isn't hard.

Brother Bruton was absolutely amazing, and this class was just as incredible. I was intimidated by the 3.5 hour classes, but the time flew by. Brother Bruton is very knowledgeable and full of personality. Shares plenty of stories (and animal crackers), and gives advice and unique viewpoints on intelligence agencies in the US. A must take class!

The nature of this class is inherently difficult, Four sessions, hours long. However, the real value of Intro to Open Source is the out of class mentoring, networking, and just honest dialogue about intelligence careers that Brad offers out of the goodness of his heart and his honest desire to help students. Meet with him every chance you can.

Office hours are a must! He is so knowledgable and has a lot of experience in intelligence. He gave me personal advice on which agencies I should apply and what I should apply for, etc. The project is easy if you choose a country you are genuinely interested in. It's tough to get thru bc of the time, just bring snacks

Going to class is really important because that is where all of the material, quizzes, and instructions are taught. However, the most useful time is spent with him outside of the classroom when he can sit down and give career advice and get to know each other. The material he teaches is pretty self-explanatory, but he offers ton or resources.

Really great and pretty easy class. Learned not just about Open Source Intelligence but how to use the Internet for research and do better Google Searched. Definitely useful for all sorts of people, including those not interested in IC work. Also, he is very open and wants to help students, not just with the class but with their resumes and such.
He's great. The class is really straightforward and interesting. I learned a lot about open source intelligence, without having to do a crazy amount of busy work.

This is a good course and Brother Bruton is a very nice person. But Brother Bruton is never clear about what he expects. It's very hard to get an A because he doesn't tell you what he expects for an A. I think he doesn't even know what his grading criteria are. Very interesting class, but audit it. Don't take it for credit. That was my mistake.

Very willing to help students in and out of class, discuss questions and opportunities and anything else of interest. Amazing opportunity to take his class! Insightful, friendly, and dedicated to the learning experience.

Dr. Bruton's class was a gem. He brings a great deal of experience with OSINT and the IC in generally, and anyone interested in working in intelligence of any kind should take the class. He goes out of his way to meet one-on-one with students outside of class, and he gives great career advice. The class is only 1 credit, and meets only 4 times.

This is one of the most useful classes I've taken at BYU. It was only two weeks long  and individual class periods were three hours long in the evening  but I learned a lot of practical information that will be useful in both intelligence and communications fields. Bruton spends time getting to know and give advice to students. Highly recommend.

The class is only two weeks long, and so it is pretty heavy for those two weeks however well worth it. Difficult to get an A. Very difficult to get less than a B+. One of the most practical and valuable classes I have taken at BYU.
Brad is specific, intelligent, analytic, and clear. I honestly wish all my professors were like him. Take this class. Take this professor.

Professor Bruton changed my life. I have never had a professor who is more engaged with his students and truly wants them to succeed. He understands government and helps you understand what needs to be done to become successful in whatever you choose. His class is long and detailed but the information is priceless. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!! THE BEST!!!
He is a very caring professor with amazing things to learn from. This is one of the most interesting class I have taken in college.

This is quite possibly the most useful class you can take. Nothing taught is rocket science but Brad taught us how to correctly use the internet for research, and you realise just how much personal information you're giving out every single day. I learned some super valuable skills, and yes 3hrs is long, but it's only for a few weeks. Worth it.

The material is simple, but very useful if you plan to go into an intelligence field. He provides great resources and makes the material very accessible. He is also very kind and definitely cares about the students, especially if you take the time to talk to him during office hours.

I really enjoyed Prof. Bruton's class. He is excellent in his field and gives very solid, real feedback for students' work, as well as good advice for their future careers. He really cares about his students and does his best to give them opportunities for future careers in his and other fields.

He is very eager to help students, very personable, very approachable.  Excellent insight into an intelligence career. He is committed to the curve and not making this an easy A. This isn't what most people expect in a 1 credit class. He did a great job considering that we only met 4 times. It is hard to judge students based on just 4 interactions.

Professor Bruton was extremely knowledgeable and focused his lectures around practical skills. He also really cares about his students and made sacrifices to make sure everyone was on the same page and understood all of the material. He welcomed questions and always offered extra help and feedback on assignments. 10/10

I took Open Source Intelligence from Brad and would completely recommend it, especially if you're considering going into the intelligence field (in any capacity). He has a lot of experience that he freely shares and the information he teaches in the class is all useful and relevant. A good class, and potentially a valuable connection!

Professor Bruton is an excellent instructor, and this is a fantastic class. Very enjoyable - Bruton is extremely knowledgeable about this field, and kept things fresh with amusing anecdotes. He's very willing to help, and I would definitely recommend meeting with him in between class periods. Great teacher who really cares about students.

Mr. Bruton is one of the BEST instructors that I have had. All of the time spent in class was valuable and he was more than willing to meet with individual students outside of class. His real-world experience and overall genuine desire to help made his class worth taking. I would take it again in a heartbeat.

Mr. Bruton was not what I expected as the teacher for "open source intelligence". Laid back, extremely resourceful and respectful, Mr. Bruton captivated our class with fun stories and helped us immediately apply knowledge we were learning into our daily lives. I love that anyone can glean things from this class. Only four classes, great experience.

Brother Bruton was awesome!! He is so passionate about his field and is so ready and willing to help or mentor students wanting jobs in national security.  His feedback was always timely and helpful. Tough grader, but overall a great class!
This guy is awesome and is a great mentor for careers in national security and other related careers. This class is super useful.
Take this class! He is such a sweet and smart man. He knows a lot and is always willing to help with anything. He definitely does the "humblebrag" but with good reason. I really loved the class.

- In-class experience was okay.  Sometimes felt a little like death by PowerPoint, which I know is par for the course in the field.  Content was very valuable.  I especially appreciated examples from his own career. - Assignments were manageable and helpful at skill-building. - Very helpful.  Would have loved more career focusadvice.

Classes were a long two hours because the course only lasted two weeks. The materiel was interesting. Make sure you have a laptop to follow along and look up the different websites. Plus, if you go in to his office hours, he is more than willing to help you with anything course, internship, or work related.

Professor Bruton really knows his stuff. I came into the class with a fair bit of experience, but I learned a ton. I really appreciated that the homework assignments were something that helped solidify the material and something I continue to use. The classes are super long and in-depth. The class is more like training than study, but thats a plus!

Brad Bruton is a top-notch instructor with a plethora of practical knowledge to make the learning experience relevant and interesting. I could tell he was interested in the students' learning experience and was invested in helping students both as a class and individually. It would do BYU well to have an instructor with a strong security background

Granted, the class was very easy. But the time spent was long and rather useless. We had the class for four 3.5 hour sessions and I felt like a lot of the information was common sense and commonly available knowledge (how to do a precise google search). He also tended toward the humblebrag, but did have some valuable information on OSINT careers.

This class was very entertaining and valuable. Prof. Bruton keeps it entertaining with personal stories from his open source intel career all the while giving his students an in-depth view of how the open source field works and how we can be a part of it.  Very willing to work with you and give career advice and I hope he gets to do this more @ byu

Professor Bruton is a great teacher. He helps you understand the basics of open-source intel and is willing to work with you privately as well. He is a wealth of knowledge. I wish he taught more classes. highly recommend.

This was a very enlightening class. It consisted of 3 hour classes twice a week for 2 weeks, but now I know a lot about Open Source. He is entertaining and tries to make the long class time more bearable. All in all a good class

This class was such a unique offering. Brad had so much professional experience, and it was clear that he was there to share it. He didn't teach theory, but practical, career oriented skills. The classes were long, but worth it. He was so willing to offer personal advice or help. I feel like my understanding of open source gives me an advantage.

Take this class! I learned SO much and Brad has a great teaching style. He's helpful and funny and really cares about the students being able to understand the stuff. Don't be fooled that because the class is 1 credit there's not homework--there is. But it's very applicable and actually SUPER interesting when you get into it.

Class was fantastic! It was a 3 12 hour block but felt like 30 minutes. Professor Bruton is extremely informative and amusing. He welcomes all participation. I wish I had done the assignments with the intent of learning. If your class is only 2 weeks like mine, get ahead in your others so you can focus on this.  Very compassionate & concerned

It was an awesome class. He personally has lots of experience with the subject matter and conveyed it in a super helpful and clear way. Definitely worth anyone's time; he did us a huge favor by providing this class. The homework was sufficient and all very helpful and valuable, but was not overbearing. Highly recommend this class and professor.

Professor Burton is an immensely valuable teacher because of his genuine desire to help people learn combined with his knowledge gained from an entire career in intelligence. He structures his class into insightful lectures and useful assignments that teach skills necessary to his field. I would highly recommend taking this class!

Great professor with experience in the Intelligence Community. Cannot recommend this class and professor enough. The class was a little long (Four four-hour sessions) but well worth the time spent. Prof. Bruton engaged the students and kept things interesting the entire time. There was no wasted time doing busy work.

Professor Bruton has a wealth of knowledge and is eager to share it. He is one of those rare professors whose only desire is to teach. He teaches through hands-on lectures where students will learn how to use important tools for their task, and his homework assignments are exactly what you would do if you worked in the field he teaches.

I would not recommend taking POLI 200 from Dr. Hawkins. He grades arbitrarily harshly and isn't very open to students advocating for higher grades. His assignments are brutal, and the descriptions are incredibly confusing. I would take this class from someone else if you can.

Professor Hawkins is one of the best professors at BYU. He is so knowledgeable about what he is teaching and he is a very caring professor. Take advantage of his office hours and actually engage with the material. There are 5 essays in this class but they are interesting and manageable. Only 2 tests but make sure you study! 10/10 professor!
He put his own spin on this class and made it something special. He's very aware of the class and wants to help everyone succeed. Was honestly a great respite from the craziness of life.

Professor Hawkins is such a caring man. He will work with you because he understands. He made UNIV such a lovely experience because he really worked to make it meaningful. He's so funny and such a joy to be around. Take UNIV from him if you actually want to get something out of it.

I am a big fan of Dr. Hawkins. He makes an effort to keep things relevant and engaging. He's always happy to provide assistance. The workload was meaningful but not overwhelming. There were basically just a few short papers, two open note tests, and short reading responses. Would 100% recommend. You could tell he really cares.

Dr. Hawkins is a really good man. I didn't always agree with the way he set up the class, but he is really open to comments/questions throughout lectures which I enjoyed. He definitely has personal biases but we all do. I grew to really like him and he knows a lot about IR

This class was such a nightmare. The huge papers due every single Saturday ate up my weekends and had little cohesion with boring lectures and readings. Rubrics confused me so badly and feedback on papers was too late or too specific to help with future work. Class structure was horribly inconsistent and deadlines kept changing. Avoid if possible.

Professor Hawkins is a good person, but his lectures do not draw out the concepts that are required for papers. He teaches concepts required for your paper two days before it is due. There are weekly papers that take up MANY hours, definitely go to TA hours!! If you take this class, be prepared to take lighter classes during this semester.

I honestly thought this class was great! I learned a lot! Even though it does consist of quite a bit of writing, it truly is helpful and gets your thinking. I found this class helped me in other classes also. Professor Hawkins is great! I can tell that he truly prepares for his lectures and cares about what he is teaching and his students!

This class is a requirement for many majors. Professor Hawkins explains concepts really well. Both he and the T.A. have high standards for grading. On the first day, he sets the tone by warning that it's challenging to get an A, but not impossible. You need to put in significant effort, but the payoff is substantial – you'll learn a lot.

This class was hard and took up a lot of time (I recommend a lighter course load), but I honestly loved it. It stretched me and helped me grow so much in my writing skills, stats knowledge, and political science knowledge. Professor Hawkins is an awesome professor and cares about his students. He's super passionate about the content, which helps!

Professor Hawkins cares, he does, but a lot of students don't seem to like him. I thought that he taught really well and from a nuanced perspective. He is very knowledgeable on the subject at had and is very accessible. The only portion of the class that got confusing was the stats portion. It's a hard class, but Professor Hawkins makes it easier.

Dr. Hawkins loves what he teaches and cares deeply about the skills he wants you to develop. While a lot of grading is done by TA's you can do pretty good in the class if you put in the effort. This class is meant to teach you how to write professionally and that is no easy task, don't give up and don't get discouraged.

Professor Hawkins is totally awesome and such a great guy/professor. The class is challenging but if you meet with your TA it really helps!! You have every opportunity to receive a good grade and Professor Hawkins helps so much and is just so great. I really recommend him and have learned so much from this class!

Dr. Hawkins is a kind, genuine person. He wants to make the world a better place, and he shows great passion for what he teaches. This is not an easy class, but don't let that scare you away! The only way you will learn how to write in political science is to go through the refiner's fire of Poli 200. He is generally good at lecturing.

I absolutely loved this class! It was by no means an easy class, but it taught me a great deal about politics and data analysis. It often feels like a lot of work, but every assignment has a purpose and I wouldn't change much. I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Hawkins!

Professor Hawkins does not understand statistics well enough and is super vague in his assignment descriptions. Assignments are nothing more than busy work and lectures feel redundant and pointless. Most things that he talks about in class are simple logic. If it wasn't for quizzes, you wouldn't need to go to class. This class was a waste of time.

He's a nice guy and knows a lot about the subject, but he is a terrible teacher. You either have to teach yourself all the material or live in the TA lab. He doesn't do a good job explaining/teaching concepts and has a time-consuming paper due each Saturday. He can be a bit abrasive as well. I would avoid taking the class from him if possible.

Every professor  who is thrown into the crucible of POLI 200 will receive bad reviews from all of the whiny first and second year Poli Sci students. Ignore them and take a class from this guy that ISN'T POLI 200. He's blunt to a fault, can come off as a little abrasive, but he DEEPLY cares about you. Papers are graded harsh, but fair.

I could have tried harder in this class. To be honest, he gives great guidelines on how to succeed and his lectures are pretty engaging. It's not the most rigorous IR or PoliSci class I've taken so the papers are not long and neither are the readings. He has a good understanding and passion for Latin America that is missing with similar professors.

This sucked. his TAs are good, but that's about it. he was repetitive and his lectures didn't really teach me anything I needed to know. I didn't understand anything he taught about statistics, which was like half of the class. Take it from someone else; any other professor would be better than him.

Despite him acting like the nice guy in class, all of my 1on1 interactions left me disappointed and feeling like he had no desire to help me whatsoever. I got the worst grade of my life in this class mostly because I learned nothing from his ambiguous lectures. If you want an A, just be prepared to sacrifice all happiness for it. I chose not to.

Arbitrary grading, and very boring lectures. He's a nice guy at heart, but that doesn't make him a good professor. There's also a lot floating around the department about him disrespecting his TAs and RAs, which I totally get after having interacted with him 1on1 just once. Okay professor but definitely not worth taking 200 from him.

Toughest major class. Feel like I suck at this, so I spend more than 8-9 hrs/wk. Big paper weekly: TAs essential, start early. Daily quizzes okay, weekly assignments awful. Not fun. Apologies if you're stuck with it. Hawkins is a below-mid professor IMO, but you find that he's at heart a nice guy as the semester progresses.

Hawkins is such a nice guy, and taught the class well given how difficult of a curriculum it is. Grading on the papers was pretty arbitrary, however, and a lot of students were frustrated at the lack of standardization. The papers are gnarly and hard to do well on. Really light on homework, which was nice. Lectures were pretty boring.

I love Dr. Hawkins - definitely one of my favorite professors. This is the best class I've taken. There's a decent amount of homework - readings & a few papers, but tests are open-note and he's always accessible outside of class. The lectures are always interesting and uplifting, and I looked forward to this class every day. 1000/10 would recommend

Prof. Hawkins lectures are dry, repetitive, and often inaccurate. I didn't learn a single thing from his lectures. His TAs, however, are fantastic, and working with them will ensure you pass. Yeah he's a nice person in the classroom, but that doesn't make him a good teacher. You'll learn way more taking this from another person.

Definitely the hardest class I've taken at BYU so far but so worth it; I've gotten much better at research and writing. The stats portion is hard. Weekly essays, one final. Professor Hawkins is amazing, he has great lectures and is also so accommodating and understanding of students' needs. Go to TA office hours often if you want a good grade!!!

He is a kind person and you can't hold anything against him. His lectures can be confusing. The grading criteria is clear and extremely vague at the same time, which makes assignments hard. The final exam is not hard. Work with his TAs, he chose them well! Attendance at lab is required, and you get points for it.

This was a difficult class. Lots of writing and half is statistics! There is a paper due almost every Saturday, though they are short. He uses podcasts a lot and he does brain breaks in class. 

Professor Hawkins is one of the kindest people I've ever met. He is understanding of students' needs, and so funny. He really cares and it shows.

It seems that 380 was polarizing, according to the other comments, but I loved the class and I loved Professor Hawkins. I'm not Latino, but always felt valued and heard in the class. Professor Hawkins obviously cares about his students and the course matter, and teaches it passionately.

His biggest draw back is that he gives almost no feedback on papers or assignments. He grades very hard. I'm latino and did not appreciate how the class was just about "whose problems can we blame on the US". Latin America needs to learn to fix their own problems, this class is not really that, more just a pity party in my opinion. Good guy though.

It is clear that he cares about his students, but grades very hard and rarely provides feedback which makes it hard. Class topic is interesting, but he seems to very heavily reaffirm the negative sentiments that his students express towards the US which is sometimes unwarranted and off topic. I don't think his class has the inclusivity he promotes.

Great class, great professor. Really insightful lectures that engaged the class well. I really appreciated the learning experiences that were given. Papers can be a bit tough, but Prof. Hawkins is clear about what is expected and is willing to communicate with the class about deadlines and requirements. Exams aren't hard, and are well communicated.

This class was by far the best class I have taken at BYU. Professor Hawkins accomplishes all of the aims of a BYU education and promotes a warm and welcoming class enviorment. Although he is a tough grader, this was vital to my learning beacuse it led me think deeply about concepts taught in class. His class was the highlight of my BYU experience!!

Prof. Hawkins is very nice, but I would NOT recommend taking this class. You read a book that is incredibly biased and blames all of LA's faults on the US without proper justification. The only people that can speak in his class are latinos, everyone else is useless. Very anti-American. If you are a LT AM major, then I'm sure you'll LOVE this.

LOTS OF PAPERS!!! Be ready to spend so much time writing. Isn't the best at explaining what he wants in the papers so talk to TAs. Gonna be honest I didn't try the hardest and still passed. Only take if you have to.

Yes, POLI200 is extremely difficult, but that's the nature of a weed-out class. Prof Hawkins is a genius and extremely understanding. He wants you to succeed and learn from this class. His TA's are amazing. Only take this class if you're positive you have to for your major.

This class is a full time job - prepare for ~9 hours a week outside of class. But it's so worth it, and he is amazing. You can tell he loves his students. Go to TA office hours and go to class so you get the most out of it. This class is a trial by fire, but it's necessary and SO worth it. I loved Dr. Hawkins and I hope I have him for another class

Professor Hawkins simply doesn't know how to teach. He's a nice guy and probably a wonderful researcher, but when it came to teaching he's horrible. The only way you can pass this class is working with the TA's which is sad since he's the professor. If you're looking for someone to teach you, this is not the class for you.

Hawkins is great. He cares a ton for students and will do what he can to help you succeed. That being said, there is a lot of work and you will spend about 9 hours a week outside of class for homework. But his grading criteria is clear, and the TAs are super helpful too. You will do fine if you just put in the work he requires.

Prof Hawkins is one of my favorite professors but the class was TOUGH! Treat it like your part time job! The TA's are accessible and Dr. Hawkins really likes to get to know his students. He cares about the mental health of his students and makes that very clear. No study guides/reviews for the final and LOTS of papers. I learned so much though!

Hawkins starts the semester by telling students that they can't do well in his class because he doesn't think we know enough. Feedback was often minimal and unclear about what exactly was wrong. The stats portion of the class was better because grading wasn't subjective. Hawkins rambles a lot and it's hard to get the point of his lectures.

THIS IS AN ENGLISH CLASS! there are a few political lectures, but be prepared to write soo many papers. Average of 1000 words due every Saturday, say goodbye to relaxing on weekends. TA grades all papers, but there are accessible TA labs. This was my least favorite class I took this semester, doesn't help that this is focused towards polisci majors

Yes the class if brutal and the grading is harsh, but the professor is fantastic. I would suggest all who have to take this class to take it with professor Hawkins. I enjoyed the stats portion more than the other material (less biased grading in my opinion), but if you spend your days in the TA lab you will get a good grade on the other assignments

I enjoyed Dr. Hawkins class even though it was difficult. He is willing to work with students and modify deadlines if needed, very understanding in that regard. Class was tough, lots of reading but I mostly enjoyed it.

I LOVED THIS CLASS! I recommend any class by Professor Hawkins but this one, in particular, is best because this is what his research has been focused on so he is very passionate which leads to a fun and engaging class.

He really cares about his students and makes time to help anyone who is struggling. He is a great teacher/lecturer until you get to the stats part. I usually get math really easily, but he just doesn't know how to teach it well at all. He goes too theoretical and doesn't help you actually develop stats skills. Really reasonable grading though.

I had an A in this class until the statistics section RIP. Become BEST FRIENDS with your TA, meet with Hawkins, and go to TA office hours and you will have a solid foundation in this class. It is meant to be hard, but it is not impossible. I put in 9 hours a week or more which is about what this class requires. It is difficult but I enjoyed it.

This was for sure my hardest class of the semester. Hawkins was kind but he was not very accessible and when you asked for help he was very vague. TAs are usually better for this. He does not give any study guide for the final, quizzes, or tests and sometimes lectures are a little difficult to follow. However, you learn a lot of useful skills!
Great class although it is hard. Professor Hawkins really wants people to succeed but he also is rally harsh with his grading so getting an A is hard. I feel like I learned so much though!

I was afraid to take this class because I am not a poli sci major, but I felt perfectly fine and loved it!! There is a lot of reading, and the essays are hard, but it is doable. Dr. Hawkins' lectures are amazing and he is a sweetie. If you are a LT AM minor, take this class!!! I learned so much!!!

He's a great professor, but the course is very difficult. The stats portion (the second half) really hit my grade. Do all your assignments and attend class to get good grades. Rely on your TA to help you! Julia L (Winter 2021) was my most favorite TA I've ever had in my college courses. The professor does a great job of getting amazing TAs.

He's a pretty solid professor and typically nice and understanding if you approach him. As far as the class, he does a fine job of establishing expectations and has the off chance of being forgiving (i.e. extending due dates or dropping assignments).

This class takes a lot of work, but it's really useful and the skills you learn are highly applicable to other polisci classes. The lectures were focused, you typically listen to podcasts instead of do readings, and if you put in consistent effort can get good scores on papers.

POLI200 isn't hard, but it is one of the most obnoxious classes I have ever taken. The lectures are perfectly simple- there is nothing difficult about the concepts being outlined at all. The papers are graded to ridiculous standards, however, and don't match up at all with what is being taught. Darren Hawkins himself is generally irritating.

He has unrealistic expectations, not high expectations. Nobody gets a perfect grade in the class and I had no motivation to try harder because effort did not yield reward. The TAs overcompensate to make sure you don't get a perfect score. His class is all lecture. He is pretentious and makes it clear that his class is hard (though it really isn't).

He really cares about his students. He knows about Latin America but wasn't afraid to say I don't know for certain issues and ask the Latin American students in the class to share their perspectives. Papers were complex but doable if you pay attention in class and ask for some clarification.

I took Christensen for 2 months before withdrawing because my grade was suffering from Ds on the weekly assignments. Then, I took Darren's class. Honestly night and day difference. I got high Bs and As on all the papers. IMO take Hawkins, it's not even close. Do you want to somewhat enjoy 4 months of pain? Or do you want to suffer 4 months of pain?

I LOVE Dr. Hawkins. He totally understands that students are people too, so he doesn't poor buckets of homework/assignments on you. The assignments can be hard, but an A is very doable if you go to his office hours and talk to him. His grading is very reasonable, he's hilarious, and he's such a great lecturer; will take this class again if possible

He is hands down one of my favorite professors of all time if not my complete favorite. I didn't know anything about politics but now I feel like I want to be a politician He is a tough grader on the essays but just do the readings and take the quizes and you'll be fine. LOTS of reading.

I absolutely loved this class. It's definitely tough. Worth it though? Absolutely. You literally feel yourself improving as a write over the course of the semester. The semester I took it Dr. Hawkins got rid of most of the reading and replaced it with podcasts so we could learn from actual experiments. THIS. WAS. PHENOMENAL. Would take again.

Prof. Hawkins is an awesome guy who cares a lot and has a lot of cool experience in the field. It is a rigorous class, but you learn so many good and necessary skills. Since Poli 200 is required for a lot of students, it's always a big lecture hall, so TAs will be your best friend. They do all the major grading so get their feedback on everything.

Great professor. You do podcasts instead of readings usually, which is way nice. Really funny and understanding. Wasn't as great at teaching the stats part of class (3 weeks), but was super otherwise. Get to know your TA like they're your new best friend (cuz they are). You will absolutely become a better writer and researcher with Hawkins.

I loved taking from Professor Hawkins! He REALLY cares about his students and will change assignment dates if he can tell everyone is too stressed about it. He also started doing podcasts instead of readings and it was amazing! I would definitely recommend taking Poli Sci 200 from him. You won't regret it.

The class was interesting and definitely made me a better researcher but the stats section of it almost killed me. I struggle in math and I didnt understand anything hat we were doing. The assignments that werent stats were hard but definitely a lot more manageable. Made me reconsider my major. If you are confident in stats youll be fine
Great teacher! So fun, quirky, and relatable. Love him and would love to take his class again. Yeehaw

Dr. Hawkins was my favorite professor this semester. His lectures are in-depth and interesting, and he has some wild stories. He cares a lot about his students, and was willing to flex on a few deadlines with us when we were overworked. He assigns a textbook chapter or two per class, but his lectures did a good job of summing everything up.

Professor Hawkins is easily the most approachable political science professor at BYU. Besides intelligent, he is understanding, relatable, and willing to help. I think that all students can appreciate his humble attitude and great sense of humor. If you are nervous to take any of his classes, don't be! 200 is a lot of work, so plan on that.

This class made me change my major. The daily quizzes were hard on long readings and he tended to talk about assignments as if they were easy to understand. TAs were not much help either. I would get help from them and would still not get good grades on assignments I spent hours on.

Hawkins was a really enjoyable teacher. He can be a little quirky at times, but he's really caring and hilarious. Short reading quizzes happen at the beginning of each class period and you have a paper due every week. Most of the grading is done by the TAs, and they do a good job. Hawkins is a good choice for POLI200.

POLI 200 is required for several majors, so you'll just have to get over how tough it is. Your grade is based mostly on toughly-graded weekly assignments, as well as easy daily reading quizzes and a final. The assignments are tough, so you need to be in with your TA constantly. It doesn't matter much who your professor is, just rely on your TA.

Professor Hawkins was a great Political Science teacher. There is an essay due every single week for the class, and he trains his TAs to grade hard. He expects a lot from whoever takes his class. That being said, it was such an accomplishment. This class made me stretch myself, and it is all very doable. His class effectively helps students learn.

Prof Hawkins is not someone I would recommend taking POLI200 from. It's difficult to understand his assignments and he acts as if they are easily explained but there is often a lot left for you to figure out on your own. The TA's during my semester always seemed to have different answers from each other and the grading was really subjective.

Prof Hawkins is a great guy that really cares about his students and does his best to help his students. His lectures are really dry, but you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. The class is hard, go to the TA lab before every paper is due.

Professor Hawkins cares about his students. He's a real dude with real problems. He totally gets that other people have problems too! He's understanding, really funny, and really helpful.  The TAs for the this class were also great.

Don't get me wrong, I love Professor Hawkins as a person. He is spiritual, genuine, and loves teaching. Poli 200 just isn't his thing. He talks about some of his research at the end of the semester, and it's clear that he would be an amazing Latin American studies professor. I highly recommend Professor Hawkins, just for anything but Poli 200

Professor Hawkins is a fabulous, Nerdy, loving, genius human being. I loved his class. It was hard and as someone who had not taken an international relations class before I had some catching up to do. He is a fanatic about his subject. He is a tough grader and the tests are hard but well worth the rigor. I learned a ton.

I really like this guy. He is smart and a good teacher. The stats portion was a little hard because thats not his area of expertise, but everything else was easy to understand. He is a fair grader and he gives the tie to the runner. My grade was on the edge and he bumped me because he is not a heartless robot. Put in the work and you will do fine.

Hawkins is a good, fair professor. His lectures are incredibly interesting and the assignments are valid and thought-provoking. Don't be scared by the 4 credit label: you have an assignment due once a week with readings due twice a week, but it's nothing unbearable. I've had tougher 3 credit classes for sure.

At first I liked the class, then hated it, then appreciated what it taught. Good professor, willing to help and give you his time. Weekly assignments can take a lot of time, but if you are friends with your TA you will succeed. Do the reading - it helps with the quizzes.
Hawkins was super fun and a good teacher. His assignments were more or less unnerving but there was a lot of help offered. Lectures were fun, but the labs were key.

Clearly concerned about making the course as helpful as possible to students. Listens to everyone's opinions and helps guide effective discussions during lecture. Homework is fairly rigorous (expected for a 4-credit class) but applicable. Laid back, reasonable, and very smart. I loved this class and learned a ton from it!

2 weekly quizzes of  3-4 questions based on readings, he has a reading guide so it's not hard The Mid-term had a good study guide and the actual midterm was 5 essay questions. There is a paper due at the end of the semester 14 pages but you can do it in pairs (7 pages each) The Final is similar to the midterm overall straightforward small EC option
I have learned a ton during his class. He is a great professor! If you take his class, be ready to work very hard - but in the end you will realize it was all worth it.

Hawkins sure knows his stuff. He is a really good teacher and is willing to listen to any intelligent opinion anyone has to offer, which makes it validating to participate, unlike with some profs. He is not an easy grader and is not always clear on exactly what he wants from the papers, so I recommend submitting a rough. Good class though.
He explains complicated ideas with clarity and thoughtfulness.  He respects student comments, but he'll probe the value of the position and think critically.  His classes are demanding, but fair.
Very helpful and the workload is perfect.  He explains things very well and class materials are interesting.

Great professor. Laid back, funny, and willing to pick and listen to both sides of an argument. Strong Human Rights focus. Reasonable work and reading loads. Fairly easy tests and papers. Highly recommended.
What a fun class!  Hawkins really helped us to learn a lot and made class entertaining. The load is reasonable, tests fairly predictable, and it's definitely survivable.  I'd recommend him to anyone.
While this is a tough class, it is bearable and often interesting. Darren's lectures are usually pretty good. Lots of reading and papers. Tests are essay, and difficult. Good teacher overall though.

I would not recommend taking POLI 200 from Dr. Hawkins. He grades arbitrarily harshly and isn't very open to students advocating for higher grades. His assignments are brutal, and the descriptions are incredibly confusing. I would take this class from someone else if you can.

Professor Hawkins is one of the best professors at BYU. He is so knowledgeable about what he is teaching and he is a very caring professor. Take advantage of his office hours and actually engage with the material. There are 5 essays in this class but they are interesting and manageable. Only 2 tests but make sure you study! 10/10 professor!
He put his own spin on this class and made it something special. He's very aware of the class and wants to help everyone succeed. Was honestly a great respite from the craziness of life.

Professor Hawkins is such a caring man. He will work with you because he understands. He made UNIV such a lovely experience because he really worked to make it meaningful. He's so funny and such a joy to be around. Take UNIV from him if you actually want to get something out of it.

I am a big fan of Dr. Hawkins. He makes an effort to keep things relevant and engaging. He's always happy to provide assistance. The workload was meaningful but not overwhelming. There were basically just a few short papers, two open note tests, and short reading responses. Would 100% recommend. You could tell he really cares.

Dr. Hawkins is a really good man. I didn't always agree with the way he set up the class, but he is really open to comments/questions throughout lectures which I enjoyed. He definitely has personal biases but we all do. I grew to really like him and he knows a lot about IR

This class was such a nightmare. The huge papers due every single Saturday ate up my weekends and had little cohesion with boring lectures and readings. Rubrics confused me so badly and feedback on papers was too late or too specific to help with future work. Class structure was horribly inconsistent and deadlines kept changing. Avoid if possible.

Professor Hawkins is a good person, but his lectures do not draw out the concepts that are required for papers. He teaches concepts required for your paper two days before it is due. There are weekly papers that take up MANY hours, definitely go to TA hours!! If you take this class, be prepared to take lighter classes during this semester.

I honestly thought this class was great! I learned a lot! Even though it does consist of quite a bit of writing, it truly is helpful and gets your thinking. I found this class helped me in other classes also. Professor Hawkins is great! I can tell that he truly prepares for his lectures and cares about what he is teaching and his students!

This class is a requirement for many majors. Professor Hawkins explains concepts really well. Both he and the T.A. have high standards for grading. On the first day, he sets the tone by warning that it's challenging to get an A, but not impossible. You need to put in significant effort, but the payoff is substantial – you'll learn a lot.

This class was hard and took up a lot of time (I recommend a lighter course load), but I honestly loved it. It stretched me and helped me grow so much in my writing skills, stats knowledge, and political science knowledge. Professor Hawkins is an awesome professor and cares about his students. He's super passionate about the content, which helps!

Professor Hawkins cares, he does, but a lot of students don't seem to like him. I thought that he taught really well and from a nuanced perspective. He is very knowledgeable on the subject at had and is very accessible. The only portion of the class that got confusing was the stats portion. It's a hard class, but Professor Hawkins makes it easier.

Dr. Hawkins loves what he teaches and cares deeply about the skills he wants you to develop. While a lot of grading is done by TA's you can do pretty good in the class if you put in the effort. This class is meant to teach you how to write professionally and that is no easy task, don't give up and don't get discouraged.

Professor Hawkins is totally awesome and such a great guy/professor. The class is challenging but if you meet with your TA it really helps!! You have every opportunity to receive a good grade and Professor Hawkins helps so much and is just so great. I really recommend him and have learned so much from this class!

Dr. Hawkins is a kind, genuine person. He wants to make the world a better place, and he shows great passion for what he teaches. This is not an easy class, but don't let that scare you away! The only way you will learn how to write in political science is to go through the refiner's fire of Poli 200. He is generally good at lecturing.

I absolutely loved this class! It was by no means an easy class, but it taught me a great deal about politics and data analysis. It often feels like a lot of work, but every assignment has a purpose and I wouldn't change much. I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Hawkins!

Professor Hawkins does not understand statistics well enough and is super vague in his assignment descriptions. Assignments are nothing more than busy work and lectures feel redundant and pointless. Most things that he talks about in class are simple logic. If it wasn't for quizzes, you wouldn't need to go to class. This class was a waste of time.

He's a nice guy and knows a lot about the subject, but he is a terrible teacher. You either have to teach yourself all the material or live in the TA lab. He doesn't do a good job explaining/teaching concepts and has a time-consuming paper due each Saturday. He can be a bit abrasive as well. I would avoid taking the class from him if possible.

Every professor  who is thrown into the crucible of POLI 200 will receive bad reviews from all of the whiny first and second year Poli Sci students. Ignore them and take a class from this guy that ISN'T POLI 200. He's blunt to a fault, can come off as a little abrasive, but he DEEPLY cares about you. Papers are graded harsh, but fair.

I could have tried harder in this class. To be honest, he gives great guidelines on how to succeed and his lectures are pretty engaging. It's not the most rigorous IR or PoliSci class I've taken so the papers are not long and neither are the readings. He has a good understanding and passion for Latin America that is missing with similar professors.

This sucked. his TAs are good, but that's about it. he was repetitive and his lectures didn't really teach me anything I needed to know. I didn't understand anything he taught about statistics, which was like half of the class. Take it from someone else; any other professor would be better than him.

Despite him acting like the nice guy in class, all of my 1on1 interactions left me disappointed and feeling like he had no desire to help me whatsoever. I got the worst grade of my life in this class mostly because I learned nothing from his ambiguous lectures. If you want an A, just be prepared to sacrifice all happiness for it. I chose not to.

Arbitrary grading, and very boring lectures. He's a nice guy at heart, but that doesn't make him a good professor. There's also a lot floating around the department about him disrespecting his TAs and RAs, which I totally get after having interacted with him 1on1 just once. Okay professor but definitely not worth taking 200 from him.

Toughest major class. Feel like I suck at this, so I spend more than 8-9 hrs/wk. Big paper weekly: TAs essential, start early. Daily quizzes okay, weekly assignments awful. Not fun. Apologies if you're stuck with it. Hawkins is a below-mid professor IMO, but you find that he's at heart a nice guy as the semester progresses.

Hawkins is such a nice guy, and taught the class well given how difficult of a curriculum it is. Grading on the papers was pretty arbitrary, however, and a lot of students were frustrated at the lack of standardization. The papers are gnarly and hard to do well on. Really light on homework, which was nice. Lectures were pretty boring.

I love Dr. Hawkins - definitely one of my favorite professors. This is the best class I've taken. There's a decent amount of homework - readings & a few papers, but tests are open-note and he's always accessible outside of class. The lectures are always interesting and uplifting, and I looked forward to this class every day. 1000/10 would recommend

Prof. Hawkins lectures are dry, repetitive, and often inaccurate. I didn't learn a single thing from his lectures. His TAs, however, are fantastic, and working with them will ensure you pass. Yeah he's a nice person in the classroom, but that doesn't make him a good teacher. You'll learn way more taking this from another person.

Definitely the hardest class I've taken at BYU so far but so worth it; I've gotten much better at research and writing. The stats portion is hard. Weekly essays, one final. Professor Hawkins is amazing, he has great lectures and is also so accommodating and understanding of students' needs. Go to TA office hours often if you want a good grade!!!

He is a kind person and you can't hold anything against him. His lectures can be confusing. The grading criteria is clear and extremely vague at the same time, which makes assignments hard.
