This was a difficult class. Lots of writing and half is statistics! There is a paper due almost every Saturday, though they are short. He uses podcasts a lot and he does brain breaks in class. 

Professor Hawkins is one of the kindest people I've ever met. He is understanding of students' needs, and so funny. He really cares and it shows.

Great class, great professor. Really insightful lectures that engaged the class well. I really appreciated the learning experiences that were given. This class was by far the best class I have taken at BYU. Professor Hawkins accomplishes all of the aims of a BYU education and promotes a warm and welcoming class enviorment. LOTS OF PAPERS!!! Be ready to spend so much time writing. Isn't the best at explaining what he wants in the papers so talk to TAs. Gonna be honest I didn't try the hardest and still passed. Only take if you have to.

Yes, POLI200 is extremely difficult, but that's the nature of a weed-out class. Prof Hawkins is a genius and extremely understanding. He wants you to succeed and learn from this class. His TA's are amazing. Only take this class if you're positive you have to for your major.

This class is a full time job - prepare for ~9 hours a week outside of class. But it's so worth it, and he is amazing. You can tell he loves his students. Professor Hawkins simply doesn't know how to teach. He's a nice guy and probably a wonderful researcher, but when it came to teaching he's horrible. Hawkins is great. He cares a ton for students and will do what he can to help you succeed. TA grades all papers, but there are accessible TA labs. This was my least favorite class I took this semester, doesn't help that this is focused towards polisci majors

Yes the class if brutal and the grading is harsh, but the professor is fantastic. I would suggest all who have to take this class to take it with professor Hawkins. I enjoyed the stats portion more than the other material (less biased grading in my opinion), but if you spend your days in the TA lab you will get a good grade on the other assignments

I enjoyed Dr. Hawkins class even though it was difficult. He is willing to work with students and modify deadlines if needed, very understanding in that regard. Class was tough, lots of reading but I mostly enjoyed it.

I LOVED THIS CLASS! I recommend any class by Professor Hawkins but this one, in particular, is best because this is what his research has been focused on so he is very passionate which leads to a fun and engaging class.

He really cares about his students and makes time to help anyone who is struggling. He is a great teacher/lecturer until you get to the stats part. I usually get math really easily, but he just doesn't know how to teach it well at all. He goes too theoretical and doesn't help you actually develop stats skills. Really reasonable grading though.

I had an A in this class until the statistics section RIP. Become BEST FRIENDS with your TA, meet with Hawkins, and go to TA office hours and you will have a solid foundation in this class. It is meant to be hard, but it is not impossible. I put in 9 hours a week or more which is about what this class requires. It is difficult but I enjoyed it.

This was for sure my hardest class of the semester. Hawkins was kind but he was not very accessible and when you asked for help he was very vague. TAs are usually better for this. He does not give any study guide for the final, quizzes, or tests and sometimes lectures are a little difficult to follow. However, you learn a lot of useful skills!
Great class although it is hard. Professor Hawkins really wants people to succeed but he also is rally harsh with his grading so getting an A is hard. I feel like I learned so much though!

I was afraid to take this class because I am not a poli sci major, but I felt perfectly fine and loved it!! There is a lot of reading, and the essays are hard, but it is doable. Dr. Hawkins' lectures are amazing and he is a sweetie. If you are a LT AM minor, take this class!!! I learned so much!!!

He's a great professor, but the course is very difficult. The stats portion (the second half) really hit my grade. Do all your assignments and attend class to get good grades. Rely on your TA to help you! Julia L (Winter 2021) was my most favorite TA I've ever had in my college courses. The professor does a great job of getting amazing TAs.

He's a pretty solid professor and typically nice and understanding if you approach him. As far as the class, he does a fine job of establishing expectations and has the off chance of being forgiving (i.e. extending due dates or dropping assignments).

This class takes a lot of work, but it's really useful and the skills you learn are highly applicable to other polisci classes. The lectures were focused, you typically listen to podcasts instead of do readings, and if you put in consistent effort can get good scores on papers.

POLI200 isn't hard, but it is one of the most obnoxious classes I have ever taken. The lectures are perfectly simple- there is nothing difficult about the concepts being outlined at all. The papers are graded to ridiculous standards, however, and don't match up at all with what is being taught. Darren Hawkins himself is generally irritating.

He has unrealistic expectations, not high expectations. Nobody gets a perfect grade in the class and I had no motivation to try harder because effort did not yield reward. The TAs overcompensate to make sure you don't get a perfect score. His class is all lecture. He is pretentious and makes it clear that his class is hard (though it really isn't).

He really cares about his students. He knows about Latin America but wasn't afraid to say I don't know for certain issues and ask the Latin American students in the class to share their perspectives. Papers were complex but doable if you pay attention in class and ask for some clarification.

I took Christensen for 2 months before withdrawing because my grade was suffering from Ds on the weekly assignments. Then, I took Darren's class. Honestly night and day difference. I got high Bs and As on all the papers. IMO take Hawkins, it's not even close. Do you want to somewhat enjoy 4 months of pain? Or do you want to suffer 4 months of pain?

I LOVE Dr. Hawkins. He totally understands that students are people too, so he doesn't poor buckets of homework/assignments on you. The assignments can be hard, but an A is very doable if you go to his office hours and talk to him. His grading is very reasonable, he's hilarious, and he's such a great lecturer; will take this class again if possible

He is hands down one of my favorite professors of all time if not my complete favorite. I didn't know anything about politics but now I feel like I want to be a politician He is a tough grader on the essays but just do the readings and take the quizes and you'll be fine. LOTS of reading.

I absolutely loved this class. It's definitely tough. Worth it though? Absolutely. You literally feel yourself improving as a write over the course of the semester. The semester I took it Dr. Hawkins got rid of most of the reading and replaced it with podcasts so we could learn from actual experiments. THIS. WAS. PHENOMENAL. Would take again.

Prof. Hawkins is an awesome guy who cares a lot and has a lot of cool experience in the field. It is a rigorous class, but you learn so many good and necessary skills. Since Poli 200 is required for a lot of students, it's always a big lecture hall, so TAs will be your best friend. They do all the major grading so get their feedback on everything.

Great professor. You do podcasts instead of readings usually, which is way nice. Really funny and understanding. Wasn't as great at teaching the stats part of class (3 weeks), but was super otherwise. Get to know your TA like they're your new best friend (cuz they are). You will absolutely become a better writer and researcher with Hawkins.

I loved taking from Professor Hawkins! He REALLY cares about his students and will change assignment dates if he can tell everyone is too stressed about it. He also started doing podcasts instead of readings and it was amazing! I would definitely recommend taking Poli Sci 200 from him. You won't regret it.

The class was interesting and definitely made me a better researcher but the stats section of it almost killed me. I struggle in math and I didnt understand anything hat we were doing. The assignments that werent stats were hard but definitely a lot more manageable. Made me reconsider my major. If you are confident in stats youll be fine
Great teacher! So fun, quirky, and relatable. Love him and would love to take his class again. Yeehaw

Dr. Hawkins was my favorite professor this semester. His lectures are in-depth and interesting, and he has some wild stories. He cares a lot about his students, and was willing to flex on a few deadlines with us when we were overworked. He assigns a textbook chapter or two per class, but his lectures did a good job of summing everything up.

Professor Hawkins is easily the most approachable political science professor at BYU. Besides intelligent, he is understanding, relatable, and willing to help. I think that all students can appreciate his humble attitude and great sense of humor. If you are nervous to take any of his classes, don't be! 200 is a lot of work, so plan on that.

This class made me change my major. The daily quizzes were hard on long readings and he tended to talk about assignments as if they were easy to understand. TAs were not much help either. I would get help from them and would still not get good grades on assignments I spent hours on.

Hawkins was a really enjoyable teacher. He can be a little quirky at times, but he's really caring and hilarious. Short reading quizzes happen at the beginning of each class period and you have a paper due every week. Most of the grading is done by the TAs, and they do a good job. Hawkins is a good choice for POLI200.

POLI 200 is required for several majors, so you'll just have to get over how tough it is. Your grade is based mostly on toughly-graded weekly assignments, as well as easy daily reading quizzes and a final. The assignments are tough, so you need to be in with your TA constantly. It doesn't matter much who your professor is, just rely on your TA.

Professor Hawkins was a great Political Science teacher. There is an essay due every single week for the class, and he trains his TAs to grade hard. He expects a lot from whoever takes his class. That being said, it was such an accomplishment. This class made me stretch myself, and it is all very doable. His class effectively helps students learn.

Prof Hawkins is not someone I would recommend taking POLI200 from. It's difficult to understand his assignments and he acts as if they are easily explained but there is often a lot left for you to figure out on your own. The TA's during my semester always seemed to have different answers from each other and the grading was really subjective.

Prof Hawkins is a great guy that really cares about his students and does his best to help his students. His lectures are really dry, but you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. The class is hard, go to the TA lab before every paper is due.

Professor Hawkins cares about his students. He's a real dude with real problems. He totally gets that other people have problems too! He's understanding, really funny, and really helpful.  The TAs for the this class were also great.

Don't get me wrong, I love Professor Hawkins as a person. He is spiritual, genuine, and loves teaching. Poli 200 just isn't his thing. He talks about some of his research at the end of the semester, and it's clear that he would be an amazing Latin American studies professor. I highly recommend Professor Hawkins, just for anything but Poli 200

Professor Hawkins is a fabulous, Nerdy, loving, genius human being. I loved his class. It was hard and as someone who had not taken an international relations class before I had some catching up to do. He is a fanatic about his subject. He is a tough grader and the tests are hard but well worth the rigor. I learned a ton.

I really like this guy. He is smart and a good teacher. The stats portion was a little hard because thats not his area of expertise, but everything else was easy to understand. He is a fair grader and he gives the tie to the runner. My grade was on the edge and he bumped me because he is not a heartless robot. Put in the work and you will do fine.

Hawkins is a good, fair professor. His lectures are incredibly interesting and the assignments are valid and thought-provoking. Don't be scared by the 4 credit label: you have an assignment due once a week with readings due twice a week, but it's nothing unbearable. I've had tougher 3 credit classes for sure.

At first I liked the class, then hated it, then appreciated what it taught. Good professor, willing to help and give you his time. Weekly assignments can take a lot of time, but if you are friends with your TA you will succeed. Do the reading - it helps with the quizzes.
Hawkins was super fun and a good teacher. His assignments were more or less unnerving but there was a lot of help offered. Lectures were fun, but the labs were key.

Clearly concerned about making the course as helpful as possible to students. Listens to everyone's opinions and helps guide effective discussions during lecture. Homework is fairly rigorous (expected for a 4-credit class) but applicable. Laid back, reasonable, and very smart. I loved this class and learned a ton from it!

2 weekly quizzes of  3-4 questions based on readings, he has a reading guide so it's not hard The Mid-term had a good study guide and the actual midterm was 5 essay questions. There is a paper due at the end of the semester 14 pages but you can do it in pairs (7 pages each) The Final is similar to the midterm overall straightforward small EC option
I have learned a ton during his class. He is a great professor! If you take his class, be ready to work very hard - but in the end you will realize it was all worth it.

Hawkins sure knows his stuff. He is a really good teacher and is willing to listen to any intelligent opinion anyone has to offer, which makes it validating to participate, unlike with some profs. He is not an easy grader and is not always clear on exactly what he wants from the papers, so I recommend submitting a rough. Good class though.
He explains complicated ideas with clarity and thoughtfulness.  He respects student comments, but he'll probe the value of the position and think critically.  His classes are demanding, but fair.
Very helpful and the workload is perfect.  He explains things very well and class materials are interesting.

Great professor. Laid back, funny, and willing to pick and listen to both sides of an argument. Strong Human Rights focus. Reasonable work and reading loads. Fairly easy tests and papers. Highly recommended.
What a fun class!  Hawkins really helped us to learn a lot and made class entertaining. The load is reasonable, tests fairly predictable, and it's definitely survivable.  I'd recommend him to anyone.
While this is a tough class, it is bearable and often interesting. Darren's lectures are usually pretty good. Lots of reading and papers. Tests are essay, and difficult. Good teacher overall though.
You can tell he is an extremely gifted mathematician, for this reason sometimes his lectures are hard to understand. Use organic chemistry tutor to get a better understanding.

Dr. Doud is the Math 290 GOAT. He literally wrote the textbook. I appreciated that he would take time to answer/work through HW questions at the beginning of class. This is a great and challenging course, but he is definitely the best professor for it.

I can see why so many people really like Dr Doud, but I did not feel supported at all by him when I was really struggling and was even told by him directly that I shouldn't consider any majors with math in them :( which I just feel like you shouldn't say to a student who is actively trying to get help, but yeah, it was a tough semester.

He is such a smart and patient professor. I swear people would ask the same question 100 times and he gives each student time and attention to get the help they need. The course itself is a little challenging and there is a lot of homework, but Dr. Doud is definitely the guy to take this class from.
Take calculus from Dr. Doud. I haven't taken a Math class in 6 years, and was honestly so overwhelmed at jumping into calculus. He was very caring and willing to help. Great guy!

He's a fine professor. He didn't really stand out to me either way - good or bad. There wasn't anything exceptional about him, but he taught the material effectively and answered questions well. I learned what I needed to learn.
Honestly didn't learn a ton in class, I mostly taught myself from the slides after. But pretty good teacher! Shoutout Calvin our TA he rocks big time

I switched to be a math major because of this class and professor. The textbook is so well written (he wrote it) and the homework problems are perfectly chosen. I always felt like I was right at the sweet spot of learning and difficulty in this class. There is no point in taking 290 from someone else if you can avoid it.

The class material is super tough and made me want to give up and become a housewife, but Darrin's a king who actually cares about you. I once forgot to turn in an assignment and he accepted it and manually put it in so that I could receive full credit. If you're going to suffer through this class, he's a good professor to take it from.

Dr. Doud is a great guy. I had never taken Calc before, so I didn't have the easiest time in the class. However, Dr. Doud was always accessible during office hours (and even outside his usual office hours) to help me out. His lectures are a little hard to follow because it's difficult to cater to the 150+ people in his lecture halls.

Dr. Doud is an AMAZING calc 1 teacher, he made all the material very accessible and easy to understand even if you haven't taken it before. The homework prepares you very well for the tests and the lectures prepare you very well for the homework. Take from Doud!

Dr. Doud is the greatest math professor I've ever had. He was really funny, and there is also also no better person you could take Math 290 from. I loved taking this class, and the material is super interesting too, especially the way he teaches it.

A really good math teacher. He explained the concepts really well. He goes through homework examples in class if you ask. There's a homework for each lecture and lab. It's really helpful if you do each homework the day of the relevant lecture.
If you are taking 290 not from Dr. Doud, then I am truly sorry. You are missing out.
290 is a super tough class but Dr. Doud is the best. He is so caring for his students and is a great lecturer. Lectures can be tough to follow if you aren't paying 100% attention though.
I love this man

Dr. Doud is such a good professor. I took Math 112 because I didn't score high enough on the AP test in high school to test out, and Dr. Doud was nothing short of amazing. Kind, caring and loves his students a lot! Can't recommend him enough!

MATH290 is hard, but Dr. Doud literally wrote the textbook and is ALWAYS willing to answer questions. Don't spend too much time on hard problems and instead ask for help in office hours/in class. He will lead you to the answer. Exams are tricky but fair. Make sure to memorize important theorems. If you take 290, take it from Dr. Doud!

Doud is a genius on a level typically inaccessible to mortals. He literally wrote the book that you will use for this class, and it shows in his depth of understanding in his teaching. He's funny too, in a mathematician sort of way. His class made me consider switching to a math major.

Could not ask for a better math teacher, considering he cowrote the textbook. Explains things very well in class and has open office hours that anyone can come to. Homework assigned for every lecture but also goes over some of the harder questions in class before due date. 3 midterms and a final, get ready to memorize definitions/theorem proofs.

I'd highly recommend! Dr. Doud wrote the textbook and teaches very well. Homework is about 8-10 proofs every class period, but he goes over the hard ones in class every period and gives you the answers, and he'll work with you in his office hours until you understand. He has super big "old man math nerd" vibes that I hope to obtain someday XD

This professor is the best, especially for Math 290. I highly recommend you take it from him and attend his office hours to receive help on homework and studying. This class is really hard, but he will work with you to understand it. Best lectures ever. He wrote the book for the course and it is the easiest math book to read.

After two semesters at BYU, Dr. Doud is my favorite professor I've ever had. This class is hard because you have to learn to look at Math from a whole new perspective, but it's fun if you wrap your head around it! He encourages attendance to his office hours and will always make himself available. He's also just a great guy. Would reccomend.

This class is not easy, but the professor makes it enjoyable. He has office hours to help with homework, which I usually spent 2 hours on each time. The exams are tough but fair, the average was always between 70-90%. He gives explained examples in lecture to make sure we understand the concept, and you can tell he cares. He is one of the best.

Now this is one professor you do not want to miss. He wrote the book and is super flexible with office hours. The exams are hard but that it the class, proofs are not easy. But he teaches with such simplicity that the class average was really high. He avails himself through office hours and is super friendly. Take him and you won't regret.

Dr Doud is a really good guy. It's clear that he cares about the students, and was super willing to help me when I got sick and had to miss a week of class. That being said, he's not the best teacher. His lectures were fast and confusing and I usually didn't understand the material until later. If you're not a math person, take from someone else.

What Math class at BYU doesn't have a lot of HW or lectures? Linear Algebra is no exception. I got a C because I suck at tests so don't let that steer you away. Professor Doud hasn't taught Math 213 in almost 15 years and he nailed it!! He cares so much to answer questions and give extra help. Very funny and kind. Take it from him if you can!!

Dr. Doud is a great math professor. Some of his lectures could be pretty dense, but you'd usually figure most of it out doing the homework afterward. Where he really shines is in office hours, which he offers multiple times a week for each class he teaches. Every time I went to his office hours he took the time to make sure I understood the concept

Linear Algebra was hard but Dr. Doud made it bearable. He did skim through the class since it was so much material. If you show up to his office hours, you will pass with flying colours. He has a way of tailoring the material to each individual if you come to his office hour!!

Professor Doud is terrific. He knows the hard-to-get concepts for students and is great at providing additional explanations and ways of explaining. The class itself is a bit heavy for 2 credits. There's online and written homework for each lecture, which is helpful but can take a while. Overall, the concepts aren't hard, but just different.

My favorite class I have taken at BYU. Dr. Douds class is set up perfectly: we covered all the material in class, and then completed every homework problem in the lesson in the book. Dr Doud co-wrote the book, so he teaches from it perfectly, making catching up on classes and review super easy. Clear, consistent grading and an excellent teacher

Best math professor, no, best math educator I've ever had. Obviously very intelligent and very experienced with bringing concepts down to our level. Will spend as much time as you ask on examples and clarifications. Regularly stops for questions. Very approachable and affable. Can't recommend him enough.

Solid professor, be prepared for a lot of homework. Tests are fair and based on homework/textbook (which he is one of the authors of, and they give you PDF access for free). I spent most of my time in the on-campus upper division math tutor lab to complete the homework (there's no answer key so I never knew if I was doing it right or not)

Dr. Doud is fantastic. This was a hard and time-consuming class, but he always answered questions and was willing to explain things in different ways. He understands how to teach according to people's questions. Also, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS!! This was a life-saver . You can spend an hour there and almost finish the homework. Best prof I've had.

Dr. Doud wrote the textbook for this class, so he basically teaches straight out of it and all the homework comes from it as well. This isn't really a problem, but if you want the textbook to explain a concept differently than the professor does, not the best choice prob. But overall he's a good prof, so really not a bad choice.

Dr. Doud is a solid choice for Math290. Many days of class, he would lecture practically the whole time and no one said a word, so if that is not how you best learn, it might be difficult for you. He is very fair with grading and really prepares you for the exams. Homeworks are usually harder than the exams. All around, a solid professor for sure.

Dr. Doud is the best teacher I have ever had. This was my hardest class for my first semester freshman year but he made it very bearable. Office hours are so helpful, plan to go to them every other day if you can. He is a very generous and fair grader, I would never blame his teaching for a bad grade in the class! GET HIM IF YOU CAN!!

Dr. Doud is one of the best math professors I've ever had. He's extremely patient, kind, and focused on helping the students. On top of that, he knows his stuff really well, and is great at adjusting the way he explains things based the student's understanding of topics. If you can take from Doud, DO IT.

Professor Doud is a great math teacher. He teaches concepts clearly and spends a ton of extra time helping out students. It is easy to get feedback and learn. If you pay attention in class you will do well. That being said, it almost felt too easy because you didn't really have to think outside the box. It was just learn the basics and apply them.

Prof. Doud is a great professor. He did 3 review sessions at the beginning of the semester so everyone could pass the diagnostic test and did lots of reviews before each test. His lectures are great and you don't need to read the book if you pay attention to his lectures. Go to lecture, do the homework and test reviews and you will get an A

I loved taking Calc from Dr. Doud. He was a great professor that really knows his stuff! Id never been exposed to Calc before but I feel really prepared and I learned a lot. This semester I experienced a lot of health issues and Dr. Doud was very understanding and accommodating. He also worked really hard to make online class doable and clear!

Dr. Doud explains things very simply, but I also had some experience in calculus, which really helps. There is homework due six days a week but it never takes too long to do. This is a very doable 4-credit class. I felt like I was prepared for the tests. Go to the Math lab and TA sessions with questions if you need help on homework!!!

Kind of a dull professor but I grew to love him. He's very experienced and knows how to explain. Sometimes he goes quickly, but the class has TA sessions every other day, and a math lab always available. Not a bad choice overall, but expect to be doing homework every single day of the week.

His pre-calc lectures at the beginning were crazy difficult to understand, but as soon as he starts on actual calculus, he does a good job explaining the different principles. His homework is difficult but never overwhelming, and he makes the homework worth a significant amount of points so the tests don't impact your grade as much.

If you have the chance to take 473 from Doud, I would recommend it. Can take it right after 371. Maybe my toughest class yet. I'm NOT one of the super smart math majors - you know those kind ;), & I made it through the class, so you can too. Doud is a good guy, good teacher, accessible, and a very nice & fair grader. Homework is majority of grade.
Dr. Doud is absolutely incredible. I had a hard time with the concepts in this class, but his lectures, the textbook he wrote (AND GIVES OUT FOR FREE), and his office hours made it my favorite class.

If you have the opportunity to take 290 from Dr. Doud, I'd recommend him without reservation. The homework is very time-consuming but the tests are fairly easy and he's one of the most generous graders I've ever had. Super nice guy, immensely knowledgeable, and has a great pedagogical approach!

Dr Doud is my favorite math teacher at BYU thus far. 371 was a difficult class, but he explained things well and answered questions thoroughly and respectfully. Patient, friendly, brilliant, accessible outside class. Take a class from him if you have the chance. He is wonderful!

The best part of this class is that he wrote the textbook, and it's really well done. He's great at explaining the material clearly in class, and if you miss class, the textbook has exactly what he explained how he explained it. Class can be pretty boring, but he's a solid choice. Also very available for homework help.
Dr. Doud is awesome. He does a great job of teaching the material, and I never felt like the tests were too difficult. Plus he's just a genuinely nice guy. Super recommend his class!
290 was not easy but Prof Doud did a good job of helping when the class was confused and was easy to see outside of class.

Doud was energetic and cheerful about Math 290 which made it pleasant for me (I don't usually enjoy math lectures). In addition, he was exceptional at teaching the math classes. However, the class was very hard. I had to read the textbook for about the same amount of time as I spent in class. Tests are really hard.

Dr. Doud can teach proofs. He does well at both explaining proof methods and giving lots of examples in class. He readily gives help if you go to his office. Stay on top of hw and make sure you understand. Might want to bring a snack if you struggle staying awake. Book was a free pdf, but he's writing his own (I think it will be free). Reasonable.

Professor Doud does an amazing job at explaining concepts and answering questions. I took this class after 3 years of not taking math classes, and was able to catch back up because of how well Doud taught.

Came in to this class freshman year. Didn't know complex math, or even Rings or Fields, so the first few weeks were really tough. I consistently found myself in his office, which is fine any time (not just during office hours). Tough, but I learned a whole lot. I had some of the most fun I've ever had in his class. Cooperate with classmates on HW.

I had already taken calc 1 in high school, but Professor Doud still explained many concepts more clearly and differently. He makes sure to derive most of the theories, which really helps explain why things are important. He wants to help out each and every student, and is always willing to answer questions inside and out of class.

Dr. Doud is the best you can hope for. He is maybe the best math teacher I have ever had at BYU. He controls the pace of the class really well and his HW is fair and doable. Tests are also fair and doable.
Dr. Doud is super quirky and inadvertently funny.  He really knows his stuff and is VERY helpful despite being a bit socially awkward.  Teaches with clarity.  I highly recommend him.
Excellent class. Dr. Doud really knows his stuff, and makes the class interesting. He's a great teacher.
Amazing teacher. He teaches extraordinarily clear, very easy to learn even the most difficult of topics. One of the greatest teachers I have had. Take him!
He teaches clearly and tests fairly on what you were taught.  Get him if you can

Dr. Doud is amazing. This class was tough. Don't expect a cakewalk if you've never learned how to do proofs before (like me). But he's incredibly helpful and fair. Visit him during office hours if you didn't understand in class. He WILL help you. Be sure to take Dr. Doud for this class. He's one of the best math teachers I've ever had.
He speaks as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
Probably the greatest math teacher at BYU. The class is as easy as math can be without dumbing anything down.

Dr. Doud is easily one of the best professors I have ever had! He gives crystal-clear explanations of even the most difficult topics. He is genuinely interested in his students doing well, and is always available to help. He will always stop to answer questions before moving on, and makes sure that everyone understands the topic. Take his class!
Awesome professor, willing to spend extra time to make sure you understand the material, really cares about his students.

The best math teacher I have ever had. He is very clear in his teaching and breaks it down to your level. Plus, he offers one-on-one help and extra helpful reviews before exams. The final was a few problems exactly off previous chapter exams. Homework/quizzes daily but quizzes are easy.

This professor was amazing.  He is very logical and if you enjoy math, he is the professor for you.  He explains most everything with proofs, but takes things down to a level at which most everyone understands.  Great professor.

Man, this class was a beast.  Dr. Doud is the most logical person on the planet, I'm not kidding.  If you enjoy teachers that aren't inconsistent, this is the guy for you.  Incredibly smart, incredibly helpful, extremely nice, what's not to love?  Great teacher, hard class.

Dr. Doud is easily one of the greatest professors I have ever had.  He explains things well, without being derogatory, and is willing to help you with specific homework problems (before they are due) - one thing I especially respect him for.  Also, he had our homework be due at 5pm the day it was to be turned in, which made life so much easier!

I took 334 AND 371 from him. I swear by Dr. Doud. He is the most amazing teacher I have ever had. If you can take a class from him, DO IT! He is so good at explaining, and he is SO patient. He'll explain things over and over until you understand them. He is ALWAYS willing to help. Life is better with Doud, guaranteed.

Dr. Doud explains things more clearly than any math teacher I have ever had. He can make difficult concepts very clear. I was never intimidated to ask a question in his class. He will give great help during his office hours as well. His homework and tests can be demanding, but he goes to great lengths to prepare you for them. Great for math majors.

I came into the class dreading it, as I dread all math classes. Doud is an absolutely terrific teacher. He teaches difficult concepts, but he talks it down to your level. If you still don't understand, he will dumb it down even further, or invite you into his office to help you. he's not intimidating like many professors are. Heavy on proofs though
PROF DOUD IS THE BEST TEACHER I HAVE HAD AT BYU. HE EXPLAINS THINGS EXTREMELY WELL AND MAKES HARD CONCEPTS EASY TO UNDERSTAND.
By far the best math teacher I've had at BYU.  He has an talent for explaining abstract concepts clearly.  There is a heavy emphasis on proofs in the class.

At first you get the impression he could teach this stuff to 3rd graders, but it gets progressively harder.  He is a very good teacher, and very helpful on the homework, but he expects a detailed understanding of all the theorems, so the tests are pretty hard.  He is fair on the grading, though -- unlike other teachers like Tolman.

Very smart man! He is very nice and teaches very cleary. There is daily homework and quizzes but the quizzes are a joke(easy). He doesnt write the tests, which can be hard, but he holds reviews which are very helpful.
He explains things as if we were all 10 year olds, but is fairly reasonable with what he expects. The only hard thing about the class was the final.
Compared to what other sections were doing, all the proofs he does is useless! Who needs to know?! His test were just tricky too! Nothing was clear in his class.

Dr. Doud knows math like no one else. He's amazing at what he does. But he required WAY too many proofs. Other linear algebra sections did less than half of what we did. The proofs are useless to the normal student, but linear algebra techniques in general were very good to know.

I didn't know if this class would be easy or hard when I started, but Professor Doud made everything seem simple. He was more than willing to answer any questions, and his answers were helpful. This ended up being my easiest class and I give a lot of the credit to Professor Doud.

If I were to enjoy dumb math jokes the class might actually be interesting. Too many online quizzes and way too many proofs. When in the world will I ever need to solve a proof in my life. He's dreaming
He is very easy to talk to and get help.  He gives practice exams out prior to the tests which are very helpful.  He is very clear in explaining math and very patient if you don't understand.

Great professor!! Interesting, makes math a bit fun w/ jokes, etc.  Would expect you to know certain things. Tests were extremely hard and class/ homework didn't really prepare you for them. Tough because classes are hot shot honors freshman mixed with normal upper-classmen trying to get GE credit.
Awesome professor. Even though i already took the course in high school, he teaches it so I actually understand it.

He is a really good guy, very knowledgeable, once was an amazing lawyer and translator. He is however, very unorganized, goes on tangents, isn't good at reviewing what's going to be on tests. Test were so random and tricky. He often forgot a lot of things about the organization of his own class.

He's a great person, but as a professor he didn't work for me. If you're a very organized, orderly person then this may not be the class for you. He often goes off in tangents. I didn't always feel comfortable answering questions because of the way he responded, even though I do comment in many of my classes. Study guide formatting was weird.

Dr Hague is very knowledgeable in the field of translation especially as it pertains to legal contexts given his professional background . Any class from him is a joy, easily my favorite class to be in any semester I have him as a professor. He is a great mentor and cares about your success outside of academics. I would recommend him highly.

Daryl Hague is a great guy. He has done a lot in his life and he cares a lot about his students. I just didn't like the format of the class whatsoever. The tests take up way too much overall credit (2 tests, each one worth 22.5% of your grade) while other teachers just have no exams whatsoever. He also goes on a lot of tangents.I would avoid it.
I was a fan of Profe Hague. His teaching style is interesting, but it is a very easy class. If you meet the basic requirements, you will do well. He really cares about the students.

Professor Hague is great! He goes on tangents quite a bit, but they're always fun. He responds extremely quickly outside of class, and wants to help students succeed. You'll definitely want to get the book he has on the booklist, because quite a few assignments pull directly from there, and those will be on the exams. Would definitely recommend!

Dr. Hague is an expert in the translation field and doesn't just teach you how to translate, but about translation theory in general. Super interesting lectures! Go to class and do the readings and you will do great. He's also accessible outside of class for anything. If you're looking for a class for the Spanish minor, I highly recommend this one!

Really cool teacher. COVID kinda wrecked the Taco trips he puts on though. As long as you attend class you can understand and do all the homework. The tests are a bit whacky only because its difficult to take notes (or at least know what you should be taking notes on). Besides that he is a great professor and its a good class.

This class was great! I learned a ton about translation and interpretation. Sometimes it got a little repetitive, but overall it was a super fun and informative class. Professor Hague is very fun and entertaining. Be sure to participate in class.

Dr. Hague is a great teacher and is so passionate about translation. He is super knowledgable about this field and will really help you out when you have questions. He is very understanding when it comes to knowing how it is to be a student and understands all the other assignments we have to do. Really great class and overall great teacher. 10/10

Such a kind, thoughtful, funny, personable, helpful, compassionate teacher who really cares about his students and taught in all different ways using fun examples, videos, and interactive experiences. He knew us by name and looked for ways to connect with us even outside of class.

Dr. Hague is the ideal professor. His lectures are entertaining and instructional. He doesn't assign busy work, every assignment directly relates to the test. He gives you two chances on every translation assignment so grading is always fair, and he's accessible and gets to know all his students personally. Take his class.

Dr. Hague is literally the sweetest professor I have ever had. He is so kind and loving and is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject material. His class is organized, and it is so clear he wants students to succeed. Before our final, he invited us all to go to Don Joaquin's and eat lunch with him which was a blast. Take class from Dr. Hague!

I have taken several Spanish classes from Hague and enjoyed them all. He really knows his material and enjoys teaching it. His teaching style allows for plenty of participation and discussion and he grades fairly. For this specific class: the readings are provided online and are the basis for the final exam.
Awesome awesome awesome. Very interesting lectures. It was enjoyable to go to class. If you fill out the study guide, you will do fine on the tests. What are you waiting for? Go add the class.

Best professor I've ever had.  He makes class fun with optional taco trips to the best taco shop in Provo.  He also translates Spanish and English for a living so he knows his stuff.  Take his class if you want to master Spanish.

HE IS AWESOME!! A great choice for Spanish. His criteria is very clear, his tests are great if you know the study guide. He was always helpful outside of class, if you stopped by his office. I enjoyed his class, and he often has surprise quizzes at the beginning of class, but they are only worth about 1% of your final grade! Great choice!
I loved coming to this class. I learned a ton and Hague is hilarious in his own special way. Very informative class, but not too difficult. Excellent choice for any class!
Very dependable. Teaches well the subject material. Does a great job. I leave the class feeling like I was treated extremely fairly, and with a wealth of knowledge about Latin American history.
Good professor.  Clear. Concise.  Nice guy.  Really cares.  Willing to work with students.  Interesting.  You get what you put in and then some in this class.  Solid option

My actual favorite professor ever. Not kidding. Profe. Hague is so helpful and he has a wealth of knowledge to offer. He's willing to work with you and he helps you with pretty much anything you need. I'm really happy I have a couple more classes to take from him before I graduate.

Dr. Hague is one of my favorite professor's that I have taken at BYU. His lectures are amazing and really interesting. It really made me enjoy coming to class. His tests are really fair and straightforward. I loved this class, and would absolutely recommend him.

Dr hague is so straightforward that you think he must be trying to trick you, but he is not. almost every assignment in his class was a completion grade, which ended up being about 55% of the overall grade. the tests are super easy if you just study. stay on top of the syllabus. Learning suite showed that about 75% of the students got an A

Most straightforward class I've ever had at BYU.  Everything on his tests is on the study guides so you don't have to worry about random details.  I took the second midterm and the final without opening the textbook, his slides cover it all.  Super interesting class though, I retained more information than normal and would recommend it for sure.

This class was a miserable experience. I have had no idea what I was supposed to be learning all semester. The tests are ridiculous. He has PowerPoints everyday in class, he never refers to the slides so I never know what's important or not. He doesn't do a very good job preparing you for the test. Would not recommend this class.

The class is great, I would highly recommend Prof. Hague any day.  He cares about the students and the class had clear expectations and wasn't stressful at all.  I really felt like I gained a lot of useful knowledge and understanding about other cultures.  I didn't have to read that much, he's really funny also.

This is the only time I have rated a professor on here cuz Dr. Hague is a boss so I had to. He is super helpful, he makes a somewhat boring class really fun, he gives study guides that are exactly what you need to know for the tests, he is understanding, he cares about his students, and he is way funny. One of the best professors I have ever had.

Hague is the best!  He was one of my favorites.  His class is pretty consistent each time with power point presentations.  You can tell he loves the students and the class. His tests were super easy! He doesn't give out too many assignments and it just a good class overall!

Prof. Hague is a great teacher. I was upset that I bought the textbook because the tests are based on what he talks about in class. Take good notes and try to get together a google doc for the study guides he gives and you will do well. Ave. final grade in his class this semester is a 91%.

Professor Hague is one of the best professors in the Spanish department. He gives tests that challenge you and help you learn but they are not impossibly hard. His Spanish is easily the best in the department (apart from the native speakers).
he teaches very clearly and helps you understand the concepts.  his tests are very reasonable.  he is a great teacher who is very reasonable

Dr. Hague is a great teacher. He is very good at teaching grammar and makes sure that the students are understanding the material. He teaches the grammar so well because he knows it really well, and he knows the reasons behind all of the rules. He is very helpful and flexible with his office hours. He has a very good sense of humor. Class is fun.

Great class, great professor.  He tends to get distracted and then falls behind, but everything he talks about is interesting.  My advice: don't bother buying the textbook. There are no reading quizzes and he covers all test material in lectures and gives out study guides before each test.
Excellent teacher I would recommend him to everyone. Honestly the class wasn't too difficult if you would put in a decent amount of time into it.

he is a good teacher, funny and really tries to help you out, but e is a stickler for the little things, which can get annoying, willing to help you out, i dont really enjoy spanish but this class was better than most spanish classes ive had

Very good teacher.  Explains concepts with great clarity.  If you have any experience with Spanish grammar/writing, this class is incredibly easy.  His jokes are so bad that they're actually funny.  His accent isn't that great, but he is the head of the translation department, a.k.a. his Spanish is great. I definitely recommend him.
He is great, best Spanish teacher of the 5 I've had.

Hague is a good funny teacher, but his lectures can be boring as they come straight from the text. There are pop-quizzes but they are easy. The tests are easy if you know the study guide well. This is the easiest Spanish class I have taken so I would recommend it.
He uses Spanish songs in every class to demonstrate grammar principles which is extremely helpful and entertaining

Professor Hague is by far the best teacher I've ever had. He taught so clearly and explained hard concepts in ways that I will always be able remember them. If you are taking any Spanish classes, seriously, take at least one from him. IT'LL CHANGE YOUR LIFE. Oh, and he's hilarious.
He's a cool guy, pretty helpful, teaches pretty clearly.  Plus he's hot.

He's a really clear teacher and is really interested in helping students understand everything. He is really funny and gets to know the students. His tests aren't bad at all and it's really an easy class, as long as you study a little bit.

Capitan Hague is excellent at explaining grammar concepts, throwing jokes into his lectures, willing to go over material outside of class even if it's not his office hour and incorporates singing popular Latin music into the class to help you learn grammar. The material is hard and requires studying but he is outstanding.
funny guy, and very helpful but, if you haven't mastered the spanish language this class can be very difficult to get an A. I took this class from a different professor and it was a piece of cake.

This teacher uses a lot of interaction and expects his students to think for themselves...which is refreshing.  He will push you and challenge you to your limits, but in the end, he will prepare you better than any other teacher.  Exceptional.
loved him.

I hate his classes. I think he has the worst sense of humor ever. Probably what he says its funny for Americans but for latins its totally offensive! I agree with what the person before me said. He is arrogant and think he knows everything. He doesnt even have that great spanish!

Best Spanish teacher I have ever had.  Extremely challenging, but you grow so much in his class.  I ended up having a better and greater knowledge of Spanish than other students in other classes.  He's hilarious and he teaches according to the class' needs.
Excellent professor.  Syntactigrams are the worst, but he is an amazing teacher.

If you have a choice, take it from him. Hes so funny!  The most helpful prof Ive had @ BYU.  I didnt do as well as I should because he changed the syllabus in the middle of the class and there was a lot of confusion.  But, given normal circumstances, a very easy class from a great guy.
Great professor, one of the best I have ever had.  He teaches all the translation courses, so you get to know him well.  Very smart, very helpful, and very nice.

Best professor Ive ever had! Not only does he know Spanish but he can explain it EXTREMELY well. You will not leave confused-he wont let you. I learned a ton in his class. Aside from being a great teacher hes hilarious and personable. Grading is very fair. Taking his class was the best choice I made all semester. I strongly advise taking his class.
Excellent, excellent teacher. Great sense of humor, knows his stuff. Homework is busywork. Compositions are average. Tests are on the easy side of average.

Definitely very knowledgable about the spanish language and only wants that his students understand the language. Homework is ridiculously easy, tests are the same. Honestly. But at the same time youre learning the language correctly.

HILARIOUS guy!  If all of my classes at BYU were like this one, I would LOVE going to class!  Tests may be a little difficult, but if you know what you are doing, you will get a good grade.  Homework was a joke, it was so easy.  Compositions, though challenging, were great learning tools. GO FOR IT!

My favorite BYU professor. Great sense of humor, extremely helpful and patient both in class and on an individual basis outside of class. Not too much homework, and hey, you still feel like you learned something. Have taken 6 classes from him.
Outstanding Professor, very helpful and has a great sense of humor.  It was a very enjoyable class.  I learned a lot.
This man is one of the Best Professors that I have ever had.  He teaches very well and is not too hard.
He is a great teacher! I was not a person who liked going to school until I had his class. Not only is he interesting but also a really good teacher!
This man rules!  Seriously the best spanish teacher I've ever had.  He's great about explaining everything so it makes sense...and so patient.
HATED HIM!!!
Interesting.

Course content was very applicable to how data engineering is used in enterprise solutions. I recieved questions about technology we covered in his class during job interviews. Overall felt very prepared to do real data engineering after this class.

I have never had a professor put as much time into his students like Prof. Wilson. I'm especially appreciative that he understands that his assignments are difficult, and so he works very hard to make sure we have everything we need to succeed. Incredible teacher and person.
great professor, however class needs to be more organized, felt like did not learn much on lectures, mostly chat explaining to me what happened
He is nice and can be helpful
He is a very kind professor, and I appreciate his demeanor. However, I didn't always feel fully supported or helped during the course

I have never met such a good and caring professor like Dr Wilson. His assignments are hard (how else will you learn data engineering?) but he guides you every step of the way, he is willing to help you out. He will put in late nights just to help his students. Incredibly goated

The most telling thing I have to say about this professor is that we had our final project due last night at midnight, and I kid you not when I say he was on video calls until 11:59 PM helping students. He is extremely respectful and willing to help. Yes, his class was very hard, but he is there to help.

He is so awesome! Great personality and is super caring. The nature of learning a new language (R) makes it so the class is going to be a bit of work but that's why we're in college! He explains things very well and constantly seeks feedback. Good balance of the data science process and everything from basic R to tidy models and model deployment.

Professor Wilson is a WONDERFUL person. He really cares about his students and genuinely wants for your success. He can get a little distracted and sometimes his "answers" to questions leave more to be asked, but he knows his stuff and he has a 5 star personality.

Dr. Wilson is a great person, but not a great professor. He teaches at an elementary levels while exams are at a college level. I had an A in the class until the final, which I had no idea how to do most of the programs. Much of what I learned in this class was self taught because he didnt cover things well enough in class.
He is an amazing teacher who really cares about his students. I had friends that took this class from other professors and did not enjoy it as much as I did.
The goat at teaching calc. Super good at explaining, was easy to do well on tests because he made them straightforward and prepared us well for them.
A joy to learn from, and I never felt intimidated or slowfor asking questions. A very difficult class but the homework and tests are extremely fair

Great teacher. Knows the material very well and prepares you for the tests in his class. The class is very hard and very fast, we covered 3/4 of the linear algebra in the first two weeks so you better pay attention in class and do the homework. Fun guy, shares stuff about his family and other areas of life that show he's a really good guy.

Take Obata! He does a great job explaining concepts and walking us through difficult problems. His lectures are well paced, although sometimes they could be a little confusing - which was more to do with the class content than his teaching. He writes his own tests so you know what to expect and our final wasn't cumulative which was nice.

The best professor I have had at BYU. The way he teaches is so effective and helpful. He has the ability to explain tough concepts so simply and clearly. He is so good at summing things up and answering questions. He was always available during office hours and he is very knowledgeable. He cares about your success.

This professor was extremely unorganized in lectures. I had previously taken this course by a different professor, but yet I was confused in most lectures. The homework does prepare you for his exams because it is way more difficult than the exams, although the lectures do not prepare you for the homework. He grades very generously.
tough class, but he's a dope professor. Lectures prepare you for the exams more than anything. He does good examples in class, follow along and take notes.

Dr.Obata explains concepts clearly with 2-3 examples. Always answer questions, so ask them. The practical midterms are harder than the exams.The exams are still hard, but he gives partial credit.HW is useful, though its style differs from exams. It's a traditional class—attend all lectures and take notes. He uses the board & shares his notes on LS.
This professor never made things harder than necessary. clear expectations and grading criteria and very perceptive to student's questions. He made a challenging math class easy

He is honestly the best teacher I have had at BYU thus far. Teaching style is great, the homework can get challenging, prepping you for thorough practice exams for easier midterms and final. He challenges you while still being reasonable and full of grace for due dates and exams given it's experienced in the same way by the majority of the class.

Take notes during lectures, and you will be fine. Don't go to lectures, and it will be extremely difficult. The exams may seem intimidating, but Professor Obata gives lots of partial credit. Lots of homework, but ask questions, and he can answer them well.

Genuinely looked forward to this class, SL center is SO fun! A few assignments, depending on your TA's grading, can be tough. He is a good guy and will work with you and give you extra credit. Some nights feel really long, but overall, I wouldn't trade it. I loved having him as a professor. Make friends with your classmates and carpool its so fun!!
Lectures are kinda boring but Prof Bolingbroke is a nice guy. The commute is a bit rough and it feels long in the evenings. He is pretty reasonable to work with though
Great guy! Class was easy and there weren't many assignments. He is very understanding and willing to work with you on things. Worth taking in SL over BYU campus.

Professor Bolingbroke is a really nice man and genuinely a good guy. The content itself is interesting, but the classes were often pretty boring and the assignments felt unorganized. There aren't many things graded, so you really have to do well on all of them to succeed. Grading can take weeks, but overall it's not a bad class.

Lots of essays writing.  Class felt pretty unorganized with assignment descriptions on PowerPoints, syllabus, or just given in class.  No serious tests.  Great professor but lectures do get long in the evenings.  Just make sure to have him review bigger assignments before final submissions. Attendance is mandatory (in SLC Center).

By far the best religion class I have ever taken! Fascinating and engaging, Brother Bolingbroke is an immersive storyteller, and his passion for the scriptures shines through in his lectures. The workload is reasonable and the grading criteria are clear. I credit this class with igniting my interest in studying the scriptures. HIGHLY recommend.
The nicest guy! He uses a free online textbook (yay) and the lectures are long but include a good amount of discussion. Class was pretty easy and flexible.

Dr Bolingbroke is new at BYU, but he's passionate about US history and very open to helping students. There are a LOT of essays (including a book report), but the topics are generally easy, they're the only real homework, and he's an easy grader. Also has lectures dedicated to writing good essays, which helped me a ton. I would recommend!

Dr. Boren is awesome and we are still friends like 4 years after I took his class. It's an easy A but I learned so much and his class was really what made me want to stay in El Ed. Won't be that interesting of a class if you're not serious about becoming a teacher, but if you are, definitely would recommend!

I really like Professor Boren's class. As long as you show up and participate it is really an easy A. He cared about each of his students and really wanted us to be successful. His class helped me learn a lot and I would take it again!

He is so nice. Former principal. He is a good person to ask questions about career in EL ED. He is super sweet and helpful. His class helps you prepare for your interview to become a teacher. Love his class and him! He is super understanding, helpful, and caring professor. Definitely take if youre considering!

Bro. Boren was an elementary school principal and that helps us get a good perspective on education. His class is based off a "interview" with him as a principal that you have at the end of the semester for your final. He keeps his lectures very unbiased and poses questions to help us think critically and deeply.

Hardest thing is you can't get away from this professor. Exams are incredibly convoluted and he is zero help. My group went from the highest-scoring deck to the lowest after he dismissed our work as "low effort"—the ultimate irony for such a low-effort teacher. Harder than Chem 105 or Calc 2 because there is no actual instruction.

This is honestly my favorite class that I've taken at BYU. It's everything I was hoping to get out of the strategy program, and while the experience that Dr. Bryce creates for the students is challenging, it's highly impactful. Most people will finish with an A or A-, there's a heavy curve applied at the end of the semester!

STRAT 560- Professor Bryce's class was disorganized and poorly structured. Key topics were crammed last minute, and he often showed up late or didn't finish the material. The TA was unresponsive and unhelpful. The content itself wasn't hard, but unclear instruction made it frustrating (and stressful) due to his poor teaching and lack of clarity.

You can't do anything about having to take this class, so this is just commiserating. Bryce doesn't equip you with the tools you need to succeed. Felt like I was running as fast as I could all semester to guess what was in his head and very rarely could. My grades have been great throughout the entire strategy program, and this class changed that.

Dr. Bryce doesn't really teach anything to you. It is expected that you create "CEO ready" presentations with no skills being taught to you beforehand. Everything taught in class is made up of abstract thought. Students gave feedback about the class after the midterm, but Dr. Bryce didn't seem to listen to or implement any of it. Good luck.

Dr. Bryce's class is my least favorite class I've ever taken, and he's my least favorite professor I have ever had. I made an account on this website JUST so I could write this review. Not a ton of space on this, but basically he is completely unreasonable, doesn't really teach anything, and is unwilling/unable to listen to peoples' concerns.

The whole class is 4 group projects, however you never learn in class what to do for each project. You have to meet with the TA's multiple times to get different clues to guess what was originally in Dr. Bryce's head. The most frustrating class in the whole strategy program. Good luck.

The schedule for the class is best characterized by "hurry up and wait." Deadlines for the group case projects had fast turnarounds, and then we had 2 weeks "off" after the midterm. He set up a "feedback" session after the midterm where he proceeded to spend a week collecting and invalidating our concerns and recommendations to improve the class.

Tough stuff. Good luck to all. He teaches really complicated things in a really complicated way, and you have no way of predicting what your grade will be. Class-high of 55/100 on the first presentation. That's all.

This was the worst class I have taken in college. The material was fantastic, but Prof. Bryce was arrogant and doesn't understand undergrad students whatsoever. For a 3 credit class we worked about 20 hours per week only to fail the first 2 cases. The class was curved, but it made so that you were just trying to beat everyone else.

I promise Dr. Bryce cares about you. While his grading standards may seem rigorous, it is because he values real-world applicability and strives for industry-level work. The class is curved, so don't freak out. You will learn so much more because of his teaching style. Just hang in there, take good notes, and listen in class.

Dr. Bryce's 411 class is definitely the best strategy class I've taken thus far. The concepts and theories discussed in the class are mind-blowing, and Bryce teaches them clearly. Make sure to get feedback early from him and the TA's on group powerpoint presentations. Don't be scared of bad grades early on; everyone's grades got better by the end.
I learned a TON in Dr. Bryce's class but it is super difficult! Get ready to put in a ton of work on the group cases.

Dr. Bryce does a great job at explaining difficult strategy concepts and relating them to real world scenarios, as well as providing exposure to analysis and slide building. My only qualm is that grading seemed unnecessarily harsh in the beginning - it doesnt end up hurting your grade but just lowers the curve.

Professor Bryce comes off as pretty high and mighty. He likes to talk about how successful his consulting career was, and prides himself on not giving higher than a 90% on group projects. The class focuses on some pretty challenging strategic concepts, and Bryce sometimes seems to like to explain it as difficultly as possible to sound smarter.
The vast majority of your grade was based on group work and powerpoint "style" rather than actual understanding of the course material. There is a bit of a strange curve as well.

Dr. Bryce is an amazing teacher. The lectures are super interesting and focus a lot on business applications. This may have been my favorite class I've ever taken. Pick a solid group so you can bounce ideas off each other for the excel exercises. If you understand what he does in class you will aces every pop-quiz. Such an interesting class!

Your course grade depends too much on the work produced by your group.  Your group is selected randomly at the beginning of the semester, so if you get stuck with a poor group, over 50% of your grade is screwed (or you can try to pull the weight for your group on every project).   Project grades also seem to be assigned really arbitrarily.

I took MicroEconomics before, so this class was more of a review.  If you have a good math base, it's breeze so try to take calculus before this class.  Do the practice questions before quizzes and tests, and go to his office if you don't get something - he is very approachable outside of class.

Dr. Bryce is an awesome professor.  His lectures are really interesting (though sometimes over my head...) and he really focuses on life application.  I really enjoyed the class even though it was pretty hard.  We had four group assignments, 1 big project, and 2 tests.

Outstanding professor.  You will learn a great deal from this course.  1 Midterm (in class), 1 Final (scheduled), pop quizzes, 1 large project.  The class was not easy, but the tools you learn are things you will actually use.  I'm currently interning for a management consulting firm and have used several of the things I learned this past semester.

A top-eschelon professor. I don't know if his students realize what a rare bird he is in academia: years of top level management consulting experience, broad knowledge of business, economics, and math. He is a good presenter, extremely friendly, and the material is the stuff that a world-class business education is made of.

He knows his stuff. I recommend the class with him. Tests are difficult, but not hard.  He gives lots of pop quizes, so refresh what you learned the past session so you can get a ten.  You can get by without the textbook, but it is a nice help, but you could get an A without the textbook.
Very, very good professor. Really know his stuff. Never stops smiling :) Quizzes are easy, tests are very, very hard.

Extremely smart, enthusiastic and knowledgeable.  Can off as a bit arrogant at first (Wharton PhD), but he really knows this stuff inside and out.  Learn from him, don't let your first impression color your experience.  It's a great class.  Take anything he teaches.

What a stud.  He really is a great teacher and very engaging.  He knows his stuff and gets the class involved.  I had him for Manec and Strategy 498 and both classes aren't too hard and both are interesting.
What a stud.  I really liked the class.  Yes, it's hard, but it is interesting.  He is a great guy.
Nice guy, enjoyable class. Workload is way overboard for a 1.5 credit block class.
He's a funny guy.  Good teacher and very interactive with his students.  One time he wore two different colors of shoes just for entertainment purposes.
Awesome course! A must for the Manec requirement. He's funny, interactive, and entertaining. The class is very interesting, farily easy, and very applicable. Take this course!

I like the class layout. All the study guides were posted beforehand so you can fill in the questions as the semester goes by. That made the tests easy. The homeworks took 10 minutes to do usually and there's no required reading in the class :)

This class felt very disorganized, and I often wasn't fully sure what was expected on assignments. We had a large group project where scheduling was challenging, and clearer guidance on expectations would have been helpful. The class itself was easy, but felt boring, especially if you prefer structured planning.

Easiest religion class I've taken. I enjoy how Brother Calabro wants us to enjoy the content rather than worry about a grade. However, it's easy to get distracted in class. His voice is a bit monotone and he can be a bit boring, but if you put in the effort you'll learn a lot! He's very smart and knowledgable.

The class itself was great! Overall, it was a good experience. However, he pushes for students to deeply analyze scriptures, which is good for some, but I'm not at a point where that was helpful. it made the assignments frustrating because I didn't feel like I was learning anything, and I was lost 70% of the time.

Bro. Calabro is really nice and learns almost every students name. He really loves history and adds lots of ancient history into the class. Lectures can be a little boring but tests and homework are very easy.
He's just a kind guy. He is insanely knowledgable. The exams were really difficult, in my opinion. But he tries his best to get to know his students and be available to them.

I would absolutely recommend! Brother Calabro is very knowledgeable and kind! I always left the classroom with a smile on my face. The tests are kind of difficult but he gives you a study guide that's awesome!

David Calabro is a nice guy. But honestly the classes are soooo boring and the weekly study journals are so in depth. The TA is a harsh grader and I think she randomly decides when you get a 100 or when she wants to doc you some points and then gives no feedback. This class is alright, take it if you want, but there are probably better options.

Calabro is the kindest soul and super sweet. His lectures were a little all over the place and it was hard to know what to gleam from them, but he always did a review day in class where he told you everything that was going to be on the exams. Easy class!

He is a nice professor. He is clearly passionate about his areas of study and will occasionally go down a random tangent. He cares about each individual student and wants them to succeed. The workload isn't too bad- just an assignment that usually takes 15 mins before each class. Pretty easy tests too (he gives a really good study guide).

It's only my fault for not getting an A. This class is pretty simple in terms of workload, but the content is great. Any class you can take with Brother Calabro is a class you should take. He's the best. I'd give him 6/5 if I could.
Lectures are pretty boring but if you're looking for an easy A with a professor who cares about you take from Dr. Calabro!

Brother Calabro is the best! He is just a great guy, has lots of Old Testament knowledge, and his class was well organized. The workload was light and the tests were very fair. He is just very kind and you can tell he really cares.

Professor David Calabro is one of the few professors at BYU that is very passionate about what he teaches. His classes are a little boring but his class is very easy and manageable. Attendance is mandatory.

The love and care Brother Calabro has for his work is incredibly evident. He teaches earnestly and intently, truly trying to help his students grow. Some may find him awkward, but he makes the class so that you truly get out what you put in. If you want to learn, he's there for you. He's incredibly knowledgeable and prepared. Old Testament-heavy.
Good professor/class. Test reviews were held in class, and exams were easy. Not very challenging, but the topic and subject matter is interesting. Easy A. Isn't overly engaging in class.

Professor Calabro is the GOAT!! He has so much gospel knowledge it's crazy. He's super kind, his class is structured fairly easily, but I learned more in my classes from him than any other religion professor here at BYU. His lectures are top notch- not in terms of entertainment, but in terms of content for sure.

Brother Calabro is a very knowledgeable guy who loves what he teaches. He's kind of a dusty old professor, but the class is very easy. All you have are weekly study journals and a couple tests where the study guide is very similar to the test. Attendance is mandatory but he has a lot of good insights.

Honestly, I didn't pay attention in lectures because this class wasn't engaging at all to me. Did none of the readings and still did fine on the tests. Tests are all online and there are weekly assignments you have to do. If you want an easy A, this is your class!

Professor Calabro is amazing!!! If you still need a book of mormon class take it with Calabro! He is the sweetest and easiest professor! One of my favorites professors ever. His lectures are great. He goes over the study guide with you in class and the exams are super similar. Weekly journals are super easy. He is very knowledgable and kind.

Probably the easiest religion class you can take. Not hard at all. Attendance is mandatory, but the tests are really straightforward. If you know the Book of Mormon at all, it is a breeze. Study journals can be on any topic. The class was very chill though sometimes lectures put me to sleep.

Very chill, easy class. Not too many assignments, fun (though non-critical) lectures. Doesn't dive too deep into the text, just enough to get the most important surface stuff. Easy enough tests with them mostly based off the study guide (which you can just fill out throughout the semester as your notes and then studying is easy). Great class.

Brother Calabro is a really nice guy but some of his lectures kind of dragged. Attendance is mandatory and part of your grade so make sure you attend classes. All the stuff on the study guide is also from the lectures and the test questions are also pretty straightforward.

You have to mark your attendance in class everyday. Honestly his lectures are pretty boring, but his tests have questions based on specific things he says in lecture so you should go and try to listen... or just go to his test review days. I feel like I actually learned from the BoM this semester because of his weekly assignments.

AMAZING class. It is easy to know what/when to turn stuff in. He gives a study guide for tests, which are all online. Attendance and readings are self-recorded. Fill out the study guide and you will do great on the tests. Besides tests all you have to do is one super short Study Journal per week. Very nice guy who wants his students to do well.

Professor Calabro is a great professor. He is really sweet and puts a big effort into his lectures. The study journal assignments are a little bit tough to get full credit but he lets you resubmit until you get full credit. attendance is mandatory and self graded.

The lectures in this class were insanely boring and hardly ever related to the scriptures or class content. I got very little out of this class. The tests could be very random, and the study journals were almost impossible to get full credit on. I was in a smaller class, but it was a lot of being talked at and he only knew about 5 kids names.
If you're looking for an easy religion credit that will change your life, take this class. I LOVE PROFESSOR CALABRO. He's literally such a nice guy. Take this class!

Attendance is 10% of your grade, self-reported. No testing center. Exam online, closed book. I thought his lectures were a bit boring. Lots of reading. 1 easy assignment a week. Go to the review lecture and do the provided review, pretty much like the exam. Easy extra credit. Has many stories and guest speakers. Had field trips around campus...

Professor Calabro is the most innocent and kind man. the class was so easy. Not really any homework and the tests weren't bad. If you are looking for a super easy A class that requires no work but gives you credits this is the class for you. I won't take him again because it just wasn't engaging for me personally.

amazing and kind professor! 10/10 would recommend to anyone! his study guides are an exact replica of the exams and he goes over them a day before the exam. you can get by without doing any readings tbh just use the study guide. there are weekly journals but its super easy just write about your impressions and attendance is mandatory

the easiest religion class! gives out great study guides for the exams which are NOT proctored or timed and can be completed in like 30-45 mins. very accommodating and you can see him during OH to redeem some points back. take detailed notes though, like everything he says can end up on the exam.

He was a good teacher, but I didn't click with him. If you need help, he is there and willing to move things around for you. Lectures are a little boring, but very informational. He knows the material very well. Make sure you are thorough with how you study for the exams.

FOR REL A 327- PEARL OF GREAT PRICE: gives out great study guides and answers that reflect the exams, no quizzes and only study journals to write. great professor, take it from him, super easy A and learned a lot. will miss the class!

Brother Calabro is easily one of the best professors that teach religion. He's constantly asking for participation and is very sincere. He brings the spirit in his classes, and helps prepare you for the exams very well. His tests are super easy and he builds you up to succeed. 10/10 take David Calabro for any classes.
