I loved Bro. Calabro! He is so passionate about what he teaches and knows the scriptures like the back of his hand. He is kind of socially awkward but still super caring and funny. His class was pretty easy, the only hw was an easy weekly study journal that had a really clear grading rubric. He also gives a good study guide and reviews it in class!
Bro Calabro is amazing. His lectures always teach you something new while promoting the spirit. SO grateful I had his class

Bro. Calabro knows his stuff for sure. I think you could ask him a random verse in the scriptures and he would be able to recite it from memory. I would describe him as giddy, because he really loves the topic he teaches and wants his students to love it too. Very caring teacher overall and gives a great study guide for the exams!

Dr. Dahl definitely knows his stuff and is willing to work with students. He's fair and does a good job of explaining things (though his lectures make *a lot* more sense if you've read the text before class).

Dr. Dahl is a funny guy, I actually really enjoyed lectures from him. He is super smart, though sometimes I feel like he explains things in a confusing way. Use the TA labs for homework, huge lifesaver. There is one group project at the end of the semester but that's it. The tests are pretty intense but nothing too crazy. I enjoyed this class!

Dr. Dahl is insanely smart which sometimes makes his lectures difficult to follow. You have to use R for your homeworks, which is fun to learn but is tricky at first. After the first couple homeworks, things get easier. He is willing to help and wants to make the class as fair as possible for everyone.  You've got to put in the work.
Dr. Dahl is a solid professor, in my opinion. Not extraordinary, but knowledgeable, willing to answer questions, and a good test writer. No complaints.

Worst teacher I have ever taken a class from. The in class lectures are unrelated to HW or tests. Then the HW is unrelated to tests. You take the tests near blind, having never covered any of the test material in class or on the HW, only in the test reviews done by the TA's. Tests are 60% of your grade. Avoid this teacher at all costs.

Dr. Dahl is a solid professor. He is not the most exciting teacher, but he really wants each student to understand. He is very approachable and takes time to answer questions without making you feel dumb. Dr. Dahl is very straightforward in his grading and there are a lot of different ways to get points. Which is good because his tests are brutal!

Dr. Dahl has high expectations for his students. The exams (no help available) are graded harder than the homework (TA help available), which sucks. Class is really boring and unnecessary (especially at 8am), but he gives 2 pop quizzes worth 5% of your grade at random points in the term. Exams are EXTREMELY difficult and worth 70% of your grade.

Dr. Dahl is everything I would hope for in a professor - prepared, intelligent, approachable, humble, and organized. The course was very well organized and I felt like I was given all the resources I needed to do well. I would highly recommend Dr. Dahl.

Dr. Dahl really is a nice guy, but my goodness, I've never been more nit picked in my entire life. The days where you were graded on whether or not your code worked are long gone. Every tiny detail has to be EXACTLY how he wants it. If you can't get the solution his way, don't expect full credit on anything.

Dr. Dahls speciality is definitely statistical programming. It was very interesting to learn about a principle conceptually and then see an example in the code. It seemed like he was working through some of the kinks of the course since it was his first time teaching STAT 230. Overall I appreciated his enthusiasm and approachability.

Dr. Dahl is very friendly, but the material is very un-engaging and difficult. Be prepared to do a lot of out of class studying and work to get the concepts down; A lot of in-class material is not what's on the homework, but there to provide background for concepts from 121, and provide a basis moving forward. Lots of theory and proofs.

He is ok at teaching but he is not helpful at all. You have to go to his office to ask something. If you ask through email even though it is really easy for him to answer, He is not usually giving answers. And, when you go to his office, he is busy. He is ok but not pro-actively helpful.

Dr. Dahl does a good job of making material that is not super interesting, more easily accessible to the average student. He expects students to learn more then is taught in class outside of class and this is reflected in the homework assignments. Tests are very reflective of what is covered in class, they are difficult but very doable.

I'd like to say that Dr. Dahl has to teach tough classes. I think if he was teaching 121 or 230 he'd get fantastic rating, because he's a stellar teaching. Because of this he's been relegated to teaching R and 340, which sucks. He does a good job teaching them. He isn't the most exciting lecturer, but he's fair and always there to give help.

Also for Stat 123I learned a lot in this class, but probably more from doing the homework than from the lectures. Homework is manageable but don't procrastinate it. Some of his tests I thought had curve-balls that lowered a lot of peoples' grades. The textbook helped me for one test but it didn't do much else for me.

The material for this class is just plain hard, but he teaches it very well. The book is hard to read, so you will do best if you go to his lectures. He is very friendly and willing to help students who are struggling.

Dr. Dearden is a caring and earnest professor. His physical science lectures for this class were fairly clear and straightforward, and the homework assignments were generally not too difficult (similar for the two exams). I know this isn't the type of class he usually teaches, but it was interesting and not too hard nonetheless.
lectures were very confusing and did not help very much with hw. Very difficult class and TAs aren't very helpful. Tests are difficult and hard to prepare for

Dr. Dearden is a kind person. This class will take up all of your time and sanity. Effort is not enough to get a good grade, you need to attend hours of TA help just to complete the homework. The tests are difficult and worth almost everything. This class is unnecessarily hard, and not a reflection of chemical engineering.  Take CHEM 105 instead.
I took Chem 111 from him and he was such a good teacher. You definitely have to show up because if you try to study the slides, it doesn't make sense.

Dr. Dearden is a caring and competent chemistry professor. His lectures weren't the most engaging or clear (I would recommend Dr. Sevy) but I attended his class all semester and was able to be successful nonetheless.
This is the class that made me switch out of chemical engineering. The lectures were not only boring, but totally unhelpful. Expect to teach yourself all of the material.

Make sure to attend class because he does in class quizzes for attendance but he tells you the answers. I am terrible at chemistry and physics but this class made me feel smart. He lets you bring one sheet of notes to each test and the TAs are amazing. Definitely take tis class to fulfill the GE requirement.

This class made me really want to learn more about science to the point it made me change my major. He loves his students and wants them to learn. Sometimes it's hard to get concepts, but if you go to the TA lab the TAs will help with everything you need to know. The reviews I will admit don't help much, and the tests can be very hard.
Probably my favorite professor in the entire department. Incredibly nice and willing to take as much time as needed to help you learn something outside of class.

Chem 111 is a really hard class. Dr. Dearden is clearly passionate about what he teaches and loves doing demonstrations. He cares a lot about his students and about the gospel. I had only one semester of chemistry before this class, and I struggled a lot. Do the readings and talk to the TAs!

Each week we had written and online homework. Both were difficult and typically required TA help. If you have not taken AP chem or another college level chemistry class, I would really not recommend starting here. I had only taken high school chemistry and it was hard to keep up with the kids who had already taken a lot of chemistry classes before.

Dr. Dearden is an absolutely brilliant scientist and a great teacher. The class itself is not easy, but Dr. Dearden does great work in preparing students for tests and homework. He displayed an obvious appreciation for questions and curiosity, and he was always willing to help us in any way he could.

Dr. Dearden is a very nice person but that can only get you so far. He is very lecture heavy however if you don't attend lecture he posts the slides. The tests are VERY difficult and cover many things that were never discussed in lecture so be prepared. The homework is impossible without TA's, they will be your best friend throughout this class.

The class was very demo heavy, which was fun, but required me to teach myself everything. Professor messes up a lot in his lectures which is confusing. Assumes you know more than you do. Thinks you can make assumptions on things he hasnt explained. CONSIDER A DIFFERENT PROFESOR FOR THIS CLASS.

He's a little rough around the edges, but truly and honestly a great professor with lots of teaching experience (and enjoys doing explosions in class). I felt prepared for the exams and the frequent but short exams helped a lot. Encourages questions all the time, students just have to be comfortable cutting him off because he doesn't pause much.

Dearden loves doing some type of explosion so go in person! The main thing youll want to pay attention to during lectures are the practice problems. When doing readings outside of class, try to understand the concepts around equations on the equation sheet. The TAs are your best friend for this class when it comes to completing hw assignments.

Dearden was a great professor and very kind. He really loves chemistry and blowing stuff up. In order to do well GO TO TA HOURS FOR HELP ON THE HOMEWORK. The homework can be difficult (and often a little different from lecture content) and reflect the tests really well so if you do well on the homework, youll likely do well on the tests.

Dr. Dearden is an awesome professor, always ready with a demo to make the class more intriguing. He teaches a hard class, but is great at building on the material to help you understand. Its not an easy class, but definitely the best to take it from. He gives random spiritual thoughts too, which I loved.

I loved Dr. Dearden's lectures. He's super open to questions and more than happy to talk with students during office hours. It was a hard class so definitely use the TAs too. The material was confusing sometimes, but half the time Dr. Dearden had a demo ready to blow something up in lecture, so we got lots of experience feeling the enthalpy.

Dr. Dearden is very capable and intelligent, but I had an extremely difficult time following his lectures. He goes on tangents a lot and does not seem to be able to "dumb down" the material or explain it adequately. If you are naturally good at chem, I suppose he'd be fine, but I would recommend taking another professor who is better at explaining

Dr. Dearden is amazing! He does his best to make this class the best experience possible. With that said however, know that this class is quite tough. It is meant to be a weeder class for the chemistry department majors. It is very test heavy and the homework isn't easy. But Dr. Dearden makes it doable if you follow his lead.

Dr. Dearden is amazing. I felt like he cared so much about his students' success. I loved coming to class every day; Dr. Dearden is a phenomenal lecturer and he is great at answering questions. He is a spiritual giant; I often felt my chemistry class was more spiritually enriching than my religion class. One of BYU's finest. Highly recommend!!

This was a research credit that I did with Dr. Dearden. I appreciated how accessible he was during the day and how quickly he responded to my e-mails. I almost always saw him teaching students from his chemistry classes during office hours. A great guy.

Dr. Dearden is a living legend. I am forever thankful for the growth I experienced in Chem 111. He will make you work and if you accept his challenge with determination you will get the result you want.

It's a hard class. He challenges you, but I never once felt helpless or stupid. It's all a matter of how much work you're willing to put in. He wants to see you succeed, and his office hours are worth gold. There will be many explosions/ demonstrations in class. They're awesome. Go to lectures.

The class was very difficult, but Dr. Dearden kept his lectures engaging and easy to follow. He really likes explosions, so that was fun. The tests are hard since there was no multiple choice, but we were allowed to do reworks for a quarter of the points back. Do all your homework, use the TA labs and review sessions, and you'll be fine.

Because the course is heavily regulated by the department, it does not matter so much who you take it from. The homework, tests, and grading is the same across all sections. That being said, I really enjoyed the lectures. Dr. Dearden knows what he is talking about. Just be sure to read beforehand and bring your questions to the lecture.

I am currently in Dr. Dearden's class. I think he is a very merciful and caring man. He also knows what is important to talk about in his lectures, which makes it all the more important to come to class ;)
Obviously Chem 111 isn't easy but Dearden loves to blow stuff up and make class fun. Also very organized and head of department so he makes the tests... SO being in his class is good

Awesome prof, and the class wasn't too bad. Use the TAs and other resources, go to the reviews, etc. Turn your homework in on time and it's pretty easy. Tests are a little on the hard side, so make sure you read the question really thoroughly.

Kind, caring, loves to teach, the only downside were the tests-almost every 3 weeks plus a final. The bright side is that the questions came almost directly out of the textbook. Homework is based on the honor system, and there are easy in-class iClicker quizzes. Easy A. GREAT G.E. teacher.

Homework is great, it reflects the exams however it is not graded. He will ask if you did it or not and you will get credit for it that way. Be sure to take notes and focus on what he says and you'll be fine. He's the best.

This class was super disorganized. He would talk about all this random science stuff in class, but not actually explain it, just briefly go over it in the slides. Then he'd assign homework with all these crazy science problems that we had never even talked about before! The tests were hard, again because he did not explain any of the science stuff.

I took the Univ292 honors class. Absolutely stunning lectures. I cannot more highly recommend taking that class from this prof. I know it won't be the same every semester, but if he ever does anything related to space and aliens again, jump on it! It was an amazingly well-designed course.

You will do a lot of reading in this class, but they are very interesting SciFi readings. I honestly didn't put a whole lot of effort into this class, but I enjoyed it a lot. If you are doing the honors program and have to take UNIV 292, take it from him. Hopefully he does the aliens theme again.

He's a great teacher and all around great guy. He really is patient with every student and has clear, organized powerpoints. You'll need to learn some things on your own, and visit the TA lab probably more than you want to, but anything he taught in class I felt like I could do easily. Still a hard class and 5hrs/wk of various types of homework.

Univ 292 has two sections-- the one I took is affectionately known as the "Aliens class." It's engaging, informative, and incredibly cool. Decent amount of reading required, and college-level work needed on exams. TAs and Professors always willing to help.

This class is an honors class for a reason (it's a lot of work). However, I loved it and would take it again. Dr. Dearden is very passionate and respectful.  I feel like I learned so much more than I would in a regular physics class!
Expects you to put time and effort in, but is always there to help if you are doing your part.

He is confusing sometimes and goes off on tangents. He assigned homework without going over how to do it. He is so much fun but this class is hard just in general!! Tests are not what you learn in class. I would just take regular physical science because its easier.

I am very glad that I took this class from Dr. Dearden. It is a hard class regardless of what professor you had, but Dr. Dearden made it easier by being so helpful. He responds to e-mails quickly and addresses student concerns (such as moving a test back) while still being fair to the other sections. He has a strong testimony of Christ.

This class is super tough but Dearden lets you know up front the grading policy and what to expect. He teaches on our level and doesn't ramble or go off on tangents like Asplund. Really nice and does awesome explosions and demonstrations in class. Definitely recommend! He really helped me understand the hard material. Extra credit and a curve.

Dearden is one of the best professor I have ever had.  I had him winter semester.  His is the most helpful teacher ive ever seen.  He would let me come into his office almost at anytime.  He was super respectful and never made me feel dumb for asking questions.  This class is tough but if you do everything youre suppose to do you will be fine!

This was definitely a hard class, but Dearden is a pretty good teacher. I would definitely take it from him - the homework assignments are reasonable and TA's are helpful. Make sure to read the assigned reading. It definitely helps with in class quizzes and the exams, which are impossibly hard. There's a nice curve once the course is completed!

Dr. Dearden is a great teacher! Chem 111 is a really difficult class, but if you put in the time and do the work it will be great. The TA's are extremely helpful and you will need to use them especially for the labs and homework.

This class was probably my most challenging one, yet it was also my favorite. Dr. Dearden was funny, captivating, smart, likeable, and spiritual -- I strongly recommend him. This class takes a lot of time and effort, but if you're dedicated you can do well. Exams are somewhat difficult, but you can gain a third of the points lost if you do reworks.

Last semester I took Chem 101 and came out of the class with a B. If your not at all familiar with chem thats my recomendation before jumping into 105. Especially if youre shooting for an A in the class. I ended up with an A-. The class is very similar to chem 101 but at a much faster pace so if you dont understand the basics you may fall behind.

After the many horror stories that I heard about this class, I was pleasantly surprised.  Dearden is caring and humble and explains concepts well.  The TAs for Chem 105 are awesome as well.  Be sure to attend recitation and take it seriously.  Take advantage of the resources available to you, and this class is very doable.

Dearden is your best bet. He explains concepts well, but does expect you to come to class prepared. Test averages usually in the mid 60s. I was pleased with the ending curve. Honestly though, the TAs are vital, more so than the professor. If you go to the TA lab and get clarification on anything you don't understand then the class isn't that bad.

Professor Dearden does a good job, he is a really nice guy and willing to talk with you. The assignments are very fair, it is the exams that drop your grade so much but they are department-wide you'll have the same exams no matter who your professor is. From what I heard he's probably your best bet. Your recitation TA makes a huge different, do your best to get a good TA.

This class is fast paced but VERY do-able.  Especially with Dearden! If you get a good TA and go in to talk to Dearden you will do fine in this class. DEFINITELY take it from him before any other professor.

As chemistry professors go Dr. Dreaden is very good.  The material we cover is difficult and the tests are hard, but I never got tired of gong to class.  He has a funny sense of humor which kept things lively.  He really likes to blow stuff up.

Dr. Dearden is a great lecturer, but Chem 111H is incredibly difficult. The tests are challenging, but Dr. Dearden does what he can to help. He is humble, sweet and loves his students. EXPECT EXPLOSIONS! He blows something up at least twice a week

Chem 111 is a BEAST! Regardless of the professor, this class requires about 14 hours a week outside of class to do labs and homework. Dearden is a caring man who is approachable, and covers the material fairly well. The TA will become your savior. Tests are brutal. tough, tough, tough, tough

Reading the book is essential to do the homework and understand the material. He ties in the gospel which was really cool. Sweet and smart guy, really takes his students success to heart. Be prepared to teach yourself out of book a lot, go to TA lab for help and put in a lot hours outside of class. Interesting class though!

Brilliant Class. Dr. Dearden knows what he is talking about, and truly cares for his students. He is enthusiastic and humble, very entertaining, and instills a love for the subject. The class is hard, so unless you're up for a challenge, take 105. But, if you want to know and understand chemistry, take Dr. Dearden. Very gospel-centered too!

Great professor.  He really knows what he is talking about and if you go ask him for help, he's more than happy to assist you.  His lectures are pretty clear, and he makes an effort to make sure most people in the class understand before he moves on.  Chem 111 is a hard class. You have to work but Dr. Dearden in an excellant professor.

Great teacher, in the truest sense of the word. He is super nerdy and knows everything about chemistry, I could rarely ask a question that really stumped him. Very approachable more in to the semester, affable. Tough class, he's pretty hard line, but it motivates people instead of feeding them useless stuff they'll just forget later. Great teacher!

I'm one of those people who will never understand chemistry. The class was lots of work, extremely difficult, and frustrating. And when I changed my major halfway through the semester I learned that I couldn't taken 101 instead, so it ended up being completely worthless. He does blow stuff up a lot.

I took Chem105 during my first semester at BYU. It was my hardest class, but it ended up being my favorite. Dr. Dearden is great and gives students every possible chance to succeed if they try. He is a phenomenal teacher. Lectures are always interesting and he is very well prepared. He doesn't talk super fast and it is very easy to understand him.

If you like stuff watching stuff blow up, you will probably like Dearden. If you get bored after the first time he blows something up like me, you will probably not like him. In-lecture was nearly pointless. If Dearden is the best Chem 105 prof. I don't want to know how the others are.

For the hardest class at BYU, Dr Dearden definitely makes your life easier.  He's really great, kind of geeky/nerdy, and totally wonderful. This is my second time in Chem 105, and he's making it a lot clearer.  He really makes an effort to make everyone understand the material, even the harder stuff.

Love Dr. Dearden! He is so sweet and funny and loves to blow things up! Demos are the best part of class and for the most part he does at least one everyday. The material is difficult and he sometimes doesn't explain things very well and takes a long time to answer just one question during review days, but overall he is a great professor!

Very passionate about chemistry. Wants you to learn concepts and not just how to regurgitate the necessary information. Difficult class. Raises average GPA of class to meet chem department standards so this "curve" of sorts helps everyone.  Can be slightly boring in lecture, but he makes up for it when he blows things up (usually twice a week)

wow. hardest class ever. dr. dearden is the BEST!!! really. his first time teaching 111 and he did a great job. so nice and i felt like he really cared. i signed up for 105 and 111 and decided to take 111 cuz he was so nice and helpful. if i were to take it again i'd get sevy. then probably dearden. and he's only getting better the more he teaches.

This was his first time teaching 111, but he did a good job. Tests are the same for all 111 classes, and they are brutal. Homework is due every friday and there is a lot so dont procrastinate, its hard. Dearden is awesome he made an effort to know everyone's name and he blows things up all the time (it makes the whole class worth it) haha

Dr. Dearden is one of the best professors I have ever had.  He is incredibly genuine and truly cares about his student's grades.  He is a fair grader.  The only reason his test were so difficult was because all of the sections of chem111 had the same tests.  They are killer!  Be prepared to work but definitely take it from Dearden

Dearden has a real knack for taking difficult chemical concepts and explaining them on a simple level. I've TA'd many chemistry classes and he is one of the best at clearly explaining concepts. His class is fair but requires effort. The test will roast you if you don't study.He also does an excellent job of showing students WHY the subject matters.

Professor Dearden is an excellent teacher. The class requires a lot of time and is not for the faint of heart. I took it just for fun, because all the Pre-Med wine about it. I did just fine. Do not expect the grad to be given to you on a silver platter. This a meritocracy. If you want the grade then work for it.
If you go to class, do the assignments and got to recitation its not that bad.  He's easy to listen to in lecture and likes to blow stuff up... so that's a plus.  Has lots of opportunities for mercy.

Dr. Dearden is clear and knows his stuff.  Very fair when it comes to grades.  If you get behind, good luck catching up.  I'm retaking Chem 105 because I allowed myself to get behind halfway through the semester.  You really will do your best in the class if you follow his syllabus to a tee. Material isnt too hard, just incredibly time consuming.

Dr Dearden is by far the best chem 105 teacher! Dr Shirts subbed for our lecture one time and I had no stinking clue what the man was talking about. Don't get me wrong Shirts is a genius he just is really really hard to follow. Chem 105 is a really hard class if you don't stay on top of it so you may end up not liking any teacher. Dr Dearden understands it's tough and does a good job of being clear and keeping attention. Also very fair with grades
Dearden is great! He is such a nice guy and he makes his lectures interesting. Chem 105 is a lot of work, that is a given but Dearden really wants everybody to succeed. He is great!!
The jokes about his daughter are the best...

Very challenging course, but I liked it. Dr. Dearden is an awesome guy, and really cares about his students. He wants you to succeed. Very time consuming course, so buckle up. Provides lots of opportunites for practice, and learning, so USE THEM. awesome guy.
Great teacher I just don't get Chemistry! Really tries to help students out.

Dr. Dearden is a very invested teacher. I really enjoyed his class, even though it was pretty tough. If you are very diligent and hard working, you can do fine. He gives you many opportunities to redeem yourself, and a 3X5 card is allowed on all tests. Take from Dearden.
Good teacher, but intense class. Tons of homework, but if you do it, its worth the effort.

Dr. Dearden is an AMAZING teacher! He cares for his students' success and is quick to reply to emails. This class is a lot of work, but if you do all that you're asked to (i.e. assigned readings before lecture, homework, etc) then you will walk out with a solid A. He makes the most-failed class at BYU enjoyable! My best advice: DO NOT FALL BEHIND!

Dr. Dearden is a great guy and does everything he can to make one of BYU's hardest (and most failed) classes enjoyable.  Tests are challenging but his lectures are very helpful and he is always willing to answer questions. I would recommend him for CHEM105

Dearden was awesome! Always willing to help anyone with questions, and I thought his tests were fairly easy. Lots of Hydrogen/Butane balloon explosions which is always fun. Chem 105 was amazing he is a way cool and hilarious guy take it from him if you can!!!

Dr. Dearden is a way good guy and really cares about his students, but I think he makes the course a little more difficult than it needs to be. There is way too much busy work that interferes with your time to actually rehearse the concepts you may not understand. Tests are hard, but what chem test isn't? Just too much hw and way too time consuming

Dr. Dearden is the man! He teaches so well that you understand everything you need to. His tests are a bit hard but if you study well, do all the assignments, micro exams and practice sheets, you'll get a solid A! And he curves the final, plus gives you chance to drop one of your lowest scores in mid terms! TAKE IT! you'll love it!

Dr. Dearden is very good and cares about his students a lot. The class can be quite challenging, especially if you fall behind. However, he is perfect for those going further in chemistry - he will prepare you more than any other professor. I highly recommend-just be prepared to spend 1-2 hours doing something for this class nearly every day.

I do not feel that the class is very organized. Most of the time when I go to my recitation lab, we are given material that has not been covered yet. We jumped around instead of going in some type of order. Science courses require lots of work but having a class thats organized helps. I wish I took it from someone else.

He isn't the most exciting speaker, but he does like to blow things up, which is definitely a plus. He is very helpful and easy to understand. It's pretty easy to fall asleep during a lecture that doesn't involve explosions, but if you read the text, you can easily catch up with the material. Excellent class, very interesting subject matter.

He's funny and spiritual, and his lectures are always clear to me. I love his class and his style of teaching. He's a genuinely nice guy, and its my favorite class of the day. I'd love more of his classes
love him

not that bad of a class.  i enjoyed it a lot.  make sure you understand what he's talking about in lecture, because everythign builds on itself.  i went to his office once, and i think he was having a bad day.. he didn't really help me very much.

Dr. Dearden was a very good teacher and made everything very clear to me.  I don't understand why so many people had a hard time in his class - he provides you with all the information and instruction you need to do well.  I would definitely take another class with Dr. Dearden.

The reason that this class was so hard is because there was an unbelievable work load. A lot of the work didn't really help, but was just time consuming. It was as if he thought this was the only class anybody had. Take it from somebody else.

It's a hard class. It's a good idea to study up and/or get a foundation for the course. Dr.Dearden is a very nice, very helpful teacher. He'll meet with you and do anything he can to help you prepare for his extremely difficult exams. I thought I'd fail, but I stuck through and got a C-. Effort pays off, even if you don't have much experience.

Good teacher, willing to hepl, get a good TA!!! Don't give up after the third Macro exam, the whole class probably did bad. There is a really good curve. Make sure to go to RL's and DR's and do the BR's most of your grade depends on it.

This class has taught me tons but it was not with out lots of work, (as a college class should be.)  The times I went to his office he was very helpful and did not treat me like an idiot.  the lectures are interesting and how many other classes get to blow stuff up?   Make sure you read everything and review and you'll do fine.

This is a hard class that requires a lot of time outside of class if you want to do well.  I didn't do much at all outside of class and was able to pass, but not with a great grade.  He's a  good teacher and is really nice.  He also blows stuff up most days.

i tried to ask him a question in his office once and i kind of felt blown off.  but, that might be because he was having a VERY busy day and frankly didn't have the time to answer my question.  he made a hilarious joke once about how his daughter is a sophomore at BYU and doesn't want to date because she thinks that all RM's want to get married.

He's a pretty good professor. Nice Guy. Funny. Good Explosions. He teaches well, but Chem 105 is a beast, you need to put in the time on your own. If you work hard you'll do okay. Or you might fail. Keep in mind its possible to study and still get an F. Micro Exams are a great tool if you use them.

Way tough but worth it.  I learned a bunch.  Explosions are his forte but he's willing to answer questions too.  His tests are tricky but at least his weekly micro-exams (which you can retake as many times as you want) prepare you if you put effort into them. A few things could have been explained better but I enjoyed chem 105 from dearden.

He is a very nice guy, but I wasn't a fan of his lectures.His lecture slides were always confusing, and usually put slides up there that we didn't even need to know.(In that case, as if anyone cares).You learn the most in recitation, and on your online homework by yourself.  His tests are killer.  Very hard class, but he's a nice guy,approachable

Dr. Dearden is an excellent professor. Chem 105 is a hard class no matter who you take it from but dearden gives you the best shot at an A. He was always helpful with questions and wanted you to succeed. Take 105 from Dearden.
He is a great guy, but makes it tough, but all chemistry classes are tough. You have to study hard for the tests, and some questions aren't the best, but overall I learned a lot from him.

Dr. Dearden overall is a good guy. He has sense of humor which is nice. But he just didn't do too well at teaching chemistry. He tries, there is no doubt about that, but he is very fuzzy and does not teach that well. He does make lectures interesting, however, by blowing stuff up whenever possible. If you are ok learning stuff on your own take him.
He has good lectures. He blows everything up and likes to joke around. He's my favorite science teacher I've ever had.
He is a hard teacher. Sometimes his slides are a little confusing. you do have to study a lot for the test.But overall his nice.
PLEASE take PS100 from Dr. Dearden. He is the only choice, really.

He took over after Prof. Jones was given leave and I am very grateful.  I really enjoyed his class.  He likes to blow stuff up.  Tries to answer as many questions as possible.  I went to the TAs after the lab the first few times and that helped a lot with understanding details.  Not too bad of a class.  I learned a lot about how the earth works.
Dr. Dearden was clear and pleasant.  He is willing to give you help and answer questions.  He also included gospel topics.
Dr. Dearden is entertaining and fun. He really likes to blow stuff up!

he was a wondeful teacher and made sitting through lectures, and learning about physical science really interesting! He explained things very well, and his power points gave us all the important information for the tests. Go to class to take the quizzes, and study hard for the tests. Know how to apply the different concepts to situations rather then memorizing them. Overall, i really enjoyed his teaching style, and the fact that he liked to blow things up.

boring class, but that's not his fault. tests are hard, but that's not his fault either. lectures are pretty interesting (and that's coming from someone who loathes this subject). definitely the best professor to take this class from.
He is a really cool teacher.  He loves to blow stuff up.  The main thing is to review the lecture slides a lot-before and after class.
cool

Nice man, he brings in church stuff a lot. He is not the easiest man to follow and you better read the book or don't bother going to class. The department makes the tests and he does't have anything to do with them. Lab is where you will get your answers. There is a quiz every day of class so you can't skip.This isn't easy and you better take notes
This class was full of good information but I ended up going just for the attendance point. I enjoyed the lectures, but got more out of taking notes from the text.  The tests were very specific.

His tests were crazy hard. If you think about each question then it really isn't to bad. He blows stuff up every lecture. You have to have a good TA or you'll be in trouble. Just learn the material extremley well.

Deardon is an excellent teacher; he sets lectures up on blackboard.  If you want to do well, go over the lecture for the day before class, if possible, a week in advance.  He is always there to help...be sure to get a good TA, and if you can, go to different recitations; each seem to teach differently.  If possible, take 101 with it.  (know vocab)

Dearden is an excellent professor.  He knows the subject well and really cares about his students' education.  He is willing to help outside of class and grades very nicely.  The tests are hard (but that is true for all chem 105 tests).

Dearden is really helpfull as far as the students are concerned.  He's not one of those professors who say, basically, sink or swim.  He tries to give you a chance to exceed in a really hard subject.  His tests are killer, but if everyone sucks he'll drop the C+ cutoff point.  try to get a good TA.

This was a very hard class. Each test was harder than the one before it. However the grading curve was more than fair. A good TA really helps and a lot of resources are available if you need help. Professor Dearden was a good professor, the lectures were mostly good and his demonstrations were fun, lots of explosions.
Not too hard of a prof. just a hard class

Chemistry is hard. His tests are also hard, but he curves them major so you end up getting a good grade on them anyways. He likes to blow up balloons full of explosive gases in class. A way nice guy too.

Let's face it, Chemistry is HARD!  Even with this fact I'm able to enjoy Chemistry because of Dearden.  He cares about his students and tries to be fair.  A lot of your grade depends on the tests which kind of stinks, but everyone does so bad that he usually grades it on some sort of a curve so don't freak out if you get a bad grade on a test.

As far as Chem 105 goes, he is probably the easiest professor, it's not an easy subject. There is very little petty memorization of tables etc. it's all provided on the tests.  He usually can't finish lectures because there's so much info. But, go to recitation and study sessions and you should do fine. A good TA is very helpful!

Class is basically just the readings in more depth, but some were really good. He's very nice and sweet, and he has a lot of research articles on the topic so he does know his stuff. You have to show up to class. I got a B because I struggled to do so, lol.

Honestly not my favorite class I've taken but it was fine. Attendance is mandatory and if you go to class you can get an A. Class was often boring but he's the sweetest professor. I would take a class from him again because it was easy.

While lectures are essentially just the reading in greater depth,Dr. Dollahite really cares about his students. Super easy to get a good grade in his class; just do the readings and fill out the study guide as you go. While every lecture may not be the most interesting, you'll at least have a couple that will speak to you.

You have to go to class because of self-graded participation! Basically a religion class, incredibly uplifting. Class work is very easy. Fill out out the study guides while doing the reading assignments and it'll make your life easier for the midterm and final!

He's a nice guy and knows his stuff. Quizzes are open book/notes, tests he allows some notes - so it's pretty easy. Attendance/participation are HUGE - I missed a few classes which is why I didn't get an A. His classes could be pretty dry as he mainly reads from his powerpoints and that material is all from the readings. So do the readings.

It seems like things make sense until you take the test. His powerpoints are kind of all over the place and he goes off topic for about half the class, so if you don't take good notes, you're in trouble. He's super awesome and caring. Tons of readings. about 5 little papers and a big project that's pretty cool.

Dr. Dollahite is good at making the class feel meaningful and lead to personal growth and application. Lots of readings and a reading application paper due each class (not that bad). Can use 3-pg of notes on midterm and final. Final project meant mainly for your application. Really, the syllabus is the worst part of the class. Highly recommend it!
I really loved his class. The first week I was nervous by the amount of work but if you stay up to date and go to class you will do just fine. He has been one of my favorite professors so far at BYU.

Professor Dollahite is very passionate but sometimes he goes on for a long time and it can get very boring. The papers are easy but the tests are a lot harder and sometimes include things that we didn't even seem to talk about or he did not get to in time to actually let us know what the answer would be.

Bro Dollahite is a great professor! He really has studied a lot about a lot of religions and the things he taught really opened my eyes. He relates so many truths found in other religions to our own which is super cool. You can feel his passion that he has for religion and for the good it brings to families. The lots of reading is worth it!

Take it from someone else. This class was so boring. Instead of talking about family processes. We talked about his opinion of religion the entire time. Attendance is required, but I got nothing out of class every time. All of the readings and textbooks are written by him. So basically everything in this class are his thoughts on religion.

He wrote the textbook. The textbook is best part of the class. He thinks he can rely on how awesome he is and how great his life has been in order to pass his knowledge onto us but he's super boring and not a very good teacher because he just stands up there and talks about his life the whole time. Take this class but take it from someone else.

His lectures are fairly boring. He rarely allows for discussion with the class. He just likes to talk. I learned some worth while things from this course but I often wish I had taken it from another professor. I wouldn't take a class form him again.

I've taken a few classes from Dr. Dollahite & would recommend him. His teaching style and grading style are very clear cut and straightforward. Some might think his lecture's could be a little dry since he mainly goes off slides, but I found them entertaining! He tells good stories and is very open and willing to take time for you. Recommended.

Dr. Dollahite is an excellent professor.  He obviously cares about the things he is teaching and wants to help his students to be better prepared for familial roles.  His lectures are definitely not discussion based and he can go on semi-irrelevant tangents sometimes.  Good stories, though!   Textbook is also amazing, to say the least!!

If you have even the tiniest inkling of non-conservative sensibilities, his opinions Will definitely rub you the wrong way. A couple times he even preached things unsupported by church doctrine and flat-out contrary to scholarly research. Class is ridiculously easy but attendance and reading are mandatory.
Dr. Dollahite is really passionate. It's a good class. Make sure to keep track of your assignments due though. You aren't really reminded of them in class. Great class

Really cool professor. He's a great guy. Attendance and reading are necessary and worth points. Quite a few papers but they're not bad. Lets you use notes on ALL the tests! Even the final! I recommend taking this class - very interesting and learned a lot.
Tons of busy work!!! As a professor he is okay, but he expects WAY to much for a 100 level course. There are tons of papers to write and a bunch of pointless assignments!
Only thing to do with the book was the quizzes due every Monday. Beyond that he went into depth on the topics we read about. Only thing on tests was what was on the quizzes. Pretty simple. Nice guy.
He made everything clear and helped me get a much better grade than I expected. He's the reason I chose my major.
LOVED this class!  Learned so much about "friends of other faiths" and found new respect for them.  He has a true love for what he teaches and helps you to find that same love.  Such a great teacher!

Pretty good professor. All of his slides and material are on Blackboard. This course is really student-friendly. (It was basically made by students). The reading can get intensive, but its relevant. Even enjoyed writing some of the papers. The tests are on Blackboard. Approachable and enjoys class participation. I would take him again.

Dr. Dollahite is an amazing teacher. LOVED this class & learned so much. Keep up with reading & attend class & you can easily get an A. I wish he taught all of the SFL classes. More should follow up dedication and teaching style.

This is a very easy class.  The professor is THE most boring and conceded person I have met.  You'll get an A- quizzes and tests are easy: based entirely off the Eternal Marriage book.  But expect the most boring lectures of your life (luckily he doesn't test on whats in the lectures, just takes roll.)  Bring homework from another class.

Such a good and interesting class! Brother Dollahite is good at teaching this subject! A lot of papers and final project but he explains it all so it's clear on what to expect. The papers are opinion based so they're easy. I would recommend this class to everyone!!!
Amazing class. I never thought I would enjoy it as much as I am. I like am not a super studios student but I managed to do pretty well. Such a good teacher and such interesting materials. LOVED IT!

If the point of this class was learning all about HIS family, he succeeded. However, I feel like a creepy stalker because of what I know. Bro. Dollahite is a nice enough guy, and he is passionate about the subject, but he did not teach very well. Tests were poorly written and some questions were very random. TA not helpful either. Hard grader.

Very nice guy, kind of tries to be cool.  Has incredibly long lectures, and he can talk the entire time.  The material is great and you get some insight from discussion, but his opinions aren't solid. He tends to jump all over the place with his lectures and explanations to please everyone. Good class, but can't wait for it to be over.

I was surprised how much I enjoyed learning about other religions. The reading isn't terrible (especially in a normal semester I'd imagine). Very rewarding final project and open book/notes midterm and final on blackboard. It's a great class, I took it for filler credits and really enjoyed it. The work load isn't terrible. Fairly easy.

Dr. Dollahite really cares about what he is teaching which helps make the class more interesting.  However, it can get boring and be long sometimes.  It just depends on how interested you are in the material.  If you love studying this stuff, then you will love the class and do well.  Be prepared for a lot of reading, but open book exams!  Yay!
Bro. Dollahite is really chill and his class is very informative. Sometimes class lasts a little long when its late and you're tired but definately worth your time!

You really have to love Bro. Dollahite after taking his class.  He loves talking about religion and his own stories and can be entertaining at times.  The material is interesting and it is super easy to get an A.  The papers are just thought papers and the tests were open book on Blackboard...also very easy.  The final project is fun and rewarding.

Bro Dollahite was a great teacher. This class is easy to get an A and you learn more from it than other harder classes. Very interesting material, I would highly recommend it to anyone. There are 5 easy 1 page papers and the final project of your choice (takes 10-20 hours)is very rewarding.
Great teacher, very interesting, funny.  Offers a lot of mercy for attendance.
Brother Dollahite makes the class very interesting and applicable. He isn't too hard and puts forth a lot of effort to make the material understandable.
Be prepared for 5 (2 page)papers and a presentation, but the tests are take-home and not too hard. He is a cool guy that is really interested in the subject.

Great teacher, and funny. I met great people and learned so much. But beware of trick questions and mistakes on the tests. Also, some of the study guides really don't help at all, so if there are questions on the test that weren't mention before, ask about them and he will probably change your grade.

the lectures are incredibly long, especially if you have them right after lunch. But the text is good and the class discussions are really helpful. I wouldn't call it an easy A, but it's well worth it.

Really nice guy and great material but the hour and a half class was disturbingly boring for me. The class was just too large and too long for my tastes. I wound up skipping a lot since you could with little or no penalty.
Great teacher! Really enjoyed his class! Would take him again
Uses powerpoint, but fun and interesting anyway.  Uses personal examples.  Slides available online, so you don't have to take many notes.

Responds well to feedback.  Has students fill out likes/dislikes/suggestion sheet and adjusts teaching accordingly.  Very good class, one of the few where I'm keeping the textbook for later reference.

Don't remember what class; (sociolinguistics?) it was 23 years ago. Don't think I ever even talked with him outside of class (didn't do that back then). As I'm thinking of the professors whose approaches to life had the most impact on me, he's at the top. He used his discipline to see and celebrate humans in all their beauty. Thoughtful, good man.

He's a very kind and understanding professor, and he's available outside of class. That said, he doesn't teach clearly. This due in part to unfamiliarity with the tools he demos. He can do good research, but I wish I had just done the hw for his class but attended another proffessor's lectures.  :(

Professor Eddington is a good researcher, but a bit disorganized as a Professor. He didn't really have a study guide for exams and doesn't use learningsuite which is inconvenient. Overall his lectures are interesting, and homework is just a completion grade, but its hard to study for tests.

Pro: 
- You'll be hard-pressed to find a more enthusiastic researcher. He really knows how to research.
- He was lenient about grading.
- He gives you a good survey of applicable linguistic tools.

Cons:
- He doesn't lecture very well; thoughts are sporadic and confusing.
- He doesn't know all the tools he shows; lots of self-teaching.

He knows his stuff and knows how to convey it well, but the classes weren't very interactive. Mostly just him talking. Maybe it's because it was an online class and he's used to in-person. He definitely struggled a lot with the tech stuff like sharing his screen correctly. Grades come from mostly just tests, and the test content comes from lecture.

Professor Eddington is a really nice guy and funny, but I didn't enjoy his class much. Lecture was often confusing and he was all over the place. The tests were hard, as he would give study guides that covered a huge range of topics, but then the test would only have a few problems. So you mess up once and get a bad grade. TA's grade tough on hw.

His lectures were somewhat helpful but your grades are made up of homework and tests only. His tests were a bit challenging and he could have done a lot more to help us prepare for the tests. Also, he wasn't very great at answering questions. Probably best to talk to him in person and get to know him cuz he'll probably help you out more that way.

Not sure if I got a B+ or A-. Either way, the class material wasn't hard. What was hard though was the structure of his tests. Not a lot of content on the exams so if you miss just a few points, your grade tanks a lot. As a professor, Dr. Eddington was friendly and I met with him about concerns prior to an exam and he was very personable!

Did not get anything out of his lectures. He's a nice professor, but he is not easily accessible and his tests are arbitrary and ambiguous. Also don't expect to get help from the professor or the TA regarding homework assignments, just try your best to guess what they're thinking.

He wasn't always prepared for his lectures and blew through his powerpoints. The powerpoints weren't available for us to see outside of class, so it was hard to review information for tests. The tests were very specific and I didn't feel very prepared for them.

Avoid taking classes from him at all costs. Class was a joke, we did nothing every single day. He would assign homework that students had no idea how to do and then take off if class got out early, while all the STUDENTS stayed to try and figure it out together. Doesnt prepare you at all for his exams. Once again AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

The amount of tiny homework assignments was ridiculous. There is SO much busy work in this class on top of a final paper. Class is boring and usually Dr. Eddington wasted time over-explaining random things, but not explaining the material our homework would be on. He's an aloof and unorganized prof.

I don't even know why I bothered attending class. He is unorganized making it hard to know what you'll be tested on. Most days we just watched videos that did not help at all. He is extremely picky on phonetics and transcriptions. Above all else he doesn't try to connect to his students and isn't very approachable.

Dr. Eddington is a sporadic and unorganized lecturer, but more than that he is extremely disinterested in his students and not very helpful if you have questions on the homework. It's his way or the highway.
He was not very open for questions and helping students.

Professor Eddington is a decent professor, not to difficult or anything, but my main problem is that he scheduled the final for a Saturday and there was a conflict. He said university policy wouldn't allow me to take it another time, which makes no sense because I've seen other professors allow it. Without the final I probably won't pass the class.
Very unorganized teacher. Tests are difficult to prepare for.

Straightforward and clearly to the point. I approached him with a huge problem and he did a complete statistical analysis with me. He is a good guy and a good professor. No flair, no flash, just lecture and logic. Take classes from him.

Professor E is great! His class is simple and too the point, tests are written response and not tricky at all. There's really nothing to be confused about. If he has any flaws, it's that he's a bit clumsy and he confuses himself sometimes. It's more funny than anything.

Professor Eddington clearly expects you to be a mature student. Take notes on anything he puts on the board, and any terminology he goes over.  Make sure you have an example for every concept you've learned. Professor Eddington can come across as disinterested toward students, but he is very fair. Be a mature student and you'll have no problem.

I would not recommend taking any classes from Professor Eddington. He makes the subject matter more difficult than it needs to be, is not helpful or approachable in any way, and is the type of teacher who doesn't care whether material is clear or not. It's actually kind of funny that he teaches, because he  doesn't really enjoy students.

So not helpful. Half of the time came not prepared for class. Rushes through the info and does not put up the slides online yet does not give time to copy the info in class. Homework and tests are not too bad but he does not accommodate for the students. If you are not in class and homework is due you can not leave it in his box or email it to him. Thus, he takes 10 points off your grade ( out of 50 ). Did not like him at all

One of the best professors around because he doesn't care if you do the busy work or not. If you just learn what you're supposed to and tell him, he'll give you A's on the homeworks without even doing them. Just study the reviews he gives out

Class was too easy, but gave you a good history of the theories in morphology and phonology. We did a lot of problem sets in class, which he gave too much time for. Good teacher, I think the curriculum just needs to cover more (this might just be a department issue?). I felt like this class was more theory/history. Problem sets were mostly basic.

Like others have stated, he's not very approachable. He introduced complex subjects with research papers. I honestly would have preferred a textbook. I understand other languages better than the papers he assigns. He honestly made me lost all interest in morphology and linguistics in general.
Was not a bad teacher, but one of the coldest, least approachable professor I have ever had.  But if that doesn't bother you, he teaches the material, you learn it and you move on with your life.

This professor was kind of so-so.  I'm pretty much impartial. Not a bad teacher.  Not a bad guy.  But it's not as though he changed my life.  Kind of just, I learned the material well enough and moved on.
He was a nice teacher and you could tell he cares about the subject, but I often felt like he was not very approachable or tolerant of questions. I would not take another class from him.

and LING 330, and LING 427, were all great classes to take from him.  He knows his stuff and loves it.  He's funny and helpful.  Homework is very doable, and tests are pretty easy.  I loved the class structure and highly recommend taking any LING class from him.

Eddington is great. Very nice and reasonable- but still expects quality work. 273 is very basic and essentially teaches you how to do a wide variety of empirical studies. Homework usually simple. There is one paper- don't procrastinate. Take home final- quite involved with what you learned in class. It took me 5-6 hours to do a good, thorough job.

Great teacher. I was confused at first about his teaching style. He goes off on lots of tangents (usually completely not related) but he is a very understanding teacher. He is willing to help with whatever he can. There is no textbook - everything you need to know is on the website. The final is take-home and SO easy. It's a pretty easy A.

I had a hard time paying attention bacause he often went on tangents and let the class take over sometimes on off-topic subjects . . . he is very enthusiastic about the subject though and is very willing to help you out one-on-one if you need extra help.

He was so hard to follow in his lectures.  He would go off on tangents all the time and rarely stuck to the things he would test on.  He's a nice guy, but his tests are all essay questions and if you don't put exactly what he wants, he takes off all of your points.  He's a nice guy, though.
Loved his class, teaching style and personality. This class was not too hard, but very interesting. Great class discussions. A real human professor.
Loved the ties. He is easily distracted, but not boring. Not incredibly knowledgable about all the subject matter, but pretty good in general.

Great teacher. He really loves his students and what he teaches. He sometimes lets the class take too much control over the discussion though. I feel like the class wasn't stressful AND that I learned a lot. Thumbs up.

He's a great teacher.  His tests are way easy and he gives great study guides for them.  We don't learn a ton in class because he's a little random, you just have to do all the reading.  He loves what he teaches and is always available to help.  The homework is easy you just have to keep up with it.  Interesting class.

Eddington is a nice guy, passionate about what he teaches. I loved him in 340 but not so much for 450.  I haven't attended class more than twice this month and I'm getting an A- mostly, I'm not learning anything. And the assignment in Campbell are assanine. But Eddingtons a great guy.

Great style... in teaching AND appearance. There's a lot of reading, and the study guides are a pain, but the tests are a cinch. Just pay attention and you'll do fine. He won't take your crap--that's why I like him.

GREAT class! I wasn't excited about it before it started, but once I started the class, I loved it! Historical-Comparative Linguistics is now one of my favorite classes I've taken. :) Also--He always reads a bit of trivia at the beginning of class--FUN!
Great class, great teacher. Prof. Eddington was enjoyable and flexible. The tests were pretty easy... a lot of busy work, but it doens't end up counting for much.
Great class for those wanting to be introduced to linguistics. Eddington is fun and knowledgable. There is some busy work, but overall the class was easy.
Amazing teacher, definitely take this class from him

Davey is a great professor, and you can tell that he really cares about his students. He doesn't want the literature review to be too overwhelming and breaks it into chunks so it feels more manageable. He is very understanding and willing to work with you if you need more time or help. Highly recommend taking this class with him!

By far one of my favorite professors at BYU, Davey made this class such a breeze. I had never written a review paper before this class but Davey helped break it up into chunks which made the whole process so much easier. I would highly recommend taking PSYCH 307 with him!!

I loved professor Erekson's class! I have never rated any of my past professors but had to express my feedback for him because of how well he taught this class. Doing a large research paper could seem overwhelming, but he made it seem simple with the examples and humor he used during lecture. He gives good feedback and teaches concepts clearly!

If you need to take Psych 307, I would suggest 100% taking it from Davey. He is so kind and personable. This class is not easy, but he makes it a lot more bearable. He is very good at teaching it. Highly suggest!

Easily one of my favorite professors at BYU! Coming into PSYCH 307, I was super intimidated by the writing process and how I would take it on. However, Davey was extremely helpful and laid out the process very clearly, and kept us motivated with inspiring content in the lectures. He was also available outside of class, which was huge for me.

He is a super nice guy but I felt frustrated with him because it he wasted my time in class. He spent too much time introducing us to the paper and not enough time telling us what to write and then giving us time to write and revise in class. I ended up not going most the time and wrote the whole review on my own.

Just trust me and take him. He is awesome and the class is easy. The textbook you can get at the library so you don't need to pay money. I don't even know if my attendance was mandatory, I just loved coming to class because he was so funny. This is from a guy who hasn't been to half his classes the whole semester.

Davey is the most kind, thoughtful, and loving prof I've ever had. He is very responsive to the needs of the students and he helped us explore our minds and look at compassion in a new way. highly recommend if you need a break in your schedule to mentally and emotionally recharge.

Davey is awesome, this class was a very good class that leveled out my more rigorous ones. Yes there is assignment but he's very understanding and big on not making your life difficult. I do recommend you do the readings if you want to take something from the class because in class he basically sums up or gives explanation for the readings.

Dr. Erekson was by far the best professor I have had at BYU!! He clearly cares about his students and is willing to help. The way the class was set up made it manageable even though the literature review was overwhelming at times. His lectures were engaging and he used a variety of methods to teach. Highly recommend!!

Professor Erekson helped me not only get through the class, but actually become a better reader, writer, and researcher. He teaches skills you'll use throughout the rest of your college career. He  made the class very entertaining and didn't waste my time at all. I would recommend him to students of all writing levels! Very caring and charismatic.

I was dreading taking this course, but having Professor Erekson made ALL the difference! This was my favorite class I took all semester because of how engaging his lecturing style was. I learned a lot and enjoyed doing it. I also really appreciated the way he structured our literature review assignment into smaller, more manageable sections.

This is the best PSYCH307 class. Don't bother taking anyone else. Davey is super awesome all around. The class is designed extremely well, the entire class is geared towards your final project, your literature review. It's guided learning the whole way through, and then the training wheels come off at the end. I very very very highly recommend him.

Davey is an awesome professor! He takes the time to go through important parts of writing, and really wants you to succeed. He also makes class engaging and fun, and isn't too tough with grading. I would definitely recommend a class with him!

I LOVE THIS CLASS! I am even feeling sad about finishing the class. He made me feel like writing/publishing a paper is doable. He cares about all his students. One assignment/week with a simple final exam. The average score in class was like 94. You get to publish your paper and put your poster on your CV. Our TA was also the best TA I ever met!

Davey changed my life. My spouse and mom noticed a change in me due to this class. I needed this class and Davey made it available and possible. This class is designed to serve you, it is powerful. It can show you why life is worth living. It is made to better you, and it works. I could take this class 17 times and it wouldn't be enough. Take it.

Davey is a solid professor. He wants you to succeed in his class, and his assignments are pretty easy because he walks you through some of them. He was super nice about grading, and helped me pass the class. I felt all the assignments were super useful. Really learned how to use APA.

Davey is the best. He is an amazing writing professor in that he teaches you the basics (grammar, scientific voice, APA style) and then guides you through your personalized research paper. You get to really explore what YOU are interested in and he does an amazing job of making writing fun and interesting. I learned so much from him!!! Incredible!
Professor Erekson is very passionate about what he does and a very caring guy. He was also a fair grader and my class didn't have a lot of work.

This isn't meant to be a hard class, and it definitely isn't. Davey is brilliant and helps you go through the process of choosing a major and career direction for those of us who have a hard time with that kind of thing. He's super funny and always reachable outside of class. You will have to work in the class, but it's not too bad.
Davey is a great teacher for career exploration! He is a psychologist so he does know his stuff. I'm glad I got him as my professor!!

Dr. Erickson has a bad rep and I completely understand why. It's a one credit undergrad class, but do not be fooled... he will grade and question you as if you are PhD student. He comes off rather aggressive and abrasive, he will not hesitate to belittle you in front of the class. I would definitely avoid him if possible, save yourself the grief.

This professor I believe is the anti christ. He is everything wrong with every bad professor you have ever met in a person. I don't understand how he's married considering how bad of a person he is. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

This is a hard class and getting an A would be really hard. That being said, his lectures are amazing and the way that the class is structured is geared towards actually learning and applying the material. I think it is one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at BYU. Weekly writing assignments are hard, but he'll help you if you ask.

Taking Bacterial Pathogenesis from Dr. Erickson is a gargantuan mistake. I personally enjoyed Dr. Erickson's lecture style, but the way he organizes and grades his class is atrocious. Do not take this class if your GPA is important for your future. The class is virtually impossible to get a good grade in, and the professor doesn't care.

The highest score in the class is an 86 percent. Only one person has gotten 100 percent on any of the HW assignments. He expects you to understand the textbook, with participation being graded on him randomly calling on you to teach his slides. If you want a good grade, steer clear.

Worst professor ever! I asked for accommodations for my baby and all he did was suggest that I find a babysitter. I have never had a professor at BYU that was so full of himself that he didn't care about his student's success.

A LOT of memorizing for only a 200 level...tests were very hard, what you need to know is unclear, 2 different & confusing rubrics for the paper that you had to pass to pass the class (but only worth a small amount of your actual grade) does not give any explanation for lost points on digital dialogues, not friendly, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM

Everything on this site about this guy is true. Great researcher, seems nice enough, but is unclear while teaching and tests are extremely specific. Probably makes this course harder than it needs to be. If you're trying for MMBIO 261 and see that Erickson is the only prof teaching it, wait to take it until next semester: he and Poole take turns.

Take the negative reviews with a grain of salt. Dr. Erickson's class is all about teaching you be a better scientist and critical thinker. As such, his class is no walk-in-the-park. If research interests you or you want to be a better problem solver, take this class. You'll grow and learn a lot! If you want an easy A, you best find another class.

His lectures have nothing to do with the tests or the three papers he assigns during the semester. The class is entirely graded on being able to read scientific papers and then respond to them and he teaches you NOTHING about doing that. He is condescending and makes you feel dumb when asking questions if you don't know your stuff. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. This is my last semester and I considered dropping out every day before class. 

Tests are most of your grade and are doctorate-level essay questions that he grades ridiculously hard. The test questions are insanely specific and if you don't read his mind and say exactly what he would say, he'll fail you.

Professor Erickson is nice as a person but made the class unnecessarily hard. I heard this class was supposed to be pretty easy but taking it from him was the biggest mistake. He assumes you already have a high level understanding of chemistry and microbiology even though this class is a pre requisite for many higher level classes.

Unclear! Vaccine writing assignment only asked for "peer-reviewed scientific sources" but his grading criteria which were not connected to the assignment at all but just in a random spot on learning suite specified "primary research" sources. He clarified this during the only class period I ever missed and by the time I found out it was too late.

If you like professors who don't care about students, refuse to communicate, fail to give clear instructions on anything, and just the worst, this is the class for you! He is always disagreeable. All I have from his class are horror stories. DO NOT DO IT. I don't know how he manages to not get fired.

This class is a mixed bag. It is an incredibly hard class with Dr. Erikson. This should be a 400-level science class. For a sophmore class, it is insane on the amount of information needed to do well. He let us pick our grades. Which is amazing and a godsend. I don't think he will do that in the future, but he normally puts the 'A' cutoff 91%.

A nice enough guy, but the class is terrible. The books we read were interesting for sure, but there's just too much work for a 1-credit class. Two group presentations and a book review make up pretty much your whole grade and the rubrics are extremely vague. If this class is required for you, good luck.

He assigned a paper with two different rubrics and criteria for two categories of students. If you were vaccinated, the paper was a piece of cake. If you were unvaccinated the paper was required to be longer and would be graded more strictly. After the school got involved, he retracted the assignment, but take from that what you will!

Dr. Erickson was a fun man! The course could be boring at times but he often did things to make class engaging. He does not deserve to have such a low rating. He also let people choose their own grade in the course. He really wanted people to learn in a safe space. He also addressed current problems like COVID vaccines and lack of women faculty.

Don't take it. He wants you to think exactly as he does, but it's impossible to figure that out. Belittling comments in essays and group meetings. You have to give presentations, and feedback will include things like "didn't answer questions not listed on rubric". IMPOSSIBLE TO COMMUNICATE WITH. AVOID!!!!!!

Its unfortunate that hes usually the only one to teach this course. He practically sets you up for failure with his vague expectations and then rips you in grading for not being able to read his mind. Your grade is heavily influenced by competence of your classmates, so choose your group wisely.
Do not take this class. He gives awful feedback and always felt belittled after meeting with him. Not worth the stress.

Perhaps it was just an online struggle, but Dr. Erickson's class was tough. I remember thinking I had the course material down and being confident in the tests and essays and always being disappointed with my grades. His class definitely takes a lot of time and effort to succeed, but I wouldn't say it's impossible. Be willing to go the extra mile.
Not personable. I did not enjoy this class at all, he grades paper so harshly with feedback that doesn't make sense. Do not take his classes.
Class content was incredibly specific. Exams were very difficult. Made me switch me switch my major.

FOR THE LOVE OF ALL THAT IS GOOD IN THIS WORLD AND ABOVE DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN'S CLASS. Unless you are already on a doctorate-level knowledge base, be prepared to get dumped on with pure information, and then be tested on like 6% but super specifically. He gives extremely vague test review questions. Really makes you consider dropping out.

Professor Erickson is extremely vague in his grading criteria and is vague in what to study for exams. He is not very helpful in how to better prepare for his class. His class is very interesting, but you have to work excessively hard to get a good grade in his class.

I felt very disrespected and didn't feel like he cared about my learning. His grading was very nitpicky, especially for a 1 credit class. I lost 2% of my grade for being 5 minutes late to class one day. For the final book review, he gave us a rubric and a student example in which he dissected all of the errors as if to scare us into writing well.

His class is straightforward. Quizzes in small groups, research paper, and tests. You dont need a book- even if someone says you do. Everything is on the slides. The lectures are somewhat dry, and tests are super hard. He does have lower grade cutoffs to compensate for it though. Average quality class

Nice guy, but kinda nitpicky with grading. That's frustrating since he doesn't give you a lot of guidance as far as what he wants to begin with. Some of the books he lets you pick from to read are okay, others are long, tedious reads. Not really what I would describe as an enjoyable class. If you get lazy groups for your projects, good luck.
He has you write 3 papers which he grades poorly. His tests average almost an F and its just not a good class. I do not recommend taking him

For this class you have a couple meetings with Dr. Erickson. Through the meetings you find that he is very degrading and rude. He expects very specific papers and presentations but leaves you with little instructions. Tough grading mixed with no instructions makes this class very frustrating. To top it off Dr. Erickson makes you feel unintelligent.

For a 300 level course, the amount of time you spend is almost insane (I am a graduating senior). His lectures are really interesting and he knows everything there is to know about microbiology, which is really cool. His grade scale is very low compared to regular (helpful), but you still need to put in tons of time if you want a decent grade.

Dr. Erickson is the man. His class is a lot of work, but at heart he wants you to succeed. He's always willing to help out and is very kind, sort of like Dumbledore minus the hair and beard. Overall, a great man with a ton of knowledge about Microbiology. I highly recommend taking this class from him.

Dr. Erickson is a good professor and he really does love the subject he teaches. I just thought it was unnecessarily hard. He would give us a study guide and promise us that if we studied that, we would be good on the test so we would study well and walk into the test feeling confident and leave feeling like we knew nothing. very discouraging.
He is not very good at explaining assignments. He is not very helpful and comes off slightly rude. Definitely not a people person.

Dr. Erickson knows his subject, but his attitude belongs in a laboratory, not a classroom. He expected us to know as much as he did even though for most of us, this was our first experience with microbiology. I felt disrespected and like he didn't really want anyone to succeed; he just wanted to prove how smart he was.

Dr. Erickson is always willing to help and wants to help you get an A from his class. He automatically curved the class and the average before the final was  just shy of an A-. He wants to help you really learn the information and can be pretty funny as long as you come prepared for his class. Expect to learn a much as you ever have in his class.

Dr. Erickson has a very unique teaching style where he expects you to do work outside of class to learn the material and come and discuss and teach one another in class. If you try to do this, you will learn more revelant information in this class for a career than any other class you will take. Also Dr. E. is always available to help and wants to.
