This class was hard. The material was super interesting and learning was enjoyable. However, he is very picky and gets caught on details. There's a quiz about every week on the readings. He is not super clear on what he wants you to know, which can be frustrating. He grades on a curve which helps.

This class was definitely a lot more work than I was expecting it to be, but I still enjoyed it! I thought it was really interesting and probably my favorite class this semester. It even made me want to change majors. It does require a ton of reading and memorizing, so if you don't think it's interesting, it would probably be hard to do well.

It says you don't need any prerequisites but you will suffer if you haven't taken any biology. Vey disorganized and goes theough the slides too quickly. I wish we didn't do disease of the day and instead spent time on basic principals. Skipped the learns cycle which doesn't make any sense. I'm probably going to withdraw.

Probably a nice guy, but as a teacher he isn't great. Speeds through slides and then tests heavily, regardless of how well he taught it. Lab was unorganized, lots of busy work. The course material was interesting and the class could have been great, but I'd recommend taking a different upper division elective both for your GPA and sanity.

He is by far the worst teacher that I've ever had. don't take him if you can get out of it. He doesn't respond to emails, doesn't teach what you are required to know but expects you to read it, do research about it to understand it, and understand it completely in order to apply it on tests. I did ok in the class but he is the worst teacher ever.

Lectures were more complicated than they need to be. He is very intimidating and not very warm. The exams are difficult; the material is extremely specific. There are quizzes every week (the whole class bombed the first two so he made them group quizzes), and there's a group project (very lengthy and intense). Expect to WORK if you want an A- or A.
He had very long lectures that tended to drag on. He wasn't a very "nice" guy. There is a big group project that takes a lot of work. If you work hard to study you should be able to do fine.

Learning objectives are given but aren't helpful at all, so you must take extremely good notes and memorize all slides for tests. Schedule is not clearly defined, sometimes lab procedure are poorly written. Overall, it's manageable, but I'd try to take microbial genetics or ecology instead for the microbiology major so you can take a better prof

This was a hard class. It seems like you will fail all semester until the end, he is fair.  You have to teach yourself from the book because you only get a little clarity from his powerpoints. Use the learning objectives and just find those when you study and read.  2 quizzes weekly online. He loves what he does but he isn't the best teacher.

Erickson is an extremely inconsistent professor. It's difficult to know what he wants from you. I basically taught myself by studying the textbook on my own. Micro is far from the hardest class at BYU and if you end with him you will survive; however, he makes it more difficult than it should be. I strongly recommend another professor.

DON'T TAKE HIM! He puts you on the stop alot and he expect you to know and learn everything on your own. He does lectures but it's more of pic. on the slide and he talks about it. Over all just do not take him. His test are highly detailed and about small things not princles and sometimes of things we didn't even learn.

If you enjoy reading textbooks and teachin yourself, then take this class from Erickson. He's nice and says he's there to coach you but the class is HARD. Our first hw had OChem on it, the TA helped me but even he got stuff wrong. I would highly recommend you take this class from someone else.You teach yourself by reading then go for help if needed

Very difficult class. You never know what to expect from Erickson-- extremely inconsistent as to his expectations. May say one thing but base grades on somthing completely different. Tests are unreasonable. One good thing is that he is a great lecturer. I learned lots in class.
Definitely NOT as hard as people say he is. You have to do all the reading, study hard, and do the extra credit, but I got an A. If you get less than a B, it is simply due to lack of effort.

Unnecessarily hard class. He rarely outlines exactly what he wants but grades you very hard. Expect presentations, project proposals, lots of unguided lab work, hard quizzes and tests, and a long research paper. Great guy but I would have enjoyed the class more if it was formatted differently.

I've seen that a lot of the comments for his MMBIO221 class say he's really hard. I would have to say that the 464 class is not easy either but it's definitely manageable. He cares about his students but he avoids spoon-feeding you everything. He does expect some accountability though so be prepared to spend some out-of-class time for his class.

Erickson makes his class a lot harder than it needs to be. His tests are really hard and ridiculously specific. He doesn't do anything to help you with the exams. He offers extra credit but he unfairly grades it. You would be lucky to get half the points on his extra credit.  This is a weed out class and very dull. Take mmbio with robinson!

LOVES trick questions in his quizzes, so make sure you're good at reading and comprehending everything you read. Okay teacher, but he doesn't consider students' concerns ? he's ALWAYS right.  Just ask him.  Sign up asap for the extra credit b/c it goes fast!

This class is not easy, but it is the reason I am considering majoring in Microbiology.  Prof Erickson is so willing to help every student.  I have learned so much from this class that is relevant outside the classroom.  Love it!!
His lectures are extremely disorganized. Weekly quizzes and his tests are impossible. He does give extra credit but it's a lot of extra work.

This class is hard but it will force you to learn a lot. He offers A LOT of extra credit opportunities throughout the semester so take advantage of that. He always sticks around to answer questions after class. His grading is quite fair. Weekly quizzes from lecture and reading so class attendance and reading the chapters are essential.
I learned a ton in this class. Great prof.
Prof Erickson was relatively clear in class, but the tests we had were completely different from anything we learned in class
He tried really hard to help the students, but the class was really unclear and lacked organization. I would shop around for other professors.

honestly thought he was great.  yes tests are hard, you have to really have a good understanding of the material instead of just memorizing things.  attendance is mandatory, there's not a real way outside of class to catch up.  overall the class was well worth taking
A lot of fun. The class was fascinating. Tests were hard, but you learned a lot on them. He's very willing to have one-on-one relationships with each student.
Horrible teacher ever... Maybe he knows alot but doesn't teach well... Test is just random from anywhere...

Prof Evans is my new all-time favorite math teacher. He did a great job teaching us as a group and individually. He really cares about the success of his students. His classes are hard (the course is hard) but it's nice that it ends up with the exams not being as hard as what you do on the homework. He's a solid teacher and a fun one at that.

One of the best teachers I've had at the Y. He really cares about his students and makes sure to yeah everything clearly. He's very sociable and a very good teacher. Our class was fun and felt like a family, learning math together. Again- this has been one of my best classes yet. It's such a hard subject- Evans makes it bearable

Evans-sensei is awesome!!!!  He really cares about how well you do in the class and teaches accordingly. He goes over the material efficiently yet if you have questions he won't move on until you understand it. He is super fun throughout class as well. If you can, TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!

The class was good, average difficulty. There were no reading quizzes, which resulted in me reading infrequently, but lecture references the readings. The homework was usually pretty easy, the tests were reasonable. For the group project and labs it is really important to read the instructions carefully, because they aren't explained well in class.

He's lecture and textbook heavy in his teaching style, but he takes the most important principles that you need to know and puts it into his presentations. His lectures and presentations alone are not sufficient for his exams, but they do guide you in the right direction. I read the textbook before each class and found it complemented his style.

Professor Fullwood is a very nice man but a truly awful professor. By far the worst professor I've ever had at BYU. His lectures lack any sort of organization and you DO NOT LEARN 90% of the material that you are actually tested on in class. The tests are brutal, the average scores are the lowest of any class I've had. Avoid his class at all costs.

I took ME 250 from Dr. Fullwood because there was no other option. His lectures were disorganised and unclear. Homework assignments were difficult and average test scores were the lowest out of any BYU class I have taken. His teaching style turned me away from the ME degree. I would recommend taking this class from anybody else possible.

Dr. Fullwood is willing to work with students to help them outside of class as it is hard to get much out of the lecture. Unfortunately, the slides are unorganized and occasionally have incorrect info, the self-check slides for the project have numerous incorrect solutions, and all posted solutions are unclear- hard to follow and hard to learn from

Dr. Fullwood is a good teacher.  He is willing to work with the class on assignments and deadlines.  His plastic classes are a lot better then 373 because anyone in the ME department will tell you you will never use C++ other then this class.  He expects a lot from the final project and the labs great really hard.  learn matlab and excel if you can

I really liked Prof Fullwood. Sometimes assn. requirements/what to study for tests was vague, but he is very helpful if you email him. Its a little stressful beforehand but it turns out assn. aren't graded too strictly and tests aren't too grueling. It won't kill you if you miss studying one little thing. Glad I took this class from him.

This class was at times quite random and the tests were very strange. Dr. Fullwood himself was a pretty amiable man, but his lectures were sometimes taught little. It was hard to know what would be on the tests and the average score was very low usually. Not a great class, not the worst class I have ever taken.

Dr. Fullwood was very easy going and very aware that students are taking other classes other than his.  On several occasions he delayed homework when he felt students were falling behind.  Very understanding and helpful.
I think it was his second semester. Pretty good. Still some kinks to work out, but much much better than his first semester. Cares about his students, and listens to advice.

I think this was his first semester teaching and it was very apparent.  He was very unorganized and his tests were all over the place.  He doesn't explain things well, but at least he is a nice guy.  i wouldn't recommend taking his class.

Class is pretty tough conceptually. The class is combined online via canvas and is actually managed by the other section professor Bean. Therefore, the tests and homework were created by Bean, and Dr Grimsmann could not provide much help in preparing for them. Prof Grimsman is a super nice guy, but I probably wouldn't take another class from him.

Dr. Grimsman is a very knowledgeable person who you can tell really knows his stuff, but his teaching style did not click with me. He talks about an algorithm one time in the abstract sense in class, then you have homework to go and answer questions about it. I feel like the lectures really did not prepare me for the homework or the tests.

Fantastic professor. Learned more from the classes (312 and Reinforcement Learning) I took from David than any other CS classes at BYU. The assignments were difficult but grading was generous. Don't take if you want a quick and easy class. Do take if you wanna push yourself and learn. Highly recommend his classes if you're planning on grad school

Projects and homework felt insurmountably difficult, more than any CS other class I've taken. If you take any other intensive classes at the same time as this, be prepared to lose weeks of sleep rushing to finish these projects days late. Tests are a huge chunk of your grade, and as the lectures' topics are one-and-done studying is a nightmare.

Lectures could sometimes be slow but were always very informative. Slides are great for review and Grimsman is usually active on Slack to answer questions. He was also very understanding when some external circumstances affected my attendance. Labs aren't that tough but do take some time, don't skip homework (no late work). Solid choice for 312.

There are a plethora of small factors that add up make this course more difficult than it needs to be. It felt like it was sloppily designed. His lectures were like he was giving an impromptu speech. Starter code and specs for projects were unreasonably vague. Lecture sometimes wouldn't start until 15 minutes in. Everything had some small problem.

Dr. Grimsman is still new but is a good teacher. Lectures can be a bit dry, but he knows his stuff so anything that isn't clear you can always ask about. Really good at helping students when they need it (grade wise) and even let us do test corrections for the first midterm. Overall, I'd recommend taking his classes but beware of 412 as it is HARD.

Professor Grimsman is new, but he is a good teacher. 312 has a lot of difficult content, but he tries to explain every topic sufficiently and is very open to student feedback. The lectures aren't that exciting, but are helpful for staying on track. The tests are hard but not impossible. No late assignments allowed so start labs EARLY.
Great teacher, really cares about his students.  Be prepared to write a short paper, but I felt like this helped me to connect the dots.
So much busy work. Professor is really difficult person to work with. Don't waste your time with him
If you know you know.
class and professor.
This class is clunky and has poor design. Overly complex and have to manage assignments through 3 different websites. Most of the stuff on canvas could be reduced to like one page IMO.

He comes off as intimidating and he will seem like this class is the hardes business class you can ever take but it's actually really easy to get an A, my 15 year old brother can do nothing and get an A. My grade at the end of the semester was like a 105. his puns in class is the most unfunny thing; the fact that no one laughs is pretty funny.
He's a good professor, he is a little intense but super good guy. Sometimes class wasn't super relevant but you only have to go like 5 times.

His course structure was great, felt organized and flowed well. His lectures were very good, but I felt I did not gain as much revelation as anticipated from them. The course concepts were informative, but he spent lots of time on things that already felt like common sense. One funny thing is that he likes to keep lectures light with corny jokes
I didn't feel that the in-class participation was necessarily helpful for this type of course.

This class is a lot of work. The lectures are filled with helpful information but there are only 6 classes that you are required to attend. Grading was fair and the TA's were super accessible if you had any questions about assignments throughout the semester.
You don't interact much with the Professor but when you do it is good. Mostly comes down to just who you get for the OCI. Hopefully you get a good one.

Ok the course itself is awesome. Gettign to do an internship like this is just an incredible experience. However, I didn't love the setup. All of the canvas work itself, aka the work not actually for the company, felt like a waste of time. The professor was also a little mean and the lectures were kidn of a waste too. Would reccomend it anyways.

Great teacher although you don't interact with him much since you only have a few class periods a semester and work is done outside of class. Most of the difficulty comes from sponsors or team members so it can be different every time.

Professor Hollan is an experienced and caring teacher, and the On Campus Internship program is definitely worth it if you want to learn, gain real-world experience, and build your resume. However the extra homework on Canvas can be tedious at times, and there little forgiveness if you miss any major assignments on Canvas or the OCI dashboard.
He's a good professor but the course takes up a lot of time.
OCI itself can be a of work and there's multiple meetings with your team each week. Professor is cool and class only meets 6 times a semester.

I liked the internship itself, but the class felt like busywork a lot of the time. I don't think I learned many new skills from the lectures or modules. This is also a time consuming class so be prepared for that.

Good teacher but since the class is an intership it feels like some of the assignments are unnecessary and not focused on improving the expereince and learning from the actual internship. Very few graded assignments so if you forget even one it has a big impact on your grade.

He does not understand the typical day to day life of a student. He is just very out of touch with students and is hard to relate to. Has lots of assignments that are busywork and takeaway from time that could be used to be focused on tasks assigned from sponsor.

Cool guy, corny jokes. The OCI was a great experience though the actual class periods felt like a waste of time. Oftentimes during the semester the work for the class would get in the way of the actual work we were trying to do for the internship.

Has a lot of experience and is an amazing resource for this class. The class was for an on-campus internship, so I mostly worked with my team and our sponsor rather than this professor, but I felt comfortable going to class and asking questions about work in general, internships, and best practices. Class is mandatory but only meets 6 times.
Great overall professor. If you simply do the work, this class is a great experience and you will certainly get an A.
Covers weak material

I took the OCI, and it was amazing! There were only 5 lectures, and they helped you know what big assignments were due and the expectations. Honestly, there is a lot of busy work at the beginning, but it helps you get the hours while you figure out the direction of your project. Would recommend for sure!

OCI is great if you don't have any experience or internships because you can get it on your resume and have something to talk about in your interviews. Besides that, sometimes there was lack on direction just because of the nature of an OCI. I think a lot of them are marketing related, so if your into that this could be perfect.

I'm grateful for Bro. Hollan running this program. It has provided much-needed experience in the business world. He has also integrated the spiritual nourishment I needed from a BYU experience, and it really helped me with this class. If there's anything I would like to see improved, I'd say I would have liked to meet in class more often.
Just go to class and do your work. Simple
Unecessarily serious. Busy work that provides nothing in line with the project/company youre working with. Seems like hes trying his best to make the class harder than it should be.

the structure of the class itself is a bit weird, where you have to go through every bit of text or assignment to get to what you want. You only meet a couple times which is nice but there just seems to be a bunch of busywork on the side of the OCI. The OCI itself was fantastic and Brother Hollan provided a lot of good resources in the course

This class, depending on your project assignment, can be a huge resume booster. I'm pretty sure I wouldn't have landed my summer internship without it. That being said, I didn't love the structure of the class. The Canvas all felt like busywork and lectures were just rehashing the Canvas. Definitely worth it if you need more experience though!

Brother Hollan is a good teacher, I just didn't feel like the class segments added much to the internship. What you'll get out of the internship will really depend on the company you're assigned. I would take it if you need more experience in business but if you have a job in your field already I wouldn't recommend it.

The OCI was great. The structure Professor Hollan provided helped me become a better professional. The lower rating is because he gave us a zero on a presentation when we messed up recording it and wouldn't answer our questions about why. He gave us a way to get half credit but never gave a good reason for the zero.
I thought there was a lot of fluff as far as the course content goes, but overall, a great class to get real-world experience
I had the best experience. My internship was great and I had a great team to work with
Professor Hollan was Great. Put in the work and it will be a good class.

Professor Hollan is a good professor. You only have class like 5 times a semester for the OCI groups. He can be a little intense and is quite picky about grading so make sure to check the rubric and hit deadlines.
Good teacher. For OCI you don't interact with him very much but he is more than willing to help!

He is fairly strict about how assignments get uploaded, especially presentation recordings. It is complicated doing it the way he wants it, which is a little frustrating. Overall a good experience and his dad jokes were decent. Some of the work feels a little like busywork, but I think it is so that people are more accountable in their internships.

He cares about his students. The attendance is mandatory, but all the lectures are necessary for the projects and to get the project done, so you should attend them just like other classes. His has a professional background at Microsoft and knows what matters in the business world. He teaches you about many important things for the real world.
Lectures are very unhelpful and, honestly, unnecessary. Can be a bit boring at times. The good thing is he lets you take control of the project and doesn't interject. Pretty meh experience overall
A great way to add things to your Resume and experience, but a real internship would be more valuable. I am not sure if I would do this again, but I do not regret it.

Loved This Class! Probably one of the most valuable things i've done in my college career so far, (just wrapping up my freshman year). Many lessons learned and I loved my internship. MAKE SURE YOU DO THE 360 surveys though, they are so unbelieveably important to your grade.

Great class! Took this as a graduating senior (not apart of the business school), and have had many interviews that have asked about the on campus internship. 10/10 recommend if you are trying to upgrade your resume.
Great teacher, and a great guy.
The lectures he gives are long and not full of useful information. The OCI has a lot of unnecessary assignments that detract for you time working for the company.
Most of the on-campus internship is done outside of class. Everything was well prepared and easy to follow along with. I really enjoyed this class.

Professor is always on top of letting everyone know what needs to be done and making sure that we are prepared for everything in the course. He helps students to understand that learning is something that they must take initiative for themselves.

I think that the course is quite amazing. Professor Holland does a good job at letting you know what the expectations are, but as with an on campus internship, you also have many avenues to do it as you wish. Just know that deadlines are pretty fast in place.
Great professor and great class. Class grade is heavily dependent on some assignments that feel more like busy work than anything else.

This class has quite a few time consuming projects that in my honest opinion take away from the time we can be delivering to our sponsor. He was engaging enough in class to make it worth coming in once a week for the mandatory attendance, but the lectures themselves were pretty bland. Luckily we only had to show up a couple times after midterms.

Prof. Hollan was great! With the OCI, I think we only went to class around 6 times, maybe less. His lectures were boring sometimes, but he did a great job of giving us resources for our on-campus internships. It is easy to get an A in this class! The internship is definitely time consuming though.
The byu OCI are a great opportunity, but the lectures are a complete waste of time. He tries to be very riveting and inspiring but I didn't learn 1 thing from him.
The professor was good at explaining everything the course entails. Good course, I learned a lot and benefitted from taking it.
Great professor and great class, lectures can be a bit boring sometimes.
The professor is awesome and a pretty chill guy. The class was useful but not my favorite because of the time that was put in and I didn't really feel like it helped as much as I thought it would.
The course is very engaging, but classes are incredibly dull and uninspiring.
This class is pretty hands off. As long as you get your hours in every week, you're going to do just fine.

My OCI experience was awesome! I feel like I gained lots of applicable knowledge that I'll be able to carry into my future classes and jobs. This class is set up so well, and even the "busy work" helped me to gain and practice very useful skills. I wouldn't say it's "hard" at all; it takes time, and you'll get out of it what you put into it!

If you take this class, be sure that you take the time to make sure you get a project you'll enjoy. Your group and sponsor company can make or break the experience. It's an easy class, just spend time working for your sponsor and attend your group meetings. Simple and a good filler class.
If you have no other internship than this can be a good option.
It's an aliright class
Good class, substantial time requirement.
Professor Hollan is amazing! He gives clear feedback and gives individual time to each team!
At first felt overwhelmed but as time went on it was a great class!

I wish he was more personable with his students. I had a hard time with his lack of respect for students and the sponsor we had. Overall, the curriculum was easy to understand and I was mainly meeting with my group which I loved.

The class is overwhelming at first, but it ends up being pretty easy. Prof Hollan is intense, but don't let him scare you. No matter how good or bad your internship goes, you'll probably still get an A.

The professor did a great job explaining what we need to do clearly. He emphasized that there are resources for us to use for help which was awesome. One thing he could work on is making everyone feel more cared about, he was a little harsh in the way he spoke.
Great class overall and helpful for building your resume. However, if you have other internships elsewhere then take those over taking an OCI.
Just stay on top of your work, go to class, attend your team meetings, and you'll be fine.

Nice teacher but his class requires so many hours. Our project wasn't with an established sponsor, so we spent hours watching YouTube videos about Amazon Ads to get to our time requirement. It was fun to make friends, but don't take if you have a busy semester.

This class was awesome. In order to get an a you must put in between 7.5 and 9 hours per week, so come to the class ready to put in the work every week for your sponsor! It was great resume building material as well.

This course is mainly done outside of class. Most of what is done is a part of your internship, so the level of difficulty and workload depends on your project and how committed you are to your project. There are only about 6 in person classes and they are simple, but mandatory. Great resume builder.

He's a funny guy, but it's like he doesn't want to teach this course. If you don't have to take an OCI then I'd recommend staying away from it. I've seen in many cases that the internships cause more inconvenience to students than they do help resumes.
Simple and straight forward. The OCI is determined on a clear grading rubric. Good resume building and for character development.
Good professor, only six classes each semester, but they're mandatory, majority of the work is done outside of class

Professor's good, but your experience is really determined by the company you are assigned to, and a lot of the companies are start-ups that may not know what they need, so you deal with a lot of ambiguity.
Good professor! OCI is pretty easy, just carry your weight in your group.
You won't spend a ton of time with him since you spend most of the time working with your group, and class isn't held every week, but he's great regardless.
Great guy, pretty intense at the beginning but he softens up and is kind and respectful if you do your work. Lots of assignments and group work in this class but good!
He only requires attendance for a few weeks.

Really good guy, and I really enjoyed the internship (I had a great sponsor, from what I know a lot of the experience depends on your team/sponsor). Brother Hollan's lectures were pretty pointless unfortunately, and were mandatory attendance. Great experience with the internship team, though, highly recommend it for the learning and resume boost.
Great professor, there is only 6 classes you need to attend.
They tend to be very straight-forward and serious, but with that comes a lot of experience which will help you to learn how to navigate the business world.
Good class. Better than last semester in terms of canvas. Good experience.
Professor Hollan was great! He made expectations very clear and encouraged good business professional behavior. Take it if you can!
He was a good professor I liked that he let you do your thing and figure it out your own way.
It all depends on the sponcor you are assigned to.

To be honest, I had a really hard time with Professor Hollan; it felt like a semester full of busy work with very high standards, which were hard to reach with the group I was assigned to. The intention was there but the process didn't match. There are some required days to attend but I didn't really understand the reason why.
the course is a great opportunity to get business experience.

He was a good professor to guide this class. While we work more with our sponsor, Brother Hollan did a good job at reviewing key assignments that were due. Attendance is only mandatory on certain days of the semester!
Very easy to follow along in class. Very responsive.

For this class the professor isn't a lot of help in fact he was more of an obstacle than anything and will change rule, just focus on your project, and if you need help go to the TA's they are very helpful, I never saw a point to go and see the teacher for help, he just there to enforce the rules, and warn us about the standard, of the school.

Honestly the class went well because my sponsors were super cool. But the classes that were required felt like he felt required to be there too if you catch my drift. He filled most of the time talking about AI and not much that was relevant to the internship experience.
The professor himself is not a large part of the OCI class. He is good.
You won't interact with him
Lots of busy work but the internship itself is amazing.

Enjoying the class is super dependent on your sponsor and your team. There isn't class every week, but attendance is mandatory for the few weeks you have it. You're required to have two meetings as a team one with your sponsor every week. There is a minimum 7.5hrs/ week of work (including class & meetings). Its a lot of work but a great experience.

The class is dependent on your sponsor, if you get a good sponsor you'll enjoy the class. There is a lot of busy work that's pretty annoying at the start in the Canvas course, but it chills out in later weeks.

This class was a great experience and I learned a lot, mainly from my team and sponsor. Some class assignments felt like busy work and were not very helpful for our project. However, that may vary by company. If you trust your team and sponsor, the experience will go well and be enjoyable.
The Class is good. The experience really depends on the OCI you are given. It is really helpful to learn how organizations work and look like in the professional space.

This class is great if you are looking for a way to gain some professional experience! Given the nature of the class, there is a lot of work outside of class. Class is only held a handful of times. At times the class assignments are busy work, but they aren't hard. As long as you put in time and work into your internship, you'll do great.
OCI is great for students who don't have any professional experience. I am overall glad I did it. However, the class presents a lot of busy work that detracts from the OCI in my opinion.

Brother Hollan is well humored and cares to make his classes interesting. The classes could be shorter since the content of the lectures is not difficult to understand. Bro. Hollan does a good job trying to make them engaging.

Some of the classwork is just busy work, but the experience overall is good. Keep in mind you have to meet with your team 3 times a week (one of these times is also with your sponsor), which makes scheduling a little hard. Also, it is basically a big group project, so keep in mind you'll have to be working with other people the whole semester.

The internship was great experience, but I feel like the class itself didn't help too much. He gave good tips on things to remember and more materials we could use, but it was also all found on Canvas.
easy and teaches and acts like a dad.
pretty straight forward, he is not really the focus its more of the project and the sponsor that you associate with more. and of course your team.

This professor is very strict, but I suppose you would need to be when you have close to a thousand students to work with. He is also still pretty against AI usage, but it seems like he lightened up this year and allowed us to use AI to make graphs.
Class was great. Not many lecture's. Given the nature of the class everything is done outside of class but not hard to do well in just requires effort on your part.
The class is very professionally enriching, and the professor is very focused and clear regarding the projects.

He was great! I learned so much from my OCI class with him, and he was easy to get a hold of. The OC internship requires a lot of time and attention outside of class, but the class lectures (which are few during the semester) were chill and manageable.
He teaches fine but I think that the teacher isn't that important. Most of the work is outside of class as we only meet like 6 times a semester.

The class was a lot of work, you need to complete 7.5 hours of work every week. You get real experience to put on your resume which is a positive. There are only a few mandatory in class lectures but they feel pretty pointless.
Go to class
Nice guy, can be very assertive and blunt. The course is fun if you choose to have fun.

Brother Hollan did a great job at giving instructions, supporting students, and explaining vague concepts. Only take this class if the internship you are assigned fits what you are looking for. A ton of time is required outside of class, with 3 on campus meetings a week minimum, so be prepared for that.
I like Professor Hollan, he did a great job making the class directly apply to real life and made the modules and lectures apply to everyone.
Professor Hollan teaches a great class. It seems that the 6 lectures are simply for attendance.

I loved the on-campus internship I got to be apart of! It was a great experience! David Hollan didn't really have anything to do with the experience or add to the class in any positive way. Would highly reccomend the on-campus internship, David Hollan wasn't my favorite but it didn't make a big difference in the end.

Organized professor who explains assignments clearly. Attendance is required, but quizzes and coursework are pretty easy. He seems gruff at first but is actually very nice. Biggest downside is that almost everything is group work, so your experience depends a lot on your team but you do get to rate them at the end of the semester.

The professor is pretty harsh to the students (he almost acts as if you are going to try and do the bare minimum throughout the semester if you have questions or situations that get in the way of his criteria). However, I would say you rarely interact with the professor and it depends on your group 100%
The professor is fine it's more that the course itself is not great. I would advise you to find another internship.

How good the OCI is all depends on your sponsor and project. My group got a bad project and a sponsor that was hard to work with, so we had a painful semester. Check to make sure the company you are working for actually exists. Working with the group was nice, though. Most groups become good school friends. Still worth it, just be careful.

I loved how he held us to a high standard. It was extremely necessarily for us especially since we were dealing with actual companies. I just think he could've offered us more help instead of only telling us we need to do things.

The OCI was overall a great experience and there was lots of opportunity for growth and feedback both on the giving and receiving side. Professor Hollan runs a great system, but his mandatory classes and busy work were often a waste of time

The MSB494R course is good for those who want a general experience in an internship, a mixed bag for what you will receive, but it does give experience either way. His lectures talked about the importance of professionalism, which is important but not exciting. Glad to have taken the course I'll say
Lectures seemed pretty obvious but they were required
Great experience doing my OCI. No complaints about Prof. Hollan
It was a great course! I learned so much from my intership.
Great class! I got amazing real-world experience. The deadlines are very strict.

Disappointed by both the OCI experience and the professor. Some OCI's are what they make them out to be, but 80% of them are super random, and you are not doing what you signed up for. They still look good enough on a resume, but the 8-9 hours you spend a week feel not very useful. Unimpressed overall by the professor.
Great class for an OCI
Brother Hollan is great! My only complaint is that a lot of the work in the on-campus internship is unrelated to the company you are trying to benefit.
He was very helpful and willing to answer any questions we had.
Its an internship with a real company. The class only meets 6 times to give support.

Make sure you get onto a project that you genuinely care about and this class will be very enjoyable and worthwhile. In my eyes, the one downside to this class are the Canvas modules you have to complete.

Professor Hollan genuinely cares about his students and will work with any student who puts in their effort. The class is completely what you get out of it - as long as you do your work, it's an easy A and a great internship opportunity.

Your experience in this class is based on your group and your TA. The class lectures are required but don't feel helpful while you are there. Professor Hollan is nice but every single lecture just talked about AI and felt extremely unnecessary. I had a great group so I really enjoyed that class but I can see why people don't enjoy the class.

Most of this class is done outside of lectures. There are a few lectures during the semester (5-6 of them) and attendance is required. However, most of the class is done on your own and with your team. You set your own hours but are expected to spend 7.5-9.0 hours a week working on your internship.

Brother Hollan was great! The classes are mandatory and honestly don't seem like the best use of time, but he does give some useful information in them and there's only like 6 throughout the whole semester. I would recommend!
It's fine. I didn't see him a lot.
Ultimately, you do not spend alot of time with Professor Holland in the OCI course, depending on your project type the lectures may feel like a waste of time.

For this class, just make sure you have a good team, TA, and project sponsor. You do not interact with Hollan too much. There are maybe 5 mandatory classes, but they are boring, and I feel like I didn't learn anything from them.

Brother Hollan wants what is best for you and this class is heavy with assignments, but he equips you with what you need. It is 7.5-9 hours per week, which is a commitment, but it has helped me to learn a lot and it has been awesome to work with a company and gain real world experience.

The on campus internship is a great way to get experience, Brother Hollan is kind of a stickler and you are supposed to do the class for 7.5 hours a week so it is a good amount of work, he does give a couple of extra credit opportunities. It is an easy A and good for the resume, didn't love how he set up Canvas.
He's a good professor but the lectures are boring. Also the modules feel like just a bunch of busy work but after about 3 or 4 weeks you get used to it.

The professor is great! It's just the assignments are not. The final project is necessary, but the final report on top of it is extra work. He didn't really tell us how to work on our internship and final report at the same time, and I got super burnt out at the end. Basically figure it out. too much time on final report, not enough on actual inter
He is a great professor. His lectures are either about what is expected of you on projects or about useful skills for your career.
Great class, 100% recommend.

He's a really good professor, he teaches well and there are only about 6 lectures per semester. The class is primarily group work with your internship team, and that's why there's a lot of homework because you are expected to put 7.5 hours of work into the class each week. Professor Hollan is great, he teaches well and his lectures are informative.
Great First internship opportunity
Professor Hollan does a good job teaching the lectures, sometimes he comes off as very direct and kind of harsh, but overall he wants to make sure all students are successful.
I really enjoyed this class! it takes setting aside at least 8 hours a week which is the bare minimum. It helped me a lot in gaining some more real world business experience.
Provides some good instruction during class but be sure to work closely with his TA's

This class is an internship where you work with a real company. The class part of it is mostly Professor Hollan giving general business and teambuilding advice and skills to learn. Some of the class sections were helpful, some could have been an email. Overall I had a really great experience with my internship.

Be ready to put in the hours for your OCI. 7.5 hours per week is the minimum for an A. Good class overall, but half of your work will be just doing the class busiwork and not even necessarily working on your OCI. Also, while it is good, there are some weird rules you have to follow with your OCI that aren't well explained.
He was cool.

The professor was very clear with instructions and made things easy to understand. He was kind, approachable, and always willing to answer my questions. His teaching style was organized and easy to follow.

He is a really nice guy and tries to make class fun, but he doesn't allow for any exceptions, which was hard because there were things that were out of my group's control, and we got penalized for those things.

Brother Hollan was alright. I imagine his job is pretty complicated since he has to manage so many projects. I was not a fan of how he treated students at times. I told him I had to leave for one week and it was not helpful when it came to telling me what I might miss.

Professor Hollan isn't very kind at all; he's pretty stuck up and acts like he's better than his students. However, the actual OCI with the sponsor is a great experience. Thankfully, he didn't have too many classes, so I didn't have to deal with him that much.
Good intentions. Just a little too straight forward. Overall great class and you get goods hand on experience.

I only rate him as a 4 because you only attend class around 6 times where he lectures. This class is an on-campus internship. He works very hard to line teams of students up with great projects and is open to help. There are a lot of TAs that stay in touch with the many teams involved, which is why you don't have much contact with Professor Hollan

Professor Hollan is an interesting guy haha. Love this class, it was great to get hands-on experience with a company, however for the 6 times we met as a class in person, the lectures seemed redundant.
I really enjoyed this class and always felt like help was in place when I needed it. Good TA support too.

I didn't interact much with the professor, since it is project based. There are only 6 mandatory lectures to attend and they are good. Most of the class is a big group project for a company and you are required to record 7.5-9 hours of work a week for full credit. It can be tough and is a lot of work, but the professor is good and you learn a lot.

I enjoyed my on-campus internship, but sometimes felt like the class deliverables were so substantial that we couldn't focus as much on what our sponsor wanted. Only 6 class periods are required to attend but you are required to put in about 7-9 hours per week to get full points for the class. Overall good class, got good experience.

Overall super easy to get an A in the class as long as you just do the work. Make sure you have time because you do have to dedicate at least seven and a half hours a week and have to try to organize meetings with 5 peoples busy schedules.
He was a good teacher. Always brought in the gospel. Grade is mostly based off of outside/group work. Great experience, good resume builder.
He was a pretty good teacher. There's only 6 class periods you have to attend, the rest is work outside of class.
The canvas course is not the most straightforward and has more info than you need, but definitely a great learning opportunity and resume builder!
Overall enjoyed the experience that was provided.

Your experience will likely vary since each project is different. But I really enjoyed this class and Brother Hollan did a great job explaining requirements and resources we had access to. You get out of this class what you put in it.
Great professor and he really just wants you to have a good experience to put on your resume.

I participated in the on-campus internship program with him. Most of the difficulty comes from your individual sponsor and what they expect. The class is only once a week but really helps with the project.

Professor Hollan is nice and does what he can to make sure everyone is successful in the class. He is willing to work with you if you are struggling. The lectures are a little unnecessary, but attendance is mandatory so it can just be homework time to be honest. There are also only like 6 lectures total.
This class was not hard.

Brother Hollan is Awesome. The classes were great. The OCI is time consuming so be prepared to spend lots of time working with your team and doing assignments for the company. Overall it was worth it and I learned a lot!
It's a fun class, plan to work at least 7.5 hours each week. It is apart of your grade
Bro. Hollan teaches skills that can be applied to the professional world and not just the classroom. The class is mainly group work, but it isn't too bad.

The On-Campus internship program is great. Even if the project isn't super technical or deep, you learn a ton about teamwork, communication, meeting deadlines, and writing quality reports/making quality presentations. If you dedicate the 7.5+ hours each week and put reasonable effort into the class assignments, you will probably get an A.
Straightforward class. Prof. Hollan lays out the road map of the course very well. If you do the work it is an easy A!

This class is basically a semester long group project so we didn't interact with him much. Frankly, I wish he held class more. I felt like each lesson was only scratching the surface of what concept he was trying to teach. More class periods would have enabled him to dive deeper into some of these topics.

This class takes a lot of time outside of class because you have to meet with your internship team often and log your hours on a time sheet. It was a very good class for experience and working with real people and I would definitely take this class again.

I think that Brother Hollan really cares about the success of this program, albeit sometimes at the expense of the students. My poor rating of the course is simply because I don't share his vision of this OCI class. I think that the class itself performs very little for the students and for the company, so I felt like I was wasting time.
Professor Hollan is great and is good at explaining things. I think sometimes lecture can get repetitive, but it's good how thorough he is.
This prefessor is awesome, has lots of dads jokes. Really fun class, highly recommended!
Brother Hollan was great! We only had to meet a few times in class, but each time we met, he made sure that we knew exactly what we needed to do.
If you ask for personal feedback, he is great at providing that for you. I feel that there were many class meetings that were not necessary.

This class was very straightforward in their expectations. You know what will be expected out of you and the grade you will receive. If you work hard in this course you will do just fine. Make sure you are willing to sacrifice time in your schedule because having in-person meetings with your group are mandatory.
Brother Hollan is exceptional at what he does. He might come across as too rigid, but given the nature of OCI you have to be firm and push students to excel.
Reasonable workload. Classwork is pretty little aside from your 7-10 hours of OCI work per week
It's good if you have a dope internship, it lowkey is a lot of work though. But, getting a good grade isn't too bad at all.
Helpful in helping students understand the importance of getting real-world experience.

Brother Hollan taught the OCI class. We only had class a few times throughout the semester where he gave short lectures. The class was mainly working with an assigned team and your sponsor throughout the whole semester. That aspect was incredibly beneficial!
The OCI program at BYU is great, I wish there wasn't so much busy work and the time we used on the class assignments went toward helping our sponsors.
good communication when to attend class
Brother Hollan was good. The course I took was an On-campus internship so we didn't see him much.

Funny, witty professor. Attending his lectures is optional but super helpful in learning the content. He does a good job at teaching business concepts and applying them to real world settings. He does a good job encouraging people to work hard not just for a grade, but for the growth and the experience you gain.
Super chill dude and great experience, attendance was mandatory but going to class did not feel needed.
He's a goat, mostly everything that is graded is based on your completion of the assignments

Overall a good experience as a class, but some of the assignments felt pointless, the lectures weren't very helpful despite being mandatory, and the canvas was disorganized. The actual content of the project was good though, and I learned a lot of new things.
This class provided a good experience of working in a team and dealing with ambiguity. The class will differ greatly depending on who you work for and with.
This class was fun to participate in, mostly just group/team work.
I liked this class it is mainly just working with your group.
Lots of time outside of class
Satisfactory
Provides real-world application skills during his lecture to best prepare us for our OCI
This class is an awesome opportunity to gain experience. The class differs greatly depending on who you work for and with.

The class itself is not difficult. Show up and you'll be fine. Just make sure to be active in your project and record your hours weekly! That's my only gripe with the class, recorded hours cannot be made up or corrected. If you miss a week recording your horus, you just have to tank it.
Make sure to work well with your team and you'll do great.

Honestly super chill, but depends on your internship. He is a nice guy, but you mainly just interact with your TA's. Pretty easy, just make sure you get your assignments done on time and show up for attendance.
He's really awesome.

I think one of the biggest things about the class is that it hinges on the GROUP. However, he really wants you to get a good experience out of the class. You will be doing 3 meetings a week, lots of work outside of class. If you plan to take this class, take a lighter course load so that you are able to participate. I highly recommend you do this.

Brother Hollan seems like a really great guy and he manages the intern teams well. His lectures feel a little redundant and irrelevant but there are only six mandatory classes in the entire semester, so it's not a big deal.
OCI is pretty much luck of the draw in regards to your project. It can turn into a lot of busy work and trying to figure out what to do. The lectures themselves don't provide that much value.

I was happy to have the opportunity to complete an on campus internship, but the class felt pointless. Most of what he discussed was common sense. Attendance was mandatory, which I thought was ridiculous because all of the necessary information you needed was online. However, the internship itself was a great experience. Do it if you can!
The internship opportunity is great. The classes are mandatory and pretty slow-paced.

My internship was not good and the professor is very separated from what you do. Class was mandatory, very boring, and only sometimes helpful- but you didn't really have to pay attention much and it counted toward your hours for the week so that was nice
He makes the class good eventhough the class is or internships are not very good
Class was demanding in hours but not very difficult. Lectures were mandatory attendance but not super helpful. Overall good experience.
did well with outlines
I have a love hate relationship with this class.
This class is quite rigorous, but Dr. Hollan sets it up well enough to succeed.
Brother Hollan was a great professor; although we only had a few lectures, I enjoyed his classes.
He was very nice, the class really depends on what project/group you get.
Great teacher and enjoyed his connections of what we learned in the classroom to the real world and to the Gospel.
Hard to learn in class because he mostly just reads straight from the canvas.
Tbh, the OCI experience was great but the impact TAs and the instructor has on your work is minimal. I felt the lectures were pointless and that he put too much emphasis on himself.

This class gave me a lot of hands on experience working with a company and team. It was hard for us to focus on our company work when we had to make big reports and presentations.These took up a lot of our time and took away from us just working for the company. Class was kinda vague, but you have to go for attendance. Nothing against the teacher!

Professor Hollan tries to scare the students to make it seem harder/more difficult that it is. Our company was chill, but there is a lot of ambiguity in the project and lots of it is just figuring out how to do their assignments, besides whatever project the company has you work on. The TA's can be helpful but sometimes slow to get back to you.

Professor Hollan is a very good speaker and keeps things simple. Overall, I think he is a great professor, but I think this is a really difficult course to effectively teach. There is so much ambiguity. I also wish there were less busy work.
The class isn't too hard, however the professor is not the kindest and tries hard to scare the students. Not a very enjoyable class lecture and the professor can seem grumpy.
He's an ok teacher, most of the class is working on your project with the team. Attend class the 6 times you need to and do the assignments and you'll get an A.

Looks and sounds like Tim Allen. He's a fine professor, nothing exceptional. You dont really get to interact with him much in this class. This class is meant to be mostly up to you and quite open to do what you want while still requiring a lot from you

He seems to want students to get a good grade. I had small assignment that I missed, and he wouldn't let me go back and fix it, even though it was a lot of points. Plenty of extra credit opportunities to make it up, thankfully. Even if you bomb your actual task for the internship, as long as you participate you'll definitely get a good grade.
He was a pretty chill professor. We only had 6 classes throughout the semester that was mandatory. Other than that we mostly interacted with our team and our TA's.
Easy class, all you need to do is participate with your group. We only had a couple of lectures to attend in person.

Bro. Hollan did a good job teaching and the class was very useful in order to gain valuable experience. However, there were some random busy work assignments interspersed throughout the semester. Overall helpful class to gain real-world experience.
Awesome class! Learned a lot!
He wants to help you succeed!
The professor did a good job a teaching and he covered all material in class.
Great professor, class has a lot of busy work.

this is an internship so you aren't actually in class a lot. The few classes that you do have are mandatory but feel as though they could have been sent in an email. Really this class depends on what internship you get and who is in your group
Great professor and an overall great class. The 95% of the class is done on your own and within your group outside of class.

I found the OCI experience beneficial for my resume, but it depends on who you receive as your sponsor. Brother Hollan is a good teacher and cares about our success, but the content that we completed for the class itself frequently seemed like busy work. I spent 40% or more of my time completing work for the class instead of for our sponsor.
Isn't very involved which can be nice depending on what you want. Was great at answering questions and helpful when needed. Get ready to dive into ambiguity and figure out what you need to do!
Interaction with the professor is fairly minimal but if you get a good TA it doesn't really matter. Other than that the class is really not bad just a bit time consuming.

OCI is a fine class, wasn't my favorite. Brother Hollan is a nice guy, but doesn't have super meaningful lectures or help a ton. He seems a bit prideful from a student point of view. But still a nice guy.

This professor has lots of TAs who are always willing to help. I never felt like our in person classes brought any real value to our education or tasks for the class, but the professor was always nice.

I loved my internship! I learned so many skills and met amazing people! The teacher didn't seem very involved. He would present a slide deck during class and that was about it. He made some funny jokes that were good. The TAs are amazing and very helpful. There are some repetitive assignments that feel like busy work.

Good teacher and an amazing class! I loved my internship and team and I feel like it helped me grow a lot and develop technical skills. Sometimes the assignments felt like busy work when we could be helping out our sponsor instead but it was really chill.
pretty good over all.

He seems nice, but I don't really know because he's not very engaged. The class requires more than seven hours of work a week in order to do well, which I feel is not well organized--shouldn't be about how long you can make a task last. Class is just him talking about random stuff for fifty mins.

The course is confusing and unclear in a lot of ways. It feels very self-directed, so you have to be proactive about choosing sponsors to get much out of it. A lot of the work felt like busy work without much real value. Pretty mid class.

He is a great professor and knows a lot of what is going on in this side of the buisness world. He unfortunately, due to the style of the class, is very repetitive. The first two or three times I came to class I was ready to learn but the class is very repetitive by nature.
The lectures felt like something that was a checklist item rather than an activity that actually provided value to enhancing learning in the course.
Knows what he's doing and great dad jokes

He teaches big classes so you won't know him personally but he is good and making a statement and highlighting the importance of going a good job on your internship while also giving you lots of chances to get a good grade and show your effort.

Brother Hollan is a nice guy and cares about the students, but we are all really there for just the internships. The class is mandatory, but not really that useful towards the internship. I get that it is a university requirement to have a certain number of mandatory classes, but the classes are just not useful. Good guy though.

I did an On-Campus Internship and Professor Hollan was the professor. Honestly, I am kind of indifferent about how I feel about his lectures, homework, etc. He's super intense, but then turns into a dad if you know what I mean. He was fine, the OCI in general wasn't my most favorite because of how it was structured, really is luck of the draw.
Grade heavily based on hours of work and not on quality.
The class is going to pull 7.5 hours from you each week, so just make sure to take it during a semester that you can give that time
participation every week is a must, and he has lots of TAs that will be able to help you and clarify things
Hollan was great and very passionate. Don't forget to submit your hours or you might be cooked! Great real-world experience though.
Good professor

He required you attend all the lectures he had. The canvas modules he provided were helpful when continuing your internship project. Sometimes felt like his classes were unnecessary for that reason. Overall a good teacher and cared about our success.
Its dependent on your internship for sure
The course is laid out well, but in-class time is kind of wasted. Working with your TA is necessary.
This class was a great way to get an internship in as well as getting credit for a class.
Brother Hollan made this experience great. The lectures were interactive and engaging and the experience was very valuable.
This was a great class! Professor Hollan is a very nice guy and love to crack some dad jokes during class. He also taught the content needed well.
He was a really great professor, not bad at all. Just come to class and stay on top of your assignments and you will be all good. Also be sure to do your hours for OCI and track them each week.
Professor was very clear about starting OCI work before due dates, and how best to prepare.

The only tough thing about the class that was tough is that it requires you to use an external source to update your "time log." This is where you receive a grade on your effort, which can be detrimental if you forget. There's, no reminder they give you on canvas. Therefore, it's important in this class that you use a calendar to remind yourself.
He was an ok professor. He works very hard and really cares about us and the work we do. He's a nice guy.

Honestly a great class, though that is very dependent on what sponsor/company you work with. The entire semester I had a total of two interactions via email with the professor and they were less than helpful to say the least. I relied heavily on my TA after that and there was no problem.

Brother Hollan was great, but the nature of this class was more hands-off for the professor. There was a ton of outside class homework where I often felt like I was just trying to fill the time and not make the time count, but the difficulty was in the real application of this internship class. I would take Brother Hollan again, not the class.

This class requires a lot of work outside of class (obviously), but most of the actual class work wasn't too hard. You do have to make a midterm and final presentation as well as a really long final report, and these feel like unnecessary busywork a bit. Brother Hollan does care about his students, though, and is willing to support us a lot.

It was a little bit different experience with him as a professor since it was an OCI. The actual class periods were unhelpful and I only went for the attendance points. But in terms of running the OCIs I think that he did a good job.
He talked a lot about AI, dealing with ambiguity, and working a lot each class. They are important things to learn. He made attendance mandatory and helped us when we had concerns.
Professor Hollan is a great guy but the lectures for MSB 494R were unesseary. He just told dad jokes and restated logistical information already found in the Canvas modules.

We met in class only a handful of times due to this class being very much outside work on your own time. He was very clear with what he wanted us to do and he also gave us tons of resources to accomplish what we needed to ahead of schedule. He's a great professor and I highly recommend taking this class!!

This class was demanding, but incredibly rewarding if you really put in the work to learn from it. I think that Professor Hollan has made this course easy to navigate, expectations were clear, and it was a wonderful experience. Expect to spend 7.5-9 hours outside of class working on the On-Campus Internship.

Not my favorite professor. He doesn't seem happy and something about his teaching grated. However, we only had class 5 times the whole semester and I really enjoyed my OCI. Would recommend this class, just not him as a normal teacher.

Such a incredible person to be around and work with. He is so kind and professional to students, SO capable of providing any sort of mercy on everything. He TOTALLY practices what he preaches, professor Hollan.

Seriously, such an...amazing professor...

Good luck. Only professor I disliked, I'm not sure why he's in education it doesn't seem to be for the students. Net negative experience. Asking for help results in either a no, being sent somewhere else, or being ignored. And he wants to teach you to be professional?
Seems like he doesn't want to help students at all. He's impossible to work with, no flexibility on anything whatsoever.

This class is nice to get real world experience, but there are so many easier ways to do it without these unneccessary lectures and busy work. Hollan takes the class portion of the internship way too seriously. Net negative experience.

MSB 494R is for BYU On-Campus Internships. My only complaint with this class is that there is SO MUCH BUSY WORK. I spent over 1/3rd of the time on busy work, when I just wanted to do actual work for the company's internship. Other than that, it was a great experience. You NEED a good group though. If your group is bad, drop it before the deadline.

David Hollan is by far the worst professor I've had at BYU. He is unsympathetic, and out of touch with what it is like to be a student today. Intern sponsors vary a lot, and if you have any issue at all, he acts like it's your fault even if your problem is your sponsor being horrible. Lectures are not useful at all and he never explains assignments

This class is entirely dependent on the TA and your project. The lectures are almost entirely useless, and there are assignments that are pointless which you need to do during your internship. Overall, the professor doesn't get involved much, lectures are useless but required. You communicate nearly exclusively with your team, TA, and sponsor only.
I was not a fan of this class or professor. If you don't need it for the minor, don't take it!!! The free labor is not worth the experience at all. I will not be putting this on my resume.
This class is easy if you just keep up with the work and meet with your team every week!
High standard of professionalism. I enjoyed his instruction in the OCI program. Resources were abundant towards our success

For this course he was very encouraging of participation outside of class. The course requires a lot of self motivation and the professor made and emphasis on the importance of staying on top of work. He provided motivational strategies and suggestions to do well.
Good professor but it was mostly the project you worked on outside of class
This Professor is kind, and willing to help students grow.
Be ready to put in the hours. Alot of your grade is based on the amount of hours you put in.
Just lock in and do your hours and exceed expectations, honestly not that hard.
Good experience. Prof. Holland has organized the course very well. Put in the hours and you'll get an A.

In the six times the class meets, Prof. Hollan gives guidance about assignments. I never got to talk with him, but I know he wants us to get the most out of our projects. I'd say your experience in this class will depend a lot on your team and your project sponsor. Some sponsors are highly involved with the team's progress, but others are not.
This class was very reasonable! The biggest things is making sure you keep track of your hours. If you don't do that, you'll be in for some rough weeks at the end of the semester.

Great experience. Mainly individual work with your group besides the few (around 6) required lectures for attendence points. You need 7.5ish hours of work on your project a week to get an A but its very doable. The actual course workload is reasonable, just some module surveys and then a big midterm presentation and final report and presentation.

The class is overall pretty east. A lot of it depends on whether or not you get a good sponsor and group, but it was very fulfilling working with them. There is a lot of busy work you have to do for your project, and the teacher seems like he hates when students ask for help. Almost seems like he doesn't want to be there, not sure why.
One of the best professors to prepare you for the real world. He really does want you to succeed. Your won't regret giving it an honest effort.

He was amazing, classes like twice a month. This class is like a part time job but so amazing and you learn so much ! I would recommend taking, and take time to look through the internship groups and don't select to many!

Professor Hollan is dynamic in his presentation and values old-school (more like battle hardened by epic professional experience at Microsoft type school) integrity, honesty and good-quality work. He has excellent guidance for how to exceed employer expectations and be ready for the workplace. He's also got some nice dad jokes.

You don't interact much with Bother Hollan, but he is very supportive and willing to help if you reach out to him. The coursework is very straightforward on Canvas and not very difficult. Your experience mostly depends on your internship and the group you are assigned to.
Mostly dependent upon what your sponsor wants you to do. A good experience overall
The best! Super caring!
He is a pretty chill professor. Class structure is weird, mostly dependent on your sponsor. I would take it again
Class is weirdly structured. Your work will mostly depend on your company sponsor.
The OCI experience was great. A lot of work but I learned a lot.
I never wanted to miss class!

This class is just busy work. Your experience and how easy the class is are determined by how good your team members are and how chill your sponsor is. Don't be too worried about the course load and getting an A. It is pretty straightforward.
He expects respect and professionalism when carrying out your presentations and other assignments.

You don't have much interaction with the professor except for a few mandatory classes. The professor doesn't teach anything new, all the learning is done on your own in Canvas but the modules are just principles that could be useful but it all depends on your internship. Classes are mostly just lectures of him telling the class to do better.
Brother Hollan is a good professor, but this class really depends more on your assigned group and your TA. If you get a good group, this class is great!
Good leader, learning depends on you

Brother Hollan is a good guy, as a professor he was alright. Your experience with this class really just depends on the sponsor and business you work for, and also your attitude when you deal with unexpected problems. 7.5-9 hours of work a week are required a week, but that's including class time, which isn't always mandatory.

Professor Hollan is very passionate about this class and takes it seriously. Expect about 7.5-9 hours total per week if you want an A. There is a plethora of companies to work with. I loved the company I got to work with and learned a lot. I would say there can be some ambiguity with the project, and it requires a good amount of time and energy.
Bro Hollan was a great guy

This class was pretty simple and upfront but depending on the sponsor that you get for your group project, the assignments and projects you do for that company can be challenging and stressful. So just pick the company you want to work with carefully

Does an excellent job at making the 6 classes per semester engaging! Some people felt they were not necessary, but I enjoyed them a lot. The idea of the class is super cool, but there are some internships that should not even exist and won't help you at all in the business world. Teacher is great, be super careful at what group you get into.

Brother Hollan is a good guy and always respectful of his students. The classes sometimes felt repetitive and unnecessary, but overall a good professor. The real thing that makes or breaks this class is having a good team and a good company sponsor for your OCI.

Professor Hollan was strict, but cared about his students success. He was very reasonable and good at motivating students to do their best work. He takes OCI's very seriously as a professional opportunity, which was very helpful throughout the semester.

This class was great! I took it to get more exposure to business in a professional setting and definitely received that. Projects are hit or miss but even with a trickier project, I still gained experience and developed many skills. Professor Hollan is just a conduit to take the class. Grading is easy and done by TAs! 7.5 hours are required a week.
He was good, SOOOO much busy work though that I felt was irrelevant but it was cool to work on on a project for a real company!
The BYU OCI is a lot of time outside of class every week.

Professor Hollan is not very empathetic or understanding. It's mandatory that you attend every class, and there's no exceptions for missing. You learn good business and professional skills from working on the project. Luckily, my group was great and my sponsor and project were good. Otherwise, I wouldn't take this class.

Brother Hollan is a nice guy, but the required classes (6 the whole semester) are useless. Lectures tend to be gospel based. 

Your experience mainly depends more on your assigned project and TA. Each project has its own unique requirements. If you get a good TA you're set. 

I learned a lot from the project part of the class. Would take gain.
Just do your work and you're fine. Class seemed superfluous sometimes. Just do 9 hours of work a week and things go okay. Canvas could be organized better.
Super easy class. The professor doesn't prepare much and his lectures feel like he is trying to burn time. But class is only a couple of times a semester since most of your class is the internship.
Great class!

This class was awesome! A lot of it is going to depend on the sponsor you get as well as the team you are put with. That really will make a big difference. I LOVED this class and it was so helpful! I would recommend... it looks good on your resume and shows the business school you are trying. This was a great experience, although time consuming.

I really enjoyed my experience overall, but it was only because of my TA and team. Prof. Hollan is very condescending in lectures, and the time spent in class is mostly completely useless. If you get a good team and sponsor, this will be a fun experience and you'll actually learn a lot!

Super nice and gospel based lectures when you do have class. Honestly, one of the most relevant classes I've ever taken. You need 7.5 - 9 hours of work weekly, so plan for a lot of work time for the internship and know that your weeks vary in how busy you are, so you'll want to get as much done early as you can.

The required lectures/modules were busywork, a lot of what he covered in lectures was obvious/felt repetitive. I enjoyed and learned a lot from working on my project with my team. Not hard to get a good grade if you put in the work, plan on 8 hours a week, just be careful not to forget to submit a module by the due date or it affects your grade.

Awful professor. Fantastic course. I had a great experience with the on-campus internship itself. But Prof. Hollan is just the worst lol. Definitely still take the course because thankfully you don't have to interact with him much. Just ask your TA for anything- avoid talking to Hollan at all costs.
Pretty chill guy. Just get your work done and you're all good.

Brother Hollan has the difficult task of teaching a standard class to hundreds of students, all of whom have widely different types of internship projects. Catering to the needs and circumstances of many with a single syllabus is difficult.

Prof. Hollan is very professional and gives great counsel during his lectures. I always enjoyed his cheesy jokes during class, and you can tell he cared about our success. The class is designed so each team has to take the reigns and figure out what needs to be done. That is difficult in the beginning, but the TA is very involved to help.
Very direct and clear instructions. Class was not every week but is required certain weeks. Class was a great experience and I learned a lot.

Professor Holland was good at keeping us on track and had good points in his lessons, but it always felt more like a seminary class all the time rather than also teaching us how to implement the course material in our on-campus internships.

The on-campus internship itself was amazing. I loved the course and learned so much, but the professor didn't help much. His classes were completely unrelated to the projects and the canvas work was just busy work. TA's weren't great either. But the class is definitely worth it.
Lectures were interesting, but we only had a few classes to attend. The rest of the time was for us to complete our projects.
Not really organized, modules were a disaster, and class was pointless. The TAs are of great help.
