I took an OCI from Brother Hollan and it was a great experience! It's definitely pretty time consuming (7.5hrs a week or more) but for the experience it was a really great opportunity. He was open to answering questions if they came up and has good TAs that help project groups too.
He is a nice guy but kind of feels like a waste of time to go to the lectures.

Professor Hollan does a good job at providing opportunities to get real world experience. Because you only go to class a handful of times through the semester and most of your interaction is with your TA, you won't really get to know Professor Hollan that well unless you mess something up bad or go out of your way to meet him. Great guy, ok teacher
He is a passionate teacher and you can tell this class means a lot to him.
In-class lectures are not super helpful, but far and few between. The skills I learned through working on the project I had with my team are priceless. Highly Recommended!!
Classes were required and helpful for knowing about upcoming assignments.
Great professor, class has a lot of homework that kind of takes time away from actually helping your sponsor company. Great class overall and great experience!
Professor Hollan seemed pretty uninvolved and didn't seem to be the most positive uplifting guy. The course gives pretty cool experience though.

Brother Hollan was really nice and passionate about his class, but I don't think the course was very organized very well. The canvas modules weren't always related to the work I was doing in my internship. A large part of how well this class went depended on how good your internship team and sponsor was. Not a hard class though, just need to work.
He can be very intense in class lectures, but he does so to show how vital this project is, and he emphasizes spending on it, as this project could really help your resume.

An OCI is what you make out of it. I would recommend signing up as soon as possible in order to have a higher likelihood of getting an internship that you're really interested in. Professor Hollan cares about his students and cares about their success.
The on campus internship is the real deal. Just make sure you have plenty of time in your schedule to put work into it, or else it will be very stressfull.
It was a fun class. I learned a lot but 7.5 hours is a little hard to carve out of a busy schedule.
Hollan has genuine care for his students.

Professor Hollan was pretty good. The Canvas course was kind of old-school looking. Not sure if he set it up that way or someone else did. I did get an A, although it took a lot of work. It wasn't hard work, just the expected hours for an internship. He tried his best to speak millennial, although he could probably use some tips from other teachers

He was pretty good. I'm not sure if it's him or BYU, but the canvas assignments were super old and out of date feeling, with rubrics for assignments not clear. However, he did explain what he expects in class clearly. He tries his best to speak millennial language and be entertaining. (he's kind of old.) Lectures are short and sweet usually.

This course requires a lot of time! The lectures and required meetings feel unnecessary but are required. The Canvas course is pretty confusing and doesn't give you much information on the assignments.
Professor Hollan is very focused on preparing students for their future careers. The lectures are required but the majority of the grade comes from the work done outside of class.
The internship was a great experience but the classes themselves were not super helpful to the overall learning/internship experience.
Only have to attend 6 classes, felt like a waste of time but weren't hard at all. Class really depends on the group you're put into.

The class is completely dependent on your group. I had a good group and we got the job done, but bad groups could make it more challenging. Direction is not super clear and classes were a waste of time, but it was free hours for me & I never paid attention. Timesheets are very annoying and would be the reason I wouldn't take this class again.

If you haven't done an internship and want easy professional experience, this is a good class to take. If you want to be told never to use AI and hear terrible dad jokes, this is the professor to take it from. Classes were pointless, in my opinion. Busywork isn't typically graded. TA didn't help me at all. But worth it if you want the experience.
The lectures for this class felt a bit unnecessary but the interactions I had with David were good! It is really more dependent on your TA and Sponsor!

This class is a good way to get real world experience and to build your resume. At times there was uncertainty with the project but as long as you follow the course guidelines you should be good. Professor Holland is very blunt but hides it behind a big smile. On multiple occasions I felt like he was very condescending and unempathetic.

This class is a great way to receive real world experience and to build your resume. There is a lot of ambiguity that comes with the project but as long as you follow the course guidelines and work with your TA you'll be fine.

Overall the class was a good learning experience. Brother Hollan comes from a place of experience and knowledge but I didn't find the mandatory lectures very helpful. I also found the course content on canvas to be a little annoying, and the dates seemed to be out of order for some of the assignments.
This professor has no empathy for his students and treats them like toddlers. The course is very outdated as well as his teaching methods.

We are required to attend a handful of classes in person but most of those classes have very little useful content.  The online content is a little haphazard and confusing.   Most of your interaction will be with the TA.  Choose your preferences for your internship carefully as it could make or break your experience.
This class is really good and I learned a-lot.

Professor Hollan was instructive and straightforward. Some students might take this as strict, but if you enjoy clear communication and proactively, Professor Holland and the class is great. It's all on you to make this class fun and worth it.

Lots of busywork and unforgiving. OCI is great if you can't find other experience outside of school. Otherwise it's just free labor. Grading criteria is hard to find/vague. We had to meet w Hollan at one point. He was condescending & we had to strategize on how to talk w him rather than being open about our situation.
The class is just busywork, but the internship can be fun and is a good resume builder.
Great guy with a good sense of humor. Inside classwork can feel a little like busywork or unnecessary but the OCI experience is a great opportunity to learn.

I did the OCI class and it was awesome

the professor is good most of the class time is spend with the team, sponsor and TA with numbered amount of lecture. lectures seem a bit pointless but other than that the class is pretty useful.

This class is really good, the teacher seems to find joy in your suffering. I got weird vibes from him and he does cold call in class. Overall the class is super fun and I loved my internship, I just didn't get the vibe that the professor was very adjustable for students

Good professor who was clear about what was necessary to excel in the class. Not difficult to get an A at all.

Pretty good experience overall. I think the classes were redundant and not really beneficial. You could honestly just post the slides online and you could look over the info in 10 minutes or less. lectures were mandatory but most were not helpful at all. likes the drama of big projects and assignments but is unclear about grading. just hope you have a good TA because they will be the ones explaining what you need to do.

Brother Hollan taught concepts in a way that was easy to understand, however I sometimes felt that time spent in class was not necessary. It was nice only having class 6 times the whole semester though.

He doesn't really do much to determine how the class operates, it has more to do with the sponsor you work with. You have rank-choice for the sponsor you have, so make sure the highest ones are projects which align with your major/job field you want experience in.
The nature of this class does not lend itself to group instruction. I would have liked a little more individual interaction or interaction between our 4 person internship group and the professor
The teacher isn't particularly helpful to be honest. Most of your helpful information comes from your TA's. The lectures are mostly pretty pointless but attendance is mandatory.

Professor Hollan was great at being very clear of what is expected out of the students. He reminds you very often of what you need to be doing and offers resources to help you succeed!

class has many developmental opportunities for students rather than just get a good grade. The internships are sometimes interesting, all depending on which one you get. He's a solid teacher, but it really just depends on the company that you get assigned with. He is pretty distant from the students and has 6 lectures that you have to go to and that's it.

This class has a little bit of a unique structure. I was confused about it so I asked the professor and he refused to help and responded in a very demeaning way. i was shocked and offended ot see a BYU professor respond in such a mean way.

It mostly depends on your sponsor and team (both were incredible for me!), however Brother Hollan doesn't actually do much. Great professor, easy to get an A. Just go to class and do your work and you'll do great!

Great on-campus internship opportunities and experiences that add to your resume. Practical real-life projects working with off-campus companies. Collaborative teamwork and independent individual work. All majors are welcome.

Just sorta lectured in class a lot. I don't mean teaching lecturing I mean lecturing like your mom does when you forget to make your bed. Class was pretty pointless but the overall OCI experience was a good learning opportunity.

Great class to take.

Class mandatory but all focus is on the project your are assigned not the class.

He is a good guy and encourages us to be creative and work hard and build our testimonies of Jesus Christ. He could really organize the course in a much better way though. This class is great for building Resume skills, Professor Hollan is great and offering advice and encouraging students to do their best!

The main thing about this class is that it's for experience to build up a resume. Professor Hollan didn't do much except facilitate our having this internship experience. If you get a great TA, they'll be more helpful, IMO. Lectures felt pointless despite being mandatory, but at least they weren't every single week.
Classes are mandatory but feel pointless. Professor Hollan is fine. I never needed to meet or talk with him throughout the semester.

The OCI was an amazing experience and I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to build their resume. Professor Hollan is a little cold but he's still a great guy and you most likely won't ever talk to him one-on-one. Attendance is mandatory but you only meet for class like 5-6 times the whole semester, the rest is meeting 2x week with your team.

He didn't care what was happening in anyone's life and refused to make exceptions. There are only 6 classes but they are mandatory. Class time was a waste and I didn't learn anything from him. The course is great because it gives you experience. Everything is turned in online. It is super easy to follow along, but the professor isn't great.
A very serious but good professor.

I enjoyed the class, my team, and the ability to have experience in an internship. The class requires a lot of work outside of class and lots of busy work. The modules feel disorganized and the in-class lectures don't add much value to your project. However, I recommend you do at least one OCI during your time at BYU

It's difficult to rate this class, given the unique nature of an OCI. There's only so much he can do when everyone is experiencing completely different projects, issues, etc. 
As far as the classwork goes, it's pretty minimal but also feels outdated and like busywork most of the time. Great guy though, and you'll have a TA that helps a lot.

Hollan is a great guy, but his lectures are worthless. I learned nothing during his class and spent my time playing chess while listening to him berate us for the sins of a past generation of students. The work for the company itself can be a good experience but Hollan tacks on a large amount of redundant modules in Canvas.

Graded on participation and self evaluations mostly. The lectures pointless and were him chastising us. My company we interned should've been vetted because thy need CS and IS majors due to the fact that they're a social media app. He's very strict on due dates and my grade was destroyed. If we had a real project it would have been worth it.

Good professor but is really into the "tough love" treatment. Every lecture we were getting scolded for what past students did. He makes his expectations clear and sets them high. This class had potential, but the actual business we were working for should have been vetted. They need CS majors to run it so we made pointless videos all semester.

Professor Hollan is a good professor but is really into the "tough love" treatment. Every lecture felt like we were getting scolded for what past students have done in previous OCI's. He makes his expectations very clear and sets them pretty high.
He gives a ton of busy work that makes the class tedious. He sometimes talks down to students. He is not very respectful. The class is not hard, but it was not very enjoyable

This class takes a lot more time than I thought it would. Each student logs time, and must record at least 7.5 hours every week. My group was great, but sometimes Professor Hollan was hard to get a hold of.

The class is fairly easy since you're more focused on accomplishing what your internship project is. Attendance is required about 6 times out of 14. Don't let the other reviews affect you too much. His teaching style wouldn't be a problem if students were more open-minded and professional. Assignments for the class are more for reflection.

This class is good in concept because it can put some good experience on your resume but the assignments that you have to do for a grade actually detract from your OCI project. This class structure needs to be redone!

Brother Hollan is a pretty stern guy. He takes BYU policy very seriously. Don't even think about taking a picture of his slides in class. He will see you and make a big deal out of it. You can tell he's a good guy though.
Just kinda mid, seems like he likes having the power
Great experience with the OCI, professor didn't show a lot of mercy but he did a good job at organizing the class.
David utilizes a variety of styles to teach effective business principles. Some of it may seem like busy work but none of it was terribly difficult.
Class was a waste of time, and super Anal about marking times. Very annoying, but the internship experience was worth it.
Good professor, good class. If you take his class, you'll do great.

Dr. Hollan is really kind, but his class wasn't my favorite. The lectures aren't engaging or useful, but attendance was required. Your enjoyment depends on the group and team you get assigned. This class is also super time consuming (must put in at  least 7.5hrs/week), and the class assignments were way more time consuming than they needed to be.

You only meet 6 times the whole semester as a class so there aren't a lot of opportunities to get to know Professor Hollan. The class was fun because you get to work with a real company, but the assignments that were for the class were not very useful.
Brother Holland is good but this class should be 4 credits. Extremely time-consuming. 7.5 hrs per week is the minimum amount of time in order to get an A

The class did give me experience through an internship but it is very hit or miss. If you have a bad group or project it will be a miserable year. His lectures are useless but you have to go. I wouldn't take the class again but I see how someone else would.
Overall good class.  Gives you some good experience to put on your resume.
This class was tough. I was sick with the flu and got a doctors note and didn't let me have an excused absence. talks a lot of nonsense but i loved my sponsor.

The class itself was not incredibly demanding. Professor Hollan has a few mandatory lectures throughout the course of the semester, but that's about it as far as in person attendance goes. Actual classwork is minimal, and most of the time you'll devote to the class depends on the demand of the project you are assigned to.
He's classes as long as you do the work, you will get an A. I wish the descriptions of things were a little more clear, but it was great.
He's like a cool military dad. I loved his lectures and analogies. As long as you're following directions, you should get an A+.

Professor Hollan is very passionate about giving students good internship opportunities. If I would have known how much of a time commitment the OCI was before I probably wouldn't have taken the class. I learned a lot from my internship but I don't think I would do it again. You spend a minimun of 7.50 hours a week on the internship.
This wasn't a super hard class, but it does require lots of time outside of class.
Professor Hollan is fine, he wants things done a certain way which is his way but it makes sense for the structure of his class.

Hollan takes the course seriously and does his best to help us learn applicable skills. However, he's really serious and can be difficult to work with. If you can get an internship outside of an OCI that is somewhat useful/applicable for your resume and career goals, I would opt for that over an OCI. It's easy to get an A but it is time consuming!

He was effective in getting the content across, but was a little unapologetic in his teaching. He did help us learn certain business skills that would help us in the long run. Overall, the experience was good, but only really good for resume building.
Great class! You gain real world experience and is a fun class to take. Brother Holland only lectures a few times a semester and you mainly just work with your sponsor.

The class is great to just get something on the resume. However the professor is not the nicest guy and the class is poorly organized. The internship can often be something that is not very useful for your field of study, but thats more luck than anything. Overall I took it but wouldn't take it again too much red tape and busy work to be worth it

The OCI is an awesome experience and I have learned a lot from it, highly recommend it to anyone. Just be aware that because it is a university class for credit there is a lot of extra coursework to do in addition to actually doing the internship stuff, which can get kind of annoying. Lots of "red tape" one might say.
Good class to get some easy credit and real world experiences.

Brother Hollan sets high expectations, which I think is good. The business experience is great and his advice is applicable however the canvas is poorly organized and the class assignments take away from being able to focus on the business needs you will work on. This is still a great course, but it has its flaws.

The professor frequently called on those who had not raised their hands. He demeaned students who answered "incorrectly." The class is poorly organized, making it difficult to understand what is required. For every large assignment, we had to meet with a TA to discuss the rubric since most of what was required was not listed. Worst BYU class ever.
Professor Hollan was awesome. He demanded the best out of us and gave us real life experience in this internship.
Great teacher, although not necessarily the most engaging

I'm filling this out to get extra credit. The course itself is great, 10/10 recommend to anyone wanting to find a first internship b/c the experience is good. Professor Holland was not my favorite - attendance is required but adds NOTHING to the project. Nothing bad to say about him, but not much good as well. He is not very involved in the class.

This class is a lot of work and time, so be willing to dedicate hours a week to it. However, I learned a lot and found it to be really valuable for me! I also got close with my team, and it was fun to make connections that way! If you want to be fully immersed in real-life scenarios, then take this class!
he is quite boring but I really recommend the course
The OCI was fun but it is kind of luck of the draw what project you will get. Try to have a good attitude and be positive about the work because it can be a hassle sometimes.

The class itself was great. Being able to learn in a work environment and also get credit for it was a great opportunity. That being said, the classwork side of things proved to be frustratingly complicated. The professor seems to care for students but goes about his class policies in an unnecessarily cynical way. Be prepared for lots of busy work.
Overall pretty easy class you might get some points taken off here and there. Some assignments are lengthy and it will take a good amount of your time to complete.

The rubrics are not followed when they grade assignments; they tell you to just "have your TA check your work before you turn it in," and then still dock you. The class was a joke and is mostly completion based except when they take points off occasionally for no reason. Hollan is rude to students and to the companies you work for.

I work 30 hours a week, getting paid for the kind of work I did for free for this class, so that was ROUGH. This class introduced me to people I am genuinely grateful I met. Class is worth meeting the people in it. The unpaid labor is unfortunate, but great for getting your foot in the door if you don't yet have experience!

I loved this opportunity—tons of cool internships and real-world experience. Just know it's a group project class, so your group really shapes your experience. Brother Hollan had no impact on my experience. His lectures have nothing to do with the class or my experience. The class assignments were frustrating because they didn't fit my internship.

Good teacher, gotta go to class for attendance but lectures were interesting and not over bearing. Homework was not difficult and reasonable, I would take this class again as I felt I gained valuable experience.

Brother Hollan is great! The class work itself is pretty chill and easy to follow. You do need to attend class but he only holds class a few times throughout the semester. The main focus is working for the company you are assigned to work with. Overall this class is a great way to be able to gain some experience for your resume.
His lectures were not my favorite, but the class was very well organized and easy to follow!
Great class. Lots to learn. Lectures were very heavy in talking about what not to do in the class. Great experience to work with companies.
The class is an easy A if you do your work. The internship can be very good experience but the class content is pretty much pointless. Worth taking for the experience and resume.
Prof. Hollan is a good teacher. He wants his students to succeed and actually learn rather than just get things done as busywork.
Had to attend class around 7 times during the semester. Prof Hollan was helpful in guiding your OCI. For the OCI internship your grade really depends on how much work you put into it.
Mandatory class only 6 times throughout the semester. The classes felt super tedious and didn't go into anything deep that students probably don't already know.
Good man but not a good professor. Doesn't have any flexibility when working with students. He has you spend most of your time doing random busy work assignments rather than helping your sponsor.
Lectures felt pretty useless at most times, but the experience with the actual companies was very helpful.

Professor Hollan was great in the fact that he really let the students deterimine their own sucess and experience with this course. He gave us the neccissary information that we needed, but let us determine how it went. The assingments for this class were very beneficial in helping us stay on track and see the progress you make.

If you are doing an OCI the class can be difficult in the sense that you have no idea what to do at the start and you kind of just have to figure it out as you go. You will hardly ever interact with professor Hollan, you will mostly interact with the TA's. The more you put into the class, the better experience you have

Use your TAs! Especially if you are doing an OCI with him each project is very unique. The TAs are helpful and understanding, but beware of professor graded assignments. Dr. Hollan will expect you to follow the criteria and structure of the class even if it works poorly with your project.

This class depends more on the sponsor you get than on the professor. If you have a good sponsor, it's valuable, if not it serves only as a resume builder. The mandatory classes are a waste of time and you have to work well on a team in order to do well.

He was very helpful when my team needed to meet with him when we were having issues with our sponsor. However, the modules are disorganized and it is difficult to find rubrics and assignment instructions. Classes are not weekly, more sporadic, but mandatory.
The class is mainly busy work, and that's what we spend most of our time doing compared to internship tasks.

Professor Hollan tries to make sure that the businesses and BYU is protected as a whole and so his lectures are pretty repetitive about us not messing up the image of BYU. I would say that sometimes the actual "class" part of doing an OCI can be pretty ambiguous with not super clear instructions so that can be challenging.

Prof Hollan clearly has experience in the field, and boy does he know it. His attitude frequently comes off as condescending, which can be rather off-putting. This class is essentially a part-time job, that you won't be paid for. If you don't work well in groups, absolutely do not take this class.

Brother Hollan has a unique sense of humor and tries to keep the otherwise boring lectures somewhat entertaining. The mandatory ~7 classes are not the most useful but required for grade. The entire class is dependent upon your team and your sponsor. Try to pick a project that you feel will allow you to do actual work and measurable results.

Good professor, I just feel that many of the assignments related to the OCI aren't particularly relevant to either of the internships I've done through the OCI program. Particularly the Work Plan. I hate the Work Plan.

OCIs are mostly out of class work, just make sure that you turn things in on time and keep up with the schedule. Hollan isn't very leanant, so as long as you know when things are due you will be fine.
Class can be very beneficial, just make sure to stay on top of the work and your project and you will have a good grade in this class.
Great professor. The class was pretty large so there was no one-on-one contact, but the class is structured well to accommodate. I enjoyed my OCI and will likely take this class again.

He just seemed to be kind of condescending in his lectures kind of like a guilty until proven innocent kind of thing. I think too many students have cheated in the past so he is very concerned about it. I feel like the whole lecture was him just begging us to follow rules that we already know we should follow because of the gospel. Internship was:)
This class isn't super hard material-wise. It does take quite a bit of time, though.
There is not much class time with the professor, almost all of the class is only with our internship groups. However, professor Holland was great in class!

Great class to build your resume with internship experience. Very doable class. David Hollan is a little harsh and strict, but that does not at all affect your class experience through out the semester or your performance/letter grade. You only attend about 6 class lectures. The rest of the work through out the semester is meeting with your team.
On Campus Internship is a great opportunity. You don't deal with the professor too much anyways.
This class was a great learning experience and very hands on. The class was pretty easy to navigate Canvas wise.

Brother Hollan is very passionate about what he does and the On-Campus Internship class, but much of the content on canvas that he assigns is very redundant and not super helpful. His directions are very clear and he sets you up for success in terms of executing the internship. Overall, the class is a great opportunity for guaranteed experience.

The class felt very oriented for a specific type of internship, and our group did not fit that mold. This created some friction with the class assignments. The canvas assignments are easy, but feel unrelated and frankly a waste of time. Get ready to clock >7.5 hours a week for an A.

I loved this class. The idea of everyone getting an internship is so clutch of byu to do. It's been incredibly helpful to my career. Huge value add. Not too stressful, good group work, nice to meet people, get experience, low stakes, learn a ton, and a lot of fun if you do it right.

Professor Hollan isn't great. But that doesn't really matter
He's pretty chill. He just has a handful of classes you attend where you just learn how to work as a team and be a good mentor. Teaches the content well and has clear assignments and grading.

He is great, however I felt like he wanted to scare his students and make them feel like they weren't doing what they were supposed to. Easy class though! It really depends on the group and company you get assigned.
He is lowk a boring professor, but he does good for helping us out with the internship.

This class is 100% your effort and time that you can put into it. In person classes felt pointless sometimes but they are mandatory to your grade. He also seemed to give my team very vague advice when we needed help. Our TA was wonderful and was able to relate and validate our struggles. This class definitely gives you the hint of experience.

This class is 100% based off of how much time and effort you put into it. Professor Hollan gave vague advice when we went to him for help, but the TAs were really helpful and were able to relate to our struggles. The class might have some growing pains but you definitely get real business experience and will be great for your resume.

The class itself is not very difficult, and your grade is mostly based off of how many hours you put in each week and completing the surveys and other assignments. I recommend looking into the project/company before signing up for it to make sure you will have work that can be used as resume builders later on.
He was a strong lecture teacher, with only a couple of lectures a semester. He covered the material clearly and prepares you well for the projects.

This class is very much what you make out of it. In-person classes were useless. The only reason I went was because attendance was mandatory. Plus, it seems like Professor Hollan doesn't care about his students. He's not rude or difficult, though. So if you get assigned a good project, this class will be chill and give you a good experience.

This class has nothing to do with Professor Hollan and everything to do with the project you get. Some projects aren't the greatest, so be careful.

It's a pretty easy class, just takes a lot of time and commitment. Professor Holland did a good job of teaching good principles to apply to your projects.
Lectures were a little dry and covered material that was already covered in Canvas. There were only a few lectures during the semester, so it wasn't bad.
He is excellent. Classes can be weird, but overall, you will have a good experience. Ensure you get along with your group and are ready to hold each other accountable.

Professor Hollan's class is extremely helpful for learning more about the business world. Attendance is required but there are only several classes during the semester. Project load can be heavy if your team is not as engaged, but overall it was a great experience!

The class structure was great. It's an amazing resource to get more company and industry experience. The lectures were not super valuable in my experience, but I am a Junior. I could see the lectures being very helpful as a freshman. It's all group project, which was great. TA's seem to dictate a lot of your grade, but they're great!
We met together 6 times during the semester to talk about how our team projects were going. The classes were pointless to attend, but there were easy attendance quizzes at the end of each class.

Solid professor, the majority of the course depends on which internship you end up getting, and how good your company is. You'll be in way more contact with them than the professor. Attendance is mandatory but we rarely had class.

OCI is a good class for building your skill set. The lectures were fine. It was not a favorite class of mine by any means, but it had its pleasant moments. Attendance and completion of things are essential.
The class totally just depends on what project you do. I loved our project so it was good, still a lot of work!
I took him for an On-Campus Internship class. He was good. Not that many assignments and good at talking to you if you need the help. You can tell that he cares.

The way the class is set up, Brother Hollan doesn't play a huge role in the class. There are only 6 lectures in the semester. The structure of the class is a little strange because there are a couple of modules about the final presentations that start around the midterm which is strange.
Honestly great real life experience doing the OCI. The canvas modules are a little tedious but you can fly through them. Goated class in my opinion and good resume builder.
professor Hollan was a good teacher, the modules were a little tedious

Brother Hollan is a good easy professor. We had class six times during the semester. Attendance was mandatory. 
When I emailed him for help during the semester and he never responded.
He has a NO AI policy which makes him feel a out of touch, especially because every other professor I have had tells you to use AI as a tool. 
Love the OCI program!
Attendance is mandatory, but class period is not very informative.

Professor Hollan is great! The OCI program was a fantastic experience and I would recommend it to everyone. Sometimes the in person classes were boring and somewhat a waste of time as all the information can also be found throughout modules. Overall I had a good experience with this class, it was a lot of work but was rewarding.

Professor Hollan is a great person! The OCI program is a neat experience and I would do it again. The in person classes aren't super useful sometimes but they are mandatory to go so not much you can do about that.

Choose your Sponsors carefully as that will dictate the experience you have in the class.The professor is only there to provide additional guidance and advice, but you see your sponsor far more than him. Remember, the sponsor company is who you deal with at all times, so pick carefully and make sure the company is one you would like to do stuff for
Pretty frustrating guy and same with our TA. Lectures are funny because they're not really helpful.

Going to class is mandatory but it really is a waste of time. The midterm and final projects are kind of ridiculous in that they grade so meticulously on things that really don't matter. The internship itself was great, but the class part of it is terrible.
Professor gave way too much homework and made assignments unnecessarily tedious. This took away from the time and energy our team could give to our sponsor.
He is awesome and is really trying to prepare us for our future careers.

Really loved this class, some of the rubrics can feel a bit vague to navigate but I got a ton out of this and if you put the work in and want to make the most out of your internship you'll have a good experience. Prof Hollan holds high expectations for the students but is really understanding and likeable.

Super solid class, I was super grateful for the opportunity to receive some real world experience from the OCI program!! Some of the rubrics are a bit confusing, but overall the class isn't difficult if you put in the work and have a desire to make the most out of the real world opportunities that is provided.

With this class, it is very important to separate the internship from the professor. I have taken this class twice and been lucky to recieve two incredible internships with great companies, however both semesters I had major issues with how Professor Hollan ran his class. You must come to this class willing to put in work to reap the benefits.

The OCI class is very busywork heavy. There is a TON of class work which takes away time from being able to work on the internship. The final report is between 80-200 pages and is ridiculous. He was always yelling at us in class and the rubrics were not clear at all. It is not worth it at all. Just get a regular internship. Worst class of my life.
This Professor and this class is super fun, but intensive. The hour limit can be a lot when you have other things on your plate, but the class does provide great experience for a resume.

Your group and TA are a HUGE part of this class. David was ignorant and didn't really do much. He failed to recognize the uniqueness of each internship and assumed everyone was having the same experience, and he never fully answered my questions. Major projects had very vague rubrics, so it was hard to understand what the assignment was.
He was a good professor. Don't like how stingy the class structure is sometimes, but David was a great OCI teacher. Loved my OCI.

It really depends on the group and sponsor you receive. I thought that the class work was just busy work and pointless. I spent my time and energy work on other stuff during his lectures. Overall, I liked my group and project. I received good experience that is valuable for my resume.

Class is great for experience, lots of ambiguity so you need to be self motivated to get things done. Overall a good experience. I wish that the experiences I received could have been applied more directly future work desires.

I had a serious health emergency and couldn't attend in person for 2 days. I explained everything, but the professor showed zero flexibility or empathy. He preaches professionalism yet fails to practice basic compassion. If you're looking for a professor who treats students like people, not policies, I'd strongly suggest looking elsewhere.

This class is on you to get the work done for your sponsor. It really depends on your sponsor if it's going to be hard, frustrating, or easy. Brother Hollan is great though, he cares about your success.  but overall it's a good experience to get some real world experience!

Overall I believe that this class was great and Brother Hollan was a great professor. A lot of this class depends on the sponsor you are assigned to. Sometimes the sponsor has very little work for you to do and getting the required time for the week can be challenging.
Really easy class but at times the lectures can make the project seem way more intense then they actually are.
Lectures are pointless. The on campus internships give you experience but isn't like the real world and is usually pointless.
Class is pointless. Everything you need to know is on the Canvas Modules. The class is easy so no complaints.
It was okay. He can be a little intense and maybe passionate about the wrong things. I feel like I learned less about business and more about BYU policy and dad jokes when he lectured.
Professor Holland is very knowledgable and helpful. He is very willing to help students one on one if they need. The class pushed me and helped me learn a lot.

I like that this class gives you experience without having to go through a heavy recruiting process! However, I felt like Professor Hollan's policies often got in the way of the work we were doing for our sponsor. He seemed less focused on us doing good work for our sponsor and more focused on the busywork we were supposed to complete for class.

It all depends on the sponsor you get and your group too. To be honest I did not enjoy the OCI because my sponsor would not provide the tools I needed. I actually started working on my deliverable 5 weeks after which ruined my time and work achievement. As I said it all depends on your sponsor and groupso good luck!
He was a great guy, the class itself was kind of mid. Its hard to get a good sponsor and it is kind of a lot of assignments. I would maybe take again.
Easy class, if you have a good group and sponsor you'll have a great time.

This class is very helpful and it helps students to be connected with real companies and get real world experience. The only problem is if you get stuck with a bad company that does not give you much guidance or projects you are stuck in a bad spot for the whole semester.
Great experience, although the class material was not the most engaging.
Lots of busy work for that class, main work load depends on who you intern for.

You barely see the professor in this class. The class is you meet like 5 times in class and then you have to have 7 1/2 hours a week of doing a project for your internship. Doesn't seem like they vet who you work for. In my experience the company had forgot that they signed up for us so they didn't have anything for us for like the first 2-3 weeks.

He was alright, felt like the class was structured for a certain type of project and ours didn't fit that mold. The stuff he puts on his Canvas page and the things he talks about in class didn't really seem all that relevant to my project. However, my project might not have been built for that information so keep that in mind.

Professor Holland tries really hard to be funny, and it feels like he belittles students and doesn't take them seriously. Quite frankly his in person is boring. He's probably a great family guy though.
He's fine, we just had class a few times and he wasn't flexible sometimes. The class is good.
Worth it if you need the experience, but if not, don't do it. Getting a good group matters a ton and a project you like

I'm sure Brother Hollan has great intentions, but all his lectures go over the same ideas and the modules are also pretty repetitive. So his class isn't very interesting but I don't blame him too much because teaching a class about "real life" seems like a tough task for anyone. I would only take this class if you have a really good reason for it.
This class was super helpful in that it paired every student with an internship, but in the actual class it was a lot of busywork that would sometimes detract from the actual internship.

If you get assigned to a good team you'll love this class. It's an easy A as long as you simply do the class. Be ready to do 7.5 hours a week in this class but it could be a great way to build your resume if you put in the work. Super easy, just try to get assigned to a good project.

I didn't feel like his lectures were very helpful as we were working on our group projects and I only went to class for attendance credit. The internship was a good experience but the class itself wasn't very helpful.

The class itself provided a great opportunity to work with a sponsor and get experience but the class itself felt outdated and many of the actual class assignments added little value and wasn't organized very well which took away from time that could be used to do additional work for the sponsor.
This class is such a cool concept. I think it could be delivered in a better way. Class work and class time felt very pointless. Working with your sponsor makes this class worth your time.
Very dependent on group, due dates are kinda funky.

This class was a great opportunity to build business experience and your resume. The experience you have is more dependent upon your team, project, and business sponsor. You do not interact with Brother Hollan that often. The classwork and mandatory classes can feel like busy work, but it is a pretty easy class overall.

I loved my sponsor (the company I worked with) but I honestly didn't really vibe with Professor Hollan.  He was a nice guy, just kind of rubbed me the wrong way.  But I did enjoy the class, you don't have class for a lot of the semester and most of the work is to get things done for your sponsor.

Good/bad depends on your OCI team/sponsor. Prof is tough&no exceptions for some grading because so many students but he is clear about it in advance>Be aware of class format, always ask TA first. You will get out what you put in! No matter what you can learn a lot and get great experience even if it doesn't go the way you hope w Prof/Sponsor/Team!

Honestly, this class depends on the type of project that you get. I found it kind of exhausting to keep up with the 7.5 hours every week. I got some decent experience though. The in class projects and class work doesn't align with our project and I didn't find productive. Our company sponsor thought the same thing.
He's a great guy and the class is well organized with clear instructions and expectations. He wants you to do well and makes it very possible.
Stick to the syllabus, be attentive in class while enrolled in this course

Professor Hollan's lectures are pretty boring. I think one lecture during the whole year had info that was actually helpful for the class. The TA's are significantly more helpful to help understand the actual class assignments. It's very much a self guided class.
He so chill and so helpful

His lectures are honestly boring but required. There's only like 5 classes to attend the entire year so that's good. He just loves his soap box and telling stories. If you communicate really well with your sponsor and team you'll be fine.

Horrendously organized class and Professor Hollan is difficult to work with. He showed no empathy to my questions and gave no explanation to his decisions on my behalf. Classwork negates full opportunity to help the internship sponsor. Wouldn't recommend unless you truly have no experience on your resume.

Your experience depends on where you get placed honestly but the class aspect gets in the way of the internship. My team had to spend the last week and a half preparing our final report and presentation for the class grade instead of doing what our sponsor needed because of our time constraints.
Disorganized class. The in-person classes were a complete waste of time

Great professor, definitely wants what's best for students. You will probably have more contact with your internship sponsor but Brother Hollan and TA's are always there to help and support. Definitely recommend if you want real world business experience!
Class seemed to be pretty unorganized and didn't feel like the professor was very helpful or understanding.

Brother Hollan is good and the class is super interesting. You only have to show up to a handful of classes throughout the year. A lot of the class honestly dependent on if you have a good group and your TA.
He is pretty good just has a lot of busy work for the OCI
He was awesome there was one class period where he felt disappointed in all of us but he was able to take correction from his TA's and was a lot better after that.

Honestly, this class is one where you don't interact with the professor very much. It's an internship with a real company, so most of the instruction you get is directly from your sponsor. However, when Brother Hollan does talk to you, his lectures are pretty good.

Great class overall! Even though every internship is different the requirements to succeed were very clear, and Professor Hollan is definitely passionate about this class and provides resources to help.
The internship is time intensive but a good experience. Get ready to put work in but you will gain good experience.

This was such a great experience! loved my squad and the internship! Be prepared to commit a lot of your life to your internship tho. It's no joke. the class portion itself felt very pointless but you need to go since there is a class quiz that you can only get the code if you are in class. class is only for half of the semester so not bad!

He once took an entire class period to yell at his students. Some students were dishonest with their work, but rather than talking to them privately, he took his anger out on all his students. 

The class was about form over fill. Only cared about how many hours we worked and how long our reports were. The classwork got in the way

Great class to put on your resume for program or job applications! This class is built to feel like you're working as an intern for a company, not like a student in a regular class. Highly recommend. Very little interaction with the professor.
Professor is a no BS kind of guy. If you do the work in the OCI class, you'll get credit. Just take the internship seriously and actually try your best because you get out of it what you put into it.
No-nonsense guy, but cares a lot about the subject and provides all the resources necessary to succeed.

The internship is good but there are requirements for the class that take away from the actual experience of the internship. A lot of the assignments are not really helpful to you at all and can be a waste of time for the company sponsor you are working with.
Taught useful skills to complete the internship. The class periods felt less effective than the modules on Canvas. Overall a good opportunity to gain working experience.

How well you like this class will entirely be based upon the company that you are assigned. Make sure to read through companies and choose ones that you would actually like. Some assignments can have a lot of grading criteria. 7 hours a week and meet with your group twice a week. Fun if you do get a good group though.

Your experience in this class is highly dependent on the company assigned, be sure to read through and actually choose things that interest you, or else it will be a long semester. At least 7 hours of work are required each week towards your project and two weekly meetings. At times lots of ambiguity, also sometimes grading criteria can be a lot.

Professor is a great guy but the guidelines he gives for the TAs and the time sheet audits are a bit over zealous. I knew many great unproblematic students that were falsely accused of staging hours or not giving enough explanation for the hours they put into their project. He does have some goo jokes though.

Professor Holland Does a good job of explaining the course and the expectations, but the difficulty of the course will depend a lot on which company you are assigned to. I would definitely recommend this class.

Professor Hollan expects high work ethic and sets that expectation very clearly. He provides resources on canvas to help with class work, however this is an on campus internship so most of the things you do will come from your sponsor. He was good at responding to questions on time and usually gave helpful answers.

He is a good professor. This class was about doing a proejct for an assigned company. Meeting with your team during the week and doing research each week is not too bad but takes time. There are multiple presentations to do but professor Hollan and the TAs help a lot and explain them well. If you and your team work well then it should be an easy A.
Lots of experience in the work place. Super awesome internship. Actual class not as demanding.
This professor is amazing to keep motivating us as students! He wants the best for us.
Work hard and stay on top of your work.
He was a very responsive professor, but also had a short-fuse when it came to work ethic. If you take the class, you have to be willing to put in the effort!

This is an OCI class. He has high expectations. But he is very nice. Honestly when taking an OCI class, its really your responsibility. You get out what you put in, and Prof Hollan gives you all the resources you need to succeed.

Super good chance to get some real experience along with credit. The course itself was a major burden though. There are presentations/assignments that you have to put together including a rather large final report at the end. Good practice for those kinds of things but they expect way too much effort to be put in apart from the internship work.
Good class, super good experience. Lots of focus on internship and a little bit on actual class.

This classes expierence depends on what company you are assigned to. My TA/Professor said i needed to attend meetings on vacation and outside of regular business hours which i was though was bs so i didn't.

Good professor, overall good class. Some of the ways that he sets up the class is really frustrating and he's not super willing to work with students. But overall good experience and glad I did an OCI.

Professor Hollan was a great mentor through our OCI project. Our team had a lot of questions and the modules answered most of them. When the midterm came around and our team had some hiccups he reached out and scheduled a meeting to see what was going on. He helped us in the right direction to end the semester strong.

He has a great system that helps you have a positive introduction into the business world. I do think that an unrealistic amount of time is spent on creating presentations and reports rather than being able to do work for our various sponsors.

Dr. Hollan's class was great! I learned a lot through my OCI and I was glad I did it. He was a great professor and lead the class well. Expectations were set very clearly and any help you need is given in a timely manner.

Professor Hollan is a great teacher and presenter. We didn't have class every week but each class we did have taught me something important that helped move the project forward. I appreciate the help he provided our team and the resources that were provided to help figure out how to execute our project. No tests, just presentations/ reports

This OCI is structured super heavy. I am a super ambitious, motivated, and trustworthy person, so the structure and setup of this internship was not great for me. Beware that there is so many different experiences, but my experience was totally trash. Waste of time and effort, and many days I questioned why I was in this internship at all.
The class is a lot of work, but it can be very beneficial if you put the work in. It can be resume building and experience driven. Make sure to select a project that really interests you.
Had a great experience with the class. Their was a lot of busy work but it was doable and it's not hard to get a good grade.

He was fun and engaging. I enjoyed his lectures, and everything made sense. I wish we were able to have more guidance from him directly because it sounded like he has a lot of valuable experience but we were more connected to his TAs. There are only a handful of in-person lectures so nothing crazy.

He's super tough on the timesheet. Just make sure that you fill it out every week. If you don't fill it out before Saturday, you will receive a zero, with no exceptions. I strongly disliked this part of the class. He leaves barely any room for extenuating circumstances.
The canvas modules weren't very helpful but he was an energetic lecturer and the lectures didn't drag on.

I was very disappointed with the organization and execution of this class. I thought it would be a cool opportunity to gain a valuable experience to add to my resume and work with a company—it was not. I would not recommend this class for internship experience, look elsewhere.

Overall, the class is not bad. Just work the hours and make sure you do what your sponsor wants. He scares the students during lectures even though the TA's grade pretty easy. A lot of dumb homework assignments that had nothing to do with the project at hand.
Very vague instructions and almost impossible tasks. Sponsor was tough to communicate with sometimes as well.
Great Professor!

He's a business man and he knows his stuff. While I may not always agree with his methodology of things, he's successful for a reason and there is something you can learn. Prepare to apply yourself, endure dad jokes, and to get your stuff together.

I LOVED this class though. If you're interested in doing business but don't know what you want to do specifically, this is a great class to help you figure that out. However, this is NOT a blow-off class. You will be spending 7.5-10 hours per week on your project.

I enjoyed this class and 100% recommend it. There are only 5 lectures in the semester, but attendance is required. The canvas work might be "busy work," but it offers great information and direction if you're lost. I also really enjoyed my project, which I didn't expect going into the class.

This class is whatever you make it.

This class was decently helpful although I didn't feel like Professor Hollan was super involved on a personal level with people. Seemed like a nice guy though, didn't mind his lectures although they didn't feel that important/necessary to me
He is a good professor, however very stern. He cares a lot about the church and staying organized.
His lectures were engaging and he had a lot of passion for the class, however, I felt like some of the coursework was unnecessary.

The idea and concept for this class is great in theory, but I think there needs to be some restructuring to how this course is ran. Less busy work for the class and more focus should be put on working with your sponsor. This class can be great if you get put into a project for work that you are passionate about.
He was intense but a good teacher. The OCI itself was an incredible experience.

The project itself is awesome. The lectures and canvas work are a 100% waste of time. The midterm presentation, final report, and final presentation are also a complete waste of time. So frustrating. The coursework on canvas is also super unorganized. Again, fantastic project, but everything else is just ridiculous.
I took his class for my OCI (on-campus internship). the class that we had I just went for the attendance quizzes and to be honest it didn't help with my internship or with the sponsor.

Experience really depends on your sponsor and your team. Put in some good research beforehand and make sure everyone on the team is dedicated. Professor Hollan expects that you are professional and represent the school well. Also a lot depends on your TA.
The professor was really helpful, and if you had any problems he was very happy to help. Attendance is mandatory, but if you go to class and work well with your team you will be fine.

This class gives you good experience and is an excellent learning opportunity. I understand that the lectures were necessary but they did not feel useful for my project. The expectations for my specific project from our sponsor were clear, but the expectations for my specific project from Professor Hollan were not clear.

You can put this class on your resume which is nice, but it requires so much work. It is a great class to take if you are passionate about the project you sign up for, but you need to clock in 7 1/2 hours each week.

David Hollan is fine, but half of the 100+ hours you will put into this class will be just for busy work for the class. Let us do our internship. That is why we are here. You have to meet with a group 3 times a week, two group meetings and a meeting with your sponsor, plus class, plus busy work and plus just doing the actual internship.
If your are very accountable and have enough time to set aside 7.5 hours to complete work, then your get an A.

Hard to rate Hollan because you only go to class a few times, but work with your group for several hours a week so ratings are more contingent on group and project than anything. Clear grading criteria, TA readily available. This is a very time consuming class requiring 7.5-9 hours per week as part of your grade. I had a good experience overall.

Professor Hollan is passionate about what he does. I don't think this class is very involved though. The class and internship dynamic does not blend very well in all honesty. There was also bad connection between Hollan and the sponsor. I have heard that the OCI is either a way good or way bad.
Lectures are pointless but required for participation grade. Most important person is your sponsor. Class assignments are busy work and try to help you in your project but rarely do.

You spend no time in class (maybe 6 lectures you have to show up to). The difficulty of this class is not determined by Professor Hollan but the internship you get. Could be anywhere from 100 total hours to 300. Great class for a resume and MSB application but a huge time commitment. No tests, no studying, just a lot of projects.

We didn't see him much but he gave us good feedback on our internships. He has high expectations and when we as a class didn't live up to them he let us know but overall he was good and made the internships easier.
Overall great class and professor.
Great professor and class overall.
This class was tough but it was great experience and a lot of fun.

You're only required to attend class 6 times, which is nice. However, the online course content in Canvas often felt like a waste of time. You're also required to average 7.5-9 hours a week for internship work, so make sure to set plenty of time aside for that. Regardless, it's good experience for pre-business students and a great resume builder.

Professor Hollan is a great professor and his lectures were interesting and you can tell he cares. I gave him a difficulty of 3 instead of a 2 or 1 isn't because any of the course work is particularly challenging. Actually it's quite manageable, but what is hard is making 7.5 to 9 hours for the project. With three meetings sprinkled in those hours.

Professor Hollan is a great teacher! His lectures were internesting and gave me a lot to think about. Especially about the business world as a whole. The reason I put the difficulty as a 3 isn't that any of the course work is challenging, it's actually quite manageable. What was hard for me is finding 7.5 to 9 hours a week to spend on your project
Loved the OCI. The only downside was that our sponsor thought we were going to work 20 hours a week instead of the required 7.5-9. I felt like that could've been better communicated beforehand.
It was a good class but had this weird thing about only using microsoft teams, even if our sponsor felt more comfortable using a different platform.

Professor Hollan told us we were the worst group of BYU students he had ever worked with. I loved my project and my group and sponsor, but Professor Hollan was rude when we had a question about something with our project and truly expects your entire life to revolve around the OCI.
would take again

Professor Hollan has put together a great course for those looking for a simple way to get into business. The course is really only as good as your project and team. Some assignments felt redundant but I believe this was just Prof. Hollan doing his best to make sure no one screwed up and make BYU look bad. Good for fresh/soph or pre-business
Good class. Pretty simple as long as you do your homework and do good in a team environment. Attendance is mandatory.

OCI is a great opportunity and a great class to take to gain business experience. Only required to attend class about 6 times, which is nice because it gives you more time to complete the required minimum 7.5 hours per week working on your project. Professor provides helpful information and is clear on due dates, was sometimes frustrated with class

Professor Hollan cares deeply for the success of his students. He wants them to embody the values of BYU alumni. He does what he can to ensure you get help, and can get the most out of your experience.
I thought this was a good course overall. I would recommend that if you don't get a good internship company just drop the class
I felt like Professor Hollan could have engaged more with OCI groups to help guide them towards success more. The online course material was useful, but the lectures felt like a waste of time.
Prof. Hollan is not really a good professor but OCI's are so helpful! Take an OCI!!!

It was a lot of work because you are working directly with a sponsor but Brother Hollan gave good resources to work with. Additionally, the TA is another good resource for feedback on the midterm presentation, final presentation, and final report. I loved the experience I had with the sponsor I worked with. Would recommend taking this class!

Its a good class to get experience on the resume but really depends on the project you are assigned to, your group, and your TA for how impactful and useful your experience will be. Class periods are more so just to faciliate your project, as thats the main focus of the class.

In the 494R MSB class, you are doing a group project. You have to attend class like 6 times. Almost all of your instruction comes from the weekly modules outside of class, and very little instruction and guidance in the actual classes, they are just a reminder of your timeline. Be ready for some heated lectures when deliverables are closing in

Professor Hollan is a really smart dude. His lectures are really good. His class can feel a little disorganized at first, but after a week or so you get the hang of it. TAs are a huge part of this class. Some are super helpful and want you to succeed (like mine) but I've heard of others being a huge headache.
Dave is an awesome guy!
Professor Holland is very funny and connects well with the students. He makes it very clear on the work you will have to do throughout the semester.

This was a great opportunity to receive real internship experience. Professor Hollan was great and was super passionate about us doing a good job to help our companies. My only gripe is that some of the classwork didn't really align with the project and deliverables that we were working on. Regardless, Professor Hollan was great.
Great professor, cares about helping students.

This class is a great to help give real world work experience. Make sure to set aside at least 7.5 hours each week for this class. Professor Hollan is a great professor that wants you to succeed, but makes you take responsibility. His lectures are good and help to explain the assignments.
Lecture attendance was required but offered little to no substance. The opportunity can be great, but be prepared for busy work that isn't very informative.
The internship was great! Sometimes the classwork would seem counterintuitive since it often interfered with the progress on the project.
Good! lots of hours.
Great Class! Kind professor, he makes things clear.
I think this class is a lot of busy work that detracts from the actual internship experience. While it's not hard to get a good grade, I feel like the class has much wasted potential.

There's a lot of unnecessary busy work. It can be a good experience if you get the right project and the right group, but there's still a lot that the professor and TA's are super picky about for no reason. You work a lot with a TA, but it's kind of luck of the draw with how responsive and helpful they are.

Everybody has a different experience in this class because it's based on which project you get.  Treat this class more like a job rather than a class and you'll succeed no matter which project you get.  This class will give you experiences that you will talk about in interviews.  Brother Hollan seems more like a boss than a professor.
Lectures are a little redundant but he's a good professor and is very smart.
Good teacher, mostly valuable information but occasionally felt like he was unmotivated to teach or just wanted to leave.

The opportunity to work with real businesses was great. However, the class is poorly structured and not efficient at all. In fact, if you do work efficiently, in some areas it penalizes you, even if you do a great job and exceed expectations. It is focused on time spent, not results. Most class periods are mandatory and a colossal waste of time.

This class is an excellent opportunity for people to get real hands-on experience. It's challenging in a good way and the TAs can be helpful but only if you get a good one. Professor Hollan can be stern, but he wants his students to succeed and he offers great insights if you ask him questions during and after lectures. Very much would recommend!
This class all depends on who you get in your group project and your TA if you don't have a good luck of the draw you are out of luck.

This is a relatively easy class, but this varies depending on your sponsor and the workload that they give you. The workload for the class assignments is not much if you manage your time well and prepare in advance for the midterm and final presentations. Overall a great class to take and learn from.

This class requires very active participation and the whole semester is one ongoing group project. You are required to meet with your team for 1 hour twice a week and with your sponsor for 1 hour every week and then put it a total of 7.5-9 hours every week. Hours cannot be made up. Profess Hollan is intense but cares deeply about student learning.
A lot of this is busy work, however if you put in some good work you will learn valuable things about how a company works and how you can have an impact.
Class is a lot of work, can sometimes be confusing and hard, professor can be intense but he really does care about your learning. Wants you to do well.

This class is a lot of work, you go to a weekly class meeting where most of the time you don't learn anything new or applicable, because you already went through all of the information in the canvas modules prior to class. You spend more time with talking to your TA than with Professor Holland, but overall you learn good skills in this class

The professor Dr. Hollan is a very good professor.  The real trick to this course is what sponsor and project you get.  I got a bit a tough project and the sponsors were a bit tricky to work with, but I learned a lot of good lessons.  It it teaches you so much about how to work in the real professional world.

I was disappointed with the structure of the class. 3 credit hours, but you are required to work 7.5-9 hours a week, and report your work on a timesheet each week throughout the entire semester. 

Make note of that time requirement before you sign up for the class, or you may be deceived into doing much more work than you bargained for, like I was.
Dr Holman was very insightful and was a great mentor. I would recommend him 100 times over again.
Had a great experience with the professor but what is more impactful in this course is the sponsor you recieve. Only a couple mandatory classes during the semester.

He is not very amicable. He also does not work with his students on things. I had a very reasonable request, and he shut me down pretty hard. I am not putting the request here not because it looks bad, but because it is a lot of typing, and I don't have that kind of commitment to this post.

This class offers a fantastic opportunity to get real-world experience through an on-campus internship. While the course content doesn't always align perfectly, the hands-on learning and professor support make it worthwhile. Unstuckstudy AI was a helpful study tool alongside the free textbook.

The class it self is super easy. However working with Professor Hollan is the worst. I had jury duty the day of a midterm presentation (we tried to move the presentation but the sponsor could only do that day). Even though I let him know in advanced he wouldn't excuse my absence. I had to go to the dean for help.

This class consists of modules meant to support you in your on campus internship. The internships themsevles are helpful, but the quality of your experience rgely depends on your teammates and your sponso. Im giving a relativley low quality rating becuase the course itself only occasionally aligns in a useful way with the goals of the internships.

This is an internship class so he isn't really involved other than having to go to class six times. You work with your internship sponsor and your teammates. You do have a feedback survey you fill out multiple times for your teammates which is nice, and you work heavily with a TA.
This class gives you such a great opportunity to get a real life work experience! I highly recommend especially to those applying to the Marketing program!

You don't interact with Professor Hollan much, it is mostly between you and your sponsor and your team. He is a bit intense but a good professor.The hardest part is the final report which is a LOT of work, so be ready for that. This is a really great opportunity for you, IF you are ready to put in at LEAST 7.5 hours of work towards it each week.

This class CAN BE one of the best you take at BYU. A lot of it depends on the amount of work you are willing to put into it, what company you are assigned to, and how you work with your team. The coursework itself is super easy and feels a bit extraneous, but will nicely pad the 7.5 hours you will need to log each week to get an A in the class.

There were only 6 in person class times the whole semester. Basically the class is built to give you a template and structure for your internship. Basically all of the work you do will be for the company you are assigned to, and very little is required for class assignments

This class was great! He sets it up in a way that you can learn a lot on your own while still getting guidance for business processes. Attendance is mandatory, but there isn't class every week. Be prepared to meet weekly with your internship team.
This class was challenging, but I enjoyed the project and group I worked with and grew significantly as an individual.

Professor Hollan is great! He is a serious guy and expects you to be very professional, but that is because he has to look over 200 ish projects for the whole semester! Your OCI will be the determining factor if you like that class or not. Overall Hollan is super helpful and nice when you meet him!
This class was great but time consuming. You are required to spend at least 7.5 hours a week on it, which makes sense for a 3 credit hour class.
The classes are required, but they are not very useful. If you put in the work, it is a great experience to talk about in future interviews and include on your resume.

Although the content that was taught in class didn't always have a clear relation to my specific project, I still learned a lot from attending his lectures. He has a great system with lots of connections to tons of different companies so if you want real world experience this is the class to take. I really enjoyed my on-campus internship.

Professor Hollan clearly outlined expectations concerning deliverables and what to except from our internships. We were prepared and equipped with everything we needed in order to have a great internship!
He is awesome!
Overall a solid class. Does not budge on the syllabus/turn int dates, so do not forget to get anything done.

Professor Hollan is one of the greatest professors I've had. He does not beat around the bush in class and only uses the amount of time thats needed to say what he needs to. He is so good at inspiring us to do our best.
He goes over the material well. Slightly repetitive sometimes, but he just makes sure you know what the expectations are and how to get 100% in the course which is good.

Great course that is completely autonomous. You can plan out your hours, work with an awesome team, and make sure you research which project you want before hand. It also is a great resume builders for those with little to none experience.
he is amazing! pick an internship you are interested in and you will love this class! need to spend 7.5-9 hours a week for this class/internship.
He cares about his students and is very knowledgeable! I would definitely take his class again

Great professor! It was more of a hands-off learning style. He taught basic principles in class and then gave us the resources to apply them to our on-campus internship projects, which worked perfectly. He had enthusiasm for our work and encouraged us to succeed. Overall, wonderful experience!
very good class! the difficulty can range depending on if you get a great team or not! my group was amazing!!
He is a great professor

I had Professor Hollan for a class for students participating in On Campus Internships. Although classes weren't my favorite, I loved my project and I am very grateful for this class as it taught me so much and prepared me for my future career. I would highly recommend!

A must if you want to start an internship! You have TA's who are there to guide you every step of the way, professor does great giving lectures on items that are important (there are weeks you won't need to go to class), and you gain hands on experience. NO TEXT BOOK needed but you will have to spend at least 7.5 hours a week on your internship.

Professor Hollan is great. He made good dad jokes. I loved that he never let a class go over 30 mins long. He was good at answering questions when I had them. To be honest his lectures were full of pretty common-sense information.

This class was awesome! YOU LEARN A TON! Real world scenarios! I loved the project that I worked on. I also loved his dad jokes in class. They made me smile. He was kind and really wanted us to succeed. I liked how he focused on the gospel throughout class.
He seems strict but you don't interact with him that much. Very helpful class for the resume booster as well as good real world experience
He was good at engaging the class, and helping us to understand what needed to be done for the companies we were working with.

The class was great! It requires about 7.5-9 hours per week and the first few weeks are difficult in trying to figure out how the course works and what needs to be done. However, it's great real-world experience and I feel like it will help out in getting future internships

He is a really nice guy but the class wasn't very engaging and the canvas was very messy. A lot of assignments were general and didn't have anything to do with my specific project. He will talk a lot about sand castles. Have to do at least 7.5 hours of work each week even when your sponsor doesn't want you to or has nothing left for you to do.

This class was great! I loved my project and my group. Professor Hollan was helpful although his lectures were highly repetitive. As someone who has already taken many business classes at BYU, I struggled to stay engaged during class. He is very old fashioned when it comes to AI which is strange compared to most other business professors.

This class provides a good opportunity to get real-life experience working in the business world. Be prepared to put in 7.5-9 hours per week and to feel lost at times. It is mostly self/team-directed which builds great skills but can be frustrating. You'll get out of this class what you put into it! Overall, I learned a lot!
It's a relatively easy class but it is time-consuming. As long as you put in the work you'll get a good grade.
