This class was very good for me to gain real life working experience! Professor Hollan was slightly helpful, but I had a great TA and they were great. Pray you get a good team and a good project! 7-10 hours per week required!

The class was great! It requires about 7.5-9 hours per week and the first few weeks are difficult in trying to figure out how the course works and what needs to be done. However, it's great real-world experience and I feel like it will help out in getting future internships.

The internship demands a lot of time, about 7.5 to 9 hours a week is preferred, but the experience of working on an actual product or project is really cool. The first few weeks are so hard because you are trying to figure everything out and how to do it, but it is fun, useful, and real-world experience that will help you with interviews.

Make sure you are self-motivated for this class, because you pretty much do everything on your own time. You meet as a team regularly, as a class a few times, but everything else will be on your own. It is good business experience though!

Professor Hollan teaches a very structured course and tends to have a hands-off teaching style. What you put into this course is what you will get out of it. Be selective and thorough with your project ranking; the sponsor you're working with will heavily influence your class/internship experience.

He was a respectable guy. I appreciated his willingness to help us if we asked. I also appreciated that he knew most of us were taking the class for resume and skill building and helped gear us towards that!
If you need resume experience then this class is worth it, but I would try to find it elsewhere if you can (a job or internship). The projects here are pretty hit-and-miss.

The experience you have in an OCI project depends almost entirely on the sponsor/project you get assigned, so make sure you choose wisely when ranking your choices. You'll only go to class 6 times, and attendance is mandatory. Sometimes class projects get in the way of your internship, which is frustrating, but the overall experience was good.

If you do the modules (not hard), punch in the weekly time, go to class (attendance quiz but easy), and have a good working relationship with the company (deliverables, etc.) then it aint bad. Be slightly picky and actually read about the company when you choose which one you want. I had some friends who got stuck in projects they did not like.

Prof. Hollan truly cares about your success in MSB 494R. He sets clear guidelines, you only have class like 8 or so times throughout the semester for like 30mins or so, your grade is based mostly on group projects, and the TA's are a great support. Grading is not tough at all, anyone can get in A so long as they put in the time and effort. 10/10
Professor Hollan is great! His lecutures were inspring and uplifting.
Professor Hollan did a great job of making this semester fun and stress-free
Professor Hollan really cares about Integrity
It's a very good program, MSB really helps me to gain experience and it has been awesome
He really likes to go on a power trip, and do not expect any given leeway on assignments. Just do the canvas things on time and do not add the class even a day late!

This class is a great opportunity if you do it well. Be cautious to apply for internships you are interested in and focus more on the internship work. The class is secondary to the work you're actually doing, but you need to insure you are on top of all assignments-- they aren't hard, just tedious. You'll be fine.
Teaches with the Spirit and encourages you to be excellent in word and deed.

One of the more useful classes that can be taken at BYU for any aspiring Business Grads. It is no gimme, a minimum of 7.5-9 hours of work per week, which is tracked and mandatory. But it is among the best resumes a class can generate.

Your experience depends on the team and company you pick. Do your research on the company to pick a project you care about.
My team was great, although I didn't enjoy working with my sponsor. We had just one issue but Professor Hollan was very supportive and helped us to solve it. TAs are great.
Attendance is mandatory for a few lectures.

Don't take this class for the professor or for the grade. Take this class for your freaking professional future so you can put something on your resume and aspire to a better job. Literally a game changer.

This class very greatly depends on the group and company you get assigned to. I had a great group and company, so I had a good experience. This class is a lot of what you put into it though. If you want it to be a good experience, you have to work hard yourself. No one is going to force you to learn things and have a good internship.
Great professor, really wants you to succeed.
Great Professor overall! Mostly a self-guided course and lot of learning on your own depending on what internship you get. Class once a week
amazing class to grow - he gives you a lot of opportunity to learn. There's a class code to show that you made it to class but it's a fairly easy class.

Try and be very detail-oriented. OCI is professional in nature, and Prof. Hollan really wants you to experience that. As a result, a lot of the class assignments feel very detail-heavy and sometimes repetitive. Overall the experience of the OCI is great and can aide you in getting into the MSB and prepared for real work.

This class gives a good experience if you are interested in Marketing, as that is what a lot of the internships are geared toward. It was a cool experience, but your experience is based on your Sponsor. Professor Hollan is really funny and is willing to help answer questions. They do assign each group a TA, and that was super helpful.

Professor Hollan is the best! His lectures are engaging and informative, and the course as a whole helped me develop tons of new skills. You definitely need to apply yourself, but they do everything possible to set you up for success.
He's alright. He gives some dad jokes in class, but the class is more self guided and really depends on the internship.
Very few classes but attendance is mandatory. Very instructive class. Would recommend to recieve real life experince.
Professor Hollan is great, the class is well structured, and it's easily possible to get a good grade.
Lot's of busy work and unnecessarily long reports.
Solid class and I loved the project with the sponsor. Felt like a lot of the modules were busy work.

Helpful class designed with a lot of resources to help you succeed in your internship. In-person classes mostly felt redundant, but it was nice to get points simply for showing up. Felt a little like he was more concerned with BYU's reputation than helping students succeed, but overall an awesome professor, and I got a lot out of this class.
Good class but I never felt that I needed the 7 lectures we were required to go to.

Professor Hollan was an average professor. We only went to six lectures throughout the whole semester, and I didn't feel like I necessarily gained anything useful from them. The TA's were the real helpful ones during this class and in my opinion did most of the work, while professor Hollan was kind of just there the whole time.
You get out of it what you put in. If you're not excited about the sponsored project, the class is fairly dull. The best part of the class was our project with our sponsor, not the class itself.

Dr. Hollan did not help students when we were having issues with our company. He chose to meet with the Sponsor first and chose to ignore the red flags the Sponsor showed. Because we had a terrible Sponsor/company I did not do anything valuable and I would not recommend this course. He was hard to approach and did little to help us.

I felt like this was a huge waste of BYU's resources. It is a tough task to coordinate on such a large scale, but I was often frustrated by the outdated study materials and aspects of this project that made it much more "school" and a lot less "work." If you don't have to take this class, I wouldn't. There are much better ways to get experience.
He is alright

Professor Hollan wants to make sure you succeed in your internship projects. The modules were sometimes a little tedious, but they were still manageable. This class totally relies on your own ability to put in the work and get stuff done for your sponsor company. I got a ton of valuable experience, would totally recommend.
This is a great class to get experience helping a company and working with a team. The one hard part for me was reaching the hours needed, but everyone is different.
This is a great class to take if you're looking to build your resume!
Great class, fun, and interactive. Sometimes can be annoying but I recommend.

P Holland was cool. The module work on Canvas we had to do for this class felt pretty useless and not applicable to the work I needed to do for the company I was an "intern" for, but besides that, if you pick a good company to "work" for that you will enjoy and help with your resume, this was a good class. I enjoyed the company I worked.
awesome class!! I'm planning on taking this class again next semester !!

Def recommend an OCI! The structure of this class was great. The TAs and professors are pretty accessible and grading is straightforward. I suggest signing up early for a better pick of the internships but either way it is worth it!
A really useful class, but the mandatory attendance classes seemed to repeat the same information with story telling that wasn't relevant to the tasks in the course.
Talks down to his students a lot and wasn't an engaging speaker at all
He's great! You will learn a lot from this course
It is an internship class and in all honesty, the grade you get is determined by how hard you work.

Professor Hollan is a nice guy but he is too focused on making his class the most important that you have that it detracts from the actual learning and makes the class far less enjoyable. The class itself is worth taking but just know the prof is too focused on himself being the best professor on campus to actually help you with things.

The internship was awesome. TAs were super helpful. The mandatory classes were repetitive of online work. There are a lot of little assignments that if you miss, your grade will go down a lot. Overall, I would take this class again.

I loved the internships, and it was very fun and I loved my team. The mandatory classes are a waste of time, and the grading is so specific and if you do everything right but record it on the wrong platform and upload it to the right place, they dock your grade even if everything is right about your project and your work. Loved what I learned tho!

He was fine. I got the sense that he was some kind of big wig during his career and he wants all of us to know that? He seemed slightly arrogant to me. I don't know why though. He never did anything to me, but I got that feeling as he lectured.
The internships are amazing but sometimes the course doesn't line up with the internship.
Lectures are mandatory. Extra credit is offered throughout the semester to boost your grade a little bit. Overall not a bad professor.
Great professor, was available if you needed help. You have to participate and stay caught up. Other than that, it was a straight forward class. Do your project for your sponsor and work your team.
Useful class and he does a good job teaching

MSB 494R is a class you should take seriously. Honestly, my interactions with David were limited due to how few real classes there were so my rating is neither good nor bad. But take my advice, this OCI experience will be everything you make it to be-- if you treat this like a class, don't take it. Take it if you will treat it like your project.
Wanted students to succeed in the internship and provided everything you needed to do so.

Professor Hollan did a great job of helping us a students to succeed. He gives great guidlines to help in the ambiguous projects that are assigned. If you are looking for a guarenteed, real world working experience, take this class!

This class is easy to excel in but requires a lot of work. Only 6 classes required attendance. Your experience will depend heavily on your team. If you have a good team its awesome, if not its very stressful and a bad experience
He is a great teacher who definitely cares about what he is teaching. The class isn't very hard except near the midterm and final.

Disappointed overall. I had a really great team and sponsor/company. However, Prof. Dave Hollan and our team's TA really fell far below my expectations. Instead of aid, they built roadblocks like telling our company sponsor to intentionally create ambiguity. When I asked questions, I felt as though I was challenging their authority or power.

The class itself is an interesting premise. Very cool opportunity to basically be handed an internship. Your experience will HEAVILY depend on the internship you are matched with, your group, and your TA. Has potential to be really interesting and fulfilling, but also could be really annoying and painstaking. Just be aware of that.
Depending on the company you get to work for it can be an incredible learning experience in a real business environment. Would take the class again.

Would recommend this class. I'm not going into business but have found that the projects done through these internship teams grant good real world experiences. This is a resume booster and would recommend this if you are looking for an experience that isn't a lecture hall type class.

I listed Professor Hollan as hilarious because of his dad jokes.
Professor Hollan is a great professor and is not too hard. I was nervous about taking this class and completing an OCI, but he makes this class doable and manageable.
Really great class. The quality of your experience is largely up to you and the company you get assigned to.

The class is designed for your team to help your sponsor and do assignments from them so you see Prof Hollan like 5 times in mandatory class and you just get an update on things due and then he lets you leave. Not all projects are created equal so really take time selecting which ones you would like.

I took Professor Hollan for my OCI. He's a great teacher. The only reason I didn't give him a 5/5 is because I didn't have any interactions with him. OCI's are mostly done with your team and sponsor, so I didn't know him well enough to rate him a 5/5. It's evident that he cares about his students from the lectures and makes them meaningful.

Personally this internship wasn't my favorite experience. The class seemed very unorganized. I went to the professor with questions and thoughts about my project and I felt that he didn't handle them in the best way. It was a little discouraging. However I had a GREAT team! That was probably the best part of this class for me.
This professor was super helpful in guiding us to be good interns for the companies we were assigned to  I learned so much and grew as a person through this class.
He is a great professor with clear guidelines for success in his class! I took an OCI from Hollan and had a great experience!
Good professor if you are taking him for an OCI.
Good class, The class periods could have been better, but they're not the focus of the class so its not a big deal

Professor Hollan does a great job at facilitating the OCI projects. Each project is so different, so it is hard provide an all encompassing rating. Something to be aware of is that you have to dedicate 7.5-9 hours a week to your project. There are a few small reflection prompts on canvas but other than that it is fully working with your sponsor.

Doing a OCI was an amazing experience and I recommend eveyone do it. Professor Hollan himself was a decent professor, he was funny and very clear in the few lectures we had to go to. The structure of the class isn't my favorite and grading can be confusing as far as what is expected of you.

I thought the experience in this class I gained from working with an outside company was amazing. However, the class periods outside of the internship itself could have been far more effective. I also didn't find the homework assignments useful. Overall though it was a great experience and a really good resume builder.
Great opportunity if you are looking to beef up your resume. Alot of work though, so don't take a heavy course load.

Professor Hollan is fairly easygoing, but he does require attendance for the weeks class is held. He is inflexible with those. The final report of the internship must be around 100 pages in a pdf, so if you take the class start early!
He was strict but helped the class be hardworking!

While he is the professor, you work mainly with your group. He didn't come to our midterm presentation. He tells jokes! He reminds you of things during class. I don't remember how he teaches or conveys material (we only have class 6 times and it doesn't always last 50 minutes.) You work on canvas some as well.
Chill class but you do need to attend. You work with a different company as an internship so you don't really interact with Professor Hollan much but he shares great dad jokes.

Professor Hollan is good about helping his students gain real world experience. Often, he will help us to think of our own solutions to problems in order to prepare us for the future. He is very future focused.

While Professor Hollan was okay, I disliked the structure of this class. I don't think it should be a class, but should be a program hosted by BYU if possible. The assignments we had to do for the class did not help in our project and got in the way too often. I would recommend making this a program or just going directly to a company to interm

This is a good class for anyone wanting to get experience in the real world. I unfortunately was assigned a project with a sponsor who was unprofessional and the project was kind of a joke but that clearly was not Professor Hollan's fault. He's a good guy.

In the On-Campus Internship class it was very hard to get help from the professor and I felt little to no love from him. The help that was offered honestly wasn't very meaningful. The assignments on canvas and lectures that he gave were honestly pointless and just busy work to make it a course worth credit.
Great teacher. Attendance is mandatory but only a few times throughout the semester. Not too much work from the professor a lot is just focused on the sponsor and the team you are given for the OCI
Most of the work is outside of the class with an external company. You don't work much with the professor. Fun class, internship experience.
He was a great professor i just didn't like my OCI. Honestly if you get the right OCI this is a super chill class

The course itself was great, but we didn't get know Dr. Hollan cause the class is so big. I kind of wish there was more flexibility with making up missed classes. They weren't very effective. The TA for your team though is super helpful, so stay in contact!
Hard teacher but he cares a lot for the success of the students! He is serious and has really high expectations. If you don't meet his "expectations" then you feel belittlel and small.
The class itself was great! However, the professor was always mad at the class for whatever reason. Attending class was pointless but the experience of the OCI is awesome.

He was a great professor but his classes felt very limited. Sometimes it felt like he didn't want to be at the few lectures we had. Attendance is mandatory, but by no means would be necessary to perform well.

This class is great for those who want to get experience with companies outside of the university and build their resume. The class is very simple, and you get what you put into it. Class is mandatory otherwise that'll hurt your grade. Awesome experience.
This course was great in terms of getting real world experience for jobs and the business school. Overall great experience!
He is a great guy and wants you to succeed in his class!

David Hollan as a professor does the bare minimum, which makes sense given how many different classes/teams he is responsible for. However, he could definitely make an effort to be more approachable and personable. Don't get me wrong, the OCI experience was great... but honestly I would say that David Hollan adds little (if any) value to the class.

Professor Hollan is a great teacher and has set up a good way to get professional experience. He is always there for support and guidance on projects. I enjoyed his lectures and his modules create a good learning experience for anyone wanting to increase professionalism and gain more business knowledge.

Professor Hollan gave good analogies and is very clear on expectations which is good. The class is set up where you work in teams which was super awesome. The thing that was hard for me was the 7.5 hour requirement when I probably could have gotten things done before that.
The class is set up where you work in teams which was super awesome. The thing that was hard for me was the 7.5 hour requirement when I probably could have gotten things done before that.

Professor Hollan was a nice guy, but this class feels like a LOT of busy work. Looking back I only think it is worth it if you need to pad your resume. There was good content, but not enough time to review it all.

Professor Hollan is a good professor. I didn't like the format of the class more than Professor Hollan himself. If I was taking a lecture-based class instead of an on-campus internship, I would take a class from him again.

For those curious, grades have not finished posted for the class yet, but I am pretty sure I will receive an A+ in the class. 

GOOD:
-Your resume will be so much better if you take this class seriously
-You will also dig deep and learn things you didn't think you were careful of

BEWARE:
-The final report is MASSIVELY intensive.

The lectures were useless. Great opportunity to learn about a company and it really depends on if you get put with a good group or not. I wish this class focused more on working with the company and less on pointless modules. 7.5 hours of work outside of class.
Class was required but there is hardly anything to take away from it. The OCI projects can be good depending on your sponsor/the company you sign up for.

This class was incredibly easy and the professor provided needed help to students who required it.  However, the lectures, that were mandatory to attend, were not engaging.  Most of what was being talked about seemed like common sense or inspirational quotes.  The majority of the class was on their phones or computers working on other projects.
Demanding class

100% the worst class I have ever taken at BYU. I don't doubt other people have had okay experiences, but it depends on the project you get/the group members you get. I got a lazy, unmotivated group and a project that was not guided well, so I was left to do all the work. Outside internships should be able to cover this requirement.

You honestly don't have a ton of interaction with Professor Hollan other than the few times you are required to meet in class. The times in class that I did interact with him they were usually pretty pleasant. He's pretty chill and honestly doesn't have much to do with your grade. It's more about how you meet your sponsors expectations.
Funny, chill teacher. He wants students gain valuable experience
Great resume opportunity to receive credit for an internship and to gain experience.
Modules were set up clearly so you could complete the assignments and projects. Lectures often helped to grasp a better idea on what was in the modules

The class is mostly dependent on the project you receive. The classes are just him lecturing and they aren't the most engaging. But the class definitely helps you prepare for the workforce and learn to communicate in a team setting.

I didn't have a good experience with this course because our sponsor wasn't helpful at all (he didn't even give us a project to work on) and Professor Hollan had a meeting with us because he felt like we weren't doing good work with our project (again, we didn't get one). He was extremely rude to us and didn't let us explain our point of view.
Be ready to deal with group work.

Professor Hollan is a mediocre professor; he doesn't teach very much or add a ton of value ot the class. The course, however is amazing and I recommend to everyone. It is a lot of work in that it takes a lot of time; if you put in the time and effort, however, then you will definitely get an A.
I loved my OCI group and sponsor as well as the project we were tasked with. Lectures helped gain overall course direction which was helpful.
Professor is fair. Be prepared to spend a lot of time outside of class.
Professor is fair and genuinely wants us to succeed

Your attention is often split between the project you're working on, and the class work needed. A TON of out of class work. If you need the class for your major or minor, you'll be fine, but if you don't need it, I wouldn't recommend it. There are other resources to find internships. The set up of the class is just kind of awful.

This class is great. There wasn't a lot of time spent in class, presence was required 7 times during the semester, and no class for the rest. Because of the nature of an OCI, lectures were very broad and focused on us getting the most out of our project by giving a full effort.  With a good project, this will be your most beneficial class!
Professor is good but your experience depends on your TA. A good TA makes all the difference because you are more involved with the TA than the professor.

This is an internship class. You work for a company. Professor Hollan outlines requirements for the class and directs you to resources which will help you succeed. In the end, it's up to you and your team to meet the needs of your sponsor.

This class is heavily dependent on the project and group you are assigned. Overall can be a great learning experience in the right situation of if you are very motivated, otherwise can be challenging and will defiantly be a lot of work. Expect to carve out 8-9 hours a week.
Overall great course, learned so much working with my team. Make sure if you take this class that you have 7-10 hours in your schedule every week because that is what you are grades on

Totally recommend this class. I like that class is only 6 times the semester and that the workload is self reported. I have taken 2 OCI's and I think it is the best way for underclassmen to get real experience in the workplace.

Professor Hollan taught me how to Professor Hollan taught me how to excel as a professional and more important, as a disciple of Jesus Christ. My career is important, but my discipleship will always be the center of all my decisions in my life, and lead to real/meaningful success.
Super easy and simple lectures, but he has high expectations for your work outside of class. He provides great resources and wants you to succeed!

Enjoyable internship class. He has high expectations, as he should since we are working for real companies! You'll get out of this class what you put in, since the Professor provides all the resources you could need to succeed.
It is an internship class, you will be put in groups do your part, do your hours and you'll be set.
Pretty tough grader and deadlines are strict

We are all working on different projects throughout the semester, which makes for a hard class to teach. Class felt very irrelevant and unnecessary at points. We also had to complete presentations and reports that seem kind of silly considering the projects are so different but we were all graded on the same criteria. It didn't make much sense

This class is very tough to teach seeing as all students are working on different internships. With that being said, Professor Hollan does do a good job at teaching the class. You will mainly be working with your sponsor for the project and your TA so the professor doesn't matter too much. I would certainly recommend taking the class.
Great professor always willing for help students.

His lectures are boring at times, but the overall class and content that he teaches is good. Something I enjoyed was that I got a lot of good experience working with other students to achieve a goal. If you want a resume builder go for it, but if you're just trying to take another class take a SWELL class or something.

This class was very challenging.  The class just gets in the way of the internship and grading is unfair. If individual group members decide not to do their work you are all punished collectively even if you have done all in your power to get these group members to do their work.

Really good opportunity. I learned a lot an my OCI was super beneficial. Would recommend.
Biggest challenge was balancing the class requirements with the Sponsor's requirements. Often the two would conflict.

I took the OCI class and it was great. I think Prof. Hollan has the class organized really well when it comes to timing of assignments, but some of the major projects can be a bit unclear. However, it was a good experience. If you're looking to have an internship while having to take less classes to be a full time student, this is a great option.
The OCI was good experience working with a real company

They get so caught up on the timesheet and there is no wiggle room. One time I submitted my hours and they didn't save and even though I worked the hours he didn't count it for credit and got mad at me.
oci's are great for those applying to a business program. hollan likes to hear his own voice. oci canvas work was a lot of busy work, but the work you do with your company is great!
Be prepared for 8 hours a week of work. My team was great and we had a good time going through our OCI. Lots of time though.
He was a great professor, just get ready to put work into your project.
Overall great experience, class itself was just a repeat of the modules and didn't seem necessary.

Overall, I felt like this class prioritized classwork over the actual internship experience itself. The classwork had some valuable knowledge, but it took away from the hands-on experience and professional development I could have gained from the actual work experience.

I understand that the professor was just doing his job, and he needed to be very strict due to the large number of students in class. My team and I had a very difficult sponsor, which ultimately affected our grade. Instead of the professor understanding us and recognizing our efforts, I feel that he trusted the sponsor's word more than the students

I really enjoyed the class, but the professor didn't really have anything to do with that. His participation is very passive. It also kind of ticks me off to go to a 5 pm class where the lecture content is a knock knock joke and an attendance code.

This class is an internship. In class you will learn skills to help you, but other than that class is not really used to complete your project. All of your work is outside of class. It is hard. You are working with real businesses. But it is incredibly valuable. I learned a lot about working in business fields because of this class and Professor.

Not much interaction with the teacher himself but this class was awesome to take since it was convenient to get real business experience on campus! Lots of work but I heard it depends on the company you are assigned to and your team, I lucked out andmhad an awesome semester. Highly recommend to anyone wanting to apply to the business school.
This class is a great way to get experience in the professional world. I loved working for a real company and learned a lot of valuable skills.

The class is easy if you get a decent team who gives effort. 8+ hours of work outside of class each week, but this is easy to hit consistently considering the professional work as an internship class. Attendance is graded but no content from lectures is tested.
Professor Hollan was a bit intimidating at first, but once we personally met with him, I learned how nice and fun he is! This class has given me great experience.

Professor Hollan is a great professor for MSB494R. The class I took from him was the on campus internship class, which meant that he was more of a facilitator that a traditional professor. We only had class a few times throughout the semester. The times we did meet were simply times for him to give us advice and direction on how to work efficently.

Originally, I wanted to give Professor Hollan a scathing review. However, I realized that he did his job, and did it well. He treats his stduents like employees, which can seem harsh from the student perspective but wonderful from the learner's perspective. He helped me grow, even though it was a difficult growth.

Does not have compassion or understanding for student situations in an internship. Does not attempt to see things from a students point of view. Is the epitome of a professor whose mantra is "suck it up"... but not in a growth perspective. Seemed like a nice guy overall but my group's experience was .... less than enjoyable.

The actual project taught me valuable skills and he tried to make the assignments as clear as possible, however, sometimes they as straightforward as he intended them to be. We had support from our TA who helped clarify the deliverables. Overall, super valuable class I would definitely take it again.
Do the extra credit
He offered lots of great and helpful advice throughout the course, and truly wanted to see all his students succeed.

This professor often set clear expectations for students and their projects. Class was mandatory and you get credit for completing the in-class quizzes. I didn't have a lot of interaction with asking questions with the professor specifically because you do more of that with your assigned TA, but ultimately enjoyed his class!

Professor Hollan didn't really teach anything. Class was mandatory/attendance was graded, but class was always a waste of time. Our group needed help and all he said to do was "work harder". Not very insightful.
This class has poor organization and you won't learn much. It consists of a lot of busy work and expectations can be unclear at times. If you are looking for an internship, I'd look somewhere else.

It really depends on the internship that you get. This will determine the difficulty. Professor isn't involved too much besides the times that there are class, which aren't super insightful anyways. I would say definitely take this class for the experience because that is what it is about.

This is an amazing class!! you get out of it exactly what you put into it. Amazing real life experience that you can put on your resume. There are a lot of hours required outside of class (7-10 hours) but you get to work with a team and learn a ton!

Professor Hollan guides the class, but you work with your team and sponsor for your internship much more often. Class once a week with some weeks off. 7.5-9 hours of work expected for your internship each week, get ready to work. If you work hard and care about your company, it will be worth it.

This class sorta depends on your sponsor for your internship. You don't interact much with Professor Hollan, most of it is with your group, the sponsor, and your TA. The class is pretty confusing in the beginning and the modules you have to do every week always sort of seemed like busywork. But it's a good class for a resume and an application.

He is a great professor, but the success of your semester will depend on your assigned group and sponsor. It is a great class and would recommend it for any student trying to get more experience for resumes.

He seems like a tough grader and sets the bar high, but you get out of the class what you put in. Honestly its all self-graded. You can get a good grade if you follow his expectations and push yourself to be helpful to your sponsor. Take this class for good experience in a business field.
OCIs are a great way to get some experience and exposure. You will have to do some busy work for the class, but it is well worth it regardless.

The on campus internship is a good program, but I wouldn't say it was great because you could probabaly get better experience looking on your own. The lectures are average, but I do enjoy the way Professor Hollan runs the class. It could definitely be worse, but it could also be improved in what you can get out of the class.

This class is great for people who can't get an internship; it's not necessary if you already have an internship. Be sure to choose the project you want to do carefully at the beginning. Most of them were marketing internships, which wasn't what I wanted. The skills you develop still look good on a resume. Met in class only every couple of weeks.

This opportunity is super awesome. It is not only intellectually challenging it also helps you to learn how to work at a company and how to interact in the business world. It is an awesome program. It is not too hard but make sure not to fall behind because it can be hard to catch up. Professor Hollan overall is super awesome and kind!

I did the OCI, and it was a good experience. I'm not sure if I'd do another On-Campus Internship, but I'm grateful for how Professor Hollan organized the class. I just wish we would've known how big the final report is from the start of the semester.
Overall this class was good, it is a lot of work. Expect 7.5-9 hours of work outside of class. Professor is chill tho but attendance is required

Professor Hollan is passionate about what he does, if you are looking for more work experience, an OCI is a great place to start. I believe the class has many helpful resources but the mandatory modules sometimes seemed inefficient and like busy work. However, there were valuable insights and ideas in most of them.

This class is very interesting. You get to select projects that you are interested in and then you are put into a group for a specific company. I personally did not like the project I got placed in because I had zero background in it. Also, it was the first time the sponsor had done one and she did not fully understand the purpose of the class.
Wants you to succeed but you have to be flexible and put in your own time and efforts.

This class helped me grow a lot as a leader but that growth didn't come easy. Your experience depends primarily on the effort you put in, the effort your team puts in, and your sponsor you get. A lot of variables but gives a very unique albeit challenging opportunity to grow as a professional and get experience.

Attendance is required, but the lectures are sorta boring. The OCI depends a lot more on the project that you're assigned than on the professor, but overall his lectures are pretty mid. Not bad, just not super helpful.

He is a great professor at letting you know what needs to be done and when. He is always reminding you what could be improved and what you are not doing good at. He honors people in class who excel at the projects and work. He honestly loves his students just sometimes it may be hard for him to show it. He can be hard on the students sometimes too.

The OCI program is one of the greatest things about BYU, and I'd highly recommend for anyone looking to get into the business school. Make sure to put a lot of effort into your application so you can get a good sponsor, because a good sponsor company determines everything. In class lectures themselves are pretty useless, but they are not every week

The class requires 7.5-9 hours a week of work. There are 3 meetings a week outside of class. My group got a terrible sponsor that never answered emails, so much of the class is determined by luck with the sponsor that you get at the beginning of the semester. Hollan is a nice guy, but if you get a bad sponsor the class feels like a waste of time.

Professor Hollan is one of the rudest professors I have ever had. I took this class a year ago and the internship was good, but he was not accommodating at all. I went in to and talked to him about a week before I was going out of town to see what I could do, and he would not help and basically said we will see what happens to my grade.
I definitely recommend doing an OCI. The difficulty of this class depends on your project I think. You are expected to put 7.5 a week into this class though to get an A

I would recommend anyone to take an OCI if you have not taken it before. I am planning to take another OCI next year. You are assigned to a project based on your interests. You work together with other team members. You learn things in your field of study by working on an internship project with an actual sponsor company in a real-world context.

Professor Hollan himself is not an outstanding teacher, but this class is an amazing opportunity and def should be taken to gain experience, learn about the business world and get an incredible resume builder.

Structure of the course did not align with the "real" business world and got in the way of our sponsors' needs in the first half of the semester. Tom's planner is terrible and nobody actually uses it tbh. The professor is great. Sponsor was not that good but it was a good experience overall.

This class was great as a real world learning experience, and Professor Hollan cares about what he teaches. There are only a few class periods he holds throughout the semester, which are mandatory to attend. Everything is a hard deadline and he gives no leeway, so don't miss any assignments.
This class is very self-led and you have to figure it all out. Professor Hollan will help you though if you need it. Class is also not every week.

Professor Hollan is very upfront and blunt, almost intimidating. There are canvas modules for every week, but the focus is on creating deliverables for your sponsor. Recording hours every week is really crucial to success in this class. Such valuable skills, especially because I feel like you're just thrown into it head first!

I honestly didn't really interact with Professor Hollan outside of lectures, but I appreciate his efforts to make his lectures engaging and comprehensible. I didn't feel like all of the required class periods were entirely necessary, but some of them were very informational.
He is nice, he explains things well, and is pretty chill. You mainly need to deal with your sponsor.

Professor Hollan is a bro and his classes are great and informational. You only have to attend like 6 class periods throughout the semester. It's definitely not easy. It took up so much of my week and always kept me busy. It was kind of annoying in that way, but I learned a lot and it really helped me.

Depending on what type of experience you want, this class can be beneficial for learning new skills or a waste of time trying to fill the required hours you need each week.  Some of the assignments due through the week were busy work that didn't align with what we were working on with our sponsor. Good for networking

I appreciated the experiential learning opportunity. I had a great team and sponsor and felt that I learned a lot. However, I do feel that the structure of the course did not align with the "real" business world and often got in the way of our sponsors' needs. If you don't need to take the course for credit, there are better internships out there.

The OCI was a lot of work but a very good experience. The project itself was very engaging but the course material often did not line up with our sponsor's needs and we were forced to do less on our actual project to complete all the necessary classwork.
This OCI was awesome! I loved the hands on experience that I was able to gain! It takes a lot of time (7.5-9hrs a week) but is so worth it!

There are only 6 class periods to attend over the course of the semester. That being said, expect to spend 7-9 hours per week working on your project with your team. It's pretty rigorous but not difficult to get an A if you dedicate the time and work hard. You get meaningful, real world experience.

My experience in the BYU OCI program was awful. The professor had not verified earlier whether the company my team received had a project for us. They did not and we spent the entire semester struggling to receive the weekly hours that OCI required. I was also put in a team with extremely conflicting schedules, and so we could never meet.

Professor Hollan has a tough exterior, but he will become friendly once everyone has agreed to take the class seriously. The lectures he gives are somewhat sarcastic, but include jokes to make it worth your money. Get your team up and running with some solid deliverables as soon as possible. Canvas is very useful. Communicate with your sponsor.
It is a lot of work with hours but a super good experience!

This class is fun. I'm sure Professor Hollan is a top notch professor, but the class only met 6 times throughout the semester. I hardly interacted with him but when I did he was great. The class is far more dependent on the sponsor and internship you are selected for. I did Marketing for a fitness app startup, it was great, others were not so lucky

Loved my internship, I felt like it taught me a lot about how to deal with ambiguity and how to deal with difficult teammates lol. It made me excited to start a career in the business world and is a great addition to my resume. Very happy I took this class, but expect to put a lot of time and work into it (7.5-9 hours a week for an A).

Had a great time doing this On-Campus Internship! It was very heavily project influenced based on if you'll enjoy it or not. Professor Hollan did everything he could to promote it to be a ideal, accomplishable, and fun course. I would definitely recommend!

Professor Hollan is an exceptional professor  who genuinely prioritizes optimizing the internship experience for students. His dedication to ensuring the best outcomes and fostering a positive learning environment makes him a standout educator.
David Hollan is an awesome professor. Very genuine and very caring guy, and he is funny. His class really isn't that hard. You can get an A if you want to

Professor Hollan is great and helps guide you through your OCI experience. Classes are mandatory, but he only holds class six times throughout the semester. He gives you great information on how to excel in any project you choose and provides various resources to help.

Professor Hollan's OCI class was great and I learned a lot of great things. Just make sure to research the projects to make sure you are interested in what the project is. I recommend it to anyone looking to get their feet into the business world. It is also a great opportunity to have something on your resume.

Do not take an OCI. If you REALLY want to take one, make sure to do a lot of research prior. Sponsors were terrible.The classwork is easy to do, but it's not relevant to the experience you are having to deal with. The online course materials are unorganized. Prof Hollan was super unhelpful. When we did meet he was rude and condescending.

Do not take an OCI. If you REALLY want to, do a lot of research to your options before. It take so much time and effort. My sponsors were pretty terrible. It's not worth the 3 hours of class credit. Prof. Hollan is super unhelpful to specific groups. The classwork online was easy, but not relevant to actual experiences with your company.

This class is a great opportunity to get real world experience. Unfortunately I think I grew the most from misunderstandings and confusion on class requirements. Professor Hollan guided the course but I didn't like how he occasionally made fun of student questions. We are mostly supposed to communicate concerns with our mentor TA's.
Super good professor. You don't really met with him that much but seems like a good guy.

Professor Hollan is a good professor. The class is pretty demanding to get an A (7.5 hrs a week spent on working on your internship). He's pretty uninvolved throughout the semester since you only see him a few times for class. Seems like a good guy though.
Pretty mid, not leaning one way or another as a professor but cool class.
Great professor

Professor Hollan is a good man! Sometimes I felt like the time we spent in class wasn't super productive, but the actual course material is straightforward and he does a good job at making sure everyone is getting the most out of their learning experience.
He is a great professor.
The class was very helpful to me as an introduction into the business world. I had a great experience.
Do your part, and his uplifting lectures will keep you going!
The class structure was hard to follow, but other than that he was a great teacher. He seems to care about the success of his students.

Professor Hollan is an awesome professor. He is quite a fan of dad jokes. The first two weeks you will feel a little bit confused as you are just beginning your project, but after week two you have a good idea of what you are doing. This class provides excellent real-world experience. I would recommend you take this course!

Great class to get real world internship experience working with a real company! Unfortunately, I got matched with a company that only had us making tiktoks, blogs, and pinterest posts, so it wasn't super impactful. But I gained a lot of skills such as writing a final report and working with a team to formulate new ideas.
The class is a fully fledged internship where you will work in groups for the duration of the semester on your assigned projects.
The class overall was a good experience, but in-person classes were not necessary.  Professor didn't seem to care much.
It all depends on your TA and company. It's kind of a joke how easy the actual assignments are, but the course is very "busy work heavy" and requires 8 hours a week.

A great way to get experience for your resume. The members of your group will determine how the semester goes so make sure to all get on the same page. If you have the oppurtunity to add this class to your schedule it will give you great experience and can get the ball rolling for your resume! Would definitely recommend.

Professor Hollan is a good teacher but I took his OCI class which is mostly team work and a lot of interaction with your TA. If you had a very important question he was available but most correspondence was done with my peers and the TA. It is a good class and helps you get real world experience without having to go outside of school and find it.
He is a good professor, sometimes he is hard to communicate with outside of class through email. Overall a helpful professor who cares about the students.

Overall, the class was easy. It just requires a lot of time. You need to get 7.5-9 hours per week outside of class which was a lot for me this semester but that was my own fault. I also wish there would have been a way to make up the class quizzes because I was sick one day and he said there was nothing I could do. Overall a good experience.

Professor Hollan was a good teacher. There were only a handful of required lectures to attend, and he provided you a lot of resources and advice on how to be successful in your project. The class work itself was easy, but the project with your sponsor company can be difficult sometimes. It's just a lot of work, so be prepared to be busy.

In order to get an A in this class, you have to do above 7.5 hours per week and at least a total of 105 hours of work for the entire semester.  Does not seem like a lot but it was hard.
This class depends on what kind of sponsor you get and the kind of deliverables you are required to do.  You will have great experiences for your resume.

Lots of times the mandatory classes are about the deliverables you have to turn in for the class, BUT, the class about the deliverables and what they are usually comes after the deadline for that deliverable. So you'll have to kind of figure out what you're supposed to turn in before you're told what it is. Its not that difficult, just confusing.

This experience is largely based on the project that you get assigned to and the sponsor that you interacted with.
This is a time consuming class to get an a in the class you have to do 8 hours a week. Which doesn't sound like a lot, but it is brutal.
Professor Hollan has a genuine interest in his students. It was a fun class but with lots of assignments to do for the project.

He is a great professor and really helps you to get a foothold when you are trying to do a first internship. I would really recommend this anyone trying to get experience but doesn't know how to find it yet. This is a great opportunity.
On campus internship was a great class. I would take the class again!
Gave good advice on how to stay on top of OCI projects. Good lectures and very helpful.

While the actual internship and business experience was helpful, if you can get an internship without this class I would recommend that. There is a lot of busy work that is solely for the class and doesn't help build your prefessional skills, just wastes your time. Very. Frustrating.

Professor Hollan is great! The class definitely has some busy work. Sometimes the tasks we complete for the class feel a little useless and the meeting number requirement of 3 per week can be annoying if you don't have anything specific to meet with your group about.
Class was easy but he did a good job teaching.

We did not have very many interactions with him as the class is large and not meant to be personal. His lectures were very informative but the online modules we had to complete were pointless. You are mostly in contact with your TA.
There is not a lot of interaction with him since the classes are large and most interaction comes by way of the TAs or the company sponsors, but his lectures are great, you can tell he really cares

This class was actually great for getting me professional experience. However, I felt like the actual "school" part of the class got in the way of the goal of professional development. Almost all of the work we had to do for the class (rather than for the company we worked for) was busy work.

Overall I had a great experience with my team and sponsor. Nice that there were only 7 classes to attend through out the semester. He gives some pointless assignments that are time consuming that has nothing to do with the project. The class also seems unorganized and when it comes to the mid-term/ final... nothing is clear and its confusing.

On campus internship, didn't have much interaction with him besides the 6 mandatory classes/ semester. The TA's were great and help a ton. Our group had Cody Allington and he was the best. Time consuming class and a lot of work, but I learned a ton more than all of my other classes combined.

Professor Hollan clearly cares about the success of his students and takes every opportunity to encourage them to put in the work and invest in their experience. He provides and assigns TAs to each project for questions. His puns are definitely groanworthy. Grading criteria is kind of vague, but that's because of the wide range of projects.

Professor Hollan is a good professor. I really enjoyed my experience with my team and sponsor in my internship project. It is a great opportunity to learn real life business skills and build up your experience and resume. The class itself could be organized better and was the source of the only negative feelings I had toward taking the class.

This class was taken for my business minor. It is a lot of group work and your hours will be tracked. The real life experience was awesome. I don't feel like I took a lot from the class lectures and got more help for the midterm and the final projects from my TA. Overall good real life experience to add to your resume.

This is an On-campus Internship. For the most part, you are working on your internship but Dr. Hollan has added a bunch of assignments to make the course "academic". Each of his lectures was a waste of the company's time. If you take this class, the internship will be a great opportunity, but you will also be given lots of busy work for a grade.
Great Professor, Lots of work outside of class but you have a TA that helps a lot!

Great professor. Very responsive to emails and helped out my team when we had members not cooperating. Tries his best to have engaging classes with stories and jokes. Overall, really nice guy, would recommend

Our TA told us that he purposefully hides his no-tolerance late policy, and when my team turned in an assignment 2 hours late because we were helping with an event for our company, professor Hollan responded rudely to our email politely asking him what partial credit we could receive. This class was only worth it because I had a good team & company

Prof. Hollan is great. He doesn't give much busy work, and only keeps you in class as long as you need to be there. A lot of this class relies on the group you do your project with and your mentor. My group was great, which made everything easy but my peer mentor was not so that made grading hard. But there was enough extra credit to make up for it

He had so many resources for the project and he wanted us all to succeed. He established from the beginning how the class would help us get jobs in the future. A hard part about the class was having a team of random people (some could be great and others not so great). Professor Hollan is personable who genuinely cares about his students futures.

This class is good for experience regardless of the company you get assigned, because the effort you put in determines what you'll get out of this class. The deadlines are hard for this class so don't expect any leeway with that at all! Professor Hollan has a tough luck mentality. Easy A, but meant for experience.

This is a very worthwhile class even in the difficult moments! There's really not a lot of interaction with the professor directly, but the time when I did have to contact him he was super responsive and helpful.
Great professor! The class is strict on making sure you get enough hours for your internship otherwise its very easy.

This course was good and it prepares you for real world experiences. Professor Hollan emphasized this a lot and he was very encouraging about making this internship experience the best that it could possibly be for us. He made his lectures engaging too which helped.

Professor Hollan is a nice guy. Lectures weren't particularly noteworthy, but the class itself is what you make of it. It can be really easy to get an A, and if you don't like dealing with ambiguity that can be a bit uncomfortable, but I had a great group and a great sponsor with cool experiences.

Professor Hollan is pretty decent, he has kinda a funky personality that results in zero in-class participation. OCI was a great experience, I would definitely do it again despite the weird class requirements.
Professor Hollan excelled in giving his students the opportunity to work in a professional setting and learn best practices for internships and jobs.
David is awesome and will help you do your best in the internship.
This course was time-consuming and required creative thinking. You are required to do 7.5-9 hours of work outside of class weekly. Some TAs grade assignments more harshly than others.

Professor Hollan is not super involved with each student/group individually. However, the few times you meet for class, he provides a lecture. I did not find the class sessions itself beneficial. The course itself is structured great, and the skills you develop are priceless. There are a ton of awesome resources that he provides as well. Def take.
This class was cool because you get real-world experience but it was a lot of work outside the class! It is expected that 7-9 hours of work be done outside of the class every week.

Professor Hollan is a good guy, he is funny and makes jokes during lectures. I didn't interact with him at all and mainly worked through the TAs but felt that he was there if I needed something. Getting a good grade in the class is not hard if you do good work.
Good class if you're trying to get business experience. Choose your project wisely. Professor Hollan is great, just wish we didn't have to attend his lectures since they were not helpful.
Professor Hollan was super great and his class was a very useful class to take.

A BYU OCI was a great experience for anyone looking for business experience and opportunities to put on your resume. The beginning of class the expectations were a little difficult to understand, but as long as you stay connected and communicate with your sponsor things clear up. The modules are pretty quick and easy to accomplish.

Holland is a good man. He gave helpful advice for the workforce and encouraged us to keep reading our scriptures & such. The course is easy, just be sure to follow the modules and work on your deliverables (projects and tasks for your company or sponsor). The lectures feel pointless sometimes tbh but nothing unbearable.
The class was pretty easy as long as you kept up with the modules. Sometimes the in-person lectures felt unnecessary though and didn't seem helpful when trying to reach deliverables.

Some parts of the class were a little confusing, and I wished there was more clarity on it. Other than that, great class if you put in genuine work, and a good opportunity to learn skills and gain work experience.

He was clear and unmoving in his expectations. You could tell he cared about the students and wanted them to work hard because he wanted them to get the best out of their experience. I didn't get to know him very well but appreciated him taking time after class to answer questions/concerns.

We only had class a few times during the semester, since most of our work was for our actual internship project, but when we did have class he was inspiring and got me hyped to do my best work for my internship.
BYU's OCI is definitely a valuable experience for anyone looking for professional experience. The class itself was informative and helpful for those seeking to prepare for entering the workfield.

I never interacted personally with Professor Hollan during this course. The TAs basically run the whole class. It's a great opportunity to receive hands on business experience. I'd recommend it to any student, especially those who are trying to figure out what they want to study.
He was a fine professor, but the course was set up in a way that made it feel like there was a lot of busy work or just "clocking in."

He was a pretty nice professor. Worked well with students and wanted to help them learn. Lectures could have been more engaging and gone into more depth on some assignments. If he taught other classes I might take them.

Professor Hollan was awesome. He was straightforward and didn't mess around. I appreciated his real-world attitude and advice. He treated us all like business professionals, not just college students. I learned so much from this class and my project, I'm so glad I took the class!!
The course is a lot of work but well worth it. Only take it if you are willing to work hard and put in a good effort.

Dr Hollan is a great instructor for the OCI because he makes expectations very clear even though our projects may differ. He never interacted directly with my group but has taught this class so much that he knows all the issues we may face and gives us great tools and resources to ensure that no matter what we feel successful.
Did a good job at teaching the content. Was slow to help students that needed extra assistance.
He has some amazing insights about entering the workforce.
He was super fun during this internship class! He is very helpful and gives lots of great advice and we had just a handful of classes for the whole semester. Would take from him again!

His Lectures are great. He really cares about his students and wanting them to succeed in the real world. Just put in the 7.5 hours a week for the class, and you should be fine. The assignments themselves are super easy.
Dr. Hollan takes himself very seriously - to the point where it feels like he is unwilling to listen to new prospective from students. Also, he is not flexible at all with deadlines.
Dr. Hollan takes himself very seriously - to the point where it feels like he is unwilling to listen to new prospective from students.

The OCI program was very well taught by professor Hollan. He makes it very clear that he wants his students to develop professional skills and be prepared for jobs and internships. I would recommend him if you want a professor who is direct and gives tough but honest feedback.

Professor Hollan did his best to create a real-world business atmosphere with his class. As far as the lectures go, they did not add much to the internship experience and were only attended for the mandatory class credit. The internship coursework required by Professor Hollan felt like busy work at times and did not always benefit our company.

This class was tough, I feel like the lectures were good, but honestly did not add much to the OCI project specifically. Everyone that showed up to the lectures showed up only for the attendance quiz code and then left afterwards. Nothing against Professor Hollan, but it just wasn't an engaging lecture that added anything outside of the project.

Very professional with lectures and if you talk to him after class. The class is much more about how much work you put into the internship. Get ready to work basically have a part time job - you will be working hard for a company. You do not get to choose your project or teammates so it really helps you to work with all kinds of people

Honestly, I didn't see much of Professor Hollan in this class, but he seemed cool! The internship was really interesting and I definitely learned a lot. Be warned though, it is really time-consuming. For an A, you should be reporting 7.5 hours a week, which includes class, 2-3 team meetings, a sponsor meeting, and projects in between.

This class is awesome. I gained a lot of valuable skills by doing this internship. It was a lot of fun and now I have a lot more connections. It is more of an internship than a class. It is easy to get an A but if you want to make it a good project it takes more effort.
Overall, it was a great class. Make sure you like the company that you sign up for. Motivate your team from the beginning and you'll do great.

This class is great exposure and experience and I highly recommend taking it. It is a lot of work, but that's what you sign up for. Professor Hollan has a sort of tough-love way of caring for his students. He wants us all to do great and learn as much as he can, but has an intimidating way of showing it.

This class was great and typical for any OCI, but the way Professor Hollan addressed us really irked me. He seemed to like to remind us that we're supposed to be good, righteous BYU students whenever someone didn't immediately jump up to volunteer for a prayer. The class was good and a great experience, but he left a really bad taste in my mouth.

Great class, I needed more experience for my resume and this class accomplishes that need. Class requires you spend on average 7.5 hours per week, and you report this on a timesheet. You have to meet with your team several times a week, this was a little inconvenient at times but got easier as the semester went along. Not too difficult of work.

This isn't a class, it's a job with class assignments. There was a lot of confusion about the assignments and the rubrics aren't very clear. It's confusing using different platforms to learn and submit assignments.

Professor Holland is a wise teacher who knows how to set us up for success in the business world. His direct approach and rhetoric can come off as intimidating, but it plays a key role in making sure we students are prepared for the real world.
Definitely a teacher who expects full participation and isn't fond of excuses but is good at knowing what the class needs and addresses accordingly.
I took his On-campus internship class. They are very strict about their policies and technical graders but overall this is a doable class.
Professor was awesome and we didn't interact with him as much. Understanding yet firm which was needed for the on campus internship projects.

Professor Hollan basically sets you up for success from day one. He relates everything you will learn to the real world and wants you to take advantage of all the information he provides you regarding business. Opportunities for extra credit as well. If you do what he says in class your resume will be boosted exponentially.

MSB 494R is what you make of it. There are a lot of assignments that are really just hoops you need to jump through and at times they seem meaningless. However, this class is really great because you get to work a real internship and relatively low stakes.

Good class but mostly depends on what project gets assigned to you. I was a little annoyed because I had a lot of interests checked and he wasn't able to assign me any of them and had me fill out my interests again.
Don't forget to come to class and put all mandatory class dates on your calender!!!!

Very time-consuming class. Hate the way it was set up, but I got some great experience from it to add to my resume. One of the reasons I got my internship for the summer was because of my experience here, so I would recommend it, especially to freshmen and sophomores.
He is a good professor but I did not interact him to much.

I learned so much from doing the on-campus internship with professor Hollan. It was definitely a lot of work, but it gave me a lot of good experience to add to my resume. I would definitely recommend taking this class.

Interactions with this professor were rare because the whole class was a group internship, so you mostly worked with other students, your TA, and the company you're an intern for. This class all depends on what you make of the project and what company you intern for.

Amazing professor. This On Campus Internship experience was very valuable. There is a lot of work needed for this course, however, it is real world experience. There is not a heavy homework load necessarily but you will spend between 6-9 hours per week on this course through meetings with group, sponsor, lecture, and research.

The internship itself was enjoyable due to a fun team and sponsor, however relevance of many of the assignments was difficult to see. This class is a time commitment. I also did not feel like Hollan's lectures were helpful.

This was my first OCI. It was not the most enjoyable experience. The company I worked for was great, and it was fun to be a part of an internship team. But the amount of work outside of the actual internship work was distracting. The professor was not very approachable. My TA was absolutely amazing! Get ready for lots of work and LOTS of ambiguity.
A very chill class that you have the opportunity to learn a lot in. What you do is very dependent on what your group does. Very team-oriented.
Doing an OCI is good. I learned and had a good experience, but it feels like busy work sometimes.

This class is great for some real-life business experience but was also frustrating. Our sponsor and project were frustrating, and Professor Hollan and the TAs were not helpful when they needed to be. This is not a legit internship, so the teacher should be there to help and assist you since this is a BYU class and we are here to progress.
I had a good time in the class and I enjoyed Prof Hollan's teaching!
He was a good teacher. Lectures were kind of boring, but we only met 6 times.

The online internships are super helpful because you get an internship through the school for school credit. It is not something that you can fake. You log hours and meet with your team often for the entire semester. Super engaging. You do a lot more work with the TA's than the professor.

The class is very helpful to gain experience working with a real business. Professor Hollan gives some helpful resources in class. The in-class time wasn't super helpful to me but the experience in the internship was.

The On-Campus Internship is a well put-together course with great experiential learning opportunities. The professor an TAs were always available to help develop group projects in a semi-professional setting. Great course!

Took an OCI material was pretty straightforward if you follow along on Canvas. Mandatory to attend class to receive the credit and get the answer to the attendance quiz. The class wasn't every week. The class part was a breeze OCI part was hard.
He was an alright professor, but just threw a bunch of resources and requirements at us and said good luck. Most of the help from the course came from TA's and the sponsors we worked with.

This class is super helpful to building your resume and getting professional experience. The class teaches you how to have a better professional experience. Work hard by consistently by logging 7.5 hours each week, take advantage of the resources, communicate and ask questions! I'm glad I took this class!

Professor Hollan's MSB 494R class is super helpful to build your resume. I had a good experience overall. There are like 6 required lectures to attend and they felt unnecessary. You're mainly graded by your project sponsor and teammates, so work hard and you'll do well.

The professor was really hard to work with and my team and I felt like we were always talked down to. The classes were more distracting than helpful and the assignments took away from the work that we were doing for the company. Our TA was always really hard to communicate with and we felt like we were micromanaged.
He did a good job but there is no control over how your project and sponsor is for your OCI

You have to meet with your team 3 times a week and make sure you stay on top of your timesheet hours needed each week! Most of the class time is spent on the internship, completing your deliverables and certain documents for the class. He had a few lectures that you had to attend which served as good instruction for the coming assignments.
All you need to succeed in this class is to participate and clock in the hours outside of class. All other assignments are simple. The class gives all the resources you'll need to do well.

The internship was awesome, but I felt like the assignments and modules actually distracted us from the tasks given to us by our company sponsor. Classes were more focused on completing the assignments rather than improving as interns and making a difference for the company. CSIP was a much better internship class for me!

The class required a lot more time than I initially assumed. In all honesty, the team makes or breaks the experience. If you have a good team then it's a joy but if not the heavy workloads like the final report and Tom's Planner" are very difficult.
Amazing professor!

There was little professor-student interaction. It is an On Campus Internship with a variety of different businesses (your team of 5 students works with one throughout the semester). My team was left confused about what to do because out Internship did not fit with the mold of the class, specifically the midterm and final project.

I didn't get to know him a lot during classes, basically, he says the stuff on slides in the 6/7 mandatory classes, reminds you of the byu standards, and makes someone say the prayer. 
He doesn't make a lot of interaction with students. 
Read carefully what the internship is about, and pick the one you really like, there's a lot of teamwork.

Class was mandatory, but often felt like the time could have been utilized more effectively. There is plenty of busy work in this class, but thankfully the assignments aren't graded too tough. I would say that this is a great way to get something on your resume early in your college experience, as well as learn to work in a team and meet new people

The OCI was a fairly good learning opportunity although I did find parts of this class repetitive and silly, such as the Tom's Planner assignment. The professor lacked a bit of personality, diminishing the experience of attending class.

If you are looking for credible professional development, apply for a real internship. An OCI can either be really good, or really bad. There are too many deciding variables to confidently say you will benefit from this course. As far as David goes, he doesn't relate well to his students and he gives off a "my life is harder than your life" vibe.

This was a good class. The actual lecture part of class seemed to be kind of confusing at times as it didn't always seem to be super necessary but attendance was mandatory. I really enjoyed the experience that I got out of this OCI. It was very time consuming though so take it with a lighter load.
Loved this OCI!
I definitely would recommend taking an OCI if you want valuable business experience.

He doesn't really seem to connect with students well and mostly makes people feel awkward or even bad about themselves. He has super high standards and doesn't really seem to take into account that we are students in the process of learning and not business professionals already. The OCI program sucks in my opinion not helpful at all.

Almost all of the work for this class was spent doing work for a sponsor, which can be hit or miss as far as effectiveness. There were only a handful of classes all semester, but attendance was mandatory. Lectures were kind of pointless, and lot of fluff was added to take up time.

The setup of the class is kind of confusing. It's like a weird mix of freedom to do whatever, but then also includes a bunch of really specific details or guidelines that need to be followed. Overall, I learned a lot from the class and the professor was good, just wish the class was set up differently.
He was fine. Doesn't connect the best with students but knows his stuff.

Prof Hollan cares about his students. He has organized the course VERY well on canvas. MSB 494R doesn't rely heavily on the professor, we only had class like six times. However, most the classes felt like a waste of time and not relevant to our projects; I often felt like I was being talked down to and we were covering very simple things.

There is not a great deal of interaction with the professor, but he can be appreciated for the work that he has put in to make the projects and experiences like this possible. In class, nothing was life-changing. Be prepared to make good friends as you work on a project that will require long hours and be what you make of it. Check in with a TA.

The class is great experience for future jobs and you get the chance to work with many solid companies. Professor is really there for advice but he gives great advice and helps with the process a ton!
It was a good time. Definitely, pick a good project with a topic that you enjoy or the class can be a little bit of a drag.

He is a good teacher that will explain the information well! Often times though I felt like going to his class was not necessary and he had to add a lot of fluff in order to take up the whole time. But otherwise he is a great teacher that want's to help his students out!

The class itself was great, I would definitely recommend it. The teacher isn't really what determines your grade, but rather the project and your team. Professor Hollan comes off as a bit intimidating but overall the course was great. You are required to work 7.5-9 hours a week so you'll need to plan for that.
Great class, the teacher isn't what is going to make this class great it's going to be your own efforts and how your team is.
