The OCI program directed by Professor Hollan is a fantastic professional experience and networking opportunity!

He will expect you to know and involve yourself with the course material by yourself almost. Class time is a review normally of what was already studied. Can be vague describing how to accomplish certain things but overall is a solid professor.
His lectures provided a lot of potentially useful information. The internship doesn't require much communication with him.

This class really helped me to implement what I have been learning at school to an actual business. You have to spend 7.5-9 hours a week on your project, so it is not a class that you can just be passive about. It's great for your resume!

You meet 6 times for this class, so you don't really get to know Professor Hollan. Your class experience is really dependent on what internship you get and how your group is. The internship I got was not the best, but my team was. Overall, I feel like it was a good learning experience. You have to spend an average 7.5 hours a week on internship.
The nature of this course/internship requires a lot of time and attention. That said, Professor Hollan is willing to make himself available to help give direction as needed.

the internship itself wasn't bad, but, required a lot more work that was not specified throughout the semester and grades the midterm presentations pretty harshly. David Hollan also comes across a little stuck up and gave me unwanted stress about my grade the few times we met. He knows what he is talking about but comes off like a business man

Only had to attend the actual class 6 times, so that wasn't bad. This course is really hit or miss depending on what company you are assigned to. It's not too hard, but you will have to put a decent amount of time into this course. Prof. Hollan is chill, but you rarely interact with him.
Had amazing lectures filled with great communication. Took an OCI from him and he made sure we were very prepared. He cared about our progress and our spiritual learning too.

He was awesome! You only have to meet 6 times total the whole semester because you are mostly working with your company for the internship. I learned a lot of good skills doing this and also he gave lots of useful tools for life in general in business.
Professor Hollan is great! He has lots of experience in business and gives great advice and resources in class.

He did a really great job giving the instructions. He always reminded us to stay on top of our responsibilities and record TIMESHEET!!!! overall, he was such a great instructor. I would definitely recommend him!

Professor Hollan was a good lecturer. We would only meet for this class every other week, once a week. When we met, attendance was mandatory. His lectures were inspirational, insightful, and made me want to be a successful intern for my OCI company.

I loved my OCI team and project and I learned a ton. The format of the class itself wasn't the best, and Professor Hollan is fine. You only attend in person a few times, so you don't really get to know him, but his lectures are informative. OCI is a great way to gain business experience.
Be sure you get involved with your project and apply what you learn in class.

This class was structured in a way that made it really confusing on to what exactly was wanted for each assignment. The TA wasn't the best and made things more confusing because the feedback that was given did not exactly match the reading assignments. Great experience though. I learned how to work in a team setting

He is there if you need help. Most of what I loved from this was the team I worked with and the business we had. It was African Braiding Salon, so if you have them, they're great and there's so much room to grow! We had a good TA and my team members were awesome!

Since this is for an OCI, the overall course difficulty is determined more by the company than by him. I enjoyed going to his lectures - they helped me in the context of the course, and directed me to great resources that BYU offers. Since there are a lot of people in the course, I recommend relying on the TAs for help and specific questions.
This man will give you an incredible amount of resources on how to be a better student on canvas. Take advantage of them! OCI's are a lot of work, but worth it!

This is more a review of the OCI class than the professor, just because there wasn't a lot of interaction with him. I learned a ton, but I wish there hadn't been a minimum time requirement because some weeks I had a lot of work to do for my internship while other weeks I felt like I was just filling my time with busywork to hit the hours.
Professor Hollan is an amazing proffesor that genuinely cares about his students. He wants them to succeed and do well not just in college but in life overall.
Great course. I would say it mostly depends on what internship you're assigned to, you don't have much say in exactly which on you want. Useful to put on your resume.
Did not love the format of this class, but I really appreciate the experience I got through my internship.

I think he was well organized and I appreciated that we only held class for important things to talk about. He did well at reminding us of important dates and guiding us to use tools that would help us succeed. Overall I don't think I would take another class from him though because I felt that he wasn't very caring, helpful or polite.
Lots of great projects to choose from for this on-campus internship. There are a lot of resources within the class's Canvas course to help you succeed.

Professor Hollan is a nice teacher, however, the structure of the class will have you working more closely with your TA. The internship requires at least 7.5 hours per week and will have you work with a team. Overall, it's a great chance to work with your teammates and a real company. If you put in time and effort, your grade will reflect it.

The workload is much more dependent on your internship than the class modules. There is a weekly module that takes 1-2 hrs and class is only every so often. You need to average 7 1/2 hrs total on the class/internship. Hollan gives good resources to help your team succeed. Good guy overall. The class looks good on a resume.

When you are selecting on-campus projects you are interested in making sure you think about how comfortable you are putting yourself outside your comfort zone. This is a good class. You have support the whole time but you have to do the work and it is ambiguous and not clearly defined.

This was such a fun class! There aren't many classes you have to go to for OCI, but there is work that needs to be done each week outside of class. The modules can be helpful but have a lot of surveys that can take time. Use your TA to answer questions and be sure to communicate with your group and sponsor a lot.
Dave is a great teacher, but the class has a lot to do with who you get for your sponsor and who ends up on your team.

Not really about the professor, but about the structure & the sponsor of the company you're with. Lots of assignments, some that take up so much time it's hard to get enough done for your company that week. Class sessions don't really add anything to the experience, but overall I learned new things despite ambiguity and some unmotivated teammates.

This class is what you put into it. I thought my project was awesome but also a ton of work. The classwork did not corroborate with the company work. I did not find in-person lectures useful or helpful. Get ready to spend at least 7.5 hours on this class/week.

Interactions with this professor are rare, as lecture is only held 6 times throughout the semester. Your TA is essentially your real teacher. Feels like meaningless assignments are thrown into the course to add some sort of value, but time could be better spent focused on the actual internship aspect.

An OCI is a great learning experience where you can get your feet wet in a certain industry without having to commit to anything long term. The mandatory lectures should be on demand, going to class is pointless if you have taken this class more than once.
I would hesitate to do an OCI. There are project that sound great but other projects with painful sponsors and underdeveloped companies.
Really nice professor who cares about his students!
Great internship opportunity! Met great teammates and learned a lot.

Great experience! You only have to go to class a couple of times a semester. The rest of the time is spent with your internship group. It is almost all group work with your internship team and sponsor.
He isn't the kindest person of all time from what I could see. Not terrible but not great. The class was pretty boring and it was a lot of work even though it  was quite easy.
Only a few lectures throughout the semester, mostly group work! Overall cool experience.
This class was a great learning experience, but it was definitely my most time consuming class this semester. I had an amazing sponsor and team, which made all the difference.
The class will heavily depend on your project, sponsor and group. But overall, good class
This class was simple as long as you put in the work and average 7.5-9 hours outside of class. It was a great learning experience.
Class is useless but you are still required to attend class every time it is held.
I thoroughly enjoyed this class. Come ready to work and be stretched. There are 6 mandatory class periods, other than that you are working with your internship team.

Professor Hollan is the best! I really enjoyed the course and how he created it. You only see him 4-5 times in the semester since the rest of the time you are working with your group on the internship you were assigned. It honestly depends on your group and the willingness of the members to work if you enjoy it. I highly recommend OCI!

This probably has more to do with the course than Professor Hollan, but I felt like the lectures were a waste of time besides recording mandatory attendance. There is so much busy work and I felt like while they encourage variety in projects so many of the graded reports have such a strict structure that doesn't fit the variety of projects.

Dave Hollan gets the job done. Not the most inspiring teacher, but works hard to provide a great learning experience for students in OCI. Don't miss classes (check the calendar because classes are randomly scheduled here and there). Don't miss assignments, every assignment has a hard deadline.
Professor Hollan is the best. He clearly explains how to get an A and how to be successful in jobs and internships. Definitely take from him!

The OCI is great as a resume builder and not very difficult either. It's a bit annoying having to log 7.5 hrs/week to get an A but overall doable. I wouldn't take the course again since I've got real internships now but would definitely take it if you're just getting started and trying to gain some real-world experience.

Professor Hollan was a great professor and I enjoyed his lectures. However, I did not particularly love my OCI internship experience. This was primarily due to the sponsor we worked with and the work they had us preform. I did not gain much value from the work we did from our sponsor.

It was a great class overall. I loved how hands-on the learning was. It was definitely life-changing and a great experience. The lectures were a little dry but they didn't happen that often so it was a good class.
He was good about answering question my group had and gave us lots of resources to succeed

Professor Hollan is awesome! The class only had 6 mandatory lectures for the semester. All of the assignments are completed online with the main focus working with your group and sponsor the whole semester. OCI is a great way to get experience and this class will help you learn a lot while also getting credit for your major or minor.

The class has a good structure, so it's easy to follow and get a good grade as long as you remember to log your hours. The only thing I would change was how many reports were due during the first half of the semester which made it hard to get actual work done. I would recommend taking the class if you get a cool project you're interested in!

This class is good for getting real business experience, but you must be careful when choosing your project. Mine, Live for Music, had a completely irrelevant/incorrect project description. The more established companies should be ok. It's 7.5-9 hours of work outside class, but your team meetings and class time count toward it.

I would look for an internship elsewhere. Professor Hollan assigns so many reports, projects, planners, etc. that you barely have time to help the company. All the assignments are a waste of time and try to teach skills you'll most likely never need.

Professor Holland is organized and sets clear grading criteria. I don't necessarily think that all of the in-person lectures were necessary, but there weren't that many so it wasn't the biggest hassle. Most of the work you'll be doing is with your group, so he's not going to be hovering over your shoulder the whole time. He is very helpful.

MSB 494R was a good class (it's an on campus internship). Most of the work is spent working with your sponsor 7.5-9 hours a week. This includes any homework and class time. You really only meet as a class 6 times in the whole semester and attendance is mandatory. Work hard, show up, be nice, and listen to your team and you'll do fine.

There isn't much interaction with Professor Hollan throughout the semester, just 6 required classes. The rest of the semester is spent meeting in teams and with company sponsors, and the workload and type of work depend a lot on what your internship is.
Easy class, lots of outside class work. An actual internship.

This class was organized well. You will complete modules which will then translate to what you talk about in class. There are only 6 times you go to class in person. You will primarily be working on your project with the team you are put into.  Professor Hollan was nice and explained things well.
I had a great internship experience and was able to work well with my team. The TA's were always available and willing to answer questions. I would recommend taking this class.

Professor Holland teaches a good class for the On Campus Internships. Your workload will determine on the internship you get assigned to but you need to put in at least 7.5 hours every week. The assignments aren't too bad and you only have to attend class 6 times. You should get an A if you turn in everything on time and your sponsor likes you.
The class is easy, but the lectures are rather un-engaging. This class is spent 90% with your team, so the success of the class depends on how well you work with your team.
The class was pretty easy. Attendance is only 6x over the semester. Learned a decent amount. Lots of busy work.

Be prepared for a real internship and the workload that comes along with that. Make sure to have be in contact with your TA as often as possible, especially so they can review all of your documents and presentations. This class is definitely great to understand the business world and the needed personal attributes you need to succeed in it.

Just do your work outside of class and make sure you get in your hours and input them every week and you should be good. Attendance is mandatory but you only have to go to class like 5 times in the semester not every week.
Hollan was good, but I still felt like there were too many assignments for the class, and I wished I could have given all 7.5-9 hours every week to basically just the company I was interning for.
Super awesome class and professor. Nothing too difficult, just lot's of time commitment to the project. Class is mandatory.

There are only 6 classes you attend all semester long and the lectures usually don't go along with your OCI project. He likes talking about resumes during that time and other things that are helpful. You can tell that he really is there for the best interest of his students but delegates pretty much everything outside of class to his TA's.

Bro Hollan is a businessman first and an educator second. He's direct with what he teaches, which can rub some people the wrong way. When you take time to actually meet with him in person, he can be very kind and helpful. The grade overall is determined more by how your company sponsor thinks about you than the professor. Heavy workload is a given.

Good professor, he gives good lectures that are relevant and not super redundant. We only had class 6 times in the semester. The OCI class itself is what is time consuming because it's about hours, that part of it was super stressful to have to spend that much time. However, it is a great course where it's all about application and I learned a lot.

The group you are in for your internship and your project make a big difference, but you do not really get much say. If you do the work you'll get an A. Definitely a work heavy class, if you want an A you have to spend at least 7.5 hours working on your project each week.

This class all really depends on your team and sponsor. Professor Hollan does a great job helping and teaching us to connect, work well and communicate with our sponsor. He is very real about deadlines and no making up work. He does a great job of reflecting the reality of the real business world.
You need to input your hours each week and do the modules which take zero brain cells. I got lucky with my team, but if you aren't lucky this class could suck.
Knowledgable about the business industry, has great connections for his students, comes off just a touch arrogant

This class has been an absolute blast. MY OCI was so fun and professor Hollan sets it up so that you can achieve maximum learning. You have to be willing to put in the hours each week and coordinate with your team. This is not a class where you can get by only by doing the bare minimum. Work hard and this experience will be extremely beneficial.
Great professor. Funny and helpful. Clear professional. Set me up well for success outside of class.

My experience with Professor Hollan was decent. He is a genuinely good person. As for his lectures, they were often just reiterating material that was already available online. While this may be necessary for some students, I personally found it a bit repetitive and would have appreciated more in-depth discussions or real-world examples.
Gained great experience working with a professional company. Professor Hollan outlines what is expected, and as long as you execute this you can easily get an A in the class.
Taking an On-Campus internship was a great experience. The only problem I had was remembering to update my timesheet. As long as you stay on top of that it should be easy to get an A in the class.

He is a business man, and don't seem too likely to bend rules for anyone. OCI's are awesome, but I think this class has too much class work instead of focusing on what the sponsor and the company needs.
annoying and useless course work that detracts from the actual work projects you do

I honestly did not learn very much from the professor. The class was entirely group based, so the only time I saw Professor Hollan was during class. I am not quite sure what the point of class was because he just read the slides from the modules online. He did show us some resources that will help for applying for jobs which was appreciated.

I took the On Campus Internship class which made interaction with this professor pretty infrequent. If you are taking an OCI class this semester be warned that not every internship is made equal. Professor Hollan's tone in class had "talking down to small children" vibes which was irritating. However, the principles taught are invaluable.

David Hollan was by far one of the least considerate and rudest professors of my entire college experience. He has the type of attitude that makes everything "his way or no way." In class he would basically pick on 1-4 students and humiliate and drill them to make them feel stupid. Literally no consideration for you or your sponsor at all. F-

Professor Hollan is great! He really encourages participation and makes you feel very welcome and accepted in his class. This was a great opportunity to learn more about creating a professional career. Definitely would take again!
He is a great guy and is really easy to work with.
Loved this class! Prof provided insights that were useful for all projects, clear grading, good experience.
David Hollan is super nice. There are only like 6 lectures total in the whole semester. Just do your part and put in the hours for your internship.
The OCI is a good opportunity to get some good hands-on experience, but I didn't like the busy work the class itself gave.
I think it's annoying that we can't logs hours the next week. Also, he calls on people who don't raise their hands. However, I did learn a lot in his class!

This class is honestly a must for every business major. I got to work on a project for Boeing and it was a really incredible experience. Adding that to my resume got me an interview and a job offer for after graduation. The class can be taken as many times as you like (I've done it twice) so you have no reason for graduating without a full resume.

At the end of the day, this  on-campus internship class really isn't about the professor (you're only in class like 6 times). That being said, the material while in class was helpful enough, but nothing incredibly engaging. What I most appreciated about Professor Hollan, though, is his inextricable link with the gospel. He's a good man!
A lot of group work and meetings. Projects focus on dealing with ambiguity. Be ready to spend a lot of time every week on your project.
Professor was good, it's the sponsor that really determines what your semester is like.
class is chill but the actual course just depends on your team and what company you end up with. It's a lot of work outside of class
Extremely helpful when needed, TAs are very helpful as well, easy A if you stay on top of everything and communicate
Well educated in his field. Gives great insight during lectures.
This professor is very clear and to the point would highly recommend.

Professor Hollan was a super easy-going guy, but watch out for the TAs. Our project's TA gave us more to do than our actual sponsor... and made us re-do big assignments multiple times because they were never good enough. The sponsor didn't care at all about the class projects we had to complete.

OCI's are so loved by the business school but it honestly all depends on your project, group members, and TA. I liked my project and my sponsor, but not my TA. Our sponsor was really chill and not super worried about the final report or the presentations. However our TA was not chill and she was the worst.

The On-Campus Internship course is a great opportunity for students to gain exposure to the business world early in their education. Asks students to do 7.5 hours of work a week for their business which depending on the week can be hard or easy to complete. Course content consists of really depends on the company you are assigned to.
Does a good job guiding you throughout the project
Professor Holland cares so deeply about his students. He works hard on the OCI program and makes it a great opportunity for all of his students to learn and grow professionaly

The On-Campus Internship at BYU has great potential, but I feel like the class structure makes it drag a bit. I felt as if I was doing busywork to "learn" about how to work well as a team and a company, while I feel like the true learning this course provides comes from actually working with the OCI team, TA and company sponsor.
Great guy, easy grading and would take again.
Good class if you have a nice project, kinda sucks if your sponsor/company is bad.

Professor Hollan is a great teacher and mentor. My OCI team had some group dynamic problems (students not participating much or helping with the project) and some issues with our sponsor but he was terrific at helping us work through everything. I learned a ton in this class, especially how to deal with ambiguity.

This class really opened my eyes to what being a part of a start-up business is like. I was exposed to a new environment that is very difficult to describe, but enjoyed every part of the experience. Professor Hollan did a great job in guiding his students to set appropriate expectations for the course and projects we were assigned.
Most of this class is just work outside of class for your sponsor company. It's an easy A but it's more about what you want to get out of the class related to your career.
Has an interesting sense of humor but means well. Cares about the students and gives the tools needed for success.
Very fun guy. Lectures were always helpful and everything we talked about was applicable to the real world.

Professor Hollan seemed like a nice guy though we only saw him a few times throughout the semester during mandatory classes. My only critique was the amount unnecessary busy work on canvas especially at the beginning of the semester which made it a little more difficult to jump into the actual projects/internships. Great experience otherwise.
This is a great opportunity to get real-world experience in the business world. The class itself is mostly just busy work, but there are some helpful resources given.
Professor Hollan is a great teacher. This class is awesome to get real-life experience and to build your resume. Take it!
Great experience. Class is super organized, though it does require a consistent time commitment due to the timesheet. Great TA's and allows opportunity for hands on experience.
He was awesome and involved. The course takes up time due to the nature of the timesheet but it's straightforward and great hands on experience.

Professor Hollan provides an immense number of resources for you to be able to use during a project in this course. I regret not being more communicative with him and the TA throughout the course of the project, I think their input would have been very valuable.

Professor Hollan was great in helping us understand more about the world of business. He had very good lectures that really helped to move our projects foreward. I would totally recommend taking this class to anyone! Just don't be afraid to get randomly called on haha

There are a few class periods that are mandatory but there really aren't too many lectures. Most time will be spent working with your group on your internship so time spent in this class depends a lot on your internship and how motivated your group is. I had a great group and it was lots of fun, but definitely time consuming. I learned a lot

I appreciated how he made us aware of how we could build resumes and find opportunities for career growth. I didn't love how he randomly called on people to give their thoughts. Some lectures feel "fluffy" or some of the class content and assignments feel like busy work.

Only a couple of classes are mandatory. 
Lectures are super laid back.
The only work you do is outside of class with your group.
Professor Hollan does a good time of guiding students with what they need to do in their Internships. I felt like he was pretty understanding and made it clear what was expected
This class was great! I felt like it had so many tools necessary to help me prepare for future jobs and internships!
Professor Holland is clearly very passionate about what he teaches and he wants us to be successful. I could tell he set up our ocis so we could really get real life experiences.

You don't do much with the actual professor. When you are in class, he provides some great advice and tools on how you can succeed in your project and in your future career, but the success of this class is way more dependent on who your teammates, TA, and sponsor are. If they are great, it'll be a great class. If not, it will be a long semester.

Professor Holland and more importantly his TA's made my experience taking an OCI fantastic. I didn't ever feel like expectations were unclear and they were always willing to help. They sent out reminders of when things were due quite frequently. Overall a wonderful experience.

Professor Hollan is a decent professor that cares about students. You wont see very much of him as you'll mostly be working with your group, but he offers to meet with groups to give help when needed. Plan to put in at least 8 hours of work weekly. There were good learning opportunities, but this class was a source of stress for me this semester.

David Hollan for the On Campus Internship course at the Marriot Center is a decent professor. He is a stickler to a hard set of policies and rules for the course. Despite experiencing a few negative extenuating circumstances arise this semester that took a real toll on my attendance and internship hours however I received no help or way to recover.
He is an excellent professor willing to answer your questions and make sure your internship is a great experience for you.

The class overall is great if you have a great team to work with, but there is a lot of assignments not related to the project you are working on. There are a lot of things that take up time you could have spent on the project.

Professor Hollan is the no-nonsense professor that a course like this needs. He's serious about his job, trains his teaching assistants well, and ultimately delivers the on-campus internship experience as promised. However, there are some administrative burdens on students in this class that could be reduced.
Professor Hollan is super professional and kind. He and the TA's know how to help you have a good experience, and if you follow their counsel you will have a super good experience from the OCI.

The OCI class was a great opportunity to learn and Prof. Hollan was a great teacher! He did a great job of laying out what is expected of you and how to do well in the class and also in your future profession. There is one class period a week (50mins) and classes are optional and other time there is an attendance code you have to submit.
Professor Hollan was a great teacher. He provided useful TA's to help you every step of the way. Would take the program again.

I think the professor was fine but it's mostly based on who you get as your sponsors. be prepared to do a lot of work outside of school. Also I would have been ok but our sponsor had more busy work but I still learned . When choosing what companies to work for be very detailed in reviewing them and  what you can learn.
Its a good class but does take a lot of work. Also if you do not like group projects, then DO NOT take this.
This is a great class! Professor Hollan gives such great advice on how to work with large companies and is willing to help in anyway!
Prof Hollan is super insightful and will help you succeed in your internship!
Take the class and you will learn a lot.
Brother Hollan is a good dude and cuts the crap of normal professors
A lot of work outside of class. Your experience totally depends on your Sponsor's expectations. Besides the final project, the class itself doesn't ask too much of you assignments wise.

Prof. Hollan is a good professor! The main thing affecting your experience in his class is what project you get assigned. I got a really good sponsor that gave us clear direction with our deliverables but enough freedom to be a bit creative in our approach
Cool guy. Lectures aren't always required, most of the class is done with your group, outside of class.
He is a great guy and really looks out for students and their overall experience and life.

MSB 494R with David Hollan was a great class. It is an internship class, so most of your time is spent outside of class. There are a few classes throughout the semester that are mandatory attendance, but those classes often felt kinda unnecessary. Although it was an internship class, there was a lot of required coursework at times so be ready.

Professor Hollan is great, but I didn't really like the course or the project I had. I would say it is worth taking if you make sure you get a project you really vibe with, if you get assigned one you don't like I would say to drop it and try again another semester.
I really loved the way professor invited us to connect with others. Being professional is also crucial to your grade!
There are certain mandatory days, but this class will be mainly be working with your group. Overall an easy class and learned a lot!

Professor Hollan was a fine professor but this class really depends on the project you get. Some are awesome and some just okay. Canvas work isn't very helpful and tedious. If you know the experience is gained outside of the class and not with the professor in class you will do great.
This is a great opportunity to get real-world experience through an internship. You don't meet much as a class but you will be meeting a lot as a group outside of class. Overall a great experience.

Good professor overall, wants you to succeed and thrive in whatever you want to get into! Good class for internship credit and not too difficult. Make sure to work well and communicate with your team, sponsor, and TA. Workload heavy.

Professor Hollan's class is not a "real world" work experience, it's actually far from that. For example, If for any reason you missed updating the timesheet one week, you're screwed for the rest of the semester, and the hours of work you put into the project that week won't count. Also, the syllabus isn't 100% true, just keep that in mind.

This class has probably the best opportunities you can have in your freshman or sophomore year. Professor gave us a lot of insights and things to be aware of in business workplace. Definitely recommend the class!
The OCI class is about how much work you want to put in, and how much you want to get out. The teacher doesn't do much, the TA is honestly more involved.

Dave is great! He has a lot of professional experience and his insights are gold. 

OCIs provide you with useful, but not exceptionally impressive resume material. Still, its a great way to have something concrete. 

Dave encourages taking the class more than once and reserves the internships with high-profile companies for returning students.

Dave is hilarious. My favorite class this semester. 10/10 would recommend. If you have a bad group Dave will just make jokes about it and make you feel better about your group. He teaches you life long skills and ways to look at life. Out of all my classes this semester this one has been the most enjoyable.

You could tell he meant well but the material learned in class and in modules was redundant and not helpful. Professor would just call on people at random and force participation and that was always uncomfortable. Lots of busy work but easy class.
His approach to teaching MSB 494R is to metaphorically throw us into the deep end and give resources as issues come up. You will feel unprepared, but you'll get through it.
Professor Hollan is a real world teacher, he doesn't care for your comfort zone. He cares that you learn and grow, put in the work and you will come out of this class better for it.
This class is literally the best, great opportunity!

Professor Hollan is super chill as long as you get your stuff done. We only had class about 8 (eight) times during the semester and Professor Hollan used these class times to educate us on how to improve our professionalism and how to gain the competitive edge going forward in the business school.

He was a great teacher. I wish I had been able to give more input into the project I received. It was a good experience, but the project was very unimportant and unrelated to topics and careers that I have interest in.
Pretty good class. really depends on your project.
Helped me to become more prepared for the workplace and great for getting experience on your resume during the semester.

Professor Hollan is a fantastic teacher, there is not a lot of homework on canvas but you need to work each week for 7.5 hours at least, you need to work on your midterm presentation and your final, is not easy but you get a lot of experience.

This class is not was I expected from what the advisor said. I don't regret taking it, but I do wish I had a different internship. I did mine at BYU and I imagine that was different from what a lot of other people got to do. The classes were very unnecessary which was incredibly frustrating. I was glad I got a great group of people to work with.

I did an on-campus internship, which I would STRONGLY recommend! It's easy to get an A, but it requires a lot of work and time (7.5-9 hours a week for an A, which includes research, meetings, etc.). There are modules that you complete each week, but they're graded easily. There is also a midterm presentation and a final report and presentation.

This professor was passionate about what he did, i had no problem with him or the way the class was set up. Luckily my group was on top of things which made my experience much easier, a bad group could make this class tough.

Professor Hollan was a solid professor. He didn't have much to do with the actual class as most of it is direct communication between you and your sponsor. The class itself is an easy A as long as you log 7.5-9 hours of work per week on the dashboard and complete all the weekly modules (which are extremely easy and take no longer than 20 minutes).
Great experience. Every student's thoughts on the class are mostly influenced by the internship they got, so it really depends. I personally enjoyed the class and the new experiences I got from it.

Professor Hollan is a wonderful person, he can help you a lot with your networking and he gives you all the resources you need to build your resume. Is not a hard class if you get involved in your project and work on your deliverables and build a good and healthy relationship with your sponsor.

The On-Campus Internship is an extremely good option for I believe the vast majority of students. Everyone receives a company to work with no matter what! Great resume builder. Helps a lot to get your feet wet in learning business functions and how to work with a team. Easy 3 credits, but it's on you to challenge yourself and go the extra mile.
This class is a lot of fun, and as long as you manage your time well it is pretty easy.

The lectures are all very good and applicable, even beyond the scope of the OCI projects.  It's really easy to get an A in the course, but if you actually want to get something from the experience then you're going to have to work.

Basically, this class is 65% doing stuff for your sponsor, 10% class attendance, 20% working on a midterm and final, and 5% looping the TAs in on what you're up to. Go to the mandatory classes for points and to learn about the rubric for the midterm and final. Professor is nice, TAs are helpful, and the class can be funny.

Overall, it was a great class and Professor Hollan was very inspirational and excited to help us out. However, I feel like the class was more focused on the assignments, papers, and presentations than actually helping the sponsors/companies that we were interning at.
Professor had a very clear and to the point teaching style, very easy to comprehend.

This internship and class format is perfect if you have no business experience. For someone who has extensive full-time business experience, this felt like a waste of time and like I was teaching my classmates everything as we went... I wish there was a way to qualify out of this class.

Expect the unexpected! Ambiguity is what makes this opportunity enjoyable and valuable. This isn't a class where you can read the textbook, regurgitate information on a test, and get an A. The OCI is 100% what you make of it--if you choose to do your best work and adapt to change, you'll turn both setbacks and successes into learning experiences.

My internship experience was incredible, but my experience with Prof. Hollan was just ok. Tons of busy work and confusing class layout, additionally he wasn't very accessible or personable. I would still strongly recommend this class.
it all depends on the business you are assigned to

His outline and criteria helps you understand on how to complete a OCI project successfully and will give you the tools you need to overcome any setbacks you come across. His feedback was very helpful and helped our team get back on track

Professor Hollan works very hard to help students meet their sponsors expectation. That being said, students are expected to give the best impression they can and help keep up the school's reputation.

Prof Hollan's lectures mirrored homework assignments and readings that were due before class, making class feel very pointless. Make sure to put in the rqd number of hours or he'll meet with your whole team and threaten your grade if you don't perform better. Felt like he cared more about the optics of the program than the students. Fine, not great
Professor Hollan was a pretty chill if you did everything asked during the course. The OCI program is pretty cool.
Great teacher
Great course
I enjoyed this professor, I think he is good about telling you what you need to know without wasting your time. He understands that participation is what matters.

You will rarely see Prof. Hollan (maybe 6 times the entire semester) but this class is unique because almost 100% of the class is done outside of the classroom. Each team will meet together and work on their internship which can be really good or not so depending on what project you get. For the times that we did meet, Prof. Hollan was a good guy.

I'm honestly very grateful I took this class. It's an awesome class for people that need something to build up there resume. I wouldn't do this class again because the company I did the internship for didn't really care about the work we did.

Professor Hollan comes on very strong at the beginning of the semester. I felt a bit nervous. He slowly eases up as the time goes on. He has very clear expectations and very little (if any) room for error. Even if your computer glitches causing a mishap, it is your responsibility. He is willing to meet students one on one.
This class is a huge time commitment so be prepared to put in at LEAST 7.5 hours a week if you want an A. Professor Hollan is great and I found what he had to say very useful.
You barely interact with the professor, which isn't a criticism. The class is focused around interacting with a project sponsor, a real world company.

Good teacher for the most part just given a lot of busy work it seemed. Not a huge fan of the tools that he chose to have us use, seemed more complicated than useful. Didn't really feel I got to know teacher due to size of class, and such few classes.

This is a hands-on experience internship offered through BYU. The work load is 6-7 hours of work each week. You truly will work in a hands-on experience with a group of students from a similar major. Professor Hollan was a great motivator and he pushes students to learn and grow. This course was definitely a class to learn and work hard.
Gives brutal feedback, sometimes for the better but mostly not.

In the few lectures held, Professor Hollan was straight to the point and focused on what was most important. He expects you to represent BYU well. The class itself was primarily interactions with your group, TA, and sponsor. I was blessed with a great team, TA, AND sponsor, but I know that not every student is that lucky.

David Hollan is "no-nonsense." He encourages students to be proactive and engaged, and to really make the most of the class experience.  After almost all of the lectures I came away feeling inspired and often humbled.
Professor Hollan is an awesome guy that is always willing to help his students. He wants all his students to succeed and is willing to work alongside you to help that happen.
Not a lot of interaction with Professor Hollan. This class was awesome though.

This was a great class to gain experience in the field I am looking into! It was a bit of work and it took some time but overall, I thought it was helpful. Brother Hollan was helpful in providing resources and open to helping us by giving us feedback and an outside perspective. This class is majority the project you are assigned to.

Professor Hollan is a business professional through and through. He shared lots of good information, was fair in grading, but was lacking in interpersonal skills. Be prepared for well-intended but rude comments.

This class is kind of a drawbag I feel. If you get a good sponsor and you want some industry experience then it will be good for you. If your sponsor is unorganized and doesn't really know what they're doing then it's gonna be tough. The modules and class required homework felt like a lot of busy work to me.
In-class material was always super clear. Not every in-class material was relevant to individual internships however, but that's why you have your own TA for your team.
Professor Hollan was a great teacher. We had one day a week with him and he provided information on what we  needed to get done for the week. He also gave us great resources.
He's grouchy and sassy

The majority of this class is working on your internship project. Great real-world experience. Professor Hollan is genuine and passionate about what he teaches, but I didn't feel that he cared for the students as much. You only actually meet in class a few times each semester. I would recommend taking this course to make a stronger resume.

Professor Hollan - He's a good guy. He does have a sort of passive-aggressive personality, like he is more used to dealing with others on a very high professional level, and if you aren't quite there yet he has little patience for you. However, the class is an amazing opportunity to get real business experience, so I'd definitely recommend it!

I think this course is very beneficial. It helps you gain more professional experience and it's not difficult to get an A. The projects vary in difficulty. Mine focused on social media marketing, and I'm happy with the skills I gained. Professor Hollan knows his stuff, but can be unnecessarily stern. Be sure to attend class and log your hours.

The class is great! I didn't find the lectures Dr. Hollan gave to be anything very useful though, and seemed that most of the module assignments were a necessary evil in getting everyone a grade. (All the projects are so different, standardization is difficult.) If you think of the modules more as "professional development" that helps.
If you want to be lectured in class about being an ungrateful entitled BYU student then take this professor. Waste of a semester.

The On-Campus Internship was a great experience and resume builder and I loved my team, sponsor, and project. However, the in-person class seemed to be a bit pointless and could've been done over zoom. Some of the work in the modules also seemed to be busy work but some were helpful. Overall a great experience and well worth it.

Good opportunity to gain experience, so I recommend the course. The class periods were pointless, and required you to come in person to attend a 15 minute class that could have been a zoom call or module on Canvas. Besides the class periods, he didn't really affect my experience in the class though, so overall I wouldn't recommend against the class

The experiences I had in this class were amazing! I had a wonderful team and sponsor for the internship, and we were able to accomplish a lot together. Class itself and some of the assignments we had to complete were kind of annoying because they had nothing to do with our project, and didn't feel very helpful, but they were easy.

This class was amazing for getting real-life experience with low risk. I love the creativity and opportunity associated with this class and would recommend it. The only negative part was Professor Holland's impertinent attitude. Class time was mostly fluff and not necessary. However my experience with the sponsor and team were excellent.
Professor Hollan was a fine teacher. We only met in person 4 times throughout the semester so he didn't have much effect on the class. It was mostly just us in our internship groups working together.

Definitely do an On-Campus Internship, it is a great experience and can be fun! However, I was not the biggest fan of Professor Hollan. His classes were pointless and he had a rude attitude. His class was the only negative part of my OCI experience.
BEST CLASS EVER!!! I highly reccommend taking this course for anyone going into the business school! Stress free class and you get to work with some amazing companies!

An on campus internship can be an awesome experience and looks great on applications. Professor Hollan himself was good. Lectures are mandatory but don't add a whole lot to the experience. The hardest part is that you need to average 7.5 hours of work on your project per week in order to get an A, and catching up can be hard if you fall behind.
The OCI program is awesome! Would definitely recommend to anybody.
Great class with lots of opportunities to learn new skills and actually apply them in real life scenarios. Great resume building class as well.

I took Hollan's class for an On-Campus Internship. The internship is a good way to get work experience and business opportunities for college credit. I learned a lot, and had an amazing TA who helped my group through the whole process, as there is a lot to remember for the course. The actual class was not super helpful but attendance is mandatory.

Only 6 classes for the whole semester and most were less than 1 hour. Some busy work, but mostly to ensure people are on track. Most of your grade is weighed on your performance in the internship, so busy work isn't too bad.

Although I somewhat enjoyed my on campus internship, I felt like Professor Hollan is not who you should take it with. Although you only have class 8ish times a semester he made it grueling and a chore.

This class is different for each person because it depends on what internship you get assigned, but I had an amazing experience! This class has opened doors for me and has enabled me to get an awesome job before I apply to the business school. Highly recommend taking this class. Youll get out of it what you put in:)
Super helpful and easy to talk to, this class is purely focused on your assignments and projects for your internship.
This is a great opportunity to get an internship on your resume. Make sure to report your hours and keep your average up.
The class didn't require much time within the class but the time there was good. It provided what it needed to.

Professor Hollan was more like a supervisor rather than a team manager. Since this is an internship, we only talked to him in class about twice a month. Besides that, there was a lot of autonomy. I recommend choosing an internship that you are wanting to be passionate about because this class requires about 8 hours of work per week.

The OCI Internship is a fantastic opportunity, don't hesitate to sign up if you're interested. I wasn't the biggest fan of Professor Hollan. He has very little impact on your experience though, so don't worry about if you like him or not. I learned a lot of professional skills and would recommend this class to anyone.
He was great. Told us what we needed to do to succeed.
Good teacher. Although his lectures were mostly useless except for before big projects.

I took this for my On-Campus Internship, and this class is fairly easy, but the busy work for this class is ridiculous. While trying to satisfy the sponsors needs, you're also required to go through modules for this class over things that are pointless. Nothing you learn from Bro Hollan is relevant/applicable to your actual project.

Professor Hollan is more of a facilitator rather than a traditional professor. He does a good job laying out the structure of the class, but mostly you are going to be just meeting with your assigned group and TA. It's easy to get an A, but if you actually work hard and try to get the most out of your experience you'll actually learn something.
The class is a ton of fun, learned a lot with my team. The lectures are pretty much useless but you have to show up for credit.
Required attendance in class, but class doesn't happen every week. Great teacher and the TAs are awesome.
An awesome class with good experience.

In the class you don't participate too much with Prof. Hollan, but his few lectures are always awesome. He's always available to answer questions and will fight for you if the internship isn't going the way it should.

The class is a group project, which makes it difficult at times. Luckily, as long as you do what you need to for the class, you can get a good grade, but ultimately, what you get out of the class is what you put into it. Most important is to learn skills and habits of professionals through your efforts in this class.

The class itself is kind of useless. The internship you get will depend heavily upon what you learn. There is always something to learn from the different internships. Even if it is how not to run a company

He is a good professor. You have to go to class, but it can sometimes feel somewhat pointless. Otherwise, he is an incredibly helpful professor, and wants you to succeed. Make sure that you pick a good project!

I took the OCI class (On-campus internship) and you dont have much interaction with the professor. It was a fun class and it was very different from a traditional class in which you have assignments to complete. Instead, you have an overall project goal and you figure out how to complete it with your group.
all depends if you get a good company. loved mine, but wayyyyy too much classwork that I wish I could have just focused on helping my company.
This is a difficult class, but no one can run it like Professor Hollan. He's always willing to help with your internships.
Not too bad. Classes felt a little pointless at times but usually never actually took the whole class period.
A really helpful class and he is the facilitator of it. I had to work hard in my group to do well and if your group is a good one then you will love the class. Professor Hollan just helps you along.

Prof Hollan is not super involved in your class experience because it is an internship but on the days we do have class he gives good insight. You must attend class to get the credit. His work and expectations outside of the internship are manageable and not too difficult.

Professor Hollan was hard to approach and learn from. He almost condemns you for making a small mistake. He throws a lot of information towards you without much guidance or direction on how to do things. A lot of little class work to do with no feedback. Felt more of an obligation to do than an internship. Felt watched all the time.

This class gives you internship experience for credit. Class is mandatory, but is only held a handful of times each semester, and is usually only 20-30 minutes. Workload is manageable, but expect putting in 7.5 hours per week to get an A in the class.
Be prepared to work really hard and put a lot of effort into this class. It is not easy and is very time consuming.
Great professor, smart, logical, resourceful, and funny.

Doing an OCI was a really valuable experience I would 100% recommend for anybody in any major to do one. Professor Hollan really cares and I didn't need a ton of help from him throughout the semester but when I did he was really helpful.
Totally depends on the sponsor you get. The lectures were chill. You only have to go a few times a semester and listen to what you do in the modules.

Professor Hollan is a true professional. He is very straight forward, but unless you take this class for a joke, there is no reason why you should score below an A-. This class will be a waste of time if you allow it to be. It's really up to you to develop yourself as a professional in preparation for your career.

This was a great class, because we got to work with a "real-world" company, but we had class with Professor Hill about once a week, sometimes not even that though. He's good, but I personally just didn't jive too much with him. I don't know why. Probably just a personal problem.

This class was required for the business minor and I had no idea what to expect! Essentially, you will choose a company to be an intern for and you will have a semester-long project helping that company. Expect to spend a lot of time on this course! Prof Hollan is happy to help. You'll work more closely with the TA's in this course, though.

This is an On Campus Internship course. Class only meets like 6 times during the semester, but you're expected to attend 2+ meetings with your team per week. Be prepared to think and produce without micromanaging. This class helps you to understand how the real world works- in other words, making quality work to fulfill a need other than a due date

Prof. Hollan gives amazing opportunities to students to get real work experience within a school setting through this OCI class. You need to forget the grade and put forth valid work for these companies to use. The grade will follow if you treat these internships like a real job and perform. I had an amazing experience. 100% recommend to ANYONE!
There is a lot of work each week and may seem overwhelming, but very worthwhile learning skills you can't obtain in a regular class

Its more like a a part time job paired with a class. Its useful in learning professional skills in a workplace setting. If you put in the hours, do the work correctly, you can get an A. Not cognitively demanding.
great teacher, easy A

This class was really fun and different from any other class I've taken. Every internship and project is different however so I would say choose your internship carefully. Professor Hollan was great though and very helpful when we had difficulties with our project and/or sponsor.
He did his job.
Great class and professor. Gain real-world experience, easy A but heavy time-commitment

This class was good because of the connections made with the business we were assigned to and actually got good experience. The bad part of the class was the busy work that we didn't actually need to do but we were required to do to help us be more organized.
This isn't your normal class. It is an on campus internship. Just stay on top of the random assignments and put time into your internship and you will be good
You do not have much contact with Profesor Hollan, but if you need him he is available. Typically everything you do is through the TAs.

OCI with Professor Hollan was great. He was very willing to meet with my group and help us and walk us through some of the difficulties that we were having. He really knows his stuff and is well respected by his TAs and everyone else that knows him.

Great experience and I learned so much about working with a team and about the industry I am going into. 12/10 recommend this class Professor is great and willing to help and meet outside of class. Other than than that though, it truly is the best experience-based class. You will learn with your team as you go.

The class gives great opportunity to experience real-life company's operations. It allows you to see the inner working of a company and a glimpse into what the working world looks like. Do stuff the Professor's way or there will be problems, not very approachable or helpful when asked. Use the TA's for questions.
This class wasn't too difficult. Just hope that you have a good group and a helpful TA.
The internship itself was super fun, but attendance for the classes are mandatory, and I felt like a lot of the time the classes were more of a burden than a help.

The on-campus internships are very valuable and put students in a somewhat controlled work environment while sharing the reasonability's with a team. The class itself is very helpful in guiding you through the internship and setting expectations.
Hollan is great! Helps you succeed and gives lots of feedback when asked. The class is set up to work and gain actual experience.
This class was a great start for my schooling and career. It provided me with a lot of experience and knowledge that will help get me achieve other great internships and job opportunities.
OCI is your chance to obtain professional experience on campus. You will work with a group on a project given by the sponsor. Good luck!

This class gave me a lot of experience in the business field. Professor Hollan kept classes very short. Most of the class was working with your internship group and your company sponsor. You need to work 7.5+ hours to receive an A and that became tedious week-after-week.

As long as you put in the work for the class and do your timesheet on time you should easily get a great grade but your focus in the course should be the professional experiences. The class was helpful with the opportunities to work with real companies and gain actual professional experience. Highly recommend to take this course!
very easy as long as you work with your sponsor well
Class is a lot of work but overall a rewarding experience
Pretty easy class, professor made expectations pretty clear. As long as you follow what your internship sponsor tells you to do and what the rubrics tell you, you will be successful.

You learn a lot in this class but there isn't much interaction with Professor Hollan. Make sure to get a project you will be interested in for the whole semester. I am grateful for the experience, but I don't think I will do another OCI.
learned a lot
You have to put in consistent work for this class, make sure to get a project that you are interested in and want to do for a semester.
working with the company was super fun but the professor is very blunt.

Professor Hollan is fantastic! Super helpful with our projects and always ready to give feedback. We also only have six class periods in the semester and most of them were about twenty minutes, so a lot of our grade comes from our sponsor.

Overall a good class if you're looking to get some sort of experience before leaving the university.  The professor gets to the point, though there isn't a whole lot of interaction since most of the interaction should be with your sponsor company.  If you get a good team and stay consistent, you will like this class.
I really loved my internship! Professor Hollan does a great job at picking out meaningful experiences

Good teacher. This class does require you to put in the hours for your project. The whole class is essentially a group project- so be prepared for that. You will be putting in about 8 hours a week for this class (required). If you get a good team and TA, turn your assignments in on time, and put in the effort for your project, you will get an A.

I enjoyed this class for the experience however I felt as though much of the information talked about in the class periods was common sense. In addition, much of your experience in this class is determined by your sponsor and the group you're interning with. Your teammates can really make or break it for you.

I would not recommend this class to anyone. Our team got called in to meet with professor Hollan because our TA told him we weren't producing any work and wasting time in our team meetings due to our sponsor. Our team then met with the professor where he berated us with insults, and disrespecting us even though we had no control over the situation.

Throughout the course of the internship, the quality of this class relies more on the willingness of your group members to contribute to the project rather than Professor Hollan. The outlay of the class is effective and you don't notice him much throughout the course of the semester. He seems nice enough though.
Easy GPA booster

I didn't interact with Professor Hollan much because it is a group project semester and we all had a TA over our group. But he seems super chill in class and other than the first few classes, class is only 15-20 minutes long.
Great teacher, though this class focuses more on working with your internship group as opposed to working with him. Great class and I learned a lot
This class requires a lot of time to be set aside every week. He isn't very nice and doesn't make you feel good. Class is good for a resume and a little bit of experience. Lots of busywork.

You only go to class 6 times during the semester so you don't get to know him well, but he will answer any questions you have quickly. You mostly interact with your team and I enjoyed mine, but it will really depend on your project. It was a good experience, but keep in mind you are required to spend 7.5-9hrs/week and it's a 3 credit class.

He works very hard to provide his students with many resources and opportunities. I don't think the classes were altogether very necessary, especially considering the nature of the class. He was understanding with COVID-19. I wish we could have chosen our groups for the internship, however, since most of the class is just working with them.

This class really depends on the project you are assigned to. I loved my project and the people I was working with, but it may be different for everyone. Professor Hollan does a good job at letting you know about due dates and basic professional skills, but most of the work is done outside of class with your team and sponsor.

Good professor, class was kind of a waste of time and he talked about a lot of stuff that I feel is more common sense. It was a good experience and I'd recommend the class more for what you get out of the internship than the professor. There really isn't a whole lot of interaction with him other than about 6 or 7 times during the semester.
He was fine really, the class I took was definitely more affected by the people that were in my group than professor Hollan himself. He keeps classes short and gives you all the info you need.

I took the OCI class and while he's a great professor in organizing all of the internships and creating an environment where you can succeed, you don't interact with him much. The TA's are phenomenal though and help throughout the entirety of the project.

Prof Hollan keeps the OCI organized well, but class is practically useless. You are required to attend, but there was rarely any discussion that was helpful to the upcoming assignments. I relied a lot more on my TA than on the professor.
You have to attend class 6 times and lectures are kinda a joke. Just work on your internship 7.5 hours a week and you'll do fine.

Professor Hollan is a really nice professor and just wants everyone to get a good experience out of the class. He makes it pretty simple, you just have to work for your sponsor and then provide some proof to him that you did work.
You don't interact with the prof too often, its mostly with your sponsor. I loved this internship and I would do it again.
Overall a great class. It helps students get some relevant experience on their resumes.

It's a great opportunity to build your resume and gain experience. If you have a good team and a good TA you'll be fine and get an easy A. If not then it will probably feel more stressful and hard than it actually is.

This class is extremely helpful for students looking to get a head start in the business world because you do real work for a real company. You are required to log at least 7.5 hours per week to get an A in the class so effort is required, but it is all applicable to the real world. Would highly recommend taking this class more than once.

Professor Hollan is a good man who has a great concept for a class. The chance to work with a real company on a team of students is an amazing opportunity. Be prepared for ambiguity and autonomy in this class. There won't be many hard skills learned unless you initiate it. The course content isn't very beneficial unfortunately.

This class was not very upfront about how heavy it would be at the end of the semester. Working with a client is fun, but class assignments seemed to get in the way of the company projects we were doing--especially at the end when we had to wrap up our projects but also create a 50+ page report, professional presentation, & cover letter.
Class was enjoyable, totally hit or miss depending on the company you get.
Prof Hollan really prepares you for the business world and provides opportunities to work with professionals
The OCI class is a really great way to get both professional experience to add to your resume and class credit. Professor Hollan is very accessible and wants everyone to succeed.

It feels like he doesn't care about student experience at all. I took the business internship class from him and it felt like the in-class work we did was wholly unrelated to our projects. He didn't offer any help when problems arose (like someone dropping out of our group) and he clearly doesn't vet the businesses (ours had NO sales/employees)

I wouldn't take his on-campus internship again. Experience varies, but here's mine:
The internship with the company I have consists mostly of google searching for questions that the company has.   It took a great deal of focus and discipline to make it feel anymore than dull. I would much rather have spent these 3 credits somewhere else.

The OCI program is fantastic. The focus is on real life experience, not unimportant graded assignments just to fill your schedule. The fact that if you do your work you'll get an A inspires real development and not just doing as little as possible. Great class, great experience, I'll probably take it again.

Professor Hollan is a nice man. OCI is a really great opportunity to learn how to work with a group and get some resume boosting! His lectures, however, are really boring. The in-class meeting were kind of a waste of time in my opinion. But, don't let that deter you from taking an OCI! It's worth it.

An internship is a wonderful opportunity and while it is an easy A, it is hard work to deliver quality material to your sponsor and really get the most out of the experience. Be prepared for the longest group project of your life and real-world experience of working with others who may not have the same work ethic or expectations of quality work.

David did a great job helping us understand what the university expects from the OCI. We would pretty frequently only be in class for 20 minutes because he knew they were contributing to the internship. make sure you report your hours though! they are hard on deadlines.
I loved the project I was assigned to. I was able to get an awesome internship for this summer. I just wish we could have spent more time doing the project then going to lectures and doing modules.

You have to show up for the occasional lecture that's at most 30 min. You need to complete a few tasks with your team and put in 7 and a half hours per week to get an A. You're assigned a project sponsored by a business.

The class is strictly effort-based. He says at the beginning that this is the only class at BYU that you can fail every week and still get an A. He focuses on the things you need to know to help with the OCI, and doesn't add any fluff.

The OCI experience is awesome but the class is not. If I didn't have a sweet project I would have hated this class. There is a lot of unnecessary homework not related to your internship and he makes you work a certain amount of hours even if your project doesn't require to work that much. The internships are a lot of fun but the class is the worst.
The company that I was given for the semester was terrible. It had nothing to do with my major. Professor H loves to claim that this class is a resume builder but really it was a big waste of time.

I learned a ton and gained really valuable experience. You have to put in like 7 hours of work a week and keep track of it. But depending on your project it isn't that bad because it is stuff you'll enjoy doing.

Professor Hollan was a fine teacher but I did not feel he put that much effort into the students in the class. I did not feel like I learned that much during the classes but I also do not think that was the intention of the class periods.

The modules are easy because doing your deliverables for your company is the main thing. I would go to class every time because its easy and chill and most of the time only lasts like 20 minutes. Professor Hollan is very respectful of people's time and so if he finishes the lecture he just lets you leave. You can also go to any of the 3 class times
This was a challenging class but it really prepares you for the real world and getting a job.

This professor made it clear that he did not want to teach the class. He was not very respectful to his students. The nice thing is that you only have to attend the class a few times because the semester is full of working with a team and a sponsor for an On-Campus Internship.
Great class if you work hard then you will succeed.
MSB 494R is a great class to take from Professor Hollan which helps you gain real world expertise and build your resume.
He is really chill and his classes are really only 15 min not 1 hour
MSB 494R is an awesome class! You will learn so many different skills by doing real life projects and impacting major companies.

Professor Hollan expects a high level of professionalism from his internship students, which is to be expected. However, he is quite condescending in the way he teaches and speaks to students. He also will expect that this class is one of your very highest priorities, so be prepared to devote 8 hours a week.
Very good for relevant experience and to boost resume

This class is a lot of work. Each week you need to complete 7.5 hours to receive an A, but it is fairly easy. I was lucky and got a really good team, so I had a great time. I do know people that did not have a great team and struggled a lot during this project. Overall, I highly recommend this class! You will get a lot of great business experience.

Most of what I did during this On-Campus Internship wasn't with Professor Hollan. You have to hit a minimum number of hours each week that you've worked with your team. There are only about six lectures throughout the semester and everything else is done outside of the classroom.
Just stay on top of deadlines.

The OCI project itself was a super interesting and helpful way to be introduced to the world of business and gain  experience for a resume. The actual lectures, however, were not as interesting and helpful. David Hollan is a great guy and does well with the OCI program, but the lectures had no purpose. It was boring and a waste of time each week.

OCI's are great, just be prepared to spend a lot of time on your project. Grades are by hours spent, not work completed which can be frustrating at times, but that's just the nature of the class. Good professional experience as well.

The class itself was fantastic. The difficulty level and time spent each week will all depend on your project and your team. You get to put in recommendations on what project you work on but not your team. There are a few classes throughout which are kinda pointless tbh. They are like 15 min (so could be worse) but can def be sent in an email.

I loved this course! It really does help you gain some real world experience. But, I really did hate reporting hours, and feel like my grade suffered unnecessarily. Also, you never really know your grade in the class until after the final presentation of the semester.

Professor Hollan is super helpful but the nice thing about his class is that you're pretty much able to do most things on your own. He gives you the info you need to get a good grade but a lot of the guidance comes from your TA and sponsor company. The TAs are great and super helpful.
The classes were completely useless, I didn't learn a thing with him I learned it all on my own. The class is good but going to class in pointless and Professor holland doesn't help in any real way.

This internship was a great opportunity to learn about the outside business world, and learn in areas you want to learn about. I would take it if you want to enhance your learning in real-world business.
OCIs are an excellent opportunity to receive experience in the business world. Put in the work and try to learn from the class.

You only have to go to this class 6 times through the semester I think, but it's because your main focus is on the internship. You have to work at least 7 hours outside of class to get full points. Great learning experience though.

Take this class. You learn a lot from brother Hollan. Most of the time spent during the week is outside the class (Working with your team) Class only meets 6 times a semester and the class is usually 15 minutes.

Brother Hollan is a great professor and guide for your internship class. This internship will push you outside of your comfort zone and will test your ability to work with others. However, working on an OCI is extremely beneficial to your personal and educational growth. Take an OCI or multiple before you graduate and do not forget to enjoy them!

Professor Hollan did a great job of not babying us, and I appreciate that. A lot of people thought he came off as kind of arrogant, but I thought he was fine. Not my favorite professor ever, but you'll barely interact with him anyways. The class is awesome.

While class attendance is required, there are only 6 classes in the semester and though you have to put in the work to get the A (7.5-9 hours a week) its really just because you're doing real work for a company (so you're getting actual experience)! Final reports and presentations can be tedious but not out of the ordinary for a class like this.
Great class for your resume, and gaining experience in the business world. I highly recommend it, but make sure you choose companies you are interested in.

I enjoyed this. class, but I wish it was a little bit more internship directed than course directed if that makes sense. I felt like I was completing more coursework for the class rather than working for our sponsor. I loved my group and met amazing people!

This class looks really good on a resume when applying to the business school. I did spend about 8 hours a week working on this class but it honestly wasn't that bad. The lectures are boring but they are only about 20 minutes.
A great class if you want to gain experience in the work field

Hollan didn't really do to much actual teaching. You really just do everything in this class with your group and the TA assigned to you. Overall this class is great for gaining experience and adding to your resume. Would definitely take again.
Professor Hollan is a great professor. He requires that you go to class, but the classes only last 10-20 minutes each time. Would take again.
Good class, I learned a lot.

Professor Holland teaches a unique class with only a few lecture opportunities that are mandatory. He is great at communicating the importance of professionalism and quality in work. Sometimes the ambiguity in the OCI is frustrating, but it will work itself out with good teamwork.
Professor Holland teaches an interesting class with few lecture opportunities, but he really communicates professionalism and good information in the teaching opportunities he has.
Professor really encourages learning and professional growth for each student, and provides the opportunities and resources to do so if you take advantage of that.

The experience in this course is more dependent upon which project you get assigned to. You spend more time with your group and project than anything else.
