As long as you show up to class and put in your hours on the project, you will get a decent grade. If you hate the project or you don't do well in group projects, this will be difficult.

Professor Hollan is a stud, and exactly what you'd hope for with a professor running a few dozen internships. You're experience in the class, though, is much more dependent on what company you get paired with and your team rather than the professor. The internship requires at least 7.5 hours of work weekly, but will likely end up being a bit more.

As long as you do your hours, you'll do great in the class! Great experience for job resumes. The actual in-class was a little boring, but attendance is mandatory and was helpful for some assignments. He'd usually let you out early. Great teacher though.
Holland is a pretty bland professor, but the class itself is really cool. I got to work with a healthcare company in South Carolina. You get to use a lot of cool resources to do research.

The class is a great way to get hands on experience without having to go look for internships, as well as it gives students the opportunity to work with others they wouldn't normally associate themselves with. The groups are pretty diverse in what majors the students are going into as well.
Great class. Gives some real world experience

David is an amazing professor. He really cares about the students and he wants them to succeed in life. This OCI opportunity is really amazing. It helps us become responsible and learn what it is like to work in the real world. David and the TA's really want you to succeed! Great Course!

Honestly, an OCI is a good experience but a lot of projects are busywork and working with really difficult people. Make sure you are interested in your project or it will be a long semester! Class isn't bad at all. You meet a couple of times a semester and it's always less than 30 minutes. Overall, it was good.

David Hollan is very straightforward. He wants you to succeed and he also won't let you fail because it reflects badly on BYU. He wants the sponsors to like BYU students, because they are great and hardworking. Don't spoil it by being lazy.

Profession Hollan was pretty good for this class. I took the On Campus Internship so we didn't interact with him a whole lot. Mostly we talked to the TA's but he was always available and obviously wanted to help. An overall good experience but be ready for a lot of work. I would recommend if only that it looks good on your resume.
Great resume builder!
Great Resume builder! Watch the timesheet

Being in an OCI takes extra time considering it is an internship. But, the class portion was enjoyable. There are only 6 classes in the semester and they are mandatory. Prof Hollan does not waste time, and the classes were sometimes only 15 minutes.
The internship itself was a good experience, but Professor Hollan didn't seem to care very much. sometimes his comments were kind of mean
Great professor.

I felt that Professor Hollan was pretty demeaning towards the students and would always treat us like little kids. He would make constant comments assuming the worst from us and said on several occasions that it was time for us to all "grow up". This was not in direct response to our behavior. The OCI was however a great experience.

The actual work you do in this class is with the internship sponsor. It was a lot of fun! I had a great team and sponsor. There is very little that professor Hollan adds with his classes. He's a really nice guy though!!

Professor Hollan gave us all the answers to the quizzes that he gave us. Most of the work is graded on effort and simply following directions. The class itself isn't very challenging, but you get out of the internship what you put in.
Overall it was a great class.

He is pretty good, he has good experience but I never felt like the actual class period was that valuable. Sometimes we would show up for a 30 min class that easily could have been put in an email or video. Class gets out early pretty often which is great it just doesn't seem that necessary. The OCI itself is great experience!

Professor Hollan is great. This class gave me so much real-world experience and he always gave it to us straight up and never beat around the bush. He was really honest with us about the course work and how to succeed and everyone that followed that did well as far as I can tell. Take this class if you want to boost your resume and learn a ton.

We only had class about six times in the semester. When we did have class it was always about twenty minutes long and then he would let us out. Class is more of just a pow-wow to make sure everyone is on the right track. He is a funny guy and gives good tips about career development stuff as well as tips for the class itself.
Class is super helpful in choosing a career! Highly recommend Profesor Hollan
Prof Holland is perfect for this class. He's been doing it for a long time, so he has a seamless structure and knows what he expects and how to help.
The only thing is a lot of the things he goes over in class are things we already go over in the online module. It sometimes seems going to class isnt really necessary. Other than that he is great!

Professor Hollan is a good professor and he was pretty helpful a couple times, although honestly, there are only 6 class periods you need to go to and most of them don't last very long. The class is a good opportunity to get work experience, although there are definitely challenges. Make the most of it and it will be a good learning experience.

I loved this course! It is an awesome opportunity to get real world business experience. Prof Hollan is intense, but a nice guy. He only holds class a couple times throughout the semester, but attendance to those is mandatory, so go!
Self important business man on a power trip. Useless class. DO NOT take.

Overall not a hard class but super time consuming. There are a couple of mandatory classes you have to attend but the rest of the time was spent on the project you are assigned. As long as you get your hours in, it's all good.
Pretty manageable class. Just make sure you get a good group. Also, the lectures are pretty boring but you only have to go to 6 of them throughout the entire semester.
He is chill and the class is super informative. He tries to scare you a little bit but good practice for business world. Your sponsor is everything.

If you are looking for a very average professor, congratulations, you've found one. Nothing special here as far the professor goes. Thankfully, the class is structured so you really spend little time with him and rather you work with your group and sponsor. This class is full of ambiguity and team work. Good option to strengthen resume.
Best way to describe him is "corporate." He's a nice guy, but doesn't budge at all with any of the rules.
Can be a bit abrasive but it is clear he is doing his best to provide meaningful experiences and skills for the students.

The class itself is great! Prof Hollan is sometimes hard to listen to but you only have to go to class a few times. You learn a lot from this class, it is a great way to build your resume and have job experience for interviews.

Great opportunity for you to get real life experience while solving real problems. You don't hear much from Prof Hollan during the semester, but when you do he's a straight shooter. Sometimes it felt like there was a lot of busy work but it he's still a great teacher that gives great real life advice.
Make sure you show up to the six classes throughout the semester to get that easy credit and get the hours in outside of class and you're golden.

Don't go into this class expecting an easy A. You have to work for it and there is a ton of work to do outside of the class. That is all this class really is. You have to meet with your team at least 4 times a week and spend a minimum of 7 hours a week to get an A in this class.
OCI is good class to gain experience, just put in the hours and have a good relationship with your sponsor and you'll get an A.
Great experience to add to your resume.

Professor Hollan is kind and caring towards his students. He helped us to learn how to be better business people and more professional in our interactions with real companies. He does require attendance for class which only meets 6 times a semester. He is strict on this. He expects much, but this is how the business world works so it's helpful!
Good class, very unique set up

If you want to gain professional experience while still getting credit for school take an OCI. I really enjoyed it and didn't feel like this class was that hard. You will gain valuable skills and will be working in a team. I would highly recommend this class to anyone that is looking for experience working with a company.
Great Class, and an awesome opportunity to improve your resume. Professor Hollan is an easy grader on the projects and cares more that you had a great expierence.

Its a really good class to gain good resume experience but the project is completely up to you and your team. Class isn't every single week but you have to put in a certain amount of time each week which by the end of the semester gets boring and annoying.
He expects a lot of professionalism from his students and this can be interpreted as intense. He cares and wants us to do good work which is respectable and appreciated.
Professor Hollan was pretty chill, and the work isn't necessarily difficult, but the class takes a lot of time out of your week.
This was a pretty good internship. Not really what I expected but if you put in the work then you can get quite a bit out of it. A lot of it just depends on the internship that you get assigned.
Professor Hollan is a great professor! It was an online class so it was a little hard to get to know him as well. However he is always open to doing zoom calls and helping you out!
Super great class and great experience. There is just a lot of meetings every week and attendance is mandatory for the classes you do have. Work load is a lot, but good class.

Class material wasn't very engaging, but the projects student are assigned to are challenging and rewarding. I know that the work I did impacted a real organization and helped them complete work that they didn't have time for.

Great for resume if applying to MSB. Internship is hit/miss. Many sponsors are just in it to exploit university students for free labor. Six mandatory classes with an attendance code on canvas, but the lectures were 20 minutes and pretty pointless. Semester long group project, have to put in 7.5+ hours/week for an A. SUFFER THROUGH FOR THE RESUME!
This class lets you participate in a real internship.

This class gives you the opportunity to be an intern for a real company. Because of that, people's experiences vary a lot depending on their internship. Professor Hollan is a very smart man and a good teacher. There are only 6 classes. After the first couple of classes they rarely go longer than 15 minutes and feel kind of pointless.

Professor Hollan is a great guy and I can tell he wants the best for his students and their expereinces in the real business world. While it was good to brush up on internship expectations and practices, class did seem a little pointless. The hours we were required to clock in for the class were sometimes difficult to reach with a full schedule.

Professor Hollan is clear about his expectations. However, you only attend 6 classes the whole semester and the rest of the course is working with a company and group of students on a specific project.  Helped me learn more about what working with professionals will be like in the future. My group was awesome which made the class more enjoyable.
Wants to help students succeed. For sure use him as a resource during your on-campus internship.

Great professor! The class time and lectures feel a little bit pointless at times throughout the semester but the experience gained and relationships built from doing the internship is amazing. I would definitely recommend... this class is a great way to build your resume!

Personally, I didn't see him much since there are only six classes throughout the semester. I was lucky to be put on a good team with an amazing sponsor. If you want to have a good OCI experience, make sure to be a good communicator with your teammates and sponsor.

Great Professor but you don't see him much because the vast majority of your class is done with-in your groups. Gives great advice, but it only works if you take it :) Willing to meet with you, just set up an appointment on handshake.

Prof. Hollan can be rude and is a harsh grader, he is unforgiving and has very specific deadlines, if you miss or forget to input your hours then too bad, sucks for you. Class is mandatory but you only go like 6 times in the semester, shortest one was 15 mins, so kind of a waste of time. Internship was good overall but probably won't do it again.

Brother Hollan tells you exactly what you have to do to get an A in this class. Show up to class, go to your meetings, and put in your weekly hours. I you do this, you'll get an A. Tons of weekly meetings which is frustrating, and he's an intimidating guy in class. Great class though, definitely recommend to anyone considering a business major!
Great class! Worth it if you are really interested in learning about how businesses work!

He lets you loose and you are able to learn a lot. Though he gives a few assignments such as company feedback that can kill your grade if you do poorly on. Though the grade depends on what the company thinks of you. Which can be a challenge if the company has unrealistic expectations. I learned a lot in the class though.

Professor Hollan was awesome! Just make sure to always do anything you can to come to class because he is very strict about that! And also make sure to fill your timesheet out on time because for some reason he is very strict about that deadline as well and offers no exceptions.

Prof. Holland was super grumpy and rude to students. Boring lectures so I did other homework during them. I had COVID and had to miss class and he wouldn't let me make up the points. Doing an OCI was a waste of time, not near as helpful as actual internships I've done. If you have to do an OCI do all you can to have a different professor for it.

He runs the class well but can be unforgiving. I didn't feel like he understood what our team's capabilities were and how difficult the project was. The project is now being taken over by a professional full-stack developer instead. He expected us to deliver the product that no other team has been able to do because of a similar lack of training.
Class attendance was required but very pointless

I wasn't the biggest fan of Dr. Hollan (when he lectured us it felt like we were being babysat and that he didn't consider we were adults). That being said, I was a huge fan of the on-campus internship! It was a great experience that I'll definitely throw on my resume.
It is all one big group project so you have to be prepared to put in the time. There are only 6 lectures a semester so it is not class heavy. It is a great class.
Really great I would recommend taking an OCI to anyone who wants to get real-life experience or have a real resume

Doing an OCI was something I wanted to do to boost my resume. Your experience in the class really depends on the sponsor you get and how well they work and communicate with your team. The teacher is fine but doesn't really do much but go over what you learn in the online modules. You only have to attend class about 6 times throughout the semester.
OCI is one of my fav on campus, all BYU students should do one! Dr. Hollan is very caring and supportive. REACH OUT to him about anything, he is there to help!
OCI was pretty easy and a fun thing to do. Class had a lot of strange busy work. Prof Hollan did not seem to be very responsive to my needs
He is a really cool guy, as most Entrepreneurial Professors are at BYU, and he gets right to the point of the class, gives good life and career advice, and often ends class early.

This class is not for the faint of heart as it pushes you to do your best every single for both yourself and your team. However, this professor does a great job of helping guide you through the process and making it understandable. Furthermore, he assigns your team a specific TA, which he has helped prepare to make this amazing experience easier.

I loved this class. You get to intern for a sponsor for this class. Professor Hollan gives lecture throughout the semester to help you better know what you can do to help the sponsor. He is super friendly and helps answer any questions you may have. He also has a lot of TAs that can help you whenever you need it. I would recommend this class.
Great experience working with my group in this class and only having 6 lectures was really nice. He is very clear with his expectations, and they are easy to meet if you put in the work.

Professor Hollan's class is one of the best on campus. Having this on-campus internship game me real life experience and helped me find business strengths I didn't know I had. You need to participate and give effort in the project and for your team, but it's one of the most helpful classes for gaining experience. I am taking this class again.
It's not bad if you are desperate for credit and work experience at the same time. Don't expect too much from it though

The internship class I took with Professor Hollan only required 6 days of in-person lectures to allow for more work outside the classroom. The time I did spend with him was really great as he knows his stuff and knows how to help and advise students with these on campus internships.

Participating in an OCI has been a great experience for me! It has been an easy way to gain some professional experience, and I was really able to enhance my resume from this class. As long as you're willing to put in the time, this is a super easy and beneficial class!

If you have ever considered doing an on-campus internship with Dave DO IT! I had such a great experience and could not recommend it more. Great way to vamp up your resume too. You definitely have to put in the work (you are required to do 7.5-9 hrs a week) but that's honestly how you get the hands-on internship experience.
Prof Hollan was a pleasure to have as an instructor. If you are doing an OCI with him. make sure to get your hours in and do your modules and you'll be golden.
Great class for building your resume!
7.5 hours a week minimun outside of class and 2 meetings. Great experience but the most time i spent on any class as hours are tracked and reported with a 7.5 hour minimum
You get out of this class what you put into it! You have to be willing to put in the hours. A really fun class to gain hands on experience.
This class took a lot of time each week, you had to meet with your team 3 times, each week. Class only happens a few times a semester so that is nice. But just be aware that there is a lot required.
Great course with lots of resources.
This class it seems will largely depend on the Sponsor and group you get. There is some busy work outside of what you decide to work on with your group for your Sponsors.

Professor Hollan was nice and understanding. He met with our team when we had some challenges with our sponsor. It feels like the class takes itself a bit too seriously, and the expectation is that you exceed your minimum required hours, which is ridiculous. However, Professor Hollan was great, and I enjoyed this class overall.

While the actual internship was great, the class seemed like a lot of busy work to justify its existence, or to force students who normally wouldn't work into actually doing something. The professor was nice, but the lectures weren't all that useful. Logging time hours and completing evaluations was a waste of time. Let the students roam free!
Hes a great teacher!

I loved this course and would recommend it to anyone! It is the perfect way to get real experience working with incredible companies. Professor Hollan has done a great job with the structure of this class.
The internship is super useful. I loved being able to work with a start up. Not a lot of interaction with Professor Hollan though.
Professor Hollan Was the perfect professor for the OCI Project, he gave us all the information we needed and we knew exactly what had to be done to get a good grade.
Through the lectures, it is evident that Professor Hollan is well-experienced and qualified to teach the MSB 494R class.

It's tough being a teacher for like 100 different internships all at once, but the class is kinda silly. It's just extremely generalized and the work you do is only there so if you have a bad TA or sponsor you can still salvage your grade.
Professor Hollan is a solid choice. If you do the work and submit the assignments, you'll do fine
It was ok its such big class he was not really involved. He is super blunt so don't take it personally

I didn't interact with him too much personally. In class, he's an ok guy but his lectures aren't really that important, you just have to show up for the attendance grade. He's kinda rude over email which I didn't appreciate since I had our company sponsor cc'd on those emails. He's aight I guess.
Its a great opportunity to get real life experience that will prepare you for future internships and jobs. Easy grade, majority of work is done outside of class with your team.

I don't think that Professor Hollan is necessarily a bad professor. I had a good experience with the internship part of the class. There was a lot of busy work and additional things you have to do for the "class portion" of the OCI experience. Not great. Unnecessarily strict with expectations.
Great class, but everything depends on the company you get assigned. Overall, would recommend.
Prof. Hollen is rad, but you don't spend much time in his classroom. The TA's are a bigger part of you instruction.
On campus internships are great. Didn't really interact with the professor much, which was honestly nice. It was a hands off project on his part.
It's going to vary a lot depending on what project you are working on and with what company, but I had an excellent experience. I would highly recommend it!
Great speaker and clearly explains the expectations of his students in his class.

This course was an internship so of course there was lots of assignments but I felt like some of the assignments were just busy work and didn't really apply to the internship. Other than that, it is a fairly easy class if you stay on top of your work.

The work you do for your sponsor is fine, what doesn't make sense about the class is that logging 7.5 hours/week is the thing that matters the most. Class requirements and rubrics for reports and presentations get in the way of us actually working for our sponsor. I had to think more about logging hours and checking off the boxes for the grade.
A great class! Not a lot of in class learningit is great work experience, though. Will require 7.5-9 hours of work per week and hours are graded, so make sure you put in enough hours!

Professor Hollan seems to care a lot about his students and their experience in the course. I never interacted with him directly but he seemed very approachable. This class is no joke, be ready to work and solve some problems. It's a good experience even if it can be a little frustrating at times.
He is a solid choice as a professor for your internship class!
Not really around to help and thinks way to highly of himself.

The online modules are busy work designed to waste your time. The work load on a weekly basis is hard to achieve, especially when your company doesn't give you much to do. Professor is also unwilling to be flexible, we lost points for missing class to attend an event for our internship, which is ironic for a class centered around an internship.

Professor Hollan does a great job teaching the class portion of the OCI. The material he gives is very beneficial and he doesn't give you a lot of assignments. This is nice because you are usually very busy with your internship.
Great class! You get tons of experience and lots of PAR stories. Great lectures that usually end early because there's no busy work for this class. Just really useful stuff for your career.

Great class. I really like Dr. Hollan. He's a super genuine guy who really cares about his students. He gives interesting and very engaging lectures. I learned a lot from the class. Just know that it requires a lot of work and time to get a good grade in the class. You can't really take shortcuts because there aren't any.

Professor Hollan has such a great set up for this class. He keeps the class simple so you can focus on your internship responsibilities but still assigns coursework that is beneficial and helps keep you on track.

This class is great experience for future jobs and prepares you to work with groups at a professional level. What is expected of you is made very clear. The professor and TA's do a great job of helping.

This was for the OCI and professor Hollan provided a great structure to the class. Most of it was up to my team and our Sponsor but professor Hollan did nothing but improve my experience. Nothing in the classwork felt super unnecessary. This was a great class and the most worthwhile class I have ever taken.
Professor Hollan cares about his students and wants them to succeed not only in the class but in the future as well!
Just a lot of busy work when all I wanted was to do was work on my project and focus on my sponsor

Professor Hollan was great. Much of your time for this class is spent in teams working for a sponsor company. Expect to spend 7-9 hours per week working on project. TA's can at times be helpful to help you in your project.

This class was required for a business minor. I had a great internship based on the team I had and the company I got to work for. I think it's based on luck and what you make out of it. The professor is terrible, he doesn't care about his students at all and just lectures what you already learn in Canvas. But the internship was a great experience.

This is a good class, but really all depends on the team you get. If you have a good team and they are willing to work hard you will be fine. The professor wasn't a big part of the experience. Get started on the final report early because it is a lot of work!
great class with awesome hands on experience

This class is an on-campus, unpaid internship. You're put on a team with other classmates for a local company. Graded on class attendance (6 sessions), deliverables (cover letter, presentations, final and midterm reports etc), your timesheet (2 meetings and 7.5-9 hours a week to get an A), and your team and company feedback. oci < paid, better co.

Professor Holland is great. This is a really cool program to help students increase their marketability for the job market. I would highly recommend this class to anyone who needs work experience, especially freshmen or sophomores who haven't interned anywhere yet.

Really enjoyed his class, only thing that bugged me were the assignments/readings you were supposed to do before the semester started so watch out for those. Overall not a hard class to do well in and a good experience.
The difficulty of class depends on what internship project you get. Either way, the class is set up for you to get a good grade no matter what.
The OCI is an awesome experience. The amount of work depends on the project you choose. Prof Hollan was helpful and made an extra effort to help our group. The TAs are a great resource for help.
Great class. What you get out of it really depends on your group, though - so if you can, choose your teammates beforehand.

Professor Hollan gave so many mindless assignments. I felt as if I had to manage all of his assignments as well as what our sponsor needed from us. That being said the workload is not huge but it is definitely there.
This was one of my favorite classes I have ever taken. It gives you real world experience. You get to pick when you and your team have team meetings and how you are going to work through things.
I loved my OCI great experience!

For my OCI, I got to work with 3 teammates where we had to aim to work 7-9 hours weekly (once you get started, getting hours is pretty easy and not as bad as it seems). Class wasn't every single week. When we did have class it was only a max amount of one time a week and class usually lasted 30 minutes tops.
Great guy, just felt like classes were a little slow. Still enjoyed the class.
Honestly he doesn't affect you very much because of the way the class is. He's a nice guy and keeps classes short and to the point. Great class though and good real world experience.

The class itself is a 1 in difficulty as the modules are super easy (the downside is that the modules felt like busy work to me). The overall class difficulty will be more dependent on what your deliverables are from your sponsor. You are required to log 7.5-9 hours of work outside of class otherwise you'll get a major point doc.
The class itself is very easy. Your experience will be more closely tied to the project you end up working on. I had a very positive experience.
He's great, but mostly the experience in the class is all up to you. He gives you general business advice then you go out and get it done in the real world. I loved it.
I really enjoyed this class. It's a great experience and it looks really good on your resume.

This class is touted as being life changing, but that is really up to the project, the sponsor and you. Mine was not what I wanted it to be, but not quite regrettable. Still feel like I had an impact, but also not the best use of my time. It can be really great if you get a good fit, but your say in that is limited.

I liked taking this class from Professor Hollan. It really depends on who you get for your sponsor company and which project you are assigned to, but I had a good experience with this internship class. You have to attend class, but class isn't every week.
You don't really interact with the professor, so the professor is great. However, the TA that we got assigned, made our OCI unpleasant. Overall, easy class and a great learning experience.

494 is an On Campus Internship course that requires 7.5-9 hours of work a week. This work isn't homework that's graded, but it is work assigned to you by your company sponsor (you pick your top choices and get assigned to a company). It's a great way to get resume experience and work on a team. It requires hard work, but doesn't feel like homework.
Great class, loved getting real world experience!

Professor Hollan cares about all the students involved in OCI projects. He and his TAs give you all the help you need to succeed in your projects. Work hard with your teammates, make sure you put in the time and effort, and you will have an incredible semester.
He is a great professor that teaches concepts very clearly and cares that we succeed.
I really liked this internship and the experience that is provided. I felt that I was able to add a lot of valuable skills that I can take with me for future work.

Professor Hollan does a fantastic job of facilitating the group projects that comprise this course. His lectures are pertinent and he does not believe in wasting time. Most of the lectures were only around 20 minutes, and attendance is not even weekly. All grading criteria are clearly established and the TA's for this course are particularly adept.

The course is organized so that it assists the internship and so that most of your time can be devoted to helping your sponsor company. Professor Hollan and his TA's are accessible and offer very specific feedback that can help you and your team meet your goals.
Great class.

This class was great! I learned a lot. This class is a great opportunity for hands on experience. I am not even a business major but really enjoyed this class! The project I worked on helped me realize what I actually wanted to study. It requires time commitment during the week, but if you do your work, you can fulfill the hour requirement.

You honestly do not have a ton of interaction with Professor Hollan for this course. You meet for class only about 6 times and he doesn't waste your time-- he just gets right to the point and then lets you leave. You do have to average 7.5-9 hrs to get an A so the class does require quite a bit of work. The difficulty just depends on the internship

The experience you have in OCI depends on the project you're assigned to. He tells the sponsors not to give too much detail as to what they want out of us so that leaves a lot of ambiguity during the first couple of weeks. There are a lot of assignments not related to the internship that are not helpful and a time-waster more than anything.
Professor Hollan is a good professor, however, a good experience in this class is highly dependent on the sponsor you are assigned.

The class is very much based on the project you get and the teammates you are assigned. If the team is fun and works actively and hard, this class is incredible, worthwhile and fun. On the other hand it has the potential to be a semester long mess.

You definitely have to put in the work for the class because well, it's an internship! Professor Hollan is definitely the guy you want to take the class from though! I had a few friends that took it from different professors and they hated their experience but I loved mine! He is so kind, classes are simple and he truly cares about hit students!

Prof Hollan is a great resource for the OCIs. When my team had struggles, he gave us solid advice in order to navigate meeting the goals of our sponsors. He understands the business world and knows how to teach it.
If you contribute to your project you will pass.

This class is a great option to gain real-life experience by working with a business for an internship. Several hours of work are required every week. You have to average 7.5 hours of internship work every week (unpaid internship). Attendance is required. Participation quiz every class. Only 6 classes during the semester.
useless busywork on top of the internship
Very concise in his lectures. Teaches students to be suitable in the workforce. Intimidating because he is so talented at what he does and know how to get things done effectively.
Really its just outside of class work for the internship - honestly that's what I liked. Only 6 classes a semester and they were extremely straightforward, its just important to show up.

Dave did a good job making sure the class time was not a waste of time. He wouldn't get sidetracked and let you out once the important information was shared. The class is 99% group work and not a lot of "regular hw". Good learning experience, hopefully you get the project you want but if not it'll be a good experience for the resume.
He's the best! This class gives amazing experience and he helps you to enter the "real world."

A lot of the class just depends on who your sponsor is. This is definitely a class I wish was online, and he just posted his lectures online as there are a couple of mandatory classes that don't feel necessary. Not a bad class at all though and the professor is a good guy, just do the work and put in the hours and you will get your desired grade.
He was good but this class is pretty stressful.

You get assigned a company to work with to help with some aspect of their business. We only met for class 7 times total during the semester, but you are expected to spend 7.5 hours a week at least on the class so be prepared for that type of time commitment.

He has high expectations for you and your team with your internship, which is good and bad (depends on the nature of your internship). You only have class a few times a semester, but will require attendance for those few classes.
make sure to get a good sponsor or else it goes downhill

Professor Hollan was a great professor. For this internship, the majority of work is done within your groups and graded by your TAs. However, I liked that Professor Hollan kept his classes short and only used the time to go over the most important parts of the internship that would help his class. Put in the time, and you'll do well overall.

Everyone should take this class with Prof. Hollan. He sets you up to go into the real world with a plethora of skills in your toolbelt. Nothing beats real experience. He's pretty hands-off once you get working with your sponsor, but the TAs are always on hand and are super helpful. Get ready to put in some real work on this, but it's also a blast.
Great professor who shows real interest in the development of the students. Overall, as you complete your time over each week and stay up to date on the coursework, your grade should be fine.
There are only a few classes in a semester.

My OCI was a lot of fun, and I would recommend it for anyone, no matter what major; I am not a business major, and I did not do a business oriented OCI. Professor Hollan was personable and did not waste time. There are only a few class periods, but attending them is mandatory for credit.
He is a great professor and was very clear with expectations.
Pretty average.

Professor Hollan is very passionate about his students. He wants us to have a good experience so that we can have a better future in the work field. He has set expectations and if you don't meet it, you will be letting your team and sponsor down, which is worse than letting your teacher down and getting a bad grade. Great experience!

The internships are great. Once you get going, there is very little interaction with Professor Hollan, considering the classes are large, don't meet very often, and lectures are usually 30 minutes at the longest. I was not professor Hollan's biggest fan, I thought he lacked compassion and care for the students. But he knows what he's talking about.

This class is great especially to gain some real world experience for your resume before applying to business school. Professor Hollan himself can be a bit abrupt but the class itself is well designed despite the busy work from the canvas modules.

Great professor for a great course! You only have to go to class 7-8 times over the course of the semester BUT attendance is MANDATORY for those classes. His lectures rarely run over 35 minutes and he only shares super useful stuff thats relevant to your project or your career. No tests just projects, great resume builder!

The OCI class is really what you put into it. Brother Hollan is no barrier to whatever it is that you seek to achieve through an OCI. Do you want an Easy A? He's not going to police you. If you want to learn professional level skills, Brother Hollan is an exceptional mentor that also has effective TA's to help you along that process.
This internship class was great! It gives you real world experience, for credit! As long as you make the time to find and do useful work, you will have a great experience and get an A!

This class only had a few class days, but they were worth points. I loved my internship and felt like Prof Hollan prepared me for it, but it definitely takes work. You're grade is based on if you spend at least 7.5 hours a week working on this class which can be a lot.
Doesn't waste time in class, but you'll likely talk to his TAs more than him.

This is an on-campus internship project, so a lot of it is done outside class. What I loved is that you can work through Canvas units pretty quickly, and Prof. Hollan keeps the lectures short and to the point. They say they're an hour, but honestly the longest he ever went was like 45 minutes. He gives you all the tools you need to succeed though!

Professor Hollan is awesome! He's super helpful and willing to meet with you to answer any questions you have. The class itself is alright; however, make sure you're keeping up with it. You have to do a lot of work in hours to get a good grade in this class.

Lectures required attendance, and we few in number, but very boring. The material in the online course was mediocre and didn't give you any feedback and sometimes felt like busywork. However, the actual internships granted by this program are awesome! Focus on those.

On Campus Internships are a lot of work. Especially if you have a job and are a full-time student. You need to average 7.5 hours a week so be prepared for that. The experience was phenomenal though and you will get great experience. They do a good job at assigning projects based on your interests.
Class is straightforward. Most of the work is done in your respective internship, the rest is more reflective participation assignments to show what you are getting from the internship.

I highly recommend taking this class! Not only for credit, but also for the experience. While working with a team on an on campus internship you will learn so many things that will help you gain experience and exposure in the real world. Not to mention it's something to beef up your resume!
He did a great job! I was very happy with how the class turned out

Professor Hollan was a great teacher. Honestly, we worked mostly just with our project sponsors and teams, so there wasn't much time spent with him, but the Canvas modules are helpful. Professor Hollan is pretty cut and dry about guidelines.

You don't interact that much with Professor Hollan. You have a few mandatory lectures throughout the semester and some deliverables you have to submit, but he mostly lets you and your team do your own thing. If you take it seriously and work hard, it is a huge career booster.

It's literally an internship but you're graded on your participation. There's important documents and presentations you have to do but it's all based on the company you're working for and you never present to the class. There's only like 7 classes the whole semester and he just gives you tips on how to do good. Grading criteria is super clear!

For an OCI, honestly, the professor doesn't matter too much because you don't really work with them. The only time you do is when you go to a few lectures during the course. Dave Hollan was nice, encouraged us to hold ourselves to a high standard when working with our sponsors, and the grading was clear. Do the (easy) work, and you'll get an A!

David Hollan was awesome. You don't really interact with him because your main focus is on the internship. But in class, he tells you what is expected and just wants you to get it done. He doesn't take any crap. Overall had a good experience with him.

Due to the nature of this course (on-campus internship), I didn't get to know Professor Hollan very well. Much of the work is with your group and project sponsor, and there are only 6 class lectures. Overall, easy to get an A but what you put into it is what you get out of it!
Contact with this professor was very short and sometimes rude.

I would highly recommend doing an on-campus internship to any pre-business student. I was very pleasantly surprised by the amount of things that I learned and it was a great opportunity to apply some things I've learned in other classes and develop new skills. You're required to do at least 7.5 hours a week, but if you can make it work, do it.

Professor Hollan administers the OCI program. He is good but seems to be a little too serious about everything. That being said he is trying to prepare us for the business world. Only 4 classes all year the rest is working on your OCI
OCI's are great but they take up a lot of time. You should expect to actually devote 8+ hours a week to your project and the class.
This is a phenomenal course! The class itself is incredibly easy, it's all about the time you spend working on your deliverables with your team. Would recommend to all for real work experience.

Prof Hollan is OK. The vast majority of your time in the class will not include him. You spend the most time working for your OCI sponsor. Your sponsor has the most influence on your experience. Be careful with startups. Things change rapidly and the project you end up doing might be completely different from the one described on the OCI dashboard.
Not respectful to students questions.

Professor Hollan is clear about his expectations and will help you make the most of your internship. Your experience varies a lot based on the project you are assigned to, but either way the grade will remain the same as long as you report your hours and work hard.

This class is totally project-based as it's an internship for class credit. It is super fun and a great opportunity to get professional experience in a class environment that guides you through each step of the process.
I liked the course and the TA's were really great.

It was hard to tell because our class had hundreds of participants over Zoom, but I was always bored during the lectures. He seemed bored and annoyed as he talked, as if he just wanted to be done. I had the chance to talk with him one on one, though and he was nice and understanding then.
Fun class and great teacher!!

Most of the work will be done outside of class, with the class being more like advisory time. However, the required papers at the end are more than was expected at the beginning, but even if you procrastinate, it isn't a difficult class.
Awesome internship courses!

Professor Holland is awesome! On campus internship can be good or bad, depends on the company that you are assigned to. Whatever the internship might be, it is always helpful to have a conversation with Professor Holland since you'll be inspired a lot.

The OCI is pretty cool to get real experience working with companies. The class side though is so annoying. They have a bunch of reflection assignments and meticulous rubrics for reports that really aren't that important to your sponsor. A lot of the grading depends on how hard your TA is.

Class mostly depends on who you get as a sponsor company. Ours was kind of a mess, they didn't know what they wanted half the time which made it hard to know how to help. No matter what you are expected to put at least 7.5 hours.

This class gave me real world experience. Doing this internship was tricky at times but the professor and especially the TA's always answered my questions. Professor Hollen made an effort to attend or watch the recorded version of our final reports even though he wasn't the one grading them. I think that says a lot about a teacher.
Great semester class for real work experience
He is great but most of his lectures aren't super necessary. I would zone out quite a bit because it was just him griping about things slackers do.

You work with your intern team the whole semester and have class once a week, but not every week. This class pretty much depends on what intern you are teamed up with and that can make or break your experience.
Great teacher. wants to help in any way possible.
This class is mainly between your team and sponsor. Prof. Hollan isn't heavily involved.

You should go to class. Professor Hollan really just wants to help everyone enjoy this internship experience. It's not too difficult, and you get class credit as well as resume building experiences!! I would take another OCI!
He does a great job as our instructor for this internship class, he taught us many things to help us be effective during our projects and with our companies
It was a great way to have an Internship and still get BYU credit for the hours and work put into it.
The class was very well organized on canvas. From the beginning I understood what was expected of me. No tests or quizzes.

This class was a great experience for me. It definitely requires your time and effort because you are required to spend 7.5-9hrs each week. (you report this in a time sheet on canvas) It was super fun to work with an actual company and perform valuable work throughout the semester.

This class was very helpful to get real world experience. I would definitely recommend taking it, but the teacher isn't a huge factor. Everything depends on your group and your company. If your company or group isn't motivated or doesn't help, you will get a bad grade. The teacher just lectures maybe 5 times a semester. Get ready for a lot of work!

There's only a couple class periods, but they are mandatory. The homework each week isn't bad. You don't really get to know professor hollan be he is a great guy and you can tell how much he values this class/experience. He always reminds you how awesome it is to be able to participate in this OCI.

Doing an On-Campus Internship is an incredible experience. It is a great way to get access to organizations that you may not be able to otherwise. Professor Hollan makes sure to give you all the tools you need to be successful and is available to ask questions. As long as you put in the hours for the internship you'll get an A. Highly recommend.
Loved the class. Heavily depends on the company you're assigned to, but professor Hollan gives great professional advice.
Everything is about your group that you get and what company you're working for. Professor didn't do much imo
I loved the class and got real world experience!

This is one of the most valuable classes I have taken at BYU! It should be required for all students that do not already have internships lined up. The class is almost entirely real-life experience in your assigned internship which is great. Definitely recommend!!!
Great way to gain experience. Highly recommend.

Professor Hollan was a great instructor for this internship class! He really let us loose to figure everything out on our own, but was always willing to help us if we ran into problems. You are required to spend 7.5-9 hours per week on this class, and your average hours is the majority of your grade. It is a great way to get experience plus credit.
Professor Hollan is very knowledgeable in the business field and he is able to provide sufficient help for you to be successful in your project.
He doesn't teach much because this is an internship but the class is well structured and he make's sure you stay on course.

This is a great class! Looks great on your resume and gives real-world experience. It is very time-consuming but not in the same way as a regular class. The time is spent working on projects and attending meetings rather than studying textbooks. Also, my team and I became great friends!

My experience with my on campus internship was tough. I'm glad that I had the opportunity to go through my first internship with BYU's resources. You will have to deal with a lot of ambiguity, which can be frustrating, but you will gain great skills. Professor Hollan wasn't my favorite, but he trains amazing TA's.
Professor Holland is good, but sometimes goes through the motions. If he likes you, then he's there for you.
This class was fun and I learned a lot, but be prepared, you are expected to do 7-8 hours of work per week outside of class.
The OCI is a great opportunity, take advantage of it! You will have something to put on your resume and you will have business experience to refer back to.
Attendance isn't always mandatory, but the stuff you get from each class is really helpful.
Awesome class. Easy A if you participate with the team.

Professor Hollan was great! The class is more focused on your group and sponsor and the experience really depends on your project and group, but he was always there if we had questions or to help us complete certain tasks. 100% would take again!

The OCI itself is a great opportunity. They will give you the bottom rung of the ladder if you just sign up. From there you climb- building your resume and whatnot. There's only 5 classes all semester, and honestly I didn't pay attention because they didn't seem very important to the work I was doing for my sponsor.

This class was good and gave me a lot of real life experience, however it is a lot of work and requires you to be extremely self driven. The prof is good but since you are mostly working on your own project I did not really interact with him at all. Overall good experience and I would recommend it if you are looking for a resume booster.

This class is obviously an internship coupled with some mandatory class meetings. Class meetings are just a time for Professor Hollan to give us reminders, updates, teach a few basic principles and do a Q&A session. Class is super chill and you have fewer class periods than most courses-- just be sure to show up when attendance is mandatory.
As long as you submit your weekly hours and complete the assigned deliverables your team comes up with, you will get an A!
He's there to help you if you need help but you most definitely won't need help.
Good professor. Very little interaction with him. Only 6 classes to attend. As long as you average 7.5 hours a week and the sponsor rates you well, you will get an A.

This was a great class to get real-world experience! You only meet a few times in the semester. Most of the time is spent with your team and sponsor. If you have a good sponsor and team, then it will be a 10/10 experience. Each project is different, so the difficulty really depends on the project.

I would recommend this class to anyone looking for some easy resume building content. There are so many internships to choose from and Professor Hollan works with each student to make sure they are in an internship they will enjoy. My TA was super awesome and helped clarify assignments. This class requires 7.5-9 hours per week of work.

You don't communicate directly with Professor Hollan a lot just because of the nature of the class. You work mostly with your team and sponsor to complete your project. However, throughout the semester, you have required zoom meetings with David that are mandatory where he makes sure you are up to speed with where you should be. Amazing experience!

This class was great but did require up to 8 hours of work a week in order to fulfill time requirements. The classes were only every other week or so and were mandatory but short and sweet. David Hollan is a good teacher.

I had high hopes for this internship but it was a big disappointment. Tons of busy work that did not have a lot of value. I reached out to Professor Hollan before the semester started and I was surprised and how standoffish he was.

Professor Hollan was great! Since this specific class is an internship class, I didn't see much of him, but he organized the class in a way that made success possible. The only thing that was hard for me was trying to get the 7.5 hours in each week. My specific project didn't necessarily need 7.5 hours from each of us.
good teach
Great professor. He cares for students and wants them to succeed. He offers a lot of materials and insights to help students. He also makes it so that TAs are easily accessible and there to help out.

PRofessor Hollan is a great teacher for taking an on campus intership in the way that he does not require a lot of assignments for the class specifically. The real work is for the company that you are doing the internship for so it is more motivation to work hard for them. If you do the work, it is an easy A, but you gain so much more in experience

Kind of an intimidating guy, but knows his stuff. He is very specific about how to do everything in the class, it's very professional. You'll understand all your expectations very clearly from the start.

I loved my internship and my team! Prof. Hollan is a great teacher and was very understanding when I was sick and missed class for awhile. He is very fair, and knows what he is talking about. The only strict thing is hours. You cannot forget to log your hours because he won't take them late. No exceptions. You reap what you sow in this class.

The Professor did not seem to care about me as a student. Felt a little disrespected in a personal scenario. It was not a hard class and I recommend the class, but be careful of little details with him. Learned a lot and still got a good grade; just felt like the professor was not caring of his students.
Professor Hollan was there to help if we needed him, and the OCI course didn't require much time in class, which was nice.

This is an on-campus internship class, so be prepared to work in a real internship! It gives great experience for your resume/application for programs and everyone is able to take it. It does require 7.5-9 hours per week, but it's worth it.

It's basically an internship with grades. Hollan isn't super involved, except for 6 20-30 min online classes throughout the semester. He has a no-leniency policy on your hours (which is a big part of your grade); if you forget to submit them you are screwed.

This class was a great way to get experience for outside of school without having to sacrifice tons of time for an official internship. Although it required time each week and lots of teamwork, it was one of the best classes I've ever taken and taught me so many useful skills. 10/10

The OCI program is an incredible way to gain experience as an undergrad. With that being said, you are pretty much on your own for the semester. David Hollan is clearly experienced, but seems more concerned with upholding the reputation of the program than supporting students. Get ready for ambiguity, log your hours, & always go to class.
The class is exactly what it sounds like and he is an average professor. Not amazing but not terrible either.
The project was too hard for students
Taking an OCI class is great experience. Glad I did this class!

This class is an Internship for a company, so you are expected to do a lot of work for them. The class is very well organized and walks you through it. Best way to do your first internship. Lots of mandatory team meetings and work to do but it's worth it for the internship experience and real-world application.

Professor Hollan was not my favorite personnnnn, but a good teacher. Only had to go to a handful of classes, they were kind of unnecessary but the class is an easy A so I didnt care. He is very passionate about what he does, but do not slack off or try to get a pass for late work/forgetfulness or else he will roast and toast you and have no mercy.

Professor Hollan is not really the person you will be interacting with in this class. This class will be a lot of work, but it is extremely rewarding to have your work mean something. I would highly recommend, it is a great experience to get exposure to the work force. It is more work than I expected though.

I was scared to do an internship so that's why I took this. Super beneficial to get real life experience. The professor is intense but you really only go to like 5 mandatory classes and all other work is done with your teammates and sponsor. Its as hard as you make it but required to log in 7.5 hours of work a week.
Not too hard of a class (OCI) just stay on top of your hours and meetings.
Good guy. We don't work with him personally much in the class, but I loved my internship. It was a great experience

- 6 class meetings throughout the semester. - You only really interact with the TA assigned to your group. - The unnecessary class assignments stole time that could have been used on the actual project. The class interfered with the project itself. - The project I had was amazing. Learned a lot, gained great experience. - Highly recommend!
Great experience doing an on campus internship. I highly recommend!
The OCI experience is based more on the OCI itself than on the professor.

As an on campus internship we dealt more with our TA and project sponsor than Professor Hollan. The course has a lot of incredibly tedious requirements so if this is your first internship experience then this course is a good opportunity to get familiar with internships. If you already have experience don't take this class.
This class requires a ton of work each week outside of class, but if you do everything and go to team meetings and the required lectures then you will get an A.

Overall the class is great. The ability to get an internship through BYU opens up a lot of opportunities to get experience and learn. The class does feel like it has a lot of red tape that is unnecessary. The professor himself has a bit of a "if you're having a problem, it's your problem" type of attitude and is not the most accommodating.
This class was awesome! I learned a lot of things through my OCI and Professor Hollan and the TAs were always available if my group needed help! Definitely recommend.

This class is a great way to gain professional experience in your desired industry and profession. I have taken it twice because I enjoyed it so much the first time. You have a decent say in what project you are put in, which is nice. The class isn't so much about the grade (It's very easy to get an A) as it is about gaining experience.
This class is a great way to get experience with a real company in a real internship. I would highly recommend it.

You only meet with him a few times during the semester but he's available to help out when your group needs it. He definitely gets right to what's important and doesn't mess around. Great professional minded teacher for the course!

Honestly, it's such a big class you won't be working closely with Professor Hollan. You work more with your group and your TA. My TA was great and I'm sure all of them are. It all depends on your team and sponsors, to be honest. I got a great team and a fun project and great sponsors!

You only meet 6 times in the semester with Professor Hollan. I didn't love his teaching style. He didn't seem very lenient with students, but tells you what you need to know. For the bulk of class you mainly just communicate with your TA and your project sponsor so the bulk if the class is mainly your actual internship work.
Nice guy and a mellow class. You get what you put into it.
Well-organized course with helpful teaching assistants.
My TA helped a lot more than the professor. In this class you dont really need a professor though, just guidance every now and then. I would take the class again though! It wasn't bad at all!
This teacher provides opportunities for the development of real-world skills. Is considerate and provides support through TAs, course material etc. throughout the course.

The internships are nothing like what you signed up for. I signed up to get finance experience and became the entire marketing department for a company that had no marketing. The class is 1 big group project which would be fine depending on who you end up with, but if you get put in a group of students who never respond or help out then it'll suck.

How this class goes really depends on what you put into it and how much you care. If you want an easy A, you can get it. If you want a good grade and learn things that can help you in the future in your professional career, it is up to you to make that happen.

Professor Holland moderates the OCI experience, but he honestly isn't involved much. We had like 6 classes during the semester. He is very dry and appears to be unapproachable, but you don't see him much, so it's fine. He should not affect whether you do an OCI or not.
This was a great class to gain real experience and Professor Hollan provides great resources for learning.

The class will change your life. It's likely you won't have much interaction with Professor Hollan due to the nature of an On-Campus Internship, but the way the class is designed will give you the kind of experience you're looking for to boost your resume beyond academics.
Great professor, the content of this class is very light. You just need to be prepared to put in 7.5-9 hours a week for your company project. Other than that super chill, great class!
It was a great class that exposes you to a lot of great opportunities. Just make sure you have the time to do it each week.

Professor Holland knows what he's talking about when it comes to the business world. HOWEVER, he himself is super rude to students and TA's in class- I would HATE to work with this guy. I didn't enjoy the course itself (I hate group work) but it did give me experience and something to add to my resume if that's something you're looking for.

Professor Hollan is a solid professor but honestly your OCI experience will depend more on your sponsor and the specific project you're assigned, so I feel which professor you have doesn't matter as much, at least in my opinion.

Hollan is great. Make sure you would like the OCI you sign up for and look up OCIs early as they get sparse. Remember that there's a difference between stretching yourself and doing something you don't enjoy. This can be a great opportunity. Use it!

An OCI experience can be found nowhere else. I love the real world experience, but the professor didn't feel as super helpful, it felt more like reading off of slides in the lectures. I would like a little more real world application in the actual classes.
It requires a lot of work put in each week but it is a fun internship!

This class depends on which group you get assigned to, put preference on the ones you are actually interested in. The modules are easy to complete but they seem pretty pointless, I normally just skipped through them. I recommend this class cause you can put it on your resume.
There was not a lot of one on one time with the professor, but he does a great job at providing enough resources to be succesful.
Professor Hollan goes through exactly what you need to do and sends out plenty of emails to help you know the due dates of upcoming assignments.
The class itself wasn't bad. It honestly is more important who your sponsor (company that you work for) is instead of the professor.

I highly recommend an OCI. The most difficult part of doing one is that you are supposed to spend 7.5-9 hours a week on your project. However, if you get 100% on all the assignments, you only need an average of 6 hours per week.

Dave wants to help us all succeed in the OCI program. He provides a lot of resources and makes sure to let us know that he's there to help. I appreciated how he included the gospel in his lectures. Make sure to do the weekly Canvas modules in addition to working with your team/company sponsor and you'll do fine.

Prof Holland is a nice guy. I've done 2 OCIs and the course content didn't change at all. OCIs are a beast. Really depends on how competent your sponsor is and how much work they give you. Workload is insane at the end of the semester because you have a final report to submit and final presentation to give.
Overall a great course with great experience.
Professor is great, very helpful and informative

We don't have much contact with him because so much of our work is done directly with the company sponsor. But he is great at making sure everyone is on the right track. Everyone should take this class!

Professor Hollan was a great teacher and mentor. I didn't have the opportunity to speak with him since the TAs are the ones you mostly talked to, but his lectures were always helpful when my team and I had to make decisions.

The OCI program is structured in a way where the grade takes a back seat to the experience you can gain from your project. Prof Hollan understands this; essentially, you don't have to worry about what grade you're going to get if you are engaged with your project.
Just do the work as demonstrated in class and syllabus and you should be fine.,
Great learning experience and looks good to gain real world experience on your resume.
Good professor! A little intimidating at times, but cares for his students. Would recommend
Great guide for completing a good OCI. Gives good resources and helps guide you throughout the internship. The class itself is awesome if you are in need of resume boosters.
He was excellent at providing us with the necessary info to succeed. He also was good at delegating responsibilities to his TA's to insure everyone had the help that they needed.
This was a great course to receive real-world experience. If you are looking for a way to learn new skills, make new connections, and make solid additions to your resume, this is the class!
The class was great. I liked my project and group. When we actually had to meet as a class, the classes were short and helpful.

I loved the experience of an OCI. The class itself, however, was poorly structured. The assignments you have to do in order to receive credit often do not correlate with the work you have to do for the company. Professor Hollan was also hard to work with. He always seemed kind of grumpy and often didn't seem happy to answer student's questions.
Great experiential learning class
Great class. Depends on what project you get though.
Professor Hollan is willing to help you in whatever help you need. This class really need effort.

The modules do feel like busy work at some points but it is pretty easy at that. For me, it never really got in the way. Classes felt redundant but were also pretty lax. Our TA graded us very lightly so overall was a pretty easy A, but good way to beef up the resume.

This is an on campus internship and due to that fact you don't interact with the professor a lot. However, the few times I have it has not been super positive. He is not very helpful with individual emails. If you have a good TA than you should be okay. However, it was definitely worth it to have the internship and gain experience!
Easy but requires a lot of time

Doing an OCI is such a great experience! The class is focused mainly on your internship project but there is occasionally a lecture held. The modules are supposed to help you as you go through your project. In the end I felt like it was a good and professional opportunity.
It is a project based class. Do your work, and you'll be fine. He is a great teacher and I would certainly take him again.

The professor is almost none of this class. I think we had class for about 4 hours total over the course of the semester. The professor is a great guy and the class is good to take, but don't worry about the professor when evaluating whether or not this class is for you.

He is a very serious instructor but as much of the class interacted with people in the business world, that seriousness showed what was expected from the students from potential employers. Some think he is strict, but he is a fair professor as he constantly tells students what is expected and it is up to them to comply. Overall, a great instructor.
It was hard to gage difficulty in this class because the professor made it seem like everything was way harder than it actually was almost trying to scare us in thinking it was too hard

I have taken this class twice and highly recommend it. Prof Hollan organizes this class very well and gives you lots of resources to succeed and gain professional experience. I did find that sometimes the class work doesn't pertain to the project, but it's easy. Put in the work and time, and it's an easy 3 credits and an amazing experience!
Fine class. Better for Freshman but it was fine.

This class will benefit you! Even though you're not able to pick which business you'll be working for, you will undoubtedly learn hard and soft skills that will benefit you whether you work for someone or start your own business. You complete fairly brief modules for class, while the majority of work is done with your sponsor's business and team.
Prof Hollan is great, really OCIs are more about your sponsor than what he does tho. I've done two OCIs and had a great time with both thanks to Prof Hollan structuring the class really well.
Great internship opportunities through this class. Professor isn't super involved as you are mainly working with a company sponsor. Keep on top of your hours and you will do great!
I feel like I would have had a better experience if I was part of a different internship team. I still was able to learn a lot.
Not much time is spent with him. There is only about 5 classes for the semester required to attend.

You only actually have to go to a few lectures throughout the semester which is nice. But its annoying that you have to meet certain time requirements for each week. I wish that if I just finished my work quickly and in good quality that was enough. But it is defiantly a great learning experience!
A lot of this class depends on the company that you get put with.

Bro. Hollan is a great guy, but beware. If you don't know exactly the type of internship experience you are looking for, you may end up with a project you're not passionate about at all and logging those 7.5 hours per week will be SO hard. So DO NOT be lax when selecting your project preferences. This class can provide good professional experience.
Professor Hollan is very helpful when students ask and wants you to be successful in the class.
He's very professional but often comes across as impatient and not willing to help students.
It was such an easy class. Just get your hours in weekly and show up to class.

You have to show up to class to take the attendance quiz, but aside from that, I didn't feel like the class period was really necessary. The on-campus internships are a great opportunity for resume building. Depending on your sponsor your experience might be entirely different, but I really enjoyed the work I did with my team.

I highly recommend doing an OCI. However, your sponsor will greatly impact whether or not you will have a good experience so choose wisely. Also, you will spend a lot of time on your project so make sure you are doing something you are actually interested in. This class takes a lot of time and you will need an average of 7.50 hours to get an A.

This class is very helpful to gain real-world experience while also receiving credit it for it. It does require a good amount of work, but it is all hands-on learning and is very applicable to anything you do in the business world.
Allowed me to gain great real world experience and get credit!
the difficulty of this class all depends on who you get as the company you intern for.

The class definitely requires a ton of work each week. I felt that the amount of time that was required for the class was above what most classes would have expected. The internships are great though and provide a lot of valuable experience.
This instructor clearly explains the expectations. If you follow them you will do well, but there is no sympathy for late work.

Solid professor, never assigned anything too difficult. This was a project-based class where we collaborated more with certain companies, so I never had to do much more than show up to class and work on the project. Easy A and good experience as long as you meet the hours requirement.
Great class! It is great for experience and helps you to gain a lot of skills that you would not normally in a regular classroom setting. Highly recommend that everyone do an OCI!

Honestly the internship is great but I did not like the class part at all, all of the assignments seemed pointless and it really ruined my experience with the internship. Forcing students to work 7.5 hours a week is really not needed and causes students to waste a lot of time doing pointless things just to rack up hours. Not worth it.

This class has six lectures in total, but if you do not attend you will lose credit. It is mainly working with a company, and you must put in more than 7.5 hours each week which sometimes could be difficult to do. There are a lot of rules, so study through the syllabus and make sure you are clear with every expectations.

Professor Hollan is a great guy who wants students to actually care about their work instead of doing the bare minimum required to get an A. That said, much of the coursework is busywork that doesn't inspire the student to do more. OCI's, however, do a great job of motivating students to work and be proactive.

I liked this professor- he was not overall involved in our projects, but his lectures (which were not every week) were helpful and efficient. He did not waste time and the things he taught were very applicable to real life.

I got a good project to work on which made this class enjoyable and valuable. My only complaint is that it is still too academically focused. We had to do a midterm and final report in a specified format and that only wasted our time. Those reports weren't useful to our sponsor either. But we had to do them for the A.

Work with a team and get real world experience! Attendance is required but there are very few classes. Super fun and worked with a great team. Class modules almost every week were helpful and easy. Do you work and put your hours in and youll be fine!

OCI's require lots of hard work and dedication. Professor Hollan makes it his goal to inspire you and push you to success. He expects the best from you, because in your work as an intern, you represent BYU. You have to do the work and put in a bunch of hours, but it is worth it. He gives lots of resources, and the TAs are incredibly helpful, too.

Great experience to work with a team. I was lucky to have a fun, yet hard-working team. Learned a lot about my field and gave me something to talk about in job interviews. Opened the door to paid summer internship opportunities despite me being an underclassman. Work hard, be a good teammate, and you'll leave with a good grade and work experience.

He's harsh but experienced. The actual coursework of the class doesn't feel very helpful or fulfilling at all, what matters most is the work you do with your teammates directed towards your sponsor's specific needs. Come into the course ready to make it a priority among your courses. Don't sign up thinking you'll get an easy item for your resume.

The lectures greatly supplemented my experience with the on-campus internship. I felt more prepared through the lectures to provide good insight at team meetings. Overall, this class makes me feel more prepared to apply to business school because it's hands-on experience. It is what you make of it.

Your experience really depends on your sponsor, so make sure to choose wisely at the beginning. It is not that hard to get an A if you are willing to put in the work, it was great for real-life experience!

The level of difficulty for this class is based on your project. My class was super easy and chill, but I still learned a lot. Others were more time-consuming and took up to 9 hours a week. The class part is just once a week and isn't that difficult. Overall really enjoyed the class.

Prof Hollan is a good teacher. The nature of the class is such that you don't interact with him much but he gives plenty of tools for you to succeed in your On Campus Internships. There are only 6 lectures during the semester and attendance is required. Other than that, you just need to meeting with your team regularly.

I thought this was a great class to get some more experience on your resume! Professor Hollan wants to see you succeed and represent BYU well and he will give you all of the resources you need to do so. I really enjoyed this class and all of the opportunities it gave me.

You will spend most of time with your team and sponsor throughout the semester and at least work 7.5 hours per week on your project. We only met Professor Hollan 6 times and his class was just a navigation to upcoming assignments. Get working with your partners and complete assignments on time (weekly module, midterm and final presentation).

I took this class during Covid so I didn't really have any opportunities to interact much with the teacher. The class/internship instructions for class are pretty vague which makes class assignments pretty difficult. The TAs are your best friend.
