Professor Hollan is a great professor. His lectures are very intelligible and helpful even in the real world. There were occasions that some of the team assignments were docked off points without explanations, but other than that, this class was amazing.

This was a really useful class. You really get a chance to learn more about business (or whatever internship you do), and I would definetely reccomend it for experience. Professor Hollan is good, although it's more important what YOU do than what he does for this class. There's only a few mandatory classes throughout the semester.

It was a really great class and Professor Holland has set it up in a way so that students can be successful. If you do the work, you will get a good grade and more importantly, you will get to add things to your resume. Great experience with really great people!

Overall a great project! Gain real-world experience by working for a company. Great Canvas resources to help you learn business principles. If you turn everything in on time and spend at least 7.5 hours per week on your project, you'll get an A.

I highly recommend the class. It is a lot of hands-on, real-life experience. The course is based on the hours that you put into it so expect to spend about 7.5-9 hours a week of good work on your projects. It's one of those classes that the more you put into it the more you get out of it. The teacher is good but you don't interact much with him.

I enjoyed my internship a ton and I would consider doing another one. Professor Hollan doesn't really get to know you personally but he gives helpful advice and resources during class and he keeps things short and to the point which is nice.
He was a great teacher. The lectures were a little boring though. It is a very easy class to get an A and to learn how to work with a team.

What you put in is what you'll get out. The group and sponsor do make a huge difference though. If you're looking to do the bare minimum you can just put in the 7 1/2 hours a week and get an A but it'll probably help your resume if you actually try.

You only meet as an entire class a few times throughout the semester so interaction with Professor Hollan is limited. He's a decent professor, but the class is set up for the group project and work associated with it to be the main sources of learning. If you want a good experience, try to get in a project that has to do with your preferred career.

As an internship course, you need to put the work in and you will see results. It is a large class though so your Ta's will be more accessible than Professor Hollan but if you schedule office hours with him he is very helpful, as well as a little blunt. Stay on top of your hours and communicate and you'll be fine

You must put in 7.5 to 9 hours of work each week in order to earn an A. Very simple assignments for the class, but there is a lot of work to be done for the internship. Only 6 class periods throughout the semester, but these are mandatory.

This is an awesome class! It is different than a normal class because it is technically an internship. You have to dedicate a lot of time each week (7.5-9 hours), but you really learn so much! It isn't hard to get a good grade if you do the necessary work.
This class is one of the best you will ever take!! It gives you real world experience, while still giving you guidance. Rather than jumping into the deep end, they give you help all along the way.

Professor Hollan does not give a ton of information regarding your specific deliverables. You find out exactly what to do from your sponsor. I would advise to be very communicative with your sponsor and make sure you are both on the same page throughout the project. Modules were fairly easy to complete, feels like busy work sometime though.

This class expects 7.5-9 hours of week towards a given project. With that in mind, this class is a great resume builder, and can help students find their strengths in a professional team setting. I loved this class!

He is a great professor! He has 6 classes to attend throughout the course with a participation quiz at the end. His instructions as to what you should be doing with your group for your internship are very clear. Overall, I loved this class!

Holland is pretty uninvolved in your OCI. It is entirely up to you to complete your tasks, meet with your team, and reach out for help. This is a great learning experience and opportunity. But do not underestimate the amount of work and time this will take.

The internship was good. There were a lot of assignments for the class itself that kind of detracted from our actual internship. You are required to work 7.5-9 hours a week on the internship for full credit. You need to collaborate with your team and be unified or else it will be difficult.

So I guess by "Homework" I really mean that you need to do work. You have to do a minimum of 7.5 hours weekly for this class. You only have to go to class like 5 times during the semester. This is a real internship that you work hand and hand with the company working to help solve their problems. It was a very useful class to get life experience.
He was willing to help but also really clear on what the expectations were.

Hollan is pretty much hands off with MSB494R except for the few classes you need to meet with him in. That's to be expected since this is an internship. However, he expects you to give this internship first priority and to be willing to take crap from mediocre company sponsors. He's not very understanding when it comes to special circumstances.
Simple class. Takes lot of time though.

You will be in a group all semester, where you will essentially be an intern for another company. You will meet 3 times a week. If you choose to work hard, you will get networking, job opportunities, and experience. If you do not work hard you will get one of the easiest A's of your college career. It is a win-win. Take this class.
Take an oci for some unpaid internship experience!

Professor Hollan is not my favorite professor - he is not very understanding of situations or life events. He expects that this is a top priority. THE GOOD THING about this course is that it is an internship for school credit. So it makes sense because he is trying to prep you for the professional world. He provides what you will need to do well!

The class itself is pretty awesome and fun if you get a good sponsor and company, overall there isn't much interaction with the teacher, we only had class every other week. He's a decent professor, nothing amazing though. Be prepared you will get tons of emails from this class. Everything you do is with your group, so be prepared for that.

This class is awesome! Prof Hollan is a great teacher. It is a really big class so if you want one on one with him you need to take time outside of class. You basically get a team and a company to do a project for. In order to be successful be ready to put 7-9 hours a week of work a week. Great class if youre looking for professional experience.
Professor Hollan is the man for the job, and I think this course is so helpful for anyone looking for experience in their field of study (though, business-oriented).
Make sure you do the deliverables on time.
Great class to take depending on the project you get. Professor is hand-off and lets students run with their projects.

You have to put in a lot of time, but it is a good experience, and would recommend it for sure. My biggest advice is to make sure that you report your hours as they come, make sure you get them in, he doesn't have any leniency on reporting hours after the week. But other than that, good class, great professor

Professor Hollan is great professor and I would highly recommend. I took his OCI class and his direction were really straight forward and easy to understand. It is important to attend the lectures because he gives important details.

If you're going to take this class, just realize that you're expected to put in 7.5 to 9 hours a week to get an A. It's a ton of time, and honestly you kind of just have to make up work sometimes to meet the time requirement.

I had heard from a couple of different people that their internship really wasn't too difficult. My group worked with a very new and small NGO, so our experience was totally different. Spent 9+ hours a week on this dang internship. Reallllllly do your research before committing to an internship and make sure it is the experience you want!

The course is good real-world experience to put on your resume. However, the weekly workload requirements make this class very work-intensive, and it has been very tiring for me to do multiple Zoom group meetings each week (we couldn't meet in person due to Covid).
Very Time Consuming class, but easy if you put in the work. Professor Hollan is a great guy and wants his students to succeed, but you spend more time with your team and sponsor than the professor.

Expect the course itself to be very time-consuming (in order to get an A in the class you have to dedicate 7.5-9 hours a week). Director Hollan himself is rather stern and can seem scary but you have to be aware that is to create a "professional" environment. He has high expectations for BYU students and he expects you to prioritize this course.

The class structure is really great. You only meet for class a handful of times through the semester, the majority of time is spent working on your internship with your team. You are required to meet with your team at least twice a week and with your internship Sponsor at least bi-weekly.
This class is project based, but a great opportunity. Professor Hollan does a great job at providing the materials needed and helping the students be successful.
I loved my internship but honestly I felt like the class portion of the OCI was just busy work and not very helpful.
Mostly just a bunch of busy work. The main focus is on the company you are working for. Be a good team player and you'll have a good experience.

On-Campus Internship is an unpassable opportunity for any student, no matter the major. My only words of warning would be to research which project you really want to do. Some projects are significantly better than others.
A fun great experience

Professor Hollan is great. I never needed to speak to him individually, but I would feel comfortable speaking to him if I had a question or concern. His class is beneficial because it provides real-world experience for students.
Great class. You will get out what you put in. Fairly easy to get an A if you stay on top of the assignments and get your hours in each week.
Prof. Hollan provides many useful resources apart from his modules. The modules help students regardless of their background to succeed and provide meaningful contributions to their groups.
Great class. Takes a lot of time but it is worth the experiential learning that you gain.
Allows you to determine the fate of the course. Was very hands off unless you confront him for advice.
Great guy - always tries to work the gospel into class meetings
I was in the MSB 494R class which is On-Campus Internships and 100% recommend it. It is a lot of work but I gained so much experience!

I think Professor Hollan is passionate, but he's also pretty harsh. I think he wants to push us in our OCIs, but it almost seems like he thinks we don't have any other classes (or that they don't matter) and that if we aren't doing well in this class, we are failing in life. I'm glad I did my OCI, but I can't say I really enjoyed the class part.
I loved Prof Hollan. The class Zoom meetings are required/mandatory but you don't have meetings every week and Prof Hollan keeps the meetings short and to the point which is extremely appreciated!
Mandatory attendance and timed attendance quiz

Brother Hollan is a great professor. He cares about his students and their success in each OCI. There's only about 6 times you will meet with Brother Hollan for lectures. The lectures are set to last 50 minutes but they usually only go 20-30 minutes. He has his TA's keep track of questions and is good at answering any and all of them.
He was a good professor. The class itself is really easy to get an A in, but the projects you work on can be very ambiguous. He gives you plenty of guidance on how to succeed in the course.

This class is a great way to gain professional experience while working as a non-paid intern for a company. Professor Hollan has a ton of experience under his belt and provides everyone with an equal opportunity to get whatever grade you would like, as well as which company you would enjoy. Classes workload overall is dependent on the company.
You work a lot as a team, the assignments are easy, its the mid-term and final reports that take the longest time. Really good class for getting internship experience.
A solid choice for an OCI professor. As long as you go to class you get a code to prove you were there (I took it online). The assignments are super easy, but you obviously have to do them.

The internship was a good experience that pushed me to apply lots of things I have been learning in my other business classes. Some of the things we did for the class (not the project) were helpful but others were easy but a waste of time. Overall I recommend this class if you are looking for some professional experience during your undergrad.
This class was great! Only advice I will give is that most of your grade is on the amount of hours you spend working for your company. Make sure you are getting your hours in!
good class, brother hollan provided helpful guidance for the projects
You don't have a lot of homework for professor Hollan. The workload is entirely dependent on the company you intern for. Great resume builder.

He is the professor over the On Campus Internship so most of the bad feelings I have definitely aren't his fault. I do feel like the project I was assigned to should never have been allowed to be an OCI so maybe the screening could be a bit better. Also my project had nothing to do with the major I am hoping to get in to.

It's literally just an internship disguised as a class. There are a couple of weekly assignments and midterm/final presentations but other than that everything you do is decided by your team. If you don't work at least 7.5 hours total during the week you can't get an A.
Professor Hollan is a great professor, he doesn't waste your time and only has a few class sessions a semester. I recommend taking the class. Gives you a good real-world professional experience

This is one of the best opportunities for any student at BYU. This internship program is organized really well and you won't ever be caught off guard. If you're interested in doing an internship, this class helps you every step of the way with amazing feedback from the TAs
My OCI was a waste of time but the professor cared about the success of the students and really wants you to grow.
Professor Hollan was very helpful throughout the course. He always gave very useful lectures.
This class was a great way to gain professional experience and an easy A.

This specific class is an on campus internship with a local company so you don't end up really having a relationship with the professor and the reason why its an easy A is because the assignments are easy. What matters most is that you do your best to have a meaningful project with a local company - thats what is important.
Though I didn't interact much with him personally (ahem, COVID), I found this class and this professor to be very educational and professional.

Graded mostly based on how many hours you put in every week. He takes a hands off approach, you guide yourself. If you need help there are great TA's assigned to your group! This is a great opportunity to build your resume and get credit at the same time!

Professor Hollan is a good teacher. His lectures were straightforward and helpful. He gave us excellent resources for the class, dealing with stress, and mental health. He is extremely respectful of his student's time and once he covers the material he planned he will dismiss class. If you do the work you'll do just fine. Great class for resume.

Interaction for this class specifically with Professor Hollan is very minimal. The on-campus internship class is a great opportunity to expand your resume and work in the "real world." You only have to attend a few 20 minute lectures by Professor Hollan throughout the semester. But, you are expected to work 7.5-9 hours a week on your project.
These classes are huge, so interactions with Prof. Hollan are limited. However, he has set up a great network of TAs who are very helpful. Rely on your TA and you'll have a great experience.

This is not a normal class that you would expect. It really makes you work with problems that the company or project that you work with. The team effort really matters. If you are not very committed and willing to work with sometimes challenging and ambiguous problems, then I wouldn't recommend taking this class.

Very good class. I only wish I had received a better company. However, the experience was great! Professor Hollan is great and his work experience speaks for itself. I will probably take one of his classes again.

This class is the best possible version of itself. BE PREPARED to work hard and invest 8+ hours/week- there is no getting around that. That being said, I really felt like the professor really wanted you to succeed (& get an 'A'). Class was mandatory, but wasn't every week, never wasted a minute, and was always enjoyable.

Professor Hollan was a great resource. He managed the OCI program very well. For a class that is very independent, he provided great resources and direction, but wasn't overbearing and let you take control of your project. I felt he had a great balance.
Solid class and great internship experiences.

This class was great! Getting an A is pretty easy, but the more effort you put in, the more you're going to get out of it. Not graded on many assignments and you can easily complete them. The difficulty of your actual internship will just depend on what you choose, how your team works, how your sponsor works, etc. Highly recommend to everyone!
Professor Holland is a good guy. You do not have much interaction with him. You only see him on zoom calls. You mostly interact with the TA's.
Great class because gives you real life experience. Not lots of interaction with professor just communicating with your team about your project all semester long.

There are only a few class periods for the semester but you need to attend them. The bulk of the work is within your groups and working with your sponsor. Professor Hollan does a great job on outlining what you need to accomplish and experiences about working in business world.

Great professor. There is quite a bit of busywork outside of the actual internship work. Definitely worth taking, though. The difficulty depends on what your project is. He works hard to get great projects for students. He really cares about the students and genuinely wants to help out. He could make way more money at a different job but stays!

Professor Hollan teaches how a professional internship should go. One of the issues with the class is that some of the project choices aren't that great. You'll learn a lot, but it's A LOT of work to get the 7.5 hours a week (to not lose points at the end of the semester...)
I loved taking this class! It definitely takes a lot of work but it's a great experience and awesome for a resume. I'd definitely recommend this class!
Cool opportunity for an internship, but just make sure you really communicate with your team and are all on the same page.
The class is clear about your grade. You won't be surprised what you get. Make an effort and you'll get an A. However, the class is a huge time investment.

This class is a great way to build your resume and have great real world experience while still being at BYU. I loved the project I worked on and my team was awesome. Make sure you choose projects you are actually interested in doing when signing up. Not hard with grading. Assignments are just things you should be providing the sponsor with.
Wonderful professor, very professional and wants you to succeed and develop life-long skills and professional behavior for future careers.

Professor Hollan is a great professor! He really helps you to be able to work effectively in a business organizational setting as well as learn the tools to be successful in your career. It is clear that he cares about his students and their future professional goals.
Great professor and wants you to succeed.

Highly recommend this class- such valuable experience without the pressure of it being a "real" job environment - (although definitely treat it like it is one). Very clear expectations from day 1: work for the required amount of hours --> get an A. It is definitely a lot of work, but super rewarding!
The most important thing is updating your timesheet and making sure your average hours are the appropriate amount of time.

Professor Hollan lectures about every other week to inspire you through your internship experience. If you put in seven hours each week, you will get an A and stay on top of your project. Not an easy A because this class does take time

Loved the class and gave me so much experience. Professor Hollan will help you with anything and gives you really good resources and advice for your project. How much you enjoy the class depends on your sponsor and group, but Professor Hollan was very helpful.

This class was online this semester. Only had to attend 6 classes that were max 30 min. You just have to do super easy modules each week and fill out a survey 3 times about your team. Really everything is easy you just have to work with your team on your assigned project.
The class didn't seem to be very well organized but the criteria was clear for grading and if you do your stuff you'll get an A. Make sure to build a relationship with your sponsor.

This class is good in theory. It depends a lot on which sponsor you get to work with. Some are good, others are not. Professor Hollan is basically just a supervisor for this class, you communicate mostly with TAs but Professor Hollan has provided lots of resources to aid your success.
Great opportunity to gain real world experience on campus.

The class is an on campus internship so David Hollan doesn't spend too much time with every single student or group because of how massive the class is. Focus more on your assigned TA and you'll do just fine for the class.

This class is an on-campus internship. This means that most of the work is team work done outside of class. You will need to log at least 7.5 hours a week working for your sponsor. This class is an amazing opportunity to develop yourself professional in a low-risk environment. It looks really good on a resume too!

Definitely worth taking if you are lacking some professional experience on your resume and are interviewing for internships or full time positions soon. I have used this on campus internship as answers to behavioral questions for internships. Super helpful!

I really enjoyed my experience with my sponsor company and my team, but the class period and class assignments were a waste of time. The professor didn't allow questions, and he literally only reviewed what we had read throughout the week. The forms we had to submit were unnecessary for my team and sponsor, and we were graded harshly for no reason.
Such a great class. Professor Hollan is a super nice guy and facilitates the internship project well. Everyone should do an OCI.
He is a good teacher, this class will help you develop new skills at a professional level.
He's an ok teacher. If you do all the assignments you would get an A. That's it. The group projects' difficulty depends on your sponsor.

The On Campus Internship experience is well worth all the work! It was the perfect stepping stone for me to gain real life experience in an environment made for students that have never done an internship before. I feel so much more prepared for future internships and my career because of this class!

The class was pretty easy. There are mandatory classes that you have to attend a few times during the semester, but you don't really have to pay attention. The work honestly isn't bad, you just have to make sure you log enough hours each week. It is good to build your resume and get experience easily.
Great way to get experience for life. Professor was helpful and supportive of learning environment.

The on campus internship experience is a lot of work but will prepare you for your career and life ahead. The Professor & TA really make sure you know what is required and are there to answer any questions and ensure you get the most out of the internship.
Great class and helps you develop your resume. I love my team and working with people to help a company develop and grow. Ive learned so much taking this class

Professor Hollan is very caring for his students. The class is an easy A, but it can be stressful as it is not a typical class (494R) because you have to deal with a real business situation beyond grades.
easy and experience-enriched class. but pick great company and good luck with the team members.

Really depends on your company. My group got put with a company that was just using us for busy work, so we got nothing out of it. The professor was understanding though, and at least gave us a different option for the last month of classes.
Make sure to log your hours every week and be honest! This class is a great resume builder and the professor/TA's are super helpful.

I really liked the Idea behind an on campus internship. I just felt like we had so much to turn in for the class that our Sponsor just didn't care about. The class structure works for some projects, but ours didn't fit at all under the structure of all the assignments we had to complete. Just hope that your project fits the class structure.

The teammates that I was placed with were really great and I loved that part of the class. Additionally, the sponsor that I was placed with was really great. However, in some ways this class was kinda a waste of time. I don't think I developed any great skills that can be used outside of this class.

Just put in the hours and you'll get a good grade. Not much interaction with the professor  just a 30 min class like six times a semester that didn't really seem to have a point besides maybe answering questions.
I loved taking an on campus internship. You only have class 6 times and the rest is just meeting up with your group and working on the project.

I would recommend doing an on-campus internship. If you get a good sponsor and a good team then it can be a lot of fun, as well as teach you a lot. Professor Hollan has mandatory class every few weeks. I thought the classes were very short and not super helpful. Overall good experience, but did not feel like the professor helped a ton.

Although there isn't much to do with Prof Hollan, I wasn't a fan. He seemed to take special attention to my group for some reason. The work we did outside of the project is understandable, but still dumb. The project itself is up to you and your teammates. My group worked really hard and had a great experience. Bring up problems @ the start!

Whatever you do DO NOT DO AN ON-CAMPUS INTERNSHIP WITH HOLLAN. He said that more students need to fail it. So you will receive a fail even if you do all the work. You wont receive any indicators that you are failing, in fact you could be doing really well. If you email him for an explanation, he wont reply. Its your future he ruined not his.
Does not give any feedback on why you received a grade and does not look out for the interests of the students.

You don't really work with Prof. Hollan much at all in this class since it is an On Campus Internship. You more just work with your sponsor (depending on your internship) but Prof Hollan is chill. Lectures are short. The required things you have to do for class I thought were pointless but easy.

This is an interesting class. Probably the most relevant thing on my resume right now (as a sophomore). Prof. Hollan is a hands-off kinda guy, so you don't work with him probably at all. That being said, the rest of the work is all on you. 7.5 hours a week for 14 weeks. It isn't easy, but if you get lucky with a good team/project, good experience.

Had a great experience during my two OCIs - choose your project carefully, but as long as you work hard and get creative, you'll gain experience for your resume and experiences you can talk about during interviews. This class wasn't too difficult - 7.5 hours per week, but on a flexible schedule. I'm glad I took this, and an A is very achievable.
Learned a lot about team communication and communicating with the sponsor of our company. Had a lot more fun with this class than I ever expected.
I learned a lot about project management and the development process. Our team learned to be flexible and at the same time we needed to stay on schedule and push the project along.
Learned a lot and helped me land a paid summer internship
Had a great team. Had an okay project.

Stepped in for our team when our sponsor was slacking off. Get your stuff done and go to class (you only have to go like 8 times, so easy). Easy to contact and always willing to led an ear and give guidance. Poor reviews must be from students who didn't want to do any work. He's a good guy and doesn't expect too much.

Good guy. Stepped in for our team when our sponsor was slacking off. Get your stuff done and go to class (you only have to go like 8 times, so easy). Easy to contact and always willing to led an ear and give guidance. Poor reviews must be from students who didn't want to do any work, he's a good guy and doesn't expect too much.

Dr. Hollan was great about answering any questions. He was very clear with what he wanted and when things were due. Anyone who has negative feedback must not have been a diligent student and expected him to do everything for them. He is a great professor who is clear and the class is not hard, just do your work with your company.

Compared to other on-campus internships the coursework you do in Hollan's is ridiculous and not productive, and his classes are extremely boring. I feel there is a lack of trust between him and the students ability to work with their assigned companies based on the assignments he gives out. Not to mention his assignments have strange due times.
Got some great experience added to my resume which helped me land a great internship this summer and also helped me with my summer project.

While the internship was a great experience, the Professor, his instruction, & the tedious assignments that he loaded on top of the internship was a total waste of time. He made class attendance mandatory but taught us nothing useful. The timesheet had too much weight on the final grade, especially for a thing that every students lied about anyways
Helped me get my summer internship
Prof. Hollan is a good guy and does his best to teach 400+ students who all have different projects and needs.

This program is incredible for students to gain valuable experience in the workforce. I have taken the class multiple times and it has always been fantastic. I even tried to get permission to take on two internships. Class, on the other hand, has no other description but a complete waste of time. Dave is a great guy, but class is totally useless.

David Hollan cares about his students. Although you don't have class often, he is happy to meet and give amazing feedback. He wants you to succeed and gain relevant experience to help you in the future. He is on your team. Be ready to work a lot on your project. 7.5 hours are required each week, you'll present two times throughout the semester.

The internship portion of this class was great. Good business experience that can be applied to a young resume. Class with Professor Hollan was, frankly, quite boring and much of the in-class material seemed frivolous and only mildly applicable. It almost seemed like class was designed to make us worry about our projects more than we needed to.

The internship portion of this class was great. Good business experience that can be applied to a young resume. Class with Professor Hollan was, frankly, quite boring and much of the in-class material seemed frivolous and only mildly applicable. It almost seemed like Professor Hollan wanted us to worry about our projects more than we needed to.

He doesnt grade the way he says he will. He told us to not worry about doing some assignments and then docked us for not doing them. His class is pointless and useless. The internship part of the class was great but everything else was a waste of time.

Dr. Jensen is a really great professor. He is just another example of how BYU CE dept hires only the most highly respected men/women in their field. If you have any interest in aircraft or composites definitely take a class from him. He really cares about whether students understand or not.

I thought he was one of the best professors I've had. He is sincerely interested in helping people understand the material, instead of just giving you the equations and exactly how to use them. I would say most people who give poor reviews are bitter and didn't put the time in that is necessary to succeed in a difficult course such as this one.
Points for attendance are lame. Tests are tricky (study a LOT!) But he tries really hard to make students happy. He's a good guy his lectures just aren't the best.

Avoid at all costs! He cant write tests! and when you mess up because of him its somehow your own fault. He cant do anything wrong. The entire class pointed out his mistake on an example he was working on the board but he would not admit that he was wrong. He kept giving a magical explanation as to how he was right. It was sad and obvious. stayaway

Assignments took forever to complete in his class and going to him for help is a joke.  I have never met a more condescending and rude person in my life.  He will belittle you in his office if you try and visit him.

Great teacher.  He really cares about his students, but he is going to push you hard to make sure you learn the material.  Let's be honest.  Once you become a full professor at the Y, students' opinions don't really matter.  Saying that - he is one of the best engineering profs out there.

He is a nice guy. However, the class was very difficult, made much more so by the professor. The lectures often didn't have anything to do with the homework.  He didn't listen to students, and dismissed questions he felt not good. The homework was well over the 2 to 1 ratio (up to 10 hours on one assignment, there are three assignments a week!)
Worst teacher I have ever had.  He was never prepared for class, terrible at explaining topics, and errogant.
Disorganized.  Class Felt like it should have been 7.0 semester hours.  I spent 25 hours on the first lab report and did not finish!  It was the hardest B+ I have ever earned.

Dr. Jensen is a great guy, and I enjoyed his class.  This class was very interesting, while also being very difficult.  Students may not like Dr. Jensen's 305 class, but I think that they will like him a lot better if they took higher-level classes from him.  Let's face it-CEEn 305 is an annoying class no matter who you take it from.
Hard to understand and not organized

This guy seems to be in his own little world, where everyone is a genius.  He refuses to meet students half-way; rather he expects them to understand everything from reading the advanced textbook.  His assignments were either ridiculously hard or ridiculously easy.  Tests were not a good reflection of what we had learned.  Avoid this guy if you can
Great teacher, funny and knowledgeable
His class was amazingly hard but i learned a lot
Total awesomeness
He is the most down to earth funny professor i have met in byu take him

I was possibly the worst student Dr. M has ever had. Always missed class (not purposefully), did horrifically bad on exams, barely came to office hours. Both semesters he was beyond caring and patient with me. Hilarious, always has a smile on his face, and holds so many extra reviews for students. Undoubtedly one of the best professors out there.

A great professor! He really cares for his students and wants them to succeed. Graded on quizzes, practice exams (homework), and exams. Exams in chem building. Has instructor led reviews, he posts them online as well. TAs also help, they usually have reviews on the mornings of fridays, when we usually had a quiz in class. Course put together well.

His genuine enthusiasm for his area of expertise is infectious. It is clear that he cares deeply about his students. He is respectful of questions. The class was extremely well extremely organized. There was an abundance of resources available, which helped ensure deep understanding of the material. If you put in the time you will get a good grade.

Dr. Michaelis is one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are always interesting. Attend his reviews and watch his review videos (and do the homework problems) as they are really helpful for the exams. I learned so much from his class and he made me love organic chemistry!

He's great and very accessible! Genuinely wants his students to succeed, just make sure to use those opportunities! It's a lot of work - but if you put in the work and ask for help you will be alright! He is not memorization heavy and more conceptual for the first part of class! The nature of the class means more memorization at the end.

LOVE Michaelis!! Tests are based on lectures. Know the why behind things and you should be good. Quizzes are easy if you look over the lecture notes. Go to his reviews, they are really helpful. I took this during spring and it was easy. He is very funny and nice and really just wants everyone to do well in the class.

Dr. Michaelis is the best choice for CHEM 352, he's very fair and only tests on what he covers in class. The quizzes aren't too bad, the homework is completion based, and he has amazing review videos which you should definitely watch. He's very energetic and makes you feel excited for organic chemistry.
First-class professor.

Dr Michaelis is seriously one of the best professors I have ever had. He is energetic, accommodating, funny, and truly, I don't know if I have ever had another professor so devoted to their students' success. Dr Michaelis worked constantly to give us every opportunity to succeed in his class. I cannot recommend him enough for 352.
Very difficult but he prepares you well. Free response tests are the move. He is entertaining even though some of the stuff he says is so out of pocket

I took this class spring semester. He is a very fun and energetic teacher and you can tell he cares about your success in the class and beyond. The assignments all helped prepare for quizzes and tests and I never felt like I was doing busy work. I was nervous about all free response tests but they gave back points in any way they could.
Full of energy and super fair teacher. Best way I could describe him is as an advocate (aka you put in the work and make sure he knows, things will work out). Tests are free response but very fair.
Great professor, hard class

Dr. Michaelis is hands down the best professor I have ever had. He has SO MUCH energy. There was not a single boring day no joke. He personally hosts three hours of review sessions outside of class, which are a must and are very helpful. He is a merciful grader and teaches principles instead of rote memorization, which I valued a lot. He's the best

He is one of the best teachers I've had at BYU! I took the section of o-chem for majors only, and it moves FAST, but he teaches the subject matter very well! He is so funny, entertaining, and is a VERY reasonable grader. His tests are very fair and are all free response. Overall 10/10 recommend!

Best professor I've ever had. He does three hours of review a week outside of class that are recorded and posted so you can watch them if you couldn't make it or go back and review. Hw is graded on completion, weekly quizzes aren't bad, and tests are fairest I've ever had in chem and he will regrade if you think the TA should've given more points

Chem 351 is a hard class in general, but out of all the classes that I have taken at BYU, Dr. Michaelis's was the class that I felt was set up best for students to succeed. His lectures are extremely engaging. He not only teaches students the material, but includes bits of advice every lecture to help us to become better people and disciples.

He is literally the best. I was premed but after taking his class I switched to chemistry completely. He has a way of making you LOVE the subject if you give it a chance. 81% tests, 11% quizzes every friday and 8% completion grade hw. Free response tests, but easy grader and material is from lectures. MWF 1hr review session (in person/recorded)

Dr. Michaelis understands how to motivate and teach students. The majority of the class got an A or an A- and all of the tests were free-response (so you could show what you know and not get tricked by multiple-choice questions). Do all of his problem sets and attend/watch his recorded review sessions as much as possible.

Dr. Michaelis is the best option for organic chemistry! He loves the subject and wants everyone to pass. He offers review sessions 3 times a week for students to practice material. His tests are hard but reasonable. Be prepared to spend several hours outside of class studying. It's a hard subject, but Dr. Michaelis makes learning ochem tolerable.

Overwhelmingly fair grader. Held 3 reviews every week personally to help students. Held review for each exam personally. Was very accessible to students. Graded with a lot of leeway!!! I wish I could take every chemistry class from him. So many resources available for students.

I was terrified for Ochem because of the horror stories. But, Dr. Michaelis made this class completely doable. He's amazing. He's not super by the book so you can skim reading, and he's SOOO forgiving on his grading. Grade is mostly from exams, but that's department wide. He's hilarious, 10/10 lectures. If you have to take ochem, TAKE IT FROM HIM.

Loved taking ochem from him. Provides guided notes, does lecture reviews after each lecture (they are recorded), did an ochem prep set of videos before the course started that were VERY helpful. Tests are all free response, but he gives a LOT of partial credit. He is very funny, made lectures more fun. He made ochem very easy and straightforward.

Dr. Michaelis is one of the best professors I have ever had. If you're taking his class to jump through a hoop for med school, without the intention to really learn, then you won't like him. But, if you really want to learn about chemistry, there isn't a more passionate and caring professor who wants to help you learn! I would 100% take him again.

Worst teacher I have had among all the teachers I have taken at BYU, UVU, or my graduate school. He tries to be the cool teacher and seem laid back. It is a facade. I visited him in his office hours once and he was extremely rude. As another reviewer has mentioned, Michaelis's "office hour" lectures are so unfair for those who cannot attend. 0/10

Professor Michalis is as good as it gets here at BYU. His Ochem 2 class was great, it was very difficult but everyone knows that's how Ochem 2 is going to be. If you are willing to put in the time, and study hard using his notes and go to his reviews then you will do great. I would take him again for Biochem if I could.

The best chem professor I have had. His enthusiasm rubs off if you let it. He is very organized with his lecture notes which makes studying pretty easy. He doesn't believe in multiple choice tests, but this actually helps because he is pretty generous on grading.
A very difficult class was made manageable by him. His lectures were clear and his tests are very fair. Pay attention and go over the chapter notes and you'll do well.

Dr. Michaelis does a spectacular job at explaining the why behind reactions. which makes remembering and understanding organic chemistry a million times easier. I can't stress this enough Dr. Michaelis is truly an amazing teacher. Just remember to actively do the textbook homework, and reach out to him if you need help. He really cares.

Dr. Michaelis turned what could have been a very difficult class into a very manageable one. He does 2 reviews every week where he will answer questions and make up practice questions for you to do that will be very similar to the actual test. Go to his reviews and you'll do absolutely great!

Hardest class I have ever taken. 6 tests were 88% of grade. Study group saved me. We learned that other professors went slower, (we were studying in the library and the group next to us had a different professor and their class was a whole test-unit behind us) so we think he is the hardest ochem professor due to pure speed. Very available though.

Dr. Michaelis truly cares about his students. Obviously, Organic Chemistry is difficult, and there's no way around that. but he was so enthusiastic and so willing to provide help. He smiled the entire lecture long. He also provided bi-weekly review sessions to prepare everyone for the test. Truly an amazing professor.

Michaelis is great, but he makes his tests WAY harder than the rest of BYU's professors. He teaches the material well, but puts way too much emphasis on memorization and insane preparation for tests. This class will consume your life more than any other OChem professor. Overall, though, he's effective, clear, and fun. Just ridiculous expectations.

Worst professor I have had at BYU. I retook the class from a better chem professor and did well. Michaelis just wants attention and to be the "cool professor". His tests are so much harder than any other chem teacher at BYU (which is unfortunately saying something). His outside class review sessions are unfair for the students unable to attend. 0/5

Dr. Michaelis makes Ochem 1 super interesting. He gives clear note templates so you never have to worry about what you need to copy down from the board, you just follow along in the notes and fill them out as you go. He tries to give you all the help he can and holds valuable reviews and office hours every week.

I really liked Dr. Michaelis! He cares a lot about his job. He does weekly reviews where he spends an hour answering questions (probably because the class is so fast-paced there is no time for questions during class). He is willing to do extra work (like personally regrade your test if you don't agree with the TA) to help you succeed.

I found his teaching style to be a bit tough. He would go through the information so fast and dive into concepts that seemed more complicated than what we needed to know at the time. His class was very test heavy and they were extremely tough with no curve. I appreciated that he focused more on understanding concepts rather than just memorization

Dr. Michaelis is the MAN! Seriously, take him for Chem 351. Print off his lecture note templates and follow along with lecture, and definitely go to his office hour reviews. He is very understanding and wants you to do well. Test heavy, I think there were 5 but study and you'll do fine.

Dr. Michaelis is one of my favorite people! He is eager to help and is encouraging. That being said, his class is DIFFICULT. I spent easily 12+ hours a week practicing, and I could only pull a B+. Full confession, I had taken o-chem 1 at another highly respected university, but this course made the first look like child's play.

Dr. M is such a great professor. I enjoyed every lecture. You can tell he loves what he does. His class is hard but hes always willing to help. Just gotta put in the work. Would highly recommend taking OChem from him!

Dr. Michaelis is contagiously enthusiastic. You can tell he loves what he does and that makes a huge impact on his teaching style. Be aware that this is a very fast-paced class, with just about 0 time in lectures for questions. He invests a lot of time in extra-curricular review sessions. For this class, you get out what you put in!

You must listen to me. If you are taking ochem, take Dr. Michaelis. He's test heavy, and his tests are hard, but he really wants to be a good teacher, gives weekly content reviews, does not teach directly out of a book, and wants his students to succeed. There is no curve, but an A in the class is only a 91%.

I had heard awful things about ochem but the class wasn't bad at all. Of course it is chem so you have to put in a lot of work but not more than other chem class. He is hilarious and engaging. To do well pay attention in class, go to a couple of his review sessions and study for a few hours before the test and you will be golden!

Honestly the greatest professor -- He helped me learn to love organic chemistry. He teaches in his own way, not a walking textbook, which I loved. Wasn't your typical boring professor. Awesome lectures, and I seriously enjoyed taking his exams. They were all free response, hard but really fun. You're making a mistake if you take it from anyone else

He is great! Our grade was determined by 3 midterm timed essays, attendance, and participation. He is a tough grader, but offers extra credit opportunities. Not a very hard class, but very important to do well on the exams and to show up every day to class. I enjoyed the content.

Dr. Laraway was great! I took History of Philosophy 1 from him. His discussions were interesting, and I found the workload to be very reasonable. Looking back, I would have taken the extra credit options he gave us, and I would have gotten an A. The only feedback I'd have for him is to make the study guide a little more comprehensive

This class was good! Although the quizzes and tests are worth a lot so make sure to do the readings (you can find pdf's of all of them online). Listen during lectures because those are exam topics. The class isn't too hard but attendance is mandatory! Overall, pretty good! (there are 3 exams and each exam has an essay section-so be ready to write)

he covers important topics. He has in class quizes that he claims are objective but the students in the class consistently feel that they are partially subjective, and tough. He has questions on the exams that are also debatable. If you want to do well on the papers, go to his office hours and walk through your entire argument.

He is a great professor! He's very understanding and is willing to work with his students. He offered a ton of opportunities for extra credit, and I feel like his grading was fair. Tests were good; I felt like they were very doable but really just tested me on if I did do the readings and paid attention in class.

I really enjoyed his class. I actually had him for SPAN 345 (Cultures of Spain). He did a good job of making the lectures engaging, but useful for the exams. The exams were a little difficult, but if you do good on the project and quizzes you will be fine. He's a really good guy and respectful.

The readings (2 per week) often took 1-3 hours each and were boiled down to 4 question quizzes (2 min time limit) that would ask about tiny details buried somewhere in the reading or would require a black and white answer to a subjective claim. The midterm and final were the same way. Lectures were usually either pretty good or fine. Great guy tho

The 2 weekly quizzes were not difficult as long as you read the material. I felt like he was not very strict with the written portion of the exams or the essay. As long as you're in class listening and grasping the general ideas of the content you're good. He is a smart guy and the lectures were fascinating and thought-provoking.

He is alright, although the weekly quizzes will give stress because the way the questions are worded are pretty tough. And he only gives you two minutes to do the quizzes and the midterm and final are timed as well. You have to really get what is being put down which in a philosophy class is a little hard. He is a great at lecturing and will help.

He is a pretty harsh grader and very unclear with assignments, expectations, and content. Although this course was interesting and he often had some good lectures, it was a hard class to get through. If you are taking this intro class you should be familiar with philosophical or artistic concepts.

2 quizzes each week on the reading. you have 2 minutes to answer 4 questions from the reading, if you miss 1 question that drops to a C. He's very picky about the essays and is not lenient. He expects you to understand philosophy like it is common knowledge even though this class is a GE for most. He is a lovely person, but not class is not for me

Intro to Spanish literature did NOT sound like a class I would have enjoyed, however Professor Laraway did a fantastic job making the class and material engaging and relevant. The way that he facilitates discussions is so enjoyable, and his assignments were perfectly reasonable. I would definitely take any of his other classes if I have the chance.

Dr. Laraway is a great professor for anyone wanting to get into philosophy. He will make it as complicated or as simple as it needs to be for you to understand. There was a lot of assigned reading, but all of it was relevant to the course. The class was heavy on discussion so do be prepared to talk.

He was very attentive to his students and care more about the students learning than spitting back information (when he sensed a reading was too difficult he wouldn't test on it). His tests were relatively easy as long as you'd study. I don't recommend him for Zoom, his words and ideas are too difficult to understand without discussion.

Took his philosophy class as a GE and thought it would help me understand philosophy more but it was the complete opposite. The entire class makes no sense and still don't understand philosophy now that I have finished the class. DO not take this class unless you understand philosophy.

Professor Laraway is my favorite professor I've had studying philosophy at BYU. He is kind and charismatic, and he is great at teaching difficult material. I've taken multiple classes from him and I'd recommend him to anyone.
Welcome to the BYU philosophy department:)

He's not the worst teacher ever, but there isn't much to write home about. He understands when students are struggling and adjusts the schedule to review complicated topics, but he does go off on long tangents about the material. Take the class only if you're interested in your brain melting from confusing texts. Sparknotes will be your friend
Dr Laraway can ALWAYS be reached by email and he makes it his goal to respond to your emails quickly. He can tend to lecture for most of class so if youre into that hes your guy.

Prof. Laraway was great! You could tell that he was very passionate about the subject and that he cared about his students. He is very smart so sometimes what he said in lecture went over my head, but he is good at going back and reviewing the important things. This class was a lot harder than I expected, I took it for a gen ed but it was worth it.

Prof. Laraway is awesome. The class was super interesting and very engaging. I'm not even a philosophy major and I really enjoyed it and learned so much. Homework is mostly reading and two papers. Lots of reading and discussion. If you don't like talking in class this is not for you. But I loved the class discussions and the readings.

Professor Laraway is both very smart/insightful, and down to earth. He gives interesting lectures that turn into class discussions. No tests - most of your grade comes from 4 essays (one of which you can drop). You can do well on them if you put in sufficient work. Frequent quizzes - easy if you've done reading. Highly recommend this class.

Laraway is awesome, I've loved his class and it's helped me develop a deeper appreciation for Spanish literature. The class only consists of in-class quizzes, and 4 essays with him dropping your lowest graded one. He won't just give you a 100 for turning in the paper, but he's a fair grader I'd say. Cool guy, but we only spoke like 40% Spanish.

It is a literature class, but there are no tests! Just four essays! There are pop-quizzes in class but if you do the readings then you should be good. He's fun and teaches the class in a mix of spanish and english. He's passionate about the subject and helps to teach and analyze literature in a way that can be understood. No textbook, just a packet

Nice professor! The class is weighed heavily (40%) on your final paper. There are reading quizzes every class, and the midterm/final are based on these readings. You definitely can't glide through this class; if you want a good grade, plan on working for it.

Laraway is an incredible professor. He is super passionate about the material and is great at invoking thoughtful and interesting conversation. He has a big paper that you write, but he works with you on it throughout the whole semester. Watch out for daily reading quizzes; they add up. Also, his final is OPEN NOTE/BOOK.

His class wasn't bad... I took it a couple of semesters ago. He was passionate and loved the material he was reading, but he didn't make it an easy class. His quizzes were sporadic and required you to know a LOT of the material (weird details) and was pretty tough with his grading. If he thinks you're not giving your all he will dock points.

You should take SPAN339 from him if at all possible. No tests, pass/fail final and only 3 essays throughout the semester.  There are readings throughout the different sections of the course that you must do to be ready to participate in class which is 20% of the grade. Overall the best option for the class is to take it from him.

Professor Laraway centers the course around classroom discussion. A big part of the grade is your participation in the conversation. Each discussion is very interesting. He is also great at making each student's comment seem like a great interpretation and a valuable contribution to the discussion. Most of the grade is based on the essays.

Absolute worst teacher ever. I hated every moment of class. Quizzes were almost everyday & focused on unimportant points & exams were extremely difficult & almost impossible. Hardest & worse class I've ever taken.  DO NOT TAKE FROM THIS PROFESSOR! He's horrible & prideful & expects you to know everything. Don't get fooled by the other ratings.

Hes great. I want to take him again.  Good teacher, interesting subject matter he chose to put in the class, and very easy going chill dude.  His tests are pretty easy if you know the study guides he gives you.  You gotta go to class to get a good grade, which is ok cause class is fun. He uses movies to teach too. Lots of extra credit oppertunities

One of the best teachers I have had at BYU.  He was VERY fair. Reading quizzes each class period, but gave a lot of opportunity to get extra credit to make up for hard quizzes. Tests were a very fair judgement of what we learned. Direct correlation to what was covered in class. Knows what he's talking about. Likes test essays.
Can't say enough good about this lit class. Very engaging lecturer, and he included film too! Favorite Spanish professor at BYU so far.

He is one of the best professors in the Spanish department! His lectures are engaging and interesting. He puts a grade on participation based on your attendance and how much you talk in the class, so be sure to go to class and talk a lot. Not too hard of a class if you do the reading. This was my second class with this guy and it never got old.

Awesome teacher. He wants to make the class as simple as possible. Attendance is a must as he changes the syllabus around sometimes.  Tests are fairly simple. He gives you a study guide with all you need to know.  I'm not a big LatAm history person, but this class was enjoyable.

A great teacher.  He is very interesting, asks engaging questions, and does a great job of selecting the subject matter, which is a difficult task considering the amount of material that COULD be included in the course.  Tests require lots of studying because there's so much info to learn, but A is possible.  Offers plenty of extra credit.

Professor Laraway rocks.  He is a great professor, his classes are interesting, he is involved in students' interests, etc.  I enjoyed his class - some of the tests and quizzes were a little nit-picky and difficult, but it was worth it for sure!

He's easier than 345. You have to go to 3 eventos culturales, but you get full points for typing 1 page about it. The study guides give you more detail than is on the actual test. I was surprised on the first test that I didn't need to know the study guide in and out. ATTENDANCE is a MUST. He's lenient and curves grades  sometimes.

We had a reading quiz almost every single day. The quiz questions were actually very specific and although I did the reading almost everyday I rarely got full credit for the quiz. In order to prepare for the quiz make sure you have read in depth. Test questions are the same. The test questions are very specific and sometimes very tricky. On one mul

I took him for 355 as well, and he is a great teacher.  His tests are not too hard as he tells you exactly what you need to know for them.  Lectures are interesting and worthwhile.  One of my favorite professors.

Prof Laraway was fun and I'm taking him for 451. He's got a great attitude and the class isn't too hard. You do need to do the reading, but he's very liberal on the essay sections of the test (which is half the test). You do still need to be prepared for the multiple choice and t/f sections though. Overall, a great teacher. Would recommend.

There weren't any quizzes on the readings this past semester and I realized later on in the semester that I only had to skim the readings before class.  Just print off a copy of the online readings so you can highlight the parts he reads in class and jot down notes right on the reading.  He only tested us on stuff we'd read together in class.

Well, his class is a little different since the last rating, but I still liked it a lot. He is a fun teacher and is good at explaining things. There are a few opportunities for extra credit. Going to the cuktural events was fun (required to for class).

3 tests, 1 final. All tests have essay section. Not too bad if you've studied. Final is take home essay. A million pop-quizzes on your reading...only 10 count...they are pretty easy but you do need to read which can be boring and take a long time.

Professor Lignell was a very kind teacher. He was very spiritual, which was good for the UNIV 101 class. However, I didn't enjoy the class so that put a bit of a damper on my view. There was a lot of reading and homework, but Lignell was always understanding and polite.

Professor Lignell represents the worst parts of BYU. He repeatedly spend half of class talking about his time at church over the weekend instead of teaching the material the students are paying to learn. If you break the dress and grooming standards, Lignell will be the professor who gets you in trouble for it. I switched schools after this course.

He is a really cool and nice guy. I always felt respected and welcome, and even had some spiritual experiences in his class. I loved having 4 midterms. It eased the pressure and gave me lots of feedback. Attending class is not necessary. He always posts lecture notes. Sometimes not great at explaining things, and homework at times was excessive.

Dr. Lignell was overall a great professor. I loved the video examples he provided for the Python class. My only gripe was that he didn't have any mercy on the grading for the midterms; however, he did counteract this with a second chance testing that allowed for 50% credit back on problems missed. In addition, he used the final exam as a curve.
Homework assignments sometimes took hours but most were reasonable. Beware of a midterm sneaking up on you (4 of them plus a final in one semester). A great professor all around.

I really liked the way Dr Lignell had the class set up. The homework and the lectures were designed well to help you learn how to learn Excel and the Python coding language. The tests were doable if you kept up in the class. I was very impressed with how Dr Lignell was willing to help us out. Great class!

Dr. Lignell was an excellent professor! He's extremely willing to help any student who comes to him. He's very down to earth and clear with you. To be honest, his class was probably my favorite class because he relates what you're learning so well to any application.
This course is challenging if you have not written computer code before. It is a very difficult course, but Lignell is willing to help you. He desires feedback and cares about your success.

You can tell Dr. Lignell really cares about the students, and is also passionate about his work. He tells us that his rule is "make the test, then make it easier," but dang that final was HARD! To be fair, I didn't study the final unit material, but it wrecked me over.  The lectures were a little unclear at times, but he and the TA's were on point.

Hard class, but Dr. Lignell is a brilliant professor who really cares about helping his students succeed. Lectures hard to follow but he has really good online lecture notes and he is very helpful at office hours.

He's a really nice guy, one of the smartest I've ever met. His lectures are good to go to but he doesn't take attendance and usually what he goes over is either intuitive or straight off the notes. Once in a while he will go over tough HW problems. His class is all the tests and projects, so good luck.
Professor Lignell does a good job teaching a huge variety of things. He respects his students and has great spiritual insights. I plan on taking classes from him in the future.
Coming to class is useless and I left more confused. The cherry on top is when he spent the entire class period writing a proof on the board that even he didn't care about.
Dr. Lignell is a great guy, and very helpful. His lectures can be a little boring, but what he hits in class is what's on the test, and he's great at explaining tough concepts.
Dr Lignell is a very good guy and a very good professor. He tests you on those stuff which he mainly focuses on class. So, get notes on his class and review his lecture slides and you'll be fine.
Total awesomeness
He is the most down to earth funny professor i have met in byu take him

I was possibly the worst student Dr. M has ever had. Always missed class (not purposefully), did horrifically bad on exams, barely came to office hours. Both semesters he was beyond caring and patient with me. Hilarious, always has a smile on his face, and holds so many extra reviews for students. Undoubtedly one of the best professors out there.

A great professor! He really cares for his students and wants them to succeed. Graded on quizzes, practice exams (homework), and exams. Exams in chem building. Has instructor led reviews, he posts them online as well. TAs also help, they usually have reviews on the mornings of fridays, when we usually had a quiz in class. Course put together well.

His genuine enthusiasm for his area of expertise is infectious. It is clear that he cares deeply about his students. He is respectful of questions. The class was extremely well extremely organized. There was an abundance of resources available, which helped ensure deep understanding of the material. If you put in the time you will get a good grade.

Dr. Michaelis is one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are always interesting. Attend his reviews and watch his review videos (and do the homework problems) as they are really helpful for the exams. I learned so much from his class and he made me love organic chemistry!

He's great and very accessible! Genuinely wants his students to succeed, just make sure to use those opportunities! It's a lot of work - but if you put in the work and ask for help you will be alright! He is not memorization heavy and more conceptual for the first part of class! The nature of the class means more memorization at the end.

LOVE Michaelis!! Tests are based on lectures. Know the why behind things and you should be good. Quizzes are easy if you look over the lecture notes. Go to his reviews, they are really helpful. I took this during spring and it was easy. He is very funny and nice and really just wants everyone to do well in the class.

Dr. Michaelis is the best choice for CHEM 352, he's very fair and only tests on what he covers in class. The quizzes aren't too bad, the homework is completion based, and he has amazing review videos which you should definitely watch. He's very energetic and makes you feel excited for organic chemistry.
First-class professor.

Dr Michaelis is seriously one of the best professors I have ever had. He is energetic, accommodating, funny, and truly, I don't know if I have ever had another professor so devoted to their students' success. Dr Michaelis worked constantly to give us every opportunity to succeed in his class. I cannot recommend him enough for 352.
Very difficult but he prepares you well. Free response tests are the move. He is entertaining even though some of the stuff he says is so out of pocket

I took this class spring semester. He is a very fun and energetic teacher and you can tell he cares about your success in the class and beyond. The assignments all helped prepare for quizzes and tests and I never felt like I was doing busy work. I was nervous about all free response tests but they gave back points in any way they could.
Full of energy and super fair teacher. Best way I could describe him is as an advocate (aka you put in the work and make sure he knows, things will work out). Tests are free response but very fair.
Great professor, hard class

Dr. Michaelis is hands down the best professor I have ever had. He has SO MUCH energy. There was not a single boring day no joke. He personally hosts three hours of review sessions outside of class, which are a must and are very helpful. He is a merciful grader and teaches principles instead of rote memorization, which I valued a lot. He's the best

He is one of the best teachers I've had at BYU! I took the section of o-chem for majors only, and it moves FAST, but he teaches the subject matter very well! He is so funny, entertaining, and is a VERY reasonable grader. His tests are very fair and are all free response. Overall 10/10 recommend!

Best professor I've ever had. He does three hours of review a week outside of class that are recorded and posted so you can watch them if you couldn't make it or go back and review. Hw is graded on completion, weekly quizzes aren't bad, and tests are fairest I've ever had in chem and he will regrade if you think the TA should've given more points

Chem 351 is a hard class in general, but out of all the classes that I have taken at BYU, Dr. Michaelis's was the class that I felt was set up best for students to succeed. His lectures are extremely engaging. He not only teaches students the material, but includes bits of advice every lecture to help us to become better people and disciples.

He is literally the best. I was premed but after taking his class I switched to chemistry completely. He has a way of making you LOVE the subject if you give it a chance. 81% tests, 11% quizzes every friday and 8% completion grade hw. Free response tests, but easy grader and material is from lectures. MWF 1hr review session (in person/recorded)

Dr. Michaelis understands how to motivate and teach students. The majority of the class got an A or an A- and all of the tests were free-response (so you could show what you know and not get tricked by multiple-choice questions). Do all of his problem sets and attend/watch his recorded review sessions as much as possible.

Dr. Michaelis is the best option for organic chemistry! He loves the subject and wants everyone to pass. He offers review sessions 3 times a week for students to practice material. His tests are hard but reasonable. Be prepared to spend several hours outside of class studying. It's a hard subject, but Dr. Michaelis makes learning ochem tolerable.

Overwhelmingly fair grader. Held 3 reviews every week personally to help students. Held review for each exam personally. Was very accessible to students. Graded with a lot of leeway!!! I wish I could take every chemistry class from him. So many resources available for students.

I was terrified for Ochem because of the horror stories. But, Dr. Michaelis made this class completely doable. He's amazing. He's not super by the book so you can skim reading, and he's SOOO forgiving on his grading. Grade is mostly from exams, but that's department wide. He's hilarious, 10/10 lectures. If you have to take ochem, TAKE IT FROM HIM.

Loved taking ochem from him. Provides guided notes, does lecture reviews after each lecture (they are recorded), did an ochem prep set of videos before the course started that were VERY helpful. Tests are all free response, but he gives a LOT of partial credit. He is very funny, made lectures more fun. He made ochem very easy and straightforward.

Dr. Michaelis is one of the best professors I have ever had. If you're taking his class to jump through a hoop for med school, without the intention to really learn, then you won't like him. But, if you really want to learn about chemistry, there isn't a more passionate and caring professor who wants to help you learn! I would 100% take him again.

Worst teacher I have had among all the teachers I have taken at BYU, UVU, or my graduate school. He tries to be the cool teacher and seem laid back. It is a facade. I visited him in his office hours once and he was extremely rude. As another reviewer has mentioned, Michaelis's "office hour" lectures are so unfair for those who cannot attend. 0/10

Professor Michalis is as good as it gets here at BYU. His Ochem 2 class was great, it was very difficult but everyone knows that's how Ochem 2 is going to be. If you are willing to put in the time, and study hard using his notes and go to his reviews then you will do great. I would take him again for Biochem if I could.

The best chem professor I have had. His enthusiasm rubs off if you let it. He is very organized with his lecture notes which makes studying pretty easy. He doesn't believe in multiple choice tests, but this actually helps because he is pretty generous on grading.
A very difficult class was made manageable by him. His lectures were clear and his tests are very fair. Pay attention and go over the chapter notes and you'll do well.

Dr. Michaelis does a spectacular job at explaining the why behind reactions. which makes remembering and understanding organic chemistry a million times easier. I can't stress this enough Dr. Michaelis is truly an amazing teacher. Just remember to actively do the textbook homework, and reach out to him if you need help. He really cares.

Dr. Michaelis turned what could have been a very difficult class into a very manageable one. He does 2 reviews every week where he will answer questions and make up practice questions for you to do that will be very similar to the actual test. Go to his reviews and you'll do absolutely great!

Hardest class I have ever taken. 6 tests were 88% of grade. Study group saved me. We learned that other professors went slower, (we were studying in the library and the group next to us had a different professor and their class was a whole test-unit behind us) so we think he is the hardest ochem professor due to pure speed. Very available though.

Dr. Michaelis truly cares about his students. Obviously, Organic Chemistry is difficult, and there's no way around that. but he was so enthusiastic and so willing to provide help. He smiled the entire lecture long. He also provided bi-weekly review sessions to prepare everyone for the test. Truly an amazing professor.

Michaelis is great, but he makes his tests WAY harder than the rest of BYU's professors. He teaches the material well, but puts way too much emphasis on memorization and insane preparation for tests. This class will consume your life more than any other OChem professor. Overall, though, he's effective, clear, and fun. Just ridiculous expectations.

Worst professor I have had at BYU. I retook the class from a better chem professor and did well. Michaelis just wants attention and to be the "cool professor". His tests are so much harder than any other chem teacher at BYU (which is unfortunately saying something). His outside class review sessions are unfair for the students unable to attend. 0/5

Dr. Michaelis makes Ochem 1 super interesting. He gives clear note templates so you never have to worry about what you need to copy down from the board, you just follow along in the notes and fill them out as you go. He tries to give you all the help he can and holds valuable reviews and office hours every week.

I really liked Dr. Michaelis! He cares a lot about his job. He does weekly reviews where he spends an hour answering questions (probably because the class is so fast-paced there is no time for questions during class). He is willing to do extra work (like personally regrade your test if you don't agree with the TA) to help you succeed.

I found his teaching style to be a bit tough. He would go through the information so fast and dive into concepts that seemed more complicated than what we needed to know at the time. His class was very test heavy and they were extremely tough with no curve. I appreciated that he focused more on understanding concepts rather than just memorization

Dr. Michaelis is the MAN! Seriously, take him for Chem 351. Print off his lecture note templates and follow along with lecture, and definitely go to his office hour reviews. He is very understanding and wants you to do well. Test heavy, I think there were 5 but study and you'll do fine.

Dr. Michaelis is one of my favorite people! He is eager to help and is encouraging. That being said, his class is DIFFICULT. I spent easily 12+ hours a week practicing, and I could only pull a B+. Full confession, I had taken o-chem 1 at another highly respected university, but this course made the first look like child's play.

Dr. M is such a great professor. I enjoyed every lecture. You can tell he loves what he does. His class is hard but hes always willing to help. Just gotta put in the work. Would highly recommend taking OChem from him!

Dr. Michaelis is contagiously enthusiastic. You can tell he loves what he does and that makes a huge impact on his teaching style. Be aware that this is a very fast-paced class, with just about 0 time in lectures for questions. He invests a lot of time in extra-curricular review sessions. For this class, you get out what you put in!

You must listen to me. If you are taking ochem, take Dr. Michaelis. He's test heavy, and his tests are hard, but he really wants to be a good teacher, gives weekly content reviews, does not teach directly out of a book, and wants his students to succeed. There is no curve, but an A in the class is only a 91%.

I had heard awful things about ochem but the class wasn't bad at all. Of course it is chem so you have to put in a lot of work but not more than other chem class. He is hilarious and engaging. To do well pay attention in class, go to a couple of his review sessions and study for a few hours before the test and you will be golden!
