Honestly the greatest professor -- He helped me learn to love organic chemistry. He teaches in his own way, not a walking textbook, which I loved. Wasn't your typical boring professor. Awesome lectures, and I seriously enjoyed taking his exams. They were all free response, hard but really fun. You're making a mistake if you take it from anyone else

HE. IS. THE. BEST. PROFESSOR. He is so clear and so good. Last year I tried to take Ochem from Dr. Castle and I had to withdraw because he was boring, monotone, and basically I was failing because I didn't understand his teaching at all. Dr. Michaelis has changed my perspective on Ochem and I am so glad I took it from him. Read and do the problems!

Dr. Michaelis is a fantastic teacher. He is kind, energetic, and really passionate about what he does. He loves teaching and loves students. He has high expectations but teaches and provides resources accordingly. Do the assignments, go to his reviews, ask as many questions as possible. He will help!

Organic is awful no matter who you take it from. I started taking this class from Castle last year and withdrew because I just couldn't vibe with him. Taking it from Michaelis was the best decision I ever made. Do yourself a favor and take it from him, get to know him, and spend time working hard on the material. He will help you out.

Ochem is just a nasty class, but Dr. Michaelis did a great job of teaching the material. He goes out of his way to help, and he personally gives several review sessions a week. You have to work really hard, but he gives you all the tools you need to succeed. He understands that it's hard, and really wants to help students do well.

Dr. Michaelis is a little crazy, but he is a good chemist. He doesn't grade very harshly, but he is not always available when you need help during lab. He is usually helpful when he is there though. He makes the class more fun. I feel like I really developed my chemistry skills in this class.

Absolutely fantastic professor. Exams are worth 85% of your grade so you really have to know your stuff, but he leads review sessions three times a week so if you attend at least one of those per week (and study hard) you'll be in good shape for the tests. I feel like I really understand the concepts we learned, which didn't happen for me in 351.

Professor Michaelis really is on the students side. He wants you to succeed and to do well and he tries his best to help you in any way possible. He jokes around a lot but he's also really good at teaching and makes lectures engaging and makes you want to learn and do well. I LOVED taking this class from Professor Michaelis.
Awesome professor! Definitely who you want to take organic chemistry from. He likes to tease pre-meds a lot but he really wants all of his students to succeed.

I took Michaelis for both 351 and 352. He's a great professor who puts in a lot of time for reviews (he does them all himself). All of his tests are free response and are long and challenging but he gives very detailed review sheets and the material always comes from his class notes.

Dr Michaelis is a real peach! He holds office hours which is pretty much mini review sessions where he goes over questions and practice problems that reflect what he would put on tests. His tests are hard, but he really prepares you well for them if you put in the work. Hilarious and an absolute gem!

Dr. Michaelis is really funny and charismatic. His lectures were entertaining , but I didn't think he was a very good organic chemistry teacher. He doesn't teach challenging concepts very well, rushes through lectures, and doesn't prepare you for his tests. His office hours weren't helpful either. I highly recommend taking it from somebody else.

Dr. Michaelis is one of my favorite professors at BYU. Lectures can be a little tough to digest sometimes if you're not prepared. Overall though, he teaches well and tests fairly. He gives a spiritual/Michaelis thought at the beginning of each class, conducts several reviews weekly, and is just a good guy. He really just cares about your learning.

Dr. Michaelis is awesome. OChem is a hard class and his tests are difficult, but if you work hard he will make sure you're prepared. Go to his weekly review sessions and work with the TAs and you'll do fine.

Dr. Michaelis is the best. Seriously, take his class. He is so caring and personally holds several test reviews for each exam. His tests were fair, but very challenging in an intellectually stimulating way. If you are easily offended and a pre-med student, this might not be the professor for you, as he likes to make fun of premeds, but who doesn't?

Dr. Michaelis is the greatest science professor I've ever had. He really cares about his student's success and does everything he can to make Organic Chemistry easier to understand. He gives lots of examples in class which is really helpful. He's really funny and makes class comfortable and fun! Go to class and don't get behind.

Hes one of the most entertaining professors Ive ever had. Hes also extremely funny. He may sometimes be sarcastic and make fun of premed students but he loves us all. Hes also very willing to talk about anything you need, just schedule a time to meet with him. His office hours are basically extra reviews so definitely go.

He's a great professor, but all over the place. The book is important for concepts but not as helpful for his tests. Sometimes he lectures on things you will read like 3 chapters later, so attendance in lectures and office hours is crucial. I really enjoyed his class though and learned tons of great and interesting things.

Creates an environment where you want to learn ochem. It is still difficult but you can tell that he wants you to learn and do well. He understands that learning is more than a grade and will help you even if he has to rearrange his whole schedule. Straightforward and honest. Super funny. Started off most classes with random spiritual thoughts.

Dr. Michaelis is the best ochem professor at BYU!!! He is clear, an awesome lecturer, and prepares you very well for the tests. TAKE FROM HIM!!!! His ochem classes have a higher average end grade than all the other professors. He doesn't teach from the textbook but you'll need it for homework. Also, go to his office hours!! Very helpful!!

80% of your grade is exams. Office hours super helpful (GO WEEKLY!), lectures not as much so. Weekly in-class quizzes at the beginning of lecture. Ridiculous amount of time required to study/do homework, and then you're tested on concepts that sometimes haven't been covered. Consistently put in the time and you should be fine. Don't lose hope :)

Dr. Michaelis is probably one of the best teachers for the first part of O chem. The class grade really depends on the tests and they are quite difficult. He is good about having reviews and office hours but get ready to use them.

I never write reviews but Dr. Michaelis deserves one!  He's probably one of the greatest people I've met, let alone the best professor I've had at BYU.  Ochem is flipping hard but you will never get a professor who is as willing to help you out and wants you to succeed as much as Michaelis. Put in the work, go to his office hours, and you're golden

Dr. Michaelis is awesome and hilarious! I took 351 his first semester teaching it and he was very reasonable about correcting mistakes and working with students. Don't get me wrong, his tests are still very difficult, but doable if you work hard. We had 4 all free response tests and the cumulative ACS final. I loved his tests, hated the ACS final.
Dr. Michaelis is awesome. He is super willing to help his students and is hilarious in lecture. Take O-Chem from him

Dr. Michaelis is hilarious! He's a relatively new teacher, so he's still a bit disorganized, but I believe he will get better and better. He cares about his students and makes himself available to help. Attend lectures, read, and go to his office hours. The tests are VERY similar to the homework, so do it and do it well. An A takes a lot of time!

Fun professor, likes to make fun of med school students and tries to convert you to become a chem major. But thats most chem professors. He is a really fun lecturer and is always willing to help. just don't fall asleep in class or he will call on you to do a problem on the board, also don't wear sweatpants unless you are ready to be made fun of.
Fantastic lecturer, loves organic chemistry, covers everything in incredible detail. Tests are BRUTAL. Super nice guy, wants to help with anything he can.

Hardest class I've ever taken.  Yet, Dr. Michaelis is the most helpful, personable professor I've ever had.  He's also very passionate about the organic chemistry.  He really knows the material and is very helpful for office hours.  If you don't understand something, he'll explain it until you do.

Dr. Michaelis is one of the best professors I've ever had.  The class is hard with long, rough tests, but he does everything possible to help you succeed.  He is often available during office hours for help and review.  I don't think I've ever had a professor that cared more about my long-term professional (and personal) success.  Hard but worth it

Dr. Michaelis is a bro. Seriously though he is really funny and kind. I learned a lot in the class. 552 is a super hard class, not surprising since it is graduate level. However, it has an A- average so don't be afraid to take it. He's very helpful and explains things clearly. And he has a lot of free office hours which improved my grades a lot.

Fantastic Teacher! He is very personable, helpful, and cares about his students. He holds review sessions during office hours. Attend his pre-test reviews!!! He teaches the concepts behind the reactions and to me his teaching was very clear. Few people love organic chemistry as much as he does. Use all of your resources to do well.     Good Luck!

Organic chemistry is simply a hard class. Dr. Michaelis focuses a lot more on the principles and the "why", although he still requires that you memorize quite a bit out of his lecture notes and the book. His test reviews are extremely helpful and are guided by the test material. Take advantage of those, and use the homework problems to study.

Compared to my previous chemistry teachers, Dr. Michaelis wasn't that great. However, he was new and it was a summer term. Read the book and do all the problems. Go to class and take really good notes. Tests are difficult but fair. His tests unfortunately though only focus on few of the taught concepts.

For his first time teaching, he's actually pretty good. Do the homework problems in the back of the book to prepare for the test, and be prepared to be quizzed A LOT in lecture. But beware of his tests: they are all over the place difficulty-wise. Prepare as much as you can, but sometimes, just know that won't be enough to get a good grade.
Pushes you to become the best designer you can be, very supportive of student success.

Professor Morgan is the BEST. If you want to be an industrial designer you have to learn to take constructive criticism all of the time. Professor Morgan gives out constructive criticism in a way that is super helpful and with good intention. He really pushes you and his projects are no joke, but are also the projects I always learn the most in.
David is the coolest. His style is great, he is quite honest about your work. Be ready to be pushed. :)

His lectures don't help all that much for understanding the material. I feel like he could be a good research professor because he is hands off, but for a class where you need to go through a lot of hard concepts there needs to be a level of lecturing that he just didn't do.

He was ok. Explaining content clearly was a struggle for him, but I think it's because he's super smart and he was trying to explain basics to students in an intro class. Nice guy, just hard to follow.

I took astronomy, physics 121 for part of my physics credit, and this class was way too hard for a 100 level class. It's interesting material but the tests are SO HARD and the homework assignments were so confusing. The lectures are confusing but he posted all the slides after so that helped a little. I never felt prepared for the tests.

Tests were often on material not covered (even remotely) in class. Assignments were unorganized and often not labeled right on MAX to turn them in. Due dates were often changed verbally but not online, which led to confusion. Midterms took months to get graded. Everyone got a C's and D's on the midterms and he refused to curve them.Overall,not fun,

His lectures felt meandering, with lots of "ums", "well any ways" and other filler like that, and he lost a couple assignments of mine and just gave me a zero. Midterms weren't written well, and had really low averages, and took him (and the one TA who might have been helping) almost a month, and after finals had ended, to grade and get back to us.
Interesting class but tough professor. Be prepared to wait over a month to receive test scores back.

360 is an interesting class. I recommend taking it for anybody who is in condensed matter, optics, materials science, or astronomy research groups. The class is difficult because the concepts are difficult to comprehend, but the math itself is not bad. Dr. Neilsen is always a good teacher. Would recommend.

Taking PHSCS 321 from Dr. Neilsen is difficult, but it is worth it because he is a great teacher. I enjoyed the class because I learned more than I did in my previous physics classes but it has probably been my most difficult physics class so far.

I would not consider Dr. Neilsen's classes easy, but he is a good teacher who is willing to help you. Going to class might feel like a waste of time if you understand the reading perfectly, but he gives some good examples and explanations in class, so I would recommend going anyway.

Dr. Neilsen is one of the harder professors in the physics department. He grades on a strict curve (which usually raises your grade, ironically) and assigns a lot of tough homework, but he tries his best to be accessible and designs his lectures to give you the tools you need.

I loved this class but it was super difficult. I took 321 at the same time as 318 (from Van Huele) and that was the biggest mistake of my life! Combined there was about 40 hours of homework a week (I calculated it one week). Lots of reading and a reading journal which you can bring into the tests. The tests are timed for 4 hours. Loved this class!

Dr. Nielsen seems to design his classes to be ridiculously hard. This can be a good thing because it forces the students to make his class a priority, but it's bad because I don't feel like I learned nearly as much as I could have if he'd have focused on teaching us physics instead of helping us build character by taking hard tests.

He was very unclear and intentionally made this class incredibly difficult. The class average on most tests was around a 60% even though they were open book. He curved it at the end, but only 3 people got A's. The whole class had to use solution manuals to get through the homework. I would save yourself the stress by taking this from someone else.
Extremely nice professor with a great sense of humor and very willing to help. Unfortunately his class is ridiculously hard and his grading policy is very strict so only a few people get A's.

Only two out of about 30 students got an A in this class. Most probably received Bs. Lecture consisted mostly of thick, overcomplicated mathematical theory. The homework took so long each week that it is difficult to estimate how much time was spent. Tests were terrible. Easily the hardest class I have yet taken at BYU. Dr Neilsen likes it that way

If you were to read the words, friendly, self-motivated, easy going, and fun to be around you would see David’s name shortly after. Great Teacher who didn't let you get away with things, but helped you attain what you desired. I would recommend him to anyone that was looking to retain the teachings. He gets an A+ from me.

Prof Nelson's goal is to teach truth in the secular world & integrates teachings of the church in his lectures. Lots of readings but they are interesting and apply to the class lectures. The lectures are interesting, enlightening, and Prof Nelson makes them engaging and applicable to life. Clear expectations on papers, hard tests. TAKE THIS CLASS!

He is smart enough and the subject matter is all memorization but he adds an obscene amount of unnecessary politics into his lectures. It was very forced and what he was only bashing on was Left wing ideologies including feminism and LBGTQ+ groups. I just had a really hard time listening to him for 4 hours a week.

I absolutely loved this class. There were readings due every class, but you can get by without doing them if you attend class. His class is mainly lectures, but the lectures are very interesting and engaging. Nelson is so funny and entertaining. It was a pretty easy class. Tests are all multiple choice and papers are very clear and straightforward.

A fantastic teacher and passionate about his field. He uses the textbook as a supplement for his lectures but uses about 15% of specific in-class examples that are on the midterms. There are 4 exams, the 1st has 75 questions and the rest has 100. They aren't super hard, as long as you actually study the slides and book! GET STUDY GROUP! 3 papers.

Really solid professor! Assignments and tests are clear and straightforward and if you work hard you can get As. Go to the TA labs for the papers for sure! They'll tell you exactly what to do to get an A. He's super hilarious and tells awesome stories (that are sometimes on the test!) Super great class and awesome knowledge to take into the future.

I loved this class! It was so interesting and really useful in my life. Dr. Nelson is really funny and you can tell that he loves what he does. He tells all sorts of cool stories and makes you feel like you're in a class of 20 instead of 300! He does talk quietly, so I'd recommend sitting in the front.

I love this class because Dr. Nelson makes the lectures so interesting. He shows videos and tells stories from his family and others' to illustrate the topics. The reading is interesting, you just have to dedicate time to it before each class. The tests are straight forward if you do the study guide. Go to the TA lab several times for your papers.

His class was SO boring. I've heard the other teachers are good, so I would recommend trying to take it from someone else. The tests weren't too bad, but the lectures themselves were almost unbearable.

Professor Rasmussen did a good job of clearly communicating class expectations and reviewing material in class. He gave good lectures with lots of opportunities to practice the material in a way that prepared students well for exams. Highly recommend taking Comms 300 from him!
He is a great teacher! He is so caring and fun and gives lots of extra credit opportunities. There is hardly any work and the tests are easy and open note! Definitely take from him!

Incredible professor. This is a no brainer decision for taking Comms 300. Bro Rasmussen is kind, promotes interesting discussions, and is super organized. Homework load is very reasonable and super easy.

If you have to take Media Law, this is the way to do it! I'm so glad I took it from Professor Rasmussen. He was a good lecturer, learned our names, and I felt like I actually learned the material but wasn't ever assigned busy-work. You can use your notes on the tests, and if you show up you'll get an A. Take it from him!!

Prof. Rasmussen is THE teacher to take for Comms 300. He gave awesome lectures and gave proper attention to students. 3 papers and all 3 were graded really easily. Discussion post due every Friday and McGraw Hill assignments at the end. Show up to class and turn in your assignments on time, its an easy A. TONS of extra credit opportunities!

Canvas is super organized. He gave us exponential extra credit for the number of classes we showed up to in a row. Tests are NOT hard. The material is not super exciting, but class is still really fun!!

Professor Rasmussen is excellent!! He is adjunct, so he does it out of passion for the subject material. The week-to-week assignments are super manageable, and he gives ample extra credit. It is a blended course, but going to class made the exams much easier.

I enjoyed this class a lot, you could tell he really knows what he's talking about, and cares about his students. It was a blended course, so there was class once a week. If you went in person there were a lot of extra credit opportunities, but he also had a zoom option and recorded the zoom and posted the recordings as well. He was great.

Professor Ridge is extremely knowledgeable about scripture and history while being super humble. He focuses on the process of religious learning, devotion, and testimony building rather than forcing you to memorize random dates and facts. He is extremely caring and kind. Do the coursework, and you will learn something new and get an "A".

He warned us this would be the hardest religion class we take, but I thought it was the opposite. If you show up to class (30% of grade) and do the assignments, it's a pretty easy A. I really liked how we set our own goals and worked towards them, but I felt the class wasn't the most engaging and I probably would prefer to study the BOM on my own.
I'm sure he's a great guy but I'm not a fan of his class. I took it online and would NOT recommend. It wasn't very engaging and he didn't seem to care much about his students.

Prof. Ridge scared me at the start of the semester, said he would be treating this class seriously. He is a super easy grader and cares more about the process of religious education than just focusing on a grade which I respected. It is however, a little to easy to blend in and not pay too much attention in class.

Brother Ridge is a super understanding professor. I found his class super boring, and the homework assignments were incredibly repetitive. His class is easy, but the homework feels like busy work. There are no exams, but a big project at the end of the semester to teach a Book of Mormon lesson to someone. Overall, a good guy, just boring class!

Professor Ridge was a good teacher, but I found his classes a little boring. The homework assignments are extremely repetitive and are honestly just busy work. He is a good teacher and cares about his students, but I found that the way he taught religion was a little dull.

I found the tests hard and graded off of very specific details, but each of the four exams are worth about 5% so don't fret it. Assignments are graded basically on completion but were a great source of gospel insights and test preparation!

Probably one of the easiest religion classes out there. Yes there are 4/5 tests and lots of busywork, but he lightened the load halfway through. You need to submit your work on time. The real kicker was that the exams were hand-written with identification terms, summary, and essay. I found them easy.

There is a big workload. Homework is graded very strictly. Tests are based off specific things in his lectures that you could miss. Very wordy and hard to understand questions in homework. tests are multiple choice and free response taken in testing center.

Fantastic Professor. I learned so much about the Book of Mormon and he made it really interesting. There is quite a bit of homework, but if you make sure to stay on top of it then you will get a good grade. His tests are very reasonable.  He is willing to help and answer any questions you may have. I definitely recommend!

I love Professor Ridge. He is very real, he doesn't pretend to have it all figured out, he's open and very honest, and he really cares about his students. I honestly kinda started the class with a meh attitude, but he changed my mind. Fairly easy, 2ish hours of homework per week. You get out what you put in. Gotta study for tests, not bad though
Very genuine professor who is not a harsh grader whatsoever. Follows the same format of class throughout the entire semester and gives good study guides for tests.

I would HIGHLY recommend his Arab-Israeli conflict class. There is a lot of reading and the lectures are pretty dense. But he knows so much about the conflict and he is amazing at creating an environment that avoids tension and hate. He is very objective, and his goal isn't to change opinions. He wants his students to be informed and to care.

Professor Romney is a very nice professor and talking with him one on one helps to clear up many questions that students might have. 

However his classes are super heavy and unorganized. His lectures are very difficult to follow and he often assigns crazy amounts of reading, essays and tests that are way too much to ask of students.

He gets a bad rap bc of poli 300, but it's bc of the class, not his teaching style. He teaches and structures the class to help students learn. he is very knowledgeable, and accessible outside of class. He wants students to succeed, and if they don't, it's probably because they didn't put in the work. If you put in the work, you'll do well.

Seriously nice dude, but the workload is crazy. Expect 15 hours/week. He expects you to have a ridiculous understanding of statistics and doesn't explain things well. Generous curve (because the midterm average was a 50%. No, I'm not exaggerating). My A came at the cost of my sanity. I got lucky.

Probably the nicest guy ever but has no idea how to teach. Struggles to explain concepts and has very subjecting ways of doing curves and writing midterms. Exams are very difficult and are written poorly. Expect to spend 20 hours a week, maybe even more on this class. Very poor prof but nice guy

He teaches the class like it should have prerequisites. The weekly homework assignments took more time than all my other classes COMBINED. I hope that as he teaches the class more, he'll learn a better way to do it because he really is a sweet guy.

Doctor Romney is so awesome, the class is very difficult and I think that can mix into peoples feelings about him. He is always there for his students, will stay late or come to campus to meet with you. He emails back so fast and is flexaible for those who make an effort to reach out. The class is hard but he brings treats. Take 300 from him!!

Really nice guy, just a difficult course, and he is still nailing it down. He regularly incorporates student feedback and tries his best to help us succeed. The weekly problem sets take a LOT of time- think 12-15 hours- and they are super coding-heavy. Labs are really helpful, especially if you're having a hard time understanding the "lingo."

Romney is a great professor, but this class is time-intensive and fast, with 10-20 hours of homework a week; plan accordingly. 300 is a reverse-lecture course, so the readings are not optional. The lectures are primarily for answering questions and filling gaps in your understanding rather than teaching content. Use the TAs, and you'll be fine.

This professor cares about his students and knows a lot but cannot explain concepts simply or in a way that students could understand. Most of the time we left class more confused about the material. The lectures were confusing and consistenly lost the engagement of his students

Awesome professor! He's very knowledgeable about the subject matter and he answers any questions you have. Very friendly and really wants to get to know his students. He gives super good notes on assignments and he uses the feedback students give him to adjust his course if needed. Seriously one of my favorite professors.
10/10 recommend. He is always willing to help and gives great feedback. Classes and hw are geared to push you to think critically.

I loved this class and the professor. He genuinely cares about the subject and about being a good teacher. The tests are easy if you study and take notes during class. There is lots of group discussions in class. Very intriguing class.

I love Dr. Romney. He is awesome and super knowledgeable, and honestly one of the best professors in the department. The classes are filled with information, and Dr. Romney is communicative and super flexible. The youth and passion that he brings to his classes is commendable, and I have truly enjoyed each of my classes with him. Highly recommend.

He is a great professor even though it was only his second semester teaching. It was a LOT of information to take in under such a short amount of time. There are SO MANY readings. However, he mostly expects you to understand the main themes and ideas, not every single last detail. He gives a lot of opportunity for anonymous feedback.

He's a good guy and nice; this was his first time teaching the course so it was EXTREMELY scatterbrained. Once we were able to establish some guidelines for expectations it became much easier to anticipate tests and papers. There's a lot of reading, but you don't need to know everything. It's all about understanding the most important points.

Professor Seely is an awesome guy, super passionate about the New Testament and extremely knowledgable. He cares a lot about his students and is a very fair grader. His tests are not very hard at all, I probably studied for each midterm only an hour and averaged around a 95%.

Brother Seely knows his stuff but isn't great at teaching it. Lectures were VERY content heavy and we never got through a full slideshow presentation. We spent the whole semester trying to catch up, which created a disconnect between the readings and the lectures. Quirky guy, not super difficult class if you use the study guides.

Has like 11 pages worth of material in study guides on each test, a vast majority of the test isn't even related to the study guide making it hard to know what to prepare for. However his grading on every other assignment is very gracious. He does get pretty behind in lectures and rarely ever gets through a whole slideshow in one class. Quirky guy.
This class was the absolute best. I loved Professor Seely and his interesting lectures.

He has a deep testimony of Christ in the Old Testament and is hilarious. He doesn't always stay on topic, BUT always ensures we have everything we need for tests. Do the readings, go to class. For a fun religion class where you really dig into the scriptures together, take from Bro Seeley! If you dislike tangents take from someone less fun.

Took more than one class from him if that's any measure of what I think.
Yeah you might get tired of quirks, but he's a good guy who tries to help his students out and he knows a ton. 

Fun fact: I learned this from another class's religion assignment- sometimes he writes things in church magazines.

I loved Dr. Seely! He was hilarious. My class must have been tired but he dropped the funniest lines that no one would laugh at. He also has lots of experience with the New Testament. Lecture heavy, and we got behind. He is quite merciful, and the tests aren't too hard, I would do the readings and go over the study guide, but you'll be fine.

He is super funny and has lots of awesome inspiring stories....except we are always behind on lectures and never finish the study guide so you have to do a lot on your own. You actually have to study for the tests but if you do you will get an A.

I think Bro Seely was a good enough BoM professor, he often went on irrelevant tangents during class that put us behind, but if you did the work you likely passed. Assignments included: weekly reading checks + digital dialogs, 2 midterms + the final (not cumulative & weighed the same), 3 short writing assignments, and longer art writing assignment.

Brother Seely is a lecturer. If you prefer discussions, you won't get those much from this class. That said he teaches everything very clearly. He is respectful and highlights the heroines in the Old Testament

Brother Seely is super nice and caring, he is patient and cares about what his students are going through. Each class is a lecture that has a study guide that he goes through. He is very fair with tests and grading. He is a bit scattered when it comes to lectures but I still learned a lot and enjoyed his class.
Great teacher, even better person. Pretty chill and is willing to give extensions for work(don't abuse it though)

Brother Seely is an amazing person. However, I don't think that he's the best professor. I often found that i would come out of classes more confused than before. The study guides are not, in my opinion, the most useful for preparing for the exam

Brother Seely was a pretty good teacher. He gives you all the tools to pass the class as long as you try. He got behind in a bunch of my classes and tried to catch us up, and the slides were very numerous and kind of unorganized, but he did make sure to cover anything possible on the test, and his test prep sheets are super, super helpful.

Kindest professor you'll ever have. Passionate about the subject material, and very responsive to individual needs. Very lecture/reading heavy and he often got behind, but exams only tested the covered material. Tests were hard, but he gave very detailed study guides to fill out in class- test questions were directly taken from the guides.
THE BEST PROFESSOR YOU'LL EVER HAVE.
Just a really caring professor who is passionate about what he teaches and teaches in an interesting way. Sometimes we'd get behind but that was alright.

Amazing man. Hardest class I ever took. So much memorization of people/dates/events that extends beyond the Old Testament and the writings of Isaiah. Willing to accommodate and wanted us to become friends with Isaiah, but lectures were overwhelming. Lectures off of 50+ slides per class and oftentimes gets behind. Insane amounts of reading.

Professor Seely cares more about his students actually learning than just being ready for a test. Yes, the tests can be pretty in-depth, but he goes over all of the material in class, and is willing to boost the entire class's scores if he thinks the average is a little low.

Bro. Seely is SUPER kind, and accommodates, no questions asked. I submitted many assignments late and got full credit. All assignments are graded on completion, not content, so do the work and you will pass easy. Beware that he assigns quite a bit of reading and is lecture heavy. His study guides also end up around 30pgs per unit once filled out.

I absolutely loved Prof. Seely! I took his 9 am class this semester as a freshman. I thought it would be really difficult but it isn't. As long as you show up to class, take notes during lectures, write the response papers, and study for tests, you'll do great in this class! He is really funny and flexible, so if you have a problem, just reach out.

Of all the religion courses I have taken at BYU this has been the most difficult. I had more homework each week from this class than I did from my 5 engineering classes combined. It's a lot of reading, online discussions, difficult tests that quiz you on "who said what", and some short papers. He is a very kind man, but I can't recommend his class.
Brother Seely knows his stuff! So if you wanted to learn about the Old Testament- you will. Wonderful teacher.

Hes really nice and is passionate about what he teaches. He says he balances spiritual and academic but I didnt feel the spirit because during lectures I was filling out the long disorganized lesson study guides. Hes not a tough grader and gives most points for the written questions on the exams. Keep in mind this class is designed for seniors.

Only take this class if you actually love the Old Testament. I really enjoyed it and thought the lectures, readings, and tests were straightforward. Bro. Seely is definitely someone you can learn from.

He is very nice and cares about his students. However, he expects you to remember specific verses of scripture, who said what, and who really obscure people are from the bible. His study guides are 6+ pages long, so its not helpful or specific at all. I felt that I had to teach myself a lot of the time.

What a great dude. He tries to balance the spiritual and academic aspects of the gospel and does so very well. If you show up and do the reading, its an easy A. The study guide is a breeze, but he doesnt really cover it explicitly; he more covers the main stuff that are actually on the test. Reading is well-spaced. Tests are straightforward.

Brother Seely is a great teacher, but if you are looking for a class to get an A in, be very careful. The way it is set up is there are 3 exams (very specific/difficult - 650 terms of Quizlet) and one exam's points worth for attendance and if you have read. That means to get an A, you need at least a 92 or above, average, on each of the tests.

Prof. Seely is a nice person, but not a great professor. His lectures are very disorganized as well as the study guides, and slides. The only thing this is well organized is the textbook, that was written by a different professor (Prof. Pike) I experienced changes to the study guide, after an exam had opened! I got an A out of spite. Very annoying.

Funny dude with all of his stories. You can tell he loves what he teaches when he argues with himself not to keep rambling about some doctrine. He does get rushed because he doesn't use time wisely but overall a genuine guy. Fun class, relatively easy. Very little work required but you need to study for the tests.

Bro Seely cares so much about the students! He is very passionate. His lectures are a little scatterbrained and he would rather teach than start a discussion but he makes up for it with his personal experiences. He does all he can to make the class easier for you.

Brother Seely's passion for the BOM comes through in this class. I took a few classes from him because I love him so much. He's very sweet, has so many inspirational stories, and is extremely knowledgeable. Take his class. Some people complain that the tests are hard, but you can fill out the study guide with his PPs. A on test 2-3 hours of prep.
It's a great class, you'll learn so much about the Old Testament and you'll get a great deal of historical background along with the doctrine. He's funny and makes it all very memorable.

Perhaps not quite as enlightening as I hoped, but I do understand better why the OT can be so repugnant sometimes. It was good to review a lot of OT stories and learn some new ones. He had some mostly edifying, interesting personal experiences too.

Brother Seely is a great teacher. He removed the stress of BYU scripture trivia from his classroom. His lectures are insightful and entertaining. He posts his powerpoints on learning suite. As long as you read your scriptures, go to class, and do the study guide you will get an A, and be spiritually lifted. I would recommend it 100% of the time.

While Bro Seely is a very kind man, would not recommend his class. Took 10 minutes at the beginning of class to get to know the student saying the prayer. Very kind, but as a result, the lectures were always rushed. Had 3 tests total, including the final. Other grades based on attendance and reading. Study guides about 20 pages, way unreasonable.
Brother Seely was a great professor and was very caring towards his students. Great professor.

Exams have lots of scriptures you're supposed to memorize but no study guide to tell you a list of specific scriptures to memorize. All he does in class is read slides and say "We're so behind. We gotta be quick." etc. bad teacher. tough exams. boring class. I would avoid unless you like boring teachers....

Brother Seely is a seriously humble guy, but he knows almost everything there is to know about the Old Testament and how Judaism connects to the scriptures. He's a very chill teacher and it's a low-stress classroom environment, but I feel like I learned a lot from him. Take this class! His stories are hilarious and he cares about you as a person.

Brother Seely is awesome! His tests are a breeze because he gives a very specific study guide to go along with each lecture, and posts his powerpoints so you can go back and fill it out later if you want. He goes off on tangents sometimes, but they are always very interesting, and uplifting. Take BOM from Br. Seely!

Prof Seely is a great person! He is hilarious and has awesome stories. When it comes to the tests, there's barely anything on it from what he taught you. Its all based off of the study guide. Its probably the hardest Religion class I have taken at BYU. Again, great professor with great stories, if it was a pass/fail class....

I took old testament from Brother Seely and he is honestly a really nice guy. He wants students to succeed and will meet one on one with anyone. Unfortunately, over class he basically only covers like 25% of the study guide, so the rest of them you have to find on your own. I found the tests to be very challenging, worst grade i've gotten at BYU.

Brother Seely is the cutest and the nicest man on the planet.  He is such a genuinely caring guy, it's seriously a joy to go to his classes.  Yes, his lectures are very scattered, but all you have to do is have the study guide open on your computer and take down answers as he says them.  If you do that, the class is seriously a piece of cake.

I liked his stories okay but he tried to cram WAY too much into the course. I don't even remember much (if any) of it at all now. Tedious readings often weren't very relevant or interesting. I didn't get much of my huge study guide filled out during the actual class and had to resort to thoroughly going through power points.

He is the cutest man.  I do adore him, he's a really great guy.  He really wants the students to succeed.  He cares about all his students, and is really funny in class.  He is a riot to listen to.  He is very scatterbrained, however, but if you fill out the study guide during class you'll be fine and it's an easy A.
Lectures are very interesting and informative, although he usually gets behind with funny stories/tangents. You're expected to read a lot of scripture for credit. Tests are easy if you study.

His lectures are extremely scattered. He has hardly any structure to his class. Spends the first 10-15 minutes of each lecture talking to students and getting to know him. He has really bad handwriting and its hard to read what he write on the board. His scattered structure makes it hard to follow what he is teaching. He is a very nice guys though!

Bro Seely is awesome! He is the type of guy that we are all trying to become. His lectures are fun and he tells entertaining stories. Make sure you bring your study guide to class and fill it out every day and you will get an A. He is also very willing to help students out. I loved taking new testament from him. I learned a lot.

Bro. Seely is one of the greatest professors I've ever had. He is passionate about what he teaches and really is an expert. No one can match his lectures for information and entertainment. Bro. Seely changed my life. Anyone who passes up the opportunity to take a class from him is missing out.

Brother Seely is THE BEST teacher I have ever had in my entire life!  I don't like history, but his passion and excitement for the subject made me excited for class every day! He is always willing to go the extra mile to make sure his students succeed! In short, I would recommend him to a friend, to you, and I would recommend Bro. Seely to God!

I loved Bro. Seely's lectures! He always had awesome stories to tell every class! There is a LOT of reading, but I don't mind that. My only frustration was that he had one question per test about something he never mentioned in class or the studyguide. But I would definitely take one of his classes again! Just one tip: go through the studyguide!!

I really like Brother Seely. This class is a lot of work, but I learned so much. The best part is you know exactly what he expects of you on the tests. He gives great study guides. So you work hard, learn a lot, and get a good grade!
This guy is great. Study his review papers great and have fun learning from him cause he is great!

Great teacher! Take old testament from him! He knows so much and loves what he teaches. Only downside,there is a lot of reading. The class and the tests were easy. Everything that is on the tests will be on the study guide, which follow the powerpoints he explains in class.
He's a fun guy. I look him for both of my BOM sections. The final was quite easy. It took me 20 minutes and got 99%. Just pay attention in class and it should be a breeze.

Bro Seely is great! He loves what he teaches and that makes you love it too. He is always talking really fast but get sidetracked with stories so you get behind anyways, but the stories are worth it. It kind of gives him a sense of urgency that makes the class fly by, which I loved. Definitely taking another class from him if given the chance.

He is an extremely boring teacher.  Started this class days after my mission and he killed my desire to read the Book of Mormon.  He makes the scriptures more of a homework than enjoyable.  Would never recommend him.  There are many other way superior/interesting teachers.  He is also very boring and his tests are long and have massive study guid

On your mark, get set, go: Bro Seely is an energetic guy and has some funny stories. However, he takes so many pauses from the lesson to tell stories that it becomes frustrating, and his questions are usually "what am I thinking" type. He really does help bring the OT to life though. The reading assignments can be summed up with one word: TEDIOUS.

Professor Seely is a nice guy. His stories are funny, but he gets lost in them sometimes and it can be hard to follow the subject matter. He gives a study guide and will answer any questions you have about it; look at the study guide as soon as he posts it and bring questions to class. Grade is entirely tests and self-evaluated reading/attendance.

Dr. Seely has great stories.  He could entertain a wall.  I enjoyed his insights into the scriptures.  He did not get to the meat of a lot of chapters.  I felt like he could have focused on more important doctrines.  I liked the class

Is fun and entertaining, but also gets lost in his own stories and then falls behind in the curriculum which then requires him to rush through what he meant to teach. The test's can be hard because they often require "what we said in class" answers, and because he gets so rushed it's often hard to know what he was saying.

I look forward to going to class because Dr. Seely cares about the subject he teaches and about the students. He makes the class more enjoyable with his humor, stories, and personal application. I recommend this class.

Do not take from this teacher. Tests are extremely difficult and the things he tests on have no sigificance to the scriptures. With the number of religion teacher at BYU, I will not be taking from him again.

Brother Seely kept the class interesting and brought the Spirit. He is SOO smart! I would take a class from him every semester if I could. There is some work, do your reading, fill out the study guide and you'll ace it!

Why would you ever take a religion class from another professor after you have had one from Brother Seely? Some work, but a marvelous teacher. Really cares about the students and the class. Teaches with passion.If you do your reading, attend class, and fill out your study guide, A's all around!
FANTASTIC teacher. Classes are engaging and interesting. Really cares about the subject and his students. Tells stories that are applicable, and even entertaining. I highly recommend this teacher.

Rad. Yes there is a bit of reading and some work, but really fantastic. Cares a lot, tells great stories, and willing to do a lot for his students. Anyone who complains about this professor is clearly not willing to do work in COLLEGE.

Professor Seely is the man! I missed the midterm on accident and he was very understanding and let me retake it. He really teaches the old testament well, and whenever he's unsure of interpretation or studies he lets you know to take it for what it's worth. Thanks Bro. Seely!!

Very good teacher.  Just write down what he says in lecture, do the 12+ chapters of reading for each class, and study every little thing on his review and you have an A.  You WILL do more work in this class than any of the other 'required' religion classes.  I spent at least 2.5 hours reading for each class. Good man, and want to help you.

Fantastic professor. Really knows the material and teaches the background, doctrine, and application. Really cares about the students. Very funny in class! Has great stories. Do the reading and fill out the study guide and you'll do well.

The Seelys were phenomenal teachers who really inspire the desire to learn. However, the class covered A LOT of material in depth but still skimmish. I spent an average of 6-8 hours per week on readings, and about 10 hours studying for exams. The exams cover lots of material, but nothing that isn't on the study guide is on the test. Excellent prof!

ENTHUSIASM!!! Professor Seely is a spectacular teacher. Every day is an adventure in his class. He provides excellent overviews, integrates class information with student interests and lives, and describes his extensive personal research and travel to make the material come alive.

The Seelys are nice; however, the assignment load was   heavy, repetitive in some basic content, and overly detailed in others. The tests were mostly memorization.  The lectures were interesting but poorly organized.  We never finished anything despite the rapid pace.  Also, they changed the class so that it started earlier, then often went over.
I took both Honors 201 and 202 from the Seelys and I loved this class! It is a lot of work, but if you stay on top of the assignments the tests really aren't that hard. Highly recommended.

The concept of the course is fascinating. It's execution is less so. It took me half the semester to figure out the unique lecture style.  Both of them are highly knowledgeable scattered. Instead of detailing significant events they try to skim 3000 years of history. This class gets a mixed review.  Some parts were good some parts were def. not.

Crazy crazy crazy! He tries to cover everything really fast and ultimately never does. I often wondered what was going on and mostly sat in class and laughed at how lost I was. He makes up a study guide for the test that is HUGE and then asks questions about less than half of the material. The other part of the test are things you have never seen.

This class is a LOT of work, but as long as you keep up with the readings you'll do well. The Seely's are really great people as well as excellent teachers (even if Brother Seely does talk really fast).

Amazing class!  Highly recommended.  Keeping up with all the reading is difficult, but it is worth it; it is interesting and makes you feel cultured.  The Seelys team-teach the class and they are excellent.  I learned a lot.  You write a 2 page response paper every week or so and a theme journal in which you trace a theme throughout history. take i

He's a really nice guy & always happy to help. But, he talks super fast & jumps around a lot. It's really hard to follow what he's talking about. He does give study guides before tests, but there's TONS of questions, & only 20 will be on the test.  Also, I don't know where he gets the study guide questions cuz most aren't from lecture! He expects a

He rambles to no end and at the end of class he kind of just tries to sum up everything that he missed! However when the tests come around he hands out an awesome study guide which tells you absolutely everything that you need to know on the test and alot of other things too! Not very easy tests, if you dont like going to class :D Overall well done

Dr. Seely was one of the best professors I've ever had. Very passionate about his subject, and really loves his students. The readings are always relevant, and the study guides for the tests, though they sometimes take some time to do, help you learn more and do well on the tests at the same time.
Professor Seely raised a fine son. His classes were good too.

An amazing professor.  He is passionate about the subject matter and teaches it in a way to get the students excited about it too.  Applies teachings in a very real and useful way.  Care a lot about the students.

Bro. Seely is passionate about the subject matter, knows a ton, and cares a lot about his students. This class is a lot of work, but I learned a ton, and Bro. Seely was very good about pushing back due dates when we were struggling to keep up. He talks really fast sometimes, but he's so excited and cute that you just have to love him.

bro seely and his wife team teach this class. they are very nice and try to get to know their students. for an honors class its not that hard. you have an essay about once a week. and there is alot of reading, but if you do the study guides the tests are managable. class lectures are alittle unorganized, but good.

He was awesome.  It is true that he speaks quickly and rushes sometimes to get through the material, but he teaches a lot and is very passionate about it.  His Civilization classes taught me a lot in a very spiritual light.  He is moderately hard, if you do the required reading and go to class you will have no problem.

This class changed my life! Prof. Seely and his wife team taught and showed me how to view history, art, and literature in an entirely new manner. I grew spiritually in this class because the professors challenged my way of thinking. The class is difficult, but doing the reading and attending class will allow you to perform fine on the tests.

I really liked this class. I didn't know anything about the old testament and now I know plenty. I can see how this text really affected other scripture. Bro Seely is a fast-talking guy who always seems to be behind, but when test time rolls around, you will be fine as long as you took lots of notes
This teacher was very knowledgable and made class fun and interesting. He is very helpful to the students and is available for questions whenever you need him. Plus I thought he was funny.

I took Dr. Seely for Teachings of Isaiah in 2000 or so. He knows his material and presents it intelligently and enthusiastically. It wasn't an easy course, but he taught the subject matter so well that I couldn't help but get excited about the subject too

I really don't like this professor.  He has way too much information he wants to cover in a class period. Usually, we are always behind and he never covers all he wants to in class. To compensate, he talks really fast...

This class was a great introduction to the field of urban planning. Prof Simpson has a lot of expertise and teaches well. He's not at all strict and I think I got 100% on everything except the midterm and the final. The reading are definitely not necessary, just go to class and take good notes because the final exam is open note.

Simpson is great and always tries to make the classroom environment fun. The class is easy and helps you learn the basics of urban planning. There aren't many assignments, just a couple projects here and there. Relatively easy grader if you follow instructions.

Prof. Simpson is a great professor who has a strong expertise in urban planning.He provides in class exercises to solidify more the reading and material learned.He gives assignments that are fair.He grades fairly. He assigns readings which are essential for learning and understands the lectures.He is the man for those interested in Urban Planning.

Professor Simpson is super nice and a great guy, very knowledgeable, but not very organized. I didn't do a single reading and was totally fine. Projects were pretty easy, but graded randomly specifically. He doesn't have slides or anything and canvas was disorganized. Great guy, easy class, but not the most rewarding and I didn't learn very much.

Dr. Simpson is brand new at BYU and is still figuring things out. He knows his stuff when it comes to Urban Planning, but is not the clearest grader. His rubrics are kind of ambiguous. If you are not sure, just go talk to him. He is very kind, and is very helpful and understanding if you actually take the time to go talk to him.
Provided a great introduction to Urban Planning and inspired me to look further into it.

I took this class for fun and to learn more about urban planning but it was a waste of my time. The professor never graded anything on time and the rubrics were ambiguous. He would essentially just assign you a grade based on his opinion. Ended up with an A- even though I never missed a class or assignment. Nice guy but unfair grader.

Take this class with Sims for sure. The course itself isn't astoundingly interesting, but he tries his best to make lectures funny. There were no essays, most of the grade was exams and lab assignments. There is technically required reading, but "required" is a strong word if you know what I mean.

Probably the most organized professor I've ever seen, this guy was on top of EVERYTHING. Super easy to work with, and cares a ton about his students. Frequently brought his classes to tears during his lectures, and knows a lot about his subject material. The class is brutal, but it's curved at the end so it's not as bad as people say.

This class was the most inspirational class I've taken at BYU. The entire class sets up a beautiful message and call to action. Almost every class brought me to tears because of how touching it was. The tests are not too bad. I'm so glad I took this over Econ 110. I'm proud to be an American
He did a great job of teaching American Heritage. The class was pretty easy. His lectures were interesting and engaging, it's very important that you go to those, your labs, and the review room.
This is just a hard course regardless of who you take it from. He doesn't have essays though which is nice. At first I hated his lecture style but it grew on me.

Professor sims was an excellent professor. There are a lot of readings but no writing essays. Lectures can be boring but he genuinely cares and is passionate about what he teaches. Go to the TA review room. If you study and do the readings you will do fine on the exams and final.

Least favorite class I've taken at BYU so far. Lectures were so boring and exams were unreasonably difficult. Lots of readings.The only good thing about this class were the TA labs and reviews. I studied for hours every single week and still did terribly on the exams. Avoid taking American Heritage at all costs.

I had him for American Heritage! He makes a tough class enjoyable. Great lectures and didnt make me absolutely hate the class lol. If youre going to take American heritage take it from Simms! Work load isnt as heavy compared to other profs

Dr. Sims is the best of the best for econ 380! He is funny, engaging and answers questions extremely well. He also takes time each class period for a break and talks about current events and how they play into economics. His tests are tough but if you do the homework and study it the class becomes easy.
David is incredibly smart and always provides good feedback and explanations. 380 is a difficult course but he makes it very manageable for anyone to be able to handle the class.

I loved Dr. Sims! I thought he was really funny and taught pretty clearly besides his handwriting lol. The homework is hard but if you do it in groups and go to TA hours its not too bad. It's also really similar to test problems so is great practice for that. The tests were also hard but all got curved and the class as a whole was curved as well.

Textbook is not needed. Lectures don't even follow it. Do hw in TA hours with others. Lectures don't make a lot of sense, but if you can decipher his handwriting, he posts his lecture notes. Review/rewrite the lecture notes outside of class-this saved my grade and understanding. Weekly assignments take anywhere from 1-10 hours. One paper-not hard.

The first third of this class, I did not love it and had a hard time understanding Dr. Sims' lecture style. However, after the first midterm, the class got so much better and I actually really enjoyed his lectures. The tests are tough, but they're curved, and I highly recommend going to the TA office hours.

Great guy, just a bit tricky of a class to teach with vigor. A solid choice if you're looking into any 400 level classes, its just a bit monotonous at times. Tests are simpler than other econ tests (more writing out about general principles and not so math-focused). Super accessible outside of class and really cares about us overall. Group project.

Professor Sims was incredible! American Heritage gets a bad rap, but it's been one of my favorite classes. Slides are available outside of class, but the exams and weekly quizzes are much more difficult if you're not familiar with what Sims emphasized. He can move quickly through important topics, so utilize the TAs/exam reviews. Know the syllabus!

I stopped attending lectures and doing the readings halfway through the semester and started doing better on the Exams. The powerpoints and going to lab are really all you need to pass. Lecture was boring

American Heritage with Doctor Sims was brutal. The course consisted of weekly quizzes based on the textbook readings and in class lectures. The TA review rooms are the only good thing about this class.

Professor Sims is the best! His lectures are super interesting and he does a great job at keeping you engaged. A lot of people say AHTG is this awful class and it is honestly not bad at all. I didn't do a single reading all semester but went to the TA review rooms and was fine.

The class is heavily weighted toward the tests, so if you do poorly on those, you will be in trouble. I was inspired, as a graduating Senior, to better fulfill BYU's mission to go forth and serve. The class is not as bad as people make it out to be. I would recommend taking it later, because you will probably get more out of it.

I might be crazy but I LOVED American Heritage from Dr.Sims. I found his lectures inspirational. It is quite the class in terms of effort required to get a good grade. My biggest advice is GO TO THE REVIEW ROOM EVERYDAY. That seriously was my saving grace, the TAs are all amazing and the 15 minute reviews helped me understand what was important.

I took Dr. Sims for American Heritage, and he was ok. His lectures were very boring and he hardly deviated from what was on the slides. I also didn't like how the tests were weighted so heavily, I didn't do well on the first midterm and it screwed me over for the whole semester. That being said, the TAs are extremely helpful. Go to the Review Room.

beware the 8 hours of required service!! Class had SO MUCH READING I could never finish it all. Weekly quizzes suck because they're due thursdays at 8:00 am and you always forget about them. There are 4 essays based on films, and the lectures don't always make sense. He also moves through slides way too fast for you to take any notes. good luck
DO NOT TAKE FROM DR. SIMS HIS LECTURES ARE SO BORING AND MAKE NO SENSE AND THE TESTS ARE EVEN HARDER UNLESS YOU ARE GOOD AT HISTORY AND ALREADY KNOW A LOT THIS CLASS WILL SUCK
Don't pay attention to the slides as much, pay attention to what he's specifically saying. Memorize all of your notes for the tests...

For someone who doesn't know much about political terms, this class is making me less inspired to learn. The readings are getting so hard to understand and the lectures even make me more confused. I wish the lectures were there to help with class concepts and be more relatable. But it's just so confusing and makes me frustrated.

The lectures were actually fairly interesting, but I felt like they didn't help much with what was on the exams. Mostly the readings help with exams, only problem is there are a million readings. There are a couple short papers, and a few required films to watch too. It's just a big time commitment and brain strainer.

Not too difficult, lectures were interesting. If you took the practice tests and reviewed the homework, it was pretty easy to get a decent grade on the exams. Would recommend for an econ 400-level elective.
Prof Sims gives great lectures and his class is structured very clearly. It's a hard class but he explains concepts well, so you if put the study time in you will get a decent grade

Only reason Sims' ratings are low is because he teaches American Heritage. Take Sims without fear. Great class, good choice for a 400-level course. Class is relatively easy without being painfully boring. Sims is a good lecturer and I felt engaged in the class (I usually don't). Papers are not scary, didn't require immense effort.

Dr. Sims is great, his rating should be higher. ECON 380 isn't an easy class, but he makes it manageable and provides a lot of resources to do well. The problem sets are pretty hard, but they are helpful with tests. Take from him! You won't regret it!

I thought this class was fair. The homework was the most difficult part of the class, but he lets you work w/others and ask him/his TA questions, so it's not too bad. Tests don't stray too much from the homework and his lectures. My only complaints are that his handwritten notes were hard to read and he made us buy a textbook we never used.

Dr. Sims is a legend! Labor econ may not sound like the most interesting of the 400 level classes, but this is one you should for sure take! Totally possible to get a good grade and he is really on the students' side

Professor Sims gives great lectures. They are engaging and interesting. I found when I did the assigned reading consistently, I was able to get a lot more out of the lectures. There are weekly quizzes in lab, daily reading, 3 essays throughout the semester, and 2 tests. Stay updated on the reading, attend labs, and the tests will be manageable.

Dr. Sims is a good choice for American Heritage. Get ready to work in this class and take it seriously, but American Heritage really isn't as terrible as people make it out to be. His lectures were interesting and easy to listen to. The American Heritage TA's are a really good resource too for doing well in the class.

Fantastic class. AMHER has a tough wrap here but it was one of my favorite classes. Dr. Sims uses tons of videos in his class which help you visualize things. He conducts the class in a kind way and is pretty straightforward. Lectures come directly from the reading so do that and pay attention and you'll be fine. I definitely recommend him!

This class was amazing for me because it was basically doing the reading, paying attention during lectures, and reviewing for tests. There were 3 essays, but overall there's little homework besides the reading. Lectures were super interesting and I wanted to show up. Sims requires less reading than the other profs and only makes you buy one book.

Prof. Sims taught me American Heritage. He really knows what he is talking about and explains things very clearly and logically. He clearly cares about how the content he teaches will affect students longterm. He's funny and shows you the real-life, practical application of what you are learning. Take AH from him!

Professor Sim's lectures are interesting but his tests don't reflect what he teaches. They pull from a ton of content and it is very hard to anticipate what will be on them. He does not provide study guides. Overall this class is a lot of reading and a lot of stress! AHTG 100 lives up to it's bad rep!

Dr. Sims is a good professor, but I often felt a little lost in the class and there wasn't a lot of clear guidance on what to expect for the tests. He is very fair with grading though, and because he curved the class I got a good grade. He is very intelligent, but sometimes his lectures could be hard to follow.

Dr. Sims is a great guy, and outside of class he was really helpful. But his lectures were probably the hardest I have ever had to follow. The textbook was super math heavy with little explanation, and his lectures didn't really help me fully grasp the concepts. The subject matter is really interesting, but get ready to do a ton of calculus.
I didn't like his lectures, they always seemed dry and very confusing. 10 minutes with the TA usually taught me more than an hour and 15 minutes did with the professor.

Sims is fun to listen to and really cares about the studentsstats is a bit dry. Lectures are solid, but not super well-organized. Textbook can be rented for $20 online. Practice midterms are greatdo them. Weeklyish homeworks, and problems from the homework and textbook appear verbatim on the exams. Notecards during the exams are really helpful.

Excellent way to take Stats - lectures are a little dry (but let's be real, it's a stats class). Notecard for tests, straightforward homework (which sometimes appears verbatim on the tests). Best way to take your "pre-388" class.

Sims is a great teacher. He gets excited about what he's teaching. He's really available for student questions and easy to talk to. I found his lectures super interesting but I'm into labor econ. There's way less math in this class and it's not that hard. (5 math problem sets. 7 article readings & questions. 12-15 page partner research project.)

I was so afraid to take American Heritage, everyone has heard of the horror stories of this class, but I was shocked to find that this has been one of my favorite courses I have taken at BYU. Dr. Sims was amazing at presenting the information through a different lens. Loved it, would take again.

I had heard horror stories about American Heritage but I think Sims was a great choice. The reading and assignments were manageable, and his lectures were typically pretty interesting. He'd always incorporate video clips or activities. It wasn't my favorite class but he was a great option for it.

Professor Sims was very good about making the course less scary than everyone says it is. The syllabus is very clear and you can tell during lectures that he cares about the subject and wants to make it interesting. The only criticism I had is that the readings often didn't line up with the lectures. Make sure you work hard to keep up with the text
Dr. Sims made lectures interesting and I learned a lot, but his tests were super abstract and very difficult. Also there were extremely detailed quizzes every week. This class hurt my GPA. :(

History is really hard for me but Professor Sims knew what he was doing when he taught American Heritage for the first semester. He's not so good with getting across what information he will be testing for, but the TA's really come in handy. It's so important to go to the TA lab. That's what makes or breaks your grade.

Solid professor, created good lectures and did a good job explaining concepts. Friday labs are super important so be sure to go. Readings were pretty long, and there were weekly quizzes at the labs over lecture and readings. Since you have to take the class, I would definitely recommend Dr. Sims.

Overall a generally tough class, with lots of info to know, readings, etc. but I really liked him as a professor for it. Very nice, caring, fun lectures, and I like the way the class was structured. You'll need to study well for the quizzes every recitation and the tests, but his lectures were great.

This was the best professor to take American Heritage from. The class is hard by default but the lectures were entertaining and Dr. Sims taught in a clear way. The TA labs are very important and have attendance/weekly quizzes. The essays were fine but the tests were difficult no matter how hard you prepare for them. I enjoyed the class material!

The lectures were fairly unorganized and hard to follow. He covered enough material that I felt prepared when I started ECON 388, but you really need to know how to follow his logic. He's helpful to students who need it, but with his style of teaching, you're going to need it. If Stats don't come easy for you, take it from another professor.

I have never felt like I was struggling in a class before, but honestly, his lectures were so dry that I was nearly falling asleep the whole time and I was bored out of my mind. The tests are not just bad, they're brutal, but you get a note card which is essential

I seriously love Dr. Sims. He explains concepts well and is enthusiastic and fair. He posts class notes online which you can print out beforehand. Homework and tests are difficult, so I worked with my TA quite a bit. I would recommend taking 378 from Sims!
Great teacher.  Material can be a little difficult at first but it's pretty straight-forward, put in the time if you want an A.

Professor Sims was an excellent teacher when it came to teaching a very difficult subject. His teaching made topics very clear and he was very willing to stop and answer questions when asked. Very good teacher, I would take a class from him again, but not 378.
I took Econ 378 with Prof Sims, and he is by far the best economics professor I have had so far.  Very helpful explanations in class, and everything is very relevant to the material.

He is very smart with statistics so some of his answers to questions can be confusing. You can use a 4x6 notecard front and back for the midterms and two of them on the final so you don't have to memorize anything, just know concepts. It is a very doable class as long as you keep up with it.

I like the guy, but he isn't personable at all. Good luck asking him any question - you'll come back asking twice as many, that's if you can even understand him. The TA completely saved me in this class. She was great, and I learned all of the material through her. He is the type of teacher that will make exams harder is the class is doing too well
Dr. Sims is a good guy and the class was palatable, definitely not a life changer, but overall a good experience.

Surprisingly tough. Expect to spend a good amount of time on homework and test prep. Use Microsoft Publisher for your note card. And always be ready to take a crazy anti-derivative, like tan or sin or something on the test.

He didn't have a TA so if you are used to doing your Econ hw with the help of a ta your out of luck. He gives lots of busy work like reading long, terribly boring papers which he gives you questions which are almost always ambiguously asked questions. Not a good class to take unless you really want to learn labor economics. You have way too much work a midterm final and a 388 style final paper to put a cherry on top!
Dr. Sims is funny and interesting to listen to. Unfortunately he can be hard to follow at times. If you work with the TA's you will be ok.

Professor Sims is very passionate about what he teaches, which make the lectures as interesting as possible for the subject matter, but I didn't feel that he had a good understanding of how the class was doing the lectures were difficult to follow. If you aren't a math major, I would suggest another professor. Otherwise, go for it.

Tough class.  He moves pretty quickly but the homework and past exams prepare you well for the tests.  TAs help a ton in getting you to understand the material.  He is a fair grader and willing to help.  Just a tough class though.

Very difficult class. An introductory stats class should be a required prerequisite. He goes so fast in the lectures that sometimes its all you can do to take notes, let alone comprehend what he's talking about.  However, you are allowed to turn in the homework as groups, and take a notecard into the tests, which helps given the difficulty.
Great teacher.  He explains difficult concepts quite clearly.  The class isn't easy, but is manageable if you go to class and study hard.

Professor Sims is an excellent professor.  I got a poor grade in his class, but it had nothing to do with his teaching style.  I learned more from his class than I have in many of my other courses.  This professor cares that his students learn the material and he makes you work hard for a good grade.

He has good energy for the subject. The TA is crucial for the homework as the material covered in class alone usually is not enough to do it. Some test problems come from the homework and he gives you 2 former exams.

Dr. Sims is way hott. He is also very kind and helpful.  He made several exceptions for me which helped me out a ton.  If you need any help go to his office and he ismore than happy to help.  He has a dry sense of humor and is a total nerd, but I love it. Class is hard, but if you work hard you will do well.

He is very excited about econ. He doesn't always explain things very clearly, and the way he writes on the board is hard to take notes off of. The homework/tests didn't seem to correlate to the lectures very well either. He is very willing to help outside of class though. Don't buy the textbook, you don't use it.

I really like Dr. Sims. He is a very nice and willing to help outside class. He even sacrificed his own personal time if you need  help. He has a great passion which is what I really abmire. Take his class if you have a choice.

Dr. Sims' has the disadvantage of having taught a difficult subject to mostly IR majors. Though I like him personally, he did not help me much with his teaching. The test, generally, were quite difficult, as were the homework assignments too. Just be prepared to work really hard, and live in the Econ TA Lab.
Professor Sims is a great teacher.  Some lectures are more interesting than others, but overall it is a pretty good class.  I would recommend this class and Dr. Sims as a teacher for sure!
The best econ professor!  Very willing to help outside of class. He loves the material and treats the students well.  The textbook is crap, so you have to go to the lectures.

He was so enthusiastic about what he was teaching.  He had so many real life examples.  He was always willing to help a student in need and made sure everyone understood before moving on to the next topic.

Dr. Sims is a great teacher.  He does an excellent job of gauging whether students understand the topics he is teaching or not and is able to present things in different ways to help people understand.  The subjects are boring, but he tries to apply them to the world and I enjoyed his classes.
Pro. Sims is a fun teacher teaching boring statistics. He makes the class fun and is very helpful.
Good teacher, sometimes too theoretical, but enjoys teaching.  Not easy, but curved.
Sims is a very intellectual teacher and does a great job at bringing real life examples into lectures. He provides enough opportunities to learn concepts outside of class. Very fair grader.
It was very clear and I understood very well the concepts.  He will take the time to explain things and easily persuaded.

tough class, but he will teach you what you need to know to make 381 and 382 a breeze. Make the sacrifice, it is worth it. You can basically phone it in on 381 and 382 if you take the time to really learn what he is teaching you. It takes effort, but as econ professors go, he is not really harder than most.
No Comments

He's a very bright, goofy MIT grad.  hard tests and homework.  You don't have many opportunities to grasp the concepts before you are tested on them.  Most of the class doesn't understand what is going on.  Take Lefgren.

Class was fine. Professor tried to come to the hospital to give me my final the day after I had my baby in an emergency C-section at 32 weeks pregnant.
