Super weird, every other professor was very accommodating and did not try to come to the hospital the day after I had a baby in an emergency situation. He was difficult to work with.
There's not much to say. The class wasn't hard. Just listening in class pretty much guarantees you a B. And a couple hours of study before the exam and it's an easy A.

I loved my class with Dr. Dave! Physiology is a challenging course that requires studying outside of class, but it is clear that Dr. Dave genuinely wants his students to succeed. He explains the material clearly and is always accessible during office hours. His TAs are also excellent and provided very helpful review sessions before each exam.

He's a really good professor, with good lectures and tells you EXACTLY what you need to know to do well on the exams (learning objectives, not necessarily the slides). The final is 40% of your grade and each midterm (3) is 10%, which is kind of rough. The only other thing is that we were often way off schedule which could get stressful.

Staying on schedule is not his strong suit, but he does make class engaging. Oftentimes, we would finish content and then the test would open the next day which is a little stressful. Attend class and the TA reviews as those are helpful. He records lectures so watch them back when topics get confusing. EC is available which is helpful.

I had the privilege of working with Dr. Thomson in his lab for 2.5 years. If you stick with him, he will stick with you. No one will push you and help you grow more than Dr. Thomson. His attention to detail and ability to explain concepts is unmatched. I would take any class I could from him. He is excellent.

If you don't care about a schedule, this is your class. I don't think we were ever on schedule. We would be learning new content when the test opened. That was incredibly stressful and frustrating. Other than that he's cool. He'll go off on tangents about things and has some cool stories. The final and tests are weighted pretty heavy

TAKE FROM DR DAVE. He is a caring professor and is great at explaining different concepts. And he provides really helpful materials to make CELL305 easier to understand. Don't look at the TB it's way too dense and doesn't help at all. Just use youtube and chatgpt to explain the TB concepts. But he lets you get points back on exams thru corrections!

Not my favorite teacher but he was very entertaining and fun. Most of the grade is exams so I just reviewed the slides a million times until I had them memorized. There's a textbook but I never used it so don't buy it lol. Good amount of extra credits. In class quizzes but often he would drop questions or have them be group work.

Literally the worst class I have taken in my entire time at school (I am in my last semester). The professor is a great person and an expert in physiology but somehow is so bad at teaching that not only does he cover the stuff required for tests at the most surface level, but he falls behind by multiple units and then the schedule falls apart.

Dr. Dave is awesome! Cares about his students and the material. The class material tough but he records and posts every lecture, and there is a review before the exams that are extremely helpful. He has office hours weekly and is so great at working with students. He is a fair, honest, and all around great professor!

Great professor! TA reviews tell you everything you need to know for his tests. He typically gives a moderate curve on every test and lets you replace your lowest midterm with your score on the final. Attendance + class prep is graded.

Dr. Dave is awesome! The class and material is hard and challenging to learn. But if you put in the time and effort you will do well. Dr. Dave wants each of his students to do well, he will give points back and opportunities to do better. Don't buy the textbook, I didn't use mine at all. Go to the TA reviews, they are very helpful.

Dr. Dave is funny, caring, & excited about what he teaches. Exams can be difficult but lectures, online resources, & office hours are helpful! Quiz every week & 75% class attendance required. Lots of opportunities for some extra points though and Dr. Dave wants you to succeed! Overall, a challenging class but not impossible and super interesting!

Professor Thomson was an amazing professor. He always took time to explain material to students and made his expectations for us very clear. His class is test heavy, however, he is very generous with giving points back to the class. Coming from studying for the MCAT this class was easy. I spent 10 hours of studying throughout the entire semester.

Don't take from this professor! Worst professor I had at byu. Doesn't explain topics well just reads it, tests are extremely difficult (every ? which is not, all of the above, 2 or 3 are correct...) designed to make you fail. Exams worth 80% of grade. Insane amount of material required to know every slide/diagram shown in detail. Just ridiculous.

I do not like this class, it has been set up for COVID-19 and his in-person lectures are useless. They make me stressed out, and waste time because he has you watch them before class. His recorded lectures are also scattered and so hard to learn from. I wish that there were more than just tests/quizzes on the grade as well.

Super great guy that cares about his students. He helps students understand the most missed test questions, posted videos (during covid) that really helped prepare students for the in class quizzes, and made past tests available for the final. He's one of my favorites and is super knowledgeable about physiology!
I thought he was a decent enough professor. I wish I would have taken the class with a different professor--I just really hate in-class quizzes.

Dr. Dave is one of my favorite professors ever! He cares about the success of his students and loves to answer our questions. He is truly an expert at what he teaches. I love that he updates his lectures and makes new and improved slides each semester even though the content is generally the same. Take his class!

Dr. Thomson is an okay professor. The lectures are clear enough that you can do very well in the class without outside material. I'm not a fan of Dr. Thomson as a person. While I know several students like him, I thought he came off very egotistical and I heard uncomfortable stories from students in his lab.

This class was more work than I expected. Exams were 70% and in class quizzes were 20% of final grades. I thought the textbook went into the level of detail needed to understand the material for exams (I did extremely well on exams - I credited this to the textbook more than lectures). Final was 35% of our grade. Very scattered class discussions

I really loved taking Physiology from Dr. Dave! I didn't use the textbook much, only once in a while on homework assignments. Dr. Dave does a great job of explaining the material, and offers a lot of extra credit. A huge percentage of your grade is based on tests, but if you succeed on the mini-exams and go to TA reviews, then you will do fine!

I 100% recommend taking physiology from Dr. Dave. Although quizzes can be somewhat specific/hard, it forces you to keep up with the material each week. Tests were generally straightforward and he gave opportunities to make up points. He is a laid back guy and make class pretty entertaining. Definitely easier than I expected.

Professsor Thomson is pretty chill and laid back. He has study objectives that he expects you to know by the time class comes. You will have mini quizzes each week so if you study the powerpoints from the previous week you'll be ok. He makes it bearable and easy to learn physiology.

Dr. Dave is such an awesome professor. Physiology is always gonna be hard, but he does a great job of teaching and making sure we have opportunities too succeed. Make sure to STUDY, because there will be weekly mini-exams that are worth a good chunk of your grade. Definitely made physiology super fun to learn!

Dr. Dave is amazing! He is a great professor and tells you what you need to study for the exams. Definitely go to the TA reviews before each test, and they will help you out a ton! Just memorize the lecture slides/TA review slides and you'll be set for the tests. There is a lot of material but Dr. Dave is a fun and engaging professor!

Dr. Dave is the best! If you study the slides from class you will easily do well on weekly quizzes and exams. Exams were straight forward and not tricky. Plus he curves each test and has a lot of extra credit opportunities. He is very accessible outside of class and his lectures are very entertaining. Also, there was no busy work which was amazing!

I really enjoyed Dr. Dave's class, even at 8am! He gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit that are really fun! His tests are difficult, but you do very well if you attend class and study his slides (of course). He makes physiology interesting and fun. First time in a while I felt a professor was really on the student's side. Take from him!!

Highly recommend!! Weekly homework isn't hard but is a lot of reading. Weekly quizzes aren't bad if you study the pptx slides which are available to you. Only used the book for homework and memorized the slides for tests. It's difficult but definitely doable if you study. He's funny, entertaining,knowledgeable and has very helpful open hours!
Interesting lectures, but sometimes his tangents go way too long and they don't help you at all for the exams. Go to the reviews, they will help a ton with the exams. Tests are extremely hard.

Dr. Dave has strong opinions. He's a good guy though. He is fair. I learned a lot, especially about insulin (super important!). There's a quiz every week, a 6-page research paper , a presentation on said paper, and 3 exams plus a final. It's honestly not too bad. Repro with Arroyo was slightly easier, but this is a solid capstone choice too.

Dr. Dave is a great guy, but I don't think I'd take his class again. His tests are SO hard. I feel like he's trying to trip you up which just isn't cool. I am totally happy to study as long as the tests aren't purposely designed to make me fail. I taught myself 80% of the material, and the TAs are useless.

Dr. Dave is the best! You can tell that he really loves teaching physiology. I learned so much from him. This is a hard class and you really need to put in effort, but Dr. Dave will be there to help every step of the way. I highly suggest keeping up on all the material and all the assignments. There is A TON of material, but it is so good.

What an awesome class! Dr. Dave is the man. He has a way of explaining physiology really clearly. This class is difficult and covers a lot of material but the weekly quizzes help you keep up if you're disciplined in preparing for them. Plenty of humor mixed in to keep things interesting. Highly, highly recommend. I learned a ton and had fun too!

LOVE DR. DAVE! He is so fun and only stresses the material you NEED to know. We have a quiz every Thurs, so go to that class at least. I wouldn't miss class though, it's a pretty detailed course. There are 3 midterms and a final. The final is cumulative, but if you get a better grade on the final than on a past MT, he replaces the midterm grade!

Dr. Dave is the Man! He is super friendly and he makes his tests and quizzes friendly too! There are mini quizzes small HW assignments and Tests but he gives you extra credit. He gives you a study guide and if you know everything on it then you WILL get 100% in the class. Great guy and great classs!

The class is set up well. Mini exam once a week were you can miss one and still get 100%. Semi regular readings and quizzes on the readings that are very easy and not harshly graded. The tests can be tricky. You've got to know the material well. As a lecturer he is  really good. He makes it interesting and get you to care.

Overall I liked the class. I loved that Dr. Dave always seemed happy and excited about the material. Sometimes the slides were confusing and the material was rushed but I felt that Dr. Dave always tried to be fair. He also let's you go over some common missed test questions to try and get some points back. You can get an A if you study hard!

Dr. Thomson was amazing! His class was definitely tough - weekly quizzes and tough tests. But his lectures were so funny and interesting. He also really cares about his students and will go out of his way to help you. Go to test reviews - they help SO much!

Dr. Dave is laid back. He gives lots of chances for getting a good grade. He is always open to help people who will ask questions (in class, abt class paper, etc.) His grading is always clear. I received a grade that I felt I earned for every assignment based off the rubric. Discusses current science and encourages students to do so as well.

Excellent course. A TON of material is covered throughout the semester, but Dr. Thomson makes it digestible and enjoyable. No book is required, and any assigned is very light. Exams are fair and usually curved. The research project can be a doozy if research and academic writing is foreign to you, but most people are able to handle it fairly well.

Dr. Dave has tons of chances to make up points in his class, which is a god buffer for his weird test questions. He asks a lot of "which of the following is NOT true" type questions. He is an awesome lecturer though and teaches you about life, not just a subject. You can make up your grades very easily from the exams though. Take from him!

I loved taking this class from Dr. Dave. His tests are straight from his lectures and are not terribly difficult - if you study, you'll get an A. His lectures are entertaining; he has a unique sense of humor and does not hesitate to state his opinions. Take this class from Dr. Dave!

A lot of assignments (even extra credit) to boost your grade. He is there for you and makes that super clear. Look over the powerpoints and know them well for the tests and you should be fine. In class quizzes every Thursday. Amazing guy though!

Take this class as your PD bio capstone!!! Endocrinology might not be every bodies favorite class but with Dr. Dave it will become one of your favorites. Class was always interesting tests are straight forward and Dr. Dave is always awesome. TAKE THIS CLASS.
Love, love, love!

Dr. Dave is an amazing teacher! He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. There are mini exams at the end of every week. There are three midterms and a final. On all the midterms are bumped up to have the highest score be the 100. You will learn so much from Dr. Dave. EVERYBODY SHOULD TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM!!
Dr. Dave is on of the best professor I've ever worked with.

Dr. Dave is the best! He is helpful and entertaining and more than generous with curving grades. He also takes the time to learn all of his students names, which is more personal than most other professors at BYU.

Tricky wording on in-class quizzes and tests. There were timess I knew the material but had no idea what teh question was. GIve a packet, but you defnitely need to take notes still! There is alot on tests and quizzes that are not in the packet, which is what bothered me the most. 4 tests+1 final. The final was the easiest. Cool guy.

Like what others said, he does go off to a lot of tangents, but everything you need to know is in his study guides. His TAs are very knowledgeable too, but I feel like the labs accompanying this class is a waste of time.

I cannot imagine a better professor to have.  Dr. Thomson cares about how each student is doing and has organized his class to allow every student to succeed. Dr. Thomson is helpful, knowledgeable and interesting. Take physiology from him.

Dr. Dave is awesome! This class is well organized and interesting. The lecture was great, but I felt that the accompanying lab was a waste of time (and unfortunately, mandatory). I'd definitely recommend taking Physiology from Dr. Dave!

Dr. Dave is the man! His class is very well organized and he gives you a sheet at the beginning of the course telling you EXACTLY what you need to know for each exam. He gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Easy A if you go to class and study a bit.

Thomson as stated before does go off on a TON of tangents which leaves the class scrambling to cover the material. He went to Japan & his TAs were out of town for the first test(which was also over conference weekend)leaving us feeling unprepared, and the final was a cramfest towards the end to see if we could get to all the slides. It was hard.

Thomson is a great Lecturer but his class was pretty tough. You will learn alot in his class but his quizes and tests are pretty tricky. If you put forth effort you can get an A, but Ive heard that his class is tougher than other Physiology professors.

Very friendly, laid-back teacher. I felt that his overall ability to teach the material was a little bit sketchy at times. I also didn't appreciate how he went on so many tangents, that we weren't at all prepared for the final which had about 35-45% new material, which we barely went over because he got side-tracked all semester long.

Very nice guy. Overall somewhat difficult class given what I've heard from previous semesters. This sem we had 21 reading assignments with questions due, 13 in class quizzes, 3 midterms and a huge final. No EC offered. 2 points per class period, so attendance is almost mandatory. Great guy, but changes teaching styles so often, it's unpredictable.
Great teacher, tough material, but easy to get an A in this class. Good guy

Very good teacher! The material is tough but he makes it very possible to get an A. Just go to class(which are usually pretty fun anyways) do the readings, and go to the reviews. Tests are not bad at all, great teacher, great guy.

He is very nice, helpful, and listens to the suggestions of his class. Tends to get sidetracked during lectures and fall behind on the syllabus a lot. Has weekly mini-exams and daily reading quizzes. If you don't go to class for these they'll eat away your grade. Slide handouts are given in class. Tests are tough. Study the slides. TA reviews help.

He is an awesome teacher. PdBio 305 is not hard in general and that goes for this class as well. Just study the PowerPoints and go to class to take the easy easy in-class quizzes. He really tries to make it interesting and has a great sense of humor and love of life. Wish he taught more courses!(very straightforward and fairly easy tests)

Honestly Thomson is one of the best teachers at BYU.  He provided slides so we didn't need the book. His lectures relate to life and are interesting. He understands pre med students and the grades they need and did everything to help get what I deserved (plus he helped a little). It's a hard subject, but he is the best teacher you can get for it.

Cool Guy,  Great with helping you outside of class during office hours! Gives a little Extra Credit 6 pts- But You should ask for more. Curves ea test, U have to go to class b/c u will have a quiz worth 4pt. 2PT is ur name other 2pt are 2 questions related to last class. HIS TEST ARE REALLY HARD STUDY UR POWERPOINTS & all the questions he Gives u
Really great prof.  Really cares about his students and wants them to learn.  Willing to go the extra mile for you if you put in the effort!
i think he is one of the best teachers at byu. he's good at making things understandable and i like how he answers your questions

Tells you exactly what to study, don't have to memorize as much as in other classes. Offers extra credit, bumps test grades up, easy in class quizzes (2 pts for writing your name), open book blackboard quizzes. obviously cares about students and topic. good teacher. answers questions well! take it from him

One of my favorite teachers I've had at byu. He tests on what he teaches in class, not on random textbook facts. Really wants his students to do well. I learned a ton and got a good grade as well. Definitely recommend taking from him.

Awesome Professor!  His classes were fun and applicable.  He offered quite a bit of extra credit.  Was very fair with grading.  Made his class low stress, but I learned a ton from it.  Grades were made up of about 10 quizzes, 3 tests, and a final.  Didnt use the book much (used old edition also), but used PP slides.  Definately would recommend him.

I loved Professor wingate. He is very passionate about what he teaches and wants us to feel the same. This class is relatively new so there were some minor issues along the way but he always wanted feedback to make the course better. I definitely will look for chances to take courses from him again in the future.

Great guy, lots of interesting topics in this class. He is really good at interacting with students in class and making sure they understand. This class is as tough as you want it to be. If you want to learn a lot about ML and probability, gear up for some long nights. If you want to coast and get an A, you totally can, but you'll waste your time.

The labs are difficult if you don't know a lot about coding. His exams are open note/open book which is nice. There's lots of homework due each week which but they don't take that much time to complete if you get help from TAs. Overall, he's a decent professor and I would recommend him for cs 180.

Wingate is easily my favorite professor in the CS department. He is super excited about ML/DL so you'll learn a lot from him in that area. I really enjoyed my Deep Learning class that he taught and the projects weren't super hard but they were very fulfilling and fun since they are kind of on the edge of being state of the art.

Dr. Wingate knows his stuff. In 180 most students haven't taken very rigorous classes yet so he did a great job of dumbing down ML for non-calculus/programming students. He's super flexible with the workload. Even so, I learned more useful stuff in this class than any other programming class I've taken. Also, funny guy.

The course is very disorganized, however prof Wingate is one of the best teachers I've had at byu. He really does want you to learn and will take time in class to go over any questions. He is very considerate of due dates and will not make anything too overwhelming, which for a cs class is very rare. Take him.

This course is very disorganized. The difficultly levels of the assignments are all over the place. There were two labs in the middle of the semester that were extremely difficult and than other assignments took something like 30 minutes to 1 hours to do. He knows his stuff when it comes to data science, but this class is all over the place.

Dr. Wingate is the best professor at BYU. I wish he was my dad. He has a way about teaching that makes you interested in anything. He brings humor and the gospel to every lecture and you learn so much. The class is hard but doable. The TA's are very approachable, they wrote the labs, and they know their stuff.

Dr. Wingate is an excellent professor--he is passionate about the subject and cares about the students. He's just an all-around great guy too. I loved the format of the class--no tests, just a lab every week. I wish I had the chance to take more classes from him.

He's so awesome. He can teach you anything. He loves his work. I would recommend him to anyone. He's super understanding about situations, and is always willing to help. He is on the busy side, but he will always make an appointment with you if you email him.

Dr. Wingate was awesome. Very funny, very good lecturer. Definitely recommend taking a class from him. We were guinea pigs for a newer 330 class so that made it a little difficult, but he was great (Dr. Morse was too, btw).

Profe David is the best! Took him during spring semester and he is so caring. He explains well and helps us to look deeper at each subject. He's one of those professors who cares more about what you get out of the class than your grade, that being said, he is an easy grader. He finds ways to relate all things to the gospel!

Professor Wiseman is the best. He really loves his students and cares about the subject. There is a lot of reading but if you go to class and pay attention, he helps you a lot on the tests. Great teacher.

Professor Wiseman is SO nice. He is so understanding and cares so much about helping us become better humans and more understanding of different cultures, especially Spanish ones. He is so intentful and very accommodating. He cares about the well-being of his students! He's taking a break from BYU right now, but when he comes back, take his class!

Never met the guy in person but you can tell he cares so much! His class is very structured, however, I did often find myself wondering why I was doing some assignments because they didn't feel necessary. I have a hard time doing class online, so that was probably it. There are lots of assignments and readings each week. Assignments are super easy

This class was more spiritual than some religion classes.The way Prof. Wiseman put the class together I felt like the material actually applied and connected to life. If you want to walk away from a class as a more open-minded person and not just to check a box, this is the class for you. Weekly readings, discussion boards, and papers not tests

This class was very structured, and I enjoyed the material a lot. The midterm and final were both papers, and I much preferred that over exams. He knows a lot, and the TA's are pretty flexible with late work.

He is one of the most genuine and kind professors I have ever had. The structure was easy to follow and even though there was a good amount of coursework, it all felt impactful. I learned a lot and felt inspired throughout the semester by what I learned. I absolutely recommend taking a class from him, even if it's just online.

Professor Wiseman is the greatest teacher I've had at BYU. He is so kind and is incredibly aware of the needs of his students. He is really inspiring. The structure of his class is set up really well. I have learned so much and haven't felt too overwhelmed. If you have a chance to take from him I would definitely suggest you take that opportunity.

Prof. Wiseman is one of the best professors I have had. The way the course is set up is very organized and allows you to plan and study well. Prof. Wiseman also gives good lectures and is very compassionate and knowledgeable. I really enjoyed the material and felt that this class benefited me and my future. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!
This class was super easy and required very little of me while still imparting some interesting perspectives. You have to buy the book, but it is very easy to get a good grade in this class.

Wiseman makes the material super meaningful and the class was very fulfilling! I honestly don't understand how anyone could write a negative review about him lol. Loved the material and loved him as a teacher!

Professor Wiseman is 100%, without a doubt, my favorite professor that I have had at BYU! He genuinely cares for each of his students individually and teaches it in a way that even those who hate reading will enjoy the course material. I am very self-conscious about my speaking but he creates a welcoming environment for everyone to participate.

This man might change your life. He is the most caring professor I've had, especially for an online class! You can get by with an A by BSing things but don't. He gives opportunities for you to apply everything you learn to your life in a spiritual, intellectual, and character-building way. Take this class for Span certificate!
Professor Wiseman was the best! I had him online and he was super great to interact with. It is an easy A and I mean really easy. His online format is the best I have ever had.

This was my favorite Spanish class. Professor Wiseman really helped me to stay calm throughout the semester and understand that everything will be ok. He really wanted us to succeed. I loved the set-up and organization of the class. Literally the best professor I have had, and I haven't even met him in person.

This was an amazing, learning-focused class that had just the right amount of work. Prof Wiseman cares about his students and is helpful and flexible. There is a lot of reading, but it's not excessive. Small assignments, discussions, participation and effort, and a few papers. Would 100% recommend - plus it's not going to stress you out.

Profe Wiseman is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He cares more about education rather than grades. He gives readings and assignments that I found inspiring and worth-wile, and not just busy-work. He was also super caring and involved for an on-demand course. This is an educator, not just a professor, would take again any day!

He was so nice and overall a great teacher. Even though the class was online he was a very involved teacher and would frequently comment on the assignments that I submitted. He made us feel like he really cared about us. His lectures were fun and not boring.

This was an on demand class, so I was worried at first but it was AWESOME! Profe Wiseman cares so much about you and you can tell he means it. The papers (one for midterm, one for final) aren't too bad as long as you don't procrastinate. Keep up with the course (it goes by week) and you'll do great!

This guy is amazing. It was an online class so I wasn't able to interact with him in person, but I could tell how caring he is. He really mixes spirituality with learning. He's so caring and I know he'd do anything for his students. Take this class. The only hard part was putting together some longer papers, but it's an easy class besides that.

Dr. Wiseman is the nicest man on the planet. This class was super easy, but so uplifting and interesting. Like, you can do all the coursework in a day if you want. The readings are sometimes a lot, but you can skim and do well.

There are a lot of reviews on here that are pretty confusing because I had a great experience in the class. Dr. Wiseman is really approachable and from what I saw in the class he really showed he cared about our learning and success. There is a lot of reading in the class, but you can get by if you skim it.

Profesor Wiseman Is probably one of the best professors ive had in my time at BYU. He was super considerate of making assignments worthwhile and he did not assign so much work that the class felt undoable. Amazing professor, would recommend to anyone!

This was on-demand class that really didn't demand much from me. It's an easy A. If you are looking to learn a lot and apply yourself and grow intellectually, this isn't the class. That tends to be the case with on-demand classes, but I imagine that Prof. Wiseman's class isn't that challenging in person anyway.
Wow. Best professor I've ever had. His focus is on the students and their progression. He values all opinions and he makes it clear that he is on a learning journey with us.

I don't know why David has any less than 5 stars. His teaching oozes with sincerity and importance. He cares much more about you and your positive experience in the class than nitpicky things about grades and he's totally willing to give you leeway if you run into personal challenges. The class organization was also awesome in my opinion. 10/10!

Honestly was so surprised that his rating is this low. Really awesome guy. I took him for both 339 and 355 and he was incredibly kind and taught well. While visiting him in office hours, I never felt like he just needed to be done with me. Took the time to help. Genuine dude.

David was a great teacher. This class was an easy A but also very uplifting and very well structured (very important for an online class). David is one of the most genuine professors I have ever had, and I really respect him for his perspective and the motivation he gives students. He also always gives positive feedback on weekly reflections.

Great class and great prof. The most attentive and understanding prof I've had at BYU and it was an online/on demand course. I was taking a full course load while working and living in CA +Im lazy (hence the B+), but an A was easily attainable. I think I turned in every assignment late and he was the one messaging me to make sure everything was ok!

Professor Wiseman was one of the best professors I have had a BYU, and I've been here for almost 5 years. He is extremely helpful and caring, and he gets that his class is not the most important thing in our lives but just wants us to learn. I constantly found myself really enjoying his class, and each week was enriching! 10/10 would take again!

Professor Wiseman is the best! I honestly which every professor was like him and understanding of the current situation. He really cares about his students and really allows students to think about the literature. I would take another course from him because it really helped me. You will not regret taking a class from him.

I love this man. He genuinely cares about his students. It was an on-demand course, but whenever I sent him a message with a question, he responded back within minutes. Grading is relaxed because he actually just wants you to learn and grow as a person. I have never felt so cared for by a professor and I never even met him in person!

He is amazing! I took this class as an on-demand course. It was organized super well, and the content was always meaningful. He is clear with expectations and is not a tough grader. He genuinely wants to help students progress. Great professor! Take this class from him!

This was the best class I've taken at BYU. Everything was on-demand and pre-recorded, but you could tell that he genuinely cared. When I was doing my assignments, I felt like I was doing more to just check a box; the readings were relatively easy and really make you think about Hispanic culture. All tests were open-book essays which was also a plus

It was online, so all pre-recorded. We didn't have long lectures, but rather he had like a 10 minute video before each section of the homework. He really cares about his students, and you can tell that he is trying to help us grow - not just give us a grade.

He is literally the best teacher I have ever had and if he ran for president, I would vote for him in a heartbeat. His lectures are focused on Spanish culture, but in a way that makes you ponder and rethink even our own culture. It is seriously like philosophy mixed with Spanish, in an amazing class with an incredible teacher.

Prof. Wiseman is kind and understanding. He has said multiple times that the most important part of our education is us and not our grades. He is really lenient if you are struggling and is such an easy grader. As a Spanish major, I can say it was one of the easiest (too easy, hence the 4 rating haha)and least stressful classes I have ever taken!

This was hands down the best class I have taken at BYU so far. Professor Wiseman is so inspirational and caring toward all of the students in his class. He doesn't teach just to cover material; he really wants to help his students become better people and be happy in life. He's always willing to help and is never critical. I would highly recommend!

This guy's ratings are really skewed for some reason. Yes, his Spanish is kind of annoying to listen to, but his class is SO easy and he really focuses on individual growth which is awesome. This class was like taking a deep breath and trying to change for the better. Wiseman is very inspirational and he's a good guy in general, solid choice.
Honestly one of my favorite classes that I have taken at BYU

Professor Wiseman is honestly the best professor I've ever had. He cares so much about his students and wants the best for them. He will help you and work with you when you run into any sort of problem and he really focuses on helping you grow as a human being. Not sure why theres bad reviews!! Do not have enough good things to say about this man!

I don't mean to sound dramatic, but I would go to war for this man. Professor Wiseman is one of the most kind, understanding, compassionate individuals I've ever met. His course--which is laid out so clearly and follows the BYU AIMS so exactly--was inspiring and personalized. Far and away the best professor I have ever had in my life.

Dr Wiseman has been my favorite teacher and it is not even for his personality (not meaning that in a bad way or anything). He set up the class in a way that it followed the aims of BYU. I actually felt like I could apply what I learned. He made me want to do the very best because it was relatable. He was the most understanding of all of my teacher

David is seriously one of my all time FAVORITE professors at BYU, he completely changed my outlook on life. Class structure was great & he taught me so many life skills that I still use. Almost didn't take it from him bc of these negative reviews, but I am SO glad that I did. He's super caring & accommodating. One of the best that BYU offers.
David Wiseman is one of the best professors I've ever had at BYU. He cares about his students and is always very prepared for class. You will NOT regret taking any class from him!

He's a baller! Super cool, his classes are honestly super inspiring and not too difficult. You do have to put in work, but the work is honestly pretty enjoyable and you can apply it all to your life. He cares a lot about your personal growth and spiritual progression. He is super clear with his instructions and cares for his students. take him!

Dudes, this guy is THE BEST. honestyl i dont know whats up with his rating cause it does not reflect him at all. He is super willing to work with his students (can get extensions on stuff). He does not assign a lot of busy work. all of his assignemnts are super clear and not hard if you just put some work in. he's Great. take his class for sure.

He is awesome! So nice and willing to work with students. Really cares about the students learning and progress. He will answer all your questions within a day of asking them. If you do the work required, which isn't a whole lot, you will get an A and love the class. Take him! Also, a super spiritually enlightening class.

This is my second class with professor Wiseman. I only took another class with him because it worked with my busy schedule. I think the saying goes, if you cant say anything nice, dont say anything at all. I will stick with that. My rating says it all.

Dr Wiseman is the man, he's super nice, I took him for 321, 355 and 451 and really enjoyed it. It was so nice to just know that you could get an A if you just meet the basic requirements. I only bought 1 of the super cheap textbooks that he used and was totally fine. He's super understanding and extended a deadline for me when my life got crazy
I hate this class with professor Wisman. He is unkind and frustrating. I can never speak to him without him acting upset. I wont take another class with him.

Do not take this class at all. You will regret it. Wisman is a typical dude, but I did not like his teaching. Classes are so boring. Too much reading and no feedback. I concur that his Spanish is hard to listen to. Take a different class.
The type of class is interesting, but the professor was the worst thus far. There are many professors who teach this class, so avoid Wiseman. He always seems unprepared.

Despite the ease of this class, I had a hard time because of prof Wiseman. He just was not helpful when I needed it most. He was never in office hours and gave very little feedback on assignments. His classes felt boring and lackluster. I agree with some people on here that his Spanish stinks.

Stay away. There are many better professors in the Spanish department. I have taken a few classes. Wiseman is frustrating to students. He is often late, and does not seem to care about us. I will not take another class with him.
I am not a fan of this professor. His class always feels rushed, messy, and at times disrespectful. I would avoid.
this is the wost professor in the Spanish program at BYU. I agree, as a native speaker, that his Spanish is unbearable and hard to follow. I wouldnt take him again. I don't like his class at all.

Professor Wiseman is the best professor at BYU. Period. You will not meet someone who cares more about a student's scholastic and professional success than David Wiseman. Those who are complaining about his Spanish skills are obviously lacking in overall Spanish comprehension and only understand when everything is spelled out. Take his class!!
I think this is a horrible professor. Terrible Spanish. Chaotic syllabus. Seems rude. Not timely. Avoid.

Professor Wiseman is one of the best Professors I have had at BYU. He cares so much about the students and about your personal growth, it was so refreshing to have a professor like this. Your level of learning is entirely up to you, if you want to stretch yourself, you can, if you don't want to, its up to you. Such a great class.

This is the worst professor I have ever had at BYU. His Spanish is so hard to understand, making it difficult to follow instructions. I asked three of my classmates if they thought the same thing, and they confirmed it.

Professor Wiseman is amazing; I haven't met a professor that strive to teach so closely to the BYU aims and mission. He's not afraid to change things up and to have a little fun. He understands the reality of college and his classes were so inspiring and felt like an escape. He wants to see that you try and care and is always there to help.

Professor Wiseman is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is caring and considerate; you can tell that he cares about each one of his students. If you ever have the chance to take a class from him, do it!!
Go to class. Pay attention. Participate. Do the readings and the assignments. This class is one of my favorites I've ever taken because of Profe! If your'e going to take 339, take it from David.

Fabulous class. I recommend this professor to all my friends that take Spanish classes. This was class was more spiritual than my religion class and I learned a lot. I left every class with a mind full of ideas. Dr. Wiseman actually cares about all of his students actually learning about life, not just getting an A in Spanish literature.

Spiritually uplifting. He always connects the class material to the gospel. He has good Spanish, so not sure why there are so many haters below; ignore 'em. Only critique I have is sometimes the assignments given are vague and he gives little direction on what he's looking for. What you take out of this class is what you put into it.

Super nice, loves teaching, however I felt more spiritually uplifted than intellectually uplifted. Good if you need an easy class; you won't learn much about literature unless you take this class from someone else or go on to take the higher level literature classes. Despite what others have said, his accent is much more tolerable than some others.
Great professor! I loved his class. He really want you to do good. He has a vision for his students that goes beyond the classroom. I was in Spanish 339

Professor Wiseman was great, the class is not hard at all there are just a lot of readings but they aren't too bad. He is very flexible and will work with you, he basically asked us if we wanted to have a final. I thought he was great.

I am a senior at BYU now. I have taken classes with tons of professors, and in my opinion, professor Wiseman is by far the worst. He does not seem organized, prepared, or very knowledgeable on the literature he teaches. He is also hard to understand when he speaks Spanish. It seems like he makes lots of grammar mistakes. Avoid his classes.

Professor Wiseman was one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He helped me enjoy learning. He always offered to meet one on one and he truly cared about each student's success. Such a nice guy, and the individual project we had taught me SO much. I would definitely recommend him to anyone!

It is hard for me to say anything positive at all about this literature class and professor Wiseman. I just did not feel this professor knew what he was teaching. He seemed lost all the time and it drove most of the students crazy. I would discourage all student from taking classes with this guy. His bad Spanish doesnt help at all.

Prof Wiseman really cares about all his students and is always available for help outside of class. I didn't particularly enjoy the material from Span339, but he at least helped me to learn other concepts and especially to become more open minded and a better overall thinker about concepts. It isn't a tough class, but Prof Wiseman opens your eyes.
This class was beyond boring. If you can get over the gringo talk, you might be able to make sense of the frustrating lectures. Stay away!

Professor Wiseman comes extremely prepared to class. Some of the poor comments that he received are utterly false. He is one of the best professors I've had. He's open to hearing new ideas and is never hostile, nor does he impose his own opinion as the only right answer.

There really isn't anything positive to say about this professor. Once you get past the subpar white guy Spanish accent, you have to try to sift through the confusing lectures. I often found that this professor contradicted the class readings, making me think he did not know what he was talking about. I expected more from such an educated man.

Nice guy. Cares a lot. However, his class was one of my least favorite that I have taken at BYU. What should have been teaching on his part, was him calling on uneducated students to share what they learned from the readings. For the entire class period. I would have expected a more prepared and organized class from someone with his education.

Professor Wiseman is AMAZING!! He is so respectful of everyones opinion and class is very enjoyable. He doesnt give tests or quizzes, so be prepared to write a lot of essays and  speak up in class  to get participation points. This is honestly one of my favorite classes I have ever taken at BYU and he is by far one of my favorite professors.

Best Spanish class I've taken at BYU. Your grade is proportional to how much you work, and the whole class is centered on discussion and participation. Midterms and finals are all essays, so it's all based on what you learned and how you can communicate it. Dr. Wiseman will bend over backwards to help you with anything and he always makes class fun

The class overall was not what I was expecting, but I guess you can't go into depth about Latin America in one semester. What we did cover was so applicable to issues today. Dr. Wiseman is seriously the most supportive professor I have ever had. He really does care about us as people and tries to apply the material to our lives.

By far the best teacher I have ever had!!! Very caring and is more interested in your learning that he is the grade. His straight-up honest about how you can improve and is flexible with how he teaches. FANTASTIC TEACHER

He looks mostly like a teenager, and he has the energy of one too! Really sweet guy who is willing to bend over backwards to help you succeed. You do need to be prepared to read--a lot, and there's a huge focus on class participation, please do! It makes the class so much more exciting.

100% would take again. He is super respectful and respected. He encourages you to learn by your style and offers opportunities for all students to pass and to excel. He's kind of silly sometimes but in a good way that is very endearing. He wants you to work hard but it's totally doable, and class is interesting. He is a great professor!

Professor Wiseman is a great professor, he's really dedicated to helping his students and truly tries to meet their needs. He offers individual help outside of class and responds quickly to emails. Classes are usually discussion style, so make sure to do the reading to comment in class.

He is one of the best teachers I've had at BYU. He is so flexible and understanding. He really cares about his students and made me care about actually learning than my grade. He tries to adapt his assignments to your learning style. The readings and papers are still challenging, but interesting.

I had him as a substitute for both 201 and 202 (he substituted for his wife). He is hilarious and his speaking is very easy to understand. He just seems like he would be very effective as a professor.

Prof Wiseman is the best teacher that I've ever had.  He makes learning Spanish easy because he honestly cares for the subject.  If you have the opportunity to take any class form him, don't let it slip away!
Dave is an amazing human being and an engaging professor. He infuses the classroom with positive energy. He practices what he teaches and makes his students want to do the best they can.

Dave really cares about his students and their success. He understands what it is like to be a student so the assignments actually matter, no busy work. Dave is an inspiration (dude's in the military, has a PhD, masters, rides motorcylces, etc.)
He is one of the best individuals I have ever interacted with. He is very understanding and validating. He is also extremely intelligent and I learned so much from taking his class!

Dr. Wood leads his classes with an impressive balance of experience and humility. He is sensitive and caring towards students and thoughtful in his feedback. He has an ability to pull out the most important topics that are relevant to real-life application rather than focusing on obscure tangents.

Dr. Wood is one of the best professors Ive had during my whole college career. All of his assignments contribute to what were learning. He is excellent at giving great feedback and you can tell he honestly wants the best for his students!
He is such a great professor and person!
Dave is a gem. He cares about each student and genuinely cares about what he teaches. He is a blessing to the MSW program.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. It is the most politically biased class I've ever had. When the professor isn't shamelessly preaching his political opinions as if they are facts, he is usually known for going on long and unrelated tangents. He barely teaches class and leaves the teaching to the students. Excessive readings also from biased textbooks.

The lectures are quite biased, but he is interested in creating informed dialogue between students. If you aren't ready to spend TONS of time using strange research sites and writing, this class is not for you. I misunderstood LearningSuite (my 1st semester here) and received no mercy on the late work I turned in. This prof is for US HIST majors.

This professor will tell you that he isn't interested in courting political controversy. Do not let him fool you; hist 221 from david-james gonzales is designed to validate his particular political fetishes through historical revisionism.

That being said, he is altogether a nice person and a fairly economic lecturer. Credit where credit is due.

History 221 with Dr. G is a great option, there are a lot of readings but they are interesting and there is very little homework. There aren't any tests, just 4 papers and a big final project/presentation. He is a great teacher who may get off topic a little in his lectures, but its a good class, and fairly easy to get a good grade.

Read 7 books in one semester (get the audiobook to save time). Had a few short 2-3 page essays and a final creative project. Dr. G rarely gave anyone less than 85% on an assignment. Most people were getting A's and A-'s. 3% of extra credit. Make sure to go talk to Dr. G during office hours to understand what he is looking for with assignments.

A very opinionated lecturer who uses his lectures as a soapbox to rant about race, feminism, economic inequality, and 'social justice'. He effectively uses his course as a way to get his students to produce Wikipedia articles about activists, minorities, and racial topics, and disfavors those who choose to write about something more neutral.

Why is everyone is talking about how political Dr. G is? I never got that vibe. He was very respectful to both conservatives and liberals. Overall, the class requires work, but getting an A is achievable. 4% points of extra credits. Essays were graded a little harshly. The Wiki project is fine as long as you meet with Dr. G. Great class!

As a professor, Dr Gonzales is AMAZING. He really cares about his students. However, the expectations for this class are insane. I spent more time on this class each week than my 3 level-300 major classes combined. And if you don't get a good partner for the group project you are in big trouble. Still might be better than American Heritage though.

Dr. Gonzales is really chill, flexible, and passionate. That being said, the class is pretty unexciting if you aren't interested in race, immigration, etc. in US history. If you are, it's great - the lectures aren't usually tied closely to the readings, so he talks about a lot of interesting things that you don't normally cover in a history class.

I felt like he used his lectures as a soapbox to discuss his personal beliefs. The course involves hours of readings and podcasts per week. The unit tests were graded extremely harshly. If you take this class expect a heavy work load. (Warning: Your final worth 40% of your grade is a group project, so hopefully you get a good group.)

Professor Gonzales is awesome. This class was all about U.S. immigration, and it was fascinating. He is so knowledgable, and this class was kind of formatted like a book club, where we read books and talked about them in class. A couple of big assignments, but nothing too crazy.

Honestly, after the first quiz, I didn't even go to class. Lectures were honestly pointless, the quizzes were also graded very harshly and they said "no arguing grades". Very vocal about his viewpoints which isn't inherently bad but feel like he got a bit off-topic sometimes because of it. Only big downside was the tough grading. The rest was fine.

I don't write reviews, but this class was so rough I had to. It wasn't a US history class, instead an immigration/social justice course. I felt underprepared for every assignment, lectures did not match the coursework, and the semester-long Wikipedia project was never explained, but instead we had to figure everything out on our own. Overall poor.

I was very frustrated by Dr. Gonzalez's teaching style and class format. Lectures were completely unrelated to assignments, and the final project was unrelated to both. It also felt like a "controversial topics in American History" class and wasn't as broad as I hoped. He turned everything into a commentary on current politics with a biased view.

Dr. Gonzales is nice and loves history. The classes were great and there was not a ton of homework besides reading. However, there was A LOT of reading, sometimes 100 or so pages a day. He does provide a lot of extra credit opportunities. The final was writing a wikipedia article and the quizzes were just written papers responding to a prompt.

Took for my A HTG GE. Here's the deal. No exams or tests. Only papers and a final writing project. That means a lot more engagement with the texts and writing skill is needed, and a lot less memorization and traditional history studying. If you're looking for a class that diverges from the traditional, dry history course then take this class.

Professor Gonzales is such an incredible professor. Before his class I was considering switching my major, but his class is the reason I stayed. There's a lot of reading, but it's all interesting and meaningful. He really wants you to learn, not memorize. I've become more engaged in things that matter rather than passing a test. Take his classes!

Dr. Gonzales is a good person and very passionate teacher. I wish this had not been such a liberal class. Personal opinions were taught more than historical facts and I felt marginalized by the opinions of the professor and my fellow classmates. I would not recommend this class to anyone who does not want to take a class in a political environment.

Dr. G is awesome! A few other reviews said he has lots of lectures on immigration, but immigration and urbanization are areas that he specializes in of course were going to talk about it! He approaches history in a unique and refreshing way. Lots of reading and subsequent essays, but no real tests or quizzes. Fair grader and cares about students.

Honestly didn't love the way the class was structured, the lectures could be boring and didn't correlate well with our readings and assignments. It was a lot of reading, but if you're into history, it's all really interesting. He gives a refreshing perspective on US history.

Dr. G is a great professor. His lectures are a little dull sometimes but I learned an incredible amount in his class. The reading load is insane, you kind of have to pick and choose which readings you'll actually do. Overall I enjoyed the class but found it more difficult then I thought it would be.

Good guy, valuable material, and helpful, but relies heavily on lectures (which are pretty dry) and enormous amounts of reading. He made a large project due over thanksgiving break and shows little consideration for his students' time. His material also seemed blatantly biased to me. I'm far from a history major, but i couldn't stand this class.

I can honestly say this class singlehandedly convinced me to change my major from history to chemistry. Gonzales is one of the dullest lecturers I've ever had, assigns inordinate amounts of reading, and skipped over massive parts of history like both world wars and the civil rights movement. A few thousand lectures about immigration, however.

The problem with this class is that the lectures were rarely applicable, despite very mandatory attendance. Get ready to read at least 40 pages before every class. Prof Gonzalez is so nice, but he focuses on broad themes and doesn't cover some very important parts of US History. There are no tests, so there is a lot of writing.

Professor Gonzales assigns A TON of reading, and all from dull history books. There are no exams, which was nice, but that means that your papers and projects are graded more heavily so it's more difficult to get a decent grade. An A is attainable, but be ready to work for it. Class time is all lectures, which was very boring.

Loved it. TONS of reading, not textbooks though, and lectures weren't super applicable to the class, but very fair grader and teacher. Always gave sufficient time for assignments, was very clear on requirements, was a lot of work but an A was very attainable. Very opinionated, but overall a good experience. Definitely better than American Heritage.

He assigns a TON of reading, but has no tests, which I feel was a fair trade-off. Rather than focusing on specific people and dates, he focuses on historical themes and motifs. There is one take-home essay, three document analyses, a bunch of reading journal checks, and a final project where you write a Wikipedia article. He is a solid choice.

This is class is unique and is focused around producing relevant work. The main assignment was accomplished by completing due dates every few weeks, so there is no way one could procrastinate in this class. We read four amazing books that simply add on to each other and by the end of the class, all the students really enjoyed the truth they taught.

You can DEFINITELY tell that Dr. Gonzales is passionate about history. History is actually my least favorite subject, but I loved this class. It's a lot of reading, but if you go to class and make an effort to understand the readings, you'll be good to go! There are no MC tests and the final is a partner project. I highly recommend taking this!!

Doesn't believe in tests, but there are three in class short essays instead & you just write about 3 paragraphs so it's easy, but he doesn't tell you what day it will be on so you have to show up everyday. Also a TON of reading and journal entries to prove you read. He basically just focuses on how racist white people have been through history tho.

you will come to class and go over the math content that you did the night before, but she will add upon it. It is not difficult if you go to class. She is my favorite professor I have ever had because she actually cares about her students and goes beyond the simple requirements of being a professor. It you want to have a good class than choose her

Very unclear instructions on assignments and never knew what she wanted from us. If you want to be able to talk about things she doesn't agree with, good luck, she will just tell you you're wrong. We spent the majority of the class arguing about mathematics topics instead of learning about assessments. Now I know how I don't want to teach.

She teaches in a very abstract way that makes it really hard to understand what is going on in class. She has 3 different resources she uses for work and it gets really confusing. Her tests are so abstract and hard to comprehend and often don't follow along with her review and class content. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM THE OTHER PROFESSOR

I'd heard some bad things about Dr. Teuscher, but honestly I loved her class. It was well organized, the workload was manageable, and it's not difficult to do well. There's a fair amount of group work but it feels appropriate and you learn a lot from the group projects. She's always willing to work with students who ask for help. Great instructor.

Absolutely ridiculous. Dr. Teacher doesn't seem to care about her students, the amount of work is overwhelming, even for a 4 credit class. I spent almost 20 hours a week trying to have a decent grade and am barely scraping a B.
Worst teacher in MTHED. Does great research, but can't teach.

Honestly, one of the worst classes I have ever taken in the Math Ed program. She doesn't care how much work the assignments are or what your schedule is. The only reason anyone actually learns anything is because they want to be a teacher and the course is designed well.

She is the best and nicest person ever. She is incredibly genuine! pathways is for people that struggle in math. The people in my work group however all passed AP calculus and the class moved at their speed and to their questions. I worked my but off and spent hours every day..... still did terrible. GREAT idea for a class- just needs adjustment

Super confusing set up. The idea is you learn math a practical and logical way. However her assignments often revolve around "you should have already learned this principle in high school so we didn't discuss it besides the abstract way I wanted to"... if you genuinely struggle with math and we're hoping for help, this class is a nightmare.

Dawn's wonderful. HOWEVER, this course with Dawn is not actually a normal Math 110. It's called the Pathways program and it is the worst possible way to learn anything about math. The homework is intensive and never ending and students are never actually taught how to solve it. Pathways encourages students just figure it out on their own. DONT TAKE

If anyone here says anything negative about this teacher it is because they did not try in her class. She helps those who help themselves. She is the kind of teacher that you remember more for changing your life rather than teaching you a subject. If you take her class you will have to work hard as heck. If you want to REALLY learn math. It's her.

Most influential professor I've had at school. She makes you work hard, but it's all worthwhile and for your good. She always has time for students who are working hard and still struggling. She knows what she's talking about AND truly wants her students to succeed. Seriously, I wish I could've taken everything from her.

She is the greatest teacher I have ever had. She is GENUINELY interested in your success and she does everything to prove that. She will work with you for as long as you need. Her methods MAKE SENSE. She has changed math for me. I dont hate it anymore. She is amazing. I dont know what I will do without her as a math teacher.

Professor Hedges is a kind man, but it was extremely hard to sit through a 3 hour class with him. He is soft-spoken, very old-school, and kind of hard to pay attention to. His lectures were not engaging at all. However, grading was not harsh and he wants to help his students do well. If I'm being honest though, it was because of the TAs I did well.

Dr. Hedges is awesome!  The only graded things in the class are 3 exams (including the final), a presentation, and participating in class literature discussion, so you can really focus on the content you are learning. He has a lot of great experiences to pull from (former MD career), and is super accessible and understanding. 11/10 recommend!

I loved my class with Dr. Hedges. It was very lecture heavy, but he's so funny and good at explaining difficult concepts. The class is graded only on quizzes and 3 exams, but as long as you study, you'll be fine. He reviews everything that will be on exams in class and will let you know when certain concepts will show up. He wants you to succeed!

Dr. Hedges is very kind and makes this class easy. He isn't the most engaging lecturer, following the textbook's slides pretty closely. He was very flexible and it was clear that he wanted us to succeed, not trying to trick the students on quizzes and tests. The only grades were quizzes and tests, but he prepared his students well for them.

Dr. Hedges is FANTASTIC.  He has a MD in psychiatry, and has lots of interesting clinical insights to give in class. Pay attention to lectures, some of the things he says in class that are not on the slides are what he tests you on. He is a fair grader. Tests are taken in class which is nice so you don't have to go to the testing center :) 5 stars!

Neuro 460 with Professor Hedges has been my favorite Neuroscience class! The exams are fairly straightforward, and the class follows his PowerPoints with minimal material from the textbook. Professor Hedges makes behavioral neuroscience very enjoyable with his extensive clinical knowledge, witty humor, and willingness to provide feedback.

I took Dr. Hedges for NEURO 460 and he was great! Lectures were sometimes a bit dry, but he is a super funny and caring professor. Exams were pretty clear and fair, and he often took out questions the majority of the class got wrong. You have to read one or two articles a week and answer questions in class, but they aren't too bad.

I had him for Neuro 460 and he is easily one of the kindest and funniest professors I have had, he has cold calls for articles so you can get participation points but its super chill. His tests are very straight forward and he is transparent about what to study. Take it from him, it isn't super tough but you learn a lot!

While not tech savvy, Professor Hedges was a very easy teacher to work with in terms of assignments and projects. We basically just had one 10 page paper that we worked on throughout the semester. The lectures could be kinda boring, but you don't have to go since there's no attendance. Overall great experience, I would recommend taking 307 from him

Professor Hedges is a great professor! There are textbooks that he recommends, but they aren't required. His lectures can be a little dry, but he has a sense of humor. One big paper due at the end of the semester, with smaller ones due throughout that led up to it. If you have an issue with your grade, talk to him or the TAs and they'll help ya out

One of my favorite psych classes; Dr. Hedges really cares about his students and has a bit of a dry sense of humor. I loved volunteering at the state hospital (20 hours), and appreciated that we covered the neurobiological aspects of some of the disorders, and drugs used to treat them. This class wasn't super hard but I felt like I learned a lot.
Dr. Hedges is a great professor! The class is super interesting and he is an engaging lecturer. He is also a very fair grader.

He was helpful and available to students. His lectures were interesting, informative and funny. The class required an average amount of reading, not much homework. I loved both his class and the requirement to work at the state hospital. Great class.
Dr. Hedges is so sweet and hilarious! Just follow the study guides and you'll do great on the tests.

His lectures are all over the place and unhelpful. You're never sure what you will actually need to know for the tests that make up your entire grade along with 22+ hours volunteering at the state hospital, which was an enriching experience, but the class was boring. He lectures for part of the class, other part every day is student presentations.

Funniest, nerdiest guy I've ever met. He throws in witty humor. Pay attention in class-- he doesn't post his slides which is annoying, but the tests come from lecture & from the book. Go to the TA reviews to know what he is gonna test on. He gives a generous amount of extra credit at the end b/c his tests are hard. I loved the articles we read

He writes his tests to take 30 minutes, but you get a very generous hour and fifteen minutes to complete each one. Some like his lecture style, some don't. I liked it because he'll throw in dry, witty humor in between slides that you won't get if you're not paying attention. Very approachable, and he definitely knows his stuff. Highly recommend!

I really enjoyed him. He is super nice and very approachable. You must go to the TA reviews to do well on the exams and to know what to focus on. Make sure you read the journal article before class on journal days because you never know if you will be choosen to answer a question about it. Very light workload and an interesting class.
He's seriously an adorable old(ish) man. Some of the information can be a little dry, but his humor is so great and he always keep things interesting. I really didn't mind this class

Professor Hedges slides in clever humor in all his lectures. Lecture is very open, with lots of discussion and opportunities to participate. There is hardly any homework, so do well on the tests and make sure you come prepared for the article reviews. He doesn't post materials online, so attendance is mandatory to get notes on his lectures.

Dr. Hedges is the one of maybe 2 MDs on campus, he knows his stuff. He's a humble professor who memorizes everyone's name on the roll. The class material itself is great and he really loves people asking questions. Getting an A is very reasonable, going to the TA reviews before the test is most helpful to do well on them. Straight up baller

Tied for my favorite class at BYU. Dr. Hedges has a lot of clinical experience and knows A LOT. He is helpful and respectful. If you attend lectures and study hard you shouldn't have a problem getting an A. His tests aren't super easy, but they are reasonable and he won't test you on material not covered in class.

I thoroughly enjoyed Dr. Hedges class. He's an excellent professor. He cares about the class and is very good at explaining difficult concepts. The workload is doable and tests are easy as long as you study what he tells you to before each test. Papers aren't difficult but grading depends on your TA. Definitely recommend Hedges-one of my favorites.

Dr. Hedges is a very nice man. He's willing to work with students and is very accommodating when issues come up. This was his first time teaching Ab Psych, so there were some flaws. Overall, it was really boring but rather easy.

Dr. Hedges was a great Abnormal Psych teacher!  He is a psychiatrist by training, so he had cool stories and information to share about all the disorders we talked about and he could easily answer any of our questions off hand.  He also has a great sense of humor that you'll catch if you're paying attention.

Great professor. Go to class because there are random quizzes (2 to 5 easy questions)and the points eventually rack up. The essays are super easy and if you talk to your TA he will tell you exactly what you need to do. Tests are pure memorization so just pay attention in class. Do the extra credit! It boosts your grade a ton I ended up getting 104%

Hedges is incredibly funny if you actually listen to what he's saying. Class is super easy, I had no knowledge of psych before taking the class, and I spent most of the class just playing on my ipod and listening to what he said. I didn't take notes, hardly opened the book, and I got 100% in the class. I didn't even know that was possible at BYU.
The class is pretty boring, and the professor is not really funny though he tries to be. The class is pretty easy if you pay attention in class, which can be hard to do

The class is super easy, just don't take it at 8 am over the summer!! Hedges is really good, he is hilarious and will answer any questions. The tests aren't too bad, just study! The essays are super easy, but your grade depends on the TA, definitely do the extra credit essay- totally worth it! I also did not ever read the book, take good notes.
Hedges is so great!  Such a great professor.  His lectures are super interesting and straight up hilarious.  Plus, the class is pretty easy.  Hedges for the win!!

The lectures are extremely interesting. He cares about his students and is willing to answer questions and is understanding. He is funny and prepares the students for the tests very well. He is a neuropsychologist so be prepared for a lot of axon and dendrite and stuff. Definitely Recommended.

Prof. Hedges is easily one of the best professors at BYU. I guess it depends on your sense of humor, but I was entertained every class period. The class is easy if you study for the tests. As far as writing the papers goes, always go over your essay with your TA or you will probably get a bad grade. If you're going to take psychology, take Hedges.

A little overrated. Very funny man, but extremely disorganized; skips all around the PowerPoint, making note-taking difficult. He gives irregular in-class quizzes off the top of his head, so they are often ambiguous and confusing. I also had a very bad TA; a terrible writer, I often went to her personally to point out her mistakes on my papers.

Prof. Hedges is so great. This was one of my favorite classes of the semester. There are in classes quizzes, so you have to attend, but lecture was always Hilarious. He's always making funny comments and jokes. Tests weren't too hard if you studied. I learned alot and had a good time.

He's a funny guy. I enjoyed the readings, which is good because most of the test material comes from those. His aim is to give a general knowledge of psychology, so he's not too hard. If you show up and do the readings, you'll do fine.

Hedges is great! He is really funny, very willing to help outside of class, and best of all the class is EASY. Do your reading, study for the tests, and do the article summaries, and you will be fine.

This prof is so awesome. He teaches well and is so funny. I'd definitely take another class from him. I didn't use the book, but it could have been helpful. I hardly had to work to get an A. Just pay attention to lectures and write down the power point notes or highlight in the textbook. Take Prof. Hedges!!
Dr. Hedges is hilarious!  His humor made the class.  Do the reading, visit the TA office hours and you will do well on the tests.

Professor Hedges is great. The class itself is pretty boring and he he can be scatter-brained, but he is also hilarious and the best part of the class are his tangents and stories. It's an easy class. Only 3 easy 2 page papers and a quiz every week, plus he offers extra credit and does test reviews.

Hedges is a fantastic Psychology teacher. He explains things really well and has a hilarious sense of humor. The book is very useful and the tests are quite difficult, but the class is very enjoyable.

Very easy going straightforward guy. He's always cracking random jokes but only half the class ever gets them because they aren't paying attention. Go to class and pay attention in the reviews and you shouldn't have a problem, I hardly ever touched the book and I got an A. Three exams that are all multiple choice.

Great teacher, very funny and always willing to help. I didn`t use book at first because ratings said not to, but then I did bad on the first test. I think the book is actually pretty helpful. Extra credit is available. Good class.
By far the best Psych teacher there is. He is funny, dang smart, and tests are fair. He makes sure to cover everything on the test.  Studying is still important

My favorite professor at BYU. I laughed every class. He is very patient and will explain things clearly. Only one paper and three multiple choice tests...easy stuff unless you choke on one, then you're in trouble. Just a nice, hilarious guy; I'm sad I can't take another class from him.

Best teacher I ever had at BYU.  If you have to take Psych 111, TAKE IT FROM HEDGES. Hardly any homework (just one paper and its only two pages!)Extra credit is available.  Hedges explains everything so well and is SO ENTERTAINING! He is AMAZING!

If you take Psych 111 from any other teacher, you're making it way too hard for yourself. Go to class, all test questions are from lecture, but he makes it easy to take notes on what he's saying. Don't bother buying the book if you take it from Hedges. He's funny & clear & understands his class doesn't have to be hard for his students to learn.

Dr. Hedges is a hilarious teacher and he really know's his stuff. He's a great teacher and teaches in an interesting way. The tests were really hard for me, so deffinately study hard for them, but the class is awesome.
He is an awesome teacher. very funny. makes the subject interesting. tests are easy if you take good notes.

He's soooo funny...even through the boring stuff :) His tests are very reasonable. You need to attend EVERY class...because the test questions come from class...but class is fun...so don't panic...be happy :)

what a stud!! this teacher is the bomb ya'll!!!!  he knows what he's talking about, and has the best dry sense of humor you can imagine.  Not that hard... just do well on your research papers, and study like MAD for the tests.  awesome awesome awesome

One of the kindest professor I've had, Dr. Hedges really cares about his students success and learning. He makes the sometimes boring material interesting with his great sense of humor. It's easy to succeed in his class and if you struggle he'll drop evertyhing to help you. Strongly recommended!
His class is pretty easy.  I was a dumb freshman and still did really well on his tests.  The work is very easy.  He is also just a funny guy.
Take Hedges for psych 111.  His class is fairly easy, with minimal work.  His tests are straight forward, no trick questions.  Super nice, and one of the funniest professors I've ever had.
He was so funny because his humor was so dry.  I really enjoyed the class and it wasn't too hard.  I decided to become a psych major after taking the class if that says anything.
He was very funny.  I liked his explanations and examples.  He made the material easy to remember.  His tests weren't too bad.  The section on the brain was confusing, but overall he was very good.
i love Dr. Hedges. His class was easy and he has the driest sense of humor i have seen in awhile. i never read the book and got A's on all the tests.

easiest class ever.  The he always goes through the test and gives you a few free answers.  The only other assignments are a paper that is way easy, like two pages and not worth much at all.  He is a pretty funny guy in a weird way; I laughed a lot.  I recommend this class!
