Tests come straight from lecture, nothing out of book. Don't buy the book. Someone told me that and I ignored them and bought it anyway. What a waste of money 'cause I haven't used it once! He has the funniest sense of humor!! If you have to take psychology take it from him!

Tests are based from lectures not book. I wouldn't buy the book if I could go back.  He's funny, interesting, and knowledgable. Only one paper assigned and no cumunulative final. Great class, learned a lot from the lectures.
i loved him so much! he's so funny and his class is so easy! the paper was way easy and so were the tests.

This guy is amazing. He knows exactly what he talks about and he has a sense of humor but it's a different sense of humor and it makes him funny. He also takes the tests from the notes he gives which makes tests easier.

Dr. Hedges is extremely intelligent and his lectures are very interesting and he makes it better with his sense of humor.  He is also very easy to work with.  There was a mistake on my grade before I transferred to another school, and he made it so easy to fix!!  I would highly recommend him for any class!

A gloriously intriguing prof. & class.  You have 1 paper that is 2 pages long, 3 exams and the final is NOT comprehensive.  you don't have to read, just take good notes and you'll ace his tests.  he's also hilarious, i highly recommend this class and professor!

This is a great class and not because of the subject but because of Dr. Hedges. I did not want to take psych but it is required so... Dr. Hedges is great at explaining concepts, has a great sence of humor, and his tests aren't half bad.  I would take a class from him again. :)

Dr. Hedges is a very brilliant man.  Sometimes some of the information would go over my head, but I did learn a lot.  Usually you'll only have 3 or 4 tests and 1 paper.  He always has a TA do a review session before the tests, GO TO THEM!, they are SOOO helpful.  You will know exactly what to study, rather than trying to cram the textbook in.

Wow, what an incredibly intelligent person!  Interesting lectures, funnier than crap, and really takes an interest in students and their opinion on things.  He's really cool about feedback, too, he likes to know what you think of the class.  His tests are kind of hard.

I loved Dr. Hedges' lectures.  He is funny and keeps your interest.  He only tests over the lectures, though, so pay attention.  The tests weren't too bad, but you have to do well on them because that's all he grades on.

Don't buy the book. He only tests on lectures. He is by far the easiest and best out of the other psychology teachers. Just write one paper and take 3 tests, plus simple extra credit opportunities just for filling out a survey. Very interesting class. Prof. Hedges is absolutely hilarious.

Very dry humor to add to the rather boring lectures but he is a really nice guy and the class isnt too bad. Very difficult to get an A, but an A- isnt that hard to get. The final by far the most difficult of the tests

Ha ha ha! Is this man funny? His lectures are great. When things start getting a little boring, he'll say something random. Grade comes from 3 test and a paper. Gives you an extra credit opportunity. Sit in the front! His handwritting is a beast! it is sometimes impossible to read!

Pr. Hedges only tests on lecture -- I sold my book back the first day.  The tests were always easier than I expected, but you really do have to study.  His tests are written so if you really know it for sure it's easy, but if you're going by what sounds familiar you'll fail.  Only one short paper.

This class was really easy. The tests were pretty much right out of the lectures, the book was pretty superfluous. He's a pretty funny guy, although his sacrament meetin gjokes got old. Oh, and sit close, because his handwriting's kind of bad and hard to see.
lectures never matched tests, always went away from the tests confused because the material never made sense. never saw a TA, didn't even know he had them.

Professor Hedges is the coolest guy. He has a great sense of humor and a genuine desire for the students to do well in the class. Make sure to show up to all lectures, since he bases the tests off of them. However, he does do reviews before each exam.

Lectures are awesome! For such a dry topic, Prof. Hedges can be very funny. His class is very easy, he tests only on what he teaches. You don't even need the book. Take good notes. Sit up front because he writes only on chalkboard, can be hard to see.

Dawson is awesome!  He has a great sense of humor, making lectures so much fun if you catch his jokes.  If you take attend class, take good notes, and study what he says in lecture than it is pretty easy.
Great prof! He will answer any question you may have and is always availible via email. He tells you what yo study for the tests and they are relatively easy!

awesome!  he is hilarious and only tests what is covered in class.  get to know him personally, he will answered any and every question you have.  great professor, nerdy (he's hilarious!), and a really interesting class.  TAKE HIM!
Awesome professor! Absolutely hilarious!  His tests aren't rediculous and he tests on only the important aspects of the topics discussed.  His class will be the best part of the day so don't miss it!

Professor Hedges is freakin' awesome.  He is nerdy, but hilarious.  Beware of his notes that he writes on the board.  They are impossible to read, and are very chaotic.  But overall, I love this class.  He always answers lots of questions.

It's everything you expect from a general psych class-fat textbook, slightly nerdy (but very funny) professor, and easy tests. Great lecturer and (an often unheard of trait) only tests on what was covered in class or in the text.
He's really funny!  And not too difficult.
Dawson  Awesome  Hedges is quite possibly the best professor in the Psychology department.  Take every class you can from him.  He's fair, funny, a great lecturer, and rad.

Professor Son is awesome! The TA's do a lot of the grading it seemed and even when I had to turn in an assignment late Dr. Son still worked with me and was accessible even when it was towards the end of the semester. The assignments are fairly easy, lectures are sometimes slow but the way tests and quizzes are designed was perfect for the class.

This class is very easy. Quizzes and exams are all open note and lecture. Grading on bigger assignments was extremely slow. Book reports were due over five weeks ago and she still hasn't graded them, which is frustrating because we've already had the last day of class. She often cancelled class and showed up late. Lectures were pretty boring.

Prof Son was great but was often late to class. Overall the class is very content heavy where we would read up to 60 pages for a one page assignment, one group project, and a research presented at the fulton conference. It often felt more like a graduate-level class

She is so kind and incorporates her beautiful testimony into her teaching. However, she was often late to class and cancelled a lot. The material was pretty superficial; I took other classes that only spent two lectures out of the semester on parenting that honestly covered about the same amount. Great if you're looking for an easy class

SFL 240! Professor Son is so sweet and caring! Definitely a great professor! On the other hand, I wouldn't take this class again. It was an interesting class, but there were 3 large papers (around 10 pages) at the end of the semester that were worth 50% of your grade, and the basic information you were learning in class wasn't worth all that time.

SFL 490!!! She cares about her students and is willing to meet with students to help with assignments. Just be prepared for the magnitude of reading and writing. You typically will read 2-3 research articles and write a page and a half paper on the articles for each class. There are also 3 large papers at the end of the semester that were hard.

The SFL 490 class & title is misleading. We spent the semester dissecting what was wrong with the human development research field instead of looking at complex topics in human growth and development across life. Rubrics were vague, assignments graded slowly. I didn't find the material useful and would recommend taking Moral Development instead.

This is the easiest credit you will take. There is no weekly readings or homework. The lectures are pretty surface level which makes the tests easy too. There are a few big projects that take time but thats literally it. She is so caring and fun to learn from!

Professor Son is so caring and sweet! You can tell she cares about her students and their questions and concerns. She is very respectful of students' backgrounds and perspectives, and you can tell that she loves what she teaches. Our class discussions were relevant and meaningful.

Professor Son is one of the sweetest professors at BYU!! You can feel the love she has for her students as she teaches. I'd feel comfortable coming to Dr. Son for any life challenge I was experiencing. She seriously is in your corner! Throughout the semester, the group discussions we had in class were very meaningful & honestly inspiring.

This class is amazing! I reccommened so much for women AND men of all ages. The content is super interesting and we've had great conversations. The work load has not been bad so far and Professor Son is so sweet.
Jessica is hands down the best dance 180 instructor, she's fun, easy to learn from and is always, always ridiculously positive!

people laugh when you tell them you take this class but it will make you much more educated on sexuality in marriage and how sacred and unifying it is. People saying people over 120 pounds will feel more insecure leaving, I say I felt the opposite his goal is to push towards accepting one another's bodies and appreciating them for how they change.

Busby is a straight to the point guy, as long as you go to the lectures and take notes you'll be good. I didn't read the book at all still got an a in the class because what he goes over in class is the same as the book. His lessons were so informative and really changes your perspective of Sex, what it is and how important it is in a relationship.

I enjoyed what I learned about healthy sexuality-however he is extremely fatphobic and constantly made comments that would make anyone over 120 lbs super insecure and feel awful leaving class.  I enjoyed some content but he is quite the black and white professor regarding people's sexuality.  As well as he would yuck people's yum. Tests were tricky

This class was really awesome and so informational. I think every person at BYU should take this class right before getting married or after. It was a bit challenging with tricky essay questions on the test. He is a tough grader, or his TA's I am not sure. I really liked this class but ended up with a B- because of the tests.

Dr Busby was inspiring and insightful. The topics of this class are so important and Busby teaches them in the most sensitive and honest way. There was one research paper that is really easy to get full points on weekly reflections but they are sooo easy. This class is super chill and the exams are easy. Highly recommend.

Dr. Busby was a fantastic teacher; his lectures were very engaging and very focused on the gospel AND social science. I took SFL 376 with my husband and we thoroughly enjoyed it. One thing to note is that attendance mattered, he would post pop quizzes and mini response assignments after each class period. His TA was a VERY tough grader for tests!

He uses the PERFECT blend of proven data and the Gospel. This class is seriously the key to a happy, fulfilling marriage. You might not learn anything shocking, but it completely changed HOW we see marriage and sexuality—with way more openness and growth mindset. My husband and I took it before we got married, we still talk about it ALL the time.

Dr. Busby is a great guy, and his class is very insightful, but I really don't agree with it's organization. Beware of the exams. The essay question prompts are generic, but if you don't include EXACTLY what he is looking for you will lose 10-15% of your final grade. Though I averaged an A+ in every other part of the course, those alone got me a B.

Good: 
Lectures
Quizzes fairly easy
Bad: 
Test questions can be ambiguously written
Essay questions are graded harshly (class average quite low)

If you're not an SFL major, consider taking this as an audit.

Dr. Busby is amazing IMO. He gives stellar lectures & facilitates discussion. He's uplifting and Christ-centered (I teared up a time or 2). No matter your comfort level with sex you can learn great things from this class! An avg amount of work for an SFL class. Tests had general study guides. Be ready to take notes bc he didn't post his slides:)

I would only recommend this class if you feel a lot of anxiety regarding sexuality. For many people, this class can be life-changing, but if you're already sex-positive, it's not ground breaking. Also, I thought this class was much harder than it should have been. And Busby has some bizarre opinions about sexuality that I sometimes disagree with.

*Mic Drop* This class is hands down one of my favorites. Healthy sexuality is not talked about, but Dean Busby talks about it with such reverence, honesty, and rawness. Exams felt a little memorization-heavy. Aside from that, I'll advocate every friend of my mine to enroll in this course. Seriously, this class can save a marriage before it begins.

I cannot tell everyone enough how incredible this class is. It doesn't matter if you are single, dating, engaged or married every single person can benefit from this class. About half the people in my class were single but I took it married. Best class I've taken at BYU and Professor Busby is the best professor I've had here as well.TAKE THIS CLASS

This was a super inspirational class and he is such a kind prof. Attendance assignments after every class that are easy, exams do require studying, a major essay, and content quizzes. Read the readings and go to class and you'll be totally fine. He is passionate about the subject and the lectures are really insightful and interesting!

This is a perfect class. Enough work to keep you engaged with the intriguing lectures, but low on your rankings of work load compared to your other classes. Just one 4 page paper. At the beginning of the semester the lectures were kind of dry, but towards the end I was always on the edge of my seat and sometimes almost in tears.

Dr. Busby is inspirational, knowledgeable and kind. His lectures were awesome and I learned so much! My only complaints were that each slide had so much information on it and quiz questions were sometimes confusing or based on small details from class/reading assignments. But many test questions came directly from quizzes, so that was great!

Dr. Busby is one of BYU's very best! His lectures were clear and engaging and he knows the material well. There's an attendance quiz due after each class that's super easy, and then a paper due at the end of the semester on a topic of your choice.

Every student at BYU should take this class!! It was literally life changing!

I really liked Professor Busby, he's an interesting dude. He really knows his stuff and I really enjoyed his lectures. Class workload was not bad. The biggest thing was a 4-5 page paper near the end of the semester. This class was seriously one of my favorite classes that I have taken so far, I don't think you can go wrong with any of the profs

He is incredibly tangential and most of the time I am confused about why we are talking about the things he is lecturing on. He is entertaining, but it is incredibly frustrating for an academic class. It is never clear what we will be tested on, and they were random minute details we were expected to remember verbatim. I would not take him again.

Professor Busby is an amazing professor and his lectures are inspirational. The course has 6 content quizzes to help prepare for the tests which are easy and there is a attendance question for every class. The tests aren't bad if you take good notes of the lectures and key points of the research he has you read. Professor Busby is my favorite!

Yeah not great. I liked the content but not a fan of Busby. Tests/quizzes were a little ridiculous. Final had a study guide from which we were told the Qs were created, but there were Qs from content not listed. 3 out of 32 have an A in the class. Not a complete waste of time, but mostly.

One of my favorite lecturers. His study guides are super helpful; use them and take good notes and you'll be in good shape for his tests. Lots of reading but most of it was interesting. I still think about some of the things he taught. The material was amazing and he taught it really well, and with a good sense of humor.

Very good class. We're terrible at talking about this topic in our culture, and I honestly think everyone at BYU should take this class. The readings aren't too dense (except the research papers, but you can just skim those and be fine), and he gives study guides that tell you exactly what to know for the tests. We had very valuable discussions.

Dr. Busby is an amazing lecturer! This class was great - 3 tests (final non-cumulative), 1 paper, and attendance quizzes that are pretty easy. Pay attention in class and take good notes and you'll be fine. We had readings every class but most were engaging. He does a great job of keeping the subject spiritual and intellectual. TAKE IT FROM HIM.
This class should re required. IT is incredible. So many things I always wondered about. He conducts the class and topic in a way that is very comfortable and natural.

Dr. Busby is one of my favorite professors. He really is a wonderful teacher, his classes are great, you'll learn a lot. It takes work, you'll read tons. You'll have quizzes often, which will help you prepare for the exams. The exams are very fair.

Classes are mandatory. Do the reading...he will quiz more often than not. Papers aren't bad. Tests are more than fair. I learned a ton! He has a great perspective. Has lived all over the country, not just Utah County. Awesome teacher!

Everyone should take this class. Tests take some studying but nothing too wild. Learned A TON! And would take the class over if I could. Readings are annoying and you have quizzes in class semi-often. Must attend class every day!

Dr. Busby is an amazing teacher-LOVE HIM!There is a ton of reading that is fairly difficult at times-but the lectures are INTERESTING,entertaining and VERY clear. He is extremely fair when it comes to tests-they come straight from his lectures and the readings-no tricky or unfair questions. Loved the course content-Loved the Class!

This was the best MFHD class that I have taken at BYU. Professor Busby is an excellent teacher. He gives pop quizzes but prepares you for them so you need to go to class and 95% of the stuff he tests you on is straight from the notes that you copy from PP slides. His lectures are NOT BORING!

Prof Busby is one of the best teachers at BYU! He is funny, spiritual, knowledgeable, and sincerely cares about his students. Every time I left his class with a stronger testimony of the gospel and a clearer idea about what to do with my life. I recommend every one to take this class from him. Even if you are not a MFHD major or minor, audit it!

I took this class Winter 2006. I liked Prof. Busby as a teacher and thought he was smart. But there are a lot of readings to do for every class which aren't very easy to read, for the most part. (they come from journals and such)

Dr. Busby is one knowledgeable, amazing professor. He truly knows his stuff. The class is incredible but you do need to attend every lecture and study the reading material--but it is totally worth all the effort.

Dr. Busby is my favorite BYU professor.  The man is brilliant and the class is amazing.  Everyone should take this class from Busby.  There are a lot of assigned readings but the are generally facinating.

This man is amazing! I loved him as a teacher, and I loved this class. Not too hard--just go to class every day and keep up with the reading. It was seriously one of the most interesting and inspiring classes I have ever taken. Dr. Busby really knows his stuff, and is entertaining, too.

A lot of people loved the class. For me the subject matter was boring. He gives pop quizes, but puts the answers on blackboard. This helps because he uses many of the questions on the test. There is a lot of journal article reading. So if you like that sort of thing then take the class. The class helped me to decide marriage therapyis not for me.

This class is so great!  Dr. Busby has a lot of MFT experience and shares a lot of great insights about the field.  He does give a lot of pop-quizzes which can be brutal, and there is a lot of reading...but the class makes up for it.  Great class, great teacher.

His marital relations class was awsome! He has a great knowledge and genuine interest in the subject, and shares a lot of stories and video clips that drive home the points. He also invites a lot of class participation which is nice. I usually fall asleep in morning classes, but never did in his- I would really recommend it!

Teaching was fine, but grading was uncool. We'd get points taken off for things that weren't on the rubric and little things that didn't have to do with the material. Exams were always way easier than the homework though, and we got way more time for exams than needed.

Dr. Wheeler in lecture is clear about what you need to know. Lab was super fun and I looked forward to each lab. The course is very broad and the tests always had some obscure MC question. Dr. Wheeler holds office hours and the TAs are great so if you put in the work and get the help you need you should be fine. Midterms have 2nd chance points too.

Dr. Wheeler is a good professor and will take time to help you out with whatever you need. Go to his office hours, it will make your life so much easier. This class is a very difficult class in general, but he allows you to get points back on tests, and you'll struggle through things which will help you to learn.
Dr. Wheeler is very good at teaching difficult concepts in a clear way that I could understand. I would highly recommend taking a class from Dr. Wheeler.

Dean Wheeler is an exceptionally effective teacher. Course materials are extremely neat and organized. Material is presented clearly, effectively, and in an interesting and interactive way. I would highly recommend Dr. Wheeler.
I didn't see Dr. Wheeler much during this course, but the course was well outlined, I learned quite a bit with the hands on material, and the final was pretty non-stressful.

I've had Dr. Wheeler for a few courses now, and have found him to be the lowest quality professor in the Chemical Engineering department at BYU. Just to make potential freshman aware, this guy encouraged me to change majors rather than try to help me understand the course work. He is very unsupportive and lacks interest in his students.

If I have to take another class from Dr. Wheeler I will probably drop out of the MS program. It's not that he's not a good person, but he is a bad professor. His idea of teaching is to let students struggle, and that doesn't work for my preferred learning method, and it seems like a crutch for his poor teaching. Homework looks nothing like lecture.
Amazing professor and great guy.
Awesome professor.
Professor Wheeler is a great professor, who makes you work for your grade, and doesn't pamper you with partial credit. If you study and learn the material, you will do well in his class.

I like Dean Wheeler quite a bit. He's a tough grader though! I went to him for help and he told me to read the book again.  I feel like the tests aren't very consistent with homework. And homework is not very consistent with what is taught in class.  I think they try to weed people out in this course.

Least favorite of the Big 3. Dr. Wheeler would get caught up in an irrelevant question for half the lecture then end up rushing the rest. Examples were scarcely explained. Also beware, the midterms are relatively easy but are not models for the final. Be meticulous about accuracy in the exams and pre-exams.
Tests are very different from your typical engineering classes because he wants you to get away from the "partial credit" mentality. Great class, stay on top of the material.
Wheeler writes hard tests and his homework is not very helpful in preparing for them.  The class has gotten easier due to the recently added lab.  Not my favorite class ever, but definitely doable.

Dr Wheeler is a great teacher for the intro chem engine. He does a great job of keeping our interest level with examples and explaining in depth at times. The pace of the class was great as the homework load is much less compared to previous batches (happened with him introducing the weekly labs).

Really nice guy and a decent lecturer. He assigns difficult homework, but it's hard material, so that's reasonable. The real issue is his tests. He's a big fan of writing tests that would take at least 2-3 hrs for any normal, non-robotic human being and making you take them in a 50 minute class period. Not sure how that benefits my education.

Dr Wheeler though is a very good person is a pathetic teacher. He gets confused himself while teaching and confuses his students even more. Moreover, his tests are impossible to take, no matter however hard you study.

Dr. Wheeler was a really nice guy, the projects were really fun, although time consuming for a 2 credit class.  Tests are mildly ambiguous, he lets you use notes, so he tests on seemingly irrelevant topics, and asks for them word for word from the book.  I took this class concurrently during high school, so experienced students would do better.
Great at explaining basic concepts. The projects he had us do were fun too, but he can take a while to explain something. Great professor, but he can take some getting used to.

Absolutely love this woman! The class felt like a lot of review from Skills 1 and Health Assessment, but was a little more in depth. Dr. Himes holds weekly office hours where she goes through practice questions on all of the material. So helpful!

Deborah is amazing. Her class is SO well-organized and she even made a calendar of all the due dates for all second-semester classes. She's so kind and was willing to work with me with some of my extenuating circumstances. Her class was difficult for me because I second-guess myself but I still feel like I learned a lot. She also values feedback.
Deborah is awesome! She is super thorough and incredible helpful. She really wants her students to learn and succeed. She is super organized and she made it possible to survive second semester!

Deb is amazing and is so dedicated to her students and the advancement of the nursing practice. She is seriously SO organized; she gives you a calendar that outlines every second semester class for you, which was a huge help. Exams are fair and an A is definitely achievable. She is inspiring and truly cares about each of her students.
She was awesome!  She is extremely organized, always eager and willing to help her students.  Her tests are relatively easy compared to other nursing classes in this program.  A rather doable A.

Class content was very applicable to real world application of cloud technologies. Professor Kettles is very good at taking feedback from previous years and adjusting his course to help prepare students to get jobs.

Capstone is the group project of all group projects and in all the worst ways. This rating is more for the class than for the professor, though I admit he didn't seem very concerned about our learning experience during this semester.
Prof. Kettles is a... quirky guy haha. He is really nice tho. The class however is very hard and very bland in my opinion. I think he did a good enough job at teaching it, but it was really tricky.

201 is an easy class. It is very straightforward. Prof Kettle is a gem. He is spiritual and hilarious. He will show you how to do your work in class. You technically do not have to go to class because you can learn everything from the online textbook and Google/GPT. GPT is allowed in most of your projects.

He's a super nice guyThe whole course is online and his lectures weren't very helpful, I recommend taking it from someone else. He spent a lot of class time not even preparing us for the next project, you kinda have to do it on your own.

Class can be pretty hard a times. Going to TA hours is really helpful for any questions about assignment or topic. I find it helpful to go over my assignment with a TA if I don't want to miss any points. The first exam is the hardest bc of the time limit, however both exams are open everything but AI. Group projects aren't bad, ask TA for help.

As an international student, and with this being only my second programming course, I initially felt unsure about coding. However, with Professor Kettles' guidance, I found that coding was a great fit for me. The key to success in this class is practice, and Professor Kettles is always willing to explain the content until you fully understand it.

Prof Kettles was great! I didn't think the class was too difficult. I learned A LOT but it was very rewarding. A bit fast paces, but to be expected for a term class. Did a great job walking you through class examples and preparing you for the exams. He was super great though!

Professor Kettles is one of the kindest professors I have had. Genuinely invested in the well-being of his students. He gets a bit off-topic sometimes, but the course content and structure weren't too difficult.

Professor Kettles is an amazing at teaching IS 303. He explains things plainly and helps you when you need it. What I loved most is how organized he was with his lectures and being understanding when technical problems happened.

Professor Kettles is very personal, he cares more about the student than anything else. He really wants you to learn and enjoy the class. I had trouble throughout the semester and he was very understanding and really kind-hearted and helpful. I think if anyone is looking for a teacher that will truly uplift them, they should take this class!

Most students didn't quite know what to make of Dr. Kettles at the beginning, but after getting to know him he's one of the most caring, knowledgeable and enjoyable teachers I've ever had. His assigned subjects may not be the most exciting in the core, but he makes them enjoyable; and make hands-on, usable knowledge readily available.

Goofy professor, but love em. He's really funny and energetic. His course content can seem unorganized (and sometimes, it is). But just follow along for the fun ride. 401 isn't too bad - he'll get you on some trick questions, but overall, not difficult of a class (except for Intex)
Sarah is the best! She's always energetic and so much fun. The class is easy as far as grades go; as long as you attend and participate you'll be fine.
Dr. Stephens is a master teacher and astronomer who cares deeply about her students. If you have any problems or questions, just ask! She is always more than willing to help.
This class was just very unorganized. Dr. Stephens herself was great, but the class was just not good.

I loved Dr. Stephen's class. I really liked how she wants you to truly understand the material. However, the class was messy when we first started and the majority of us had no idea what was going on. Nevertheless, I would definitely take a class from her again.
I took PHSCS222 the first year Dr. Stephens taught it, and it was great. It's easy to stay invested in her lectures. She's fun and understanding. Her tests can be hard, so study well!

This class is awful! Very unreasonable professor. Super disorganized with both online and paper assignments. Mid-semester, there are 20+ HW tasks every week! Most of the HW isn't graded until after our final. Don't take this if you think it will be a "fun" gen ed. You'll be putting in more hours here than in American Heritage or ECON 110, no joke.

This class is very homework-heavy and takes up a lot of time but I would still take it again. The content was really interesting and Dr. Stephens is really understanding of deadlines. TA hours are a must! Just prepare to do a lot of homework.

This class was absolutely BRUTAL. Dr. Stephens expected a ridiculous amount from us. At the end of the semester, we had completed 172 assignments. Assignments also weren't graded for months, and I still have assignments I did in January that haven't been graded. This class is absolutely NOT worth it unless ur ok w/astronomy being ur whole life.

Way too many online assignments. Not sure if she realizes that we have other classes besides hers. The organization of canvas is awful. We have 3 midterms, not including the final, throughout the semester. The TAs are pretty awful at catching up with grading homework. It wouldn't be a problem if we didn't have to do so much. A let down for sure.

This class was very interesting and I feel that I learned a lot. However, we were given much more homework than I was expecting. There's a lot of hands-on things, so if that's your thing, you'd probably really enjoy this class.

I love Dr. Stephens as a person and expert in her field.

Her class is a bit of a mess in many aspects. Her lectures are great, but the amount of work for this class is INSANE. I need to be conscious of my grades as I am thinking about grad school, and this class may cost me my good GPA. The amount of work is insane.

She loves astronomy, but she gives about 5-6 assignments for everyday we meet. We meet 3 times a week so you end up HAVING to do 15-18 assigenments. Canvas is very unorganized, because of this many assignments were missed and I had no idea. Lots of busy work that she grades hard.This class was awful. I will never take another class from her again.

She loves astronomy, but the work you do in class is just the homework. She gives 4-5 quizzes for everyday we meet. We meet three times a week, this is not including any extra homework she gives. Canvas is very disorganized. If you are thinking of taking this for an easy GE DONT. This class is awful. I will not be taking another class from her.

There are so many pointless assignments 5-6 a day that are complete busy work. I took this class for a GE but ended up getting 18 assignments a week on a super unorganized canvas that is difficult to maneuver. Don't make the same mistake I did, this class ain't it.

She's very passionate about Astronomy, but she assigns an insane amount of homework. The average day has about 5-6 assignments plus reading. The class is 3 days a week, so your doing about 15-18 per week. Canvas is very poorly organized and confusing, and so are the assignments. Most of them were busy work, and you have no choice but to do them.

I genuinely think that this professor is AWESOME. She knows what she is talking about when teaching. Like seriously, she knows her stuff. Don't miss class because your attendance is graded through iclicker. One thing that is difficult is that there is a LOT of smartwork, and it can be difficult to keep track of. Other than that the class is fine!

Really good professor. Lots of homework, lots of reading, but tests were very fair. She also lends a ton of support with review sessions, ample TA hours, and supplementary videos. The class was a lot of effort but she matches the students' efforts with her own, and you end up learning a lot and feeling accomplished. Highly recommend for 228

A little disorganized at the beginning of the semester, but she is very forgiving with deadlines. We were never tested on things we hadn't extensively covered in the lecture or homework. Overall a very enjoyable class and Dr. Stephens is a great teacher!

Dr Stephens is a brilliant educator; Ive come across things and ideas in other classes or research and Ive always struggled to explain those ideas to friends, but upon hearing her explain it, it is crystal clear, said in the most concise and easiest way to understand. If I ever become an educator, shes the person I will look to for how to teach.

Not sure how Dr. Stephens has so many good reviews. Her class was THE WORST class I have ever taken while attending BYU. So much homework, lots of quizzes and surprise/ random projects throughout the semester. I'm a hard working student but the amount of work that was needed for this class (a GE class mind you) was insane. Do not take from her.

Dr. Stephens is dedicated and genuinely enjoys her work. There was a lot of group work, but it was very evenly distributed between everyone. She is very easy to access outside of class and is forgiving with deadlines. Lots of mini assignments that take dedicated time however.

Dr. Stephens was one of my favorite professors at BYU. She loves astronomy and really teaches the material in a way that is easy to understand. She is willing to answer any questions, anytime! Everyday, you do a group assignment (usually aren't hard). She gives reading and lecture videos to watch beforehand, but I rarely watched them and did fine.
So much busy work... lots of group work. Lots of individual projects

I love Professor Stephens! She is super respectful and does just about anything to help you succeed. It's a decent workload, and you're graded on a lot of things, but also the tests aren't a huge chunk of your grade, and she lets you use the study guide and your notes. She is really understanding too, opens assignments if you need more time and ask

Dr. Stephans really knows what she is talking about and is so so smart. However we often went over class time because we had group assignments everyday and never finished them. Class would consist of 15-20 min lecture, rest of class group assignment. It really was up to you to learn what she posts on CANVAS for you to watch and read.

Prof. Stephens is really good at relating astronomy to the gospel and is very passionate about what she teaches. I learned a ton in her class, but it was much harder than I thought it would be. There is SO much homework and each test covers a lot of material. Grading takes forever. Also expect to fall asleep in the comfy chairs at least once haha

WAYYY too difficult and stressful for a GE class. Outrageous amount of assignments, quizzes, projects, tests, etc. that made it impossible to keep up with it all! Things take forever to get graded and several got lost in the process. Even though I tried my best to succeed, I struggled BIG TIME on each exam.
Dr. Stephens is incredibly intelligent and really knows her stuff! Her tests are a mix of memorization and comprehension so watch out for those

This class has a lot of busy work, however it is very helpful to understand what the information on the tests are. There are in class quizzes that aren't too bad. Large possibility of falling asleep because of how comfortable the chairs are. I took this as a GE and I would take this over again instead of physics. Do the work and its a fun class.

By far, the best teacher at Brigham Young University. She ties the Gospel with whatever she teaches, and has such a deep passion for what she teaches. Her lectures are very inspiring and invites the spirit. If you do the readings and assignments, you will be fine. If you take astronomy, take it from her! :)

Dr. Stephens is a good teacher, and I would recommend her for this course. However, be prepared for a lot of work. There are a lot of assignments due, but it helps with grades. Her test are not bad, and as long as you study, you will be fine. She posts great slides to study from, so everyone has the opportunity to receive a good grade.

Dr. Stephens is a sweetheart. She is so kind and caring. She wants to talk to you and get to know you. Her lectures can be rushed, and taking notes during the last 15 min of class can be almost impossible though. A fair amount of out of class work is required (more then just studying). Can be hard to keep your eyes open. Overall, I'd recommend her.

The reason this class is a lot of work is because of several weekly little assignments, 4 midterms, and other projects, but the work really does help you understand the material very thoroughly so you don't have to stress for tests. Prof. Stephens helps her students out so much and she really cares. She's one of my favorite professors so far.

Great class. Learned a ton. Sometimes the amount of assignments seemed unnecessary, but in the end I felt super prepared for tests. She goes over everything enough times and gives you enough opportunities to practice that it seemed impossible to get lower than a B.... only issue was staying awake in the planetarium in the morning.

Dr. Stephens is a phenomenal professor. I loved her class and found it super interesting. She is extremely caring and will work with almost any circumstance if you talk to her. There is a lot of homework but it is honestly not that hard. She throws in jokes and funny videos to keep you awake in those comfy planetarium seats. Such a fun class!

I hate science but had to take a class to fulfill the GE. Unfortunately, there was a ton of homework and I consistently scored Bs on every test. Dr. Stephens is super cool and friendly and smart, but I feel that the class was too much if you are just doing it for the credit. Also, I really struggled to stay awake in class.

This class is not what you think it is! The class is super fun until the add/drop deadline. You will spend a lot of time doing busy work assignments that are due each week and a quiz before each class. The material deals a lot with physics although there is little math. The test aren't too bad but make sure to go the reviews. You will fall asleep.

Dr. Stephens is one of the most brilliant professors at BYU She is passionate about her subject and she makes learning fun and interesting. She gives practice exams and review sessions for every test. Her classes are challenging, but she really wants her students to do well and gives them every opportunity and resource to help them do so. Amazing.

I loved this class! Dr. Stephens is a great professor who is passionate about her subject. She teaches the concepts clearly and interestingly, although sometimes it's a lot to take in at once. She is straightforward about grades and tests. The homework sometimes felt like busy work, but it effectively reinforced the concepts and was good test prep.

This class was my favorite class I've taken in college. You get weekly homework, a few projects throughout the semester, and the tests can be hard, but if you put in the work it is a great class. Dr. Stephens was always very helpful and understanding and she seemed to genuinely care about her students. I used the textbook to review but that's it.

A wonderful class from a wonderful professor. Weekly assignments, use of the observatory for a project or two, an exam for each month of the semester, and a quiz on the stars and constellations of the Provo sky. Readings are not that important. Taking notes in class, however, ARE important! NO MATH! A little EXTRA CREDIT! FUN!

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. Especially if you are just trying to fulfill a general credit. There is SO much homework. 3 assignments every week. and 4 tests that are extremely difficult. and you have 4 observation products that take a lot of time to complete. If you are wanting a challenging. busy work class take it. But i wouldn't ever again.

Dr. Stephens was a great professor and made astronomy really interesting.  I felt like her tests were pretty tough, but I'm also not the greatest at science, so that could be an explanation.  I always left astronomy feeling like I learned something cool.  Take this class for an awesome gen ed!

Professor Stephens is amazing. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER! She makes difficult material easy to understand. Do your projects at the beginning of the semester and it will save you. If you pay attention and study the homework, tests will feel easy. She makes the test and its answers available for studying for the final. Fantastic teacher!

Class is actually worthwhile! If you're an active learner, you'll thrive. She's extremely clear & fair about grades--the only people who don't pass are the ones who aren't willing to work & show up. It's fascinating and she makes it fun, even though I don't normally enjoy science. All homework is helpful in learning the concepts. Take it from her!

Loved her class! She's very passionate about the subject which transferred nicely into her teaching. I strongly considered changing my major to astronomy after taking the class, so if you're one for stargazing and want to know how the universe works, check it out!

While she knows her material, she is not very flexible with students and does not seem very willing to help. A lot of the homework is busy work, and I did not like that attendance was effectively mandatory (you have to turn in your lecture tutorial books at random during class), especially because the lecture material is all covered in the book.

I thought Dr. Stephens was great! She makes astronomy really interesting and is always willing to clarify material and answer questions. There's a lot of lecture tutorials, but they help with retaining the material. Just make sure you don't procrastinate your observing projects. They're not hard so just get them done early. Overall amazing class!

She likes Astronomy, but I the workload is unnecessary and the lectures could be more concise and clear. I would not recommend her to others. Seems to have a too bad so sad attitude when it comes to tests and assignments.

She's a great professor who really knows her stuff.  However, the class in general is not worth it with the amount of work.  3 midterms and a comprehensive final. Minimum of 4 observing projects. At least 3 assignments every week.  So much info to memorize for tests.  It's really easy to fall asleep in class, since it's in a dark planetarium.

I loved this class! Teacher is great, very kind and passionate about the subject. Kind of feels overwhelming sometimes, but easy to get an A because of all the extra points from homework. Get homework done with TA's in 1 or 2 hours every week. Textbook is in the TA room usually. Complete all assignments thoroughly and you should get a high grade.

Okay, I thought this class was tough. There's huge homework assignments every week that are very time consuming and the lectures usually fly over my head. She is awesome though and really easy to work with. If you're taking this course because you like stars, you're in for a rude awakening. I did enjoy the projects though, and the TA's are helpful.

Dr. Stevens is amazing.  She is so easy to work with and the TA's are very helpful.  The class is very straight forward and easy to understand. The only downside is that it takes place in the planetarium which makes it easy to fall asleep.

Dr. Stephens is amazing.  Just don't fall asleep in class and you'll get an A.  Homework seems to be hard until you actually do it, especially the projects.  I finished all the projects in just one night to not bother myself later.  Fun class.  You'll end up being able to teach Astronomy.

An amazing teacher and class.  It was the funnest, most intellectual, and interacting class I've taken.  Make sure you don't fall asleep in the planetarium.  Dr. Stephens wants you to do well and she teaches you as a mother (just as weird as it sounds).  You will end up leaving the class being able to teach Astronomy.

Dr. Stephens was a WONDERFUL teacher! each class was very interesting and got me excited for the next class! tests are not too bad... but if you study and go to the reviews you should do well. She posts all her slides online so its not necessary to take notes. She has an amazing attitude and really made me appreciate the world around me. TAKE HER!!

Dr Stephens was excellent. I was in the Descriptive astronomy class (127) so most material was pretty basic. There's a lot to do, but it's not too hard and lots of help is available. Also it balances your grade so it's not just weighted on a couple tests. Just keep on track and you'll get a good grade. Comfiest chairs of any classroom

Dr. Stephens is a GREAT professor! She shows genuine interest in her students (walks around class and helps with assignments). However, I just thought that astronomy overall was a hard class. There is a lot of information to remember for tests. Stephens is the best astro professor there is. Her test reviews are very helpful, when she teaches them.

This was an awesome class! I liked physics before, but this class made me want to get into astronomy. The homework and assignments weren't very challenging. The tests weren't too hard either. She is a wonderful professor. I recommend the class even for people who don't think they like physics.

Dr. Stephens is one of the best professors at BYU. I am not an astronomy major, but her classes were so engaging that I wanted to be! There is a decent amount of work, but it is all beneficial. Definitely take this course!

Makes you see the world in a completely different way. Totally worth taking, especially from professor Stephens. I wasted my time in Physical Science, but this class was amazing. You won't regret taking this class!

I am not a science person at all and took this to cover my physical science GE. I didn't do so well on the tests because they were difficult, but after going in and talking to her she was extremely helpful and understanding. As long as you do the homework and show an effort, you will do well.

She was awesome! I learned so much in this class. Occasionally the homework seemed really tedious and difficult, but you are given a week to do it and if you go into the TA labs it really helps. Tests are pretty straightforward if you study the reviews she gives you. Fun class!
One of my favorite teachers. She is very approachable and more than willing to spend what little free time she has helping you understand the tough concepts.

I took this intro Astronomy class from Prof Stephens in Winter 2009, and she's one of the best profs I've had!  She is patient, approachable, and the requirements for a good grade a clear-cut.  The first time through a concept can be confusing, but she reviews them over and over to make sure you understand. GREAT CLASS, GREAT PROF!
Great Professor, I would definitely recommend her to anyone.

Astronomy was great. She talked a bit fast sometimes and got sidetracked. Review sessions were not helpful. Do your hw with a friend so you understand better. Random attendance quizzes, but she gives you the answer if you pay attention. Tests were iffy on the wording. Other than that, she cares a lot about students, and it was a fun class.

Dr. Stephens is one of the best professors at BYU.  She really cares for her students and she wants you to succeed.  Just review your lecture slides and go to class.  Oh! The class is the best she has a daily joke that will wake you up and help you focus for the rest of the class.  She rocks!!!

A.M.A.Z.I.N.G. Never loved a class so much. . . ever. She makes an interesting topic absolutely gripping. She's so easy to understand and what she expects is so clear. Review the powerpoints and you'll ace the tests. Did I mention she's fun? We had a joke everyday :) Take this class!

She is great. Helpful, crystal clear explanation. I clicker quizzes are easy. I have heard of horror stories about i-clicker quizzes  in other classes from my friends. Good Class. Not that bad. Keep up with the homework and you will be fine. Believe me it will be an A eventually.

Tough class but great teacher. I did struggle with the class at time but that was nothing. Her i-clicker quizzes are not tough at all but then it really prepares for you for the departmental midterms and finals which can be little tough but the exams are same for all teachers. She ausm!

She is an awesome teacher! She makes the student understand the concepts so clearly. The exams for all the teachers are same. But, its not that tough if you take this class. I would strongly recommend her!

Astronomy with Dr. Stephens was fun and interesting. She is very interested in students' success, and is always willing to help. The class isn't terribly difficult, but staying on top of homework and projects is key. Study reviews before tests were extremely helpful, and grading was fair.

She is a perfect teacher. Her class have daily quizzes but they are so easy and its because of the quizzes only that you see your grades going nice. The assignments due weekly amake you learn more. By the time exams are up you know almost everything. Its not a big deal to ace this class with Dr. Stephens. I strongly strogly recommend her.
Dr. Stephens is the most helpful teacher I have ever had.  The class is hard, but if you need help, then she will do anything in her power to see you succeed.  Highly reccomend her!
She teaches good.
Hard class but great teacher.  She really pushed us, but was fair in the grading.  Learned a lot in this class.

Dr. Stephens is the best science teacher I ever had.  She really cares about her students, and goes out of her way to help them.  She is friendly, accessible, and kind.  The material is hard, but she makes it fun.  I would definitely recommend.
Boring class.  Boring teacher.  She has a ton of iclicker questions in her slides, so you can only miss class if you don't mind losing points.  I mainly slept in that class.
Dr. Halverson explains things clearly in lecture. She grades written questions on exams quite forgivingly, and her class has lots of extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Halverson explains things well in lecture. She grades written questions quite kindly, which is a blessing, and also offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. There was a lot of homework, but I think there has to be if you're going to understand something like multivariable calculus.

While Dr Halverson is brilliant and good at explaining the material and answering questions, she failed to structure the course in an optimal way. She made things harder than they needed to be by splitting assignments into multiple parts submitted in different ways at different times. The cognitive load of this class comes purely from the structure

She is such a sweet woman and really cares about her students. She gives lots of extra credit opportunities and is willing to help if you go to her office hours. Her lectures are pretty good, just make sure to read the textbook so you know what is going on since the class moves super fast. Lots of homework but it prepares you for the tests.
Do not take from this professor. She doesn't want you to come to office hours and tests take more than 3 hours. Absolutely miserable and no help when I was struggling.

This is a tough course, nothing against the professor. It combines linear algebra and multivariable calculus into one semester. Prof Halverson is great; showing up to her lectures and participation is key. She gives tons of extra credit throughout the year. The tests are hard so study up, but she does a great job of helping. Go to her office hours!
Professor Halverson is brilliant and kind and caring but for whatever reason the teaching style didn't connect with me. An A is definitely doable as long as you do the homework though.

This is the second time I've taken multi-variable calculus and I liked my previous teacher but Dr. Halverson explained way better the concepts and theroems so that I feel like I'm walking away from this class capable of teaching someone else about multi-variable calculus and linear algebra. Very homework heavy, but definitely worth the work.

Math 302 and 303 are tough classes. Only take if you're ok with 3 hours of hw a night and exams every week for two semesters. You go through a lot of content, but she does a good job explaining it all. Very possible to do well in the class, but also very easy to fall behind.
She explained the hard content of the course very well

There is an incredible amount of homework in the class and material to cover. Everything builds on past topics, so make sure you're getting everything ingrained or Week 2 material will bite you in the last week of the course when it comes back. Dr. Halverson is very funny and is great at explaining the topics while making it enjoyable. Super nice!

Professor Halverson is a decent teacher, but biweekly tests, pre-class work, and heavy homework assignments made it so I was studying 20 hours a week just to keep up. She would only lecture 25 minutes per class, forcing us to spend lots of our own time teaching ourselves material that was never covered in class but appeared on her tests regardless.

Terribly formatted for online-covid types of classes. Despite the lectures being recorded, she doesn't post them. Doesn't allow calculators so make sure you know your calculus. Required you to buy an iclicker reef subscription which wasn't necessary. She also speaks in a way that is hard to listen to and I frequently got lost in her explanations

MATH 302 is simply a difficult class and should be counted as a 4 credit class instead of a 6 credit class. Dr. Halverson really cares, but over-explains the concepts. She takes at least half of the class time on the quizzes and devotional, with 20 minutes max to actually teach. It just simply takes a lot of time outside class.

In this class you are taking multivariable calculus and linear algebra at the same time, but only in one semester. It's one beast of a class. Given that, she does a decent job of teaching it. Largely theory based, and very challenging. Don't expect to have a life with this class. Lots of tests, but they help to even out your grade. Good luck.

Dr. Halverson is a good Professor. 334 isn't an easy class but lecture made a difference. Quizes at the beginning of class were very helpful. She required reading from the textbook, which ended up being a total waste of time. She's really nice and easy to talk to unless you're a complete moron or put zero effort into the class

Excellent professor. She explained concepts well for a difficult class, and really cared about her students. She even came in on a Saturday to help the class review for an upcoming test. I highly recommend her as a professor.

She spent half of the lecture time doing a spiritual thought and quiz on the reading. This did not leave enough time for her to cover her prepared slides most every lecture. The material she did cover didn't make anything more clear as she focused on setting up the details of a proof rather than what it means. literally gave us a surprise midterm
Lectures are very abstract. She does very few numerical examples. Hard to reach outside of class because she doesn't post office hours online.

I took 313 from her. Prof Halverson is very caring and really wants to help students to success. however, she couldn't explain the concepts very clear, and most of times her answers to student's questions are very vague. i learnt more from math lab than her class. she made the class extra hard and many people withdraw from her class.
Most unreasonable professor I have ever had. Still take Math 342, but find somebody else

Excellent professor, enjoyed the class. Lectures were centered on working through problems. Dr Halverson did a great job explaining concepts and theorems so I could visualize the work I was doing and understand the material better.

Outstanding professor. Gives boring lectures but thats just because the material is boring usually. She really wants her students to do well, and is very helpful at office hours. Very friendly and competent as a professor.

If you have her as your professor, good luck, you need it. She wants to help you, but she almost always has no idea how. Online homework was annoying more than anything else. If you want your learning to be made more difficult, take her. I only got an A because I took this class in high school.

Math 302 is a hard class! But Dr. Halverson is a good teacher. Sometimes she starts talking in math language and you wonder what's going on, but usually she gives enough examples that I was able to understand. Loved the spiritual thoughts. We had daily quizzes, but they were all for extra credit which was nice. Definitely possible to succeed!
She doesn't really teach how to do problems but only does proofs and then expects you to learn on your own. I learned more from the TA then anything

The tests are extremely hard.  The rest of the Math 112 classes use a standardized test but she prints her own.  They are very tricky with plenty of trick questions.  You can't use a calculator in the tests but the answers are almost all complex numbers.  If you can I would take another teacher.
She makes so many mistakes trying to explain concepts that by the time she is done with the lecture her students didn't learn anything.

I definitely enjoy the teaching style of Dr Halverson. She really makes sure you learn a lot but not by telling it to you. She goes over basics and then expects you to extend your knowledge of those basics to new problems. The take home tests were hard since we had never seen the problems before. But it helped you gain a deep understanding.

Professor Halverson was fair but she is not merciful. It was very unclear what she expected of us and she was demanding. She gave help if you asked for it. By far the hardest class I have ever taken. Theory of Analysis is hard and she did not make it easier. She did give great spiritual thoughts, and she was encouraging. The tests were insane.

Overall score here is deceptive she is more of a 2.55 not 3.6 as listed now. Homework is hard but ok if u go to TA lab. She writes her own exams and they STRONGLY emphasize obscure hw problems that if you don't have memorized your doomed. 90% correct proof missing one line 210. Most common score on final ,F ,no curve. Find easier, better prof.

Dr. Halverson is not very exciting but she knows a lot. Her tests are pretty difficult but gives you a study guide with word for word questions that will be on the test. Attendance and reading are a major part of your grade.
Class itself was boring and easy. Tests, on the other hand, were very long difficult.

Sister Halverson is a great teacher and is really passionate about the BOM. But her lectures are loooong and boring, and most of the things she talked about weren't on the test. Attendance was mandatory, but I would've been fine had I not attended the class. Be ready to read a few chapters of the BOM a night, journals, and ponder questions.

She was very difficult and not  helpful. I wouldn't recommend this teacher or this class. I really liked the subject, but she ruined it for me. She was super nitpicky about annoying details that other teachers don't care about.

This class is all proofs, and you have to be very exact with your wording and structure.  It's challenging, but if you pay attention and follow her examples you will know what she expects. Homework every day, 3 midterms, and a cumulative final. She is very nice and always willing to help. Just be prepared to work hard and put in the effort.
I thought Dr. Halverson did an amazing job. The way she presented the material made the material easy to understand. The tests are a reflection of how well you did on the homework.

She's a very nice lady and really does want you to learn and understand the material, however I found the tests very difficult. I ended up with a B in the class by the skin of my teeth, and although the class wasn't terrible, it wasn't great either. If you read the book, you'll survive, that's what she teaches from.

Math classes are always hard, but Halverson is really good at preparing you for tests. She has extra credit quizzes daily that show you the kinds of test questions she will use. Sometimes she gets off topic into abstract concepts that aren't on the test, but never holds you accountable for info she didn't teach you. If you can, take 290 from her.

She is a really nice lady, but just seems socially awkward.  She is always smiling, but it just looks creepy.  She explains things well enough, but is monotone and easily lost my attention, since everything she said came directly from the book.  Lots of busy work, and half of class wasted on the participation quiz daily.

Dr. Halverson was an awesome math teacher. At first I wasn't so sure I would enjoy the class but I really grew to appreciate the way she taught and the interest she had in the success of her students. She wrote all of her own tests instead of using the department ones which prepared us well for the final. The class was graded very fairly.

I had her for Book of Mormon-and I was not impressed. There is no interesting discussion or insight into the scriptures at all.  The homework is hours of frustrating busywork.  Tests aren't too bad if you read the chapters and tune into the lecture every now and then. She is a nice person, but I do not recommend her as a religion teacher.

Dr. Halverson is probably one of the best math teachers at BYU.  How hard the class is isn't decided by her at all, it's all the math department, but she does prepare you for the tests really well.  Go to HER test reviews.  That's what saved me in the class.  She doesn't prepare you for homework real well, but that's what friends are for.
The class is fast and challenging, but Dr. Halverson finds a way to keep you up to speed. I don't know how she taught us so much in so little time. You will not find a better teacher for this class.

Horrible Class, monotone, barely understand her.  Extremely boring. Doesn't like student and will randomly report students to honor code office without evidence and without speaking to the student.  One of the worst classes I've ever taken at the Y.

Hard to stay interested in class. Teacher just reads the slides and rambles in a in-audible voice saying oh-k an average of 50 times a day. Very abstract with what she wants you to do. Take a different teacher for religion, she needs to stick to math.
Dr. H is an awesome professor. This class is hard no matter who you take it from, but she explains concepts well and takes time to help students.

Very fun and educational at the same time. If you ask a question she will answer and make sure you understand it before moving on. about 2 hours of homework a day, but worth it. Extra credit up to 2% of final grad possible. do the reviews and you will do well on the tests. one of my favorite math teachers ever! :)
One of the easiest class that I have ever taken. Dr. Halverson is great and helps you outside the class too.

Dr. Halverson is a really good math teacher. She always knows how to explain things and you can really tell she cares about her students. She spends a good amount of time on proofs, which I never understand but I think all math professors do that.
great teacher. better than the rest.
Awesome teacher. Class is tough but thats because the department makes it that way.  Very spiritual and willing to help enjoyable class.

Dr. Halverson is a great woman.    She's always happy and a great example, and is probably the smartest mathemetician I have ever met.  It's a hard class though, so be on your toes.  I thought she was a bad teacher at first, but it's just that I was bad at paying attention.  It's like a chipmunk trying to learn from einstein.  She'll always help.
Horrible at teaching.  I got an A, but it wasn't because of her.  Take Cutler instead, he can explain things better, and keep to a schedule.
Great prof, very willing to help outside of class and goes out of her way to make people understand.  highly recommended

It might be helfpul if she actually kept to a schedule.  We will be learning info for a test that began the day before, and ends the next day because she doesn't keep to the schedule.  Also, she will never tell you the relevance of the information.  All in all too much busy work, i learned far more from the books than from her.  Take another prof.

Very hard Class. Dr Halverson tries so hard to help. She is always available for extra help. Go to her reviews. If you have to take Math 302, take it from Halverson (also quit your job and break up with your girlfriend to free up time)

The class is ridiculously hard but if you have to take it you can't go wrong with Dr. Halverson. Things move quickly but she does a good job of explaining things clearly and making sure you understand. She is very nice and will go out of her way to help you succeed.
She is great.  Explains everything pretty well.  She will take time out to help you individually.  Very nice lady.
She can answer any question and is willing to spend as much time as you need to help you understand the material.
She's great!  Even though the class is hard, she is more than willing to help you understand the material and answer any questions.  I highly recommend taking math from her.
Dr. Stephens is a master teacher and astronomer who cares deeply about her students. If you have any problems or questions, just ask! She is always more than willing to help.
This class was just very unorganized. Dr. Stephens herself was great, but the class was just not good.

I loved Dr. Stephen's class. I really liked how she wants you to truly understand the material. However, the class was messy when we first started and the majority of us had no idea what was going on. Nevertheless, I would definitely take a class from her again.
I took PHSCS222 the first year Dr. Stephens taught it, and it was great. It's easy to stay invested in her lectures. She's fun and understanding. Her tests can be hard, so study well!

This class is awful! Very unreasonable professor. Super disorganized with both online and paper assignments. Mid-semester, there are 20+ HW tasks every week! Most of the HW isn't graded until after our final. Don't take this if you think it will be a "fun" gen ed. You'll be putting in more hours here than in American Heritage or ECON 110, no joke.

This class is very homework-heavy and takes up a lot of time but I would still take it again. The content was really interesting and Dr. Stephens is really understanding of deadlines. TA hours are a must! Just prepare to do a lot of homework.

This class was absolutely BRUTAL. Dr. Stephens expected a ridiculous amount from us. At the end of the semester, we had completed 172 assignments. Assignments also weren't graded for months, and I still have assignments I did in January that haven't been graded. This class is absolutely NOT worth it unless ur ok w/astronomy being ur whole life.

Way too many online assignments. Not sure if she realizes that we have other classes besides hers. The organization of canvas is awful. We have 3 midterms, not including the final, throughout the semester. The TAs are pretty awful at catching up with grading homework. It wouldn't be a problem if we didn't have to do so much. A let down for sure.

This class was very interesting and I feel that I learned a lot. However, we were given much more homework than I was expecting. There's a lot of hands-on things, so if that's your thing, you'd probably really enjoy this class.

I love Dr. Stephens as a person and expert in her field.

Her class is a bit of a mess in many aspects. Her lectures are great, but the amount of work for this class is INSANE. I need to be conscious of my grades as I am thinking about grad school, and this class may cost me my good GPA. The amount of work is insane.

She loves astronomy, but she gives about 5-6 assignments for everyday we meet. We meet 3 times a week so you end up HAVING to do 15-18 assigenments. Canvas is very unorganized, because of this many assignments were missed and I had no idea. Lots of busy work that she grades hard.This class was awful. I will never take another class from her again.

She loves astronomy, but the work you do in class is just the homework. She gives 4-5 quizzes for everyday we meet. We meet three times a week, this is not including any extra homework she gives. Canvas is very disorganized. If you are thinking of taking this for an easy GE DONT. This class is awful. I will not be taking another class from her.

There are so many pointless assignments 5-6 a day that are complete busy work. I took this class for a GE but ended up getting 18 assignments a week on a super unorganized canvas that is difficult to maneuver. Don't make the same mistake I did, this class ain't it.

She's very passionate about Astronomy, but she assigns an insane amount of homework. The average day has about 5-6 assignments plus reading. The class is 3 days a week, so your doing about 15-18 per week. Canvas is very poorly organized and confusing, and so are the assignments. Most of them were busy work, and you have no choice but to do them.

I genuinely think that this professor is AWESOME. She knows what she is talking about when teaching. Like seriously, she knows her stuff. Don't miss class because your attendance is graded through iclicker. One thing that is difficult is that there is a LOT of smartwork, and it can be difficult to keep track of. Other than that the class is fine!

Really good professor. Lots of homework, lots of reading, but tests were very fair. She also lends a ton of support with review sessions, ample TA hours, and supplementary videos. The class was a lot of effort but she matches the students' efforts with her own, and you end up learning a lot and feeling accomplished. Highly recommend for 228

A little disorganized at the beginning of the semester, but she is very forgiving with deadlines. We were never tested on things we hadn't extensively covered in the lecture or homework. Overall a very enjoyable class and Dr. Stephens is a great teacher!

Dr Stephens is a brilliant educator; Ive come across things and ideas in other classes or research and Ive always struggled to explain those ideas to friends, but upon hearing her explain it, it is crystal clear, said in the most concise and easiest way to understand. If I ever become an educator, shes the person I will look to for how to teach.

Not sure how Dr. Stephens has so many good reviews. Her class was THE WORST class I have ever taken while attending BYU. So much homework, lots of quizzes and surprise/ random projects throughout the semester. I'm a hard working student but the amount of work that was needed for this class (a GE class mind you) was insane. Do not take from her.

Dr. Stephens is dedicated and genuinely enjoys her work. There was a lot of group work, but it was very evenly distributed between everyone. She is very easy to access outside of class and is forgiving with deadlines. Lots of mini assignments that take dedicated time however.

Dr. Stephens was one of my favorite professors at BYU. She loves astronomy and really teaches the material in a way that is easy to understand. She is willing to answer any questions, anytime! Everyday, you do a group assignment (usually aren't hard). She gives reading and lecture videos to watch beforehand, but I rarely watched them and did fine.
So much busy work... lots of group work. Lots of individual projects

I love Professor Stephens! She is super respectful and does just about anything to help you succeed. It's a decent workload, and you're graded on a lot of things, but also the tests aren't a huge chunk of your grade, and she lets you use the study guide and your notes. She is really understanding too, opens assignments if you need more time and ask

Dr. Stephans really knows what she is talking about and is so so smart. However we often went over class time because we had group assignments everyday and never finished them. Class would consist of 15-20 min lecture, rest of class group assignment. It really was up to you to learn what she posts on CANVAS for you to watch and read.

Prof. Stephens is really good at relating astronomy to the gospel and is very passionate about what she teaches. I learned a ton in her class, but it was much harder than I thought it would be. There is SO much homework and each test covers a lot of material. Grading takes forever. Also expect to fall asleep in the comfy chairs at least once haha

WAYYY too difficult and stressful for a GE class. Outrageous amount of assignments, quizzes, projects, tests, etc. that made it impossible to keep up with it all! Things take forever to get graded and several got lost in the process. Even though I tried my best to succeed, I struggled BIG TIME on each exam.
Dr. Stephens is incredibly intelligent and really knows her stuff! Her tests are a mix of memorization and comprehension so watch out for those

This class has a lot of busy work, however it is very helpful to understand what the information on the tests are. There are in class quizzes that aren't too bad. Large possibility of falling asleep because of how comfortable the chairs are. I took this as a GE and I would take this over again instead of physics. Do the work and its a fun class.

By far, the best teacher at Brigham Young University. She ties the Gospel with whatever she teaches, and has such a deep passion for what she teaches. Her lectures are very inspiring and invites the spirit. If you do the readings and assignments, you will be fine. If you take astronomy, take it from her! :)

Dr. Stephens is a good teacher, and I would recommend her for this course. However, be prepared for a lot of work. There are a lot of assignments due, but it helps with grades. Her test are not bad, and as long as you study, you will be fine. She posts great slides to study from, so everyone has the opportunity to receive a good grade.

Dr. Stephens is a sweetheart. She is so kind and caring. She wants to talk to you and get to know you. Her lectures can be rushed, and taking notes during the last 15 min of class can be almost impossible though. A fair amount of out of class work is required (more then just studying). Can be hard to keep your eyes open. Overall, I'd recommend her.

The reason this class is a lot of work is because of several weekly little assignments, 4 midterms, and other projects, but the work really does help you understand the material very thoroughly so you don't have to stress for tests. Prof. Stephens helps her students out so much and she really cares. She's one of my favorite professors so far.

Great class. Learned a ton. Sometimes the amount of assignments seemed unnecessary, but in the end I felt super prepared for tests. She goes over everything enough times and gives you enough opportunities to practice that it seemed impossible to get lower than a B.... only issue was staying awake in the planetarium in the morning.

Dr. Stephens is a phenomenal professor. I loved her class and found it super interesting. She is extremely caring and will work with almost any circumstance if you talk to her. There is a lot of homework but it is honestly not that hard. She throws in jokes and funny videos to keep you awake in those comfy planetarium seats. Such a fun class!

I hate science but had to take a class to fulfill the GE. Unfortunately, there was a ton of homework and I consistently scored Bs on every test. Dr. Stephens is super cool and friendly and smart, but I feel that the class was too much if you are just doing it for the credit. Also, I really struggled to stay awake in class.

This class is not what you think it is! The class is super fun until the add/drop deadline. You will spend a lot of time doing busy work assignments that are due each week and a quiz before each class. The material deals a lot with physics although there is little math.
