He offers lots of extra credit to make up for bad exam scores. I ended up getting an A, but did I understand very much? NO.

It's obvious that he really knows his stuff, but it can be hard for him to explain things in ways the class understands. We barely opened the textbook at all, so you could probably skip that. There is a big group project, but it was easier than I thought it was going to be. Lectures were often confusing, so be prepared to figure it out by yourself.

Professor Tolley is fine but not my favorite. He's funny but I never felt like I learned anything from lectures because he just goes on about random stories. I had reached out to him once about certain circumstances and he told me my email baffled him rip (I was offended). Would not recommend personally but gotta do what you gotta do I guess.

Professor Tolley has a personality that some people connect with and some don't. I personally really enjoyed his real work stories and thought they brought some context to what we were learning. Overall the class was easy. There is a big group project. His lectures can leave you still needing more information to do the homework.

Dr. Tolley is hilarious and I enjoyed his lectures even though they weren't really an effective way of learning the material. He is very smart but had trouble explaining principles simply. Thankfully the TAs really helped cover the gaps between the lectures and the reading but I didn't like that I needed to go to them to learn.

This class is tough and he did not make it easier. Super difficult to follow lectures. Luckily, I don't think he will teach 240 ever again. I learned pretty much all of the material from studying the textbook because it was impossible to understand what he was teaching in class. Do not take probability from him ever.

He is a hilarious professor, literally never laughed more in class. Not super difficult material to learn. I would never want to take a hard class from him because he isn't always the best at explaining difficult concepts clearly.  No need to get a textbook. Tests are 10x easier if you know how to program all questions in R.

Dr. Tolley is funny and a good guy, but not great at teaching (lectures hard to follow and often go off on tangents). I was frustrated all semester because the class was not organized. I never knew what I was supposed to know or where to learn it. Material is not difficult, but there are few resources available, which made tests hard to prep for.

I feel he used to be a great professor 20 years ago. Now he's old and can't hear half his students. He'll think students are bored when really they're confused and then try telling stories to liven everyone up. Can suck with technology. My biggest issues is he would show you how to set up problems but then not actually finish solving them.

DO NOT TAKE IF YOU'RE NOT A STAT MAJOR. This class was so difficult for someone without a love for or a background in statistics. Lectures do not explain concepts, and the tests are difficult to study for. Choose a different professor.

Dr. Tolley has been teaching this class for so long I think a lot of the time he doesn't explain things well enough because he assumes you already understand it. Really hard to pay attention in lectures. I learned more of the material in one TA review than an entire month in class. He goes on multiple tangents every class.

Love Dennis. If you have to take STAT 230 make sure you take it from this man. Not only was he hilarious, he also made this class incredibly easy. So much extra credit was offered. If he messed up on a test question or if it was confusing he would give people their points back. Homework was very doable and it only took 20 minutes to 40 minutes/day

Dr Tolley is a legend. He's hilarious and he has a TON of experience in the field, which made for a lot of great stories. Homework never took me too long, R isn't hard to get the hang of if you read the R Markdown tutorials. Exams were 90% of the grade but are open note, book, etc. If you can answer homework questions you can do well on the exam.

Don't buy the textbook, find an online PDF you only use it a couple times. Pay attention in lectures, do the HW, and you will do great. He is funny in class if you click with his humor. Just get in the habit of paying attention in class and you'll do great. 90% of the grade is tests though so be careful coming in. Those are what matter study hard

Great Professor.  Clearly has experience outside of academia which makes it easy to see the application behind what is taught.  Make sure you understand the homework.  Most example problems that he uses come from Exam P, so actuaries get well versed to take Exam P.

His lectures were often comical and somewhat on topic. But you have to be going to TA hours and carefully how you're doing your homework on RStudio. Since the tests are open note, open book, your guide to the homework will save you. Tests are very hard if you try to skim through the class.

I NEVER go to classes nor watch recordings but only view slides, do HWs (2 attempts), and go to TA session (5 hours per week) throughout the spring term ending a grade of 99%. Dr. Tolley is quite fair and got my points back when I missed a few ambiguous and controversial questions on the exams. Take him if you need to pass the class!

I know that Dr. Tolley really knows what he is talking about but his lectures were very confusing and hard to keep up with. A lot of the time, our homework wasn't even related to what we had gone over in class that day either. I learned the most putting in a lot of time at the TA lab. He is very fair when it comes to the exams.

Dr Tolley is amazing. Hes the funniest guy. He is a perfect teacher and he makes some mistakes on the exams, but he always lets you get points back when he does make errors. Class has very little homework and if you go to the tas youll get 100% on it everytime.

I like Dr. Tolley and think he's funny, as many others have mentioned. However, he doesn't know how to organize a class in a way that clearly communicates to students what is expected of them. Assignments are graded harshly with no rubrics. Midterms approach, and you feel like you have no idea what you're doing. Wouldn't recommend his class.

Super Funny! Knows what he is talking about and tells stories to illustrate concepts covered. Kind of reads of off slides but is straight to the point on how to answer the problems. You get extra credit for your iclicker, so bring that. Overall, class isn't too hard. Just be sure to buy the Stats notebook with the slides and you'll be fine.

Statistics is a tough class but Professor Tolley made it enjoyable and much easier than I initially thought it would be! He's a funny guy and explains concepts clearly. You get extra credit just for going to class so don't skip. If you need help, go to the TA's--they are amazing. Would definitely recommend taking this class from Tolley!

Dr. Tolley's class helped me decide to get a STATS minor. He is funny, and gives great examples to show how statistics applies to the real world. Tips for the class: don't skip class, you'll get lost real fast. Also the i-clicker is worth up to 2% extra credit. Go to the open-lab for specific help. Buy the lecture notes, but not an additional book

Dr. Tolley is a very funny guy who has a lot of great stories. He gives extra credit for being in class and the papers aren't very hard. He moves pretty fast through the lecture and sometimes I have to go back and reteach myself. Aside from that, it was much easier than I thought stats would be.

SO funny and a very good teacher. His slides were so helpful, and he explained concepts very well with interesting stories. He gave extra credit for coming to class, and lab is available if you want extra help. "Papers" were not hard at all, and tests were very doable if you went through the study guide, slides, and practice test. Great professor!

Dr. Tolley is a really funny guy and he has so many really cool and funny stories he tells to keep class engaging. That being said, I almost fell asleep a few times and I skipped because the iclicker is extra credit. He isn't the best at explaining things, and I had to reteach myself a lot. Overall you can definitely get an A if you put the work in

Dr. Tolley was an awesome teacher. This class is one that you definitely need to work for, but he is great to work with. He works hard to help his students succeed while also ensuring they have to work for it.

Easy A. Tests are a piece of freaking cake. More than half the class got 100% on a midterm. In fact, half the questions are just reused from the study guides. Pretty sure I could have gotten the same grade if I hadn't gone to class, but his stories are the best (even though he'll retell the same ones 50 times)!

Tolley has a lot of stories and life experiences which he tries to apply to what you are learning and usually does a good job. Class can be boring at times. Clear grading criteria so you always know what to expect. I learned more from going to my TA lab than from his lectures. That being said, I would still consider taking another class from him.

Knows how to teach well and says things as they really are. He shares stories to help illustrate concepts--it's impressive that he has a story that actually connects to everything. Don't bother buying the textbook! Everything you need to know is talked about in class and you can go to the labs if you need to. He also helps you get iClicker credit.

Stats 121 isn't a super difficult class but you do need to make sure you know what you're doing and are prepared for tests. Prof Tolley just tells lots of off topic stories and runs through his powerpoints without doing a great job at explaining things for understanding.

He's a cool professor, but the class was basically a repeat of AP Stats, but less in depth. I used my old AP textbook/notes and mostly self-studied, I only went to class sometimes for iclicker extra credit. Super easy for the statistically-inclined. He uses stories to try to keep the class awake, although they didn't always work, haha.
Definitely one of my favorite professors I've ever had. Super funny in class. He tells stories that help you get through the class and a  subject that maybe you're not super keen on.

Dr. Tolley is literally the man! I took Stat 121 with him two years ago and he is what inspired me to be a Stat Major. He does tell random stories sometimes but they always relate to the material and are comedic relief to help us get through hard material. He'll always be willing to help accommodate you.  I wish I could take every class with him!

Dr Tolley is amazing! He is a hilarious guy with many years spent in the statistics field. He loves telling stories of when he used certain statistics principles in his career, making the class feel more practical. Go to class, take the quizzes, and go to lab and you do great. Thoroughly enjoyed his class!

Dr. Tolley is the hilarious grandpa that everyone wants to have. He is a stats genius which will sometimes leave students confused, but he is just on the verge of crazy. That is what makes him the professor that he is. GO TO LAB!!! They are there to help you and it is essential to do well n the class!
He is a great professor. If you do well on the tests you will be fine.

Dr. Tolley's lectures were practically the highlight of my day! He's extremely funny and it's obvious that he really loves statistics. This was a really easy class for me (there's hardly any actual calculation math).  Also, he drops your 4 lowest quiz scores at the end of the semester, which was great. I highly recommend him!

His lectures are pretty useless. He's a funny guy, but speeds through important material. I learned more just by studying the online textbook. In fact, there was a period where I didn't go to lecture at all,  just used the online textbook, and I still aced all the quizzes and exams—and this having never taken a STATS class before.

Dr. Tolley is an incredible story teller. Unfortunately, he teaches mostly theory so it is difficult to understand the material. The assignments are hard and the book is no help at all. It's a hard class and a hard professor, but if you pass the P exam, you're guaranteed an A. It's only worth it if you plan on taking the P exam.

Professor Tolley is hilarious! He moves a little quickly sometimes, and it's such a big class that he doesn't have much time to help individually. Compared to the other statistics teachers that substituted for him, he is the best and most entertaining. If you go to labs you should be fine.

This class was always enjoyable. Dr. Tolley is extremely funny. He always realized when class interest disappeared and was able to bring it back. The class was not hard at all. The tests were easy. I loved it.
Loved him! Although I'm not the best on catching onto mathematical concepts, he taught the class well, and kept the class interesting by telling stories to break up the monotony.

EASY class.  Got a 99% in the class with very little effort.  I did, however, have an excellent TA, which really helps.  Lecture are pretty dull and boring, but I've heard Tolley is one of the better lecturers.  Go to lab to do the homework, and know how to interpret the test equations and symbols and you will be just fine.

Professor Tolley is actually one of the best professors I've had. He's super funny, knows Stats like the back of his hand, and cares about his students. Sometimes he'll move quickly through material, but he was always willing to answer questions. This was not a hard class, and I felt like I learned a lot about statistics.

Dr Tolley is the best teacher I've ever had. And after 7 years of college, I've had a lot! He is very generous with the assignments and grading, and very approachable when you have questions. He is excellent!

Great professor. Easiest stats class out there. That being said, stats sucks unless you're a natural. Tolley has the easiest work load and best shot at getting an A.  He is HILARIOUS. If you're trying to learn stats to actually LEARN stats... you may want another teacher. If you are taking this because it's required and want a good grade, take him.

He is crazy. He doesn't really care about students, and the exam is ridiculous, homework can't be graded on time, some of them are ungraded! it's unfair. The grade is very hard to get even if u spend a lot of time on it, though this class is hard.   Avoid him if possible!!

Dr. Tolley was a pretty good teacher.  He really knows Stats very well, and his stories were pretty fun.  Sometimes I'd reather he wouldn't tell them so we could get out earlier, but it was still fun.  He offers opportunities for extra credit and if you study for the tests and listen in class, it's a pretty easy A.

One of the best lectures I've ever had.  I learn best by lecture and not book.  Of course I want to do Stat's as my major and have 5 years of experience in the real world.  Good teacher, he just has little control over the tests since the department handles that and grading.
Professor Tolley is not a very good professor.  Even my TA said he was confused about what he was teaching.  He goes way too fast and skips slides that are important, just to get out of class early.

Dr. Tolley is the worst professor I have ever had.  Going to class is a complete wast of time.  I have no respect for him and he is VERY rude to the TAs.  He is not motivating and tells stupid stories that made me fall asleep.  I would never take a class from him ever again
He is a funny guy, but not good at explaining stats too well. he is very scatter brained, though tells good stories. the TA helped me the most.

Professor Tolley is the man! He is the best statistics teacher out there. The class is VERY easy if you just do your homework and study a few hours for the test. His lectures are HILARIOUS and you  get tons of extra credit in his class. the tests are easy and he gives you a practice exam VERY similair to the actual test every time. GREAT CLASS!!!

Tolley is great; he's interesting, tells stories when it gets boring, very clear, eager to help, but he doesn't let you see your tests unless you attend an extra lab hour that I couldn't, so I couldn't find out what I did wrong.  I REALLY hated htat and it hurt me a lot in the class, but if it weren't for that I'd definitely take the class again.

Dr. Tolley is a good teacher. His lectures were good but I got most of the class through the TAs and going over the slides and the book. The class is kind of tough and requires a lot of work. If this class is a necessary evil the I would recommend him. The tests are not too bad, but are time consuming (2-3 hours).
He's so funny. I liked this class. he's funny and if everyone looks like they're not getting it, he rephrases it and tries to clarify.
He actually made statistics funny. We were laughing through the whole class but I was actually learning, too.
The best teacher I have ever had!!!!!  No one has ever increased my interest more for statistics than him.  He has a great talent!
It's worth taking Stats 441 just to take a class from him.
Dr. Tolley's class is an absolute waste of time.  Read the text - you'll get more out of it.  Dr. Tolley spends most of the class period telling lame jokes and tooting his own horn.
Dr. Tolley is hilarious, and he knows it.  It is difficult to determine how much he really cares about the student.  I think the stats people like him, though.

His class is a bit of a challenge as far as religion classes go, but he's very bold in lectures, which worked great for me, not so much for others. He isn't shy about explaining calmly how most members of the church could still do a lot better. If you don't want a reality check, don't take this class.

I grew accustomed to his realist and semi-rude demeanor after about 6 weeks. If you don't like writing, don't take this class. He grades on an absurd scale. However, I was impressed by his willingness to change the course after the first midterm- he gave us longer time on the quizzes and less on the final. I hated the role playing though.

Attending this class was fine but the work outside of it was absurd. There's a 5 page single-spaced take home mid-term and final and each week you have to spend 2-3 hours doing a reading assignment followed by a quiz. The quiz questions are so obscure and you have so little time that you can't easily find them in the lessons. Take REL C elsewhere

I usually have a problem with religion teachers and religion classes at BYU, Professor Wright is the exception is the exception.  Hes not dogmatic but hes informative, he has a sense of humor and hes a realist.  Tests and assignments are not hard, online and open book. Wright is actually OPEN MINDED and he has a sense of humor.  Take Wright's class

He is an amazing professor!He isn't your typical religion professor(it's not touchy,feely class)he actually teaches you facts and insights.he is open minded to every question & admits when he doesn't know & i love that in a religion professor.Visit him in his office cause he likes to know his students& he can help you if you are having a hard time.

Brother Wright was an awesome!!! I loved his class! Be active in class and you'll get an A also go in and visit him, Brother Wright loves getting to know his students...the best religion class I have taken so far

This class was one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken.  Bro Wright is one of the nicest, most helpful professors I have had.  He always responded to my emails and helped with my questions.  All tests and quizzes open book.  He is a very fair grader.  Just go to class and be involved and you'll get an A.

Br. Wright's class was the best class I have ever taken at BYU.  It offered ideas and insights that complemented Church doctrine in new ways -not the tired concepts you learn over and over. The class doesn't focus on memorization, but personal application and deep understanding.  I wish I could take every class from him! I highly recommend him!

Don't listen to past comments. Bro Wright wants his students to learn and feel comfortable to ask any question. He isn't going to trick you, only help learn the material. I was always so excited to go to class because I knew we would have deep discussions, and I would still do well on assignments. Best religion class I've taken.

Dr. Wright created one of the best learning environments I have ever experienced in a class.  All class members felt open to participate and the class became highly interactive, in the best possible way.
This man is amazing. I learned alot. All quizzes and tests are opened book.

His personality gets some getting used to, but he's funny once you get to know him. His tests are cake if you take them online (avoid the testing center test, and do the online practice tests several times and you'll be fine).

His tests are ridiculous.  I studied hard for them and they were still out of this world hard.  I also thought he posed a very negative attitude while in class toward students, Joseph Smith, etc.  I didn't like his teaching style, alhtough he was good to approach out of class.
I learned a ton in this class. For all you winey people, you should have just studied for the test. He is pretty hard, but really smart.

By far the best religion professor I have ever had. He took time with me to help me learn. His insights into the D&C are incredible. Some find him arrogant. I disagree. He cares about his students, and loves teaching the subject.

I took D&C online, so although I never met the man, I am not impressed with him as a teacher at all. Anyone who uses the word "warning" as a subject line in all his emails has got something wrong. He seemed arrogant and rude. The class was ridiculous, the quiz questions vague, and trivial facts were emphasized instead of the gospel.

I took this class through independent study and was assigned Bro. Wright. The lessons were good and I learned a lot, and got A's on all the homework. BUT...on the final, worth half my grade, I got an 80, and Bro. Wright refused to talk to me about it because I was not a "real student" at BYU. Thanks, pal. My advice: stay away!

He is the most smug, arrogant, self-righteous, condescending professor I've ever had. He acts like he walks on water, and that the rest of us are just lucky to breathe the same air as he does. His tests are ridiculously hard (memorizing tons of dates, map locations, obscure facts). Stay far away from this guy!
No Comments
250 question final worth about 65-75% of your final grade.  Need I say more?

Quiz questions vague and easily interpreted differently.  Likes to trick you.  The online class was really worthless.  Felt like he focused way too much on "who's who" as opposed to doctrine.  Questions like, who sat in the third row in the 4th seat when Proph Joseph gave this talk.  Not fun.

The class was worthless. More interested in "who sneezed when sec. 121 was given" than actual spiritual knowledge or useful history. Never met the guy, but he contributed nothing to my learning and tested from the CD, manual, scriptures, not his own stuff. I could make a better class.
The online class is fine for those who like that kind of thing.  One problem is that sometimes quiz questions can be vague and unclear.  Doesn't take up too much time.
Excellent teacher.  Very knowledable and a great sense of humor.  The tests were super easy.

Br. Wright expects a lot out of his students, but rewards them with incredible insights into the scriptures and their application in our day.  If you want to learn powerful doctrine from Church History, he's the man.  The best religion class I've taken at BYU!

Bro. Wright is great!  He tells you exactly what to study for tests, not to mention, uses lots of questions from quizzes.  He's pretty unorthodox in his teaching, but really makes you think.  He's a great teacher and you'll learn tons and be entertained.

Comes across as very arrogant and condescending, likes to put students on the spot and watch them squirm.  His tests are very hard and focus on very nit-picky things like matching D&C section numbers with exact dates, etc.

Dr. Haderlie is one of the best philosophy teachers in all Utah. Having been to classes at BYU and Salt Lake, the difference is huge between him and other professors. The class is very difficult for most people, that really can't be avoided. But, Dr. Haderlie does all he can to help you succeed and learn it fully. Amazing lectures.

Haderlie is an amazing guy but this class was killer. There were five short papers and all were graded very harshly. There were two oral exams which were tough to prep for. The reading load is heavy and not all the material gets covered in class. Some of the content is great but some is very dry. It's a 400 level but still, very tough

Dr. Haderlie is super charismatic and is clearly very knowledgable on the material he teaches, class feels very stimulating. The course is very difficult, however, Dr. Haderlie and his TA's are VERY available and willing to help. Without going to TA hours for help you're pretty much doomed. If you're trying to fulfill the GE credit, go elsewhere.

One of my favorite professors at BYU! Dr. Haderlie is incredibly smart, but also humble. And his lectures are hilarious! I loved taking this class and highly recommend taking a class from him if you get a chance. He changed my life.

205 was very difficult for me and I ended up dropping the class since the TA hours conflicted with my work schedule, but Dr. Haderlie did a great job of teaching and helping after class and is a great professor! I took 205 from another professor and TA labs were still so crucial to doing well

Dr. Haderlie is the best professor at BYU. He is hilarious and yet so caring. Take this class to fulfill your GE. Only four assignments but graded very generously. I didn't the readings until the exam and did really well. He is so genuine in his views of the gospel, which means sometimes he is wonderfully NOT regretfully sacrilegious. Go to class

Dr. Haderlie is an excellent professor. He is compassionate and relatable. 413 was one of the more difficult classes I've taken but also one I learned the most in. I walked away from this class with a deeper understanding of ethics and morality. I would highly recommend taking a class from Dr. Haderlie. His classes are worth the work they require.

Dr. Haderlie is a good professor. The lectures do not prepare you adequately for the HW so beware. Utilisation of outside resources are crucial, TAs especially. It is a relatively easy A if you do that.

I think Dr. Haderlie is a great guy. I found this class a little challening, especially because the TAs were basically unavailable outside the logic lab. You have to be very resourceful. I would recommend taking this if you are taking upper level logic classes, but if you aren't taking logic classes in the future, this is beyond what you need.

Dr. Haderlie is honestly such a good and caring professor. Going to the lectures is definitely a must as they will help in the assignments but also going to the TA hours can guarantee an A in the course. They are willing to help you check your work and help you understand the concepts more but just know that they don't have an answer. Def recommend

BYU really focuses on a great undergraduate teaching experience, and it shows in how many amazing professors there are. Even among the best professors I've had Dr. Haderlie stands out as special. He genuinely cares about the success of each student and will go above and beyond to ensure they have the tools and the means to learn and do well.

Dr. Haderlie is a great professor who clear cares about his students and his work. His classes are entertaining and he is generally effective at explaining material. Every once in awhile I feel like he doesn't undertand the questions that students are asking, hence the 4 instead of 5 rating. Overall though a great teacher who cares a lot.

Dr. Haderlie is a great professor and has a ton of great insight that he shares in a very inspirational and thought-provoking way. The class relies heavily on discussion, which Dr. Haderlie does a great job of leading without dominating the conversation. If you want a philosophy class that you can really get into, Dr. Haderlie will provide.

Dr. Haderlie is a great professor. His lectures are engaging and hilarious, and he is able to explain difficult concepts in a simple and clear way. I highly recommend him. I have taken a couple of classes from him, and in each of his classes, he is caring, funny, and passionate about his work.

PHIL305 is a tough class but Dr. Haderlie does a great job explaining the tricky concepts. The entire grade is 9 homework assignments and 4 exams, so a little stressful if you don't enjoy that. Genuinely hilarious and good person.

Dr. Haderlie does an excellent job with intro to the philosophy of religion. Readings are not required (but they're excellent, and free, so you should read them!). Extremely thought-provoking and enjoyable.

Professor Haderlie is INCREDIBLE. 
His classes are hit or miss, but it is all about you, not him. Easy A. What you need to work for, and what Haderlie's teaching makes you want to work for, is an introspective look at what you're learning, and a true understanding of the content. If you didn't like the class you didn't understand it.

Dr. Haderlie is by far my favorite professor at BYU so far. His lectures are very entertaining. They are both educational and hilarious. I think his humor is by far my favorite. Not only is he a great teacher, but he is a brilliant and inspiring person. He is incredibly caring and wants students to have a good experience in his classes.

A pathetic hypocrite teaching an incredibly easy A class; tragically believes efforts may make up IQ. (English and phil are easy so I understand) Contents were stupid and ad hoc (doom Cuneo's trashy "isomorphism" -- an insult to math). This class entrenched my impression to philosophy -- stupidly easy, seldom applicable, and never rigorous at all.
The readings are tough but Dr. Haderlie is a fun guy. I've taken him twice now and highly recommend him.

I really liked Prof. Haderlie, but this class was kinda boring. Make sure you write a lot in your journal or he will take off points. There are no exams so it's super easy, but the course material isn't the most interesting and sometimes the lectures drag a bit. I could tell my classmates enjoyed the class, but I don't think it was for me.

Dr Haderlie is my favorite professor at BYU!!! He is a very reasonable when it comes to grades, tests, homework, etc. His lectures are HILARIOUS--maybe he should rethink his career choice and be a stand-up comedian. Joking aside, he is very smart, humble, and instigates thought-provoking conversation in class. The class was easy and I learned alot!

Easy A class -- philosophy is super easy and straightforward as usual. The materials are entertaining (I love Clarke-Doane's paper!) and explore my mind to multiple topics (time, modal realism, identity, etc.) Due to the limited-term length, this class covers only a small part of contemporary metaphysics, so outside-class readings are necessary.

Took PHIL 213 with Dr Haderlie and it was a very easy GE. Barely any homework and some of the topics were interesting. He understands that most of the students are here for a general and conducts as such. Would highly recommend, he’s engaging and makes things interesting.
Good professor and easy class.

Dr. Haderlie is amazing! If you take this class, do not miss ANY of the metareflections. They're only worth a few points, but they can tank your grade. Do the readings and follow instructions and you shouldn't have too much trouble. I think that the only reason I didn't love the class is because I hate the subject, but Dr. Haderlie is awesome!

Never did the reading but felt really good about the class. It's just a discussion of people's views on stuff and digging deeper into religion. I am a big fan of how the class is oriented. You have one homework each week that's a reflection, so easy. And the tests are open note, and he tells you the question before.

Dr. Haderlie is an AMAZING professor and I really learned a lot in the class. He genuinely cares about his students & is very understanding. The class itself wasn't too difficult though there were some tough concepts. But he helps you with the problem sets and the TAs are great as well. As long as you are putting in the effort to learn, youll be ok

Dr. Haderlie is a gem. He is super caring and does everything within his power to ensure that his students understand the material, which at times can be challenging. Outside of class, he is quite accessible and responds to inquires quickly. Also, he is *hilarious* so lectures are engaging. Please take 205 from Dr. Haderlie!

Professor Haderlie is a young professor and very caring about his students. He isn't out to prove that he's the best professor ever, but he does a great job a simply being that. He uses discord in the online classes and is very quick to respond there. The textbook is online and free; he provided it in the first few days of class.

Dr. Haderlie is a fantastic teacher. Definitely on my top 5 favorite teachers at BYU. He is extremely caring, very knowledgeable. His lectures and recorded lectures are excellent. He makes incredible podcasts; his readings are insightful; he is friendly and thoughtful. His book was an online tool that is helpful and easy to interact with other peer

I had a B+ in this class until he automatically failed me for missing too many classes.  He thinks he's really funny and expects way too much out of an intro class. This guy has a complex to have to change your mind because he wasn't successful in life.  Not the worst professor, but also not worth taking his class.

Derek is a great teacher.  He doesn't make us do more work than necessary, but gives us plenty of opportunities to read, discuss, and write about the coursework.  He's funny at times and will take time to explain difficult concepts during class.  If you still don't understand he'll be happy to talk to you afterward or during his office hours.

Would not recommend this class with this professor, The homework load for a religion class is a joke. pages and pages of reading every week, just for him to stand up and unload his life issues on the class. buy the Saints books and read them on your own and it will be a better professor then this class was while he taught
Brother Sainsbury's class is ridiculously hard. I do not recommend anyone to take this class
I don't love the way the course is set up. He's really good at teaching the material but there is a lot of busywork.
amazing professor, makes you work

I really enjoyed his teaching style and his lectures. Requires attendance and gives a decent amount of homework for a religion class. Lots of readings and some homework every weekend. Really passionate about what he teaches.

I often felt like the assignments did not align with the class material. Pre-class reading is INTENSE! Be prepared to read 1-2 hours before every class, pretty much 4 hours of just reading every week. This does not include all the weekly assignments every single week. Professor does not work with you very well.

Requires mandatory group work that is impossible to receive a good grade in if your group members fail to do their part, as you need to respond to their submissions. Constantly teaches non-doctrine material, and instead of email uses your personal phone number to reach out to you.

He's very easy, he just assigns a lot of homework, at least compared to other religion classes, so be ready for that. A reading (usually super long) and quiz every class, a post about your topic every week, and a few essays and projects throughout the semester, but VERY passionate and engaging.

The professor relies heavily on assigned readings and written responses instead of clear in-class explanation. Key concepts are often not synthesized or reinforced, forcing students to piece material together independently. The approach emphasizes volume over clarity, making expectations and core ideas difficult to grasp.

I love him! Genuinely an inspirational figure in my life. He feels very human, and he's very wise in a lot of ways. I took his class just for the Foundations of Restoration credit, but he taught me so much about the controversial topics. Lots of reading and classes are only lectures, but he's engaging and hilarious. I could listen to him for hours!

I love Prof. Sainsbury! He shows genuine interest in what students have to say and their thoughts. But this is a Level 300 class, which means that there is homework due before lecture. They aren't hard, but they can be a bit time consuming depending on the reading (I skimmed for important bits and was perfectly fine). But 10/10, would recommend!

Professor Sainsbury is a great teacher. I just think the content was hard. We had to read multiple chapters of Saints before every class, along with other readings. Quizzes before every class required 500 word responses at times. I did enjoy going to the actual class though. If you want a challenge, go for it

I took his restoration class right after my mission and I learned some incredible things that I wished that I had known before my mission about how to interpret the past and find answers to questions. I took this class and it has made an incredible impact on my life. He is an incredible teacher and loves all his students. Be ready to read andlearn

The class is very easy to pass, but will require a large amount of participation. Lots of reading outside of class. He is incredibly knowledgable and has answers to hard questions that people tend to shy away from.
Loved the class. Probably more than two credits of work though.

If you want to have a nice 2-credit class, do not take this class. I took it with a couple of friends, and it was insane, the amount of work. This class has so much work involved, and all he does is lecture. He takes forever to grade. Be ready to have 4 essays, 3 tests, 1 major project, and 3 hours of readings a week. Avoid this class at all costs.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He teaches false things. Your grade depends upon on other people writing a small essays every week. There is also A TON OF READING. Almost 3 hours worth every week and its not scripture or general conference talks. it is his own writing.

Please do not take this class. He mixes things that are true with things that are not true. I have never heard more false doctrine and it is making me very confused. There is a lot of group work and your grade relies on everyone writing a small essay every week. There is also SO MUCH READING (and he wrote it so it often has false doctrine).
A lot of your grade is based on group projects. Your group is chosen for you by the professor.
Too Much Reading. The professor often gose off on tangents that are not factually true. The professor has many opinions that contradict the university's policy.

Sainsbury had fantastic lectures when teaching. Everything about actually being in the classroom was great, and I felt very prepared for the tests...but HOLY READINGS, DUDE! You need to read like, two hours of readings per class and then take short tests on them, which felt like a lot. Just get ready for that if you take his class.
Great lectures. Prof Sainsbury really loves and cares for each student. Lots of reading!

Brother Sainsbury was AWESOME for this course. He would write his own readings for each class, which were long but super interesting. He graded super generously and it was exactly what a religion class should be: insightful, learner-based, and not at all stressful. He really knows his stuff. Definitely take Foundations of the Restoration from him

Bro. Sainsbury is an incredibly entertaining professor. Loved attending his lectures and I felt like I always learned something in each of his classes. However, there are A LOT of assignments, most of which felt like busywork. I would not recommend taking this class if you're looking for a chill and easy religion class.

I like Brother Sainsbury, but this class was insanely demanding for no reason. So much reading, like 6 hours a week. So many assignments, but I wouldn't say it was necessarily difficult. Go to class, skim the readings, and you'll do fine. Just a lot of busy work. However, Brother Sainsbury is an awesome professor for this class. He is very smart

Bro Sainsbury is a nice guy. I have pretty neutral feelings about this class overall but I wouldn't really recommend it to anyone. Incredibly time consuming outside of class and a lot of assignments that feel like busywork. Strict on attendance but intellectually engaging. If you want a fun chill religion class I wouldn't suggest taking this one.

Sainsbury had a tendency to go off on tangents that had nothing to do with the material, and often were incredibly factually incorrect. There is a slew of projects and papers that will catch up to you really fast at the end of the semester. You don't get the opportunity to start working on them early. Lectures became progressively less coherent.

Professor Sainsbury is actually a great great teacher! At first I wasn't sure about the class, but as the class went on i really learned to love him. He has a quiz due before every class period based on reading a lesson that would usually take about 2hrs to read. Lots of work tbh for a religion class is the reason i gave him a level 4 difficulty.

About 70 minutes of reading twice a week. I learned more in this religion class than any other one I have taken thus far. I always left feeling spiritually uplifted. The only downside was the weekly group assignments. There are several projects but it never felt overwhelming, but it does push you out of your comfort zone. He is very kind and fun.
Brother Sainsbury is amazing. An amazing balance of challenging and engaging, but not overbearing. He cares so much for his students. Would take again!

Brother Sainsbury was a very caring professor who's lectures were very interesting and fun! The workload is a lot but it's not hard to do. Didn't have any tests, just a couple of projects that I enjoyed. He is a very fair grader and gives opportunities to get extra credit. I really enjoyed taking this class!

Super caring, funny dude. Really ready to talk about difficult gospel topics. This class definitely had more reading than other religion classes I've taken, but it's a 300 level class and it's a college course (i.e., not seminary).
Teaches well. There is a lot of reading. Didn't give a final exam.

While there is a significant workload in this class (lots of reading, writing, and assignments), learning from this professor is amazing and enjoyable. I think all the work is worth it. I looked forward to each class with Pro. Sainsbury and he is also really funny and caring. He grades fairly and provides many opportunities for extra credit.

I really liked Brother Sainsbury because he has an interesting perspective on the gospel. I will say his lectures were dependent on the readings, so you def had to read before class. I didn't like how a lot of the class depended on your assigned group's participation.

This was an amazing class. I learned so much and was able to feel the spirit every single class. He does it in a flipped classroom style. Which I felt was extremely beneficial because I learned everything before and then brought questions to class. The tests were super easy, and he made it very easy to succeed. Just do the readings before class!

There were so many final projects and I spent way too many hours each week on this class. There are 1+ hour readings before each class that have a review quiz. "Seeking Answers Skills" is the theme of this class but I still don't understand that. If you truly want to go into depth about church history, great class. Concepts make no sense sometimes.

Prof Sainsbury knows his stuff and I like what he taught. He seems like a really good guy and is super funny and nice. However, WAY too much work for a religion class. 5 hours of service, 3 midterms, 2-3 papers, 2 weekly quizzes, final project, and digital dialogues (300-500 words and responding meaningfully to 3 others)
Just too much. Don't take.

There are way too many people glazing this professor here. In reality, he's horrible. Way too much work for a rel class. Hours of homework each week and giant projects. If you have other hard classes then you're especially in trouble with grades.

Brother Sainsbury is awesome! I took Rel C 225 from him. He is a great example of what I want from a religion professor. He cares a lot about your own understanding. The graded material is not your readings, but rather a series of apply 'seeking answers' skills to understand the topics well, aka: easy. The lectures were awesome and he cares a lot.

Derek is a super spiritual teacher with very interesting course materials that he MAKES you learn. You feel smarter leaving his class the last time. Cons: Lots of homework, due on Saturdays and you have to rely on OTHERS to do it with, which sucks if you get a bum group it's tough going. He's also a reasonably hard grader. But either way loved it!

I genuinely think Sainsbury is a great person, but the class is horrible. It is filled with so much busy work. I spent more time on this class than any other class. You have two weekly reading quizzes (1-2 hours each), a weekly digital dialogue (300-500 words), 5 hours of service, a major project, midterms, and two final papers. Wouldn't reccomend.

This class was wayyy too much work for a 2 credit religion class imo, but at least none of it's difficult so basically as long as you do everything you'll be fine. I enjoyed lectures, which were more like class discussions, and learned a lot from the reading even though it was long. Take from someone else if you can, if not, this class is fine.

I LOVED this class and learned so much. That being said, it's a lot of work for a religion class. Bro Sainsbury cares so much about the Restoration and focuses everything on Christ. You will be prepared to defend your faith and help others understand church history in a way you never have before. Fun midterms, no final, just some papers.

Honestly, the worst class I've ever taken. Double the amount of work of a real 2 credit class. Lots of useless assignments such as going to a museum for 2 hours. 6 page essay due on the last week of class. 2 quizzes and a digital dialogue weekly on top of 4 hours of reading. Hes also extremely unforgiving with grading and due dates. DO NOT SIGN UP!
One of the most kind, heartfelt professors I have taken from. Interesting lectures.

Brother Sainsbury is awesome. The readings are pretty time consuming, but they are super good, so it makes it worth it. He really understands the Restoration and teaches it very well. 10/10 recommend him to anyone.

Brother Sainsbury is a fun person and cares about his students. But he's not a great professor. He's very unorganized. Several times the class readings were not posted on time. The reading and lectures could be confusing at times. We were put in "Zion groups," but I had no idea what function they served. Too much homework for a 2 credit class.

REL 225 with Brother Sainsbury was amazing! You usually have just over an hour of reading to do before each class period which isn't bad for a religion class. He also offers a ton of extra credit. I ended his class with over 100% and it's very doable to get an A. Midterms are straightforward he never tries to trick you. Also no final, just a paper.

He's great. His lectures are good. He's a funny teacher- engaging. There is a lot of reading and you need to manage your time well. There are two midterms but no final. There is a final essay instead. The midterms are very doable if you actually print out the notes he tells you to print. There is a big project- also doable with time management.

Professor Sainsbury is an awesome guy. He is super knowledgeable and explains gospel topics in an exciting way. I really enjoyed his enthusiasm and how much he truly cares about his students. The class is hard though, there is a lot of reading and tests are long. Overall, the experience was worth it. You'll learn a lot in this class.

Professor Sainsbury's class isn't awful by any means, but be prepared to do a lot of reading each week. The quizzes before class require background knowledge (the reading) and take a lot of thought the majority of the time. There are group discussions each week and the two midterms were both written this semester and took 2.5 hours a piece.
You either love him or hate him. It's easy to get through his class without learning anything. Lots of assignments and projects. Especially group projects.

Bro Sainsbury is a great guy and can be fun and full of humor. His class is not structured well. It is very difficult to learn from his lectures and it feels like he just talks about whatever he wants and not what we should be learning about the Restoration.His assignments are horrible and lots of your grade is based on working with other students.

This was the worst class I have ever taken at BYU. Study guides for the exams did nothing to help you prepare for the material, thus resulting in you feeling lost as soon as you read the first question. Not to mention there were about 8 hours of homework a week on top of everything else. A complete mess of a class that I would suggest you avoid

Without a doubt, the worst religion class I have ever taken, an ungodly amount of busy work week after week + they give out a study guide for the exams and none of the questions on the study guide pertain to any of the exam material. -1/10, avoid this class like the plague.

Three weeks into this class, it has been the most time-consuming religion course I have ever taken. This class is supposed to be a "2 credit hour class," however, the first week of class required 8 hours of modules, and the second week required 4 hours of in-class work, keep in mind this is what is required in class and not outside of class. AVOID!

I absolutely loved Dr. Sainsbury's class. He has become one of my favorite professors at BYU and he is extremely considerate of students' needs. He is very open about his personal struggles and he provides a living record and witness of the power of the gospel of Jesus Christ. Every class was super powerful, and I hope he stays at BYU.

He is so great! Made boring lecture topic interesting and always relevant. He used to be a seminary teacher, and it shows--he is great with connecting and really cares about the students and the content. A big teddy bear pretty much. (He also clearly outlays his expectations--attendance is crucial, but as long as you're there...easy money.)

Brother Sainsbury is one of the best professors I've had at BYU, I would recommend taking him for Foundations of the Restoration. He's extremely smart and can talk about any topic in depth and with ease. Anyone was able to ask any question they wanted and he really lets you know that he's on your side. He's a forgiving grader but loves hard work.

There were SO many readings before every class and a digital dialogue every week. Lectures every class but they were interesting and he answered any questions people had. He didn't skirt around the difficult topics but would sometimes interrupt when students voiced their concerns. He taught in an entertaining way, and was an good teacher overall.

I really enjoyed his class, the lectures were really interesting. There is a lot of reading to do but it's pretty manageable. He's also open to final project ideas for the class. The exams were more difficult than they needed to be, with a lot of essay-type questions, they're open scripture but paper only, and your notes have to be written inside.

Read some other reviews and I agree, take what everyone says and put it together. Amazing, funny, inspirational, truly listens to students. Nightmare class tho. Digital dialogs every week �� Crazy amount of reading. Short answer test questions. Great guy, hardest religion class I've ever taken at byu. Steer clear if you have a hard major.

I learned a lot when in Sainsbury's class. He is very inspirational and funny in lectures. He also loves when you ask questions and will take the time so everyone is comfortable. He does have a lot of pre-class reading but it is great material. He is also pretty straightforward on his tests and your work is peer reviewed and graded by him.

He has no structure to his lectures, and they're l.e.c.t.u.r.e.s. Long winded. Boring as heck. Random. Lectures. There are so many little things for you to remember to do and the study guides are 6 pages long with random information. Take notes on literally everything he says because his tests are guessing games about things he said one time.

Professor Sainsbury is my least favorite religion professor Ive had here at BYU. His lectures and tests just feel like He is just trying to show to how much he knows and he is very cocky about his knowledge. All his tests are guess what Im thinking games and most of what you are tested on seems like it is just how he interpreted things...

BR SAINSBURY IS AMAZING! His class is not very hard -2 easy essays, 1 midterm, 1 final, weekly readings and forum. He's an easy grader. Lectures are educational and spiritually enriching. He's funny and authentic -not cookie cutter Utah type. Most importantly he cares about his students. I met with him outside of class and he helped me SO MUCH.

Brother Sainsbury is pretty great. He truly cares and wants you to succeed. The tests are a little difficult, but they don't seem to count for much after the participation and readings are in tact. Most BYU religion professors focus on making things extremely difficult rather than focus on the student. Bro Sainsbury wants to help your testimony.

Prof Sainsbury is a good man. He is my only professor who has taken the time to learn my name. The class is an easy A bc we self-grade our participation and he gives nearly everyone 100s on papers, but his exams are extremely difficult. His lectures are spiritually uplifting, but tend to go on tangents to topics not on the exams he gives.

My main issue with this class was that there were so many readings. I felt like I didn't get much out of them because I just had to try and get through them. The first midterm was also really tricky because he expected us to write a certain amount and graded us on hw much we wrote, but he never told us we would have to do that.

Each week you self grade how well you participated in class, whether you did the readings and study questions, and how much you posted in the weekly discussion board. Papers weren't bad at all, and going to the review lecture and taking extensive notes in your scriptures is good for tests. Dr. Sainsbury is great and always willing to talk/help.

Wonderful teacher. Caring, takes time to explain things again, has good organization. If you work on the main principles taught you'll do fine. 2 essays, 2 pre-readings a week, all easy to get good grades on. Tests are a bit harder. He's good at tying things in spiritually but it's not overdone.
Great professor who knows what he's talking about, not too much work if you pace yourself.
Absolutely fantastic professor! He loves his students very much and wants them to get close to the Savior. I learned a lot of cool stuff.
Professor Sainsbury was so nice and I learned so much from his class. On the midterm though there was a lot of stuff about the Old Testament so make sure to pay attention to the stuff he mentions.

I learned a lot of valuable information. It is a hard course and the final is ridiculously long and challenging, but the information you learn in this class is great and the assignments are worth it. Get ready to read and memorize though because it is rough.

I appreciated taking this class on demand since I got to deep dive into the material on my own schedule.  Assignments are pretty straightforward with a decent late work policy (10% reduction each day). The test questions are given to you beforehand, just make sure you actually prepare. Loved my TA, didn't get much interaction with Professor Cobia.

They just changed the entire course structure this semester!!  Each week you have: 1-2 hours of video lecture, 1 hour journal, 1 hour weekly write up, 1 discussion post (250-300 words). For exams (2x), he gives you 7 prompts but you only get tested on 4 (3-4 paragraphs). Finally theres a stupid timeline project that is done through ppt. dont take:(

loved this class! seems like a great guy, just never saw much of him besides weekly intro vids. easy class, but I liked the materials he provided. up to you wether or not you learn. TAs gave VERY clear reviews for exams, don't stress. get to use AI for short essays. every other discussion you just post a song that can relate to psych. recommend!!
Very easy class, it's pass or fail. Lots of helpful information about grad school, mostly geared towards students looking to get a clinical psych PhD.

Probably one of the easiest online courses I've taken. We just had a couple of relatively simple assignments every week including reading quizzes, an occasional short paper, and super helpful test reviews from the TAs for the midterm and final. If you must take this class for the major, would recommend taking it online from Professor Cobia.
Easiest psych class I've ever had. Online through Canvas. Almost entirely done with the TAs. Two exams. Exams are easy if you use the TA reviews (the final took me

Dr Cobia was okay. I personally wouldn't take him again, but it was a class I have to take as a PSYCH major. there are two homework assignments each week which are small but it feels like a drag. there's not a lot of assistance or help outside of class. There are 2 exams- midterm and final, however they're both online proctored which is nice.

Take PSYCH 210 online from Dr. Cobia. The course is conducted through Canvas. You just need to do a short easy quiz & a discussion post each week and you have a short paper every other week. He literally has you use ChatGPT for your essays. I got an A on the exams just from attending the TA reviews.

I would read the textbook at least in the beginning while you get a feel for the class. Online. Relatively easy. Discussions and quizzes/short papers due wednesdays and saturdays. Not a hard class. TA reviews made the test the easiest thing in the world (if you follow the TA reviews you WILL get a high A on the tests). 2 tests the whole year.

simple and easy class. one group project per week that is very easy and one chapter write-up that is very simple. He explains the relevant chapter from the textbook during his lectures. The lectures are invigorating and he leads by discussion. Definitely my favorite class because of the lectures. Studying for Midterm/final was easy to study for.
weekly writeups, a group activity, one midterm, and a final make up the course. Go to class and ask questions. Cobia is funny and cares. If you need to take this course take it from Cobia!

Totally recommend doing this class online! I mostly interacted with the TA's, who were super helpful, but Professor Cobia was also accessible whenever I needed his help. There is a fair bit of reading, but the assignments are not difficult, and neither are the tests.

Dr Cobia is amazing! So long as you remember to submit your 2 assignments per week, you will do great. BEWARE  TAs are tough graders on the midterm/final. You are fully prepared for the 2 tests unlike any other class but TAs grade differently and very harshly. The lectures turn philosophical a lot but it is interesting. Group assignments are fun!

Professor Cobia was an amazing teacher!  He had very little assignments one you would do on your own with ChatGBT and the other in class discussion assignment each week. He gives you 7 of 5 discussion question that appear on the test. So truly the work you put in is the grade you get if you prep for the test you get a good grade!

I took his on-demand course of PSYCH 210 and it was really easy! You have a short paper due every week along with a quiz and a discussion board (which are super easy). Attend the midterm and final exam review and you will get a good grade on the exams. I got an A on both from just attending the reviews. Trust me, take it from him!!

I love Dr Cobia. He truly cares about students. The homework load was okay. Not the best...not the worst. He knew the names of everyone in his 60+ person class. He knew mine at the beginning of the semester despite staying quiet in class.

Dr. Cobia's class was super easy. The textbook readings are quite lengthy, but the assignments themselves are pretty straightforward and simple. He gives you a study guide with all the questions that could potentially be on the midterm and final. Honestly, just keep up with the work and turn in your stuff and attend class and you'll do fine.

I never got much interaction with Dr. Cobia but his TA was amazing! Her midterm and final reviews are 10/10. The assignments are also pretty easy and don't take much time. Do yourself a favor and take PSYCH 210 from Cobia. I talked to some friends that were taking it from other professors and they wish they took Cobia's online class.

Take Dr. Cobia for PSYCH 210! 1 easy quiz, 1 discussion board, and 1 short paper every other week. Papers were super easy, and the TA sent out a weekly email explaining the papers and she was always available to meet with you. Just make sure to check for grammar before turning it in. The TA's exam reviews were the best reviews I've ever attended!
The class is fun but you get graded heavily on writing and grammar. Be prepared to deal with a history and English class at the same time

Take this class if you are a junior/sophomore preparing for a Clinical Psych PhD. If you're not, this class is kind of irrelevant. Dr. Cobia is a very kind and knowledgeable instructor and does a good job of presenting resources. The class in general is just designed for prospective PhD students who have time to do longterm stuff before graduation.

If you are looking for someone to take PSYCH 210 from, take it from Dr. Cobia. He knows the class in mandatory and organized it in a way where you don't have to memorize obscure details and dates. Definitely not a hard class but not an easy A either.

Dr. Cobia knows that most of the students taking PSYCH210 have to take it because it's required for the psych major. He doesn't make the class any harder than it has to be, but if you are actually interested in the history of psychology you can ask him all the questions you want and he'll give you pretty good answers.

Professor Cobia is amazing! He's funny and his lectures are always great to listen to. There were two assignments every week (a reading comprehension assignment and a group discussion) that are worth 50% of your grade then there are two exams, also worth 50%. Not too hard but not easy either. He's great though! Take him if you have the chance!

Dr. Cobia made history of psychology very interesting and engaging! He learned every student's name in a large class. Get ready for some funny lectures and good class discussions! As far as workload there are no essays, two weekly assignments, the midterm and final. Definitely recommend taking his class!

Dr. Cobia was awesome. His lectures were great and his sense of humor was really engaging. The content is easy to understand even outside of class in readings. The questions and conversations we have in class are so interesting. Overall, he is a fantastic professor for this class and a great person to connect with.

Dr. Cobia was a nice person, but the lectures are jam packed with information and he always went over or just didn't finish all the slides, but we still had to know the information. Make sure to read the textbook, the chapters are long, but if you don't you'll be extra lost. Study guides aren't helpful, I would say meet with the TA instead.

SUCH a good professor, and a SUPER helpful class if you're wanting to go to grad school. The class is so easy and the assignments aren't very time-consuming at all. Prof. Cobia does a great job of tailoring class discussions to our questions and concerns. Definitely take this class!

Professor Cobia is a really nice guy, but the class is almost unreasonably hard. Quizzes on each chapter cover very small details that are hard to pick up from reading/lecture. Tests are about the same as the quizzes. Hes a good guy, but I wouldnt take his class.

Dr. Cobia tries to make neuropsych interesting, which is much appreciated. Study guide is useless, just study the powerpoints. Tests are HARD - the class average on the exams were around 70% so he would give 5-10 extra points for the exams to make up for dud questions.

Dr. Cobia is a really nice person. He wants us to learn and he is passionate about what he teaches, BUT his class is VERY DIFFICULT!!!! Seriously. Super hard. His class is lecture-heavy and the tests are worth a lot. He gives difficult quizzes every week. No study guides for the exams.
Dr. Cobia is funny and a great teacher. Come to class, ask questions, do the reading, and attend TA reviews, and you'll get an A
She's the sweetest person ever. Some of the activities were fun but others seemed unnecessary. You do have to job shadow and interview people.
Lots of very unnecessary projects but not too difficult. Prof Clayton is so sweet and kind!
Dr. Knighton was a great professor. He is very helpful, so supportive, and wants his students to succeed! Be sure to review all of the study guide material for exams.

Dr. Knighton is such a sweet, funny guy. He teaches every class with a smile on his face and really works to get to know us students. He made every class engaging, even with subjects that might be boring. He is very accommodating, and just makes the class fun.

Took him for 333 and 318, Knighton is awesome and genuinely cares about his students. I love the way he teaches, and his assignments are challenging except he grades off of effort put in and not if it is done perfectly. He is super understanding, and even offered to cancel the last exam if we did extra client work! I cant recommend him enough!

Prof Knighton is so kind. He is so passionate about PR and you can tell in his lectures. The papers and tests are not hard at all. I never did any of the readings and was just fine. You take quizzes with the people around you over the material you covered in class, so be sure to be nice to the people around you. Take this class!

genuinely cares about his students and he shows it. If you are passionate about PR, his class will be a walk in the park. The readings were always interesting, and there were only 4 big assignments. Exams are easy if you watch his reviews. I didnt know how I felt about PR when I started the class and because of him I am applying to the program now!

Dr. Knighton is awesome! He clearly loves his students and wants us to succeed. Decent amount of readings but nothing crazy. A few projects that take some time but aren't too difficult. Lots of group discussions. Closed book, open neighbor quizzes that were manageable and reflected what would be on the test. Really good class if you want to do PR.

One of my favorite professors! He's upbeat, passionate about the material, always smiling and making jokes, and make lectures engaging. He makes sure you are really prepared for the three exams with a review video and study guides. You also can take in-class quizzes with your classmates.

He's your go-to mentor—like having a mission president at home. I have learned something valuable from every class with him. He creates an environment where you feel secure and supported, and you'll want to take every class he offers. He is truly the PR school's greatest asset.

Professor Knighton was one of the best teachers I had! He had amazing lectures with real world applications. He was also very easy to get into contact with as he consistently stayed after class to talk to students and responded to emails for feedback and to answer questions.

Dr. Knighton is the BEST! He has been my favorite professor here at BYU. He cares so much about his students and wants the best for them. He really has done the most so that his classes can get the best grade. He also is passionate about PR. Assignments aren't bad at all and rubrics are clear, and you take quizzes in a group. Take 235 from him!!!

This man is amazing!! He wants so badly for his students to succeed! He worked with us and listened to us. The most clear rubrics I've ever seen. If you followed each question, you'd for sure get 100% on the papers. 

My favorite thing was how Christlike he is and how his testimony and passion was shown in every lecture. One of my fav classes

Hands down the KINDEST, most sincere prof I've ever had. The only assignments are 4 3-4 page easy papers, 2 tests + the final, and a weekly quiz you take as groups. He let us take the final in person as a class, just because we asked too. Offered extra credit, not that anyone needed it. Total sweetheart, loved him. Definitely would recommend

Professor Knighton is GOLD. One of the kindest professors on campus. He genuinely cares about his students! The class is easy with clear grading criteria, he gives great exam reviews, and exams are mainly just on vocabulary terms from the textbook. 

He would push back due dates for us and said the nicest prayers for the students!

He's awesome! He always asks us about our lives and cares about us getting a good grade. He's pushed assignments back when he noticed that we were struggling to keep up with other classes (especially during midterms). His lectures always include slideshows and fun anectodes, and his exam reviews are extremely helpful.

If you have the opportunity to take a class from Professor Knighton, DO IT!!! He is seriously the best professor and the sweetest guy. He took the time to get to know our class, his tests were really easy, and he was even willing to extend assignment deadlines for us. He's also just so passionate about PR and gives us great real-life examples.
One of my favorite professors by FAR!

I'm not super into lecture-based professors but Dr. Knighton's lectures are always so engaging and incredible. He is the best professor in the PR program by far, and I can't recommend him enough. He puts a lot of work into making his class successful, and is honestly just the nicest man I've ever met.

Dr. Knighton is the best teacher in the PR program, no questions asked. It is super easy to get an A if you just show up and pay attention somewhat. Not that you will struggle to pay attention- his lessons are super interesting and relevant to PR. Dr. Knighton truly cares. He's genuinely invested in your success and is my favorite professor ever!

Professor Knighton is awesome!! He is seriously the nicest guy and makes class fun and engaging, even over Zoom. At the beginning of every class he would play a fun song and I loved it! He's really passionate and knowledgeable about PR. I gave him a 4 instead of a 5 is because he never gave feedback and he was always behind in grading.

KNIGHTON ROCKS. He cares so much about the subject and he is so open to meeting and working with you. The class made me learn PR wasn't for me but it certainly wasn't from a bad experience with the professor.

Great instructor and even better person. He cares about his students and the material and is always willing to meet. Even when he got Covid and was not doing well he held class over zoom. 10/10 recommend.

I really loved this class! It was remote but we did a lot of breakout rooms and group work. There is a quiz every week but theyre open note! You definitely need both of the textbooks but they are super helpful. Prof Knighton was easily accessible outside of class too on Slack! Take him! :) (easy extra credit opportunity as well).

Devin is one of my favorite professors I've EVER had at BYU. He is actually invested in students' success and gives great advice. He's a great professor in every way! Take capstone from him if you can.

Professor Knighton is experienced, caring, understanding, and an all-around great professor. His class is relatively easy, but it's because he's a great professor. He's clear in what he expects from you and is very straight forward with what's on exams. I love Professor Knighton!

CRE is a very difficult class, but Dr. Rappleye made it doable. We had homework 3 times a week that took a long time if you don't pick up on the concepts quickly. His grading seems confusing at first, but makes it easy to get an A. I felt like I learned so much from this class and didn't have to stress about my grade. I wish he taught every class.

Dr. Rappleye is one of my favorite professors. This is class is hard, but if you are taking it, you already know ChemE classes are hard. He makes the content very manageable and teaches very clearly from the basics. His grading policy is designed to help you learn, allowing retakes on exams and every chance to master the material. Love him!

Chemical reaction engineering is a tough subject, but Dr. Rappleye very much cares about the students learning the material, and provides a lot of opportunities to perform well in his class. Genuinely one of the most caring professors I've had. The tests and homework are very difficult at first, but become more manageable.
Loved his teaching styles. Just be prepared to take so many tests, but that is actually more helpful than it is hurtful.
I really enjoyed Professor Rappleye's class, and I learned a ton. He is a great man and a wonderful mentor.
Wonderful professor. He cares and he is overly generous in his grading in my opinion. Gives the answers to homeworks to check.

Class was excellently organized to promote mastery. Exams and homework were very difficult, but grading was structured so that if you went back and figured out what you did wrong that you could get most of your credit back. He pushed for understanding and not equation memorization, but in a way that it was actually feasible and inspiring to learn.
He teaches the material clearly and always corrects any mistakes he makes. Quality professor who cares about how his students are doing. Made a potentially difficult class very manageable.

Dr. Rappleye was one of my favorite professors. There were a few mistakes as a first semester professor, but he was very merciful on grades for that reason. He truly wants his students to learn, and provides tons of resources and different methods for them to do so.

Great Professor. There were a few hickups along the way (I can't imagine how brutally hard it would be to start teaching during COVID), but Dr. Rappleye handled all of them so well. Tests were hard, but he offered opportunities to make up points and dropped a couple low questions from midterms. Very focused on learning and growth. Glad BYU got him

Dr. Rappleye did a fantastic job teaching CRE, even though it was his first-semester teaching. He really focuses on making sure you LEARN, not just get a grade. His style is very clear and easy to understand. While his tests and assignments are graded hard, he gives you plenty of chances for partial credit and getting credit back.

She gives a TON of extra credit which is really nice, and she is a nice person. That being said she didn't teach in a way that was easy to understand and the tests are really hard to prepare for. She is extreme on attendance and if you miss a certain amount of days you straight up fail. All in all, really nice lady, but I wouldn't take hist. w/ her

The class was unorganized--the assignments posted in learning suite changed all the time and didn't follow the syllabus provided. The test questions were very specific facts, making them insanely difficult. There were many opportunities for extra credit. Duan's lectures were boring, but the tests were based off of the content.

Duan is a very kind and caring professor, she's also super funny. She doesn't post lecture slides, so attendance is very important. Her assignments are designed for you to learn, not just complete. I ultimately learned a lot, but her style isn't for everyone.
Dr. Duan is a fantastic person, if you're willing to put in a little effort to read and study, you'll have no problem with this class.

Dr. Duan can be a bit disorganized, but she is an awesome professor. She's always offering to help students in their research and finding opportunities for students to get involved in academics. She structures her class like a graduate-level class, so you'll have to read lots of books and be ready for discussion.

She can be a little bit disorganized at times, but overall a really fun professor to have. She's very passionate about helping students become better writers and is eager to help students find opportunities to do and present research outside of class.

Do not ever take this class as a GE. She sets these unclear expectations and grades super tough. Honestly expects her students to perform higher and doesnt really care if you tried if it doesnt reach her expectations. I followed her comments to edit my final paper and she still said my paper was not good enough for an A which doesnt make sense.

She cares about the class as much as you care. If you want to get a lot out of it and ask questions you will have a great time. If you just take the class because you have to then she isn't the right teacher for you. Her feedback on my writing was some of the best I've ever gotten and she went above and beyond helping me with it.

Dr. Duan is an amazingly kind, witty, and fun person, but her class was very difficult. She was often unclear on what she wanted from you, and her feedback on the semester-long paper often changed what she originally required of you. That being said, she answers emails very quickly and is available to help. Her class was just confusing at times.

Super nice, sometimes unclear but if you ask her she'll tell you ASAP. A lot of reading and a lot of essays but also had like 10% extra credit to help out. She wants you to succeed but you gotta reach out. The TA was nice

I have such mixed feelings about this class. Dr. Duan is an amazing and kind person, but as a professor she's unclear about expectations, and demands an absurd amount of work on your research paper (25% of your grade), which, not matter how hard you work on it, will not pass all her criteria. Do NOT take as a GE class, or another heavy one.

Dr. Duan is the most amazing professor I've ever had at BYU. She has such a light around her!! Dr. Duan is one of the very few professors I know who really work with you to help you not only pass, but succeed in the class. She understands that life gets crazy sometimes and is flexible with assignments if you talk to her about it. I LOVE HER! :)

I really enjoyed her class, and it was a joy to learn more about China in a world history class, something that we often don't get as we go over world(European) history for the 5th time since junior high. I really appreciated her insights into history and perspective on history. She is also quite willing to talk after class about questions you have

Pretty poor professor in my opinion. Rambles on subjects she is teaching. Focuses on China the most though it's a World History Class. Very nit-picky when it comes to grading assignments. Never felt so rushed in learning History in my life. I love history and this class really disappointed me. Do yourself a favor and don't take her class.
