I took this class as a live remote class. The first 45 minutes of class would be a pre-recorded lecture, and the last 30 minutes of class would be a discussion with our groups. She is really nice and cares about her students.

There is a lot of work you have to do for this class. Dr Tice is nice but her TA's are the ones grading your work and leading discussions. The weekly reading took a few hours to geth through along with the weekly videos and assignments. It shouldn't have been as hard as it was. I wish I would have taken it in person with a different professor.

TAs are great since you only really interact with them during your weekly zoom meetings. Every week you are expected to read 100+ pages on your own, watch recorded videos, and get quizzed on very specific things, that your notes won't necessarily help you. Not a very fulfilling class.
Dr. Tice is incredible. She cares about her students more than anything. She's happy to help them in any way possible, she just wants them to feel seen and successful.

TAKE THIS COURSE! Professor Tice is so understanding and her class is very straightforward and forgiving. It'll be hard not to get an A. Also you meet twice a week for a 30 min zoom discussion that is always super fun and engaging. 

THE BEST ONLINE CLASS YOU WILL EVER TAKE! :)
Weekly proctored exams. 2 midterms and a final. Exams are hard. Long readings.

The class is super straightforward and super clear. It's obvious she really cares about the content and her students.
The class periods are twice a week, half an hour each (consisting of just discussion with your online group about the readings). Super straightforward class, extremely low stress (midterms are open book). 10/10 would recommend

Dr. Tice is one of my favorite professors. The class is low-stakes learning - very effective. Quizzes are open note; tests are open note & open book. You can turn in make up work till the end of the semester with very low penalty. The course is very reading-heavy, and attendance for zoom calls with small groups are mandatory. She's super nice!

Before this last week, I would have rated her higher, but Dr. Tice and I had multiple discussions after she changed the syllabus and now she is making our class take a final without any study guide/resources after we were told to expect an open-book test. With the changes, I won't get a good grade on the final and I won't get into law school.

Nice lady, but similar to the other comments on here her quizzes/tests are super ambiguous. She'll list 4 correct answers and it becomes a game of guessing her mind rather than something we have learned. It feels like we are being tricked. Again, this might not be her fault and is a department issue but the class was much harder than anticipated.

The class is straightforward and has lots of potential, but Professor Tice's grading is extremely difficult. Her weekly quizzes are VERY hard/ambiguous. Our entire discussion group has agreed that she writes her questions to trick students. When you talk to the TAs they refuse to help. If you care about your grade avoid it. Please fix the quizzes!

Dr. Tice is a great professor. Her lectures were awesome. Lectures were all online but it was necessary to watch them as each class period was an online group discussion about the lecture. Grade is based heavily on attendance, but I thoroughly enjoyed watching and attending this class.

Dr Tice is one of the most genuine professors I've ever had! She constantly seeks feedback on how to improve the class and is very willing to help students who are struggling or falling behind. The zoom setup was great and the quizzes and tests aren't too bad as long as you do the reading.

Professor Tice is fantastic. She's willing to work with students, expects a lot of us but formats class in a manner that provides ease of passing and excellence if you try. Group exams, open textbook exams, information relevant to life.

Dr. Tice is a wonderful teacher who really cares for her students. She teaches in a very straightforward way and her tests are easy, but you still learn a lot. Group projects were fun; hopefully, you get a good group.

I loved this class! It was a very easy A. The class is focused on helping you learn the information through discussion instead of tricky exams and heavy homework. I learned a lot from this class, so I appreciate it a lot. Do note that there is a lot of reading, but if you spread it out over the week, it's doable. I highly recommend Dr. Tice!!!!

This class was almost entirely participation (points for commenting, group tests, etc), but the weekly quizzes were impossible. We had to read the chapter and take a closed book test that was ridiculously difficult every week. Overall these quizzes were maybe 20% of your grade and all multiple choice, so easy pass, but not necessarily an easy A

Dr. Tice wants all of her students to get an A. She is amazing and super caring. There is a lot of reading and the reading quizzes are tough, but a super small part of your grade. Tests were taken as small groups with optional TA help. Lecture was super cool as well and done on your own time.
She's a great professor, makes the material easy to understand.
Dr. Tice puts a focus on the learning, rather than just memorizing material which I really respect. She cares about her students a lot, and designs the class in a way for you to succeed.

This class was great! There was a fair amount of reading each week, and a quiz on the reading, but you were able to use notes on the quizzes and the quizzes weren't worth very many points anyways. The tests were open note, book, group and TA. She recorded her lectures and we just had to watch them and meet with our groups twice a week to discuss

Because of covid I took the class online. She would pre-record lectures and then there were discussion groups. Dr. Tice is great, but the TA does a lot of the grading and leads the discussion groups and so there is little interaction with the professor.

I loved Dr. Tice's class and I was surprised to hear that some people had a hard time with her. I really enjoyed her class and I always found her to be a really sweet professor! The class is pretty lecture heavy but she says herself that she wants all her students to get A's. The tests are open book and the TA's help a lot. Take the class!

I don't know why some people say she is rude because Dr. Tice was one of the sweetest profs I have ever had! She really wants all of her students to succeed and was always willing to answer questions. Tests can be a little tricky, but they are open book/notes and you can ask your TA 5 questions. Overall, the class was a true gem.

I would take the class again for the material, not, however, for the teacher. Dr. Tice has been rather blunt and offensive via email which ruined her general "niceness" during class periods for me. Even the class setup itself was not what I prefer, whether her "evidence" supports these open-book quizzes/exams or not. Take someone else!

Professor Tice fought for her students to have open-book tests to increase learning. She is a true advocate for students personally, and as a larger body. I respect her as a scientist, as well as as a person, and she brings up a lot of good points in class. She's a lovely woman.
Dianne Tice has a great lecture class, however, she is generally a rude professor. She verbally attacked me several times through emails and was just aloof as a teacher. Really disappointed.

She is kind and I enjoyed the class material. That being said, there is a LOT of reading. Although I actually enjoyed reading this textbook, it took hours for me to do so. I took really good notes but still had a hard time on reading quizzes. Open book tests but still difficult, somehow I'd only get 90% despite finding all the answers in the book.

Dr. Tice is REALLY NICE and caring and knows psychology well. But this class was super lecture heavy and I don't feel like I learned much from it long term. It is a simple class and had the potential to be really easy, but I found the quizzes to be really difficult and randomly specific. It could be an easy class for you, but it wasn't for me.

Dr. Tice is an incredible person. She genuinely cares for every student, even though its a big lecture class. The class is an easy A as well. There is a lot of reading and the quizzes are tricky, but the tests are open note.
Dr. Tice is an amazing woman but I DID NOT LEARN ANYTHING the class is ridiculously easy but also completely dreadful and boring. So if you need an easy elective take her.
Best class I have taken at BYU. Dr Tice is amazing and the class is fascinating.

Tests are SUPER EASY! Focus more on the quizzes and the readings! I highly recommend studying 2-3 quizlets online about the material, and then reading and taking the quizzes! I learned a lot from her. Shes incredibly smart, and everything she does is research-based! Also, her iclicker questions are super interesting!

Piece of cake easy A class. I'd be surprised if anyone got less than 98% on the tests. Dr. Tice is very kind and encourages her students to keep learning, but her lectures are boring, esp if you take the 1.5-hour-long class. Hardest thing is the quizzes on the readings, but they shouldn't kill your grade if you do the readings.

I enjoyed this class. I learned a lot, and it truly wasn't very difficult. Tests are open everything, and you meet with a group each week to go over the material taught in lectures. The quizzes were a bit rough/annoying at times but overall this class was pretty easy and enjoyable. Attendance is mandatory, but Professor Tice is a great professor!

This a pretty easy class. The midterms and final are all open book, open TA as long as you try to answer the questions yourself first. There are weekly quizzes that are not open book, a final paper, and digital dialogue requirements. Attendance is taken every day. Dr. Tice is such a caring, devoted teacher. Take this class, you won't regret it!

Prof. Tice is amazing! She is so thoughtful/caring., wants to help her students in any way she can, she emailed me and made sure I knew how to write the paper because I was still a Freshman and not familiar with APA format. You do have Digital Dialogues and group discussions for participation points. I learned so much in this class though, 10/10!

Professor Tice is the absolute best. She strives to have her students succeed. Every test is open book, neighbor, TA, etc. and the reasoning behind it is awesome! There are quite a few quizzes online, but theyre super easy. Lectures are very interesting too. There are too many good things to say about her, best professor Ive ever had!

Pretty solid choice. She knows her stuff and is very organized and clear. She tries really hard to make social psych an easy class and does a good job of it. Tests are open note and online, including the final. Weekly chapter quiz from the textbook. It's a lot of reading, but you get a full page of notes. One easy paper. Pretty easy.

This class was extremely easy. Theres was a weekly learning statement and reading quiz and that was it. All the midterms are open everything. The lectures are fairly interesting and she says that her goal is for you to get an A. The only downside is the 2 hours of participant studies but those are required for every psych111 class

One of my favorite professors in BYU. Everything she does is research based... tests, quizzes, assignments, you name it. She is really smart and she has an answer for everything, once again, based on research. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER. Your gpa and life will become better!!!
Dr. Tice is amazing! This class helped me so much not just to understand material but also in life. You need to take this class regardless of what you want to do. Definitely take from her!

Dr. Tice is definitely the best professor to take this class from. No essays. One closed book quiz a week. All other tests are open book/note/neighbor/TA/professor. Lectures are engaging and informative. One "learning statement" due a week which is just a paragraph about what you learned that week. EASY MONEY

Easiest class you'll ever take. All tests (midterm & final) are online and she encourages taking them with your classmates. I never bought the book and did just fine w/o it. Going to lecture is not necessary, but you'll want to because the material is really interesting and you'll just want to spend your whole day with Tice. She is an angel.
The best teacher at BYU. Open to the world and very nice. Does not judge you and gives you new perspective. I learnt a lot. I loved this class even if I think social psych is kinda common sense.

Dr. Tice is seriously the best! Easiest class ever, but you still learn a lot because she is such a great and interesting lecturer. Hardest part of the class was getting myself to show up since class isn't mandatory. All of her tests are online, open note, open TAs... easiest A but not a waste of my time either!

Dr. Tice is the best. Easiest class I've ever taken. Hardest part of the class was getting myself to show up so I didn't feel bad for missing her interesting lectures. Online, open note tests, weekly learning statements that I did during class every Friday. Easiest A and worth going to

Best teacher! She cares about the students and will take any feedback seriously. Tests and exams are open book (but not always easy) and you can ask questions with Tice and TA during their hours while the test is running. Super nice and genuinely wants you to learn, great and easy to understand during lectures! Good power points too

Professor Tice has a super easy class. Daily iclicker quizzes. Every week you have to say a couple sentences on what you learned. Tests and exams are open book and open note and they last a week. Super easy! Best professor to take PSYCH 11 from.

Dr. Tice is truly an expert when it comes to social psychology and had a lot to offer to the class. There were no quizzes or papers, just weekly learning statements and three take home, open book, open neighbor, open professor tests. Just stay on top of the reading and take good notes and you'll be fine.

Easiest class i have ever taken. Great teacher and has a great testimony. The class is very interesting but i don't go much because you do not need to. You only have to write a sentence or two a week about what you like from the class. All exams are open everything including the TAs. The answers can all be googled too. I have a 100% in the class.

Seriously, take this class. Dr. Tice is the most caring, kind professor you'll ever meet. All you have for class is a 1 paragraph paper a week about what you learned. The tests are open book/notes/friend/EVERYTHING. You don't even have to go to lecture, but you should because she is that great.

Very good at explaining difficult concepts. I liked that we talked a lot in his class, so we got good speaking practice. Very clear about grading criteria and even went above and beyond to remind us what we needed to do. Provides extra credit opportunities. Be ready to write essays in French for this class!

The final exam and weekly quizzes made this a tough class as a pre-med at BYU (with an almost 4.0 GPA). The quizzes were impossible so get ready to memorize 200 slides before coming to class each Friday just to do OK. The final exam was a poor reflection on the thousands of pieces of info you had to learn over the sem. Take Sudweeks instead please!

Told me I should change majors/careers when I came to him for help studying for his class. Rarely worked with students - even ones with accommodations. Tests are a BAD reflection of what we learn in class. know ALL figures/random numbers. felt like a guessing game as to what would be on the test. I have never felt so discouraged from a class ever.

Difficult class but very clear what he expects. If you only go to lectures and do the required work, you might not get an A. The tests are difficult but everything is in the book and he does a good job of explaining things through analogies in class.

He's a nice person, but a bad professor with unreasonable exams. Anything from the lecture slides, anything mentioned in lectures, and anything in the textbook is fair game for exams. This was my first B grade ever in college after 3.5 years of challenging STEM classes. Do not take this class from Dr. Woodbury.
great guy but not so great professor. lectures were hard to follow and I ended up teaching myself a lot outside of class. exams were difficult

Amazing professor & person. Difficult, but doable. I started doing a lot better in the class when I went to the TAs every week, visited Dr. Woodbury's office hours, and did the readings with the slides in front of me so I knew what to focus on. Going to lecture is worth it. He tests mostly from slides, but a little from the book as well.

Dr. Woodbury is such a sweet guy. During the in-class final exam, he would pause every 30 minutes to tell a funny story, and even brought props :) I am a 4.0 student and I usually know what it takes to be successful on tests, but I struggled so hard. Going to class does not help. Just memorize everything from the slides. Including obscure numbers.

Lectures were not helpful for exams at all, I stopped going to classes 2/3 of the way through and did just as good reading the book. His lectures are meandering and i spent every lecture thinking "what is the point or takeaway?" Harder than OChem. 3 exams plus final, weekly quiz on random stuff every friday. nice guy but blegh

Dr. Woodbury is amazing! I wouldn't take a class from any other professor over Dr. Woodbury. Here's what I did to do well in the class: read & annotated lecture slides before class, took additional notes during class, made flashcards with ANKI for every slide, and reviewed them before the test. He is anything but a difficult professor.

Dr. Woodbury test heavily on his slides so if you study them you should do well. His lectures can be a bit boring if you have not done the reading and already looked at the slides. I started doing this after the second exam and it made a difference. He shared a few spiritual experiences which were some of the better ones I have heard at BYU.

Do not take CELL 362 from him. I LOVED the material we learned in this class, but I taught myself everything using the textbooks. His tests are unfair and a poor reflection of what we are supposed to know. When I told him I was struggling with the tests he told me it was bc I'm a below average student and should consider PA instead of med school.

While Dr. Woodbury is a kind and caring professor, his class is structured horrendously. He doesn't teach the material that is covered on his tests, and nothing matches the lecture topics. His slides are ambiguous and his tests simply don't match up with his 1000mph lectures just vomiting information at you and hoping it matches something in class.

Professor Woodbury is a really nice person. His class is one you do have to do some studying, but it is in no way overwhelming. He knows what he's talking about and loves to answer questions. Midterms can get a little confusing, but if you prepare you should do fine.

I didn't have a super good or a super bad experience in his class. I was a pretty average student in the class. His tests weren't bad. Study the lectures, do some of the reading and its totally fine. He isn't always the most engaging lecturer, but he definitely enjoys teaching and working with students. Very approachable and willing to help.

Teaching skills are abysmal. He's "available" and "wants you to succeed" but isn't actually willing to work with you; he'll just show you how he's right. Use his study guide to prepare and the test will feel like it's in Greek. Monotonous, basically rephrases the textbook, but poorly. I'm a junior in PDBio; this class is so disappointing.

This is the hardest class I have ever taken in all of my life. I have a 3.94 GPA and have never got less than an A-. After taking PDBio 568 from Dr. Woodbury, I got a 60 on the final and will likely get a C in the class. If you can avoid this professor in any way, shape, or form, please do so. You will be a happier person in the end.

The class is just okay. Computer simulations are boring, and the labs are based off a series of packets that too often ask bizarre or irrelevant questions, and data from the computer simulation may not represent realistic physiology. Some test questions are vague or poorly written, which is frustrating, but most of our class did quite well.

The lecture portion is required due to iClicker participation, but it was not even slightly helpful for lab completion or test preparation.  Dr. Woodbury was not a clear teacher.  The saving grace of this class is that the lab write-ups and quizzes are easy to get full points on, and it ends up being a large portion of your grade.

I think this class needs to be revamped. Computer simulations were mostly boring. We just skipped to the questions at the end and figured out what we needed to do to answer them instead of going step by step. Took a lot of time for being a 1 credit class. He is very nice though and willing to work with students. His practice tests were helpful.

Professor Woodbury was great. He has cheesy jokes, but he is a good teacher and he tries really hard to make sure everyone understands the material. It is pretty easy to do well. Just study the slides for the quizzes and tests and you'll be fine.

A difficult class, but put in the time and you will do well.  Read the book and you'll do well on weekly quizzes and they help prepare you for the tests.  Extra points added to grades if averages don't match other sections of 305.  Dr.Woodbury is the sort of person that grows on you- fair and helpful during office hours.

I'm sure there are easier 305 teachers but I really like Dr. W.  So helpful and genuinly concerned about his students. Tests are not hard at all if you just study the lectures. Don't bother with the book, get the lecture outline, take good notes and you've got yourself and A.

After the first couple weeks you get used to his fast paced talking. He posts all the lectures online so you can review them. Study hard, its a 4 credit class, what else do you expect? Focus on his lectures and not the book. Take him, you'll learn a lot!
He is the worst teacher I have ever had.  His tests are so random.  Studying does not help.  Do not take him if at all possible.

It took me a while to get used to his teaching style (he talks a million miles per hour), but I never appreciated how good he was until we had TAs or another professor guest lecture (they were crap).  Forget the book, study the lecture notes and powerpoint slides and you should do well.

I really like Dr. Woodbury as a person and a teacher.  Yes, his test were difficult, but if you put the time in and study you can do well.  He does curve if the grade distribution isn't as high as he would like.  His grade distribution is almost identical to the other physiology professors.  Overall, I would highly recommend Dr. Woodbury.
Really good teacher, tests are really hard however, and barely ever curved. average grades on tests are in the low C range
didn't feel prepared by him at all for the tests. tests are very specific and difficult. no curve and no mercy.
Great Class.  It was hard but he was a good teacher and I enjoyed getting to know him.  Felt that I was pretty well prepared for all the tests.

Amen to the other comment. I HATE his tests. He never answers ANY questions and goes off on random tangents to compensate for not knowing the answer. You can NEVER figure out his teaching and testing style because it fluctuates so much
He's too smart and expects everyone to understand what he talks about.  His tests don't reflect what he teaches.
Sweetest man you will ever meet. I took his music teaching class. I want to be just like him when I am a teacher.

I thought this class was absolutely ridiculous! He was super harsh with his grading and was very unclear with what he was looking for on his tests. He doesn't prepare you well and goes off on random tangents in the middle of class. I would avoid him and take this class with someone else.

I came in expecting an easier class than what I got! Dr. Peterson had high expectations for our conducting, and wasn't too forgiving when we deviated from them, subjective though conducting may be. Still, he's a great professor, one of my favorites, and I feel like I learned a lot from the class! Would recommend, while warning not to underestimate.

I've taken several classes from Dr. Don, ensembles, conducting, music ed. He is a very passionate person and cares for each student -even if it may not seem that way all the time. Don't be afraid or intimidated by him. He has personally been an advocate for me on several occasions. Do the work and you'll reap the rewards!

Symphonic band, he awards points for a playing test, attendance, and listening to pieces online when he puts them up. Music is fairly easy, all generally the same, but he's very nice, a good musician, adequate conductor. I would take him again.

You will work your tail end off just to get a decent grade in any academic class of Dr. Don's.  His conducting class is ridiculously subjective and his second practicum class is filled with so much busy-work you'll go insane.  I got A's on everything, turned in one assignment late = A-

Dr. Don is one of the nicest and greatest men I know. He love music, teaching, and his students. He conducts great performing groups and pushes students to play their best without being a jerk. If you want to play with a very good ensemble, but don't want it to have to consume your life get in one of his groups.

He does not challenge his students.  He chooses music that is simple and ungratifying.  If you want to just play around for a semester, then have at it.  If you want to improve techniques and feels as if you are apart of something worthwhile, try another school.  Does not accept criticism.  Enjoys the rut of mediocrity.

Practicum. Mostly an advanced (applied) conducting class. Two days of choral training for band and orch people- pitiful. Gather "rehearsal techniques" on your own for the final portfolio- they require a lot! Prepare your scores or you'll be really sorry. Video tape req. for tests.
Great guy.  Very sincere and caring.  Lots of fun to be around.  Great sense of humor.  Probably my favorite teacher in college so far.

Drumline has tons of music to learn, plan to spend good time memorizing if first year or new. He is very sincere and always makes sure to compliment us-usually through emails following performances. Doesn't yell, pretty much never mad, just expects it to get done right-no competition so diff from HS
Dr. Don is a really cool guy. Even had me over for Thanksgiving because I wasn't going home. Great teacher and motivator.
Great teacher!  Makes marching band exciting and fun.  Always have enjoyed him!
No Comments

Marching band is quite an easy "class", as long as you show up, you'll get an A.  Dr. Don is a great director, as he makes sure rehearsals stay fun.  He tends to get excited, but it's always amusing.  Good experience.

If you aren't great with flipped classrooms DO NOT take this class. Almost 100% of the class is taught outside of class, with SO MANY homework assignments, each worth 0.05% of your grade, for a total of 25%. 3 tests makes 60% of your grade, and making a podcast from scratch makes another 15%. Nice teacher, bad class.

This was definitely my favorite class of the semester and I'm a non-major. Dr. Chapman is extremely caring about his students' wellbeing, super knowledgeable and nerdy about his specialty subjects, and the funniest (in the most genuine, unprepared way) professor. I loved all of the activities/discussions we did---and I'm a hardcore introvert. :)

I love Professor Chapman so much. But this was also the hardest class I have taken at BYU to date. The content covered in this class is tough, and Dr. Chapman treats you like you're smart. If you do the work, study hard, come to class and participate, it's totally possible to pass. Just don't overload your schedule when you take it.

The class is flipped where you listen to lectures outside of class and do activities in class. It makes class really fun, but most of the learning is done outside of class. Dr. Chapman isn't very tech savvy and leaves the grades and assignments up to a pretty absent TA so that makes it a litte hard, but he is very willing to be flexible.

We watched pre-recorded lectures ahead of class then applied what we learned in class. Felt like a graduate level class where we were expected to tackle language issues together. Some students got it, others were lost. Caring and willing to help. Tests were similar to  the problems we solved during class. Not just regurgitating memorized info.

Nice guy; bad professor. He has tons of material in so many places that it's hard to keep up. Lectures are actually recorded PowerPoints that you have to listen to on your own time  TONS of homework. Classes are usually useless, but sometimes essential for hard concepts (OE translations). Tests are 60%; paper 15% TLDR: take it with ANYONE else.

Just. So unorganized. Some of it is technical difficulties, but he should have learned LearningSuite by now. He also changes his mind about what he's going to teach constantly, and goes on tangents for half of class so doesn't teach enough. Not a hard or bad class, though.

Dr. Chapman really knows his stuff but he is very disorganized, to the point that even he sometimes doesn't understand his own lectures and has to back track. If you take this class, don't take it from him.

Interesting guy who really knows his stuff, but not the best at teaching. The class was very disorganized and he frequently forgot about assignments and changed due dates. Not very good at getting the class engaged with the material. Tests were fair. One disclaimer: TAKE GRAMMAR (ELang 325) before taking this class. Phonetics would also be helpful.

This class was tough. VERY disorganized, the TA grades all assignments with no grading criteria given to students, and he goes back and forth during lectures on what the correct answer is. I couldn't even use the textbook for reference because his lectures differ from it sometimes. Not impossible to pass, but take it from someone else if you can.

Took the online class and don't know what kind of lecturer he is.  Online classes were humorous.  Some errors in the lessons, probably just proofreading glitches which didn't make that much difference.  The biggest problem was that he differs from the text on some terminology creating confusion.  Tests were harder than expected.  I aced the paper!

As an independent study professor, Dr. Chapman was the best I've had. He gave such generous amounts of interesting and instructive feedback, it really made the class into an interactive experience. I wouldn't hesitate to take a class from him again.

Frankly, I would take this class from another teacher. He's a great guy, but his lectures are sometimes unclear and he doesn't prepare you for the tests. The TAs grade the papers and never leave feedback; the grades seem randomly assigned as there is no information on why you were docked points. It was a dull, frustrating class.

Great teacher and really makes it a group learning process rather than just him lecturing the whole time. He is incredibly willing to work with you personally and the projects are interesting and worthwhile, not just busy work.
Good solid teacher.  Tries to get the class to think about how we use language rather than just memorize a bunch of usage rules.  I learned a lot.  Cares about the students and helpful.

Don't take this class from him! He was totally disorganized and would make us watch movies as part of class while he took a nap against the wall. His syllabus was a mess and he had no idea what he was doing. The lectures were all over the place, and it was obvious that he hadn't prepared the night before.

Don't let any negative reviews of Dr. Chapman keep you from taking his class. He is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. He sincerely loves teaching & he's very humble and funny. His class may be a bit disorganized, but he's just dying to give you extra help if you need it. Talking to him one on one is helpful. It's easy to get an A.

It was a good class. Chapman is funny and really tries to help students out. At first, the material and HW seemed quite intimidating, but it's not bad. The tests are very thorough, you can't fake it on them. Memorizing facts isn't good enough, you must be able to learn principles and apply them to tough, ugly real-life examples.

The biggest problem with this class, is that you can go to the lectures and understand everything that is being taught and feel like you know it, but then do awful on the tests.  This is deep grammar, and he often disagrees with the textbook, as a lot of it is subjective.  He's a nice guy, but it's really tough to prepare for the tests.

Dr. Chapman is really nice and helpful, a prof who really cares for the students. The subject was really tough, and each test was progressively harder. However, I did enjoy class, and the subject wasn't impossible if you put forth some effort. I wasn't a fan of the text, I mostly used the glossary and that's it.

I LOVE DR. CHAPMAN. He really is geeky and quirky. He loves discussion and discovering new things about English. He teaches the material very efficiently and has pretty easy tests. His teaching style may not be for everyone, but it was definitely for me.  Highly recommended taking any class from him.
I had Chapman for 3 classes while doing a BA degree at BYU 2000-2003. He was straight forward and fair in his grading. I felt I learned a lot in his classes.

It takes a while to get used to his teaching style. He LOVES the subject though, and you can tell that he really does know a lot. He has a good sense of humor, mostly because he is an English history geek - but it's what makes his class so interesting. There are a few tough projects, but they are very doable if you do your part. I would recommend!!

He's a fun guy--super quirky, but funny. The sentences he uses for examples will crack you up. He's super easy-going. But if you want any organization at all, DO NOT take the class. His thoughts jump all over the place--there were days that I took notes that were completely wrong because it was just so jumbled. I'd recommend someone else.

I am so glad his class is over! He is a very knowledgable professor, and he really wants everyone to understand the material.  Unfortunately, his lectures are muddled and confusing.  It's difficult to know what he's talking about unless you've seriously studied the text. I don't feel like I learned a thing.  I would recommend taking somone else.

Professor Chapman is one of the many delightfully geeky professors in the department. He's quirky, thoughtful, and intelligent. Not a breezy class. You want a good grade, you'll work for it, buthe gives you the freedom to focus on those things interesting to YOU. He's easy-going, which makes the work very stress free... if you do work.

Early Modern English... what a joke! He rarely taught a thing. He opened most class time to students to say things about the "readings" and then he theorized about the principles. I didn't learn a single concrete EME principle. The quizzes every week simply review the assigned readings. The tests aren't too bad if you can manage to stay awake duri

This class was the most boring class I've taken at BYU (I learned more in my high school English classes). He seems like a helpful guy, and he has a subtle sense of humor and likes to randomly break out in song. I've heard he's good in the Old English course, but this one was incredibly painful for me to endure.

He gives a lot of projects and work outside of class, but it's not too bad.  He's one of the best teachers I've had at BYU.  He's incredibly helpful and kind, and he has a great sense of humor.  I was never bored in class!

Fantastic guy- he'll learn your name and is very friendly. After every class you know the material very well. Come time for the test though, and it can be difficult to be in that same mindset with all the other stuff you are to know. There is a ton of homework, but it's not worth much toward your final grade. Fa-flippin-tastic class.

Kind-hearted, interesting man and fantastic professor.  I often went into class confused about the topic and came out an expert.  Seems to enjoy those who make comments, answer questions, and ask related (or somewhat-related) questions.  Makes class enjoyable through sidenotes and dry sense of humor.  For help, go to his office any time he's there.
Dr. Chapman is a great teacher.  Sure, he may be weird sometimes, but he's very funny and also helps you understand what may be a difficult subject for some.
It may take a semester to get used to his humor, but every time I see him now I want to laugh. He's a wonderful guy, very fair, sort of dry, but a good teacher. Take him with a grain of salt.
Very helpful and knows his stuff.  Cares about his students.
Dr. Chapman was one of my favorite teachers at BYU.  He's a little dry and flat sometimes, but he really loves the stuff he teaches, and that makes his classes really great.

Dr Parry is by far one of the most caring and concerned professor on campus, He deeply cares for his students and his work, He moves quickly and its easy to feel left behind, grades are based on tests and quizzes only. He will do his best to help you keep up and pass. I am autistic and struggled with the teaching style though.

Biblical Hebrew is hard but Prof Parry made it really accessible. He knows so much about Hebrew and is so passionate about it. There are vocab quizzes every week, but they are necessary so you actually learn the vocab. Tests are hard but Prof Parry helps you prepare. If you want to learn Biblical Hebrew, I wouldn't take this class from anyone else.

I've had to take 273 from both DJ and Dr. Knotts, and honestly, I learned way more in Dr. Knotts' class. Be ready to spend 2–3 hours on homework after every class. He's nice during office hours, but if you didn't already understand things from lecture, you probably won't get much out of them. If you can avoid taking 273 from DJ, do it.

191 is a simple pass/fail class and Dr Seo provides very clear information on how to pass (just making sure to turn in the very easy assignments). I really enjoyed his lectures! The Make it Stick reading was also super interesting and also easy.

This is a super easy class. He has a heavy accent which can provide somewhat of a language barrier, but I had no problems understanding everything. He sets the class up in a way that if you do the assignments, you will pass, but if not you will fail. The assignments are easy so this is generally not an issue.

DJ is likable and funny. He wants his students to succeed. He always wants to help. This course is hard though. Homeworks are difficult and take a lot of time. Slides are available and tests are open book. I felt like I never knew what I was doing, but then surprised myself when I took the exams. Exams are much easier than homework.
Dr. Seo works very hard to give you all of the information that you need to pass up front. It's not hard at all, just make sure you turn the assignments in on time.

Dr. Seo could not have been clearer on how to pass the class and when the due dates are. The assignments were easy and simple to complete, plus I felt like they helped me think about learning and better my study habits. I'm not sure how I would feel about a technical class, his accent was a little difficult to understand at times.

This was the easiest class Ive taken. Just make sure you complete EVERY assignment to pass the course. If you dont do every assignment, you fail because its a pass/fail class. Professor Seo is very understanding and fair. He will work with you if you slip up.
Easy class, as designed. Dr. Seo is very clear about what he expects, but it not very flexible, and its hard to understand him sometimes.

With enough difficulty and effort it takes understanding his slides, his English, and the grading criteria, add the fact that this is a class for chemical engineers and thus you cannot expect it to be easy. Seo makes it a lot worse. Seo enjoys the prestige of his Korean background and therefore has set his expectations to be outrageously high.

He was willing to help and he always kept us in the loop with his emails. The lectures were usually helpful, but sometimes it seemed like a lucky shot in the dark to succeed on the homework or tests. The homework load was usually 6-7 hours a week. It was hard to feel prepared for the tests, but luckily he let us retake the final exam.

This was his first semester teaching and it shows. The homework is difficult, but that is the nature of the class. His exams were easier than the homework and doable if you study hard from the book. He's fairly clear what will be on the test. I never found his lectures to be very useful in preparation for any of the concepts in homework or tests.

I really enjoyed taking this class from Dr. Atkinson. It was clear that he cared more about his students learning and success than making the class excessively difficult. Take a class from him if you are able to!

Professor Atkinson is hands down one of the best professors I have ever taken a class from. He cares that you learn rather than memorize. He explained concepts in a way that I was able to understand. I was very nervous to take a stats class, but he exceeded my expectations. I genuinely learned the material and enjoyed it!! Great guy.

Professor Atkinson is hands down the best professor at BYU, especially for Poli 300. He cares more that you learn the material than memorization. I was nervous for this class but I can say that I enjoyed it and learned so much. His tests are frequent but very fair. This guy is the best. You will not regret taking a class from him.

Amazing! I feel like I won the lottery with this professor. It was difficult and stretching, but Professor Atkinson took any stress away from it. The class is so organized and expectations are super clear. There are so many resources available to help. I was really scared for POLI 300, but it turned out to be nothing but helpful and doable.

Professor Atkinson cares deeply about the material! He put a lot of effort into the class, because it was his first time teaching 300. We gave him some grace as he worked through the first run, and he returned that same understanding to us. My favorite part about Atkinson is that he was actually human, and he cared about my success individually.

The course felt extremely disorganized throughout the semester. Lectures lacked clear structure and rarely aligned with labs or homework, making expectations confusing. Even with consistent participation, full credit was uncommon. Grading was often delayed for weeks, and very limited office hours made it difficult to get help or clarification.

He wants you to succeed and is known for being a too lenient grader. He does not like to use technology and doesn't know how to use learning suite that well. I took this class as a freshman but I should have waited to take it until after poli 200 mb. Lectures were interesting but hard to follow which topics we were on because of the disorganization

Dr. Atkinson is a nice guy, but your time is better spent in a different IR class - this is my least favorite one I've taken during my time here. He was unorganized and I felt that lectures could have been way more engaging. Tests were arbitrary. He refuses to use Learning Suite which was just annoying. Class felt like a waste of time.

Very little things graded and doesn't use the traditional routes like LS. A little awkward lectures but is very excited to teach. Asks for people to attend office hours often, so try to do that. I honestly would take him again, but maybe not my first pick just because I enjoy more structured courses.
Professor Atkinson's class was one of my favorites!

Easily one of the best POLI professors at BYU. Wants you to succeed, and spends considerable time and energy to help you. While the course was not as structured as I typically like (nothing on LS, no rubrics, etc.), he more than makes up for it in lectures, feedback, and his accessibility outside of class. 100% would take classes from him again!

I had him for 270, lectures were engaging and funny, and Prof. Atkinson ensured that you knew he cared about the students and their outcomes in the class. He would often check in with us to see how we were doing and to get updates on our final project. The final simulation is entertaining, and he is a relatively lenient grader.

Took this class as my Senior capstone and I lucked out by having Prof. Atkinson. Not only does he give good feedback, he cares about his students and wants us to enjoy the projects we have. He has plenty of resources and his course was very evenly distributed. Lots of focus on the final project so not too heavy on HW! Makes learning interesting!

Doug is incredible. He's only going to be here for one more semester but I had to add my input here because he's an absolutely amazing man. He really, really cares for his students and wants you to do well. Like other commenters have said, he'll try to save your idea regardless of whether it's any good or not, but he means well. Very funny guy.

He seems a bit intimidating at first, but once you get to know him better he is such a nice, cool guy. He used to own his own ad agency and he knows his stuff. Super cool guy and I learned a lot. Take his class.
Nobody cares about his students more than Professor McKinlay.
Rocks the Advertising world and will help your portfolio... Lots of committment but get results

I love Doug - he cares (to the point of tearing up). Take his idea critiques with a grain of salt; sometimes certain tones of voice get past him, other times he'll try and mold a hopeless idea into something useful.  Class was hard because the ad lab got integrated and we didn't get any sleep for a few weeks, but not really his fault.
Doug is one of the best professors I had at BYU. He cares and has a lot of real world experience.
Great teacher. If you want to get into the creative track, this is the guy to know. Listen to his feedback and you'll go places.
Freaking awesome teacher.  Made the class very interesting.  Would definitely take more classes from him.
Great class, great teacher. If you're interested in Advertising Creative track, Doug McKinley is a guy you need to get to know, and he teaches well.
Doug is a stud.  take all you can from him
Wonderful teacher who really knows his stuff. Get to know him well.

Great teacher.  He has his favorites, so make sure you talk up in class and drop by his office to say hi.  He is an awesome source of knowledge if you need help on any of your other proejcts- he's really good with slogans too! :)  He was one of my favorite Ad. teachers
Great teacher, pick him first before any others.
Best teacher.  Only problem- if you want real critiques on what you are doing, he may not be the one.  He is a bit too lenient and encouraging even when an idea isn't worth it.
