I had him for ME 275 and 335 (not options on RMP yet ig), and he really tried to make the class as meaningful for the students as possible. He got a lot of feedback from students on what they understood and then oriented the class to focus on the topics we found confusing.

Professor Cook will take the time to help you figure things out! I didn't study as much as I should have and got behind. I was hesitant to approach him, but when I did he helped me make a plan to get back on track.

Dr. Cook is caring, that's for sure. Some of the coding homework is pretty tough, but the TAs know it well and can always help. If you do your part in studying and putting in the time outside of class (maybe 2-5 hours), you can get the grade you want.

One of the most inconsistent classes I've taken in 4 yrs at BYU. Nobody gets 100% on any anything. Barely learn in lectures - just blows through the slides, talks through examples. Just 1 test (final), timed, average 67%. Daily and Weekly quizzes. So many lab reports - not clear on expectations (which keep changing) and graded harshly by TAs.

I had a friend who took this class from another professor. During the semester I was a little unhappy because they seemed to have less work to do and easier grading. In the end I was glad I took it from Dr. Cook. I've seen that I learned the material well and I'm not sure that I would have in the other class.

It took me a while to get used to the pre class reading. When I didn't do it, I was totally lost. When I did the work ahead, the class periods paid off. Dr. Cook walked us through our questions and let us solve them, only jumping in if necessary. Most professors just jump in and give the answer and don't have the capacity to wait patiently.

A lot of students expect to be spoon fed in class. Through my summer internship it became really clear that engineers are supposed to SOLVE problems. We wouldn't be needed if the answer was already known. Dr. Cook could just give us answers, instead he gives us the tools to build the confidence to answer questions ourselves!

The worst class I've ever taken at BYU, he doesn't teach the material in class and gives an insane amount of homework for us to figure out ourselves. I am convinced he doesn't understand the material himself I went to him for help on a project and he told me to look it up on Wikipedia or youtube because he couldn't explain it himself.

This class is very frustrating for people who have never programmed before. He has written a program to grade your code, let's just say that it's not very merciful. Professor Cook is a nice man but not very good at teaching the material. The amount of class time that he spends on the material itself is pretty minimal. Insane homework load.

I had done coding before, so that part of the class was easy and I had an A all semester. That didn't matter because the final was hard, on learning suite, worth 20% of your grade, was only about numerical methods and was timed. He curved the class down also. Be ready to write and ask for help editing in office hours because his criteria is unclear

Hes a good man. I got behind when I had covid and he let me catch up at my own pace. My issue is that his final exam was not representative of the work done in this course. Simply put, we learned how to code math. The final had no code and was nothing like our quizzes. The avg. on the final was a 66%, which he didnt curve. Ill leave it at that

This is 2 classes in one (numerical methods and coding) and I didn't learn much about either as a result. Dr. Cook is smart but does not spend class time teaching. The final was impossible lol. Not super difficult content, but avoid Dr. Cook if you can because it is not structured well. Nice guy, frustrating class tho. Skipped most classes.

Dr. Cook is honestly one of the best professors I've had at explaining certain concepts. He takes the time to think outside the box on how to explain difficult things. He also takes the time to make sure we're all following. Class is tough but mostly because I've never coded before. I learned a lot in this class.
By far the laziest professor ever. He does not care about you or your academic progress. Avoid like the COVID plague.
Absolutely worthless as a teacher. Avoid at all costs.

Dr. Cook has teaching methods which he uses in class. I honestly have never been more confused by a professor. I get the class is difficult to teach with coding & numerical methods. The tests are impossible to get an A without writing exactly what he wants. Projects are awarded at best 80%. Class time is waisted answering questions not teaching!

He never tells you what he expects you to actually get out of his lectures. This makes taking his tests ridiculous because that's when you actually learn what he expected you to learn and understand. His preHW quizzes don't do crap to help you. They only cover the easiest parts of the topics while the tests delve into them and sometimes beyond.

Professor Cook has good intentions . He wants us to learn on our own which is fine but there is very little guidance in this class when it comes to learning how to code. The textbook for this class is horribly written. If you want to pass this class make sure you are able to go to the TA hours.
I was going through health problems and Dr. Cook was 100% understandable and helped me catch up in his class. He is not perfect but its clear that he cares for his students.

If you want to take his class, you better be an active learner and be responsible for your own learning outcome. That is his teaching style. He is a professor that is very easy to talk to if you spend time to talk to him.

Honestly, he is the worst ME professor I have had so far. He doesn't give homework. Instead he basically makes you come in and take mini test every week. Most students fail the quizzes. He just justifies whatever answer he had and doesn't bother checking or fixing his mistakes. Rarely was ready for class with pre-class quizzes.

He clearly cares a lot about his students and has lots of good insights. He does a good job of giving you his perspective of what you should and shouldn't do to write good code and be a good future employee. The only downside is that he is a slow teacher, and it often feels like he could take far less time than he does.

He's not great at teaching. The slow pace of his lectures means he doesn't get through all the subject matter for the day. I learned more from the online slides,videos, and going to the TA lab. The TAs were amazing!

Professor Dougal is an excellent professor. He never rushes material, and that makes his CS110 class great for freshman who aren't used to programming. He shares lots of spiritual messages and answers students' questions thoroughly. Attendance required but I mostly did homework during class since it wasn't super hard.

He's a nice guy, but his lectures are SOOO slow and felt like they could've been 15 minutes if he didn't go on so many tangents. I would usually just do work for other classes while in lecture and then learn the content on my own afterwards through online materials. Probably wouldn't have gone to class ever if not for the daily attendance quizzes.
Good guy. Cares about his students.
No leniency whatsoever and makes false accusations of students. Bad teacher overall would not recommend taking this class. Makes CS way harder than it needs to be. I cannot believe he was hired here.

Professor Dougal impressed me by his ability to answer questions and understand what the student was trying to say. He was very willing to meet outside of class hours, but with so many students sometimes there was a wait to see him. But I enjoyed his class.

I loved professor Dougal. I have no idea why his ratings are so low. I had zero coding experience before this class (CS 110), and He taught the material very clearly. As long as you do your homework, and go to your CS lab, you will be fine. side note: His spiritual thoughts are amazing. He loves his students, and you can feel it.

The lectures are super boring and slow. I think he could teach in 30 minutes but felt like he had to take up the whole 75. He would often go on tangents about things that weren't related to the class. I think he knows a lot about CS but isn't very good at teaching it yet. It does seem like he cares a lot about his students though.
I learned a lot in his class. He does a good job explaining things in a way people can understand. As long as you stick with it and go to the labs you'll do great.

I wish he taught software engineering. I think that is where the bulk of his expertise lies. It was the first time he taught CS 235. I feel like his understanding of the material was lacking. Lectures were tough. Instead of just being open about that, he would become defensive when students confronted him on it. If you can, take from someone else.

Professor Dougal is a great individual and cares about his students. His lectures weren't the most interesting, but he was always willing to answer questions. Lots of resources to succeed in this class.
His lectures were really boring, and he doesn't respect his students much. He just reads off the slides, and I had to basically teach myself this class.

Super easy class but the lectures were super boring, I ended up not going to class and did all the assignments through the online resources that he gave us. Found I could finish the work in the same amount of time and then the final only took me 20 min. Super easy but super boring lectures however, interesting class if you want to learn coding

Professor Dougal is awesome! He often starts class with a quick spiritual thought and always makes sure to be friendly with each of his students. After class he is available to talk to and ask for help. Many times the course content he was given had bad coding practices that he would always clarify for us and explain how to do better.

We love Professor Dougal. I was in a small class, and he'd often just chat with us or share a spiritual thought for the first few minutes, super casual (too much? idk). Lectures were very participative. Sometimes, it felt like he presented the material as super easy and simple—it was, but that threw me off.

Class structure is very unclear and unorganized. There is a lot of conflicting information between the website and what he says. Impossible to work with if you have any grade discrepancies. The workload is very manageable. A lot of reading and a few papers. For a 400-level class, it is kind of a joke. Professor considers himself always right.

The class is fairly condescending to CS majors - a senior level course which operates under the assumption that CS majors are terrible writers who need English major TAs to correct their neolithic grammar. Class is only offered at 8AM and tends to quickly devolve from intellectual discussion to angsty debate. Highly recommend against taking this.

Not many CS students that I've met are also passionate about ethics, so the course might not have class if it weren't required. That being said, Professor Dougal does just about as good a job as anyone at making a less-than-exciting subject bearable. He respects students with strong supported opinions and steam rolls over the rest. :)

CS404 with Professor Dougal wasn't too bad. People gave him a really hard time but I think it was mostly just that CS students didn't want to write papers. He brought in a number of interesting guest speakers and showed some interesting films. Not all bad and overall an interesting course.

Professor Dougal generally has good discussions in class and listens to students. There was a lot of reading but not all of it seemed to matter if you read it. He allowed resubmissions for some of the papers and some extra credit.

Prof Dougal's course curriculum was unorganized and there were multiple confusions on due dates. Talking to him personally yielded no help. If the entire class was angry however, which happened frequently, he would eventually make corrective actions. The most irritable thing is how he treats students, like serfs to his empire.

Very easy class, every class period is very activity-based. One thing I am disappointed about the class is the grading criteria. I took his class before and assumed everything is graded by completion, however some homework was graded by correctness. If I know that earlier, I would have worked harder.

Duane is an excellent teacher in the fact that he cares about the students and forms his lessons for them. He cares about how many observation hours you get but is more concerned about you becoming a good teacher. He has hands on activities every day in class. Great class to help learn if you want to be a teacher or not. Lots of experience.

Duane does a great job of inspiring you to be a teacher and give you ideas that you can use in the classroom. Going to observe classrooms is a big time commitment (3-4 hours a week), but it helps you see if you are in the right career. He is a little disorganized with some administrative things, but most of the homework is very interesting.

Mr Merrell is the BEST teacher in the world and truly cares about the success of his students. He does all he can to support his students and help  them be the best science teachers in the nation. He has 20+ years of experience teaching in the public education system. He does his best to pass along his experience and knowledge.

Duane expects you to engage in the process of becoming a teacher.  The reading and class room observation hours that are given in class only become important if you make them.  One thing that I have learned is that teaching takes effort and I appreciate that it cannot be forced on anyone.

An introductory class to seconary science teaching.  Duane is good at interacting with his students and supporting them, but the class is pretty pointless.  Attendance is mandatory even if they don't come out and say it, so make sure you come to class.

AWESOME guy! The concepts are difficult, but Professor Bruening is super understanding and is always willing to reteach concepts and help us out. You do a lot of group projects. Homework and readings are combined into one assignment due before every class. 3 exams and a final that are all administered on learning suite.

I was nervous to take this class because I struggle a lot with physics but Professor Bruening is an amazing teacher and does his best to make sure we actually understand his content. He shows us how to apply biomechanics to our everyday lives and it helps so much. This is by far my favorite class and I look forward to going to it every week!

This is the best professor I have ever had. Professor Bruening is an incredible teacher and an even better person. He truly cares about each and every one of his students and about their education. His grading is clear, he does practice exams, and his tests are perfect reflections of what he teaches and class is very interactive and applicable.

great class! very low maintenance, Bruening is so nice and cares about his students. I literally had to leave for 2.5 weeks mid-semester to get married, and he helped me not miss out on any points! Easy peasy class, you need to give like 35% effort and you can get an A!
Exams online and can get points back. Class is a bit hard but professor is great. A must take with him
Guys take this class from Dustin! I never waste my time writing these but he deserves it! He is an amazing teacher!

Dr. Bruening is so kind and wants everyone to succeed! He is super engaged and wants to work with you to make sure you actually learn and understand the material. He knows most people in this class are less interested in physics and he does a great job catering to the majority and helping the individual.

I've heard this class is super hard but with Bruening it was so easy. You can retake tests for a big chunk of points, retake the homework quizzes as many times as you want. The labs are easy. Lecutre is SO chill it's like a conversation with him. Sometimes the questions on tests are confusing but if you tell him after he would just give it to us.

Professor Bruening is one of the nicest guys in the department and is really smart. Sometimes subjects in lecture and certain test questions can be confusing because he's not always the best at expressing what he's envisioning, but for the most part this class is quite easy to do well in if you read and study.

Dr. Bruening was great. He had the class set up really clearly and organized. The TAs were easy to contact and so was he. The readings werent too difficult to understand and he goes over whatever you want in class. There was a project (individual or group, you chose) and it was really organized and explained well. Solid choice for this class.

Dr. Bruening is a great teacher! He's still relatively new but he seeks earnestly to improve and help. He is not trying to make students prove anything to him but really just wants to help people learn. If you have a background of physics, this class is a breeze. If you don't, it's still doable. Assignments are super simple and not time consuming.

He was a great teacher. It was his first semester and that can be difficult. He is very smart and improved significantly from the beginning of the semester to end. I would take this class from him again. Easy ready assignments and online learning report for each class. The class period is more discussion based which I found helpful. Learned a lot.

Professor Bruening was awesome. The material is kind of tough, and he is just super smart, so sometimes the teaching comes off as confusing, but he really tries to help his students. He is totally willing to meet and help you understand things which i totally recommend. Overall a good class, and a great teacher.

Professor Barton is an adjunct so he doesn't have office hours, but he's very good at responding to messages fast(his office ours are only if you email him and set something up). Class has a LOT of material, especially in spring term it's super fast paced, but he's very flexible with schedules. Lectures are really important because of fast pace.

Prof. Carter is very knowledgeable about media law and has been up and down the ladder of legal and communications work. He's very kind and cares about your success. For a class on law, it is simple, well organized, and mainly focused on your ability to apply law concepts to case studies and situations. Because of that, you're tested on application

Ed Carter's media ethics class is blended, so in-person attendance is not required. The course is easy to pass with weekly assignments and tests. Physical attendance is not taken, which makes the class very flexible. Overall, the workload is manageable and straightforward.
he's a great guy take his class!

Professor Carter is amazing. His class is straightforward. It is quite a bit of reading, but it honestly taught me a lot about law. For the comms major I did wonder the relevance of the class and why it is required for any of the comms majors, but it is informative if you are interested in law.
Kind. Interesting insights.

Ed is the best. Easiest teacher and has very little assignments/HW. Tests are easy as he requires you to fill out a study guide, then lets you use it on the test. He has clear grading and organization. My class was blended, but he allowed for the in-person day to also be on zoom if you wanted. AND he recorded all lectures. The BEST

This class was pretty easy with not too much reading (he even highlights the parts of the reading that we actually need to know and let us ignore the rest). It was kind of a boring topic but that was fine for me. There were 3 papers (one of them was just a get-to-know-you paper) and the grading criteria for the other 2 weren't super clear.

I took the blended version of the class which was nice because he never requires you to go in person if you dont want to. There was a lot of work and the tests were pretty hard, get ready to memorize a bunch of terms.

Dr. Carter teaches Media Law very well, in a way that's not hard to understand so you get the basics for comms. You work on an outline during the semester and get to use that on the midterm and final. The course guidebook is the best, so just refer to that! Always willing to meet with students, which is a plus.

Dry subject, but he does a good job. Has really clear expectations/criteria and tells you how to do well. He responds fast and accommodates. He literally highlights the important bits in the reading so you can see what's important and gives guidebooks about the biggest ideas for each module. Weekly discussions and a few papers. Take this from him!

Prof. Carter is very kind, caring, and understanding of his students. His course is laid out well, but I was frustrated that his grading was unclear (he looked for very specific wording and use of examples). It seemed that the course was more specific towards journalists, and not other comms majors. His quizzes require answers unrelated to exams.

He was one of the most understanding professors I've ever had. I had a lot of personal things come up throughout the semester, but I actually felt that he cared about me and wanted me to succeed in the class. Although the material in class was somewhat challenging, he used a lot of stories and this helped me to understand a lot better.

Great course, great instructor. Professor Carter does a great job of making tricky briefs understandable and applicable. He teaches us so we can actually learn and isn't too focused on us memorizing things so we can just regurgitate and forget--instead, he helps us learn how to think about issues and how to apply concepts going forward.

Pretty simple, straight forward class. There are readings due every week which you discuss in class (thanks heavens, because I rarely understood the them). Prof Carter is a super nice guy and really just wants everyone to succeed. Most things are graded based on your effort to think through the scenarios.

Law is complicated, and this course reflects that in its assignments and grading. There are opportunities to apply what you've learned from mistakes, but the slip-up is still there. ALWAYS DOUBLE CHECK YOUR READING. Sometimes he doesn't assign all of the chapters he should because of different textbook editions.

Just a really great guy. You make an outline (glorified study guide) for the test which you can then use on the test and it totally saves your butt. A couple papers that aren't hard at all and lectures are interesting. I did it during spring so maybe it's different for other semesters, but we were let out at least 30 minutes early every day.

His lectures can be a little dry, but he genuinely cares about the material he teaches and is very knowledgeable. It's a really easy class, just make sure that you attend every class period to earn quiz points.

Professor Carter it literally the most caring professor I've had at BYU. He doesn't care about your grade or if you get every question that he asks right, he cares that you learn. SUPER lenient with grading, will always meet with you/answers emails quickly, and is just a nice guy. Pretty boring lectures, but kinda wish he was my bishop.

Once you get past the monotone voice, you really can enjoy the class. Prof Carter knows his stuff and flaunts it often. Not a difficult class at all. He assigns readings but they aren't essential to your grade. Solid professor, would probably take again.

ONLINE SUPER easy workload (most boring thing I have ever done). You watch a couple of videos (and he has THE most monotone voice in the world) and you do the TONS (40+pg) of readings and take the quiz. The quizzes are SOOOO hard.. but I also didn't always do the reading.. tests are the quizzes so that makes it real easy. 2 papers and that's it.

Prof. Carter is wonderful. This class was fairly easy, if you take notes you will be good to go on the open-book tests. Prof. Carter is super helpful and has a great ethos, I really respected him and he teaches things in a way that invites discussion.

This was my third online class from BYU and of the three, the easiest by far.  It was well-designed and straight forward with only a few "curve balls."  Obviously the professor knew it was a core requirement class and designed it for meeting the school's criteria without overburdening the student not pursuing a degree in this field.

I took his online class & it was very well-structured. He always made himself & the TAs available for us. As long as you know what he expects and have a clear understanding of the syllabus, this class is an EASY A! Just put in effort. Lots of reading but quizzes are ALL open book! He can be a little dry, but is very knowledgeable!

I took his online class and it was very easy! You had a total of 12 quizzes due throughout the semester (20 questions each), 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. Super easy, and the class is run really well. If you have any questions the TA's are very helpful. I'd totally take it again.

TAKE COMMS 300 FROM HIM DURING SPRING/SUMMER! This class is just as hard as it should be-  "required" reading, and daily quizzes, but they are simply attendance quizzes and you learn the material during class, so just lightly skim. He makes his expectations very clear and grades fair. Go to class and spend time on the 2 papers and you'll do great.

Super nice guy, passionate about what he is teaching. You learn a TON from this class but assignments are not difficult at all so you have time to actually enjoy what you are learning. Definitely recommend this class with Professor Carter no matter what your emphasis is! :)

Professor Carter is one of the nicest professors at BYU! He's so considerate and definitely knows what he's talking about. As long as you go to class and labs you'll be completely fine! The labs take effort but they aren't too difficult! Definitely take this class from him!

Professor Carter is such a nice guy and he genuinely cares about each of his students. Go to class for the attendance quizzes and make sure to do well at the labs and you'll easily get an A in the class. The final is NOT comprehensive and theres only 2 tests in the class including the final - both super easy. For sure a great professor.

Really nice guy, I found the lectures a bit boring, and the labs were really what was important as far as your grades go, but overall I liked Prof. Carter.  Very helpful and accessible, teaches good practical skills for Comms majors to know.
Professor Cater is a great teacher! His class is fun and easy if you just listen and do the work. I learned a lot about all of the comms emphasizes and I'm hoping to take a class from him again!

I have taken a couple classes from Prof. Carter and there's a reason I keep coming back. He's one of my favorite professors and is a very down to earth guy. First reaction is he's a little shy and the class is boring, but you really get into it later. He's super super smart and willing to help out more than an average professor. Highly recommended.

Professor Carter is a very fair teacher who obviously cares about his students. He's one of the most approachable professors I've ever had (I had him for 300 and 321). After the first class I thought he would be boring but I grew to really enjoy his lectures. He's a super nice guy and if you do what he asks you'll have no trouble earning an A.
After the first day, I thought this class would be really boring, but I ended up liking it a lot. Professor Carter is a little shy, but he's just a wonderful man.  I learned quite a lot in his class.

Recommended.  Definitely not the most engaging lecturer, and the 3 hour class is long, but the subject matter is still interesting and you get to discuss within small groups.  He is a very nice person and willing to do whatever he can to help his students succeed.  Papers require a LOT of work, but he is a VERY generous grader.

I was not excited about taking this class but Prof. Carter is awesome.  He is the most approachable and down to earth prof. I have had. Ethics and Law paper are required but he is very willing to help if you have any questions. If you have to take this class definitely take it from him! Just do the work and you will be happy with your grade.

Just skim the readings, daily quizzes are way simple.  Ethics paper is easy but law paper took me approx 30 hours with all the reading of cases we had to do.  He is a very generous grader though and tells you exactly what to expect on the tests.  Great professor: professional, nice, answers emails immediatly...I highly recommend him

The first day of class, I thought I was in for a LONG semester.  However, he grew on me and I enjoyed the class quite a bit. The lectures and group activities are interesting and he is a very generous grader.  I took his once a week class and we got out at least 45 minutes early.  He is very approachable and helpful.

Prof Carter is an incredibly smart guy - he knows his stuff. Comms 321 is a hard class by nature but Prof carter made it interesting. He is helpful if you seek help. He is very fast at replying to e-mails. He isn't the most "warm and fuzzy" professor but he is smart at least!
His advanced media law class was surprisingly interesting.  His open-door attitude is refreshing.  One of the best teachers I have ever had.

Carter is not always easy, but he tends to be understanding and doesn't try to make life miseralbe.  His lectures can be boring, but there are alot of class activities.  His tests can be hard, but he makes sure that you know all the information.  I would recommend him.

He is a great teacher because he is actually a lawyer and knows what he is talking about.  His assignments are not hard just time consuming.  He lays out everything you have to know for the final and midterm.  I would love to take another class from him.

Nice guy! I loved the material. However, despite his knowledge, class can be dull. Class was easy. Go to class b/c he gives a quiz everday and it is 10 easy points. Overall, a very fair man, very easy to talk to when you need help.
He is a great teacher and you learn from his teaching.  You will enjoy this class, especially the take home final.

He's a real lawyer so he has a pretty good perspective.  At times you feel like you are guessing at what he wants out of an assignment.  But he is pretty fair and is probably one of the easiest professors to approach that I've had.

haven't met a single graduate student who liked this class lol. history of psych is overall not it and with professor gantt, every class felt never-ending. great person yes, but all he does it talk the entire class which can get tedious and uninteresting very quick.

Idk what the other reviews are talking about. Dr. Gantt is one of the most uplifting and inspiring professors I've ever had. You won't like Dr. Gantt, or this class if you're gonna have a bad attitude because it's a tougher course. But if you put in the effort, you'll absolutely love it, and it'll strengthen your ability to think critically.

Professor Guyon is hard working and puts a lot of effort into her classes. However I found myself struggling to focus in class due to extended tangents on various class subjects, that often led to her repeating herself and leaving us more confused than before. She has good intentions and is willing to provide feedback, albeit sometimes confusing.

I enjoyed the class! It is so EASY and really helpful. She cares a lot about not giving a lot of busy work and she will try her best to accommodate with our busy semester schedule. I got an A and got an A on my final! I highly encourage taking this class from her! Only readings, a big paper (but it builds through semester so that's easy).

The class was extremely frustrating for me. I did not feel expectations were clear and grades took months to get posted, so feedback was not always available. She is such a nice person, I just never knew what was due because the posted schedule was often inaccurate.

I have nothing but positive things to say about her. She was flexible and easy to work with. She would do whatever she could to help you with the class, including giving helpful feedback on drafts of long papers. She is a fair grader and tries to make it clear what is expected from you. Definitely worth the drive to SLC. Great class and an easy A.

I enjoyed this class. All assignments were understandable and Elisabeth made sure we understood what was asked of us. The work load is decent, but she is not a hard grader; she is more concerned about us learning something from the course and applying it to our lives.
Guyon is a great teacher. well worth the drive down to BYU SLC. If you want to get an A and learn something in the process this is the class for you.

She is a great teacher. She made this class a pleasure to come to each week even though it had a great many assignments.  I really learned from this professor.  She is personable and willing to listen to students.

Sis Guyon is amazing. Her class was worth the drive up to SLC. She genuinely cares about what students think of her class and will do all in her power to make it worth your while. There was 1 grammar test but she took 2 classes to teach all that was on the test. If you show up and do the assignments, not hard and very clear you'll get a good grade

Oof this was a rough class. Not in the sense that it was technically challenging, but I can't remember a single zoom meeting in which I actually learned something, they felt so incredibly pointless (no actual teaching occurred, just continuously throwing us back into breakout rooms to discuss the readings). Too much busy work for simple principles.

There was weekly discussions with class members, reading reflections, case studies, a big midterm paper, and short essay question final. It felt like a lot of busy work and often times the discussions felt useless and repetitive. I liked the material but wished it was applied better.

Professor Hawkins is super nice but I was not prepared for how the class is set up. If you take it online, the entire class is spent in Zoom breakout rooms with students. The professor barely talked/taught in class and I was talking to other students the entire hour+. It's not a super hard class, but lots of reading and lots of talking to students.

Professor Hawkins is honestly super chill. I was worried going into this class because of her ratings, but she is super kind and cares a lot about her students. She gives great feedback on assignments and all of the homework assignments and discussions are helpful in teaching students how to think critically and build their own ethical framework.

The grading in this class was hard for no reason. Even the homework was graded tough. Why would you take points away on a homework assignment? There is a lot of work throughout the modules for no reason.

An extreme amount of busy work and the grading is absolutely ridiculous. There was also a few times during the class where I was given a 0 on an assignment because it was “flagged as AI” when it was completely my own work and I had to specifically ask to have it looked at again and then was given full credit. Take this class from ANYONE else

Ok honestly I was scared to take this class online but it was not bad at all. There are summaries once a week based on reading that isn't horrible. TA was super easy grader and the midterm is literally just composing your own ethical model and relating it to cases it can be seen as a lot but just put a tiny bit of thought and you are chillin.

Okay here's the thing about Prof. Hawkins.  This class is a lot of work, with about 4-5 hours of homework a week.  But she is super understanding, always willing to help, her class is fun and interactive and you will get a lot out of it!  She really teaches you and so I loved this class!

Professor Hawkins has a vast knowledge of media ethics, that's for sure. The issue is that she is not a very good lecturer and her class is full of busy work. You can learn the same amount by doing half the work. If you can avoid taking this class from her, do it.

Lots of busy work, but it's pretty easy to get an A. The final is just case studies that are similar to the ones you do in class. At first, her grading style is pretty frustrating, but you can resubmit things and her TA was super helpful. Live discussions are once a week, as long as you participate you get an A.

Be prepared to write in this class! She grades very technically, but gives great feedback and lets you resubmit as many times as you want. Prepared me very well for high-level comms classes that expect you to write flawlessly. 

**Lectures are on-demand, but you have to be present on zoom for live review/discussions once a week.

The most frustrating part was the TA and the grading!! It felt more like an English class with the way they decided to grade your assignments. You'll score a 10/15 for missing a comma or for a sentence appearing "too confusing" but then give feedback saying "Great job! You're doing amazing." The entire class is made up of breakout rooms

This class is structured horribly and grading is ridiculous. You could spend hours on an assignment and follow the outlined rubric perfectly and still lose points... and the only feedback you receive is, "Great job! You can resubmit this for a higher score." Unless you want to be frustrated the entire semester, take this class from somebody else.

This class was easily the worst of all Comms required classes. Learned entirely from the textbook, pointless required zoom discussions that were purely breakout rooms and repeated info from the textbook and assignments prior. A lot of busy work but it definitely is doable, just frustrating with such interesting subject material.

She makes attendance mandatory and requires your camera to be turned on at all times or else the TA personally messages you asking what's wrong. The whole class is done through various breakout rooms and she never actually teaches because all the learning is done through the textbook. She shouldn't require cameras to be on, and she should teach.

I have never had so many writing assignments in my lifeeeeee this is crazy. It's 10pm on a Saturday and I'm still sitting here doing assignments. Plus, literally the whole course is taught through reading the textbook and it makes me SO MAD because why pay for tuition when I can get all the info from a book.

While I believe she truly cares, I don't exaggerate when I say this was the worst class I've taken at BYU. Prof. Hawkins is inflexible and unwilling to understand that students might learn differently than she does. The class is 90% busy work that ends up being way too important for your grade, which is a shame with such interesting subject matter.

Professor Hawkins is respectful and has great motives to help students learn. That being said, Comms 304 with her was wayyy more difficult than it should have been. Get ready for lots of writing assignments including incessant weekly reading summaries, case studies, and other assignments. Very stingy grading. Webinars have tons of breakout rooms.

Dr. Wood is awesome! Stats can be tough, and you get what you put into it. Her lectures are great, and the book is really helpful. She is SO nice! For an online class I could tell that she really cared about all of her students and wanted us to do well. Rubrics are clear and easy to follow, and she and the TAs were always willing to help.

The beginning and middle of the course were fine. But in 301, towards the end there's a big project that is kind of overwhelming and I wish she would have prepared us better for that. Most of us had to have an extension on it, especially because it was combined with our 10 hour practicum! The only upside was that she was quick to answer emails.
She's awesome! Typically have one reading or video to watch then write 1 page response! Makes the learning fun! Interactive in class! Guides are perfect for tests. I totally would take again!

Come to class and complete the assignments and it is an easy class! She cares about her students and is patient. She has fun activities for the class to do together that we can use in our future classrooms. Side note: she does tend to speak very slowly which made it a little bit difficult to stay completely alert during lectures at times.

Dr. Knell is an amazing teacher! I learned so much about Immersion Education and I felt prepared to tell others about its structure, mission, and results. Highly recommended for anyone who is even considering the Dual Language Immersion minor.

Prof. Dishman is very professional and has a wealth of real world experience.  His lectures are strictly powerpoint based and are usually entertaining (marketing is often entertaining), but sometimes dry. He offers plenty of opportunities for extra credit.  As always, attend the TA reviews and memorize the review to get a good grade on tests.

Great man.  The course covers a broad level of material on a more shallow level.  Consequently the tests require a lot of memorization, but they really aren't too bad if you have done your part.  We did several projects in this course of varying sizes.  A couple of the larger ones were very interesting.  Overall a great course.
Pro Dishman is cool guy who treats the students like professionals.  He can be intense, but his class isn't too hard. His tests are extremely long, but if you study hard, you'll do fine.  Cool guy.

I really liked Dishman. He's not rude, he's just real. I guess people in Utah aren't used to that. He won't pretend to like you. He is a really good teacher and does care about his students. Classes were really interesting and I learned a lot. You don't need your book too much. Tests straight forward, no quizzes, easy grading. Lots of xtra credit.

Class: good media, random info, in class assignment once/month. Hmwk: group-work and one individual paper.  Tests: easy-- just memorize review slides.  Book: no need to read or buy.  Dishman: sarcastic/rude.

Not a great experience. Felt like he copied and pasted past class schedules and assignments to the current semester. Blackboard was disorganized and busy-work was ridiculous. Nice guy though. I don't wanna dog him but the material was all over the place. Good use of media during class.

Dr. Dishman is a wonderful teacher! I took his sales class when he taught in place of Dr. Bone. Dr. Dishman runs a very professional class; be respectful, interested, and diligent, and he will reciprocate. The class was very challenging, but Dr. Dishman is very open and willing to help. I wish I could have taken his competitive intelligence class.

Dishman was a good teacher, but sarcastic towards student, not very friendly, and occasionally rude. The tests were completely brain dumps from his slide, the book was not even needed. Other than the most pathetic tests I've ever took, it was a marginal class.
I emailed him a few times and he didn't get back to me, which shows he doesn't seem to care much for students.

Great class. Dishman can seem intimidating in class, but he's actually really, really nice. Incredibly helpful even though there are like 400 other students. Do NOT, I repeat, do NOT fall asleep in his class. He will go up to you and wake you up mid-fling into his lecture. Also, study the powerpoints and take notes in lecture.

If you wanna coast, take his class.  If you wanna learn anything valuable, avoid him at all costs.  The guy is ego-centric, his TA writes and grades all assignments, including the exams.  Lazy old professor who doesn't do anything but show up and regurgitate the textbook you read last night

Dr. Dishman's lectures were interesting and were effective in helping students remember the concepts. The textbook is for quizes and lectures are for exams. Both quizes and exams are verbatim from text and lecture... so lots of memorization, but still.  Overall, interesting class... i recommend it!

Dishman is awesome! He's very entertaining, very engaging, and very good at explaining the concepts. I really looked forward to each class and learned a ton. Tests weren't hard, quizzes were a breeze (open book), lectures were interesting--this was just one great class!

Good teacher. Class is challenging and interesting. There are weekly reading quizzes that are open-book and taken on Blackboard. Not bad at all.  Tests require diligent study to do well. Interesting class and Dish knows his stuff.

He's very intimidating, and there's lots of group work without class time to do it. He won't hesitate to say your opinion is wrong. It seems like he talks about how useful CI is, rather than how to do it. I didn't learn a whole lot from the class, and I honestly couldn't recommend it, though the class title sounds cool--competitive intelligence.

This class was not what I was expecting, but it was so fun! Felt a little silly sometimes when we would play elementary aged games and sing, but it's a great class. The final is an integrated lesson plan you present in front of the class, which is a little daunting if you hate public speaking like me, but it wasn't bad. Professor Knell is awesome!

I felt like I learned a lot from Sister Knell. You grade yourself on attendance, participation, and preparation everyday, so being in class and doing reading before hand is essential. The things I did and learned in class really helped prepare me to be in an Elementary classroom. It also helped me know how to incorporate music in the class.

A little bit of an awkward class, but good to get you in the headspace of teaching little kids. A lot of the work is done in groups so get to know the people in your group and try to become friends with them. A lot of silly dancing, singing and stuff like that, so it can either be a really fun class or a total bummer.

A lot of work for a 2 credit class, but very fun nonetheless. Most of class is spent singing and playing related interactive games. Lots of reading required before class, some journal entries, several assignments, much group teaching, 1 midterm, lots of extra credit opportunities. You grade yourself on attendance, participation, and preparation.

Sister Knell is very sweet and caring. However, I do not recommend taking her class at 8am. It is kinda brutal. She has some fun activities, but a lot of the time her lectures were dry and a bit on the boring side. She works really well with kids, not so much with college students. Also the readings are pretty redundant and seem like a waste.

Sister Knell is great. She really cares about her students. She gives good feedback. Attendance in class is very helpful. There was only one test, a midterm. Most of the big grades came from projects. If you come to class, she goes over them and gives multiple examples.
She was a great teacher. I loved the Music for Elementary Ed class; we had so much fun. It was a look at music from a whole new perspective.

Dr Brunson's Biological Anthropology class was delightful! She did a great job of breaking it down into sections that all made sense. I also really appreciated her use of science to dismantle racist views in the world. I highly recommend taking it from her!
Dr. Darowski cares about her students. She has high love + high expectations for those in her class. She is also very passionate about what she teaches

This was a 4 credit class, so there was a lot of homework and readings to do. It was very consistent and you knew what was due and when. Anytime I needed help she was quick to respond and was actually helpful. I will say that she/the TA's were really tough on grading. However, they gave clear feedback so you knew why you lost points.

Had to take it for my major, it was irritating. Dr. Darowski is a good teacher and a kind person, she is very likely to be understanding if you have difficulties come up. She did assign a pointless and condescending book for us to read during the semester. I often felt like I was being graded on things in my writing that I had not been informed of.

The entire class is building an 8-10 page literature review. Prof. Darowski is very involved and does care about her students. Procrastination in this class is what will really get you. Resources are available and accessible, and feedback and guidance is always given. Great opportunity to learn how to write an APA paper, with a great professor.
Great teacher. Sometimes her English grammar was less than perfect but hey, its a math class. The course structure is reasonable it's just that calculus is not easy.
Really amazing at explaining the concepts, homework isn't more than necessary, is entertaining and engaging, would 100% take for every math class if I could!

Dr. Evans is really trying to make the content easy to grasp which I commend her for. However, I feel like in her efforts to make it easy for students she inadvertently glosses over content and makes the class much more confusing than it needs to be. She is a great person, but I really really dislike her teaching style.

Best math teacher I've had yet. She's energetic and makes math fun and entertaining. READ YOUR TEXTBOOK BEFORE CLASS. Do it diligently and you will have an A. Her teaching style assumes you didn't read, and so if you do read and take notes before class, you will understand the difficult material much easier. She will help you at almost any time.

Dr. Evans is really a great teacher. She explained everything clearly and made an effort to engage the class always. I would totally recommend her! However, the final and last chapter are DEATH so try and brace/boost your grade beforehand or your GPA might hate you.
I liked Dr. Evans. She seems a bit stiff, but she cares a lot about her class and wants everyone to understand.

Really hard class. If you are in ACME you don't have much of a choice on who to take, but if you get Evans be ready for 5 hour tests, lots of homework, and typos in the textbook. She demands way too much from her students. If you are in ACME or thinking about it, consider switching. They make a lot of empty and dishonest promises.

This has been one of my favorite courses here at BYU. Dr. Evans is amazing and my favorite math professor I've had. She is incredible at breaking things down into an intuitive level while still maintaining and communicating the mathematical rigor. She really knows what she is talking about and is willing to admit mistakes when she makes them.

I LOVE Dr. Evans. She is the most fair/straightforward math professor I have ever had. Her lecture and class were so organized. She taught simply and clearly. Class prepared you for the homework, and homework prepared you for the test. Lots of homework, but that is to be expected in a college math class. Seriously, take her! You won't regret it.

Awesome professor, does a great job of teaching new material by drawing on knowledge from previous math classes. Very accessible and helpful outside of class. She weighs homework heavily so if you just do your homework you're already set up for a good run. The course material got really hard at the end but she told us it would from the beginning

She is awesome! She explains things really clearly and actually wants students to ask questions and succeed. She's funny too. The usual amount of homework. She warns you that the difficulty of the class ramps up at the end, but FOR REAL it gets way harder, so make sure you're keeping up.
I loved taking this class from Professor Evans! Definitely one of the best Math teachers at BYU.

Dr. Evans is very knowledgeable and competent. Her lectures were generally helpful for succeeding in the class. Her exams required extensive studying and time; I didn't always put enough in. Her coauthoring the textbook meant she knew and taught the material well, but also had high expectations of her students. But she's also kind and understanding
Definitely a difficult class, but Dr. Evans makes it doable. I enjoyed the content and the feeling of finishing it.

Once Dr. Evans put on a Captain America hoodie and became Doctor America. She's that cool. Math 344 was good, but Math 346 with her was amazing. Taking this class was by far the most helpful experience for learning how to do math and do it right that I've ever had. Kudos, flowers, and many thanks for you Dr. Evans.

Dr. Evans is easily one of the best teachers I've ever had. In her classes you not only learn the material -- you also learn how to be a mathematician. This class was very challenging and we all spent lots of time in her office hours, but it was worth it. I feel smarter, more confident, and ready to advance. Thank you, Dr. Evans. You're the best.

The subject matter was extremely difficult, but she really focused on helping students understand the material. She was really accessible, and was always reminding us to come visit her in her office hours. She really tried to make the course as understandable as possible. She's the best math professor I've had at BYU!

I had Evans for 113 and it was the hardest class I have ever taken (my only B in college), but I attribute that more to the class( very much run by the evil math department) than to her. In contrast, she was very much in control of 314 and while the class was hard it was WAY more reasonable. She is very helpful and it was my best math class!
Math 113 is designed to kill students. I do not think that evans did a horrible job and she had lots of opportunities for students to receive help. But 113 is designed to kill.

THIS CLASS WAS SO HARD. It made Chem111 seem easy. My first B ever. I love math and usually do well at it. I would not recommend Evans for 113. She was very frazzled and unclear in lectures. It helps if you took AP Calc BC in high school. If not, good luck. Get a tutor.

Hardest class I have taken in my entire life. However, that wasn't because of Dr. Evans. She does a great job of explaining difficult concepts. She cares about students, and she grades fairly. I thought her open book tests were very hard. Homework was tough. (I recommend working on it with other students) But take 342 from Dr. Evans if you can.

I had Dr. Evans for math 342. It was a great class. Homework was reasonable. It covered exactly what was needed. The tests can be tricky if you don't know what to expect. She tests on reasoning, so they will mostly be problems you haven't seen before. Great class. Great teacher. Take a class from her if you can.
Hands down the best math professor at BYU. She really cares, gives fair tests(in 314 at least), and is extremely helpful and nice if you go see her for help.
I had her for 342. Her assignments and test are very difficult for anyone less than brilliant. A good teacher with a good lecture/textbook use balance. Quickly understands questions from students.

No secret that this class is brutal, but Professor Leslie is the BEST case scenario. She is super genuine and brilliant, and the course is super well organized and paced. The material is tough, but the structure helped me learn it without extra busy work. Plus, I made some really close friends as we struggled together.

Dr. Leslie is an amazing lecturer and I loved her class! She taught complex content in clear ways, and truly cares about her students. She does everything possible to encourage learning and reduce stress in a difficult course, including giving extra credit to those doing group work. One of the best professors in an incredible Econ department.

The content of this class is hard but there really is no way around that. It's definitely important to attend class so you know what is going on. Homework is pretty light and you get extra credit for doing it in a group, which was helpful for my grade and my understanding of the material. If you have to take this class, choose Leslie, she's great.

Dr. Leslie has by far been one of my favorite professors in the Econ department. She really cares about helping you succeed and makes an effort to connect with students. Econ 378 is a heavy course load but if you show up to classes and attend TA hours etc. this class is really enjoyable.

Dr. Leslie is one of my favorite professors at BYU! She makes the effort to learn each student's name before the class even begins, and is always kind and understanding. 378 is not an easy class and there's a lot of homework, but her lectures are very clear. The tests can be tough, but if you understand the homework, you'll be fine.

One of my favorite professors I've had at BYU! I loved her lectures. She was masterful at teaching challenging concepts in a clear way while also keeping the class fun and engaging. Data project seemed scary at first but wound up not being nearly as bad as I thought it would be. Utilize lab and office hours!

Dr. Leslie is super organized which helps out a lot. She does a great job of answering questions and helping everyone to understand the material. It was tricky, but she is really good at explaining in simple terms. There was homework due almost every class, but it wasn't too hard, and really helpful. TA lab helped a lot!
Tough class, but Dr. Leslie is an awesome professor who cares about her students and is willing to help. She also prepares you well for anything you might see on tests, which is awesome.
If you're not enjoying her teaching style for econ 378, it might be worth considering a change in your major for the sake of your future. She's one of the best lecturers in the department.

One of the hardest classes I've ever taken, and she teaches it in such a way that makes you want to pick a new major. Stata along with most of this class you have to learn on your own time and with the help of the TAs. Curved at end, but when the average for midterm 1 is mid 50s it's hard to stay positive about the class. Course content is insane.

I absolutely loved Dr. Leslie. You can tell she cares about her students and she gets to know all of her students and knows them by name. She lets you submit homework in groups which helps a lot since it is graded for accuracy. Her exams are hard but that's because economics is a hard subject. You will not regret being in her class.

Dr. Lesli is incredibly passionate about her students and her research. This class was not the easiest to be taught by anyone but she offered extra credit for working in groups, and also for midcourse evaluations. She cared about the structure of teaching and its effectiveness and implemented real change from feedback. Phenomenal teacher.
Dr. Leslie is an amazing professor. She cares about her students, cares about the material, is personable and funny, and is just such a phenomenal teacher. Definitely recommend her.

Professor Leslie is probably the most caring professor I've had throughout all of college. 380 is a HARD class no matter who you take it from, I would highly suggest taking it from her. Very knowledgeable and a good teacher. Cares about student sentiment. Genuinely wants you to succeed. Once you get past 378,380,381 and 388 the major eases up a bit

She is a great professor - explains things very clearly and is very accessible. I did great on the hw and quizzes, but the tests are difficult. You need to clearly understand the concepts in order to do well. Definitely recommend taking class from her.

Professor Leslie is awesome! I would say her class style is simple, organized, and reliable.Tests and homework are much harder than the in-class examples we do, but I guess that makes sense haha:) ECON 378 was hard for me because it had been awhile since I had taken math, but she gives a lot of opportunities to earn extra credit on HW/research proj

This class was awful. I'd select lecture heavy, but about once a week there was a HW problem that she didn't teach, didn't introduce, didn't mention at all. Sometimes she'd teach it the class after the due date & there weren't any textbook readings to help! Also teaches Stata very unclearly. Without stats or coding experience, avoid 378 from Leslie

Doctor Leslie is incredibly smart and caring. This class is just immensely difficult and math-heavy. The hardest class I've taken yet at BYU. Weekly homework and quiz that are much harder than the lectures in class. The tests are worth 70% of your grade, and are crazy. She's a good teacher in a crazy hard class.

Professor Leslie is a really nice person and a good teacher. Her lectures were straightforward enough, the real problem was the difference between lectures and homework. The problem sets are, at points, absolutely insane. When we asked her to go over some of the questions in class she said she wasn't going to in class time.

The thing I liked about this class the most, was the clear grading criteria. It was clear the path to an A. I also really liked how there were no readings, just short pre-lecture videos you had to watch that were super helpful. Tests were open-note. Pretty easy A if you like math and show up.
Lectures are pretty straight forward but the tests are pretty tough. She organizes homework groups which is very helpful.

Prof. Leslie is super caring and want you to succeed. She knows this is a challenging class, and she and her TAs try their best to help you. Some of the concepts are hard, and she explains it very clearly. The switch to online instruction helped because I can shamelessly replay her lectures until I understand the concept.

Dr. Leslie is amazing. It's true that her explanations of new concepts are difficult to understand for people with little background in statistics, but she cares so much about her students and does whatever she can to ensure that we comprehend the material. Out of all of my professors, she made the transition to online courses the easiest.

If you've never taken a stats course before, DO NOT TAKE FROM EMILY. I've never seen so many people drop out of a class before. I did great in Calc and died in this class; she doesn't explain the math well AT ALL. She makes a lot of assumptions about what you already know. I was constantly lost.

Dr. Leslie is awesome! Whenever teaching a new concept, she always gives multiple examples to ensure everyone understands what is going on before moving forward. She is entertaining and wants everyone to succeed in her class. Homework is straightforward, and the one project is a cool real life application of the course material.

Dr Leslie is a great teacher, the class content was always clear, but the tests were hard. Only 5/30 students got above 80% on the final. I thought I understood everything in the class and felt good about the final but got 50%. There is a curve, but when that much of the class did so poorly, theres a problem. Do the hw, dont buy the textbook.

ECON 378 is a really hard class, I would recommend taking it from Dr. Leslie for your best chance at a good grade, she's great at explaining really difficult subjects and is always willing to help. Class is mandatory to get a good grade as is group study and visiting the TA lab regularly.

Dr. Leslie explains things in a clear and concise manner that makes difficult material easier to swallow. She genuinely wants you to succeed as a student. I've yet to experience a more fair and effective teacher than Dr. Leslie.

Professor Leslie is brilliant and very good at explaining challenging concepts. There is a homework assignment due every class, but they are usually not particularly hard or very long. There is one midterm and one final; both are tricky but not impossible. She is not an easy teacher, but she is a good one.

I am obsessed with Dr. Leslie. She is probably one of the very best professors I've ever had at BYU. 380 is a hard class, but she teaches it so clearly, it's hard to misunderstand. GET A HOMEWORK GROUP, it will save you on the problem sets.
love it
Excellent. She's a great professor and teaches the material without making it too hard.

Professor Leslie has a great teaching style. She teaches you a general concept, then a specific part of that concept, then has you do an example on your own to judge how well the students are understanding. This helped us know what we didn't know a lot better. she was very caring and really funny.

Professor Leslie is honestly one of the best! The way she works through problems on the board and then gives you class time to work them in small groups was really helpful. Her humor is on the dry side, but I loved her for it! She goes lighter on the regression section which is nice. Well-balanced course schedule. Wish she taught more classes here!

I really enjoyed this class. You will have to do lots of textbook readings and the exams require a lot of memorization. Dr. Patten was very good at communicating with the students each week about each assignment and was always willing to help.

Professor Patten didn't teach much directly. She often made old recordings that often contradicted the textbook readings. Test material was inconsistent. Sometimes it was based on the textbook, other times on what she said in the outdated videos. Tests and quizzes were mostly random facts and trick questions.

Teacher does literally nothing (She has recorded videos from years ago and delegates all of the work to the TA's.)  Exams focus on memorizing trivial details and trick questions instead of real learning. Tons of textbook reading, but it'll give you your GE credit lol. Positive side, very little work 2nd half of semester

I definitely recommend taking this class online with Dr. Patten. The class is very organized, and from what I've heard, nutrition is a lot more difficult in person. As long as you follow and take notes on the learning objectives, you'll be fine on the test because it's mostly just memorization.

NDFS 100 is difficult no matter who you take it from. If you want an A, get ready to make lots of flashcards. I never read the textbook and scraped an A by less than 2 points. You can finish this class as fast or as slow as you want within the semester. It helps take the edge off finals week if choose to get it done early. Online proctored tests.

The textbook pages she provides do not match the lectures. I emailed her about it, and she said it would be fixed but it never was. This made it difficult as she does not teach and we just teach ourselves with the slides and activities. Not to mention the textbook was like $100. Her exams were also pretty difficult, so you for sure have to study.

I thought this was the best way to take NDFS100. I have a lot of friends that took it in person and they were always complaining about how hard it was, however I never found myself stressed with this class. The four exams are the majority of your grade so study hard for those, but if you use the study guide/past homework/quizzes you should be fine.

-50/10. Most of was on exams wasn't in the textbook/lectures, and the studies used in the course are wildly outdated. Close to zero teaching from the professor, it's just reading from the textbook. The professor was completely unhelpful and hard to reach when there was a problem. DO NOT take this if you don't have to. I had a 4.0 before this class!

NDFS 290 is a super easy and inspiring course if you are thinking about dietetics. There are a couple assignments at the beginning of the semester, but the rest is only based upon attendance. LOVED this course.

The last review is from a lazy student. I've taken lots of online classes. This has been the most clear by far. The tests are literally just the answers to the learning outcomes, which she gives to you for every chapter. Don't need to read, just do the modules and fill out the LO's. I usually studied hard the day before an exam and got all A's.
do not take this class. it is so much unnecessary busy work and the exams are sooo long. its such hard information and no one is there to help you understand it

Professor Patten cares about her students. She helped expose us to dietetics careers and the pros and cons of the many routes we could take. She clearly explained the process of applying to the dietetics program and was open to answering any questions we had. She was helpful and the class was very informative.

this class was SOO easy and super fun! prof patten is great, she's super kind and gives such a good intro to dietetics. lots of guest speakers and only a couple super easy assignments. only 1 credit and it's definitely not hard. prof patten is a great lecturer and the class is awesome. also it's just pass/fail. take this class!!!
Dr. Patten was amazing! This was an online class, and she was super understanding with some technical difficulties I had. She is quick to respond and wants to help.

I took the online version and it was great. You could get ahead and be done in a month if you wanted. TAs were great. Lectures and materials were all on canvas. There are weekly quizzes (that you can use your notes on), 2 projects and 4 exams, all of which you can do well on if you study.

This intro to dietetics class is pass/fail, super easy. You could easily crank out all the assigments at the beginning of the semester. The guest speakers she brings in are super helpful, attend at least 5 of the days to pass. The assignments really help you gauge if dietetics is right for you. She's super down to earth and sassy which I loved!

This class will give you what you give it. There is a lot you have to know and memorize and no one will reach out to you since it is online. The weekly quizzes can be pretty hard, but halfway through the semester, I learned that the TAs would literally walk you through the problems. So reach out and ask for help, you'll do just fine :)

Straightforward class, mostly just reading, open note weekly quizzes, discussion posts, and tests. I appreciate that she cares about what she's teaching. Skim the textbook reading and take notes on the Canvas modules, and study for the tests. I learned a lot and I never had issues.

Tough grader, one time I spelled a word wrong in a response and she docked me points just because of that. She wasn't super helpful, modules are basically just straight text book reading(not helpful). Lots of small assignments but docked me points for things I thought was unfair. Due dates were very inconsistent! Not super well put together class.

Took this class online and those who took it in person/different teachers were struggling. I worked on it once a week for a few hours-pretty easy! Weekly quizzes and modules to read/watch, 4 online tests. Don't forget to comment on the discussions even though they are dumb! And don't stress reading the textbook; important stuff is in the modules.

Professor Patten is nice, but the online class was hard to navigate. Due dates were inconsistent, constantly caught me off guard, and no late assignments are accepted. If you want to catch everything then you HAVE to pay attention to the announcements at the beginning of the week AND you should look through the module at the beginning of the week.

This is just an introductory course to dietetics and only one credit, but it is still a lot of work for only one credit. Make sure to do the assignments. My experience was fine, nothing stellar, but she does bring in some really good speakers to tell you about your jobs. The job exploration she has you do is fantastic.

Dr. Patten is an amazing professor who I really wish I could have taken a class from in person! I took the online course (COVID) and still was able to do ok in her class. It is hard though, there is a TON of material covered but she explains everything really well and shares lots of visuals and charts to understand harder topics. Highly recommend:)

Go to class and read the textbook and you'll do great. Lectures are pretty dry, but Dr. Patten is funny and will spice it up sometimes. Material is interesting, but if you don't put in the work, you won't do well. A few assignments throughout the semester. Most of the grade comes from tests. Clear grading criteria. Just follow the study guide.

For Psych 210, shes the best option Exams require you to write like 5 in depth paragraphs per question all based on memorization, which takes a lot of preparation. Most homework is manageable lectures are great and there is a timeline project Do not cram to enjoy the course.

I took Basic Mediation from Prof. Taylor and it's changed the way I think and act. I'm a Jr and there are only a few classes I would say have impacted me as much as this one. I would recommend it to everyone. Prof. Taylor brought the spirit into almost every discussion. There were a lot of textbooks, but they were genuinely interesting!

She is a super kind teacher, and willing to help! However, I felt stressed because she was not always organized and changed assignments last minute. The class wasn't hard, but her organization skills were frustrating! Her lectures were sometimes long and felt all over the place, and the information we learned wasn't on the tests most of the time.

Mrs. Price is great! It's a good idea to go to class, but if you miss here and there it isn't the end of the world. Daily small assignments, and the tests are manageable if you put some time into studying. She's very willing to accommodate extenuating circumstances and adjust some deadlines. Lectures can be hard to listen to sometimes.

She is a super kind teacher, and willing to help! However, I felt stressed because she was not always organized and changed assignments last minute. The class wasn't hard, but her organization skills were frustrating! Her lectures were sometimes long and felt all over the place, and the information we learned wasn't on the tests most of the time.

Daily small assignments, and the tests are manageable if you put some time into studying. She's very willing to accommodate extenuating circumstances and adjust some deadlines. Lectures can be hard to listen to sometimes.

The class wasn't hard, but her organization skills were frustrating! Her lectures were sometimes long and felt all over the place, and the information we learned wasn't on the tests most of the time.
