Daily small assignments, and the tests are manageable if you put some time into studying. She's very willing to accommodate extenuating circumstances and adjust some deadlines. Lectures can be hard to listen to sometimes.

(For English 203) Professor Esplin was amazing! We read some challenging but amazing texts during this course, and Professor Espin's enthusiasm for them made me excited to come to class every day. This class has the occasional assignment (usually annotations or short essays) but otherwise was entirely reading. I would highly recommend him!
I took Emron Esplin for 203, but regardless he is my favorite professor at BYU. I really enjoyed all the material we went over simply because I could tell he was excited as well.

I have heard so many complaints about other UNIV 101 classes but Professor Esplin was very caring and accommodating. The curriculum itself can get a little repetitive, but our additional English readings were interesting. Professor Esplin would also often bring sourdough bread to our 8 am class to bring a little joy to our mornings.

Professor Esplin was so awesome!! I took this class not really knowing what to expect, and he chose an interesting topic that didn't make me dread doing the readings. I had his class at 8 am and he always kept me awake with his jokes so that's a plus. There was only five grades when I took the class so that was a little stressful but I survived.

I took Dr. Esplin for American Literary History and it became my favorite class! You read everything outside of class which can be heavy. However, his lectures and discussions were outstanding! I had his class at 8am and didn't fall asleep once. If you pay attention during class and take decent notes, you will do well on the test!

Professor Esplin is awesome! He is very funny and he really love these authors and stories. He is really passionate and he inspires you to be passionate too. He helped bring the stories to life. I took this class Spring term and he was really understanding and compassionate about the schedule and tried to moderate the course load for us.

I really loved his class.  It's super reading heavy, but at a survey of literature so that's expected.  He's very engaging, interesting, and just all around a nice class.  His class itself is pretty easy, one paper near the beginning of the semester.  His tests are kind of a beast.  They are easy but super super long.  Overall, highly recommend.

His lectures are AMAZING -- informative and enjoyable. You will read a lot in this class, but it's definitely manageable. He's a funny professor and easy to work with. There is only one essay in the class and most of the remaining points come from 3 tests. Work hard on that essay--he grades them tough and they count for a lot.

Professor Esplin is wonderful! I already loved this period of American lit. but he made me love it even more. His lectures are great, and if you take notes you'll pass the tests easily. His spot-quotes are easily identifiable and he is always willing to help the students. I'd definitely take again if I could.

One of the best teachers I have had. He has the most wonderful lectures. I didn't want to take this class (but had to) - not a big fan of American lit, but I LOVED it. If you attend class and take good notes, it is easy to study for the tests and get good grades. He is very willing to help too. Awesome teacher.

I took American Literary History with Professor Esplin in the spring and it was amazing. Seriously one of the best classes I've ever had. He is super clear about what you need to do to do well in the class (prepare to read), the tests were fair, and I absolutely loved how he involved the class in discussion--I learned a lot and loved this class!

I took his class when he was teaching in Georgia. He is by far the best teacher I have ever had. Granted, i love literature, but his class was the best I have ever taken. Great content that you do have to read. The class is outlined from the beginning and extremely interesting!

I love this man. He is so absolutely clear in his lectures, and he's super intelligent. Tests aren't super hard because, if you listened in class, you know what to expect. Very organized. Cares about his students and their learning. He gives really good feedback on papers, too. I learned so much in his class. Definitely recommend, one of my faves.

Professor Esplin devotes so much time to helping you improve as a writer. He grades like a beast, but if you put forth good effort you shouldn't have a problem. Definitely take any class from Professor Esplin if you can.

Dr Dahlin is so kind and understanding. The coursework is hard, but he looks for opportunities to give points, even if you were not necessarily correct. The TAs are so helpful. You will spend time in the lab doing the homework assignments, but they prepare you well for the exams. Dr Dahlin is hilarious and just the nicest professor ever.

Great professor! Stata can be difficult to learn but he really wants to help you and wants you to succeed. Ask lots of questions and pay attention to the study guides and you'll do fine. Following along with the textbooks (like he suggests) will really help you understand Stata and the slides better. Super interesting class!

Dr. Dahlin is a great professor! If you take a class from him, know that your attendance and digital dialogue participation is critical to your grade at the end of the semester. He will tell you, but won't remind of these things. If it's in his syllabus, he means it. If you just do what he says (read, participate, know the readings), it's great!

Professor Dahlin is AMAZING. This class material is difficult, and definitely has a learning curve, but he is so helpful. He cares so much about his students, and gives you everything you could ever need to succeed. He is such an awesome guy.

Eric is the best. I absolutely loved this class. He is an expert in his field. He gives the most amazing lectures and is an inspiration. Everyone should take a class from him. The class is stats, and there is a learning curve in statistical software, but Eric is so willing to help and such a great teacher you are sure to succeed if you do the work

Data Management is difficult but Dr. Dahlin explains it well. Tests are open to all material we've used except the internet, but they are timed. No final, instead there is a group project. Very fair grader and will help you raise your grade if you talk to him. One of the most caring teachers I've ever had. Take the class from Dahlin!

Prof Dahlin is a great teacher! The class is a hard class as you are learning how to use a new software programming system, but Professor Dahlin does his best to make it clear and concise. Pop Quizzes are easy. Tests are open everything besides internet. He responds to emails promptly and will help you pass. Take this class, you wont regret it!

Withdrew because the class was so hard to endure. He isn't very effective  at communicating what he understands. It's a very dry lecture that seems very ill prepared (stumbling). Pop quizzes and test made of commentary from weekly group discussions make up most of your grade. You have to read 4 long academic articles each week for the discussions.
Eric is such a well rounded professor, extremely knowledgeable and fair grader.

Eric is a super good guy, very knowledgeable and he's got some humor which makes lectures fun. I didn't love his exams, I felt like they were trying to trick me and it didn't help that they were the only scores in the gradebook. But Eric was pretty lenient with curving scores and helping us out that way.

Great class! online which was great. videos were super helpful and insightful for anyone looking to start a business and wanting to learn digital marketing or going into marketing career. Videos are all really well made, nice guy, and cares about the subject. Straight forward class.
Great guy obviously loved his work and wanted you to succeed. You get what you put in.

I am SO frustrated with this class. I want to work in digital marketing, and I am a marketing major. Did I learn anything useful? Not really. It's all online which I hate, and its just straight up not helpful. He should not be teaching this course, this subject is constantly changing with the times and so much should've been taught that wasn't.

I loved the way Professor Derosia taught! I learned a lot! He is spunky and fun. It can be a hard class to get into at first and it feels confusing as to what the class is about but then it makes sense a few weeks in! Group projects are easy if you follow guidelines. Exams are open book and are written response. Highly highly recommend!

This professor teaches like he has no idea what he's talking about. Nothing is clear. His teaching style has students questioning where he got his qualifications to teach. His lectures are confusing, and his quizzes are designed to trip students up rather than assess their understanding. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM ANYONE ELSE!!

Professor DeRosia's teaching methods are so confusing. 415 is a terrible class. His quizzes are written to confuse students rather than assess knowledge.  Despite appearing easy, assignments are heavily scrutinized, with minor errors resulting in significant grade deductions. AVOID THIS CLASS. Take this class from any other professor.

The class isn't too difficult- two recorded lectures that you can watch and take a quiz on anytime during the week, some textbook reading, an easy midterm and final, and many group projects. If you're a marketing major, I would recommend taking during winter so your group consists of more marketing students (fall has more non-marketing students)

Even though this is an online course, Professor Derosia records the lectures as you go so that everything is super up-to-date and relevant, and he makes them entertaining. I learned a lot about digital marketing, although I'm not sure how much of it I'll remember because the online format makes it harder to take notes than an in-person class.

Great professor! The class was online with most everything due at the end of the semester so be sure to stay up to date with the workload. It wasn't overly difficult, but there were a lot of group projects so be sure to make a group chat or something with your group. There is a midterm and final that aren't too bad either

DeRosia is an excellent teacher. He REALLY puts effort into all his classes to make it applicable. Lectures are extremely up-to-date with the latest digital marketing know-how. Digital Marketing changes quickly and he updated videos and the textbook to keep it relevant. I'd say this class is mandatory for marketing students. Plus he is hilarious.
He used a packet of readings, not a "textbook."  He's funny, but content is more important, and his content is great!  He's really innovative.  I wish he taught more classes.

DeRosia is hilarious and really cares about his students. He validates every comment made, and does everything to make the class entertaining and interesting. he lets YOU decide whether the test is in group and/or open-book!

Way funny, class is interesting, and you'll learn a ton.  However, his grading is heavily based on a group simulation.  Basically, if you get a crappy group who doesn't come through for you in the simulation you CANNOT get an A.  Then again, if you're a lazy mooch, land yourself in a good group and they'll earn the grade for you.

Hilarious teacher, and interesting subject matter! He's incredibly witty, and VERY good at making concepts and theories very clear. He's an excellent teacher, and very good at understanding different comments and questions in order to respond well. He gives GREAT feedback, and it's very specific, which makes it very helpful.

Great teacher.  Very interested and enthusiastic about the subject. He puts a lot of time into the PowerPoints & usually gives some "Free Advice" to the class which is really interesting and useful. To be honest, walking out of the class I don't feel as if I RETAINED much of the information he taught in lectures. He's still fun to listen to though.

One of the best teachers in the school.  He cares enough to grade students assignments himself and give specific feedback.  An excellent teacher and presenter, very entertaining.  Genuinely cares about his students--encourages one-on-one help for the class and for careers.
He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes everything crystal clear, and we only had group tests, so those were pretty easy. Highly Recommended!
A very useful class.  When I started it, I didn't think it would be useful to me (I'm in the MAcc program).  But now that it's almost finished, I see that the info will be very useful.
He is a great teacher. His tests really are not that hard. As long as you do the readings, you should be fine! In Busm 444 the tests are group ones, so it is not a tought class to do really well in.
DeRosia's a great guy.  I love his dry sense of humor.  If you like the comic book guy on the Simpsons, you'll like DeRosia.  I never read at all, and tests can be tricky, but I got an A-.

Great! Funny+interesting+greatTeacher. No busywork or quizzes: just tests and Harvard business cases. The cases are complex, and you learn a lot. The tests aren't too bad, and they are about *understanding*, not memorization. If you come to class, read the book *regularly*, and understand the concepts, you should score in the 90's and learn a lot.
Hell yes the tests are tough.  The lectures are cool and he keeps you interested, however, listen for his one liners because they will be on the tests.

Very ethusiastic about the subject.  He's hilarious, he keeps you rollin' the entire class period.  His tests are kind of tough, and almost the entire class is based on the tests.  Otherwise a great teacher!
Would recommend to anyone who likes engaging learning. Dr. Dursteler has a very open and kind soul and is both so sincere and super funny. Nothing felt like fluff.  10/10

I took Honors 290R with Drs. Dursteler and Ahlborn (a food science professor). Dr. Dursteler clearly knows his stuff, but he didn't get much of a chance to teach in this class because other things took much of the time. But he was always willing to listen to us students and take our questions and opinions into account. Good professor overall.

Easy class for the GE but pop-attendance quizzes scared me all the time, they were easy, just showing that you went to class. Everything is open book and open note but you have to write down like everything he says. He doesn't take attendance just randomly checks who's there like 5 times in the semester but offers extra credit.

Super lecture heavy, and all the things on the test are about the lectures. Cant have the lecture slides and you only have your notes for preparing for tests but they are open notes. Would recommend making lots of friends and get lots of people to share notes when it comes time the tests. Participation points sometimes in class too.

This class wasn't too hard, but it seemed like it was harder than it needed to be. The reading is due in huge chunks with almost nothing in between, so it was hard when I failed to plan ahead. You need to attend every lecture and take good notes. 
Also be prepared to write an essay on modern climate change... in an ancient history class

Professor Dursteler is a perfect example of just because you are smart doesn't mean you are good at teaching. He doesn't know how to teach the concepts effectively. Don't bother taking his tests unless you've written down EVERYTHING HE says. Even when you have, the questions are worded incredibly hard and confusing. Avoid this class if you can.

Honestly one of the easiest classes I've taken at BYU! There is not much work outside of class, lectures are interesting, and tests are open note. Highly recommend taking this class to fulfill the civ credit.

He was a fun professor and taught interesting things, but it was really hard to focus because he teaches from a few slides. You have to pay CLOSE attention the lectures because that is what the tests are on. It is open note, so as long as you go to every class you will be good. I skipped 1 class and there was a pop quiz, so it was kind of annoying.

This class wasn't my favorite; I took a good amount of notes and still didn't do great on the tests. Lectures are so hard not to fall asleep in. I don't love history though, so I'm biased. The professor is super nice but the class just drained me. Lots of reading and notetaking; exams were difficult. No study guide provided other than your notes.

I do not like history and I LOVED his class. He taught in a way that was easy to understand and kept me engaged. His test are open note and open book so it is important to show up to class. His slides are mostly pictures so you have to take notes on what he says. There wasn't too much reading and the readings that were assigned were intentional.

Be VERY careful about taking notes. His slides are just pics, so you have to take notes on what he says. The tests are open note/book, but the questions are often worded pretty weirdly. He gave easy extra credit, and I liked most of his class, but some of the material was SOO boring. Overall, he is a funny dude, and the TA's are very helpful.

Professor Dursteler's HIST201 class is a great option to fulfill your civilization credit. The lectures are engaging, and if you stay on top of the readings and take good notes, you'll do well. unstuckstudy is a helpful study tool alongside the open-note exams. Recommended for an easy A!

I really liked Dr. Dursteler! He was kind and easygoing, but his teaching style was not my favorite. His slides didn't have much content, so you had to take notes just based off what he was saying, so it was hard for me to pay attention. TAKE LOTS OF NOTES! Open-book quizzes, 2 open note exams, one big paper, and mandatory class events throughout.

Amazing professor! All of the tests and quizzes are open book and open note so make sure that you take really good notes in class. Don't be spooked by the number of readings, he specifically states at the beginning of the semester to not read them cover to cover, but rather skim them. As a non-history major I recommend taking this class as a GE.

Dr. Dursteler is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. His History 201 class was engaging and thought-provoking. He cares a lot more about you learning the material and cultivating a love for history than the difficulty of the class. Take it for an easy A, but enjoy learning along the way.

Super great Professor. The class was pretty easy if you kept on top of the readings. ATTEND LECTURE!! He does a ton of pop quizzes and most are extra credit so go for easy points!!! Super great lecture and an interesting class I definitely would recommend Dr. Dursteler.

Professor Dursteler is super reasonable and awesome! The midterm and final are open note, open book. Attendance is not mandatory, but the midterm and final are entirely based on the lectures, so go and take good notes and you'll be fine.

Professor Dursteler was amazing! History 201 is the perfect class to complete the Civ 1 credit. He's such a nice and caring teacher, and if you go to class, take notes, and do the readings, you'll get an A. This isn't a hard class at all, but it is super interesting and Professor Dursteler's lectures are great. I highly recommend! Take this class!

I was not looking forward to my history general ed, but Professor Dursteler made it so applicable and engaging, even for a STEM major! There's not a ton of homework, but when there is, it's a hefty amount of reading. There's only one big paper at the end. The tests are all open note, so if you take good notes, you'll do fine. Loved this class!

Exams are harder than you think so take really good notes because you can use them on the exams! There are not many grades in this class so do everything well. He randomly had extra credit in class so make sure you go to take notes and can do those activities. Slides are not posted so you can't skip. He is super chill and easy this is a good class.

Eric Dursteler has very interesting classes. It's clear that he knows his stuff, and his lectures are engaging and interesting. He does tend to grade harshly, and he takes a long time to grade things. His tests were fair, however, and I would definitely take from him again! Food and history was a fascinating class, and we got to eat during it. Fun!

Lectures were fun and informative. Could use notes on tests, and no textbook required. A few times he seemed annoyed by questions students asked, but besides that was a good lecturer. Definitely recommend to fulfill your civ credit.
I liked his class. If you take notes well, you can use them on a test.

Eric Dursteler is a great person and a very generous professor. This class is probably one of the easiest options for fulfilling the Civ 1 credit. The tests and quizzes are open book and note, which is super nice. There was no textbook, but instead 5 different books. Overall, glad I took the class, but I found it hard to stay awake during lectures.

Three tests and one paper, lots of reading quizzes. Read about 100 pages or more a week, 5 books and crazy amount of reading. Did not do well on first midterm so recording lectures saved me!! Tests are open book and open note. Said he wouldn't give extra credit and ended up giving some points that also helped my grade. Had trouble staying awake.

Pretty good professor. Class is not required but he doesn't post slides, so you should go. Lots of reading, but all quizzes and tests are open book/note. One big paper and one other small writing assignment. Overall, the class was decently interesting.

Participation isn't required for a grade, but go. Take really good notes! They can be used on the online tests, but the tests are very specific. They are a combination of multiple choice, short answers, and select all. It isn't very hard, but the main focus should be going to class. The quizzes are easy, just get the books.

Dursteler was honestly the worst professor I have had here at BYU. He comes off as a nice guy but doesn't really care about his students. You can definitely tell he is ready to retire and it shows in the way he teaches! If you don't record lectures and take stellar notes you won't pass the class!

Dursteler doesn't make this class too hard (he knows it's a GE). You do not have to go to class, but take really good notes during the pre-recorded lectures (it will makes tests so much easier) and this class will be a breeze. Tests are open-note and quizzes are open-book, so you just have to do the work and you will be fine.

If you're trying to knock out a GE this is the way to go. Easiest class ever. just watch the lectures/read the books/take notes, and you are set. Dr dursteler is chill and focuses on general themes/impacts rather than specific details. I wish all GEs were done just a little more like this

This class is history done the right way!  Pre-recorded lectures are extra credit and tests are open note, so you never have to worry about memorizing little details.  I normally dislike history classes because there's lots of busy work, but this class I was able to focus on appreciating other cultures rather than worrying about memorizing.

I 10/10 would recommend this class for fulfilling GE credit!  I am not a history person and hate GE's because there is a lot of busy work, but I loved this class!  Watching the pre-recorded lectures is extra credit and the class is very straight forward.  It's an easy A but I I learned valuable information about different cultures and religions!

Good guy, just terrible class. The "lectures" were just zoom recordings from 2020 and the quizzes are 3-5 questions each. The physical lectures are completely useless. The midterms are nothing like the lecture quizzes. You're better off learning from crash course.

Interesting class, pretty easy. 2021-22 was flipped class, went to class once a week to discuss prerecorded lectures, zoom option in class too. Can skim books but know them for tests. He has dry humor, is nice but slightly conceited. Weekly participat. quizzes for ex cred but will be docked if don't do them. On analyses must include quotes. Easy A

Genuinely seems like he's mentally done teaching. Met for class infrequently and even then he only reviewed what we learned on our own by watching his prerecorded zoom lectures from a previous semester. Midterm and Final combined are 40% of your grade. He says he grades on the general theme and not specifics, but his tests are very particular.

Usually, I hate history classes. But, I actually liked this class. The professor has a good vibe which made me feel less stressed over the class but made me want to put in the work. There are quite a few extra credit assignments that can be easily done if you watch the lectures you should be watching anyway. Also, the tests were open note.

He is a funny professor and is very knowledgeable. There are 2-3 books read during the class, but try to find the audio on youtube if you want to do it quickly. It's very interesting and fun with no homework other than the midterm and exam. Take good notes and remember what he says during the lecture.

Dr. Dursteler teaches history the right way. He doesn't try to fill your brain with dates and facts until your brain explodes but rather helps you understand the big picture, concepts, and ideas, and generally tests on those criteria. A few short books and 4 films with quizzes, 2 actually interesting essays, a midterm, and a final. Great GE class!

If you want an easy A (-) take your GE from this guy. Came to BYU for a quality education, but left this class wishing I had spent my money elsewhere. He seems too comfortable with his status in the department, and should probably either work harder to engage his students or end his career in academia.

He had random assignments he would come up with throughout the semester, and he never made a description for them online. The due dates and assignment details were rarely clear. He didn't remind the class of these assignments either. Hard grader. Doesn't give much to prepare for exams, just told to study lecture notes. Nice and funny guy though.

Dr. Dursteler definitely knows what he's talking about and is super knowledgeable. His lectures can be a little dry, but as long as you take good notes and keep up on readings and assignments, the tests are a breeze.

He teaches history in a totally different way than I'd every experienced before. No date memorizing, not much name or place memorizing either. Instead, he taught and tested on overall concepts and themes. There's a lot of reading that I think really adds to the class, but if you just skim it you'll do okay (again, general themes and concepts).

Not boring or monotone. Spoke fluent Italian which was very beautiful to hear. A bit of a tough grader though, but he was so inspirational that I ended up enjoying the material rather than worrying about a grade. I've had a class from him before, and I ended up switching my major to History because of him. No textbook, interesting assigned readings

Wouldnt take again. He is kind of nice, but in a neighborly way - Im more interested in paying for a professor that is engaged in his work. Class was easy, but as others have said ... that wasnt enough. Not sure why he has a position at the university.

While so many history professors focus on exact dates, he focuses on the ideas that caused the events to happen. Tests were super easy. Only required us to skim read the books. Very helpful outside of class. Super interesting lectures and only tested on what he says in class.
Wouldnt recommend. Look elsewhere.

Dry humor + Long, dry lectures - Minimal homework + No test reviews/study guides of any sort - Each test (3 total) worth 23%; grades quite hard - Tests on obscure details - Extra credit (5 pts) + Doesn't take attendance + 5 books (-), but allows you to skim + 100% on the tests possible if you make audio recordings of the lectures. :

Pro. Dursteler reads off his slides during the whole class with a little of class discussion. His powerpoints are pictures that relate to the lecture but you have to be paying attention for the entire class. Be ready to read the books he requires for class. No midterm or final with TAs or professor so get with a group

Tests are essays/short answer and based solely off lecture. Write down every word he says: his slides are pictures, there's no textbook no reviews, he tests on specific details he finds important and will knock you down for using facts off the internet. All of that said I slept through half the class and got an A ... so? It's hard but doable.

Honestly, I'm not sure where all the negative reviews are coming from: I thoroughly enjoyed taking Dr. Dursteler's class. His lectures were extremely interesting & inspiring, & his breadth of knowledge of history is clear from all the cool trivia he includes. The tests are all short answer though, & you read books from different time periods.

He's vague on what he tests on, he says to learn general concepts. He also doesn't have a study guide for the test. But he gives 4 1 page papers and random points aka in-class quizzes (easy). It's not hard to get a decent grade and he doesn't ask THAT much of you. Start a google doc & get a study group! He's easy vs other civ teachers. GO TO CLASS!

Boring lectures. Sits in front of class and reads notes off a paper. Slideshows don't have content, just pictures that rarely change. No textbook, so hard to review material and must make friend if you miss class. Says he tests on "important things" but when we ask specifically, he asks us what we think is important, no straight answer/studyguide.

Just avoid this guy. Take a different class for your GE. The class material is good but he is a super dry guy. He is extremely disorganized and expect you to know small details for the tests. Take a different class and don't make the mistake I did.

This would be a great class if we didn't have to take the tests. HINT: On the test, he says you don't need to know dates or details, but be SURE to know both. I like the class and the content, but the tests are impossible and there is no study guide. Take good notes and pay attention to every detail. This class is doable, but tricky.

This is one of the worst classes I have taken. His lectures are extremely dry and boring. You have to attend though, as the material for the test is only covered in class. He also gives random assignments in class. He is extremely disorganized. He is an easy grader, but that doesn't make up for his classes. I would take it from anyone else.

Disregard the other reviews! I don't know what people have against easy grading teachers, It helps me learn more. This class was very educationally enriching. I personally love history, and learned a lot from this class. Because of the nature of the class I was more able to focus on learning, and enjoying the material over stressing about grades.

Easy A, just read the book and plan on getting 90-100 percent on everything. Kinda cool professor, but not engaging at all.I ried to go to his office hours but he was always busy and not interested in helping a student who was already meeting the standards for an "A" even though I had deeper questions about the material. It was an okay  experience.

Easiest A I received my entire time spent at BYU. I left some generals for my last semester and I should have simply tacked on his class to any of my 18 credit semesters in the past because this one required ZERO mental power or effort. I got an A but barely remembered I was taking his class once or twice a month. Take his class if you want an A.

This class made me love history! Professor Dursteler is awesome, he taught me a ton about history and his class was super interesting. You have to attend class!!! It's really doable if you just attend and do the assignments.

He's a brilliant man and gives really interesting lectures. Given the breadth of history he covers, he's good at going into interesting subsections instead of trying to cover everything in class. Have to read a dense textbook but it doesn't come up on midterm or final. Class is 100% lecture. Overall an easy A if you read and pay attention.

He had a great attitude about the coursework, but was rather blunt at times towards students about grading and performance in the course. Had very interesting lectures with inspiring references. He will grade hard, but he will be fair most of the time.

I took European History. His tests comes mainly from his lectures, which can be boring but are sometimes interesting. Most days he would sit in front of class and talk but the days he used powerpoints it was more engaging. An unreasonable amount of reading but he seemed okay with us skimming. A good grade is doable but you have to work for it.

Attendance is not mandatory but he does little "assignments" randomly for points so it helps to be there, plus his tests are almost entirely from his lectures. Quite a bit of reading, but you don't have to know specifics. Tests can seem daunting since they're all short answer, but if you were in class you'll do fine. I'd take the class again!

Test material was 99% from lectures, 1% from the reading. There's a LOT of reading to do but you can get by with just finding summaries online, as long as you understand the purpose of the books. You have to pay attention to what he says in lecture because that's what's on the tests, not what's on the powerpoints. Tests are all written, no MC.

Dursteler is very, very sarcastic, and won't take any BS and I think it's probably one of the funniest things I've seen. Lectures themselves are kinda boring, but he doesn't require attendance. No review sheets, but the questions are absurdly easy, "Name some causes for the French Revolution". Didn't read the textbook much, tests are from notes.

Dr. Dursteler is great! I learned so much in his history class. He is great at explaining difficult concepts and ideas. He has you do quite a bit of reading, but he just says to skim. He is a fair grader on essays and tests as well. All tests are free response, but the questions are very straightforward and fair.

Dr. Durseler was legit. He made things interesting and his tests were cake. You have to do the readings to get a good grade, though. It was just skimming instead of actual reading, which helped. Liked the class and recommend it to anyone.
Doesn't matter what you do you can't seemt o get above an everage grade on the tests. You get 100 on all the quizzes and then get screwed on the tests. Readings are pretty boring too.

This class is a lot of writing. Not much is done to evaluate that you have learned all the material in class. Thus to do well you need to understand the big ideas for the exams and do a good research paper.

Prof Dursteler is great! As long as you pay attention in class and do all the readings, you'll get an A. He hints at the essay questions on the test so that makes it easier. He's pretty funny sometimes and is a nice guy. He knows what he's talking about and likes to engage the class in discussion.

Professor Dursteler is fantastic! I'm not a fan of history at all, but I enjoyed the class. I took it because the class is a GE, but I don't regret taking the class. Professor Dursteler assigns some books to read and then requires a five-minute, in-class essay on them. He asks very thought-provoking questions during his lectures.

I learned a lot in this class and the books were an interesting read. If you like to skip class on a regular basis do not take this class! The two tests were based primarily off of lectures and were very subjective but were not too difficult if you attend class and take good notes.
READ THE BOOKS. As long as you do this and have a general knowledge of history the class is a breeze.

I would not recomend taking one of his classes. I was extremely dissapointed with his helpfullness towards students, his tests and quizes seemed to be poorly created, and the readings he chose were often repetitive or poorly written.
He is a great professor. my writing has improved tremendously and I am soooo glad I got to take this class from him! He is one of my favorite professors at BYU!

He grades his tests very subjectively. Just when you feel you have followed his "guidelines" for success, the rules don't seem to apply when he grades your tests and assignments. He doesn't indicate why he marks you down, he just marks you down. It feels like a stab in the dark trying to please him, even after talking to him. Sporadic lectures.

Very good teacher.  Most interesting history class I have ever taken.  First test may be a little surprising because they are a little different, but by test two and three, you should know exactly what is coming.  Lots of reading, but pretty interesting readings.

Great teacher and class, I don't like history but I liked his class a lot.  You will read a lot (and I mean a lot) and put a lot of time into this class, but it's really good.  Take lots of notes in lecture and study in groups over most important themes in history, similarities and differences between civilizations, etc. and you'll do well.

I was surprised to see so many good comments cause this was the worst class I've taken at BYU thus far.Doesn't really seem to know what he's talking about, & classes are discussion based, but then he tests on things he never taught.  Impossible to study for tests since there is no textbook. Nice class for interesting readings, hard hard hard though

I was excited to take this class prior (because of past reviews).  However, this class was the WORST class and professor I have ever experienced at BYU.  Teacher was not helpful at all when I went into his office hours--didn't want students to do well on his tests, readings were ridiculously long, tests were very hard and classes were boring.

Prof. Dursteler is the man!!  He makes class really interesting and gets you to think.  We don't use a textbook, you do have to read a lot, but its not too bad.  Best history teacher here.  Class is fun!

Makes class very interesting.  He wants people to think and not just come and take notes.  There is a lot of reading but a lot of it is also fun.  His tests are straightforward essay tests but it is sometimes hard to get an A on them at first.    Overall class was one of the better history classes I have had.

This teacher is great at teaching history and has a great personality. His personality makes the class fun and you do learn a lot from him. He does assign books to read but they are interesting and you don't have to read a textbook. The tests are not hard if you spend time on them, read the material, and study. Overall a wonderful history teacher.
This class was awesome! I enjoyed lectures as they were very organized and thorough. He doesn't have a textbook but  assigns interesting books for reading. Very easy assignments. Great professor!!!

The class was great. He was incredibly interesting to listen to and he has a great way of teaching history. He's very personable and pretty cute too! Lots of reading, but most was enjoyable and pertained to the class. Tests are challenging, but if you go to class and take notes, you'll be fine. I highly recommend this class.

Professor Dursteler had a different and refreshing view of history. There was a LOT of reading though, but if you can power through a few books and take good notes you will do fine in the class. Just make sure you go to every class or the test will eat you up. Only problem is that the TA's seemed rather stingy, I could never satisfy them.

Ths was a great class! Learned a ton. Prepare for alot of reading, but you will enjoyed all of the books. Be sure to attend class as notes are required for exam prep. Not a history major, but really liked this class. Tests are somewhat hard, but with proper study you will do fine.

Information-dense lectures, sometimes tough to keep up with.  TONS of reading in many books.  TA's did most of grading, frustrating b/c I couldn't satisfy them on certain points; professor reserved the right to grade down if you approached him about a grade, so I never felt comfortable doing that.  Amusing professor, liked his approach to history.

I had his Machiavelli class for Late Summer Honors and really enjoyed his teaching style. His laid back, discussion-based focus kept me comfortable and fascinated with our material. Make sure to do your reading, though; you won't be able to contribute if you don't.

Outstanding Professor. He is able to effectively teach as well as keep students interested. He has a very laughable personality and wants his students to do well. Be prepared to work hard because the work is not easy, but he definetely makes it more bearable.
You must be ready to work your tail off.  The tests are hard, but it is a good class with lots of discussion.  Lots of reading, but you don't have to know memorize dates.  That is a big plus.
Good looking and good professor. What more could you want?

Dursteler is one of the best professors in the history department. He knows his material and keeps class interesting. I have never been bored. He honestly cares about his students. I highly recommend taking his class if you are prepared to work hard. If you do work hard, you will do extremely well.

He has a fun teaching style. He doesn't bore you with dates and abstract facts. He is all about concepts and critical thinking. If you are willing to work hard and think openly you will love his class. It is not by any means easy though. He requires that you do tons of reading. You can read cliff notes but be careful since you need to give examples

He has a fun teaching style. He doesn't bore you with dates and abstract facts. He is all about concepts and critical thinking. If you are willing to work hard and think openly you will love his class. It is not by any means easy though. He requires that you do tons of reading. You can read cliff notes but be careful since you need to give examples

Very clear and interesting professor. Encourages discussion). Clear lectures and good use of multiple book sources. Tests and assignments are essays and rely on arbitrarily guessing the answers the TAs and teacher wants. Most importantly, though, he encourages students to think for themselves and overcome cognitive dissonance.

Took his Machiavelli class for Late Summer Honors.  You've got to do a lot of reading, but the class itself is very enjoyable.  Dursteler is very amiable and shows that he understands what it's like to sit in class for hours by giving time for breaks or having class outside on occasion.  Overall, a great experience.

Great teacher, interesting lectures... Just keep good notes on the lectures because his tests (all essay) are on the lecture. Readings you can usually find cliff notes for and get an A. Easy, but go to class.

This class was great.  He promoted excellent class discussions and deeper thought.  Though there was a lot of reading, it was just for the main idea.  He is a fair grader and respectful of his students.  He sought to help us figure out what world views fit with our religion.  His lectures were fascinating.  Highly recommended.
Interesting lectures, fair teacher, on papers and tests he excpected more than i thought was needed.
He assigns an impossible amount of reading, most of which is irrelevant; definitely go for Cliffs Notes.  Watch out for crusty TAs.
No Comments
Refreshing views. Good lecturer

He's an okay teacher, but vague on what he expects for tests. When it comes to the Middle East, he lacks any knowledge whatsoever. Just bite your tongue. He requires a lot of reading, and you leave feeling like you haven't learned much at all.
Eric is a very personable, enjoyable teacher. He is an expert on the Italian Renaissance and Italy. He offers refreshing viewpoints and allows others to do so also. HIGHLY reccommend.

ok I know I didn't take him for econ, but I loved him for univ!! definitely take him for univ, he loves bringing treats to class (he brought pizza one day, costco muffins another time) and we did yoga as a class where he did a headstand! so he's a really cool guy, definitely recommend him for univ.

Eide is entertaining but his expectations are unclear. The class is participation with two exams. While the pace is manageable, grading lacks transparency. When I asked how detailed exam answers should be, he simply said to include the author and main finding to support my answer.  Despite following his advice, I still scored lower than expected

The worst part of the class was not really knowing how I was doing until I got my final grade. Dr Eide's grading system is more lenient than it appears at first, but it was still mind-harrowing as I was convinced through the entire semester that I was getting a B. The textbook isn't vital to do well on exams, just pay attention in class.

Professor Eide is a gem. First of all, he is so funny. He makes class interesting and makes sure that we are understanding the content that he is teaching. The only downside is that his tests are hard and they make a large percentage of the overall grade.

Eide is a great guy, but the nature of introductory econometrics (the proofs and assumptions mostly) combined with his tendency to overexplain concepts made lectures very dull. Econometrics is a really useful subject, but I didn't feel that Eide's lectures made the subject particularly appealing. He's not bad, but there are better sections.

Professor Eide does a great job teaching an already difficult subject. He doesn't over work you, although this does result in a lot of points coming from tests. I definitely spent a ton of time in the TA lab. We only had 5 asssignments, all graded on participation, two tests worth 75% of your grade and 3 coding assignments.

Everyone knows ECON 388 is hard, so put that aside. Eide is a super clear teacher and has posted lectures on LS that are really nice to watch when preparing for tests. He's very open to questions during class. Tests are difficult, especially the final. But the class is curved at the end. Really good teacher.

Great option for econometrics. Not an easy class, but he makes it very straightforward and will only focus/test on things that are applicable to real research. Not nitpicky about tiny details. Highly recommend

Don't pay attention to the reviews for Econ 110, that class is hard regardless of who teaches it. HE IS AWESOME! Clear expectations, great at explaining, and he is not a hard grader. I wish he taught more Econ classes

Eide is a real gem. He helps you understand the theory intuitively instead of purely mathematically. Great guy, hilarious. Would absolutely recommend if you are not planning on getting a PhD and want to pass 388. To do well on exams, make sure you can explain in your own words all the proofs and the biases and examples of them.

Super easy class if you just need one more class to get an econ major. Quizzes are a breeze, and the tests are just a few essays. He's clear, straightforward, and a nice guy. One 8 page paper, but no homework problem sets, and reading was optional since quizzes were after class discussion anyway.
Great professor. Cares about the students. Doesnt try to make the class hard. Grading seems a little random, but still an awesome class. Not hard to do well

Dr. Eide is an engaging lecturer who is more concerned that his students acquire a solid understanding of the fundamentals of the economics of education than they memorize needless facts or understand econometrics in-depth. You can definitely learn enough from lecture to do well on tests, but you will need to read (skim) for quizzes. Recommended.
I absolutely loved Dr. Eide's class. He's a great lecturer, very personable, and wants you to succeed. Great guy, I'd absolutely recommend his class.
Great Professor.

Prof. Eide is probably the best professor I've had in the econ department. The man is on your side. He pushed back homework due dates, set up review sessions, was always communicative in class AND via email about assignments, took questions, joked around with you, & gave us two minute breaks every class! Stats is dull, but Eide's the man.

Professor Eide is a really caring and friendly professor, but not extremely helpful. I sometimes felt like he had just memorized the book and taught it in lecture. Find a study group early on, do the homework, and go to review sessions. Econ 110 is the basically the class of the devil, no matter who you take it from.

He's a nice guy, just not a terrific teacher.  The Mankiw text book is great - best textbook I have ever used, and the subject is interesting, but the test's were pretty hard, and I think you would be better off taking another teacher, even if they are more challenging.

I learned a lot in this class, he had a lot of good interesting information even though lectures sometimes were a bit dull, tests were tough and there was lots of homework. even though it was tough i enjoyed the class   i learned a lot and he has a fair grading scheme   he teaches the class very well    i would recomend him
If you read the text carefully you don't really need to go to class.  The best way to prepare for tests is going through the previous midterms.

Pretty good. As noted, lectures are very similar to the text, so if you read ahead you'll probably take a nap in class. His tests are a little tough, but he's reasonable, we all did extra-poor on this last test so he gave us all 5 extra points. I'd certainly recommend him, and I imagine things get more interesting when you pass the 100 level class.

Prof. is a good teacher, with passion for what he does. I was very interested in Econ before class, but through the semester I learned to hate it. Alot of homework, tests are pretty hard, and its really hard to stay awake in the lectures.

Eide put me to sleep every lecture (really - it was a great nap time).  I felt like his lectures were too similar to the text, so I was really bored in class if I had done the reading ahead of time.  The grade is based on a bell curve, so all you have to do is better than other people. There's lots of help if you need/want it.

I loved this class! He was really approachable and helped me on several occasions. He was respectful of students and obviously loves Econ. His lectures were a little boring but really well put together. His teaching style is straight forward. Take his class! For the most failed class on campus his grading is really lenient.

Prof. Eide's down to earth and a likable guy! Homework consisted of online aplia problems and a couple book problems due Monday nights as well as book response papers due Thursdays. The practice midterms helped me prepare for the real ones. I really enjoyed going to lectures, but the text book is just as good, so people skipped. Good luck!
Dr. Eide is the man.  388 was a fun class and he made the subject matter very interesting.  I recommend taking 388 from him.

Eide was a decent teacher.  He was nice and willing to help you out a little bit, but it took him forever to email me back.  The tests were ridiculous, he gives you previous tests to study from, but it still didnt seem to help at all.  I studied literally for 26 hours for the final and got a 62! No matter who you take it from it's gonna be hard

If you understand graphs you'll do fine in this class. I had it at 8 in the morning tues/thur and I slept through it every time I went. I skipped it a couple of times too and I still got an A. If you want a hardcore class, don't take it from Eide. If you want an easier grade, I highly recommend him.

I had high expectations for this course with Dr. Eide. I found that his teaching style was imprecise, disjointed, and confusing. I work hard in all my classes and it is not a function of tenacity. If you can, switch to a more "difficult" teacher because you will get precise information. "Easy" classes come down to work and correct information.

I didn't like his teaching style at all.  He used power points that someone else created and tried to just go along with that instead of making his own.  The only way he helped you prepare for tests was by giving you the old test from his honors section.  It wasn't until I was preparing for the final that I finally understood how to set up problems

Hard to stay awake. One time I went to class so excited to learn and finally not fall asleep... ten minutes later I was out cold. Periodically during class he'd turn on the lights to wake people (not a lie.) Text book has a chapter that starts off by saying "most people find the following topic boring." I did take a 8:00 am class, maybe that was..

Eide is a really good guy. He is very fair and reasonable. I hate Econ, and this class didn't raelly make me like it any more, but it did help me to understand it. The tests are definitely hard, but not impossible. The homework load is very reasonable. Awesome class!

He is a great teacher that knows what he is talking about. He is very knowledgable abd wants you to succeed. Its a hard class, but as long as you stay on top of the work, you'll be fine. Tests are tough, but thats due to the course. I would recomend this class.
He knows the information very well. He also knows how to convey it to you.
Good Class and fair grading
Great class and professor. Makes the material very easy to understand and is a very fair grader. I got my first A in Econ by taking this class which should say something about this class.

He knows his math and can make you leave class feeling pretty clueless.  He especially loves matrix algebra so if you struggled with that in 378 watch out.  He responds very respectfully to any questions and provides plenty of resources to help you learn the material.  Grading is based mostly on two exams and the paper (which can be good or bad).

This class requires a lot of reading (2 books other than the textbook).  Be prepared to put in around 4 hours of work outside of class each week.  He is a good teacher.  The tests are hard but fair.  The smaller class size is a big plus.  I would recommend this teacher to anyone who really wants to learn something
He is a stud.  I was very scared of this class coming in but he made it a very pleasant experience.  His final was a take home and it was a bear.

Great Class - one of my favorite at BYU.  I like Dr. Eide's style because he teaches a concept, and then gives the class a practice problem and a couple of minutes to try and figure it out on your own.  it forces you to come to terms with the material, and helps you to figure out what questions you might have.

I enjoyed the class. I asked a lot of questions, and he was willing to address things I was interested in (within reason) even if it wasn't fully in the realm of the curriculum. He knows his stuff, and he has substantive real-world experience outside the classroom. I felt lucky compared to my friends who had Kearl.

Dr. Eide's a fun teacher that really likes the material he teaches. He delegates a decent amount to his TA's, but he provides past exams to help prepare and does a good job lecturing. The homework load is not too bad and the tests are moderately hard if you prepare well. I would recommend him to anyone.

This was his first year teaching econ 110 and he seemed unprepared.  He just used the slides provided by the book and I think a lot of his test material came from other teachers.  Tests were a little subjective and fairly difficult.  Aside from the generic slides, he was an enjoyable lecturer and an enjoyable prof.

Dr. E very passionate and knowledgeable but slightly disorganized. The content is important and relevant. I think everyone should read How to Read the Bible by James Kugel. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit. You will engage with uncomfortable ideas.

Every class has a quiz on the reading and a lecture, so if you miss class your grade takes a hit. Overall not hard, but he is equal parts passionate and disorganized. Sometimes if was unclear what his grading criteria was. The final is 30 questions given ahead of time, but beware that every question is 7-8 parts, with info not covered in lecture.

He is awesome!! I loved his lectures and I learned so much from this class, it's genuinely my favorite class I've ever taken. Lots of readings and the final includes three parts (oral, group, personal) but it's so easy and enjoyable. Be prepared to buy a lot of textbooks but they're super useful for extra credit-I got so many extra points bc of it.
I loved this class so much. The Bible as Literature is my favorite course I've taken at BYU so far. He's a great professor. If you consistently show up and do the readings, you're chillin.

He is a super interesting guy. You can tell that he is very very passionate about folklore. He is super positive and even though I wasn't a super big fan of the content he made the class very interesting. I would totally take this class again.

The whole course is worth 185 points, which means each point is more than 0.5% of your grade. It's pretty stressful, but he's a generous grader, so it isn't too bad. He is a great guy and wants his students to succeed. It's pretty much just a slightly disorganized lecture each time. Don't buy the books, they're not required at all.

Taking this class from Professor Eliason was absolutely worth it! Going to class is really important, but he offers so many opportunities for extra credit that you can basically guarantee yourself an A. The only thing that I really had to study for/stress about was the Final Oral Exam, but it ended up being great :)

He's very kind & understanding, and he makes the lectures very engaging! However, be aware that there are no powerpoints, and each lecture is based off his words alone, so make sure you're taking notes and actively listening to what he's saying! Attendance is pretty important, since most of the projects rely on it.

Overall a great class. Every once in a while he was harder to listen to and taking notes was hard to follow, but overall it was engaging if you chose to be engaged. Some projects seemed intimidating, but he's open to giving feedback before the due date. getting started ahead of time really helps too. I see things different now from this class!

No information is given outside lectures so attendance is required to pass. Note-taking is required since the midterm is based on lectures: no slides just talks at you. final project might be easily graded but needs a lot of time. the final exam is based on peer final projects that were presented. One book quiz and its pretty detailed. Verbal tests

Professor Eliason is a remarkable professor. I learned so much and my testimony grew so much. There are daily quizzes but you can use your notes. The projects are fun and engaging and he doesn't grade harshly. The oral exam was stressful but he is accommodating if he can tell you aren't a fan of public speaking. This class is incredible. Do it.

Professor is so sweet and funny, I adored having him. His class was very easy, I skipped a lot of class and finished with a 94 in the class. He offers a lot of extra credit that can end up moving your grade like 7 whole points. Small papers, couple quizzes, one big paper, and one presentation.

This class was a great way to fulfill the letters requirement. Super easy, hardly any homework, and lots of extra credit opportunities. Dr. E is a super cool guy! The midterm is really easy to study for and open notes, and the final is based off of student presentations, also open notes. He grades pretty generously also!

SO GREAT! Take this class! He helps everyone get a good grade and there is a ton of extra credit. No midterm and the final seems like it will be easy! But that's not even the best part-- he is just ADORABLE and so amazing. He cares about us and loves what he is teaching. His lectures might be the most interesting, fun, and mind-blowing ever!!!

Professor Eliason is quirky (in a good way), knowledgeable, and fun. I learned how to read and study the Bible in this class. Eliason cares more about students actually learning rather than preparing them to pass semester exams for grades. This was a fun class and one of the best GE classes. TONS OF EASY EXTRA CREDIT, class average is 110%.

Wow. Dr. Eliason is a fantastic professor. His class was easy, yet really interesting. Learning about the Bible through the lens of literature was defintely life changing. He's always happy to help students as needed and he provides ample opportunities for students to get whatever grade they want as there are probably 100 extra credit opportunities

Class material was really interesting, and lecture was always lots of fun. Unfortunately the class was not organized very well, with lots of typos in the syllabus and not much detail explained on projects. Tests are easy, but has a huge final project that takes a lot of time. Decent class to take for the letters requirement or whatever though

(FALL 2020 COVID SEMESTER REVIEW) Doctor Eliason is AMAZING. He gives you literally every opportunity to be successful (like giving enough extra credit to make up for 7% of your grade). You're not graded on many things, but he's very clear on expectations. If you take good notes and pay attention, you'll be totally fine. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

A great class. There is a decent amount of reading, but just easy reads from the Bible. Other than that, there is basically no homework , just short quizzes before each lecture and a final project. Lectures are very interesting and the class size is small.

This was the best class I have ever taken in college. There is almost no homework, every lecture is hearing a new story or learning a new joke and Eric is so excited about folklore it's infectious. I'm so sad this class had to end because I loved it!

Easy A for your letters requirement. He really cares and his lectures are super interesting! The pop quizzes are easy if you did the reading, and he gives you the questions for the midterm beforehand. The final project can be cumbersome but start early and you won't have a problem with it!

Bro. Eliason is awesome. His folklore class is really interesting and you learn a lot of cool things. I love listening to his stories and you can tell he really loves what he teaches about. He doesn't use powerpoints, but I feel like his lectures are fairly easy to follow.

Take your Letters class in Intro to Folklore with Bro. Eliason. I promise it is worth it. There are quizzes that are super easy, and there are several extra credit opportunities. The final project can be cumbersome- but it isn't too hard and it isn't graded that hard either. Genuinely cares for his students as well.

The tests are a breeze! Follow along with the midterm study guide as he lectures and the midterm will be very easy! The final is 10 questions (take home) and based on student presentations. HIs lectures were funny and interesting! Only a few readings total and easy quizzes on those readings. Lots of extra credit opportunities!

I could never say enough good things about Dr. Eliason. He absolutely loves the subject. I learned so much through this class. He is very fair and if you try you will do fine. It is all about the effort and learning. Take classes from him.

Dr. Eliason was very open to the students ideas and encouraged class discussion. We had quizzes every day that were very hard, but the test was a breeze. One really annoying thing was that he never graded two pretty important projects that i worked really hard on. Overall a nice guy though.

This is a very interesting and fun class. I signed up for it because I thought it would be an easy "A". I walked away from it having been changed in some of my core beliefs. This class is really fun, but it is also very introspective. You start to think about why you think certain things, and who you are in relation to the world. Really cool.

Eliason is a great professor. I looked froward to the readings and the lectures every class period.  The tests are not difficult so long as you are doing your reading and paying attention and study a little bit.  This class was my favorite GE by far and I recommend taking the Bible as Lit from him any time. Great guy.

Eric is very organized and his classes are easy A if you do the work and pay attention in class. I really learned a lot from him and twelve years later, I still know stuff I learned in his folklore classes. I took three classes from him.
Great professor, Great class, Nice guy, workload not overburdensome or hard to understand. Would take another class from him in a heartbeat.
Great, engaging professor. NICE person. Concerned about students. Classes not overburdonsome or difficult to understand. Interesting subject.

Amazing! Loved the class, and Dr. Eliason made it super interesting. My favorite class this semester, hands down, and it doesn't even have anything to do with my major. I would definitely recommend it to everyone.

Loved this class!  So interesting, learned a lot.  Didn't attend class all the time, but I would have if I could. Study guide is very extensive and the study groups helped a lot. Extra credit is offered-easy, so do it. I never cracked any books open, but I'll probably come out of that class with a B- or C+. An A is definitely possible though.
It felt like we were playing the whole time. I'm sure alot had to do with the topic of folklore but this is a fun class and you can easily get an A if you want to.
There were a lot of textbooks I never used. The class was more about religious scholarship rather than literature, but it was interesting nevertheless.
Fun class, not to difficult, and really interesting. The assignments are fun and they're graded pretty leniently. Great class and great teacher!

The final project was graded easy and fun to do. Class is worth 275 points only. The lectures are really interesting. The textbooks don't seem to be necessary at all. (you can probably just borrow from other people) The tests are confusing, he gives a vocab list/study sheet, but there were always surprises and he grades VERY STRICTLY. Loved DR. E!
He was great and fun. He understands that life happens and will work with you.
Professor E is awesome!!! You'll totally enjoy this class... it's really facinating and fun!
Really fun class, lectures are great and Dr. Eliason is really interested in the subject matter.  As long as you go to class and do the assignments it is not too difficult!

This class is simple to study for as long as you go to every class and take good notes. Eliason is a good teacher because he loves his subject and, even if you don't, you may still enjoy the lectures.

I think he has a chip on his shoulder with people not thinking that the study of folklore is a serious science so because of that it seems like he goes out of his was to make the class rough. The material isn't hard, he is just super unflexable and unwilling to change things to help you out if you run into a bind or something.
This class was good, much better (I imagine) than any other class that fuffills the arts and letters elective.

Prof. Eliason is a pretty cool guy.  His folklore class wasn't the "most interesting or stimulating class around, but he taught on our level and made us use our talents in presentations and projects.  How many times do you get to play MASH in a folklore class? This guy rocks!
He's totally hot!
No Comments
Eric is such a well rounded professor, extremely knowledgeable and fair grader.

Eric is a super good guy, very knowledgeable and he's got some humor which makes lectures fun. I didn't love his exams, I felt like they were trying to trick me and it didn't help that they were the only scores in the gradebook. But Eric was pretty lenient with curving scores and helping us out that way.

Great class! online which was great. videos were super helpful and insightful for anyone looking to start a business and wanting to learn digital marketing or going into marketing career. Videos are all really well made, nice guy, and cares about the subject. Straight forward class.
Great guy obviously loved his work and wanted you to succeed. You get what you put in.

I am SO frustrated with this class. I want to work in digital marketing, and I am a marketing major. Did I learn anything useful? Not really. It's all online which I hate, and its just straight up not helpful. He should not be teaching this course, this subject is constantly changing with the times and so much should've been taught that wasn't.

I loved the way Professor Derosia taught! I learned a lot! He is spunky and fun. It can be a hard class to get into at first and it feels confusing as to what the class is about but then it makes sense a few weeks in! Group projects are easy if you follow guidelines. Exams are open book and are written response. Highly highly recommend!

This professor teaches like he has no idea what he's talking about. Nothing is clear. His teaching style has students questioning where he got his qualifications to teach. His lectures are confusing, and his quizzes are designed to trip students up rather than assess their understanding. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM ANYONE ELSE!!

Professor DeRosia's teaching methods are so confusing. 415 is a terrible class. His quizzes are written to confuse students rather than assess knowledge.  Despite appearing easy, assignments are heavily scrutinized, with minor errors resulting in significant grade deductions. AVOID THIS CLASS. Take this class from any other professor.

The class isn't too difficult- two recorded lectures that you can watch and take a quiz on anytime during the week, some textbook reading, an easy midterm and final, and many group projects. If you're a marketing major, I would recommend taking during winter so your group consists of more marketing students (fall has more non-marketing students)

Even though this is an online course, Professor Derosia records the lectures as you go so that everything is super up-to-date and relevant, and he makes them entertaining. I learned a lot about digital marketing, although I'm not sure how much of it I'll remember because the online format makes it harder to take notes than an in-person class.

Great professor! The class was online with most everything due at the end of the semester so be sure to stay up to date with the workload. Brother Hansen is a great conductor. He's fun and knows his stuff. To anyone considering playing in the symphony, I recommend it!

No Comments

Overall, great experience.
Dr. Hintz is a great teacher and a great person as well. Highly recommend taking 127 with him! The workload is completely reasonable in my opinion and the tests are doable.

Honestly, I have never been interested in physics until I took this class. I loved it because you get to learn about all the amazing laws and reasons why our universe is the way it is. Tests are kind of annoying because some questions are ambiguous and dont make sense. There is quite a bit of homework. The material is interesting, but there is no point of a lot of the homework. I loved this class. I learned a lot. Dr. Hintz has great options for the course for all types of learners. He teaches a hard subject in a way that helps his students really learn the subject. Dr. Hintz also tied in the gospel to his subject in a beautiful way that helped me understand more fully. It helped me be more excited about the class.

By some miracle, I got a B in this class. I'm sure it's fairly easy if you put in the time, I just did not do that. Don't take this class if you have a tough schedule. You have lots of assignments (that I don't recommend you procrastinate...) and there's some reading. Go over the slides and your notes a bunch before each exam.

Though a difficult class, there is some benefit to taking astronomy. Out of all the professors, Dr. Hintz is probably the best. Though lectures are long, boring, and often put you to sleep, you might actually learn something about the universe. There's a lot of out-of-class work and studying, but in the end you get a GE and know some constellations

I didn't love his exams, I felt like they were trying to trick me and it didn't help that they were the only scores in the gradebook. But Eric was pretty lenient with curving scores and helping us out that way.

Great class! online which was great. videos were super helpful and insightful for anyone looking to start a business and wanting to learn digital marketing or going into marketing career. Videos are all really well made, nice guy, and cares about the subject. Straight forward class.
Great guy obviously loved his work and wanted you to succeed. You get what you put in.

I am SO frustrated with this class. I want to work in digital marketing, and I am a marketing major. Did I learn anything useful? Not really. It's all online which I hate, and its just straight up not helpful. He should not be teaching this course, this subject is constantly changing with the times and so much should've been taught that wasn't.

I loved the way Professor Derosia taught! I learned a lot! He is spunky and fun. It can be a hard class to get into at first and it feels confusing as to what the class is about but then it makes sense a few weeks in! Group projects are easy if you follow guidelines. Exams are open book and are written response. Highly highly recommend!

This professor teaches like he has no idea what he's talking about. Nothing is clear. His teaching style has students questioning where he got his qualifications to teach. His lectures are confusing, and his quizzes are designed to trip students up rather than assess their understanding. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM ANYONE ELSE!!

Professor DeRosia's teaching methods are so confusing. 415 is a terrible class. His quizzes are written to confuse students rather than assess knowledge.  Despite appearing easy, assignments are heavily scrutinized, with minor errors resulting in significant grade deductions. AVOID THIS CLASS. Take this class from any other professor.

The class isn't too difficult- two recorded lectures that you can watch and take a quiz on anytime during the week, some textbook reading, an easy midterm and final, and many group projects. If you're a marketing major, I would recommend taking during winter so your group consists of more marketing students (fall has more non-marketing students)

Even though this is an online course, Professor Derosia records the lectures as you go so that everything is super up-to-date and relevant, and he makes them entertaining. I learned a lot about digital marketing, although I'm not sure how much of it I'll remember because the online format makes it harder to take notes than an in-person class.

Great professor! The class was online with most everything due at the end of the semester so be sure to stay up to date with the workload. It wasn't overly difficult, but there were a lot of group projects so be sure to make a group chat or something with your group. There is a midterm and final that aren't too bad either

DeRosia is an excellent teacher. He REALLY puts effort into all his classes to make it applicable. Lectures are extremely up-to-date with the latest digital marketing know-how. Digital Marketing changes quickly and he updated videos and the textbook to keep it relevant. I'd say this class is mandatory for marketing students. Plus he is hilarious.
He used a packet of readings, not a "textbook."  He's funny, but content is more important, and his content is great!  He's really innovative.  I wish he taught more classes.

DeRosia is hilarious and really cares about his students. He validates every comment made, and does everything to make the class entertaining and interesting. he lets YOU decide whether the test is in group and/or open-book!

Way funny, class is interesting, and you'll learn a ton.  However, his grading is heavily based on a group simulation.  Basically, if you get a crappy group who doesn't come through for you in the simulation you CANNOT get an A.  Then again, if you're a lazy mooch, land yourself in a good group and they'll earn the grade for you.

Hilarious teacher, and interesting subject matter! He's incredibly witty, and VERY good at making concepts and theories very clear. He's an excellent teacher, and very good at understanding different comments and questions in order to respond well. He gives GREAT feedback, and it's very specific, which makes it very helpful.

Great teacher.  Very interested and enthusiastic about the subject. He puts a lot of time into the PowerPoints & usually gives some "Free Advice" to the class which is really interesting and useful. To be honest, walking out of the class I don't feel as if I RETAINED much of the information he taught in lectures. He's still fun to listen to though.

One of the best teachers in the school.  He cares enough to grade students assignments himself and give specific feedback.  An excellent teacher and presenter, very entertaining.  Genuinely cares about his students--encourages one-on-one help for the class and for careers.
He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes everything crystal clear, and we only had group tests, so those were pretty easy. Highly Recommended!
A very useful class.  When I started it, I didn't think it would be useful to me (I'm in the MAcc program).  But now that it's almost finished, I see that the info will be very useful.
He is a great teacher. His tests really are not that hard. As long as you do the readings, you should be fine! In Busm 444 the tests are group ones, so it is not a tought class to do really well in.
DeRosia's a great guy.  I love his dry sense of humor.  If you like the comic book guy on the Simpsons, you'll like DeRosia.  I never read at all, and tests can be tricky, but I got an A-.

Great! Funny+interesting+greatTeacher. No busywork or quizzes: just tests and Harvard business cases. The cases are complex, and you learn a lot. The tests aren't too bad, and they are about *understanding*, not memorization. If you come to class, read the book *regularly*, and understand the concepts, you should score in the 90's and learn a lot.
Hell yes the tests are tough.  The lectures are cool and he keeps you interested, however, listen for his one liners because they will be on the tests.

Very ethusiastic about the subject.  He's hilarious, he keeps you rollin' the entire class period.  His tests are kind of tough, and almost the entire class is based on the tests.  Otherwise a great teacher!

Very funny guy. Chill lecture environment. Weekly projects with clear goals. Projects are difficult enough they force you to learn by easy enough that they are simple when you know what you're doing. Would take again.

If you like student-led lectures based on questions and you don't mind side tangents on developing learning skills, he's a great professor. If you're looking for structured lectures with prepared material, he's probably not the professor for you. He's caring and funny and all around a great guy, but his lecture style just didn't work for me.

Mercer said himself this is likely the hardest conceptual cs class. He is an amazing guy, available, and was very generous in lots of ways. Canvas showed that avg for hw was 60% usually, even with redos for sometimes full credit, but don't know overall grade avg. Very little material on this stuff outside of class (web), so class time is valuable.
