He is by far the best CS professor I have ever had. CS 224 was pretty challenging sometimes, but he did a great job at seeing what we needed and helping us to understand the material. He invites people to ask questions and he is also hilarious.

It's clear Dr. Mercer cares about his students, and his lectures are honestly very student led. He wants participation and students to ask questions. I thought the tests were weighted a bit heavily and felt a little bit convoluted, but the projects and labs were totally doable as long as you were willing to put the work in.

The class is unbelievably difficult thanks to vague lectures & project instructions plus incompetent TA support. If he didn't have easily accessible Zoom recordings of every lecture, I would've failed the course. The lack of late grade penalties was a godsend, as it's impossible to finish projects "on time," but it felt like a band-aid solution.

A real gem of the CS department. Mercer records all of his lectures and has a gift for explaining course concepts in both a logical and clear way. He also has a sense for where students struggle and works out examples live to explain new ideas. 329 has a lot of nuance and can feel overwhelming, but it will help you grow. Would take him again.

Remains my favorite CS professor to date. Such a kind and genuine guy. You can tell how much he cares about his students. Does a wonderful job of explaining complex concepts (and believe me - this class had plenty of them). Love him.

Dr. Mercer is one of the kindest people around and wants you to succeed so much in his class, so take advantage of that. CS329 was really hard for me and often very confusing (and the class did seem a bit disorganized at times), but when I got help from Dr. Mercer it cleared up so much.

This class was excellent. It was one of the first classes that I've taken that I felt like I was able to focus on learning over anything else. It wasn't too stressful, the assignments and tests were reasonable, and you could tell that Dr. Mercer was excited about what we were doing.

Dr. Mercer is a very kind and flexible person, though this particular class seemed a bit disorganized to me. Lectures consist mostly of him walking through practice problems. Late policy is very lenient. Time commitment is about what you'd expect of a CS class.

Mercer is fantastic and may be one of the best CS Professors I have had at BYU. Incredibly caring and was able to adapt to online classes well! Don't buy the textbook for this class as you can find it online incredibly easily. He expects you to read the chapters in the textbook but never gives any specific readings. Easy to get lost in this class.

Hands down my favorite class I've taken, and Mercer is AMAZING! He doesn't assign busywork. The few labs/homeworks are difficult (but doable). Most classes, he just works examples similar to the homework or labs, which is SUPER helpful. The class is really hard, but he will to adapt the schedule when the students need it. 10/10 the coolest prof.

CS224 is a hard class, but Prof Mercer has it organized very well. His lectures are student oriented so attending them live is more helpful than watching the recording. He understand that students are busy and adjusts the assignments and schedule according to the needs of the class. Seriously the coolest CS professor ever!

Dr. Mercer is the best CS professor I've ever had. He celebrates diversity, is kind and caring and a REAL person, and overall just wants his students to succeed. The course is hard but he sets it up in a really manageable way (no busy work!!) and is always available and happy to take questions, however trivial. 100% I would take him again. So good.

The best professor I have ever had. Period. We were super confused on a topic and the next lecture he said "You didn't understand last class so I am going to reteach it today" He wants you to pass some much! He knows its a hard class so he set up all the resources to pass. Always answered questions clearly and wouldn't move on until we understood

TAKE 224 from Mercer! SUPER caring, & WANT U to SUCCEED! His in-person lecture is phenomenal. He could tell that we were confused by reading our facial expression and explain hard concepts clearly. You won't regret it. He also made the class vibe great by telling students who already finished to help answer other students' questions on Slack.

Dr. Mercer is my favorite BYU CS professor so far. He is very skilled and very willing to help students outside of class. His lectures are mostly working through examples, and he makes a lot of sense when he teaches. CS224 is the easiest and 2nd most fun CS class that I have taken so far. (I have taken all the classes < 252 for the CS major.)

Mercer teaches difficult concepts with ease. He clearly knows the subjects but teaches as if he is learning with the class, which makes the class fun and lighthearted. Don't get me wrong, the class is very hard, but he makes it as manageable as possible. I'd take another class from him any day.
Most students didn't know what was going on so there were a ton of questions and he couldn't teach.

I think this class was hard not because Professor Mercer did poorly explaining its concepts, but because it's just a really hard class. Once you understand the concepts, you can figure out the homework relatively easily, but the learning curve is more like scaling a castle wall than it is hiking up a hill.

Dr. Mercer provided so much assistance to me this semester, from mercy with grades to understanding difficult concepts. He knows his class is difficult and tries his hardest to make it bearable for all students. I truly felt he cared for my personal success. Best CS prof I've had so far, cannot recommend enough.

Dr. Mercer is a true gem of the CS department. He is AMAZING at taking very complex concepts and either simplifying it for you or covering it so in depth that you'll never forget. He really seems to care about every student and he answers questions very respectfully. Wish I could take all my classes from him!

Ah my homie Eric. He is an amazing professor. There was SO much homework, so get ready to say goodbye to a social life, but that wasn't Dr. Mercer's fault, it was the course load. He's super understanding and has given me extra credit due to incidents outside my control multiple time. Again - take any class from Dr. Mercer!

This class was difficult and a lot of work. I learned how to solve problems with very little information. Dr. Mercer does a great job of being adaptive and encouraging through the process. I would take any class from him. He can handle this subject matter really well. You can do it, a study group was helpful, and reading the book was helpful.
Difficult, but I learned so much in this class! The book was invaluable in working on the labs. The labs can be frustrating when you hit roadblocks, but are really instructive.

Hardest class I've ever taken at BYU, and up there for hardest class in the entire CS major. Mercer really cares about student progress and challenging us. Make sure you aren't taking any other heavy classes. double hoursForLab  4; for(int labNum  0; labNum < 6; labNum++)  hoursForLab + labNum * 2.5

This has been the hardest class I have taken at BYU, but Mercer tried his best to help us all through it. He originally wanted us to do each lab with a partner (we weren't able to use the same partner twice), which he eventually made optional (because of complaints). This class sucks, but Mercer was good about helping the students

He cares about students and will stop and answer any student questions if something was unclear. I took this class class twice and I felt that he explains way better than other teachers. Take this 236 from him if you can! Projects build on each other so don't fall behind. Also projects get considerably harder after lab 2,  hardest labs are 3 and 4

He has tougher expectations than other 236 professors, but he also teaches better, is reasonable, and goes way beyond what is required to help students out. His classes are uplifting without feeling contrived, and he's also hilarious. If I could clone Dr. Mercer and take all my classes from him, I would do it in a heartbeat.

Great class. Dr. Mercer explains things on a level that all types of CS students can understand. He cares a lot about the students and is willing to do what is necessary in and out of class so that all students have success. Loved each of his lectures.

Really nice guy. The lectures were a bit dry (he's kind of dry but can be surprisingly funny sometimes), but very helpful. The textbook is really confusing and the lectures were much better. Pretty much lays out the tests on the study guide and has good projects. DON'T fall behind as each project builds on the last one.
Really difficult material and it seemed like lecture lacked the explanation required in the tests and homework assignments. Lecture could be much better.
CS345 was very hard, too hard for a 3 credit class.  However, this was a well taught class, and I learned a lot.  Dr. Mercer is very good.
Dr. Mercer is a fantastic teach with a passion for what he teaches. Definitely one of the best if not the best professors on the CS dept faculty!

Dr Mercer is great. CS345 turned out to be my most enjoyable class of the semester, not because it was easy, but because I really learned a lot and enjoyed the challenge of most of the projects. The homework helped cover topics that you didn't cover in projects, and it was very clear what was expected to know for tests. Highly recommended.

Dr. Mercer is awesome. I have really enjoyed CS345 from him. I have been fearing the class because I've heard it's so hard, but he makes the class very interesting and is very willing to help you as much as he can. Highly recommended.

Dr Mercer is an awesome teacher! He taught the class very well, and gave huge opportunities for students to get help. I once emailed him on a saturday evening about an issue I couldn't resolve, and got an extremely helpful response back within two hours. I would take any class from him, anytime. Do yourself a favor and take 345 from Dr Mercer
Mercer is a very chill teacher.  He's always willing to help answer questions in or out of class.  The subject material for 345 isn't the easiest, but he's very willing to help.
His greatest desire is to have a chili next to his name on this site.  You can now feel accomplished Dr. Mercer!  Great Teacher, works the schedule to help the class.

The best 400-level class I've taken.  The material is somewhat esoteric, but Dr. Mercer teaches it masterfully, and within the context of gaining applicable real-life skills.  Basically, it's the polar opposite of every other CS class I've ever taken.
Dr. Mercer has a good sense of humor, he doesn't take himself too seriously, and he shows an honest concern for his students. I felt that he actually did care about how we were doing.

I had a somewhat fun semester. He does spend a lot of time answering questions and I didnt mind that. I was glad he was flexible in moving the HW or test date once! He's a funny teacher once you get to know him.

Best CS professor I've had. He teaches really well, assigns a fair amount of work for 3 credits, and lets things slide (for the whole class) when we were just too busy or if he hadn't lectured on what the homework topic was yet. He wasn't easy, but he was good.
Perfect professor. He's so good you just know it's your own fault if you do poorly in the class. Doesn't force people to learn the material but is so available to explain anything.

I was in the class where students averaged 65 on the exam. The exam was difficult, but the rest of the class was fine.  I got an A because he taught very clearly and made sure every student understood. He is difficult, but great at teaching.

Spent too much time answering questions, many times resulting in an inability to cover all of the relevant material.  Tested on topics that were not exactly covered in class, expecting students to "synthesize" from considerably more basic subjec

Awesome teacher! Sure the class was hard, but it is supposed to be. The material covered has made the next CS classes easier. He went out of his way to make the assignments doable, and even provided skeleton code.
If those other people thought Dr. Mercer was too hard, they should not be CS majors.  He was more involved with our class than any other professor I've ever had in the department.
WAY TOO HARD!!!!!! On one test his section averaged a 65 and the other section (that he didn't teach)averaged an 80. The worst part, he was happy with the class average.
Dr. Mercer is a good teacher always willing to help and not too far removed from being a student that he doesn't understand where you're coming from.
Dr. Ringger will get to know you personally. He is engaging and teaches very well. I highly recommend him!

One of the best professor I have ever had.  This class has very difficult material but Professor Ringger explains things very well.  The text book is online and free which is great.  Class is not required but there is homework due almost every day so class is virtually required.  I would recommend Professor Ringger nomater what class he is teaching

This class was very similar to Dr. Ringgers 479 NLP class. I was tough but Dr. Ringger is very helpful and genuinely cares for you as a student. He is very knowledgable on the subject. It was a very interesting subject and I recommend this class.

Dr. Ringger is a fantastic professor! He took the time to explain things clearly. If students had homework questions he would take all the time necessary to answer them. The homework wasn't easy, but it's a hard class so I didn't expect it to be.

This was a very enjoyable class. You'll understand the material in due time with hard work. Sometimes, it comes right off the bat. Other times, it may take a few days (and a visit to Dr. Ringger or the TAs) to get it. Take CS312 from Dr. Ringger. You won't regret it.
Great professor. His Google Group helped the students a lot when it was hard to visit the TA's. The projects were a lot of fun. His tests can be hard though.

Good teacher.  I would definately recommend taking the class from him.  He graduated with a math major, but makes everything really easy to understand.  He doesn't dwell on a lot of the mathematical jargon of the class and focuses on the big idea concepts. DO THE PROJECTS EARLY!  you'll get an A if you do.

Chem 111 is a dense and difficult class for anyone. I attended lectures from all of the professors, and Sevy definitely teaches the best. He goes deeper for comprehension's sake and is always priming you on how concepts might show up on the test. More than the professor, though, the TA's are how to get an A in this class.

Dr. Sevy literally blew something up every single class period. It was awesome. The homework and exams were both pretty hard, but he gave really good review sessions before each exam. The course itself was also just a hard course. He explained things really well so that the concepts made sense.

This class was very difficult, and sometimes Sevy went too in depth during lectures. However, the concepts were explained well and he was always willing to answer questions! He is very passionate about physical chemistry and he knows his stuff! He also allowed for test corrections on exams. Make sure to start the homework early!!!

Dr. Sevy is a great professor. Chem 111 is a very difficult class, but he does a good job helping students understand the material. You can tell he truly loves chemistry. You will definitely have to put in a lot of effort if you want a good grade in the class, but there's a lot of material available to help you study.

Chem 111 is a genuine college class. In order to really absorb the lectures, you have to do the reading before class to get a basic idea of the topic. The tests are hard, but the written homework is pretty good prep for it. Dr. Sevy is an amazing professor though, and he loves doing demos and blowing up stuff during class. So yeah, hard but doable.

Dr. Sevy is the best CHEM 111 teacher. He is funny and a good teacher, his lectures are very informative and pretty much cover everything you would need to know. The HW is generally harder than the tests, but the tests aren't very easy :) Sevy blows stuff up all the time, so that is fun too.

I did not take CHEM from Dr. Sevy, but I took UNIV 101 from him and he is amazing! He is so chill, fun and kind! He cares a lot, and you can tell how knowledgeable he is. He also is very passionate about the gospel and includes that in his lessons. I would definitely recommend taking this class from him.
One of the best professors I have ever had. It is by nature a difficult class, but he keeps it well organized, manageable, and interesting.

Dr. Sevy is a passionate professor who loves his subject, but CHEM111 is a challenging course. Attend lectures, read the textbook, and use resources like Unstuck AI to succeed. The class is hard work, but worth it if you put in the effort.

Chem 111 is just a hard class, Dr. Sevy did his best to teach us the material but it takes a lot more than just attending the lectures to understand the material. I would recommend reading the textbook! You think you can skip but you can't.

I loved taking Dr Sevy's class, but it was definitely a hard class. He teaches really well and tries really hard to make sure you understand the concepts he teaches, as long as you put in the work he's happy to work with you and help you learn, definitely don't take it for an easy A though.

Professor Sevy is a fantastic professor! Yes, the class is hard, but not impossible. He did a brilliant job explaining difficult concepts. It helps to do the reading beforehand and get a jump on the homework. Also, we had 83 explosions by the end of the year. He loves doing demos and is clearly very passionate about his job. Totally awesome class.

Dr. Sevy is a great guy. He curves his classes and is decently accessible outside of class. He uses a lot of PowerPoint and goes way too fast in lectures. I would recommend reading the text BEFORE class and also looking at the homework problems at the beginning of the week to make sure you get an explanation of how they are done.

Dr. Sevy is an amazing professor. He knows what he is talking about and has incredibly well organized lectures. If you go to the lectures and use the TA office hours/test reviews you will be able to do well in the class. This being said, it is still difficult as it is a Chem class and he doesn't pull punches when grading exams.

A pretty good professor, but some of the more difficult concepts required more explanation than was given. Labs often weren't very helpful in understanding what was going on in class. Clearly passionate about what he teaches, but moves at a breakneck pace. He does regularly break up long lectures with demonstrations, usually involving fire.

Every time I went to his lectures, whether I had studied/read beforehand or not, I had literally NO IDEA what he was even talking about for 50 mins. He goes off on tangents a ton just to appease the genius students in the class, while leaving all other students in the dust. His tests were impossibly hard & timed. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Dr. Sevy is a chill dude but Chem 105 is a disaster. There are a rare few that drop tests and assignments, but let's be real, only dropping tests is what matters. The tests are standardized for all of 105 so it doesn't matter who you take. However, some teachers drop tests so get one of them. I averaged straight A's... but not with Dr. Sevy.

Honestly, Dr. Sevy is great but its the BYU chem 105 course that is flawed. His demos are interesting and is always at his office hours, but the Chem 105 tests are tricky. I am currently in Chem 106 and spend a fraction of the amount of time studying and doing homework and I have an A. Dr. Sevy's iclicker quizzes are annoying but don't affect much.

Chem 105 is just a difficult class, but he gives a good amount of assignments to try and prepare you for the exams. He is very clear in his lectures and allows a few assignments to be dropped. Although the exams are difficult, those are the same under every professor. However, this professor gave really great assignments to help prepare.

Dr. Sevy is a really awesome teacher! Chem 105 is well known for being very difficult, but Dr. Sevy's lectures were very entertaining and interesting. He assigns several homework assignments each week which seems overwhelming at first, but he believes that doing practice problems is the best way to prepare for the test, which is absolutely true.

HANDS DOWN THE WORST teacher Ive ever had. I got an F in this class and decided to take chemistry at my local community college after where I got an A+ I recommend you do the same. Hes also really arrogant, but thats not what Im basing my rating off of. Please consider that theres a reason why Chem105 is the number one failed class at BYU.

He was a good professor, the class was SUPER hard. Lots of homework, and there's a TON of information in one lecture. If I had to take it again, I would definitely pay better attention in lecture, and find outside resources to get practice problems.

Eric Sevy was a wonderful Professor. Not gonna lie his class had a workload to it, but I loved every minute of it. As long as you read, attend lecture, and do the Smartwork early enough to get feedback then you will be fine. He was very open to talk to and also loved explosions which was my favorite part ;).

Chem 105 is a hard class no matter who you take it from, but Prof. Sevy is a pretty good choice. There's a lot of homework, but lectures are super helpful and we exploded something almost every class. He does a review before every test and gives a really generous curve at the end too.

Toughest class I've taken at BYU, get ready to work hard. Dr. Sevy obviously loves chemistry and knows a ton so that helped a lot. Make sure to use your TA and the TA lab, get a good study group, review his lecture slides often, redo the problem sets before each test and you should be fine. DO NOT GET BEHIND. I would reccomend Dr. Sevy to anyone!

Prof Sevy was my one of my favorite professors! CHEM105 is a hard class, but Sevy does a good job explaining concepts. The tests are challenging but he does reviews before every exam. He exploded something almost every lecture. His class was hybrid when I took it because of COVID and he did a decent job balancing both virtual and in person class.

I've heard that Dr. Sevy and Woodfield are the hardest chem 105 teachers BYU offers. I'd suggest taking one of the other teachers. Good person, but he's a tough teacher. Way, way more homework than other teachers, excluding Woodfield. Tests are insane for all chem classes. Not super available. Super awesome TA's though.

I'm told they removed half the content in this class before I took it. They could remove half again and it would still be challenging! Hard to keep up, the lectures are so fast, covering multiple concepts in one lecture. Read the textbook, especially if you haven't done Chem yet. Use TAs and tutors. Dr. Sevy is wonderful, faithful, and fun. Pyro.

He is a great professor if you need/want to take chemistry. Dr. Sevy starts off each of his classes with a prayer and often relates chemistry to the Gospel. He is good at explaining concepts and gave a generous curve after the final. Though I realized that STEM wasn't for me, I still appreciated Dr. Sevy and his teaching style.

Dr. Sevy is one of the most intelligent people I know. Sometimes it can be to a flaw but, I never questioned his passion and drive to help me learn the material. He can be a little brash at times he really does care. The thing that is awful about this class is the book, worst book I have ever had. I promise the tests are much better than Atkins.

Dr. Sevy is a great chemistry professor! There is usually one thing that gets blown up every lecture period and there is a ton of HW (written and online throughout the week). There are four tests in the course, but if you do the work, the material you learn is very interesting and exciting! DO NOT get behind. If you do, catch up quickly! Good luck!

Dr. Sevy is a solid choice for Chem 105. Its a super hard class, but his no-frills teaching style was just what i needed to be able to understand the course. Read the book and pray for a good TA to help you through the concepts. The reviews before tests were a LIFESAVER!

Sevy really is a solid choice for Chem105 but he does go fast, doesn't always simplify concepts, and the tests are tricky. This class is a challenge but I don't think it was because of him, just the class itself. Be sure to READ the textbook and do NOT get behind. The class goes so fast it's hard to catch up.

Dr. Sevy was very passionate about chemistry but wasn't the best at explaining complex topics. I felt his lectures spent less time on the foundational concepts and what was covered on the tests and more time on small details. Attending recitation will be very helpful because there you will focus on these more important concepts which help on tests.

If you struggle with chemistry this class will kill you. I met with a tutor every week and got help from the TAs in the tutorial lab weekly too and still couldn't pull off an A. Lectures go quickly. There are daily in class iClicker quizzes. Fascinating stuff but he's not particularly great at explaining.

Yes, this course is difficult and Dr. Sevy expects more of his students than most professors. Yes, his exams are difficult and expect you to apply what you've learned, but in my experience there was never anything on them that we hadn't been taught. Great course to prepare for the rigor of graduate/professional programs  hard, but preparatory.

Doctor Sevy is one of the best professors I've ever had. Sure, Chem 105 is a hard class, that's not gonna change, but he gives you all the resources you need to succeed. Everything is very organized and laid out to help you. Very clear what he expects from you, and he obviously cares about the students.

Test are unfair! Doesn't tell you what's on them. everything in his class is a guessing game. You just have to go for the clicker points but be ready to teach yourself everything. take from the other professor haven he even has same test but they always had better class average. Also don't believe other reviews he gives no curve at the end so dumb

Dont take it from HIM take from another professor he did not help at all limited office hours. Doesn't explain things well in class everyone is always lost really not tough of a subject he makes it harder and his test are written to confuse you! Be careful multiple times in class he would say u don't need know for test and it would be on there!

Everyone says that chem 105 is the hardest class you'll ever take and I DEFINITELY disagree. Sevy makes all of the homework completely doable if you stay on top of it. All of the homework is mostly participation based-except for SmartWork- which is totally doable as well. Sevy is super fun and was dedicated to helping us pass the tests. Great prof!

I think the reason why Professor Sevy isn't rated higher is because chemistry is just hard. You have to do all the work and extra practice and have a good TA to do well. However, Professor Sevy gives great powerpoint lectures: he is great at explaining hard concepts and almost always makes something explode. Low key a pyromaniac but I loved it.

Very tough course. I encourage utilizing study groups, doing the extra credit assignments, and meeting with Sevy during his office hours to review difficult topics or exam results. He is more than willing to help. I also strongly suggest getting the online textbook. I wish I would have. The smartworks give direct links to online textbook pages.

Chem 105 is hard no matter who you take it from but I thought Sevy was a great choice. He wants everyone to succeed. My only complaint is that sometimes he would get behind in lecture so the worksheets wouldn't match up w what we learned that day. Work hard, don't get behind, pray for a good TA and you will do just fine in this class!
Sevy moves too fast and often emphasizes topics in lecture that have little or no relevance to the rest of the course. I learned way more from my TA's then I ever did from a lecture

Dont take chem from him. Lectures are pointless you will learn everything on your own- take from a different professor who slows down and will help you learn. Test are meant to make you fail not test your knowledge.

I really liked Sevy's class. Definitely had to work for the grade. Started every lecture with an inspirational/spiritual thought. Helpful and kind during office hours. I felt like he really cares about his students but there's only so much he can do to help grades per chem department policy. He hires good TAs. Blew something up almost every class.

I really liked Sevy. We had Hansen sub a couple days and it was awful. Sevy makes it easy to pay attention in class and is pretty good at teaching difficult concepts, and all the demonstrations are entertaining. Make sure you stay on top of things or it's easy to get behind. Tests are difficult, but if you reach out for help and study its fine.

Professor Sevy is very smart and he knows what he is talking about. I wouldn't bother purchasing the textbook. I only used it for the first test. Review the slides and stay on top of the 3 assignments a day and you'll be fine. I got a tutor for extra help as well

DIFFICULT class, okay guy. Speeds through lectures and in-class participation quizzes. You hardly have time to think before you have to answer. Homework load is heavy. Tests are very difficult/purposely tricky. I have a hard time differentiating between my feelings for Pro Sevy/my feelings for the class. Overall TOUGH experience, but possible...

Just not a good professor doesn't explain concepts well more concerned with getting class over with than actually helping his students learn. Has lots of students but still not an excuses to not care about your students individually. Take it from anyone else.

A lot of the class time is wasted with little stories, the class is just very difficult and that time wasted is not appreciated. Good professor the material semi makes sense however the tests are nothing like the homework or the in class problems. Way trickier then it needs to be.
Dont take from him test way hard no curve he doesnt really care class is set up to make you fail. Just a way to get rid of students and discourage them. Sad to see they treat students this way.

Test are impossible you can understand all the material and know everything and still get bad grade on his test his class test average is around a 60% and didnt curve do anything you can to take from someone else his lectures also are waste u learn more on ur own he just reads PowerPoints super fast. Also an A is 94 for a hard class so dumb!

You can tell he knows a lot about Chemistry. He doesn't dumb down the terms, however, and lectures are lightning fast; taking notes is near impossible. Class is only fun/interesting with his demonstrations, and his tests are literally impossible. Take ANYONE else.

I really like Professor Sevy and thought that his lectures were very clear and made difficult topics understandable. He helped me enjoy chemistry a lot more than I thought I would. While the tests are hard, especially the final, the tests are the same for all Chem 105 classes as it is done by the department, so it's hard no matter the professor.

Doctor Sevy is great. The two times he had two professors come in and teach the subject, because he was gone, I felt taught it better than he did. He tries to go over concepts slow to make sure you get it.

I took Chem 105 from Dr. Sevy, and it was my hardest class. I typically did about 5.5-6 hours of homework per week. He is really good at explaining hard concepts and really tries to help students understand. I didn't really use the textbook because he explains things so well. If you put in the work, you can do well.

Chem 105 is a brutal class, but Dr. Sevy is solid option to take it from. He is clear in lectures and explains concepts well. Don't depend on just his lectures though to get you through the class, outside practice is definitely needed!

Dr. Sevy is a great person and you can tell that he really loves what he teaches, however, his lectures can be hard to follow and he often doesn't cover all the material that you are tested on. As with all Chemistry classes there is a lot of homework and doing the reading is very helpful. During his office hours and after class he is very helpful.

This class was really difficult, but it's a 400-level chem class, so that was expected. Dr Sevy is an amazing professor and he teaches very clearly. You can tell that he's passionate about the subject and he made me more interested in it too. He's available outside of class and hired great TAs, so it was all okay. Highly recommend him!

This is a hard class no matter who you take it from! Might be the most failed class at BYU. To get an average grade (B) you will need to work 16-20 hours, that is no exaggeration. 3 online assignments, 3 worksheets, 1 lab, 3 iclicker questions each week. The online, worksheets take at least 1-3 hours to complete. Get ready to work!! I learned a lot

Dr. Sevy is a great teacher. He has a great sense of humor that gives a lot of flavor to an otherwise dry subject. The class has more work than any other class you've taken, but if you will be fine if you put the work in, do the readings, and go to lecture.(It's possible: I dropped out of AP Chem in HS halfway through bc I understood nothing!)

I think all the CHEM105 teachers use the same powerpoints, so no matter who you take, you'll get the same material. I found Dr. Sevy's explanations very clear and easy to follow, although sometimes when working a sample problem, he would rush through the work in the middle. He chooses good TAs, so you should be good in this class.

Dr. Sevy gave great lectures, but we didnt always get through all material each lecture to complete the homework that was due the next recitation meeting. Attendance wasnt required for his class, but there are iClicker quizzes that you will miss each lecture and most of the points you get in recitation are just for being there so dont skip!

This class requires a ton of outside work. I spent 95% of my time studying for chemistry. The tests are short but really hard. Only 20 questions on the tests but miss a couple and you're done for. Lectures are hard to keep up with.

Professor Sevy makes the lectures entertaining, we blew something up practically everyday. However, his lectures were fast paced and hard to keep up with. There is a ton of homework, I spent more time doing chemistry homework than any other class. A good TA is essential to pass. Tests are hard to study for because there is so much information.

Much of his homework and tests doesn't reflect anything taught in class. The TAs told me the homework problems required knowledge from more advanced Chemistry classes. The time it takes to study and do the homework for this class makes it impossible to both have a job and do homework for the rest of your classes. Made me rethink my major and career
Two thumbs up! Sevy is a great professor and very personable in class. His final exam was brutal but it all worked out in the end.

This was one of the most rewarding as well as one of the most difficult classes that I have taken. I definitely had to work hard but Sevy understands how difficult the course is and you will feel like he treated you fairly by the end. I highly recommend the course!
Dr. Sevy is a fantastic professor. His class was challenging but I left the class with a solid understanding of the material. He really wants you to master the subject.
Although the class was extremely hard, he gave a very generous curve at the end which I don't think a lot of people realize. He tries to give as many A's as possible. You can tell he cares.

The final exam was incredibly difficult and only the smallest fraction was covered in class. Dr Sevy does not test how hard you work or how dedicated you are. His exams test how well you can solve things that have nothing to do with his class. My least favorite professor at BYU.
This class was ridiculously hard because Sevy focuses more on being a good test writer than a good teacher.

I came to BYU wanting to be a chemist but I now know that I want to be anything but a chemist if it means that I'd have to interact with people like Sevy. Also, his exams are designed to specific test things he did not teach well in class. There were some questions where literally everyone got them wrong.
This class made me hate chemistry. This class is so hard I considered dropping multiple times. I ended up staying but failed the final. I thinks that the best way to learn is by failing the exams.

His exams are so ridiculous! They are timed and very difficult to finish. If you are the kind of person who needs to double check your answers. Avoid this class! A good percentage of our class ended up dropping.

If you can take 468 from Dr. Sevy, do it!!! You're going to learn a lot of the "partial truths" you've been told in classes leading up to this and get to learn what is actually going on. This also means the class is really difficult. The tests are hard, but they are close to the homework. Buy the solutions manual and you'll be okay!
I really enjoyed Dr. Sevy's class. His tests are hard, but they mirror the lecture and homework very well. If you do the work you should be fine.

Don't be deceived by his decent average score! Scroll down to the bottom and you will see that all of the good ratings come from when he used to teach religion. Recently he decided he wanted to be a chemist and his classes are so frustrating! Every one of his chemistry classes are difficult to the point of being cruel.
Pre-meds BEWARE! Dr. Sevy is unreasonably difficult. I lost my 4.0 in this class and put in 30 hours a week.

I went into this class really wanting to like Dr. Sevy but the learning environment is just so terrible that I honestly felt like he wasn't even trying. I understand the physical chemistry is hard but I wish he would put some effort into what he teaches.

Dr. Sevy really knows his chemistry or at least I assume he does. To be honest, I understood very little of what he taught. It feel like he teaches for himself and doesn't care if the students understand. He judges his skill as a professor on how difficult his exams are. He gives very few A's, because he doesn't teach anything useful for the exams.

Really tough class, but that's just CHEM105. All courses are going to be tough. Sevy is reasonable, but strict. Not much leniency in grading, but he does drop some low grades at the end of the semester and lets you replace your lowest midterm grade with your final grade if you do better. Clear policies so you know whats going on most of the time.
He is not approachable during office hours and does not give enough resources/ practice problems to do well in the class.

His teaching style feels like he is constantly trying to prove to everyone that he is smarter than you. I noticed this most on the exams which are extremely difficult and have nothing to do with what he taught in class. I would not recommend him!

He was a good professor overall, but the tests were really difficult and ultimately determine your final grade. He offers second chance grading with the final, but it was difficult, and brought my grade down 5%. He also talked about curving the whole semester and then never did curve.

Dr. Sevy was a great choice to take Chem 105 from for me. His lectures are very clear and definitely helped me understand the book material. I would suggest reading the assignments before class. Just make sure not to get behind on homework and you'll be fine.

Dr Eric T Sevy might as well have invented Chemistry. He is the smartest chem professor and he is super funny. He makes people better by pushing them to their limits. I went into his office a few times and he was very helpful and made sure that I'm excelling in life. If you like learning and a dry sense of humor, take Eric Sevy's class.

Professor Sevy is a great chemistry professor. I had never taken chemistry before (even in high school ) but he explained it in a way that i was able to quickly catch on. Great choice of a professor for chemistry beginners. All of the assignments and tests are the same for all Chem 105 classes, so the only difference between classes is the teacher.
10/10 would recommend. Lectures were always interesting. Be prepared to spend 1+ hours outside of class each day on homework.

Not a very good person.  He doesn't take questions in class very well and often ignores them because "we're behind schedule". He is not nice during office hours so go to the TA unless you absolutely have to talk to him.

I though his lectures were amazing! I learned a ton about the Book of Mormon, even though it wasn't what I was expecting, as it wasn't that spiritual. Tests were definitely hard, make sure you take good notes in your Book of Mormon. The papers weren't hard to write, but he grades them based on if he likes the style, so make sure you talk to him.

Professor Sevy's class was kinda stressful because there wasn't a clear grading criteria or any reviews to help with tests & since that makes up the bulk of your grade that wasn't awesome, but we had a lot of good, deep conversations during lecture. He answered student's questions and always had interesting lectures. All his tests are openscripture

Test are all free response and very subjective! He is a nice guy but there are book of mormon classes you can take that will be MUCH easier.  He isn't clear on what is on the tests and doesnt have reviews.  Because tests affect your grade so much, this upset me

Easy class, take notes in your scriptures and you have an A. You do have to attend class though, there are easy clicker quizzes every class and he drops like the 5 lowest scores. Its an interesting class and would recommend it to anyone.

I loved Brother Sevy! He addresses every student's questions and concerns about the material or gospel in an interesting and insightful way, and provides a really refreshing take on the scriptures. If he ever teaches another religion class, I would definitely take him again.

Dr. Sevy tries very hard to help you understand  material. His lectures are also engaging and easy to follow. If you see him in the halls he'll ask for your feedback on the class and how he can make it better. Stellar guy and stellar class.

Professor Sevy is great and his class is too. I was surprised at how much work friends in other Book of Mormon classes had; the only assignments in this class are three short application papers. Tests are open-scripture but all questions are short answer and can be difficult. IF YOU TAKE THIS CLASS TAKE THOROUGH NOTES IN YOUR SCRIPTURES

Dr/Bro Sevy has been my favorite religion professor at BYU so far. He cares for his students, is inspirational, and very willing to meet outside of class to continue talking with you about topics you're particularly interested in that came up in class. I just love him!
I never wanted to miss his classes! He always had wonderful insights and comments to offer. He was extremely helpful, and very obviously cared for his students. He was a wonderful professor.

Dr. Sevy is definitely the best of the three Chem 111 teachers. We blew stuff up on a daily basis! He explained things in a clear manner, but it's still Chem 111. Probably one of the hardest freshmen classes offered. Be prepared to devote your life to this class! But it is well worth it. I looked forward to going to class every day!

Chemistry is, by nature, a hard class. But Dr. Sevy made it one of my favorite classes to go to.  There are iClicker quizzes pretty much every day, so be sure to attend, but overall, he makes sure to explain everything multiple times so everyone understands.  Also, I quit trying to keep track of how balloons he blew up after one month. Awesome.
Chem 111 is a really hard class, but if you have to take it, take it from Sevy. He likes to derive all the equations which helps everything make way more sense. Plus he really loves explosions.

Dr. Sevy is awesome. He really cares about his students. He is very easy to talk to. You can ask him anyything. If you like explosions, you will enjoy his class. Best Chem 111 professor. The class is hard but it is a chemistry class so it is supposed to be hard. Just go to TAs for help with homework and exam reviews.
Hard class. Good teacher. If you are in anyway not a compleate genius, expect to spend a lot of hours on this class, but it gets easier after 1st exam

He really knows his stuff, but since he doesn't want to tell you exactly how to do something if you go to him with help, only trying to lead you to know how to do it, he can be difficult. I thought class was interesting, but thermodynamics and work killed me. iClicker quizzes are most every day, and you can rework exams for 1/3 the points back.

Dr. Sevy is a great professor.  Unfortunately, this class will make you seriously evaluate your desire to be a Chemistry major.  He is fair and wants to help you, but he also doesn't curve anything.  There is a lot of homework and lots of TA time you will have to do.  Only 8 students out of 92 got a full A, so take that as you will.
Hard class, but good teacher who liked to blow up things. Explains things well, lots of work and TAs saved my grade. I recommend him
Holy cow this class was hard!!! Don't take any other hard classes at the same time as this one.

Great teacher. Cared about the students and was willing to meet with us during his office hours. TA help sessions were a life saver. For having such a hard class, he did great. He was nice and approachable. Plus, he loved to randomly explode things (hilarious) and had an interesting way of explaining things in real world terms.
Excellent teacher

He's a great teacher and he teaches the history along with the chemistry which is interesting.  He will help you, but is sometimes impatient.  If you go to his office, he lets you know that he's busy and doesn't have time, but he'll help.  You can redo the missed portions of all tests (except the final) for 1/3 of the credit (i.e. 70% goes to 80%).

Dr. Sevy's class is very doable if you stay on top of the homework, take notes in lecture and go over them, and go to his office hours and the TA sessions. That being said, it is still very difficult. His tests are designed to be "learning experiences" and take about 4 hours, so make sure you study.

Dr Sevy is an excellent teacher. He presents the essential information in a concise way (for better or for worse) while still addressing applicable side notes. His daily quizes sometimes seemed easier if you hadn't read (because then you wouldn't second guess yourself). His tests were difficult and it takes an incredible amount of work to get an A.

He is a good guy, but not a good teacher. He Never had time to talk to me out of class. You can learn from him, but it takes investment. Do all homework, (early) attend lectures (be on time for quizzes) and study like crazy for the tests. For non chem whizzes, this class should be 4-5 credits, not 3. Class is either interesting or deadly boring.

This was the first class in I didn't get an A in since the beginning of my scholastic debut.  The class sucked me dry, and put a lot of new swears into my vocabulary, but Prof. Sevy's a decent enough bloke.  And if you like learning, a lot of people did that in this class, I heard.  I got an A-, after much ado.

This class is not easy.  Be prepared to devote many many hours a week doing difficult homework and reviewing the material.  Best test prep for me was doing all of the odd problems in the chapters.  It took a long time, but it helped a lot.  The lectures are awesome though.  He loves to pop balloons.

This class was pretty difficult, but Dr. Sevy did his best to teach the material.  Lecture was an absolute must, otherwise the homework was VERY difficult (and often was difficult regardless).  Make good use of the TA sessions, and study hard for the tests.  Tests are pretty fair, they usually include a short essay and homework problems.

Dr. Sevy is the best prof I have had at BYU!  He was really interested in students who were willing to learn.  I am not gonna lie, his tests were VERY difficult, but it was definately doable.  Great class.

This was genuinely the worst math class I have ever taken. I stopped going to lectures after about a month because Dr Swenson would come in, do a bunch of practice problems, do a ton of steps in his head, and then realize that the problem he created is unsolvable without a calculator. This is the lowest grade I have in a math or physics class.

The actual course content wasn't too bad, but the students literally had to make a big group chat to decode what was taught. His lectures were not interactive at all and he would not really answer questions, just refer to his scribbles as if the answer was obvious. Overall, an okay class but the lectures were rough.

Stopped going to class 2 weeks in. ChatGPT is a better math teacher than him. He did give a really nice curve but besides that lectures were pointless and office hours confirmed that I was on my own for this class. He's a nice guy though just shouldn't be teaching complex math anymore.

Not a great professor. Lectures were uninteresting and unhelpful. He didn't like to answer questions and when he did, I just found myself more confused than before. He's definitely a caring guy but he made this class an unenjoyable experience. I only got an A because I read the textbook on my own time and am a good test taker.

Dr. Eric is fine. I didn't like his lecture style as it lacked interactivity. He is extremely caring, though. Calc 3 is hard, so with any professor that difficulty would be the same. If you were to take this class from Dr. Swenson, I recommend reading the material beforehand. There were 4 midterms and the practice tests he gives are very similar.

I have very much enjoyed Prof. Swenson's class, but I can also understand some people's complaints. A typical lecture has him introducing one or two new topics and working through a few practice problems. There is a lot of homework (which is typical), and he does give out practice exams and answer keys, which are very helpful for the real thing.

His lectures are pretty repetitive without a lot of interactivity, but he's a funny and caring guy. If you don't understand concepts, you'll likely have to teach them to yourself. There's a ton of homework that's worth little of your grade. He does give practice tests for the 3 midterms which are very representative of the actual exams.

I enjoyed taking Math 314 from Swenson. His lectures can sometimes be confusing. Swenson doesn't respond well when questions are asked and always responds like the answer should be obvious. His practice tests he provides for the class are very helpful to use before taking the actual test. The final is work 33% of your grade.

The content is fine, but pretty repetitive. He is a very abrasive when asked a question and often refers to what is written on the board as if it should be obvious. He often makes comments that show that he doesn't care about teaching the class and also claims that he is too lazy to do a part of the problem. He likes lectures, not really teaching.

Cengage textbook is needed.
If you want to learn about assassins, the chainsaw massacre theorem, and the Pac-man method, take his class. He makes learning engaging while still teaching the concepts very well. When we do exam reviews with the rest of the 213 students, everyone who has Swenson can do the problems faster and using better methods.

It was a difficult class, but that's to be expected. The real deal-breaker for me was that he didn't seem to want to be teaching the class.  He could rarely explain the applications of any concepts he taught or the reason we were learning them, or the intuition for why theorems worked. He might be a good teacher if he cared about the subject matter

I really regret taking this class from this professor. Lectures are composed of him getting up and writing the definition of what we are learning from the textbook, doing some examples (Where he skips steps), and getting angry or confused at questions asked about what he is doing. The only way to learn is from other people taking the class.

5 quizzes were 45% of the grade, and the final was 33%. The quizzes usually only had like 7 or 8 questions, and were mostly multiple choice, so if you miss one, you get a B. Homework assignments were brutal at times, and he seemed to get frustrated when students asked questions and didn't immediately understand his answer. Barely (barely) got an A.

A fairly standard math class but with some twists. The grading for the class was interesting and very heavy on the final. The final was worth 1/3 or 2/3s of your grade whichever is a higher score. The rest is made up of online (worth 1/4), written (worth 1/2), and 5 quizzes (worth 1/4). His lectures were effective and his math jokes are pretty good

I went to his class for the first couple weeks, but I found it confusing. I did the rest of the class on my own. There was a lot of homework (online and from the textbook). Tests were a little tricky, but if you learn the proofs and theorems well it will help. Lots of work for a 2 credit class.

Dr. Swenson rarely explains anything he's doing and never gives any review materials for his 6 quizzes throughout the semester. These 6 quizzes are weighted approximately the same as a midterm, so you effectively get 6 midterms during the semester, along with a final. He also put one of his quizzes over thanksgiving break. Would not recommend.

Lectures were mostly him going through examples without explaining the principles. Very confusing. When students asked questions he would usually just repeat whatever he had just said, except more insistently. Within 3 weeks I gave up on going to class at all and instead just taught myself out of the textbook. Exams are reasonable but had mistakes.

Knows the material very well. His class was one of the most structured classes I've ever taken. Perfectly aligning with the book, so its easy to use the book for further explanation. He is a bit intimidating at first, but he is actually a funny guy who really wants to see his students succeed and will help any way he can to see this through.
Very good. He expained the subject very clearly and gave good examples during class that prepared us for the homework. Great professor.

Professor Swenson knows his stuff, but often doesn't see when students are not understanding. So you really have to be clear when you don't understand, and ask lots of questions! The work load is not that much, but the challenge is in the concepts. He took some warming up to, but he is a pretty hilarious lecturer too!

Pretty clear in explaining things in lecture, but his teaching is fairly different from the book so it can be confusing if you miss class. Humorous and nerdy. Doesn't give much feedback on the tests and they are usually harder than what you'd expect from the reviews.
This was honestly the worst taught class I have ever had in my entire life. He was very unhelpful and actually made the material more difficult then it really is. Avoid this teacher at all costs.
Professor Swenson was a good teacher! The course was very difficult, but he made it a lot easier than it could have been.

The beginning of the class is kind of a shock if you haven't dome much proof-based math before, but it gets easier as it continues.  His sense of humor is ubiquitous and refreshing, if a bit odd.  He cares about the students more than he lets on, I think.  He wrote the textbook and it's almost exactly the same as the lectures, which is helpful.
This class really isn't that bad. He isn't that great at explaining things, but I thoughts his tests were easy. Just memorize the proofs that are on his practice exams.

He was good at answering questions at the start of class, but outside of that, he wasn't a big fan of questions and found ways around them. He commonly stopped before completing a hard problem. My notes weren't very helpful. Not a bad class if you go to the math lab after for help.

His textbook is stll a rough draft and yes there are lots of mistakes. But it is generally apparent what things should be. He is very willing to answer homework questions before class and in his limited office hours. But he doesn't listen well.

Dr. Swenson is an excellant teacher. Of course, he is harder than the "other guys." But if you actually want to learn how to do analysis, take Dr. Swenson. He knows his stuff, and expects you to know it too! His lectures are interesting and he answers questions in an easy to understand fashion. His book is awesome too!

Very tough.  Goes really fast in class, so only answers questions in the beginning of class.  But he will glady answer questions in his office hours or other times.  For 315, if you don't really want a really hard time, take it from someone else.  It's hard, but you'll learn more and better.

His class is definitely not easy, but Swenson is a good guy, and he's quite funny. Although a good portion of the class is completely lost half the time, Prof. Swenson will help the class with homework, both during class and office hours.
good guy but his explanations are not as good as they can be for a college proffessor.

Unless math comes easily for you take 315 from anyone else.  He has no time for any of your questions.  If he does happen to answer a question he seems to just repeat what he said before and move on.  The subject was interesting, but no thanks to him.  He's a pleasant man and brilliant mathematician, but a poor teacher.

He knew what he was talking about. Even though it was difficult, it made me work, which is good when you're taking advanced math courses. You need that push and actually want to succeed. You can't be lazy and expect good grades

I loved Swenson for 315.  I took his class a semester after the person above, so his "rough draft" is actually very complete and error-free now.  His textbook is very clear and concise, and builds on itself beautifully with very few mistakes.  I agree that the class is difficult, but I found his tests/hw to be straightforward.

He's a nice guy, but the class is extremely difficult and confusing.  The textbook is a rough draft by the professor, which is extremely confusing and impossible to follow; lecture is straight from the textbook.  To do well on tests you basically have to memorize the textbook.

Contrary to syllabus, he isn't willing to set up an appt. w/ you, except for office hours. He will give you excuses for being too busy. TA's in the math lab can't help you much w/ this class. He isn't good at communicating or helping you understand.

Professor Hansen is amazing! She teaches the content really well, and even though you have to learn a lot to succeed in this class, I felt like she prepared us well for tests. Also, there wasn't much homework.
Professor Hansen was amazing. She taught so well and clear. She is incredibly passionate about what she teaches and wants her students to know the material for their own benefit.
I loved this class! Amazing lectures. Tests are long but not too bad if you pay attention in class and study.
Very caring and kind professor

Overall this professor was amazing. Her lectures are engaging, fun, interactive and spiritual. The homework prepares you for the lectures and exams. She cares for the success of each student. Her love for nutrition and for the students is felt in class.

Heavy lectures and lots of reading but if you put in the effort, you will do good. Go to the TA hours and get ready for long tests! This class has 3 midterms plus the final. She is a really nice professor and had a lot of activities and fun ways to explain things interactively. You will get attendance points by participating on a poll so don't skip

Dr. Hansen is INCREDIBLE. Talk about making complicated subjects so easy to understand with her visual aids and fun games. She would sometimes even incentivize participation with nutritional snacks. The assignments are pretty light, however, you do need to study pretty hard for the tests as they are long. If you're gonna take nutrition, pick Hansen
She was awesome!! Really loved what she taught and her teaching was clear. The tests were slightly difficult, I probably averaged a 88% on them, but she prepared us for them well.

Hansen is honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. She tries hard to make her lectures engaging and enjoyable. If you do not do well in this class it is because you do not try, and you don't pay attention in lectures. Tests are not hard if you study the study guides.

If you're gonna take nutrition, take it from Hansen. She wants to help her students understand and apply what they learn. I don't really like nutrition but she made it interesting and fun so much so that I currently miss being in this class. I would only do the textbook readings if I didn't understand something from the lectures.

no extra credit for this class, which sucks. Nutrition is hard, but I would totally recommend Professor Hansen. her lectures make sense & she is really caring. she is more than willing to help, so if you need it JUST ASK. pretty much no assignments in this class so you need to be extra prepared for exams. mainly memorization.

Professor Hansen is really sweet, and she cares about her students so much. We had an online textbook for the class, but I never read it because her slides pretty much had everything you would need to know for tests. I'd highly recommend taking nutrition from her!

I really enjoyed this class. Professor Hansen's lectures were super engaging. She really cares about her students and this came across in her lectures. The only homework is one or two online quizzes a week, which are easy if you take good notes in class. If you are going to take NDFS100, take it from Professor Hansen!!

Totally recommend taking NDFS 100 for a bio general. Professor Hansen was good at teaching what was relevant to the tests. Her slides were also posted, which was helpful. Grade was comprised of quizzes, tests, and a handful of assignments. Not too time consuming and very interesting. To study for tests I read over the slides and quizzes.

Cutest teacher and makes class fun and engaging even though it's a big lecture class. Lots of memorization in this course, but she teaches mnemonics to help with difficult content! Probably the best teacher for this course. You're not overwhelmed with assignments, but they're meaningful when you have them and quizzes are open book and note.

I'm in my 4th semester of college and this is the first B I've gotten. My biggest issue with this class is that they seemed like they were making it overly difficult on purpose. Most of the exams were super hard, the TAs weren't very helpful or accessible, they wouldn't let me fix an assignment at the beginning of the semester to earn points back.

Professor Hansen is a very nice and an engaging professor! She has us break out into rooms which are super helpful and on top of that she does practice quizzes at the end of class (not graded) on prior lectures, which helped me retain information better. The tests are not that bad, but they are VERY LONG.

This was one of the most challenging classes I took this semester. There's so much information to learn--which is why there are 3 midterms and a comprehensive final. Prof. Hansen made the class interesting and helped narrow down to the important information. Super useful class, but be willing to put in the work if you want to snatch an A.

Professor Hansen is amazingly intelligent and great at giving lectures. She explains concepts well and answers questions with clarity. The class content was a lot to take in, but if you follow the study guides, it's easy to keep up. Lots of textbook work, but it's manageable.

NDFS 100 online was a good class that took effort but was doable and interesting. The information needed on tests was clearly explained in the online modules and the TAs were easy to reach with any questions with quick responses. The tests were moderately hard, but doable with a decent amount of studying, and the quizzes were open note.

The professor is nice and understanding but the class itself was very tough. It was not an easy online class. There are a lot of learning activities to do and they took a long time because you have to read the textbook. The tests are very hard and specific, a lot of the questions on it were not taught in lectures and answer choices are very similar

She tells you at the beginning of class that the textbook contains a lot of information that you don't need to know, so she will summarize it in her lectures. However, she tests you on all sorts of information she never even covered or lectured about. Also, lots of questions are subjective and very specific. Was not an easy online class.

She seemed nice enough, but as an online instructor, the "mini-lectures" were bland and unnecessarily long. She did not prepare us for exams, at all. She took a "general" nutrition approach in class but tested on obscure specific nutrition details. I would've had an A if not for the tests.

Professor Hansen's love for nutrition was visible in each class she taught. Her explanations are confident and concise. The class fits as a good an intro class or gen-ed, because she gives in-class reviews before each exam, the assignments are not intense, and the exams had many questions, allowing for wiggle room. Overall an inspiring professor.

Dr. Hansen is the absolute best! I would stay after class sometimes and ask her questions and she was always super helpful and approachable. There are 4 projects, 3 tests, and 10 open book quizzes. I suggest making sure you get no lower than a 9 on any quiz, pay attention in class, and use concept maps to study and you should do fine.

Professor Hansen actually made science enjoyable for me! I'm not a fan of biology but this was such an interesting class. there's a lot to cover so make sure you study consistently rather than cramming it all! She's such a genuine person and truly cares for her students, very thankful. also, this class is a game changer when it comes to cooking!

This class really isn't that hard. I went into it expecting to be bored out of my mind, and I was for part of it, but Dr Hansen made it so enjoyable. She is so kind and caring and really knows her stuff! She teaches clearly and answers questions well. I ended up liking this class a lot more than I thought I would!

A very prepared and caring professor. Attend lectures, go over her PowerPoints, and study the study guide and youre golden. Definitely recommend prof Hansen. She wants the best for her students!! Better GE than bio100 for sure!
I really enjoyed this class. Erica Hansen knows her stuff and obviously cares deeply about it. She made lectures really fun and even brought us cookies! Definitely recommend taking from her.

Prof. Hansen is great! She's so adorable and sweet, and I learned a lot from her class. She moves pretty fast in lecture, so it helps to read the chapter beforehand so you don't get lost of overwhelmed. Not many assignments, a few quizzes, and four tests. Basically just memorization, but Prof. Hansen gives lots of opportunities to quiz yourself.

I love Prof. Hansen! Her lectures are interesting, and she is so cute and funny. There are only 3 assignments, no readings, and a weekly open-book quiz. She provides a study guide for every test and if you show up to class and take notes, you will have everything you need for the exams. Take NDFS100 from Prof. Hansen! She is amazing!

When you walk in the room, you will see a ton of freshman. One of them will be blonde and will standing at the front of the room. DO NOT BE DECEIVED. That blonde freshman at the front is the teacher, and she is married, so do not hit on her. Super great professor.

NDFS 100 is not a very tough class and I really enjoyed Professor Hansen. She is patient and will definitely answer your questions. Tests are based almost completely off of criteria outlined in true learning objectives so if you study from that list you will be set.

The structure of the course is standard across all professors: weekly quizzes, 5 assignments (3hr each), 4 reviews and 4 exams. Textbook was more important than lectures, but lectures can help. Hansen is kind and knowledgeable, but only an okay lecturer. I dislike biology, but some of this class was interesting. Took it as a GE. Fair but difficult.

Loved this class, learned a ton, and enjoyed the lectures. Attendance isn't necessary and neither is reading the book, but I did both to help me remember stuff for the tests. You really only need the textbook for the quizzes that aren't bad at all. As long as you study for the tests they aren't bad either. She grades by a point system which is nice

Normal difficulty class. Prof Hansen knows material really well from on the job experience. TA's are always available. Easy to get 100 on all quizzes and homework. Exams aren't tough, prepare in advance and you can get 100 on them too. Recommend Prof Hansen to anyone!

I loved Professor Hansen! She kept lectures engaging and was very good at answering questions. Quizzes are from the textbook, but otherwise, you don't need the textbook. The tests are pretty much straight memorization of minerals, vitamins, values, etc. I would definitely take this class again!

She is very good at communicating what will be on the test, mostly from her powerpoints. If you ask her a question she doesn't know the answer to, she will research it and get back to you, which is nice. It is a great alternative to BIO 100

She is amazing! 10/10 recommend her for Nutrition. She is caring and funny and very knowledge able about what she teaches. All assignment criteria was clearly laid out and if you put in the studying/work you can certainly pull off an A.

Prof. Hansen is so sweet and really funny. This class will teach you a lot of good material! The tests are department wide so make sure you memorize terms and study. She posts her Powerpoints and they are probably the best resource.
She is awesome! Always very prepared, clear study guides for tests, shes young and cute and funny and made an 8am class enjoyable.
Proffessor Hansens' Nutrition class was great. There is a lot of material covered, but she is organzied and covers everything clearly so that you are really prepared for the test.

Professor Hansen is the best!! I LOVED her class. She is so caring and really wants everyone to succeed. This course is tough because of the tests, but just read the textbook and go to class and you'll be fine. Memorization is the key to passing. Such a great class and wonderful professor!

Hansen is easily one of the best professors on campus. Her lectures go along with the reading, and as long as you do the reading and attend the lectures-you'll ace the test and the class. She does have a few assignments that are a little long and tedious, but there's only like 5 of them. So do yourself a favor, and sign up for NDFS 100 from her.

This is such a great class to take, especially as a freshman in college. It teaches you everything from how to eat right to how to exercise properly. To make it all better, Professor Hansen is an actual dietician so she knows her stuff. I highly recommend taking this class from Hansen.

Not an easy A, but not a super hard A either. Every point counts so try not to get lower than 9/10 on the quizzes. Take them asap. It's open book and all the answers are in it. Hansen was good at explaining concepts in her lectures, but review the textbook and PowerPoints anyways. She's also good about answering questions after and during class.

This wasn't my favorite class, but that wasn't because of Hansen. She really knew her stuff and was very intelligent. She's also very helpful outside of class. My main complaint is that the lectures were basically textbook readings. It wasn't too difficult, so if you're going to take this class, Hansen is a great choice.
Pay attention to the powerpoint slides and read the textbook and you will do fine.

Professor Hansen is the cutest lady! She is super passionate about what she teaches and implements the gospel into her lectures. Funny and engaging too!  You will have to memorize a lot and study for the tests.  If you put in the effort though, it's not too difficult to get an A!  Straightforward assignments and you can use the book with quizzes.

I loved Professor Hansen. She appiled the class to our daily lives and the gospel. I enjoyed learning from her. I would reccommed you take it with her. She also has great stories that help you apply the material.

Sister Hansen is one of the most caring, genuine, engaged professors I've ever had at BYU. She's incredibly passionate about the material, and she makes sure that students are prepared for the test and life.  Additionally, this class is incredibly easy if you're willing to study the textbook--I hardly paid attention in class.

I thought this would be a really easy GE class but it wasn't. Prof. Hansen is such a wonderful teacher though, I just wished I would have tried harder. Keep up on your reading and review often because the course covers a lot of material and you don't want to forget any of it.

Prof. Hansen is wonderful! She does go a little quickly through some material and I was confused at times, but the textbook helps. The assignments aren't too hard, but you will need to study and memorize some stuff. All in all, I enjoyed this class. It was at 8 am so I missed it sometimes, which I wouldn't recommend. Go to class, it's very helpful.

Erica is a very knowledgeable woman. She has been practicing for many years and she uses good object lessons and stories to teach concepts. She is straightforward with what you need to know for the test, however, she does go through the information really fast at times. It is hard to keep up even when she has the slides posted on line.

Professer Alder was a fantastic professor to take SPAN 321 from. If you're taking the class, you likely already know spanish, and are just trying to get the challenge exam credits. He knows that. He doesn't make the class hard for no reason, and instead just tries to have a good time with everyone while honing your skills for the challenge exam.

Professor Alder is a super nice guy. This class was mostly discussion based, and we learned a lot about Spain. There was sometimes a lot of reading, and some of the papers were challenging for me. He assigned us to read academic articles about a Spanish topic, and boy do I struggle with reading academic articles in Spanish.

Professor Alder is very nice and gets to know each student. We had class on Zoom and he had us do breakout rooms every single day. You have to have the Spain book as soon as class starts or you will struggle. There is a lot of reading, but overall it is a great class.

This was a tough class. Basically all the work is reading and papers, which I am not a fan of, but thankfully Professor Alder grades fairly. He's a really good guy, and always willing to help you. He's a little awkward at first, but also really enthusiastic about literature and it rubs off. You'll need a good attitude and work ethic.

This class honestly felt more like a book club than a class, which I loved! The quizzes aren't "pop" - they're just a fact of life. Every day in class there's a quiz, sometimes on the reading and sometimes on your plans for the weekend, but if you read the chapters you don't have to worry. The class is discussion based, and you have papers to write

The first half of the semester is all heavy lectures on Spanish history, and the second half is different modern culture topics. Tests are lots of memorization. Lots of writing for this class, every week. He's a nice guy and lectures aren't bad, it just wasn't the best. Kinda mediocre.

Dr. Alder is a good guy. I didn't find his teaching overwhelmingly engaging, but I still enjoyed class. You have to write a short article each week, as well as one 5 page essay at the end. Honestly, I thought my essays were crap and I got 100%.. so he's not a very tough grader. I think his class will get better with more teaching experience.

For the class, a mini 300 word essay was due each week. Each day a big reading from the textbook was assigned along with some additional readings. You could get by without doing them (and even pass the tests just fine because of the way he does test reviews) but because he does group discussions you look pretty stupid not having done the readings.

After taking three Spanish classes at BYU, this is my least favorite. Professor Alder is disorganized and at times seems clueless about what he teaches. I dont have anything great to say about this professor and class.

He gave little expectations or criteria about assignments, but graded super specifically. He assigns A LOT of reading so just look up summaries if you dont want to read. Just take super good notes and pay attention to what he emphasizes. His tests are pure memorization. He is still willing to work with you and help you out and is a good guy.

Dr. Alder is engaging with his students and dedicated to their success. The grade consists of two tests, a final, a five page paper, and numerous homework readings as well as additional sources. Do the homework and you'll get an easy A. Don't do it, and get a B.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!! I had no interest in art history and dreaded this class, but Dr. Yingling made art history come to life and had me laughing and even crying in class. There was a lot of reading and a good bit of memorization for tests, but he is willing to help and the TA review sessions were incredibly helpful for exams. TAKE THIS CLASS!!

Very energetic, but somewhat confusing when teaching. Helpful to students who miss things. Final projects are fun just make sure you chose the right one for you! Recently changed the tests to be essays instead of super random multiple choice Q. so they are easier to prepare for, but be sure to prepare an outline. Focuses a lot on BYU aims

I dreaded taking this class senior year, but it became one of my favorites at BYU! Professor Yingling makes the content fascinating by consistently tying it to the gospel. To get an A, start the study guides early and focus on those rather than the readings.

The most phenomenal professor I have come across! He goes beyond traditional ways of studying art, making it interesting and fun. He is energetic and dynamic in his lectures. Attend class regularly, take good notes and you will have what you need to study. He cares for his students greatly. I cannot say enough good things about him-take his class!

I took it Winter 2024 and I still tell anyone I can how great of a class it was. I was crushed that he didn't teach any other courses needed for my major and I heavily considered adding an art history minor to take more classes from him. Months later he still remembered me and my wife's name who wasn't in the class. Great disciple of Jesus Christ.

Erik Yingling is one of the best professors I've ever had at BYU. He was energetic and wanted us to learn in unconventional ways.
