I was not expecting art history to be a fun class for me but he made it fun! This was a hard class still, since it is art history you do still need to study a lot and be prepared for the tests but it is totally worth it!

This instructor is the best I've ever had! I took this class as a GE, but his engaging teaching style made it a favorite. He uses volume and movement to capture attention and creates a dynamic, inclusive environment. His passion, approachability, and dedication to success make him an outstanding professor who truly inspires learning.

Honestly this was the first time in my life that I cared about an Art Class. He made it interesting. He is a very kind person and shared powerful stories. Just a good overall guy that loved his students.

Professor Yingling is one of my all time favorite professors!  He is very energetic, fun, and caring! There are note guides and study guides, if you utilize them you are sure to do great in this class. Readings might be a bit heavy. This class was very inspirational to me, and helped me learn things I will incorporate to all aspects of my life!!

Such a fun professor. He is very quirky and passionate about everything he talks about. He definitely does everything he can to make the lecture amazing. He loves sharing his testimony! He changed my perspective on art and how I can appreciate it. Would take him again! Midterms and final require memorizing art images, but overall not a hard class

This class has been life changing! Professor Yingling is awesome; he's so passionate about art history and especially the ways it ties to life lessons and the gospel. I loved learning from him! Attendance and taking detailed notes in class are vital to do well on short weekly quizzes and the tests. Take this class from him ! You won't regret it.

I absolutely LOVE Professor Yingling! He really knows his stuff & is so kind, fun, & incredible at relating course material to the gospel. Simple 10 question quizzes each week. The exams require a lot of memorization, but pay attention & go to TA reviews and you'll be fine. Lectures can be kind of boring, but he does his best to make it engaging.

He is super excited and motivated to teach! Professor Yingling is very approachable and is very willing to work with you. I feel like his main goal is to help his students love art history. I'm not a big art history guy, but his class has definitely changed my mind on it. I would totally take another class from him.
This class is very, very boring unless you are already passionate about the material. That being said, it was very easy and doable. He was kind and understanding, and he told interesting stories.

I don't care for Art history, but I like this professor. He cares about students and does a good job of making the material applicable to your life. He brough his giant rabbit to class once. I see him around and he still remembers my name. Just a good dude. The class was pretty easy. Grades were based on discussion journals and essay-based tests.

Don't look at the lower ratings. Prof. Yingling is an amazing teacher. He really cares about what he teaches and he does a great job doing it. He doesn't post the slides, but if you pay attention, take good notes, and participate, it's not needed. Make sure you study for the exams though. I am taking another class with him next semester.

Pro Yingling was so fun and cared so much for all of us. He is accessible outside of class and really easy to reach with any questions or help. He wants you to succeed so if you go to class, do the readings, and study the study guide for tests you will do great.

Dull lectures with slides that are not posted online. Weekly quizzes that were open on days we didn't have class - very easy to forget, zero reminders. Extremely confusing criteria on exam IDs. Exams all in the testing lab, very long, very arduous, a ton of writing. Extremely disorganized lecturer that expects way too much for a Gen Ed. Don't take!

I enjoyed this class more than I expected. Prof. Yingling is passionate about art history which made the lectures interesting and enjoyable to attend. Attendance counts towards your overall grade. The exams were doable as long as you prepared for them. You were given options for your final exam which caters towards different styles of test taking.

Professor Yingling is super  enthusiastic about art! He knows his stuff. Class is almost completely lecture so be prepared to listen. He changed the format of the class after the first midterm (extremely difficult). Rest of the class was incredibly easy. I don't know if he will change it but he does listen and respond well to student feedback!

A complete waste of time. Yingling has a superiority complex that needs to be checked. He relied on the textbook & excessively long readings to teach irrelevant topics. Lectures were disorganized and we discussed 5 works of art throughout the semester. Students were graded extremely harshly and expected to have PhD-level essays and presentations.

He is passionate about what he teaches which makes his lectures enjoyable. He does a lot of story telling which allows you to immerse yourself in the culture, not just memorize facts and names. There are 2 midterms and a final "pick your own adventure project". Overall super great!!

I loved having Erika's class, she is so caring and passionate. The class assignments were not too heavy and were beneficial. I did not love how my stuff was graded, but I think that was the TA that I did not like.

Dr. Feinauer is more of an academic than a teacher. She is caring and loves her content, but I feel like I could have come away with so much more from this class than I did. That being said, it's not a difficult class at all and the assignments were practical, so it was okay in the end.

I really enjoyed Dr. Feinauer! She is such an intelligent person and her research is really interesting. Her TA mostly graded everything and we got 100% on everything if you did it. Her weekly assignments were pretty easy and I felt like I learned a lot.

Professor Feinauer is a nice person who is very kind and cares about what she does but she is not the best teacher. Her class was 2 very long hours. I don't think I learned anything in this class as most of what she taught was stuff I had already learned, was common sense, or was just her rambling about the same topic over and over.

Avoid this professor! She has about 30 minutes of content prepared and stretches (and stretches and stretches) it to last for two hours. I dreaded class every day because it felt like such a waste. She seems like a really nice person and is obviously very smart, but should not be teaching a class about teaching.

Not gonna lie I always dreaded this class. It was only an hour and 20 min but it felt like forever because it was straight lectures the entire time. She is very educated and knows her stuff, but her class is poorly organized and is EXTREMELY unclear about what the learning objectives are supposed to be. Don't know what I was supposed to learn://

Going to be honest here. Feinauer was not my favorite. Idk if it was because the class was completely online or just because she is a boring teacher in general. Her exams were fine, but definitely frustrating cause she said she never wanted to "trick" us but did. Her criteria is very vague on assignments. Take from the other teacher please!!

I love Dr. Feinauer!! Her lectures are awesome and I found her readings super interesting. She really cares about what you're teaching, and she will work her hardest to answer any questions you might have. Her midterm is super straight forward, she's a pretty black and white kind of gal, but she is so kind and understanding to everyone!

Very easy - I skimmed the readings and still got an A. Weekly digital dialogs, video guides, and quizzes, along with a few papers and tests. While it's an easy A... I hardly ever enjoyed going to lecture. She was a nice lady... but I still have no idea what we were supposed to get out of that class. I don't really feel like I learned anything.

Dr. Feinauer somehow takes an hour and 20 minutes and turns it into 3 days. The lectures are boring and useless, because she spends half the time talking about her personal life. Assignments are confusing sometimes. She is well educated but her lack of focus makes lectures boring and pointless.

Very vague with grading criteria, all lectures kind of blend together. It is hard to know exactly what she wants for assignments and she doesn't explain things very well if you don't understand the first time. A few small things to do every week, midterm, final that is not comprehensive, and 3 papers. Not hard to get an A, just confusing at times

Dr. Feinauer is clearly educated, but the course is pointless. It is not advertised as a blended class, but half of the classes are "online modules" that are busy-work video guides from online videos. This course seems to be integral to the success of an Educator in helping students learn to read, but I feel I got nothing out of the class.

Dr. Feinauer is awesome! She has a passion for this class. She is very approachable and super funny! Lectures could get a little boring, but go because there are iClicker questions and you get points for each question. There are a couple group projects and papers. There is a lot of reading and videos and then there are digital dialogue questions.

She is awesome! Her lectures are interactive and there's lots of good discussion. The tests are super easy and not weighted very much. None of the papers or other work are too bad. The partner project at the end seems like a lot but it's actually super fun! She is funny and sweet and overall I learned a lot! She also gives lots of extra credit!

I think Professor Feinauer deserves a higher score than she has on here. Her class was a lot of busy work, but it wasn't too difficult and I learned a lot from the readings she assigned. The course was partial face to face and partial online, so we only met once a week. That might change, but that's how it was for me. In general, would recommend!

Dr. Feinauer is great! Really loves her subject and super friendly and approachable. She was always willing to take questions during class and I felt like she knew her stuff. I was nervous  about taking her because I read some reviews that said she was disorganized, etc. But after taking her class I disagree. I would recommend her.
Dr. Feinauer is a great professor! I enjoyed attending her "lectures". Class was usually spent having a group discussion. She is funny and likes her students.

Dr. Feinauer is darling. She was pregnant for the whole semester I took it, and she's just the cutest. Plus she knows her stuff and she gives great lectures. Her tests are straightforward and easy if you just study her study-guide. Overall- she's awesome and I would definitely recommend her!!

This class is basically a repeat of human development, so if you've already taken that, this should be a walk through the park. Which also means class can get a little boring. :P There's a ton of group work and busy work, but hey, I appreciate easy points. As long as you stay on top of the assignments, it's really easy to get an A. No midterms.

There are six different things you have to do for this class each week besides attend lecture, which you also have to do or you won't pass.  The first week, everyone was so confused we had to spend two whole class periods just explaining the class.  Absolutely ridiculous.  Point distribution is way uneven.

The course was highly unorganized. The whole class was group project after project, paper after paper. Lectures were required for attendance points, but lecture did not relate well to our readingsprojects so no one paid attention. She's kind in class, but doesn't ever respond to emails & makes her TA's do the majority of the work.

This class was an absolute joke. The lecture don't even pertain the the assigned reading and the teacher allows her over confident TA's to run the entire class. This was by far my least favorite class this semester.

The content is interesting, but Dr. Feinauer doesn't make it interesting. I don't think she's ever actually taught in an Elementary classroom. She is good with theory but lacks examples of practical examples or personal experience.  Take it from Dr. Wimmer if you can.

Dr. Feinauer is a smart woman, but a terrible teacher, especially for someone who is supposed to teach others how to teach. The class is basically run by the TA's. She lectures once a week and you get participation points for going. Be prepared for at least 4 assignments a week. Lectures are boring, do the readings if you want to learn something.

Dr Feinauer knows her material and welcomes discussions. This is not a class you want to fall behind in.  I found it helpful to make practical connections to the content and comment in class.   I would recommend skimming the readings to find the important facts.  Tip - Study  her PowerPoint presentations & digital dialogues to prepare for exams.
Prof Feinauer knows her stuff and is super hardcore. The class is a lot of work, so if you're willing to work hard, you'll do fine. Easy participation points just for attending class.
The lectures were unclear and the tests were not related with the lectures.
Tests were tricks. Attendance is mandatory. She isn't helpful but TAs are. She is nice and funny in class though. I would not take it from her again.

She is a good professor but the class is not very good.  The readings (which are the same regardless of the professor) are dense and useless--just read the powerpoints instead.  If you do the work (i.e. papers and weekly discussions), you'll get an A.
I enjoyed this class. Erika is entertaining and understanding.  The material is interesting and she makes it fun.  I would recommend taking a class from her.

This course has potential to be great. However, Feinauer thinks she's funny but really is just offensive and rude. The course is unorganized, she is not flexible at all, and in short, this class was a huge disappointment. She does not admit her mistakes or work with you. Class is mandatory-if you don't go your grade WILL suffer. I don't recommend
Amazing woman, clearly cares for her students well being. You know going into class you will have a fun time

This is without a doubt the most entertaining and engaging class that I have ever taken. Dr. Bailey is both very knowledgeable and incredibly humble. Her class is fun and a great time to bond with classmates through music (and silliness). There's a decent workload, not too heavy but you definitely can't just procrastinate everything.

Dr. Bailey is AMAZING! She is organized and expects that you are as well. I do not recommend procrastination in this class. Stay on top of it, and you will have a great experience. Dr. Bailey is understanding and approachable. She is dedicated to giving the best education to her students.
Dr. Bailey is an amazing professor! She has many great insights about Music Education, and gives fantastic feedback for lesson plans.

I loved having Erika's class, she is so caring and passionate. The class assignments were not too heavy and were beneficial. I did not love how my stuff was graded, but I think that was the TA that I did not like.

Dr. Feinauer is more of an academic than a teacher. She is caring and loves her content, but I feel like I could have come away with so much more from this class than I did. That being said, it's not a difficult class at all and the assignments were practical, so it was okay in the end.

I really enjoyed Dr. Feinauer! She is such an intelligent person and her research is really interesting. Her TA mostly graded everything and we got 100% on everything if you did it. Her weekly assignments were pretty easy and I felt like I learned a lot.

Professor Feinauer is a nice person who is very kind and cares about what she does but she is not the best teacher. Her class was 2 very long hours. I don't think I learned anything in this class as most of what she taught was stuff I had already learned, was common sense, or was just her rambling about the same topic over and over.

Avoid this professor! She has about 30 minutes of content prepared and stretches (and stretches and stretches) it to last for two hours. I dreaded class every day because it felt like such a waste. She seems like a really nice person and is obviously very smart, but should not be teaching a class about teaching.

Not gonna lie I always dreaded this class. It was only an hour and 20 min but it felt like forever because it was straight lectures the entire time. She is very educated and knows her stuff, but her class is poorly organized and is EXTREMELY unclear about what the learning objectives are supposed to be. Don't know what I was supposed to learn://

Going to be honest here. Feinauer was not my favorite. Idk if it was because the class was completely online or just because she is a boring teacher in general. Her exams were fine, but definitely frustrating cause she said she never wanted to "trick" us but did. Her criteria is very vague on assignments. Take from the other teacher please!!

I love Dr. Feinauer!! Her lectures are awesome and I found her readings super interesting. She really cares about what you're teaching, and she will work her hardest to answer any questions you might have. Her midterm is super straight forward, she's a pretty black and white kind of gal, but she is so kind and understanding to everyone!

Very easy - I skimmed the readings and still got an A. Weekly digital dialogs, video guides, and quizzes, along with a few papers and tests. While it's an easy A... I hardly ever enjoyed going to lecture. She was a nice lady... but I still have no idea what we were supposed to get out of that class. I don't really feel like I learned anything.

Dr. Feinauer somehow takes an hour and 20 minutes and turns it into 3 days. The lectures are boring and useless, because she spends half the time talking about her personal life. Assignments are confusing sometimes. She is well educated but her lack of focus makes lectures boring and pointless.

Very vague with grading criteria, all lectures kind of blend together. It is hard to know exactly what she wants for assignments and she doesn't explain things very well if you don't understand the first time. A few small things to do every week, midterm, final that is not comprehensive, and 3 papers. Not hard to get an A, just confusing at times

Dr. Feinauer is clearly educated, but the course is pointless. It is not advertised as a blended class, but half of the classes are "online modules" that are busy-work video guides from online videos. This course seems to be integral to the success of an Educator in helping students learn to read, but I feel I got nothing out of the class.

Dr. Feinauer is awesome! She has a passion for this class. She is very approachable and super funny! Lectures could get a little boring, but go because there are iClicker questions and you get points for each question. There are a couple group projects and papers. There is a lot of reading and videos and then there are digital dialogue questions.

She is awesome! Her lectures are interactive and there's lots of good discussion. The tests are super easy and not weighted very much. None of the papers or other work are too bad. The partner project at the end seems like a lot but it's actually super fun! She is funny and sweet and overall I learned a lot! She also gives lots of extra credit!

I think Professor Feinauer deserves a higher score than she has on here. Her class was a lot of busy work, but it wasn't too difficult and I learned a lot from the readings she assigned. The course was partial face to face and partial online, so we only met once a week. That might change, but that's how it was for me. In general, would recommend!

Dr. Feinauer is great! Really loves her subject and super friendly and approachable. She was always willing to take questions during class and I felt like she knew her stuff. I was nervous  about taking her because I read some reviews that said she was disorganized, etc. But after taking her class I disagree. I would recommend her.
Dr. Feinauer is a great professor! I enjoyed attending her "lectures". Class was usually spent having a group discussion. She is funny and likes her students.

Dr. Feinauer is darling. She was pregnant for the whole semester I took it, and she's just the cutest. Plus she knows her stuff and she gives great lectures. Her tests are straightforward and easy if you just study her study-guide. Overall- she's awesome and I would definitely recommend her!!

This class is basically a repeat of human development, so if you've already taken that, this should be a walk through the park. Which also means class can get a little boring. :P There's a ton of group work and busy work, but hey, I appreciate easy points. As long as you stay on top of the assignments, it's really easy to get an A. No midterms.

There are six different things you have to do for this class each week besides attend lecture, which you also have to do or you won't pass.  The first week, everyone was so confused we had to spend two whole class periods just explaining the class.  Absolutely ridiculous.  Point distribution is way uneven.

The course was highly unorganized. The whole class was group project after project, paper after paper. Lectures were required for attendance points, but lecture did not relate well to our readingsprojects so no one paid attention. She's kind in class, but doesn't ever respond to emails & makes her TA's do the majority of the work.

This class was an absolute joke. The lecture don't even pertain the the assigned reading and the teacher allows her over confident TA's to run the entire class. This was by far my least favorite class this semester.

The content is interesting, but Dr. Feinauer doesn't make it interesting. I don't think she's ever actually taught in an Elementary classroom. She is good with theory but lacks examples of practical examples or personal experience.  Take it from Dr. Wimmer if you can.

Dr. Feinauer is a smart woman, but a terrible teacher, especially for someone who is supposed to teach others how to teach. The class is basically run by the TA's. She lectures once a week and you get participation points for going. Be prepared for at least 4 assignments a week. Lectures are boring, do the readings if you want to learn something.

Dr Feinauer knows her material and welcomes discussions. This is not a class you want to fall behind in.  I found it helpful to make practical connections to the content and comment in class.   I would recommend skimming the readings to find the important facts.  Tip - Study  her PowerPoint presentations & digital dialogues to prepare for exams.
Prof Feinauer knows her stuff and is super hardcore. The class is a lot of work, so if you're willing to work hard, you'll do fine. Easy participation points just for attending class.
The lectures were unclear and the tests were not related with the lectures.
Tests were tricks. Attendance is mandatory. She isn't helpful but TAs are. She is nice and funny in class though. I would not take it from her again.

She is a good professor but the class is not very good.  The readings (which are the same regardless of the professor) are dense and useless--just read the powerpoints instead.  If you do the work (i.e. papers and weekly discussions), you'll get an A.
I enjoyed this class. Erika is entertaining and understanding.  The material is interesting and she makes it fun.  I would recommend taking a class from her.

This course has potential to be great. However, Feinauer thinks she's funny but really is just offensive and rude. The course is unorganized, she is not flexible at all, and in short, this class was a huge disappointment. She does not admit her mistakes or work with you. Class is mandatory-if you don't go your grade WILL suffer. I don't recommend

Dr. Martin is a very clear teacher and loves math! It made learning the math not bland and dreary and I enjoyed the way she taught. She's readily available to help in office hours and wants her students to succeed!
Dr. Martin is a very clear lecturer. It was always easy to follow along with the class, and she does great helping students during office hours.
She's a great professor with a deep love of mathematics! She has lots of office hours so it's pretty easy to find a time to meet.
She's the best, and super willing to help. Beware of hours and hours of homework though, it's a brutal class.

It took me a minute but I did come to like Dr. Martin. I did feel like I could learn just as much from the lecture notes/textbook as I could going to class. And I sometimes felt like she was talking to a kindergartener. But I would take her class again
Although Math 113 is a difficult class, Dr. Martin is a kind professor that is very enthusiastic towards math. This is definitely not an easy A class, but she is always willing to answer questions.

She is the sweetest! I love absolutely her energy. I unfortunately have to say she has a hard time leveling down to our understanding. She knows so much about calculus that many terms are normal for her, so she uses them and ends up talking like a textbook. She does have the patience to go over a topic a billion times just for you however.

I have always struggled with math, but Dr Martin made her class so manageable! She allows you to do test correction (which really saved my butt). She is so caring and kind; always made time to meet in person or via a zoom call (she met with me at 9:00pm over a zoom call because I couldn't meet any other time). The class is hard, but she is awesome!

She is amazing and teaches Calc 2 in a way that's easy to understand. I had a really hard time with Calc 1 but Calc 2 with her is so much easier. She provides a lot of extra credit that can really help and provides great resources for tests. She takes time to answer each students question which is awesome because some teachers won't.
She wasn't very good at teaching tough topics. Her lectures felt very rushed and her tests were pretty hard.

Dr. Martin makes a difficult class (Calc 2) much easier. She is great at explaining difficult concepts, but sometimes gets lost talking about theory and stuff we don't need to know. Very intelligent and a great teacher, but man it's a hard class.

(I took Math 113) 

Professor Martin is honestly an amazing professor. Super caring, dedicated, driven and cares about the students' success and is more than willing to meet with us outside of class. She teaches well in a way that is easy to understand. The classes are very intellectually active, caused by the student-teacher participation.

Calc 2 is hard. Dr. Martin did a good job teaching and the TA's were helpful as well. The biggest downsides were the time it took to get grades back from tests and the inconsistency of the difficulty of the homework.

Dr. Martin is a delight to be around and learn from, but the wait on midterm grading being over a month was brutal, and didn't give us a lot of time to learn from our mistakes before needing to study for the final exam. 6 homework assignments a week, with a wide spectrum of how much time it takes.

I took Calc BC in high school and got a 4 on the AP exam, yet I still did very poorly in this class. The tests were very hard and it's almost impossible to do well without getting extra help. Lectures were not very useful and the final gave us FRQs that were unlike other examples we had seen before. Be wary of taking this class from her.

Calc 2 is a brutal class, regardless of who you take it from. I enjoyed Dr Martin's lectures all semester, except for the chapter on series (I felt that she was a little unorganized), however, she's a solid math professor. Take advantage of the math lab.

Dr. Martin is an amazing professor and made a decently difficult class much more enjoyable. This section was a part of the EMC2 Cohort so the students in it were very smart and overachievers which isn't necessarily me, but it was good to have peers in the class who could help me out sometimes. Take 314 from her!

Yes, calc 2 is hard. I feel like this teacher just rushed through the hard parts of it and spent way too long on the easy stuff. She also would dismiss student questions if we started going off her lesson schedule, which made it even harder to learn things. Would not recommend.

Dr Martin is great! Learned a lot in MATH213 and will be sure to take Dr Martin again if I have any other math classes I need to take. Her lectures are amazing and I learned a ton. She has office hours but if very flexible and if shes in her office you can usually pop in and ask a. Quick question.
Learned A lot from Dr Martin! Taking Math 113 was enjoyable and I learned a lot. Class was difficult but very doable! Lectures were great and had lots of examples to follow along too.

I TOOK 113 NOT 112 (no option to select 113)
I struggle with more theoretical mathematics, and this course was hard to visualize. Prof. Martin is a great, caring individual. But she was out of breath at the end of every lecture trying to squeeze in all the content. Felt rushed and incomplete. My TA was a bad teacher, so no help in the labs either.

Dr. Martin is such a talented teacher. I've never had a teacher more interested in answering a student's question fully AND within a reasonable amount of time. She loves her students and remembered all our names. The class was hard but not crazy, and most importantly there were no curveballs. Her tests were straightfoward to prepare for and take.
Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. She is so sweet and provides many chances to learn from your mistakes. Calculus is hard, but she teaches it very well and makes it enjoyable.

I loved Professor Busby's Class! I thought the way he structured homework/readings made it incredibly simple to understand what we were going to cover in that specific reading. The tests are very unique, but I thought they were intuitive once you got into them.

I really liked this class and Dr. Busby was the best professor for the course. He was extremely respectful and led the class into discussing very controversial topics in a calm way. There are two oral exams and a paper, and while they were very intimidating, he was very kind and helped me a lot. Best professor in the political science department.

Dr Busby doesn't suffer fools, but in the best way possible. He has high expectations and communicates them clearly, giving students every possible chance to live up to them. I love how engaged with the material and how willing to answer any question he is. His oral exams were wonderful and his lectures were a good balance of inspiring & insightful
Dr. Busby is my favorite professor I have ever had. We read a lot, but it is all engaging. The things I learned in his class are things I hope to remember.

While the class had quite a bit of work (mostly reading and studying, and one big paper), Dr. Busby is an excellent teacher and is very knowledgeable on American politics. He was really helpful and accessible, and gave great feedback. Definitely take POLI 210 from him if you can.

I highly recommend Prof Busby. He teaches a very complicated, difficult subject in a really clear and well-organized way. He has fantastic TA's, gives good lectures, and has some great pre-class videos. His class has weekly assignments (Problem Sets) that are difficult but really good at teaching the material.
This class sucks, but Busby makes it passable. Take it from him or you'll definitely regret it.

This class is so hard but Busby is the professor to take it from. He's super friendly and clear and he's very helpful outside of class. He cares a lot of about his students and he's very accommodating if you're up front with him. Hated the class but really liked Professor Busby.

Could not ask a better professor for Poli 300 (formally 328). Dr. Busby literally taught the material clearly and was very accommodating if you had any special circumstances. The material and problem sets were very challenging, but doable if you started them immediately. He gives you so much help with the TAs and he's good at emailing back.

This is my first ever rate my prof, but this man deserves it. I took 328 (now it's 300), and he was the best professor I have ever had. I didn't think I could have a class this hard and actually enjoy what I'm learning, and feel like the professor had fair expectations of us students. If you can take 300 from him, do it!

This is a hard class, but Dr. Busby handles it very well. I love the format in which he teaches his class, and it makes his lecutures make more sense. 328 sucks for sure, but you'll get the best experience taking it from him.

Professor Busby is literally the best. This class was very time intensive but it was doable because Professor Busby does everything he can to make your life easier and to make the course effective for learning! He is also super accessible and fast at responding to emails, as well as makes sure the TA lab is open all business hours!

This is an extremely hard class, but Professor Busby is wonderful because he wants everyone to pass and succeed. It's a hard course but if I can do it, you can too. There is a lot of homework each week and a lot of time spent in the computer lab. The TA's are very helpful! Rely on them and their office hours.

Make no mistakes about it, 328 was a beast. With that being said, I really enjoyed taking this class with Dr. Busby. There's a lot required of you each week to complete the problem sets, but his lectures and TA labs are geared toward helping you succeed. Dr. Busby also holds office hours by appointment if you need it. It's difficult but doable!

This class isn't so much difficult as it is opaque. It is incredibly hard to get feedback on the exams despite the harsh grading requirements. The techniques and skills learned in the class are 80 years out of date. Dr. Busby is fine as a professor but he didn't keep me from hating this class.
DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IF THEY ARE STILL USING STATA.
This class is incredibly difficult but busby makes it extremely clear how to succeed. he is so patient and kind and he teaches super clearly. I would not want to take Stats from anyone else!

This class wasn't nearly as hard as I had heard, and Dr. Busby was very helpful and likable.  However, you only learn to use stata (the software) in the TA labs, so if you're stuck in a lab that takes a slow pace and the TA office don't work for you, you're on you're own to figure that part out.

Poli 328 is going to be a difficult class, but if you take it from Busby, you'll have everything you need to succeed. Both him and his TA's are super accessible. His lectures can be a little boring at times and he may come off as a little harsh at times, but Busby really is a great professor. Take 328 from him over anybody else.

Busby is truly the BEST! His method of videos before class and then discussion and application in-class is so effective. He truly is so accessible outside of class and he has so many tools to help you succeed. He just wants you to succeed, and he's willing to help you do so, even though it's a super difficult class.

Look, POLI 328 is not supposed to be an easy class, but Busby makes it easier to pass. He teaches very clearly, the readings/videos before class are manageable, and he provides so many resources to make success possible. If you're going to take 328 from any professor, take it from Busby. It's just as hard taught from any other professor.

POLI 328 is definitely the hardest class of the program. I would definitely choose Dr. Busby to take this class from. He is super involved and genuinely cares about his students. There are plenty of opportunities to get help that you need. Don't get me wrong, this class was challenging, but utilize the resources and you will be fine.
Absolute trash of a professor, such a mean dude.

This class is probably the hardest in the major, and it lives up to that title every single day. Basically a part-time job so take minimal classes if you aren't stats savvy from the get go.
This class is survivable thanks to the professor. He cares and is willing to help in any given moment. So take advantage of his help and the TA's.

328 is a beast not for the content so much as the tedium of the homework. It's a lot, but he has given so many resources and the TA's are awesome so there is a lot of support. My advice is to spend an hour or two every other day checking work with the TA's and reviewing. It's totally possible to do well. Don't let it scare you or stress you out.

Professor Busby knows this class is hard. However, he bends over backwards to make it as doable as possible. He is incredibly helpful and you will learn a lot in his class. Prof. Busby is also super available outside of class and is happy to help you in whatever you need. He even helped me with employment stuff over the summer.
Busby was a fairly good lecturer and kept class interesting. 328 is a lot of work, but if you ask questions and stay on top of things, you'll do fine.

Lots of big weekly assignments for this course. GO TO THE TA LAB - it saved many hours of time on the projects each week. Professor Busby didn't teach us how to use stata before we started, which I thought was weird, but otherwise he is a good teacher I would take again.

This is a hard class, but Dr. Busby does everything he can to help you succeed and make sure you learn skills that will help you in future endeavors. Dr. Busby's lectures are very helpful and you can tell he cares a lot about his students. Very accessible and respectful.
Dr. Busby cares about you and wants you to succeed. He will do what he can ethically do to help you achieve your academic goals in this class. Not much more you can ask from a professor.

Professor Busby is willing to help you in any way he can, and his lectures are organized and very clear. The class itself is difficult and the grading can be really frustrating but overall I am glad I took it from Busby because he was so helpful!!

Frustratingly vague instructions and unspecific grading criteria on assignments. People went to TA office hours often to check their answers and avoid losing points for something we weren't told to do. Contrary to what Professor Busby thinks, the readings are in fact not helpful . He is otherwise very approachable, likeable, and a good teacher.

328 is one of the hardest classes for any political science major, and I can't imagine taking it any other way. Professor Busby has one of the most organized ways of teaching I have ever scene. His lectures are great because he takes the time to show us constantly what is coming up and takes time to do examples during class. Great guy.

Professor Busby is one of the best professors I've ever had. Be aware, Poly 328 is no joke. The class requires a lot from you and stretches you academically. But I've learned skills and gained momentum in my academic career that I would not have been able to without his instruction. Use the TAs as your resources in helping you get correct answers.

I think POLI328 kinda sucks overall in terms of just the course load itself. But, Professor Busby tries make the class as manageable as possible. He makes sure that he is clear in teaching and answering questions, and overall is just a super caring professor who takes time to help his students succeed.

Dr. Busby is great, very kind, and caring about everyone in the class. Teaches very clearly and makes sure that everybody is caught up, always takes time to answer questions. Makes himself very available and wants to help you.

Super great class for a GE. I have not enjoyed GE's and while this one had its days, I was overall very pleased with Dr. Ward and his lectures. Study a few hours for the test and you will be fine. Go to class to get free test questions and answers too.

Dr. Ward is by far the best professor to take for this class. I looked forward to going to every lecture. He would make jokes that made the material easier to learn, and it was obvious he cares about each of his students. He was very accessible outside of class and understands that the class is a GE, so he makes it easy to get a decent grade.

The textbook was not needed; I only used it to glean exact vocab working for each test. He also made the final optional if you were satisfied with your grade by then. GO to the TA reviews, and you will do fine on the tests. Dr. Ward is funny and genuinely caring. Make comments and ask questions, and he loves the participation with the class.
You'll find few professors better than Evan Ward! He cares about his students, he's funny, and he gives you the greatest possible chance for success! Take as many classes as you're able to from him!

Dr. Ward was an awesome History professor! He teaches clearly and even gives out extra credit for attendance. His test will account for most of your grade, but the study guides tell you exactly what you need to know. If you enjoy history, it will be a fun and easy class. If not, you'll have to study hard to get good grades on the test.

Professor Ward is great. Very in tune with teenage slang. Professor Ward was so helpful and took time to meet his students and help them succeed. He was very kind and an engaging teacher. His TA is also amazing, and he truly doesn't want his class to be hard. Minimal homework, 3 tests. Don't expect an easy A however, you have to work for it.

I love Dr. Ward!!! He is AMAZING! He is so kind, gives extra credit a lot for just showing up to class. He does little music performances for us on Wednesdays. Textbook is not needed. I never read it and get a's. he tells us short question test answers

Dr. Ward is the most humble and supportive professor I have had in my time at BYU. He will make you laugh every day even if history is not your favorite subject. Not a better one to take your CIV credits from.

I never went to class and never read the textbook. Just put the (extremely good and comprehensive) study guide + the textbook into Chat and studied what it gave me for 4-5 hours the day before the test, and I got A's. He gives you the essay questions. He also dropped the final (unless you wanted to take it). 10/10
Loved Dr. Ward! An incredible professor that cares a lot about you as a person. Would definitely recommend taking univ 101 from him.

Professor Ward is the nicest and funniest professor at BYU. His grading is fair, he is very accommodating, and his study guides are a reflection of the test. If you want to laugh every day and love your life take Prof Ward's class!!!

love prof Ward! he has such a passion for history and is such a funny guy! if you go to lecture, you should do perfectly fine in this class. tests were multiple choice, matching, and brief short answer questions (the easiest of which are of content from the lectures). the TA reviews were so helpful, so don't miss those!

Great lectures but not very helpful for tests, focus on the textbook and study lots to do well. Fav Quotes:

dr. ward wants you to succeed.

Professor Ward was super awesome, however this class is primarily exam heavy. There are a few papers and a few other easy assignments throughout the semester, but the exams weigh like 70%. I never went to lecture and still did well.

I liked him a lot and he was really funny. I didn't love the class however. There was only a handful of things we were graded on so if you do bad on one, its tough to make it up. The tests in this class are worth like 70% of the class and then there is one paper that is 20%.

He has his history 202 class organized well, but I personally didn't like his lecture style. The information is there, but I feel like he wastes a lot of time not talking about the information. He is aware, however, that most students take the class for GE and so he mostly teaches for the tests.

The class was pointless but Dr. Ward did a good job of making accommodations for everyone and taking the time to get to know everyone. He is super chill and its honestly hard not to pass the class with him.

Dr. Ward is very caring and accommodates to needs. He understands the busy college life and helps work with you. I took his UNIV 101 class, and he was so kind and got to know each of us individually. However, I did feel like I was in a middle school class instead of a college one. I felt like I was seen as so young.

Professor Ward was absolutely incredible! I love him and his class. He sang to us and did so many fun things for us. I took his UNIV in the summer which was difficult. He made sure to make accomodations for us so that we were able to get our assignments completed.

Very knowledgable, focuses mainly on textbook info, but diverges depending on if he's travelled to a place recently (we got a lot of India, Thailand, and Australia). His lectures are useful, but lethargic. I had a really hard time feeling engaged, because of his lethargic pace and disorderly PowerPoints. Not bad by any means, but not amazing.

He is a really nice man but the lectures feel like tangents about who knows what. He does provide extra credit for tests but the tests can be really random with the questions. Pretty much if you just wanna coast in class and not really understand the lectures this is the class.

good class just not my forte, dr. ward is very enthusiastic about history but lectures can be very dull. As long as you read the textbook you'll be fine on the tests. One big 6 page paper due at end of semester about a memoir which was actually a cool assignment. requires a lot of studying before the exams!

Professor Ward is the best and I would recommend his classes to everyone! He truly cares about his students and wants each of them to succeed. If you go to the lectures and take notes using the study guide, you are going to do just fine. His lectures are very interesting and he is a super funny guy!

As someone who isn't the best at history, I would recommend Dr. Ward. Go to lectures, go to the reviews. Tests are a big portion of your grade but he bases them strictly off of what you talk about in class and and the reviews. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Always willing to help outside of class. You'll have to put in work but it's manageable

overall an easy class w just map quizzes, two tiny write-ups, one paper on a memoir, & three tests. I gave up trying to follow his lectures which are super confusing & unorganized, but using his study guides with the textbook & google worked just fine. His slides are 95% pictures & videos so if you're a visual learner you'll love it lol

The most uninspiring teacher I've ever had. Horrible jokes & off topic lectures on random people in history who really don't matter much. None of the test reviews, lectures or textbook terms match up on the tests. Super unclear what to study for tests, which are worth more of your grade than they should. Do yourself a favor get other professor.
Great teacher. Read a chapter a week and clearly points out what is on the test. Tests not too hard. Fun guy.
Great professor! Never did any reading, still did really well in the class. Lots of extra credit available too.

I took Prof Ward for Spring Term and so we had two hour lectures three times a week, this seemed really intense going in but Prof Ward kept the lectures engaging. He is very passionate about the material and while 72% of the grade is based on midterms and final he gives lots of opportunity for extra credit and tells you what will be on the tests.

This class wasn't very hard, but the professor kept making not-funny dad jokes that made me lose attention. Attendance wasn't taken, and as long as you study with the study guide he provides, you can get an A. For assignments, there are some map quizzes, a couple of writing assignments, two midterms, and a final.

Dr. Ward is really caring with a huge heart but his lectures were so hard to get through. I'm not the type to fall asleep in class but sometimes I couldn't help it in this one. It requires a lot of effort to pay attention and get all the details for the exams, which btw are lecture-heavy. Exams are doable but are worth most of your grade (like 80%)

Doctor Ward is my favorite professor from BYU. He actually cares about the students! His lecture style is engaging if you are attentive and his tests (while not 'easy') are doable if you pay attention and attend reviews/ask follow up questions. I'm not the greatest at history nor do I really like it, but he made attending class a joy!
I loved Professor Ward! He was so nice and caring and you could tell her really had a passion for his work and teaching!

Dr. Ward is a really nice guy, and is really passionate about the material. Grade is pretty much just based on exams and a final paper, so if you don't do well on the first exam like I did then you're kinda boned. Lectures were kinda long and hard to get through sometimes. Textbook reading was required. Sometimes tested on silly things.
Prof War is great. Really friendly helpful guy. I enjoyed his class and learned a lot. I appreciated all of his travel stories, etc. Recommend.

Really awesome professor. My only complaint was how long the class was and sometimes the lectures were pretty dry, but he did a good job of making class interesting. I wish there was some more class participation, but he loves what he teaches.

Lectures pretty much required for getting high grade. Tests entirely based on lecture material, if you take really good notes textbook isn't required. 72% grade was exams, which were tough and graded on subtle lecture material. 1 project: Read 300 pages of a book and write a report, you must actually read the book. Extra credit offered if youattend

Professor Ward is so kind and wants to help students do well in the class. He gives out extra credit and offers test reviews that are helpful! Overall an awesome Professor and tried to keep class entertaining went it felt long and boring.

Professor Ward cares about his students and wants them to succeed. As long as you go to class and take notes, you should be fine. There is a study guide for the tests and not a lot of busy work. I didn't really read the textbook, but it would be helpful, especially if you struggle with history.

TAKE HIST 202 FROM DR. WARD! He's the best professor I've had at BYU. He doesn't have TA's because he wants to be there for his students. He's super accessible outside of class and ENCOURAGES you to come to him for help. He offers clear study guides for his exams that cover everything you need to know. His class is a very easy A with no busy work!

Dr. Ward is wonderful. His lectures are fascinating, and I love his enthusiasm for history. He cares about his students and is always willing to help. He tends to get a little sidetracked, but he's always very clear about what you need to know for the tests. If you follow the study guides and pay attention during lecture, you're sure to do well!

Prof. Ward is such a good guy and really wants us to succeed! That being said, he gets super excited and often gets sidetracked with unimportant details. And there is just so much to cover in little time, so youll definitely have to study the book and pay attention in class.

Professor Ward is a very nice guy and his lectures aren't all that boring. He cares a lot about his students. If you aren't a history wiz you will have no idea what he is saying. His tests are virtually impossible he does make some questions clear but others are small ideas from the lectures. Impossible to remember and study for.

Dr. Ward is enthusiastic about history and it's fun to see the light in his eyes when he's lecturing on something he's particularly passionate about. He's slightly dry, but once I got used to his sense of humor that made things better. He's very clear about what will be on the tests and doesn't give us many assignments. There's not much discussion.

Professor Ward is very kind and really wants to see his students succeed. He loves what he does and does a great job of teaching new material that a lot of history classes would skip over. He also brings in inspirational speakers from diverse backgrounds which is awesome. The reading is long but his assignments and tests aren't that hard.

Evan is such a great teacher. He truly cares about his students. He is extremely passionate about history and approaches it differently than most teachers. We don't memorize dates, we experience personal stories.

Dr. Ward is a great professor. He takes the mundane parts of a 202 class and makes them more exciting. He is very creative and loves his students.

Prof Ward is a great professor. He is very clear about homework, quizes, tests, and papers. He definitely cares about each student having a good learning experience.

Dr. Ward is the nicest guy ever! You can tell that he truly cares about his students. His lectures are sometimes hard to follow but overall the class isn't too bad. STUDY FOR THE TESTS THOUGH! Dr. Ward was great! The class could be boring at times but he really cares about the success of students and will do everything possible to help. I highly recommend him!
