Great guy, though, and you can tell he is invested and wants to help you. Study guide accurate, but sometimes it seemed like info on tests was never covered.

Professor Ward is a great, caring teacher who loves the subject. That being said, his lectures are long and it's hard to stay awake, and his midterms and final have 8 short response and are fairly difficult. The homework load is low however and weekly tests are predictable.

Ward is passionate about history. He tries his best to teach lectures in a way that's interesting and advantageous to learning. His exams are half multiple-choice/short essay, but he grades fairly. If you love history, take Ward's class. If you don't, take it anyway because it's not a very intense class and you gain a lot of insight.

Dr. Ward deserves more 5's! Great teacher, not easy, but I have never gotten so much feed back and help from a college professor.  He is genuinely interested in his students work and was a great part of my college experience. If your thinking about history Dr. Wards class is a good place to start.

Great teacher!  His lectures are engaging and entertaining, and he really helps you to learn the material.  You will have to read the books, but if you take notes on the reading and use his weekly study guides, you should be good for his test.  If you struggle in his class, go talk to him.  He is very friendly and will help you succeed.

Loved Dr. Ward! So genuine and concerned about students. Tried very hard and often successfully to make lectures interesting. Awesome grading "deals" on quizzes, tests, and extra credit. Dr. Ward has an impressive vocabulary that can be difficult to follow, and I really disliked the textbook; however, definitely THE BEST history teacher at BYU.
Dr. Ward is a great professor. He takes the mundane parts of a 202 class and makes them more exciting. He is very creative and loves his students.

Professor Ward is great. He is passionate about what he teaches and is willing to help you understand everything. Hist tests consists of multiple choice, matching, and short essays. He prepares you well for the tests with a clear study guide and review session. Will not start class without a prayer because he says he needs the Spirit's help. Great!
Prof Ward is a great professor. He is very clear about homework, quizes, tests, and papers. He definitely cares about each student having a good learning experience.

Super nice guy and wants his students to do well without making them miserable. He tells you exactly what you need to do to get an "A" in his class. Do the readings, follow the study guide, and attend glass and you can EASILY get an A+. It really depends on if you're willing to do all the reading because it can be pretty intensive.

Dr. Ward is a great teacher but he can become boring in the lectures that he gives. The tests are not necessarily easy, but they are fair as long as you study. I don't know why I had to buy a text book because I didn't use it after the first test and I got a 91 on the final. I like Dr. Ward and say that he is a good teacher.

Dr. Ward is the best teacher I have had so far at BYU. His lectures are extremely interesting. You are never bored in his class. The tests aren't bad if you study the study guide well. He is funny and well-organized (I don't know why other reviews say he isn't). I highly recommend him.

Dr. Ward is the nicest guy ever! You can tell that he truly cares about his students. His lectures are sometimes hard to follow but overall the class isn't too bad. STUDY FOR THE TESTS THOUGH! The tests are difficult and a lot of information. But it's not a super heavy work load until then, only a few papers here and there. I really like Dr. Ward.
Dr. Ward was great! The class could be boring at times but he really cares about the success of students and will do everything possible to help. I highly recommend him!

Professor Ward was great. There were required weekly journal entries and some random simple assignments, but they were very manageable. The bulk of your grade is your research paper and related assignments. He is always willing to help and give you input. I would highly recommend.

This class was everything a GE class should be. Grading was fair, tests were tough but manageable. Dr. Ward focused on putting things into a historical context, rather than on random facts and dates. Very interesting--he's a smart guy, and he's humble. This is a class a good student can enjoy. There was quite a bit of reading and a paper or two.

The class was very interesting, and the lectures were full of good information. Studying for the tests is labor intensive but totally worth it. Take all of your papers and outlines to the TA and they will be extremely helpful. Take good notes and keep the big picture in mind
Tests are pretty easy if you know the study guide, and the essay part is not that bad, but killed a lot of people. The actual essay killed me. Class not required, and is kinda boring.

Boring teacher. Really nice guy and he tries really hard to make class interesting, but the monotone voice put me to sleep. he chooses odd topics to speak on and he makes many topics boring. he has a special gift in being able to make WW1 boring. The textbook is great though. The TA's are really picky on essays.

Dr. Ward is a GREAT person, just not the best teacher.  He is so sincere, but his lectures are disorganized, confusing, and boring.  Try not to take this class, if you can avoid it.  His TAs are also VERY picky about the essays.  It's really hard to get a good grade on them.  Study A LOT for the tests, and review with Dr. Ward at his office first.

Sir Evan Ward is a great guy. He is really helpful if you go talk to him about anything and he's really nice. However he is not a great teacher. The lectures were really boring and when it came time for the tests there was a general panic because nobody really knew what to expect or what we needed to know. I wouldn't take another class from him.

Dr. Ward is a great teacher, but you have to make sure you pay attention because your entire grade might be based on only less than ten assignments/tests for the whole semester, so if you mess one up, you could be in trouble. Overall he is a fantastic teacher. Very enthusiastic and loves the topics he teaches. Very student-minded!

I liked Prof Ward enough, he's a nice guy, but his class was always really hard for me to go to because the material covered wasn't very interesting and the classroom was really hot and the class was later in the day. I wouldn't really recommend him for a teacher, and I wouldn't take another class from him.

His classes are incredible. Attendance is not mandatory but once you get engagedy, you want to be the first in line! He cares for students. He will expect you to visit with him to see the best way to help you succeed. His off. library is open to you for researh. He easily becomes like part of your family. I would like to take his classes endlessly.

I really have enjoyed this history class,  I was dreading it all through out college, my last class as a senior and last class in to graduate. It was great! I did read 2 books and did a 3 page analysis and 2 midterms. His quizzes were mostly participation quiz, so if you went you could pass. Class was very hard to want to miss. I always wanted to g

Professor Ward was so helpul and interesting!! He made me enjoy history and his class wasn't impossible hard because he gave clear study guides of what was on the test. I would definately suggest taking his class. He is great!!

Pro. Ward is very very approachable.  He went out of his way to help students out of class and attend all the test reviews. He even had special reviews and discussions of the books we had to read so that we could understand them better and have quality papers. Very nice man, great deal of experience in the Latin American area.

I took 202 the first semester Dr. Ward came to BYU and he's fabulous! His lectures are very stimulating and he is very open to answering questions that others have. He or his TA's do review sessions before the tests which is extremely helpful. I'm a history minor and will be taking another class from him this fall because he's great. I recommend hi

nice guy... easy class... I got a D in Hist 201 the first time I took it, and I was dreading taking the class again, but I enjoyed Ward's class. He seemed a little unorganized at first, but after the first exam, I had his teaching style down. The pros outweighed the cons with this Professor.

Nice guy... easy class (for a history class that is)... I got a D in Hist 201 the first time I took it, and I was dreading taking the class again, but I enjoyed Ward's class. He seemed a little unorganized at first, but after the first exam, I had his teaching style down. The pros outweighed the cons with this Professor.

Professor Ward is amazing at teaching Latin American & Mexico hist. which is his specialty. You should check out his ratings at the last school he taught at in Alabama (they are really good} As far as worldciv goes, I don't know, but if you want a HELPFUL, NICE, INTERESTING history teacher that will not kill you off with busy work, take Dr. Ward.

Dr Ward is a very nice man, but he is also very unorganized. You can ask him all the questions you want, but I guarantee you will still be confused about what is required. He likes to take huge pauses in his lectures. Really nice, but I would suggest finding another teacher.

Professor Blackhurst is very focused on participation and application. She would teach the content and material for a couple of lectures, and then would assign a project, either personal or group, to help apply it. If you don't like that vibe, just know that's a huge part of her teaching, but she always supported the process and it was simple.

She creates a positive class environment and is very approachable. I enjoyed her class. There are several readings and videos before class, but no textbook is required. Projects were engaging and manageable. The workload is heavier at the start. She encourages interaction and wants students to succeed.

Professor Blackhurst is super kind and does not grade harshly. There was a lot of reading and group projects during the semester but all of this was manageable. I think If you do everything you can get an A without much effort.

I enjoyed this class, I learned a lot more than I was expecting. I wasn't prepared for how much reading there was, but if you've been in college for a bit you should be fine. There were lots of projects/group projects that required lots of time outside of class. I felt it was a little excessive to have so many. Other than that it was well organized

I was a little intimidated when I saw on the syllabus that there would be pop quizzes, written tests, and a lot of projects, but I ended up loving this class! The content is fascinating, the workload is manageable, and Profe Blackhurst is incredibly kind, helpful, and understanding.

Lots of out-of-class work, including several group projects and presentations. Only two exams but the grading for them is extremely picky and there's not much pre-exam help for reviewing the topics sufficiently. That being said, this class is engaging, covers some fascinating topics, and the instructor is very knowledgeable about the material.

She is a very good person and professor, but her teaching style didn't match my learning style well. Lots of the learning happened outside of class instead of in the classroom. It also took a while to get grades back (for example we didn't get our first test scores back till the day before the second exam) which made studying difficult.

Great course! The professor chose great topics to study and brings in many interesting historical events. There is quite a few assignments but if you stay organized, you'll do just fine. Reading/watching the homework is worth it, you'll learn a lot.

The beginning of the class is a little slow and sometimes the discussions are a little slow, by wow, I learned so many amazing things from this class and had so many fun hands on assignments. Sometimes the readings are long, but it is doable. Two midterms in the testing center that are not too difficult and she doesn't really have a final.

She explains material clearly and is very knowledgeable about South American history. The class includes several group and individual projects, but the workload felt manageable. She emphasizes humanitarian issues and cultural perspectives, and I learned a lot from her lectures.
Lots of projects but they are manageable and pretty fun!

This class was pretty easy and more focused on actually learning about and experiencing Latin-American culture than memorizing facts. There was no textbook, but we did have quite a bit of pre class readings that came from a variety of sources. There were many pop quizzes about these readings. Most of our grade came from several projects.

Dr. Blackhurst was a great teacher! She taught important themes of culture in Latin American history, but also the current situations of the different countries of Latin America. Great class and very insightful.

Dr. Blackhurst is the best!!! She is the sweetest, most understanding professor I've ever had. I would take one of her classes again in a heartbeat. She is just wonderful. Super streamlined learning experience.

Professora Blackhurst was a truly amazing professor. I learned so much info in this class that I never knew before and am grateful I now know. Her tests are mostly written so be prepared to write about what you have learned.

Honestly, she was a fantastic professor who clearly cares about her students. There were lots of group projects, but they were good experiences. They all genuinely built on the class and made the experience incredible. Essentially no busy work as all the assignments felt like they were aimed at something. Tests were hard but she helps you improve.

Professor Blackhurst is super awesome! She cares so much about her students and wants everyone to succeed. There are a lot of projects but they're actually really fun and pretty chill. They're not very challenging but definitely important to do. Also a lot of pre-class reading, but I really enjoyed the discussions in class, very interesting!

I enjoyed Professor Blackhurst's class. She had various projects throughout the semester that gave the class a more hands on feel. This is not a class with annoying busy work - the assignments are spaced out and meaningful. There are lots of pre class readings.
She assigns a lot of projects and they are time consuming.

Profa Blackhurst is the best Spanish professor I've ever had. The class is well organized, and the content is fun to learn about. The beginning half of the class has a long of reading, to do well on the test you have to have actually read, but readings are enjoyable. Other than that, the tests are not too difficult. I would take this class again

This class has a lot of fun group projects, most of which are not terribly time consuming or you get time in class to work on them. The assigned readings and videos before class can be pretty heavy, so make sure you set enough time aside for them. Overall she is a very caring professor, leads great discussions, and is a fair but generous grader.
Great professor! Lots of interactive and group projects, some during class which was nice. Tests are straight forward, just lots of pre class material but you'll do fine if you put in the work.
She is a great teacher and the class was very enjoyable! I highly recommend taking the class from her!

There was a lot of assigned reading for this class, but it wasn't too bad. Just do the readings, go to class and participate in the discussions and the tests aren't too hard. Dr. Blackhurst is so sweet and caring and wants you to succeed and learn from the class.

I'm not an artsy person, so this class was tough for me. Several projects, an unnecessary amount of readings. Didn't like the structure of the class in that you do the readings and discuss the entire next day, plus you don't know whether you're going to have a pop quiz. I feel that she didn't teach much, just led discussions. She's caring, though.
She is great.

I really liked Profe Blackhurst! There are a lot of group projects- so be prepared for that! But the project are pretty fun be prepared to make food, simple art, and PowerPoints.There are a lot of readings but the pop quizzes are pretty easy if you have a general idea of the texts. Exams aren't too bad as long as you know the study guides!

Professor Blackhurst was a great teacher! She is sweet and caring, and you can tell she cares about the topics that she is teaching in class. Lot's of group projects--they're fun, but if that's not something you enjoy then expect to be pushed outside of your comfort zone.
Dr. Blackhurst is a kind person and teaches class well. She is easy to contact outside of class and she is very fair. If you put in a good amount of effort, you will do well in her class.
Wonderful teacher and very fun class. Learned so much!
Lots of projects, sometimes a lot, but pretty manageable and some are pretty interesting/fun.

This ended up being one of my favorite Spanish classes! Professor Blackhurst does a great job of presenting the material and leading thoughtful discussions. You get a lot out of the course if you do the readings, and I genuinely enjoyed most of them. Several group projects but as long as you choose a good group you'll be fine.

I love Professor Blackhurst! She brings so much passion and excitement to her teaching. Though there are lots of readings and projects, I found that they were usually very interesting and helped me engage with the material. Also, Professor Blackhurst wants to help you succeed and provides lots of opportunities to do well in the class.

Dr. Blackhurst is a great professor. She organized the class so that we would have many opportunities to really experience the cultures we were studying. Some of the reading was a bit heavy, especially towards the beginning of the semester, but besides that I have no complaints.

She is very caring and passionate about her job. Lots of group projects and an average workload. She is lenient on grading too so there are many assignments but lots depend on participation and effort.

Professor Blackhurst is a great teacher! The class itself is not very difficult if you do the readings. The group projects are enjoyable and there is an individual project that replaces a final exam. I really like this class and Professor Blackhurst's style of organizing her course.

The professor is very kind and patient with her students. I felt if I ever had a question about anything, I could just stop in and ask and she would be very nice about that. She would assign long reading assignments that were impossible to finish before class. Class is just talking about the readings with your classmates the whole time.
Class is mostly based on readings and videos with no textbook and there is a lot of homework but you do not need an in depth understanding to do well
Really good class!

Profe Blackhurst is the best! Her class is super organized, along with many projects and readings. The load is very manageable and if you stay on track with everything you will excel in this class. Projects were fun and overall she cares a lot about her students!

She really cares that we learn in a meaningful way using different methods, through readings, videos, as well as individual and group projects. Recommend this class highly for a great learning experience of spanish cultures across America!

Prof Blackhurst is awesome!! You can tell that she really cares about the course content and about her students. There are a ton of projects, but they were all super fun. The readings are usually pretty long, and there are unscheduled quizzes at the start of some classes, so make sure you do the readings.

Love Profe Blackhurst! Super caring and understanding, and genuinely wants you to learn. There are reading assignments for every class and a few group projects as well as some outside of class stuff. Would take from her again!

She designs her class in a way that helps students learn and stay engaged with the material. The homework is very reasonable and usually includes readings or short writing assignments. A large part of the class is centered on discussing cultural topics, which was especially helpful for developing my Spanish skills.
Prof. Blackhurst is patient with all students and  you a good course load. I would recommend this class for those who are willing to work with groups.

Profesora Blackhurst is amazing! I've taken two classes from her and in both I've felt that the expectations were clearly outlined and that she graded super fairly. There is a lot of reading for this class, especially at the beginning of the semester, and a ton of group projects. Overall she cares a lot about her students and makes succeeding easy.

She gave great lectures and broke up the class period with talking in small groups or other activities. Assignments are fair, and she's a fair grader. Group projects were great to get to know classmates and didn't require too much scheduling. Would highly recommend taking from Professor Blackhurst for this class!

This class is very interesting! She has combined lots of awesome readings to base the lectures on, however there are LOTS of readings. The class discussions are always very informative and interesting. She offers lots of help to her students if they need it.

The class was really enjoyable, and a big part of that came from getting to know people through group projects and presentations. There's definitely a solid amount of reading outside of class, so staying on top of it makes a big difference if you want to participate and keep up.

Prof B is awesome! She is super reachable and you can tell she truly cares about her students and their academic success. There were a lot of really fun group projects and only two exams (that you have to take at the testing center, UGH!) but overall an easy class

Professor Blackhurst is a very caring and great teacher. There are a LOT of group projects and two tests. The tests aren't super hard, but the questions were mostly written response, and she graded them pretty tough. The grading criteria for them was also a little unclear. Besides that, she gives full credit for pretty much all other assignments.
Prof. Blackhurst truly cares about the success of her students! She is great at finding various ways to discuss class topics and make them creative!
Lots of group projects and projects in general. Not as much emphasis on tests, so if that's your thing, I would definitely recommend. Great professor in general, super sweet and kind.

Amazing class, the overall structure was fitting for my busy schedule and allowed me to enjoy learning more about latin american culture. Although there are lots of projects outside of class, by setting aside to time to work on them, they were easier than I thought and she is a relatively kind grader. You'll enjoy this course not using AI 24/7.

I took both Span 321 and Span 355 from her. She excels at teaching course curriculum in a way that is both intellectually engaging and possible to manage with a heavy class load. She provides students with creative, hands-on projects as opposed to just a bunch of essays. If you show up to class and do the readings, you should do well in this class.
Dr. Blackhurst is kind and genuinely cares about her students. Overall, I learned a lot and always felt supported, and she was very willing to work with me when needed.

Professor Blackhurst is awesome! There are a lot of group projects and projects in general. Lots of reading and out of class assignments. All in all great class would take it again and she is always available to help out and answer your questions which is great!.

Great teacher! A pretty good amount of reading and lots of different projects. A few group projects and an individual semester-long project. It was a fun class and pretty easy but it'll keep you busy. Dr. Blackhurst is really nice and I've taken 2 classes from her, both of which I've enjoyed.

This class had more reading and writing than the spanish literature class that I also took from her. LOTS of reading before each class and tons of projects. They are manageable if you space them out but can be overwhelming at the end of the semester. Shes cares about the material and teaches well but was a bit more difficult than it should've been.

Loved Dr. Blackhurst. Her class is super organized, so you always know what's due and what's expected. 
There is a good amount of reading (normal for lit), but even with 19 credits, I never felt overwhelmed since she reviews key info before quizzes and exams. 
10/10 recommend, one of the best teachers I've had at BYU.

Dr Blackhurst is great and I would take her again! Super reasonable, caring, and accesible. Was very understanding and flexible with some assignment deadlines, and grading is very clear. Highly reccomend!
She is a great teacher! A lot of reading in this class, but it is manageable. She really appreciates participation so try and be an active learner and she will be very helpful to you.
Professor Blackhurst was a great Professor. She was very understanding of time constraints and valued participation and effort more than perfect performance.

I loved this class! Dr. Blackhurst is so kind and willing to work with you if you need it. Attendance is mandatory, but you do get one free mental health day. Readings can be heavy, so give yourself enough time out of class to do them. You will want to do them before class because there are random pop quizzes that you can only take in class.

A very good class and a great professor. Very caring and a great communicator. I felt like my writing skill improved this semester and that it wasn't too much of a workload. I could have been pushed more but I was also grateful for the feedback and variety of different types of assignments we were expected to do.

She is such a good teacher and willing to help with anything, but the rubric for most of her papers is unclear and she doesn't explain her assignments very well so you have to ask her what she is looking for.

Professor Blackhurst was not trying to make the class hard at all. Spanish literature isn't the funnest or most exciting topic in the world but Professor Blackhurst was very easy to work with. The test in her class aren't weighted heavily at all so if you get a bad grade you are fine! Just focus on the papers for sure.
Sister Blackhurst was great! She has by far been my best Spanish teacher. The class is very well organized and she grades fairly.
Profe Blackhurst is fair, kind and understanding. I would take any class she offers.

Professor Blackhurst is a kind professor who wants to help her students succeed! She took feedback into account and always made an effort to clarify any content that students didn't understand. If you do the readings, make an effort to discuss them during lectures, then apply what you learned to the assignments, you'll do great in the class!
Professor Blackhurst is great! She makes learning fun! The only thing I would say is there is a lot of reading, but it isn't bad.

Profe Blackhurst is the best! She treats us with respect, believes that each student is capable of improving and learning, and is so understanding of the language learning process. She used a variety of partner/group activities and her classroom is a safe place to learn and have fun! You'll read lots but Profe makes this class totally doable!

This professor is very skilled in the Spanish language and with knowledge of literature. She can talk about the difficult topics in literature in a professional way that invites people to be more comfortable. She favors class attendance and is good at getting class participation because she asks a lot of questions.

I was often confused and that made it feel difficult because we were kind of in the dark on some assignments. The midterm for example was way harder than we thought it would be. And the papers we didn't receive much guidance on until we already were writing our second one.
Professor Blackhurst is a great professor. She does a great job at assigning fun projects to keep the class interesting

Profesor Blackhurst is great. Her class honestly isn't too hard, but the midterm is sneakily hard. The organization of the class was a little disorganized because there were deadline changes but she was good to give us a heads up and enough time. Make sure you do the readings because there are pop quizzes in class. Attendance is mandatory.
shes awesome and assignments were easy

Professor Blackhurst truly cares about her students, and this has been one of the first Spanish classes at BYU that was well organized. Learning Suite kind of sucked sometimes, and sometimes we weren't given a huge heads up on upcoming assignments but if you read the schedule and put in the work you can succeed in her class.

Professor Blackhurst is extremely kind and caring--you can sense her desire to teach and increase understanding. The class itself is very easy, with little outside homework and a small portion of the grade being composed of exam scores. There are a few projects, but they are all very manageable. Take it from Professor Blackhurst if you can!
Well run class. Fair and fun.

She was a great and very understanding professor. I had lots of things come up this semester and really was only able to go to her class about half of the time. She understood and worked with me and allowed me to submit assignments late anyway and still get credit for them. She is willing to work with those who show her they actually care.

Lots of extra credit options was super helpful for those looking to get a great grade. We did some group projects which were actually kinda fun. There were pop quizzes, but she told us ahead of time. They were on the readings, so make sure to understand what the gist of the reading was.
Great class lots of reading and essays

One thing I loved about Professor Blackhurst's teaching was how she gave plenty of time for discussion with our classmates. Sometimes it felt like too much time but it was actually super helpful. I also appreciated that she didn't make us feel dumb for not knowing certain words in Spanish and even admitted when she didn't know em either. Super nice

Professor is a good Professor. She gives a reasonable amount of work and is very understanding of a student's time and schedule. There were some random art projects that caught me off guard but they were graded very gracefully. The mid term was surprisingly hard compared to the rest of the class, but the final is all multiple choice so that's nice.

The group projects make it more engaging because the material is pretty dull with lots of reading. My only complaint is I feel like for a lot of the assignments there was not a clear rubric and she graded pretty harshly. The midterm is weighted more than the final and I feel like the material was not well explained.
She was really nice and understanding but the content of the class is tough since it's all Spanish Literature.

Prof. Blackhurst is awesome. She makes the class engaging and fun. She is super understanding and wants to help you succeed. Just a note, it is a graded assignment to write her a review on here. That is why is an abnormal amount of reviews for her.

Profesora Blackhurst is a fantastic professor who sincerely cares about her students and is passionate about Spanish literature. She is very knowledgeable and explains concepts well in class and is always willing to answer students' questions. The projects we got to participate in were also fun and helped me to connect with the Spanish literature!

Profesora Blackhurst is a super caring professor who is always looking for ways to better the class. She puts students first and cares about the material. Good introduction to Spanish Literature. It is literature though, so you will have to read. Easy grader, just get the assignments in.
Wasn't expecting to enjoy the content of the course. Pleasantly surprised Profesora was great.

Profesora Blackhurst is super nice!! The class is pretty easy but you still have to do work. Class is always interesting and goes by fast if you participate. The assignments aren't too hard and I feel like she's a pretty lenient grader, but still offers good feedback. I enjoy the class and will be taking another from her!
Probably the best Spanish professor I've had. Lectures are engaging and relevant to the exams.

Professor Blackhurst is super caring and has a deep passion for what she is teaching! She explains concepts clearly and fosters a classroom of discussion. There is a good mix of types of assignments- papers, creative work, and group projects. This class does have a lot of reading, but if you keep up with it, you will be very successful!

There are a lot of readings (it is a literature class) but the assignments aren't difficult. Lots of opportunities to discuss the readings/assignments in class, and you often discuss them before you take one of the few reading quizzes. She genuinely cares, and personally reached out to check in. The more you participate, the better off you'll be!
Honestly just a good class and not to hard.

I loved Professor Blackhurst! She is such an amazing teacher and her lectures and classes are always so engaging. She helps you connect to course material and it is evident that she is passionate about what she teaches. I loved going to her classes and she always had fun activities planned. I'm definitely going to take another class from her!

Profe Blackhurst was great! Most classes consisted of discussions on the readings which helped a lot to reinforce the readings and remember them. She teaches super well about the terms needed for exams and projects. She is very understanding and was very willing to work with students to help them succeed. Would highly recommend!!!

I really liked this class. It is easy to see how the same class given by a different professor could be very boring, but professor Blackhurst does a good job making it interesting through many small projects and activities. She was also very understanding when it came to due dates and technical difficulties with assignments.

Profe Blackhurst was amazing! Most of class is discussion based so make sure you do the readings so you have something to talk about. She is very understanding and was very willing to work with students to help them succeed.
She is such an amazing professor! I always felt like she was there to help us learn, not get a grade. She really helped the class be enjoyable and engaging.
Super caring, if you reach out, she is always willing to help. Attendance is mandatory, but she gives you a free, no-questions-asked day off.

She is awesome!! I will be taking another class with her next semester. There is a fair amount of reading to do, but it is fun to discuss in class and I felt like most of the reading was pretty enjoyable.

I love Professor Blackhurst. She is a very kind, fair teacher, and she has so many fun activities and projects in class. There is a lot of reading involved, but she is very understanding with grades. She also gives great feedback on written papers. I would definitely recommend her as a teacher.

Prof Blackhurst is super caring and understanding. She was pretty clear about expectations for assignments and provided lots of help. Because it is a lit class there were a lot of readings. Also she often has pop quizzes which can be a little difficult but usually she'll allow students to ask questions about the readings beforehand.

Involves a lot of participation/group conversations in class, which helps to keep Spanish fresh when we don't normally use it daily in that form/environment. Readings have a purpose and are important for understanding literary principles. Overall, she's a great teacher and is willing to help with whatever you need.
I would take this class time and time again. Just do it

This class was an easy A if you keep up with the reading. The material was interesting and not hard to understand, and she does a good job of giving you everything you need to be successful. She is very forgiving and gives a lot of grace for late and/or misunderstood assignments. Quite a few readings, but nothing compared to my other classes.

I absolutely loved Professor Blackhurst. She was not only very clear with her grading and expectations, but she also gave us assignments that were to help us prepare for exams and essays. Everything in this class is intentional, not just busywork. Make sure to do the reading and pay attention in class! She's great!

Professor Blackhurst is one of the best teachers I've had. I took this class during summer and we had more to do with less time to do it, it never felt unfair or overwhelming. Dr. Blackhurst is a great professor! She works really hard to help her students succeed. I enjoyed the class a lot and I felt like I learned a lot. Professor Blackhurst is a great professor for the cultures of Spanish America. You learn a lot from the art group projects and from the readings. Professor Blackhurst is very kind and helpful for her students. She really wants to help her students improve and to grow in their Spanish ability. Love her!!!

Profe Blackhurst is seriously amazing!! She makes learning super interactive and fun! She also cares a lot about the students and making sure that they are able to complete everything. Very kind and helpful. There are pop quizzes that aren't that difficult in class if you do the reading. The exams aren't too bad, but it is important to study well. Great teacher overall.

love love love love LOVE profe blackhurst!!! if possible i am definitely planning on taking another class from her. Awesome teacher, was good at covering lots of material and cultures in a short time while diving deep enough to feel like you actually learn something. lots of lectures were about readings you would do in between classes, and there was lots of class involvment with discussion. Professor Blackhurst is a great teacher and it was evident that she wanted everyone in the class to succeed. Professor Blackhurst is super clear and organized. Lectures were engaging and is always happy to answer questions during office hours or through email. Exams matched the readings as well as what was taught so no surprises. Would definitely take again!

Professor Blackhurst is wonderful! She really cares about the students and wants the best for your learning. Class was enjoyable and she implements multiple styles of teaching which is epic. I really enjoyed the class, and Professor Blackhurst is great. She really cares for her students and she has organized that course to be very straightforward on what needs to get done. She's great! She really wants you to exceed and if you do the short readings before each class, you'll be fine. The class is super chill.

Profe Blackhurst is the best Spanish Professor I've had so far. She really cares about the material and wants to help you. This isnt a difficult class but its also definitely not a helpful one. He is kind and offers help when you ask, but teaching often seems like an afterthought to Fidalis.

I have never met a professor that is as respectful of student opinion as Fidalis is. I have taken 2 classes from him and wish that I could take more. He is talented, encouraging, funny, and really wants his classroom to be an uplifting place.

Fidalis is a fantastic artist and teacher, and he seriously cares about his students. He gives great feedback, is pretty chill, and really knows his stuff. Workload is more than manageable if you enjoy drawing. He's hilarious in that slightly dorky, awkward dad sort of way. I've learned tons about who I want to be as an artist from him & his class.

I LOVE Fidalis! He is my favorite professor by far in the art department. He really cares about each of his students individually and gives great feedback. He's really laid back yet he challenges you to work hard and to set goals for yourself and inspires you to improve.

Great class and he is willing to give you lots of feedback. However, he gives no grades throughout the semester until the final grade which is extremely frustrating. Overall, he is a great teacher and a lot of fun.

He gave guidelines, but the actual work was up to your imagination. He wasn't afraid to say what he liked and what he didn't like so be ready for that. He was super laid back and it was overall a really fun class. No textbook or tests are required, but you will have a final project but it's just another piece due. Take his class he is a great guy!

Fidalis is my favorite professor so far here at BYU. He is so chill and you can tell he really loves what he does. Take from Fidalis if you can, if not, switch to a class he teaches, because you don't want to miss out on learning from such a great teacher.

Freshman Seminar was a required visual arts prereq. Fidalis is in charge of the class but there is a different speaker every week. Fidalis is a brilliant artist who gave good presentations and is always very nice and helpful. The class was fun, our final was making a pinewood derby car.

Since I took the seminar from Fidalis, I was never quite able to see how he is as an art teacher... But he's a nice guy who's willing to help students out when they have a problem, and I assume that would translate over to a workspace.

Fidalis is the best! he is really interested in the development of each students personal art but also pushes you to explore new mediums,techniques,ideas. the multi-layer painting is a specialty of his. Fair and understanding but you must be a hard worker in order to thrive and survive this class-painting takes alot longer than most people think

Amazing professor!!! Dr. Christianson cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Going to his office hours is super helpful and he is always willing to work with students. Always do the readings or else you can't participate in class and will be really confused. Prepare for the midterm and final more than you think you need to.

I absolutely loved Professor Christianson's class. There was a lot of reading, but I felt all of it was very well selected. The discussions we had in class were very deep and thought-provoking, and feedback on assignments was personalized. Definitely worth my time. Would highly recommend for anyone who wants to become a deeper thinker and learner.

I LOVE Pro. Christianson! The class was just readings and annotations. We would return to class and discuss what we read. His class was very interesting, thought-provoking, and I would HIGHLY recommend.

Probably one of the most understated comedians I've ever met, it makes sense that Professor Christianson loves Twain so much. This class was unique in that it was mixed with 384R, so it focused on one author (Twain) while also including other authors from the era. You really need to be on top of things, though, since he won't remind you

Really enjoyed this class! Class was discussion based, so I could see how having a good group would impact that. Only work was readings, annotations, and small writing assignments which were tedious/due each class, but very manageable. Very thought provoking discussions that made me want to take more classes from him. Really can't recommend enough!

I loved professor Christianson. He is a very smart guy and was too smart for me at times. Whatever the opposite of down-to-earth is how I would describe this class. He invites you to think very deeply. Sometimes I struggled to interpret the "english major speak" but I definitely grew as a student.

Going on London theatre program was best decision I ever made. Dr. Christianson's class was focused on Shakespeare and experiential learning. It helped us make the most of every moment in London and helped us make the connections between what we studied and what we did. Fabulous teacher. Fabulous program.
I enjoyed these course particularly the course content and the class discussions. It made me appreciate the literature we were reading and Christianson was very engaging in the way he taught.

I liked the readings and that our class time was mostly discussion. I came to adore American literature because of his class. He asks great questions, and as students we knew his priority was helping us engage meaningfully with the material. I also enjoyed the structure; the main focus was the readings and we didn't have busy-work assignments

Christianson was a good professor, but he's not the greatest. His lectures were very confusing and I always left class wondering what I was supposed to take from his lessons. He's not very good at explaining things, but is an easy grader. His tests are all memorization, and he gives you a study guide; you'll need to memorize 100+ terms.
The major project was really cool. Prof C. paced it out over the whole semester. He made class time well spent.

At the beginning of the semester it seemed like it would be an impossible amount of reading, but I got in the groove with the workload as the semester progressed. He is SO SMART and compassionate!! You learn a lot of words just hearing him talk. Thought-provoking class.

Class was very participation based with great projects that have practical applications. Professor Christianson was very engaging and dynamic. His enthusiasm for the course material was contagious. He stretched our intellectual capacities, but gave us the resources to do it.
Great class. It was a small seminar, so the professor could take time to meet with us on our projects multiple times. Learned a lot about research and writing.

He co-taught this class and he was great. He made American lit interesting, even though it's my least favorite. He's very passionate about the topics and you'll learn a lot. There's a lot of reading and you'll have to study a lot for the tests, but it was my favorite class of the semester.
Prof. Christianson did a great job of generating discussion. Made the reading interesting even when it wasn't.

We read many different pieces from anthologies. Prof. Christianson was really good at explaining the significance of each work and making even boring reading (the puritans) seem interesting. Great class.

He doesn't leave notes on papers, which is beyond frustrating in trying to improve. Because of this, his grading rubric for papers and exams feels arbitrary. His teaching style felt disorganized and random. He tries to be accommodating with assignments, but I never felt like his help changed or affected anything. Vague assignments requirements.

No one can just skate by, but if you take a class from Christianson, you aren't likely to want to. He expects a lot but he gives you all the resources and more to succeed. Take advantage of consulting with him!

Frank was just an amazing teacher. He's very clear, which is sometimes hard to find in upper division English classes. We had meaningful assignments and the tests were not too hard as long as you pay attention in class. I highly recommend his classes.
total rockstar. loved his class and his sense of humor. met with me a couple times throughout the semester, and he was quite helpful. also--good looking.

Very knowledgable professor, but bases way too much of your grade on two ridiculously hard exams. He's very approachable and willing to help however. If you want a good grade, paying attention and being part of class discussion is a must. Don't underestimate his tests!

Dr. Christianson is amazing. He's a subject expert. He teaches with extreme clarity. His expectations are always precise. He's witty, and loves class participation. your grade is based on self evaluation for daily reading points, done at the start of class, and essays. Essays are not hard, they're precise, if you get low scores he's eager to help.

I loved this class. It is really hard, you have to do all the reading, and take notes on everything he says. Dr. Christianson is very helpful if you go during office hours, and makes a point to emphasize in lecture the quotes he will put on the exam. Very funny and nice, straightforward tests.

I took his night class and at first I was nervous at a 3 hour english lecture but after the first day I realized how wrong I was. Dr. C is so willing to help you learn. The Norton anthology you read from is THICK but he doesn't assign it all. I suggest you complete all readings, participate in class discussion, and DO THE STUDY GUIDE for exams.

I personally had no interest in American Lit, but his class always had me walking out excited about what we discussed.  He is an amazing lecturer--he has a real talent for teaching.  He gives a very detailed study guide for the midterms, which are based on class notes.  He is the best professor I have had here at BYU.  Take a class from him!!!

Great teacher. But at least in trans lit, we covered so much material that I didn't get as much out of the class as I had hoped.. as far as the discussions went. You do come away w/ great overall knowledge of lit history. He's really nice, looks like brad pitt a little :) so that definitely made me pay attention more. Tough w/ grading papers though

Frank was hot, but really boring. I felt like there weren't too many insights on the actual reading, but just a ton of background knowledge on the literary time periods. If you're looking for a Lit class with a ton of discussion do not take Frank.

This class was team-taught and it was great. Transatlantic is the only way to study American lit. If you are going to take the 292 adn 293 surveys, wait and take the combined class when it is offered again (not every semester).

I think he did a great job of covering a survey course. While attendance was definitely necessary and it was not an easy A, it was still very enjoyable. He is very willing to help you get the grade you want if you are willing to work for it.
Great overview of am lit. Loved the clips and the discussions. Exams covered a lot but were fair.
Pretty heavy reading but he covered most of it in class. Use a lot of power point and video clips to keep things varied in class. Has a good balance of lecture and discussion.

Previous comments from a moron. Class is challenging but learned a ton. If you don't like the experience, you are probably in the wrong major. Great class. Just be prepared to do real work and it will pay off.

Nice guy, but it doesn't seem like he actually knows that much about literature.  His ideas are unclear in lectures, and sometimes doesn't seem to know what he's talking about.  He also grades papers really hard but doesn't give very helpful feedback.

this prof was very interesting, and humorous.  He shared many stories about his childhood that made class a joy! Good luck though....watch your butt cause this class will spank you hard!  Not an easy A

Professor Christianson is a good professor. He is a little tough on his students, and sometimes his ideas are hard to follow. If you make use of the office hours, though, he is so willing to help, and your grades improve a lot. Put in effort, and you will do well.

I loved this class primarily because it was a combined 292/293 class. Definitely worth taking. However, he tends to drone on in his lectures and that can get boring. Prof Mason taught the 292 part alongside him and that made class much more interesting. Aside from dull lectures Prof Christianson is way awesome and very helpful.

He is sometimes very hard to understand with his very elevated vocabulary.  Notes are hard to take because he sometimes assumes you know exactly what he is talking about.  But his class was very interesting.  I had to work really hard to get a decent grade.  He keeps a reading log so you have to do the reading but it was good reading.

This was an amazing class!  I absolutely loved it and enjoyed going to class (even though it was a night class and was 2.5 hours long).  Pro. Christianson is a complete genius and is very willing to help students on papers - just make an appointment with him.  That said, this class is no easy A.  Study hard for the tests and keep up on the reading

If you are a free thinker, take a different professor.  Grades depend highly on how closely your opinion matches Dr. Christianson's.  45% of the grade is tests (very subjectively graded to opinion of professor). 40% is essays. 15% is 'on-time' quizzes (also very subjectively graded).  There isn't a whole lot of room for personal application.

This is such a wonderful class!  Dr. Christianson loves what he talks about, and he talks about it well.  I felt like every class period was well worth my time because I learned so much.  I also appreciated Dr. Christianson's willingness to be ehlpful to his students.  The best teacher that I have had so far at BYU!
I have one piece of advice for you - Take a dictionary to class...this professor has a vocabulary as big as his ego...can be hard to understand at times. lectures were very interesting. good luck.

Incredible lecturer! I felt like I learned so much after each class period.  Tests aren't bad; just make sure that you take really good notes in class.  Papers aren't too difficult either, and he's perfectly willing to help his students.  Highly recommended.

Decent, better class than others... make sure to take your papers to him before they're due--much harder than his tests--but study a lot for them too. Take super notes and ALWAYS have a study group--he kind of rambles on in a scholarly way, and can be harder to follow/understand.
Do it. Take it. Dream it. He's a really good teacher, tests are kind of long... take good notes and enjoy the lecture. I really liked this class.

As said, as long as you do the readings and pay attention in class, you'll be fine in this class. Prof Christianson is a genious, think about bringing a dictionary to class or you might not be able to understand him.  He's relatively entertaining for an English professor.  Tests aren't too bad, and there's not much busy work.  Good class overall.
Amazing class!  Amazing Teacher!  Just do your reading and listen in class and the tests are no problem.  This class was the highlight of my week.

This professor is a sweet relief from the boring, overaged English teachers that seem to have infested the department. He is the Guru of American Lit. I enjoyed every class period, and even the tests were a reason to celebrate. Leaving the testing center, you felt proud of yourself for learning so much. Take this teacher, he is fantastic!

Dr. Christianson is an excellent teacher who loves American literature and wants his students to understand and love it, too.  He is easy to contact for outside help.  But beware - you earn every inch of your grade in this class!  No easy A.

He was very nice and laid back, one of the best profs I've had so far. Very respectful of students' comments, fair workload and interesting material. I would take another class from him. Fair grading, not too easy, not too hard. Really enjoyed him and his class!

His arms are massive--almost as massive as his brain! His philosophy of life is consistent with the standards and principles of Kant, but with a little bit of Husserl and Wittgenstein to modify it. Take this class if you want to live as no other, and miss it if you know where you're going!

THIS CLASS WAS THE HARDEST AND WORST CLASS EVER, and I have taken american heritage!!!! Like literally the worst tests of my life and sooo much busy work. Not spiritually strengthening at all, just stressful and annoying. I don't recommend!!!

This class was horrid. The exams made you remember menial details from the 30+ videos we had to watch. There was a lot of busy work that wasn't meaningful at all. This makes me hate religion courses and I am so blessed to be done with those. Frank was fine but offered no support. The exams are proctored and closed everything.

Amazing canvas organization, very consistent and easy to follow. Lots to read and watch, but you can honestly get by without doing all of it if needed. I feel like all the assignments were actually pretty meaningful and I felt the spirit a lot even though it was online. If you want to be successful on exams, do the reviews they are a game changer

Professor Judd's RELA211 class has its pros and cons. While the lectures can feel like a lot of unnecessary information, engaging with the material and using study aids like Unstuckstudy can help you succeed. Overall, it's a challenging but manageable course if you stay on top of the work.

Professor Judd is an excellent professor. I came to every class excited, and left every class fascinated by new things that I had learned. He is very clearly an expert on the subject matter, and fits so much good information into his lectures.

Brother Judd is the best! Everyone should take a class from him. He knows so much about the Bible, and taught the stories and principles in a way that helped us learn for ourselves. Homework is manageable if you put in the time to make it meaningful rather than just doing the assignment. That's the whole purpose of his reading assignments.

I understand the frustration about the workload, it is a lot, but if you commit to it you learn So much and the tests really aren't hard at all. Professor Judd is so kind and so smart and is willing to help outside of class, kindest soul with such a fun class

tbh this class sucked! yeah I did well on his tests but I had to work hard for that grade. so much reading and on top of that just so many quotes we had to memorize. I took this class last spring so everything is really fast paced but doesn't hide the fact that he is a bad professor. refrain from taking his class and please find a better professor.

class was disappointing. not very spiritually engaging and didn't grow my testimony at all. felt like I was just constantly studying the tiniest details for the exams and wasn't fun at all. hated the additional general conference talks/ videos he assigned and on top of that reading from the New Testament. memorized a bunch of stupid quotes

Professor Judd is a very smart man and you will learn a TON. I learned so much about the New Testament and he was able to effectively explain the history, background, and context of the Espistles of Paul and the Book of Revelation.

This class was HARD in the online format. I would take it in person if you want to take it from Brother Judd. The tests were super difficult, and we weren't given answers to the homework guides so we could have been answering incorrectly. It was open note, which was nice. I think I would have done better and enjoyed it more in person.

Get ready to take notes in the class period and make sure to attend every lecture, would help you a lot. Also, answer the study guide questions, it's very helpful. Had a great time despite I took this class in the spring term.

Professor Judd's class was fairly enjoyable. I learned a lot from his class and although there were a lot of reading assignments it helped me expand my knowledge on topics I had questions about. He truly cares for the students and wants everyone to succeed.

I honestly don't get why there are so many negative reviews. If you struggled that much in this class, it was due to a lack of effort. He gives you the answers to all test/quiz questions as long as you fill out the study guides as you do the readings. He was such a passionate professor and I learned so much from this class!

first, the excessive handouts he had us read within a short period of time is truly unnecessary. Brother Judd tests our knowledge on the most minuscule and mundane facts and we don't even know if they are true. this class felt like a waste of time.

Great class. You can use study guide, scriptures and notes on tests (but can't google!). You have to go to very class or will be docked points. He is very fast to answer emails and knows a TON about the scriptures. Respectful of time. Wants students to do well. Reading will save your grade. Don't do the reading and you won't do well.

Judd utilizes an abundance of extra reading handouts that are mandatory for this class which is completely unnecessary. For example, he had the class read 4 handouts within 1 week, and each were 6 pages long. His lectures are definitely a hassle because he includes information that aren't on the study guides. Judd is very entitled and condescending

lazy professor. majority of his lectures are just long quotes from past prophets and seers and revelators. lots of unnecessary information is being taught in his lectures that don't wind up on exams yet he expects us to remember every minuscule and mundane details of the Bible. disappointing class.

Judd goes on these relentless tangents during his lectures and there are just a plethora of information we don't need to know. specifically, most quotes he uses in his lectures are insignificant and majority of his lectures are his ideologies and personal testimony about specific topics that we need to know and understand. anywho good luck to ya'll

Judd preaches only about his own doctrines/opinions. he regurgitates worthless facts that don't focus on spirituality. absolutely boring professor and lectures are not engaging. so much worthless information you have to remember. dreadful class.

SO MUCH REDUNDANCY!!! would not recommend his class so much supplemental reading that does not pertain to the New Testament, there are so many quotes we have to remember, and on top of that we need to know the chapters well along with information he provides during lectures. genuinely hate and dread this class. simply awful.

don't listen to reviews below. brother Judd takes his class very seriously. everything feels unorganized and you'll get caught up in the minutiae of details that aren't very helpful for you to succeed on exams and quizzes.

he's great don't get me wrong but it feels more like a history class. not spiritually enlightening just feels like there are a lot of minuscule details/facts he quizzes us on. I found it redundant that he made attendance mandatory, don't really see the point of that. lots of reading btw and his lectures sometimes don't reflect the reading

I loved the structure of Professor Judd's class! Weekly quizzes based on readings, additional your choice activities, and exams were all your grade were comprised of. Attendance is required, but if you pay attention to lectures you can easily get a good grade. I also loved the cool insights that he provided about the New Testament and Jesus Christ.

I love Bro Judd. The way to succeed in his class is clearly and plainly outlined at the start of the course, and he gives reminders and tips all the time. The only way you will not succeed in his class is if you don't put in any effort. His lectures are intellectually and spiritually engaging, and I definitely plan to take a class from him again.

Brother Judd was an AMAZING professor and I would recommend taking this new testament class especially during Winter bc it was so meaningful learning about the life of Jesus through the Gospels right before Easter. He is very well organized and has LS laid out very nicely that it was very helpful to stay on top of things. Would very much recommend!

Amazing Professor, easy A. The readings were very engaging and the study guides helped to make them rewarding. The grading is clear and tests were open note entirely from the study guides. Brother Judd is extremely knowledgeable and an excellent lecturer. This is a class everyone should take.

Pretty solid for a religion class. Attendance matters, so come take notes and do your readings. Quiz every week, three tests, no papers. Not hard to get an A, but not as easy as some classes. Lecture is always interesting, but the test seem to kinda be all over the place on content.

Make sure to take good notes during class (quotes, scriptures to remember, etc) and you'll have all the answers you need for the quizzes and exams. The quizzes are short and easy, the exams are 100 questions long and you have 90 minutes to answer them, open book and open notes. He's a great guy, especially with his mask off, I loved him so so much.

Brother Judd represents the best of BYU. He cares deeply for his students and their learning, having them read the entire scripture (in this case, the 2nd half of the NT), but has instructive study guides and extremely clear expectations and grading criteria. He does NOT test you on his opinions of scripture. Very forward-thinking about faith.

Professor Judd is AMAZING! His lectures are incredibly insightful and fascinating, it seems like I learned something new every class.  The tests are open-note, although they are timed so you still need to study.  Sometimes the homework can feel like a lot, but just answer weekly study-guide questions and you'll be set.

Pretty easy class. A bit time consuming, a 2 - 3 hours outside of class a week. But if you do the study guides and take really good notes during class (Just write down everything he says) the exams are easy. Exams are open note, open scripture, but good class notes are gonna be your best friend. he gives you 2 absences without penalty.
Everything is open note, so just fill out the study guides and you will get an A in the class! He really knows his stuff and has spent a lot of time in Jerusalem, so it is fun to hear him lecture

Brother Judd is awesome! I was nervous at first to take this New Testament class but Brother Judd has made a hard subject seem simple and approachable. Brother Judd gives the students EVERYTHING they need to succeed in his class, just be ready to read and fill out some questions about what you read and you'll do great.

Prof. Judd's class was quite uninspiring and focused on meaningless and esoteric minutia. This made the material incohesive and difficult to remember. I spent so much time filling out the study guides, but his interpretation of certain passages were far-fetched and he tested on them!! Also, his timed tests and quizes were WAY too short!

Tests are online, open note+scripture+study guides. Fill them out, take notes in class, you will be prepared. He tells you a lot of what will be on the test from lectures+ what you don't need to write down. Write down his quotes, a lot of them are on the exams! 7 min quiz weekly quiz on study guide + class lecture. Learned so much and felt spirit!

Super straightforward class. Just weekly quizzes and the exams, NO PAPERS. The information was interesting; Brother Judd can just be a bit dry at times. However, he is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. Do the study guides, take good notes, and it's a super easy A.

Professor Judd is awesome! He dives into the history surrounding scripture in order to better understand the scriptures and their context. He discusses questions about the scriptures, explains the history, and provides several interpretations. Do the homework and take good notes in class and you'll do fine.

If you do the work, you'll get an A. It'll be about 2-4 hours a week not including 2 hours of lectures, but all the tests are easy if you've done the readings and study guides and gone to class. Amazing person, very understanding and there was an issue that came up during class that he dealt with extremely well and kindly, would recommend

I honestly took this class because New Testament with Brother Judd was my mom's favorite class when she was here, and I did not regret it. He does a good job of teaching the historical and cultural context of the New Testament, and it was super interesting AND spiritual. Just do the study guides, and the tests will be easy - takes 3 hrs/week max.

Professor Judd gives interesting lectures and overall I enjoyed the class. Sometimes, he'll rant about political stuff for a bit and make you watch the lectures online, but for the most part it was good.

Professor Judd is probably one of the best options for a religion class. All quizzes, midterms, and final are open book and questions are based off a study guide he gives you. If you do the study guide you will get an A. I spent about 2-3 hours on this per week. Pay attention to quotes in class, as he frequently tests on their teachings. Nice guy.

If you stay up with the weekly study guides (which took me about an hour a week) and take good notes you will do great. His exams are open book and you don't have to write any papers. I liked that this class was very in the scriptures and was very clear cut. Lectures could be boring but overall a good choice.
Brother Judd's class was very interesting and enlightening. I learned a lot about Acts through Revelation. His tests were kinda stressful though and pretty hard. Overall, I really enjoyed the class.

Worst professor I have ever had. I do not normally write reviews, but I reached out to him at the beginning to notify him of a sensitive issue, he showed no sympathy at all even though I followed the instructions of the syllabus. The online format is dull and a waste of time. Ive never had a religion class that I've dreaded this much.

Bro. Judd's class was great. He's not exciting or anything, but his class is very much in the scriptures which is why the class is great. Just fill out the study guides and you'll be fine. His tests and quizzes are based off those study guides. It's enough rigor in the class to make you learn, but not hard either. I really like Bro. Judd

His online was straight forward and no nonsense. No papers or reading logs. Just a quiz once a week and midterm and final. Quizzes and tests were timed because of online (very short time limit, less than a minute a question). They seem scary but all the answers are from the guides and the handouts. Good choice for a religion, interesting class.

I was honestly scared for what the class might be like after the first day, but Bro. Judd turned out to be very reasonable. Do the study guide, take detailed notes, and study them before class and exams, and you should be able to get a good grade. I was pressed for time most weeks and I still managed to do all of this.

Bro. Judd is amazing!! He is one of my favorite professors. Attendance is mandatory, but his lectures just give the test answers away, so pay attention. There is a weekly quiz in class, but as long as you do the study guide you will get 100% because the questions are pulled from there.

Dr. Judd is one of the best professors I have taken at BYU. I've never been a real fan of Religion classes, but this was my favorite. NO HW, ONLY 3 EXAMS & 10 QUIZZES. He gives very clear and concise lectures and makes it very easy to take notes. Just make sure to fill out the study guides (not for a grade) & take good notes and you'll pass.

Brother Judd is very straightforward and prepares you well for the tests, which are multiple choice and based off of study guides and lecture notes. No papers. Occasional in class quizzes over reading material for that day. Only a few chapters and handouts to read for class, with the study guide, very reasonable. Judd wants his students to do well.
He is a good guy, just takes his class too seriously. If you miss class then you are screwed, also study, study, study for tests.

Excellent teacher! Really learned a lot about the context of the New Testament. He keeps people on their toes with random pop quizzes, which with the midterm and final, make up your entire grade. Study hard and you'll get a good grade. Testimony building class.

Professor Judd is an incredible teacher. He is very knowledgeable, and communicates his knowledge very effectively. His class covers both the spiritual and historical aspects of the New Testament. Also, he is very clear and fair about the way he grades. I would definitely recommend taking a class from him!

Brother Judd is very spiritual and comes to class prepared every time. He clearly and concisely explains the doctrine and makes good connections. He only requires two hours of preparation per week, which is fairly low. Just do the reading and study guides and you'll be prepared.

If you have to take New Testament, take it from Bro. Judd. He is definitely the best professor I have ever had! His class is very straight forward, If you do your work you will get an A. There are no tricks. You have to study for his tests, but he doesn't require any extra busywork or projects. You can tell he cares about every student in his class
Bro. Judd is AWESOME! Favorite religion teacher on campus. You must attend class, but Judd makes the lectures enjoyable and inspirational. Takes notes and you'll do fine.

The class is tough and he makes you study for it. He has prep guides which help you on the readings and prepare you for the tests and lectures. He also keeps the lectures entertaining and actually notices individual students performances and wants to improve the entire class.

He is one of the best professors I have ever had! I seriously recommend taking a class with him. What he asks for isn't hard... just do your reading, keep up with the homework, take notes in class and you'll be okay. If you do not do well, his office is always open and I really recommend for you to go see him. I am not LDS and I still love him!

He is an awesome professor. The class is not easy by any means, but he is incredibly clear about his expectations and how to meet those expectations. If you do the study guides before  each class you'll be fine. Make sure to do the reading.

Brother Judd is easily the best religion professor I've ever had. His priority is LEARNING and growth, not grades or busy work. He doesn't require useless essays or any fluff--he carefully teaches the material and then tests on it. Tests are not comprehensive, neither are the quizzes. I definitely suggest him for anyone taking New Testament!

The best religion professor I've had by far. He goes into a lot of detail and gives lots of interesting insights. It's always clear what will be on the tests. He's very organized and stays on topic, which I love. I'll admit it involved a little bit more studying than some other religion classes I've taken, but it was worth it.

I REALLY enjoyed taking this class from Brother Judd. He is VERY up front about all that is expected in his class. If you don't like taking notes or going to class, don't take his class. You have to work to get a good grade but this really helped me to learn more and a good grade is totally possible. He curves tests depending on the classes scores.

Your grade will be based entirely off of tests in Brother Judd's class. He takes attendance but it's not a part of your grade. However, if you don't go to his class you won't pass because he asks very specific questions on his tests, and the only way to know the answers is by going to lecture. I loved him, I learned so much from his class!

Terrible professor. Pushes his own agenda and has no meaningful element to his teaching. Midterms are 80 questions with answer choices A-F (yes, those are just the midterms). DO NOT TAKE him unless you want to be a slave to attendance because of all his pop quizzes. Worst religion professor I've ever had at BYU.

I feel like I learned a lot in this class. I would definitely take it again. Bro Judd is very clear on his expectations and what you need to do to get ready for the tests. He didn't assign a lot of reading, but you had to know everything he assigned really well. He makes you keep track of your own grade instead of posting  them online. Good overall

My name is Jade Julian. Going into this class, I honestly was expecting it to be uninteresting, extremely difficult, and time-consuming. Professor Judd knew the material well, and delivered each lecture with precision, humor, and inspiration. I looked forward to coming to class each week and grew a love for the New Testament.

Bro. Judd takes a VERY academic approach to the New Testament. It was definitely not my type of class because I felt that the material we were covering was close to pointless, and so much of the spiritual depth of the New Testament was set aside. I can't say I felt uplifted or inspired from the class, mostly just annoyed and frustrated.
Judd's class is nice. The tests are kinda strange but the lectures are good and he definitely knows what he's talking about. This is an easy A.

Brother Judd really just wants to help you strengthen your testimony of Christ. He's an amazing and intelligent man. I love him to death! He's so great. He teaches very well, and is never boring. You can tell he cares about his students and loves what he teaches. He really gets into the hardcore doctrine and just really teaches you the material.

These high ratings are a lie.  A dead lie. I promise.  He only gives pop quizzes, and they are hard about random things so even if you have read you will fail.  sucks.  Wouldn't suggest to anyone. What a let down.

Professor expects a lot from the students and as a result you learn a ton!  Really enjoyed Prof. Judd's class and the academic approach that he took, but I don't suggest it if you're looking for an easy A . . . you won't find it.

Absolutely hated this class. I was hoping to learn a lot about the Old Testament. Instead, I we had to read over 20 chapters per day, and then we were quizzed on the absolute most obscure details from the reading. This class was such a waste of time, and I would never suggest it to anyone. I did well, but at the expense of enjoying my OT study.
It was a great class! Each day he keeps the lectures alive and interesting. The tests were a fair assessment of what was taught.
WONDERFUL TEACHER! as long as you take good notes, and do all the readings, you should do quite well. his tests are based a lot off of lecture notes, and story background. overall great expirience!

He's a great, interesting teacher.  Dr. Judd makes you study and take good notes, but tests aren't harder than religion tests should be; at the same time, he's very spiritual and well researched.  Take good notes and study them pretty well and you'll do just fine.  You'll enjoy his lectures too, always great with lots to learn.

A bit of a religion nerd, but nice and fun enough.  Prepares you for his tests very well.  The only trick is to keep up on the reading (highly recommend using his reading guides), and you have to take your own notes from lecture (his powerpoints don't lend themselves to note-taking).  Easy grader, nothing tricky, just stay on top of it for easy A.
This was an excellent class!  You will learn a lot about the New Testament, and the grading is very fair.

Judd gave me a very bad impression at first. He came off like he was running the class like it was 10th grade, what with the attendance policy. But as the semester went on, I actually grew to love the guy. He was a great professor, very clear and to the point, great teaching style. He applied the BOM to help us improve our lives. Definitely takeit.
Really enjoyed his class. As long as you do the reading, the quizes are easy. I'd take another class from him.

Nice guy, but I didn't like his style. I am sure there are far worse rel professors, but I have liked other teachers styles a lot more. He is nice but kinda creeped me out, I'm not gonna lie. Class wasn't too hard, and he was easy to live with overall. He quizzes on the reading about 1 in every 3 classes.

Great teacher. He knows his stuff. He brings up things that I had never thought about the Book of Mormon. Fair teacher. Be sure to go to class!! He has pop quizes, 10 a semester, and drops the lowest grade. A lot of the material on exams are from class lecture.
Great teacher. You NEED to go to class to get any kind of a decent grade.
