He is the best professor his classes are interesting that you learn every day. The only thing you have to do is read the assigment because he gives pop quizes.

Bro Judd has great class lectures.  He doesn't just regurgitate the BOM stories, but he explains some great doctrines that are hard to pick out at first.  Attendence is a must, but if you go, take notes, and read the assigned chapters, an A is cake. 3 tests including the final, and final isn't comprehensive.  No outisde assignments.Great professor!

Amazing class, great teacher. really knows how to both teach and discuss and picks great topics to discuss. throws pop quizes from the daily reading, tests are basically straight from lecture and he lets you know during lecture what he will test you on. no papers or assignments. i will definetely take him for 122.

I enjoyed his class a ton when I took the time to prepare. Do your reading, attend class and take good notes and you will learn a TON and love it.  Bro Judd knows a ton about the scriptures.  He sends scary emails to you if you miss class, so don't miss class! It's as simple as that. This class was well worth the effort. I was sad to see it end.

Bro Judd was a great man, but the main thing that bugged me was I felt when he taught, he always said "You don't need to know this... I want you to know this," etc.  I felt like he was telling us what we needed to know about the BoM, and this bugged just a little

I added this class after the first day, and got a smug email from him explaining that since I missed the first lecture I now had "two abscences"... and that I should carefully "read the attendance policy".  Are you kidding!?  I've been in school long enough to know it's not worth putting up with a prof like that no matter how smart he thinks he is

Amazing teacher. He loves details. He throws pop quizes maybe 75% of the class periods, but if you red the chapters you were supposed to, you'd be fine. The tests are pretty much based off class lectures, so take good notes. I took him last semester and I'm taking him again now because it is so great! Awesome detailed teacher.

Professor Judd is an excellent teacher. I had him for his BOM class for RM's and am taking the second part now. He teaches by the spirit and as long as you DO YOUR READINGS and take GOOD lecture notes you will make an A.
Brother Judd was awesome in covering the material in the Book of Mormon and ensuring the students learned something new.  If you attend class and study the notes and do your reading you'll have an A.

Brother Judd is a great teacher! He makes you want to learn more about the Book of Mormon and knows exactly how to get his ideas across to students. If you go to class, take good notes and love the Book you will get an A. During class he says the things to know for the test! He is an awesome teacher.

I enjoyed his class.  Spark a new interest in the Book of Mormon.  I felt it was an appropriate balance between the spiritual and secular aspects of the Book of Mormon.  Would highly encourage taking this class from him.
Bro. Judd is an excellent and fun teacher. The test reflect what he teaches.

He is a great teacher.  His Lectures were helpful.  I learned answers to questions that i was trying tofind since my mission.  It is a great class as long as you read what you are supposed to and take notes in class the test are a breeze.

Brother Judd is the best teacher I have ever had.  I took it in the spring and didn't have to do any papers or homework.  If you pay attention to what you are reading and take good notes and study those notes before the test you will do just fine.  I highly recommend this class and teacher.

LOVED this class.  Brother Judd is extremely clear and to the point.  Yes, you have to study.  There are daily prep guides you need to use and you definitely need to take detailed notes.  oh and take notes on what you read..the last test is the hardest because it's all about the storyline.

Loved this teacher. He kept me interested and his powerpoint presentations make the class much more engaging and note taking much easier. He covered the material well enough for students to know vast amounts and his tests were all completely multiple choice.

Bro. Judd is my favorite teacher, he's awesome! There are pop quizzes but they're easy if you do the reading. His tests aren't hard as long as you pay attention in class and take good notes. His lecutres are fun and interesting, and you learn a lot. When he's teaching he tells you what's important to know for the tests. Great teacher!

Brother Judd is a great teacher!  His tests come straight from class lecture notes, so study your notes and it's a breeze.  Go to class because he ALWAYS takes roll and you ALWAYS have a quiz at the beginning of lectures.  The quizzes come straight from the reading, but are very detailed (only hard part of the class).  I'd take him again!!!
He's fantastic!  I've learned incredible things, and I love being in class.  He's there to get you through with an A, but more than that he's there to get the information to stick with you.

Great religion professor. Teaches with an academic style and does very well at explaining the New Testament.  The entire grade comes from little pop quizzes (crazy easy if you read) and three tests (non-comprehensive).  No dumb papers! No annoying journal! No pointless 'thought papers'!  He says it's hard, but take good notes and you'll get an A.
He's my favorite religion professor.  You learn so much, even after years in sunday school and other religion classes!  Nice guy, too.

He is my favorite religion teacher so far.  I love his teaching style.  He gives the historical perspective on the New Testament and answered questions I have always had.  Stay in his class, no matter what he says the first day.
teaches in an academic and a historical fashion.  as a new member it was hard to keep up on all the new info. but the ta practically gives you the answers during the review session.

I highly recommend him if you like to learn specific historical ideas and understand how the four gospels work together. He gives random quizzes that are dumb somtimes, but there are no papers, and the tests are pretty easy as long as you take good notes. I really enjoyed the class, however. He's my favorite Rel. teacher so far.
super smart guy, good teacher
I enjoy his class and his lectures very much-very clear and interesting.

Brother Judd is a great teacher.  He isn't the "touchy feely" type of religion professor, so he may not be your type specifically.  He teaches religion in an academic sort of way.  He is very reasonable on his tests and quizzes: you always know what to expect from him.  Great guy, great class, I would definitely take from him again.

Brother Judds clsss is awesome.  I have learned so much from him he knows his stuff and there is no homework or essays you just have to stay caught up in your reading and take good notes and it is a piece of cake.

This class is amazing!  Seriously it's hard, but if you really want to get to know the BOM take it.  I feel like I have learned more in a week of his class then I have my whole life.  YOu actually learn the BOM instead of just the touchy feely stuff you get in church.  If you seriously want to know the BOM take this class

Take notes and class, then study a few hours before the test and you are very likely to get an A.  Everything comes from the notes.  Dont be scared after the first day its not bad at all.  In fact it is my easiest class.

He's a really great teacher.  He really does try to scare you and I think it discourages a lot of people, but if you study hard and take excellent notes, it'll be great!  You learn a lot in this class!

He will try to scare you off on the first day...run!  There are some religion professors that conduct spiritual, uplifting classes (the kind that encourage you to make change) and others who teach facts.  Just facts.  He is a fact kind of man.  I understand this is a personal preference, but choose wisely.
The first day of class he'll try to scare you off; don't drop it. If you take good notes on his lectures, and keep up on the readings, it's a pretty easy class.
pay attention to what he says in class. fairly difficult for a religion profossor

He was great.  The tests are pretty much form the lecture so if you pay attention you'll be fine.  His lectures are fun and he teaches well.   He has no outside homework except for four little readings, there are no papers to write!!

The man is a butcher with in class quizes, tons of them, and without notice too!! the exams are fairly challenging,..but what will kill you off will be the quizes. I wouldnt recommend it if you wanted your GPA to increase instead of take a severe beating from a REligion class!

He is extremely hard. If you want to fail the class, make sure to take the class from this professor. If you have extra 3-4 hours to spend doing homework for every class period, just go ahead. Make it a good semester or not, the choice is YOURS!
Bro. Judd is an excellent teacher. His class is extremely informative and if you pay attention and take copious notes you will do well. I would highly reccomend taking this class.

Really good teacher.  Knows what he's teaching.  go to class, most of his exams are on class lectures.  Exams are easy if you read the assignments.  He cares for his students.  I recommend him to anyone.

the first day he tried to scare us off, but i have really learned a lot.  he really knows what he is talking about and backs everything up with the scriptures and general authorities.  you really have to keep up on the reading and take good notes if you want to do well on the tests.
He is very knowledgable. Take very very good notes and the tests will be easy. All that is required is to read. He curves too so the class average is a mid B, thats always nice.

He will scare you the first day, but don't be frightened off!  He knows his stuff, and as long as you never get behind in the readings you will do fine.  Remember what you've read and take good notes and the tests are incredibly easy! Amazing Class!!
No Comments
He's so knowledgable! You will learn so much. If you try, his tests are not hard. Make sure you go to every class and do your reading though!

I learned so much new information from this class--some people said it was really hard, but if you study the class notes and do the readings and go to class you'll do fine on the tests.  You can't slack off on readings though

If you are willing to put in the effort, this is a great class.  I had him for BoM and then took him for NT because it was so good.  He will warn you, its a hard class. Its worth it. Very organized and straightforward. Take good notes, use reading guides.

Bro Mac is a sweet person, but rehearsal is a mess. His explanations are confusing and rehearsal doesn't feel productive. Band policies are old-fashioned compared to university guidelines, and the grading isn't transparent. The only reason I come back to band each year is due to section leaders picking up the slack and making fun experiences.

Brother Mac seriously fails as a leader. He does not communicate effectively, does not listen, adheres to outdated school policies, and can be uncompassionate, uncollaborative, uncompromising, and very unapproachable. I've only loved Cougar Band as much as I have because I've kept my distance and have never expected much from him at all.
He is a great director, knows his stuff very well

Look, I'm going to do marching band every year until I graduate, but it doesn't excuse Brother Mac's mannerisms. He leans in too heavy to the "grumpy old man with funny retorts" archetype way too much. As a result he is unprofessional in aspects of his job. There is no method to his madness, but it does not discourage my love for marching band.

Brother Mac is an excellent band director who loves BYU and is quite hilarious. I was in marching band with him and also U-band, and I will say that marching band was much more enjoyable than U-band for me. I felt called out a couple times in U-band, and if you're in the percussion section, there's a lot of sitting around while the winds warm up.
Not very transparent grading but other than that it was a good class. Prepare to live in fear of your grade, you won't know it until the semester ends.

I just don't know if he can even count (musically speaking of course). He can't seem to follow basic conducting patterns or give specific musical feedback on things. He doesn't have a doctorate. I don't feel like I'm receiving good instruction from him. In other ensembles on campus I've had really good communication from directors, but not from him
He is a great music teacher. Had him for marching band, and he did not disappoint. Just make sure to memorize music and represent the university well.

I love Bro. Mac. He is the heart and soul of BYU. If you have the opportunity to meet him or be in his band, do it. I'm a better person now than when I started because of his example and his testimony.

Brother Mac is great! I took marching band from him, and he was super positive and caring even through the tough times of COVID. Like all good band directors, he expected the best from us, but he was understanding and took time to get to know people.
Amazing director.

I never realized how great of a director Brother Mac is until I was in some other ensembles on campus. He's strict on his policies, but if you can respect those, he's honestly a great guy and a fantastic director. He makes class fun while also teaching and pushing you to be a better musician. I've had him for Marching Band, ROC Band, and U-band.
I love Brother Mac! He is an amazing individual and really cares about people. He definitely knows how to run a marching band with how little time we practice.

He was quite possibly the worst director I've ever had. He treated me rudely in a condensing manner over information that he had that was false. Doesn't really care about the quality of the marching band. My high school marching band was better than his college marching band by a large margin despite the difference in average individual skill.

Bro. Mac is great to have as a director. He loves sports as much as the rest of us in the Roc band and he does his best to stay up with music trends so we play songs that are popular now. Roc band is super low key and as Bro. Mac always says "It's the best gig on campus."  I would highly recommend auditioning.

Brother Mac is great. He is excellent at helping the band mesh and the music come to life. His piece choices are exciting and fun but not overly technical or difficult.  He is respectful and friendly and funny. He expects a lot from you so be prepared to dig in and play for all you're worth, but to have fun doing it.

Roc Band with Brother Mac is a blast.  If you make it in then chances are you won't need to practice too much to stay on top of the music.  Mostly its just a fun environment where you get to play a whole bunch of great music at basketball games.  It can't get much better than that.    I would highly recommend Roc Band with Brother Mac.

Brother Mac is a fantastic director.  I really enjoyed my time in University Band.  It was a fun environment where we could just have fun playing music together and sounding really good too.  Definitely a good choice for a group where you can have fun, quality, and low stress all in one.

Brother Mac is an amazing director.  He pushes the group of beginners and experts to a high level of performance.  I didn't have to do a lot of outside work.  The pieces he picks are enjoyable and have plenty of variety.  Be prepared for a fun class and some great music.

Brother Mac really cares about quality.  He doesn't tolerate slaking off which is necessary for high quality performance.  He sets you up for success and invests his heart and soul into the show.  Do what is required and you will have a wonderful experience.  Be prepared to work hard and have fun.

I had him for Cougar Marching Band and he is great.  He is very nice and really wants all of his students to succeed.  He gives positive feedback which is really nice.  Marching Band is nothing like a top competing high school band, but it is a great experience.

Brother Mac is like a stern father. I took marching band with him, and I think he and Brother Young make a great team. He's encouraging but definitely not afraid to criticize, which is a good thing for growth. I don't think I personally liked him, but that's up for your decision.

University Band was fun, but I did not like that the practices were held all the way at the stadium.  Brother Mac is a great guy and reminded me a lot of my high school band director who I loved!  The  music selection was great and we really grew as a band throughout the course of the semester.
Bro Mac is incredible. He's just a fantastic teacher and director. Everyone who has a chance to be in his band or take lessons from him is lucky. A true BYU professor - teaches the whole person.

I took personal snare drum lessons from him. Fred is very good at snare drum and understanding music and will teach the basic techniques so clearly that you will be surprised at what you can do. However, I always felt like less of a person and completely intimidated when I went to class. I don't feel that he teaches with love, but rather with fear.

Bro. Mac is the best Marching Band director a player can ask for. He knows what to do to make this band work and sound like "a million bucks"!! He's from the south, so he still has a southern drawl and idioms that are hysterical to listen to. Most importantly though, he ties in the gospel and the spirit into ever rehearsal. Bro. Mac is the best!
Marching band is a great experence and I recomend it to anyone willing to work hard, show up, be musical, and have fun.

I second what the guy below me says.  Marching band with him is fine, but as a percussion teacher - he is indeed, a joke.  A good musician?  Sure.  But he misses lessons without notice and then blames you for it.  In a nutshell, it's about him looking good at your expense.  I would think twice about paying him to teach you music.

This guy is a joke. If you can avoid it, don't take lessons from him. He'll probably miss half of them and then come up with some story about how it's your fault that he wasn't there. He relishes in opportunities to make you feel like the little guy and isn't afraid to make up stories to make you look stupid in front of other people.

Bro. Mac is the best! Marching band is awesome but difficult. You really have to work hard and want to be there and put you heart into it. Lots of rehearsals out in the heat but performing at the football games makes it well worth it! Bro. Mac is a super awesome and loves all his students! He tries to be funny :P Also love his wife she is the best!

Excellent teacher. Maintains high standards but is extremely compassionate. It's rare to find a professor that cares so much about his students, especially when he has so many. A fantastic example of what a BYU professor should be.

"Yippy skippy," Brother Mac is one of the greatest directors ever! He keeps your focus by making things interesting, funny, positive, and challenging. I find myself really wanting to do my best in Marching band and also in University band.

As far as I'm concerned, he should take over music ed.  He knows how to teach.  He's fair, honest, personable, approachable, doesn't get angry.  He truly cares.  You can talk to him about anything.  He makes his classes very enjoyable and challenging(in a good way), but he gets down to business.  If you like to misbehave, you won't like him.
I loved this class.  The director doesn't waste time and his comments are useful.  He's also funny.
University band was awesome!  He really motiviates you, but your grade counts only on attendance.  He is so funny, so the long rehearsals aren't bad.  Bro. Mac. is totally awesome!
University band was a great class--very easy but fun.  Bro. Mac is awesome--he's a great musician and teacher whose class I definitely recommend.
Great teacher, good guy that seems sincerely interested in his students.

Fred is probably my favorite professer here at the Y. He is so much fun, and he makes the pep band even better. BTW, pep band is the best. you get money, you play fun music, and you get to go to the basketball games for free. But Fred is so awesome, just a pleasure to work with

Very nice professor, really cares about the gospel. Tests however are super difficult and do not reflect the lectures in class. To me it felt more like listening to his testimony meeting everyday rather than prepping for the test. Super specific questions like “when are where was the first bishops meeting”.

A reminder for Dr. Woods President Clark said: “You are not expected to advance new theories, to give private interpretations, nor to clarify the mysteries” I don't want to hear your personal opinions as doctrines!  theories

This profesor made my life hell. His classes are chaos and lack structure. Twice, he skipped teaching lessons. Once, we had to attend a school event and submit a report on that instead of having the lecture, yet he still included questions in the final from those skipped lessons. Do yourself a favor and never take a class with him-you'll regret it.

Great guy, but don't take this class from him if you can help it. His lectures are nice and chill, so I expected his tests to be the same. His tests were misleading, nitpicky, and incredibly difficult. He asked questions about things we never went over in class. Memorize his slides and you'll be ok. He added a curve because everyone was suffering.

Amazing professor! He learns every single one of his students' names! Lectures can be a bit confusing (for test purposes) but he gives a good review before the test which tells you what you should know. He is very passionate about the material and is funny! Very easy and manageable classwork. If you take his class, make sure to just enjoy it!

It's a history class, not as much religion as I hoped. There was doctrine, but only a small percentage. He was very passionate about it and wanted to share that fire with all of us. He has some ideas that don't seem perfectly cannon, but end up on the test so pay attention to what he shares in the lectures. He has test-ables for every lesson
Called me after class was over to confirm if I had actually attended or not. A bit strange. Rarely ever finished his PowerPoint lectures in class. I had to go back and read them.

You're in charge of submitting tests on learning suite of your attendance, if you forget than you're screwed. I'm not passing even tho I was at every single class, I just forgot to mark my attendance. Lectures have very little to do with the actual exam, on the bright side, there's only two exams. Super sweet dude, poor set up of class

He is a sweet man and He loves his students and what he does. The only downside is that his tests are heavily focused on lecture material and it is hard to know what to study because a lot of it isn't in the powerpoint or reading! Other than that he is great!

Dr. Cardon is a great professor. The class is set up in a number system to encourage learning and take some stress off learning. At first, I hated it. But now I love it. There are 2 exams. No final. One huge, semester long project but if you stay on track and get help from the TAs you will be fine. I learned so much in the class and LOVED it!!

Dr. Cardon wants you to be focused on learning the material, rather than just testing on it. He grades his class uniquely that allows you to be more involved in the learning process instead of stressed about your grade percentage. The concepts are tricky, but he takes good time to answer questions and resolve concerns.

Dr. Cardon is very passionate about what he teaches. His grading style is a little bit different but in the end I felt like I learned SO much more than I have in other classes. He really encourages being curious and wanting to learn. His lectures did drag a little bit, because he takes so much time to answer student's questions. Highly Recommend!

I loved this class!! You can tell Dr. Cardon cares so much about his students and really wants us to succeed. I personally liked the different grading system and how it emphasized practice and understanding. My only complaint was that he sometimes spent so long answering questions and we'd get behind, but I don't have any more complaints! Loved it!

I really enjoyed this class and thought it was interesting! I have mixed views on the grading system. The tests were difficult but you will be fine if you go to the TA reviews. The semester-long project was not bad but make sure to keep on top of it and not fall behind. Professor Cardon is a really nice guy and genuinely wants you to succeed.

Dr. Cardon was an incredible professor! He really knows his stuff and works hard to explain difficult concepts to us. Studying for the exams was hard, but the TA reviews helped. He has a couple big projects that were hard, but as long as you don't procrastinate them, you'll be ok! He's also secretly hilarious...

I took this class when it was his first time teaching it at BYU. He is such a great teacher and explains things so well! There was a bit of confusion about expectations for our project, but mostly because it was the trial run. He was very understanding and adjusted throughout the year to make sure we had every chance to succeed

Fun and passionate guy, however the midterm and final both had two parts-- in class coding and testing center test. The final was not even testing what we learned and made us code up something we had no experience with. Did not even test what we learned and is worth 20% of our grade. Would get docked for the smallest things on homeworks.

I took Page's UNIV 101 class, and it was great! He cared greatly about his students and made sure we all felt welcome in his class. If you have an undeclared major, get ready for him to try to get you to do statistics, haha.
Dr. Page is awesome! I enjoyed this class more than any of the other ones I had taken at BYU. He is a great professor and is always available to meet to go over anything that you need help with

Dr Page is a really solid professor. Very passionate about Bayesian statistics, so I recommend taking this class from him. Class itself isn't too hard, however the tests can be tricky and they count for a lot of your grade. Attendance was only counted some days when there were in-class quizzes.

Dr. Page is a fun teacher to learn from. He is quirky but he is always availible for his students and will go out of his way to make time for your questions. The class is hard and his teaching style is going through and annotating slides. He is generallyy accomidating for his students and puts them first.

Professor Page is the best! He explained all the concepts simply and really cared about his students' success in the class. The exams are straightforward and easy if you understand the homework. He doesn't accept any late homework though so don't fall behind.

This was Dr. Page's first year teaching this Capstone class. In the class, you are paired with a company and work with them to analyze data and build an ML model. The class itself was tedious at times because of our internship company, but Dr. Page helped us a lot. He is very understanding and overall the class was great for the experience!

Dr. Page is super likeable and funny but Stat 121 is Stat 121. Its pretty standard across the department so there's that. He gives you the tools you need to succeed. Not so hard if you pay attention, that's just the challenge, because its boring. He's patient and pretty cool. Recommend him if you have to take this anyways.

Dr. Page is funny and very personable. He is SMART, I felt like an intro stats class was beyond his ability to teach simply sometimes. he kinda went off on tangents and had trouble explaining certain things but was awesome regardless. the class is very striaghtforward in expectations and there's lots of help. easy for upperclassmen, hard for fresh

I loved Professor Page! He was super relatable, engaging, and overall a super engaging teacher. Coming to class was something I looked forward to, and you could tell he really cared about stats, and also the students.

he can be really funny but honestly not super great at explaining things. i thought this class started off super easy but got really tough lol. i think i could've gotten a much better grade if the power points didn't suck and professor page actually knew how to thoroughly explain things.
He doesn't quite understand students' questions so the TA comes in handy during lectures. If you review the slides and take the practice quizzes you'll do fine. He can be funny.

I really enjoyed Dr. Page. He's super friendly and approachable. I didn't enjoy stats very much, but Dr. Page made it fun. He does go on side tangents quite a bit, but he makes things easy to understand. Tests are like 70% of your grade.
Page is great. Stats is horrible. He's a cool guy, but the class is obnoxiously difficult

I love Garritt Page as a person and he was actually a pretty great professor but Stats is HARD! And the department makes him speed through lessons, but every teacher will do that. Prof. Page is so sweet and funny and he is super willing to help outside of class. Take from him, but be ready to study for this class its a tough course.

Dr. Page is an amazing professor. You know exactly what to do to pass the class. The course is extremely organized and there are recorded lectures that are accessible on learning suite in case you miss class. Dr. Page is funny and always willing to answer questions. Also, tere is an online textbook you can buy but I never used it.
Awesome guy. Classes can get pretty boring.

Class is extra credit. Not a focused lecturer. He is nice, but there is no way he is easier or better because its a department class. He also skips the questions that give you extra credit - so he hurts more than helps. Take it from Lynne Nielsen so you have a professor that actually knows what the slides talk about and what the test will look like

Stats is complicated & Dr. Page is alright at teaching it. He's hilarious but often got off track, resulting in playing "catch-up" all semester. It felt rushed but Dr. Page tried to make the principles clear. He's very easy to approach and wants everyone succeed. Get ready to put in some effort, a good grade won't come easy. Use the TA lab!

Statistics can be a tricky subject, but Dr. Page teaches it well and does his best to understand where the students are at. If you're worried about taking statistics, Dr. Page is a great teacher, but you might still struggle because it is a difficult subject. But I would recommend Dr. Page!

Dr. Page is an awesome professor. He is very engaging and answers questions when you are confused. The test are fairly difficult and there is a good amount of outside work. Overall, would definitely recommend taking this class.

If you are bad at math, take this professor! He is the best math teacher I have ever had by a long shot. Makes things so easy to understand and takes his time making sure you've got it in class before moving on. Go to class and keep up with the reading, and you'll do well. So understanding and easy to follow, takes care of his students. Loved it.

Dr. Page is a really good prof. My only complaint is that we had a group project and two finals due during finals week, which makes up 50% of your grade. So you'll end the semester not knowing what 50% of your grade is, but if you pay attention in class you should do fine.

He's super nice, and very willing to help if you go to office hours. He explains everything thoroughly if you have a question, and homeworks aren't too bad. He gives quizzes occasionally during class, but he drops some of them. Homework is more application, quizzes/tests more conceptual. One group project.

I liked Dr. Page, but hate stats. I think there's a lot about how the class is set up that didnt mesh with my learning style, but it wasn't Dr. Page's fault so much as a department thing. He cares a lot and is super willing to help if you need it. which you probably will because stats sucks.

Super funny and he knows his stuff. He's willing to answer any questions you have. Stats from every professor will be graded the same, but he was fun to take it from. I enjoyed stats because of him. The tests weren't that hard if you just payed attention in class and do the quizzes. I would definitely take stats 121 from him again!!

I love Dr. Page! All of the STAT 121 professors follow the same syllabus and class notes, so it really doesn't matter homework wise who you get. I liked Dr. Page because he was entertaining, but also was always willing to answer questions and he wouldn't move on until we understood the concept. there are in class attendance quizzes for extra credit

Overall a good teacher! He has good explanations, sometimes I learn more from the TAs but he is really helpful when you have questions. There are at least 3 assignments every week but they're usually easy and quick.

Garritt's humor is what keeps me focused in class. It's a Stats class. It's hard. I definitely felt like I learned more from his TAs than his lectures, but I have a very hard time paying attention when the classroom size is large. Not an amazing class, but you'll be just fine if you take it from Garrit.

Prof. Page is a funny guy. Weekly homework assignments, quizzes, but at least he tells you when they'll be. Lots of mathematical derivations for conjugate priors but he walks us through them a few times. And finally a project that's not too bad and you get to pick the subject. Not an easy class but not a hard one either.

Page is the best! I learned more in his first class than I did my entire time in 123. He made everything seem so simple: simulation studies, Monte Carlo, bootstrapping, permutations, and web scraping. Definitely my favorite class in the major. The take-home tests are pretty difficult, but if you get stuck, he gives hints.

I was dreading stat223 because of my terrible experience in stat123. Luckily, the class is not at all the same. Dr. Page is very good at explaining the concepts in class, but tests and homework are not exactly the same as the examples he gives to explain. To do well, you need to understand the concepts, not just copy and paste the code from class.

I enjoyed having Dr. Page. I have very little coding practice & I was able to get help from him & the TAs for the HW & only from him on the examsonly a midterm & final!(: Not picky with grading on HW. He was VERY responsive & accessible to help & was very sympathetic. I would take this class from him again. Con: takes forever to update grades.

It's a really practical class, and it's pass/fail. The whole point of the course is to build your skill set in SQL and R. Really useful if you're planning on doing anything related to data/analytics kind of work. Class is a little disorganized, but fun. Most of the class is putting your project together, which you present at the end. Great class

Dr. Page is amazing. He is very open to helping you if you struggle. He generally responds quickly to emails and is really understanding. He is a clear teacher. Teaching R programming is not easy, but he does a really good job at breaking it down and making it easy to understand.  I highly recommend him!

I liked Gary's class alright but he is a very tough grader. Even if you create some great pieces there is always something he will nitpick. I understand that it is to make us better but because there is not a way to revise the projects without doing them all over again, I wish he would give us the feedback and grade a bit easier.

Professor Fuller is a great professor that has a deep knowledge and passion about what he teaches. I learned a lot of fascinating things in this class. He is super kind, willing and able to work with students. Assignments are really easy and if you've done the readings and are familiar with them you will do well in this class and in the tests

I took this class for fun and I was not disappointed. Most of your grade comes from the pre-class reading reflections, which are really short and easy. I found the projects engaging and the lectures interesting. If you turn in the assignments, you're pretty much guaranteed a good grade.

Both professor and students are very into J.R.R. Tolkien, so if that's not your thing don't take this class. There is a lot of reading and lectures are very participation heavy. There is a mid term and final, the exams are long and difficult. There are two reading responses a week that are short and easy. He is a really nice guy.

I loved Professor Fuller! He was insipirational in his class on literature by J.R.R. Tolkien. I learned so much. If you go to class and pay attention and take notes, you should be decently set up to do well. It was so fun that I loced doing all the hw and projects for it!

There are two versions of this class: Tolkien and Medieval British Lit. I took Tolkien last semester and now I'm taking the other one because I had so much fun. It's a deep dive into the material with Professor Fuller. He is very knowledgeable and made 3 hour classes seem short. Plus we watch all of the LOTR movies (extended editions, obviously).

My version of ENG236 was about Medieval British Lit, and it was actually so much fun! The class is really chill, and the discussions are super interesting. Sometimes Prof. Fuller would get a bit sidetracked, but I feel like I've learned a ton. The coursework isn't hard, but the readings are sometimes a bit long, so plan your time accordingly.

This is my favorite class I have taken. Professor Fuller genuinely cares so much about his students and his lectures are so entertaining. Class is a giant discussion each week that he guides and helps you understand the material even more and the symbolism in each text. Really fun break from regular college classes- this class is genuinely so fun!
Took Technical Communication from him a great class to knock of the Advanced Writing GE

I took this class last semester but I would highly recommend to any student that wants to knock out their letters credit and is a big fan of Tolkien. There is a lot of reading (70-100 pages a day) but Prof. Fullers lectures are extremely interesting and engaging. We also watched all of the LoTR movies as well which was fun.

Lots of well-organized reading, fantastic lectures and discussions, and new, mind-opening information. "J.R.R. Tolkien: Myth Maker and Sub-Creator" with Professor Fuller changed my life. He knows his stuff, and provided a framework to better understand Tolkien and his works. I have never before cried at the end of a course, nor written a review.

Professor Fuller is great! You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches. The readings arent too extensive and he doesnt grade harshly, and he gives you exactly what you need to know for the midterm and final. Hes all around a really nice guy!!!

I really enjoyed Professor Fullers class! He is really passionate about the subject and knows a lot about it. His tests are pretty tough and require a lot of studying, but he tells you exactly what is going to be on it. As long as you go to class and do the reading, you'll be fine!

Gary Fuller is nice, his class, however, is not. The midterm and final were completely out there and I was not prepared for it. He is really excited about the subject but he doesn't do well at explaining some topics. The class was way too hard from what it needed to be and he took forever to grade literally anything.

Professor Fuller is a nice guy, but his class is way harder than it needs to be. His midterm was awful, and he didnt prepare us for it. There was no study guide and the test was not what he said it would be. Hes very passionate about British literary history, but class is hard to follow and you dont learn much. Good guy, not a great teacher.

Very good and caring teacher. Makes you feel like he truly cares about your life and the other stresses you have. He brought candy every week and brought pizza and soda for the final. Awesome teacher.

Very laid back professor, INCREDIBLY kind and you can tell he's just a naturally Christlike person and teacher. SO willing to go out of his way to help you out if you miss assignments or something doesn't make sense to you. Easy A if you go to class and complete the work, although much of the class was discussion-based.

Very good and caring teacher. Makes you feel like he truly cares about your life and the other stresses you have. He brought candy every week and brought pizza and soda for the final. Awesome teacher.

Very laid back professor, INCREDIBLY kind and you can tell he's just a naturally Christlike person and teacher. SO willing to go out of his way to help you out if you miss assignments or something doesn't make sense to you. Easy A if you go to class and complete the work, although much of the class was discussion-based.

She is very merciful, and understanding, but don't rely on that alone. It wasn't the easiest for me to understand, but she was very helpful whenever I had any questions or concerns. Make sure to pay attention in class to what she says exactly.

Truly the worst professor I've had. How you can talk for three hours straight and think that your students will get anything out of it? Her LearningSuite was an absolute mess so we all had to cobble together our best approximation of what we thought or heard she wanted. Her assignment descriptions were completely unhelpful.

Professor Strathearn's REL250 class is challenging but rewarding. The lectures are engaging and bring a strong spiritual component, though the readings and assessments require significant effort. For prep, ChatGPT and unstuck ai were helpful alongside taking thorough notes.

She's fine. 3 tests in the testing center, 1 you have to write short answer questions on paper you must buy at the student store. Tests were really hard. reading quizzes before class. A project you do all semester you can bs though if you are smart enough. I always felt the spirit in lectures, but shes just really hard and expects you to know a lot

She clearly loves the gospel. Her lectures were interesting and she definitely has helped me feel the spirit. But for a 2 credit religion class it was hard. There were TONS of reading assignments. Sometimes would take me 2-3 hours to get through. Quizzes were based on the readings so make sure to not just skim through and take thorough notes.

Dr. Strathearn is a gem; however, this is the hardest religion class I've taken. You will not survive by doing the bare minimum--exams are the toughest religion exams I've taken, and they're worth 60% of your grade. That aside, her lectures were incredible and she is deeply passionate about the Bible. Looking to actually learn? Take from her.

I feel like this class was unnecessarily challenging. She expected us to know the Greek origin of a lot of words, and random facts. There was a lot of reading for this class. The tests were challenging and although she provided a study guide, a lot of the topics were only covered for a minute or two in class. She is very knowledgeable.

she always goes over time. she is very passionate about what she teaches, but the tests and quizzes are too fact-based rather than spiritual. exam questions are very specific and were vaguely discussed in class. PowerPoints and study guides can be a mess and not in order.

Sister Strathearn is super super awesome. I loved going to her lectures and she seriously knows her stuff. Not only does she know it but she feels it and cares about helping us feel the power of God's word. The reading was a lot but definitely doable.

The class was interesting BUT, in general I felt that the readings, quizzes, and tests were all very hard and not related to spiritual things but more to random facts and technical things. Not the reason I take religion courses. Look for some other professor to take this class from, even if she is very knowledgeable and a good teacher.

She makes the Old Testament absolutely fascinating. Each class is like when you find an Easter egg in a video game, except with the Bible. It's a stretch, but that's how it is. You'll do a lot of reading and rote memorization. You do the study guides as you complete her class and you'll be fine.

Dr Strathearn is my favorite religion teacher to date. Although her class isn't "easy" I never felt like she was trying to make it harder than it needed to be. She made sure to bring the spirit every class and I actually felt like I learned things that could help me personally. There is a lot of reading but it was worth it.

I Loved Sis. Strathern! I felt the Sirit very frequently, and loved learning from her endless supply of knowledge. She made the people in the New testament seem so real and like I could really relate to them!

She is a spiritual and powerful lecturer with great insights. However, the class is structured poorly. The slides are old compared to what she presents, with different names as what she refers them to. They also have little detail compared to the info on the tests so it is lecture heavy but her tests don't seemed to be made specific to each year.

To be fair, I thought that she was very good at TEACHING the gospel. I was always inspired by her testimony, and I appreciated that. However (and maybe this was just cause it was my sophomore year) I felt like the class was a little hard and stressful. I would have at least liked to see the answers to quizzes, but those were hidden even afterward.

Sometimes the instructions for assignments can seem a little vague, but if you ask for details she'll give them to you. She cares about the students and has a strong testimony of the Gospel that comes out in her lectures.

Sister Strathearn cares! It is clear that she has devoted her life to the gospel and the study there of. She personally reached out to me to have one on one discussions. Hard class but I have learned a lot and become a better person through this class. Thank you Sis Strathearn!

She gives amazing lectures and you will learn so much about the New Testament in this class. However, her tests are extremely difficult. Instead of testing you on the doctrine, she tests your knowledge of where to find specific scriptures in the New Testament. You will have to memorize hundreds of scriptures. Learned a lot, but don't take for grade

I have had several experiences with religion professors where it seems to stray from spiritual to analysis of translations and history. She actually did a great job of making it a spiritual class while also teaching a lot about the context.

I loved Sis Strathearn! There's tons of reading, and tough reading quizzes but her lectures were amazing. I've never felt the spirit as much in any other religion class that hers. Her test study guides require a lot of work, but if you do them, the tests are pretty easy. She expects a lot of you, but it all pays off because her lectures are great!

Knows her stuff, and the exams are pretty fair, plus, the study guides are good. However, for a basic religion requirement class, she makes it seem more like a graduate class, or at least something you would encounter farther into a religion major. Some of the readings seem irrelevant (they probably aren't in her sight, but for an average student)
Tests and quizzes especially ask the most insignificant and trivial questions. The type of class that gives a bad name for required religion credits.

Sister Strathearn is an exceptional teacher. She is very passionate and knowledgeable about what she teaches. She brings the spirit in with her testimony and lectures. You will learn a lot in this class. You need to take notes and you will need to read, if you do these things you will do fine grade wise. You cannot slack in this class.

She loves all things New Testament. Make sure you take /really/ good notes and if you're more of a private type you will definitely want to make friends so that you have people to study with. She would never sway or round or let you make an assignment up, so stay on your A-game at all times. Strathearn is a professor who really wants you to learn.

I loved Sister Strathearns class. I wish I would have taken it sooner in my college career so I could take more courses from her! She is an amazing teacher. Her class isn't unreasonably hard, but she does make you work for your grade. If you come to class, listen and take notes, you will do well and learn a lot.

Seriously, don't take this class if you're looking for a happy spiritual religion class.  She is so intelligent, but the class and readings are so detailed and she is not terribly sympathetic towards her students.  Memorize the syllabus though and you should be ok.

Sister Strathearn is amazing. The class isn't overly easy (it shouldn't be), but it's nothing more than you'd expect from a religion class. She brings a perfect blend of academic content with spiritual content that is hard to find elsewhere. Take this class if you want to learn and build your testimony.

She is the most Bible knowledgeable teacher I have ever had and she helped me understand the New Testament in a very testimony strengthening way. (super awesome) But... The tests were insane, and what killed me is that she opened up the LearningSuite quizzes and homework points just one day before class time and the homework was a nightmare.

I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS CLASS  TO ANYONE. Yes, it is difficult, but not ridiculously so and if you do the (extensive but interesting) readings and take notes you will do just fine. Even if I had gotten a bad grade, I would be grateful I took this class. I learned so much about Christ and discipleship and came out a better person (and learned a TON)

Sister Strathearn knows her bible!! If you are looking for a difficult class, wanting to memorize Greek and Hebrew meanings of words and phrases, and spend all your free time reading 3, 20 page articles per class period and then take a quiz every time, looking for minute details, not to mention the 3 tests and final, this is the class for you.

I have never taken such a bad religion class. The reading is long and there is a lot of it. There is at least one test a week over the reading, she asks for the smallest details. I found no matter how I studied it was never good enough for her test. The class was more of a bible history class than a religion class. Do NOT recommend!

Sister Strathearn is a baller. She knows an incredible amount and will make you read the scriptures in a way you never have before. She's the best I've seen at making the subject both academically enlightening and spiritually uplifting. It's not the easy A some religion classes are, but follow the study guides and it's very doable to do well.

Gaye is an incredible teacher. She teaches her classes in a way that any student could have a intelligent conversation with a student in Divinity School. You definitely have to pay attention to details for the reading and study well for tests, but it is INFINITELY worth it. RUN to this class.

AVOID: it felt more like a biblical history class than a religion class. She gives more reading than I've ever had in a religion class, then gives impossible weekly quizzes asking for minuscule details. The tests are also ridiculously tricky - harder than any of my other classes. You can study your butt off and get a C.

This class was not easy for me, the reading was long and sometimes confusing. However, the lectures are amazing! I loved going to class! Every time the spirit was there and I learned so much.  The quizzes can be tricky, but she provides great study guides for the tests.

I loved taking this class from her . She changed the way I looked at the New Testament. I love her she is an awesome lady and an awesome teacher. She really know her stuff. She is a strict grader but she is up front about it. Her tests are not easy so make sure to study for them. She does give a study guide and it is comprehensive.

I took Sis. Strathearn's Old Testament class while studying at the Jerusalem center. Best teacher I have ever taken at BYU! Difficult, yes--It's the Old Testament! However, I learned more than I could imagine. Her love and knowledge of the scriptures is evident daily.

Easiest classes at BYU. I have had her for 5 classes. Her reading is light and super easy. Just pay attention to minor details in the reading because she will have an online quiz every week that will cover the reading. Her tests are the EASIEST tests I have had at BYU. Her study guides are exactly what she tests. She is kinda mean though.

Strathearn's lectures were interesting and helpful but the tests are extremely difficult. She tests every little detail, however insignificant, that is covered in class and the readings. Be sure to attend class and do the online quizzes because those make up a large part of the grade.

Honestly, it was a fairly easy class. I only got a B because I skipped a few classes in the middle of the semester and pretty much bombed a test, but that was my fault. Sister Strathearn is such a cool lady, and I learned a lot about the Old Testament.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!! Her class is very difficult and her tests are unfair. Principles taught were often opinionated. She was very unwilling to help me after class. Do not make the mistake of taking it from her way to much time for a 2 credit religion class.

If you are looking to take religion classes because they are mandatory, this is not the class to take.  There is almost no opportunity to ask questions because she's trying to cover more material than is necessary and then you are left puzzled, trying to answer your own question.  She's clear about things, but never goes back to them. Thumbs down.

LOVED THIS CLASS! Hands down one of the best classes I've taken at BYU. She teaches with a perfect combo of the historical side of the Old Testament as well as the spiritual, which I loved. Her tests aren't too bad, and if you go to class and take good notes you'll be fine. HIGHLY recommended!

I had read these other reviews hoping she would change my life. Unfortunately I didn't like her much at all. She micromanages every little thing about the class (like a very strict cell phone and attendance policy). She is passionate about the subject, but almost too much. Her tests are tough too. I'd recommend a different professor.

This woman has CHANGED MY LIFE! I have never been closer to Jesus Christ than I have since I took this class. The absolute perfect blend of secular and religious. Everything she teaches academically she teaches in a light that grows your testimony of Jesus Christ. Take this class.

Sister Strathearn is an exceptional teacher.  I absolutely loved sitting in her class and listening to her talk about the four gospels.  She is this small Australian lady with the biggest heart I have ever seen.  Her love for the life of Christ is truly inspiring.  She will push you, but it will be worth it 100%.  TAKE HER CLASS!
AMAZING professor! She is truly passionate about what she teaches.
She is a very good teacher-engaging and easy to listen to.  Her tests and quizzes are fairly easy.  If you do the reading and journal, this class isn't very difficult.
she is amazing. Her class is difficult, but she's extremely passionate about the subject and is so willing to help you out if you go talk to her. She's interesting and kind

If you really want to learn about the New Testament, take from Sister Strathearn. I gained such an appreciation for the New Testament after I took that class. Tests really aren't that bad if you study for them. Pretty easy class, and you learn a lot.

I Loved Sis. Strathern! I felt the Sirit very frequently, and loved learning from her endless supply of knowledge. She made the people in the New testament seem so real and like I could really relate to them! Take GOOD notes, study, and show up for class. Tests really aren't that bad- just study! You'll be fine

I didn't have much of a problem in the class, I enjoyed it very much.  She explains concepts very well from the New Testament, and points out meaning that I would have never thought of.  Very great teacher, learned a lot.  As long as you study, it's a pretty easy class.

She's tough, but good. I always learned a ton in her classes. She's very strict, but not mean. There are quizzes online and daily participation points you have to enter. Her tests were difficult, but not impossible. She knows a ton about the Old Testament and teaches things that are interesting and spiritually helpful. I really liked her class.

This class is NOT easy, but Sister Strathearn is an amazing teacher. I never cared about the Old Testament until I took her class and now I think it is incredible. Just pay attention, do the review sheets and reading and you'll do well.

I took her for both 211 and 212. I enjoyed her classes a lot. You will need to study in this class; it is not seminary. She expects you to know the Bible as an academic subject. I wish I could take more classes from her.

Most ridiculous class EVER!!!  She cares more about where Paul taught than WHAT he taught.  Only teaches meaningless info and tests you on it.  She also degrades the JST calling it his "opinion" and not scripture.  She says in order to pass a test one MUST study at least 6 hours.  RIDICULOUS!!!  TAKE IT FROM ANYONE ELSE BUT HER!!!!!

She was an amazing professor. She knows so much about the New Testament and I learned so much! I loved her lectures and didn't even need to study for the test because she was so interested in lecture I remembered it all and paid close attention because she was so enthralling. I highly recommend her.

THE BEST class I have ever taken at BYU!Take very good notes, and you will do well on tests. If you are not planning on coming to lectures, just pass-they cover 90% on tests. I loved the class. I thought I knew quite a bit about the NT- I was very wrong! AMAZING! INTERESTING! Worth getting even a C.

One of the best religion courses I have taken at BYU. Sis. Strathearn is a very knowledgeable person and you can learn a lot from her if you take the time. Class was not as demanding as many people make it out to be. If you are lazy and want someone to spoon feed you and give you an A then don't take this class.

This class was interesting in the begining, but nose dived after the first two weeks. There is no clear way to study for the exams, and they are graded in a very one-sided fashion. By the end of the first month I was dragging my feet down the hall.  This class is read/learn the NT outside of class, and get random historical facts in lecture.

She has the most amazing lectures I have ever come across.  Her knowledge of the new testament is amazing. Attendance is important and so are class notes (if you don't take them you won't do well).  I'd put it this way: If you are more interested in getting an A dont take her. If you're more interested in great lectures take her.

I was excited for this class, but Sister Strathearn let me down big time. At one point I pointed out that D&C explains something differently than she explained it. she defended herself by saying it was "just another interpretation". I hate being taught false doctrine.. and sometimes I left this class feeling sick bc of it. I wouldn't take it again.

I thought she was an amazing teacher.  Online quizzes fairly easy if you carefully do the reading assignments.  Her tests are very straight forward and easy if you pay attention and take good notes in class.  One application paper, also very easy if you put some thought into it.  I would highly recommend her new testament class.

This class was okay. I didn't learn tons, but it was a decent class. The tests were a pain and tested a mix of random details and the stuff she added on in class. It's easy to get a B very hard to get an A. She does NOT have an extensive knowledge of Hebrew. Doesn't provide much to help prepare for tests. Not a bad class overall, though.

This woman knows how to bring the spirit into her classroom. If you go to class, do your reading, and take good notes you'll do fine; you can definitely get an A if you do the work. Her extensive knowledge of hebrew makes the class super interesting.  If you want an increased resolve to live the gospel, this course is highly recommended!

Sis. Strathearn knows her stuff. Her knowledge of the subject makes the class almost worth it (too much hard work for 2 credits). Really spiritual if you can get past the worrying about her tests. I couldn't believe how difficult she made the tests and how many hours you have to study just to get a B on them. In my opinion, too much for 2 credits.

This was one tough class!  I barely managed to scrape out a decent grade. She is passionate about what she teaches, and knows the subject very well. However,her teaching style reflects more of a divinity school approach to the N.T.  There are a few good lectures, but the tests are freakishly difficult.  You will learn, but you will pay a high price

This is a really rich course. It is not an easy class though. Although the class is worthwhile I feel like she asked a a little too much for a 2 credit class. Two weighty papers and 3 tests is not what I expect from a 2 hour religion class...

Great at teaching - clear, interested and shows love for the subject. Great knowledge. The turning point comes during the tests. Essay questions are generally chosen well, but graded arbitrarily. If you know the information but use other wording in your answer than that used in the lecture you will miss points. Great class, but keep this in mind.

No offense to the last reviewer, but stay on for more than one class period and you'll enjoy the class. Extensive knowledge of history and origins and the spirituality to back it up. Tests are nice but essay sections somewhat iffily-graded. Great, warm teacher. Highly recommended.
WAY TOO HARD! Maybe you'll learn a lot but i got scared and dropped it the first day.

By far my favorite Religion Teacher. After taking 211, i had to take 212. The lectures are involved and you have to attend, but it is a rewarding experience. Tests are not difficult to prepare for if you study your class notes and the scriptures.

Detailed tests.  Good teacher for those who are familiar with BOM. Assumes you know story line of BOM. Would be incredibly difficult if from another faith.   Good insights.  I enjoyed her class.  Attendance and reading are part of grade
Sister Strathearn is a great teacher!  If anyone finds her class too hard it is because they don't study.  If you want to learn something about the gospel; take her!

Sis. Strathearn is a really great woman, but her class was poorly organized. She spent tons of time discussing sketchy ideas and unofficial doctrine in class...and the tests didn't cover this information at all! Take ridiculously detailed notes and attend study groups and you'll do okay.

Great teacher.  I would recommend her if you want to learn a lot and are willing to put in some time.  Take good notes.  I took my laptop every lecture and wrote down every little detail and it helped tremendously.  If you listen, take good notes, and pray you should be ok.
This class is a little on the difficult side because the tests are hard, but if you study and take good notes, you'll be fine.  I learned a TON in this class.  I really liked it a lot.

Best Religion teacher I have had in four years at BYU. If you want an easy "A," go attend a seminary class. If you want to study the scriptures how they are meant to be studied-take from her. Just study class notes for tests.

I love her australian accent!  Unfortunatley her class was really hard but I learned so much.  I suppose I would reccomend Auditing her class or take it if you are feeling lucky...or working your butt off.

DO NOT TAKE FROM HER! She is way too hard for a religion class. She is knowledgable.  Some of her lectures are interesting. But she is too hard core.  Her quizzes are hard and her tests are rediculous. You cant prepare for them. She requires you to remember everything. Rel classes should be relatively easy. Definitely not the case here. Do not take

She is very tough, but extremely knowledgable. IF you are interested in understanding the scriptures and not just looking for another seminary class, take her. her class is super hardcore, but not ridiculously so.  I learned more from her than any other religion professor.  her tests are very hard and so are the quizzes, but if you put in the time to study, it's not hard to get an A.  make sure to take meticulous notes.  her lectures are amazing!
Good and Spiritual teacher.  I still use notes from her class for hometeaching lessons sometimes.  I guess she is hard.

Don't do it! I read the reviews and thought that I could handle it. I did my reading, went to class, took notes on every word she said, and even went to study groups (something I never do). Her tests were insane. There is no reason to put forth that much effort to get a D. She is an interesting teacher though. AUDIT!!!!

Avoid at all costs - simply take another professor.  The course was by no means spiritually uplifting, and the workload required was much greater than 2 credits.  Her quizzes are completely preposterous and ridiculously hard - there is NO NEED for a religion class to be as frustrating as hers was.  I will be retaking the course from another prof.

Hard tests.  She expects a lot out of the you, especially for her application paper.  The paper reminded me of "getting graded on your testimony".  You learn a lot and grow a ton if you apply yourself the way she wants you to.  However, it is more work than a 2 credit hour class is worth.
she is really a funny teacher and kind of goofy on some days. she is very knowledgeable and you learn alot. her tests are semi hard but if you listen in class you can get a b

I loved this teacher!!! This is the best class I have taken at BYU.  She keeps the lectures interesting and only requires outside reading, no papers!!  I would say that her class  isn't too hard if you go to class and take notes.  I would recommend this teacher to anyone!!!!

I was really worried about being in this class at first because of all of the bad reviews, but I ended up LOVING it. I didn't know a whole lot about the NT going in, but I still pulled off an A-. You just need to show up to class, take notes, and just absorb the information she gives you. She makes it intriguing so you actually want to listen!
Hardest religion class on campus, no study guide before tests, too much history to memorize, never taken that class if known the situation early.

I really enjoyed Sister Strathearn's class.  She points out things about the Gospels that I never would have thought of, but which make the scriptures much more interesting.  Though she does teach some history, it is relevant to the course, and she does not test heavily on it.

Horrible class. Read her horrible reviews and thought that I would take her anyway because some said that she was very knowledgable and spiritual. Not true. She does know alot about history and traditions and what not, but not a spiritual teacher.Also requires a 94% for an A. A complete waste of a good subject, take a different teacher please.

This class is hard. I put forth 100% effort, was in class everyday, took great notes, stuided all the time, couldn't get an A. She is very smart, a great tecacher, but the tests do not reflect what you learned! I would suggest auditing this class so you don't get the bad grades.
I didn't like this class at all.  This class is one of the lowest grades I have gotten at BYU.  She teaches more about history than anything.  DID NOT LIKE THIS CLASS OR TEACHER!

She was an AMAZING professor!  Yes, she has her moments, and her sometimes non-standard way about doing things, but she knows so much, and truly strives to teach her students as much as possible.  There was never a dull moment!  Study hard, and it's totally worth it!

Carefully read the scriptures, spend some time with the Bible dictionary, and maybe read some supplemental materials to get a good grade.  She teaches effectively but has a bit of an attitude.  From Australia.  If you care about understanding the 4 gospels, this is a good class.  If you just want an easy "A" and a vague knowledge, don't take it.

My first impression was a bad one.  However, once the class got rolling, I thought she was an amazing teacher.  In fact, I would go as far as to say that she is the best I've had yet at BYU.  She tells it like it is, and yes the tests are hard, but the class is fantastic!  I learned more in this class than any other. Two thumbs up.

Wow...Gaye Strathern is a nutcase!! Her tests are ridiculously hard.  I didn't like her...but maybe you will...you live and you learn right? And what i learned from this class is to never take a class from her again.

I LOVED this class.  She is an amazing teacher and is so knowledgable about the subject.  I learned so much.  There wasn't much reading, so it is easy to get an A on that.  I'd recommend her class very highly!

Difficult class.  She is a decent teacher, very knowledgable, but tests are very detail based on lecture which she flys through.  Take very good notes on everything, everything is fair game.  Details are important.
Boo on this class, this is the only class at BYU that I stopped going to and plan on retaking with another teacher. Seriously, this class is for the zealous.

She is a wonderful teacher. Very smart and full of knowledge of the Bible.  Her tests are killers though.  If you go to class and REALLY pay attention and REALLY study your scriptures hard you will do great.  Personally I would take a lower grade in order to enjoy my class and teacher better though.

Terrible. Very hard tests. If you want to learn history then take this class. If you feel like yout GPA is a little overstated and you want to lower it then this class will help you do that. Worst class I have ever taken.

She's a difficult teacher but teaches a lot. Take this if you want to be very informed but don't care about your grade. There's not a lot of mercy. The amount of knowledge I gained was worth it though. If I told you a doctrine and you could tell me what books it's found in... isn't that learning?

Her tests are overly detail-oriented.  You'll have to take really good notes.  The grading of essay questions isn't an accurate measure of what you should learn (you have to mention 10 of the 13 different points that she THINKS you should write, without telling you what she will test over. She is by far the worst religion teacher I have ever had.  She teaches things that are not even taught in the scriptures or mentioned by any of the bretheren (first presidency, apostles, etc.)  I would never recomend her to anyone.  She is horrible and very cocky too.

Her tests were reasonable, if detailed and secular.  There really is no other way to make a religion test since she can't assess your testimony.  I found the lectures very spiritual and I know I grew a lot because of her class.

She revised her syllabus a million times before the final,which fyi was more of a history test than of doctrine.better know obscure people & places if you want to do well on the final.no scriptures on tests purely memorization/short answer.must memorize pointless lists reviews are a waste of time

If you're looking for an easy BOM teacher, forget this one. You have to work for your grade. The second midterm is a beast too. Her questions are tricky and it is easy to think there are two answers. You must work hard and study at least six hours for the final to get an A, I promise!
Steer clear of this teacher. Reading quizzes are a beast and are weighted as much as the other things in class. Unfair grading. TAKE AT YOUR OWN RISK. Study groups don't even help.

I enjoyed this class a lot. Sister Strathearn is a good teacher who enjoys teaching and gives good insights on the scriptures we read. Her tests are easy if you study for them. This was one of my favorite classes that I took.

Professor Strathearn's tests are full of busy-work questions, like which apostle introduced which apostle to Jesus? Who cares? What historical / religious significance does that have? The answer is none. Her quizzes and tests are both unreasonable and pointless.

I definitely do NOT recommend this teacher. Her "interesting" gospel perspectives are often iffy and not founded on established Church doctrine. I grew to dread her lectures. At the very least, I recommmend you double check her theories before you take them to heart.

Sister Strathern is a good teacher. I learned a very great deal from her. However, I found that her tests did not focus as much upon the learning of spiritual matters, as it was to test our ability to memorize every single point of scripture.

Sis. Strathearn is the most amazing teacher I've ever had.She has such love and understanding of the scriptures that she makes you want to learn more.Her tests aren't bad if you pay attention in class, which is easy, because her classes are amazazing!!

Sister Strathearn is an amazing woman. Very knowledgable. She is slightly uptight, but she is most definately willing to help you out if you ask for it. Tests aren't too bad; just make sure to pay attention in lecture and you'll do fine.
Great reacher, nice lady, cool perspectives and lots of knowledge. Unreasonable tests, though.

I didn't like the class at first because she seemed really uptight and kinda mean. I kinda warmed up to her during the semester and I really like her class now.  The tests are not easy, make sure you take good notes duing her lectures.
Everything's clear, she gives you the answers to her test questions in your note. She really knows what she's talking about.
I did not feel spiritually uplifted by this class.  She graded way too harshly and the tests were unreasonable.  I received my lowest grade thus far from her, but did not feel it was justified.
Great teacher, good perspectives; not the typical busy-work religion class. Her tests are demanding, but its cause you learn so much. She's funny and I always look forward to a class with her.
Very fun and upbeat teacher.  I like her.  She is from Australia, and has an interesting gosple perspective that clashed with a few kids in my class, but I like her a lot.
I liked her she was nice and a good teacher
No Comments
Very knowledgable about Biblical geography and culture. Upbeat & great teacher!

Dr. Ahlborn is a kind professor, albeit a little disorganized in the way he teaches. This was the first time he was teaching this class, so I understand that it wasn't easy to make it flow well, but I didn't get too much out of it. Great guy, though, and I'm sure it's easier to follow his other classes because he's taught them several times.

Professor Ahlborn is incredible and knows his stuff! Class was not too difficult. Only tricky part was he talks very fast and blows through lessons quickly. If you're looking to see if food science, nutrition, deitetics, etc. is for you, this class is a great start. He always brings food to class and certainly welcomes the spirit.

Dr. Ahlborn is awesome and wants you to succeed. He is a little disorganized but he doesn't penalize you because of it. There is a lot of memorizing but he literally tells you what you need to know for the quizzes. The final was super easy. He also brings food to class. Overall fun class, definitely recommend.
Do not fear Gene. He is there to help you succeed. He also brings food and stuff from his garden to class. PS the built bar project is boring and the yogurt project is incredibly taxing.

Dr. Ahlborn is so kind. He cares about his students so much. However, the class was straight memorization. If you're into that sort of thing, the class will be a breeze. If you prefer understanding things and actually applying them instead of regurgitating them on a test, then you'll find this class frustrating.

Prof Ahlborn is very invested in his students and he is a great professor. Lectures became very boring and mundane but the topics that covered were interesting. This class is just an introduction so it glosses over the tops of many topics. He made us lots of food that he gave to us during class. Seriously the nicest professor ever!

Dr. Ahlborn is a very caring professor; you can tell he cares about every student individually. His projects are geared towards applying his principles that he teaches into your own life. The stuff he teaches is interesting and his class is very forgiving. I would definitely take a class from him again.

Dr A knew all of our names the first day of class, he really cares and will work with you. The lectures are pretty interesting but he throws in other activities during class. He knows a lot about food science. There aren't that many assignments and he always lets you redo things to get more points so it's an easy class and an interesting topic.

Truly my favorite class and professor. I truly learned so much in this class, it was very content and lecture heavy. Dr. A truly does care about his students - enough to know our names on the first day. His lectures are informative and entertaining. I truly aspire to be a teacher like him once I hit the field.

Such a great guy, he really cares about his students. He's very understanding and flexible and doesn't want anyone to stress about his class. The assignments are really easy and there aren't many. The exams and quizzes are all online. Take this class! Dr Ahlborn is absolutely the best!

Easiest class I've ever taken, with no homework. Also the most boring. He really cares about his students, and is passionate about the class, but it just drags. There is a 2 week project where you try to change a habit of your life, and every now and then he'll bring food in. It's incredibly easy. It's not worth it.

Professor Ahlborn is excellent - his quizzes are pretty straightforward, and he always described what was on the tests during class (so be sure to attend class). Even if you struggle a bit, there is extra credit and he works with you to make sure you get an A.

Dr. Cole was the best professor I have had at BYU! If you go talk to him during his many office hours, he will alleviate your worries and go the extra mile to help you succeed. His class is very simple: 3 essays, 3 tests. If you attend class and pay attention to his videos, you can get an A. He is very fair, and wants every student to successful.

Dr. Cole is nice, but this was easily the most boring class I've taken. He's monotonous and it was hard to stay awake. There are three exams, open ended, TA reviews are helpful. Two papers, they're horrible. Instead of writing the third there was an option to take a photo- way better. That's all you're graded on. Mess up once and you're screwed.

Take from Dr. Cole if you (1) don't want to learn anything, and (2) want to be forced to sit through painful lectures. You won't learn anything in this class that you couldn't find on google in 10 minutes. Do yourself a favor, take it from Sloan.

Took for 322 (modern american usage). This class (the learning suite) was extremely disorganized; I never knew when things were due and deadlines were always shifting. So much of the homework was busy work. Beyond that, Baker was belittling when I asked her for advice and insulted my major, my career, and my future aspirations in the process.
