I've taken two classes from Dr. Baker. Both were great experiences. She is knowledgable and experienced. Her classes are thoughtful and well structured. But she is a firm grader and will dock points, but will always give you helpful feedback. I've grown and learned a lot in her classes. Do it.

I really loved taking this class from Professor Baker. She's really open to what the students have to say, even adjusting answers when you present your evidence for answering a certain way. She has a lot of experience in the field and gives you lots of opportunities for employment or internships.
I really enjoyed her class
She is an awesome professor and her class was well-structured and thorough!

I respect Baker as a person and a professor so much. She is high love, high expectations. She has so much real world experience and is a master in the field. She will prepare you with what you need for the real world.

Dr. Baker is a very fair grader and lets you know what's due when and what she expects you do get done. If you talk to her about a bad score, she probably won't raise your grade, but she'll definitely help you understand concepts. She doesn't try to trick students with difficult projects and gives extra credit to students who find extra errors.

Holly Baker is fantastic. She's an author and professional editor, so she knows her stuff. All the assignments in this class had real world application, and at the end of the course we even worked on live manuscripts from real authors. I had so much fun every time we met for class, I always looked forward to it. Strongly recommend
Professor Jenkins is a great professor and he really knows his stuff. The class was really interesting!

Did I have to read an entire 200 pg book between class periods? Yes. Did it happen more than once? Also yes. And the readings weren't even useful or up to date. We spent a couple of weeks on an in-depth analysis of things from the Bush administration. Don't even get me started on the final paper.

Really awesome Poli Sci professor. He gives really good lectures and asks his students to engage with the material. He also goes over the main points for each concept and book, so that makes exams all the much easier. Exams have sufficient study guides to them. The paper is fairly graded as well as he is looking for what you have to say mostly.

The class was ok, I feel like it could have been great. The material was interesting, but presented horribly with wither death by powerpoint or using the whiteboard to write thigs because he didn't make slides. Grading took a very long time for every assignment, and a day after final grades are supposed to be available, noting has been submitted.

Awesome professor! While there is a lot of reading it is definitely doable and he teaches you how to reader faster and more effectively. You can get 100% on all the quiz assignments over the material and he is a fair grader. The long paper is split into 3 parts and he gives clear criteria, he is also helpful and responds quickly to emails.

Professor Jenkins knows his stuff, I enjoyed his lectures! He is a busy & caring professor who could possibly benefit from a TA to help with grading so things can be inputted faster, but he wants to help, & wants his students to succeed. With covid, he's been very generous with deadlines and has made this an enjoyable class. Thank you!

Classic first year associate professor. Takes over a month to grade tests and writing assignments. Makes you buy 4 books for the semester and you only read a few chapters out of 2 of them. Class is lecture heavy with over 100 pgs of reading for each class. 3 tests, 12 "reading response" essays, and a 12 pg policy paper. Take from someone else.

I don't know if it was a matter of the class itself or just his teaching style, but the requirements for essays and homework was very sparse. Thankfully, he made office hours readily available to clarify, but it would have been nice to have it all already available on LearningSuite.

He is such a good professor! His lectures are super insightful and I learned so much. The only assignments are readings and 4 short essays. Attendance isn't mandatory, but each class is a group discussion or guest lecture so you really should go to class. Highly recommend!

Dr Handley is a great professor who really cares about what he teaches. My perspective on the world changes throughout his class. I loved 90% of the reading he had us do, and I'm really grateful I took his class. 10/10 recomend.

Dr. Handley is a great professor. He is very caring and is well thought out in the way he teaches and expresses himself. His love for the environment and his steady/level-headed approach to solving climate related issues is contagious. I gained a greater reverence for our planet and went away with specific things I could do to be a better citizen.

Dr. Handley is the best! 370 was one of my favorite classes this semester because of how he taught. He makes you think about relevant, current-day issues and fosters the development of constructive opinions. He's very encouraging and inclusive when it comes to lectures/class participation. There's just a few papers, and he's a very fair grader.

Professor Handley is amazing in Book of Mormon, he really understands and cares about the text. He offers unique insights. He also cares about the individual, he had everyones names memorized in the first day and give constructive feedback on essays and tests. His tests make you think and ponder but are easy if you pay attention in lecture.

George is amazing - he's one of the most insightful professors I've ever taken a class from. Though intellectually demanding, his lectures and the ensuing discussions are inspiring and thought-provoking. Do all the required reading and come to class ready to discuss and you will have an amazing experience with him.

I had him for Book of Mormon. Since he is an English teacher the tests and essays were a lot more writing and I got points off for things unrelated to religion. Additionally, it didn't really stay in line with what other classes were learning so you could only study with your class. However overall pretty uplifting and inspiring.

He is an AMAZING professor. While he does get off on tangents sometimes, he teaches the Book of Mormon in a very wonderful way. He doesn't take attendance but he does grade on participation and his tests largely focus on themes talked about in class, so it's important to go. Believe me, you'll want to go anyway. He'll make you think, so take it!!

Humanities & Sciences was the best class I have ever taken at BYU! Professor Handley asks the best questions. There is a lot of reading, but the discussions we had in class were so good that you truly wanted to do it.  We had a small class so he let us rewrite the papers as many times as we wanted. I have never learned so much in a class!

Dr. Handley is a great professional and an excellent human being. I just took a class from him and do not regret my choice. He is really helpful to students and his lectures are so fun that it is really easy to get involved in his discussions. You can feel his commitment towards students and his class. I enthusiastically recommend Dr. Handley.

One of my favorite professors that I've taken from at BYU. I learned a ton of stuff from his lectures and the readings he assigned were so interesting that I didn't mind doing them at all. I would love to take another class from him.

I have taken several classes from George Handley. His class discussions have opened a new world of thought to me. Don't miss taking a class from him just because you are afraid of it being hard. He gives great feedback on papers. My writing and critical thinking improve with every class that I take from Dr. Handley.

I didn't notice this class was "hard" because I enjoyed the lectures and assigments so much! Dr. Handley is so willing to invest in his students' learning processes and is totally passionate about everything he teaches. He's fun, brilliant, and really dedicated. I loved it. I got a great grade because of his engaging teaching.

Worst professor at BYU.  I have loved every humanities class I have ever taken EXCEPT for his...  Reading well over 75 pages a night as well as writing papers that never recieved higher than a B-.  Take this class from another professor if you want to actually enjoy the humanities.
He's intelligent. Very kind and heartwarming. If you listen you will learn a lot. great guy. can't say enough good things about him

He's a good guy. He can be funny sometimes too. He is very knowledgable, and he's always prepared. He is tough on essays, but fair. He will quiz you if you don't read. He loves Latin/South America. He's a good teacher overall.

Fascinating lectures, he's extremely knowledgeable in his subject, and a lot of others as well. His book selections are excellent-introduced me to a lot of new genres. Papers graded fairly tough, but he's very clear on what is expected.  Tests kind of hard,but he covers all the material on them in class. Definately take him if you can!

Dr. Handley really knows his stuff.  He is the Humanities Dept. Chair and is really passionate about what he does.  His goal is to broaden the horizons of the arts in oblivious students.  He is really good at connecting history, art, literature, the gospel, and real life for a different view of the world.  Grades on attendance, 2 tests, & 4 essays.

Dr. Handley is a good guy, he's class is alright.  The first test was super hard, the next super easy.  The reading is mostly good except for one STUPID textbook he's getting rid of in the future.  Not the most fun class, but I made it though and probably learned something.
There is a service project where you have to do 10 service hours. The tests are online and there is a study guide.

A very informative class, prof Pierce made sure if was never boring with funny jokes. My only complaint is the class being extremely back-heavy, with a long final project, final essays, and the final un-exam all being due incredibly close together. Start on them early!

Professor Pierce was excellent. His assignments are stacked to the end of the semester so be ready! With that being said, work load is manageable, lectures are interesting, and Dr Pierce is really well versed in the material. You can tell he really loves the Lord, AND cares for his students. This class was really impactful.

Super cool professor! He joined the church during his PhD program I believe? His love and deep knowledge of the Old Testament and his conversion to the church give him a unique perspective and depth that you don't usually get from BYU religion classes. The course wasn't too difficult, was uplifting, and I didn't feel like there was much busy work.
He's not bad. I learned some things. There wasn't a lot of things you had to do until the end of the semester, but at the end there were several small papers and a project all at once.

Dr. Pierce was great! He doesn't have midterms or finals, but he does have lots of projects to work on throughout the semester, including 4 small quizzes, a service project, a map project, and an analytical/creative project. There are readings for every class period but all he asks is that you write a few questions or thoughts from your reading.

Dr Pierce is what a religion prof should be. His lectures are engaging and well researched. He is more on the historical/archaeological side of scripture, but that is part of the unique BYU experience. The class isn't too hard, and he does a great job of making the OT apply to us, including emphasizing service. So he is spiritual and edifying.

Much of the grade in the class is based on the amount of readings completed in an honor-based self-grading system. He is engaging and hilarious. He clearing cares about what he teaches, and he shared with us personal spiritual experiences he has had that relate to what we are discussing. We learn a lot of historical context, but it is relevant.

He's SUPER knowledgable and funny. Basically all you have to do is read the chapters and submit a few thoughts for each reading and do 10hrs of service during the semester. Very light workload. However, he basically just lectures all over the place and sometimes its hard to follow but its SO important to take notes or you'll be so lost on the exams

I feel like I was coasting most of the semester and then the last week had a ton of work but overall it was a great class. Professor Pierce is a hilarious guy who knows so much about the old world. I feel like it could have been a bit clearer but overall he did a great job. He also tossed out the final exam for you creating a lesson plan on Isaiah.
Nice guy. Tests are hard but ok if you pay attention in class and study.

D. Pierce is an amazing professor with a great testimony. He is also hilarious! He teaches really well and loves to add in archaeological pictures and examples. Homework includes readings and writing down a few questions prior to class as well as a few papers and a service project assignment. Take his class!

I can't overstate how amazing Prof Pierce was. This is how every religion class at BYU should be in my opinion. He is not focused on nitpicky grades, he grades easy but focuses on what you can take away from this class. He wants you to learn and grow, not memorize random details and info. Also he is hilarious and his testimony is powerful.

Dr. Pierce is really nice and passionate, lectures were entertaining. The class is pretty easy, but tests were kind of unreasonable. Expects you to know really specific stuff about the NT and lectures cover a lot of material. There are also three pretty long papers due right at the end of the semester.
Weekly Service Requirement Lectures were entertaining but confusing No clear Correlation between lectures and test content Funny, entertaining, nice professor

Fantastic professor! He understands that the religion courses should not break your back. Outstanding lectures and he includes lots of interesting historical information as well! Tests are easy - just study. Homework is only reading assignments and there are 3 simple papers as well. Definitely worth it!

Live remote was hard for everyone but he made it work. My favorite lectures were when he bore his testimony. Old testament is dense, but he knows his stuff. The projects were fun and super manageable as long as you dont procrastinate;)

Dr. Pierce is so easy to work with and cares much more about spiritual growth than actual academic growth. Tests are not proctored and even if you don't get a good grade to begin with, he will work with you until you have an A.

Definitely one of my top 5 teachers of all time. Dr. Pierce is so incredibly educated in everything history. He is hilarious and he truly cares about his students and I feel like he understands the balance of too much homework and not enough, ending in the perfect workload. You won't regret taking a class from him. 10/10!
HOMIE. Man of the people. One of the best I've ever had.

Great class! Very easy homework, you just read the assigned scriptures and make a comment or two about it, but they are due the night before each class. Grade is mostly based on the midterm, the Final, and the one Analysis paper we have. It is 8-10 pages, but as long as you don't procrastinate (a big if) it's not too bad. Study hard for the tests!

Dr. Pierce is one of my favorite Religion professors. He definitely focuses on the historic side of things, but ties it all back spiritually. The class was pretty easy, with readings for each class and one major essay at the end.

Dr. Pierce made class super fun! He really cares about his students and is hilarious. And i love how in his class he makes historical connections which helps me understand the scriptures more. If you are in his CEG class there is a pretty big essay! But other than that there barely any homework (just read a scripture and write some comments on them

Dr. Pierce is amazing. He changed my perspective on so many things and really made me so excited to learn about the gospel. He is hilarious, engaging, and kind, and while there were lots of awesome moments where I learned a lot of history there were also some really really incredible moments where I felt the spirit so strongly in his class. 10/10

Professor Pierce has been one of my most favorite professors here at BYU. I've seen that some people say his classes aren't that spiritual, but this guy can drop some Spiritual BOMBS when he wants to. It's amazing. He perfectly combines the material of the class with his wit and I loved it. You can tell that he's a real people person too.

This class did not make very much sense. It seemed pretty clear the Dr. Pierce had no idea what was on his own syllabus, and he really only cares about historical information. I feel like the gospel knowledge I gained from this class was exactly 0. He should really be teaching a history class.

Dr. Pierce was a refreshing professor. One of the better religion professors I've had. He took a more historical approach to the scriptures rather than a Sunday School approach. Not super spiritually strengthening but it was interesting and easy. Dr. Pierce is a sweet guy and he wants everyone to do well.
I loved Dr. Pierce. He really opened my eyes to a lot of things, not necessarily gospel related. He's so funny, and even though attendance isn't mandatory you definitely want to go to class.
Super funny and chill professor. Lectures often had good insights.

Homework is very little, except for long papers. Class felt long since it was all lecture. At first, Dr. Pierce seemed tough and not accessible, but he really wasn't. His focus is more academic and historical, and his knowing Greek and Hebrew really opened up some scriptural passages to me.

He is very knowledgeable which is refreshing! I look forward to his lectures. Homework is not bad at all, just read a chapter or two in the scriptures and submit two questions you had while reading. There are 2 papers that are not bad at all. So far, one of the better religion professors I have had.

Meh. Not the best religion teacher. He's much less spiritual than expected. His Greek language knowledge is enlightening though. He doesn't post the slides so you have to go to class. He doesn't give a rubric for the papers and said if you complete the paper you'll get a good grade but I got a B (for who knows what since there wasn't a rubric).

Dr. Pierce is super cool, he makes the religious learning environment really relaxed which doesn't always happen at BYU. You can tell he wants everyone to succeed and you can also tell that he really knows what he's talking about and teaches with the spirit. I learned a ton from this class!

Brother Pierce is such a sweet man. He is always willing to help and wants his students to succeed. He gave me a few second chances on things due to legit computer probs. He holds office hours where he's willing to explain anything. He is also hilarious! I really dig his sense of humor, he kept me awake during my 8am class.

Pro. Pierce is a good choice for your religion class. He is a convert to the church with extensive knowledge of ancient scripture and gives interesting insights. His lectures can be a little dull at time but lectures weren't mandatory. Grading was fair, tests hard, but gave over 3% of extra credit for the overall class. He's a great and fair guy.

His lectures are not posted online as a way to get people to class. Any form of study is going to be completely from notes you've taken in class so it's important that you go. He's pretty funny. If you wanna get through all the material, don't ask questions. He goes on really long tangents.

Great professor and a great person. He has been my professor in multiple classes now, and I have always loved the experience that I have gained from his teaching style. The class wasn't overly difficult for the sake of being difficult. I like that about his classes. Class is easy, there are about two 3-page papers. Easy A, really. Just show up.

Dr. Pierce was a great lecturer but the tests are a little ridiculous. He gives you a study guide, but you need to fill it in. Any small tiny detail is fair game, which I didn't like. The material was super interesting and presented in a unique way as Dr. Pierce has a degree in archaeology.

I think this class was the perfect balance of religious and academic. Test are hard, but if you try, Professor Pierce will give you a good grade final grade. For instance, I failed the midterm and didn't do awesome on the final, but I got a B. There isn't a lot of homework besides reading the New Testament.

Dr. Pierce is one of the best professors I've ever had. Not only does he paint a picture of the New Testament, but he entertains along the way. His quick wit & humor are very much appreciated, and you gain a much better understanding of the gospels. Grades are based on weekly reading reports, three essays (not hard), and 2 exams. Highly reccomend.

Really knows the history of the New Testament very well, and you can tell that he loves his job and loves his students. He has an awesome sense of humor. His tests and assignments were all very easy and not time consuming, and I felt like they were very helpful.

Professor Pierce is an outstanding professor. His class is hard, and his schedule is busy, but he is always willing to help after class or at office hours. He presents the material very clearly. Only problem is, he tests on things that he may have only mentioned once, and is detail oriented. ATTENDANCE ABSOLUTELY MANDATORY.

He is great, excellent insights and lectures. He lived in Jerusalem for a while, so if you are looking for an interesting class with real information and understanding of Israel, he is the right professor for you. Homework is easy and he does not grade hard.

Brother Pierce is a kind man. He teaches about the gospel passionately. I could tell he knows his stuff and has a strong connection with our Father in Heaven, and his son Jesus Christ. I would LOVE to take another class from him! I recommend him! Go to class and do the homework!! Easy A incorporated with laughter from his jokes.

He was all about memorization on purely historical & geographical locations, with very little to no spirit felt in his class. The only time I felt spiritually enriched was when we had to do the one writing assignment outside of class. If you're really into the geographical aspect and not looking to feel the spirit in class, take it from him.

Brother Pierce was an amazing teacher for my Book of Mormon class. He makes the class easy enough that even people who are not Mormon or have never read the Book of Mormon can still easily pass his class. The value is highly placed in his lectures. He clearly walks you through the scriptures and makes them easy to understand. Take his class.

It took me a while to figure out what bothered me so much about this class. It finally occurred to me that I had never heard Pierce share his testimony once that semester. And I don't even mean overtly; we just didn't really discuss gospel doctrine a lot, the focus was very much on history and memorization; important but often spiritually empty.

This was a pretty good class. The tests had some weird obscure questions that don't seem very important to understand the scriptures, though. The BOM reading assignments were several chapters at a time, which I liked because I felt like I was able to follow along better with what was going on.  He was helpful if you had questions.  I liked him.

I had a BLAST in this class, and I'd highly recommend it to anyone. I learned so many crazy new things and got to use lots of fun tools to make sculptures. Also, Gian is an AWESOME professor! He's super helpful and will always go over how to use a machine with you, help you brainstorm ideas, offer helpful critique, and even just talk to you!
This class was extremely fun and engaging. You get to explore many different mediums and Gian is very understanding. 100% reccomend.
Not fit to be teaching in his condition, do NOT take a class from him, rearrange your schedule if you have to avoid him. Your grade will thank you.

Professor Fellingham genuinely cares about his students and that shows through. Lectures aren't always the easiest to follow but there was an online textbook that you could review with. The TA's were also very helpful. The majority of your grade is the tests, but they're open note and the questions were all reasonable.

Not a good teacher and didn't know how to explain anything. Spent time talking about the honor code and would go on tangents about things that weren't important. The TAs never answered their emails and the tests are weighted super heavy towards your grade. The only reason I passed is because he did a mini curve at the end. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

I loved taking this class from Dr. Fellingham. He knows what he is talking about and gave some great examples and guidance. He is specific on his expectations, but he gave a lot of freedom to us students. I would highly recommend taking this class from him. Also, go to the TAs if you need any extra help!

If he ever teaches 330 again I would avoid him.  His tests were poorly put together and was lazy about assigning homework.  He did not like teaching this class at all and it showed.  He taught the material good enough for me, but it was confusing for many in the class. Basically the class was taught ok but designed terribly.

DO NOT TAKE FROM HIM. It was hard to respect him because it was obvious he never prepared for the class. Each quiz and test was practically a guessing game, and the class average was a 74% but he still offered no extra credit. Choose another professor, you will be much better off.

Disorganized, rude, and absolutely did not put any effort into the class after the first midterm.  It was hard for me to take him seriously as it was obvious that he did not prepare for the lectures.  He prepared us so little for the homework that they were basically graded on completion.  Take the class from another professor if possible.

Dr. Fellingham is a true expert in his field. This makes lectures somewhat hard to follow. If you can focus through the anecdotes, you can learn a ton from him. Tests are intuitive, and he provides most of the information/tools in the lectures themselves. He's quippy and somewhat harsh, so if you can handle that, and focus, he'll be great.

DO NOT TAKE STAT121 FROM THIS PROF!! He is absolutely horrific!! Lectures consist of him reading from the slides and ranting about how much he hates his life, puts all the work on the TA (hes freaking lazy), no extra credit, and basically sets up for failure with average grades on 4 tests being a C. 20 ppl failed, 5 ppl got an A at the end.

Really a terrible experience. He doesn't try is the bottom line. I have no idea why, but he is totally checked out at this point. He is not a good teacher and doesn't put in the effort to teach anything effectively. Additionally, he is incredibly disorganized. He is also rude to students.

He seems literally incapable of teaching effectively. As examples, he took 20 minutes to answer a question I asked that could have been answered in one sentence. We also had to push back the first exam literally one month since he needed the time to teach us the concepts. This is exacerbated by him using about half the lecture time to rant.

The class was fine, grade is based 90% on two midterms and the final so if you're good at tests it's not hard to get an A. Fellingham is a poor lecturer, I tuned out most of the time. Gets on these boomer rants every 15 minutes and doesn't explain things very well, and very full of himself. R is not as bad as people say but takes some figuring out.

By far the worst professor alive. Gil Fellingham is not only a bad teacher, he is a horrible human being. He yelled at someone for asking a question. Avoid for your own good. He insists on using R without teaching you how to. A huge waste of time. Take it from someone else. Avoid avoid avoid

Great guy, and passionate about statistics. His lectures were long, and sometimes a little boring(I mean, it's stats, after all), but he would try to keep them fun. I've seen several complaints that he doesn't teach R very well, but I think he did fine. I have no programming experience and I made it though without needing anything outside of class

Lectures were VERY hard to understand; long tangents, slow pacing; reads slides; over half the class was skipping by week 5. He fails to put concepts simply and focuses way to much on R. I switched to excel partway through, an improvement. If you have to take this class, just remember that most of the TAs can explain things better than he can.
He prepares you for the real world by going over real situations in which you would apply Statistics. Can get on tangents. He really wants you to understand, and he'll help you if you need help.
Expects 100% effort from you. Dr. Fellingham makes you really think about all your homework. He will really prepare you for real-life situations. He is very honest with his feedback.

Funny guy, gives lots of good life lessons. Class is taught very slowly, so I usually just skipped and read the powerpoints. Not much work, but tough to get an A. Tests are 90% of the total grade which is stressful. Good teacher, though. The content is not super difficult, just make sure you know how to use R studio.

Reads from the slides in his presentation like he has never seen them before. Expects students to teach themselves how to use R without giving instruction or aid on how to use the software. Felt like this class was more of an R studio class than a Stats class. He is more concerned about you learning how to use R than learning the concept. Very poor

Dr. Fellingham is an interesting guy. Most lectures I attended were quite dull, but every once in a while (maybe once a month) he gets on a roll and tells some absolutely *hilarious* stories. The class was difficult for me mainly because of a lack of clear R tutorials, but the textbook was very good. I'm glad I got this class out of the way.

All I know is when I went to the TA lab, they said the other teachers handed out As like candy, but that his tests are way hard. Super lecture heavy. Doesn't really teach you how to use the R-software. I taught myself excel instead. Take home tests are very challenging and he is not forgiving with grading.

Dr. Fellingham is an intersting character! He has very strict honor code and late policy standards, but, honestly, if you just email him before class if you know you're going to be late, he is chill. A word of caution: You better know R before you take this class from him. Almost all the tests and HW are done in R. I learned a ton!

He wants to make lectures more of an "Exploratory time" (which is confusing!!) and then the homework is like the cold hard application. Homework and tests can be really easy if you go to TA hours & if your TA is helpful. Personality-wise, Fellingham can be a funny guy but he is strict on the honor code/being late.

Dr. Fellingham is one of the most honest and straight forward professors at BYU. His feedback is usually very helpful. I feel like he will be very sincere while helping you, if you put forth the effort. He won't give you a chance if you seem to be slacking. If you are a humble learner, you will learn a lot from him. He prepares you for a career.

He is pretty scary.  He yelled at my class for 20 minutes straight one time.  He is unorganized and about 50% of the time, his examples don't work.  He is a genius but sometimes struggles with conveying difficult concepts.  Go to class. DON'T BE LATE.

DO NOT DO NOT DO NOT arrive or turn anything in late. I was 8 seconds late handing my final project to him (even though I was in class on time I just walked too slow) and he wouldn't accept it. Get to class 15 minutes early or dont take the class.

Not very challenging if you go to class and do the homework (tests are exactly like the homework, final is explained well). But I wouldn't recommend as an intro stats class. While a good grade is possible, you won't get as much out of the class and won't have the necessary skills. Really nice and helpful professor, though strict. Overall good.

Do not take this as an introductory stats class. There is no textbook -- all the information you will get comes from Dr. Fellingham in language that is inaccessible to those without a stats background. You will not become excited about stats in this class, you will hate stats because of the poor curriculum of this class. Very boring and difficult!

He is a no-nonsense type of guy, but as long as you follow the rules you'll be fine. He might seem intimidating in class, but during office hours he's extremely helpful and genuinely concerned about your learning. He gets a bad wrap because he doesn't put up with lame excuses from students, like being late. Easy A if you go to class. Great teacher.

He really ticked me off at first because I added the class a week late and thus did not catch the interesting homework policy. But this class is probably worth taking if you want an easy A, and it is great for learning or getting better at R. Lecture is entertaining...just  don't be the person making it entertaining!

He hasn't improved. I took his class so I wouldn't have to pay for a text book. He is really obnoxious but talks about sports a lot if you are into that. I found him very disrespectful and crude. He degraded people who asked questions if they showed any hint that they were taking this as their intro stats class (which it is designed to be).

He's definately tough. All HW is due BEFORE class, he's very strict. But for this class he was a very good teacher, but he can be kind of vague. I learned a lot, the HW and tests were always clear and simple. I'd recommend him, just make sure you're on time.

This guy is a lunatic. Doesn't show any interest on how much students want to learn and doesn't care about what background they have. He just keeps teaching his own way, no matter if someone understands him or not. not respectful to questions. Totally waste of credit...To get an A in the class you just have to do what he says but you learn nothing.

When you're one-on-one he is very kind and understanding, but in class is opposite. Insanely strict with puncuality--when a freshman was late the first day of class because of getting lost he called him a "slob", and he didn't accept assignments that were literally 2 seconds late. Not a good teacher either. I would never recommend Fellingham.
easy subject. do exactly what he says.

This class was a major let down.  The professor is nice but his lectures are very boring... no class discussion, impossible tests, vague directions for papers.  He made an interesting subject into a nightmare.  STAY AWAY

I really love church history, but Fellingham's class is a JOKE! He lets the students write the questions, so of course you get the over-zealous-achievers who ask for specific sections and dates of scriptures. Lectures are super boring, your grade is based on tests, and he is not understanding AT ALL. HORRIBLE CLASS--NOT RECOMMENDED!
Doesn't encourage class discussion, so can be boring. Good class if you're good at multiple choice, since that's pretty much your whole grade.
No Comments
The course is tough, he tries to be tough, but he's a good guy.  Write down everything he says and does in class, you'll get an A.
Really tough class, tough tests, tough homework, but a real great professor.  Makes things really enjoyable.

Profesora Villalobos is one of the BEST professors I have had at BYU, hands-down. I took SPAN322 (the writing class) from her, and it genuinely improved my writing skills so much. Take that class if you want to get better at writing in spanish! Don't be scared off by it. I also took SPAN411 from her- I also really reccomend. She cares about you!

This was a fantastic class! The topics are well chosen to help you learn how to communicate in difficult topics. She expects you to put in effort, but it was never overwhelming. Her feedback is super helpful and I could see myself getting a lot better over the course of the class.

I recommend this class to EVERYONE I know! Profe Gina Villalobos is incredible. She is so funny and witty but also takes this class and its material very seriously. She fostered a non-threatening environment where we could express our opinions and learn to debate in a healthy way. I learned how to express myself more eloquently. 10/10 recommend!
Gina is such an amazing professor. Really not too hard at all but still a real class. One of my fav Spanish professors at BYU!

Lo mejor! Very clear on grading policies. Offers tons of extra help and feedback. So kind and caring. Lots of writing, but you do it in phases, and the workload isn't bad. 
Take her for sure!

Professor Lobos is a great Professor. She was very professional and respectful to all her students. I took her class a year ago and I still remember a lot of the things she taught in that class. She also invited us to her house and cooked for us. I would for sure take another class with her.

Fantastic class, and she teaches it super well. Attendance and preparation are necessary, which makes sense for a conversation class. You'll get more out of it as you participate in the discussions and really read the material. She was great at bringing up meaningful topics of debate and helping us to be better communicators.
Amazing professor. Super sweet and understanding but also total jefa and great professor. Not too hard of a class. 10/10 would recommend Gina.

Professor Villalobos is a fantastic professor. She was very insistent on everyone participating, but the lectures and classwork were very enjoyable. She's engaging and brings a very fun atmosphere to the class. I would recommend anyone take Spanish from her!!

Professor Villalobos is more concerned with the outcomes of your Spanish abilities after the class and less concerned about the often random, test-driven ways to grade you. I like that she guided me to do some self-examination and some self-proving so that I could feel more confident about my Spanish. If you let her be honest, she can help you.

Profesora Villalobos is amazing! This class quickly became one of my favorites because of her engaging lectures and insightful explanations of the cultural significance behind the literary works we studied. She was always helpful and genuinely invested in our success. I learned so much from her, I highly recommend taking her class!

Professor Villalobos did everything to help us prepare for the OPI oral exam. I felt confident when I took it! The one complication was that due dates got changed a LOT, sometimes they were even set sooner without notice. If you missed a due date though, she was good about reopening assignments. Check the dates in LS every week and you'll be fine!

Take classes from Professor Villalobos. She expects you to use your Spanish and participate but does not judge you if it is not correct. She is approachable and willingly admits when she makes a mistake. Often if there were misunderstandings on due dates she would move them later to accommodate well for all students. Homework is reasonable.

Hermana Villalobos is a caring, effective teacher. She ends class early often, and she gives good feedback on papers and homework (she actually reads them!!!) She loves effort, but is also very flexible with your schedule.Great teacher. Would take again.

Profesora Villalobos is an incredibly kind person and has her class structured in such a way that helps you write in Spanish without getting overwhelmed. You have to write four essays in the semester, but she has you write an outline and rough draft for each one that helps make it more manageable. She gives good feedback.

She's one of the best professors at BYU and the first one to ever sit down with me and ask "what should I know about you for this course to help you succeed?" From bringing candy, to being flexible, to even making a 3 course meal in her home for a class "cultural opportunity" she is the best of the best and you won't regret taking her class!
She is very kind and willing to work with students to get the best outcome possible. She is big on attendance and participation. If things come up she will help you out. Awesome profesora!

Probably the best spanish professor at BYU. She is very caring and very helpful to any student who is struggling. Lots of papers, but they aren't too difficult and she doesn't grade too harshly. Her assignment instructions are not very clear and due dates are always changing, but other than that she does an incredible job.

Profe Villalobos did really well directing the class and focusing on writing skills in Spanish. The textbook was a little expensive, but we used it every day. Because it is a composition class, the essays have the most weight on your grade. The activities in class are supposed to help you prepare for the essays. She gives good feedback.

Profe Villalobos is phenomenal. Funny, teaches clearly, and makes the material engaging. We write a lot inside and outside of class but it was all very manageable and I feel like my writing improved. She's very understanding and genuinely wants all of her students to have the opportunity to do well.

Profe Villalobos is awesome. She's hilarious, engaging, and makes class fun and interesting. She is very helpful in preparing her students for the exams and there is never confusion about what is expected to get a good grade. The homework is very doable and she gives opportunities to do a lot of it in class.

She is my favorite! I moved my schedule around to take this class from her. She brought the stories to life and helped me understand the more difficult stories and poems. We had some of the best discussions I've ever had. She helps you think on a deeper level and analyze the text. In her class you learn a ton and it's not very stressful.

I was very nervous to take this class, but it became one of my favorite classes because of Profe V! She structured the class perfectly so that we were constantly writing in a low stress environment. My writing and my Spanish improved exponentially and on top of that, my confidence in Spanish improved. Hands down the BEST Spanish professor!!

This is a class with a lot of writing -- yet somehow it felt like nothing!! You don't even realize the work you are putting in because Professora Villalobos makes it SO fun! She is the best of the best! She works with you and wants you to succeed, and my spanish has never been better!

Professor Villalobos is the BEST professor not only in the Spanish department at BYU, but that I have had in all of BYU. She is SO kind. She is the perfect mix of having high expectations and high love for each of us. She learns your NAME -- which I feel is particularly rare for most college classes. I couldn't recommend her enough.

Profesora Villalobos is INCREDIBLE! Classes were purely discussion based, but she made them very fun and interesting. I would recommend her to anyone needing another Spanish credit, especially if you're planning on taking the OPI.

Profesora Villalobos is such an amazing professor! She is so helpful, kind, and respectful towards her students. She is very flexible with everyone and is always there to help students fix their grades. It is a writing class so there are about 4 big writing assignments, but honestly they weren't bad at all. She made the class so fun and easy!
She is incredible and one of the best professors I have had at BYU. She is very kind but holds her students to high standards. I learned so much in this class.
She is the best 321 teacher, and it isn't even close. One of my favorite classes of all time. Ella es la cabra!!!

Take all your Spanish classes from Sra. Villalobos! Genuinely cares about her students and is available outside of class for any help you may need. Assignments are straightforward. She won't make you talk in class if you don't want to. This is a class I actually wanted to go to :)
LA CLASE MAS FACIL QUE HE TOMADO EN MI VIDITA. Yo adoro esa mujer. La verdad es ella es un poco desorganizada pero ni modo.

I LOVE this woman. She's hilarious. She cares so much about her students learning Spanish and couldn't care less about the department and their rules, or homework, or grades. She wants everyone to get an A. Doesn't call you out in class in case you're self conscious of your Spanish. She truly creates a great learning environment. You'll feel #safe

Profe Villalobos is so understanding. If you want a chill class where you come to class to learn this is it. There isn't hardly any pressure for the class as long as you get your stuff done. She is very open to make time to meet to help reteach things and also super leniente for late work.

What an amazing women! I have never had so much fun in a class or laughed so much. She made Spanish fun to learn, and make it totally stress free. She is on your side and will fight for you to get an A. If you need help just talk to her. She is a mom to everyone and even invited us over to her house for dinner!

Professor Villalobos makes writing essays manageable with a planned timeline and rough draft (bosquejos) to turn in to help brainstorm. You will write 4 essays over the course; 3 being 2 pages long and the final being 6. She's very kind and willing to help!

Spanish Writing and Composition with Prof. Villalobos was a good time. Her class is very participation-based, and much of the lectures are intended to be group discussions on literary techniques to improve your writing in Spanish. She's very focused on helping you succeed and improve in your Spanish, and less about how she grades you.

I loved this class! She's super attentive. There's a lot of work/writing but it really matches the pace of the class, and isn't hard. You do write essays but she gives you plenty of time to work on them and you can turn them in early to get feedback and re-turn them in for a higher grade! Grades fairly quickly and the quizzes were easy. Take!

She is nice, caring, and always available outside of class. The class is pretty straightforward, but there is a TON of grammar you have to learn on your own. There are a few small papers, routine textbook work, 2 midterms and a final. After the midterms she lets you talk to her about them and she is generous about giving points back on them.

My favorite teacher so far at BYU. Class was fun, participation-based, and just enjoyable. The teacher is sweet and really cares. I think most of my class had nicknames after the first couple weeks. Wish I could take it every semester. Work load is light at most. Never really stressed about the class at all.

I will take every spanish class I can from Profesor Villalobos! She is an amazing teacher who creates an amazing classroom dynamic where you feel comfortable speaking up and participating in class. Go to her office hours! She is always more than willing to help you with difficult concepts and learn from your past mistakes. 11/10!

Villalobos cares a lot about her students. She offers plenty of time outside of class to work and study with her which helps a lot. She is an easy grader but really wants her students to participate in class discussion. I would take Spanish from her again, you can tell she is passionate about the language.

I loved her class! I highly recommend taking any courses with her, she is very involved in her classes, participation is important and she really makes you think. Lots of in class discussions and a few papers and research is important. Very sweet and is always willing to help students out.
She is the best take her and you will not regret it. Not much homework and very flexible.
She is the nicest teacher ever. Cares a ton about your learning and doesn't try to shove it down your throat. She is super funny and all about the "chisme"

There were a few times when the instructions on homework and papers weren't clear, but she always gave us more time and many chances to get it right. You have to write a huge paper, but we worked on it 2 pages at a time, so super easy. Class was fun. I loved the class and I learned a lot too about the importance of writing.
super fun Spanish teacher. she makes class interesting, and not hard

Hermana Stallings is the best professor you could have for 321! She's like your adopted Columbian grandma and treats all her students as such! She doesn't design the course, the department does, but she was always so good at explaining things and adjusting assignments to meet our needs. Her class is a joy to be in because she loves it and you!

Hermana Stallings is the most amazing teacher I have ever had. She is so kind and caring and legitimately cares for the success of her students. She will do everything she can to help you out! I highly recommend this class, especially if you are just returning from your mission.

Hermana Stallings is so sweet and wants all of her students to succeed. The new pilot program that we did this semester was not great but that's not her fault and she did what she could to make it easier on us. She is very passionate about everything and very sweet.
She is super caring and the only professor I've had that actually knew our names. Her class was easy and the homework wasn't very heavy.

i LOVE profesora stallings so much!! at first, the class was so confusing just because of how the canvas page was set up. but she truly is so sweet and so amazing. there are quite a few readings, but they're not the worst thing ever. you can tell she truly cares about her students beyond the classroom. you will not regret taking spanish from her!!

I loved Hermana Stallings. She is so sweet and passionate about the material she is teaching. She really wants her students to succeed and is willing to work with you to do so. The homework is every other day and although it is not hard you definitely need to read and go to class to understand.
She cares about her students a lot. She tries very hard to help you improve your Spanish. She is basically the Colombian abuelita you always wanted. Very merciful.

Hermana Stallings was a great teacher; I grew to adore her! At the start of the semester I felt like the class was unorganized and hectic but she proved me wrong. Give her a chance! She prepared us well for tests and wanted to see us all succeed! If you ask for help she WILL help you! She loves her students!

Hermana Stallings is an incredible human being and the best professor for 321. The class itself isn't too hard and she is a pretty chill grader which is super nice. She prepares you very well for the Challenge exam (which you should definitely take) and the tests, and she is very caring and responsive to emails. Take this class from her!
The most unorganized class IVE EVER TAKEN. Absolutely infuriating.

Sr. Stallings is a saint. She is super kind and loving but her class is not organized very well. You don't know what's expected of you and her tests are all about the obscure details in the stories. Save your GPA and take from someone else.

Hna Stallings is angelic. She is the sweetest person I've ever known. Even now when I see her on campus she walks up to me, hugs me, asks me how I'm doing, etc.. Her class was a challenging but it's an upper level grammar and reading class. Very clear expectations and she always wove fascinating personal insights into her lectures and discussions.

Spanish lit. was a lot harder than I'd anticipated. However, Hna Stallings is a wonderful teacher who is passionate about literatura española. I loved her lectures and knew she genuinely cared about each of her students. Be ready to read and (especially!) to comment in class for a good grade. This was my favorite class and teacher of the semester.

This is a difficult class but Hermana Stallings is very passionate and is willing to work with her students. Make sure you keep up with the homework and review her slides before the tests. She loves participation so answer questions and she'll love you.

Hna. Stallings es una buenísima profesora. Toma mucho interés en sus estudiantes. Sepa bien que se tiene que leer bastante en esta clase (¡ya que es una clase de literatura!). Las lecturas pueden ser difíciles, pero la Hna. Stallings se pone muy disponible para ayudar a cualquier que quiera aprender. If this was hard to read, don't take this class!

Professor Stallings is one of the kindest people I have ever met. She wants you to succeed and gives opportunities for extra credit. There are 3 tests; the poetry one was hard but the other 2 were fairly easy. Participation MATTERS! I thought I commented in class a fair amount, but I still only got a 90% in that area. Work hard and you'll do great!

Gloria Stallings is super caring. She grades papers and test super liberally. As long as you participate in class and make it to all of the International Cinemas you will get a good grade in the class.

Hermana Stallings is an angel, she is very caring and wants the best for her students. She outlines what she is going to test on the exam very clearly and she is a fair grader. The class was enjoyable from the various poems, movies, works we studied.

Sister Stallings is probably the most caring teacher I've ever had. She sacrifices a lot to do the best job she can, and she truly loves her students and what she teaches (in the case of SPAN 339, literature). I learned a lot in the class, Sister Stallings made it enjoyable. The class took work, and while it wasn't perfect, it was a good one.

Great class. I don't even like poetry and she still made it interesting. The tests aren't hard at all if you go to class and pay attention. I found the books and short stories we read to be quite interesting.

Hermana Stallings is an amazing professor. She cares about her students and helping them learn. She loves it when students come for extra help during office hours and spends hours with them if needed. She adjusts to her students' needs and is a very fun teacher. She has a very positive attitude and is very proud of her students' success.
My favorite Spanish professor yet. She cares about her students and the class material. She's really helpful,and she cooks good arepa. I'd recommend you take this class from her.

Hna. Stallings is hands down the most helpful and caring professor I've ever had. She loves when you keep in contact with her too! If you can take this class from her, do it!!! You will really become a better writer.
Hermana Stallings is funny. She puts a lot of emphasis on how to write good papers, but she graded really easily. She is really nice - especially if you visit her during office hours.
She's soo adorable!!
Hermana Stallings was awesome - she was always helpful and her class really helped me learn a lot.  She really cares about and works with each student personally :)

Most caring professor I've had at BYU. She does love the RMs, but she loves everyone else, too, and is very approachable if you have any questions or need help outside of class. She always made sure the students understood what they were doing, the papers were fun to write (I had fun with them, anyway...) and I always looked forward to class.

She truly loves her students (especially any RMs because she's a convert) and wants them to learn Spanish.  Perhaps relies to heavily on PowerPoints.  Fun class, always looked forward to the social environment and group in-class exercises.  Very helpful outside of class.  An A is very attainable.

Very very nice lady who is almost always in a good mood and willing to help.  She explains concepts well and knows the language well. Class isn't too hard, and she often extends the test deadlines. Just don't talk while she is talking and it's all good!
She is a wonderful teacher, she really care about her students.If a student need extra help she is really hepful.
She is a wonderful teacher, she really take care of her students. She is really clear and organized. If students look for help for sure they will find it.
Great teacher who really cares for her class and students, can't wait to have another class with her.
Easy class for returned missionaries.  She is really funny and nice and understanding. Classes are very fun and easy and homework is short and simple.  Tests are easy if you pay attention in class.
She is very caring for every student.  She has an intuition about what every student needs outside of class and is the kind of woman you will enjoy seeing after the course is over.
she is the best teacher at BYU. She cares so much about every single student. I love her. you will never find a better teacher in your life.

Great teacher!  She works so hard to come up with ways to teach the concepts so that we will understand.  It's a hard task to teach RMs who think they already know everything.  Never met a teacher who cares so much about her students.  Take her!

I loved spanish but decided I was done after this class. Senora isn't really hard but there is way more busy work than is necessary. It isn't a bad class. Watch out because she frequently switches between English and Spanish as if they are the same language and it can get confusing.
Lovely professor. She's very spiritual. Also very fair. Her accent is a little hard to understand.
No Comments

Great class, you guys should definitely take this class from him.  It was pretty easy, didn't have very much homework, and he made sure we understood the assignments very well.  I did have some previous coding experience, so it made it extra easy for me, but even people with zero coding experience did amazing.  Definitely take this class from Bean.

Bean is the kind of professor who you know genuinely cares about your learning and growth. He sets project completion in tiers that produce the grade you're willing to work for: 'Baseline tier' = C, 'Core tier' = B, 'Stretch 1' = B+, 'Stretch 2' = A. Don't start projects late. Take the class with a buddy or be prepared to make new friends.

Absolute legend. Really caring and nice guy, starts each lecture with an amazing spiritual message, teaches really well. 5 exams (called progress-checks), each has infinite attempts. I would take him again in a heartbeat.

Professor Bean is amazing and so sweet! Warning though: he does not allow computers in class, which personally made it really hard for me to grasp some of the concepts. The class is relatively easy as long as you show up to class and stay on top of the homework.

I loved Professor Bean! He structures the class well and makes it easy to learn and get an A. He's great at answering questions and encouraging participation. He really cares, and is good at connecting the material to why it really matters. Even if I never code again, I learned great problem solving skills in this class.

Professor Bean is one of the best CS professors at BYU. He is great at explaining concepts and made 312 an easy class for me. Projects have definitely been improved this semester as most extraneous coding tasks were already completed for us. The exams felt appropriate and were even fun to complete at times.

I learned how computers handle memory management and how to write c++ stuff. Dr. Bean is a force for good, and an S tier lecturer. If you want a CS professor to model your life after, he is a good place to start. He has the same energy as Jensen if you know him.

I took this class when it was CS401R but it is now renamed to 301R. Agent engineering is a new field for most everyone involved and the course developed itself as we went, but Dr. Bean/Professor Jones were still able to build an effective curriculum that covered a lot of the emerging topics in the field. Semester project is a great resume builder!

His ratings seem misleading. I dropped his class for a different section after the first class. He seems to talk a lot without saying much. The class is structured, effective, and soft for an easy A, but it's religiously wired. Less of an intellectual environment and more of a spiritual one; one that felt toxic to me. I don't recommend. Good luck!
Excellent professor, teaches very well and is engaging and funny as well!

Bean is an amazing professor, although explaining sometimes a little fast. Concepts in this class are hard yet useful. My biggest complaint for when I took the class a bit ago were the TAs and how they graded. The grading criteria was not clear so sometimes they graded nice, other times brutal. There was no late work, but they might've changed.
Good teacher, actually brought the spirit into class without it detracting from the material. Good lectures, and seems to enjoy teaching!

If you know nothing about code or need a refresher, this is the professor for you. He taught things so simply and the lecture is genuinely engaging. He's also just a humble, nice, good person. Worth taking! I skipped the labs because he taught so well, I just did them with a buddy from the class

I took this spring term, and it was great. I have some basic coding experience, and the class was a breeze. 
Dr. Bean is hilarious and super willing to help his students. You will only get better at coding by participating and practicing yourself. Those who struggled didn't really try to apply themselves. TAs are also a great resource.

Dr. Bean is able to teach you more about the gospel in a 5 minute spiritual thought at the beginning of class than most religion profs are able to teach in an entire class period. Learning C++ is tough, but he's a great teacher. Follow his advice and try doing the assignments again after doing them once -- it'll help you actually learn the material
One of my all time favorite classes. Bean is a phenomenal teacher, and an even better man who will inspire you to be more than you were before.

This is the second class I have taken from Dr. Bean and there is a reason I keep coming back. Not only is he excellent at explaining new topics but he is also very willing to go back and explain things another way until everyone understands. Around 2 hw/week, unit progress checks (closed everything), 1 midterm, final (similar to progress checks).

Dr. Bean was a fantastic teacher. I don't enjoy computer science, but his lectures and the fact he cared about every person in the lecture hall kept me coming back. I think the material is a little mundane, but his teaching style is very interactive and encouraging when you make mistakes. He always encouraged us to make mistakes so that we grow.

Inspirational Teacher, focuses on you being an excellent programmer and person. Course is really tough but worth it. Hands down best CS professor you can pick at any level (I took 110 and 312 from him)

Lectures were entertaining and helpful. Every class began with a spiritual thought. He gave plenty of opportunity to work together in classes and to practice what we were learning. Dr. Bean cares a lot about his students and their wellbeing. Very accommodating. Also evidently has a passion for computer science and for teaching.

Awesome guy. Very funny and makes his lectures entertaining. Sadly, they are not necessary; all of the material is posted online so I stopped attending the second week to free up time. The class itself is a breeze, I had almost a perfect score with no prior coding experience. Still makes you learn a lot though.

I loved Dr. Bean. He starts each lecture with a great spiritual thought. His lectures are amazing and very useful. Attendance is not required. Super easy class if you do the homework. I would absolutely take him again and again.

This is not an easy class if you don't have any programming experience, but there are a lot of resources that make it doable. Dr. Bean is a great lecturer who is clearly passionate about the subject and cares for his students.

All the resources you need to succeed in CS110 are supplied on the website. The course is set up very well, Dr. Bean is a very charismatic lecturer, with that being said the lectures were almost never helpful and very easy to skip. His devotionals also eat up half of class which is more than a little exhaustive. Good in-class experience regardless.

CS 312 is a difficult topic and Dr. Bean teaches so well. He spends an hour before class prepping. That way when you go to lecture, he is prepared and is ready to answer. He is very firm but fair. Do not expect to turn in things late or get exceptions because you may receive a respectful no. This slides in this class will also help you.
Professor Bean is a fantastic teacher. The homework load can be a little heavy, but worth it.
The class is a lot of work, but Professor Bean is a wonderful teacher, and is very helpful. I would definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Bean is an amazing teacher. He really really cares about the success of his students and explains concepts in an engaging way. The class's biggest weakness is its lack of due dates. This killed a bit of the learning experience 'cause you know, I'm lazy sometimes. But keep up and it'll be an amazing experience!
Professor Bean was the best! I felt like he truly cares about his students. He was always willing and eager to help students if they were struggling.

Amazing class. Lots of resources to make sure you succeed. Not a slacking class by any means but if you are willing to work you will get a lot out of the class. Every lecture has a lab and homework assignment and projects at the end of each unit. Exams aren't worth much, grades are more heavily affected by projects.

I stopped going to class after the first couple weeks, because it was just easier to do it by myself. I loved going to class when I did because Dr Bean is an incredible person, and has set this class up perfectly for people who have no experience coding.

Dr Bean talks too much and doesn't teach enough. He explains concepts poorly. I found myself turning to the online lecture videos (by Dr Stephens) which were great. The class is not too bad - not too much homework. The final was way harder than he made it seem like it would be. His devotionals were too long and would stretch 30 minutes sometimes.

Dr. Bean is my all-time favorite professor at BYU. He is crazy good at explaining tough concepts, and the way CS110 is structured is very organized and easy to follow. He is a very inspirational guy, too. Five minutes before each lecture he essentially gives a mini BYU devotional. You'd be crazy not to take a class from THE Dr. Gordon Bean.

I can't say enough good things about this man! He's a brilliant teacher and a fantastic person. He is always mindful of his students and will do everything he can to help them succeed. If I could take every class from Dr. Bean, I would. He exemplifies Christlike teaching even while teaching something seemingly unrelated to the gospel.

Dr. Bean is an excellent professor. He lets his class go through the course according to their own timeframes. There are no due dates except for with tests and the last day of class. Dr. Bean is also passionate for this field, and he constantly encourages participation in his lectures. He is one of the best professors I've ever had in BYU.

Professor Bean is awesome! His lectures are great and he explains things in a really clear way that makes difficult concepts easier to understand. He is very good at fielding questions and keeping the lecture on topic and effective. My only criticism is that sometimes the spiritual thoughts were a little too long, taking up class time.

Dr. Bean is amazing. Explains things really well, is always available to meet and help on understanding or on projects. Will always invite the spirit into his lectures and is open to questions and improvement! Would highly recommend taking a class from him.

Dr. Bean was always so helpful and a GREAT introduction to CS. I eventually stopped going to lectures and labs, but that is only because the material was pretty easy. If you are taking 110, take Bean.

Dr. Bean is an AWESOME professor! 312 is generally a difficult class, but Bean does a great job of going over information in a way that makes sense. He gives plentiful advice for labs and targets his lectures to fit the needs of the homework. He also talked about the weekly devotionals, which provided a nice reprieve from all the information.

Dr. Bean is awesome! He does a great job teaching difficult concepts and always tried to bring the spirit in class. He also cares a lot about his students. The labs and some of the concepts are difficult but Bean does a great job of trying to give his students all the possible tools to succeed. I would definitely take another class from him.

Love Doctor Bean! Made so many opportunities for kids to be able to pass the class and so many resources available for help. TA lab available almost 24/7 and encouraged to work with peers in bi-weekly labs. Did have extra-credit survey and brought the Spirit into class. TAs were also awesome. This class made my head hurt at times but glad I took it

What with CS110 being a new course this year, it's no surprise that it was a little rocky when it came to the organization of the classwork. Luckily Gordon Bean is fantastic at hearing his student's needs and helping them respond. Lecture is not required but I would recommend it (he publishes the lectures). Labs are the hardest part. He's awesome.

Professor Bean is a really great guy and super nice. There were a few times throughout the semester where he felt a little unprepared for lectures but I'd attribute that to being his first semester teaching the course and I'm sure he'll be more confident when he teaches it next year. Was always willing to do his best to accomodate students.

312 is a tough class, but I think Dr. Bean did a great job in his first semester teaching this course. There were some times when he ran out of time to cover a topic that was in the homework, and sometimes his spiritual thoughts took up too much class time. You can tell he cares about his students. Attendance isn't required, but it's very helpful.

I really liked Dr. Bean as a person and I enjoyed listening to his lectures. I do have complaints about CS 312, but this is his first semester teaching it and he didn't have much say in the organization of the course. Definitely would take him again though.

Only complaint is that sometimes his spiritual thoughts take too long.

I actually took him for CS 110, and it was pretty good. I had a lot of previous experience in Java and some experience in C++, but I had never done Python, so I decided to start with this class. Dr. Bean does a great job of explaining his logic in problems and working through things. He is actually one of the most goated people I have ever met

Lots of homework. Several lectures where he does not fully explain concepts even though they are on the next homework assignment. He spends too much of the start of each lecture not teaching so the end of every lecture is rushed.

Dr. Bean is new to teaching, and he treats lectures like standup comedy bits. CS 312 is a difficult class and we frequently don't cover critical things because he spends a lot of time talking about his personal life and cracking low quality jokes. He also taught his own ways to solve labs that were not in line with the course and confused students.

I was extremely nervous about taking CS235. The class is difficult, sure. His office hours were amazing, he really wants you to succeed, will sometimes adjust assignments if the bulk of the class is not understanding, AND he is not super high and mighty like many professors at BYU. I usually left his classes feeling inspired, uplifted, and trusted.

This was Dr Bean's first semester at BYU and he did a great job. He is really good at explaining the concepts of the course, and I understood everything really well. Labs were a little tricky but that's just 235 for you. Dr Bean is so merciful and I really appreciated that.  I am so glad that I took this class with Dr Bean.

Dr. Bean is an excellent professor and teacher. He uses lecture slides on projector screen and demonstrates ideas in how to code various functions for the data structures we learned, such as linked lists or binary trees. He was very understanding when students' weeks were busy and extended due dates for lab assignments.

I haven't left a review here before, but I felt I had to because Professor Bean is new at BYU, (this semester was his first) and make sure people knew how great he is. CS235 is a difficult class, with the labs taking a lot of time, but he is amazing at explaining CS concepts. He really cares about and relates to students. Take him if you can!

Dr. Bean is probably my favorite professor at BYU so far! He makes CS fun and makes a real effort to help his students succeed. There is a textbook, but I barely touched it. He doesn't take attendance, but I highly recommend going. He explains concepts well and will often walk through how to code a project similar to the assignments. 10/10

Professor Bean is an amazing person. He really cares about his students and their success. He will change projects if they are too difficult and is always willing to answer any question. He gives good insights about life in general and really knows coding. The material is difficult but he explains it well. I overall really enjoyed the class.

Dr. Bean is a ton of fun to have and it's easy to tell he really cares about his students. He's always willing to give his time to help you outside of class with anything you don't understand and is very good at giving feedback that not only helps you solve the problem, but helps you learn! C S 235 is a tough class, but Bean's got your back.

I walked out of this class many times thinking about how cool some of the ideas we talked about were. While readings can get a bit dry, I was fine if I skimmed them and paid attention in the lecture. Only two papers the whole semester, neither of which I felt were very difficult or strictly graded. He gives you all the test questions ahead of time.

I wasn't a huge fan of Gordy. His lectures got off topic very easily and gave all the coursework in the second half of the semester. He only has you talk with TAs and doesn't seem to care about how we do. Class is decently easy and grades are decently fair but I wouldn't take a class from him again.

guys im in the second day of his class and its ridiculous. bro just talks and talks and you have no clue what you need to know. also he's always yelling?? ik this class covers two GEs but literally do not take. he made us get NINE books from the bookstore. Shakespeare and other boring books and you have to read ALL of them. goodbye fr. im dropping
Gotta love Dr. Mower. Take a philosophy class from him sometime. He does go on tangents but doesn't expect you to remember them. He is always super excited to discuss that day's topic.

Gordy Mower is a solid choice for an online class. He made his lectures easily accessible and always posted at the same time every day of class. Very few things graded so you have to make sure to do well, however they are graded easy-ish. (Participation Quizzes - 25%, Midterm - 25%, Term Paper - 25%, Final - 25%)
It is impossible to understand what he wants in your assignments and papers. His lectures are very hard to sit through. It takes ages for him to respond to any questions or concerns.

Dr. Mower seems like a teacher that would be amazing in person but when it comes to Zoom he struggles. His class is teaching great things but he teaches it in a way that can make it hard to ask questions and it can be hard to understand what he is looking for in assignments. Overall he is a cool guy but in the world of Zoom I would not recommend.

Prof Mower is the best! I think rmp underrates him. No need to memorize weird things at all like other profs for a GE in byu. If you are a good note-taker you will do well in this class. Everything from lecture will be on the test and I didn't read a lot of the textbook but I managed to get an A.

Weakness: Can be disorganized, a bit intimidating, and falls behind schedule. Strength: Extremely knowledgeable, entertaining, insightful, and willing to help students succeed. If you just need his class for a GE and dont really like philosophy, his class probably isn't for you. For philosophy majors, he's a great lecturer and easy grader.
Gordy Mower is the Anne of Green Gables trifecta: divinely beautiful, dazzlingly clever, and angelically good.

Took a total of 5 classes at BYU from Professor Mower. He was always kind, easy to work with, quick to respond to emails, brilliant and hilarious. His course format is the traditional 2 tests and 2 papers a semester.
BEST PROFESSOR IVE HAD AT BYU. He is honestly such a great resource, extremely intelligent and has incredible lectures. He ALWAYS is there for his students to learn.

He is extremely intelligent, probably one of the most intelligent professors on campus and has incredible lectures. He does well to help students really understand the material. If you support your arguments in papers, he will give you full credit(that is what I did) and he sincerely wants everyone to do well.  Most beneficial class I have taken.

Professor Mower really makes you think about the way you think. He wants to make you think for yourself and to have your own opinions. He teaches out of the book but also what he thinks we need to know. Doctor Mower makes does give out a lot of essays but these wrap up everything we were taught very nicely.

Dr. Mower is passionate about philosophy and I enjoyed his class on contemporary political philosophy. His lectures are extensive and the course is well structured, even if he diverges from the syllabus to explain better other concepts. He will work with you concerning your career interests and wants you to succeed. One of the best at BYU!

Not sure what class the people below me were in, but Mower is one of the most entertaining lecturers on campus. Additionally, he is an extremely intelligent person. If you didn't recognize that, then it all went over your head. Yes he's opinionated and will push back a due date now and then, but that won't stop me from taking more classes from him

Prof Mower is a good guy, but not clear in his expectations. If you do not agree with him, even if you love and study philosophy such as I do, he grades you harshly because you disagree with him. If you are okay with regurgitating information, then he is fine, but if you cherish independent or different thought, then he is not the professor for you

Dr. Mower is an amazing professor because he makes philosophy not only entertaining but very interesting. He is also very helpful. However, there is a lot of reading in his courses, primarily for citing and writing papers. Nonetheless, my writing has sky rocketed and I am all the better for it. Take his classes-- They are life changing!

I had Dr. Mower for Phil 150 and this class is a lot harder. It's very interesting but the papers are pretty tough. The prompt is close to 3 pages and your papers have to be 1000 words or less. It's pretty tough to do everything that he asks.  Other than that, the lectures themselves are pretty enjoyable if you like to question things.
Frustrating because the expectations are so unclear in EVERYTHING. He's a nice guy but probably one of my most dreaded classes.
Dr. Mower is very passionate about philosophy but has a hard time making it clear and understandable. Expect lots of tangents. But he does give lots of extra credit opportunities.
