Dr. Madsen is awesome. The class was Economic Policy from Roosevelt to Reagan, and never has a class given such a wonderful narrative of where we are in the world as this class has.

Loved his class. There's a lot of reading, but every history class is like that. He's young, fun, and really wants to help you do well. He frequently asked for the class's opinion on how tough assignments were and what he should change. Open book quizzes every 1-2 weeks, open book final and midterm, and one short paper were the only assignments.

There was a good amount of reading, but it was all applicable. He always asked and heard everyone's responses in how we felt about the readings and if it was too much. He would cut a lot of things down and all the tests were open book and open note. He is quick to respond to emails and always wanted people to come to his office. Very helpful.
easy and interesting professor

Professor Carling is so passionate about geology! I took the Water Planet version of this class and I learned so much as a non-science major. This class is applicable to everyone and helps you understand how to make the world better! He's super understanding and helpful, he really cares about his students' success. And the field trip was so fun!

This is the best way to get your physical science credit at BYU and Dr. Carling is the nicest professor ever. I had some untreated thyroid problems that made it hard for me to get a good grade but under normal circumstances it would be easy to do well, and I still did okay. The best part was how he made a class on water so spiritual which was lit.

I took Water Planet with him, and it was amazing. The way he ties the gospel into every lesson was so cool. For the Physical Science credit, this class was very easy. Assignments due Mon, Wed, Fri, and Sat, but they're always easy. Barely studied and I did well. Highly recommend! You will gain such a deeper understanding of the world.

He was ok but he did not know 2/3 of the content he was teaching us. He told me how he has not looked at chem or physics for around 20 years. For those lectures and questions the TA's would answer it all the time. He knows geology but nothing else! Take the class from someone else!

Professor Carling is a very sweet guy but isn't very knowledgeable about Physical Science. He many times doesn't know how to answer questions and makes his TA's answer almost every question. I ended up going to the lectures from other professors since attendance wasn't mandatory. Other professors teach it much better

PHYS100 is taught by different professors, but all the material, hw, & tests are the exact same. Dr Carling is so nice, but it is obvious he isn't a chem or physics professor. He often asks the TA's for help answering questions and it was hard to understand his explanations. I'm sure he's a great geo prof. but take PHY S 100 from someone else!
He is the sweetest professor and his class was super organized!
Not the most interesting subject but it was still a great class, I learned a lot and if you put in the work its super easy to get a great grade.

This class was good and honestly pretty fun. He taught it joint with Professor Lemont and focused on hydrology rather than geology. It sometimes felt like both an on-demand and a live class at the same time Weekly quizzes too, sometimes they were easy and sometimes unnecessarily hard. Lectures sometimes felt like rambles rather than information.

I took the water world version of this course and it was very easy but also very good. We learned a lot of very interesting stuff and didn't have to stress about studying too much. If you show up to class and pay attention in addition to doing the very easy weekly assignments then you will do just fine. He practically says what's on the test.

Professor Carling is the sweetest guy on the planet. But, his lectures are pretty boring and the tests can be tricky. He gives lots of other assignments but they're usually a little bit boring. Not the most exciting class but I would definitely recommend taking this as a GE. The best part of this class was the field trip!

My geology 101 class focused entirely on water, which Professor Carling is very passionate about! The tests are incredibly easy and taken online- you should be golden if you do all the modules on Canvas, come to class, and take notes during lecture. There wasn't even a final exam! I'm BEGGING you to take this as a GE. Best decision I ever made.

This class isn't the worst but definitely not the best. It's definitely a easy A class if you are about that life but for the average student just trying to get the GE done then you can pass. Prepare to do everything online because it feels like an online class and there is a ton of homework.

Such a Christlike man. The class was hard and they didn't make it easy, but I loved Professor Carling. I wouldn't take another class just because it was poorly designed, but he is a good man and will make you feel welcome.
I skipped a few lectures, and I got a 101%. However, I felt bad after skipping, so I started going back. That's the kind of professor he is: You don't want to let him down.

An assignment or lab every week, 2.5 field trips, two exams. The exam review used to be extremely helpful until a nosy person reported the professor claiming the TA has given too much information on the exam, so our final exam review becomes no use at all. there's a study guide but it asks you to read the whole textbook again to find the answers.

Dr. Carling is so sweet! He is soft spoken and gentle! This class is super easy and has ample opportunities for extra credit. Flashcards and simple labs make up pretty much all your grade. One midterm and a final! Super easy and interesting!

5+ Definitely my favorite professor! He has a passion for geology, but he is amazing at explaining it at the most basic level, and his love meant that nothing was just busywork. There is a lot of reading, with open-note 15-question quizzes for every chapter that can be a little rough if you miss a point. Some work, but recommend!
This class was fun! Professor Carling is very kind and respectful. I enjoyed taking his class.

Professor Carling is quiet but quirky, in a good way. He is passionate about geology and you can see it when he is lecturing. There is an in class quiz type thing every class, you can miss class sometimes, but you'll get points off for missing the quiz. The lectures can get kind of boring, but it is about rocks and earth processes. Pretty easy.

Prof. Carling is very quirky and kind. He is always good about answering questions. The slides that he shows in class are through TopHat online, so you don't necessarily need to go to the class as long as you're following along and answering the questions as you go.

Prof. Carling made this class way harder than it had to be for a 101 GE class. The homework was relatively easy but the tests were obscure and many of the questions were debatable. There's also lots of vocab so if you want an easy GE, this is not the one.

Prof. Carling is very quiet and calm. I fell asleep a lot in his classes. He used TopHat for participation and attendance. I found the class to be somewhat easy. I didn't study as much as I could have for the tests, so that impacted my grade. I have heard that he is better than Skinner because he doesn't use the book!

I don't find the stuff taught in class very exciting, so I thought the class was extremely boring. The tests are fair, and the powerpoints he uses in lecture are clear and available to study off of. The class isn't difficult. We had one field trip assignment.

Took this class for a GE and ended up loving it! Pro. Carling cares about your success. He knows his stuff and communicates it in an easy-to-understand way. Field trips were fun & homework was not difficult at all. For tests, study vocab, lecture notes & the slides and you'll do fine. But don't miss class or you'll be in a world of hurt!
Great class. Prepares you to work in teams on projects that matter.

He's very helpful and so are the TAs. He goes over unclear points from the previous class. Frequent assignments and quizzes but they're online and pretty easy. He's got a kind of dry, dad-like humor thats pretty funny. He knows his stuff. Good class.

Great teacher and cares about you, but the class was more intense than it needed to be, with long, tedious assignments due with alarming frequency.  The pre-class quizzes were often very aggravating, because they covered material that was hard to find in the confusing book.  Easy grading for tests and amazing field trip. More engineering than geol.

Super kind teacher with a completely un-engaging lecture style. He gives you a lot of freedom in what to write about for big projects, which I loved. Tests felt really fair. Make sure to follow syllabus guidelines about original work, because he's very serious about them and will give zeroes if not followed.

I took Anthr 209 -- Intercultural Communication -- with Greg and I loved it! There was a lot of reading, but all the readings were important, interesting and relevant to class. I could really tell that he cares about his field of study. Lectures were always interesting and really got me thinking!

I took this class Fall of 2024 and hated it. This class was the most stressful class I had and I was taking Calculus 2. The class is focused around doing an ethnography, but Prof. Thompson did not cover the expectations or how to conduct the hours of research needed for it. The only reason I survived this class was because I had an incredible TA.

The textbook Dr. Thompson chose for this class was excellent. The Friday TA labs were also good. The project asks a lot, but overall, this is a good class.
The lectures are the weakest point. At one point, Dr. Thompson fell behind, which led to days where he lectured on stuff we had already been tested on, which got frustrating and boring.

If you actually do the readings and sit through the lectures this class is a piece of cake. Weekly quizzes on friday with TA's that are really helpful. Very thorough study guide for the Final that should be a piece of cake as long as you have actually previously done the readings and took a few notes.

Large class with many TAs. There was a decent bit of assignments outside of class but most of these were graded for completion. Rubrics for all assignments. Weekly quizzes and discussion in TA labs on readings and lectures. Very thorough study guide provided for final. "Textbook" was just a book that taught about anthropology and was interesting.

Please consider taking another class. Professor Thompson assigned so much reading and we often didn't cover the reading in the lecture because he rambled so much. The final project was too much work and it brought so much unnecessary stress. My TA was knowledgeable, but unhelpful during the lab and wouldn't respond to my emails.

I enjoyed most of his lectures and he is a fair grader. Although he is a tad scattered when he sidetracks into other anthropological discourses. Just be warned that once the lectures get behind, your scores begin to drop because he has specific answers to questions that are only found in the lectures.

If you work with your TA and do the readings, you can do this class. If you aren't interested in Anthropology and you have a bad attitude, you will not enjoy this class. Not an easy A. The readings are tough, but mind opening if you really consider them. 
He describes the assignments well IN class (you should go to class).

Lectures were disorganized and rambling, readings were dense and extensive, and the main project was extensive (15+ hours outside of class) and everything was graded slowly. Rubrics were rarely clear and often changed at the last minute. Homework load was honestly ridiculous. Don't take from Dr. Thompson if you want free time or an easy class.

gives vague descriptions on assignments and when asked for clarification, he just refers you back to the vague descriptions. not very organized and he kind of just rambles in lecture. Its almost like he doesn't know what his TA's are putting on learning suite and doesn't care

Terrible class. So much reading, talking like 50 pages twice a week. Attendance is not required except for friday TA labs which quiz on what was gone over in lecture. Not good at presenting the things you need to know. Most of grade comes from massive projects that are way too much for an intro level class. Not clear with what is expected in projec

Attended lecture twice the entire semester. HOWEVER attendance is mandatory for TA labs once a week. LOTS of reading and tedious ethnography project that includes interviewing, writing a 10 page paper of your field notes, time log, and 6-8 pg paper. Another 2-3 page paper on one of the textbooks, three one page page papers on events out of lecture.

Great guy!! The class is honestly pretty easy. Attend the lectures and actually do the assigned reading beforehand (skimming is a solid enough foundation for the lecture), and you'll be just fine. The instructions for the writing assignments are sometimes pretty vague, but if you work closely with your TA on it you'll get 100% every time.

Dr. Thompson is a professor who genuinely cares about his students. I have taken multiple classes from him and he has always gone above and beyond to help me succeed. He listens to his students, wants them to participate and to really get the course material. If you put the work in, you will get an A in his class. One of the best anthr profs at BYU

He has the perfect attitude that an Anthropologist needs, he looks at all sides of the picture and loves hearing student input. He yearns to make every lecture more of a discussion. The class I took with him was Summer 2020, so it was done over Zoom and he still managed to make every student want to participate.
I have taken multiple courses from Dr. Thompson and I have loved each and every one. He teaches simply and clearly, and he has a sincere interest in the success of his students.

Class isn't that bad. Lot's of Freshmen complained about work load, so he lightened it up even. Tests you could type notes and print it out. Weekly quizzes weren't too hard. Just do the reading and type everything on the slides and you'll be fine. Just print small font for the 4 pages of notes on the test. Ethnography is bearable. Extra Credit too.

If you're just taking it for the GE it can be extremely hard from Professor Thompson. He's very knowledgeable about the subject, however his lectures can get very confusing sometimes. The material is heavy for the class, lots of reading and writing. There's a huge project and quizzes every week on homework and what happened in class.

I've taken quite a few classes from Greg and I have loved all of them. He is really good at being available for his students and helping them make the most out the class. I would definitely recommend going in for office hours if you have questions or want feedback on anything.

He gave us over six papers to write, some of them with a requirement of 10 pages long. There was a huge project where you have to spend six hours observing an activity of your choice and write about it. Over 40 pages of reading every time you come to class, and all of it was difficult to understand. Quizzes on reading every week in labs.

Difficult reading. Harsh grading. Disorganized class. I still don't understand anthropology. Greg's a cool guy, very knowledgeable on his subject. He cut back a lot of the workload. But I don't think he knows how to teach students at a beginning level. The expectations were a little too high for a 101 class. Only take it if you like anthropology.

Despite a lot of negative ratings, I wouldn't have wanted to take Anthro 101 from any other professor. . His lectures are great and require you to do the readings and understand the concepts in order to understand why he's saying certain things. I learned a ton! If you want an easy A, don't take it from him. But if you want to learn, do it!!

Worst professor ever! Outrageous homework load! Most distracted professor I have ever had! Hardly ever covers what we were supposed to. I got in a car accident THAT WASNT MY FAULT and had to change my project topic cause I didnt have a car to get me to the places I needed to study. Docked me half for it! Least understanding professor I ever had!!

Thompson is smart but isn't the best for large lecture-classes. Lectures super aren't straightforward or easy to understand. Assignment heavy at end of term, be prepared for that. Not alot of explanation for the final project, you're basically on your own.

P. Thompson is a nice guy but that doesn't make you a good teacher. He seems to be a good anthropologist but definitely can improve as a teacher. His lectures weren't good and he just went around and around in circles with hardly any good explanations. There was a ton of homework that was really difficult and time consuming. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

Dr. Thompson is genuinely one of the best teachers I have ever had. He does have a lot of assignments, but they are manageable and they all help in understanding the course material. He showed me that anthropology concepts can be applicable in most any discipline, not just in anthropology/social sciences. Thanks Dr. T!
There is absolutely no reason for Dr. Thompson to make this class as difficult as it is. He gives an outrageous amount of big projects, and then is a very tough grader on those projects.

I loved Dr. Thompson's class! It's no easy A but he's really good at explaining hard concepts. He's really flexible to meet outside of class and wants his students to understand the basics of anthropology in a meaningful and fun way. A lot of the assignments are due at the end of the semester but if you work on it early on you'll be fine!

P. Thompson is a nice guy, but this class is just ridiculous. There is an insane amount of reading for a 101 class. Literally with only 17 days left of the semester, we have only received 37% of our grade. All of his major assignments are at the end of the semester, and they are incredibly time consuming. I would never take this class again.

Lectures are boring. Time consuming. All the hw is in the last month. I wish someone had told me not to take this class. I haven't met someone who liked it yet. I'm writing this to save you PLEASE HEAR ME

This class was absolutely terrible. Professor Thompson is nice, but this class was WAY too much work for an entry level class. The lectures were boring. The assigned readings were very long and boring. The amount of homework was too much. This class was awful.
Extremely disorganized, not great at giving lectures. Piles all the work on the last month. Do not take his anthr 101 class. May be great for other classes, but NOT this one.

Professor Thompson is one of the best professors in the Anthropology department. He really cares a lot about each student and is invested in their future. Keep on top of deadlines; the class has a lot of reading and a few papers throughout the semester. If you are need help with papers (or life in general) you can easily go in and talk to him.
Greg is a great guy-a little goofy, but he really cares about every student individually, and helping every project along the best he can, providing excellent feedback.

Learned a lot. TAs do most of the grading, but Professor Jolley is willing to listen if you believe your grade is not justified. Class requires high quality work, but individual creativity is encouraged as well.

Greg is Awesome! Lots of good extra credit opportunities to help in case you don't do good on a test or assignment. Make sure you read the rubric for the drawings, they are very time consuming. The class can be super rewarding as long as you are willing to put in some time in the labs. Even just for a GE you should take this class!

Greg is the coolest prof. I love the guy. BUT PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AS A GE. Most time consuming class for me this semester, and I'm taking American Heritage. I put so much time into drawing my little plant symbols just to lose tons of points from his picky TA's. They are nice but really harsh graders! If this ain't your major, don't do it.

Such a great professor!! There are a few time-consuming projects but you will do well if you ask for feedback and follow the rubric!! Jolley always takes the time to answer questions, making sure that you understand and is super willing to help students outside of class!!I am taking 2 more classes from him this semester bc I loved him so much lol

Greg himself is a good professor. He is really nice and caring and understands that several students in the class are only taking it for an art credit, but some of his TA's do not understand that. They are incredibly picky on the projects. The projects are insanely time consuming and the expectations are super unclear from TA's.

Greg is a wonderful teacher who goes above and beyond his responsibilities to help his students. He uses examples in class from his own career for irrigating and design and makes the lectures applicable. Sure, sometimes the lectures can be a little dry, but that may just be due to the days' subject matter. He expects you to work hard, b/c he does!

This class is really hard for a GE. The projects make up most of your grade, and they are very very time consuming. If you're looking for an easy art credit, this isn't it. That being said, the class is actually pretty interesting and Prof. Jolley is amazing, but I still would't recommend because of all the time the projects take.

Greg is an awesome guy, however, the class he teaches lowkey sucks. I anticipated this class, which fulfilled my art credit, to be essentially a bunch of completion grades, but no, the TAs love dinging you for the smallest of mistakes. Every other week or so, there is a humangeous project that takes a very long time. THIS IS NOT AN EASY A.

Even with the pandemic, Greg was very flexible with his students and was very accommodating, he teaches great from his own personal experiences. The TAs often do not grade fairly, even when you get positive feedback prior to submission and then they give you a grade that they could have prevented by giving you feedback in the first place.

Greg is clear and precise and doesnt care if you are a good artist or not. I appreciate the approach to projects as he gives plenty of time to work on. Go to class! He gives tips, tricks, and will help you a lot! Greg appreciates working hard, so if you put the effort and time in you will be just fine. Do NOT leave projects till the last minute.

Greg is awesome! Funny, caring guy. The class is interesting, the assignments are time consuming but Greg and the TAs are always around to answer questions and help you. Only 2 tests, a few practice assignments, then a giant final project that they give you 2 months to work on.

Greg is the nicest guy ever!! He understands that being an artist isn't easy so a lot of it is your own efforts to improve. A few of his TAs are incredibly intense when it comes to grading because they expect it to be perfect (which is dumb since we don't have the experience they do). If you want critique, go to Greg, not the TAs.

The first thing Greg said about this class is that you can do good even if your "not a good artist. But I think the TAs got creative with taking points off for no reason. This class is not an easy A. Also the assignments had nothing to do with the lectures. Its really said, but I don't think I learned a single thing in this class.

I was really looking forward to this class because I thought it would be fun, but I was mistaken. The grading is unclear and ridiculous. I would spend hours on assignments, yet the grades would never show. The TAs weren't helpful at all because they would just give you their opinions instead of actually helping you. Do not take this as a GE.

Greg is great! His projects for PWS 103 can be a lot of work if you drag them out, but they are a lot of fun. He's very involved in helping us and super friendly. Also very spiritual and loves to pull the world landscaping together with the Gospel.

One of my favorite professors. Super nice guy and helpful during labs. However, the projects in this class were incredibly time consuming and the TA's graded WAY too hard. I always got help from the TA's and they said it looked good but I always received a lower score than expected.

Greg is great!. He sets the class out in phases where each phase grows on each other until it turns into the final project. Each project will take 10-20 hours if you want to get a good grade on it. He gives you 2-3 weeks for the project. If you procrastinate his projects you won't pass. If you show up pay attention and seek help you'll be fine!

His class was by far the most ridiculously graded and time consuming class I have EVER taken at BYU. The projects take an absurd amount of time and you are expected to be a very advanced from the get go and are graded that way. Tests are extremely nit picky (as in line by line) about details from the readings. Would not recommend for a GE AT ALL.
I really learned a lot from Professor Jolley in this class. He is a fun engaging and inspirational teacher! I would totally take more classes from him! I have heard that PWS 103 with him is great!

Greg is Wonderful! He is one of the most caring and best professors I have ever taken from. He is the kind of professor you can get to know him on a personal level. I loved all the classes that I have taken from Greg.
This is a great class, especially if you love art, business, or science. This is a great class to take for fun or convince you to join the Landscape Management major!

Worst class I have ever taken.  Studied tons for the tests and still got Cs on both. (usually A or A- student.)  When I asked about a grade on the project, he told me I probably deserved a few more points but refused to give them to me.  The project is awful; they do not explain what you have to do well & the profs & TAs tell you different things.

Greg is a very good teacher with a lot of working experience since he worked as  a professional for many years.  He makes the assignments very clear and participation in class counts towards your final grade. So show up and do the assignments and it wont be hard to get a good grade.

Greg was such a great teacher. I got married last semester and he was very flexible and understanding. Pretty simple class and really fun drawing assignments. The class has two midterms taken from the lectures and book and then multiple drawing assignments that do take a while so just start them early and you will definitely get an A.

Greg is AWESOME! He's really chill, makes class interesting(always has a funny video which doesn't relate to class), and he's very willing to help you personally. He has lots of field experience but teaches from the book too so read the book and go to class(he'll bump your grade up if you do). I'd recommend him to anyone. Loved his class!

It's impossible to not love Greg. He's that loveable teacher who starts most classes with a youtube video or story that has no relation to you class. He is willing to help students who ask and will go over difficult concepts with you many times. Don't buy the Structures book unless you really want to, there's one in the lab if you need to use it.

If you are good at drawing and are willing to put in a good amount of time on your assignments, I don't see you getting less than an A. I am not an artist, and I recognize the disadvantage. I am trying my best. The tests are fair.If I get an A, it will be because I will have made major changes for my final drawing and got an A on the last test.

Awesome teacher, he is by far one of my favorite teachers that I have had while at BYU.  He is very fair about grading and if you take the time to do the assignment you will get a good grade.  You have to spend a lot of time in the design lab but don't procrastinate and you'll do great.

Greg is an awesome teacher. He's really chill and he's always willing to help. His teaching method is just teaching from the book and using powerpoint. There's about four projects that will take at least 12 hours to complete but other than that this class is great!

Greg Jolley is a great guy and a good teacher - and very experienced in the landscaping field which makes his feedback really helpful, and he's one of those professors that really wants you to do well in his class and get to know you.

He is a very good teacher. Very helpful.  His TA wasn't the most helpful person, but perhaps that will change in the future.  Unless you are persuing landscaping as a career, do not buy the book. It is very expensive and you hardly use it.

Wonderful!  Wish I could have him for more classes.  Extremely helpful with class material and anything else you need.  Teaches what you need to know in the real world, not just out of the book.  Honestly cares about the students.  Great guy - highly recommended!

He is an amazing teacher.  He really cares about his students and he is really good at explaning things the way that you need it learn it.  It is impossible to no become friends with this guy. He is a fair teacher as well. Very recommended.

Super kind teacher with a completely un-engaging lecture style. He gives you a lot of freedom in what to write about for big projects, which I loved. Tests felt really fair. Make sure to follow syllabus guidelines about original work, because he's very serious about them and will give zeroes if not followed.

I took Anthr 209 -- Intercultural Communication -- with Greg and I loved it! There was a lot of reading, but all the readings were important, interesting and relevant to class. I could really tell that he cares about his field of study. Lectures were always interesting and really got me thinking!

I took this class Fall of 2024 and hated it. This class was the most stressful class I had and I was taking Calculus 2. The class is focused around doing an ethnography, but Prof. Thompson did not cover the expectations or how to conduct the hours of research needed for it. The only reason I survived this class was because I had an incredible TA.

The textbook Dr. Thompson chose for this class was excellent. The Friday TA labs were also good. The project asks a lot, but overall, this is a good class.
The lectures are the weakest point. At one point, Dr. Thompson fell behind, which led to days where he lectured on stuff we had already been tested on, which got frustrating and boring.

If you actually do the readings and sit through the lectures this class is a piece of cake. Weekly quizzes on friday with TA's that are really helpful. Very thorough study guide for the Final that should be a piece of cake as long as you have actually previously done the readings and took a few notes.

Large class with many TAs. There was a decent bit of assignments outside of class but most of these were graded for completion. Rubrics for all assignments. Weekly quizzes and discussion in TA labs on readings and lectures. Very thorough study guide provided for final. "Textbook" was just a book that taught about anthropology and was interesting.

Please consider taking another class. Professor Thompson assigned so much reading and we often didn't cover the reading in the lecture because he rambled so much. The final project was too much work and it brought so much unnecessary stress. My TA was knowledgeable, but unhelpful during the lab and wouldn't respond to my emails.

I enjoyed most of his lectures and he is a fair grader. Although he is a tad scattered when he sidetracks into other anthropological discourses. Just be warned that once the lectures get behind, your scores begin to drop because he has specific answers to questions that are only found in the lectures.

If you work with your TA and do the readings, you can do this class. If you aren't interested in Anthropology and you have a bad attitude, you will not enjoy this class. Not an easy A. The readings are tough, but mind opening if you really consider them. 
He describes the assignments well IN class (you should go to class).

Lectures were disorganized and rambling, readings were dense and extensive, and the main project was extensive (15+ hours outside of class) and everything was graded slowly. Rubrics were rarely clear and often changed at the last minute. Homework load was honestly ridiculous. Don't take from Dr. Thompson if you want free time or an easy class.

Difficult reading. Harsh grading. Disorganized class. I still don't understand anthropology. Greg's a cool guy, very knowledgeable on his subject. He cut back a lot of the workload. But I don't think he knows how to teach students at a beginning level. The expectations were a little too high for a 101 class. Only take it if you like anthropology.

Despite a lot of negative ratings, I wouldn't have wanted to take Anthro 101 from any other professor. . His lectures are great and require you to do the readings and understand the concepts in order to understand why he's saying certain things. I learned a ton! If you want an easy A, don't take it from him. But if you want to learn, do it!!

Worst professor ever! Outrageous homework load! Most distracted professor I have ever had! Hardly ever covers what we were supposed to. I got in a car accident THAT WASNT MY FAULT and had to change my project topic cause I didnt have a car to get me to the places I needed to study. Docked me half for it! Least understanding professor I ever had!!

Thompson is smart but isn't the best for large lecture-classes. Lectures super aren't straightforward or easy to understand. Assignment heavy at end of term, be prepared for that. Not alot of explanation for the final project, you're basically on your own.

P. Thompson is a nice guy but that doesn't make you a good teacher. He seems to be a good anthropologist but definitely can improve as a teacher. His lectures weren't good and he just went around and around in circles with hardly any good explanations. There was a ton of homework that was really difficult and time consuming. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

Dr. Thompson is genuinely one of the best teachers I have ever had. He does have a lot of assignments, but they are manageable and they all help in understanding the course material. He showed me that anthropology concepts can be applicable in most any discipline, not just in anthropology/social sciences. Thanks Dr. T!
There is absolutely no reason for Dr. Thompson to make this class as difficult as it is. He gives an outrageous amount of big projects, and then is a very tough grader on those projects.

I loved Dr. Thompson's class! It's no easy A but he's really good at explaining hard concepts. He's really flexible to meet outside of class and wants his students to understand the basics of anthropology in a meaningful and fun way. A lot of the assignments are due at the end of the semester but if you work on it early on you'll be fine!

P. Thompson is a nice guy, but this class is just ridiculous. There is an insane amount of reading for a 101 class. Literally with only 17 days left of the semester, we have only received 37% of our grade. All of his major assignments are at the end of the semester, and they are incredibly time consuming. I would never take this class again.

Lectures are boring. Time consuming. All the hw is in the last month. I wish someone had told me not to take this class. I haven't met someone who liked it yet. I'm writing this to save you PLEASE HEAR ME

This class was absolutely terrible. Professor Thompson is nice, but this class was WAY too much work for an entry level class. The lectures were boring. The assigned readings were very long and boring. The amount of homework was too much. This class was awful.
Extremely disorganized, not great at giving lectures. Piles all the work on the last month. Do not take his anthr 101 class. May be great for other classes, but NOT this one.

Professor Thompson is one of the best professors in the Anthropology department. He really cares a lot about each student and is invested in their future. Keep on top of deadlines; the class has a lot of reading and a few papers throughout the semester. If you are need help with papers (or life in general) you can easily go in and talk to him.
Greg is a great guy-a little goofy, but he really cares about every student individually, and helping every project along the best he can, providing excellent feedback.

301 was my first but not last class from Dr. Wurm. Genuinely knows theory, loves sociology, and cares about his students. He was very open to feedback and is always shaping his classes for the students. Do the readings, participate in class, and ask questions and you'll be fine. Listen to the song Dr. Worm to get in the mood for Dr. Wurm's class.

I've taken Social Inquiry and Sociology of Religion from the big Wurm. One of the kindest and most genuine professors at BYU, he is endlessly curious and wants to learn from his students. He is always available to students and responds to emails lightning quick! You'll read a LOT. Like so much. But the content is incredibly worth it.

I loved Prof. Wurms' Social Inquiry/Theory class. You will read a lot, but there's some really great material in there. Wurm is very inquisitive and likes to explore questions with students. Would recommend.

Oh sweet Wurm. He is a great fellow and is super caring and chill, but class just felt pointless to attend at a point. He is quite prone to tangents and it felt like there was no structure to his lectures or motivation to get through the content he needed to get through each class. It's easy to get an A but hard to stay engaged.

Dr. Wurm is great! He is a really easy grader and is super flexible and willing to work with students. Sometimes his lectures can go on tangents or be confusing, but he is always willing to answer questions and clarify, and his tangents are always relevant to the class.

I loved Dr Wurm. He is pretty new to teaching at BYU, but he did a great job. Readings were super long but I learned a lot. He is so caring and loves his students. I thought I would hate his class but I actually really enjoyed it

He's definitely one of my favorite professors. You will have readings due before each class and occasional quizzes based on those readings but they are really easy and not at all stressful. He has a few papers due for this class but they're only like two pages long. Overall, this class is really interesting and fun and taught by a great professor.

A fun class with an even better professor! Wurm is really understanding and personable. The theories discussed are really interesting and Wurm has read nearly all the literature making him very knowledgeable on the subject. There are a few papers and an end of the semester project but they're more fun than they are difficult. Highly recommend.
Great professor who wants students to do well. Super engaging class, but his TA grades all assignments HARD. I often got 70% on assignments I spent hours on with no explanation

Really solid, kind, humble professor. He really cares about our success, and makes a big effort to get to know us personally. I really love the class structure, and you learn a ton working with a mentor in sales. There are some weekly reading assignments (make sure to do this), and stay engaged in class. The tests are easy.

If you're interested in B2B Sales, take this class! Professor Zippi runs this class just how college classes should be; incredibly useful and applicable, with relevant readings, and applications that actually help you improve your sales skills. The tests are easy and the assignments help you grow. Great class overall.

The best thing you can do for yourself is just pay attention in class. Zippi is a seasoned professional who is willing to share all of what he has learned about B2B selling with you. Fun teacher and genuinely wants to help you learn valuable selling skills. Take this course from him!

Professor Zippi is absolutely amazing. It's very easy to see that he care for each of his students. If you get to take his class (B2B Sales - MKTG 422), you will have one of the best opportunities at BYU. 

My favorite quote is "take professors, not classes". Professor Zippi is one of those professors that everyone going through BYU should take.

Professor Zippi is incredible! He provides a unique perspective to the classroom from his years in industry. He knows what he is talking about. If you enter this class to learn versus just to get a grade, you will be extremely satisfied with your experience! He is a tough grader because he wants you to grow. He provides feedback on all assignments.

Professor Zippi is an awesome person. He is very caring and always makes sure that we are doing ok with the stress of our other classes. This class has a good amount of homework and projects that can feel like a lot at first but are helpful. I'm not going into sales but this class is helpful to understand how sales work

Prof Zippi is a solid choice. Class is basically reading "SPIN Selling" and then practicing it. The only downside to Prof Zippi is he treats some subjective things as objective. In other words, sales and business both often have multiple "right" answers, but Prof Zippi will often mark you wrong if you don't put HIS answer. His opinion reigns

High tech sales is the best class I've taken at BYU. Everything you learn can be immediately implemented to your work. This is a summary course of Greg's wisdom & learnings from 30+ years in tech sales. He gives direct and specific feedback so that you learn and continue to improve. If you're at all startup-minded, take this class!

I took this class at the same time as his high tech sales class I preferred high tech. He teaches great principles in regular sales but honestly most of the time it kind of feels like a glorified SPIN Selling book club. That being said, he does create lots of meaningful chances for you to practice selling skills. Still would highly recommend it!
One of the best classes that you can take if you considering sales, especially a career in tech. Professor Zippi has such a rich career with so much wisdom to impart. 100% recommend.

Professor Zippi is the absolute best. I heard him lecture the year before and knew I NEEDED to take a class from him! Have you ever had an easy class that you learned more from than your others? That's how Professor Zippi's class is. This class is great if you're considering sales or just want to be a better marketer. Lots of psychology involved.

I took Professor Zippi's advanced sales course the first semester he taught it. Despite it being his first semester, the course was laid out clearly and Professor Zippi did a good job at making the course fair. The content was interesting and the readings were really relevant. Would have liked to see more role plays, but he will adapt and improve.

He is really passionate about sales and has had a lot of real-world experience that he brings into the classroom. He really likes to challenge conventional wisdom and go against the grain on a lot of sales methodologies. There were somethings I would have like to see done differently. I would have liked to see less lecturing and more application.

Great guy, very knowledgeable about his subject. You can tell he cares a lot about his students and wants them to be involved. The class was interesting as well. Make sure you do the readings because he gives lots of pop quizzes.
Took professor Zippi for advanced sales. He was very reasonable with his expectations and you can learn a lot from him. He has great insights!

Professor Zippi is a seasoned sales professional who has worked with top tier companies throughout his career. In addition to teaching, he actively consults tech companies in the valley. If you are considering a career in Sales, Marketing, or Entrepreneurship this class will be worth your time. Zippi is extremely humble and want to see you succeed.

I love Professor Zippi! I was in his Advanced Sales class the first semester he taught at BYU. He is highly experienced in sales, but not so much in teaching, so there were a few hiccups there. However, he cares a lot about student learning and puts a ton of effort into the class. You'll have to read quite a bit, but you'll learn a lot in this clas
Professor Zippi is awesome! Take his class. He is learning how to teach and grade but he is fair and insightful. He has an interesting career that has lots to share.

I am a pre-med student who had to take a handful of Physics courses in preparation for the MCAT. He knows that his entire class is pre-health, so he prepares you so well in that regard. He has taught for ages and knows what works. I don't know if I ever saw a student (out of the 230+) in the class disengaged and bored. Legend.

Great teacher and I appreciated his form A and B exams. However, he doesn't curve any of the exams and even though I was incredibly confident and well prepared for every exam, I would get pretty low scores. The average score for the class final was like low 70's. I would highly recommend Greg, but be careful with his trick answers on the exams.

Dr. Francis is the type of teacher that makes you want to go into teaching. He is willing to do anything for his students and puts so much effort into making his class as accessible as possible, all lectures online, 2 chances for each exam, very lenient attendance and homework policies, just go to the TA lab to do your homework and youll be great!

Please please please take his class for physics. It's SIGNIFICANTLY better than all the other options. You learn more in less amount of time. Plus Greg is so awesome. Just go to the tutorial lab to get your answers checked off (and learn the material better) and its a guaranteed A (need to average 85% on tests and you get a retake). Love this dude

It wasn't a tough class, but the concepts are tough regardless. He does a lot to help you, between extra reviews, additional topical videos, recording lectures, demonstrations, and open office hours. He also has a kind grade scale, with an A at 90%, much kinder than others. He was always willing to help students and seemed prepared for each lesson.
Best teacher
Great teacher

Greg is a GEM. He loves students, is an amazing teacher, makes confusing things SO clear, has TONS of resources outside of class like his YouTube channel. So excited to take another class from him. Homework correlates directly to tests, lectures are helpful, all assignments actually help you learn. He's so awesome.
greg francis is the michael jordan on the 96' Bulls of physics. the goat.

if you have to take physics take it from francis. He is so kind, passionate, and does a really good job of explaining hard concepts. His lectures are SO fun to listen to and he usually does cool demos. 2 chances at each exam with your higher score being your final score. I recommend reading the textbook before class! seriously one of the best profs

Professor Francis is awesome. Genuinely the best lectures I've had at BYU. He teaches the concepts in an easy way to understand. The homework is good preparation for the exams and I never felt overwhelmed with the workload. He lets you take the exams twice and keeps the highest score. He doesn't move on to new material until the exam is over. Epic!
Greg is a great professor. His class is very fair. You can learn everything just from attending the lectures. Go to the TA lab if you need more help
Actually the best guy ever!
GREAT CLASS!!!!!! HE IS A GOAT IN TERMS OF PROFESSORS AT BYU

Francis is the best! You have iclickers just for attendance. Homework is not that bad just go to the TA lab to check your answers before you submit. Lectures are awesome. Tests are not bad, just do the practice exams before and you should be just fine. I would love to take another class from Francis if I could.

I took this class from one of Greg's graduate teaching assistants, but the course was set up by him. The class is very well organized, and the few time Greg did teach he was spectacular. An A is a 90% and about half the class got it. I'd recommend working on the homework in the TA help lab to make sure you don't lose too much points. Great class!!
Super good professor, super clear and everything made sense, knows how to teach, class set up really well. I feel like it was a lot of hard work but worth it.

One of the kindest professors at BYU and genuine. His first time teaching 106 at BYU. His 105 class was really well put together, so I was surprised for 106 to be so much harder. It has harder for me than O Chem 2. I spent hours in the TA lab and worked very hard in that class only to perform poorly on every exam. Exams were very difficult.

Great professor! He's taught physics for decades, so he knows how to clearly and simply teach concepts and answer questions. He's always kind and willing to help if you're confused. He also posts all of his lectures on YouTube as well as the homework helps. Definitely a good option!

Greg has his own equations that he uses that are "easier". This makes it difficult because only people who took physics from him can help you. Youtube can't help you nor can the TA's because they didn't take physics from Greg. Greg will teach you one way and the TA's and the internet will teach you another. This made the class extremely difficult.

Dr. Francis is great as a person. He is very caring and very accessible outside of office hours. However, the way he taught many concepts were very unconventional so don't expect youtube to help if needed. The exams were sort of similar to the practice exams depending on the concepts. I really struggled in this class.

Dr. Francis is an amazing teacher and such a kind man. He is rooting for the success of students and gives so many opportunities to do really well in the course. Sometimes the tests are challenging but there are lots of other assignments that can keep your grade up, especially since an A is a 90 or above! Would recommend him!

Dr. Francis is one of my favorite people ever. I am not much of a fan of physics, but Dr. Francis made this class enjoyable and taught very clearly. He also made the cutoff for an A 90% and an A- 85%. Still a class that requires some effort, but it was very manageable with Dr. Francis.

Physics was always interesting to me, but after deciding on a different major, I accepted that I would never learn complex physics like relativity. Then Professor Francis explained things simply enough to ruin my plans of ignorance.

I highly recommend Professor Francis

Professor Francis is amazing! He explains difficult concepts well and really simplifies things so that they're easy to understand. 106 was a little harder than 105, but I just think it's because the course covers harder concepts. They had to open a whole new section because so many people wanted to take it from Professor Francis.

Professor Francis is an amazing professor and person. Physics is not my strongest suit, but his passion for the class is so apparent that it rubbed off on me as well. He is an incredible teacher, and I am so blessed to have taken it with him. If you don't understand something during lecture, don't panic, reach out for help. It will all work out.

Greg teaches physics in a unique way where instead of just memorizing equations you get a glimpse conceptually into how the world actually works (particularly with building models for optics and circuits). He's also a great/kind person!! He makes physics very doable. (I would also recommend rewatching his old lectures before each test)

Dr. Francis is one of the best teachers I have had at BYU. He really cares and you can see he is trying his best. Physics is a hard class but with Dr. Francis it is doable. I never did great on nay of the test and still ended with a B+. Make sure you go to him and the TA's for help and do your homework and you will do just fine in the class.

Greg is an amazing teacher who makes difficult topics understandable. I would pick him over anyone else to teach me physics. I have actually found a new love for physics problem solving because of him. Great experience. Can be hard, but that's the nature of the topic.

Dr. Francis is probably the best physics professor in the United States. If you're like me, physics is really really hard and daunting. Dr. Francis dumbed it down for me and made the material make sense. If you want to learn physics take this class.

Dr. Francis is truly a heavensend. He makes hard concepts understandable and makes class incredibly interactive and is good at capturing your focus on what he is teaching. Truly would recommend anyone to take him.

I'd never taken a phsycis class before Dr. Francis's classes, but he is very good at explaining tricky topics, especially with fun demonstrations. He's patient and cares about his students. The class content is hard, no denying it, so take it from a good teacher. Go to the office hours he offers! He helped me through finals when he didn't have to.

This is one of the only classes I have taken where rewatching the lectures is legitimately more useful than watching a random youtube video. Dr Francis has worked on how to teach students, not necessarily what to teach them. Lectures are amazing and I felt like I understood physics for the first time. Do the practice tests, attend the lectures.

I really like Professor Francis! I thought he really cared about me and wanted me to succeed. Physics is a hard class, you have to work hard and study. I would highly recommend taking this class from Professor Francis, he is the best in the business.

Greg is a great professor in a lot of ways, but this semester was a letdown. The exams didn't feel well put together, and there weren't any real chances to bounce back if you struggled early on. People often mention that his grading scale is low, but that's mostly because the class itself is really tough. He's great with 105, with 106, not so much.

Greg is an absolutely amazing professor! He is funny, kind, and explains topics in a very coherent manner. With his past career, he has a lot of experience on the subjects, and as such knows how to work with studies and help in an understandable format. Take physics 106 from Greg! His grading is reasonable, and he is just an amazing person :)

Took him for 105 and 106. Amazing professor, I am so glad I waited for Greg to be at BYU before taking physics. Tests are straight reflections of homework and practice tests. People who say otherwise just don't know how to study, tbh. cannot recommend Greg enough, best physics prof. for someone who HATES physics.

Dr. Francis is seriously a gem. His love for teaching makes learning enjoyable even when concepts are hard. he works SO hard to simplify hard concepts. He genuinely cares for his students, even postponing a midterm so we could better prepare. His kindness, warmth, and dedication make him not just an amazing professor, but an incredible human being.

I am fortunate to have taken PHSCS 105/106 from Greg Francis. He is a MASTER teacher of physics and is truly singular in his ability to make introductory physics both intuitive and fascinating. THIS is the quality of education you'd expect from BYU. Do yourself a favor and experience Greg's class firsthand. The course is structured for success.

Gregory Francis is the best thing to happen to Physics at BYU. He is a stellar teacher and if he senses the class is not understanding he will take time in lecture to go over it in a simple and understandable way. He made physics simple. You'll still need to study, but you'll have a teacher that is on your side.

Greg is hands down the best physics professor at BYU. I look 105 from a different professor and it was a night and day difference from 105 without him to 106 with him. This class is hard, but doable. Just don't go into it thinking it's going to be easy and be prepared to spend lots of time in the TA lab.

If you are taking Physics 106 or 105 at BYU you need to choose Greg Francis. This man is one of the best professors at BYU. He loves his students and wants them to succeed. He pushed back a midterm so we could review and study. 106 is harder than 105 but if you put forth college effort you will do well with the nice grade scale. Greg is the best!!!

One of, if not the best professor I have had at BYU, took 105 and 106 with him. He wants nothing more than his students success. Don't mistake 106 for an easy class, but Greg makes learning difficult concepts achievable. Only professor I would take physics from at BYU.

When we had a hard time understanding one unit, Greg set aside an extra class period and extra review sessions and pushed the test back and then about 60 something people aced it. He held three class sessions this semester to fit everyone and you could attend any section for points. 85 is an A-, practice tests mirror the real test. Dream prof.

Dr. Francis asked students to stop writing bad reviews and everyone decided to come to his defense. Greg wants you to succeed. Please, reach out to him if you're failing he WILL help! Despite what some pretentious students say, 106 is anything but easy. Greg would frequently downplay the difficulty of test Qs. Get ready to study hard in this course

Greg is THE best professor at BYU. I am trying to tell you with all of the energy I can muster in my soul that you must take physics from him. Greg does a phenomenal job of teaching tough concepts. Again, he does an exemplary job of teaching really complex physics concepts and makes it easy. He is so kind and caring he feels like a beloved grandpa.

Greg was by far the best person I could've taken both 105 and 106 from. Only reason the difficulty is 3 is because the content itself is difficult. However, it would've been a 5 hands down if I took physics from any other professor. He cares deeply about his students, provides ample resources, and is overall a great human being!

Dr. Francis is the goat. 106 was definitely more challenging than 105, but still very manageable. The grading scheme is set up for you to have success (A is 90%), but that being said the tests will cook you if you don't have a mature understanding of the concepts. Greg wants you to succeed and is an amazing teacher of very challenging topics.

This is a tough course because the content is hard! Greg does such an amazing job teaching these challenging concepts as best as he can. Even though some parts were tough, putting in the work with the TAs and yourself out of class is enough to do well in this class. This is the only man that you should take any basic physics class from.

Class was more complicated that it needed to be. I like him but the information we got from class and reading wasn't really what we needed to know from the test. It just wasn't clear how to best succeed. This was agreed upon among classmates. He does a great job teaching and is brilliant, but it becomes hard to overcome his tests.

Greg makes physics easy, I played on my phone in every 105 and 106 lecture and got an A+ and A- respectively. If you do bad in his class… college may not be your thing because Greg provides some of the easiest courses you will see as a PreMed or PreDent student.

See my review for his 106 class. If you don't want to go there just know that he is an amazing professor and really knows his stuff. He also does his abosulute best to make sure his students understand as well. If there's a topic that is notoriously more difficult, he'll spend more time on it to make sure everyone is where they need to be.

I used to really hate physics. It was my least favorite of the sciences and I was dreading taking it. But then I took it from Professor Francis and everything changed. He is an amazing teacher. His lessons are both engaging, funny and educational. He made some super complex topics much clearer for me. My favorite professor. Wish I could write more.

Going into 105 was scary for me as I had never learned physics concepts and dreaded starting. As we got into it I was surprised how hard the problems were and how prepared I felt to do them because of Greg's explanations. He made the geek stuff I'm not good at normal talk and intuitive and I was never tested on something he didn't prepare me for.

He is the best Physics professor teaching 105 and106. He really cared about his students, as he chose to teach an additional section just to accommodate students on the waitlist (which means that he got to teach 6h total every Tu and Th!!!) His test is tough, but HWs should prepare you well. It is a blessing that we have him at BYU.

Dr. Francis is one of the best professors I have had. Amazing lectures, cares deeply for his students. Many of the concepts are difficult to grasp, but Dr. Francis offers many opportunities to practice the material in class. He takes time out of his day to record videos to review homework, tutorials, and midterms, which are extremely helpful.

Best professor I have every had at BYU. Yes its a hard class but that's just from the content. Dr. Francis makes it way easier than any other professor! He is super caring and literally makes himself always available to help out. Just pay attention in lecture and actually do the homeworks and you will do great! He is amazing and cares so much!

Honestly if you are taking any physics class, I would take it from him. He teaches the material well and gives you every opportunity to succeed. It is a challenging class but I mean that is physics so take that as you will. He is one of the greats here at BYU. If I had one word to describe him, it would be DAWG. Enough said.

Professor Francis is amazing! I've never taken a physics class I actually understood until his! He helped write the textbook and so it goes along really well with what he teaches. He is very clear in everything we need to know and his practice tests represent his actual exams well. Do the readings and homework and you will be ready for the tests.

Dr. Francis is the best professor at BYU and probably the world. He is caring, intelligent, and just knows how to teach. He can teach in a variety of ways that allows every student to learn. Physics is hard in general, but not because of him. If you need to take physics, then wait for Dr. Francis. I would take a class from him over and over again.

Greg is great. That doesn't mean the class is easy, but he gives SO many resources and some attendance and hw drops to help you. You definitely still have to work hard especially if physics isn't your thing, but there's no way you wouldn't get a high grade if you actually use all the help Greg gives.

If you have to take Physics 106 you have to take it from Dr. Francis! I have never had a professor who cares so much about his students than Greg Francis. His lectures are interesting, spiritual, and easy to follow. His grading scale is goated too. 90% is an A. 85% A-, 80% B+, 75% B, 72% B-, 69% C+, 65% C.  I'm not a good test taker and I got a B+!

Greg is the best physics professor at BYU. Negative comments are inaccurate, probably from students who thought they deserved an "A" without effort. HWs are hard, but you can submit answers twice and still get 100%. Answers are shown for every assignment so you can check your work, and you can check all your answers with TAs. Easiest pre-med class

Dr. Francis is amazing! Had him for both 105 and 106 and did not disappoint. 90% is an A, and his expectations are always very clear. He tests what he teaches and never tries to trick you. Any negative reviews are just from people salty that they didn't do well in the class despite it being very manageable.

This class always made my day. Greg is the most caring teacher I have had at BYU. You will never find a teacher more dedicated to his students, and who will do everything he can to help them succeed. I would recommend Greg to any student!

Dr. Francis's lectures are memorable and engaging, and he also RECORDS them and posts them on Youtube for you!! He is organized and experienced, and clearly loves his job. If you have a hard time with physics, you should expect to struggle regardless of which professor you have, but Dr. Francis is the move. Pay no heed to any negative reviews.

Greg is the best teacher. 106 has more abstract concepts, but Greg teaches them in the best way he knows how. It will take time to learn them for yourself, but he makes it as easy as possible. An A is a 90%, and it is very achievable if you put in effort. Greg cares about each student and is happy to help you if you ask him. There is no one better

He literally researched how to teach more effectively and led trainings most of his career to help other Physics teachers improve! His teaching predicts the questions I'll have and answers them in a down to earth way. The concepts in Physics 105 and 106 are challenging but with Greg it's down to earth reasoning supplemented with suspenseful demos.

Dr Francis is the best! He has to be one of the most dedicated, caring, knowledgeable, and clear professors at BYU. He loves teaching and does it quite well. I took both 105 and 106 from him, and he made me love physics (a subject I was not really looking forward to). If you can, take physics from this wonderful individual. You will not regret it!

Greg is amazing, highly recommend! You can tell when a professor knows what they are doing and especially knows how to teach it. Greg kept lectures entertaining and made sure that we understood the content before moving on. It's a hard class and obviously any physics class will be but Greg does an amazing job teaching tough material!

One of the best professors at BYU. An incredible teacher, genuinely cares for students and the uniqueness of BYU. Always willing to answer questions, goes over more difficult homework in class and makes practice exams available to prep for tests. Not sure what the bad reviews are talking about... do yourself a favor and take this class from Greg!

Professor Francis might be one of the three Nephites. This Montana beauty of a man makes physics fun and relatable. Honestly, such a good guy. It is a physics class and can have challenging topics, but he does his best to help every student out. If you put forth the effort to get TA help and go to his office hours, you will learn physics well.

Dr. Greg Francis is the best lecturer I've ever had. He does tons of demos and he makes class a lot of fun. Every single thing he does is recorded as well so you can rewatch it if you are struggling with the difficulty of the material. He genuinely cares about his students and he works really hard to make it a good class. A is a 90Greg is the man.

I struggled, but Dr. Francis had everything there to help. I should have reached out more but I didn't. His lectures were great, and he always went out of his way to try to make sure we understood something. His grade scale made up for the toughness of physics, an A is a 90%! He had great demonstrations as well. He is one of the best prof I've had.

Dr. Francis made it so that PHSC106 was simple to me. That doesn't mean that it was easy, but his course and TAs helped me to understand physics in a way that my PHSC105 professor did not. He is a incredible guy and you can't help but enjoy his lectures. Also, the class is fair.

Professor Francis is amazing! He has been my favorite professor at BYU and teaches Physics extremely well. Lectures are very engaging and Greg makes it easy to learn. Homework is important and putting in the time is necessary to learn challenging physics topics, but Greg has so many resources and prepares students very well for exams.

Dr Francis is one of my all-time favorites! I think this was his first semester teaching 106 at BYU, specifically optics. He made complicated topics easier to understand. He is willing to help his students who are struggling. 
It looks like an unhappy student made multiple bad reviews because they didn't do well. He is the best professor for 106

He is incredibly caring and helpful. He is the best professor I have ever had at BYU. He is incredible at teaching the material, even when the concepts are tough. He is always willing to meet with students to help them get the grade they want. As long as you're willing to put in the work, you will do great in this class.

I have never met a professor who cares more than Greg. The material in this class is difficult and very complex at times, but for someone who is willing to put in the work Greg will be a great teacher. He is always willing to answer questions, be it before or after class or whenever. This class would have been so much harder without him.

Awesome professor. Cares a ton about students and gives you a lot of opportunities to succeed. The lectures were clear, but you need to come to class having done the assigned reading. If you don't understand the concepts, get help in the TA lab or from Dr. Francis's office hours. Do the homework early so you have time to ask questions.

Dr. Francis only cares about one thing more than what he teaches: who he teaches it to. He is deeply invested in our success as students AND our well-being. Physics is definitely hard, but I feel like I have a better gut understanding of the concepts because of him. I wouldn't take it from anyone else.

Dr. Francis is the best physics professor I've ever had. I've taken 105 and 106 from him, and I can truly say that no professor cares more about your success. Physics is not an easy material to learn, but if you're still confused, he has office hours and is more than happy to help one-on-one. He is truly the best, you won't find a better professor.

Others are saying this class was hard. It's not. 
He is a fantastic teacher, taught the principles we need to know and the homework used those same principles. Those saying it was hard either didn't pay attention in class or didn't watch the posted tutorials/lectures, it is ridiculous to think this class was hard. 
Pay attention and you'll get an A

Greg is one of, if not, my favorite professor from BYU. I took 105 with him, and he's the absolute best chance you have at loving physics AND doing well. This class is harder compared to 105, but that's expected as it is a higher level class. Go to class, stay on top of your work, and you will do just fine. 1000% recommend!! He's so caring and nice

Greg is such an amazing professor. He truly knows how to teach physics at a level that is understandable to all. It was his first semester teachings some units and there were a few hiccups. But I know that he will continue to work to make it more clear. Can't imagine not taking his class. One of the best professors ever. Genuinely loved his classes

I would die for Greg. I'm not sure why anyone would have issues with the class. Sure its tough, but no where near as difficult as other courses I've taken at BYU. As far as other people claiming that it is disorganized I have had far far worse and I'm not really sure what they are all talking about as it was fine for me. 90% is an A, 62% is passing

Greg is seriously the best professor I've had at BYU. He does his best to make a difficult subject as easy as it can be, and he's incredibly kind and caring to his students. Physics is difficult but Greg makes it enjoyable. People who left poor ratings obviously didn't put in the necessary work to understand the material, its not Greg's fault

Don't listen to the previous reviews. Greg is one of the kindest, most understanding, engaging teachers I've had at BYU. Physics 106 has a few more difficult topics than Physics 105 but everyone I've talked to has said that Professor Francis taught it better than previous teachers. His grading system is so forgiving too. TAKE CLASSES GREG!

I want to choose way more good tags than 3, becuase Professor Francis embodies all good things a professor should be. Yes physics 106 is difficult, but it would be regardless of who's teaching it. Greg is a wonderful teacher, person, and example. TA lab for homework, study with friends for tests/tutorials. Read the textbook. Very doable class.

Took 105 from Greg and now 106. 106 is definitely harder content. The final was brutal, but the online sample exams help. I would recommend him for 105 but not 106. The last unit just felt really condensed and confusing. Hw is hard, but TA lab helps...doesn't mean you will understand. He sets up grading to make sure you don't fail, but it is brutal

I cannot emphasize more about how great Greg is. He really wants you to succeed. Yes, some topics are hard, but that does not mean it's not doable. His class structure is well organized, and it was such a pleasure to take both 105 and 106 from him. 100% recommended! He is the best physics professor.

Prof Francis is kind, caring, funny, and an incredibly good teacher. I took both 105 and 106 from him and thought he taught clearly, had clear and fair expectations, and got good grades with a normal amount of effort. If you get above a 90%, you get an A. Seriously, take these classes from him.

there is no teacher at BYU or in the world that cares more about his students, Greg is an amazing person and teacher and I cant empasize that enough. I loved learning from prof Francis, but with that said, I dispise phisics. I dont think it's the professor, just the subject. Some thrive, some suffer. Study and go to the TA lab!

This class was so unnecessarily hard... The tests and homework were always confusing and impossible to do without a TA's help. The TAs wouldn't even know how to solve his questions sometimes... He quite literally butchered the whole last unit that was what our final was over. He was sloppy and disorganized because he had never taught it before. RUN

Greg's a great guy, but classwork didn't match the tough homework or sample exams. Questions were vague, solutions never posted, so I couldn't check my work. Some units were harder than needed; even TAs questioned his extra equations. Friends in other sections solved things more simply. Brilliant prof, but over‑complicates and under‑prepares.

The first part of this class was great but the last unit was an absolute mess. It was disorganized and he jumped to a completely different topic every different lecture. I did not talk to one person who understood the last unit. Not even the TAs could help us with the homework problems. The lectures were also not helpful at all.

I have never had a professor more caring and reachable than Dr. Francis. A 90 is an A in his class, and he offers plenty of help prepping for his exams. It's not an easy class, but he's an expert at taking complex physics principles and breaking them down into simple patterns. He's a true friend to his students and will fight for you. He's awesome!

I actually took PHSC 105 from Francis and that class was very good. However, it seems that something changed when it came to PHSC 106 and as a student, despite studying more and being more diligent when it came to phsyics ironically, the class has decreased signficantly in quality. Francis is a nice guy but his exams are poorly worded and prepared.

I cannot express how amazing of a professor Dr. Francis is. He truly is dedicated and very intelligent, but more so than that, he is an amazing teacher. He is able to explain topics so complex so simply and understandably. He is, by far, the best professor I have had in any university class.

If you just take the practice tests a few times before the exams and pay attention in lecture, you will do great. This was genuinely one of the easier classes I have taken so far, only because I took it from Francis. My friends took it from other professors at BYU and would skip their lectures and watch The Francis lectures on youtube instead.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH ANYONE OTHER THAN PROFESSOR FRANCIS! HE IS A GEM TO BE TREASURED! Only complaint I would have is the tutorial hour is a COMPLETE waste of time but all the professors have that. SIGN UP SIGN UP SIGN UP!

His lectures are very enteraning and he tries to be super engaging. There is a decent amount of workload and the class make you spend time on complicated concepts but he teaches in a very straight forward way. He has taught these concepts for years and has worked hard to refien them so students can understand. I genuinely wish he was my father.
Incredible professor, very forgiving grading scale, amazing lectures.

His lectures are usually pretty good and entertaining. The problem is the assignments. Questions on homework and tutorials are often trick questions, are a lot more difficult than the ones in lecture, and sometimes expect you to know stuff that hasn't yet been covered in class. Tests are also extremely difficult and count for 56% of your grade.
Great sense of humor, and does a good job teaching difficult topics.

69% C+ 
puts his life on the line for the demos 
has the greatest superpower known to man

If you have to take physics 105, take it from Greg. He cares so much about the students and makes himself as accessible to us as possible. He is fair in grading and makes sure that you understand the concepts. He also makes class very fun. I never thought I'd enjoy physcs. I could talk about how great he is forever but the word count won't let me.

One of the nicest guys ever! I did not do as well as I wanted on the tests but he made the class worth it with his kindness and humility. He is very accessible with office hours, email, and he even gave us his phone number! I wish the tests weren't online but whatever. I wish he were teaching PHSCS 106 next semester!!

Dr. Francis has been the best professor I've had at BYU. Physics can be a tough course but he made it both enjoyable and easy to understand. He includes lots of demos and example problems in his lectures that help prepare you for the exams.

Genuinely my favorite professor I have had in college. Super entertaining lectures, I actually enjoyed them, hilarious guy. He also will take as much time as you need outside of class if you need help on something. You can just tell he LOVES physics, and doesn't mind taking extra hours to help you learn. Made a usually hard class very doable.
Great professor! Just get ready to work. This class is hard so make sure to use help from the TAs and have a study group.

Professor Francis is one of the best professors I've ever had at BYU! I got to have him for his first semester teaching here for Fall 2023. He's humble, has a good sense of humor, and teaches in a very entertaining way. There were three homework assignments each week and you could reattempt most missed questions with no penalty for the first retry.

Professor Francis is an amazing teacher and a great person. He is very experienced while still being humble and kind (rare nowadays). He gives all the tools necessary to do well in the class. As long as you take advantage, you will do very well.

The TA's grade your HW like you're sleeping with their spouse. Macfarlane is entertaining during class but lectures don't translate to convoluted HW problems. Little to no help with test prep from the TA's as well, and no practice exams. Luckily content is easy, just expect to be swimming on your own.

Professor Macfarlane prioritizes research over teaching. He grades harshly and responds rudely to questions about his grading, discouraging engagement. The class feels tense, with students belittled for asking questions. While the material is interesting, the course is disorganized, and his lack of kindness hinders learning.

Dr. Macfarlane is a great professor. He worked in the industry before coming to BYU and knows his stuff. The tests and homework are reletively easy.
