He also brings in guest speakers which I think provide valuable opportunities to learn about transportation. Just be aware that he is a hard grader, especially on the final project.

Dr. Macfarlane is a great teacher and allows for discussion past the basic principles of the class to allow for further exploration. Sometimes these discussions are fatalistic in that solutions are hard to come by and are often just complained about.
But class was very good, a lot of great content. Tough grading on papers though.

Class feels like a middle school lecture. Homework due every class is almost impossible without help from TA's or the professor. Exams are based on topics brushed over in class but are made extremely difficult or complex applications of the material we did not learn. TA's grade extremely hard. Not worth the struggle for 2 credits of hopelessness.

Professor Macfarlane is really nice. He was easy to reach and supported his students outside the class room.  I do have something to say about the homework however. The homework was extremely difficult and me and other students in the class would spend 2-3 hours per assignment which were due every class. Felt like too much work for 2 credits.

Macfarlane is super knowledgeable about tons of different topics, which in the end can make this class super tough. It is basically an ECON class mixed with complex engineering topics in sustainability.  Class ends up being really tough especially when the TA's grade everything insanely tight. Mix of Engineers/other majors make the curve wild too.
Dr. Stallings is awesome

Professor Stallings is an amazing professor who really cares about his students. He is really understanding and willing to support students 1 on 1 and wants them to succeed. It can be a lot of material and kinda hard exams but he's great. Make sure to memorize authors full names and literary concepts (mise-en-anyme, anáfora, hipérbole, etc).

Professor Stallings is great! He genuinely cares so much about his students. You'll do a weekly digital dialogue, several readings before each class, and two exams. You'll also go to the international cinema 4 times each semester and write a lil essay for each visit. He doesn't grade super harshly, so if you put forth sincere effort, you're golden.

If you can look past the very white accent, Stallings is great. He really does care about his students and wants them to love learning. He loves writing letters of recommendation, so make sure to connect with him outside of class if you're looking for that. Lots of reading, but the tests were pretty easy, and he offers tons of extra credit.

Professor Stallings is amazing! He loves his students and wants them to succeed. This class does have a lot of reading materials so be prepared to have a lot of reading homework! He provides detailed, outlined study guides for all his exams so if you study what's on it, you'll do really well. I would highly recommend taking Spanish 341 from him!

Greg is one of the best Spanish Professors I have had. his class was very fun, he's very easy to get along with, and his spanish accent always makes me laugh. You can tell he really cares about the material, he knows his students well, and if you pay attention in class you might leave with a new friend. he's super willing to write letters of rec.

You have to read a lot, but i mean, its a literature class. He is so kind and caring and loves his students and knows the material! His lectures can feel dry sometimes, but he's great. Weekly digital dialogue, 2 midterms and final, final paper, international cinema, a few opportunities for extra credit. Self reported attendance and participation.

Lots of reading and writing. Prepare to go to the International Cinema 4 times per semester and write a couple paragraphs inside and outside of class each week. He does a good job explaining things and is ready to help if you need it. Super caring, even if the first email he sends out might make you think otherwise.

Profe Stallings cares so much about his students. He's not the most organized, which I didn't love, but he wants his students to succeed! Digital dialogue posts related to the reading are due before each class. He cancels class the week of tests so you have time to study. He gives points back out of the kindness of his heart.

Huge, expensive list of course materials that were unnecessary.
His accent was painful to listen to.
Every lecture was irrelevant or just him reading from a textbook.

Professor Stallings is by far the worst professor I have ever had. His Spanish accent hurts to listen to, even if you understand him you wouldn't understand what's going on. Mostly digital dialog. His exams include specific quotes from reading you have to identify. Every lecture he finds a way to make the main topic racism and diversity.

When I was in this class I thought that it was so hard but now when I look back on this class I realize that it wasn't that hard. You basically watch movies, read poems and just talk about them. Gregory y hermana stallings are awesome and really kind. I would totally take another class from them. The movies you watch are also really cool.

Professor Stallings and Sister Stallings are very kind and caring people who are passionate about Spanish literature. Some of the readings were pretty confusing and weird, I'm not sure if I don't like Spanish lit or just the selections they chose. Most of what I learned was very much stored in my short term memory, like names and titles and terms.

Unrealistic expectations for his students. Tests are extremely difficult and are almost PURE memorization of names and vocab. If you are going to keep up, you will have a ton of reading to do. Go to class, because you'll get deducted 3% from your final grade if you don't. Overall organization was just poor. Never felt prepared for any of the tests

He expects way too much out of his students and doesn't give enough help for it either. I didn't learn much in lectures and nothing is put in the gradebook until the end of the semester so you can't track your progress. Tests are really hard and they expect you to identify everything about a poem or story by one line given on the test.

I thought Professor Stallings was okay throughout the semester until the days after finals, You turn all your homework in at the end and even though I completed it all i received a C on it. That put me at a 93.3% and learning suite said an A was a 93, until he changed the grade scale to need a 94 for an A the day before grades were due.

Worst organization ever!! I am never taking another Spanish class again. This class was mostly spent memorizing random information of his favorite authors and movie directors. I never understood what was happening in class, and asking questions never helped. Nice person but his class was very frustrating and confusing

This is probably the worst organized class I have ever taken at BYU. It is never clear what he expects of you as far as homework. All homework is turned in as a lump assignment at the end of the semester. 5 Mandatory movies outside of class (usually don't have anything to do with class). 2 Cultural activities. Takes attendance in lecture hall class

Prof. Stallings is definitely one of my favorite professors I've had at BYU. He is very cognizant of his students and their needs, and he really cares about our learning and our well-being. I've taken a couple of Spanish classes with him now, and I really wouldn't have it any other way. You won't regret this class!

If you enjoy reading in Spanish, take this class. It does require activities outside of class so make sure you're not super busy with school or work if you do. To pass this class you have to remember what the professor says. The lectures were incredibly enjoyable and the participation was fun. Great guy.

Participation is huge, readings are long and can be difficult (cuz reading in a 2nd lang is HARD), but he makes the class interesting and worth it. The readings are really well curated and the films you watch are intriguing and fun. He uses a ton of musical examples to help you contextualize literary terms and it makes the class easy and relatable

Awesome class! Dr. Stallings is very passionate about literature and cinema, so we watch lots of movies. Tests are very doable if you read and pay attention to lectures, small details like paintings matter. Flash cards and study groups help a lot. Attendance, readings, and bringing books are recorded yes/no on the roll, which affects participation

This was the second class I took from Prof Stallings. This class seemed much easier than the first. Stalling expects you to do lots of reading and analysis, but he talks you through it. He asks you each day if you did the reading and homework so you can't fake it. He is very passionate about literature so it makes it interesting!

This is my 2nd class w/ Stallings & I loved it! W/ my first class, I felt more comfortable after the 1st exam because I knew what to expect & how to study better. His classes require reading & work, but they are SO enlightening and I've really enjoyed them! I've learned so much and I feel like he always makes things applicable to life. He's great!

I liked Stallings as a professor. He's very passionate and has a lot of good points. The only thing is that it's kind of hard to understand what he expects on tests, assignments, etc. and he's a hard grader. I liked the class, but felt that he was a bit hard on grading. Very few things that go into your grade so be prepared.

Stallings is super cool, he loves spanish lit and does a lot to make it interesting. You watch some great movies in class, almost every class has a few minutes spent watching something. The outside class stuff is tough with a busy schedule.

I really appreciated how he genuinely listened to students as they spoke in class, and praised them frequently for their efforts. Personally, I took this class during an incredibly busy semester which was unfortunate because I probably would have enjoyed the class more. It was difficult for me to attend the outside activities required for the class

Stallings demands a lot of your time after class (attendance to films in International Cinema, lectures, etc) which, if you happen to work evenings, will make it almost impossible to get a good grade in the course. And his Spanish isn't on point either, although he does have a real passion for Spanish art and culture.

Great teacher I learned a lot from him. He does require a lot of information to be processed for the tests but he always hands out extra credit so you should do fine if you do the extra credit. He weighs your grade heavily on participation so pay attention in class.

I love Dr. Stallings for so many reasons, he is very passionate about what he teaches. The only thing that made me feel really uncomfortable in class were the movies he showed. I was shocked we were allowed to watch some of the movies he had. I took him for Summer semester and it was very doable. Loved the little skits as well. Very, very kind man!
Dr Stallings is amazing. I hate poetry before his class, but he made everything so awesome. The class was easy enough but you still learn a lot of cool stuff. Best SPAN 339 teacher.

Profesor Stallings is incredibly passionate about Spanish literature, and it shows. Interesting lectures. He even includes films in the curriculum. Tests are all free response, but if you've read and studied, and paid attention in class, you should be fine. Participation is important. All comments are welcomed and respected. Great class.

Dr. Stallings was the straight up man. I loved his class, mostly because reading interesting fiction was a great break from the usual textbooks. The best part is that, although his class requires a lot of work in the sense of reading and writing, he's very open minded and you can say anything as long as you can support it. Take 339 from him!!

Prof. Stallings is very passionate about Spanish literature and makes the class more enjoyable than what you'd think. There are homework assignments for each class that are essential to knowing what's going on in class. Only two midterms (entirely free response) which he grades VERY easily.

Great guy and very passionate about what he teaches. That being said, get ready for lots of work. LOTS of reading and questions before every class. Participation (not just attendance) is 20% of your final grade, so I hope you like to talk and discuss in large groups. Only two midterms and a final during the semester, but there's lots of info!!

Stallings is a great guy. His slides are pretty confusing, it was hard to take notes because his ideas don't really flow. I had to do 8 hrs of homework in 1 day once, because of all the reading, movie, and mandatory event that he assigned us. TONS OF HOMEWORK. Should be a 4 credit class coming from Stallings. But he's nice.

Dr. Stallings is one of those professors that makes you want to delve into a subject. His class is the reason why I upgraded from a Spanish Minor to a Spanish Major. Great teacher. He expects participation, so you need to go to class and come prepared, but if you do, he will teach you so much.

There was a ton of information covered on each test and it was difficult to know what was important from each lecture.  Tests are all hand-written and have no multiple choice, so you really need to know the information.  Other than that, the class is very simple and straight-forward.

The exams were super challenging. This was my first B-. The lectures are really fascinating. We watch movies and discuss time periods, art, literature, and history. If you want an easy A, take it from someone else. If you want to unlock your mind to a new world, take it from Stallings. If you're pre-med, ask him for a letter of recommendation.

Don Gregorio Stallings is not good, he is amazing! Definitely my favorite professor at BYU. He is passionate about what he teaches and what he has his students read. You will find a true sense of humanity within his teaching style. What he has taught me by using literature has made me a better human being.
Stallings is the man. Somehow he got me to love Spanish poetry and literature. Easy A. Anyone who says this class was hard didn't do the homework. Sloth makes everything hard.

Professor Stallings is great! He teaches 339 a little differently than other professors, but I think I prefer his method. By the end of the class you'll feel that you really learned some worthwhile things. Go to class, participate, do the reading, study for the tests, write a good paper, get a good grade. Great class!

Dr. Stallings is awesome. He is so knowledgeable and class is always interesting! He has a funny sense of humor. He is passionate about what he teaches. (Lot's of reading and homework but tests aren't too difficult if you know the theories and ideas he presents in class.) He is also willing to work with you which I really really appreciated!
Stallings is amazing. All he cares about it coming to class prepared and thinking about what you read. It doesn't matter what you think, just that you do.
Awesome teacher. If you participate, do all the work, study loosely for the tests and have someone who knows Spanish grammar correct your final paper you can get an A easily. Take  this class.
He is a great guy and his class is pretty interesting. He is very personable and easy to talk to. I would take another one of this guys classes in a heartbeat!

Stallings is awesome! One of my friends in grad school is taking another one of his classes just for kicks. He lets you know what is expected and doesn't expect ridiculous amounts of work, and is interesting to boot.  Really, his class opened my perspective on Spanish literature (and literature in general) a lot.

Stallings is my favorite teacher at BYU.  HE ROCKS!  I tell everyone I know to take all classes possible from him.  I have already taken 339, 441 and 444 from him.  I am done with my major, but am considering taking another class from him JUST FOR FUN.

Professor Stallings is, by far, my favorite professor at BYU.  He loves class participation and helps to prepare you for tests.  While he can require a lot from his students, he is an easy grader and any decent effort will be rewarded with an A.
He is the best teacher Ever!!

One of the very best Spanish teachers I've ever had! He's fun, funny, creative, dynamic. He just makes class very enjoyable and interesting! I love the clips of current movies that he shows to demonstrate several of the points of class we are learning. He turns a boring topic into a very interesting and fun one. Cares so much for the students!

BEST spanish lit teacher ever! He cares about you so much. SUPER ORGANIZED! Class is NEVER boring. Shows modern day examples (hollywood) pertinent to Spain lit themes. HIGHLY recommended. His 2 tests are LONG.  I wrote for 2 hours non-stop, but got an A. He does NOT focus on grammar, but rather on IDEAS and comprehension. You MUST do assignments.

Es un profesor muy bueno, muy intelegente y que sabe bien explicar lo que enseña. Me costó trabajo hacer sus examenes, pero siempre es disponible para ayudarte con cualquier duda y de pronto no es tan dificil tener exito en su clase.
Professor Stallings is hilarious. He's just an overall nice guy who is very approachable and friendly. He's a wonderful teacher, a fair grader, and a genius.

I wouldnt take 339/441 from anyone else! He is helpful, makes classes interesting! He makes sure everyone understands, and with all his fun video clips you will understand. fully prepares you for midterm and final. Extra credit available bc the tests can be hard, but follow handouts and take good notes you'll be fine!
Stallings is the best teacher at BYU, no joke.  He is a genius that will change your life.  Get into his class [if you can] and enjoy!
Great teacher! He prepares his classes so good, that it makes it easier to pass the tests.I recomend you to take classes with him. I loved his class. Best teacher in BYU.

Good teacher! There is a lot of reading, but he is fair. There is a mid-term and a final as well as a paper, but if you prepare you can do well. He makes class interesting with movie clips,etc. I learned a lot from this class.

Dr. Hart is the best general ed professor I've had. I was shocked he knew like 95% of the classes names by the first week. He is great at teaching things in a clear way (I was always so sad when we had a substitute). He's funny and helps you not just understand the content, but grow a love for our earth. If you take PS100 take it from Gus Hart!

I thought PS 100 as a class was hard, but really liked Dr. Hart, who isn't over the class materials/structure. He was a really good teacher and helped us learn from each other. He always prioritized our learning and our questions.

This guy is really good. He is enjoyable in lectures and makes them exciting. He is very respectful to the students and strives to know them. He is very helpful when you don't understand a topic and will take time to help you understand.

Dr. Hart is my favorite teacher on campus. He was very passionate about giving opportunities to learn with intent. Although it is a difficult class, his lectures were open to working out our questions and helping us figure things out together. I was amazed at how clearly and passionately he explained things. Taking his class is well worth it!!!

This guy is one of the best professors I've had. He helped me like and feel good at math, which I thought was impossible. After taking many other math classes at BYU I had kind of given up at understanding things thoroughly but Professor Hart changed that for me.

Dr. Hart is a VERY good teacher. When he explained things, I immediately understood them, even if it was a concept I had previously struggled with. He is current on educational research and tries his best to apply it in his class. Given the nature of the course, some assignments were quite difficult, but if you try your best you will get an A.

Professor Hart is the kind of teacher that actually looks into the research on how people learn--instead of just doing what was done before. This reflects in his teaching method. There are no midterms or final, but instead small weekly tests/quizzes that aren't any longer than the homework. If you want to learn physics--he's your guy.

Dr. Hart really excels in a small-classroom environment through clear, concise explanations to any questions the students have. He expects the reading to be done and questions sent to him before class. 581 was extraordinarily difficult, and required enormous amounts of time and energy, but it is by far the best class I've ever taken at BYU.

Professor Hart was my favorite! He was very engaging in class and I was rarely bored. The lab hours were extremely helpful and as long as I did my reading and paid attention in class I was fine. Great choice for this class.

Prof. Hart is a caring guy but the lectures are truly a waste of time. I only went because of the clicker quizzes that would happen 1-3 each class. The TAs are your bet friend with the labs and reviews. If you took Physics and Chem before, this class will be a breeze.

Science is my worse subject. I was afraid to take this class but Hart made class really enjoyable. He loves what he does and class was rarely boring to my surprise. Do the readings and you'll do fine. Tests were somewhat hard. Take this class from Hart!!!

I often felt confused after lectures but I feel that it was more the random questions people would ask more than Hart's teaching. He explains things very quickly though. This class was hard for me but I'm not really good at chemistry or physics. Read the book, go to lab and you should be ok. TA lab is the best! go often and you'll be ok.

I loved Dr. Hart. He is really animated and enthusiastic and really cares about his students. There are frequent tests but if you study and pay attention in class you will get a good grade. I only took this class because I had too, but Professor Hart made it very enjoyable.

I thought this class was way harder than it needed to be for GE credit. But Hart loves the subject and learning from him is interesting. He gets excited during lectures which makes going to class more enjoyable. Tests are brutal and frequent.

Dr. Hart made class interesting and gave good lectures, but sometimes he left me feeling confused. Often the material made more sense in the book than in lectures, and he didn't invite questions very well. Still an easy A if you're willing to put in a little work.

Absolutely the best professor I've ever had. I've a BS in physics and have taken quite a few classes and Dr. Hart by far surpasses every professor in every discipline!  The class is Very Tough but he focuses on what You don't understand. No rote learning. I would take any course he offered because I know I would learn from him and the material!!!!

I love Professor Hart. He loves the subject and his students, so every lecture was interesting and applicable. He memorized every one's name in a 300+ sized class; he'll notice and compliment a haircut. I didn't like science before taking this class, but his class changed that for me. Hart is truly a great teacher; take PS100 from him if you can!

The tests for this class are the same no matter who you take it from, so the difficulty won't change no matter who you get. Bro. Hart is funny and is a good guy. The key to doing well is going to TA review sessions. They give you the answers to the tests. Overall I thought this was a boring class though, and Hart didnt do anything to make it better
He really loves physics and will make you love it too. His lectures are extremely helpful. He is very willing to help you individually and is great to talk to. He really cares about his students.

Hart is the man! He really cares about the students and the course (he memorizes every name and face). He is funny and helpful, and he'll try his hardest to get you interested in PS100. Does good demos and understandable P.P. slides. Test are fairly easy and the course is super curved. If taken AP Physics, will be fine. Try to get B+, A- on tests.

I love this guy. After finishing this class, he still remembers my name when we met accidentally in the Wilk. If you have to take this class, take it from him. The first three exams are not difficult. But the last exam about Geology and Cosmology is really challenging. You have to memorize a lot. Go to TA's lab for help. Good class overall.

Professor Hart was great! He really is a great teacher. He really cares about students' questions and bases his lectures off what students don't understand as long as you are forthcoming in what you're confused about

Professor Hart is awesome! Attend lectures and read the text book and you'll do fine. It is easy to get a good grade in this class because there are 3 different ways to earn an A. I would suggest taking the Exemption Exam early just so you have an idea of what the final will be like. Also, Professor Hart is very funny, if you look for his humor.

Physical Science isn't necessarily a fun class, but Prof. Hart made it way more fun than it should have been. I enjoyed learning from him; he is so excited about teaching what he clearly loves that it motivates you to want to learn. You do need to do the reading every day or risk falling behind, but it's not difficult.

Good teacher, but I didn't love the subject. Hated the tests and never felt like studying helped. Makes you read the book, with the motivation of daily quizzes. Great guy, just not a super interesting subject for me.
Hart is the man! He is a great guy who really cares, and makes a terrible class a little bit more enjoyable. Awesome guy, definitely take Physical Science from him if you can.

Ok, Professor Hart is a great guy, he's a natural teacher, but there are concepts that I don't think any teacher could explain well. The class was horrible for me (and I'm not a dumb person). I prepared so well for exams and then did horribly on the tests...WHAT?! This shouldn't be a GE, it's a waste of time if you're not interested in physics.

I did not expect to like Physical Science 100.  That's why I put off taking this GE class until my senior year.  But Gus is THE MAN.  He makes class fun and interesting, and yes, he memorizes everyone's name in his huge classes.  He cares about his students.  And his TAs are great, too, especially Katy.
The class materials are difficult, and students are super dumb. They ask many irrelevant questions. Having said that, Hart is the best professor for this class.

I had little to no interest in science before this class, and even less after. I somewhat understood science before this class, and not at all after.  Since the material is covered no matter what teacher you have, he's as good as any to take it from.  The only annoying thing is he takes attendance every class.

This class was one where if you put the effort in you got decent grades and you learned interesting things. Professor Hart is caring and he will answer any question you ask, he is great about being patient and understanding. It is a great GE class to take, I say take it!

Really cool guy, and interesting to listen to. Unfortunately the class is too big and about five students ask hypothetical questions every day that will never be on an exam and he takes lots of class time to answer useless questions. Easy class if you get and like science, hard if you don't.

Awesome teacher! He really cares about you understanding the material which helps you to actually get a good grade. I in no way wanted to take Physical Science but after having it with Prof. Hart I found myself toying with the idea of becoming a physics major.

Great teacher! He doesn't just lecture, he really engages the class and makes sure everyone understands a concept before moving on. I did not expect to like PS100 at all, but I have actually not dreaded going to this class. Go to the reviews (Chad's, if you can)!

Hart was amazing. He learns everyones' names and is really good at explaining very confusing concepts. He's extremely enthusiastic about what he teaches and makes it applicable to every day life. It was a great class. Reading the chapter everyday is really the only homework.  Hart is amaizing!
Professor Hart is incredible.  He really understands what he's talking about and he makes an effort to memorize all 300 students names in the class (and he teaches two classes that large).
GUS IS THE MAN!  I went into PS 100 thinking it would be boring and I'd barely pass.  Gus made class fun, interesting, and actually enjoyable. And, I ended up with an A!

He has a passion for what he teaches and is very knowledgable about the material, but goes into way too much detail answering questions.  Stick to the book for studying for the test!  You can either take the grade of your assignments, quizs, and tests or if you get an A on the final you get an A in the class. Alot of busy work involved!
great professor, really knows his stuff.

I actually really enjoyed taking this class. I went in to PS100 thinking I was gonna hate it. But, professor Hart made me love it! I really liked that he made an effort to learn all of his 200 something student's names. I felt like I was learning from someone who really loved to teach and help students learn.
Gus rocks!  I actually liked this science class.  He teaches the material so well and is extremely clear.  Very, very fair

He was very interested in his students learning and knew almost all of our names (there was 200 of us). He presented the class material in a clear way that was easy to understand and kept the class lively/interesting. It was one of the best classes I've taken.

He's really good! If you're going to take Physical Science take it from him. He somehow amazingly remembers everyone's name in the class. His lectures were pretty interesting, sometimes he even blows stuff up which was cool.
Excellent teacher.  He reminds me of George Baily from it's a wonderful life.  Very clear, makes material interesting, fair.  I highly recommend him.

Really liked him as a teacher. Really easy going. Gets to know everyones name and makes sure everyone can be involved. Makes students ask and answer questions. If you get a higher grade on the final then your grade throughout the semester that is the grade you get for the class.

To Dr. Hart's credit, this was the first time he taught Physics 360. He is a great person - he learns your name and tries to help you if he has time. The homework can take a long time and the tests can be difficult, but the class isn't overly difficult. He does have an interesting lecture style, but that might change as he teaches 360 more.

don't take thermal physics from him. lectures were insane- he has this debate theory read the chapter and then argue about the material in class those who agrued loudest and most seemed to have the concept wrong and I always left class feeling more confused. my opinion lecture is to teach the student concepts and clarify our misunderstandings.

TAKE PHYSICAL SCIENCE FROM THIS GUY! He's funny, interesting, and really helpful. He'll learn your name and help with anything you need. The material isn't the most interesting, but he makes it enjoyable. Such a good teacher...

I loved Professor Hart.  He is extremely smart and still doesn't talk above your head.  He is actually funny and just loves life you can tell.  He truly wants his students to understand the material and he does a great job at making the subject interesting.  Take it from him!
One of the best teachers I've ever had!  He wants to know everyone's name.  He's very clear and very funny.  Highly recommended!!!!!!

Bro. Hart might be the best teacher I had all semester. His lectures are creative and he tries to involve everyone by learning 150 students' names. He explains concepts very clearly and is welcome to any questions during class. I strongly encourage taking this class!

Professor Hart is an awesome at explaining his knowledge of the subject as well as incorporating the text book material as well.  He is personable and whitty, which helps to make lecture more bearable if you are disinterested in the subject.  He helps everyone in any way he can.  Highly recommended.

He makes an effort to get to know ALL of his students. He explains things really well and mostly wants to answer your questions, so make sure you read the chapters before class.  Basically, if you read the chapters, ask questions, and go to labs, you will do fine.  Professor Hart does everything he can to help, so ask for help if you need it!

He's a really good teacher.  I like him alot and he answers questions very well.  And also, to add interest in the lectures he's funny too.  He makes science fun for me and understandable.  He also gives a lot of effort to know your name.
Stay on top of the work and it won't be bad.

She taught well and recorded her notes for the class. Although the class was heavy on proofs and math, the ease of accessing her notes from class made it very reasonable and easy to learn the material if you put the work in.

I had the opportunity to take 378 from both Miner and McMurray. Both are amazing professors who give great lectures. Dr. Miner definitely leans more towards proofs and is math heavy in comparison. The only piece of advice is to be comfortable and prepared with any calculus equations around the concepts taught in class. Very smart and well prepared.
Great class kept it very interesting and provided difficult but rewarding problems. Felt like a math class but I didn't mind

Loved Prof. Miner's class. She is a fantastic teacher and prepares students well for her tests. Her online notes are clear, but I found that her in person lectures best helped me understand the concepts. She also offers quite a few opportunities to get extra credit on the homework's and in general, she is a very fair grader.

Professor Miner is one of the best profs I've ever had. She is invested in her students and wants them to be successful. She also prepares really thoroughly for lectures and teaches all the concepts in a very accessible way. Definitely take a class from her! You won't regret it.
Deeply cares about her students. Makes class fun and posts in class notes on learning suite. Tests are representative of material learned in class. Flexible with extra office hours.
Dr. Miner is the best! She is wicked smart and is very great at explaining tough concepts. She is very personable and humble. You're going to want to take her class.

Best Econ professor I've had so far. She is new to BYU and obviously loves econ and her students already. She goes the extra mile to be involved with her students. The class isn't overly difficult but it's not easy. She takes feedback and improves from it. Highly recommend taking from her.

This was a necessary class for my schedule.  Nice teacher. Didnt learn anything.  I think BYU is just hiring nice people to try and build back a tarnished reputation.  Thank goodness she is only a visiting professor. Hopefully her visit ends soon.

Prof. Leavitt is super nice, but not super on top of it.
Unorganized and is too busy to help with anything.
I am not sure she is super smart, but can manage her lectures.
Super nice person tho.

Nice person, but is not a leader. 
Learned nothing. 
She should stay in elementary school where she belongs. No business teaching people smarter than her.

I really enjoyed Professor Leavitt's class! She made the material interesting to learn and very interactive. She was very helpful in guiding us to know what assignments we had and assisting us along the way.

*Not a difficult class!

I really enjoyed Professor Leavitt's class! She made the material interesting to learn and very interactive. She was very helpful in guiding us to know what assignments we had and assisting us along the way.

She is so sweet but is a harsh grader and requires a 96% to have an A which is unlike any other course I have taken at BYU. She gives no grace period on attendance and participation when you are sick. I did not learn anything from this class. Lots of busy work. Her learning suite and instructions for big assignments are unorganized and unclear.

Hailey is honestly the sweetest person ever but she should NOT be a professor. She is an incredibly biased grader and doesn't believe in 100 percent so she will take off points on things like "aesthetics." She is "too busy" to help you with papers but then does not provide a specific rubric. Hopefully they find someone to replace her.

Hailey really helped me learn foundational theories about early child development and assigned projects that were meaningful and helped me put theory into practice. She was great at modeling activities that I could take to the classroom and she was very supportive and approachable!
She grades pretty easily, but there is a lot of busy work and group projects. She is super sweet and caring, but not sure I took a ton away from this class.

Professor Leavitt is super nice and tries to make class great, but she teaches us like we are her kindergarteners. The class did not teach me anything new. She grades easily, but I didn't actually learn anything.

She is really nice and tries to make it fun but the class is kind of pointless, it is just everything that we have already learned in other classes. The class is super easy and she is an easy grader, but the class is pretty pointless.
Hank Smith is so much fun! He helped me see the gospel in new perspectives and there wasn't much homework.

He is very funny and his classes are super entertaining. I have learned so much from him, such an amazing guy. His tests are a lot harder than most religion classes, so study hard for them and you will do fine.
Great lectures

Dr. Smith is the best! His lectures are so hilarious, yet you still always leave feeling the Spirit and with a better understanding of the gospel. He tells you everything that is going to be on the exam ahead of time, and he sticks to that. The workload is relatively small and fair for a religion class.
Brother Smith cares a lot about his students and is so funny. His exams are super hard for no reason but other than that 10/10

Stand up comedy for an hour every MW. If you read your scriptures every day and enjoy laughing, this is definitely your class. If you think that joking shouldn't be in a classroom, don't take this class. If you're like most other people though, this'll be your FAVORITE class of the year
He needs more 5/5 ratings, otherwise I won't say anything new
Engaging lectures, spends too much time on student questions sometimes. You have to actively try to not get an A
he is super funny and entertaining. explains well. Attend class and you'll do fine

I LOVE Hank Smith. I've taken him for various classes multiple times just because he's so good!! He dedicated the first half of class entirely to doctrine questions, and even will talk after class with you (as long as he doesn't have another one after). I bring most of my honest questions to him and I hope I can one day be a TA for him!!!

This was definitely one of my favorite classes this semester. Professor Smith is absolutely hilarious, and his lectures are engaging. It is easy to pass the class if you come to class and do the readings. There were several times in this class that I felt the spirit, too. I would recommend him to anyone!
He offers so much extra credit, as long as you do it you will get an A.

Very cool class. I wish he would do less questions so we could actually get to the lesson, because he knows so much! Very easy to pass, the tests were a breeze. Just be aware that your final is a 10 page project. Other than that pretty simple class.

I loved his lectures! They were very engaging and I loved going to class. However, the exams were very difficult and that is where I struggled. He is hilarious; however, I feel like it would be nice if he lectured in class on the content instead of assigning us video lectures to watch. Overall, it was a very difficult, but very high-quality class.
Great teacher!

I had lots of fun with this class. Hank offered to answer questions during every lecture. He gives study guides for his tests during lecture and lets you to take a picture, "as a reward for coming to class." The final was mildly difficult, but not too bad. Maybe 3 hours study time. Readings were 600 words a week. He teaches time effective lectures.

If you are struggling with your testimony, he is a great professor. What he teaches/says is very non-judgmental and makes you feel accepted. Not afraid to talk about difficult church subjects. Does get carried away/goes into devotional mode, but you're getting a deeper takeaway than Sunday school.

Bro Smith is hilarious, but sometimes it was hard to figure out what we were learning about. His lessons were kinda all over the place, and sometimes he'd tell stories that were long and unrelated and then left no time for scripture convos. Again, SUPER funny, nice dude. But if you are looking for a super spiritual class, I'd look at another prof.

He definitely has a very specific teaching style that isn't for everyone (jokes around a lot) but he lets all the students know that from the start. He makes the classroom environment/lectures an enjoyable place to be and is really understanding/flexible.

Some people believe in a heliocentric universe; I now believe in a Hankcentric universe. If Bro Smith jumped off a cliff, I would be right behind him. He was more than a teacher; he was a stellar role model, a caring mentor, a father away from home, a spiritual giant, and kinda funny.  UNIV was one of the greatest classes due to his care.

TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM. Although the exams can be hard for some, he will help you succeed by preparing you well, he will answer your questions and explain the material well. In addition, he posts lectures on you tube on those days that he's missing which are a great addition to help you prepare for the exams. I learned so much from him!!
Professor Smith answers questions unrelated to the course material through the entire class period. Material learned entirely on your own. lots of writing.

He's hilarious and spends the first half of class answering students' questions. He also gives a review slide at the beginning of class that makes it easy to know what you need to know for the exams since he won't test you on something that isn't on the review slides.

He doesn't teach at all. He's a funny guy but it's not worth it because you don't learn much from his classes. He spends majority of the class period answering questions which could be helpful but its mostly only applicable to the person who had the question. He gives a review slide at the end of class which is what you need to study on your own.
I really like how Bro Smith interacts with his students and his passion for them and the course but I felt that he did not prepare us for the tests well.
He's hilarious and outgoing. And his lectures are christ-centered, they are inspirational. He encourages us to ask him questions that we have while we read the docturine we study in class.

I am infinitely grateful for the semester I spent with Hank Smith. God bless this wonderful man. If he was my dad, I would be so proud. Man, I wish he was my dad. He is hilarious, goofy, and so incredibly fun but also has the strongest testimony and loves his family, this Gospel, and his students so deeply. And he's a fantastic therapist! Take him!

Brother Smith is an amazing teacher! His tests are challenging, and your grade relies heavily on them, so be sure to study. He provides review slides that cover the material you'll be tested on, so if you prepare, you'll do fine. He also strengthened my testimony and tells great stories to keep the class engaging!

Hank is one of the strongest reasons that I literally came back to the church this semester. If you have left and want to come back and aren't sure how, take his class. He teaches in such a wonderfully non-judgemental way.

Just being in the pure presence of this wonderful specimen has altered the trajectory of my life forever. My entire posterity will be blessed with the stories of Hank Robert Smith. You will never find a better professor at any other university on this planet. Some might even say he is the GOAT. I love this guy! Ask about the cactus story…;)

Stop scrolling through Rate My Professor at 2 a.m. trying to decide whether to take this class. TAKE THE CLASS! Brother Smith is AMAZING. Half the time I wasn't sure if I was in a real lecture or an improv show. Best class ever! If you want a professor who's funny, understanding, and legitimately cares, this is your sign. Would love to take again!

I truly had a great experience with Bro. Smith. He starts every lecture with questions from the class and makes an effort to answer as many as he can. He was super funny but also knew when to be serious. If you ever take a class from him, ask him about the Cactus Story!

Michael Jordan, LeBron James, and Hank Smith. The greatest to ever do it. I will be naming my firstborn son Hank after my experience in Univ 101. I will also be writing Hank Smith on every electoral ballot I receive in the mail from this point forward. This university, state, and country would FLOURISH under his leadership. Life CHANGING class.

Hank Smith is a very hilarious guy and tells a lot of jokes and stories. He also has a Q&A session in the beginning of the class and I've learned so much from that even if it means we don't make it to the actual content of the lesson. You'll definitely learn something from the class but it may or may not be about the BOM.

Yes there are a lot of times you hear stories, hear answers to questions, and laugh a lot but he tells you this is going to be the case at the beginning of class! So worth it so hear his insights and feel uplifted after his class. I've learned a lot, because he wants to help you in your own life. He also is so willing to help you get a good grade.

Brother Smith is the absolute best religion professor. He spends the beginning of class answering any and all gospel questions, and his method of teaching is super engaging, funny, authentic, and refreshing. He tells great stories and jokes around a lot (so don't take his class if you can't take a joke). I learned so much about the Book of Mormon.
I liked the lighthearted atmosphere, but I struggled with the lack of structure and clarity. At times, it felt more like an open Q&A than a guided course.

I would never take a religion class from anyone but Bro Smith. He is so funny, and makes lectures always super engaging. He also has infinite knowledge on everything and is always willing to answer questions. Tests can be tough, but he gives you every answer to study beforehand. Only real assignment is one big paper at the end of the semester.

Not only is Brother Smith HILARIOUS, but he has a satisfying answer for almost any gospel question you can ask him. He's so good at making confusing scriptures easy to understand. His teaching style isn't for everyone, especially if you're easily offended by his jokes, but I loved his class. Get an early start on the final paper.

The Legend of Professor Hank Smith:
Listen close, and hear the tale,

As someone who struggles with solemn sappy crying emotional religion teachers (no offense), Hank Smith was a godsend (literally lol). 1/2 the class was him answering questions about ANYTHING which was very helpful. He can get a lil adhd but gives all the info for exams and is super entertaining to listen to. Don't take if you are easily offended:)

Incredible lectures, absolutely hilarious and spiritual at the same time. He is extremely clear about what will be on the test (review slides). Attendance is graded, and critical to doing well on the tests. All course questions go to your TA, but he will happily discuss any gospel or personal questions. There is some homework, but it's easy.

Bro. Smith is great. Easy professor with few assignments- 1 big paper that was for your testimony & growth. He does talk a lot, sometimes about off-topic questions, but he tries to answer everyone's gospel-related questions because he cares very much for students' comprehension/understanding. He teaches fast & with humor.

LOVED HIM!! Seriously an amazing professor and takes great interest in his students. If you dont keep up with the reading you can fall behind. Tests were a little difficult but he gives you very clear study questions so definitely manageable. Take this class from him!

I CANNOT RECOMMEND BROTHER SMITH HIGHLY ENOUGH!! I now have such a greater understanding and love for both the Savior and the New Testament. If you attend class and really study (honestly memorize) his review slides, his tests are fine and hw is basically reading scriptures, journaling, and one paper. I will be taking another class from him!!

I've taken two of his classes, and they were great. His classes are fun to go to because he makes each lecture fun and engaging. He says that the purpose of his class is to gain knowledge because that's what he can test you on, but i think my testimony has grown the most from his two classes than any other class ive taken here at BYU.

Bro. Smith is amazing. He starts class by asking if we had any questions before diving into what we need to know. He is genuinely so caring and wants to get to know you. He shines the light of Christ in his class. His comedy isn't half bad either. He really prepared me for my mission, take the class from him.

Brother Smith is one of my favorite religion professors. He cares a lot, is spiritual, is funny, and you learn a ton from his classes. This class was reasonably easy and my testimony grew substantially this semester. Cannot recommend him enough.
bro smith is legit so good. i loved his teaching style and how he incorporates humor, but he balances it out very well with the spirit

I cannot recommend him enough. If his name does not already persuade you to take his class, then his knowledge and how he structures the class will. The syllabus looks stiff, but it loosely resembles the class. Every lecture is engaging and amusing. He makes sure that every student has a chance to do well in his classes. I highly encourage it!

Hank is hilarious! His lectures are so enteraining, but they have nothing to do with exam questions. He gives you all the information you need to get an A on every exam, but the questions are dumb. His tests are purely memorization of random facts. He's such an amazing guy though and I loved attending his class regardless!
It was an easy A, but for a New Testament class, it was focused very minimally on Christ's gospel.

Was not a fan of this class, he makes this class so much harder than it has to be. The tests are in the testing center and if you miss a class period you don't get the study material. Attendance is also MANDATORY, there is a QR code he puts on the screen everyday. There is also a journal you have to do every week. He is cool but the class is not.

Brother Smith's class has been one of my favorite religion classes! He made the New Testament really come alive and has a passion for what he teaches. He is hilarious and doesn't really have a filter- so if you're not a fan of that for a religion class, I would pick someone else.

He is seriously so awesome! 10/10 recommend

The only reason I received an A- and not an A is because I turned in too many assignments late. Late work is docked, but the workload isn't big at all. Journal entry and a 3 question weekly review due every week. You will have to study for tests, but Brother Smith is very good at reviewing, and there will always be an opportunity to make up points.

I loved this class. Brother Smith is like one of the voices in my head come to life. If you want a serious professor or can't take a joke, find a different professor. Brother Smith is amazing. I left the class with a much greater knowledge and understanding of the New Testament. He spoke in a language I could understand.

You think you know the scriptures until you take a class from Bro Smith. You can see how knowledgeable he is and how much he cares. I left class knowing 4x as much about the Book of Mormon and with a testimony 4x as strong. He's also hilarious and will never make a class boring. He made the scriptures real-life applicable and more realistic.
Gret guy gives good feedback, actually reads the homework

He isn't the teacher for everyone, but I enjoyed his class. He does get easily sidetracked, and even though he says, "if you come to class, you'll do well on the exams," I still had to study a bunch to do good. There are a few exams, a paper/project that was fun, and weekly journal entries. Overall learned and stretched my knowledge!

Very fun and engaging in class however gets off topic very easily so if you want a serious professor, go somewhere else. He will entertain you in class and give you all the answers to his exams as well but you are able to have spiritual experiences in class if you pay attention and participate.

Hank teaches by humor. This approach usually doesn't work in my opinion but hank pulled it off by very clearly outlining course content, I was never surprised by the test questions and tests were easy if you put in the work, it was hard to do really bad, plus we had extra credit if you were struggling, He really does care and rewards hard work

There are 2 exams and one final which are a decent portion of your grade, but he provides review slide and basically tells you exactly what kind of things will be on the test. It is a pretty easy class with not much homework. Attendance is also a huge part of the grade, and you need to attend to get lecture slides. The professor was amazing!

Very engaging. He did get off topic often, but it was to answer questions asked by people in the class. Make sure to take pictures of the review slides. My main gripe with this class is that his TA's graded incredibly slow. I know there are a lot of students but after the last day of class I still had probably 20 ungraded assignments.

The amount of jokes this man made is literally copious. Every class I was dead from laughing while still learning more about my Savior and feeling closer to him. Definitely shows how you can grow closer to God in a comedy environment. Definitely take this class

Brother Smith is really fun, but he structures some of his classes around his jokes. There are some good lessons and teachings in some of his classes, but it takes a while to get there. His tests are pretty hard. This is not the religion class you take for an easy A. You have to study for it and do well on the exams.

I have never wrote a review before but Hank Smith deserves it. I wouldn't say this is a very easy show up and get an A class if you don't study. His lectures are literally amazing though. I've never had a professor inspire me as much as he has in a religion class and thats worth any amount of studying required for the class. TAKE THIS CLASS!

His lectures are seriously so entertaining! He is literally the funniest and you think class is going great until the tests... all the material on the tests you basically teach yourself. He teaches so well, just not necessarily what you will be tested on. The review slides are CRUCIAL. Go to class to make sure you don't miss those.

His lectures are funny and spiritual at the same time. His review slides are crucial!! so go to class to get them. I've taken him 3 times and am doing it again next semester haha because he is that good!!
I love Hank Smith, he is bae. If you are his kid reading this, I hope you know that I am jealous and wish Hank was my dad.

Hank smith is one of the best teachers I have ever had. The way he teaches the Book of Mormon is like no other and is incredibly effective at getting principles and lessons across. Really the only problem is that his classes are often to large so you never really get to talk to him really only ask questions. But he is still a incredible teacher.

I LOVE THIS MAN. He makes your heart happy and teaches you so much about the scriptures. He he hates tests becuase this is a religion class and thats dumb. He teaches through humor and stories. I have never learned so much about the scriptures. He is so awesome. You do have to write a 10 page paper but its not hard its like a talk.

I was looking forward to taking Hank's class for years, and I was not at all disappointed! He is one of my favorite people in the world. His lectures are so amazing that I continued attending even when I wasn't taking his class. He knows so much about the gospel and the scriptures and I love his humor. He really loves the Savior and his students!

Bro Smith is a hilarious and engaging professor. While the workload can be heavy, his classes are so entertaining that you won't want to miss them. Unstuckstudy AI proved super helpful for prepping for the tricky exams.

Brother Smith is amazing! He's fun, he's funny and makes the class enjoyable. Readings aren't bad and just have weekly quizzes to go along with each which just ask if you went to class and completed the reading! I've taken two of his classes and the exams are easy if you go to class he shows slides of what will be on the exam!
Hank Smith is amazing, you already know this. If you go to class he preps for perfectly for every exam. You have to not care to get a bad grade.

Really fun class. Such a funny guy who's fun to learn about the BOM from. I already read the BOM a lot so the daily readings + journal entries weren't much of a burden, and I already knew most of what showed up on the tests. He gives review slides so there's plenty of opportunity to know what'll be on the test. Fun class if you try.

Brother Smith is incredible. Genuinely increased my testimony SO MUCH. my only complaints were the 10 page paper (graded super easy tho), and tests that you kinda had to study for. A solid 1-2 hours of studying should prep you well enough for each midterm/exam. The class is not hard at all if you go to lectures and cram for 1-2 hours before tests

Not the easiest religion class you'll take but Hank is a funny dude. He get's on tangents a lot in class but makes class engaging and fun. Tests require you to memorize a decent amount. Use TA reviews and treat the tests like any other test and you'll do fine. Requires biweekly journals and a 10 page paper at the end of class.

Favorite religion professor. Also the funniest professor I've ever had. Your grade based on a journal entry before class about the readings, a 10 page paper due the end of the semester, and 3 tests. Alyssa is BY FAR the best TA because her test review slides are word for word on the test. Study those slides for a few hours and you'll be golden.

Hilarious professor, don't take him if you don't like jokes in religion classes. Tests aren't that hard, TA reviews give you all you need. I studied for ~2.5 hours and got A+ both times. Gave the most engaging lectures out of any other religion professor I've had, good mix of spiritual and funny. 10 page paper is devotional so it's not terrible.

Really funny and I liked him but tbh I thought I would like him more. Good but nothing as magical as I expected. I feel like I did not really learn too much, just a lot of plot memorization- I love the nitty-gritty scriptorian approach- this is a lot like a seminary class with 200 people. Tests are easy if you want to memorize lil bits, not if not

Brother Smith is hilarious, and you learn a lot from the class. He gives a review slide every class with ALL the material you might need to know for the tests, so as long as you show up to class and review the material he gives you it's an easy class. Super engaging professor. Don't take him if you don't like to mix humor and religion though.

Lectures are awesome, and Brother Smith is super engaging. Tests are on the tougher side, requiring a lot of memorization and stress (because who doesn't stress in the testing center?) There are quite a few assignments and a paper/project throughout the semester.

Brother Hank is a phenomenal teacher! This class has been my favorite religion class at BYU so far! I will say, the exams can be HARD. Brother Hank gives you review slides every class, but it is very much "what happened in this chapter." There is a 10 page paper as well, but I did not think it was bad at all! biweekly journal entries too.

If you like funny, knowledgable, story-teller, and rambler, then take it from him. People say you cant feel the spirit, you can, but it just depends if you like his style of teaching. Really helps you understand the scriptures better. Tests are really hard (straight memorization) but go to TA review, narrows down what you need to know.

Personally thought the workload was fine for 2 credits...Bro Smith is AMAZING, so funny, knows so much, and is great at explaining things well and teaching with stories. if you don't go to lecture consistently you'll be lost (missing a couple days is ok) but honestly it's so good you won't want to miss!

Very good speaker and interesting to listen to... but often goes on tangents unrelated to the BOM. The tests were unnecessarily hard. The reviews do not help. You have to write a 10-page paper and take 3 tests.
(I do not recommend it, there are definitely easier religion classes!!!)

Hank Smith is a fantastic lecturer. You can tell that he really cares about the Gospel of Jesus Christ and the students. 
600+ words per week and 2-8 chapters per class period. 
Weekly reports were awful, lost a TON of points on them because I didn't do all the readings or 300 word journals before class. 
10 page paper or project required

If you do not go to class you will not do well. This is a religion class that is focused on spiritual literacy, so you will need to memorize BOM chapters and their contexts. Bro Smith is really entertaining, but I will say his class felt a bit more geared towards pre-missionary students. That has more to do with culture rather than content.

I absolutely love Professor Smith, I would take his class if I was auditing the class and not taking it for a grade. The class is very test heavy and chaotic.  I loved the class atmosphere however, he rarely taught.  It was constant funny rambles which were great! But regarding learning and feeling prepared? missed the mark for me. Amazing man fr.

Honestly I will never understand why some think this class if difficult. If you go to class and pay attention, tests are easy. Winging the first one I got a 94 percent. There are little journals due every week but they are easy. Amazing guy who somehow balances spiritual experiences and amazing humor. Love this man and would recommend him.

Brother Smith is worth all of the hype. He is super funny and does make light of things so maybe not for the faint of heart... He explains things uniquely and helps you understand the history and connection of the BOM. Tests ARE NOT HARD if you go to class, get the review slides, and UNDERSTAND THEM.

Bro Smith has been my favorite religion professor. His lectures are so entertaining and I have learned so much about the Book of Mormon. You read multiple chapters of the BOM every week and write journal entries but its great personal study. 10 page paper too. He literally gives you the info that will be on the tests so if you study you're good.

Brother Smith is such a great professor. I learned so much about the Book of Mormon from a historical perspective and left each class feeling uplifted. He prepares you very well for the exams, and though studying is definitely required for his exams, you will do great if you study the material he provides. Take a class from Brother Smith at BYU!!

Hank Smith knows his stuff. But his lectures are all historical based and not principle based. If you are looking for an an easy A DONT take this class. 600 words of writing are required each week, a 10 page paper l, and the tests are IMPOSSIBLE. Would not recommend.

Very overrated. Class is focused more on the history of BOM rather than principles and doctrine. 300+ word journal responses due every class. Tests are very hard for a religion class - he gives a review slide each class that the test is based off of, so just try and memorize those. There's a 10 page paper as well which is a bit excessive.

Best religion class I have ever taken at BYU. Lectures are insightful and engaging. He tells you exactly what he is going to put on the test so you know exactly what to study. Never been happier with a religion class, ever.

Hank Smith strengthened my testimony at BYU. This is who you want to take for religion. He is one of the funniest people I have ever met and is amazing at teaching the gospel. He helped me strengthen my relationship with Heavenly Father and always gave me a good laugh. You do personal journals every day and one paper, but tests are straightforward.

Hank certainly lives up to the fame, if you want to laugh every lecture, definitely take from him! I will admit though, it was rare to have frequent spiritual moments since we laughed pretty much the whole time, and that's my only complaint! He sure knows his stuff and has an incredibly strong testimony!

He is an awesome guy and a very entertaining speaker, but the amount of work needed to exceed in Christ and His Everlasting Gospel class was unnecessary. A 10 page paper and a 100+ question final in any two-credit course is way too much in my book. I also was hoping to learn more about Christ's actual gospel, but instead it felt like Bible history.

Brother Smith is a great guy with a fantastic sense of humor. However, in lectures he seemed to easily get distracted and would rush through his slides. The 10 page paper is very excessive. Tests are okay. I'll be taking my remaining religion credits from other professors.

Professor Smith is the BEST religion professor at BYU! Definitely take as many religion classes from him as possible. Anyone who says his class is hard is lying, he literally gives you the answers for the tests and the TA reviews give you everything. You will learn so much about the scriptures and gain a bunch of cool insights! Highly recommend!

okay I love hank smith as much as everyone else here does but BRUH his exams are legit hard. they were the hardest exams out of all my classes this past semester. a lot of memorization and history and scripture things. his lectures can also get a little crazy sometimes. good professor otherwise!

He's hilarious so it makes going to class fun. His teaching/lecture style might not be for everyone though. He makes a lot of jokes and doesn't go in depth on some concepts and just asks you to memorize what's on the test. So if that's not your thing, take a different professor. If you go to class/TA reviews you'll do well on the tests.

This was easily my favorite class this semester! Brother Smith's lectures are very engaging, teach you the material (both for the test and to understand the doctrine for life), and at least once per week I walked away from class inspired to be a better disciple of Christ. Go to class and you shouldn't have any problem on the tests.

One of my favorite professors at BYU. I really enjoyed Brother Smith's teaching style. His presentations were well organized and had an easy to follow flow of information. He encourages participation during lectures and cares for his students.

He is funny and high energy. Everyone loves him. The class is pretty easy and reviews for the test are the biggest help. There is a paper that is more graded on effort and the weekly assignments are reflections on what you learned. The assignments helped me learn more and made the lectures more fun. Great class would recommend.

LOVED this class. Not hard at all. There is one big paper at the end, but you just write about your relationship with Christ so it was really enjoyable. You have to study for the tests but the T.A's set you up perfectly for them. No surprises. Also Brother Smith is truly the greatest teacher and I wish all my classes were from him.

Bro Smith is a great guy! Don't take if you don't love humor mixed in with religion. Jokes felt unnecessary at times. Tests were somewhat difficult considering how memorization it was. He LOVES the history of Israel so the class is heavy on that. Unfortunately I don't love it as much as he does so it was hard to follow along sometimes.
Very funny and engaging; tests are heavy on memorization but he tells you exactly what you need to know.

He is a very funny professor. However, I had trouble understanding his teachings. He kind of expected his students to have a perfect knowledge of the scriptures. I did not do well on his tests and they were very doctrine heavy. If you aren't a scriptorian or don't exactly know a lot about the specific details from the stories, I don't recommend.

Great fun lectures. Memorize the slides shown at the beginning of class and you'll be fine for the 2 midterms and final. TA review also helps a ton. He sometimes gives answers to the tests during his lectures. Very fun and uplifting. 10 page paper is a pain but if you work on it ahead of time, you'll be fine.
Loved his class! The tests were very memorization heavy which is hard for me. I recommend going to the TA review or watching the Zoom she posts. This will help you get an A.
This is an amazing class. Brother Smith is so hilarious and time goes by so quickly. As long as you study the test aren't too bad.

Lectures are hilarious and invite the spirit. Day-to-day assignments aren't too much work. But his tests are difficult. His tests are finishing quotes, who said quotes, where quotes are from, and dates. It feels impossible and unimportant. There's a 10-page paper but it's not too difficult. I do not recommend taking this class from him.

Hank Smith is my favorite religion teacher at BYU. His lectures are so interesting that time flies by. The workload is light but the tests go into detail. Go to the TA review before each test because they basically give you the answers. 10/10 recommend, so spiritually strengthening.
I really loved this professor he was an amazing teacher, however his lecture style is hard to memorize things for the test.n

Brother Smith is a great professor and has amazing lectures. The tests are pretty difficult, however and there's lots of reading but other than weekly journal entries and a big paper at the end it's not too bad of a work load. He's super fun to listen to and emphasizes enjoying the lectures more than taking notes.

I have taken classes with this professor before and love every second. He believes that humor and religion can go together and uses it to help us understand the scriptures and Christ's ministry in a modern way. One of the best classes I've ever taken. If you think Brother Smith would not be good for you, listen to one of his youth talks on YouTube.

The best. The only religion class that I do not get bored in. He gives you plenty of resources to do well on the exams. The 10 page paper is a big assignment but not the worst if you spread it out and get it done early.
Easy A. Take his class 100%. His TA give you all the answers to the exams basically.

He is so funny and explains things about Christ and His life so well. He basically gives you all the test answers if you go to class. The only thing that is kind of hard is the 10 page paper, but it wasn't graded very strict at all.

Take this class from him. Bro. Smith is super funny and has a way of making the Book of Mormon come alive. If you want to succeed, you need to come to class for the review slides that he shows at the beginning of class. The tests are pretty simple if you study the review slides, as he discourages note taking so you can pay attention to the lecture.

LOVED this class. He made the Book of Mormon really come alive. His tests require you to know what happens in chapters and books, but I loved that. Not an easy A: you'll have to study and do readings, journals, and a paper. If you want an easy religion credit, pick someone else. If you want to know the Book of Mormon, take it from Hank Smith.

Brother Smith knows his stuff and is a great lecturer, but his class is set up in a way that focuses on memorization rather than learning which was frustrating to me. The tests are hard because you have to memorize slides and slides of information but if you actually know all of it you'll be just fine. Liked the class, hated the testing style.

HANK SMITH IS AS AWESOME AS HE SOUNDS!! He taught such great lessons and increased my love for the Book of Mormon!! Through his personal stories and funny jokes he made me excited to go to class! We had one essay and a few tests and weekly journal entries which were very manageable!! I loved this class! I highly recommend!

This class was so uplifting and fun! I learned so much and always enjoyed going to class. The exams were easy because the TA does reviews and literally tells you everything that's going to be on it. There is one big paper that's easy to get full points on. There are weekly 300 word write ups. Super great and easy class, take from hank!

Amazing professor! I learned a ton and had a great time in class. He makes things fun and memorable. He tells you exactly what you need to know for exams and the homework is basically just a short journal on what you read. Loved this class!

Taking from Bro Smith was what a religion class at BYU should be!  The main homework of the course was reading the assigned scriptures and doing a journal entry before every class, and then in lecture he reviews what we need for the test before jumping into the content.  He is super funny but also teaches really profound and meaningful doctrine.

I really wanted to enjoy this class, but I spent so much time feeling so stressed and overwhelmed by memorization and frantically trying to remember quotes and stories than I did feeling the Spirit. If you are well-versed with the Book of Mormon I'm sure you'd thrive in this class.

Hank is such an amazing teacher and is super funny! I learned a lot more about the New Testament! He provides review slides and the TA Julia gave exam review sessions that pin-pointed almost exactly what was on the test. The exams are in the testing center and you will have to memorize the material. Overall not too hard to get an A.

Do yourself a favor and take REL A 250 from Hank Smith. He's the best. Simply do the journal entries/readings before class, enjoy his amazing lectures, do the easy post-class weekly report, go over the review slides before the exams, and don't procrastinate the 10 page Living Christ paper too badly and you'll get an A no problem.

He is an amazing speaker and teacher and does a great job engaging the class. His tests are a lot of memorization, but if you study they aren't unbearable. I love how he incorporates humor into the gospel and creates an environment where you can have fun and still learn in a spirit-filled area.
He makes learning about the gospel fun and engaging. He gives you all of the information for the tests on a single review slide in each lecture.

Best professor I've ever had. Love his stories and he brings the book of mormon to life. Work is manageable and he sets super clear expectations of work and tests. I loved every moment of his class, wish he had more classes offered. I am tempted to retake the same class again for fun. If you don't like humor and the gospel don't take Hank Smith.

His class is easily the best class I have ever taken. He gives you all the answers to the tests if you go to class, he gives fantastic lectures, and is super funny! At the end of the semester, there is a 7-page paper, but that is the ONLY challenging assignment and the prompt is very open-ended. I would 100% take another religion class from him.

This class is solid if you want to understand the new testament. Make sure to do the reading if you want to get the most out of this class. The exams are easy if you show up to class and study. There is a 10-page paper due near the end of the semester but it is quite easy if you have been going to class. I Highly recommend this class.

He's entertaining, but for a class focused on Christ & his gospel, it wasn't as spiritually focused as I would've imagined/wanted. He focused a little too much on making people laugh, which took away from the subject matter. He required a 300 word journal entry about the readings for each day of class. It wasn't hard but seemed kinda redundant.

I DO NOT like how this class is set up. Every class he gives you a slide for the next exam that is just packed with bullet points. The exams are based on JUST what is on those slides so you have to memorize it all. It feels like I am memorizing the ENTIRE Book of Mormon between all the conference talks and direct scriptures you have to know.

You will have to write a 10 page paper on Christ for Hank's REL250 class. That's the hardest part. The tests are straightforward if you attend lectures, and he even gives you a lot of the test questions directly. Smith wasn't my favorite professor but his class was fair and I see why a lot of people like him.

I can honestly say that Brother Smith's class strengthened my testimony of the Book of Mormon. Besides being the funniest professor I've ever had, he also gives very engaging lectures and the homework load is minimal. I found the exams to be easy (he gives you all of the answers) but beware they are memorization based. You should take this class.
Hank Smith is one of the best religion professors for a reason. His lectures are so engaging, enlightening, and entertaining. He has such a captivating way of teaching.

He gives you study guide slides from last lecture at the beginning of every lecture. If you study those then you'll pass the tests. If you get the easy reading/participation points, then you should have no problem getting an A in the class. He's super funny and shares good insights. He tries to get to know as many students as he can.

This class changed the way that I view the BOM. Seriously BYU is so lucky to have bro smith. Going to his class was a joy, and I learned SO MUCH. As long as you study for his tests you will do great! I actually liked his tests because it was clear what I had to study and in the process I learned so much! Alyssa was an amazing TA.

Brother Smith is amazing! He tells good, relatable stories and brings the spirit so well into class. You can tell that he just KNOWS the gospel is true and he really helped me love the Book of Mormon.

The only thing to watch out for are the exams. They are a bit more difficult than most religion classes but still a lot easier than the average class. He gives you all the info on the exam, you just need to memorize a lot of information. His lectures are awesome.

My A minus was more my fault than the difficulty of the class itself.  Always know when every assignment is due.  The TA was great, and as long as everything is turned in on time, you almost never get less than anything right around full credit (even on the papers). The tests can be difficult if you struggle with memorization. Memorize his reviews.

Brother Smith taught me so much about the Book of Mormon! I always looked forward to class. He makes lectures entertaining and often will have class discussions. There is a good amount of reading and writing required but the work is worth it. It is easy to get an A. He gives out some of the test questions and makes the tests easy. Take it from him!
Brother Smith is inspiring for anyone who comes to class with a desire to learn important truths by the Spirit.

Hank Smith knows and loves the gospel and does a great job at teaching his students.
