Otherwise it really isn't that hard!

Dr. Pierce is amazing. She knows her stuff and although I definitely wasn't quite prepared for how tough the TAs would be on grading and how important attending class and doing the reading would be, her class was amazing. I learned so much. But wow I did not do well grade wise because the assignments were weighted heavily and graded harshly.

She was honestly really good. Grading is a little bit more tough, but she definitely is a caring person and will take care of you if you need it. Utilizing the TA's will help you get a good grade in the class cause she is fairly specific in what she looks for! Overall great though.
One of the best classes ever! Very clear expectations, super interesting lectures, and life-changing principles. Anyone who wants to go into the social sciences should take this class.

One of the best professors I have taken a class from. Class time is focused a lot on discussions, and you can tell she cares about student input, even from those who express different opinions. The tests are harshly graded, make sure to reference lots of class material and make connections. All in all, I couldn't recommend Professor Pierce more!

She's a compassionate teacher and expects quality coursework. Given how sensitive the subject material is and the oft tense relationship it can have to the church, it's seriously impressive how she is able to balance academic rigor and sensitivity to church teachings. However, the reading quantity is really excessive for a 3.0 credit class!

This was far and away my favorite class I've taken. If more of her classes fit into my schedule in the future, I will absolutely be taking them. The class discussions are the perfect balance of lecture and discussion, and you can tell she truly cares about student thoughts. The exams are graded kinda harshly, but besides that, excellent professor!

Pro. Pierce is so INTELLIGENT! Prepare to do LOTS of reading and take occasional pop quizzes in class. There is one group project that you participate in, but it is very easy. There are some discussion boards throughout the semester. Get the textbook. Exams are timed essay responses to prompts. Sensitive topics are discussed in sensitive ways!

Dr. Pierce is an amazing professor! She is knowledgeable and really cares about what she teaches! She prepares you well for the tests and if you use the TA's the paper is relatively easy. I wish I could take all my classes from her.

Dr. Pierce is a really great professor! I do agree that her tests are pretty frustrating and unnecessarily difficult, but I loved the lectures. She is so open an shares so many stories from her life that relate to what we are learning. Overall, I enjoyed this class and think that everybody should take it!

Dr. Pierce is AMAZING!! She is so caring and gives incredible lectures that she approaches with care. There's quite a bit of reading for the class, but it's all great. Highly recommend this class because you'll learn so much!
This class is extremely interesting and Dr. Pierce does a great job of facilitating discussion. Sometimes the readings are a lot, but if you do the work and prepare you will do well in the class.

In a class of 60 people, 8 got A's. The class average was high but almost everyone got an A-. There is a weekly response essay and a big group project and the TA's are looking to take points off for anything. I got points docked for things like "creativity". You don't really learn much in class but the tests are surprisingly hard.

Way harder than an intro class should be. TAs were looking for any excuse to dock points. For the final you had to have every slide memorized. None of the material was hard but she makes the class stressful. To get a 10 on the response essays you NEED to: 1.reference another part of the class 2.rant about any liberal talking point. Saved my grade.

Dr. Pierce has a great understanding of sociology. Her lectures are very informative and inclusive. She respects everyone's opinions, while maintaining a very scientific approach to her class. This class can be very eye-opening, if you do not block out the evidence she explains. Also, the class is introductory level, so it is pretty relaxed.

Good professor, and a good intro course. Dr. Pierce is understanding of what college life is like and is fairly chill (she told us she isn't offended when students don't show up to class, etc) Very open-minded and respectful of different opinions, and tells students clearly and repeatedly to respect all opinions regardless of whether they agree.

Dr. Pierce is one of the best professors I had at BYU. Her lectures are engaging and fascinating, and her tests are open notes and application-based free-response questions. So, you have to know what you're talking about to do well. Be prepared to read the textbook, but if you put some work into it, you'll do well.

Great professor! The lectures are super engaging. Make sure to look at the feedback she gives you on papers. The assignments are really well set up so you work on portions of your paper a little at a time. Super amazing class and really intelligent professor.

Dr. Pierce is amazing. Even though we have different opinions on a variety of topics, I loved her class. She is so kind and genuinely cares about every single human being.  The class offers a very progressive perspective on gender, but she never tries to tell anyone how to think. 

TAKE THE CLASS! You will learn something new!

SOC 345. Professor Pierce was a wonderful professor. She was respectful, very knowledgeable, and had clear grading rubrics and assignments. We had a reading quiz and homework assignment each week. These homework assignments combined were essentially our final paper. Plus she is so sweet, it's obvious she cares about our success. Highly recommend!

I was not sure if I would like Dr. Pierce, but I was pleasantly surprised by her class. Dr. Pierce gives interesting lectures, and you can tell that she is still interested in the subject, even after mastering it years ago.  Her tests are a little more difficult than other class assignments might suggest, but she is a great professor overall.

Dr. Pierce is a fantastic professor. She has both the charisma and knowledge to make lectures enjoyable to attend. She had clear expectations and stuck to them. The tests were difficult, but she provides a study guide. I would recommend Dr. Pierce for any Sociology course. She facilitates a great learning environment.

Dr. Pierce is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. She is incredibly caring, so she will work with you as needed. She is a safe prof for LGBTQIA+ people, which is incredible at BYU. Her class does take effort, but it is worth it. I cannot recommend Dr. Pierce enough. She changed my life for the absolute best.
I have taken two classes from Prof. Pierce (111 & 367) and absolutely loved them both. She is an amazing professor. 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Pierce is so knowledgeable and very good at explaining complex topics in simple terms. She is very responsive and accessible to students. She is understanding of the stress of students and would be a good mentor to talk to.

This was a really great class! The material is super interesting, and even though the readings are kinda long they are super interesting to read. It's very clear what you need to do, and each week has basically the same layout. Make sure to study for the tests but the class really isn't too bad. Just a couple discussions and assignments each week
Y'all know the awkward last day of class where everybody claps for the professor? Hayley Pierce is the only person who deserves this.

I LOVED sociology of gender. Super interesting and Hayley did a great job at presenting the information in an unbiased way. All of her assignments were super straight forward and she was very willing to help us! Eye-opening material and I'm so glad I took this class.

TAKE SOC 367 FROM HAYLEY. This class is a real gem. Hayley is respectful, inspirational, and personable. This class isn't hard (you can easily get an A if you stay on top of deadlines and pay attention in class) but will force you to think critically. I came out of this class wanting to be a better person, and feeling like I had tools to do so

Honestly the hardest class I've taken at BYU. The tests are nearly impossible, and the paper is awful. I almost never knew what I was supposed to be learning. That said, Dr. Pierce is a great lecturer. This class is an eye opener for many. If I could have just gone to the lectures, this class would have been great.

Hayley is truly an amazing professor. I took her my first semester of freshmen year and she really changed my perspective on so many things. Many people rate this class badly because it does challenge your expectations, which can be a little weird for some people, but the things she teaches really do open your eyes and make you feel the spirit.

Dr. Pierce is really likeable, and she was good at explaining things (at least I thought so). My only complaint was the grading set-up, about 50% of your grade will be tests and 30% will be papers, so the projects can be pretty stressful. And the midterm didn't even really seem like it had relevant questions.

Dr. Pierce was fine. Her grading structure was kind of a mess. The two tests are application-based (and therefore somewhat subjective) but you only get a few example questions to study. I basically did the group project myself and was totally fine. If you're not willing to question your conceptions of society just don't take the class

Hayley is a breath of fresh air at BYU, but her class isn't organized very well. Most of your grade is from one midterm and one final, and both are much harder than you would expect. Very personally invested in her work, almost to the point of distraction from the material or relevant concepts. Not the best at explaining things.

Hayley is an amazing professor! I wish I could take her class over and over again! She opened my eyes to new perspectives and showed me that there is more to the world than I previously thought. She isn't biased, she's a realist and sometimes that's hard for people to take, but it's truly inspiring. Take this class! It will change your life!!

Prof Pierce is one of the best professors BYU has to offer. Though many students think she's biased and liberal, I'd blame their opinions on BYU's Mormon culture. She always thoroughly discusses the sociological concepts, providing opinions and ideas from both sides. The class is super interesting and organized, but the tests can be challenging.

She does a good job giving the material from the sociology point of view as is her job. which is the liberal view. But the student body is not on par with opposing views and there is a lot of mockery on that part. it is a biased class as is the nature with sociology but that is what there to present from the class.

Hayley was an amazing Professor! I loved taking her class. It was definitely hard (my lowest grade of the semester) and makes you think a lot, but she is so amazing! Her tests are focused mostly on application rather than definition, so be aware of that.

Hayley was a pretty good professor, but she didn't seem to have a super wide breadth or depth of the material. She only had one side of things which consisted of highly liberal views (which isn't bad - she just didn't really know the other side). The tests were about nitpicky stuff. She was willing to work with and talk with the students though.

Hayley Pierce is an absolute gem. Honestly one of my favourite professors this semester! I didn't read the textbook at all but you can probably get away with just going to class and really paying attention. my advice: pick a good group for the group projects and always do the extra readings (you'll be tested) 11/10 would recommend this professor.

I would not take Sociology from this professor. She constantly shared her opinions and argued with students if they didn't agree with her. You don't really learn anything from this class, but the midterm and final are easy. You can't take notes because she moves too quickly through slides.
Hayley is a great professor. I loved going to her classes. She knows what she is doing and does it well. She could improve on her grading methods though.

Hayley was a great teacher. She really knows her stuff and her tests aren't hard if you study and go to class. Attendance isn't for a grade but helps a lot. There are a few in class responses, 10 response essays through the semester (they are only one page and the prompts are interesting), 4 group assignments, a midterm and final.

Hayley is a great teacher but don't expect any mercy from her. Deadlines are deadlines and there shall be no lifelines to save you. The class is easy if you do the reading. Prepare for some very fun discussions.  P.S. When you inevitably start to incorrectly think that Hayley is biased, remember she is merely explaining the sociological perspective

Prof. Pierce is a qualified Soc111 professor. As mentioned in another review she doesn't provide great examples for sociological theories. The class assignments are easy, but it's mostly busy work. She is NOT unbiased. However, the class was a very easy A/A- (you need to average 90% on the exams for an A). She's nice, but could improve her methods

This "teacher" likes to use her classroom as a platform to push her own political opinions. Those who dare disagree are shut down or told their "data" is irrelevant. Rather than provide substantive data or studies to support her theories, she prefers to incite arguments and debates in class. Not much science being taught in this class.

soc111 is an easy class, you pretty much just need to go to class everyday though, because the midterm and final are based off what she talks about from the powerpoints in class.  Other than that just easy weekly assignments and there was a group project, but it was very manageable.

Awesome class, she makes it so cool and interesting.  She will listen to your concerns.  Super nice, answers emails, refuses to be called Professor.  She's great and obviously is passionate about sociology.  TAKE THIS CLASS.  It will expand your horizons.

Haley is very laid back. You have to go to class. The tests are based on what you discussed in class and only use the book as a foundation for the topics. She is very open minded and respects everyone's opinion. This class is really great if you want to hear many different opinions without the professor telling you what is right or wrong.

Hayley's class was a great introduction sociology.  She's caring, openminded, unbiased, and encourages discussion and participation.  The class is easy but the midterm and final are pretty challenging.  Her powerpoints aren't posted so be sure to go to class and take REALLY good notes in order to do well on the exams.

First of all, she had us call her Hayley, so she's a real boss. Second, her lectures are really engaging and she definitely opened my eyes to a lot. She's unbiased and makes everyone feel comfortable enough to share their opinions on things. Lots of homework, but it's manageable.

Hayley gives great lectures. Unfortunately, she doesn't put up any of her power points online so don't skip class. There are group projects, papers, open book quizzes and tests. It's not too much work as long as you stay on top of it.

Professor Pierce is incredible, she is young and vibrant and really cares about her students. She brings a fresh, unbiased perspective to the world of Sociology and does an incredible job of teaching the class through engaging lectures, relevant videos, and her own experiences. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

It was difficult to keep up with this course because assignment due dates did not always match the posted schedule. I struggled with major projects because instructions were limited. There should have been clearer assignment expectations, lectures that better prepared for the exams, and more consistent communication throughout the semester.

Although this class is about creating a good life for oneself, I felt that this class honestly made my life a lot worse that semester. The content of what we were actually learning was really interesting and helpful, but the homework and exams were a lot. Worst of all, our prep for exams was weekly lectures that did not cover anything on the exam.

The tests did not match the study guide well, and the due dates were inconsistent. (Says its due on 12th one page, but its actually due on the 11th type) And the lecture's did not match that weeks materials. I struggled because I often did not know what was expected of me, and it was not communicated clearly.

Lectures didn't correspond with the material being graded on- felt like two different classes. Teacher cancelled half our classes during the semester, nearly 30% of the required readings were fully inaccessible. No organization inside the modules- due dates were out of order in every module. No communication on upcoming assignments/tests 0/10

Super easy class. The professor is very kind and the work is pretty simple. There seems to be a lot of reading but the questions for the readings are word for word the same that will be on the reading quizzes (which are open note). Very confused on why there are any poor reviews on this course and teacher

I noticed multiple 5-star difficulty 1 ratings posted the same day with little explanation, which felt unusual. While I'm doing well, the heavy reading, videos, and exams make the class feel overwhelming rather than engaging. The workload feels disproportionate to the value I've received. I hoped for a more enriching experience.

Unless you're majoring in EXDM or for some reason have a passion to learn about it, stay away from this online class.

She seems kind, inspiring words. However, the online webinars just don't correlate well with exam material. All teaching is done through videos (not by her). No joke, there's more reading here than in my English Literature class.

The 10 5-star reviews on the same day are pretty sus.
Dr Johnson is a lovely person, she does care. However, I don't think the online format benefits her positive traits.
The TAs are hard to contact, grading is inconsistent, exams don't reflect the TA reviews. It's not a fun course . If you're going to take it, I suggest you do it in person.
Changed my life
Best class my whole time here!!
No words, learned so much!!
Easy! So very inspiring!
Favorite class at my 4 years here! Love it!
I love her! Best class ever! Easy! Changes your life!
Best class ever
Amazszzzing
Spirit lead
Best class I have ever taken. Inspirational and life changing!!!! Really I loved her.

Also a review for EXDM300 online class. As others said, webinars had nothing to do with content and the TA marking was harsh in my opinion.
So hard to contact! I was told to reach out if close to a grade for potential extra credit- close to the end of the semester. I've sent 4 messages/emails between her and TA in the last 2 weeks and no response.

Lovely person. However the course (EXDM 300) was brutal. Online class- none of the webinar content was relevant. Instructions unclear. She was hard to contact outside of class. TAs were hard to contact also. Also- no extra credit at all during the class? TA exam prep sometimes was irrelevant to the questions in the exams. Not a great experience.
Only gave her a 2 because she seemed like a good person. Would have probably gone lower. Lectures had nothing to do with what we were learning. Get ready to learn everything on your own.

This is actually for EXDM300 but it wasn't an option.

The webinars (this is online) have absolutely nothing to do with the course material for the week. The work on canvas basically needs to be done solo. The TAs mark heavily and even though it says on the rubric you can do certain tasks, you get marked down for it.

Class is full of great information applicable to anyone. Textbook is required, but you can get away with skipping some readings. Final project is a lot, but start early and it's no biggie. Creativity is key for the final project. Lots of memorizing for quizzes and the final test, but it's not too much. Most quiz/test information comes from lecture.

DO NOT take from her! She has a very specific idea of what she wants your paper/project to be, but doesn't actually tell you. Then she grades you based on what she had in her head. Tests are VERY difficult. Extremely nit picky & prepare yourself to memorize everything(like Highschool). Lectures were great, but exams and papers were ridiculous.

This class was a mess! It probably is better in person, but Sister Johnson did not start using Learning Suite until over halfway through. Her projects and papers were very unclear and her final was way harder than she made it out to be. It also was given before finals, which is against school policy. She was not accountable for her mistakes.

Best class. And most applicable. Heather is probably one of the coolest teachers I've had. Weekly quizzes, a few essays, a fun group project, and a final that she gives a killer review for. Most enjoyable class for me since I the content was interesting!

She really cares about the class participating and will have lots of interaction in lectures. Quiz every Monday based on mainly the lectures. I didn't buy the book and I am doing fine if you attend class and take good notes. Group project at the end of the semester but so far the class has been really laid back and she is pretty cool.

Professor Johnson was BY FAR my favorite professor! She teaches the best class at BYU!! It should be a general in my opinion. Anyways I loved her and feel like I can actually apply things I learned in her class to my life. Also she was the first professor to show any kind of appreciation for my hard work as a student!! TAKE HER CLASS!!

This was literally the best class I have ever taken. Heather is a freakin boss and it's the only time I have EVER literally looked forward to doing our group presentation or the class readings. This class is the bomb dot com

Sis. Johnson is a great lecturer and very approachable with questions. I have never left class with a question about the material because she does a very thorough job of explaining. Do not take this class for an easy A, but do take it if you want to learn a lot of things that are applicable to your every day life.

Sister Johnson teaches so you understand the material! She cares about your learning! This class will help you the rest of your life! I LOVE IT AND IT'S AMAZING!!! She's an amazing teacher who will teach you the true significance of wholesome recreation and why it's important to families!!! ALSO, you get to play every Wednesday!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS TO JUST FILL CREDITS!!! Based of other ranking here, I made the mistake of taking this, thinking it would be an easy 3 credit filler class. It is not. This class requires lots of work/reading. I wouldn't have taken it, if I had know how much time it would be. However, it is a very interesting class, if you have the time
Heather Johnson's Family Recreation reshaped my way of thinking. By far the BEST class I took at BYU.

Sister Johnson is a fun teacher. As long as you study for the weekly quizzes and attend class (not mandatory, but it gives you helpful points for your grade), you will be fine. She really taught me a lot. She compiled a bunch of articles into the textbook we use, and I'm not returning it! She cares about the students and wants to help them succeed.

She is really nice, tells great stories and is very understanding. i love the class. It isn't super hard but you have to work a bit. Fridays are "Portfolio" days which means we play games. Love the class and love her.
You will never take a better class than this.  Heather is the best teacher I've had during all my time at BYU.  I recommend this to everyone.
FANTASTIC! No midterm. One quiz a week takes place of midterm. Final. Few papers. You play games every Friday. You'll love going to class.

Heather is FANTASTIC!! One of the best professors I have had so far and I am a senior. She knows everything, and she is a stellar example of all the concepts she's teaching. She cares about each student and is more than willing to help. She's absolutely fascinating to listen to.

This class was really fun!  You need to go to class to get the info for the Friday quizes and attendance points, but she gives you all you need to know from the reading and makes them super easy and grades easy on papers.  Friday you just play games in class- it was fun!
Great teacher!  There is a lot of reading and papers, but they are easy and all about what you feel and think.  Fridays are great cause all you do is play games!!!!
Heather is AWESOME! Take the class from her. you'll never regret it. (I mean, come on. Fridays you just play games!)
Least fav class by far

She is one of the worst professors I have ever had. She is such a harsh grader (96% is the lowest A!!!) and docks points for the smallest things. She is fairly rude in class when she believes a student has misunderstood a concept. Whenever we are put into groups, all of the students vibe over how awful the class is. No idea who gives her 5s.

Professor Pack is amazing. She is super fun and cares about her students. She is a bit of a tough grader but she is available to give you feedback because she wants you to learn. Her class is super applicable to the real world (which I learned right away in my internship). If you have a chance to take MCOMM 320 from her DO IT!

The class isn't particularly difficult or useful. She cares a lot about the visual aspect (color schemes in powerpoint or fonts that clash), perhaps more than the organization of the information. A lot of time spent on things that aren't practical for the everyday workplace. You also feel like you have very little control over your grade.
I dont know how so many people like her, she seems like a nice person but grading criteria is very unclear and there is a ton of homework. Also, she heavily pushes her liberal leaning agenda

Professor Pack is absolutely awesome! She cares about your development and teaches you valuable skills that will actually be used in the real world. There are some challenging major assignments, as well as a tough grammar exam, but she and her TA's are super helpful and want you to succeed. I bombed the grammar exam and still got a B in the class.

Professor Larson is a really great professor. She does everything she can to help you; she really wants you to succeed. She isn't a big test person, but her grammar test is pretty difficult (she does curve it). Her grading material may be a bit confusing at first, so use the TAs (they are amazing)!! The class itself is VERY useful and appliable.

Prof. Pack is great for this class. She understands a lot about general business practices and gives a lot of good feedback. Honestly if you want a good grade and to do well, TALK TO HER! I asked for feedback from her and the TA and I did really well. Some instructions are vague but if you present your ideas to her she'll tell you if she likes it.
She is so personable. I took an online class from her. It was very straight forward, simple to understand, and easy enough. I learned quite a bit. The grammar portion is a pain, but you do learn.

This was an awesome class and I can not recommend Professor Pack highly enough. Genuinely invested in the students success, good lecturer, entertaining, very knowledgeable. Learned things I use today as a working professional 7 years later. One of my favorite classes I took at BYU and the one I remember best.

This class is very useful. Its also very easy to be successful. Professor Pack is gracious and helpful, is genuinely interested in helping her students succeed, and will go out of her way to accommodate her students. Also, she has a great sense of humor and hosts Sunday evening gatherings at her home. You would be a fool to take from anyone else.

I have always hated English/writing classes. I dreaded this class. I was wrong. It was amazing. Every assignment was real/practical - I use it every day in my job. Prof Pack is someone that really cares about being up to date and not wasting time on theory. Take this class. Just do it. Not hard to get an A, but will actually help prepare you.

Professor Pack really knows her stuff on this subject. I learned a lot. She is so helpful outside of class if you need some tips. She is also a pro at design- Your CV will never look better after this class. The business writing textbook is one I go back to reference years later.

Professor Pack really cares about each student, is super organized, and has great content. She spends hours making the course material clear and interesting. The course is tough, but SO worth it. Learn this stuff now rather than on your first job. Recommended!
Does not explain the material well enough for basic understanding. It was definitely a challenge to work with her. I wouldn't take the class again if I could.
Super useful class and great teacher!
Respected and caring. The contents are very helpful for ACME students who want to find a job.

This class was not about world music, it was a library research class. I wanted to learn about music but instead we had class prep assignments that would be 30 pages and big project was reading an ethnography and finding other sources with citations. No exams which was great, I don't feel like I've learned much of anything. Take another general!!

This class was not what I was expecting. We didn't learn about world music cultures as much as we discussed the philosophy of music and its connection to our identity. Mildly interesting, but expect that. Stopped going halfway through. Lots of really busy work that takes up time; we read about 20 pages almost every week for Class Prep Assignments.

This class was a slog. Super easy, just loads of easy busy work. I tried to be engaged and found a few things interesting but overall it felt like the class shoved other cultures down my throat. I love other cultures and they have amazing attributes but this was just overstretching it. She is great as a person but I did not enjoy the class.

Unbelievably boring. Class felt like going to nursery. Easy GE, but never felt engaged or learned anything. Honestly just felt like a big waste of time. She's very nice and cares about her students, but not the best teacher. Constantly going on about DEI - class felt like it was only about why we need to be nice to people who are different from us.

Easiest class at BYU. I took it for the Arts GE and didn't feel like a GE. I probably spent 2 hours every week outside of class working on assignments and this was in the Spring. No Tests or Quizzes, instead lots of easy assignments, in which you can easily get 100 percent. Also lots of extra credit. I ended up having a 107%.

Dr. Reed is awesome. She is passionate about music and has great insights to offer on the different topics covered in class. She is very kind and respectful. The topics covered are interesting and helped me view music and culture in a new way. I would highly recommend taking this class!

Professor Reed was amazing. She doesn't overstep bounds with this GE. She knows that most of us were there to fulfill the credit. The class has no due dates and no exams. There are around 30 assignments that can be completed at any point. Highly recommend taking this class!

Music 203 was so fun with her! I took it over the summer, so the material was spaced out differently, but I genuinely enjoyed the large project we did. It was basically an annotated bib, and she is very sweet and just wants to help. She is very passionate about world music, and knows how to handle tough questions and scenarios. Very respectful

Dr. Reed was an amazing professor! I took this class summer semester, and she was very understanding of each student's needs. We were allowed to turn in all assignments late with no penalty. There are no exams, just a research project that you work on throughout the semester which is very easy. I highly recommend!!!

Dr. Reid is so nice! She made this GE easy but interesting, and I gained more awareness of music. Lectures aren't worth a ton of points, but I liked her comments and stories. We would often discuss a musical example and the reading assignment. Sometimes I missed the reading assignment beforehand, and I was still fine participating in class.

If you're looking for an easy--but still fun and engaging--class for the arts GE, this is a great option. Lecture attendance was definitely not necessary, and there were no tests, but I went to the lectures because they were interesting. She did "show and tell" at the start of class and we watched musical artists and discussed them, which was fun.

Dr. Reed is delightful, and this class was so easy, but also very interesting. Most of the assignments are pretty easy, and the only bigger assignment is a research project, which is very personalized, and is split up into sections, so it's pretty easy. Definitely would recommend this class with Dr. Reed!

Dr. Reed is great and is really understanding of the different circumstances of students. She cares about the students and understands that her class isn't the only class her students are taking. Every assignment is pretty much completion. Easy A, but also a high-quality professor. Would recommend taking this class.
This class was so so easy. I didn't show up for half the semester and I still got a 107% in the class.

The kindest professor ever. She will work with you on anything you need, and her class is very easy. There's a bit of work, but it teaches you a lot, and you're able to explore things on your own. Go to her class! You'll learn something, and she's super funny and just wonderful to be around. I loved going even when only 3 people were there.

I absolutely love her. She cares a ton about students and was great about working with people if you needed help with something. The project for the class was easy and let me explore what I wanted to. It does a really good job of showing you more perspectives and just bringing a nice view of worldwide music and cultures.

Dr. Reed was a great professor! I learned a lot about ethnomusicology in her class, and doing a project based on what I was interested in allowed me to apply what we were learning to something that I wanted to learn more about. We listened to a lot of music from a lot of different cultures, and it really felt like it broadened my perspective.

Heidi is amazing and gives great disccusions! There is lots of reading different articles and papers, you mark your reading if you did it or not based on integrity. If you are looking for a filler class this is a great one!! You get to know everyone in your class on a fun, deeper level than a typical college class.
Such a sweet lady, she is so kind and understanding. This class is so easy and you don't even have to show up. No exams, just weekly readings and lifestyle activity and it's all self graded.

She is a relaxed, open person. You can tell that she genuinely cares for her students and wants them to succeed and get something useful from her class. It is very low stress. The class is very discussion based. You discuss things in groups and then with the whole class. This is the first class I have felt comfortable discussing things openly in.
Heidi is an awesome person! I had a unique situation and she was incredibly accommodating to me. Loved her class. I'd recommend it to anyone, but especially women planning to enter the workforce
Dr. Vogeler is really cool. She's super nice and the class is very discussion based. We had a lot of guest speakers which made the class very interesting.
This is a useful class (Career Strategies) for if you're lost about how to make a resume, cover letter, and how to network in order to find a job. Very easy A, and Heidi is wonderful.

Heidi is amazing and gives great disccusions! There is lots of reading different articles and papers, you mark your reading if you did it or not based on integrity. If you are looking for a filler class this is a great one!! You get to know everyone in your class on a fun, deeper level than a typical college class.
Such a sweet lady, she is so kind and understanding. This class is so easy and you don't even have to show up. No exams, just weekly readings and lifestyle activity and it's all self graded.

She is a relaxed, open person. You can tell that she genuinely cares for her students and wants them to succeed and get something useful from her class. It is very low stress. The class is very discussion based. You discuss things in groups and then with the whole class. This is the first class I have felt comfortable discussing things openly in.
Heidi is an awesome person! I had a unique situation and she was incredibly accommodating to me. Loved her class. I'd recommend it to anyone, but especially women planning to enter the workforce
Dr. Vogeler is really cool. She's super nice and the class is very discussion based. We had a lot of guest speakers which made the class very interesting.
This is a useful class (Career Strategies) for if you're lost about how to make a resume, cover letter, and how to network in order to find a job. Very easy A, and Heidi is wonderful.

The curriculum is well designed! He or the TA always gave clear feedback on the homework, and he was very responsive outside of class. There are a lot of readings and biweekly 50 question quizzes (keep up) but they are very concept-based and really help you learn and internalize the material. He genuinely cares about you and wants you to learn!

He never really taught anything. Most of the semester, you're kinda on your own. There is an absurd amount of work, multiple long quizzes a week, labs, etc., and none of it is clearly explained. The Stata software is frustrating and difficult, and again, very poorly taught, so you're on your own. Don't take this teacher if you can avoid it.

She really wants her students to succeed in her class. She even removed a midterm because she felt like the workload was too big for the class at that time. The labs were challenging and sometimes graded harshly. There is a language barrier so lectures can be somewhat confusing at times, but she works really hard to make sure we understand.

I loved Dr. Ran, and felt that she was incredibly kind towards of all of her students and really wanted to get to know all of them. This class naturally has a lot of homework to it that takes a long time, but if you put in the work, you'll be able to get through it. Exams/Final are 70% of the class, so study hard for them to do well.
Great teacher, cares a lot about her students. I would recommend taking any class from her. English is her second language but lectures were still very helpful.

I took Mr. Howard for IDFM 431, and it was difficult for no reason. There were only discussion boards, exams, and one paper. The tests were hard, and determined your grade in the course due to them being 100 pts each. No powerpoints/lecture material..he expects you to read and memorize the textbook. However, he did reply to emails quickly!
Seth is an awesome professor. He always presents material in a clear and useful manner.

His lectures are a little slow, but clear and he uses a ton of examples to contextualize the material. It can be challenging sometimes to answer the conceptual homework questions, but I think that application is one of the points of the class and the TAs are always willing to help clarify. The research reviews are also pretty tedious.

Amazing professor who is passionate about biomechanics. I would not recommend the course to students who do not enjoy physics and sports. The exams are not easy but you can do well if you do all the practice problems. He is an amazing professor who really cares about the class.
Amazing guy. Would take any class from him.

Professor Hunter was a great professor, he works to get to know his students personally. He only holds class once a week (except for exams weeks then its 2 times a week for reviews) and there isn't a ton of outside work so his class is fairly easy! I loved the class discussion and would highly recommend him for biomechanics!

Dr. Hunter was a very nice guy and tried to make his class the easiest it could be. You don't have to go to class to get a good grade. Just follow the online calendar and you'll be good. For exams, he would do a review and tell us what to study, but my group and I would do that and still not do well, like he would tell us the wrong things to study.

Class attendance is pretty optional as the class is a blended class with most of the material learned from doing the readings. If you do attend class, he talks through the quiz problems for that week, which can be helpful. Very easy class.

Dr Hunter is one of the most caring professors. He really wants everyone to succeed and you can tell that he loves what he teaches about. The content is interesting, although I sometimes got a little lost in class. Physics isn't my strong suit, so some of the concepts were difficult for me. But he is literally always available if you need help.

Go to the classes that review the midterm and final. The rest is pointless. He loves to take class time to tickle himself pink talking about track and cross country. I just want to know how to do well on the test. So class is a joke. But by far the best option for this course because its so darn easy anyway.

Dr. Hunter is pretty cool. I found the course content really interesting and loved applying it. I didn't take any pre-reqs for this class and did just fine. However, if math isn't your strong point you could have some frustration.

Dr. Hunter is definitely a good choice for this class. His class is fairly interesting if you like track and cross country or just sports in general. I took it more as an elective credit and it was pretty easy. Just do the weekly assignments and you're golden. If you've taken physics 121 or 105 you already know most of the material.

Dr. Hunter is the bomb. Hopefully you like sports, especially running, but if you don't I don't see how taking it from another professor would be any better. He is super clear and helpful, and his spiritual thoughts are always great.

Pretty easy, especially if you took physics 105 already. I felt like this class was basically a re-do of 105, just an easier version with a few different concepts here and there, and I didn't find it beneficial nor did I learn much. But its required so ah well. Dr. Hunter was a great professor, and the blended online class was really flexible

Professor Hunter gave good class time and clearly knew his stuff. He's involved with research at BYU and often shared what he was working on and showed that this material really did apply to life. We used the Canvas interface for classwork, not Learning Suite. The FREE online textbook that was very helpful. He's a fair grader but you should study.

Dr. Hunter is the man. Knows his stuff about all the material, is super passionate about it because he has worked with the BYU Track team and many Olympic athletes from there as well. He knows what he's talking about. He is super helpful and always willing to answer questions and clarify.

Take Physics 105 and this will be a breeze for the most part. I took the hybrid class which I would recommend. Dr. Hunter makes sure you are prepared for the exams and is really helpful on getting help inside and outside of class. Tests are worth quite a bit.

Dr. Hunter is the best EXSC professor. The class is very straightforward. He is very helpful and willing to hold open lab hours and answer emails. He genuinely wants his students to succeed. Class is entertaining, because he shows sports clips every day. There is online homework, but it is brief. Tests can be tricky, so be sure to ask questions.

Very easy A if you stay on top of things. All his lectures are recorded online, so you don't even have to go to class. However, there is an in-class quiz after every chapter. He provides the book for free Theres 1 project, but its easy Homework is easy if you read the chapter. only 2 tests that are easy too. if you already took physics 105, ur good

Hands down best teacher for the class. Assignments are clear and fairly simple. Holds reviews before the midterm and final (not comprehensive) and tells you exactly what you need to study. That being said, study hard-tests are straightforward but hard. Would definitely take again if he was teaching another class. Great professor and really helpful.
Amazing professor, very clear with teaching and prepares you well for exams.  I can't say enough positive things about the course and professor!

Dr. Hunter gives very entertaining lectures. Quizzes are online and can be taken throughout the whole semester. Dr. Hunter does not prepare you for the tests very well though. But if you take very good notes and go to the review before the test you should be able to get an A on the test.

Dr. Hunter is a great teacher. He is very helpful and caring. Assignments are important in this class for they are worth as much as a midterm in points. Tests consist of more difficult material than assignments but if you study you should be fine. Dr. Hunter is the best teacher for this class.

You want this class from Hunter. Hands down. He's very clear about what he wants from you and does his best to make his assignments simple and do-able. Super helpful too so if you don't get something he'll work with you until you do. Amazing professor. Explains difficult concepts very well too. I'm slow and if I got them, you'll be fine.
Great professor. Goes out of his way to help you out. Doesn't over-complicate concepts. Great class.

Awesome teacher, he is really helpful and goes over everything you need to know until you understand it. Class is not hard at all, quizzes are easy, as well as most of the assignments. One mid-term and the final, and a term project that he goes over in depth. Great class!

Great teacher. Goes over material to study. If you don't grasp physics and the equations I wouldn't say it's an easy A, but probably an easy B for most students. 2 tests, 8 short in class iclicker quizzes, 8 HW assignments, 8 other practice assignments on blackboard and a term project. Great class with a wonderful teacher.

Take from Hunter. Easy easy A. He gives you all the answers to the quizzes and assignments before you submit them on blackboard and he goes over the test question by question the day before it opens and tells you just what you need to study. Only tests on basic principles and vocab.

Overall a good class. He is much easier than Seeley. There is one midterm- multiple choice with a handful of math problems. There are some quizzes/homework assignments, but he gives you the answers if you ask, so don't worry. The final is not comprehensive which is always nice. There is also a term project which isn't hard. Plus he's a great guy!

I've never had a teacher care so much about his students. He will help you with anything, even quizzes. The class isn't hard as long as you go to class and do all your assignments. TAKE FROM Dr, Hunter!
He is a really great professor. He wants his students to do well. He will help you with all of the quizzes, homework, and semester project before you turn them in.
Awesome guy and a great teacher, you can tell he loves what he teaches.

Dr. Hunter is one of the nicest professor I have ever had. He is so willing to help with anything. You can pretty much get 100% on all quizzes and assignments because he'll check them before you turn it in. This class is a lot simpler than 105 if you've taken that. I would highly recommend Dr. Hunter. He's so good.

Dr. Hunter is an awesome guy!! Probably will be one of my all time favourite teachers! His class is a cake walk if you did descent in physics 105 but i still learned a lot.You definitely don't have to kiss up to him. He genuinely wants everyone to do well and is willing to do anything to help you. I would recommend him for sure!

I took Physics 105 concurrently and it was an easy A. Not too much work, pretty straight forward. I went to class and always learned what he expected of us for the midterm and non-comprehensive final. Not the most interesting but very knowledgeable and a great guy.  I never kissed up and most people get B+ or better (even when not really trying.)

Hunter can be a confusing teacher sometimes.  So make sure you go to class, copy all the work he does on the board, and study the quizzes.  The work load isn't too bad.  Just 8 weekly quizzes and 4 assignments, all on black board.

Dr. Hunter takes a relatively difficult subject and breaks it down so it is easily understandable.  He is so willing to help and very approachable.  His tests come off pretty hard, but he takes a lot from the quizzes and the sample problems.  He is extremely lenient and is an all around nice guy. Take this class from him!
Dr. Hunter is the most genuine teacher I have had at BYU. I have no physics or calculus background but he helped me through the course like a stud. AWESOME TEACHER...not the easiest course tho...
He was very helpful and always considerate of students.
if you haven't had physics already then prepare to stuggle!  teacher is very helpful, however lectures are quite boring.  tests are very hard if you're not a math expert (lots of word problems too).
good professor for this class.  very straight foward.  good lectures. no busywork.
very helpful outside of class.
Pretty decent class.  Everything is straight forward.  All tests and quizzes are multiple choice.  If you can do all of the quiz problems then you shouldnt have any trouble with the tests.

Dr. Hunter set aside many hours to help me becuase I had class during his office hours.  He's a really nice guy who really tries his best to help you understand. The test are very reasonable... I would study the notes and the sample problems he gives in class.

Pretty simple class, esp if you have had any physics background. Quizes and homework are open book so you should do well, and tests are fairly simple. It's easy to get an A, because above a 92 you get an A and the final is not comprehensive!! Very personable as well!

Professor Wright is one of the best professors at BYU. He knows his stuff very well, is humble, and encourages learning, not just grades. His lectures are engaging, and he always makes sure to apply to the real world. 40% of your grade is participation in this class, so make sure to speak up!

Participation based class. Needed to participate almost every class to receive an A. Bit intimidating at first, but I learned so much about the markets in this class. You need to make a 3 slide presentation for every class and a random number generator picks who presents. But it helps teach yourself everything on the topic. Get out what you put in.

Investments Academy with Ian Wright and Bronson Argyle was AMAZING! Only take this class if you are willing to participate in every class. I was intimidated initially, but the instructors created a learning environment where I felt comfortable sharing my thoughts. I learned so much about the market and different investment options. 10/10 recommend!

Ian is extremely insightful, organized, and considerate. He gives fantastic lectures and excels at explaining difficult concepts in a clear manner. He cares deeply about the learning and achievement of his students and designs the course in a way that isn't about memorizing facts and formulas but rather about enhancing understanding.

Best professor i've ever had at BYU. I took his Eternal Families class during the spring term, and he is easily the best professor I've had. I think he is no longer going to be teaching in the religion department because of the class, we did not have tests, only three projects, and readings. Best class ever, felt the spirit. "I love you, go away"

Lectures were amazing. The point of the class was learning and personal growth. Freedom to make the assignments what you need them to be. Classes were a respite from the stress and overload of college life. Truly cares about his students and their well-being.

BEST teacher. 0 assignments aside from a monthly project you get to make as detailed or simply as you wanted that you present to a few peers. You grade yourself on attendance and effort. His lectures were truly interesting, coming from someone who despises religion courses because they're usually boring. You can tell he loves what he does.

No complaints at all about this class, this is how every BYU religion class should be. He is super respectful of other religions and helps us gain the appreciation he has for them. I learned so much about the Gospel in a class about other religions. I came out of that class with a new perspective and appreciation for other cultures.

I loved this class! It changed my life. Isaac is an amazing and gifted teacher. I was challenged by examining how I think and live. Not a lot of pressure on the assignments, but my choice to put time and thought into them changed how I saw myself and the world. Lectures are enjoyable and rejuvenating. I would take every class of his possible.

This was the lowest effort class I have taken. The course page was empty with no assignments and a very bare-bones syllabus. The professor frequently discouraged students from putting little effort into the class, while he himself put almost no effort into it. This felt like a Sunday school class from a teacher who doesn't care.

Professor Calvert consistently made us feel guilty if we did not put in our best effort on our assignments, which felt hypocritical as it felt like he was putting in minimal effort. All of the assignments we did were graded based on self reported completion. The professor never looked at any of our assignments and we never received any feedback.

He is the type of guy you feel like knows literally everything. He is genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. The way he structures the class is purely for learning. I leaned so much about other religions and how to be a life-long learner. I walked away from class always feeling inspired. 10/10 would take this class again!!!

What. A. Class. Dr. Calvert is a fascinating, entertaining dude with a remarkable background. He brings in all sorts of religious leaders and members and just lets you learn to love and see other faiths. You don't HAVE to really do much to get an A, but because of that, I could just focus on learning because I wanted to. 100/10.

I cannot give Professor Calvert enough praise. Amazing person, amazing professor, just an overall great guy. World Religions was so enjoyable from him because he's not focused on grading, he truly just wants you to learn. Your whole class grade is based upon effort. If you're thinking about taking world religions, TAKE IT FROM HIM!!!
Best professor I have had in a while. This class was interactive and he was respectful of all religions and opinions. Definitely take it from him!
He is the best religion professor Ive ever had. No tests just learning. We learned to be inspired and better ourselves instead of for a grade.
Isaac has a huge focus on encouraging students to value learning outside of their grades. His lectures are inspirational and so insightful. He is a great guy and a really good professor!

Dr. Calvert is both inspiring and wickedly intelligent. His teaching philosophy is rooted in agentive theory—the idea that students retain what they actively work for. Every class left me deeply reflecting on life and its purpose. The courses I took from Isaac were truly transformative and favorites at BYU.

To Dr. Calvert: thank you, thank you.

Really cool deep-dive into the history of education. Lots of reading done in this class, though none of it is technically mandatory. Big learning project where you choose to learn how to do something and then present it to the class with applied principles. You also read 3-4 books of your choice (kind of) once a month. Easy A if you actually read.

He is an amazing professor and genuinely cares for every single student. He is passionate about education and gives readings and facilitates group discussion that help students understand the purpose behind education. I would take this class again!

Best class ever. I loved the open ended structure of the class. There is a few book projects but there are very few other assignments. He really changes your mind and changes your perspective on learning. This is by far my favorite class. It is a flexible learning environment so be ready to learn as you go. 10/10 recommend Dr. Calvert.

This is my favorite class at BYU! The lectures in this class are so amazingly good and thought provoking. This class was life-changing because Isaac isn't trying to teach to you he's learning and engaging in learning with you! He is a professor who is the closest to really understanding education and learning. He is the best professor I've had.

He is very caring and understanding of students, their needs and how people learn. We read a lot, wrote in our journals, had group discussions and more. But none of it felt like homework, it was all something that I wanted to do, that I enjoyed doing, and helped me be a better person. If you get a chance to take a class from him, do it.

One of the most amazing professors I've ever taken. Super kind and insanely smart. One page paper every few weeks, a fairly easy midterm if you try, final was your philosophy on education. Super easy to get an A. Attendance wasn't taken but you will actually want to show up because of how inspired you will get after every class. 12/10 recommend!

This is by far the best class I have taken in my time at BYU. Isaac changed my views of education and this class changed the course I want to take in my education and career. Isaac is one of the smartest people I have met and he truly cares about his students and helping them succeed. If you want to grow from the class, it can change your life.

Isaac is an incredible professor! He is very knowledgeable and passionate about the topics, which makes his lectures fantastic. He truly cares about his students and their learning. Take a class from him, you wont regret it!

If I could take this class again I would! I learned so much in this class things that I am going to be using forever! He has so much background, knowlege, and passion for what he is doing. I was blown away by this class! 12/10 would recomend!

I love JB Haws! He's incredibly knowledgeable about his subject and is always open to discourse from students. He gives lots of opportunities for extra credit, and he drops the two lowest quiz scores. He has a strange proctor policy for the midterm and final, but it's doable. Great guy!

(I had him for UNIV 101) I love JB! Definitely my favorite professor so far. He gets to know all his students and remembers them and shows he cares about our learning and our lives, and makes class so fun and interactive. Most people don't like univ but I loved it and would say a huge part of it was because of the professor.

JB Haws is genuinely one of the coolest guys I've ever met. His classes are so fun and he is so engaging. You have to get one book for the class but it's cheap on Amazon. He is so smart and so passionate about the gospel and history. Take his class! So worth it.

Actually probably the best religion prof at BYU. So welcoming of new ideas, handles sensitive topics really well, will remember your name for forever. He is so intelligent and hilarious. I wish I could take every single class from him. He helps you out so much and just wants you to have a good time learning about cool topics. He's simply the best
My favorite class I have taken from BYU. Professor Haws is the best!

This Professor was really nice and I learned a lot in his class but there was a lot of content. Tests were all very specific and includes things we talked about one time. Midterms were very picky on information, and included questions on pictures in the slides from weeks ago. I took this as a freshman and wouldn't recommend to other freshman.
He's super good at answering questions and hitting key ideas. So caring, fun, and accommodating to ensure student success. I would absolutely take another class of his.

Just registered for another one of his classes just because he teaches it. He's sensitive to prominent issues, really funny, and wicked smart. He's your biggest hypeman and just wants everything good in life to happen to you. Being around JB is like drinking an energy drink in terms of how alive and excited you feel. Can't say enough good ab him.
Great professor. Best religion class I have taken!

I could not have loved Bro Haws as a professor more. I took him almost two years ago and he still remembers me by name and stops to talk to me every time he passes me on campus. This also is my all-time fav religion class I've taken at BYU, it's seriously sooo good. Everyone has to take it from Brother Haws if they can!
Made a great effort to remember everyone's name and show that he cares about you. Amazing professor, better person!

Professor Haws probably changed my outlook on religion classes at BYU. Being a non member here and having experienced the atmosphere and bubble it can be a bit discouraging and isolating but Haws just lifts every room he is in. He is so caring and loving to his students and is very sensitive when it comes to difficult topics. He is incredible 10/10

I would take any class taught by Professor Haws just because it is taught by Professor Haws. If you liked his BYU devo, the class is basically just more of the same. He discussed tough topics in super sensitive ways, and answered some of my questions/concerns in his office after class in a way that made me feel so seen and loved.

I took RelC353 & RelC343 from him. He is absolutely fantastic. You want to take a religion class from him. Very nice, very excited about the topic, he cares a lot about his students, and it isn't hard to get an A. As an added bonus, 343 and 353 overlap a lot, so if you take one, the other becomes a lot easier.

Brother Haws is seriously such a good teacher. I would 10/10 recommend him to anyone and everyone. The questions for his tests and quizzes are pulled equally from readings and in-class discussions, so definitely do both. His tests are also equal parts multiple choice and free response, and he is super generous in giving points to the free response.

Professor Haws was a good professor. The class was organized well and the requirements were clear. There is a steady amount of reading and a few projects/essays that can feel a little bit heavy. But his class and lectures are really interesting, and I learned a lot.
Reading heavyyyyy. Attendance is taking which is kind of lame. I think that brought down my grade. Great teacher though and really knowledgable. Fun class.
Great guy. There was a lot of really boring reading but the lectures were awesome. The tests were literally just asking random facts that have been mentioned so memorize everything.
Amazing! I was nervous to take a church history class, but Pro. Haws was incredibly intelligent and compassionate about all subjects. This class was transformational for me. Take this class.

Made an account just to praise Brother Haws! This was my last religion class of my college career and it was the best one I have taken. I never pay attention to almost any lectures, but I was tuned in every day in this class. Take him! A few short papers, online testing (less intimidating than TC), and weekly online quizzes. Can't recommend enough.
Hands down one of the best. He is passionate about what he is teaching which makes the material SO much more enjoyable. If he could teach all my religion classes I would be ecstatic.

Professor Haws is clearly a guy who knows his stuff. I enjoyed how communal the class felt and the spirit of participation he created for all of us. Some of the material can take a while to memorize, but on the whole it's not an especially difficult class.

Dr. Haws is super funny and entertaining. I really looked forward to his class every day. My only warning is that his tests require memorizing a list of obscure dates and names. Otherwise, he's a cool guy that sincerely cares about his students and wants you to succeed.

Amazing lectures! He really leads some great and revelatory discussions. He really cares about his students and you can feel it. Class is very heavy on memorizing small tidbits of information, so beware. Overall he is a fair grader and not hard to do well in his class.

I loved his class! I will say that you need to know a lot from the readings and lectures to do well on quizzes and exams. He's funny and really cares about his students. He will personally take out the time to know your name and a bit about you. It was a fun class!
He is an amazing professor that really helped me to appreciate the need for history classes. Super funny and a great teacher. 20/10 would recommend

By far my favorite class and professor of the semester! Brother Haws cares deeply about each person and makes everyone feel important. He brings the spirit so strongly, and at the same time tackles difficult questions of modern church history. Also mention the town of Hooper, UT and you will get an A (his hometown). 20/10 TAKE HIS CLASS

I had only been to his class a few times over zoom and he somehow remembered my name when we randomly met on campus! He cares deeply about his students and the subject. Eye-opening and testimony strengthening. He isn't afraid of tough questions and has an amazing perspective on the gospel. Take him and you won't regret it!

Brother Haws is one of the most respectful, loving and kind people I have ever met! There's quite a bit of reading, but for the most part it is very interesting! Class lectures are really just guided discussions, and Brother Haws creates an atmosphere conducive to feeling the spirit. Tests are based heavily on class discussions. You'll love him!

Bro Haws is one of the best professors I've ever had at BYU! His lectures are very interesting, even when you're discussing something boring. As of Winter 2020, his tests were on LearningSuite, so that was nice. I did not do the readings and did just fine, but if you do not have a prior understanding of the topic, do them. Class is discussion based

Honestly probably one of the nicest professors ever. Genuinely cares about his students and will make accommodations to help them succeed. Memorized every student's name. Class was very interesting, and really straightforward what will be on the test. Readings sometimes were long, but always worth it.

Brother Haws is the best professor I've ever had. His class requires diligent reading and keeping on top of assignments, but I found I was actually excited to go to his lectures. I learned the most in this class, and recommend it for anyone who wants a broader view of religion in America.

Best BYU religion professor, Maybe best overall professor. This class covers some of the heaviest things about the Church's past, and he handles perfectly. My testimony was strengthened every class. Honestly every BYU student should be required to take this from him. Lots of reading, but it's good reading. He knows everything about church history.

I loved Professor Haws. He was absolutely amazing. I loved his lectures. He was so nice and remembered everyone's name which was SO impressions since I was in a large class. He is very personable and is so reasonable to work with. This class was really easy too. Just show up to class and you will be good to go.

This was an amazing class! There was a lot of reading but I thought that was to be expected as it basically is a history class and the only way to really learn history is to read. So if you pace yourself on the reading you will be fine! And the lectures and the spirit felt in the class make the reading worth it! I would definitely recommend!

I thought Dr. Haws was a cool person, but there is SO much reading and the tests require memorizing like 50 dates. This is way more work than other religion classes I've taken. Don't take from him if you have an already full schedule.
This class was by far the best religion class I've taken at BYU, and one of the best overall classes I've taken. It was very interesting and I highly recommend it.

I never choose religion professors that assign papers, but this was not a problem. Papers were more like visit a museum, interview someone about church history, etc. Lectures are important because that's where test material comes from. But he often says "make sure you have this in your notes" and explicitly states what we need to know. Great class!

Best religion class I've ever had! I Looked forward to every class! Professor Haws is totally reasonable in his expectations and cares about all students. There is a bit of reading but it's interesting and didn't even feel like homework. The 4 papers were probably the hardest part of the class but they were still manageable, just time consuming.

I absolutely loved brother Haws and his American Christianity class. If you have difficulty with religion classes like I do this is a great one to take! He really knows his stuff and does a great job integrating the gospel into each class. Learned a ton!! Just all around genuine and awesome guy.

Awesome teacher. Really cares about his students. Gives a lot of extra credit. But takes way too much time. Hours of reading every week with daily quizzes that are too specific. There is a ton to memorize for the tests. Our final study guide was 25 pages of "things to know" aka things to memorize including dates people and places.

I love professor Haws! He is so understanding and flexible about certain assignments. If you are going out of town or need help he will help out big time. He teaches such a fact heavy class in such a digestible way. Would take his class again in a second!

Brother Haws takes the most interesting approach to a religion class. I took him for an American Christianity course, and loved his unique way of talking about the Gospel alongside other Christian denominations. His funky sense of humor, interesting discussion questions, and knowledge about the subject make me want to take this course again.

I have taken many religion classes but Haws has got to be my FAVORITE religion teacher. I learned so much and felt the spirit and tests are straight forward and he offers extra credit so I ended up getting over 100% in the class. PAY ATTENTION in class and study off of the study guides and quizzes and you will be fine! There is a lot of reading.

Brother Haws tells you what he expects, so if you just keep up on the reading you wont have any problem at all! He gives a study guide for each exam. The quizzes tripped me up sometimes because the questions can be pretty specific, but he also offers A LOT of extra credit. Take his class!

Like previous comments have said, Bro. Haws is a nice guy. He cares about you as a person. The class was not a church religion class, it was a history class. Jackie is one of the worst math teachers I've ever had. She doesn't interact with the class--she just does problems on the board. Math is not my forte, and her teaching style didn't help AT ALL. Jackie is a really nice teacher, but she does not know how to teach  very well. She makes mistakes constantly during lectures and does not answer questions very well. If you haven't had Calc before, good luck. Otherwise you should be fine.

Jackie is ok. Her classes consist of her doing problems on the board the entire time, and then it's over. I felt like she never really "teaches" the material, she just shows you problems and how to do it, although she does answer everyone's questions. The test correction feature of her class is helpful, but you HAVE TO SHOW YOUR WORK on the test.

Take from Wadley (or anyone else that is available). The test correction factor is appealing but if she gets busy at all then you won't get any help there. Decent teacher. Seems to care about student learning. I wouldn't recommend the evening class because she is usually tired and frequently lets class out early. Test corrections are the same as a class being curved, so don't use that as a reason to take from her.

She is horrible at teaching but the nicest lady you'll ever meet!Take it from her! Shes the only teacher who gives test corrections...just go to Wadley's lectures and you'll be fine. Add her class, but go to someone elses

The professor herself is TERRIBLE. She's ornery, stuck-up, bitter, and has grade C teaching skills.  The only reason it's worth taking her section is for test corrections for half-credit back. Attendance to labs is semi-mandatory, but lectures are not. If you're pretty good at calc, you're ok. If you are looking for a teacher to help you, stay away

Jackie is the nicest teacher in the world. She cares 100% about her students success... and gives out extra credit and test corrections when she doesnt have too!  You ROCK Jackie! Math was not easy for me, but now I got to graduate from UVU.  Keep up the AWESOME work!

Jackie is wonderful! Fun class! It's hard, but I am a math freak, so I enjoyed it. Jackie is very helpful and tries build good relationship with every student! She knows most of t   he names in class. She lets do test corrections to increase the grade for the test, she is understanding and very loyal. GREAT PROFESSOR!

I really learned a lot. It is true that she makes mistakes when she explains but she corrects it and it is not a big deal. Everyone makes mistakes. She helps a lot after tests to get points back. You have to do homework and if you dont mind to do it during the weekends, it is ok. She is funny and finishes class early. I recommecd her.

She is the worst teacher I have ever had. She knows math but makes mistakes in lecture constantly. She is the head of the math lab which is scary considering the mistakes she makes and then argues with students when she needs to make the corrections. She strictly observes the honor code in her class. Guys if you have scruff you will be kicked out o

Jackie is a really nice lady, but its hard to get anything out of her lectures. She doesn't explain what she is doing and often makes mistakes. She is a great teacher, if you put in the effort and attend her lectures you are able to get an A. But it requires studying. She is great, it is the Math department in general that is ridiculous.
She is very helpful and she always try to help students to do well in the tests.

Its not Jackie that makes the class hard, its the department. It wouldnt even be that bad of a class except the tests are pretty brutal. Thankfully Jackie is always willing to help and explain things; she's an awsome teacher, a little motherly, but that only makes her better.

Jackie tries hard to take care of all her students, if you respect her, she will respect and help you. She's fun approachable, she gets a bad rap becuase students either don't like math, or haven't taken a tougher class and BYU and think it's just her. Not many teachers will do for students what she does.

Its not Jackies Fault its the departments.  You don't have to go to class which is nice, but  plan on being in the math lab for forever.  She gives great curves at the end of the year, so if you think that your failing you probably have a B. Hardest Class ive taken but no matter who you take it from the tests are all the same.

Jackie is the coolest teacher that I had, the class is very hard and you should plan on spending lots of time Math lab for extra help, i was in night class and she let us out early most of the time, great lady hard class

Jackie is a great person, and an okay teacher. The class goes fast, but that's just the way it has to be, since there's so much material to cover. She gives you points back on your tests if you rework them, and as long as you do the homework and study, you'll be fine. She's really nice and makes jokes in class, which makes it fun.

I don't understand why Jackie is teaching at a university. I stopped going to class half way and have done better without her confusing explanations. The TA's are awesome, but she herself is quite a poor teacher. I learned from the textbook and classmates. Business majors have to take MATH 119, but don't take Jackie! Avoid her at all costs!

This woman is ridiculous. I spent the first weeks caring what she said in class, but after realizing that the students knew more than she did, stopped going to class. Work is redundant. She makes you do homework online, and on paper, quizzes online, and in the testing center.

I really liked her teaching.  How could people not follow?  If anything, I felt she was a little too basic sometimes in her explanations.  Anyway, I can't imagine not doing well if you do the homework.  And you get points back on the tests if you go back for help after a poor score.  I highly recommend taking her for Calculus.

Jackie was great.  A lot of students complained during class about her teaching style but it always seemed to be the younger students who wanted someone to hold their hand.  The course was set up well and Jackie is over-accomodating, which is great.  She does seem overly concerned with people talking in class though.

Jackie did not teach at all, did not explain concepts to students clarity, i had to learn with a group of friends, the only thing we liked about jackie was that we could retake the midterms in the math lab with help so we could credit and boost our grades.
Jackie is fabulous! She's really funny and let us out early half the time. If you pay attention and do your work then the class is easy. She gives lots of opportunities to get points back, too.

Jackie does a really poor job of explaining the concepts, but this course is set up so you can teach yourself.  The online homework takes you through each step of a problem which is wonderful.  Also, the study guides are right on, so in the end, I quit going to class but pulled an A anyways.

Jackie does a poor job of teaching and explaining concepts BUT the course set-up is really nice! All the questions in the test are from the book; if you get A in all the mid-terms you don't need to take the final. So if you are a self-learner and/or good at maths take this class from her.

She was really nice and really interested in helping her students out. I flunked two of her exams and still got a really good grade. She was always willing to discuss problems and in class she made sure you understood the problems. i liked her alot.
works very well with the students.  makes class pretty fun and interesting.  is concerned for students and wants them to do well...works with them so they can do the best possible.

Her teaching style didnt match my way of learning.  I would have to teach myself everything to do for my homework and labs.  I stopped going to class all together half way through because the lectures didnt help me.  Its not a hard class but be prepared to spend a lot of time on this class.  She is very generous with giving test points back.

Jackie is probably the best teacher for 119. She allows you to rework test problems to get points back. I doubt I would have gotten such a high grade with a less understanding and helpful teacher. She can get a little distracted with problems on the board but she's helpful. If you aren't a Wiz in Calculus yet then she will help you learn it best.
She makes you feel stupid when you ask a question
she was ok, but the LAB was there to help... her tests also made the class easy.
