I loved his class. If you're a minority you'll feel welcomed. There was a lot of reading and it was hard to remember it all, but this is a class that can change your life for good. Highly recommend!

You won't meet another teacher that cares about his class more than Dr. Rugh, this guy is a real gem. While I loved Dr. Rugh, I have to admit that his class was pretty hard for a GE. LOTS of reading. Lots of Iclicker questions. Tests aren't easy. The key to the class is going to TA hours and TA reviews.

I loved this course and recommend everyone to take it. This class is definitely reading heavy but it has changed my perspective on many social issues. Professor Rugh is a great professor and super funny. Tests are not overly difficult and if you study TA review you will be fine. If your are hesitant on taking the class just do it!

Dr. Rugh is one of the best professors I've ever had! My world is shifted because of this class! So worth it!! Take it from him if you want it to change your life! There's a lot of reading, but it's all really good and worth the time. I honestly always looked forward to it.

Dr. Rugh is the best professor I've ever had. There is a lot of reading for this class, but it's easy to find what you need to understand for the quizzes, and all the readings are interesting and enlightening. He is very understanding, empathetic, and incredibly intelligent. Everyone should take this class, and I would highly recommend Dr. Rugh!

I can't recommend this class enough! Prof Rugh is so insightful and thoughtful in his lectures and assignments. You can tell he really cares so much and the TAs are amazing as well. The homework is not too much or too hard and the writing assignments are more of reflections about what you've talked about in class and your perspective of them.

Seriously amazing class. I did not want to take this class but need it for medical schools, and I would take it again. Professor Rugh is an amazing and understanding professor. Class has a lot of reading with in class iclicker quizzes, but they're pretty easy and the midterms are straight forward.

This class is AMAZING and Prof Rugh is incredible. His lectures are so interesting and informative, and he does a great job of making them relatable. The coursework is a bit tricky, but it's so interesting. There is quite a bit of reading, but again, it's all really fascinating stuff. Take this class from him! You won't regret it.

Dr. Rugh will change your life. He does an amazing job of presenting the material passionately but professionally. He is very accessible and it's clear how much he cares about and respects us. I looked forward to class each day, and I loved how he encouraged us to learn from each other, not just lectures. I wish I could take more classes from him!

I was VERY hesitant to take a class on race and ethnicity from a white male, but Rugh is WOKE. I loved his class and I love him -- relatable, funny, well-read, opinionated, intelligent. The class was rigorous but highly spiritual. He's everything a BYU professor should be. Would take again a hundred times, and I recommend it to everyone.

Dr. Rugh is great! He's a fun guy who is passionate about what he does in both sociology research and teaching! He's super legit and has been published in a lot of academic journals, but he's really humble about his achievements and just wants to help students to learn! He's willing to work with you and help you succeed, and is great to talk to!

AMAZING class and teacher. He really cares about the students, and the subject, and knows so much about it. Everyone should take this class. If you do the reading and work you will get an A, and it's super interesting. Tests are clear and fair. Lectures are never boring, great teaching style even in a big class.

Outstanding Professor. This man's SOC 111 class changed my life and made me a new, better person. Students actively participate in class, and Dr. Rugh gives them his attention and respect. This class involves TONS of reading, which was hard, but interesting. Tests include some things that were discussed only in class. Always plan to attend.

Dr. Rugh is super kind and passionate! It's easy to sit in his class and enjoy a healthy discussion. He is kind with everyone's questions. Being a student of color, I felt like this class was mainly for white students and how to help them understand concepts outside of themselves. Lots of reading. Tests are way hard even if you do the reading

Dr. Rugh is the smartest man I know. He knows so much about sociology and I learned a ton every time I went to class. He is a great teacher overall. I have nothing but respect for the man. There are an absurd amount of required readings for the class though, with iClicker attendance and performance questions every class. Lots of reading and writing

Dr. Rugh is HILARIOUS. Sometimes I would look around and be so confused why everyone wasn't laughing as hard as I was. Seriously awesome class. Became a better human being because of it. Hires incompetent TA's but other than that- easily the best class I've taken at BYU in 3 years. Tests and assignments are totally doable and not difficult.

Dr. Rugh is a really great professor and is super inspirational. I'm a Neuroscience major and only took this class for credit with no interest in the subject. However, I ended the class with a good grade and a renewed sense of sociology. If you go to class and do the reading for homework it's an easy A.

Taking this class from Dr. Rugh is such a great decision! He has such a unique perspective on things and his lectures are awesome! He's very open-minded and willing to work with you. Pay attention in class, his tests are a good mix of information from the readings and class discussions.

Dr. Rugh is legit. He teaches an interesting subject in a fun, intellectual way. There is at least an hour's worth of reading/listening between every class & you write 4 papers throughout the semester. The daily quizzes are 1/2 participation, 1/2 comprehension from the hw and prepare you for the 2 tests. TA review sessions are a must too!
Dr. Rugh is one of the funniest professors on campus. His class was great and very interesting. Definitely would recommend taking this class ever for a GE.

Dr. Rugh is the man. This class was a 300 level but the content is go good is doesn't really feel like work. He is super knowledgeable and each lecture has A LOT of info. Still he he really willing to work with you and help you through it. Also, just a life changing class. Must take if you're at BYU

Dr. Rugh's Sociology of Race Ethnicity class is exceptional. There is a lot of reading and the majority of each lecture is looking at lots of graphs and statistics. Prepare to have your beliefs challenged!

Dr. Rugh is absolutely amazing! He is honestly one of my favorite professors at BYU and his Race and Ethnicity class was my favorite class this semester. This class isn't easy and requires a lot reading, but Dr Rugh is a fair grader and the subject material is interesting enough to not make it feel like a chore.

His sociology of race and ethnicity class is the best class I have taken! I feel that I understand society so much more now and this was a life-changing class. I cannot recommend taking it highly enough! The tests are a little difficult, but the TA reviews are solid ones. There were lots of readings, but they were mostly interesting ones!

Rugh is super passionate and knows his stuff. Do your readings and attend lectures and you'll do fine. We had a midterm and a final which were hard, but if you go to the reviews literally everything is covered in them. He offers extra credit which is pretty easy and he will meet with you to discuss anything you are struggling to understand.

Dr. Rugh was a great professor. It was really cool to have a professor lecture about what they research. The class is really reading heavy and the lectures can be overwhelming sometimes, but overall the content was good. I thought the exams were difficult even though I understood the concepts. But, he is a very nice guy and wants you to learn

We didnt have a traditional textbook, just several books we read parts of throughout the class. Dr. Rugh is an amazing person and professor and is so generous. Sociology of Race and Ethnicity is my favorite class this semester but DONT GET BEHIND ON READING. Even though its a 300 level, I took it easily as a freshman.

Dr. Rugh cares so much about making the world a better place and inspires all those around him to do the same. The class required a lot of work between papers, readings, quizzes, and tests but it was worth it to learn more about race in America. If you put in the work you can get a good grade, although it's not easy.

Dr. Rugh has amazing insights into race and ethnicity. His tests were really hard for me, though. Even though I could conceptually understand the topics and write about them, the multiple choice always got me. Lots of reading, quizzes, and writing, but an amazing professor.

AMAZING PROFESSOR. The material really opens your eyes and Prof. Rugh teaches it in a way that really helps it hit home. This class will change your life. The quizzes and essays are super easy if you keep up on the reading, and even though he puts a lot of numbers in the slides, there are no numbers on the test. TAKE THIS CLASS.

He is my favorite sociology professor. He is so caring and passionate about the subject. He helps you look at life in a different way and inspires you to be a better person. There is a lot of reading but it is so interesting and he does a great job explaining it. Go to class and you will succeed! Highly Recommend!!

Dr. Rugh is AMAZING. I've taken both urban sociology and racial and minority group relations from him, and I would take more if I could! He definitely expects you to read a lot, but the material is interesting and fun to read. He cares SO much about social issues and is one of the few professors I know who is truly passionate about what he teaches

For a 300 level class you have to read A TON, although most of that is from articles he provides. Other than that it is a relatively easy class. Class is slide and lecture heavy, and just know going in that he is quite liberal, and he doesn't really try to hide it. Don't expect both sides of the argument, cause he doesn't give both sides.

Professor Rugh is my favorite so far in the Sociology department. I took the Race and Ethnic Group relations class and learned so much because he is an expert in this area! We did do a lot of reading and then talk about it in class so do it! All book are required, tests can be difficult but there's a curve, answer questions on essays and it's easy.

My favorite professor at BYU! He really cares about his students and offers different opportunities for extra credit. TAKE THIS CLASS! As long as you include personal experience and sociological terms in assignments you'll pass with flying colors. Plus, all of the material learned can be applied to real life. So it's extremely interesting and worth

Dr. Rugh is a fantastic professor. He makes the lectures involved and relatable while keeping it interesting. The class is super relevant and applicable to everyday life. You study a lot about issues like race discrimination, gender discrimination, poverty, etc. It's information that will actually matter, and Dr. Rugh knows what he is talking about

Professor Rugh's class is really intriguing, especially if you're interested in issues regarding race, gender, family, and education. There are a lot of quiz questions that you do in class, plus there's often a lot of reading outside of class. However, you definitely feel changed after taking the class, so the heavy workload is definitely worth it!

Dr. Rugh cares about what he teaches and knows a lot about it. He gets excited about the concepts we're learning which makes learning more fun. There is a lot of reading, but it's all important to be able to understand the concepts in class. He tests our grasp of the reading concepts with graded and participation iClicker questions so come prepared
A lot of reading and difficult tests but this class is interesting and I think it is worth taking. Prof. Rugh is a good guy who does a good job at teaching the class.

If you care about issues like the modern family, race, education, gender equality, you'll love this class! If you don't, the professor probably won't make much of a difference. I loved his lectures and the class discussions. He's super fun. You have to go to class, but I'm always excited to go! It's really not that hard to get an A either.

This class changed how I view myself and those around me. I wish everyone could take this. I seriously believe this could better the world if we could all understand the principles taught in this class. Take it!

Go to class, he gives points for attendance and pop quizzes at the BEGINNING of class. Lectures can be boring and the slides don't make a lot of sense unless you are in class and hear him explain them. A couple essays and a group project. A good class but I didn't super enjoy it. Make comments, you get graded on participation.
The lectures were interesting and it was definitely worth taking. Rugh was an awesome professor. Would definitely take again.
I would take this class again- I learned so much! Professor Rugh is helpful and passionate about what he teaches.

I thought that Dr. Rugh was a very nice and funny guy, but I thought that he was an extremely tough grader. He is also extremely bad at writing tests -- his tests are some of the more difficult and confusing ones I've taken at BYU. Expect a lot of reading and assignments. You can miss 5 classes before it affects your grade.

The class is really easy except for two things: the reading is long, and the tests are extremely difficult. Dr. Rugh is really smart, but most of the lecture went over my head. There is so much info given during the lecture that it is hard to take notes. Tests ask you for really obscure facts. This class was really difficult.

Great guy, I learned a lot in the class.  But his tests were just so darn hard.  I felt like I understood everything we learned, and I studied like crazy, but I always did poorly on exams.  So far his tests are the hardest I've taken at BYU.

His 1.5 hour class drags a bit because he reviews over the homework's reading. An interesting class, nontheless. Relies very heavily on the textbook and teaches straight out of it. Read it and go to the min number of classes and youll be fine.
Dr. Rugh is THE BEST! He really makes Sociology interesting. His speciality is looking at race. Friendly to liberal students as well.

Dr. Rugh definitely knows his stuff, but all he teaches in class is exactly what is in the textbook. It was hard to be interested in class because diagrams, facts, and pictures are taken directly from the textbook. It seemed pointless to stay in class, except there were attendance and performance points through iclicker.

Dr. Rugh is my favorite professor by far.  If you're taking sociology take it from Rugh!  He tells you on the first day of class that if you skip class you won't do well on the final.  Great class with great lectures.  He really knows his stuff and is always willing to help you succeed in any way he can.

I loved coming to class for SOC 370 with professor Rugh. There was a lot of reading and work, but I learned SO much from his lectures and the reading. It truly opened my eyes to the whole world of Urban Sociology and I am so glad I took the class. He is a TOUGH grader but he believes in you and wants you to succeed. He needs to teach more courses.

I heard that Dr. Rugh had bad ratings and started a Rate My Professor profile.  He is one of my favorite professors at BYU.  You need to read for sure, but the reading isn't bad comparatively.  He is a tad liberal, perhaps some people at BYU don't like that. He is definitely respectful of all viewpoints. Seriously awesome, funny professor. Take him
Dr. Rugh is an amazing teacher, I wish he taught other subjects because I would take all his classes without hesitation. His lectures are clear and the test reflect what you learn in class.

Dr. Rough is a good professor.  He is very approachable and will help you if you take the time to meet with him.  He has a passion for what he teaches.  Make sure you read and turn all your assignments in.  Go to the TA reviews, they help you with basic information but they take forever and if you don't participate the TA's will not help you out.

Dr Rugh is a nice guy but one of the most confusing classes I've ever taken. I learned more from the textbook than from him which is counterproductive because all the questions on tests were from class. The assignments never made much sense and it was extremely unclear what was expected of us both on assignments as well as tests.

Dr. Rugh makes it easy to relate this course to your life. His tests are tricky, but he does curve them. You do need to do all the readings and take good notes in class. It is manageable though. If you go in to talk to him, he helps you out. He also promotes good class discussions.

Took this because I heard it was interesting, easy, and covered MCAT topics. The classes tended to be chaotic and poorly organized. Rugh is really interested in the topics, but he does not explain or teach them very well. Questions are usually poorly written with trick answers and require you to read his mind.

Really didn't like this class. There were a ton of confusing charts and graphs used in class, a few on tests. A few assignments seemed like busy work. Huge amount of required reading some days. Quite a few poor questions on his tests. He is very helpful if you visit him in his office, though.

If I had an hour to live I would spend it in Dr. Rugh's class because it felt like an eternity. Nice guy for the most part, but super boring and confusing lectures.  Tests were virtually impossible.  Super confusing and miserable class!

Dr. Rugh is a great teacher. He is a little new to teaching, but you can tell that he is genuinely interested in the material and his students. The reading was a little long, and I'll be honest that I started to slack on that a lot but I still got an A- in the class. He tells what is going to be on the test and the assignments are easy and helpful.

Dr. Rugh is nice, but he is a terrible teacher. Lectures are boring, full of confusing stats and graphs. Tests are impossible - badly worded and confusing, and he asks obscure questions on things mentioned maybe once in class. The study session is useless. I felt like no matter how hard I studied I never did well. You have to beg for extra credit.
Very nice guy, but he does a terrible job of utilizing class time or preparing you for the tests, which are incredibly vague and badly worded. The actual workload was quite manageable.

Dr. Rugh is a nice guy, but is not a great teacher. There is way too much reading for his class. Other teachers don't require as much. He only cares if you know the material if you're passionate. I went in to his office and he couldn't care less. He didn't try to help me understand the material like most teachers, I was just wasting his time.

The class has great potential, but you don't discuss a lot. You do A LOT of reading. Probably 20-30pgs+ per class. Remember, this is a 100 level GE. His tests are way confusing. Most things in his class are worded poorly. Very confusing or very specific. If it were worded better, I'd give his class an A+, but now it's like a C+. Nice guy though

Dr. Rugh is a great teacher! He graduated from Princeton and you can tell that his intelligence rubs off onto his students. His reading guides are super easy, his quizes are easy, but his tests are a bit challenging. Be sure to study and ask lots of questions before taking it. Furthermore, Dr. Rugh really cares about his students. He's great!

I really liked this class and Dr. Rugh. He's supernice and really cares about the subject and the students. He's still figuring everything out since he's pretty young, but he's a good professor and he's reasonable.

Prof Steffen is incredible! My only advice is don't buy the textbook. I spent $120 at the beginning of the semester, and used it once on the first day. Prof Steffen is so good at explaining things that you don't need the textbook. I had 0 coding knowledge before this course and got an easy A because I followed his instruction and practice problems.
One of my GOATs at BYU. Class is pretty easy if you don't have previous Python knowledge, even easier if you do. The layout of the class is very easy for students to succeed.

Great guy, super approachable and nice. One of the best parts is that he gives super clear study guides, so you know exactly what you need to know for the test. I would highly recommend taking the class from him.

Some people are nice because they fake it, some are because they are genuinely good. Professor Steffen falls into the second category. His spiritual thoughts were probably the best part of the class. He just shares what he's been thinking about. This class gives you great skills and we could use AI on almost every assignment. Take IS 201 from him!

Prof Steffen had some incredibly difficult personal things going on during the semester I had him, and he still managed to be super helpful and understanding toward my own challenges. One of the genuinely best people I've met at BYU. Good professor as well.

The class is very doable and never felt unreasonably challenging.

Absolute GOAT. One time I saw him save a litter of lambs out of a burning barn and then donate $1 Million to completely rebuild the barn. He also was part of Seal team 6 I'm pretty sure

great teacher, super chill and teaches well. Puts lots of effort into the class. Impossible to dislike this guy

I highly recommend taking IS 303 from Steffen. He's young and relatable. He's very knowledgeable. This class would have been really hard if I had no coding experience. Even with previous python knowledge, I barely squeaked out an A.

Professor Steffen is one of the best professors at BYU. He is very good at teaching the material and answering questions in class, as well as outside of class on Slack. He teaches to the needs of each class, always asking for feedback and listening to see if he needs to slow down or pick up the pace. He always brings the Spirit to his class!

Prof Steffen is such a sweetheart. The content in this class came easy to me, so can't say much about difficulty because I know quite a few students struggled. You are given all the tools you need to succeed, just need to put in the work. You will learn a lot from Prof Steffen, he does a great job and he takes feedback because he seeks to improve.
Great professor, he does a good job explaining the coding we need to know to complete the assignments. Class is very helpful, and the lectures always stay on track.

This was my favorite class that I've taken at BYU. Professor Steffen is amazing, he loves getting feedback from students and is really looking to constantly improve. He records all of his classes and posts them to watch later and his assignments are perfect preparation for exams. Amazing class 10/10 would recommend.

Teacher is very nice, but still very new which means that the assignments and class structure shifted several times. The test was much harder than the hw, and it was timed, so make sure that you do all the test practice questions. You can attempt to do the whole class, besides the tests, before class even starts. Used Python and SQL for this class.

He made sure class material was very relevant, and we understood it. He is one of my favorite professors ever, I'd highly recommend his class.

I actually took ELING 322 from her but it wasn't listed as an option. Anyway, 322 was a great class and I learned a lot. The lectures were great and there were a lot of assignments but most of them didn't feel like busywork and I learned a lot of valuable things from them. The class was also very organized which was super nice. Highly recommend!

I adore her. Professor Christensen is so kind and caring. She understands that student life is stressful and is willing to make accommodations. Her tests aren't hard at all if you pay attention in class and study for maybe an hour or two.
Christensen really knows her stuff. She is organized and passionate. Her lectures are a little hard to follow and take notes for, but she will answer every question.

This class was phenomenal!  I've also had Professor Christensen for ELING 325.  She is a caring professor and always willing to adapt to students' needs.  ELING 448 was a wonderful class and I learned a lot.  It was challenging, especially with the amounts of readings and homework assignments, but they were all worth it.  Highly recommend!

I have taken Professor Christensen 3 times and enjoyed all of her classes. She has a lot of readings and longer tests, but her classes aren't too hard if you do the readings and assignments (can be long but are pretty easy). She makes class fun and has so much excitement for the material. ELIING 448 and 447 are both fun if you love language!

I took both Early Modern and Late Modern English from Prof. Christensen and loved them! She does give a decent amount of homework, but it all has a purpose and helps you learn to use the available tools. Professor Christensen is very kind and understanding, and she truly cares about her students. It may be a little more work, but it's worth it!

I took 3 classes from this professor because:
- She genuinely cares about students and is invested in their success.
- Courses are well organized.
- Tests encourage further learning (as opposed to the cram & regurgitate method).
If you're looking for an easy ride, this is not the professor for you. (She requires work commiserate with the level.)

This was my fourth class with Professor Christensen. She is an amazing teacher and really cares about her students. She is also easy to work with. With that being said, she does have a lot of homework. The homework does serve a purpose though in learning the subject. If you stay on top of the work, the class is enjoyable and fun!

She is super helpful when it comes to answering any questions and explaining concepts you might be confused on. She is really great at leading class discussions and is able to help you understand literature in a linguistic point of view.

I loved this class. I do not like English, reading, or papers, but I enjoyed this class. Professor Christensen makes it easy to succeed if you do the readings and come to class. Plus she is so wholesome and nice.

She is literally the kindest human. Also her constant homework quizzes (you can take as many times as you want) are literal life savers for this class. I struggled to understand a lot of the concepts in this class, but she gives you PLENTY of opportunities to practice what your learning and explains things multiple times and is just really helpful!

Truly, I don't know why these reviews are so positive. I had a very hard time with this teacher--she barely taught. One time in a lecture (the day before the test, mind you), someone asked the difference between a phrase and a clause, and she said "I don't think I have a satisfying answer for this". Not the worst, but I would avoid going forward.

This woman is the GOAT!!!! She is the sweetest professor and cares about her students. Shakespeare is so fun to study with her and you feel the spirit every time. I cannot recommend this class enough for everyone.

I loved Prof. Christensen - I honestly DID fall in love with Shakespeare during this class, it was just a delight. It was a good deal of work, fast paced reading and you watch a performance on your own time as homework for EACH play you study and you write several significant papers. But still one of my favorite classes, and she's a good choice.

Professor is really sweet, but I wouldn't take another class from her. Her structure is really faulty, so you do 2+ hours of work outside of class, then come into class and keep learning new topics without review. She moves very quickly and assumes you know things. She said she expects an average grade of a C on our exams (which is what happened).

An empathetic woman, a deep thinker, and an engaging teacher. Conversations instead of lectures. Sincere, deeply thought out feedback for papers and projects. Some of the projects near the end got a little cheesy but I just love her so dang much I was willing to humiliate myself for her.

Best choice I've made for a GE credit, and she made our zoom class feel like a real class. I learned a ton about Shakespeare and now I feel cultured. My best advice for the papers: read the book and annotate, then watch the film after you get the prompt for the paper so you know what to look for. TAKE THIS CLASS! (But get ready to work hard!)

Professor Christensen is outstanding! She has clear expertise in the subject that she teaches. She is passionate about Shakespeare's works, and she is compassionate towards her students. She is incredible at making class an engaging, valuable experience, despite the Zoom format. All activities are valuable, even though I was doubtful at the start

Professor Christensen is a gem. She is the sweetest woman and knows just about every aspect of Shakespeares life and literary works! She makes it clear as to what is expected in her class and does a great job at making you grow such an appreciation for Shakespeare. BE PREPARED TO READ THOUGH!

Best class I've taken. Christensen's very passionate, which leads to GREAT classroom discussions. Get ready to read for every class, write two long essays, memorize two passages (14+ lines), and perform a scene in a group. To really enjoy this class, make sure to talk! Participating makes it so much more fun. ALSO, ANNOTATE the textbook!!!

The class was full of busy work, felt like there wasn't a real point to her assignments and yet she graded very harshly. Says she accepts feedback but doesn't actually change very much of her class. Very little energy/enthusiasm for the material. Rarely felt appreciation from her as a teacher/mentor role. Wouldn't take again

She is very caring and very professional at the same time. Cares so much about her students, extremely willing to meet outside of class. She uses interesting examples in her lectures, which are pretty interactive. Two midterms, one final, one research paper (which was very very very interesting - favorite paper I've ever written.) Highly recommend!

This Shakespeare class was one of my all time favorite classes I have taken at BYU. Dr. Christensen really brings Shakespeare to life and has made me fall in love with all of his plays. This class requires a lot of work outside of class, you have to memorize, perform a play, attend performances, just be ready for that. Lots of work, but worth it.

Prof Christensen is awesome. She uses a lot of examples and really wants you to know the material. Her tests are hard because you're used to working in a group to do the pre-tests and other coursework, but she's always willing to go over questions and help you out. I took her class during summer and we had two midterms, a paper, and then the final.

I LOVE Sister Christiansen. She really loves Shakespeare and gets you excited about each play. You read 8 plays, and I got by with A's on tests by sparknoting 7/8 of them. Drops questions on tests if too many people missed them. A paper for each play, but not hard. Really interesting lectures. Very discussion based. Such a good class for a GE
Unlike most GE's and their professors, Sister Christensen and her class was fun, enlightening and not hard at all. I would take it again just because I liked it that much.

She's actually the nicest person. Not a super tough grader. Understands that most people take Shakespeare for a GE credit and aren't devoted English majors. Lots of reading and papers, but it's not that hard. Quizzes are easy if you keep up with reading. Group work is limited and she's forgiving in grading it. Fun class if you put in the time.

Professor Christensen did an amazing job teaching Shakespeare. You can tell that she LOVES the subject - and it keeps the lectures open. There are a lot of papers in this class, but she is completely fair and unbiased when grading them, so just put an honest effort into them. Be prepared for Hamlet and Macbeth. This class is definitely worth taking
She was a good teacher with awesome test preparation.  Because it was a summer class, we didn't go SUPER in depth into most concepts, but if you went to class that helped.
She's great at listening to what students need to hear more about.  Her lectures are amazing--she does a great job at explaining the English language.

Mrs Christensen is such a nice lady, and she's very clear about expectations for you in the class. I learned a lot about Shakespeare from her class, even though it was very easy. Make sure you attend class and take notes, and you should be fine.

This is one of the very few classes I've taken at BYU and said afterwards, "wow what I learned in this class I will actually use in life" it was very practical and well worth my time. She was great at giving prompt and helpful feedback and was always willing to take the time to help you improve.

Professor Christensen works with her students so that useless assignments are weeded out. I found that every one of the projects we did were valuable to my learning and somewhat enjoyable to complete. She is always there to help and her feedback is very pertinent.

Christensen is not the greatest teacher. She makes her tests extremely hard using very obscure sentences for her examples. Sentences that don't occur naturally in English. I don't recommend taking this class from her. My disinterest in grammar had decreased. I didn't know that was possible. I will say that she is a very sweet person.

This was the easiest class I took in college, yet at the same time I feel like I learned more about english than in any other previous english class. Really prepares you for writing in you future occupations. Lots of group work, but the assignments are easy A's.

Prof. Carter is very knowledgeable about media law and has been up and down the ladder of legal and communications work. He's very kind and cares about your success. For a class on law, it is simple, well organized, and mainly focused on your ability to apply law concepts to case studies and situations. Because of that, you're tested on application

Ed Carter's media ethics class is blended, so in-person attendance is not required. The course is easy to pass with weekly assignments and tests. Physical attendance is not taken, which makes the class very flexible. Overall, the workload is manageable and straightforward.
he's a great guy take his class!

Professor Carter is amazing. His class is straightforward. It is quite a bit of reading, but it honestly taught me a lot about law. For the comms major I did wonder the relevance of the class and why it is required for any of the comms majors, but it is informative if you are interested in law.
Kind. Interesting insights.

Ed is the best. Easiest teacher and has very little assignments/HW. Tests are easy as he requires you to fill out a study guide, then lets you use it on the test. He has clear grading and organization. My class was blended, but he allowed for the in-person day to also be on zoom if you wanted. AND he recorded all lectures. The BEST

This class was pretty easy with not too much reading (he even highlights the parts of the reading that we actually need to know and let us ignore the rest). It was kind of a boring topic but that was fine for me. There were 3 papers (one of them was just a get-to-know-you paper) and the grading criteria for the other 2 weren't super clear.

I took the blended version of the class which was nice because he never requires you to go in person if you dont want to. There was a lot of work and the tests were pretty hard, get ready to memorize a bunch of terms.

Dr. Carter teaches Media Law very well, in a way that's not hard to understand so you get the basics for comms. You work on an outline during the semester and get to use that on the midterm and final. The course guidebook is the best, so just refer to that! Always willing to meet with students, which is a plus.

Dry subject, but he does a good job. Has really clear expectations/criteria and tells you how to do well. He responds fast and accommodates. He literally highlights the important bits in the reading so you can see what's important and gives guidebooks about the biggest ideas for each module. Weekly discussions and a few papers. Take this from him!

Prof. Carter is very kind, caring, and understanding of his students. His course is laid out well, but I was frustrated that his grading was unclear (he looked for very specific wording and use of examples). It seemed that the course was more specific towards journalists, and not other comms majors. His quizzes require answers unrelated to exams.

He was one of the most understanding professors I've ever had. I had a lot of personal things come up throughout the semester, but I actually felt that he cared about me and wanted me to succeed in the class. Although the material in class was somewhat challenging, he used a lot of stories and this helped me to understand a lot better.

Great course, great instructor. Professor Carter does a great job of making tricky briefs understandable and applicable. He teaches us so we can actually learn and isn't too focused on us memorizing things so we can just regurgitate and forget--instead, he helps us learn how to think about issues and how to apply concepts going forward.

Pretty simple, straight forward class. There are readings due every week which you discuss in class (thanks heavens, because I rarely understood the them). Prof Carter is a super nice guy and really just wants everyone to succeed. Most things are graded based on your effort to think through the scenarios.

Law is complicated, and this course reflects that in its assignments and grading. There are opportunities to apply what you've learned from mistakes, but the slip-up is still there. ALWAYS DOUBLE CHECK YOUR READING. Sometimes he doesn't assign all of the chapters he should because of different textbook editions.

Just a really great guy. You make an outline (glorified study guide) for the test which you can then use on the test and it totally saves your butt. A couple papers that aren't hard at all and lectures are interesting. I did it during spring so maybe it's different for other semesters, but we were let out at least 30 minutes early every day.

His lectures can be a little dry, but he genuinely cares about the material he teaches and is very knowledgeable. It's a really easy class, just make sure that you attend every class period to earn quiz points.

Professor Carter it literally the most caring professor I've had at BYU. He doesn't care about your grade or if you get every question that he asks right, he cares that you learn. SUPER lenient with grading, will always meet with you/answers emails quickly, and is just a nice guy. Pretty boring lectures, but kinda wish he was my bishop.

Once you get past the monotone voice, you really can enjoy the class. Prof Carter knows his stuff and flaunts it often. Not a difficult class at all. He assigns readings but they aren't essential to your grade. Solid professor, would probably take again.

ONLINE SUPER easy workload (most boring thing I have ever done). You watch a couple of videos (and he has THE most monotone voice in the world) and you do the TONS (40+pg) of readings and take the quiz. The quizzes are SOOOO hard.. but I also didn't always do the reading.. tests are the quizzes so that makes it real easy. 2 papers and that's it.

Prof. Carter is wonderful. This class was fairly easy, if you take notes you will be good to go on the open-book tests. Prof. Carter is super helpful and has a great ethos, I really respected him and he teaches things in a way that invites discussion.

This was my third online class from BYU and of the three, the easiest by far.  It was well-designed and straight forward with only a few "curve balls."  Obviously the professor knew it was a core requirement class and designed it for meeting the school's criteria without overburdening the student not pursuing a degree in this field.

I took his online class & it was very well-structured. He always made himself & the TAs available for us. As long as you know what he expects and have a clear understanding of the syllabus, this class is an EASY A! Just put in effort. Lots of reading but quizzes are ALL open book! He can be a little dry, but is very knowledgeable!

I took his online class and it was very easy! You had a total of 12 quizzes due throughout the semester (20 questions each), 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. Super easy, and the class is run really well. If you have any questions the TA's are very helpful. I'd totally take it again.

TAKE COMMS 300 FROM HIM DURING SPRING/SUMMER! This class is just as hard as it should be-  "required" reading, and daily quizzes, but they are simply attendance quizzes and you learn the material during class, so just lightly skim. He makes his expectations very clear and grades fair. Go to class and spend time on the 2 papers and you'll do great.

Super nice guy, passionate about what he is teaching. You learn a TON from this class but assignments are not difficult at all so you have time to actually enjoy what you are learning. Definitely recommend this class with Professor Carter no matter what your emphasis is! :)

Professor Carter is one of the nicest professors at BYU! He's so considerate and definitely knows what he's talking about. As long as you go to class and labs you'll be completely fine! The labs take effort but they aren't too difficult! Definitely take this class from him!

Professor Carter is such a nice guy and he genuinely cares about each of his students. Go to class for the attendance quizzes and make sure to do well at the labs and you'll easily get an A in the class. The final is NOT comprehensive and theres only 2 tests in the class including the final - both super easy. For sure a great professor.

Really nice guy, I found the lectures a bit boring, and the labs were really what was important as far as your grades go, but overall I liked Prof. Carter.  Very helpful and accessible, teaches good practical skills for Comms majors to know.
Professor Cater is a great teacher! His class is fun and easy if you just listen and do the work. I learned a lot about all of the comms emphasizes and I'm hoping to take a class from him again!

I have taken a couple classes from Prof. Carter and there's a reason I keep coming back. He's one of my favorite professors and is a very down to earth guy. First reaction is he's a little shy and the class is boring, but you really get into it later. He's super super smart and willing to help out more than an average professor. Highly recommended.

Professor Carter is a very fair teacher who obviously cares about his students. He's one of the most approachable professors I've ever had (I had him for 300 and 321). After the first class I thought he would be boring but I grew to really enjoy his lectures. He's a super nice guy and if you do what he asks you'll have no trouble earning an A.
After the first day, I thought this class would be really boring, but I ended up liking it a lot. Professor Carter is a little shy, but he's just a wonderful man.  I learned quite a lot in his class.

Recommended.  Definitely not the most engaging lecturer, and the 3 hour class is long, but the subject matter is still interesting and you get to discuss within small groups.  He is a very nice person and willing to do whatever he can to help his students succeed.  Papers require a LOT of work, but he is a VERY generous grader.

I was not excited about taking this class but Prof. Carter is awesome.  He is the most approachable and down to earth prof. I have had. Ethics and Law paper are required but he is very willing to help if you have any questions. If you have to take this class definitely take it from him! Just do the work and you will be happy with your grade.

Just skim the readings, daily quizzes are way simple.  Ethics paper is easy but law paper took me approx 30 hours with all the reading of cases we had to do.  He is a very generous grader though and tells you exactly what to expect on the tests.  Great professor: professional, nice, answers emails immediatly...I highly recommend him

The first day of class, I thought I was in for a LONG semester.  However, he grew on me and I enjoyed the class quite a bit. The lectures and group activities are interesting and he is a very generous grader.  I took his once a week class and we got out at least 45 minutes early.  He is very approachable and helpful.

Prof Carter is an incredibly smart guy - he knows his stuff. Comms 321 is a hard class by nature but Prof carter made it interesting. He is helpful if you seek help. He is very fast at replying to e-mails. He isn't the most "warm and fuzzy" professor but he is smart at least!
His advanced media law class was surprisingly interesting.  His open-door attitude is refreshing.  One of the best teachers I have ever had.

Carter is not always easy, but he tends to be understanding and doesn't try to make life miseralbe.  His lectures can be boring, but there are alot of class activities.  His tests can be hard, but he makes sure that you know all the information.  I would recommend him.

He is a great teacher because he is actually a lawyer and knows what he is talking about.  His assignments are not hard just time consuming.  He lays out everything you have to know for the final and midterm.  I would love to take another class from him.

Nice guy! I loved the material. However, despite his knowledge, class can be dull. Class was easy. Go to class b/c he gives a quiz everday and it is 10 easy points. Overall, a very fair man, very easy to talk to when you need help.
He is a great teacher and you learn from his teaching.  You will enjoy this class, especially the take home final.

He's a real lawyer so he has a pretty good perspective.  At times you feel like you are guessing at what he wants out of an assignment.  But he is pretty fair and is probably one of the easiest professors to approach that I've had.
Dr. Sorenesen is an extremely nice professor. He is super approachable and I'm very glad I took Exercise physiology from him. Take any class you can from him!!

Great professor. Very kind. Very knowledgeable. He wants to help students succeed in life and is teaching at BYU for the right reasons. He will help you get access to opportunities you wouldn't otherwise have if you ask and show care.

Jake is one of my favorite professors I've had at BYU! You can tell he genuinely cares about the students and we always had fun in his class. One of my favorite things that he had us do was get into groups the first week of classes and get together outside of class. I loved my group, and we have become good friends. 10/10 recommend this class!

This class is so chill. Tests are open note and take home - I got 95-100% on all of them without studying at all. Homework is really light. There are quizzes you have to do during class, so you should go to class. I never minded going, Professor Jensen is so kind and always made little jokes which was funny and made class a more interesting.

Professor Jensen is a super nice guy, and you can tell that he knows what he's talking about. Sometimes the lectures can be hard to follow, but you get multiple attempts on pretty much everything, and the TA labs are really good.

I totally recommend Dr. Jensen!!!! Our tests were open-note and even open-lecture-slides. He helps you understand exactly what you need to know. And he's funny and will throw in jokes or spiritual thoughts.
Professor Jensen was good at explaining the concepts and always made sure to answer and explain any questions asked during or after lectures.
Professor Jensen is very nice and truly cares for his students. You get multiple attempts on every homework and even the tests. TAs are also very helpful and nice.

I learned hardly anything in this class. Lectures were confusing and anything I learned, I learned in the TA Lab. GO TO THE TA LAB, it'll save your grade. You get multiple attempts on almost everything, even the final, and exams are open note. However, that only really helps if you understand the content. Some of your lowest scores will be dropped.

I love Dr. Jensen! Even though it was a big class, I felt seen as a student-- he remembered my name! He is personable, deeply knowledgeable, and teaches in a clear, accessible way. His of real-world experience and stats jokes made this class fantastic! I was nervous for this general, but Dr. Jensen made it easy and enjoyable! 1000% recommend!

Dr. Jensen is super caring and respectful. His assignments have multiple tries and you only keep your highest score (4 tries per homework, 2 per exam). He also has some in-class analysis assignments that were fun and collaborative (you can work in a group or alone). His lectures were sometimes easy to zone out, but the class is pretty easy.

This class is like every other stats class, so there are not a ton of differences. This teacher, though, makes sure the class understands the topics before moving on to the next. He gave time in class to do the longer assignments and get help from the TAs. He is only an adjunct teacher, so he doesn't teach all the time.

Professor Jensen is very nice and willing to work with you if you reach out to him. He has awesome TA's and works a lot with them. If you pay attention in class, the assignments and tests are not overly hard. He allows multiple tries for homework and tests. I would completely take another course from him. Be willing to ask for help if you need it.

Don't get scared off by the fact that tests are 90% of your grade -- they are just like the hw and practice tests so super straight forward and easy to do well on. Very clear instructor who teaches you exactly what you need to know. Don't buy the textbook, I only used it once.

His lectures are information heavy, but you mostly only need to know what he writes on the board. We only used the textbook once so just find someone who bought it without checking and get the homework questions from them. The exams are very fair. The major downside is the HW wasn't graded until the last week of class and the TA was unreachable.

This class is literally only graded by homework (which you can get 100% on if you use his lab videos) and exams. If that's a problem for you, do NOT take this class. The material is interesting, and he's a really good lecturer. There are very few support materials outside of lectures though, so you really should attend class. Funny, kind person.

Probably one of the smartest econ professors at BYU. Not always the most engaging lectures, but I definitely learned a ton. Expects his students to be way smarter than we actually are (if you're reading this, I'm sorry). I would say it was worth it to take 382 from him.

Professor Cardon may be the smartest man alive. The material isn't always exciting, and he can have a monotone voice at times, but he knows what he's talking about. This class isn't too bad if you can study the material. He was nice enough to go over homework with us each week. Class is graded by tests, a paper, and homeworks (for completion).

Completion grade HWs & paper; straightforward exams; amazing lectures. BYU Econ department has many commendable professors, like Dr. Cardon and Dr. Stovall. This class is definitely an easy 400-level class, especially if you studied well in 382 or 478. No econometrics, no codings -- just basic calculus. A useful class for business as well.
The homework is easy and gives you good practice at what you might see on the tests. The tests are challenging but fair. Dr. Cardon is very friendly and willing to help you if you need it.

Professor Cardon is a chill guy. Tests are VERY straight-forward. If you come to class and study for a couple hours before the midterm/final, you'll be totally fine. Homework load is light. Might be the easiest 400 level ECON class available.

This class is a mix of dry calculus proofs and really interesting intuition. I found that 70% of the time I was bored out of my mind and 30% of the time I was completely engaged with the material. This is a great class for anyone interested in taking a business route, basically an anti-trust class. He's soft spoken and very accessible out of class.

Professor Carden is amazing and cares about his students! You can't go wrong with taking this class if you just want to build on what you learn in 382. He is a very clear grader and you know what will be on the test. He also curved my grade very generously at the end of the course!

Dr. Cardon is an amazing professor. One of his best qualities is his consistency; the tests, though not always super easy, are always straight from lectures. If you go to class, pay attention, and do the homework, the tests will feel unbelievably straighforward. Excellent class, better professor.

Cardon is a great professor, I took 476 because i took 382 from him. It's an extension of 382. He is a great prof and if you do the work and attend lecture you should be fine. In hindsight if you want an easier credit, take 431 or 461 instead. this class uses some equations but its mostly intuition. but by far one of my favorite professors.

Everything you need to know is taught in class. Answers to problem sets are usually given in class. TAs can make your life much easier and give direction as to what will be on the tests/quizzes. Do well on the tests/quizzes or else you're done.

I definitely recommend taking this class and Econ 382 from Cardon at the same time. They are basically the same class for half of the semester. It was so nice! The two in-class quizzes are basically in-class midterms, so make sure you study for them! Some questions come straight from the problem sets, so I highly recommended doing those.

Professor Cardon is the best! He may be socially awkward, and completely nerdy funny, but you will not regret taking his class. His tests are straight forward. If you do all the problem sets, and studies those plus his study guide you will for sure pass. There wasn't a curve though, so make sure to do well on everything.

I seriously love Dr. Cardon! His lectures are great. He often breaks them up with the theory part, and then a real world part, which is a nice break from scribbling down notes. Tests/quizzes are challenging, but he's an extremely fair grader. Problem sets are doable and the paper is a breeze. If you liked 382, then you'll like this class too.

Dr. Cardon is awesome. The material can be slow at times, but he keeps it interesting with stories and real world examples. It is just more advanced microeconomics, and the class isn't too demanding. Tests are easy if you study the homework. A few hw problems are from the book, but hardly read in it - you don't need it.

I was really nervous for this class, but Cardon made it doable. The material is difficult, so make sure to attend every lecture and write down everything so that it makes sense to you. His study guides and homework prepare you really well for tests, and it is not a difficult workload. Make sure to keep up on your calculus, especially at the start!

Dr. Cardon is very intelligent and interesting. Sit close to the front so you can hear well. ECON 382 is a survey of many topics in economics so the class structure/schedule was a little scattered. I would take a class from Dr. Cardon in the future.

This class will focus very heavily on game theory. Best if you've had the game theory class beforehand so that this is a breeze, otherwise he does a good job at explaining new concepts and he's not a bore to listen to. Homework isn't terrible but don't postpone doing it.

A witty and underappreciated professor, he is able to clearly explain clever examples to illustrate the models that he presents. There is some distance from his lectures to application, but the TA can be a great help. The answer key for the text book problems are online and most of the concepts are easy to grasp. He teaches to the lcd.

Cardon doesn't really seem like he cares enough about the course to make it challenging.  Homework is easy and short, tests are tough but don't count for enough of your overall grade to destroy you if you don't do well.  And he makes you write a short paper but I'm almost positive its just a completion grade, not based on quality.
Very confusing. A nice guy but gave unclear lectures and unpredictable tests.
Cardon is not a very interesting lecturer and lost most of the class during his 380 lectures. He was not very clear and the TA was the reason most students learned anything. Take another 380 teacher.
Dr. Cardon is a great guy. His humor is a little subtler than other professors, but if you pay close attention, it turns out that he's a pretty cool guy.
This class was perfect. Professor Cardon was very clear and fair. His tests are easy if you understand the lectures and visit the TA. Definitely my favorite class at BYU so far.

Don't buy the Oz Shy book (answer guide's online). Soft-spoken, straightforward, and fairly methodical in lecturing. Sit close, his handwriting is atrocious. The class is essentially a continuation of 382, no paper or econometrics required. So if you need a break from intense 400-levels, take this class. Great TA help too.

I did 382 and 476. These two classes go great together. Great teacher, don't get put off by his understated style at first; if you pay attention he's actually a really clever, witty dude. Exams are 90% of your grade. Pretty much just straightforward math problems for everything. Not bad at all.

I took him for 382 as well. He is a great teacher. The beat thing about his classes are the usefulness of his ta's. He is very funny once you get to know him and he will answer any question in class. Take this class for sure.

Not the most interesting lecturer. Straightforward tests closely follow the practice exams and homework problems. Homework out of textbook - not challenging, especially with TA's help in lab hours.  You'll probably fall asleep a few times in class, but if you go to TA hours and understand the homework you'll get an A.

Cardon is a great professor.  He assigns homework approx every week or so, and the TA was really helpful.  No quizzes.  The tests (2 miterms + final) were quite straightforward--just like Cardon.  He's a very nice guy, too.  Quiet and softpoken, but very pleasant.

A great teacher. The subject matter isn't too fun but he makes the calculus seem not so hard. Unlike many economists he seems to still be human. Be prepared for weekly quizzes and study hard for the exams. Go to the review sessions offered by his TAs.
One of my more favorate econ classes. It wasn't confusing at all, his tests aren't too bad, and his leactures are very interesting. I totally recommend this class.

This guy is the best teacher ever!!! I've never met a more intelligent person in my entire life.  Do anything you can to get into his class.  It must be something in the Cardon name, because they are all intellectual giants.
He's a really good teacher and not confusing like most econ professors. His tests really aren't too hard. As long as you study his review sheets and a little bit more you'd be fine.

James Gaskin is amazing. He is super funny and personable, and really cares about every student. When learning a coding language, instead of giving a clear rubric and outline, he just jumps in, which can make it hard to start. Go to every lecture, even the optional ones.

Professor Gaskin knows how to relate to students. He is super awesome and genuinely just a great guy. Class is hard, but doable. I only went to like 3 classes this semester and got an A. Just read the textbook and you will do fine. He does use AI to grade his exams, which constantly made mistakes which was annoying. TA will fix it.

I love Professor Gaskin! You will need to go to the TA lab for projects but he makes lectures very entertaining and he is super smart. Missing a lecture can be hard or easy it just depends on the day you miss. The class is a hard concept but he makes it entertaining to learn.

Gaskin is an awesome professor. He's funny, engaging, and I enjoyed his lectures. He's great at teaching beginners, and there are TAs available for anyone who needs extra help. As long as you stay on top of the work and do the readings, the class is very doable, and the projects can even be enjoyable. Would definitely recommend taking IS from him.
This class is super doable without going. I went to class probably four times the whole semester and easily succeeded. Study and memorize the book and you'll be just fine.

I loved Professor Gaskin! He is incredibly hilarious and interesting. His tangents (crazy life stories) are short, sweet, and to the point, and generally has the entire class laughing out loud. He is very fair and considerate about grading while still expecting you to work hard and put in the effort. Lots of help available if you're struggling.

He is a really funny, nice guy. However, HE GOES SO FAST IN CLASS, I can't keep up. He's extremely smart and jumps around a lot without explaining, especially while writing code. Only very computer savvy people can do well in this class. Projects are harder then homeworks, and no matter how hard I try I can't do well on them. Im fs discouraged.

He is really bad at teaching. He kinda just does everything without explaining. For example he will just start walking through something without explaining anything. You will need to go to TA labs or youtube if you actually want to learn. the content is hard and he moves fast he is really smart and he kinda just assumes everyone understands.

Professor Gaskin is one of my favorite professors! He was hilarious, had entertaining stories he shared, and did a great job explaining complex subjects. He paced the lectures well for a class that relied heavily on technology and the TAs were helpful in class. AI and collaboration were allowed on projects which helped a ton.
I LOVE Gaskin!!! He is so hilarious and made class so enjoyable. He is very smart and successful. His teaching inspired me to major in IS.

James Gaskin is an amazing professor. It was super easy to pay attention in his lectures and he laid things out super clearly how to do the projects in class. It is very project heavy but there is plenty of TA help. I had no experience with coding before this class but I had an amazing time

Professor Gaskin makes IS201 fun, even for non-tech savvy students. While the coursework can be challenging, his engaging lectures and helpful resources like unstuckstudy make it manageable. Stay on top of the work, and you'll learn a ton.

Dr. Gaskin is one of the best professors at BYU. The class, material, and grading are straightforward. ChatGPT is helpful for course material. I was in the online section but found attending class beneficial. The TAs weren't very helpful since they often relied on ChatGPT as well.

Dr. Gaskin very nice, he'll give you a tour of his cool office if you stop by during office hours. Took the on-demand course which only used the textbook. Would recommend the in-person sections as I personally found it harder to learn using just the book. There's a lot of coding, so would recommend learning some VBA basics or SQL beforehand.

Loved IS 201. I wish there were less Big Quizzes (ie Midterms) because I enjoyed the projects a lot more and felt that was the best way to learn--there were a lot of random things you had to memorize for the midterms. Other than that, the class is set up so well and everything builds on top of each other so you can build you own website!

He seems like a good guy. If you care about getting an A, you'd better know the entire textbook like the back of your hand because you will be tested on wildly specific questions. Test questions are also poorly worded and answers feel subjective. Additionally, I hate testing that isn't proctored because people cheat. This was on-demand. Good luck!

Great professor overall. He moves a little fast but it's really easy to get help. He keeps class really entertaining. If you're in the online session he will still let you come to class which is what I did and found very helpful.

I am taking this class online. The only difference between taking it online & taking it in-person is that there is not a lecture for the online class, so you have to learn everything by reading the textbook. I started attending class in person because it was impossible to do online with no teacher instruction.

Probably the hardest class Ive taken at BYU so far. This class is super homework, project, and test heavy. In past semesters everything was open book, notes, and AI but they changed it this semester so the tests are all closed book everything which is super hard when they encourage you to use AI on the other assignments. Do not take this online!

Prof. Gaskin is hilarious and I really enjoyed his class! IS 201 is a difficult class for most students, but he gives you many tools to help you succeed including a chat bot to help with a lot of assignments. He structures his class so the hardest content is covered in the middle of the semester which means your final isn't too difficult.

Should be a 10 credit class. His online class has 0 explanation of the topics unless you can magically transform the IS textbook jargon into something meaningful. The homework and quizzes are not very clear. Seems like a great guy but this class is just not it. Do yourself a favor and take a light load or just use AI for this whole class.

Took it as on-demand, and he is not caring about the students at all. He told students to go to the TA for EVERYTHING, including grades. When I emailed to him about an unfair grading method, he was very much reluctant to even deal with it. I petitioned out of his class eventually. If keeping a good GPA is important to you, avoid his online class.

Professor Gaskin is a really cool guy and a really good teacher. IS201 is naturally a hard class and Professor Gaskin did a really good job teaching us difficult subjects and helping us to understand the material. I would definitley recomend him to anyone taking IS201.

I enjoyed this class! Lots of resources to succeed. Definitely a doable class if you put in the effort Gaskin's lectures were fun, but my only critique is that he didn't do much explaining during lectures. It was mostly watching him create a code rather than him explaining what things meant. He is very intelligent and I would recommend him.

I'm not a very tech savvy guy but I loved this class. The lectures were very entertaining and I find Prof. Gaskin hilarious. Some of the work was difficult but I learned a lot. Learning the basics to IS has helped me out a lot and he teaches them great!

Such an awesome teacher. Quick at responding to emails. Such a cool guy, a real genius. Really cares about his students. What makes the class hard is the fact that coding is so new to most taking the class like myself. Eventually you get the hang of things and learn a ton. Open book, open internet, open ai. This was my favorite class.

Gaskin is an awesome professor and cares about his students. He is good at explaining things and will help you if you reach out to him. However, this class is super hard. It's easy to get behind, so make sure to stay on top of everything and get help. This is not an easy 3 credit course. The assignments, projects, and tests take a lot of time.
Chill professor and tries to make IS fun.
My favorite professor ever! Cares about students and goes out of his way to help. Also answers emails very quickly. Amazing, if you are taking IS201 take it from him for sure.

Gaskin was a dope teacher. His class was very interesting and will probably come in useful for the future. Going to class is optional as you can just do the tests and quizzes all from the online textbook, but I felt going in person was helpful. He makes his lectures interesting and engaging. Overall a good professor.

Gaskin is the absolute best choice for this class!! Funny guy that makes all the lectures engaging and interesting but you can tell he's very knowledgeable. (With fascinating life stories while waiting on technology, too!) He teaches just as much as we need to know, and tells you if it's more. 10/10 would recommend and absolutely take it from him

As someone who never did anything related to this class, I was way nervous. But he was such an amazing professor! He's super energetic and engaging, takes time to go through each step, and he and the TAs are available outside of class. Difficult class but an amazing professor! Taking this class from him has me considering applying to the IS program

Professor Gaskin is great. He knows very well what he is teaching and he tries to always be available to help his students. The class is hard but you will succeed if you read the book and attend class even though it is not mandatory.

He openly accepts AI which is awesome and the class is pretty difficult not gonna lie. You have to buy a $90 textbook because all the work is done on there. I feel like we moved super fast through concepts so you'll have to read the textbook in depth for sure.

I love this guy. He is so funny and engaging. His classes flew by and a lot of times I didnt want them to end. He is super flexible on the schedule if we are struggling with things and he teaches all the essential stuff. Main thing is he is so enthusiastic and passionate that it makes it hard to hate IS stuff. Honestly the class was easy.
Genius and great man

One of my favorite teachers ever. If you want to learn the material the best from any IS201 teacher, you have to take it from Gaskin. The man is a literal genius. He teaches everything he knows from real-world experience, so you know what he teaching is real. He goes the perfect speed in class and teaches very clearly. Fun class. Take it from him!

This is a hard course but he is a very kind professor who wants you to succeed. I knew nothing about coding so this was extremely difficult for me but the TA's were very helpful and I really appreciated that.

I really enjoyed this class. The YouTube videos in the textbook were a lifesaver for the completion of the projects. Attendance is not mandatory but for some harder concepts I would definitely recommend attending. The TA lab is helpful and the in-class TAs are a big help too. Gaskin has so many cool stories, I would ask him about them!
Really good class! Material can get hard but he teaches it very well. His classes are fun and interactive and has the coolest stories.

This class was hard for me, but I am grateful I took it! Prof. Gaskin is one of the best professors I have ever had and genuinely cares about the success of his students. He even changed class policies this semester to accommodate more students. . I loved it even though it was a challenging class. Also, I recommend using the online TA lab.

Took the class online. No lectures and just the textbook. A lot easier if you have a study group to help with projects. They take a long time but once you get your code right there is no way to do bad on the assignments. Just don't turn things in late and you'll get an A.

There are a lot of nasty reviews on here from people who took his class online during covid. If you take this class from him now and pay attention closely in each lecture you will be extremely prepared for every homework assignment or test. This has been my favorite class I've ever taken at BYU and I would recommend it to anyone.

This class was fantastic! Even though it is online, you have all the tools you need to succeed as long as you are willing to put in the time. Professor Gaskin and the TAs were always quick to respond and help out. Very clear grading criteria and you learn great computer skills for business. I am happy I took this class and recommend it to anyone.

There were some aspects of this class that were indeed difficult and time consuming but I feel like all the tools that are needed to succeed are given to you. Lots of office hours for both him and his TAs and the entire course is available and open starting day 1. Just don't underestimate how long the VBA unit and the final project will take you.

I loved this class. Gaskin did a great job realizing this was an intro class and not everyone in there was planning to be an IS major. His class is set up so you can work as far ahead as you would like and can move at your own pace. You don't have to go to class, but if you do, he gives you pointers on the assignments. The load isn't too heavy.

This class was the hardest ever. I literally would not have gotten the grade I got if it weren't for my friend being an IS major and basically tutoring me for 2+ hours a week, no exaggeration. What made the class so hard is that there was little instruction from the professor. He made a 15 min video to say what was due each week, and that was all.

Honestly one of the worst classes Ive ever taken. So many annoying things about this class. A ridiculous amount of material and so little direction into which material we should actually focus on. It constantly felt like the professors of this class arrogantly thought like their class was 10x more important than any of our other classes.

Taking IS201 online from Gaskin is just not the way to go. I'm sure he might a great teacher in person but dang it was pretty terrible online. You genuinely teach yourself. The textbook was pretty useless. You can still do well in this class, but don't expect to actually learn or have a professor that actually helps you understand the concepts

Did on-demand for this class, and it was a good choice. You just go through one or two chapters a week and your own pace, take notes, watch the videos in the chapters, and do an assignment every week or every other week. Never really saw Gaskin, you would just hear his voice in a weekly video, but he formatted the class well and you learn a lot.

His class was difficult, I won't lie about that. But his class is SO interesting, especially HTML and VBA. He also is super willing to help you out with whatever you need. I am very grateful for him as a teacher.

The hardest class I have ever done. The projects take an insane amount of hours. Professor Gaskin doesn't have lectures, we just watched old youtube videos. It is hard to get help from the Ta's because the Ta lab is always full and they aren't the nicest people. The things we learned were useful, but we had to teach it to ourselves.

Difficult class but doable if you're willing to work, and you do learn useful skills. TA lab is usually of no help. You don't interact with Gaskin at all, you just watch LOTS of videos by another professor. My advice: Leave plenty of time for each project and focus on learning skills, not memorizing since everything is open internet/book.

Unless this course material comes easy to you, this will be a very difficult course. Everything takes longer than you think it will. Because it is on demand remote and you are teaching/learning everything yourself, make sure you have/make a friend or two that is taking it as well. As you get stumped on projects/assignments that will be crucial.

I was extremely disappointed in the lack of effort to teach anything shown by Prof Gaskin. Mid way through the semester he acknowledged that he had received MANY emails from students asking for help. The sad thing is, he did nothing different to help. The assignments and projects take hours to finish & the TAs cant help bc the lab is always full.

This is my fifth semester at college. Im a 4.0 student. Im not afraid of working hard for an A, but this class was absolutely ridiculous. All these bad reviews are not exaggerating. The concepts arent overly difficult but because this professor hasnt taught a single lecture and we have all taught ourselves exclusively, it has been miserable.

I honestly don't even know what to say. I have never been more disappointed in a professor in my entire life. All of the ratings have been accurate. Such a disappointing professor. The lowest possible amount of teaching. He assigns incredibly difficult tasks without any explanation or teaching. It is so disappointing.

This is the worst class I've ever taken!! Gaskin DOESN'T do any lectures or any type of instruction. You have to teach yourself through the textbook and videos that are outdated and old. He doesn't even grade anything, so IDK what he has been doing all semester. The TA lab system is horrible; there isn't enough TA's to help the 3,000+ students.

If I had to rate the actual course, I would say 10/10. Learned so many applicable things! Worked hard and learned cool stuff. However, this is a professor rating site. Professor Gaskin doesn't teach. It's not fair that BYU is still paying him. I learned 100% of the material from the textbook. I wish I had saved $ on tuition and just gotten the book

Absolutely atrocious class. Im confused by the polarity in reviews as it seems everything before Winter 2021 was positive. There are no lectures or any real teaching done. We learn solely by his YouTube videos from like a decade ago. TAs are impossible to get help from. If you can avoid this class from this clown, do it.

As many have said in the past, this class is by far the worst class I have ever taken. It makes me feel so badly to rate a professor so poorly, but this teacher does not even teach. Forget getting help from the TA's or the professor, because they have "too many students." EVERYTHING takes longer than it says. Just crossing my fingers I pass.

Very hands-off and difficult class. Professor Gaskin seems really nice but did not receive much, if any instruction. Its difficult, be prepared to set aside a lot of time for each project, quiz, midterm, and test. When it says something will take an hour or so that directly translates to like 5 hours so heads up on that.

I don't even consider him my teacher because I'm the only one doing any teaching to myself. He, nor the TAs, are any help at all. Worst class I have ever had. I do not feel as though he cares at all about us students or that we get taught these important skills for our future careers. Good luck getting any help from him or TAs, you can't reach them

WORST class, professor, and TAs I have ever had. He doesn't even teach. No lectures, no help at all. The only material given are old youtube videos that are no help for the projects on coding "languages" we're supposed to learn in a week and a half. Don't take this class, you're basically thrown out to the wolves to teach yourself.

I do not recommend taking this class from Gaskin. I'm sure he knows what he is talking about but he doesn't even teach. We just watch old YouTube videos on the 'textbook' and we are expected to know how to do it in just a few, poorly made and poorly taught videos. Way too difficult and he just sends his students to the TAs when we have questions.

The only "lectures" in this "class" are old videos recorded before covid by other people as a supplement to in person lectures. Because we never received the in person lectures, we only see the how and not the why when trying to learn complex coding languages. You only get 2 weeks to learn the entire coding language too, which is almost impossible
