I'm super confused from the previous reviews. This is without a doubt the worst class I have taken at BYU. The main problem is that Prof Gaskin teaches NOTHING. That is not exaggerated. Also, I've never been able to receive help from the TAs. I have personally emailed him and he honestly doesn't care about what I say. BYU should let him go.

I really don't understand what this guy even does at BYU. He isnt the guy teaching you in the ALL VIDEO online course, and he does not offer any help when you are struggling. He pretends that this is not hard stuff, then assigns HW, MIDTERMS, and other stuff all in ONE week. He literally is not responsive at all, and you will hear NOTHING from him.

I agree with the last rating as well. Professor Gaskin seems like a great guy & all, but he doesn't teach squat. Forget getting help from the TA's, the TA lab is beyond terrible. Also, he assigns chapter readings, quizzes, projects, and midterms in the same week. The flowchart project that was supposed to take "an hour" ended up taking people 5+

I don't know why his ratings are so high. The class is very hands-off for him, all he does is send weekly videos telling us what's due that week. I ran into him once in person and introduced myself as his student and he was very cold to me. You have assignments due every Tues/Fri but he makes tests on Wednesday so sometimes you'll have all 3 to do.
Great on-demand class! He does weekly videos talking about the schedule and gives some good, short spiritual thoughts. Super nerdy but really cool
On demand is a great format for this class. His weekly videos are always super helpful.

Professor Gaskin is amazing. When I accidentally submitted my test after 5 questions, he happily restarted it for me and wished me good luck. The class does involve a lot of reading and videos, but the concepts aren't super difficult. But do make sure to follow along in the videos, especially when you get to the last few chapters.

On-demand was a great format for this class. The video walkthroughs in the skills chapters really helpful. If you follow along with those videos and stay engaged you'll learn the skills and do fine on the projects/test. The skills learned are so valuable! Prof. Gaskin sent out short weekly videos outlining the week and giving good life advice

Loved having this class, great class to take during covid since it's all online. Prof Gaskin is so nice and sends out great little videos every monday that are 2-5 minutes and talk about deadlines, helpful tips, and a little motivational thought or fun random topic he wants to share with us. Class isn't too hard but it does take lots of time to do

This was one of my favorite classes at BYU. Since it was online due to COVID, there wasn't much interaction with Prof Gaskin, but from the weekly videos and other communications he sends out, he is very awesome and understanding. There is a lot of material but the online textbook makes everything super easy to learn conceptually.

I took this class online, so there wasn't too much interaction with Professor Gaskin. He only posted a concise video once a week explaining what we could expect from the upcoming week. He seems like a great guy though. Reminds me of Babish from the cooking YouTube channel.

Gaskin is a funny guy, and made this class really doable. It was an on-demand class so he wasn't around much, but he provides every opportunity for you to do well. Definitely get help from the TA's. The assignments can be time consuming and hard, but they always help a ton.

Professor Gaskin is amazing. He is really helpful and understanding. The class has hours of videos that you have to watch, but the content isn't all that difficult. It is a really helpful class in preparing you to be successful in your future internships.

Professor Gaskin is solid! His class is challenging if you haven't done any programming before, but having done CS142, it wasn't so bad. Just be sure to give yourself enough time for tests. The material wasn't overwhelming. Definitely would him. Rumor has it that he was almost cast as Spider-man in the 2002 Spider-man. Also he's been on Oprah.

Professor Gaskin is awesome. I have never coded or done anything with computers in my life, but he made everything accessible and fairly easy. My course was on-demand online, so he sent out videos every week detailing upcoming assignments and exams. Not an easy class, but definitely a doable one.

I took the online section of this class, after previously taking CS142, IS110, IS115, and IS120. If you already have experience with coding, Excel, and/or web development, then those sections will be super easy for you as this is simple a surface level class. The reading was sort of a reminder for me of what I'd already learned. Worked well for me.

Loved this class. He made learning about technology and programming fun and easy. I did well in the class because I am a hands on visual learner. Almost every class was him on his computer showing us how to code in excel, SQL, or html and we just followed along. He never tried to trick us. Projects seemed ominous, but just need to be broken up.

IS 201 isn't hard, and Gaskin makes it even easier. If you want an A, take it from him. The tests and homework are easy. Less than 1.5 hours per week, on average. He tells a lot of jokes, but some aren't that funny. Class usually includes some type of plug for the IS program, so you can usually show up late with no repercussions.

You can tell right from the start that Prof Gaskin knows what he's talking about: he's young, he's dynamic, and he often shows the class his own projects in order to relate what he's teaching to the real world. His class gave me a ton of skills for me resume while remaining well-paced. I was afraid of coding classes but he changed my mind about CS

Professor Gaskin is very smart but can dumb stuff down very well for us who are new to coding. After taking this class, I decided to apply for the Information Systems major. Follow closely in class because a lot of what he does is basically the same as the homework, but he might not tell you. Just secretly helping you...

The class was interesting, but taking it online was a mistake for me. It is incredibly hard to keep up and know what's due when. 1 of the most stressful classes I took. Super great guy, and quickly accessible through email, but I would recommend taking the in-class section to stay oriented.

The class is totally doable online (as it's structured to be). I am not a computer whiz, and I took this class along with accounting, finance, IS110, and an OCI but still did really well. The key is PRACTICE (mimic everything done in the online videos) and TA HELP (go early because they get swamped a couple days prior to due dates). You can do it!

I love Dr. Gaskin. He's an excitable little nerd, in the best way possible. He is good at gearing his lectures toward the test material. I looked forward to going to class everyday! I learned a lot of helpful things that were completely new to me.

The benefit of actually going to class is that he drops hints of things that will be on the test that are rather difficult to do, given that tests, although open-note, are timed and can press you for time. Gaskin is a great person, super charismatic and ingenious, and accessible within minutes 24-7. PRACTICE forVBAsection- it is hard but I got an A
If you consider taking IS 201, definitely take from Dr. Gaskin. His lectures are so enjoyable and give you an idea of what the test is going to be like.

Prof Gaskin is hilarious and always has interesting and rather impressive stories about his life. He is really good at explaining difficult concepts and if you do well in computer science this class will probably be really easy for you.
He's a very good teacher. He is very clear and his lectures are enjoyable. He is very accessible and responds quickly. Highly recommend.

This is a great class! I'm generally scared of computers and could only take the online section, but I had a great experience. Prof. Gaskin/the TAs always get back to me quickly if I have questions, and the textbook/videos are thorough and (fairly) easy to follow along. If you put in some time, you'll learn great things and have a good time!
Professor Gaskin is great. This is the most useful class that I have ever taken! There is quite a bit of homework, but it isnt bad. He is a very fair grader and wants everyone to do well!

This has been the most useful class I have ever taken! I knew nothing about computers before this class and now I feel like I have something to put on my resume. I actually felt like this class was worth my tuition money! It's not hard if you practice, especially VBA.

To be honest, I spent the most time a week on this class out of all my classes, which isn't Dr. Gaskin's fault. I believe the content for the class is the same no matter the teacher. That being said, Dr. Gaskin is an understanding person. If you don't have prior experience with the information covered, to get an A can take time, but you can.

I have some coding experience, so this class was not too hard for me at all. I took this as the online option, and I have really liked it. Gaskin sends an email weekly to give study tips and whatnot to brace you for the week. The course load is not too heavy, but it can sneak up on you if you do not keep up. All in all, take this from Gaskin

Gaskin is GREAT. I took the online section of his class (I went to class about 1/3 of class periods). It is a TOUGH class. You're coding and doing advanced excel and access work, but the skills you learn are invaluable. Go to the TA lab EARLY, they know their stuff. I had some late nights, but overall very enjoyable. Gaskin makes it worthwhile!

This is one of the best classes I've taken at BYU. Dr. Gaskin is the best!! His lectures are really funny and engaging. Plus, everything you learn in this class is really useful and cool! Class is basically a review of the textbook chapters but it helps to go and review everything. 10/10 would recommend.

This is a tough class especially the last 4 weeks but it's manageable. If you don't get VBA down you will be punished on the final so make sure you really practice. Class moved very fast for me but some of the TA's are really good so go to the lab often. Recommend taking it from Gaskin cause Jenkins doesn't do points back or appeals.
Dr. Gaskin is a great professor. He teaches the subject matter in an engaging, hands-on way, being sensitive to the different skill levels that exist in the class.

The content of this class is invaluable. Dr. Gaskin is a gem. If you don't do well on a midterm due to extraneous circumstances just go talk to him he is very understanding. Spend a day on the WebDev and do it a day or two before it is due. He gives lots of extra credit. The class is easy the first 3/4 and then picks up end of semester.

Gaskin is a great teacher! He really pumps you up about the class and is very honest about the curriculum. He keeps you updated on everything you need and is really conscientious about the students even in big classes. He knows the struggle! Gaskin is great and if you have to take this class, I definitely suggest him.

Professor Gaskin in a nutshell: Proposed to his wife after like a month of dating, daughter memorized all the countries in the world before she could talk, has been on Opera, was lined up to be SpiderMan before the company sold the script and the new company contracted Toby Maguire, can backflip(and will if encouraged). Great professor.

Professor Gaskin is great very knowledgeable about all things computerdom! Theres a LOT of material in this course, but he does a good job covering it all. The class is offered as an online course, but class attendance is VERY helpful. Exams vary in difficulty, depending on the topic; some exams will press you for time. Overall good experience.

Gaskin is hilarious and he makes information systems bearable for someone like me who doesn't really have any experience with computer programming. Class was fairly easy up until the last module, VBA. It jumps from like a level 2 to a 10 on the final, so beware of that...

Prof. Gaskin is the man!!! Seriously, I wish he could teach all my classes at BYU. He has so much passion for the subject he teaches and is just a great, down to earth guy. This made him very approachable and personable. I could ask him questions without feeling embarrassed and he could usually catch my early mistakes before I was completely lost.

This guy is legit. Clear, fair, and cool as hell, he's on your side from the beginning, and gives more than enough helpful hints for you to succeed in the class. He also curved the class by more than the department average, which is a beautiful thing. You should take 201 from him.   Seriously, go to byu edu right now and register for his section.
Dr. Gaskin is a phenomenal teacher and his IS 201 class was easily one of the most interesting, informative, and interactive courses I've taken thus far!
Great professor.  Gaskin is engaging and made the class interesting.  A little disorganized at times, but if you keep up he gives you all the info you need.

Professor Gaskin is awesome! He is very clear and straight forward in his teaching style. He'll give you hints & prepare you for tests & projects. One of the hardest classes I've taken. The final will kill you if you don't study & practice, practice, practice the material. Learned so much from the facts of the day that Gaskin gives during class!

Best teacher i've ever had at BYU. Very funny, straight forward, extremely helpful, gives huge hints for tests and anything graded. Curved class even though it was above the bus school needed average. Definitely knows his stuff- has a PHD in IS. If he is an option, take it from him! you won't regret it, or get an easier grader and still learn a lot
Super awesome professor! Learn a lot and laugh a lot~ You will never regret to take his class~

One of the hardest classes I have taken so far, but I wouldn't have been able to do as well as I did without Dr. Gaskin. Learned so much and he loves this area, which made it much more interesting. Stay on top of work and utilize the TA's, but definitely recommend taking from Dr. Gaskin.

Brilliant professor who is patient and willing to explain concepts until you fully understand them. Read the assigned packets, watch all the YouTube clips, and ask questions IMMEDIATELY when you don't understand something are the three keys to success in Prof. Gaskins class. Oh, and google is your friend too :)

Professor Gaskin is amazing! The material is hard but he is a great teacher and good at explaining tough concepts. He is a phenomenal guy who does take an interest in the lives of his students. If you have to take this class, take it from him!
Great teacher.  I hate technology but loved the class.  It has a lot of stuff that seems like it could be useful in everyday life.  Take it from this guy.

I really enjoyed IS 201 with Professor Gaskin! I learned SO MUCH! It was hard, but totally worth it. Professor Gaskin is relatively new and still figuring out his style. Don't be fooled, the final is MUCH harder than he or his TA's let on. You need to figure out how to do stuff in VBA that was never mentioned in class or any reviews. He is great.

Professor Gaskin is a good teacher, but I wouldn't say he is a great teacher yet. He's relatively new, so I think with time he'll be really good. He knows his stuff, but I felt he was a little disorganized and disengaging at times.  If you work hard (because this IS a hard class), then you should get a decent grade.  Always seek help when needed.

Gaskin is great teacher.  He really cares about his students.  Most students dont do well on HTML so if you can own that, you'll have a huge advantage. The tests given in the testing center were more difficult than the in-class tests.  Isys 201 tests are now the same department wide.  So, the difficulty level is the same regardless of the teacher.
Best teacher for isys 201. Will be a difficult class if you don't know computers well. If you do then you'll have a couple late night, but not too bad.
Professor gaskin is awesome. I really loved the class. He is a really good teacher and is really helpful. This class can be hard, but professor Gaskin always is willing to help.
He's very good with computers, you might have a hard time keeping up with him. He's also awesome. Take this class from him.

Gaskin is a brilliant man.  ISYS has to be a tough class to teach, but I suppose he taught it as well as anyone could have. Rather than giving lengthy lectures, he gives just the meat of the material to you in each class, a teaching style which some love and others don't. Overall, would I recommend him? Yes

Fact of the matter is this class takes work and their are a good number of projects due, but Gaskin is a great teacher, no BS kinda guy that regularly would not go over something he thought would be a waste of your time.  He makes every class engaging, which helps you learn the material really well

Professor Gaskin was an awesome teacher that kept things interesting. His attitude really helped me pay attention and enjoy the class. If you are willing to put the time in and wrap your mind around the concepts you will do well in the class.

5 thumbs up. If you're going to take IS 201, take it from Gaskin. Very clear and straightforward and even pretty funny. You don't even need to do the readings with this guy... which is awesome. But do them anyway, it's good for you.
Professor Gaskin is a great Professor. He made me love a very difficult course. Highly recommended you take this class from him.

My favorite Professor here at BYU so far. Didn't even know what ISYS was before this class and now I'm thinking about Majoring in it. Makes class fun and interesting and you learn a lot! Great class, great prof! Take this class from Gaskin!

Prof. Gaskin is one of my favorite professors. He's laid back, humorous, super helpful, and has an excellent understanding of how to make Information Sciences exciting, even to Management majors. He incorporates some cool projects into the class, such as creating a video game and a web page. He also uses YouTube and Wikipedia to help students learn
Uses sources other than textbooks to keep the class interesting and entertaining.

Great Class!  I learned a ton and enjoyed being taught things which I use every single day at work.  He keeps your interest by telling hilarious stories when the class may tend to drift on a difficult topic.  What I like most about his teaching is he?s energetic and loves what he talks about!

His lecture is clear and well-organized, frequently it's also entertainting.(We played Jeopardy to learn computer hardware once)Welling to help students, and the exam review is so helpful!he guides you to the right direction. Grading on efforts rather than absolute accuracy.He gives chances for us to improve our grade by simple yet helpful activity
Super caring and presents lots of data to back up what he teaches. He teaches empathy and being educated.
UNIV 101 - Awesome class!
Dr. LeCheminant is easily one of the best professors I have had at BYU. He genuinely cares about his students (who he knows by name) and wants to see them succeed.
Dr. Lecheminant is THE BEST!! The kindest and most caring professor. 100% recommend any of his classes.

Professor L is a dawg! Very personable and learned each students name. Homework is minimal outside of a few fun projects/papers, and a group project/paper. Tests are relatively easy and he always accepts constructive feedback on how to improve them. Get ready to memorize quite a few things if you take this class. Make sure to attend class too.

Dr. LeCheminant is a gem! Very kind and hilarious. He was very understanding and willing to work with me when I had to delay an exam for sickness. I'd recommend attending class because the slides are tricky to understand without the lectures. All the tests are online on proctorio and fairly easy if you study.

Dr. L is the SWEETEST. 4 in class quizzes, 2 tests + the final, 5 reading quizzes roughly a month. 1 group presentation + a 4-5 page group paper. 3 1-2 page individual papers. Homework wasn't super difficult, course content could be a bit dense sometimes. Build your exam study guides directly off the published lecture slides and you'll be great!

Probably the kindest, most caring professor at this university. Should be given an award just for how incredibly genuine he is. Class was super interesting, all of it based entirely on the latest studies in this field. Tests and quizzes were not meant to trick you. There aren't difficult but you definitely should study. Loved this class.

Dr. LeCheminant is an absolute doll. So kind and so passionate about nutrition. He brings in the most up to date literature to class. The class is very insightful. The tests are very doable if you study for them. His slides are okay and expectations for tests are somewhat clear, but he is willing to meet and clarify outside of class. Awesome.

I was pleasantly surprised by how much I loved taking this class. I could tell that Dr. LeCheminant is really passionate about what he does, and he provided a lot of insightful information (in my opinion). He was also really accomodating and understanding to my and other students' needs throughout the semester. Taking a class from him in the fall!

Dr. LeCheminant was fine, but his tests were harder than they needed to be. The textbook is awful and expensive, and if I were to take the class again I wouldn't even read it since it sometimes contradicts what he says in lectures. His tests are based on his lectures, so take good notes. There wasn't a lot of homework, which was nice.

I really enjoyed this class! It was demanding, but pretty straightforward. The tests are pretty hard- you can't just get away with memorizing things! You really have to know the material, since most activities and tests involve real world examples. Dr. LeCheminant is great at helping you understand the material, though, and I loved this class!

This class requires lots of effort. You'll need to put in the work, but it's doable. Dr. Lecheminant is extremely kind and really cares about his students. The TA are also really accessible and will answer any questions that come up.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class, but know you will have to seriously study to do well on the tests. They were each 75 with the final being 100. There is a lot of information to know. Pro. Lecheminant is a great teacher who is passionate about the material and teaching his students. The quizzes could be tricky, but they are open book.

He is an amazing teacher and I would definitely recommend him to anyone! The quizzes and exam reviews are open notes, textbook, and lecture slides. To be honest, I did not really read the textbook at all, I only used it when I needed clarification on a few things. If you pay attention in class, take notes, and review then overall you will do well.

He was nice and taught well, but a little boring at times. Online textbook is literal garbage to navigate. Exams and exam reviews can be pretty challenging. Try to get as many points as you can from small assignments to buffer poor exam grades. TAs were okay, not great. Not very helpful with my personal concerns. Very boring class imo.

The class is fine. It was over zoom, which he'd record if you couldn't make it to his class. He often stops class to answer questions, even for silly ones, which seemed like the majority of them. The book was difficult to navigate. The TAs weren't helpful at all and took days to respond to messages. The reviews did not prepare for the tests.

I liked the class and I could tell Prof. Lecheminant enjoyed teaching. What I didn't like was the online textbook. It's AWFUL. Buy the physical copy. The quizzes and test can be tricky, but he tells you in class exactly what you should know for them.

The professor cares but honestly, this is the worst class I have taken at BYU. I did not feel like I learned anything, the tests I felt were made to trick you (I would make low B's but I have never gotten below an A through all of college). The grading scale is atrocious. Try to take this class near the end of your college experience.

Dr. L is very kind and his lectures are extremely well put together. His class may seem unimportant because its only two credits but the information is more pertinent than anything I've learned from classes in the nutrition department.
Prof LeCheminant is great! Easy grader, quizzes and exams are straight forward. Very willing to help students outside of class. Positive attitude and very humble. Fantastic professor.

Professor LeCheminant is passionate about the subject and genuinely wants you to succeed, but there were several times where his lectures felt rushed. The department also does not give extra credit so you have to study hard from the beginning, especially for the exams. As someone who struggles with science, this was not the easiest class.

He cares about his students, and he goes out of his way to answer questions. If there is one asked to which he does not have a good answer in class, he will go home and find an answer and present it in the next class period. He explains things pretty clearly! He is good.

This class was one of the easiest ones I have taken. He gives you the study guide to take notes on so you know exactly what you need to listen for during the lectures. He is a really caring guy that wants his students to succeed. I had to email him once because the TA's weren't helping me and he got back to me in less than 15 minutes. Great teacher

Dr. LeCheminant is great. He knows his stuff and he really respects the students. He makes learning fun and is always willing to answer questions or talk about things. Definitely a worthwhile class! The tests were a little specific, but that was a department thing

He is honestly so amazing. He is the best professor I have ever had. He understands that we are students with other classes, and that we are people with lives. I got sick and he helped me make it up and was amazing about letting me do tests late and turn my stuff in late because I was sick. He cares about us as students. He is truly the best.

This was Professor LeCheminant first time teaching HONRS101! His course topic was, "The Science of Obesity." He was an amazing professor and made sure important concepts were made known to my class. He was passionate and I never felt bored. What I learned in this class has helped me with my current classes. Wish I could have taken him for NDSF100.

The professor was really nice but everything had to go through his TA's before he would even see you. The class was too hard for what it was and the structure of his class was really unorganized. I usually do well in my classes, but this class kicked my butt.

My favorite professor I have ever had at BYU. He is so kind and humble and prepares you SO well for the tests. There is also an $8 PDF of the book you can buy online. If you're going to take nutrition 100, TAKE IT FROM HIM!!

He cares about the material and his students. The class was based on articles that we read and he presented on. Always latest evidence. Unbiased. You can feel the care he has for his students as he lectures.

He is very caring and will go out of his way to answer your questions. I asked him a question in class and later without even me prodding him to he somehow found my email in the class of over 100 and sent me a ton of useful resources on the topic. The expectations for tests are clearly laid out. Learning a lot from him and he is a good person.

My favorite professor this semester. His lectures are very informative and easy to follow. He lets you know what will and won't be on the exams while taking notes, but sometimes teaches a little fast-paced. Super willing to help and takes time outside of class to answer questions and put together really interesting power points. Take his class!

I took this professor for Obesity and Weight Management, but I liked him a lot more for Worksite Health Promotion. I learned a TON in this class. He is a fair grader for quizzes and even gives you some of the answers to the quiz before it starts! The exams aren't that bad either. I'm glad I was able to have him twice as a professor.

I felt like I didn't learn a lot from this class. I worked so hard and studied so much, but his tests were not clear and he is just really boring. Monotone and not fun to listen to. If you need to take a nap somewhere, his class will put you right to sleep.
Great teacher. Very fair. Wish he taught all EXSC courses.

Worksite Health Promotion with Dr. LeCheminant was one of my favorite classes so far. His lectures are very applicable to our professional careers, he brings employers in and discuss opportunities you should take advantage of. Basically the class is organized around his power points, quizzes every other week and the 3 exams during the semester.
Super helpful and caring about his students.   I would recommend taking this class to anyone!
This class is no fun.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He's so genuine and kind and willing to help with anything you need. You have to make sure and memorize important facts for tests, but it you study it's a pretty easy class. He makes sure to keep his classes interesting.

I thought he was an excellent professor! He really cares about his students and is very knowledgeable. He will go out of his way to give his students help and even brings in professionals in the field that offer advice in getting a job post-graduation.
One of the best professors I have ever had. If you go to class and pay attention you can get an A for sure. He's also an expert in the field and has some very valuable insight.

Excellent teacher! He did a great job at focusing on the important things. No busy work, just lectures, article reading, and a couple projects. Quizzes and tests were pretty straight-forward. Lots of practical application. I liked how he encouraged class discussion, so he wasn't the only one talking all the time.

This class was interesting at times, but he depended on the slides way too much. I like to write notes, but could never keep up. He thinks that all his students have time to memorize all of his slides. Attending class gets boring a lot of the time and I struggeled to stay awake since the lights were half off. WAY NICE though and very helpful.

Nice guy, ok class. Take class early in exercise science course work b/c otherwise the class will bore you. Pretty easy, but lots of group work. Tests are pretty sweet..he experiments with letting you use powerpoints & classmates, just classmates, or sometimes just your knowledge.

Exam-heavy course with poor structure. Flipped classroom required hours of low-quality, confusing lecture videos. In class quizzes became overly hard and hurt grades. Study guides didn't match exams, which made up most of the grade. We had to teach ourselves, and the professor didn't respond to emails or offer support. Very frustrating class.

Flipped format with unclear videos that did nothing to prepare us. Study guides were useless, and exams felt like mind games; you had to guess his exact wording (which wasn't taught). No TA support. The only reason students succeeded was by teaching ourselves on YouTube, not because of Dr. Moody. This class was a disappointing reflection of BYU.

He's has "flipped" curriculum where you watch video lectures outside of class and ask questions in class. Not super great imo. Didn't get the text and still got good scores. He graded on tests, iclicker, and small quizzes. he's clear on what you need to know and provides pretty good practice questions per chapter. responds fast regarding off. hrs.

Warning to future students. This semester and possibly future semesters, Moody stated that he will not curve the final grade (a final that is known to be horrific), every exam is cumulative, and he won't have TA reviews or TA hours. Idk about practice exams. It is as bad as it sounds. He seems nice but his policies and actions say otherwise.

Med student here. Just had a flashback of this class and felt the need to caution others about this class. Maybe he has changed, but this was an unnecessarily difficult class that very much felt like he was trying to get a curve instead of teach. I learned more about biochem studying on my own than from him. Take from someone else if you can.

One of the best biochemistry professors at byu. His tests are difficult, but fair. He teaches you everything you need to know for the tests, and gives you plenty of resources to help understand the material. His lectures are well paced and he really takes the time to ensure you understand the topic. Do not be afraid to ask Dr. Moody your questions.

This is one of the senior classes in the major but I was surprised how much I learned and how smooth the class went. His lectures clearly teach what is tested which is also very clear before exams. His recorded lectures make it really nice to go back and catch things you didn't get. He is one of the most patient lecturers I've seen!

Dr. Moody is by far one of the best chemistry professors at BYU. His teaching pace is not too fast, but he was still able to cover all the material. He provides very helpful study guides for each exam and grades fairly. He is passionate about biochem and clearly cares about his students. This class was a lot of work but he made it manageable.

Dr. Moody was excellent, his lectures were interesting and he is a nice guy who is very willing to help you succeed. That said, Biochem is HARD, there really isn't any way around this. I'd advise opening the study guides and filling them out as you go during lectures and reading. If you have those down you will do well on the tests.

Really great professor, I wish I could've taken him for all of my science classes. He's really nice and approachable. He teaches the difficult material really well, very knowledgable and answers everyones questions. Lectures, weekly hw, and study guides prepare you well. Homework is tough unless you find a study group!

Scored above 95 on all the exams, and then mine and the class avg on the final was 60%. He was unwilling to do anything except keep parroting "86% class average" which was what he curved to. In the end he admitted he and the TAs made many mistakes on exam grading but wouldn't fix them, so the curve wasn't accurate. TAs also take months to grade.

He couldn't write anything on the board without consulting his notes. We have to memorize it, but he doesn't. His free response was graded by "guess what magic words I want you to use." He had a 4th midterm the week before finals. I've never worked harder for mediocrity in my entire life. Doesn't teach to MCAT-way more in depth. Find someone else.

I was scoring anywhere from 80-90% on the tests and had an overall A- in the class. Final exam was more difficult than the mCAT. The average was 63%, high of 89. Other than the final I would say he is a good professor. Rewatching lectures was more helpful than the study guide (scored better on tests). Textbook not necessary.

Dr Moody is awesome. His class is very organized and he tells you exactly what you need to know (bullet point study guide before each exam). He is very good at clearly explaining difficult concepts. That being said, there is a TON of memorization and a good amount of application on the tests.

Felt like I had to teach myself twice the material we covered in class, cuz he tests more than what he covers in lecture. Got tested on things not directly covered in the study guide (that he lives by). I think he somewhat cares about students, but it seems like he is more concerned with a curve. MC tests were ridiculous. Take from someone else.

Dr. Moody is a great guy, caring, and very intelligent. What I didn't like about this class is it was geared to prepping you for the MCAT and not really learning chemistry. The multiple choice sections of the exams were ambiguous and did not truly test your understanding. I like to learn material and all he had me do was memorize.

Professor Moody was great. Was so worth taking an 8am class. The class was hard, similar to Ochem, because there was so much material, but he doesn't make it any harder than the department makes him. He gives study guides so you know what to study. He is EXTREMELY accessible outside of class. He obviously cares. His office hours are very helpful.
He is a great professor. His class should be easier than the Organic Chemistry Classes however it is still not too easy. Overall I would choose Dr. Moody 10x out of 10

Great guy, definitely serious in his desire to be a better professor. Homeworks were sometimes grueling but were basically graded based on completion by the end of the semester. His tests could be tricky and sometimes I walked out feeling like he didn't test my knowledge very well. With that said, with a lot of hard work, you can get an A.

Dr. Moody is an incredibly nice and humble professor. He is new- which can show, but he is super willing to learn and improve. The homeworks can be dumb / busy work, but the tests are pretty fair (but hard) Know the study guide. Dr. Moody is really smart & always willing to help. It's not as hard as ochem in my opinion, he makes it pretty simple!

Dr. Moody was fantastic. Biochem is dreaded by many students here at BYU due to the horrible professors that generally teach it. Dr. Moody was different. Incredibly caring, and made it clear the first day that he didnt want to steam roll us and he has been true to that. He has HORRIBLE TAs though! They took over a month to grade each exam.

Nicest guy. Brand new at teaching so he's learning. Wasted a TON of time in class so I feel like we didnt learn as much as other classes. Still, he taught very clear and will get better. A lot of people rated his class as hard but biochem is hard, not him. Our class average was 87 and the other professors was 75. Half the class got an A- or better.

Great teacher. He really cared about the students. Showed that by always respecting questions and trying to find what was best for us. He wanted us to succeed and do well in the class. Biochem class this semester was a fun atmosphere with him. It's biochem so it is hard but he has been my favorite chem professor at BYU

I really enjoyed his class. This was his first semester teaching so I was a little nervous. However, by far, the most understanding professor I have had so far at BYU. One thing that made the course more difficult was he did want you to understand the why or the reactions and relate them to other things, but in the end this was very helpful

Was a great teacher, even though it was his first year. I think he'll get even better in the future. If you don't like long tests, don't chose him- he feels that they should aim to be 3 hours long, all written. He cares a ton and is very willing to work with students if they struggle. Although it was a bit rough, I think he'll become BYU's best.

New professor, and sometimes it shows, but a really genuine and hilarious guy. Cares a lot about students and takes plenty of time in class to answer questions. Tests are difficult, but the study guides are really good. HW due each week, but its basically free points. Definitely more fair than typical BYU chem professors.

Dr. Moody is pretty cool. Just finished his own education, so he's brand new at teaching, and it shows. That said, he is reasonable and, honestly, kinda lovable. He really cares about students and he listens to their requests for changes. He uses quirky metaphors, but they work. Tests are long, but not awful. Lots of homework, but it's helpful.

Save yourself the trouble! This is an inherently frustrating class that he makes harder with 8 PM deadlines, arbitrary grading policies, and ineffective lectures. Dr. U is supremely stubborn and impossible to reason with. Surprisingly out of touch for his age, he will not make exceptions for students who make simple mistakes.

I do not recommend. While she chooses interesting content and knows her stuff, class discussions always devolve and confuse, and exams are unnecessarily hard (I've spoken to other students about this so it's not just me lol). I have found her to be inconsiderate and at times straight up unkind towards students in feedback and in meetings.

Here's the thing. She clearly knows her stuff and her passion is contagious, but she is quite simply mean. On multiple occasions, I have seen her make catty and condescending comments both in person and on essays as feedback. It's such a shame. If she weren't on a power trip or overdramatically stingy with points, it could be a favorite class!

Horrocks is a great person, but a very harsh grader. Her tests and quizzes ask for nit-picky and ultra specific details. I would not take her class again but I am glad that I had this experience. If I had the choice between her and a different professor, the latter is enticing.

I took this a little while ago and it was unnecessarily difficult. She is very nitpicky when grading assignments, taking off points for non-issues when the instructions themselves were unclear. Feedback is harsh and oftentimes ridiculous. The reading quizzes really took down my grade even though I only missed one day of reading the whole semester.

Expectations were never clear. Impossible to please her because she had no guidelines. Only graded assignments well if she personally liked the topic, disregarding textual evidence. Constantly told students in class their ideas were just wrong. Flippantly dismissed several students' concerns about grades in front of the class. Awful experience.

Took because a friend recommended her, what a mistake that was. She is vindictive and petty and she seems to really enjoy taking all of her repressed anger out on students in her feedback. I haven't had a professor who was so condescending and cruel like this before. Avoid avoid avoid!

We made paper, ink, printed and I really did enjoy it! However, Professor Horrocks is such a harsh grader. There are no rubrics for assignments so they are vague and a lot. There are reading quizzes almost every class and did some damage to my grade. There are also two tests and a giant paper for our final. Read everything and do not miss class.

Life is good if you're one of her favorites, and terrible if you aren't. Beyond that, she is easily the least understanding and flexible professor I've ever had. She doesn't care about your mental health at all, and insists you drop her class if you need even one-off extra support. Also, really rude in written feedback. Wouldn't recommend.

Professor Horrocks is a good professor and really engaging, but this class was very difficult! The three tests were very tough, and there were lots of homework and projects. The class discussions were super interesting, but I did not think it was worth it for the amount of effort I had to put into the class.

Professor Horrocks is amazing! I took 291 from a different professor and hated it, so I was dreading 292, but the way she taught was just fantastic! She's very organized and teaches author by author which was perfect for my brain. If you pay attention in class and take notes, you should do well on the tough exams. Class discussions were THE BEST!

I will always remember Professor Horrocks's amazing lectures. Seriously, the way she talks about history makes it seem like she's sharing drama from work; I couldn't get enough of it. The tests, however, were brutal.  She makes very clear study guides so that your studying will be to good use, but you will need to study lots.

Prof H wasn't my favorite teacher, but once I learned how she worked, class went a lot better for me. She's passionate about the subject, maybe too so for an entry-level class. However, before the first exam we met and I asked for help preparing. She listened, and we build a good relationship that helped me succeed in class. Very kind!

Polarizing professor. I think her high expectations, blunt humor, and pushback on students's opinions (regardless of whether or not she agrees) is off-putting for some people. I learned a ton from this class and feel like I grew as a writer because of her feedback on assignments. Cool lit. material. May not be for everyone, but I liked her a lot.

All other reviews aside, I loved this woman. Dr. Horrocks is insightful, incredibly funny, and a master at teaching. She takes time to learn names and use them in class. Her exams are tough and so is her grading, but she makes learning the literature fun and offers extra credit on all quizzes. She's become a favorite professor for me.

Dr. Horrocks really cares about the subject and it shows. Her lectures were very interesting despite what could have been stale material. The second half of the semester is definitely more enjoyable than the first half. Her tests are difficult, but if you put effort into studying you can do well.
Professor horrocks is really interesting in lectures, but this was an insanely difficult course. I really struggled with her criteria for writing and was just frustrated all semester long.

Looking for someone that cares about your success and will help you if you’re struggling? Find anyone else. 
She teaches class very well, but her lack of consideration to situations and their impact on student work was insulting. She will not bend her late policy, even due to extenuating circumstances. 
My advice? Find another 303 class.

The tests are hard and specific, but not terrible. You definitely need to take notes and do the readings. Daily quizzes (open book) The class itself was fine, but Dr Horrocks has a tendency to look down on people. She regularly makes people feel stupid if their answer isnt hers. Also, there were things on the test reviews that we didn't know.

Dr. Horrocks is an amazing teacher! I'm not the biggest fan of reading, but I often found myself enjoying the readings and loving her analysis of them. You'll have about 3 hours of reading each week, and you'll have to work for the tests (which are horribly long), but you really learn SO much!!

I hope everyone gets to take a class from Professor Horrocks because she is incredible! My favorite professor I have ever taken a class from, and genuinely cares about her students. I would go in after exams and she was happy to work through concepts and authors with me. She develops a very personal relationship with every student, and shows it.

Think of your worst elementary teacher. She is strict on tardies, phones, won't take HW unless it is printed out, has clear favorites, makes rude comments. Degrades students with mean comments/shame and finds power in it. Not understanding at all. Run while you can!

Professor Horrocks was one of the rudest people I have ever taken class from. She was extremely condescending. She was not understanding of students. If you would try and talk to her about something she's respond with "So what" or "Who cares"? She set extremely high expectations and then would shame students for stressing about them. Don't take!

I absolutely adore Professor Horrocks. After looking at her reviews, I was hesitant to take her until another English major told me that I should. She is one of the most amazing professors I have ever had! If you're looking for an easy A, don't take this class. However, if you're looking for engaging lectures and to learn a lot, she is awesome!

Prof. Horrocks really knows her stuff and overall has a lot of amazing teaching skills and fosters a lot of great discussion in class. But, over a third of reading and class discussion and homework questions were purely political and she definitely seemed to push some political agendas and were completely unrelated to literary theory or english.

I've never met a professor more like Harvey Dent (Two-faced) in my life. In class and in her office hours, she was always pumping us up about how well we were doing (later in the class she later started revealing favorites by showing their good work and the non-favorites bad work) and then in her critiques, she would totally tear apart your paper.

I took 292 from Dr. Horrocks a couple of years ago, and I had a much better experience this time around. She has VERY high expectations, meaning you will need to read your texts meticulously, participate, and study hard for tests. However, she also really cares about getting feedback and improving her classes. I would take from her again.

I had her for both 495 and 375. Both classes were a lot of reading and writing, so you will need to make her class a priority (taking two of her classes one semester was a mistake). In class discussions were a lot of fun, she was really respectful of the students and their opinions. But she was the hardest grader I've ever had. Still enjoyed class.

She's excellent! I loved her classes so much. She's engaging, and extremely caring. She gives all the tools to succeed, you just have to use them. She's passionate about her subjects and transmits this well to students. Work load is reasonable.

Very interesting class and teaching style. Unfortunately incredibly biased. Grades dropped the more she showed her disinterest in students who weren't English majors and often tells people the wrong things to write on papers so they will get marked down. No interpretation is correct unless it is her interpretation and same goes with opinions.

Her teaching style is very entertaining, and I was never bored. I always could pay attention. Her grading, however, is very difficult. She is very opinionated and you better write how she would see it. Very intelligent, witty, and she knows it. Insane amount of reading

I had Professor Horrocks for English 251 and 294. Her classes are quite challenging, but immensely fulfilling. She is a tough, fair grader, and always helpful if you seek her help outside of class. Her sense of humor is sharp as a tack but never personal or derogatory. I think some students dislike her because they don't understand her humor.
This miserable beep sure loves company.

Incredible! I took ENGL 251 from Dr. H too--classes with her are always very conversation heavy, so there's plenty of opportunity for students to participate and discuss. She's hilarious, engaging, and super personable, and she's a fair grader. There's a lot of reading to do, but it's an English class, so that's normal. My favorite teacher at BYU!

Prof. Horrocks is extremely rude. She sees things only her way and doesn't mind openly mocking students in class. I didn't learn a lot from her except that the English major was for me, because that's what this whole class was about -- why not to be an English major (no money in it, etc.).

Professor Horrocks is incredible! You will do a lot of reading in this class, but if you do the reading guides and go to class you'll learn an incredible amount. If you want a class that will prepare you for an English Major, take 251 from her. Keep an open mind and remember that you don't have to agree with every literary theory taught.

Professor Horrocks is a fabulous teacher--she isn't easy, but she is fabulous.  I have learned so much in this class and I recommend her to anyone wanting to major in English. She is also super laid back and fun to talk to, which can be nice when you are struggling and want to meet with her.

Horrocks was the worst professor I have ever had. She seemed to dislike me for petty and personal reasons. It was very unprofessional.  Her job is the only significant distraction in her life, and this makes her persnickety. She considers herself a true academic. I think she believes she is superior to all who do not share the same obsessions.

Respectable teacher. nothing to complain about. do the work and you'll get an A. her feedback will tell you everything you need to know to get an A. Assignments are blunt. follow instructions and you'll be fine.
She is praiseworthy... gotta hand it to her for finishing grad school.  #benicetoher

Prof. Horrocks was awesome. It's a class about different theorists so it may not be the most exciting class for some people. It was interesting! You have study guides for the readings that you turn in and that's basically the only hw besides 4 different essays. And then tests. She's awesome but she expects you to be adults so just be respectful.

Tests require close to verbatim recall of 1200+ pages  and ability to infer what any number of authors think about any given subject - to madame's satisfaction.  If you're open minded enough (or have the type of brain that can binge and purge copious levels of "he said, she said" without the book/s on hand, this class is easy as.
Super hard class, but I learned more than in any other class. She is one of BYU's best professors. Makes you read more than is reasonable though so balance this class with other lighter load classes.

Team-taught with Christianson. The class is supposed to be from about the 1600s-2000, but you can tell her favorite era is the Victorian -- you spend about half the class in it. There's a lot of reading (200pg every other night), and the tests are really hard at the start bc they don't tell you how to study.
I loved Professor Horrocks! She's funny and super passionate about literature (makes you want to be too). She is extremely willing to help you when you ask for it.
She's very clear. As long as you are willing to follow her directions closely and bring new insights to papers and discussions, you should be fine.

Prof Horrocks is really nice and gave a good introduction to the English major. I wasn't an English major but I still found a few helpful things in this class. For a one hour class, this had a lot of work! We had to go to a few things and write papers and there was a bit of reading. Do the extra credit and study for the daily quizzes.

Prof. Horrocks is the hardest and best professor I've had. It was a difficult course and the tests were intensive, but  I learned more in that class than any other. It prepared me for my future English courses and continues to impact how I study and work. If you go talk with her she offers great advice and genuinely cares.

I was very disappointed with Prof H. She seemed cool at first, boy was I wrong! She had a personal vendetta against me for no reason (talking to other students later, I found out they felt the same way)  She would shut down any comments that she didn't like. She was rude & inconsiderate. The tests are ridiculous. Save your time, don't taker her!!

Horrocks's version of 251 feels like a continuation of high school English.  Be prepared to go through a lot of printer paper-- she always requires clean copies of everything and asks you to turn in the same assignments more than once, each time costing more printing resources.
Prof. Horrocks is awesome! She was very helpful and was always respectful to students. I would take her again in a heartbeat!

Prof. Horrocks is the best! She is willing to help you out when you ask for it and cares for her students. There's lots of reading to do, and you have to write one page summaries for most, but it's beneficial for you. The exams are fair and overall this is a great class!
I thought she was brilliant! Very smart, very clear, super interesting. If you do the readings and come to class, you should do great! She is very helpful and easy to talk to during office hours.

There are 5 exams (not including the final), so it seems like you're back in the testing center every few weeks. Additionally, many of the exams end up using terminology that she knows, but we don't, so some of them can be somewhat hard to answer correctly because you don't understand the question being asked. Otherwise, it's a pretty easy class.

I would not recommend this class. I wanted to learn about Biology but she teaches about why science and god connects and which scriptures work with which science thingy. It's not biology. If you want to learn about Biology this is not the class for it. It's not too hard but do you want to pay for this though? Teacher is nice though.

This class is harder than a normal BIO 100 should be, and that's what the TA said, not just me. This class has 5 midterms. 

The tests don't even cover anything you learn in class, which was the disappointing part. It was always full of things she mentioned ONCE. If you do not go to the after-class study reviews, you're cooked. You will not pass.

Professor Jensen is an amazing teacher who really cares about helping her students learn and reconcile religion and science. Her lectures are engaging, and I loved that she took the time to answer every single question to the best of her ability. There is a lot of what feels like busy work, but the class overall was incredibly easy.

Dr. Jensen is a great teacher. Her lectures are super engaging and easy to understand. There's a lot of homework, but it's easy and helps you understand the material better. Her tests are all open-note. My only complaint is that her class was a little TOO easy, but I would definitely recommend.

Most of your grade comes from a book she has you make throughout the course. There was no rubric on any of the assignments, which made it hard to tell what level of depth was sufficient for assignments. The intro BIO-100 course heavily focused on religion in the context of biology. I wanted a biology course, but got a second religion class.

Dr. Jensen did an awesome job with the class and I really enjoyed it. Not going into med or science at all however, I was motivated in the class to do well. She did a lot of the class through canvas and allowed for credit to be given back from tests if you go into the lab for help. Shes pretty fair

I am not at all a science person, and this is one of my absolute favorite classes I have taken at BYU. She does what she can to help you succeed and knows most aren't science majors. Points for attending and extra credit for going to TA reviews. The final was tough, but that's the nature of the class. 100% recommend for your science general!

Maybe my favorite professor that I have had. She is very organized and if you do the HW and come to lecture you will be very prepared for her tests. She is SO engaging even though she teaches a huge group of students. I just wish that I could take more classes from her even though I am not studying biology.

Unless you already know the class content beforehand you won't do well. She expects students to understand super complex content after hardly even touching on it or not mentioning it at all. Super exam heavy without clear guidance on how or what to study for the exams.

Dr. Jensen is an engaging lecturer, and the class was very interesting! If you've taken AP biology this class will be manageable, but its pretty tough if you haven't. 

I was sorely dissappointed to find that a large portion of the final exam was material we had never addressed in class or lab. It dropped my grade froma solid A to an A-.

UNIV 216 with Dr. Jensen was SO GOOD!! 100% recommend if you just need a biology GE credit!! The class is based on simple biology topics with a lds religious aspect based on the book, "Let's Talk About Science and Religion" and other various articles! We created a book the whole semester about what we learned. (Bonus: there are NO tests!)

Go to office hours and it'll be way easier. Still challenging, just not impossible. She is a bit persnickety when it comes to grading, but it's usually because she wants a particular answer, and the TAs will tell you what that is. The lectures were engaging, but the labs will kick your butt - the homework attempt is due the next day.

This class was hard for no reason at all. You're taught the basics and are supposed to understand everything else. If you have a bad lab TA, you're screwed. The tests are all pure application so you need to understand everything, but you're not taught everything in lecture or lab as there's a gap between lecture and lab, which makes it harder.

I LOVED Professor Jensen's lectures and her. But this class was extremely hard for absolutely no reason. The TAs are great. The exam reviews were not helpful and were never before when the test opened. Questions on tests were so difficult. We did not practice the application she wanted on tests. If you are premed/dental, take cell 120 instead.

Dr. Jensen is very enthusiastic about what she teaches and I learned a lot from the class, but her tests are NOTHING like her learning outcomes or what she teaches in class. She teaches you at the most basic level and then tests you on higher-level applications that she has never had you think about.

She is not good. The is no structure to the course and it's impossible to prepare for exams. She "teaches" what she wants to but really, she just briefly mentions complex subjects without explaining them or helping her students understand the subject. Random questions appear on the exam that you've never heard of. Bad, take from different prof.

This supposed to be an easy class, but professor Jensen made it 100x harder than it needed to be. Quizzes were not entirely on her "learning outcomes," and the exams were so difficult. She even said she doesn't go along with the textbook we have for the class. She teaches and tests students on whatever she feels biology is all about. Avoid her!
Dr. Jensen is knowledgeable, but the class is disorganized. Exams don't align with lectures - extra studying is a must. However, unstuckstudy AI was a helpful study tool alongside the lecture notes.

This teacher would have a much higher score if her BIO100 class wasn't mostly freshmen. As a Junior, I loved her passion, engaging lectures, and openness to feedback. Tests were tough but fair. Freshmen, brace yourselves, BYU is tough. Upperclassmen will find this class fun and manageable.

This was one of the worst classes I have taken at BYU. Dr. Jensen is very knowledgeable about Biology and made this GE course WAY harder than it needed to be. I am a straight A student and struggled so much I ended with a B. I went in weekly to the reviews, did all of the hw and nothing helped. DO NOT TAKE! The course gets harder as it progresses.

Looked forward to lectures--dreaded the labs. I ended up finding a good lab group later on but man did they take a lot out of me--quizzes held at the beginning of every lab that you largely can't study for. Tests were hard. Attendance not mandatory but I never missed. TAs saved my life, I met with them once/often twice a week.
Super kind but very unorganized. Tests had nothing to do with what we learn in class. If you want to pay to learn bio on your own, take this teacher.

I loved Dr. Jensen! I thought I didn't like science but she made it so interesting and fun to learn. The only reason I didn't give her a 5 is because sometimes there was stuff on tests that we didn't cover or learn very well. But as long as you do the assignments, come to class, and take notes, it's not too hard to do well. TAs are also great.
Some sections do pre-class instead of homework, which was actually super cool. She understands that this is a general credit, and doesn't make you do much at all, really.

She's a really nice person but a tough professor. The course goes really fast with little to no reviewing. If you miss a day of class it could very well set you behind. If you love science and you have a knack for it, she might be a good professor for you. Exams are super tough and questions are not worded like anything you answer in class.

I did not like the reverse setup, you take canvas "quizzes" to learn the content which is then covered in class. I was not prepared at all for the final even though I thought I was. Took my grade from an a+ to a b+ (one percent away from an a :( ) Dr Jensen is a great person however I did not feel like I learned anything.

Very nice professor but the lectures/pre-class assignments don't prepare you for the exams, extra studying is a MUST. My biggest gripe with the class is that your submitted answers for the exams are hidden, meaning you can't review them on your own or with a TA. Prevents you from learning from your mistakes. Very frustrating.
I LOVED HER! She is SO organized and passionate. If you have to take Biology, take it from her

Dr. Jenson is sweet but not a great teacher. She uses a reverse format: learn on your own before class with a brief review the next day (Take good notes). Tests and finals are open note but feel like they are meant to trick you. I failed most, despite feeling confident. I wouldn't personally recommend her, especially for freshman students.

Mrs. Jensen is a really sweet person, but probably the worst professor I've had at BYU. Her lectures don't help at all, the class structure is horrible, and the tests are INSANELY hard. Take any other professor for this class, please. Oh btw, I had an A- in the class that went down to a B- because of the final.

The classroom was a flipped classroom so it was hard to understand the concepts because they were taught by yourself. Each test was online + you could use notes. But the final was in the testing center. Didn't feel prepared for the final test. She is really nice but wouldn't take again

She uses a flipped schedule and claims that it is the best way of learning - but, consistently in the lectures, I would overhear that no one would know what is going on. I also felt like the tests were meant to trick us... but that's just me. She is super nice, but her structure of teaching is not helpful. Not my fav!

The structure of the class is a flipped classroom, which I don't think was the best approach to this class. Her lectures weren't very helpful because they seemed completely disconnected from the homework. I felt like the tests were extremely application based, and the material leading up to exams did not prepare students for the exams.

Everything I learned in this class was from a peer, or learning it on my own. The T.A. labs are a help as well, but they don't understand the material that she gives us either. She is so confusing. Tests are open everything but google, but the final is completely closed note, how is that supposed to prepare me for the final? Don't Recommend.

She is very king and caring! Downfall to the class: what is taught in class and in the homework is extremely different from the material on the test. There are questions about different materials on the test that we were never taught about in class.

Dr. Jensen is a wonderful professor! Her lectures are informative and fun, and her class is very organized. There are very few assignments, just a few smaller projects throughout the semester, and weekly lab assignments which you can complete during lab. She has guided lecture notes, and the tests are fair and representative of what she teaches.

I love Dr. Jensen! She makes class fun and really shows that she cares about us. She is very good at relating science to real life and also connecting to religion. However, the tests are SO HARD. They take a long time

I was impressed since her very first email. Dr. Jensen is incredible! She is so organized and her grading criteria is clear and fair. I loved how many opportunities there were to do well in the class and how well-designed her tests are. She is passionate about the subject of biology and teaches it well. She has cool mom energy.

Dr. Jensen is awesome. She's focused on teaching you how to learn and think. She's heavy on application of principle instead of memorizing information. I thought she was a fantastic teacher. She knows her stuff and is super happy to share what she knows. She wants you to succeed. I'd definitely take a class from her again.

Dr. Jensen is an amazing professor and definitely one of my favorites to learn from! I still think about things I learned from her BIO100 class almost daily. There are a lot of pretty difficult exams taken in the testing center, but if you go to the TA reviews and take notes you'll be fine! She also allows you to use your notes on exams.

Dr. Jensen is very passionate. I learned a lot from this class and was excited to attend. The downfall is that what is taught in class and what is on the homework are not like the test. She is all about application based things so it is a little tricky to know what to study. The TA's are extremely helpful.

Dr. Jensen was such a nice and fun professor. I really appreciated that she understood that we were not biology majors and explained things in a way that was easy to understand and didn't get too far into details. Sometimes we had fun little activities. Tests are pretty easy and she drops a lot of low grades on assignments.
Very hard class but I'm just terrible at science. Jensen is a super awesome teacher though!!!!
Dr. Jensen is the best! Her lectures were super engaging and helpful, don't buy the textbook you don't need it! Study and do your assignments and an A is definitely manageable.

She's a nice person and she really knows her stuff. The material can be kind of hard, but all the exams are open note, and there's lots of extra credit. TAs are a life-saver if you're struggling. Don't be fooled by thinking this is an easy peasy GE, there's still a lot of hard things to learn, but it's managable. She's trying to make it fun.

She is a very caring teacher. She, however, did not prepare us for tests properly and it felt as if I was expected to learn things on my own. The homework that she gives us doesn't apply to the class lectures and also are not related to the many tests we have to take. If you take this class, prepare to be visiting the TAs a lot.

Don't take BIO 100 from her. I hated how there was no textbook and our homework assignments were random videos and readings. Lectures were hardly based on what we learned on the homework. Very test heavy as well, with 5 tests plus a midterm and a final, all in the Testing Center. She's a nice person, but not the best teacher.

Save yourself $70, don't buy the textbook: I never used it. Lectures move quickly, but you can learn all the material there. Definitely go to TA reviews and work with them on difficult concepts! Also use 'Learning Outcomes' as notes since that's what she bases tests off of. Hard class because you will need to study, but it's manageable.

Her class was a bit all over the place, and the constant homework was a bit much, but she really and truly gives you everything you need to succeed on her tests.  open note, test hints, gives points back post test.  She's hilarious, has so much passion for her work and honestly made me love a class I should have hated.  GO TO TA REVIEWS

Dr. Jensen is an amazing teacher. She knows how to lecture in an engaging way that breaks down difficult subjects. Far and away the most I have learned from a bio class. If you take it beware that the last test and final have a huge impact on your grade so do well on those, and use the TAs because they are awesome. Overall not too hard if you study

Dr. Jensen is a great professor! BIO 130 gets easier as you progress. Dr. Jensen is aware of this and makes the first test worth a lot less which is super nice (I got a C- on the first test and still got an A in the class). A lot of your grade comes from the labs too.
Make sure to study hard for the tests, do well on the labs, and you'll do great!

Dr. Jensen was an amazing teacher! Her lectures are very clear and she has such a fun personality. The exams can be a bit challenging but there are lots of reviews before them so it's not too bad. We cover so many interesting topics in this class. And most importantly, this class strengthened my testimony of the Gospel and my faith in our Creator!

I'm sure Dr. Jensen had good intentions for the BIO130 class I took from her, but it ended up being what I dreaded most every week. I felt like I learned next to nothing about biology- all she wanted to do was show off HER knowledge. The assignments felt like busy work 99% of the time, as did the labs. There was practically no structure or order.

Very knowledgable about Biology and a fun personality. She knows youre not a biology major if youre in BIO 100. Didn't really like the flipped classroom, but she is super fair in her grading. She drops your lowest homework scores, quiz scores, and one unit exam (not the final), which was super nice. All test are open note. I didnt study for any.

Dr Jensen is so great. She is always so full of energy and which helped me pay attention in class. Pay attention and note take in lectures and labs and you'll do pretty well. I didn't read a lot of the textbook but when I did it was helpful, j not 100% necessary if you understand the concepts. The tests are very comprehension and application based.

Not sure why Dr. Jensen gets such a bad rap, because she is a FANTASTIC professor. She really knows how to teach complex material and convey it in a way that's easy to understand. She is also super bubbly, kind and caring towards her students. One of my most favorite professors

Loved her class! I hate biology but she made it interesting and applicable to my life. I liked the way her class was formatted, it was really focused on helping us to learn and apply, rather than just memorizing things. Definitely find a good group to work with in class, study hard for the exams, and you'll have an easy A. Great professor!!!

I really enjoyed this class because it was a different format from most of my generals. She didn't just lecture the whole time; we got to do activities. The tests were very application-based, and they weren't weighted very heavily. So if you do the homework and come to class, you'll be fine. The evolution unit was really cool and well explained.

Dr. Jensen is the coolest person! I had a flipped class where I learned the material on canvas before class and learned further in class. Make friends in this class so you have partners when going through in class assignments. Make sure to ask questions and become familiar with the TAs. Go to TA reviews to get an added 5% on exams!

Dr. Jensen is really nice, but girl doesn't know how to teach. On daily quizzes you can just get the answers aka copy and paste them because they are given in the next questions you read afterwards. So, you don't learn . The monthly exams are open book but she asks things that you never went over.
Super enthusiastic about the subject and writes great tests. But you will have to work for your grade.

Really nice teacher. Compared to other Bio100 teachers, Jensen assigns A LOT less homework, only takes about 25 minutes each day. The issue is, it means that you're not really prepared for the open note tests, which are really hard. Overall, her class was pretty confusing, but the grading system really favors students so your grade will be fine.
Hardest and most confusing biology course I have ever done. I wish there was a textbook and not random readings and assignments.

I honestly would not recommend taking this class from Dr. Jensen. I met with lots of tutors and all had no clue what we were doing in this class. She is really nice and tries to engage with her students which is nice but the content that she teaches doesn't make a ton of sense and wasn't great.

Jensen is honestly one of the most amazing professors I have ever had. I loved her class so much that I later became her TA. She teaches clearly and inspirationally and clearly shows her love for students. She wants you to succeed and gives you every opportunity to get good grades. She is especially good at reconciling evolution and religion.

Loved this class. Dr. Jensen is awesome. TAs were super helpful. 5 exams, but they are online and open note. Final is in the testing center. Before each class period we have a homework assignment, but they're always doable. I was worried bout taking this class since science is not my strong suit, but I got an A without too much stress.

If you are a traditional learner exiting high school, do not take this class. She provides no textbook, only certain "helpful readings" that do not explain things to the detail. Tests are hard, very application based learning. It is not simple repetition of definitions. If you are looking to get a GE out of the way, and don't like bio, do not take.

Lectures are amazing and Jensen knows how to teach and respect so many people at once! One hw assignment a week from lab, but don't fall behind in reading. Super easy to reach and willing to work things out with students

I don't like to be dramatic, but Dr. Jensen changed my life and major. She taught this class in such an enthusiastic and informative way. I looked forward to lectures every day because I knew I would learn something fascinating. She also built my testimony by helping me reconcile evolution and religion and now I feel so comfortable with it!

Professor Jensen was really sweet. For a college course, this class was relatively easy. Help was always provided if needed and I loved professor Jensen's passion for the relationship between religion and science. You just need to show up and do the homework if you want to pass. She doesn't even require memorization, we used notes on everything.

Doctor Jenson is the worst teacher I have ever learned under. She doesn't teach you anything in class and expects you to learn on your own. Encourages students to google homework answers. Especially rough in her numerous tests as she often tests on things you were supposed to "learn yourself" but didn't because she gave no indication you needed to.

I really enjoyed this class. Professor Jensen is organized and I had plenty of help understanding everything. She doesn't require a ton, she doesn't even make you memorize vocab. all you need to know are the concepts.

Professor Jensen is a great teacher! Lectures were interesting, and the homework wasn't too hard. There are several tests every couple of weeks, but they're generally short and multiple choice. I learned a lot and I'd definitely take it again!
This class was basically mormon myth busting in biology. As long as you did the work it was an easy A. I had it almost entirely online too.
I took the on demand online class, she explained things great. Diffidently combines religion and science really well. I felt like the lectures were worthwhile.

Every week is the same. You have two to three homework assignments that take forever to complete every two weeks; you have a test. The test wasn't too hard if you really study the homework. It was just a lot of busywork

She is very passionate about biology and wants all her students to succeed. But the amount of work required in this class is waaaay too much for someone who is taking a full schedule with other tough classes.
Super sweet and kind to all. LGBTQ+ friendly. There is a lot of work involved in the class, but I was always engaged and excited to learn!

I loved Dr. Jensen! She is seriously the best and such a great teacher and inspiration. She truly cares about her students and I always found her lectures interesting. In BIO130, your lab is only with your lab TA, so it helps to have a good relationship with them. With covid though, we had lots of online homework outside of class.

This was the worst professor I've ever taken. Half of the material on the tests were never covered in class, and the textbook was not helpful in that regard. Very tedious and undescriptive homework assignments and extremely hard tests led many students to fail the class. If there are any other professors available, take them instead.

Rather than route memorization, she makes sure you understand every concept so well you can explain it to others. This is SUPER IMPORTANT for tests because you need to know your stuff.
