Dr. Martin had wonderful lectures and group discussions. Papers and projects were different. She was very strict on grading, and was not open to talk about them after. Somehow a mistake was made in my study log, but she wouldn't even look at my study journal to confirm the mistake. Lectures are good, but not worth it to take from her.

For real this class was tough. For a two credit religion class, it required a lot of my time. The lectures aren't very academic and she is a tough grader. Whether or not you are studying religion, I wouldn't recommend this class. This sounds harsh, but Jan Martin embodies everything wrong with religion classes at BYU: too hard & not a lot of value.

Dr. Martin was a very kind teacher. She clearly cared for her students. There was no tests at all!! However, you are meticulously graded on papers and projects. If you are one that does not test very well, then I would highly recommend her!

Dr. Martin is a very nice person and takes the time to get to know her students. She is a tough grader and makes it difficult to get high scores on her assignments. She doesn't have any tests, but her assignments take longer than studying for a test would and your scores are usually lower.

Dr Martin is a great person but I wouldn't take a class from her again. On top of classes that matter, I don't need a religion class that's going to make me struggle to get an A. You fill out a log for your own attendance and scripture study(which you have to do every day and is worth 40% of your grade) 2 paper, 1 projects, 2 parts to the final.

She does a good job of creating a discussion based class, focusing more on the doctrine of the book of mormon rather than just memorizing it, as well as gospel applications. She is a very tough grader and will hand out assignments that are extremely rigid and every mistake will cost you a lot of points. Not worth it in my opinion.

Take this class if: 1) You like difficult assignments that aren't centered on the main material. 2) You don't like tests. 3) You like subjective grading. 4) You like reading multiple pages of instruction for each page of assignment. She's nice and knowledgeable. Some people can jump through the hoops in this class, but others just can't.

Dr. Martin almost seems overqualified to teach a Book of Mormon class. She is incredibly educated and I loved getting to see the scriptures from an actual historian's perspective. No test, just projects that are very doable. Take this class!

I have never felt more cared for by a Professor. Sister Martin is an absolute blessing and truly cares about her students. She takes the time to know your name. There's one big paper and a couple projects. She's extremely clear about her expectations and will take the time to help you so utilize it! Her classes are spiritually uplifting too.

I loved Sister Martin. She grades your papers and projects pretty hard. But I felt the spirit every class and learned a lot about the Savior, but also about myself. I would definitely recommend Sister Martin every time. She doesn't have a single test or quiz.

I've taken ALL of Sister Martin's classes and gotten an A in all of them. Almost all of your points come from attendance and scripture study, which you keep track of. No tests. The final wasn't a test, we just analyzed other people's projects. There are a few projects, but she outlines exactly how to get an A

Sister Martin is awesome! I don't know why there are so many negatives scores on here! I have taken two classes from her and both were awesome! This is exactly what a religion class should be! all you have to do is study every day for 30 min (its a big part of your grade), write 2 easy papers, and a change poster instead of a final. Seriously great
nice lectures, worst grader!! dont take her for an A!!
interesting class and lectures. hard grader. If you're looking for an A, dont take her. hardest assignments ever. I regret taking her class
WORST TEACHER EVER!! hardest grader ever. dont take her

Professor Martin is exactly how a religion teacher should be. Show up to class, do a self-change project, and read your scriptures everyday and you will get an A! She has no tests and the purpose of class is for personal growth. At the beginning of the semester she asks what you want to learn and then incorporates that information into her lessons.

I liked how the class was set up. There is no midterm or final, and there aren't any tests, all the information she presents is applicable to daily life, so that's her focus of the class. If you don't want to read your scriptures for 30 minutes a day, though, don't take this class, it's a huge part of the final grade. No grade curving or ex credit

I absolutely loved taking Book of Mormon with Professor Martin! She goes out of her way to learn your name and make you feel included in the lecture. Her discussions are thought provoking and she is always willing to help you outside of class. The main grades are attendance, reading and writing. Do the work (it's not that hard) and you will pass!

She was an ok professor. I didn't think the lectures were that interesting and I felt like she had an "I know everything" attitude. She grades pretty hard and I felt like she wasn't open to my way of thinking.
Very interesting lectures. No final exam but big activity. Daily Scripture reading for 30 min and attendance are required.

She knows her stuff when it comes to the Book of Mormon, yes. But multiple times we talked about speculations that are inappropriate. Does it really matter where the Nephites MIGHT have landed? No. The grading is too hard and if you're sick one day? Forget about that A because attendance and reading are such strict requirements you can't miss once.

Looking for a quality religion class at BYU? Don't sign up for Book of Mormon from Professor Martin. The classes aren't very spiritual or meaningful, the lessons include so many non-official doctrines, and the grading is extremely vague.  However, if you're looking for a class that teaches you where the Nephites PROBABLY landed then sign right up.

I loved Sister Martin's classes, they were the highlight of my week! She really knows her doctrine and taught in such a way that you could understand it and feel inspired. There are no tests, but it's on you to do the reading otherwise that will greatly damage your grade. She is a tough grader, which was frustrating, but the lectures are worth it.

Every time I go into Dr. Martin's class, I am uplifted. She has amazing insights and a great way of teaching. She doesn't get too involved with how you should study your scriptures, just that you need to be studying which I loved. She doesn't have exams, just projects that invite you to live the Gospel more precisely which is another thing I loved.

She is the best! One of my favorite classes, always very aware of what students need and willing to go out of the way to help individuals. Just be sure that you read the syllabus carefully because her grading scale is different.

Loved Sister Martin. No tests, just two big projects and reading your scriptures everyday. The final is a poster board project that details a past project. You are graded on attendance. Very inspiring class, she knows her stuff and is very respectful to comments. Highly recommend taking from her!!

Sister Martin was a real treat! There are a lot of interesting, open discussions about the material and she really knows her stuff! Super nice and compassionate. The few papers we did have were easy and very subjective and you can gain a lot from them!   I am taking another class from her next semester if that says anything.

Probably one of the most insightful and instructive classes I've ever had. She REALLY knows what she's talking about and really does a good job of applying the scriptures to our lives. Super insightful and very accessible. Has two major projects but no tests. Ten out of ten, would take again if I could.

Absolutely loved class with her. You need to be totally responsible for your own action but my goodness you get so much from the class!  I love the woman! SH knows the doctrine of Christ so well and teaches it clearly. She is direct and respects her students seen if they disagree with her. Very powerful teacher and worked one-on-one with me! 3

Thirty minutes reading daily. About two papers and a major, two week project. (I spent about thirty minutes a day on that project.) Very inspirational lectures; she focuses mainly on doctrine and its personal application, making for a fresh religion class.

I love love love Sister Martin. She doesn't give too much work, but expects you to read everyday and come to class. She doesn't even give tests, she has two papers and a final project. Pretty easy, but I learned so much at the same time. BEST TEACHER.
Fabulous.  She knows her stuff and cares about every student.

She is willing to help and answer questions. Her lectures are good but usually drag out. She pounds application on you rather than just teaching doctrine and letting you decide what you're going to do with it. A lot of work for a 100 level class and only two credits, but you will learn some cool stuff.

Super pretentious & very unhelpful. You need a 95% to get an A. Do NOT take this class.  I came in at the end of the semester with a 94.96% so I emailed her to see if I could get any help. In response I received a 5 paragraph essay, from prof. Martin, telling me how prideful and stupid I was for asking. Her grading scale is super tough.

Dr. Martin is a great teacher! She encourages participation and her lectures/discussions are really great! I could really feel the Spirit in that class a lot. There are no tests, which is nice, but there are papers instead. Those are difficult to do well on but be descriptive and clear and you'll be fine. Also, you MUST do your scripture study!

Dr. Martin gives excellent lectures BUT she is an extremely harsh grader on the paper and both projects. She expects students to know as much as her on Gospel topics when writing the paper, and she grades like its a writing class. If you want an A you have to blow her out of the water with your Gospel knowledge and research.

I LOVED sister Martin's class. This class is not really focus on the details on the Book of Mormon but the doctrines. Most of times I learned the doctrines I never knew were there. I learned A LOT. So there is no mid-term& final test. 2 essays. You choose your essay topics. Not a hard class if you are willing to work.

Outrageous grading scale. According to our class statistics only about 15-20% of the class ended with an A. For a two credit class the workload is insane. Grading criteria is vague. By doing everything her prompts ask you to do, you will get a B. She wants you to WOW her.

Doctor Martin is an amazing teacher! She does not give tests, instead there are a couple long papers. But if you do not procrastinate them then you will be fine with them. She really wants her students to understand the material and her lectures are amazing. She knows what she is talking about and encourages class participation. Take her class!

This has been the worst class I've ever taken at BYU. It was cool that she doesn't do any tests, but she rains down on you with a few 8+ page papers which she grades vary harshly. In our class statistics only 8 students out of 54  ever got an A on any given assignment. I don't think she ever figured out it was a 2 credit class?.. Don't take!

Dr. Martin is an excellent professor. She teaches the doctrine really well but also makes her lectures spiritual and fun to attend. There were no midterms and no final, but she had us write a research paper and do some other assignments that were graded pretty hard. Overall though, great course, great professor.

Sister Martin is more of an English teacher than a religion teacher. She makes you write a 2,500-word essay and another even longer essay. It is ridiculously hard for being a Book of Mormon class. Only take this class if you are a really good writer. She also does not explain her assignments well unless you go and ask for help.

There were no tests, only two very lengthy writing assignments, one of which was a 2500 word research paper. Thus, lectures seemed pointless except for the participation points. The required daily scripture study is a bit ridiculous too. You can get a lot out of her class, but if you are looking for an easy A, keep looking.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.  Way too much work for a two credit class.  Her lectures are alright, but her class demands way too much of your time, and her grade scale is tough. You'll spend 3 times as much time working out of class as in class. If you have a part time job, and an otherwise full class workload you will not get an A and still get sleep.

I absolutely loved Sis. Martin and her lessons.  Classes didn't feel like lectures.  Taught concepts instead of storyline but always made sure you understood the storyline and how it fit in.  She knew all the students by name.  If you needed help you could go in after class and she was more than willing to assist and help.  Loved her. Would take 2.

to be honest way too much work for a 2 credit class. I wish I had found a different teacher because she seems to be confused in the fact that she isn't teaching an English class when it comes to grading her essays and her personal study requirement is a little over the top.

lectures are super spiritual, and tests are open scripture(easy). you do have to write a few two page papers on a scripture you read, and how you applied it, but overall its super easy. she is super nit picky on the formatting though. I had Merrill the semester previous, and this class was WAY easier. I got A's in both, but tests were so mucheasier

I love Sister Martin.  She is so qwerky and I love her personality.  I felt the Spirit countless times in her class and she is there for her students.  However, I actively participated and met with her outside of class and she never knew my name.  Also, be prepared to memorize A LOT of quotes and random church history facts.  No study guides either

Professor Martin is wonderful! But this is not an easy A. If you get an A, you earned it by attending class, taking good notes, having quality DAILY scripture study and following the instructions for assignments PRECISELY. It's all laid out though, so look at the syllabus and if you don't think you can do it, then don't. I learned SO MUCH.

I love Dr. Martin. Seriously, she is so amazing you walk away from class having something new or a new perspective about the gospel. She knows her stuff and is super spiritual. Only 5 two page assignments. Reading and attendance is your grade. Come to class. Read EVERY NIGHT.  Read the quotes for the tests. And you will get an A!!
Sister Martin is a moving target. She tells you something in class but if you email her for clarifications then tells you something else. She should be an English teacher and not a religion teacher.

Sister Martin is an amazing teacher! She teaches the concepts rather than the storyline. Classes are discussion based and rely on the concepts on the chapter and different prophet quotes that she has. Because class is once a week reading is extensive but the class is amazing! I highly recommend it to those truly interested in   the gospel.

Easy class! If you are an english major who loves writing (& is great at it too). This is also a great class if you can control revelation, don't mind doing assignmentsreading 7 days a week & like memorizing quotes. She always changes her mind so don't trust what she says in class. To top things off the study guides are completely useless.

I love Dr. Martin!! She seems to care about her students. I love the direction that she takes her lectures and explores new things about the gospel that you might not have thought about before. A few assignments here and there but nothing too hard. The tests actually cover what she teaches in class.

This class is relatively easy. You are graded on your attendance and scripture study, so make sure to do both! She really clarifies a lot of confusing doctrine. She is kind enough to test on what we actually talked about in class, not just what was on the syllabus. That was great.
Very easy class. I expected it to be very difficult but as long as you show up and take notes it is exceptionally easy.
Professor Greenhalgh wants us to appreciate family history and how applicable it is to our everyday lives. She's a really great professor

Sister Greenhalgh is a professional genealogist and is well suited to teach the class! She really cares about her students and provides great opportunities to make the projects meaningful for each student. The only reason not to get an A is not showing up or doing the work (you can re-submit assignments if you miss points). An ideal religion class.

Professor Greenhalgh is the BEST. I wish everyone at BYU was able to take HIST 205 with her. This class gave me a passion for family history. She is very caring on an individual level. Her assignments are clear and her classes are spirit-filled and energetic. One of the best professors I've ever had.

It's pronounced "Green Ouch," you're welcome. She is awesome and has a clear passion for family history work. I was not really into that topic at all, I just wanted it to double count for GEs, but she helped me see not only why it's important, but also how to work the FamilySearch magic. You'll do a few projects and but it's not bad at all.

Cannot recommend her enough!!! Love love loved her and her class and I was able to learn so much about how to do family history. If you are remotely interested in doing fam history and you need an elective religion credit, TAKE THIS CLASS!! She genuinely cares about her students and if you show up to class and do the assignments you'll get an A.

Professor Greenhalgh is such an amazing human! I was nervous to take this class incase I would be bored or if it would be too hard but P. Greenhalgh is the kindest lady and guides everyone at a good pace no matter your family history level. I have learned alot and found is so worthwhile since we got to research our own family. Highly recommend!

Professor Greenhalgh is an amazing person who is probably one of the best genologists in the world. This class helped spark my fire for family history, and honestly, the assignments didn't even feel like work. Each week, there is an assignment due that is focused on a research family. One exam and final presentation that were a walk in the park.

Take this class if you want an easy religion credit. She paces the work well and there are simple weekly readings with discussion boards. You will be researching the same family in your family tree all semester so choose a good one! Prepare to spend at least 3 hours on the most intense steps of the project. One class presentation. One final exam.

This class was one of the best religion classes I took at BYU. Sister Greenahalgh really cares about her students and family history. It was a great intro to family history and felt like meaningful material. The workload for this class was significantly lower than most religion classes at BYU. No midterm, simple final. I would recommend.

Professor Greenhalgh is passionate about family history. Class time is only spent reading from a slide show you can access on LearningSuite immediately after class, so, every class felt like unwise use of my time. The content of the class could have been easily self-taught through common sense, I felt bored and idle every class period.

Super kind! Just a super boring class. She holds such a great passion for this but unless you enjoy family history don't take this class. You feel guilty for being bored, and even more spiritual guilt because you are dealing with your family's history. I did all the assignments and scored high in the class but was still so bored of the information.

This is a great class! She is so nice! you have a discussion board due monday and a longer assignment due wednesday!  This class is not a religion class you can do nothing though, family history is time consuming! That being said, she is so understanding and helpful, if you try you will get an A.

This was a really great way to get religion credit and do family history! There is a pretty good amount of homework, but it's not challenging. Professor Greenhalgh is super fun and brings food to class and keeps lectures fun and interesting.

Dr. Greenhalgh knows her stuff about family history and is super passionate about it. You do a big research project throughout the semester on a family in your tree and she basically walks you through every step. There are a lot of tedious assignments that are easy to miss, so check LS often for due dates. Easy religion credit and so rewarding!

Amazing!! She knows what she's doing. Incredibly understanding teacher, she just wants students to connect to their ancestors. Very educational class, and with a new perspective on family history (cross-generational love, instead of old handwriting). She literally just wants to teach people the tools to find their families, love, and connection.

25 hours of a research project you do not have time to do, because there are so many "mini" assignments. 3 hours of indexing. On zoom, if you are late, leave early, or have your camera off at all, you are marked absent. Don't take family history during a spring/summer if you can help it. Good info. Learned what I wanted. Horrible amount of work.
Box wont working

I enjoyed this class a lot more than I thought I would. Lots of material but I primarily focused on what's on the study guide and did just fine in the class. She makes a weekly 10-15 minute recording and tells you exactly what to focus on for exams. She really cares about the material and I genuinely learned a lot! She also provides lots of EC ops

I wouldn't take a class from her again. She is very politically motivated, and spins everything her way. She puts a huge emphasis on feminism. Lots of surprises on her tests and she doesn't do a great job preparing you for it. There's lots of extra information that isn't on the test. Not the type of teacher you would expect at BYU.

I took this class in my last semester so I could simply graduate but was not prepared for the essays and readings which are a lot. Also, don't use AI for anything because she will automatically give you a zero based off a flawed AI flagging system and you will fail the class. Other than that, if you enjoy humanities, this is a great class for you.

One of the best teachers ever, so caring and passionate. If you go to the TA reviews before exams, you will do great. Always do the extra credit because she gives a lot. She makes it super easy to get an A.

Dr. Hinckley is unafraid of connecting historical topics to current events, and makes her American values and beliefs clear. Avoid taking her classes if you are afraid of thinking critically or confronting your own values in ways that might make you uncomfortable. She's willing to work with you if you need help. Long may reign Queen Jane reign!

I really liked Dr. Hinckley as a person, and I feel like she gave us lots of extra credit. I didn't buy the textbook and it worked out. There's lots of assignments every week, just blast through them and study the quizlet, music, and what she tells you to in the recordings. The papers were annoying, and sometimes my TA was too.

Would tell you NOT to take this class. Take any other GE. So much to study. Expect to memorize random facts, not the history. The test questions come from a question bank, so she isn't even in control of what questions you get on the test. Humanities is about the study of what makes us human, this class is a bad blend of art and music history.

Dr Hinckley did a phenomenal job of meshing a wide berth of historical context, various types of literature, and sharing interesting stories to make the material engaging. The lectures were well organized and she shared meaningful personal perspcetives. The cultural events were valuable. I learned a ton from her about culture and life in general.

I enjoyed this class and didn't find it particularly difficult.  There were three midterms and three midterm papers, so on top of the assignments that were due weekly, this class was pretty time-consuming.  The content was super interesting though and I'm glad I took the class.

I took IHUM 202 online with Dr. Hinckley and you should too. The class claims it's not 100% memorization but it is. If you memorize the art and music you will get an A. Also pay attention to the test reviews and weekly videos. I watched them all twice and otherwise wouldn't have gotten an A.

I took this online and it was just a ton of busy work. It wasn't hard but it was time consuming. There were 3 tests, 3 papers and a bunch small assignments. It's really hard to get a hold of the TA and teacher if you need them. Tests took forever but weren't hard. Just another stupid GE you have to take for BYU.

This review is more for the class than professor because I took it online. If you are hoping it will be like her in person class it is not, but she does provide weekly video recaps to go over info for exams. 3 exams, 3 papers, and a ton of little assignments. Do not take online/in a term unless you are ready to work because its a semester load

Professor Hinckley has remained my all-time favorite professor I had while at BYU. She cares so much about her students and the class material. I simply took this class for a GE requirement and began with a mere curiosity about other cultures and art and left being fascinated by them. There's definitely some reading, but it will help you in class.

Professor Hinckley was probably my favorite professor that I ever had while at BYU. I took this course for a GE, but ended up being so inspired by what was taught. I had a curiosity of other cultures and art before this course, but after, I found myself fascinated with them. Take this course!

My favorite GE class at all of BYU. It was also my last GE before I graduate. If you can get in the class take it! the test reviews are exactly what will be on the test. She wants you to do well in the class. If you dont get an easy A in the class it is all on you. She is the best.

I Hum 202 w Queen Jane is incredibly organized. It goes extremely fast for spring/summer, but that is expected. The quizlets she creates are so helpful for doing well on exams! There are three papers, three exams. The study guides she creates are everything!

1. only way to survive on tests is to go to TA reviews.Queen Jane teaches you absolutely nothing useful love her to death tho. 2. three papers + rewrite and extra credit available. if you do the papers (go to research and writing center for extra credit on them) and the rewrite you'll do great. 
3. class is pointless EXCEPT for the attendance quiz
Very willing to work with you. Put in the bare minimum and you will succeed!

Queen Jane is the best! She is so sweet and learned all of our names. The reading isn't bad and every class has a writing quiz (mostly for attendance). There are 3 papers and lots of extra credit. The tests are not bad if you attend the TA reviews. Queen Jane's lectures are interesting and I really enjoyed taking this class from her!

Dr. Hinckley is so sweet, accommodating, and loving. I HATE generals at BYU and she couldn't have made it any more enjoyable. She's super chill and understanding of the fact that college students are human. She's awesome, would definitely recommend taking a class from her.

I loved this class with Prof Hinckley. Her lectures were really fun and interesting and she gives you everything to succeed. If you put the effort in and do your best on the papers and projects as well as pay attention to class and the readings, you will be just fine in the class. There are also plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Queen Jane seemed very intimidating and I thought it was going to be the worst class. However, she cares so much about her students and just wants them to succeed and does anything to help. She memorized each student's name and even said hi to me at the grocery store. I still am not a fan of IHUM but she is the best teacher I've had at BYU.

I wouldn't recommend taking this professor to anyone. The lectures are extremely boring and monotone with little to no participation from the class, but you need to be there because of the in-class quizzes. The tests are extremely long, and only way to prepare for them is by going to the review because taking notes in class doesn't help at all.

Queen Jane's class was by far my favorite class last semester! Her lectures are amazing and pretty straightforward, and the material was super interesting. The only things that I didn't like were the tests. There were 3 tests, and each had around 200 mc questions. Other than that, it's an easy A because of all of the extra credit opportunities.

I took the online version of the class and her class was easily one of the most organized online classes Ive taken. Her tests are very straightforward and she doesnt try to trick you with any of the options. If you pay attention in class and fill out the study guides you will not have a problem. The lectures were enjoyable as well.

I took the online course and it was pretty brutal. Proff. Hinckley doesn't actually give a single lecture, she just sends out reminder emails. The course was not even run by her. You have to get all the information on your own without lectures which means its up to you to determine what is important and what is not. Tests are difficult.

I struggle with humanities and online classes, but I really enjoyed this one. Dr. H makes quizlets for the paintings and architecture you need to recognize for tests. There was a lot of reading but there always is for humanities, and most of this material is super interesting. I learned so much. Also she extended a few deadlines when I got COVID.

Canvas is confusing. No lectures makes it very hard to keep up on the material. Some weeks there is almost 300 pages of reading assigned. There are 3 papers and the tests are insanely long and very specific. I put SOO much time and effort into this class. In the end my grade was fine and we get to redo an essay. You learn all on your own by reading

I truly love everything I learned. The problem is that she assigns a lot of reading from the book, and then other books like Odyssee. This is a full 4 credit organized class with more to do than just reading. Cool glasses, beautiful person, and full of knowledge. If you love humanities, you will end knowing the coolest things about the past. GLuck!

I'm not a humanities person and find it hard to analyze music and art. Prof Hinckley made this class enjoyable and I actually looked forward to what we were learning about next. This class is the best set up online class I've ever taken. Lots of reading but easy assignments and papers aren't too bad. Exams are easy and study guides are lifesavers.

I actually did learn a lot in this class. The reason why I am rating it so low is because it is total overkill for an intro-level course. Be prepared for things like 100 pages of required textbook reading in a week, test questions on really obscure quotes, and essays due the same time as the exams. Good luck!

Queen Jane is the most caring and loving professor I've had. She really knows humanities and her lectures were fun and engaging. 3 papers, but they were fun to write. Tests were long, about 300 questions (all mc and matching), but she prepares you well for them. She is the sweetest and funniest professor. 10/10 would recommend.

Queen Jane is amazing! The tests were long (130 questions about) but she really prepares you well for them. There were daily quizzes at the end of class depending on it we finished the lecture or not. There were four cultural event write ups and three 3 page papers. Queen Jane really cares about her students and is willing to help out of class.

Queen Jane - as she refers to herself - is an amazing professor. Very understanding and flexible. Understands not everyone is interested in humanities, but does a great job of explaining the importance of art and music. She does a great job making the class relevant. I would highly recommend taking IHUM 202 from her.
Queen Jane was a fantastic teacher. I had her for both IHUM 201 and 202 and she was great. Easy A, just do the work she assigns and you'll do great.

She is the best!!! She is very caring and wants each student to succeed in her class! She gives amazing lectures and knows everything there is to know about humanities. The tests can be challenging, so do the reading and study! I would highly recommend her for humanities.

Professor Hinckley (or "Queen Jane" as she is sometimes called) is everything a teacher should be. She's passionate about what she teaches, gives great lectures, doesn't assign busywork, and she's absolutely hilarious. This class is easy to pass if you do the readings and study for tests. Daily quizzes aren't hard. Can't recommend this prof enough!

I took this during spring and it was not bad at all. Theres a quiz every class but she usually gave a lot of freebies and if not if you do the readings, you know the answer. the projects and tests were easy as well! gotta study and make flash cards but definitely easy to get an A

Prof. Hinckley is a great teacher. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches and displays a deep amount of care towards her students. She saw me working on campus once and came to talk to me about school/life. The tests were somewhat long but studying slides and memorizing the names of artifacts/artworks/buildings will help you pass.

She assigns a lot of reading, but that's pretty normal for a humanities class. Her lectures weren't always super interesting, but she has a good attitude about it and tries to make it fun. The tests were mostly memorization of paintings and art and were kind of long, so a few hours of cramming beforehand really helped.

Dr. Hinckley is a PHENOMENAL woman and teacher!! She has such a passion for the humanities and in turn made me want to learn and appreciate art too.. She knows her stuff and could answer any question we had. Classes were engaging and she wasted no time in teaching as much material as possible. We had 2 cultural events, 1 paper, and daily quizzes.
She's a harsh grader, and rather nitpicky. She's an amazing person though and super kind and caring. For both exams and projects, her expectations are not expressed clearly enough.

I am a huge fan of Professor Lopez as a teacher, she is considerate and cares deeply about each student. However, her class is not built for success. I was able to maintain a mid to high A for most of the semester but due to a group project dropped down. I cannot recommend her for this course because you could work your hardest and not get an A.

Dr Lopez is caring but a bit of a harsh grader. The final report was graded based on a rubric that was hard to find and buried after other information - the expectations are there but not clear and accessible. Go above and beyond on revising your final report and incorporating every piece of feedback - you won't get away with giving partial effort.

Dr. Lopez is super smart, but the organization of the class is a nightmare, and the grading is harsh. You do a ton of reading and then in the last two weeks of class are supposed to complete a paper and a project that are worth over 25% of your grade. The assignment expectations are confusing. Do yourself a favor and take a different class.

Dr. Lopez was an amazing professor! She knows a lot about what she's teaching and is clearly very passionate about it. Her lectures are very interesting and she does a great job answering questions. She is very considerate when you need extra help or a deadline extension.

This was seriously the best class I've ever taken,  Dr. Lopez is so kind and inspirational. She incorporates gospel principles into lectures which I didn't expect and really loved. There is a lot of reading, but it's diverse and   worthwhile. There are some projects and bi-weekly smaller assignments, but she is very understanding about deadlines.

The class is really interesting and she makes it exciting to go to. The grading all depends on the TAs and they change each semester. The tests aren't hard if you pay attention in class and study a little beforehand. The workload goes down around the end of the semester.
She is very sweet, and she is willing to work with you. She is super flexible and loves what she teaches. She is awesome.

Professor Lopez is a great professor for this topic and class. Her slides in class explain the material necessary for the exams and quizzes perfectly, so I highly recommend attending class every week. She is super understanding with personal circumstances. If you are interested in sociology, her class is a must-take!

Dr Lopez is a great person, but this class was not great. She is a really tough grader, and never sets the expectations very clear on the projects and tests. This class kinda screwed my gpa, and it was only a 100 level course. I would NOT recommend taking this class for the Social Science gen credit, take something easier!

Professor Lopez is great and respects her students and all of their opinions and beliefs. Some of the projects were graded harshly and I didn't feel like it was clear what she was looking for. Overall, interesting class and easy enough!

I honestly enjoyed this class. My only complaint is that a lot of the concepts were abstract which made quizzes a bit difficult until I got a hang of them. The paper and project were graded kind of harshly and I didn't really understand what they were looking for, but the extra credit for the student rating saved my grade at the end.

Easy class IF YOU DO YOUR WORK. Her TAs are always willing to help. Tests/quizzes aren't hard if you take notes in class. Her slides show what you need to study. We had 2 big papers/projects. Assignments were easy. Felt like I couldn't always voice my opinion if it was different than hers. Still loved the class regardless. 2 tests all year no final

Dr. Lopez is alright because she is so open to care about her students. This is my first class that requires you to get a 94% for an A, and I don't see a reason why. I had a 93.5% and she wasn't willing to do anything about it which is quite frustrating when you're trying to keep a scholarship. I loved the topics we covered, and it's needed at BYU.

I felt that this class was very biased. This class had the opportunity to enable informed opinion development but rather only gave one-sided sources and opinions. I ended up withdrawing not due to the political opinions of the class but felt that it was not worth my time to only engage in extremely biased and far sided lectures and assignments.

Doctor Lopez is a really awesome professor! She is really understanding when it comes to turning in work and has great T.A.'s working with her. You do have to be willing to challenge your current biases and learn about social problems in a way that you may not have previously, but honestly I learned so much and really enjoy it.

I love, love, LOVE Dr. Lopez. She is amazing. Shes an expert in the field of immigration, so she knows what she is talking about and is passionate. The class sessions are centered around the readings (which are pretty hefty, but worth it). Other than weekly readings, the only other assignments are papers and take-home tests. Would recommend 100%

Professor Lopez is amazing! This class legitimately changed my life. There's a solid amount of reading but they're interesting. She also goes over the readings in the lectures, which are AMAZING! I've seen other reviews bashing her for liberal views, but c'mon, it's sociology. She knows her stuff and she presents it in a respectful way. Loved it!
This class is amazing and despite what other people have said it is clear what you need to do well. Even if you are new to college.

Professor Lopez is amazing! She cares about the course and her students. There is a bit of reading, but she provides all the article links and it is very enriching!! I would take this class again in a heartbeat.
If you are a freshman avoid this class at all costs. It is far too difficult for those starting college to succeed in.

I love Dr. Lopez! Please take a class from her, doesn't matter which one. In the first week of class, we did an activity where each of us could anonymously state our identities (orientation, nationality, occupation, gender, etc.) and she then read them to us so we could all be aware of the different people in our class.
Doesnt actually teach much and is not very open to differing opinions

LOVE HER. Dr. Lopez is extremely qualified and she can back up any of her opinions with a million facts. She's very passionate about sociology and this class has given me a better understanding of the experiences of marginalized people. only 2 tests and a take home final. There's 1 big paper, and the rest is attendance.

This professor is an extremist liberal and it shows in her lectures. She won't let people who are not liberal share in lecture without arguing with them and then not calling on them again. Took a test that had true/false questions based on opinions. Don't take if you get annoyed when only one opinion is shared and you're graded on agreeing with her

She's definitely not for everyone - the class is very political and if you have fundamental ideological differences with her then you will not enjoy the class. However, she gives room for debate and is very technical in what she teaches. The readings are hard to understand, but they're pretty optional and you can usually get by.

My favorite class at BYU so far. Current Social Problems will change you life and how you see everything. Lopez has great lectures and is good at creating class discussions while also using videos and illustrative activities to help us further understand. I honestly think that everyone should be required to take this class. Lopez will change you!

This course was amazing. Dr. Lopez is very passionate about immigration and it makes the class really interesting. There is a decent amount of reading and the class discussion is based off of it so reading is a must. Its also a great class to take if you are wanting to improve your qualitative research skills.

Lots of reading for this class, homework and exams are based heavily off of it so don't fall behind! This class is called "Current Social Problems", so obviously there will be some sensitive subjects discussed. You cannot go into lecture close-minded, as Professor Lopez will not shy away from calling you out or discussing real issues. Great class!

Discussions in the class could've have been beneficial for tests if they didn't go off onto tangents on different political ideologies. Dr. Lopez will make time for you though if you need help. The TA's grade are very difficult graders. Just a fair warning Dr. Lopez has very strong political opinions that may offend some.

TA's graded super hard and marked me down on papers for things that didn't quite make sense, but overall the class was great! Great content, 2 in-class exams and 2 papers, otherwise it's just reflections and attendance points. There're a lot of readings too and it's actually important to do them because you're tested on them for the final.

I liked Professor Lopez and the class, but this was too hard for a 100-level course. I never had more than a vague idea of what she wanted me to know. I studied harder for her final than I've ever studied for anything and I managed a B. But that said, she does care about her students and this was her first time teaching this course.

Don't listen to the haters, Dr Lopez is the best + so is this class. You do have to read a lot and work an average amount, but she and the TAs are more than willing to help you out. You talk about sensitive and relevant subjects in the class, which requires charity and open-mindedness. It was pretty life-changing tbh, and so interesting!!

I'm not sure why people are salty on here. It might be that there were a lot of freshman in this class who aren't sure how to do college yet. She is super willing to work with you and wants you to succeed. The content was really eye opening but you do read a lot of articles. Take this class to learn about social problems not just fill a GE.

Perhaps the easiest class I've ever taken which was nice, but I feel like I didn't really take much away from the class. I would just work on other stuff during class and I was totally fine. Oh and she brings snacks to class-- so nice!

Jane is the best of the best! She cares so much about her students and genuinely wants people to learn. The class is not super hard but it is so helpful. We had a consulting project where we got to consult a real company and all of their executives. Take this class if you want to learn and grow! Plus she always bring snacks:)

The professor is the sweetest and kindest person ever. However, this class shouldn't be a required general business class. Some things were applicable, but the class structure didn't help to facilitate learning. The class itself isn't hard, and neither are the assignments, but the sheer number of things we're graded on (80+) seems unnecessary.

WOW. YOU NEED THIS CLASS AND YOU NEED JANE DAY AS A PROFESSOR. She knew my name on the first day of class because that's just who she is. This class transformed me! Lectures from Joseph Grenny (look him up!), Dave Durocher (life changing), Lee Bird (don't miss!), and so many other powerful speakers. If you show up and invest, you will love this!!

Janeen is awesome! Her lectures are super engaging and she really knows and cares about what she's teaching. I love her focus on lived experience and understanding the doctrine, I almost forget I'm there for class! She makes a real effort to get to know the students and does a good job at involving everyone in a way they're comfortable with. 10/10
Take this class if you can, it will change your life.

Sister Martin is such an incredible person and professor. I felt the Spirit every single class and I've never been more excited to study the Book of Mormon. I would take this class again in a heartbreat!

Professor Martin is probably the best professor I've ever had at BYU. She is incredibly smart, her lectures are engaging and she teaches with so much passion. I recommend her to ANYONE especially those looking for a spiritual experience every class. She is the BEST!

Sister Martin is incredible! She is one of my favorite professors at BYU. Her classes are always thought provoking and inspirational. Her assignments are not hard, and as long as you do the readings and take notes, the exam is made to be easy. Definitely take from Sister Martin!!
I loved this professor and her class, would take another class from her again. She cares about her students and their well-being and is passionate about what she teaches.

Sister Losser is a wonderful professor for UNIV! She eliminated a lot of busywork I heard other UNIV students had, and focused instead on more meaningful class discussions and assignments. She really loves and exemplifies the spirit of BYU, and is so kind and caring to each of her students! I had a wonderful experience and highly recommend her!
Sister Losser is AMAZING!!! TAKE HER CLASSES!!!! BEST PROFESSOR EVER!

I love Sister Losser! Her classes are fun and she makes great use of the long time. The homework requires  a lot of papers, but they aren't difficult. She is so knowledgable and really helps you prepare to manage a classroom. The things she has taught from her own experiences have left a lasting impression. She is also really fun to be around!
I LOVED this class! She made it totally fun and exciting even though it was 3 hours long. She is sooo funny!
You will be LUCKY to be in Sister Losser's class! She is amazing! She is nothing but positive and helps motivate you to do well! I learned SO much from her class that I still use daily!
Sister Losser is one of the greatest professors I've had at BYU.  She really cares about her students, and she is hilarious!  Her class was so much fun, and I highly recommend her!

Awesome presentations that captivates your attention and makes the class fun. This professor provides quality insight to lesson plans that really helps once you get into the classroom. Highly recommended.
This class is just genuinely the worst. Her teaching just is so bleh.

I would recommend this class to anybody who wants to get physical science out of the way. Quizzes are unlimited attempts and the exams are based off the quizzes. Free response questions aren't super hard as long as you listen to lectures. Lots of videos to watch and there's homework daily, but it's still better than taking physical science class.

There are reading quizzes every day that are unlimited attempts, and the midterms and final are based on these quiz questions. It is very easy to navigate but there is a moderate amount of reading and work. Great class!
I sent countless emails and she never responded. It was a lot of work and the final was SO HARD. Don't take this class
This is a very convenient class to do virtually. The assignments were quite tricky for me, but everything else was relatively simple.
I loved this class! However, the assignments were kind of difficult sometimes. I will say that it's extremly easy to get an A in this class. She is amazing!

This is THE BEST class for the physical science GE. I'm a space fan now?! I do not do well with online classes but this has been a breeze. Professor Radebaugh & the TAs are so accommodating. Tests are almost purely made up of the quiz questions, and if you're struggling with the quizzes there are a million quizlets for each. TAKE THIS CLASS.

For someone taking it for credit it is really in depth for a 109 class. Hardest thing is instructions, they are not super clear but you can eventually figure it out. Tests aren't too hard if you do the weekly quizzes, it's mostly the same questions. You don't really interact with professor or TA's, if your a hard worker you'll be fine.

She was amazing! I took the online version, so it was recorded lectures. She and the TAs were super easy to reach and very quick to respond! It was so so interesting and genuinely so much fun. I would 1000% take a class from her again.

This was one of the easiest classes I've ever taken, but it was also super interesting! Exam 1+2 questions come straight from quizzes (unlimited attempts). The Final exam still had about half the questions from quizzes, but the other half really tested my critical thinking skills. Watch the final exam review! Her class is also 90% to get an A!

Big fan of this class, only downside is it's just half of the Physical Science GE. There are very frequent quizzes but they have unlimited retries, and you really don't need to do all the reading. This class is an easy A if you just stay on top of things; the A cutoff is 90. Prof Radebaugh is great. If you like space, you'll like this class.

BEST OPTION TO FULFILL YOUR PHYSICAL SCIENCE CREDIT. Piece of cake class overall. Lectures a pre-recorded, but not needed. Lots of quizzes, but super easy and can retry until you get 100%. 5 assignments for the semester - instructions are bad, but you can figure it out. Midterms and final questions are all just pulled from the quizzes!

This was a fairly easy course, but there are assignments due 3x per week, and 5 large assignments throughout the semester. For an online course, it was more difficult and time consuming than I expected, but I am glad I took it. ALL TESTS ARE MADE FROM QUIZZES

I took this online class to fulfill a GE requirement. I was surprised by how in-depth we went and just how much homework there was (~2 hours a week). I am not a science major and did feel like it was too much at times as far as the depth of the content went. Dr. Radebaugh is a great professor and if I were a geology major, would take her again.

The class is super organized and it's set up so you can get ahead really easily. Also I read the date wrong on one of the exams and didn't notice until after the test was closed which was super dumb of me but I emailed her and she let me take it after the deadline with no penalty. She's a very understanding person and wants us to succeed.

This class was by far the easiest class I have ever taken in my life. You have weekly quizzes that allow multiple attempts and tell you what you've gotten wrong. Tests are taken directly for quiz questions. I never needed to read the textbook and just watched the lecture videos at 2x speed. If you are looking for an easy online class, this is it!
Professor Radebaugh was so sweet! Her lectures were very interesting and if you paid attention, it was so easy to do well in the class. I learned a lot and enjoyed all that I learned.

I did the online class, so much busy work. There was one week where we had 2 quizzes, an assignment, and a midterm. Other than the insane amount of work, I loved the material so much, Dr. Radebaugh was amazing.

This class was easy and straightforward. Jani made it fun and the TAs were all super helpful. There is homework assigned for Monday, Wednesday, and Friday but that makes sense since it is an online 3 credit class

Easy, straightforward class to get an A in with consistent minimal effort. The assigned readings are long, but all relevant info is covered in the lectures. So, no biggie if you skip the readings. I probably put in 1.5 hours per week tops in this class and got a solid A. Lectures were fascinating! Space is cool! Take this class!

This course was such an easy A. The lectures can be put on 2x speed, and the quizzes have unlimited attempts. Exams use exact same question as quizzes, and assignments are graded loosely. I never expected to like this class, but it really is just meant as an intro to Geol of the planets. Not too complicated!
Personally, I hate science. But this class was very straightforward and everything on the tests comes from the quizzes. Grading is generous, would highly recommend this class!

The lectures were well done, and the content was cool to learn about. The quizzes have unlimited attempts, and tests have questions pulled straight from the quizzes. You can tell that Professor Radebaugh wants everyone to succeed and that she is passionate about what she is teaching.

This was my favorite class this semester. I learned so much new and cool stuff about our solar system. She explains concepts very well in her lectures. There are homework quizzes but you get unlimited attempts and the exam questions are mainly taken from these quizzes. This is a great class to take for the Physical Science GE.

Online course. Theres 3 modules each week with an open note quiz, that you can take unlimited amount of times. Theres 2 midterms that uses the exact same questions that are on your weekly modules. The final is a bit harder but the review video helps and redoing all the modules quizzes will help as well. Anything above a 90% gets an A in the class.

This class is absolutely fantastic for getting your physical science GE. The online lectures are well-made and the subject matter is in-depth enough to be interesting without getting difficult. It's basically a semester of learning cool facts about the Solar System.

Just make sure you stay ahead on the 3 assignments every week and you're golden.

Professor is so respected in the science community and her work for NASA is super cool. She is very passionate about what she teaches. Online class has super dense readings but test questions are on quizlet; memorization is key and you'll be fine. Easy extra credit options. No need to watch all online lectures. Learned a lot, cool class!

I usually don't like online courses, but this had to have been the easiest GE class I've taken in college. You can tell that she loves what she teaches and I enjoyed the videos a lot. There are a lot of quizzes, but they have unlimited attempts and are open book. Test questions come directly from the quizzes, and she made it very easy to pass.

This class was honestly the coolest ever and Jani did an amazing job teaching it. She explains things really well and her lectures are so interesting. The class was a super easy A, but I also felt like I learned a ton. Definitely would recommend to anyone.

Easiest physical science credit ever. The on-demand style was so convenient and most lessons can be done very fast. There's a few projects that were not very difficult and readings that I either skimmed over or skipped entirely. You are given the exam questions in the practice quizzes and you can do them as many times as you like (except the final)

Quizzes unlimited attempts and study answers for first two exams. Last exam based on general knowledge from whole semester but watch exam lecture and study quiz answers to prepare. So much reading, dont know if its necessary to do well. Had some projects, but could work w other students to do well. Not too hard of a class but lots of homework.

This class is super fascinating and very easy. Take it! I wish I spent more time on this class because the information was super interesting, but I was able to get an A by just memorizing the quiz questions and for the final memorizing the slides in the review presentation. I did not take notes once or watch any videos and got an A. Highly recommen

My favorite thing about this class was how passionate Dr. Radebaugh was about the material and getting to hear some really cool geological experiences that she's had. The quizzes are open note and open book. Exam questions for tests 1 and 2 are taken directly from those quizzes. For the final, the review video is the most helpful resource.
Ok GE class. Was online so didn't really interact with the professor. Pretty standard course setup. One presentation, no papers.

A very clearly structured and well organized class. You don't get much interaction with the professor directly when it's online, but in the recorded lectures she's excited and passionate with what she's teaching. I liked that there were so many resources to help us learn and apply our learning.

40 quizzes: unlimited attempts and open book. take whenever before deadline. 2 midterms and 1 final: timed and 42-52 questions. 5 huge assignments which can be tedious. first two midterms, questions are taken directly from the quizzes so memorize, final was a bit difficult as some questions were more conceptual so understand specific principles.

Prof Radebaugh knows a lot about this subject, and is clearly passionate about it. I felt like this class was really fun and valuable, and pretty easy too. There is an open note quiz after every lecture, and the exams are just an accumulation of the quizzes you have already taken.

Amazing Prof, she is an expert and so passionate about what she does. Was a bit wary of this class being online, ended up being the class I enjoyed the most. Set up so clearly and enjoyable to participate in. Stay on schedule and you'll be golden.

Jani was a great professor. She taught the concepts clearly and passionately which helps with some dryer topics. The only part I didn't like was parts of the class organization. 3 lessons a week plus quizzes with each one. Two midterms and a final but the structure of the final was different than the first two midterms which was frustrating.

Professor wasn't really active since it was online. easy ge class, exams are pulled directly from the quizzes and 5 assignments and semester long project. wish she was more involved with grading, one of the TAs grades pretty harshly which I didn't like and the professor replies really slowly.

Curriculum was super confusing during the first week of school but after it was pretty smooth. Quizzes are unlimited takes, 7 assignments I think there are 2-3 retakes, group project super easy, midterms are super easy. they come straight from the quizzes and 2 FRQ. TAKE THIS CLASS

Super easy A! I haven't gotten my grades back technically, but almost all questions on the tests are pulled from the quizzes, and if you just watch the lectures (you don't even need to do the readings) you can use the quizzes to study directly for the tests. I love Jani! She's super fun and entertaining, loved her class. I'm sad it's almost over!

I took Geology of Planets from Jani, and it was honestly my favorite online course I've ever taken. The schedule is given early, and you NEED to turn your quizzes in on time, BUT you can take them as many times as you want. There's nothing on the exams that isn't covered on the quizzes. Very interesting class. Jani is a passionate professor!

I loved this class! Easy credit for a GE! Midterms were questions taken directly from lecture quizzes (quizzes you can take multiple times) so if you do those and basically memorize them you'll be fine. 5 hw assignments which weren't too bad and you can submit multiple times. Final exam was a little difficult if you don't study or understand basics
I took an online version of Geology of the Planets and wish it was in person since I loved the class so much! This is a great general alternative to physical science, 10/10.

I LOVED THIS CLASS! She is a wonderful professor and NASA scientist. She has the coolest stories and is so passionate about her work. You will learn to love space as much as her. The content is easy to learn. 5 major assignments and 1 semester long project. There are 40 lectures with a quiz at the end. Best class at BYU. I would take it again!
Content was not too bad especially with unlimited quiz attempts, but the tests suck hard. Worst grade I've ever gotten in a GE. Forgettable class.

I took this class as a fill-in class, mostly because I thought it was interesting and wouldn't be that hard with my course load. I was right but I did not enjoy it. While the class was interesting, the class is graded WAY too heavily on tests, and the tests were on minute details and we were given no study material. Only take it if you have to.

Jani is a brilliant scientist, but not the best teacher. Going to class won't help you learn the material. The best thing to do it just take the quizzes and then memorize those answers for the tests. I felt blindsided by the final exam. We were told it would be like the previous exams, just a comprehensive version, but it was nothing like them.

Dr. Radebaugh is great! Take this class with her if at all possible and you'll be mind-blown and inspired nearly every class. She really cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. Quizzes can be a little tricky but you can take them as many times as you need. Tests can be a little challenging, but if you study well you'll do just fine.

Taking GEOL109 as an online class from Professor Radebaugh was awesome! It was easy, so I felt like I could actually take my time and enjoy learning. It was clear what we were graded on and the grading was fair. The exams draw heavily from the lesson quizzes, so you can definitely be prepared. Highly recommend!

This class is awesome because you learn about the planets (their formation, geologic history, and what they're like today) which is something so unique that it's quite fascinating. I read the textbook and took copious notes, but in hindsight I probably could have done just as well by skimming and taking notes on the important stuff. Solid GE choice

The online class was honestly easy once you got the system down. Skim the textbook, look over the powerpoint, take the quiz, then study the quizzes and main ideas for the exams. The information itself is really cool so don't get caught up in just trying to get a good grade--think about what you're learning.

This class was super easy. I spent maybe 1 hour a week total. Watch the 5 min vid, take the quiz, rinse and repeat. 2 midterms worth 10% of the grade each that are completely multiple choice taken from the quizzes and a short answer or two. A final worth 20% which is also largely recycled questions. Shes also a really amazing woman.

I took this class on-demand remotely and absolutely loved it. It is well organized and consistent for each module. Tests were from the material in quizzes. Jani is so caring and made the material so fun to learn about. I found myself doing the work for this class to put off my other classes' work.

This class was super easy. All I had to do was watch the 5 minute lectures, read a paragraph or two, take a quiz, and repeat on different topics. I took this class online and had no problems at all. The tests are pulled straight from the quizzes which makes it super easy to study. I would highly recommend taking this class for easy credit and fun!

I was nervous about this class being on-demand online, but it became my favorite class this semester. Passionate, knowledgeable and very clear; grading, assignments, quizzes and tests are all clear. No wondering at all. One of the best things: she wrote the textbook (so it actually is what you need to know) and she gives it to you!

Jani's awesome! Her class is super fun/easy. She really gets you excited about other planets. She's an active, respected researcher (e.g. she's part of NASA's Dragonfly team sending a probe to Titan) and has cool perspectives from her research/field work. Easy weekly quizzes with unlimited retakes. Homework can be unclear; go to TA reviews for help

This is one of my favorite classes I have ever taken at BYU. Jani is one of the most caring and awesome professors at this university! The class is a GE and she makes it like that. She knows most of us don't want to major in geology so she makes it interesting for us. I would HIGHLY recommend taking this class from her!

She was often absent from class at conferences. Even once during a review time and exam. However she really cares about the students and she is super knowledgeable. I feel like a learned a lot about a subject I dont particularly care about. She makes it interesting and understands her class is a GE so most arent here for their major. Go to class!

I took geology of the planets and absolutely loved the class. She is such a cool professor and really explains all the concepts very well. There are weekly quizzes but they are open book and the tests are fair as well. The daily lectures are very helpful but i skipped a couple of times and still did well, would not reccomend making it a habit.

I loved Jani's class! Yes, a lot of the lectures can seem useless because she just goes over slides she posts later, but she tries to get you excited about space. She also realizes that this is a general for most people, so she tries to emphasize the most important things, which I appreciated. Easy A, study for the tests and do the homework.

The material in Geology of the Planets is fascinating and Sister Radebaugh's experience in the field added so much to the class. She is very knowledgeable and very kind. I had a conflict in my schedule and had to miss half of her class once a week and she was easy to work so I could still succeed.

Dr. Radebaugh is one of my very favorite professors. She has a real passion for planetary geology and is one of the leaders in her field. She travels all over the world to find ways to relate other planets to Earth. Every day of class was fascinating and I learned a ton. As long as you go and pay attention all the work was easy.

Good class, she is very passionate about everything, which can sometimes lead to her talking about things that aren't 100% relevant to the subject matter, but overall really good teacher.  Class is in the planetarium, so grab a redbull or something before class, otherwise high risk of snoozing.

What a gem! I love Dr. Radebaugh, she really cares about what she studies, and explains concepts so clearly. I don't care much for the class topic (geology of the planets), but I enjoyed her style of teaching and her friendliness to all students.

Dr. Radebaugh is one of the best professors I have ever had.  She is genuine and friendly, and she loves everything space.  I have never had a class where I learned so much without putting in a mountain of effort.  I would highly recommend Dr. Radebaugh and Geol 109 for anyone interested in planets and having a good time learning about them.
Very inspiring and has a way of explaining difficult concepts clearly. She's the kind of person that nobody can say anything bad about because she's always super nice.
Good, fun, easy-ish class, she is great and helpful, although sometimes what we are supposed to do, like for tests or the final paper, is unclear.

Jani does talk a lot about her research concerning other planets, but she loves it so much, and explains geology so well. She is very fun, and very nice. Tests are the most difficult thing about the class, but if you attend lecture and take notes, you should know most of the answers.
I never went to class because there are no iclicker questions or quizzes. The tests are really hard...so study up for them.

Ridiculous. Class was canceled a lot and the days we had it, half of the students didn't show up. It was VERY unorganized!!  Lecture consisted of her telling about her trips she had taken which was cool, but useless to your learning. The tests are HARD and even though everyone did poorly there was no curve. Lab and TA's save you in this class.

I really just loved laughing about this professor.  I never really went to class because all she talks about are her trips and you don't learn anything.  The TAs are very helpful, luckily.  She grades WAY easy except for her tests.  She's really nice but kind of not all there.  Overall I liked her and would recommend her if you want an easy class.

The TAs will save you, really. The class is way unorganized and she canceled over a month of classes. She spends more time talking about her adventures then she does talking about information important to the test. I did OK but the Lab grade saved me. She refuses to curve and the final is comprehensive.

She's really great at explaining the material since she actually lives it. I loved HER. This class was SUPER unorganized though. Her tests were pretty challenging, but she wouldn't curve it (even when the entire class did pretty poorly on it) due to the fact that as women, "we judge ourselves too hard." Lab saved me.

Easy! Online timed quizzes, she drops the lowest 3 but you should get 100% on them b/c no-penalty retakes are allowed on all.  Do well on and don't miss any assignments.  Tests: REVIEW HER POWERPOINTS! They have everything you need to know on them! Use the textbook just to reinforce confusing concepts, that's the only time I ever really used it.
TAKE HER!!!! easiest class

This class was good! There were only two tests throughout the semester, both very easy. Some of the class concepts were a bit too abstract for my liking, but I did learn a lot. A great class if you're looking for a good professor and an easy class.

Her lectures can be boring if you are not interested in the subject. If you are interested in the topics, it's awesome! She is an easy grader and is very open to various opinions on a topic. She is a remarkable teacher. Would 100% take her class again.

Nuckolls is a solid teacher. Her lectures can be kind of roundabout and sometimes hard to follow especially with the abstract ideas of semantics, but she knows her stuff and doesn't overwhelm you with unnessessary work.

Dr. Nuckolls really seems to care more about your learning than about grades or assignments. For the capstone on gesture, we essentially had to do the readings for the day and 8 other assignments none of which were too hard if you put at least some effort into them and paid attention in class. Super chill for a capstone course, but I learned a ton!

Professor Nuckolls is one of my favorite professors I've had at BYU. She is very transparent about her expectations and doesn't assign us gobs of homework. It is interesting material and low stress. I've taken several classes from her and would do so again.

She is very kind and incredibly respectful. She takes on a diffucult job in teaching undergrads difficult course content on a managable level. She takes time to answer questions though, and she gives no shortage of extra credit opportunities. There was a book to buy that was necessary, though she didn't agree with a lot in it. It's cheap though.

Dr. Nuckolls is one of the most understanding professors. She's easy to work with, patient, kind, and very knowledgeable about semantics/pragmatics. She's an anthropological linguist, so she's unique within the department. She doesn't believe in homework, so all the assignments are very short and very doable. I've been her TA before and loved it!

This was the study abroad prep class, W Dr. Nuckolls is super on top of making sure we have all of the travel information we need to go to Ecuador. We started learning Quechua (textbook is free) and she's such a patient and positive language teacher. Practicing in class is fun and she goes at your pace. I can't wait to travel with her this summer!

There are a lot of extra credit opportunities, and the assignments are very well-explained. The lectures are interesting, and you can tell that she really cares about the material. I'm taking LING551 with her this fall and I'm really excited!
Not sure what the last person is talking about but this class is super clear and quite easy. One of the most humble and accesible professors at BYU.

Dr. Nuckolls has a very sweet, quirky personality. Her lectures are rather slow-paced and it takes awhile to get used to her quiet, sort of monotone way of teaching. However, she is very knowledgeable. Her class style is very stress-free while still providing ample opportunities to learn. I am taking another class from her in the fall!

She is great! There's a lot of reading of academic journals and the classes are all discussion based on those readings but she helps make it so clear and I feel so much more confident discussing linguistic concepts now. She's an easy grader, basically she just wants to see that you did the work.

Love Dr. Nuckolls! Lectures were extremely interesting and engaging, students were heavily encouraged to participate and it was a comfortable environment.  Dr. Nuckolls is very open to students' comments and opinions and we had some great discussions about language. There is homework and a final research paper but it is fun and very interesting.

Overly easy assignments and midterm (gave us a list of 30 really easy questions and then the test was 25 of the exact same questions) and extra credit galor. The vast majority of the class has well over a 100%. We'll see how the final paper changes that, but I don't anticipate it being really difficult. I could fail the essay and still keep my A.

Dr Nuckolls is another one who really cares about her students and will WORK with you if you need help.  She actually let me design a final semester project instead of a research paper because I had a solid idea and asked.  She really cares a lot about you.  This class is mostly dense essays with discussion after. So do the readings, and come.

Ms. Nuckolls is BRILLIANT. She is very good at teaching concepts in a concise, simple, applicable manner.  She gives one page of hw a week. This homework is very straightforward and easy to do if you attend class.  She prepares you well for her tests and is so kind and fair. One of the best professors I have ever had. Plus, she is adorable!
The class was pretty typical, but she did a great job of explaining the assigned readings.  If you pay attention, it shouldn't be a hard class.

This class is easy if you simply do what she asks. I got hosed on the final project because the rubric was so vague. Make sure you know what she wants and it is a very easy and interesting class. No offence to her but if Eggington is teaching I'd take from him, he is hilarious.

Professor Nuckolls is one of the most understanding, kind professors I have ever had.  I feel bad for not paying attention in class because, like I said, she is such a kind amazing person.  She really is a good teacher, knows her stuff and gives great feedback.  It was just boring, intuitive subject matter, and the textbook is useless.

Understanding and kind. The class consists of lectures and discussions, which I found interesting. Prof. Nuckolls is able to discuss issues from many different points of view, and she is respectful of those with differing opinions. 10 short papers, a midterm, some easy reading quizzes, and a final project are what make up your grade.

LING 110 is an easy A! Professor Nuckolls makes the expectations clear and the assignments are pretty simple. Attendance is mandatory, but again, it's an easy A if you show up. The lectures are a little uninteresting.

Dr. Nuckolls was awesome. I loved how she explained things and her class was cake. She is a little technologically handicapped, which could have made the class more interesting, but she is a great professor and I really enjoyed this class.

Sometimes interesting discussion, but that's all it is, discussions. She knows quite a bit. 10 1-page papers. Mid-term is exactly the same as the practice test. Final project is a poster or essay with presentation. Not too hard to get an A. Readings for every class. Some are interesting.

Dr. Nuckolls was great, she knows her stuff and encourages students to learn and be active participants in their learning. Only one test, the midterm, and it's super easy. The final was a poster so if you put effort in,you'll get an A.

This class has a few interesting topics but overall, very dry class.  Lots of long, boring journal articles to read and then class discussions about what you read.  10 1-page papers over the semester about each topic.  Easy class just very boring.  If you're into Linguistics you'll love this class, if you're not sure this class will decide it.

This was the best class I've ever taken. It was really easy, too. I got 100% because the midterm was the same as a practice test we got to take home, and the final was just a poster. Do the readings, have an open mind, and it will be easy. Professor Nuckolls makes you see multiple sides of issues. It's really enlightening.

She is a good professor. She really has a way of taking potentially  hard concepts and making them understandable. Her tests are really easy and she usually tells you exactly what to expect on the test. This was a very worthwhile class.
By far the best instructor I've ever had.  Very tough, but able and willing to help.  She truly made the subject come alive for me.  I recommend her highly.

Super nice lady...makes the class harder than it needs to be with poor organization.  Ask her to proofread your papers before you turn them in to avoid bad grades...also, be prepared to do badly on the quizzes :)
Very smart lady but her organization and lecture skills are poor.  Also her essays are subjective and graded poorly.  Avoid taking her class if possible.

She is a very nice lady but definitely not cut out to be a teacher. She does not explain the course material well and cannot keep the attention of a class. Grading system is very random. Soc 111 was very easy from her because you don't have to go to class, but Soc 310 is awful.

She made this class painful.  The entire class is based on three essays that are not graded fairly.  She is really boring and has such a huge vocabularty during class that I swear she makes up words.  Avoid taking soc 310 from Nuckolls if you can.  I think anyone would be better.
