She's a nice enough person and is very smart, but was not meant to be a teacher.  She is hard to understand, that is if you can stay awake even.  There is TONS of dry difficult reading.  Worst soc teacher I have had at BYU and it's my major!  Please avoid her if you can at all costs.

Well, If you enjoy boring lectures and someone that does not know how to use technology, Nuckolls is for you. Lectures made everyone fall asleep.  The tests were somewhat easy, but you had to really study for them.
So much extra credit. Lots of quizzes, but not too time consuming. Professor honestly wants you to succeed. Information dense, great review class for any STEM major.
Dr. Barrott is great. He wants you to succeed. There are tiny quizzes that you do at home that help you prepare for the exams. The tests aren't too bad.
Really fair with grades. He does a really good job at preparing us to take the test and his tests are written very fairly. He also has a ton of extra credit so doing good in this class is really easy

I loved Dr. Barrotts class! This class had no homework outside of class, except for small weekly quizzes that covered what we went over in class. All of the lecture slides are available on learning suite! The test reviews are SO helpful, and they cover basically everything that will be on the test. And the TA's are incredible!

I love Dr. Barrott! He puts an emphasis on knowing his students, and actually cares. He is so nice and funny. He understands bad test takers and has a bunch of extra credit work to do to make up for bad grades.Overall 10/10. 
Also his TA's are amazing. Miles the TA puts in the work and truly understands everything, he is so amazing!

You can tell Dr. Barrott loves what he does. His lectures contain everything you need to succeed. If you can't make it to lecture you can look up the slides online. Definitely go to the review sessions before the exam though. My only critique is that he missed a few weeks and had his TAs lecture and some weren't very good.

Not a bad class. The extra credit assignments are so nice. If you don't have a huge biology background this class was fine, just go to the TAs for help. Prof Barrott is super accessible outside of class and willing to help you. The slides are available which was super nice too.

Dr Barrott is a good guy, responded to emails promptly. 
He teaches this class as if it is a 300 level class. He didn't explain concepts thoroughly and expected us to already know a lot.
His exams are difficult averaging below an 80 but does offer an extreme amount of extra credit. Possible to get a good grade but difficult to understand concepts.

Super easy class just because of all of the extra credit offered. Not the most engaging lectures, but he is really kind and good at answering questions and wears bowties every Monday. I would feel comfortable approaching him for help. Personally, I need more engaging lectures in order to learn content, I had to study on my own for tests.

Solid professor for Cell 120. He had accessible office hours, encouraged students to come for help, and answered emails quickly. He's a cancer researcher, so he adds in a fair bit about it throughout the course. Lectures technically aren't required attendance, but he assigns an online quiz after each class with questions specific to the lecture.

The class is taught through slideshows that you can also access remotely. CELL 120 does a really good job of covering lots of bases in biology! And study sessions are always available. However, I wish there were more cool videos to watch

I took this class during Spring semester, I learned so much from Prof. Barrott! Come to class ready to take notes; it is lecture-heavy. Yet, he teaches very well and loves a good class discussion. He encourages students to go to his office hours. DO IT! Tests in testing center, quizzes usually after lecture, GOOD extra credit points. Choose him!

I am someone that loves biology, but sucks at taking tests and memorizing information. But Dr. Barrott honestly has the easiest class I've ever taken, and even during the spring term, was manageable. There is some complex material, but if you re-read his notes as well as his study guide for the tests, you'll be just fine and pass with an A

Dr. Barrott is awesome. His class was great, and he gives a ton of extra credit opportunities. The amount of information covered in this class was crazy. He knows his stuff, but it got a little overwhelming for me. His slides are super detailed which is nice for reviewing for tests. Take cell120 from him.

Dr. Barrott is one of the nicest and people I know, but he is still learning more about how to teach. His lectures are kinda boring and he de doesn't realize this is an entry-level biology class. He uses big words without explaining them. He offers TONS of extra credit though so its a pretty easy A.

Dr. Barrott is an incredible professor! My first-ever cell biology course with him was an amazing experience. His lectures are both engaging and inspiring. If you take good notes and review them consistently, you'll do well in the class.

This is an intro class, so it's more focused on getting you familiar with thinking like a scientist than actually exploring cell biology, but definitely provides a great foundation. Dr. Barrott cares a ton about his students, and puts a lot of emphasis on engaging with students during lectures. There's plenty of extra credit, so an A is not hard!!

I didn't like biology before, but his lectures were so interesting I looked forward to going to class and studying. There is extra credit, but most of your grade comes from quizzes and exams. Memorization heavy, but because there is no homework assigned it is very manageable. I didn't read the textbook and just used the slides to study.

Dr. Barrott was an incredible CELL 120 professor! He does a lot of cancer research which he incorporates into the material. DON'T PAY FOR THE TEXTBOOK! I never used it once. He covers the needed material in his lectures. As long as you take notes and pay attention, you will do fine. His tests are pretty difficult, so make sure to study! 10/10

He offers LOTS of extra credit and he or the TAs will help you with them, so it is very easy to get a good grade. The only things in the gradebook are weekly quizzes, exams, and extra credit. He is very kind and good at explaining things during lectures with slides. He does however, add in random information about his cancer research.

I do not recommend this class. Though it is called cell biology it does not go in depth about cellular biology at all (way less than AP Biology at least which is supposed to be general biology). It is incredibly easy even before Dr. Barrott's ten extra credit assignments, and thus boring and a waste of time and credits.

For Dr. Barrott's cancer biology course - I took this graduate level course as an undergrad and thought it was fantastic. Lots of extra credit available, so don't need to be worried about your grade, just learning. Structured around understanding primary and secondary literature on cancer. Dr. Barrott did a great job teaching challenging concepts.

One of the most boring classes I've taken. Professor is super smart but doesn't know how to teach, lessons are not engaging. The lecture slides are unorganized its black and white bullet points of lists of facts. You never actually know what is important to learn when he is talking. learning objectives help but hard to find while he is teaching.

Prof. Barrott is an awesome teacher! He teaches fairly well, but I learned most of my information from the slides. He wants his students to succeed. I did well because of the slides and going to his office hours. The tests and quizzes could be tough but he offers a good deal of extra credit. He was the best I found out of all the Cell 120 profs,

I absolutely adored my Cell class with Dr. Barrott. I was initially worried from previous reviews during his first few semesters, but I gotta say, I have never had better discussions during lectures or a more inclusive professor/TAs in my college experience. Dr. Barrott wants you to succeed and gives you many opportunities to do well in his class.

Extra credit saved me. The class was a little disorganized because this is his first year teaching undergrads. Dr. Barrott is a super compassionate guy and really cares about his students and his field of study.

His first year teaching undergrads was very rocky for me. If you fall behind on one section you'll tend to fall behind on later ones. Also often times his study guides don't go over exam content 1:1, so take good notes.
Don't buy the textbook! All the lecture slides are free on learning suite. I bought it for $80 and never used it.

This was his first semester teaching undergrads I think and he did a great job. The class is almost solely based on what is on the lecture slides. All of our point were from weekly quizzes and midterms. I doubt that the extra credit assignments will stay, but do them if they are available. It's the only reason I got an A. Really nice professor tho!

Probably one of the smartest dudes I know.  I got an A in the class because there is SOOOO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT IM NOT KIDDING ITS AMAZING. I got 1 A and 2 C's on the midterms and im gonna get a 100 in the class soley from extra credit. If you don't do the EC then buckle up bc its gonna be tough

Good class. The material itself is kinda hard but the stuff you are actually tested on is totally fair. The hardest material is on the homework. I agree though that there were some kids that would just talk all class (in a small classroom) and he wasn't really one to police it.

A great professor and pretty easy class. Nice teaching style. The only issue is that he does not know how to control a classroom and its a small class so if there is a loud group in the class you won't be able to hear him and he won't say anything to them. Otherwise, great guy and chill class.

Dr. Fisher is great 340 professor. If you get a chance to take it from him do it you won't regret it. The class itself is obviously difficult, but if you try your best to understand the topics you'll be just fine.

Dr Fisher has a process in which he gives everyone pre quizzes to do at home to confirm foreknowledge, followed by a lecture in which he explains and proves the math on the board, followed by an in-class worksheet which we try and he then explains. I found this to be very effective and engaging and fun.

Dr. Fisher is a perfect professor for this class. He clearly puts time and thought into presenting the info in the order that makes the most sense. He occasionally has a class break or an activity which is nice, but mostly lectures. That said, they all relate to the homework well, which is due same day once a week; tests were easy to study for.

Dr. Fisher deeply cares for each student. I adored his class even though lectures were sometimes not in line with the homework. Homework involves one weekly assignment totaling around 3-6 hours, depending on the topic. Work with the TAs, and you'll figure it out. He's also so willing to help in his office hours, thanking YOU for coming in.

Dr FIsher lectures by writing stuff on the whiteboard and it's just SO hard to stay engaged. Almost never any class interaction. His teaching style did not work for me and I wouldn't take from him again.
Dr. Fisher is a fantastic inspiring professor. He made 340 feel easy. Certainly would recommend to other students.

Lectures go on tangents and rarely follow the slides. Professor Halverson shared random thoughts or connections that he had, and rarely finished those thoughts. I left class unsatisfied. He also came across as though he felt superior to us. Grading is arbitrary and he assigned my grade based on what he thought I deserved after the semester ended.

Bro Halverson is an amazing professor! His lectures are so engaging & the main assignment for this class is 30 minutes of scripture study daily. He genuinely cares about his students, and the structure of this class is amazing. If you put effort into this class, it can genuinely change your life for the better :)

Wow. This was the best experience I've had in a religion class. I often sat in class wishing that everyone I knew could feel what I was feeling. Bro Halverson has incredible insights into the Savior and his atonement, and I really felt something different in his class. The study guide is every day for 30 minutes and it really is what you make it

Your grade is pretty determined by what you want it to be. "self graded" It is 30 minutes a day of scripture study in a guided scripture study journal that you turn in every week and by attendance. He is such an incredible teacher. Talks about concepts in a different way and so lovingly so I was able to have so many "aha" moments. An honor.

I'm sad that I didn't find Bro Hal earlier. I would have taken all of my classes from him. Focuses on the reading and has great lectures. Not a hard religion class either. Super spiritual, he's so passionate about what he teaches. I'm going to listen to his podcast from now on to get the same spiritual high that I got in class.

Have you read the Book of Mormon for 30 minutes every day? Has it changed your life?

Your grade in that class is directly correlated to the answer of those two questions and nothing else. Greatest religion class I've ever been a part of.
If you have a chance TAKE BROTHER HALVERSON'S CLASSES! He's the best! A solid amount of work, but it's really easy to get good grades.

Brother Halverson's class was beyond inspiring and has changed my approach to personal study. His lectures were phenomenal, his study journal assignments were well thought out, and my relationship with God has deepened as a result of taking his class. To not take a class from him would be a missed opportunity for spiritual growth. Highly recommend!

Absolutely amazing teacher. The way he brings the Spirit into his lectures is something else. Super light course load, just a daily study journal that helps you create good study habits and be better prepared for life. Honestly loves all of his students and wants to help them be the very best that they can be.

Great guy and great lectures. You're graded on a study journal you do every day that's self graded. The journal wasn't always my favorite, but there are no exams and no other assignments. Overall, a good religion course and be prepared to justify the grade you give yourself.
Brother Halverson is fantastic! He has such a great understanding of the gospel, I would recommend this class to anyone trying to dig deep and learn more doctrine.

Although this is a class for non-members I must do Bro Hal a service. This guy is absolutely amazing and is by far my favorite religion class I have taken at BYU. He really wants us to learn about the church instead of grade. Easy online midterm, self reports each week, super easy learning activities. The class is a breeze but spiritually amazing.

Bro Halverson loves to teach and talk about the scriptures. He really focuses in on scripture study, teaching, and faith crisis. He is really unbiased, and it would be hard to be offended by him. He doesn't do traditional exams, mostly you just have to read and teach lessons on your honor.
He knows the gospel and is very passionate. I passed his class very easily and also genuinely grew spiritually. 10/10 would recommend.

Super awesome class, I highly recommend taking religion from Brother Halverson. Overall the class wasn't super hard and there was just enough work to keep you interested without being to much. He is super helpful and flexible if you need it. Would 100% take a class from him again.

Bro Halverson was a super passionate guy who was really fun to learn from. He brought lots of cool perspectives on the Book of Mormon stories that made me more interested in what the book was about. His class was graded by 50% daily reading for 30 minutes in the scriptures and he really wants his students to dive deep. Super cool guy

bro hal is awesome! he knows his stuff, he cares about his students, and he wants them to have life-changing experiences in the scriptures. as such, he expects a lot of reading and reflection. if you go all in, it's so impactful and wonderful. 10/10 would recommend
So glad I took this class.  Helped me understand the scriptures.

Reading the Book of Mormon for 30 min every day is 50% of your grade. If you have actual extenuating circumstances such as mental health issues, he will be accommodating with grading if you talk to him during office or after class. Great to talk to out of class, very available, very understanding, but also a very busy guy with his outside endeavors

In 442 we had a great time, his class was a bit disorganized but he was going through some personal stuff so i give him a pass. He was very receptive and caring and I had some really great discussions in that class. He's a great guy!

Jared is a very kind professor and very accommodating. However, his class structure for CPSE 300 was not good. We read a chapter of the textbook- which repeated itself over and over- and then he'd just reteach it. I really only learned from the volunteer hours outside of class and through projects. Very caring, but I wouldn't take from him again.

Jared is such a nice professor. He was very receptive to student questions and concerns. His lectures and kind of boring and there's a decent amount of homework, but it's manageable. His class is also a little bit disorganized. But, if you do the assignments it's really easy to get an A in his class.

This was probably the most time-consuming class I have ever taken. There are 6 group projects, which is really difficult to do in an online class. There are about 3-4 hours of videos, a quiz, a discussion post, and a group project or exam every week. This class isn't super hard, it is just unnecessary busy work and takes up a ton of time.

TBH, one of the worst online classes I have taken. The class is a mess, and the things in the learning objectives are not in the lecture. Never had a class with more unclear instructions and busy work. At least he gives points back for the exams, I guess. Bottom line, what could have been a cool class is now a nightmare.

Cares so much about his students, wants to make sure every single one succeeds. He broke down the concepts into smaller parts that made it easier to understand, and the coursework was a lot but not overwhelming. He made stats seem so much less scary and I learned so much!

Jared is now one of my favorite professors at BYU. He doesn't use a textbook and just wants you to come to class and learn. He uses a lot of examples as he teaches which makes the concepts easy to learn. Sometimes it feels like a lot of info, but if you take the time to review, you'll be fine!

Great professor!!!! One of the kindest people I have ever met, knows everyone by name. Stats is not the easiest thing for me, but he made is passable and he understands that we aren't taking this class just for fun. Responds to emails quick. Tests are hard but aren't worth that much, so it's easy to get a good grade in the class.

Amazing teacher, with interesting lectures and clear expectations of what we need to know. That being said, his tests are far more difficult than in other classes, so buckle up, but it's nice bc if over 50% of the class misses a question he gives points back

I did not enjoy this class. As a psychology major who struggles with the more traditionally STEM heavy classes, I do not recommend taking Jared's class. He is a kind man and he genuinely loves the subject and he's willing to help out, but I was honestly just lost all the time and I wasn't sure how to ask for help. His exams are incredibly difficult
He's a great guy, I felt the lectures were interesting, and the exams aren't that bad. I enjoyed this semester and it definitely was a lot easier than any of my premed classes

I loved this class! Professor Nielsen is funny and so good at explaining concepts. Lectures are engaging and they're recorded if you can't make it. The three exams were a little tough and there is a research paper to write, but there's small assignments to help you stay on track. I didn't have to dedicate a ton of time outside of class to homework

Perhaps one of the more difficult psych classes I've taken. The tests are difficult, but manageable if you study hard and do TA reviews. Jared helps with anything too. He is genuinely one of the nicest people I've ever met. He will help you when you need it. I would recommend this class, but be ready to work for it.

The class itself was blended, so attendance was only mandatory half the time. We learned the material through an hour or so worth of videos and then reviewed and did activities with class time. At first, the class was brutal bc I kept putting off the videos until the day the video quiz was due...but as soon as I spread them out I was good

I absolutely love Jared. He does such a great job of teaching and is really good at explaining things so that everyone understands the material. He will take extra time during lecture to make sure everyone is on the same page if theres any confusion. Very personable. The tests are long but honestly not too bad. He records class and posts slides!!

I liked this class overall, but it caused me a lot of stress. Get ready to memorize a million different terms. Jared is great and clearly caring, most of my frustration was with the TAs. I wouldn't reccomend taking this class if you have any other difficult ones to worry about.

Jared is such an amazing professor and I really enjoyed being in his class. He always was willing to answer everyone's questions and showed that he cared. His tests were a little challenging but he did curve and his daily quizzes are very similar to what actual test questions look like. He has many assignment to receive points. Definitely worth it.

Professor Nielsen is the best professor I've had at BYU! He cares so much about his students and is willing to work with them. His lectures are super interesting and he presents the material in an engaging manner. His quizzes and tests are super fair and provides a lot of help to be able to succeed in them.

I can't say enough about how great Dr. Nielsen is. His lectures are insightful and he takes time to make sure students understand any confusing concepts. When he realized that a large portion of the class got certain questions wrong on exam 1, he gave points back, and told the TAs to give more specific reviews moving forward.

This class was super interesting and Jared was a great professor. He really cares about each and every one of his students and tries his best to learn everyone's names. The test were pretty hard though, and with no study guide and a ton of information to learn, it is difficult to figure out what to focus your attention on.

The tests that Nielsen gave were extremely difficult compared to other courses at BYU within psychology, including the cognition class. The study guide did not really prepare you for the test nor was Nielsen up front about the difficulty of the tests. You dont learn much in class and you are required to do a ton of independent studying

Jared is genuinely one of the nicest professors I've had at BYU. He learned everyone's names (even in a huge class) and the last question on our final was a reminder that he loved us. He's so genuine and kind and the class has very enjoyable with him. Tests were pretty easy and the class was great.

Jared is an amazing professor who truly cares about his students. Psych 111 is not a walk in the park, but an A is easily achievable if you attend lectures and somewhat apply yourself to the homework. Jared is not afraid to lecture about things that may be considered "taboo" at BYU, including gender, sexual orientation, etc, which was refreshing.

Jared was such a good professor. He had required readings, then would have a short reading quiz at the beginning of class each day. Then the lectures would be about what we read so we could come with questions. He also required attendance at review sessions which was really helpful. Jared was open and respectful towards students and graded fairly.

Jared is super personable, and a great professor. Assignments aren't that bad, and he is flexible when necessary. Almost all grading is done by TAs, which can be annoying sometimes, but overall a good class. There are daily attendance quizzes, and the tests take studying. Don't take it for a free credit, but it isn't hard to do well.

Great guy who just teaches hard concepts, but he tries very hard to make sure everyone understands everything. Exams were long but not too hard. Lots of opportunities for help. There were long quizzes for every lecture, but they help prepare you for the exams well. He cares about his students and even had most names memorized before the first class

Take this class from Jared! He's very accommodating, and will always take time to answer your questions. The class structure was also very clear and organized, which I loved, and as long as you do the assignments and readings, you'll do fine on exams. (TA reviews also helped a lot.) Jared is the best!

Jared clearly outlines learning objective and key terms for each reading assignment, then has a 2 question reading quiz to start off class each morning. His TA's also hold reviews every week. This class is very easy to excel in (if you do not miss often.)

Jared is an awesome teacher who really wants his students to be successful. Do all of your work and make sure you read cause you will have a 2 question quiz every single class which makes attending class mandatory. I will say that as long as you study and do your reading you will have an easy A in the class. Also there are 6 mandatory TA sessions.

If I could, I would take Jared for every class! He's caring of his students and truly wants you to succeed. There's readings before every class, six short papers, two longer papers and a semester long project. While this sounds like a lot I PROMISE IT'S NOT!! It's all super lowkey and chill, and if you let yourself be interested it'll be fun.

Jared is one of the most meaningful and intentional teachers I have had at BYU. He cares a lot about his students. Lots of busy work and tests are relatively hard but definitely doable with enough studying.

Prof. Nielson will take the time to answer thoroughly any and all questions. If you need repetition and examples to comprehend things, this is a good choice. If that bores you to death like me, bring something to work on. It's still worth taking, though. Prof. Nielson will hold review sessions and do his best to make sure you understand.
This class is very easy if you study using the learning outcomes, go to exam reviews, and read the textbook.

This class was overall great, there's a lot of assignments that feel like busy work but it's all super simple. The tests are easy and there are reading quizzes each day but he drops the 3 lowest scores. There are connection papers and weekly lectures each week which were kinda a lot but they ended up helping me understand the concepts much better.

Dr. Nielsen is a very careful teacher. He had some fun lectures when he allowed us to ask questions to different individuals. There are papers due weekly that aren't hard...just a bit of a pain. The reading is really interesting.

Jared (that's what he wants to be called) is a great professor. Super caring, and really loves his subject. Lectures were meaningful and the class was very manageable. I probably spent like 2-3 hours a week outside of class doing homework each week, so it is pretty easy. Although easy, he makes the class personally impactful if you give effort!

I hate psych but I love this professor. Cares about students grades and often gives back points if a question is unfair. Lots of mini papers, but take like 20 mins to do. Quizzes at beginning of class for reading, but lowkey easy. Tests are tricky but just know obj & you're fine. He is super caring and wants you to get an A. He's the best!

I absolutely love Jared. I honestly could not have asked for a better professor to be my mentor for research experience. He is so respectful of his students, and you can tell that he really cares about our success.

Dr Nielsen was by far the best professor I've had at byu. The material is challenging and hard to grasp at first, but he explains the concepts well. He also reviews the concepts until you get them down and is very respectful and cares about all of his students.

AMAZING professor. He cares so much about his students and will explain a topic 50 times in 50 different ways if that's what you need to understand. This was his first time teaching, so there were some hiccups, but I loved how he analyzed every quiz and test to see if the material was taught adequately. He is so respectful, and TAs were INCREDIBLE

Ugh, it pains me to write this review because Jared is a fantastic person. But home boy does not know how to teach a class, write tests, or grade. I would assume he focuses on research because he does not know, in the slightest, how to write a test or actually check for understanding. They are misleading, horribly graded, and downright bad. bad.

Dr. Nielsen's Sensation and Perception class has probably been my favorite class at BYU so far. He cares about his students and you can instantly tell that he is very intelligent and loves his job! He memorized our names before we even came to class(which was amazing) and he answered all of our many questions honestly if he didn't know the answer.

Dr. Neilsen is one of my top two professors at BYU. His high interest in the class material is equal to that of his interest in his students as you feel welcomed in the classroom. there are daily quizes so read the book and attend class. This class does require studying and effort but is so interesting and applicable to multiple areas of study.

Dr. Nielsen is a talented and passionate professor who really cares about his students. I very much recoommend you go to him one time during his office hours. Talk to him about your career plans, and I promise that he will provide constructive feedback. This is a fair class. There is no busy work and no surprises. Pure learning.

Dr. Neilsen is great. The class isn't too sweaty but it definitely does encourage you to learn a lot. I have already taken multiple neuroscience and psychology classes so this wasn't too bad, if you're worried about this class you dont need to. Show up to class, read the textbook, and work on the homework adequately and you can do great. TA's great

Dr. Nielson is the best! He is a very kind man and you can tell that he cares a lot for his students. He is good at explaining the material and is willing to help you outside of class! At the same time, do expect a work-heavy course that has almost daily assignments - it is a 4 credit class. If you keep up you won't have any issues.

Jared was a good teacher! He was kind and spiritual and cared about his students' understanding. His class was MWF for me, with a pop quiz due in the first 10 minutes about once a week, so make sure to attend! They were lowkey hard but always open note so that helped. His tests were very straightforward though so if you study you should be okay!

Great class! Professor Nielson just loves psychology and loves to teach it, he makes the concepts pretty easy to understand and you can tell he is passionate about them. It is because of his class and specifically his lessons on the brain that I switched my major to neuroscience. The quizzes are easy as are the tests and papers. EASY A

This is the best class I've taken at BYU! While I didn't interact with Jared that much, this class was so applicable and interesting. All of the concepts were presented in meaningful ways, and I found myself thinking about the material throughout my day. I highly recommend taking this class!

Jared is super respectful and caring and was a joy to listen to during lectures. He is also super understanding and humble and was kind enough to get rid of mandatory review sessions with the TAs after everyone agreed they were unproductive. I didn't find the tests too difficult, just take good notes on the learning objectives and you'll be fine.

Brother Nielsen is one of my favorite teachers! His lectures are really interesting, and he's super reasonable with grading. There are daily reading quizzes, 10 short papers, and 5 midterm exams throughout the semester, but they're not very difficult.

I would love to give Jared a 5.0 for who he is. Overall, this class was terrible. Tests and quizzes are filled with grey area questions. There's a ridiculous amount of content from 40 different sections! The resources are limited and include poorly led reviews while excluding a true study guide for test prep. Way too much for a 100 level class.

Jared is one of those teachers that really cares about his students succeeding, both in the class and in their life. Not only did this class make me more passionate about psychology (I wasn't at all before), but it also made me reflect on the attitudes I can adopt in my life to be a better person. Jared is AWESOME! Take this class!

Jared Nielsen is literally one of my favorite professors at BYU. He really is passionate about his field and really practices what he teaches. He is caring and he looks out for his students. He does his best to make things as fair as possible. If you're going to take PSYCH definitely take it from him.

I'm never one to actually leave reviews for professors, but I HAD to for Jared. People are right that there is a fair amount of reading and quizzes, but the questions (including test) are not very hard if you pay attention and read. Jared is so kind and inclusive. He really makes you think about how to apply what you learn into your life!

Jared has a great personality and his lectures were quite entertaining. Aside from the lectures, the class consists of constant busy work through out the week. Tests and quizzes are poorly written with "grey area" questions. If you enjoy poorly written tests, this is the class to take.

I took this class online, so the structure may have been different from students experiencing the in-person class. A big part of our grade in this class was a group project, and my group ended up having a lot of problems. Dr. Nielson was very understanding and kind throughout the entire process. He was a great teacher.

Dr. Neilsen is a great guy, but I would never take another class from him. Unfortunately, this class consisted of 90% busy work, and there was way too much of it. He doesn't grade things super harshly, so if you like busy work and tests that are poorly written, then this is your class!

I literally created an account so that I could give Jared a good review. I LOVE THIS MAN. He is seriously one of the sweetest professors ever and he is super caring and accommodating to his students. Textbook was online/free, readings req. before every class, but they were easy and weren't too long (but you are quizzed on it so come to class!)

The best class. Textbook is free and online. This class also has the BEST TAs, & it's super easy to access them outside of class. You are required to go to one TA meeting every week (for an hour) and that helped me with the course material a ton. Jared likes lots of participation in his lectures, & he is a super caring professor. HIGHLY recommend!

Jared really cares about psychology and all of his students. He wants to give everyone the best grade possible and teach everyone to apply what we learn so that we can lead happier, more successful lives. Find a TA that you like and listen to what they say and you'll do well.

Jared is an amazing professor that really cares about his students. His lectures are super entertaining and he does everything he can to get you a good grade. I learned so much in his class and the tests were pretty easy.

He was a very good lecturer! He made PSYCH 111 very fun. The only homework was to read from some online sources and keep track of some goals throughout the semester. Definitely take this class with him if available!

Jared is an AMAZING professor that helps further the learning process. He is fair, intellectual, and so so caring. He didn't require the use of a textbook or clicker (provided free options). You need to attend TA lab once a week and attend class to get Bungeelink points. He has clear learning objectives and he knows each student by name. Love him!

Great lecturer, does his best to make sure students understand the material and goes over the important things multiple times so everyone knows it. A lot of points come from lecture attendance, though, so make sure you can attend most of the time.
This was my favorite class ever. Jared is the best professor! I would recommend this class to everyone! I learned so much.

Professor Nielsen is an awesome professor and helped me come to enjoy psychology which I didn't think would ever happen. If you study, the tests are straight forward and not too difficult. A required reading for every class but the textbook is online and the readings are never very long.

Awesome Professor! Clear and straightforward tests. Relatively simple material. Lectures cover the important material but also include interesting facts about neuroscience. I would definitely recommend taking from him. Anyone who puts in some work can get an A.

I loved him! This was his first semester ever, and he did a great job. He really cares about his students and asks for feedback to get better. His tests are fair, and he'll give points back if questions were too tricky. The class prepares you a lot and the readings aren't long. He makes the content easy, and I felt like I felt I learned a lot.

This was Dr. Nielsen's first semester back to teaching after a few years so things may change a little as he gets into the swing of things again but this was an amazing class! Lectures prepared you for exams (mainly vocab heavy) & readings helped with in class clicker questions. Group project worth a lot of points. Easy A if you study! Very caring!

He's a really caring teacher and nice guy. He helped me with my piano skills, and this class didn't overly stress me out. He didn't give us any exams in the testing center, which was really nice! He is an amazing pianist, and sometimes plays songs for us.

Dr. Pierce teaches Supervised Studio Teaching by having each member of the class give a lesson for 25 minutes and then critiquing it for the next 25. It is very organized and easy to know what to expect. He is fair and understanding when difficulties arise. He is kind and smart and wants to see students succeed.

Not my favorite psych class by any means but was required for my major and was pretty easy. Just three major projects that make up the majority of your grade and if you follow the rubric, you should do well. He changed the tests to be open note this semester so I just didn't even study and still did well.

Professor Warren clearly cares about the material, but his classes are poorly planned. A lot of class time is spent talking in groups ad nauseam. I rarely left class feeling as though the time spent was valuable. Most student input feels generally brushed off, which doesn't inspire confidence in learning.

This class is totally what you make of it. There are some really valuable lessons, but I'm not sure it needs to be a full semester long. There's a lot of reading, and every class is a long discussion based on the reading. I just lost motivation to go to class after a while. The TA's were super helpful though, and it's easy to get an A.

I did not enjoy this class and I don't know how I received an A, I really didn't do very well. I heard more about Professor Warren's photography than anything else in lectures. Maybe a 1 rating is harsh, but my dislike for this psych class made me consider a change in majors. Lots of textbook reading and quizzes but little enjoyable learning.

Very kind guy who is passionate about this content and really cares about his students. The content is super interesting and helpful, my only complaint is that you don't really know what's on the tests and the study guides aren't too accurate, but wonderful class!
This was an amazing class that I recommend to everyone. The class itself is very easy and you will learn a lot. It is a chill class that you will have a lot of fun in.

Best class of my life. Lots of reading and the tests were impossibly hard and the review sessions from the TAs were a waste of time. Definitely changed my whole life though so just study a lot and make sure to do all of the readings because the quizzes are timed but open book open note and come straight from the book/website. 3 projects. so good.

Best teacher to take this class from and learned so much! I wasn't sure I'd get a good grade but the extra credit and final were manageable. Very enjoyable class lectures and learned lots. TA Friday discussions were key for the weekly quizzes. Lots of textbook reading so focus on key points. Be careful/concise on the final project video.

This class is awesome and highly recommended. The point of this class is to teach you things that you can then apply to your life to improve your subjective well-being. It's almost like a STDEV class in psychology. No real req. textbook but lots of reading. Take the class seriously and it can change your life and be an easy A.

I liked Dr. Warren's PSYCH 111 class, so I took his positive psychology class and enjoyed it too. There are many papers, but the majority of them are just based on your experiences with the 21-day personal growth experiments. The lectures are very inspirational, and I learned a lot from this class. I highly recommend!

Dr Warren is a good guy, but his lectures are useless. Don't bother going. They're full of fluff and discussions like "turn to your neighbor and talk about your childhood trauma." Attendance is mandatory for Friday discussions. The only useful lectures are the exam reviews. If you go to those and do the study guides, you'll get A's on the exams.

A good professor! I think he is a great guy and fun to learn from. The course I took was challenging to a degree but it was not too overwhelming. It is easy to get an A if you just read the material, show up to class, and stay active in what's going on. You can tell Dr. Warren cares about his students and their success.

I really loved this course with Dr. Warren! If you want to get credit for improving your life, take this course. I have a lot of respect for him and he is so so so caring of everyone's comments and opinions. The tests were kind of annoying and specific, but there's other grades to make up for it. Just turn stuff in on time and you're golden.
Engaging lectures with lots of class discussions. Projects are used to help students apply the information to their everyday life. Loved this class! Would definitely take again.

The class was pretty easy but very boring. Professor is nice but nothing special to add about him. I didn't really take notes and did well. There are weekly quizzes based on online textbook readings. Use the TA's Powerpoint for test reviews and you'll do great.

Dr. Warren is a great guy and you can tell that he is a good psychologist, but I didn't love him as a professor. It's not a hard class-- that being said, if you're looking to learn, this isn't the place for you. There's a decent amount of reading, and all of your quiz/test questions will be self-taught from that reading. Lectures are pointless.

I liked Dr Warren and the class, but everything we learn is just from the readings (there was a decent amount). We didn't learn anything in class and lectures were often spent killing time. I enjoyed the small recitation groups we had and felt there were lots of opportunities and easy assignments to raise grades.

The class is a great intro to psychological science! There are reading quizzes every week, but they should be easy points if you actually did the reading. Also DO THE STUDY GUIDE! It covers very specifically what will be on the midterms/final. There are small Friday discussion groups (10) in which you will have a large project to do.

Dr. Warren is such a kind person and is very welcoming and accepting to everyone (ally to LGBTQ+ community). He helped us not only learn the material, but also how to apply it to our own lives. He can sometimes get caught up on little tangents, but overall really enjoyed this class. Take it from him!!

Professor Warren made my first semester at BYU a dream. He is hilarious and made going to class something I looked forward to. The class is set up so as long as you do the reading, you will be fine. TA discussion groups are super helpful, and the tests are easy as long as you do the reading.

TAKE THIS CLASS!! Warren is an amazing and it was a great class with easy papers and tests! you even emeditate in class sometimes. I loved his class and my TA group that I met with every friday. You won't regret taking this class from warren!

Dr. Warren is a really great professor and his class was engaging and beneficial for me. There can be a lot of reading if you get behind, but it isn't too bad. If you do the readings, you'll do well in the class and I really enjoyed it.
Absolutely loved Dr. Warren! Definitely my favorite class. I would 100% take this class again. 10/10 would recommend! For tests I recommend just studying the from the TA review (slides)

Very mindfulness based. He even sometimes has meditations in class. The Friday lecture is a discussion group with 8-12 people and a TA that teaches it. He loves participation and encourages conversations with the people sitting around you. I loved the concepts he taught. MW lectures are basically just reviews of the readings you've already done.

Dr. Warren is a great guy and seems really into psychology. However the homework was almost exclusively reading and memorization. The lectures spent half of the time talking about random things not related to the class, and the tests were almost all random fact memorization. If you take super good notes you will probably be fine.

I love Dr. Warren! You can tell he's a good psychologist. Weekly quizzes aren't that bad as long as you do the readings. The readings can be a lot sometimes but they're usually pretty interesting. Go to the TA reviews for the tests and you'll be fine.

Professor Warren is amazing! He's so chill and really inspires you to become a better person. The class is unlike any other that I've taken- it's less of a class, and more of a character building exercise. I found his class to be really enjoyable, and was able to get an A pretty easily. He also offers a ton of extra credit! I highly recommend.

I really enjoyed Psych 111 with Dr. Warren. He's really fun - he played music before class and told terrible dad jokes in class - and we had discussion groups where we were able to think about the material and how it applied to us. The readings prepared you for the exams which prepared you for the final, so I never felt very stressed about exams.
Dr. Warren is the man. He is so caring and wants so badly for his students to succeed and feel cared for. Just a genuinely great professor.

Dr. Warren is incredible! This is one of my favorite classes that I have ever taken. He is so genuine and caring. This class is super interesting and his lectures are very engaging. I HIGHLY recommend everyone take this class!

Professor Warren is a great teacher. He cares so much about positive psychology. Overall, this class was a good experience for me. I learned some very practical information. I would recommend taking this class, especially if you are trying to improve your mental health or "find yourself".

This class is great for if you genuinely want to feel happier. Teaches psychological principles, but centers around helping you make yourself a better person with 3-week well-being projects. Class discussions are meaningful and Dr. Warren is pretty chill. Overall, it's a pretty easy weekly class that could really make a difference in your life.

I have learned so much from Dr. Warren! I really feel like I'm a better person as a result of taking this class. He truly cares about his students & the course material, and it shows. The reviews don't lie - he really IS zen. He's very in tune with himself and is willing to share his life stories to help students. TAKE THIS CLASS!!
He's a great professor. The subject is really fun, but don't expect it to feel like a rigorous science course. Lot's of fun, heartwarming and meaningful conversations, though.

Dr. Warren is one of the best teachers at BYU. He is so passionate about what he teaches and his students and really wants to help. He is extremely clear and methodical in his teaching style and expectations are very clear for assignments right from the start of the class. This guy knows his stuff. Plus he's totally jacked and so zen.

Dr. Warren is so passionate about what he teaches. He is so kind, cares about you and wants you to do well. His lectures are inspiring and truly impactful to your life if you choose to commit to them. The class was very eye opening and life changing. Tests are based off reading & lectures. 1 group project/ presentation. Highly recommend!!
'Zen' describes this man perfectly. Fantastic class, few assignments, heavy focus on helping students to improve their own well-being.
Great teacher! Absolutely practices what he preaches and is very dedicatedly. Great teacher and great person overall and very committed to helping students succeed. Most zen person Ive ever met.

I highly recommend taking this class! I love learning about what is good in life and thinking of how to help future clients to get to that level. The class was easy enough besides the tests which are a little more challenging.

Do anything you can to stay awake. It'll be hard, trust me. But he's a super nice guy and the material is kinda sorta interesting. Know that he quizzes you randomly on the readings.. so read. It'll help on the tests later. Easy A if you study for the test-- STAY AWAKE and take notes during his lectures!!!!

Nice guy. Boring lectures that are irrelevant to tests, but there are super good nuggets of inspiration sprinkled in that make it worth it. Great videos and activities to engage the class. Very responsive to e-mails. Easy exams straight from the readings (but it is from reading--do them!!!)

I loved this class! (Positive Psychology) Definitely worth taking. Dr. Warren was a really interesting lecturer - but got off on tangents more often than not in class. Lots of reading, but it's from a great book that's fun to read.

I really liked him as a teacher! He had great examples for all of the disorders we talked about and you could tell he really cared about his students. The tests were REALLY difficult, though....but he always curved them by at least 6 points, so it all ended up okay. I kind of got sick of in-class group activities, but other than that, he was great!

Dr. Warren is great! He's so funny and he has GREAT case examples for most disorders we discuss. He's dedicated to always improving the class (he actually omitted a once-required paper). It's heavy reading, not gonna lie, but class is interesting. PowerPoints are a good way to study for the tests. He offers 25 e.c. pts. and grade is evenly weighted
Class seems fairly simple when you go to lectures but the tests are ridiculous.  Very heavily based on the textbook. The only reason to go to lecture is to take the pop quizzes.

Nice guy, but not a great professor.  His lectures are basically story hour with kiddish class activities included.  Tests are pretty beastly and are pretty nit picky.  Lecture doesn't really prepare you for the tests.

The grade in the the class is really heavy on tests.  The only other points come from in class participation stuff. However outside of getting the points, class isn't really necessary to do well on the tests, since they are almost totally from the book.  The tests are the most difficult multiple choice tests I've ever had, and I'm graduating.

Loved Prof Warren- the class is really interesting and relatively easy. It took me a couple tests to figure out how to study for them. I didn't think the study guide was all that helpful. Carefully reading the text will get you the best grade.

Dr. Warren was great! I loved taking child psychopathology from him. He has a quiet humor that makes class enjoyable and interesting. He shows a genuine concern for students that he teaches and tries really hard to make his classes interesting. If you're interested at all in child psychopathology, you'll get a lot out of this class. Do the reading!

I was nervous about this class a first but I ended up really liking it. The professor is great and funny.  The tests are the thing to really worry about.  Make sure that you read.  Most of the material is from the book.

Dr. Warren is a really great guy who honestly cares about his students. The class isn't always interesting, but there were parts of it that I think are really important to know. I thought it was an easy A, and I don't consider myself super smart. Tests are hard, but everything else is easy.
Mostly girls take this class.  Its pretty mother oriented.  I wasn't particularly impressed with the teacher, but if you are interested in the subject matter, you will love the class.

I loved Dr. Warren.  He's pretty funny.  The lectures are a little boring sometimes, but he can usually liven it up with a funny story or Jack Handey quote.  He even took out the term paper for the semester!
Tests are hard, but fair.  He is a little hard to pay attention to in lectures (kind of boring) but overall, I enjoyed the class.
Fun class, you will have to work hard tho, but you'll learn a lot while taking this class; he looks like ferris bueller!

Had him for abnormal child psych.  He's alright.  Uninspiring.  Grading policy isn't very comprehensive or fair – you'll probably get a lower grade than normal.  The class was only semi-interesting.  I've had much better.  I'd take it from someone else if I were to take it again.

Professor Whitehead is always open to questions during class and is willing to go over a couple of homework questions in the beginning of lecture. He also does a great job at explaining concepts in a way that you can easily understand harder concepts for the homework.
Jared's pretty chill.

I found the class very easy, but that's mainly because I took calculus in high school. Toward the end of the semester, I skipped a lot of lectures and almost all the recitations, and even when I did go I mainly just did my homework. Jared is still a cool guy though.
Practice tests and homework are very good at preparing you for the exams.

Professor Whitehead is a great guy. He may be a little shy or introverted but he teaches the material very well, and always makes sure that everyone understands before moving on. You can tell he cares about our learning. He gives practice problems in class and will walk through tough homework problems with the class. Overall a great professor.

When he knows you're being lazy, he's pretty sassy about it. I find when he knows I'm not trying my hardest, then I don't want to disappoint him and I push myself. He tends to overbook himself, but he bends over backwards to try to help his students. He's humble when he doesn't know something, so then it becomes a puzzle you both work out together.

Whitehead cares about his students. Sometimes hard to follow along in lectures because of math-y language. Textbook reading was more confusing than helpful most of the time. Not too heavy of a work load, and there are lots of resources to help you succeed in the class. Overall, I liked it, but it wasn't anything exceptional.

Calc at BYU is hard regardless of who you take it from. Dr Whitehead is the man though and did a great job at explaining the challenging concepts. There were a couple of times he was gone and we had a sub, and each time I looked forward to Whitehead coming back. Also, I thought his dry sense of humor was hilarious.

Dr. Whitehead is a great instructor. Calculus is pretty dry, but when he can, he makes it funny. He tries to keep the mood light and everyone awake, and generally does a good job. Just watch out for the tests-- you have to know the material well because you can't use calculators. Take the extra credit opportunities he gives- you will need them.

I loved Whitehead for Calc 1, take him! His math jokes are awfully funny. I did feel like sometimes the practice questions we went over in lecture did not apply to hw though. & I also felt like I couldn't personally ask him questions. You TA will be great help though!
He is a great teacher! He teaches the content well, and also is very open to questions. He will even sometimes throw in a joke to the lecture.

Absolutely awesome! He teaches very clearly and can always teach you why the math is important and how we can apply it, which really helps you to enjoy the math. You should absolutely take a class from him.

Jared is a great guy, not much to complain about. Our class was honors and we got to learn how to do linear algebra using python on a basic level. He likes to make jokes and is willing to laugh with the class at our own jokes. Also he thinks 42 is the answer to everything which is awesome. Explains clearly and accessible during office hours.

Explains things very clearly, even though he speaks monotously. He goes through a lot of example problems, so he teaches all you need to know to do the homework, and for the test. He'll stop class once in a while, and he'll either throw a joke in there, or give some sort of useful life advice which was cool, and it helps you stay awake.

Very good at explaining tough concepts. He barely looks older than some of the students so he knows what it's like to be one. Calc is always tough but Whitehead makes it easier. Unfortunately the class is so large that you don't get a lot of personal attention from him; a lot of your success depends on your section TA and going to the labs.
Professor Whitehead likes to focus on the theory behind the mathematics instead of doing the math showing example problems. Your TA in the restitution classes can be very helpful.

Professor Whitehead was very clear in his example problems and taught everything we needed to know for the exams. He loved calculus and all math, and threw in enough jokes and attention-grabbers to keep the class awake. He spoke kind of monotonously, but his teaching was sound and very useful.

He is not very good at explaining things. Take this with another professor if you do not enjoy reading math textbooks in your free-time, sitting through boring lectures, or having your professor answer a question other than the question you actually asked.

Dr. Whitehead super chill and great to work with one-on-one. His lectures are usually pretty good, and he throws enough dry humor in to keep the people who are awake entertained. Fair grader, good teacher, great person. I hope I can take another class from him.

The class was extremely difficult, but Dr. Whitehead is super helpful and very interested in engaging his students in the course through relevant examples and constantly taking course feedback. Highly recommend him as a professor.

Dr. Whitehead is a special math professor in that he remembers what it is like to be a student. He excels at explaining difficult ideas simply. His tests are hard but fair. He is the kind of teacher that Math needs.

Dr. Hinckley was an amazing professor and I enjoyed taking Music 101 from him. It was a very easy class and did not have a lot of homework assignments. I took the class in one term and it was 6 hours of lecture each week and about 2 hours of homework. The lectures were hilarious and definitely worth the time.

I didn't love this class and thought the exams were pretty long for this just being a GE. I stopped attending class and did just fine though. You have to be able to identify a set list of pieces just by listening as well as be able to identify instruments by sight and sound in addition to understanding all the concepts discussed.

Dr. Hinckley is great! This class is super straightforward and is a great choice for a GE credit. You'll leave being more knowledgeable about the evolution of music over the decades. I attended lecture each week, but you hypothetically could pass the class without ever attending lecture, but you'll be missing out on a ton of extra information.

Dr. Hinckley is an amazing professor. He truly cares about what he teaches, and he's good at teaching it. He lets students know exactly what they need to do to succeed in his class, and he gives them every opportunity to do so. This class is a great way to fill a GE while gaining an appreciation for classical music.
I absolutely loved Dr. Hinckley's class. His lectures were always fun to go to, and his course content was highly digestible. I would 100% recommend taking this course if you have chance.

One of my favorite professors I have taken at BYU, His lectures are awesome and he is very passionate about what he teaches. You can also tell he genuinely cares about his students. He understands that most students in his class aren't studying music or have music backgrounds and adapts the course to fit that. I wish I could take more from him.

Dr. Hinckley is awesome. Great Art GE and easy A. You don't have to attend lectures, but honestly he made me appreciate music so much more than I expected to. If you can take this class from him do it.

Music 101 was a great GE and easy A. I am not musical at all and skipped this class a ton, but still ended with a 99%. Prof Hinckley is super kind and passionate about what he is teaching, he is funny and cares a lot about his students. You do have to attend 6 classical music concerts for this class, but it wasn't hard to find free ones on campus.

Lectures are 3 hours twice a week. Lots of reading and listening. Mandatory outside of class concert attendance. The exams are difficult and long. He is a nice guy but it isn't enough to make up for the stress and work load of the class.

Professor Hinckley is a great guy. He teaches well, although if you take this as a term class it can be a lot to read and take in (3 hour lectures). But all the tests and assignments are on learning suite. Not open note and long exams, but they are pretty simple if you do the readings and pay attention in class. Attendance not mandatory, but helps.
I have no interest in music history, but Professor Hinkley made each class really fun. He's super nice, and the work is pretty easy.

One of my favorite courses at BYU. Professor Hinckley is very knowledgable and engages himself in a wide range of subjects. He's open minded to all kinds of music and pop culture throughout history and you will learn a ton. The lectures are engaging and funny and the exams are fairly simple if you take notes and memorize the assigned listenings.
Great professor with engaging lectures. Exams are straightforward if you pay attention in class and review the listening exercises.

I love dr. hinckley. He's funny and the class is not hard. Its not the most interesting topic, but I took it with some friends and really enjoyed it. Take notes on the short readings each class and you'll easily get an A. You also have to go to 6 classical concerts, but the music building has multiple every week.

I had pretty much zero interest in the class topic, but Prof. Hinkley made each class very interesting to the point that I enjoyed each one! I took the class in one term, so lectures were long, but the assignments were never overwhelming. Straight up, if you pay attention in class and do the listening assignments, you can ace every test.

Professor Hinckley is AWESOME! I loved this class. You do light readings from his online textbook before class, and he lectures on what you read and gives tons of fun examples. Tests are super easy if you take reading notes and pay attention in class. He always takes time for comments and questions and is just a friendly and funny guy.

I took this class just for a GE and was surprised how much I ended up enjoying it. His grading criteria is incredibly clear and if you follow the instructions you'll do well. He also grades things quickly and gives feedback on each assignment. He's a funny guy and he basically tells you whats on the test in class, so showing up is helpful.

This class was seriously SO EASY and SO FUN! The lectures were very entertaining, I genuinely looked forward to them and Hinckley is so funny and does a great job at teaching the material! The course is also very organized and he has detailed instructions for all the assignments which is super nice. I highly recommend this professor and class!
I learned a lot in this class, he was very generous while grading things and gave amazing test reviews. If you pay attention in class and do the readings you can easily get an A.
I literally love Jaren so much, he brightened my day so many times. Please take this class. I love him, he is the most wholesome, funniest man I know

It's clear that Professor Hinkley knows what he's talking about, and he's very passionate about it. The whole goal of the class is to expose you to different styles and genres of music. Not too hard and he keeps it fun.

Professor Hinckley is an awesome professor! You can tell that he is passionate about music and loves his job, as well as cares about and loves his students. The class was very easy and attendance in class is optional. Would highly recommend for an arts GE!

Dr. Hinckley is a great professor and this class was both interesting and super easy. I took the term class, which was faster paced, but it wasn't hard work. His recorded test reviews are pretty dang good for studying for the tests. Also, class attendance isn't mandatory which is great! 10/10 would recommend!

Dr. Hinckley was amazing! He's super funny and tries to make class engaging. I thought the content was super interesting and this is the easiest GE I've ever taken. He offers extra credit and leaves clear feedback on assignments. I recommend taking the term option for this class because it seriously is that easy.

Professor Hinckley was great! The tests really aren't that difficult and the assignments are really straightforward. I honestly didn't go to class very often but I took thorough notes on the reading, so I thought the class was really easy.

The BEST prof I've had at BYU by far. His passion and real-life stories about the material kept every lecture a blast, and they enforced the book reading. Minimal homework. Exams seemed daunting at first, but ended up being pretty easy. Super nice guy who wants you to succeed, and truly gave me a deeper passion and understanding for music.

Professor Hinkley is super passionate about music. You need to go to quite a few concerts, but many free options exist. The tests are easy, and the posted video study guides powerfully help you. You don't need to buy textbooks if you are attending class. Overall, the class is simple.

Such a great GE! Dr Hinckley very passionate about music and you can tell. Even if you aren't super musically inclined, this is a great class. Pretty easy, you can get by without going to lecture if you keep up with the readings.
Lectures were so fun and helpful, honestly you don't have to read if you go
Holy this guy is the goat. I did't really love music or care about the history but he actually made it interesting and fun!
Great professor, fun content, manageable!

Hinckley was a great teacher. His class was extremely easy for an arts credit, and the homework would take me 30 minutes max. The only problem I had was that lectures felt pointless. I skipped class often because he just goes over the reading, which I did for homework. Tests were nice because they were taken online, wherever, whenever.

Prof. Hinckley makes this intro music class an absolute breeze. Lectures are engaging, and with the help of unstuckstudy ai and the free textbook, acing the tests is a piece of cake. Definitely an easy arts credit!
Prof Hinckley is a funny guy and you can really tell he loves music and music history. I would definitely recommend him for the general art req. His textbook is important, but super expensive though.
He is pretty good. But on some of the assignments its hard to know what you are supposed to do. also the test are super tricky.

Dr. Hinckley was a great professor! He had us mostly learn through reading the textbook and then showed us how to apply it in class which worked very well for the format of the tests. If you put in the work, this class is pretty easy and fairly rewarding.

For homework, you read a few pages of the textbook and then go over it in class with him. Two midterms and a final, and the final is NOT comprehensive, which is awesome. You have to go to 6 concerts and 3 of them require a very short writeup, but it's really easy. He is an amazing, nice, funny professor! Take his class, it's really easy and fun.

Prof. Hinckley was an amazing teacher. He explained everything well and was always willing to help. If you know anything about music, you'll be totally fine in this class. Gives good feedback on assignments and genuinely seems passionate about what he's teaching. Good intro class for music.

This may have been one of the easiest classes I've taken. Honestly if you read the textbook you could skip lectures and still get an A. Though he is really funny and entertaining so I did go to the lectures. I really didn't like the class material because it's more of a music history class but it's an easy arts credit and he's amazing.

Professor Hinckley is the GOAT. I took this class to fill my art general and professor Hinckely was so chill and funny. This class was really easy as long as you do the listening assignments and attend the review classes. Take music 101 from him!
Wow, wish I could take all my classes from Dr. Hinckley! He makes everything fun and interesting while still being organized and giving us the most.

Dr. Hinckley's class was a blast. I'd recommend taking this class with a friend if possible; it was a lot of fun that way going to concerts together etc. He's super good about telling you what you need to know and all exams are online! Just do the listening exercises, short readings, and go to lecture and you'll be good to go! He's funny too.

Professor Hinckley is incredible! I took the class as a general and, as someone with a heavy background in music, expected an easy but boring A. I was pleasantly surprised though-- it was still an easy A, but the lectures were entertaining and I learned tons! Professor Hinckley is very insightful and passionate about what he does. Highly recommend!

This professor is one of my favorites. He prepares you very well in lectures, study guides, and reminders. He constantly is reminding us of when things are due, tells you word for word what to look for on the exams, and makes lectures enjoyable. Do need to study well for exams for you have to memorize the info, and write good notes in class.

Professor Hinckley is AMAZING! He's very knowledgeable and makes the lectures interesting and fun. He's probably my favorite professor I've had. Homework consists of reading and listening but honestly you could get by without doing the readings.

Very nice guy and makes the class as fun as it can be for non-music majors. Don't buy the textbook, just pay attention in class and do the listening assignments and you'll ace the tests. Do the extra credit, it's super easy. Honestly, if you don't get an A in this class, that's on you. Prof. Hinkley makes this class very simple.

Prof. Hinckley was a pretty good professor. If you're in his MUS101 class, DO THE LISTENING ASSIGNMENTS! I can't emphasize that enough, it's the only way you'll pass. He's flexible if you have an emergency come up and will extend deadlines for some things which is awesome. You can tell he really does try his best and loves what he teaches

Professor Hinckley is awesome. Probably the most knowledgeable professor I've had at BYU. He is extremely well-rounded and cultured and I really appreciated that. You don't need to get the textbook to get an A if you study for the tests. I was pleasantly surprised.

Professor Hinckley is a great, talented, funny guy. I enjoyed his class, but made the mistake of taking the 1 term version instead of the full semester version, which meant I had 2 3 hour evening lectures a week. There is a lot of memorization involved, but other than that this class is not too difficult.

Professor Hinckley was great! Music 101 was very interesting and informative, without being stressful. It was made clear exactly what you needed to know for a test. Make sure to know the songs you're supposed to, and you should do very well. I didn't even need to take notes. I would definitely recommend! I would also take from him again.

If you missed class you'd immediately get behind. I learned most of the content in class. He required a textbook but the readings weren't as helpful as his lectures. Lots of listening to music, prepare to listen to stuff on repeat if you want an A. Listen memorize listen = A.
Very easy class. Taught me a lot I didn't know before, helped me get into classical music, and was simple in structure. All the tests are easy and straightforward.

This is my favorite class I have taken at BYU. Professor Hinckley is so kind and genuine. Lectures are engaging and insightful. He cares deeply about music and it shows. The homework/tests are straightforward. Subject matter is easy even if you don't come from a musical background. His puns are hilarious-I always left this class in a good mood.

I LOVED this class. Never thought I'd say I miss learning about classical music but I do. He's funny and teaches affectively. I thought concert attendance assignments would be more annoying but there's a lot of options on campus and you can do half online. Review sessions before tests were great. I just really loved this class and this teacher.

Nice guy, but can be boring. Super easy class, may be a little more challenging if you have no music background. Can get by not going to lectures. Test can be tough, but use the study guide and DO THE HOMEWORK and you'll be fine. 3 tests, 6 required concerts (3 can be online). Extra credit available and easy. Great easy credit.

Cool class, some of the music is pretty out there though. I didn't go to any lectures for the first test and got a B- so I decided to go to class, and just by sitting there I got 100 on the next exam. You can definitely do well if you don't go to class and just read the textbook/listen to Naxos, but I would recommend going.

Professor Hinckley is great! The lectures had a dose of fun and inspiration. If you read the textbook and attend the lectures (not mandatory, but they solidify the knowledge), you'll do great. There are 6 concerts to attend, and the workload is pretty light- also extra credit! Professor Hinckley teaches the class really well, highly recommend!

Took Music 101 to fulfill GE requirement and he was great! I took the 3 hour lecture version, he kept us engaged the whole time and we sometimes finished early. Tests you have to memorize tracks but he goes over everything you need to know. You also have to attend 6 concerts outside of class but he gives clear criteria of how to fill the out.

Dr. Hinckley was INCREDIBLE. I took his MUSIC101 course as a block class, which meant enduring 3-hour long lectures twice a week. But Hinckley did an absolutely amazing job making me feel engaged and interested in nearly every lecture (they rarely took all 3 hours.) Have an open mind, do the work, take good notes, and you will do just fine!

I always loved attending lectures. It is nice to sit through the lectures and actually enjoy learning what is being taught rather than rapidly taking notes. You're basically just graded on attending six concerts out of class and three online exams (not proctored or anything). He is passionate about what he teaches and it shows!

Dr. Hinckley was a great professor. His lectures were very interactive and you can tell he prepares a lot to help his students understand. He loves music and is very knowledgeable, that being said sometimes it's hard to relate to medieval music.The class is information-heavy but it is super easy to pass. It is sometimes boring but an easy A.

Professor Hinckley is hilarious! He really loves what he teaches and makes class fun. He'll often slip in a wholesome music joke that will make your day. You do daily reading and listening, so just make sure you do those. The six different concert attendances are easy too. As long as you pay attention to the readings and understand it, you're set!

Professor Hinckley was pretty great and I enjoyed this class. He knows a ton about music and makes his class very easy to get an A. The reading before class is very short, you have to go to 6 concerts, and he is super clear about what you should know for exams. Class was usually interesting and you'll find he has a funny sense of humor.

He gives assigned readings, then basically covers it all in class. Readings are very short. A huge portion of the tests is being able to recognize songs, but it is multiple choice. His class was very fun, and he was hilarious.

This class was a little hard to sit through but I don't regret taking it. You have to go to 6 classical music concerts and do a write up about each of them. The tests were very hard if you don't understand the concepts. The tests were based off of applying concepts you've learned and not definitions. There was a little extra credit which helped.

The lectures are long and it's hard to sit still for 2 hrs but it is also recorded and online which I suggest doing instead. He does exam reviews the day before the test opens so I suggest watching those lectures to pass tests. The textbook helps with the concert assignments and he is pretty lenient when it comes to grading those.
This class is easy. Just go to class and you will be fine. The tests are easy if you study a little bit. Take from Hinckley if you need to take music 101

Prof. Hinkley is really intelligent on music and does his best to make the class fun for non-musicians. So many great anecdotes about composers and stories of his life in performance. Highly highly recommend this class! I looked forward to class every day! If you care about classical music, you'll love this class.

Super easy A, never really had to go to class. Picky about the weirdest things on assignments. Professor is more concerned with giving his opinions to you about things than actually teaching you about the subject. He should be teaching music lessons, not a music class. 

Just buy the textbook and do all the online stuff and you'll be good.
Jaren Hinckley is very passionate about his job and inspires his students. I throughly enjoyed his class, even though the tests were a little tricky.

Professor Hinckley is awesome. He has a unique perspective on music, and teaches about music in an interesting and engaging way. He has a unique and subversive sense of humor. He's fun to talk to in-person after class, and all of his tests are 100% fair. The course is just the right difficulty for an entry level GE class.

This class is a great class to knock out an art credit. It's a free A as long as you do all the work. Beyond being easy, it was really enjoyable. Hinckley is a laid back professor. I only used the the textbook like three times so try to get it as cheap as you can
