classes are kinda boring (for anyone who has any background with music). buuuuut it's a good class. you do learn things - tests aren't too hard. TA reviews not very helpful...attend class even though you don't have to just because he gives a lot of answers to the tests. definitely the best teacher to take for Music 101.

Great class. Great professor! He's so funny and makes music fun. Even if you don't understand music and have no past experience with it you can succeed in this class. About 9 songs to listen to and "memorize" before each of the 5 tests -he'll usually play the most popular/memorable part.Attend 8 concerts. He'll make you enjoy music-even "classical"
Great teacher, easy class. Tests are easy as long as you learn the listening samples. Not much reading required.
Good teacher, 5 tests, no final.  You have to go to 8 concerts and write a paragraph for 4 of them.  Tests are fine, theyre not super easy, but they are do-able.  Good guy, kinda funny too.
Aside from the annoying music majors who would prattle on when called upon, the class was good. Dr. Hinckley does the best he can with a class of 150 kids in a dim auditorium

He is a very entertaining professor who communicates the concepts of the course with clarity and interest. I little to no interest in music before taking this course. After taking his course, I am considering taking more music courses. His lectures were a real treat.
I wasn't a big fan of class, but Dr. Hinckley is still a good teacher.

He makes quarky work. I loved his class and learned a ton of useful information about music.  His test questions are like reading comic books.  Well prepared with an I-pod full of strange selections. Lots of movie clips too.

Dr. Hinckley is one of the greatest teachers I have ever had.  I thought he did a really good job explaining the concepts.  The class was pretty easy, but interesting.  I looked forward to going to class every day.

Dr. Hinckley is pretty awesome. He's weird and spontaneous, which is a good thing in his case, but the class is easy. I got A's or high B's on all my tests and I didn't really study that much, but I still learned a lot about music. And if it helps, he's related to President Hinckley. His grandpa is Pres. Hinckley's cousin.overall, it's a fun class.
Dr. Hinckley was such a good teacher! I looked forward to the class every day and I enjoyed his music examples! He's very funny and very nice! I would totally recommend this class to anyone!
His was the best GE class I've ever taken! Not only did I score an easy A, but I learned a lot more than I thought I would. Recommended to anyone!

Easy, easy, easy. This is the deal with Hinckley's class: do the (small amounts of) work, get the A. That's all there is to it. It's not hard, the concepts aren't hard to understand, eight concerts really aren't that many to attend. Just do the work and get the A. Piece of cake.

Dr. H is an awesome teacher! He really loves the subject and is enthusiatic and funny. Some of his comments in class actually became inside jokes between my friends and I. He involves the class in the lectures, and is very easy to talk to. He is also very respectful of students. The class itself was a piece of cake, easy to get a high A in.

This was the funnest class. Dr. Hinckley is an amazing teacher and quite funny. It is a very easy A if you already have some back ground in music and if you don't then it would still be an esay A but you just have to learn and understand music terms. I loved this class and would highly recommend it!

you will have to listen to some lame music... but it's a fairly easy class.  most test questions come straight from the book.  you will also have to attend 8 concerts on your own time, but it's easy points...
Hinckley is way funny, he will do almost anything to help you learn. He covered everything in the lecture, reading was a waste. I really enjoyed this class, take it, its fun!
The class is an easy A. The tests are easy if you study, but the lectures can be boring. There is minimial writing, just four concert reports. Overall it is a good class.

Thoroughly enjoyable class, and you can't help but love Dr. Hinckley! Easy, but I learned a lot. If you miss a class or five, just make sure you go to the review sessions- they'll tell you everything you need to know for the tests. And for the record, Dr. Hinckley's exam actually made me laugh out loud in the testing center.
Here's a great professor: funny, knowledgeable, reasonable.  The class was easy and entertaining, but I learned a lot in it.  The tests were actually fun to take.

This class was great! The course felt relaxed, but you still learn a lot of stuff (that unlike other GE's, is actually interesting and useful). Dr. Hinckley tests are easy because they focus on vocab and basic concepts (that he hammers in lecture). It was the once class where I could relax and learn

One of the easiest and most enjoyable classes I have taken.  Tests and assignments are very straightforward.  Easy to get an A if you attend class and read the material, which isn't very much. Highly recommend.

This class was really easy, but I learned a lot. If you listen in class, he will tell you 100% of the information that is on the test. If you miss a day, it is ok, just go to the TA session right before the test. If you are worried about the listening examples of music, don't worry, they are easy.

Not only was the class a very nice break from the rest of my schedule, but I also learned a lot and Dr. Hinckley made the class very enjoyable. He is a great teacher, and it shows that he loves to teach. I highly recommend him as a professor.
Easiest class I have ever had.  The tests are just plain ridiculous.  Go to the help sessions and they will straight up tell you 90% of the answers for each test. Easy A
one of the best classes I've ever taken! Dr. Hinckley knows the stuff and is a great guy to listen to! You learn a lot and have fun at the same time! I recommend it!
Great teacher---funny guy, passionate about his subject. He'll also work with you, but he's not going to let you get away with murder so don't try to take advantage of him. I highly recommend.
I really enjoyed this class. It made me appreciate music that I don't usually like. The tests are very easy if you just study for them.
This class was great. Hinckley is very entertaining and very clear when teaching. This class isn't hard at all. You just have to make sure you study. Highly recommend Hinckley. He is SO funny.
He is great.  Entertaining and also helpful.  I do question the intensity of this class as a 100 level GE class?????  I think it should be easier.

It's pretty obvious that Dr. Hinckely loves teaching. He is cool. His tests were hard for me. It seems that the tests should have been written for music majors. But it's a fun class. The only thing were the tests that got me.
I loved this class!  The tests really weren't bad, but lectures were fun and Dr. Hinckley is a very reasonable person.
Awesome teacher and knows his stuff.  Lectures are fun and entertaining.  He's great at giving examples.  I wouldn't consider the tests EASY necessarily, but rather, reasonable.
Very easy class, and Dr. Hinckley is a nice guy with easy test.
not bad
Interesting and pleasant person.

This class builds on earlier classes by applying the theory to real-world situations. The lectures are engaging, it's clear Professor Pope cares. The readings can be lengthy, and the course structure isn't very clear at the start, but it becomes more organized as the semester goes on. Overall, I enjoyed the class and would certainly recommend it.

Professor Pope is very enthusiastic about teaching this class which made it so much more interesting. This really is an applied economics class with a specific emphasis on environmental economics, so definitely recommend taking econ 398 to prepare. The quizzes and tests were a little hard to prepare for.

Coach Pope is great! He has a lot of fun and you'll definitely feel more welcomed to BYU after taking UNIV with him. It's obvious he cares about everyone in the class and he makes you feel very known.
This guy is a legend. Class is very hard but he wants you to succeed. Funny guy
Professor Pope is awesome! He truly cares for each student and has a very interactive class.

I love Coach Pope as a person, and he is really a very smart guy, but I had a hard time following his lectures and I did not find his tests to be super fair. He believes in his students and will try his best to help you out when you reach out to him. This class was not a terrible experience, but you should try not to take courses from him.
THIS IS A REVIEW FOR UNIV.  I took him for UNIV 101 and he was amazing!  Would definitely recommend him for UNIV.
Doctor Pope is great! He is so kind and friendly, and the class is very reasonable. I thought all the assignments were valuable and the quizzes are not too hard. All in all it's a great class!

Dr pope's class was much easier than 388, and the beginning of the class is the hardest part, the entire second half is just working on your project and doing hypothetical analysis. I loved his class and I would take it again! My grade was lower than I wanted, I bombed the final after I felt super solid in the class content.

Dr. Pope is clear and patient in explaining concepts and connecting theories with real-life cases. He and our TA were super helpful in my research paper on DST energy saving. It was the first time I took an empirical-based Econ class, but with Dr. Pope, I felt working well. Start the project early, take detailed notes in class, and you'll get an A.

Dr. Pope explained the concepts of econometrics very clearly and was good at bringing in real world examples and studies to explain his points. He does have reading every class and he will call on you to make sure you did the reading. I found this motivating to keep up on readings and class work. He is also nice and loves what he does.

The class itself was good and Dr Pope really does a good job at being accessible at all times. It's easy to ask questions and you can expect good answers. The class itself wasn't structured super clearly and the grading criteria and learning objectives were also not clear at all. Otherwise it's a great class and a good professor.

Professor Pope is an outstanding professor. For context, I was a repeat student. I had him for both Econ 382 and Econ 398. He makes difficult concepts fun and easy to understand and provides an unmatched level of personal attention to students that just ask for some help. I can't recommend him enough. As always, be prepared to work.

Professor Pope does a great job at helping you out as an individual student. He is passionate about both the subject and your success. I came out of it more pleased with what I learned than with any other economics course. I highly recommend this course and its professor.

Professor Pope teaches this class really well! I didn't really get it all the way all the time, and sometimes the papers we have to read are kinda tough to understand but the class is really cool. definitely get a partner for the project though, I wish I had done that

This was one of my favorite ECON classes I have taken. Professor Pope was extremely helpful with our final project which made it a really good learning experience. You have all the resources you need to succeed in this class.

Really great class in understanding research better, especially for those whose math skills are rusty. Homework, tests, and the class project are not easy but if you show Pope your effort and have a genuine interest, he is happy to help. He's a great professor for those who don't love proofs. An A is very possible, but attendance is a must.

Professor Pope is the lecturer I understand best in the entire department. I took this class with him while it was still considered 488, but it was an amazing experience. I learned the material very well and felt much better about my understanding of econometrics after this class. I can't recommend Professor Pope enough.

ECON 398 is a great class and Professor Pope does a good job teaching it. The problem sets he assigns are much more conceptual (as opposed to math-heavy practice sets common in other ECON classes), and usually didn't take longer than 1-2 hours to complete. The tests were fair and the practice tests he provided for those were very helpful.

I think Pope's teaching style is unlike most professors, hence the bad reviews. If you have ADD, the stories are helpful. 382 from Pope was the easiest econ class I took. I guess I can understand the reviews about his lectures seeming patronizing, but it never seemed condescending to me. He's explaining new concepts like you are a little kid.

I was scared going into Prof Pope's class because of the score, but he was a really good professor! If you put in the time then you can definitely do good in this class. He believes that he teaches you tools and then tests and homework he expects you to apply those tools in a variety of different ways.

I was really scared to take his class based on his score, but he was perfectly fine/normal, so idk what people are talking about on here. He wasnt revolutionary but he was a good, solid teacher, extremely fair grader, & always willing to take time to help outside of class. Good guy, solid teacher. Definitely as good as any other BYU econ teacher.

I love professor Pope. He knows economics and he is genuinely interested in helping you learn it. Go to class, don't be a jerk, do the homework during office hours and you'll enjoy the class and learn a lot. Econ classes are hard no matter what professor you get, but he did a very good job

Dr. Pope teaches this class in his own way, which might be hard for some students at the start. Pros: no need to read the textbook; he explains hard concepts with vivid examples; lectures and slides are put on LS; nice TA. Cons: HWs are hard so go to TA office hour or search problems from the textbook; I was completely lost in behavioral economics.
Dr Pope does not seem to mean to be this way, but I completely concur with other reviews saying that Dr Pope is condescending and patronizing. Dont take courses from him if you can avoid it.

If you absolutely have to take it from him, you can make it work. But if possible, take it from someone else or wait another semester. He does genuinely try and is a nice guy, but he's just not a good teacher. Tests and homework do NOT match the in-class material, and he's not good at explaining difficult material. Will cause you a lot of grief.

I didn't gel well with his teaching style and class structure. He tries to be enthusiastic but it felt forced and he treated us like little kids. My least favorite part of the class structure was the self-graded idea journal because I grade myself harsher than others. Also, some test questions felt like they came out of nowhere.

I genuinely loved going to Professor Pope's class. He is so passionate about economics and makes class so interesting. He also cares a lot about his students. His problem sets and tests can be confusing, but the TA is there to help and is very helpful. I would recommend Professor Pope!

I beg you in the name of all that is holy to not take 382 from Pope. The homework and tests are very difficult and seem to be totally independent of the material covered in class. Also, the TA was MIA all semester and we suffered big time. Take it from someone else. I have taken a LOT of classes at BYU and this is the worst I have had. AVOID PLZ

He's a good professor, especially if you learn by engaging with the teacher. this semester(winter 2019) The class was organized around relaxing the assumptions of perfect competition 1 by 1. He went out of his way to relate how this set of lectures relates to everything we've already talked about. Biggest complaint is a lack of study guides.

Dr. Pope is a great guy. He cares about Econ and he comes prepared with a lecture that he thinks will blow your socks off. However, he makes you more confused than when you walked in. All his examples are written on the board and most of the time they make no sense. The homework assignments are tough because 80% of them have no relation to class.

It's not too hard to get a good grade. He teaches the testable material clearly enough. That being said, I didn't love the teaching style. He felt paternalistic to me which I know is a weird complaint. In 380, reading the textbook helped me do better in the class but for this class, reading the textbook wasn't helpful because he taught his own way.
Seemed irritated when asked questions about content. Stopped asking questions after a while because of his poor responses. Would take from someone who is better at helping his students understand.
Enthusiastic, friendly, and organized. This was an interesting and useful class.

Lectures can make the material seem easier than it really is. Really pay attention to what you do in class and on the homework (definitely go to the TA for help) and you'll do fine. He's a good lecturer and a good professor overall.

I don't know what's going on. He seems to neglect his teaching prep, and is always flustered. Lectures are the same every semester, and exactly the same if you took his 382 course, maybe he neglects his teaching because he is so busy doing amazing research, I dont know.  Expectations are confusing. Don't take a class from him. Nice guy though.
Don't take this class from Jaren, take it from his father......
The concepts learned in the course are not very difficult to grasp. Tests are very ambiguous and unfair...... If you can guess what he is trying to say, you are a wizard.

He would be wise to ask for a little feedback on his problem set and exam questions. The concepts in this course are really easy to understand, applying them is pretty simple, but understanding what Dr. Pope wants for an answer is a complete guessing game. Study as hard as you want, it won't matter, your grade will be up to chance anyway.
He needs to spend more time teaching rather than telling stories. Good guy, not the best professor I've had.

His tests are pretty ambiguous. Even if you understand all the material and do the practice exams, you still won't understand what he is asking on tests. An example to illustrate "Does the sun rise in the morning?" Obviously the answer is yes, but if he asked this question his answer would be, "No at 7:20 am it ascends" And you would have missed it

Sometimes lectures are a bit confusing and you might need help to understand what the questions are asking on the HW, but the material is interesting and you can tell he likes teaching.  Tests and homework aren't easy but they are fair.

I can second what has already been posted about this professor teaching to the whiteboard. In my opinion the homework and tests were too hard and the lectures poorly prepared students to succeed on them--even if they put in the time and studied. TA was essential to passing. My A- was simply a result of a VERY generous curve.

I did not know how bored the human body could become until I took this class from Dr. Pope. One specific thing that bugged me was that he talks to the whiteboard the whole class. When he asks if you have questions you  literally have 1 second to come up with a question or the opportunity is gone. Avoid this professor if possible. TA is a must.

Professor Pope is a great professor. Very intelligent. Very helpful and interested in students' learning. Tests were fair; the problems were problems from class or the homeworks. However, the homeworks were often unrelated to class material. He posts keys for the homework, which helps for studying. He's a great professor and I high recommend him.
Enthusiastic professor with a knack for teaching.  Class was a great experience and I learned a lot.

I really enjoyed this class. Pope is very passionate and gets excited, which was great. You won't need to read the textbook, but class notes, homework, which   you will need the TAs help with usually, and past exams are a must to do well, but if you do that, you'll be in good shape. I liked this class a lot.

It took me about half of the semester to figure out Dr. Pope's style - but once I did I really thrived. He is extremely energetic, and tries interesting approaches in his teaching style, which were much appreciated. Take lots of notes, class problems will be on homework and tests. Go to TA reviews and hours. This class is tough but doable.

Very passionate about his research and his profession.  Kind of fun to watch him get excited.  Class is fairly easy, but lectures are a little dry.  He basically just reads off his power point slides, and then does math on the board.  The project was fun, but it will push you.  He was always helpful when speaking with him personally.

The first half of this class is a joke, but he didn't require a final and made us a do a paper using the hedonic model. He doesn't get close to even explaining how to do the project til 3 weeks before it's due and was very stand off ish when you went to him in person for help.

Watts is genuinely an amazing human being, but this was the most stressful class. Each test was a different format, and one of the tests was supposed to be an oral exam and then she changed it to a testing center exam with only a few days notice. She doesn't teach or lecture, because she just asks for students' thoughts literally the entire class.

Class with Prof Watts is so interesting! Readings are a reasonable length, and class discussions are so interesting! She knows her stuff and knows how to teach it, and she loves hearing student thoughts. No busywork, lots of support to complete the few assignments. Super chill and I learned a ton. WOuld totally take again!

ENGL 251 isn't really a thing anymore, apparently, but Prof. Watts is the best! She cares so much about her students and wants them to succeed! She was flexible and willing to work with us when some deadlines seemed tough. If you have the chance, take a class from her because she is such an amazing human being! I loved her lectures and this class!
Learned a lot from this class, but the tests were killer. Dr. Watts is a great professor and knows her field very well.

I had to take 295 for my major and I wouldn't recommend this class. It was very overwhelming, she often went on tangents rather than give clear instruction. I have email her to ask specific questions about my work because she fails to tell me in class. If you disagree with her she will disregard your opinion entirely. She takes days to email back.

While I really enjoyed her class content, I found Professor Watts rather unprofessional. There were multiple incidents in which she would express opinions and or make 'claims' that were just not appropriate for a professor (as an individual in a position of power) to share with her students. The class itself is fairly easy and interesting though.

Professor Watts is an amazing teacher. She is very kind and cares about all her students. Her classes are funny with her comments and examples. The class itself can be a bit difficult, but she makes it really easy to understand. If you don't understand, she encourages you to talk to her so she can better explain everything. You won't regret taking!

Dr. Watts is amazing. She's brilliant, passionate and classy. I gained a lot of respect for her as the semester went on because she just wanted to help us, and understands what we're feeling. There are three main papers that do require lots of work, but she helps us through well. It will stretch you but it's worth it! Take Watts!

I love Dr. Watts! This class completely changed the way I write papers. I feel so prepared for my upper-division English classes now. If I could take every class from her, I would! You definitely have to work for your grade, but she's reasonable and it's so worth it.

Dr. Watts was very enthusiastic and it spread to the students even though it was at 8:30 . The readings are diverse enough that you get a taste of everything but you do go through a lot of readings. The tests were intimidating but she curved them. Make sure you memorize dates, titles, and authors of works and you'll be set. Participation is huge!

Professor Watts was an absolutely dream! Class attendance is a must and the discussions are excellent. If you attend class you'll have no trouble with the exams and she really wants to help you love the literature. One of the best professors I've had!

I loved taking this class from Professor Watts. She really knows her stuff and helps the students gain a deeper understanding for the works. It's difficult, and she grades on what she fells your participation was, but overall it was a great class.

Not only is Dr. Watts the coolest (runs marathons, impeccable fashion sense) but she genuinely prepares you for academia by increasing the caliber of your writing & thinking critically/creatively. This class is hard work, but she's accessible and gives valuable constructive criticism. She taught me so much & I would definitely take from her again.

Dr. Watts is probably my favorite professor at BYU. She expects a lot from her students but she prepares you and gives you lots of tools to succeed. She's brilliant and funny, and I always looked forward to class. Whenever I had a question or concern, she was willing to meet with me and give me legitimate help and feedback. She's the best!

She is not the most clear when she teaches, just blabs a lot about her opinions, and if you disagree with her you will be treated differently. She doesn't respect different ways of thinking, and she is arrogant and often class was just her trying to show off knowledge. Would never recommend this class to anyone.

This is my favorite class I've ever taken at college, and that's saying a lot. I wanted to study English before 251, but experiencing Dr. Watts's amazing teaching really solidified that decision -- my classmates and I were sitting outside the classroom hugging and feeling depressed on the last day because we never wanted to leave. Brilliant.

I love Dr. Watts. I've taken two classes from her and have found her to be incredibly engaging, passionate, and dedicated. She definitely knows what she is talking about and is good about managing course work and fair grading.

This class was great! Don't let her syllabus scare you. She's notorious for her occasionally humongous reading assignments: there's the textbook (which is actually an awesome book) and then actual literature to read. Give yourself permission to skim, most everything gets read in class. Weekly response papers (easy), 1 short answer midterm, 1 final.
Got to know the students well, was helpful with questions, really interesting discussions and activities.

This class changed the way I look at the world. I would take from her again in a heartbeat. She's not super easy, but it's well worth it. There were a lot of times when I was confused by the hw, but her lectures made everything clear. For me, participation was key for understanding. She tries really hard to make everyone's opinion count.

I took her class because of this site. I was disappointed. Nice lady. Passionate about what she does. Not a great teacher. I would never take another class from her. She's not clear. She's not interested in your opinion, which is fine, just don't expect me to raise my hand. Her mid-term is a joke. The class is a waste of time.

I gave her a 2 on easiness - don't let that dissuade you. That's not to say you can't earn an A.  This is one of those classes where I really feel that every effort is rewarded. Put in the time and you'll do great. That said, Dr. Watts is incredible, funny, clear, passionate, and kind and her lectures are entertaining, informative, and involved.

Dr. Watts makes a hard class worth your time. She changed the way I looked at the world in the best way possible. Her passion for this material is second to none. If there is any professor to take English 251 from... take it from her. It's her favorite class to teach and that makes all the difference.

Dr. Watts crushes it. The course sounds so daunting, but she makes it all so clear. The best teacher you could expect to have for 251. There is a lot of reading, but it's all so good. This class expanded my world. I love Dr Watts.

Take this class! Texts that I thought were indecipherable and murky (uh...Barthes, Derrida and Foucault), I now understand with perfect clarity thanks to Prof. Watts. The material is mind-blowing, and I can now say that I know what it takes to be successful English major and critical thinker. Prof Watts is also super energetic and very, very helpful outside of class.

Let me sum up Professor Watts: capable, energetic, passionate about the subject, and smart as a whip. She's super interested in her student's opinions and encourages class discussion. A tip for anyone taking classes from her: read the works, take notes in class and study that for tests. Even if you think you understand the stuff, STUDY.

Dr. Watts is clear, helpful, energetic, and funny. I learned TONS in her writing class. I'm ashamed of anything I've written before I took it, and excited to write now that I have. Class is a little difficult with a lot of writing, but Dr. Watts helps whenever you need help.

I had a vastly different Watts than the rest of the reviewers. Midterm was awful and if you bomb it, you will bomb the entire class (even with extra credit points and 100%s on assignments.) She clearly knows her stuff, but hasn't showed it off - we just read other people's reviews ALL THE TIME. You'll kill 9000 trees printing all the readings too.

So much energy and great enthusiasm. Beautiful (like amazingly beautiful, if that sort of thing matters to you) and BRILLIANT. Dr. Watts knows her stuff. Tough grader but fair. You won't regret taking this class...i'm a far better writer because of her lessons and dedication.

Dr. Watts is amazing. She was clearly passionate about the material we were covering (Virginia Woolf). I was impressed with her knowledge of the difficult books we were reading. She gets to know her students and cares about their success. She's professional and funny, highly educated but down to earth. I think her assignments were worthwhile and her grading fair. If you do the work, your grade will reflect your effort. BYU needs to keep her. I'm convinced she's the best professor in the dept.

I've never had a professor care as much as Professor Watts. She made difficult literary theories clear and understandable, her lectures were well planned out and exciting, and her feedback on my written work was useful. She's tough, but I learned more in this class than any other class I've taken as an English major.  Take a class from her!!

She made us do our midterm in an hour time limit, which wasn't even close to enough time since barely any class members finished it in that time. Then she tried giving us extra credit assignment papers to help our grades, but it didn't help. She's a good professor, but I got a B instead of the A that I wanted just because of the stupid midterm.
Professor Watts is great.  She is really invested in helping the students improve their writing.  I felt like I became a much better writer because of her.

Professor Watts is easily one of my favorite professors at BYU. You can easily tell that she invests herself into the material as well as into each student. It isn't an easy class, but it made me a far better writer. Not just stylistically, but in a way that allowed me to think more deeply into a subject.

Great professor! Assignments were not too difficult, and as long as you do the papers and reading you can get a good grade. She keeps class interesting and is more than willing to help you on any assignments. Would definitely recomment this class.

Dr. Hansen has amazing energy and was always to upbeat while teaching. His slides were nice to reference, but I wish he did more on the board practice. There is just so much homework and the tests are hard. Chemistry is hard.

The chem department rotates on teaching 105, so if you ever have the opportunity to take a class from Dr. Hansen, TAKE IT! This class is really rigorous by nature, but if you are willing to put in the time for reading, studying and attendance, you will do great. He gives amazing lectures and is very engaging so it's never a bore.

Things seemed to make sense in lecture, but by the time I got to the homework, it was like I'd never seen it before. Good lectures, but every once in a while made a (very slightly) off-color joke. Homework consists of Problem Sets (find Jeremy Halversen on YouTube!! LIFE. SAVER.) and Smart work (digital) assignments. Class is very hard but doable.

Dr. Hansen was good enough, but he is definitely one of those professors with an ego. He made concepts seem totally manageable and then the tests were super difficult. However, CHEM 105 was not as bad as everyone says it is. The final is super hard and takes a long time, but if you put in a good amount of effort into this class you should be fine.

Take from him!!! He is so good at explaining. Chem 105 in general is designed to be a hard course but he made it better for sure. Loved him. So friendly and easy to talk to. I attended office hours frequently and he took the time to explain tough subjects.

Classes were entertaining! He is passionate about chemistry. There was a lot of homework outside of class, but grades are mostly based on exam performance. Difficult and heavy class, but Professor Hansen was good at making it fun! I liked that he did lots of practice examples for harder concepts.

Listen guys, (gender neutral) Chem 105 is a difficult class no matter who you take it from, but Dr. Hansen is a great option. His lectures are engaging and he is really good at explaining things multiple times so they make sense. He's so passionate and funny. If you need to take Chem 105 and he's teaching it, take it from him.

I was a TA for this professor, and he is definitely the best chem professor for general chemistry! He is hilarious, kind, and communicates well with the class. His lectures are organized and are applicable to the exams. Chem 105 is overall a tough class, but as a TA, I would for sure say that he is the guy to take it from!

The chem department is praying on our downfall. Dr. Hansen is super awesome tho. He is obviously an expert in his field and answers your questions thoroughly. There is a high volume of work and exams are worth 70% of your grade. I failed my first test, but kicked into gear thereafter. You can get that A. Just don't get caught off guard.

I worked as a TA for this professor and two others (Asplund and Woodfield). Hansen is by far the best option. His lectures are informative and actually helpful. Your TA is your best resource; find a good one if yours is iffy. Readings aren't really necessary, all the tests come from the problem sets and practice exams.
Honestly really enjoyed his class and lectures. While it's hard, it's definitely possible to get an A. Tough class but Dr. Hansen is the right prof for it.

This class is ridiculously hard for no reason. A huge portion of the class did not pass. That being said, Dr. Hansen taught it the best he could. If you MUST take chem 105, take it with him. Work crazy hard, pray you get a good TA, and you will be fine.

Chem 227 was awesome - probably one of my favorites. Dr. Hansen is a very entertaining lecturer and really cares about helping his students figure out their experiments and grades. This looks like a hard class, and it kinda is, but it's so fun and way less work outside of class than Chem 113.
Super funny, really bright, and a very respected professor! Tough course, but Dr. hansen grades fairly and is very helpful when you reach out.

I personally don't feel like it matters which professor you take from for Chem 105 because every class gives out the same homework, exams, and labs. I did enjoy taking from Professor Hansen because his class was entertaining and he was really funny. These tests are just really hard, so good luck!
You could could give this class everything youve got and still score low on the exams. Theres also so much busy work that you dont have a lot of time to understand the concepts. Hes funny tho

This class was taken online during COVID but was run completely by the TAs. The professor wasn't reachable at all and all of the video recordings looked like they were from the late 90s. That being said, I seemed to have an easier experience in his class than my friends who had other professors

CHEM 105 is inherently tough, but he definitely didn't do anything to make it easier. He seemed very uninvolved with the actual teaching. I don't even know what he looks like because he only had us watch pre-recorded lectures from another professor made in the 90s and told us to go to the TAs for help.
I had to take this class 4 times to pass. It was so hard.

Ended up being his TA over the span of three years. This guy is solid. With departmental exams, his classes consistently scored higher than those of other professors. He teaches it almost every semester (at least up until Apr 2021), so he can go pretty quick, but everything in the class is set up to benefit you. It takes work, but you can do it.

He did nothing the entire semester. He made us watch pre-made videos and if we needed help he made us go to the TAs. He also openly said some of the material was too easy and he went out of his way to make the exams a lot harder. I wouldnt trust the rating on here.

Hard to say much about Prof. Hansen himself. It seems like he isn't very involved in the educating, as he used pre-recorded lectures from another professor, and then the assignments were all through other websites. He is very accessible and helpful if you have a question or problem. Tests are hard and homework is daily! Not an easy class.

Prof. Hansen is awesome, funny, explains things clearly. I'd already done CHEM101 and 285 but this class was still tough! That's the way CHEM105 is though. Graded on iClickers during class, Smartworks, recitation problem sets, labs, 3 midterms and a final (which can replace one midterm). If you don't get a good TA just go to a different recitation.

Chem 105 is brutal but Dr. Hansen was great. I really liked lecture and this was while we were on zoom. Our class scored much higher than the other chem classes on the first two tests. The third test was brutal because it was a weird format. If you have to take this class Hansen is great.

Any Chem 105 class is hard, but Dr. H is great! Honestly if you are willing to put in the work, an A is possible. If you are willing to pay attention to the lectures, do ALL the homework, go to TA reviews (which I would strongly recommend), and study you should be fine. (Also if you plan to taking future chem classes, then this won't be too bad :)

Chem 105 is a hard class, but if you have to take it, trust me: YOU WANT HANSEN! He loves chem and genuinely wants you to love it too. His lectures are interesting and understandable, and he cares about his students! This class takes a lot of work, but if you do the homework, go to the TA reviews, and take the practice tests, you'll ace the exams.
Dr. Hansen is a great teacher! The class is super hard, but Hansen explains the concepts well and gives you all the resources to do well in the class. Definitely the best CHEM105 teacher at BYU!

Hansen is an amazing professor! He moves really fast, but checks for understanding and loves answering questions. Generous drop policy. Do the reading before class if you struggle with concepts so you know what's going on. Never skip lab or lecture and make sure you have a study group and you will do great in this class!

HANSEN IS THE BEST!!! He moves quickly, so be prepared, but he really cares about students, answers questions, keeps lectures light and will take the time to slow it down if needed. I also had an awesome TA for the class, so it was easier for me to grasp concepts. Use a lot of time out of class to study and DO NOT SKIP LECTURE OR LAB

Dr. Hansen is a great professor. He moves very quickly through material though. Chem 105 is difficult no matter who you take it from. Textbook reading and utilizing your TA will save you. There is a ton of HW and if you do it all, you can manage an okay grade. Expect to spend a TON of time studying for this class.

Hansen is an amazing teacher and I recommend him if you're anxious about Chem 105. He knows the material very well, jokes around a lot, and teaches simply but fast. The Chem 105 tests are harder than the examples he goes over in class, so be prepared.

If you have to take CHEM 105, take it from Hansen. This course is hard no matter what professor you get, but he makes it entertaining and he cares about his students. A lot of hw you have to do, but it's good practice for the tests. The problem sets helped more than the smartworks. Some people didn't get good TAs, but I did so I got a lot of help.

Chem 105 is a difficult class. Hansen's lectures are really helped. He is very engaging and honest. He will repeat and emphasize key concepts. So, you know what you will be tested on. If you have to take Chem 105, take it from him. He is one of the best. Also! Make sure you like your TA. They can make or break the class.

Professor Hansen teaches the material in a way that I could understand. Chem 105 is a hard class with any professor. Be ready to spend 10 or more hours a week on this class. The only downside is that he moves through material very quickly. The TA's help with that though. He is a funny professor and loves saying, "Guys, gender neutral.".

This was my favorite class at BYU so far. I feel that Dr. Hansen provided me with every resource needed to succeed. To get a solid grade I recommend doing every textbook reading plus textbook problems, attend every review possible, review lecture slides, (I think taking notes is a waste of time) and redo problem sets. Dr. Hansen was excellent.

Professor Hansen is a great teacher, clear, concise, and understandable. Gives a lot of Homework, but the problem sets really help you learn the material and prepare for the tests. The Tests are like the problems sets, but difficult nonetheless, and since they make up most of your grade, you will need to study A LOT. With work, an A is achievable.

Dr. Hansen is awesome! Like Chem105 sucks, but he helps to make it at least bearable. Hes also great at teaching clearly but in an entertaining way. Hes focused on helping people understand instead of just rushing through the material.

Dr. Hansen is such a great professor. His lectures are always fun and lighthearted, he is so funny, I loved them. He also is very clear in how he teaches and is always willing to re-explain during lecture to help you understand. Chem 105 is a hard class and requires work, there's no getting around that, but Dr. Hansen made it enjoyable! 10/10

I took it online and never actually met Dr. Hansen. But this is the most organized online class I've ever taken. If you're motivated enough to take online classes, this is a really solid choice. Lots of other assignments help the tests to be weighted less. Flexible and I feel like I really learned a lot!

Very hard class, but bright and fun teacher. He is THE best option for this class. I think he was a great teacher though the material and concept are very challenging. I recommend in part b/c of how good he is and in the other part b/c of how much other students said they struggled b/c how rough it was to understand from the other professors.

Dr. Hansen made CHEM 105 as interesting as it could be. The class itself is just really hard no matter which professor you have, so don't take him thinking it will be easy. I had a really good TA who also helped a bunch. The tests are with 70% of your grade, and they are made to confuse you. Hard class, but he made it better than it could have been

Dr. Hansen is very intelligent and HILARIOUS! This class sucks but he makes it entertaining. Online hw is stupid and crashes all the time. Paper hw due every recitation. Labs every week. Go to as many reviews as possible and take advantage of your TAs. You have 4 tests and they were all trash. Do the reviews and don't be afraid to ask questions.

This class is hard, but from what I heard from other classes, Hansen is one of the best professors to take it from. His lectures were a little boring sometimes but he put in funny stories to make it a little better. There is a lot of reading to do, smartwork, and problem sets each week, but that is what is expected for Chem 105.

Sorry that you have to take Chem 105. The class is gonna be tough whoever you take it from, but Hansen makes it bearable. He is funny and good at explaining tough concepts. He basically gives you the answer to most Iclicker quizzes and he blows stuff up on Fridays.

Dr. Hansen was the best Chem 105 prof. I could imagine. He is very organized and excited about his lectures. He even has explosion Fridays which was a plus. It will be a hard class no matter who teaches it, but he is a great choice.

No matter who you take this class from, it's going to be a lot of work. There's so much material to cover and not enough time to do so, but Prof. Hansen does a pretty good job at covering as much as possible. He's entertaining and willing to meet one on one. This class is not that hard if you put in the time and go to the TA lab.

Having taken CHEM106, I know that Professor Hansen did a very poor job in teaching CHEM105. We got through an entire powerpoint about 8 times that entire semester, and were always behind other CHEM105 classes (which all had the same tests). Dr. Hansen left for a week, and gave us TA's who would just read us the lecture. Would not take from him

You all know that Chem 105 is a weeder class. It's supposed to be like that. But it has to be done! Honestly I wouldn't have picked anyone else to teach me. Dr Hansen is my favorite professor at BYU so far! He is amazing at explaining, he is so funny, and he answers questions very well! If you have to take this class, take Hansen!!!!

Thank goodness for Dr. Hansen. Hes probably been the best professor Ive had so far! Hes engaging, he cares, and he knows his stuff. The material is difficult, but hes more than willing to help and actually cares how well his students do. I have a learning disability, and would have crashed and burned without his help.

Dr. Hansen is a great professor and really cares about his students success. He wants to help all students pass so take advantage of his office hours and TA's. Tests are really hard, but if you know how to work through practice problems and homework, you'll be fine. He is a solid choice.

Dr. Hansen is a great professor. Any problems with the course that I had came because of how it is set up (as a weed out course). No avoiding that unfortunately. Do yourself a solid and pick Hansen for this class, you won't regret it.

Dr Hasen is a good professor. He is really engaging in lecture. Chem 105 is a difficult course no matter who you take it from, but he really cares and attendance isn't required but you do iClicker quizzes every lecture that are worth points (that you need!) Loved the professor just hated the course.

Dr. Hansen is a great professor. He really knows what he's talking about, and explains it in a simple way. If you don't understand don't be afraid to ask questions. He uses a lot of visual examples to show what he's teaching. He's hilarious. His tests will include everything you learned, so make sure to study up on the "insignificant" details.

Dr. Hansen is so great! You definitely need to attend and do extra work and studying outside of class, but his lectures are entertaining and vety helpful. He and his TA's are very accessible and willing to help. Some of the "busy work" can be tedious but doing it absolutely helps you understand the concepts. Take this class from him!!

Best teacher that I have ever had, period. Teaches great lectures, is hilarious, and any girl would want to marry him. Watch out for LOTS of tough homework and really really hard tests. Definitely recommend being in a study group!

Hansen is one of the best. Gives you plenty of chances to get a decent grade. My advice: do the online assignments. They're only worth 5 points but those babies add up and can make a whole letter grade of a difference. (only reasoned I passed the class). Very possible to get an A or B in this class, if you actually try and learn the stuff.

Teaches like if you are in pre-school and test like if you are a graduate student. My TA at the beginning of the semester did not know how to manage time, Dr. Hansen will at least let you check other TAs out. You can't fully review test making it hard to learn what you did wrong. Dumb website. Lectures not related to HW at all. Read the book.

Dr. Hansen is a great professor. He makes lectures interesting and is very clear in what you need to know. There are daily clicker quizzes so go to class. You get to drop a couple of your lowest scores which is the best. 10/10 would reccomend

He is very funny and teaches the material well. The class was hard, but that had more to do with the content than the teacher. There is lots of homework, but if you actually try on all of it, it usually pays off on the tests.

Super funny, does a great job of reviewing material constantly, answering questions, and explaining concepts clearly. Lots of homework, probably almost an hour every day, but TA's go over everything in recitation, which is helpful. Daily quizzes count for attendance, and tests are reasonably hard but not tortuous.

Brother Hansen is a great chem teacher! He makes class so interesting because of how passionate he is. The class is a lot of work, but if you do the smart work, recitation, and take notes in lecture you'll do fine. The tests are hard, but manageable.

Best. Chem. Professor. EVER. I took chemistry from him my first semester and it was one of the best choices I made! He is extremely good at explaining difficult concepts and makes chemistry really fun. You definitely have to put in the work to get a good grade in the class. Do everything you can and talk to him about test questions you missed.

Good grading curve and plenty of drops. He really wants you to pass if you try. That said CHEM 105 is the most failed classes @ BYU so it isn't easy and Hansen knows that. The class sucks but Dr. Hansen makes it enjoyable.  I squeaked by with a C. Plan to send lots of time in this class. Uses I clickers which can be good and bad.

Dr. Hansen is a hilarious, awesome professor! Chem 105 was incredibly hard and his tests are very difficult, but it is possible to get a good grade with lots of work. He has a very general drop policy, is helpful whenever possible, and cares about the students. Don't let a hard class turn you off from taking a class from Dr. Hansen.
Chem 105 may be dark, cold, and unforgiving, but Dr. Hansen is not. Great professor, really funny, cares about students. Chem 105 on the other hand is a monster.

Doctor Hansen doesn't give bad lectures, that is, if you already know what you are doing.  The tests are super hard.  Homework every Monday Wednesday and Friday on a ridiculous website. Iclicker quiz closes roughly 60 seconds into every class. The worst thing is the TAs. I don't know if he picks em, but they know nothing. There are no test reviews

Prof Hansen gave good lectures and was pretty clear however the class was hard. The tests were pretty difficult and you had to spend several hours out of class studying and doing homework. If you put in the effort you should be fine but it definitely takes work.

Dr Hansen will make you love Chemistry! He's the funniest professor by far (always has random comments and stories in the middle of lecture). There are worksheets and online homework due during the week, and the in class quizzes are easy. Tests are tough, but the practice tests he posts are very similar to actual tests. Totally recommend taking him

TAKE THIS CLASS FROM  DR. HANSEN. Hansen is hilarious. Chem can be boring, but he keeps it entertaining. His slides have lots of practice problems. He will tell you what you need to know/have memorized for the test. 3x5 notecard on final. Drops bunch of assignments. Replaces worst test grade w/ final test grade. Best prof. I've had a BYU

Dr. Hansen is a funny guy. He entertains you during class although he can be very offensive at time. All of his lectures are powerpoint with VERY few practice problems. And when he does do practice problems, he flies through them assuming you know how to do it. I have seen many people raise their hands in class and he doesn't even acknowledge them.

Dr Hansen is a nice and funny enough guy, lectures are very entertaining. However, of all the professors teaching this class, his were far behind the others. We often were learning material for a test that opened the same day we were learning it. The textbook is useless. The exams are unnecessarily hard. But chem105 is hard on its own anyway.

Hansen is awesome! His lectures are intriguing and well explained. He usually goes over easier problems in class than what's on the test. Chem 105 is overall a very hard and time consuming class.. but Hansen really does his best to help you understand and he's pretty funny.
Dr. Hansen is amazing! He made Chem105 so much more bearable. He also is super good to work with outside of class and really wants you to make sure you know what you are doing. Take Hansen.

Chemistry 105 is one of the most failed classes at BYU. This class takes a lot of time, but it is a 4 credit class. The lectures make up for the dedication and time put into class. Dr. Hansen is clear about what is graded, drops a lot of assignments, and offers help to students who need it. The relationship with the students to TA's is good too.

I loved Professor Hansen with a passion. I've never been a huge fan of chemistry, but he makes it so interesting and fun that I enjoyed the class a great deal. We had a pretty good amount of homework, but as long as you understand the concepts you can get it done quickly. Lots of grades are dropped to even out your average. Awesome guy/class.

Dr Hansen is really enthusiastic about Chemistry. His explanations make sense and the class provides plenty of resources for clarifications. Go to office hours, ask your TA's questions, go to review sessions, do the online practice problems, do the reading. It's a tough class, but it's manageable if you use your resources and go to class.

Hansen is a great professor! Just make the most out of all the resources he provides and the class really isn't that hard in my opinion. He's a pretty good lecturer but I think he's a lot better when you go into his office and talk to him one-on-one. Super helpful, smart guy.

Hansen on his own really isn't that hard of a teacher, it's the class that's difficult. But he is willing to meet with anyone to help out, and explains things again, one on one if you need it. Lectures are absolutely hilarious, I don't think I've ever had a funnier teacher

The way he taught chemistry was so simple. His teaching style is great. Not to mention he's hilarious, which made lectures easy. If you want a teacher who cares about you, take this guy. There is one caveat: if you get offended easily from politically incorrect comments, DO NOT take this class from Hansen. He makes them a lot.

Oh man, Dr. Hansen is awesome!  He the best Chemistry teacher you can take for 105, because he tells  really wants to help the students.  CHEM 105 IS NOT EASY, but as long as you memorize whatever he tells you and record when he says a question will be on a test you will do fine.  Read the book and do the practice problems if you don't understand!

Professor Hansen gives very good lectures, but the tests are unreasonably hard. What is actually on the test is not always consistent with what he says will be on it. Make sure you do the readings and homework assignments.

Super nice guy who keeps you entertained during lecture. Do the reading before class and things will make more sense, definitely do the homework and writing assignments. He's really reasonable with homework and stuff. The tests are pretty intense.

Dr. Hansen was fantastic. Probably my favorite professor of the entire semester. He is very fair and helpful, although the tests were very hard. You should have a good background in high school chemistry before you take this course. Do the homework well, because it ended up being more important to my grade than I thought.

Hilarious guy, chats with students before lecture, and gives great demos on Explosion Wednesdays. He tries to help a lot but I get the feeling that with research and everything, he doesn't have much time for a freshman class. Takes years to email back. Go to reviews and study the review info the TA's give. They are the ones that will save you.

This is a very hard class but Prof Hansen is hilarious.  He makes going to class fun even though it's hard.  He is very willing to help and listen to the students.  Over all he is a great professor.  If you have to take 111H take it from him.

CHEM 227 has a reputation for being extremely difficult, but Dr. Hansen tried to give everyone as much help as possible to make it easier.  Dr. Hansen is an excellent professor and is always available for help.  I highly recommend him for any class.
If you have to take this difficult test, he is the best to take it from.  He is very willing to work with you.
Dr. Hansen is a fabulous professor and I learned a lot in his class.  He tries to make the class interesting and he is a captivating speaker.  I highly recommend taking Chem 111H from Dr. Hansen.

Dr. Hansen was a very good teacher! I was able to understand most of the concepts and he made the class extremely fun to go to. This class is very hard though, so if you are not willing to work at it, I suggest you not take it. On the other hand, if you are willing to work, I highly suggest Dr. Hansen!

Best professor ever! He's on the younger side (40 something i think) so more energetic, and he tries to make boring lessons interesting. He's really approachable and really makes an effort to get to know all his students. This is a tough class, but if you take him, he helps prepare you for tests. I loved how passionate he was about the material!
This was an extremely hard class--expect to live and breathe chemistry for a semester! But with Dr. Hansen's very flexible office hours, one can certainly survive the rough material.

This is a review for ENGL 322 (Rhetorical Foundations). I loved this class. He helped us overcome our fears and reservations about rhetoric. The readings were all meaningful and even the writing assignments made for good rhetorical practice. He is a professor that cares about his students and you can tell.

I took the 211 class from him. I'd say that this class is very reading heavy and the text is a little hard to digest but all he really wants you to do is try. He wants you to take the concepts and apply them to your life which I respect. Grading wise, he is pretty chill. I think that he is a really cool guy. I'd take this class again for Civ 1.

Professor Slater is actually an angel. He is the best general class professor I've ever taken in all my years at BYU. If you show up to class you'll be fine. Prof Slater loves and cares about his students, is so smart, and will help you SO much. I made some super great friends in this class because of the chill and fun environment. 10/10 recommend

Lots of readings, but you can find most books online or at the library. Lectures are very conversational and interesting, and Professor slater is the sweetest guy. He brought us breakfast for our final presentation. Graded mostly on effort, so as long as you try your best, the class is easy.

Class is very discussion based and Dr. Slater lets the conversation go where the class has questions. It's hard to fail this class if you just show up and do the readings. He's also very relatable and a great speaker--if you're looking to take two generals at once, this is probably both the easiest and most interesting option.

Dr. Slater is one of the most caring and genuine people. He seeks student input often (on assignments, readings, etc.) and can be flexible if needed. He cares a lot about rhetoric and will help you love it too:) There are a lot of readings to do (which can all be found on LS. Don't buy the textbook), but if you skim them you will be fine!

This class is very easy!!! Prof Slater is very energetic and a super sweet teacher. I didn't do the reading and only skimmed the spark notes and I got an A still so I wouldn't spend too much time on them. I regret buying the textbooks

Easy grader. Lots of reading but it's manageable and not the end of the world if you can't get to it all. Professor cares about his students truly learning and applying the content of his class. Easy to get an A. Interesting class.

Great GE class! Prof Slater is very willing to work with you and even modify the course load to make it less stressful. Super passionate about rhetoric and explains concepts well! (I now know what rhetoric is and why it is important!) There was a lot of required reading, but you shouldn't have to buy any books unless you want physical copies

Professor Slater is AMAZING! Trust me, you will want to take a class from him. The readings can be a bit long (and somewhat confusing at times), but the discussions we had in class were also so fun, engaging, and super informative. Most of what you were graded on what application of rhetoric principles rather than rote memorization.
Amazing professor. Responds to emails quickly and he is very fair with his grading. I 100% recommend this class as for your GE credits

This professor is the GOAT. Hands down the best English professor i've ever studied under. Professor Slater's lectures are engaging and funny, and he is inspiring. He doesn't have a lot of grades so be sure not to miss deadlines, but he's very fair with grading. 12/10 would take again

Awesome class overall, definitely one of the best GEs I have taken. Professor Slater is really passionate about rhetoric and assorted assignments don't take up too much time, lots of group discussions in class. For the final project, I put together more info about the class structure on my github: oliviamorganstl. github. io

There are no tests, one final paper 6-8 pages. Reading is not mandatory, the easy 10 question quizzes are open book anyways. The instructions to the assignments are not clear at times but he makes you point them out in discussion posts. Major assignments are resume, a weird simulation thing, a PPT presentation, and final paper. The PPT is in groups

Kinda goofy, but amazing. The class was really small so we all knew each other and used each other for paper feedback. The papers are the only thing really graded, but you can write about basically anything you want. Pick something you are passionate about and do all the research. It can be really fun especially with him.

My favorite thing about Dr. Slater is that he constantly asked for feedback from us. He'd be like, "How'd that assignment go? Were the expectations clear? What should I change?" and then he'd change assignments and due dates accordingly. You could really tell he has the students and their success as his main priority. He learned everyone's names!

Professor Slater was an AMAZING. There was a bit of reading required for the course, but it was always interesting. Professor Slater's lectures were clear and he provided several opportunities for peer review on writing assignments during class. You can tell he loves teaching this subject and that he cares about his students!

Take WRTG 316 from Dr. Slater! While this class has some annoying assignments he makes it so much better. He is so kind and will work with you. He will spend as much time as needed to help you with your writing. I had friends take it from other professors and they did not get as much help. It is a lot of writing but it is a senior writing class

Professor Slater really cares about his students. He is incredibly passionate about what he does too, which makes his classes very enjoyable. I thought this class would be boring, but his upbeat attitude and passion really made it interesting. I feel like a better writer now too.

This class was super helpful and I feel like we really focused on writing that was beneficial. I left knowing how to do professional writing! He is super accessible and will work with you and answer any questions. His classes were really fun and didn't add too much busy-work to my course load, just helpful projects!

Professor Slater is great! Sometimes the instructions for some of the smaller assignments were unclear, but the bigger assignments were always explained in detail even during the short term. Be prepared to participate in class and in breakout rooms on Zoom. The class was overall super chill and easier than you would expect from a writing class!

I LOVED Professor Slater. He is a great teacher. We had a couple papers that made up the large majority of my grade. The great thing is that the prompts are pretty open-ended and you can choose topics that interest you to make them easier to write. It is an easy class if you just do the work. I would definitely take this class from him!!!

I was dreading taking this class, but  Jarron was fantastic and I can't believe how much I learned. There is some work involved, but he gives INCREDIBLY helpful feedback and you can resubmit everything for a better grade after editing. BYU: HIRE HIM FULL TIME. HE'S GREAT. Everyone in the class would say the same.

Jarron cares for every student, his lectures are entertaining, and he wants you to learn and apply the material. Attendance is mandatory but gives participation points that really help w your grade. Expect lots of assignments but he lets you re-do them (except presentations). I recommend Jarron. You will enjoy his class!

Great teacher! Lots of assignments, but if you put in the work you will do well. He cares about his students and is willing to help with anything. Able to rewrite anything you aren't satisfied with (grade wise). Take Eng 316 from Slater!!

I have done well in literally every other math class I have ever taken. If you take this class be prepared to teach yourself ALL of the material, I don't think I learned a single thing from him all semester. He is a good person and very very smart but not a good instructor.

He teaches mainly through theorems and proofs, which works if that's how you learn best. Otherwise, he didn't explain the concepts well. He expects students to read ahead (lectures were still confusing). I was uncomfortable asking questions because answers were critical and unhelpful. I relied heavily on the TA math lab, textbook, and classmates.
I took math 213 from this professor. Do not take math 213 from this professor.

I needed to take his class in the Summer.  With the shorter time frame and the difficulty in understanding his accent and the material generally, it was unnecessarily complicated.  I never completely understood the material.  His class is very proof heavy and he will require you to memorize proofs and regurgitate them for the midterms and final.

He did not connect hard concepts to previous course material. Tests progressively harder. I had to retake the class (take from professor Tuan Pham) and when I looked back on my final, I saw that I knew what I was doing, but I didn't solve it his way and so I didn't get any points. His class is very proofs based for a computations class.

Communication: explicit about what is on tests (to a degree), provides past tests to study, handwrites everything he says, soft-spoken, poor handwriting, very poor interpersonal skills, demeaning, adds confusion when answering questions. Classwork: 3 weekly assignments, 3 midterms, 1 final, PROOF HEAVY!

His teaching method did not work well for me, and there is certainly a bit of a language barrier, but he tries his best. If you're a math major, his teaching (focused on proofs and stuff) is probably helpful, but if you're any other major taking it more for the applications, I would recommend a different professor. His test reviews are very helpful

The good: Gives very specific and clear test reviews, so you're not going in blind. The bad: The worst professor I've had when it comes to answering questions. Both in class and in office hours, he would frequently misunderstand questions or change his answers, leaving you more confused. We didn't have a TA either.

Class felt disorganized and his proofs didn't always make sense (I spent a lot of time rereading and sometimes correcting them, and sometimes just inventing my own). It often felt like he was making up HW questions on the spot without knowing what he'd already assigned. However, he has you grade your own HW, the class isn't hard, and he's very kind

I didn't particularly enjoy Dr. Chahal's class or teaching methods, but it was clear that he cared about his students and wanted us to succeed. As others say, his practice tests and test reviews are EXTREMELY helpful: they're borderline copy/paste from the tests themselves, so DO be sure to complete them and attend his test reviews!

Dr. Chahal is complicated. At the beginning of the semester I was frustrated with his quiet attitude and communication barriers. But eventually I saw that he cares about his students. I hadn't been doing my homework and was expecting a C, but I did well on the final and got an A. The final was easy (and I honestly used more geometry than calc).

He's a nice man, trying his best. Lectures sometimes hard to grasp, but you can find good Youtube videos on some of the topics. Go to his office! You can do well if you choose to. He doesn't want to give bad grades. If you want a not-so-rigorous, easier/interesting elective, take it! You'll be fine. It's the math class I've laughed the most in.

Dr. Chahal wants to help you succeed but he does not teach well. Lectures were hard to follow, confusing, and overall useless. Many math teachers focus on examples to teach concepts, he does not. He uses proofs which can be hard to apply. Slader, the textbook and test reviews helped me understand. Always go to class when he has test reviews.
This was my favorite class at BYU. I took it back in 2015, but LOVED it. Graph Theory is awesome. Definitely recommend the class and definitely recommend it from Dr. Chahal.

Honestly this was a tough class. He is super nice though, but there are some times when he doesn't understand students questions so other students will help you. His test reviews are incredibly helpful. Usually he only changes the numbers for the problems he gives in the tests and the questions are generally the exact same
Dr. Chahal is a very kind person, but I feel like he doesn't understand the students very well. His teaching methods are hard to understand. I learned most things from the textbook.

Great guy. If you put in the time to learn the theory, you will do well. His tests are about  the theory, definitions, and combinations thereof. The homework was not excessive, and the class was interesting. Tests were mostly t/f, but don't underestimate any of the questions--they are difficult, but can be answered based on definitions and theories
There is not extra credits. You really want to get good scores from the exams.

His accent is alright, but the way he taught me was very confusing. I tried to regularly attend the class. I found the textbook is a better way to learn materials. His exam was not easy. You might get B or C. You won't get too much homework.

(Taken during summer term) Professor Chahal is a nice man who really does want to help, but his communication skills are a little low. Many times when he was asked a question, he seemed to be puzzled and a little annoyed because he had "already answered that" and the student was still confused. It wasnt uncommon for the textbook to make more sense

I took this class  because it was the only one that fit into my schedule. Dr. Chahal is a very kind person and cares about his students. His accent is not hard to understand, but he has a very confusing way of explaining the material. I spent most of the lectures thinking "What??!" His tests are easy if you review the material gives in the review.

Dr. Chahal was a very fair professor. His lectures aren't very clear sometimes. But  he helps you relearn old concepts, and most of his test questions come directly from in-class examples or from the book, which he goes over in in-class reviews. He helps you earn a good grade while learning the material. Best math professor I've had at BYU.

By far, Dr. Chahal was the most useless math professor I've had at BYU. He mumbled through the lectures while standing in front of the board and spent an eternity explaining simple concepts and rushed through the difficult concepts. He often explained concepts so poorly that he would explain them five or six times and still leave people confused.

Dr. Chahal was hands-down my favorite professor I've had so far at BYU. 1. He cared about us individually. 2. He sets you up for success, telling you exactly what will be on the test and reviews much of it in class. Don't miss the in-class reviews! 3. He teaches the fundamentals. I've never understood math so well until I had him as a professor.

You have to beg him to help with anything wrong with your grade, even when it was his fault.  Whether or not he gives any points back, he makes sure to go through everything that you did wrong and emphasize "it should be like this" "it's easy, watch" and "I don't see this on yours." Also, proofs are 1/3 the points on the final.

Only a few of the homeworks were really challenging. The test policy was really good (he takes your best 2 midterms out of 3) and he prepares you really well for the tests - no surprises at all if you come to the lectures. His lectures were usually good, but know that for the difficult topics you better pay close attention or you'll get lost.

I learned almost nothing from attending the lectures. The only reason I went is because some of the theorems and proofs on the test came directly from class. I didn't learn much and he made a lot of typos on his tests, making them really tricky. Tough course.

Dr. Chahal is awesome. This was the first class I took from him and I LOVED it. He's a pretty funny guy. His tests all come from in class work. He also has in class reviews that help a bunch. The homework is sometimes hard, but he'll adjust due dates if needed. He also drops a test. Would definitely take from him again!

He isn't very good at explaining things. If you can understand the material from reading the book the class is easy. Pay close attention to the proofs presented in class, they make up  most of the test grades.

I feel like Chahal often gets a bad rep that he doesn't deserve. He truly cared about the students was always willing to help. He was very good at clarifying things in the textbook and would repeat important things we needed to know for the tests. And despite what a lot of people have said, he speaks English perfectly well; he just has an accent.

It might take you a while to realize it, but Dr. Chahal really does care about his students and wants to help them learn.  It is a little hard for him to explain what things mean conceptuallyphysically, but if you work hard (and I mean HARD) on the assignments, you'll get it. You need to be 100% prepared for the tests because each question matters
his lecture is not good, but he will tell you some question that will be on the exam.

I found first few weeks of the course to be pretty slow-going and easy. The subject matter gets a little more difficult towards the end of the course, but Dr. Chahal is super helpful if you visit him in his office. One of the nicest professors I have had. Also, he speaks English just fine. I didn't think he was hard to understand.

Professor Chahal was one of the most helpful professors I've ever had. He didn't have great lectures, and is pretty hard to understand, but one-on-one he is super helpful. He wants his students to succeed and will adjust his class so they can do so. He tells you basically the exact questions that will be on the tests, so they aren't bad at all.

Confusing lectures. In hindsight, I might have been better served just to read the book on my own and go to test reviews than bother showing up to lecture. Tests weren't too difficult. Questions came straight out of the book's examples.

He asks broad questions to see if we understand expecting specific answers. His English is poor. So it just adds to the difficulty of following his lectures. After each midterm he insulted the entire class that we did a terrible job. He also insulted us during discussions because he felt we're not having material fully grasps during the same lectur
Great teacher, hard to understand at first but really cares about making sure we understand the material. He is very forgiving on the exam and the reviews really prepare you. I would recommend him.

His English is very bad so he is hard to understand. He changed the grading method of the homework twice during the semester. We disagreed with it but he just said it was fine. Worst of all, I hope this doesn't happen to others. I got a B+ in the class and 6 months later he changed it to a D+. Because of the time gap he would not let me contest it.

It my regret to say that his class was the worst class I've ever taken : Every test had material not formally covered in class, lectures were recitations from the book most of the time, unscheduled reviews on fridays were nice but were the only times he taught truly test-relevant material, and understanding his expectations were hit-and-miss.

He was a great teacher.  He worked really hard to make sure all the students understood the material.  It takes a little bit to get used to his accent, but it's really not that bad.  You have to definitely work for your grade.  He's very willing to work with you and wants everyone in the class to succeed.  I would take a class from him again.

I enjoyed him as a professor. He can sometimes get sidetracked on things not necessarily on the test although still useful. But he gives plenty of examples in class, and the test questions are basic concepts of each section. If you read the book, and do homework, the tests are a super straight forward. I would take him again. Incredibly kind guy.

He understands math, but does not know how to teach it very well. He is very hard to understand. 25 people are enrolled or more and only 8 go each class...my study group had to teach ourselves Differential Equations from the textbook.

This is the ABSOLUTE worst teacher I've ever had. He is a little confrontational when you ask questions. He doesn't speak english very well, and it completely incomprehensible when it comes to teaching math. His tests were impossible, but fortunately the curve ends up very favorable because the entire class does poorly. Choose a different professor
if you follow along in the book as he teaches this class is super easy

Dr. Chahal is extremely nice and tries to be helpful, but teaching is not his thing. He is very hard to follow and does not have excellent explaining skills because his english is his second language. He also throws a lot of random topics into it and sort of skips over some things that should be covered in the course. I would not suggest him.
