Dr. Chahal doesn't explain what he is writing on the board and only gives abstract examples which makes it difficult to understand what he's doing. It takes hours and hours to do each homework assignment because they are problems that he created. He also wrote his own book that is almost impossible to understand. Take it from him at your own risk.

Nice guy who wants to help students do well, but he's hard to understand. He gets confused a lot and has to explain things multiple times. Weird grading method. I made A's on most of the homework and got an 85 and a 90 on the two midterms, but somehow got a C+ in the class. He only gave out one A in my whole section.
I understood almost nothing from his lectures. I had to mostly learn by myself from the book. Course load was pretty typical for a math class, but some homework assignments were very long.

I had an A until the final. I thought the final was much harder than the other tests in the class. I had to go to MIT's open course ware to be able to do the homework. Only a small part of the material was covered in class.

Dr. Chahal seemed like a very good teacher until after the final exam. I entered the exam with a 99% in the class and received a B+ due to not being able to complete a proof on the final. Grading does not reflect what students learned. If you do A work expect a B+ at best. He gave no A grades in my class. I would never take this professor again.

If you do A work, expect a B+. He has a bizarre grading method, doesn't give out many A's, I think he only gave out three to my class. He's very kind and merciful, but cannot bring math down to your level.  His tests are weird but the test review does help.  Homework is 20%, tests 40, final 40. I would never take from him again horrible experience.

Chahal is great!  His lectures are kind of hard to follow at first until you get used to his teaching style but his tests are very reasonable.  If you go to the review he tells you exactly what you need to know and he is really generous with his grading.  I recommend him.
Terrible Teacher! I've never had a worse teacher in my life! Do not take it from him because you'll just be teaching yourself. Not helpful at all!

I took both 343 and 214 from him.  His 343 was slightly better, but I still have no problems with the 214 class.  His grading is fair and his test aren't too tough.  Most of the questions on the test come straight from homework and the examples in the textbook.  As long as you do the homework, (and understand it)you'll do fine.

Dr Chahal is Awesome.  HIs tests are easy.  IN his reviews he tells you exactly what is on the test and what he expects.  He is very dedicated to the Definitions and Proofs, so memorize them, but the computational stuff is easy.

Class was always fighting, grading was inconsistent, we had TAs from our section (yup, TAs grading our homework/tests from within our class), and class consisted of memorizing the text. It got so bad that I didn't bother coming to class for a month because of all the bickering.  Only missed 1 chapter (of 11) in that time & still did well
A very pious man, good teacher. He cares only about learning the material in a really old fashioned sense. His course was fascinating.

Chahal is a really nice guy!  I loved this class.  The course is an awesome course and is totally applicable to all other math classes.  It's true that after the section on geometry, the class lost definite structure.   Chahal is extremely nice and willing to spend extra time outside of class with you on any class you need help in.  I recommend.

He does not explain things clearly at all.  He will do proofs on the board but will erase and change things at least 3 times for each proof, which makes taking notes next to impossible.  After the first section, where you do Euclid's geometry, the class has no structure and is all over the place.  NOT RECOMMENDED!!

Nice man but not a great teacher.  Material was not difficult but the way he would explain it rarely made sense.  This wouldn't have been so bad if there was a textbook to reference to.  Didn't learn much.  Course poorly organized.  Made himself very accessible for help outside of class.  Easy to get good grade.

He's a very, very, very nice man, but at least for me, his lectures are way confusing.  And you only use the book in the very beginning of the semester - after that he just teaches you in his own words, which to me aren't very clear.

Very nice man. He makes the effort to get to know each student - beyond their name! The classes themselves are rather boring, but the material is fairly simple. He has an obsession w/ Euclid. You do proofs as a class, then rewrite in your own words. He is very helpful, and even offered to help me with another math class I was taking. Recommended!
He is a great teacher. The test is not hard. You just need to pay attention on the review.
Great professor.  He cares less about grades and more about what his students learn.
He is not chill

I took Dr. Adams in the spring 2026. Lectures and lab are each 50% of your grade. For lecture tests he gives you learning objectives and I filled them out based off the information on the slides and how he described the slides in class. I did very well with this tactic. His office hours are great to go to to understand more difficult concepts

This class is brutal, he doesn't really teach he just reads off the slides. If you take this during spring it will consume your entire life. Make sure you are dedicated to studying the lectures and going into lab hours. It's basically just hours of memorization but you can not procrastinate! Make sure you study the lecture slides very well

Lots of material. Most anatomy lecture teachers were about the same quality, though. What matters is having good TAs. Both lecture and lab TAs are all incredible. The lecture material is just something to get over with. The lab is where you thrive and love life.

His lectures were so boring I feel like I wasted my opportunity to enjoy the class because of him. He doesn't care about student's situations and no matter how much you need his help he won't help. Also, one of my friends was taking the class from Dr Gonda and her exams were way easier than his. Don't take it from him. I wish I was told that before

He is really nice and very accomodating and unfortunately really really boring. He speaks with the same level of tone every lecture every day. Really easy to fall asleep in his class and most learning has to happen outside of lecture. I recommend choosing another teacher

Dr. Adams loves anatomy but he isn't caring. His Lectures are not interesting at all. I think that he has great knowledge but doesn't have the ability to teach it well and him not caring about the students makes it even worse.

The materials for the lectures and the lab are both very interesting. If you put in the time you will do great. On the other hand Dr. Adams doesn't care about the students. His lectures are not engaging.

Prepare before the lectures, fill out the study objectives after the lectures. Go to TA reviews. This class is a lot of work but if you know the slides and study objectives, you'll be just fine. Professor Adams was a fun teacher and for almost every test gave us 2 points back because we all missed some questions.

I took Cell 520R from Dr. Adams in the Fall and it was one of my favorite classes! He took time to get to know each of his students and is very knowledgeable. He is one of the kindest professors and I would highly recommend him!

I loved this class! Dr. Adams is the nicest man and he does a great job explaining the lectures. My tip is don't slack on studying for lecture exam. Read the textbook it's helpful and label the photos in the lab manual before each lab! Practice writing out lab terms, spelling is a huge part of the lab. I wish I could take it again its the best!

I had Dr. Brown for lecture but I just want to shout Dr. Adams out! I was struggled to work with the cadavers at first and as the Lab Pro, he did everything he could to help me succeed! I was going to drop out but with his help I managed to stay in the class and got an A!! If you're struggling, dont give up!!
One of the worst professors i have ever had. Doesn't care about his students, or situations. I would highly suggest not taking any classes from him. Worst teacher i have ever had at BYU.

Lectures were not engaging. If you take this class from Adams, you're better off studying solely from the textbook rather than wasting time going to lecture. Really cool class though, and you'll learn a lot!

This class is a ton of work. I grinded all semester trying to get an A and ended with 0.1% away from an A, a single point from and A. I emailed him and he had no sympathy. I understand keeping a consistent standard but there were several points that I missed because the TAs taught us wrong and I thought he should've given us more grace on grading.

I absolutely loved Prof Adams. He was very passionate about anatomy and you could tell that he is an expert . He explained things in a way that was easy to understand and his class is set up for everyone to get the grade that they want. This course is memorization heavy but he helps us take advantage of all the resources available.

I really loved taking dissection from Dr. Adams!  He took the time to learn everyone's names and cared about our lives.  He is really good about creating a good environment for us to gain critical experience and learn in the lab.  It was definitely one of my favorite classes.

This class was definitely challenging. Lab TA's were amazing. For lecture, I feel like Dr. Adams was just reading off the slides. This class is purely memorization and I feel like there was a lot to memorize for the exams. Overall, I learned a lot from this class but I would probably not take it from Dr.Adams.

The course material is interesting and Dr. Adams demonstrates a strong knowledge of the subject matter. However, the pace of the lectures tends to be slow and Dr. Adams isn't super engagning. Additionally, the course requires a significant amount of memorization, so it is essential to stay organized and keep up with the material from day one.

His lectures are a little slow but contain useful information. If you miss class, it's pretty easy to catch up by reading the textbook. The tests are pretty fair and not too hard as long as you use the learning objectives as your study guide.

Class set up lecture vs lab. Dr. Adams is OK. Did not go lecture because exams were based on slides. Just memorize the slides and you will be set for the exams. Lots of slides though so be prepared to study. TAs taught labs, attend the open lab hour if you want to do well on the lab quizzes and the two lab exams. Rec take someone else if you can

Dr Adams prepared me A TON for future STEM classes. I barely study for physiology because of how much I learned in his class. His lectures are straight forwards and test questions come right from the slides. The class is only hard because of the lecture/lab combo but if you stay on top of it and use flashcards its super doable. Great professor!

It's clear that Dr. Adams loves the study of anatomy. However, I struggled with his teaching style a little. His lectures were an hour of listening to him read off of the slides that he made, and basically the entire grade is exams. If you can memorize his slides exactly, you should be okay on the tests.

His learning objectives and the online text (for lecture) and the lab manual (for lab) tell you exactly what you will be expected to know. High volume to memorize, though.

Lab is about 75 structures to memorize (written response) a week.

Lecture is about 75 flashcards' worth of material to memorize (recognize on multiple choice) a week.

This class is structured so anyone can succeed IF you put in the work! I spent probably 20 hours per week outside of class for labs and lectures combined. For the lecture exams, they're easy to score well on if you know your stuff. He provides learning objectives, and the tests are taken straight from those pretty much.

I mostly skipped the lectures and just memorized everything on the slides which gave me a pretty good lecture exam score, but for labs, you have to force yourself to go in free labs, as much as you can. The lab exam specimens are not what you usually see in class so make sure you study every angle. This class is hard no matter who you choose.
Lecture was very dry and often something that I could review myself. I think that I learned more from the TAs than Adams

Dr Adams is a nice guy, you can tell he cares. Lots of reviews mention the boring lectures and how they never went. I actually found it valuable to go as he did explain the slides. But, at the end of the day the tests are based completely off what is written in the slides. Anatomy is just hard but lab is sooo cool.

Dr. Adams was a great professor. His tests were fair and the resources he gives you to study from prepare you well. He is known to have boring lectures which rang true in my opinion, but he cares about his students and your grade. I was nervous to take anatomy from Adams (in comparison to Gonda and Brown) but he turned out to be great!

This class takes a lot of time and studying. All of the test questions come from Dr. Adams' slides, so you need to memorize them. I stopped going to lecture about halfway through the semester and it didn't affect my grade. He basically just reads off the slides. Going to free labs for the lab helps too, but I mainly just focused on the lab videos.
lectures are pretty boring but I loved this class. lots of studying is required

Labs were great, but lectures were AWFUL! I didn't learn anything in lecture, so I stopped going. I taught myself from the textbook and did better the second half of the semester. When I actually went to lecture, I remember him going way too fast and never covering all of the material. Do yourself a favor and take it from someone else.

Anatomy is a really tough class! It should really be split up into two 3 credit classes imo. Professor Adams is a super nice person but his lectures can be a little boring. Honestly never went to class and just memorized the slides and was fine. Lab is definitely the highlight of the class and is awesome!

Anatomy is HARD! No doubt about it but this class is my favorite one I have taken. His tests are specific so allot a good amount of time to study. MEMORIZE the slides and go to interactive reviews to help for lecture. For lab, attend free labs and watch the lab videos. They are super helpful. Become friends with the TAs as they are there for you.

This class should be 6 credits and 2 different classes. For the test MEMORIZE all the slides. He will pick a small detail from a random slide. For the lab quizzes, just go to free lab and you will be super prepared. He is kinda boring so just teach yourself...

Professor Adams bases his lectures off of the slides and textbook. You need to have everything on the slides memorized and should read the textbook at least once. He is very enthusiastic about the topic and is happy to meet with students. For lab, quizlets are a lifesaver. Make sure to go to free labs and watch the lab videos, as well.

For lectures, memorize the slides, and you will do great on those exams. He literally takes all his exams from the slides. So I would definitely get the printed slides. For lab, QUIZLET PREMIUM! Just do the written mode and practice the lab terms on there. Free labs were very helpful, but also the LAB VIDEOS are also amazing. You can do this!!

Dr. Adams has the most detailed tests of all the anatomy professors. He reads off of his slides for lecture. Treat lab and lecture like two separate classes. To get an A you must put in a ton of work outside of class. Go to free labs and reviews. The TAs are amazing--listen to everything they say! Working on the cadavers was epic!

Don't get behind in studying for lecture. Pick at it every single day. I took it during spring and would memorize a full lesson everyday since he teaches 2 in one day/ 4 a week. He wrote the book and it explains it way better than he does so use it ALWAYS to fill in info. TA's are key to success. Hennd was my life saver. For lab, GO to free lab!!!

Dr Adams gets some heat but his class is so easy if you teach yourself from the book. His lectures are boring and only introduce you to what you'll spend an extra 4 hours teaching yourself for each lesson... so skipping his lectures and teaching yourself = guaranteed A; study along with his slides and KNOW every learning objectives WITH the book

Dr Adams is deemed not the best for anatomy but I thought he was fine. Anatomy is just a lot of info and goes fast. If you stay on top of the weekly lab quizzes and don't forget to study for lecture an A is totally possible. I thought the textbook was super helpful. His tests are straightforward and I never felt like he was trying to trick me.

This class is like 2 classes in one. Lab and lecture overlap slightly, but not much. Lab was probably my favorite class to go to this semester, but lecture can be hard to go to sometimes. He just reads off of the slides which you can learn on your own. Be prepared to study! It may be hard but it is worth it. I learned so much from this class!

Anatomy is an intense class. Lab is super fun, and no matter the professor, lab is going to be a similar experience. As for lecture, Dr. Adams can be rather dry, which can make lecture hard to get through. I got more out of not going lecture and studying the material by myself.

Anatomy is amazing!! Requires lots of memorization no matter who you take it from, but Adams will never try to trick you on exams. He's a kind guy. You'll want to reference the textbook a lot just to make things more clear, but it's an easy read. I loved this class more than anything. It's well worth the work and time. But it should be two classes.

Honestly, CELL 220 should be two classes. The lab portion, taught entirely by TAs, is very doable and you can be successful if you put a lot of hours into going to free lab each week. The lecture portion is also doable, but also requires many hours of memorizing. Overall an awesome class. Learned so much, loved it, but it required a ton of time.

Dr. Adams is a really caring guy and wants you to succeed. He's willing to meet outside of class and go over things you don't understand. His lectures are pretty dry, but the labs are really cool. This class is a super cool, so I definitely recommend taking it!

Anatomy has a bit of an infamous reputation at BYU, but Adams is as fair as it gets! The expectations for what you need to know are SO CLEAR. Yes, you have to work hard to know those things, but you know exactly what you need to know. He's not boring but not overly exciting and he's the kindest human being! My lab TA's were BOMB!

This class is straight memorization. Technically you could pass without going to class, but Dr. Adams adds things that aren't on the slides. He's a genuine person and is an expert in the field. His tests are very detail oriented. Memorize everything. He's very fair in his expectations though and teaches everything on the tests.

Adams is fine. Not amazing but not bad. Heres the key: study the learning objectives with the textbook. memorize. go to TA reviews. memorize. youll do great. All lab work is the same no matter what prof. Dont let other reviews scare you. This was still my fav class even w/ not loving Dr Adams.

My view may be skewed because CELL 220 has been my favorite class in my academic experience, but Dr. Adams gets straight to the point with his lectures and thats exactly what I needed to learn most effectively. I have an excellent grasp on anatomy, though I needed to work for it. There are easier teachers, but dont let that deter you, hes great!

Monotone and uninspiring. Avoid his lecture at all costs. The entire program has gone down hill since Wisco left. You want to learn and do well? Take it from Brown. You want to be inspired and feel like a million dollars? Novak is the best professor this school has. Don't take it from Adams-- you have options. Know your worth people! Nice tho...

Avoid taking lecture from Adams at all costs. He's a nice person, but I would rather have a mean professor that actually teaches me things. He reads off the slides in a monotone voice and doesn't make any effort to help students retain information at all. After the first exam I just skipped lecture to teach myself the material.

Dr Adams is a great person and very knowledgeable professor. He will make you work harder than other professors teaching Anatomy at BYU. If you are looking for easier exams try to get into Dr Brown or Professor Novak's classes. If you don't mind reading a lot of the textbook for 2-3 very specific questions on the exam then take it from him.

Anatomy is such a fun class. Adam's texts are exactly from his lecture slides and most people do well on the lecture exams. This class is definitely work, but if you put in the time for memorizing, free labs, and studying you will be good. This class is mostly dependent on your TA, but you can always go to free lab and interact with other TAs.

I had Dr. Adams for both Anatomy (220) and Advanced Topics in Clinical Human Anatomy (520R), and I liked him in both. He's super focused during lectures, and clearly knows anatomy super well. He also obviously cared about our success and was super helpful whenever I went to him outside of class.

He makes test questions and lectures based off of learning objectives from the textbook, but the textbook honestly is really helpful and not very long or hard to read at all. Go to TA reviews. He is very kind and nice and intentional about the structure of the class so there are no surprises. Lots of material, so study a lot.

Hardest class I've taken. Anatomy is a hard class and I worked my tail off for an A. Got a 97 on the final and finished the class with a 92.9% but he doesn't round up. I really enjoyed the class though and gained a love for the human body. Just make sure you go to TA reviews and study lecture slides. The tests are based off the slides.

Some will say hes bland and boring but I realize now that this means there are no surprises. Midterms and the final are all super-super similar to the practice questions that youre given in ever lecture. Learn the slides, read the book, and you wont have any surprises

Dr. Adams is nice. He just reads off the slides. Tests come from lecture and specific details in textbook. They are straightforward if you memorize everything. The lab is what hurts people. I never went to a single free lab and still got a B+. The people who do well in this class just spend lot's of time at free lab, that's all. Don't be worried:)

Professor Adams is fine as a professor. Everything was Live Remote Delivery, and he recorded the lectures so I just watched the lectures on double speed later because his lectures are kinda boring. Tests are pretty straight forward if you know the learning objectives and slides (I got A-s). He is a very kind soul and helps with accommodations,

Dr. Adams seems like a nice guy and I don't have anything against him. His lectures tend to be just reading off the slides. His tests come directly from the textbook, which is different from every other anatomy prof at BYU, so I think they might be a little harder. He will get the job done fine, but I recommend taking someone else if you can

Anatomy is a hard class, it needs to be your 1st or 2nd priority class for the semester. It takes a lot of work with the lab and lecture. Dr. Adams is a great choice for anatomy. Do not fall behind in this class! Ask for help, go to free lab, go to lecture TA office hours and their lectures. Do everything you need so you can memorize the info.

Prof Adams is a nice guy, but does just read the slides. He provides some insights, but going to the TA reviews are essential. Lab is the beast part of the class. The tests really aren't bad if you prepare. This class requires a lot of work, but if you're interested in the content it won't be too bad.

Dr. Adams is a nice guy but lectures were boring. He just read the slides off his powerpoint which he posts so going to his lectures seemed useless. His tests were fair and came straight from his powerpoints. If you can memorize a large amount of information you'll be fine. Not an entertaining or life changing professor but a nice and fair one.

The lecture exams are very straightforward and not too hard. 98% of what is on the tests are in his powerpoints so just study those. The lab is the hard part of this class. Going to a few open labs during the week should be enough to be able to identify most of the structures for the weekly quiz. This class will take a lot of work outside of class.

Great professor for Human Anatomy. I took this class as a non-major required course and loved it. Heavily relies on the TAs to help teach review sessions and answer questions. One of those professors you only really see during lecture, but very nice and has some jokes too. Take advantage of the TA's review sessions and open labs.

Dr. Adams is super nice but not great at explaining things. It is worth it to go to lecture however, to see what parts are confusing and need clarification and then ask clarification in the lecture TA QandA. He does a good job of doing research on questions he didnt know the answer to.

I went to class for the first few weeks and then quit because all we did was go over the slides he posts, and the class got yelled at for talking (it was quiet and barely noticeable in a large lecture hall). I got very high grades on the tests by following the learning objectives and reviewing the textbook, but it took a ton of time and work.

Dr. Adams really knows his stuff and is constantly trying to be a better professor. Lecture is basically going over the slides, but I still went. The study objectives are very true to what is on his tests. He encourages students to go to the Q&A's with the TAs - do it!! They are under-used and key to being successful in this class!

This class was an absolute joke, he just read straight off the slides (which were posted online anyways) so lecture was a snooze-fest. Lab was certainly interesting, but when exams came around, we all expected a curve because, historically, there had always been a curve, but no curve appeared. Incredibly frustrating, hurt a lot of people's grades.

Anatomy lecture and lab are different. You mainly choose a professor for the lecture section. The slides have everything that is on the test which is nice because you know exactly what to study. He does add 2 textbook questions which aren't too bad. Go to the lectures and take notes on what you are confused on, then go to TA lectures and ask there.

Had a tough time staying awake in class. Prof essentially read the slides. Learned more from TA's. Difficult to approach. Schedule worked well. Doesn't encourage participation from class often nor talking among ourselves for clarification.

When I first took Dr. Carrolls Marriage prep class I thought I was a bad listener and was not actually interested in Family life studies. After taking other classes from other professors in the school, I have realized it is just him. Sweet guy but what he is teaching doesn't feel relevant or applicable. He was fine but if you can, scout out others.

I loved my Marriage Prep class from Dr. Carroll. The papers weren't too bad especially given that the rest of the class has very little homework. This class is a serious must-take for both married and single people.

I love this professor, his class is pretty easy overall. There are two 10 page papers, and you have to get two textbooks and read them quite a bit. But there are no final or midterm. Super chill, he loves his students, very informative. I would take his classes again.

The lectures are informative, but the class can feel a bit repetitive. Attendance and readings are both graded, so be sure to stay engaged. Unstuck AI was a lifesaver for study prep - definitely worth checking out alongside the textbook.

Dr. Carroll is such a sweet man, and genuinely knows the material so well. You can tell he cares a lot about what he teaches. The lectures are a bit long winded, and I unfortunately couldn't pay attention because of how long the class was, just because it was a bit boring. I missed quite frequently and still got an A.

Dr. Carroll is smart, passionate, and kind. This class is extremely easy. You just have to go to the lectures, write a couple papers, and take a couple exams. I learned a lot of valuable information from this class and would totally recommend it to others.

I'm going to be honest, there are better ways to prepare for marriage (SFL 376). Lectures and readings cover the same quotes and materials, and given that eternal families is a required class, this feels repetitive and could stand to give us a more well-rounded, social science understanding. A little boring and attendance and reading both graded.

Dr Carroll teaches with clarity and emotion, helping students to understand the content and feel its significance. He is passionate about his subject and the gospel of Jesus Christ. Dr Carrol embodies learning "by study and by faith" to me.

I love Dr. Carroll! His class was life changing & I gained a new perspective on dating, marriage & family life. A lot of the class content was applicable to our everyday life/interactions with others & overall helped me become a better person. There were some large papers but they weren't too bad, the rubric was clear. Take it from him if you can!
I was recommended the marriage prep class from a friend, and boy did it disappoint. lectures were long and felt very boring. Just overall disappointed in this class - take from tammy instead.

I took the online (a mistake, because the highlight of religion classes is the in-class professor enthusiasm. This is lost when recorded). We had 2 large papers, a midterm and final, and a self-reporting attendance/participation. Good content, but a little boring without the human connection.

I left every class feeling inspired. Dr. Carroll is amazing. You do have to try to get an A, but it's not too hard. I learned so much in this class. Take it from him if you can! The only problem I ever had was he has a hard time sticking to his lecture schedule because he just has so much to share.

Jason Carroll is my hero. I can't even tell you how much this class changed my life for the better. I loved it SO much. There is a lot of reading each class, otherwise just two papers, one midterm and a final, and a few other small assignments. You need to do the reading and go to class to get a good grade, but it's so worth it bc you learn so much

This was a great class, but a lot of work. 2 tests, 2 seven page papers, 2 other reports (pretty easy), and TONS of reading every class. Dr. Carroll is very passionate about this subject which made lectures engaging, but he sometimes wouldn't finish the material. Still, gained many new perspectives on the gospel and would take his classes again!

Dr. C is very passionate about what he teaches, which makes class more engaging. Some papers are LONG (start early!) and TAs are harsh graders. I had to petition my grade on one, and Dr. C reviewed it and gave me a better grade. Fascinating material, and pretty easy tests as long as you attend class. You can grow both spiritually and intellectually

Dr. Carroll is a great professor. I grew so much spiritually from this class, I felt that I understood church doctrine instead of church culture. The tests aren't too bad but there are a lot of true/false questions which I don't love, but other than that he is great. I would take a class from him again!

Two seven page papers. Lectures are long and boring. He rambles. What do you need to know for test? unsure. Need to go to class to find out, but he's so boring that you want to leave halfway through. First half of semester is uplifting and inspiring. Last half, boring as heck. I don't know what happened, but it gets super boring.
Dr. Carroll is a great teacher in general. He likes to discuss things so you can lead him astray with comments so he usually doesn't finish the lecture, but he posts his slides.

His class was really easy mostly, although the TAs sometimes graded the papers harshly. He takes 30 minutes to say what could be said in 7 minutes- but other than that, the material is interesting and he presents it well. The tests are based on class learning.

Dr. Carroll is THE BEST! He cares, inspires, is knowledgeable/passionate about his subject, and well prepared. Everyone should take SFL200 from HIM to improve their life/relationships. Nothing matters more. He invites comments and articulately/kindly/wisely shares undiluted doctrine. As an older student I know he teaches TRUTH greatly needed today.

Professor Carroll is really important; I wish everybody at BYU could take his course. He's incredibly intelligent and lectures with purpose. The class is a religious and academic credit and, though this makes the class more difficult, I loved how he blended the two together. His perspective is blunt and refreshing.
He's a great teacher. Really handles controversial topics with a lot of compassion and respectfully.

Dr. Carroll is one of my favorite professors at BYU! He is very inspiring, encouraging, and caring. There are two papers to do during the semester, but they are pretty easy because of the clear instructions. He has a sense of humor and is willing to answer every student's question. Going to his class will definitely enhance your spiritual growth.

Dr. Carroll is hands down one of my favorite professors at BYU so far. His class was AMAZING, and so inspirational. He is really passionate about what he teaches, and he is really easy to work with. The class isn't very demanding, as long as you stay on top of the papers. 10/10 would recommend taking ANY class from him.

Dr. Carroll is hands-down my favorite teacher at the Y. Not only did I think he was charismatic and interesting, but his lectures always brought the Spirit and helped me to learn so much about marriage/dating, with great supporting evidence from prophetic teachings. Definitely would take this class again.
Really great lectures. There are powerpoints for each lesson where he talks about the material. SO HELPFUL. I wish every online class had this. I loved his class!
All the good things are true. He's awesome! He explains things moderately and truthfully. His lectures are so entertaining my spouse came every class. He's a real gem and BYU.

Interesting, applicable material and amazing metaphors. I still use what I learned in daily life. His tests, papers, and assignments were all reasonable. Although you need to be familiar with some specific principles, the tests were pretty intuitive if you went to class, and he doesn't expect students to cite his own lectures in the two papers.

IF you are to take this class, take it from him. Pretty sure he was the one to design the course as it is relatively new. I learned much more than I thought I would. The readings are a lot but they are interesting. I highly recommend this class and this teacher. Pretty life changing stuff.

Dr. Carroll is so full of the spirit! There are two papers that are fairly easy and a midterm and final. Everything you need to know is on the study guide! If questions arise you can ask the TAs. There are also daily reading quizzes. Super easy! Each one is four questions and not timed. I highly recommend Dr. Carroll!!

In Every class you leave feeling elevated. Teaches with the spirit. Cares alot about his students and has a way of teaching that makes it so easy to pay attention and learn. Tests are dece, lots of quizes but if you pay attention you will do fine. Amazing Teacher, and a wonderful person.

Professor Carroll is amazing! He really knows his stuff and his lectures are entertaining and the material is applicable to your life. There's only two papers, two exams, and daily quizzes so if you just keep up on your work and pay attention in class it can be an easy A.

Dr. Carroll requires two big papers in addition to two midterms and a final exam.  Exams are easy if do not overthink them! Attendance is not mandatory, but his classes are dense in material and high in quality, so make sure to attend.  There are lots of required readings from Conference talks and the textbook.  Very willing to meet with students.

Highly recommended! It is evident that Professor Carroll knows the material he teaches, and lives it! Between his real-life experience and research applied into the lectures, you will walk away feeling more prepared for dating, marriage, and parenting. Getting an A is totally do-able, just do your work!

Eh, I didn't care for him. He's prideful and stiff. He didn't like comments from the class and always moved on quickly, as if what he said was more important than answering questions. He took a whole lecture to say something that could be said in one sentence-that said, the slides aren't too helpful if you don't go to class. Wish I didn't take him.
LOTS of reading- too much, I'd say. The lectures are amazing and inspirational, and the tests are straightforward and simple.

One of the best classes I've taken at BYU. Dr. Carroll knows his stuff and explains clearly and enthusiastically. He makes class discussions enjoyable in a way seldom accomplished in a 200-student lecture hall. Takes an interest in students--go to his office hours!

Doctor Carroll is a great teacher who is able to  present the class material in a very knowledgeable manner while impressing upon the students to integrate the lessons  into their own lives. He is super inspirational and cares about all his students. Do the work and the class will be amazing. A life changing class for sure!
He is a good professor. The test and papers are most of your grade. The papers are not hard. The test can be hard if you do not study.

Dr. Carroll is so awesome! His lectures are so informational, and he really encourages open discussion in class about tough subjects. He always welcomes questions in class, and even says we can contact him with questions after the semester is done, because he is just that passionate about helping us in our lives.
Dr. Carroll is funny & inspirational! He cares about his students. The class itself is pretty easy --  2 papers, 2 tests, and reading quizzes. I got an A.

Dr. Carroll was a great teacher. Very funny and made class fun. Clear grading, was always willing to work with you on assignments if you need it. Daily quizzes about readings and attendance. Pretty basic assignments, nothing too hard.

I took Eternal Families/Marriage Prep and it was the BEST. Everything you learn you will use in your life and he has amazing insight. Especially for topics that are harder to discuss. He will having you laughing one minute and feeling the spirit so strongly the next. Easy papers that reflect on your life. I still pull out my notes from time to time

Good professor. Taught in concurrence with prophets' teachings, even in tough subjects like same-sex unions and abortion. Super specific syllabus, so if you can read and follow a syllabus you should be able to do well on papers. Specific study guides, so easy tests, but there were often ambiguous test questions. Tried too hard to be funny though.

I learned so much from Professor Carrol. This class totally changed my perspective on marriage in the best way possible. The three papers he has you write will help you learn a lot about yourself. The tests aren't hard if you go to class and listen.
The Eternal Family class he started is amazing. Hands down my favorite professor at BYU. Hilarious but spiritual class. 3 papers, long but not hard. Take his class, you won't regret it!!!

I never wanted to miss class! I was totally enthralled during every class period. The only assignments are 3  eight-page papers and 2 tests. His tests are straightforward and helpful.  He assigns a lot of reading (which is actually quite valuable), but you can get by without doing it. Do the reading, though, because it will help your life! Worth it

This is the best class I've taken at BYU. Dr. Carroll is not only an amazing professor, but an amazing person. He offers such a unique perspective on preparing for marriage and I honestly loved every second of his course. Grading material is super clear-cut. This class changed my life and my attitudes about family, marriage and dating. TAKE IT!

This is the best class at BYU, and Dr. Carroll is the perfect teacher for it. The truths in this class will change your life. It is not a stressful work load, he is funny, spiritual, and engaging in every class. His assignments effectively help you process the principles taught in class. Take this class or regret it for eternity.

Dr. Carroll teaches in such a clear manner, and perfectly balances gospel teachings with research findings. Lectures are enjoyable, and learning the "secular" parts of marriage prep along with the spiritual was invaluable. It is a three credit class, so do expect to write 3 eight page papers, and have a midterm and final exam.
Great class great Professor. Basically teaches you how to handle and future marriage issues. Class should be made mandatory for all BYU student. Sit back and soak up the teachings like a sponge.

Dr. Carroll is a phenomenal teacher. He's clearly an expert in his field, yet he's still very relatable and understanding of how everyone feels about dating, relationships, and life. He relies perfectly on both scientific research and gospel teachings. It's a class that I wish everyone would take, he knows what he's talking about! Funny & cool guy

Such an amazing professor and man. I learned so much about relationships, marriage, and life from this class. Papers and tests are all super easy; it's an easy A, but you shouldn't take this class for the easy grade-take it for the valuable life lessons. Strongly recommend him and this class for single, dating, engaged, married... Anyone.

Dr. Carroll is by far one of the best teachers at BYU. He has a great interest in the course and in the learning of his students. Three pretty straightforward papers and easy midterm and final as long as you study. Take his course, you will love every minute of it and it will change your life.

BRO. CARROLL AND THIS CLASS CHANGED MY LIFE. It is a class that everyone should take. Single, dating, married, it doesn't matter. The insight, and personal revelation that happens in this class is amazing, and it will change your perspective on marriage. The papers are relevant and insightful. It opens your eyes, heart, and mind, it is a MUST TAKE.

BRO. CARROLL AND THIS CLASS CHANGED MY LIFE. It is absolutely amazing, and I would recommend it to anyone. Single, Dating, Married, it doesn't matter - the principles taught and the spirit of revelation that is in the class will change your perspective on life and marriage. The papers were work, but insightful and helpful as well. A MUST TAKE!

MUST TAKE FOR BYU:) Seriously awesome course- I will use the class principles through the rest of my life. Dr. Carroll is engaging, funny, and so professional with awkward concepts. Papers were fun and taught me a lot. Wish I studied harder for the tests. Overall awesome course!
Great great class. Won't lie had a bro crush on him. Engaging, hilarious, and fun class. Take it from him for sure!

As you can see, everyone who takes this class loves it! An amazing class that helps you gain a testimony of marriage, answers any question you might have, causes you to grow as a person, & teaches you so much. Dr. Carroll is respectful, clear, & teaches the material SO well. You don't have to be dating anyone or ready for marriage, TAKE THIS CLASS!

He is EXCELLENT. So passionate about his field and has so much knowledge. I wasn't even dating someone while taking the class but it changed how I worked with roommates, my family, everyone. Its more about becoming the best person you can be than it is about being married. LOVED it. Wish I could take it again. 2 tests, 3 papers

This class literally changed my life. I think about the principles I learned all the time. I took it when I wasn't dating any one or anything and I'm so grateful I did because I learned SO much about relationships. A beautiful class! Everyone should take it. The papers were kind of too much I thought but not hard.

This was the best class!  Seriously, everybody who has the chance to take the class should!  You learn so much, and he teaches with such enthusiasm.  He helps you find ways to talk about the things that you might have not been able to talk about before.  You learn so much, and think about yourself and life in new ways.

I loved Dr. Carroll. Although SFL 223 doesn't count for religion or GE credits, he really brings the spirit to the subject. He is an amazing professor and you really learn a lot from him.  I would HIGHLY recommend taking marriage prep from him because you learn so much about marriage as the world sees it, and as we see it in the Gospel.
Dr. Carroll is an awesome teacher! I loved his class. He is very insightful and really cares about his students. Great lecturer. The course work and tests are straight-forward.
Loved this class. Dr. Carroll knows his stuff. Never did I not want to go to class. You learn valuable stuff! Highly recommend.

Great class. He teaches so much that is insightful and useful. He also had the best designed PowerPoint presentations of any professor I've had. I just studied the slides and got 100% on the final. Grading procedures and tests are straight-forward and fair. I highly recommend this class, no matter what your current dating status.

This was by far the best class I've taken at BYU!  I have never learned so much that was so applicable to my life right now.  The material can honestly apply to anyone, not just those who are getting married soon.    Professor Carroll is an incredible teacher; I loved listening to the way he explained things and talked about things of such a seriou

Dr. Carroll is a spectacular professor. I think he is one of the best at BYU. He teaches with the Spirit and genuinely cares about his students. I never hesitated to ask a question because he never made anyone feel out of place. SFL 221 is such a great class I learned so much. Take it from Dr. Carroll.

Marital mythbuster. Confidence, peace, understanding. Both highly spiritual and extremely practical. Teaches principles, give examples. You never leave confused. Realistic yet encouraging. Only class I have ever had perfect attendance for. Friend-servant kind of teacher. Walked in as a dating Scrooge.

This professor changed my life!!!!! He is my favorite professor and what I learned from him was incredible. I also gained a greater understanding of the gospel and a greater love for our prophets. Most of all, I learned to be a better disciple of Christ. Seriously one of the most enriching and spiritual experiences of my life. Take it!

BEST CLASS EVER!  Professor Carroll is amazing.  I recommend that everyone take this class.  If you care about finding and becoming the right person in life, TAKE THIS CLASS from Professor Carroll.  It is well worth any effort you have to expend.

This is the BEST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN! I took it because i needed another credit and i am SO glad I took it from Dr. Carroll! I'm not getting married anytime soon but learned SO much about myself and gained amazing insights to what marriage is like. The papers and tests are SO easy and i felt the spirit very often. Wonderful class and teacher!!!
This is the BEST

This class was extremely enlightening! I loved learning from a teacher who is so obviously invested in what he is teaching. The papers are fairly graded and the tests are easy (as long as your study). He is helpful and willing to answer even the most "awkward" of questions with a sincere desire to instruct you.
EVERYONE at BYU should take this class. Great insights for marriage and life in general. Always interesting, never difficult.
Dr. Carroll is dynamite.  Absolutely a dynamite teacher. Easy but engaging class. I learned a lot without feeling unneeded pressure over tests. Easy A but better yet, awesome class.

This is one of the best classes I've taken from BYU, and Dr. Carroll is amazing! He has some very insightful things to teach, and he keeps you interested the whole time. The class is easy, but you learn so much. This was the one class I was really sad to leave on the last day.
Great teacher!!!
Great teacher.  Loved the lectures and easy too talk to.
Great teacher. Go to class, do the readings, and you will get an A. 3 papers. 1 midterm and 1 final. Attendance and reading counts for points.

He is very thought-provoking and kind. I LOVED the lectures. There was a lot of reading, but I still got an A on the tests without reading them. You grade yourself on reading and attendance, so it's based on integrity. Great class.

Second class i've taken from him.  Do your readings and listen in class and you will get an A. He is a leading researcher in the field and several of the reports you study he was a part of. I loved going to class and even went to discuss class topics outside of class and talked to him as more of a counselor/mentor.  A great guy and a great class!

Very caring professor and really knows what he's talking about.  Not a terribly hard class.  Grade yourself on reading and attendance, three papers, and a midterm and a final.  As long as you understand the concepts and put a bit of effort in, you'll be fine.  Highly recommend this class, even if you aren't planning on getting married right away!

Clear, organized, and passionate about the subject matter. Listens to students, genuinely interested in them. Curves his tests quite nicely. Uses the book but goes mainly from class discussions on test. Good teach!

LOVE LOVE LOVE! Thought provoking lectures, interesting readings, no tests. Two large papers but sections were due throughout the semester. He was very clear on what he was looking for in the papers. I loved this class. I was really sad when the semester was over. You will grow as a student but in a comfortable and fun way.

this is an amzing class! He is a marvelous professor and the books are wonderful! I wish this were a core class for everyone to take - it has so much information in it that is useful in all life situations - Take this class! It is wonderful. I took iti n the summer and it was fast, but not unbearable (like AmHtg in the summer!)Two tests and a paper

Dr. Carroll is, hands down, one of my favorite professors at BYU. I absolutely LOVED his class and I can honestly say that it changed my life. He's a fantastic professor and he genuinely cares about his students and his subject. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Great teacher!!! Definitely my favorite teacher so far at BYU. I absolutely loved this class and would recommend it to anyone. You can really tell that Dr. Carroll cares about the information he is teaching and he really loves his students!

An amazing teacher! He captures the essence of a 100 level class—stimulating and educational without being ridiculously difficult. Only one paper and two tests that cover exactly what we go over in class. I would recommend this class with this professor to anyone.

This class was amazing! He is very passionate about the material. He tries to get to know everyone personally and will answer any questions you have. He's a funny guy and he teaches well. This class should be required for all students. The material covered is valuable. 1 paper. Attendance & Reading required- Honor System. Great class!
Best class I have taken at BYU.  It is challenging with the research paper, but he doesn't give tests which helps out.  It is so interesting a class I think everyone should take!

Great teacher.  Every class was educational and enjoyable.  Tests were easy and only one paper was assigned.  Only other assignments were attendance and whether or not you read the chapter before coming to class.  Not only was this an easy class, but it's actually important stuff you'll apply to your life forever.
Take this class! He is a wonderful teacher and you will learn so much. He is very organized and his tests are ridiculously easy (just two tests and a paper). I loved going to class!

At first, I was a little weary about this course. It seemed boring and repetitive. However, after a couple weeks Dr. Carroll became one of my favorite professors in this department. He is an amazing teacher who conveys the subject well. If you read and go to class, you'll do great!

The material covered in this class is EXTREMELY basic. You have to write 2 papers which will require some preparation (start at least a few days in advance).  Tests are rediculously easy.  Take this class for an easy "A".

Dr. Carroll is my favorite teacher in the MFHD department (and I'm graduating!)  I heard wonders prior to the class, and he was even better than that!!  Just go to class and do the readings and you'll get an A.

He is an amazing professor.  He is passionate about his lectures, and relaxed about his exams.  If you attend and keep up on readings, exams are easy.  Papers really aren't hard.  One paper might require planning ahead.

A teacher who understands students at their level, and cares about them on a personal level. I took his class at night and thought it would be hard to have a night class, but he kept my attention the whole time. His class is work, but you learn so much. Amazing teacher!

First couple of classes I wasn't very impressed, but it ended up to be a really good class. Passionate about families and good social scientist. Very easy exams. Two papers that aren't too bad. You just need to start on them early.

I liked the lectures. He planned them so that they built off of the readings. The "study guides" (reading quizzes) helped me learn more during readings. He told the class that the study guide for the tests would be easy to use... he was wrong. The final/midterm study guides were cryptic riddles that kind-of sort-of maybe told you what to study.

Brother Combs is amazing!! My new favorite religion professor. Lectures were spiritual and interesting, and staying engaged was very easy. Assignments were super reasonable: one straightforward quiz per lecture that covered material from the lecture and the upcoming reading assignment, a midterm, and a final. Take his class, you won't regret it!

SUPER interesting lectures. Professor Combs really knows what he is talking about, and I learned a lot about the Bible. There is a good amount of homework, but it's not too hard if you do the reading.
Good professor. I really enjoyed his lectures. His class is fairly easy as long as you put the work in. HW is just reading and then answering some questions from that reading.

He goes into a lot of detail, and the quizzes are easy and don't take very long. If you study at all for the tests you'll do well, and the main class project is engaging and he is lenient on grading things.

Dr. Combs is an excellent professor. This class is a seriously deep, academic dive into the context of the New Testament, and I appreciated the fact that it felt like an actual class rather than a seminary lesson. However, I found the tests ridiculously difficult. Dr. Combs is very receptive to feedback and cares a lot about student input.

I don't know why everyone is giving this guy a good rating. This class is not fun unless you are a scriptorian or wish to be one. I had a tough time focusing in the classes because of how much detail he went into. All of this detail was then graded on the tests. I don't recommend this class unless you are very passionate about the bible

I thought this class was interesting and I learned a lot. There are quizzes for every class reviewing reading but the nice thing is the exams are literally copy and pasted from the quiz questions so just study those. You did have to study for the midterms, but I spent 1-2 hours before each one and got As, because it's easy to find the info!

Super duper amazing teacher and class! I have learned so much and I LOVE Dr. Combs! He is one of the sweetest people ever and crazy knowledgeable!  BTW though, tests are close-not and close-scripture and are thus pretty difficult because you have to memorize some of the chapter summaries. Far from an easy class, but I loved it! Hat tip to this gent

I loved taking this class. He made the course material genuinely so interesting. The class consists of 2 quizzes a week that cover lecture material and reading. They're very simple as long as you pay attention. The class consists of just the class quizzes, attendance, and 4 exams. It was very enjoyable and the class never felt like too much.

Do NOT take this professor. There are TWO 20-25 qtn quizzes each week w/ short answer. Tests are around 60-80 qtns with 3 essay qtns, plus scriptures are not allowed. He tells you what the qtns are in the study guide but that makes it worse because that means he just wants you to spend HOURS of busywork memorizing what HE deems as important.

This is by far the best religion class that I've ever taken at BYU and I can't recommend it enough. It is definitely not easy, as there are a lot of quizzes and a lot of material that is covered in the lectures-- be ready to take notes. Although it demands a lot of work, I learned SO much. It's such a good class and he's the best professor.

Professor Combs is outstanding. His lectures are well prepared and very spiritual. The quizzes are great because they really help you review and prepare for the test. I had a great experience and learned a lot.

Professor Combs is an excellent professor! There is a quiz before every class that take a very long time. He is very approachable and kind, and his teaching style is wonderful. Take notes on everything he says in class!

Professor Combs is incredible! Heavy workload but amazing teacher! Very approachable and good-natured. I definitely recommend. Take notes on what he says in class!! There's a quiz due before each class that's open-note but takes a long time. Study the quizzes for the tests!

Take Professor Combs! He does have a hard (open book/open note) quiz due after each class, but if you really pay attention in class, they are doable. The tests are the EXACT questions from the quizzes, so it balances out. No papers or projects! It was very manageable for a religion class, and Professor Combs does everything he can to help you.

Professor Combs has very engaging lectures and this was such an awesome class to take material wise! However, I think it was way to much work for a religion class. There are 2 quizzes every week that are about 25 questions which are pretty difficult even in you do all the readings. Tests are very hard. Overall too much work for a religion class

I loved taking Dr. Combs as a religion professor! If you're very forgetful (like me) he is awesome because he is constantly sending out reminder emails for the week. He makes sure his religion classes are at a college level while also teaching with the spirit, which I love. The expectations for an A are clear and very doable. Would recommend!

There is a 25-30 question, in-depth quiz after every class. The quizzes have short answer responses as well. Way too much work for a religion class, and not very spiritual. Almost completely academically focused. You'll have a better time with another class if you want anything inspirational.

He's a really good professor, and I really liked how good he was about teaching the facts, and encouraging us to share our own opinions and thoughts. I took it spring semester, so it was condensed, but there was quite a bit of work for a religion class. Not too hard, just time consuming.

Professor Combs is my FAVORITE religious professor. He is so uplifting, has amazing insights and knowledge, and is such a great person. Always genuinely happy. His teaching is amazing and I learned so much. The last time I learned this much and felt this spiritual was being taught by a man who went to Princeton and makes violins. So he's incredible
High spirituality, moderate effort. Exactly what you're looking for in a religion class.

Professor Combs is exactly what you want in a religion professor - he strikes the perfect balance between history/context and doctrine. He is incredibly professional and the lectures are engaging. The textbook is just NT. I took his class during spring term and we didn't have tests, just three easy essays. I wish I had discovered Dr. Combs earlier!

Professor Combs is what other religion professors should strive to be like. I loved his insight as someone who studied Hebrew and theology and didnt go through CES. Theres a real balance between historicity and spirituality. You get to know Christ and gain more knowledge about ancient Israel

Professor Combs really cares about students succeeding in his class. I liked how he spread out the projects to make them manageable. The daily readings and quizzes are kinda hard and require some pretty good notes. An overall great professor! He helps you look at the life of Christ as a historian and a disciple.

Dr. Combs is a good professor but not great. I never had a problem with him or his class, I felt he was respectful and a good teacher, but I did not feel he focused on the spirit much at all. I love academia in the gospel, and this was still too much of a purely academic focus for me. Also, every week there are 2 25-30 Q quizzes every week :/

I loved this class! Each class has a pre-class quiz (you take it while you do the reading so it's low-stress) that I learned so much from. Make sure you stay on top of your work and take good notes in lecture. You learn about scripture of Christ with historical, doctrinal, and application approaches. Great class!

I LOVE Professor Combs. He set up his class with a perfect balance between history, doctrine, and application. His tests are easy because they are based off the quizzes and they are open book (atleast during COVID). He does have a MAJOR project that is made up of lots of papers and takes time every week but it made for a good experience. 10/10.

I took New Testament, and it was a good experience overall. Prof. Combs was very caring and interested in his subject of teaching but I didn't always feel that he projected it onto the students very well. All test questions come from quiz questions, and quiz questions come from weekly readings and lectures. Easy A if you pay attention.

I will say that Prof. Combs is straight forward. What is in the syllabus, is what will happen in the class. There is a lot of reading. Quizzes after every class. Overall not too difficult. Gives a study guide for the final that really helps. But, if you are looking for inspirational - wrong class. Sometimes I felt the quizzes were there to trick me

Good news: Combs is the best. He's knowledgeable, interesting, and cares about his students. I messed up with essays and after talking to him he let me resubmit all of them. He is very approachable and has office hours and unofficial office hours every week. Bad news: two quizzes a week, and a paper every week. It's a tough class, but he's great.

This class has a lot of work to stay on top of, but I don't think that is a bad thing. Analyzes the scriptures from more historical perspective, which might be off-putting for some but I thought it was super interesting. Very structured class. If looking for something easy, not this one. Something difficult and different, this one. Take good notes.

Professor Combs assigned the most homework I've ever had for a religion class. We had a quiz and a writing assignment before every single class and the quizzes were so hard. If you missed class then you would not know a large portion of the answers. He is a really nice guy, but not super interesting. Not the best religion class at BYU.

Prof Combs is kind, clear, always willing to answer questions, and he includes writings from multiple perspectives. I actually learned useful things about biblical history instead of empty words meant to build a testimony on a foundation of fluff. He's great, especially if you're outside mainstream BYU culture (eg. LGBTQ+, not LDS, etc).

He said on the first day that it's not his focus to have the spirit in class and I should've dropped the class then. Each class has a lot of assigned reading and a 25-30 question quiz, which the tests come directly from. Prof Combs knows a lot and is nice but I was very disappointed with how little we talked about Christ in a class about Christ.

Brother Combs is nice and cares about his students. The class isn't hard and the 2 tests make up 50 percent of your grade. However, I felt like he spent way too much time teaching about the historical Jesus and didn't focus at all on building students' testimonies in the Savior. Pretty easy A, but didn't feel like my testimony was strengthened.

The midterm and final make up half of your grade, but he takes all of the test questions straight from the quizzes, which you can look at any time. Still, there are 450+ quiz questions to review per test. Tests aren't comprehensive. Write an easy paper before ever class period. Much harder than some other religion classes, but not bad at all.

Professor Combs is a good guy, but I felt like all his quizzes and tests were more like a trivia game and that he focused WAY too much on Jesus as a historical figure and not as the divine son of God. Overall I felt like I learned a bunch of random facts about history and nothing about the character of Christ in the New Testament.

Professor Combs is a wonderful professor. His lectures are engaging and interesting. There is quite a bit of reading before each class, and a corresponding quiz . To make up for all the time you spend on quizzes, though, he creates the tests based on the quizzes. He usually takes questions directly from the quizzes and puts them on the tests.

It's Comb's first time teaching this class, & he is great. I'm not Mormon anymore so religion classes are painful, but he is amazing to learn from. He is both factual and spiritual, and wants his students to really learn history and context about the Bible. His lectures have made me interested in learning more on my own about religious history.

Dr Combs is a New Testament historian, NOT a seminary teacher. It's definitely not a "come to class, feel good, and get an A" kind of class. He's totally upfront about that, and is even willing to recommend other teachers if you already have a heavy semester. But if you want to really deep-dive into the NT, take his class! (Also, it's not TOO hard)

Professor Combs gives great lectures, and attendance was taken in class. The homework consisted of some readings and an online quiz, which would generally take over an hour to complete. The two tests were very straightforward and based on the lectures and readings. Definitely recommended!
Reading, quiz, and a paragraph or two before each class. Tests were basically the big points from the quizzes. It has been easily my favorite religion class so far.

Professor Combs is great. His lectures are enjoyable and he definitely cares about the success of his students. Most of the grade is based off of the midterm and final, both of which consist almost entirely of quiz questions taken throughout the course. If you put in a decent amount of effort you will get an A in the class.

Professor Combs really knows his stuff. I have learned so much about the New Testament by taking this class. There are plenty of thought-provoking concepts and it is very easy to have a discussion and ask questions. It has definitely opened my mind to new perspectives! I feel that I have a much deeper, and cooler, understanding of the New Testament

I loved this class. If you do the reading and pay attention in class, you will definitely get an A. This isn't your typical religion class either. It's not like seminary. There's a lot more secular and academic content, which I really liked. Bro Combs is super caring and funny. He wants to help his students grow and succeed.

Professor Combs is so caring and willing to work with students. Tests are based off of the quizzes you take so don't stress about them too much. The class takes a very academic approach to learning the Gospels, but its definitely doable. Overall, Professor Combs is one of my favorite teachers thus far.

Dr. Combs is a very caring and kind teacher, but I will say that this class is incredibly difficult for a religion class. I got an A but it was like a 95 and that was one of the top. There are quizzes after every class and if you don't take a ton of notes it's hard to do super well on them. Tests pull from the quizzes but aren't identical questions

Prof Combs is the best! Very organized lectures, takes time to listen to and respect student comments or questions. Loved the more academic approach to New Testament. I learned a lot. Maybe more difficult than fluffy religion classes, but a lot less speculation and a lot more spiritually enriching.

I liked this class because it was super organized so you knew what to expect every week. Each week there is a 150 word journal entry-like essay on the readings and an open book, open note quiz thats around 20 questions. The two lowest quiz scores are dropped. Tests are based on quiz questions, no surprises. Great lectures. Great guy.

Bi weekly 150 word essays, and bi weekly 29 question quiz. You will miss 2-3 per quiz, sometimes 6. Drops lowest 2 scores. Readings can get long. The Midterm is your main concern. it ranges from 45-55 questions which come from your bi weekly quizzes. Sounds easy, but you have over 220 quiz questions to memorize. Avg Score for the class was 75%

My favorite religion professor ever! He maintains a perfect balance between uplifting and educational. I learned SO much about the New Testament. He's super caring and available all the time and VERY knowledgeable about what he's teaching. I would highly recommend! Super easy tests and all quizes are open book.

Professor Combs covers lots of interesting/controversial topics in the Book of Mormon. He is not afraid to answer and discuss questions and he provides lots of resources. There is a daily quiz and writing assignment, but they go by quick once you get the hang of them. The 3 tests are based on the daily quizzes and you'll do well if you study them.

Combs is good. Not your average religion class. Goes more in depth with history and context rather than spiritual aspects, but he says that at the beginning. 2 quizzes a week, 20-30 questions but if you pay attention and do the readings it's easy. Also write 2 reflection papers a week, 150-300 words. Tests pull purely from quizzes.

He is a great teacher. The tests are way easy. All you have to do is read, take a quiz, and write 150-300 words for each class period. He gives you the things you need to know from the lecture for the quiz. The tests are made up of only quiz questions.

This was my favorite religions class I've ever taken! Prof. Combs was super awesome, very clear with what we were graded on, and the test material was based on what we learned in class and our reading. Lectures are important, but he makes everything very clear and will usually point out what you really need to know. Awesome class and teacher!
This guy is GREAT! Tests were easy, and in class which made them super short as well. Overall I would say this is a great professor to take the class from. It was an easy and fun lecture.

I actually really enjoyed Bro. Combs's lectures! He had interesting ideas to present, and wasn't afraid to approach controversial topics. LOTS of reading.  The biggest problem I had was his attendance policy was more unforgiving than any class I've ever taken. Watch out, if you're more than 5 minutes late to class, he counts it as HALF an absence.

Lectures are always interesting and worth going to, final grade is based off 3 exams (not cumulative) and short quizzes/writing assignments due before each class period. Really easy to get an A if you do the busy work.

Brother Combs' class is very discussion heavy. He's more on the liberal side, so if you're still living in 1965, maybe don't take his class (that being said, this comes up maybe 3 times throughout the semester). The work isn't hard, the tests are pulled from the online quizzes directly. Would recommend

This class is the easiest religion class I've ever taken. His tests are all  based off weekly quizzes on learning suite, so study those and you are good to go! Just do your readings and show up to class and its an A. The lectures are pretty good as well, so you learn something new each time.

I feel like the purpose of religion class is to help us be more spiritual and be able to recognize the holy spirit. This class is more focus on historical topics and view BOM as a literature instead of a scripture. I'm not saying it is not a good class, but I expected more inspirational insight.

Combs makes sure that each class you leave with a new understanding of the section of scripture you're looking at. There is quite a bit of reading but they're great! There are weekly quizzes, but there nothing to be afraid of. He was really good with dealing with tough subjects and questions that came up in class. Overall, great Religion teacher.

Jason challenges you to think about the Book of Mormon in different and interesting ways. He is not afraid to discuss difficult and pertinent topics. There is a lot of reading, a quiz and a small writing assignment for each class and a lot of participation in class. The class defintely is worth the work. Will take from him again!
Great testimony! You learn lots of fun facts from him. Doesn't post reading assignments for next class until a day or two before.

There was reading for each class, both from the BofM and a supplemental reading. Sometimes heavy, but never overwhelming. The quizzes are open book but you really need to pay attention to the reading and lecture to get the right answer. Tests are not cumulative and are only based on what was covered in the quiz. Overall good professor.

After every class there is a quiz and writing assigned to go over what was talked about and the readings for the next class. Amazing lectures. Really knows his stuff. Is very nice and willing to answer any question. If you skip class it can be hard for the quizzes but normally not bad. Highly recommend

There are weekly quizzes and writing assignments on readings and lectures. But there nothing to be scared of. If you participate in lecture and at least skim all the reading assignments you'll pass.  He's a super chill teacher and he makes the scriptures fun and new to everyone. Every lecture and reading I learned something new.

This is the first official class of the Ad program and believe me, you won't regret taking it from Jason. Jason cares about his students and helps us develop skills to succeed in the program. The class set me up for the program ahead and validated my choice of major!! The bulk of it is two very manageable campaign strategy group projects.

I've taken a few classes with Jason and he's incredible. He cares so much about his students and their success. He also does a great job tying the Gospel into class. I have learned a lot from him and he has helped me improve in many aspects in preparation for my career. He is the best professor for Advertising Management students.

I was sadly disappointed in this class...lots of people say Jason has experience "working in the field" but he doesn't seem to have much. I was hoping for more tangible, actionable information that we could use in our jobs, but the this class focuses on advertising theories rather than HOW to accomplish the course objectives in the workforce.

This class is not for you if you prioritize anything above school. In person attendance is absolutely mandatory. If you've done the classes before this it's just the same thing as before, so the work is not hard. But if you think you can miss class get ready for a phone call from the professor.

I would do anything to have every class possible with Jason. I have NEVER had a more caring professor in my time at BYU. He works so hard to be engaged with each student and takes time to help groups work through their projects. He also has great real-world experience in the advertising industry. IF YOU CAN TAKE A CLASS WITH JASON, DO IT!!!

I took Comms 230, it was his first year teaching it. He did a really good job. You can tell that he really wants his students to succeed and get into the Ad Lab. He is willing to work with you at all times to make sure that you feel confident in your work
Jason is great! Sometimes class can drag on a bit but he's so educated and has great resources.

I've taken a couple of classes from Jason now. I love having him as a professor. He knows the advertising industry well and cares ab our success. Classes are pretty easy but also effective. No busy work. I feel like I have learned so much from him. If you are an account management student, Jason is the best advertising faculty person to work with.

I have taken 3 classes from Jason and would take every single one of my advertising classes from him. He has real industry experience which is super valuable. No tests, only simple but meaningful projects. Class is always discussion based. Little workload. Super nice guy and really cares about his students.

Jason is a newer professor but knows a lot about the field. His grading is tougher than other professors in the program. A lot of this class was talking about what we had read the night before as a class and then maybe a few slides of new material. He brought in guest speakers which were fun to listen to. Our final is a group project.

Jason was a great professor! While the material wasn't my favorite, he definitely tried to keep it light and interesting - even while we were all on zoom. I love how he brought in guest speakers, gave us opportunities for discussion, and how we could work with others in the class. Also no tests, which was a huge bonus. Just some group projects!

Jason was great! He's a new professor, but has lots of experience in the ad industry. No tests, but weekly readings & responses, group projects & presentations. Does a great job of making the class fun and engaging. He's young which makes him feel more relatable! Brought in great guests speakers. Gives good feedback.

Dr. Hansen is the best professor I have had at BYU. He KNOWS his stuff. There are in depth tests and quizzes - you will not do well if you don't know how to study. He wants you to actually know and understand, not just memorize. He really does care about his students. Meet with him during office hours!! I highly recommend taking CELL 305 from him!

Dr Hansen is a funny guy, but he shouldn't be teaching physiology. He is not good at teaching, but he does know his stuff. Granted I could have studied harder, but every single quiz in class was either short answer or had genuinely 10 options to choose from. His tests were always worded horribly and he tries to trick you and only talks about sports

CELL 305 Insanely hard--there were tears. Teaches too fast and only based on his slides he would fill with jokes and quirky pictures to the point that when I studied the slides I wasn't sure what it was saying when its just a picture of nicolas cage. Pretty sure he is only a professor so he has an audience for his wannabe stand up comedy routine.
