Finally a professor in the bio department that actually cares about understanding and application over rote memorization. His 305 class is TOUGH but it's excellent DAT prep. At least 7 or 8 times during the DAT I referred back to something he said during class. Awesome lectures too. Loved loved loved this class

Professor Hansen is incredible! Physiology is genuinely my favorite class I've ever taken. The class itself is very difficult concept wise, and the tests are your entire grade. Quizzes every Monday in class and iClicker participation. He's hilarious and engaging and makes you love the subject even though it's hard!

Easily one of the best professors I took from at BYU! I took the independent study course and my meetings with him were the reason I was able to do well, in addition to extensive studying. Dr. Hansen listened to my concerns and strived to meet my needs. He did whatever he could to help me succeed! I would recommend his class to anyone.

He is a very entertaining professor and knows so much about physiology. His quizzes were really hard and tests even harder with questions A-J answers. You have to memorize and be able to apply every slide he every shows you. I ended up retaking the class from a different professor and got an A.

Some things he told us to specifically write down: "Out of control ovaries." "That's the unit of measurement, crap ton, of coronaviruses." "hopeful urine." "For every gram of hemoglobin you have, you can carry 1.34 milliliters of oxygen." "The worst time to make urine is when you're running from a bear." It's difficult, but you'll like his class.

By far one of my favorite professors ever. Physiology is a hard subject, and I do believe he went way more in depth than other classes, but the class has made me understand things a lot more. He definitely prepares you to work in the medical field and understand why things work. Hilarious professor and loved the class, but hardest tests ever.

I loved taking Physiology from Jason Hansen! He was by far my most favorite professor at BYU, and I would recommend him 10/10 for anyone. He's caring and upfront of what the class is like and the expectations and grading. The in-class quizzes are hard, but it prepares you well for exams if you actually study for them. I never used the textbook.

I loved Dr. Hansen! He was very engaging which was good because it was a very hard class. The grade is made up of 3 midterm exams, a final and weekly quizzes which are all curved. Physiology is a hard class but I appreciate that Dr. Hansen knows that and was very supportive and fair.

There's never a dull moment in Dr. Hansen's class! He got me laughing out loud on several occasions. His tests are tough but curved generously. This class is very conceptual; you can't get by on memorization and test-taking techniques. The content builds on itself so it's worth taking time to actually grasp it. The TAs are your greatest resource!
His lectures are awesome! Genuinely funny and nice guy. Tough class but he is open to review the exams with you. Study hard and take Physiology from Hansen.

Hardest. Exams. Ever. Hansen is such a great professor and he really is helpful outside of lecture to work with, but your grade is mostly based on exam scores, the final being 40% of your grade, and his tests are anything but easy. Simply memorizing all the material on the slides will get you nowhere in this class. Very conceptual based.

One of the few high-level classes that really reflect your grades on your study habits. The effort and time you put in mirror well with your scores. He's the most entertaining professor I've ever taken, and his quality of teaching is unmatched.

I went into this class feeling I would get pummeled and that Dr. Hansen was harsh regarding tests and how class ran. However, I have finished this class LOVING Dr. Hansen's lectures. He always is fun, inspirational, and has high expectations. I was pushed in this class, but I have never learned so much and been so diligent. Would take this again.

I am now a 2nd year medical student but I just wanted to come back and praise Dr. Hansen's course. The tests are difficult, but they're also heavily curved. He structures the curriculum like med schools teach it and if you learn it in Hansen's class, you will honestly be more than prepared for grad level physio. Study lots and go to TA reviews!

I am so grateful for Dr. Hansen. Physiology is a difficult concept to grasp, but he taught clearly and helped us have a fun time while doing so. He cares about his students and is willing to work with you to help you improve! My favorite professor at BYU so far. Be ready to study though. Physiology covers so much.

Professor Hansen was easily one of my favorite professors I have taken a class from at BYU. His lectures were hilarious, but more importantly, he always the concepts in class clearly and effectively. The course emphasized learning over rote memorization. Professor Hansen was always helpful, kind, and supportive. I'd give him a 6 if I could.

I freaking LOVED Hansen. I was FREAKING out about physiology, but it ended up being one of the best classes. He teaches so you understand, not just memorize so it is a lot of concepts. Lectures feel like a firehose but then you go over it and it's not as much as you would think. This tests are super hard, but also very fair. 10/10 would recommend.

This has been the hardest class I have taken at BYU. Dr. Hansen uses humor and videos to keep you intrigued, however, I found myself having to teach myself a lot of material using the textbook I purchased. He teaches very, very quickly. Weekly quizzes that were set up very differently than exams. 4 exams total -- the final being 30% of your grade.

This is a very hard class, but he goes further than what the department requires. I wish that I had taken this from the other professor hansen, I watched her lectures with a friend and they were so much clearer and understandable. Be ready to take notes, have things thrown at you at light speed, and be confused beyond help.

He really made me feel dumb a lot during class. He would put me and other students down when we would ask a legitimate question, just so he could make a joke about our "apparently" outrageous and nonsensical question. If you take this class just be ready to review every single PowerPoint slide.

Don't take CELL305 from him. He can be very arrogant and he acts like he knows more than anyone else alive. While he is very smart, he cannot teach well. I was very confused and the only thing that helped was going to the TAs. If you do take this class, make sure to become best friends with your TA.  There is no other way to survive without them

I would never recommend taking this class from Hansen. He masked his terrible teaching and confusing/incoherent lecture slides with jokes and funny videos he would pull up during class. He made the lectures very light-hearted, and then the tests were so deep I swore I was given the wrong test booklet.

LOVED this class. Easily the hardest class I have ever taken. His tests and quizzes are really hard- and those are the only things in the grade book. He is amazing at curves tho- he knows his tests are tough. Legit answers are multiple choice sometimes A-i !!!!!! But whatever you do, take it from him, he is hilarious and helps you understand!!!

I wouldn’t bother with taking this class from him. He is a terrible teacher and goes on huge tangents but still expects you to learn the slides we would have went over if he didn’t get distracted. Just take it from someone else

Never take this class from him. He makes class funny and easy to sit through but his quizzes and tests are extremely difficult and you never really know what to study. He is clearly only at BYU to do research, and he is hardly accessible outside of class. I started going to other phys classes and those teachers made things much easier to understand

Dr. Hansen's class has been my favorite class that I've taken while at BYU, it was also the hardest. But overall he makes it super rewarding. Just make sure to study really consistently and reach out if you need help. Find a weekly study group that you can go over the lectures with. Just apply yourself and you'll be golden! Super interesting class.

Dr. Hansen was the most amazing professor that I have had at BYU! The entire class is based off of quizzes, participation and tests. This class requires a lot of studying, but if you put in the work you can do really well. If you are going to take this class, definitely take it from Dr. Hansen. Also, don't buy the textbook.

Definitely one of the hardest classes I've taken at BYU, but one of the most rewarding! Lectures can be overwhelming, but if you ask questions Dr. Hansen is more than willing to slow down. Start a weekly study group early on to go over lectures/learning objectives and you'll be just fine! Didn't use the textbook. Gradetests & weekly quizzes.

I loved Dr. Hansen's class! Absolutely zero busy work--grades are solely based on tests (which are heavily curved), quizzes and participation. The class is very fast paced, but Dr. Hansen and the TA's are very helpful and the TA's hold great reviews before tests. Also, do NOT buy the textbook! Just review the lecture slides/study objectives!!

Don't listen to the bad reviews. This class takes work, he kinda needs to go fast because there's so much material. Come ready to be focused for 2 hours. He uses good humor to give your brain a break. I was very overwhelmed by his course at first. However, AS I REVIEWED HIS LECTURE SLIDES AND TA REVIEWS, it became 10x easier. Just study a lot.

I felt like I was in a whirlwind every-time I sat down for lecture. I probably developed carpel tunnel from writing notes in this class. He moves through the slides at an impossible speed, assuming we all comprehend the madness that is going on around us. His tests are made to crush your soul, theres options A-I for each question. Brace yourself.

Don't listen to negative reviews! Dr. Hansen is honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. He has a gift for making difficult concepts easier. You definitely need to put in the work, you can't expect to just go to class and have it down. Study hard and it'll be worth it! Use learning objectives to guide your study and you'll be just fine.

One of the worst, if not the worst professors I have ever had. His lectures are just him spitting out a ton of information 1 million mph and then expects us to know it all in 5 seconds. He is not clear in what he wants us to know for the tests ("anything I say can be used"), he doesn't record, and his tests are worded to trick you. Don't take!

His lectures mostly consist of him spewing out information with little info on slides, and he doesn't record lectures so we can't try to find info we missed. Very friendly and remembers peoples' names. Brags about how hard his class is, and how no one has got 100% on any tests. The department requirements are MUCH lower than his. Go over all slides

Dr. Hansen is one of the best professors I have ever had. He responds quickly to emails and he teaches the material clearly and gives time for students to ask questions. He is very funny and made this super hard course enjoyable! Not an easy class, but if you put in the effort you will do fine. Doesn't offer extra credit, but curves tests!

Not a good teacher, TA's don't even always know what's going on. Think's he's hilarious but puts students down during class when they ask questions just to make a funny joke. Not very approachable when discussing tests, just makes you feel stupid. Definitely try to take physiology from a different teacher

He is amazing. He is honestly the best teacher to take this class from. He teaches the material really well and is clear on what he tests you on. He also curves a lot of stuff. You have to study but this is the best way to take PDBIO 305. He truly is the most amazing professor.

Dr. Hansen is an awesome professor. His lectures are super interesting and he explains complicated systems in a way that is super understandable. His tests are hard and the course itself is a lot of work, but he is willing to work with you. He always has office hours and really wants you to succeed.

I Love Dr. Hansen. He is seriously the best. There is no busy work. His test are off of the lectures and he doesn't try to trick you in the tests. You have to know your stuff but if you study its super easy to do well! His lectures are super interesting and engaging and he really cares about his students. I wish every class was like this one.

My favorite professor at BYU. He is super funny, makes the class interesting and cares about the success of his students. Weekly quizzes are a blessing and a curse, they make you stay on top of studying but are pretty difficult. The quiz questions more difficult than the exam questions. If you do well on the quizzes you'll do well on the test.

Prof Hansen is super funny. His lectures contain a lot of material but he does well at explaining them. Use the TA's, I would not have gotten a good grade in this class without them. Stay on top of reviewing lectures every week - he has weekly quizzes over the previous weeks material, they aren't too bad usually if you study for them. Awesome class
Dr. Hansen is AMAZING! There is a lot of material to learn but he makes it fun and engaging. Don't get intimidated by the quizzes and tests, just meet with the TAs and you'll do great.

VERY good at explaining concepts. FUNNY. He & his TAs are readily available outside class for any questions (100% RECOMMEND). 3 tests+final, in-class participation pts, & quiz about once/wk. Tons of info, but interesting. Study at least twice a week(1 hr each time w/a study group), & see TAs or Hansen once/wk. Make note of his "random" stories.

Dr. Hansen is hilarious and I love going to class. It's tough, though. Physiology is not my thing. The ONLY things in the gradebook are tests, quizzes, and participation. He grades really strictly, especially on quizzes. Luckily he curves the tests and is really willing to help out.

I took physiology from two professors and Dr. Jason Hansen was MUCH better and WAY more clear and fair. He curves every single test, usually by a lot. He knows the class is hard but makes up for it by being humorous and relating the material to real-life. His tests are not bad as long as you put in the time. Would take the classfrom him again.

You will spend hours upon hours studying for this class. Tests and Monday morning quizzes are HARD and the only things in the grade book.. He has a curve but it is not dependable. Screw whoever said its an easy A. He's hilarious but not a great professor. iClicker Attendance basically daily but if you go most of the time you get full points.

Dr. Hansen was my favorite teacher I've ever taken at BYU. He is hilarious and he actually cares about you and that you learn physiology. People say his tests are hard, but really if you just know what's on his slides and go to class it really should be an easy A.

Jasen Hansen is awesome! A funny dude who cares about his students. Weekly quizzes can be tricky, so study HARD. The tests are hard too, but he curves those suckers. I read the book along with the slides which helped a ton.

Professor Hansen is awesome!!! He is soooooooo funny, but he also is a great teacher! You don't need the book at all, just his slides which are all on LS. He also curves all the tests based on the average of the top 6 people, which is super nice. His only grades are tests and weekly quizzes, and if you go to class and study, you'll do great!

Prof. Hansen is freaking hilarious! He makes the hard lectures/material so much more bearable with his funny lectures and tests. I would recommend using the textbook & getting in a really good study group for this class. Make sure you study for the weekly quizzes each Monday-or they will come back to bite you. Overall, Hansen was an amazing teacher

HILARIOUS. Hansen is the man! I actually want to come to class and his office hours. Physiology is really hard, but he tries to make it easier and fun. The tests aren't that bad. The only thing to worry about is the weekly quiz. Those are HARD. He usually gives an extra credit question on the quiz to redeem yourself. He curves tests!!!! a ton!!!!

Prof. Hansen's class is tough no doubt. All PDBIO 305 are not gonna be easy. BUT his class was super fun to attend because he is always cracking jokes and you definitely don't need the textbook, just read and study the slides. You do have to go to class though and study outside of class to get a good grade but I'd definitely recommend him.

His class is only exams and weekly 5 question quizzes, plus participation/attendance points. Each lecture's powerpoint has a slide of learning objectives which are GOLD for the exams. If you understand those then you're set for the exams. Dr. Hansen is outgoing and his lectures are clear. He is always helpful in and out of class.  Highly reccommend

This is one of those classes that can change the course of what you want to study at BYU. Professor Hansen is a hard grader, but if you go to class, pay attention to the lectures, and work with the TA's, you'll learn a lot and pass the class. He is easy to reach and always willing to help. Also, never laughed harder than during his lectures.

Dr. Hansen is really great.  His class is fun, he's super funny, and he definitely is passionate about physiology.  He's great at explaining difficult things and making real connections that are interesting and applicable.  This being said: his class is hard.  I worked my tail off to get an A and the vast !VAST! majority of points come from exams.

Professor Hansen is one of the best professors i've ever had. He is hilarious and is able to teach is such an entertaining way. He has weekly tests, but if you go over the lecture material it's fine. I loved his class and teaching.

Dr. Hansen was one of the best professors I have ever had. There was a quiz every week that you had to study for, but if you paid attention and took good notes, you could do fine on them. No joke, he was the funniest person ever. His lectures were so funny, entertaining, and helpful. I wouldn't take 305 from anybody else if I were you.

Dr Hansen is nice enough in class, but if you're not part of his fan club, good luck getting anything from him outside of class.  He sometimes seemed more interested in making a clever joke than teaching.  Aside from that, teaches fairly well and the material is interesting.

Students who don't do well probably aren't reviewing the material in a study group outside of class. Tests are very fair and demonstrate how much effort you put into the class. He is SO funny and willing to help you with whatever questions you have. He WANTS you to understand.

This class is AMAZING. He is great at explaining things. If you don't understand, it's as simple as asking him to repeat or explain in a different way. If you only show up to class and reviews you will not do well. You must be able to study to explain it to another student. If you can do that, EASY A. You have to put in the effort BEFORE the test.

He is the man! He is a super funny lecturer and he is good at explaining things. Physiology is tough. If you think it is going to be easy then you are in for a rough ride no matter where you go. As a premed student preparing for the MCAT, I found his testing style to be very helpful because it is pretty similar to how the MCAT tests. He is great.

He was a really funny teacher and it seemed like things made sense sometimes in class. The tests were so hard I felt like I was making an educated guess on every question even though I had attended all the reviews (which are not always helpful), extra reviews and studied a lot. Hardest tests I have ever taken and I am about to graduate.

He made jokes in class and was funny, but he just assumed that you knew the material and what he was talking about. Moves too fast and grades too hard. Quizes every week and the tests are not straight forward but very confusing. If you want to dedicate your life to a class, this is the class for you.

awesome teacher! just know what the learning objectives ask and ask questions during class if he goes through a process too fast and he will re-explain it. i went to his office hours often and he was very helpful, the TAs also saved me. totally possible to get an A, just have to have solid notes and make sure you know them

Dr. Hansen is a really nice guy and is willing to help. He is funny and lectures can be entertaining. However, you take quizzes every other day in class and his quiz questions, and especially test questions, are incredibly vague and hard to understand.

Dr. Hansen is one of THE MOST HELPFUL TEACHERS I'VE EVER HAD!!!  His willingness to work with me after I missed (more than several) weeks of school was lifesaving.  Everybody passes, but not all get a great grade.  But he will go to any length you ask to make sure you understand.  Very approachable, just overall great.

Dr. Hansen's class was awesome! Probably one of my favorites at BYU. He gives a quiz every Monday, but I studied for an hour before class, and did just fine. Some were trickier than others. Tests were fairly easy, but make sure to study anyway. You won't need to get the textbook, but make sure to go to class!

This class is tough, but it's physiology, for heaven's sake.  What do you expect?  Dr. Hansen is freakin hilarious!  He also wants you to understand the material.  He's very approachable, and if there is a concept you don't understand don't be afraid to ask him.  If you're having trouble, please go to him.  He's so understanding and helpful.

Dr. Hansen is an awesome professor. I absolutely loved going to his class and it helped me learn so much. His tests are tough, but he's very reasonable and there was a major curve in my section so that everyone was able to perform well. He's hilarious and makes physiology super interesting and has prepared me for my later science classes. Great!

Way nice guy, super willing to help and answer questions. Hilarious. Fascinating lectures. But the quizzes and tests are your only grades and they are harder than heck, so be ready for that. Like really ready.

Professor Hansen is great ! His lectures are entertaining,but cover what is needed for the quizzes and exams. There is a quiz every Monday-they are HARD and the exams are tough too, but if you study up on the slides  you will do fine. No homework which is great!  He cares about the students and makes himself available for questions and help.

While this class is hard, it is also one of the best classes at BYU. You will learn interesting, applicable information. He is an awesome teacher with entertaining lectures. His tests are hard but he gives a generous curve.

Dr. Hansen is awesome, very nice & entertaining, makes long lectures go by fast. If you want to learn physiology and not fall asleep in the process but gain some real insight into how the body works: this is the class! He really knows his stuff! His tests are hard but fair if you study the learning objectives you are set and no busywork at all!

I'm not sure why Dr. Hansen has low reviews. This it the type of class that if you go to class every day, and really pay attention and take notes you will do well. I believe all the people who do poorly in this class don't pay attention in class, or skip class and try and make up by reading.  Also, he gives an extremely generous curve so he is fair

Dr. Hansen is a really cool guy that gives very interesting lectures. That being said, this class was ridiculously hard. Weekly quizzes and tests that most people did not do too well on. Test questions are hard to understand, and while he does curve test scores, he doesn't give ANY study guides or help as to what will be on the tests.

Dr Hansen is awesome. He does everything he can to make sure you succeed and is super helpful if you need help with anything. Tests are hard, but fair. You'll have to study a lot but you will learn a ton from him! Study hard for every quiz! Overall this was one of my favorite classes.

New to teaching at BYU. Was in his first PdBio 305 class, so it was difficult. Powerpoints for every lecture but not all info is there. TAKE GOOD NOTES!  You might want to record lectures, they saved me when studying for tests! Quizzes every week, tests are pretty tough, but curved! Struggling? Ask him for help. He wants you to do well. Use the TAs

He is fun and lectures are super interesting, but he can be disorganized and hard to understand sometimes. Also, tests and quizzes are pretty hard. You pretty much need to be studying all the time. Its not impossible to get an A, but pretty hard. However he DOES care about students & offers great help when one on one!!
Don't take physiology from Hansen if you can. He is really tough. Terribly worded questions on quizzes and tests. It's possible to get an A, but its tough.

This is a tough class, but Professor Hansen is a fair professor. The quizzes and tests and hard, but if you put in the time and study for them you will do well. Each test was curved, which was great! Go to class, spend time out of class studying each week, and go to his office hours to ask questions. He wants you to do well!

Don't take from Hansen! He's a nice, funny guy, but his class is very unorganized and you don't really know what will be on the tests. He just says to study everything. Also, the tests themselves are ridiculous. The wording of the questions and answer choices completely threw me off and I felt like my hours of studying just went down the drain.
He is not chill

I took Dr. Adams in the spring 2026. Lectures and lab are each 50% of your grade. For lecture tests he gives you learning objectives and I filled them out based off the information on the slides and how he described the slides in class. I did very well with this tactic. His office hours are great to go to to understand more difficult concepts

This class is brutal, he doesn't really teach he just reads off the slides. If you take this during spring it will consume your entire life. Make sure you are dedicated to studying the lectures and going into lab hours. It's basically just hours of memorization but you can not procrastinate! Make sure you study the lecture slides very well

Lots of material. Most anatomy lecture teachers were about the same quality, though. What matters is having good TAs. Both lecture and lab TAs are all incredible. The lecture material is just something to get over with. The lab is where you thrive and love life.

His lectures were so boring I feel like I wasted my opportunity to enjoy the class because of him. He doesn't care about student's situations and no matter how much you need his help he won't help. Also, one of my friends was taking the class from Dr Gonda and her exams were way easier than his. Don't take it from him. I wish I was told that before

He is really nice and very accomodating and unfortunately really really boring. He speaks with the same level of tone every lecture every day. Really easy to fall asleep in his class and most learning has to happen outside of lecture. I recommend choosing another teacher

Dr. Adams loves anatomy but he isn't caring. His Lectures are not interesting at all. I think that he has great knowledge but doesn't have the ability to teach it well and him not caring about the students makes it even worse.

The materials for the lectures and the lab are both very interesting. If you put in the time you will do great. On the other hand Dr. Adams doesn't care about the students. His lectures are not engaging.

Prepare before the lectures, fill out the study objectives after the lectures. Go to TA reviews. This class is a lot of work but if you know the slides and study objectives, you'll be just fine. Professor Adams was a fun teacher and for almost every test gave us 2 points back because we all missed some questions.

I took Cell 520R from Dr. Adams in the Fall and it was one of my favorite classes! He took time to get to know each of his students and is very knowledgeable. He is one of the kindest professors and I would highly recommend him!

I loved this class! Dr. Adams is the nicest man and he does a great job explaining the lectures. My tip is don't slack on studying for lecture exam. Read the textbook it's helpful and label the photos in the lab manual before each lab! Practice writing out lab terms, spelling is a huge part of the lab. I wish I could take it again its the best!

I had Dr. Brown for lecture but I just want to shout Dr. Adams out! I was struggled to work with the cadavers at first and as the Lab Pro, he did everything he could to help me succeed! I was going to drop out but with his help I managed to stay in the class and got an A!! If you're struggling, dont give up!!
One of the worst professors i have ever had. Doesn't care about his students, or situations. I would highly suggest not taking any classes from him. Worst teacher i have ever had at BYU.

Lectures were not engaging. If you take this class from Adams, you're better off studying solely from the textbook rather than wasting time going to lecture. Really cool class though, and you'll learn a lot!

This class is a ton of work. I grinded all semester trying to get an A and ended with 0.1% away from an A, a single point from and A. I emailed him and he had no sympathy. I understand keeping a consistent standard but there were several points that I missed because the TAs taught us wrong and I thought he should've given us more grace on grading.

I absolutely loved Prof Adams. He was very passionate about anatomy and you could tell that he is an expert . He explained things in a way that was easy to understand and his class is set up for everyone to get the grade that they want. This course is memorization heavy but he helps us take advantage of all the resources available.

I really loved taking dissection from Dr. Adams!  He took the time to learn everyone's names and cared about our lives.  He is really good about creating a good environment for us to gain critical experience and learn in the lab.  It was definitely one of my favorite classes.

This class was definitely challenging. Lab TA's were amazing. For lecture, I feel like Dr. Adams was just reading off the slides. This class is purely memorization and I feel like there was a lot to memorize for the exams. Overall, I learned a lot from this class but I would probably not take it from Dr.Adams.

The course material is interesting and Dr. Adams demonstrates a strong knowledge of the subject matter. However, the pace of the lectures tends to be slow and Dr. Adams isn't super engagning. Additionally, the course requires a significant amount of memorization, so it is essential to stay organized and keep up with the material from day one.

His lectures are a little slow but contain useful information. If you miss class, it's pretty easy to catch up by reading the textbook. The tests are pretty fair and not too hard as long as you use the learning objectives as your study guide.

Class set up lecture vs lab. Dr. Adams is OK. Did not go lecture because exams were based on slides. Just memorize the slides and you will be set for the exams. Lots of slides though so be prepared to study. TAs taught labs, attend the open lab hour if you want to do well on the lab quizzes and the two lab exams. Rec take someone else if you can

Dr Adams prepared me A TON for future STEM classes. I barely study for physiology because of how much I learned in his class. His lectures are straight forwards and test questions come right from the slides. The class is only hard because of the lecture/lab combo but if you stay on top of it and use flashcards its super doable. Great professor!

It's clear that Dr. Adams loves the study of anatomy. However, I struggled with his teaching style a little. His lectures were an hour of listening to him read off of the slides that he made, and basically the entire grade is exams. If you can memorize his slides exactly, you should be okay on the tests.

His learning objectives and the online text (for lecture) and the lab manual (for lab) tell you exactly what you will be expected to know. High volume to memorize, though.

Lab is about 75 structures to memorize (written response) a week.

Lecture is about 75 flashcards' worth of material to memorize (recognize on multiple choice) a week.

This class is structured so anyone can succeed IF you put in the work! I spent probably 20 hours per week outside of class for labs and lectures combined. For the lecture exams, they're easy to score well on if you know your stuff. He provides learning objectives, and the tests are taken straight from those pretty much.

I mostly skipped the lectures and just memorized everything on the slides which gave me a pretty good lecture exam score, but for labs, you have to force yourself to go in free labs, as much as you can. The lab exam specimens are not what you usually see in class so make sure you study every angle. This class is hard no matter who you choose.
Lecture was very dry and often something that I could review myself. I think that I learned more from the TAs than Adams

Dr Adams is a nice guy, you can tell he cares. Lots of reviews mention the boring lectures and how they never went. I actually found it valuable to go as he did explain the slides. But, at the end of the day the tests are based completely off what is written in the slides. Anatomy is just hard but lab is sooo cool.

Dr. Adams was a great professor. His tests were fair and the resources he gives you to study from prepare you well. He is known to have boring lectures which rang true in my opinion, but he cares about his students and your grade. I was nervous to take anatomy from Adams (in comparison to Gonda and Brown) but he turned out to be great!

This class takes a lot of time and studying. All of the test questions come from Dr. Adams' slides, so you need to memorize them. I stopped going to lecture about halfway through the semester and it didn't affect my grade. He basically just reads off the slides. Going to free labs for the lab helps too, but I mainly just focused on the lab videos.
lectures are pretty boring but I loved this class. lots of studying is required

Labs were great, but lectures were AWFUL! I didn't learn anything in lecture, so I stopped going. I taught myself from the textbook and did better the second half of the semester. When I actually went to lecture, I remember him going way too fast and never covering all of the material. Do yourself a favor and take it from someone else.

Anatomy is a really tough class! It should really be split up into two 3 credit classes imo. Professor Adams is a super nice person but his lectures can be a little boring. Honestly never went to class and just memorized the slides and was fine. Lab is definitely the highlight of the class and is awesome!

Anatomy is HARD! No doubt about it but this class is my favorite one I have taken. His tests are specific so allot a good amount of time to study. MEMORIZE the slides and go to interactive reviews to help for lecture. For lab, attend free labs and watch the lab videos. They are super helpful. Become friends with the TAs as they are there for you.

This class should be 6 credits and 2 different classes. For the test MEMORIZE all the slides. He will pick a small detail from a random slide. For the lab quizzes, just go to free lab and you will be super prepared. He is kinda boring so just teach yourself...

Professor Adams bases his lectures off of the slides and textbook. You need to have everything on the slides memorized and should read the textbook at least once. He is very enthusiastic about the topic and is happy to meet with students. For lab, quizlets are a lifesaver. Make sure to go to free labs and watch the lab videos, as well.

For lectures, memorize the slides, and you will do great on those exams. He literally takes all his exams from the slides. So I would definitely get the printed slides. For lab, QUIZLET PREMIUM! Just do the written mode and practice the lab terms on there. Free labs were very helpful, but also the LAB VIDEOS are also amazing. You can do this!!

Dr. Adams has the most detailed tests of all the anatomy professors. He reads off of his slides for lecture. Treat lab and lecture like two separate classes. To get an A you must put in a ton of work outside of class. Go to free labs and reviews. The TAs are amazing--listen to everything they say! Working on the cadavers was epic!

Don't get behind in studying for lecture. Pick at it every single day. I took it during spring and would memorize a full lesson everyday since he teaches 2 in one day/ 4 a week. He wrote the book and it explains it way better than he does so use it ALWAYS to fill in info. TA's are key to success. Hennd was my life saver. For lab, GO to free lab!!!

Dr Adams gets some heat but his class is so easy if you teach yourself from the book. His lectures are boring and only introduce you to what you'll spend an extra 4 hours teaching yourself for each lesson... so skipping his lectures and teaching yourself = guaranteed A; study along with his slides and KNOW every learning objectives WITH the book

Dr Adams is deemed not the best for anatomy but I thought he was fine. Anatomy is just a lot of info and goes fast. If you stay on top of the weekly lab quizzes and don't forget to study for lecture an A is totally possible. I thought the textbook was super helpful. His tests are straightforward and I never felt like he was trying to trick me.

This class is like 2 classes in one. Lab and lecture overlap slightly, but not much. Lab was probably my favorite class to go to this semester, but lecture can be hard to go to sometimes. He just reads off of the slides which you can learn on your own. Be prepared to study! It may be hard but it is worth it. I learned so much from this class!

Anatomy is an intense class. Lab is super fun, and no matter the professor, lab is going to be a similar experience. As for lecture, Dr. Adams can be rather dry, which can make lecture hard to get through. I got more out of not going lecture and studying the material by myself.

Anatomy is amazing!! Requires lots of memorization no matter who you take it from, but Adams will never try to trick you on exams. He's a kind guy. You'll want to reference the textbook a lot just to make things more clear, but it's an easy read. I loved this class more than anything. It's well worth the work and time. But it should be two classes.

Honestly, CELL 220 should be two classes. The lab portion, taught entirely by TAs, is very doable and you can be successful if you put a lot of hours into going to free lab each week. The lecture portion is also doable, but also requires many hours of memorizing. Overall an awesome class. Learned so much, loved it, but it required a ton of time.

Dr. Adams is a really caring guy and wants you to succeed. He's willing to meet outside of class and go over things you don't understand. His lectures are pretty dry, but the labs are really cool. This class is a super cool, so I definitely recommend taking it!

Anatomy has a bit of an infamous reputation at BYU, but Adams is as fair as it gets! The expectations for what you need to know are SO CLEAR. Yes, you have to work hard to know those things, but you know exactly what you need to know. He's not boring but not overly exciting and he's the kindest human being! My lab TA's were BOMB!

This class is straight memorization. Technically you could pass without going to class, but Dr. Adams adds things that aren't on the slides. He's a genuine person and is an expert in the field. His tests are very detail oriented. Memorize everything. He's very fair in his expectations though and teaches everything on the tests.

Adams is fine. Not amazing but not bad. Heres the key: study the learning objectives with the textbook. memorize. go to TA reviews. memorize. youll do great. All lab work is the same no matter what prof. Dont let other reviews scare you. This was still my fav class even w/ not loving Dr Adams.

My view may be skewed because CELL 220 has been my favorite class in my academic experience, but Dr. Adams gets straight to the point with his lectures and thats exactly what I needed to learn most effectively. I have an excellent grasp on anatomy, though I needed to work for it. There are easier teachers, but dont let that deter you, hes great!

Monotone and uninspiring. Avoid his lecture at all costs. The entire program has gone down hill since Wisco left. You want to learn and do well? Take it from Brown. You want to be inspired and feel like a million dollars? Novak is the best professor this school has. Don't take it from Adams-- you have options. Know your worth people! Nice tho...

Avoid taking lecture from Adams at all costs. He's a nice person, but I would rather have a mean professor that actually teaches me things. He reads off the slides in a monotone voice and doesn't make any effort to help students retain information at all. After the first exam I just skipped lecture to teach myself the material.

Dr Adams is a great person and very knowledgeable professor. He will make you work harder than other professors teaching Anatomy at BYU. If you are looking for easier exams try to get into Dr Brown or Professor Novak's classes. If you don't mind reading a lot of the textbook for 2-3 very specific questions on the exam then take it from him.

Anatomy is such a fun class. Adam's texts are exactly from his lecture slides and most people do well on the lecture exams. This class is definitely work, but if you put in the time for memorizing, free labs, and studying you will be good. This class is mostly dependent on your TA, but you can always go to free lab and interact with other TAs.

I had Dr. Adams for both Anatomy (220) and Advanced Topics in Clinical Human Anatomy (520R), and I liked him in both. He's super focused during lectures, and clearly knows anatomy super well. He also obviously cared about our success and was super helpful whenever I went to him outside of class.

He makes test questions and lectures based off of learning objectives from the textbook, but the textbook honestly is really helpful and not very long or hard to read at all. Go to TA reviews. He is very kind and nice and intentional about the structure of the class so there are no surprises. Lots of material, so study a lot.

Hardest class I've taken. Anatomy is a hard class and I worked my tail off for an A. Got a 97 on the final and finished the class with a 92.9% but he doesn't round up. I really enjoyed the class though and gained a love for the human body. Just make sure you go to TA reviews and study lecture slides. The tests are based off the slides.

Some will say hes bland and boring but I realize now that this means there are no surprises. Midterms and the final are all super-super similar to the practice questions that youre given in ever lecture. Learn the slides, read the book, and you wont have any surprises

Dr. Adams is nice. He just reads off the slides. Tests come from lecture and specific details in textbook. They are straightforward if you memorize everything. The lab is what hurts people. I never went to a single free lab and still got a B+. The people who do well in this class just spend lot's of time at free lab, that's all. Don't be worried:)

Professor Adams is fine as a professor. Everything was Live Remote Delivery, and he recorded the lectures so I just watched the lectures on double speed later because his lectures are kinda boring. Tests are pretty straight forward if you know the learning objectives and slides (I got A-s). He is a very kind soul and helps with accommodations,

Dr. Adams seems like a nice guy and I don't have anything against him. His lectures tend to be just reading off the slides. His tests come directly from the textbook, which is different from every other anatomy prof at BYU, so I think they might be a little harder. He will get the job done fine, but I recommend taking someone else if you can

Anatomy is a hard class, it needs to be your 1st or 2nd priority class for the semester. It takes a lot of work with the lab and lecture. Dr. Adams is a great choice for anatomy. Do not fall behind in this class! Ask for help, go to free lab, go to lecture TA office hours and their lectures. Do everything you need so you can memorize the info.

Prof Adams is a nice guy, but does just read the slides. He provides some insights, but going to the TA reviews are essential. Lab is the beast part of the class. The tests really aren't bad if you prepare. This class requires a lot of work, but if you're interested in the content it won't be too bad.

Dr. Adams is a nice guy but lectures were boring. He just read the slides off his powerpoint which he posts so going to his lectures seemed useless. His tests were fair and came straight from his powerpoints. If you can memorize a large amount of information you'll be fine. Not an entertaining or life changing professor but a nice and fair one.

The lecture exams are very straightforward and not too hard. 98% of what is on the tests are in his powerpoints so just study those. The lab is the hard part of this class. Going to a few open labs during the week should be enough to be able to identify most of the structures for the weekly quiz. This class will take a lot of work outside of class.

Great professor for Human Anatomy. I took this class as a non-major required course and loved it. Heavily relies on the TAs to help teach review sessions and answer questions. One of those professors you only really see during lecture, but very nice and has some jokes too. Take advantage of the TA's review sessions and open labs.

Dr. Adams is super nice but not great at explaining things. It is worth it to go to lecture however, to see what parts are confusing and need clarification and then ask clarification in the lecture TA QandA. He does a good job of doing research on questions he didnt know the answer to.

I went to class for the first few weeks and then quit because all we did was go over the slides he posts, and the class got yelled at for talking (it was quiet and barely noticeable in a large lecture hall). I got very high grades on the tests by following the learning objectives and reviewing the textbook, but it took a ton of time and work.

Dr. Adams really knows his stuff and is constantly trying to be a better professor. Lecture is basically going over the slides, but I still went. The study objectives are very true to what is on his tests. He encourages students to go to the Q&A's with the TAs - do it!! They are under-used and key to being successful in this class!

This class was an absolute joke, he just read straight off the slides (which were posted online anyways) so lecture was a snooze-fest. Lab was certainly interesting, but when exams came around, we all expected a curve because, historically, there had always been a curve, but no curve appeared. Incredibly frustrating, hurt a lot of people's grades.

Anatomy lecture and lab are different. You mainly choose a professor for the lecture section. The slides have everything that is on the test which is nice because you know exactly what to study. He does add 2 textbook questions which aren't too bad. Go to the lectures and take notes on what you are confused on, then go to TA lectures and ask there.

Had a tough time staying awake in class. Prof essentially read the slides. Learned more from TA's. Difficult to approach. Schedule worked well. Doesn't encourage participation from class often nor talking among ourselves for clarification.
Grind out the reviews and you're chilling. I wouldn't say his lectures are the best, but the reviews are just like the test.

The class is insane, so fast-paced, and an information dump constantly. Be aware that you will have multiple hours of homework a day. If you have to take this class for your major, though, Prof. Sorensen is a great teacher to have because he explains things well.

Chem 105 is insane, but professor Sorenson made it fun! There is way too much content to learn in a semester, so there's lots of homework and the class moves quickly. Sorenson cared about us, and you could tell he enjoyed chemistry which made it so much easier to learn. He taught in a way that made sense and had plenty of fun demonstrations!
Great guy, he blows something up every Friday. Be prepared for a lot of tests and homework. However, Dr. Sorenson will make the class fun and entertaining.

So glad I took Chem 105 from Sorensen! He works hard to cover as much material as possible during class times, and even though this often results in him having to fly through slides, it's clear he truly cares about us understanding each topic and knows exactly what he's talking about. There's also some sick explosions so be sure to come in person!!

Professor Sorensen was a really solid professor! The class itself is tough, that's a given. But he is very good at his lectures, he explains the content quite well! And he does want you to succeed, and is very willing to help if you ask.
Chem 105 is a tough class, but doable. Professor Sorenson is a great teacher, and explains concepts in a way that makes sense.

Professor Sorensen is a pretty good professor. He really wants his students to succeed. He tries to be as accessible as possible. Chem 105 is a tough class. If you stay on top of the homework and take good notes (handwritten is probably best) you'll be okay. Professor Sorensen is generous and drops the lowest assignments/tests.

Awesome dude. He likes blowing stuff up and joking during his lectures, yet he is very good at covering the needed material. He explains concepts very simply without going on tangents or adding confusion. Best of all, he is super approachable and will become your best friend in his office hours. He's the man

Chem 105 is going to be a hard class, but I think it was manageable with Sorenson. You won't get any extra credit, and the grade is almost entirely tests but he is really open in office hours and there are lots of TAs to help you. His lectures were engaging if you like blowing things up. Do the readings, do the HW, and go to office hours.

Dr. Sorenson was really great. He genuinely cares for students and is willing to go over past exams. He made me appreciate chemistry more. He also does really cool demos in his lectures. His expectations are clear but you do have to put in work for Chem 105. Highly recommend taking it from Sorenson.
This class is tough, but professor Sorensen is made it possible, and actually one of my favorite classes. If you put in the work and do all the assignments when you should, you will be fine.

I think Jason is the most GOATED chem professor! His lectures are so engaging and he really knows his stuff. If you go to his office hours, he is super willing to help and gives great advice. Yes this class is difficult, but I think he teaches it perfectly and if you just do what he says you will do amazing in this class.

Dr. Sorenson is an overall really good dude. I just feel that he went way too fast on the lectures. He is available in office hours, but there are a ton of people there, so it is hard to talk to him one-on-one. 

Chem 105 is easily the hardest class I have ever taken. The homework and workload outside of class is easily 4 hours a day.
Engaging lectures and homework that prepares you for the tests.  If you put in the work Dr. Sorensen will help this beast of a course become very doable.

Dr. Sorensen was a really good teacher, and most difficult concepts he explained well. If you struggle with math, make good use of your TA or it's going to be a difficult time. There is a LOT of homework and the exams are pretty intense. Dr. Sorensen is really funny and his lectures are really engaging. His class was hard, but still very fun.

Chem105 is a hard class. Know that and you will be fine. Jason is very willing to help and keeps you involved the whole lecture. He is extremely approachable if he can see that you are trying. He doesnt have the most involved lectures out of the professors available but definitely does the best job at preparing you for the exams. Would reccommend.

Honestly, CHEM 105 is simply a hard course no matter the professor. Professor Sorensen was fairly good though. He is accessible outside of class if you need him, but I wouldn't say he explains things in the best way possible. If the professor you want is not available, Professor Sorensen is a good alternative for sure.

Chem 105 is hard, but Dr. Sorenson was always willing to help if I was struggling with something. He moves fast, so DO NOT miss a lecture or you'll fall behind. There was a lot of time consuming homework, but in the long run it was helpful when prepping for exams. Do the homework, go to class, go to office hours, ask questions, and you'll be fine.

Chem 105 is a beast, but Professor Sorensen made it possible! His lectures are great, and he does an amazing job of breaking tough concepts down. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are iClickers every lecture, and they are part of your grade. Get ready to work and go to the TA reviews before the midterms and the final.

Lectures are engaging, but fast-paced. There are iClickers every day so attendance is mandatory. There's a lot of outside work. Professor Sorenson is very willing to help if you go to his office hours. You'll be good if you keep up with the reading and assignments and attend class every day.

if you have the opportunity to take chem 105 with dr sorensen, do it! he is by far my favorite professor at byu. he offers so many office hours and will go over anything and everything in an incredibly helpful manner. he wants to see you pass the class and succeed and he'll help you get there!

Chem 105 is an incredibly hard class but Professor Sorenson is a good teacher. He moves incredibly fast in his lectures and at times it can be hard to follow along, but his slides were very helpful. Anything on the slides is fair game for the test so make sure you study the slides and the test questions are very similar to problem sets.

Dr. Sorenson is overall a good professor. His lectures were hard to understand at times because he talks so fast in class. CHEM 105 is overall a hard class, but he is definitely not the worst teacher you can take it from. He is very helpful in his office hours and genuinely wants to help you succeed.

Dr. Sorensen was an extraordinary Chemistry professor and a good lecturer. BYU makes Chem 105 hard for no reason, so the tests are primarily uniform among teachers and tricky, but Dr. Sorensen was always very approachable and helpful. The TA you get for recitation will significantly affect your understanding in this class.

Professor Sorensen was one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He was always excited to meet outside of class and worked with me with various health problems I had. He is very genuine and always made us feel capable of succeeding. He would even go through the entire midterm with you question by question and explain concepts you struggled with

I'm so glad that I took CHEM 105 with Professor Sorensen. He was so helpful during office hours, and very personable and understanding of students with extenuating circumstances or health issues. He's a good lecturer, and an amazing teacher 1 on 1. He wants you to succeed in his class, and he will help you get there.

Professor Sorensen is a great professor. Chem 105 is an extremely difficult class no matter who you take it from, but in my opinion he's the best. His lectures were clear, and he did a great job and explaining complex material. There is a lot of work, but it's doable. He makes it clear what you need to know for exams. Study!! And you'll be fine.

Hard class but he's the best imo. There's like 3 problem sets due each week, and a lab, but they are all participation so as long as you complete it you will get a 100. If you don't want to rent the textbook you don't have to- he never refers to it in lectures. Great professor, especially considering this was his first semester teaching!

Lectures were fun and interesting. I think the class in general, regardless of the professor is pretty difficult and there is a lot of homework due for each lecture. Tests are pretty difficult as well but its not impossible to get a good grade. Professor Sorensen is super caring and personable however his available office hours were inconvenient.

I took him during his first semester teaching. Nice guy, if you go into his office hours, he is more than willing to help you and answer questions. However, I feel like his lectures were sometimes focused too much on things that weren't focused on the tests, and the types of practice problems he used didn't always transfer to the test problems.

Professor Sorensen is a really nice guy and for his first semester teaching Chem 105 he did an okay job. He is willing to help his students however the lectures were not great and the material was always presented in a confusing manner. Honestly, any Chem 105 class is going to be rough so he might be the best you're gonna get.

I took him during his first year teaching chem 105. He is very willing to meet with students outside of class and encourages you to ask him for help! A really funny and caring guy. However, his lectures and practice problems poorly prepare you for the types of questions that are asked on the tests.

This past semester was his first at BYU and I really enjoyed taking Chem 105 from him. I loved him as a professor and I think he teaches clearly and helped me really love chemistry. I've heard this class is notoriously hard and it definitely is difficult, but it's not impossible to get an A. I'm an ME major. #firefriday

Teaches nutrition with a biochemical focus as it should be done because this is a metabolism class. Tests are frequent, but fair. You will succeed on them if you study the course material. He's a funny dude. Would recommend for anyone that actually wants to learn about nutrition.

Prof. Kenealey is a really kind person with a lot of heart. But, his teaching style is really difficult to comprehend. He struggles to teach complex topics and I constantly felt like everything was going above my head. Even with spending hours doing readings outside of class, I was still lost.
He has the best and most engaging lectures in my opinion!! And he is able to hold two opposing ideas with dignity which is needed these days.

I really liked the material of this class, but didn't love how it was taught (professor basically just reads the slides). Although, he is a really nice guy and cares about his students questions and concerns. Tests are hard so study and watch TA reviews. The paper you have to write is time consuming but not difficult

I like nutrition in general, but I loved this class! Dr. Kenealey is great a teaching the concepts, so definitely attend all lectures. He's a chemistry pro but don't let that scare you, he's always down to help. TAs were helpful. You get to choose the subject for your class paper. Final is required now prob for good reason. *Study the textbook.*

Honestly, this class wasn't the worst. It's way easier than the chemistry classes you must take for a nutrition major. Sure the tests are a little tricky, but the current TAs (at least from Fall 2023) tell you everything on the test. They are a little too nice, so that made it easy. I didn't even have to take the final because you can drop it.

Prof. Kenealey is such an amazing lecturer and is super passionate about nutrition and science. He always starts off with an inspirational quote/scripture verse which helps to invite the spirit in. There are 5 midterms and the final exam (one of them can be dropped). You leave with a deeper understanding of how important nutrition really is!

This class was hard but VERY doable. When I learned that the majority of our grade is from 6 tests and we take a test every other week I was so mad. But honestly it was so nice, they are mostly only over 2 or 3 sections with very little cumulative questions. So it's a lot less studying for each test, and one test can be dropped including the final!

Professor Kenealey is an awesome guy. Teaches really well, really funny, very willing to help out and answer questions. Always got back to me real fast when I emailed him. If you're looking for information on this class, it's amazingly fun but brutal. Papers every week and the grading is hard. I had to work my butt off as a non-bio or chem major.

Make sure you pay attention to due dates because he does not accept anything late. He has things due at weird times. Also, attend TA reviews, they cut down how much information you have to study for each test. He is a decent teacher, but overall, I found that reading the textbook was the most useful thing. Beware, you have to write a paper.

This professor is extremely difficult to work with. He will not respond to any emails, when you reach out for help, unless you email him multiply times, visit his office, and leave a message on his office phone. Even on the off chance that he does respond, it will be to tell that he does not believe in mercy. Extremely non-understanding and rude.

Professor Kenealey was a co-teacher, and for the first week or three, he was a tough grader. After that, he loosened up and was really encouraging. He has a high standard for grading but is willing to talk about things after class.

The classes are good because he pauses lectures for you to explain to your peers and make sure you understand things. Other than that, super frustrating class. The tests focus on obscure details and are full of trick questions. The paper is basically impossible to get a good grade on. Quizzes are closed book BEFORE he covers the material in class.
Dr. Kenealey studied Biochem his ENTIRE life. NOT nutrition. I don't know how he even got the job. Choose someone else if there is an option, but if not, look up quizlets and go to TA hours A TON.

The material of this class is fascinating and pretty easy (especially after CHEM285). The administration of the material is impossible to navigate. TA availability was low (there were two for a class of 35...I saw them in person twice). The online information, TA information, and professor information all contradicted each other.

I had him as a co-teacher for an Honors course. Many expectations for this class were incorrect because there were non-science majors and freshman in this class who were unable to meet what the professors wanted. However, I found Dr. Kenealey to be very caring and willing to help anyone who needed it! He was overall fun and kind in lecture.

Has unnecessarily confusing slides, takes off significant points on papers for silly mistakes, and doesn't give opportunities outside of class to test our knowledge on the material. For tests, all I can do is reread my notes and the lecture slides, rather than taking practice quizzes or tests. His uploads on learning suite are so disorganized.

The subject matter is supposed to be intro-level biology. The textbook (one he uses for other classes) is an upper-level biochemistry text that requires organic chemistry to understand. The non-science majors are totally lost. Kenealey is dismissive, rude, and holds grudges. If he doesn't like you he will just ignore you. AVOID HIM if you can.

Dr. Kenealey is an extremely knowledgeable professor. He is also very down to earth but makes things difficult SO you learn. We read each chapter and took a (hard) quiz before going over it in class. You have to have a good understanding of his lectures and thought process to do well on the test. His TA reviews will help. Very insightful class.

I didn't always agree with his approach to Nutrition, but I am not sure the freshmen/sophomores who take this class understand how much he has to know to answer their questions. He is one very smart dude.

Dr. Kenealey was a really nice guy but man this was a hard class. The tests are ridiculous and in my opinion impossible to get a good grade on. They were not really what we studied in class even. I would wait to take this class in person- maybe it is clearer in person.

Great guy! He is always willing to answer questions and re-explain topics from lecture. You have to read about 2 chapters per week with a quiz. Quizzes are often difficult. The chemistry involved is not too difficult. Some test Q's come aren't on slides, so take good notes in class. Overall, if you fill out the learning objectives, A is doable.

I really enjoyed Dr. Kenealey's class. It's a difficult class but by no means impossible. Make sure you work with the TAs and form a study group with other people in the class. He expects you have to a good understanding of chemistry, but if you need extra help with that, he's really accessible out of class and is always willing to help.

Dr Kenealey is a very good lecturer and professor. He memorized the name of every student in our hall of 60 students. He actively seeks to be a better professor. As for the material for the course, it's a ton of memorization. There was a chapter reading quiz due about every 1.5 weeks, two projects, 3 midterms and a final. Not a lot of buffer.

Professor Kenealey is awesome! He's likable, interesting, and knows his field, but also knows how to admit when he doesn't know the answer. It's a tough class, but I would definitely recommend it from him. Maybe things have changed since other reviewers took the class, but o-chem is DEFINITELY a prerequisite, don't skip that.

I really enjoyed the class, and the lectures are good. He even tries to use a variety of learning styles to engage the class. f you did well inO'Chem and BioChem (or Chem 285), the first two sections will be easy.   He rushes through the vitamins and minerals SUPER fast.  The final is WAY harder than quizzes and other exams.

He is one of my very favorite professors! His enthusiasm is contagious. I felt his desire for us all to succeed and understand. He often tried new methods to help us learn better than other years. He is very humble: always willing to learn from us, admits when he doesn't know answers, and looks things up for students. Hard class, great professor!

This class was TERRIBLY organized. He uploads a new set of slides every class but they all overlap a ton so studying from them is super time consuming. The tests were pretty difficult, especially if you hadn't taken BOTH ochem 1&2 before. Grading on the paper was pretty harsh - markdowns for small inconsequential things.

He has a charismatic personality. His tests and quizzes are tricky. He does not cover all the material you need to know for them in class or on his power point slides, also many times the material isn't in the book either. He grades pretty tough for the paper and project that you need to do in the class. The class was a challenge.

Tough class, but Dr. Kenealey makes it enjoyable.  Tests are difficult but reasonable.  Assignments are straightforward.  Very knowledgeable about the subject material.  The chemistry portion of the class was mostly just memorizing structures, so nothing difficult.

I have never studied harder, and it didn't seem to make any difference. His slides had different information than the book, and there was a LOT of information! Unclear expectations. The TA was helpful. The book was helpful. Groups were helpful. He's a relatively new teacher. If you go to him personally, he may be more willing to help you.

Prof./class  AWFUL. Chem not a prerec, but do NOT take if you don't have any Chem background. Need to know TONS of different structures and metabolic pathways and if you don't understand every tiny detail, you will do awful on tests. He moves so  fast that it's hard to know what to actually take notes on and study. If you take it, good luck.
There is a lot of reading in this course, obviously. But professor Kerr really cares about his students and is very interested in what we have to say.

Dr. Kerr is an awesome professor! I always felt so educated after class. The focus of this class was female poets of the English Civil War, which was fascinating! It's definetly my favorite literary history class offered at BYU. LGBTQIA+ friendly too! Would recommend, would take again.

Dr. Kerr likes to teach his classes in a seminar style, which is great because you can participate a lot if that helps you or only participate a little if that helps you. He is extremely knowledgeable about the content, and gives great feedback because he knows what he's talking about. Homework is more flexible, and assignments are spaced out.

Professor Kerr really cares about what he is teaching and is super helpful and open to meeting with you outside of class! I didn't get the grade I wanted on my first paper, so I kept meeting with him and ended up doing really well. Such an interesting subject I hadn't learned about before!

Dr. Kerr is a very talented teacher that makes what could be a very boring subject entertaining. He has a real passion for the material and makes sure that you understand the concepts. The tests are hard and the reading is a lot to handle, but the class is very well structured and easy to figure out. A few short papers and weekly reading checks.

Dr. Kerr is a great teacher, extremely competent, and insightful. He meets with you regularly outside of class to ensure you understand what is expected for the assignments and help you get the most out of the experience. The poet you discuss is commonly cited as a lesbian, but Dr. Kerr helps you see the nuance and dive deeper than surface issues.

The class was mostly graded on 2 papers, 25 & 40% of grade. 50pg rdgs and up. Not spiritual at all, in fact most of the readings sickened me. He's a fair grader, but the subject material is all about masochism and lesbianism in wales in the 1600s and I could not have been more bored. 2hr MLA training required. Take the Shakespeare sec instead.

Professor Kerr cares about his students and wants them to succeed, but classes were long and boring. He gives good feedback on assignments and leads class discussion. This was one of my least favorite classes because it was boring and confusing. I think it was the class though, not necessarily Professor Kerr. Maybe his other classes are better.

He loves this topic so much and helps you really understand the writings of Paul. He's such a nerd for this stuff (in the best way) and it makes you interested and want to participate. If you care at all about early Christianity and how our ideas as Christians came to be, this class is for you. Professor Kerr is the best!

He really is a nice guy, and I think he is a genius professor. Personally, I found it difficult as a math guy to understand his interpretive brain, but if that's you, great. The thing I disliked most is that he doesn't believe in grades, and will force that onto you. He thinks a B is a solid grade, and you have to work your butt off for an A.

ONE OF MY FAVORITE PROFESSORS AT BYU!! Dr. Kerr is truly amazing and his lectures incredibly engaging. I love his teaching style and his desire for honest participation. I wish he were my professor in every class!

Ive taken 2 classes from Kerr now, and hes absolutely the best. He cares about each students individual improvement and learning, and is willing to work with you to achieve that. His lectures can be fun and witty, especially when students participate. He is simultaneously a genius and extremely considerate towards each student. An absolute icon.

Dr. Kerr is easily one of the best professors I've had. He truly cares about each of his students individually and is amazingly kind and caring. Super understanding and easy to communicate with. If you have the opportunity to take his class, do it.

Professor Kerr is one of the best teachers I've ever had. I've taken two classes from him now and both have been discussion based with the only assignments being regular reading (a chapter or more per class) with responses and three papers the entire semester. The class is just difficult because of deep questions but it is really engaging!

Professor Kerr was the best professor I've had at BYU. He was incredibly caring and understanding and he was always very careful to make sure that students felt safe and understood in his class. His grading criteria was incredibly clear and I enjoyed his class very much.

Prof Kerr is a fantastic teacher. I loved this class. Yeah, it was really hard, but I learned so much and grew a lot as a writer. I had him during the COVID semester, where we went online halfway through, and he was super chill and understanding about any and all issues which came up. He's willing to work with you to make sure that you succeed.

By far one of the best professors at BYU. His Shakespeare class incorporated learning about the construction of whiteness, which was not only timely, but imperative to our educations. His expectations were clear. If you take this class, prepare to be challenged, and be willing to change. He was also very understanding during the time of the virus.

Professor Kerr is incredibly nice and respectful, but his lectures had no structure or clarity. For a Shakespeare class, we only (and I mean only) focused on racial politics for 3 of his works and some other loosely related works. For the papers and final, you had to cater specifically to his taste and respond to abstract, weird prompts.

One of the most admirable human I've known. He simultaneously emanates kindness and intelligence at a level I've never seen. You will come out of his classes (group writing therapy sessions) a much better writer if you are willing to realize just how difficult good writing is. Grades based on arc of personal improvement and really want to help you.

Professor Kerr was a truly phenomenal instructor. His class is difficult, but by no means too much to manage. I left having improved as a student. All my assignments were centered around King Lear--which was nice to have a small subject studied through a variety of applications. He is extremely kind, respectful, and accommodating.

Oh man, Jason Kerr is hands-down my favorite professor at BYU. This is my second time taking him and I'm taking him again next semester. He is brilliant, hilarious, super chill. He was incredibly helpful and accommodating. I feel like I have a much deeper love and understanding of Shakespeare as well as literary theory. And I'm a better writer!
Dr. Kerr is great. His lectures are more like discussions, which is really nice. He helps you enjoy things you thought you'd hate. Had him twice. Loved him both times.

I took Dr. Kerrs Milton class during the winter semester of 2018. The guy knows his stuff, is a heavy hitter in the field, and is very aware of how to make 17th century poetry and prose accessible. Hes extremely great in class and one-on-one. He pushed me to be a more responsible and competent writer. I would take that class again in a heartbeat.

TOUGH CLASS. Honestly, I learned so much with Professor Kerr. He is a solid choice when taking this class. I promise you can do it and you can get through it. He grades tough but also according to YOUR progress. Class is pretty monotone but overall, he is a GENIUS professor. There are also only 3 papers and one short oral presentation.

I really enjoyed Professor Kerr's class. It tended to be somewhat dry material, but he always got a laugh out of us. He also grades very quickly and very fairly. Really enjoyed the class and you could tell he wants you to succeed in the class.
Probably one of the kindest professors at BYU. He is very knowledgeable and he's always willing to help his students. Make sure you take a class from him before you graduate!

Lots of reading, but no reading quizzes. Class isn't mandatory, but you will want to attend to take good notes. 3 pass/fail exercises and 3 short papers, which all were fairly easy. The tests are not hard if you use the study guide and prepare. Overall, he had some great insights on works that tend to be boring but that he made more interesting.

Prof. Kerr is a very intelligent man and really passionate about his field. Lectures are fascinating; he helps make sense of confusing/dry readings. I appreciate having a male professor who is conscious of gender politics and incorporates texts from female authors, even in such an early time period. Would take another class from him in a heartbeat.

Professor Kerr was supportive when half of the fill-in-the-blank text fields in my midterm malfunctioned. He allowed me to email him the other half of the responses "on my honor." He graded assignments fairly and gave feedback when he gave me a less-than-perfect grade. I learned a lot in this course even though the reading material was challenging.

Dr. Kerr helps the dry reading we have more approachable. If you write down what is on the Powerpoint slide in the class, take notice of the passages he reads from, and participate in discussion, you will do great on the tests and papers. Not many assignments over the semester and he is willing to help you on anything! Witty and very intelligent!

I don't know why there are negative review of Prof Kerr. The material was potentially extremely boring but he made it enjoyable and humorous.  He is more than willing to help his students and he is never haughty. In class lectures were clear and helpful, while still focused on class participation.  Tests and assignments were fair. Take him!

Dr. Kerr is one of my favorite professors. It's hard to know the extent of the writing assignments because the concepts are CHALLENGING. So if you're not sure ask. He WANTS TO HELP. Even though he is VERY smart, he doesn't act like he thinks he is above his students. He's HUMBLE and VERY APPROACHABLE. And he really helped me improve my writing!

While this is generally one of the more boring English classes, Pro. Kerr made it worse than it should have been.  Class was very dry and I never knew what from the lecture was important.  His grading of essays and the tests is also very subjective, which was frustrating.  I wouldn't recommend taking from him.
Dr. Kerr was really great, really knowledgeable. Made old English and middle English really enjoyable even for an introductory level course. Really glad I took this class from him.
Professor Kerr leads interesting discussions with knowledge, humor, and passion..

He was very good at leading discussions in class, however he tended to answer questions in a roundabout sort of way that was slightly confusing. Attending class is only important if you don't understand the essay prompts. He WILL bother you about it if you don't attend, although attendance isn't mandatory technically.

Prof. Kerr graded according to short papers that replaced tests, readings were effective. We had many great discussions and he led them without any apparent bias. He was willing to listen and help his students understand and learn from the readings. He was easily my favorite professor of that semester.

I took his class bc of the reviews, but for my class he made the Shakespeare emphasis political theology. I kid you not, I could not understand half of what he said. Added to complex readings, it was a hard class. But he's a nice guy who is willing to work with you to help you succeed.

Prof. Kerr is a nice guy, although kind of awkward. When I took the class, the whole second half of the semester was focused on creating our own editions of a Shakespeare play, which I felt was a bit pointless.
