He's easy enough, but if you want to learn something significant, I would take it from someone else.

Prof. Kerr is a very good teacher. He leads very good discussions and seems incredibly intelligent. His feedback on papers is very useful. I'm not sure I really liked the class curriculum, with its emphasis on Shakespeare editions and creating your own edition, but it was still enjoyable (and, to be honest, quite easy). I recommend him.

Professor Kotter is a great professor for this class. He is very knowledgeable and has a lot of real world experience. I personally don't mind the grading criteria as it is based in making sure you understand the material. Tests are allowed revisions to get the "Check +" which allows you to learn what you didn't understand.

Good lecturer and knowledgeable about the FED but one of the absolute worst at class structure. He has a bizarre and terrible grading structure. You get either a check minus, check, or check plus. Feels very silly and there's a lot of hoops you have to jump through to get a good grade. He also changed the grading criteria halfway through the class.
Class consists of weekly homework, three tests, and a group project. Grading criteria for all of them are a bit unclear.

Awesome teacher. Very knowledgeable about economics. Great guy. Definitely would take another class from him. 

My only issue was the TAs. They grade all of the exams. Pray that you get a TA that grades easy. Comparing my exams to others in the class, it was clear that one TA graded more harshly than others. Unfortunately, I got that TA...
Very passionate about his subject.
Grind out the reviews and you're chilling. I wouldn't say his lectures are the best, but the reviews are just like the test.

The class is insane, so fast-paced, and an information dump constantly. Be aware that you will have multiple hours of homework a day. If you have to take this class for your major, though, Prof. Sorensen is a great teacher to have because he explains things well.

Chem 105 is insane, but professor Sorenson made it fun! There is way too much content to learn in a semester, so there's lots of homework and the class moves quickly. Sorenson cared about us, and you could tell he enjoyed chemistry which made it so much easier to learn. He taught in a way that made sense and had plenty of fun demonstrations!
Great guy, he blows something up every Friday. Be prepared for a lot of tests and homework. However, Dr. Sorenson will make the class fun and entertaining.

So glad I took Chem 105 from Sorensen! He works hard to cover as much material as possible during class times, and even though this often results in him having to fly through slides, it's clear he truly cares about us understanding each topic and knows exactly what he's talking about. There's also some sick explosions so be sure to come in person!!

Professor Sorensen was a really solid professor! The class itself is tough, that's a given. But he is very good at his lectures, he explains the content quite well! And he does want you to succeed, and is very willing to help if you ask.
Chem 105 is a tough class, but doable. Professor Sorenson is a great teacher, and explains concepts in a way that makes sense.

Professor Sorensen is a pretty good professor. He really wants his students to succeed. He tries to be as accessible as possible. Chem 105 is a tough class. If you stay on top of the homework and take good notes (handwritten is probably best) you'll be okay. Professor Sorensen is generous and drops the lowest assignments/tests.

Awesome dude. He likes blowing stuff up and joking during his lectures, yet he is very good at covering the needed material. He explains concepts very simply without going on tangents or adding confusion. Best of all, he is super approachable and will become your best friend in his office hours. He's the man

Chem 105 is going to be a hard class, but I think it was manageable with Sorenson. You won't get any extra credit, and the grade is almost entirely tests but he is really open in office hours and there are lots of TAs to help you. His lectures were engaging if you like blowing things up. Do the readings, do the HW, and go to office hours.

Dr. Sorenson was really great. He genuinely cares for students and is willing to go over past exams. He made me appreciate chemistry more. He also does really cool demos in his lectures. His expectations are clear but you do have to put in work for Chem 105. Highly recommend taking it from Sorenson.
This class is tough, but professor Sorensen is made it possible, and actually one of my favorite classes. If you put in the work and do all the assignments when you should, you will be fine.

I think Jason is the most GOATED chem professor! His lectures are so engaging and he really knows his stuff. If you go to his office hours, he is super willing to help and gives great advice. Yes this class is difficult, but I think he teaches it perfectly and if you just do what he says you will do amazing in this class.

Dr. Sorenson is an overall really good dude. I just feel that he went way too fast on the lectures. He is available in office hours, but there are a ton of people there, so it is hard to talk to him one-on-one. 

Chem 105 is easily the hardest class I have ever taken. The homework and workload outside of class is easily 4 hours a day.
Engaging lectures and homework that prepares you for the tests.  If you put in the work Dr. Sorensen will help this beast of a course become very doable.

Dr. Sorensen was a really good teacher, and most difficult concepts he explained well. If you struggle with math, make good use of your TA or it's going to be a difficult time. There is a LOT of homework and the exams are pretty intense. Dr. Sorensen is really funny and his lectures are really engaging. His class was hard, but still very fun.

Chem105 is a hard class. Know that and you will be fine. Jason is very willing to help and keeps you involved the whole lecture. He is extremely approachable if he can see that you are trying. He doesnt have the most involved lectures out of the professors available but definitely does the best job at preparing you for the exams. Would reccommend.

Honestly, CHEM 105 is simply a hard course no matter the professor. Professor Sorensen was fairly good though. He is accessible outside of class if you need him, but I wouldn't say he explains things in the best way possible. If the professor you want is not available, Professor Sorensen is a good alternative for sure.

Chem 105 is hard, but Dr. Sorenson was always willing to help if I was struggling with something. He moves fast, so DO NOT miss a lecture or you'll fall behind. There was a lot of time consuming homework, but in the long run it was helpful when prepping for exams. Do the homework, go to class, go to office hours, ask questions, and you'll be fine.

Chem 105 is a beast, but Professor Sorensen made it possible! His lectures are great, and he does an amazing job of breaking tough concepts down. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are iClickers every lecture, and they are part of your grade. Get ready to work and go to the TA reviews before the midterms and the final.

Lectures are engaging, but fast-paced. There are iClickers every day so attendance is mandatory. There's a lot of outside work. Professor Sorenson is very willing to help if you go to his office hours. You'll be good if you keep up with the reading and assignments and attend class every day.

if you have the opportunity to take chem 105 with dr sorensen, do it! he is by far my favorite professor at byu. he offers so many office hours and will go over anything and everything in an incredibly helpful manner. he wants to see you pass the class and succeed and he'll help you get there!

Chem 105 is an incredibly hard class but Professor Sorenson is a good teacher. He moves incredibly fast in his lectures and at times it can be hard to follow along, but his slides were very helpful. Anything on the slides is fair game for the test so make sure you study the slides and the test questions are very similar to problem sets.

Dr. Sorenson is overall a good professor. His lectures were hard to understand at times because he talks so fast in class. CHEM 105 is overall a hard class, but he is definitely not the worst teacher you can take it from. He is very helpful in his office hours and genuinely wants to help you succeed.

Dr. Sorensen was an extraordinary Chemistry professor and a good lecturer. BYU makes Chem 105 hard for no reason, so the tests are primarily uniform among teachers and tricky, but Dr. Sorensen was always very approachable and helpful. The TA you get for recitation will significantly affect your understanding in this class.

Professor Sorensen was one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He was always excited to meet outside of class and worked with me with various health problems I had. He is very genuine and always made us feel capable of succeeding. He would even go through the entire midterm with you question by question and explain concepts you struggled with

I'm so glad that I took CHEM 105 with Professor Sorensen. He was so helpful during office hours, and very personable and understanding of students with extenuating circumstances or health issues. He's a good lecturer, and an amazing teacher 1 on 1. He wants you to succeed in his class, and he will help you get there.

Professor Sorensen is a great professor. Chem 105 is an extremely difficult class no matter who you take it from, but in my opinion he's the best. His lectures were clear, and he did a great job and explaining complex material. There is a lot of work, but it's doable. He makes it clear what you need to know for exams. Study!! And you'll be fine.

Hard class but he's the best imo. There's like 3 problem sets due each week, and a lab, but they are all participation so as long as you complete it you will get a 100. If you don't want to rent the textbook you don't have to- he never refers to it in lectures. Great professor, especially considering this was his first semester teaching!

Lectures were fun and interesting. I think the class in general, regardless of the professor is pretty difficult and there is a lot of homework due for each lecture. Tests are pretty difficult as well but its not impossible to get a good grade. Professor Sorensen is super caring and personable however his available office hours were inconvenient.

I took him during his first semester teaching. Nice guy, if you go into his office hours, he is more than willing to help you and answer questions. However, I feel like his lectures were sometimes focused too much on things that weren't focused on the tests, and the types of practice problems he used didn't always transfer to the test problems.

Professor Sorensen is a really nice guy and for his first semester teaching Chem 105 he did an okay job. He is willing to help his students however the lectures were not great and the material was always presented in a confusing manner. Honestly, any Chem 105 class is going to be rough so he might be the best you're gonna get.

I took him during his first year teaching chem 105. He is very willing to meet with students outside of class and encourages you to ask him for help! A really funny and caring guy. However, his lectures and practice problems poorly prepare you for the types of questions that are asked on the tests.

This past semester was his first at BYU and I really enjoyed taking Chem 105 from him. I loved him as a professor and I think he teaches clearly and helped me really love chemistry. I've heard this class is notoriously hard and it definitely is difficult, but it's not impossible to get an A. I'm an ME major. #firefriday

Prof Romo is a very humble, honest, and caring man with a lot of professional experience. If you're looking to learn more about the localization industry, he's your guy. The class he teaches offers a lot of information about the industry and its great that he uses some personal connections to have as guest speakers in the class. 10/10 recommend

Professor Romo is a good professor. He helped me to better comprehend a lot of the Spanish concepts I did not understand. He cares alot about his students. He likes to have conversations with you and get to know you better.

Good, caring professor who honestly does a really good job of explaining Spanish grammar in his lectures. My only real criticism is that his LearningSuite isn't very organized. Stay on top of the tareas and you'll do fine. Would recommend.

Incredible professor. The best class you'll ever have. If you can take him, DO IT. I cannot recommend Professor Romo enough! I seriously never give ratings and I want the world to know how awesome he is. Thanks for everything Hermano Romo, lo aprecio mucho.

Hermano Romo is such a great professor! Definitely one of my favorite teachers I've had. There are small homework assignments each class periods, but they're super easy. He is really funny and makes the class engaging. If you take this class I would highly recommend taking it from Hno Romo!! If you do the homework you'll get a good grade.

Prof. Romo makes this class a breeze and fun to attend. Cares about your life and about bettering your Spanish. Lots of busy work but good learning experience. Let us out early more often than not but still taught enough to get A's on the exams

Professor Romo is one of the best people that has walked the face of this earth. Hes funny, charismatic and he knows his stuff. As for the class, all 321 courses follow the mandated curriculum so he did incredibly well for what he had. If you served a mission and studied hard, this class will be easy, and professor Romo makes it really enjoyable.

Hermano Romo is a good guy that wants you to pass his class. He's understanding with different situations that arise and will help you better your Spanish and get a good grade. There's daily homework but it's not hard and at the start he doesn't teach for the midterms but he's too good a guy I couldn't mark him down for that. I enjoyed the class.

Professor Romo is a good teacher, knows what he's teaching but doing this class online was awful. The tests are graded on rather obscure passages read throughout the unit which makes studying for tests nearly impossible. The daily tareas weren't hard, just hard to remember to do. Take this class from someone else if you don't want to teach yourself

I absolutely LOVED 321 with Professor Romo! He was always so kind and wanted the best for us. He is the best Spanish teacher I have had at BYU. This may be dramatic but I WOULD TAKE A BULLET FOR THIS MAN! He is the best!

Most AMAZING teacher. I loved his class. Hes so caring and funny and focuses on conversation and he always brings really interesting topics to class. His class is all about participation so get ready to talk. He said attendance goes toward your grade but he never actually put that in our grade... but you should still go. Also he has a PHD

He was told to teach a new curriculum assigned by the department, so that made the class a little disorganized, and we were graded on memorization a few times (not his fault). He was helpful, but I didn't really feel pushed as a student. It seemed more like just a fun class to hang out in.
Prof Romo is really good. He was always able to help with any type of error. I would definitely recommend him for Span321. He is very knowledgeable and willing to help.

Professor Romo is a really great professor. He's Peruvian. The class is helpful and he does a good job. He's really personable. If you try your best, then you'll get a good grade. It definitely wasn't my hardest class. I would totally recommend him. There are a few writing assignments. He's a realistic grader. The tests come from the department.
Teaching style is very unorganized. Very hard to understand material in class

I would not recommend taking this professor. His lectures are extremely boring, and his teaching style makes the material difficult to stay engaged with. The class also feels very unorganized, which makes learning harder. If you have the option, I strongly recommend taking this class with a different professor.

Dr. Buckley is awesome! He really loves and cares about his students and is always trying to help them succeed. He frequently sent me sources he thought I would find useful. I especially appreciated the periodic check-ins he scheduled throughout the semester to help us stay on track, and I loved how regularly we prayed and discussed gospel insights
He was the nicest teacher ever. His tests are a little wacko but he's a nice grader.

Professor Buckley was incredible! I could tell and feel that he cared about me and my interests and success. He is funny? A great listener, and a disciple of Jesus Christ. I'm grateful for him and for my time learning from him this semester.
He is a great UNIV teacher and really cares about each student! He invited us over to his house and we had dinner and played games!

I had a very positive experience in Dr. Buckley's class. He is very kind and funny. He's willing to meet and work with students outside of class to help with assignments. His class was involved, but not difficult. It was easy to get a good grade if you put in the effort to do the assignments and study for the tests.
He is awesome! Would totally take his class again! :)

Professor Buckley is a wonderful professor! I can't imagine taking my capstone course from anyone better! He'll work with you and give you fantastic feedback on every aspect of your writing that helps you grow. It's not an easy class, but he makes the process of writing your bachelor's thesis both enjoyable and doable.

I love Professor Buckley! He made me want to switch and be a history major. There were hardly any assignments in this class besides 4 tests and a couple papers which were easy. He is super funny, however studying for the midterms can be tricky. Do the readings though, or have chat summarize them and you'll be fine!

Dr. Buckley is passionate about Indigenous history and catering to his students experience in his class. Be prepared to engage with your peers and with the professor in meaningful discussions--often based on the readings for that day. I found that this class was relatively reading "heavy" but the readings were enjoyable. Totally recommend!
Amazing professor! This class was awesome and I really enjoyed learning all the content. I highly recommend.

Professor Buckley is obviously passionate about his field of study, which makes lectures enjoyable and interesting. The research paper is worth a lot of the grade and as long as you keep up with it you'll do fine. Fair chunk of reading, but what do you expect from a history course.

Professor Buckley is immensely kind and caring. I am so glad to have taken his class and would recommend it to anyone. There are relatively few grades throughout the course, so be sure not to miss an assignment, and the grading can be somewhat harsh, but overall, it is an amazing class and teacher

I loved taking my capstone from Dr. Buckley! It was super awesome to work on it throughout the semester in small chunks and have the draft done before the end of the semester. He gave great feedback on the draft and was super available to meet with for help throughout the semester!

Dr. Buckley is a great professor! He is extremely knowledgeable and kind. I wouldn't have taken my senior capstone from anyone else. He holds students to high standards but provided great, thorough feedback and a lot of time to improve our papers. He helped my paper be the best it could be. Take your senior capstone from him!
Professor Buckley is an engaging instructor who makes history come alive. While the tests can be tricky, using Unstuckstudy alongside the textbook and lecture notes helps stay on top of the material.

Dr. Buckley was an amazing professor! I really enjoyed how he included the Native American perspective in U.S. history. 

There were a lot of papers, but if you start on them early they are manageable. The Study guides for exams were extremely helpful as the questions helped me review all of the important details.

Dr. Buckley is a very kind, understanding person, but I learned just about nothing from this class. His lectures focus a lot on discussion & general historical trends, but his tests ask extremely specific factual questions. If you study textbook/lecture notes you'll still be very surprised with the test material. Very unorganized & unclear overall

I learned so much in this class that I had never been taught in other history classes. Doctor Buckley does a great job at showing different perspectives not often taught. He is such a caring man and I really felt his love he has for me and all other students. Wonderful class. Textbook is provided, along with most required readings.

Dr. Buckley is a genuinely spiritual, kind, and caring person! Although getting a good grade in this class was very difficult, he sets up the class that way so that his students can learn a lot. If you want an easy class for your GE credits, don't take this class, but if you want to learn and grow, I 100% recommend this class!

Might be my favorite teacher I've had through 3 years of college. I've never rated a professor before, I'm only here cause I love the guy. Professor Buckley is just the nicest guy. I'd very much recommend him.

Lecture slides are 100% not useful because they are vague. Tests ask extremely specific questions. There is no helpful material to study. Tough grading on papers. The TA was totally incompetent, only giving general answers to questions. Attendance is mandatory, and you'll learn absolutely no skills in this class that will help you in life lol

Professor Buckley really cares about his students. He wants to make sure everyone will succeed. If the criteria for his projects are unclear, make sure you ask clarifying questions about the assignments! He is constantly reaching out to help students and wants to accommodate needs if possible. Just communicate with him.

I really enjoyed Dr. Buckley's class. His lectures were diverse in topic, focused on many perspectives, an engaging. The readings and write ups provided opportunities to learn and better understand history in an entertaining manner. He was helpful and gave great feedback.

Dr. Buckley is a great professor who truly cares about his students. Be sure to take notes while reading the textbook, as information in the textbook can show up on exams. I learned a lot from Dr. Buckley and am grateful I was in his class.

I enjoyed his class, I learned a ton of relevant, interesting things. He emphasized parts of history that are often overlooked. I thought that the grading criteria was unclear at times, especially with essays. His tests are randomly specific and focus less on themes/events and more on people, and small details that were rarely discussed in class.

Dr. Buckley is a great professor, easily my favorite I've ever had in a social Science major. Every day we learned something new that made an impression on me. He always worked hard to keep the class a fun learning environment while still sharing new groundbreaking perspectives from our Nation's History that really change everything.

He told us the last day of class would be a "review" and I expected him to review the content for the class. Instead, he spent class asking "what was your favorite topics?" and "what skills did you learn?" and had us take a U.S. citizenship test. He never prepared us for the tests well.

Okay, Dr. Buckley is probably the nicest teacher on campus here at BYU. He genuinely cares for each of his students. However, there are questions on the tests that were never even mentioned in class. Just one midterm covers 7 chapters of a textbook. The test however would ask very specific random questions. You will NOT get an A in this class.

He gives you ZERO heads up on what the tests will be on, and they are a huge part of your grade. Studied for like 10 hours and as soon as I started the test I realized I didn't study the right things because he doesn't provide a study guide or anything helpful. Even the TA was left in the dark so there were no resources to succeed.

Leaving a 2nd negative review for emphasis. This class is unfairly hard. Ruined my scholarship and now I pay full price for school because of Professor Buckley's ridiculous grading and inability to prepare you for tests.

I have a 3.9 GPA and work very hard for my grades, but he completely setup our class for failure. His study guides were not like the test, and super vague. He never shared details with his TA, so even the TA wasn't a good source for help. He had a derogatory tone and made you feel stupid for asking questions.

Professor Buckley is the kindest man at BYU. His class had a lot of outside readings and the tests are all essay based. I struggle with essays, so I had to stretch but if they are your thing take this class. Very informative and very kind professor who helped me improve. Grading was occasionally unclear but that is my only complaint. Wonderful guy.

Dr. Buckley is one of the rare professors you are excited to find! He started the semester as our tour guide through history. It was fun and enjoyable lots of work but very worth it. I highly recommend taking this class. If you have two classes that conflict .. choose his. You won't regret it. He grades fairly and quickly.

I loved taking History 490 with Dr. Buckley! He really cares about students' success and makes class fun and a joy to attend. He excels at helping students refine their ideas and polish up their final papers.

Dr. Buckley is one of the most genuine and kind professors I have ever had at BYU. I have taken two of his classes because his lectures are so interesting and engaging. He is also really willing to work with his students and wants them to do well in his classes. Highly recommend

He's great, Idk how he doesn't seem to be tenured. Class included lectures, papers, a research paper, 2 exams, and a fun visit to the MOA. It is manageable, but fyi he has high writing expectations for the papers. Truly cares about student success and is very knowledgeable, passionate about the subject, and very kind/approachable. Highly recommend.

Dr. Buckley is the nicest and most understanding professor I have ever had. He cares so deeply about the course and the students. His lectures are great and always entertaining. There's a decent amount of reading but it's really not that bad. He is very clear about assignments and tests and everything is organized really well.

Fantastic professor. I took HIST 220 early in the morning, but I was still able to stay awake through it because he made it interesting. He is complete accepting of people and their comments in class, and is willing to work with you outside of class. Lots of lectures, lots of reading, and a little bit of writing.

Buckley is awesome. He's one of my favorite professors. The work-load in his class was reasonable and the tests weren't very hard, just a lot of writing. Also, just wanted to add that Buckley is just a good person who wants what is best for his students and is always willing to talk to them. I would 100000000% recommend taking a class from him.
He really was the best.

As a Native American, I was wary of taking this class taught by a white guy, but Dr. Jay is humble, sensitive, and able to teach history without bias or one-sidedness. Sometimes his lectures can get boring, but he tries to make it relatable. Tests are all writing, final is a big research project. I got by without ever looking at the textbooks.

Dr. Buckley is an incredibly caring and kind professor. US History isn't my favorite but he went out of his way to help us engage with the material. The exams were reasonable, and he made sure we knew he was accessible out of class if we needed help with anything.

Prof. Buckley is a great professor - As a Native American I was amazed at his respect when dealing with sensitive subjects. Not a hard class to keep up in - a few readings, but about interesting stuff, written tests (which were graded fairly), one bigger paper but not too hard, and a few group projects which were fun.

I have taken multiple classes from Dr. Buckley and I have enjoyed every single one. This was a capstone course, so it was pretty writing heavy. Regardless, Dr. Buckley set us up for success by having us make drafts early on and giving us thorough feedback. He expects quality work but it makes you a better writer. He truly cares about his students!

Professor Buckley is an amazing professor! This was my first time taking a class about Native American history or even the intermountain west and he made everything so accessible and engaging. I learned so much and Professor Buckley was always very welcoming and understanding with his students. A fun class with clear and reasonable expectations.

I took Dr. Jay for my capstone class my senior year. It was pretty reading-heavy but he is a history professor so that was to be expected. He has a great relationship with students and I laughed in this class probably more than one should in a university class. HIGHLY RECOMMEND- but don't expect to rush through papers. He expects quality.
Great class. Prof Buckley is willing to work with you on any circumstance and deeply cares about source material!

Dr. Buckley is one of the kindest professors I have had. I took his class during COVID and he was extremely caring and willing to work with us. The class wasn't super difficult but I learned sooo much. I've already signed up to take more classes from him!

Dr. Buckley is super knowledgeable and very willing to help students. Ask for help! There are a lot of little assignments and he usually doesn't give an A unless you go above and beyond, so make sure to put in the effort and he will be generous. Also, show up and participate. I learned so much in this class.

I love Dr. Buckley! He is incredibly kind, passionate, and cares about his students! His class is certainly not a walk in the park, but if you work hard, pay attention, and ask for help when you need it, you will definitely succeed. Dr. Buckley has your best interests at heart. His classes truly influenced my education and outlook on life!

Professor Buckley is a very passionate and enthusiastic professor! He cares a lot with about the students and designs assignments that help you gain an appreciation for the Native American community. Would recommend this class to anyone! His grading is tough but worth the challenge if you are trying to learn.

Dr. Buckley is a really good and caring prof. His class was really interesting and I learned a lot. It is reading heavy and a lot of work. There were about 6 papers and a ton of reading. Studying for the tests was hard because I didn't know exactly what would be on them so pay really close attention in the lectures! GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS IT HELPS!

Prof Buckley was very kind and obviously cared a lot about his students. Definitely the sweetest prof! However, he definitely made you work for your grades. A bit frustrating that he would never give full points on assignments i.e. almost-weekly papers; the top scores would be around 94%- you would have to go above and beyond for a perfect score.

Could have gotten a solid A if I put a little more effort in; it is achievable. 3 exams, not cumulative. Exam MC is small details from lectures + textbook. Essay portion is main topics from lectures. TAs grade papers, don't be afraid to contest grades & ask for clear grading criteria. Prof is alright, lacks emphasis on some important concepts.

A HTG gets a bad rep, but trust me it is easier than HIST 220. The readings took me about 3+ hours A NIGHT and that is the only reason I got an A. There is an essay due nearly every week and the TAs grade extremely harshly but give very little instruction. The lectures are pretty boring, though Buckley is a great guy, and the tests are impossible

Dr. Buckley cares about his student so much! He is a very kind person. I learned a lot in this class, but it wasn't very easy. The tests are pretty hard, and the textbook is pretty dry. But the papers were generally fun to write and the TAs are super helpful.

Buckley is an incredibly nice man, but his class was rough. He stumbles through old powerpoints every day and it's hard to pay attention. He is a tough grader, and a lot depends on your TA's. I had terrible TA's and they kind of ruined this class for me. There is a crazy amount of reading and you'll fall behind. So many papers that are graded hard.

Most caring Prof I had the pleasure of learning from! Sent emails to encourage/remind us we have resources to help cope with Uni stress. A lot of reading but you learn valuable information! Papers for each book/one major research paper (ur choice) that he helps you prep for. Loved his class so much Im taking another! TAKE HIM YOU WONT REGRET IT!

IF YOU PLAN ON GETTING OR MAINTAINING A SCHOLARSHIP LISTEN UP! You wont get an A you just wont, my class only had 1 student who received above 94%. He is extremely unfair in his grades, this isnt a me thing this is an everyone thing. He is kind in his words but his actions say differently. If you dont care about grades go for it.

Professor Buckley is a nice person but his class was challenging. He is a very difficult grader. This class was heavy in reading and writing assignments. His lectures were dry and uninteresting. If history is not a subject you thrive in and don't enjoy then I would not recommend taking this class.

I don't think I could say enough good things about Dr. Buckley. The class is interesting and challenging, but not bad. As long as you do your best and work, you will do well in the class. He truly cares about his students and is there for help. I loved the class so much I am take another one next semester!

Professor Buckley does very well at making the course material entertaining and easy to remember. It is tricky when trying to take a half in person, half online course but professor Buckley makes it fun. I would definitely take from this professor again if I get the chance.

Dr. Buckley is a fantastic professor! His class is definitely challenging but so worth it. He relies on material from lectures, the textbook and extra readings for midterms and the final so make sure you read and take good notes. He loves history and encourages participation and differing opinions from his students.

Professor Buckley is one of the most caring and kind professors Ive ever had! The class is interesting, but there is just a lot of material so the tests were pretty hard as there was just so much to review. Overall though, a good class! Important subject matter that focuses a lot on Native American influence on American history.
Professor Buckley is a super cool person and he is super nice too. Pay attention in class and read and you should be fine.

This professor is very good. He knows a lot about history and is more than happy to answer your questions if you have em. The class was half online half in person so I wasn't sure how it would go but professor Buckley made it not only doable but Enjoyable. His exams are fair and he prepares you for them. Lots of papers, but that's to be expected.

He's one of those teachers who says he doesn't really give As. as in of you do everything you should do you'll get a 93. Getting a 100 is nearly impossible on an assignment. He really is a nice human being, but if you're just wanting to avoid taking American heritage, maybe pick a different class. There is 1 extra credit assignment that's worth 1%

Professor Buckley is a nice guy who is very passionate about what he is teaching, however, it is impossible to pay attention in class. He is boring and dry. I have solely depended on my prior American History knowledge to get through this class.

Professor Buckley is extremely knowledgeable, and cares a lot about his students. He is willing to meet with you and help you. He is a bit of a tough grader, and you should expect to work your grades, but not impossible at all. He gives a lot of assignments, but none are too large. I really enjoyed the class.

I would recommend Dr. Buckley's class to anyone looking to become more familiar with Native American history! He is one of the most approachable professors I have taken a class from, and he gave me really good feedback on my research project. Participation is mandatory, so plan on coming to class. Do readings, and ask him if you have any questions!

I don't recall a question ever being asked throughout the entire semester that Dr. Buckley did not know the answer to. He effectively cultivates an environment of respect, safety, and growth. His grading is tough, and his feedback very helpful. I highly recommend Dr. Buckley's class.

Jay is the best! His lectures were always interesting and his assignments werent busywork, everything in his class had a purpose. He was always really caring and respected and treated all of us like family. It was a small class so you participated a lot, but everything was very flexible. Loved this class and would totally recommend it to everyone!

I was hesitant to take this class after reading reviews, but this class was NOT time consuming, NOT hard to get stuff done, and I NEVER felt intimidated to contact him about anything. My only complaint is that he's transitioning from paper copies to digital copies and sometimes there are discrepancies for requirements. Just clarify with him :)

Mr. Buckley is a great professor! He keeps lectures interesting and fun to attend. He does take attendance so it's important to go to class. You will learn so much in this class in a new and entertaining way, he dresses up and does accents. He is wiling to talk to and help students with personal issues, very understanding and considerate.

Professor Buckley is passionate about History, and it shows during his lectures. They are engaging and contain info important for the midterm/final. Tests include multiple choice and short essay questions. Like any class, it requires effort, especially in the reading of the textbook and other texts. However, Prof. Buckley is great.

Professor Buckley genuinely cares about you and what he teaches. The lectures are interesting and I always stayed awake which is saying a lot because I took his class at 8am! The multiple choice on the tests are pretty hard so you have to do the readings and pay a lot of attention in class. He is a very generous grader when it comes to essays.

Loved the professor and the class. Made history interesting. Taught with positivity and a love for American history but didnt hide the uglier parts of it. Really left me with a broader and deeper understanding of our history. He really cares about his students and likes to get to know them.

Professor Jay Buckley is a great teacher. I would take any of classes. Great lectures and material that prepares for the exams. Just review the material and stay ahead of papers you will write and you will do fine.
Tests are difficult, and the class isnt easy, but if youre willing to work, it will help develop you a lot.

He is a great professor, he knows so much and cares about each of his students. You can tell he wants to know everyone even in large classes. However, because he knows literally everything about American history he covers a lot of information very quickly, so sometimes it can be difficult to feel prepared for tests but they are doable if you study.

Dr. Buckley's class was always super fun to go to! It's rigorous, and you get a whole lot out of it. Be willing to go visit during office hours-he's definitely willing to help you to improve your grade as well as make sure you understand the material.

This was one of my favorite classes at BYU! Dr. Buckley is an engaging teacher and found ways to bring to life what he is teaching. He is also willing to work with you if you give effort. Not an easy A, but a good class nonetheless. If you don't love/moderately enjoy history, this is not the class for you. This helped me to love American history!

Dr. Buckley is an enjoyable history professor. He teaches clearly and in a fun manner, dressing up as Lewis and Clark when discussing them. His class is definitely hard, and you have to work hard to receive an A, but you will learn substantially. I loved his class and would definitely take it again!

Professor Buckley is great. He cares about his students and values education. He teaches great material and I always learn so much from his classes. If you do your reading you will be prepared for the quizzes. He grades fairly and if you put in the effort you will learn from the class and get a good grade.

I couldn't have chosen a better teacher/mentor to work on my capstone research paper with. Even though I chose to research an area outside of Dr. Buckley's emphasis, he helped me immensely by directing me to resources and by being available. He  is great to work with and encouraged me to pursue additional opportunities outside of class.

Dr. Buckley is one of the most accessible and caring professors. He is very authentic and cares a lot about his students' success, not only about class content. He is approachable, flexible, and reasonable. He makes class humorous and enjoyable. He does expect a lot of his students, but he rewards those who are willing to put in genuine effort.

Now that I am working in Washington D.C. I really appreciate the things I learned in Dr. Buckley's classes.  His classes have prepared me better for this experience than any others I have taken at BYU.

I took this class instead of American Heritage and it was honestly the right choice! Lots of outside reading in addition to the textbook with papers that went with each book. They are only 500 words so not bad. Test questions came straight out of the textbook, NOT lectures although attendance is mandatory. Do the readings and you'll pass easily!

This is my second class with Dr. Buckley. He is a phenomenal professor. His grading criteria for the paper are clear. He is quite critical in drafts, but fixes every little thing so if you incorporate his changes you will do well. He spends lots of time one on one making sure you are on the right track.  I would take another class in a heartbeat!!

Dr. Buckley is easily one of the best professors I ever had. Classes are very well organized and interesting. For the paper, several drafts that he grades pretty critically, but he fixes every little mistake. In the end you get a really great grade if you fix your errors. Very willing to help in all aspects of the class and life in general.
I never wanted to miss class.

Dr. Buckley is very knowledgable about the subject material. My only issue was that he can be an unreasonably tough grader, but really it's not that hard to get a good grade in his class. He encourages class discussion, and is respectful of students' opinions. I learned a ton from Dr. Buckley, I would definitely recommend him!

The tests don't have anything to do with the lectures, but you still need to come to class because he gives pop quizzes. The pop quizzes are only 5 questions and on really specific details, so if you miss even just one, it will hurt your grade.

Professor Buckley is a nice guy and cares however, his classes are all lecture and very dry/boring. I basically just read the book to learn. He takes attendance every class and randomly gives pop quizzes. There are several short papers to write which aren't too bad. Midterms are multiple choice with a couple of essay prompts. I wouldn't recommend.

Do not take this class as an independent study course. He doesn't return emails. Quizzes have questions that aren't even in the chapter that you're being quizzed on.  His "feedback" was so off-base and generic that I swear he must not have even read my essay but just sent a canned response. RIDICULOUS!!!!!

Beware! In the independent study class many of the quiz questions deal with picky details and material that is NEVER presented in the textbook or online course materials. Other questions are on material that isn't covered until a chapter or two later.  Also, it's literally impossible to contact him if you're in the independent study class.

Professor Buckley is a really nice guy who wants you to do well in the class. He expects a lot of reading. His lectures are long and hard to pay attention to. I found the readings a lot more helpful than his lectures. There are lots of short papers due throughout the semester that are not too hard. It's the pop quizzes that will get ya!

Brother Buckley is a nice person, but there is no good way to study for this class. You have to read four books over the course of the semester in addition to the textbook and other assigned readings. Attendance is mandatory, but lectures don't cover majority of what will be on the test. If you decide to take this class, good luck.

Dr. Buckley is approachable, knowledgable, hilarious, and fair. His dry humor and surprising pop culture references make class fun, while his berth of knowledge makes it interesting. Dr. Buckley expects students to be responsible for their education. If you need help or have feedback for him, approach him. He's invested in his students successes.

The test study-guides say "multiple choice from all reading and lectures" so you have to class to get all the information and do well. Make comments in class for sure!!! It is a smaller class which allows for more fun debates and questions and discussions among students. Dr. Buckley knows each student by name, and I would recommend him

Dr. Buckley is one of the best professors at BYU. If you go talk to him,  he will help you learn the material and understand the concepts better so you will do well on his tests. It is AMAZING how much he knows about this subject. He is for sure an expert in his field. If you are willing to go to class and try, you will really like this class!

I truly felt like I learned something important in this class. Not too much reading, fascinating lectures, slightly difficult tests but completely doable. Dr. Buckley is so funny. He has a really smart, dry sense of humor -- you have to listen closely to appreciate it. Thankfully, he also loves to dress up like Lewis and Clark. Great class.

If you want to LEARN about history, then this is a great class. If you care about your grades or have scholarships you are trying to maintain, then this is not a great class. Please learn from someone who has been in your shoes--just take American Heritage instead. There are TA's to help, and a huge curve too! This class has neither.

warning to all those wanting to take HIST 220 to fulfill part of the American Heritage required credit--DON'T DO IT! Really, unless you already have an interest in American History, and I mean read books about it for fun and debate about it at lunch with your friends, you will not enjoy this class. AND NEITHER WILL YOUR GPA!

Professor Buckley is great!  He really knows what he's talking about and he cares.  Just do the reading and pay attention in class. His lectures are a little hard to follow, but he's funny.  Definitely recommend!

If you are not a textbook reader, this is not the class for you. Buckley is funny enough, but although I'm majoring in the subject I found his class painful. The study guide says, "Multiple choice from reading and lecture." That's it. Things that appeared on the test were in the reading but didn't appear on the lecture until after the test. Beware.

Its true, you do have to do the reading to prepare for the test, so read through the chapters and be ready for the test. Professor Buckley teaches a really enjoyable and entertaining class, and no, he will not read out of the book for you, sorry. He is also very cordial and helpful if you are struggling in the class.

Dr. Buckley is the best prof I've had at BYU. Class is interesting and he encourages participation. Not boring at all. He knows the subject incredibly well. It is time consuming--lots of reading, difficult to know what's on the tests, and no feedback on essays, so it's hard to know how to improve. But it's fascinating and he'll work with you.

Dr. Buckley is has extensive knowledge of American Indians and the Lewis and Clark Expedition.  He is a very friendly guy with a fun personality, but his course was very challenging.  Lectures could be hard to follow but his enthusiasm was always high.  He will really push you in your writing, and most of the tests were essay questions.

I LOVE Dr. Buckley! He is really funny, especially when he makes fun of kids who think they know everything. He is open to questions and helping the students and is really nice. He grades essays on tests nice. The tests were rough though, the multiple choice didn't really reflect lectures in class, you have to read a lot, but I highly reccomend him

Professor Buckley is a good teacher but do not take him for American History 220. His lectures are interesting but almost NOTHING he talked about showed up directly on his midterms. The majority of his lectures were where he just sat and talked to us. We also had 2 full text books he expected us to read and 3 books to do papers on.

Dr Buckley gave me the best feedback on my writing that I've ever received.  I really developed as a researcher/writer during his course.  He grades fairly but has high expectations.  Actively engage with the material and you'll get a lot out of this personable, helpful, knowledgeable professor.

Dr. Buckley gave me the best feedback and criticism on my writing that I've ever received.  I really developed as a writer and researcher during his class.  He grades fairly, but expects preparation prior to class.  I don't recommend passively going through his courses.

Lewis and Clark was an awesome class. I wasn't too excited for it when I signed up, but by the first class I was hooked.He is a really hard grader, but he was always willing to help. There's tons of reading, but the class is extremely rewarding.

Dr. Buckley is a very nice person and is passionate about his subject, but his grading is something you can't live up to.  He almost never gives out As.  Plan to do well in the class before the final because he usually gives you the option of not finishing it.

Very enthusiastic professor! Really nice lecturing style--and I appreciated his effort to include students in discussions. This class had a lot of work, but I really enjoyed it because of Prof. Buckley.
It was not an easy class, but I learned a lot and he was a good teacher.
This class was interesting, but I found that the tests were really difficult.  His study guides were short and not very useful.  Pro. Buckley is a funny guy, but I didn't like his class at all.

He had a seating chart which i found odd but that was to learn everyones name.  He is funny and energetic, seems like he is nervous sometimes but a good professor i really enjoyed the class and would recommend him to others.
He has a great sense of humor and I always enjoyed his lectures.  He memorizes everyone's name and makes everyone feel very comfortable.
AWESOME, AWESOME, AWESOME!!! Dr. Buckley is very helpful, lecture are interesting and enjoyable to attend. If you enjoy the West, this is a must...not very difficult.

Dr. Buckley is awesome. His lectures are mostly interesting, and he is always willing to do something corny to wake everyone up. Some unclear instructions on the film and book reviews, but that was a problem with the TA. The mid-term is really important, don't blow it off.

Best class I've ever had at BYU. Fantastic subject, and Dr. Buckley is awesome--very knowledgeable and loves to share his interests with his students. The lectures were always very good.The book and film analysis instructions were a little ambiguous so it was difficult to do well on them, but otherwise it was a fair class.
Dr. Buckley is a great professor. He cares a lot about his students and is willing to help.

If you are a history buff, you will like Buckley's class. The course organization is good despite other's comments. He emphasizes the west so you must have an interest to enjoy the content.  If you do the work, including readings, and form a study group you will do well in the class. He also has guest lecturers and films.

Buckley is a very nice man but he is also very scattered and a bit disorganized.  I never paid attention in lecture because they were so random and he is very difficult to follow.  He doesn't teach the material well and it's hard to know what he wants sometimes.  I hate to be rude because he is so nice but I don't think you should take his classes.
Yuck.  I took it in the Spring and had two and a half hour lectures at 8:00AM.  Probably the worst experience of my life.  He's a good guy but I hated the class and the TA was terrible.

I enjoyed Buckley's class, organized with powerpoint outlines, you know what you need to know for the test. There is a term paper, and the normal reading for a history class. Incorporates more than just lectures. Get a study group in the beginning of the class and you'll do great.

Lectures can get pretty boring, but Dr. Buckley knows his stuff. He tries to make it interesting. His focus is on Western US history and Native Americans, so be prepared for a lot of that information. A lot of reading. I did well... it is easy to get an A-.

not really excietd about the class, but heard he was a good teacher..and he was great!  he's nice and he's funny, and his tests are a little long he gives you a study guide.  I LOVE him as a teacher.  and he's a very nice man too.
While the class can be hard and unclear at times, if you take to him then he goes out of his way to help you get back on track. very nice and very helpful!

His lectures are very scattered and he goes off topic a lot.  Spends a lot of time on stuff he doesn't test about like Lewis and Clark (he's obsessed with them).  His tests are beastly (3 hours).  There's a lot of reading to do and the questions are specific like, "Who wrote this useless passage?"
No Comments
Great Class, I would recommend it

Means well, but that doesn't help us who are history majors.  Needs to be more focused and clear about his topics. Students need to read assignments before coming to class, otherwide they will get lost in fuzzy presentations.
He's funny. He's sometimes unclear in his points during lectures.
No Comments
He is very passionate about what he teaches. I actually really liked Professor Goodliffe, I wasn't really a fan of UNIV 101

This is moreso a rating of POLI 428 than Goodliffe. I wouldn't want anyone else in the department to teach the class, but it was so ridiculously hard. Goodliffe does a better job explaining things 1on1 than he does in a class setting. I feel like I learned how to run code in R than actually learned the statistical methods. So so so hard

The class is brutal, but I trust no one else other than Dr. Goodliffe to teach it.  I learned a ton, and I feel like I can compete with some of the best stats, econ, and comp sci annalists now because of this class. We covered regression on categorical variables, multilevel models, causal inference, and simulations, to name some topics.
He is the main cause of BYUs love of POL 328. He is full of himself.

Goodliffe is a smart man, and he has a lot of connections in D.C. But he is not personable. For example, my classmate asked him a question about the syllabus and Goodliffe told him that that it was a bad question and he better be careful about asking such questions. I am a law student and his Syllabus is very difficult to understand.

This will be the hardest class you will ever take. You should be prepared mentally for it. To be honest, I had nightmares about this class before I took it. You have assignments that take 10+ hours and tests that take longer. BUT, you learn a ton! I loved the class and I struggle with statistics. Take it with Dr. Goodliffe! You will not regret it.

This class was a terrible experience for me. Not entirely Goodliffe's fault, but he made it worse in most ways. I spent 30 hours a week trying to figure out the homework assignments and still failed them all. He seemed more interested in marketing his own brilliance than teaching me anything.

He's a really good lecturer; you can tell he understands the material well. The class is just really hard. Prepare to devote 20+ hours a week to this class if you want to do well. You might feel like you're going to fail the class, but as long as you do most of the assignments and all of the tests, you will pass. Good luck.

The rumors are true--this class is a big time commitment! . The TA's have plenty of office hours to help students with the weekly assignments. The lectures are helpful, but the majority of learning comes from putting it into practice. There is a solid curve, so your raw score doesn't matter as much as how well you do compared to other students.

This class is the most demanding class I have ever taken. The weekly workload is ridiculously intensive, and the material is not taught well in class for you to do it on your own. He "leaves you to figure it out on your own" which translates to living in the TA lab if you want to have any hope of doing well, which still won't save you.

I was terrified because of the ratings but I'm glad I took it! Goodliffe is a qualified, caring guy & loves statistics. He teaches clearly but does move quickly. The work is fine, just go to class & the lab and you know everything you need. Students who get mad at him are the ones who derp around during class, learn nothing, and say it's his fault.

I've taken both 328 and 304 from Goodliffe and he was the same in both. The homework was exceptionally hard and long. He was hard to access and he's scary to talk to. He has a hard time relating to students who don't understand the material. Take 328 from a different professor. He literally makes his class harder than Gubler and Barber.

Rushes though lectures.  You HAVE TO go see the TAs multiple times per week to succeed. If you have ANY personal issue (including unexpected serious health issue) DO NOT expect any kind of understanding. Comes across as cold and uncaring. He treats you like a child who needs to be taught how to handle life, without knowing anything about you.

Dr. Goodliffe is definitely intimidating, but he really is a great professor. Just go into his office hours and he's great at explaining things in a way that you'll continue to understand after the assignment. It's simply tough material! But he's organized and handles it well.

This was one of the hardest class I have ever taken. That being said, this is one of the best classes I have ever taken. Dr. Goodliffe is very knowledgable about statistics and statistical analysis. This class will benefit you in the rest of your political science career so it is best to take it from Dr. Goodliffe who knows it the best.

This class is extremely time consuming. For me it took 15-20 hours per week. The reading quizzes were unnecessary, most students just googled to find the answers. Don't bother reading the textbook. Even class was unnecessary sometimes. The best way to succeed in this class is to 1) go to lab. 2) Use the TAs 3) Do every question on every assignment.

I was one of Goodliffe's old students and TAs. It definitely helps to have him for another class before taking Game Theory. The course is kinda difficult because material is new (game theory you learn in Econ 110 is easy). Know how probabilities work (328 useful). More time than most 3 cr. classes, but is useful for real life and academic papers.

This is the hardest class you'll take in the Poli Sci department. However, there's no better teacher for the job. He's very helpful and loves Stats, so his enthusiasm will give you motivation to try harder on the 12-18 hr weekly assignments you get. The material isn't too hard, but the time commitment is extraordinary (20+ hours a week). Good luck
great!

This is probably the hardest and most time consuming class I have ever taken. That being said, it was also the most worthwhile class I have ever taken. Professor Goodliffe knows the material is hard, so he does his best to simplify it. He really cares and wants you to do well! He loves this stuff, so his passion makes it worth it!

This is probably the hardest class I will take in college. That being said, I loved it. I learned so much and Professor Goodliffe is an amazing professor! He makes class interesting, is very helpful, caring, and super legit and genius. I would absolutely take this amazing, so worthwhile class from Prof Goodliffe!

Tough class, regardless of who you take it from.  Most work of any class I've taken.  TAs helped a lot, and they grade your papers.  Lectures can help and you need lab to get the Stata commands but the most important thing by far is doing the homework. Really interesting class though, and Goodliffe is very good at relating the skills to real life.

I've seen the benefit of this class even more after going to grad school (and I thought it was great before). Develops intuition and practicing grasp of material (especially through weekly "memos") that gives motivation to more advanced econometric theory. Tons of work, lots of sleepless nights, but completely worth it. Great class.
I find a lot of these comments by students to be more emotional than objective. Great teacher, always willing to help. Hard class, but he made it tolerable.

The class is hard. Very hard. But Goodliffe teaches clearly. Some people are over the top on this site. He is pretty good...in fact I thought his lectures were very clear and he was helpful. Be prepared to work 20+ hours a week though.

This was the hardest class I ever took at BYU.  But. It was the most useful class as well.  I only remember things I learned in PLSC 328 and 200. Goodliffe demands a lot of you, but if you do it, you will have skills that you can use for the rest of your life.

HORRIBLE Professor! He made a difficult subject even more difficult, which is hard to believe. He was of no use what so ever! I put in about 20hrs a week and only got a C. He's awful! Avoid him as much as possible!!!! Worst class of my entire career!

It's been a couple years since I took 328. Since then, I've taken a couple of more advanced stats classes (in grad school). Looking back, I can see that Goodliffe was by far the best stats professor ever. The material that 328 covers is very difficult by nature, but Goodliffe makes it as clear as it can be made--and he'll help if asked.

Easily the worst professor I've had in my four years at BYU. Very arrogant and condescending toward students. Rude and vague when students ask questions. Unfair grader; no one knew what he expected on papers. DO NOT do Washington Seminar if he's the faculty adviser; he will ruin the experience. Students had virtually no time for sight-seeing in DC.

Very difficult topic, very challenging, but extremely worthwhile.  If you put in the time you will master a difficult subject and be well prepared to go on.  The single most useful poli sci class I took at BYU.  The level of work was on par with my grad school classes and am forever grateful.
Excellent source of information for a difficult topic.  Like running a marathon, a difficult class but forever a source of pride.

WORST professor EVER! He's demeaning to students when you attempt to ask questions. The work amount for the number of credits is INSANELY high! The TAs are not helpful; there was maybe one that gave any useful information. I CANNOT believe that he is here, let alone teaching AT ALL!!! He's horrid!!!

This class did not help me at all. Going to every lab, every class, and doing every assignment only got me a D. Not approachable. Wants to flaunt his stuff instead of actually teaching. TAs do nothing. Assignments are just STATA instead of really learning what you need to know. I'm surprised this minion of satan teaches at the "Lord's University."

Going into this I knew the class would be hard, but I found Prof. Goodliffe to be a very good teacher. He uses the feedback students give. The readings aren't necessary but class, TA hours and especially the labs are. It took about 10 hours a week, but I got an A. Do the assignments early and check with your fav TA during TA hours. That's the key!

This class is hell. I spent about 8-10 hrs. a week and that was enough for a C. Some of the TAs are helpful while others are pompous brats who think they are the world's elite. I actually liked Prof. Goodliffe and thought he was tough but fair. At least this class is graded on a curve and if you have 12-15 hrs. to put in each week you will be fine

Goodliffe is very smart but his teaching style leaves much to be desired. He requires LARGE amounts of work without guidance. Lectures are tangentially related to the homework(15+ hours/week) at best, and he admits that he doesn't explain parts of the homework in order to make you figure it out. Takes an interesting topic and makes it unbearable.

The class is worth it.  It is a hard and time consuming class, but if you do well in the class you might think that it was all worth it.  People call me crazy, but this class is better than plsc 200; if you are a math person.  I would suggest only taking the class with limited credits.  Use TA's.  Class is not useful, but TA's and Labs are!

Worst professor at BYU. Awful lecturer, selects TAs that kiss his butt but have no grasp on effective teaching. Lectures have nothing to do with the assignments or tests. Horrible class, horrible professor. I will not give a dime to BYU until he no longer teaches here.

He is the worse professor I have ever had and a disgrace to the university and everything it represents. He couldn?t teach a kid to tie his shoes. Most students don?t bother with his lectures, as they are useless. Sure he is intelligent, but who cares? We are paying for tuition and not getting our money?s worth. He cannot teach whatsoever.

A brilliant man and good professor. I can't compare him to the other theory profs, but he's not easy but he made theory interesting. Sign up for the Power I presentation.  I didn't do one single reading (too many). Get the notes from someone who took it from him the previous semester, make writen copies of them.  I aced all the quizes that way.

Go to class. Do the readings. Probably not the WORST teacher, but definitely not the best. I didn't get anything from that class. DO NOT sign up for the last presentation. Try to talk to him if you have a question. Use the writing fellows if he's still has them. I don't recommend the class, though, unless you really love political theory.
I'm crying right now.

This class is ridiculous.  The material is very difficult and the class requirements are worse.  Unfortunately it is now a requirement for the major, and Goodliffe is the only professor who teaches it.  Be prepared for 10-15 hour weekly assignments.  Goodliffe will not help you. Get a group of other students to work with.
Very hard class. the key is other students and some of the TA's. To be blunt, Professor Goodliffe doesn't care about you. He becomes aggitated when students don't undertand.
Required class.  Have to take who teaches it when you are ready, but Goodliffe is dangerous.  Makes you work hard in order to "learn more."  Weekly homework assignments take hours (i.e. 10-12 hours).

This class is HARD but it has to be, he does a great job considering the curriculum. No need to read the book. Go to class and GO TO LAB. The TA's are fair but the key are his office hours and other students.  Lots of work but you learn a ton, especially once you get the hang of it.Loved the class
He is not extremely clear and talks down at students.  His teaching style was debasing and not inducive to learning.

Hard class. But I'm a freshmen who took 200 my first semester, and then took this the next semester. It's for juniors and seniors. Just go to class, answer the study quesitons, and take good notes. I only needed my class notes to get an A on the final. The papers are easy if you know what is going on. He is hard to talk to though use other sutdnets

It was a hard class but not impossible. The readings were intense but i learned a lot. He is always willing to help after class and in his office although his help isnt always the most helpful. He is a little crazy but it made things more enjoyable. It was a hard class and a lot was expected but it was good.

I've had many professors at BYU, and he is by far the worst. He is confusing, goes through a 2 semester book in one semester, becomes infuriated when students do not understand the material, and decides to move on even without understanding the subject previously covered. The TA's are inconsistent and unavailable (taking many trips for enjoyment).
He is crazy.

Brother Jay is an awesome professor. I have had multiple classes with him and would take another class from him any day. He will take the time to make sure you understand something and is super easy to work with.

Professor Snell is one of my favorite professors. I've taken a couple of his classes and he cares about his students and if you put in the effort you will get an A. He works with you when you need help and wants everyone to succeed.

Professor Snell is kind and cares about his students. That being said, his class structure isn't my favorite. 8am deadlines, no study guides for learning checks, and scattered class material. The online textbook is nice but is also very comprehensive, so it's hard to tell what information is important. Still, he is a great guy. Overall OK class.

This class required a lot of textbook reading and in class we only ever talked about vague questions based on the reading. The projects were very time intensive with buggy software that would just delete the whole project and then we would have to redo everything.

Jay is both an amazing professor, and a quality person. It is very clear that he genuinely cares about the success of his students. He is extremely passionate about what he teaches, and makes it easy to digest and understand. A true 10/10 professor in an already amazing program. I will certainly be taking more classes from Jay in the future.

One of the nicest professors I've taken a class from. He talks frequently about mental health and has reasons for all the assignments, nothing feels like busywork. He's very accommodating and knows his stuff. I entered the class not knowing a single thing about how the internet worked and now I can fix my router.

I cannot say enough good about Jay Snell. He has an awesome teaching style, he's passionate about the content and about his students' success, and he's great at explaining difficult concepts. Projects and assignments are relevant, and he prepares you well for exams.

Professor Gifford is a good teacher. Intro to Exercise Science is such an easy class and will get you prepared for the major. The class is once a week and is based off in-class work and pre-class reading and quizzes. The classes can be boring sometimes with other guest lecturers, but he is a good teacher and cares about your success.

Awesome class! He's a great teacher. There were 3 midterms and an oral final exam. After each midterm we would go over commonly missed concepts, then you could do a retake. The oral exam was like a presentation; he asked questions and we answered using a whiteboard. It was a bit stressful but a really good experience, and graded pretty leniently.

Dr. Gifford isn't the easiest person to take 463 from but I think he's the best. He takes time out of class every day to talk about and give advice for secondary school. Get to know him and you've got it made. He is super approachable as well and loves to help however he can. Final is a bit interesting but working as a group made is so easy.

I loved Dr. Gifford's class! The material covered in this class is fascinating. Also Dr. Gifford has a passion for what he is teaching which helps to make the class engaging. He backs all his lectures up with research and data, which I appreciated. He finds ways to connect what we're learning to "real life" and he cares about his students!!

Dr. Gifford is very respectful and cares about his students. He always connects the material to ways that we can "lift and strengthen" other people, especially elderly populations. He uses research in the lectures and explains things clearly.

Gifford is a smart person but his class sets you up for failure. Attendance is required and he was strict about not allowing absences for ANY reason or else your grade will drop 2% each day you miss. He lectures about what he likes to talk about and not what you are tested on. Whatever you learn is on your own from the book. Would not recommend.

He's super chill, this class can give you an idea of whether or not you want to do exsc. If you know you want to do exsc this class can help you figure out what direction to start in and kind of prepares you and connects you with classmates

Oh my goodness his course was so confusing. The grading system is wack and you have to "qualify" for an A. He has a few midterms which you can take twice but his questions are so wordy and confusing. He hardly preps you for tests. Plus he doesn't really allow his TAs to prep anything for a review so those are a waste of time. Condescending as well.
Would not take again with this professor. Attendance was mandatory. Tests were very applicable but felt like he was trying to trick you. Interesting grading system.

Gifford is a nice guy, but not the best teacher.I am constantly confused by his lectures and his grading system is wack.Not everyone will even qualify to take the oral final. If you just want to pass, this class is for you! If you want an A, I would take this class from another prof unless you have tons of time to read and prep for the exams.
Very easy class to get a C+ in without having to do any midterms or final

Professor Gifford is, hands down, my favorite professor! His class is very engaging and he is great at explaining difficult concepts. He truly wants to see you succeed and will do everything to help you do that. His exams are application based, which I loved. He made the material very applicable to everyone. Take this class from him!

Dr. Gifford is easily one of my favorite teachers at BYU. His lectures were very clear and he wants you to succeed. Tests were application based, so know his slides well and how to apply them. If you can, take it from him.

Dr. Gifford is the man! He's a really great lecturer and organizes the material for physiology so clearly and well. The class is tough because it's a 400 level course and it's physiology, but TAs and professor are SO accessible if you need help. Study the slides, do the quizzes, be there for class and honestly you'll be just fine. Loved this class.

Dr. Gifford is rad. He cares about what he's teaching and he cares about you, but he also pushes you. What he teaches is always applicable and he treats the class like they're the up and coming top doctors and scientists. He's always there to help and wants you to succeed. He pushes you, but that's because he knows you're capable of doing well.

Dr. Gifford is one of my favorite professors! And, he's younger and easy to relate to. He really cares that you can apply the material to your life so even though some material seems like review from regular human physiology, his tests are geared towards application in an exercise setting. Light online textbook reading; always willing to help!

Gifford will give you every opportunity to get the extra help you need. Trust me when I say you need it. The course comes across as review material from PDBIO 305, but the tests use more application questions than is gone over in class or homework. It is a challenging class and requires earnest effort/understanding. The tests are only 30 questions.

You would never know that it was his first semester as a college professor! He is a personable guy who is interested in the students' lives. The class isn't easy, but that made doing well more rewarding. He makes challenging concepts easy to understand by using real world examples. He is accessible outside of class and is very helpful and caring.
Dr. Gifford was a great professor! I highly recommend you take his classes!

P318 was insanely hard for me and was transformational. Dr. VanHuele is particularly great at answering questions and he cares about the students. He went above and beyond in helping students. I didn't love the class structure, but he's flexible if you talk to him. I thought the class took too much time, but I also learned a lot.

I had Dr Van Huele during the Spring, so it was different. He's a great professor, but lectures weren't very helpful. He would usually talk about a lot of stuff that we didn't need to know and that was beyond the scope of the class. The tests were pretty hard, but Dr Van Huele is solid. There was no scale posted but I got 93% which I guess is an A-

I took physics 123 from Dr Van Huele during the Spring, so it was a little different. He's a great professor, but the lectures were not very helpful. He would usually talk about a lot of stuff that we didn't need to know and that was beyond the scope of the class. The tests were pretty hard, but Dr Van Huele is a sold professor

PHYS100 is a tough class to begin with, but Dr. V made it somewhat enjoyable. He has his class set up in a reverse way, you read the chapters at home and then he has lectures during class about what you read. He is pretty entertaining so that helps. Go to the TA Labs and reviews and take advantage of the cheat sheet for tests

Professor VanHuele was an amazing teacher! I took PHY S 100 from him over summer term and he always made me excited for class and learning. He is very fun and cracks lots of jokes but doesn't let them take away from the lesson. Professor VanHuele was willing to answer any question, easy or hard. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND TAKING FROM VANHUELE

The class is flipped, which means you teach yourself the lessons and come to class just to see demos and do the graded classwork. I don't think Dr. V does much in terms of teaching, but he does try his best to answer questions and help everyone do well. If you do the readings and get the TAs help, you'll get an A.

Physical science is one of those classes that kind of just sucks no matter who teaches. BUT Dr. V is definitely the guy to take it from. He was funny, clear in his lectures, always offered help, and had great demos. They want you to pass, so use the TA's, study, and you should get an A. Highly recommend Dr. V for a great semester!

Professor V is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. I am not a science person, but his lectures combined with a really good textbook made it doable even if science isn't your best subject. He was really funny, lectures were engaging, and there was so much help inside and outside of class to make sure you had the opportunity to succeed.

I took from Dr. VanHuele over spring term, and it was a fast but good class overall. I found reading the textbook to generally be of more help than his lectures. Homework standards felt excessive at times, but he was clear about it and did a good job of teaching overall.

Be prepared for ineffective lectures, long readings, and a lot of tests. His lectures answer the student's questions, but they don't always cover the material. I stopped attending lectures in favor of working on the homework assignments. Beware of reading quizzes that grade on completion. I love physics but I hated this class.
