Professor V. is the best! He is really kind and willing to work with students. The class is a lot of work, but I took it over summer term so that is probably why!

With online classes and in Spring term, I found that there was heaps of outside reading. He spent the first part of most class periods answering questions from the students, and he was always willing to answer clarification questions mid-lecture. He asked us about how we preferred to have a final and adapted based on feedback. A top bloke.

I was having lots of problems with staying on top of everything, and Dr. Van Huele was 100% willing to work with me. This is the first time I've ever rated one of my professors so he's great to work with!
Pretty good professor. Take over the summer if you need an easy general out of the way.

Dr. V is a really relaxed professor and teaches everything in a very simple way. He posts his slides online and gives plenty of visual examples of principles in class. He sometimes goes off-topic but only if people ask off-topic questions. Great professor, use your TAs, go to the labs, you will need the book and make sure to study.

Dr. Van Huele is hands down the best professor I've had. He's very approachable and fun to talk with, and is excellent at teaching concepts and figuring out which ones confuse students, then reviewing those multiple times so that they understand. His tests are very conceptual, so make sure you know both how to get the answer and why it works.

Dr. Van Huele is a great teacher and I would recommend him for anybody taking any of his classes. He wants the students to learn and adapts the course to how the class learns the best and listens to feedback. You are required to write a journal about the readings but you can take it into the testing center.

Pretty easy to get an A in this class--do the reading quizzes, go in before homework assignments are due to discuss them with the TA's (there are certain things they are looking for), and go to your labs! Reading from the textbook is recommended but not necessary.

His class was very enjoyable and he made hard concepts very easy to understand. There are a ton of free points given just for attending class and doing reading quizzes (which have unlimited attempts btw) that make getting an A very doable. I highly recommend taking PS100 from Dr. V.

I took this class in the summer so It went super fast, but It wasn't impossible. If you put in the work and read and do homework in the TA lab outside of class then you will do fine. Dr. V is so funny and you can tell he's super smart, but I learned a lot more from the TA's then him. The topics themselves aren't hard but theres just A LOT.

The amount of reading I had to do for this class was overwhelming, but it was interesting. Prepare for difficult tests. Not an easy A. Dr. V is really funny and really cares about what he does. The TA's were so helpful and their reviews were great.
Great guy, hard tests

Dr. VanHuele has been one of my best professors at BYU. He's extremely fair - if you put in the work, you'll do just fine. He's got a great sense of humor. The lectures feel redundant because of the journal you keep, but it's also your best opportunity to ask questions. He cares about his students and makes it his goal to get to know everyone.

DO NOT TAKE 318 AT THE SAME TIME AS 321!!!!! Dr. Van Huele is a great professor. He has a thing accent that I struggled to get used to but other than that he is fine. There is a reading journal you are required to keep but you can bring it into the tests. Also uses multiple books but only required to buy 1 of them. I only attended half the time.

Dr. V IS REALLY Funny and pretty chill. His lectures are exactly like in the book and the only reason I showed up was for the iclicker quizzes. GO TO TA labs cause they will help. A TON and look up videos on YouTube for clarification. DO NOT take this class over summer term cause it is very compacted and kinda stressful

Professor VanHuele is a fun teacher. You'll learn a lot of cool things in his class. Be sure to attend the TA reviews and study! The material is very interesting and Professor Van Huele always has good demo labs in class so you won't get too bored.

I took this class from him summer term and loved it! It was easy, & he understood that we were college students who didn't want to spend summer doing physical science. Summer term moves fast, but there are many quizzes & assignments dropped. I was super lazy, & got a decent grade. Just do your work and use your resources.

Brilliant professor with a great attitude.  He genuinely wants you to not only learn the material, but understand it as well. He often asked questions to gauge how effective his teaching was for us personally, and really wanted to help you understand.  Great guy as well, so far as human beings go.

Dr. V is the bomb! He is very funny and does lots of demos during his lectures. If you are a visual learner then he is a great professor for you. The class is designed for you to get an A with the assistance of the TA's. There are a ton of resources for you to use.

Loved Dr. V! He's funny and you can tell he really enjoys what he teaches. Readings are a must (reading quizzes), and you have to attend (iClicker quizzes), but if you do all the work it's not hard to get an A. Use the TA lab (and go to your hw labs!). It makes a difference. (I would know, I decided to TA for this class after taking it :) ).

The only reason i show up in class is for the iclicker quiz. His lectures are exactly in the book. He drops a lot of quizzes and some hw assignments. the class content is hard to understand, he is not. the multiple choice tests have some tricky questions, but the essay part is a lot easier. TAs play a huge role, but some are super condescending.

I hated Physical Science, but not because of Dr. V. He loves his subject and teaches well. Be warned- daily iclicker quizzes for attendance. The iclickers are the only reason I showed up. Go to reviews and labs. Daily quizzes before class online, but any answers accepted so pretty easy. Good Luck. I didn't use the textbook, but others did.

Mr. V's class was impossibly difficult. I went in thinking he was a good teacher, and was sorely mistaken. He has iClicker quizzes on his powerpoints that are worth 7% of your grade and gives you no time to answer them. He is hard to understand, partially due to the accent, but also how fast he goes through topics. Also, you must read the textbook

This class is an absolute joke. Dr. V is really funny, but he is an AWFUL teacher. He's  the worst professors I've ever had. If you want to have to study for thirty hours a week and still get blindsided by concepts you never talked about in class on every test then this is the class for you. Lots of hot freshman is the only redeeming quality.

Dr. V is AWESOME. His lectures were amazing. I learned so much from him. He is crystal clear and answers all questions in a very respectful, detailed manner. Super nice guy. Lots of reading, but very enjoyable. Tests are moderately hard--just be sure to study for them, and you'll do fine. A 90% is an A, not an A-.
It was pretty easy, but there was a lot of work. Go to TA reviews if you want to do well on tests

Dr. V is a really funny guy who loves to make science hands-on and entertaining. However, his lectures are usually confusing because he talks too long on topics that aren't needed for the test. You have to rely on the TAs for good test reviews and clear instruction.

Best teach I have had in a LONG time. His teaching style was a breath of fresh air and his energy and attitude towards science was contagious. I would recommend him to anyone. The TA reviews are a MUST, you wont pass with out them. I took the class in the summer so the  lectures were fast paced  2 chapters a day with a midterm every other week.
Awful lecturer. By the end of the semester, there was no point in even going.  BUT if you go to the reviews for the tests you don't have to ready or pay attention and you can still get a good grade.

Funny guy, lectures are entertaining but not super clear. He really cares about his students and incorporates questions students have from reading quizzes in the lectures. I didn't feel like he prepared me super well for tests.. but TA reviews are super helpful!!
This class is tough. His lectures aren't amazing and there are so many tests. The studyingreadingthinking about this class never ends.

The TAs are the best. They're always there to answer questions and tell you what you need to know. Readings are important, even if you just skim them. Reviews are a must. Dr. V is pretty good at explaining.

Dr. V (as he is called) is a great professor. He has a passion for what he teaches and will try to teach it in any way that the students will understand. sometimes he looks silly when he explains his analogies but it is great because it helps us to remember the concepts! He really cares about his students and he is really funny as well!
Dr. V is pretty bomb the lectures are very entertaining and the accent is cool.

Doctor V (as he calls himself) is funny and interesting and truly loves what he teaches. His enthusiasm transfers to his students and he always keeps things dynamic through neat demos that illustrate the lessons really well. I hate science but it was my favorite class of the semester!

Love Dr. V! He manages to make even physical science pretty hilarious. His accent is great and wasn't hard to understand at all. TA labs and reviews are life savers! You have to do the textbook readings and attend class!! Also, if you get a higher grade on the final than you have in the class, you get the final grade.

Doctor V is such a great guy, he's kind, funny, and really knows his stuff and wants you to do well.  Unfortunately he's not the greatest communicator.  I was often more confused after the lecture than when I had read the text.  The TA lab and reviews are a saving grace.  The tests can be confusing but it is possible to do well.

Dr. V was a pretty good teacher. He'd explain concepts very well. Sometimes he'd get off on tangents and I couldn't really tell how what he was saying related to anything we were talking about. But he tells you that you don't need to know any of that. Do the readings, go to class, go to the TA reviews, and use the TA lab and you'll be just fine.

This class isn't very fun, and if you don't have much prior science knowledge you may be overwhelmed. Dr. V. makes it tolerable and explains it decently, but your grade ultimately depends on what they tell you to memorize at the review. The tests are poorly created and the grading is confusing. If Lauren is still a TA, GO TO HER REVIEWS.

Dr. V is hilarious, but I have learned very little from him. He often goes on huge tangents then ends them with "but you don't need to know that." Attend the TA reviews! I learn more in 2 hours than I do in a month of class.

Dr. V is a nice guy but his lectures are very confusing. He goes off on tangents and never gets through all of the slides. I learned more in 2 hour TA review sessions than I did in three weeks of the class

Dr. V is the bomb!  He makes science interesting so you'll never fall asleep in class.  Take this class from him, as his main goal isn't to relay information, rather to help all his students understand.

Best teacher I've ever had. Really entertaining lectures. He made science very simple. The tests definitely aren't easy but if you have any questions they will be clarified. Do the readings, go to class, use the TA Lab and you'll do fine. Best teacher at BYU!
I loved Dr.V's class. I really don't like the subject but thought that he did a great job of explaining physical science. The tests were hard for me.

Dr. V is an excellent teacher. He's a genuinely kind person who cares about his students. He explains things clearly and he's really funny. AWESOME accent, but still easy to understand. Definitely take from him if you can.

Dr. V is an amazing teacher! He is passionate about what he is teaching and his number one goal if for everyone to understand it! I went to him at the beginning of the semester and told him that I was having a hard time and he did everything he could to help me and he has continued helping me! take it from Dr.V.!!!!!! You won't regret it!

The class wasn't too bad. Just make sure you attend so you can receive clicker quiz credit. Go to lab to do your homework, but if you don't like yours, you can go to a different one. Go to as many reviews as you can and then the tests are way easy. As for Dr. V, he was really nice and taught things at an easy yo understand level.

Dr. V was a great teacher!!! He was very helpful with any questions. Lectures are mandatory for doing well on the tests. You have to go to the TA reviews and read the text!!! Do all of this and you will succeed. Again, Great teacher!

I'm not a science person at all and the material isn't my favorite but Dr. V makes it so fun! He's funny and adorable and has the cutest accent! His lectures make the material actually make some sense and his powerpoints are great and available on blackboard. TAKE PS100 FROM HIM! You won't regret it! :)

I am not a science person, but i absolutely loved this class. Dr. V was really good at explaining the material in lecture.  Find the good TA's and go to their review's/ labs.  You'll be golden on the tests if you go to the reviews.

I loved VanHuele! I thought he was hilarious, and I can not get enough of that Belgian accent. I thought he was clear and helpful in lectures, all flared with some fun, but I tend to like to move quickly in science. Overall, I loved the class. Read the textbook and ask questions, and you'll do great. And go to reviews!

Dr. V was very entertaining and very open to student comments.  Even though he is not a member of the Church, he brought interesting insights to the class.  The TAs were extremely helpful--go to the lab!  Even though I am not a science person, I loved the class

Dr V. is from Belgium and has a very awesome accent and fun sense of humor. His demos are very interesting and help you better understand the material. Science has never come easy for me, so my best advice is to read the book. Read the Book! His tests contain many story problems which require you to apply the principles you've learned. Great class!
Great teacher and nice guy. Will do a lot to help students out. Just go to TA labs and do your homework and reading and you'll be fine. Not overly hard.
Dr. V is amazing.  I really didn't want to take Physical Science. However, he made me excited for it. I love going to class every day.  It's so fun!

I LOVED Dr. V! I dreaded taking PS100 but Dr.V got me to actually love going to class! His lectures are hilarious and really easy to understand. The difficulty of the course won't change, but Dr.V helps to make hard concepts easier to understand. I couldn't recommend him more!

Dr V is a great professor. He is willing to change his teaching styles to the desires of the class. Very open to students opinion and feedback.  I loved the demos that he did in class. He also has an awesome accent.
My favorite professor so far! His lessons are interesting and he's very funny. I didn't like physics before taking this class, but he made me love it!
Great teacher... has relevant lectures, is very helpful, cares about his students, and has a sense of humor
Dr. van Huele is in my opinion, definitely the best professor in the physics department. He is helpful yet challenging.
She is amazing! She is really good at praising her students and also requires a lot of them. Be ready to practice outside of class. So worth it

She was very caring, genuine, and such a light. Her dance tests weren't too difficult; however, her final written exam was tricky. She most definitely persuades and inspires her students to do their best in everything.
She is a very sweet women and teaches very well. The class can be difficult because you learn a lot of dances, but you have plenty of time to work on them. It's just a fun environment.

Jeanette is a tough director/teacher but she makes you improve dramatically. She knows her stuff, is good at what she does, and knows how to be kind at the same time. She won't put up with low effort but won't bother you with busy work. Wonderful experience with this woman. Love her!

Okay, when you get to the advanced levels of the Ethnic dance classes, they will lay the smack-down on you.  But Jeanette does it nicely, and she's always willing to help you, individually or as a class.
I love Jeanette! She is an amazing dancer and such a good teacher. She really cares about her students and is SO patient! She's a very sweet person and I loved going to class. :)

Great teacher who cares about her students: as students, as dancers, as people, as children of God. She knows what she's teaching, and knows how to get the results, but by being kind. A great teacher--for people with or without dance talent.
Jeanette is such a sweetheart! She's so creative and a pleasure to work with! I have great respect for her as a teacher and dancer!
Amazing teacher.  Really cares about the students.  One of the most patient teachers I have ever seen.
Jeanette is so fun, and super nice.  She is always willing to help students improve and feel good about themselves.  She is an amazing dancer, and an even better teacher.

I have taken 5 classes from Jeanette so I can safely say that sh is my favorite professor at the university. She is clear, down to earth, and truly cares about her students. Her grading is always fair and she gets to know her students personally. I look up to her so much! I would definitely recommend any class she teaches!
Wonderful person. She went above and beyond in every way. Fair grading, good teacher, loves what she does and made class FUN! Even taught in dutch when we asked her to! :D

Such a cute lady.  She really cares about what you learn and goes out of her way to make sure you've got the steps down and have good technique.  Spends time evaluating each person and giving you really helpful comments.  She's so cute when she dances, too.  Just a lighthearted, helpful person.  I loved her class.
I had Jeanette for Folk Dance (I hope that I have spelled her names correctly).  She was great; I enjoyed the class a lot.  Her testing and grading was fair, and easy, by my estimation.
This class was amazing! The professor truly cares about his students. I learned more about how compassionate living is not just being compassionate towards others, but also towards myself.
Very nice, actually wants to help you grow and learn habits for the rest of your life.

Prof Beecher was amazing. He really took the time to get to know the students and what we learned in this class was really invaluable. I think all students should take this course, it was that good. Highly recommend it to anyone. There arent any tests but activities to do each week, some readings and a 3-4 page reflection paper due at the end.

Professor Beecher was my favorite professor this semester. I took his class on a whim and didn't regret a second of it. Each student feels like he actually cares about who they are, and his assignments actually help you live a more positive life if you're willing to put in the effort to experience them.

I almost never leave reviews for professors, but Mark is the best!! His lectures were always so inspirational and you can tell how much he genuinely loves hearing the thoughts of students in class discussions. He cared less about grades and more about helping everyone find ways to live more positively. Can't recommend him enough!!

I have taken multiple Japanese classes, all from different teachers at BYU since 301, and none of them burnt me out like this one. I had so much to do that I could never properly study for tests and averaged like 65% on every exam. Most of my peers were in the same boat. This class had no objective, just torture.

Peterson Sensei is very nice and gives good explanations on all the readings and relevant info. Basically just do the readings and try your best to learn and use the vocabulary and you will be fine. 1 exam gets dropped so you don't even have to take the final if you don't need to. Don't forget to mark attendance quizzes for fact class

I didn't have too many problems with the class being a return missionary with a good grasp of the language, but if you don't have that foundation I feel like this class would be super hard. Even at my level I struggled with the workload alone, so I can't imagine how difficult it would be to stay caught up if you found those things difficult.

As long as you have a decent understanding of Japanese, you should be fine. Yes, there is a good amount of homework, but it is not difficult in any way. If you show up to class and pay attention, you'll get an A. Also, Peterson sensei is very kind

I'm a bit confused on others frustration in this class. I am an RM, but I knew that not everyone's level in 301 would be perfectly in line with the class. It may be tough, or easy depending on your prior knowledge and humility to just read and learn the stories no what. My speaking skills improved a ton from this class, I thought it was great.

Great professor (5), awful class(1/5). Professor Peterson himself is a great teacher, but the demands that the humanities department places on the 301 classes for languages is absurd and mundane. Learning languages is straightforward, evaluating progress is not. Competency in the course is reliant on knowledge of the textbook and not the language.
He may have the credentials, but he clearly lacks the expertise.”

If there's one thing I've taken out of this class, it's to *never* take another Japanese class at BYU again.
Peterson-sensei's teaching style really didn't work for me.

If you're here for the challenge exam, no one got an A on all, JAP 101.. 202... It's extremely difficult, even for return missionaries. This class wasted my time, tuition, and effort at BYU. Awful experience—don't take it! I hated this class because it's not designed to actually teach Japanese. This isn't a proper Nihongo class.

So much busy work. It feels a little pointless and like you're not learning helpful Japanese. It's kanji heavy and tests are pretty difficult. However, you could get not good grades on the exams and still get an A in the class if you do the rest of the assignments.

It's hard to teach a language. I didn't like that the class got very difficult and kanji-heavy midway through. I did not have the bandwidth for a 4-credit class, and would recommend that you have a strong motivation for Japanese and a lighter course load when you take it. We had 4 TA's rotate in our class at random and that was the WORST!!

Rough class. Don't believe the whole "it'll be so easy as an RM" ish. It isn't easy for anyone. But it will help you keep up your japanese and if you try you will succeed. Peterson sensei cares so much about his students and is fr so kind. I wish he taught all the japanese classes. Attendance is SO mandatory and this class will kill ya but have fun

[non-RM] it is more of a game of guessing what Peterson Sensei is thinking. he gives SO much busy work I feel so overwhelmed and unable to actually learn. I am only learning how to pass the class, not learning Japanese. The material isn't even that hard, but i am struggling :( can't wait to finish this class. he's a nice guy tho

Non-RM here. The class was a lot of work, but an A is achievable. Discussions twice a week are conducted only in Japanese, but you had the discussion prompts beforehand to prepare. To pass the tests, you need to go to midterm and final review days. Without them, you will fail. For other assignments, follow the rubrics closely to get full points.

Peterson sensei is just a really nice and chill professor. He knows A LOT about Japanese and always has an answer for questions related to grammar and vocab. His class is set up in a way to help his student had speaking opportunities which is what students studying Japanese at BYU need. Overall pretty good professor!
His class isn't too hard, but you don't really learn too much, especially for RMs. If you want to just get language credit, it's perfect for you.

Peterson Sensei is great... I am not sure why he doesn't have better reviews on here. If you are an RM, this class will be an absolute breeze for you. If not, it could be pretty difficult. There are so many assignments in this class but the tests are worth almost nothing, you just need to come to class prepared every day and you'll do great.

EVERYTHING you do is graded, so as long as you complete your hw and show up to class you'll do just fine. It's a lot of work and the course is not organized that well in my opinion, but Peterson Sensei is overall really caring and you can tell he is very passionate about teaching Japanese. You're definitely graded more by the TAs though.

JAPAN 301 is a time-intensive class. Expect to spend 10+ hours on the class each week. The grade is divided between many different assignments, so having a bad day won't hurt you too much. Overall, a great class. Like every Japanese class, you will get out of it what you put in. Go to Peterson-sensei and the TA's office hours and ask questions!

I think that most the complaints aren't the fault of Peterson sensei. I think it's the fault of the people over the Japanese program at BYU. The class set up isn't very great and if you have lived in Japan you won't learn much. BUT Peterson sensei is a great professor who is very willing to answer questions and accessible outside of class! 9/10!
Not a great professor. I didn't feel like we were learning anything. It's more of rote memorization and a lot of trying to guess what the professor is thinking.

Expectations surrounding projects are extremely unclear and his grading is wildly inconsistent. The class is comprised of student-led presentations and discussions every time. He fishes for certain answers and penalizes you for having a different opinion.

The class isn't super difficult to get a decent grade in, but I didn't feel like I learned anything outside of the work I had to put into the assignments. Peterson is pretty easygoing, but doesn't really prepare you or give you direction on what you need to do to improve.

There is a lot of work needed for this class. It required a lot of my time, but easy to get an A when I put in the time. If you have a good TA and friends in the class, it's a very fun class to take. The teacher is very easy-going, but I don't think I learned that much from him. It was more from doing the assignments.

4 credits means lots of work. It was mostly completion work, so if you put in the time it's an easy A. Participate in the TA classes. I loved learning Japanese in Japan but didn't care very much for this class. But some love it! The challenge exam credits are great! Peterson Sensei is very easy-going and teaches what's on the tests.

Prof. Peterson is a really easygoing guy, and goes over the textbook pretty thoroughly on his T Th classes. The TA's teach the MWF classes, so your grade is tied much more to their classes. The tests are worth only 20% of your grade, and have 3 sections taken separately. There are midterms every other week, but he drops your lowest scores.

Professor Chadwick is passionate about what he teaches and makes it interesting. There isn't too much homework and he wants everyone to get a good grade. This was my second class with him, 100% would recommend.

Brother Chadwick really understands the gospel and wants his classes to understand it deeply. He makes sure that everything he teaches, assigns as homework, or puts on the final has a purpose. There was never any busy work. The final was completely open source; we could use the scriptures, the recorded lectures, or even just the internet.
Easiest religion class ever.
I'd highly recommend! Amazing Professor!

Only weekly assignments were ~40 pages of reading and a 250 word response on anything you read. Open-note, open literally everything he has published on learning suite for both midterm and final. Interesting class with light workload.

Truly amazing, I will be taking from him again. As long as you take notes during the lectures, you will pass. Hilarious and generously overqualified for this position, you will not go wrong taking this class.

Seriously my favorite professor at BYU so far. He is incredibly knowledgeable about Christianity and just religion in general so it is really cool to be able to ask him quesions and listen to his lectures. 1 midterm and 1 final both with multiple attempts. 250 word reading response every week. I couldn't recommend him more.

Chill class. Exams on learningsuite. Super nice professor who wants everyone to succeed. Gives multiple opporutnities for final and gives extensions for assignments when needed. One midterm and one final. Short writing assignments throughout the semester

Bro. Chadwick is so sweet! This class is quite interesting, and you can tell he loves what he does. He has 2 "text"books, 4 exams, and an SRR due almost every week of 250 words. Going to class, talking notes, and reading the books does matter for a good grade. I found this class interesting, and enjoyed the way Bro. Chadwick teaches. I suggest it!!

If you want an easy, but interesting religion credit, take it from Chadwick. He is the coolest guy, an archeologist and in a band. He kind of just yaps in his lectures, but you can get all of his homework done in class. Not a ton of assignments, just quick 250 word responses, and the exams are so easy if you take notes and do the readings.

If you want an easy religion credit, take a class from Prof Chadwick. He has very simple homework that gives you the test questions. The two tests you take (midterm and final) have 4 takes total that take your highest grade, an easy A. For lectures you mark your own attendance for points, and I mostly ended up doing other homework in the class.

Fact checking every thing he says quickly leads to learning that this man knows absolutely nothing about what he claims to have such broad knowledge about. The bias and personal interpretation that is so prevalent in his “lectures” should not be allowed in a collegiate environment. Being a religion professor should not give leeway from facts.

Prof Chadwick is an engaging lecturer who wants students to succeed. The class has a few exams and readings, but isn't too difficult. I found Unstuck ai really helpful for studying alongside the textbook and lecture notes.
He can get very distracted and content moves slow at times, but if you want an easy religion credit, this is a good one.

This was my second class from him and I loved it! Not too much reading and writing assignments. Pay attention to the lectures and the readings because the tests are on what he says. I loved going to class and I learned a lot about Book of Mormon archaeology. Take this class for a good time!

Really interesting class. Would be better as a lecture series as he is prone to going off on tangents. Attendance is graded but there is an online option is available in a pinch. Tests are open resource and online.

Brother Chadwick is the coolest! He is really old (he even taught my dad) but from that he has a lot of experience and expertise! He is very respectful of the cultures and religions he teaches about, his class isn't too hard, just do the readings and you'll be fine.

This class was focused on the small plates of Nephi through Jerusalem/ancient Israel lenses. It was totally fascinating and really helped me to learn how to think critically about the Book of Mormon. He shares a lot of his opinions, and it was really cool to learn more about the land of Israel and what life was like back then.

Great professor. He doesn't take himself too seriously despite knowing SO much and having tons of experience. His assignments are fun and his tests aren't too hard, as long as you do the readings and pay attention in lecture.
Very good class to take while taking other busy classes, on 300-word essays a week and open book exams that you can do twice.

I loved this class! This has been my favorite religion class at BYU! He is very understanding of students. All of the exams are open note, so you don't need to stress about them. He records his lectures, yet you are expected to be in the class unless you're sick or other reasons, you can Zoom in. Highly recommend!
He's the best religion professor I've had! Hilarious guy and very insightful lectures.

Very kind and interesting lectures, but the tests are extremely hard. They are open note/book, but the questions are so specific that it's really difficult to study for them or have adequate notes. I'm a good test taker, and I got a C on the midterm! There are few assignments, so make sure to do them all. Overall fine and lets you submit late work.

I loved Brother Chadwick! I can tell he loves his job and his students. He wants everyone to succeed. You have to read two books and take an exam on each. Start early, and don't make the same mistake I did reading them all in one week because it can be a lot to digest. But I absolutely loved this class. I wanted to go to lectures! Fun class :)

Loved Prof Chadwick! He has very good lectures! Super funny and caring. Wants to do whatever possible to help you succeed. The exams are a bit hard, but that is just the nature of learning new religions. 4 exams, and a weekly (minus test weeks) 300 word reading response are pretty much the only assignments.

This was a pretty interesting class, it sometimes took a bit to get into the lectures but I learned a lot and Prof. Chadwick is pretty knowledgeable. The tests are not hard at all with a bit of studying, there's also a few writing assignments but they weren't too difficult either. Extra credit opportunities are offered.

Brother Chadwick is so sweet. He knows his stuff! He reminds me of my grandpa :) He'll also make you laugh. He also will give you every chance in the world to succeed (he let us take a midterm 4 times until everyone had 100%). The weekly readings sometimes took forever but it was considerably not bad and the class is a great easy A.

Great class and nice professor. You have to read two novels and take tests on those as well as the lectures. Tests are not too difficult and the assignments are easy. I liked the professor's easygoing attitude and passion for the subject, and I do feel like I learned a lot. He does talk a lot about the Jerusalem center.
Judaism and Islam was my favorite religion class. It wasn't very difficult at all, (just required you to read some books and write the occasional paper). He's hilarious and very intelligent

Professor Chadwick is so laid back. His assignments are really open-ended and he just wants you to be able to engage with the text. It was definitely the easiest class I have taken at BYU! I watched a lot of the lectures online though because the lectures can feel really long. Regardless, I loved the content and how passionate Chadwick was!
You can tell that he truly cares about his students. He posts helpful study guides for some of the tests, use quizlet and other resources to study for others! This really was a wonderful class!

Pretty easy A and I felt like I learned a lot of the basics in this class. He will be the first to say that he isn't a professor by trade so he is pretty different from any other professor at BYU. Worth taking if you are interested in Islam and Judaism but somedays you will leave the class thinking that he taught literally nothing for 50 minutes.

This guy is amazing. If you can take his class please go and take his class. He cares deeply about his students and he is trying to create an area of respect and tolerance. His class is inspirational and if you do the work (which isn't too much) you'll do great. 10/10 would recommend

This class is not about Judaism & Islam- we spent the majority of lectures talking about Mormonism. So shockingly and consistently self-referencing and unacademic. Judaism "texbook" was written by a play-write in the 1950's and is not only outdated but also frequently sexist and racist. Don't take this class if you actually want to learn something.

This class was amazing! Professor Chadwick has such a vast knowledge and love of what he teaches. He has unique experience that really adds to his class. Exams are easy if you study what he tells you. Not a ton of assignemts. Class attendance is a must. Would suggest this class to anyone.

The class was easy, but I learned more about Judaism/Islam in 2 weeks in World Religions than in 4 months in this class. Chadwick might have the worst time management skills on campus. Class felt like a waste of time. Tests can be studied for on Quizlet to avoid the reading. Never knew what to take notes on. Just a wasted opportunity to learn more.

You can tell how much he cares about what he teaches, and he makes you love it too. He gives you plenty of warning on any assignments, and they are not bad at all. There are two books that you read, but you have the whole semester and he is always reminding you. The tests are pretty much exactly what he teaches you. My favorite class this semester!

Great Guy! Really cares about the student. He bases his class mainly on the 4 test grades. He provides interesting and minimal biased analysis on different religions. He also has pretty cool stories too. Definitely one of the best religion classes of the semester. Just make sure to read the books and take notes in class. You'll do good!

Professor Chadwick is HILARIOUS. He's like the grandpa you always wanted and says random things just like a grandpa OUT OF NO WHERE. His best quote, Sorry Im late, but now Im ready to let her rip. His lectures are a bit dry but this class is super easy. If you do the assignment you get 100%. He knows his stuff and is just a nice guy

He spends at least 20 minutes (sometimes 30) at the start of each class by going over what assignments are due, and other random things that he cares to share. Sometimes its nice to have a reminder, but I'm pretty sure he spent more time talking about BYU football than Judiasm or Islam. Its not a super hard class, but it felt like a waste of time

This class is a hidden gem here at BYU. Dr. Chadwick brings the gathering of Israel to life in his lectures and you can tell he has been studying this his whole life. What made this class even better was that he is a lot more focused on you establishing a base for future study, so the assignments and tests aren't hard.

4 memorize-based exams. Regret taking it:( Doing other rel classes would be much easier since I already know the concepts. 2 exams are based on two books you read in your own time. Use flashcards and memorize ALL of the vocabulary. This class it's like taking another language course that aren't gonna do any good in my life. 7 small essays.

I loved this class! Professor Chadwick definitely spent a lot of time on slightly off topic tangents, but I still learned everything I needed to in class. Assignments were easy and he's very clear about what's expected, if sometimes a little late. Overall, I really enjoyed his class
Professor Chadwick is the best! It's clear that he knows a lot about and loves what he teachers. I learned a lot in his class and really enjoyed it. Easy "A" if you use the study guides he provides.

The worst lecturer I've ever seen. I had to teach myself most of the class material through the assigned books. The tests are extremely memorization based. Also, he says he's the most politically conservative professor on campus. Take that as you will.

Dr. Chadwick is awesome! He really knows about Judaism and Islam and has lived in the Middle East for over 20 years. You'll learn so much and he is so respectful of other cultures and beliefs. You definitely need to study for his exams but it's not impossible. Definitely would take his class again!

Professor Chadwick is awesome! He is an amazing storyteller and really knows his stuff. Take his class! He also makes it very doable. If you just put in a little bit of work, then you'll be able to do well in the class.

Professor Chadwick is a great, caring guy. His lectures just aren't terribly engaging. He uses the first 20 minutes of class to go over due dates and pointless administration, then uses the last 30 minutes to ramble about a question that a student asked about something, rarely actually answering the actual question. I don't feel like I learned much

He repeats himself a lot from class to class, but he's really nice and not boring. Take good notes and you'll do fine. Study guides perfectly tell you what will be on the tests. The work is not too time consuming. And Judaism and Islam are a fascinating topic. I've heard from some that not all his info is accurate, but to my understanding it was.

Dr. Chadwick is a great professor who wants his students to succeed. He gave us all the information that we needed to know to pass the tests and succeed. In this class, an A was 96%, which seems really high, but if you put in the work, it's an easy A. I learned a lot and enjoyed most of his lectures. Overall a good experience.

Lectures are a little unorganized, but Chadwick more than makes up for it with his knowledge of the subject. Half the tests are straight from a study guide. I learned a ton about the religions in this class and didn't have to stress about my grade. He's sent out weekly emails since the switch to remote learning which really shows how much he cares.
I can't believe some of the people who have bad-mouthed Chadwick--the man is a saint!! Best religion class (and teacher) ever!

If you want an easy A, take his class. His lectures are long and I found them hard to follow. I liked the material the class covered, but I dreaded going to lectures because they were confusing & slow. When answering questions, he will interpret them how he wants to, which can cause frustration.
I think Professor Chadwick is incredible. His lectures were amazing. I learned so much. HIs knowledge of Islam and christianity is ridiculous.

Prof Chadwick is my FAV, he's so funny and caring. His class is easy as long as you pay attention and read the books. The semester is broken up into Judaism and Islam halves with two exams, and several reading responses in each. Offers extra credit and all tests (four in total) are on learning suite, so that was nice. He has a lot of stories lol

Bro Chadwick has a ton of experience in the middle east and knows a lot about the Muslim and Jewish communities. You'll learn a lot of history! You learn the doctrine of each faith from 2 textbooks (test at the end of each) and the history (incl dates!)from the lectures (2 tests over lecture). A is 96 or higher but lots of extra cred. Loved it!!

This was a pretty cool religion class. You have to read a lot, but the tests aren't too hard if you study. I liked Professor Chadwick, he was a cool guy and interesting teacher. I would recommend this as a good religion class for those extra religion credits.

Professor Chadwick is the best!! He gives so many extra credit opportunities, you really don't need to worry about your grade. Just show up and listen to his lectures. He's so passionate and knows what he's talking about. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Prof. Chadwick knows a lot about what he's teaching, but he's really condescending about it. He'll cut off questions before they're even fully asked. Basically, his way of thinking is the only way of thinking. And if you want an A, you better plan on missing no more than 2 questions on each test. Still learned a lot, but not my favorite atmosphere

I LOVE BROTHER CHADWICK!!!!!!!!!! Survey of Judaism and Islam with him was definitely my favorite class ever. He is so captivating, and as someone who has studied these religions and the Middle East for his whole life, he has so much to say. He is very respectful with how he teaches other religions. Go to class and make sure to read the two books!!
I love Brother Chadwick! He is super understanding about extensions on papers and missed attendance. Tests are super easy and online--just find someone to give you the notes if you missed class.

Prof Chadwick is a stellar professor. I don't usually feel the need to leave reviews, but I had a great time taking his class. Straightforward teaching style, no surprises on the test. Super doable. He makes his lectures fairly light hearted. He's a huge football fan so don't be alarmed when his two minute warning goes off every class haha!

Loved this class from Professor Chadwick! He really cares about Islam and Judaism and teaches it beautifully. There're 4 tests, 2 on books, 2 on lectures. Otherwise points are on attendance and responding to readings. He's a great teacher, and really cares about his students! Only bummer is 96% is an A. If you can answer study guide q's you're good

He really knows what he's talking about, and has real respect for Islam and Judaism. It's not too much work: attendance, 4 midterms, and some reading responses (300 words each, only graded on grammar). A few test questions were kind of unfair though (subjective or outside what we discussed). An A is 96, so this was kind of a problem for me.

Brother Chadwick is amazing! I appreciated the respectful way he discusses other cultures and religions, and I learned a lot. He is a dynamic speaker but also very down-to-earth. You definitely need to study for the tests, but he is clear and fair about what will be on them, so you are set up for success. Two great books for the textbooks! A joy.

So easy!! I took it for global awareness. The tests are all online and they're based on 2 books and then 2 lecture tests. Attend class, read the books before the tests, take notes on them all and youll be totally good. Such an easy A

This course has been my favorite religion class thus far! Professor Chadwick is a spectacular professor that I look forward to hearing from. If you take good notes during class and complete your assignments, you're in a good spot to study for tests and to get an A.

Professor Chadwick is such a great guy. He's had tons of experience in the Middle East and definitely knows what he's talking about. Just do the assignments and you'll be fine. The only hard part about the class is making time to read the two books required. Other than that, be sure to take notes on the lectures, there are 2 exams on class lecture.

I LOVE Jeff Chadwick with my whole heart. His class was super easy, interesting, and inspirational. This class is such a fun treat. Show up, enjoy lecture, read the books he assigns (which are short and informative) and take a couple tests that reflect exactly (!) what we learned in class.. and you're good to go! He is such an amazing person. 10/10

Even though it takes a 96% for an A, it is definitely do-able. Tests are very easy but require straight memorization, don't put it off too much. Also offers extra credit to help out, very little homework.

Half of the test questions are direct quotes from the reading. The other half are straight from his lectures. Attendance is almost a third of the grade. Only real bad thing is the grading scale is 96 for an A. Pretty easy and fun class to take. He does his best to leave his personal opinion out of sensitive discussions and only focus on the history
The 96% required to get an A at first is daunting. It really isn't a hard grade to get. The class is a very good class.

Professor Chadwick is a very experienced and sincere teacher. His lectures are very entertaining. Judaism is taught for first half of semester, and Islam is taught for second half. The content/homework is VERY well organized and in my opinion, entertaining. Class is not heavy at all on busy work, but there is reading and exams on those readings.

Loved prof Chadwick as a person. Lectures could feel long but usually very interesting. He teaches religion very differently and I loved what we learned about because it wasn't like any other class. An A is a 96 though and mainly dependent on the midterm/final. Weekly hw and a few papers don't count for much.

He is a great lecturer, gives easy homework, study guides, and easy tests. You still learn lots of spiritually and intellectually enlarging things. He is everything you came to this school to experience.

Professor Chadwick is an amazing teacher. His lectures are entertaining and hilarious. His class is not hard, but filled with good information. I valued every class I went to and I'm looking to take a class from him again. His tests are very easy and he teaches you to keep an open mind.

Bro. Chadwick was a good professor. I enjoyed hearing his take on Judaism and Islam. The 96% cutoff for an A was worrisome at first, but it's pretty doable if you study well enough for the tests. His lectures were pretty interesting, and I liked the readings he selected. I found the class to be an overall enjoyable experience.

Chadwick loves Judaism, so it's hard to stomach how clearly he looks down on Islam 2nd term. Instead of teaching the 5 pillars of Islam, he spends a day trying to convince you "mozlem" is an ok pronounciation of Muslim, despite the fact the book he assigns says that's incorrect. Do the book study guides & memorize dates & you'll pull the 96% A.

This class is a great class if you are interested in foreign religions. I learned a lot and Professor Chadwick is great teacher. You need a 96% for an A, but there are only four tests and six short write ups that are all pretty easy. If you go to class and listen you should get an easy A and learn a lot.

Prof. Chadwick is very lecture heavy. He never gets to all the material because he takes so much time talking about Jerusalem and Jewish culture. He is very opinionated and you are tested on how he teaches things not necessarily how youve read it elsewhere. This class was more of a history class than a religion class.

He's a way cool dude. Not much work outside of class and he does a really good job preparing you for the tests. The tests are online so you don't even need to go to the testing center, which is fabulous. Also, you pretty much get full points on all essays just for turning them in on time.

This is definitely a hard class for the credit you get. Two books of reading, and prior knowledge of some Hebrew or Jewish history definitely would help. I took this as a Freshman and I got a higher grade in Chem 105 than I did in this religion class. Just be aware you're in for the long haul when you take up for this. But interesting material!
He really knows his stuff and really likes to talk. We had a lot of good class discussions. The course itself isn't hard, just make sure you don't wait until the last second to read the texts.

Entertaining professor with encyclopedic knowledge of Judaism and Islam.  Attendance mandatory.  Judaism book is great, Islam book is kinda dry.  Grading scale is wack - 96% is an A.  Six 300-word write-ups on articles assigned.  4 exams, closed book.  Study guides he gives are great, though.  Enjoyable class overall.

I enjoyed this class.  His grading scale is ridiculous, 96% for an A.  But it is manageable if you do well on his tests.  Just take notes on everything for the power points because they'll be on the test.  He doesn't post slides on learning suite.  Attendance is mandatory.  2 small books to read during semester.  4 tests.  Good class overall!

Boy oh boy Professor Chadwick was great. In addition to being hilarious and beyond entertaining, I learned so much about the Jewish and Islamic faiths. This is information which I feel is necessary in this day in age.

Takes 96 percent to get an A. You can only miss 12/300 points in the entire class. The tests are pretty straightforward, though. Be sure to read the books early and carefully and then record/re-listen to the lectures. You definitely have to study, but if you work hard (or have a strong background in Judaism/Islam) then you can get an A.

Really helpful and knowledgeable about the New Testament. If you're looking for a class where you can learn a lot, and not have to put in an overwhelming amount of time or effort, this is the class for you.

You are required to read two books throughout the semester. An exam is given for each. The other tests consist of lecture material. His class is not very entertaining. There are assignment due throughout the semester, but they are pretty easy.
The book tests are easy. Watch out for the second test though on the in class content. It's a toughy. Great teacher though. Cares about educating the students. A lot.

Professor Chadwick is absolutely fantastic. If you go to class and read the books and study, you will receive an A. you do have to put work into it, but it is easy to receive a good grade if you are willing to put in the work. He's a fantastic, non-biased teacher and I love him. I absolutely recommend taking this or ANY class from him.

Going to lecture is like getting to watch your favorite TV show every week.  Prof. Chadwick is witty, funny, deeply knowledgeable, sensitive, tolerant and outgoing.  The course itself is remarkably well-organized, always relevant, as is the testing.  Moreover, he succeeds at teaching potentially controversial ideas non-controversially.
Very enthusiastic about Judaism! His lectures don't seem to do much with what we're tested on, but it's still a pretty interesting class.

Professor Chadwick is a very eccentric man, which makes his classes amusing as well as interesting. His class is incredibly easy and the tests are all matching, so as long as you learn vocab, you can easily ace the tests.

My eyes came out of this class with a whole new understanding of the Jewish religion and culture.  I of course took the course where he is most expert in. I don't know what kind of teacher he is while not teaching this class but it was amazing!  I deeply appreciate this once a week class. I learned so much. You come out of this class remembering.

The tests are harder than you think. They are all 100 questions and all matching. The test is mostly vocabulary terms and definitions including dates and important events and leaders. Brother Chadwick is very knowledgeable and a funny guy. But keep in mind the tests are a large part of your overall grade.

I didn't like this class. Bro. Chadwick is really biased in his opinions, appears to be teaching false doctrine half the time, and always insists that he is right. He stutters and mumbles the whole time so sitting in class was sooo annoying. Nice guy, but not good at teaching.

Best. Professor. Ever.  Chadwick's class really changed my semester.  The grading process is easy and clear, but you still learn a ton.  He is an anthropologist and lives in Jerusalem part of the year, and his insights were incredible.  I will be taking more classes from him!

Rel 351 with Chadwick is an amazing class! Bro. Chadwick is brilliant, engaging, and straightforward. I highly enjoyed learning from him every class. The tests are all vocabulary, so know every term from the slides and every other word he says to review from the book. Inspiring professor. He loves the subject and loves teaching. Highly recommended.

If you're looking for an easy A, then you've found your guy.  Reading and weekly summaries of your reading are required.  The tests are multiple choice and come straight out of the handouts he gives.  Warning: He's a little bit crazy.  This is not as much of a spiritual class as it is a learn all these crazy OPINIONS about Christ and his life.

Overall, the class is easy and fun. Chadwick manages to keep lessons flowing, and the hour passes quickly. Midterms and finals are easy multiple choice, and homework is a 300 page summary each week over a given chapter or article. Expect only an hour of homework a week.

I absolutely LOVE Chaddy! He taught at the Jerusalem Center, so I got to know him personally.  He is SO knowledgeable about all things Jewish, Israeli, archaeological, etc.  Sometimes he has a bit of an ego ;) but justifiably so! He'd make up songs to help us remember things and dress up like Indiana Jones-- SO funny, wonderful man. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Professor Chadwick is little eccentric, but I love it. He really knows what he's talking about, and I really appreciated the way he taught - it was entertaining at the same time as being very instructive. I really learned a lot in his class.

Great class to fill a religion requirement and Global awareness GE. Chadwick is super passionate about the subject and a great guy. Read the textbook, do the weekly assignments, go to class, memorize tons of terms and you will get an A. I would recommend him for sure.

I love Bro. Chadwick! Probably the best professor I've ever had. Because of his incredible knowledge, his lectures are very interesting and go in depth of the context surrounding events during Christ's ministry. You only have to write a couple short papers and do daily chapter summaries. Tests are rediculously easy. The study guide was the final!
great informative class. not a lot of homework. great background to have, enlightens understanding of Old and New Testaments. he has genuine experience to back it up.

I found this class fascinating. I enjoy learning from life experience and not just from text books.  He is funny and slips inside jokes into his lectures and tests. There is loads of gospel backing to his lessons. If you don't see that, then you are not paying attention. I'd take any class taught by him.

Amazing! World Survey of Religions could not have been better. Prof.Chadwick is amazing and class isn't hard. You turn in a weekly journal of 2 paragraphs about a weekly reading. That's it. You can actually sit in class with no worries (unless you don't do the assignments-which are simple) and enjoy the Spirit.

He's a great professor- super funny and extremely knowledgeable. He's very passionate about the subject matter and has a lot of first-hand knowledge about it, as well. He wants you to do well and will help you if you put forth the effort.  His tests are more difficult than I expected, but not impossible. Excellent class, and an excellent professor.

Bro. Chadwick is a facinating teacher--take world religions from him!  It's a great class--however, his tests don't follow his study guides so even if you have the study guide memorized, you won't necessarily do well on the test.  Just know the chapters perfectly!  He's a helpful and well-read teacher.

I took REL211 from Chadwick, and I absolutely loved it. It took a practical look at the life of Christ, and his teachings. It definitely strengthened my testimony by learning about his life on earth really was. He's a wonderful guy, he's funny, and he keeps the class entertaining. Take him if you can!

He's one of those teachers everyone has to have!! Absolute best teacher, he makes class really fun and interactive and spends more time answering your questions as opposed to lecturing. He gives you the answers to every test so if you make any sort of effort it's an easy A. He's been accused of singlehandedly inflating grades at BYU

Chadwick is an incompetent teacher, in my opinion. He tries to make up for it, by making his tests very easy, but there was almost no set schedule, his lectures are disjointed, he acts like a know it all, and yet very little of what he taught had gospel backing.

Nice guy, but not very clear on certain concepts.  Tests were all matching, but he hands out the study guide only the day before the tests.  Plus, a lot of terms on the test are not on the study guide.  He's definitely passionate about the subject.

I loved professor Chadwick! To some people he may come across a little "know-it-all-ish", but that is because he really does know a ton! His experiences as an Archaeologist really makes the Book of Mormon come alive!! He's way chill about attendance and understands that life happens. I'd take any class from him.

His tests were all matching about different things that the book covers and that he covered in class.  Doesn't really explain the concepts very well adn you could get through teh class cramming for the tests all the concepts in the book and never going to class.

I loved this class! My friend told me to take it, but I was skeptical.  He blew me away!  You come out understanding heritage, history, and present times and how they relate to your life.  Take every class you can from him! Great tests, little HW, and class are discussion. He's the best!!!  He loves to teach, and you won't want to miss a day!
Prof. Chadwick is amazing! I learned so much in his class. He loves the students and what he teaches. His tests are way easy, just do the study guides. Take all the religion classes you can from him.
Prof. Chadwick is a great teacher. He loves the subject and makes it very interesting. His tests are not bad if you study your notes.

Great professor. Easy class for sure. One midterm and a final, all multiple choice. Sure, you had one assignment due every week, but it was an email response to the chapter you read. Extra points at the end for attending class. Go to class, read the chapters, and you'll get an A.

Brother Chadwick made a pretty dreary subject very interesting, and tells you exactly what you need to know on the exams, making his class easy as long as you do the homework assignments.  2 very short very easy papers, and you have the perfect class! I am taking every class I can with him for the rest of my BYU career.
This guy is really not as good as people say.  I took his class based on these ratings.  He's fairly easy but don't think you can slack.  I didn't think he was insightful at all.

He is a very interesting lecturer. He knows his stuff about the religions of the world. His tests aren't bad. They are multiple choice. You get one point a day for attendance. The only homework is a 500 word summary of a reading once a week. Not too bad at all.

THE BEST RELIGION PROFESSOR ON CAMPUS! ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS PERIOD! You'll learn more than you think. You won't be able to stop thinking about his lessons. Take both REL A 211 and REL C 351. Also take his Judaism class. You won't regret it!

let me put it plainly.  IF YOU WANT TO LEARN SOMETHING NEW, TAKE THIS CLASS.  He starts a little slow (took us 3 weeks to get past the nativity), but you learn a LOT of new material every day.  Test are only hard in proportion to class topics ignored

HE HAS INSPIRED ME TO GO TO THE JERUSALEM CENTER!!! He's such and awesome teacher! He's basically a mormon rabbi :) He's funny too! He knows what he's talking about. His midterm was VERY easy...I got a 98% on it. Take this class!!!!!!

Professor Chadwick loves the subject (Judaism and the Gospel) and has had experience living in Jerusalem.  He knows what he's talking about and, though he sometimes has opinions that other religion professors might not agree with, he doesn't force the students to share his opinions.
His tests are in a format that is ridiculously hard. It's like he is trying to trick you. Plus he gets side tracked in class a lot so I think there are things he thinks he has taught, but he hasn't.
Taught stuff you can't get from anyone else, the most amazing religion teacher ever. Tests were fairly difficult but very reasonable. TAKE THIS CLASS

Jeff Chadwick honestly loves what he does, which makes the class more enjoyable.  He is so religiously open-minded, sometimes I wonder which religion he's actually practicing (that was a joke).  I reccommend him whether you need religion credit or not.
Chadwick is the man.  He can answer any question you have about the New Test.  Howework is easy tests are open scripture, yet I learned more in this religion class than most.  Take him. He is great.

I loved this class. Brother Chadwick knows his stuff and classes were always interesting. 1 page reading responses every week, but only on one chapter. Yu get attendance points. the test is matching and multiple choice.

Brother Chadwick was awesome! He was so interesting. I had him in the Spring and the 2 hours flew by! His tests aren't that hard and he lived in Israel and knows Hebrew. He taught me things that were so interesting. I would definetly take a class from him again. One of my favorite classes. I definetly recommend him.
Very interesting.  Easy East Tests.  I got 100% on the midterm and 98% on the final.  This class provides a good background of judaism to our mormon views.

Nice guy, interesting class. Fairly easy and doesn't require much work. He really knows his stuff (sometimes he came across as a tad arrogant) and I enjoyed his lectures. I definitely recommend his class.
Easy class and great teacher.  I usually struggle with religion classes but this was cake.  Just copy all the notes into your scriptures and you will do great on the tests cause you can use them.

Just a great class. The teacher was great and very funny. Nothing hard about it. Very interesting insights to the 2nd half of the New Testament that I have never heard anywhere else. Highly Recommended. You won't regret it!

I really enjoyed this class. It was VERY interesting. Bro. Chadwick was a VERY good teacher. His notes were very organized and easy to understand. His tests are matching and mainly vocabulary. This class does require a bit of memorization, but it's not bad. Overall, really good professor and class.

I loved Professor Chadwick! His knowledge of other reglions was impressive and his classes were fun. I had the lecture at 8 am and I still enjoyed it. There is a lot of information to learn for the test but if you study for them you will be fine. Great class!
A one credit class does not need such tedious midterms and finals. It is semi interesting, however it is pretty much straight lecture, rarely any class discussion. Meh.

This is a lot harder than a 1 credit class should be. Unless you are really interested in learning about the history of the Jews (not modern), then don't take this and take a religion class where you won't fall asleep.
Such a good class!!! He is such a good teacher and I swear he practically is a Jew. I loved this class! Class is very easy, and yet SO interesting and I learned so much!
My favorite religion teacher on campus by far.  Learned a ton about the 4 gospels from him.  Take him if you get the chance.
This guy is HI-larious! He brought the NT into an entire new light for me. It was sooooo interesting. He is very clear, I found it very relaxing to simply sit back and enjoy his lectures.

Good class and i learned alot, however it is nearly impossible to get an A at 96 precent.  The final was difficult and i dont understand where he pulled some of the questions from, other than that it was one of my best classes i've taken at byu

Take this class!  It's one credit and so easy.  The tests are matching and not bad at all.  You have to write a short essay every week, but they're not graded.  This guy knows his stuff, and I thought the class was really interesting.  I'm looking forward to taking his world religions class.
He is an amazing teacher!!! You learn so much from this class because the love he has for the Jewish people shines through in his teaching.  The tests are super easy if you do the reading.

Amazing. His knowledge of the jewish religion is incredible. And that he can tie it into the gospel is unbelieveable. I really, really liked his class and him. For anyone even slightly interested in learning the connection between Mormons and Jews, I highly recommend this class.
Very interesting class, I learned a ton. The tests were cake if you studied for them. I strongly recommend the class and the teacher.
Class is very interesting and you learn a lot of useful information.  Tests are all matching and are mostly based on vocabulary.  Easy class.
FAN-FREAKIN-TASTIC.  That's all I have to say.

Bro. Chadwick is such an awesome teacher!! You learn a ton about other religions, and he helps you appreciate them. He also compares them to the gospel, and you can tell that even though he is so interested in other religions, he has an unshakable testimony in the gospel. Great class and teacher!!
Great Class.  I learned a lot.  Not hard.  He knows what he's talking about.  Used to do the Jerusalem Center.  I recomend the class.
Great teacher.  Teaches an interesting viewpoint.  Tests not that bad.  Pay attention in lectures and ask question and you'll do well.
Great Prof!  I loved the class, and learned tons about other religions!  CAn't be beat!
No Comments

He teaches you so much in a semester, but makes learning fun. I was always excited to go to this class. His tests are straightforward, and you know what to expect beforehand. I can't wait to take another class from him.
Quite a few quizzes and like 3 exams as well as some projects throughout the semester but not bad. some math but it is doable. you need a ti-84 calc.
Absolutely loved taking a class from Jeff!
good class
Pretty easy class with useful information

Easy and useful class but the lectures can be a bit slow. Also the grading can be unforgiving for such an easy class. I accidentally submitted a project a day late and lost 5% of my whole class grade.
This class is pretty easy, there are lots of assignments but nothing hard. Lecture can be boring but the information is useful.

Jeff is a great professor who is very knowledgeable about finances. Pay attention to the slides and do the readings, or you will not do well on the exams. They are lecture and reading-heavy.  Overall, a great class with lots of applicable concepts.
Awesome class!
Simply put: the GOAT

Brother Dew has a great class that encourages learning about financial strategies and spirituality. Get ready to talk to your neighbor a lot. There are 3 tests, weekly journals, attendance quizzes, and some other assignments in between. They are all graded easily. Go to class to get the link to the slides, that is the biggest help on the test.

If you feel like you have a good grasp of basic finances, don't take this class. He couldn't answer questions that weren't basic. Doesn't accept late work, even for partial credit. No extra credit, no grace period, inconsistent due dates, unwilling to work with you. Good guy with good intentions, just not a great professor.

Bro Dew is a great teacher! He is very knowledgeable in these topics and teaches them in an accessible way. The class itself is very easy, and nothing is graded harshly. I think this is a great class for those just interested in learning more about finances. Everything that he teaches is very practical and helpful in the real world.

Professor Dew was nice but probably one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. Found myself fighting to stay awake or off of clash everyday. Easy material to understand, and not much to worry about. He does focus mostly on the spiritual aspect of finance which can be helpful and interesting. Lots of filler assignments, but way easy general.

Professor Dew is a dawg and I would recommend taking SFL 260 from him if you want an easy GE math credit.  There isn't much math at all in this class and the assignments are straightforward and engaging.  I highly recommend SFL 260 for those who don't like math from Professor Dew.
One of my favorite professors! His class was very easy and he genuinely cares about his students. I made sure to give him the best review on the semester student ratings.

Brother Dew was such a good professor, and I really enjoyed his class. It was not hard to get an A as long as you go to class and study for the tests. He has links to the slideshow from the day if you come to class. TAs give good reviews. There aren't a ton of assignments, and the most important thing to focus on is the tests. I learned a lot!
I thoroughly enjoyed taking Family Finance from Brother Dew. Very applicable content, and easy to get an A.

Brother Dew does great at making finances seem less scary and more manageable. The class is mostly lectures, readings, tests, and exams, with a few assignments. I learned a whole lot in this class and now I feel a lot more confident. His lectures are funny. He also includes the Savior and the Gospel into his teaching a lot, which I appreciated.

Brother Dew is very relaxed and he encourages asking questions so that everyone can best understand finance. Overall, it was an easy class, but it was helpful for a very basic/broad overview of finance and "adulting"

Brother Dew cares, he makes sense, and I can tell taking this class will help me later in life. I would 100% recommend him as a professor and as an excellent person. I honestly don't know how someone could dislike his class. Some problems with students cheating, he will catch you. Be nice, don't cheat :)

Professor Dew is a great teacher. He is passionate and good at explaining financial concepts. There were a lot of long lectures where he mostly read off of slides and bullet points but I think that's just the nature of the subject. He is very knowledgeable and cares about his students. His tests are alright, but definitely go to the lectures.

This class was very enlightening and not difficult at all. The things you will learn will be very beneficial for your life. He connects financial strategies to gospel doctrines and gives you opportunities to apply the strategies to your own financial situations. Overall great option for this credit!

This was an extremely easy class with no exams. However, I did still learn a lot. It's basically a class where you can take what you want out of it. Prof Dew has occasional attendance quizzes, but not every class. He's very understanding, and it's an incredibly easy A. It's honestly worthwhile to take to learn the material too.

Professor/Brother Dew is fun, relatable, and easy to listen to and understand.
He is a teacher that is willing to look foolish to make students more comfortable and endorses light-hearted teasing.
It would be fun if we had a button that we could buzz whenever he had any slip ups like when he called the Deathly Hallows the Lord of the Rings.

Brother Dew is a funny guy. Taking his SFL 260 class was super interesting, and I learned a lot. As long as you put half a thought into any of the few quizzes and assignments there actually are, it's a free A. I would encourage you take the class at some point in your life.

Professor Dew is so kind and taught the content with the spirit and so much love. I enjoyed the content so much and will take what I've learned into my life. TA's are very helpful for the assignments and papers and are so kind and willing to help at all times! Professor Dew's testimony alone is so remarkable and was the main reason I went to class
Dew was a good professor. He knew what he was talking about in his lectures. I like how open he is to question, even during the lecture. He even matches his outfits to his slides sometimes.

Brother Dew and SFL 260 are awesome. Super applicable to the real world. There are no exams, but I found myself not paying attention in class because I wasn't being tested on the material, but it's an easy class to pass. Brother Dew is super nice and is very knowledgeable. Would recommend to anyone, especially if you know nothing about money

Brother Dew is so chill. He answers lots of questions in lecture and just really wants you to learn. No exams, only online quizzes. Need some basic calculator skills but they really teach you everything you need to know. The textbook and he gives it to you on learning suite.

Professor Dew is the best. He teaches life applicable things and keeps it simple. I learned so much in his class and would recommend to anyone who is looking to learn about finance. I will use what he taught me throughout my life. He is also a very understanding and caring professor who understands the craziness of college life. 10/10 RECOMMENDED

Lots of busy work, but super nice guy. Just not very accommodating with deadlines. NO EXAMS including NO FINAL. Just a short essay on how your financial views have changed. Easy class, interesting lectures. Definitely learned a lot.

Class is very easy. There are little assignments and I found the class to be very boring. I had a really hard time going to class each week. It almost felt like more of a religion class to me. No exams, but few assignments worth a lot of your grade. The guy is really nice and caring, but very strict about assignment deadlines.

Brother Dew is one of my favorite professors. He is so kind and teaches very simply. There is little to no homework and NO EXAMS which is the best. Take family finance from him and you won't regret it!

This man is so precious. He is so kind and helpful. His class is quite easy if you just go to the lab days which he labels but I truly enjoyed going to class even though you didn't have to. If you are looking for an easy A with a great teacher and fun topics...take this claaaaaaass.

He was the BEST!!! I enjoyed his lectures and he tied everything back to real life and the gospel! If you do the assignments you can easily get 100% and learn a lot! He was very entertaining and he reminds me of Luke Skywalker. The only thing is that sometimes he had guest speakers who were not as interesting as him. TAKE IT FROM BROTHER DEW!!

This class was really easy. That said, if you learn better when things are challenging take it from another professor. If you learn better without the pressure of tests then take it from Bro. Dew. I was grateful to have this class to balance out my semester but sometimes I struggled to pay attention bc I knew I wouldn't be tested on the material

I absolutely love Brother Dew. He is goofy and kind and gives fantastic lectures. I recommend taking this class if you really do want to get something out of it. it is not a hard course and the quizzes are not crazy challenging. Brother Dew was very inspiring and was great about teaching information that is needed in life. I miss the class already!

Brother Dew cares about his students, but I'm less convinced he cares about the material. When he talks about things he is passionate about he is engaging, but at other times lectures can feel like a bit of a drag. Easy and extremely useful class however.

No exams in this class, Dr. Dew is a good teacher, but the class is a lot of doctrine based. You still get a lot of financial literacy and knowledge though. Not a very hard class overall, easy to get an A or B.

It is very doctrine-based, but you learn so many principles that are important financially. There were four quizzes, and the final was a 3-page essay (easy). A few assignments are passed/fail (you get one redo). (not that hard) You get essential things out of this class if you participate, read, and pay attention! TAs are also very helpful!

Easiest GE ever. He focuses more on change and growth as a human than he does making us do assignments and tests. He knows a lot too, and is passionate on what he teaches. Overall, super nice professor and a very easy class.

I barely went to class and got a 99%. No tests, one paper (that is super easy), and 4 quizzes. If you just go to the class that specify as labs before each quiz you will get an easy 100% on them. You are able to redo the assignments that are worth quite a bit of points so you can also get a 100% on those as well. Easiest class of my life.

Great class! Obvious that he cares about you and what you learn. Had a few weekly assignments, a few quizzes that he basically walks you through. There is a textbook and some other readings, but all free. Attendance/readings were self-reported.

A few quizzes, zero exams, very easy class. He knows his stuff, and I really try to care, but the material feels so bland.
