Regardless I would recommend this class because it's so practical for people who know nothing about money. Labs are helpful for quizzes, but otherwise lectures can feel redundant. His answer to most questions is, "it depends."

Brother Dew is a really sweet guy, but not my favorite professor. His lecture style is not very engaging at all. The entire first unit isn't even about family theories, and it was hard to connect. It's not hard to get a good grade, you don't even really need to show up if you don't want to. Easy grade, but a little boring and a little monotonous

He is an expert and I would recommend any class with him. This class could be one to blow off but you get what you put into it. He was super caring and invested in each person succeeding long past the class.

Amazing class and he's such a good teacher! Clearly explains concepts. Read the PDF textbook cause it teaches you so much for the future. The homework can be complicated, but having the right calculator helps a ton. His lectures can be dry, but they have a lot of interesting concepts that kept my attention.

Pretty easy, a few dumb mistakes cost me the A. No exams, and the readings were helpful and fairly interesting. Some lectures seemed redundant and could have been shorter. All in all, class was pretty good.

This class was super easy. I learned quite a bit without having a lot of homework. Most reading was pretty easy and not very long, but the lectures were pretty dry. I felt like the info that lasted a few class periods could have been summed up in about 30-40 minutes. Super easy class though.

If your looking for an easy A this is the class for you! His a kinda goofy guy which leads to some fun stories during his lectures. He doesn't give any exam but does have pass fail assignments. He walks through the assignment in class and tells you everything you need to do to get credit plus gives you multiple attempts if you missed something.

There are pass/fail assignments. If you fail, you get two more attempts. The assignments were actually really easy. There are no tests. He wants you to learn what you want to learn about financial literacy. While this isn't a required class, I highly recommend taking this class to know how be financially literate (ex: buying a house).

I love Brother Dew. He stopped giving exams which really helped me learn better. Without the stress of exams, I could hyper fixate on the topics I needed advice on while not learning things I didn't need. It was a super easy A and I learned so much about finances.

This class is very easy, Professor Dew recently stopped giving exams. The class is graded off assignments that take very little time. It's a very useful class if you don't know anything about finances! But if you already know about things like mortgages and credit scores then you will be really bored in the class.

One of the best professors at BYU for sure!! He explains things clearly and simply. He cares a lot more about your learning than giving hard tests or assignments. Very easy to get an A. You will learn things that will bless you for the rest of your life! He is the nicest guy and will help you in any way you need. Definitely recommend!

Amazing teacher, pretty laid back class! Lectures always go by quickly and he makes it easy to understand financial principles. You don't have to have a spouse for this class to relate to you. There are only a few assignments that are graded on a pass/fail basis because there are no tests. It's easy and informational; totally recommend this class!

This class was quite easy, and Professor Dew is a really nice guy and a good teacher. I sometimes found lectures a little bit slow, but they were always still interesting. My only real complaint is that the quizzes, which he did not write himself, sometimes didn't match up with what we talked about in class. I would recommend this class!

This class wasn't always the most engaging, but I'm glad I took it anyway! Dr. Dew is such a genuine, caring professor and he truly wishes his students the best. I had a friend take it online from a different professor and had a negative experience in the class. This class teaches principles I want to apply later in life and I liked Dr. Dew!

If you're thinking about SFL 260, take it online. The in person version is very boring and long. This class format would be so much better online. Dew is a decent professor, he knows his stuff. The class just talks way too much about the gospel for a family finance class. There is like only one homework assignment each month so good and bad.

Professor Dew is a good guy and good teacher. If you study and use the examples from reviews in class to prep for the tests you'll be fine. Assignments were easy. He yawns constantly during lectures but you can't really blame him, the material is boring. Helpful class to take, I recommend.

Professor Dew is very nice and know his stuff. He is sometimes absent-minded, so make sure to ask for clarification if he contradicts himself. The class is very laid back and almost relaxing. I still learned a lot about finances though.

I loved Bro. Dew! Great secular and spiritual approach to finances. The textbook is on learning suite, open note open-book quizzes, tests are in the testing center, based on book and lectures. He provides a link to lecture PPT during the lecture. Bro. Dew was very well-spoken and knowledgable about this subject and he clearly explained all the math

Ok, I LOVED this class, the content is so helpful. Brother Dew was a little bit harder of a professor though. He just seemed to not super care about the class, he was very vague on expectations. Assignments are automatically docked half the points if turned in late, and he doesn't communicate this. He also will not remind you about assignments.

As the semester went on I felt like Professor Dew cared less about the class. He told us he loved questions, but he would never really answer them that made me feel like I could ask in class. He yawns so much-like enough for everyone to notice that he yawns a lot.

This is a boring but good class. You learn a lot of good information that applies to the real world. Do not turn in assignments late because you won't receive credit. Also the TA Gaby is horrible. She is super rude, and unacomadating, even if you are extremely ill in the hospital with a note from the emergency room. Professor Dew is great though

Professor Dew loves his subject, but is pretty dry otherwise. I had heard lots of good things about this class and definitely came away with things I am grateful for, but felt the class took alot of time to cover things that could have been covered more simply.

Make sure you do all assignments on time in this class - you get docked 50% for late assignments even if they're turned in the next morning. I emailed him about the dent this policy had on my grade he said he couldn't change it because it would be unfair to the other students. But don't let that keep you from taking the class! Professor Dew is rad

I took Family Finance (SFL260) and it was awesome. I learned so much from this class. You can learn everything from the lectures and don't need the textbook. He's a wonderful person and is great at explaining concepts. I enjoyed his assignments and was impressed with his devotion to actually having us learn the stuff.
Brother Dew is an amazing professor who looks at all sides of an argument and helps his students to know how to make their own choices.

Brother Dew is INCREDIBLE! He is so kind, accommodating, and really passionate about what he teaches. I learned so much from this class and walked away from class every day feeling uplifted and wanting to be better. If you have the chance to take a class from him DO IT!

Bro Dew is great! His lectures are inspiring and I learned SO much about finances Now I feel like an actual adult. You'll want the textbook, it's cheap too. He focuses on gospel principles and connects them to what we're learning. The assignments are easy and have clear criteria. Don't skip class if you want the lecture slides. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!

Dr Dew is quirky and fun. The lectures and math are easy to understand, and he doesn't hesitate to take questions or extend lessons. The class discussions are pretty cool, too. Overall, SFL 260 was just a great class to take. I highly recommend!

Brother Dew genuinely cares about your success and understanding of the principles he teaches. I didn't know anything about finances when I started this class, but he explained things in such a simple way that made sense, which is important when teaching life skills. The assignments are easy to do.

A very easy class in my opinion. I learned a lot from the later units. Brother Dew is great, but I don't think I would consider him or the class amazing by any means. If you need a buffer class for a hard semester and want to learn about finance, it's a good way to go. Tests are pretty easy, just read the directions on the assignments!

Everyone dreads this class but I honestly don't see why. It's actually really interesting! Pay attention in class and do the readings and you will do just fine. The tests are really easy. Professor Dew wants you to succeed, and he will help you out if you need it. If you have to take this class, I'd recommend Professor Dew.

Brother Dew is fantastic! Great person. I loved his class. Engaging and learn alot. It's a 3 is because of the tests. You need to study for those but they are totally doable. Study and you'll be fine. He prepares you well. The rest is easy A as long as you follow instructions on assignments. Loved the way the gospel is incorporated into the class!

Brother Dew is a great professor. I learned a lot from his class. He shared a lot of personal examples/stories which I feel like is very beneficial especially in a finance class. I also loved how he related a lot of principles of finance to the gospel. We talked a lot about how being good financial stewards can increase spirituality.

Fun class to learn about finances. All material was easy to understand in lectures. Tests are always multiple choice, and based off the readings and the lectures, so it is important to attend class everynow and then. Super fun class tho, and he gives a lot of class time to understanding the math parts of the class.

If you've done the reading, you're good. He won't cover anything new in lecture, and you aren't graded on attendance. Lab days, on the other hand, are important for doing well in the quizzes and tests. If you just care about the grade, you can skip class. If you want advice on how stuff applies to your life, go to class and ask him questions.

He is great! There are a few assignments, 2 tests, and a double unit final. The assignments are focused and simple. He is motivated to do things the best way and is open to feedback and change. He is relatable, engaging, and understanding. I really enjoyed the course!

I've never been so inspired by a teacher before. Family finance is a hard subject but he did an awesome job teaching it and showing how it applied to us personally. He's very much a dad figure, and is easy to be around. I went from knowing nothing about money to finally feeling like an adult. This class inspired me to switch to the SFL major.
He is a great teacher and his lectures help break down this information so that it is understandable. He is very down to earth and has made this one of my favorite classes that I have taken.

Dr. Dew is great. SFL 260 is a tough course, but he made it doable. He is friendly and loves what he does. His tests aren't bad, study for them and you'll do just fine. I relied pretty heavily on the math lab, as math concepts were only briefly touched on during class. He's really easy going; take him if you're looking for a finance class!

This class is an easy A if you actually do the assignments well and study for the tests. He gives you the lecture slides in class, so if you want those you have to go to the actual lecture. His lectures are boring and he focuses a lot on gospel principles.

Brother Dew is really a really nice guy, but his lecture style isn't very engaging. The whole first unit is focused on church stuff rather than family theories. If you really like it when teachers incorporate the gospel into class, you would probably enjoy his lectures. The pop quizzes on the readings are super specific and hard to get an A on.

Dr. Dew was a great professor! He really cares about the students. The class wasnt too hard, but you do need to study for the exams. Go to class and take notes, because a lot of the things covered in class are on the test. Quizzes are online and open book, which is super nice!

Professor Dew is a nice guy, but he's not the best teacher. Lectures can drag on and be rather useless half the time, without covering important information that is on the test. Poor pace as chapters of math won't be mentioned in class or practiced until the day before the exam.

Brother Dew is awesome. Super clear, helpful, and engaging. Honestly his family finance class was the most helpful class I've ever taken. He's super fair about grades, and his tests aren't bad. If you can, definitely take 260 from Dr. Dew. Or just take the class in general, it'll be the most useful one you ever take.

Wonderful class, he was truly an amazing professor. I learned so much from the course and also from him as a person. I looked forward to learning more in class each day. There's quite a bit of writing, but as long as you fulfill the basic requirements he's a pretty straightforward grader.

Dr. Dew knows so much, and teaches in a way that makes you think for yourself. He's very intellectual but I really enjoyed his class. He would be a good one to take from! There are short essays and random reading quizzes. You will learn a lot about family theories. The tests were easy, and the quizzes are easy if you do the reading.

I've always been a fan of learning through class discussion, rather than straight-up lectures, and he is excellent at this. And although it doesn't always shine through, you can tell he's a funny guy. Easy enough class if you do the reading and listen to the lectures. The subject is relevant to just about everyone as well. Would take from him again

This was Dr. Dew's first semester at BYU, but he has taught another school before teaching here. He is an awesome teacher! He made the subject interesting, had excellent assignments that were not very time consuming and he gives good lectures.  He is also very caring, and works hard to help each student. Take this class from him!

This was my favorite class at BYU. It was a lot of work, and there were many times that I had no clue what I was doing. I struggled with the group work, and sometimes found the assignments unclear. And yet, I learned so much through the process. I learned how to see the world differently and ask good questions about why things work the way they do.

He taught the same outdated material every class. Slides were literally from 2015. Assignments had little to do with what he “taught.” Lectures were repetitive and boring. Couldn't go five minutes without mentioning his time at Bain, Wharton, or glazing Clayton Christensen. Exams and assignments were vague with unclear grading done by TAs.

Prof. Dyer is the best professor in the Marriott school. His class set me up for success in the strategy core and has changed the way I think. He knows exactly how to connect homework and readings with class discussion and gave real world examples about how everything he teaches applies. The man is interesting, gives no busy work, and loves strat.

Professor Dyer seems intimidating at first but he is a super genuine and caring guy. The class requires some work but it's not crazy. Basically, just make sure you read all the material and do yourself a favor and take good notes of the main ideas in each chapter with examples given.

Professor Dyer is super great, and CCG was super helpful. I've been thinking about doing management consulting, and I feel like CCG was a fantastic trial run of what working a case would be like. My team was great, my director was helpful, and Professor Dyer gave great feedback. I would do it again next year, but it doesn't fit my schedule. Try it!
Professor Dyer is an incredible and insightful teacher and every class that I have had with him has been amazing.
Dr. Dyer is a great teacher. He pushes you to think better.
Professor Dyer's class was difficult but it was also great at the same time. I learned so much from him. He "cold calls" on random students in each class so be prepared to be grilled.

Excellent professor. The class is tough, but all of the assignments, class discussions, and projects are interesting and meaningful. It was my favorite class this year even though it wasn't my best grade.

Absolutely fantastic professor. Does a great job of pushing you to think more and really apply the concepts. DANGER: the sears/rebox cases are brutal, budget time to do them well. The midterm is also savage. Make sure you are thorough in EVERYTHING. I got a good grade in the class but had to work for it, and i learned a TON as a result. Great class
My favorite class that I've taken at BYU.  Jeff Dyer is the man.
AWESOME!!! READ HIS ARTICLES. CHECK HIM OUT.
Inspires students to come up with new business ideas.  Attacks the mindset that only certain people are creative.  Excellent professor.
Dyer is one of the best professors I've had.  He is engaging, has amazing ideas, and pushes you to think about how you approach creative ideas.
Very interactive class. The class is about creative thinking in business, and provides a unique opportunity to study something that many MBAs are not good at.
Dr. Dyer is a good teacher who does some interesting interactive things in class.  I don't feel like we're getting concrete skills in this class, but there are some great concepts and ideas here.

By far one of the best professors at BYU. Has a wealth of real world experience that makes class extremely interesting. He requires a lot of reading in preparation for lectures and discussion during class, but it is all very beneficial.  Grades are based heavily on tests.  A few group projects required. Fantastic class and awesome guy.

Exceptional course and professor.  I am currently interning for a management consulting firm and am using a great deal of the information that I learned in this course.  Prof. Dyer is among the best professors at BYU.

I think 4 is the perfect rating for this guy. Not over the top amazing, but solid. I was prepared for a much harder class. He curved every test like 5-7%! I consistently got around 88% on the tests and got somewhere around 95% after the curve. It could've been better and could've been a lot worse. Solid teacher.

I love Dr. Edwards! He's super chill but also very knowedgeable so I learned a ton! He loves to answer student's questions in lecture, and he's very funny. He is reasonable and wants his students to succeed and gives a generous test curve based on how well the class did. Go to lecture because he drops a lot of test hints!

I really liked taking this with Dr Edwards. He really knows his stuff & tries to make sure we all understood the material. He has a lot of experience & is pretty laid back. 

The tests aren't too bad and he included free points, threw out questions that were badly written & brought our grades up a few % points so that someone always got a 100

You have to buy an online textbook that you won't use much, but it's not super difficult material. Just stay on top of the material as there is a lot you need to memorize. If you took neuro 205 from dr. edwards that helps as the whole first unit is the exact same stuff. All the info comes from the lectures so attendance is important.

Dr. Edwards is a very nice person, but had poor class room management. Most days were spent waiting for classmates to take a hint and shut up, while we wasted time answering non-topical questions. When we were able to get through content, it was a really solid class. Tests are curved, and low quizzes are dropped.

Dr. Edwards is absolutely amazing. Would 10/10 recommend, lectures are great and you can tell that he is passionate about the subject which helps gets students excited too. Very helpful and wants to help students succeed.

Dr. Edwards' class is graded purely graded on exams. There is no homework, only lectures so it doesn't take a lot of time to pass this class. However, if you want a good grade there is no room for error as messing up on a single exam will irreparably harm your grade. his communication about policies and reviews was very poor.

Dr. Edwards was clear about what we needed to know for exams. His exams were sometimes worded a little funny but doable. He sometimes left questions on there by accident that we didn't cover in class, but he curves the exam so that the top scorer gets 100% Sometimes he added a few percentage points to the curve.

Prof. Edwards is the second worst science prof. I have had at BYU. (PDBIO major, graduating) His lectures are very dry, extremely unorganized and he skips half of his slides that he will test you on. He doesn't teach, he shows pictures/diagrams. His tests are on little details instead of the big picture. Waste of money and time. Very disappointed.

When I switched my major to Exercise Science, I was most worried about Anatomy; well, this class is WAY worse. Dr. Edwards is a nice guy but his organizational skills are severely lacking which makes it hard to succeed, and he's almost impossible to meet up with outside of office hours. Lectures are extremely boring and he doesn't explain clearly.
He was the best teacher that I have had and I enjoyed his class so much. Very easy quizzes and homework and the tests are not very hard if you study the slides really well. Definitely take his class!

Dr. Edwards is a great teacher! He does a great job explaining difficult concepts and he truly cares about his students. He does all he can to help you understand and succeed. His tests are straight forward. Pay attention in class and study his slides and you'll do fine.

Way nice guy. Not a good teacher. His lecture was unorganized and he does not teach effectively, he just lectures about everything. He spends way too much time answering random questions that people ask that are unimportant to what we're learning.

The Life Science Department here at BYU is really lucky to have this professor. Crystal clear lectures. He manages to break down the most intricate body systems into morsels of information that anybody could understand. Tests are quite difficult, but a 90% is an A and he curves every test. There should be no complaints there. TA's are great too.

Dr. Edwards was an amazing professor. He is great at explaining both simple and difficult concepts. His grading scale is also so easy-- 90% is an A. His tests were difficult, but he would curve them, and give curves that truly reflected our performance (once, he gave a 10% curve). He is also a really chill guy, and I enjoyed his class a lot.

Edwards has been one of my FAVORITE professors!! He's not super hard, he's a great human being, he's a genius but teaches so simply!  He almost always curves his tests, and is very fair. Totally worth taking the night class from him! I only used the textbook for the web code I needed.

I love Dr. Edwards.  He really cares about this class and shows it in his lectures.  He is passionate about the subject.  Hard tests but other than that the class is not really hard.  It is important to read the text.

Dr. Edwards is a great teacher who structures his class and lectures well. He cares about students and responds quickly to emails. The class is very fair. The cut-off for an A is a 90% and there are huge curves. I learned a lot about physiology and it helped that the atmosphere was a little more laid back than other science classes.

Dr. Edwards was recommended to me and is excellent.His lectures are easy to follow and he makes the subject come alive. He gives out the power points so students can pay attention to the lecture instead of frantically writing.My roommate took Reese the same semester and had to memorize tons of extra, pointless information. Highly recommend him!

Very glad that I took this class from Edwards.  Fair grading and tests.  Does not try to trick you on tests, just tests what you know.  Study hard because there is a lot of material, but he's great at lecturing and making sure that you understand principles.  Does not expect you to memorize ridiculous lists of things or meaningless details.

Professor Edwards is very kind and approachable.  There was very good communication between Professor Edwards and the TA's which made the reviews actually worth my time.  Go to class and study the notes and there's little reason to read the book.

Dr. Edwards is an awesome teacher! I never read the book and I still got an A in the class. He curves his tests so as long as you know the powerpoints really well and go to the reveiw sesions you will do great! Just make sure you learn the material.

Bro Edwards is such a good guy; he really cares about if we understand what he goes over and explains it as many times as we need. it's a super super hard class, since it's a 4 cr hr class. But if you go to class everyday and take notes, & go to the review sessions, you'll be fine :)

This helped me realized the human body is truly incredible. I got an A, but I had to study for about 8 hours straight before each test, otherwise I would have bombed it. GO TO THE TA REVIEWS AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE! I'm serious. Go to like, 3 of the reviews before each test. Edwards is a nice guy, always in a great mood. Loved this class.

Edwards was alright. He had a hard time explaining difficult concepts because he simplified too much for the "less bright" people in class, which was frustrating. Just make his job easy and make sure you know the basics of biology before you go to his class. Tests are long, but doable. I passed with an A- with a little effort. Memorize the slides.

Dr. Edwards is a really good professor.  He explains things very clearly and is very helpful.  There is a lot of information to learn but it is doable.  Averages on tests were about a B+ after he curved it.  Seemed much easier than the other 305 teachers.

You learn a lot in this class, which makes it nearly impossible to know what to study for the test.  Go to the TA reviews, and pay attention in class! Reading the textbook is not necessary-but study the slides hard core. Tests are curved alot due to super low scores-the final this year was curved about 13 points due to the fact that everyone failed
Professor Edwards was alright but not that great. Its almost impossible to do well on the tests due to lack of direction on what to really study. I studied my butt off and will be lucky to get a B.
Loved his class!

He's a great guy, but not that great at explaining difficult concepts.  He knows his stuff, but most things that I learned in this class were from the TAs and review sessions. I rarely understood when Prof Edwards taught because he mainly reads off the slides.  If you take this, make sure to go to TA hours and reviews

Dr. Edwards is definitely the best teacher I've had at BYU.  The class is well structured, interesting, and he wants the kids to succeed.  If the TA Ashley is still there, go to her reviews!!  If you do that and study the slides, you can learn a ton and do really well.
He's the man! Go to TA reviews and study the slides hardcore.

I took Dr. Rheese last semester and didn't do as well as i would've liked. Re-took the class with Dr. Edwards and was way impressed. He curves his tests with avg 4-7points. You take about 20 online open note, no timed quizes. He then drops the lowest 4 quizes. It's very possible to ace the class if you study the powerpoints. : )
If you are going to take PdBio take it from him!! He tries to help you do well, explains things very clearly.

He curves his tests a few points, drops the lowest 4 quiz grades out of 20, and curves the class at the end a little.  If you do the work, you will get a good grade.  I enjoyed this class and his lectures.  I'd take it from him.
Great teacher! Very interesting and knows his stuff. Work hard and go to class= A

Wonderful teacher and lecturer. His course material is well-organized and clear. He is very helpful in answering questions in and out of class and is very willing to meet with students to provide assistance. He has a deep understanding of the material, and is shows in his ability to help

This man is a legend! I am constantly amazed at his punctuality and his care for students. Grading is punctual labs are clear and fun. Answers to questions are usually posted within an hour (typically 10 minutes actually). He is extremely helpful and has worked with students for long periods to help them fix their problems on multiple occasions.

Dr. Goeders is amazing at teaching! He works so hard w./ Dr. Hutchings to make sure 330 is run effectively, and despite COVID, they were on top of EVERYTHING! They had incredibly quick responses to questions on Piazza, & they do the best they can to help students in lecture. Tricky quizzes/tests, but do the readings & lectures and you will be fine.

Dr. Hill, and SFL 260, is absolutely amazing! I have loved this class and learning from him. He has been so influential in my understanding of family finance! He seems like a really great guy, and this class is invaluable. Take this class before you graduate!!

also, all the tests are open note and open book
You will learn a lot of things in this class that you will remember for the rest of your life.
I learned a lot of really good things that will help me in my everyday life and in the future. I did think the class was a little heavy on assignments and tests.
Dr. Hill is a very kind man who loves finance in relation to families and cares about the work he does. He told fun stories and had fun lectures!
The class is super fun and engaging. Hill does a good job teaching the material.

Dr. Hill was great! What he taught was very helpful information and skills needed for managing finances well. The assignments were practical and offered personally relevant application of what was taught in class.

This class helped me understand important life skills like how to create and maintain a budget, how taxes work, and what kind of life insurance I need. Anyone who wants to learn more about finances they will use every day of their lives, I recommend this class.

SFL 260 is a very helpful class if you are about to get married or you are starting to have kids. It has some of assignments that can feel like busy work if you aren't quite at this stage of life yet.
This professor is amazing! Class is entertaining and I learn a lot.

Class was actually really useful to get to understand finances better! It was pretty easy too! Just lots of assignments that take time, and there was a lot of classes that were really off topic that seemed more fitted for a sexuality class.
Professor Hill is such a genuinely good guy. He loves to share stories from his life and others, and tries to get to know the people in his class.

Such a fun and engaging class! The content is very applicable to our lives, and Dr. Hill did a wonderful job of sharing lots of personal stories to teach the content. Lots of readings and you have to work with a group throughout the semester on some assignments, but we didn't have any tests which was awesome!

Professor Hill is a sweetheart. His class was the easiest I've taken at BYU thus far. There is an attendance quiz each class period and there is a group project and some other smaller projects. I never spend more than an hour outside of class preparing for class or doing homework for class a week. Highly recommend!

He is the sweetest soul! He cares deeply about teaching finances because he wants students to do well in school and in life. I learned a lot from him - in his lectures and from his example. I felt more confident with facing the future because of his optimism for life and faith in us and Jesus Christ. His course is structured so all could succeed.
Jeff Hill was so nice and such a great teacher. I loved his class, and he taught me so many great things about family life.  He was very easy, and very likeable.

Dr. Hill was amazing!! SFL 260 was really helpful and I learned a lot of really important things about finances. I think this class should be required for everyone because the information is so useful. Some assignments were a little long but overall it was fair! The tests were open book/notes so you could pretty much find every answer. :)

I loved this class! Professor Hill is a very passionate teacher and I learned a lot. Some weeks you had WAY more homework than others but overall it was pretty well spaced out. If you put in the time you'll do well.

*For Dr. Hill Sr., not his son. Not sure which RMP page is his.*
Dr. Hill knows his stuff! He cares about our well-being. Biggest issue: way too much math hw. Maybe because I didn't take this for a Math GE but rather to learn about family finance (the name of the class), but I was less-than-thrilled about how much math busy work there was.

Great professor who is enthusiastic about what he teaches.  Very organized and knows his stuff well.  I took the hybrid format (online and in-person), which was excellent because his organization on Canvas is easy to navigate and everything you need to know is clearly laid out and available.  Most useful class I have ever taken at BYU.

Professor Hill is an amazing lecturer. I took the hybrid version of his course. Though attendance wasn't mandatory, I still enjoyed attending because lectures were engaging and filled with fun stories. There are condensed lectures online. Weekly online quizzes were easy. Quizzes and tests were open-book. Learned a lot nonetheless. Highly recommend!
Very passionate about what he teaches, cares a lot about his students. Lots of information and resources.
Best teacher! So nice and so funny!! Also, easy class! The math part wasn't as hard as I thought it would be! Everything is open note!

I loved my time taking SFL 260 with Jeff Hill. He is a great instructor, has a lot of experience on the topic and he cares about his students. I love the design of the course and how you learn in relaxed environment. I would definitely take this class again!

Family Finance is amazing! It teaches so many principles with real life application that everyone should know! It is not a hard class but it for sure requires about 2 hours of work every week! Not hard but plan schedule accordingly!
Great lecturer. Learned a lot of valuable things in his class like spend your time, money and talents on the things that are important to you in order to have joy, and invest every month
Great professor, really enjoyed his lectures. A fair amount of reading and discussion boards every week. Very manageable work load.
He was awesome and his teaching was very clear and full of personality. This class was great!

Dr. Hill's class was amazing! I learned so much about finances this semester and I loved how he always tied in a spiritual lesson to each one of his lectures. The tests weren't super hard, but definitely study for them and it will be easier. There are a lot of papers and assignments, so make sure to turn in everything on time.
The class is easy, but taking it online makes it easier to forget about assignments/procrastinate. I would recommend taking it in person.

Jeff Hill was so funny and always kept his students engaged. It can be hard for me to focus in my online classes but I was always interested in what Jeff had to say. I also enjoyed doing all the homework and projects because they were things that I would definitely be applying in my marriage.

this class is such a useful class at BYU. However I felt like it wasn't as helpful as it could have been- I wish it had gone more into insurance and what you can do with what kind of coverage. But if you're wanting to learn how to invest and be prepared for retirement, this is such a good class!

Dr. Hill is great at making the lecture material relatable and easy to understand. As someone who went into the class with very little financial education, I felt that he was able to deliver the course content in a way that was both challenging and approachable.

Honestly such a good class. The math was frustrating... but that's probably because math is always frustrating to me. At least the math is totally useful! 
Professor Hill is a truly good person and I am grateful that I was able to learn from him this semester. I love that I was able to learn about how to have a family in his class.

Honestly loved this class and professor. The math was frustrating, but that's because math is usually frustrating to me! Professor Hill is a truly good man and I'm grateful I was able to learn from him and the way he lives his life.

Class was pretty easy, not overwhelming, and applicable to real life. Dr. Hill is really good at breaking down the material into manageable and understandable pieces each week. The math is pretty simple, and all tests and quizzes are open note and open book.
he connects well with his students
Great class from Professor Hill, he has lots of good advice. So much good financial knowledge for adulting!

I took this class completely online but still loved it and Professor Hill! I also took Marriage Prep from his wife and they are power teachers and a power couple! I will use what they've taught me forever! 
Dr. Hill made things simple to understand and provided tons of resources for help on assignments and exams (they're open book!).

But in person, he is great!!!

He mentioned at the beginning of the semester that analytics was a new class to the curriculum so he's kind of learning along with us, which is understandable. It did mean that the semester was disorganized, assignments were vague, and I often had to seek 3rd party help outside of class or else I wouldn't have passed.

Didnt explain things clearly at all. Was a harsh grader that through his feedback made students feel dumb and didnt really encourage improvement. Basically he would just say you are way off on this one or this part is wrong. Lazy professor.

I really wanted to enjoy this class, but I didn't. I don't regret taking it though because internet marketing is essential to know about these days. The class was structured with a lot of in class group work, which made it difficult for me to learn everything.

Doesn't really teach much material in class. Instead, he has you do pointless assignments in class. That leaves you to do all the learning on your own through reading the textbook. I wish I hadn't taken this class because of the teacher.

Internet marketing is Professor Larson's domain of expertise, and it shows. He is incredibly knowledgeable in digital marketing, analytics, SEO, PPC, etc. Classes were very useful, as they were patterned after practical applications of content taught in the book. Loved the class and found my passion because of it. Definitely recommend the course.

Jeff is probably the smartest professor I have had in the b-school. His class is very applicable  and useful.  Unlike many classes, he actually teaches you skills rather than memorize a bunch of terms. This class is challenging, but maybe the most useful I have taken at BYU.

Jeff is a good professor--ignore reviews prior to 2011/2012 because they don't really reflect how he is now. His classes are challenging, but he's fair and always willing to provide out of class help. I went to his office a lot for our marketing research project and he was really helpful. Go to class, keep up with the assignments and you'll be fine

Jeff is a great teacher with lots of skills that he is willing to teach the class. I feel everything I learned would be applicable to my studies and career. He can move pretty quickly, which may be a little overwhelming, but he is very helpful. Just follow his guidelines for assignments, go to class, pay attention, you'll be fine. TA is helpful too

Jeff is the man!  His class is really interesting and really applicable.  I already used some things I learned in this class in my internship.  he is a great teacher.  His class is not easy, but the subject is difficult (nothing he could do about that)

All the raters up to this point have been harsh. Prof. Larson is great, and his class really isn't that tough if you go to class and keep up with the work. You will learn a ton. Prof. Larson will push you so if you are lazy and don't really want to learn this isn't your class.

He is new and is getting better adn I got a good grade in the class, but, he is still a somewhat bad teacher.  He tried really hard to be good, but his ability to explain things is poor.  But the biggest problem us be is still learning how to run a class.  His class seems unorganized at times and his directions are very unclear (very frustrating)

Prof Larson is amazing!!! he is a brilliant teacher who goes extra miles to help the students learn. He loves teaching and it shows through his classes. The class is super-hard, but it is so  much worth. It is the best class I took last semester.

Really brilliant and nice guy, but an awful teacher. Goes through material way too quickly, and even when asked for clarification, it doesn't help much. He does ask for feedback to improve the course, and he did get better, but overall, one of the worst classes I've taken and professors I've had at BYU.

He's new and still learning how to teach, but he's worlds ahead of where he used to be.  He's brilliant so he goes thru the material quickly and assumes you get it.  He is great when he loves the topic, so do take his Marketing Research class and ask him questions when you're lost.  And if you don't go to class, you'll be lost! No textbook.

He is a genius but a horrible teacher.  He would be better off applying the principles himself in the real world, rather than teaching it to students.  He teaches at such a high level that it goes over everyone's heads.  He was open for suggestions about making the class better and implemented them.  But the class was just a complete waste of time.

He's nice and super attractive, but can't really teach...  The ENTIRE class was on statistics and different than what I expected.  He would lecture on one thing and then assign homework problems or group cases that have nothing to do with anything ever talked about. Toward the end of the semester he seemed more willing to help, though.
Shows lack of interest in his students. Exams are poorly written---seems as though he likes to test students only on how well they can memorize.

Hands down, the best professor I've ever had. I always looked forward to class and loved being there. I didn't find 105 very interesting, but Dr. Macedone made me fall in love with chemistry. Sure the exams are hard, but he does 5 and drops the lowest one. He is very entertaining and incredibly kind. His class genuinely made a big impact on my life

This class was hard. The tests were the hardest tests I've ever taken; too difficult honestly. The only way I found worked for studying was redoing all of the homework leading up to the exam. Even then there were test questions that were nothing like anything we had seen before. I felt like we were tested on test taking skills instead of material.
really great guy. but our class average was 10% less than other classes because there is not just exclusively multiple choice tests he gives written answwers too.

His lectures were constantly off topic. He teaches more about his hobbies than chemistry. Additionally all of his tests are free response and he does not allow you to review your test or see your mistakes. He misses his office hours regularly. When I went to his office hours he was abrasive and refused to help me do better in his class.

Honestly this class was one of the hardest things I've ever done and the tests were so hard but l put in the work and grew so much as a student. Dr Macedone isn't afraid to push us which is scary but I feel so much more prepared for future classes and tests.

There are pros and cons. Pros: I thought Macedone was a great lecturer and I thought he was a good teacher. Cons: His tests are hard and are definitely a step up from the homework and practice tests. The final was also very difficult. He is a lot of love but very high expectations. Not a bad option, but see who else is teaching the course.

Professor Macedone was a fantastic professor to take from! He brought a lot of fun energy to class, and he explained things very clearly. If any students had questions he made sure to take time to answer them and reexplain things in a way they would understand. He also had lots of extra credit opportunities!

Macedone is upbeat, but homework doesn't prepare you for the difficult, obscure midterms with little partial credit. He doesn't release tests or explain wrong answers. Worst of all, he refused accommodations for emergency surgeries, mine (appendicitis) and a friend's. Nice person, but I wouldn't recommend him. Save your GPA + mental health instead.

This is definitely one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. He does 5 mini tests and 1 final, which I really liked because it helped break everything down into smaller chunks. He cares a lot about his students and if you go into his office hours, he is very willing to help you in any way he can. He also offers about 1% of extra credit.

He was the hardest teacher I have ever had. Fun lectures, but his exams were ridiculous. I got a 98 in Chem 105, but barely kept an A in his class, even though 106 is supposed to be easier. Don't take it from him, it will not be good for your mental health or GPA. Each exam feels impossible, and you can study for hours and still walk out with a 20%

I feel that sometimes the material we learned in lectures didn't help with the homework, I had to do a lot of teaching myself outside of lecture in order to do the homework. I really struggled with the exams because they are free response questions but you don't get a lot of partial credit, he doesn't look at your work. Overall, he's a good teacher

Professor Macedone was an amazing teacher to take chem 106 from. He made all of the lectures interesting, and was very caring. If we were struggling on a concept, he would take the time to make sure we understood the material. There are a lot of midterms, but they are small and if you study and review you'll do great. 100% recommend!

People say Macedone is one of the harder 106 professors at BYU. He's just like everyone else. I took 106 from Paxton and got a D-. I learned my lesson and I had to retake it. Macedone was WAY better for me. His tests are pretty infamous but they have legitimately helped me nail down study techniques that have helped me do better than last time.

I liked Dr. Macedone. I liked his teaching style, and his midterms weren't too bad. I had an A in the class until the final. Several other people also bombed. My grade dropped two letters before he decided to curve a tiny bit. I'm still not sure what happened. I couldn't find him in his office and he didn't respond to my email. I still feel scammed

This is a good, hard class. In the moment, it's actually fun. You learn so much that by the end, you feel genuinely grateful for the challenges. The professor runs the course like an internship and is incredibly gracious with late points. He holds high expectations, but as long as you show up and put in effort, you're supported and taken care of

Macedone is a wonderful teacher; the class is pretty hard, especially if you're not into math or chemistry, but he did a great job of teaching it in a way that made sense. He's a very funny and kind man, truly passionate about his work. Watch out for the midterms though; they are both frequent and challenging. Make sure to take notes and study up.

Dr. Macedone does his best to ensure that a hard class is very enjoyable. The textbook is available online and free though the BYU library. Tests were a written exam which was pretty chill and an excel spreadsheet which was really difficult, but you had all week to do at home. Do the homework and labs to understand them and you will do well.

This class is no joke, but he has made changes recently to make it more doable, and it is indeed doable! Dr. Macedone is high love high expectations. He expects a lot, but also loves and care so much. I would not have made it through this class without him. He is a wonderful person and professor. This class is hard, but he makes it worth it.

This class was so hard and also so fun! Don't let it scare you. I felt like I nearly died going through it, but it is so fulfilling in the end. Dr. Macedone is super caring and will help in any way he can. He is a great guy. Our class average Spring 2025 was 90.37%. We all worked our tails off, but he made it worth it. I had a great time at QQI!

Dr. Macedone is such a great professor! He cares deeply for his students and their success. Chem 227 is a very intense class and as a result Dr. Macedone's grading can be seen as tough but it is fair. My tips would be to understand what you are doing before the lab for accuracy scores and take time to study for tests. 8/18 got an A for Sp 2025.

Chem 227 has been completely overhauled and is excellent now! Like seriously, all the complaints of the past (such as the coding nightmares) are addressed. There are far fewer homework assignments, and Dr. Macedone is great at doing everything he can to help you out. Remember that this is still a difficult chem class though; discipline is needed.

This class broke me. Macedone is a great lecturer, but unwilling to help you in any way. Sometimes wished the UTA bus would hit me while walking to this class. I lived in the library taking this class. OCHEM1,2,and BIOCHEM were a delightful and carefree experience compared to this brutal class meant to suck the joy form your soul.

His lectures were fairly engaging and he is a very sweet guy, but I would not recommend taking Dr. Macedone. He is condescending when answering questions. He doesn't allow students to look at past exams and had unnecessarily difficult exams, as seen in the test averages being in the 60s while the other chem professor scored consistently higher.

I loved Dr. Macedone's lectures and felt like learned from them. I reached out to Dr. Macedone bc I was getting a range of 80s-50s on the tests. He boosted my morale and helped me feel like a better student. That was, however, not helpful academically because, after a week of constant chem study, I got a 40 on the final. Love him but HARD TESTS!

I have nothing against Macedone. Just was not my teaching style as someone with ADHD. I always had a hard time listening in lectures and trying to understand how to apply it. Chem is hard in general, but his open-ended exams made it harder. I got a D mostly because all homework was on a different website and I forgot to check that website a lot.

I found this class enjoyable, but the tests were very difficult. Once, he even had us do riddles for a review lecture instead of covering the actual material, because the tests were more similar to riddles than the chemistry we had been taught/practiced. Not a terrible professor, but if possible, I would avoid taking his class.

If I could go back, I would definitely take him again. No chemistry at BYU is easy and honestly he gives you every chance to get a good grade. His final was one of my highest test scores and it was the most straight forward final I have ever taken. You don't need to be the smartest to get an A. Super good guy and fair Professor.

Dr. Macedone taught the material well but had a frustrating amount of material that wasn't covered well found on the 5 midterms (free response) and final (MC). He has high expectations for his students. Sometimes treated us like children by shushing us. He will prepare you for the MCAT if you put in the many hours required to do well in his class.

Entertaining professor but his class is not set up for your sucess. Exams have averages in the 60s and all he says is that they are in line with historical trends. If the class is averaging that low, you're literally the problem. You aren't allowed to review exams, you only get to know the general topic of incorrect ?s so there is no room to grow.

His lectures were fun and entertaining, he also gives a lot of extra credit which is nice. However his test are incredibly difficult. They don't match homework or examples at all. I would walk out of his tests feeling like I got hit by a bus even though I felt I knew the material. He is a nice person but DON'T take unless you like crying.

If you want a good grade in chem them do no take Macedone. My friend who got 80s and above on the tests for all the tests got a D- on the final. Macedone is a GREAT person but a terrible professor. He always talks about why the reason his students struggle is because they don't know how to manage their time. His advice was to quit our jobs wtf.

He gave a lot of extra credit, which made it nice because the 5 test averages were so low (3 60s, 2 70s). honestly, i felt so smart and like i understood everything until the tests came around. Save yourself the GPA with Kelly cause I probs will retake this class with kelly to replace my grade:) come take kellys class with me!! save your confidence

Loved Dr. Macedone he was really likeable, BUT his tests were SO hard. they were all free response with some multiple choice here and there, but the multiple-choice questions were SO hard. We had 3 tests that had an average of below a 70. one 63, 68, 64. And he didn't curve them. He doesn't admit when he is wrong and blames it on the students.

Not worth bringing your GPA down.  He makes a joke about dating and having threesomes and thinks that will make up for the fact that the class average on his exams are anywhere from 65-75% His lectures and homework are stupid easy and then the exams are as if he threw a brick at you. He also cried about how great of a teacher he was??

Professor Macedone definitely has his quirks, but he's a great professor who genuinely cares about his students. Lectures are engaging and align with exam materials for the most part.Tests are weighted heavily, but one is dropped which is nice.
He seemed like he cared more about making the lectures entertaining than actually teaching.

Enjoyable lectures, but time-consuming material.  His tests are super difficult. I would be fine with the course-load and the effort-to-grade ratio if he graded on par with the other professors in the department. There is a huge department discrepancy here. 40 A's vs 150 A's in Kelly's class. Not worth losing a scholarship over.

I initially was nervous to take chem with him based off of these reviews, but he was so much better than what some people say. He is a little silly, but if you can get past some of his quirks he is such a great professor. He knows how to teach, is understanding, and really cares about his students. Work load is very manageable.

I'm pretty confident that Professor Macedone is clinically insane, but he is also one of the best professors that I have ever had. Cares a ton and puts in a ton of work to help you do the best you can. The easiest chemistry class to get an A in that I have taken so far, but only if you are self-motivated to learn. There isn't a lot of homework.

He puts a ton of effort into his lectures and cares a ton about his students. Class is hard but on par with other Chem classes. Not too much of a course load and as long as you keep up with studying and put in your part it's manageable.

If you want to learn chemistry and how to think critically, take this class. If you want a good grade, stay far away. 

He does a good job explaining the material. His class is structured to effectively help students grow. 70% of your overall grade comes from tests. The tests are not multiple choice. He doesn't let you see what you missed sadly.

His laugh sounds like King Candy's from Wreck it Ralph. He's a good teacher. Very big on having the students act professionally (listen to his lectures without talking, come and leave on time). His tests are really hard because they aren't multiple choice. He's an entertaining teaching though and if you put the work in you do well.

Tests are hard. They are short and free-response, and you're only given credit for the right answer (no partial credit). The average test grade is 63-75%, and he doesn't curve them. His lectures are entertaining, but they don't prepare you well for the tests. He is nice outside of class but isn't very helpful if you are struggling or behind.
He should be embarrassed of his low test score averages. When the average is a failing grade, something is wrong with the test.

VERY DIFFICULT TESTS
Good lecturer, but be careful how you phrase questions because in his class there IS such a thing as a stupid question
Homework and quizzes are manageable, but there are tons of them, check them every single day
Pretty entertaining, I was never really bored in his class which is saying something for chemistry

He is very entertaining but doesn't always explain things very well. It is really hard to catch up if you get behind. All 6 tests are free response with questions that are way harder than what is practiced in class. Almost 10% of your grade is going to class. Recitation is not helpful. This is a VERY hard class.

This is a very challenging class and if you fall behind it is really hard to come back and not fail. Tests are all free response and the questions are very hard/different from the practice questions in lecture. You must go to class for participation credit. Recitation wasn't helpful. Go to the chem lab with TAs to help you! He is very entertaining.
Shows a quirky persona in class. He cares about professionalism and keeping to policy.
Bro legit thought the Baghdad battery was real and that it made the Ark of the Covenant dangerous
very cringe, do not recommend
The so-called ''mini-tests'' are so different from all the homework they might as well be for another class.
Tests are big part of grade, and they're all free response so good luck. Not very sympathetic if you don't understand. But his lectures are fun and he's a good guy.

5 midterms and a final, I barely knew what he was teaching before I was being tested on it. Exams average ~68%. He ignores feedback; acknowledged his poor ratings and said he didn't care. I went to office hours desperate for extra help or practice problems, and he just told me to quit my student job. Told me to go slower, but there are time limits.
If something is on the practice midterm, you can know it is not going to show up on the actual midterm.

Dr. Macedone made me lose my love and motivation for chemistry. The homework and quizzes are not up to the calliber of the exam. He doesn't take feedback seriously. He does have some captivating lectures, but he doesn't go over any exam calliber questions until the exam review where everyone feels lost. He is a good man but a terrible professor.

I liked Macedone, but his class is harder than other professors. You will do good if you read the textbook. He really cares about your success. Recitation was a waist of time, Our TA wouldn't show up half of the time. Class is graded fairly. If you fall behind you will fail this class, but thats just chemistry.

Really funny guy. You'll love 106 with him if you:
-Don't really care about chemistry, just taking it to fill the req
-Like lots of exams
-Have oodles of time

You won't love it if you:
-Care about the why beyond his curriculum (he'll shut you down)
-Dislike lots of exams
-Have harder classes you want to focus on

Be ready to be tested on anything.

Professor Macedone is kind and funny, but his teaching style could be improved. He didn't always clearly explain the material, and the SmartWorks assignments weren't helpful. Office hours were intimidating, and the tests didn't align with what we studied. The class was tough for me, but others seemed to manage better.

I retook this class this semester. Got a D the first time and a B the second. I have never made below a B+ before then. This class broke me down mentally. The tests do not align with the course work. I felt confident before most exams only to get a 68 or something close. However, my 67s were above the class average so I guess I should be grateful.

He understands that chem isn't your only class and has set his course up for you to be successful. The tests are only open for 2 days, but one gets dropped. He also has iclickers for every class so you need to show up. He's one of the best professors I've had at BYU.

If chem 105 was rough for you, take 106 from Macedone! Less busy work than 105, and his lectures were very entertaining and straightforward. 5 midterms, but there's less content per exam, so honestly not too bad. Do the textbook practice problems and study the lecture slides and you'll be set. Lots of EC throughout the semester. Would recommend!

Macedone's lectures can be engaging, but the class structure is a challenge. Tests don't align with coursework, and he can be condescending. However, with dedication and tools like unstuckstudy ai for study prep, the class is manageable for motivated students.

I had a negative experience with this professor. I thought that he could come off as passive-aggressive, and it kept me on my toes the whole semester. It seems like the class is set up to make students unsuccessful when it came to lab work. The exams were fair and learning about the instrumentation was interesting.

It just seems like this class is set up for you to not do well. out of 30 students 2 got an A. Memorize the lecture slides for the exams.  Typos everywhere and there was a grading error which brought everyone's test grade down after they were posted. Apart from the absurd amount of HW, the experiments are pretty fun. Cool project at the end.

The only thing good about Macedone as a teacher is the way he lectures. He is condescending and won't help you if you are behind. He is a good teacher for robots and valedictorians, but that is about it. If you are neither of those, find a different teacher and spare yourself some misery.

Do not take this class. He spends more time trying to be funny than he does actually teaching. Tests are nothing like what is taught in class (avgs of ~69%). He is insanely condescending towards students and overall just a bad professor. He also doesn't hold his TAs to a high standard so they don't help. Wait and take it from a different professor.

First of all, no one's perfect. If you have a knack for chemistry, then taking 106 from Macedone will probably be fine. But, if you're like me and just can't seem to wrap your brain around it most of the time, Macedone himself will be no help to you. Pro-tip, if do you take him and struggle, rely on youtube (don't go to office hours).

This class was almost my 13th reason why. Macedone is a nice guy, but the way he structures his class is beyond me. Even his TAs don't understand his thought processes. When I say his tests are nothing like the homework or practice exams, I mean it. He claims to make them super short to help us, but it does the complete opposite. Avoid if possible

The class itself is structured well, you just have five tests throughout the semester and a final. Lecture attendance is graded using iClicker. I found his lectures to be very annoying and agitating. He tries to make it interesting but his big personality is annoying. You are never allowed to see your test after you take it which is hard.

Really does care about his students and gives lots of extra credit opportunities and drops. Tests are free response and hard, but I felt I had been prepared for all but the last one. Definitely will have to do the readings and go to recitation because he doesn't cover topics in-depth during lecture. Overall hard class but Macedone makes it doable.

I would highly recommend Macedone. I have taken 3 other college chem classes and this was the first one I actually enjoyed and found interesting. His lectures are fun and enjoyable if you get into it. If you had a bad mindset then you might not enjoy it, it is what you make it. Exams aren't terrible, it's a just a hard course.

Going to lecture was a waste of time, but required to attend for random Iclicker points. I spent more time with my TA trying to learn everything. Lots of homework that is super picky and hard to answer. You don't get to see what your test scores are and they take forever to get graded. Don't take this class from him unless you want to cry everyday

Dr. Macedone has an insane ego and clearly is just here for research. He is condescending and does not prepare you for the exams. Tests are recycled so you can't see what you did wrong. 5 exams throughout the semester, plus a final. The exams are not at ALL like the HW, practice exams, or any other material given throughout the semester. AVOID!!!!

Very entertaining and fun lectures! Need a physical clicker, meaning you have to be in class to get participation points. There is no recorded or Zoom version of the lecture. There are like 5 mini-tests that are mixed free response and multiple choice, but he does drop 1. Also, he doesn't offer practice tests like other professors might, soo yeah.

I hated the midterms soooooo much. the BYU chem department wants students to get C's on all tests. Requires so much time to study. Dr. Macedone is great though. A great man who is a geek for chemistry. I didnt have a good experience in his office hours though. I wouldnt talk to him 1 on 1. He is a good teacher tho.

I was fooled by the glowing reviews. He is a good guy with a nice personality but his exams hardly resemble any practice work you do in the class, even the sample exams and theres 6 of them. Also told students with jobs to simply quit them to do better. Very condescending in office hours. Uses iclicker for random graded questions in lecture.

Dr. Macedone himself clearly knows the content well, but I didn't feel his class prepared me for the tests. He also does not allow you to see what you did wrong on the tests, so it is difficult to improve. Homework, lectures, and practice tests didn't really resemble the tests themselves.

Piss poor professor. Sure he knows his stuff about chemistry and can be entertaining SOMETIMES, but 1 on 1, he is the worst professor ever. Went into his office hours asking for help multiple times, and every time I was told "that's not the best way to learn" AND said that if you work and struggle in his class, either quit the job or the class.

He had entertaining lectures and did a good job applying what we learned to things we are already familiar with. His tests are super difficult and the prep materials given are not very helpful. I spent countless hours in the tutorial lab with TA's studying for this class and continued to get bad grades regardless of how much preparation I put in.

Homework often was confusing and overly time-consuming, exacerbated by a lack of coding instruction. I felt like I needed to go to the TAs for everything. The exams were poorly written and had many spelling errors.
Macedone, while promoting an open-door policy often seemed demeaning when seeking help. Overall, I really don't recommend this class.

Dr. Macedone is a high-love, high-expectations professor. Some may take his enthusiasm as condescending but I respected his commitment; he wants you to become a good chemist/biochemist. The TA hours are ESSENTIAL, go to them as often as you can for help with the reports and homework because they will practically just give you the answers.

If you're required to take Chem 227, know what you're getting into. DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE EXAM 1. The whole class agreed that it was the hardest exam we had ever taken. It's no exaggeration to say that I spent 25hrs/wk on this class only for a B+. This probably the hardest class in the biochem major, and Macedone is merciless and provides no help.

Fakest professor I've ever met, pretends to be fun and nice but if you ever go to office hours he is super demeaning and terrible at answering questions. Tests are written poorly and filled with typos and mistakes in values and since you can't even see them afterwards you don't know. Terrible avoid at all costs.

In comparison to the professor I had for Chem 105, Dr. Macedone is very passionate about what he does. The tests were pretty hard though, and you don't get a large window to take them. As one who appreciates frequent demonstrations to engage the class, I liked his efforts to keep us interested, even if the class was too fast-moving at times.

I always enjoyed the lectures and the energy he brought to class. He was genuine and I enjoyed being in class. The tests were hard, more fair than other chem classes but I still found myself disagreeing with questions I felt were ridiculous.

Don't mention things about the test at his office hours or he will flip.

Professor Macedone was very engaging and nice, but sometimes he can be condescending to the class. Tests were tough and you are only given two days to complete them. My class was a higher performing class and the average score for our final was a D. Topics are frequently rushed, not fully explained, and later tested harshly.

Professor Macedone is funny, but he will take the time to do a demonstration rather than teach you what you need to know. His lectures were rushed, and hard to understand. You have to answer Iclicker questions everyday on the reading. I went to every TA review, got tutored, practically anything I could and still did horribly. DO NOT RECOMMEND!

He's amazing. Very hard class, but he made it very possible. He really knows what he's talking about and he cares about his students a lot. Also, he's an amazing lecturer and super entertaining. 227 is a beast, especially spring term, but Dr. Macedone made it great. You still have to work hard and do things right, but he's always fair.

A truly wonderful person and man of God. That being said, I do not think he is a very great teacher. He is very lecture heavy and gives a lot of fluff that is not needed. The grade is tests and Smartwork along with some iclicker points.

Not the best. The style of teaching and the material covered were not equivalent. He did not clearly teach a thing. This extended into the wording, and sometimes the TA's didn't even know what he meant. I worked wayyyy harder for a B than what is usual. I would never take him again and would actively avoid his childish manner of teaching lectures

His lectures are amazing, and he addresses many real-world applications which makes it kind of fun. He truly strives to make a positive impact however so many of his policies are rigid, old school and unaccommodating. He grades using Iclickers in class which means if you don't understand a concept immediately you may miss points.

Macedone is a wonderful professor. Lectures are amazing. He's a competent teacher. Practice problems are relevant and help with test prep. Tests are super hard, but I think that is true for every professor in the chem department. Definitely take him! He makes chem enjoyable, and I looked forward to his class.

So I genuinely believe Professor Macedone is a good man and wants the best for his students, but he seems pretty stuck in his ways and gets defensive when questioned.  He can get pretty rude and demeaning if the class isn't understanding the "simple" lecture he's presenting.  Tests are hard, homework is easy.  Average for final was 67

Dr. Macedone was my favorite professor. He genuinely cares about his students and he brings lots of examples to class to help his students grasp new material. Don't skip, you won't understand new material. There are 5 midterms but the lowest gets dropped. His tests are hard and only open for 2 days. If you put the work in though you should be fine.

Dr. Macedone was a great lecturer, but when it came to the tests so much of the information on them was not covered in the lecture. We also were unable to review our exams after taking them, so it was difficult to understand what we did not know. You need to be in class for iClicker points and tests were all free-response in the testing center.

Dr. Macedone is an amazing professor. He demonstrates over and over again that he truly cares about your success. He's amazing with questions and will devote his time to you until you understand it. I didn't do the best in this class but I would say that's due to my own faults and not Dr. Macedone's. He's truly an amazing and kind professor.

Macedone's exams are INSANELY hard and unfair. I got As on all my 105 tests but for most of the 106 midterms I got Cs and I felt like the tests did not reflect my effort at all--super stressful. TAs are nice though and lectures are actually engaging I just felt like an idiot taking the tests even though I put in all the work for the class

I loved Dr. Macedone! He was the most passionate professor I've ever met and wanted students to succeed. I actually wanted to attend class every day. He also did some really cool chemistry demonstrations. 'There were 5 small tests (one dropped) plus a final. The tests definitely weren't easy but if you put in the work, the class isn't too bad

Best CHEM 106 professor no doubt. His lectures are funny and engaging. The material is difficult, but the TAs are your best friend. I didn't read the textbook, but the HW and quizzes are essential for success. The tests are difficult, but he gives you practice tests which are helpful.

Professor Macedone is a good guy and lectures are fun, but his tests will absolutely destroy you. His tests are all free response and so hard! He doesn't do open-note tests anymore. His lectures and the smartwork will not prepare you for the tests because he tries to give you the hardest problems, and he only gives you two hours to figure it out!

He's funny, amazing lecturer, and all that but when it comes down to your grade he is extremely strict on arbitrary grading criteria not specified and is extremely condescending to students if you ask him to explain why. He's very humorous but also equally rigid which is hard to read as a student.

Professor Macedone is an incredible lecturer and teacher. Many students experience academic whiplash when tests begin, as his cheery nature does not translate into his often brutal tests. If you put effort in to his class, you will have an exceptional chemistry experience.

Great teacher. I really enjoyed his class, and he really cares about helping you succeed. The class was very hard, there was a lot of homework, and the tests were very difficult, but nothing was unfair or "tricky," and once you get into the routine it's not too much to handle. Utilize the TAs and go to his office hours and you'll be ok :)

His lectures were super engaging, but once the frequent and difficult tests came, I realized fun lectures aren't worth getting screwed on the test. He wouldn't let students see exams or learn from mistakes. Any time you would ask him questions he would have little patience and thought anyone struggling meant they had no study habits. AVOID HIM.

He was my least favorite professor and person I've met at BYU. We had every test open note which was cool, until the week of the final he changed it last min to closed note in the testing centre. Not  super fair IMO.  He was a good lecturer, but so condescending and tests were horribly written. The class didn't promote learning at all

I love how he teaches and makes lectures lively! The TA reviews and his PPTs help for the midterms, but the final is 40% of the grade & there's no class-final review, so study in advance! The final was supposed be open-note online, but it switched to the testing center due to cheating, yet he was nice and curved the class afterwards which was nice!

Dr. Macedone's lectures are fantastic. He is a good guy, but he seems really set in his ways, even if they clearly need to be improved upon in some ways. It seems as though student feedback is largely unimportant to him. His tests were very unfair and as a result, they were extremely difficult despite knowing the material.  it was very frustrating.

Macedone was the worst professor I think I've ever had. He acts really nice and funny in front of the whole class (claims to care about his students), but when confronted in a one on one scenario he became condescending. His tests were unlike the homework he gave, so it was hard to prepare for them.
Didn't turn in a single homework assignment in on time yet still got 100% on the homework.

Probably the best prof for 106, but made students feel dumb. Decided to change the format of the Final two days before it opened because he couldn't take the time to write more exam questions, it was non-negotiable. Was petty about people talking in class. But slides and lectures were helpful with studying. Ask for the practice test questions early

For sure a difficult class but Prof Macedone is fair and tries to give his students what they need to succeed. Make sure to read the book before lecture to get an idea of what you will be learning. His tests are difficult, but there are five of them so each counts less and one gets dropped which helps. Overall a difficult class but I learned a lot.

This class is hard. However, Dr. Macedone make his lectures easy to understand and is a very good teacher. Lectures are always interesting and engaging. Come to class!! He does his tests in a "mini-test" style, which means more tests than your average class. You can't go over missed questions so studying can be a bit challenging.

First I would like to say that he really really cares about both chemistry and teaching, and it shows. He is passionate and I appreciate that. However, his class is structured horribly. I also had numerous experiences of my own and of other students that indicate that, in person, he is dismissive and makes you feel kinda dumb.

Professor Macedone teaches with lots of passion and enthusiasm. I really enjoyed his lectures because they were easy to listen to and he taught very clearly. However, when I spoke with him one on one, he was often rude and seemed to not care about my concerns. When you speak with him, it is a "too bad, that's your problem" type of vibe.
Hands down the best chem professor I have ever had. He is a little quirky, but his lecture are great and his material makes sense. take it from him if you can cause he is the best

My major and emphasis are extremely heavy with math and sciences classes, but from these classes I have learned that the most important attribute a professor can have is passion for their subject. Dr. Macedone loves what he does and you will learn so much if you are willing to put forth the effort. I highly recommend taking 106 from him!

Professor Macedone is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are incredible, and he isn't afraid to change his lesson plan in the middle of class if he can see that the clas isn't getting it. Although there is a lot of homework and exams, he prepares you well. He is clear in his expectations and doesn't try to trick you on tests.

Professor Macedone is by far the best option for CHEM 106. His lectures are very clear and very enticing. While there are multiple online assignments throughout the week, his tests were open note and he prepared us very well for them. He is funny, VERY caring, and incredibly inspiring. He changed my attitude toward chemistry for the better.
