His ability to explain concepts is adequate, but everything in his demeanour illustrates how much he is invested in the success of his students. He's upfront that his class (TMA241) is a doozy and he's not lying, but nearly all of it is for your benefit. A real treasure.

Jeff was a great teacher and the class was a lot of fun. I'm not a film major so I was taking the class to fill credit hours, but I'm glad I chose this one. There is actually a lot to learn about film, and he makes it interesting and fun. The class is super easy as long as you show up and write the weekly papers which become easier as you go along.

I'm a film student and I've taken 102 as well as other classes with Jeff. For anyone worried about the workload of the class: it's the same with all profs. Jeff is extremely helpful and has a lot of experience to back up the things he's teaching. Don't take to get an easy general, take if you're interested in looking at films differently.

Jeff is a cool guy but not the greatest professor.  He doesn't really teach, but more just tells you what he knows and expects you to suck it in.  My TA in this class was great, as most of them are, but Jeff wasn't the best lecturer.  This class wasn't as fun as I thought it was gonna be, but is still fairly easy comparatively.

Jeff Parkin does to students what Morgan Freeman does to microphones--he turns them into bars of gold after speaking with them. When he talks to you (privately or publicly) he is respectful, genuine, instructive, and just makes you feel like you can do it! He is NOT just a "feel good" teacher. He teaches, enlightens, and reprehends when needed.

This is an easy, relaxed, fun class. You only see Parkin once a week, but his lectures are always interesting. He's very good at incorporating the Gospel into them. Most of the time is spent with your TA. You have a quiz once a week and have to write a short paper on a movie once a week. I really enjoyed it.

It was his first time teaching this class. Good guy and was funny at times. Enjoyed the class but did not enjoy the weekly 1 page thought papers about films. You only needed the book for open book online quizzes. I did not read the chapters but aced them. If you enjoy film and like to write, this is the class to take.

This was probably the class that has had the most direct effect on the way I make movies. Even if you're not planning on screenwriting, this class will help you be more effective in your chosen field. Take it. There were times that I disagreed with Parkin, but I've come to realize he is usually spot on about everything. You will learn a ton.
He reads off the slides and doesn't care for the students or their opinions. He always deviates from 'teaching' to talking about his lab. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS

As mentioned by other students, he marked down quizzes for leaving the tab (which he could have prevented). He was disrespectful over communication outside of class and seemed to teach to be allowed to do research. Very passive aggressive as well. Would recommend waiting a semester rather than take a class from him.

VERY UNFAIR- Worked so hard to have an A so I could get into medical just To have him dock me an entire letter grade Becasue I had left the tab during a quiz. No where in the syllabus does it say you can't leave the tab during a quiz. Assumes everyone was cheating even though I was not. If you are reading this do not take from him.

I would take from another professor at all costs. He's probably the worst professor I've had at BYU. Docked like 60 percent of the class and threatened to fail the a ton of people due to people leaving the tab during a quiz. Does not teach well. Does not write tests well. It is worth waiting to take from a different professor at BYU

Take someone else. I feel bad for everyone who was caught "cheating" and lost points on their quizzes, dropping a letter grade. The tests were based off of the slides, but the FRQs proved challenging and I would get docked points on such miniscule things. At least you have lots of extra credit, I wouldn't have survived without.

Never take from tessem. Hands down worst proff I've ever had. He just read off slides and rarely explained things in clear ways. Take from Hope. He obviously is only teaching so that he can do research.
There are alot of bad reviews over here - They are an UNDER STATEMENT!!!  Do yourself a favor. Don't take this class from him...Dream Crusher...

He read off the slides to us. The slides were dense and hard to understand, and he always deviated from the topic we were discussing to mention his research lab. We tallied through the semester how many times he mentioned his lab and counted hundreds, I'm not even joking. He is not a good professor and grades harshly without grace. DO NOT TAKE THIS

NOT A GOOD PROFESSOR. Take from someone else! He reads the slides off to you, they are dense and hard to understand. His tests have written portions and you are graded on only 14 quizzes, and your exams. He is not the kindest person nor understanding, and he disregards accommodations, emails, input, and inquiries. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

He's a nice guy, but he isn't great at teaching difficult concepts. Its clear what you need to know vs what you don't, but I don't understand the stuff he wants me to know! I survived thanks to the TAs. I skipped lecture the last half of semester and still scored the same on tests. He is the only prof with FRQ. Take someone else instead.
Does not explain topics very well at all. His slides are very hard to understand.
Very dismissive and rude outside of class, is not focused on teaching or learning at all. He is completely focused on just testing and memorization.

DO NOT TAKE FROM TESSEM! He is a very smart guy, and obviously knows a lot about biology, but he also obviously does not know how to teach. The tests are hard, and he is difficult to work with outside of class. If you are not already a pro at mmbio, you will not learn anything in this class.

Dr. Tessem is great! Your grade is based on tests and weekly quizzes. Makes it easy to study for tests as he puts the learning objectives on all the slideshows for the unit, and bases his tests on that. FRQ questions on tests, but you can do corrections. Tons of extra credit, and always went to TA hours for help and they were very helpful!

Do not take this class him. Dr Hope is much better. He accused more than half of the class of cheating for switching out of the tab during weekly quizzes. He does not explain hard concepts well. I found that not attending lectures was a better use fo my time. Hard tests. Decent guy to talk to otherwise not effective at his job. Just study slides.

This class gave me a new respect for molecular biology. If you read and take notes from the slides before lecture, you'll do good. Really focus on the learning objectives because all the exam questions are based directly on those. Super nice professor and always tying the principle learned to a bigger picture. Rocks a bowtie daily.

Didn't require a textbook but only had slides that were not very comprehensive to teach material. I always walked out of lecture feeling like I didn't understand what we'd just talked about. Poses as a nice guy who wants to help you, but when I reached out with an email, actually made it harder for me to succeed. At least there was extra credit.

Tessem does not teach hard concepts very well and doesn't always answer questions well. He presents as a kind person, but behind closed doors (emails) he is difficult and is slow to take responsibility. He is easily offended and bragged about tackling mentally ill patients in a past job. If taking MMBIO 240, take from Sandra Hope.

Professor Tessem = great professor. He really cares about his students but it is very hard in class to be able to follow his teaching. Most of my learning was outside of class in study groups. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit and you can redo your FRQs from the test for 1/2 points back. Very hard concepts to grasp on weekly quizzes.

This class was fairly easy; I could have gotten an A if I had studied more, so that was on me. It has a reasonable amount of work, and I wasn't stressed out of my mind like my roommate, who took general biology instead.

This class was interesting. His lectures were a little strange, as his learning objectives are far more complicated than the exam questions. But he allows a notecard for all exams, and he loves to give extra credit. So even though I didn't do great on exams I still got a great grade in the class. Overall it was an easy class.

This class takes a lot of memorizing but Dr. Tessem was phenomenal at clearly showing us what we needed to know for the test. He deeply cares about his students and shows everyone respect. The topic was not my favorite but Dr. Tessem made the course doable. As long as you can study from the slides, attendance is not super crucial.

Dr. Tessem is a very intelligent and respectful teacher. He clearly knows a lot about Biology but he does not teach it well. He would just read off his slides and talk more about his research. I often left the class stressed because there was way too many things that could have been on the test. The class was a little disorganized and stressful

Dr. Tessem cares a lot about his students.This was the class structure: each class is a powerpoint that starts with clear learning objectives that he goes through. Each Wednesday, there is a closed note quiz on the past few classes. Tests follow the learning objectives pretty closely. I heard other professors were easier but he is an ok option.

Couldn't recommend more. He genuinely cares. He always had his priorities in line and doesn't want this class to be too stressful. Help is always available if you ask for it. He's so understanding. Lots of extra credit for reading the Book of Mormon. No homework! Also doesn't require a textbook. His slides and learning objectives are all you need.

Honestly, I read through some of the other reviews and think they were too harsh. You don't have to be the smartest, show up every class, or even understand every lecture to get a good grade. He is a stud and gives you legit every opportunity to succeed. There is a reason why I had a 102% going into the final and the class average was a 92!

This class wasn't as challenging as some of the other science courses I've taken at BYU. It is a ton of memorization, so get ready to essentially memorize all of his lecture slides. He is a confusing lecturer, and can easily get thrown off track by student's questions. I wouldn't say to avoid this class, just know what you're getting yourself into.

Tessem is a nice guy, but not a good professor. He's difficult to follow during lectures and explains things from a professor-level understanding. The questions on quizzes and exams aren't aligned with knowledge that is useful in a real lab setting, though that is the majority of the content. Do NOT take this class if you've never taken chemistry.

I took Professor Tessem for MMBIO240 and he was great! He makes time to answer questions in class, and has great lectures. He applies the lectures to real life. There's no homework, just weekly quizzes, 3 midterms and a final. Lots of extra credit. Go to TA reviews! You have to study a lot, but he tells you the free response questions on the exams.

Dr. Tessem is incredible. There are few professors  that truly have a knowledge as in depth in what they're teaching as him. He's clear, gives grace with our grades, and sets realistic expectations. The class is intensely difficult due to the sheer volume. None of the difficulty of the class is due to Dr. Tessem. It was an honor to learn from him.

Biochemistry finally makes sense!  This is the best class ever.  Lots of information, lots of work, lots of tests. He drops your lowest test, which is nice. He does a really good job. I am so glad I took this before the MCAT.

He is hard to reach outside of class time so be ready to ask him questions either during class or right afterwards. He is upfront about the class being a heavy load but he underestimates the time you need to do well. I studied 5-8 hours M-F and barely got a B-. Took this class in spring but either semester you take it in, this class demands.

Best class and best professor I had at BYU.  The class is a ton of work, but if you put in the time it is fair. There are lots of ways to earn points, and if you are organized it isn't hard to get a good grade. I love that he drops your lowest exam.  That saved me. This class tied all of my chemistry and biology classes together.

This class has a ton of information. It is really hard and take a lot of time, but Tessem is upfront about it. It was the last class I took in the major, and definitely the toughest. Lots of reading, lots of studying is required. It completely saved me in my med school biochemistry class.

For your sake, I wish there was another option. He's friendly in class but tough behind the scenes. Do yourself a favor and take this class alone or with very easy classes, you'll be spending most of your time on this one. Assignments aren't too bad (just time-consuming), it's the exams that kill your grade. Focus on the essay questions. Good luck!

Good: Grading system and assignments are clear from the beginning. If you are willing to put in the effort, you can score well on assignments. Bad: HARD tests. Mistakes on exams which Dr. Tessem was not willing to discuss or examine. You have to memorize literally everything on the slides. Occasionally demeaning but probably isn't intentional.

Tessem is the only professor for this class, so he's your only option. In order to succeed in this class you need to go to office hours and memorize all the pathways and all the slides. No Joke. It's super intense, and Dr. Tessem isn't interested in lightening the load. I would defs take this class with a 12 credit load, the resentment gets real.

Professor Cannon is super nice, fun, and really knows his stuff. There is a lot of reading and homework, but it's honestly very easy and manageable. Attendance isn't mandatory—I only went a few times and still got an A. Overall, it's a great class if you stay on top of the work.

Not REL C 225, but REL C 351(world religions). I CANNOT speak higher of a professor. Dr. Cannon always brought the spirit to class and his lectures were clear, engaging, and interesting. Throughout the semester you'll have a number of pop quizzes, if you read the textbook you'll be fine!  Reviews are great prep for exams.  Such a fun class!

Lots of reading that have to do with the quizzes at the beginning of class. the professor is willing to work with you and zoom streams classes in case you can't come to class. Fun to work with and cares about the kids.

Dr. Green is incredibly nice. I loved his teaching style, even though syntax isn't my jam. He shows some evidence, asks 'why does this happen?', presents hypotheses, gives evidence, has the class evaluate which hypothesis fits best, rinse and repeat till we had a comprehensive theory. One assignment/week, never busy work. Overall a good fit for me.
Prof Green truly cares about his students and improving his classes. His lectures feel like conversations and he is funny in an unintentional sort of way. Highly recommend!

This is a group-project heavy class. But don't worry! Prof. Green knows how awful group work is. He is willing to shift groups around and has a group assessment at the end of every project so you can honestly rate your classmates. I have had the best group projects in my life through this class; Prof. Green knows what he's doing.

Honestly, he was just so fun. If you're in the editing major, and your procrastinating taking this class, take it with him and it will probably be a good experience, as long as you're willing to do group projects, which actually went really well for this class.

Prof. Green has an organized system and knows what he is doing. It was nice to be able to know what was going on, even when the subject material was confusing. There is a lot of homework but it's all helpful.

Professor Green is a great teacher who really cares about his students. He's definitely a bit of a nerd, but who isn't in the linguistics department? Syntax is a little bit like the math of linguistics, so be prepared for deep thinking and problem solving. The class motto, "It's okay to be wrong." is the essence of the classroom as well.

I've never hated a class more. Do NOT take this if you aren't super passionate about OUTDATED SYNTAX THEORY. You will never take a more irrelevant, useless class. This whole class was a nightmare and felt like a math class (that gross). Complete waste of time. Also, it's listed as an editing elective but is really only suited for linguists.

I have taken multiple Japanese classes, all from different teachers at BYU since 301, and none of them burnt me out like this one. I had so much to do that I could never properly study for tests and averaged like 65% on every exam. Most of my peers were in the same boat. This class had no objective, just torture.

Peterson Sensei is very nice and gives good explanations on all the readings and relevant info. Basically just do the readings and try your best to learn and use the vocabulary and you will be fine. 1 exam gets dropped so you don't even have to take the final if you don't need to. Don't forget to mark attendance quizzes for fact class

I didn't have too many problems with the class being a return missionary with a good grasp of the language, but if you don't have that foundation I feel like this class would be super hard. Even at my level I struggled with the workload alone, so I can't imagine how difficult it would be to stay caught up if you found those things difficult.

As long as you have a decent understanding of Japanese, you should be fine. Yes, there is a good amount of homework, but it is not difficult in any way. If you show up to class and pay attention, you'll get an A. Also, Peterson sensei is very kind

I'm a bit confused on others frustration in this class. I am an RM, but I knew that not everyone's level in 301 would be perfectly in line with the class. It may be tough, or easy depending on your prior knowledge and humility to just read and learn the stories no what. My speaking skills improved a ton from this class, I thought it was great.

Great professor (5), awful class(1/5). Professor Peterson himself is a great teacher, but the demands that the humanities department places on the 301 classes for languages is absurd and mundane. Learning languages is straightforward, evaluating progress is not. Competency in the course is reliant on knowledge of the textbook and not the language.
He may have the credentials, but he clearly lacks the expertise.”

If there's one thing I've taken out of this class, it's to *never* take another Japanese class at BYU again.
Peterson-sensei's teaching style really didn't work for me.

If you're here for the challenge exam, no one got an A on all, JAP 101.. 202... It's extremely difficult, even for return missionaries. This class wasted my time, tuition, and effort at BYU. Awful experience—don't take it! I hated this class because it's not designed to actually teach Japanese. This isn't a proper Nihongo class.

So much busy work. It feels a little pointless and like you're not learning helpful Japanese. It's kanji heavy and tests are pretty difficult. However, you could get not good grades on the exams and still get an A in the class if you do the rest of the assignments.

It's hard to teach a language. I didn't like that the class got very difficult and kanji-heavy midway through. I did not have the bandwidth for a 4-credit class, and would recommend that you have a strong motivation for Japanese and a lighter course load when you take it. We had 4 TA's rotate in our class at random and that was the WORST!!

Rough class. Don't believe the whole "it'll be so easy as an RM" ish. It isn't easy for anyone. But it will help you keep up your japanese and if you try you will succeed. Peterson sensei cares so much about his students and is fr so kind. I wish he taught all the japanese classes. Attendance is SO mandatory and this class will kill ya but have fun

[non-RM] it is more of a game of guessing what Peterson Sensei is thinking. he gives SO much busy work I feel so overwhelmed and unable to actually learn. I am only learning how to pass the class, not learning Japanese. The material isn't even that hard, but i am struggling :( can't wait to finish this class. he's a nice guy tho

Non-RM here. The class was a lot of work, but an A is achievable. Discussions twice a week are conducted only in Japanese, but you had the discussion prompts beforehand to prepare. To pass the tests, you need to go to midterm and final review days. Without them, you will fail. For other assignments, follow the rubrics closely to get full points.

Peterson sensei is just a really nice and chill professor. He knows A LOT about Japanese and always has an answer for questions related to grammar and vocab. His class is set up in a way to help his student had speaking opportunities which is what students studying Japanese at BYU need. Overall pretty good professor!
His class isn't too hard, but you don't really learn too much, especially for RMs. If you want to just get language credit, it's perfect for you.

Peterson Sensei is great... I am not sure why he doesn't have better reviews on here. If you are an RM, this class will be an absolute breeze for you. If not, it could be pretty difficult. There are so many assignments in this class but the tests are worth almost nothing, you just need to come to class prepared every day and you'll do great.

EVERYTHING you do is graded, so as long as you complete your hw and show up to class you'll do just fine. It's a lot of work and the course is not organized that well in my opinion, but Peterson Sensei is overall really caring and you can tell he is very passionate about teaching Japanese. You're definitely graded more by the TAs though.

JAPAN 301 is a time-intensive class. Expect to spend 10+ hours on the class each week. The grade is divided between many different assignments, so having a bad day won't hurt you too much. Overall, a great class. Like every Japanese class, you will get out of it what you put in. Go to Peterson-sensei and the TA's office hours and ask questions!

I think that most the complaints aren't the fault of Peterson sensei. I think it's the fault of the people over the Japanese program at BYU. The class set up isn't very great and if you have lived in Japan you won't learn much. BUT Peterson sensei is a great professor who is very willing to answer questions and accessible outside of class! 9/10!
Not a great professor. I didn't feel like we were learning anything. It's more of rote memorization and a lot of trying to guess what the professor is thinking.

Expectations surrounding projects are extremely unclear and his grading is wildly inconsistent. The class is comprised of student-led presentations and discussions every time. He fishes for certain answers and penalizes you for having a different opinion.

The class isn't super difficult to get a decent grade in, but I didn't feel like I learned anything outside of the work I had to put into the assignments. Peterson is pretty easygoing, but doesn't really prepare you or give you direction on what you need to do to improve.

There is a lot of work needed for this class. It required a lot of my time, but easy to get an A when I put in the time. If you have a good TA and friends in the class, it's a very fun class to take. The teacher is very easy-going, but I don't think I learned that much from him. It was more from doing the assignments.

4 credits means lots of work. It was mostly completion work, so if you put in the time it's an easy A. Participate in the TA classes. I loved learning Japanese in Japan but didn't care very much for this class. But some love it! The challenge exam credits are great! Peterson Sensei is very easy-going and teaches what's on the tests.

Prof. Peterson is a really easygoing guy, and goes over the textbook pretty thoroughly on his T Th classes. The TA's teach the MWF classes, so your grade is tied much more to their classes. The tests are worth only 20% of your grade, and have 3 sections taken separately. There are midterms every other week, but he drops your lowest scores.

This was a great class! So much of it was focused on becoming a better scientist and student, and I feel like I was able to improve on both of them. He gives really good feedback and the discussions are effective in making students think. He makes it clear when he is making an educated guess. Tests were fair, yet pushed me to do better.

This was one of the first college level course I ever took and I wasn't totally sure what to expect. Luckily, Professor Shumway makes himself very available and is so easy to talk to, if you reach out he won't leave you in the dark. The reading is fair and you can definitely succeed in this class.

This was one of the first college level courses I ever took. As an incoming freshman I didn't know exactly what to expect but Professor Shumway makes himself available and is very easy to talk to. This class is very do-able if you pay attention to lecture and keep up with the readings. I got an A- as a very green freshman.
I liked this class and did not find it overly-difficult. Lots of reading and very lecture heavy but the assignments were straight-forward and fairly graded.

Mixed feelings about him! I'd recommend taking it in the spring/summer! If you do the reading and take notes in lectures you'll be fine and he's a nice / funny guy that cares a lot. Exams were rough though. You are need to retain a lot and free write an essay using sources yet no book or notes. Hard for my learning style but it could work for you!

Definition of a mixed bag. His lectures are awesome, super nice guy. His tests are formatted in a way that makes studying really easy. But...on the last day of finals only 2 assignments from the entire semester had been graded (out of only 7). Each exam was 44% of grade (so 88% total). Some stuff on the exams we straight up never talked about.

Probably the worst professors I've ever had. He's a great guy, but he blows through content way faster than anyone can keep up with. He tests on obscure content and forces recall unrealistically. He claims it is because historians write, but any self-respecting historian will have sources infront of them when they write about them.

Super good guy but this class is set up so terribly. It's super lecture heavy without a clear understanding of what exactly you're supposed to be taking from the lectures. A lot of readings with the same problems. You are expected to memorize a boatload of things very throughly. Again, good guy but this class is not it.

Taking this class felt like being dropped into a maze with no map, no flashlight, and a pop quiz at every dead end. Lectures were a chaotic blend of vague and off-topic rambling, leaving the whole class collectively confused and slightly afraid to ask questions. History really interest me but I left the class with no knowledge of the subject.

Professor Shumway was awesome! Most people complain about the amount of reading, but I felt it was pretty standard, and if you actually did the reading and did the work everything makes sense. He is a great teacher with good humor and he did good at making things that should be boring actually interesting. Would take again.
lectures are very unorganized. not very personable. won't give you your grades until the end of the semester. midterm and final over 60% of final grade. would not take this class again

Professor Shumway shows up late to every class, and begins his lectures without introduction, or review. They are extremely unorganized, and most times irrelevant. His exams are very poorly structured, and no amount of studying will help in performing well. If I had known what this class entailed, I would have dropped it as soon as possible.

DO NOT TAKE! Regardless if you are a history buff and have always enjoyed history - this class will make you regret all of your life choices. Professor Shumway gives lectures that DO NOT help on the exams. Almost impossible pop quizzes: 7 paragraphs written response questions in 8 minutes. Lots of pointless reading useless for lectures and exams.

I wish I dropped out of this class when I had the chance. There is so much reading, lectures are all over the place, he doesn't make sense most of the time. He doesn't answer the questions and just promotes his Latin American class or he just goes way off topic. His quizzes are impossible to finish on time and doesn't give the class enough time.
Shumway can't organize a lecture to save his life or his students.

I would not recommend this class, especially to first semester college students. I came to find out that you don't actually need to read, if you don't have a history background going to class is helpful ( eventhough everyone else is asleep), and get ready to memorize for tests. Memorizing 7-10 sources for three essay prompts and 40 vocab terms.

Do not take this class. There is SO MUCH READING. And, his lectures do not correlate with the reading! Tests are 40% of your grade with like 5 assignments total in the gradebook. His instructions for everything are so vague and the TA's are so difficult to find/ use/ get a ahold of. Please please please do not take this class! You WILL regret it.

Dr. Shumway is a nice guy however his teaching style is not great. The organization of the lectures are confusing, he jumps around several different topics and does not follow a singular line. The reading is very heavy, there are pop quizzes and he grades very slowly. The midterm and final are each about 40% of the class grade

Dr. Shumway is a great guy! His classes are very interesting and are overall quite easy (compared with other history classes). He isn't easy to get ahold of, so make sure to use the TA's. Also keep on top of readings for quizzes. He's a very easygoing person, which I love. Great guy and great class! I would definitely take it again.

This was my least favorite class I have ever been in. I went to every lecture, all the lectures were rather scattered information-wise. The midterm was worth 40% of the grade, as was the final exam. The essay portion of the exam, we were expected to answer the question using tons of primary sources, closed book. Don't take this class!

Professor Shumway is a good guy and really enjoys teaching but the lectures weren't very focused and never made me feel like I was prepared for the exams. Barely any assignments so you have to do good on the midterm and final because both are worth around 40% of your grade each. Not much help from the TAs either.

I learned nothing, the pop quizzes are on small details I didn't even pick up when I read. He does care about what he teaches and the books are kinda interesting but you don't get your grades until the end of semester and the grading is very strict and hard. I hate this class and wouldn't recommend unless you like reading a ton.

This class was ROUGH! I went to class every time, took extensive notes on the readings and lectures, studied hard and didn't get an A. The tests are incredibly difficult, expected to memorize 28 different sources for final essays with NO NOTES. This class shouldn't be a general. Shumway was nice but had little interaction with him.

I spent hours doing the reading for this class, but didn't do well on the pop quizzes. He doesn't respond to emails. You will not know your grade until the week before finals because he doesn't update grades. You will have to study really hard for the midterm and final to be able to pass. I would avoid this class with this professor at all costs.
Heavy on the reading between classes. There are pop quizzes, but that is clearly stated in the rubric. Genuinely excited about history.

not accessible outside of class. Heavy on reading, and had a lotof pop quizzes that were difficult to prepare for given the large amount of reading assigned for a GE. Not very willing to offer up a lot of feedback, and even after meeting with the TA to have a paper fully checked, the advice he gave was not used in the grading. Would not take again

This was the only time Ive dropped below an A at BYU. I did all the readings, came to every lecture, and slaved over the tests. He was a super harsh grader for the essay questions and on the exams you had to match an entire person/event/definition to a one word description. Very late grader so I didnt know my status until the end of the semester

Professor Shumway is kind and loves what he does, but man his tests make no sense and we read a lot. He is very slow to get grades in and so you never really know what you've got in the class. He does provide a study guide, but all of the terms were things that were maybe mentioned once. The class and assignments aren't too bad, but the tests are.

He assigns very long and convoluted readings and expects you to remember the tiniest details. He's one of those professors who expects you to have memorized everything you've ever read and everything he's ever said (which often rambles on seemingly insignificant details) and be able to write about it as if you have been studying it as long as him.

Super nice guy and quick to respond to email. Never went to class- lectures were WAY to long and boring. Read a chapter before each class, and 2 books throughout the semester. Takes forever to grade. I read the study guide about a week before exams and still managed a B. He's a great person, but I probably wouldn't take him again.

Made it clear he didn't like teaching online and didn't care for the GE he was teaching. He teaches history through in depth studies of specific people, but almost none of his lectures appear on tests. Only grades are pop-quizzes and exams, questions are almost all trivia found in footnotes of the textbook. Did not grade a thing until finals week.

He is a very nice guy and you can tell he loves what he teaches. But his lectures are dull and way too long. Waaay to long. They go on forever. Unfortunately, he always asks silly questions that no one wants to answer and I am sure having class over zoom makes people want to answer them even less. Nice guy though. Super specific questions on tests.

Professor Shumway is a super nice guy, but his class drags on forever. The two tests (midterm and final) that we took in class made up 75 % of the points we were graded on. It's clear that he knows his stuff, but the material is presented to you in a very boring way. Most lectures consisted of a powerpoint saturated with 80's references.

Very boring lectures, they seem to drag on for an eternity. Tons of reading, with a very dry textbook. I usually love history classes, but this one was an exception. Used a standard textbook, sourcebook, and two novels for the class text. You'll read most if not all parts of all of them. Very friendly guy definitely knows his stuff, just boring.

SO MUCH READING!!! Gives random pop quizzes on the readings he assigned. Assigns 30+ pages every night and expects you to read it all deeply because he will give you tests based on ridiculously specific details from those 30+ pages. Lectures are very boring and seem to drag on and on.
Great class filled with a lot of reading. Dr. Shumway is a really great and understanding professor. Provides a study guide for each test, do it and you're good.

Worst class I've taken in my 4 years at BYU. His classes were unprofessional (cheap 80's movies made up 50% of class), disorganized, and unrelated. His tests were 80% what you read, 15% never heard of it, and 5% from class. Grading was impossibly harsh, where even a 5 point extra credit reflection paper doesn't get an A. Avoid at all costs.

This class is VERY hard and frustrating. Be prepared to read a lot every night. He gives pop quizzes and none of his exams include multiple choice. The midterm and final are mostly just short answer and exam questions. His Powerpoints are hard to take notes on and he tends to ramble. A very nice teacher, but a difficult class to pass.

I really love history but I felt frustrated with this class. He tends to ramble about information that is not really very important. I liked him as a person but I didn't feel like I learned from his lectures. You need to read the text book to understand. And the tests are basically just an essay. I wasn't ever sure how to study efficiently...

This class has SO much reading. The teacher just lectures. He is a nice guy, but I don't think I have learned anything but I've spent hours reading for the class. Also, he grades really hard and the tests involve lots of writing and are very hard. For a generals credit, this class is not worth it.

Jeff's History of Argentina class is amazing because he feels really passionate about it and that passion passes onto the student.  Great course, lots of good reading material.  Not very strict on reading completions, but it helps on the midterm.

The difficulty is more of the class than the professor. Be flexible to have various teachers come in and teach their lectures about their topics of study. Attendance is important because there are lecture quizzes. Through much work and reading, one will be even more ready for future social science classes. Stay on top of the research paper.

Lecture is basically useless. He spent more time talking about Hawaiian sovereignty than both world wars combined. Boring, drones on, tries to be funny but fails miserably. Unfortunately, he gives pop quizzes, so you have to attend the entirety of his annoying lecture. I wish that I had not taken this class.
Hard history 1500-present. LOTS of reading, pop quizzes, and the tests are pretty difficult, but he gives a pretty good study guide. Worth taking his class, it can be pretty challenging at times.
I took three classes from him and I always enjoyed them. He puts in a decent amount of effort to make his classes enjoyable and he's a fun guy. I hope he's still hosting Argentine Asado's.

Nice guy but the lectures are pretty boring. He posts a study guide for the midterm and final so work with your class mates on Google Docs or something and that should be helpful. There aren't many assignments except for a few random pop quizzes on the readings which are usually pretty long and not that helpful.

Dr. Shumway is a very skilled teacher. He uses a variety of techniques to help everyone learn. As a history professor, i felt like he didn't give enough assignments and relied too much on a challenging 8 page paper and 2 midterm tests. His lectures are great. Take this class if you want to be challenged and love to read. If you don't, avoid it.

I loved this class! There is a lot of reading involved but it is completely doable.  The midterm and the final were not bad at all because he gives you a study guide with literally everything you need to study to do well.  He really wants you to learn and succeed in his class.  I enjoyed his lectures a lot and how much they made me think.

He tells you that it is moderate reading but it's about 30+ pages a day. He is very boring and teaches so much useless information. Didn't learn anything beneficial in the class, seemed like I was just listening to him read a text book every class.

I enjoyed his class. He is a good person and is willing to work with you, but he is confusing. His tests are really hard and he gives you the study guide just a week before the test so you have to work super hard to memorize it all on time. Also, he does not have many assignments, so the biggest portion of your grade are the midterm and the final.

In this class you will have to read an immense amount from dismally dry textbooks. These readings have random pop quizzes that make up a fairly large portion of your grade. Tests are huge and entirely written--thus, entirely subjective. Additionally, you have to read two novels and write an 8 paper on one with brutally vague parameters.
He will meet with you and answer any questions on an individual basis. Very helpful. I would take this from him again.
Lectures were entertaining enough and we watched a lot of movies in class.
Great class! Honestly didn't even work that hard and still did fairly well. Professor Shumway kicks butt, and he's very literate on many important issues. Take any class from him that you can!

I didn't have too hard of a time with this class. Just make sure you read every day (occasionally there are reading quizzes) and make a shared Google doc for the midterms and finals. The Prof has skills at basketball!

The first day of class he gave an awesome lecture; by the end of the semester I was disappointed. Its a history class so obviously there's lots of reading. Occasionally he does pop quizzes on reading and they're hard! Final paper on a book you read on your own time (don't procrastinate it!). Tests cover TONS of material barely mentioned in class :/
The best lectures at BYU in my opinion. Very entertaining. Test can be hard though.

Good teacher, the lectures are really interesting, he engages people in the class by asking questions.  Uses media which makes the class more interesting.  There aren't a lot of assignments so make sure you study for the midterm and final and do a good job on the paper and its easy to get a good grade.
He's a nice guy, but really boring and there's tons of reading.

This class was very "meh." He wasn't on top of things in the class. He canceled our term paper because he forgot to assign it. Beware of the pop quizzes, they can be rough. But he uses a lot of audiovisuals. He seemed to dwell a lot on some things that didn't seem as important as he purported them to be.

Awful! Horrible! In 9 semesters of college, this has been the worst!  He just talks and talks and talks. And when he does ask a question, he gets afraid of silence so he'll answer it himself after 3 seconds.  There is absolutely no homewrok which means that there is no preparation for any exam or quiz. Ifyou care for your grade,don't take this clas

I really enjoyed this class. Shumway was great teacher who brought some interesting insight into our classroom discussions. Sure, there is a ton of reading in this class, but this is a history class and it would be impossible to discuss everything in class.
He seemed to me to be somewhat cynical. I found it difficult to feel intellectually stimulated by his biased persona and inability to focus on and tie together main ideas.

Awesome guy and great teacher.  Not as intellectual as some, but really down to earth, and easy to talk to.  Good discussion, humble guy, doesn't have the typical god-complex.  I really enjoyed his class, and thought the grading was very fair.

I was looking forward to "modern" latin american history, but it was LAME! I do not think he considered the fact that we all had lives. Too much reading, the exams were ok b/c they were easy b.c. I learned because I read, his lectures were pointless.

I was a big fan. Lots of writing and a big research project for the final, which was tough but very rewarding. Class discussion was great and had lots of variety. He seems to have a few detractors, but, everybody hates their 201/202 professors ;)

He is a great professor who makes his lectures entertaining and interesting. His teaching tends to focus on specific events and themes rather than a rote memorization of facts. He is also very willing to help, you just need to ask.

I really enjoyed this class. Professor Shumway was great. His stories are interesting, and I think he grades things fairly. He had an Argentine asada for students at his house that was amazing. Also, he's pretty cute. I took Latin American History on a whim, and because of this class I changed my major to Latin American Studies.

Dr. Shumway is knowledgeable but his lecture outlines are cryptic and he doesn't follow them closely. I agree that note taking was difficult. His tests are ridiculously subjective, almost all essay and short answer. Not my favorite cl**** but you can do well. You must do the readings if you hope to p****, quote from them relentlessly in your essays.
Incredibly ridiculous class.  Boring teacher, too much reading and other homework, seems to grade arbitrarily.  Just too hard.
There are quizes every couple weeks from the readings.  Turn in a couple papers.  One long paper.  For the tests, just study the study guide he hands out and you'll get perfectly fine.
Good knowledge of topic but unorganized.
He's a great teacher.  The quizes are pretty specific so make sure to do the reading but he is very interesting and really cares about his students.
Posted an outline for lectures which wasn't followed to closely. This made note taking difficult. He has a good personality though and is pretty humerous. His tests are a little on the harder side.

Class was pretty boring. This is not his best subject; I think he usually focuses on Latin American history, so when students would ask him questions about Hist 202 material, he usually said, "I don't know." Tests were harder than necessary, TA's do all the grading and take forever. Only 2 tests over tons of material.

He is pretty boring and his help sessions are unhelpful.  He doesn't seem like he cares about the students.  Also, he is pretty bad at using technology in teaching.  I love history but I     d this class.

Lectures are long and sometimes really boring-but it's history, what do you expect. It was hard to follow his outlines, but if you read and study really well for the tests, a good grade is possible. If you fall asleep a lot, this is not a good 2 1/2 hour class. We had to take the final, so don't be fooled.

His lectures are sooooo dry!  It sounds like he is just reading a book all of class.  I hated preparing for his tests but I did fairly well in the class.  The one great thing is that he didn't make us take a final if we didn't want to.  If you were happy with your grade, you could skip the final which is the best way to go!

Dr Shumway knows this subject well but the essay tests are hard.  It is difficult to khow what he is looking for in answer to the essay questions and he grades hard.  He showed a lot of film clips to illustrate his points but is delivery in class lectures is dry.  Stay awake in class and read the text and you'll do well.
I've definately had worse History classes.

If you aren't interested in this class you will have to try really hard to do well.  It isn't that he isn't a great teacher because frankly I think he is but the material is hard.  Read and study and you pass.

If you do your reading and take notes on EVERYTHING he says then i'm sure its easy, but you cant sleep through class at all and still expect a good test grade. shows lots of media clips, but its hard to pay attention sometimes because he sounds like he is choppily reading everything he says.
Very interesting lectures, very bright guy. Did the coolest thing ever, at the final, just before we started, said,"If you like your grade as it is right now, you can walk out." So I did. SWEET!

Dr. Shumway is a very good teacher.  It is a demanding class, but I highly recommend it.  He knows his stuff and makes you interested in it too.  Lots of reading, but most of it is interesting.  Tests aren't too bad if you study the review sheets.

This is a great professor. His lectures are interesting and insightful. Work load is reasonable. There is quite a bit of outside work (movies, etc), but it doesn't feel like busywork. Test questions are handed out before each test. 1 midterm, 1 final.

Exams are tough but if you have a study group, you're golden. There's also lots of extra resources for help. Everything you learn and do in this class is applicable and useful. Professor Derrick so kind and has a lot of insight in real-world application. If you put in the effort, you can absolutely get an A

Professor Derrick is amazing. She is extraordinarily kind and responsive. She puts effort into making things helpful and engaging. If you are interested in pre-nursing, she has a lot of insight into healthcare from actually working in clinical settings. The tests are tricky, but there are a lot of resources provided to assist.

She has no idea what she's talking about, she goes off on rants and anytime someone asks a question she asks the class for an answer or looks it up. she reads straight off her slides and can't even pronounce things correctly. I also wouldn't take nutrition advice who needs it more themselves.

Didn't seem to know the content herself, only used borrowed slides and homework, if asked a question in class she would deflect, not answer or just pass it onto the TA. Exams are hard however, with much studying you may succeed but I always felt as they were unnecessarily difficult with tough graders on everything. Learned and had fun on occasion.

Professor Derrick is on the ball. She is very kind. Her lectures are clear and she values every student and their questions. She prepares you well for her tests. It's not an easy class but she makes it very manageable without asking too much. You will spend very little time outside of class studying because her classes are very well done.

NDFS 100 is already a tough class because of the amount of material you have to learn, but Professor Derrick broke it down and made it fun! She cares about her students and is so fun to be around. Her class is easier too.

Exams are tough but if you have a study group, you're golden. There's also lots of extra resources for help. Everything you learn and do in this class is applicable and useful. Professor Derrick so kind and has a lot of insight in real-world application. If you put in the effort, you can absolutely get an A

Professor Derrick is amazing. She is extraordinarily kind and responsive. She puts effort into making things helpful and engaging. If you are interested in pre-nursing, she has a lot of insight into healthcare from actually working in clinical settings. The tests are tricky, but there are a lot of resources provided to assist.

She has no idea what she's talking about, she goes off on rants and anytime someone asks a question she asks the class for an answer or looks it up. she reads straight off her slides and can't even pronounce things correctly. I also wouldn't take nutrition advice who needs it more themselves.

Didn't seem to know the content herself, only used borrowed slides and homework, if asked a question in class she would deflect, not answer or just pass it onto the TA. Exams are hard however, with much studying you may succeed but I always felt as they were unnecessarily difficult with tough graders on everything. Learned and had fun on occasion.

Professor Derrick is on the ball. She is very kind. Her lectures are clear and she values every student and their questions. She prepares you well for her tests. It's not an easy class but she makes it very manageable without asking too much. You will spend very little time outside of class studying because her classes are very well done.

NDFS 100 is already a tough class because of the amount of material you have to learn, but Professor Derrick broke it down and made it fun! She cares about her students and is so fun to be around. Her class is easier too.

Printmaking is such a hard and demanding class, but Jen makes it as easy as possible. She gives amazing personalized feedback, and perfectly clear instructions. You will have a lot of work but this is how every art class is. Jen is so funny and sweet, and willing to answer any and all questions. Definitely take this class from her!

Jen is a wonderful professor and is so clear with the directions and information she shares. She has an amazing balance of being your friend but also being your teacher. She gives amazing feedback and helps you to see new ways to improve your work. She has very reasonable deadlines and assignments as well.
Jen is a sweetheart and a real gem in the BYU art department. She is very approachable and willing to help each student succeed, even though the subject matter is difficult.

Professor Watson has been my favorite Art Professor so far. Printmaking is not an easy subject and there are a lot of different steps and chemicals. She is extremely helpful and allows you to redo prints if you so wish. She grades fair and gives you the opportunity to improve. Jen is very soft spoken, so sit close. 10/10 would recommend.

An excellent teacher but her class and subject are hard. She is amazing in that she will let you turn in anything at any time so long as you have something to show for it on the due date. You can rework any projects (and once you complete them once it goes a lot faster, so it's actually worth redoing things in this class.) Awesome teacher, love her

Dr. Nelson is awesome! The class was pretty discussion heavy, but it honestly helped me learn a lot. The hardest part of this class was the anthology project, but you have all semester to work on it, and the TAs and Dr. Nelson are really helpful with it too. She cares so much about this class and her students.

Psych 310: This class is SO hard. The homework takes 60 to 90 mins to complete and are full of trick questions. The lectures just don't teach you well on how to conduct and report your research nor how to analyze the results. The class was more focused on learning about the technicalities of research, but not on HOW to DESIGN and ANALYZE your own

This class was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at BYU! Her lectures are so interesting and she has a lot of group discussion time so you get to know people in the class really well. My biggest complaint is that the reading quizzes take like an hour to complete, but they prepare you really well for the lectures and discussions.

Dr. Nelson is amazing! I learned so much in this class, and it even helped grow my testimony, even though it "should have been" one of my less spiritual classes. She is so passionate about what she teaches, which made me excited to learn. She is such a cool person, too, with an amazing story and inspiring resilience.

I LOVED Professor Nelson! She is passionate and bears her testimony very frequently and related what we were learning about back to the gospel. Her class is set up in a flipped classroom model, so you learn new material outside of class and then apply it in groups in class. So its super important that you read the textbook before class.

Professor Nelson is a wonderful teacher. She is very passionate about what she teaches and is very inspirational. Her class is super fun and not very difficult, but you learn a lot! I really enjoyed her class, it was the best class I have taken at BYU. I feel like I came out of the class not only knowing much more, but also as a better person.

dr nelson is fantastic! super nice, a spiritual giant, and loves her students. you can tell that she loves her job. lots of in class participation but it's totally doable. i recommend, as a psych major.

Prof. Nelson is so awesome! I loved this class and learned a ton. She is super passionate about psychology, and that made everything so enjoyable. She also makes it super easy to do well. Be prepared for group discussions every class and mandatory readings though. Probably the most interesting textbook I've ever read though, so its not too bad.

I LOVED Dr. Nelson's class! Everything she teaches is applicable to real life and it's clear she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Course can be a little difficult at times but nothing too challenging if you study hard. The quizzes are all based on completion and I love that she has us in groups because I made great connections.

Was very open to discussing grades and willing to change the grade if you made a strong case for why you should get it. I felt like her lectures weren't very informative or worth going to if you had taken any other Human Development courses beforehand.

I liked having weekly quizzes instead of exams -- I printed off the quiz questions before class and used them to guide my note-taking. AI was not allowed for essays, but the focus was more on improvement than producing the perfect essay. Phones/laptops were not allowed during class. Write lots of notes to have material for essays.

She designed her class to be easy but still impactful, especially by choosing weekly quizzes over those big finals and midterms. As a professor, she was very kind, earnest, experienced, and made the effort to take in the input of students if they wanted to share.

She gives very engaging and well-prepared lectures—probably some of the most consistently strong lectures I've had. Be ready for a heavy workload (a lot of readings and assignments), but it's manageable if you stay on top of things. She clearly cares about students and creates a supportive classroom environment. You'll learn a lot and be challenged

I only have good things to say about Dr Erickson. She is the most amazing professor I have had yet at BYU. She genuinely is one of the kindest people, so understanding, merciful, gracious, and knowledgeable. You could tell that she has a passion for what she does. The class is fairly easy. Just attendance, quizzes, and 4 easy essays.
Amazing professor. This course alone is enough to improve anyone's life, but the way Dr. Erickson teaches is just phenomenal. Couldn't recommend anyone more than her.

Professor Erickson can be a little overbearing. I can get by just fine doing the weekly quizzes and attendance just fine but be prepared to share your thoughts a lot in class and online. She also does not enjoy it when you critique the articles rather than just summarize/comment on them.
I absolutely loved this class! She is so kind and smart! It's a discussion based class, so you get a lot of different ideas, which is fantastic!

Super thoughtful and caring. Class had a littttttle more work than the average religion class, but it wasn't bad at all. No midterm, no final, just a couple short essays. Her lectures were great and taught me stuff I'll actually use in my life going forward.
There's a good amount of articles you'll have to read, but it's not bad. She's a great teacher and her material is super organized and it's really hard to fail the quizzes if you do the study guides.

I adore her!! I have no idea why there are a few bad ratings. She is so educated and passionate on what she teaches and has rewired my brain on the way I think about families. She connects it back to gospel truths and everything is clear and feels healing to learn about. TAKE HER!!!!!!!

I always love my religion classes and was really looking forward to this one... she is so kind and passionate- has the "almost-crying voice" all the time... beware you cannot have laptop or phone out. and if you don't discuss things with your neighbor long enough she will come talk to you. The readings and quizzes realllly felt like busy work sadly

University Accessibility students beware... she gave me a pretty hard time about asking for an extension on something (which is a part of my University accomodations) and I never felt comfortable in that class after that.

Wouldn't recommend taking Erickson. There was weekly quizzes that were way too difficult and multiple long papers. She talks just as much about science as religion. Very rarely did she actually rely on doctrine. Intense eye contact holding her heart style of relief society president. So if that is your thing I guess...

Respectful, very clear what is expected from you, and spend time with the TA's!! They are your direct ticket to success on the papers. Meet with them and you will get an A. Learned a lot about myself in this class and Prof Erickson cares a lot about the material and it shows.

Sister Erickson is one of the most amazing people I have ever met. I have never felt so seen, understood, & cared for by a BYU professor. She will get to know you by name, she really cares about your life & other classes. The assignments & content are not difficult at all, easily my least stressful class. Her lectures changed my life forever.

I loved professor erickson, she had amazing lectures and you can tell she is very passionate about what she teaches. She only has a weekly quiz, and 4 papers throughout the semester. There are weekly study guides so you know lookout for in lectures. The papers are specific but there is clear rubric and even example, cant get more easy than that.

I loved this class!An amazing professor that cares so deeply for her subject matter. 4 papers throughout the semester, to do well on them you must follow her format with exactness. But follow the examples and you'll be fine. There are weekly quizzes that are easy enough and some extra credit opportunities. DONT GET THE TEXTBOOK (it's not necessary)

I love this professor, she is so smart and has so much good information. There is a quiz every week which is proctored, there are also 4 papers throughout the semester and the TA's grade hard. There is a textbook she had us get but we barely used it and felt like a waste of money to me. Her information was very helpful though.

She is really passionate about what she does, and has some interesting perspectives. However, I simply did not like this class. I felt like I was in Sunday school for 3 extra hours a week. 
The powerpoints in lecture are usually very word heavy or disorganized.
Attendance and readings required, also weekly quizzes with a study guide. No big tests.

Out of all the religion professors I've had, she is one of my favorite. She is very genuine and despite other comments Im seeing teaching correct doctrine. She teaches truth that is revealed from prophets and apostles along with stats that back it up. She is amazing, planning on taking another class from her if the opportunity presents itself.

Doesn't like research that goes against her beliefs. Disagreed with a Meta Analysis I shared about outcomes for kids with traditional vs. LGTBQ+ family structures (it concluded no significant differences). Rhetoric and vibe were on brand for your average BYU Eternal Families class.

Professor Erickson is my favorite religion teacher! She really cares about the success of her students. Weekly quizzes that are very easy, and mandatory attendance. But, not exams, and just a couple essays, with extra credit opportunities! Her lectures had doctrinal evidence to back up everything- with scriptures and words from living prophets.

Easy enough class, lectures were awful. Her facts were sometimes incorrect and a lot of what she was teaching was based on personal opinion, or confirmation bias of things she believed. Liked to use "scientific studies" to back up her things even if it was wrong, and deff not the right teacher unless you LOVE the ideas and rubric of the class.

Do the study guides for the readings for the quiz. Do the quizzes soon after class while its fresh in your mind. 
You can learn a ton from this class if you are willing to be humble. 
It was harder than I expected, but an average amount of work for a religion class. Look for the content she repeats in class and it will likely be on the quiz.

There is a scripture that perfectly describes Dr. Erickson, 2 Nephi 9:28: "When they are learned they think they are wise, and they hearken not unto the counsel of God, for they set it aside, supposing they know of themselves." If you are not a member of the LDS (Mormon) faith, NEVER take this course. Dr. Erickson does not teach correct doctrine.

Dr.Erickson is seriously one of the kindest and most inspirational teachers you will ever meet! She explains everything so well and genuinely cares about all of her students. Her class requires about 1-2 hours of talks or recorded lectures a week, weekly quizzes, 3 papers, and no final. One of my favorite classes this semester!

Professor Erickson is one of the most genuine people I've ever met. I felt the Spirit every time I attended her class, and she made me feel seen and heard. She covers some tough topics with as much sensitivity as possible without compromising the doctrine. I can't recommend enough how much you should take a class from her. An angel of a person.

Professor Erickson was so sweet! I love the way we didn't have big exams, but instead unstressful weekly quizzes. She was awesome, and despite reviews complaining about politics, I felt she was fairly moderate. Some sensitive topics could have been handled with a little more flexibility, but she has a lot of compassion and love for the students :)

This class is not based off doctrine this is families according to her personal philosophies. If you're okay with probing questions, invasive and incorrect teachings, and taking a class that the Spirit is not present in- you found the one! I think she just teaches based off of her personal whimsy, a very traditional, outdated whimsy.

My review is so low because of the way she handles sensitive topics. I was very disappointed in the way she talked about homosexuality & law of chastity. Every discussion is very awkward and brings shame to students if they do not fit the ideal LDS standard. If you are looking for an open minded professor on BYU campus- she is not the one!

graded on weekly quizzes from things discussed in the lecture and 3 assigned talks and 3 papers. the class is a blend of real-world statistics and evidences that prove the inspiration behind the family proclamation. not a super "preachy" class. prof Erickson is great and really cares about the material and students

She is very knowledgeable abt the family. This class impacted my life- she provides lectures on sexual relations & gender that other classes do not discuss! She is a fair grader- talk to her if you have any struggles she is understanding. This course had a decent amount of hwrk but was enjoyable unlike some other religion classes. 10/10 recommend

She was an okay professor, but I was really hoping for an uplifting religion class and she just wasn't it. She didn't have a final and the assignments were super easy. That was the only reason I stayed in the class. Erickson is an easy out for the eternal family requirement.

LOVED this professor. Her insights into the family and family dynamics are great. She tells great stories and you can apply everything you learn to yourself and your family. 4 big papers which take time, but are just about your family. I wrote them all the day before they were due, took 7 hours each ish. Weekly quizzes but based on stuff from class

I LOVE JENET. I cannot say that enough. I seriously rave about this class because I loved it so so much. It really made me see my relationships in a different light, and Pro. Erickson is the kindest, most genuine and sincere person you will ever meet. I learned SO much. I feel so loved and seen by her. I would take this class again in a heartbeat.

Although some content was repetitive, especially if you've taken other SFL classes, Professor Erickson was amazing. She has a passion for what she teaches which makes the course so much more powerful. She handled some hard class circumstances very well, which made me appreciate her even more.
Really caring professor. Gives amazing lectures and insights on the eternal family. Doctrine and research augment this class. Highly recommend. Super easy religion class.
Professor Erickson is a passionate, loving, and incredibly spiritual professor. Every lecture felt like a BYU devotional, and I learned and grew so much from her class. She is amazing!

Dr. Erickson has really engaging and interesting lectures. Attendance is required and reported on your honor. There is a weekly quiz that's pretty easy if you fill out the study guides she provides. The essays can be a little time-consuming but expectations are very clear and TAs are accessible. Take this class from her!

Take this class for an easy A. Do NOT take this class if you get easily uncomfortable. I was fully expecting to learn about the ETERNAL FAMILY but instead listened to 50 minute lectures about gender issues and sexuality, and probably heard the word "intimacy" 6 million times. Her political views are obvious by the way she teaches. Meh class.

She is my favorite professor! She taught the most amazing lectures that were so insightful. She is caring and kind. You just have weekly quizzes and a couple papers that aren't bad! No tests. It was the best religion class ever. Definitely take it!!

Dr. Erickson is a great professor but this class was so so boring. The quizzes are relatively easy if you go to class. Her 4 papers have a very specific grading rubric that is confusing. Dr. Erickson is very passionate and a great person, but I would not take this class if you don't need to.

Loveliest woman on the planet! Very organized with her content on Learning Suite. Always posts slides and lectures after class. She keeps them up all semester for you to refer back to. She gives weekly quizzes on lecture content. She gives study guides to prepare for these quizzes.
Papers take a good amount of time. Recommends starting early.

Dr. Erickson is phenomenal! The key to success is attending class. Weekly quizzes and three papers, with a study guide fore very quiz. No midterms or final! Her passion and social science background allows for you to learn about the Doctrine of the Family in such a powerful way. You will leave this class so much better than you start it! I promise!
Easiest religion class you will ever take! Sweetest professor you will ever have!!

She was incredible! Weekly quizzes with study guides that outline essentially the whole quiz. No tests and four papers but the TA's are super helpful and it isn't very hard to do well on them. Lectures are interesting and you can tell she really cares. Really grateful I took it from her.

Prof. Erickson was so kind! Her lectures were inspiring and informative. We had weekly, lecture-based quizzes, and no exams. We had to write 4 6-7 page papers that were difficult but helped me evaluate my own family and what I've learned in the class. It can feel like a lot but she's a great teacher!

She teaches about the family combining doctrine and social science. If you are sensitive to public discussion of law of chastity/health class topics, this could be a bit of a traumatizing experience. She cares about her students and so does her TA. She shares lots of really good talks and quotes that are so applicable to building a good family life

A great caring and kind professor. She brought so much insight from her background into family studies and made the class really enjoyable. There are a few papers, weekly reading quizzes but no exams! She is always open to answering any questions and will take time out of her day for you to talk to her after class.

Sister Erickson has got to be one of the most kind, caring, sweet human beings on the planet. I don't think anyone could honest say anything against that. This class is what all religion classes should be like: meaningful, inspiring, and low stress. This class has weekly reading assignments and quizzes, 3 papers, and no tests. Super good and easy!

This class was a breath of fresh air! It wasn't too hard and no tests, just 2 essays the whole semester. There are weekly short quizzes that are easy if you attend class. I learned great principles that I want to apply to my future family life and strengthened my testimony! Sister Erickson really cares about her students and is so encouraging.

Professor Erickson is an amazing religion teacher! I have had many individuals recommend me to her class, and I can see why! Her lectures are amazing and you can tell she is passionate. When I took her class, she got to give the devotional to BYU, which was amazing to watch. She is also a kind and caring professor who loves her students very much!

Professor Erickson is an AMAZING professor who genuinely cares for her students. The class consisted of weekly quizzes and the occasional paper, but no tests. She only wants you to focus on the lecture and participate. She made an effort to learn our names and used studies as well as gospel sources to teach familial topics. She's the best!

No big tests, just a few essays scattered throughout. The majority of the class is just attending the lectures and then reading a couple talks each week. You can tell Dr. Erickson cares a lot and wants everyone to understand the importance of the Proclamation. Lectures are all driven on comments that people share, so feel free to ask questions!

Professor Erickson was respectful to the best of her ability when talking about such church-culture-driven topics. Her audience is very much the "Utah-Mormon" kids. I appreciated her willingness to talk about difficult topics. She tried to include everyone in her lessons. Sometimes she would get very passionate, and I would honestly check out.

By far the best religion teacher you will find.  She says things as they are in a caring manner and doesn't allow politics to rule her classroom.  Class is always interesting, and she does an amazing job at proving why "The Family: A Proclamation to the World" is such an important document.  If you want the best experience, take it from her.

This was the easiest religion class I have taken but I really did not enjoy it. Prof Erickson seemed like a great choice but the information she taught seemed very traditional and backwards. She did try to include LGBTQ+ conversations but then would go back and teach the contrary. Always contradicting herself and dodging "controversial' important q

Such an easy class and spiritually uplifting. Weekly quizzes on lectures and reading that weren't bad. 4 essays throughout that were graded easily and took me roughly 1 or 2 hours to write. Talked about controversial topics due to the nature of the course but really made them easy to discuss and understand the church's view while hearing concerns.

I think she is a great professor for someone who feels they do not already know a lot about family dynamics, but if you have a grasp of the family from a gospel and intellectual standpoint then you will learn absolutely nothing. She creates artificial difficulty with tests, which are all purely based on memorization of quotes from class. No Spirit.

Dr. Erickson was very caring and respectful. She led insightful discussions and handled sensitive topics really well without shying away from them. The concepts were really applicable, and the essays helped make them so.

I took her for Eternal Families, and I absolutely loved it. She is a wonderful teacher, and I recommend her to everyone. I feel that I learned an incredible amount from her, and every day I am spiritually strengthened and uplifted in her classroom. She remembers almost everyone's names, and always says hi and checks in with me before class. 10/10

She is a fantastic teacher. I took her for Eternal Families and she was so passionate about it. Obviously some controversial topics had to be discussed and she did a very good job addressing both sides. There is no final or midterm, just a weekly quiz that she helps you out with right before. It's easy enough that you can actually enjoy the content

Wouldn't recommend taking a religion class from her. All I heard come out of her mouth was false doctrine and controversial topics. Learned nothing about marriage or any topics related to Eternal Families. I would sign on for attendance and do work for other classes. No final so it wasn't worth my time and effort to pay attention.

I absolutely love Dr. Erickson. She is really passionate about what she teaches and I left every class feeling the spirit. I recommended her to tons of my friends. If you haven't taken a class from her, you need to!! Great person inside and out.

I loved taking Intro to Family Processes from Professor Erickson. Take SFL 160 if you want an inspiring, informative, and applicable class. She is lovely. The weekly quizzes are easy and no information comes as a surprise. The 4 essays are not hard and allow the student to think critically about their own families. I honestly loved them.

Dr. Erickson is a genuine and caring professor that really knows her stuff. Her lectures are awesome and she's not afraid to tackle a lot of tough subjects. There's a weekly quiz based on the lectures. Take them seriously and do the study guides. The class is only graded on weekly quizzes and 4 papers. Each quiz is about 4-5% of your grade.

Dr. Erickson is so sweet and her class was wonderful! There are four 6-7 page papers, but they aren't too hard and the TA's do a good review. Weekly quizzes that she goes over and gives you a study guide for. The final is a longer quiz that also is super easy. Slides weren't super organized, but that's okay! Take this class!! Please!!

Dr. Erickson is my favorite professor at BYU. If you go to class and pay attention, the weekly quizzes will be super easy. She usually will prep you for them at the end of class as well. I liked not having tests and the papers were fun because you are analyzing families. They are pretty long, but I wrote them the day before and did really well.

Dr. Erickson is so knowledgable! She does really well at connecting the course to the gospel and real life. Felt the spirit like I do in religion classes. The hardest part about the class is the 4 papers. Start working on them early and get feedback from the TAs to make sure your analysis is solid. Weekly quizzes aren't bad-the study guides help!

As a senior, I have taken a lot of classes from different professors, and Dr. Erickson is one of my favorites by far. Very knowledgeable. Very kind. The class has no midterms or finals. Weekly quizzes that have study guides. If you do the study guide, you will do great on the quiz. 4 papers throughout the semester. Pretty straightforward on grading

Professor Erickson is a wonderful professor. She is compassionate, genuine, knowledgeable, and gives clear instructions. I want to be her real life friend! You can do without the textbook. She gives a study guide for the weekly quizzes that tells you exactly what you need to know. There are 4 papers that are lengthy, but you learn a lot from them.

Dr. Erickson was easily one of the best professors I've had. She cares about what she is teaching and she shows that she cares about her students. She teaches about social sciences but is also very spiritual and has a strong testimony of the gospel. As long as you pay attention in lectures, you will do just fine in this class.

Sis. Erickson is a fantastic professor. She taught clearly and effectively and indicated exactly what we needed to know for the weekly quiz, which I found quite easy. There are 4 essays, which I found challenging but definitely doable. There are lots of great resources to help you with those. Textbook is supplemental, I never read it.

I absolutely LOVED professor Erickson! She is very passionate about what she teaches so learning the material was very easy because of that. Grades are based off of weekly quizzes. She creates study guides and if you know the study guides you will be fine and papers. attend the paper reviews and rely on was to pass. Highly recommend this class.

Dr. Erickson is a wonderful woman who stands for church family values in an intelligent, kindhearted way. She dealt with sensitive topics gracefully & we had great discussions about Heavenly Mother, LGBTQ issues, abortion, etc. Maybe she is too conservative for really woke students, but I found the lectures intellectually and spiritually enriching.
