Jenet Erickson is truly knowledgeable about family life and has great insight because of this for the eternal family class. I took it when this was her first time teaching REL C 200 and am glad I took a chance on her. I found her lectures engaging! There are no midterms and the final is just a record of our insights from each unit.

Seriously one of the best classes I've ever taken. More spiritual and inspiring than my religion class. I was so impressed by Professor Erickson. She is so understanding and such an amazing teacher. The class wasn't hard and there's no big tests, just weekly quizzes, and 4 papers. Seriously can't recommend this class enough.

Dr. Erickson is a very well-spoken, intelligent professor. Her lectures are well researched and I loved listening to her lectures! I feel like everyone needs to know what this class teaches. The papers are hard, though. Go to your TA's and get help on the analysis!! They don't give much feedback so you NEED to go to them if you want to improve.

Dr. Erickson is amazing!! She is passionate and knowledgable. You do not need the textbook. She is great, so its not her as a prof, but I will say her TA's are harsher than they need to be for a 100 level class. I would go to the writing center and the workers knew the 160 TA's were notorious for being way too harsh

Dr. Erickson is so sweet! She is very kind to all of her students. The class itself is fairly easy. Also do not buy the textbook, because you won't need it. The most time consuming part of the class is writing the papers. There are 4 in total, but as long as you work with your TA, you should be in good shape.

Easy class, she doesnt grade on attendance but you have to attend the lectures to get credit on the weekly quiz. She teaches things that literally contradict what I learned from other SFL professors so I kinda took what she taught with a grain of salt. Kinda traditional teachings.

Dr. Erickson is one of the kindest souls at BYU! She is so understanding if something happens in your life, and is willing to help. Her lectures are incredible and very interesting! There are quizzes every week and 4 papers. Other than that, no tests! Attendance is mandatory, but you won't even mind because it's a treat to listen to her lectures.
Super easy and amazing class. Dr. Erickson is inspiring and i loved her lectures. Papers aren't too bad either.

This class is pretty easy. You don't need to do any readings, just show up, take the weekly quiz based on the lecture, and write some papers (which are helpful ways to think about how to apply the material and think about your own family). We didn't have any exams, just a final quiz that was weighted the same as the others, although cumulative.

Dr. Erickson is an absolute GEM. Honestly, I think she is the most caring professor I have ever had. She loves her students and knows many of them by name. Before class starts, she will discuss any questions that you have on assignments. She is not a harsh grader and sincerely wants her students to succeed. TAKE ANY CLASS FROM HER AND YOULL LOVE IT

I really enjoyed the class and Prof. Erickson's passion. Her quizzes are hard and you don't have a lot of time to take them, so good luck if you have quiz/test anxiety. Also, she is a tough grader on the papers, especially when you don't come from a strong family background which can make analyzing your family and fulfilling the rubric difficult.

By far my favorite professor. There aren't any tests, just weekly quizzes that you'll need to pay attention for and 4 papers. Her lectures are so engaging and her passion was so contagious that I changed my major to SFL. You should take this class even if you just want to understand your family better!

Prof Erickson is my favorite prof as BYU. Attendance was not graded, but you take a quiz every friday and the lectures give you the answers. She is interesting, engaging, and loves what she teaches. The first day of this class made me change my major to SFL. Loved this class and want to take it again. 4 essays, quiz once a week, no tests.

She got married recently, so to see more ratings check under Jenet Jacob. But I took her for 105 & 371, and she is one of the sweetest people I have ever known. A great teacher. So inspiring. If you take 105, take it from her! I was sad when the semester ended.

By the time you write down your notes for one slide, she's already five slides ahead. She also says the tests are about the same level of difficulty as the homeworks, which isn't true at all. She expected us to teach ourselves a concept because she forgot to cover it in class, then put it on the final.

I struggled to stay on top of the insanely fast lectures. She talks at the speed of light! For Spring, there is so much content you can't digest it all unless you plan to do nothing in your life except finance. I am asking BYU to please split up the content unless they want us to know everything superficially and nothing in-depth. Hard class.

She tells to many stories and doesn't focus enough on explaining the intuition behind the actual material. I took this over the spring and never has a 3-hour lectures felt so long. The good news is, the exams are modeled after what you do in class so go over those problems and you should be good. (Definitely don't take this before Acc 200)

In class exam reviews aren't really worth it, but she does provide a lot of different ways for study. Use the resources that help you most, she's not going to hold your hand, but there a lot of things you can use to get a good grade.

Classic business school at BYU: the test is really hard. She's good but there isn't enough review or busywork to be able to get anything close to an A without having to spend a lot of time studying throughout the semester. Don't try studying the last week before the test it won't work.

I ended up ending with an 89% and then getting curved up to a flat A. Set to get an A the whole time but I only studied for the final two days prior, when I should studied weeks prior. The midterms is alot easier than the final. Be prepared to study A LOT for an A (500+ slides).Tons of formulas to memorize, but put in the work and you will be okay.

PEOPLE, Take this class from Larson! Trust me, EVERY other professor goes really fast, they have to. Larson is a lot more clear on what is tested (even though the tests are slightly harder than what she says). Unlike others, she doesn't expect you to know finance concepts beforehand, but highly recommend ACC 200 before any FIN 201 class.

Expect to study a lot or don't expect to do well when your midterm is on concepts from weeks ago. Par for business school w/test difficulty

I didn't mesh with her style b/c I need to review and didn't realize how hard the tests were. You'll be fine if you're serious about the class. She let the final test replace midterm if you scored higher

She is super kind, but I did not mesh with her teaching style. I taught myself 90% of the material outside of class. I never went to the TAs because they weren't helpful. Tests are HARD. I only got an A because of the final curve. Doable, just not easy. Take it winter from Brow if you're in it for business core and not to get into finance program.

Other reviews are fair. She's tough, like all finance professors, and I'm not criticizing difficulty or personality. My issue is that grades were published a day after finals, and then later lowered due to a grading formula error. It sucks to think you earned an A only to have it reduced later. She should finalize grades before 2am after finals.

I've never written a review for a professor before, but I felt morally compelled to. No one is being dramatic here. Lectures were so fast, impossible to keep up with. Had to teach myself the whole course. I'm a senior and she's the worst teacher I've ever had. Spent DAYS studying for the final, took me 4 hrs to take, only to get a 66. STEER CLEAR!

Worst professor I've had. Class is a waste of time—she moves too fast, doesn't work through problems live, and is hard to follow, yet attendance is required. Be prepared to teach yourself the entire course from the slides before the final. Slides are good, but exams are tougher than the practice slide problems because it combines several concepts

YOU NEED TO TAKE FIN 201 FROM HER. People hate her because she is hard but she is 100% the easiest FIN201 prof. I'VE ASKED AROUND A LOT. Please take ACC 201 first and go to TAs if you need help. The tests are a bit harder than she says but just know the study guide really well. The guide is long, but quick to move through, I just used that to study

She is a great person NOT a great professor. She talks SO FAST (2.0x speed) and clicks through her slides so fast that you can't write anything down. Studying for the exams is ridiculous because she gives you a slide deck with over 500 slides and then puts questions on the tests you've never seen.

Worst professor in the Marriott school. Flat out lies saying the tests will be the same as her review slides when they are full of trick questions. Sends out 500 slide reviews with practice problems only for the tests to have one you've never seen. Talks way too fast and doesn't know how to answer questions. Annoying clipart on every slide.

Pros:
- She is nice and will remember your name
- Sends out review slides (they are between 400-600 slides long)
- Exams are online

Cons:
- moves too fast
- her slides are difficult to follow
- doesn't explain concepts very well
- tests are not similar to what is done in class or in homework
- isnt great at answering questions
- TA reviews are mid

Class is extremely disorganized. Doesn't really teach, mainly just demonstrates how to work problems and then shares personal stories. Not a good teacher. Be aware that her class is heavily exam weighted and her exams are just trick questions. Not an extremely difficult class or a big time commitment though.

I took her in the spring of 2025 and honestly it was a 4 for difficultly because of the concepts and equations needed to be learned and memorized. However, if you do that then it becomes a 3. She is an amazing professor, she gives lots of help for exams and also USE the TA Lab, they were so helpful!

Most of these reviews are pretty dramatic. She goes through lectures quickly, but if you do the assigned reading before class, it's pretty easy to keep up. There are multiple practice problems in class, and before each exam, there is a 400-slide review summarizing everything you need to know for the exam and plenty of practice problems.

Took this class during a spring term. There's a lot to memorize and keep straight in your head, but she teaches this course well, and prepares the TAs to help you succeed. Sometimes her lecture slides can be a bit dense, but all the key information is there. Study lots before exams and you'll crush it. Dr. Larson cares about her students.

Some of the other reviews are a little dramatic. Lectures are fast and hard to understand, but finance is also hard. There's 1 midterm and 1 final which is a blessing and a curse. I didn't understand much during the lectures, but the key to success is going to the TA lab! I knew nothing a week before the midterm but got an A by studying hard.

Professor Larson is a really sweet lady, but does move really fast in her lectures. You definitely will want to have taken ACC 200 before this class, but you could also teach yourself the material. She gives you a massive slide deck for the test, which covers everything you need on the test, but it is really tough to get through. Really kind though

Professor Larsen is kind and cares about her students, so I hope she reads this. I studied hard and did well on homework and class problems. Though I prepared carefully expecting tricks, the exam was still not what she told us it would be. We aren't asking for easy exams, just fair ones that don't trick us and are inclusive for all students.

DO NOT TAKE. The midterm had a 69 percent average. You will not learn anything in this class. She doesn't teach for understanding, she just wants to get through her never ending slideshows. She is a nice lady but is not a good teacher. If you need to take this class then take it with someone else!!!

Do not take this class from Prof. Larson. Like literally all of her other reviews say, she is a nice person but she talks WAY too fast for you to understand anything she goes over in class. The review material for the midterm is 436 slides and requires extreme memorization. Attendance is mandatory and again, you WILL NOT understand her in class.

She's nice, but she talks super fast and zooms through her slides. Don't expect to learn the material in class unless you are a human computer and can download everything you see and hear instantly. Her tests are very difficult and you have to memorize a million things for them. If memorization is tough for you, like it is for me, good luck.

Frustrating and discouraging. She talks SO FAST and doesn't recognize that everyone is tuned out. Be prepared to teach yourself the entire course from the textbook and slides (or live in the TA Lab), because class time is useless unless you come fully understanding the material. You're graded on attendance every class though, so it's frustrating.

I took this class after I had already learned a lot of the material through my major (accounting). Lectures were sometimes hard to sit through, but overall, I think this class is very fair. Even if I had taken this class without prior knowledge of the material, if you put in effort, you'll be just fine.

Prof Larson was great for this class. The tests can be hard but she has a 600 slide optional review that has questions for every type of question on the exam. The questions on the review are basically the same as the tests so the exams are easy if you study the review. Super easy A, and Prof Larson makes It easy to understand the content in class.

Yeah, basically my main issue was her tests. The tests are just HARD. Like it's all about catching errors in the way she stated the question rather than understanding the material. I know she would argue that is understanding the material but it's just a funny way to set up the class. Wish the class was set up differently.

Professor Larson is a great person and very knowledgeable. Tests can be deceptively tough as it requires a bit more understanding than the textbook or even the lecture slides and an ability to catch small conceptual errors. My take is, though it is a general class it is a filter to see who is serious about finance.

Respectfully, ignore most of the negative comments for Jenn. They're just students that didn't do well, and Prof Larson doesn't have the glorified reputation like Prof Brau, the other Fin 201 teacher, so she gets ripped on. I took this class in the Spring, its hard work but manageable. Larson's EASIER than Brau, with only 2 tests instead of 4. :)
Teaches at a low level. Hard to master content. Quizzes, tests are slides feel like kindergarten. She doesn't test understanding, it's more about if you can catch typos.

Overall, she is really a good teacher. If you study the readings and exam prep slides you can and will do well on the exams. The exam prep slides had very similar practice problems as the tests, and all the other assignments were very easy to get A's on. You will have to work for a good grade but I think that's the class more than the professor.

I got an A in Econ and an A- in Accounting and this class kicked my butt. Prof Larson talks so fast it's difficult to keep up despite coming prepared. Tests are nothing like the quizzes or weekly assignments and make up most of your grade. Asking questions usually left me more confused. Would definitely recommend choosing someone else.

Jenn Larson makes me come to a 3 hour lecture two times a week. Makes me track my own attendance, then gets it wrong and marks me down 30 points. But super nice. she's a mom so she hates the word stupid. Stupid, Stupid, Stupid. Grew up on a dairy farm, she'll make sure to tell you that every class period.

Classes are incredibly dry and the tests are extraordinarily difficult. You don't see it coming until you're sitting there reading questions asking yourself if you're accidentally taking the wrong test. The worst part is they're worth most of your grade. What's supposed to be a business gen ed ended up being a GPA killer. Trust me, stay away.

I am typically a good student, but this class was insane. Jenn moves super fast through everything. She then downplays the tests and they hit you like a speeding train.
Stay away. Take from another professor - I have heard great things about the other 201 professors.

Do not take anything from Jenn Larson. Her FIN 201 class was an awful experience for me. She did not explain concepts well, had way too high of expectations, and spoke way too fast. She ran a really awful class. Take FIN 201 from someone else!

FIN 201 is a difficult class, but Prof Larson kept it interesting and made it possible to succeed. Her lectures are extremely fast paced, and if you don't come prepared, you'll have no idea what's going on. This class was very time consuming, but teaches very valuable and applicable information. Utilize the TAs and you can definitely succeed.

Larson is great! The great lectures give you everything you need to succeed.

However, prep hard for the midterm & final. The exams require a deeper understanding of the material than what is used in class. She does, however, curve hard at the end, which makes up for this.

I would take her again if I could, and I recommend her to you.

Jenn Larson is a nice person, but her teaching style is ineffective. She talks way too fast, and her lectures feel rushed and disengaging. I barely learned from her and had to rely on TAs for explanations. If you take her class, be ready to put in extra work to understand the material. If you want to keep your GPA, beware!

FIN 201 is just a extremely hard and info packed class but Prof Larson did her best to prepare us for the exams. She gave us plenty of review materials and went over it in class as well. I got an 88 on midterm and final and still got an A. Took it with ACC 310 and it was a great combo. I would not want to take it from another prof.

She's a good person, but I feel like I taught myself more than she taught me. We read each topic before class, but she mostly repeated what we'd already read for homework. While we did some practice problems in class, I wish there had been more. The midterm and final covered a lot of material, and the tests were tricky.

This professor was absolutely terrible. If you are really good at reading minds then you'll do really good in this class. Here are some highlights:
Cons:
1) If you don't have her specific calculator, you will fail
2) If you don't show up, you will fail (but they are useless)
3) Worst exams I have ever taken (Mostly "read my mind" questions)
Not that bad so long you have a general understanding of how money works.

She's a terrible teacher. Her tests take around 3 hours which is too long for a 201 class. She also expects students to memorize all the formulas. She only cares about getting through the material, not student comprehension. Do yourself a favor and take FIN 201 from someone else because her class is terrible. So bad!

Jenn is a nice person but a terrible teacher. She wastes a lot of time during lecture (which you're required to be at) but then still tests you on the things that were never taught. She talks so quickly and it's hard to understand her. She's very stuck in her ways and won't adapt anything for the different needs of a class.

Love how she organized class w/ weekly practice for the topics
VERY down to earth with demands of student life (just 1 midterm and a recording to watch over thanksgiving)
Encouraged participation & graded class attendance
Sped thru some hard topics at times but created extra practice problems & emailed out the slides so that students could practice

Professor Larson reads her class very well and responds accordingly. Once, she saw we were all dead tired towards the end of a lecture and let us out ten minutes early instead of beginning the next topic. She's very fair and structured the class to optimize our ability to learn. You have to earn your grades but she provides all the tools to do so.

I know a lot of people have left bad reviews, but I really enjoyed taking Finance 201 from professor Larson. Taking a class during spring or summer semester can be tricky because all the material is condensed into a shorter amount of time. If you put in the work you can get an A! She is very personable person!

Useless lectures, bad professor, long exams. The only reason I went to lecture is because you are forced to go to get the participation points. One of my relatives took this course from her and said that attendance was not enforced before and not a lot of people showed up to class. Now, I get it, her classes are the worst

She is genuinely a good person but a TERRIBLE TEACHER. I am amazed at how dry and long are her lectures. This class will only teach one thing and that is that you need teach yourself and prepare yourself for the exam. Her exams are hard and it is not that she does not prepare you well for the exams, SHE DOES NOT EVEN TEACH YOU.

Awful class, terrible instructor. I am so sorry for those who had to take this course from her. She will spend little to no time actually teaching the material. Do a favor to yourself and don't take any class from this terrible instructor.

She will just fly through the slides and read from them. Everyone is too afraid and tired to ask questions. (Her lectures are boring and long). She wastes a ton of time going through career tips and random information that is not relevant to the course and she will spend very little time in the course material. Attendance is mandatory!

Jenn is awesome. Such a good soul. The class is objectively difficult for most people, but she does a great job at teaching. She also provides nearly all the material you could need to study for tests. No surprises. Very solid professor and I'd take her again.

She's fine for FIN 201. She's nice and tries to be fun. And she will remember your name if you ever talk to her. But it does feel like she makes the class harder than it needs to be. And she spends a large chunk of class telling random stories and not prepping you for the exams. If you want an A, you'll have to work for it.

Agree with a most of these reviews- Professor Larson is very caring but I felt like I taught myself all of the material. I came to class to get the participation points but honestly did not find class time useful or productive to me. Class is not engaging and important things are talked through too quickly.

You have to distinguish between a good person and a good professor. She wastes class time on career tips when majors have a class dedicated to that.  She showed up late to a lot of our classes, occasionally even between 6-10 minutes late.  She does not prepare you sufficiently for exams. She teaches to a difficulty of 3, quizzes are a 6, tests a 9.

Worst class I've ever taken. She's kind but just showed how much she knows rather than taking care or enthusiasm to teach/thoroughly explain content. No homework to reinforce what you learn in class except 1 weekly quiz with a fraction of the material. Spoke too fast to understand what she was saying or take notes. 480 "final exam review slides"

Every time a test comes up she says, "This test will not be more difficult than what you've seen on the review slides." In reality, the calculation questions are MUCH harder than the review slides, and the multiple choice comprehension questions e testing your mastery of the English language and NOT of Finance.

Her lectures were confusing. I think she was use to teaching online, meaning students could pause, rewind, rewatch. But in person? She wasn't easy to follow, yet you HAD to be there for attendance. Example: she'd have us do practice problems before explaining how to do them. 

If you take her in person, find a tutor or a friend to help teach you.

Worst class ever. This is a difficult class, and she is terrible at teaching the material. She spends and insane amount of time on random information, and then skips over all the everything you need to know for the class. I think she just enjoys hearing herself talk. Don't take this class if you want to learn anything, terrible experience.

Literally the best professor I have ever had. She is not trying to trick you so her exam study guides tell you exactly what to expect. Homework is a little difficult but there is lots of help so as long as you put in some effort you'll do just fine. You can easily get an A as long as you put in a little effort.

She talked very quickly and breezed over important information in favor of giving job search tricks and other information not relevant to the course. Each class period consisted of about two hundred slides that would be gone over quickly with little to no explanation. Few practice problems to prepare you for tests.

Professer Larson knows her stuff. She makes sure everyone in the room knows that. She is the fastest speaking professor I've ever had. It makes it very difficult to understand, especially with all the new terms. 

I'd recommend:
-Take Accounting 200 first (essential)
-dont take in spring/summer (she'd probably be alright in the winter or fall)

You don't need to buy the textbook! Conceptual questions on the test are hard but the calculations are straightforward. The group projects are a pain. If you study the slides before the test you will be ok even if you haven't read the book!

Prof Larson is the easier of the professors in Fin 402 and Fin 520.  DO NOT TAKE DIETHER.  She only has 2 exams compared to Dither's 3.  Diether makes you memorize everything, prof Larson makes you memorize essentially nothing if you remember how to do functions on your financial calculator and lets you take tests at home with excel.

She would spent copious amounts of time on job search highlights and "tips and tricks" for getting a job. But then she would pull up a slide with actual important information for the class and then skip thru super fast. I basically just taught myself everything in this class. Also if you didn't take accounting 200 first do not take this class.

Finance is a notoriously hard subject, but Jenn is a wonderful teacher! You will succeed if you:
1. Took ACC 200 before taking this class
2. Review some slides/problems before lectures
3. Drill the problems in her slides after class and before exams
If you can meet these requirements, by all means take from Jenn!

DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK, you will not use it at all. Super nice and her tests are doable, but the conceptual questions can be challenging. Calculations are just like her in-class problems, and her slides are all that matter. She can rush through material sometimes and it will still be on the test. Group projects suck. Organized. Great professor.

If you have taken ACC 310 and understood it, this class is a breeze. There is 1 midterm and 1 final and then some weekly quizzes. Professor Jenn was pretty chill, not a bad choice. I took this class in the spring semester and the lectures were a bit long and dry but it was totally worth it getting over so fast.

Professor Larson is the reason I got into the Finance program at BYU. She is incredibly consistent and always prepared, she's incredibly understanding, only a midterm and a final, and you always know what to expect on exams. If I could take every class from Jenn, I would. She's incredible.

Professor Larson is a good person and really cares about what she is teaching and her students success. Dont buy the text its a waste of money. just attend the class, learn the slides and do the practice problems and you will do fine. TAs where inconsistent in quality this semester and often contradict each other especially around group project

Large walls of text on almost every slide, group project grading is super inconsistent and all over the place, the test are more about knowing random stuff from the huge walls of text than anything. I can honestly say this was by far the worst class I have taken within the business school...

Well organized class that takes you through all of the principles clearly and concisely. She goes quick but tries really hard to make sure everyone understands. Checks for understanding and her TAs are available outside of the class all the time. I would recommend Prof Larson to anyone!

She is one of the best professors I have ever had! Finance 201 is not easy, but she gives you all of the resources she can, has lots of TA's to help you, slides are very useful and detailed, study guide for the exam contains about 90% of the exam material, and she is generous with the curve. She is also very inspirational and relatable.

Even having had no prior knowledge of finance, (I hadn't even taken accounting,) I understood it well. She has an interesting teaching style, and is easily the most organized professor I've ever had. I had to put a lot of time in out of class, but her slides are amazing and it is so easy to study for her tests because of her amazing study guides!

Jenn is extremely organized and systematic which is a huge plus. The tests are very difficult, but the class has a large curve. It seemed like we spent too much time talking about conceptual ideas that weren't factually correct. Don't buy the textbook, and don't go to lectures unless there is a quiz (lectures were a waste of time).

Professor Larson is a good teacher but her grading is very steep. Tests and projects are most of the grade and they are tough. A-E which one is not true and the projects are graded against the other students. Basically on who has more time in the class. I would take her again if she changed her test methods and made her projects more rubric based.

The class content is a little bit dry, but Professor Larson does her best to make it interesting. She adds in a lot of content to really help us in our lives as well. I think that the issues are more with the course than the professor. She is super organized which is so nice as a student. The POWs and projects are very time-intensive so be prepped.

She is superwoman when it comes to managing her career and her family. She has a habit of talking to her students like they are stupid when they ask questions in class which I absolutely despise. Use the slides to help prepare for tests and you should be okay. Prepare to study a LOT for her exams. Use the TAs for the weekly POWs and you'll be ok.

She's a really caring teacher, but I wouldn't recommend taking FIN 201 from her. She talks too fast and doesn't recognize it. You can succeed but be ready to put in heavy hours outside of class. She doesn't use class time effectively, spending a large amount of time talking about her career tips, neglecting confusing, important concepts of finance.

She's a nice person but I didn't love her class. Had some beef with her grading and how she handled certain things. Also 50% of her test questions are a-e and ask "which of the following is not true" that was a joke. finance class should be doing finance problems not guessing which bullet point from the slides was not there.

Go to the lectures, all the test material is talked about in class, all the tests questions on concepts start with: "All of the following EXCEPT" I found that very difficult. The class was interesting, quizzes are easy. She waits an extra couple of seconds when asking if you have questions to make sure your q's are answered. Exam 1: 70 Exam 2: 60

Worst class I've taken at BYU. Lectures just made material more confusing, but if you don't show up you miss some of the material for a couple of the topics. Even going through the slides I couldn't find a couple of the things that somehow showed up on the tests. Emailing her was not helpful. Take from another professor if you have the option.

The most down to earth professor! She understands college life and sets up assignments/expectations accordingly. She is busy outside of class but TAs are always able to help, though sometimes they aren't helpful. Hard class but she gives all resources needed to do well. I would not take anyone else for FIN 201.

She is such a good teacher.  She is very good at helping you understand tough concepts and gives you every opportunity to understand and ask questions.  Top 5 favorite professors at BYU.  I also loved that she got to know everyone's name in a very large class.  I am not a good test taker, so I struggled, but feel learned alot.
PowerPoint slides are useless, messy, CHUCK FULL OF TEXT.   Talks FOREVER to explain simple things.   She's super nice, but super inefficient. Needs to take a class on how to make useful PowerPoints.

She's the only option for FIN 402, but you're in good hands. Class is very straightforward and organized (compared to other ambiguous management core classes). If there's not a quiz you can probably just skip, I just looked at the slides for the tests and got 80 percentile + each time.  Never read the textbook or did the practice problems.

She is a nice person and would be a great friend. She talks really fast and then asks for questions but everyone is just like, "ya how do you do all of that??" Her slides are very text heavy, so basically to study for the test memorize 250 slides and you're good. Also there are a ton of assignments, some days there will be multiple assignments due.

I loved this class! Super straight forwad, and if you stay on top of your work, you should be fine. The TAs are very helpful, and Professor Larson is very willing to answer questions you may have. Approachable and kind, she also cares a great deal for the students.

I really liked her. She was a very straight forward teacher who covered exactly what you need to know in class. Didn't open my book once, don't think anyone did. Personal finance tips and days. Weekly homework problems, 2 hours max with a small group of friends. Tests are rough. Ending curve was about 13% but she said final was unusually hard

Nice lady however I took this class during spring semester so the lectures were 3 hours long and usually boring. She talks really fast and it's sometimes hard to keep up. She doesn't give out practice tests so your next best resource is slides which isn't specific enough for the tests. The final exam was RIDICULOUS, the average  was a D!

Took Finance 201 before with Brau last semester and barely squeaked by with a B.  Prof. Larson only has 2 tests during Spring term, Final is considerably more difficult, but very manageable if you study and keep on top of the study topics.
She talks way too fast.  Beware if you haven't taken accounting because she does not clarify basic terms and business lingo.  I learned most of the material from the textbook.

Gives you plenty of resources to do well in the class. Talks fast but is easy to understand, especially if you do the reading. I didn't do any homework except the weekly POW and did great. Lots of PWPT slides but easy to get through. Taught us how to make great finance decisions like how to build credit, buy a house, negotiate, credit card, etc

Best Teacher at BYU to take Finance 201 from. She talks fast, but her material isn't impossible. She provides all the tools so you can do well in the class. I wouldn't take this class from anyone else. She is super nice and helpful and even gives great tips during class on religious thoughts and tips about jobs in your future.

I wouldn't take this class from anyone else. The material can be hard no matter who you take it from. Professor Larson does a good job of explaining things and she will even teach you helpful shortcuts. She talks a little fast but if you stay after she will explain it until you get it. The final is hard but curved.

She is a very nice lady, but not a very good professor. She just reads off the powerpoints word for word. The first half of class is cake, the second half is way harder. The midterm was much easier than the final which  was really hard. Hard to stay attentive in class. Reading quizzes and annoying Problems of the week are due every week. Bad class

One of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Only two tests, and they are super easy. Homework is very easy as well. Going to class seemed like a waste of time sometime, you could ace the class just by going over her slides. Friends who took other teachers seemed to have a much tougher time!

I would not recommend this class to anyone.  Professor Larson is a great person, but not her class was ridiculous.  I did well on all the homework assignments, never missed class, and still couldn't do well on her tests...I can't memorize over 250 slides WORD FOR WORD!

AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS! Half the time we were finding her errors in class. She did so many of her own problems wrong on the midterm that after correcting her, several students got more answers right than she did. The class was a constant frustration. The final was the hardest test I've taken at BYU. Confusing and unorganized. She's nice tho.
Fun professor. Fun personality, fun teaching style, fun to watch. That's good because the subject isn't the most thrilling.

This teacher is over rated. She is nice and smiley with students but not very informative in the field of finance. If you want to have a teacher who makes your life easy this is the one. But if you want a teacher to explain things in clarity and beyond the book is not this one.

Great teacher! I felt she kept the assignments relevant, and would specify if we didn't need to know something. Sent out an email after every class with attached slides and reminders of assignment deadlines. I would take from her again. Homework load was reasonable and the 2 tests were very doable. I got an A.

She did a good job teaching this class for the first time. Because of the nature of the class material, she has to go everything through quickly, so you may want to be diligent enough prior to attending her class, but it is a good class to attend.
Awesome Professor! All you need is her class slides.  If not on the slides, never in the tests/quizzes!  And she is super nice. Wouldn't take it from any other prof.

I learned the material better when I didn't attend class. She speaks so quickly that you can hardly catch what she is saying. She sends out the powerpoints of the class material to everyone after class, this is very helpful. The material is not hard, but when you can't write notes on what she is saying, the class gets harder.
My favorite thing about Professor Larson is she makes the whole class practical and useful for everyone in attendance.  She's entertaining and teaches the material well. I enjoyed her class.

I honestly was very skeptical of taking her class given that she was blind. I worried she would be very impersonal and difficult to connect with. But boy was I wrong, she is easily the most engaging professor I have taken at BYU. She truly cares about her students and is always willing to help a struggling student. TAKE HER CLASS!

Professor Brooks is easily my favorite Math teacher I've taken so far, and the only teacher I've cared enough to give a review for. She makes lessons interesting and engaging, while explaining concepts carefully and intuitively. She is also hilarious and will answer any question you could ask in depth. Take Professor Brooks!!!

Jen is incredible! I ended up withdrawing from 341 because I switched majors and didn't need the class anymore, also it was incredibly hard for me. She is very knowledgeable and can answer any questions you have. Proof classes can be tough and this one is no exception, just use the TA and her and you should be alright.

Dr. Brooks is amazing!!! Things to know: she wrote the textbook we used in Winter '23 and gave it to us for free! The homework applies to what we learn and preps you for her tests. I went to her office hours and the TAs and I attribute them for my success in this course. I honestly cannot recommend her enough!

Jen is a fantastic professor! The class goes through a lot of material and it moves very fast. There is a lot of homework, if you stay on top of it the class isn't too bad. Be prepared to spend a lot if time on this class. I would highly recommend going to as many office hours as possible, TA's and Jen's both. Jen is amazing and I learnt so much!

Professor Brooks is always there willing to help you even though the class is super tough. She has amazing lectures and she always tries to simplify very complex and abstract concepts in tough courses like MATH 341.
She's the absolute best! She literally has a score of 5 as a math professor. Does anyone else see how crazy that is? Very helpful and very merciful.
Jen is super caring and down to earth.  I had some struggles this semester, but she worked with me and I was able to pass the class.  She is always so understanding.

I love Dr Brooks! I had a great experience in her class. 290 is notoriously pretty difficult no matter who you take it with, but I can't see myself taking it with anyone else. Dr Brooks very clearly knows her stuff and the way she explains things works so well for me. If I can ever take her class again, I'm definitely doing it.

She is a fantastic person and a great teacher. Her philosophy for tests is how she can make it as easy as possible while testing for the material. She also gave very comprehensive study guides for you to go through. I really felt like I learned so much, and while there was a lot of homework it felt like it was meaningful.

I have taken many classes from Dr. Brooks, and every time I'm so glad I took the class! She really cares about her students and does a great job teaching. She roughly follows what is done in a specific chapter/section of the textbook, but she will skip easy things or things we won't use and will instead spend time on the most important/hard things.

If you ever get the pleasure of taking a class from Dr brooks you should. She is an amazing mathematician, an amazing instructor and most of all an amazing person. She is the entire reason why I study mathematics and went on to pursue a PhD. I cannot say enough good things about this professor. BYU should be honored to have her!
Jen is an amazing professor and a great person. Complex analysis is a tough class, but she made it so simple and easy to understand. I would take any class she teaches.
Dr. Brooks is excellent at conveying the concepts.

Took it last fall semester. The contents were harder than Math 341 imo and not my favorite, but she explained them pretty well. HWs were in a heavy load, and the exams were time-consuming (probably not if you take in-person), but she gave extra credits to those who typed their work. Take her class if you had the chance.
Professor Brooks is one of the best professors that I have had, she makes really difficult concepts understandable.

Comp Analysis was not my fav but Dr. Brooks gives off good vibes. If she's an option, take her. Not sure I would have made it through with another prof. You can also consider Dr. Cardon or Robbie Snellman if they're teaching. But Jenn is a good teacher. Communicate with her, reach out to her, and you will make it. She's fair & nice. B- but made it!

I honestly was very skeptical of taking her class given that she was blind. I worried she would be very impersonal and difficult to connect with. But boy was I wrong, she is easily the most engaging professor I have taken at BYU. She truly cares about her students and is always willing to help a struggling student. TAKE HER CLASS!

Professor Brooks is easily my favorite Math teacher I've taken so far, and the only teacher I've cared enough to give a review for. She makes lessons interesting and engaging, while explaining concepts carefully and intuitively. She is also hilarious and will answer any question you could ask in depth. Take Professor Brooks!!!

Jen is incredible! I ended up withdrawing from 341 because I switched majors and didn't need the class anymore, also it was incredibly hard for me. She is very knowledgeable and can answer any questions you have. Proof classes can be tough and this one is no exception, just use the TA and her and you should be alright.

Dr. Brooks is amazing!!! Things to know: she wrote the textbook we used in Winter '23 and gave it to us for free! The homework applies to what we learn and preps you for her tests. I went to her office hours and the TAs and I attribute them for my success in this course. I honestly cannot recommend her enough!

Jen is a fantastic professor! The class goes through a lot of material and it moves very fast. There is a lot of homework, if you stay on top of it the class isn't too bad. Be prepared to spend a lot if time on this class. I would highly recommend going to as many office hours as possible, TA's and Jen's both. Jen is amazing and I learnt so much!

I. Love. Dr. Wimmer. Do anything you can to take a class from her or your experience at BYU will not be complete. She knows her stuff well and will teach you amazing things. She is accessible outside of class (GO TALK WITH HER, it will change your life...+snacks!) and wants the best for you. Put effort into her class and assignments--it is worth it

Dr. Wimmer is AMAZING! She genuinely cares about your success! Talk to her about anything and she will do her best to help you. The class is not bad. There are several papers, but you know in advance. She makes it very doable. Keep up on everything and you will be very successful. You will be enriched academically and spiritually. Take from her!!!

LOTS of reading, but it helps with the learning reports if you take good notes. Some other people have mentioned the tediousness of the learning reports, and I agree; you have to cite 3 sources from the lesson for each question, which is not hard; it just takes a bit of time. Overall, easy A, just felt like I was teaching myself with the textbook.

VERY EASY A. The content is easy. Learning reports are due each week and are tedious, but everything you do is open-book. No final exam. I think this class works well online. It is very chill. Dr. Brooks is very respectful and sensitive when discussing difficult subjects. If you want a chill class to take the edge off, here you go.

I didn't get to know Prof. Brooks, but the class was easy. One Lit Review that you work on throughout the semester, so it doesn't feel like much. The learning reports at the end of each week were a drag, but not very hard. Also, my TA graded really kindly. I don't know if all TAs grade the same for this course. Overall, I recommend this course!

Psych 307 Online. Jenny leaves really good feedback on papers. There are a lot of papers leading up to one large literature review. She offers extra credit at the end. This is a writing course, so you will write a lot, but overall I felt the course load was fair and easily doable. I didn't get the best TA so my advice would be to reach out early.

Dr. Brooks helped me grow my writing skills more than any other professor I've had. She cares about her students and is accessible to them. I had her for PSYCH 307 (Writing Within Psychology), but this site didn't have that listed as an option. I would definitely recommend taking that class with her, she's awesome and wants you to get a good grade.
Get ready to write so many papers they are called "learning reports" but they take so long. Just busy work. Honestly easy class but you have to put in the work and there is so much homework.

Easy class but LOTS of busy work. 1 2-minute lecture response video, 1 written response quiz a week. Quizzes will take you FOREVER if you want to get full points. 4 papers throughout the semester. No final, but a big semester project. If you can get good scores on everything during the semester, you can get an A without doing the project.

The most overwhelming online class I have ever taken. I spent HOURS on writing assignments every week. Some required citations from the module, so I couldn't just skip the readings (and there's SO much to read). Feels like a ton of busy work. No tests. The TAs grade everything. You can't get by easy, you have to put in crazy effort for an A.

I have taken two of her psych classes and they were hard but rewarding! She has great TAs and works with you on everything. Since its online she is clear about no extensions but other than that I have had great experiences!
Online class so I never interacted with her. A lot of busy work, but no exams so that was nice. I didn't learn much from this class, just seemed like a hoop to jump through

I love Dr. Brooks! Took Psych 220 with her then 320 in Summer 2024. Very understanding teacher who will hold you accountable to your words and actions. 8-10 page double-spaced lit review you work on the whole term. Assignments centered around developing this paper. Easy A, just stay on top of it. Dr. Brooks and TAs were helpful and responsive!

Dr. Brooks is awesome! Took in Fall 2023, lots of tedious busy work- answer review Qs on the week's material; write a short 2-page paper on each stage of development every two weeks or so, and a short, easy book report. All open note! An easy A, just stay on top of work. She allows for extensions and gives extra credit. Very understanding teacher.
Dr. Brooks is incredibly kind and understanding. It is clear that she genuinely cares about her students and her subject.

The class subject was not bad, but there is so much reading and work it becomes uninteresting. I think things would have been more interesting and I would have learned more if I was learning not just cramming in assignments. That being said it is an easy A if you stay on top of things.

I took the online course of human dev. and it was awesome! The canvas was organized very well and the TA's were super helpful. There was a decent amount of homework since it is a completely online class but I learned a lot and all of the content was very engaging and enjoyable. I would definitely recommend taking this class!

This class was very easy, which was nice. My TA was also great, but I don't think I ever heard from the professor. It felt like the TA ran the class. It was hard for me to get invested for those reasons. If you're looking for an intellectually challenging class, I wouldn't say this is the best option. But very easy.

Very vanilla class. Nothing more that they could do since it is an online course. You have assignments due on Saturdays (sometimes discussion posts on Wednesdays), which include chapter quizzes. There is also a semester-long lit review. Up to 10 extra credit points are available by the end.
This class is awesome if you want an easy A with a lot of busy work. You won't learn anything, but you can crank out the final project in a few hours.

This class was all online and self-paced with assignments due on Wednesday and Saturday nights. Super easy class and I could usually finish all the work in a 2 hour sitting. No tests, just a semester project. There is a lot of extra credit offered if you happen to get behind or do bad on an assignment.

This class was the biggest waste of time. I did not hear from Dr. Brooks one time. The TAs were honestly not great. I tried to meet with them for a scheduled zoom meeting and they "forgot about it" three times in a row. My assignments were graded late and incorrectly repeatedly. I did not feel like I learned anything. Very easy though!
This class is a literal joke. Take it if you want to get an A with zero effort and zero learning. Just a bunch of busy work. Take someone else if you actually want to learn something.

I took this Capstone class from Dr. Brooks. The class is pretty easy as long as you do the assignments. The grading is super lenient if you show effort. Lots of things you learn are so that you can apply them to your future career. You will get out of this class what you put in. I liked this class being online too, it feels like a good way to do it

No tests/quizzes, but four 2.5-page & one 10+ page paper. Only the long one is really a headache, the others are application on observations you do. After doing readings, lectures feel redundant & pointless. You basically teach yourself in this class. Dr. Brooks was good though about quickly reaching out to me after I sent my accommodation letter.

No tests, just weekly open book quizzes throughout the semester. Big Paper due at the end. Pretty much, you are teaching yourself by reading the textbook. Super interesting material, not hard to understand.

The class is super easy. I got an A easy and never read the book. There's a number of papers and quizzes, but those are easy to do without reading the book. No tests and a semester long project for the final. The project took me a couple of hours.

This course was completely on demand so you really get what you put into it. There is a lot of extra modules and readings you can do, but not necessary to get an A. Assignments are not time consuming and quizzes are open note. No final test just an easy project. I would recommend if you are looking for a laid back psych class

No tests in this class, which makes it nice to take when you have other heavier classes. Material was pretty boring. Tons of modules and textbook readings that you only had to do for the homework assignments and weekly quizzes. Number of assignments was not balanced throughout the weeks very well either. Just trying to pass.

I'm not going to lie. I was really excited to take this class, but I am disappointed. Unfortunately, this class is so much busy work. 2 book reports, 10 hour project, weekly textbook reading, quizzes, and and reports on the book, and lessons and discussions along with many papers. I am not impressed by the course and just want to pass at this point

I like Professor Brooks! I didn't get much interaction with her though because I took the class online. It was pretty easy and interesting. There were a few understandable glitches with it being a pilot semester, and some woke messaging which was silly. Other than that, I would recommend!

I really enjoyed this class! There wasn't much direct interaction since most the material was either pre-recorded videos or the textbook. Since it was a pilot course, there were some bumps but Professor Brooks was very accommodating and made sure to offer extra credit opportunities. The quizzes are easy and the a few papers. No tests.

Grading criteria is really clear. There's a lot of busy-work assignments, but as long as you complete them you'll get an A. Lectures are fun and interesting. She's really great at applying things to real life. I liked understanding human development and was surprised to find myself making lots of notes to use for my future family (e.g. sex ed).

Professor Brooks is the worst professor I have ever had. She changes the schedule frequently, and moved the due date for our final paper up by a MONTH! She is passive aggressive when students ask for help or tell her that they're upset she moved the due date. Its a good class, but DON'T take it from her.

Prof Brooks is amazing!! NO TESTS. As a lazy senior, this class was perfect for me. I took her 2.5 hr night class and did hwk during it. Her lectures were interesting though, and I did learn a lot about adult dev. She is a gem and is so open minded and kind. If you're looking for an easy psych class for your cluster classes, TAKE THIS ONE.

A ton of reading - you're required to read the entire textbook over the semester plus two full length books. But you're graded mostly on whether you do those readings or not. Very interesting class, very understanding and open-minded professor!
She is an awesome professor who is very knowledgable. Yeah there is a lot of assignments to do but they are all easy, if you don't fall behind youa re good. Also, you can easily work ahead too.

Great professor, and super easy class. No exams, just a final group presentation. There are 2 quizzes and 2 shortish papers due every class. If you do the hw on time and go to class, you're guaranteed an A. Attendance is taken at the beginning and end of class for a grade. Honestly, I sat in the back and worked on other hw during class.

She is so awesome and gives amazing lectures! She also goes on field trips and has guest speakers come in and lecture us. She really tries to go beyond the textbook. She does have you turn in about two papers a week on the chapters read but it's not difficult.

I love, love, love Professor Brooks. She organized amazing field trips for us to go on that I learned so much. Her teaching goes beyond the classroom and the textbook. She is an amazing teacher and I would highly recommend her class. There were lots of paper to write, but nothing that was too hard.

Dr. Jenny is AWESOME and so kind. She's the most unconventional professor I've ever had. Her teaching style emphasizes real-life experience. We had tons of guest speakers, took a field trip to the local jail, and had really awesome in-class discussions. I learned a lot and highly recommend her as a professor. One of my favorite classes in college.

Jenny Brooks is a great teacher. She has a unique teaching style and her classes are never boring, even though I took a long night class. The class was really engaging. My favorite thing we did was interesting field trips and I feel like I learned so much that most conventional classes don't teach.

Dr. Brooks was my favorite professor at BYU. She teaches in an unconventional way and her classes were always very interesting and engaging. It was a 2.5 hr. class and it flew by.  She is very understanding and brought an amazing perspective to every topic. I loved this class and would take her again and again. Lots of little easy to do assignments

Lots of little assignments, but SUPER EASY grading. 20 min presentation = midterm (avg 100); research paper = final (avg 99). Chapter quizzes + short write ups each week; several small writing assignments; NO TESTS; 1 field trip; attendance = points; extra credit can make up 10% of total grade. VERY nice down-to-earth teacher, unconventional class.

I had zero coding background, so this class was a lot of work for me. But Dr. Brown was always willing to help whenever I asked him for it. Most of what he teaches is through videos, and class attendance is optional, which gives you more homework time; but there's a lot of homework. Worth it! I enjoyed the class and learned a ton!

He's good at what he does and assignments were reasonable and helped you learn and get better at web development. He had good resources for reviewing and practicing for the midterm and final. He was pretty accessible outside of class if you signed up for a time on his calendly, but in my experience it was hit or miss whether he responded to emails.
Professor Browne is a nice guy, and is always there to help us students out. Assignments are pretty easy as long as you pay attention.

He loves what he does which makes it really fun. He's funny, and obviously cares about students. Do wish he would just let you remind him your name since he insists on memorizing but isn't very good at it, but it's part of his charm. I really appreciated it was more project-based than test-based since this built skills much more than memorizing.

A really good intro class. Browne has the tendency to ramble, but it's always interesting. Multiple times outside of class he helped code programs for us to use on our projects. Very quick email responses, and fair grades. I'd take it again.

Brother Browne was a great professor! In class, we covered a few different Adobe programs which can be challenging but he made it possible to learn them. He is accessible, reasonable, and helpful. There are a few textbook quizzes, but no tests. There are just projects, which can be revised for another grade. I would take a class from him again.

Browne was a good Book of Mormon teacher! He is very funny and I agree very smug. He assigns a lot of essays (usually one a week) but as long as you do all the work it is an easy A. He brought treats every class too which was awesome!

I am sorry, but he was very smug (as has been mentioned by other reviews) and basically refuses to acknowledge others' opinions because his is the only one that matters. I learned a good amount of material, but class time was basically him just showing off and telling us how great he is.

I felt like most of the time in class was spent watching him show us things that he discovered using the tools we learned. I didn't find this too educational. He grades the assignments really easy and if you do them you should get an A on them. He's a fine person. I'm just not a fan of his teaching style.
Jeremy is a great guy to work with and is really good at explaining tough concepts and making you understand them.

Jeremy is a great teacher who grabs your attention in class. He is quite smug and will show off how much he knows, but he is a good guy. He likes to recap the devotional and likes to engage the students.

Brother Browne's class was very interesting and I felt like the time always flew by in his class. We always had really interesting discussions and he is very open-minded. Assignments aren't hard but he doesn't use learning suite. So I didn't like that. Very kind and wants to get to know his students!

Bro. Browne is the perfect person to learn web design from. He's been apart of the history and really knows it. He is also very current with the internet and it show's in his lectures. He's really funny, he works in jokes and meme's into his lessons. I'd recommend him to anyone wanting to learn web design, even if you already know it.

A great and informative class. I was very interested in the material and he taught it well. He was helpful and very clear at explaining things. I recommend  it to anyone who wants to learn web design. It is basic and perfect for beginners and people that have done a little before. My friend who has done web design for awhile actually learned a lot

Brother Browne is awesome! Sometimes the concepts in these classes are hard, and he does everything he can to make sure you have all the help you need! More projects than tests or quizzes, but he's very easy to work with and will give you any help you need! He's also funny!

Arrogant, un-organized, ineffective. Did I mention smug? The worst part is, he is probably proud of his snottiness. The class should have been interesting, but he made it boring and his lectures offensive. Quite difficult to succeed since he had few points offered per semester. Would never take from him again. He ruined a perfectly good class.

It felt like South Indian and Balinese music instead of world music. He mostly focused on that the whole semester and rarely talked about other cultures. It also seemed like he would get through 2 of his 26 slides each class and just talk about random tangents. I wish I would have taken History of Jazz. Dr. Grimshaw is a super nice guy though!

Easy class. Never went, had to study a bit for tests, but still got a good grade. Dr. Grimshaw's lectures are hard to follow, but he's a super cool guy and very passionate about his field. If you want to get something out of the class, it's easy to do. The bit I did take away from the class was actually really applicable and informative.

Dr. Grimshaw is a funny guy. Hes the schools only ethnomusicologist, and it shows. He probably has the most informed take on music and what it is and will have a lot of insights into the field of music. He genuinely cares about his students but is suuuuuper hard to access. Hes always busy, and can feel hard to approach but is solid dude.

This was the most worthless class I have ever taken. Take History of Jazz instead! Dr Grimshaw didn't teach. He showed youtube videos and plunked stuff out on the piano. You could just read the study guide, take the tests, never show up and be totally fine. It didn't enrich my cultural understanding  or give me greater appreciation for the world.

I took the class because it was mandatory for my minor. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone unless they are into anthropology or musicology. His lectures are pretty long and you only know what is going to be on the test by going to the reviews. He is obsessed with Bali. I never opened the text book and I still passed.

Professor Grimshaw is my ideal professor: passionate about his material, knows his stuff backwards, forwards, and upside down, and extremely helpful and personable. He's very interested in his students doing well (easy tests, 4 extra credit assignments, etc.) His lectures are super engaging, with being able to play the instruments and music studied

He did not teach the material very well. He moved through it all very quickly. There is a lot more work for the class than I was expecting for a GE. You will have to study and work for whatever grade you get.

Dr. Grimshaw is enthusiastic about the material and presents it effectively and cogently. His class is the best designed class I have ever attended - he used blackboard in a way that made all the assignments easy to understand and complete. Everything you need to know is explicitly stated in the study guide - if you miss a question it's your fault.

Jeremy is a great guy. He really understands the material and he is enthusiastic. He uses a very complex vocabulary to teach the class but other than that, I recommend him highly. There is more work to this class than you'd think but don't let it stop you since you will learn some cool stuff.

I begged for an add code to get in to this class, wish I hadn't. He knows what he's talking about but he just stands there and talks and talks and I had no idea what I was supposed to be learning. Tests are all online, make a googledoc of the study guide for the class. Group project is  HUGE deal, tons of work.

He's a great guy but overall I found this class actually very difficult. I see myself as very musical but in this class everything was new because of the global sense to it. I would say take the class but work hard. I tried and I'll still probably end up with a C+.

I always look forward to this class. Prof. Grimshaw is funny and passionate about his subject, but doesn't rely on students' passion to get them to pay attention--he works to teach and entertain simultaneously and does a really good job of it. Study guides for the tests are just what they say on the tin--no surprises in the testing center!

It really helps to have a basic knowledge of music. Definitely interesting. 4 Unit tests, all online. His study guides are pretty comprehensive; class Google docs are the BEST. No final-just a group project that's kind of tedious but pretty easy if you plan it out good. Does a couple fun workshops with foreign instruments. Good sense of humor.

For those who say this is an easy A class... Obviously this site is very skewed toward smarty pants. It's not easy. I see why people like this class, but if you are looking for an easy A, just for the sake of GE, then most definitely NO.

If I gave this class an award, it's this: the surprisingly good class.  If all the culture you have lives in your stomach, not a good choice for you.  I took good notes and barely read the books. Lectures may get a little long, but great class overall.  No final, fun teacher, you should have at least a basic understanding of music (what's a scale).

Easy class. Take notes off his powerpoints and study the study guide. It got boring sometimes, but what class doesn't? The final was a group project (easy) and he had extra credit opportunities.  For an interesting GE and 3 credits of A, take this class.
The lectures were the MOST boring thing in the world. Not just that but confusing too. He's a nice guy but not such a great professor.
great professor- you can tell he has a passion for music. lectures were interesting- just make sure you take good notes about everything and read the books and you'll ace the tests every time.

I took this class to fill a GE but really wish I hadn't. Lectures were dry. If you don't think of yourself as one who is interested in World Music, you'll be so bored. It's definitely a doable A though, he gives you study guides before each online test, and the final is a group project.

He's a nice guy but this class is not interesting. If you are planning on taking this for GE, don't. Take good notes also and pay attention to the videos/songs he play in class. You will have to attend three concerts and write papers, his tests are on Blackboard (Close book), and assignments are also on Blackboard. Textbooks with CD's are must.
Great class.  I'm not musically inclined at all, but found this class to be both interesting and educational.  I look at 'foreign' music in a different light now.  Really enjoyed going to class.

This class was really good and easy. There are four unit tests and no final. He gives you a study guide for each test. There is a group presentation at the end which was really easy too. Really no need to read the books, just go to class and take notes. Dr. Grimshaw is a great professor!
Great professor. Gives a study guide before every test with everything that will be on the test.  Very fun class.
Gamelan is the BOMB Dizzle! Dr. G is the best. What more is there to say?
He is a really awesome teacher and involves the class a lot.

Really fun class, great professor.  Professor Grimshaw is awesome.  He prepares you really well for the exams so nothing is a surprise.  You do a group presentation that is actually pretty fun as well.  This class really is not difficult, even if you're not a music major.

His class is the best designed class I have ever attended - he used blackboard in a way that made all the assignments easy to understand and complete. Everything you need to know is explicitly stated in the study guide - if you miss a question it's your fault.

Jeremy is a great guy. He really understands the material and he is enthusiastic. He uses a very complex vocabulary to teach the class but other than that, I recommend him highly. There is more work to this class than you'd think but don't let it stop you since you will learn some cool stuff.

I begged for an add code to get in to this class, wish I hadn't. He knows what he's talking about but he just stands there and talks and talks and I had no idea what I was supposed to be learning. Tests are all online, make a googledoc of the study guide for the class. Group project is  HUGE deal, tons of work.

He's a great guy but overall I found this class actually very difficult. I see myself as very musical but in this class everything was new because of the global sense to it. I would say take the class but work hard. I tried and I'll still probably end up with a C+.

I always look forward to this class. Prof. Grimshaw is funny and passionate about his subject, but doesn't rely on students' passion to get them to pay attention--he works to teach and entertain simultaneously and does a really good job of it. Study guides for the tests are just what they say on the tin--no surprises in the testing center!

It really helps to have a basic knowledge of music. Definitely interesting. 4 Unit tests, all online. His study guides are pretty comprehensive; class Google docs are the BEST. No final-just a group project that's kind of tedious but pretty easy if you plan it out good. Does a couple fun workshops with foreign instruments. Good sense of humor.

For those who say this is an easy A class... Obviously this site is very skewed toward smarty pants. It's not easy. I see why people like this class, but if you are looking for an easy A, just for the sake of GE, then most definitely NO.

If I gave this class an award, it's this: the surprisingly good class.  If all the culture you have lives in your stomach, not a good choice for you.  I took good notes and barely read the books. Lectures may get a little long, but great class overall.  No final, fun teacher, you should have at least a basic understanding of music (what's a scale).

Easy class. Take notes off his powerpoints and study the study guide. It got boring sometimes, but what class doesn't? The final was a group project (easy) and he had extra credit opportunities.  For an interesting GE and 3 credits of A, take this class.
The lectures were the MOST boring thing in the world. Not just that but confusing too. He's a nice guy but not such a great professor.
great professor- you can tell he has a passion for music. lectures were interesting- just make sure you take good notes about everything and read the books and you'll ace the tests every time.

I took this class to fill a GE but really wish I hadn't. Lectures were dry. If you don't think of yourself as one who is interested in World Music, you'll be so bored. It's definitely a doable A though, he gives you study guides before each online test, and the final is a group project.

He's a nice guy but this class is not interesting. If you are planning on taking this for GE, don't. Take good notes also and pay attention to the videos/songs he play in class. You will have to attend three concerts and write papers, his tests are on Blackboard (Close book), and assignments are also on Blackboard. Textbooks with CD's are must.
Great class.  I'm not musically inclined at all, but found this class to be both interesting and educational.  I look at 'foreign' music in a different light now.  Really enjoyed going to class.

This class was really good and easy. There are four unit tests and no final. He gives you a study guide for each test. There is a group presentation at the end which was really easy too. Really no need to read the books, just go to class and take notes. Dr. Grimshaw is a great professor!
Great professor. Gives a study guide before every test with everything that will be on the test.  Very fun class.
Gamelan is the BOMB Dizzle! Dr. G is the best. What more is there to say?
He is a really awesome teacher and involves the class a lot.

Really fun class, great professor.  Professor Grimshaw is awesome.  He prepares you really well for the exams so nothing is a surprise.  You do a group presentation that is actually pretty fun as well.  This class really is not difficult, even if you're not a music major.

This class was covered what is covered in AP Chem, just more in depth, with a few new things. Professor Johnson is very respectful, open and willing to help. You have an online assignment due every week and a written homework due each week, with iclicker quizzes in class (so in this way attendance is kind of mandatory). It was difficult but doable.

This class is definitely a weeder class. If you don't have to take it then you should take CHEM 105. That being said, Prof Johnson is the best professor you can have for this course. If he sees you making the effort to learn, he will meet you where you are and help you improve. Take advantage of office hours and the TAs, you will need them!

This is a hard class but doable. I would recommend Johnson for this class any day! If you care and put in the work, he will help you. If you are ever struggling with questions, especially before exams, go to his office hours he is super willing to help! He really gets to know you and is definitely one of my favorite professors I've had.
He was nice, but he barely taught. I learned everything from the textbook.

This class is so brutal. I recommend going to multiple lectures a day if possible, doing all the weekly reading on sunday or monday night before lecture, and getting the homework done early. Make friends with the TAs and get a study group. While this was a hard class, dr. Johnson always did a good job answering any questions that came up.

Chem 111 is absolutely brutal so no matter what teacher you have, it's going to be rough. Dr. Johnson does care about his students and is available outside of class. I would recommend going to his office hours and he will help you with concepts you don't understand as much. He doesn't do a lot of example problems in class which is difficult though.

Chem 111 is probably the hardest Level one class at BYU. If you're not studying Chem, Biochem or Chem Eng, take Chem 105. Dr Johnson is a really good teacher. He's very accessible outside of class. Him or Dr Sevy are the best options for this class. Dr Sevy does a lot more examples and Dr Johnson goes very in depth on concepts.

This was by far one of the hardest classes I have ever taken, take CHEM 105 instead. You can interchange them. I wish I had. The homework for this class is unbearable. Professor Johnson is nice and cares for his students. He learns EVERYONE'S name. Out of all the teachers for this course, I would pick him or Professor Sevy.

Dr. Johnson is great. His exams are difficult but doable if you understand the homework and quizzes. He's extremely understanding and is always reminding us to come in for help, his office hours are super helpful. Test reviews are given by the TAs and they're helpful. Overall it was a great experience!

Dr. Johnson is very approachable and answers questions well. His exams are pretty tough, though, and the homeworks were difficult, but overall not unbearable. Biophysical chem is already a tough subject, but he tries to help students understand derivations, which comes in handy during exams. Be ready to do calc, readings, and join a study group.

Well-versed professor and loved what he was teaching. The content was a little difficult to understand at times but by studying, attending TA and office hours, asking questions, and doing the assignments you'll definitely pass.

Amazing class, amazing professor! If you care, he will care about you. He goes out of his way to be available in his office. He is also very personally forgiving and gives everyone the feeling that he wants them all to succeed. He is definitely a 10/10 professor. Even if I received a low grade in the class, I would still respect him for everything

Dr. Johnson is really great. I really enjoyed his class, even though it was really difficult at times. He is a really nice guy who cares about his students. He also does a lot of demonstrations, which help to make class periods more interesting and help students to understand the material in a real-world setting. Definite thumbs up!

Dr. Johnson is an awesome professor. He cares about each and every one of his students. His class is definitely a challenge but if you put the work in, you can succeed. He brings the gospel into the classroom which is something I didn't expect going into a chemistry class-- but it was wonderful. If you take CHEM111, take it with Johnson.

Dr. Johnson does a decent job at teaching chemistry. The chemistry course itself is just hard in general no matter the professor. The lectures tend to run at 1000mph and we always seem to be behind the curriculum somehow. However, Dr. Johnson is a fun, loving, and approachable professor.

I love Dr. Johnson. He explains the concept very well, is passionate about chemistry, and treat students well! CHEM 111 is a hard class and requires a lot of work. I consider him one of the finest young professors at BYU. Highly recommend!

Dr. Johnson is clear and cares about his studentsI would highly recommend him as a person and teacher. This is a difficult class, and the TAs are a requirement for completing the homework. (Prep for exams by being able to do every homework problem on your ownexams are fair and generally much easier than the homework problems.)

This class was one of the hardest I've taken so far. Dr. Johnson kind of flew through the material at times, but going to class is definitely important.
