He always emails back really quick and gives you great feedback, so that you are ready for the final presentation. 10/10 take 436 from Professor Vick!

It's pretty easy to get a good grade in his class, the assignments are busy work, his slides are screenshots of the textbook, he gets off-topic easily so lectures aren't the most engaging, there's a semester long group project but the requirements are unclear until the week of the presentation. he has a lot of real world experience which is cool!

I loved this class and the professor is amazing! The whole course is working on a campaign recommendation for a client with a team. Jeremy is super willing to work with each team and help in any step of the process. He is super easy to talk to and super helpful. 10/10 would take this class again. I grew very invested in my teams proposal!

Jeremy is a fun teacher! He tells lots of stories to illustrate the principles he is teaching. Unlike many teachers I have had, these stories are actually relevant to what he is teaching us and help you understand the topic. He will take time to help you understand topics if you ask him. He is very encouraging!

Good class overall, but deadlines kept getting moved, which made planning hard. Some assignments were excused after I submitted them, and the reading load was heavy taking about 5 hrs total. Juggling the client project with regular work was a lot. Professor Vick is great, just needs more consistency and clearer expectations.

His class was interesting, but he didn't provide clear guidance on assignments, which made things difficult. He often changed expectations throughout the semester; I'd finish work and it would no longer be relevant. Still, he was willing to help and offer extra credit, and overall I did enjoy the class. The experience was challenging but enjoyable.
Professor Vick really cared about the subject material and was passionate! He took the time to get to know my class on a personal level and was personable!

Jeremy is a really nice funny guy. His lectures sometimes got a little off topic from the textbook, but they were almost always about a real-life experience that he had. Also he grades a little bit harshly, which is tough because he was really slow to grade.

Professor Vick is really funny. He has a fun dry sense of humor. He is always willinging to change and improve. Very hands on class. He has a lot of real life experience that makes it very meaningful.

I enjoyed this class. The instructor brought a new perspective based on his experience working for other companies. I appreciated getting to work with a real client. One thing to be aware of is that due dates can be adjusted, so sometimes working ahead can actually create more work for you. Overall, I loved this class.

Professor Vick is a great guy and is always willing to help out his students. However, this class had quite a bit of busy work. Lectures often got off topic and it felt like our class time could have been utilized more effectively.
I liked Professor Vick a lot, he cares about his students and does seem to really like teaching at BYU. I will say its a super group work heavy course, so be prepared for that.
Jeremy was a great professor! Lots of group work, overall loved this strategy class.

Jeremy always finds a way to celebrate your work and provide feedback. However, lectures would go off topic, and the homework was busy work. He has great real-world experience, but his stories often eclipsed the learning material and group project time. Expectations were not properly outlined until much later, and we rushed to prepare our projects.

Jeremy is a great professor! His lectures are engaging and he is willing to help students be successful in their group work and individual assignments. The individual assignments are a bit extensive but they help support the overall group project in the class. I would definitely recommend taking this class from Jeremy!
Jeremy is great, he was awesome to take a class with

I think that Jeremy is a great guy, but I had a tough time with him as a professor. He got off topic a lot during lectures and we would rarely have sufficient class time to work on our projects. That was my biggest issue with the class. Explanations for assignments were also pretty confusing and he was tough to get in contact with over email

I genuinely loved having Jeremy as a professor. He is engaging, shares incredible stories, and consistently connects the material to real-world experiences in a way that makes everything feel meaningful and practical. The homework occasionally felt like busywork, but overall I truly enjoyed the class, and Jeremy is an outstanding teacher.
Professor Vick is great, but there is a lot of busy work so just beware!
Such a wonderul professor! Has great real life experience that he brings that is so valuable. Very reasonable, learned a lot. Grateful to be able to take from him! Whole semester is a group project.

Jeremy is an awesome professor, definitely take a class from him! He is great at explaining concepts in ways that students can grasp and will take extra time to ensure you fully understand the material. He is very kind, funny, and his lessons are always spiritually uplifting. I learned many applicable PR strategy tools to use in my future career.

I LOVEEE yorgason. I went into the class thinking i'd hate the topic, but its really interesting and he makes it fun. We did several field trips which was awesome. I didn't buy the Big Al book and I did just fine in the class. the exams are just a cumulation of the daily quizzes. Yorgason makes and effort to know each of his students personally.

MFHD 605: Would not recommend! He is awful at teaching and basically just assumes that everyone is at his level. Our final project and paper included a majority of things that weren't discussed in class that he just assumed we should be able to do. I was also hospitalized during his class and he was not accommodating. Goodish guy, awful professor.

Not a hard class, but I felt like Dr. Yorgason didn't actually teach much at all.  He has you read the textbook and take in-class quizzes (password given in class, only 2 dropped) and tests have quiz questions (which was nice) and mostly info from the readings. Unorganized teaching style which is not my thing, but super nice and accommodating guy.

Dr. Yorgason is hands down the best professor I've had at BYU! He cares about his students and his research. He gave me great career advice and is always willing to go above and beyond for his students. I have loved working with him and would take his class again. The material can be tough at first but after a day or two it becomes second nature.

Dr. Yorgason is great! Since this class is project-based, he would take time every class period to come around, see what progress we had made, and offer advice as to how we could make our project better. You could tell that he really cares about the success of his students. I would take this class again!
Dr. Yorgason is so great at helping people learn how to do research and is so great at being accommodating. I loved this class and would definitely recommend to everybody!

Professor Yorgason was so passionate about this class! He felt like everything we studied was worth publishing. :) He was always available to help and meet if needed, and I felt like he genuinely cared about me and all of my classmates.

This was a faculty-mentored research course, and Jeremy was so helpful in the process. He was really encouraging of all his students, gave us all good feedback on assignments, and was always in a really good mood which seemed to cheer everyone in the class up. He really cares about each of his students and was very understanding.

Dr. Yorgason is really invested in his students. Dr. Yorgason was willing to help us so much in the research process. He was clear with his expectations, and had lots of good feedback. He was easy to work with, and genuinely wanted to help. I would recommend this course to anyone looking to get involved in research.
He is super great and very understaning. He really cares about his students.

This class was a mentored research course where we used the CREATE Project dataset to do our own research analysis on a topic that we chose. Dr. Yorgason helped us to run the statistical analyses and we made posters for our topic and also wrote public scholarship pieces for them. Overall, this was a really fun class and I definitely recommend it!

Tests are straightforward if you attend lectures. Fill out and study the study guides and tests will be easy. Attendance isn't required, but you need to attend to get passwords for reading quizzes to take in-class. Class can be boring, but Professor Yorgason tries to keep it interesting with fun stories. 10 hours of service to older adults required

340 is one of the most challenging classes in the CS program. Dr. Wilkerson does a great job at teaching it. It's fairly common for students to withdraw from this class because they didn't put in the effort. The key to success is do all of the homework and projects on time.

Dr. Wilkerson makes an effort to know his students by name and help them as much as he can. I found myself enjoying class because he explains the material so well that attendance saved me time in the long run. Don't put off projects until the due date; work for 1-2 hrs every other day, asking for help when needed, and you'll be just fine.

I've taken CS 202 & 203 from him. He is very knowledgable but he's the least accommodating professor I've seen at BYU. The classes aren't too difficult– only some of the labs are hard to understand. For a 1 credit class it's ruthless in terms of flexibility– don't expect any extensions ever. He doesn't seem to care about you nor your circumstances.

You will learn a LOT in this class, which can easily overwhelm you if you get behind. Don't underestimate the class project as the videos make it seem easier than it actually is. Dr. Wilkerson is good at deconstructing the textbook in an accessible way and encourages working together in class on the exercises. The class is worth the challenge.

MISM or IS students: This class is hard. Instructions are vague; you have to figure out a lot on your own.  You will learn so many great principles and coding practices in this class that you won't find in the IS program. Don't take this class during a hard semester, leave lots of time for it. I recommend taking this class, but it is difficult.

Professor Wilkerson isn't the most engaging professor you'll ever have, but I found that he was very competent at teaching the topics covered in class and has plenty of relevant industry experience that enabled him to give relevant and insightful advice. CS 240 isn't a cakewalk, but he does a good job of making the material approachable.

CS240 sounds like it was hard in the past but it really isn't now.  CS 235 and 236 were difficult for me, so I'm not some genius.  The lectures are boring, but you don't even need to go to pass the class.  Everything you need is available online.  Each phase of the main project takes around 10 hours which isn't crazy for a CS class.

The guy is competent and passionate about CS. And to be fair he teaches the two hardest classes in CS (240 and 340). But my experience was negative. I couldnt get extensions when I needed them, and Ive seen him turn down other peoples requests for exceptions or extensions. His main piece of advice for those struggling was "Just dont get behind"

CS240 is going to be hard no matter who you take it from but Dr. Wilkerson is a great choice. The semester-long chess project can easily overwhelm you but is manageable if you plan your time wisely, lectures/readings aren't strictly necessary but are very helpful. Dr. Wilkerson is great at answering questions and really cares for his students.

I didn't love his teaching, but the fact that you could skip class and just watch the video lectures when you're actually writing the project code is a HUGE plus. Wish the other CS classes had this structure. Pretty hard projects, especially the completely unnecessary Programming Exam at the start. So much time wasted on brute force memorization.

Dr. Wilkerson is an amazing professor! 340 is a heavy class on its own, but Wilkerson explains each of the concepts thoroughly and gives plenty of in-class time to work on exercises and ask questions. I couldn't recommend him enough!
203 was just like 202, super easy, nothing surprising, nothing was too much work.

CS202 is an online class. It is very well organized and you know what to expect each week. The quizzes are not difficult if you actually do the readings/watch the videos. The labs are not difficult but are informative. You have one of each, each week. And you have plenty of time to get them done.

I have taken multiple classes from Dr. Wilkerson. In each of the classes I have the same complaints. I really don't like his readings, and without a photographic memory you won't remember the obscure detail that he randomly puts on the reading quiz. His exercises are broken and often the TA had to help me set it up. Overall negative experience.

Professor Wilkerson cares about all of his students and tries to give you all the resources you need to succeed. He is a fantastic teacher and does a really good job teaching difficult concepts. He is also very caring and willing to help. 340 is a tough class no matter what but I would definitely recommend taking it from Wilkerson.

Dr. Wilkerson is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. CS 240 is a difficult class no matter who you take it from, but Dr. Wilkerson gives you all the tools you need to succeed. He also makes himself available outside of class to students who need it.

CS340 has a bad reputation, but it's not THAT bad of a class. They've done a lot of good work fixing up the main project so your time isn't wasted. The twice-a-week quizzes/exercises are pretty easy (but not worth much). The tests were weird, the midterm was proctored but the final was open-book. Prof Wilkerson opens every class like seminary haha

Wilkerson is a really great professor for a really difficult course. He asks a lot of students but also provides the resources necessary for our success. He's always willing to make time to meet outside of class, which is also great. I think 240 is pain no matter who you take it from, but he definitely doesn't make it worse.

CS 340 was the hardest/most time consuming classes i've taken but I'm grateful I was able to take it with Professor Wilkerson. He teaches things in a way that's easy to understand and he really wants his students to grasp the concepts being taught. Get ready for loooong hours of coding! Also, the late policy can be pretty rough if you fall behind.

Dr. Wilkerson is inspirational as a master in the world of Computer Science. He knows what he is talking about. He truly cares about his students as evidenced by how kind, patient, and respectful he was when we asked questions. The knowledge I gained by taking CS 240 and CS 340 from him enabled me to launch my professional career.

Solid professor, for a CS prof. He's better than the usual prof at explaining things. Will make you work for a good grade but does things to be helpful. I will say however that at times I felt his classes were more demanding, without an equal increase in help

He isn't the most flashy or funny professor, but his clear and deliberate style of lecturing worked well for me. Yes, he relies on powerpoints for most lectures, but he doesn't just read them verbatim, and the code examples he writes to supplement his lectures were always applicable and clear. CS240 was going to be tough for me no matter what.

Although the class is very difficult, Professor Wilkerson gives you all the material needed to success in the class. The projects are very large, so do not start late, that is the best way to fail the class. Overall Professor Wilkerson is very sincere but also very focused and somewhat serious. If you want there is a ton to learn from him.

I'm a bit shocked reading some of the reviews that hated Dr. Wilkerson. I think a lot of students hate CS340 and blame the whole experience on Dr. Wilkerson. While the class CS340 is absolutely insane to the extent that it led me to drop other classes until I wasn't even a full-time student, in my opinion, Dr. Wilkerson is a fantastic professor.

He is an easy grader but a firm educator. He cares about what you learn and the class revolves around understanding material that will benefit you the most. 240 was a lot of coding and you can't procrastinate. However, if you start early you will do great!

Dr. Wilkerson is a decent professor who has the hard task of teaching 340, a truly horrible class. The project is time consuming and you spend so much time coding that you don't care about the design patterns that are actually supposed to be the point of the class. I know it's being improved; hope it gets better. There's also a TON of reading.

Dr. Wilkerson is a divisive personality. He has a lot of industry knowledge, but you really have to pull it out of him (he'll just read slides unless asked a specific question). He says that he cares about feedback but didn't apply any of it during my semester with him. His teaching was just okay, but the actual material is interesting.

60 hours a week on this class! This class is taught in Java, yet the textbook is in C#! You will spend 5 hours reading twice a week for assignments harder than needed. You will have to depend on someone else for a project worth half your grade. He gives you code (never works) and instructions (unclear) for the project made of untaught concepts.

Don't take classes from Dr. Wilkerson. When he got bad ratings, he created a survey to see what he is doing wrong. Everyone gave helpful answers, which he then addressed in class. However, he failed to correct any of those problems, assuring that next semester the class would be different and better. He puts 0 work into this very difficult class.

Why BYU students love profs who just read powerpoint slides? Everyone can do that without PHD degree. His class materials are very unorganized I had to watch videos way ahead to understand his assignment explanation video (which is also just reading the powerpoint slides)

Professor Wilkerson is the only professor that I have ever specifically sought out to take a second class from. CS340 is hard, and the flipped classroom probably makes it harder, but I've never learned as much in any other class as I have in CS240 and CS340. I couldn't have survived an internship without all that I learned from Dr. Wilkerson.

He does a great job teaching this class. It's meant to be a tough class, and it is, but he gives lots of opportunities to ask questions and clarify, and is willing to help you individually outside of class time, and help everyone pass. If you are willing to work, this class is great, and doesn't eat up too much time provided you start early!

Professor Wilkerson is the worst professor I've ever had. He gives us ridiculously long daily assignments that, on average, take 2-3 hours to complete, plus the massive project we have. Each part of the 4 part project alone takes probably a good 30-35 hours, if you're lucky and Wilkerson's code doesn't break everything, which it often does.

Professor Wilkerson is probably the single worst professor I've ever had. His version of teaching is just giving us outdated readings and then giving us overly complicated exercises that don't do anything to actually help explain what the readings went over. We also have a massive project on top of all that, with no actual instruction from him.

If you enjoy being asked to read unhelpful readings and having tons of homework plus a project that makes the 240 one look small, then this is the class for you. Wilkerson doesn't teach anything, he just assigns readings, and makes sure that we have overly difficult assignments for each reading in addition to a massive project over the semester.

If you enjoy a class where the professor does nothing, you have more work than most 5 credit classes but only get 3 credits, then this is the class for you. Professor Wilkerson doesn't teach in this class at all. He assigns lousy readings that do a bad job of explaining the material, then gives us an exercise with no instructions on how to do it.
He's a great professor! Knows his stuff, and wants to help the students through. It is a hard class by nature, but doable if you put in the time.

Stellar. He is spiritual, understanding, and fair. He wants his students to succeed and does all he can to help them. His slides were good and so were his lectures. CS 240 is an insanely time consuming class. Much of the time, the material he lectured on wouldn't be used for another couple weeks, but there wasn't much he could do about that.

I truly believe that Dr. Wilkerson is the best CS professor at BYU; he is definitely a master of the subject and has a ton of person real-life anecdotes that make his class truly valuable. He is available outside of class and willing to help you understand anything. I wish every professor was like Dr. Wilkerson.

Fantastic professor, him and Barker are both great options for this class. Cares about his students, makes time to talk about the projects, and has done a lot to make this class easier on the students.

Dr Wilkerson is by far one of the best computer science teachers at BYU. His background as a Software Engineer and Consultant give him years worth of experience that can't be beat. He cares about the students, wants to learn your name, and is making significant changes to the computer science program to make life easier for everyone.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He tries to learn each of his students' names before the semester starts, and he invites his students to meet with him outside of class. The projects are most of the grade, but he has slides full of information that are available all semester with examples of all the concepts he teaches.
This class is always super project heavy. Professor Wilkerson is extremely nice and helpful with helping learn the material.

Great professor. One of the few who really understands that he is susceptible to mistakes instead of always blaming the student for their shortcoming. Very helpful and understanding when the student reaches out. Lectures are clear, concise, and very applicable to the homework and projects.

Dr. Wilkerson is a great professor. One of the first professor I've ever had that knew my name. The material in cs240 is HARD. It takes a lot of work and effort to not get behind. If you stay ahead on the projects, the lectures make more sense and are easier to incorporate into the project. He provides lots of materials and example code to help.

Professor Wilkerson has lots of industry experience, and it shows in his teaching style. He uses real life examples to explain things in an applicable way. He is understanding and wants to help you succeed. Personally dedicated to his students.

Dr. Wilkerson is one of the few professors in the department that gives a darn about the students and teaching software engineering. He is a solid choice for 240 along with Rodham. His lectures are the most useful thing in the world, but the material is easy to access and he is available to help.

Not my favorite professor ever. His lectures are fairly useless and he loves to talk himself up at every opportunity. His class is also very disorganized, with lots of material spread out across many slides. He's incredibly self-righteous and has zero sympathy for students working together at all. Don't procrastinate the client or you'll regret it.
Great teacher, very clear presentations and takes the time help you understand the projects thoroughly. 100% would take again, and I plan on taking him for as many classes as I can (3 so far)

Teaches the material clearly and in an interesting manner. He really cares for his students and will do everything to help them succeed. 240 is a hard class, but you can do it! Start on the projects early and get help as much as possible. Go to class because he'll go over tips and tricks that'll make the projects easier.

Dr. Wilkerson is a great person and a solid professor. This was my second time taking the course and he actually taught the material. 240 is tough. He helps you on the project during lecture. Easily, one of the most well-rounded professors in the CS department. Barely read the textbook. Go to the TA's early and often and you'll succeed.

Dr. Wilkerson is a great professor! I really appreciated that he teaches his industry specific experience in addition to the theory of design patterns. He did a really good job of providing lecture slides and examples full of material to help with the projects. He cares a lot and really encourages lifelong learning!

Great professor! He really cares for the students! Of all professors Ive had hes the most likely to learn and remember your name. He teaches pretty clearly and jes willing to meet one-on-one if you need it.
Dr. Wilkerson is one of the best professors I've ever had! His lectures are very helpful, he is very caring and considerate, and he truly has the students' best interests in mind.

Dr. Wilkerson is great! Good lecturer and really understands what the reality of the difficulty of these projects and how new the information can be. He teaches to the students needs and is a very fair professor.

Jerod Wilkerson is a good professor. He is an expert in Java and good at explaining the concepts that we needed to learn. CS340 involves a big group project that takes the entire semester. He recognized that we were spending a lot of time with the group project, so he decreased the requirements for the last part of the project to lighten the load.

Dr. Wilkerson is an excellent teacher that cares deeply about his students. It is evident that he puts in a large amount of time preparing for lectures, and teaches with lots of real world examples. It's refreshing to have someone with a lot of recent industry experience in the department!

Yes, take this class. The slides a packed with information which is good and bad. Good because it makes studying for the tests easy, bad because it makes the lectures harder to follow. He's a great teacher, easy to listen to. He'll help you. This class is hard though, you have to get above a 70% average on the final and midterm in order to pass.

Cannot stress enough how worth it it is to go to SLC to take marketing 201! Prof Wiest and Prof Christensen are some of the funniest guys ever. They don't really believe in the traditional school system, so their tests are just projects and they have barely any graded work. Despite that, they are SO knowledgeable and you learn a ton every time.
Jerry is a great caring teacher that loves what he does.

He teaches with Steve Wiest and these guys are legends. They are so hilarious and play jokes on each other all the time. They love having application based learning. No tests, just projects that are not too hard and pretty interesting to do. Totally worth going up to salt lake for. You do have to show up, but class is interesting so its worth it.

I took his class a couple years ago and had to give JC another solid rating. Also, I put attendance as mandatory because if you are not showing up to JC's baller presentations, then you're not really going anywhere. In life, if you are blessed enough to know JC, you will be successful.

THE BEST! He teaches the class with Steve Wiest, and honestly i loved going to class each week. They are both retired marketing professionals, and know how to make learning fun. The class is about experiencing marketing rather than memorizing textbook stuff. Super funny. No exams, just 3 projects that are easy and fun. Going to SLC = worth it

GUYS!! My friend told me to take this class through SLC because of how easy it was and I can't even put into words how true that is. No textbook, I NEVER went to class not even once. Very few assignments overall and the midterm and final have options to do projects instead which are SO easy. Literally free credits.

I appreciated MKTG 201 from Prof. Christensen more than I thought I would. He cares a lot about the subject and approaches the subject in a way that seems friendly and exciting - and doesn't grade based on memorization of the concepts. He is more concerned about you experiencing the topics than memorizing.

Jerry loves his students and makes his class as easy as it can be. You choose whether or not to take the tests and let us do projects instead. I was able to use projects done in previous classes and received full points. He even changed one of my online quiz scores to 100. I went to class the first half of the semester and then did not go again.

He puts a lot of thought & effort into class and you'll save yourself the GPA plunge of taking mktg in Provo. We voted as a class to replace the midterms/final exam with projects that were graded based on turning it in. Very flexible with assignments. 5 question, open note reading quiz available for a week based on the class just after. Love him
Professor Christensen is a legend in marketing. I took his class last winter and it was great experience. His class was so interesting, so you must attend and be part of the discussion. Love it.

This is the best professor at BYU!!! Jerry is the man who cares about who he teaches and more importantly what he teaches. Every thing he says is worth gold. What he teaches will make his students successful in life!

Professor Christensen is the BEST. I had an excellent time in his class! He loves to do hands-on learning projects. He is very understanding of his students and wants them to succeed. No reason not to get an A. Also, take this class if you have any Danish ties or have/or will serve in the Denmark Copenhagen Mission. He treated me the best.

Professor Christensen is an excellent professor, he is very respectful and caring towards his students. He has a very warm and humorous personality that makes him very approachable. You can tall that he prioritizes your success and is willing to work with you to help you succeed. The class was not to difficult and was fairly enjoyable.
JC will actually teach you the art of marketing, and not just test you on forgettable principles. Great class.
This class was probably my favorite one I took all semester. Super engaging and fun. Definitely take it when offered!!
He is amazing, I 10/10 recommend that you take a class from him! Just make sure that he makes Danish food for you!

Absolutely GOATED professor. Learned so much about marketing and was such a joy to hear from every week. Never had a professor like this who involves the students so much and helped them love what is being taught.
I highly recommend taking this class especially from Professor Christensen. He has been my favorite professor so far. I loved this class and his class was very entertaining.

Jerry is the best professor. Don't take any other marketing classes from any of those scrubs from Provo. He puts in hard work. This is the only professor I've seen that has actually had a career in the subject he teaches, (marketing) which means he cares about teaching us real-life marketing.
Professor Christensen is the boyyyyyy. He offers project options to make up for points missed on the test, so everybody should get an A. Super easy, and Professor Christensen is a dope guy

He is the best professor at BYU. His lectures were really fun and easy to understand the concepts. There is only one quiz a week for homework. He loves to interact with students. He is also caring for international students. There are lot of extra credit opportunities you can get as well. Please take Marketing from him.

It was a pretty good class, the lectures were long and sometimes it was hard to focus and know what we were supposed to be learning, but overall it wasn't bad and it was a good intro to marketing! He's a great guy, he just likes to talk a lot!

Honestly one of my favorite professors and a great class as well. The tests were hard but the weekly quizzes helped prepare. The lectures always ended on time and were entertaining while helpful. If you have to take this class, take this professor for sure. (And if you dont have to take this class its good to take anyways with him)

Professor Christensen really tries his best to explain how the marketing principles taught in the textbook are relevant in today's world. I really appreciated how much Professor Christensen cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He allows for opportunities to apply what we learned in real-world applications.

Tests are worth 60% of your grade, but extra credit can be done to improve your test score. Requires participation in every class. He likes to have active discussions during class. I didnt do that awesome on the first exam, but extra credit helped me still get an A out of this class.

Doctor Christensen was the best! His lectures were geared to help you learn with many examples to help you remember concepts. He is very considerate on tests - he threw out questions that were confusing or that most students missed. He also offered extra credit which was geared towards helping you apply the material learned in class. 10/10 amazing!
A little unorganized, but gives us an opportunity to apply marketing which was good for people who are not the best at taking tests.
Honestly one of the beat professors out there!! Super fun class and super funny guy!! I will truly miss having him as my teacher!

Prof. JC is seriously the best professor I have had at BYU. He sincerely cares about student learning and offers great opportunities to meet with local entrepreneurs in marketing to earn extra credit if you struggled on the midterms (which are fair). He is hilarious, caring, respected, and a breath of fresh air for BYU. TAKE FROM HIM

Super engaging lectures with a cool, funny, and caring guy. Open-note quizzes every week, a midterm, and a final. He even gave us the option of doing a presentation to replace one of our exams with full credit (which I did on Chick Fil A in under 10 minutes to get 100 on my final w/o taking it). SUPER manageable with an AWESOME professor. Take him!

Jerry is one of my favorite teachers. He really teaches us what is happening right now in German speaking countries. I learned a lot in his class. This class however is what you make of it. If you want to learn, you will learn a lot and Jerry will assist you every step of the way. Because the content changes every semester I'm taking it again.
Great class.

Professor Christensen did a great job of making this class actually relevant.  He brings extensive knowledge and years of experience in the business world and helps us make judgments about current economic events in Germany and around the world.  Use the Wort des Tages on your assignments if you want GermanSwiss chocolate!

Professor Christensen is really respectful, professional and great. I learned a lot in his class, and he gave good feedback and helped each student improve. I enjoyed learning a lot of maybe "random" things about Business in Germany and German words, but it was awesome and useful to do so. I improved as a result of his class.

Professor Christensen is the man. He allows for you to really learn at your own pace and also step outside your comfort zone. I came into the class not knowing what to expect, but he helped us choose what we wanted to learn, and made an awesome curriculum out of it. If you want to learn a lot about both business and German, this is the guy to take.
This class was great! There wasn't too much as far as assignments, but you still learn a lot about the environment of business in contemporary Germany.

Business German is far and away the most useful German class that I have taken at BYU. Professor Christensen molds the curriculum to fit with CURRENT topics in Business relevant to Germany. This class is a must take for any returned missionary and anybody interested in applying their German skills to their future career no matter what the field.

This class is awesome for German speakers.  It is learning about the side of Germany, Switzerland, Austria that you never learned on your mission or in any other class on campus.  Professor Christensen is awesome and helpful if you ever have any questions or concerns.  He just wants you to participate and you will be good!

This class was a ton of fun, chill, and super interesting.  There is no real book for the course, just news and business reports.  The assignments were weekly and easy to accomplish if you attended class.  Dr. Christensen did a great job teaching this class according to our needs and wants of learning German Business language and German business.
A Fantastic Class! If you are interested in Business in Germany. He worked in Europe and knows the ins and outs. It is super useful for Life not like many other College Classes.

Professor Christensen is very effective at using current material to help paint the picture of the current german business world. He gives excellent feedback and his classes are always very interesting and engaging.

Professor Christensen is very knowledgeable and is able to teach effectively by engaging the students in every stage of the learning process.  Class is not a lecture but rather a discussion on current events analyzed through the 'marketing' and 'business german' lenses. I highly recommend this class to anyone serious about learning the subject.

Great class and a great environment! Jerry is a really chill guy and easy to work with. He got to know all of us and it made the class a lot more fun. It was pretty chill too but you still learn a lot of interesting stuff . If you are a German RM and are remotely interested in international business take this!

This class is great.  I would highly recommend it to German-speaking returned missionaries.  It's a great way to keep up language skills and re- immerse yourself in the current culture of Germany, Switzerland, and Austria.  It's also not that difficult, so your grades will also be stellar.

One of the best business professors I have had at BYU.  I had surgery during the class and he went out of his way to help me out.  Test can be a little challenging but his lectures are great and he covers the material. Take him!!
Great teacher who is willing to help. He understands what it is like to be a student and he wants you to succeed in the class.

Professor Christensen was wonderful. He was clear and concise. He uses a lot of real life examples to help you understand the words and definitions. He's easy to talk to and helps work around potential problems. His marketing class was one of the only 8am classes I made sure to be on time for and truly hated to miss.

Jerry Christensen is really a great teacher.  His presentations are well thought out and presented.  Class time was very productive and just seemed to fly by.  I really enjoyed every minute in class.  Mr. Christensen was willing to help those needing help and knew everyone by name in the class. Impressive!

Appearance? Can't help ya there JC. Not enough options for us guys. Not that there's anything wrong with that! jk  It was a great class and everyone should take it just to understand the world of marketing. JC was helpful, material was relevant and the class was very fun to attend.
what a teacher! he is an absolute stud...make sure you take it from him. Read the chapters and you're golden!

He is totally worth the drive to SLC.  He makes marketing fun and interesting.  He totally gets the whole class involved and makes you think.  The quiz's each week are open book, the two midterms are open book and he tells you what he's testing on.  It is the best class I have ever taken at BYU.  It's not a cake walk, but well worth it.

He is incredibly unorganized. The TAs and the professors were never on the same page, everyone was always confused. We got behind on the material because Dr Johnson would get sidetracked during class.

Jerry Johnson was a great professor and I really enjoyed his class. I enjoyed his lectures because him and Byron would try to make boring lectures a little more interesting. I did not enjoy how the class felt pretty disorganized. Some of the bigger assignments didn't give very many instructions it oftentimes felt unclear. The textbook is not needed

I had Dr. Johnson, Adams, and Klabacka. They were fun and made lectures entertaining, though sometimes random. The class felt easy since I took AP Bio, so much was review. The “What Should I Know” sheets helped for exams. The mandatory TA lab was annoying and I didn't really learn anything from it. The final was also way harder than the midterms.

Taking BIO 130 from Jerry, Byron, and Randy in Fall 25 was often confusing (class organization is kind of all over the place) but was also an overall fun, edifying experience. Lecture attendance is not mandatory and they rant about silly things often, lol. You'll read a book & write a semi-research paper about evolution. Also there's a TA-led lab.

I don't get the dislike, Dr. Johnson does an excellent job teaching alongside Dr. Adams. Up to the first exam the class is a little disorganized but doing the test review papers saves you and TA reviews. Really nice and willing to help you. Class is really easy to either learn, or to retain nothing. Depends on you. Textbook is not super necessary.

I hated this class. It had so much potential but it was so poorly organized. Exam dates were moved last minute. Textbook readings are irrelevant and we were always behind in lectures. The only way to suceed is to memorize the TA exam review slides, like word for word. They say the class isn't about memorization but it totally is. I learned nothing.

If you took BIO130 from him and want another of his classes, this is not the one. There is almost no new material, though it's interesting stuff. I never read the textbook. If you're looking for a low-stakes chill BIO class, this one is pretty good. Keep in mind that the free response sections on the tests are quite long. Jerry's a funny guy :)

Don't take this course. It is awful. Jerry and Byron seem to go to class without any plan or preparation on what they're going to talk about. They are anti pre-med and do what they can to put down doctors or medical students when possible in class. It is impossible to know what will be on tests.

(FYI, I never used my textbook.) Professor Johnson is a really great professor and he really loves to bring gospel topics into lectures. Labs were not quite lined up with lectures, but the class was great. I would definitely recommend his class for BIO 130! :)

Lectures did not make any sense. They involved Jerry and Byron having a discussion back and forth often getting sidetracked. The labs never matched with the lectures because we were so far behind. There is a paper that helps with your grade so its not just tests. The TAs were never on the same page and always had something different to say,

Good professor, the course itself was disorganized from the start but the content was comprehensible. If you have no prior biology knowledge you will struggle with how glossed-over topics are in this course. Due dates kept shifting all semester and the rubric would always be outdated. Overall while Johnson was funny it was mediocre.
Very engaging teacher and presents the material really well. The class itself isn't too hard, just make sure you go to the TA reviews for the tests.
Taught with Professor Adams. Hilarious class, loved every second of it. Really made the material interesting and fun without taking away from the educational apects.

If you are pre-med, PA, dental, or any other preprofessional, take this class your senior year after you have applied to a professional school. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS before then, even if your advisor puts it down for you to take a sophomore. I have never taken a class that is so inapplicable to medicine and it is waste of time. Ten thumbs down.

I hate this class. Jerry is very unorganized and he does not make it clear what needs to be done to succeed in the class. The TAs do their best but they don't keep up to date on grading and so it is difficult to determine what you need to change to get the grade you want. I wish this class was not required for many life science majors.

Jerry is an interesting guy and good lecturer. That being said, this class is very unorganized.  The TA's do their best but they get behind on grading and so I never knew if I was doing things correctly. Interesting class and I like how Jerry teaches but the disorganization was a big hindrance to my learning.  Needs some fixing for sure.

Took his BIO 130 class with him and Byron. They are amazing teachers. It felt more like standup comedy than class at times. That being said they sometimes get behind on lectures so it is important to no slack up and do your own homework studying.
One of the funniest professors ever, but also very kind. Would take from him again in a heartbeat.

Byron and Jerry taught BIO 130 together. I rarely read the textbook - just for diagrams and questions. Pay attention to any posters and homework they assign, stay on top of the book and and go to review sessions and this class is easy! They do tend to wander during lectures, but attend so you understand the major points better.

His lectures were great, but organization is not good. Half of the "study guides" weren't on the tests, and some of his assignments either made me feel like I was in middle school or weren't clearly explained. The worst thing was that they clearly explained the curve they'd put on the class, then they never applied it
No organization at all. I never knew what was coming on the tests. Lectures are not helpful. TAs are as helpful as they can be, but they do not know what is coming on the tests either.

I highly recommend taking this class even if you're just considering life sciences as a major, it'll change your life seriously. Jerry has been my favorite professor here so far! Bio 130 was a hard class, the exams are TOUGH, but Jerry and Byron are hilarious and make class fun and also teach really well.

I do not recommend. While she chooses interesting content and knows her stuff, class discussions always devolve and confuse, and exams are unnecessarily hard (I've spoken to other students about this so it's not just me lol). I have found her to be inconsiderate and at times straight up unkind towards students in feedback and in meetings.

Here's the thing. She clearly knows her stuff and her passion is contagious, but she is quite simply mean. On multiple occasions, I have seen her make catty and condescending comments both in person and on essays as feedback. It's such a shame. If she weren't on a power trip or overdramatically stingy with points, it could be a favorite class!

Horrocks is a great person, but a very harsh grader. Her tests and quizzes ask for nit-picky and ultra specific details. I would not take her class again but I am glad that I had this experience. If I had the choice between her and a different professor, the latter is enticing.

I took this a little while ago and it was unnecessarily difficult. She is very nitpicky when grading assignments, taking off points for non-issues when the instructions themselves were unclear. Feedback is harsh and oftentimes ridiculous. The reading quizzes really took down my grade even though I only missed one day of reading the whole semester.

Expectations were never clear. Impossible to please her because she had no guidelines. Only graded assignments well if she personally liked the topic, disregarding textual evidence. Constantly told students in class their ideas were just wrong. Flippantly dismissed several students' concerns about grades in front of the class. Awful experience.

Took because a friend recommended her, what a mistake that was. She is vindictive and petty and she seems to really enjoy taking all of her repressed anger out on students in her feedback. I haven't had a professor who was so condescending and cruel like this before. Avoid avoid avoid!

We made paper, ink, printed and I really did enjoy it! However, Professor Horrocks is such a harsh grader. There are no rubrics for assignments so they are vague and a lot. There are reading quizzes almost every class and did some damage to my grade. There are also two tests and a giant paper for our final. Read everything and do not miss class.

Life is good if you're one of her favorites, and terrible if you aren't. Beyond that, she is easily the least understanding and flexible professor I've ever had. She doesn't care about your mental health at all, and insists you drop her class if you need even one-off extra support. Also, really rude in written feedback. Wouldn't recommend.

Professor Horrocks is a good professor and really engaging, but this class was very difficult! The three tests were very tough, and there were lots of homework and projects. The class discussions were super interesting, but I did not think it was worth it for the amount of effort I had to put into the class.

Professor Horrocks is amazing! I took 291 from a different professor and hated it, so I was dreading 292, but the way she taught was just fantastic! She's very organized and teaches author by author which was perfect for my brain. If you pay attention in class and take notes, you should do well on the tough exams. Class discussions were THE BEST!

I will always remember Professor Horrocks's amazing lectures. Seriously, the way she talks about history makes it seem like she's sharing drama from work; I couldn't get enough of it. The tests, however, were brutal.  She makes very clear study guides so that your studying will be to good use, but you will need to study lots.

Prof H wasn't my favorite teacher, but once I learned how she worked, class went a lot better for me. She's passionate about the subject, maybe too so for an entry-level class. However, before the first exam we met and I asked for help preparing. She listened, and we build a good relationship that helped me succeed in class. Very kind!

Polarizing professor. I think her high expectations, blunt humor, and pushback on students's opinions (regardless of whether or not she agrees) is off-putting for some people. I learned a ton from this class and feel like I grew as a writer because of her feedback on assignments. Cool lit. material. May not be for everyone, but I liked her a lot.

All other reviews aside, I loved this woman. Dr. Horrocks is insightful, incredibly funny, and a master at teaching. She takes time to learn names and use them in class. Her exams are tough and so is her grading, but she makes learning the literature fun and offers extra credit on all quizzes. She's become a favorite professor for me.

Dr. Horrocks really cares about the subject and it shows. Her lectures were very interesting despite what could have been stale material. The second half of the semester is definitely more enjoyable than the first half. Her tests are difficult, but if you put effort into studying you can do well.
Professor horrocks is really interesting in lectures, but this was an insanely difficult course. I really struggled with her criteria for writing and was just frustrated all semester long.

Looking for someone that cares about your success and will help you if you’re struggling? Find anyone else. 
She teaches class very well, but her lack of consideration to situations and their impact on student work was insulting. She will not bend her late policy, even due to extenuating circumstances. 
My advice? Find another 303 class.

The tests are hard and specific, but not terrible. You definitely need to take notes and do the readings. Daily quizzes (open book) The class itself was fine, but Dr Horrocks has a tendency to look down on people. She regularly makes people feel stupid if their answer isnt hers. Also, there were things on the test reviews that we didn't know.

Dr. Horrocks is an amazing teacher! I'm not the biggest fan of reading, but I often found myself enjoying the readings and loving her analysis of them. You'll have about 3 hours of reading each week, and you'll have to work for the tests (which are horribly long), but you really learn SO much!!

I hope everyone gets to take a class from Professor Horrocks because she is incredible! My favorite professor I have ever taken a class from, and genuinely cares about her students. I would go in after exams and she was happy to work through concepts and authors with me. She develops a very personal relationship with every student, and shows it.

Think of your worst elementary teacher. She is strict on tardies, phones, won't take HW unless it is printed out, has clear favorites, makes rude comments. Degrades students with mean comments/shame and finds power in it. Not understanding at all. Run while you can!

Professor Horrocks was one of the rudest people I have ever taken class from. She was extremely condescending. She was not understanding of students. If you would try and talk to her about something she's respond with "So what" or "Who cares"? She set extremely high expectations and then would shame students for stressing about them. Don't take!

I absolutely adore Professor Horrocks. After looking at her reviews, I was hesitant to take her until another English major told me that I should. She is one of the most amazing professors I have ever had! If you're looking for an easy A, don't take this class. However, if you're looking for engaging lectures and to learn a lot, she is awesome!

Prof. Horrocks really knows her stuff and overall has a lot of amazing teaching skills and fosters a lot of great discussion in class. But, over a third of reading and class discussion and homework questions were purely political and she definitely seemed to push some political agendas and were completely unrelated to literary theory or english.

I've never met a professor more like Harvey Dent (Two-faced) in my life. In class and in her office hours, she was always pumping us up about how well we were doing (later in the class she later started revealing favorites by showing their good work and the non-favorites bad work) and then in her critiques, she would totally tear apart your paper.

I took 292 from Dr. Horrocks a couple of years ago, and I had a much better experience this time around. She has VERY high expectations, meaning you will need to read your texts meticulously, participate, and study hard for tests. However, she also really cares about getting feedback and improving her classes. I would take from her again.

I had her for both 495 and 375. Both classes were a lot of reading and writing, so you will need to make her class a priority (taking two of her classes one semester was a mistake). In class discussions were a lot of fun, she was really respectful of the students and their opinions. But she was the hardest grader I've ever had. Still enjoyed class.

She's excellent! I loved her classes so much. She's engaging, and extremely caring. She gives all the tools to succeed, you just have to use them. She's passionate about her subjects and transmits this well to students. Work load is reasonable.

Very interesting class and teaching style. Unfortunately incredibly biased. Grades dropped the more she showed her disinterest in students who weren't English majors and often tells people the wrong things to write on papers so they will get marked down. No interpretation is correct unless it is her interpretation and same goes with opinions.

Her teaching style is very entertaining, and I was never bored. I always could pay attention. Her grading, however, is very difficult. She is very opinionated and you better write how she would see it. Very intelligent, witty, and she knows it. Insane amount of reading

I had Professor Horrocks for English 251 and 294. Her classes are quite challenging, but immensely fulfilling. She is a tough, fair grader, and always helpful if you seek her help outside of class. Her sense of humor is sharp as a tack but never personal or derogatory. I think some students dislike her because they don't understand her humor.
This miserable beep sure loves company.

Incredible! I took ENGL 251 from Dr. H too--classes with her are always very conversation heavy, so there's plenty of opportunity for students to participate and discuss. She's hilarious, engaging, and super personable, and she's a fair grader. There's a lot of reading to do, but it's an English class, so that's normal. My favorite teacher at BYU!

Prof. Horrocks is extremely rude. She sees things only her way and doesn't mind openly mocking students in class. I didn't learn a lot from her except that the English major was for me, because that's what this whole class was about -- why not to be an English major (no money in it, etc.).

Professor Horrocks is incredible! You will do a lot of reading in this class, but if you do the reading guides and go to class you'll learn an incredible amount. If you want a class that will prepare you for an English Major, take 251 from her. Keep an open mind and remember that you don't have to agree with every literary theory taught.

Professor Horrocks is a fabulous teacher--she isn't easy, but she is fabulous.  I have learned so much in this class and I recommend her to anyone wanting to major in English. She is also super laid back and fun to talk to, which can be nice when you are struggling and want to meet with her.

Horrocks was the worst professor I have ever had. She seemed to dislike me for petty and personal reasons. It was very unprofessional.  Her job is the only significant distraction in her life, and this makes her persnickety. She considers herself a true academic. I think she believes she is superior to all who do not share the same obsessions.

Respectable teacher. nothing to complain about. do the work and you'll get an A. her feedback will tell you everything you need to know to get an A. Assignments are blunt. follow instructions and you'll be fine.
She is praiseworthy... gotta hand it to her for finishing grad school.  #benicetoher

Prof. Horrocks was awesome. It's a class about different theorists so it may not be the most exciting class for some people. It was interesting! You have study guides for the readings that you turn in and that's basically the only hw besides 4 different essays. And then tests. She's awesome but she expects you to be adults so just be respectful.

Tests require close to verbatim recall of 1200+ pages  and ability to infer what any number of authors think about any given subject - to madame's satisfaction.  If you're open minded enough (or have the type of brain that can binge and purge copious levels of "he said, she said" without the book/s on hand, this class is easy as.
Super hard class, but I learned more than in any other class. She is one of BYU's best professors. Makes you read more than is reasonable though so balance this class with other lighter load classes.

Team-taught with Christianson. The class is supposed to be from about the 1600s-2000, but you can tell her favorite era is the Victorian -- you spend about half the class in it. There's a lot of reading (200pg every other night), and the tests are really hard at the start bc they don't tell you how to study.
I loved Professor Horrocks! She's funny and super passionate about literature (makes you want to be too). She is extremely willing to help you when you ask for it.
She's very clear. As long as you are willing to follow her directions closely and bring new insights to papers and discussions, you should be fine.

Prof Horrocks is really nice and gave a good introduction to the English major. I wasn't an English major but I still found a few helpful things in this class. For a one hour class, this had a lot of work! We had to go to a few things and write papers and there was a bit of reading. Do the extra credit and study for the daily quizzes.

Prof. Horrocks is the hardest and best professor I've had. It was a difficult course and the tests were intensive, but  I learned more in that class than any other. It prepared me for my future English courses and continues to impact how I study and work. If you go talk with her she offers great advice and genuinely cares.

I was very disappointed with Prof H. She seemed cool at first, boy was I wrong! She had a personal vendetta against me for no reason (talking to other students later, I found out they felt the same way)  She would shut down any comments that she didn't like. She was rude & inconsiderate. The tests are ridiculous. Save your time, don't taker her!!

Horrocks's version of 251 feels like a continuation of high school English.  Be prepared to go through a lot of printer paper-- she always requires clean copies of everything and asks you to turn in the same assignments more than once, each time costing more printing resources.
Prof. Horrocks is awesome! She was very helpful and was always respectful to students. I would take her again in a heartbeat!

Prof. Horrocks is the best! She is willing to help you out when you ask for it and cares for her students. There's lots of reading to do, and you have to write one page summaries for most, but it's beneficial for you. The exams are fair and overall this is a great class!
I thought she was brilliant! Very smart, very clear, super interesting. If you do the readings and come to class, you should do great! She is very helpful and easy to talk to during office hours.

I really enjoyed this sewing class! There was a lot of sewing, and I had a hard time getting everything done every week, but Professor Dredge was very kind and understanding. She worked with me when I had some personal things come up this semester, and was pretty quick at getting back to me when I had questions.

Professor Dredge was very easy to reach despite this being an online course. She was also very friendly and flexible with student needs. Note that SFL 287 does require a large amount of time for being a 3 credit class.

I have been sewing for years but I felt like the workload was a lot for the amount of credits that this class is worth. Jessica Dredge is really nice though and would respond to emails quickly and kindly. I think that Jessica is great but the online organization could be improved.

Professor Dredge is super nice and good at communicating which is super helpful in online classes. Her grading wasn't too harsh and she sent weekly reminder emails with an overview of the week and some encouragement.

Prof. Dredge cares so much about you!! She doesn't grade harshly and is very understanding. She has a very lenient late policy and open lab is available to online students -- going to open lab made all the difference for me!! There is however, so much hw. And, if you are not a fast sewer, then this class is going to take up all of your free time.

I learned lots of useful and fun skills. The class was enjoyable and worthwhile. Professor Dredge explains things really well in her videos. Don't expect an easy A, though. You learn a lot about sewing because there are a lot of assignments and things to learn. I lost points by being careless, so take it seriously.
This professor will push you to learn and enhance your skills, so be prepared to work hard. She is clear about expectations, and responsive to students who seek personalized help.

I did not take the beginner-level sewing class, so I was a little nervous jumping straight to the intermediate-level class, but I loved it! I learned a ton and felt like I wasn't behind for not taking the entry-level class. I think I spent 6-9 hours a week on this class (maybe because I kept having to unpick), but overall great class.

Professor Dredge is great for this course, I loved learning more about sewing. I would just say make sure to plan extra time for the weekly work because it always takes a little longer than you initially think.

She is very kind and helpful. A very wonderful professor. I had a lot of really intense things happen this semester and she was the most kind and accommodating of all of my professors. Made it so I could still pass.
Not a bad professor, I took on online class and didn't love it but that was just personal preference.

Not what I expected. While all the information is accurate, the class videos are old, hard to see/understand, and aren't the actual professor talking. Instructions for assignments are different on rubrics, in videos, and on written information throughout the course, so be careful! You might be doing it all wrong. In person would have been better.

This class is very organized, the rubrics are very clear and specific. Doing small things wrong can affect your grade a lot in the long run. Read the rubric VERY WELL before the assignments, and don't make mistakes. I loved the class, and learned SO much! I would highly recommend it.

I loved this Professor! She was always so willing to work with me to get through any issues I was having. The online class can be difficult to navigate at times but I thought that it wasn't any worse than most online classes.

This class was not easy - if you're looking to casually learn how to sew, this isn't the right class for you. A lot of concepts feel a little abstract and are difficult to navigate in an online course. Also, all of the quizzes are open book open note but are extremely hard and nitpicky and the final is closed everything and cumulative. feels silly.

Professor Dredge is so nice. She was always willing to meet with me and help me with the many questions I had. She was really good at making herself available and approachable even though it was an online class
Not a super well-designed course. But the professor and TA's are willing to help if you reach out.
Prof. Dredge was very responsive and provided help quickly when I had questions. Course was online.
Didn't interact much with the professor since it was an online class, but overall class went well.

This class is very detail oriented, which my ADHD brain did not do well with. We learned some really useful techniques that really elevate garments to look more professional, but I got really bogged down by having to document everything so clearly for an online class.

Jessica is such a caring professor! If you reach out to her she is happy to help in any way possible and answer all your questions. The class itself can be very challenging so it is a relief that the professor at least is great. Be aware that the TA's grade super harsh!

This online sewing class can seem daunting at first, but it has really clear grading rubrics, fairly clear tutorials, and reasonable requirements. If you are not familiar with sewing, you might need to put more time in than the credit hours ask of you.

This instructor is really nice and was always helpful with questions and confusion. She wasn't the fastest to respond to questions via email, but she was forgiving with deadlines if something went terribly wrong like your at home sewing machine breaking right before the assignment was due. I'd take a class from her again especially  in-person.

This was a great class! SFL 287, and in know sewing online seems like it would be way harder, but it was actually not that bad. Do not take unless you have taken the intro class, you learn important things in there that they breeze over in here, but the class overall was super fun and I love what I have made!
