I took a new course by her (COMMS 481) and she was amazing! great professor, well respected, interesting lectures, and inspiring. By going to class and participating you will succeed.

Professor Zurcher is just the best!! She's so positive and makes it clear that she wants her students to succeed. She cares deeply about what she teaches, and inspires her classes to do the same. I love the way she teaches, and the group projects were all super fun! (take this class during summer it's 10x easier!)
Dr. Zurcher was a great professor overall. Her lectures were interesting and super relevant to current events. If you do the readings and participate in class, you'll get an A.

She is fun, hilarious, and clearly knows what she's doing. I took her class from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m. on Mondays. I don't know many professors who can make me enjoy that long a lecture. However, she did. Quizzes are easy. I wish I could take this class again. She also offers a great deal of extra credit. Me and MANY others and I got over 100.

She is a great teacher! She really focuses on applying everything so most tests are essay-based but they're fairly simple. Weekly quizzes, and attendance is important because she offers no make ups for quizzes and only drops one. You definitely have to buy the textbook, but it's pretty pricey so I got it online.

I LOVE JESSICA ZURCHER! If you're thinking about this class, TAKE IT! She is the best professor I've ever had and genuinely cares about her students SO MUCH. She taught me so much and this was my favorite class of the semester. Also there were so few assignments, and no busy work because she just wanted us to learn from her instead of someone else!

One of the best professors I have had. She is very kind and helpful. Whenever you have questions don't be afraid to ask because she will help you out. She has clear expectations that she outlines at the start of the semester and in her syllabus and she will stick to them but they are by no means difficult to meet. Lectures are fun and engaging too.

One of the best COMMS professors I've had at BYU. She is fun and gives good lectures, but she also knows her stuff and is very professional. Her classes are very interesting and make you think. Some reading, but it's easy to get by if you don't get it all done. No testing center, which is awesome. I would highly recommend her as a professor.

Loved taking this class! Zurcher's lectures are interesting, and I walked away having so many things to think about. She was also very caring. Felt like I was in the right place, and this class helped me choose my major! Tests are timed essays. You also have to do an interview, and a group presentation. Homework was fairly easy!
I loved Dr Zurcher! The class was entertaining and she sometimes gives opportunities for TAs to help you get your grade up on papers. A 3 hour class was tiring, but she made it interesting.
I love her so much! Attendance is so important so I would recommend going. She gives 10 free points just to be there. Follow the rubrics and you will be fine.

Professor Zurcher was incredible. Very engaging, fair grader, genuinely cares for her students. I took the section offered once every week, so while attendance wasn't mandatory, absences set you behind. Lots of writing, which is to be expected, but the topics were interesting. A couple group projects. Take this class to become more media literate!
This professor is amazing! Take all your classes from her!

Dr. Zurcher's class was very easy if you paid attention to due dates. I felt that everything was gradely fairly amd her lectures were clear. She loves interactions through her classes which kept it from being boring. Her TAs we're very helpful and would proofread essays if you got it to them early.

Dr. Zurcher's class was well organized. There are weekly quizzes and discussion boards that are pretty easy as long as you read the textbook chapters that are assigned. The essays and interviews conducted outside of class have clear grading criteria and are easy to do well on if you put in effort.

Prof Zurcher is amazing! She ends the evening class early. Super easy assignments and tests are not hard! You have to take a quiz in class each week, but it's not hard! The papers are super fun and not as difficult as you would think. Take her if you have the chance!!

I LOVE DR. ZURCHER!!! Everyone that has the opportunity to take her class definitely should. She is very knowledgeable about the subject and her lectures are incredibly engaging. I was nervous to take a 3 hour class but it ended up being my absolute favorite, she makes it even better then a one hour class. Could not give a higher recommendation!

For an evening class, Pro. Zurcher made it pretty manageable. She would often let us leave early! The workload isn't very heavy and tests are written exams and TAs grade very fairly. In class there is a lot of group discussion/participation. She grades attendance through weekly quizzes in class. She's a very nice person!

SHE IS THE BEST! Great teacher and creates FUN, clear and concise lectures. Easy projects/HW. As long as you know key points you'll get A's on tests. She provides a FREE TEXTBOOK. Class time is provided for HW and group projects. You won't regret taking her classes.

I took this class online, but professor Zurcher was very kind to get to know all her students. She recorded lecture videos and it made it so much easier to understand the material. If you had questions, she responded very quickly and you could always visit her on campus during her office hours.I highly recommend taking this class from her!!

okay, so I don't really have much to say about Dr. Zurcher since it was an online class and I never even interacted with her, but the TA in her class was really disorganized. No one in the class ever knew when things were due, I lost points for turning in late assignments when it said they weren't due for 2 more days. Super frustrating class.

Dr. Zurcher made 3 hours feel like 1. Lectures/discussions were fun. I always looked forward to the class though rarely looked forward to the homework. I did about 3 hours per week on average. I thought the material was really hard for me to get my head around but lots of study and hard work paid off. Participate, participate, participate.

My comms 101 class was a 3 hour Monday night lecture, and yet it was my favorite class. Prof. Zurcher is one of the most caring people I have ever met and she is one of the few professors I have had that has made it a priority to make sure you apply the class material to your life. Take comms 101 from her, you won't regret it.
Great class. Super easy. Midterms and Finals are easy As. Even if you arent sure you want to go into comms, this class is great.

Even though I took this course as a three hour class once a week, I always looked forward to it. Professor Zurcher is the best lecturer I've seen at BYU. The exams are timed essays, but you get used to them. There is reading for the course, but not too much. Only downside were my TAs.

I have NOT had good experiences with Dr. Z. I got a 0/100 on an exam 2mo ago bc of a Canvas issue. It still hasn't been resolved, largely bc of her lack of communication (ironic). She's implying that I am at fault & does not seem to advocate for her students. If you're looking for an understanding, interpersonal prof, do not take classes from her.

Professor Zurcher was a doll! She is an absolute sweetheart, yet very professional and legitimate about making us learn communications. She stayed after at the end of all her online lectures to answer personal questions we had and was happy to help when possible. The class was discussion and papers based, which should be expected from a comms class

She is awesome! I took comms 101 online and it was the best online class. Very accessible for questions, super easy to follow and the tests are essays which is a way better way to show what you learned. there is a group project at the end but it was the easiest thing ever. She isn't a strict grader, she just wants to see what you have learned:)

Although this class was very informative, there was a lot of reading and a lot of lecture videos to watch. Even though this class took a lot of time, Professor Zurcher is a really cool person and you can tell that she loves what she teaches. She knows how to communicate well and her lecture videos were produced very nicely.

Professor Zurcher is awesome. I took this class online and everything was laid out and clear on canvas. It is a lot of reading, but you can find Quizlet flashcards that break down everything the readings cover. As long as you do the assignments and apply yourself in the least you will find yourself inspired and with an easy A.

Maybe it was just me but this was the easiest class I have ever taken. There is a number of somewhat large assignments, but they are easy, and the exams (at least for us) were open book essay questions. Gives you the perfect view of the Comms school without being excessively difficult. If you have any interest in comms, take this class, easy A

There were things I liked and things I didn't. It was a pretty easy class and very big-picture oriented. Final exams were just essay questions. I took the on-demand class and she would just add extra live class sessions in the middle of random days, which was super frustrating and attendance was mandatory despite it never being mentioned earlier.
Professor Zurcher makes class fun and the assignments interesting, I learned so much from this class.

Dr. Zurcher is the best! She is lively, entertaining, and makes her lectures engaging and intriguing. There were minimal assignments that were useful, well explained, and graded fairly. All tests were short essays including vocab terms from the class which was super manageable.
I would highly recommend taking COMMS 101 with Professor Zurcher! I learned a lot from this class and the assignments were always thoroughly explained and the lectures were always interesting!
Dr. Zurcher was a fun professor with an easy class. The reading quizzes were super easy, and the tests (I think there were 3) are quite doable.
She does a great job teaching this class and making it interesting. If you get the opportunity to take a class from her I would 100% do it.

I took this online but there was a webinar every Monday. You will likely talk to the TAs more than the professor, but the TAs were awesome so I didnt mind! Theres a lot of assignments but none of them are brutal. Each test is a short essay format and you just need to write well and include/define vocab terms. No multiple choice type tests yay!

Worst class I have ever taken at BYU. I'm on scholarship at BYU but literally felt like I lost money by taking this class. The material is just common sense stuff with terms that you have to memorize. Never read the textbook and just crammed for 45 minutes before each midterm/final. I got 100% on the midterm and 99% on the final doing that.

DR. ZURCHER IS THE BEST!!!! The TAs are all awesome too! I took this class to see if I want to major in comms, and this class proved it is really fun (although I still might go into something else). She made sure we understood the different fields within comms. It's not an "easy A," but as long as you try, you can get one! Such a fun class!

Prof Zurcher is a nice person and I liked her! But the class was pretty mediocre. Three exams and they are written essay questions, which is really annoying and difficult. Also a group final project. Most assignments felt like busy work and the webinars were super long. Overall, not too bad, but felt like a lot of work for an intro class.

Dr. Zurcher was AMAZING! Even though the class was fully online, she did a great job of hosting amazing lectures and really making this class feel like it was taught in person. The layout on Canvas was very clear making it easy to tell what was due and when. The TA's were also so great if you have questions they are very helpful- go to the reviews.

Dr Zurcher definitely passed the vibe check. She is kind, passionate, uplifting and organized. The class in itself feels like it has a bit too much busy work and doesn't feel very personal because there are sooo many students. Don't take online if you can help it.

I loved this class because of her! She gave one lecture a week that you could watch on your own time! There was an attendance quiz for that and than a reading quiz everyweek, both were open note hwoever! All her exams are written with no multiple choice so If you like that than this class is perfect for you!

Dr. Zurcher is a good person, but not so much teacher. Her class is concept-based, meaning the material is entirely ambiguous and indirect. It's common sense stuff yet she tries to make it complex where it doesn't need to be. I'm frustrated by her lack of specificity. Perhaps that's part of the nature of the course, but I feel she could do better.

Take Comms101 from Dr. Zurcher. She is fair, assignments have meaning, and a good grade is very attainable. She does a fantastic job mixing in what we learn with the gospel. Its a very helpful class to get a grip on what the School of Comms is all about. Tests are essays only, but she prepares you well and they account for only 30% of your grade.

I LOVE Professor Zurcher! Her lectures are inspirational and exciting and always tie back to the gospel. She always talks about application and how we can actually use communications principles in our lives. Her tests and projects are super easy, you just have to go to TA reviews and participate. Seriously, so easy and so beneficial!! Love her!

I loved this online course. I spent about 1.5 hours watching the weekly lectures and 2 hours reading the textbook and taking the online quiz. There are about 3 papers and 1 group project. The TAs are super helpful and give online and in-person test reviews. The tests are writing 2 essays. Do all the assignments and you will get an A.

Dr. Zurcher is AMAZING! I absolutely love her teaching style. She uses the majority of class time to facilitate discussions that help you think about and apply important concepts. She never gives a homework assignment unless there is a significant real-life application to be learned. Tests were very fair and the end-of-semester project is so fun!

Professor Zurcher is amazing! She really cares about her students succeeding. I have never met someone so passionate about their topic of study. You will learn things that will help in you in your career and life in general. Take your comms elective class from her!

Jessica is one of the best professors I've had here at BYU. Her lectures are organized and the projects actually serve a purpose rather than just being busy work. Her grading is also extremely fair and as long as you show up to class and put a decent amount of effort into your homework you'll be fine.

Of all the online classes I've taken at BYU this one was the most organized and intriguing. There were always videos to watch that were like mini lecutres from Dr. Zurcher. There was quite a bit of work to do but I could usually complete all of it in 2-3 hours each week. There were weekly discussion boards and a reading quiz but overall great class

I would 100% recommend taking a class from Dr. Zurcher! She cares so much about her students and will really help you to succeed in her class. Her tests are pretty straightforward and as long as you put in clear effort, you will get an A.

Professor Zurcher is the kindest and most Christlike person I know. She wants what is best for her students and her lectures are always very engaging. There was a decent amount of assignments/papers, but they were all worthwhile. I'm not going into communications, but this class is applicable for absolutely everything and everyone! TAKE FROM HER!

Professor Zurcher is very passionate about communications and really helps convey that to her students. I learned so much in this class and will most likely go into comms because of it. Even if you're not going into comms it's a really interesting class. She really cares about her students and does a good job of incorporating the Gospel.

Sister Zurcher and her class were fantastic. Learned a ton about the communications field. I love how every aspect of what we learned was taught through applications to truly make sure the students understood. Would love to take another class from her.

Take this teacher! She's so sweet and answers her emails quickly. She does a great job preparing you while keeping things interesting and interactive. I took it online and it was paced really well. We watched clips from the Office and analyzed them as an assignment for example. It's a fun and relevant class. Beware of the heavier reading/notes.
Great teacher but I struggled with her tests. Make sure you read the book and know the vocabulary very well!

My favorite class from this past semester. Professor Zurcher gives amazing lectures and is clearly passionate about communications, teaching, and the gospel. If you want to see what a BYU education is this is the class to be in.

Dr. Zurcher is a wonderful teacher! She always relates everything we talk about back to the gospel. We didn't take normal tests, we were given 3 prompts and had to choose 2 to answer. Not hard at all. We did a lot of fun projects. It's been really enjoyable and not too hard, but I have definitely learned a lot.

Dr. Zurcher is absolutely wonderful. Her lectures are entertaining and relevant, and she really takes into consideration her students' wants and needs. She's constantly taking feedback and applying the course to real-life problems and concepts. And it's not a hard class, either! I definitely reccomend

Dr. Zurcher is the best professor I have ever had! She genuinely cares about her students. If you put in the effort, you can't NOT get a good grade in the class. She learns her students by name and works with each student individually to ensure their success. Light hw, three manageable essay exams, lots of application. Take this class!

I'm not a Comms major, but now I want to be. Dr. Zurcher is Fantastic! Her passion for the subject and care for her student's success in it is so evident. She teaches for understanding and everyday application. You work for the grade, but she is down to earth, flexible, and willing to work with anyone who is willing to communicate with her. BEST.

Truly an amazing teacher who cares not only about your success but also about you as a person. Doesn't give out any busy work and although the class is writing heavy the work is enjoyable as it usually allows you to explore your interests in the comms field. It was my most spiritually uplifting class this semester, even compared to religion classes.

amazing engaging teacher. every day her lectures are different. tests are 2 papers & you have to include 5 vocab words in each (30points). 5 question quiz every class; sometimes group quizzes based off of reading. 5 point homework questions every week. a couple papers. 1 group project. 1 interview project. prepare to write. worth it.

Professor Zurcher was such a fun teacher for this class. The lectures and content were enjoyable and tests were fairly easy because they were in class and short essay responses. If you put in the basic needed work, you will pass easy.

Dr. Zurcher is amazing. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER! She gives you homework that matters. No busy work. She is also very spiritual and very inspirational. She is a total gem. Love her!!!! Not too hard of a grader. Really wants to make sure you understand the material. Cares for you as a person, as well as a student. TAKE IT!

She is a great choice for this class! She is very engaging and she'll get you excited about communications. The class was wayyy easy. Just skim the readings, show up to class, do half decent on the papers and you'll get an A. My only warning is that because it's so easy, it's easy to let things slip. Late worked gets docked so turn it in on time.

Dr. Zurcher is a phenomenal teacher.  Her lessons really help you understand communication on a deeper level. She is very caring and energetic and keeps class very entertaining. I wish I could take more classes from her in the future!

Here is my advice to save your souls before this class starts. There are instructions on how to do all the projects early, so get them done early because if you type slowly you are going to be spending some time getting the papers/project done. Besides that, super easy. NO TESTING CENTER. Easy tests. Tons of extra credit.

Sister Zurcher is the best professor I've had at BYU! Her class was upbeat, positive, and you learned a lot. She really really cares about her students and you can tell by the way she talks to each student. She doesn't try and fail you- but she wants you to do your best. IF YOU HAVE A CHANCE TO TAKE A CLASS FROM HER- DO IT. You will not regret it!

Dr. Zurcher is one of the most inspiring teachers/professors I've ever had.  She holds an authentic enthusiasm for the field of communications that is absolutely infectious. Going into communications?  Take her class!! Not going into communications?  Take her class!!

Dr. Zurcher is a great professor! She's really nice, makes lectures interesting, and discusses lots of spiritual applications. There's a quiz every class period. She constantly had us doing assignments outside of class that were not really difficult, just time consuming. Overall, an easy class, just too much busy work in my opinion.

Professor Zurcher is a passionate professor who knows what she's doing. I definitely enjoyed her class. There are quizzes every day, so don't expect to skip class! Overall it is a very manageable class.

Professor Zurcher made a potentially boring class into something interesting. We I took it class was 2 1/2 hours long but she usually let us out early and it never dragged on. She is enthusiastic and if you participate, it is an easy class. She makes sure everyone learns and enjoys communications. I recommend her completely.

I really enjoyed this class but it was 2 1/2 hours which got long at times. There were only a few times where we actually went the full time but just be aware of that. I loved her insights and real-life applications. Jessica definitely has a gift when it comes to teaching! I would definitely take it again!

This was one of the easiest classes I've taken at  BYU! There are quizzes in class and assignments, 3 tests (no cumulitive final) that are writing 2 essays (super easy!) Professor Zurcher is enthusiastic. inspiring, and super kind. Take this class from her!

She's an amazing lady. I never enjoyed an evening class so much. Though she still expected good work and a decent amount of effort, it was obvious she cared so much more about our understanding and application of the information than about our grades. She really wanted me to do well. We did a decent amount of group work, but the tests were easy.

Favorite class I've taken at BYU so far. Zurcher has a passion for the subject that is infectious, and she expects you to think but the work load isn't bad. Reading quiz daily, a few video analysis papers, and a media journal were the main assignments. This professor incorporated the gospel tons, it was inspiring to hear her testimony daily.
Really entertaining and intriguing. Cares more about the experience than about the grade (But wants everyone to pass). Not too hard, but takes constant effort. Tests are easy and taken in class.

Prof. Zurcher is the best! I took her during the Fall 2015 semester. She was a new professor at the time but she is very keen in helping everyone. She wants everyone to learn something from the class. She empowers you and teaches really well! She promotes group discussion and her tests are pretty easy. Being able to apply the concepts is key!

Take chem 106 from Jessie! She is super accessible outside of class and offers extra office hours you can sign up for to meet with her 1:1. She also has a few extra credit opportunities and the tests are very similar to the mock exam! Just make sure you go to the lecture and stay on top of the class

Jessie is the best professor. Coming from 105 super discouraged and not really loving chemistry, or school I was not excited for this class. This class made me excited about learning and chemistry again. Jessie is so kind and really cares about her students. She is very accommodating and wants you to do well. 100% worth the train up to slc

Jessie's a very good professor - I took it at the salt lake center and it wasn't too hard. The class is designed with a lot of reading, because you only meet for 2 hours once a week. The tests were a little difficult, but the homework was all useful. Also Jessie is just so nice- probably the nicest professor I've ever had

I took Chem 105 last Winter and was surprised to do well in a class dreaded by so many freshmen. Jessie helped me to apply myself to her class, and I found myself more dedicated to this class than any other I have taken so far in college. She is such a caring and helpful professor!

Jessie is a super caring and nice teacher. Super accessible and will help you anytime you need it. She teaches things well and knows her stuff. However, I would say because she wants to help everyone, the class sometimes gets behind with the material. Or there are long periods of time in class with some of us doing nothing.

Jessie is such a great professor! She is super caring & truly just wants you to succeed. Although Chem 106 isn't the easiest class, tests were straightforward, homework assignments were easy, & she explained concepts very well! She gives a few extra credit opportunities & zoom tutoring hours twice a week. Take Chem 106 from Jessie!!

Jessie is easily the best teacher I have had at BYU. She is very accessible outside of class (answers emails at midnight sometimes) and is very invested in everyone doing well. Definitely take CHEM 106 from her.

One of my worst experiences and professors at BYU! She often went to class and said that she had to leave or wouldn't come for weeks to hang out with friends come from far places. She clearly didn't want to or care to be in class! She is smart, but her lecture is super rushed, and I totally even gave up on the class and attending it.

Dr. Wang did not really teach me any statistics. Her lectures are very scattered and very hard to understand. Luckily, all the tests and quizzes were open-AI, and we were supposed to use coding software, which she never taught us how to do. Super easy class, but feels like a waste of time.

Professor Wang will make sure that hard-working students receive the grade they deserve. Tips for an A in her class: - Attend classes in person   - Write detailed notes in R Studio with example R code from lecture  - Frequent the TA lab

She is kind, but she doesn't explain things well. Going to her lectures IS a waste of time. You are much better off just using her slides and going to TAs or looking things up on youtube. Dr. Wang does use R studio which is a pretty difficult software and she has tests in testing center. Other professors make it much easier.

I like Dr. Wang as a person and her humor, but I have beef with the midterms/final. I got an A, but the final literally had questions on things NEVER covered in class or homework. Most likely just took a final from another stats professor without screening through it. I rarely attended class and just taught myself from the slides.

I ended up teaching most of the class to my self because lectures were not very helpful and it was super hard to follow along sometimes. She is sometimes hard to understand and I felt like there were a lot of times she would go on a tangent when we really needed to cover the material in class. Be prepared to teach yourself.

The kindest person, but just not a great teacher. Difficult to understand, and doesn't explain concepts clearly. If you took AP stats in high school, the class will be a breeze. Each exam has a testing center portion an online portion with no time cap and each homework gets two attempts. She is willing to answer hw qs during class time if you ask

She can't speak English and she is almost impossible to follow.    

If you take this class you need to teach yourself in the Stat's Lab in the WVB.   Her lectures are a waste of time and are a discrace to the mission of BYU.

Professor Wang is an amazing statistician but struggles to clearly teach principles of statistics. She relies heavily on the sample problems in the textbook but struggles to teach the principles necessary, instead often rambling.
Homeworks were completion and exams were open for a long time. Get help, and you'll be fine.

The lectures felt like a waste of time. It feels like I was just teaching myself stats with the slides and outside resources which was quite annoying because the learning doesn't feel near as deep. She's very kind and caring though!

I took this during spring term. I can't speak for the people taking it during a normal semester, but I'd recommend that you take it during the fall or winter semesters. We were rushed as a class, and she had content on our midterms and finals that we never got to cover. She is a very nice professor though, and is very willing to explain concepts.

I took stats 511 after taking 201 from professor wang. The difference between the 2 classes is 511 has a lot less homework. We had 1 assignment per week. Took about 2-3 hours max to do with the help of a TA. The other difference is neither the lectures slides by Dr. Wang, nor the lectures were very helpful. The downside is it's not organized well.

A lot of people don't go to her lectures, but that's because her slides are so good. I started going to lecture about a month before the end of the semester for code help, and her lectures were super helpful because she had noticed where we needed help and was actively working to get us fluent before the exam. She cares and she's competent.

Now, professor Wang is admittedly not the clearest when teaching, but I absolutely love her lectures. I think the key thing about her class is that you do the textbook pre-readings or at least skim them. Their not graded, but they are important to understanding. Her teaching is not for everybody, but if you put in the time, she is absolutely great!

Honestly not a bad class, but if you haven't taken Stats before it might be a little difficult. I pretty much just ended up teaching myself all of the content by doing the homework and looking at the slides but not going to lecture because I didn't get anything out of it. Tests aren't too bad, she gives extra credit and puts practice tests online.
Prof. Wang is super sweet and caring, but her lectures can be hard to follow. I just looked over the lecture slides and did the homework. Go to the TA reviews, and do the extra credit!

Lectures are not good because she doesn't know how to explain the material well. Her lecture slides and TA's make the class doable. There's technically 6 exams for the class, including finals. She has 3 quizes but they're 2.5 hrs and around 40 questions each one, so they're really exams. The hw is doable, but not easy, TA's will carry you.

Her lectures are mostly reading off slides. You'll have to teach yourself stats to pass and do well. Don't recommend attending class. Watch out for the tests & quizzes they are weighted very heavily in the class and doing poorly on them will kill your grade. The TAs are great I recommend going to OH and going to midterm review sessions.

Super nice lady. Awful teacher. It is hard to understand her and class is just reading off the slides. The TAs were ok but it seemed like some just wanted to get their own homework done, not help students. There was 7% extra credit this semester, so getting an A isn't too bad, but good luck figuring out what the heck is going on in statistics.

Even if you do every homework. If you do poorly on one test or quiz, your entire grade goes down. Homework is only 20% of your grade. So tests and quizzes are EIGHTY PERCENT?? Crazy. Also, she just reads her slides in class so there is no point in going.
Attending class is pointless. She just reads the lecture slides but doesnt really explain much of what is going on. The way to pass this class is YouTube and skimming her slides
The course was scattered and due dates were fluid. The course wasn't too hard as grading was easy, but did not learn much of anything from the content.

Dr. Wang will give you all the material you need to be successful. Lecture slides and her R materials are enough. If you can do the homework quizzes and practice exams, you will be successful on the real exams.
That being said, if you thrive in an environment where the learning is mostly done in the lecture hall, consider taking another professor.

I really really wanted to like Professor Wang's class, but I just couldn't. She's a really nice person, but her teaching style isn't for me. I stopped coming to class after the first week because she just read the slides verbatim. Tests/quizzes are weighted ridiculously high, so doing well on HW doesn't really matter. She is really nice though.

Prof Wang does literally everything she can to help you succeed. She gave us unlimited tries on our homework outside of class & she tells you what is important for tests. She’s not hard to understand even with the accent, & she goes over things without going too fast. She even went over homework with us many times. I would recommend!
It is hard to understand this professor. Her accent makes it hard to listen. You should expect to read tons and watch videos outside of class in order to understand the material.

I found it extremely difficult to pay attention in her lectures, which isn't something I usually have an issue with. She's funny, but it sometimes makes her explanations confusing. The textbook that's required for this class was rarely helpful for the homework assignments and tests. Most of your grade (80% of it, in fact) is based on test scores.

Exams make up 80% and her practice tests are a lot easier than the actual tests. The TAs are the only reason I passed this class, her lectures just ramble on and don't teach you the needed material most of the time. The only saving grace is that you can review the midterm with her and she'll give you points back for some things.

I quickly discovered lectures were of no value and the only useful part of class were the shared slides for the department that she posted in LS. I went to class, copied the slides, and played on my phone for the other 30 min of class and did just fine on hw and tests. Relatively easy class but completely incompetent professor.

Professor Wang has been one of my worst professors here at BYU. There is definitely a language barrier here, and her lectures are often scatterbrained and (for me) made concepts more confusing rather than clarifying. She also refused to curve grades even while more than half the class had failing grades.
She is not a good teacher and just reads off slides. She is a kind person but not a good teacher. Get ready to study and learn 100% outside of class.

I learned absolutely nothing from going to class. I just asked the TAs lots of questions and figured stuff out on my own. The first half of the semester gets tougher. She talks so fast and just reads ppt slides during lectures. Not helpful. Most of the learning is on your own. I would definitely take if from someone else if you can.

She's a great option for this class. She makes it really easy for her students to know exactly what she wants them to know. I didn't go to class the entire semester, and still aced the final. She has TA's who are always there to help, and she'll even meet with you outside of class if you want. Her lectures are scatterbrained however.

Professor Wang would just blabber on aimlessly during her lectures so much so that I actually found it easier to learn by looking at her lecture slides and doing the homework rather than attending class. I didn't learn a single thing during lecture. A bomb of an exam hit the class the last week of school and the average was a 50%.... No curve.

She is a great person but I had a hard time following her lectures. The key is: talk to her outside of class. She went through the R quizzes and tests and even gave back points for things. She cares that you learn it and if you use her office hours she loves the effort! She really loves her students and the material.

I love Jie Wang, alright? I love her. She has made me laugh harder than any other professor. But I can't recommend her class! I've never skipped ANY other class's lectures, but she is SO bad at explaining stats, and what she teaches in class is SO disconnected from what we end up being graded on, that I stopped going after a month and a half.

Dr. Wang is a really kind professor and teaches simply. The R quizzes were new this semester and the final R quiz's difficulty was a bit unexpected for all of us. However, she covered all the concepts and code in class necessary to do pretty well on the quizzes and tests. I do think that the R quizzes were a bit unnecessary and weighted too high.

I agree with most of the negative comments. She knows the material extremely well, but does not how to effectively teach it. I am a computer engineering major and I struggled with the R code as she give proper examples. If you have this professor, be ready to teach yourself the content.

Class isnt hard, she makes it hard because she doesnt teach. She reads from her lectures that only have 20% of the skills and knowledge you need to get an A on her tests and quizzes. There's no point in attending her lectures or going to her for help because she will just ramble about something irrelevant to your question. Worst Prof Ive ever had.

I took AP stats and stat 121 so the material was familiar, BUT Dr. Wang does not teach. You're better off studying the posted slides than to attend lecture. 40% of your grade are the R quizzes and she does NOT teach R in an effective way making those quizzes very difficult to pass. The tests are nothing like the homework. Find a different professor

She's honestly so nice and accommodating, and she will do anything to help you. Drops 2 homeworks, and exams are weighted a lot, but you get a cheat sheet. Of course the class is very difficult regardless of the professor, but I would recommend her.

First, Dr. Wang is a nice person. However, she is not a good teacher. Her lectures are very confusing and very difficult to understand. The homework is not representative of the tests. Lectures don't really prepare you for the HW. There are no practice tests or study guides which can be frustrating at times. Make sure to attend the TA reviews.

Okay so heres the thing. She is easily the worst stats professor at BYU. I didn't understand a single thing from any of her lectures, some of it is due to her heavy accent. . HW has nothing to do with the tests, with Ta review tests aren't that bad. this is the hardest core class for stats majors so either read the book or take it from Tolley

I couldn't understand what she was saying half of the time. She was really spacey when it came to lectures. Also at the beginning of the semester she would just skip through slides and say ," you know all these things right?"
Very difficult homework and tests.

I took AP Stat, and this class was just not very difficult. I went to class maybe half a dozen times; it really wasn't worth it. The online HW was reasonable and was good for testing your understanding of material. 2 submission attempts without penalty made it easy to not lose many points.

Professor Wang does her best. She is also kind to talk to students in office hours. However, she doesnt teach! She reads the slides and even told us the first day of class not to come to the lectures. SHE READS the slides. Homework was straight forward and doable. But the Tests and online tests were much much harder! BEWARE. R commander is a joke!

I went to the first few lectures, but soon found I good glance over the lecture slides and examples and do the homework with little difficulty. I went to a total of about 5 lectures the whole semester. I wish I'd gone to lecture for like 1 or 2 of chapters but I was fine. Tests were reasonable, but not my favorite format.

Dr. Wang is a very nice person, but she is not a good teacher at all. When she writes on the board, she jumps around so it is very hard to follow. She is also constantly canceling office hours. Avoid if you can, one of the worst professors I have ever had as far as being able to teach the material.

She's a good teacher, that knows her stuff. She didn't care if we came to class or not, so a lot of times I didn't. She posted all her materials online, so it was easy to do the homework without going to class. She was good at responding to emails and helping students.

I really liked Dr Wang. She was funny and I feel like I actually learned quite a bit in her class. She wasn't always the easiest to follow during her lectures, but she had a great TA to help and was always accessible in office hours. Her tests were easy if you studied, so getting an A wasn't a problem.

85% exam 15% homework online homework every day of class half the exams are online computing exams (27%) all the lecture slides are public so don't worry if you miss class Prof Wang is funny and understanding about glitches in Learning Suite. Not the greatest explainer due to language barrier. One on one during office hours (wait in line).

She definitely tried to make the class enjoyable and generously curved the test scores. She also allows you to bring a full page of notes for the tests. However, she's really disorganized and lectures are incomprehensible. Class average was an A- whereas the class average for Dr Tolley's class was a D.

She knows her stuff, but is hard to understand in class. She's an ok option for this class. The most useful thing was to go to her office hours because she really understands statistics and can explain it super well one on one.

Shes quite hard to understand and she just reads her powerpoint slides the whole class. Honestly i quit attending because it was not a good use of time. If there is somebody else out there to take this class from you should do it.

She's from China and it's actually pretty hard to understand her lectures because of her accent. I learned from the textbook. She makes really easy tests though and is very helpful if you come to her office hours or after class. Very nice lady.

This class centers more on homework assignments (due each period) over tests. The tests were surprisingly easy, especially because we were allowed a note sheet and the final was open book! That being said, Dr. Wang is probably not the clearest teacher.

Really loved taking this class from her. Lots of theory stuff that's native to the course, but she covers it really well. She says a lot "I hate math/proofs," so she doesn't focus on that stuff as much. She lets you bring a page of notes to her tests which was way nice. Really approachable too!

Her class was super easy! Her homework are due once a week and usually take less than an hour to do. If you are stuck on a problem, you can ask her and she will do them in class. She lets you take a whole 8.5 x 11 sheet of paper in to the testing center for notes. And her exams are 7 problems choose to do 5 of them. Super easy!! Super chill!

"J" as she'll have you call her, is a really sweet Chinese lady who kind of struggles with her English sometimes. Doesn't always teach things in the clearest manner, but she throws you a bone on the exams (you can bring in a 8x11 note paper) so you won't do terribly. If you get TA help and make a good cheat sheet, you'll do fine despite her English

Skipping class is possible, but if you want an A you need to be going. The textbook isn't clear and her lecture slides don't do well on their own. When I needed to improve my grade, she was willing to work with me and loved helping me understand the material. She doesn't prepare you well for the exams (since the other professor writes them).

Jie is a really nice person but I found her lectures difficult to follow and the tests were hard for me. When I talked to her outside of class she was very helpful but in general I thought that her class was more difficult than the other sections and our overall scores were usually lower.

Dr. Wang was one one of my favorite professors. She organized her slides logically, and made it clear what was important and what was not. Her choice in TAs were good, although they took forever to grade homework. She was available outside of class time as well, and was very good about explaining concepts to me. Get the book used.
Such a nice person. Very helpful when you have questions. Very lenient. As said below, she has great lecture notes!
Professor Wang is great. Her lectures are a bit confusing, but are all posted online and clear when you go through them by yourself. She is also very helpful after class and with office hours.

This was one of the best organized classes I've ever taken. Jie gave us a study guide at the beginning of the semester that summarizes every topic to be covered in the class, and she followed that study guide in her lectures. That made it really easy to follow along, take notes, and remember and study the information later for the tests.

RUN! Very difficult to understand and lots of proofs. Not clear on homework or tests in expectations. How she phrases the test questions you aren't sure what she is asking for. She does a lot of theoretical ideas but no real life applications.

Professor Wang is incredibly knowledgeable about statistics. This is an upper level class so obviously the material is challenging. Having said that the tests are not too hard and she curves them. The homework makes up a large part of your grade so do all it and you can easily pull out at least a B.

She's chill, but hard to understand and her lectures weren't clear  and were long. I only went to class because she would randomly do attendance checks and if you were there, you didn't have to do the hw. She does give a 2% extra credit to your final grade for doing ratings though. And there is a big group project worth about 25% of your grade

Yes, she is Asian and hard to understand.  Yes, the tests are obnoxious (though they are similar to the study guides).  But she gave 2% to our final grade for attendance and another 2% for doing the teacher review, that bumped me up from a 83% to a 87%.  Would I take another class from her? No.

She's a really nice lady, but it's hard to understand her. She has an accent and her lectures are really boring. I only went to lecture for the iclicker extra credit. The grading criteria is the same for all stat121 classes. TA's taught me everything. She did go out of her way once to change the assignment due dates for the evening classes.

She's impossible to understand. I'm sure she can explain it all fine in Chinese but not so much in English. Tests are departmental, but the study guides do pretty well. She gave 2% extra credit for coming to class. There is a group project that if you don't do, you fail. It's a hard class, you have to keep up and be prepared to google a lot.

This class felt scattered; there were assignments we never talked about, and then random assignments that would never be graded and then be taken off everyone's grade because she forgot them. I think she's very knowledgeable; she's involved in a lot of cool things, so a good lady to know!

I cannot say enough good things about Jill. She is a real mentor and friend. You will learn so much about the social impact cycle through this course that will help you solve problems throughout life. Take it.

I love Jill! The textbook for Do Good Better was more of a workbook/notebook and we used it a lot. (It wasn't expensive.) Amazing class, amazing teacher, 10/10!
I took it when my mental health was trashed, but even so, the class wasn't overwhelming. And Jill was super caring, even though I never told her what was going on outside the classroom.

Jill has lots of experience in social impact. The class was very unorganized and whatever was in the gradebook usually wasn't right. We worked with our internship ID to figure out due dates and assignments because Jill was very confusing. Lectures weren't helpful and assignments were mostly busy work. Internship was a great experience though!

I'm the biggest Jill fan there is. I took her Do Good Better class last year and did the SIPS internship this year. She is hilarious, isn't afraid to joke around, is forgiving on assignments and lets you resubmit to get better scores. Overall just cares about your success as a student and I LOVE HER.

Jill is Great! She cares about her students and she makes sure her class isnt stressful or overly tricky for the students plus she adapts the course to fit everyone's needs. If you take Do Good Better, take it from Jill! the issue brief is kind of hard but the late policy is great, I turned literally all my papers in really late but still got an A!
Amazing class, amazing professor!! Would recommend to anyone who has the time for an on-campus internship.
Jill was one of the best most inspiring professors I've had at BYU!

Jill is hilarious! She is really good at making lectures entertaining which is an undervalued skill in most university professors. Sometimes she can be a little disorganized or unclear, but she is really willing to talk outside of class and actually cares about her students. Any class she teaches is going to be good.
She is a fantastic and caring professor. She gives amazing feedback to your team that leaves you feeling inspired. Highly recommend her and this course!

SIP is the best! Jill isn't your main contact, but she does try to make lectures fun. If you're interested in the how of social impact, I recommend taking Do Good. Better. That said, SIP was the best thing I did last year. I LOVED my team and LOVED my project!

SIP Projects was one of the best experiences I've had at BYU these past 3 years. Jill made the online class feel like a community and seemed to see the value in everyone, a real multiplier leader. The class part of this on-campus internship was challenging because you work in groups and depend on the work of others, but teamwork's the point. Do it!

Jill is amazing! SIP is the best class I've taken at BYU hands down. There are no tests, and amazing lectures. SIP gave me an opportunity to be hands on about things that I learned. I also felt like I was really making a difference while I was in this class. Jill is super funny and helpful. She really wants her students to succeed.
Jill is so enthusiastic and eager to help students succeed. She's a lot of fun and often brings treats. SIP is an incredible experience for an internship that makes a difference.

This class felt scattered; there were assignments we never talked about, and then random assignments that would never be graded and then be taken off everyone's grade because she forgot them. I think she's very knowledgeable; she's involved in a lot of cool things, so a good lady to know!

I cannot say enough good things about Jill. She is a real mentor and friend. You will learn so much about the social impact cycle through this course that will help you solve problems throughout life. Take it.

I have loved Professor Winters so much. This class was so interesting. It's a hard class, don't get me wrong, but it's worth it if you choose to engage yourself. Read the textbook, I promise it's not bad.  Winters is so knowledgeable, talented and the best professor I've had yet. The other ratings here don't do her justice one bit. Highly recommend

Don't take this class from professor winters if you're just trying to get easy generals. Docks points for wording even if the idea of your answer is right. The lectures were maybe ⅓ about music history and the rest about general history that wasn't interesting. Tests on insanely specific, unimportant details. Lots of extra credit opportunities tho.

Utterly horrid experience. Answers often marked wrong even if correct and/or verbatim from the slides. Attendance not taken, but SO MUCH info given in lecture and slides barely covered any. At finals she forgot to grade assignment worth 10% of final grade, leading to a lower grade. Fixed later once I emailed her. Unnecessarily difficult for a 101.

4 hard & long online tests, each with an essay and music listening test. Each week had a long reading quiz that was online. Have to attend 3 concerts and write a paper on it. You do a presentation on a composer that you upload to YouTube. Lot of info you need to memorize. The lectures were long, but ok. Did not feel like a 101 level class

Professor Winters made the class so unnecessarily difficult and gave so much busy work. Each midterm/final was comprised of three separate exams that took hours to do. SO MUCH busy work for a 101! So much content and slides didn't cover all of it. Requires "copious notes" by hand, laptops not allowed. Extra credit offered, but abhorred the class.

She has 3 exams and a final all cumulative each 3 parts, so studying and testing took hours, and only got longer each test. She goes over a needless amount of material too quickly. Lots of homework and she's a very harsh grader (marks things wrong even if copied them the slides). The one redeeming quality is there is lots of extra credit.

Professor Winters is very passionate about her class and the music which is great but goes over way too much too fast and almost expects you to know everything from the jump. She also does not like students using laptops for notes but notes are NEEDED to pass the class. A lot of homework and a harsh grader and harsh criticism.

Good class overall, Prof Winters is very knowledgeable and experienced in the music world - very interesting and insightful lectures. There is a lot of homework though, and the midterms/final are ridiculously difficult. Get ready to memorize a lot. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit, it you do them it's easy to get an A in the class.

This class was awesome and very educational. fun subject with a teacher who knows her stuff. There is a lot of homework and it's harshly graded. exams are detailed and difficult. however, there is TONS of extra credit, so getting a good grade shouldn't be an issue if you just put in the time to do it all.

Professor Winters is one of the most caring teachers! Yes there are a lot of long quizzes but she sets them up so that you will do better on tests. She gives a lot of extra credit and really works with her students to make sure that you do well. Lectures are very interesting, she is really passionate about what she teaches.

Too much homework. Every week there is a quiz of 30-50 questions which require you to search hard and long for the answers in the book and lecture notes. Tests are even longer, around 100 questions. She is professional and kind, but it is nearly impossible to get A's on assignments. However there are lots of extra credit opportunities.

Brau is the reason I majored in finance and the reason I left for a mission when I did! Extremely inspiring. I went on to TA for him. To do well: attend each class and TAKE GOOD NOTES, memorize all those notes for the test, and do the drill problems. His tests are tough, but if you make sure to do those things, you'll get a good grade.
The best teacher I've ever had at BYU.

Dr. Brau is an amazing professor. His lectures are very engaging. This is a hard class, but very doable if you utilize his resources. Attendance is basically mandatory if you want a good grade, he will literally tell you exam answers during the lectures.
Has a few tests and thats your whole grade. They are difficult if you haven't studied Finance really well. By difficulty the class comes right under Econ 110 almost head to head.
He is very entertaining, and his lectures are great. Overall, the exams are what kill people, so definitely study in the way he tells you.
Super fun guy.

Bro Brau is the best professor I have ever had in the Marriott school. I usually get Bs but I got an A in this class. His lectures are funny and he's very inclusive and understanding. He says to know the notes and you seriously need to know the notes, try your best to be at every class. The math just takes practice so an A is definitely attainable!

Brother Brau is honestly my favorite Professor I have ever taken. He gets a lot of hate but I don't think a lot of people are ready to put in the work. Helped me a lot in this class, professionally, and was even there for some tough stuff in my personal life.

TAKE ACC200 BEFORE THE CLASS! Many of these reviews say that this class is near impossible. An A is 100% attainable. He gave us a 4.5% curve. I would study 15 hours for each exam, which is a similar workload to a course like ACC200. The best tip is to understand class notes and do the practice exams. Although he says not to, they helped me the most

Maybe his teaching style just isn't for me, but I felt constantly behind despite doing exactly what he recommends. Notes were very dense (which isn't inherently a bad thing) but did make studying difficult. I poured a lot of time into this class every week but still was only able to pull off an average grade.
Brau was a great teacher. I learned a ton about finance. KNOW THE CLASS NOTES!

Brau is one of the best professors when it comes to teaching you valuable things for your future. I don't understand why people are complaining about his tests when he literally tells you exactly what to study and the answers are directly from the class notes. Always brought the spirit into class as well and gave great professional development.

This class was a nightmare for the first half of the semester. You're thrown into a bunch of material and finance terms with little explanation. Only memorize class notes for midterms, the tests are based ONLY on that. I ultimately got the hang of it and was able to do good in the second half of the class. Bro Brau curved 4.5%, so that was nice.

Taking this class from brother Brau is a cannon event. Words cannot describe what this class was. I learned a lot of practical finance, and was able to succeed using his notes and online drill problems.
He tells you exactly what you need to do. His spiritual thoughts are amazing. One of the best professors I've ever had. The bar for an A is a bit high tho.

I highly recommend taking FIN 201 from Bro. Brau! The way to succeed in the class is very well established from the beginning of the course. If you really buy in, his lectures are helpful in understanding the content while his professional development and spiritual thoughts show he really cares about the success of his students.

He is a fantastic guy. I appreciated his testimony. Outside of that though, this was class was ridiculous. Everything I learned was on my own. I would study the class notes and knew them super well but they don't actually teach you everything you need to know. If you're going into finance take the class but others it's not worth it.

If you're planning on finance, take this class. He really wants his students to understand the intuition behind things. If you're not, take it elsewhere. Confusing topics taught at a quick pace, no equation sheet on exams, acts like this is the most important class you'll take at BYU. Much of my energy went to this class rather than my actual major

If you're looking for emotional support but not good teaching, go ahead and take this class. Everything I learned about finance this semester I learned on my own. The TAs talk about how Brau teaches things in an overcomplicated or just wrong way. BYU, take this man out of the finance program and put him in religion. Way too hard for a 200 class.

Do not take the online class for students already in the business school. Extremely disorganized with the TA's and teacher saying vastly different things. Out of my entire time at BYU I have never had to calculate my grade but here you do. Outdated content, and very disorganized.

Online course for students already in the business school is completely unsupported. First two tests did not reflect material taught by online videos and other resources, making him apologize and create new tests. It was a 25% curve. He is a good guy, I appreciate what he does and the service for our country, but just take it in person.

This course requires a $90 digital textbook which he wrote. Lectures use a lot of finance jargon with limited explanation, which made it hard to follow without prior knowledge. The class frequently centers on investment banking and private equity starting salaries, so students outside finance won't find it accessible or relevant.

This class was definitely tricky, but Professor Brau made all the difference! Class was always engaging and gave many good professional development and spiritual thoughts. He literally writes all of his tests straight from the class notes, so make sure to look at those primarily when you're studying.

Do not take this class unless your only passion in life is finance and want an insane challenge. His teaching style is so confusing and difficult and the class is super exam heavy, which are all based off the hard to follow class notes. He brags about only 7 out of 1400 students getting perfect scores on tests which is totally unreasonable.

Lots of people give bad reviews because the class is hard, but bro Brau is an amazing professor that knows his stuff well. The class is designed to push you to understand finance and not just get an A. it's NOT an easy class. Lots of people don't like his style/mannerisms, and if that's the case, then finance probably isn't a good fit for them.
Says some wild things that should definitely not be said at BYU. His notes make no sense and he is by far the most non professional professor I've had in all my time here.

I took a W. This class made me drop my finance major. The TAs were not very helpful because they hadn't taken this class from him. I spent 5-7 hours a day on homework and 95% of your grade is exams. I know he works for some people, but it was definitely not me.

Students were called out in ways that were discouraging and I did not feel comfortable. For an intro finance class, it was very difficult even after taking ACC 200 and 310. I would not take a class from him again. 4 midterms and one was even a week before finals. I think the ratings are rigged. only finance bros will do good in this
Very difficult, lectures were inefficient, expected an unreasonable time commitment: “if you're struggling, just spend 4 hours every morning reviewing notes and practicing”

Brau is super energetic and teaches like a drill sergant. He cares a lot about student success in the real world. I went in expecting it to be really hard, but it was totally manageable. His tests are weighted heavily and the quizzes are a lot of work, once or twice a week. He seems like one of the better FIN201 professors though.

His teaching style is very aggressive, confusing, and overwhelming. He does all his class teaching in the first 20 minutes and then spends the rest of class on spiritual thoughts, "career building", or tangents. If the content was taught differently it would feel a lot more manageable. The exams are difficult and the class is overwhelming.

Brau is a really nice guy, but I learned almost nothing in this class. He goes on long spiritual tangents every single lecture, which takes away from the material. He isn't very effective at teaching, and the TA lab is always full. I would recommend taking it from basically anyone else if you actually want to learn finance.

This class is brutal. Someone said you have to solve a puzzle to see your grade, and I could not agree with this more. The exams are difficult and confusing and he switches things up mid semester, despite what his syllabus says. Definitely one of the tougher classes at BYU, but luckily he curves it a little bit (but do not rely on this).

What a joke of a professor. Makes you solve a puzzle to see your grade. Sure, you can drop a midterm, but only if you do surveys, which end up in spam mail so you miss it. If this is who BYU is hiring these days and keeping on staff, the institution is headed for disaster. Do better, Brau.

Didn't ever feel like I was getting taught the material that was going to be on the test. A bunch of information is thrown at you and then you are tested on the most finite details that he mentioned once. Incredibly difficult to know what to study. Tests made to trick you rather than test material. Super disappointed.

He doesn't take anything seriously and it is incredibly difficult to learn anything in this class. The whole thing is just a game to him. A lot of questions are midterms are about one super specific thing he briefly mentioned in class. He always just complains about his one autistic son that disappoints him greatly.

Brother Brau is a great guy, but I usually left lectures and exams feeling more confused than before. He even prides himself on the fact that a lot of students struggle in his class. I love his spiritual thoughts though. It would be great if he could be more clear about what exactly will be on the test, and not try to trick students on purpose.

Lectures are really quick, but he focuses on what you need to know without unnecessary content. Compared to other sections of FIN 201, this class was more manageable. The workload is challenging, but if you study hard, you'll do great. I really enjoyed the class and would strongly recommend him.

He's hands down my favorite professor I've ever had! Super inspirational, knows his stuff on finance better than anyone, gives great spiritual thoughts, and makes the entire class laugh out loud multiple times per lecture with his jokes!

Brau is extremely caring and passionate about BYU, finance, and preaching the gospel. His lectures are interesting, albeit all over the place and confusing. They were extremely difficult to follow. I would advise reading the chapters before lectures if you want to understand them at all.

I love JimmyB as a person. He is a guy with a good heart. BUT I am not a fan of his lecture. If you are good at memorizing things without putting meaning to it, you will do well. I just could not memorize so much in short time because I could not find why I was doing what I was doing. I managed to get an A though.

this guy's class was him scrawling incoherently on some paper under a document camera (zoom), interspersed with some WEIRD comments on religion and his wife(?). like literally my jaw dropped every class at the things he would say. he prayers were only offered by return missionaries in other languages.

This class is not hard if you study, but you really have to study. NOT an easy A. I did all the readings, reviewed notes, did all the practice problems and exams, but still found the class to be fairly difficult. There is a good curve, and he does have an extra credit opportunity. I wouldn't advise against taking him bc he seems to be a canon event

His spiritual messages are thoughtful, powerful and had an impact on my life more than any teacher I have ever taken. Students who complain about certain things acting like Brau didn't do exactly what he said he was gonna do from the beginning. If you do what he tells you to do you get an A. I would recommend taking the class in-person tho.

An Amazing and Hard Class. I honestly chuckle at bad reviews for him. People say you're tested on notes, not finance, but that's not true - his notes are finance! He teaches in a certain way so you're actually forced to study and learn to earn the grade they want. You can do great in this class if you listen, work hard, and give the course respect.

Brau is loved by many of his students. I loved his spiritual thoughts and felt like I grew spiritually big time in his class, not so much in Finance, but spiritually. He teaches in a way that many people like me don't learn. You have to memorize notes he made a few years ago, and engaging with the material is on you.

He brings a ton of energy to lectures. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students. Spiritual thoughts and professional development moments were awesome. However, your grade is 95% determined by exams, so if you aren't a good test taker I would consider choosing someone else for finance. Practice the drill problems and study the class notes!

He is clearly a master at finance himself, but he does not know how to teach it. Lectures go way too fast. Misleading emphasis on the notes and their importance. You need an excessivley high level of intuition on how the equations work or you will fail. Just taught myself from the book and practice exams. Great guy, just not my kind of teacher.

Brau cares deeply for his students and wants you to succeed. He has an open-door policy for anyone needing help. You definitely will need to put in the work and read the textbook before class because his teaching can be very fast. His spiritual thoughts were some of the highlights of my semester.

Be ready to spend hours a week studying for this class. Homework load itself is very manageable, but the exams will kill if you aren't prepared. He does drop one, but be ready to work hard. TA's aren't super helpful, textbook is. I would recommend relying on his drill problems and videos for exams and you'll have it down.

This class made me want to get run over on the walk to the building. The exams are 95% of your grade. The only pros of this class were the spiritual thoughts. If you are not a good test taker, AVOID THIS CLASS. He goes crazy fast, terrible writing, no recording, and no visuals. He brags that the final is the hardest exam in your BYU career.

I am absolutely appalled by all these high ratings. Not only was this class extremely difficult, surpassing the difficulty level of all the graduate level courses I am taking, but he was actively disrespectful towards several students in class and otherwise, myself included.

This is likely the worst course I have taken at BYU.

I respect Jim so much. Great man with a great heart. His teaching style isn't my favorite and his notes are TERRIBLE. Almost unreadable and hard to understand if you weren't in class. He abbreviates everything and is tough to understand when reading the notes. Great spiritual thoughts and heart of gold tho

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM! Im in the online section and the materials is not helpful for the exams. Apparently his class notes are what are most important, but I'm an online student. The class videos DO NOT HELP! The syllabus talks about dropping your lowest grade, BUT he expects you to fill out surveys, which was NOT STATED on the syllabus

If you don't care about finance or don't want to major finance, you do not want to take his class. I promise you. I know more about bunny (his wife) than finance. You learn and are tested on his notes, not finance. His tangents are long and unhelpful. He goes through the motions, gets his notes written and you don't actually learn intro to finance.

No slides so you couldn't reference anything or have visuals. His notes were very hard to decipher and he went really fast so its hard to follow. Tests were super hard and 95% of your grade and no TA reviews. Taught this class to myself. I did like his spiritual thoughts. He made this class way harder than it had to be.

Brau is hilarious and preaches understanding finance, and not just knowing how to do the problems. I feel like questions aren't always answered in a way that is helpful, but other than that he is great! He is very inspiring! Compared to other classes like Econ 110, this class is a piece of cake. Read the book, do the hw, and go to class.
Not a fan of his teaching style
Very disorganized class. He has bad handwriting and his notes don't make sense.
Jim is a great professor and has great lectures. I learned so much in his class. He is a very entertaining guy and you definitely are not bored in his class.
10/5 stars. You cannot take from a better professor. He has been my favorite professor at all of BYU. In addition to this, he has the best spiritual thoughts I've ever heard. Thank you, Brother Brau!

Prof. Brau gives good spiritual thoughts but isn't great at teaching finance. He lectures so quick and doesn't explain things, just says "use your intuition." He doesn't cater to people learning for the first time. His notes are pretty bad too, they're hard to read and he shorthands everything. And exams are 95% of your grade, cumulative final too.

Do not take if you don't want to be a finance major. He is a great professor but purposefully teaches a little bit tougher to prepare those going into finance, and it helps you prepare for the program. Take it from another professor if you just need to take the class. If you do want to be a finance major this class will help a ton, just study a ton
He's a great professor with amazing spiritual thoughts. Your grade is based on very difficult tests.

A very hard class, but worth it once you see how much you've learned that's real world applicable. His spiritual thoughts were the highlight of my weeks- it's humbling to watch a military finance professor cry because of the spirit. He could fill the entire auditorium with both laughter and the holy ghost. Highly highly recommend.

I love this man. Jim Brau will change your life for the better. Not gonna lie, I would take any class he ever teaches no matter the subject just because he is that good. So funny, and also a great teacher. He teaches much more than just finance

Wow, I think he should teach note-taking rather than finance because that is what he does. From a person who got an A in Accounting and learned a lot, I'm surprised how this made me not love the business school and want to drop out. I thought BYU was about repentance. This is just brutal and unforgiving. He doesn't teach he writes notes.

He is an incredibly hard teacher and his class is not very helpful. He doesn't care a ton about his students and his test is all to do with the notes. His test questions more try to confuse you then actually you learning.

His teaching style and speed will single handedly give you depression if you struggle on tests or don't understand something. Unnecessarily hard for an intro class. Entire grade is based on exams, TAs don't show up to TA labs. He's a stern military guy and moves insanely fast. He has some really good spiritual thoughts though.

Currently retaking this class. Read the book, take notes, sit up close in class, take more notes, and it will be easy. There is a lot of hard work and reading, but it is worth it. Didn't go last time and got a C. Got 100% on the first test this year. Had an internship interview yesterday. Brau's class helped me land the internship easily.
Wouldn't reccommend.
Stud. Big fan of his spiritual thoughts.

Really enjoyed his class last winter. The class is test-heavy, but if you follow along in class you will know everything that you need (no curveballs on the test). Brau gives some awesome spiritual thoughts that I remember to this day. He is very energetic so don't expect to fall asleep in this class!

Brau requires you review him that's why he rates well. No grades besides tests,class is just him writing things down. No assignments,no way to know if you're prepared and not allowed to see what you got wrong. Asked for an exception,he called me out in class. Class structure is based on what he thinks would have helped his kids do better in college
He has a very specific teaching style and he expects a lot out of his students. Pay close attention in class more than anything. Tests are 95% of your grade.

In my interactions with Brau, he was super caring and kind! He was compassionate, especially with those graduating that semester. Often adjusting the structure of the course/extra help with study guides and practice problems as would help students. Exams were hard and worth most of the grade.  (Taken Winter24-online class)

Brau is awesome, this was one of my favorite classes taken at BYU, thanks to him. He moves fast and content can be hard to understand, but his spiritual thoughts are memorable and impactful. Learned a ton.

Brau's class is challenging but worth it. He's passionate and engaging, with great spiritual/professional insights. Use the textbook, take detailed notes, and try Unstuckstudy AI - it really helped with test prep.

This is the only class where I have cried over hw. Like, violently sobbed. I cannot fathom why he is ranked so high. Some of the spiritual thoughts made me uncomfortable. Especially as a woman. He is a textbook finance bro in all the worst ways. God help me forgive this man.

His class is funny and super engaging- which is a good thing because if you stop paying attention for even half a second, you're screwed. He writes notes by hand on a projector and has you copy them while he explains (which means you have a lot of handwritten notes but not a lot of resources to look back on if you have questions/didn't get it).

James Brau has been my absolute favorite professor I've taken so far. He has incredible spiritual thoughts that make you feel more than any religion class. He teaches more than just finance and he's incredibly funny and it's impossible to fall asleep in his class, also very dangerous if you do so because his lectures are crucial and move very fast

Professor Brau brings a lot of energy and passion to his FIN201 class. While the material is challenging, attending lectures and studying the textbook thoroughly are key to success. I found unstuckstudy ai and ChatGPT helpful for exam prep. Overall, a rewarding experience with insightful spiritual discussions.

The prof is high energy and passionate, but you gotta keep up in class. Lots of good advice, but be ready to study hard for the exams. Using tools like unstuckstudy ai can help prep for the tests. Overall, a challenging but rewarding course if you put in the work.

The class is challenging but the professor is very passionate and engaging. Attending lectures and keeping up with the textbook are key to doing well. Though tests are the main focus, the professor provides valuable professional development and spiritual insights during the lectures.

The class is fast-paced and requires a lot of preparation, but the professor's engaging teaching style and valuable insights make it worthwhile. Attend lectures, study the textbook, and you'll do well.

Professor Brau's class is fast-paced, but if you stay engaged and prepare diligently, you can succeed. His lectures are energetic and insightful, providing valuable professional development and spiritual perspectives. The tests are challenging, but mastering the content is key to doing well.

Brau is an engaging and passionate professor, but his class is fast-paced and challenging. Attend lectures, take thorough notes, and study the textbook material thoroughly to succeed. The tests are focused on mastering the content, so be prepared to put in the work. Overall, a rewarding class if you're willing to rise to the occasion.

He goes so fast I eventually just stopped going to the lectures and teaching myself the material through the MyEducator Textbook. He's a great guy and very inspirational, but he will say his class isn't fast if you just read beforehand but even then it's SO fast. I personally didn't enjoy the class or his teaching style, but he is a cool person
