This was by far the worst course I've taken at BYU. Brau is a good guy, and clearly has good intentions, but is way too prideful to teach a prerequisite business class. He covers his notes in abbreviations that only he understands... and then bases his tests on small comments that he makes in class. He would make a great Sunday school teacher...

Finance is a harder class just because of how much material you learn in a short amount of time. Make sure that you read the textbook and take good notes in class and you should be okay for the tests (they are all of your grade). I personally like Prof Brau's personality, you won't fall asleep in class.

1. This class does not have a lot of homework. If you learn primarily by solving homework problems, this class will be very different.

2. Most of the test questions are taken directly from his lectures. Be there or be square.

3. He really cares for the student. He has lots of enthusiasm and lots of good advices.
Brau's class is all tests, no hw. Take good lecture notes and you'll be fine.
Very very test heavy. Tests are difficult, must listen to lecture and memorize notes to pass.

Professor Brau cares a lot about your success. His class is very clear on what he expects. It is very test heavy, but it you study his notes and learn the intuition rather than just cramming, you will be just fine.

Bro Brau's class is amazing! The daily spiritual thoughts and career developments were incredibly helpful. You come out of this class well-versed in finance and prepared for interviews in the financial sector. Grades are test heavy with 5% quizzes, 75% midterms, and 20% final but he prepares you well for them. STUDY THE NOTES and you'll be fine!

One of my favorite professors in terms of personality. In his tests each question will have unnecessary numbers (for example tax percentage as well as the not needed WACC percentage) so if you are not airtight on the concepts you will likely mess some of the test up. I'm a 3.97 student who will likely get a B in the class.

No doubt my favorite professor I have ever had. I'm not a very spiritual person to be honest, but he gave spiritual thoughts every class which are extremely moving. VERY test heavy so if you aren't good with tests this isn't the class for you. Brau is an excellent teacher as well and his lectures are not boring at all. I highly recommend!

Brau is a very energetic professor who definitely is passionate about Finance.  He can be a little hard to follow in class because he talks and moves fast through the lectures.  He does a spiritual thought and professional development moment every class which can be insightful and interesting.
He is a great guy but his class requires you put in a lot of work outside of class. You need a solid grasp on the notes and readings and you will do decently.

If you want to learn "FIN-ance," then you should take this class. If you take your time to learn the material and want to learn, then you will be fine. It's not an easy class, but it is doable if you make it a priority. Amazing teacher.
Engaging during lectures. Pretty good at teaching concepts. But bad at teaching us how to do the problems that are actually on test.

Brau is a really good professor. He is also nuts, in a good way. This dude has crazy amounts of energy and he made finance really fun, I enjoyed every lecture with him. He knows his stuff and if you listen to him then you will do well in the class, that being said, you have to be willing to work hard in this class.
Brau is a character, but a great guy with a great heart and really knows his stuff. Your grade is extremely weighed on your exam performance but if you take good notes you'll be prepared.

I loved taking this class from Dr. Brau.
He's very inspirational in his teaching and instills a love for finance in his students. He also spends time sharing daily spiritual thoughts that are very motivational. Tests are the biggest part of your grade in his class but he tells you exactly how to study for them.

Brau is a man with tons of energy and passion for finance. He can come across as intense but he is very genuine and cares a lot about his students. He gives clear expectations for the class. He emphasizes the ways to succeed in his class and that is key to performing well. Don't be afraid of the material, study hard, READ CLASS NOTES, and enjoy it!

Brau is a great lecturer, and I really appreciated a lot of the attitudes and experiences he brought to class. His nuance and care afforded to people and topics was incredibly refreshing at BYU. You gotta do the reading and drill practice problems for the tests, and you'll get out of this class what you put into it. Everything comes down to tests!

Hands down the best professor I've had. The course itself wasn't easy, but his policy on taking hand notes makes an incredible difference in retention and preparation for the tests, which the course is graded by almost nothing other than exams. His lectures never hard to sit through and he genuinely cares about every students wellbeing and success.
Great professor, have to attend lectures and take notes to do well on tests. Reading textbook before class will help you out a ton.
The professor is very energetic and knows his stuff. It is very test heavy, but I believe this is the same for other professors that teach this same class. I would recommend him.

Brother Brau is dope. If you want an A be prepared to spend a lot of time reading the textbook, doing practice problems, and going to every lecture. I don't care for an A that much so I skimmed or skipped a lot of the readings. It's pretty tough but you'll survive. For most people your academic commitment and grit will likely determine your grade.

I loved this class. Professor Brau goes really fast so do the reading beforehand. The tests are mostly based of the lecture notes so it is important to pay attention and take notes in class. He is an awesome teacher and keeps the lectures interesting. Definitely recommend.
He cares a lot about the students. The test questions come directly from the notes every time. It is worth it to rewrite them out before every midterm. The spiritual thoughts are a highlight!

Professor Brau is very passionate about finance and makes the lectures exciting.  He taught us the concepts but I sometimes found it challenging to understand the "why" behind what we were talking about.  I felt like those explanations were missing in his lectures.  It's very test heavy so you have to study hard.

Dr. Brau is a extremely good finance professor. However, his style of teaching is geared towards those who already have a foundational knowledge in finance and accounting. Take this class after you have taken ACC 200 and other business school classes. Awesome class, I really enjoyed it.

Hilarious teacher, but get ready to learn your notes like the back of your hand for the test. The tests come directly from the notes, so as long as you know them, you will get an A. Take time to study! Test heavy, but he will drop your lowest midterm score and your grade on your final can become your final grade if you need it to.

He is an awesome professor! Take the time to read the textbook before class and you'll be totally fine for the exams. It is test heavy, but you just need to review what he tells you. Brings the spirit every class and is super engaging. I definitely would have fallen asleep with another teacher, but he kept things alive. So funny and so spiritual.
The class was interesting and Jim Brau makes lectures engaging. Tests are really the only grade and they take work to study for but is very doable if you talk with the TAs.

Even though my learning style didn't completely match with Dr. Brau, he is an excellent professor. The concepts he teaches are very difficult but he explains them decently well. Be prepared to take handwritten notes and do the readings beforehand. Sometimes the lectures are really confusing but just read and study on your own and you'll do fine.

Professor Brau is great! You can really tell how much he cares about each of his students and is willing to help them in many ways. He really loves his job and it shows. The class was difficult, mostly because 95% of your grade is determined by your test grades.

Professor Brau is a very good professor, but his class is definitely difficult. You have to put a lot of time and effort into the class in order to understand the material. Your grade is heavily based on tests, so if you're not a good test taker, maybe choose another class.

Brau loves finance, and he loves his students. His spiritual thoughts are always inspiring and entertaining. Your grade is based almost entirely off of tests, so know the notes super well. He goes pretty quickly through the notes in class lectures so pay attention and go to class every time!
He was a good professor, but sometimes he didn't explain things that well. If you keep up with the readings you should do fine in the class.

Very passionate guy. His lectures are very entertaining but not necessarily the most helpful for understanding the concepts needed for tests. Most of your learning is up to you and the time you put in outside of class, but there also aren't very many curveballs thrown at you, so if you put in the time you can do pretty well.

The class isn't easy in the slightest, but I think Brother Brau is the best option for this course. Engaging lectures, not too much homework, and attendance isn't graded. But if you want to do well in the class, you'll need to get the notes from class down and memorized, so go. Your grade is pretty much just from the exams, so know the notes!!!

Professor Brau means business. He is there to teach and help students grasp the concepts and principles of finance. He goes fast and it is up to you to study and prepare for the exams. It is exam based, and they are hard. This has the most study heavy class I have taken at BYU so far, but I have learned a lot. Professor is great overall.

Professor Brau's class pushed me in new ways and caused me to grow a lot. His tests were hard and I think 95% of your grade being tests is a little high, but he gives all the students the keys to success if you're willing to pay attention and put the time in. He repeats a lot of random stuff in every class so making a bingo sheet makes lectures fun

"You all are part of the entitled generation" "It is going to be impossible for you guys to find jobs because you're so entitled" "How did 50% of you miss that question? It was in the freakin' notes" **It in fact was NOT in the notes.
"This is the hardest final you'll ever take at BYU" "I'm on preworkout, good luck keeping up."

I loved Brau from the second I walked into his class. He is super engaging and is an awesome professor. He keeps you on your toes, is super funny, and I love the spiritual thoughts that he gives every class. Your grade is 95% tests so be ready for that.

Prof Brau truly cares about his students and wishes for their success. Before lectures, make sure that you read over the MyEducator readings that will apply to that days lecture. If you do that, the lectures will be much easier to follow. Brau literally tells us what the test questions are, and they typically come right off the notes. Great class.

Brau is a phenomenal man. He is very passionate about helping us succeed as individuals and in the workforce. Even though I did not do as well in the class as I hoped for, he is my favorite professor up to this point. He is hilarious, passionate, and hard-working. He is very personable and self-deprecating which makes him very easy to relate to.

Lectures are so great and he is very straight forward telling you what is on the test. Your grade is completely exam based and they are a lot to prep for but the key is just studying notes and being in class. If you skip class you will not do well.

I loved Brau from the minute I walked into his class. It was interesting, he was energetic, and he does a great job keeping students engaged and teaching the course material. Get ready for big tests, tests are 95% of your grade.

While Brau seems like a decent person, his teaching style is unique and an acquired taste. He explains concepts adequately and one feels confident leaving his lectures, however, his tests have very detailed and specific information that is barely mentioned in his lectures or textbook. His class is entirely graded by the 4 midterms and final.

Brau has extreme ADHD so his lectures are wild. He's a good guy, but very particular in his teaching/testing style. You basically read the chapter before class and then he takes notes with you in class. Copy the notes. Follow his advice on how to do well. You still probably won't get the grade you want though, cause you're not good enough.

Brother Brau is a great guy and super passionate about finance. FIN 201 taught by him is very interesting but a hard A. 95% of the grade is from midterms and the final, and the test questions are often about random things that he talks about in class instead of the concepts that the course is focused on. Super cool dude though.

Brau is pretty great. He is really good teacher who knows the material and really cares about it, and makes hard things seem easier than they are. He focused on applying what we learn to life which was great, but the class is tough with 4 hard midterms and a huge final making up 95% of your grade.

This class is 95% tests so make sure that you study for them. Sometimes it can be hard to follow what professor Brau is saying in class but he does cover the material. Reading the textbook before class makes it easier to follow.

Dr. Brau is awesome! I feel like there is a unique approach to relating the course work to our lives. He doesn't just leave it as a wishy-washy, business, business, business approach; he makes sure to help his students see the relevance of the work. Get ready to study hard for tests, and manage yourself.
Brother Brau moves pretty quickly through the notes so make sure you come to class prepared. Not the best learning style for everyone.

Brau is super passionate about finance, but I feel like his class could be better organized. It is very lecture heavy, and he uses an overhead projector to take his own notes which you copy down. The tests are pretty difficult, and you have a midterm 2 days before the final. Decent class, but it could definitely be structured better.

Great lectures, despised the tests and quizzes. He makes it clear what you need to do to pass. However if you like feedback and a chance to see tests/quizzes to figure out what you struggle with, I'd avoid. Other than that it was an enjoyable lecture and I learned a lot.
Love Professor Brau. He is very knowledgeable and cares about the students. Tough class be prepared to work a ton! Would recommend Brother Brau to anyone needing this class!

Professor Brau has been one of my favorite professors at BYU. He recognizes that his class is very challenging and equips students with the best resources to succeed on the four midterms and cumulative final. Although attendance is not mandatory you should attend each lecture as he hints at questions and concepts that will be on the exam.

Professor Brau is a very passionate teacher. He is extremely energetic and his lectures go by super quickly. However the entire course depends on you doing well in the exams which you cannot review after you have taken. On top of that, the exams feel like a lot of memorizing rather than just actually understanding the important concepts.

If you are planning to be a Finance Major take Brau's class. He makes sure you know finance in and out. His tests are tough, but put in the work and you should get an A. His lectures are always entertaining as well!

I would recommend Professor Brau to anyone taking Finance. His lectures are amazing, and he is a great guy. Be ready to study because 95 percent of your grade is based on exams. If you go to class and take good notes and study them, you will do well.

One of the best professors on BYU campus. His lectures extremely engaging, but are fast-pace, so make sure to do all readings before class. Expectations are very clear and he's committed to helping students succeed in his class and also spiritually.

Professor Brau knows his stuff so well, but he flies through the material. It is tough to follow at times and you've got to be really locked in to be able to understand the material. His teaching style definitely isn't for everyone

Brother Brau only teaches 201 in fall and has his course set up very well. Clear grading criterium. There are 4 midterms, chapter quizzes from the online textbook, and the final. Overall the course content is manageable if you stay on top of it and do the readings before class so you come prepared to answer questions and practice.

Professor Brau was the most entertaining of all my professors this semester. It is necessary to go to class and copy his notes. Between that and the practice problems online, an A is definitely achievable. His teaching style is not for all, but I would recommend him to anyone!

I enjoyed Professor Brau's class. He is a very engaging teacher and interesting to listen to. He knows what he is talking about and teaches finance in a way that is easy to understand. His class is straightforward and if you do what he asks and put effort into the class you will do well.

Professor Brau is an excellent and very capable teacher. I wish more time was spent on each topic and that we covered more topics because this class moves very quickly! Be prepared to work hard and do a lot of math, and also be prepared for an incredibly useful and interesting class that will challenge you in the testing center!

Very entertaining professor and a right of passage here at BYU. Your grade is your tests so do well. Brau was very off-topic and not clear but he got through the material. Go to class! The tests were frustrating because you could not go through and know what you missed, this made studying for the final difficult. Take the class but be ready.

Has an interesting teaching style. All students handwrite notes in class and copy down exactly as he writes. If you write it all down AND understand what EVERYTHING means, this will help you. If you don't come prepared to class, it is more difficult to make sense of the notes later. I wish we had more practice problems and less tangents in class.

I felt like the tests were pretty easy if you study. The way he sets up his notes and his spiritual thoughts are great. I hated the textbook and how you can't see what you get wrong on the quizzes. The TAs should do review sessions for the midterms. Easier than ECON110, but harder than ACC200. It was annoying how the grades tab was taken down.

I believe that Professor Brau is a great person, but has room for improvement as a teacher. He's constantly going on tangents in class and then will rush through the material. You're tested on his exact words when the test comes around, rather than real world problems, and you can't even see what you did wrong afterwards! He also yells everything

Professor Brau has an interesting style of teaching, if it doesn't work for you at first, I recommend taking a different professor. Your grade is based on 4 midterms (one being dropped) and the final exam. You can't review the tests or see what you got wrong so that is difficult. Overall, I really enjoyed the class and learning from professor Brau.

Entertaining guy but a poor teacher. He understands finance really well but has a difficult time explaining it in terms that others can understand. He uses too many acronyms and expects us to think as he does. Tests are pretty much the only grade and do not truly reflect an understanding of finance.
Professor Brau is a great teacher. The class was a bit difficult though. The course is very test-heavy and some questions come directly from things said during lectures.
This was my favorite professor that I have ever had. The class is tough, but the lectures are so engaging. I thoroughly enjoyed going to class.

Brau will teach you what you need to know. He gets the job done. The grade in class is mostly based off of your midterms, there are 4, and a final. As a person his kind of odd, and will make some wild comments in class, but overall this is your best choice for a FIN 201 professor. He makes it very clear what will be on the tests.

Professor Brau cares a lot about his students and wants the best for them. Paper notes are taken in class which I really liked as it required you to pay attention. He would do a fairly good job explaining the notes, sometimes I wish he explained them in real terms instead of just algebraic letters. Very test heavy. Good overall experience.

Brau is an amazing guy, and I really respect him on many levels. However, he does get super intense and yells most of the time in lectures. Only take this class from him if you're a good test taker or a genius. Exams are 95% of your grade and they're no joke. Stay caught up and study like crazy- especially what he writes in class notes!

Dr. Brau was an amazing professor. I learned so much in his Fin 201 Class. The class was very test heavy but all of the answers can be found in the notes and the reading. I would take a class with Dr. Brau again even though it was very difficult. Dr. Brau always has your attention and makes class interesting.

His class is 95% tests, and the way he lectures is horrible. He puts a pad of paper under a camera, and just writes. His handwriting is horrible, so it is hard to know what he even is writing. Definitely think ACC 200 should be a requirement to even take this class. I think taking ACC 310 as well made the class at lot more manageable for me.

Tough but rewarding class. No matter who you take it from, it will be hard. Brau just keeps you entertained and makes sure you don't fall asleep. Overall great professor. Hard tests though. Be prepared to work a lot in this class.

Great Professor that makes his expectations clear from the get go. It is a lot of material to learn and the tests are hard but Professor Brau teaches what you need to know and basically tells you what material will be on the test. Pretty much anything he writes down in class is testable material. He is caring and accessible outside class as well.

Brau is a engaging and fun professor. The classes go through the material very quickly and are basically useless unless you read the textbook chapter before. 95% of your grade is from the midterms and final exam so you have to score straight A's on almost every exam to get an A in the class. Brau jumps around a lot in his lectures.

I love Professor Brau and the energy that he brings to class! Come to class prepared because the lectures are fast paced and it is very hard to keep up if you haven't done the reading before hand. Also a lot of the test problems come from the notes so make sure you are writing anything down that could be valuable and then study your notes.

Professor Brau is awesome! His classes were always fun and uplifting. He gives great spiritual thoughts and professional development moments that help in the real world. Take good notes and you'll do great!

He is a great professor and really cares about the students! I wasn't always the biggest fan of some of the test questions because they were very specific. To be fair though, he does warn how his tests are formatted and he sticks to that.

Brau is an awesome guy and is very passionate about finance. He is a good teacher overall. His classes can be pretty spastic and there's just a lot going on. This semester he hid the grades tab from us on LS so that was interesting. Almost your whole grade is based on the 4 mid terms and the cumulative final. It's a tough class, but Brau is solid.

Brau is a very intense guy. He yells 80% of the time in class. Preparing for class by doing the readings is very important. I was not a big fan of the tests because some questions are based off of random things he said in class one time and he expects you to remember it. Some people like his teaching style, others and myself do not.

This was a great class! The tests are rigorous, but the expectations are very clear. If you come to class and take notes you will be just fine. Study the notes! And take the practice exams both are very helpful.

Honestly, people are dramatic about how hard this course can be. Brau tells you everything that is going to be on the exam. Brau teaches you so much about finance, job markets, and the gospel and is so entertaining while doing it. If you are going to take FIN 201, I would recommend taking it from him!

Professor Brau is a great guy and always gave entertaining and inspirational lectures. The class is very test heavy but the tests aren't overly difficult. My only complaint is I didn't feel like he always explained things great in class and it can feel a little rapid fire.
He us absolutely amazing. The exams and concepts are tough, but going to class and studying will take care of it!

This class is so hard but Brau is a real homie. Lectures are very entertaining and shares some of the best spiritual thoughts. Really wants us to be prepared for the finance industry and the real world.

Brother Brau is a great, difficult, real, caring, and diligent professor. He shares what will help you in the real world. His tests are tough and I would have rather have taken 10 credits of other classes compared to this class, but he drops the lowest exam score you get. 95% of your final grade is tests. It's doable though. Study hard

Professor Brau is an incredible professor. However, I don't believe that he is the best fit for a lot of students. His lectures are heavy and move at an incredibly quick pace. 95% of the final grade is based on exams. Personally, I'm not a strong test taker and had to study for an average of 30hrs per exam just to pull of an A or B. What a grind...

I did fairly well in this class given that I spent on around 2 hours a day studying. Tests are hard but if you memorize EVERY detail from class notes you will be fine. Gives very good spiritual thoughts that I loved. Entertaining class.
He is amazing professor. We wants each student to succeed in his class. He gives us every opportunity to be able to do well in the exams.
Very passionate teacher. Loves what he does. Going to lectures and taking notes are crucial. Basically the only grades you have are exams, which is annoying. Great guy tho.

This class is TOUGH. Bro Brau does a good job of going over the material in lecture, but you really need to deeply read the textbook to supplement. His lectures get a bit intense, I often left with a headache. But overall, I did learn a lot of valuable material and spiritual insight during the class.
Very test heavy, study the notes from class.

Professor Brau has got to be the most interesting professor I've ever had. He was probably the most practical teacher there is. The class is very lecture heavy (you aren't graded on attendance but all of the notes are in class), but Brau mixes in each lecture with amazing spiritual and professional advice. I would 100% recommend him.

Professor Brau is a great teacher, very inspiring and with amazing lectures. Some of the concepts are challenging, but he provides all the resources you need. You do need to study for exams but as long as you do, you'll be fine. That being said, 95% of your grade is based on exam scores so if you don't do well on tests, beware.
Professor Brau is great! His lectures are fast-paced but he is very clear about how to do well in his class.

Professor Brau is a great teacher, very inspiring and with amazing lectures. Some of the concepts are challenging, but he provides all the resources you need to succeed. You do need to study for exams but if you study, you'll be fine. That being said, 95% of your grade is based on exam scores so if you don't do well on tests, beware.

Brother Brau is extremely passionate about Finance and cares about the long-term success of his students. His class was very difficult for me but in a good way. I do wish there was more weight on homework/quizzes than on the exams. Overall great class and an awesome Professor!
This course is very difficult! Study the class notes and read the textbook before class. Tests are the biggest grade in the class so prepare a lot!

I love Bro Brau, he is amazing. He keeps the class engaging and interesting, and you learn so much in this class. 75% of the grade is midterms, so the class is pretty test heavy, but if you take good notes and study based only off of those notes you'll be alright. I promise you won't regret taking Fin 201 from Bro Brau.

Professor Brau teaches a rigorous course and as such has very rigorous tests. Anyone who works hard doing the reading and pays close attention in the lectures will have all of the knowledge necessary to succeed. Overall great guy, great class. 10/10 recommend.

I enjoyed the class. All the questions in the class come straight from the notes, study them, and you'll do fine on the tests. The teacher is a great guy, he has lots of nice life lessons to teach over the year. Recommend taking this class if you're into finance.
10/10 professor. Easily the best professor I have ever had!

By far the best Professor I have ever had. He teaches in a way that makes you fully understand what you are learning and retain it. His lectures are very interesting and prepare you very well for the tests, so you need to go to them. He is the most accepting and genuine Professor I have ever had in my time here so far. His class is hard so study.

Brau's lectures are amazing. He always includes a spiritual thought and advice about getting jobs. He's one of the few faculty from the south, which, being from the south, I could relate to a lot. He's wicked smart, and while his lectures are fast, he gives plenty of time for questions. 10/10 recommend for ALL students, not just business students.

Absolutely fantastic class. I'm not a business major and I took this class for my minor and it has honestly just helped me understand the economy in general so much better. If you go to class and read the textbook you will most likely understand the concepts he teaches pretty well. I personally very much enjoyed his energy and the overall class.

He teaches fast but it's still easy to understand. The key to success is reading the chapters before class to already have an understanding of the material.. He does take small breaks to include real world advice as well as spiritual thoughts. Tests are fairly hard but if you prepare well using your class notes you'll do fine.

I loved having Bro Brau this semester, he did an amazing job of keeping students engaged. While also providing moments of spiritual discussion. If you're going to take FIN 201, I would recommend that you take it from Bro Brau.

Everybody should take Dr. Brau's class. He's hardcore about finance and knows how to teach it. Lecture was always fun to attend. Your grade is going to be decided completely off your test performance, but his curve is generous. He wants his students to understand finance and be prepared for the world. He gives awesome spiritual thoughts each class.

Dr. Brau is an insanely caring person. He shares so much to uplift his students. The class is mainly graded by tests, but pay attention to his class notes, copy them and study them, and you will do well. PREPARE BEFORE CLASS by reading the material. The course will take a lot of work, and will feel fast at times, but prepare and you will do well.

Bro Brau is an amazing professor. Spiritual thoughts are awesome, class is fun (almost never boring), and he teaches very well. Only thing is that it is hard to know what you don't know because you can't see your scores on any of the homework quizzes but it is what it is. Great class all around though.

Jimmy Brau is the best Professor at BYU. He is slightly crazy, but an amazing teacher. FIN201 is just a hard class in general, but he made it barable. There is no formula sheets for his test, so you actually have to know your stuff -- but if you want to be prepared for the Finance Junior Core --> TAKE IT FROM HIM!
Spiritual thoughts - Perfect!

Prof. Brau has been one of my favorite professors at BYU! I felt that FIN 201 was more difficult than MRKTG 201 or ACC 200, but if you will spend the time to prepare for each class and study the in-class notes, you will do great on the exams and in the course (95% of your grade is exams).

Brau cares about his students and their success! FIN 201 is a hard class but Brau provides all the things you need to do well. Pay attention in class and take good notes, read the textbook chapters before class, and study the way Brau tells you to. Tests are hard but you will do well if you put in the time. Overall, I loved his class!

Professor Brau is an amazing teacher who really cares about his student's spiritual and professional development. His lectures are great, so make sure you show up to all of the classes because the tests are based completely off of class notes. As long as you study the notes you will do well in this course.

As a moderately smart student who works hard to get As, this is a HARD class, but possible to do well in. I was often bewildered by spiritual thoughts and things Brau said in class, but overall he is a good guy. You have to study HARD before even going to class. Your whole grade will be based on 5 tests. I would say take from Brau over other profs.

This class was really good, it is very test-heavy and you have 4 midterms and a final. Tests are based on what is talked about in class so sometimes he can throw in things that aren't covered in the material yet. No electronic notes, they are all on pencil and paper which makes it hard to get everything down or for it to make sense afterward.

Professor Brau gives some of the best spiritual thoughts on campus. He is inspirational and an upstanding person. However, his lectures are confusing and do not facilitate learning. He does not give assignments which help you to engage with the material, so if you are looking to have an engaging learning experience you should look elsewhere.

Brau is the most engaging professor I have ever had. He holds you to a high standard but also teaches at a high level. The tests are very easy as long as you pay attention in class. Most importantly, he genuinely cares for every single one of his students and wants the best for you both in and out of the classroom.

Brau cares about his material and his students SO much. He always answered my questions in class (and usually made fun of me being from Georgia lol). Tests are worth 95% of your grade- so study the notes well!

Professor Brau was an amazing professor. He really cares about his students, and wants us all to succeed in life, not just getting a good grade. The class is fast paced but is totally worth it. He is a really energetic and fun teacher to learn from, and I am glad I have him.

Brau is a great guy with amazing spiritual thoughts and lectures. If you study the notes thoroughly then you will score well on the exams. The only grades in the class are based off of exams. You aren't allowed to see what you missed on the test because "thats how the real world works" which I thought was very frustrating.

Professor Brau is incredible! His high energy and strong personality make for an entertaining time. But his clear expertise, great intelligence, and genuine care for his students stand out even more. His teaching was fast paced, but when I prepared for class by doing the readings and practice problems, it was just the right speed. Great professor!

Prof. Brau is an awesome guy and super funny but he is intense. We fly through material like nothing else and you have to stay on top of it. He does go a little crazy sometimes with the tests and he doesn't let you review your test to know what you missed. But he is a good professor

Brother Brau is very passionate and wants his students to do well on the tests but this class is VERY hard. It is manageable if you go to class, read the textbook and take really good notes. Be prepared to work hard but it will pay off.

Brau is awesome! Loved his class. It can be a little intense at times, but if you take everything in stride and budget enough time for it, Brau will give you all the tools you need to be successful, both in his class and out in the world.

Brau is really passionate about finance. He doesn't let you go over exams to see what you missed which can be hard. The class is very exam heavy. If you love finance, this is the class for you. Overall, he is a nice guy and does want you to succeed. It is definitely a different learning style than most other classes.

Professor Brau held engaging lectures that were very relevant to the world of finance. His lectures not only prepared me well for his tests, but they also gave great insight into the real business world. His tests are daunting but I prepared well and got good grades on all of them.

Professor Brau is the most energetic guy I've ever met in my whole life. While attendance is "not mandatory," you'll want to go to every class, as he makes the tests based entirely off of the notes he makes in class. Read the textbook, and pay attention during lectures. He's an amazing guy, and recommend taking his section.

Amazing professor. He genuinely loves his students and loves what he does. Super funny and super inspirational. He gives the best spiritual thoughts in class. His lectures are intense, but definitely beneficial and helps you learn a ton! Hard class because it is 95% tests but it is 100% doable. Take his class!

Brother Brau is a loving and funny guy! He cares deeply about every student and wants each to do well. He does go pretty fast in the lectures, but it really helps if you do the readings and practice problems in the book before class. Lectures are usually very entertaining because he breaks up the content with spiritual thoughts and stories.
If you attend lecture and know your notes very well, this class will be a breeze. If not, it will be a challenge.

Very passionate about what he does. From a purely educational perspective, I highly reccomend taking classes from him. However, from a more general perspective, he is very out of pocket. He mixes in good advice with gross exaggerations, and is the quintessential "finance bro".

Amazing professor. So kind, loves his students. Grade is 95% exam based (may not work for some). Comes off as tough but really is teaching in a way that prepares you so well for real life. Amazing lectures, so funny and amazing devotionals. Would definitely take again
Good class. I didn't really show up ever and did fine on the tests just reading the textbook. Would recommend showing up to class if you want to get an A though.
The class isn't difficult because he is a bad teacher, it is simply just a very important class with lots of info. Never procrastinate in this class and you will probably do fine.

He is a great professor that is super spiritual but pretty wild at the same time. Make sure to take really good notes during class and you'll do fine on the tests. There is like no homework, but if you read the chapters before class it will make it a lot easier. The only grades are the tests pretty much. I really liked him.
He is an amazing lecturer, but his class is very test heavy and all grades come from midterms and the final. I would strongly recommend if you want engaging lectures and do well testing.
The key to succeeding in this class is thoroughly studying and understanding the notes and drill problems done in class. Understand the concepts and how to apply them to these problems.

Professor Brau is a very energetic teacher that keeps you awake during lectures. He is not the best teacher though. Hard to understand sometimes and I feel like he just doesn't have that teaching knack. Other than that, great guy!

This class is no joke! You seriously must study the notes from class until you have them down perfectly. He says so many of the exam questions straight in lecture. The tests are basically all of your grade so study hard for them! Also don't ever miss class you have to be there to understand everything

Powerful speaker. Almost more uplifting than my religion classes (this is not sarcasm). The course is difficult, but Prof Brau is not. Study the notes you take WITH HIM in class and you'll know what's on the exam. He makes this very clear in lecture. That being said, the material can be very challenging. 10/10 reccomend Prof Brau.
He was an awesome teacher and great person. I really enjoyed his lectures but his test are pretty hard.
He is such a kind man and a great teacher, there are 4 midterms and a final though, all based on things he says in class so GO TO LECTURES. 10/10 teacher, harder class made easier.

Proffesor Brau's class is structured like a complete joke.  he goes 5,000 MPH and he's one of those teachers that trys to trick the student on his test by putting everything NOT in the textbook and drill problems on the test. Everything on the study sheet won't be on the test. another ego-filled PHD teacher takes from someone else.

Good and funny guy. You have to pay $90 for the online textbook. Pretty much ur whole grade is based off of his tests!!! STUDY THE NOTES HARD!! He's a hardcore army guy with crazy energy but that made it fun lol. If you dont attend class ur screwed, dont rely on the textbook. I haven't taken the final yet but I heard its crazy hard.

Good and funny guy. You have to pay $90 for the online textbook. Pretty much ur whole grade is based off of his tests!!! STUDY THE NOTES HARD!! Your grade is almost entirely based on a few midterms and a final. The exams are difficult and mostly based on the lecture. The classes have lots of professional development moments and spiritual thoughts. The TA lab is super helpful in filling in any gaps.
Great teacher, motivated me to get into the finance program. 10/10 recommend.

His classes are so entertaining. Go to class because basically every test question comes from what he writes down on his notes so don't skip. Your grade in the class is what your exam grades are cause there are very few assignments that won't change it really. Do the textbook readings before you go to class!! Everything will make more sense.

Read the book. Go to the lectures. Brau serves more as a guide than an instructor (like any college professor). This is a good section to be in if you're self-motivated and are passionate about finance. My testing strategy was to reread the chapters and lecture notes the night before each midterm. Learning development and spiritual moments - GOOD!

Ridiculously hard class. Brau is a very caring, inspirational guy, but assumes you have the content mastered. Tests were soo difficult for me and are worth 90% of the grade. Lectures are fast and difficult to comprehend even if you think you understand the readings. TAKE ACC200 FIRST!

If you've ever wanted to take a class taught by a summer sales bro, this is your shot. Genuinely baffled at how high his reviews are. The lectures were incomprehensible, the whole class was graded on the tests. "spiritual thoughts" were mostly personal opinions on gospel topics.

Worst professor Ive ever had. Doesn't let you see your test answers or what you got wrong and he doesnt know how to actually teach a class. He also only writes in acronyms and tells you to study the notes but then when you do and people get mad at hi he says its the class' fault.

He said that the online version is so much easier, but that's a lie.The quizzes were easy, but then the test was nothing like the quizzes and book.  There were videos to watch but he said not to trust what they said and just focus on the textbook. So why did you add those? Not very helpful either. Tons of memorization. UGH dropped my gpa! :(

The class was difficult, but following the perscripted study habits from Brau was a sure-fire was to be successful. Lectures are great to become more familiar with material, but outside ready is necessary. He is great at leaving a spiritual impact on you as well.
Amazing class and teacher, but very difficult tests. You'll need to know every detail of what he has covered in class. If you're a poor test-taker, I would not recommend this class.
Professor Brau's class is straightforward. There are no tricks. Everything on the test is covered in class

Brau is a good guy. He brings high energy to the class lectures. The class is what you put into it; because I studied, I found the tests to be fairly easy. The final was a bit hard but I ended up with an A regardless. I would recommend. 

Also, there is no attendance; however, if you do not attend you will likely fail.

James Brau impacted my life more than any other professor I've had. His spiritual thoughts are genuinely moving and he is so passionate about the students as well as finance. This class is 90% based on exams every few weeks but they're not that hard - 30 questions. If you understand the concept of each chapter, you'll do fine. It never felt unfair.
90% of the class is determined by your test grades. If you are not a strong test taker then get ready to study.

Professor Brau is very energetic and passionate about Finance. He has a long history of helping students succeed in Fin201. He has outlined a great roadmap in order to do well on his tests and assignments in FIN201. The class is extremely test heavy with the option to take the final as your final grade.
I was really impressed with Professor Brau. He works really hard to create an effective learning environment. His class is not easy but it is effective.

lectures can be hard to follow and involve tangential stories that while interesting distract from the content. Take notes or you wont pass. Very difficult, wouldn't take again cuz I'm a bad tester. Leaving a good review cuz I got an F in the class after all I did but then he gave everyone a boost which gave me a D so thanks for that!

Brother Brau is amazing! There's essentially no homework, so the tests really count, and they're difficult to pass without doing the reading. If you come to class, take good notes, and do the reading, you'll do great on the tests. Despite having a massive amount of students, Bro Brau is super accessible. His lectures are inspirational and clear.

Brother Brau was amazing. His lectures are crucial to go to. I barely ever did the reading and just did his class based on his lectures/in class notes and did really well. Also super inspirational in his spiritual thoughts. Helped my testimony and knowledge of finance a ton. Love this man.
If you are good at tests this is the class for you.

Professor Brau is great! He is very passionate about finance and about helping his students to succeed. The tests are the majority of your grade but if you study the class notes super well and use the TA lab frequently there is no reason why you shouldn't succeed. Brau provides many resources to help you, it requires work but is definitely doable.

Professor Brau moves fast! If you read the book before class, you'll be able to follow his lectures. Know his notes like the back of your hand and the intuition behind, and you'll be able to pass the midterms and exam. His midterms and test account for 90% of your grade, the other 10% are quizzes you can retake as many times as you want.
4 midterms, TA lab before each is pretty much essential. Lectures are entertaining but definitely not good enough to help you do well on the midterms. Quizzes are super helpful for midterm prep

Brau was awesome! His spiritual thoughts in class were honestly life changing! He is so full of faith and cares for each student despite the class size. Grade is based almost fully off of tests, but if you pay attention in class, take good notes, and use all test prep material he gives you, you will succeed. Seriously such a good professor.

Bro Brau's super funny, cares about his students, and has high expectations. 90% of the grade is tests, so all you have to do is prepare for class (1.5-2.5 hours a week), go to class, take one 20 question quiz/week (which you can resubmit until you get 100%), and do the midterms. Huge fan of him and his spiritual thoughts in class.

Pros
-Dr Brau has great energy and is a solid teacher
-Focuses on real-world applications
-Homework grading is generous

Cons
-Lecture is pointless if you haven't done the reading
-Lectures are important because sometimes test questions are based solely on lecture discussion
-You don't get an equation sheet for the test

Brau is a super entertaining professor. He moves at lightning speed which is okay if you've done the reading before lectures. Whatever is on his notes (which he writes with you in-class) will be on the test. Tests make up most of your grade- 4 midterms (one gets dropped if you do his research surveys) and the final.

Brau deeply cares for his students and their success. This class isn't as hard as it is made out to be. He will prepare you well for exams. Consistently review and take GREAT in-class notes. Final is a bit harder than the midterms. TAs are helpful and available. His mind is all over the place, but lectures are fun and inspiring. Highly recommend!

Jim Brau is an amazing man. I don't know of many professors who care more about their students than he does. His criteria is really clear. He gives amazing spiritual thoughts and is so funny during lecture. He moves really fast in lecture so pay attention. DO THE READING BEFORE CLASS AND STAY CAUGHT UP ON QUIZZES.

Very entertaining, and bounces around a lot so for some may be hard to follow but overall he was very clear in his teaching and expectations. Amazing grading policies dropped worst midterm and other helpful things. Readings and class notes are essential to passing the tests. He also really cares about students' overall success in and out of class.
If you go to class and review your class notes weekly you will ace the exams. Great information in each lecture and great spiritual thoughts each class.

He was entertaining. He lectures and goes through the notes (which you are expected to memorize for the test). Not a super complicated class, 90% of your grade is based on the tests so get an A on the tests and you will have an A in the class.

10/10 would take again. He explained concepts well and had amazing spiritual thoughts.

To do well in the class:
1. Read the textbook before class
2. Commit 8 hours a week to outside study
3. Do the practice problems in the textbook
4. Take good notes in class

Put in basic work = A

But just for the spiritual thoughts I would recommend the class!

I loved Brother Brau!  Such a great person and mentor. Everything about him is BIG, his personality the way he wants to scare you into doing well on the exams and in life. 
I struggled because everything was super exam heavy and there was hardly any extra credit, but then he curved the class 5%. He seriously wants his students to succeed!

Brau is something else. No laptops in class, all handwritten notes and you need to stay focused. The class is based off of your performance on the 4 midterms and the final exam, expect to study an hour a day if you want an A. What is nice is that the exams are based off of the notes in class, study the notes first and foremost, then drill problems.

Professor Brau is very passionate about student development not only in his class but life as well. In the course, most of the grade is based on tests. If you want to succeed, go through the textbook chapters and quizzes at the same rate as the class and study the in-class notes because the tests are entirely based on those.

Brau is absolutely hilarious and gives great spiritual thoughts. Make sure to study the class notes before exams -- if you know them well, you will get an A. The exams and final are worth 90% of your grade. The final is difficult, almost every equation you learn in class is on there. Class is definitely doable, you just have to put in the work.

Good professor, lives up to his word. He will teach you everything that comes up on the test. 
Too many tests (basically one per month plus the final), and you need to know/memorize the formulas (way too many, btw). 
If he took more breaks while explaining the formulas, it would be great. Be ready to rush through topics and problems in class.

Great Prof. He intentionally "puts on a show" every class period to keep everyone entertained the whole lecture. Most of your grade comes from the midterm and finals. The assignments for the unit are all do just before the midterm which helped me learn the material rather than just getting the assignment done. His spiritual thoughts are phenomenal.

His five minute spiritual thoughts are worth more than an hour in any religion class. Pay attention in the lectures. If it's not at least mentioned in the lecture, it won't be on the test. Jim Brau is great. Highly reccomend.

5% curve to everyone at the end of the class, 89% got you an A (1/3 of the class). Study the notes and go over all topic quizzes before each midterm and the final. Keep track of your questions as you go and take them to the (very helpful) TA lab. Boom, A.

There are 4 midterms the lowest gets dropped. The final is comprehensive. Each test is strictly based on memorizing the class notes. Prepare for class by reading the textbook before. I found the TA lab essential to help build intuition behind equations. Brau is very loud and funny, he gives great spiritual thoughts and professional development tips

Dr. Brau cares about the success of his students. He grades almost entirely on exams, but if you study the way he encourages you to, you can succeed. He encourages and teaches personal application of both finance and gospel principles.

I loved this class! I wasn't even too interested in finance yet Professor Brau always made class so enjoyable and engaging. While the class is difficult, he provides you with all the tools you need to succeed. I felt like I left this course with not only an increase in financial knowledge, but a better testimony and desire to work hard.
Make sure to memorize equations! He is super inspirational!
He is really inspirational and I think a good man, but his class was just very hard for me and hard for me to grasp his way of teaching.

Brother Brau is awesome! It is a test heavy class but everything comes from the notes we take in class. MASTER YOUR NOTES!!!! Going to class is very important and so is reading the book! Overall hard class but Brau makes it doable.

Very difficult final, but other than that, Professor Brau was awesome. He gives amazing spiritiual thoughts, He inspires us, and he really knows his stuff. You have to read the text book before going to class, and then practice as much as possible to get a good grade.
Brau is a hommie. The lecture is pretty great amount of contents. You just have to really preview the course and master the concepts. He is loving and spiritual and amazing! Take from him!!

90% of your grade are 4 Midterms/1 Test. 10% quizzes on MyEducator, take as many times as you want. Lectures are you copying down the notes he writes out. He moves fast but posts them to LS after class. You'll find 90% of the test answers on the notes, the other 10% are stretch questions. Understand intuition behind the equations. Nice guy.

The main thing about how he teaches (no slides, just projecting his written notes and examples on the screen) is that you need to come having read from the text (free, online) and have to listen.  He makes sure his notes cover all necessary content for exams, but he'll go too fast for you if you haven't already read the textbook.

Professor Brau is is very clear about what to expect from the course and exams. If you want to do well then I suggest that you put in the effort to do all the readings and consider class attendance as mandatory. If you do so, then it is not difficult to perform well on the tests.

Important to read before class, focus on drill problems and notes to prepare for tests. Overall great professor, cares that you succeed and is willing to help you but definitely follow his advice to prepare for the tests.

This class was not too difficult. However, it is crucial that you are in class for the notes each day. Professor Brau does tend to get off topic during lectures, but overall he sets you up to succeed in his class.

Dr. Brau has been my favorite professor. His spiritual thoughts have greatly impacted me. This exams take a decent amount of studying, but the material you are tested on is made very clear. When he says to master the notes, do it. The TA lab is super helpful for the topic quizzes and any questions on the notes.
Take Bro Brau if you want a good time, and be inspired! The class is really difficult though!

Professor Brau knows finance very well and teaches in a way that is easy to understand. Success in his class is based off of your understanding of the class notes. If you do not attend class or do pre-class readings, you will struggle. I wish we could have had the option to review our midterm exams.

I just didn't identify with his class style. There are other students who love it, but I do not feel like his notes and exercises prepare for the tough questions in the exam like he claims. He gives a lot o material support for the exam, but I honestly didn't feel like any of those truly prepared me for it.

Hardest class I've ever taken in the Marriott School. He includes random details he may have mentioned once in class to trip you up on the tests. He won't let you go over the past tests with TAs to see what you did wrong so there is no way to correct your mistakes and relearn tough material ahead of the comprehensive final.

Grade is test heavy with interesting and inspiring lectures.  He shows you how to take the notes for his class which include the vast majority of all testable material.  He teaches with logic and topics will all connect together by the end of the semester.  Read before class and study his notes and in class problems first.
He is an amazing professor! Although, he expects you to really know the material for the exams which is most of your grade. If you are not a finance major, I may consider picking another professor.

He was very good in incorporating a spiritual thought and professional development into almost every lecture.  Even though its exam heavy, your grade will reflect the effort you put in.  I very much encourage consistent studying before the concepts are covered in class (not just cramming before any one of the exams).

The way he tests is much different than the standard professor. There is no midterm review slides to review, and you pretty much just have to memorize his notes to get an A instead of just using critical thinking skills.

Although I loved Brau, I understand he's not for everyone. 90% of your grade is based on 4 midterms and a final. His tests are tough but not impossible. Everything on the test is from your notes so you just need to study and make sure you understand intuition. His personal development and spiritual thoughts are awesome and he's a great guy!
professor brau was by far one of my favorite professors. his spiritual thoughts always left me leaving class feeling like a better person. i highly recommend taking a class from him.
Test are focus on notes not textbook
His tests aren't very hard, but he isnt a very good teacher. So I guess it evens out

Brau is a great teacher! His lectures are engaging because he moves very quickly. Come to class prepared or you'll most likely be confused. There's a lot of work outside of class required to do well in the class. It's a hard class, but also fun!

I had to retake this course and the way that Professor Brau teaches really works! He was my 2nd class of four, and I always went away with enough energy to finish off the day. He is extremely spiritual and always makes time for a prayer and thought. No phones in class, but 110% worth taking!!
Good teacher, hard tests

James Brau is an amazing person and you will definitely have the full BYU experience in that class from intellectually hard to spiritual growth. When it comes to his teaching I think he an okay teacher but you need to study the class notes a TON at home, do drill problems, and talk to the TAs a lot to succeed. Its a very hard class but a good one.

Overall, Brau was a good teacher. I personally did not like the way the class was conducted. To give him the benefit of the doubt, he has 800-900 students at a time. Didn't like the amount of Exams as well as the pacing of having a midterm a week before FINALS WEEK. Also doesn't encourage actually knowing the material. Rather memorizing notes

Tests are the majority of the grade. TA's review materials on Fridays don't really help prepare you for the test.  The most difficult thing for me is that you copy his notes the whole class and he says, "Remember this!"  It does not feel as organized as other Business classes I have taken.  I guess that is the benefit of being a tenured professor.

Professor Brau is very personable and makes the class very engaging. I appreciated that he made us learn for ourselves. You will only get an A if you work really hard and study. Make sure that you are extremely familiar with his notes and that you memorize the equations so that you can do well on the tests, which are worth 65% of your grade!

Professor Brau is very personable and makes the class very engaging. I appreciated that he made us learn for ourselves. You will only get an A if you work really hard and study. Make sure that you are extremely familiar with his notes and that you memorize the equations so that you can do well on the tests, which are worth 65% of your grade!

Brother Brau is such a passionate and spiritual guy. His class is very fast-paced and rigorous, but not impossible. If you keep up with the readings and actually work-out and understand all of the quiz problems you will do just fine. His final is cumulative, but it surprised me because it wasn't all to terrible.
brau should change his name to brags. he is extremely arrogant. he is a munch too.

Pros:
-Amazing spiritual thoughts
-Real life application
-High energy
-Cares deeply that students succeed
-Drops one exam
-Often says what will be on each exam

Cons:
-Grade comes purely from exams
-Course moves quickly through material (hard to keep up)
-Lecture and book don't always match
Brau was a positive and energetic teacher. My only complaint is he would pull random and obscure things he may or may not have said in class and put them on the test and expect you to know them.

Has an intense personality but is also genuine and caring. Your grade is mostly (like 90%) from the 4 exams and the final, so make sure you are good at taking tests. His lectures are handwritten notes on a projector. His handwriting is often difficult to read and has a lot of abbreviations, so make sure to pay attention and write quickly.
Loved his spiritual and real life insights. There was a lot of tests, but I'm glad I took his class.
Lots of tests, lots of study time required. Your entire grade is essentially the average of your test scores. If you do well in those you will be fine.
Your grade is SUPER reliant on your exam scores, so study hard for those. Attend every class and take good notes in class. His lectures can also be really confusing, so prepare before class as well.

Professor Brau is by far my favorite professor at BYU. His class is tough yes, but he cares so much for his students and gives every opportunity for success. It's critical that you attend class if you want to succeed in his FIN 201 class.
His tests are unnecessarily hard. He is so intense. But I did like his spiritual thoughts.

People say his tests are impossible but they really are pretty easy. If you study the notes and know the intuition, you should at least get a 90% on every test. A lot of students blindly memorize his notes and get destroyed on the tests. If you have a hard time reading his notes, go into the TA's and they can interpret them for you.

If you apply yourself and work with others, you'll be fine in this class. Brother Brau not only teaches finance, but spiritual lessons that will change your life. Just thanks to that I would take his class again.

This class was really hard! Professor Brau is a really cool guy and you can tell that he really cares about his students. The tests are on the notes from class but there aren't really practice problems which was really hard for my learning style. He is a good teacher and really knows his stuff.

The only way to be successful in this class is to attend every lecture and copy the notes exactly as he writes them. He does keep his lectures entertaining with spiritual thoughts and professional development but you have to pay attention and cant talk or be on your phone/computer or you will get yelled at in front of everyone.

James Brau is the king of good lectures. Everything in the class is well explained during lecture and every test is based on what you learn in lecture, nothing more. He is also hilarious and entertaining, and his messages are inspirational and create self-reflection. He is awesome! Makes a difficult course more enticing.

Brau is an intense guy, but honestly one of the best individuals you can find on BYU campus. I am a last minute crammer type of student so this class was like impossible for me. If you are disciplined and can be consistent throughout the semester then you will thrive.

Does his best to help you learn with physical note taking, but even though I rarely missed, I never knew how to study them, which meant I failed every test. Leaving this class feeling dumber than when I started. He has a hard personality, I left class feeling upset multiple times. I hope I pass bc I honestly never want to take this class again.

I am a senior and this is the hardest class I have ever taken. Brau goes so fast and his notes make no sense and are illegible. I have read every single page of the textbook, taken all the practices quizzes and still do poorly on tests. He says "just memorize your notes" but that doesn't work if the notes make no sense...

Brau is such a difficult teacher. I have never been much of a test taker and it was hard for me to know what was on the test. Bray always says to look at the notes and study them and youre guaranteed a 90%, this is not the case. No matter what I did or how many quizets I made I could never get a good score on the midterms and ultimately the final.

Brother Brau is a great person and teacher. He really cares about his students and he gives amazing spiritual thoughts.  Pretty much the entire grade is based on tests and quizzes, but if you know the notes you will be fine. He teaches clearly and will tell you what is on the test if you listen carefully.

Brau might be my favorite professor at BYU. He gives you everything you need to be successful in the class plus he's funny and has a spiritual thought every lecture.  10/10 would take one of his classes again.

His class was great. He is a great guy. This class is pretty much all tests, so if you are not a good test taker, maybe not the best professor to take it from. I was very inspired by some of his stories and thoughts. Overall, I enjoyed the class!

Brau does not teach the material. You have to teach the material to yourself and then he adds details in class.  I loved his personal finance section but other than that maybe take this class from someone else unless you have no choice.

Good finance teacher, with clear lectures that are extremely tied to the tests. Lots of times his lectures are pretty interesting, but sometimes he goes on rants and makes you feel like majoring in finance is the only way to be successful in life and hates on the accounting program.

I've always looked forward to Brau's lectures and didn't expect to feel the spirit so strongly in a finance class. 

Things to note:
- Lectures aren't mandatory BUT there will be stuff covered in class that isn't in the textbook
- Brau handwrites everything. It can be hard to read his handwriting
- No formula sheet = memorization = easier exam

Brother Brau is a great guy, genuine, and high energy. Teaching style might not be for everyone. I don't think class time was organized well, each class had 15-20 mins of filler stuff, such as spiritual thoughts (which I did like), "professional development" moments, and random stories. We could have learned a bit more with less filler stuff.

Very bubbly personality, fun stories, and helps make the material meaningful and engaging. Test question often relate very directly to specific things he mentions in class, so to do well class it is crucial that you take detailed, organized notes and attend every lecture.

Great guy who knows his stuff. He has a unique teaching style but you learn a lot if you follow what he tells you to do. His class is hard, but if you want super easy classes all the time you're probably missing the point of school. Would take him again!

Prof. Brau was amazing. Loved every one of his lecture. Study the class notes really well and you'll get a high grade. Those people who complain this class was hard is mostly because either they didn't read the textbook, didn't do the practice problems, or didn't pay attention to class (or procrastinated all) which is the case with so many students

Professor Brau is definitely a great professor if you like his style. I slacked and didn't do as well as I would've liked, but I can say that he really does provide all the resources you need to do well. You just have to apply yourself.

Brau was great. His lectures are super interesting and easy to follow along. The notes are the most important part of the class. Very little homework, Tests are everything in his class. Memorizing the notes is the biggest part of success in his class.
He's a very engaging lecturer and does a good job teaching tough financial principles. The class is manageable but very test heavy and can be difficult to do well in unless you test very well.

I took ECON 110 and it was easier than this class. It's important to memorize the notes. If you have any questions about the reading, ask the TA's or look it up yourself. He will most likely not see you raise your hand, so be sure to yell when you have a question. He is an awesome dude when you get to know him personally, but teaching a bad subject

He is a brash personality but he is also really good about helping you think in the mindset of how to be a professional now. His big personality definitely keeps you engaged. Whether you like him or not, the class is based off of how well you know and can apply the class notes-that's the key. Takes a lot of work to do well but it is possible.

Read the textbook before class or you'll be lost. Study for the tests the way he says and you'll succeed. He's a great lecturer, but I struggled with him as a person, so make sure you can handle his personality, which is energetic and devoted. His good advice is littered with virtue-signaling, and he'll often make statements that aren't true.
Good Professor. If you're going into accounting, be prepared to get roasted a bit. Funny guy, keeps it engaging.

He is a great professor and cares a lot about the success of his students. The class is hard and does require a lot of time. Always read the textbook before class. Regardless of if it's talked about in class having a basic understanding of the concepts beforehand is extremely helpful. LISTEN TO HIS ADVICE FOR THE TESTS.

As many reviews state Professor Brau is very passionate and shares many life lessons. The class is extremely test heavy and the tests can sometimes be difficult to study for as everything comes from class. So, reading the textbook sometimes feels pointless unless it's talked about in class. The notes aren't very legible and things class goes fast.

The online textbook is essential to read to do anywhere near well in this class but dont rely on the practice problems since they are very different than the tests. He likes to focus on a lot of the vocab of the chapters and knowing all the terms and ways things work rather than the actual full in-depth problems. Make sure to study the right stuff.

Brau was an awesome professor. His lectures were amazing and always very entertaining. Do be warned, the lectures were fast-paced and sometimes tough to follow. He also gave great spiritual thoughts and shared great professional development thoughts. I would recommend Fin 201 with Brau over anyone else.

If you are going to take FIN 201, only take it from Dr. Brau. I was initially taking FIN 201 from Dr. Holmes and had a terrible experience. I withdrew from Dr. Holmes class and decided that I'd take the class from Dr. Brau the next year. This was the best decision I made. Dr. Brau delivers incredible lectures and prepares you for the real world.
Super nice guy and cares a lot about the students. Have to put in a good amount of work to get decent grades on the midterm exams and final.

Professor Brau gets a pretty bad rap for the speed of the course and his illegible handwriting. While I admit the course was fast paced, it was certainly not as bad as people say. If you show up and take good notes and study well you can easily pass this course. It is a challenging course and I would recommend taking it with a light semester load.

For some, he is a great - if  you already enjoy finance. He acts like we should already perfectly know a lot of the principles. Definitely take this class in a less busy semester. The reading takes a lot of time if you want to do it right. He was discouraging and says a lot of things that are not true (we would fact check his stats in class).

He was really fun and good in class and I learned a lot of life lessons. However, in class he shows you everything by taking notes and sometimes they're hard to read. Read the book to learn things because class won't do it all for you, I guess that's all of college though.

Brother Brau is awesome! Take fin 201 from him if you want to be uplifted every class. He tells you exactly how to get an A on the tests and it works. He also doesn't try to trick you on tests which make up most of the grade. I got As on the first 2 tests, and then lost motivation which describes the B grade, but it is possible to get an A.
Brau is probably the best option for FIN 201. His lectures are engaging. Just write down everything he says and memorize it for the tests. Be prepared to study, its not easy material for most people.

He does all lectures through hand written notes projected on the screen that are often illegible and written very quickly. Make sure to read the textbook before class and attend TA lab because he often doesn't really teach how to do it, just briefly covers the topic without applying it. Tests are straightforward, closed notes with no formula sheet.
Bro. Brau is amazing! He really cares about his students which is impressive considering he has a huge class. This class is mainly test so if you are good at taking test this is the class for you.

Loved learning about finance from Brau! If you master the notes he gives in class, the tests are very manageable. I also appreciated that he sprinkled in so much practical financial advice in his lectures.

Brau teaches fast-pace lectures and expects that you've read the book before class. Definitely test heavy, but you can drop one of the four midterms scores by taking three research surveys. Most test questions are taken directly from the notes. He splits up the lectures with professional development and powerful spiritual thoughts.

I loved this class and Professor Brau! He was so inspirational and gave the most powerful spiritual thoughts. It definitely was not easy, but if you put the work into the material and don't procrastinate you'll do fine. Brau is an amazing person and I highly recommend his class! The material covered is very applicable to real life.

Really you just need to understand the book & do the practice questions in there. Study the notes for the qualitative test questions. He's a nice guy, though says we can meet him at the gym while he works out, which I think is wildly inappropriate, especially for female students. Have an A- with 100 on every quiz, midterms I got 90, 93, and 90

I think this professor is super entertaining and funny. He makes learning the principles pretty accessible and easy. The wording on some of the test probelms was a bit confusing at times and you have to do extremely well on the tests to get an A which is hard.

Professor Brau is a good professor, and loves the content that he teaches. His lectures are fast paced, probably faster than I would prefer. It is a test heavy class so you just have to devote your life to studying his notes and practicing drill problems if you want a good grade in the class.
Great Professor. I loved how he would cut the fluff and prepare you for his exams. If you come to class and do what he asks you will do very well and learn so much. 10/10 would recommend.

I do not like finance at all, just isn't my thing. But this was my favorite class this semester because of Brau. It's hard, especially if finance isn't your thing. You have to read the text beforehand because he moves quickly. But his class changed my life because of who he is as a person and his stories. Loved him! Still don't love finance.

Brau was an awesome choice for a finance professor. You have to be good about studying and doing the reading before class, but it's very possible to get a good grade. Make sure to take good notes. Brau is great about answering questions and is a great all around guy.
Professor Brau is a great teacher, especially for finance being a very large class. The class is very test heavy and requires many hours of studying the notes and drill problems.

Prof. Brau is very clear about what will be on the tests. While the tests are weighted very heavily, you will be prepared if you study like he tells you to. He does a spiritual thought and professional development in each class period, which were always very helpful and I appreciated his advice.

I liked Brother Brau as a person, but I thought that he wasn't a very good teacher... he was super entertaining and made class fun but I thought that he was really unclear in the lectures and didn't adquately teach the material that was on the midterms like he said he would- he honestly kind of felt all over the place. I recommend another teacher.

This class is a lot of work, so don't take it with a heavy load. Prof Brau is a super awesome guy and his lectures are actually so much fun to watch. He also has the best spiritual thoughts. The class is super organized, and everything he teaches comes from the notes. The notes have A LOT of content, though, so study hard.

He is a really good guy but I did not resonate with his teaching style of spitting out information that you have to copy down. The good thing is practically everything taught in class (minus some reading stuff) is on the tests, so you will be solid if you have the notes down. I didn't enjoy this class a ton, but it is manageable.

Solid professor, he gives you all the tools to do well in his class. If you take good notes and study those notes, you'll do well. The tests are difficult if you aren't prepared but they are also very fair.

Brau is a great professor and is very passionate about finance, which makes learning from him easier. He is very fast paced, but there are a lot of TAs that are willing to help. He also shares spiritual thoughts and keeps his students up to date on current events in the business world.
