Bro Brau is a great guy. I always looked forward to the daily spiritual thought every class. Bro Brau is clear in what he expects and if you read the textbook before each class period and do all the suggested and additional problems, you'll be well-prepared for the tests. The trick is just to stay on top of it because you go fast through it all.

This class is only graded on quizzes, four exams, and a cumulative final. The lectures go fast and are sometimes difficult to follow. The textbook readings are super helpful. Do the readings and practice questions in the textbook before class. If you love tests and not having regular homework assignments, this is the class for you!

I didn't like Professor Brau's style of teaching where he would copy down notes in 1st grade handwriting each class without explanation, and I felt like I learned a lot more from the textbook, so I mostly skipped class and did the reading instead. I wouldn't recommend this, though, because every test had questions that he only mentioned in lecture.

Super awesome guy and his lectures were super entertaining. But it was just hard for me to feel like I was getting enough out of class because it was such a massive section. I felt like between reading the books and going to class I still didn't know enough to do well on the tests, so I had to join TA labs in order to know what I was doing and why

Overall, great professor and great class. Flies through the notes but teaches clearly and expectations are very clear for the class. Study your notes, do the practice problems, and read the book and you'll be fine. Spiritual thoughts were something I always looked forward to in class. Tough class and requires lots of studying but would recommend.

He is so awesome. He cares about his students and gives students all the information they need to know to succeed in his class. He handwrites all of his notes and you copy what he writes. This is not always the most effective because his handwriting is hard to read. Otherwise, he is one of the best professors I've ever had.

Brau is a great professor. FIN 201 is just a tough class to teach. It is only offered in massive class sizes and you need to be in class to get info thats needed for his exams. All your one on one learning is done through TA lab so don't skimp on it. This is required for business majors, good luck to everyone taking it.

Professor Brau was a great teacher, but difficult for some people.  Your grade is made of 4 tests and a final with 94% being an A. I felt the Spirit more in his class with his spiritual thoughts than my religion classes. If you use the TAs and put in the work you can do well. If you do the practice problems and memorize his notes you'll do well.

Professor Brau was good. I wouldn't say he was my favorite. He's kind of intense and for sure a big personality but entertaining. I would suggest taking him compared to other Fin 201 professors. Lots of exams.

Brau is a great guy, I enjoyed his lectures a lot. Gives really powerful spiritual thoughts. Class is pretty tough if you want an A, your grade is nearly completely test based. If you do readings before class, and never get behind you will be ok. Know everything on the in class notes before test, which is sometimes a little different from textbook.

Bro. Brau gives a spiritual thought in the middle of every lecture--by far the most spiritual class I've taken at BYU, including religion classes. The content is pretty difficult and test questions can be tricky, you have to memorize the notes. I used the practice exams a lot to study, which was honestly more helpful than anything else.

He's energetic and fun. He will require you to pay $100 for access to the course quizzes that you must take to get credit for the course. I did not like his teaching style, and he made remarks that were hurtful and specifically targeted towards my job and my coworkers. He's not a bad man, and it isn't a bad class. Just be sure you want to be there.
Great professor for a tough class. If you simply do what he says, study how he recommends, and read the textbook this will be a great class.

Brau is an amazing person and loves teaching and loves his students. He taught very fast for me and it was often confusing. Read the chapter before class, study notes from class, and pay attention to what he says and should be fine on the tests. Tests are worth 90% of grade.

Very spiritually uplifting and practical advice. However, the tests are very difficult and based almost solely on the lectures. Make sure you are reading and learning the material be fore you go to class, or you'll be lost the entire class. 90% of your grade is tests and there are 4 tests before the final. Make sure you stay on top of the material

Professor Brau is a great professor! He is a very encouraging and an inspirational professor. He cares a lot about his students and wants to prepare them for living and working in the real world. His tests are very lecture based, so knowing and understanding what is taught in class is key to doing well on exams.

Brau was awesome, he really helped us prepare for his tests, and he taught the material well. You'll worry about the abbreviations in the notes but just make sure you ask him to explain them well. Besides that, he was super nice and helpful for the tests.

It's a fair class and if you put in the work you can get the grade you want. My issue was the way he handled himself. He blew up for 5 minutes yelling at 2 students for talking in class and making them and the whole class feel very uncomfortable. In his rage, he said he is "tenured" and what we say about him doesn't matter. Bit of a Power complex.

I loved professor Brau! Finance 201 is a difficult class for most people, regardless of the professor. I think Professor Brau was great at keeping students engaged during lecture. His class is heavily based on tests. Studying Brau's notes is the best way to do well!
Great professor, super knowledgeable in the world of finance. Lectures were interesting and life changing.

Brau is a rad teacher to say the least, his energy is higher than any other teacher I've ever had. Which is sometimes good sometimes bad. He really loves finance which also can be really good or bad. If Finance is something you want to pursue this is the right class if not I would take it from another teacher.

I really like Brau. He is super fun and he makes the class very enjoyable. Never fell asleep. The tests are just super hard and the concepts are confusing so get ready to spend a lot of time in the TA lab and studying crazy hard for the tests.

Professor Brau is very fun and energetic! His spiritual thoughts are inspiring and my favorite part of class. However, I didn't love how his spiritual thoughts and other tangents took up a lot of class time. When it was time do to finance practice problems, we had like 5 minutes left of class. A lot of the harder concepts I had to teach myself.
He is awesome and passionate. But he goes so fast and sometimes is confusing as he teaches.

He is a good professor although, he may not be everyone's style. His classes are fast paced and his handwriting at times can be a little hard to read. But at the end of the day, I can tell that he really cares about making students ready and he knows his stuff.

I was never bored in class and he teaches really well. The only thing is he teaches really fast so if you like a fast paced teaching style he is your guy. Also all the tests are based on the notes so take good notes. Copy down what he puts but add extra so you understand what is happening later.

Make a quizlet for the notes and you will get an A on the test. Write down everything he says and study it! 
I loved this class, it was a beautiful blend of spiritual and practical. Learned more about life than Finance (but still lots of Finance).
Bro Brau is a solid professor. He moves through the material pretty quickly but if you go to all the lectures and study the notes you will do well.

Finance is not a new topic for me so I thought this class was pretty easy. In order to prepare for the tests do the practice exams. The practice exams are a little harder than the drill problems and in class problems and will definitely help you do good on the exams. I'll stress it again, do the practice exams in preparation for the exams.

Didn't love Professor Brau or how he taught. I know a lot of people like him but he was not for me. He insisted that his questions were not trick questions and that they were taken straight from the notes but there were always little details that he would throw into questions and I always feel like I was falling into traps he would set in tests.

Class is easy. Brau told us exactly what we needed to know for the exams so if you studied that then you got an A. This is another one of those classes where business majors expect everything to be given to them so when they need to slightly work for something it's the hardest thing they've ever done. Sometimes I'm ashamed to be a business major.

Professor Brau is great, I have a lot of respect for him, but for my preferred style of learning it wasn't great. I am typically an A/B student, but in this class I have worried about passing. Concepts are difficult which is not a reflection on Brau, but he goes through the material quickly and his writing can be difficult to read.

Here's what I wish I knew before: Your grade is weighted at 90% tests, 10% homework, and he has raised the grade scale so 94% is an A. So even though I have gotten an average of 90% on all the tests, I'm probably stuck with a B+. It's REALLY hard. He's also an ally, SO caring, and you can guarantee you'll be spiritually enriched from his class.

Bro Brau is an intense guy. Deep down he is a softy, but this crash course forces you to study super hard. He wants all of his students to succeed, but your success is going to be between you, the book, the lectures, and the TA lab. Never a boring class, though.

Good class where you honestly learn a lot. He's a cool guy with really cool spiritual thoughts every class. Only downsides, you can't go over tests even though the final is cumulative which makes it hard to know the gaps in your knowledge. Also you HAVE to do well on tests. I got 2 93s and 2 90s and it still says I need a 94 on the final for an A.

At first Brau and his class are very intimidating and I was not excited for it. After the first test I felt like the environment lightened up and it was easier to follow how he taught. Really follow what he suggests for how to study for the tests and get help from TA's - they really help you understand better intuition - and you'll be fine.
Okay Fin201 is a hard class but Bro Brau makes it so interesting. His tests are very much based off his lectures. Put in daily consistent effort and you'll do great, if not you'll pay the price

literally my favorite class/ make two changes

1. Record your lectures, or VERY LEAST a recording of you explaining your notes. 
2.try using slides instead of writing notes. It will keep you on track, and make your notes less confusing. most students spend all their mental RAM writing instead of understanding what you're saying.

I've had a hard time with this class. Brau's teaching style didn't really work for me. He moves quickly through the notes and doesn't give very much time for problem solving. I put in a lot of time and effort into this class, and I don't think that will reflect in my grade. Brau is a great person, and he genuinely cares about his students.

Brau is a great professor and really cares about his students. He makes it seem like the class is going to be more difficult than it is but if you read the textbook and attend class you will do good. He can sometimes seem all over the place but he was super easy to stay focused on.

Professor Brau expects you to learn finance, and he covers a ton of information really fast. If you come prepared to lectures, you'll generally be able to keep up. Exams are 100% based on class and his class notes. Very doable if you come prepared. He's hilarious and you'll never have another professor like him. Spiritual thought every class.

Honestly, Bro Brau is an amazing human being. His spiritual thoughts made me want to be a better man! That being said, the way he teaches was definitely not for me. I felt like all we did was memorization, so I have a ton of equations in my head and I have absolutely no idea how to implement them for test questions.
His tests come straight from the notes, so as long as you go to class and study the notes you will be fine.

Attendance is not mandatory writes down notes and swears test answers are in the notes. Talks very fast and quickly through material if you have a question/confused forget about class helping. No exceptions are made to take a test at a different time even if a family member dies and you have to attend their funeral. Tough class and requires work

This is a difficult class but it is fair. Brau is extremely clear about how to succeed in the class I have never had a professor do in-depth spiritual thoughts in class every day. Brau's testimony is one of the best takeaways from the class. I loved his teaching still because of how fast and animated he is. Definitely one of the greats here at BYU.

Brau has high energy and cares for our actual lives and where we are going. His spiritual thoughts are amazing and grew my testimony. There is a moderate amount of reading in the book but mostly the lectures are what he tests on. He tells you specifically what he tests on and if you MEMORIZE your notes you'll do great!

I really enjoyed Bro Brau's teaching style. Prepare to study the notes really well and be in class every period. Great speaker, really funny, and always does a spiritual thought and a professional development moment. Definitely not an easy class, and the majority of your grades are the test,  but overall a great professor.

Bro Brau is a great professor, but not right for everyone. His exams are very difficult, but passable with enough effort. It's important to not miss lectures as lots of exam content comes from his lectures. There's 4 exams, plus the final, so this class is not one to take if you're very busy. Fin 201 is worthwhile and teaches a lot of good skills.

I absolutely loved this class. Bro. Brau is awesome and the material is very interesting. The key to success in this class is to read the textbook before class, make sure you understand it, go to class, take some notes, and then you'll do great! It's not that hard if you put some actual effort into it. 

Make some good friends in the class too!
Bro Brau was a really great guy and I loved his spiritual thoughts, but his lectures were a little bit confusing. Overall, I would take the class again, but wish his notes were more clear in class

He goes really fast through the material in class, and basically expects you to teach yourself from the notes and the book. Homework is basically nothing in the grade, just 4 tests and the final. He does let you drop one midterm however. Tests are hard, but if you study the notes, book, and do practice problems you will do fine on them.

Brau is one of the greatest people I have been fortunate enough to meet in college. Tests are tough and worth a lot of the grade, but he gives you all the resources needed and then some. Bad grades can only be blamed on yourself not him

This is one of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU. It is very challenging and test heavy but if you READ THE CHAPTER BEFORE CLASS you'll be fine! There are tons of TA's to help with homework problems and concept understanding. Lectures are incredible, hilarious, and inspiring. His daily spiritual thoughts are unmatched!

He breaks up his lectures with either a spiritual thought or a professional development moment so you don't get bored during class. If you study his notes you will do well on the test. Most of your grade is based on tests but you can get one midterm dropped. Overall, I would recommend this class from Professor Brau.

I loved taking FIN 201 with Prof Brau. I really enjoyed this class and I learned a ton. That being said, this class is HARD. I found the material fairly intuitive and understandable, but the grading curve is steep. Prepare to work hard and study a lot to get a good grade on the tests. That being said, he drops your lowest midterm which helps a ton.
Loved Dr Brau. Really great guy and super cool. Pretty hard tests, but do-able if you study the material
He is really intense but teaches very clearly. If you enjoy having a really engaging lecture then you should take him. Also he drops your lowest test score so he has a bit of mercy

One of my favorite teachers I've had at BYU! Class is copying his notes as he writes and explains (no phones or laptops), super conducive to learning and he is a great lecturer. Amazing spiritual thoughts and professional development. Tests are hard and content is hard but he goes from the notes. You can drop 1 of 4 midterms. Would take again.
Awesome teacher. Brother Brau gives some of the best spiritual thoughts I've had in a college class. The class is pretty test heavy, but if you study the notes and practice problems you will do well.

Brau's class is graded almost exclusively on the four midterms and final exam. If you just study the textbook, you'll get 70-80% on each of the exams. It's necessary to study the in-class notes, there are quite a few exam questions based on in-class discussion. His notes are disorganized and hard to follow but he's a fantastic lecturer.

I've known students who didn't like professor Brau but I really liked him. We are both from the south and so I immediately understood his teaching style; which I will warn you, is very different from many of the professors here at BYU. Your grade is entirely based on the tests but if you go to the TA lab often, you will do fine.

Bro Brau is awesome. He includes professional development moments and spiritual thoughts in each class.
His tests are hard if you don't study. 1. GO TO CLASS and study the notes he writes out with you. 2. Read the textbook. 3. Do the drill problems to prep for the test. 4. Go to TA lab.
Professor Brau tells you everything you need to know. As long as you show up to lecture and take notes you are golden.

Brother Brau is a great lecturer. He breaks up lectures with a spiritual thought and a "professional development" moment. Grading criteria is clear and fair, and it's a reasonable amount of work as well: 4 midterms, but the only homework assignments are three online quizzes due the night before each midterm that each have infinite attempts.

This class isn't nearly as difficult as people make it out to be. Your lowest test score gets dropped if you do his research surveys, and the tests (total=4+final) are not overly difficult to get solid scores on. That being said, REVIEW QUIZ QUESTIONS and textbook. He'll tell you to just master the notes, but that is not enough. Very fast lecture.

Brau is a super dope and funny guy but his teaching style was pretty tough for me. It is just him going all over the place for an hour and a half. If you really study the notes and go over every detail in the book, you'll do well on the tests.

Simply put, Brad has been the best professor. He gives each student everything they need to succeed. That being said, this class is not easy, especially if you want a good grade. Read the textbook, go to class, study the notes, and you'll be fine. I will miss this class as Brau had the best professional dev and spiritual thoughts I have ever heard

Professor Brau is awesome! His spiritual thoughts are better than most religion professors! He did a great job of explaining the concepts that we were learning. The exams are a very large portion of the grade, but if you study extra hard and know the material, you'll do well on them. I would 100% take Professor Brau again!

Brau is the type of professor who claims everything is "intuitive" and easy but then proceeds to give the most difficult exams. Lectures are all over the place and 90% of the time he is on a soapbox talking about irrelevant things. If I wasn't desperate to graduate this semester, I would have dropped his class.
Great professor! Awesome spiritual thoughts. Know the notes and you'll do fine.

I would take this class from Brau again because he's energetic and lectures are fun, but wish I had considered other finance professors. I wanted to coast through this class in my last semester (non-finance major) but that's not possible. Must attend class to understand, no formula sheet for tests, lectures and textbook aren't aligned well.
Professor Brau teaches this class very fast-paced. If you do the readings then you'll always be ready. Notes are crucial for his class. his spiritual thoughts are 10/10.

This class is very heavy with tests but his notes that you take in class are 90% of the test. I never read the textbook and only studied his notes from class and it worked pretty good. He does very really moving spiritual messages every day

Professor Brau is one of the most caring professors/faculty that I have encountered at BYU. He makes sure that he is available to all of his students and is there for each of them if they need him and genuinely cares about each one. His class is very difficult, and if you don't prepare well for each class, you will be completely lost in lecture.

Overall, I think that he is a good teach but the class is very fast paced. If your are not willing to put in the work to be prepared for class you will not do well in this class. The tests are not too bad if you are familiar with the textbook, but most of the information on the test comes from things specifically talked about in the lectures.

The material is only slightly difficult, but I had such a hard time with the way Prof. Brau taught. He has really great spiritual thoughts, but his notes on the actual material are pretty illegible. My advice, learn it on your own first (from the internet or a friend), and treat his class as a review. Otherwise, you'll be so lost.

very entertaining and enthusiastic teacher. The class is very structured and organized and moves at a fast pace. Only thing that was hard for me was his style of note taking. His handwriting can be hard to read and because he moves so quickly, it is very easy to get lost in his notes which are extremely helpful in studying for the tests.

Professor Brau has a lot of energy and teaches well. The hardest thing about it was the speed and intensity of the lectures and the course. It is very test heavy so performing well on each test is crucial to get a good grade.

I loved attending the lectures as I think that he is a very entertaining person. However, he does not teach concepts super clearly (at least for me) so you must put in a lot of time on your own to actually understand the material enough to do well on the exams.

Professor Brau was amazing! The class is hard, but it's manageable. There are 4 tests plus the final. He is high energy and keeps class interesting. It always goes by quickly. He gives the BEST spiritual thoughts. He informs the class of professional development opportunities. He genuinely cares about his students and is always there to help out.

Brau is a great professor! He is an engaging lecturer. I especially appreciated his personal finance chapter. Only thing to beware of with taking this class is how your grade is heavily weighted by midterms.

90% of your grade comes from four mid terms and one final. 10% from quizzes. 
Pros: Brau knows his stuff, lots of TA hours, lots of practice problems to work
Cons: Brau moves very quickly through material, no formula sheet for exams

Professor Brau is the man! The class was solid but if you do take all the notes you will be just fine. I think the most part is that  professor  goes in really fast pace. However it is a total doable class

Professor Brau is military, so his lectures are intense; it often felt like a drill Sargent was yelling at me for 75 minutes. There were a lot of guys who loved him, but I wish I had transferred to a different professor. Brau's teaching style just wasn't for me.

Bro B is awesome, he really cares about his students. If I could, I would have taken this class earlier in my college career when I was in more easy classes. If you want a good grade in this class you have to put a good amount of time towards it. I wouldn't have wanted to take finance from anyone else.

Lots of material. Very fast pace. TA lab VERY helpful. Brau/lectures are entertaining. Exams VERY stressful if you care about grades.

Got 100% on two midterms...had to spend a LOT of time going over the notes. Did best on the tests where I completed all the practice exams (helps get from A- to A on exams).

Valuable class. Glad to be done though!!

Seriously one of my favorite classes I have ever taken and Professor Brau is a big reason for that!  It's a tough course with a lot of material, but if you do the readings, take class notes and study from them as instructed, you are fully prepared for the tests.  He also was really helpful with job finding advice and spiritually uplifting messages.

Brother Brau is a great lecturer and teacher. He is engaging and inspiring in class and his tests are straightforward. If you listen to what he says and how you should study, you will do well on the exams. He has been my favorite teacher at BYU.

Brother Brau is my favorite professor at BYU so far. His lectures are so entertaining and engaging and his tests are straight forward. As long as you do the homework, read the textbook, and attend lecture, you will be prepared to succeed in FIN201.
Enjoyed the lectures, but definitely not my teaching style. The class felt very unorganized as opposed to Accounting 200. I would take a different professor if you liked how that class was set up.

Brau is an effective teacher, and really good at coordinating TAs. Definitely plan weekly time to visit TA lab. And all the grades come from the tests. Really interesting teaching style tho. Doesn't include a formula sheet for tests and other profs do, so keep that in mind. I really enjoyed the lectures, he sets you but for real-life sucess.
Brau is a great thinker and super engaging. He's just a youth pastor that happens to teach finance during his sermons.

He cares about his student and always includes a spiritual thought in his classes. He is kind and caring and you can tell he wants his students to succeed in life. He does talk a little fast in lectures, but him and the TAs are always there to help. He is really funny and works hard for his students. Great guy to get to know and network with.
Come to class everyday and follow along with the notes and you will be fine. Bro Brau tells you everything you need to know for the test. He is also a very energetic and fun professor to have.

The class is 90% tests and 10% homework. 
Do the reading before class, take notes in class, study from notes posted on learningsuite, ignore the practice tests and you'll do great

Bro Brau gives you everything you need to succeed. His spiritual thoughts are great, and you can tell he really cares. The concepts can be difficult but STUDY THE LECTURES!! If you understand his lectures, like really understand them, you'll do fine on the tests. I suggest reading the book before the lecture (it really makes all the difference)

Brau has a really unique style of teaching. He handwrites notes and projects them (which are hard to read). The tests are pretty much written directly from those notes, so if you study them well you can definitely be successful in the class.  He also goes on a lot of tangents. He is very kind though and gives great spiritual thoughts!

Brother Brau was an amazing teacher. He cares for his students so much. Not only did he do a great job at teaching finance, he always took part of the lecture to give a spiritual thought which was always uplifting. If you want to do well in this class just listen to the advice he gives you in class. He knows what he's talking about.

Amazing professor but honestly a difficult class. The only things graded are the 4 midterms and the final, and the department only looks for about 12-15% A's in the class so you have to do your best. As long as you don't stack your schedule with touch courses, you should be fine. Just for reference, I took Chem 105 but still did fine.

Brau is a great professor, but know you are entering a challenging class. It's difficult material, moves at a fast pace, and you have to do things his way - VERY test heavy. If you're not willing to put in the work, take from a different professor. He is a very motivating guy!

Professor Brau is an entertaining and knowledgeable professor who is difficult to forget! This class covers a lot of important material and maintains a rigorous pace, but is manageable if you work hard and put the time in.

Brau is the best for reals! He's super clear on what we need to know, so even though the class is tough and there's a lot to cover, you know what you need to know to do good. He moves fast in lectures so do the reading before, and take GOOD notes - the whole grade is tests so that helps. He's also very spiritual and makes class a good environment!

Professor Brau is a phenomenal teacher. He will level with you about his class, the expectations, and what it takes to succeed in his class. It is essential to be in class and to do the reading before class to understand what is going on. He splits up class with spiritual thoughts and professional development which is nice to help break it up.

Professor Brau is a fast talker, he expects you to have read the textbook ahead of time, so that you are ready to be introduced to new material at full speed. This makes class really rewarding and engaging, because you are always learning something new, while getting your prior study reinforced.

Professor Brau's class is surprising for the first few lectures. He is high energy and I sometimes had a hard time following when he was lecturing. 

However, if a student wants to do well in his class they have all the resources to do so. The grading is clear and fair, TA labs are fully staffed, and his tests are rigorous and do their job.

His lectures are great and he translates a lot of ideas to show their real world application and usage. 90% of your grade in his class is from exams, and half of each exam has questions asking about specific stories and things said only in class, so attendance is mandatory if you want a good grade in his class.

Jim Brau is the goat. His lectures are kinda all over the place which actually makes finance more entertaining then it should be. If you read before class and study the class notes+drill problems in prep for the test, in theory you'll be fine. Godspeed

Brau does a good job of making his lectures interesting, but it can definitely be very difficult to follow him at times. I found the textbook to be more understandable and easier to follow than his lectures. He does share lots of great spiritual thoughts and life lessons that would make this class worth it alone.

Brother Brau is great man however his class is a little too hard. I left lectures feeling exhausted. All the lectures consist of is Bro Brau explaining the book his way without diving into the hard concepts. He brushes over them super fast. I had to teach myself everything I feel like. The exams math problems always are harder than practice ones.

Professor Brau clearly cares about his students and is very knowledgeable about finance. His spiritual thoughts are often very inspiring. If you want to do well on the exams, it's important to know and understand everything in his class notes.

There were a lot of things about this class I didn't love but the material isn't one of them. The material is super interesting and valuable for life. Bro Brau just wasn't a good fit for me. If I could go back, I would take this class from a different Prof either fall or spring semester. Didn't like Brau's teaching style and he's very opinionated

Brau is a nice guy but it's frustrating to take a class from him because you HAVE to do things his way to succeed. There are 4 midterms and a final which make up your entire grade. He is very verbal about his opinions and I often left class feeling I didn't learn anything. Tough class with lots of material.
Knowledgeable in his field. Teaches by way of notes in class. Does not allow electronic devices in class. Conveys material clearly and always makes room in lecture for questions.

I absolutely loved Bro Brau! He is the epitome of what every BYU professor should be. I am so grateful for his spiritual messages in class. He cares for his students. But yes the course is very hard, but manageable.
Great professor. Lectures are filled with enthusiasm. Grade based mainly on tests. As long as you learn the notes well and make sure to practice the qualitative stuff, shouldn't be too hard.

Brau's spiritual thoughts are the best at BYU. The class is pure memorization and knowing your stuff in and out to do well on the exams - your entire grade. Don't take this class with a full schedule, while it's a 3-credit class, if you want to do well, you should consider it a 4 credit class. You will spend hours upon hours studying to do well.

Great man. His lectures were a little hard to follow, but he more than makes up for it in his ability to captivate and inspire. A lot of this class is self-taught using the book and reading his notes after the fact, so if you're okay with that then he's a good choice.

Bro. Brau is an engaging teacher who genuinely cares! His lectures move at a fast pace. Know your lecture notes and study hard for the exams. He is very good at responding to emails and will often do so within the hour! There are plenty of opportunities to get help for this class in the TA lab. I highly recommend taking FIN201 from Bro. Brau!
Great job with the lectures and everything on the test is in the notes. however, your grade is pretty much dependent on the exams, so study well and learn well from the lectures and textbook

Don't take this class if you're not a business bro, it's not worth it. It's treated as a weeding class for the business school. He assumes everyone in the class has a background the things he teaches, so there are big jumps from the content to the actual problems that were difficult for me to fill without already knowing everything about finance.
Definitely the most inspiring professor I've had at BYU. Fin 201 is a tough class so get ready to put in work. It's worth it though, definitely would recommend.

I did not enjoy this class although the content was interesting. It is very fast paced and I felt like even after attending all the lectures I was still going home and teaching myself. He takes his notes very quickly, has very dramatic opinions that I personally did not vibe with. That being said he does know what he is talking about.
Bro Brau is an awesome professor. His tests are based on lectures so attendance is important. Stay on top of the reading and start studying early.
Professor Brau's class is for people that can learn quickly from reading and note taking in lectures as well as excel in test taking. The key to the class is understanding your notes well.

Reading the online textbook before class was the indicator for those who will understand what is being said in class. The class moves fast and if you're not paying attention you'll miss it. Professor Brau loves sharing what he knows and it is amazing to get that sort of knowledge. I would highly recommend it.
He is a great professor. Very test heavy and fast paced. It is fairly easy to handle though if you plan well.

Everything you will read about Professor Brau is true. He has terrible handwriting, flies through the lectures, and occasionally gives good inspirational thoughts. I found him to be abrasive and childish in his examples and arrogant in his teaching. I wouldn't recommend him at all.

Good professor. Make sure to show up to class because the notes don't make a ton of sense without being there to hear him explain them. Generally a kind guy, but can be a little intense at times. When he says 90% of the tests come from the notes, he means it.

Jim Brau has a really good heart but his teaching is terrible. His lectures consist of him taking notes in his poor handwriting and you following along. He does not do a good job at building intuition as to what you are learning. Overall, a very self-centered man that I did not jive with.

Brau is an amazing professor who really cares about his students. He constantly is trying to tell his students that they need to make the decision that is best for them - whether that be teacher, major, religion, etc. He is extremely energetic and very good at maintaining attention. I enjoy going to his class even when my other teachers were boring

His good structure for the class (only 1 quiz per chapter and 1 midterm every 3 chapter) makes up for not being able to take notes on electronic devices (and he will notice if you use them). He is entertaining to listen to, and he knows what he's talking about, even if his writing is hard to read at times. Don't underestimate the tests.

Bro Brau is a person very passionate about finance. If you are planning to use financial skills in your profession, take from Brau because it is super important to him to teach you what you need to know for real life and not just curriculum. You have to work your tail off to do well in this class unless you're a genius. But its worth it.

Professor Brau has a good heart but has missed the mark in helping students learn. You basically just have your head down trying to copy his notes because he is going so fast. Maybe this class is good for students going into the Finance major, but it is not helpful for anyone else. I have never felt true anxiety until taking this class.

Professor Brau is awesome! He's super energetic and a big personality and has heavy weight on tests for your grade, so make sure you fit with that style. He gives you everything you need, you just need to be very meticulous and really study the notes he gives in class. The tests will be based largely on those. Overall, it was a great experience!

Professor Brau is down to earth. He often points out which questions will be on the test during lectures and will star other important things that will be on the test. Fin 201 can be a firehose especially without ACC 200 taken previously, but Brau makes it easy (ish) to understand. 

*1 test is dropped and there is a curve at the end of the class!

High energy, cranks through materials to the lecture. Talks a lot Everything on the test is covered in lectures. all test qs from notes. spends 20 minutes giving life advice or telling stories. Ngl not my type of professor. just prefer someone who gives it to me straight and doesn't fluff up the lecture. If you overthink, probably not for you.

Professor Brau expects a lot of memorization and intuition which he will teach you but he moves quickly. He includes current events into his classes which can be helpful if you understand the concepts being taught in the class. He is very animate and his stories are funny. Read the textbook before class or class can be hard to understand.

Professor Brau expects a lot of memorization and intuition which he will teach you but he moves quickly. He includes current events into his classes which can be helpful if you understand the concepts being taught in the class. He is very animate and his stories are funny. Read the textbook before class or class can be hard to understand.

He was great! Sometimes he would get side tracked with stories during the notes, but that was my favorite part. Basically If you show up to class and pay attention and know the notes then you'll do well.
This class was a tough class that required a lot of studying and reading. The tests are hard and are based heavily on the notes taken in class.

Professor Brau was an amazing professor. If you really want a good grade in the class you can get one. He tells you exactly what is on the test, and he is a very engaging lecturer. If you just study you will do great in his class, and he has a lot of very helpful professional development moments and spiritual thoughts that are amazing.

Brau has been one of my favorite professors thus far (Definitely top 3 out of the 24 I've had so far). He goes above and beyond to help his students find value in this course. Regardless of your major, you will come away from this class being glad you took it and being better informed about all aspects of finance. He helped me spiritually too.
Get ready to take notes all class. Very fun and engaging learning environment! Spiritual thoughts are powerful and motivating! You will learn a lot of real life things that will be very applicable.

Brau is an awesome teacher. He really drives you to learn the class concepts in depth and to be prepared for real life. Loved his teaching style, lectures, and spiritual thought. You have to be very on top of reading the textbook and mastering the notes because the tests are very difficult if you don't.
Honestly great professor, notes were clear, easy to learn from. Only take this class if you're okay with the 4 tests and a final deciding your entire grade.

Finance 201 was a really tough class for me. It's not Brau's fault entirely though. I enjoyed the spiritual thoughts in his class, and he always let us out a few minutes early, but he did blow up at a couple of students for a good chunk of time for talking (fair, but I'm a fan of praising in public and correcting in private).

This has been one of my most difficult but enjoyable classes! I'd take it again if I had to. Brother Brau is awesome! He does a spiritual thought and professional development moment every class and they're always fire. If you don't do the readings you will be super lost during lectures so make sure to do them even if they're long.

Professor Brau is awesome!  He doesn't really teach, he reviews the material you were already supposed to have read. He goes over everything so fast but he only tests what is on his notes.  He posts his notes so if you miss class you can get caught up by reading the book and going to the TAs.  He lets you drop a midterm!

Professor Brau is an awesome teacher. His tests are an extension of the notes that he writes in class, and so memorizing the notes is the best way to perform well on the tests. I really enjoyed his lectures he keeps them really entertaining and helps you understand the WHY of your learning experience.

Professor Brau is a great professor! His lectures are difficult to understand most of the time, but if you study the textbook and his notes well you will do alright on the tests. He shares the best spiritual thoughts that are super inspiring and uplifting. The class is graded solely on quizzes and tests so be ready to be self-disciplined and study.

Brother Brau is very dynamic and energetic. He keeps you engaged in his classes, and he shares lots of useful spiritual thoughts and professional development moments. He relies heavily on his notes for the exams, which is kind of difficult because his notes are messy and often are not clear outside of class. My advice is read and practice A LOT

While this class is very hard, as long as you do the readings, attend class, and really try to pay attention, you WILL get a decent grade. I thought that Brother Brau seems to genuinely care about his students. Just study the notes and follow his studying recommendations.

Professor Brau is a great professor!  He really cares about his students and loves what he does.  Although he is intense, he teaches the material well and the class is well organized.  He gives spiritual thoughts every class that are so powerful, he has a really sweet, relatable testimony.

Overall I enjoyed this class. As a senior about to graduate it was hard to be motivated to care but I was still able to do well enough. I would imagine getting an A would take a lot of work. I found the lectures to be a little bit all over the place at times but the material is clear enough if you take time to understand it.

Prof. Brau knows his stuff! He can be a little intense but that is just his personality and I still really enjoy his lectures! He wants his students to succeed so he makes sure to teach in a way to fully prepare his students to do well on the exams. All you need to do is study hard and you will do fine!

Prof. Brau is such an amazing professor. He goes quickly through the lecture material but if you memorize the notes you're guaranteed at least an A- on the exams. There is very little homework and attendance and reading are not mandatory but I would definitely recommend it.

I love Brother Brau. I think he is so funny and I enjoy his spiritual thoughts. That being said, I found this class to be very challenging. 90% of your grade is based on exams. The other 10% comes from open book quizzes. To succeed: do the readings before class, stay engaged during lecture, visit the TA lab and practice the problems over and over.

Dr. Brau is intense! They call him shock and awe for a reason. He's a really good guy and his tests are relatively straight forward. If you don't attend class you probably won't do great on the tests because he basically answers all of the questions in class. TA's are a big help explaining difficult concepts!

This class is difficult, but if you understand the notes really well you'll do fine on the exams. This class is exam heavy with 4 midterms and 1 final. Brother Brau is a great professor who keeps lectures interesting. His professional development and spiritual thoughts were helpful.
Very motivational. 90% of the tests come from the notes
Brau is tough but reasonable. Lectures are fun and engaging. Don't skip class much.

Brother Brau is great! He is so caring and truly wants his students to succeed. That being said, this class is very test-heavy, with the majority of the test questions coming from notes in lecture. If you do the reading before class, pay attention in class, and go to the TA Lab, you should do well! Be prepared to work!!

He is a good professor, you have to make it to class. The notes are so important to do well on the test and tests are pretty much your whole grade. He moves fast in class so come prepared and use the TAs beforehand. Sometimes I feel he says things non-class related with little or questionable research done but it didn't bother me much.

Finance 201 is a hard class regardless of who you take it from, but Brau makes it manageable. There are four midterms and one final that make up the majority of your grade, so if you're not a good test taker, maybe take a different teacher. That being said he's good at finance and the TAs are a great resource.

I was not really interested in finance at all, but Brau was able to make it interesting. The tests come from his class notes. So don't miss class ever, pay attention, take good notes, and you'll do fine! I genuinely wanted to go to class because he's so entertaining and energetic. He does go really fast though so that can be the hardest part.

Professor Brau is a wonderful teacher. You can tell he really cares about the students and loves helping us learn. The only problem is studying for a test can seem a little ambitious and most if not all your grade comes from the exams so be aware. But if your a sucker for spiritual thoughts this is the man, his class is very uplifting.

Very fun and engaging class. It is essential that you come prepared, having read the chapter in the textbook and worked the practice problems before class. Otherwise, you're left in the dark. As someone who is not in the business school, it was a little crazy cramming basic accounting principles the first week of class and then jumping into finance

Professor Brau's lectures are based on class readings so if you don't do the readings, you might not understand the lectures. He also talks a bit fast and he expects no laptops. His tests are based on class notes. The materials Brau taught are very relevant to real life and he truly cares about his students. I learned so much from him.

Bro. Brau uses a guided notes format to lecture that I really liked- you write down what he writes down. He moves quickly, so if you haven't read you will have to go back and read in order to understand it. He also does practice problems each class period. Each class period includes a spiritual thought and a professional development message.

The class has a lot of tests, but almost every question is covered in the lectures. He also made time for spiritual thoughts and professional development in every lecture. Professor Brau was my favorite professor this semester. 

In short: hard class, but attend the lectures and study your notes and you'll be fine.

Brau is definitely passionate about finance and teaching it. He goes over things really really fast so be prepared to take really good notes and spend a lot of time teaching yourself the material. No busy work just preclass reading/quiz and then four tests. The class is definitely a grind but manageable.

Brau is easily one of the best professors I have ever had. He's tough but fair, teaches incredibly well, and deeply cares about his students. His lectures were the best part of my Tuesdays and Thursdays. This class was hard but I wish I could take it again.

Professor Brau is hands down the best professor I have ever had at BYU. He cares SO much about individual students and in a class of 1000 kids still makes time to help you, talk to you, and counsel with you. that being said, his teaching style was pretty different than my learning style, but the class was easy enough I could just read the book.

Jim Brau is one of the best men I have ever met, he is also very hilarious. If you pay attention in class and get down his notes, you will be fine in the class. Just listen to how he tells you to study. You will definitely need to spend hours working and studying, but it will pay off.

Brau is honestly one of the best guys I have met. He really cares about all his students, even in classes with 600 kids. You need to go to lecture and you NEED to study his notes. If you don't study his notes you will fail the class. Great teacher, tough but just getting you ready for the real world. His spiritual thoughts rock. Totally recommend.

Knows his stuff and gives good daily spiritual thoughts. His teaching style is writing 2-4 pgs of notes per class while talking, not my favorite but I learned. DO THE READINGS BEFORE CLASS. Quizzes have unlimited attempts. Tests are 90% of your grade, 30ish questions, no "none of the above", and he lets you drop one. TA lab = good test score.
Brau was an entertaining teacher to say the least. He was always very energetic and funny. This class is extremely test heavy and if you don't do well on those you are toast.

This class is difficult, but Brau teaches in a way that ensures that the information given in each lecture applies to any major taking the class. The lectures are fast-paced but very engaging. He also offers very well-thought-out spiritual thoughts. TA's are very helpful, and there is a lot of them, so if you are struggling there are options.
Good guy, but concepts were not explained clearly and so much material was covered in such a short amount of time. Going to the TA lab was the only thing that got me through this class.

Professor Brau really really cares about his students and is super passionate about Finance. His lectures are entertaining and he gives you all the resources you need for the exams. The class is graded mainly on exams so it can be hard to get a good grade in the class if tests aren't your strong suit.

Solid professor, has high energy which can be fun. The class isn't hard. I will say that as far as a finance course, I feel like there are probably better professors as far as actually teaching an in-depth understanding of finance. That comes with the way he teaches which is by projecting his notepad as he writes (he has poor handwriting).

Brau is a great professor! The class is tough, but not unreasonably so. If you show up to class, take notes, and study for the tests you'll do great. And it is worth going to class, he always takes time for professional development and a spiritual thought. A genuinely great guy!

Brau is the only reason I made it through finance. It is a well structured class and his tests are very doable if you study his notes. While the class is difficult, so is any finance class. Great, great guy with tons of passion and someone who genuinely cares about each and every student.

Brau is a pretty good professor, but the class is significantly difficult itself. If you don't read the textbook before class and pay attention to every detail in class, you will not do well. If you can master his notes, then you will do fine on the exams (4 + final). His notes are often utterly illegible however and terms unclear without TA help.

Professor Brau was awesome! I'm glad I had him for Finance 201, and he was very energetic and shared some amazing spiritual thoughts and professional development moments in class. The tests are a huge part of your grade (65% for the midterms and 25% for the final) so study hard and you'll do great in the class! The tests aren't bad if you prepare.

I'd hesitate to recommend this professor to anyone who:
- Is not a good test-taker (you'd rather write papers or do endless homework),
- Is a slow writer or cannot part with their laptop (he has a closed-laptop policy), or
- Is just looking for a grade rather than actual learning.

To anyone else, Prof. Brau has my highest recommendations.

I loved Brau's class, his lectures are great and he teaches the concepts very well. Almost all of the grade is tests, so if that's not your thing then don't take FIN 201 from Brau. However, if you're okay with the test heavy work load then Professor Brau is an absolutely phenomenal professor and you'll learn a ton.

Brau is an awesome guy. His lectures are always super entertaining because of his high energy and passion for what he is teaching. The class  is test heavy and based on 4 midterms + a final. You need to take notes during class and its best to read the textbook prior to class. The tests are pretty hard but the TA lab is very accessible and helpful.

It's a good class, with lots of notes and studying required to achieve success in the class. You have to do the readings on time before every lecture so that you can have a better understanding of the curriculum in the lectures. Pay attention to test dates as well as they can really sneak up on you!

Bro Brau is an awesome guy! He gives great spiritual thoughts every class and he answers lots of question about the material. His class is difficult but if you study and do the readings and take good notes you should be fine. His tests are mostly what he wrote down in class so pay attention.

Make sure you read the textbook before coming to class. If you dont, you will not understand anything, he teaches as if you already understand the topic which rewards those who put the work in. He is a good professor, but as I stated teaches as if you already understand which can cause comprehension problems.

Brau was great! The only work you had to do was take notes in class, read the online textbook and take a quiz on what you read (but you can take it as may times as you want to get 100%). His lectures were great, he always has a spiritual thought, professional development, and accounting jokes. He is quite high energy, so be ready. 4 Midterms+final

FIN 201 was a demanding course, but Dr. Brau brought such a great energy to very morning class, had very clear expectations, taught clearly, was respectful and spiritual, and was willing to help anyone that needed extra help. 10/10

Dr. Brau is a fantastic professor and you will learn a lot in this class. As long as you study his notes and do the online reading before each class, you will succeed. Make sure you really have the class notes down as they will be a large portion of the test qualitatively, and also make sure you can do the different valuations quantitatively.

He's super knowledgeable and has really funny stories that he uses during class. It is really tough though because 90% of the grade is based on the midterms and final, so prepare a lot for the tests and DON'T PROCRASTINATE. You can't go over the tests to see what you did wrong, which is hard, so make sure you understand his notes! Really funny guy!

Professor Brau was one of my favorite professors personality-wise. He has exceptional spiritual thoughts that rival most of my religion class lectures. Took this while in two chems and a physics which I don't recommend. Class is test heavy which is difficult if you're spending other time in more difficult classes. Overall I liked the class.

Brau is easily one of the best professors I have had at BYU. His grading criteria and testing is very straight forward, so as long as you go to class, study the notes, and put in the work to read the chapters, you will get an A. On top of this, his spiritual thoughts literally changed the way I see a lot of spiritual matters. Amazing class and prof

This has been a class where I leave inspired everyday and rejuvenated to take on life's challenges. His spiritual thoughts are better than most, if not all religion classes, and he takes time to teach you things that are pertinent in real life that might not be in the textbook. Gets off topic sometimes and hard to read handwriting, but I loved it.

Brother Brau is an awesome teacher. He uses real-world examples to make application easier to understand. He also is super funny, high energy, and gives some great spiritual thoughts. I would definitely recommend taking him if you want to learn the basic principles of Finance.

He has definitely grown on me throughout the semester. It is a tough class since there is a lot of content and the grade 90% exams, but if you do the textbook readings, textbook problems, and learn the notes, you will do well. The practice quizzes on LS weren't helpful though.

Notes are taken via pen and paper and no digital devices are allowed in class, even for study materials. He can often be loud and abrupt in lectures which is often off-putting. Class grade is based on 4 midterms and the final; you can drop one midterm if you take a bunch of surveys giving personal info for his research.

If you're looking for a funcitonal understanding of finance that is what you will get.  After taking this class, you will have a general understanding of the principles of finance and how you can apply them to both your career and your personal life.  Along the way there are also some great spiritual messages and personal development thoughts.

Dr. Brau is very focused on preparing you for a successful financial life. He has a great understanding about relevant financial concepts and tries his hardest to prepare you for the real world. He is energetic and his lectures are never boring. Tests are hard, but based on lectures. Awesome spiritual thoughts and great professional dev moments.

This class is almost entirely tests. If you prepare for class and pay attention to the lectures and study notes you should be fine in the class. I missed a lot of class due to sports which made the class much more difficult than it seemed.
Awesome professor. Hard class, but manageable if you are laser focused during class taking notes. Tests are 100% based on class notes and practice problems.
Super tough class, will kick your butt. But, Brau is amazing and if you have the opportunity to take from him do it.

Very good at lecturing and makes the class very simple. What you study is what is on your test. I found the class to be difficult and even when I was confident in what I was doing I still didn't do as well as I had hoped on the test.

Professor Brau is a great professor. Fin201 was a closed laptop/phone course. The course is Test heavy; there are 4 exams and a cumulative final. But Professor Brau provides you with all of your needs to be successful. He gives great spiritual thoughts each class period, along with real-world advice. He tends to move through his lectures quickly.

I have LOVED Dr. Brau! The class is hard, but I feel he makes it the most manageable. He tells you everything you need to do to get a good grade, so listen and actually do it and you'll be fine (read the chapters, study how he tells you to)! He is super energetic, funny, and genuinely cares about his students! Definitely take this class with Brau!

Brau is awesome. His class is hard but that is just because finance is difficult in of itself. If you come to class and study the textbook and class notes then you will do well. Also, you get to drop your lowest test score so that is awesome.

The class is set up very poorly and teaching style is awful. 65% percent of your grade is on 4 midterms (last one is 8 days before the final) and 25% is a comprehensive final. Teaches by writing almost illegible notes, explains a new concept 1 time and then always uses an abbreviation. If you don't already know finance, it is a very difficult class
His teaching style was hard for me, however it is a good class. The material makes sense and he has great energy when he teaches.

Professor Brau gives inspiring life lessons. He says a lot about other majors and really wants you to pursue finance. Make sure to study your notes really carefully for the exams because a lot of the test questions are taken directly from them.

Brau is a great teacher! He's old school and uses a projector with hand written notes but you learn a lot more by writing things down. I enjoyed his class and his lectures. The tests are hard but if you go to class and study his notes you'll do fine.

Professor Brau cares about his students and makes the material relevant for anyone in the class, not just finance majors. He made it clear what was on tests and the requirements were reasonable. I had to put a lot of outside work to understand the material, but there's lots of resources available to help. It was a difficult class but manageable.

Brau is extremely clear in his expectations, it is a tough class but manageable. He cares a lot about his students. At first he was intimidating but a grew to really care for him and respect him throughout the semester. I would definitely recommend him!

Took this a couple semesters back. This class led me to getting back on my meds for anxiety. I finally had to withdraw from the class because of how much stress it was causing me and now I won't walk for another year. He will teach you and treat you like you are a brown nosing finance bro. Class is shiz fire. Read this for career development Brau!
Do not take Brau. Do not take Brau. Do not take Brau. Do not take Brau. Do not take Brau. Do not take Brau. Literally take anyone else. This was my least favorite class of all of college.

Not the greatest professor for my learning style, basically just threw formulas at us without really explaining their intended use. However, if you study the notes and do the practice quizzes, a good grade is easily attainable. Brau shares great spiritual thoughts and professional insights. 4 midterms and a final, can drop 1 midterm. Need to work

This class was very frustrating. The majority of the course is determined by midterms and the final. The material in the textbook had many minor inconsistencies with the "drill-down" problems used to prepare for exams. Scoring highly on the textbook quizzes and practice exams did not translate to scoring well on the midterms.

I hated this class and it was not him or the material. It was the way he taught the material. It felt like a fire hose of information every class. Taking tests, I always had all the formulas memorized and could write them down on my note sheet, I understood all qualitative questions, i understood the intuition behind topics but still scored low.

He doesn't let you use laptops during class, so you have to hand write them. Attendance isn't required but he puts in-class material on the tests (and they aren't in the textbook). He does post class notes online, but his handwriting is terrible so you won't be able to read it. If you do go to class, be prepared to write for an hour and 15 minutes.

Get ready to memorize formulas you will never again use in your life (unless you study finance/accounting). Can be an easy class if you don't have a job and have a relatively light semester. I have heard other professors are easier but not sure.

Not a fan at first, but eventually I realized he's tough because he cares. Hard-nosed (army guy) and teaches fast (yes, even for college). No laptops, paper notes only. Slightly unfeeling if you have a complaint. Defers to TAs heavily, who are a little fuzzy on some concepts since most don't go to lecture. A is not impossible if you pay attention.

Ok the last 3 reviews are all ridiculous so I am gonna jump on and bring some truth in this. I have taken every business perquisite out there and to say this class is harder than Acc 200/310, IS201, or Econ 110 is just plain crazy. Yes he teaches fast but thats college my friends. He is super nice and wants students to win in life. Take this class!

Brau is a super funny guy and I loved him as a person. His spiritual messages are awesome. However, his class is ridiculous. He teaches us all like we chose to take the class or like we are remotely interested in Finance. REQUIRED CLASS!!! Won't remember anything from this class in one month. I got a 98% in accounting and scraped a B in his class.

Im writing this just before taking the first test and so far Professor Brau is horrible. He speaks extremely fast and all his lectures are is watching him write equations. He tells you to write everything down so you end up going home with PAGES of notes of equations without any context. No explanations ever, worst class so far at BYU.

Most conceited professor. Always bragged about himself. Lied about other programs in the school. 
Asked him for major advice once, told me I wasn't good enough for the finance program (I ended up getting in but declined because of him.)
Doesn't really teach. He takes notes on an overhead and expects you to memorize it all.
Worst experience at BYU.

The class, easy breezy covergirl. Wish the professor put more effort into his work. Goes off on self centered rants and offended lots of students throughout the course. Unable to see his own faults. Healthy criticism will be turned on you (gaslighting). Thought army taught that growth comes from ownership #JockoWillink #extremeownership

Difficult class, but I really enjoyed the concepts. I prefer tests to assignments, so I liked that with Brau. I also enjoyed his remarks on professional development. Really pay attention to what he says in class. Being present in class is absolutely necessary.
You need to memorize the notes to do four midterms and one final (there is no homework, just tests). The class is challenging. Brother Brau is a genuine person.
Worst professor I've had at BYU, pushes personal values over school priorities and is the embodiment of sanctimonious

His tests are pretty hard and you have to really know the stuff and not just be able to work the problems cuz he wants you to know all the little definitions of everything. Everything is based on the tests so you have to do well on those.

Bro Brau was a really great professor. He balanced professional development, spiritual thoughts, and course curriculum very well. You are only graded on 3 midterms and the final so if you're not a great test taker, then I would avoid taking this class. 3% curve helped bump me up to an A. This was a really great class, I would suggest it!

Bro Brau is a cool dude but I'm not a fan of the way he teaches. All the material taught in class, in the textbook, and the extra practice problems aren't near the difficulty of the questions on the test. There isn't any homework for this course so you have to be really disciplined to study consistently throughout the whole semester.

Professor Brau has some amazing spiritual thoughts in his lectures, but that was the only good thing about this class. I had to leave class a lot because I was having panic attacks. Professor Brau didn't help this in any way by constantly saying how hard his tests were. Also, he spends a lot of time bragging about himself, which doesn't help anyone

Brother Brau is a very good and inspiring man, but not a great professor. He spends class writing notes with many confusing abbreviations and very poor handwriting. If you want to do well in this class be ready to teach yourself all of the material. He treats the class as if you're all going to be Finance majors. If you aren't one avoid at all cost

I love Bro Brau. He is so passionate about his lectures and also gives awesome spiritual thoughts and professional development moments. He only grades on tests and they are very challenging. I did not do well in the class but I really liked him. He does his best to prepare you for the real world.

Your grade for the class is based on the average of the 4 midterms + final or just the score on the final, whichever is higher. Midterms are 30 questions each, no assigned homework throughout the class. He tells you what's on the tests. Study those and take the practice exams and review frequently. No busy work so the class was enjoyable

Brau was incredibly difficult. I almost hated going to class, however, I learned the most life lessons from him. The class grade is based off midterms and final so you really need to know what you're doing. Even though the class was hard, I learned real life examples and was inspired almost every class. Brau is awesome!

Your grade in the class is based off of 4 tests, including the final, which was daunting, but also nice to not have to worry about busy work. Altogether a good class, and his lectures were great.  You can tell he cares a lot about his students and wants the best for them.  The class is worth it just for the experience of having him as a teacher.
This is the model for how I feel every BYU professor should be. He teaches the content, life lessons, and shares his testimony in an amazing blend.

Your grade is based on your 4 midterms and the final. The tests are difficult. He teaches the material well. You will need to put in effort. He seems like a good person. Each class has a spiritual though and a professional development moment.

One of the best professors I've had! HIS SPIRITUAL THOUGHTS ARE LIFECHANGING. His class often feel like drinking from a firehose, but he's really good at keeping everyone engaged and awake during class. Since his tests come 100% from the notes you'll want to copy down the notes exactly how he writes them.

Professor Brau is a great person and really smart. He expects a lot and sends a lot of info in a short amount of time. However, if you do the readings beforehand and take notes on it, youll be good. Study the notes and take the practice tests before every exam.
Great Professor. If you struggle with time management, he is not the professor for you. No hw but only tests. Very kind man and great connection.

Brau is amazing! Such a great guy and is super connected spiritually!   The only thing is the class is based on 4 tests and the final (one of the tests can be dropped w/out hurting your end score) so you need to know your stuff. Sometimes feel like a firehose, but its good. Just make sure you know the WHY behind everything and youll do just fine!

I really enjoyed this class despite the difficulty. Prof. Brau is very energetic and cares a lot about every student. The class is entirely based on exam grades (which sucks) so make sure you spend ample time studying the book before lecture and prepare well for each exam by knowing the lecture notes back and front.

This class was very fast pace, but the concepts as well as what is expected are clearly explained. Professor Brau focuses on preparing you to apply for the finance major, to interview for finance internships, and a little bit of personal finance. He shared professional development and spiritual thoughts every class that were very helpful to me.
Great lecturer, and really knowledgeable in the field. Helpful class, but hard tests

I really enjoyed the experience that Professor Brau provides. His lecture always incorporate a spiritual thought an a professional development lesson. You can tell he genuinely cares for his students. The class is difficult because it is only graded on test but he makes it clear want things will be on the test.

Jim Brau is one of the best instructors that I have ever taken a class from! Although he teaches a ton of students at a time, he is great when it comes to explaining concepts and principles. He does talk really fast, so you better be ready to write fast! He only grades through tests, so be ready for all of your grades to be based on the tests!

Brau is a fantastic professor! He is focused on teaching what you need to know to pass the tests and be financially successful in life. The grades in his finance course are based entirely on test scores, which some people might not like, but he is pretty clear about what he will test on and how difficult the tests will be.
He cares about your success in this class and makes his expectations of the course clear.
Professor Brau's class was very straight forward in format. I am not the biggest fan of test only classes but if this is your favorite type of class than he would be a good teacher for it.

Prof. Brau is a great professor. He knows the material well and wants to help. The TA's are amazing and are willing to try different things to help you understand the material. However, the material is difficult to understand if you aren't inclined to Finance. So, if you struggle with the material, start studying extra hard early in the semester.

Professor Brau is a fun, exciting teacher. If you love Finance, he does a really job of explaining principles and vocabulary that you will hear all over the real world. The class is based off only 4 tests so make sure to study hard and don't slack because there is no homework. Most of his tests come from the notes so be attentive in class!

Brau is an amazing teacher and knows the struggles of his students well and will accommodate for any needs you may have. 4 midterms and a final are the only grades in the class, and the tests are difficult but manageable if you study instead of cramming.

Brau is awesome. One of the best professors at BYU by far. He's very real and takes two breaks during lecture- one for a spiritual thought and the other for professional development advice. That being said, the class is 100% graded by tests. He drops your lowest midterm if you do surveys. The final is cumulative and very hard. Be sure to study hard

Professor Brau's class is definitely a weeder class. Tests make up your entire grade. All the material he goes over in class is what will be on the test but, you need to do a lot of studying outside of class to understand the material well. If you don't go to class you will fail the class, however he doesn't require it.

In my personal opinion, Brau's FIN 201 class is the model of what classes at BYU should look like. Starts with a prayer, fills your brain with knowledge, throws in spiritual thoughts and professional development moments every class, it was an awesome class.

Probably my favorite professor I've had. He cares about everyone in his classes. He is super engaging and makes the principles learned applicable to real life. I always looked forward to going to his class. Your grade is made up completely by tests but everything on the tests is based on what you talk about in class.

Great professor, but class based on 4 midterms and comprehensive final. Being successful requires reading all chapters before class, writing everything he says and writes during class, and studying those notes for the tests. Anywhere from 2-4 pages of notes per class period. Great guy, and teaches the material well, this class just needs effort.
His lectures are a bit scattered and you need the notes to do well in class. If you don't test well don't take his class. Tests are the only grades you get.

Professor Brau cares about his students, all of them. You leave class feeling inspired, and maybe with a slight headache because of how fast everything is covered. Read the chapters before class, pay attention to class, and review the notes like crazy and you'll do fine.
Not great at explaining difficult concepts. Leaves a lot up to you to learn so don't join if you aren't willing to put in lots of effort on your own.

Brother Brau is the most energetic professor I have ever met but this class is extremely difficult to succeed in if you are not naturally gifted at math or finance. The entire grade is composed of 3 tests and the final (there are 4 tests total but your lowest one is dropped). No hw or ability to see what you did wrong on past tests.

Brau's lectures were one of my favorite parts of the day. He always starts with a prayer, he has a spiritual thought, and a professional development moment in each lecture. But I was not a huge fan of his class and the content. He teaches towards students wanting to go into finance. It's a very tough class so if you take it, be ready to study.

Prof Brau is an AMAZING person!!! Now Finance is a SUPER HARD CLASS!! One has to devote one's entire semester and life to that class to do well!  My biggest thing is that I wish this class had video walkthroughs on the drill problems and practice questions. I wish this class was structured like Prof Larson's ACC class! Intense class!

This class has zero graded homework- grades are based exclusively on 4 tests and the final. Dr. Brau has a great teaching style, he's knowledgable and likes to tell short stories to make the topic sink in. His lectures were a pleasure to attend. If you don't do well on tests this class isn't for you. Study is mandatory to get a good grade.

One of the most enthusiastic people out there, despite it being a huge lecture class, Professor Brau makes it feel like he really cares about you and your well being. Get ready to study and a lot if you want a good grade.

Professor Brau's lectures are clear and concise. He cares a lot about his students. I think his spiritual thoughts are great too. We need more professors like him. The tests are challenging but if you follow the notes you will get a good grade.

I really loved taking FIN 201 with Brau! His lectures were really fun to attend and I loved how there was a spiritual thought as well as career development advice in every class too. I found that I learned a lot of important information without getting bored which is a plus! I would definitely recommend taking this class :)
Not hard if you are attentive to all the lectures, as everything in the exams are in his notes and such but it can be hard to take everything, especially with 4 or more pages of notes every class.
GREAT PROFESSOR. The tests are the whole grade and if you listen to what he says and study the way he recommends you will do well.

He's a really genuine, caring guy. Offers a lot of opportunities to meet with him one on one, and gives good advice. However, only take this class if you are good at test taking. The only grades are 5 tests, and they can be tough. You have to be willing to study really hard, but if you do, the tests should go well.

Professor Brau is so passionate about finance and life in general. Attendance and reading before lecture is a must.
