If you don't read you'll fall behind in the lecture (I swear he takes pre-workout before every lecture with how fast he goes). The grade is only based on the tests, however, he's very clear about the material he expects you to know.
Tough class but really cares about you as a student.
He is really cool and brings a good spirit to the class, but his tests are really hard and that is the only thing your grade is based on. You need to know your notes inside and out!!

Professor Brau is a very realistic and inspirational teacher. He is entertaining to learn from. My spiritually improved by listening to his spiritual thoughts and taking his invitations. He has very clear expectations. . He is a fun, high energy teacher who is a total stud! Only tests, no assignments, but it wasn't bad if you studied the notes.

He definitely has his own way of teaching. Make sure you get help from the TAs. It was a very very difficult class for me so make sure you get help early because he builds off of things and if you do not understand it then he will be assuming you know things you do not know.
he gave a lot of spiritual thoughts

AMAZING TEACHER. Know yourself before taking this class. If you tend to procrastinate take a different teacher who has assigned homework so that you can stay up to speed easier and avoid last minute cramming for tests. Entirely graded on tests, which aren't too hard if you don't get behind -- if you do, you'll want to take from a different teacher.

Brother Brau is great! Grade is completely based on the tests, but it moves fast so read the book before class and work all the practice problems. Everything you need to know is in his lecture notes. He shares spiritual thoughts and professional development thoughts every class which is neat. I'm not going into finance and I still had a blast.

He is intense, but cares a lot about his students and what BYU stands for. I personally didn't love his teaching style but he doesn't try to trick you. He tells you what you exactly what you need to know to be successful, he just tells it in a fire hose type of way. Although I'm sure if I enjoyed finance more it wouldn't have seemed so fast paced.
Love this guy as a person. Great lectures and his BOM lessons every class are good. No HW, everything is based on tests. Tough material if you aren't going into finance!

He is a great professor. Heh as spiritual thoughts every class that are very motivating and inspiring and I really enjoyed those. It was a difficult course for me because I had a couple other challenging courses and finance kind of got put on the back burner because there weren't things due every week like my other classes. Very reasonable class.

Bro B was a beast. The class was too. Although super challenging, it was a manageable class if you had a lighter load outside of it. The notes will give you every answer you need for the test so study those. He would always give a spiritual thought and a professional development moment to break up class. Showed he really cared about our success.

Jim Brau is easily one of the craziest, hard-working, funny, and spiritual teachers that you'll ever have. He teaches at a fast pace so if you want an A then you must,
Read the book, take notes in class, do the drill problems on LS after the lecture, and master the practice exams before taking exams. 
I liked him and would highly recommend him.

He Is a great teacher. He has 4 midterms 1 final. Midterms 75% of grade and final is 25% of grade. there are no assignments unless you want to get your lowest midterm grade dropped. Also if your final is better than your grade in the class it replaces your grade. the lecture goes over a reading, a spiritual message, and a personal development tip.

Professor Brau is my favorite professor I've had so far. His lectures move fast, but he is entertaining so it is easy to stay involved. The only grades in his class are the tests, but if you take good notes and study, then you do fine on the tests. He only tests on what he lectures on. His spiritual thoughts and career development moments are great

Honestly, Bro Brau was a fine teacher. I can see how for some people he would be the best and others wouldn't think that. Copy his notes, go back and practice the problems from class and you're pretty set for the tests, which are the only way he grades you. Exam drop was a life saver.

Legit class. 100% test based, so make sure you study your notes. Overall, tests are not crazy challenging. If you do research projects, he will let you drop your lowest test score which is helpful. His spiritual thoughts are also pretty good. I enjoyed it.
Notes are the most important, only professor that shares spiritual messages every class! Grades come from only exams

I loved Brau's class. If you put in the time you will do well. Just memorize your notes and work the drill problems. Trust him when he says "I LITERALLY TELL YOU WHAT IS ON THE TEST". I wouldn't take finance from anyone else.

Professor Brau was a cool teacher! He sped through the notes pretty quick and his tests were hard. If you do the reading from the textbook and take notes before hand and do all the practice problems and exams, then you should be fine on the tests. Not the professor for everybody but I would take his class again.

I absolutely loved this professor. His spiritual thoughts are what got me through class. He has a very specific teaching way that didn't quite work for me, but for some people this class was a piece of cake. The best advice I have is STUDY THE NOTES. If you do that you're guaranteed a good grade.

4 midterms, 1 final. It appears there will be a 7% class curve, haven't confirmed yet. You will get a 90% on all the midterms if you memorize the notes. I never read the textbook, just pay attention in lectures. The final is harder than the midterms and has problems very similar to Holme's practice tests. It isn't as hard as he says it is though.
Grades are only based on 5 tests (4 midterms  drops the lowest score, and one final), dont require attendance, very specific with note taking, fun class overall! But VERY challenging.

Brau is a GREAT man! Love his spiritual thoughts every class (no, im not 100% active in the church, but he shares some good stuff and they are inspiring to me!). This class is definitely intellectually challenging! Finance is difficult. Brau tries to make it easy by writing identical notes with the whole class every class period.

Brother Brau is a great professor who sincerely cares about his students. His lectures are fun and he doesn't make finance harder than it needs to be. He is focused on helping his student not just do well in the class but be better prepared for life. The tests are hard and you need to study, but as long as you take notes and study youll be fine.

This class was hard! I only needed it for my business minor otherwise I wouldn't have taken it. If you love math and are passionate about finance then this is the class for you. His class is based on five exams and they are based solely on the lecture notes that he provides during class. Awesome guy that really wants to get to know his students.

Professor Brau is a seasoned finance professor and he won't let you forget it. His office hours are at the VASA gym which made me uncomfortable and overall he was very unprofessional. A lot of my fellow classmates loved Brau but his teaching style did not match my learning style. Be prepared to be graded solely on tests

For tests, he will explicitly say "you should know this for the exam" but adds in extra info on the test to really see if you know what info you need. Hard, but great class! Requires work and effort, but you can do really well if you put in the effort! I would 100% recommend Brau! It's lecture heavy, but his spiritual thoughts are the best!

Brother Brau is a nice guy, and I enjoyed his spiritual thoughts, but he doesn't teach that much. I felt like I was just copying the notes and not actually learning the content. I had to read the textbook to understand anything. You still have to go to class though because he occasionally uses an example or says a name and it ends up on the tests.

His teaching style was hard for me. Very fast & lots of memorization. But you can tell he cares about his students so much and his devotionals were the best I've heard at BYU. You just have to be very self-disciplined & be prepared to study a ton for the 4 tests & the final. This class helped me realize that finance is not for me lol.

One of the best professors I have ever had. His class was very engaging and it made it easy to study for the tests because of that. This had been one of my favorite classes. If you work hard you can receive an A and I promise if you put in that work it will pay off. Brau also goes out of his way to mentor his students. He's great!

Prof. Brau is quite the character! He is awesome. I loved and appreciated his career thoughts and his spiritual thoughts. I also like the clear grading criteria and the personal finance lectures. When he says that his tests are all about knowing your class notes, he really means it.

bro b is a great professor! He's very fair. Downside might be that there are no quizzes and you are only graded on exams, but he prepares you very well for them in his lectures in class. His spiritual thoughts and professional development moments are the highlight of the class :)
Brau is a great teacher. He served in the military, so it seems like all of his stories and advice is EXTREME. So, take it with a grain of salt. The grade is based on midterms and the final
This is an amazing professor! Take him for finance 201!

Professor Brau has an extremely intense personality. He takes pre-workout before class which might seem fun but usually just means he speeds through lectures. He gave a lot of questionable financial advice which made me skeptical of his credibility as a finance specialist. I did appreciate some of his spiritual thoughts though.

Dr. Brau is a really good professor.  He is very enthusiastic about Finance and it makes it pretty interesting.  He is very inclusive and seeks to assure that all students regardless of who they are and what they believe feel welcome. The only thing you are graded on is exams but if you memorize the notes and know how to do problems its not bad.
Professor Brau is very energetic, passionate, and loves finance and his students. He gives great spiritual thoughts.

Professor Brau is a passionate teacher who has a lot of energy and a deep love for finance and his students. He  teaches to the real world, so he expects things be memorized. The work load is very light, all that is expected of you is that you study for exams and stay caught up on chapter readings. Professor Brau is very spritual and inspiring.

This is a tough class. Brau is a good teacher, but he moves quick. You have to take good notes and know them super well and read the material before the lectures to keep up. But if you know everything that Brau teaches in class, you'll do fine on the tests. Know the notes.
Brau was great and an awesome teacher

Brau is a great teacher and I looked forward to his classes. That being said, I feel like it was difficult to really grasp the concepts because we went so quickly. It is a class where I had to study a lot on my own to be successful because there aren't homework assignments. Overall, I think he is great at teaching finance.

The only grades in this class are four midterms and a final. He does drop a midterm, and he lets you take your final as your overall grade if it's better than your average, but get ready to study for those tests.

Professor Brau is one of the coolest teachers I have ever had! He is non a traditional finance teacher as he is very energetic and inspirational. As far as a class, it is not very difficult or time-consuming. Your grade is solely determined by exam scores, all of which were not too bad. I would recommend taking this class.

Professor Brau is an amazing person! I really struggled with Finance, but Brau made it a good class. I learned a lot, but this class is VERY test heavy. Meaning the only thing on your grade are the midterms and final. No homework assigned, you just have to make sure you STUDY! He gives amazing spiritual thoughts and he really cares for students.

Professor Brau is great, if you learn the notes as he explains in class you will get at least a 90 on the 4 midterms. Make sure to read the online textbook before class and you'll keep up with his fast-paced lectures. He also records class and posts it online for those who can't make it to class.

Would highly recommend taking FIN 201 from Brau- he is a great teacher and truly cares about his students. The class is based entirely on test grades, but if you write down his exact notes and know them, you'll do great! The lectures move pretty fast too, but Brau will break them up with a spiritual thought or a professional development moment.

Dr. Brau is amazing. His tests come right out of class notes and the book. Do a few practice problems and focus the rest of your time on gaining the intuition behind the concepts, and you will do great. He's my favorite professor at BYU hands down. Tests are not bad at all if you put the work in to truly understand the concepts.
Great professor and lecturer, but hard to know what is he going to be testing you on. Anything that is said in lecture is fair game for the exams.

I am not a good test taker, so exams determining grades made me anxious. I am an accounting major so most of the material didn't make sense unless it included accounting principals. Brau is a phenomenal man that inspired me with daily spiritual thoughts, but he isn't my type of teacher. I would appreciate more clear practice problems in class.

Awesome dude, I am not a finance guru so this class has not clicked but weirdly enough I did do exceptionally well in both Econ and Acc. I think it really is about putting in the work. I would study for ACC 200 for about two days and get A's easily. Finance I study for two days and I will get an 80. So make sure you have time allotted to prepare.

Professor Brau has a lot of energy but definitely caters towards a particular type of student. He talks about weightlifting and the difficulty of his class all of the time. I felt like I was in a summer sales meeting for a lot of the semester. It just depends if that, for lack a of a better word, vibe is something that you want or not.

Brau is so freaking awesome! I absolutely loved how his class was structured. The only grades that are in the textbook are the tests but it gives you plenty of time to just study and learn the material! He tells you EXACTLY what is going to be on the test and what you have to study! Just put in the work, learn the notes and you will do just fine.

Professor Brau is very caring and delivers his lectures in an engaging way. While I don't want to take Finance again, I would take a different class from Brau again. Finance is just not my forte. The only assignments you have are exams, but he is very clear about what's on the exams. He doesn't grade you on attendance, but class is VERY beneficial.

Brau is an exceptional guy and is always willing to help his students! His daily spiritual thoughts are the best. That being said, his class is really challenging. Brau repeatedly says to learn his notes like the back of your hand and it works! Learn his notes and do practice problems and you will do fine. "That's hola, brah."
I love his lectures. Demanding but very upfront about what will be on the tests (which constitute your whole grade).
It's 100% tests, so be ready. That being said, he is passionate about his students and very willing to offer outside help.

Heads up: the class is graded off only tests. That being said, Professor Brau is phenomenal, he is caring, takes time to listen and teaches the material. The tests can be really difficult. If you want to succeed, keep dicipline and study a bit everyday because you will only get an A if you really, really understand the material inside and out.

I learned a lot in P. Brau's class, but mostly in the later chapters about entrepreneurship and personal finance. He gives great spiritual thoughts and insight into careers and life. I didn't like how the class is only based on test scores and wished there was more variety in the learning. The class size is too big to get any personalized help.

go to class, take good notes, rewatch lectures before the tests, and do the practice tests and research surveys!!! Brau's tests were super hard, but learning how to study is going to be your saving grace. I pulled a solid C on the first test and got As on the last 3 because I changed the way I studied completely and learned the notes like crazy

My favorite Professor I have ever had. He teaches you what you need to know for test so there is not any guessing. Be prepared for the test they are not easy and that is all you are graded on. Gives great life advice, and better spiritual thoughts than my religious courses offer at BYU

Took this class before my mission, loved the man, but I had to take it again for a better grade now. Probably my favorite teacher, its the only class I can pay attention the whole time, his spiritual thoughts hit it out of the park, but I also really like this material. If you hate math/finance/business it won't be an easy class

Graded only on tests. For me, it was either really good notes on lectures or on the online textbook. I feel like if you were good on the book, going to class isn't necessary. You still may want to go since he gives pretty good lectures with spiritual moments and professional development moments. Either way, do the practice exam problems to prepare.

Professor Brau has a lot of energy and his lectures are pretty fast paced. That being said, everything he says is important and worth paying attention too. This class is solely based on tests, but if you go to class, Brau will prepare you for the tests because it is also what you need to know for life. My favorite part were his spiritual thoughts.

I am not a finance major but I took this class to graduate and I didn't hate it. If you are not a good test taker then don't take the class. I don't consider myself a good test taker and I am not a finance person but I still managed to get A's on the tests. Make sure you study the notes good and you should be fine.

Professor Brau is a workhorse and he is proud of that. His class is only lectures and tests. The textbook reading is encouraged, but not required. There is no assigned homework. That is where the difficulty lies: figuring out how to study. Make sure you follow along and take good notes and review frequently. Spiritual thoughts are awesome!

Professor Brau is honestly such a good guy. You can tell that he genuinely cares for his students. His class is extremely difficult but in a good way. The class is completely based on tests, so it requires initiative on the part of the student to make sure every concept is understood thoroughly.

Professor Brau is awesome! He is the most upbeat teacher I have had that makes lectures entertaining. He does go extremely fast though so get ready to write fast. The entire grade is based on tests so study hard and do your best on them. I loved his spiritual thoughts in each lecture.

Professor Brau is a great teacher. Class is pretty tough but makes you stretch yourself and learn the materials. I really enjoyed his spiritual moments. Overall, his class is upbeat and hard but very rewarding and I would recommend everyone to learn finance from him.

Brau is a great professor and teaches really well, but he definitely has his flaws. If you vibe with his energy, you'll have a great experience with his class. I didn't like that he has a very "my way or the highway" attitude about studying. He also talks up his and his kids/friends success as a way to motivate but it can come across as peacocking.

Prof. Brau does a great job of teaching you what you need to know in finance. He is very up front about what is on the tests (mostly lecture based with a few occasional things from the reading), and he builds a lot of time into class to practice and walk through problems, which I really appreciate.

This class was difficult but I really enjoyed it. Your grade is based entirely on 5 tests which can be difficult if you are not a good test taker but there is no busy work which I appreciated. I always left class feeling inspired and motivated to work hard and learn more. Study the notes you take in class, that is what he bases the test on.

Awesome professor, but be prepared to study! He does spiritual thoughts and gives professional development advice every class. This makes class fun, interesting, and worth attending. I would go to class because a lot of what is on his tests he mentions in class. SO GO TO CLASS!

Make sure to do the readings and the practice problems on your own. He goes really fast in the lecture, covers a ton of material and will ask questions about ambiguous things asked in class. 100% of your grade comes from the tests so take really good notes in class and study them. I wish I could take it from Holmes.

If you have to take Finance 201, absolutely take it from Brau. He has no homework (good and bad ya know) so it's on you to learn the material from the textbook/ class lectures but the entire grade is just the midterms and the final. Super funny, wants to help students, and love his spiritual thoughts every single lecture.

His lectures are awesome! He teaches exactly what is on his tests and is very specific to tell you what will be tested. I realized from this class that the Finance major wasn't for me, but he taught in a clear enough way that I could determine that because of the field isn't my passion, not because the class was a bad experience.

Impactful and hilarious, love that he cuts the busy work. Your grade is fully based on exams which can be stressful but you do fine if you pay attention and study. Wish he did a better job explaining concepts to those with little to no experience in finance or business.
He spends sooo much time rambling in lectures, usually talking about himself. His content is good though and the exams were easier than everyone said they'd be

Finance 201 is a tough class, but Professor Brau is a great teacher. His lectures are full of great examples and stories to help you understand finance concepts, but it's really up to you to study the textbook and practice to understand the material.

Dr. Brau is a very good lecturer and packs a LOT of information in his time to also include professional development. It's a difficult course but manageable. His personality is very preachy and performative, he claims to be a safe space for students but his rhetoric in lecture does not match those claims. His comments are inconsistent/problematic.
Really know the lectures and follow what he recommends and you'll do great

I love Jim Brau. His lectures were very inspiring and he gives off a lot of energy that motivates his students to do their best. His class structure, however, was not for me. His lectures are hard to follow and he uses a lot of finance "slang" (abbreviations and real world words) that take a while to get used to and understand.

Dr. Brau has a way of teaching that not only educates but inspires his students to be the best that they can be. Whatever your reason for looking into this class my advice would be to take his class as soon as you can because you'll learn lessons that will be of real value to you throughout your life. I gained so much from this class.

Brau is an old fashioned (no tech in class + handwritten notes) convert/army brat who gives off provo bro vibes but also is very progressive and has a heart of GOLD! It takes a sec to figure him out, but he's a great dude.  His lectures are hard to follow and tests are hard. You may or may not pass the class, but you'll be a better person. :)

I did not love this class nor does the way it's taught work for me but I did appreciate Brau's energy and spiritual thoughts. Finance did not click for me so it took a lot of work and focus and I still might have to retake this class later. It's a great class to take but is a tough one if finance does not come naturally.

Brother Brau is one of the best professors I have ever had at BYU. When you talk about a professor that truly cares about your personal life, success and growth, Brother Brau should be at the top of that list. Your whole grade is tests, so study hard, listen and take good notes. Do all of this and you will get an A in finance!

If you don't test well, don't take this class. The only grades are the four tests and the finals. His lectures are fast-moving even if you've done the preparation reading, but I was always able to catch up if I studied a lot before the exams and it worked out well for me. He gives super inspirational spiritual thoughts every class that I loved.

This is a very hard class. Bro Brau does a really great job at teaching the material but you really need to do the work outside of class (study till your brain explodes) if you want to do good in this class. Each class he gives a spiritual thought and a professional development moment (life advice). My advice to you... study study study
Make sure to watch the recorded lectures again, so the class notes make more sense.
Very test heavy, lectures are worthwhile and content isn't too hard

If you like the idea of a course 100% graded off of 5 tests, then this is the class for you. Procrastinators; beware - haha.

Brau is funny and I genuinely enjoyed going to his lectures. He DOES holds some VERY interesting opinions, which he is always very vocal about, but to me, it just made the class more interesting. Normies; beware.
Finance 201 is just 4 exams and the final. No assignments, just tests.
Had for Fin 201, 100% of grade was determined by tests. The lectures were interesting and he includes spiritual thoughts/professional development moments in each class period.

Professor Brau is not a good professor.  Good person?  Yes.  Good teacher? No.  All he does is go through notes fast and then expect you to know everything for the test without giving you any sort of study guide or outline for tests.  He is passionate about finance but thinks everyone wants to major in that.  Not the case it's a general biz class.

I thought Brau was a great teacher. Your entire grade is dependent on the 4 Mid-course exams and the final, so you have to make sure you are ready for those tests. His lectures I found really interesting and were typically beneficial for those not even studying finance specifically. He is extremely clear with what is going to be on the tests.

Brau is my favorite professor I've had. His class structure is hard for some to follow, but it worked well for me. Your grade is based off of 5 exams. No homework. If you do the readings and pay attention in class, you should do well on the tests! He gives great spiritual thoughts which are a nice break during lecture.

Professor Brau is an absolute beast! You can tell he really knows the material and teaches it in a way that can be applied in real life. It's very clear what you need to do to get an A in the class: memorize his lectures and know how to do the problems, so the tests weren't very hard. I'd definitely recommend Brau to anyone taking this class

Professor Brau is probably my favorite professor at BYU. He cares about the students and making sure you understand Finance, but also wants to help with Spiritual and Professional development. I would definitely recommend any class taken from him!
Professor Brau is one of my favorite professors. I love his passion for finance. He makes me passionate not just about finance but about life.

Professor Brau is a great guy. He cares for all of his students. His class is extremely difficult. The grade is determined by tests. The notes Prof. Brau writes in class are unclear and written in short-hand. I spent a lot of time re-learning the material using the textbook and practice tests. If you care about grades, take from another Prof.

Brau's class is difficult and you have to work hard to get a good grade. That being said he is one of the most influential proffessors I have had at BYU. Teaches financial concepts and how they relate to real life (i.e. buying a house, filing taxes, etc.) very helpful and insightful class for business and non-business majors. 100% would take again.

Professor Brau is awesome and is a very dynamic and fun teacher! His class is only graded by the tests, which is nice but also hard because there's no lee way room. But his tests are fair and he doesn't try to trick you at all - he tells you basically exactly what is on the test, study your notes and practice everyday!!

He's an inspirational teacher that wants to help everyone even if they don't care about finance.  The class is quite difficult because it relies only on tests, and he wants you to memorize all of his notes. If you study hard for his midterms through his notes, you can do well. However, because the final is cumulative, it is really difficult.

Professor Brau is one of the best professors I have ever had. He's funny and caring and super involved. He is also incredibly overqualified to teach Fin 201 and gives incredible real world advice. 11/10 professor, 11/10 human being.

People that rate him low most likely just didn't get along with his teaching strategies and the class might have been too difficult for them (which I can understand). However, he sets you up for success if you just do what he says. Know the notes, review the lectures, and you'll do fine.

I love finance. I'm 21, buy real estate, and have invested every paycheck since I was 13. Brau dissuaded me from pursuing a finance degree. He has a do-or-die mentality with learning, which stunts a lot of students' growth. Yeah, you throw some mud on a wall, and some of it will stick. But students aren't mud, and neither is a BYU education.

Brau's class only consists of overwhelming lectures and 5 difficult exams. The few class materials DO NOT reflect what is on the test/ the difficulty of the test. Do not take this class if you need homework and study materials to do well in a class. This class may be helpful for prospective finance majors, but avoid it if you are not one!!!
Nice professor but very difficult class. Your entire grade comes from exams so be ready to study a lot. Exams are very difficult. Great content, hard class.
Amazing lectures, don't miss them. He's super clear what will be on the test. But tests are 100% of your grade

Professor Brau's class was great! He is a super awesome guy and his lectures are inspirational and motivating. Class is 100% graded by tests (which are pretty hard), but if you study hard you can do well in the class.
Professor Brau doesn't assign any homework. His class is literally just 5 tests. He is an awesome guy and an amazing lecturer. I really enjoyed his class though it was a lot of hard work.

When he explains how to do well in the class LISTEN! I am a pretty good academic student, but you cannot skip reading and do well in this class. The only grades are four tests and a final. Other than that Professor Brau is great! His lectures have inspired me so many times and the information on personal finance is very relevant to anyone.

Brau is an amazing person! I honestly really enjoyed hearing his spiritual outlook on life. On the other hand, His class was super hard and overwhelming. Your grade in his class is based on only a few exams so if you are not a good exam taker this class is not for you!

Brau is an amazing person but his class maxed my stress and anxiety. The exams were hard and the exam prep available to us did not prepare us for the exams. Also your grade is entirely based on tests.

There are many concepts in this class that are difficult to grasp, and Professor Brau does not give enough resources to students to help them understand. Homework is important, and if he took the time to give us assignments and resources, his students could have learned much more effectively. Other than that, he is amazing at what he does.

VERY HARD. The whole class revolves around your test grade and almost all of your learning will be done in the finance lab and by yourself. He will not take finance questions during office hours and goes on tangents every class that usually take up large parts of lecture time. Overall, do not take it from him unless you feel like making life hard.

Grades are straightforward- 4 midterms, lowest one dropped and the final each worth 25% of your grade. He emphasizes this in class but test questions come from the lecture notes, so learn and understand them. I'd recommend going through the practice questions before each test. He's an awesome professor who prepares his students for future careers.

Professor Brau is one of the most genuine, caring, entertaining professors at BYU. To be clear, his introductory finance class is insane--intense lectures, exams make up full grade, lots of stress. Get ready to work your tail off for this class. But he has great advice and it's an awesome class for anyone interested in the finance program.

Prof. Brau clearly outlines what is necessary and crucial to be successful in his class. His lectures are well-organized and helpful. Make sure you read before the lectures so that the lecture just fills in and helps the reading. He does a great job balancing work and humor during class, and he brings a lot of energy to the table every class!

He seems very intense at first (and he is) but he is also very caring and very effective. He has great class structure and management and can very spiritual and inspiring. His grading is 100% based on exam scores so be prepared to study extra hard on his exams, but he makes sure everything you need to know is in the notes.

One of the greatest teachers at BYU. He goes VERY fast and seems to expect you to have a slight background in finance. ONLY thing in gradebook is exams!!!! You can drop the lowest if you do 3 research surveys. There is a curve. All this said, I would still take him again. My testimony has grown so much b/c of him and he teaches real world material!

Professor Brau is an amazing professor and his lectures are entertaining and spiritually uplifting. He's an intense guy, but knows his stuff and is good at teaching. The material can be difficult, but there isn't any required homework. Read the textbook before class and TAKE GOOD NOTES. Grade is entirely based on 4 midterms and a final.

Tough but good class. Prof B is an energetic teacher, but he can't teach very well. I spent a lot of time on Youtube learning the concepts he tried to teach in class. I always attended the same 9:30am and 2:00pm lecture bc this man talks so fast. The class is manageable, but just know it's going to be tough.
He is an entertaining lecturer! I really liked him but be prepared to completely memorize your notes that he takes during class!

Honestly one of the best professors I've had at BYU. His class is hard but it is because the material is difficult. If you study hard and pay attention in class, then you should do fine. The tests are hard, but you expect that at BYU. No homework or quizzes, just midterms and a final. He drops the lowest midterm. He connects well with students.
Very useful class. As a non-business school major, I learned a lot of useful skills and knowledge that can be applied to my career and life.

I really enjoyed this class, but it definitely wasn't the easiest class I've taken. Your grade is only based on exams so keep that in mind. I personally liked not having to do any extra busy work and it allowed me to put the time I personally needed into this class. He also does a spiritual thought in the middle of class, which was my favorite.

So much respect for this man. He is moves really quickly through material, but is very clear about what is on the exam. There are 4 midterms and a final (the only things on your grade). I wish I had taken this freshman year, it opened my eyes to so many opportunities I've missed now since I'm a senior. It's hard, but don't let that stop you!

Bro. Brau is an amazing professor. Take Fin 201 from him. He has clear expectations and communicates them well. Take notes in class and make flashcards from them and you will get an A (I got 100% on 3 midterms). Only grades are 4 midterms and 1 final. Content exclusively useful to life and career (no jazz and fluff). Rigorous but very manageable.

Bro Brau is an incredible person, he would genuinely be willing to help anyone out in ANY hard situation they are going through. I also loved how aware he is with less prominent groups at our university or in the finance major: including women, people of color, LGBTQ+, and non-member students. As for teaching, he rushes through material too quickly

Professor Brau is tough but fair. He tells you from the start, know his lecture notes, pay attention and make connections. He teaches the concepts of finance well, relating them to the real world. Lots of energy in his teaching style but thats what this class needs! Not gonna lie though, it's a tough class. His spiritual thoughts were my favorite.

Bro Brau is a great guy and really cares about his students. If you have to take finance 201, he's a good option. The tests are really really hard, and there are zero other assignments. If you don't have to take finance 201, don't. If you want to learn basic finance stuff then take a personal finance class. Overall great guy, really hard class.

Brau was a great teacher. He only teaches what you need to know in real life. I wish he would have done exam reviews and had more example problems. I learn best through repetition, but did not get a lot of opportunities for that. Study the crap out of his class notes before the tests and do the practice problems he does give and you'll be fine.

A great guy who clearly loves his students and wants them to succeed. Take good notes and you will do great on the tests! He is very transparent about what is on the tests, so just pay attention and enjoy the class!

You want to attend class because he gives you everything that you need to know. He is super energetic and gives amazing spiritual thoughts and career tips. This class has little assignments so tests are your grade.
Pay attention in class and study notes from lectures for exams.

Professor Brau is a great guy and knows his stuff! His course is tough in the sense you will be graded by few assignments, but if you're down to teach yourself everything via the textbook you can get through. His spiritual thoughts/professional advice make going to class worth it.
Study the notes from class and you'll be fine on the tests. Class is always entertaining, so it double pays off to attend, even though it's not mandatory.

Best teacher I've had yet at BYU. His class is so interesting and he does an awesome job at keeping students engaged in class. It's a very hard class but he tells you literally what will be on the tests. Just learn your notes really well and read the chapters and you'll get a good grade. You definitely have to work hard for your grade.

The tests are highly weighed. Make sure you study your notes. You will have plenty of resources available to you; however, you need to be self-disciplined to actually do the studying on a consistent basis because there is no homework, only tests.
Brau the goat fr fr. Tests can be lightweight hard no cap but if you study the notes and read the textbook you boolin. Bruv keeps things one hunnid wit you da whole semester if for the people fosho

Brother Brau is awesome! Finance 201 has a fair amount of content but Brother Brau makes it entertaining, and the lectures just fly by, easily one of my favorite professors at BYU. He cares a lot about student's being successful in his class and in life in general. Take finance from Brau!

Brother Brau is an awesome teacher. He really knows what he's talking about. His spiritual thoughts are also super uplifting. That being said, his class is really hard, especially if you're not going into business or aren't a business minded person. The only grades in the class are the tests, and you have to memorize EXACTLY what's on the notes.

Although FIN 201 is difficult (no formula sheets are provided on tests and content requires lots of practice to master), Professor Brau makes the class worth it. He focuses on applying content to the real world with engaging and energetic lectures. Brau also holds excellent professional development moments and spiritual thoughts during class.

Professor Brau is a good teacher, who is very knowledge of Finance. You know right from the beginning what you need to study. The issue I had was that after each exam, you are unable to review what you missed. Creating knowledge gaps, this adds up overtime. I am not a Finance person, so be prepared to study and use the TA lab consistently.

Hands down the best teacher at BYU. He cared about our success in life and not just teaching the material. Treats us like we are his kids, meaning he trys to give us the best advice as well as deliver awesome spiritual messages.

Finance is a beast in and of its own, but if you have to tackle it, take it with Brau. He is a straight shooter, in that he prepares you for the real world, your job, and he doesn't try to trick you on his tests. He teaches very clearly and he gives you all the resources to succeed in learning the principles of Finance.
He is a great professor! He is really driven by gospel topics, and God in general. I would definitely take him again. The tests are hard, but study the notes super well and you will be fine.

He teaches really fast so read through the textbook chapter prior to class. Your grade is based off exams only and there aren't any TA review sessions. Study what he teaches in class and make sure you can run the practice problems. He gives really awesome professional development moments and spiritual thoughts everyday that are the best!
A great class and a great professor. Take finance from Brau.

The spiritual thoughts were the best part of his class. He is respectful and not one of those "Let's say a pray to start this off just to say that we are religious" He is genuine and NOT pushy at all.
The book is absolutely not mandatory. Never read it and only studied his notes and got above a 93 on all the exams. Prepares you for the real world.

I highly recommend this class! Professor Brau prepares his students for the real world and his spiritual thoughts were so inspiring. Make sure to take good notes during his lectures to do well on the tests!

Professor Brau is a good teacher. He prepares us with knowledge to use in the real world and possible questions for interviews for internships. He covers a lot of content which is a bit difficult to follow due to his handwriting sometimes. Overall Professor Brau is good but the content and the speed at which it is covered can be overwhelming

Lectures are entertaining and very applicable to life. Highly recommend. Take it seriously at the start and consistently study and you will enjoy the semester

Professor Brau teaches so well. Everything he teaches is on the test and can be applied to the real world. The tests are hard but as long as you study hard, you'll get a good grade. Amazing professor!!
Brau is such a good guy. I really loved coming to class and learning from him. Get ready to work!!

Professor Brau is the best! His class is hard but if you attend the lecture, memorize his in class notes, and study hard.. you can get an A. He only teaches things you will use in the real world. He also gives great spiritual thoughts!

I highly recommend taking a class from this professor. He really cares about each of his students, and is incredibly good at teaching financial concepts.
He gives spiritual thoughts in class. They are really powerful and inspiring.

Professor Brau is amazing. He is great at explaining difficult concepts and is helpful when answering questions. He was always very honest with us about what we should know. If you come to class and learned the notes really well, you'll do well in his class. The only grades in 201 come from 4 midterms and 1 final exam, so be prepared for that.

Jim Brau is a fantastic and brilliant man. His lectures are entertaining and he cares about being at BYU and his students. His teaching style just didn't work at all for me. You had to go into lecture with at least some idea of what he was talking about. If you are passionate about finance already he would be the perfect teacher. Rounds up a lot
This man is amazing. Be prepared to work hard and nail class notes, that's the key to getting a good grade.

Professor Brau is very good at lecturing and writing the textbook. His tests are what are the hardest part of his course. He only grades the exams so there is no way to get a good grade unless you do well on the tests. He does go over everything in his lectures that will be on the test but there also seems to be extra.

I love Dr. Brau's teaching style. His lectures are incredibly focused and organized.  He tells you exactly what you need to know for the exams so if you study your notes thoroughly, you will do well. I would recommend reading the chapter before class to become familiar with the material. His lectures are inspirational and hilarious. Love the guy!!
Spiritual thoughts are amazing. Hes a great guy. Tests are so hard. Read before you come to class. Know your notes for the test. Really try to understand things don't just memorize.

Good class and teacher. Teaches you what you need to know for real life. Lectures are recorded on zoom. Only things that go towards your grade are tests and final (comprehensive) exam. Brau gives you everything needed to success on tests.
I love this dude! His spiritual thoughts every class had a big effect on my testimony and learning experience. He really knows his stuff. Study hard and you will do great.

Professor Brau knows a lot about Finance but assumes that everyone in his INTRO class are prospective Finance majors, who have previous experience with living and breathing Finance. His handwriting is barely legible, even though he teaches old school by writing all of his notes by hand. His TA's almost never knew the answers to my questions.
One of the best professors I've had at BYU

Great class with awesome lectures. Very intense but good teacher overall. Keeps your attention with his different way of teaching. Only grades the tests and they are heavily based on lectures. Very inspirational class and he seems to really want the best for your future.

This class was incredible!!! Dr. Brau is careful to ensure that we have the tools that we need in order to be successful. Due to the structure of the class, I was able to focus on learning rather than doing busy work that was not relevant. There aren't shortcuts in this class, but I'm grateful for that!

Professor Brau is a great guy that really cares about his students and wants to prepare them for the real world. But be warned, the tests make up the entirety of your grade and they are TOUGH. Get ready to work hard and take really good notes.

Brau is the sickest teacher ever. I respect teachers like him that are straightforward about what is on the test, and he will tell you all the material that's on the test. I really vibed with him because it's very apparent that he's constantly striving to be better.

Brother Brau's FIN 201 class is phenomenal. Material is very in depth. Grades in the class consist of 4 midterms and a final. All exams are part qualitative, part quantitative. Keys to success in the class are taking notes in class everyday, studying consistently rather than cramming, and reading the online textbook before and after class.

Professor Brau is probably not for everyone but I learned a lot from him! He's extremely fast-paced and comes off as rather aggressive, but there's nothing in his class that I felt was irrelevant for the real world. He is very open about and strong in his faith, shares a spiritual thought and professional development moment every class.

Brother Brau was a great professor for me, although he is not for everyone. Your entire grade is based off of 5 exams, and the lowest one gets dropped. The exams are not easy, but if you read the textbook before class and pay attention you will be fine. His lectures kept me engaged. He gives a really good spiritual thought which is a nice break.

Bro. Brau does a phenomenal job of giving you a clear direction on the course content and what will be on his tests. The grade is four midterms and a final, so no assignments to pad those scores. If you learn how to study his notes, you're good to go!

Brau is a great guy and I appreciated how spiritual he was, but the class was extremely difficult for nonbusiness majors. I'm sure it was great for finance majors or those joining the program, but there were lots of things we were expected to know that I couldn't have known since I had to take the class for an unrelated major. Tests were very hard.

Professor Brau is a great teacher, but very intense. Though intense, he prepares students for the real world. You must attend all lectures; he will tell you exactly what you need to know for the tests! Your grade is made up of your four midterms and final, if you are not a good test taker don't take this class!

His lectures keep you engaged and interested, but his tests are so hard to prepare for. I would study a ton and go into the test only to realize that I had studied all the wrong things. I learned a lot but if you want to make sure you get a good grade I would take it from a different professor.

He is hilarious, and he cares a lot about his students. His lectures are VITAL to getting a good grade in his class. Four exams plus a final, and that's your grade. The tests are straightforward, but the problems require that you master the concepts. Be ready to study hard for his exams!

Brau is the best professor I have ever had! Do the reading but mainly come to class and take super good notes (write down everything he writes). Study the notes for the test more than anything! Homework and readings don't count for anything in your grade - only tests.

The only thing that matters is the tests, but class is set up to make it very clear what is on the tests. It's VERY straightforward and just takes work. Stay caught up on reading before class, pay attention in class, and study a bit outside of class and you will do great!

Brau is amazing. He cares so much about his students he will meet at VASA with you to talk about whatever you would like. He lets you know exactly what will be on the test if you watch the lectures. He gives an amazing spiritual thought and professional development experience each day

He is amazing, honestly, he is the best professor I have had. However, the class is hard. Simple as that, you'll have to put the work in, and while I did and still did not get the grade I wanted, I would 100% take it from him again. Brau is a beast, and hopefully, you win the march madness brackets!!

Professor Brau is a beloved member of BYU faculty, is extremely qualified to teach finance, and is very experienced in the realm of finance. He is personable and caring towards the students and teaches as a labor of love. He cares a great deal about the careers and success of his students just as much as their happiness.

Brother Brau keeps it real. Every class includes a spiritual thought and a career development moment. 

Some people will tell you that the tests are difficult, but as long as you know the notes from class, they're very straightforward. 

Best part: there's absolutely no busy work. If you know the material you don't have to do any homework.

Dr. Brau really cares about his students and goes above and beyond to help you feel loved and give you the resources you need.  I am a bad test taker, and the class is graded ENTIRELY with exams (Brutal).  Lectures are great.  He bases exams on notes, but you cannot review past exams to see what you missed.  If bad at tests, prepare to die inside.

Professor Brau is passionate about what he does and cares about each individual's success, both in and outside of his class! I really enjoyed his lectures because he is a dynamic teacher, explains concepts well, and share spiritual thoughts and professional development moments. Your grade only comes from exams, so have the discipline to not cram!

Brau's a West Point graduate from Tallahassee - you already know the class is high energy and entertaining. He's funny while still explaining everything clearly. You have to go back and review, though, otherwise you will not do well. It's high paced, but completely doable.

If you haven't taken Brau's class, be glad you're reading this because you definitely should take this class from him.  He is the best teacher I have ever had because he cares.  His class requires work but its one of the classes you learn from if you get a good grade.  Go STEROID MODE and you'll enjoy this class as much as I did!  Thanks Brau!
I really liked how Professor Brau incorporated the gospel into every single principle that we learned. It was a very self-motivated class which made it hard if you fell behind at all.
This class is really difficult so put in the time to learn! TA labs are open which is helpful. Brother Brau will tell you everything you need to know for the test, just really study your notes.
Study the class notes and you'll be fine.

Bro Brau is a legend! I felt truly inspired, spiritually uplifted, and hyped every class. He gave REAL life financial advice and about graduating, getting a job, etc. His class was invaluable to me, although it was intense. Lots of studying and the only thing in the grade book is tests. Yet, I would do it again. Be prepared to work hard though!

Teaches very quickly. Take notes on what he says about the notes he writes. 
Gives a spiritual message each lesson and begins with a prayer. 
Definitely take him if you're a finance major, he makes sure you know what you're doing.

Professor Brau is such a great guy! His class is definitely test heavy but there are TA hours every day so if you feel like you are falling behind or need extra help, there is always someone to help you. All you need to know for his tests are the class notes...seriously that's it! Plus, he's hilarious and his lectures are very entertaining!!
Teaches well, only worth studying in-class notes.

Professor Brau is intense!  If you are taking Finance to learn Finance, this is the class for you. If you are taking Finance to pass, take it from someone else. No assigned homework, but you'll end up doing more outside of class than inside anyway to keep up. I've been at BYU for a year and a half and this is the hardest class I've taken.

The grade only consists of midterms and finals. STUDY HIS NOTES. The tests are exactly what he writes in class and often tells you tests answers. He is a great teacher. Take Fin201 from Brau. You will learn so much.

He has a lot of passion for the subject and love for the students. Sometimes I question his teaching methd of only lectures and showing his notes on the projector, but he does tell you exactly what you need to know for the test. If you follow in class and study the notes its an easy class.

Professor Brau is an amazing person! He is kind and will work with you on any problem you have in life. His class is difficult because there are only test grades but the tests reflect the notes he goes over in class. I can count on one hand how many questions on all of the tests the entire year were things he did not explicitly go over in class.

I love Professor Brau! His class is hard, but if you put in the time and effort you will do well. If you attend the lecture, read the textbook and study what Bro Brau says you need to know you will do good on the tests.

Great Professor! At first, I was cautious about how he takes notes (Does them by hand on a projector), but after the first couple of classes, I enjoyed doing it that way. Your grade for the class is based on 4 midterms and a final. Really enjoyed the energy of the professor. He really cares about his students and does all he can to help them.
Tests are pretty difficult and that's literally the only thing that goes into grades.
Solid class. No homework, just 100% tests. Study his notes and do the practice a day or two before, and you will do excellent

Brau's tests are extremely fair. Every question has a clear reference to something that was explicitly stated in class. Brother Brau does a great job explaining the material clearly. The hardest part about the class is that your entire grade is dependent on 4 midterms and a final. Takes notes on a piece of paper and projects it to the class. All grades are from tests. If this is your style of learning he is great for you. It was not for me, I prefer graded assignments to get me to do the work and actually learn. No formula sheet.

Professor Brau is a great teacher and really knows almost everything when it comes to finance. I struggled to keep up in his class because I'm not a finance major and haven't ever studied anything business related. If you're like me and have no basic understanding of finance, this class is going to be a grind. But overall he is a great professor.
Great professor, if your study his notes you'll do fine!

Really study the notes taken in class. You need to know everything talked about the notes super well to be able to get A's on the test. The class is based 100% on the midterms and the final, so be prepared for that.

Brother Brau is a great guy but he treats his class like everyone is going into the Finance Major. He runs the course like we are all in the core of the finance major. There are 4 tests and 1 final and that is your grade. No formula sheet. Get ready to memorize 50 formulas and no study guide either for the test and the test is only offered one day.
He is a super funny guy who tries his hardest the teach the best way he knows how. He isn't perfect but puts some serious effort into showing love to his students and into helping them learn.

Super great guy. Awesome Professor. He really knows his stuff when it comes to Finance and boy did I just suck it up. Really hard if you're a senior and this is in your way to graduate. Professor Brau is an amazing teacher. He is an inspiring and funny lecturer. I really liked the way that he emphasized understanding the intuition behind the things that we learned. Prof. Brau is honestly one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He's NOT interested in tricking you with test questions: he tells you exactly what will be on the tests and nothing more nor less. 
The main thing you have to do to succeed is master your notes, use the practice materials on LS and you'll get an A.

Brau was such an awesome teacher. The tests are almost completely based on class so you better come to class and be prepared to study well but it's worth it. It's all real-world knowledge and super helpful. For sure take this class from Brau. His spiritual thoughts from the book of Mormon were always the highlight of the class.

I think Professor Brau is very knowledgeable about finance, and a great teacher. However, I did not enjoy this class at all. You are only graded on the midterms and the final. JIm Brau is engaging and passionsate about what he teaches. You need to show up to class and take hand written notes along with going through the online textbook. I would advise forming a study group to do problems with.

Entire grade comes from exams but that is what you sign up for. If you take good notes and know them well, you will do good in the class. I personally didn't figure out how to know the notes for tests and that is why I didn't do better in the class. Only professor that has lived up to my expectations at BYU so far.
Brau is very clear in how he goes about the class. I enjoy his spiritual thoughts and professional development moments. I feel like they break up the class well.

Professor Brau is amazing. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Every class he has a spiritual thought and a professional development moment. These are so amazing. Dont let the tests scare you. Just take good notes and study those notes. If you study the notes you will do so well in the class! Brau is amazing!
Super awesome teacher! Has a lot of good energy and his lectures are super interesting. Tough class, all your grade lies on how you do on the exams, but doable. Great class

I think it was a great class and although it was difficult, it forced me to study hard and really learn about the finance principles. There are 4 exams and a final. If you do surveys you can drop the lowest test score that is not the final.
If I was a finance major I would have loved the class. Because I am not, I did not enjoy how hard it was as a business general course. Don't take Brau's class if you are not a finance major.

So the class really doesn't require to much time in my opinion, you got to study a bunch for the tests, but besides that there isn't any graded homework so average weekly hours put in aren't that bad. His tests are based  mostly on the notes, take more time studying them because the tests will as you very specific words and concepts from the notes.

So in this class, you are ONLY graded on the 4 exams and the final. There is no homework or attendance or quiz grades. So to do well, you HAVE to read the textbook. But Brother Brau is fantastic in class. He teaches simply, is open to questions and shares stories from his own life to make things more interesting and apply the concepts to real life.
Brau makes the difficulty of finance enjoyable.
Great Professor and class! The class is super straightforward and easy to do well as long as you study and know the class notes.
Your final grade is based solely upon exam which can be good or bad. He tells you exactly what you need to know and if you follow along with the notes you will be well prepared for the exams.

Professor Brau has one purpose in mind. he wants us to be successful in life. This class is directly applicable to real life He is very clear about what is going to be on the test. As long as you do practice problems and learn your notes, you will succeed in this class! He is inspirational in every way.
Brau is by far one of my favorite professors. He has amazing lectures that are very entertaining. He teaches concepts in a way that is applicable to real life. Would recommend 100%.

Brother Brau is simply the most amazing professor I have had at BYU. He is very entertaining in the classroom- he is the only professor that I don't zone out during lectures. He was an amazing professor. He is very clear about what is on the tests. He also gives amazing spiritual thoughts. He really cares about his students.

Brother Brau is genuinely such a nice, caring guy. This class was difficult, but as long as you study the way he tells you to, you'll do fine on the exams. I feel like the class could be taught in a more intuitive way.

Brau is a great guy, but his tests can be difficult. Study the notes you take in class and you should be good for the tests. Brau is a super spiritual professor and he shared some great insights. It was sometimes difficult to read and follow Brau's notes in class.

I enjoyed Professor Brau's lectures. He writes down the notes and you copy them down as you go. Studying these before the tests will be VERY beneficial. I don't like test heavy classes but I really liked his class. Here's basically all you need to know:

Prof. Brau is direct and to the point which makes expectations super clear for exams. He is passionate about 3 major things: the church, his family, and lifting (oh, and finance). Your grade is only based on 4 midterms and your final. He covers a lot of material in his lectures. Spend some time studying and going to the TA lab during the semester and you will do well. Make sure you know everything that he goes over during his lectures. Review your notes. He is an awesome professor and very inspirational.

Brau is a phenomenal teacher.  He's energetic and teaches very clearly. He's a bit intense and hands off, but if you spend some time on the class you'll do fine.

James Brau is easily the most respected Professor at BYU. The notes he takes in class are exactly what is on the test and he prepares you perfectly for it if you are prepared by reading the textbook before hand, and use the additional practice resources as well. Every day he shares a spiritual thought and professional development advice.

Professor Brau is an engaging and passionate lecturer -- he gets and keeps you excited about finance! 100% of your grade in this class comes from 4 midterms (one of which is dropped) and a final. Nice guy and knows his stuff. Tries applying finance to the real world and not necessarily to just the class which wasn't the best for me as I don't want to go into Finance and was just taking as a prereq but if you are going into Finance at BYU then I recommend him.

I loved Professor Brau's FIN 201 class. He deeply cares about his students and about their future success, and everything he does in class he does to help his students succeed. That being said, his class is not an easy one. It takes a lot of work to get an A, but it is well worth it.

Prof Brau is SUCH A GOOD GUY. Prof Brau is a phenomenal human being, and he records his lectures which was SO useful. Professor Brau cares about his students as real people which is refreshing. He always gives professional and future advice because he wants us to be happy and successful. He shares spiritual insights every class which are often really inspiring. This was a difficult class for me because it's fast and the grade is just the 4 tests and the final.

Bro Brau gives the best spiritual thoughts I've ever heard at BYU. Just study to Bro Brau's lectures and you'll be great!

Bro Brau is a good man, he gives great spiritual thoughts, but he's intense. He speaks so fast and it sounds like he's yelling at you personally. He is very passionate about what he teaches and so it makes it more interesting to learn about the things he teaches. He has a huge ego which makes lectures not enjoyable. There is no way to see what you did wrong on previous tests, so you don't know what to improve on. Took this class because of his great ratings and it was my biggest regret. Beware!

Finance 201 with Brother Brau is a difficult course, but not impossible. The only thing graded is tests, though most test material comes out of the class notes. Always do your readings before class. Bro Brau is an excellent teacher with so much passion behind his teaching. As long as you take good notes, study, and understand them, the tests are relatively straight forward.

Heres how its set up: read the online textbook before class, go to an awesome lecture, study hard and take the midterm. Only grades in the whole class are the midterms and the final. 

One of my favorite professors at BYU. He is funny and caring and respectful and knowledgeable. He shares spiritual thoughts that help me feel good and hyped for life

Professor Brau prides himself on covering everything that is on the test in his lectures. Taking notes is very important in his class! He is an amazing teacher that has helped me become a more professional individual more so than any other teacher. He respects others and their opinions and expects the best of his students. Dr. Brau is awesome! The only downside is his high-paced lecture speed. If you want to understand finance and take a class that is worth the money you pay for college then take it from Dr. Brau. Entertaining, inspirational and high energy! The entire class is 4 midterms and 1 final. There is no homework so you actually have time to study the material. All of his test questions come from the guided notes you take in class, so write everything down. Look forward to spiritual thoughts and professional development moments every class!

Jim Brau is someone that will teach you lessons to apply to your life. He has helped me in more ways than just finance. He is intense and his tests are really difficult but he does his best to prepare you.

AMAZING! This course has grown me as a student and a person. It is fast and stressful, which is hard to appreciate at the beginning, but after enduring it, I wouldn't have it any other way. Brau is genius and truly cares for his students. I strongly advise memorizing the notes - this changed my test scores from 60's to 95's.

Great guy. The class is very applicable to the real world. My only complaint would be a lack of TA reviews before the midterms and final. The entire grade is based on the exams and comprehensive TA reviews before the midterms and final would've been much appreciated.

Dr. Brau is one of the most chill professors I've ever had. He is such a bro and is passionate about everything he does in his class. This isn't an easy class, but Dr. Brau does a great job of teaching. Your grade comes solely from tests. The tests come almost entirely from the notes he writes in class, with a few questions from the textbook.
Bro Brau is great, teaches well and clearly, if you take notes and study the notes you will do well. Lectures are high speed.

Brau makes it so incredibly clear what's going to be on the test. He goes hard, but it's very fair. Study his notes and that's LITERALLY all you need to know for the test. That's no exaggeration. It will not be on a test if it's not on the notes.
Fin 201 is a challenging class. This man teaches you finance in steroid mode! Memorize all the notes he gives in class: no homework but has rigorous tests.

Test heavy but very engaging. His lectures move pretty quickly but if you've read the book beforehand you'll keep up just fine. He's very clear about what's on the test so if you know your notes and do the practice tests on learning suite you'll do great. Makes time every day for a spiritual thought and professional development moment.
Brau is a very straight forward and motivational guy. He tells you exactly what you need to know for the test. You have to study the notes not so much the book. Go to class. Class is chill.

I loved Professor Brau. His class is challenging, but if you go to class and do the readings, youll understand. Professor Brau is great, he wants to help his students with problems they may have, his class is great despite being a bit harder, and he has a spiritual moment in every class that helped me. His class grade is 100% exams. There is no homework but there is a lot to study. All of the information on the exams comes from the notes in class and from the assigned reading. Loved taking this class by Bro. Brau. Very engaging and full of energy. Class moved at a reasonable pace and was easy to digest as long as you kept up with the readings. This is the right professor to take if you want to be a Finance major. If you are a Landscape Management Major like me DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM BRO. BRAU. He was really nice and a good person, but super intense and his class feels specifically for finance majors.

The class is really great, he is an amazing teacher and it is super helpful. However you have to be on your A game for these tests because that's the only thing on your grade and they are hard.

Professor Brau is great at getting you to learn the material because the only things that contribute to your grade are the tests. He shares great spiritual thoughts everyday. Professor Brau was super great in the lectures and is very passionate for finance. He always brought the spirit with his spiritual thoughts and gave great advice with his daily development. Professor Brau is a good teacher, but his class is tough! You need to really emphasize this class if you want to succeed, around 20 hours a week to be able to get the grade you want in this class

Professor Brau is great at explaining exactly what will be on his tests, but you still need to study a ton to be able to do well. I loved learning Finance from him, but only take his class if you’re ok with your entire grade being based on 4 tests.

I feel that Brau's teaching method didn't really work for me. He was very fast-paced. He mostly just writes on a piece of paper that he puts on a projector in front of the whole class. For some that might be effective, but it wasn't for me. I respect the guy and I feel his lectures are engaging.

Hardest class I've ever taken, but worth it. He makes learning finance fun. You really have to study though, a lot! If you really want to learn, you'll learn and do well. If you're not willing and able to put in the time, good luck.

He is such an amazing Professor and is a really good teacher. His class is super hard though and he want you to take it more seriously than any of your other classes. He is a very spiritic instructor and talks at about a million miles an hour. Only the try-hards should take his class

Great professor! If you're willing to work, you'll do well. My advice: Read the chapter and take good notes before class. Pay good attention and take notes on his notes during class. A perfect example of a professor that has a doctorate degree but lacks a general sense of how to teach so that it can be understood. He uses a lot of acronyms and his hand writing is horrendous. Bro. Brau is a great guy who seems to really care about his students. That being said, his FIN201 class is quite difficult. Brau was an inspirational teacher, but his class was incredibly hard. Grade is based on 5 tests, thats it. No homework, four tests piece of cake. I was originally scared of the class, but he drops one midterm and they arent hard at all if you know the notes and know some accounting. One of the earliest 100s ever.

Jim is great! No homework. 4 tests and a final. If you go to class and take good notes you'll be totally fine. (it's easy to take notes because he tells you exactly what to take notes on) It does take work but it isn't as impossible as people make it seem.

Brau has changed my life. He is an INCREDIBLE human. Just know if you take his class, you will learn spiritual and career lessons that will impact the rest of your life. Brau is pure gold. If you want a solid foundation for financial learning, he is great.

Prof. Brau was one of the best professors I've ever had. He's super passionate about finance and pretty much everything else he does. The class is all tests, but if you don't attend class, study, or do the readings, you likely will not do well on the tests.

Brau is likely the most understanding and sympathetic professor you will have. Concepts of the class are difficult but his lectures break them down well. There are ample resources for help in the class. He drops your lowest test score which will almost definitely come in handy.

Brau cares so much! He is willing to work with all his students even when he has a billion of them. He shows he cares, and also teaches the class well. I have SO much respect for Professor Brau- there is not a more genuine, unselfish, and compassionate person. He is very good at teaching lectures and offers many resources to students. BEST TEACHER AT BYU. BEST PERSON AT BYU. BEST FATHER AT BYU.

class is 100% based on test scores so just go to class and take good notes and you should do great. He is a great teacher!
