His class is fun as far as finance goes, but it can be confusing. The good part is he gives TONS of time for people to get help and so many opportunities for everyone. His TA's help with the homework so you can't fail it, but it is challenging in that it takes time and practice to get a good grade. It you're going to take finance, take it from Brau
Bro. Brau is great! He really cares that you understand the material. He goes the extra mile to help you if you need it. He makes class fun and exciting! Definitely the best FIN201 Teacher.
Dr. Brau is a good guy. He wants his students to succeed and he provides a legitimate TA team to help students with assignments. His class was difficult for me but he is a motivating professor.

Br. Brau is the man. He always is pumped to teach finance. The test requires that you really understand the concepts, not just memorize. Wasn't the easiest class for me but maybe finance just isn't my thing.

Love Brau. First day of class he played Space Jam music. Always pumped to teach. He goes through material quickly-key to success is reading text before class. Very fair tests-he teaches to the tests but expects you to be able to expand problem on own. I like him because he teaches intuition, not just equations. Hard class if you're not prepared

Jim Brau is a great guy. I love his spiritual thoughts. I honestly get lost in class because he jumps all over the place. He doesn't convey the material in a clear way in the lectures. I would like more practice problems in class and in the textbook.

Brother Brau is a nice guy - he definitely loves finance and wants to be a great teacher. However, his class was rushed and very unclear. If you have not taken accounting it will be a very difficult class. I felt that he spent most of the class time justifying the way he taught class instead of teaching. Super rushed, not my favorite class at all.
Dr. Brau is very enthusiastic, and made the class about as interesting as you can make Finance. Would recommend him to others.

This guy is one of my best teachers. He cares A LOT for the students. Homework is only due once a week. There are extra credit opportunities. The tests are fair. My easiest class this semester. He even has a suggestion box so that students can give him suggestions on how to improve the course. The course is complex, but he makes it very simple.

Although the classs was extremely difficult and it covered an incredible amount of material, Professor Brau was the only thing that made it bearable.  His teaching inpsires you to do your best in and out of the classroom.  I have a ton of respect for him and he will always be a role model for my future.

I really think that Brau is a good guy but his teaching  style does not mesh with my learning style.  He is somewhat all over the place when he teaches.  The textbook doesn't provide students with enough practice problems either in my opinion.  Again, as a person, he is a really great guy, I just struggle really learning much during his lectures.
Make sure you do your reading before class.  Lectures make so much more sense that way.

He didn't seem very helpful one on one but he's pretty good in class. He provides a lot of TA's and lets you check your answers with them. All the homework is open book, open note, open friend, open TA which I really liked. His tests aren't too bad but he asks some questions specific to his lectures to punish those who don't go to class.

I felt like I had to teach myself all of the material. Brau's class confused me most of the time. He is a nice guy and his exams and homework are very do-able. Once you understand the material then it is generally easy, but getting to that point is a real pain and takes a lot of time!

Great guy who is super enthusiastic about what he teaches. He is more than willing to help anyone who tries their best and truly wants to succeed. Can be a little unclear and rushed sometimes, but his engaging teaching style makes up for it.

Bro. Brau is another reason that the Marriott School is so cutting edge.  He has real practical knowledge of finance and real interest in student success.  He regularly points out in class when something he writes down is going to be on his test.
Brother Brau is a super likable guy that does a great job explaining finance. The thing I liked the most about him was his enthusiasm for the subject material. I highly recommend him.

Brother Brau is awesome! He is really energetic and teaches very well. The content is difficult, but if you do what you should (read the text, do the home work, go to the lab, and study for the tests) you will be just fine. I enjoyed this class.

Professor Brau is high energy and gets off topic a lot during class which keeps it entertaining but kind of complicates things. His class is very easy though. There is not too much deep thinking and as long as you stay up to date on everything you will do fine.

Brau is energetic and his classes are enjoyable.  Class time tends to be half about how he teaches and half him actually teaching.  I do think that he is very aware of student needs and he adjusts for them to help us out.

Professor Brau is a great teacher!  He does a great job of keeping the class involved and entertaining.  He is very clear with his notes and what is going to be on the test.  That being said, this was a very hard class for me personally.  I would highly recommend using the TA help desk as much as possible.  They help out a lot!!
Really energetic but his tests are a lot harder than questions worked it class.
This is a great class. Very useful. It is very involved, and if you want to do well, you need to read prior to coming to class. There is a lot of memorizing key terms and formulas.

The classes seemed like a waste of time.  Material could have been condensed to 30 mins instead of an hour and 15. Always showed easy problems instead of going in depth.  I heavily relied on TAs and textbook to learn.

Brau is really passionate and really funny.  You need to understand both the equations and the concepts to do well in this class.  You can basically get 100% on everything but that makes the test that much harder.
Helpful.  Fair.
I enjoyed this class. Some of the readings were a little long, but the material is manageable as long as you stay on top of it. Class was generally interesting.

Brother Brau is awesome. He is very passionate about finance and you can feel that in his lectures. His class isn't easy but very interesting and you learn a lot. He really wants each student to do well and will help them out with anything!

Bro. Brau is the best teacher to have for Fin 201. Although he talks fast and his handwriting can be a little hard to read sometimes, he keeps you engaged and entertained. I learned more in this class than I thought I would. He also ties in spiritual moments which keeps you attentive. He and his TA's provide all the opportunities to get an A.
I really enjoyed the class. Yes you have to work, but it is good.
Brother Brau is a great teacher. Sometimes he gets a little too ahead of himself but he definitely puts the material out there that you need to know.

I loved Dr. Brau's class! It is very challenging, but he is a great teacher and keeps the class engaged. He also tries to help his students with the "real world," such as how to build a resume, network, get a job after college, be financially independent, etc.

Bro. Brau is just as passionate about the Gospel as he is finance. He speaks fast so you have to be fully invested. As a teacher he does a great job at making a difficult subject clearer. His tests can definitely work you if you don't go to class so go and pay attention.

Brother Brau is a good teacher. This is the second time I have taken this class from him. The first time I withdrew because I was trying to take accounting at the same time. If you have not taken ACC200 do not attempt this class! Brau uses a lot of terminology used in Accounting and it is easy to get lost if you don't have this prior knowledge.

Dr. Brau is a nice man. He is energetic and keeps students attention. He does seem to make the assumption that students know more than they do at times. Overall, there are plenty of opportunities to succeed. If you do poorly in the class, you have no one to blame but yourself.

Brau is a great guy that gives great spiritual thoughts.  There is no role or in class quizzes.  However, he writes the tests from his notes in class.  His writing is not always clear so be sure to pay attention.  Tests are fair but challenging at the same time. HW due every Friday for the chapters covered that week which is usually 2.

Bro Brau is the sickest teacher at BYU! He knows how to get people pumped up on finance. If you just do the reading, and work out the practice problems, you'll get an A. This dude connects better with students than any professor I've ever had. If you have to take FIN 201, wait to take it from him.

Prof. Brau is GREAT, he loves finance and loves helping people learn finance. The subject matter is tough, but there are tons of opportunities for you to be able to get help and succeed. There is a spiritual thought everyday which helps to bring attention back to the lecture. Pro. Brau also helps to bring the spirit into class which ROCKS.

Good teacher. Very excited about his job. Loves the students and gives great spiritual thoughts. Often he goes a little to fast in class to keep up and his notes don't make sense. Also, between myeducator and learning suite there are a lot of hickups.

I loved this class. Professor Brau is an energetic teacher and that helped to keep me awake. He explained things very clearly and his spiritual thoughts were awesome. His class isn't super easy but it is manageable.
He explains things clearly and is very organized which helps. He does move pretty fast through the material so be prepared for high intensity note taking.

Brau is a good professor, I respect the guy. The only reason i went to class is because he creates "softball" test questions based off of the the inclass lectures. I learned everything from the textbook though. Tests arent too bad if you know how to study effectively. Get 100% on all your homework by going to the TA help desk

Professor Brau is a great sincere guy who wants the best for his students. The material can be difficult if you have no business background but it is doable with the help of TAs. The only thing is that there are not enough. He ties in relevant information to the class as well.
Brau is awesome. Love his spiritual thoughts and energy he brings to class. It is not a walk in the park. But if you come prepared and wanting to learn you will succeed.

Funny guy, ill give him that. You dont learn much in class, so a lot of time is spent on the software online. He is engaging but you dont really learn much from him. Large class size, and not enough TAs to really get help.

Bro Brau is an enthusiastic professor and he tries to keep peoples attention by breaking up the class time with spiritual thoughts and professional development. If you do the readings before class and listen during lectures you should do well in the class.

Professor Brau's class is very dynamic. His strengths include: tying in relevant information from real world events, capturing students attention, simplifying important information that is testable, offering major and career advice, and creating a spiritual environment. Room for improvement includes: writing more legibly. Use the T.A. help desk!

Brau is a good dude and wants his students to succeed but his class is no joke. Unfortunately, he thinks students will pick up Finance better than they do and certain concepts are sometimes not explained as well as you would hope. Going to the TA lab every a couple hours a week is almost necessary to get an A.

LOVED THIS CLASS! It was very well structured and the grading was fair. Bro. Brau's requirements were very clear, and he tried to maintain a consistent schedule.The tests are challenging, but if you TAKE NOTES IN CLASS and understand the material you'll do great. He's all about professional development and bringing the spirit to class. Favorite!

Bro B is an amazing teacher. He really does all that he can so that he can help the students be ready for the real world and his exams. I would recommend him to anyone. But you have to do the reading and go to class or you will be out of luck

Professor Brau is a great professor. He really cares about his students and he wants you to do well. The material is difficult, especially if you don't put in the time and don't do the reading. Doing the reading before going to class will benefit you significantly since Professor Brau goes over the chapter again to solidify the ideas. Great Class.

Professor Brau expects a lot of his students, and will berate students if they ask a "dumb" question. I would have taken from someone else, but there weren't any other professors available. Pay CLOSE attention to the reading and stay on top of the homework. Study hard for the tests and remember, the class is curved. Good luck!!

If you go to class having read and attempted some of the homework problems, then this class is manageable. Professor Brau is really energetic and cares about your success. He knows his stuff and loves Finance which makes a difference. His lectures are fast paced, and if you don’t prepare before class it will be easy to feel lost.

Such a frustrating class!  He YELLS the material at you and he writes illegibly!  Going to class only helped confuse me, but I went anyways because he tests on his lecture. He is energetic and funny at times, but it doesn't make up for the lack of learning in his class... He runs over the material way too fast and is super unclear.
Bro Brau is a very animated guy who loves what he does. Tests are difficult,so know your stuff.

Brau is an awesome teacher! He simplifies complex concepts, and makes them easy for students to understand. But this by no means an easy class, you need to put in the hard work if you want to see the results.

Prof. Brau is an upbeat, knowledgeable lecturer and is always excited to come to class. As this class covers a lot of material, most of the learning for this course comes as you work problems on your own- not from lectures. The only complaint I have about the course is that the homework problems were unnecessarily tricky and confusing.
Bro. Brau is awesome!  He teaches very clearly and he is always willing to help.  He also always has a spiritual thought to lift you up during the lesson.  Very positive and great teacher.

Brau's teaching style matches his personality, which shows me he really is passionate about the material. The course moves quickly and you can get left behind, so take this class in a semester where you can afford to make it a priority!

This class is difficult, but manageable as long as you keep up with the readings, attend class, review/study a lot, and visit with the TA's during lab hours. I really appreciated Bro. Brau as a professor. I thought he really tried to help his students succeed and tried to make class interesting. He is a very good professor.
He was really great.  Helpful and basically tells you 20% of the questions that will be on the midterms.

The Finance class is an interesting class, but does require weekly assignments to be completed and submitted online which can be time consuming.  He expects you to have done your reading before class and will frequently reference abbreviations and acronyms from the text during his lecture.  He is a great teacher and very entertaining to listen to.

Bro. Brau was awesome. He tried to make the information interesting and kept the class attentive during his lecture. The class was hard, but only because the information itself is hard. But, getting a good grade in the class is doable as long as you keep up with the work, and make the class a priority.

Dr. Brau is a really great teacher and does a great job of keeping the class entertaining while also helping you learn. He is very helpful and really cares about his students. You definitely are going to have to put your effort into this class and study hard for the exams but overall it is a really great class.

The class material was interesting and useful. It goes by fast so it's easy to get behind. Sometimes there is just so much information it is hard to understand it all. Not a bad class though, just need to work hard to get the grade you want.

Dr. Brau is a great professor, but he goes through things way too quickly sometimes.  The exams are very difficult.  Prepare to face a variety of questions that are vaguely or never mentioned in the textbook or during the lectures.  With that said, he's probably one of my favorite teachers I've had at BYU.  Very funny guy.  Learned a lot from him.
He is an awesome professor! Very down to earth and he has a passion for helping students and teaching the content.

Professor Brau is a great guy, and he really wants the class to succeed. He tries his best to teach the material, and does so well. With class alone, you will not get an A. You need to study the material on your own and even visit the TA lab, which is really helpful. I would recommend taking the class from him.

Brau is the man. He really wants his students to succeed in his class and in life. He's more than willing to help in any he can. He's down to earth and makes class interesting. Class is not easy because finance is hard. Life's tough, get a helmet. Go to class and you'll literally do great on his tests, bro.
He is very helpful and holds you to a high standard of learning. I felt I got out of this class what I put into it. Sometimes the textbook homework was frustrating.
Moves at a fast pace, if you keep up on the reading and homework you're fine. Make friends in the class, studying for the tests can be hard if you go at it by yourself. Do the practice problems!!!

Brother Brau is a really good guy. You can tell that he genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Assignments included readings, 2 assignments in Microsoft Excel, and 3 exams. Tests weren't terrible, but make sure you come to class and prepare well.
great guy and wants you to work hard to earn everything you get. Its a pretty good but not as hard as acctg 200
He is a great teacher and I loved the Spiritual thoughts he brought to class. I don't really care for the subject but he did a great job teaching finance.

Brother Brau is a really nice guy and his class is really fun! You should read the texts prior to class, so you know what is going on. He is very helpful and tries to make it as easy as possible for the students...

Jim Brau is a great professor.  He is really concerned about his students.  He will do whatever he can to help students with anything.  The material is tough and you need to stay on top of the material but you won't find a professor who cares like Jim Brau.
Brother Brau is awesome. Love his spiritual thoughts and the lecture. IF you want to learn finance and also help your spiritual preparation, take Brau's Finance 201!

Brother Brau is an awesome guy, he keeps lectures interesting and is entertaining.  The material is somewhat difficult and the way he teaches it isn't very helpful.  It made sense reading the book though. Tests are straightforward which was nice.
He is very excited about the class and he does his best to help everyone understand the concepts that he teaches.

Brother Brau is a very enthusiastic and excited guy.  He is very much passionate about finance and tries to share that enthusiasm with the class.  Sometimes he gets too excited and his clarity is thus lacking.  Overall I would say he is an adequate educator and an excellent guy.  You won't fall asleep in this class!

Brother Brau is great. Some people don't like his style of teaching, but I feel like his spiritual and professional development intermissions are helpful in breaking up dense class material. His upbeat demeanor and love of Finance are contagious. It's not the easiest class, but he tells you exactly what to do to make a good grade.

If you want finance on steroids take it from Brother Brau. The class is fairly simple yet because everything is done on the overhead, lecture notes are often illegible with a lot of acronyms that make using and studying from them very difficult.

He is very energetic and excited about the subject.  Make sure you read the book before class because he sometimes does not cover all sections of the reading.  Sometimes the textbook he wrote is poorly written and tough to understand

Bro. Brau is very passionate and excited, all the time. The class is extremely difficult but doable, and his daily spiritual thoughts are very meaningful and touching. I dislike Finance, but Bro. Brau is definitely the professor to take it from.

Bro Brau is a really good guy. That's being said, this is a difficult class for individuals that struggle with math and equations.  I found his class more difficult than Acct 201.  Pay attention to the textbooks and work the study problems, I feel like more is learned in the book than the lectures.

Bro. Brau is an awesome dude and he tells you a lot of stuff that will be on the tests... He works hard to keep the class awake and pumped. However, the class is hard for me, but I'm not a finance master.
Very energetic and helpful.
It's a tough class. Brother Brau really works with you if you are  struggling. he has a passion for learning. I feel like a few things weren't taught clearly and the book was awful.
Super excited dude. Always. Loves finance, which is cool.
Plug n chug baby.  Go buckwild with those drill problems and you will literally do well if you understand the guy intuitively.
Brau is a great guy really wants the students to succeed in life and in the class.

He doesn't really help that much but the TA's and the book are all you really need.  It is not a fun class but the TA's are able to help you with homework, so the only thing you need to worry about is Tests. Not a bad class.
Keeps the class interesting!
You will need to go to class because he shares important info in class regarding tests and answers. Go to finance finance lab, study drill problems and read the book.
Hard class, but Prof. Brau is awesome. He works really hard to help every student and really wants them all to succeed. One of my favorite teachers.

Brau is a great professor! Finance is a tough class in general, but Brau makes it enjoyable and possible to get a good grade. He's enerjetic and makes class fun! Super willing to help any student that needs help.
Great class. Do the work and you will be rewarded. Plenty of help in the TA office hours and good material to learn for life. Really enjoyed his personal finance days.

Brother Brau is a great teacher. He has a lot of energy and is good at keeping your attention. He is also very willing to help. In order to do well it is important to do all of the reading and to take good notes in class
I didn't like how fast he talked and how he repeated things multiple times. He probably thinks it helps gets his points across but really it's just annoying and distracting.
The class isn't impossible but you do need to study and stay on top of things. Easy A if you do what is asked of you. Prof. Brau is always willing to help those who seek it.
good professor. lots of energy. if you don't leave the class at least a little bit interested in finance you did something wrong.
He's fun, but the material is pretty tough

Brother Brau is super funny and entertaining, but to be honest his lectures don't help you understand the concepts very well.  Attend class and take good notes to get the random conceptual questions right on the test, then do the homework in the textbook to nail down the number problems.  Just keep up with the homework and notes and you'll be fine.

Brau's great. The content of any Finance class will be difficult at BYU, but he doesn't try to trick you or make it difficult in any weird way, it's just difficult material that you have to really understand in order to get an A. I liked his lectures a lot!

His expectation is very straightforward. His homework and assignment are easy as long as you go to class and do your work on time. Tips for this class: Read materials and study ahead before coming to lecture each day. It helps a lot. Try to attend TA help desk as much as you can. All of TAs are very kind and helpful.
Bro Brau is a good professor for the class size. Plan on attending TA help desk hours if you want to do well
For a large class with tons of students Bro. Brau does a good job. If you want to do well you will probably need to go to TA help desk. I like that he gives spiritual thoughts in class.
great professor ,make sure you got the TA lab to get help, the exams are easy and the class is super exciting
This class is super hard, and Bro B is off topic sometimes. Too much unnecessary talk in lectures sometimes.
This has been pretty straight forward, as long as you do your readings regularly and finish homework and any other assignments on time.
Bro. Brau is an awesome guy. He really does want the best for all his students. Following his teaching/lectures is sometimes difficult. Goes 100 mph.

This class is tough because of the material, but I would recommend taking it because you can apply the material to whatever you do in life. Take the class from Bro B. He's the best teacher I've had at BYU.  He's uptempo and very respectful. Spiritual thoughts every class are great.

This class is challenging, but everyone should take it even if you aren't a business major.  Jim Brau tries really hard to make the material applicable to real life situations and help you in personal finance.  Utilize the TA lab when you need help!

There are two types of people in this world. Those who like Dr. Brau's teaching style and those who don't. If you like skipping class, memorizing a text book, and crazy hard tests, Dr. Brau might be for you. If you get frustrated when the professor goes off topic, has illegible handwriting, and writes very vague quiz/test questions, look elsewhere.

Simply put the class feels rushed. We only seem to touch on topics, and are expected to master them.  This class would be a bit more manageable if it were broken up over two semesters.  There's a lot to learn is so little time.  Brother Brau does a great job breaking it down in class, but it doesn't make up for the sheer amount of quantity.

Dr. Brau is one the best professor at Marriot School. He really care about his student. As student we have to do our part and be fully invested. The nature of the class is demanding. Do all you homework and reading then try your best on the mid-term.

He is one of my most favorite professors.  He is crazy, but he loves what he does. His teaching sometime wasn't very clear, but if you read the book ahead of time, it helps. Also, going to the TA lab helps a TON. Some principles are hard to understand, but once you get them, everything makes sense.  take it from Brau, he knows what hes talking abou
Great at keeping the class awake and energized, very dynamic teacher, but the class material moves quite quickly.
Its not his fault that finance is boring

Brau is a great guy full of energy, but the class is very hard. The reading and homework assignments given are the way you learn the material, and if you don't complete them before class, you won't understand the lecture at all. It is very time consuming, but if you use the plentiful help available you could probably do well.
spends more time talking about himself than what we actually need to learn

He is a great guy, not the best professor though.  He uses terms that are interchangeable and very similar and expects us to know they are the same without really telling us.  The homework requires a lot of time to get done.  The tests aim to basically fail you. Sometimes his writing is unclear and hard to read.  He also rushes through stuff.

Brau is great.  He's aware of his students needs, and he adapts to them.  Approach him, tell him your concerns about the class.  I had to take this class for my Nonprofit minor, and it was very challenging for me, especially because it's not a subject I am particularly interested in.  I imagine that Brau makes it about as enjoyable as it can be.
Nice guy, expects you to attend class but not required. Rough tests but if you like finance I'm sure its helpful in the long run.

All around good guy who really enjoys teaching.  The class is pretty helpful and you learn relevant stuff, but Brau's way of teaching isn't to efficient.  You have to learn a lot of ratios and equations, and most of the time they aren't explained very well, so you have to look over them a bunch of times for them to click.
Brother Brau is a great teacher. He doesn't try to trick you with his test. If you go to class and pay attention you'll get at least a B. Use the TA lab before you submit your homework.
Great class. Always very helpful. Tests are fair. If you go to class, you will be very prepared for the tests.
Intense guy. Really passionate about the material. Enjoyed the class a lot. I recommend anyone taking FIN 201 take it from Brau

I've never seem 45 years old professor pumped like a college kid. Though his lecture often times allover the place, as long as you read the material before class and get good help from TA's his lecture is understandable and very engaging. Yea, better get to know TA's - Toshi is working crazy to make sure the class function and other TA's are super!
I absolutely loved Dr. Brau, he was extremely helpful.
Good Class   Good Professor

Brau is awesome. I'm not a fan of finance, I prefer accounting, but Brau made the subject engaging. It's a class you can't sleep in, lots of info is involved, but if you stay on the ball with everything you can do relatively well.

Professor Brau is very interested in his students doing well. He gives you all the materials you need to succeed, but you can't rely on just lectures to get by. You need to go to the finance help desk and have a real interest in understanding the finance principles. The class is challenging, but doable, so be ready to dedicate yourself.
Professor Brau is the nicest guy ever. Although the class is pretty difficult, the professor makes sure you can get all the help you need.
Great class! He is very entertaining and makes finance really fun!
Dr. Brau is really an awesome dude.  Cares alot about finance as well as the success of his students regardless of their major.  The class is just rediculously hard!

Dr. Brau clearly cares about his students. He wants everyone to succeed. The course material can be challenging, especially if you have trouble with numbers. Dr. Brau is incredibly animated during class to help you stay attention. That said I often found myself confused as he doesn't always explain things clearly. Go to the TA's for clarity.

If you are a finance major, or know anything about it, you will be endlessly frustrated by how uninformative Bro. Brau is. He wastes so much time in class talking about his opinions that he doesn't teach the material effectively or deeply enough. Much of your learning will come from the terribly written textbook, and if you have for it, the TA lab.

Strong teacher that cares a lot about how his students perform. As far as the subject matter is concerned, he does the best he can to make it clear. He provides a lot of helpful information for life and understands that many in the class are not finance majors. Overall, great class but definitely involves a lot of work in order to do well.

Brau tries his best to make this class good for everyone, and he really takes opinions into consideration. But for non-finance majors (I am a recreation management major) this class is really hard. Everyone I know in my class practically failed the first test. Hopefully there is a huge curve at the end of the class.
Very passionate professor. His spiritual thoughts are eye-opening. Hand writing is kind of confusing. TAs are helpful, especially Toshi.
Class is tough but as long as you keep up with the reading and homework you should be fine.

Covers material extremely fast. so you have to read the textbook before class, the math is not hard to understand at all, basic algebra. what was difficult was remembering all of the different equations and forms, for every hour in class expect 1 to 2 hours outside to study, brau is a spiritual giant, very hard to fall asleep in this class
Great Professor, easy class, highly recommend.

Brother Brau is AWESOME! he wants all his students to do well and overall the class is really enjoyable. If you need or want to take Fin201 take it from Brau. He isn't about weeding people out of the business program. Fantastic professor!

My favorite thing about Brother Brau is that while he thinks his subject is important he knows that most everyone just wants to get an A in the class and he teaches you how to do that. Plus all his steroid jokes. Priceless.

Great professor. He knows the material and how to teach in an interactive way. The class is difficult, but so is every FIN201 class, that is how it is designed. He gives you the tools you need to succeed in the class and gives great advice to succeed in life.
Brings really good energy, sometimes his notes in class are just very unclear.
This is not the easiest class. He will teach enough material for a month in an hour and then move on without going into detail or helping students understand.

Difficult material. If you don't do reading prior to class you will be even more lost than usual. A lot of memorization of equations. Brau is the best teacher available to take this difficult class from.
It is hard to keep up with his notes in class.

Jim Brau is not a difficult professor. TO be successful in his class is simple. 1) Read the text BEFORE class. 2) Take good notes that YOU will understand later when reviewing them. 3) Do ALL your homework. You cannot slack off in his class, but it is not difficult material to learn. No heavy math, all the calculations are understandable.
Bro Brau is a spiritual giant and is a great teacher. He loves being personal and likes to keep the lectures interesting. He takes breaks in the middle of lectures to help you concentrate.

Bro, Brau is a really good teacher who enjoys interacting with his students. However, the class is difficulty because you are forced to memorize the different financial ratios.  Also the tests are killer if you do not study.  I enjoyed and learned alot in this class.
Very fun teacher. Has a great attitude on life that he conveys to the whole class. He is very knowledgeable about finance.
Dr. Brau is amazing!  He is so energetic.  Yes the class requires work.  Welcome to the real world.  But if you want to know Finance, he is the guy to teach it to you.

Do the readings before even if its just a skim.  Pay attention in class and then do the problems.  He is effective if you do your preparation too.  Be ahead in class!  Tests are good if you understand all of the concepts if not it will be a struggle.

Not a finance major but he makes the class entertaining. A lot of energy. Not as hard as the class leads on to be. Pretty easy to get at least a B but might need to do some extra studying to get the A.

I think a small class with professor Brau would be awesome; however, a class of 600 just takes away some of the magic. Overall, he was effective at teaching difficult concepts and made the subject fun (as much as possible).

The material was helpful and interesting. Class attendance is required, and he leverages test questions and a no phone/laptop policy in order to increase attendance and participation. That is the only problem I have with the class.

Dr. Brau is one of the best teachers in the Marriott School. Much of what we learn will apply to many areas of our life. He literally bends over backwards to help each student know the material and succeed not only in the classroom, but also in life.
Super clear. He loves to help you. If you pay attention and work hard. You probably will get at least B+. The exam is little tricky. TAs are super helpful.

Brother Brau is really nice and really interested in what he is teaching. He tries to keep lecture interesting and mixes it up with a spiritual thought in the middle, which I like, although sometimes class feels a little disjointed. It's a hard class, but Brother Brau wants you to do well and doesn't make it more difficult than necessary.

Dr. Brau is pumped about finance, and honestly I think the guy would be great if he wanted to get a job in sales. He knows what he is talking about, but is difficult to follow at times. With Brau you will be sacrificing some clarity, for an animated, entertaining personality. So it's a trade-off. If you don't do well studying on your own, avoid it.
Great Class. Very helpful and interested in the students.
Great guy. Really knows his stuff, but he can be confusing because he is all over the place. But there are tons of ways they help you so it makes up for it.

Don't get me wrong: this is a hard class. Now that being said. Professor Brau is probably the best teacher for this class. Completely transparent and fair about everything and literally gives you all the tools you need. i would take another class from him in a heart beat :)
Professor Brau is great! His lectures are engaging and fun! Be prepared to work in this class. Doing the readings for the class is crucial!

Be prepared to work HARD! Attendance/reading, not reqd, but skip even 1 class or reading and you'll fall way behind! To pass the class, you have to learn to think like Prof. Brau. He teaches you how to think like him so you know how to study for the tests. It also REALLY helps to get in a study group where all of you want an A.

Unorganized. Textbook had 200+ errors. He was too hyped up on energy shakes to ever focus. Says he will only test on relevant material - but tests on random sentences he says. I knew more finance before taking this class. He teaches wrong equations until someone points it out the day before the test and then you have to re-study.

Really poor teacher.  He is s super nice guy and willing to help, but his lectures are terrible.  He tests on random stuff he says in class, and never explains what we actually need to learn.  Half the time I had to go home and correct the notes I took in class.  Gives poor examples and it stressed me out going to class.  Horrible experience.

Brau's a funny, but good guy.  His lectures will keep you awake.  Take this class after taking Acc 200 and it will be pretty easy.  You'll still need to watch a few of the software videos to learn the material, (and attend class), but an A is very doable.

Some of you may have heard that his class is easier and easier to get an A. But his class will be harder to get an A starting 2013 since he has to. If you care to learn the material well, I would recommend to take it from Holmes.

Professor Brau is cool but is hard to understand. He rushes through the material so fast it is hard to take in. If you ask a question he usually answers another question or doesn't explain it clearly. His work is doable as long as you have a background in the topic. If you don't and need more explanation then he may not be the best teacher for you.

Brau is awesome. His class is also really easy if you just study his notes and do the practice problems. I also really loved Brau's spiritual messages. They also seemed to be exactly what I needed to hear. His lectures may be a little erratic, but they were decent.

Seems like a nice guy however he was not prepared at all to give the lecture.  Spent all the time reading off from the slides that he obviously did not study before hand.  We asked him to slow down and focus on the most important subjects and what he ended doing was rushing some of the important material even more.

brau is an inspiring person to be around. he's a little full on so if you're lazy you won't do well in the class. the class kicks up a gear after the first test, but i would go just for his spiritual thoughts. i slacked off a bit and only got a B but if you work the problems and understand the concepts you can definitely get an A

Great teacher, tough material. People commented that his tests were too hard, but you just have to put in the effort. I studied 15-20 hours for each test and aced them. Class can be a bit useless at times, but it is still necessary to go so you can get his "softball" questions. Actual learning came from the software, it felt like an online course.

Hes ok.  Tests are not an accurate representation of what you have learned and they are very tricky.  Hes a good guy and fun, but should not be teaching classes over 50 people.  He fails to explain things clearly or apply what we learn to real business.

Overall I enjoyed Dr. Brau. He's   really enthusiastic about finance which is cool because it wasn't hard form e to pay attention. Even if you're not going into business this class will teach you some important life lessons on how to utilize your wallet so pay attention, take good notes, do the practice exams and you'll be fine.

Brau is a great guy at heart, but he is a terrible lecturer. He went through the material WAY to fast and did not give enough time to understand what was being taught. I feel like would have learned better and retained better the material had I not gone to class, and just learned software.

Sped through material WAY to fast, gave very little time to actually understand teh material while in class. Brau is a great guy at heart, but a terrible lecturer. I probably would have been more successful in this class had I not done to class, and just learned from the software.

This course was the hardest business school per-requisite for me.  It's not that the materials were hard.  It is that the tests were poorly made.  I would spend 10+ hours preparing for tests only to get tripped up by "softball" questions that had no math involved.  I feel that the tests in this course are not as math oriented as they should be.

Brother Brau really cares for his students and is the most effective professor I have ever had.The spiritual thoughts that were incorporated into every lesson helped strengthen my testimony and made me want to be a better person. The class is challenging but worth it.  Four tests and a final are the only thing on your grade, but he drops one test

Brau is a good guy, but is not a coherent professor. He has a REALLY hard time staying on topic, which is frustrating and distracting. Brau always starts with an opening prayer and he always has a spiritual thought in the middle of class, which I always appreciated. Overall, try taking this class from Dr. Holmes or someone else.

Brau is the best! His classes are so captivating and entertaining. He lets anyone ask questions and does a great job answering everything. He is very open to suggestions. TAKE HIM!!!!! HE'S ONE FO THE BEST!!!!!

Brau is legit, he works hard to keep everyone motivated and tries to be understanding.  If you dont do well in the class it is your own fault, he has TA's at almost all times, he tells you exactly what you need to know, if you actually pay attention you will be fine.  He also tries to bring the Spirit to his classes.

Hardest course in the business minor that I have taken. The material is very straight forward but the tests are poorly made. The "give away" questions are harder than the problem questions. I studied 10-12 hours for each test (5 tests) and didnt get above a 90 on any. Very helpful professor though and fun classes. Posts lectures online.
This is the hardest class I have ever taken at BYU. Brau is an interesting lecturer, but he tends to stray a little from the subject matter. He is helpful when asked and cares about his students.

Professor Brau is passionate about finance and portrays that every class period. He is the type of guy that will help any way possible, whether landing an internship, or just to get some advice on how to do well in his class, go talk to the man! He is awesome, plus his coil shoes are amazing!!GET HUGE

This professor is a wonderful teacher and mentor. He is very knowledgeable, and helpful. He always tries to bring the material to real life with real examples of its uses and applications. He is willing to help in any way he can. You have to read the book, and do easy quizzes before the class and solve problems after class. The TA's are helpful.

Professor Brau has got to be the most athletic professor I have ever had. This aside he really knows his junk. He is able to drive a small prius with swag which is defenatly important for the classes I take. His fashion is also outstanding. and for a forty year old man he has great hair. Keeping it tight. I would compare him to Denzel Washington.

Good professor. His personality is very energetic, so he really can keep your attention. The material is hard, but you can get it if you read the packet(textbook). Sometime he mentions things that aren't in the book. So it's a good idea to go to class. Assignments can be insane - but it's doable. Study partners are a good idea. Use the TAs.

I hated this class and I got an A.  Dr. Brau is a very good man, but he's probably the worst lecturer on campus.  You won't understand anything in class (he talks as though he's always in a hurry), but I would say 90% of the tests come from what he decides to cover in class. So study it well on your own!
Professor Brau is not only a great instructor of business but he is an inspirational man.

He's definitely over the top, kind of crazy so just get used to it. He tries really hard to motivate everybody, and he's super intense about everything so prepare to be humbled. Listen to his advice he really does try to help, but don't listen to the whiners, just man up and realize this isn't an "easy" class, it is meant to filter students.

I found his class to be incredibly easy.  Unfortunately, I didn't learn very much about finance.  He spends the majority of the lecture talking about himself, his family, the gospel, the army etc.  If you don't care about finance but are majoring in business, his class is the one to take.

This is a very discouraging class, if you aren't able to fully understand the information before coming to lecture. He moves at such a quick pace that you feel lost almost the entire time. He does prepare great spiritual thoughts though. Great businessman, poor lecturer.

This class was pretty discouraging.  Dr. Brau is a really good person, but he isn't a very good lecturer.  He assumes everybody knows what he is talking about, leaving you frustrated.  However, he is good about pushing you towards getting internships, and he prepares great spiritual thoughts.

Great professor. Lectures were always interesting. He'll tell stories and keep lecture exciting. There's not required homework, but you need to do the reading to stay on top of things. But that's about it. The reading is clear, his lecture is clear. I found the tests easy. I HIGHLY recommend this class, it's way worth it.

Brother Brau is a friendly professor, understanding, and helpful. He will go out of his way to help his students and make them understand. Class is fun and he is always changing it up to keep your attention. Everything is for the benefit of the student spiritually and intellectually. Brother Brau IS the best teacher you can have for this class.
Brother Brau is awesome! He made this class great. He is very helpful. The class is a fair amount of work, but take it from Brother Brau if at all possible. He is very helpful and very fair.

Prof. Brau is the MAN!! I LOVE TEH GUY! He makes finance applicable and easy for non- business students. He has great spiritual thoughts and really cares about his students. Read the chapters, do the practice quizzes and your guaranteed an A on the test. I would highly recommend Brau. He is hilarious!

Brother Brau is one of the most inspiring men I've ever witnessed.He has a way to make you want to be your best self and always makes a point to remind us that although Business is all about competition that church is still the number one in our life.If your taking any class that he teaches don't miss out on the opportunity to have been his student
Prof. Brau inspired me in countless areas of life, not just finance. He is an incredible person who is happy to help his students however he can. You will LOVE this class.

A good teacher.  He tries to be clear in what he will test you.  If you read the textbook and go to class you will succeed on the tests.  No homework.  Your grade is just 4 tests split evenly.  A pretty straight pitch.

I like Dr Brau. He's pretty animated which helped me pay attention in class. Your grade is based off the tests which aren't too hard. If you read a little, do the practice quizes on blackboard, and go to a review then you should know everything on the tests.

Fantastic professor.  Goes over the test before, so you know (almost) every question before you even take the test.  (he changes the numbers, so they are "different" questions) Writes test from class notes, so go every lecture and almost guarantees at least an A-.  I loved his spiritual thoughts.

Amazing Professor! I've never had a professor who was so on top of everything. He really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He's pretty funny too, he's an intense guy and he'll tell plenty of stories to prove it.

Dr. Brau is outstanding.  It's obvious he spends a huge amount of time preping his class to be top notch.  He is more than available after class hours if needed.  He's exciting to listen to and makes a very dry subject entertaining and always brings in the Spirit!

Brother Brau is awesome! If all professors on campus were like him, BYU would have 100% success accomplishing its Aims. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to help them succeed in school and in life. I especially loved how he took some time out every class to share a short spiritual thought-usually that only happens in religion classes

An amazing guy.  Extremely dedicated and over-the-top intense.  You'll be laughing the entire time.  In between laughs you'll be scratching your head on some of the principles...but ANY and ALL resources are available to help everyone understand the principles.  Great class.  READ THE BOOK

Bro. Brau does an amazing job making sure you have every resource you need. It's like he structured the class and teaches in a way to ace his student ratings. I would recommend taking Accounting first, but it's not necessary. It was a tough class, but the test curves were huge. Bro. Brau really wants his students to learn the materials.
Best Professor I have ever had.  Truly cares about the students and prepares you for real life.
Great teacher highly recommend him

Very helpful, bends over backwards for you. Curves were around 20 points on each test. Got an A no problem, didn't have to take the final. Read the book and do the practice problems to understand the material, go to class to clear up any questions. Fun class. Brau is extremely nice.
3 tests. I got a good grade on the 1st on and stopped going to class. I was fine. Read the book before the test and do the practice problems. I got an A- no sweat. Jim Brau is one intense dude.

Bro. Brau is an amazing teacher who is pationate about finance. Read the chapter before class and you will do fine. I thought the class was pretty easy. no assigments, only tests, which I like. not hard to get an A.

By far the most helpful professor I've had.  Truly cares about students.  Tough class.  Total grade is based off 3 exams and nothing else so its easy to procrastinate. In order to do well you have to get help from TA's and go to help review sessions because too much is covered in class to understand real well.     Brau is a nice guy
Most engaging teacher, hands down.
amazing teacher.   prepares you for the real life.

I loved Shrum as a professor. Yeah her tests are a little tricky but if you do the readings and pay attention/ask questions during her lectures you can get a good enough grade. The extra credit assignments help too. She was considerate in listening to questions before or after class. Isn't the type to change a test grade though

Since she teaches in Salt Lake, she does do it differently from the professors down in Provo. But even if you attend all lectures and read everything, you still will not be prepare for the test. She does  extra credit. Up my grade 13% if you do the extra credit.  Also WILL NOT ROUND SORCE. I literally got a 89.87 and would not round it to an A-.

She is a pretty boring lecturer, but the class was small enough that there was still some discussion. Took it at the Salt Lake Center. From what I have heard about other AHTG classes, this seems like the best option
For the tests all she tells you to do is read the textbook and review your class notes (100+ pages). Not helpful and her lectures were not beneficial. Poor teaching skills

Professor Shrum is great! I had her class at the Salt Lake center over the summer, so things went pretty quickly, but she was super organized which was nice. The tests honestly weren't that bad as long as you paid attention in the textbook and listened in class. Definitely would highly recommend taking American Heritage from her!

If you have to face the American Heritage beast, take from Shrum. For sure the best way to go. Class was made up of 3 tests, 3 papers, and an extra credit assignment. The tests are super intense and I never did better than a high C, but I still managed to pull an A so don't stress too much. Honestly if all u do is read the textbook, you'll be solid

Shrum's A-Heritage class seemed to be much easier than a typical A-Heritage class. We had two easy papers and an extra credit paper that required no research. She goes over pretty much everything that will be on the exam in class and on her slides. She also was very caring to students. If you want an easy A-Heritage class, take it from Shrum.

Hard to get an A. Pay attention in lectures! Things she mentions only once will appear on the test. The tests have tricky questions. She thinks having one student get 100 on a test makes her a successful teacher. She does not curve. Is unhelpful outside of lectures. Email responses are generic and refer you to readings- if she responds at all.

Worth it to take Professor Shrum for AHTG! You'll end up reading the whole textbook, but the tests are broken into chunks that are non-cumulative, so it's not too bad. Cares more about key concepts, people, and events than dates. Her lectures help you understand concepts and give review tips for tests. Easy essay and extra credit help your grade!

Just a tip on the text book, you can get away with just checking it out and doing the readings in the library. If you prefer studying at home or outside of school you'll probably want to get one, but she never uses it in class. She focuses on concepts and their application which can make for some tricky test questions and don't stress the essay.

Shrum's better than Provo classes from what I've heard. That being said, this class was still no walk in the park. The entire grade is 3 tests and 1 paper. Her tests are tricky so study hard. It's nice not having to worry about homework, but stressful that there's not much to help buffer your grade. Not much class participation either so it drags.

Professor Shrum is very lecture-oriented and doesn't provide much of a study guide. The tests were rather difficult, even after studying many long hours. There was no homework, minus a paper. Two midterms and a final exam (and the paper) are all I was graded on outside of attendance.

I took this class because I heard that it was easier than Provo and I dont like history. I realized that it is only easier in the way that there isnt as many assignments or homework. The average for the three tests was an 85% so its not an easy A (the tests are your whole grade.) Shrum was good but often taught unnecessary info. Hope this helps

Prof. Shrum was a great choice for the American heritage credit. She is super passionate about the things she is teaching and wants you to actually learn and apply the material. There is A TON of reading and your grade only consists of 3 tests and an essay, which could totally kill you. Just do the readings and take notes in class and you'll pass

I loved this course and wish that everyone could have Professor Shrum for American Heritage. Highly HIGHLY recommend! The course is three exams (not cumulative!) and one response paper-- super straightforward. Her lectures were interesting and engaging and I found that I was always looking forward to her class.

Sister Shrum is amazing, my favorite BYU Salt Lake professor ever! Read the chapters and go to lectures and you'll pass. Three exams and a paper and she gives you every opportunity to learn the material for the exam. She's not trying to trick you so just pay attention. If you live in Provo, she's worth the drive to Salt Lake.

3 tests and 1 paper! Professor Shrum is awesome. The class is super straightforward and actually interesting. She does a great job and explaining what youll need to know for tests. As long as you take good notes and do the readings, youll get a good grade!

Professor Shrum gives amazing lectures. She asks you to do the readings but there is no homework associated with that, which is nice, your grade is based only off your test scores and a paper. The tests are kinda tricky so you will want to study, but her lectures are interesting and she really is a phenomenal teacher.
Very good lectures. Just really study for the tests.

I learned so much from this class and Sister Shrum did a great job clearly explaining concepts. I no longer dreaded history. 3 Tests, 1 paper. Come to class, do the readings and the tests are too bad. She does give extra credit.

Your grade is determined by three tests and a response paper. The tests are tricky and come mainly from the book, but if you study and read each chapter carefully, you should do just fine. She gives extra credit on tests, and there are no extra assignments which is nice, but the lectures aren't very interactive. It is still much better than Provo.

dont miss class and take a ton of notes during lecture. she only gives the three tests but if you talk to her she's super helpful super kind and nice doesn't interact during class a ton no homework tho

Grades are based solely on three tests and one essay. Wording of tests are a bit tricky. No review or anything for tests. Basically told you to read every text book chapter twice and write an outline over them and compile them with you class notes and form a study group. I did all of this and still may not end up with an A

I am very glad that I took American Heritage here at the SL center. The class size is significantly smaller than taking it in Provo, which allows for a little more intimate lectures. The class is based on 3 tests and an essay, so don't do bad on any test. You have to do the recommended reading and take detailed notes in class. Overall a good choice

Not the greatest class I've ever taken. Lectures were not exciting or interactive, which I found disappointing given the small setting of the Salt Lake Center. That being said, I would have rather taken it from Shrum than to take it in Provo. I wasn't nearly as stressed or flooded with assignments. One bad test score could destroy your grade though

Definitely take this class over Provo AHTG, it was the best decision I made. This class had 3 tests (non-cumulative) and an essay. The tests are a little tricky but they're based on the reading, and she tells you what to study in class. Prof. Shrum offers extra credit and the essay is a reflection on something you learned in the class.

Prof Shrum is the best American Heritage teacher at BYU. If you don't want your GPA wrecked, I would highly recommend her. Her lectures are fun and full of stories, you can tell she is passionate about what she is teaching. If you do the reading and study for tests, you will surely get an A.

This course was based off of 3 tests and an essay. The tests were a bit difficult and based solely on the reading. She offers extra credit multiple times throughout the semester. This class is the best choice I made this semester. So much easier than BYU provo AHTG.

Prof. Shrum is a nice lady but the 2.5 hour lectures are soooo boring and your only grades are 3 tests (final is not cumulative which is really nice) and an essay (super easy) and some extra credit. so minimal workload (which is nice compared to provo) but the tests are still hard. read TB and get a study group. no homework ever which is cool

I thought Mrs. Shrum was a fantastic professor. Her American Heritage class was infinitely easier/better/more enjoyable than that of any other professor at BYU (from what I've heard from others who have taken American Heritage from a different professor). I finished her class feeling grateful American Heritage is a required course.
Super boring clase a just history. Show up and you'll pass. Study for the tests and you're good.

Professor Shrum did a great job making this class interesting, even though history isn't my passion. I am glad I took her class instead of taking American Heritage in Provo. You don't have to write a research paper, and you have everything you need to do well as long as you take good notes and do the readings.

The lectures for this class were amazing! It is easy to see that Prof. Shrum cares about her subject matter. The reading was really good. Unfortunately, the tests were difficult. The multiple choice answers were ambiguous with several answers being almost the same thing. The whole grade is three tests and one paper that isn't worth much.

Shrum ain't no bum! She's a great teacher, very passionate, and made learning history very enjoyable. Class sometimes seemed long (cuz it is, like 2.5 hours), but she keeps it interesting. Your grade is based on tests, and she's not about to curve them, so study hard for the tests! If you take good notes, study those notes and read  you'll be good!

Professor Shrum is awesome!!!! I truly enjoyed her class! You will learn a ton more and most likely get a better grade than taking it in Provo. Don't skip class and do all of the readings! I have always struggled with history, but I got a great grade in this class, because I put the effort in.

Worst Teacher at BYU, she gives 2.5 hour lectures that rarely have anything to do with the actually material that will be on the test.  She gives 3 test and 1 essay. So if you get bomb one or two of the tests you are screwed. She shows old black and white videos that are pointless.  Usually 10-13 people show up to class out of 30.

This is not the easiest class to take but it is worth it. Professor Shrum structures the class to really teach you American Heritages and she cares. Do not fall behind in the reading. Do not skip class. You have to put in an effort to get an A and you will if you work hard. The test are CRUCIAL for this course. So, study for them!

Lots of people complain about this class but I highly enjoyed it! There's only 3 tests and 1 paper so if you do really bad on one you might be in trouble. But if you study and actually do the reading you'll be fine. Also skipping class is a bad idea.
At first she seemed like an easy teacher, but there are only 3 tests.  The second and third tests are not that easy
Mrs Shrum is a great teacher. She gets everyone involved and teaches things that you can actually apply! I loved this American Heritage!

3 Tests and 1 paper that makes up your grade for the class.  Use the study guides in the back of each chapter of the book and attend class to get good notes and you will be fine.  Study the notes well for the exams and they are not that difficult, she even includes 5-10 points of extra credit on each test.  Paper is easy.
Awesome teacher enjoyed it a lot

Sister Shrum actually cares about the subject she teaches.  But if you read the chapters before the lectures (no quizes) and take notes you will do just fine. She uses great examples in class. Plus she offers extra credit. She is VERY clear in what you need to study and prepare for. Love Sister Shrum!

Lectures are pointless even if you take notes. They have nothing to do with the tests and the tests are very difficult. Too many trick questions. There is no homework or assignments in her class, so if you bomb the tests you are out of luck. She does offer extra credit which helps.

Attendance is mandatory but her lectures have nothing to do with the test. Read the book and take notes and you will pass. She doesn't use power point or any visual aids. She just talks at you for 2 hours. It makes it very hard to pay attention.

Professor Shrum is seriously the nicest lady. She's there to help you and really wants you to learn about history. Her tests are from the book and as long as you study the "self-quiz" sections at the end of each chapter, you'll be fine. One paper but its not too bad.
She is a great teacher. Much easier than most A HTG classes. Her tests go totally by the book, so it is really easy to do well if you read the book.

I really enjoyed this class. I love history so I found it very interesting. It's not the easiest A ever but it's definitely the best American Heritage class you'll find! You only have to write one paper the entire semester. Shrum is a very sweet and happy to explain anything if you ask. Do the extra credit too its super easy and it will help!

I loved this class! Professor Shrum is an amazing teacher and gives perspectives from more than one point of view. It does take work and a lot of reading. She does offer extra credit up to 10 points. She really cares. :)

Best class for American Heritage EVER! The absolute easiest class for American Heritage that you will ever find in the State. Sister Shrum is the most helpful and insightful Professor that you will ever find teaching this course. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

Sister Shrum is not a good teacher. She does not try to help you in any way and does not stay true to her word. Her lectures are never on the test so really there is no point to even come to class. Do the reading and that is the best you can do to study for her tests. I would never recommend her to any of my friends.

Sister Shrum is more than willing to talk with you and help you when she sees that you care about the class and your grade. The class requires a lot of intense studying and reading, but she gives really good outlines for her exams. Read the textbook before coming to class. She gave an extra credit opportunity, but make sure you study a lot!

Sister Shrum is a really good professor. If she sees that you really want to get a good grade and you work hard and take the class seriously, she'll be glad to help you. Overall, A HTG requires reading to be done and intense studying, but Shrum gives you guidlines for the exams-little hints on what to study. Just study A LOT!

Professor Shrum is awesome! This was my favorite class last semester! The tests are hard so make sure you study. There are 2 essays and they are really easy. Read the book every week she gets a alot of her notes from there and take careful notes in class. You can get an A if you Read, STUDY FOR THE TESTS! and do good on the essays.
Ms. Shrum is a very nice and interesting teacher. I would say the class is easier than it is in Provo. Though the tests are hard, papers are easy. Plus, you have chance to get a lot of extra credit.

Prof. Brignone is a kind guy and I agree with many of his politics. But it gets to a point where even I can't listen to an opinionated rant for 2 hours. Taking Economics as a night class once a week and trying to learn the rest on my own just didn't work for me and the time we did have with the professor wasn't utilized.

Econ is a class hard, everybody knows it and it doesn't get miraculously easier. But in his class, you understand the concepts with a huge clarity. Tests are not tricky, but you do have to study. However, Professor Brignone makes the class smooth and attaches the concepts to our day to day, so it is interesting and it does keep your attention.

Everything I know about economics, I taught myself. Why? Because Joseph Brignone sure isn't going to teach it to you. He'll consistently waste entire lectures on his politically charged rants, and then cram 2 hours worth of lecture material in the last 10 minutes. Even though I share some of his politics, I greatly resent being a captive audience.

Don't take this class from him. You teach yourself with your weekly homework that takes forever. He is no help whatsoever. Every test contains things you never learned. The only nice thing is that the papers are graded super easy, he doesn't even read them.

Brother Brignone teaches very well and clearly. He is helpful when approached after class or emailed, and is very effective at helping you understand why you should care. TAKE HIS CLASS!!! 
The class is difficult by nature, but if you do well in the assignments they'll slightly help cushion your grades on tests if you arent a test taker.

Prof Brignone was awesome. He teaches a hard course, but you can tell he loves the topic. He does go into "rants" but he does it on purpose to help you remember the concepts. The tests are hard, but he doesn't write them and will curve them if needed. If you pay attention in class and do the readings you will be fine. He's accessible if needed.

He is a breath of fresh air in an academic world full of liberal professors that shove their radical opinions down the throats of students. It's a tough class but he teaches it well. Really appreciated how much he truly educated us.

A great choice for ECON110! He's very fair & friendly. Hw, 2 papers, and participation can be free points IF you put in the work. Exams are fair and totally doable if you READ THE BOOK. Requires more time than most 3-cred classes, but if you put in the time to READ THE BOOK and really learn the concepts you will do great. Very interesting material!

I do not recommend his class to anyone that hasnt taken any business classes prior. The only class I felt was harder than this class was a 400 level accounting class. I was disappointed because the material was relatively entertaining but his class organization, lecture quality, and failure to teach difficult technical concepts was well below par.

Professor Brignone is a good ECON 110 teacher. He knows the material very well. He isn't very accessible outside of class. I don't know if it's worth it if you live down in Provo to choose his class at the Salt Lake Center.

I don't have as many issues with Professor Brignone as I do with taking Econ110 at BYU. Incredibly difficult class. Spent 200+ hours on Cengage (textbook/HW website) and barely managed a C. He's a good guy, but his lectures didn't make a huge difference for me. 25% of grade is HW, 10% is book review essays, 65% exams. Really tough class.

Econ is hard no matter what, but he would spend half the class going on political rants that were not even related to the topic at all. He would even say that they were not. So you come all the way to class to get help with really difficult concepts that he would never even get to. Dont waste your time.

Don't sweat the essays, homework due every weekend online, two midterms and a final all fairly difficult, does get off topic on lectures but is really passionate about application of economics so I learned a lot.

Great lectures, even though the slides he reads off of can get pretty boring sometimes. This class made me decide to change my major to economics because he showed me how important and interesting it can be. Go to class and do the readings and homework and you should do fine in the class.

The bad reviews are from the people that never showed up and didn't do any of the homework, also this class is the most failed and retaken class at BYU. Really passionate about his work and gives inspirational economic and spiritual thoughts often. FYI he doesn't read the book reports we wrote and gave 100% .

Not an effective teacher at all. he spent the majority of class going an tangents and the rest of the class reading the textbook publisher produced slides. He was also highly opinionated and expressed that to the class very clearly. Not worth driving up to Salt Lake for and made an already difficult class more difficult. 10/10 would not recommend

If you are reading this you have to take Brignone's class. The only part though is that you have to accept that Econ is just a hard class, it is the most failed and retaken class at BYU. His test reviews don't help, but he allows a note card for all of his tests. It's way easier at the SLC center and worth the free train ride down to take it!!!
This was honestly one of my favor classes at BYU so far! Professor Brignone makes the material way more interesting by giving real life examples of economic principles! I seriously loved it!

Honestly, it was a pretty easy class. Read the text-book, do the homework, and study for exams. Going to class wasn't all that important because literally all of the information is in the book and reiterated on the homework.

This class is hard, no doubt about it; Professor Brignone kept a long and hard class interesting. Professor Brignone has stories and examples to help illustrate each subject area. He is also very opinionated, but in a way that helped me evaluate different economic issues.

Bro Brignone is a boss. He enjoys teaching ECON and understands the content well. He is passionate about helping students not only learn the material, but also learn why ECON is so important, including the real-life applications found within. He keeps the class entertained the whole 2 and a half hours and cracks lots of escalation humor jokes. :)

Two midterms and a final. The first test was reasonable, but the second he "miswrote" but only gave a 6 percent curve on the test when the average was a 62. going to class is nearly pointless, because he just reads his slides, and he gives you what he calls a "review" for his tests that is absolutely zero help. No practice questions or anything.

I learned absolutely nothing when I would go to his class. He told stories that had nothing to do with what it was we were studying. Reads his slides word for word. Isn't clear when answering questions. He had about 2 1/2 hours to cover 2 chapters. We barely got through 1 chapter all because of his stories.

Show up to class for an extra bump in the grade at the end--well worth it for many people I talked to. Final was different from midterm so if you do well on midterm don't ease up studying for the final or study the same way. I read and did powerpoints which saved me on some things so if you're after an A I recommend both. HIGHLY recommend Brignone.

Shout out to Brignon. He loves econ and teaches decently well. Can go off on tangents and is opinionated. Overall great professor. 1 midterm, 2 narrative summary type papers (easy 10% of your grade) and the final. Tough final and a lot of questions from the text somewhat of a curveball. Homework readings take long and can be tough. Great teacher!

Look, Brignone isn't as passionate as most business professors I've had, and he teaches straight from online textbook so it's dry, but the class isn't as terrible as you've heard. If you are wanting the chance to get an A in econ 110 take it from him. Writing assignments are auto A's if you hand them in, tests are rough but doable.

This class is very doable, but expect to study a lot cause the tests cover 10 chapters with 45 questions. There is one midterm and a final, so if you mess up on the midterm your chances of getting an A are slim even if you do great on everything else. Work hard and you'll get an A.
Great Teacher. Great Class. Do it.

Professor Brignone is by far the best professor I have ever had! It was so refreshing to have a class where my standards and beliefs were not challenged. For all of you constitutionalists out there, take this class! Also, the way he teaches the economic principles is very applicable to real world situations. Cannot recommend more!!!

This class consumes your life. The amount of suck from Econ 110 comes the fact that it's a hard class and is not Brignone's fault.   Brignone is very passionate about Econ and is really good at making the class like it too. He's merciful to those who invest in the class so even though the material can be difficult, know that he's on your team.

I took ECON with Kearl in Provo, and he made me hate Economics.  Brignone was more clear with his points, and he made this class pretty easy. He changed my whole perspective and applied everything. DO THE HOMEWORK. STUDY FOR THE TEST. READ THE TWO BOOKS. Easy A if you do this. I put in an hour a week for homework and 6 hours for the test.

Professor Brignone is the man! He gives you every opportunity to be successful. Although the homework and tests are a little challenging he gives you 3 tries to re-do your homework and a study guide for both tests. I'm not the greatest at ECON but if I had to take this class again Brignone would be my number one pick!
HE WAS TERRIBLE

I thought the class was very doable. I have heard the horror stories about other econ teachers and am thoroughly convinced that his class is by far the least amount of course work and gives you the best opportunity to get a decent grade.

This class is a tough one (But that's just ECON). He is very understanding and will work with you. He is very opinionated and passionate about ECON. I enjoyed his lectures. If you put in the hard work it is doable to get an A. There are about 2 assignments a week, midterm, two-2 page papers, the final and possible extra credit. Great professor.
I took this class twice. The SLC center with Brignone is the way to go. It's still not easy, but it is very doable.

I loved being in this class. He helped his students with any confusion or questions. You have to approach him when you have questions. The only thing really confusing was the syllabus, I would not depend on his student development syllabus. He's very busy so sometimes he would have to change assignments and lecture days.
Brignone never really had a lesson outline but I always learned something regardless. Got boring at times but its an easy class.

I really liked taking Econ from him. The lectures were long but he went over everything we needed in class to do well on the HW and on the tests. You have to write two 2-page papers but they are basically just reaction/opinion papers on a book and on a conference talk from the 60's.

This is the best teacher to take Econ from at BYU. His lectures are interesting and he is very passionate on the subject. To make everything better there are only 2 tests (including the non-comprehensive final), and he lets you take a 3x5 card in with you!

Seriously one of the best professors BYU has to offer. This is probably the most relevant class I have ever taken before. Definitely recommend Brignone. He throughly explains concepts that are pretty tough to grasp.

As a teacher he was not very good. I don't know why I even went to class. It more of just an online class. As long as you do the online work you can get through the class just fine. He teachers a little and talks about a lot of nonsense. It still took a lot of work so I don't if taking it from him is any easier than other teachers.
