Very interesting topic, class attendance is not necessary and honestly doesn't benefit you much. If you read the textbook and do the homework that is where almost all of the learning comes from.  He has a genuine love for teaching econ and helping the students understand the topic

Sure it wasn't easy, but no Econ class is a walk in the park.   His grading scale was very self explanatory. Grades are as follows. (30% midterm, 30% final, 30% weekly online homework, 10% book reports.) I fee like everything on the tests were covered in class.   He is very very conservative politically which I liked.

There are 2 tests and both are difficult. He does a great job of telling you what to study though. He is a hardcore libertarian. If you don't like his political views, you will not enjoy the lectures. He is probably the easiest professor for econ 110, but the class is still difficult. The class is interesting though and I strongly recommend him.

Professor Brignone is a really good dude, I've gotta say. I took his class at the BYU SL center and I found that it was well worth it. Attendance is not mandatory, but definitely helps with some of the tougher chapters. I would take the class from him again if I had to. Very straightforward homework, and the midterm was very manageable.

The whole reason I took this class was to avoid getting a C in Kearl's class in Provo. I got low B's on the midterm and final and still ended up with an A-, so driving up to Salt Lake each week was well worth my time. He is very conservative fiscally, almost libertarian, so keep that in mind. Overall, I'd say this is the way to go for ECON 110.

If you are taking Econ just to get an A may not be the best class. More importantly if you want to understand how having an understanding of economics effects every aspect of your life  no matter what you do. Then take this class. It was hard But I LOVED what I learned!!!

##Bro Brignone is a great guy.  He tied the Gospel into lessons well and loves economics. But, after the final I realized his lectors are near useless.  He rips on the Government like crazy, but respects other opinions. Our classes Midterm average was above the norm, so I think he made the final crazy hard. No one did well at all. Great guy. EasyB

He has a descent philosophy on economics, but he doesn't know how to teach very well and you have to depend on the online textbook to learn. Loves to get on useless tangents where he preaches to you about how spiritual he is with economics.

Brignone requires you to learn a lot. What less could you expect in BYU ECON?  The Aplia online homework was demanding, but you learned a ton.  He was really a cool guy and he does care about his students.  I would much rather take this class from him than take it in Provo! He was fair and only has two tests, each worth 30% of your grade.

I thought that this class was absolutely great.  I took the class because I had to but i left with a huge respect and interest for economics.  He teaches you things that you can actually apply in your life.  You do have to read a lot, but if you do you can get an A in the class. The people that rated him poorly were probably left winged:)
Did really well in his class, final was only 40% when I took it and the questions are just like the ones that we have in quizzes.  Everything seemed pretty fair to me...

Going to class is pretty much a waste of time. You can do equally as well or poorly on the homework without him. In fact I am almost sure I would have done much better if I devote the two hour class period to reading the textbook. The final is a mystery that he will not help you solve. Very poor teacher.

He one of the worse teachers i have had. He is at explaining the concepts and goes off on random topics throughout class. His final test is the worst part. He tests you on the hardest material without teaching any of it beforehand and the test lasts about 3 hrs. You can average an A+ the whole year and then get a D because of the final.

Brignone openly admits that he likes to hear himself talk, which in my opinion is the only reason he teaches.  Horrible communicator, who needs to learn that teaching isn't about HIM it's about the students and the subject matter.  He views any question as a challenge of his authority.  He's a weird guy on an ego trip.  AVOID HIS CLASS!!!

I would not take Econ from Brignone if I could do it over again.  His final was incredibly unfair and with it being 50% of your grade, don't expect a good grade.  He would mess up a lot in his lectures and left you so confused.  He doesn't like to be wrong and is kind of arrogant.

Brother Brighnone is a cool guy and I really liked him.  However, I didn't like the grading scale of the class.  50% of your final grade depends on the final exam.  You could get 100% on everyting else and bomb the final and end up with a D-.

Dr. Joe Price is such a fantastic teacher and I loved taking his class. He was VERY accessible outside class, takes student feedback seriously and is very personable. Didn't feel the textbook was necessary but PRACTICE IS!!! Test heavy class so practice, practice, practice and take advantage of the TA lab or this class will eat you alive!
Brother Price knows this is a tough class and does everything he can to help out. Enjoyed his lectures, and this class as a whole.

I loved Joe, but he did not teach the exam material that well. I never did any of the readings or TA reviews, and still succeeded with only the given study materials and quizzes. Super awesome lectures though, felt like a Tedtalk every morning.

Econ 110 is a beast of a class, but I loved the way Joe Price taught it. He explains topics very well, but you will have to put in time outside of class and probably at the TA lab if you want a good grade. Joe Price isn't afraid to share his opinions on occasion in class, and has thoughtful takes on the world. He clearly cares a lot about students.

Dr. Price is a very generous professor. He has a lot of built-in mercy in this class, and tries to help everyone. There are midterm reinforcements, a bunch of assignments dropped (including a midterm), and just overall a lot of help. Econ is a hard class but he helps you as much as he can. Take ECON 110 with Dr. Price.

Dr price is good. Econ is a hard class. Some material in lectures is unnecessary but most is interesting. One thing I will say is throughout the semester he was hyping up a curve. “You will be shocked with how merciful I am” only to change an A from 93 to 92 and A- from 90 to 89 so that was overhyped. Curve really only helped lower grade students.

Some things to note. He drops 1 of the midterms we take out of the 3. His lectures are always interesting and engaging. He articulates his thoughts so well and his beliefs sound weird at first, like we should have a tax for tall people, but his reasons are solid and valid so it is fun hearing him explain. The final is like 33 percent of the grade.

Amazing professor, he kept things very interesting during the lectures and explained things well. Econ 110 is extremely difficult regardless of who you take it from, but Dr. price builds the course well with lots of practice and help as well as forgiveness. Your lowest midterm and lowest assignment from every category is dropped.

Dr. Price is caring and knowledgeable about Economics. His class is very tough, and planning is the key. Plan to read the textbook, take quizzes multiple times, do midterm reinforcements, and go to the TA lab and reviews. This is a 4-credit class in disguise so treat it that way and you'll do good. If you want the A put in work. Good Luck!

I would not recommend taking this class from Joe Price. He tends to ramble about loosely related topics during the lectures, taking time away from practice problems and explaining things more in-depth. I just don't feel like I got anything out of his lectures. Honestly AI taught me everything I know for this class.

Econ 110 is a hard class, but Dr. Price teaches it incredibly. His lectures are interesting and relate to a lot of relevant real-world events. The class also has a lot of built-in mercy with a dropped midterm and curve. People don't like the difficulty of Econ, but if you actually take the time to learn the content well, it's extremely fulfilling.

Honestly this class is hard but made harder by the professor. The lectures are rambling for 75 min and truly acts like he doesn't know what he's talking about either. The TAs were great but lectures won't help understand anything. the textbook is better but the tests aren't really set up from the textbook. I would recommend taking from anyone else.

Professor Price teaches a hard class. You definitely need to put the work in, but it is very rewarding. His lectures go over a lot of material, but they are really interesting and explain lots of the concepts. the best way to prepare for exams in this class is to take the quizzes over and over.

I really enjoyed taking this class from him. His lectures were insightful and inspiring. That being said, the class is pretty clear cut. Most of your grade come from 3 midterms (lowest one gets dropped) and the final. You need to put in work outside of class to do well, so get into the habit of going to the TA lab and taking the practice quizzes.

Joe Price is the absolute GOAT. His lectures are fire and you wouldn't think you'd leave an econ lecture inspired, but you do. Prof. Price knows what's up.That being said, Econ is a HARD class. Even though he's a good teacher, you'll need to spend hours outside of class to fully understand the material. TAKE THIS CLASS IT'S WORTH IT

nice guy. has been teaching for 20 years. could explain simpler (surprising he still explains this bad sometimes given he's been teaching for 20 years). makes us do problems in class. suggestion to him: show HOW to do the problem before giving it to us by walking through a couple practice problems with us.

I'm having trouble verbalizing the hatred that I feel towards this 'professor' and frankly the entire economics department. Supposedly he went to Cornell for his Phd but you would never know it when taking his class. Class is designed for you to NOT succeed, the TAs admit it. Don't take ECON, ever.

I really struggled in this class and got no help from the professor. He is not approachable. The homework is not terribly difficult and you work with a group. The class is not set up for student success. Stay away from him.
Tough class but learned a lot

Dr. Price is a very sharp professor of economics and an exceptional person. He gives plenty of resources for you to learn if you are willing. Take good notes, go to the TA lab when you have questions, take the practice quizzes over and over, and watch the Econ w/ Adam videos. I cannot recommend Dr. Price and this class enough.

One of the best professors I've ever had! I think people only rate him low because it's a hard class they weren't ready for, which is mostly due to things outside his control. Lots of built in mercy with a midterm and several quizzes dropped, and he teaches with a great balance of clear concepts, real world applicability, and practice test problems
Dr Price is incredible! He gives a large test bank so you can study exactly the kind of material that will be on exams. He provides the tools for success. And he's just all around a great guy!

Class is incredibly difficult and Price does not explain the concepts well. He does have a lot of built in "mercy" where your lowest midterm is dropped. You can also make back some of the points. He also drops some of the attendances and quizzes. The text book is also useless. Pick someone else, or even better, AVOID THIS CLASS.

If you want your GPA to die, take this class. It's extremely difficult, lectures are a waste of time, and you basically have to teach yourself. So, if you enjoy pain, you'd love this class. The textbook is useless and expensive.
Love this guy.

Tests are 73% of the total grade and brutal, especially the final. I had an A the whole semester and I still got a C on the final after 12 straight hours of studying. The class itself is easy but the way questions are worded are confusing and multiple answers could be argued for most if the time. Tangents about social issues were common in lecture.

Definition of "skip class, won't pass." He goes FAST in lectures and the practice tests he puts on learning suite WILL NOT prepare you for the actual tests. A lot less mercy in 380 than 110 --- no dropped midterms. He rounded my grade to an A- from an 89.8. I think the difficulty was more the class than the professor.

Good professor, had his heart in the right place. Difficult class of 800ish students, so rely on TAs for help. Quizzes after lectures due 30 mins before the next lecture - tedious but good practice. Random 5 papers 2 on news 3 on the second book we had to buy. Class participation recorded for attendance. Grace built in with option to drop a midterm

Econ is a hard class, it is a miracle that I got a B. I heard the TA's say over and over in the lab that Price is harder than the other professors, mostly because he wont spend time in class showing us what well be tested on rather just the definitions so that's the best advice I can give take it from another professor or you'll do all the learning

Price was decent, and explained concepts fairly well, he would just go on tangents that didn't seem super relevant. Concepts can be confusing, but if you do the quizzes (unlimited attempts) and ask questions in the TA lab before exams you should be fine. However, the final is worth 33% of the grade, so make sure you study hard for it.

The course is very straight forward with lots of materials and practice problems. The "Econ with Adam" videos and practice exams are all that I did to study, and I got around 95% on all the exams. I even stopped going to class for the last month, and as long as I did the homework I was fine. Probably wouldn't recommend that though. Over-hated class

I don't understand the complaints about Professor Price. He's INCREDIBLY merciful, despite what others say. He drops 1 midterm, 1 essay, 3 quizzes, and 4 attendances, plus allows makeup on exams and curves the class. The quizzes are old test questions, and there's plenty of practice. You won't see this kind of help or mercy in most other classes.

PLEASE do not take this class unless you absolutely have to. This class is extremely difficult and we barely have things to do outside of class to prepare for exams, which make up the majority of our grade. Professor talks about "built in mercy" but the only mercy I've experienced is the mercy of God helping me to not act violently in this class.

My advice: go to class for attendance points, then watch econ w/ Adam and Dr. Azevedo's micro and macro playlists on YouTube to learn. Do every practice quiz and midterm. IT WILL HELP!! Lowest midterm dropped, midterm corrections if you get

Dr. Price is great! His class is honestly tough, but that's ECON 110 for ya. There is so much mercy built into the class that anyone willing to put enough time into it can get an A. He provides so much material for you to study and practically infinite practice problems, which come super in handy for the exams.

I think Prof Price is a nice guy, but his perception of "mercy" is skewed. He originally told us that we could miss 8 days of class and then at the end of the semester said that it's actually 4. Even if the syllabus says that students shouldn't be held accountable for the mistakes that he makes in setting up the course. Not fair or merciful.

Professor Price is just great, explains the concepts, and answers questions. It's hard to practice the concepts with only a 10-question quiz per lecture and no real homework. You need to put in the effort to be successful in this class, like doing the pre-readings and reflecting on the lectures (something I wish I did).

It's hard to review cause the class is just so hard and there were like 800+ kids in the class. He does well at teaching, he is so genuine, and is clearly so passionate about the subject. I think he could explain it a little more simplistically to us, but thats kinda what the TAs did too. Just put in the work, and you'll do fine.

Despite the poor reviews, Price is actually the goat. This class is difficult, but an A is attainable if you put in lots of study hours and make it a priority. I gave a 4 for quality just because I personally feel that he doesn't answer questions very well. I wish he could teach us economics like we were kids so we could actually understand lol.
Dr. Price is a nice guy and a great option for ECON 110. His class is so hard but I know that the other ECON 110 professors are also super hard.

Professor Price does give a lot of mercy with his grading which is nice, he drops quizzes, attendance, and even on test. However, it shows that he does not care about his students, only about his content. On LS we originally had 8 attendance quizzes dropped and then he went and changed it to 4, without any warning. The mercy is nice, but that's it!

Dr. Price loves Economics, and that passion can be felt in these lectures, I don't love economics, but Dr price showed me why one could love it. There is a fire for this material that very few other professors have. It was a great pleasure to know him, and even though the exams were pretty tricky, he was the best person to take Econ 110 from

Prof. Price is really kind and caring. You can tell he is passionate about econ. Sometimes he struggles breaking things down for those who are just learning these concepts. Just go to the TA test reviews and you will do just fine on the tests! Not that bad but it for sure takes some outside work, and dedication to do well.

Dr. Price is the best! There are easier professors to take Econ-380 from but he is still great! He cares about you so much and you can tell. He is a brilliant economist and his class would absolutely be beneficial to take. He skips allot of Algebra when teaching so just make sure you have that down!

Price doesn't teach what you actually need for the tests and it all falls to the students to learn most of it on their own or with TAs. For most of the semester up until the last month of class, he was teaching the materials for the quizzes after they had to be turned in, and, even then, he didn't teach us how to do most of the questions.

Economics is hard to wrap your head around, but there are a lot of willing and wonderful TAs. Dr. Price did a great job at providing examples to make hard concepts easier to understand. You'll definitely need to put in time and study, but it's possible to do well. Most of the class did well on each exam.

Horrible teacher. Avoid him at all costs. Take Platt. Classes are massive, 200+. TAs carry and are the only reason this class is doable. Take it from me, there are better things to do than waste time/money on this professor. Platt is awesome, go for him instead.

Dr. Price is easily one of the best professors I have had at BYU. I took his Econ 110 in the spring and loved it. He isn't just a good teacher, he is a good human. You can feel his sincerity and love for economics and the gospel. I would recommend that everyone take Econ 110 from Dr. Price. The success rate of our class was really high.

Not a good teacher. He explains the problems by throwing numbers in the air and expects you to understand them. We had another teacher come for one day, and it was 100X better. The TAs are the only reason his class is doable. Even the YouTube videos he recommended only explained half the solutions to the questions. Choose another teacher.

I learned nothing while in class. Everything I learned came from the TA videos. He also calls himself "merciful" but if you miss any classes, there is no empathy for any extraneous problems you have. The paradigm of this class expects you to focus 100% of your attention to it, despite it being just another general. Just take it in SLC.

I honestly learned more from the Econ with Adam YouTube videos made from a previous TA the year before than in class. I have to go research myself the content after the class since his teaching style is not visual, more talking through the concepts. It seems the TAs are willing to work with you but not the professor at times.

This professor actually didn't teach me anything about economics. Maybe someone who already knew most of this content would've succeeded in this class. But I had to spend hours outside of class, not studying, but simply reteaching myself all the content he was trying to teach. I would've died without the TAs. They should get paid, not him.

Professor Price's lectures made me excited to come to class every day, despite the 8:00 am start time. His research breaks were fascinating and I always understood the application for the math we were doing, which was super cool. The homework was pretty light but I would highly recommend studying intentionally for the quizzes.

Professor Price is legit the goat. He is super nice and explains everything super well, but sometimes goes off on tangents although they normally are pretty interesting. 3 midterms but your lowest is dropped and a final that is worth about 33% of your grade. Watching the Econ with Adam youtube videos will carry your grade. Take it from him for sure
If you are taking Econ 110 TAKE IT FROM Professor Price. He tries hard to make the content understandable and cares about your success as a student.

Price is a nice guy and does fascinating research, but everything I learned in this class was from the TAs (the lab is so underrated) and Khan Academy. Price just got totally off topic in every lecture and I often felt totally clueless on quizzes. Unless you're ready to teach yourself super tough material, take this from literally anyone else.

Attendance wasn't necessarily mandatory, but you'll want to go to class in order to do well; this class is hard by nature but Dr. Price is a phenomenal teacher. His teaching is fun, exciting, and interesting. Best economics professor I've had and one of my favorite professors. I took 110 and 380 from him and loved both.

Dr. Price was the best econ professor I could have had. He teaches the material simply and gives you lots of opportunities to succeed. You can take the quizzes unlimited times to really learn the material. This is a very hard class but if you read the textbook before the lectures and study hard you will succeed. Take econ from Dr. Price!

I highly recommend Dr. Price. Econ can be tough, but Dr. Price makes it enjoyable. His unlimited quiz attempts let you practice and learn from your mistakes and learn the material in preparation for the exams. He is very gracious when it comes to grades and isn't there to tank your GPA. You will need to work hard though to understand the material.

Dr. Price is incredible. He gives the keys to success for a hard class: reading the chapter before class, and then being in class to learn with other students makes success possible. He teaches engagingly and loves his students. The class has lectures with iClicker and then quizzes with unlimited attempts. TAs are great. Take Price!

Dr. Price is the most wholesome person I have ever met in my entire life. He is very passionate about economics and makes a very difficult class quite enjoyable. His research breaks were awesome, and he gives you lots of tricks to remember things. The class was hard, and sometimes he went a little fast, but if you put in the work you'll be fine.

Take it from this guy! Gives you the opportunity to take the quizzes as many times to get a perfect score (no other prof does that) You can miss 4 days of class. One midterm drops. You can do midterm corrections which he promises if you do the corrections for each test he will pass you. He is committed to change econ where everyone just fails tests

"Teaches" "one of the hardest classes at BYU", which I realized too late is called that because he loves to ramble off on tangents and get his own material wrong rather than actually teach the curriculum. Can't recommend to my worst enemy.

Dr. Price has very clear lectures and expectations. Though in a large section he can't give every student the attention he wants to, he does his best to be available to each student and provide great resources to help each person succeed. I have loved this class so far. It takes quite a bit of time to do well, but that would be true with any prof.

He is really kind and super fair with the class. He gives all the materials to succeed. His test averages are super high. If someone thinks this ECON 110 class is hard they would definitely fail with the other professors.

The person who left the previous review obviously did poor on midterm 1 and wanted to leave a negative review as a result. If you don't study, read the textbook, etc., you will do bad in any economics class. Joe Price is getting in trouble by the other econ professors because our class performed so well on the first midterm. Almost 80% class avg.
Was hard for no reason. If you want to take Econ 110, please take a different teacher if you love yourself
Very tough class, but Dr Price strengthened both my intelligence and my spirituality. Great person and great professor.

Dr. Price is easily my favorite professor I've had at BYU. He is super smart and is very good at conveying the information to his students. He teaches the class in a way that will be helpful no matter what you choose to do in life. Tests quizzes and homework are all very hard but Dr. Price provides tools to prepare well (& there's a curve)

Dr. Price is awesome. He is so smart and explains things in a very detailed manner. I never got bored in his class. His exams/quizzes are super hard but go to the TA if you are confused and you'll do fine. I never read the textbook but still did fine in the class. Not a lot of homework which I loved. 10/10 recommend.

If you were ever to read a review that suggested Dr. Price is arrogant or something like that, know that it's not at all true, because I was (hypothetically) in the same class as that hypothetical reviewer who would say that and I honestly have no idea how they could get that impression from that (hypothetical) April 2022 class. Great class!

One of the best professors I've had at my time at BYU. The tests are tough, but he preps you well and the practice quizzes are very reflective of exams. Joe is awesome though so definitely take 110 from him if you plan to take it.

Dr Price is an amazing teacher. He cares about his class so much and is incredibly passionate about his field and the gospel. It's genuinely a life changing class if you allow it.

It's a demanding class, but if you sit on the front rows, take notes, and use the TA labs regularly you'll do great. Just don't let yourself get caught behind.

Dr. Price is very impressive & down-to-earth. Lectures are amazing; their only flaw is that he sometimes brushes over a step in process-based problems & doesn't write some things on the board. Other than that, lectures are so great. You could most definitely succeed without purchasing the textbook & only revising his lecture notes before class.

Professor Price is a fantastic guy. He explains challenging concepts very clearly and expects his class to put in a lot of work to succeed. He wants his students to do well and gives them all the tools to do so. His in-class advice is stellar and his behavior/attitude towards many things is exemplary.

I enjoyed the class, but did not like Dr. Price. He is quirky, prideful, and arrogant. Expect a quiz every class, though they are not too bad if you do the reading. His grading is arbitrary, and doesn't give you an explanation for why you missed a question. We had to do a group paper, but he gives little instruction and has no grading rubric.
Joe Price is one of the most caring professors I've ever had! He is brilliant and his class can transform his life if you let him. The research paper is hard but if you start early it isn't too bad.

My second class with Prof. Price. Great guy that's very personable. Gives pretty interesting lectures. I only read the textbook like 3 times so it's not necessary. Some tough concepts but the class is structured such that you can get help from the TAs or other students. Tests and homework are tough but doable.

He has an uncommon and vital gift for creating a judgement free and genuinely amicable classroom experience, even in a university which actively fosters academic and spiritual comparison and judgmental competition. On top of that, he's just a great teacher. This course is what every BYU professor aspires their courses to be.

Dr. Price is the best. He loves Econ and he loves the Lord. The two things mix wonderfully as he gives you tools to confront challenging problems. His handwriting is a little sloppy and he goes fast but as soon as you ask questions he'll slow down and explain the concepts well. Also, great professor if you use the UAC.

Dr. Price is really relatable, humble, and caring. He made econ really interesting through research breaks and interesting studies. The class was a lot of work and studying. Assignments are straight-forward and fairly easy but midterms and finals are tough. Read the book and attend the lectures and you'll do fine. Take this class from him!
Extremely inspirational and intelligent... I love Dr. Price so much!!!
Great professor who takes time to teach you how economics apply to the real world. Tough tests and a paper is due every week but it was manageable. Loved this class!

Econ 110 is a dreaded class, but Dr. Price guides you through it with clear lectures, great real life examples, and access to TONS of practice problems. Go to class, do the reading and homework, take advantage of the practice tests, and you'll survive!

Dr. Price was incredible! I was really worried about taking this course during Spring term, but I am super glad that I did! He was fair with grading and the lectures were always engaging. The assignments and tests were fair, and the workload never felt like a burden. I definitely recommend taking the class from him, you won't regret it!

Dr. Price is a great teacher. He is passionate about economics and his lectures were usually engaging. However, he moves very quickly and it can be extremely difficult to keep up in class. I found that I learned more from the reading and homework than from the lectures. Tests are hard so go to the reviews. He curves the final grades!

One of the best professors in BYU. His lectures are attracting and inspiring. The exams are not hard too. However, remember to listen to those videos in Mind-tap, which counts to the grade of attendance.

Hes passionate and well respected in Economics which made learning from him fun. I thoroughly enjoyed each lecture. He clarified the important concepts in class and shows how to apply the knowledge. If you want a good grade you will need to take the time to learn with the TAs and use additional materials (AC/DC ECON SAVED ME). Its a fun class.

Dr. Price was not the best professor, he does not prepare students for his tests at all. Be prepared to read prior to every class, go to class, do the homework after every class, and then live in the TA lab. If you do not put a lot of work in this class, you will not do well, the only reason I will pass was COVID made tests open note. Avoid Price.

Terrible. I do not care if people think he is nice. He asks terrible questions that are not based in reality or utilize critical thinking. He gives the stupidest life advice, I mean truly awful. He works in absolutes. Is the class hard? Not really. Study on your own, he does not cover all the material. Easy enough class, terrible teacher.

Dr. Price is a good guy. He doesn't have much experience teaching 110, which was very evident. His lectures were really interesting, but I feel like they only covered 30% of the material we were tested on. Make sure to do the reading and practice tests and you will be fine.

Professor Price is a great guy and a pretty solid choice for Econ110. It was his first semester teaching this class but I feel he was very fair and open. Buy the Notes packet or you're basically sunk. You absolutely have to work for your grade but that's to be expected. If you have to take 110, I would 100% take it from Price.

He often goes through the slides fast so buy the slide packet, read the chapter before, and get ready to write. The online reading quizzes can sometimes be hard, depending on the type of question. Get ready to work hard, do a lot of reading, and study a lot.

Issues: 1) Arbitrary grades, even when you accurately answer a question it's a tossup whether he'll count it as correct (See 2 reviews below, this was common). 2) Not helpful in working with students: Ex. He requires in class quiz taking even when issues like job interviews, medical, court arise. Pros: Interesting topic, passionate professor.

Price decides to teach behavioral economics as if it were a 100-level survey course  very broad, little depth. Which would be fine, except he assigns arbitrary grades to his easy assignments to get his desired grades so BYU doesn't get on his tail for giving an easy class. Very frustrating. He is not very understanding or helpful outside of class.

Pro: Every class had a practical lesson. Cons: Price's unbendingness and grading procedures. Quizzes must be taken day of, no excuses (even athletic or medical). Tests are easy, but very broad and poorly graded. He docks points arbitrarily to get a distribution he likes (I used verb " choose," my cousin used "determine," somehow I was wrong?)

Dr. Price is incredibly passionate about economics. He appreciates students who are willing to put in the work needed to thoroughly learn the material, and is willing to adjust the curriculum according to the needs of the class. This class might be difficult if you are unfamiliar with reading and understanding academic studies.
Subject material was interesting but he talked through everything really fast and it was always confusing when/where to turn in our exams, and there didn't really seem to be a good grading criteria.

Price is the man. He teaches clearly (he talks fast, just tell him to slow down) and is interested in us learning. His grading is fair and consistent. Tests are exactly what we did in the homework and he knows the answer to everything. Definitely take 380 from Price.

This class is interesting, but Dr. Price often breezes through the really hard concepts, which makes it difficult to grasp the concepts sometimes. The research paper is a nightmare if you hate group work, and top of that, there is very little guidance for it. You'll love it if you love the research aspect of Econ. If not, I do not reccommend it.

Professor Price is genuinely passionate about Economics. He does sometimes go quickly through important topics. You just have to raise your hand and tell him to slow down. He often explains concepts in several different ways (mathematical, economic theory, or just common sense), which helps all types of learners. Take advantage of the past exams!

I tried to like Professor Price, I really did.  But I did not feel like he cared about me.  I liked his research breaks, and his habit of inviting people to lunch occasionally after class.  He goes fast.  I'm amused that some described his tests as easy, but maybe they had a helpful TA and felt comfortable going to Professor Price's office hours.
Great Class! Every lecture is super interesting. Tests aren't that hard and you have practice tests and quizzes to help you study.
He is a genius, but he lectures at a level far above the ability of most students. Too busy doing his research to help you.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU. Fairly difficult subject matter, but it's interesting and he explains concepts in such a way that even a non-quant like me could do well in the class. This class should make you love economics.
Not well organized, poor at explaining concepts

Dr. Price is a genuinely great guy, very caring and passionate about economics. My main problem is that he breezes through conceptual explanations very fast, and sometimes he just doesn't even give them. Mostly he just expects us to memorize the formulas. This gets confusing and overwhelming very fast. Homework groups are a life saver though.

This is a difficult class, so expect to work hard. Dr. Price realizes how tough it is, and he is great at helping you to grasp as much of the material as possible. Upper level Econ classes are simply difficult. You will feel like you are drowning. Just remember how awesome Econ is and that everyone else will be dying right with you.

I loved Profesor Price as a person. He would take a step back from class material and open our eyes to some cool things in Economics. I struggle with math and i often found myself lost during the class. Professor Price is a genius and i felt like the class lectures were going too fast for me. I would take another class from Professor Price.

Dr. Price is a great teacher and he's brilliant. Sometimes it feels like he lectures above the level of the class and caters to the student who he is familiar with, but overall it was an amazing class.
This is a good class and a good professor to take it from. He takes time to focus on economics research which really brings the material to life.

I really did not like Dr. Price's class. The material was interesting, but I always felt extremely confused when I left his class. The TAs were great, and they are the reason that I got an A in the class. Dr. Price is smart, but he is not really a good teacher. Assignments were helpful. Tests were hard, but similar to assignments Don't buy the book

The class is organized in such a way that if YOU put in the work YOU will get the GRADE you want.  Dr. Price sincerely tries to keep everything as unambiguous as possible, and his "research breaks" keeps everything relevant to the news. I would say Price is as much of a sure thing as it gets with professors.

Dr. Price is the man. Lectures are great, well organized, and interesting. He is the most patient professor I have ever had. He makes it fairly easy to do well since he is very clear what kinds of questions will be on the test. He puts amazing lecture notes online that are a big help. I really don't know what more you could ask of him!
Easiest class I ever took.  Look over past exams and quizzes, and it's easy to score high on them.  Dr Price is really interesting too.

Incredible course designed and taught by an incredible professor!  Behavioral Economics is the best course I've taken at BYU and Dr. Price might be the best professor I've had.  He teaches very practical knowledge and assignments actually build useful skills.  You can't ask for more from a course!
Good lecturer. Helpful, wants you to do well. Organized class. I suggest him.

One of the best lecturers I have ever had at BYU, in or out of the Econ Department. He moves fast but is happy to go back and clarify, and posts very detailed review notes online that were EXTREMELY helpful. He uses a lot of similar problems from quizzes, and practice tests on the midterms so if you study them hard you'll do well. HIGHLY RECOMMEND
Great teacher. Gives quizzes on certain days, but they are all given on the syllabus. Exams use a lot of the same questions as the practice tests so make sure to go over them before the tests.

Everything you need is online. Great lecturer, you know exactly the types of things that will be on the tests. He takes a break every class to talk about econ research which is awesome. I basically never used the book, all his notes are online.
My favorite professor so far at BYU. Was very interested in student success and made lectures interesting with a high level of class participation. Take 380 from Price.

Posts everything on blackboard: past exams, quizzes, lecture notes...exams are 80-90% taken from past ones.  He's super willing to take questions and re-explain concepts.  Definitely take 380 from him, and any other classes he teaches

One of the best professors I have had at BYU. Very kind good man and great teacher. He wants everyone to succeed and gives you all the tools to do so (past exams, lecture notes online, past quizzes, good TAs etc.) Younger so not as well known, but he will be ranted and raved about more and more as he has more and more students.
I enjoyed every moment in the class. The bloke really loves economics and taking this class with him really will you if you'll love or hate economics.
He is a wonderful teacher.  If you are an economics major and haven't taken 380 yet, take it from Price.

If you do the reading, the lectures are pretty easy to follow. Sometimes he flies through the math pretty quick. He really knows his stuff. He'll make a point to know your name and say hi to you when he sees you on campus.

Super nice guy who loves the topic but has no idea how to teach it.  He flies through material so quickly, doesn't explain anything as he's going, and it seems like he's often talking in another language.  Only take if you have a very strong intuitive understanding of calculus and a decent background in economics (more than 110)
Awesome class. Outstanding professor.

Professor price takes a lot of time discussing current issues, and presenting them as "cool economic topics" but has trouble relating them to the class cirriculum. The homework is done in groups & the tests usually have a couple of the current homework problems on them, so if you make sure you understand the homework you'll be fine.
A great professor! He absolutely loves the material and is passionate about economics. He makes the class fun and his enthusiasm makes you want to learn it all. I highly recommend him.
New professor this year, very intelligent man.  You can tell he loves the subject by the passion he has while he is teaching.

Such an incredible professor. He teaches with such genuine joy and passion and is so knowledgable. Loved going to lectures and learning, did get confusing sometimes, but go to office hours and he will teach you any topic in a way that you can understand. Form your own study group and run through the study guide for the test every other week.

Amazing professor. A test every other week but no official midterm or final. These tests are only on the content that you learned in that two week period. He gives clear "study questions" that will help a lot on those tests. His assignments are about two-three a week where the use of AI is encouraged and they help you to learn the material.

Dr. Griffitts is really kind and knows his material well. His lectures can be hard to focus in if you get distracted easily. He gives about 26 assignments (discovery logs), which are weighted more than the seven bi-weekly mini-tests (learning checks), so strong assignment scores can boost your grade even if you don't test well.

Dr. Griffitts is an extremely kind guy and really knows his stuff, but his lectures are hard to follow for those of us who have a hard time paying attention in the first place. His exams are extremely difficult. TAs will be your saving grace in this class if you do not understand a topic. Dr. Griffitts knows a ton about sourdough starters too.

I was taking 121 from Sandra Hope then she became I’ll halfway through the semester. Dr. Griffitts took over her class and told us he would keep with the flow and difficulty of the class…WRONG. The class become x10 harder he tested us on things we didn’t learn and was not clear on a study guide or expectations for the class. Bad experience.
You know those people that make you feel stupid for any little question you ask? Yeah, that's Professor Griffitts. That's all I need to know about you.

Dr. Griffitts is a real gem. He expects a lot out of his students, but I have learned more from him that I have from most of my college professors combined. He really likes to make students think and figure things out on their own, but he is willing to help and is very available. Would recommend to anyone, and would take his class over again.

If science is not your thing, this will be very hard. But if it is, you will work for it but your knowledge will be expanded and enriched! Griffits is super passionate about his subject matter and makes lectures interesting. He is kind and wants you to succeed, but you'll work for it. Overall, though, its worth it because you'll learn so much!

Dr. Griffitts was a great professor and made Molecular Biology so interesting! I thoroughly enjoyed going to each lecture and taking the tests. He really likes to make us "think like scientists." He is extremely funny and I laughed multiple times each lecture. He may not be the easiest to take the class from, but it is SO worth it.

This is a hard, fast paced class, but if you memorize the slides (which is much easier said than done), you will get an A. He is extremely nice and helpful. I recommend him! The only thing I wish was different is that the only material you have for the entire class is lecture slides. I just wish there was a book to go along with them.

It was a good class and Dr. Griffitts was a good teacher. No textbook required, but KNOW his slides inside and out. Tough class if your not a good test taker. Impossible to be very prepared for this final, its a level way beyond anything you will see during the semester.

No homework, no time wasted. Pay attention in class, study for the tests, and that's all you have to do. Dr. Griffitts is very interested in his students' success and wants you to do well. Very engaging.

Straight foward. Everything you need to know for the tests is in his slides. This makes it really easy to study only what you need to. He is funny and enthusiastic and makes class fun. Less detailed and in depth than the other 240 teachers.

Completely agree that Griffitts' idea to cut the textbook out of the class was a horrible idea. Is not very clear in class what exactly you will need to know on the test and if you miss class reviewing his slides are a nightmare. He has 6 tests and a final and that's it. Class model only beneficial for students who love test taking. Don't take him.

Wasn't a big fan of this class. Griffitts attempted to streamline the content by removing the textbook/readings, which really was not a good thing. He glosses over concepts he drills you on in the tests and tends to not be really clear on what he wants you to learn or how you're supposed to learn it. Take from someone else.

You couldn't have a more straightforward class. Dr. Griffitts makes it simple: 6 exams then a final. I love the format. You decide how you will learn the concepts and just take the exam biweekly. He is sure to emphasize the things you should know. He loves teaching and makes class fun with his quick humor. Don't look directly at the laser pointer!

No text book needed. Attendance not required. The only grades come from the tests so hopefully ur a good test taker. Everything comes from the power point slides for tests. I loved this teacher all the way until the final. The comprehensive final is A LOT harder than all the tests throughout the year....SERIOUSLY DR. GRIFFITS?!?!

Lectures were very straight forward and enjoyable. The tests came straight from the slides. I would recommend to take this class from him, but be ready to work/memorize! 6 midterms seem like a lot, but it works really well.
Best teacher ever. If you put in the work, you got better grades. No bell curve so everyone who learns the material properly is properly rewarded. Take this class from this teacher!

Dr. Griffitts is an incredible professor.  Any student that passes up having him as a professor at least once is missing out on a lot.  I'd specifically recommend taking his Microbial Genetics (460) course.

Dr Griffitts is great. I really loved his class. I thought he was straight forward with his class lectures. His exams were based directly off the slides and he doesn't have any busy work. Plus, he actually likes teaching. I recommend him for MMBIO 240 any day

In a previous rating I commented that Dr. Griffitts was "condescending" and that he wasn't helpful.  I am retracting these statements. In a moment of anger I wrote them due to a lower than expected grade.  He really does care about his students and desires to serve them and help them.  Take from him, you'll have a great experience!

Dr. Griffitts was a wonderful professor. He really cares about his students and loves teaching.  He puts in a lot of effort into his lectures, and is so willing to clarify things when you approach him.  You do have to study and really know your stuff for the exams because his questions test your critical thinking skills.  I highly recommend him!

Dr Griffitts is great.  He teaches his course like a real University level course, so if you want to be treated like a high school student you may be disappointed.  Otherwise I would highly recommend his class.

I loved Dr. Griffitts! He was an amazing teacher that really cared about his students. I can't believe people call him rude and condescending! He's a really nice guy. He gives you lots of time to come see him during his office hours, and wants you to come in to talk to him about your tests. The tests were definitely do-able, kinda tricky sometimes.

Dr. Griffitts never responded to any of my emails, was fairly condescending to students in class, and loved to use trick questions on tests. Having a test every other week that requires you to memorize virtually every single powerpoint slide becomes old quick. In my opinion, take from someone else.

Prof Griffitts's class is awesome. There is no homework and you never use the textbook. but we did have a test every other week. I thought the tests were pretty easy. (i got a 99% average with minimal studying) his lectures are interesting if you pay attention to his sarcastic comments. My favorite class this semester by far.

A is very plausible in this course, gives a decent test curve. Never cracked open the textbook, but studied the lecture slides intensely and did well in the class. He did a better than average job at keeping class interesting

Poor choice for MMBIO240. Condescending and rude, unapproachable. Text book is a total waste. Tests confusing, often poorly worded. At times his lectures contradict the book and he won't give points back ever, no matter how legit your reason. He teaches alright but seriously I will never take from him again.

He is very helpful but uses a lot of words which you would only understand if you have studied this material extensively before.  Also, the exam questions are worded so that it is difficult to understand exactly what he is looking for in your answer.

Dr. Griffits is great! His tests are completely from the lectures, so he says to read the text book just for clarification if you're not understanding something.  Really knows his stuff and is very open to help you.  Doesn't test on memorization, but on understanding and applying the concepts.  Just make sure to go to class and you'll do great!

This was a challenging course, but Dr. Griffitts always made himself available to answer questions. We read papers instead of a textbook. For half the semester had take home exams which although challenging effectively helped me learn; Dr. Griffitts was also available to help and clarify. This class, especially the lab made a phenomenal experience.
Fairly hard class, but an excellent way to earn variable credits. Has a different sense of humor, kind of sarcastic.  Overall a very easy professor to work with. Very available. Read some fun papers.
He is extremely helpful and you will learn a lot, but he is fair and if you do your work you will do great!  Highly recommended!

I hated this class. Granted, it was his first semester teaching when I took it, but he always spoke in a 'High-and-Mighty' tone as if he was so much better than us. Whenever I asked questions he always made me feel stupid and so I quit paying attention after a while because the class sucked. Don't take it from him if you don't have to!!
HE ROCKS! VERY INTERESTING!!

Professor Selway is an expert in the field, and it shows. His lectures are so enjoyable. Though the organization is sometimes an issue, he leans toward being lenient with the students. He gives study guides for the tests.

Professor Selway is actually one of the best professors I have ever taken classes from. He genuinely cares about his students and is flexible to work with. If you have an interest in Asia, taking class from him is imperative!

I LOVED going to Selway's classes every day. His lectures were always awesome and he valued student participation and legitimately considered our ideas. He didn't teach us what to think and to regurgitate on the test; instead, he taught us how we should think. Would 100% recommend if you want to have an enjoyable and valuable class.

Amazing professor! Super kind, humble, and understanding! FYI, you can find some of his textbooks at the library, don't waste money buying them. Would 110% take his course again and any class from him!

I genuinely wish I could give a better rating. Dr. Selway is so nice and down-to-earth. The organization/structure of the class sucks. 40-80 pages of reading (textbook or academic articles) for every class period. Impossible to study for tests. You're expected to know everything about every country in Asia. Save yourself the stress, don't take him.

This was an interesting class but his grading criteria was not only very subjective, but very unclear. Grades were mostly based off a midterm, a final, and a paper. He takes a long time to grade, which doesn't help you know where you stand in the class and his feedback isn't constructive. Lectures weren't very organized, so studying was difficult.

Professor Selway is the most disorganized professor I have ever taken. He is actually a great teacher, he has the ability to explain concepts very well, but if you try to email him, he will not ever respond. If you are okay with never asking a question outside of class, or assignments taking months to be graded, then he is the professor for you.

He is hard to contact, but is a really merciful grader. he really cares about his students and honestly will do anything to help you succeed. get to know him personally and your life and the class will go better

Very disorganized class, IMPOSSIBLE to contact. Sent him an email asking him to upload a reading (4 days in advance) and then he acted as everyone slacked and no one had told him. Map quiz (with a make up opportunity), midterm (with curve), and then a final (no curve). Group paper (20 pages) that he will grade harshly. Very nice professor though.

If you're someone who values organization and clear directions -- AVOID THIS CLASS! Seriously. Find another class to take. Professor Selway is a caring professor and he tried to help students, but this class was super frustrating because it was so disorganized. 

2 group papers, 1 final individual paper. Disorganized online lectures. No rubrics.

The most frustrating political science class of my BYU career. Professor Selway is hard to communicate with, made my group meet with him on our day off, and his entirely recorded lectures are totally incomprehensible. In the Zoom labs you're sent to breakout rooms and he maybe comes and talks for 4-5 minutes. No support at all. Avoid.

Professor Selway is my favorite political science professor. He genuinely cares about his students and knows us by name. I appreciate that he is always willing to help, & he prepares lectures even when he is gone. He goes above & beyond to teach us what we need to understand. My favorite class, & favorite professor! Prep work is reading, & movies!

Professor Selway is really caring. He wants his students to succeed. If you do not understand something he is very open to meet and discuss the material. The only negative thing was how much you had to get done between each class. A lot of times you were required to watch documentaries or movies that took a lot of your time. Overall, great class.

Maybe this was an off semester for Professor Selway. On the other hand, I have never had a more difficult to reach professor in my entire life. No communication with students, no organization. Also, all of his papers are focused on doing his research for him. Final was a 15+ pg paper to supplement research he is trying to publish. I'd stay away.

I just got done with Selway's 351 class. Every lecture was a pre-recorded one accessed through Box, and honestly, BYU should take notice for advanced-level courses. Selway just may have become the revolutionizer for these courses through online. You definitely should be prepared for lots of prep work for every class, but overall a great professor!

Dr. Selway was a really great professor. He clearly knows his subject and had us read really useful, timely articles. He is teaching the cutting edge information on comparative politics. Take this class if you have the chance. His expectations were always very clear and he makes class fun and interesting!
Great professor that knows his stuff.

I think Selway is one of the better professors I've had a BYU. He teaches you how to think, not what to think. I've fallen in love with Comparative Politics thanks to him. Try to participate, and you'll get more out of it.

This class was awesome, and Professor Selway is a fantastic teacher. Interesting lectures, meaningful assignments, fair grading. It's not an easy class, but not too difficult either. Lots of reading, but he assigns good articles.
Excellent course. You will learn a lot and work very hard. He curves high.

Personally I really enjoyed Prof. Selway. There's no paper, just some labs that are very interesting to do and help prepare you for the exams. Exams are tough to prepare for but are curved. The book is really interesting, and lectures usually are too, although maybe you have to like politics and international events to feel that way.

I was somewhat pleased with the class until time for finals. For the review sessions we were prepared for 2 essays. The only thing we were told by the TA that was on the test was specifically essays. It turned out, we had one essay plus multiple choice responses, etc, we were not prepared for. I guess the teacher didn't communicate it well to TAs.

Lectures were alright put me to sleep often, quizzes are on obscure current events and difficult, labs graded harshly, 2 midterms and a final- all written. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS from him if you can avoid it!

Very disorganized and vague about assignments and questions on test. One lab per week which are graded very harshly for specific things. The professor is a nice guy and tries to be helpful if you go talk to him but I often left not really feeling like I really got helped. I would HIGHLY recommend another teacher!!!

Professor Selway was pretty bad. His class was very disorganized.  The lectures were based mostly on what the kids in the class wanted to talk about.  He puts almost everything on the TA and I had an AWFUL TA.  The tests were extremely hard and the TA, once again, got to grade them.  I would suggest not taking this class from this professor.

Prof. Selway is a great guy. Had good lectures but was very disorganized, wasn't clear on what he wanted on the labs and his TA graded SO HARD. It was an intro class and he graded us like PHD's. The final was the hardest test I have ever taken and I took econ 110. 80 something short answer and a very vague essay all in 3 hours. Dont take his class

Really fun teacher and makes you interested in what you are learning. However, the grading system is pretty tough, and the clarity of what he wants on the labs is pretty foggy until you really get a hang of it (at which point your grade has already suffered). Be prepared to work hard. I enjoyed it though.

Professor Selway is a great professor and teaches well. The daily quizzes are easy to get good grades on. Make sure you're reading the newspaper and doing the readings. The TA was a jerk though and graded like we were master students. The labs are a lot of work and there is one every week. Class is curved, that's always good.

Professor Selway is awesome! There is a lot of group discussion in class, he is very helpful and willing to work with you. That being said, there is a lot of work! Weekly labs, must attend 5 lectures outside of class, 2 exams and daily quizzes.

Selway is brilliant. 350 is a challenge to do well in. A lot of reading, but he teaches you how to read by not reading every word. Very interested in the success of all his students. Very helpful when visited in his office, especially with papers. His classes are engaging. If you want a class that will not require you to think, don't take it.

I took LING 210 (not an option here) and loved it! Pro. Stanley is very passionate, and he makes difficult concepts incredibly interesting and fun to learn. I loved his class, however there is a TON of material to cover, and while the tests are open note, you will use every minute given for them. Homework can be difficult, but it is necessary.
Seriously awesome!

Dr. Stanley is AMAZING. If I could take every class from him, I would. I took his Applied Phonetics class and the homework was application-based which helped me understand things a lot better. The final was a 10-page paper and presentation, but totally manageable if you start thinking about it early.

Four synthesis papers where we applied what we learned. Short, applicable weekly homeworks (look at them early in the week). The final project was so much fun, but definitely should have started sooner to have more time to write 10 pages. Lectures were engaging, and I never opened the textbook. I'm a repeat student, highly recommend Dr. Stanley!

Cares about his students! Respectful and approachable! No busy-work! All assignments are practical applications of course content. Textbook readings are helpful... but not required. Although attendance is not required, you don't want to miss a single lecture. They are incredible!!
I have taken multiple classes with Professor Stanely and he is fantastic. He genuinely tries to make class interesting and accessible. Thank you, Professor Stanely.

I have taken 2 classes from Professor Stanley and he is incredible. He's a new teacher (I was in his class his first 2 semesters teaching!) but he is so passionate about linguistics that it's contagious. He's respectful and flexible with his students and really did make things I didn't really care too much about way more interesting and fun.

I wasn't excited to take this class at all, but Dr. Stanley made it amazing. He is so passionate about what he teaches, and it shows in the quality of his lectures. He is extremely accommodating and organized the class really efficiently.

Professor Stanley is a great professor, and you should take 240 from him. He knows what he's talking about because he's had first-hand experience with the tools we discussed. The only thing I didn't like was that he posted most assignments on LS right before they were due which made it hard to plan out my homework for the week ahead of time.

I love Professor Stanley! He is so chill - he's totally fine with late work, and he's always willing to help with assignments. He made it easy to do well and learn a lot about various Linguistic programs/tools. There are no exams, although there are a few open book reading quizzes and some homework assignments. There is a semester-long project.

Great professor and guy. The class was pretty difficult, but that's the nature of tax law. TAs were super helpful. Make sure to utilize them if you need it. This class stretched me, but my research skills are so much better than before. I'm actually excited to use what I learned from this class in the future.

I really enjoyed this class and though Professor Barrick did a great job. He has a lot of experience in tax and I appreciated that he was able to make the class more relateable with those experience. Super good guy, and always willing to help.

Professor Barrick is one of, if not THE worst teacher I've had at BYU. He rarely came prepared for class. He literally yelled at us for doing 0.4% below last year's average on the second exam. He often uses examples that make the tax law more confusing. The only reason I did well in this class is because of my group members and the textbook.
He understands tax really well. Get ready to study a lot out of tax. Hard but doable.

I really hate taxes. I get panic attacks. I wasn't very excited to take the class, but Barrick was beyond helpful, kind, and genuinely interested in his students. He is the trifecta of professors: good researcher, great teacher, and kind human. If one of his students needed a kidney, he would get tested. Prof. Barrick also makes great BBQ.
He livened up income taxes and kept the students attention. I would recommend him as a teacher. He has some good personal experience to add to the class and the learning.

You won't regret your decision to take his class. He's fun, entertaining, and keeps the class going. He's great at explaining difficult concepts too. He's a great guy! One of my favorite professors so far.

Prof Barrick is the man!!! His lectures are VERY entertaining, and he explains difficult concepts well.  You will be very glad you took his class. He has a sincere interest in his students, is very funny, and is a real chili pepper!
Barrick's awesome.  He's tons of fun, and his lectures make good sense.  Take his class!

He seems like a nice guy and cares about the material, but the grading was way harsher than he ever made it sound at the beginning. It felt like expectations weren't fully communicated, so a lot of assignments came back with tougher scores than most people were prepared for.

Professor Bingham is a really nice guy and I think has good intentions. He's not very merciful and his class to him is the most important thing in the world. I was disappointed by the way the class was graded and handled. Doesn't care about other work responsibilities, classes life events etc. you miss a class or assignment, youll pay for it.

(MSB 413) Honestly, hate that I'm on here but felt I needed to leave a review. I took this class in the fall and was really looking forward to it. It ended up being the most frustrating class of the semester. I would go into detail but there is a word limit unfortunately. Long story short, he is not humble and it is his way or the highway.

John Bingham is a legend. He loves what he teaches. He loves who he teaches. You can really tell that he is a sincere human who is just trying to do his best. If John isn't in the celestial kingdom when it's my time to pass on then none of us have any chance. 10/10. Will take another class of his if he is teaching it
Great professor!
Professor Bingham is amazing! He did a great job involving students in the learning process. Really cares about each individual.

Bro. Bingham lives what he teaches; he believes the principles of people mngmt. He is very fair & classes are exciting, with intense discussions & activities. But, class is required, his tests were ambiguous and fairly subjective, there are 2 huge projects (1 ind.+1grp.), &the readings were excessive and a large part of the grade, but interesting.
John is amazing!

Professor Bingham is great. He cares a lot about being a good teacher and it shows in his enthusiasm. Textbook is required - there are reading quizzes for every chapter.  Tests are mixed multiple choice and essay - fairly difficult but manageable. Several cases and a large consulting project round out a fairly heavy workload.

He's a decent teacher, but a great guy.  The class was pretty interesting - heavy on class discussion, which meant that it was really up to the students to make each day engaging.  Grading was kind of all over the place, but in the MBA program, grades are a lot less important.

Very nice and honest guy, you are lucky if you have him. "I'll be your friend" is his motto and is very sincere. 'I want to be popular among students' kind of professor and he does his job well. :) Teaches material well.

Professor John is by far the best professor I have taken at BYU! His lectures are genuinely hilarious but still teach you a lot. He really cares about making every part of the class valuable and most importantly never wastes students' time!!! The assignments are also actually fun and you can get ahead in the class if you want.
Kevin John is great and so passionate about what he is teaching! The tests are open note and are super easy!
Kevin John is the best professor I have ever had. So interesting and fun. He's awesome

DEFINITELY TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! I wish I could give him more stars; I couldn't recommend him more! You won't regret it. He's the best! (I actually took him for Univ, but I couldn't put that... anyways, he is so great and helped me out tons!!)

Phenomenal professor. I took his ind. study course and it was perfect for me. Each lesson was an entertaining + engaging video lecture (that you can watch on 2x speed), a short quiz (with a retake option), and then a reflection (easy). He also lets you use a notecard for the exams, so it's a fun, easy class where you learn a lot.
Professor John is THE MAN in any class that you take.

Dr. Kevin John is the best professor I've had. He's so empathetic and inclusive to different belief systems which is so refreshing. He truly cares about our mental health and made it a positive, meaningful, and relevant class. One time he could tell we were burnt out, so he told us to use the zoom call time to do something nice for someone. So kind

Such an amazing person. If you want a teacher who really loves his job and cares about his students, this is the professor you want. I also took Comms 411 from him, and it was such a good online class. He teaches things you actually want to know and is very understanding about grading. Prioritizes real understanding and real discussions.
Best professor I've had through BYU.

#1 favorite professor at BYU. Kevin is a passionate, personable, enthusiastic friend who breaks the mold with his teaching style. He is the type of professor who prioritizes you having a meaningful learning experience over meaningless busy work. I have taken 3 different courses from him. He is a Comms professor who is actually good at communicating

Media Effects is the best class I've ever taken at BYU. Period. Kevin does a very good job of teaching the concepts in a way that everyone understands them. Word of advice, the final project/paper is a big one so try to start it as soon as possible. Every Comms student should take this course, as it is very helpful and useful for all the tracks!

Somehow Media Effects was the easiest class I've taken at BYU and perhaps the one where I learned the most. I took it online and still loved the lectures and learned so many applicable things. Dr John is so funny, passionate and personable. I think every comms student should take this class!

I wish I could have Dr. John for all of my COMMS classes! His lectures and discussions are about topics that are interesting and he's respectful of every opinion. He is very real and isn't afraid to discuss "touchy" subjects. He's great at making every student feel listened to and is great at explaining hard topics. One of my fav professors at BYU!

Kevin's lectures are engaging and thought provoking. He cares about his students and invites each to share their perspectives. Homework was just as interesting and engaging. I feel this helped the concepts we learned to really become part of our understanding. This class was simply so amazing and mind-expanding. Take this class!

Dr. John is awesome and I highly recommend taking any classes from him! The class was online and you can go at your own pace, although I would do a module a week. The lectures are great and I learned a lot from them. We covered a lot of different topics and also had (an optional) 30 minutes a week to join a Zoom discussion and talk about the class!

Dr. John is the best in every aspect; as a class professor, an advisor, & a person. He cares deeply about his students, and truly wants the best for them. His teaching methods are super engaging and really fun. As an advisor he goes above & beyond-helping you immensely & wanting you to succeed. Truly an amazing person!

Really fun and easy going professor. I thought the content was interesting but, even if you didn't, it was a very easy class and a really good way to get a COMMS elective. Only one midterm and a final. Only one project that is graded very lightly. Highly recommend.

I've taken a few classes from Kevin at BYU and I can honestly say he is the best professor I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and wants to see us succeed. He understands how stressful college can be and focuses on helping us prepare for the future. I would highly recommend taking a class from him!

Kevin is an INCREDIBLE professor. He knows what he's talking about, but he's great at being able to simplify and explain the material. He made the class so accessible, so you never have to worry that you might be sick one day and suddenly be 3 chapters behind. Kevin also made his office into a "safe space" for his students. 10/10!

Dr. John is a lively lecturer that has a genuine interest in his students. His online courses are very well organized, and he provides clear study guides for exams (midterm + final.) Includes a final project, but students are granted a lot of autonomy regarding the execution. Honestly, why would you take this class from anyone else?

Kevin is one of my favorite professors, I've taken several classes from him. His classes aren't hard, he trusts you to put in the effort on your end to learn the material and doesn't plague you with tests and meaningless busy work. Everyone respects him because you can tell he is an expert in his field and he genuinely wants his students to succeed
I've taken Dr. John every possible chance. Best professor ever. His classes are legitimately what a college learning environment should be like.

Kevin Johns is an awesome instructor! I enjoyed his COMMS 411 Media Effects Class. I took it through BYU Independent Study. He is enthusiastic about what he teaches and makes the lectures fun! He makes himself available for questions or concerns. It's an Independent Study course, so that's saying something! Take this course! You will be glad!
Best professor I've had. He knows his stuff, makes it easy to succeed, and has a great sense of humor. Lectures were never boring.

Super funny guy with really interesting lectures. Honestly, just show up and pay attention and you'll get an A, no problem. He genuinely wants his students to have a good time and understand why the class matters.
I am Groot. (Translation- Good guy, good with kids)

I actually took COMMS 417 in the Spring which is Advertising Research Methods, but that wasn't an option listed in the course code thing. Kevin John is seriously such a cool guy. He won't push you if it isn't something you aren't interested in, but is more than happy to elaborate and teach you more in depth if you are interested. Take his class!

Cutting edge and brilliant! One of the best professors I know. Dr. John genuinely cares about every student and has an open door policy. He has an incredible and lovable energy! He gives a lot of autonomy to the students (so the class is really what you make of it), while providing tons of expertise, mentorship, and insight to the topic. Take him!!

Such an easy class. I put off most of it until the final weeks and I passed with an A. His lectures are interesting and relevant. There is a pretty big research paper/project at the end, but he says himself he doesn't want it written academically. Take this class!

Kevin, or Dr. John if you prefer to be super formal, is the best professor I've ever had. I've had a lot of professors in BYU's communications program and all of them are better than any other professor I've ever had. Kevin even tops them. He's the best of the best. I've taken two classes from him and loved both and learned a lot in both.
BEST PROFESSOR AT BYU BY FAR! I wish Kevin John could teach every single class I have at BYU!

He was a fantastic teacher, and I met with him during his office hours multiple times during the semester. As others have said, no midterm or final, but he made the quizzes harder to make up for that, so make sure you study! Other than that, he is the first professor I felt was a kind of mentor for me.

Professor John is hilarious and really relates to students. I wished that his class had been harder and a little more in depth some times. I took a class from him in the evening, so he often skipped over things to move faster. Overall, he was a funny teacher and the class was an easy A.

This class changed my perspective on communications. I didn't know what to expect going in, but Kevin challenged us to figure out what we were passionate about, and to work toward that. The class ended with a final project, which was a chance for me to deeply explore the things in the class that were interesting. I loved this class!

It's pretty much an easy A, but that's because he wants you to learn on your own. He hates busy work or making us do projects that aren't useful, so I really love that. Quizzes are easy and there were no midterms or final-just a final project. If you're just exploring communications without being serious, he's the guy to take it from.

Absolute legend! Includes memes in his powerpoints, pulls up random cat videos if he gets bored, and presents the material in a fun way. Would take every class from him if I could. Show up to class to take the quizzes, no midterm or final, and a final project that is on whatever you want it to be. Literally

Dr. John is awesome! he really cares about whether or not students are learning from his class. No textbook, midterm, or final. You have a quiz every week instead so make sure to show up. Awesome class, awesome professor.

One of my favorite professors at BYU. He's young and knows what it's like to be a student and thus acts accordingly. Class was super easy, but I learned a ton. Lots of power point slides, but he was a great lecturer, so I was fine with it. He even told us not to bother buying the book

He was the best! Literal quiz question: "Draw a picture of a dinosaur." If you skim readings you will do fine on the quizzes. Lots of powerpoints but loaded with pictures of cats. (he loves them) He's a student himself so he's super chill, "Lowest presentation score was 46......out of 50." He's funny, take 411 from him.
He is the MAN. Seriously an awesome class. He makes the theories and effects fun and interesting. Quizzes are fine, just do the reading.

Great guy, makes the material easy to understand. This section is way easier than others, but keep in mind you won't get the same intro to secondary research (Mintel, etc.) that you would get if you were to take it from Callister. He also helps out a TON with the final project, which is great, but also kind of inhibits you learning skills yourself.

I took 317 and 411 from him this semester and he has been the most down to earth professor I've had at BYU. He's always willing to help and makes the class as easy as he can. He is concerned about you learning the material and grades easy. Take him if you can.

Loved Dr. Kevin John, he is a hero, however, not yet a Doctor. But he is close. But you should take his class. Numbers make my head fuzzy like a storm of boredom. But Kevin was an expert at making it interesting.
