Professor John made what would have been a boring class into a subject that was genuinely exciting. He was hilarious, and was willing to help us in and outside of class. If you have the chance to take a class with "Dr. John," DO IT!
This class was pretty fun and relatively easy, depending on how good your Spanish is. He's very helpful and the class isn't hard as long as you participate!

Professor Chaston really cares about helping you understand and is very available if you need help. You get a grade each class for being there and participating, so try not to miss class. His tests are very fair and not too difficult and he gives a study guide which is a really good example for how the test will look. He is very funny and caring.

Much of the class is focused on literature and culture which was ok but I felt like I wasn't improving my Spanish a whole ton. The tests and assignments are straightforward though and it's a manageable class and the small class size is fun. It's needed to continue in Spanish program and professor Chaston is a good choice for the course!

I don't know that I've ever had a professor care so much about student success. Great teacher, he literally wrote the textbook. You'll learn a lot and improve your Spanish if you put the work in. Turn things in on time and it's pretty easy to get a good grade. Class format was very straightforward.

HE WROTE THE TEXTBOOK. He knows his stuff for sure and will help you to know it as well. I took this as a zoom class because that is all we could choose, and he did a great job of it. I can not imagine how great he would have been in-person. He will work with you do no worry! Would make time outside of class to help me a lot.

BEST PROFESSOR AT BYU! I took his class when we switched to online, so I feel cheated because I loved going to class. He is incredible - He cares about the success of each of his students. My Spanish improved a ton. There is a decent amount of work but the class is engaging and fun, so it is worth it. TAKE SPAN 321 from him! Fav class so at BYU!

Professor Chaston is an awesome teacher! I was in his class when we had to go online due to covid, and he did a great job helping us transition. The class is a great place to get to know other students and he brought pizza and donuts on a few occasions. Make sure to do the reading and participate in class and you'll have a great experience!

Professor Chaston has been my favorite professor here at BYU, great spanish teacher, explains very clearly and is an easy grader. Personally, I love the man. He's now one of my character references on my resume. Amazing teacher, even better person!

Prof. Chaston is literally the best teacher that I have ever had. The textbook was online and all of the assignments were organized. He really cares about his students and does what he can to help us succeed. If you are looking for a great SPAN 321 professor TAKE THE CLASS FROM HIM!!!

Dr. Colton is great. Lectures are heavy on derivations (both for 441 and 471). His tests aren't too hard, very comparable to his practice tests. Tests are super conceptual. Homework takes long time but working with TAs helps tons. 10 labs (~1 hour) and 25 homework assignments (~2-3 hours ) across the semester. Super nice guy! Learn Mathematica!

If you go to class, do the readings, and ask questions you will do great. This guy is a great teacher. Anyone that is putting a bad review about him just didn't do the work. The lectures are also really interesting if you like science. Overall he is a great teacher.

Teaches simply and clearly. Does a lot of worked example problems in class which was very helpful. Homework is difficult but possible, and doesn't take too long. Tests are fair and one page of handwritten notes is allowed. He likes participation so he'll call on students randomly unless you opt out. One of the best professors in the department.
A nice guy teaching the most boring class in the history of general education requirements.
Do the reading and attend the lectures to gain any needed clarification. Overall the difficulty of an entry-level course required for graduation.

Dr. Colton is a really good professor. This was the first time he taught this specific class so he relied on the other professors a lot but he was very dedicated to making sure all students understand the material.

I was really impressed with how well Dr. Colton knew the course information, despite this being his first time teaching physical science. Colton is super nice and helpful but a lot of outside study was required. TA review sessions are really good to go to as well.

Pro Colton is too smart to teach this class. He isn't the best at explaining what is going on, but the TAs help a ton. I took this class live remote and there are always in-class assignments. 4 tests (open book, note, and internet). Labs every week. Lots of learning on your own.
Dr. Colton's teaching style is great. About 80% of the lectures were worth going to. Difficult class work-wise and test-wise but if you work together you'll do well.
Dr. Colton does a good job of teaching the seminar classes (191, 291). It's fun since you don't have to do much, and there are a lot of guest speakers. The class is very informative.

Dr. Colton has been one of my favorite professors in physics because he is super accessible outside of class. He has 2 hour office hours in the major study room the day before homework is due, and only 1 assignment per week! Also lectures are hilarious (really connects with students) and mostly practice problems so you get experience

Dr. Colton did a good job directing this course.  Since Physics 230 is just a programming lab all any professor has to do is let the students follow the recipe book and the learning will happen as they do it.  I did like the group projects he helped us with at the end.  My group was able to go from no experience to a working solar system model.
Great class. He does a fantastic job of explaining the material in an understandable way. Very energetic! Here comes 442!
Dr. Colton has a way of explaining concepts that is much more clear than most physics professors. He is very a very, very talented teacher.

I really enjoyed this class from Dr. Colton, and it even convinced me to become a Physics-Astronomy major. He really explains how to use the formulas, and is willing to answer any of your questions in his office hours. If you have any questions on the homework, GO TO THE TA LAB! They are super helpful!

The test averages may have been lower, but he is a brilliant professor and a really good man. I have gone to plenty of his office hours for help in things, and he is always willing to give his input. And don't listen to people who think he's condescending--he has a wry sense of humor, but he is really sincerely interested your learning.

Dr. Colton is a great professor.  He learns all of the students names and tries to really be a help.  He makes great labs to go through that are really clear.  IF you take this class or any other, he is a great one to do it from.

I barely used the textbook, he gives out a packet with most of the equations.... to get by in the class I spent hours in the TA lab on each homework assignment, they were hard!  But if you take the time go through old exams and homeworks before each exam, you should do fine

At first, the class seemed very difficult, but give it some time and you'll understand physics. Dr. Colton makes his lectures interesting and is very good at stopping and asking for questions. He posts his lectures online, which is extremely helpful when reviewing for the exams. Take advantage of all the extra credit opportunities!

I've never taken physics before, so this class was challenging. The homework takes a long time, and the tests are difficult but usually curved. Plan on doing the homework in the TA lab and spending 2-4 hours doing it. Dr. Colton seemed kind of condescending when students asked questions, so don't go to him for help. Lots of extra credit.

Great professor teaching a tough subject. He's makes plenty of help available though, even showing up in the TA lab to help students with homework. You'll need to take it seriously--college level seriously, not high-school level seriously--but it's doable. He's good at explaining the concepts, but has too much content he has to teach to go slow.

Great guy, very hard class. Each week there are two homework assignments due, one for each class period. Lectures make you seem like you know what you're doing, but the homework problems are very challenging (most assignments take about 2 hours to complete roughly 5 problems), and the test questions are downright impossible (avg grade about 68%)

This class isn't even that hard, don't pay attention to all of these whiners.  If you want an A, just put in the work that you would expect for a college level physics class.  A lot of premeds are weeded out, but it isn't due to Dr. Colton's teaching- I thought he was excellent.

Dr. Colton loves physics, but the amount that he expects students to know, especially in a physics class where no prerequisites are required, is ridiculous, The homework took way too long and I spent countless hours in the tutor lab. It is easy to get 100 on. Attendance not required, but does icklicker questions. Midterms most difficult at BYU.

I thought he did a great job of explaining physics. There's only so much you can do to make physics easy, and I thought he gave good mnemonic devices and demos. The class was curved a lot, and there were plenty of opportunities for help. Do your homework in the tutorial lab.

This professor and class is ridiculously hard, and he doesn't even realize how bad it is. I spent hours on each homework assignment and often got them wrong. The test curves were generous, though, which is nice considering their averages are in the 60-70 range.
I disliked the class. He asked iclicker questions before teaching the principles. I had to put a lot of time into this class. His average test scores are 68-74% Take it if you have to.
Great professor! Charming and engaging, makes you excited to come to class every day. You can tell he loves physics and loves teaching. Very generous with test curves, too.

There were a few things that could have been better, but it was good overall. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit, is very quick to respond to emails/concerns, and is a nice guy. Homework is a force to be reckoned with, exams difficult, but he posts previous exams (which are very similar) and annotates them concisely.

He posts past years midterms/final online, if you just review those you'll do fine on the tests.  Plenty of extra credit opportunities, and generous curves on the exams.  An easy A if you put in enough effort to actually understand the homework.  Lectures could be helpful at times, but weren't always necessary (neither is the textbook).

If you already have a strong understanding of physics, you will do fine in Prof. Colton’s class.  If you struggle at all with physics, you will hate this class.  He is very condescending and unhelpful and his TA is the same.  It’s true that he curves most of the exams, but that wouldn't be necessary if he was a better teacher.

If you are already good at physics and have nothing to learn take it from Dr. Colton! he loves students that he doesn't have to teach, he also loves being condescending any time you approach him, so you better know your stuff. He expects you to learn outside of class, yes that means spending at least 3hrs a day in the tutorial lab completing the HW

I loved Physics but learned after the second exam that it just isn't for me. Go to the tutorial lab as often as possible to get help on the hw b/c that's whats on the exams. Actually complete the readings, or at least look over the example problems in the book. The lectures were well thought out, but I struggled applying what I learned to the hw.

Dr. Colton is a really nice guy, but he really doesn't know how to explain difficult concepts to beginners. If you've had a good physics background this will be a great class for you, but if not you will be pretty lost. I only went to class to get in-class points. His explanations were very quickly given and he would often skip over important ideas

He is very good at explaining on a one on one basis. During lecture it was difficult to follow what he meant. But he does give you everything you need to do well. I was never surprised on any of his tests.

If you do the readings before class which goes along with the old textbook lecture makes a lot of sense. He cares about the students. His test questions come from homework assignments. He provides a lot of ways to get help. If you approach him he will not blow you off. It's a hard class but doable. You have to put some effort in to understand.
Great Teacher and humorous at times.

Dr. Colton is not a good teacher. He believes that most of the learning happens outside of class which gives him an excuse to not teach the material in class. The newer textbooks on his book list don't go along with his homework and his office hours are very limited. Do not take Physics 105 from this teacher, you will regret it.

Dr. Colton is the best professor I've ever had. he's really helpful, approachable, and good at explaining hard topics. i definitely recommend him for any prospective student of 123. the class takes time, but you learn A LOT. I'm glad i took section 2 (majors/minors) rather than the lesser section (section 1). It was much more awesome.

The lectures were incomprehensible and the test quite difficult. The T.A was actually much more helpful than the professor. The most frustrating thing of all was that he doesn't realize how difficult his class is. If he says something will take 3 hours, plan on at least 5 or 6. That was a common scenario in our class when I took it.

Dr. Colton is the best physics professor I've had so far.  I was in the major/minor section and loved it!  So hard, but that's what the class is designed for.  Understands all the math behind what he explains and quickly derives equations you use in class just to show they're legit. I would come by his office and he would help me any time.

I was in the majors section and loved it, actually switched my major to physics because of it. Colton is the best professor I've ever had. Explains topics incredibly well and is very interested in helping his students. Learned everyone's names. Homework is due three times a week and is a significant time commitment, but really helps you learn.
I had the majors/minors section. It was unbelievably difficult. He was a good professor though.
Awesome, easy to follow, tests were clear. Clarified a normally difficult subject.

Dr. Colton is by far the best physics professor for Physics 105.  He tells you EXACTLY what will be on the test.  I'd never taken a physics class and got an A.  It takes time, especially the homework, but he's more than fair.  Those students complaining about him are most likely freshmen who don't know what a real college class is like yet.

Avg difficulty for a core science class, great professor. Very straight-up - you only have yourself to blame if you do poorly. Fun class - cool demos, extremely organized. Book was actually helpful. Tests were about half prob's like those in HW and half conceptual (from clicker quizes and warm-ups usually). HW can be tough tho. Highly recommend.
Great teacher that makes this a great class. He gives you everything you need to learn the material and get the great you want.

He is a great teacher. at first HW assignments kick you in the butt, but go to the TA lab. I have not learned so much from a science class before.  LOTS of extra credit opportunities and a curve on tests, etc. You will have to come to class, work hard on hw etc, but you will be proud of what you learned by the end. ALSO, review last year's exams!!!

Prof. Colton is the best! I He is one of those "cool" nerds and is very good at at what he does. The homework is tough, but if you can get it down you will do well on the tests. He tells you what will be on the exams and even gives you last years exam to prepare with. You can get an A if you take advantage of the TA lab and take the pre-tests.
Don't take this class from him. You put hours and hours and hours into getting a good grade and feel blessed with a C. Not worth your time.

Dr. Colton knows how to teach and he's very open to student input.  He makes class fun and brings lots of experiments.  He has a funny sense of humor.  He provides endless ways for his students to get help.  He REALLY wants you to understand Physics.  He's a great professor and I highly recommend him!

I love Professor Colton.  He is very clear in his explanations, and is very helpful.  Yes, the class is really hard.  That's because physics is really hard.  He basically tells you what's going to be on the test.  I'd recommend him to anyone.  One of the best professors i've had at BYU

Dr. Colton is the best professor for this class.He is very knowledgeable and great at breaking things down and explaining tough concepts. Come to class (do clicker quizzes), do the homework, do the reading/reading quizzes, and do the practice tests and you'll do fine.USE THE TA LAB! He offers some extra credit as well and responds to emails quickly
Possibly the worst teacher i have ever taken...take this class from someone else unless you want to spend forever on HW and still get a bad grade. Be ye warned.

Hard class because its physics. Dr Colton is awesome. He does all that he can to help students, while realizing that the average exam score should be in the 70s. TA lab saved my life. HW helped me learn the material. Good teacher.  Definitely recommended

Dr. Colton's class really wasn't too bad considering how much material we covered in one semester. Some of the homework sets took forever in the TA lab to figure out, while some were easy enough to do on your own. Dr. Colton is very sharp and teaches at a fast pace to cover everything.

He is generally a nice guy, but not a very good professor. He loves the material but cannot break it down on a basic level. He skips steps and has a hard time explaining concepts. His exams are ridiculous and his homework takes forever. I spent hours upon hours in the TA lab and its the only reason I passed at all.

Dr. Colton is fantastic and his class was fascinating! I didn't think physics was exactly my thing before this class, but I was amazed at how applicable everything was. Yes, the homework is difficult, but if you get help from the TA's and make sure you really understand the concepts behind the problems, you'll be well-prepared for the tests.

didnt like hime. take it from magelby. his homework is unbelievably hard and his tests are unfair. im not a biased student. i got an A, but it seriously took about 20 hours per week to get that grade. i hate physics now.

Rude, pretentious, condescending, etc. Do NOT take this class from him. Wait until Dr. Gee is teaching! The homework was ridiculously difficult and the tests were absurd. He has a 3 hour time limit on exams, and the averages were very low. He has no mercy. I spent well over 10 hours a week on this class and failed EVERY test.

He bends over backwards to help the class. Two problem review sessions each week. The HW is hard by yourself but easy with the TA lab. Study hard for the tests, they pretty much mimic the notes and homework. I would pick him over all other choices!

Dr. Colton's lectures are well structured and he explains things very well. He tries to help the students if at all possible, but the class is still really hard. The 2 homework assignments per week take FOREVER!! I studied endlessly for every test, but the highest grade I ever got was an 83. If you are smart, take him. If not, best of luck to you

Way too much work. You have two homework assignments per week that are graded on accuracy and no partial grading. The exam average for my class has dropped every exam 79, 73, 69. He has no mercy that his class will take you more time than 10hrs per week. He seems not to care. I wouldn't recommend the class if at all possible.

Go to class do the clicker quizzes, do the prelab quizzes and homework, then do a bunch of practice problems before every test and you'll do fine. The tests are just like the homework. The TA lab helps a lot when there are not a million people there. He is entertaining and allows a lot of mercy with homework and all! great class set up!

Excellent Teacher!  His classes are well structured with a good balance of concepts and applications.  He  responds well to questions, and accepts student input on the class.  The homework problems can be tricky, but he goes over the hardest ones in the reviews, and they prepare you well for the tests.
He explains things well. His lectures are entertaining most days. Only downside is some tricky homework problems, but if you go to the TA lab it's not too bad.

Dr. Colton is one of the most exceptional professors on campus.  He works closely with the students, gives them a bit of a say on how the class is run, and makes sure we have all the tools needed to be a success in the course.  He's straightforward and honest, and as a bonus, way entertaining.  If you're going to take physics, take from Dr. Colton.

He was a great teacher and explained things very clearly. After having other physics classes with other teachers, I recognize just how good he was at explaining and teaching physics. I felt like he was a little tricky on one test just to take down the class average, but that might change when he's not co-teaching with Dr. Hess. Great teacher.

This was his first semester at BYU.  I like him a lot.  He is young and relates to the students well.  He answered questions clearly and explained things well.  His lectures were mostly interesting too.

Decent lecturer, really if you just do the homework and do the practices tests. The practice tests are pretty similar to the final and I got away with doing like 1 or two and some review before each tests, and I got an A on all of my tests. Lectures are alright

Dr. Dallon is a great lecturer. He helps connect concepts to other disciplines, and gives real application of the math that we are learning. He does move rather quickly in the lectures, so if that is a problem for you, I would not take a class from him.

Do not take any class from him. He is old and just needs to retire. Class is more of a time for him to talk about math rather teaching math. Class is way to hard to be 2 credits worth. I was successful in the course but I spent more time on this class than any other.

Every class Professor Dallon would write on a chalkboard a large number of theorems and equations and expect you to memorize them instantly. The class and homework did not prepare me for the tests. He is incredibly brilliant, but the most confusing math teacher I have ever had. Take this class with anyone else.

Professor Dallon is a great teacher, it's just that he would be MUCH better in a 300+ level math class. He loves proofs, that we honestly don't need to know. His lectures go very quickly, so be prepared to write notes quickly. But overall, he did a good job with explaining the material.

Insane tests first midterm covering the easiest material the class average was a 70. I felt as if the tests were unfair and material was placed on them that was not covered in the homework or the practice test.

This is a professor who know the material super well, but does a pretty bad job at explaining/teaching it. He goes thorough lectures so fast that taking notes is almost impossible. The only way to know what your even doing in this class is reading the text book, watching youtube. Have questions? Ask the TA not him, he'll just confuse you.

He absolutely flies through the lecture, focusing mostly on proofs and teaching in a very abstract way that makes it pretty much impossible to learn the material if you aren't already familiar with it. He will frequently ask the class questions and be met with silence because no one has any idea what is going on.

He teaches with examples but the material moves so quickly that it is hard to keep up, very challenging, and while I did not believe it in the moment, this class prepared me for my higher-level math classes! Get ready to work and study, the tests are fair, but studying is needed because closed book. The final is very hard so there is a big curve

Really smart person, but he talks way to fast to take notes on what he says. Best to email him after and ask for copies of his slides. He is not very understanding of students who struggle, and not willing to talk outside his office hours. He really is just here to collect a paycheck and doesn't care if his students pass or fail.

313 is no joke and he admitted that he usually doesn't teach it, but I felt he did a great job. His lectures were a little fast, but he would ALWAYS stop if someone asked him a question and was very approachable. He did like proofs, but he would expand on how concepts connected to engineering or data analysis, which I found wonderful. Great Prof.

He has good intentions and loves his work. But it is very hard to understand his teaching style. He likes teaching in very abstract ways that are hard to follow for an introductory class to linear algebra. I would recommend another teacher if you are not planning on being a math major.

Dr Dallon is by far the most difficult math professor I've ever had to work with. Tests account for 75% of your grade, and he seems to pride himself in the low marks students receive on these. He rushes through topics, and then sounds irritated when students ask him to go back and explain something. I do appreciate the free textbook though.

Dr. Dallon comes to class to teach and that's it. He has good intentions assigning the reading before class but there is also online HW & HW that needs to be turned in during class every class. This is very hard for students who work and only have a few days a week to work on homework. The tests are weighted to be 70-80% of your overall grade.

He gave lots of examples showing exactly how to do the problems. It was very straightforward, even for a difficult class.  Homework takes a while, but what math class doesn't have long homework. It is great practice for the tests since the tests are all very similar to the homework. I loved this class and it is very do-able.

Great teacher. Very very smart and very very helpful! He knows what he's talking about and is really passionate about it. Sometimes it seems like he's being unclear, but he's actually quite good at explaining things. He's also very patient and flexible with the class. A great guy, great teacher.

Really superb class and a great teacher. Class was mostly theory but homework focused on practical (programming) numerical methods. Dr. Dallon cares about his students. Highly recommend this class to engineers or anyone else who will do scientific computing. Extremely useful subject and class.

He is  a nice guy, but he is hard to understand. He talks quietly so sit near the front or you can't hear what he is saying. I didn't think that he gave enough time on his exams. This was a very hard class.
Good class, fun professor.  A bit quirky, but that's what makes a math professor a math professor!  Didn't do as well as I'd hoped, but that was my fault, not his.  I recommend taking from him.
the worst teacher I have ever had.  I fo not recommend him at all.  Mumbles and goes crazy about math.  The tests are really hard.

He goes way too fast and mumbles.  If you don't get to class right when the bell rings to let the previous class out - good luck finding a seat where you can actually see what he writes on the board.  Good luck taking notes. He knows his stuff, but like many math teachers, has a hard time teaching it.  Not the best. Take Armstrong if possible.
Witty, entertaining, and informative.  Two thumbs up!

Dr. Dallon is a really cool guy.  He comes to class everyday excited to teach math.  He's funny, but not usually on purpose.  The only complaints that I had related to the tests.  His test are wicked hard/long and he likes to give them in class, but not always.  The whole class is graded on a curve, so it has a bit of an American Heritage feel.

Dr. Hedengren is a nice person, but the class felt unorganized. Lectures were very vague, and homework and labs didn't connect to what was taught. Heavy use of starter code and AI made it hard to learn the fundamentals, especially since exams were all by hand. Overall, not an effective teacher.
He taught very well and the material is good. The class is a little disorganized and all of the material is available online and is basically equivalent to taking the class.
Dr. Hedengren does a really good job at creating a class that allows you to learn what you think will be useful. He also keeps his class very recent, and all of the material is available online.
The professor taught one thing, gave homework on another, and tested on another
Dr. Hedengren does a great job applying learning to industry.

Great class and a very helpful professor. Content tends to be more application based than diving into the theory. Lot's of resources were provided in order to be successful in his class. Overall I enjoyed this class and would take it again.

I'm taking "Machine Learning and Dynamic Optimization" with Dr. Hedengren. He is an amazing professor who is kind and compassionate to his students. I really enjoyed taking it with him and learned a lot.
Dr. Hedengren is a brilliant and effective teacher. I appreciated plentiful course materials to supplement learning. I recommend Dr. Hedengren highly.

I really enjoyed this class but it was far from easy. I took it during spring so if you're doing the same I would suggest taking only one other class during this term because there is a lot of information that is thrown at you and you do not have much time to sit back and relax.

I took most of ChE 263 before I dropped out. The Python programming was too much to learn in a seven-week Spring Term course. Dr Hedengren is a good professor, but avoid taking his ChE 263 class during Spring Term unless you have a good background in coding. Online quizzes grade you on how much time you spent learning the material.

For his 263 class it is very easy and you learn a lot, but you have to rely a lot on his outside website and resources. I had to use his tutorial videos a lot, which were fine except that they were kind of long, included him making mistakes, and had a terrible whistling sound constantly. He is a really caring professor and will help you learn.
He is one of the best teachers I ever had!
This course is full of excellent material. The principles of optimization taught here should be required for all engineering majors.

He is such a kind professor. He works very hard to help students understand the material. He knows that programming does not come easily to many students and teaches accordingly. He does a "flipped classroom," so instead of actual lectures, you watch short videos and take a quiz before class, and then he goes over the homework during class.

Dr. Hedengren posts step-by-step videos for everything on youtube, which makes getting help at any time of the day/night extremely easy.  Dynamic optimization is an incredible course and can be applied to literally any field.  Videos for hw solutions are posted, 2 projects, a midterm and final.  Grading not as big of a deal for grad-level courses.

He is super nice and cares a lot. It's awesome to have such a passionate professor. I felt lost a lot because I followed along with the programming but didn't feel like it was explained. Overall this is a pretty good class, but I did struggle. My TA was very helpful with test reviews, so that's the main thing that helped me.

Hedengren is an awesome guy, but the way the class is set up makes it hard to actually learn the material, and it's stuff that is essential for the rest of the program. You are supposed to watch video lectures before class, which honestly aren't that helpful. In class you follow along as he does the hw.

Definitely would recommend this class to anyone because it's such a detailed class in the world of programming. Dr. Hedengren is an amazing professor and did admit that this is a very difficult class but managed it very well.  As long you have a thourough understanding of the homework and perform well on the exams you will get an A no problem.

Dr. Hedengren is really smart, so he can show you how to do a lot of different things, but sometimes, he forgets that programming isn't second nature to everyone and it goes kinda fast. To be fair, I took it in spring term. Overall, it is a really useful class that expands what you can do with engineering and  it is really good for internships.

Professor Hedengren was an awesome professor! He adjusted the class so we could take our quizzes before class and have as many attempts as we want. He was always willing to help out with homework; he even posted solution videos for some of the homework assignments that were fairly challenging. There are 2 group projects, a midterm and the final.

My only regret with Dr. Hedengren is not trying to work with him first semester at BYU. He has great industry knowledge and connections that turn rote learning into a fascinating, profitable environment. Work with him for a year, even undergrads, and I'd be surprised if you didn't get published.

He is always there for you and tries hard to explain the materials several times patiently when you don't understand them. His online videos and hands on examples make it really easy to follow the course. He respects the people in the class and is very helpful.

Dr. Hedengren really cares about his students.  He is really enthusiastic about learning, and will provide extra opportunities whenever he can.  His online videos are really helpful for mastering tricky material.  He's always willing to help out if you ask him, and will spend hours with students working on their projects with them.  Great Prof!

Dr. Hedengren is a fantastic professor. This was his first time teaching CHEM 273 but he did a great job. There is difficult homework in this class.  He would go through lectures in class which were covered difficult material. Not all of it could be taught in class and would put videos on Youtube explaining the more difficult materials in detail.

His expectations are never quite clear. While he is an alright teacher, he doesn't care about UO lab. I believe he feels like he is babysitting us. Then at the very end, he failed about half the class on the final assignment to bring the class GPA down so it would match other sections--made us feel really good about ourselves
Dr Hedengren is a great professor. He is very helpful to students.He makes sure that students learn the material and understand it. So far, the best professor in the department.
Good professor despite difficult class and subject material. Some subjects lacked clarity.
I enjoyed the class.  The last half of the class was much more interesting to me than the first half.  Dr. Hedengren was a great teach.  Great tests.  Great Homework.  Great Class time.

Great professor! Awesome class. Great use of different media for homework and gives decent load for out of class work. Don't let his laid back manner fool you though- he's an All American cross country runner.
I like this course and it was great Dr. Hedengren cared that we learned not just went through the material.
Awesome professor!
Dr Hedengren is always ready to help students in/out of the class. One of the best professors in chemical engineering department.
I didn't find the TA's too helpful. I was lost in class and didn't find lectures too helpful either

Great professor. He really cares about making sure we learn things that are applicable to how process control is used in industry. I always went to ask him questions at his office and he was really nice and helpful. Homework wasn't too heavy either.
Superb
He is a great person but a very bad teacher. Majority of the time he has the students teach instead of helping us to understand. I won't take his class ever again!
I started out hating his class but learned to love it. A really great professor and I learned a ton from him and his lectures. Especially after the importance of his course clicked for me.

This class is all about learning tools and concepts employed in supply chain. THESE TOOLS ARE VERY USEFUL in internships and full-time positions. Pay close attention to Lean principles and tools and try to learn the function and capabilities of all the other tools.

A couple group projects, mainly lecture and tool application. Lots of memorization and application. Class review and then test review after to get points back. Always available to help. Gives clear feedback.

He is one of the most caring people I have ever met. Probably the most spiritually enlarging too, and he isn't even a religion professor. People say he has the hardest exams in the junior core, but honestly wasn't too bad at all. He gives a great study guide, so if you listen in class and prepare using the study guide, you'll be fine!

I don't know how Dr. Gardner doesn't have perfect ratings on here. His class is so useful, and his passion for quality is contagious. His tests aren't that hard—he goes through every single question beforehand in class. They were actually the only exams I've ever taken that seemed like he wanted you to succeed. His testimony is incredible!

Dr Gardner is simply everything you need in a professor. Yes, he has a hard test or 2, but he goes to great lengths to help you learn the principles. Obliviously, there is a lot of work, as he teaches in the Junior Core. He really, really cares!
He's awesome, one of the best professors I have ever had.
The realest professor there ever was. 10/10 would take again—the quality management GOAT.

Professor Gardner is one of the most caring and kind professors that I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and wants all of them to succeed. He teaches in a way to help his students understand the content. The homework and readings are all applicable to the class and he doesn't assign extra busy work. Lots of work is done in groups.

He has 2 exam, both are 18% of total grade. No final exam, but final project. His exam are the most difficult, but are the only ones in the Junior Core with nothing random or new on it to mess you up. I did the best on his because of this. He give 1% of total grade in easy extra credit assignments. Very doable to get an A, but still challenging.

He grew on me. For me, his tests were the toughest of the core. He was almost always available to visit after class. Great lectures, good man, very spiritual. If you're an A student you will hate him, because he never grades over a 95 haha. Stinks to be you.

A new GSCM group will get to experience the TOUGHEST GRADER ever. Don't be fooled with his kindness, he is a good guy but makes the material really complicated. Exams are hard, wordy, and long. He says that he does not want to trick you on the exams but he actually does that. Take the time to study for his exams.
Tough exams! HE is TOUGH GRADER and he makes the material of the class really complicated.

Engaging classes. However, he makes the material very complicated for no reason with assignments that are very specific. TAs are nazis when it comes down to grading, there is always something missing. Exams are REALLY HARD. Finishing up the study guides that he provides for exams takes over a week. Get ready to spend a long time outside of class.

Frustrating because it's nearly impossible to get 100% on even regular assignments. Tests are very challenging but also very fair. Super caring and passionate dude. Wouldn't care to take this class again just because of the content, but he's a solid professor and it's doable

"Fair but difficult." You cannot find a more genuine, caring, thoughtful, and committed professor than John Gardner. He will set you up for success through and through. Grading is tough. Fun activities. Tons of growth and learning. If you walk away from his class not liking him or the course, you need to do some serious self-reflection.

Learning experience is burdened by the unnecessary specificity of assignments and projects. You'll learn all kinds of stuff you will never use. Arbitrary grading scale, full credit is rarely given for any assignment, including homework. Participation and attendance are forced through assignments rather than voluntary desire.

Don't buy the textbook, just borrow one from the library. The book readings are required but don't add any value. Grading criteria is really ambiguous and subjective. Disables class statistics so you have no idea where you stand in relation to the class. The majority of your grade is group projects that don't seem to have a point.

Dr. Gardner is very kind and caring to all. I wouldn't say his class was fun, or even very enjoyable. While ambiguous and challenging, the course did teach me several useful quality mgmt tools. He is a tough grader, for real. Probably one of the toughest I have had, besides an Econ professor. He definitely knows his stuff and loves his students.

Professor Gardner may seem very caring, but he's a toughest grader I've ever seen. He would share spiritual stories in class, which usually went longer than needed - I thought those stories were annoying, to be honest... He's nice but he's so full with the spirit that it's hard to approach him.

Great teacher. cares about the students on a personal level. He is a tough but fair grader. Don't procrastinate on his projects. fun in-class activities. I respect this guy as a professor, a man, and a mentor.

I love Brother Gardner! His class was awesome, and he is an amazing person. Just remember the junior core is tough. If you are in the GSCM junior core, and you only want "A's" you picked the wrong major. You will learn a lot, and you will learn principles that will change your life if you put in the effort. Do your best and kiss your 4.0 goodbye.

My main complaint, and why I ranked the level of difficulty so highly, is that no clear grading criteria are ever provided. He provided instructions on what needed to be included in assignments but not specifications on what criteria they would be graded on. When you take the class try asking him for more clear information on grading criteria.

Lots of assignments & LOTS of group projects, but that's the GSCM core in general.  Really cares about his students (wants you to understand). Not the most concise. Ambiguity is a theme of the class. Normal grading scale. Exam study guides are pretty good. He really tries his best. Hard to get an 'A'.

Gardner is incredibly nice and when you go to his office makes it top priority to help you understand and do well. His downfall is that he does not teach the subject matter well. When I understood, I did well but his classes never helped me understand. It was all on my own. Important class, nice teacher, he just needs to teach it better.

Gardner is a great professor. He's really fun and usually has cool activities for the course. The material was pretty easy, and the cases and projects we did were awesome and super applicable. Loved the class, and recommend him as a professor!

This class is one of the most useful, & the project is the hardest in the whole Management Core. Prof. G knows his stuff, and if you always go to class prepared and go to the test reviews you'll do fine. Warning - he's not very good at explaining if you don't understand the first time, and the textbook is complex, so plan to put the time in.

Gardner was a great professor.  I wasn't a huge fan of the material, but once he explained things they made a lot of sense to me.  Some of the students complained about various aspects of the class, but as long as you study and try to understand the material you will do fine.

Dr Price is one of the best professors at BYU. His class material is hard by nature of the subject. But he genuinely cares about the students and does his best to help them succeed. I took both CHEM 381M (The major version of CHEM 482) and CHEM 391 from him. In both he met the needs of the class. Go to his office hours!

Dr. Price was the kindest professor I ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and offers to write letters of recommendation (which got me into multiple medical schools). His homework/teaching style prepared me extremely well for the MCAT. Even now in med school, his class gave me a strong foundation. You'll need to go to his office hours

Hard class but a very caring professor. His recorded lectures are the most helpful in preparing for the test, be sure to understand everything taught in the lectures and assigned readings, and be more than familiar with the fundamentals. I recommend taking his class a semester right before the MCAT, which saved me a bunch of time reviewing.

Dr. Price has set his class up in a way that pushes students and helps them in future endeavors. This class prepared me for the MCAT without even trying to, not just because of the material, but because of the way that Dr. Price taught me to think. The class is hard, and you have to put in significant effort, but Dr. Price is very helpful and kind.

Dr. Price has been one of my favorite professors here at BYU. The class itself is quite difficult, but I would recommend to take it from him; he cares a TON about his students and provides everything you need to succeed. He is always willing to meet during office hours, and had amazing TA's! If you have to take it, take it from Dr. Price!!

Dr. Price is one of the best chemistry professors at BYU. He cares about his students and is willing to work with them. He is accesible through office hours and he makes you feel welcome. His tests are difficult but prepare you well for future courses and tests like the MCAT. He allows you to receive points back after tests which is super helpful.

Dr. Price genuinely cares about his students, and will 100% help you if you are struggling. Very tough class, but prepares you VERY well for health careers- Dr. Price helps you learn skills/info that you will actually use, and he cares a lot! The class is hard because it makes you think beyond just memorizing, but you learn a ton in the process.

I loved Prof Price's lectures. He focuses on teaching the principles behind each of the processes we learned in class. This was especially helpful for studying and taking the MCAT. He is super understanding and willing to work with you outside of class if you are struggling to understand. One of my favorite professors!

Biochem is hard, and there is nothing anyone can do about that. Dr. Price is a great professor, he is extremely caring and he goes to great lengths to make sure he is available for his students when questions. Tests are hard, but he gives lots of points back holds reviews, and curves each test and the class. Most helpful class for MCAT prep at BYU.

Dr. Price made learning CHEM481 material enjoyable. Yes, like all professors, he may go on little tangents here and there, but it contributes so much to his lectures - allowing him to share his passion for the subject. I wish I took more advantage of all the help Price offers (office hours, TA hours). Heavily taught concepts were all over the MCAT.

My experience with Biochem and Dr. Price was nothing but positive. It has been my favorite class to this point in my collegiate career. I have seen nothing but caring and the highest levels of professionalism from Dr. Price, and I would be wary of any comments that say otherwise. His office hours are great and helped me a lot in this class.

Dr. Price is amazing! The class is hard, especially the homework, but office hours are so helpful and Dr. Price is willing to work with you until you understand the concept! I really appreciated that the homework was current research and that I learned how to better interpret it since anyone going into a career in medicine should have those skills!

The material taught in biochem was extremely helpful in connecting topics in my other classes, along with my understanding of biochem within nephrology. I currently work in dialysis, and the topics discussed in Price's class were fundamental in my understanding of the practice. If you need assistance, Price will happily work with you.

Dr. Price is a great professor that cares about educating his students. If you're looking for an easy A this is not the class for you. This class focuses on teaching principles, not memorization.This was one of the most helpful classes I took in preparing to take the MCAT. Be proactive and use the resources and you'll do well in the class.

CHEM 481 was the most difficult class I've taken while at BYU while also my favorite. Dr. Price's homework and lectures are geared around understanding concepts, rather than memorization. You will have to work with the TAs and go to Dr. Price's office hours. If you are a pre-med student, this class will prepare you for the MCAT extremely well.

This class did more to prepare me for the MCAT than any other class by far. Dr. Price is a fantastic teacher that really pushes you to understand the material and it really makes a difference. His class is definitely hard but if you're willing to learn the right way and take advantage of TAs and in-class extra credit an A is definitely attainable.

Dr. Price is a caring, honest, and fair professor who is always willing to answer his students' questions. The subject is challenging and requires dedication but is definitely doable if you go to TA office hours and gain a solid understanding of the homework questions. This class was helpful in my preparation for dental school.

CHEM481 is hard no matter who you take it from. The comment about Dr. Price lacking integrity is completely untrue. I found him to be one the most caring professors I've had. As no one is perfect (which he recognizes and tries to make up by dropping questions and curving) his class has prepared me the best for my career. Use TAs for the HWs.

As for biochem, having Professor Price made this a great experience. I will not lie, the class was difficult, but I think biochem is always difficult no matter the professor. I learned so much in this class, and if you are in for the college experience to learn and not just for a grade, Dr. Price is a good choice.

Dr. Price is a fantastic lecturer and a fair professor. His tests are hard because he wants you to understand the information in a very conceptual way, no plug and chug. His homeworks are also pretty comprehensive BUT the TA hours and his own office hours are so helpful. I would take this class or another from him again in a heart beat.

FANTASTIC LECTURES. 1 hw every 2 weeks but they are BIG. go to TAs for sure.
Tests were difficult because lots of options A-J and lots of check all that apply questions. but provides practice exams that were very helpful. 
willing to help outside of class and actually finds the root problem of what you don't understand to help.

Really encourages internalization of the principles and critical thinking, rather than mere regurgitation for tests. Cares a lot about students and genuinely wants them to succeed. Several brutal homeworks, go to office hours to make them easier.

Dr. Price really cares about his students, but his teaching skills struggle. We had long biweekly papers that were impossible to do on your own. TAs were heavily relied upon for every assignment. Tests were very difficult and at times weirdly worded. Dr. Price is extremely smart and willing to help, a genuinely nice guy. Good curve at the end.

Price's homework are impossible alone, given with zero context. Impossible to even attempt without TA help. Hes impossible to follow while teaching and his test questions are exactly the same. Even if you know all your concepts well, you'll probably miss a lot of heavily weighted questions on the test just because you have no clue what he's asking.

A solid choice to deeply understand the material and think critically. Struggles to explain some concepts; use Ninja Nerd and a study group. 7 tough hmwks, but they promote true learning and prepare you for exams. (plus plenty of TA and professor office hours for aid) This class is the reward for 2 years of gen chem and 2 years of ochem. I loved it

Dr. Price loves biochem and cares about his students, however, his homework assignments are IMPOSSIBLE and given with 0 context. The first exam in the class, the average was 60% and he didn't take that as possibly being because of poor test writing/teaching. Nice guy but not great at writing problems- he words things really confusingly. So hard.

It's clear Dr. Price wants success for his students and wants you to LEARN biochemistry/have solid takeaways. Lots of MCAT references. HWs are a pain, but very reflective of his exams and forces critical thinking. 2 things saved my grade: 1)forming a solid study group for HW, 2)Ninja Nerd lectures on YT (teach general topics much better than Price)

Dr. Price is always willing to help. This class is simply tough. There is a ton of material to learn, but he sets you up for success. You will learn to think critically and apply what you have learned as opposed to rote memorization. Do the readings, attend class, and attend an office hour or two each week with Dr. Price, and you will do just fine.
Dr. Price was a great lab instructor. He really is respectful of students.

Dr. Price has evidently not learned from the past evaluations, his class continues to be disjointed and vague. He offers learning objectives, but he hardly ever makes it clear which point applies to what topic. I came to learn, and I did learn the amino acids. Everything else was just random facts. Also, ridiculous typos. Every question on tests.

He's new to teaching so the lack of practice does show at times. He often will get sidelined on tangents that aren't required for the test but doesn't let the class know that it was a tangent while sometimes putting little emphasis on the actual important material. Homework is long and tedious but resembles the tests fairly well.

I loved taking this class from Dr. Price.  It's a lot of work (it's also a 400-level chem class), but didn't always feel that way.  His passion for the subject is evident, and I found myself choosing to study this instead of my other classes. There are some kinds, especially with his questions. He teaches critical thinking over memorization.

Everything in this class seems like it was set up to drive a person insane like: Weird ta hours (tues 1-3), curve that pits you against others while Price emphasized teamwork, and vauge homework and test questions that are crucial to your grade. I have to say that Dr. Price is friendly and I really enjoyed his lectures some things just need fixing.

Dr. Price is not a good teacher. He cannot explain concepts and often confuses himself while answering questions. His homework questions vaguely reinforce what is taught in the class and don't help you learn the material. I would avoid him at all costs. Nice guy, just a terrible teacher.

Bear in mind that Dr. Price is new to teaching. Not sure why others have such negative opinions of him. His class is tough because it involves critical thinking which is a vital aspect if you want to go into the health profession. I loved his lectures and with the TA's help have gotten 100% on all the homework problems. Highly recommend, huge curve

Granted Dr. Price is new to teaching, his lectures are based on his personal interests and therefore follow the format of random fact, random fact, etc. He may be approachable; I wouldn't know because he never responded to my emails in the first place. Tests and homework are so vague that you will need to go to his office every week for help.

Asks bad, vague questions. If its during class he usually has to spend another 10 minutes explaining what was at the "heart" of his question, but was lost in his wording. Has so many grammaticalspelling errors on homeworkstestshandouts that he sounds like a caveman.

Dr. Price is very approachable. First, realize that this IS a 400 level course- expect APPLICATION on the exams, and NOT regurgitation. Second, take his class if you want to do well on the DAT or MCAT since he formats the exams based on passages and/or research articles. Third, the lecture slides prepare you well if you took notes. I recommend him!

Dr. Price is one of the most approachable professors I've had at BYU. Spring was his first time teaching so he was still working some kinks out of the class, but I expect most of those to be taken care of by Fall semester. His experience in industry shows in his teaching style - lots of emphasis on application. I would take another class from him.

Dr. Price is very approachable, organized, and explains concepts well. The class is difficult because of the amount of content. A couple lectures were confusing and a few errors existed in assignments b/c it was his first time teaching, but my questions were quickly clarified. I appreciated the emphasis on application rather than memorization.

Dr Price's unique background in commercial medical research makes for a good teaching environment. I appreciated his willingness to listen to my feedback during class, answer and respect my questions, and help me understand the material. I would happily take another class from Dr Price. The class is hard--but if you work hard it's definitely doable

Spring was his first time teaching ever, and it showed.  He was a researcher and this is his emphasis in teaching.  So for MCAT and DAT expect to do your studying outside of class.  There are daily reading quizzes, weekly homework assignments, two midterms, and a final, all with many typos that make them impossible.  I got a B, good luck.
Boring classes. I feel like professors should at least try to be entertaining, especially if attendance is required!

Dr. Salmon is such a good professor. This class was very difficult, but Dr. Salmon did everything in his power to help students. He also spent an entire class period talking about the importance of mental health and gave us his personal cell phone number and said to call any day or night if we ever were struggling with mental health. Awesome man.

Dr. Salmon is a really nice man. He cares deeply about his students and their success and truly wants you to understand the hard concepts. His tests were difficult but this should be expected from a Junior engineering course. Attend class, do the homework, and ask questions if you have them and you will be fine!

Professor Salmon is a good guy. He genuinely cares about his students. His lectures are incredibly dry and boring, he goes over fairly easy examples in class, but then the homework is significantly harder than the examples in class with little to no resources for help. Tests are 10X harder than even the homework, seriously so brutal.

Dr. Salmon is probably the most open professor I have had yet. He really has a desire to get to know and help his students. He gives out his personal phone number and encourages students to visit during office hours. As a teacher, his lectures can be a little confusing at times, but overall help is there. Tests are very difficult but curved.

I would recommend taking an intro to c++ class first as the c++ portion went very quick, there is a lot of homework/projects/labs but I thoroughly enjoyed most of them. Probably one of the more useful classes, the only complaint I have is that for a class with a 95% A on the grade scale, the test averages were 50% and he doesn't curve.
Professor Salmon is a very kind person, and a good professor. His tests are pretty difficult, but I feel like he does a good job explaining the concepts.

Great guy. Hard class. His tests are brutal. Projects, labs, and homework aren't bad, though. He's very willing to help out when he has time. His projects are interesting and very applicable to the real-world, albeit a little time consuming. There was a pretty solid curve at the end of the class.

Hardest thing was having absolutely no resources besides Google. His powerpoint slides showed only the most basic things about whatever we were learning, and he expected us to figure out everything else. CS 142 before you take this class would be awesome. Tests were ridiculously hard. He didn't teach us how to code in lecture, only how to do math.

Dr. Salmon is a great professor. The class is hard no matter who you take it from, just because that's how coding is at times. Dr. Salmon did a great job of trying to engage his students and help us learn. Be prepared to put some time into this class - the ones who complain all the time either start projects too late or don't ask for help.

Dr. Salmon is nice. His class is awful. While I enjoy coding, this class didn't teach me anything about it. Take differential equations, step it up a notch, & then try shoving it into coding... without being taught how to code. Without prior experience, you will spend 10-15 hrs/wk outside of class just teaching yourself. Take CS 142 beforehand.

Dr. Sproul is the best! His lectures are so engaging. You will learn a ton in every lecture, but you will also laugh a lot and really enjoy what you are learning. He does everything he can to help students succeed, and he provides a lot of resources to help you best understand the material.

Professor Sproul is a really nice guy, but the way the content is organized is really frustrating. There were many times throughout the semester where he would skip over testable content, and instead have you teach yourself with your mandatory study groups. I wish that slides were better organized and more closely alligned with testable content.

Dr Sproul is one of my favorite professors. He cared so much about all his students. He always tried to make lectures fun and made lots of silly jokes. He is super willing to work one on one with students. I had a class of ~150 students and he learned most people's names. Attendance wasn't mandatory but it is hard to do well without lectures.
Very kind, willing to meet outside of class to go over exams and discuss difficult concepts, does a fantastic job of explaining such concepts in an easy and digestible way.
Insanely awesome human being that cares so deeply about each student and knows every single one by name but man is he unorganized which makes this TWO credit class harder than chem 105 for me....

Dr. Sproul was such a funny guy, I really appreciated his lectures. He's really considerate and helpful and will have you do a ton of discussion-based work. I will say, beware of TAs who are very particular on grading; the ones I had were much harsher than he was. Just make sure to be very deliberate on writing from the rubrics.

John is a fantastic professor for welcoming first-year students into the world of biology. He has weekly office hours for any student needing extra attention in learning the course material. All the review guides (WSIK) provided for the three exams are extremely helpful in preparing for each of the respective exams!

Dr. Sproul is a super nice guy. The class itself is not hard as long as you memorize the slides (especially from the TA reviews) for the exams. The workload was about what I'd expect for a 2 credit class.
Dr Sproul is absolutely amazing. He really cares. Not an easy class, but really cool nonetheless. Lectures were super memorable, funny and interesting

Dr. Sproul cares deeply about his students, on both an academic and personal level. In his lectures, he gives you enough to understand the background, then pushes you to make your own discoveries and ask new questions. He integrates his own relevant research in a way that gets you excited about it. This was a super enjoyable and productive class.

Dr. Sproul is one of the most down to earth professors I've had here at BYU. He's focused on student growth and will definitely be in your corner should you need help. He is also all about letting students lead in the learning process. Should you get the chance to ask, he's got some crazy and hilarious life stories that are remarkably insightful.

This is an incredible class! Dr. Talbot's lectures are very engaging. The daily readings are interesting and quite manageable, and the corresponding quizzes are straightforward. If you pay attention, you'll do well (and might even grow to love some classics)!
This was the best class I have taken while at BYU.

He is obsessed with what he thinks was the “golden age” of academia where everything was run entirely by people who think and believe exactly as he does. Just retire, man, seriously. He disparaged postcolonial studies and has concerningly racist notions of literary history.

What you should know:
-very minimal class participation
-says slightly offensive stuff?
-you will be reading a crazy amount AND listening to his podcasts about the reading outside of class
-if you add up all the podcasts, it ends up being 25 hours (and this is outside of the time he spends straight lecturing in person)
-lenient grader on tests

If you are looking for someone who focuses on literature and avoids political ideology this is your professor! Talbot uses the best literature available and educates his students on the death of the university. He's quite hilarious and I always left his class very enlightened out. He believes that understanding the literature of the past is key.

Professor Talbot is the funniest professor I've ever had and is incredibly knowledgeable. He goes on a lot of fascinating tangents—if you like learning for its own sake, you'll find them delightful. Do the readings (there are a lot) and actually pay attention to them and you'll be fine. Taught me to love poetry, meter, and medieval writing SO MUCH.

If you are looking for complicated takes on race, gender, or nationality, this is not your professor! Talbot uses nearly no texts by women and spends most of his lectures lamenting the death of the university. He's quite pessimistic and I always left his class very bummed out. He believes that no interesting literary work is being done now.

While I really like Professor Talbot, I would not take his class again. His classes are mostly filled with whatever pops into his head, which, while entertaining, can be frustrating. The difficulty would be a three if it didn't have the oral exams. You'll learn a lot, but it's difficult. Keep in mind I did take the summer version.

I had Talbot for the required UNIV101 class and he was just hilarious. He is super chatty and we had a ton of fun, despite the simplicity of the course. He is a super nice guy who clearly respects everyone and  cracks tons of jokes.

Hilarious and quirky. I recommend this class to people who genuinely enjoy literature and want to discuss it subjectively and in-depth. If you're not passionate about English literature, this class might not be for you. If you do, classes will be exciting, inspirational, and impactful. I loved Dr. Talbot, but he might not fit everyone's vibe.

Taking a class by professor Talbot will be one of the best decisions of your life! Be prepared: he goes slow through the readings and plans will change at a moment's notice--but I learned so much from his class and loved every minute! He is  invested in each one of his students and will work with you to help you succeed.

If John Talbot said jump I'd say how high. If John Talbot said run I'd say how far. I would follow Professor Talbot into battle if I had too. Do the work and take this class and you will not regret it.

You HAVE to take Dr. Talbot. Class teaches you to see the world in a different way, and to get an A you really just need to show you think. Lectures are hilarious and moving, so you won't want to miss. He's a bit disorganized, but only because he is involved in SO MUCH (research, mentoring, etc). A day doesn't go by when I don't quote him.
I loved this class. Dr. Talbot is great at helping you enjoy the material and see how it applies to your life without having to stress about grades. I would take more classes from him if I could.

I'm conflicted about Talbot. He's a genius and he's hilarious. You WILL LEARN SO MUCH. You will also have SO much HW. Dr. Talbot's Achilles heel is that he's terribly disorganized. I don't think he ever gave us a syllabus at the beginning. At the beginning it was a bit distressing for me, but I got used to it. If you can roll with chaos, take him.

There are teachers at BYU that study teaching (Sweat, Brown) and do it well, but without following their styles, Dr. Talbot is one of the greatest teachers you could ask for. Read anything he has published, and you will understand.

Hilarious person but way too tangent-y. It could take the whole class period to go over a few poems. Sometimes wouldn't communicate assignments with the class and you get a surprise on Learning Suite. I'd take him again because he is a funny guy with an easy class, but he's not the best out there.

I love Professor Talbot, super funny, super engaging. Lectures are really interesting & assignments are fair, meant to make you think rather than memorize. Really cool about late work, his course will change but that didn't bug me (due dates and stuff). Being in class is important, slides don't have everything he says.

Dr. Talbot is funny and SO smart and was great to learn from. He really wants you to form your own opinions of literature and bases his assignments on that rather than memorization and testing. Enjoyed his class.

Unquestionably, favorite professor at BYU. Great lectures. Very knowledgeable. So funny. This class isn't about memorizing facts; it's about gaining a personal appreciation for our literary heritage and becoming better at reading between the lines to find meaning. Lectures mix history and text. You MUST read and get an opinion to be successful.
Be sure to do the reading! While class attendance is not required, to pass the test with a good grade you will find the lectures very helpful.

Hands down one of my favorite profs. I can't imagine taking this class from anyone else. I used to hate medieval lit., but now I love it! He's HILARIOUS and lectures were so entertaining. I learned a ton. Not too many exams, but he's kind of a tough grader. So worth it though! Do yourself a favor and take this class from him.

Professor Talbot is the funniest teacher I've had in my whole time at BYU! If you can take anything from him, I HIGHLY recommend him - I didn't think Greek and Roman literature could be so entertaining or that I'd be able to laugh so hard at Latin poetry

If I could turn back time, I would take as many classes as possible with Doctor Talbot. He is THE teacher, he is so culturally rich and teaches with so much passion that I still remember all his teachings. He is the best teacher I've ever had.
Horace came alive at the words of Professor Talbot

Professor Talbot is the best! He's funny, he cares about what he's teaching, and he gives you what you need to succeed in class. You definitely need to be motivated to work on your own, but it's worth it!

I loved Professor Talbot's class! 10/10 would take another class from him. He is funny and engaging in class, he cares about what he's teaching, and he gives you the tools you need to succeed. This class involves a lot of self-motivation. You do a lot of work on your own. The assignments are unique but they're not difficult. Don't miss class!

I've never met someone who talks SO MUCH. If you get on his good side, he'll love you. He LOVES English and England and poetry and makes you love it too, but he is a tough grader. Seems to want a specific thing without telling you what it is, and you don't get the good grade if you don't hit it on the mark.
Professor Talbot is awesome, he's a super funny guy. You have to write a lot in this class, and that's really all you're graded on. Lecture's are interesting, not your typical class.

My most favorite professor. He's incredibly funny, but it's unexpected, which makes it even better. Your grade is based solely on two tests, one paper, and final exam, though, so beware. If you get lost, don't worry: he walks you through the materials in his discussions. Expect gold nuggets of life wisdom too! You will not regret taking his course.
OMG I LOVED this class, it was really interesting. Dr Talbot it hilarious, his lectures are very entertaining. Midterms were take home which was really nice. Take this class from him if you can.
Do yourself a favor. Take a class from Dr. Talbot. You will never be the same.
He is very very interesting. The class is not challenging but there is a TON of reading and writing involved. His lectures are extremely interesting and he does everything he can to help you out
I learned a lot from him, and although I took his class almost 10 years ago, I still enjoy reading The Iliad. He makes classical literature relatable and interesting.

Professor Talbot has a very classical way of looking at things, which means he was very engaged in our subject material. However, he doesn't leave room for much creativity. Overall, I enjoyed his insights and found what we talked about interesting, but he was surprisingly close-minded about a lot of things.

If you want to learn how to write poetry better, take it from him. The work is a little hard, but worth it. He prepares you well for the final so you know exactly what to expect.  He's approachable and likeable.  He really knows and loves poetry and wants to help you become a better writer.

The man is brilliant. I took copious notes every day, and I don't know that I've ever been so engaged by a professor's lectures. Exploring the Iliad and Aeneid in conjunction with Paradise Lost was phenomenal, but be prepared to read your life away if you're taking it with other English courses. I honestly wish he taught more upper-level classes.
Awesome!  Highly recommend him.  His lectures are interesting and funny.

I've had two classes from him and both were significantly more inspiring and insightful and spiritually enlightening than my religion classes during those semesters.  Lots of writing, essays on tests, lots of reading, but absolutely worth it. Great sense of humor too.

I have had more insights about life and the Gospel from Dr. Talbot than from any other teacher at BYU.  I LOVED his class and can't recommend it highly enough.  It will change your life and the way you look at the world!  He made classic lit come alive with meaning and influence.  It takes a lot of work, but it is worth it!
Professor Talbot is by far the best teacher I have ever had.  He is an amazing teacher and makes sure the class is laughing and thinking 100% of the time.  I highly recommend any of his classes.

Professor Talbot is the best teacher I have had.  At first he seems crazy and off the wall which is fun but useless if you want to learn; however, when you think about his tangents the vast majority of them teach the exact principle that is being discussed in class.  I have never had a class that has made me laugh so hard and taught me so much.  Go

Professor Talbot is INCREDIBLE!!!  I absolutely LOVED attending class because Professor Talbot is seriously HILARIOUS!  When I saw that the class required 10 books I was a bit worried, but I learned so much; even with the hard essays, the class was completely worth it!  I would highly recommend this class as one of the best I've ever taken!

Talbot rocks, and this course was made fo a guy like him to teach it (it's double-listed as ENG 355).  He knows his Classics and his ancient languages and he knows Milton extremely well.  Besides that, he's hilarious and the the class expectations are reasonable.  He's helped me develop an enthusiasm for Paradise Lost.  Highly recommended!

I loved Dr. Talbot.  I always looked forward to his class; he was ablsolutely hilarious and really cared about the students.  Sometimes he would get off topic but he I loved him.  I would definately take more classes from him.
Hilarious. Genius.  Intelligent. Enlightening.  TAKE THIS CLASS! He know what he is talking about and every class is funny, insightful, and worth it

I had Shakespeare and Engl 300R with Talbot and he is my favorite professor.  His lectures are fascinating and relates the literature back to your personal life.  Highly recommend Professor Talbot!  Don't think I've ever learned so much from a single professor.

Professor Talbot's class was both inspiring and infuriating.  After many class sessions, I came away with new insights into Shakespeare and my own life.  I am extremely glad that I took this class. However, it often seemed that Talbot had not bothered to prepare a lesson.  Too be fair, though, this class took place during a study abroad program.

Professor Talbot's class was challenging, but thoroughly enjoyable.  He has a passion for teaching and for his subject matter.  He is also hysterical--I laughed every day.  It is hard work but well-worth the effort.  I would recommend him to anyone that really wants to learn.  I loved going to his class.

SUCH a great teacher. I am an IR major and I loved this class.  Don't expect to like this class if you don't like classical literature or don't like reading, except he does make it fun even for people who don't I would think.  He relates things to life, fascinating connections, I learned a lot. Take a class from him! I would take another.

Dr. Talbot cares about the academic consumer. He is the most enthusiastic professor I have had. Students read a lot, but he works all reading into FANTASTIC class lectures/discussions. His scatter-brained method of teaching is my favorite, by far--I love his tangential discourses. Recommend taking ANY class from him.

This was the worst teacher ever! He is so random and goes off on odd tangents. He literally sat on his chair for 10 mins trying to throw the pen behind him and land in the tray on the whiteboard! I hated the readings and the test were horrible! He grades really hard and if you have a different interpretation of the book then you fail!Worst Teacher!

This is THE BEST class I have ever taken. Talbot is hilarious, entertaining and really thought-provoking. I left class every day with new perspectives. He helped me gain a greater appreciation for literature and life in general. I would recommend this class to ANYONE. TAKE IT!!! It's a little time-consuming with the reading, but SO worth it.

Professor Talbot was one of my favorite professors at BYU. I ended the semester with a notebook full of his quotes--humorous and thought-provoking. I took this class to satisfy a GE and ended it with a greater appreciation for literature and life.  Lectures are NEVER boring.  I highly recommend taking his classes every chance you get.

One of the best professors that I have had at BYU.  Class was never dull.  This class will give you a new perspective on just about everything.  This isn't just a class about ancient literature, it is a class about life.

Professor Talbot loves literature, and he wants his students to love it, too.  Aside from the reading (which is sometimes quite heavy) there is little work, but the tests are frightening if you don't like essays.  Basically, he requires students to think, and that can be troublesome.  Oh, and he's absolutely hilarious.

Dr. Talbot is the epitome of the quirky English teacher.  His lecture are hilarious and he goes off on tangents a lot.  Even though you really don't ever have "homework" per se, MAKE SURE YOU KEEP UP with the reading.  He gives you the test questions a week before tests, but he grades them very strictly.
