He was a very nice guy with funny and interesting lectures.  I enjoyed this class.  However, the tests were difficult, there was a great deal of writing, and the reading assignments were difficult to keep up with...meaning there was a lot of work.  I have never liked early literature, but this professor helped me to like the things we covered.

Dr. Talbot is one of the best! I was worried at first 'cause he seemed so different. But I soon realized he's absolutely a great teacher, a real scholar, and very much interested in helping students find the joy of learning as well (if they haven't yet). He's very willing to help with papers and all

An enlightening,entertaining,smart teacher!Hilarious,makes you really think about what you're reading,explains well.Tests aren't bad,as long as you do your reading(there's a lot).He's nice and helpful-he let me turn in late papers w/out any markdown.I learned tons in this class!One of my favorites!

I hated this class, though I don't hate english. The professor made me hate it though. His tests were rediculous because he would have specific quotes to match with people, yet we never went over anything of the sort in class. I would strongly discourage taking this class from this professor!

This man lies. He didn't grow up in Boston.  He's from Utah and did his undergraduate at the U and then did graduate work at Boston University. Don't let him deceive you. He's passionate about the subject and there's a lot of reading to do.  He's nice cocky guy.
This guy is hilarous!!!  His class is interesting and really promotes thinking about textual allusions and where writers get their ideas.
He is a GREAT teacher, made me love what we were learning. He is crazy smart and explains himself very well. Although he is kinda hoity-toity, it's in a funny forgivable way.

Fantastic lectures. I hate English, but like going to class. If you're not a book worm, don't take it, and his tests are ok. Pretends he's from BOSTON. Really grew up in Utah but lived the last 13 years or so in Boston. Funny man!!
Very good class.  Very good teacher.  Interesting lectures.  Hard tests with long essays.

He is a good teacher, but expects a lot of background knowledge. I would advise against taking this class as a G.E. filler unless you are an english major or have strong background in it. If literature isn't your strong point, this will be a big challenge
Great teacher.  This is by far my least favorite subject, but he makes it really interesting.  Lectures are hilarious.  I am sure I would hate this class with any other teacher - he is good.
He is the best teacher ever!His lectures are fun and interesting.There is a lot to write,but you will learn tons! He has a great personality and a deep knowledge of the subject he teaches!
Test are easy, Attendance is a must, Lots of informal writing.
Classes can get boring at times, dicourages discussion. Class-easy/ test-hard

I wish I could have Dr. Allred for every class I ever take. He's that good. I've never felt so comfortable in the classroom and engaged in the material than his class. You can tell he really cares about his material and works really hard at making sure you understand it. The projects may seem difficult, but you'll workshop them in class with him.

Dr. Allred solidified my decision to be an English teacher. He'd give video-recorded feedback on assignments, bring treats to class, and create opportunities for great discussion and learning. Has the biggest heart. The time commitment for this class is ridiculous, but that isn't his fault. I would love to take more classes from him in the future.
Lots of different assignments going on at one time, but it was doable. The course is tied to ENGL 379, so you have to take them both together.
This class takes a TON of time, because you're out in the schools most of the week, but Dr. Allred was great.

Professor Allred gets to know the class and is super kind. I enjoyed his dry sense of humor haha. I struggled with attendance at the beginning but realized it was a big part of the grade. It's not too challenging, but you still get to write about things that you are passionate about. Definitely take from him if you get the chance!
Take writing 150 from Allred. He is the best teacher and super manageable work load. Good feedback and felt like he was our friend!! He was awesome!
I love Professor Allred!! He's an amazing professor that genuinely cares about his students. The projects weren't too crazy, and it's a manageable workload. I'm so glad I took this class from him!

I'm in this class right now, and Professor Allred is by far my favorite professor. This is his first year teaching at BYU, and I am SO happy that I chose this class. He makes class so fun and forms friendships with all of his students. I never want to miss class because of how great a professor he is. Trust me, take this with Allred!!!

This was my second class with Dr. Balzotti, and I enjoyed both of my classes with him.  He cares about his students and gives good feedback.  He takes the time to talk to his students and is willing to meet with them outside of class.

Doctor Balzotti is the man. He cares about his students as people, not just students. He is a great person to have on your team as you work towards graduation. Also, his classes are genuinely helpful and enjoyable without busy work.

Dr. Balzotti was the perfect professor for this class. He assigned literally 0 homework because he knew we were busy with our internships (this was a PW internship class), gave really good advice for applying to jobs, and was a super funny and chill professor. He gives lots of detailed feedback, which I appreciate. Great guy and fun class.
One of the few classes I actually looked forward to showing up.
Didn't expect to like this class, but when it ended I thought it was actually really useful. Great professor.
Way more interesting than I expected, and actually looked forward to this class.
We focused a lot on making complex ideas clear and readable, and I thought the class was pretty easy but useful
I really liked the lectures and made my civ class actually fun...
Teaches you how to think like a writer...so if you actually want to become a better writer, I recommend his class
Makes rhetoric and persuasion feel relevant. One of the best classes I've taken.
Dr. B. was my favorite professor...class wasn't too hard and I really liked attending his lectures. Highly recommend

Professor Balzotti is a really nice guy, but it pains me to say I wouldn't recommend taking a class from him. He is disorganized and does not outline class expectations, but is upset when expectations aren't met. There is very little communication concerning assignments, and source material for quizzes is LONG and selects very specific details.

He is alright as a professor, yet was super disorganized with his assignments. I felt like he only thinks that writing can be one way which is his. He made me have anxiety about turning things in because I never knew exactly what he wanted, even after asking for feedback. If you have someone else to take it from them.

He's a really caring and kind guy. His class wasn't organized very well and added assignments into Learning Suite as the semester progressed so you didn't actually know how much tests, quizzes, and other assignments were worth. Class felt a little boring, but he's not too difficult. Readings were long.
i love him he is so awesome and nice. the test and quizzes are pretty hard and there are 2 group projects. the class is a bit hard to take notes on but overall good

Professor Balzotti cares about his subject, but his teaching style is so hands-off that I wasn't sure what I needed to do or when it needed to be done by. He doesn't outline the semester, so it's impossible to know what's coming up. He was constantly gone. He set expectations then changed them on a whim. Don't take from him, ever.

He's a really nice guy, but this class was structured so vaguely. He said no due dates were set in stone, which was nice but also enabled procrastination which I wasn't a fan of. I also thought he left too much of the learning up to us with weekly readings. It was just too opened ended for me to understand his class.

Professor Balzotti is an awesome professor! I really enjoyed his lectures, and he makes everything very interesting and engaging to listen to. There were a couple group papers that were a bit difficult, but otherwise not too bad and he provides really valuable feedback.

Have to be honest, was not interested in taking this class in general and my expectations were met. It was a class full of busy work and not interesting. He also was not very accessible to explain his criticism on your papers and it took forever to get it.

This class is an internship course, so you only meet once a week for about 2 hours. You complete four different writing projects throughout the semester. Dr. Balzotti cares about his students and designs his course to best prepare you for the professional world. He takes a while to grade assignments, but he gives great feedback to help you improve.

Dr. Balzotti did an amazing job at teaching the material, providing feedback and being engaged in an online course. I have had some online courses where I felt I was teaching myself. This was not one of them. The material was clear, grading was fair and I learned a lot.
Dr. B is an amazing lecturer. Sometimes to the extent that we don't get through all the material. But he is understanding and fair.

Good setup, meant to feel more professional. My biggest complaint is that we had the class once a week but were expected to learn a ton about technical writing and document design. There was too much material to effectively learn it all. But Dr. B is a great teacher who really knows his stuff. He's a great resource for learning technical writing.

Very lecture heavy teacher, I took him for US HIST SLCC but there was no option. He has quizzes on the textbook once a week. He says "Ek Cetra" instead of Et Cetera and that bothered me. The midterm and final are probably 80% of the grade though, and its all on the lectures in class. its open note. WRITE DOWN EVERYTHING HE WRITES ON THE BOARD.
Hebertson is the man. Go to class, take notes, and study for the tests and quizzes. That's it. He can be very funny if you listen closely.
he's supper nice and funny. overall a really great class and learned alot.
great guy... great class, quizzes can be hard

I took his classes first at SLCC then was delighted to discover that he also taught at BYU. I took several classes from him at both schools. His class lectures are very interesting, he's funny and a kind man. I'd recommend any class he teaches.
Easy A. Way funny
Supper nice!

Do NOT take a class from him. By far thee most unorganized professor I have ever had. He lost classmates' midterms, not an assignment, a MIDTERM. He never comes to class prepared with any of the material he said he would have(quizzes, paperstests to return, etc) He takes breaks throughout the class period whenever he feels like it. I could go on..
I don't agree with a lot of what was said. He is a very nice guy and does the best he can. History can at times be a dry subject. If you are looking for an easy class to for credits this is it.

This man DOES NOT deserve such harsh criticisms.  His class is streamlined and straightforward.  NO BUSY WORK. BOARD NOTES = EXAM.  MINIMAL READING.  He only teaches the most interesting material.  He asks obvious questions in class...its annoying but funny.  THIS CLASS WAS FANTASTIC.  I resent all the brutally negative comments towards this man.

Prof. Hebertson is seriously as boring as the professor on Ferris Bueller's Day Off. Speaking to him is like talking to a stump. He never helps you out, always just says "speak to me next week." On the bright side tests come directly from class notes, so NO reading is necessary for exams. But, he is a TERRIBLE test writer and questions are unclear.

Ok Pro. Hebertson is the most BORING teacher you will ever have in your entire life. People told me to take his class cause it was easy but it definitely isn't because he makes no sense whatsoever.His reading quizzes are impossible and his tests have the most ridiculous questions that have no relevance.
easy A if you attend class and take notes

Worst teacher to ever be called a teacher.      communication with him is impossible, you think you are talking to him, and then you realize you are talking to the wall, at least walls echo a little...

Wow, this class was awful.  I love history but Professor Hebertson has no type of organization to his class in the slightest.  We took the mid term a month after he scheduled it.  You scores dont really calculate into what type of grade you get, he really does just "roll the dice".  If you want an easy B take him, if you want to learn stay away!

Loved the Herbanator! One of the best choices I ever made to take this class in SLC. Go to class, write down what he puts on the board, print, cram study while driving there, get A on test. Simple. Well worth your while! He's a low talker, so sit close.

I had heard about Hebertson before I had even started taking classes at BYU-SLC.  The guy is hillarious (unintentionally) - probably the nicest guy you will ever meet.  Make sure you are VERY detailed on the essay part of the exam and take good notes and study them well before the exams and you will be fine.  An A- to an A is very possible.

Hebertson is probably the least qualified teacher i've ever had. his lectures are taught by him asking "the purpose of the (insert topic here) was... what?" Tests are pretty basic and not too challenging if you have class notes. His quizzes are a killer though. when it comes time for ur overall grades I'm pretty confident that he just rolls a dice
Hebertson is the man.  Go to class, take notes, and study for the tests and quizzes.  That's it.  He can be very funny if you listen closely.

This was the least structured class I have ever had.  The tests are written horribly, otherwise it might be easy.  Even he couldn't decide on the answer to one of his confusing tests.  Absolutly horrible teacher.

His class is easy but you must have good lecture notes for the tests... he only tests you from the notes and not from the large amount of readings.  The quizzes are hard but they don't really count for a grade except for attendance.  If he likes you its an easy A and don't bother to ask for a layout of the marks; he makes it up in his head.

Don't be fooled, there is nothing entertaining about this class. It is CAKE, just get the notes. The only thing that holds your sanity through the boredom are the lively embroidered sweaters of large animals, and the occasional random comment Hebertson makes. “Between classes I love to go to 7-11, look at all the magazines and have a drink”.

This class is interesting if you sit in the front and can hear what hes saying. He knows a lot and seems to love teaching. The tests seem easy but be very detailed-probably beyond what he says in class for the essay. The class is easy.

If it's a good time you're looking for, go paint a house and watch it dry. Tests are cake as stated above, and every class he allows unspecified "nap time" by showing a 30 minute video tape which is never covered on quizzes or exams. His quotes are worth the trip north, be sure to ask about his vibrant college days and trips 2 a hot spring Jacuzzi
Took him for 201 and 202. Deffinantly easier than taking ANY class down here at BYU, but he is super borning, and he grades however he feels. Kindof weird, but I'd take the class.
This guy is great! Just study the class notes. The rest...just enjoy.
I loved his class because it was SO easy and the guy is unintentionally HILARIOUS, although he talks like the teacher on ferris buelar's day off so he can get pretty boring

I agree with what everyone has said about Hebertson!  Here are some of my favorite Hebertson quotes: On Marathons: "People, I'll never run one of these."  On Xerxes: "Very clearly, people, what kind of man are we dealing with here? a MAD man." And, "People, this guy makes Hunchback look like Brad Pitt." You have to savor the Hebertson experience!
The man is an absolute miracle.  Class is cake.  And what, people?  That's right, every class is a blast if you enjoy crazy idiosyncrasies and quotes that you'll never forget!
What can I say?  The man is pure entertainment personified.  Come to class and don't suffer a seizure and you'll get an A.
This guy is hilarious.  He's a little scatterbrained, but funny.  His class is way easy.  No papers.  All you have to do is copy down everything he writes on the board and you'll get an A.

I really like how Prof Kerr structured this class with projects instead of exams. I feel like he modified it to help students learn and retain what they're learning. He cares about his students so much and that is very apparent in his teaching. I'm not a tax kid so I thought it was hard but he does a great job.

Professor Kerr is a great professor. I have had him twice throughout my time at BYU and he remains one of my favorite professors at BYU. He is personable, spiritual, and smart. He cares about his student and I always feel that in my interactions with him. He is great at simplifying complex concepts and answering complex questions asked by students.
Great course and great teacher. Its easy to tell that Professor Kerr truly cares for his students.

Professor Kerr is awesome! Every class where we have learned about DTA and DTLs I have been so confused. He actually explained it in a very simple way that I could absolutely understand. I am very happy about that.
Professor Kerr is a great professor! He goes above and beyond for his students and helps us understand complex material.

Professor Kerr is a nice guy, but not a great teacher. He doesn't explain tax concepts clearly, the textbook is incredibly long and dense, and some of the homework is group projects that feel like a waste of time.

Dr. Ostenson is one of my very favorite professors at BYU. He combines an extensive knowledge base  and repertoire of compelling material and discussion questions with a genuine love and respect for his students to create a class environment where amazing and impactful discussions can be had. Get ready to think, read, and contribute!

Dr. Ostenson is a master teacher. As a future teacher, I've never been so inspired to be a great teacher than listening to him. He's funny, he's engaging, and he's brilliant at what he does. He'll push your abilities, but if you work really hard and ask him questions, you'll walk out of there more prepared than any other teaching course.

I actually took his class a year ago but wanted to give a review because I still think about how his class affected me. Everyone felt loved by him. From the first day he knew everyone's names! His classroom is so comfortable and feels like home. I highly recommend the YA novel class! It's a lot of reading but I learned so many valuable things!

Professor Ostenson did such a great job choosing interesting YA novels for us to read. Plus you get to read three novels of your own choice as well. He isn't a tough grader, pretty much if you are showing effort and putting in work you will do well.

Ostenson was a fantastic professor. He made it a mission to learn everyone's name in the whole lecture which created a more personal relationship with him. Even though I never participated, he knew my name which was really cool of him. Lectures were usually pretty interesting with very little outside work other than the 1 major essay.

Professor Ostenson was an amazing professor. He reminds me of an excited middle-aged dad because he would run up and down the rows of students with his microphone and talk to students about the content and the lecture. The class is essay heavy, but the TAs are great and he's easy to talk to and contact.

Professor Ostenson is awesome! We have great discussions on the books we read. You do read a lot, but they aren't boring books. We read books like Coraline and Hunger Games. He asks questions that challenge your thinking because he wants to get you to think deeper about the books. I love his teaching! Would definitely take this class again.

I loved this class with Professor Ostenson! I've never been a great writer so I struggled with the papers, but I felt like I really learned a lot and became better. Choose an interesting inquiry report topic, because it will extend to the other pieces you write. You can tell Professor Ostenson cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

He was a great guy, and I liked the class setup of smaller groups for discussion. Easy to listen to lectures. He doesn't believe in "bad" questions, so it was a great learning environment where I felt I could participate. A few big papers but they were not too difficult if you pay attention and get help from section Professors. Would recommend!

I really like him at the beginning of the semester. I gave him 4 stars because for some reason, he made the class write 3 major papers about the same topic. I would've appreciated a little more diversity for writing topics. He is very kind and tries to have purpose behind his essay assignments. He is entertaining. No belief in "bad" questions. (:

Professor Ostenson is the BEST. He knew my name by the second week of class when I never told him it. His lectures were never boring and were always interactive. As long as you try your best and get help from the RWC then your papers will get good grades. It also definitely helps if you have a good section TA! Very minimal EC in class (only 1%).

Prof Ostenson made a boring class fun and exciting. He is an engaging and involved lecturer and sets up the course so you know the true fundamentals of writing a college paper. He learned all of our names. I'm so glad I took this course, it provided me with so many valuable materials. Get him if you can, you won't regret it!

Prof. Ostenson is kind and gave interesting lectures. There was a lot of writing but that's to be expected. We did write all our essays about the same first topic the whole semester so pick your inquiry report subject wisely.

Professor Ostenson is an amazing teacher and I enjoyed his lectures! He was super engaging and very caring. I usually hate writing classes, but I actually enjoyed this class. It is very laid back and not very much homework other than a few (3) larger assignments. But there is lots of creative freedom granted which makes them so much better.
Easy class! Loved the lectures they were engaging.  I'd recommend it for some easy credit
He knows what he's teaching, and he teaches it well.

Dr. Ostenson is a good guy. When I was sitting in the hall the first day, I heard his lecture and was intimidated, but he's not intimidating at all. Even though he has a lot of students he tries really hard to remember everyone's names. He is a good, clear teacher. The class has workshop instructors, and I like the one I got.

Dr. Ostenson is a highly engaging and dynamic lecturer. He's excellent at involving each student -- even memorizing every name in our class of 100+ students -- and at helping us understand why the content is important and relevant to us. Expect clear expectations, consistent work (none of it busy work), and personal and intellectual growth.
Professor Ostenson was an engaging speaker. He worked hard to learn as many names as he could in such a large class. His chosen class-wide topic of poverty was handled with dignity and respect.

Absolutely loved this professor. His lectures are so entertaining and easy to understand- he makes each individual student feel involved. Attendance definitely matters in his class but honestly, I always looked forwards to his lectures. All of the TAs in his class are great and totally work with you. I highly recommend taking Writing 150 from him!

You could tell his political views just by the assignments he gave. He is a nice guy sometimes but calls on people randomly and expects them to have a good answer and then makes them feel bad if they don't. I hated going to his class to be honest it was so boring and I didn't learn a lot.

He's awesome! My class had hundreds of students in it and by the end of the semester, he learned everyone's name. His writing assignments were simple and straightforward. The class is designed for everyone to get an A if they put in the effort. He makes lectures interesting, but it is a lot of repeated information. Highly recommend!

I am not one to leave reviews, but Professor Ostenson is a true gem. I am currently in his "big comp" class, so while he is the main professor who lectures two days a week, he doesn't actually see or grade my work (my other professor does). He truly wants to get to know his students and has engaging lectures. The class overall is super easy!

I could really tell that Prof. Ostenson cared about the students. He always took the time in class to make sure we understood what he was teaching. He met with me a couple times outside of office hours and was willing to stay after class. He grades fairly and gives AMAZING feedback that's even helped me in other classes.

Professor Ostenson is a fabulous professor. He is one of the kindest and most passionate professors I have had. I am not someone who was incredibly excited to take WRTG 150, but because of his passion for the subject and his understanding with the students, it was a class I would take again.

Dr. Ostenson isthe single greatest professor I have ever had at BYU. He genuinely cares about and is willing to work with his students. I highly recommend taking any class from him. You won't regret it!

Take from him he's the best! His class seemed to be a tiny bit more challenging than Writing 150 taught by graduate students but he taught us so much and worked with us 1 on 1 on every single paper. He's super funny and his classes are never boring because he keeps us engaged and knows each one of us personally. 3 major essays but grading is clear.

Really great class and professor, wasn't excited at first but lectures are always very engaging and entertaining. He's very funny, and on top of that gives great lectures that are very easy to follow and understand. All course material is very well laid out and very easy to follow. As long as you show up and put in a little work it's an easy A.

Dr. Ostenson is my favorite teacher at BYU! He really makes an effort to know every single one of his students. He is extremely knowledgeable and works with you on all your assignments. He is so funny and understanding. I can't say enough good about Dr. Ostenson, definitely take a class from him! He is the best.

Dr. Ostenson is so kind and caring. You can tell he cares about you as his student. He wants his students to succeed and he gives you everything you need to do so. I'm so thankful for what he taught me about how to be a good teacher.
I LOVED this class! I learned so much, and class discussions were great. There was a lot of reading, but it was enjoyable and not difficult. Would definitely take again! 10/10

You read A LOT. but the books are fun and intriguing. His classes are very interesting and he is just a really great guy. You have to write quite a bit too, but he really makes the criteria clear for the assignments. Even though it is hard, I would take this class again in a heartbeat
Ostenson is a good teacher. Writing 150 is inheritance a boring GE, but he makes it as enjoyable as possible. He even brought donuts to class the last day!

Great Class. He's willing to clarify assignments with you and his pedagogy is fantastic. He is aware of students and challenges. Easy A as long as you keep up on the work, you get what you deserve. Every class is interesting and useful as a teacher.
Great Professor! He?s willing to help and is super nice and so fun.  Definitely recommend this guy.
So I have never taken this guy in college but I loved his class in high school.  It was like stand up 101 Every freakin day!

Love Dr. Skidmore. He's pretty funny but just kind of talks at the class the whole time. Be ready to get outside of your comfort zone for like 20-30 minutes of class and listen to him ramble for the rest. He has you buy his textbook at the beginning of the class, but I didn't read it once. There are some "quizzes" but they're self graded. Easy A
This man taught me how to juggle

You would think that a performance psychology class would teach you how to be a stronger performer, right? Well, Dr. Skidmore's idea of that is taking his class to a public space, having them sing, act like cats, and look like complete idiots. No joke. Easy A, but boring lectures, pointless content, and hearing him promote his book the whole time.

I love Professor Shober, he's really funny and he teaches well. Homework is very manageable, about 40 minutes every day for 6 days a week. He really wants us to do well.

It was pretty bad. Was his 1st semester teaching complex (2nd total). He ditched the book a few weeks in for his own notes and problems he wrote during the semester. Unfortunately he did not exactly have a gift for clear teaching, or writing homeworks or tests, or grading fairly, or taking feedback. My only non-A in 3yrs at BYU. Take anyone else.
This course while difficult, was incredible fair. Dr. Schober makes the lectures super fun and is always accepting feedback from his students. This was literally my favorite class when I took it!
The literal GOAT. Is very understanding of what it's like to be a student. He's very enthusiastic and funny.

The course itself is very difficult, but Dr. Schober explained it well and made it engaging. He's super funny and made an effort to learn everyone's names. Study hard for the tests and you should do fine.

Dr. Blotter explain things fast but clear enough. He is very accessible outside class. His notes packet was clear and it has a bunch of tips to understand the topics. The problems in the packet were very similar to the ones in the homework. To take home exams but were timed fairly. He is very passionate and want everybody to succeed in his class
He was a great UNIV teacher, very merciful in extending deadlines. He has lots of fun stories.

Super nice guy and passionate about engineering, but a very difficult course. Lots of homework, two exams, final exam, and final project. Professor Blotter wants you to do well, but all the homework and (especially) the tests are so soooo hard. Very tough grader. Tests were really hard to complete in the time given. I learned a lot of cool things in this class but it was hard to keep a good grade.

Taking a mentored coursework class from doctor blotter was one of the best decisions I made at BYU. I loved the freedom he gave me to explore solutions to the project, but at the same time he was always accessible to help and guide me. Definitely recommend him for this or any other class.
Good teacher. One of the hardest classes in the program. Make sure to understand the homework.

This is a hard class and at first Dr. Blotter made it seem worse, but it got much better as he warmed up to us. Talk to him outside of class and you will have a good relationship with him and do well. Use the TAs! Despite what is seems, he really cares, wants us to succeed, and gives us a good idea of what's on the tests. Class is good Q&A, so go.

Quit going to lecture because I showed signs of depression in lecture. When I quit my grade stayed the same and my life improved. Acts like questions are a waste of time and your fault when he doesn't know answers. His "real world experience" is nothing like actual real world experience. First words were "don't expect more than a 40%"

Dr Blotter's lectures were fairly good but almost all of the information covered in lectures was contained in the note packet handed out. Homework was a huge portion of the grade and was very difficult
Disrespectful, uncaring, but hides it well. Would give powerful, moving spiritual thoughts and then proceed to tell students "tough" when they asked for help or clarification on a topic.

He isnt a pushover, but what did you expect from Mechanical Engineering at BYU? I feel Ive actually learned engineering finally. Dr Blotter has real world experience unlike other professors. Do all the hw & youll do good on the tests, relative to other students. Final grade is curved. Bad reviews typ. come from sensitive students w/ lower grades.

Easily one of the most difficult professors I've had. He makes this difficult class twice as hard. In class, he is demeaning to students, and it is hard to get a hold of him outside of class. Dr Blotter makes a tough class 100x tougher. He expects you to know EVERYTHING contained in the reading for the tests. Dr. Blotter might be a good guy outside of the classroom, but when in class he doesn't put any effort into providing a good learning experience. On almost a daily basis he disrespects students and puts down anybody that has "obvious" questions about the material. He expects you to learn everything on your own and be perfect. Shouldn't be a prof.
His exams are ridiculously hard and you should expect to spend 10h+ on homework/week.

The worst professor I have ever had, hands down. Brutally hard, and horrible at explaining difficult concepts. TA in charge of grading homework was a self righteous jerk that took pride in finding anyway to dock points.
Absolutely incompetent with zoom, made taking the class remotely even more difficult.
Regularly included homework problems that required material not taught in class and not in the textbook. Good luck. Don't take him.
Disprespectful, and terrible at teaching. Don't take it from him at ALL costs.

Feels more like a drill sergeant than a teacher. Expects perfection and punishes imperfection at every opportunity. Gives longer HW/tests, and grades more harshly than other 372 teachers. Borderline disrespectful to students. Way difficult tests and tests us on stuff not covered in class. Doesn't own up to his mistakes much. Don't take it from him.

He is a poor lecturer. It doesn't look like he curved the grades at all. The tests are insanely difficult and poorly written (50% avg). There's a fill-in-the-blank-with-the-correct-answer option E on every question so there's no partial credit.  And if he screws up, he's covered because you should have caught it and used option E. It's your fault.

The class is 3 credits but be ready to do way more than 6 hours/week on homework.  And of these 6 hours/week, they will pretty much all be spent with the TAs.  The tests are incredibly difficult due to you not being able to use your notes.

This man will not put up with anyone slacking off so be ready to work. That said, because he expected so much of his students I feel like I learned more in this class than any other individual class I have taken. Seriously, I left this class feeling like I was ready to go take on real world engineering problems. It was super hard, but worth it.

His class is very difficult, but you actually LEARN.  He demands a lot from his classes and expects you to remember the things you have learned in previous classes. He focuses on learning not on grades.  If you're prone to asking stupid question, don't take the class, he doesn't waste time on them.  Participation is key to liking and doing well.

Does not grade anything nor care about your grade. Will embarrass you in class. Every semester is different with him depending on how much he likes your class.  He hated ours because we called him out on mistakes and things I won't go into.  If you must take it, go into his office every day and ask him questions.  Got a C, lowest previous was B. ;)
Super great teacher as a person, but definitely a difficult class. He moves fast in lecture and homeworks are time consuming. Quiz almost every class period.

Dr. Blotter really does care about students and is SOOO helpful if you go to office hours. He makes you work for it though. He goes at the fastest student's pace during lectures so you need to follow along in the packet to keep up. Tests are tough but I averaged a high D on tests and pulled an A- in the class.

Does not: Grade final exams or final projects (seriously - I turned my final exam and final project in on time and he refused to grade them) Abide by his syllabus Respond to student emails. Keep appointments with students. Post scores throughout the semester Hold class Fridays  Does: Give extremely hard tests Respond snidely to questions

Dr. Blotter is actually one of my favorite teachers.  He didn't waste time answering the stupid questions people ask, and he was probably the most careful of any teacher I've ever had about making sure everyone understood the material. I would love to take another class from him, because I came to school to learn.

The class and subject material is just a lot of work and fairly tedious. He knows it extremely well and does not beat around the bush; everything is straight up and super clear. He's not very tactful but he's honest and wants to help students succeed.
Dr. Blotter is hardcore he teaches with passion and it shows.  He is hard but I loved the class.

Do Not take a class from blotter if possible.  He constantly missed lectures, did not attend his office hours, and did not seem to care about student learning.  very inconsistent and stubborn in his grading. horrible teacher.

Blotter is a good teacher. I learned a lot in his class. He is defintely not easy. He expects you to remember what you learned in previous classes, and he expects you to figure stuff out on your own.   I'm going to take 335 from him as well, but only because I have no other choice. NOT bad enough to delay graduation. haha.

do NOT take any classes from this man!!! Dr. Blotter is a certified flying retard. He once spent half a class trying to convince us that there is such thing as a "rotational inductor". Cares more about hunting, fishing, and snowmobiling than he does about students

Great professor.  I think he's the only engineering professor I've had who bothered to learn all the students' names and tried to get to know us.  He's helpful and is willing to adjust homework due dates for the class if everyone is tight on time.  The class is kind of tough, but I learned a lot.

Dr. Blotter really cares about his students.  His teaching style isn't always the most clear, but he is more than willing to spend extra time to clarify and is extremely helpful if you go to his office.  Very energetic teacher, and you can always get him to push due dates back. Seems hard at first but softens up a bit a few weeks in.

I took the follow-up course, ME 431, believing I was prepared after 335.  Those who took it from Dr. Brian Jensen were, those who took it from Dr. Blotter were not.  I highly discourage taking any class from this professor unless you would like to start later courses behind everyone else.

Seriously? This guy was a great teacher, he cared a lot about the students, he was always willing to help, and yeah if you asked stupid questions or tried to waste class time he sometimes got on your case. The class material is admittedly difficult, but the professor could have done a better job at adressing student questions. Professor England was one of the best professors I have had a BYU! He used his History background to really help the scriptures come alive. He always testified of Christ and related it to today's world. Easily the best religion class I have taken!

He is a really great guy but I had a hard time with his teaching method. They are interesting if you participate but not very exciting.  He talks for most of class and doesn't manage time well. Dr. Jarvis was awesome! His class was pretty easy and interesting, and the TAs are amazing.

I really enjoyed this class! Professor Jarvis is super good at facilitating respectful discussions about various (sometimes tough) topics. Professor Jarvis is a really good teacher. You do not have to participate, but the class is much more enjoyable if you do. He encourages people to express varying opinions and does a really good job moderating the discussion. Willing to meet to help with assignments or answer questions attendance is graded/tracked online textbook semi-difficult tests (show up and study  pass)

Dr. Jarvis is my FAVORITE! He is so helpful whenever you have questions, and honestly he is so funny! He gives great insight into qualitative research, and is so laidback. He is so helpful and this class is pretty easy if you do the reading! I would totally take another class from him.
Easy class to pass if you don't care, great class if you do. Jarvis is so chill and funny and class is really fun to go to.

Jon is an awesome guy. The class, on the other hand, is the type you can sleep through and still get an A. I'm not interested in sociology so I was always bored in class. He is such a great teacher!! You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Jarvis is FABULOUS! The course and expectations are so clear. He is very knowledgable in the area of study but is also a great teacher. HIGHLY recommend!

SOC 380 was one of the best classes I have taken at BYU. I have taken 3 classes from professor Jarvis and this one may have been my favorite. He is so well articulated and makes the subject matter applicable and interesting. I left with different opinions than I came to this class with, and loved writing the final paper. Jarvis is the best!

Professor Jarvis is one of my favorite Sociology professors. He is very funny and laidback. The class itself was very easy- if you did the readings, you will be fine. There's not a lot of incentive to come to class because the lectures are online and he posts the powerpoints. Attendance is not taken and there are no quizzes in class.  Professor Jarvis makes the class material interesting with his insight.

I took 2 classes from Jarvis and would have taken more if I could have. He's an excellent professor and I know I wasn't the only student who thought so. His lectures are engaging and he's understanding and flexible. The reading assignments weren't long or difficult and he gives you a lot of freedom when choosing what to write your papers on.

Jon is hilarious, nice, and laid-back! There were a lot of readings but they weren't bad. We did a lot of group-work. The class was pretty hands on -- we did our own research project with observations, interviews, and focus groups. Challenging but worth it.

His tests are not difficult.  There's a research paper. Attendance is mandatory.  Don't bother getting the textbook.  I did and have barely cracked it open. The Revel code will do just fine. Professor Jarvis is a great guy, I really enjoyed interacting with him. But to me, this class was painfully boring and seemed like mostly common knowledge. The tests were pretty hard, and it could be hard to find motivation to do well. But that's just my critique of the class. Jarvis is a great professor. Easy B, harder A.

I LOVE Professor Jarvis. SOC380 was fascinating and he is an amazing teacher. Very clear with expectations and he met individually with each student in my class. The class is great! I learned a lot from reading the text book and his lectures. Class attendance and participation is mandatory. CLASSES ARE CUT AND DRY- A REPEAT OF THE TEXTBOOK. HOWEVER, ATTENDANCE IS MADATORY DUE TO 'TOPHAT' ATTENDANCE TAKING. ALSO, QUESTIONS FROM MOVIES AND CLIPS SHOWN IN CLASS ARE ON THE TEST. AS LONG AS YOU STUDY THE TEXTBOOK, YOU SHOULD DO ALRIGHT.

Absolute beast. The class is hard because of the content, but Professor Red is so amazing and caring. He gave up his job at Amazon to teach students. He loves the students and really wants them to succeed.

Professor Liljegren (Professor Red) is one of the best teachers out there He is excellent at explaining difficult concepts, funny, and spiritual. He is very open and accessible with his office hours. He is an expert in the field, and you can tell he really knows what he's talking about.

Professor Wade loves what he does. I couldn't have cared less about reading books, plays, and poetry in Spanish before taking this class, but some of the readings really won me over. 3 Non-cumulative exams and assigned readings every class, that may or may not have a pop quiz. Profe Wade is amazing! He really cares about his students and understand that we have a lot going on. I couldn't recommend him enough. This was my favorite university-level Spanish class I've ever taken. We loved him so much we got him a T-shirt for Christmas.

Take 345 from Wade you will not regret it. He is so kind and you'll learn so much. There is a ton of variety and every lecture is a good time. The tests and quizzes are very reasonable and only require you to study the material a bit.

Great professor and great class. Attendance and participation is important, missing a few days will not be super consequential. Professor Madison is a very caring guy but his class is based solely on pop quizzes and tests so if you get an average grade on even one test your grade will not be good.

He is detailed and clear with his grading, and gives lots of options for you to do better. Jones cares about helping you not only get a good grade, but to improve in all aspects.

Lots of reading, but it was all very relevant and covered church history topics that aren't frequently discussed. Brother Watkins handled difficult topics in a caring, respectful manner. I came away with a stronger testimony of the prophets and the restoration. He was willing to reopen an exam for me when I missed the deadline.

Reading was a lot. I took his class in the spring and we read upwards of sixty pages per class. This class was reading heavy, but other than that not difficult. It felt mostly historical with not as much spiritual strengthening as I had hoped. He is great at explaining complicated topics.

This is a great class! Professor Watkins is always prepared for class and knows the material very well. He teaches you from a historical point of view but always brings the Spirit into class. There is a lot of reading in this class and responses but its all manageable. There are quizzes online after every class and two online exams.

Professor Watkins is so good. He is very professional and clear lectures. Before every class, there are a few articles (often from Joseph Smith papers and other scholarly articles) and a little paragraph of summary of what you learned, due. And after every class there is a 6-question quiz. So good! I would suggest taking this from him!

He's good as far as religion professors go. His class was pretty chill and I learned some good things. I would definitely recommend taking Foundations of the Restoration with him because his class is definitely on the easier side.

This is SUCH a good class! He was amazing at teaching difficult restoration topics and his lectures strengthened my testimony so much! There is a lot of reading for this class, but you can skim! The quizzes and tests are super easy! Class was always amazing and Bro. Watkins is a great teacher!

Such a humble guy. I've never had such a touching religion class. He seriously worked through tough material (like Mormon meadow massacre, polygamy, and racism) and did it so thoughtfully. He is really smart, and you can tell he cares about you. The only downside to his class is that you have to read so much! Like seriously like 40 pages a night.

Brother Watkins is super nice and really cares for his students. He even pushed back a big paper for us. The class has TONS of reading, but I recommend skimming. There are easy attendance quizzes after every class but nothing to stress about. The final and midterm are open notes as well.

Great professor! There is a lot of reading, but some of it is really interesting. If you're looking for religion credit, this class is a solid choice. The tests are open note/online and relatively easy. Homework is manageable as well. Attendance is mandatory, but the lectures are engaging, so you'll likely want to be there anyway.
Professor Watkins is genuinely so caring, and does a great job talking about difficult topics in a way that is faith-building.

If you want a more educational view rather than spiritual view of church history, then take this class from Professor Watkins. It is nice at times on touchy subjects so you get a whole analysis of the situation. He is a very kind teacher but there is a lot of reading but he encourages skimming. Open note exams and overall the class is fairly easy.

Prof. Watkins is great. His lectures are super insightful, and he is able to address very concerning church topics in a highly productive way. He has a ton of reading, but he allows skimming as long as you are somewhat prepared to discuss the topics in class. Very chill class, easy A. Take Watkins!

Dr. Watkins is a super knowledgeable professor and knows a lot more about every topic than what is covered in class. He is happy to stop and answer questions, although I felt that the class content was pretty compressed. You have to read 20-40 pages of readings before each class, but they are really interesting and you will learn a lot from them!

I liked his class because it was pretty easy. However, he does this class from a historical perspective which I didn't find super interesting, but I did learn new things. He does care for his students and wants everyone to have success.

Dr. Watkins did a great job at teaching church history with a scholarly approach. There is a ton of reading, but you can get by skimming a lot of the time (and it's super interesting stuff). The quizzes and tests are a breeze. His lectures are thoughtful and spark great discussion. He is so kind and makes everyone feel welcome.

Incredibly intelligent historian who teaches difficult concepts and history in an enlightened and unbiased light. Interesting material, doing the assignments will earn you an a without much stress, so you can focus on listening and learning in class. Would recommend to anyone looking for a religion elective.

I loved this taking this class from Professor Watkins. He approached some really tough topics with such a good perspective and didn't shy away from controversial questions. One of my favorite professors I've had at BYU.

Professor Watkins did a great job at making foundations interesting and relevent. He dove into uncomfortable topics well and is always there for his students. If you show up and are thoughtful it is an easy A and you will definately get something out of the class.

Best religion professor I've ever had!! Dr. Watkins cares about his students and is SO knowledgeable about church history. Homework was very easy and straightforward, didn't take any time at all once you got used to it. Tests and quizzes were very easy. If you put in a little effort, you will get a good grade and learn so much.

TAKE A CLASS WITH PROFESSOR WATKINS! This was by far my favorite religion class I have taken here at BYU!! The material of the class was so interesting to learn. It really was nice to learn about the history of a church, with the perspective of not just the gospel but also from a historical viewpoint. Midterm and Final are so easy, open note/slides

Professor Watkins was an amazing teacher! He approached many hard topics with respect and helped answer any questions that came up. The homework was reading heavy, but despite the long readings, they were really enjoyable and insightful. I would definitely take Professor Watkins again!

Great teacher, kind and willing to help students, insightful, tests are really easy but the main chunk of the class is the reading. Readings are really long for each class and you have to write s paragraph response to the reading before class, but most of them were enjoyable for me, just long. Great class though.

Professor Watkins is the best! He addresses difficult topics but in a way that shows us to address history and not ignore it. His class was very educational and uplifting. You will have daily readings with short responses, and a 3-question quiz after class. Tests are very easy because they are open note and pull questions from quizzes. 10/10 class.

By far the best religion teacher I've ever had! Being a historian, he takes more of an academic approach and yet he has the strongest spirit. He answers some super tough questions with incredible insight and love, and will share his personal understanding if asked, but will never be preachy about it or claim it as prophetic teaching. An easy A!

Take this class. It's actually interesting and easy to get by. He assigns lots of readings but encourages skimming. Honestly I barely did the readings at all and I did just fine. I probably spent an hour or less on the class each week and then got to go hear interesting stuff in lecture. Easily my favorite religion class I've taken at BYU.
History professor, centered in understanding truth, both spiritual and secular. Very clear about expectations, no burdening students with busy work.

Brother Watkins wasn't a particularly interesting/gifted teacher, but his class is very straightforward and very easy. He's a historian and this was taught as a history class. There's 25-40 pages of reading between classes, but you'll be fine skimming. Easy A. He teaches confusing church history topics very openly and clearly.

I enjoyed this class, but it was a little labor intensive at times. Every class requires 50 pages of reading and a paragraph comparing the primary sources to the secondary sources. In his credit, I did learn a lot about approaching touchy topics. The daily quizzes are the midterm questions. Caring guy who will level with you.

The best class if you want to just LEARN about church history and not stress about having to remember everything for the tests! All the exams are open note, there are super easy weekly reading responses & quizzes and a couple of one page papers. Don't miss the weekly quizzes tho, they add up!! (That's why I got an A- lol). Loved this class!!

Professor Watkins is by far and away the best religion professor I've had at BYU. He is extraordinarily knowledgeable about the history of the Church, and his passion for the subject shows. He is a historian by trade, so I felt like his class was a rich educational experience and not a glorified seminary class. Take Dr. Watkins!

I love Professor Watkins! Some of the stuff that was taught is very hard to understand but Professor Watkins did such a good job teaching it. There's a lot of reading and two short papers due every week based off of the readings but it wasn't too bad. You had to go to class to be able to mark your attendance but I actually enjoyed coming to class!

Professor Watkins was passionate about the content he taught and covered controversial topics extremely well. I really appreciated his style of teaching and his love for the class. I would definitely recommend taking a class from him!

The frank way professor Watkins discussed church history was great for my testimony. I've struggled with history issues before. When someone tries to brush over them in Sunday school it is very obvious. Professor Watkins didn't do that and addressed the issue's head on which was super helpful. He did seem uncomfortable and rushed polygamy though.

I really liked Professor Watkins, he was a very entertaining lecturer. He did give us a lot of reading since this was a Spring term class and everything was condensed, which could get ridiculous at times, but overall he was great

My favorite thing about this class was that it gave us all a fresh perspective on the Restoration, the more historical side of it than simply a spiritual teaching of the events. Just make sure you go to class, take notes, and understand the powerpoints and you will be totally fine. Tests and quizzes are all open note.

Professor Watkins is a wonderful professor! While there's a LOT of readings, his class is definitely an easy one to take. Most things are open note or pretty easy, but attendance is graded, so don't skip too much! He's definitely passionate and knowledgable about Church history. If you have the choice, definitely go with Watkins!

I loved Professor Watkins! His lectures can be a bit boring, but he is really passionate about church history. He has a great heart and is willing to help with anything. If you take this class during Spring term, GET READY TO READ. So much reading, but the tests were so easy.

TAKE PROFESSOR WATKINS!! Easily one of my favorite religion classes I have taken at BYU. Professor Watkins is amazing and he knows his stuff. Pretty good amount of reading but he chooses really interesting articles to go along with the course content. Loved it!

This class was awesome! I learned so much and it was super easy. The syllabus may seem daunting with lots of writing assignments, but they are all super short and are more about what you learned than an actual paper. There is a lot of reading but it's okay to skim or skip some. Exams are open everything so they're super easy. Highly recommend!

Professor Watkins was so great! I loved the historical approach that we took as we approached the Restoration. He had no problem covering often difficult topics and we had great class discussions. Stay on top of daily readings and go to class and the rest will be really easy.

Professor Watkins is incredible and cares so much about what he does. His course taught me a ton about how to approach Church history. Work load was perfect, not too much: interesting readings and reading responses due every class and little post-class quizzes after every class, as well as a book response and midterm/final. Everything is open note.

The course content is interesting and good information for members of the church to learn about. However, his lectures are long-winded and he basically reads his lectures from his computer. It was disappointed to have such a non engaging class when the content is so interesting.

This was by far the greatest religion class I have ever taken and I would recommend Prof Watkins to everyone! It's everything you want religion classes to be... Simple quizzes after every class, short reading reflections and open note tests. The class itself was also always very interesting and entertaining. Very solid class.

His class is everything a religion class should be. You do have to read a decent amount before every class, but other than that if you just come to class and do the quizzes/readings you will definitely get an A. Super insightful and uplifting classes. Tests are open-note and not worth that much of your grade (25% total).

BEST RELIGION PROFESSOR EVER! These are some tough topics and he teaches them so well. He is open, honest and ready to answer questions. I only took this class because I needed another religion credit and I saw that he was teaching the course. Don't stress about getting a low grade. If you listen in lecture you will get an easy A

Professor Watkins was an amazing teacher, he had some amazing insight to what was learned. A daily load of work looks like a couple readings outside of class, from the D&C and also some papers that may be primary or secondary sources. Every day there is also a quiz after class that is easy to pass if you are vigilant in class. Exceptional Professor

Professor Watkins created a religion class environment that I loved. Every religion class should be structured the way he did. Open note quizzes, only a mid term and a final, and a short reading before each class. I have never had a religion class that did not stress me out until this one. It was easy but I still got a lot out of the class.

I loved Jordan Watkins. He is a genuine guy and amazing teacher. You could tell he was passionate and understood his material so well. He wants every one of his students to succeed, and stays after every class for anyone to ask questions. He is the type of professor you would have no fear in going up to outside of class too.

Professor Watkins is such a great instructor and makes sure to keeps his lectures interesting. I took D&C and there was a lot to get done each week but once you know the pattern and stay on top of it, its fairly easy. Syllabus seems intimidating at first but I would definitely take from Professor Watkins again.

Professor Watkins is an outstanding teacher! He creates really intriguing discussions and keeps things interesting. There is a fair amount of reading, but it's pretty engaging documents. Highly recommend taking foundations from him!

Professor Watkins was great. I highly recommend that you take Foundations from him. The workload was very reasonable and grading was fair. The quantity of reading is high, but as long as you do the reading and pay attention in class, there's nothing tricky about the quizzes or tests. Overall, it's a very insightful academic course.

Professor Watkins was great! Attendance was graded and there are mandatory reading responses for every day of class, but if you do it you get an A. All quizzes and tests are open note, so you'll have no problem with grades. He's very smart and knows a lot of history, and he is really respectful and takes time to answer your questions! A great guy!

Dr. Joe Price is such a fantastic teacher and I loved taking his class. He was VERY accessible outside class, takes student feedback seriously and is very personable. Didn't feel the textbook was necessary but PRACTICE IS!!! Test heavy class so practice, practice, practice and take advantage of the TA lab or this class will eat you alive!
Brother Price knows this is a tough class and does everything he can to help out. Enjoyed his lectures, and this class as a whole.

I loved Joe, but he did not teach the exam material that well. I never did any of the readings or TA reviews, and still succeeded with only the given study materials and quizzes. Super awesome lectures though, felt like a Tedtalk every morning.

Econ 110 is a beast of a class, but I loved the way Joe Price taught it. He explains topics very well, but you will have to put in time outside of class and probably at the TA lab if you want a good grade. Joe Price isn't afraid to share his opinions on occasion in class, and has thoughtful takes on the world. He clearly cares a lot about students.

Dr. Price is a very generous professor. He has a lot of built-in mercy in this class, and tries to help everyone. There are midterm reinforcements, a bunch of assignments dropped (including a midterm), and just overall a lot of help. Econ is a hard class but he helps you as much as he can. Take ECON 110 with Dr. Price.

Dr price is good. Econ is a hard class. Some material in lectures is unnecessary but most is interesting. One thing I will say is throughout the semester he was hyping up a curve. “You will be shocked with how merciful I am” only to change an A from 93 to 92 and A- from 90 to 89 so that was overhyped. Curve really only helped lower grade students.

Some things to note. He drops 1 of the midterms we take out of the 3. His lectures are always interesting and engaging. He articulates his thoughts so well and his beliefs sound weird at first, like we should have a tax for tall people, but his reasons are solid and valid so it is fun hearing him explain. The final is like 33 percent of the grade.

Amazing professor, he kept things very interesting during the lectures and explained things well. Econ 110 is extremely difficult regardless of who you take it from, but Dr. price builds the course well with lots of practice and help as well as forgiveness. Your lowest midterm and lowest assignment from every category is dropped.

Dr. Price is caring and knowledgeable about Economics. His class is very tough, and planning is the key. Plan to read the textbook, take quizzes multiple times, do midterm reinforcements, and go to the TA lab and reviews. This is a 4-credit class in disguise so treat it that way and you'll do good. If you want the A put in work. Good Luck!

I would not recommend taking this class from Joe Price. He tends to ramble about loosely related topics during the lectures, taking time away from practice problems and explaining things more in-depth. I just don't feel like I got anything out of his lectures. Honestly AI taught me everything I know for this class.

Econ 110 is a hard class, but Dr. Price teaches it incredibly. His lectures are interesting and relate to a lot of relevant real-world events. The class also has a lot of built-in mercy with a dropped midterm and curve. People don't like the difficulty of Econ, but if you actually take the time to learn the content well, it's extremely fulfilling.

Honestly this class is hard but made harder by the professor. The lectures are rambling for 75 min and truly acts like he doesn't know what he's talking about either. The TAs were great but lectures won't help understand anything. the textbook is better but the tests aren't really set up from the textbook. I would recommend taking from anyone else.

Professor Price teaches a hard class. You definitely need to put the work in, but it is very rewarding. His lectures go over a lot of material, but they are really interesting and explain lots of the concepts. the best way to prepare for exams in this class is to take the quizzes over and over.

I really enjoyed taking this class from him. His lectures were insightful and inspiring. That being said, the class is pretty clear cut. Most of your grade come from 3 midterms (lowest one gets dropped) and the final. You need to put in work outside of class to do well, so get into the habit of going to the TA lab and taking the practice quizzes.

Joe Price is the absolute GOAT. His lectures are fire and you wouldn't think you'd leave an econ lecture inspired, but you do. Prof. Price knows what's up.That being said, Econ is a HARD class. Even though he's a good teacher, you'll need to spend hours outside of class to fully understand the material. TAKE THIS CLASS IT'S WORTH IT

nice guy. has been teaching for 20 years. could explain simpler (surprising he still explains this bad sometimes given he's been teaching for 20 years). makes us do problems in class. suggestion to him: show HOW to do the problem before giving it to us by walking through a couple practice problems with us.

I'm having trouble verbalizing the hatred that I feel towards this 'professor' and frankly the entire economics department. Supposedly he went to Cornell for his Phd but you would never know it when taking his class. Class is designed for you to NOT succeed, the TAs admit it. Don't take ECON, ever.

I really struggled in this class and got no help from the professor. He is not approachable. The homework is not terribly difficult and you work with a group. The class is not set up for student success. Stay away from him.
Tough class but learned a lot

Dr. Price is a very sharp professor of economics and an exceptional person. He gives plenty of resources for you to learn if you are willing. Take good notes, go to the TA lab when you have questions, take the practice quizzes over and over, and watch the Econ w/ Adam videos. I cannot recommend Dr. Price and this class enough.

One of the best professors I've ever had! I think people only rate him low because it's a hard class they weren't ready for, which is mostly due to things outside his control. Lots of built in mercy with a midterm and several quizzes dropped, and he teaches with a great balance of clear concepts, real world applicability, and practice test problems
Dr Price is incredible! He gives a large test bank so you can study exactly the kind of material that will be on exams. He provides the tools for success. And he's just all around a great guy!

Class is incredibly difficult and Price does not explain the concepts well. He does have a lot of built in "mercy" where your lowest midterm is dropped. You can also make back some of the points. He also drops some of the attendances and quizzes. The text book is also useless. Pick someone else, or even better, AVOID THIS CLASS.

If you want your GPA to die, take this class. It's extremely difficult, lectures are a waste of time, and you basically have to teach yourself. So, if you enjoy pain, you'd love this class. The textbook is useless and expensive.
Love this guy.

Tests are 73% of the total grade and brutal, especially the final. I had an A the whole semester and I still got a C on the final after 12 straight hours of studying. The class itself is easy but the way questions are worded are confusing and multiple answers could be argued for most if the time. Tangents about social issues were common in lecture.

Definition of "skip class, won't pass." He goes FAST in lectures and the practice tests he puts on learning suite WILL NOT prepare you for the actual tests. A lot less mercy in 380 than 110 --- no dropped midterms. He rounded my grade to an A- from an 89.8. I think the difficulty was more the class than the professor.

Good professor, had his heart in the right place. Difficult class of 800ish students, so rely on TAs for help. Quizzes after lectures due 30 mins before the next lecture - tedious but good practice. Random 5 papers 2 on news 3 on the second book we had to buy. Class participation recorded for attendance. Grace built in with option to drop a midterm

Econ is a hard class, it is a miracle that I got a B. I heard the TA's say over and over in the lab that Price is harder than the other professors, mostly because he wont spend time in class showing us what well be tested on rather just the definitions so that's the best advice I can give take it from another professor or you'll do all the learning

Price was decent, and explained concepts fairly well, he would just go on tangents that didn't seem super relevant. Concepts can be confusing, but if you do the quizzes (unlimited attempts) and ask questions in the TA lab before exams you should be fine. However, the final is worth 33% of the grade, so make sure you study hard for it.

The course is very straight forward with lots of materials and practice problems. The "Econ with Adam" videos and practice exams are all that I did to study, and I got around 95% on all the exams. I even stopped going to class for the last month, and as long as I did the homework I was fine. Probably wouldn't recommend that though. Over-hated class

I don't understand the complaints about Professor Price. He's INCREDIBLY merciful, despite what others say. He drops 1 midterm, 1 essay, 3 quizzes, and 4 attendances, plus allows makeup on exams and curves the class. The quizzes are old test questions, and there's plenty of practice. You won't see this kind of help or mercy in most other classes.

PLEASE do not take this class unless you absolutely have to. This class is extremely difficult and we barely have things to do outside of class to prepare for exams, which make up the majority of our grade. Professor talks about "built in mercy" but the only mercy I've experienced is the mercy of God helping me to not act violently in this class.

My advice: go to class for attendance points, then watch econ w/ Adam and Dr. Azevedo's micro and macro playlists on YouTube to learn. Do every practice quiz and midterm. IT WILL HELP!! Lowest midterm dropped, midterm corrections if you get

Dr. Price is great! His class is honestly tough, but that's ECON 110 for ya. There is so much mercy built into the class that anyone willing to put enough time into it can get an A. He provides so much material for you to study and practically infinite practice problems, which come super in handy for the exams.

I think Prof Price is a nice guy, but his perception of "mercy" is skewed. He originally told us that we could miss 8 days of class and then at the end of the semester said that it's actually 4. Even if the syllabus says that students shouldn't be held accountable for the mistakes that he makes in setting up the course. Not fair or merciful.

Professor Price is just great, explains the concepts, and answers questions. It's hard to practice the concepts with only a 10-question quiz per lecture and no real homework. You need to put in the effort to be successful in this class, like doing the pre-readings and reflecting on the lectures (something I wish I did).

It's hard to review cause the class is just so hard and there were like 800+ kids in the class. He does well at teaching, he is so genuine, and is clearly so passionate about the subject. I think he could explain it a little more simplistically to us, but thats kinda what the TAs did too. Just put in the work, and you'll do fine.

Despite the poor reviews, Price is actually the goat. This class is difficult, but an A is attainable if you put in lots of study hours and make it a priority. I gave a 4 for quality just because I personally feel that he doesn't answer questions very well. I wish he could teach us economics like we were kids so we could actually understand lol.
Dr. Price is a nice guy and a great option for ECON 110. His class is so hard but I know that the other ECON 110 professors are also super hard.

Professor Price does give a lot of mercy with his grading which is nice, he drops quizzes, attendance, and even on test. However, it shows that he does not care about his students, only about his content. On LS we originally had 8 attendance quizzes dropped and then he went and changed it to 4, without any warning. The mercy is nice, but that's it!

Dr. Price loves Economics, and that passion can be felt in these lectures, I don't love economics, but Dr price showed me why one could love it. There is a fire for this material that very few other professors have. It was a great pleasure to know him, and even though the exams were pretty tricky, he was the best person to take Econ 110 from

Prof. Price is really kind and caring. You can tell he is passionate about econ. Sometimes he struggles breaking things down for those who are just learning these concepts. Just go to the TA test reviews and you will do just fine on the tests! Not that bad but it for sure takes some outside work, and dedication to do well.

Dr. Price is the best! There are easier professors to take Econ-380 from but he is still great! He cares about you so much and you can tell. He is a brilliant economist and his class would absolutely be beneficial to take. He skips allot of Algebra when teaching so just make sure you have that down!

Price doesn't teach what you actually need for the tests and it all falls to the students to learn most of it on their own or with TAs. For most of the semester up until the last month of class, he was teaching the materials for the quizzes after they had to be turned in, and, even then, he didn't teach us how to do most of the questions.

Economics is hard to wrap your head around, but there are a lot of willing and wonderful TAs. Dr. Price did a great job at providing examples to make hard concepts easier to understand. You'll definitely need to put in time and study, but it's possible to do well. Most of the class did well on each exam.

Horrible teacher. Avoid him at all costs. Take Platt. Classes are massive, 200+. TAs carry and are the only reason this class is doable. Take it from me, there are better things to do than waste time/money on this professor. Platt is awesome, go for him instead.

Dr. Price is easily one of the best professors I have had at BYU. I took his Econ 110 in the spring and loved it. He isn't just a good teacher, he is a good human. You can feel his sincerity and love for economics and the gospel. I would recommend that everyone take Econ 110 from Dr. Price. The success rate of our class was really high.

Not a good teacher. He explains the problems by throwing numbers in the air and expects you to understand them. We had another teacher come for one day, and it was 100X better. The TAs are the only reason his class is doable. Even the YouTube videos he recommended only explained half the solutions to the questions. Choose another teacher.

I learned nothing while in class. Everything I learned came from the TA videos. He also calls himself "merciful" but if you miss any classes, there is no empathy for any extraneous problems you have. The paradigm of this class expects you to focus 100% of your attention to it, despite it being just another general. Just take it in SLC.

I honestly learned more from the Econ with Adam YouTube videos made from a previous TA the year before than in class. I have to go research myself the content after the class since his teaching style is not visual, more talking through the concepts. It seems the TAs are willing to work with you but not the professor at times.

This professor actually didn't teach me anything about economics. Maybe someone who already knew most of this content would've succeeded in this class. But I had to spend hours outside of class, not studying, but simply reteaching myself all the content he was trying to teach. I would've died without the TAs. They should get paid, not him.

Professor Price's lectures made me excited to come to class every day, despite the 8:00 am start time. His research breaks were fascinating and I always understood the application for the math we were doing, which was super cool. The homework was pretty light but I would highly recommend studying intentionally for the quizzes.

Professor Price is legit the goat. He is super nice and explains everything super well, but sometimes goes off on tangents although they normally are pretty interesting. 3 midterms but your lowest is dropped and a final that is worth about 33% of your grade. Watching the Econ with Adam youtube videos will carry your grade. Take it from him for sure
If you are taking Econ 110 TAKE IT FROM Professor Price. He tries hard to make the content understandable and cares about your success as a student.

Price is a nice guy and does fascinating research, but everything I learned in this class was from the TAs (the lab is so underrated) and Khan Academy. Price just got totally off topic in every lecture and I often felt totally clueless on quizzes. Unless you're ready to teach yourself super tough material, take this from literally anyone else.

Attendance wasn't necessarily mandatory, but you'll want to go to class in order to do well; this class is hard by nature but Dr. Price is a phenomenal teacher. His teaching is fun, exciting, and interesting. Best economics professor I've had and one of my favorite professors. I took 110 and 380 from him and loved both.

Dr. Price was the best econ professor I could have had. He teaches the material simply and gives you lots of opportunities to succeed. You can take the quizzes unlimited times to really learn the material. This is a very hard class but if you read the textbook before the lectures and study hard you will succeed. Take econ from Dr. Price!

I highly recommend Dr. Price. Econ can be tough, but Dr. Price makes it enjoyable. His unlimited quiz attempts let you practice and learn from your mistakes and learn the material in preparation for the exams. He is very gracious when it comes to grades and isn't there to tank your GPA. You will need to work hard though to understand the material.

Dr. Price is incredible. He gives the keys to success for a hard class: reading the chapter before class, and then being in class to learn with other students makes success possible. He teaches engagingly and loves his students. The class has lectures with iClicker and then quizzes with unlimited attempts. TAs are great. Take Price!

Dr. Price is the most wholesome person I have ever met in my entire life. He is very passionate about economics and makes a very difficult class quite enjoyable.
