Professor Spencer is very knowledgable with the Book of Mormon. I was able to learn so much in this class and gain a deeper understanding. His lectures build upon each other so attend every class because otherwise you will be confused. His tests are open note and scripture but are difficult if you struggle with little details. Attend the reviews!

Professor Spencer is super knowledgeable about the Book of Mormon. Every lecture I learned something new and loved all of the new insights into the Book of Mormon. I would take this class again in order to really understand the complexity of his viewpoints of the book of mormon. Amazing class. TAKE IT!

Professor Spencer is an amazingly intelligent man. His knowledge of the Book of Mormon is beyond anything I imagined I'd be learning at BYU. His is the first religion class I've taken that added actual value to my testimony and understanding, and his activities are varied and sensible, if slightly difficult.

I just want everyone to know that Joseph Spencer absolutely changed my life and my view on the gospel and the Book of Mormon. I cannot emphasize how amazing his class was and I wish I could take it every semester for the rest of my life honestly. I should have recorded the lectures. YOU NEED TO TAKE IT.

Great professor and an incredible lecturer. I've read the BoM a number of times but I learned completely new things in his class about the Book of Mormon that have changed my testimony completely. So grateful for this class. The class isn't difficult, homework is very simple, and tests are open-note and open-scripture so not bad. Take this class!

Professor Spencer is amazing. His BoM class is focused on the true interpretation of scripture passages rather than application and he approaches it from a more academic-focused viewpoint. It can get confusing if you miss class, as the lectures build off each other, but he's a well-versed and entertaining lecturer. Would highly recommend his class.

Professor Spencer does an amazing job of introducing new ways of thinking about Book of Mormon scriptures. If you want to engage intellectually as well as spiritually about the words of the prophets in the Book of Mormon, take this class. Homework is simple for the most part and not too time consuming.

Professor Spencer does a great job of introducing new ways of thinking of Book of Mormon Scriptures. If you want to intellectually and spiritually engage with what the Book of Mormon prophets, take this class. Homework is fairly simple and usually not too time consuming. First 2 weeks are purely history of Book of Mormon people, but then dives deep

Wow, Dr. Spencer is incredible. He blows my mind every single lecture with his intellect and understanding of the Book of Mormon. What I have learned in this class has changed the way I understand the scriptures. The class is best for those who are already very familiar with the Book of Mormon, but not too much homework. This class is great!

Professor Spencer was an amazing professor, but the class setup was a little jumbled. It was sometimes hard to understand key points when he would just write notes/diagrams on the whiteboard and used no presentations. The tests and essay questions were pretty difficult. Great class but very intellectually focused...

Dr spencer is hardcore. He's very much a philosopher/scholar of the BOM, so it's a different perspective than I've ever considered. You have to go to lecture, that's what exams (and really everything else) is based on. I always feel like my brain is 10x bigger when I walk out of this class. exams aren't that hard and he actually responds to emails
I have nothing but good things to say about Professor Spencer -- he is accessible and friendly, his lectures are fascinating, and he knows the BOM better than anyone I know.
Professor Spencer is very informed and every class is full of ideas and concepts I'd never considered before. You can tell that he is passionate about the Book of Mormon and really knows his stuff.
Best religion professor I've ever taken. He's not only interested in teaching the material, but helping you find answers for yourself. He's done more for my testimony than any other teacher at BYU.

this is the second class I've taken from Dr. Spencer. He is absolutely brilliant & the most compelling lecturer. Since this was a 300 level class, there was a lot more expected of us compared to 275. Listening to Dr. Spencer is truly a privilege as he is one of the smartest, if not THE smartest, philosophers at BYU. It's not easy but it is worth it

I loved Professor Spencer. The only critique is that his tests were REALLY hard. I think he was amazing at lecturing. He was so fun to listen to because he is just so passionate about the Book Of Mormon. I wouldn't recommend though if you aren't fond of taking notes.

Dr. Spencer makes you have a crisis over how much you've missed in the Book of Mormon every single class. Absolutely brilliant lectures. Quite a quirky guy. Definitely take your reading seriously and take notes in class, but it's SO worth it to take from him.

Prof Spencer is serious about scripture and academics. I wouldn't say that he is arrogant, he is much more than that, but his confidence in himself and what he knows is what you will be expected to embrace. There is only one person who matters in his class. Buy into his way of interpreting scripture to get an A, I did and now I'm in recovery.

Every BYU student should take this class. I don't understand why people say this isn't a spiritual class. This class has kept me in the church and fostered a deep love of the Book of Mormon. Spirituality is not the absence of serious thought.

This man is really good at giving amazing lectures. He times them perfectly, and he really knows his stuff. Do not underestimate the tests, they are hardy, but he is willing to help you with what ever questions you have. He is a golden teacher:)

His tests are like playing a game of scripture chase. He has you read from more than just PoGP and expects you to know ridiculous details that are impossible to memorize. He expects you to know the text by heart. His lectures are extremely hard to follow and it never felt like clear answers were given. Only more questions asked and hypotheticals.

prof spencer is a very good teacher and knows his stuff. like he's a genius. the lectures are usually pretty interesting too but you don't really need to go to them for the exam since the exam multiple choice is just on scripture passages from that unit. pretty easy class just do all your assignments on time and actually read the readings

Dr. Spencer is by far my favorite religion professor. He greatly expanded my view of the Book of Mormon simply by making me *read* it as it wants to be read. He's a prominent BoM scholar himself, so many HW assignments involve reading academic articles, but I enjoyed that too. Tests are tough if you don't prepare or know what he wants you to write.

Take this class and you won't regret it! Readings + questions due before class, 15 minutes max. Midterms are half multiple choice, half short answer questions. He gives prompts beforehand + it's all open book. 1 assignment due each week also. Good mix of intellectual + spiritual stuff so you won't get bored ever! His lectures are amazing, loved it!

His class always blows my mind! If you want a new take on the gospel, he is the professor for you! His exams are a little tricky, but they are open note and book. There are many assignments, but they are pretty chill with the grading.

WARNING: NOT COVID FRIENDLY!!!! This class would be fine under normal circumstances - but if you are considering taking it during the COVID pandemic DO NOT TAKE! There is no way to zoom into class if you can't come due to feeling sick or being in quarantine. Only take this class if you are okay with hypothetical discussion without concrete answers.

Dr. Specer is incredibly intelligent, and he takes a new approach to the Book of Mormon. If you like to dissect scripture with a scholarly outlook, this is the class for you. Personally, I found the class hard to appreciate, so I would not take again, but I was not much of a challenge and I am glad I took it.

Joseph Spencer is a very good teacher and has AMAZING lectures. I loved every single one of them. The only thing is, its hard to get a 100% on exams and paragraph writing assignments. You go to class and take notes to get a decent grade on exams. SO MUCH HOMEWORK AND READING. Almost each exam covers 30+ chapters of reading. Open book and note test.

Good secular, analytical view. He focuses on literary devises to show new ways of understanding passages and addresses some difficult issues. Grade spread evenly over lots of assignments. One complaint: You MUST attend class b/c his understanding of a passage is what he wants you to write on tests. Take lots of notes and you'll do great!

This class gave me a new perspective on new insights on the Book of Mormon. He has daily quizzes due before class graded on participation and there are bigger weekly assignments that are easy and help you think differently. The tests are easy, you get the essay questions in advance, it's open scriptures/notes and there is a TA review10/10 take it

Has unique insights, but they're unimportant. Lectures are not on the test; only the reading. Assignments are due every class, but have sentence limits and cannot be made up despite any external circumstances. He's tedious in grading and his exams have no review to help you study. Lectures on zoom had the WORST audio quality. I would not recommend.

So I took Pearl of Great Price from Professor Spencer when he taught it for the first time and it was amazing. He comes from a philosophy background and so there was a lot of abstract thinking and complex readings but he helped me understand the Pearl of Great Price in a whole new way. Not the most spiritual or easy religion class but really good.

Great lectures. Small reading assessments before each class. The only reading assignments were a few chapters from the Book of Mormon from each class. Every few weeks there is a larger assignment that takes an hour or so. Tests were open book and over the lecture material, but timed. Great class, great professor, and would take again!

Genuinely one of the best religion classes I have ever taken. He majored in philosophy so hes got a lot of interesting takes, but has so well versed in scripture. Theres readings every class period and a small thing due every Saturday, but super easy. Not super spiritual, but intellectually enlarging enough that it strengthened my testimony. 11/10

REALLY good lectures and lays out the Book of Mormon clearly but in a new light. There are weekly assignments, if you follow the instructions you'll get an A. Three exams: open book with 1-2 essay questions that you know beforehand. Definitely go to the exam reviews - they pretty much write the essay questions for you.
I don't often review professors but Dr. Spencer was especially unclear about his class expectations. This class is not difficult but I would avoid this professor. Good luck!

I love Dr. Spencer! He is seriously one of the most inspirational people ever. I felt the Spirit so strongly during every one of his lectures! He was also super accommodating to me during the semester. Super interesting and funny guy! He made me think about the Book of Mormon in a completely new way.

Professor Spencer is so so amazing! He is SO knowledgeable and is great to work with one on one if you have personal or academic questions. The class definitely leans more scholarly which makes it more interesting than other BOM classes. If you want to read the BOM in a new way and are okay with coming up with your own application, he's the BEST!!

Take this class!! It is such a good class from an amazing professor. Professor Spencer has amazing lectures. There are weekly assignments due on Saturdays and a short reading assignment before each class. The tests are online (open-book, open note) and have review sessions that if you attend, you are guaranteed a high score.

Great class! Professor Spencer has really interesting lectures that have a good balance between spiritual and academic. Class is pretty easy as long as you stay on top of the hw. Exams are on LS. Highly recommend.

Dr. Spencer is an amazing professor who changed the way I read the Book of Mormon. His lectures are direct, fast-paced, and enlightening. I gained an understanding for the sequence of the Book of Mormon without intentional memorization. His class increased my testimony and gave me an excitement for gospel study.

If you are taking this class to learn about the Book of Mormon then there is no better teacher. I would take this class every semester if I could. If you don't think you learn from this class its cause youre not listening. Even passively going to class will help you learn a ton.

Some feel like his class isn't "spiritual," but to me it definitely was; Dr. Spencer helped me discover hidden patterns and amazing principles in the Book of Mormon, the gospel, and life. The assignments require you to think deeply, but aren't overwhelming. The Learning Suite tests are fine if you attend every lecture and take thorough notes.

Joseph Spencer knows his stuff. Every lecture opened my eyes to something new in the Book of Mormon I'd never considered before. I have such a deeper understanding and appreciation for this book after taking this class. 100% recommend. there are 3 online tests, each one having a multiple choice and essay part. Easy if you attend lectures and read!

This class was SO FUN. He has a profound understanding of the BOM due to years of research. His lectures are very engaging and made me think. He studied philosophy, so many of his presentations are influenced by those ideas. He is not afraid to address hard questions and is very open to student's questions, even when they seem to not agree. Amazing

He was very intelligent and his lectures were filled with different perspectives on the Book of Mormon. He also really cared about his students and liked to have discussions with us. That being said, it isn't a very spiritual class. Take this class if you like philosophy and structure of the Book of Mormon, not if you want to be spiritually fed.

He's a good guy but to be completely honest, I have never taken such a boring religion class. Super easy to get an A, but it got to the point where I just stopped going cause I didn't get anything out of class (still an easy A after not going). His assignments are graded easily but they are pointless. Class is approached from a scholar perspective

Relatively easy A. A few chapters of reading due each day of class, along with a few questions about that reading. Weekly responses to lengthier readings. Tests are online and fairly easy. Dr. Spencer is nice and he knows a ton about the BOM. He takes a more literary approach, but I've learned a lot about spiritual subjects as well.

Joseph was a really educated professor with lots of knowledge behind the Book of Mormon. He definitely had a different approach to it, in more of a philosophical way (his degree) than a spiritual. He was great and I learned a lot, but if you want spirituality then he is not your guy.

LIFE-CHANGING. Take from Dr. Spencer if you want to have your mind blown every lecture and learn how to REALLY read and think about scripture. His perspectives on the BofM transformed my understanding of the gospel and my testimony, which had been struggling going into the class. Rare combination of an easy A and a remarkable professor/class.

I have taken six religion courses at BYU and this was my favorite. Dr. Spencer does not entertain you with funny stories or jokes, like many great religion professors but nevertheless creates an engaging and SUPREMELY intellectually-stimulating class. He is passionate about the material and his daily and weekly assignments are the best of any class

Brother Spencer is super great. He tells you exactly what you need in assignments to do well. All of the tests are on LearningSuite and open book/note. They're timed and sorta difficult because they're only on the reading, but not worth too much of your grade. Free Response portion of exams are based on lectures, which are super cool.

Professor Spencer is one of the most amazing teachers I have ever had! In my REL A 275 class, he taught amazing lectures and really focused on teaching his students new things about the Book of Mormon. Very approachable and easy to talk to. Also, grades are easy as long as you put effort into it.

I loved Prof. Spencer's class on the Book of Mormon. I felt like I gained invaluable insights about the text that I hadn't considered before. His class wasn't homework heavy, and tests/quizzes were rather easy. Some of the assignments he gave us were somewhat time-consuming, but if you followed all the grading criteria, he always gave out As.

The BEST religion professor for Book of Mormon 1 or 2. All the tests are on Learning Suite. Multiple choice and an essay portion. He gives you possible essay questions ahead of time that could show up. He will even pre check your answers before the test. A book report and a few random assignments as well as daily reading questions. Way easy.

This is the second class I've taken from him. He's a brilliant man. His whole philosophy is to ask students to read the Book of Mormon with fresh eyes. He's not going to get mushy and spiritual, but if you want to REALLY know the scriptures, take his class. Two midterms and a final (open book), book report, and biweekly "expanding exercises."

Such an amazing, dedicated man. His insights and way of thinking really open you up to a new perspective of Mormonism and the Book of Mormon. Really engaging and funny. Assignments all increase learning and help you come to understand what resources or opinions are out there. This religion class changed my testimony and my life. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Professor Spencer is doing incredible research and teaches from what is current in research pertaining to religion and the Book of Mormon. The PhD in Philosophy makes him so awesome. This guy knows his stuff. His classes are inspiring and he is intentional in nearly every word in his lectures. Would take for every class if possible.

Dr Spencer is super passionate about the book of mormon and he know's it very well. If you are super set in your seminary traditions and views on the book of mormon, look for another teacher, Dr Spencer challenges many of these traditional viewpoints. I learned more from Dr Spencer in a semester than I did in all of my previous BoM study

Dr Spencer is pretty much the best religion teacher on campus. He dives into the Book of Mormon's teachings from both a spiritual and an intellectual standpoint. Since he's a doctor of philosophy, you get a lot of really cool insights that can really enrich your understanding of the book. He's not afraid to challenge your views and call for change.

Dr. Spencer is incredible. He has such a fresh view of the Book of Mormon and isn't afraid to talk about sensitive or confusing topics. Three tests: open book/neighbor/TA/professor, online, multiple choice (based on reading) and a short answer (based on lecture). Couple chapters to read a week. Some writing assignments that are pretty easy.

Brother Spencer is a nice guy, but his lectures are very hard to get through and not spiritual at all. I think he bore his testimony once or twice and I never felt the spirit. The tests are online and open note but they are so hard because you have nothing to go off of to study. No powerpoints and no study guides. Just his lectures.

Dr. Spencers class is really enjoyable. The tests are on LearningSuite, and they are really easy, especially if you attend a review session beforehand. The reading is required, and theres pretty much a weekly writing assignment in addition to questions about each reading. His class is definitely spiritually enriching.

Wow,Professor Spencer is truly amazing. He has a unique and fresh take on the Book of Mormon developed through diligent personal study and reading the book. He does have some interesting ideas, so still stick with what you know, but if you have an open mind you can learn so much and have your knowledge of this amazing book grow exponentially

Dr. Spencer is so knowledgeable! Be prepared to take lots of notes during lecture time, or it will be difficult for you to get a good grade on tests. He has a very unique teaching style, so being open-minded every class will help you a ton (a.k.a you either get bored in your seat or get uplifted). Do your assignments well and get an EASY A!!!

Majority of class was new freshman and he sort of exploits that. His lectures are all about what he knows. He does have great insights but if you don't like people bragging about their own exploits and how knowledgeable they are, this class is a painful nightmare. Not a good class if your struggling with your testimony.

Professor Spencer has great insights into the Book of Mormon. I really liked his grading policy. The tests were all online which was extremely nice. I did not enjoy his lectures very much, his teaching style was different from what I was used to. The test are based a lot on the outside readings so make sure you read or you won't do well on the test

Very straightforward class, as long as you attend class and do daily questions it will be an easy A. The lectures are very unique and get you thinking about the Book of Mormon in a really interesting way. Make sure to go to review sessions where he lays out exactly what to say on essay questions piece by piece.

His approach to the Book of Mormon is different . Focus is Abrahamic covanents, Isaiah,typology. Approach is very interesting.  . Grading: Daily Questions on reading,  tri-weekly page essays, 3 midterms & Final with 2 paragraph essays. His prompts ask for alot but only give you limited space to write. That would be his downside.

Best class I have yet taken at BYU. He's a doctor of Philosophy and so he addresses the text with great depth and great care. Very interesting lectures. Helps you ask questions and get at what the text is really saying. Getting an A wasn't too hard, just read a book over the semester and do some short essays.

Brother Spencer is a WONDERFUL professor. His lectures really get you thinking and his assignments are very straightforward. He's willing to help you in any way if you approach him after class or visit him during his office hours. Take good notes in his lectures and all of his exams will be an easy A! Always an enjoyable, enriching religion class!

This is the best professor I have had. His lectures are incredible--he is insightful and genuinely willing to learn about the Book of Mormon. He is not stuck in the traditional narrative of the Book of Mormon usually presented in Mormonism. His background studying philosophy brings a critical lens to the scriptures that is amazing. Take this class!

Dr. Spencer has been the best religion professor I've had at BYU. He challenges the norms of LDS culture when it comes to the text of the Book of Mormon and invites students to discover simple truths for themselves. Don't be intimidated by the amount of homework and readings, its not bad at all! Really great guy who's willing to help if you ask.
Wasn't impressed with his opinions. He's a tad pompous.

Dr. Spencer has good insights on the Book of Mormon.  There aren't a lot of graded assignments so make sure you do all of them.  Tests are kind of tricky, mostly because of the time limit, but if you study a good amount they're not that bad.  I would recommend taking notes on your computer, it makes it easier and you can use them on the test.

He had really interesting ideas and it was an overall easy class except for the midterm/final. Those tests are very difficult and timed on learning suite. It was really hard to study for the multiple choice part, but the essay portion is easy if you go to the TA review. Test is open BOM and note but make sure to know what happens in every chapter.

Bro. Spencer will blow your mind with some of his opinions on the Book of Mormon's structure and meaning. Not the most spiritually uplifting class though. No attendance required, but if you miss his lectures you won't know how to answer the essay questions on the test. Not too hard, but very detail-oriented.

He has an interesting take on the Book of Mormon that forces you to see it in a different light, but be sure to take copious notes. His exams are reasonable, open-note and open-book, as long as you know what you read; plus there's a short assignment every week plus a longer one every two weeks. He's also very accommodating and intelligent.

Doctor Spencer clearly knows a lot about the Book of Mormon. The way he talks about it is almost revolutionary. I mean, I feel like in thirty years we're all going to look at the Book of Mormon and talk about it the way he does. It's really incredible to understand the book how he does. The workload isn't too much, I would for sure recommend him.

Professor Spencer offered so many new insights to the Book of Mormon that none of us freshmen would ever have considered. He taught about different perspectives and new views to the stories we thought we knew, and he bore testimony of the powerful truths in the book. I left every class feeling inspired and enlightened.

Professor Spencer approaches the Book of Mormon in a philosophical stance while bringing the spirit to every class. His teaching style can only be compared to that of John Green. The class is not hard, as long as you keep up with readings and assignments. I look forward to going to his class every day. Take Book of Mormon from him!

I have very mixed feelings about this class. He's a smart guy, but he comes at the Book of Mormon in a more intellectual way than a spiritual way. I walk out of class feeling like a terrible person most of the time. He's a philosophy guy, so he teaches more of his insights than doctrine. Very confusing class but I learned a lot.

hisblectures are  super off the wall.  If you want a great class on possible theories of the nephites related to budhism(no joke, it's a book he wrote and it's required reading) and philosophy of the  BofM, great class...  Most of his lectures revolve around "if the 1st presidency knew this or read my book, they would be better prophets".
Insightful, if you don't learn anything new in the class, then you definitely were not paying attention

Brother Spencer is a good teacher, however he does not give a study guide for his tests so you're on your own to figure out how to study for his tests which are really hard unless you know the book of mormon really really well. He has his own interpretations for symbolism in the book of mormon which can be hard to understand at times.

For the first week or two he acted really weird. He tries to come at the Book of Mormon from such a weird angle he seems crazy, but after a little bit you'll get what he's saying. He expects a lot out of you but there's only so much you can expect in a religion class. Assigns a decent amount of homework and tests are few but not easy.

He made me look forward to his lectures! He knows SO MUCH and has so many unique insights about the Book of Mormon. He teaches in a way that you can decide for yourself rather than feeling as if he is pressuring you to agree with him. His tests were super easy if you go to class and pay attention. I'd take this class from him 10 times out of 10!!

Brother Spencer has actually made a difference in my life! I have changed some of my habits and feel as though I am a better person because of it. His tests aren't too hard, he provides a great study guide. He grades your two papers somewhat rigorously. Come to class because he shares things in class that is on the test. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!

He has unique knowledge on the Book of Mormon, some of it is very interesting. If you show up to class and listen easy A, a lot of points are based on reading and attendance. You get out of it what you put into it. If you want it to be interesting listen and think about what he is saying.

Awesome professor, it was refreshing to have a teacher who both knows the material backwards and forwards, and at the same time knows just as much about teaching. He teaches his take on the scriptures, and yet all the while makes it very clear that while you can take it or leave it, what he's trying to teach is a deeper approach to the text

I have mixed feelings about Dr. Spencer.  He is one of those teachers that teaches his opinion about the Book of Mormon more than the doctrine.  I definitely learned a lot from him and look at The Book of Mormon in a new way, but I didn't agree with some things he taught.  Super nice! But I would take from someone else.

This is one of the best religion classes at the University. Expect to spend a lot of time reading if you take it, but you will certainly learn a lot. He will always respond to questions quickly and be ready to clarify anything if you ask.

So if you're looking for an easy 'A,' take this class... most religion classes at BYU are pretty easy, however, and you could probably get more out of another class. The lectures are super boring and confusing, and he has some pretty weird views about the Book of Mormon. Spiritual enlightenment and general interest in this class are minimal.

Brother Spencer is great. His class has taught me to be able to examine the Book of Mormon by using critical-thinking skills. He focuses solely on the text of the Book of Mormon and not what modern-day prophets say about it. Make sure you pay attention and take good notes during his classes because his exams are based on the ideas we cover in class

Dr. Spencer gave fantastic lectures consistently that challenged everything I thought I know about the Book of Mormon, and I loved every second of it. As long as you read the assigned chapters before coming to class, he teaches what will be on the (2) exams in class. There were two papers assigned, but they are short and specific. Take this class!
Brilliant teacher. loved his class. Not many grades so if you don't do your work you'll suffer but what I learned was far more important from my grade.

Professor Spencer is amazing. I wish I could take all my religion classes from him. He's eyeonpening and a true intellectual. He can be slightly eccentric at times, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. I would reccommend him to anyone and everyone. Attending lectures and taking good notes are a must, but his style of teaching and testing is easy

Dr. Spencer is absolutely mind blowing. He makes you see the Book of Mormon in a way you never had before. He shares and tests you on his own ideas, so pay close attention in lectures. However, there are almost no assignments and he grades papers very easily. Completely different than seminary and I would not have wanted to learn from anyone else!

Bro. Spencer is amazing! His lectures blew my mind every single day in class. His class is not super difficult; just do the reading on time, come to class, two short papers (one on a book you have to read) and a midterm and final. Seriously not that bad. He's very kind and always willing to discuss something with you after class. Take from Spencer!

This class was fine; Professor Lemonte is a good professor but the TAs grade everything, so it really depends on that. Also, a heads up, that if you're taking this course for physical science, you need another class to cover that credit. I took this as a freshman who didn't understand BYU generals, and that part was not clear online.
He's so funny, super great teacher and really nice!
Dr. Price is awesome. This is a hard class, be prepared to treat it as a full-time job if you want an A. Content is very interesting, very useful, but mastery of these concepts takes work.
Simple, awesome class

Joshua Price was a fantastic professor. I would absolutely take him again. The class itself is very difficult but Professor Price makes it very straight forward and if you are willing to study hard and do all of the work you'll be okay. Lots of reading!
Cool professor but the class is tough, so lock in. Go to the TA Labs and study there. Visit his office hours at least once.

As a student that got an A, I would not take this class from him. He's a nice guy and entertaining lectures. However he teaches you like you're a freshman in high school. After ever class you will have to basically relearn everything by yourself, since it will not be even close to adequate. Extremely frustrating also since attendance is required.
Ignore the bad reviews, if you go to class and make sure you do the homework you will be just fine. If you want to go on your computer or phone you probably shouldn't be taking econ 110 anyway.

Professor Price is a great professor. Very entertaining and engaging lectures, and he cares a lot about every student and is more than willing to give extra help when needed. Pretty funny guy, too. With that being said, keep in mind that ECON 110 is a TOUGH class and requires lots of work outside of class to do well.
He was one of the best professors I've had. Class content was difficult, but he did good at breaking it down for us.

If you are not an economic, business, or finance major/minor, do not take this class. You are busy enough with your classes. In his syllabus, he says that you need 2 hours per credit on a course and holds you to it. Super clear when I say easy in the beginning and once you miss 1 or 2 lectures you're screwed. Not a bad professor, not great neither.
The professor is chill and class is easy, though it has more homework than expected for a one-credit course.

I think a lot of the other reviews on Price are unfair. The class was hard, but I enjoyed Price as a professor. His sarcasm added some enjoyment out of an 8 AM class. There were 3 midterms and 1 final. They were hard but I never felt like Price and the TAs were trying to 'get' you. If you do the work and spend the time on the class, you'll do well.

Honestly I felt like I didnt learn very much at all from the lectures, 99% of the learning is independent and just doing the reviews. When I went to a TA lab, even they were getting questions wrong. 73% of your grade is just midterms and a final. The average one a midterm was 69% and the final's average was like 70%

Put in the work, and you'll get a good grade. Expect to spend more time on this than on other 3 credit courses. 73% of your grade is exams: 3 midterms and a final, 1 midterm gets dropped. If you're not understanding something, go to the TAs asap. Don't waste time not understanding something. Practice quizzes are basically exactly like the exams.

Professor Price, still teaches like everyone is a high schooler. He doesn't allow phones or laptops when we're all paying to take his class. His exams are purposefully misleading. The lectures, Quizzes, and reading never really line up well so you're stuck not knowing the best resources for any of the test material.

I see that there are a few bad reviews for the class; I wouldn't listen to them. From what I can tell, his class is significantly easier than other Econ 110 professors. His lectures are straightforward, and tests are based on past homework grades, so if you drill the homework, you'll be fine. Very kind professor, use office hours.

Take this class from someone else. He pokes fun at students for asking questions. He is more concerned about cracking jokes than actually teaching. Lectures were largely him trying to be funny or selling the Econ major to freshmen. Lectures do not reflect quizzes or exams at all. I learned the majority of the the content outside of class on my own.

Great guy, tries to be funny. Not a good teacher for Econ 110 though. He is too concerned about giving out baseball cards and making jokes rather than teaching the concepts. Extremely hard to follow, I wouldn't go to class but it's required. Does he know his stuff? Maybe. Know how to teach beginners? Nope IMO. Take the class from someone else.

Covers economic fundamentals but lacks organization, with extreme level testing of understanding said to reflect real-world demands (In a 110). Most learning occurs independently due to lack of deeper level teaching. Commonly viewed as a weeder course though often required as a GE, it feels more like academic endurance training than an intro class.
Hes trying his best guys

Professor Price is not great at lecturing. Lectures feel like you're being yelled at and content in lectures is not very helpful compared to the long, dry textbook. The exams are designed to trick you and make you fail. Essentially it feels as if you are being waterboarded with work and content and then failed after weeks of studying.

He's a great guy but not a great teacher. He skips over key concepts that are confusing and leaves you lost. He also allows his TA's to make the test questions and they make trick questions (One of the TA's told me they do this) The tests don't feel like its to test your knowledge but to trick you in ways that don't apply.

Liked him at first—nice and engaging—but as the semester went on, the class got harder to succeed in. He added pop quizzes on readings, which felt unfair since I learn better through lectures. Also had a lot of trick questions and pick the best answer. Nice guy, but not a great professor. Use TAs and YouTube—don't rely only on class.

He's a good guy and funny, so lectures are entertaining, but he's a very bad teacher. He skips key material and doesn't explain concepts clearly. I had to rely on YouTube, ChatGPT, and TAs to actually learn. We even had midterms before covering the chapters. Overall, not an enjoyable experience. Good guy just not good at teaching itself. At all.

Dr Price is high energy and engaging but did tend to be quite sarcastic in lecture (in a jovial manner) which really turned me off from asking questions. As a teacher he honestly was poor. He rarely gave a thorough and in depth explanations and I felt he quite literally skimmed the surface on all the material. Works for tests I guess...

I loved having Price as a professor! Class was fun even for an 8am and he taught very clearly. The homework was very doable and you got extra credit for doing it in groups so I never got overwhelmed. We had a data project due at the end of the semester that I was worried about but it ended up being very doable and wasn't stressful at all.

Lectures were fantastic. I enjoyed every day that I went to this class. It was not terribly difficult, stay on top of the homework and understand what you are doing and you will be fine. He is pretty funny, and makes sure that everyone understands what is going on. Exams are similar to the practice exams, do those and you'll do fine.

you're fine if you just read the textbook but Price's lectures make the material so much more clear, interesting, fun, and applicable to everyday and church life. the grade you get will be the effort you put in!

Price gave really good lectures and generated great discussions with a big class. He also has a very sarcastic sense of humor which I liked. However, I really struggled with the tests even though I felt like I knew the material pretty well. Three tests make up 70% of the grade so they're do or die. Go to the TA review sessions, they help a ton.

Prof Price is an adjunct for spring/summer. He teaches economics like it's his calling. I took this class from Kearl and did horrible because I didn't understand the material. Professor Price helps you understand the material while still including humor. His lecture on dating and econ was the best ;)

Great class and great professor. Helps you understand the fundamentals of Isaiah, which helps you appreciate what Nephi talks about in the first half of the Book of Mormon. If you appreciate history intertwined with spirituality, then take the course. The tests are not too bad; he is also available to meet if you need help with them.
A bit harder than most religions where the tests can throw you off if you do not know one exact thing he said in class so prepare for that There's easier Rel profs
Had him for UNIV. Did not like the class at all, but he was a good teacher and made it tolerable. Allowed adjustments on some assignments I couldn't complete and was nice.

took him for Univ, wasn't hard at all but there is reading and a discussion before every class. Wasn't too much to do but there's probably better profs for this. Kinda boring but he's very nice and caring

Prof. Sears made this difficult course much more manageable. His lessons were engaging and he provided great study resources like quizzes and guides. unstuck ai also helped me prepare efficiently. Overall, a challenging but rewarding class.

I took REL395A. The tests are really easy, all pretty much verbatim from reading guides and topics in class. His discussion of the Fall of Adam and Eve changed my life. It was full of the Spirit and gave me a better mindset on how to approach hard times. He is a good man and has a good testimony of the Book of Mormon and scriptures.

literally the easiest class ever. you will get out of it what you put in it spiritually, but if you do the bare minimum, you will get an A. he believes in no surprises, so he gives a study guide for exams and half the questions are copy and paste homework questions. super knowledgable guy, good class.

I took the first half of the Book of Mormon class from him. He's a super nice guy, and there are short reading assignments before each class, but the classes ended up only being about Isaiah and ancient Israelite stories, and the tests were basically all Isaiah questions too. The class was supposed to get to Alma 30, but we barely got to Mosiah.

I gained so many new Book of Mormon insights from Brother Sears, especially the Isaiah chapters. He explains things clearly, grading is easy, the exams are never a surprise (I got 100% on all of the tests). You only have to write one paper, the workload isn't super heavy, though I spent more time on homework because I actually enjoyed the reading.

Bro. Sears is the best! His lectures were both spiritual and informational and I left every single class learning something new that changed my perspective entirely. He is able to explain complicated topics in a simple way. If you can any of his classes please do!! He also understands that its a 2 credit class so the workload is manageable.

I have nothing against Bro Sears, he is a kind soul and a good guy. However, his classes were the dullest and most uninspiring things I have ever been to. I am a front row type of guy and I try to stay super engaged but I fell asleep 5 times in this class. If you really like facts and the history of stuff great. Not spiritually uplifting tho.

Writings of Isaiah was quite an easy class, in spite of the material. He shows you all the possible questions for tests. There are a lot of readings outside of class, around 2 hours for each class, but they are not overly burdensome.

The professor is a really nice guy and he's a great teacher but the class itself is kinda hard. You have to really pay attention to understand and do well on the tests. I feel like he worries more about the test and checking off all the boxes rather than spiritually strengthening.

If you are going to take a Book of Mormon class at BYU, please, please, take it from Brother Sears. Every single lecture feels just a little bit life changing. Brother Sears is super smart, and the spirit in each class is nearly tangible. Yes, there are some readings, but they are incredibly inspiring and will pretty much ensure an A on the tests.

I always felt the spirit when I was in class. Brother Sears is just a genuinely great guy. There's a lot of reading for hw, but it's church stuff so it's uplifting. He always promises that there are no surprises on the tests, and he holds to that promise. He responds super fast to emails and always offers to meet with students outside of class

You read a lot in this class but his biggest motto is "no surprises on the test" and so he will always tell you what you need to know before you take it. He never puts obscure details on tests that were never even talked about in class.

There are four tests. If you're doing the study guides with the readings assigned, the tests are super easy. They are literally the exact questions word for word. He is super smart, fair, and willing to answer questions/help whenever. He is the best teacher to take when deciphering Isaiah or any Old Testament in the BOM. Overall, awesome teacher!

I was not a fan of his teaching. I took Christ and His everlasting gospel from him and not once did he expound or teach from the Book of Mormon. I was really upset when we learned about the atonement and he chose to teach us from early Christian scholars instead of our revealed scriptures. Teaching was by the power of the intellect not the spirit.

I LOVED THIS CLASS! Easy A and I learned and grew so much. Tests were a piece of cake, and reading assignments were easy and interesting. My knowledge and faith grew, and I have a deeper and more personal understanding of who Heavenly Father and Jesus are, and have a much more meaningful relationship with Them. 100/10 recommend taking this class!!!

If you're looking for an easy religion class I would not recommend Writings of Isaiah. Tons of reading and memorization for the tests! Interesting and I learned a lot but by far the most difficult religion class I've taken at BYU!

Brother Sears is the PERFECT balance of being spiritual but the class not being too hard. I still grew spiritually and the class wasn't too stressful. The tests were clear and there weren't surprises. You have to memorize a scripture for each of the 4 tests but it isn't too hard. Take him!
The best religion class I have taken at BYU. Harder than some religion classes I have taken, but not bad at all. The first two weeks have a lot of reading, but after that it cools down.

Professor Sears is a fantastic teacher and he cares a lot about the subject that he teaches and he is on the side of the students. There are no essays in this class which was really nice because most Christ and His everlasting Gospel courses do have essays. There is a reasonable amount of homework.

Brother Sears completely changed my opinion of Isaiah and made it understandable. He was so kind and caring and was great about answering tough questions. We had a small paper, five small tests that were super easy with a bit of studying, and a mostly self-graded final project. I left class every day feeling uplifted. Take his class if you can!

Brother Sears was amazing for Writings of Isaiah. He really knows his stuff, and his lectures are really interesting. He closes every lecture with a brief testimony, which left me feeling uplifted after every class. There are five small tests, but they are easy. Homework can be long sometimes, but it isn't difficult. Absolutely recommend his class!
This guy is such a hand talker and I find it hilarious. Good class though.

Prof. Sears would be a great professor for an Old Testament class. His book of Mormon class felt like a history class. If that's your vibe, great. I was not impressed and wished I had a more spiritually uplifting experience rather than an experience full of ancient facts. He also spends A LOT of time on the Isaiah chapters of 2 Nephi so buckle up.

Sears is awesome! He is super knowledgable and I loved his lectures, I felt like I learned a lot. As long as you stay on track with the reading quizzes and assignments (which isn't hard), you will succeed.

I loved taking this class from Bro Sears! He is extremely knowledgable about the scriptures, and can answer almost any question in regards to ancient texts. This made his lectures different from anything I'd heard before. He is also very kind, inclusive, and cares about the success of his students. He will prep you for the tests! Highly recommend!

This class was great! Professor Sears gives very interesting lectures and is super accessible. Everything in his class was super clear, including grading criteria, tests, and lectures. If you do the readings and pay attention in class, I don't see how you could fail. I would highly recommend if you still need religion credit!
Very nice guy. Very willing to accommodate. Passing is quite doable. He just doesnt do it for me. If youre into The Old Testament and Isaiah, this is your guy.

I loved his lectures and the spirit he brings to the class, it made my day. make sure you go to class because it is part of the grade. I would say though if you have a heavy schedule I would avoid him because he has a crazy amount of reading, which I had to often skim because I had other homework I had to get done, but other than that he is great.

Attendance is part of the grade. Do the readings and pay attention and exams are easy. No papers to write, but lots of reading. He's funny and easy to approach. He's great at explaining things. He's a very fair and easy grader. He's focused on building testimonies and doesn't want his class to stress us out (unlike some religion professors).

Professor Sears is a good guy. I can tell he genuinely loves what he is teaching. The class talks a lot about history and context rather than doctrine, which isn't for me, but some may find it more interesting. Regardless, I learned a lot. If you do the work, the tests aren't bad, but they're half lecture based-half reading, so be prepared.
Professor Sears is like that one seminary teacher that was your favorite. Pre-class readings take some time but they are really interesting. He is good at answering insightful questions in class.

For a Book of Mormon class it should have been an Old Testament history class. Prof. has 3 degrees in Old Testament so a LOT of focus on Isaiah chapters and the history behind it. Memorization of 3 Old Testament scriptures is tested on. Reading quizzes every class and are not open note. Tests are 1/2 reading 1/2 comprehensive lecture material.

Bro. Sears was a favorite this semester. I took so much out of his lectures and assignments that they didn't really feel like work. If you're looking for a religion teacher that's open-minded and considerate of all situations, this is your guy. Seriously changed my life and really helped grow my testimony. Take this class!
Just amazing at explaining the scriptures. The exams are kinda difficult but it is worth it. Other than exams nothing else is hard. He is really good at explaining the book of Isaiah.

Great professor! He is open-minded and definitely makes you feel safe and respected in his class. His lectures are easy to follow and the weekly assignments/reading is decently easy. Tests are not hard. Would totally take his class again! He understands that not everyone is LDS/has the same knowledge of the scriptures, so he accommodates to that.

Such a great professor! He is so kind and funny. I took it from him blended. The information he gave was stuff normally not talked about in studying the Book of Mormon, which was great! There are lots of exams but they are very easy and that allows them to each have less of an impact on your grade. He gives the reading quiz questions beforehand.

Brother Sears perfectly balances the spirit with academia. He goes on Rate My Professor to figure out what to avoid and adjusts accordingly. He also honors UAC accommodations which is a rarity amongst Religion Professors. He's the only professor I've willingly signed up for twice.

THE IDEAL RELIGION PROFESSOR. Spiritually uplifting, inclusive of people of all backgrounds, fun, passionate, and inspirational. Class isn't too hard but you should take him simply because he is incredibly knowledgeable about the bible. If you want a class that can shape your perspective of the gospel THIS IS IT.

I learned so much from Bro. Sears this semester. Might very well by my favorite prof I've ever had. My outlook on so much about the scriptures was changed, especially with understanding textual and translational history of the New Testament. His classes are both very spiritual and more academic than any other religion class I've taken. 10/10.

Possibly my favorite professor I've had, regardless of discipline. I read the Book of Mormon (and my other scriptures) in a completely different way and feel like I understand them a lot better from an academic perspective. This class was stellar missionary preparation. He really knows his stuff, and the class is legitimately college-level learning

Everything was pretty straightforward, but the tests covered a lot of material so be ready to put a good amount of time in if you want an a on the tests. Besides that, decent class although I might look for a different professor if I was going to take it again.

Pretty easy class for the Book of Mormon requirement. Two reading quizzes a week that are easy if you fill out the reading questions beforehand. Tests weren't too difficult if you keep up on the reading and go to class. Once a week you have to complete an exegetical exercise which is pretty straight forward as well.

Overall, Brother Sears is a great guy and although nerdy, he really knows his stuff and engages the class. Attendance is mandatory; however, I am not one who likes to read out loud and he would often have everyone read row by row, so I would end up dipping out early. Exams are really easy!

Professor Sears is AMAZING!! He's kind, funny, and genuinely wants all of his students to succeed. He includes questions from the reading checks on his tests, so you already know what's coming. If you're taking this class, take it from him! He is INCREDIBLE!

This is one of the more inclusive religion classes I've taken (despite COVID) and I would definitely recommend Sears. The class isn't too hard and the lectures are interesting. Exams always felt like they came out of nowhere but they aren't too bad as long as you pay attention in class. The reviews before the tests are super useful too.

Everything he has done has built me and my classmates and made us better people. He often took time to make the scriptures make sense without it being an hour-long lecture about some random part of the culture. He made everything applicable to us as his students and truly is the reason people like me want to be at BYU. I will be taking him again :)

No freebies (extra credit, dropped exams, etc) Wont lose points for no reason. Very clear expectations. Won't leave you guessing on what you need to know for exams. Class structure gets into predictable comfortable rhythm. Nothing is too hard, but just do it all and you will have a good grade.

Bro Sears is everything you want in a professor - he teaches from the scriptures, the assignments are meaningful but not crazy hard or complicated, and the lectures are uplifting and informative. Just do the homework and attend class and you'll be 100% fine. Minimal studying, just doing the weekly stuff. He is really relatable and inclusive too.

One of the best professors for NT! He uses a study bible in his class which makes the readings much more clear. Every week you have readings, an easy reading quiz (that makes up your exam questions), and a simple online assignment. There are four exams and no finals. He caters the class to your questions and is awesome!!

Brother Sears is a fantastic person which is evident in his teaching. I have loved his integration of the Old Testament and Book of Mormon in this class. Brother Sears is very caring and obviously wants each of his students to succeed. His class has been enriching and motivating. He is very detail-oriented, knowledgeable, and dedicated.

Brother Sears is the BEST! He truly wants his students to succeed, and he's super straightforward about what material will be on the test. I love how his class is easy enough that I'm able to have a spiritual experience in the class instead of just stressing out about the workload or difficulty of the tests! He never assigns busywork!

He is really good at helping you know exactly what to study for the tests and quizzes and is really chill. There are quite a few tests, but none of them are too hard. The only thing I'd say is to make sure you write down when each of the exams are at the beginning of the semester, but he's been my favorite religion professor by far.

A great professor who cares about his students and is super knowledgeable on this subject. Even though I had a really rough semester and couldnt put my all into the class, I still passed. Clear expectations and the assignments dont feel like busywork, unlike many other religion classes Ive had. Cool guy, cool class.

I loved taking Book of Mormon from Brother Sears! He's very caring, taking significant time to go over questions and concerns of students. He also designs his lectures around what he feels a student might need while teaching what you need to know for exams. You will learn and think a lot without worrying about your grade.

Heavier focus on the Isaiah chapters but instead of being boring, learning these stories has been super enlightening! Not much homework, not super test heavy. Brother Sears is enthusiastic and caring; I have learned so much better HOW to study the B of Mormon, and I've gained a deeper understanding and appreciation for this book. TAKE HIS CLASS! :)

He is awesome!! Always willing to work with you. He is very kind and wants the best for his students. The class is one you have to work for but it's all worth it! I would definitely recommend taking a class with him because I learned so much!!

He announces exams the day before you are supposed to take them, giving no time to prepare. There were also many assignments or lectures where we were talking solely on the New/Old Testament, instead of the Book of Mormon. (which is the class Im taking) We focused on a lot of textbook reading and it was hard to ever feel the spirit in this class.

Brother Sears is a great teacher who knows a lot about every topic he teaches. I do disagree, however, with those saying that all of the exam questions are from previous quizzes. He throws a lot of curveballs and the exams can be very difficult.

Take this from Sears! Though a bit boring on occasion, he is very inspirational and very caring about his students and the content. Sears helps us really get a gauge for what's happening, and where, in the Book of Mormon through a geographical approach as well as through his knowledge of ancient writings. Very doable and worthwhile. 10/10

Fantastic teacher! Very engaging. He would even bring in little artifacts or replicas to let us see frequently. Very clear expectations and we always knew what would be on the tests. You just have to make sure to study. He is always willing to meet after class to clarify things. *Finished online bc of COVID-19

One of the nicest guys ever, and really cares about his students. I loved how he taught the 4 Gospels; he focuses on the doctrine, but he also teaches the background and history so we understand where it came from. He's always willing to answer questions and listen. He does take attendance everyday. *I finished this class online due to Covid19

Prof. Sears is a great guy. He knows his stuff for sure and is very willing to work with his students according to their needs. Really not a difficult class if you do the reading and the homework questions. He uses the homework questions on tests word for word so if you do the homework you'll get a good grade on the test for sure.

Professor Sears is AMAZING!! I truely learned so much from his class and he prepares his students very well for the exams. The spirit was present and strong every single class which was very special because that doesnt happen in all religion classes. He was my favorite BYU professor and I highly reccomend taking his class!

Brother Sears is a great teacher and is so knowledgable. This wasn't the easiest religion class I've ever taken, but I learned so much from him! Beware, he does make you memorize three scriptures one of which is lengthy. He is so kind and really cares about his students!

Brother Sears is awesome. Extremely insightful, and I learned way more than I expected. His lectures were the perfect combination of spiritual and scholarly, and the class way more focused on learning than doing a ton of homework.

OK, if you came to this page wondering whether to take this class, the average score should answer your question! Professor Sears is probably literally the best religion professor at BYU, and no one talks about him! None of his work is busy work--you have to do it but it is so helpful and inspirational! He cares and plans class FOR the students!!!!

Brother Sears had very clear grading criteria, and he gave very straightforward exams. The homework questions reflected the exams, so if you do the reading you'll do great on the exams. Very enlightening, insightful, non-stressful religion class. Bro. Sears changed the way I view the scriptures.

BROTHER SEARS IS AMAZING!!!! He genuinely cares about his students. We had one class where we just talked about mental health! He knows so much about the scriptures. I've read the Book of Mormon lots of times, but this is the first time I felt like I actually understood it. During his class, it was like- "It all makes sense now!"

Brother Sears is awesome. Great teacher. He wants you to get a good grade. Reading quizzes before every class. The tests are the reading question, and a study guide he helps you fill in. If you put in a little work you will get an A.

AMAZING. Cannot emphasize enough how great he was. He used his knowledge of the Old Testament to explain cultural and literary insights in the Book of Mormon, plus he was able to explain the infamous Isaiah chapters in a clear and inspiring way. He is caring and very knowledgable. I loved going to this class! You will learn so much!

Absolutely loved Brother Sears! Genuinely caring guy. Only had 3 assignments per week and half the midterm questions are exactly from the homework and half from the lectures which are summarized in his study guides. So as long as you do the homework and show up to class it's an easy A.

If you are taking a religion class, take it from Bro. Sears! He is hands down one of the best religion profs at BYU. He makes his class very impactful and spiritual, without making it overwhelming and stressful on your grades. Just attend the lectures and do the reading questions and you will be fine. I learned a lot about the BOM. Spiritual. 11/10
This is one of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU. Absolutely would take again.

I really enjoyed taking this class from brother Sears! I've heard nightmares about BYU religion classes so I was nervous taking this class but it wasn't bad at all! He really knows his stuff and you can tell he cares about students. I would definitely recommend taking his class!!

LOVE HIM. He gets students so his workload and grading is easy. Def. quirky but I think hes hilarious. He has like a PhD in OT so he can answer any random question you ask. He has weekly online exercises that are the BEST- probably could get away w/ not actually reading them but if you do theyre amazing. Awesome class, not too hard for religion
Helped me outside class a ton and helped get my grade good. Quality guy that cares about his students

I normally don't write reviews on here but I had to because Brother Sears is amazing. He really knows his stuff and is able to answer any question thrown at him by students, but somehow maintains the spirit in every single class. The homework is totally reasonable and the tests aren't too difficult - TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM!
Brother Sears is great. He cares about the students, and teaches in a way that's really relatable and engaging. Not a ton of homework, but enough to keep you learning.

Oh my goodness I love Brother Sears. I felt the spirit every time I was in his class and just wow. His lectures are so amazing and I learned something new every single day. This class was also VERY easy so that you can get a lot out of it! Reading quizzes, easy exams with a clear study guide, and a few small exercises. TAKE FROM HIM!!!

He is a great religion professor with a strong testimony he isnt happy to share. Focuses on historical details so tests can be hard if you dont have a good memory or are unfamiliar with the scriptures.

I loved Brother Sears! He is a relatively new professor (I had him his second semester). but I honestly wouldn't have known that if he hadn't stated that the first day. The quizzes are straight forward, he is clear about what you will be tested on, and I felt like all of the assignments had a purpose. I learned a lot! Definitely take him if you can

Brother Sears is an amazing teacher. His Lectures are SUPER interesting and are about things college students care about. He has a short reading quiz online due before each class, which he gives us the questions before. Has a Test on each of the 4 gospels and NO FINAL. Those Tests are made from the quizzes so you have all the test questions before.

Brother Sears is incredibly knowledgeable about the scriptures and the Book of Mormon. I have learned more in that class about the Book of Mormon than any other class or Sunday school, and he makes it fun and easy! Study the reading questions for the tests and you'll get an A. It's a super fun class by an amazing professor! Take from Bro Sears!!!

This guy is amazing. You can tell throughout his class the incredible amount of time he puts into making your experience the best. You learn twice as much as the effort you actually put in to learn it. He teaches you amazing things in the classroom and through his assignments. If you want to learn the story of the Book of Mormon simply, take him!

Best Religion Teacher! He is young so he understands us. No final during finals week. Quick quizzes and reading every class. Posts Quiz questions before taking them online. Tests are from Quiz Questions. Interesting Lectures. Before I've had professors read from manuals and he actually makes the course interesting. Take any class from him!

Professor Sears is hands down my favorite religion professor at BYU! His lectures are amazing and you can really tell he cares about each of his students. He has an incredible amount of doctrinal and historical knowledge. Just memorize the questions on the quizzes you will ace the tests. I would take this class again and again if I could!

Brother Sears is an amazing religion professor! I learned SO much from him in class and for the first time at BYU, felt like I was gaining something from a religion class. Super easy class that challenges your thinking and helps expand your knowledge of the BOM. 12/10 would recommend.

Just what you want for religion. Loved learning what he had to teach. Easy reading quiz every class (he gives you the questions to study for). 5 tests (made of reading questions and stuff from class. Everything is on the study guide.) 1 paper at the end of class wasn't too bad and a few other easy assignments. Very forgiving grader too.

Bro. Sears was a good professor and wants his students to succeed! He gives study guides for the tests, which usually have lots of information but it's not too hard. He's kinda quirky but that makes class interesting! You have a big paper at the end of the semester but he can help you with it. Easy class, but you still learn interesting stuff.

SOLID religion professor! His class discussions are actually interesting and he's very clear about what will be on tests. There are daily reading quizzes, but he provides study guides for those questions. He's also pretty funny sometimes. He's a bit of a new professor, but that makes him sensitive to students' needs, which is way nice!

Brother Sears is a great professor to take Book of Mormon 121 from. He is very clear on what will be on tests and gives you the questions he will ask on the study guide and in the daily reading quizzes. It was a very easy class if you do the homework and make sure you use the study guides for the test. He's really fun and knows a lot.

He will answer every question you ever had about the Book of Mormon. I learned so much and was excited for the great lectures. He cares about students and is great with answering questions, no matter how hard they may be. Very organized, you know exactly what is expected and what will be on the tests and quizzes. Easy A if you study.

This class was awesome. If you are considering going into Bio Ed, take this class! Stowers really helped me solidify my career choice. This class was two hours a day, three days a week and should be a 4 credit class. My only complaint is he made us buy a useless subscription and the final was so disappointing. I highly, highly recommend this class!

Professor Stowers is one of the most helpful professors I have ever had. He is always willing to give me support and guidance, and answer any question that I may have. He is awesome at engaging his students, and at teaching us how to engage our students. He's an amazing example to me, and has helped change my life for the better.

This was a really good class. Brother Stowers is really good. The class is small which is nice and pretty easy especally if you are taking Bio 100 too. I learned a lot though and it really expanded my knowledge of Bio. It also helped me feel more comfortable in a lab situation. The semester project's not bad if you don't procrastinate.

Brother Stowers is a really good teacher and is so helpful. He answers most of the questions on the assignments in class. The TA's grade the assignments pretty hard though. Your answers have to be really specific. I'm way more excited to become a teacher now!

Good professor... each week, you do a lab (which he answers most of the questions on) and then turn it in the next week.  The labs are pretty easy but the ta's grading the lab are pretty specific! One end of the year project... not too bad and brother stowers helps a lot!  I would take this class!

One of the best biology classes I have ever taken! Way funny and is so interesting! Labs are only once a week for and you get to do things like make peanut brittle.You don't even have to know anything about bio for this class. One big experiment that you have to create so make sure you pick a good group. otherwise no tests just the easy lab reports

Dr. Mangelson is really good at explaining the concepts at the start of each class. He spends about 20-30 minutes lecturing each class.  Even though the class is 3 hours, he is only there for about the first hour; after that, it's just the TAs. Most of the class is just work time, but you have to do it on the engineering building's computers.

To be honest, the labs are difficult starting out, but Dr. Mangleson and his TAs were a huge help to me and by the end, I had a good handle on the material. They are willing to break things down into their most basic steps to help us gain understanding. The TAs are also available outside class, which is good for more difficult labs.

This is one of the easiest and most interesting tech electives, in my opinion. The labs are really time-consuming, but pretty rewarding when the robots actually work. Dr. Mangelson is reasonable and he does a good job at conveying the material. His exams are some of the easier ones I've had in the ECEN department

POLI357: His class is super interesting and he's a great lecturer. Several fun group projects that make up a large portion of your grade. He clearly cares a lot about the subject and has really engaging classes. Reading can be intense, sometimes 4 chapters at a time. In-class writing assignments each day are based on the readings. Would recommend

Even though the class is 3 hours, he is only there for about the first hour; after that, it's just the TAs. Most of the class is just work time, but you have to do it on the engineering building's computers.

Dr. Mangelson is reasonable and he does a good job at conveying the material. His exams are some of the easier ones I've had in the ECEN department

Brother Matson has been my favorite religion professor at BYU. He has a gift for helping people make personal connections to the scriptures. The tests were open scripture and scripture notes and he pointed out at the beginning of class what we would need to know for test, so that the discussion could be led by the spirit.

I absolutely loved Brother Matson's class. I learned something new every day and have a lot of respect for his knowledge. He truly cares about his students and goes above and beyond to help them succeed. It feels like learning from one of BYU's big name professors, but in a smaller, more personal class.

He definitely knows a lot, and you will learn a lot in this class, but it's not overwhelming. There is a big project at the end of the class and a smaller one at the beginning, but they're not too bad as long as you put the time in.
Took for Old Testament. Class is ridiculously easy as long as you show up. He teaches like a seminary teacher which can be a pro or a con depending on your preference.
Professor Matson was the best! If I could take every religion class from him I would! Such engaging lectures and you can tell he cares about his students.

Professor Matson is a great teacher! He is very passionate about the gospel & has a scholarly approach to teaching gospel concepts. The assignments are relatively light plus a few harder projects. I hope you take his class!!
Bro Matson is very engaging and excited about the content he teaches. There are a couple projects throughout the semester with clear expectations, and weekly reflections.

Professor Matson was great, his class was one of the most engaging of the religion courses I've taken. There is a large assignment, however he recommends scheduling one hour a week to complete it and gives a detailed overview of each section in class. Absolutely have to attend to get credit, but the content is very enriching.

Bro. Matson is FABULOUS! He's so passionate about scripture and Jesus Christ. I learned to love the Old Testament through him. I always looked forward to class and learned new things every time. He tells a lot of stories which I felt made lectures interesting. He is genuinely a good soul and cares so much about students' relationship with Christ.
His teaching style is very fun & uplifting. He is a very good man. I hope you take his classes!

He is fantastic with lectures that were so engaging! It is easy to get an A if you put just do the assignments, he is an easy grader. There is one big project at the end of the semester. You are allowed to use any notes that you put in your scriptures for tests and digital scriptures/notes are allowed also so the tests are really easy.

I loved this class! Matson is an expert in all things the Bible. He is so passionate and you can really tell he loves the Lord and the scriptures. This class had really easy quizzes and writing assignments once a week and a pretty hefty pericope project but he helps you plan it out so it doesn't feel like as much work. Great class!!

I'm so mad that I didn't find Brother Matson before now. If I could've taken every religion class from him, I would have. He is so passionate about what he does and focused on your spiritual learning more than teaching to a test. He gives you the best chance at succeeding, just stay on track with the big semester project so it doesn't pile up.

This class was awesome. Prof. Matson's lectures brought the spirit but were also very intellectually interesting in regard to the Old Testament and ancient Israel. His assignments were reasonable and relaxed. Staying on top of the readings will help a lot with tests (only 2 in the course), and stay on top of the pericope paper.
Sorry I have to correct my previous rating haha, I meant that his tests are open-scripture with notes, not open slide.

I LOVE Professor Matson and his class! I took his Old Testament class, and I feel like it was the perfect mix of spiritually enlightening and intellectually enlarging. I learned a ton about the Old Testament, so I had to put some work, but it was actually helpful, not busy work. Tests are open slide.

I absolutely loved this class! He is a great lecturer! I feel like I leave each class period having learned something new, and I look forward to going. He gives quite a few readings for us to do before each class, but he doesn't make you read more than an hour. He gives lots of extra credit opportunities! I want to take another class from him.

Josh loves his students and loves what he teaches, it's so obvious by the way he interacts with students and is open to questions and concerns. He is so knowledgeable in the gospel and loves delving into the history and details of the scriptures, but at the same time makes it a really spiritual experience

I love Brother Matson! I took two classes from him because he is just so amazing. He is really good at diving deep into content while still making sure we understand everything. He is so willing to help and the most important thing for him is making sure the class is filled with the Spirit. Religion classes at BYU are ridiculous, but his wasn't!

Incredible man. He cares about you, and cares to make his course relevant to your life. He is super energetic and fun, and he definitely knows what he is talking about. Extremely well educated, and does a great job of bringing to life the Old Testament while contextualizing it.

Such a great professor, I tried to take as many of his classes as possible. There is one big paper at the end that I learned from experience you do not want to procrastinate. He is funny and caring, and always says if you don't know or care enough to put an answer, you can write that Jesus is the answer for 50% (it works, believe me, I tried).

You will not regret taking a class from Brother Matson. He is engaging, spiritual, and so smart. I have recommended him so many times throughout the semester. I never wanted to miss his class. There was one pretty big paper, but if you get a start, you'll be fine. Weekly easy assignments and one midterm/one final. Highly recommend.

Professor Matson was awesome! He did a great job teaching, providing new knowledge, and inviting the spirit. He used many personal anecdotes during lectures that applied the teachings of the Book of Mormon. Some people may find or feel that he is trying too hard to bring the spirit or be "spiritual", but to me it felt genuine. His office hours A+.

So Good. I love how his first slide shows everything youll need to know for the test, that way it feels more like a really good sunday school class where you can learn and reflect and feel the spirit. Has great stories and makes it very engaging. You do have to read the BoM really fast, but he is so good. Worth it all the way.

I loved this class and professor so much. I enjoyed going to class and the work is easy and engaging. I learned a ton and it was super helpful for the future! Would definitely take Brother Matson's class again!!

I loved Brother Matson's class and I'd take another class from him in a heartbeat! Don't let the course overview scare you away. He gives you all the tools to succeed. I love that he wants his classes to be a benefit rather than a burden to his students. I always left feeling uplifted and wanting to share and learn more about what we talked about!

Every lecture I went to was filled with passion for the subject matter and love for the students, and that kind of attitude rubs off on the students. I enjoyed taking this class and would definitely take another class from this professor.
