This is the best religion professor at BYU. He says he wants his class to be somewhere we can come to feel the spirit and not be stressed out. All quizzes are open book, open scripture. He's such a nice guy and really makes your religion class the least stressful part of your course load as it should be.  Would take him every semester if I could.

He's really good. The big highlight of his class is the Pericope Paper, which you work on throughout the semester and involves focusing on a 10-verse passage the Bible and analyzing it really in depth. Highly recommend if that kind of thing sounds interesting to you.

Very easy class and very fun to attend his lectures. If you simply show up and do your assignments you will get an A. It was incredibly easy, straightforward, and fun.

Some people complained about him sharing personal stories / not finishing his lectures, but he always caught up and didn't include what was not covered on any tests.

Easy A if you are willing to work for it. Heavy emphasis on scholarly scripture study.

There is a semester-long paper, do 30 minutes a week and you're set.

Tests are easy if you've been paying attention in class--any notes in your scriptures are okay to use.

2 hours of preparation study expected for each lecture.

Professor Matson has been my favorite professor! I cannot give him enough praise! He always made the class laugh, yet always brought in the spirit. I will be seeking out another class of his! Incredible teacher:)

Dr Matson is one of the best, most insightful and intelligent teachers I have ever had. He brings a level of spiritual understanding and academic vigor that is deeply appreciated in religious education. 

His class isn't hard but it isn't useless either-- he rides the line between moderate difficulty and applicability perfectly. Take his NT class!

Super. Awesome. Professor. He is young and energetic, and connects well with young adults. He also knows all these random cool facts and knows Hebrew and Greek. There is a lot of reading, but it is not terrible and the reading quizzes are super short and direct. He responds really well to student feedback and is super caring.

Easily the most enjoyable class of the semester! Everyday we talked about different aspects of Christ's life and ministry, and I often learned things which were relevant to my life, or that I could share with others. Matson is a great guy that really cares about his students. There is a great spirit in his class, highly recommend.

Dr. Matson was a really fun religion teacher. attendance was encouraged but slides were always posted and the reading quizzes / tests made up most of the grade. One big research project that is daunting, but he breaks it down into small chunks that are clearly explained and easily manageable. Really seemed to care about us and our learning.

This was easily my most stressful class of the semester. I took this class at the same time as Economics 110, and I can honestly say that this class was more work than Econ. The sheer amount of material you're required to memorize is unreal. I also genuinely felt that we learned more about history than Christ's gospel, which was super frustrating.

LOVE Matson. His lectures super well organized, easy to follow, and good flow to it. He has incredible insights on old&new testament, and he's very invested in students' experience. Very open and responds quickly to feedback. Lots of reading assigned, but not really required for an A. A couple projects, but all meaningful and not onerous. Eyecandy

The professor is knowledgeable and passion about the topic. His enthusiasm is contagious and I found his lectures inspiring which made the study of the Old Testament many times better. He knows how to talk to students and how to help them do well in the class.

This guy is passionate about what he teaches, is incredibly enthusiastic, and cares so much for his students! He let us know on the first day that he is more well equipped to teach about biblical history, so this is a great class for anyone who's looking for a faith building class that almost exclusively uses the Bible!

This guy is like Indiana Jones; he taught using pictures of stuff his crews found in Jerusalem. It was not an easy class but I actually learned things. Even though this was a religion course, it was so grounded it felt like a history course.
Loved this class. Knows his stuff and is super inspiring.

Hardest BYU religion class I've taken. Didn't find it interesting. Barely felt the spirit. He tries to be funny, but I didn't think he was funny. He is reachable when needed and willing to help, so that was nice. I would not take this class again, it gave me so much anxiety.

Brother Matson is such a gem! The lectures were amazing and always left me on a spiritual high. The class IS allot of work but all of it is interesting and helps to help you gain both a scholarly and spiritual understanding. If you are willing to put in the work, your testimony will be strengthened and you will get an A without too much stress.

I LOVE BROTHER MATSON. He is SO funny and goes out of his way to have conversations with each student. I always felt supported in this class and like I always knew what was expected for assignments and the 2 exams. This is a very hard class with a lot of content, but if you put in the work you will do well.
This was Brother Matson's first time teaching at BYU so I'll cut him some slack, but this was the hardest religion class I've ever taken :( Cool guy tho.
Dr. Price is awesome. This is a hard class, be prepared to treat it as a full-time job if you want an A. Content is very interesting, very useful, but mastery of these concepts takes work.
Simple, awesome class

Joshua Price was a fantastic professor. I would absolutely take him again. The class itself is very difficult but Professor Price makes it very straight forward and if you are willing to study hard and do all of the work you'll be okay. Lots of reading!
Cool professor but the class is tough, so lock in. Go to the TA Labs and study there. Visit his office hours at least once.

As a student that got an A, I would not take this class from him. He's a nice guy and entertaining lectures. However he teaches you like you're a freshman in high school. After ever class you will have to basically relearn everything by yourself, since it will not be even close to adequate. Extremely frustrating also since attendance is required.
Ignore the bad reviews, if you go to class and make sure you do the homework you will be just fine. If you want to go on your computer or phone you probably shouldn't be taking econ 110 anyway.

Professor Price is a great professor. Very entertaining and engaging lectures, and he cares a lot about every student and is more than willing to give extra help when needed. Pretty funny guy, too. With that being said, keep in mind that ECON 110 is a TOUGH class and requires lots of work outside of class to do well.
He was one of the best professors I've had. Class content was difficult, but he did good at breaking it down for us.

If you are not an economic, business, or finance major/minor, do not take this class. You are busy enough with your classes. In his syllabus, he says that you need 2 hours per credit on a course and holds you to it. Super clear when I say easy in the beginning and once you miss 1 or 2 lectures you're screwed. Not a bad professor, not great neither.
The professor is chill and class is easy, though it has more homework than expected for a one-credit course.

I think a lot of the other reviews on Price are unfair. The class was hard, but I enjoyed Price as a professor. His sarcasm added some enjoyment out of an 8 AM class. There were 3 midterms and 1 final. They were hard but I never felt like Price and the TAs were trying to 'get' you. If you do the work and spend the time on the class, you'll do well.

Honestly I felt like I didnt learn very much at all from the lectures, 99% of the learning is independent and just doing the reviews. When I went to a TA lab, even they were getting questions wrong. 73% of your grade is just midterms and a final. The average one a midterm was 69% and the final's average was like 70%

Put in the work, and you'll get a good grade. Expect to spend more time on this than on other 3 credit courses. 73% of your grade is exams: 3 midterms and a final, 1 midterm gets dropped. If you're not understanding something, go to the TAs asap. Don't waste time not understanding something. Practice quizzes are basically exactly like the exams.

Professor Price, still teaches like everyone is a high schooler. He doesn't allow phones or laptops when we're all paying to take his class. His exams are purposefully misleading. The lectures, Quizzes, and reading never really line up well so you're stuck not knowing the best resources for any of the test material.

I see that there are a few bad reviews for the class; I wouldn't listen to them. From what I can tell, his class is significantly easier than other Econ 110 professors. His lectures are straightforward, and tests are based on past homework grades, so if you drill the homework, you'll be fine. Very kind professor, use office hours.

Take this class from someone else. He pokes fun at students for asking questions. He is more concerned about cracking jokes than actually teaching. Lectures were largely him trying to be funny or selling the Econ major to freshmen. Lectures do not reflect quizzes or exams at all. I learned the majority of the the content outside of class on my own.

Great guy, tries to be funny. Not a good teacher for Econ 110 though. He is too concerned about giving out baseball cards and making jokes rather than teaching the concepts. Extremely hard to follow, I wouldn't go to class but it's required. Does he know his stuff? Maybe. Know how to teach beginners? Nope IMO. Take the class from someone else.

Covers economic fundamentals but lacks organization, with extreme level testing of understanding said to reflect real-world demands (In a 110). Most learning occurs independently due to lack of deeper level teaching. Commonly viewed as a weeder course though often required as a GE, it feels more like academic endurance training than an intro class.
Hes trying his best guys

Professor Price is not great at lecturing. Lectures feel like you're being yelled at and content in lectures is not very helpful compared to the long, dry textbook. The exams are designed to trick you and make you fail. Essentially it feels as if you are being waterboarded with work and content and then failed after weeks of studying.

He's a great guy but not a great teacher. He skips over key concepts that are confusing and leaves you lost. He also allows his TA's to make the test questions and they make trick questions (One of the TA's told me they do this) The tests don't feel like its to test your knowledge but to trick you in ways that don't apply.

Liked him at first—nice and engaging—but as the semester went on, the class got harder to succeed in. He added pop quizzes on readings, which felt unfair since I learn better through lectures. Also had a lot of trick questions and pick the best answer. Nice guy, but not a great professor. Use TAs and YouTube—don't rely only on class.

He's a good guy and funny, so lectures are entertaining, but he's a very bad teacher. He skips key material and doesn't explain concepts clearly. I had to rely on YouTube, ChatGPT, and TAs to actually learn. We even had midterms before covering the chapters. Overall, not an enjoyable experience. Good guy just not good at teaching itself. At all.

Dr Price is high energy and engaging but did tend to be quite sarcastic in lecture (in a jovial manner) which really turned me off from asking questions. As a teacher he honestly was poor. He rarely gave a thorough and in depth explanations and I felt he quite literally skimmed the surface on all the material. Works for tests I guess...

I loved having Price as a professor! Class was fun even for an 8am and he taught very clearly. The homework was very doable and you got extra credit for doing it in groups so I never got overwhelmed. We had a data project due at the end of the semester that I was worried about but it ended up being very doable and wasn't stressful at all.

Lectures were fantastic. I enjoyed every day that I went to this class. It was not terribly difficult, stay on top of the homework and understand what you are doing and you will be fine. He is pretty funny, and makes sure that everyone understands what is going on. Exams are similar to the practice exams, do those and you'll do fine.

you're fine if you just read the textbook but Price's lectures make the material so much more clear, interesting, fun, and applicable to everyday and church life. the grade you get will be the effort you put in!

Price gave really good lectures and generated great discussions with a big class. He also has a very sarcastic sense of humor which I liked. However, I really struggled with the tests even though I felt like I knew the material pretty well. Three tests make up 70% of the grade so they're do or die. Go to the TA review sessions, they help a ton.

Prof Price is an adjunct for spring/summer. He teaches economics like it's his calling. I took this class from Kearl and did horrible because I didn't understand the material. Professor Price helps you understand the material while still including humor. His lecture on dating and econ was the best ;)
I really liked Professor Valladares! His lectures were interesting and really helped to prepare us for the projects due throughout the semester.

I was excited to take this class but honestly it was so hard to sit there thought lectures, he is a really nice guy but needs more energy and enthusiasm. Attendance mandatory, and I don't know if it was the TA or the professor but my assignments were always graded low.

I had Dr. Valladares for two classes this semester, Research Design and Analysis, and Multicultural psychology and he was an excellent professor in both. Directions for assignments were always clear, he was always able to answer questions, and is very personable. If you have the opportunity to take any classes from him, DO IT!

Dr. V is great! Super kind and cheerful. This was his first time teaching Psych 307, and he admitted to us that he makes us write a lot more projects than the other professors, but I learned a lot. Attendance is mandatory, and the TAs grade all your work, so there's a lot of inconsistency with the grading and you lose a lot of unnecessary points.

I love Dr Valladares, he is a kind, pure soul and one of my favorite professors here at BYU so far. He's great at leaving space for questions and answering them. Lectures are always interesting and the assignments are testimony building. I would recommend him to anyone. I have zero qualms. Epic professor, very knowledgeable.

I took this class to see how I liked psychology. I left not questioning if I should take more psych classes, rather if I should stay in college. The lectures were pretty hard to sit through. Prof. Vallardes is a nice guy, but at least when I took the class he was not very energetic. There is a quiz in each class and it always sucks.

Super easy class, as long as you read the textbook and pay attention to the lectures you will be set. The only bad part was the attendance quizzes that were only open for first 5 mins of class and are graded on accuracy as well. However, the questions are basically test questions and his study guides are SUPER helpful, really set you up for an A.

He was awesome I just didn't like the quiz at the beginning of class that was for attendance that was only open for 5 minutes, so if you were late you weren't getting attendance for the day which negatively impacts your grade. Not to mention the quizzes are also graded.

I took multicultural psych with Dr. Valladares - he has a lot of knowledge and perspective to offer on the subject and integrated unique activities and assignments to apply what we learned. Lots of writing and super strict about APA formatting. Grading criteria was often unclear, TAs and him would take off a lot of points for small errors.
Kind, has very helpful TA's, prepares you well for tests, relatively difficult but if you take advantage of the extra credit it will be very helpful.

In class quizzes (easy). A 10-week cultural research project that is NOT as daunting as it seems because he really just wants you to learn about different cultures. The lectures were amazing & matched with his tests. READ THE TEXTBOOK! The textbook matches up with his tests as well. He's funny and a super genuine guy! WOULD TAKE AGAIN!

Professor Valladares was a good professor. Most of the classes were PPT lectures, but he made sure to make them fun. There were three midterm exams, but they really helped you keep up with learning the course material. There is also a decent amount of reading and a small quiz every class on the chapter. Overall, would recommend this class.

Dr. Valladares is a very good teacher. His lectures are interesting and very informative. One thing about his class is that the tests are very hard. You read a lot between classes so you would have to split it up in the days you don't have class to make it bearable. However many of the assignments were easy and interesting.

I personally don't do well with his style of teaching. It was mostly him just lecturing and he doesn't use powerpoints or anything, it's just him talking and writing notes on the board. But he prepares you for exams with study guides, so as long as you study those well, you'll do fine. Just beware if you're not much of a lecture-type student.
I took this class to fill a letters general, and it was totally worth it. There was not a lot of homework, and when there was it was pretty simple. Professor Burton was funny and knew his stuff

Professor Burton knows a lot about philosophy and obviously really likes it. He does his lectures by memory which is impressive. The class is really interesting but can sometimes go over your head and you just zone out. I  have definitely fallen asleep in that class. So maybe bring snacks.

This is for PHIL 110. Burton is awesome. He is a lawyer who teaches philosophy because he is passionate about it. He lectures for the entire class and does a good job of making it interesting. He understands that this is an intro class and that it should be interesting, enjoyable, and not too difficult, unlike most GEs at BYU. Easy if you attend.

I loved PHIL 215. He's a lawyer so he was often swamped with work, but he still had super exciting lectures. Take this professor if you want to learn how to think and are interested in theology. There are reading and a few writing assignments but they aren't that hard if you space out the work.

As a 400-level philosophy class, it involves an unprecedented reading load with tons of writing (4 reading journals, 4 essays, and a final paper, but no exams). Dr. Burton is quite strict when grading them but provides useful revise suggestions as well. Overall a great class and professor, but be prepared to work a lot.
Dr. Burton is an awesome teacher. He's a super chill guy, and knows how to explain tricky philosophical stuff well. He encourages lots of discussion which is nice.

This class doesn't have a ton of homework at all, and Judd's pretty chill. It's a little intimidating as a 1st Phil class because he doesn't teach you how to think/write philosophically super well but still expects you to do so on parts of tests/hw, but he's pretty gracious on grading b/c of that. Probably one of the more-doable IntroPhil classes.

Professor Burton explains the concepts very well. The thoroughness of his lectures match up with the hardness of his tests (neither are too tough). This class was extremely interesting, and it was a very enjoyable and relatively painless way to pass off a GE. I probably spent, on average, two hours a week working on this class outside of class.

Judd is such a chill professor. I took Philosophy of Religion from him on a whim during my first semester at BYU and have absolutely no regrets. He understands that philosophy is a meaty subject so he grades pretty graciously on the argument outlines and test essays. 2 tests, took a fair amount of studying but were all multiple choice w/ an essay

She's not teaching phagehunters anymore, but you literally learn so many skills from this class and can actually apply things you learn in lectures to your own project. I learned more from this class than most of my other, more difficult micro classes. Dr Grose is extremely nice and ensures that everyone is given the chance to do well.

An inspirational professor! If you come to class and show up ready to participate then you will do well in this class. If you do well then she is often open to students joining her research lab afterwards. It really was a phagulous class!

She is probably the best life sciences professor I have ever had at BYU! I don't have enough great things to say about her. I have learned so much in her class, and she is able to explain things really well. She is very approachable, and she is invested in her students. I wish I could take all of my bio classes from her. THE BEST!

In this class we explored the intersection of science and religion. The lectures were really interesting and fun and you'll learn how to reconcile areas that don't seem to overlap. If you show up and are a decent student who does the work you will get an A.

This class is great to get some lab experience. The tests are not too hard, but you need to study for them. The class isn't designed to kill you. It's supposed to help you be a scientist, so it's totally doable on busy schedule. Dr. Grose is great.

Best. Professor. At BYU. EVER. She is everything you will need in a COMPETENT professor. She gives great feedback, explains things more if you don't understand, and genuinely cares about you and your grades. It would be good to make a personal effort to get to know her, she will help you a lot. Her tests aren't hard, you just need to pay attention.

This is by far the best of the best that you'll find at BYU. Not only does she care about you learning and growing, but she also cares about you genuinely. She's so sweet, easy to talk to, very humble, pretty much genius, very inspiring and all you need in a professor. Kudos to her .
Dr. Grose is always willing to help you understand a concept. She invests a lot of time and energy into the program and the students.

She is really nice and the class is way easy! lecture was a little pointless, didn't learn much because she just kind of read off the slides. I stopped going half way through the semester but still got over 100% in the class. book is unnecessary

Dr. Grose is really nice and really does want her students to succeed. She is not the best lecturer. I honestly didn't learn very much from going to class. The lectures were boring and her slides were unorganized. Her class is an easy A, tests are easy if you memorize the slides. I really enjoyed microbiology.

Dr. Grose is a fantastic teacher. She definitely will make you work for your grade, but she really helps to prepare you for tests. She provides many opportunities to learn and attending class is crucial to understand her powerpoints to study.

I really like Professor Grose, but her powerpoints and lectures were kind of all over the place. The material wasn't difficult, but I seemed to fill a lot of my time studying for the tests trying to organize the material into what I really needed to know. She offers a lot of extra credit. I was never worried about my grade in this class.

Wonderful lady, not an organized lecturer. TA's aren't the most helpful because they haven't taken her class. Random assignments like a group project & paper. I crammed for the midterms the night before/day of & got A's because the material is easy. Offered so much extra credit. But definitely stressed out for this class more than it was worth.

Dr. Grose is very sweet and cares about her students. She offers a ton of extra credit and lets you correct the written section of exams for half credit. I personally found lecture to be boring, but the class was chill and a very easy A.

Guys!! Im telling you. TAKE THIS CLASS. She is by far one of the best biology teachers I have had. She is very clear when it comes to tests and homework. SHE WANTS YOU TO SUCCEED. The exams were pretty difficult throughout the course but she lets you use the final to replace one of the exams from the past. and extra credit on top! TAKE THIS CLASS!!

This class was awful. Dr. Grose is so intelligent, and very nice, but she is an awful lecturer. I stopped going to her lectures after a month because I didn't learn anything from her. She was more concerned about getting through the material than teaching. 4 tests, with easy MC but really hard free response. Take it from someone else, it's easier.

I went into this class not excited at all. I ended up loving microbio and really found a ton of application to my life. I disagree with previous comments that say you don't have to go to class to do well. Her slides are usually full of a lot more information than you need to know. Going to class clarifies what is important. She's a great teacher.

Dr. Grose expects you to know a lot about microbiology. She is very passionate about the importance of microbiology. Her test questions come straight from review slides and weekly online quizzes. She lets you correct written exams for half credit. She gives plenty of extra credit. I really enjoyed her class. An A is definitely possible.
Easy A-, a little work for the A. She is very nice and very willing to help, half of the questions on tests are the same as the homework. Don't really need to go to class to do well.

Dr. Grose is nice enough.  Her class is manageable, just do the work and reading and you'll be fine.  Four midterms, a final, a small group presentation, and weekly online quizzes.  Exams are half written, half MC.  They're not too bad, she gives reviews and offers regrade options.  Not an easy A, by any means, but definitely doable.
Great teacher, makes sure you really understand what you're doing and helps you develop the lab skills you'll need for the rest of your career.

Excellent teacher and one of my favorite science teachers at BYU:) You do have to put in effort, but as long as you make the time a good grade is completely do-able. Her lectures are fascinating, you will want to pay attention! She is kind, fun, and cares about your success. She's always willing to answer questions and help you with what you need.
Really, really amazing professor. She's nice, understanding, approachable, easy and fun. If you can take MMBio151 from her, definitely do.

Pretty good class, very helpful that the slides were available online prior to lecture to take notes on. Tests were typically straight forward, some questions were super specific so you need to make sure you know your stuff. I really liked how she incorporated diseases into the lectures all semester instead of saving them all for the end.

One of the best teachers I've had at BYU.  She is more than willing to help students with whatever they need and always finds time to answer any questions.  Tests are fair and are over the material covered.  The tests can be challenging but if you study the slides and the review you'll be fine.  Take this class from Grose!!!

It's not a cakewalk, but she makes it about as easy as she can for Micro. Offers extra credit which you should do, and lets you rework test answers for 1/2 credit. Never used book, quiz every week online.  2 Midterms & a final. Group Project that isn't bad, and a final project that you can work in a group on. Easy A-, a little more work for the A.
If you put the time in it's not a very hard class. Dr. Grose is always willing to help and is very kind.
The class is well organized. She will do a lot to help students to learn the material and get good grades. All teachers should be like her!!
I liked Dr. Grose's class a lot.  It was a pretty easy class to do well in.  I showed up most of the time and studied a little for the tests and did just fine.
If you went to class it was pretty easy to get an A.  You did have to study a little but overall her style of teaching is conducive to good grades.  She is very willing to help at any time.
Dr. Grose was seriously so amazing.  She is one of the most helpful professors I know and is so interested in the students and their learning.  If you have a chance to take this class, definitely do.

I can't say it was an easy class, but I can say it was completely fair and an excellent class. I loved it. Labs were fun, she gave study guides for exams and she allowed us to correct the questions we missed for half credit. I would totally recommend this class if it covers some of your requirements.

Professor Holt-lunstad was very kind and accommodating! I took this class online, the TAs mostly run the class. All the homework is assignments that are building up your literature review. They are pretty difficult, and sometimes the rubric is a little unclear. however, the TAs helped me to better understandthe concepts when contacted.

She cares a lot about her research work which sometimes makes teaching feel like her second priority, but the TAs are super useful. Staying on top of assignments will help you stay on top of the class.

Dr. Lunstad is great, but I don't like the class layout. It's easy at first, and then swamped. All you have to do in this class is write a literature review, 10-12 minimum pages, and 15 minimum references. Get a topic fast, and don't procrastinate. She is often gone, and the TA's aren't that good at teaching, but low-key class isn't that important.

Professor Holt-Lundstad is the best! She's fun and cares about her students. She can be a tough grader and a little confusing when lecturing at times, but she's pretty clear about what's expected of you. You just write one 10-12 page paper throughout the semester and submit portions of it at a time to break it up. I would recommend her!!

Dr. Holt-Lunstad was amazing! She was a super kind professor and I enjoyed her class. Psych writing is known for being a more difficult prereq but she graded things easily and gave a lot of opportunity for extra credit and make up work which was unique. Although she was out of town for some classes, her TAs were great.

She is a super interesting person to talk to, and is super knowledgeable. However, she isn't a super great lecturer, and will ramble on about a point for 10-20 minutes that isn't relevant, but still expects you to know everything in the book and on her slides, even if she didn't get to it. Her research is famous, but she was gone A LOT.

This was one of the most frustrating classes I have ever taken. She was gone ALL THE TIME. Not only that, but she didn't set the class up so that we could do actually useful things when she was gone. It feel like she doesn't really care about her students, or being a professor. There were so many things on tests that we didn't learn.

It was a blended class, and it is still being worked out, so it was confusing at times. There are a lot of little assignments to do, so it is a pretty time intensive class. The TAs were super good about giving feedback and being available outside of class to meet. If you meet with them, they will tell you pretty much exactly how to fix it.

She is really only focused on her research and not a lot on her students. The class was blended and it was very unorganized. The difference between what the TAs said and the Professor, and Canvas was all different and very difficult to understand. It made me feel like I was in high school again. I would not take a class from her again

The class is organized well and easy to learn even in an online class. Everything is pretty straight forward but her grading is pretty tough. You have to do everything right and more to get an A. She makes you work for it but you get used to it after a couple of weeks. It's a lot for an online class but I left grateful that I took it that way

Dr. HoltLunstad's research is famous, and she will make sure you know; she talks about her fame nonstop. She is a poor lecturer, meandering and unable to get to the point. She also shows little respect for students as adults, structuring assignments in a way that treats students like potential cheaters, and in an effort to "catch you" on mistakes.

Get ready to do so much work, including discussion posts/comments, all to just be graded by a completely vague rubric and judged for even the smallest comment. Seriously, no matter what I wrote, shed always dock off a couple points from everything I did. I even lost 2 points on a RESEARCH PROPOSAL that was just one paragraph. Steer clear of her!!!

Dr. Holt-Lunstad is very nice and obviously does well with research. However, that's where it stops. She is not good at teaching concepts and she spends 20 minutes (or more sometimes) on one slide because she can't just get straight to the point. Class is VERY test heavy which makes it hard when she isn't very effective at teaching the material.
I really enjoyed this class. As long as you go to class, at least skim the reading, study for the tests, and do the weekly writing assignments, you'll do fine.

Warning -- if you're a sociology major don't take this class from her. It's very psychology-based and has a micro focus. The lectures are boring & the tests take up 75% of your grade (which have trick questions). The readings are long. Holt-Lundstad herself is nice enough, but her ongoing laugh is distracting and she can't teach concepts well.

The whole class comes down to how well you do on the exams. The exams aren't easy but they are manageable. Try forming a study group to make sure you all are understanding the textbook concepts alright. Her lectures are all over the place so stick to the book.
The test is 75% of the grade so be prepared to read and study the concepts. She goes into full detail on the test

Professor Holt-Lunstad definitely cares about her students but you really get out of this class what you put into it. Her lectures can be long and she honestly isn't the best at clarifying difficult concepts sometimes, but the material is not difficult and if you read the textbook you should have no trouble getting an A.

I enjoyed Dr. Holt-Lunstad. I have heard other reviews declaring that she goes on tangents and does not prepare well for her exams. I have not found this to be the case. It is essential (for your test grades) to both read the book and take notesrewrite your notesreview your notes in lectures. The blog submissions need to follow rubrics.

I never knew what to expect and the structure of the lectures were a bit scattered. You definitely need to know information from the book and lectures, and I really disliked how extremely minute details and studies were used for test questions.

Try to avoid her as a professor at all costs. I usually do not write things about professors, but she is honestly the worst professor I have ever had. Her tests are ridiculous and her TA is NOT helpful at all! She could careless about her students.

This class is not that difficult. Attend class, go to the reviews, and complete the study guides and you should be fine for the tests. There are a lot of easy points by doing the simple homework, and a lot of extra credit opportunities.

It's really not that hard to do well in this class. It consists of reading a chapter per week, writing little portfolio entries that apply one aspect for each chapter (these are due all together before each exam), and completing the exams. Prof. HL does not waste time with busy work, and she is friendly and enthusiastic. I highly recommend her.

Worst Psych professor I have ever had.  I am almost done with my degree and I have never had a class so poorly structured - with terrible assignments that don't even help you apply the materials and tests that don't measure at all what you have learned (they just see how well you can avoid being tricked).  Wouldn't recommend this class AT ALL.

Not too hard of a class but you have a lot of busy work you have to do.  Homework assignments weekly which consist of writing a one-two page paper.  Tests are based on lecture and reading the textbook.  You have a final project at the end which is the best part of the class.
Be careful in lecture or else the sandman will catch you.

I quite enjoyed this class.  I learned a lot and the class wasn't too difficult.  If you read the textbook you'll be fine.  I think people's main objection to her teaching styler is her reliance on slideshows, but I didn't mind them so I liked the class.

I took both psych statistics and social psych from Dr. HL and really enjoyed both. She is an enthusiastic teacher and very willing to help. She is very real and not afraid to be nerdy. She works hard to make things clear and interesting. I would definitely recommend her.
She is great.

If your're interested in this subject, don't be afraid to take it from her. She can be a bit repetitive and the class really isn't that hard. Study her powerpoints and read the chapters in the book and it shouldn't be a miracle to get an A on the tests.

She's really nice, and tries really hard. She does have a tendency to dumb things down a bit too much which makes some lectures boring, but it's b/c she really wants everyone to understand. Unfortunately the tests are still hard. But overall the class is really interesting- I'd recommend taking it from her, esp if the TA is good (that helps a lot).

She was a nice enough professor but the lectures were terribly boring. I'm actually in her class right now and started doing this just to get some kind of mental stimulation. Her TA's reviews are helpful for tests, and actually going to the class is kind of unnecessary except to turn in your portfolios (way easy assignment). Overall, easy class.

Class started out bad (failing the first test) but then ended great (got an A on the final).  You have to get used to her grading. She says "um" or "uh" just about every other word and laughs awkwardly.  The TA, David, was way better than her. Would take it from someone else if you can.

Health psych- Horrible class! It's amazing how a topic with such potential can be turned into such a bore so easily. Holt-Lunstad doesn't know how to teach a class, her tests are so ridiculous she apologizes to the class after we all fail them, and I know less about health psychology now than I did before I took the class. Do not take this class!

I really liked Dr. Holt-Lunstad. It is true that she classes can be boring, if you don't care about the subject matter. I really liked the subject and so I found her teaching interesting. You do need to read the book and you really will do well!
The textbook was really good, even if she is kind of awkward as a teacher. She tries hard, but she really belongs in a lab, not a classroom

Wow- was I even in the same class as the other posters??  I loved this class.  Her grading was not bad!  I got an A (It's an upper-level class - read the textbook!  Do the work & you'll get a good grade).  The material was SO ineteresting.  I want to get my Master's in Social Psych b/c of this class.  Dr. H-L is really nice & helpful. Great class!

Two thumbs way down.  What was I thinking?  This class was an absolute disaster.  She does an awesome job at boring students to death.  She is ruthless with her grading.  She has you sign a stupid contract pretty much taking away your rights to dispute grading.  The T.A. was also a piece of work--can we say BROWN NOSER! Gall, beware of this teacher

She is pretentious.  She loves to talk about how she is a female professor all the time.  I never really payed attention to that fact until she kept reminding us.  I asked her a question in class and she totally ignored me on time.  She grades harshly.  She makes her students sign a manipulating contract so you can't make disputes.  Not helpful.
Boring class.  She reads from the slides a lot.  Busy work and ambiguous tests, but overall a pretty easy psych class.
Definitely NOT hot, but worse, class is a complete waste of time. No, I take that back, the movies were interesting, but once she'd start talking again, all the life got sucked out of the room.
blah, blah, blah. I couldn't get past her lame laugh and the dumb guy in the front who wouldn't shut his mouth. Easy class though. I was glad to get it over with.

This class was the biggest waste of time. I didn't learn one thing and I flat out stopped going to class because I felt like I was losing IQ points. I did good on the tests though- just studied out of the book! Pretty easy!

She makes class fun with video clips and examples from her life.  if you read the book you'll do ok.  some days were boring, but most were quite fun.  i'd chose her again, but her tests are really hard.
No Comments
Not helpful.  Her classes seemed like a waste of my teime and her tests were unreasonable.  90% of the time, reading the textbook was more interesting than going to class.
No Comments
Cute, smart, helpful, crazy laugh.

Dr. Allen is an excellent professor. She is very personable and easy to get along with. Class was 90% discussion, so you have to do at least some of the readings (of which there is a lot) in order to contribute to class. I had a great time though and would definitely recommend this class from her.

Professor Allen is awesome! Super good at what she does, super willing to help and is amazingly nice. If you're looking for information on this class, it's amazingly fun but brutal. Papers every week and the grading is hard. I had to work my butt off to keep up as a non-bio or chem major.

Professor Allen is the absolute best! She is without a doubt my favorite professor at BYU. She is caring to all her students and is very clear about expectations from the outset. Her grading is fair and her readings, although sometimes strenuous, are typically very interesting. Couldn't recommend her more!

Dr. Allen is the reason I left the Honors Program. The instructions for her HUGE papers were completely unclear and too specific at the same time, so we never knew HOW we lost points, and we lost TONS of points. She talked down to us and made us feel stupid, despite us being honors students. Get ready to be publicly mocked if you disagree with her.

Professor Allen is great! She's very passionate about world literature, and her lectures were always inspiring. Her Digital Dialogue and essay questions were always thought-provoking and helpful for understanding the material. The only downside to this class is that there is a LOT of reading. I could barely keep up.
Great, thoughtful lectures with lots of reading as homework. She gave solid feedback on a very long paper. Would def take a class from her again.

I love Julie Allen. I honestly think she is one of the best professors BYU has. Discussion was always engaging, exciting, and challenged me to push my ideas. She gives tons of useful feedback on writing assignments so I actually became a better writer. She cares about her students as humans and has real conversations during her office hours. 10/10

Spirituality in Kierkegaard and Andersen. Julie made really difficult material accessible. She does a great job making abstract and foreign concepts relevant to everyday life. Very enthusiastic about course. Absolutely brilliant. Super understanding and empathetic in class and in office hours - genuinely cares about students. Can't recommend more.

Honestly, out of the four years of classes that I have taken at BYU, this has been the best class I have ever taken. Although we dealt with some dense philosophical content and abstract concepts, Professor Allen always kept us grounded in how it related to our lives and how we could learn and grow from it. Genuine conversation overall just amazing.

Fairy Tale Seminar. One of the best classes I've taken at BYU. She makes class discussion really engaging and does a great job tying the lit to the real world. Lots of readings, but they were fun and not super academic. Lots of short papers graded generously - just need a good thesis, topic sentences, and to actually make your argument.

She's a really, really intelligent person and understands the works read in class extremely well. She will work with students that do their best, even giving second chances. She grades hard on the two formal essays. Tests are not overly hard and it's possible to get extra points. TAs are not very useful and hold review sessions that are inadequate.

Professor gives amazing and funny lectures, but the TAs are unfair graders (who didn't really know the material well). Exams consist completely of essay questions, and a ton of reading is required. Not impossible to get an A, just challenging. SHE GRADES THE PAPERS EXTREMELY TOUGH. A good class.

Professor Allen was fantastic at lectures and story telling. However, her class was far more advanced than I was expecting. I would not recommend this class if you are taking it for GE credits as I was. Once you get the hang of the grading policy, assignments and exams are easy to pass, but the TA's just seemed uninformed/uninterested.

As other reviews state, the grading for this class was fairly shocking. TAs and teachers switch off and grade anonymously, but each writing assignment is graded VERY rigorously. You can do well on reading quizzes and exams. I love literature, but the nature of grading in this class really turned me off, and I wouldn't consider taking it again.

This class is extremely difficult, especially for being a general ed class. She assigns about 60-150 pages to read for every class period of ancient literature that, at least for me, is difficult to understand. She is very intelligent and upbeat person, but do not take this class unless your major is or you love ancient literature.

If you're a science major needing a general, steer clear of this class. Lots of papers, TONS of reading, she's a RIDICULOUSLY harsh grader on papers and exams. Very subjective and requires you to read her mind to succeed. Takes of lots of points for very nit-picky little details. Just don't do this to yourself. Ruined literature for me.

Professor is a fun person and puts a lot of effort into the class. She knows her stuff, but requires so much. There is a lot of reading every class. The grading is extremely rough. Never clear on what she's looking for, or gives new guidelines the day the paper is due, and docks points for trivial things.

The class is okay. She is a super intelligent lady and shes super passionate about literature, but she sets extremely high standards. She requires you to read A LOT. She requires you to make an argument in an essay and use ancient texts to back up your argument. I was caught off guard by how rough the grading is.

Dr. Allen is super smart and very competent. I learned a lot and enjoyed this class. However I felt that writing assignments were graded too strictly for a general education class. Tests also require a lot of studying, so make sure to devote adequate time.

Professor Allen definitely knows her stuff, and her lectures are full of deep analysis of the texts you read. She doesn't have too many office hours, but she usually answers LS messages or emails pretty quickly. She's very kind and willing to work with you. She's a tough grader, though, especially on the essays! (Or maybe I'm just a bad student...)
Her lectures aren't the best but she is nice and is willing to help you. The concepts are difficult but doable. I had to do a lot of work to learn the concepts outside of class to do well.

Dr. Crockett obviously cares about the subject and her students. Fluids can be difficult conceptually and I didn't feel like her lecture style was helpful for me or most of the other students I sat with. I do not regret taking it from her, but it is not perfect. She has lots of office hours, very willing to help students. Hw & tests not too bad.

I absolutely love Dr. Crockett. If I could take a class from her every semester I would. Lectures are engaging and she teaches content very clearly. The content of the class isn't easy but she makes it as straightforward as possible. Exams were extremely fair with no surprises. I would HIGHLY recommend taking fluids from her.

Dr. Crockett is a great professor. I felt like the quality of the lectures slightly decreased over time, but I couldn't tell if that was because the topics got harder, and I just understood less. Tests are weighted heavily: being a total of 70% of your grade, but they are graded fairly with a lot of partial credit. I recommend Dr. Crockett.

Dr. Crockett is an excellent teacher. She is extremely knowledgeable, but is still able to bring the (difficult) subject matter to her students in an approachable and engaging way. For all the work she puts into the class, she also expects work from her students, so prepare to study a lot. One of my favorite professors at BYU.

The good:

Her lectures

The bad:

Her tests are HARD and compose most of your grade. 1 hr time limit and most don't have time to finish.

The homework is HARD. Much of the material covered in the homework was taught very little if at all in class. This was very frustrating.

Not much material (powerpoints, videos, etc) are available to help.

Dr. Crockett was really nice and made fluids more interesting/engaging with videos and fascinating scenarios. It is a tough class though. Take full advantage of TA hours and her hours. Give yourself lots of time to understand concepts and prepare for tests. They are hard.

Crockett is really nice but it was her first semester teaching statics and it showed. Lectures were pretty confusing and felt disorganized most of the time. The class is just hard too (not her fault); difficult group projects, homework, and tests. With more experience teaching statics she'll probably be great, but I didn't have the best experience.

Dr. Crockett works hard to make fluids fun even though not everyone is interested in it. Fluids is a tough subject, so don't expect an easy class, but she's really easy to approach with questions and gives helpful explanations to help with understanding.

Dr. Crockett is great. Take fluids from her! She really knows her stuff and is a great professor. She makes herself available outside of class and is always willing to answer questions during class. Each class period she shows a cool Youtube video about fluids.
Her tests are very difficult and heavily weighted: two midterms at 15% each and 25% final. Homework won't save you so make sure you're ready for the tests. Beware of pop quizzes.

Kind and funny! Wants to help everyone understand and pass. The tests aren't too bad if you have done the homework, so be prepared for them. She gives great feedback on the tests and in class though. I felt that the homework was slightly more challenging than the tests, so understand the homework and practice tests!

Professor Damron is definitely the best professor to take UNIV101 from. She made the class enjoyable rather than boring. She eliminated the daily discussions, which saved us from a lot of unnecessary work. She is very endearing and sweet.

100% recommend. Prof Damron is an angel. The readings and discussion questions are optional (this is unique to Prof Damron! other profs will make you do them!!!), so the only assignments you have to focus on are the activities, and she's very generous on those grades. You are graded on participation, but her classes are hands-on, engaging and fun.

Honestly, such an amazing UNIV teacher. Very discussion-based class, and she just really wanted us to all be best friends with each other haha. Also she didn't make us do the daily readings/ discussions (which I haven't heard of any other UNIV teachers doing) so TAKE HER! She's the best :)

She was an amazing Univ teacher, very grateful for the way she ran the class, because I had so many friends that struggled in their UNIV class due to the amount of homework. Thankfully she took away the writing portions of the homework and just allowed for you to enjoy the readings and not do busy work. She often brought treats to class!

She is a good choice for a professor but you only see her 10 or so times during the semester. Because of this it's easy to feel distant from her and when you talk to her in person she can seem a little disinterested. But she's still nice and polite. TA matters more than prof for KOR 101.

This is a linguistics and not a Korean class if you're looking for language improvement. Dr. Damron has great lectures, and I learned so much about language structure including Korean. The tests are group projects. You only need to know what we go over in class. Dr. Damron is respectful, kind, and caring. Highly recommend taking this with her.

I was only with her once a week (TA choice is so important!), but she tried to have fun activities and bring treats when we did. The class itself is fairly easy - 1 week per chapter, with a vocab quiz or unit test (2 chapters) alternating on Fridays. Thur was online and doesn't take too long. You see everyone everyday, so I made some great friends!
Shes a great professor. Had good people in the class and the class ain't bad. Nothing life changing tho
Dr. Damron is super nice! However, you only see her once a week the other days are with TAs so make sure you get a good TA!

Dr. Damron is a remarkable teacher. She is so, so nice, but notices everything that students do and do not do. If you try to let attendance or assignments slide just because she's nice, she will penalize you. Her expertise is language acquisition and linguistics, so you will learn a lot about the scientific essence of Korean.

Julie is a good teacher that cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She doesn't make it too hard; you have to do the assignments and study for the tests but she is a forgiving grader. I didn't buy the textbooks. It helped that I had taken an intro to linguistics class but wasn't necessary.

I really liked Professor Damron! However, I couldn't really get to know her because I only had her on Tuesdays. Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays were spent with our TAs and Thursday class was online. I liked Professor Damron, but if you get a bad TA, you have to learn on your own from the textbook. The class also goes fast - one chapter a week.
I love her! I would definitely recommend a class with Professor Damron. She loves her topic and works with the students. Always available when I need her.

Professor Damron loves the Korean culture and that makes her an effective teacher because she is passionate about sharing it. She is invested in helping her students succeed and makes herself available as much as possible which is great!  She gives good feedback, and opportunities to take on extra credit. I would definitely recommend her classes.

We had some issues with the TA but that comes with most classes. Prof Damron was a life saver. The class looked forward to her lessons because she teaches so simple and clearly. She loves Korean and is willing to work with students

I've taken almost all the classes she's offered (102, 201, 325) and I honestly think she's the best professor at BYU. She's SO approachable and honestly cares about her students. Tests aren't that difficult, as long as you just pay attention and take notes (especially if you take her 325 class). But other than that, I strongly recommend taking her!

I've been at BYU for two years now and every semester I take a Korean class from her. I've taken 101, 102, 201, 325. She's amazing. Super sweet and so willing to help you out if you're struggling. Her tests aren't that hard as long as you pay attention and she basically tells you what's going to be on the test so you don't have to study EVERYTHING.

Julie is probably one of the best teachers I have ever had at BYU. If you are a bad student, you will not do well in her classes (obvious), but if you take notes and study 4 or 5 hours for  the quizzes, you can ace them every time. Her 325 class is simple to get an A in and she teaches it well. She also oversees 495 and does a great job there too.

I was weary about taking writing 150 my first semester mostly because I could not find anything on Professor Hollenbaugh. However, I was pleasantly surprised at how caring she is and how willing she is to help you out. Our inquiry report took up to 6 weeks to complete, but at the end of the unit she brought us cookies! Definitely recommend

Professor Schow is an amazing person. She is very knowledgeable and is super passionate about the field of speech-language pathology. However, I did not enjoy her particular teaching style or the class content. The class felt like an advertisement for ASHA, which I disliked.

This professor was fine but I wish she'd revamp the class. It should be project based. She has exams over information about professional practices that shouldn't be memorized but referenced. I found it to be a waste of time.

While Professor Schow was helpful because of her passion for this topic, there were quite a few unprofessional moments. The tests often weren't written until right before the exam making it difficult for TAs to make a review for us and whenever we gave her feedback (that she asked for) she got very defensive - creating an uncomfortable environment
Professor Schow is SOOOOO nice!!! She made us treats on Valentine's Day! She is very caring and sweet.

Julie is one of the BEST professors. She is so kind, caring, and has a lot of experience to learn from! Her lectures are sometimes a little long, but I learned so much in this class about being a true professional. Just keep up on the assignments and attend the TA review sessions, and you'll do great!
Took the online class and it was reasonably easy. There was a lot of reading but the projects and assignments were all pretty easy. Gave interesting and insightful lectures.

Everything was due at noon on Saturdays, which was annoying but ok. You can totally do the projects the day they're due (but I wouldn't recommend it). Highly recommend online, it's great to go at your own pace and Bro Dyer was good at online too. And he seemed to care about the queer community, which was a unique plus.

Great professor, does his best to remain respectful even when students disagree.
However, if you are at odds with some church beliefs, the provided explanations are not always satisfactory. Still, it is clear Prof. Dyer cares.

Everything is graded fairly, I took the online class and you really just have to do the bare minimum and can still get a lot out of the class! Easy A, midterms are just short essays based on slides, and it's open note. The final is just another midterm, not accumulative.

Prof. Dyer is incredibly caring and makes for a really fun class. I was hesitant about UNIV 101 because it seemed unnecessary, but Prof. Dyer makes it enjoyable. He really is just so caring and shows that to each of his students. I can't speak for his religion classes, but I imagine he shows the same care to all of his students like his UNIV class.

This is one of the newer classes that just got added and when comparing my teacher to my friends teachers, Prof dyer proves to be the best. He leads really good discussions and he truly cares about each of his students. You can learn so many interesting stuff from him and it's best if you participate and work on getting to know him as well.

Personally and generously answered so many of my important and complex questions. Usually not much reading. Invaluable! Teaches family and doctrine. Few, tough papers. EXTREMELY caring individual. There's a comment here that ridiculously claims that he is not - couldn't be further from the truth! I revere this man!

Bro Dyer is so kind and knowledgeable! If you struggle with the gospel or certain political issues, he tries to be very unbiased and just tell you "this is what the church doctrine is." He doesn't grade you on your testimony. He takes your questions and concerns seriously, and respects any doubts or struggles. Tackles tough subjects very well.

Professor Dyer is great! A lot of people mentioned in reviews that there's a lot of writing, but that isn't the case. While there is about 3-4 papers to write, they are very simple, straight to the point, and quite edifying. Just make sure you're on top of the. And if you are an active member of the church, the exams should be common sense!

This felt more like an apologetics and social studies class with that left more questions than answers. I always felt a stupor of thought and a strong lack of direction or conclusion in his lectures. It was just a ton of "here's why this isn't what we believe". Not necessarily against church doctrine but trust me, take a different professor
Professor Dyer does a great job with caring for his students' opinions. The classes were quite interesting and the homework was straight-forward and simple.

He cares so much about his students. I took his class a year ago, and when I randomly ran into him last week, he stopped me to say hello, and he even remembered my name. He is such a genuinely good person, and he is great at answering questions about sensitive subjects.

I have completed all of my religion hours at BYU. This class was by far the worst one. Gave way more work than necessary. Wasn't an enjoyable lecturer either. Would not recommend taking this class with professor dyer.
Don't take from him. He makes the religion class so difficult with a lot of course load.

Lots of readings required, but it's all online for you. 1 midterm and a final, both you get 1 page of notes. Lectures were absolutely incredible and he has strengthened my testimony on the Eternal family.

I really liked this class when I was in the lectures, but then I'd go home to the hours of homework and would like it a little less. Dr. Dyer is great, very kind, and treats the sometimes harsh subject matter with respect. But he doesn't give exceptions, and you have 5 essays to write throughout the semester... like it's a religion class.

While bro dyer is such a nice guy, this class was not a good fit for me . We had to write SO many essays that were 5-7 pages. He is very caring towards his students but the work he assigned was just so much busy work. There were SO many readings. He is very respectful to his students and does a great job talking about some difficult subjects.

This class was interesting and Dyer is super nice, but it was way too much work for a 2-credit class. Readings took me up to 3-4 hours and there's a paper about every other week. Attendance and applications are due every class which are easy though time-consuming. Tests were easy (similar to seminary tests) but classwork was very heavy.

If you want to write 5 1500 word essays and do 3+ hours of reading a week, take this class. Also if you want to fail for missing one class, take this class. Lets just say if you take this class, you're gonna be in a "dyer" situation, as my roommates would say. Save yourself and get out. Wayyyy too difficult for a religion class.

Professor Dyer is a must take! His class is super easy compared to all other classes. He is a super nice guy and truly loves all his students. You take an attendance grade (5min) and a weekly application (10min) and that is majority of the class.

This class has loads of work. Way too much for a mandatory religion class. What could have been a couple of heartfelt discussions a week and some good material turned into mountains of reading and writing. Too much writing to get done for me to stop and really think about what I was saying and produce quality work. Got to hit word counts.

I wanted to like Professor Dyer, but I did not like this class. I felt like there were several assignments that could have been completed in a couple pages, but I was forced to rephrase things I already said and make things up in order to fulfill the page requirement. I would not recommend this class if you're not a writer.

The lectures/discussions were very engaging. Brother Dyer cares a lot for the material and for his class. The tests were really difficult (there's a lot of short essays). I never felt like I did well on a test but my grade was always decent. Don't forget to do the attendance homework after every class.

Dr. Dyer is super fun and respectful! I learned a lot from his class. He is great for students that are willing to work hard and apply themselves to the material taught. 
If you're looking for an easy, low effort religion class, Dr. Dyer might not be for you as there is quite a bit of homework and several essays.

Attendance is the major grade killer - I'd forget to mark my attendance on LS before it was due at midnight, resulting in my very low grade. SO MANY PAPERS, need to write a short reflection after every unit (basically every class) and 5 longer papers on top of that.
Tests were great - 1 page notes on midterms, open note/book for the final!

Overly hard, the stupid assignment takes work too seriously for what should be an uplifting class; class designed for snob molly Mormon success, not diverse members.... says will help students, mentioned several times I needed it, never responded....

If you are looking for an easy eternal family credit, this is not the class for you. Two of our papers throughout the semester amounted to 11 pages each for me, so this is no cakewalk. Prof. Dyer is an amazing person and you will learn a lot from his class IF you apply the material.

Professor Dyer is amazing. His lectures are powerful, loving, and sensitive. The homework he gives is manageable and meaningful. He genuinely wants to help you as a student and individual. Not a hard class and I feel like I really benefitted spiritually.

Brother Dyer is a great person. I loved his class. He really knows and cares about what he is teaching. Sometimes it felt too much like a statistics or psychology class rather than religion. There is a lot of reading and you have to go to class for credit. Overall, it was a good class!

Basically this class will hit you with a massive essay every 3 weeks on repeat. I wouldn't recommend taking this class purely because of the essays. Professor Dyer teaches a good class however the amount of essays and the sheer length of them is very grueling. I felt like I was taking an English writing class again with the format requirements.

The concepts taught by Professor Dyer are simple, and all seemed to be variations on similar ideas making the class quite boring. There was a lot of reading assigned for every class period, but honestly you can get away with not doing them. Also, the papers assigned felt more like busy work than anything actually meaningful as others have mentioned

Professor Dyer is just a caring guy. Class was a cinch. I just did the reading during lunch everyday (most you can find audio) and showed up to class. Everything is application based. There are pretty much no real tests during the course. He just has students write papers. It is just applying the doctrine to your circumstance through each paper.

Professor Dyer's lectures were great. I loved going to class, but the papers you have to write are dumb. Now that I know that if I took another class from him I'd try to get my papers done early. Lots of reading too

Brother Dyer is a very nice man. I was excited to take this class, but I was completely disappointed. There's a reason that religion classes are 2 credits. There was wayy too much homework, the essays were absolutely pointless, and he presented the family from a very narrow point of view, to the point of being offensive at times.

Dr Dyer is a great professor. He really loves the church and is passionate about what he teaches. The class has 4 essays that feel more like busy work than useful assignments. There are also no tests which is nice. Dr Dyer is awesome but he does fall short when students have differing opinions from him or bring up facts he didn't know.

Brother Dyer was a really personable guy! I thought his lectures were great and were interesting. But, the assignments he gave us seemed pretty pointless. We had a couple essays that I felt like I was supposed to bs. Like that was the purpose for me to write them. He tried tying it in the the class content, but it was pretty useless to me.

Dr. Dyer is a very intelligent professor who really knows what he is talking about. I loved taking Eternal Families with him. He explains the material very well and easily invites the spirit into his class. He cares for each one of his students and really wants them to succeed in the class. Only a few easy papers and two exams!

Dyer cares about his students but he doesn't give much time or instructions for his papers. These papers by the way are the majority of your grade,, but there aren't many of them and you can usually crank them out in an afternoon. Don't expect extra credit but do expect to learn tons about yourself and your family from this class.

I took The Eternal Family during summer term with Dr Dyer and thoroughly enjoyed it! Awesome Professor who really cares about the students and the controversial topics we discuss together in this class. Very open and fair. Some assignments take more time than others, but mostly an easy religion class that is for your benefit! Dyer rocks!

He's a nice caring guy. A family man... which is fitting. The four-ish papers are thorough, but overall the class does not require too much out of class time. Especially on a week to week basis. The final is nothing to worry about... which is a nice contrast.

He is a wonderful teacher who really cares about what he teaches. His eternal family class was one of my favorite classes this semester. I learned a lot and I'm grateful that he respected other views on controversial subjects.

Brother Dyer for Eternal Families is my number 1 religion class! He includes statistics when he makes statements and lets everyone know that what he is teaching is supported by numbers but is not necessarily how every family works. He is kind, caring, and takes the time to help each student. The class had a reasonable amount of work as well!

Dr. Dyer is AMAZING. He makes lectures interesting & funny, but still teaches everything needed for papers (No tests! 4 papers + a final)He creates discussions in class & makes sure everyone's opinion is validated. He also isn't shy about topics that aren't as frequently discussed. There is daily reading, just don't procrastinate and you'll be fine

While I did not agree with much of what was taught, he really believed it and it was apparent he cares about students and wants them to be successful. Getting an A required close to no hard work, just a few essays to sit down and knock out.
Dr. Dyer is awesome!! Easiest class ever. You can tell he really cares about his students!

Best professor I ever had. No tests, just the occasional paper, like 1 a quarter. His lectures consistently changed the way I think and he taught with and brought the spirit when he did so. Would absolutely recommend. I took notes not because I needed to, but because I wanted to have them for when I start my own family. Amazing man and teacher.

Dr. Dyer is literally the sweetest man. He cares about all his students and learned all our names before the first day of class. He tries to touch on things from multiple perspectives and does not force his views on us. He brings up things we don't really talk about much in the LDS church, which is valuable. Highly recommend taking from him!

Brother Dyer is a wonderful professor for this subject matter. I was scared I would get a stuffy old man who was far too "traditional". He is the exact opposite. Extremely inclusive and you can see that he really does care about the Family.

Professor Dyer is awesome! His lectures are in-depth and we went over so many interesting and new things (even for a member from age 8). Even if you skip the class (which I don't recommend since it's for a grade), you have a solid chance of getting a high grade. Very nice and inclusive!

He doesn't give tests only papers, which I actually liked. I believe that you're able to better control your grade with papers. Grades on the different papers were a little subjective between the two TA's. Attendance is for a grade and part of the attendance quiz is asking if you did all the reading. There is a good amount of reading, but worth it.

Unique class style not for everyone but I loved it. No tests, instead papers. Many lectures focus on family dynamics, communication, very practical. Great in-class discussions. Dyer is sensitive and respectful if someone disagrees. Refreshingly inclusive. If you have unorthodox perspectives or are more socially liberal, you probably would want him!

Dr. Dyer is a fantastic religion professor. So long as you do your readings before class, and mark your participation, you'll do well in the class. He genuinely cares about each student's perspective, and makes an effort to focus on doctrine, not culture.

The class structure was great if you like writing papers instead of taking tests. But you need to beware of false doctrine. It also doesn't make any sense to be talking about politics in Eternal Families. Dr. Dyer just has a really hard time saying "I don't know" and he needs to do it. Because he did say a lot of hurtful things that were opinion.
Dr. Dyer is honestly the best.  He is super passionate and smart.  He loves participation and it makes the class more interesting.  No tests, just 3 essays.

Dyer has this Eternal Families class well organized. No tests, No text book! There is a required set of readings (talks and scriptures) for each new topic about once per week. Readings take a few hours so you have to space it. 2/week attendance quizzes ask how much reading you finished. A few lengthy papers. He addresses student comments in class.

THIS CLASS WAS ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC. HE CARES ABOUT HIS STUDENTS. HIS LECTURES ARE REALLY HELPFUL IN REAL LIFE AND I LOVED GOING TO HIS CLASS. COLLEGE IS HARD BECAUSE YOU ARE AWAY FROM FAMILY BUT I ALWAYS FELT SO AT HOME IN HIS CLASS HE KNEW MY NAME AND I WOULD SERIOUSLY RECOMMEND THIS CLASS.
Very boring lectures as well as ignorant views. Don't take him for religion.

You will get an A. Show up, complete the 2 page papers, and you will get an A. brother dyer is the best religion teacher at byu. His lectures are amazing and so relevant to marriage and family. NO tests!! he believes in actual application then memorizing. Apply what you've learned, make a report of it, and that is your grade for the class.

Dr. Dyer's class was the most easy class I had this semester, but it lacked substance about the Savior. It was much more a family science class than religious class, with it being new and all. Go to him, get an easy A, do the responses, and listen. He's a caring guy.  But don't expect to feel the spirit in his class. TONS OF READING.

Prof. Dyer is great. The class? Yawn. Not as spiritual as a religion class, not as rigorous as a sociology class. Seems like they're still ironing out the kinks. The readings hardly ever made it into our class discussion. Don't be late on any of the assignments.

This class was really low key but super useful. There are no tests, only papers, but they are pretty straightforward. Sometimes the lectures would get a bit off topic and we always seemed to be trying to catch up, but overall it was a good class. Sometimes I felt like he let the discussion go on for too long when we clearly needed to move on.

Super chill class. There are not tests and only 4 papers throughout the semester that are super simple if you just do them. A paragraph response is required for each class, but that's it. Often goes off on tangents but since there aren't any test it doesn't really matter. Great professor.

On the upside, Dr. Dyer really cares about his students. He would sit down and read comments made on readings before lecture, and when necessary he'd be willing to meet and talk. That said, his class felt extremely unorganized (granted, the course was new), and lecture often went off on tangents and unrelated discussion. Tons of reading.

Bro Dyer is a million bucks. Knows his stuff about the family, lives as a good example. Always happy to talk with you one on one about the class or about anything you need help with. Lots of readings but uplifting to read. A few projects that were very beneficial. However, grading was AWFUL. Still haven't seen my grade for mid-term project.

I do not have any idea how he is as a family studies professor, but do not take a religion class from him. Worst religion class I have taken at BYU in my 4 years here. It was boring and focused on the psychology and sociology of family relationships more than the gospel. To his credit though he does really care about his students.

Great Professor, Knows what he is talking about, very helpful. Encourages student participation in lectures. He is very clear. This is a class you can look forward to. Homework is not hard, about right for a 2 credit class, you just have to do it. Put honest effort into assignments.

He's Great! So passionate about The Eternal Family. His class was very enjoyable and I loved to get to know more about the topic as well. Lots of reading which will all be on the tests, but it wasn't too bad.

Dyer really loves his subject. Class is usually fairly interesting if you can pay attention. You are supposed to read the book cover to cover and journal for every chapter. There's a fair number of assignments and projects, but they were fairly easy and I still did well even though grading was all over the place.  There's 3 non-comprehensive exams.

Dr. Dyer is a great teacher! The class is also very interesting. Read the textbook. Quizzes in class on the chapter but if you read the textbook, you should do good on those. Tests are pretty good. Mostly from the slides, but some from the book. Go to reviews. Multiple papers/projects through semester but they are easy. I HIGHLY recommend Dr. Dyer!

It took me a while to get used to how Prof. Dyer talks: which is in circles. The book is just as bad. Easy reading quizzes at the beginning of 1/3 of the classes. A few busy-work (but easy) papers. Go to the TA exam reviews and study the slides and you will ace the tests. Easy A.

Dr. Dyer was an excellent teacher!! He was really good at making all concepts clear, he is very open and respectful of other people's experiences and viewpoints and just genuinely loves what he does. Take this class from him. Really.

Professor Dyer is great! His lectures are very entertaining and interesting. The tests aren't too hard, if you pay attention in class and at least skim over the reading. He does pop quizzes, but you get half the points just for showing up. The short papers and projects are fun and helpful to your learning. I definitely recommend him!
Really great teacher.  Very nice and willing to answer questions.
Nice, Nice guy!  The course material itself is very pointless.  The class is required for a lot of majors.  Make certain to go to the test reviews, otherwise you will do poorly.

really good teacher! i didn't think this class would be interesting at all, but he made it good. the tests aren't bad if you study and go to class. you have to write short essays and do small projects, but they're easy too. all in all, good teacher, and really helpful class! i really recomend him
