Good and caring professor, but his classes are just you on your own doing a project or listening to a random classmate talking about a random popular cybersecurity professional, so the classes are not really engaging, but attendance is pretty much required to get the final exam project software all set up.

I loved the way this class was organized. I took this Spring term so there were weekly assignments and tests. The assignments and tests were super similar and so it was low stress. He makes class engaging by playing short cartoon clips. He genuinely wants his students to succeed. Overall, low stress class and a great professor!

Class each day was applied work on the computers which was great. Homework assignments were Hack the Box (HTB) labs, which were good but a lot of reading and hard to get invested in. In-class assignments had little to do with HTB, but exams required HTB knowledge. You will get a good grade as long as you do all the HTB labs.

Good and caring professor, but his classes are just you on your own doing a project or listening to a random classmate talking about a random popular cybersecurity professional, so the classes are not really engaging, but attendance is pretty much required to get the final exam project software all set up.

I loved the way this class was organized. I took this Spring term so there were weekly assignments and tests. The assignments and tests were super similar and so it was low stress. He makes class engaging by playing short cartoon clips. He genuinely wants his students to succeed. Overall, low stress class and a great professor!

Class each day was applied work on the computers which was great. Homework assignments were Hack the Box (HTB) labs, which were good but a lot of reading and hard to get invested in. In-class assignments had little to do with HTB, but exams required HTB knowledge. You will get a good grade as long as you do all the HTB labs.

Justin is a really great professor! He's an amazing artist and doesn't hesitate to share everything he knows. I took DESIL 130 from him and the projects were a lot of fun. His grading on projects was a little harsh, I think, but he always gave helpful feedback and chances to improve our grades. He also a funny and great person :)

Been in all his classes, Justin is wonderful:

Relaxed teaching style (understanding of struggles/concerns, will help if asked, flexible with grades & HW)
Highly accessible (regular office hours, talks during/after class, face-2-face best)
Loves to talk (knowledgeable, great conversation, explores the nuance of subjects taught)

10/10 recommend

Justin is a great teacher, and I learned a lot from him. He understands that everyone isn't in the same major, or that everyone is in different skill levels and he takes time to work with you individually as needed. He makes sure we understand the assignment before setting us loose or giving it as homework.

Easily my favorite class I have taken thus far at BYU.  Justin is a great teacher and person to know.  Would recommend this class to anyone beginning a career in the design field.  He worked at Blizzard, Disney, and paints.  Really incredible artist.  My only complaint is we read out of the textbook in class to learn perspective and it was boringgg

I love Weid!! I am so thankful I got to take his class, I loved it! He is so caring and he knows your name the first day of class. If you do the work and ask for help, you'll get a good grade. Take notes and study the powerpoints before quizzes! #yougottawanna

CFM 105 material-wise is a breeze. The assignments and projects are tedious but interesting. The HW is the most heavily graded aspect of the class (I didn't do 1 assignment and that dropped me to the B+). The tests are easy and in class. Weidman is a great man and mentor!
Weidman rocks #yougottawanna
He keeps beating me in cornhole

I love Brother Weidman. He is one of the best professors at BYU, and definitely one of the most caring. All of the information he teaches is highly relevant to the field, and homework is never just busywork.

Bro Weidman is a good teacher. He often rushes the power points and is pretty vague about what's on tests and assignments. The TA's are the hardest part of the class. They grade very harshly and often deduct points for things that aren't even on the rubrics.

Brother Weidman is a little bit of an odd duck but he cares about every student. His class is great though and I learned so much. I never know what he thinks about me. His assignment instructions are always so vague but I feel like he does that on purpose.

This is such a fun class, but for an intro class, I feel like the class was thrown into a lot of things. While Professor Weidman did teach us quite a bit, homework assignments were explained rather shortly and I felt like I had to self teach a couple of things. But, it is a fun class, and you do learn a lot. End of the year projects can pile up.

Justin Weidman is one of the best professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students, knows them by name and sets you up for success in the field. Everything he teaches is incredibly relevant and If you can get it all you will be great in the field. I wish I could take it again.

Brother Weidman is awesome! He teaches well, and also incorporates the gospel in his classes. There are a few different softwares you will learn, but if you ask for help he or the TAs will provide it. Instead of a final there is a group project, so make sure you are with high performers.

Brother Weidman is the most organized person I have ever met. I really appreciate him and his insight. You should take time to get to know him. He actually memorizes everyone's names in the program, and he really cares about the students. His classes were always straightforward and engaging.
Great teacher, would 10/10 recommend. He cares about his students a lot and teaches in a great way that makes it easier to learn.

I loved Bro Weidman's electrical class. He was always ready to explain things for students who didn't understand and work one-on-one after class if you need a few extra minutes. He cares a lot about your spiritual health. With the exception of one assignment, everything was very related to class and easy with what we had learned. The lab is great.

Just do your work and you will get an A. Some of the projects can be time consuming but nothing too hard. He is very fair. Also study for the quizzes. Doing well on those will greatly boost your grade.

The badly crafted assignments cause students to spend more time trying to figure out what's required on the assignment than actually doing the assignment. He's more keen on whether you have a beard (university grooming policy) than whether you learned the class material. He reads straight from his notes, doesn't seem competent with the material.

I love Bro. Weidman! He does a great job at explaining concepts or ideas in multiple different ways if you are confused. He loves teaching specifics to the class but also big picture life lessons. His test are a bit challenging because he uses a lot of fill in the blank questions. However, he teaches everything you need to know for the test.

Bro. Weidman is super nice, and I thought his class was easy. He gives extra points for the people who come to class all the time so that's nice. He does get super bitter about students who don't show up though. He said his class would be hard and honestly it was WAY easier than anything else I've taken. Loved the class, it's kind of a joke though.
His class is great if you want to learn more about philosophy. He gives clear outlines on what he wants you to do. It's philosophy so you read alot. He makes it fun and cracks alot of good jokes.

Creates a very engaging environment that is enlightening even if you do not have a concerted interest in philosophy. Hilarious, excellent at answering questions, very strong at explaining difficult concepts. Lots of reading, three essays, but it could be a lot worse. Offers chance to improve grade over thesemester. Midterm and final not bad at all.

The actual class period was engaging and often interesting, but I spent more time outside of class on the homework than anticipated. Lots of reading and writing. The course felt a bit unorganized, and the grading criteria wasn't always clear.

It is easy to do well. There is a TON of reading. 3 essays, 2 exams, weekly reflections. Never provided a rubric for essays, so everything was graded arbitrarily. I would get 2 comments on my essay and then an 84?? He says hE nEvEr HaNdS oUt an A. Nice guy and interesting topics, but an unorganized class. We frequently got behind schedule.

I really liked him! I was nervous to take this class at first, but I ended up liking the class and did better than I thought. There are three papers, two exams, and weekly readings and reflections. It is a lot of reading and writing, but definitely manageable. He was really good about giving feedback and wants to make sure you do well in the class.

I really enjoyed this class. I've never taken a philosophy class but he did a great job at making the topics applicable to my life. The grading is a bit harsh but he offeres extra credit and tries to help you to end the class with a good grade. If you work with the TA and try to follow the criteria he gives you should have no problem getting an A.

Harder than I anticipated for a 110 level class. Grading was a major issue. No rubrics for the 4 papers and final paper. Following outlines still didn't guarantee a high grade(>93%). What really bothered me is he repeatedly ask us to leave positive reviews in class and multiple emails, trying to manipulate feedback to counteract the low reviews.

Justin White is the Best! He does a class around "The Good Place" which makes philosophy so much more understandable and accessible. I am so grateful I got to take his class, I learned and gained so much from what he taught me :)

This is one of my favorite classes so far! You can do well in the class if you put in the work. Dr. White and the TAs are willing to help. You're expected to write four papers and then the final. There are weekly reflections too. Keep up with the readings and the class is manageable. I recommend this class to everyone. Super fun topics!

I think the negative reviews for this class are way too harsh. Prof. White explains what he wants and will give outlines for the papers. Expectations are fair as long as you actually attend class and pay attention. If you do the readings and pay attention, you'll probably do fine. And you can talk with Prof. White or the TAs for help.

Professor White is a good professor and the way he teaches and runs his class is fair. I believe that the 1-3 star reviews are far too negative. The papers and the readings are time-consuming, and he is generally too harsh of a grader for a general class, almost nobody gets above 94% on any assignment minus rare circumstances. His Ta's are helpful.

Dr. White is wonderful! He is always welcoming and kind. He wants the best for his students. He keeps readings manageable, but also encourages us to research on our own to learn more about our interests. He will do all he can to make sure that you do well in the course. I highly recommend taking his classes!

Each time I've taken his classes I'm impressed with the depth and breadth of his knowledge on the material, willingness to work closely with students on their papers and advise on academic/career goals. He is deeply invested in each student's success. Class is discussion-based— he does close guided readings of certain texts rather than powerpoints!

I LOVED this class!! Prof White cares about his students and the topics are super interesting. We talked about living a meaningful life and we got to watch The Good Place. Super fun class and you learn a lot! Prof. White is one the best professors i've had so far. His lectures are good and he throws in jokes and knows how to make the class engaging

For those who say the grading was harsh, I disagree. Professor White is open to talking about your papers beforehand and will give you good feedback. He is caring and wants to help you succeed but you need to make the effort to seek help

Professor White is a great guy, and he genuinely cares about this class. However, it's incredibly challenging to get a good grade in Philosophy 110, which is a GE 100 level class. There are four papers, but the grading criteria seem contradictory and not represented on the rubric. Emailing him appears as though it's a burden. TA was very good.

A funny and great professor. The class is mostly discussion-based with some lecturing. I enjoyed the class a lot. Professor White cares about his class and the topics, and he knows every student's name. I recommend taking a class from him

He knows his students by name. Being a philosophy class, there are a lot of readings due each class period. I think they could have been condensed. It was hard to ask questions and not feel slightly inferior. He is willing to meet during office hours. I understand philosophy may be a hard subject to teach. Constantly reading or writing.

Professor White puts lots of effort into his curriculum. He's funny, quick-witted, and quick to challenge statements. It may seem harsh, but it's a good practice in philosophy and he's always very nice about it! Writing-centric class; is a good opportunity to practice those skills weekly. Plenty of reading, but it's all interesting and well-chosen!

I love Professor White! The class is very discussion based, and he does a good job explaining the concepts and answering questions. He's very accessible and willing to help, and I feel like he genuinely cares about his students. This was a class I looked forward to every week, and I'd definitely recommend giving it a try.

I love Dr. White's classes. For personal reasons, I couldn't finish this class, but Dr. White was incredibly caring and offered support to help me succeed. He is willing to meet with you outside of class to discuss your paper and other interests. I highly recommend taking a class from Dr. White. He's an amazing professor and a great person to know.

Dr. White is an incredible professor who cares about his students and his classes. He is willing to work with you outside of class to discuss exams, papers, or other interests in philosophy. The class does require that you keep up with the reading and really engage with the text(s), but once again, Dr. White is there to help you and discuss things.

Professor White is a great teacher because he is clear in his expectations and tells students how to be successful in his class. He expects you to be a responsible adult. He teaches the material well and if you pay attention during class you will be just fine.

I really respect Dr. White. He's accessible outside of class and patient and helpful when you don't understand something. He's understanding of personal situations as long as you let him know. Genuinely loves teaching. There's a fair amount of homework that adds up. Don't procrastinate the papers. Do the readings. Class is largely discussion-based.

Professor White is a funny and upbeat guy.  Most assignments in the class are pretty easy to score well on so long as you do the readings. The papers did seem to be graded pretty intensely and felt slightly unproportionally graded compared to the weekly writing assignments. To enjoy this class you have to be engaged otherwise it can be boring.

professor white is a good professor and he makes class generally interesting and entertaining. he can be a little bit abrupt in the way he responds to questions or concerns so just be aware of that. it has been brought to his attention, and he seems to genuinely care and want to do better. is willing to help you be successful. tough-ish grader.

He was one of the rudest professors I have ever had. He would shut down students' comments and make them feel stupid. His lectures were all over the place and usually extremely unhelpful. He focused a lot more on the literary elements of the texts than the actual philosophy. The amount of assigned reading was crazy for how dense it was.

Cares about his students, he notices when you are there in class. He takes role every day so make sure you go. There are a lot of readings for this class but then again, it is a philosophy class. I do feel that some of the readings could be condensed. This was a hard class though and took up a lot of my time. Use the TAs, they grade your papers.

The lack of clear expectations in this class makes this class unbearable. No rubrics with point values are given and every time anyone asks a questions or talks in class they are seen as wrong. It is hard to talk philosophy if no debates are allowed. The structure of the class is also unbearable as he mostly doesn't use slides, nothing is online.

I absolutely loved this class and Prof. White. He is so realistic and funny. Your grade is mostly on 4 papers, but they aren't very long. The final was 4 pages double spaced and that was the longest one. He understands it's an intro course, and is willing to adjust earlier paper grades if you show progress so that your grade reflects that.

He's ok, but assigns a ton of reading. Not very organized, and you are always confused on what he requires of you. He tries to really get to know you- he knew everyone's names in class. That being said, I'm generally an A student, but because I didn't understand what he required and I felt a bit of unfair grading coupled with that I got a B+

This is the teacher who has you watch the Good Place and discuss it in class. It's pretty great. I thought Professor White was a lot of fun, the readings weren't too much, he has you write five papers total but you have some flexibility about your prompt. He's an easy grader, I bet you'll enjoy the class.

Prof. White is great. He knows his stuff and is happy to talk with students about questions and ideas. I emailed him with questions over the summer and he was happy to reply. His lectures can feel scatterbrained, but I still did fine in the class and understood the material after working through it. An important class to take, and he's a good guy.
Not super respectful of students comments, I feel like he shut people down a lot when they discussed what they think. Pretty one-sided.

What a good dude. I always enjoy talking with Justin, and I can tell he's interested in how things are going in my life outside of school. His class is definitely worth taking whether you're just getting started in the major or are starting to take upper-division courses.
Professor White does a great job at explaining philosophical concepts, I loved his class. I learned a lot. He cares a lot about his students

There is quite of bit of reading for this class; however, it is worth it. I learned a lot from this class that is actually applicable to life. And he works with the class. He cares about each individual and is flexible. If you want a class that is not stressful, but you learn a lot, this is the class.

Professor White runs a philosophy class how they are meant to be run. He helps you to first understand the ideas and then lets you develop your own opinions and ideas. The papers were relatively easy. Although I am a good writer, I feel like he gave a better grade than I deserved. Fun class and not too difficult.

Professor White was absolutely my favorite professor. He provides easy to understand lectures and the discussions he facilitates in class are often very insightful. I also corresponded with him outside of class a few times regarding other classes and he was always friendly and eager to help. Anyone that has the chance should take a class from him.
Loved this class so much. Justin's a great guy and so nice. Great teacher too, would suggest him to anyone and everyone.

Professor White is the BEST. He combines lectures with really deep analogies that make you think, but is always cheerful and kind. If you are struggling, he is super understanding so don't be afraid to talk to him. TAKE HIS CLASS, you won't regret it!

I didn't quite enjoy the class, but that has nothing to do with Professor White. He is one of the most caring, sympathetic professors I have ever met. He really cares about the students, and pushes back due dates when the class is struggling. He teaches very clearly, but I didn't understand any of the assigned readings until I came to class.

There is nobody more fitting to teach a class on ethics, morality, and what it means to live a meaningful life than Dr. Justin White. He practices what he preaches and he truly cares about his students. I can't emphasize that enough. In this class, you'll improve your critical thinking, writing, and speaking abilities. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Professor White is great. He is passionate about the material and really wants the students in the class to succeed. His lectures are brilliant, they are a mix of just normal lecture and class interaction. Its kind of like a big conversation. They are very engaging and a great way to learn.

I'm a business major, and I took PHIL 110 as a GE. I saw Dr. White had good ratings, so I figured "what the heck, let's do it." I was pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed this class. Dr. White encourages meaningful discussion and helped me think about philosophy in a positive way I had never considered. Would highly recommend his class.

Prof. White was awesome! It's a GE class so I wasn't too excited to take philosophy, but he made philosophy interesting and relatable! Granted there were a couple of boring sections and writing papers is not my thing, but I genuinely enjoyed our in class discussions. I hope he keeps teaching this course, I hear other classes aren't so great.

Dr. White is an awesome professor overall. He really knows the content and is super funny. I struggled a lot this past semester and he took the time to help me catch up and made it possible for me to pass. I'm so glad I took his class! There is a LOT of reading and assignments pretty much every class so just stay on top of things and you'll be fine

I wasn't too sure of Dr. White to begin with, but I learned to enjoy his class more and more as the semester went on. I learned a lot in his class, much more than I was expecting to. You need to do the reading and come to class, but if you do everything and get it in on time, this is a wonderful introductory class to philosophy.

I really like Professor White!His grading is based on attendance (10%), easy reading quizzes (10%) essays and tests (short answer/essay format). There are 4 essays, a midterm (short ans only), and a final essay/exam, so few things cushion your grade. His TA is accessible and I wish I had gone to him more for essay feedback before submission.

Dr. White was a great teacher, I loved his class and he made philosophy make sense which it before was sometimes confusing. Great class and great teacher, I felt like I learned a lot but it wasn't stressful like most classes with lots of material.

Professor White always comes into class with a smile and in a peppy mood! He doesn't care if you don't have a background of philosophy and always considers your comments in discussion and doesn't make you feel stupid about any of your thoughts. He gives you the tools to succeed if you do the readings, assignments, and try on the papers.

My time here was a waste. Every class period is a one-sided discussion that is mind-numbingly dull and has no relation to your grade. Professor White is like the Elder's Quorum instructor who forgot to prepare a lesson--he shows up late and makes it up on the spot. A nice person, a lackluster professor.

Professor White is stellar! Very thought provoking and inspiring guy with really rich, interesting material and life experience. Highly recommend studying with him for a series of engaging, expansive lectures.

Professor White was amazing! He made me fall in love with Philosophy. He gives a great lecture that makes you truly enjoy what you're learning. The readings are awesome, too. Sometimes there are dense and a little difficult to understand but he always explains them in class. Amazing class, amazing professor.

Professor White is the most caring and accommodating professor that I have met during my education at BYU. He challenges students in a good way, and facilitates thought provoking discussions every class. He is someone that I admire not only as a professor and mentor, but as a person. He genuinely cares about his students.

Professor White gives great, interesting lectures, is good at explaining things, and lets the class have a lot of discussion. His grading is pretty subjective though so you have to work a lot with him and the TA on papers and getting ready for exams to know what he wants.

I really enjoyed his lectures! I have always thought philosophy to be interesting, and this course really helped me expand my idea of what philosophy is and the role that it plays in my life. You definitely need to work with the TA's and Professor White on the papers to make sure that you are headed down the right path.

Dr. White was by far one of my favorite professors at BYU. You have to keep up on the homework, and do the readings, but they aren't too long. I maybe spent 30 minutes to and hour between classes doing the homework. The classes are great because it is set up to learn together, rather than to just have him lecture. He's great at helping you get an A
Great guy. Lots of reading material so be prepared to read and then talk about it in class.

Prof White is an amazing guy. Incredibly funny, caring, and smart. The class is super interesting, and definitely will make you start to think differently. If you want to get a good grade, take notes on whatever he specifically writes down or talks about in class, come to class, and go the TA multiple times for each paper. Tests are graded easily.
Dr. White was excellent and accessible. One of the few professors that I felt actually valued student comments and input during class discussions.

Great professor that really runs his class like a graduate seminar. Great insights, great structure, and he really sets the class up as if we are all learning together. It was my first real philosophy class (I took the class through the political science department jurisprudence course), but it was super enjoyable and informative.

Professor White is great. He is genuinely interested in the success of each of his student. He gives great feedback on essays which if you follow you will do well. Tests aren't too bad either. Just try to learn the basic concepts and you will do great.

Dr White gives his workday and teaching everything he's got. He and TA offer phenomenal feedback consistently and regularly. The way to an A is very clear. It is a great GE that will improve the way you think and write. I highly suggest taking it as a GE. It is rather simple to get a good grade. He's not out to make it difficult.
Great professor. The lectures are very engaging and will definitely change your life if you let it.

Dr. White is cares about each student. There is a lot of reading, but it is an introductory philosophy course, so that should be expected. If you miss class, you'll regret it because 1)Classroom discussions were enlightening and I enjoyed having a lot of perspectives to learn from, 2)just reading won't give you enough to go on for papers and tests.

Doctor White is the best. I did not want to take philosophy at all. I had no intentions of liking it and I was not excited to take the class at all. There was a fair, in both senses of the word, amount of homework but that's expected. His tests aren't bad and, if your classmates aren't boring the class discussions are very interesting.
Too many readings. Unclear schedule. Many papers. Hard to get good grades.

Dr. White is passionate about Phil and helping his students succeed in class and beyond. He infuses his passion in his lectures and helps concepts and other key elements to stick. At times he was disorganized (which isn't out of the norm for Phil teachers), but he's willing to work things out with his students.

Dr White is awesome! One of my favorites. If you do the work and argue your points well, there's no reason you can't succeed. I've never had a more caring professor. It's very clear that he wants the best for his students. He never told me what to think, but taught me how to think for myself. I love this guy!
I loved Professor White! If I ever hear someone wants to take Philosophy for a GE I always recommend him. Class discussions were so fun and interesting.

Prof. White is a great professor! He was so kind and really cares about student's learning and growth more than just about getting assignments done. In class discussions are always fun and insightful. I feel I gained so much from this class intellectually and as a person in general. The assignments took some time, but they were totally worth it. :D

Professor White is awesome! He gives clear grading criteria and lectures are usually interesting. There is a little bit of reading, and there are a few papers, but he is clear on what he wants from you. He's very willing to help you improve and you can get definitely get an A in his class! I would definitely take another class from him!
He is nice and an understanding teacher.

This was a class that I always enjoyed coming to because of how good his lectures are. There was a lot of room for discussion, and when I did I felt like I actually contributed something. There are a good handful of papers, but I generally enjoyed writing them and felt he was a fair grader.

I took Philosophy of Law from Professor White. He did a great job at helping you understand the complex readings and relates them to everyday situations. He is very approachable and genuinely cares for your progress. It was refreshing having a professor who was so approachable yet knowledgeable.

Professor White's intro to philosophy was one of my favorite classes I've taken in my college career. He is very caring and invested in his students. The assignments he gives are fair and he always explains them thoroughly. I learned a lot in this class and would definitely recommend this class to everyone.

Professor White's class was one of my favorite GEs that I took at BYU. Though I didn't have any background in philosophy, I found it was easy to succeed if you came to class, took notes during lectures, and kept up with the readings. Tests and essays were always straightforward.

Prof White is really clear in class about the topics covered and instead of just presenting a topic he discusses it in detail using examples.  Some reading but you cover all of the assigned reading in class.  Exams were mostly essay based but if you could present and defend a topic you could get a solid grade.

Prof White is one of my favorite professors by far. His class was pretty easy if you put in the work. The tests are straightforward if you pay attention in class, he's a fair grader,  the paper prompts are clear, and he gives study guides that prepare you for the test. He's also a great human being and tries to foster friendships with his students.

Take an introductory philosophy course from Professor White. He's friendly and personable and explains heavy content in a clear way. There was a lot of reading, but that's the nature of the course. The class was paced well and I never felt like I couldn't keep up. He learns everybody's names and is approachable if you have questions.

Professor White is not only one of my favorite professors, he is an awesome guy. Do the reading, come to class, and you will have a great semester. He tries hard to be a fair grader, but he will definitely help if you reach out to him. Participate in class, the lectures are really fun when people participate!

I felt like this class wasn't as difficult as other generals I have taken at BYU. Professor White did really well at facilitating discussion and ALWAYS allowed opportunities for students to meet and chat with him. If you listen during the discussion you'll do fine on the tests. The writing isn't hard unless you couldn't care less.

Prof. White is easily one of the most down to earth professors at BYU. He will do anything to help the students. He is patient and really understands what it is like to be a student. He is young and really chill. You do need to put forth effort to do well, but it is completely bearable and he makes the topics really interesting. Lecture was great!!

there was writing from the main topics covered in class but if you pay attention its super easy! really nice guy that gets you thinking, i still talk to him when i pass him in the halls, not just about phil. personable.

LOVED this class. Prof White was just awesome; he was very good at explaining difficult ideas from the reading, too. Discussions were insightful, and I learned a lot of valuable skills in this class! Seriously. It's an easy A, as long as you attend class, participate, and do the readings (which aren't that bad). Definitely recommend Prof White!
He explained clearly some things I had always wondered about.  He's smart and he's thorough.  I never felt like my time was wasted on meaningless assignments.

Professor White is easily my favorite Professors at BYU. If you have to take PHIL 110 for a general, you should definitely take it from him! He is really passionate about philosophy and his enthusiasm is contagious. I actually found myself looking for ward to his class. He gives meaningful feedback on all papers and really cares about his students.

Prof White has an Awesome Teaching Style!  The class was structured well But if we ever wanted to dive into anything deeper we could.  His classes are how all Philosophy classes should be.   More Discussion. Less lecture/in class reading.  He also was available outside of classes too for help or just general talking  Highly Recommend His Classes!

If you are considering an introduction class to philosophy, take it from Professor White without a doubt. Although the content for philosophy classes is often heavy, he has a way of explaining it in very easy to understand examples. He is objective and kind and clearly very invested in his students and the material. A+ professor.

For Jurisprudence, Prof. White was awesome. His lectures were very loosely structured, which   allowed for a lot of discussion which I found interesting. There is TON of reading and a TON of writing, that's all it is, just five small papers and one big paper at the end, and one midterm. If you're a Philosophy major, it's nothing new.

I really liked Prof. White's PHIL 110 class. We had engaging class discussions every day, and the reading was interesting. When the text was difficult to understand, Prof. White was able to simply and clearly explain the important points. The papers were tough sometimes, but I felt like they were important for understanding the topics.

I could tell that he cared about our learning and success. Time and effort need to be put in to learn the material and write the papers, but I enjoyed the his lectures, jokes, analogies and explanation of the material. He is understanding and receptive to questions and what its like to be a student.

Great professor and great guy- he genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Very approachable if you need help outside class. Lots of reading, which can be pretty dry at times, but he does a good job of explaining the hard concepts in class. Quite a few papers, but the tests aren't too bad.

Dr White likes to use class time to review and clarify ideas from reading and to incite lively discussion. Its a philosophy class so argue using logic not feelings or personal beliefs and you will do great. Dr. White is reasonable and the class is an interesting introduction to philosophy ideas. We wrote about 4, 4-page papers duting the semester.

If I had to ever take another Philosophy class I wouldn't want it to be taught by anyone but him. I struggle with writing a lot so the fact that there is a good amount of writing made me worried I wouldn't do well in the clas. But he met with me personally a few times and was very interested in making sure I was learning and was very understanding.

You'll be hard pressed to find a professor more interested in developing a relationship with the students than Dr. White. He's knowledgable in his field of study, but not in a way that makes you feel dumb for having questions. He's willing to admit mistakes, and really tries to learn from his students. I highly recommend taking his classes. Do it.

Professor White was one of my favorite General Ed. Professors I have ever had. He took the time to learn everyone's name and really cared for each of the students. This class involves lots of discussion. The readings may be kind of confusing but Professor White alway explains them in an understandable way. I would recommend him to anyone!

I took this class to fulfill a general and really enjoyed the class. There is a decent amount of reading, but the professor spends each class going over the reading and clearly explains the hard concepts. There are four or five 2-3 page papers to do that will take some time, but as long as you pay attention in class you will do fine.

Memorized all our names. Tried to get the class engaged in discussion. Would challenge our ideas to try to help us create more sound personal ideas. He was fair with grading, but the TA I had was not helpful - don't worry, I think he graduated. Professor White  great. The TA   Miserable. Recommended him to every person signing up for Philosophy.

This course was Philosophy of Law, and White's class was very different from other Phil Law courses. The course focused primarily on philosophical theories of agency and responsibility rather than legal theory. However, the course introduced important writers in the legal philosophy conversation (Dworkin, Hart) that are crucial to jurisprudence.

Professor White makes philosophy class what college should be. I loved the discussions we had and I learned a ton. I didn't buy the book (I just borrowed it from another student) and I was still able to get all of the homework done.  The tests can be tough, but if you study you'll do great. He'll help you prepare well. Professor White rocks!

Very good at facilitating discussion. He really knows his stuff so if you're serious about philosophy, take classes from him. He's also extremely accessible and is truly genuine about his students being successful. If you're taking a class from him just because you need a general filled, realize that philosophy is inherently difficult.

TONS of papers. Very disorganized. Syllabus and LS schedule didn't match up. Grading harshly. He expects to have perfect philosiphical backgrouds. I took this class simply because it is a 100 level class and to fulfill graduation requirements. It should be easy, but NO. I am a 3.91 student, I think I can comment how hard this is. Believe it or not

I am a political science major and I have never taken a philosophy class in my life, but I was pleasantly surprised in how much I enjoyed the class, and I always felt it was a great environment to learn in. Professor White didn't treat me any differently because I knew little about philosphy. He was very respectful and inspiring. He loves his job.

very disorganized, he uses his own form of a syllabus that he loosely uses, this makes turning in assignments and keeping up difficult. he doesn't use powerpoints so note taking is almost impossible. you write papers and they aren't too hard. he is nice but not very merciful. he takes attendance so that is annoying seeing that we are adults.

Prof. White is a really good guy with good intentions, but he's really disorganized. There were so many times when the majority of the class didn't know an assignment was due,  and we just found out about it class the day it was due. He's really passionate about philosophy,  but I wouldn't say he's very good at explaining complex subjects.

The lectures were generally interesting enough and it wasn't a super difficult course load, but the difficult part about it all is the professor's lack of organization. It is difficult to know when things are actually due and he doesn't follow the syllabus very closely in assignments. Show up at class sometimes and you find out something was due.

Great professor, especially considering how young he is. You can tell he cares for students, the material. The lectures can be dry at times; but he does a good job of explaining concepts with a sense of humor.  Grading criteria could be more clear, but I'm sure he'll improve that within a year or so. I'd take him again only once he addresses that.
Lectures were engaging - lots of discussion. He really cares about the students. If you go to class and do the readings, you won't have any trouble getting a good grade. I would highly recommend him!
No clear grading criteria; not very respectful of other students' comments. He tries though.

So glad I took this class from Kaden. I learned so much and grew in my writing, but he also had inspiring lectures that made me want to be a better person. His story on the last day of class about charity and rhetoric was really powerful and I'll never forget it. Take from him if you want to grow your faith, work hard, and really learn!
Kaden is amazing! Took this class during summer: it was definitely a lot of work, but absolutely worth it. He is strict but also caring. He is also so funny! take it from him you will learn a lot!

Took during a summer term so the workload was a LOT. Professor Nelson cares for his students though and will make you fall in love with writing again if you lost it. He has a strict attendance policy and really expects in class participation but iyou'll become a better writer in his class if you do the work. Highly recommend.

Kaden cares so much about his students and made an 8:00 AM GE a lot less miserable than it could have been. He's really picky with attendance because this class requires a lot of group and partner work in class, but I learned a lot from him and I'm glad I took this class from him!
Fun class and funny professor. Assignments were pretty easy as long as you put in some work and paid attention to expectations.

Attendance REALLY matters. Make sure you are on time. If you are not a punctual person Professor Nelson may not be the best fit for you. That being said Professor Nelson is awesome. Lectures were always engaging even with the class being an hour and 15. Professor Nelson is a very fair grader and clearly laid out what was expected with assignments.
He does a good job of helping students that want to learn and improve writing.

Professor Nelson did an excellent job teaching the content of the class in an engaging way, and I have a greater appreciation and love for writing and rhetoric after taking his class. He is pretty scrupulous with attendance policy and with grading major essays, but he always gives enlightening feedback on why he graded something the way he did.
Kaden is good at teaching the material and relating it to current events to help encourage further understanding. He knows his stuff, and he relates to the class well.
Super fun class. It was awesome, and I learned a lot! It was interesting and useful. He cares about the students and is willing to help.
Kaden was a good professor. He has a lot of interesting ideas, and all the assignments are super easy.

Professor Nelson is the best. I hated english and writing before taking this class and I grew to like it a lot more over the semester. He wants you to have your own voice and style as a writer. He'd bring donuts when we did peer reviews, always responded to emails quick, and gave super detailed feedback on essays. Love him! Take WRTG150 from him!

Great guy, but very unclear. I wish we could do more in the class, because I felt like we just talked about the same philosophy every time. Never felt like there was a clear plan about what we were learning. I did not feel prepared to teach students. With our lesson plans, we were never sure what he wanted and he would grade us harshly.

Kaleb's assignments and projects were pretty confusing. We struggled to understand his assignments and even when we asked questions, we were still confused. When you didn't do the assignments like he wanted, you got a pretty bad grade. He is so passionate about teaching art but could be better at expressing himself to students.

Great personality and kind person, but I don't feel that he's a good teacher. His lectures were confusing, he changed his mind a lot/switched around assignments. It was hard to tell what his goal was for the class. He graded very harshly at times and used bias/his own opinion to decide if you'd done well instead of focusing on effort/completion etc

Kaleb is an amazing professor and I have learned a lot from his intro to art education course. At the start of the semester I felt unprepared to enter into the art education major but I am now able to make lesson plans and rubrics with ease. He also gives great feedback on what lesson ideas are the most interesting or where they could use some work

Dr. Harrison is awkward in the best way. His lectures are conceptually helpful, but don't prepare you for the homework. Go to the TA lab and his office hours for that. He is very reasonable about giving points back on exams and offered 1/4 test corrections. Also, bug him about replacing the lowest midterm with the final because he did for our year!

Tests were 60% of our grade despite having at least 10 hours of weekly homework, and I felt there were a few surprises on each test. Its an absolutely brutal class but Dr. Harrison is really nice and puts all his materials online. Learn the content yourself before you come to class and you'll be able to ask good questions, it helps a lot.

Dr. Harrison is an excellent professor. He is calm and humorous, making lectures enjoyable and easy to understand. Excellent at answering questions, very accessible to get help. Exams were long (10-11 free response questions) but very fair and graded on the nice side. Would 10/10 recommend.

Lectures are very dense with information and he knows a lot about the class. It's a very difficult class and the tests are tough but it's easier than CHEM111. Tests are difficult and require you to really understand the material but very doable.

Doctor Harrison is so kind!  I found a lot of success in his class by reading the chapters from the textbook that would be covered before each lecture.  The written homework each week was pretty tough, but we were always welcome to come in to his office hours and he would help us work through the problems.

I took 518 from Dr. Harrison. It was a very fun and low-key class. His tests are open book, open note, and open published scholarly article. He was very accommodating in many ways and is overall super nice.

Dr. Harrison is a really good professor and lecturer.  I would recommend his class to anyone.  It's very difficult and the tests can be brutal, but there isn't any getting around that in a chem class.  Go to his office hours after exams!  He's usually willing to negotiate pointage.

I love Dr. Harrison. He is one of the sweetest genuine teachers I've ever had. I will say, his tests are super hard, it was obvious he is used to teaching higher level. Go to class, but especially go to office hours. He would hold outside reviews for those who would come ask for help. Very understanding on giving points back on tests. Wants success

Nice but BAD prof, cried sm over 106. Take Sansom, she has 7 mini exams but curves +drops 2. Lectures confusing/useless +ppts have some wrong answers. For (4) exams do practice tests/review ppts, go to office hours, and do hwk in the TA lab w Addy. Hwk 3x a week. Use txtbook to self teach. Hard final, 3.5 hrs, 20 mc 71% avg, 8 SA 63% but lil curve

Professor Harrison is a great guy, and genuinely wants to help his students. Attending office hours was super helpful, and he was often willing to give a couple points back on exams if you felt your work deserved more credit. great class except his tests were super difficult and problems were often worded differently than what we did in class.

Professor Harrison was super nice, caring, and helpful outside of lecture. Definitely go to his office hours to get clarification and before exams. His exams were really fair and if you study they arent too bad.
This class was definitely difficult. Dr. Harrison is a caring, respectful professor, but he can be boring in his lectures. He goes over a lot of practice problems in class, which is really helpful.

I had to teach myself a lot of the material, especially with the textbook. Professor Harrison is very intelligent, but I was often very confused in class. We did experiments a lot instead of clarifying confusing details.

Professor Harrison is a genuine and intelligent instructor. That being said, his lectures can get boring at times as he isn't always enthusiastic about what he teaches. Also, it's not too difficult as he teaches the concepts well enough and there aren't ever any curveballs on the tests.

Professor Harrison is an awesome professor. I was hesitant based on these reviews, but was surprised on how great the class is run. He is very passionate, teaches clearly as he builds upon the subjects, not too much homework, and tests are very similar to homework problems, not trying to trick you. He loves to answer questions and teaching!

Professor Harrison and his class are fantastic! I was a bit scared to take from Professor Harrison based on Rate My Professor Reviews, but I definitely recommend taking from him. He is very accessible by e-mail, after class, and in office hours. He is good at explaining Chemistry, and gets the class going right with a prayer and spiritual thought.

Dr Harrison is a great professor, and is very passionate about chemistry so you'll vibe well if you are too! He is very kind and more than fair with grading, and he really wants to make sure the students understand the material very well. Only a few tests and not too many assignments throughout the week, and he prepares students very well for them.

Professor Harrison is a great professor! The homework and tests were manageable and there was plenty of help if needed. He made the effort to get to know his students and made it a very fair and good chemistry class.

Professor Harrison is a super sweet guy but he is not a good teacher, he struggles to explain things and all the tests are written. I really only got actual help when I went to his office during hours, other than that this class was really hard and I felt like my grade didn't reflect my work.

If you have the option to take a different professor... do it. Dr. Harrison is a smart guy but does not for the life of him know how to actually teach the concepts. My friends who took this class with a different teacher had a way easier time, while everyone with Harrison struggled. His tests are harder and had more HW. Would NOT recommend at all.
He was a great professor.

Overall professor Harrison is a pretty good teacher. Sometimes he doesn't teach very clearly during the lecture, but he was very helpful outside of class. Going to his office hours before every exam and asking questions cleared a lot up. Going to the TA lab with questions also helped a ton. You will have to work hard. Do the reading beforehand.

He's a nice guy he really is, but his lectures are so confusing that I'm often left more confused then if I had just stayed home. He'll take an already complicated subject and convolute it to the point that it's impossible to learn. If you're a really really good self-learner you'll be fine, otherwise you should probably look elsewhere.

If you don't like chemistry you won't like this teacher. You can't expect to just go to class and get the information clearly from the lecture if it doesn't come ready to you. He does do many more in class problems than other professors and you usually have a chance to change your answer and work with others on them. I found that helpful.
Lectures can be pretty boring. The tests are hard. I'm sorry if you have to take this class, but you'll make it through, I promise.

Dr. Harrison is really nice and willing to go over concepts with you outside of class. However, the lectures are not clear. The iclicker questions required for attendance often require knowledge of a concept that hasn't been taught yet. Read the book on your own to get clarification and go to TA reviews. You can get an A but it requires work.

I don't know why the ratings are so terrible for Dr. Harrison here. He is a fair professor and he was accessible during his office hours and was willing to help. The tests are difficult and so is the course. You will need to put time into this class.

Dr Harrison is always willing to help you understand anything if you go visit his office hours. That being said, he doesn't really teach you concepts while in class but instead only lightly reviews material.  If you want to do well you'll need to teach yourself everything that will be covered in that days lecture before class.  Tests are difficult.

"Those who can't do, can't teach."  This class was awful. Lectures were super disorganized and rarely pertinent to the homework. Frequently the professor would miss his own in-class practice problems and each exam had multiple items keyed incorrectly. I honestly think it's a disgrace that I had to pay to teach myself all semester. Nice guy though.

Terrible teacher. He would mess up on his own problems and confuse everyone in the class and then test on things that we had never gone over. Worst professor I've ever had. Prepare to learn everything by yourself and even if you do that you won't do too well on the tests.
I met with him several times throughout the semester,  and he really cares about all his students! He is really good at explaining things. Tough tests though, although it is chemistry...

He sometimes went too fast through the lecture material, but he was willing to stop and clarify when we needed it. He is super helpful one-on-one though, so I would recommend going to his office hours if you take him.  And the quizzes are very difficult, but you are allowed to get help from others/ the TAs on them.  The exams are reasonable.

Dr. Harrison is a super nice guy, and I was a little wary of this class from all the horror stories that people say about how hard it is, but I think he was very fair in his tests and grading.  The online homework is super annoying sometimes, but that's not really his fault.  For sure Dr. Harrison is a safe bet if you have to take this class.

This was a difficult course, but I would recommend taking it from Dr. Harrison. He is willing to adjust the pace of the lecture based on students question. He tries to learn names, is approachable and friendly. Form a study group and do the homework together! The weekly quizzes are challenging, but prepare you for the tests.

I've never taken a more boring class and students of other professors talk about how their professors allow study aids and helps on exam and he won't consider such when brought up in class that other professors are more helpful.

Dr. Harrison is SO nice and laid back. Nevertheless, it's a tough class. For someone who took chemistry for the first time ever in life, I quickly realized that his teaching style is more directed to those who already have a notion of the material. I had to rely on the book to learn how to solve problems. Tests are hard so get help from TAs.

Bro. Harrison= great guy, super nice but then the class... Rough, there are I clickers everyday in class to get some easy points that you will need. 3 short answer exams, super hard and confusing. Nothing like the book problems. Then you have a final, multiple choice and short answer. Good luck when you take this class!

He is difficult to understand and the tests are really hard short answer, and they don't really reflect what is covered in class.  He is a nice guy and he will help you if you ask for it, but he explains it as if you know more than you actually do... which is no help.

He is very hard to understand. He explains problems very poorly in lecture and you have to basically teach yourself everything from the textbook. If you like hard, 20 short answer tests with NO curve and a confusing teacher... this is your class.

PROF. HARRISON IS THE MOST ADORABLE HUMAN BEING. Seriously. That said the class was pretty tough. He doesn't know how to teach well, but the homework is really helpful. He does fun experiments in class almost every day that make things exciting. Go to class because there are always iClicker questions. Tests were pretty tough. They are graded hard.

Brother Harrison is a good teacher who wants salvation and happiness for every student. His class isn't hard, but you need to go to class and keep up with the readings. Start your papers as soon as you know you need to, and stay aware of deadlines and testing dates. You will do great if you do! :D

I had him for Book of Mormon part 1, and it was awesome.  He has a lot of good input.  He grades his tests fairly easily, just put some effort in and show you have some knowledge and you should get some points.  Read your scriptures daily, do the 3 (easy) papers, study for an hour or two for each exam, and you should be fine.

Easily the worst CLASS I have ever taken. Harrison is a great guy, but I couldn't have learned any less. I had to teach myself from the book and that did not work-out too well. He relies heavily on the Iclicker way too much so sit next to smart people.

His teaching style was no good.  He's nice, but seriously, I came away from every class wondering what the lecture was about.  I definitley used the book to try and teach myself.  His tests are very hard and I felt a few of the questions were unfair to include.  Make sure you spend lots of hours with the T.A.s or someone who can tutor you!

Dr. Harrison is a very kind person but is sometimes not very good at explaining things.  However, if you use the textbook and listen to lecture you will know what to study for the test.  Gives practice exams before each midterm which really helped me.  It is very helpful to know a little chemistry before taking his class.

Professor Harrison's class was okay.  I don't really have a great interest in the subject, but he tried to explain things thoroughly and gave interesting facts.  He did some cool demonstrations too.  Reading the book is VITAL, or understanding the lectures is difficult.

Prof. Harrison is very unclear in his lectures and very scatterbrained.Doesn't connect the dots very well.You definitely have to teach yourself the material and the book is mandatory! Iclicker quizzes every class period and was the only reason i went. Other than that i taught myself everything but he does some cool experiments in class.

He's a nice guy, and he'll help you out if you ask, but the book is easier to understand than his lectures. His lectures are somewhat disorganized, and it seemed like the class was always confused. There's no curve, so be careful. Easy quizzes, but really hard tests. Tip: Read BEFORE lectures, and don't forget to do homework/labs (easier points).

You basically have to teach yourself everything...so GET THE BOOK!! You have quizzes in the testing center for every chapter and tests after every 3 chapters. Everyone does pretty average on the tests...so study hard. He doesn't curve anything...and has unorganized lectures. Not impossible though...

I didn't like the way Prof. Harrison taught. He wasn't very organized in lectures and he also wasn't very clear in explaining concepts. I got confused a lot of the time when he tried explaining something. The textbook was actually a lot more helpful than he was. I also didn't think some questions on his tests were fair either.

An interesting class, not an interesting professor.  His lectures were unorganized, it seemed and never very clear.  The text, however was VERY well written and very clear.  The beginning of the class was easy, but most of the class failed the last test and he didn't curve because the class average ended up being a "B".

Dr. Harrison's grading system is really hard.  He is happy to have an average of 75% and he doesn't curve grades at the end of the semester, however, there are many opportunities for a few free points here and there.
Soft spoken guy with a knowledge of many specialties in the field.
Great guy helped me out with tons of stuff. Helped me to achieve the grade I needed.

Freakin hard! Class from hell. Unless your a Chem god prepare to fail every test and be fustrated the whole semester.GO in for help, he's helpful.Evyery teacher is hard though so I guess I would recommend him...hes better than cannon!
Great professor, his teaching methods are helpful if you pay attention in lecuture.  If you stay up on assignments and put forth reasonable effort the class isn't too bad.

Great teacher. As long as you pay attention in class, do the homework, and don't get behind you will be fine. The TA's are great and I highly recommend the Chem lab. Dr. Harrison cares about his students and if you visit him with a question he makes sure you leave understanding the concept.
The nicest guy you will ever meet. He really likes chemistry. My favorite comment of his was that "Chemistry is God's work, it should turn us on!" Great class.

Final was killer. Dr. Harrison is funny in a quiet way- lecture was mostly just working out problems. Use TA's. Go to Dr. Harrison after each test and argue your answer- you'll always get points back! Not a bad teacher at all.
His final is a beast.  If you take hime, make sure to go to him after ever test to try to get more points.

He may seem a little nerdy, but he's young+pretty cool in that he relates well to students.  He's usually soft-spoken and dry, but if you're listening he throws in things that are hilarious.  The class is easy if you have a good 105 experience.  Nice guy.

213 is a tough course, but I really enjoyed Dr. Harrison. He was very easy-going, which eased the stress load. He was always respectful in answering my questions, and I really appreciated that. He's a good man.
He is about as nerdy as they come.  He's hard to understand, and he doesn't understand why you don't understand him.

Dr. Landon gives great lectures, and you can tell that he is invested in his students' success. He provided useful real world examples for every concept that we discussed. Since he is a newer professor,  he knows how to relate to undergrad students and gives solid advice regarding study strategies, etc. The textbook was not needed/useful.
Tough class, but very doable. Homework load was light, so personal study was required to stay up to speed.

Dr Landon is the best. Lectures are great. He refers the textbooks chapters for every class, but you don't need the book if you go to classes. His grading criteria is clear, participation and attendance is 5%, and tests are 70%. He learns everyone's names and calls people out to participate and makes sure you are comfortable. Take it from him!
Econ 380 is very difficult but Dr. Landon made me exited to come to class. He is soft spoken, smart, and extremely selfless. I would highly recommend taking classes from him.

Great professor. Econ 380 is a beast, but he's a good lecturer and is very willing to work with students one on one to clear up misconceptions. As other people have said (and he himself says), the textbook is dense and completely optional for this course; I did just fine using my in-class notes and the practice tests to prepare for his midterms.

Dr. Landon is awesome. Super smart but also super approachable, and he really cares about his students. He did a good job getting me excited about economics! Econ 380 is tough, but he made it a lot better and was very fair. Definitely take it from him if you can!

He's really solid. The material covered in this class is really tough, but he teaches it really well and makes it managable. The textbook is completely optional, I recommend going to his class a couple of times before buying it. I don't think you need it. Overall, Dr. Landon is super chill and makes a tough class about as enjoyable as possible
Really great class, was definitely a huge jump from 110, but Dr. Landon made the material digestible and was always available.

Dr. Duraccio is THE best! Her lectures were always incredibly insightful and I appreciated that she consistently took the time to answer any questions that people had. I would take this class over and over. While her schedule outside of class is a little hectic, she genuinely wants to help in any way she can, she just needs a little notice!

Her lectures matched the textbook and the tests. However, her offers to be willing to meet outside of class felt fake. She claims to always be willing to meet during office hours about anything you want, but when I reached out for help with some research, she said no - twice. This made me feel like they were ingenuine and hollow offers.
She is amazing! Loved her teaching style, she always made everything so interesting!

Dr. Duraccio is one of the most inspiring, caring teachers I have ever had. I would recommend this class to anyone. She impacted me in ways she will truly never know. Phenomenal experience.. 10/10 for me. The class is so fascinating and it isn't hard.
I love Dr. Duraccio. She is wonderful. One of the kindest and most compassionate professors I have ever had the pleasure of taking classes from.

Best class at BYU. Not only do you learn so much and get great clinical practice but it can also be a great class to just take if you want knowledge for future parenting. Tuesdays had amazing science-based parenting tips that I will definitely apply to my kids. Thursdays were my favorite with the case conceptualizations. Easy to learn a lot!

I actually took PSYCH 310 with her, but it wasn't an option. Dr. Duraccio is a tough grader. You have to work for a good grade. But she gives good feedback and is always more than happy to help. I've even met with her for grad school stuff as well. She is genuinely an amazing person who cares that her students learn, even if it means tough grades.

Dr. Duraccio is one of my favorite professors I've had at BYU. Her lectures are full of information, but she makes them engaging and fun! I loved the case conceptualizations where you get to practice diagnosing based off of symptoms and presentations. She is so willing to help students in class and one on one. Highly highly respect her! 10/10!
Dr. Duraccio is one of my favorite professors that I've taken a class from. 10/10 would recommend.

Dr. Duraccio is one of the kindest and most genuine professors I've had during my time at BYU. She's by no means an "easy grader", but her feedback on what you need to do to improve and how to do so was amazing. Her expectations are clear and she was willing to meet one-on-one to talk through your paper and help in any way she could.

This class was great. Dr. Duraccio is so fun and made lectures engaging enough to keep my attention and allow me to learn. The class is structured in a way that is open to ask a lot of questions, which I loved. It is very heavy on reading and lectures, but it's manageable. Exams were hard but study guides definitely helped.

I really like Kara. She helped me to improve as a writer, learn APA (VERY important), and be more confident in myself. She is incredibly genuine and sincere. 307 is hard but it's not because of Kara, the psych department has standardized the class among all the professors who teach it. Kara is one of the best options for this (or any) class.

I loved Dr. Duraccio and I loved this class. I was especially impressed by how engaging and creative her lectures are. There are many opportunities for participation that helps expand knowledge so much more beyond just the textbook. It is a lot of reading, but the material was so interesting that it didn't even feel like homework. Highly recommend!

Kara is the best professor I have had at BYU so far. She is involved in every part of the class and genuinely wants her students to succeed. She designs deadlines to make sense and keep you on track. The majority of the class is graded on the final paper, but both she and the TA are always accessible and will give clear feedback along the way!

Prof. Duraccio is amazing! She cares about her students so much as was always spending extra time to help us. The whole class was focussed on writing one paper, and she spent a lot of time helping us know how to write it well with as little stress as possible. I would take all my classes from her if I could. She was a little hard on grading though.

Dr. Duraccio has been my favorite professor at BYU. She is so caring and accessible to helping you in any way she can. School, life, whatever. Shes open to feedback and wants to be the best professor she can be. Super awesome class that I figured I would suffer through but have enjoyed so much. Such a great experience and a wonderful teacher.

Dr. Duraccio is wonderful. Her class is laid out well. Lectures are engaging and the assignments are effective in helping you learn how to write in Psychology. Has been my favorite class so far at BYU!!!! Highly recommend.

Stowers is a bit disorganized but she does wants her students to do good. She writes notes in class and her handwriting can be hard to follow. she is very inconsistent with practice problems in class, making the homework difficult to do. Exams are fair, but there aren't many study resources. Overall, better than 111, but could be more organized.

Stowers gets confused by her own notes and is passive-aggressive when students ask questions. Her tests are very difficult to study for, she required online homework that was way too much. My classmates took 0s because they didn't have time to finish everything. I took 352 from a different professor and did way better.

Notes are filled out in lecture, and there aren't any slides to look back on or study from. Definitely had a lot of homework for a 3-credit class, and final exam was meant to be taken after two semeters of class instead of one, so there was a lot that was not covered in-depth.

Honestly, after two semesters of Stowers she's starting to grow on me. She's a lot of fun, but her lectures taught me nothing. She's unorganized, but incredibly knowledgeable. I wouldn't avoid her class, but I would probably choose someone else if they were available.

Dr. Stowers was such a great professor. This is a very difficult class, but she is really organized and good at providing resources to succeed. Also, it's clear that she cares so much about students, and merciful in grading with assignments dropped and points back on some tests.

She's fantastic. The subject is hard, and she talks and writes notes really fast so get ready to take notes like the wind, but she explains the concepts really well and her lectures cover all the material. There is a lot of homework, so definitely block out a lot of time for work outside of class. Go to office hours!! amazing pacing for tests

I love Professor Stowers. She explain things very similarly to how high school classes teach, which was super helpful for a lot of people. She is disorganized, writes her notes along with the class which is nice but sometimes led to me not understanding my notes if I wrote exactly what she did. She takes time to help you understand which is great!

I really like Dr. Stowers, and ended up liking OChem a lot more than I thought I would. While I don't think lecturing is her strength, if you pay attention and supplement with reading it is totally fine. She provides  lots of test prep materials and her TAs are awesome. I also though her test were very, very fair to what she taught in class.

Very smart and tries hard to teach material well. Provides lots of additional study helps and resources for every chapter as well. Lectures were essential for me, because that's how I learn best. Kind and funny too. OCHEM is a hard class but she was about as good of a professor as you can get for it!

Dr. Stowers is an overall great professor, although she isn't perfect. I was impressed that she was willing to change her teaching style and the course workload based on the results of a class pole halfway through the semester. She is very straightforward about course requirements and her personal limitations. Very reasonable.

Professor Stowers was awesome because she genuinely wants students to succeed and learn. She's pretty straightforward and doesn't want to trick you. The difficult part of this class is figuring out how you learn best. The book is super helpful and good for clarifying things that might be confusing from lecture.

I really like Dr. Stowers. She really cares for her students and is straightforward in her approach. The class is very much designed to help students learn what the most important things that they need. I would still say this is the hardest class I have taken, but there are so many resources to help! She makes mistakes, but I would recommend her!

You can feel that Stowers genuinely cares about you and wants you to succeed. However, it's impossible for her to cover all of Ochem in the 2.5 lecture hours a week she's given, she at best can only introduce a topic and go over some simple examples. So all the learning is on you; read the textbook. Fair tests that prepare you well for the ACS.

The biggest challenge is to learn HOW you learn Ochem best. The learning is on you. Dr. Stowers acts more as an introducer and clarifier of content. Our class averaged in the 87th percentile nationwide on the standardized final. That says a lot about how well she teaches and also how well she tests us in midterms leading up to the final.
It's O chem, so it's tough. Your mastery is on you... Read the textbook, do practice problems, and have a study group. I thought she was a fair professor, and I felt like she wanted us to succeed.

Professor Stowers was awesome. There was nothing on the tests that we hadn't gone over in class. Very very fair. She genuinely cared about preparing us for the tests and she posts soooo many resources on LS that are very helpful. Take it from her.

Dr. Stowers is a great prof. She is willing to work with you. This is a hard class that requires a lot of work but she wants your load to be resonable and will adjust her assignments for the class based on how the average is. Her tests are fair and her lectures are organized. You will need to read the textbook.

It was very disorganized and unclear what was kept and dropped with grading. She was difficult to meet as I sent two emails and never responded; however, she taught well and you could always have a worse O-Chem professor.

She was not transparent about you real grades. She had drops turned on (worst two hw were dropped etc) and then I missed one assignment, and they magically turned off. I was sitting at a 50% in the class and continually went to office hours concerned about my grade where she told me I was doing fine. She never cared to solve the actual problem.

Dr. Stowers is a very nice lady but is extremely difficult to follow during class. She does try to make herself accessible outside of class. She goes through material very quickly and I really struggled to learn from her. With her, you MUST read the textbook before class since her lectures are set up expecting you to already know about the topics.

Dr. Stowers is a great teacher. She really helped me understand the course material, which is pretty tough. The tests were very fair along with all grading. The problem sets were properly long and awful, but they're self graded and you can be lenient on that. She's always willing to help you out with concepts one on one. Also read the textbook.

Overall I thing that professor stowers did a really good job teaching that class and that she did the best that she could. It is just a super hard class to begin with and there is a lot of information to cover and understand. I would take from her again.

I thought Stowers made her tests fair. I rarely saw something on the test that we had not covered in detail. Be prepared to do work outside of class, and use TAs a lot for clarification. 
If she taught 352 I would take it from her. Overall she made Ochem a lot better than I thought it was going to be.

Dr. Stowers is a good professor, OCHEM is very hard of course. Lectures were good only if you read the book, she goes lightning speed sometimes, but it's needed for all the material. Her guided notes are super helpful to know what is needed and she makes them accessible. I feel like some work was busy work. ACS Final was graded by the percentile.

Dr. Stowers isn't an organic chemist but she did a good job teaching it this semester. Lectures can be a bit scattered but she's always happy to clarify.

Her lecture notes are laid out like a worksheet so we can followed along with what she writes.

She is a nice lady, but I don't think she teaches concepts well. Her class is super unorganized. She talked so fast that I found it very difficult to follow along. It happened multiple times that her practice exam keys had conflicts with what she said in the lectures, and I had to check again with her. Take this class from another professor.

Nice lady. She is open to student feedback and wants to help you succeed. Her lectures were a little confusing, and she does not curve the exams at all, even if the average is super low. The average final grade in my class was a C+.

If she taught CHEM 352 I'd take it from her rather than other professors. She opened up all of her in-class notes for us to use on her weekly practice exams, and her notes/practice exams are what are on her tests. Her format is good, her tests are decent, no curve but dropped an exam if you did good on final. Her in-class is a little hard to follow

OChem is a content heavy and challenging subject.  You must read the textbook, and lecture will make sense if you have.  She focuses on the more challenging and important topics in class.  There are quizzes (take home) just about every week and a practice exam every week.  She was still adjusting the course structure, but she responded to feedback.

Dr Stowers is awesome! She's a super great professor. OChem is just a crazy hard subject, there's no way around it. I spent about 12 hours per week outside of class studying the textbook and doing practice problems, so it's definitely a time sucker. But it was fascinating material! I decided to stick with chemistry because of this class.

Dr Stowers is awesome! OChem is definitely the hardest class I've taken in my life, so just know that in advance. I spent hours in the textbook and homework problems and also went to all the lectures. That's the only reason I was able to survive. But she is a kind person and knows this stuff is a challenge, so she's very supportive.

OChem is hard no matter who you take it from. They just have a short amount of time to go over a lot of material. She gets herself turned around with some concepts but is very humble about it when the class points it out. Grading is strict but you can do well in this class.

Professor Stowers is a great person, but I struggled with her teaching style. She talked very fast during class about difficult concepts and wouldn't turn around very often to answer questions. It just felt so fast paced and I felt like I couldn't learn one concept before we moved on to another. Lots of unnecessary assignments that didn't help me.
