This is the second class I have taken from Dr. Stowers. I like her teaching style because she works examples on the board. She doesn't use slides, so you can mostly keep up with writing. The tests really matter. You should do some studying outside of mandatory work - either optional book problems or just studying on your own.

Dr. Stowers was a great professor. Very approachable outside of class to help with hard concepts. She cares about her students and gets to know their names. Obviously, this is a chem class so it's difficult but very manageable.

I took 514 from Stowers and it was a good class. She is a little disorganized but she will talk to you outside of class and go over tests and give partial points back, etc. Her tests can be a bit confusing but she usually throws out any problems that didn't go well.

Professor stowers is the best! I learned so much from her and she is always willing to talk to you if you come into her office hours. Her lectures are wonderful. She is able to teach really hard concepts in a way that makes sense. This class is super hard and you must put in work, but she is wonderful.

Dr. Stowers is a great professor! She works lots of example problems in her lectures which is really useful in understanding the material. That also helps with the homework a lot. She really cares for her students and is easy to talk to outside of class.

Dr. Stowers is amazing! She does such a good job explaining topics and really wants her students to do well. If she makes a mistake the students are never penalized and she makes it all work out. She is accessible out of class and works with you to help you answer questions and gives good advice on how to improve. Would take any of her classes.

I took Organic Chemistry 1 from Professor Stowers, which is a very hard class.... So with that in mind I think she did great. It was her first time teaching the course so it was a little bumpy at first, but she really was such a good professor. She made time for her students, she does her best to help us succeed, and she knows her stuff.

Super knowledgeable and caring professor. Liked how she had HW being extra credit. Very good at answering questions. Make sure you do your readings before lecture, that would help a lot. The quizzes are kinda tough, but fair. Exams are reasonable and you get a lot of time to do them (no time limit). She does Q&A sessions outside of lectures.

Loved Dr. Stowers! She's hilarious but also very relatable and knows how hard this class can be. She's very willing to help outside of class in office hours and a review hour once a week. Her tests were difficult but straight-forward. Reading and hw problems were essential for mastering material. Hard class because its OCHEM, but doable.

I really enjoyed going to her lectures because I thought she was really funny and relatable. Her lectures are helpful, but you also have to read the textbook and do the homework to really understand the subject. The test content was never surprising and she's a fair grader. Would definitely recommend.

Stowers is an absolute nightmare to work with. She is disorganized and doesn't communicate effectively. Sick? Too bad! Extensions due to illness are begrudgingly given, for the shortest amount of time possible, with threat of failing you if the extension isn't enough time. Homework takes about 2 hours nightly.

Doctor Stowers is a really great teacher! Teaches a super hard class with clarity, never makes you feel bad, answers questions, helpful, cares about each student, learns every person's name, posts her slides, class demonstrations. She does expect you to do your part
The class itself is difficult but she is great. She is very available outside of class and honestly wants the best for every student. The only teacher I have had that tried to learn everyone's name.

This review is unable to be more specific simply because this website asks you not to use profanity or name-calling. I hated this class. It wasn't entirely Dr. Stowers fault as a lot of the course is set by the Chem Department, but I went to her a few times to ask for help and she jokingly dismissed me every time. This class made me lose my 4.0.

Professor Stowers always made time to help outside of class. She expects you to take the lecture content that she provides and study the materials to gain a deeper understanding. It really forces you to work hard outside of the class, which has real benefits.

This class is so hard and there is so much homework, practice sheets, in class quizzes, etc. It's like that in all the Chem105 classes though. I though talking to Dr. Stowers during office hours was very helpful. She answers a lot of questions in class, but one-on-one is way better.

Hardest class I've taken. I wouldn't have passed without Dr. Stowers help. The class is insane, but its not her fault. The department makes this class so hard so that it can weed out students who want to go to medical school.

I loved this class. I was so nervous about taking Chem 105 and Dr. Stowers helped me so much. I went to her office hours so many times to ask questions and she was so helpful every time. She is really helpful and her lectures are pretty interesting too. She does lots of demonstrations in class, which are fun.

Very difficult to follow in lectures and expects students to teach themselves all of the material on their own. Tests are pretty brutal, lots of stuff that was not taught in class is tested on, so it is difficult to know what to prepare for.

She favors intellect over hard work. My grade could have been an A or an F and I would have been equally unsurprised, the entire thing is a crapshoot. It didn't matter how much hard work I put in, I'm typically an A student here at the Y, and my grade was entirely up to luck. If you don't have a decent O-Chem background you're screwed. Good luck.

Here's the deal, If you like chemistry and want to learn more. Stowers is your teacher. She loves questions and will answer all of them and if she doesn't know the answer she will do research on her own time and get back to you. However if you're looking for an easy A, this is not your class.

Dr. Stowers is a great teacher. She is young, entertaining, and great at answering people's questions. As with every chemistry class, it was fast paced and pretty intense, but if you take time to do the readings then you will do fine. Great teacher! Only complaint is that She sometimes thinks her tests are perfect and is unwilling to change problem

I can't do chemistry, if you can do chemistry you'll do a lot better than I did probably. Professor went on so many tangents and had a hard time finishing the lecture. The way she explained things just didn't work for any of us, she went way too fast. Reading the textbook made it a lot easier to follow what she was doing in class. Rely on TA.
Great person, horrible teacher. Be ready to leave class knowing less than when you went in. On days with substitutes, you catch up by learning everything that you should have when she was there.

Writing my review now that I'm done w all my pre-med chem requirements (105 thru 481). Chem profs are generally the cream of the crop, and even among them Dr. Stowers stands out. She teaches you chemistry, as well as how to study. On top of that she's a very decent human being. Talk w her for 10 minutes in her office and you'll see
I took this class from Dr. Stowers during her first semester teaching at BYU. She did a great job and I thought that the class was fair and that I was prepared for the tests.

Hard but rewarding class. The sheer amount of material to go over occasionally made lectures very jumbled, which is why I tried going to office hours every week. She is EXTREMELY helpful on a one-to-one basis. Great teacher, and she genuinely cares about your understanding. Plus she's younger, so it's easy (easier?) to talk to her.

Dr. Stowers is very nice and really goes above and beyond to help her students. The class is tough regardless of who you take it from. She does a good explaining the concepts especially for being a first time professor. She makes practice tests which are super helpful. Most of your learning will come from doing smartwork and going to the TA labs.
Dr. Stowers is doing well  as this is her first semester teaching. Chemistry in and of itself isn't easy, but she really tries to help students.

Dr. Stowers is very intelligent and does as well as can be expected for a brand new instructor. She hasn't had the time that other instructors had to get a feel for how to teach this class. her lectures seem to cover a ton of material very fast.  Our class average on tests were consistently between 67%-70%. She is good about posting practice exams.

Great woman, tough professor. Long lectures with lots of notes taken. Assignments are easy, just take time. I had to re-teach myself everything for the exams which was hard and stressful. 4 exams, they come quick. Sometimes extra stuff said in class are on exams. She'll do practice questions that are on exams. Study guides help direct a little.
Awesome professor, super smart and will tell you all about her personal research which is so interesting. Tests can be hard so notes are crucial.

I loved learning from Dr. Della Corte. She is a master of her field and taught us so many important things about nutrition. The course is a bit dense for a 100 level generals, but that would be the same with any instructor.
Great course, I love learning from Dr. Della Corte. She cares a lot about nutrition and really knows her stuff!
Dr. Della Corte was always nice and approachable. There is a lot of material in this class but she does a great job teaching it.
This was a great class, Prof. Della Corte does an excellent job of condensing down a huge amount of information. I learned many things that will improve how my family eats.

Dr. Della Corte is amazing! I thoroughly enjoyed her lectures. Sometimes the assignments can be a bit too much for a 100 level class, but that is part of this course and will be the same with any instructor. Dr. Della Corte was always willing to talk to us and was quite lenient when it came to making up assignments.

Dr. Della Corte is a brilliant woman. She is a wonderful example of a scholar / disciple. We mastered her field of nutrition and teaches with detailed clarity, while also bearing a strong testimony and inspiring her students to strife for excellence. I really enjoyed this class!

Genius smart, terrible professor though. lectures are SO INCREABLY boring, feels like a waste of time. she is also an unfair professor; she will dock you points even if you follow the rubrics. just spare yourself. do not take classes from her.

as many others have said, she is very nice and she will answer your questions if you ask. With that being said, I could not pay attention in her lectures. Her teaching style was just reading from the slides so I ended up teaching myself almost everything. I would recommend taking it from another professor, unless your fine sleeping in class.
So kind and willing to help!

This class was actually awful.
I feel bad saying that because she's a really nice and knowledgeable person, she just doesn't know how to teach and there was minimal correlation between content and testing.
Some weeks I was did 6-8 hrs/day for this class, and I was still "behind" (by that I mean quiz dates, I was ahead of lecture, a further issue).
Dr. Della Corte is one of my favorite professors at BYU. She is such a kind and knowledgable person, while still being a young professor. I hope to be like her when I am grown up.

I would agree with other raters here: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She reads solely from the slides and is one of the least engaging professors I have had. She is very kind, very professional and very knowlegable but I would not take a class from her again.

Just don't do it, she seems to be kind but her lectures were so unhelpful I started to gain higher scores in the class when I just skipped class all together. Save your grade. This class touches some hard concepts but the lectures are so mind numbing it is impossible to learn anything besides what the inside of your eyelids look like.

While she is a very kind professor, her lectures were not engaging in the slightest. Her TA's were very unapproachable and unhelpful. You can tell she is very passionate about the material, she just fails to teach in an effective way, which made the tests very unclear and confusing.

honestly save your grade and take this class from someone else. she is a very kind person for sure, but her teaching style did not work for me and many other students. it is very hard to stay engaged in class when she is just reading from the slides and we never knew if she was telling us fun facts or things we need to know for the super hard tests

She's a good person, and very kind. But her lectures seemed so pointless. It was so difficult to tell when information was important for the exam and when it was just "nice to know." NDFS 100 is harder than I expected it to be, but I wish I had taken it from another professor and maybe I would've been better prepared for the exams.
Dr. Della Corte was very well prepared for each lecture and was always able to answer our questions. I learned a ton!

The content for all NDFS 100 classes are the same so it doesn't matter too much who your professor is. But with Professor Corte it's pointless to go to class as her lectures are boring and her monotone voice puts you to sleep. So with her you'll just be teaching yourself the content and her TAs are not helpful.
I liked the class and instructor a lot, she is engaged and tried hard to share her faith and knowledge at the same. Exactly what I expected from a BYU science class.

Her lectures were so boring I could never stay awake you don't need to go to class she just reads of the slides in the most boring voice but she seems lovely just so boring oh my goodness. Quizzes were easy all the answers are on quizlet and use the slides to prepare for the exams they can be a bit hard. It was fine but I learned it all myself.

If you have to take this class, just take it online. I stopped going to lectures halfway through the semester and did just fine. You have to pay $100 for the required online textbook which has included quizzes. There are Quizlets for every chapter quiz which is how I prepared for the exams. When I did go to class, I couldn't stay awake.

The class content and exams in all NDFS-100 sections appear to be same, so there is little difference in what Professor you choose. I find Dr. Della Corte personally inspiring, hope to become someone like her myself in the future.
Dr. Della Corte is a super smart lady. She knows so much about nutrition and is always ready to teach it. She also prepares lecture videos so we can study on our own time.

I was looking forward to this course, but it was packed with more information than I expected. Dr. Della Corte is super knowledgeable and expects a lot of the students. She was always very kind and prepared to explain the material. At times I was not sure what to focus on in my studies.

Dr. Della Corte packs her lectures full with relevant information. She is very kind, but no-nonsense in her approach to teaching. She has an inspiring personal story.
I don't understand the bad ratings for her, if you want a maximum amount of learning take this class. If you want cheap entertainment watch a Netflix documentary on nutrition instead.

Hey y'all. Currently typing this in one of her lectures lol I can't. She sweet and is new to teaching, but just reads the slides in the same monotone voice each class. There are way too many slides. You're expected to read the entire textbook. You never know what's going to be on the exam. Just take NDFS100 with another professor, it's not worth it

She talks like a robot and the lecture slides are not helpful. It is not clear what will be on the exams and the assignments are busy work and not explained clearly. This class should be interesting and cool, but low-key she makes it so boring and hard to understand. BE WARNED choose a different professor.

She's really nice however isn't a good teacher. Lectures are really boring and she throws tons of information at you. Quiz questions are somewhat covered in notes but then there are others that are completely new. Study the notes and the weekly quiz questions for the big tests and the class is manageable.

This was Della Corte's first year teaching, so she's new at it. However, her lectures were SO BORING! I fell asleep multiple times and the tests are difficult. She's really nice but monotonous. HW was easy if you have friends taking the class too. The textbook was online though which was nice.

Sister O is a phenomenal teacher, and she is very passionate about it. She is clear about why concepts are the way they are, and I loved her enthusiasm for working out the problems. Lots of problems done out in groups on the board. It's difficult because it's calculus, but if you do the homework consistently, the class is amazing.
Great teacher, took lots of time before and after class to help answer any questions we had.

Best professor at BYU! Cares so much about her students and makes lectures very engaging. We often did problems in groups on the board which really helped with learning tough concepts. Exceptional job teaching and running a class!

Professor Oliverson does a good job explaining the material and genuinely cares about the success of her students.  She gives clear expectations and if you do the work and practice she provides you, you will do well in her class.  The only downside is that this class is graded largely on a few tests, so take advantage of the practice problems.

Mrs. Oliverson was awesome in teaching the material in a way that helped me to really learn and understand what was going on. Not the most exciting course but definitely would take from her again because of how she teaches.
Professor Oliverson is my favorite professor! She is a genius! She teaches all the concepts exceptionally and is always making sure everyone gets the help they need. She is also hilarious!

Professor Oliverson is one of the best professors I've had at BYU.  She genuinely cares about her students and puts in the extra effort to make sure they're understanding the material. I'm an economics major and took this course in preparation for calculus and I was surprised how applicable this course was not only to calc but to my major as well.

Professor Oliverson was amazing! She pushes you to work hard but she's also more than willing to accommodate to your situation.  She wants everyone taking this class to pass and she gives individual attention to students that are struggling.  Her lectures are fun and I couldn't recommend her more!

Sister O is very good at getting you prepared for tests. Her class is test heavy, with 4 midterms and the final. This is a very challenging class, but she is very good about coming early and answering questions on homework or previous lectures. Her class is so worth it, but it is very difficult - as is any calculus class.

Professor Oliverson did a really good job of explaining things simply. Instead of teaching us how to get the right answer, she taught us the concept of the question and went above and beyond to explain it to us.

Professor Oliverson is nice but mixes up material and spends way too long on the easiest concepts and breezes over the hard ones. The tests were MUCH more difficult than any of the homework or practice problems done in class. Midterms really make or break your grade. She's kind and responsive, but this class was much harder than it should have been

I took this class as a BYU SLC class after dropping Calc. I realized I needed more of a background in Math and decided to take 110. I HIGHLY recommend it for people feeling the same way. Most of the information I had learned in the past but got a refresher and learned some new things. Sister O is also super understanding and wants your success.

Professor Oliverson was easily one of my favorite professors at BYU. MATH 110 isn't necessarily an easy or enjoyable class, but taking it from her definitely made it more doable. The course is very test-heavy and there are a lot of homework assignments, but if you pay attention during the lectures and apply yourself you will be just fine.

Sister O was awesome at teaching and engaging students in math. She taught in a way that was understandable and helped us when we were struggling. She was super caring and helpful to those who had conflicts or needed extra help. She is just awesome.

Professor Oliverson really cares about her students! A few students in our class had conflicts with our Friday class period time and she agreed to teach the class on Fridays twice at different times to accommodate them. The videos she has you watch before class are crystal clear and if you watch them and take good notes you will nail this class!

Professor Oliverson is one of the most caring teachers Ive ever had. She put a real emphasis on working together with other classmates and made calculus enjoyable. Class isnt technically mandatory but its worth every second of attendance. Other classes feel like a chore to be in, but I genuinely enjoyed going to and being in this class.

I've never had a professor who cared about the students more. It was a smaller class but by the second or third class she knew everyone by name and forged a relationship with each of us. She taught to the test which was nice and really made us prepare for the final with daily quizzes and was pretty lenient with late work.

I took this as an evening class Mon Wed and I don't think I couldn't have had a better teacher for this hard class. She definitely wanted us to do our best and she really tried to get us to work in groups as much as possible which helped I think. She prepared us well for the tests and was very willing to work with you. Great teacher IMO

So, the course is just really hard in general. No time in class was wasted. However, I spent more time on this class than the 11 other credit hours I was taking. I don't think taking a different prof would have changed this, the course is just a difficult one. Sis O does her job well. Your lab TA makes a big difference though.

This prof cancels class randomly and has you watch videos. When we DO have class she sometimes won't be there cause she is often sick. She also alters HW deadlines frequently; one time it was like 5 minutes before the deadline. This is usually because she will realize that she didn't teach us critical stuff. None of her stuff is on Learning Suite.

Calc 2 is an extremely difficult subject regardless of your professor. She explains things well enough but skips steps in solving equations and mixes up - and + symbols a lot. Smarter students in the class usually correct her and everything makes sense. Easy to get 100%  on the hw (infinite tries online). Expensive textbook w/ software $100

Homework assignments every day but not too bad. She's open to helping students whenever they need it.  Just like any other math class, I wouldn't suggest skipping but if you do miss, everything is online. She does have daily quizzes but she lets you know what's on them so they're not too difficult.

Lots of homework and frequent tests. She has a daily quiz each class period, but she posts the quizzes on Learning Suite. Sometimes she'll push back due dates if class is behind. However I didn't feel like she listened nor respected my opinion at times. Overall it's an okay class. When I took the class she had a hard grader - beware!
Not the most organized or helpful.
Nice lady, but would not recommend taking a class from her.  Wastes time telling math jokes and frequently left out critical concepts in her lectures.  The TA test reviews saved me, so go to those.

I loved taking this class from Professor Oliverson. She did a great job of explaining each topic clearly. Everything that she put on the test was in the study guides so I felt prepared for every test. There is a lot of homework, but it all felt useful. The homework helped me to work through the ideas and to understand them better.

Sister Oliverson was very passionate about what she was teaching. Lots and lots of homework. Daily quizzes were pretty simple. Tests were difficult and took lots of time but questions came directly from the homework. Go to class, form study groups, and you'll be fine. Although more difficult than other 305 classes-hers is well worth it!

I did not think this class was as bad as others say it is. It is a ton of work, but usually the work is not hard, just time consuming. She is a very lenient grader, both on homework and tests. I felt like she taught us everything we needed in to know in class. If you pay attention in class and keep up with all the homework then you should be fine.

Best math professor I've had so far! She tries to do lots of different examples. We ran out of time in class a lot, but if she or the T.A's didn't cover it then they would change the homework. This class generally is a BEAST, it's a time sucker but sister Oliverson really helped me understand the material, & Ta's were awesome
Be prepared to be treated like an elementary student when she lectures. She is very helpful, but not a hard class as long as you have basic math skills. A lot of work, though.

Class was often hectic/unorganized. I would try to discuss grading with her, but I didn't feel like she listened.  I wanted to leave a review like the other two, until my grades were posted.  She was very fair in giving the final grade (technically I should have had an A-, but she gave me an A).

Do not take this class from Oliverson!! It was very confusing and stressful. She did not respect our questions or opinions. She treated us as if we already knew the material (which, a lot of the time we did not...). I was just praying to PASS the class, let alone get an A...

Take the class from someone else if you can.  She didn't teach the material in class and she treated us like we were math majors rather than elementary education majors.  She didn't care what we had to say; she was always right no matter what.  Class was flaky and not very well organized in the long run.  It is bearable, but not very enjoyable.

Dr Chesnel is very knowledgeable and thorough. Her lectures are well structured and super clear. There is a lot of material we learn in this course, which can be overwhelming, but she does a great job covering each topic and provides clear summaries that are very useful to prepare for tests. She helped me better understand complex physical concepts

Dr. Chesnel is great, just the way she sets up the course is not super ideal. Everyone had to do a group presentation, but these weren't super relevant to what we were actually learning, more just fun facts. This took up a lot of class periods and forced everything else to be rushed. She is super great at trying to help answers questions!

Dr Chesnel has been a role model for me. I had her in Phys 222/451/452. She helped me gain confidence as a female physics student. She provided life-saving encouragements when i felt discouraged, depressed. During the pandemic, when teaching went online, she cared about student well-being, and provided extra sessions at night while tending daughter

Dr. Chesnel knows her stuff, and I found her lectures very clear and instructive. The only barrier sometimes was that she would misinterpret a student's question which could lead to confusion when she answered. The grading is somewhat tough but it's pretty clear on requirements to earn all the points. Homework is super helpful--give it priority.

I loved Dr. Chesnel! Fun to listen to and really knows physics well. She is not very forgiving of late work but that's because she is very fair in giving everything enough time. Tests were extremely fair given that the practice exams were nearly identical to the real ones. Only truly hard part was the labs.

Dr Chesnel is not only kind, she is a very intelligent and skilled professor. She can carry derivations on and on throughout lectures without the aid of notes and she will take the time to explain every step. She will push you to explain your reasoning and carry derivations by hand yourself. Her tips helped me perform well in graduate school now.

Good lectures; I never really walked away confused. She obviously makes an effort to teach clearly. The homework is very reasonable (two 1-2 hour assignments per week). Each test, including the final, is only 10 percent of your grade, and they are graded quite leniently in my opinion. Dr. Chesnel obviously cares about the students.

Dr Chesnel is a really good teacher. I disagree with previous comment. Her lectures are very clear and organized. Her slides are extremely well designed and helped me assimilate the complex quantum mechanics concepts. Also she takes the time to go through each step of derivations, which was super helpful not just for quantum but other courses too.

Dr. Chesnel is nice and I really want to like her but she makes the class much harder than it needs to be. The class is disorganized and constantly behind. She gives practice exams but doesnt include the answer key so you can compare your results. The material is tough and Dr. Chesnel tries to teach it well, but unfortunately makes things harder.

Dr. Chesnel is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. She gives you pre tests before each test and even uses color coding to help you stay organized. All BYU physics classes were very hard for me, but I actually still remember a lot of what we talked about in her class. She goes through each step of derivations and explains them well.

Dr. Chesnel is an inspiring professor. She works hard to communicate the material. Shell listen to you and really consider your input. I had her for 222, 451, and 452. Work hard on hw and assimilate/memorize the equations on the practice exams. She cares deeply about her students and is invested in their success. BYU is lucky to have her.

Dr. Chesnel is very caring and kind. She respects students and helps students in difficult times. The course material is hard but her lectures make them easier. I was able to understand the material much better after her lectures. Homework takes a lot of time so work in groups. She also gives practice tests beforehand to prepare you for the tests.

General physics labs at BYU are usually the worst. This class is no exception. Not sure whether it's more of an issue with the professor herself, or with the department, because I didn't see her until we started online school and she made appearances in videos. Your TAs will make or break you with this professor.

This is a lab so you you have Tas that teach and grade this class (great TAs :). When the class went online due to the pandemic Professor Chesnel recorded herself doing the experiments and did such a great job moving the class forward. be prepared to work as a group, and just show up and stay on top of assignments and you'll be just fine!

I loved taking this class from Dr. Chesnel!!! 222 is a course that tries to sum up all of physics from Einstein to present, so you can imagine that there is a TON of material to cover and the pace is relentless. That being said, I've never had a professor who worked SO HARD to make sure you could learn the material and still do well on the exams.

I hate that we all have to take this class, there was only 1 lab I learned something from. If I hadn't had such a great lab group I would have hated this class. The mid-term and final are terrible and time-consuming and although you have more freedom than 107, I still hated it. Just hope you get good TAs or you're done for.

Class is easy. But I am NOT EXAGGERATING when I say that every single thing I learned in that class was from reading the textbook. Lectures were not helpful, just derivations already in the book. You lose lots of points off tests for not doing things that were not asked for. She's kind, I just wish she would listen to student feedback and adapt.

Dr Chesnel is fantastic! I love her teaching methods and how she made the effort to implement new activities to help us learn the material. She really cares about her students and takes the time to answer questions thoroughly. I really enjoyed this course. I would love to take a course from her again in the future.
She is the best!

Dr Chesnel is an outstanding teacher! She gives excellent lectures and explains things very clearly. Her lecture slides are extremely well designed and helped me understand the material. She gives very useful reviews before tests and provides tons of help. Also she prepares delicious treats! I really enjoyed this course. I definitely recommend her!

Dr. Chesnel gets a bad rap she doesn't deserve. Her accent is a little tough at times, but she's a wonderful person and an excellent professor. I found the class a bit on the easy side, but that had more to do with me taking it after completing a math minor and some upper division physics classes. You could definitely do worse.

Dr. Chesnel is the one you want to take upper division quantum mechanics from! Her lectures combined with the reading really helped me understand the material in a way I didn't even think was possible with quantum mechanics! Her french accent does take getting used to but after the second lecture it isn't a problem. Also iclicker quizzes for credit

Dr Chesnel is the kindest and most caring physics professor i have ever had. She really cares about each student in the classroom and makes the effort to remember everyone's name. I think some students are taking advantage of her kindness by giving her a hard time and being rude in the classroom. She was very patient with them.

Dr. Chesnel can generally explain things she prepares, but she struggles to understand student questions, so her answers don't help. There is a LOT of homework, and you MUST follow her rubrics to get full credit (ex: wants things not stated in the problem). The best teaching she does is requiring you to read the book. You'll need TA help on hw.

I love Dr Chesnel! She is the best physics teacher i had in college. This is a hard course but you can tell she has a passion for this subject. She has a very positive attitude when teaching and it helped me get through the hard material.

Dr. Chesnel wasn't a very good professor for this very interesting class. She taught the material poorly, wasn't good at answering questions, and her class structure was terrible. The class itself was pretty easy, considering the practice tests she gives and the obscene amount of extra credit, but this class could have been much more enjoyable.

Wonderful class. Amazing teacher. She takes the time to explain concepts very clearly even if the material is very complex and she really cares about students' understanding. Honestly, the best physics i have ever had.

I like Dr. Chesnel as a person, and she honestly wants to help students. However, she spent so much time on the basics in class, when we already learned that from the reading. I rarely felt prepared for the homework, so I went to every help session. The tests aren't too bad because the practice tests are very similar. Do the labs (they're easy)!

Can be difficult to understand at times with her accent.  VERY used to teaching students of upper level physics, or very adept students.  Virtually no patience in explaining simple concepts or helping until you understand, will get frustrated quite easily, and struggles to teach simply.

I really liked her actually. She teaches the material really clearly and is willing to do what it takes to help. The tests are just like the practice tests for the most part. She really cares and has organized the class well. It's a lot to cover, but she does great.

Fantastic class. Physics 222 is a hard class because you have to cover so much material in so little time, but Dr. Chesnel does a really good job. If you ever have a question ask and she'll explain until it makes sense. She's a really good teacher but due to the extensive material, the class is hard.

I took this from her during her first semester teaching the class, most students struggled.  Students that have taken it since have been doing better.  Her accent is a little hard to understand at first, but after a week it wan't that hard.
Teacher is very difficult to understand (partly because of accent).

Many students complain about her accent as she is from France, but really it isn't a problem at all. She explains most of the concepts fairly well, although she does randomly call up students from the roll sheet to complete problems on the overhead, if you aren't paying attn you'll make a fool of yourself. The ta lab helps for the homework

Terrible class. She definately knows physics but academics has been her whole life so she cant really relate to you if you don't understand. Her tests are way harder than they need to be, and homework takes way too long nor does it prepare you well for tests. She pulls equations out of no where and doesn't name them in notes.

She definitley knows what she is talking about. Lectures are long, and can be boring at times. Don't even buy the textbook, I never opened it. Gives i-clicker quizzes in class that boost your grade if you're there (don't even have to get it right to get points). TA's in the tutorial lab helped me get an A, not a very hard class, ok professor.

This class could have been a lot easier with a different professor.  Overall, attendance was mandatory, but I got nothing from the lecture.  90% of your time in the class is devoted to decrypting a thick french accent over the noise of all the other students in the class. Understanding of physics: A+.  Ability to communicate it : D-.

Easiest class of my life.  An A starts at a 90 and an A- at an 80.  I finished with a 100.3 in the class.  Do the homework and the reading and it is smooth sailing.  It is not a hard class at all.  Dr. Chesnel devotes a lot of time to help everyone understand.  She cares about the success of the class and is willing to help.

I thought Dr Chesnel did a great job.  Her accent really isn't hard to get used to, and she creates excellent powerpoints.  I opened my textbook maybe once, because she goes over the material we need for the homework in the class prior.  2 assignments per week, each took between 1-2 hours, and the homework prepares you well for the tests.
It is a difficult class but a good grade is attainable if you devote enough time to it. She can be hard to understand sometimes so ask questions! Good professor IMHO.

I believe her best quality is that she cares.  She wants to be a successful teacher.  I do seem to learn more from reading the text book though.  She's French, and likes to bring up how awesome the french are alot.  It does reflect her true opinion but its mostly to be funny.  2/5 on English.

I liked this class. At first I was unsure because her English isn't great and you have to write A LOT for homework and tests, but once you get used to the accent and accustomed to explaining your reasoning about everything, it's actually pretty cool. The hw really prepares you for the tests. Be ready to dedicate a lot of time if you want to underst

She really knows her physics... just not as much about teaching.  Once you get past her french accent, its not too bad. Expect to re-teach yourself everything you are lectured on in class, and look for the red boxes(that's what you really need to know!!).

Dr. Warnick cares about his students and loves the physical sciences, but the course felt haphazard. I wish that he spent more time explaining the physical sciences aspect than always focusing on the role religion will play in solving complex problems. The slides weren't very helpful or informative, and there was just a lot of miscommunication.

The class was very poorly organized, but Dr. Warnick was a good professor. His portion of the course was well-organized and well-taught, with clear indications of what to study for the exams. Lectures were interesting, though few people wanted to participate when asked. Avoid the course, not Dr. Warnick.

Dr. Bellini is seriously one of the sweetest professors in the Dietetics program. Her lectures are always so inspiring and leave me feeling so motivated. Some people forget that NDFS 300 is a 4-credit class, so there definitely was the work to compensate for a 4-credit class, but overall it was honestly a super enjoyable class!
BEST TEACHER EVER! She is the nicest most kind teacher and person you will ever meet

I took the asynchronous course and didn't enjoy it. No late work is accepted, and all her test reviews were at 8am. The information is very interesting, but you have to memorize a lot. If you can't memorize well, I wouldn't recommend this class.

I took the online course. Basically it was just of assigned readings from the textbook and you had to teach your self everything. I would not take this class again. The test was extremely difficult for how little was taught. The questions were always obscure and hard. If you take this course prepare to eat, sleep, and breathe the textbook.

Dr. Bellini's NDFS 305 class has been my favorite at BYU! She has so much experience in the healthcare world and she brings it into the class! For the first time I felt like my medical and diagnostic knowledge was increased because of her! She is the nicest and most respectful person ever! LOVED, LOVED, LOVED this class!
Easy class, but super boring. The instructor does provide study guides and online review sessions, but other than that, it is just a class.

Professor Bellini is really experienced and knows a lot! She does give a lot of hints for her exams in lecture, but attendance isn't mandatory. She is really caring and has a very sweet sense of humor. Her exams can be pretty tough though, so make sure you study hard for them and pay attention to the readings/lectures.

Dr. Bellini is a really great professor. She has a lot of clinical experience that makes her lectures really interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she gives a lot of hints about the test in class, so I would highly recommend it!

I took the online course- it was not helpful. You basically have to teach yourself through the textbook and she is slow to respond to emails. She was very difficult and it was frustrating. The tests are nothing like the reviews and she writes very long and lengthy questions that will loose you. Class requires a lot of hard, focused work.

Lectures are not helpful at all. She seems unsure about everything she says and she couldn't answer most of the questions this last semester. She answers them in a round about way that is not even an answer. The TA's seem to know more about the subject than she does, they often stepped in during class to answer difficult or in depth questions.

Dr Bellini is an extremely nice woman, but I hated her lectures.  They didn't seem to be of much help at all -- you had to go to the TAs for clarity and in-depth.  I don't say this to be mean, but whenever a question was asked during class, she would answer it in a roundabout way without actually answering the question.  Not recommended.
Does not teach material well at all. Even if you study a lot, you will be unprepared for the tests because of how poorly she teaches the subject matter.

Dr. Bellini couldn't answer 90% of the questions asked this semester.  She dodges almost every question.  All she does is read from an outdated powerpoint that doesn't seem to benefit you on the test.  Didn't learned much of anything about nutrition.
Great teacher, great class. More common sensed based than real hard concepts to learn. tests arent too bad.

This class was lots of fun and we got to go into high schools and observe. There were readings most week but we had great conversation. The projects were manageable and Professor Johnson was SUPER helpful! She also is a fair grader and gives good feedback.

The workload was manageable, but definitely plan ahead. The TAs graded most of the assignments, but the bigger things were graded by her. Even after incorporating all her critiques into my rough drafts and taking the edited versions to the writing lab, I still got graded very harshly. She also doesn't grade directly from the rubric.

Academic writing is one of the more difficult topics for me and most of my friends and peers. Prof. Reschke helped me succeed in writing through SFL 315. She is so kind and accommodating. Visiting her office hours was a blessing and her TAs were extremely helpful as well. The class is difficult but manageable and support based.

The structure of the class jumps around a lot, which can be frustrating, but Professor Reschke is very kind. Be cautious of AI, the detector isn't very accurate but she is very willing and accommodating if you get in that situation. Professor Reschke is really helpful and gives good feedback. Ask questions and you'll get a good grade!

Going back, I would not take this class online. The layout was hard to follow and I felt like the class jumped around. Online lectures were reading heavy and felt irrelevant to the weekly assignments. Assignments took a very long time and I was accused of using AI when I didn't. Luckily she took my word for it, but it was a frustrating process.

This class is a lot of work no matter who you take it from. The writing is hard and takes a long time but you work on it throughout the semester. Be careful of AI cause she will give 0s. But she is willing to work with students and give them the benefit of the doubt.

Assignments jumped around so much, it was impossible to follow along. We talked about public scholarship and then suddenly we had huge papers written on the opposite end of the spectrum. She graded papers and I think she used a diff rubric than she gave us. Formatting was unclear. Even asking TAs for help didn't help your score. Worst ever grade.

I loved Prof Reschke! She was very accommodating throughout the semester when I was struggling. There are a lot of assignments that are due every week. I always sent them to my TA for feedback before turning them in, which guaranteed an A! The end-of-the-semester essay is the heaviest grade. I did very well on it because I had my TA look it over.

Honestly, hated this class, but I don't love writing! However, Prof Reschke is willing to work with you and is forgiving if you are honest with her. Do not use AI! She uses a detector. Also be aware the organizational is a little tricky and sometimes assignments are out of order. You can get through it if you put the work in.

This class was pretty disorganized. The instructions and rubrics often didn't match. I didn't feel like I was taught much, mainly just learned everything myself. The assignments were helpful and overall interesting as you got to pick your topics. I felt like the grading was sometimes harsh, never giving full credit. Overall a decent online option.

Professor Reschke is amazing! I didn't love writing, but I am SO grateful I took this class from her. She gives detailed & personalized feedback on all assignments and papers. The course load is very manageable & the material engaging. She is accessible for questions & help regarding course material. *Please take this class from her! She's awesome!

Nice lady, but her grading is super tough. She gives you hardly any feedback on the rough drafts and then tons of comments on the final paper. If you fix everything she tells you to fix she still finds a way to make your paper bad. This class was really tough and I felt like it was not fair the way she graded.
Professor Reschke expects you to know exactly what she wants in a paper and is unwilling to meet and work with students. I don't think she cares about her students.

Great professor and awesome human being. Genuinely cares for her students and the people around her. The lectures are a little hard to follow sometimes but assignments are clear and not too hard to complete and she is very graceful with her grading.

She is an amazing teacher who truly cares for her students. She teaches the material in a very unique way that makes it easy to learn and to get a good grade if you participate in class and read the weekly material.

Dr. Bingham is a very sweet woman who clearly knows a lot about philosophy, but I wouldn't recommend taking her class. I have nothing bad to say about her as a person, but you won't really learn from this class. The assignments aren't always super clear, and she mixes up a lot of concepts. She is clearly a great woman who I think should retire.

Professor Bingham is super sweet and a great person but most of the information in this class you will need to learn on your own because lectures can be confusing. Quizzes and Exam are a class discussion so that is nice. I wouldn't take this class if you are actually interested in Philosophy and are majoring in it.

I ended up dropping her class after a week, because there was no clear explanation on what to do for most of her homework assignments.
She seems like a very nice teacher who is good at letting the class lead philosophy lectures. 
The content from the class made a lot of sense, but there was nothing online to tell you what to do for the assignments.

I absolutely loved this class! Professor Issak is so knowledgeable and passionate about humanities. She treated us all like her adopted children and was always so kind and made me laugh. Lectures can be boring and not very engaging. Very easy grader. It was not hard at all to get a good grade. Will be taking more classes from her in the future.

She is very kind and wonderful. She cares about what she teaches and it shines through. Your grade is test heavy for sure, but they aren't too bad. She also was very gracious with late work. The only problem is the grading is SO behind. Hard to say if it was the TA's or the professor, but I didn't know my grades till the last week of the semester.

I took IHUM 201 with her and loved it! However, IHUM 202 might have been the worst class I have ever taken. Professor Isaak is great, it's her TAs that are the problem. They take two months to grade assignments, don't offer feedback, and won't respond when you ask about it. It got to the point where it started to feel personal. Don't take it!

Professor Isaak is fine. She did good review videos for exams which was nice. I have a bone to pick with this class and the TAs though. Stay away from IHUM 202 online. Take a different general. It is SO test heavy and the TAs grade WAY to harshly (and take forever) and the study guides don't even prepare you well enough for the exams.

Entertaining lectures, and EXTREMELY light reading for a humanities class. The only concern is she is super behind in grading so most of the time you have no idea how you are doing, but she is a merciful grader and has provided 6 optional assignments for up to 30 points in extra credit so there is plenty of cushion.

Professor Isaak is very sweet and kind and the class is organized well on Canvas. That being said, the tests are weighted so heavily and the material does not adequately prepare you for the tests. The first midterm, she had to curve the average up to a 75% so it was at a C. It was really hard for a general if you're not passionate about humanities.

I'm surprised by some of these ratings because Professor Isaak has been a great professor this semester. This class is great when taken online, tasks are broken down with time estimates and there are dedicated blocks of time for studying and writing. The only thing this class is lacking is thorough feedback on exam responses/essays.

Good class. A lot of reading and small assignments but all of it is very achievable and does not take that long. You do have to study and give this class some effort for the exams, but nothing to stress about. Papers felt a little meaningless but I think that is just a personal preference. I loved her communication style and learned and had fun

Professor Isaak is such a fun professor to learn from. Her lectures are engaging and she really makes the art and history come alive. There are great discussions in class when people choose to participate. Sometimes class is a little scattered, but Prof Isaak will adjust the tests to reflect what was covered in class. Go with the flow and enjoy!

Dr. Isaak is great! She's great at making the humanities accessible and it makes it really engaging for everyone, regardless of prior exposure or experience. She is funny and caring and really helpful! I'm excited to take more classes from her.

Get ready to memorize a ton of random crap and I mean a ton. All things that you could find out in a 1-sec Google search, but you now need to commit to memory. 3 papers and 3 exams, which, thank heavens, are not cumulative. At least it counts as a double general. Professor Isaak is nice and always willing to help but man is there a lot to memorize.

She is a really nice person. The class is a little bit boring, but not too hard. Her tests are super easy and she does a good review before each test. The hardest part of the class is the out of class assignments. She does not really remind you of them and if you miss one you can't get any of the points back. She also has some extra credit.

I cannot recommend professor isaak enough.  She grades accurately, the courseload is tough but managable. Exams are fairly easy if you do your reading -- and the reading doesn't take long at all, but you actually have to do it. You could glide through the class not doing anything, but then you'd fail the exam.
Isaak's lectures can be a bit scattered, but she's genuinely interested in helping students learn. Lots of reading and assignments, so stay on top of it. Unstuck ai was a lifesaver for study prep!

Professor Isaak: super nice. This class: a nightmare. Do not take this class online. The homework load is INSANE & the exams are so specific. The review guides aren't very helpful & Professor Isaak didn't share much when she did her reviews. There is lots of extra credit but the load is so heavy. The quizzes take forever and the readings are HEAVY.

The amount of homework in this online class was absolutely insane. In 4 years I have never had SO MANY assignments. Also, the quizzes are "open book" but they take forever because the book's search feature is HORRIBLE.

Took this online, class wasn't terrible. Lots of reading from textbooks and other books. 3 papers and 3 tests. Was manageable, did not feel like there was much busy work. Great option if you just need to fulfill a GE credit. The information is actually pretty interesting and the online version of this class is easy to get through quickly.
The amount of homework is actually insane for this online class. I was forced to spend more time on this class because of readings and homework than even American Heritage. Honestly kind of greedy.

Highly recommend Prof. Isaak, she is a safe space and very accommodating. Being in person for lectures matters, but if needs be, she and the TA are willing to work with you. At least 2-3 take-home assignments per subject, but are manageable, 2 arts papers, and 2 exams. Works with students to ensure they succeed and again couldn't recommend her more

There is no homework at all really tbh. Prof Isaak is very passionate about humanities and sometimes will go on a 20 min tangent of talking about her experiences viewing art in Rome or something, She was great!

Prof. Isaak is a caring person who wants students to learn. Her lectures were often entertaining and enjoyable! I had trouble contacting her outside of class (she never responded to my emails). She tends to go on tangents during lectures discussing stuff not on the test, then you have to learn it on your own. Still an enjoyable class though!

Lots of reading and essay writing and studying ahead but once you put in the work it's smooth sailing. When I'm a CS major a class like this was super nice, even if it was decently hard work, because the professor is really nice and the topics are pretty interesting. Plus it was just time that I was away from coding and I needed that.

Professor Isaak is super passionate about Humanities, and she shows it. It's nice, because I'm not exactly into humanities, and yet she made it so entertaining. I felt like I had to study a reasonable amount for midterms. I appreciated that there was four weeks of lecture on how to balance the arts with the sciences, so it wasn't all emotional.

Prof Isaak is one of the kindest people ever, but it felt as if the class was designed for Humanities or Art History majors. There is just a lot of homework. Prof Isaak is really willing to work with you, and because there's so much homework, a bad grade on an assignment won't really hurt you.
I could not get the grade I wanted no matter what I did. One slip up will cost the class.

Honestly, I haven't had to work this hard for a GE ever since American Heritage. YEAH. It's as if she doesn't realize that this class is a requirement and the majority of students aren't majoring in humanities? She's super nice and fun but just save yourself from the stress that this class is going to cause you and take it from someone else.

She teaches in a way that I was able to understand and homework assignments/reading were fairly easy and not time consuming. She knows her stuff very well and is smart. She likes to tie a lot of things in the lectures to her political views and problems she has with the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Discussions of such are frequent.

I loved professor issak's class so much!!! I have never cared about anything having to do with humanities and she gave some of the most engaging lectures. she was always so sweet and kind and in a good mood. attendance isn't mandatory but I did way better on the exams when I went bc she is a very easy to learn from and remember things. 10/10

Professor Isaak loves Humanities and makes it exciting. Get ready to memorize art and music. She's not the best at grading papers in a timely fashion so I didn't know my grade in the class until after finals were over.

I love Professor Isaak. Truly one of the kindest, most caring, and unbelievably smart professors I have ever had. She is so fair in everything she does and if you try your best, you can get an A. She goes completely out of her way to ensure her students feel loved and will do anything to help. Take Writing 150 from her, you won't regret it!

She is so funny and nice. Super understanding and willing to work with students. I never read the textbook and got an A. Just pay attention and take notes in lecture and you'll be set for the tests. Note: you have to memorize the names and tunes of music and art pieces for tests.

This is my second time taking a class from Professor Isaak and I really enjoyed her class. With the online format we didn't really have lectures and really had to teach ourselves but she's always willing to answer questions and clear anything up. Papers were graded hard but it was the TA's. Tests were okay if you read and studied available material

Like other people said, there is a a lot of memorization. Flash card are your best friends for this class. I recommend putting art (and painted), terms, and keypoints in your flashcard every time you are studying. Go through it multiple times a day. Thatll prepare you for you exams. For essays, got to the writing center. They were able to help!

This woman is so nice, but her class is HELL. Just save yourself the time and don't take it. It's as if she doesn't think you have other classes. The amount of work is obnoxious. Grades writing as if it is a writing class.

This class is a ridiculous amount of work. Not only is there an absurd amount of reading and hw assignments each week, but the tests expect you to remember pretty much everything your read. There are a few essays that are graded as if it is an english course. Nice teacher, interesting class, but I think she asks too much especially for a GE

Professor Isaak is a super nice lady, but her lectures are all over the place. If you don't know music or art, this class will be very tough for you. On the contrary, if you do know those things, this class is right for you. Either way, she is willing to work with you, but don't expect to have no homework or reading. This class will keep you busy.

Honestly Prof. Isaak is one of the best at BYU. She cares so much about her students and loves what she teaches. She is interesting and fun, and helps you learn without overloading you. Grading is fair. DON'T MISS THE CHANCE TO TAKE A CLASS FROM HER.
She is so funny and nice. Class is actually fascinating and enjoyable. Listen in class and the tests are fine.

Although kind & well intentioned, she left major papers to be graded until after the final. Most of your grade is 4 papers, but the class never seemed to instruct how to write in a more academic way. She's always willing to give feedback, but without timely grading then what's the point? Frustrating at best; I feel that I didn't learn much from her

At first, I loved Professor Isaak's class. She is fun and seems genuine. However, she did not grade anything on time! After finals, I still had 37 ungraded assignments, 4 of which were huge papers that would determine my grade. It was incredible stressful to not get the feedback I needed to know how to improve my papers and not know what grade.

Prof Isaak is a really, really great professor. The online course isn't that great, it's really reading heavy. I wish there were more days that she taught because I really did like her, but online courses are not my favorite. A general knowledge of humanities really helped me through this course, so if you've taken a past course, review your notes.

I literally cannot say enough good things about Prof. Isaak! She did an amazing job of helping me to be excited for the material and to learn it really in depth but also in a way that it didn't feel to overwhelming. She is passionate about what she does, kind, and so present for her students. I was pleasantly surprised by this class thanks to her!

I would not recommend this class unless you really like music and art. She tends to ramble a lot and doesn't really hit key points we need to know for the tests. The tests are pretty hard for a GE class and if you zone out easily, don't take this class.

The only way that you are going to do good in this class is if you already know a lot about Art and Music. She gives out a lot of busy work and her exams are absolutely insane. A lot of what she teaches in the lectures are on her tests but she barely goes over the topics and expects you to know everything about them.

She is a very nice and approachable professor. Her Intro to Humanities class is fairly straightforward (your grade doesn't ride on one assignment but is distributed evenly among different assignments). I love how she incorporates Latter-day Saint works into the different types of arts discussed in the class. She has you go to different art events.
If you are a person who likes science, math, and the facts of history, don't take this class. Take history 201 or a different professor. This class is very artsy and I hated every second of it.

She doesn't post her slides. If you don't take notes, you will probably struggle to pass on the test. Not super hard class, just unbearable. The reading assignments, listening assignments, and pretty much every other assignments were like nails on a chalk board.

Her class is pretty dense for a GE credit. There's lots of homework and the rests are far more difficult than they need to be. You have to know even minute details, even unimportant ones. I'm not sure why...

Professor Isaak is the best history teacher I have ever had, the class is well organized and she is very clear about what is expected from you on assignments, tests, and papers. Lectures are great and it is clear she knows what she is talking about.

Amazing and caring professor. I went in for every paper for help and she was so kind and helpful. Not hard to get an A if you're willing to work with and revise your drafts a lot. Barely any homework if you're not working on a paper. Papers are reasonable and requirements are clear. She is the best! Take WRTG 150 from her if possible!

Don't be swayed by her fan club reviews like I was. Doesn't clearly teach big ideas, lectures on her opinion of things that have nothing to do with class, assigns super long readings randomly and with little warning, and doesn't grade big assignments until finals week. Very frustrating experience that hopefully, she changes in the future.

The professor makes the class seem light and easy when in reality she is completely disorganized and makes your life difficult. Doesn't grade assignments until the last week of class so you have no idea how you are doing on anything. Took 2 months to grade our first paper so she could "give feedback", I had 2 comments both said "I agree"

She is ridiculous with how many assignments you have to do. Drops reading assignments like reading a full 2-hour play and 24 chapter book with just a couple days notice. Spend more time on this class than my 5 other classes combined. She is nice but spends most of the lecture on tangents. The only positive is that the tests are straight forward.

I didn't buy the textbook. Quizlet will be your best friend. This class isn't easy by any means, definitely avoid taking it in the Spring or Summer if you have to. She's one of those teachers who legitimately condenses the material of a whole semester into a term. Lots of required seminars and live group discussions if you're not into that.

Honestly such an easy class. I took it over the summer online and it was a breeze. The study guides are super helpful and the exams are straight to the point. All of the long answers come from the webinars and group discussions and also from the practice quizzes. And it counts for 2 GE's so doesn't get better than that.

The online class during the summer is definitely a lot. We have a TON of readings and homework each week but it's expected in a short semester. But honestly it's a good class, she is clear on what you need to know for the test. SO SLOW on getting assignments back though. Like 3 weeks sometimes, and when the class is so short, it's really difficul

Great class, does involve work. Tests are straightforward, especially if you go to reviews and read the textbook. Make sure you get TA feedback on your arts encounter papers; I got an 84 on my first paper (without showing it to my TA) and then was well into the 90s on the other two that I brought to office hours before turning them in

Professor Isaak is the best teacher I've had at BYU. Her study guides are clear and helpful. She takes time to meet with students and goes above and beyond to help them. She has a great sense of humor and makes learning about Humanities enjoyable. The class does require work and you have to attend class. I plan to take another class from her.

Professor Isaak is awesome! I'm a molecular biology major, so was not expecting to really enjoy a Humanities class. But she made this class enjoyable and interesting. She's got a funny sense of humor and she is super knowledgeable. She provides a clear study guide for exactly what to know for the tests. Go to class and take good notes!

She is one of the most accommodating and caring professors I've ever had. She has tons of small assignments, but they take less than an hour to complete. Her exams are easy, non-cumulative. She does require you to attend art events and write papers about it, they weren't bad. Class reiterates the reading, but is helpful for the exams.

SO. MANY. PAPERS. she will assign four paragraph papers and make it due the next class period. expect at least one page a week, with four page papers every month. lectures were pointless to attend, she would ramble on about pointless things- just read the textbook. ta reviews were useless. tests are memorization and obscure facts about artists.

Worst professor at BYU, bland and so so boring. She doesn't post assignments until the day before its due so if you like to get ahead you wont. Her lectures are boring and contain zero information on her slides so if you miss class you're screwed for that specific day. Gets off topic a lot and is super nit-picky on papers.
Her class is organized and meaningful. She is a very open person. LGBTQ+ friendly.

I took Professor Isaak again after dropping another class after a schedule conflict a previous semester. Very glad I had another opportunity to take a class from her. She explains everything you need to know in the lectures very clearly. You can tell she enjoys what she teaches and cares for her students. Exams are thorough but fair.

She is literally the most amazing professor I have had a BYU so far. She makes humanities enjoyable and easy to understand. I loved her class! Just make sure you study the art and fill out the study guide and you will be fine.

She's one of the best professors I've ever had, I took two classes from her. Very clear about what she expects of you on the assignments, exams, etc. and will never try to trick you into losing points. Great lectures, she's really passionate about what she teaches. But get ready to study and really take good notes in class.

Professor Isaak is wonderful! She is very passionate about Humanities, and it is obvious in her lectures and personality. Her tests are fair. She is clear on what you need to know for the test (study guides are detailed well). Her papers aren't difficult if you pay attention and follow the criteria asked to write on. Readings are interesting too.

She's the best! Very understanding and takes the time to make learning doable. You still definitely have to put the work in, but she works with you, not against you. Very funny in lecture. She makes you think about the world differently and ties the material to the gospel. Use her online study guide and TA sessions to study for tests.

Professor Isaak is one of the funniest people ever. I was doubtful about taking this class, but it turned out to be really enjoyable! Very rarely were there longer assignments. It was primarily a bunch of short assignments. Exams are really easy, and the papers are simple. If one were to put it in a little work, then they could easily pass.

I took WRTG150 from her and then I took her online IHUM101 class. Depending on your work load this class ranges from easy to moderate. I took it as my only class, online while working a 40hr/week job. Exams are straight forward. All multiple choice and straight from the material assigned. Expectations are not unrealistic. Would take again

Dr. Isaak is one of the best teachers I've ever had.  She makes assignments applicable and flexible.  For one of my assignments, I chose to write a letter to my department head, and I definitely put more effort into that than anything else before. She is always willing to take the time to listen and chat with you, on papers and on life.

Professor Isaak is great! She really cares about her students and makes the lectures fun. If you don't show up for the lectures, you won't pass. The book helps, but the lectures if where it's really at. Show up for class, pay attention, read the book, go to the TA study sessions . . . easy A

Professor Isaak is pretty awesome. She really cares about what she is teaching, and it rubs off on the students. I have a greater appreciation for the arts. Go to class, study for the tests, and make sure you understand the papers! Talk to your TA and make sure you know what they are looking for. Tests are easy if you study.

Professor Isaak has a deep knowledge of the arts. That being said she drowns out in lecture and is boring. A lot is learned in terms of analysis and critique of art, but a lot of material and art discussed is nonsense and is tailored to her personal taste. Grade in class is purely dictated by how good TA is, so it makes class a hit or miss.

I took this class to fill a GE requirement. Professor Isaak has a deep knowledge of the arts, yet I couldn't seem to understand the content without having to study my guts out. Plan on a paper due every Friday and 3 big response papers. One of the reasons I enjoy this class is because I have a great TA. Buckle up, Its a difficult GE.

She's a great professor, but if you're just looking for an easy GE, don't take her. There's definitely a lot of homework and you'll have to study a lot for the tests. The test material comes almost exclusively from her lectures, so don't skip. The textbook was helpful in understanding the basics, but really wasn't necessary for doing well on tests.

Fantastic teacher, difficult class for a General Ed. She is very passionate and knowledgeable, her lectures are entertaining and educational. You get to attend fun music and theatre events. The problem is everything the TA's are involved in i.e. the labs are a waste of time and they grade extra harsh on weekly papers which is infuriating.
For just an introductory writing class, the amount of homework is ridiculous. In such a low level writing course the amount of homework should be nowhere near as much as it is.
I LOVED Professor Isaak as my Writing 150 Professor! She was clear, honest, and fun to be around! I'd definitely take another class from her!

I'm not a fan of humanities, but Prof. Isaak made the class fun and interesting. There is a lot of material covered in the class, but as long as you go through the study guide and take good notes in class you should do well on the exams. Most of the exam material comes from class and she doesn't post her slides so dont skip class! Would take again!

She's a funny, interactive lecturer. She made me interested in the course even though I'm a business major, and I see aspects of it everywhere. Don't expect responses to emails for at least 2+ weeks. She has a philosophy to never give 100% on any assignment.

I loved taking this class. I'm a scientist, not a humanities student, but I truly enjoyed learning about the history and culture of this class. It was easy, and counts for Civilization credit. Definitely recommend it for Civ.

Professor Isaak is an incredibly gifted teacher. Her lectures are best described as professional storytelling time. She makes all the material interesting and enjoyable. Although there was a good amount of outside textbook reading, the tests aren't too bad. In my opinion, however, each paper should NOT be worth more than each midterm!

Prof. Isaak managed to make humanities interesting. She has a funny, dry sense of humor that made going to class quite pleasant. There's a ton of writing and a moderate amount of reading. The tests are not hard if you attend class, pay attention, and take TONS of notes. Attendance is not mandatory, but you'll do awful on the tests if you don't go.

Professor Isaak was a great professor! I really enjoyed her lectures, but there were way too many assignments. At times, we were doing two assignments each week, and most of them were a bit pointless. I totally understand having to write a couple papers, but this was too much! Also, SO many hand-written notes.

Okay, she is the best lecturer I have ever had at BYU. Or anywhere. Ever. She makes humanities sound interesting (no easy feat) and sets clear and totally attainable expectations for the class. Not hard. Not boring. If you're looking to get a good grade while enjoying a class that isn't your cup of tea, she's the go-to.

I love Professor Isaak, but her class was a tough one, unless you are really interested in humanities. She covers lots of material, and basically any tiny thing she mentions in class could end up on the test, and she doesn't post her lectures, so you take a TON of hand-written notes in class (doesn't allow computers) 2 big papers and 2 small ones.

Mrs. Isaak is a great teacher. She has a unique personality and defiantly is prepared to teach daily! So be prepared. Her classes are organized and she knows what she hopes each student will learn. She loves life and really has seen a lot of it! It is  nice to have a well rounded teacher teaching English. Great GE course!

The subject matter of this course was incredibly boring for me. That being said, I looked forward to going to class every day, just because of Professor Isaak. She is hilarious and is so passionate and knows so much about what she teaches. There is hardly any homework, but she tends to have EXTREMELY difficult tests. Stay up on readings!!

Prof. Isaak knows her stuff and is really passionate about it which makes her class fun. I usually just deal with history but I was actually pretty interested all through her class. Its a fair amount of work to be sure but none of it is dumb busy work.
Took Honors Writing from her and loved her. She's fun and energetic and connects well with students. Great freshman-level course. Would be fun to take her again.

This is by far the best GE class I've taken. Professor Isaak is an excellent teacher. You can tell she has a passion for the subject and teaching. Her lectures were so interesting and entertaining. I never dozed off once. Her class does take work, but she's fair, and she's pretty good at getting feedback to her students promptly. Will take again!

Professor Isaak is an EXCELLENT teacher. She's a master at presenting material in an educational, interesting, & entertaining way. The textbook is useful but unnecessary, she gives great prompts for the writing assignments, & the tests reflect the material presented in class to a T. If you attend class & take quality notes, you'll do well. 5 stars!

I love Sister Isaak! I had no interest whatsoever in art history and am now contemplating changing my major. She is so passionate and makes the class enjoyable. 2.5 hr lectures (summer class) went by quickly and I always looked forward to class. The papers weren't over the top easy and you need to study, but it's all so interesting!

My favorite teacher EVER. I was worried going into the class because I didn't have a much experience with the world of humanities and I'm not a very good writer. However, Professor Isaak made class so interesting and fun to attend. She was so helpful with my papers. If you go to class and participate, she will do her best to help you. Awesome.

Prof Isaak is amazing and it's obvious she knows the material really well. I found the course and her lectures interesting. There were 3 fairly long essays throughout the semester but overall if you do your work and attend lecture an A is doable. I would definitely take this class again!!

This was a wonderful class - not an easy A, but very fair and clear on what you need to know. One of the best teachers I've encountered - I learned so much from her and enjoyed her lectures. Attending lectures and taking notes are necessary in doing well on tests. A few big papers and a lot of smaller assignments. Highly interesting subject!!

Professor Isaak is probably one of the greatest professors I have ever had. She is an amazing teacher and really wants you to learn and be involved. She definitely makes you work for your grade, but it's worth it. She's hilarious and makes class fun. I learned so much from her!

Phenomenal. Not easy, but Dr Isaak is such an engaging and funny instructor that it makes up for the time spent studyingwriting. She knows the material like the back of her hand, yet is entirely humble about it. Two 5-7 page papers to go along with projects, four exams (final is not comprehensive), 1-2 quizzes, and homework papers (2 pages each)
