She was a really great professor. If you're taking humanities I DEFINITELY would recommend taking from Isaak.

Definitely my favorite professor at BYU! She's smart, funny and cares about helping her students. USE HER OFFICE HOURS. She's there to help if Humanities doesn't come naturally to you, or you just aren't understanding something. I wish she taught more classes!

Absolutely loved this class. Would recommend to anyone. There are quite a few assignments and a bit of reading, but I didn't feel overwhelmed. She's clear and makes the subject matter really interesting. Professor Issak was helpful and funny. I learned a ton in that class, and had a lot of fun doing it!

I hated and feared history before this class. She is a goofball and made the material interesting. I wish I would have taken her for 201 instead of HIST 201. A good amount of reading and writing, but I expected that from a history class. Definitely take her if you are looking to get your history credits out of the way. She is awesome. SPRING Term.

Class overall not hard. It demands a lot but you can get out of it. I sparknotes most of the reading assignments and did fine. The only thing that got me was lecture questions on the exams. Her final is not comprehensive either which is nice. She is also really bad at updating grades. Easy class if you put in time.
Professor Isaak is hilarious and she's passionate about the subject.  It's not a super hard class, just do the assignments and memorize in order to do well on the tests.

I cannot recommend this class.  Not overly difficult, and you don't have to do the reading, but here tests are all memorization and regurgitation, and most of her assignments are ridiculous: dream analysis, reading poetry out loud in nature, creating art and writing a big paper about it.  Not worth the hassle, unless you really like humanities.

This was a great class. Not too much work, and the assignments we did do were interesting and worth my time. Overall a pretty easy class. Do not buy the book, you don't use it at all, it's just for a reference (which you won't need). Her lectures were fun and interesting and the TAs were very helpful when preparing for tests. An enjoyable GE class.

She takes forever to get your stuff back to you, so sometimes that can be annoying. She's a fun lady and pretty hilarious sometimes, but I fell asleep almost every day during her lectures. You don't really need the book, she goes over everything in her slides. Not a lot of hw, just 3 papers and a few assignments in and out of class. Study for tests

Great professor!  Class discussions were very interesting and the workload was not too intense.  Just make sure you do all the work and you'll do well in the class.  If you want a professor who is fun, then take this class!

Professor Isaak made me really like Humanities. I definitely suggest her, and I am going to continue to take her classes to fill my GE's. Her tests and papers are fair, and she is really engaging in lecture. You will never feel overwhelmed in this class.
Best professor ever! I have had her for 4 classes already that is how great she is. She is seriously hilarious abut you will also learn so much. She is also extremely helpful with anything you need.

I am not studying the arts by any means but took this to fulfill a GE requirement. She is the coolest, most reasonable teacher I've ever had. She made every class enjoyable and gave assignments and papers that actually helped me learn and enjoy what I was learning. NO BUSY WORK. Just take notes and take time on hw and you'll be fine.

I loved Professor Isaak. She made humanities, a general ed, fun and engaging, even though that is not a subject I would normally be interested in. Class is easy, and the notes give a good outline of how to study. As long as you can do some memorizing and just remember what was discussed, you'll do fine. Some reading is also required.

I loved Dr. Isaak. She is quirky, funny, and makes lectures extremely interesting. She cares for her class and by the end you'll have a love for art. Study hard for tests. Follow directions for papers. Didn't use the book.
This class is super easy and a lot of fun! She is a really nice person, but still funny at the same time. We did tons of cool and unique things that made it interesting. Highly recommend her.

Prof. Isaak is AWESOME. She makes the papers less intimidating by having one-on-one consultations with each person. She brings food on peer-review days. In class we learn different tools to write better papers and she walks us through each paper every step of the way: from idea to end. I would definitely recommend her. She's also helpful and nice.

Professor Isaak is very nice and loves what she teaches. However, she mumbles a lot during class and you miss a lot of what she is saying. She is an incredibly picky grader and will mark you off for the smallest things. Tests are extremely long and hard, all in all I'd say take from someone else.

Prof. Isaak (aka Sister Benedicta) is an incredibly passionate, helpful, genuinely awesome mentor and human being. Her writing for film and theatre class was the best Oral/Written Comm class I could have hoped for. Extremely tactful and encouraging of my writing, and responsive to class needs and desires. Flexible, witty, superb professor!

I have to admit when I signed up for this class I thought it was going to be another boring GE but I honestly enjoyed this class. Pro. Isaak is a little quirky, but made every lecture interesting. As long as you go to class and take good notes tests are easy to ace. The 2 papers weren't that bad either.

This class is really fun and great.  I learned a lot.  Professor Isaak knows a lot about the subject and loves to tell interesting stories on the subject.  There are a fair amount of papers in this class, just make sure you follow the guidelines.  Good class, I recommend taking humanities from her.

Prof Isaak was super helpful and willing to meet about papers and she gave great advice! She grades all of the papers herself and gives awesome feedback! We also had a ton of fun class activities and she's super chill. Food on peer review days :) Sometimes class time felt pointless but attendance is pretty much mandatory. I would recommend her!

I loved this class.  Some say she grades hard, which is true, to a point, but she gives great detailed critique on your papers so you know how to do better, and I steadily improved throughout the semester.  She is also really relaxed, relatable, intereting, and just a nice person.  Take if you like writing!

Preofessor Isaak is awesome. She is just so likeable and intersting. She is quirky and adds her own experience to the subject matter which makes it more interesting. You dont need to go get the book. Everything from the test comes from lecture. But take GOOD NOTES. You can buy the book if you want just in case you need to clarify on certain things.

Prof. Isaak is very down to earth and passionate. Class was time-consuming but work tapered throughout sem, which was nice. Reading + writing assignment roughly once a week. 2 big projects that were very intimidating but I got through them. Exams are easy to ace as long as you study what she gives you - MEMORIZE! I would def take from her again!

Professor Isaak was engaging and very helpful! She is the best teacher I've had at BYU, and her work load isn't too bad either. No comprehensive final, great and funny lectures, and a very positive classroom experience!

I loved her humanities class! She has such a funny sense of humor and her classes were always so fascinating. I really didn't think the tests were all that hard, either. I would definitely take another class from her if I had the chance.

Great way to get a GE out of the way. The class is laid back and she makes sure that you know when due dates are and is flexible. Don't bother with the textbooks, they're unnecessary. Lectures aren't mandatory but useful. She is funny and makes class personal. This is not a stressful class and very doable.

Professor Isaak is so cool! I love her lectures, she makes them interesting and enjoyable. The grading in this class is fair even though the tests are hard. She provides adequate study guide material for the tests though, and if you fill them out you'll be fine. Highly recommended.

Here's the deal. Professor Isaak is way cool and I like her a lot. Her lectures are fun and interesting but I hated the grading in this class so much. I really felt like it was impossible for me to get an A. I felt like the exams were a bit ridiculous and I got the worst grade of the semester here(B-).

Look, people. We're in university. You SHOULD be going to lectures and taking good notes. And you won't be sorry. In addition to my notes I have funny quotes Prof. Isaak has said during class- she makes it fun! I thought I'd hate these GE's until I met her and she was awesome. Not intimidating at all and pretty fair. highly recommended.

Great professor. Makes lectures applicable and interesting. Make sure you go to class, and if you miss, get the notes from someone. Her tests aren't too bad, just make sure you memorize the slides she gives you.

She makes class really fun and enjoyable.  However, she is a hard grader when it comes to papers.  If you like writing, you will love her class.  She is very clear with her teaching.  Attend the lectures because her tests contain material from the lectures.

She made class enjoyable because she has the beset sense of humor. You didn't even need to read the textbook because she told you everything you needed to know on the test. I would definately take another class from her.
Helpful, works hard to develop relationships with students. Tests are extremely difficult but come straight from book and lecture.

Great professor, tons of reading, come to class and study for the exams and you'll do fine.  She does test on composers, artists, era so make sure you know pretty much everything on study guide.  Class is time consuming but if you attend and do the assignments you'll do fine.

Wonderful class and teacher! She is hilarious and very down to earth and gets to know her students. gives good feedback on all papers and is willing to help. Classes were fun and interesting and she would bring delicious food for us a lot!

Really interesting class. It's not hard per-say, but it is a lot of work in comparison to other classes I've taken like this.  There are frequent reading assignments, each with a short essay due with it. 2 big essays that require some outside activity or project as well.  Tests are fairly straight forward--lots of memorizing required though.

Good class! Use her office hours. She made sure to make comments on your paper so that you wouldn't get docked points and you didn't know why. She brought food a lot :) Her final was easiest of all time: write a poem, which is outlined and graded on completion. Funny and helpful face to face, and changes due dates if she tells the class needs time.

Sister Isaak is hilarious and facilitates good discussions in class. She corrects everything herself because of the small classes. This is great, but at the same time she does not have a ton of time to help you with papers. Sometimes I wanted more guidance and had to meet with her outside the scheduled help time. She is very pleasant. Solid class

I really enjoyed this class. Wonderful teacher; really passionate about the subject. Don't stress about the reading; if you don't have time, just don't do it (Sparknote it all). Go to class and take good notes, and you will do well. Tests are hard but do-able if you study. I previously hated humanities (accounting major), but I loved this class.

She's nice, and I can see how B students like her. I'm not so happy with a B, so I found her grading annoyingly ambiguous. If you enjoy memorizing useless details about things that you forget as your spit out onto the page, then her tests are fine. The papers are really annoying to write. Take a different Civ class, this one's not worth it.

You don't actually have to read from the Culture and Values textbook, just the Norton. She'll give you good feedback on your writing. She has a good sense of humor. I could have swore she was in her 20's on the first day of class. Predictable exams (memorize and regurgitate). She makes treats for class on special days.

Best Humanities professor I've taken so far. She's way fun and hilarious! Classes will never be boring. Do you reading (sparknote), go to class and studying for the test should be a cake. Going to class make a huge difference, so don't miss. Writing assignments are fun and productive. I recommend her 110% Love her!

Isaak is awesome. She grades fairly on papers. Her tests are straight forward if you've done three things. One memorize the works she lists on the study guide, two go to class, and three take good notes.

She's cool and makes class fun for the most part. Sometimes her comments don't match up with the grade(ex. I had a paper with a lot of comments pointing out flaws in my arguments and pretty much bashing my stance, but somehow I managed a B) She assigns a lot of work but is pretty lenient with due dates. Very helpful if you go to her for paper help.

Kathryn Isaak is a wonderful teacher. Her lectures are very interesting and made me excited to go to class. She is very witty and has a great sense of humor. The best part is that her tests directly reflect what she taught you in class. So as long as you go and take good notes and read, you'll do excellent on her tests. I loved her class.

WONDERFUL teacher, though initially very confusing. You ABOSOLUTELY have to keep going in to her office hours to clarify things. Once you understand her a bit better, she can help you become a great writer. This was a wonderful class!

Kathryn has a challenging, interesting, educational, do-able course. Lecture is mostly her talking, but she doesn't mind if you want to make a comment or ask a question. You'll read and write quite a bit, but it's good reading and engaging writing topics. Even the projects were well worth it. Overall, great.

Kathryn's course is challenging and educational, but definitely do-able. You will read & write quite a bit, but the it's all really interesting - even the projects are good. Her tests are absolutely fair, but challenging. Class discussion's not a big thing with her - mostly lecture - though she does let you make comments and will respond.

I loved this class, but sometimes her comments didn't didn't match up AT ALL with her grade ("great paper! really, not too many suggestions! 83%"). I did feel like I became a better writer by the end of the semester, though, because I became her friend and KEPT ASKING QUESTIONS!! Make use of her office hours!!!

I love Sis. Isaak!  She really cares about what she teaches and makes it fun and interesting for everybody.  She loves class participation, so don't be afraid to raise your hand.  her tests aren't hard at all if you go by the study guide.  Most of everything you need to know, you get in class, so reading the book isn't necessarily mandatory.

Good teacher.  Go to class if u want to pass.  Textbook doesn't provide nearly the information you need to pass her tests.  Have to write a couple papers, don't make them fluff or you will pay.  Managable class.  Use study guide and class notes to prepare for tests

Professor Isaak is the an excellent professor, I loved her class! Class notes are essential for passing exams, whereas the info in the book is not as heavily tested on. I love Professor Isaak because she really cares and that helps her to teach clearly, and inspire.

Awesome professor. Class attendance MANDATORY if you want to pass a test. Take really detailed notes. Helpful in preparing you for test. Gives a study guide. Tests were super easy with little studying. Papers were hard but doable. Easy A or A-

If you need a class to fulfill your Classical Civilization G.E., then Sis. Isaak is the best teacher to take them from at BYU. She teaches you a lot, has a moderate amount of work (fair for a 3 credit class, unlike some Civ. Classes), is a great deal of fun to listen to in class. My favorite teacher (along w/ Byron Merrill) at BYU.

Funny lady, she makes her subject really interesting. I enjoyed her as a teacher and I enjoyed her class, however, I wish we got more explanation and feedback on papers and tests. Those always seemed a little ambiguous. You must work hard in this class, but its worth it.

Wonderful woman and teacher. Had her for two semesters. Go to class and take good notes. Memorize things for the exam and it's cake. Other people who say her class was hard need to get real and understand college is not a cake walk. I totally recommend her

She is an amazing teacher.  She teaches so well and draws you in to the material.  Going to class is madatory and you have to take REALLY good notes.  I skimed most of the reading in the literature book but and did well, the big exepensive picture book is necessary.  Easy GE.  Loved this class!

I took this class with this professor because everyone said she was a great teacher and the class was easy. I hated this class. The tests are really hard. You have to go to all lectures and take good notes or else you'll have no chance at doing well. No clear expectations, especially for the papers. Busy work. Good luck if you decide to take it.

Hilarious and so knowledgeable!  Makes the class so fun.  This is my fav. class and I have learned so much.  There is a fair amount of work but I have never felt overwhelmed and I couldn't recommend a better teacher.

She is a great lady - super young and energetic. She knows the material well. Tip for tests: pay attention to the little details she says like about artists and musicians (like lifestyle, etc.).  Her tests are fairly easy if you go to class and read. So go to class and read and get at least an A-.

Best professor I have had in college!!!  For the most part class was interesting.  Her tests are easy as long as you go to class and study.  The assignments you have are mostly fun.  She is very helpful and will work with you if you have any problems.
Great teacher.

Fantastic teacher!! Never, ever boring. The passion she has for the subject is very apparent and inspiring. Very intelligent, honest, and helpful. She can be somewhat harsh on grading, but aside from that, I absolutely loved this class!!!
Classy, intelligent lady. Did justice to an interesting subject. Interested in what she taught. Interesting assignments. Highly recommend.
great teacher great class

Absolutely excellent.  Brought homemade cookies a couple of times.  Her class inspired me to go for a Humanities minor.  As I move toward graduation, I feel like after I forget all the bad stuff, her's will be the class I look back on and think "Wasn't college great?"
Everybody else has already said it: Great teacher who makes class fun and teaches you. Has fun and follows her rules. Defines criteria well and makes it a pleasure to go to class.

If you go to all the lectures the tests aer cake.  Only 2 papers and you get the criteria for them at the begining of the semester, and they are also easy if you follow the instructions.  She has a dry witty humor that is great, and I loved going to this class every day.
Great teacher, made i t fun in every way.  Cracks a lot of jokes that seem to blow past most of the class but if you listen she's really very funny
Very cool teacher, just show up to class and pay a little attention and you should do fine.  Just do the homework and you will get good grades.  Tests are cake as long as you listen.
the best and easiest class to fulfill history of civ GE credit.   very enthusiastic and fun teacher.  Tests were so very do-able. If you listen in class you will do well.
Only night class I ever had that I actually looked forward to attending.  Great teacher, very fair.  Knows her stuff and presents it in a way that makes you want to learn it.
Great teacher, humorous, really knows her stuff and makes class enjoyable. Very nice and flexible. If you go to class and pay attention you will do very well on the tests. Enjoyable class.

Kathryn is truly a gem! She is so energetic, kind, and caring. This is a capstone class. You co-teach a marriage preparation course for 6 weeks (you get trained to do this), then write a big paper about it with your co-teacher. There are a few other assignments throughout the semester and a reading quiz before most classes (super easy).

Kathryn is the best! This capstone was SO doable. Class time can appear long, but she gives a break and often lets you out early. Class time is some presentation and then lots of guest presenters to teach about family life education. I genuinely loved this class. Such a great option, especially if you like teaching! Please take this class!!

ACTUALLY FOR CLASS SFL 498 but didn't see that on the list. She is SO caring & understanding & nice & fun. She's hard not to love. Really wants to help you succeed in the class and in life. You and a partner will teach a 6 hour course to engaged couples. Time consuming but the hardest thing all semester. No final. Highly recommend.

Kathryn feels like my mom shes THAT caring. The tests arent that bad if you pay attention and study the slides. Ive heard this class is definitely easier than taking it in Provo. 3 tests, 2 papers, and no final. She does every thing she can to help everyone succeed. Would highly recommend.

For a subject that I was dreading, she made it awesome. I learned so much in her class, the papers were specific with expectations making them easy to follow the rubric and get full credit. She was awesome! Would definitely take again!

Best decision I ever made was taking Kathryn for American heritage. I was FEARING this course but she made it enjoyable and fairly easy. She wants what is best for her students. Unfortunately, she isn't teaching AMHG anymore, but she is the BEST! Minimal homework, fair tests, and 2 essays. SO GOOD!

Kathryn was absolutely phenomenal. She made every lecture very engaging with different activities and video clips to apply the things we were learning. She sincerely cares about all her students and wants to help us succeed. I would recommend her to anyone taking American Heritage--definitely one of my favorite professors I've ever had!

Kathryn is the BEST. So real and really knows her stuff. Willing to sacrifice a lot for her students. The type of person you would want to hang out with just because she's so cool! P.S. She loves black licorice!

Sister Sargent is great. I heard crazy things about American Heritage at BYU, but this class has been relatively easy. If you have the option to drive/ride up to SLC once a week, it will be worth it! Everything on her tests are on the powerpoint slides, so really the only reason to go to class is to take the mandatory quizzes which are easy.

Katheryn is da bomb! I struggle with government, history, economics, etc, but Katheryn made it interesting and was helpful. Read and do current events (super easy) and you'll be golden. Study for the tests but don't stress yourself out. I didn't love going up to SLC from Provo, but it was better than AHTG classes I've heard of in Provo for sure.

Kathryn is no doubt my favorite professor at BYU. Her lectures are hilarious and you can tell she puts in the extra effort for her students. Her class is awesome because she puts a lot of cool video clips in her presentations, gives you a 10 minute break, and lets you eat food! She knows her stuff. 10/10 would take again.

Don't regret going up to SLC for this class one bit. She is easily one of my favorite professors ever. Lectures are so interesting and relevant and she prepares you 100% for the tests. Very do-able assignments and quizzes in class. 10/10 would recommend this to anyone who doesn't want to suffer through the normal Provo class.

Professor Sargent was amazing! She is like your mother, except she's teaching you American History. She is so caring, and never makes you feel stupid when you answer a question in lecture. I would major in history if she taught every history class at BYU.

If the reading is done before class each week, than it's easy to pass the class. There's in-class quizzes and a project in the middle of the semester (5min. presentation) and tests are fairly easy. Fun class.

Kathryn is the BEST! I heard so many horror stories about American Heritage, but this was by far my favorite class of the semester. The tests are difficult, but really just pay attention and participate in class and you will have a great experience. I do not regret making the trek up to Salt Lake every week one bit! Take American Heritage from her!

I was dreading taking AHTG100 for years. Finally did from one of the best professors I've had.  Crystal clear requirements, great lectures, not overwhelming learning assignments.  I had to really study for the tests, but I learned a great deal.  This class was a pleasure to come to every week.  Passionate about her subject and excellent teacher.

Quizes every class period, 5 questions easy, gives an extra credit question.  Slides are super straight forward.  Study slides and you will be set for the exams.  3 exams and final. Not to bad. I definitely recommend Sister Sargent.

Overall, Professor Sargent teaches a great American Heritage class. Her lectures are very clear on the criteria that will be on the tests, but then I thought there were some test questions that were tricky. The weekly readings and quizzes are important to keep up on but they aren't too difficult and the big assignments are not very hard.

This was a great class.  I enjoyed American Heritage with Sis. Sargent.  Reading is necessary - every class there is a quiz on the reading.  There were 3 tests total with some very minor other projects/papers.  Sis. Sargent is very clear, class is interesting, the class was easy and entertaining.  Best American Heritage class out there!!

I was dreading taking this class, but Kathryn Sargent made AHTG 100 fun and interesting. Getting an A in this class is very easy. Do not buy the book! Just carefully read the lecture slides that are on the class website and you will easily pass all the quizzes and all the exams. There were only two written assignments. Attend class and you pass.

Sister Sargent is an awesome teacher. Her class is not easy and she will make you work for it, but she in not unreasonable in her grading and her expectations. Do the assigned reading before class and review the slides she provides from the lectures and you'll do just fine. Overall I really enjoyed taking this class.

Sister Sargent is a great teacher! I kept hearing about how hard American Heritage was but I passed with a n A-. She posts her slides online and those are excellent for study resources, they contain basically all the information you need for the class. She makes an effort to help you get a good grade and makes the class really interesting!

Easy class. No curve, point-based, so you get what you earn. There really is no reason to go to class other than the annoying mandatory, in-class quizzes, which are super easy. Her tests are easy if you just follow her slides. As far as reading goes, just skim everything and read the bold definitions. There was one short paper, that's it.

SUCH A GOOD TEACHER- Mabe the best I've had at BYU yet! You have to come to class to understand everything. She is extremely helpful if you go and talk to her. As for the readings, just read the side comments on the textbook and you will be fine for quizzes! Not very hard at all, and you learn a LOT! LOVED THIS CLASS!
AWESOME! taking it during spring from sis. sargent is definitely worth it. She makes it fun and interesting. tests are straightforward and she tells you what to study. has been my favorite class

Probably the best AHTG teacher you will have. Although best, this class is pretty difficult. There were only 2-3 students in our class who got A's. Those students already had tons of knowledge on history and American Founding. My advice would be to def. take it from Sargent and study hard. Her intelligence and style of appearance makes her hot!

Class is always something to look forward to, because you know you're actually going to learn something! It's interesting and not hard to sit through. She throws in a lot of cool facts and relevant information, too. Awesome teacher!!

Kathryn is a really good professor. Really likes what she is talking about. Incorporates facts which I really like. Tells you exactly what facts you should know for the test. Go to class otherwise miss out on class discussion that is sometimes on the test and have a quiz over reading (easy). Test are often short sentence.

Kathryn Sargent is the greatest teacher in the world! Her lectures are fascinating, very worth going to. She prepares you well for the tests. She really cares about the students. ANY sacrifice is worth making to have her as a teacher! :)
She is my goat

This class is very accessible and a great option for first-time family historians. Professor Behling was so kind and clearly cares about each and every student. Any assignment can be resubmitted for a better grade, and there are no exams, making this a very low-stakes class. I definitely recommend!

She made this class so much more than indexing and looking at census records. To do well and enjoy the class you should take the time to do the research and participate every day. She walks you through how to do everything. She is so positive and loves her students so much. The readings feel tedious at first but add so much value to the class.

Professor Behling is good and very passionate about family history. The assignments are so good. And no exams :)))) I learned so much about family history, and I really loved the readings and homework!

She's simply the Sweetest, nicest Professor I've ever met.. she cares about fam history and she's passionate, her lectures are entertaining and the assignments are easy! She wants you to love family history more than make you work

Professor Irion is one of my favorite teachers. She gave detailed feedback that helped me improve my writing. She genuinely cares about her students and creates a supportive environment. She expects effort on revisions, but it helps you grow. I would take her again.

Professor Irion is hands down the best professor I have ever had. Everyone needs to take a class from her! She cares so deeply, she will make you laugh and then cry (in a good way), and I learned so much from her. I truly enjoyed coming to class and doing her assignments. Homework was manageable and truthfully enjoyable. She is perfect!

I really love Professor Irion. She's an amazing, inspirational, caring person, and a very open and understanding professor. The class involves a LOT of reading (27 books in one semester), but she doesn't have a minimum page count so I was able to count novellas. I loved this class and highly recommend her as a professor.

I can't say enough good things about Professor Irion! She is my favorite professor at BYU and ENGL 420 was my favorite class I've taken. Professor Irion is the kindest Professor I've had, her class was FASCINATING with such fun class lectures, and I learned so much! This class felt very low pressure but there is a lot of reading! Highly recommend!

Professor Irion is such an amazing professor! She cares so much about her students, and makes class such a joy to attend. This class is very reading heavy, but the class discussions make it so worth it! This was one of my favorite classes in the whole major! Would recommend, would take again!

Dr. Irion is a wonderful teacher and person. This class is designed to have insane amounts of reading, but she really tries to make it manageable. The assignments could be a little confusing at times, and her feedback can be harsh, but she really cares about her students and their success. Some of my best experiences with a professor were with her.

Super caring professor, she would do anything for her students. Tons of reading, and the course is super back heavy, so pretty much all the assignments are due last day of class. Lots of discussion; class is more like a book club. Sometimes assignments and group work felt high school level, but overall a good class. Prepare to read though!!

I adored this professor as every lesson of hers was inventive and interesting. The one thing I would say about this class is there is TONS of homework. LOTS of reading, LOTS of assignments, prepare to work hard. The professor only wants to see you grow - so some of her feedback can seem harsh, but it is coming from the kindest place.
Professor Irion is amazing. She is so kind and considerate to each of her students. She makes sure to make her classroom a welcoming environment. She is very helpful with assignments.

Katie was such an AMAZING professor. She cares about her students and is so well rounded you want to be like her. She inspires her students to get out there and learn as much as they can to be good people. Lectures were amazing, books were amazing! If I could take her class again I would in a heartbeat. Take her class if you have the opportunity!!

Katie was fantastic. She really engaged you with the texts, and gave a really reasonable workload because the course was so reading heavy. Lectures never felt like lectures, although I learned a lot, it felt more like a book club. I was never bored in this class! Absolutely would recommend her.

This is the most unnecessarily hard class I have ever taken. It is ridiculous how much reading you have to do for a 200 level class I have taken almost every chemistry imaginable and have never had to put in so many hours outside of class as I have with this class. This is completely unnecessary, especially for a 200 level class that's a elective.

Professor Stirling is great! She's passionate about what she's teaching which makes it a little more interesting. She tests on application and doesn't have memorization on exams. The exams are pretty easy. It may have been worse since it was spring term but there was a lot of reading and a lot of projects, assignments. Pretty easy to get an A tho

Prof. Stirling was awesome! Take this class if you are looking for an easier A, and applicable humanities. Exam reviews were extremely helpful, she tests on application not on memorization. Attend lectures and review pre class readings and the class is an easy A with up to 15% extra credit throughout the Semester. Lectures were awesome!

I took this class during spring term (lots of work). Pro. Isaak is very kind and passionate. I loved how she encouraged participation and sharing of different opinions and interpretations of art. This class is very lecture heavy. Prepare to spend hours out of class on assignments. There are many extra credit opportunities which I appreciated.

Prof Stirling is a GEM! She is so cool and cares a lot about her students. Her lectures are engaging and while there is a lot of pre-class work, the content was cool to learn. We learned that knowledge is power and knowing all of these pop culture moments from different time periods makes references to them today more understandable and funny!

SHE IS THE BEST! I loved taking this class. It was just for a general but she made it so enjoyable. Her lectures are amazing and I did not feel like the class was that hard. Just read, submit assignments on time and study for the test. What I liked the most is how passionate she is about what she teaches and how caring she was for us.
Super difficult class
Dr. Carbine is the best! This was a difficult class for me but she made it so much better. She is very kind and funny and one of the professors you can tell genuinely cares about your success.
Great professor! If you took AP Stats in high school, this class is a breeze. Don't do JASP assignments the night before.

Dr. Carbine is great! She breaks up 2hr class with a 10 min break and funny stories. Homework is optional but HIGHLY recommend doing the practice problems. The 3 JASP assignments are confusing at first but fine. There is extra credit and test corrections offered. She goes through her lectures at a slower pace which is great for those new to stats.

Dr. Carbine is a great professor, she makes the lectures super entertaining and goes at a good pace so everyone can understand the content. I struggle with math, but I was able to do really well in this class. She's really funny, tells great stories, and gives us a break in the middle of class! I highly recommend taking a class from her.

Dr. Carbine is a phenomenal teacher. This class could have been worse from any other professor. She is funny and gives us breaks. The material is hard, but she makes it so much easier to understand. She makes sure to answer every single question you may have in class. There are textbook readings, but I did not do a single one of them and did well.

Professor Carbine's lectures often ramble, making otherwise manageable material unnecessarily confusing. Explanations lack clarity, and grading is extremely strict, with points lost easily. Test corrections are offered, allowing students to earn back half credit, whcih helps--but the course remains more frustrating than difficult.

Dr. Carbine was a great teacher! This is a HARD class but she makes the most of it and helps students every step of the way. She offers generous option to get extra credit and the workload outside of class is very mild. The only thing I didn't like was the JASP software assignments. They confused me and didn't feel helpful to learning the material

Dr. Carbine knows her stuff! Statistics is tough, but she makes it real world and approachable. You do have to work and pay attention, but I liked the JASP application and think I am more prepared for grad school because of this class. Would definitely recommend!

This was my first statistics class ever, and it honestly made me question my major. I found the lectures and the textbook to be very confusing. I had friends in that class who had taken a general statistics course before, and they said that they were confused as well. The JASP assignments were very confusing, and I was very lost during this class.

She was so good at teaching what is notoriously one of the hardest classes an undergrad can take! She gives a chapter to read before each/every other class, which is optional, but when she teaches it, hearing it for a second time is really what makes it stick. She gives formula sheets on exams. She's a grad student, and really understands students.

Overall a pretty good teacher but the tests were difficult and I had to work hard for a good grade (practice problems after every lecture, spending hours getting ready for each exam). She was willing to help me outside of class, would've given her a better rating if the tests weren't so crazy. Homework isn't required, but gives you good practice.

Dr Carbine's lectures have hands-down been my FAVORITE! She is hilarious! I took a 2.5 hour long class once a week, which is normally painful, but with her it felt like 1 hour. She is hilarious and makes lectures so engaging! There is however a lot of reading, but if you are interested in any aspect of psychology its not too bad!

I took a stats class in high school and felt like this class was all review. She took a lot of time on each concept to make sure everyone understood, so it was honeslty a bit slow paced for me, but others struggled with it. There are a lot of resources to help those who are struggling with it. She is very caring and funny.

She was an effective lecturer, and she was understanding of individual circumstances. Her tests were difficult, and her grading criteria of the group paper was unclear. The final paper was never turned in as a whole. We were only graded (and docked points) on the incremental sections, not the final product, so there was no redemption.

Dr. Reesor is very knowledgeable but sometimes he just lectures at students and it can get a little dull. There's weekly quizzes, but they prepare you exactly for the midterms/final and they aren't super hard if you do the readings. There's several big projects at the end of the semester that were fun, but personally difficult (composition). Eh
Not a difficult class, and probably could be worse for a GE. That being said, potentially the most boring class I have ever taken and I learned next to nothing.
skdhgeiughew

I took Music 101 from him and struggled a little bit at the beginning. I was never a huge music person, and so it was a little challenging at first. Sometimes his lectures were sometimes a little boring due to so many definitions. But overall, this class is easy; if you show up and put in a little effort, this should be a super easy GE class.

Professor Reesor is an amazing guy. You can tell that he really loves what he teaches. He is super willing to help anyone who reaches out. I thought that he was a pretty good grader seeing how almost everyone got an A in the class. I'd totally recommend him for the arts GE!!

Dr. Reesor is highly knowledgeable, engaging, and fair. His classes are enjoyable, and he makes sure every student has the resources to succeed. He's always more than willing to meet personally and goes above and beyond to help you excel. Absolutely recommend!
Hard to get good grades on presentations but easy for tests. Willing to work with students to help them out. Very fun and interesting class.

bro is doing too much. You can tell that he is very interested in what he is teaching, but he explains very simple terms in the most complex way possible. I have informally studied music for about 10 years of my life including the piano, guitar, and choir. I am still lost in this class. good luck solider

I took from Professor Reesor his first semester at BYU so he may have changed his policies now, but I really enjoyed his class. Assignments were easy but a lot of group projects. Really clear grading policy and deadlines. Quizzes before every class but they're open note. When I missed a large assignment deadline he totally worked with me--great guy

Professor Reesor is passionate, professional, and enthusiastic about music and it shows in his lectures. I learned so much by taking his introductory class and was left ready for more. Professor Reesor makes it easy to reach him and clearly cares about his student's success. The organization can sometimes falter, but he is an excellent teacher.
Such a cute and fun class! Would definitely take again. Sister Allen is the best!
LOVE LOVE LOVE HER! She is the best! Take this class it was so enriching.
Professor Allen will help you succeed and is super kind. Take her class!

Professor Allen is amazing! This is one of the best religion classes I've taken here and the course work is very engaging. Prof. Allen is super understanding and always willing to help with questions or issues.
Professor Allen is a wonderful and personable professor. Her class is quite easy and she will make accomodations for you as needed!

One of the best professors at BYU! Professor Allen is kind, in tune with the Spirit, and truly cares about her students. I came in nervous with little family history knowledge, but now I feel confident and excited about it. Get started on the final project and take the research log seriously and you won't have any problems. Highly recommend!

ABSOLUTELY LOVE HER! I wish she taught other classes at BYU. She is very peppy and passionate about Family History, which is refreshing, and so understanding with extensions and emergencies. There was a pretty consistent, relatively light workload, as long as you didn't procrastinate on the final project. I loved this class so much :)
Easy class, and super fun.

Honestly this was one of the easier religion classes. Prof. Allen is super nice and a great professor. However, I am not super interested in Family History and I will admit, it was so hard to get motivation to do the assignments. Great teacher, just not the most interesting content.

Professor Allen is the best! She explains everything really well and helps students to learn, not just check off boxes. She allows for redo's on assignments and doesn't have a formal final exam. Make sure to put in effort in this class and you will get something out of it!

If I could take every class from her I would!! She is the most caring and loving teacher I have ever had. I look forward to her lectures because I know I can learn and feel the spirit. She is very understanding if you have questions and is eager to help. If you show up to class you will be fine. Take this class!!

Amazing prof and class! Kelli is so kind and understanding. Attendance is graded and you learn more if you're in class. Prof Allen is super understanding/ willing to work with you. There are quite a few assignments but nothing too intense. Basically if you go to class and do the assignments you'll be totally fine. I learned so much! She's awesome!
He is really funny, but lectures tend to go off track. He tells a lot of random stories that he goes off on and so it's easy to lose focus. When he does lock in and teach, he shares great insights.

Have to go into the Humanities Testing Center and exams are all short answer and fill in the blank, no multiple choice. Tough grader on exams and essays, so expect disappointment on not getting an easy A. Lectures didn't add much to the class, posts the slides online, has an exam study guide which I highly recommend using.

I loved Prof. Smith! She was so kind and helpful in trying to read Shakespeare. There is not an overwhelming amount of work, only 1 group project, and 4 papers for the big assignments. As long as you stay on top of your reading and ask questions, you will be just fine!

Prof. Smith was so kind and intelligent. She made class fun and as stress-free as possible. She cares about student feedback and implements it to improve her class. The reading was heavy (1 play a week), but I did take it during summer term. The discussions and lectures are engaging, and she picks great plays. Prof. Smith made me love Shakespeare.

Taking Shakespeare from Professor Smith was an illuminating and enjoyable experience. I loved the class discussions more than any I have ever had before. She is an expert in asking thought-provoking questions and expounding on class comments. I took this class in summer so it was 3 hours twice a week, but I loved every part.

Kelsey's Shakespeare class is amazing! I took it for a GE Letters credit and it did not disappoint. Expect to read 6 plays and write 4 papers (you can choose which plays you want to write on). The reading quizzes are easy if you just do the reading and other than that, expect a midterm and final! 

10/10 class, very organized and I learned a lot!

I loved Kelsey! I took 312-- Persuasive writing, and ended the class with a very high A. I thought the workload was completely manageable for an upper level writing class. Only 3 big writing assignments--one being 10 pages, but you have more than enough time to turn stuff in. Kelsey is great to work with, always responding to emails and questions!

Took this class summer term, but it was very doable. She made a 3 hour class feel much shorter. Lots of in class discussions, which I enjoyed. Tests were pretty easy if you can remember the plays well. I really enjoyed the essays she had us write, even though there was one a week. Absolutely loved this class and I wish I could take it again!!

Get ready for a culture shock if you're not a theater kid lol. Still, I'm so glad I took this course! Kelsey's powerpoints are super interesting and related to today. There are lots of options for response papers, they are fairly graded, and none of the quizzes are super demanding. Do the readings and use your brain and an A is super achievable.
I could not recommend this class more!  The work load was reasonable, class discussions were fascinating, and the exams were approachable with appropriate studying.

I was in Kelsey's class over the summer for Shakespeare. It was a small class and the lectures were so fun! We read six plays and there was a paper for each of them, but she gave a long list of options for prompts of each. She gave a lot of extra credit for attending a Shakespeare play. The exams were easy if you did the study guide.

Kelsey is an amazing professor! Like many freshman, I started the semester with a lack of confidence in my writing abilities. Kelsey gives great feedback, she teaches the curriculum with clarity, and the class syllabus is very straight forward. Moving forward, I feel more confident as a writer and have the essential writing tools for the future.

It was a fun class. Very regular schedule I could get used to. Took Shakespeare from her, we read plays quickly, but to be fair I took it in the summer. One paper (with different options) for each play.

She's great professor and very helpful, but don't take this class for a GE or if expecting an easy A. There are three main assignments but lots of other work and smaller papers involved. It's time consuming, and there aren't many breaks.

Kelsey is a great teacher/professor! Her lectures are instructive and interesting. We had big assignments which is I guess expected in a class like ENG 311 but I was taking it for a general so I did find it very heavy and time consuming. She gives great feedback. Expect back to back due dates for big assignments and quite a bit of reading.

This class had 3 main papers (a short one, 4-5 page one, and a 10-page paper), and on every single one Kelsey was very approachable for help and gave such good feedback. She is also a pretty lenient grader, and I easily got an A in this class even though writing is not my strong suit. Good choice for a prof!
Kelsey was a fantastic teacher and gave great feedback

I love Kelsey because she is so willing to explain things and help you whenever you need it. She gives lots of opportunities to meet with her if you want to. Her lectures are awesome - she even uses  funny YouTube videos to illustrate her points. There are lots of papers but she spaces them out well so it's doable. Also great class discussions!

Great teacher, he was super accommodating when I needed to transfer to the class when my schedule was too crazy but I needed enough credits to keep my scholarship. The class is actually super useful. TAKE IT EARLY in your college career to help you make it through reading easier. Great strategies I'll use to review and study and get the gist quickly

This class was very helpful. Professor Plummer really cares and wants you to succeed. The awesome thing about this class is that it doesn't add anymore homework to your work load, instead you use your homework from other classes to learn. It's very easy to get an A if you just do the assignments and put forth a little effort.

I loved the class. But it is true that if you don't show up, you wont pass - but come on, we are in COLLEGE - we should be expected to got to class. Professor Plummer is VERY helpful and caring and he wants you to pass. The work is easy - you fill out worksheets and then his homework is actually you doing your homework for your OTHER classes! Cool.

Prof. Plummer is great and really cares about helping his students really understand the material. You also learn a lot of great strategies in this course that are helpful for any college student who needs to do reading assignments. I sped up my reading a ton.
Awesome person and professor. I learned so much in his advanced reading strategies class. Super easy class. It's 100% your fault if you don't get an A.
This class was an easy way to gain valuable skills! All homework done can help you in all your other courses and class time is used to practice your skills.

Advanced Reading Strategies is one of the most useful classes you could possibly take if you plan on reading after your undergrad. Brother Plummer is excellent at what he does & is very caring. He knows students's names and gives one-on-one feedback during in-class practice. Arrive on time - tardies count for WAY too much of the attendance grade.
He's really willing to work with you, and the tests are super straightforward. I'm pretty sure all of us achieved our goals.

Dr. Plummer does a great job at making the class meaningful and interactive. He's a super humble professor and only wants the best for his students. I learned loads from his Advanced Reading Strategies class and the things I've learned have been super helpful in all my other classes.

Dr. Plummer tells great stories and does a marvelous job of using metaphors to make connections --this class is less about speed-reading and more about learning.  So, if you want to learn how to learn a little better, this is the class for you.

Dr. Plummer's advanced reading strategies class was easily one of my favorites. I really enjoyed how we pre-read the lectures before class and then did following homework in class. We used textbooks from other classes to complete the assignments. Super useful and applicable for learning how to better your reading in college. Take this class!

Professor Plummer is one of the most inspiring teachers I have ever met. This class is not difficult, you show up and do outside reading in class. You learn how to excel and be efficient in your other classes. He goes on little spiritual rants but if you listen, it will change your perspective. I rarely rate any professor but I think highly of him.

I took his Advanced Reading Strategies class and I think he's an awesome professor. The structure and content of the course itself could be refined, but Professor Plummer is brilliant and hilarious. He makes class fun and he cares about each one of his students.

I have no idea what that person below is talking about.  Maybe (s)he mixed up the professors.  Dr. Plummer is hilarious and this class is really useful. I would take any class taught by him. To be honest, Academic reading isn't my favorite subject, but it was nice that we basically just did our other homework in that class. His stories are so funny
Lectures are a complete waste of time. Marked me down for doing an assignment early. Do not take from him.
Bro. Plummer is awesome and very humble.  He makes the lessons very applicable and references the mission often.  His tests were pretty easy if you go to class and look at the study guide.

Brother Plummer is a great guy. He's very nice and honest. He'll listen to you. Make sure you go to class.. your whole grade depends on it. However if u do that much, you'll get a great grade. His class was an awesome experience.
I had his class early and his voice is extremely calming. Tests were exactly off of the study guides, not very difficult, just an average class.

Excellent teacher with a lot of emotion in what he is saying. I was not a fan of the tests, but we cant be pleased by all tests. He is very approachable and a great person all together. He is more willing to help you than any other teacher that ive had.

Good, easy class. You learn a lot, but you don't have to stress about the class. He gives study guides and curves the tests if people do bad. There is some busy work (post thoughts on blackboard each day) but what are you gonna do?

He's awesome, he gets to know his students personally and really cares about them. His class requires some reading, from the scriptures as well as a talk to go along with the reading for every class. His tests are cake so long as you do the study guide, which can be pretty lengthy, 8-13 pages. Overall his class is easy and he follows the spirit.

Bro. Plummer is a stud.  I didn't find his tests to be all that easy but I studied a ton and got an A.  Brother Plummer is really personable and willing to listen to ANY suggestions.  He even drops test questions if enough people miss it.  Hint: Take notes on the CLASS applications of scriptures.  Do a good job on the study guide.  A

Class felt like seminary, not as in depth as I wanted. He likes to tell stories and act out things. Little homework. Tests would be easy if I would study. On tests, when responding to verses, he is looking for the emphasis made in class, making it important to go as often as possible. His voice is rather soothing, so avoid early morning classes. B+

Great person, but teaching style is not what I would expect for an honors returned missionary section. The class is very easy, but does require a couple hours to read the assigned reading. I don't feel like we go very deep into the scriptures and that alot of the things taught are obvious. Great enthusiam, but not my style
Great guy.  Class is cake if you go over the study guide right before the test.  They're pretty much the same thing.

Class pretty easy. If you keep up on daily readings and postings you'll do fine. His tests are basically the entire study guide - just know that really well. He's a nice guy and has a spiritual class.

if you take the section for non-return missionaries, this class is WAY easy. The tests require a little studying, but everything is on the review sheet and if enough people get a question wrong, he throws it out. He is really sweet and brings the Spirit to every class.
Excellent Teacher. You read alot and have three paragraph responses every week. But the class overall is easy and he is really humble and caring.
Good teacher, caring, and sincere.

He's a really humble teacher who's dedicated to trying to teach the gospel well.  Expect the overall tone of the class to be dominated by the students because he pretty much goes wherever they take him.
Very good religion teacher.  Exams not too difficult.

This was his first semester teaching I think, so things were a bit rocky. Tests were impossibly difficult, but he threw out questions and rounded grades to keep us all from failing. Expect to write a ton of papers on what you read. Not an easy A.

Great teacher, he was super accommodating when I needed to transfer to the class when my schedule was too crazy but I needed enough credits to keep my scholarship. The class is actually super useful. TAKE IT EARLY in your college career to help you make it through reading easier. Great strategies I'll use to review and study and get the gist quickly

This class was very helpful. Professor Plummer really cares and wants you to succeed. The awesome thing about this class is that it doesn't add anymore homework to your work load, instead you use your homework from other classes to learn. It's very easy to get an A if you just do the assignments and put forth a little effort.

I loved the class. But it is true that if you don't show up, you wont pass - but come on, we are in COLLEGE - we should be expected to got to class. Professor Plummer is VERY helpful and caring and he wants you to pass. The work is easy - you fill out worksheets and then his homework is actually you doing your homework for your OTHER classes! Cool.

Prof. Plummer is great and really cares about helping his students really understand the material. You also learn a lot of great strategies in this course that are helpful for any college student who needs to do reading assignments. I sped up my reading a ton.
Awesome person and professor. I learned so much in his advanced reading strategies class. Super easy class. It's 100% your fault if you don't get an A.
This class was an easy way to gain valuable skills! All homework done can help you in all your other courses and class time is used to practice your skills.

Advanced Reading Strategies is one of the most useful classes you could possibly take if you plan on reading after your undergrad. Brother Plummer is excellent at what he does & is very caring. He knows students's names and gives one-on-one feedback during in-class practice. Arrive on time - tardies count for WAY too much of the attendance grade.
He's really willing to work with you, and the tests are super straightforward. I'm pretty sure all of us achieved our goals.

Dr. Plummer does a great job at making the class meaningful and interactive. He's a super humble professor and only wants the best for his students. I learned loads from his Advanced Reading Strategies class and the things I've learned have been super helpful in all my other classes.

Dr. Plummer tells great stories and does a marvelous job of using metaphors to make connections --this class is less about speed-reading and more about learning.  So, if you want to learn how to learn a little better, this is the class for you.

Dr. Plummer's advanced reading strategies class was easily one of my favorites. I really enjoyed how we pre-read the lectures before class and then did following homework in class. We used textbooks from other classes to complete the assignments. Super useful and applicable for learning how to better your reading in college. Take this class!

Professor Plummer is one of the most inspiring teachers I have ever met. This class is not difficult, you show up and do outside reading in class. You learn how to excel and be efficient in your other classes. He goes on little spiritual rants but if you listen, it will change your perspective. I rarely rate any professor but I think highly of him.

I took his Advanced Reading Strategies class and I think he's an awesome professor. The structure and content of the course itself could be refined, but Professor Plummer is brilliant and hilarious. He makes class fun and he cares about each one of his students.

I have no idea what that person below is talking about.  Maybe (s)he mixed up the professors.  Dr. Plummer is hilarious and this class is really useful. I would take any class taught by him. To be honest, Academic reading isn't my favorite subject, but it was nice that we basically just did our other homework in that class. His stories are so funny
Lectures are a complete waste of time. Marked me down for doing an assignment early. Do not take from him.
Bro. Plummer is awesome and very humble.  He makes the lessons very applicable and references the mission often.  His tests were pretty easy if you go to class and look at the study guide.

Brother Plummer is a great guy. He's very nice and honest. He'll listen to you. Make sure you go to class.. your whole grade depends on it. However if u do that much, you'll get a great grade. His class was an awesome experience.
I had his class early and his voice is extremely calming. Tests were exactly off of the study guides, not very difficult, just an average class.

Excellent teacher with a lot of emotion in what he is saying. I was not a fan of the tests, but we cant be pleased by all tests. He is very approachable and a great person all together. He is more willing to help you than any other teacher that ive had.

Good, easy class. You learn a lot, but you don't have to stress about the class. He gives study guides and curves the tests if people do bad. There is some busy work (post thoughts on blackboard each day) but what are you gonna do?
