Very good religion teacher.  Exams not too difficult.

This was his first semester teaching I think, so things were a bit rocky. Tests were impossibly difficult, but he threw out questions and rounded grades to keep us all from failing. Expect to write a ton of papers on what you read. Not an easy A.

I have no idea why his rating is so low! Dr. Plowman was amazing. He is kind and cares about his students. There may have been a textbook but I never needed it because he covers everything in class. He answers all questions, has extra credit, and allows students to finish almost every assignment in class. Genuinely one of the best/easiest classes.

I love Plowman! His lectures can get dull, but you can tell he loves comms. Most, if not all, of the class is spent working on an assignment due that week. The lecture may last around 20 minutes. Super easy to reach outside of class, and lets you resubmit an assignment after he gives critiques for a higher grade. Easy class and a sweet professor!!

He's a nice instructor, but the class was challenging to navigate. Grading and feedback felt inconsistent, and lectures could be more engaging. AI made some assignments very easy. If your goal is to really learn 320 material, another instructor might provide a better experience.

DO NOT take this class with Plowman. He is such a nice guy and really does care about his students. But this class did not help me at all. It strengthened my testimony in enduring to the end because I cannot wait for this class to be over forever. So much of this class is just using AI and I wish I learned how to do any of this on my own.

Super nice guy. His tactics are very outdated and so are his assignments. I used AI a lot in this class so it was easy. Majority of the assignments are non valuable assignments that I may never use again.

Plowman is a kind professor. He gave good feedback on assignments and let us redo them as much as needed. I like him. I felt that the class was maybe too easy and the addition of AI made it so the course didn't require anything of me. He tends to go on political tangents and at times I felt it was controversial and not at all related to class.

Dr Plowman is awesome!! His class is interesting & his assignments are very clear & organized. He is also very willing to provide individual feedback. He made time to meet with each student individually twice throughout the semester to go over projects & give guidance. Would recommend his class!!
Dr. Plowman is genuinely a great guy and gives amazing grandpa energy. As a teacher though he can go on tangets and seems checked out and uninvested in his students. Class was a grind.

He is really not a good professor. I did not learn a thing in his class. Expectations were not clear, he didn't actually even teach any material? Yet he would get mad if the assignment was done wrong (because he didn't even teach how it should be done). He rambled, he was disorganized and did not have a respectful classroom environment.

He is disorganized. He wants specific things on the assignments but then says, "it's up to you!" when asked directly how to interpret a question to provide the answer he's looking for. He doesn't give constructive feedback, it's all over the place. He makes the class uncomfortable. No one in class respects him. He is the worst professor.
How does this man have any 5 star reviews? He's the worst professor at BYU.

Continued: he wants specific answers on his busywork assignments but doesn't ask you about the specific answers he wants, he just expects you to read his mind. You have to go to every class because you're put in a team (for God knows why) and he has little regard for your time. Not to mention, he doesn't teach a thing. Did I say that already?

There's not enough time to write all of the bad things about this class and this professor. He began each class with a controversial topic debate and multiple students left the class because they were uncomfortable or offended. He taught nothing, and each class period was group work on his vague assignments. I'll write another review to continue...

The content could have been so interesting but the way it was presented was disorganized and all over the place. Few assignments and he is extremely nitpicky making it hard to get a good grade. Which is frustrating because based on the course work it should be an easy A. He walks you through most of the assignments but you still somehow get docked?

I don't understand the 5 star reviews. Plowman was unprofessional, disorganized, & ridiculously nitpicky about EVERYTHING. I learned more how to satisfy his requirements than how to improve my PR skills. Maybe he once a well-respected, encouraging prof, but now he doesn't even use his own material. We spent class like the math meme.

Dr. Plowman has an awesome dry sense of humor and is very likable. There's a good amount of papers and he can grade a bit harshly, but he lets you re-do them with his feedback. He's also very willing to look at your papers before you turn them in. Follow his feedback and you'll do amazing. There's 1 midterm but he prepared us well. Final is a paper

Dr. Plowman is the sweet Prince of PR. He is sincerely one of the best professors I have had at BYU. He is super accessible for asking questions, extremely communicative through email. He makes sure to walk through every assignment that he gives his students and gives you time to work on projects in class. He is an absolute gem, & I loved his class

Really unclear about expectations, didn't learn anything from lectures he just rambled on about random stuff. You can rewrite the papers multiple times so it's not too hard to get an a but he is nit-picky with grading and cares more about grammar than content. Didn't feel like I learned anything from the class.

Professor Plowman has revamped Comms 336. There are plenty of bad reviews but let me tell you he has changed. I took his class in Spring 2019. He now will let you redo papers until you are pleased with his grade. You can meet with him prior to papers being due. He basically gives you all the answers for the Matrix test. No final!

He changed up his grading process this spring term. Basically, students may submit papers as many times as needed. He was very patient and willing to work with me until I received the grade I wanted. He is personable and pleasant. I loved this class.

He truly wants to help his students succeed. Get to know him because he is extremely helpful with internships and accomplishing career goals. Find a good group for projects and turn work in early for him to review! People complain that he is a tough grader, but really they don't listen to him in class and don't follow the rubric.

For the first half of the semester, it felt like we had to guess what was in his head to get a good grade on any project. He was unclear and vague, but then grades tough. However, he's a good guy, and gives lots of extra credit. Take specific notes about what he wants for each assignment, which is more specific than the rubric he gives you.

Professor Plowman is one of my favorites in the program. Instructions are sometimes unclear, but just ask for clarification! He genuinely cares for his students - more than some other professors I've had. He's willing to respond to emails or chat with you in his office. He values student feedback and has some really great insights.

Prof. Plowman is easy going. Attending class seems pointless. I would probably take this class again from him because it was so easy going, but Prof. Plowman is so vague and scatterbrained. Ask a lot of questions! Meet with him beforehand to review your papers! Get a good group at the very beginning for group projects.

Plowman is a very experienced PR specialist; he has done PR work in government, military, and business. He gives students useful and brilliant suggestions in working in the real world, but his lectures are boring (his tone of voice?) His class is all about team work, and cases. I don't think the class is too hard, but instructions are vague.

Great class, but don't take it from Plowman. He belittles his students in class, is very scattered, and grades harshly when he's only communicated very vague instructions. If you want to get a good grade, study hard for the Matrix test and send your papers into him early. Going back, I definitely would have taken this class from someone else.

Professor Plowman is AWESOME if you know a few things: 1. READ EVERY RUBRIC TO A "T".  2. Take advantage of him being willing to read your drafts before you turn in any assignment-- He gives AMAZING feedback and it's so helpful (+ extra points). 3. Study for the Matrix test!!!!!!!!! Also know that the group projects are a big deal.

His class and expectations are vague at best. He's relatively easy-going and is willing to answer questions but his responses are also confusing and unclear. Pretty much you just go into assignments hoping you can read his mind as to what he wants. Pretty easy but lectures teach you little to nothing.

Professor Plowman is an incredible teacher. Sometimes he is not as clear as he should be about grading expectations, but he is quite brilliant and willing to offer help if students ask. He has been an incredibly valuable resource to me. This isn't the easiest course but it is manageable and will benefit you in the long run.

Plowman is sweet. Take a class from him. He knows what he wants with his presentations and papers tho, so stick to what he asks and you will pass w/ flying colors. He'll meet or email you if needs be. He gives several extra credit assignments to really boost your grade too. I would definitely take this class or any other class from Plowman again.

Vague, ultra subjective, and not above name-calling of students and busywork. Any learning that occurred came from reading on our own, students teaching each other the material, and working with each other to figure it out. If you find yourself in his class, bond with the other students--they will be your saving grace and preservers of your sanity.
Some people say his instructions are vague, but you can go and ask him about it. He won't get mad. He is very helpful, very casual and laid back. Take it from him.
He is a good professor. I understood everything he said, even though i am an international student, and got an A-. I would take him again!

Dr. Plowman is a terrible professor and I don't know why BYU keeps him. He decides what grade you're getting before you turn in your first assignment. He is boring, ambiguous, and vague. His one redeeming characteristic as a professor is his willingness to talk with you about your concerns -- but that doesn't mean he will do anything about them.

If there's a class for every skill in the real PR world, this one is the one that teaches you how to fly by the seat of your pants! The syllabus is unclear and Dr. Plowman didn't even really know what was going on or what was due half the time. If you just go with it, he's good, but he's definitely vague
I didn't really enjoy his class.  Great guy who really wants to help his students, but class was boring and lacked direction.  Not too hard of a class though.

At first I was unsure about his class but once you get to know him he is great. Very knowledgeable, helpful, and very funny. He is sometimes vague but if you ask him in class to clarify what he wants he will. He is also always willing to help and go over assignments. I will take classes from him again!

Plowman was awesome. He has a dry sense of humor but is a happy guy who really wants to help. Sometimes directions are a little vague but if you bring any work to him before it's due he'll tell you EXACTLY what needs to be fixed so you can get the grade you want. I'd totally take him again.

Second time I took his class, and it was even worse the second time around. It's hard to understand what he wants in an assignment because he doesn't know. He doesn't clearly understand the material either. Everything taught in the class was from other students, and whatever he attempted to teach was just reading slides that weren't even his.

I love his class. He doesn't teach like a teacher, though. He teaches more like a boss. Grade was based on presentations and our critiques of classmate presentations and some group work. Excellent class, extremely friendly, great experience.

I had a very hard time taking this "Professor" seriously.  His job seemed pretty easy inasmuch as he delegated all learning to groups and group assignments.  Instructions unclear.  He really ought to find another line of work.

He's a nice guy, but very monitone.  He doesn't clarify exactly what he wants.  Make sure you have a friend in the class to catch anything you miss, because it is full of misunderstandings.  Not exceedingly hard, just make sure you clarify everything that he wants.
Plowman is the most boring person I've ever met. All directions are unclear and the class is void of any meaningful content.

I actually liked this class, but I agree he's not the best teacher. But he's not too hard, no tests, just papers, two quizzes, and two presentations.  Everything in this class is group work, so pick a good group at the beginning. If you don't understand something, ask.  He's not usually very clear with directions.
He is simply ridiculous. He is unprofessional and has a complete lack of regard for student's and their point of view. I didn't learn one thing from him in this class.

Ignore anything good you may have heard about this class b/c they are wrong! Worst class ever, comparable only to BIO 100 in awfulness. There are no directions. If he does say what he wants, he'll say on the day it is due. Everything you learn is from group work, never from him. Basically, this class made me change my major.

He is one of the worst teachers I've ever had. He is vague in instructions but expects you to know every thing he wants. He is not personable at all, and he is not good a facilitating classroom discussion. Not having tests was the only good part of this class.

if you like group work then this is the class for you. he doesn't believe in tests which i thought was great, but he can sometimes grade harder then you expect on the papers you turn in. if you follow his instructions to a T then you'll do well

Professor Stiles spends more time telling weird stories, puns, and complaining about his back pain then he does actually lecturing on international law. The class is easy if you show up, but it felt like a waste of time. He also gives barely any directions for the final paper but then grades harshly when you don't do precisely what he wants.

Drones on in class to literally teach nothing. Has one big paper at the end of the semester and he grades so harshly but gives three sentences for rubric. The TAs were completely unhelpful, don't waste your time taking this class.

Professor Stiles is easily the funniest guy and someone who cares about what he teaches. All assignments are done in class. Make sure to do the readings, and you will be fine. There are 7 small papers,1 research paper, and a final exam containing the exact questions from the weekly quizzes. Attend class and you will succeed. Take this class!

If you go in with a decent attitude you'll have fun in these classes, he is a tough grader and only has a few grades in for the whole semester, learn how the system works early and ask him directly for help.

Professor Stiles is great! Very interesting class and all the assignments are done in class. Weekly quizzes, in class essays every other week, not too bad if you do the reading. The exam is easy as it focuses on the exact quiz questions and essay questions. He makes class entertaining and loves his students. Take this class!

Maybe this isn't the way I learn but this class was really hard to follow. The homework is really long textbook readings and then very specific pop quizzes. The essays are in class and you don't know the prompt or rubric beforehand and it's graded really harshly. The class was not engaging and it was personally the worst class I've taken.

Professor Stiles is a great guy but not the best teacher. I took an intro class from him and he expects you to already have a lot of background knowledge on the subjects. He's not clear about rubrics because in reality, all he wants to hear from you is his own opinion told to him exactly we way he told you.

(I wanted to keep writing) That being said, I fought to stay awake in that class. Once, I went out to take a nap outside of the JSB because I couldn't stay awake anymore and I played it off as using the bathroom for 8 minutes. Expect to participate or you will get worse grades.

The course itself wasn't really what I was expected, so I was definitely less engaged, but Stiles is a good dude. He grades super quickly and is always available outside of class. He cracks dad jokes in class and really loves it if you laugh and even joke back with him. Not a bad class to take for your major.
Professor Stiles makes sure you will be accountable for the material taught in class. He is a tough grader and the rubric for the assignments usually is not that clear.

He is a genuine professor who really wants the students to engage with the material. You come to class and he asks for your thoughts on different concepts and writes those into the notes. He then posts the notes to LS for you to access. Provides study guides for exams and essay assignments are straightforward. He also has a nice sense of humor.

Its hard to rate Professor Stiles so low because hes a good person at heart, but he is a terrible teacher. The class runs as follows: read the textbook at home, go to class, regurgitate material you read. Professor Stiles doesnt actually teach anything and tells many long and pointless stories. Grading is harsh with no make ups. Better to avoid.

I really got a lot out of Professor Stiles class. He is definitely one of the most caring professors I've ever had. His lectures are fairly straight forward, and so is his grading. There is a fair amount of reading each day, so be prepared for that. Other than that, it was a great class, and I thoroughly enjoyed it.

A lot of reading, but he's a very enjoyable professor. He goes on tangents answering students' questions sometimes, which is good if you really want to learn about international politics. There aren't many grades, but participation is one of them. Stiles loves what he teaches and especially loves his students.

This class heavily focuses on his opinion and interpretation of political ideology. It was disappointing that the class wasn't deeply exploring and analyzing the readings assigned. We discussed the major ideas, but it was constructed around his own application of political ideology. This truly was politics and morality according to the professor.

Probably the worst professor I've had at BYU. He grades very subjectively so it's tough to know what grade you're going to get, regardless of the work you put into it. He tries to make jokes during the class that are oftentimes insensitive and ends up being the only one laughing at them. Haughty and patronizing, it's his way or no way.

I don't agree with most of the reviews on here. Just finished his 374 Ethics and Affairs class, seriously all you need to do is: read for the reading quizzes every class, two papers (one 4-6PG, the other 8-10PG), and two tests (study guide, duh, study). Probably the lowest maintenance 300 Poli Sci professor, which is what you want when taking 300s.
Professor Stiles is a great guy and a great lecturer. The tests and writing assignments can be difficult, but as long as you take good notes from lectures and readings you should be good.

If you want an easy A then this class isn't for you. His tests are pretty rough. He doesn't give you a study guide or any key topics to study, you just have to know all the info and hope for the best. He is an amazing lecturer though and you can tell he loves what he does. Make sure you read the textbook because there's pop quizzes.

This class is TOUGH! The research papers are intense and Dr. Stiles is a fair but tough grader. I was considering dropping this class at first but I promise it gets better. If you stick it out, you will learn a lot about international relations and you won't believe how much your writing will improve! Great preparation for higher level courses!

Honestly one of the best professors at BYU, if you utilize his office hours and connect with him, your class should be a breeze. Chances are if you take him you're a PoliSci major, which means you read a ton and lectures arent the most exciting. One of the nicest guys, and you should attend class but if not let him know and he can help you make up
He's very liberal and lectures aren't great, but the course is organized and simple. Tests aren't that hard and if you have him look over your paper beforehand you'll get a good grade.

I had the misfortune of taking Prof. Stiles International Relations class the semester after Donald Trump's election. Lectures involved nothing more than really bad jokes and even worse personal advice. Tests had little to nothing to do with lectures and were taken very specifically from textbook.

I've never met someone who is able to go off topic like he can. I've also never met someone who gave harsher critiques on papers. He basically said he couldn't see how I thought a topic for a paper was a good idea at all. You will NOT pass if you don't read the ENTIRE textbook. We proved to him that at least 4 of his test Q's were wrong. Be warned.

NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS. Stiles does not teach, he just rambles about his own personal opinions and gets angry when the class doesn't learn. Worst class I have taken here at BYU. If I could do it over again, I would NEVER sign up for his class. My advice? Find someone else that teaches the class you are looking for.

I personally loved Stiles, took 2 classes from him, but he's not for everyone. His tests are difficult; you have to really understand the material and be able to apply it. He's also definitely liberal so if that's going to upset you... you've been warned. But he's hilarious and if you're taking a boring class he'll make it way more interesting.

I have never written a review on Rate My Professors before, but I had to on this class. Avoid at all costs. He is very biased and condescending when you want to make a comment about class or IR. You are graded on very few things and the tests are obscenely difficult. Our TA's didn't even know the answers to the questions on the test.

I've never had problems with school or with my professors. Dr. Stiles doesn't teach, he just talks. He has very little class interaction, zero homework or activities to help you understand the material, and he just expects you to pick up on things. Not even his TA's knew many of the answers on his tests. He's very subjective.

I usually try to be open minded about professors, but this one was too much for me to handle. He is rude, condescending, and can't stay focused for more than 5 minutes in class. Besides not being a good professor, he is disrespectful. If professors are important to you, then don't take this class from him.

Dr. Stiles is a really experienced professor and knows his stuff. He sometimes gets distracted in lecture, but he's entertaining , and he's good at connecting the subject to current events. He teaches you how to be a professional International Relations scholar, and if you work for it, you come out of the class having learned a lot of skills.

Prof. Stiles is a good professor, but not everyone will get like his personality. He jokes a lot, but has a certain sense of humor. There are few assignments but he gives great feedback on rough drafts. As long as you make meaningful changes from what he says on the rough draft, the final will be great.
Professor Stiles is one of my favorite Professors at BYU. He is so funny and his knowledge of international relations is limitless.  I'm a huge fan!  Would recommend to anyone!
Looking at the reviews this clearly wasn't his best semester. Must be on the decline. DO NOT TAKE! When someone disagrees with him his true colors come out. Biased and boring.

Tries to be funny. Poor humor. Awkward. Boring lectures.   I guess since I'm a former enlisted Airman I "don't think". Poor taste.  The only thing he is good at is dissing others and preaching his personal political views as if it was class material.   Avoid.

This professor's sarcastic humor doesn't hide the fact that if you listen to what he says, he's  rude and unprofessional. Very condescending to students who challenge his opinions. Won't allow paper sources beyond the biased text. Lectures are more about his experiences at church, or soapboxes on grammar or politics, than about IR. Avoid.

I transferred to BYU from another university,  admittedly to be close to friends and church,  and I knew schools are different. I didn't know that BYU would have professors like this. Even for an intro, this was silly. Biased readings, and no real concrete explanations. Obviously an old school armchair analyst. Just tell him what he wants to hear.

The class is more of a history of US Foreign Policy than a discussion. Prof. Stiles is hilarious and a really nice guy. He's liberal, so he makes it fun at BYU. He's more than happy to help you. Has very few assignments, so missing a few points on the 2 tests or the 4 papers can really lower your grade. Lots of reading, but the slides rehash it.

He is great as long as you're willing to work with him. The class is pretty difficult with the grading scale he set up, but the topics are interesting if you're willing to think critically. Dr. Stiles is funny in his own way, a lot of people don't like his joking but it lightens things up. He presents things well and is very knowledgeable.

I am usually sensitive to professors that try too hard to be funny, but I actually think he is funny, because his humor is usually a sarcastic remark here or there, it isn't excessive. His lectures are well done, and the tests seemed easy, multiple choice. Average midterm was around  80% Attendence isn't really mandatory but it is fun/informative

Seems nice, but lectures are just full of him trying to make you laugh instead of actual useful information. Tries too hard to be funny, not hard enough to actually present useful material in a mature manner. Easy class, not useful at all the way he presents it. Take it from a different professor if you want to learn anything, especially if in IR.

Prof stiles is a nice guy and all, he's just a horrible professor. His tests are unnecessarily hard for an intro class. There's no study guide, or review sessions. He told us to us our final would be based on our online quizzes,  but it wasn't. So he told us to study something we didn't need to. Take a different professor if you can.
Fantastic lecturer. Clearly organized course. Requires attendance, which can be difficult. One of my favorite classes at BYU.

Stiles is the best teacher Poly Sci could ask for.  He's brilliant, caring, and dedicated to the pursuit of happiness in both life and the afterlife.  He's by far the best thing that could happen to our department.  I love you man!!!!!!!!

Stiles is a good teacher, but very hard, he expects a lot, but you don't always know what that is, so count on getting owned by your first assignment and then doing much better. The good thing about Stiles is he encourages a lot of participation and that helps you learn a lot. The bad thing is he grades really hard.

One of the greatest things about his classes is that he has students turn in a rough draft of their final paper.  He spends considerable time going over those papers.  I learned more about writing in political science from his review of my rough draft and our subsequent conversations than from anything else.

Pro Stiles was a great teacher. He was funny too. He definitely does have left views but is still an awesome guy. His course is text heavy. There is kind of a lot of work required. Paper, electives, 4 exams, and reading out of his case studies and the kegley book

I thought that prof. Stiles was very even handed in his handling of the controversial topics of this course. His lectures were power point based straight out of the book, but he would do his best to answer questions very thoroughly. Still, if you have little interest in the International Relations, don't expect this course to change your mind.

Stiles is a excellent teacher and has a great sense of humor.  I just read the book and did very well on the test and I dont have a photographic memory.  You can do great on the paper if you just do something original, I got a 100 on it.

Tests were online.  They were pretty easy.  The way he sets up the Kennedy lectures/elective activities is what I appreciated most.  There is one paper but your TA looks over it first. I didn't go to class because I didn't care about hearing about Stiles' political opinions all day and I still did well in the class.

BYU is a school full of conservatives lost in the traditions of their fathers. Dr. Stiles is a democrat but does not have a strong 'liberal agenda' although he does strongly believe in diplomacy. Indeed some of his lectures were boring but he mostly teaches you what international RELATIONS really means. The class is book heavy as well.

Tests straight from the textbook.  Full of true/false questions.  Lectures were boring and some of the TAs had some serious attitudes going on.  I thought international relations sounded interesting until this class.  take that how you will.  pretty tough grader.

The class is heavily drawn from the textbook. The tests aren't all about a photographic memory. Flashcards of terms and concepts are the way to go. He is a liberal Democrat at BYU so he seems to feel it necessary to pontificate. He is smart but class is insanely boring. I mostly played solitaire. Then I crammed and was totally fine for the test.

Do not take a class from Stiles! He loves to hear himself talk, and loves to tell students that he's interested in their opinions on completely normative questions, and then accuse them of being stupid, arrogent ideologues if they're views are anything less than radically liberal. His lectures feel like propaganda for the UN. It's totally lame.

The tests are impossible unless you have a photographic memory.  Stiles does not relate what he says to the text at all, and it is pretty hard to find a connection on your own. There's a lot of brown-nosing; as long as you say the right thing you're ok. Stiles asks for comments and makes fun of students ideologies if they differ from his own.

The tests are impossible unless you have a photographic memory.  Stiles does not relate what he says to the text at all, and it is pretty hard to find a connection on your own. There's a lot of brown-nosing; as long as you say the right thing you're ok. Stiles asks for comments and makes fun of students ideologies if they differ from his own.

I took this class during the Spring and was bored out of my mind. I felt that attending class was not necessary.  He provides lots of ways to pad your grade, but I was extremely disappointed in the exams.  He designed them so only a few would get an A.  You have to have a photographic memory of the textbook to get an A on the test.

Prof. Stiles is a really smart guy. I'd say his weakness is being able to connect with and help those who don't already have a solid basis in the subject matter. Lots of reading, tests pull heavily from textbook material. Really knows about what he's talking about, and for that fact alone I recommend this prof.

Very nice guy, fair, clear grader, responds to emails fast. U don't need to write notes; he posts his slides online. Study for tests by reading the textbook. He gives a list of terms you'll be tested on, so not too hard. The "debates" (you just present arguments from a textbook in front of the class) were annoying and a lot of work to prepare for.

Guy is super smart, and teaches well.  A rising star in his field too, guy is not at BYU cuz of contacts.  Requires a lot, but is crystal clear about how to get where he wants you to get.  Work hard, enjoy his quirky humor, and you'll come away having learned a ton (and getting the grade you deserve).
He is pretty eccentric and unclear, but overall he is alright. His grading is inconsistent, almost arbitrary.
No Comments

this class is front loaded. Expect to have lots of assignments in the first block. It was difficult to understand what he was looking for in a paper. Gives you a study guide for the exam...of about 80 terms :) If you know those really well - you'll do alright.
Good Professor, interesting classes.  Tests are challenging, but not impossible if you do the reading

Dr. Shepherd is an amazing person. He understands the topics taught in class and is amazing when giving one on one help. Lectures were hard to follow early on in the semester but he adjusted them for us which was awesome. This is the most work I've done for any class. Be ready to spend most your time on this classes projects, HW, and exams.

Yes, the material in this class is hard and the projects are difficult. But Dr. Shepherd is genuinely a great professor who cares about his students and genuinely wants them to succeed! He is great at teaching problem solving and critical thinking, and is always willing to help you understand the material and work on the projects outside of class.
Dr. Shepherd is clearly smart, but he doesn't translate that knowledge into effective teaching. His explanations jump around and often use unfamiliar terms without context.
The material was very technical, and Dr. Shepherd didn't break things down in a way that made sense. A lot of the class just sat quietly because we were too confused to even know what to ask.

This was the toughest class I have ever taken, but Dr. Shepherd made it bearable. We had five projects throughout the semester that would take up to 20 hours each to complete as well as homework due everyday. While the workload was extremely heavy, Dr. Shepherd was always available to help. You'll likely do just fine if you put in the work.

Best teacher ever.Yes, its hard, but Dr. Shepherd wants students to succeed. A project required coding. I spent hours debugging, comparing my work with a friend and couldn't find the mistake. I sent it over to my teacher not expecting him to take the time to debug my code, but he did!! He is cheerful and cares about the feedback of his students.

I have taken multiple classes from Dr. Shepherd and he is the best! He has an amazing teaching style that makes hard concepts easier to understand and apply. The classes he teaches are not easy subject matters, but the way he teaches makes them understandable and doable. His classes will make you better at python, but be ready to code.

Dr. Shepherd is Awesome! He sincerely cares for his students and reaches out to students individually to make sure they understand the material. The content is hard, but Dr. Shepherd does his best to help students understand. Just be aware that the projects are impossibly hard and require a lot of Python coding.

I LOVE DR. SHEPHERD! He is the most caring individual in the program and if you have the opportunity to take a class from him, do it. Ce 321 is a tough class, but prof. is reachable outside of class and always willing to meet. He is just the best and I can't say enough good things about him. TAKE FROM HIM!
This class was not the easiest, but overall it is doable. If you do the projects and the homework you will be fine.

Dr. Shepherd is very personable and kind but his class is really hard - probably the hardest CE class I've taken. Class time is usually pretty rushed because there is so much material to cover. Dr. Shepherd is very caring and always makes himself available. He is very smart so make sure to take advantage of that.

Dr. Shepherd is my favorite professor, he's amazing! He's so caring and genuine. 321 is a HARD class, but he always took time to make sure we were following the lectures. There are a few big projects during the semester that teach a lot but also take a lot of time, but this is a junior core engineering class, so would you expect anything less?

Dr. Shepherd tried his best. He poured his heart into the class but his way of teaching was just not the easiest. The overwhelming projects were so time consuming that you will need to start them way in advance. But if you made time to go to his office, he would really try to help you. I spent a lot of time online trying to understand topics.

He was super nice and understanding. I was nervous to take this class since I hadn't done ASL in about 2 years, but he helped me get caught up. There are a lot of video assignments but they aren't super difficult. He was really fair and easy to work with!

My favorite ASL professor so far; hes hilarious!! Always willing to answer questions, cares about his students, and wants you to learn everything to the best of your ability. You have to do the standard things most ASL classes require (Clubs, labs, CLL), but it is such an engaging class and he makes learning fun. I would 100% suggest his classes.

Professor Kennedy makes his lectures very engaging and fun. We played a lot of games that helped us practice our ASL and made it super enjoyable. He can be pretty vague about homework at times, but he is always super sweet and accommodating so even if you miss something or mess up he is willing to work with you.

Chad was an amazing ASL teacher. He is super funny and is deaf himself which makes it hard to communicate with him at first but you catch on quickly. he plays games almost every class which is super helpful and a fun way to learn. I never wanted to miss. He was understanding, when I missed tests or assignments he would allow me to turn in late.

If you took ASL in higshcool, then you probably want to go to ASL 201 instead of this class. This class was pretty easy, Chad is HILARIOUS! He isn't very clear about the homework sometimes, but overall it's a good environment. You can make a lot of friends int his class because you play alot of games. He is a really good teacher if you are learning

Class was fun but I never felt like I learned anything. He is an easy teacher and as long as you turn in the homework, etc. you'll get an easy A. But he can be hard to understand, and emailing him is difficult, so if you're struggling with sign it can be hard to communicate with him. Really nice guy, just wish we learned more.

Chad is THE BEST! I loved taking ASL 102 from him. He used games and activities to teach concepts. There is reading, homework, labs, club attendance, and 2 CLLS that are mandatory (Same for any ASL class). Chad is super funny and loves to help students learn ASL 10/10 would recommend :)
CHAD IS THE BEST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD!!!!!! He is so freaking adorable and so funny. I love the guy. He's such a good ASL teacher! Easy grader.
So funny super nice

Chad was awesome! I really enjoyed being in his class. Learning a new language can be really intimidating but Chad makes it easy, fun , and SUPER low stress. There is a lot of participation and you make friends because a lot of the class is having practice conversations with each other. You also learn a lot about deaf culture.

Chad was by far my favorite teacher, and made me feel really comfortable and have fun in class! he was very clear, patient, and made sure we learned while still having a lot of fun! Very reasonable grader. If you participate in class you will do great. Everything that was on the final had already been covered in class, so no surprises. AWESOME

Very good good class and I definitely recommend.
