Awesome Professor! Concepts are crystal clear after class and he is hilarious in the process!  He connect science with the Gospel in amazing ways!
Great Professor who will only teach you what you need to know and make class entertaining in the process... Highly recommended!
Professor Gee is the funniest teacher at BYU. He makes lectures fun and entertaining. If you go to class and go to reviews you can get a good grade.
Funny teacher, easy class if you've taken high school physics and/or chemistry.

Professor Gee is one of the most awesome professors i've had at BYU. When he explains things its easy to understand. Class is also really funny and a lot of his jokes help you to remember stuff, it's awesome!! Make sure you go to the review sessions the TA's have and you will do well on the exams. Take this class from him!!

He is a such a great teacher. You want to learn the material after leaving his classes. He has in class experiments almost every day during his class. He does a great job explaining all of the material. His TA are great too. He has clicker quizzes over the reading which aren't too hard at all. just do your reading!!!

Gee is hands down the best science professor (including Chem, Bio, and everything else) at BYU. Ample extra credit and tons of help. Plus, class was really fun. If you have to take 105, take it from him!!!!

prof gee is incredible. i hated physics with every fiber of my being but he made it so much more tolerable. he gave phenomenal lectures and did a ton of awesome demonstrations. he is very student friendly. go to the ta labs!

I cannot say enough good about him. probably the best professor i've had at BYU thus far.  He'll lay on a bed of nails while someone hits him in the chest with a hammer to make sure you understand, LITERALLY! never goes on until he's sure you understand.  If you must take physics, TAKE IT FROM GEE!

Dr. Gee really prepares well for each class.  He doesn't just lecture and say good luck.  He puts forth TONS of opportunity to learn the material.  Physics subject is hard, but Dr. Gee makes it really fun and interesting.  He is funny and devoted to teaching Physics and helping students learn.  One of the best courses I have ever taken!
Awesome teacher! Always trying to help explain things so everyone understands. Tries to make class as easy as possible for everyone. The subject itself is no fun, but he makes it enjoyable.

Professor Gee is one of my favorite professors at BYU!The tests are quite hard and the homework assignments are frustrating at times but if you work hard then you definitely can do well and learn tons along the way. He genuinely cares about each students he teaches and he loves what he does which makes it so much better! Take 105 from him!

This guy is a great teacher. He explains difficult concepts very clearly and won't leave you in the dark. He wants you to succeed and will try hard to keep everybody in the class up to speed. If you do the readings and work hard, your grade will reflect your effort. Homework and reading are worth a lot of your grade, so you can do well in the class

this teacher is weird, my first class i was like what is wrong with him is he ok? or is he normal that way? he is always excited and trust me he knows everyone in the class (400) exams are devastating its ok if you get 60 thats an A. 4 exams and a final HW is exhausting reading quizes suck, other than that its ok class is FUN really he is funny.

How cool is it to say you are getting an A in Physics? I don't know I didn't get an A but I loved going to this class. I think Professor Gee is the best instructor I have had yet. I still think about little physics problems daily.

By far the best class I've ever taken at BYU.  The tests are take home but do-able if you follow along in class and do the reading.  He's understanding about the difficulty of the material and is super approachable.

Gee is waaaaaay cool. Pay attention and don't fall asleep in class, like Cody, or he'll single you out. Lots of reviews and lots of opportunities for extra credit. Ask him to shoot himself with a ping-pong ball, its worth it. :)

I loved this class!  Gee is an amazing teacher!  If you get help on the homework in class and complete the practice exams before each test, you should have no trouble making an A.  This class was one of the best structured classes I have taken at BYU.  Though you have quizzes/homework due almost everyday, they help prepare for the exam!Gee Rocks!:)

Excellent Professor. Brother Gee makes class very interesting and does lots of demos. Not a very difficult class but you learn a lot. Probably my favorite this semester. As long as you stay on top of the homework and reading quizzes you will be set for the exams.

Dr. Gee is my favorit professor so far at BYU.  Physics isn't exactly my best subject but I looked forward to going to class every week.  The tests require a lot of thought but are managable.  After the first test average was a 65, Dr. Gee said "Don't worry, if you took the test, you pass the test."  He is really willing to help you learn.

AHHHHHHHHHHH!!!! GEE IS soo awsome! I wish he taught 106. TAke this class from anyone else and you're an idiot.  He shot himself in class and is way fair on tests. go to class and get tons of extra credit. way laid back class and super fun.
Reading is manadatory, there are reading quizzes. Read and do the homework and Dr. Gee will help you LEARN physics. One of the best professors I've had.

Dr. Gee is an excellent teacher.  Reading the manual before each class really helped me understand what he was teaching.  Fun demonstrations.  Quizes reflect the tests.  Plenty of opportunities for extra credit.

Acoustics class with Dr. Gee was so much fun!  He is hilarious and made even the simplest demonstrations a blast.  He uses helpful power point lectures, and creates "practice exams" that basically outline exactly what is going to be on the test!  If you want to take a fun Physics class, take Acoustics from Dr. Gee!

Dr Gee is a great physics professor, full of energy (kinetic), interested in his students, would help after class if you were struggling, curved tests and wants you to do well.  Dont be surprised to make between a 50-80 on the tests, especially the first one. study hard and do the homework

One of the best teachers at BYU.  Fantastic teacher, dang funny, very entertaining, great at explaining. Home work and reading quizzes each class period due before class. Requires constant effort, but not too hard. Go to the TA lab for homework 1 hr/assignment, & 1-2 hrs for reading each time,then tests will be manageable. I Highly recommend him.

What a cool guy! I was really afraid to take physics in college because I have never had it before, but this was the guy to take it from.  He is such a geek, but so cool.  His tests vary from easier to hard, but you ALWAYS have to study. Is really fair and loves his students.  Plus, you get points for his mistakes on tests...
A very good and very funny teacher. His tests aren't easy, but he prepare you well if your willing to try. Excellent teaching style. Just don't try and ask a personal favor and you'll be good.
Keeps class fun, with demonstrations and other ways of applying what you learn.  Lectures are beneficial as the concepts from the book can be confusing and abstract. Overall, great teacher!

I dare you to find a better teacher than Dr. Gee.  He really cares about our learning.  He is hilarious.  He's a mix between Dwight from the Office and Conan O'Brian.  Probably more like Dwight.  This is by far the best Physics 105 class BYU has to offer.  I have been in the other.  I mean he actually tried memorizing all our names!  Who does that?

Dr. Gee is the coolest prof i have ever taken. I hated physics just becuase I have physics naturally but he made the class so fun. He is way fair grading and tries to help you in every way possible. Great professor!

I loved this class! Prof. Gee is sooo funny and does cool experiments in class. He is way excited about physics, and makes it so much more fun to learn! The homework isn't bad, but if you have trouble, go to the TA lab. If you do bad on tests, he will curve it, and I think he even dropped a test grade. Overall, a great experience!! Take Gee!!

So so so funny. I cannot get over what a cool nerd guy Dr. Gee is. Physics is not a fun or easy subject for most taking the class, but he made it so interesting and great! He was so fair in all of his grading standards and makes getting a good grade totally possible. I definitely recommend taking the class from him.

I really enjoyed the class.  Dr. Gee is fun and he explains the concepts well.  The class is hard, but probably no harder than any physics class.  He does curve the tests, so even if they are hard he makes it fair.  I recommend taking his class.

So much fun!  He shot himself with an air cannon and gave a lecture while sucking on helium.  If tests are hard, he curves them.  I got almost 5 full percentage points of extra credit in his class.  Easy and fun.
He is the man a super nerd but still an awesome guy and really wants the class as a whole to do good.
Awesome teacher. Very energetic & enthusiastic. Super helpful -- he'll bend over backward for you and get to know you personally. He tries to make class interesting and fun. I highly recommend!
Makes class interesting.  One of the only science classes I've had where I didn't fall asleep half the time.

This was a very difficult class. The time in class was helpful, but not at all sufficient to be able to complete the labs. He expects his students to do a lot of their own learning through the textbook. As someone who struggles to teach myself through reading, this was painful. Very knowledgable, but seemed unprepared for lectures. He cares though.

The class will be hard regardless of the professor, but Seamons is a great choice. He knows his stuff and does the homework/labs himself to answer questions. He stayed up the last night of classes to help students with labs and has a merciful late policy. Midterms are brutal and lectures move fast, but reworks and the TAs will help you pass.

This class was a 5 difficulty for me but Dr. Seamons made it a 3. He messaged me when I failed to turn in an assignment and offered to help me during his office hours, which I thought was really nice of him. He probably sent the same message to a bunch of other students, but it helped me.

Talks about how much the "flipped classroom" model will help us as learners, when it's clear to see that that just means he can slack off and not come to class with a lesson prepared. Completely disorganized in terms of lecture. Unable to put himself in his student's shoes, or teach to their level. Assumes students *love* systems-level programming.

Dr. Seamons teaches the CS 401R blockchain class. It is a small class centered around self-paced learning. Dr. Seamons does a great job of providing resources for students to explore. The class isn't all that organized, which is intentional, so that students can largely study what they want to study, and then report back in the end. Great class!

CS 324 is really a Linux class. For someone who has experience with Linux, it is a breeze. For someone without experience, it would be more difficult. Dr. Seamons is an amazing professor who cares about his students. You can always reach out for help on Slack or ask questions in class and expect thorough responses. Really a phenomenal professor.

Super awesome professor, he worked really hard to make sure all his students were getting the help they needed and he is quite smart. This was the first time he taught this class but he did really well and programmed all the labs along with us. Held extra office hours to help us, pretty good lecturer!! I would take more classes with him.

Not a very good professor, hard to understand his train of thought, he jumps around from one topic to the next and mixes up words all the time. Assigns readings that are very dense and hard "just to see if you can understand what he had to" Exam questions were not useful, and not very security related.

There are a series of programming labs, they take a fair amount of time.  Start them early and finish them early for extra credit. Simple homework assignments.  Weekly quizzes in class.  Go to the open lab time for help.

I felt like he really wanted me to succeed as his student. Very willing to answer questions. His lectures and the reading are basically the same, so you can get by without reading, but the book is VERY helpful when doing labs.

I really liked Dr. Seamons. He was extremely helpful and did his best to help his students. His class was very organized and there were a lot of resources to help learn the material. It's a tough course though; a quarter of your final grade is based on the midterm, and it's a tough test.
He is very in tune with students needs. Very down to earth and able to explain complex functions, and very agreeable.

Prof Seamons is highly engaged, going so far as to do the projects himself to see what students are up against.  His lectures were great for several reasons:  he covers the material, he explains the concepts clearly and most importantly, he elicits a collaborative class environment where students feel comfortable asking questions. Terrific guy.

I took the class in Fall 2013. It was fantastic! He put lectures on youtube and spent class answering questions, giving practice problems, and generally helping you make sure you were really solid on the material and on the specific details of C++. There were a lot of resources available to me, and I was able to choose which ones worked best for me

Decent Teacher, good guy, cares a lot about teaching just doesn't necessarily do it very well. Not that he couldn't, he just uses slides a lot and doesn't actually code right there and explain how things work. Just shows code snippets which often are unrelated.
Great professor. Very caring for his students.

I really enjoyed this course! Dr. Hull explained well the second half of the NT and gave us insights into historical context, Greek/Latin translations, etc. Not a whole lot of homework but be sure to keep up on the readings. He doesn't submit his slides so be in class and take good notes. Gave us good study guides for the tests.

He knows his stuff! I have taken three classes from Professor Hull now, and each time I take a class from him, I am impressed with how well he is able to teach. Ask lots of questions and you will succeed!

I loved his lectures. This class was so spiritually strengthening for me in so many ways. He made the gospel practical and explained things from an evidential standpoint in combination with spiritual. Exams weren't insanely difficult, it was a typical religion class I think, but his lectures truly were amazing. Take his class, and PAY ATTENTION.

Great class, great professor. I have many accommodations due to health issues, Professor Hull was very understanding and willing to help me out. Tests require memorization, but if you are already familiar with the Old Testament, you should be fine.

He's a good professor that has lots of insights on anything he teaches. He knows so much about archeology, linguistics, and history and you will learn so much from him. Tests aren't as hard as some of these comments seem to think. He gives a very thorough study guide that I would read through twice before a test and I never got below an A.

Lectures were all very interesting. Dr. Hull taught about the Book of Mormon in a way that made me think about it in a way I never have before and made the history of it and the people in it feel more real. There were a lot of readings, and the tests could be a little difficult. However, if you study the study guide, you will do well on the exams.

He tests on the most obscure and weird details from lectures and class. He is unforgiving in his grading and doesn't care about health or circumstances of students, I got no help when I was sick right before a test. His class is not spiritual and his tests are on random facts and chronology that don't benefit anyone. Don't take this professor.

Worst experience. He tests on the most ridiculous details from dense articles and lectures on the final and on quizzes. You are also only allowed to miss 1 class before it takes you down almost a full letter grade. Doesn't help students who ask for help and is PowerPoint-based. he put an emphasis that students shouldn't make more than 1 comment.

He teaches a lot of the background of what was happening during the first half of the new testament. I'll admit at first I was skeptical about if I would like that approach but I think it was awesome. The background he provided helped me to have a better spiritual experience. He is a great guy and knows a lot about the new testament.

Tests on the most obscure details of class. A few of my classmates were on a shared doc taking notes the entire class every time and we were still lost on the quizzes. Missed the first day of class and continued to mix up dates in his reminder emails. Not spiritual at all, just ab literary devices and hypothetical geographic locations of bom

If you enjoy learning useless facts about the Book of Mormon and being tested on every tiny detail that was mentioned in class then you will love this guy. If you want to deepen your conversion to Christ by applying the principles found in the Book of Mormon I would go with another professor.

I despise this class. Felt like another version of American heritage. Anyone who takes this class is at an immediate GPA disadvantage. There's no reason a religion class should be this hard. I never felt the spirit, he teaches too fast, the tests ask you questions that weren't emphasized in class. Bad experience. Bad grade despite studying hard.

Prof. Hull is an archaeologist and incorporates that into Book of Mormon studies in lots of interesting ways! This class is super low-stress as long as you show up to class and do the few easy assignments every week. The only tests are a midterm and final that are easy if you go over his study guides and take notes.

I don't understand any of the good reviews he got here. He lectures the whole class and often keeps us longer than 50 minutes, all of his questions have targeted answers and are not a discussion at all, and the quizzes are about the most obscure things in class that even after 2 sheets of notes from one class I'm still lost when I take the quiz.

Loved the New Testament class. He was a great lecturer, found it easy to understand somewhat difficult content. Learned a lot and testimony grew. He provides everything you need to know for exams, easy A on all exams if you memorize slides he provides. You can tell he enjoys teaching. Would definitely recommend!

Professor Hull is a nice guy, he has a kind heart but I did not appreciate his teaching style. He loves the gospel but his testimony is based upon the history and factual parts of the gospel. He was previously a linguistics and anthropology professor so he teaches like that. If you want a history religion class, take it from him.

The tests were very difficult. It focuses more on the historical context and less on the spiritual stuff. I loved the class but the tests were near impossible. Make sure you know everything about the reign of the judges and descendants of Mosiah. And every random fact discussed in class.

A fountain of knowledge. His lectures are actually really interesting and you can tell he is so passionate about what he teaches. Study guides are super similar to the test and the assignments can be time-consuming but aren't hard. Attendance is mandatory though and is a huge part of your grade. So if you plan to skip, don't take this class.

Professor Hull is great. He used his archaeological background often in my New Testament class and really dives into the Greek/Hebrew/Aramaic translations of the Bible to help make sense of the material. Such an uplifting class spiritually and intellectually! Also, his tests are easy and he gives detailed study guides. Would totally recommend!

Prof. Hull gives a lot of amazing archaeological insight into the BoM without taking away the spiritual components. His lectures are always interesting. There is a lot of reading, the writing assignments attached to them are really short and largely graded on completion. His tests sometimes seem like they don't match up with the material though.

Super good professor and very knowledgeable! Graded a lot on attendance, so make sure you go to class. He has a super clear grading criteria, you have short papers due almost every class, but they're not bad at all (350 words) and don't take long to write. He gives good study guides and his tests are super similar to them.

Professor Hull is truly a wonderful teacher! He mainly focuses on the historical aspects of the Book of Mormon, which I find fascinating! Definitely show up to class and take notes on his lectures/power points and you'll be just fine.

I don't understand why this guy doesn't have 5 stars. He is one of the easiest religion professors. He gives you study guides that are 99.99% like the exam. Read those and you are guaranteed an A. The only thing would be attendance. If you miss 6 times, you automatically fail. He is an expert and teaches things clearly. TAKE HIM FOR YOUR GOOD

Dr. Hull's class is very straightforward. His exams aren't too difficult if you review the study guide. His class strengthened my testimony of Christ a lot through the lectures and readings. His rating should be way higher in my opinion. Attendance is mandatory in his class so if you like to skip class this isn't for you.

I honestly think that this rating does not do justice to professor Hull. He is a great lecturer and very knowledgeable in the subject he teaches. This comes across in his understanding of ancient language etymology, history, and geography- all ways he uses to explain things in the New Testament.

Professor Hull was my favorite religion professor at BYU so far. His assignments were simple and short and his lectures were super interesting. Exams are very similar to the study guide so make sure to study carefully. The content of this class was super interesting, just make sure to stay on top of regular assignments and you'll do fine!

I love Professor Hull's class. The class isn't an easy A but was extremely worth it. It is different from seminary but I loved this religion class with Professor Hull. He did such a good job going through the lectures. He was very organized and I had a lot of spiritual growth throughout this class. Tests aren't too bad but you DO have to STUDY.

Professor Hull definitely knows what he is talking about. He brings some interesting academic perspectives to the text. There is limited participation in the class, which I didn't love. Outside homework wasn't too difficult and the tests and quizzes were super easy. I probably missed class a few days and got 50% on participation so go to class
Prof. Hull is a solid choice for this class. Not only is he knowledgeable in his area, he gives you very straightforward study guides for the exams. Easy A and very enjoyable.

Professor Hull is a great mix of spiritual and academic. His lectures are so interesting but don't mistake this class for a blowoff. The tests are hard, and he gives little to no extra credit. Furthermore, there is no curve, so what you earn is what you get.

Professor Hull is a great teacher. He really knows his stuff, including several languages. I loved this because he was able to give us greater context by providing a better translation for sometimes confusing passages. If you do all of your assignments and pay attention in class, you will do great. He provides great study guides, too.

As far as religion classes go, this one is pretty good. The work load isn't too heavy at all. That does mean that you have to work to do well on quizzes and the tests but the quizzes are open notes and the test have good study guides. Lectures have interesting content but can feel repetitive.

I LOVED this class. It was much more intellectual than I was expecting it to be for a religion class, but I loved it so much. With almost every verse we discuss, Professor Hull translates it into Greek, Aramaic, and Hebrew to help us fully understand the verse. Only three tests in the semester and they're pretty easy if you go over the study guide.
This class really wasnt too bad, 3 tests in the semester with study guides with all the information. The class is not bad and is interesting to learn about. Not a hard class.

I'm surprised that Professor Hull doesn't have at least a rating of 4 on here. His class isn't super hard (he gives you a study guide for each test and online quizzes that are open note). His class was also very spiritual despite it being heavy in historical context. I would absolutely take his class again.

One of the easiest yet most inspirational religion classes I've taken. The grading criteria is clear from the start, to review for the tests he literally gives you all the information you need to know, nothing more nothing less, so there's no surprises. Always willing to answer questions in lecture, even if they aren't exactly on the topic.

Such a wonderful professor. You can tell he cares about his students' success. Tests may seem difficult, but he literally puts everything you need to know for the test on the study guide. He will say in red what is important to know for the exam. He has such a wonderful knowledge of the time period and answers any questions you may have.

Professor Hull is super duper knowledgable. I wouldn't say his classes are overly spiritual, which was a plus for me. You really get to dig deep into the history of the book you're reading. Professor Hull has studied languages and he takes a historical and archaeological approach to teaching the Church doctrine. I took 3 classes from him in total.

I learned more in Prof Hull's class about the Book of Mormon than I ever had before. 2 short papers due every week that were essentially graded on completion. Midterm & final were both pretty specific- definitely took lots of studying. If you are looking for an easy A, don't take this class. But Dr. Hull is an amazing professor to learn from!

nice guy and very knowledgeable. Tests were brutal and you had to know everything about the book of mormon. Study guides were misleading. The positive about him is he is very knowledgable and is able to explain difficult BOM concepts well. He is also really good at showing how the bom is true with real life evidence.

just dont take his class. he's a nice enough guy and there isn't too much homework and then all the sudden he drops you into the exams expecting you to have basically memorized the book of mormon and all the subtle meanings of phrases. You also have to basically memorize the articles he gives you and they are long, boring and hard reads. dont take

Professor Hull gives a very historical perspective on the BOM. It's SUPER interesting! I learned so much from him. There are two short 350-400 word assignments due every week about some readings, but they're easy to stay on top of. Midterm was pretty easy so long as you study and stick to the study guide--it's your best friend.

Dr. Hull is EXTREMELY qualified to teach this class, he is a widely known linguist who has traveled to the actual historical sites he lectures on and has extensive knowledge on the details of everything. His lectures were amazing every time and if you pay attention you will get a good grade in this class. Attendance is mandatory!!! Skipping lowers

Dr. Hull is a very smart and spiritual man. His classes are faith-building, although they can be boring at times. I took his class over zoom due to COVID, and the 2-hour classes often dragged on, however, this isn't necessarily true for in-person classes. The exams are pretty specific but manageable.

I love Dr. Hull. He really wants students to attend lectures, but it's for a good reason, going to class really allows you to understand the material and ask any questions. Also, if you don't go to class you'll miss the in-class quizzes. Professor Hull is super nice, and he gives you EXACTLY what you need to study for the tests. He's AWESOME!

This really wasn't what I was expecting when it came to a religion class. I found it really challenging because I felt like even if I did listen in lecture, that didn't mean I would do well on the exams. You'll have to MEMORIZE the scriptures on the study guide if you want to do well. The articles we read were super excessive too, wasn't a fan.

I love professor Hull! I learned SO much about the Book of Mormon in his class. He gives really interesting background info on archaeology and linguistics in the text and has some very interesting Book of Mormon theories. Assignments are boring but easy. The tests are specific but he gives very detailed study guides. And he is very kind and funny!

I loved taking this class because Prof. Hull knows a lot about archeology and linguistics, which I found really fascinating and kept me engaged. That being said, there were a lot of readings to do every week that were kind of boring and the tests did get pretty specific, but they were things we covered in class and he gives out a study guide.

In this Book of Mormon class we are talking about the book from an archeological, historical, linguistic and poetic stand point. I love the Book of Mormon, but the papers he had us read were long and a snooze fest because I do not care about most of what the articles are saying.

This was my lowest grade for most of my first semester at BYU. I was really frustrated with it, but don't have anything against Professor Hull specifically. the better notes you take, the better you will do. he curved our final exam but I think that was a rare occasion

This was a very cool class! Brother Hull knows a lot about Mesoamerica, so he gives you a lot of insight on that. That being said, it wasn't a super spiritual class but more of a contextual study of the Book of Mormon. He is very kind, personal, and knows a lot of good resources.

If you're looking a spiritual experience, this isn't the class. Hull takes the informative and rational side of the Book of Mormon and provides context within the world at that time, which is very interesting. He is extremely smart. Long readings but easy papers. Not too hard but not an easy A.

Dr. Hull is one of my favorite teachers. I took him twice. He's kind and cares about his students. Additionally, he knows a lot about Mesoamerican culture and archaeology that helps us understand the background context of the Book of Mormon. I always learn something new from him that I couldn't get from other teachers. I recommend him highly.

Not a super spiritual class. but really informative. Studied the Book of Mormon from an academic angle. If you pay attention at all the weekly quizzes are easy. You do have to write 2 papers ever week, but they're only 400 words. It wasn't my favorite class, I thought it was a little dull at times, but other than that no complaints.

His quiz and test questions can be very specific, but he gives you a detailed study guide before the midterm and final. Just make sure to pay attention in class so you can pass the weekly in-class quizzes with ease. There were weekly Book of Mormon chapters and Articles to read, but that's to be expected in a Book of Mormon class. Just do the work
I don't typically write reviews, but I wanted to put one on here. Overall I didn't like the class. It wasn't spiritual at all. I learned more from the articles that he made us read then from him.

This class isn't super hard but its more than a religion class should be. The tests ask very specific questions, although he does give you a very specific study guide. Be sure to do all the readings because those will help your grade tremendously.
He is extremely intelligent and has a great grasp of the gospel. His class is difficult, and attendance is graded, however if you just do the work you will do fine.

Professor Hull does a lot of paper writing. Be prepared to read long articles and ten chapters from the Book of Mormon for the week and they are all due on the first class day that week. And he does random quizzes.

Dr. Hull is great! I took both 121 & 122 from him because I enjoyed his class so much. He is very clear on his grading criteria, and is willing to help. His background in ancient Mesoamerican anthropology also brings a lot of interesting points to the table during lectures, though he is very careful not to push his beliefs on you.

He's a great teacher and knows his stuff. The content is very interesting. It is fun learning about the Book of Mormon from a Linguist. He's lived in Central America, so that's fun to hear about. Take good notes, though. Almost all of the test questions come from the class Power Points. You are required to read an article each week.

I really like Bro Hull. He has lots of unique perspectives on the Book of Mormon from more of a worldly perspective. He has a deep background in different languages so he has lots of insights that other professors might not have. He is very passionate about teaching. Each week you have to write 2 350-400 word papers on pretty big readings.

Brother Hull's class was way harder than it should have been. So many papers and a bunch of reading. His quizzes focused on a lot of specific details that you had to be in class to catch. The things we learned were fascinating, but this class should be way more than 2 credit hours. Other religion teachers make this class much more enjoyable!

2 papers a week, plus about an hour or so of readings. He teaches the class from a historical standpoint which makes it way more interesting. Just lots of busy work, but all the test questions can be answered in his lectures.

So much reading! If you have a decent knowledge of the Book of Mormon, you can show up on quiz day and usually pass, unless he moves quiz day just to hurt you for not sitting through his horribly dry lectures. He's really intelligent but wow he's boring. Also, I'm writing my final paper for his class right now and I'm not even sure what he wants...
This is a two-credit class. It is worth at least four. Lots of homework. Not merciful on the grading.
Way too much homework for a class of its kind. His class is worth a lot more credits than you get for it. Prof. Hull does not accept any late work.

As a professor, it's clear that he knows his stuff regarding the Book of Mormon. Like other comments have said, this class has way too much work for a 2 credit class. If you really love reading things that are way to long, this is the class for you. His knowledge has helped my testimony, but I really don't feel like I have been spiritually uplifted

I was surprised for a religious teacher I didn't feel religiously enlightened whatsoever. Nice guy and the class is super easy if that's what you're interested in, but if you really want to learn something, find someone else.

I was first in another class, I was overwhelmed with how much homework there was so I transfered into his class on the last day to adddrop classes. Ya that was a mistake.  There was more homework in this class then the one I was in in the first place. Bro. Hull was really nice but it really bothered me how much homework there was.

Brother Hull was an amazing teacher. I had always heard Book of Mormon classes were the hardest, but his class was fun, full of good insights and interesting. Has "pop quizzes" but you almost always know when they are coming. Has a study guide for tests, which are really easy if you've done the readings. I want to take part 2 from him.

Great insight with extraordinary balance of spirituality and scholarly prowess. Delves into linguistic roots of the text and coupled with the weekly article analysis you really get more out of this class. If you want to learn while still enjoying the ride, take it from Prof. Hull!
Dr. Hull is an awesome professor! He is really funny and I enjoyed his unique insight on the Book of Mormon! You will love taking a class from him.

Prof. Hull was overall a good teacher. He's a linguistanthropologist, which influences his approach to the BOM. He is very fair towards opinions of others. There is a quiz every week, but as long as you pay attention in class they are super easy, but you have to go every day. There are scholarly readings about the BOM every week, which were fun.
Dr. Hull did teach the material, but his lectures were remarkably dry. Little humor. Lots of busy work. Not very open to student opinions.
He is a great lecturer that invites participation and is super understanding of personal circumstances.  I really liked his class and hope I get him for a future class.

Professional linguist, has visited central america. Adds historical and linguistic insights that you wouldn't get from other professors.  Take him if you want to learn something different from what you've always heard in sunday school.

I would totally take another class from Bro. Hull, if I get the chance. I really like class participation. There was no text other than the Book of Mormon itself, which was nice, but also not nice for studying. He also didn't give out a studyguide.

Really disappointed by this class. He is a nice guy, but some of the most boring, "common sense" lectures I've ever had. Quizzes and tests were frustrating and things were never graded promptly. I also wish the class was called "Ethics of War" because that's all the course material is. Would not take again.

Dr. Kartchner is absolutely fantastic! He knows what he's talking about, and is clear in what he expects out of you. Willing to give you help whenever you need it, and really wants you to succeed. Makes things relevant to what's happening in the world today, and approaches things in a really interesting wat. Would 100% take another class from him!

Professor Kartchner brings a wealth of experience to the job, and he will sure as heck tell you about it. Just make use of his office hours, and you will do well in the class. He also tends to favor students who talk in class, so throw some comments out occasionally.

Extremely qualified and respectfully answers all questions. Not the most dynamic or entertaining lecturer, but you're never bored. Tests and quizzes are HARD and only free response. I performed poorly on the first quiz but asked him and the TA a few questions on how to improve and I did fine on the rest of the assignments.

Be careful about the grade you get on the very first quiz because that will be your final grade. There is no grade improvement in the class to protect his B/B- average. Talks too much about his life in a dry manner and gives little preparation for tests and quizzes. If you care about your grades, I would avoid his classes.

Professor Kartchner is one of the most amazing people! He truly cares about his students and he wants us to succeed. If it was up to him, all the students would get an A. The only reason he has to make quizzes and tests hard is because the dept didn't want him giving out so many A's. This man knows what he's talking about- take his class!

I thought this would be my favorite class due to the ratings, but the professor just talks about his life and random stuff. Then when you get to the test, you aren't prepared. The overall grade is determined by a few assignments. You will get a lower grade than you expect in this class.
This guys knows what he's talking about. He has some amazing stories to tell and knows his stuff inside and out. I would take another class from him in a heartbeat.

Pop quizzes can be a killer. He's very experienced and does care about his students. You have to buy three textbooks that you use frequently. All in all, he's a great professor who's class is very engaging.

Take Professor Kartchner just for the chance to learn. He seriously knows his stuff. As long as you are fine with sometimes a slower delivery, you'll benefit from the class. A few papers and a couple random assignments and its not too bad. Take it for the connections and experience.

Just got done with Kartchner's 470. If you want the most qualified & insightful 300/400 professor then take him. I've had about 15 professors in the Poli Sci program so far and am most impressed with Kerry. Ya, you need to work for your grade, but you get what you give. He was a lead nuclear negotiator with USSR in the Cold War. Take Kartchner.

I've take a couple classes from Kartchner, and the more I get to know him, the more I like him. He's super caring, the tests are pretty easy if you pay attention in his reviews, and he's just such a nice guy. If you're interested in a career in foreign affairs and express that interest to him, he'll give you any advice/help he can muster.

By far one of my favorite professors. His career was in a high-up position in nuclear arms reduction negotiation with the Soviet Union, so he's got real-world experience. Discussion-based course. Amazing anecdotes and insight. Really puts the time in to help his students succeed. Wrote an amazing letter of rec.

Dr. Kartchner is the nicest professor I have ever had. SO caring and thoughtful. And he is very very willing to help. I had an incredibly packed semester, so when I came time to writing my capstone I HAD to meet with him because I didn't have the time to brainstorm ideas on my own. Very willing to help. He's also pretty funny for an elderly guy.

When I was in the class, he was totally fine. I thought he gave good feedback on how each assignment went. However, after he told me "excellent job" on my presentation, he gave me a 70%. Then, after saying my paper was "much improved, good work!", he gave me another C! He didn't report the grades until the class ended so I couldn't even complain!

I loved Professor Kartchner! His experience in foreign policy made him very qualified to teach US Foreign Policy, not to mention interesting. He is willing to provide help and advice for the paper and even future career paths. As long as you participate and study for the tests and do the paper well, you'll get a good grade and learn a lot!

Dr. Kartchner is awesome. He set up his class so we learned a lot about current events and how US foreign policy is affected. The class isn't too difficult but you really want to try because you can learn so much. He definitely knows what he's talking about. He really cares about your success as well! I HIGHLY recommend taking a class from him.

I loved his lectures. It was more focused on what he could teach us instead of students talking to each other, which is something I find annoying about some other religion classes. The in-class quizzes could get pretty specific so make sure to do the readings closely.
Great! Not too hard but I learned a lot. Pearl of Great Price is awesome! Prof Muhlestein is great.

Dr. Muhlestein is one of my favorite professors! He gave such amazing lectures and truly cared about each one of us. He also got me in touch with some other professors for some opportunities for my career, and he was so nice to talk to me and give me some advice! I'll definitely be taking another class from him because he is so good!!

Grading criteria was vague at best and papers took a very long time to grade. The study guide was not helpful, might as well have said "just read everything again". It also felt like he was bashing on other Christian denominations a lot of the time.

Prof. Muhlestein is knowledgeable and I definitely learned a lot about the old testament. Tests are open note open book, but they're timed and the questions are stupid specific. Besides exams, the class itself is easy. The pop quizzes are also very specific too, so do your readings.

Dr. Muhlestein was a great professor who really knows his stuff! He has you watch a lot of really cool little videos about the historical background for whatever the class will be about, including maps and pictures of what the places actually look like in the middle east and depictions and descriptions on what they might have looked like back then.

Favourite religion professor. His tests are a little absurd. Lots of questions that aren't necessarily doctrine, but his own understanding. Great for understanding the Old Testament better. 4 papers that are more of a completion grade and pop quizes so definitely come to class.

The teacher is very kind/respectful, and is willing to discuss anything about the class. However, the class was very disorganized. The tests also are very subjective, and are based more on what the teacher wants you to say, and less on actual things we learn in the Old Testament. I did fine in the class, but it is too much work for 2 credits.

If you want an easy, spiritual class, this is it, but if you're interested in scholarly attention to the text, look elsewhere. i.e. Joseph Spencer. I would also recommend 300 over 301, as in 301 too much time is spent rehashing familiar stories like the Creation and Fall rather than the less familiar stores that make taking the class worth it.
Professor Muhlestein is fantastic! He makes understanding Isaiah a breeze. Attend class, read the textbook, and use tools like Unstuck study - you'll crush this course!

I am sure he is a great Old Testament teacher, but UNIV was hard with him. He made us do every assignment that the university put on the list. Discussions were hard because he asked confusing questions and then sometimes went on tangents. He was super caring, though, and invested in making our experience at BYU positive.

Professor Muhlestein is an incredible professor! I had him for University 101 and his lectures were never boring. I learned a lot from him and I plan on taking on of his religion classes in the future! He really cares about his students and is pretty understanding as long as you communicate with him.

Best professor I've ever taken in any subject. I took Writings of Isaiah from him, and now try to take a class from him every semester. Classes are all structured the same way, come to class, do the readings and you will very probably get an A in whatever course you take from him. Negative reviews are crazy to me, probably people who didn't read.

The first part of class is always us asking questions, which is so helpful because the Old Testament can be confusing (and sometimes weird). Brother Muhlestein really knows his stuff, so his answers are super helpful, and he's also open about things that we don't know or have the answer to yet. Take good notes in class, the tests are open note!

I walked away from every lecture inspired and wanting to live my covenants. I would highly recommend this class to anyone wanting to learn more about the Old Testament. There is a fair amount of reading (about an hour) before each class, but I found this reasonable compared to other religion classes. The quizzes can be tricky, so read carefully.

This is by far the best religion class I have taken at BYU. I went in wanting to learn and that is exactly what happened. I can study and understand Isaiah. He is really good and making Isaiah's writings relevant today. You will write four papers that aren't hard. If you want to learn how learn the scriptures, this a great class.

Hands down best class I've ever taken! Dr. Muhlestein is phenomenal. Isaiah was super confusing to me before the class, but Dr. Muhlestein knows his stuff. I can now read Isaiah and get SO much out of it. If you want to understand Christ, Israel, and the temple, this is the class! You'll read all of Isaiah, but it's not overwhelming at all.

Dr. Muhlestein is awesome! He cares about his students understanding Isaiah and seeing him in their lives. He encourages questions and discussion in class. You have to read the chapters carefully enough that you can remember important symbols and main points for his quizzes. Attendance is important because it is half of your quiz points!

Prof. is amazing! He knows his stuff for sure so pay attention in class as you will learn so much! If you take good notes the tests shouldn't be to hard as they are all open note etc. This man changed my perspective of the Old Testament. If you want to have many questions answered and these books make so much more sense take this class!

One of the lighter homework loads I've had for a religion class. Tests can be worded poorly, but they are open note so it's never too difficult. Sometimes he can come off as insensitive to some marginalized groups (especially LGBTQ+), but overall a great guy who clearly loves his students. Changed how I viewed Isaiah forever.

Dr. Muhlestein is an amazing teacher, he is very knowledgeable and gives excellent context for the reading in the Old Testament. Spends as much time as needed to answer questions about the reading. If you're not a good reader like me listen to the chapters on 2x speed and read along. Class was inspirational and not difficult, highly recommend.

Dr. Muhlstein's class was my least favorite religion class I've ever taken. Pop quizzes are overly specific. Lectures are often biased and boring. I didn't feel welcome as a minority in his class. I cannot express how dreadful this class was.

Brother Muhlestein made the Old Testament real for me. He emphasizes the Abrahamic covenant and the Lord's mercy. He also genuinely wants us to reflect on our behavior towards God. Brother Muhlestein knows a lot about the Old Testament but is clear about the parts he doesn't know. He doesn't teach false doctrines.

The students were unfriendly.

Pretty easy on demand class. Weekly journals and lesson quizzes are due every Sunday night. One midterm and the final. Semester long BoM project that wasn't too bad either. Relatively easy class for your GE religion credit.

This class is fun, taking the online course, you will have everything due every Sunday, which was nice. You will have a Book of Mormon Project that you will complete throughout the semester. You will have 1 midterm and 1 final. They are proctored exams. Great course and Great professor.

I really love Professor Muhlstein. His lectures were very spiritual and inspirational, and I learned so much from him that I remember all the time. His class made me a better missionary and opened up my view of the gospel and covenants so much. I would definitely take a class from him again!
Very academic religion class. Loved all of his expertise in archaeology and Egyptian history.

Cannot express how much I loved this professor. His Pearl of Great Price class was such a hidden gem. He is one of the smartest people on campus but is so humble about it. And he is absolutely hilarious. I would go to him with any gospel questions, no matter how personal they are. I want to take another class from him!
His religion class was awesome, and super fun to go to. I fell asleep a couple times, but he is really knowledgable about the book of mormon. There are a lot of papers due, but they're not hard.

Muhlestein turns the BoM into nothing more than a piece of literature. Luckily his tests were open note so I still did fine despite regularly leaving classes following the quizzes. Take him if you want an easy course but not if you want to actually learn anything spiritually valuable

Dr. Muhlestein is knowledgeable and reliable. He teaches a lot about symbolism and historical significance of scriptural references (ex: geography of Middle East). There were a lot of 'surprise' quizzes, meaning we knew there would be a certain number but we didn't know which days they would be, meaning attendance is essential.

The study guides never helped me on the tests. The class was relatively easy, but the tests were very hard. It was open note and book, but the questions were basically if you could interpret the teacher.

I liked Professor Muhlestein a lot. His Writings of Isaiah class was definitely difficult, but worth the work. The midterm was 89 questions plus an essay. Since most people don't know Isaiah like they know the Book of Mormon, you'll most likely have to put more time in to studying and preparing for tests. The class was very uplifting spiritually.

I do not recommend this class for a thorough study of the Book of Mormon. His professional expertise and focus on the Middle East shows when he turns every lecture into teaching about God's covenant with Israel. Otherwise, there were frequent quizzes, a few easy papers, and two tests. He is a good, sincere man but I regret taking this class.

Professor Muhlestein is AMAZING! I took him for Teachings of Isaiah and I have never learned more in a religion class ever. He's great at answering questions and is super kind. 4 papers over the course of the semester that aren't too hard. Pop quizzes are pretty easy if you've done the reading. Midterm and final are open note. Take this class!

This class was amazing. He doesn't fluff things up a ton but you learn a ton of awesome material. I loved what I learned and he is very caring and understanding. His goal is for you to learn and does NOT focus on things that try to trip you up. Homework isn't super heavy but is super fun to do. Super recommend this professor.
Zero clarity, exams were tricky and heavily weighted - He doesn't prepare you for them at all. Otherwise interesting class.

I learned more about archaeology and geography than I did Christ. It wasn't awful, it was just unenjoyable, and I don't think i'll take another class from Brother M. Pop quizzes every now and then, but they're not hard. Also his midterm and final were absolute train wrecks. The class isn't stressful, it just boring, and the tests are SO subjective.

I took Writings of Isaiah, and I LOVED IT! I actually came out loving Isaiah (did I just say that out loud?). Classes are very informative and entertaining - very Q&A based. He gives a few pop quizzes, so do your reading and come to class. Tests are about topics discussed in class/on videos. 4 not-too-hard papers. Very inspiring class

Bro. Muhlestein is a really nice guy, but his class is a mess. I do not think he has updated his video tech/powerpoint slides since the mid-2000's, and working with his class materials can be frustrating. His study guides are not specific at all and based on random things he says in class. Again, really nice guy, but this class is hard to follow.

Bro M is a good guy, super smart. And I took this class when it was his first time teaching. Quizzes should be easy since the students are the one responsible for making them. This class was so fast, that I gave up in the beginning because of the lack of organization. It felt like there was so much to learn, and no time to digest.

Dr. Muhlestein is an Egyptologist. This was his first time teaching the writings of Isaiah. I learned so much from his class and have found reading Isaiah a lot easier because I took this class. The tests are a little difficult but he provides a lot of material to help you prepare.

He's a great teacher. I took him for Isaiah so it was a HARD class but he did a great job making it a good experience. TIP for this class: You need to spend at least an hour for each class period reading the assignments or you'll sit in class clueless. Isaiah is hard to understand and takes TIME to learn.

I loved this class w/ Bro. Muhlestein! I thought it was going to be lame, but I could not have been more wrong! He changed my perspective on the Gospel so much. I have a stronger testimony of Christ and the Plan of Salvation because of this class. I plan on taking as many classes from him as I can! 10/10 would recommend.

Brother M. amazing! He is unbelievably smart, and His lectures are amazing. It's a lot of reading, and you have in-class pop quizzes about the reading so don't miss! They are worth quite a bit of your grade. His tests are online and pretty difficult, but He gives a study guide and is willing to answer any questions you have.
I took him again because I liked him so much. Taught true principles. Good man.

He's a smart guy and he presents material in a very clear way. He's very responsive to question, respects the students, and doesn't appear cocky at all. The only downside is that his personality isn't particularly engaging; he speaks in a somewhat monotone voice, but it wasn't a huge deal. Great class, I highly recommend him.

Bro. Muhlestein is extremely knowledgable, and you'll learn a lot from this class. But this is the lowest grade I have ever gotten, and it was a religion class. The pop quizzes are based off of specific details from anywhere between 5-15 chapters of reading, and they're worth a big portion of your grade. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT! Would not take again.

This class is honestly my favorite religion class out of all the ones I have taken. Professor Muhlestein is knowledgable, caring, hilarious, and his classes are truly inspirational. I learned SO MUCH from him and Old Testament became my favorite scripture. And the class really is not difficult, even though we included Isaiah!

Brother Muhlestein is great! Disclaimer: I audited this class so I can't comment on tests, but I learned tons. He has a masters in Biblical Hebrew & a doctorate in Egyptology. In other words, he is THE perfect person to teach PGP. He has this awesome, dry sense of humor and makes everyone laugh without detracting from the Spirit. Def reccommend!

I took Professor Muhlestein for Rel 301 and loved his teaching so much that I took Rel 302 from him as well. Like many, I often question the relevance and significance of the Old Testament. This class taught me useful study techniques to understand the Old Testament in the future. Tests were easy, but you do read a lot in preparation for class.

Seriously my favorite teacher at BYU so far.  Most of the class was spent on student questions and context of the old testiment.  There were quizzes about every other class.  Tests were pretty straightforward.  He is really the most sincere, kind person.

Loved taking his class. Knows the PgP very well. Can share a lot of details and background about the scriptures, and also share great spiritual insights and testimony that makes the class spiritually strengthening and intellectually enlarging. Very manageable work load. Open to questions and very helpful. Fun professor, glad I took his class.

I always felt better after one of his lectures, and I actually looked forward to his classes. He has pop quizzes randomly dropping 2 to check attendance, so you can miss class if needed. I'm done with my religion credits but considering the 2nd half of Old Testament because he was so good. All you need is Bible for class.

Extremely kind, knowledgable, and inspirational. Going to class was always a spiritual experience, and what I learned this semester changed the way I read and understood the scripture. It's not an easy class, but it's very fair and definitely worth it. He wants his students to succeed.

Hands down favorite professor. Seriously, if you want to get a ton out of your BYU religion course experience, study with Dr Muhlestein. My mind was blown too many times to count. I think about and apply the things that he taught us on a regular basis. Yes, it will be one of the most difficult religion classes you take, but it will change your life

Professor Muhlestein changed my perspective about the scriptures. He really knows his stuff and explains it very well. Definitely take this class from him! Tests are hard and the study guide can be confusing. If you need any help on the study guide though, you can email him and he will help. Awesome guy!

I took this class from him and loved it, and then I was the TA for it. In the class the student was complaining that Dr. Muhlestein doesn't give A's, the most common grade he gave was an A-. Then it was tied between A's and B+'s. So its crazy to say he doesn't give A's or that his tests are tough. He is an amazing lecturer and knows his stuff!

He is very knowledgeable and his lectures were very spiritual. However, I would advise against him because his exams are VERY tricky and  your grade is based almost solely on these exams. He is old-school; he thinks that only a precious few deserve A's and that GPA is not important. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE unless your GPA doesn't matter.

If you want to gain an education, come to this class. Holy heavens. he's amazing. He knows what he's talking about and made me look at the scriptures in a way i never have before.  He helps you understand an give purpose to your study. This class iswas absolutely fascinating. There's a bit of reading and the tests are based on lectures.
Such a hard class, he is an ok guy i guess, but tests are HARD and too much work for a religion class.

He's a very nice guy who really knows his stuff about the PoGP. He's doesn't have a ton of busy work like other religion classes. He spends alot of time answering questions though, so if you were hoping for a lecture series find a different teacher. If you pay attention you can get an easy A.

TAKE MUHLESTEIN!!!! He pushed me to know the BOM inside and out. he's an expert in ancient middle eastern studies etc, provides so much historical context and connections to the Old Tstmnt. doesn't push his personal opinions on you, doesn't tolerate mormon myths. sensitive and open-minded to issues facing the church today. LOVED this class.
Great teacher, knew his stuff, tests were clear, if you study you do well. Loved this class.

tests were EXTREMELY tricky and he thought it was funny, do not take a class from this professor. I would study my butt off and still get a low B or high C on this tests and he is only a religion teacher

One of the BEST religion teachers I've had. He is super clear about what is doctrine (as opposed to guessing and speculation). He is an Egyptologist, so he KNOWS what he's talking about with the Book of Abraham. And his personality is awesome - he's funny and engaging. There is lots of class discussion, and the lectures are very well-structured.
Best Religion teacher!  He has such a great knowledge of the culture and historical background of the Old Testament; he was able to explain so many things.  Plus, he's hilarious.
Most Christ-like person I've ever met.
I love this class. He made learning about the Book of Mormon very fun. But he also tried to stretch us in the class. So it wasn't super easy. But worth it.

Class was extremely interesting and helpful until we hit the book of Abraham. Went way to far into the egyptological aspects that are merely his assumptions (hes and egyptian scholar). While these are interesting they are far from the doctrines contained in the P.G.P. If you would like to actually study the PGP in depth take a different teacher

He is so funny, and yet thinks of things no one has thought of.  He makes you work for your grade, but is clear on what you need to know and do, so if you will work, you can do well.  He is also hot, and way too smart!

I loved Brother Muhlstein. He is very nice and really makes you reflect on your own personal life. I felt like I grew a lot in his class. The tests weren't really hard, but they are heavily weighted. He only uses the Book of Mormon and not manuals or handouts so that you learn straight from the book.

Very good class. Brother Muhlestein loves what he teaches, which is always refreshing. The cultural insights he provide help cement concepts. The reading quizzes are pretty simple if you read thoroughly. Response papers not hard, but make you think. Tests are of average difficulty, if you really review his powerpoints, you'll do great.

Very good class. Brother Muhlestein loves what he teaches, which is always refreshing. The cultural insights he provide help cement concepts. The reading quizzes are pretty simple if you read thoroughly. Response papers not hard, but make you think. Tests are of average difficulty, if you really review his powerpoints, you'll do great.
This was a great class.  You learn a lot there are 4 response papers that are very easy, and a midterm and final.  If you attend class and study you will do well.

I absolutely loved him!!  He is an amazing teacher who is willing to do anything to help a student truly learn.  He has incredible insights that are unique to most mormons I've yet encountered.  He has a great sense of humour and teaching style.  It was a great semester!!
He taught well.  He was uh a little weird but still made the class interesting for the boring subject matter.  Good guy.

Best teacher I've ever had. He was very kind. I was married half-way through the semester and then got a terrible case of the flu. I rarely attended class and never did my homework. He gave me a an A as a wedding gift! I learned a great deal in his class, merely though his example.

The best, the absolute best!  Love him.  Read, pay attention, take notes, and you can learn.  If you are not getting it, he'll help you get it.  Sees things I have never even thought of.  Amazing stuff!

Bro. Muhlestein is awesome. Random quizzes throughout the semester were a little hard, but if you do the reading you'll be fine, and there's no busy work. He really knows the scriptures well, especially the Bible, so it was cool that he could tie in the Bible with his lectures.

I absolutely loved him! He is an amazing teacher and really helps you understand the Book of Mormon better and helps you learn how to read it to make your reading more effective. His grading is fair and if you study you should be fine.
I absolutely loved him! He is an amazing teacher and really helps you understand the Book of Mormon better and helps you learn how to read it to make your reading more effective.

Professor Muhlestein is the man!  He knows everything about the Book of Mormon, so he gives amazing insights.  He has the funniest sense of humor and always wears awesome ties.  He'll help you out until you actually understand.  Quizzes are easy if you do the reading (which isn't much) and so are the tests if you have common sense and have read.

This is one of the best classes I have ever had.  You will have to learn a lot, but it is fair.  The tests are clear and if you study its okay.  The teacher knows how to teach and cares about us.  He is the best.

Professor Muhlestein is the best I have had yet.  I loved this class and learned a ton.  He loves to kid around and tell the history of the peoples we studied.  His tests are relatively easy if you take notes, read and study.  Have a great time in this class!
I have never had a class I loved more!  Grading is fair, but the amount you learn is obscene, and it is fun.  Everyone should take OT from this teacher!
He is great and the class is unimaginably good.  The tests are a bit tough, but clear, and if you study you will do well!  I love this class, it is my favorite!

This class is ok kind of boring.  You have a quiz every day, but you get half the points for being there.  You have 1 page papers that are easy to do , a midterm and a final.  Go to class and study and you will do good.
Great Old Testament teacher. Not a hard class. Gives in-class quizes, half the points are just for being there in class that day. Useful insights, good man, easy class.

This is the best religion class I have ever had!  You will have to read, but he will help you understand things you never did before!  His depth of knowledge really adds to the class.  His tests are clear, but you have to study for them.  Studying is worth it, you will learn a lot.

I really enjoyed this class. I took it over the summer term and it was a really enjoyable experience. The quizzes can be difficult at times but for our class it was out of 10 points and he gave 5 just for being there. The tests weren't that difficult. I studied for about 2 hours for the final and ended up getting a B on it.

You have to read!  The quizzes aren't too bad.  And the response papers are just annoying to write, but they aren't diffuclt.  The midterm and the final aren't too hard either as long as you go over the powerpoints and pay attention during the lectures.  Get a study group together, and you should be fine.
he's very flexible

Brother Muhlestein really knows what he is teaching.  He provides insights on the Book of Mormon many people, even scholars, overlook. If you go to class and read the assigned chapters each night, the class will be way helpful and relatively easy.  Really nice guy too.  HIGHLY recommended.
This is one of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU so far. I love this teacher, he brought so much depth to the old testament, if you take it, take it from him!

We covered a lot of material, but it was so interesting.  He taught me new ways to read the text and to ask questions.  I looked forward to class every day.  If you study for the test you will do well.  You have to read before you come to class.  This class was great!

mad-awesome!

Great!  I learned a lot!

Prof. Soper is the best. I've taken two of his classes, and they were both great. He is such a fun, engaging, and not-too-serious teacher, but his classes were always interesting and meaningful. Amazing professor. I'm not a huge humanities person, but he taught me a lot about film and pop culture. Assignments aren't too difficult, and he's very flexible on deadlines. 2nd class I've taken w/ him, he's the best. He's hilarious, a great teacher, super compassionate and kind. He doesn't like to use textbooks so he gives short readings then videos. Dr. Soper is one of my favorite professors I have ever had. He's a good teacher, he's funny, and he is really nice.

Dr. Soper is fantastic! He really does understand the student experience. The majority of class work comes from the daily study assignments, a couple papers, and 2 exams. If you have the chance to take a class from him, I would def recommend!! He truly is a gem and a great teacher!! He doesn't surprise you on the tests and makes sure that you are prepared!! Great dude!!

Took this class on a study abroad so I'm sure it was easier than on BYU campus but a super course and not a hard GE if you take it from Dr. Soper. This guy is hilarious and makes lecture super interesting and enjoyable.

Really easy class. Not too much homework and only one midterm and a final that both had study guides with everything on them that you need. Dr. Soper is a comedic genius in my opinion. I loved this class. I am not in the humanities field, but this was the best choice to fulfill my GE credits. Wonderful professor! I learned more in this class than in any other class I've taken! Dr. Soper is AMAZING! He is hilarious and his lectures are fantastic. Instead of a bunch of reading, he assigns videos before class. We even watched Star Wars for one assignment. Dr Soper is great! I would recommend him for any humanities class. He is very clear about what needs to be done and what will be on the tests. Good teacher and tells great stories. Teaches IHUM 202 in an interesting way. Tests were a surprise, be sure to memorize! Overall, the class was great with fun assignments!

Kerry Soper is the greatest thing to ever happen to the Humanities Department at BYU. Soper is GREAT at telling you exactly what you need to know. He really wants you to do well and he makes the class interesting. There's a lot of group discussion that helps students understand the material better. Super chill guy and a chill class. Awesome artist and he's hilarious!

Dr. Soper is an AMAZING professor for this class! He makes the lectures totally enjoyable and plays lots of video and music clips as well as draws his own cartoons to explain concepts sometimes. Kerry Soper is hands down one of the best professors I've had at BYU. I took Western Humanities from him and it became my favorite class. Dr. Soper is easily one of the best professors on campus. The midterm and final are fair. Four papers, a creative project and daily writing warm ups. Plus, Dr. Soper is super funny and a really engaging lecturer.

Dr. Soper is definitely one of the best professors at BYU! He is so funny and genuinely nice but also knows what he's talking about and makes class fun and interesting!! So funny. Such a good class. Best professor ever.

I loved taking Diamonds and Gems with Sister Ross! She seriously cares about her students and designed the class in a way that if you do the work, you'll get an A. Sister Ross is so fun and loves what she does!

Sister Ross is a great teacher. She not only helps academically but spiritually as well. Her lectures are great and she is very engaging. She sets clear expectations and there are lots of opportunity for extra credit. It was a great class and would take again.
Very professional and extremely knowledgeable professor!

Professor Ross is an amazing professor! This class is usually a GE, she understands that and doesn't try to make this your hardest class. She's willing to help with lab homework which is sometimes tricky. Tests are easy if you've gone to class they're open internet/slides/notes/book.
Sis. Ross is a wonderful professor! Tests are not too difficult and lectures and labs are always a good time.
It's an easy GE credit and Sister Ross is chill. Easy reading quizzes. Labs are the most time consuming part.

I loved the class I took with Sister Ross! She genuinely cares about all of her students and is an engaging professor. Professor Ross is amazing! Her class is so engaging and insightful. Her lectures are very interesting, and she is such a caring and kind person. The labs are very hands-on, which is super fun, and the assignments aren't heavy at all. I highly recommend taking this class from Professor Ross!

Sister Ross is a very passionate teacher! She truly loves and cares about what she teaches and strives to share that love with others. Her class is straight forward and easy to receive a good grade in. She offers extra credit and the majority of test and assignments are open note. I would definitely recommend taking a class from her!
Solid teacher! Take GEO105 as your general and you won't be disappointed.

I had a sister Ross for Geology 105, and it was so fun. You don't need the textbooks because almost everything is open-book and internet, except AI. The labs are fun, but you do need to finish them outside of your given lab time, but it did not take very long.
Sister Ross is great! This was a fun class, pretty easy GE

This class was great! Professor Ross is so passionate about this class, and she is aware that most of us are not going into geology, so the class is very easy! Every quiz and test is open internet too!

Sister Ross is the best! She is very understanding and wants all of her students to succeed!! Loved this class!!!! She did a really good job at teaching us about gems and diamonds. She gives a good amount of work, but if you stay on top of it it is just fine!
I really enjoyed this class. Sometimes the labs were challenging but I feel like I learned a lot. I would take this class again.

She was the best professor I've ever had, cares about students, and doesn't just read slides but fully knows everything about gems. Super fun labs, and she made me develop a love and passion for gems and diamonds. Tests are easy and online unproctored, homework is twice a week, but very easy.

The best geology class here! Sister Ross is the most passionate teacher and I really learned so much during lecture and lab! Much of it is so helpful in real life! It's so much fun and there are some great extra credit opportunities! If you need a fun GE to take, take Diamonds and Gems! It's the best! But be prepared for some outside lab work.

Awesome class. Keryn is the nicest most passionate teacher I've had at BYU so far. Lectures were clear and assignments were manageable. All the slides are posted online too, which makes the tests much more relaxed. Tests and finals are all online. You have to try to get a bad grade.

I loved taking this class! The lectures were directly correlated to the readings, quizzes, and tests. There were labs that took a few hours outside of class to complete every couple of weeks, but there was always TA help available.

I really liked Dr. Ross. This is my second class from her, and her courses are always engaging and informative. She does require attendance, but she has a generous policy. The homework load is really doable, and the exams are online
Sister Ross helped us all to understand gems better and was a great teacher. There were assignments every week, but if you pay attention in lecture, they are easy.
Sister Ross is such a good, kind person, and this reflects will in this class. She wanted us to learn a lot, and we did thanks to her teaching! I would absolutely reccomend this class!!!

Sister Ross is one of the best professors at BYU. Her class is fun and engaging even if you don't care about geology. She offers a lot of extra credit options too. This class is amazing. Sister Ross is a great teacher and makes the class so fun and engaging. Labs are so fun and give you a great opportunity to be hands on.

Prof Ross is awesome, I absolutely recommend taking this class. She's funny, energetic, and very passionate about the subject. The labs are lots of fun, and who doesn't want to mess around with diamonds and gemstones all the time?

This professor was caring and made lectures pretty interesting! It was an easy class to fulfill part of the physical science GE, which is helpful. The hardest part about this class was the labs, but the TAs are there to help during office hours.

This class was very easy and I would recommend it for a physical science credit. It did feel more inapplicable than most of my other classes because I will never need to identify gems. But good for a chill class.

She was a very kind and understanding professor. Her lectures were clearly connected to the material on the tests/ labs, making it easy to succeed. She was also very accessible outside of class, making it a flexible class.

The work to learning ratios is perfect for an entry level course. There are plenty of opportunities to make up homework and plenty of attempts on quizzes to get the grades you want. Sister Ross is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about diamonds and gems which makes lectures fun and informative. Would highly recommend this class!

Keryn is fantastic! You can tell she cares about her students and wants them to succeed and love the subject. This class is a great way to pass off half of a GE credit. The labs can be time consuming but I liked the fact that the tests were open book. If you go to class and pay attention, you will succeed. The labs are where the class gets harder, but working with your Ta will help.

Sister Ross is amazing! She goes super in depth about everything you'd need to know, and all the tests and quizes are open note. She has a great attendance policy, and really cares about what she is teaching! Definitelty attend lectures, and make sure you give yourself time to complete your labs.

She was a great teacher. I really enjoyed class. You do have to attend the lectures, but she makes them interesting.
