I would definitely recommend her class!

Attendance is required, but she is so easy to work with. If you are sick you can watch online and things like that. The labs were fun to me, but DEFINITELY go to TA hours for the labs. They are willing to help. The tests are all open note. Low stress and interesting class. Keryn is funny and nice.

She has so many good reviews for a reason. She loves teaching, loves working with students, and loves geology. She is always willing to work with students and help them in the course. Great professor.

Sister ross is very passionate about what she teaches and is very accommodating with technical and physical issues. As long as you do the readings and the labs, as well as pay attention in class, assignments are very easy. All quizzes and tests are open note, and TAs are very helpful with labs and questions. All the tests are open book, note, and internet so if you really just need to fulfill a GE, this is a great option. You have to go to the lectures, but you don't really need to take notes unless you want to take the test faster. Professor Ross is clearly passionate about gemology which shows through her lectures. The labs felt relevant to the reading which helps solidify learning. I felt like she was aware that this course is a GE so while there is a decent amount of homework, the exams are open note, the labs are straightforward, and there is a lot of extra credit.

She is so awesome! Her readings aren't too long and she gives quizes that are open note and you can retake it as many times as you want. So it is really easy to get 100 on every quiz. Exams are open note and are not too bad, they are online not proctered. Labs take a lot of time but are easy to get good grades.
I really enjoyed this class. Interesting and an easy A.
It's a pretty easy class. The labs can be a little annoying but its not bad

I loved taking her class! You can tell she's super passionate about her topics and I learned a ton from her! The coursework isn't difficult and totally doable, you just need to try! I had a lot of fun and enjoyed listening to her every class!

Professor Ross is amazing! Her lectures are so engaging and interesting. I never get bored in her class. Her labs are also super fun, and you learn so much! She is really good at explaining the material, and makes sure you questions are answered clearly.

Sister Ross is amazing! The reading quizzes allow multiple attempts and the everything (even exams) are open note/internet. The labs are time consuming and can be difficult but you can drop one. There are a ton of extra credit opportunities that really can help your grade. Sister Ross is so kind and really wants everyone to succeed.

Sister Ross was great! Her class is really easy. All the reading quizzes allow for multiple attempts and the exams are open-note/internet. The labs can be difficult and time-consuming, but she offers extra credit opportunities that make up for any lab difficulty. She is very passionate about the subject.

This class is very good. I would say that as long as you do the work you will get an amazing grade in this class. The work is very clear, straightforward, and easy. She provides a lot of extra credit and even allows you two drop two labs. The only thing that is more difficult is that you will need to work on labs outside of the lab hour.

This class was easy and fun. Attendance is mandatory, marked online on your own honor. Lectures are recorded and on Zoom. Labs are done mostly outside of class, but graded lightly. I didn't find the labs hard. Tests are open note and open internet, and you can complete them in more than one sitting. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit.

Professor Ross was such a positive teacher that honestly made it so much easier to come to class even when I didn't really want to. Most of the time participating in this class was spent in the lab, but the labs are interesting a fun.... and easy.
Sister Ross is super kind. She keeps the class very simple, good content to learn and makes learning about diamonds and basic gems very interesting. Her class is relaxed and entertaining.
Great Professor. Awesome GE (probably the best GE to take). Interesting material. If you want to challenge yourself you can, if you want to coast by you also can.

Sister Ross was, by far, one of my favorite professors. She's hilarious, lots of fun, kind, and gave me gummy worms on the field trip. You can take the reading quizzes unlimited times and exams are open notes/book. 50 stars! I saved hundreds of dollars on my engagement ring by applying what I learned from her class! TAKE HER CLASS!! You'll love it!
For me, this was a fun and informative GE. Professor (Sister) Ross is passionate about what she teaches and provides lots of opportunities for hands-on experiences in the lab.

Keryn is so kind and it's so obvious that she LOVES what she does! Her passion makes it easy to stay engaged! My only issue with the class is how large it was, it was hard to get questions answered outside of lab which is one day a week.
Sister Ross is awesome! You can tell that she loves her job and loves working with her students. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Labs are fun. Easy A.

She is super enthusiastic about what she's teaching. The labs are fun and not too difficult. There are reading quizzes due before each class. The quizzes aren't difficult or long but you will need to do the reading. Half the semester has heavy reading. Open note, open book for everything! Relaxed fun class, but still productive in learning.

I love how enthusiastic Sister Ross is about diamonds and gems. I took this class for a general and was not very excited to learn about rocks, but she is so excited about the subject, it's contagious.

I love Sister Ross. She is an absolute hoot and is very passionate about what she teaches. If you're looking for an easy GE that will also be interesting to learn, this is the class! There are super high point extra credit opportunities and all the tests are open note. She loves her students and the gospel. Take this class!

I honestly loved this teacher and the class. I would take another class from her again. The only thing that was mildly difficult in this class was the labs. Some TA's grade harder than others and going in to open TA lab hours, they aren't supposed to help you a ton. You can ask one question and that's it.
Keryn is great! She knows what she's talking about, she is reasonable and her grading system is the best. You actually learn about gems, her labs are helpful and her TAs are amazing.

Professor Ross is a very kind, caring teacher that doesn't make her class too difficult. There are lots of extra credit opportunities, and the tests are open note online. This is a great class to take to knock out a GE and learn more about geology, gems, and diamonds.

Sister Ross is one of the most caring professors ever! She genuinely wants everyone in her class to succeed and gives multiple opportunities to increase your grade, especially if certain circumstances force you to miss labs or lectures. She records all of her lectures online and is very accommodating to everyones situations! Definitely recommend!!

I loved the Diamonds and Gems class. Sister Ross was so sweet and excited about the gems which made everything really interesting to learn. She's super understanding and didn't make things harder than they needed to be.
Very easy class for GE credit.

Ross is really good in her lectures but she's fast paced so be ready to take notes quickly and a lot of them. She gives hints about exams so make sure to write down anything she says may be on the exam because you do have open notes on your midterms. Stay on top of the quizzes and attend the classes and you should be fine.

Dr Ross is fantastic at getting you to love geology. If you don't love geology, you will after this class (she has many converts to the major/minor). If you love geology, she is knowledgeable, passionate, and a fair and organized teacher. She brought the Gospel into geology in cool ways and emphasized her specialty, igneous rocks in cool ways too

I love Sister Ross, but if you're looking for an easy A, this is not the one for you. She assigns a lot of reading that you can't skip. TAKE THIS CLASS! Best class I've taken at BYU. Super easy A if you just remember to stay on top of assignments. There is a lot of "busy work", but it's not at all unbearable. Two reading quizzes a week that are both open note and three exams total, all open-note as well. Would recommend to anyone.

Labs every week, lots of extra credit opportunities. Quizzes every week but they're online, so are the exams and they're open note. Sets you up for success, you would have to try to get a bad grade in this class. Don't get the textbooks, you won't use them. Records each lecture, you HAVE to go to lab outside of class to do assignments.

Keryn Ross is very kind and understanding. Her lectures are accessible online in case you need a mental health day or can't make it. Her tests are open notes/slides/internet. Her class slides are posted. Very fun to learn about gems and a great way to get physical science credit.

This class was awesome! Clear lectures and labs with lots of knowledge to remember but also open note/book tests and quizzes. Prof Ross is very understanding and will work with you. Would recommend this class.

Sister Ross is one of the sweetest professors at BYU. She does her best to learn your name and invites you to really get into the material. She does field trips if that's any incentive. Her labs are fun and you get to take home gems! You'll learn a little about chem and religion, so it's pretty well-rounded. Had so much fun! :)

Keryn is incredible. I didn't do great just because I am HORRIBLE at science, but she was an amazing teacher and the labs were really fun and I learned a lot. But, I did spend a lot more time outside of class coming in to work on the labs than I hoped I would, but that's probably just because I'm not very science oriented.
This was one of the best GE class I have taken! I loved the lectures and I loved the labs. Sister Ross is absolutely incredible as well. If you show up and do the work, you will be just fine.
pretty easy class, she's passionate about what she teaches and it's fun to do some of the labs, but the labs can also be tedious

Relatively easy class, but labs can be a time commitment. She recognizes this class shouldn't destroy your GPA and it isn't very hard to get an A. Weekly reading quizzes are super easy with unlimited retakes. Occasional short papers. tests are a little more difficult but they're completely open book and you can open and close it while you work.

I LOVE Sister Ross! Super great class, lots of fun and I learned a ton. Attendance is required, but she does record and broadcast her lectures so you can get credit if you are sick in any way. Not stressful, just fun. Sister Ross makes me want to go out and buy real fancy jewelry haha. I have a much greater appreciation for it.

She was very kind and considerate. She really cared about the material and gave many opportunities to gain points outside of class. There is an extra credit activity that is worth like 4%. She also records and broadcasts all of her lectures so if you have to miss no biggie.
I loved this class, the labs were fun and I feel like i learned a lot.
She has a lot of energy. She likes to follow rules.

I love this class! And I love Sister Ross so much! She has a great passion for geology and almost convinced me to switch over. Before taking Diamonds and Gems, I thought geology was the most boring science of them all. Now I love it! It's so applicable and I loved the opportunities to learn in labs and how interesting the textbooks were. Take it!
I took Gems and Diamonds and loved it! I came in knowing nothing about geology, but it wasn't hard to follow the curriculum. It was an interesting class and Prof Ross is very passionate!

You will have to spend time outside of class in the lab but it's not too bad. She expects you to be in class but is easy to work with if you can't be there. Lectures are always recorded on Zoom and the slides are posted so if you can't be there you can stay caught up. She's funny and loves geology and you can tell that she loves teaching it.

I took this class for my physical science credit and I would recommend it to anyone! Sister Ross is a great professor and the homework amount is very do able. I took this class for my physical science GE and it was honestly the best decision I could have made! Sister Ross is so engaging in her lectures and really makes the class interesting and fun. She is very thoughtful of her students when it comes to how she grades work and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. I highly recommend this class!

I would take this class from her again. The course is lecture heavy and there are reading quizzes before class. However, those reading quizzes really aren't that bad. She does move fast through the lecture, but the slides are available so you can have them open on your own to take notes which is nice. She totally set you up for success on her test!

There is one lab due once a week which is what kept me busy throughout this class and took 1 2 hours out of class to finishThe TAs are super friendly, and are helpful in explaining any questions in the textbook.

Sister Ross gives more opportunities for extra credit than I've ever seen before. If you want to get an A (or higher than 100%) it is possible. The tests are completely open note. Professor ross was a great teacher, the labs were pretty mediocre but attendance was mandatory, she's pretty lenient and you get 3 free absences but also will work around extra emergencies. as long as you go to labs and do the work you'll be totally fine.
She is amazing. Would definitely take this class from her.
Sister Ross is very enthusiastic and passionate about the topics. She does a good job teaching us the material in a fun way. Lectures are just slideshows and are usually recorded on zoom.

This class is fun any easy, the only hard part was the lab. The labs were sometimes difficult but other than that the class was easy. The quizzes and test are all online and open note, book, and internet.

Sister Ross was great! I was never really interested in geology but she made this class so engaging. The labs were super fun and she offers quite a bit of extra credit. Everything is open book/open note, but you still need to know your stuff to get 100% percent on assignments.

She was great. We had work, but not super difficult. The labs took up the most time because you had to do them outside of class. Exams are open-book and open-note. Super fun class and would recommend to anyone!

Sister Ross is an amazing professor! You can tell that she really really loves geology and wants to share her love and wonder. The lectures are fascinating and fun. Such an amazing professor! She gives many opportunities for extra credit and the labs were very fun. Great teacher! Helps you understand all of the work necessary, and the homework is very light. As long as you read, and go to class, you will pass easily!

Keryn Ross is genuinely one of the kindest professors I've had the opportunity to learn from. All her tests are open book and open note so it's super easy! Attendance matters but she gives you plenty of sick days and mental health days so its really not hard at all. The professor is so passionate about her work and the success of her students.

I love Professor Ross! She is very passionate about her teachings and cares a lot for her students. Attendance is not mandatory and you can watch it on Zoom. Midterm and final is on LearningSuite and they are pretty easy since it's open book and open notes
Keryn is a great teacher! You can tell she's super invested in our learning. Definitely recommend.

This class was difficult for a GE credit. I'm in a science major and spent more time outside of class for GEOL 105 than I did for my major classes. Sister Ross is so awesome and so accommodating! The class is actually kind of tough— the labs and readings are time consuming and the really should be more than 3 credits. But it was fun.

Tests are open note and internet so they aren't vary hard. She offers a good amount of extra credit opportunities. Labs are the hardest part, but just take time. Other readings and quizzes are easy because they can be taken multiple times.

Seriously never seen someone that passionate about rocks! She cares a lot about her students and if you do the work, you should be able to get an A. She is so amazing. She is so caring and is passionate about her teaching. The labs can be slightly difficult and are done mostly on your own time out of class. I took it with a bunch of my friends and I loved this class. Highly recommend taking this class.

The professor is very enthusiastic about what she teaches! Honestly, a bit harder and heavier load than I was expecting, but overall a fun class. There isn't enough time in labs to complete assignments, so time outside of class is required to finish them.

She is incredibly kind and understanding! All exams are open book, open slides, open lectures. Not open AI (which is not even helpful anyway) and not open to other people (also not helpful). This professor also offers a ton of extra credit options and one can easily get an A in this class.

Sister Ross is the best and is very passionate and enthusiastic about what she teaches. The lectures are important, and the tests are open-book, which is nice. This class is pretty easy, and the labs are so much fun! I have enjoyed this class so much; the lab hours are a bit annoying though. I normally had classes when the lab was open, so most times I went was after 6pm. I would highly recommend this class and take it again.

Keryn is a great professor, knows a lot about what she teaches, and is very enthusiastic about it as well. Keryn is so enthusiastic about her subject and is a genuinely kind person! Everything is open note, open book, and there are unlimited retakes on quizzes. She is a great teacher. Very knowledgable. There is quite a lot of work as well as a lab but as long as you do the work, you will get an A in the class. Sister Ross is wonderful! She is enthusiastic about her subject but also incredibly patient with her students. She had such a positive learning environment and I learned so much. I loved how she even included scripture references to gems! FANTASTIC extra credit opportunities! Open book tests! I absolutely recommend taking this class with her!

I loved her as a Professor, her energy is infectious! There was a fair amount of reading and work outside of class, especially since the lab time is meant mostly to go over the instructions for the labs, so the labs had to be completed on your own time, but it was so much fun it was worth it!

Sister Ross was amazing! She is very passionate about what she is teaching, and always made the lectures interesting. She also really cares about her students. I loved taking this class and really learned a lot.

Labs were pretty time consuming and could be difficult, but the TA's grade generously! And Sister Ross is so fun and understanding! I had to meet with her 1-1 to get help for a lab one time and she was so helpful and kind. We had an optional/extra credit class field trip to topaz mountain which was an absolute blast. Very hands on class. Loved it!
She's awesome!! Definitely take this instead of physical science. Super fair and doable, but you learn a lot
She's super passionate about geology and her lectures are very enjoyable. The work load is reasonable.
Good Class! labs were tough though, TAs grade nicely though
Took this as a GE and it was chill and not too difficult, but wouldn't recommend if you're just trying to get a GE out of the way.

SO much extra credit! Sister Ross is so kind! I have a disability and didn't know how I could do one of the labs. She met with me 1-on-1 and we figured out how I could complete the lab. Keryn is an amazing professor! Her lectures are entertaining and she is very understanding that unplanned things happen. Lab attendance is required so when you sign up for that date be aware of that. Cares about both her subject and her students. Her passion can help you get excited, even at 9am, and she's always willing to help out students both in and outside of class. Pretty straightforward class, and not too difficult, making it a great choice for physical sciences GE. Professor Ross is awesome. She is very passionate about what she teaches which makes her lectures interesting. She is extremely understanding and wants her students to succeed. Sister Ross is great! I don't care about Geology, but her passion for the subject is infectious. I enjoyed being in class, not so much doing classwork.

She has daily quizzes for credit so just remember to do those. She is often behind on lectures which can make the schedule feel weird or rushed at times. Ask for help on the homework assignments, resources can be difficult to locate.

I loved this class. She is very passionate about what she teaches. It was super easy and there is very little homework. I would definitely recommend taking this class if you need the physical science GE.
Amazing and fun class, tests are super easy

She is very passionate about geology which made it fun to learn about these things. The quizzes and tests are not too hard. She is really nice and always willing to answer questions. She was awesome! All exams and quizzes are open book/notes. Make sure to go to the labs though cause you don't want to get behind on those. Its not too difficult if you go to class, do the quizzes, and assignments. If looking for an easy GE for physical science, take this class. You do have to use the textbooks though, so you'll have to buy them.

This class was a great physical science GE and was not too difficult. Prof. Ross is very understanding and kind, especially around attendance. She loves the material, which helps the lectures to be interesting. The exams were not too difficult either - I just studied the reading quizzes. Sister Ross is a great professor.

This class was really fun. I spent about an hour each week outside of class in the lab, but most of them were not too difficult. As someone who does not like physical science, I still found this class and the labs really interesting. Everything is open note and open internet, and you record your own attendance.

Sister Ross is amazing! She's super laid-back. She also gets that a lot of people take Diamonds and Gems as an easy GE rather than a serious class. Attendance is a little over 3% of the grade. Labs + readings can be somewhat time consuming, but not compared to most science classes, and the material isn't difficult. Was a fun, easy science class.

Sister Ross is fantastic. I took this class not to take physical science, but it was SO worth it. It was literally one of the easiest science classes I've ever taken, and she genuinely cares about you and wants you to learn. Every class is recorded, so you don't have to go, but she's such a sweet lady, and I still showed up. Take this class!

Sister Ross is the best ever! She really cares about her students and geology! Everything including exams are open note, open book, open google! Labs are interesting and sometimes hard but are not graded harshly at all. Definitely recommend!

Sister Ross is an amazing professor! I took this course to fulfill a GE requirement and I'm so glad I did. Attending lectures is part of the grade but Keryn is SO lenient if you miss class for mental/physical health or other important reasons. Some of the labs were somewhat time-consuming so expect to put in a couple hours aside each week for them.
She is a great teacher who cares about her students! I am definitely glad I picked this class!

I thought this was going to be a boring class just to fulfill a GE credit when I signed up. Since the first day, I was proven wrong! Professor Ross is awesome. She loves her students, and loves teaching. Homework took on average about an hour a week or less. This class wasn't hard, but it did take effort to do well. Super engaging class!

I was always engaged and impressed during her lectures. She has an amazing way of explaining new material and concepts. When I reached out to her about needing more help, she created a customized plan to help me succeed. She is enthusiastic and passionate about what she teaches, and caring and understanding toward her students.

This professor is super fun and you can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches. Her class also had a lot of cool labs and a super awesome field trip. I'd highly recommend this class especially since it fulfills a GE credit!

Solid physical credit class. Decent amount of homework, but definitely not overwhelming. Lots of opportunity for extra credit. Attendance required, but she gives you 3 or 4 free days, and you mark attendance yourself on Learning Suite. Reading Quiz every class, but they're easy to find the answers and you can take them as many times as you want.
Keryn Ross was amazing as a professor, she made the class fun yet challenging. The workload was very manageable and the labs were super helpful for the class.

All of the tests are open-book and open-note. She is a professor who genuinely enjoys the subject she teaches. She teaches the hands-on aspects of examining gems and expects students to also be able to master them.
Did a great job teaching lectures, you can tell she has a passion for it and cares about her students. Would definitely take again. I'm not a geology major but I found it really cool and interesting.
Professor Ross is one of the most fun professors I've had at BYU. She's insanely passionate about geology and her energy and enthusiasm is contagious. Would highly recommend!!
She's great and the class is super fun!
This professor was amazing! Sister Ross is so understanding and loves to see her students thrive.

Sister Ross is awesome! I honestly hate science and had no interest in the course material, but Sister Ross made this class one of my favorites this semester. Ross is so incredible and obviously very passionate. Her lectures and labs are engaging and help you learn a lot. there's also so many extra credit opportunities that are really fun to do. she also loves to answer questions and is very easily accessible for anything and her TAs are wonderful.

Super easy class if you just show up and do the work. Two classes plus a lab per week but not a huge workload. Best part is that she lets you have open internet and open book during exams. Literally baller.
Sister Ross is amazing! The labs were sometimes difficult to understand what I was supposed to be doing or how to do it. Practice is essential for the labs.

Sister Ross was such an amazing professor! Her lectures were fun and engaging and she taught information in a way that was really easy to understand and clear. Homework was very manageable, and tests were very straightforward and easy. This class is a really great way to get credit for generals and learn something on the way. I highly recommend it!

She is very nice and enthusiastic. I went to about half the lectures and did fine. You get points for attending, but it isn't a huge amount of the grade. You definitely have to go the the labs, and a few of them are pretty long. Small reading quizzes each week and a few simple assignments. Overall, an enjoyable professor.

She was great professor, who you could tell was super passionate about what she taught! The class was super easy, and all the tests were online and open note. The labs were sometimes a little tricking but manageable.
This class is fairly easy for a general. She's silly and crazy but passionate about what she teaches. Tests were online and you can watch the lectures from zoom.
She was an amazing teacher. She is super passionate about her subject but understands that most of us take the class as a general. Tests are open book!

Professor Ross is amazing! If you are willing to do the work, it is easy to pass the class. The exams are online and open book and open note. There is a lab once a week where participation is mandatory. For a majority of the labs, you will have to go in outside of lab time to complete the assignment. There was a lot of effort required with the labs

Sister Ross is so awesome! She loves what she teaches, and her excitement makes the class enjoyable. It isn't too difficult, but some of the labs are ridiculously hard, and they can take a lot of time depending on the week. Overall, this course is good! It just doesn't cover the entire physical science credit, so be aware of that.
Professor Ross was a queen and helped us feel a passion for gems!
She is really such a great teacher who really cares and it is a pretty easy class!

Sister Ross is amazing and super helpful if you have any follow up questions about the material or an answer on the tests or quizzes. You have to come in on your own time to do labs but, most of them only take about an hour. Find a good TA to help you during lab hours!

Professor Ross has a very great class the lectures feel a little heavy at times because of the amount of information, but she makes them fun and engaging. Labs are mandatory, and you do have to come in on your own time to finish but most did not take a lot of time to complete

I would highly recommend taking this class from her. I have gained a lot more appreciation for gems even though I am a medical major. The lectures are interesting and there isn't too much homework. The best geology teacher, she makes attending lectures fun, and if you read outside of class about the material you will be well informed and better able to do labs, tests, etc.

I absolutely loved Keryn's teaching, she's amazing (she reminds me of Doc Ock from Into the Spiderverse in the best way possible). The class was fascinating and pretty light on readings and homework. Very accommodating for students. We are given many resources to succeed and are allowed to use them on the tests. There's also a lot of opportunities for extra credit that are super fun. If you want an amazing time and a pretty easy A for your physical science credit, take this class.

Professor Ross was a very kind and understanding person. The class was so fun, especially the field trip! Sister Ross is so genuine and the kindest professor I have ever had. She makes class and lab so fun and exciting. There are many opportunities for extra credit and she is constantly looking to help her students get a good grade in her class.

Sister Ross is an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students and is super understanding. Her class isn't too much to handle. Reading quizzes, one project, and 3 exams. She even gives you her personal phone number. Highly recommend.

Keryn Ross is amazing! She is truly passionate about the subject, which helped me enjoy it even more!

Keryn is the sweetest professor I have ever had, she truly cares about her students and loves what she teaches. TAKE THIS CLASS
Professor Ross is so passionate about what she teaches, which makes it enjoyable. She is so willing to work with her students. Do all the extra credit! All tests are open note, book, internet.

Sister Ross is one of the kindest professors I've ever had! She cares about all of her students so much and wants make sure you feel cared about! Professor Ross is awesome, she cares a lot about her students and does a lot to help them succeed. Some of the Labs are really time consuming, defiantly my most time consuming class this semester.

This class was the best! Sister Ross cares about all the students and wants to help you succeed! Highly recommend this class!

Professor Ross was an amazing teacher! You can really tell that she cares about her students and wants them to succeed in her class. 10 out of 10 would recommend taking this class from her.

One of the assignments of his class is to read the Book of Mormon for 30 minutes a day and there are a few essays, but the class is not very hard.

Suuuper passionate, and made me super excited for this class. There is a fair amount of writing but that's really easy to stay on top of. Take the class with Professor Whitehead if you want to feel the Spirit and really enjoy coming to class.

He's really passionate and understanding, but expect to read the scriptures 30 minutes a day, and a list of scriptures to read before class. There is an attendance quiz based off those readings each class, just 1-2 questions. Micro Essays each week, 400 words on what you learned. 3 majors assignments, Midterm, project, final, just a lot of writing.

I really liked Professor Miller! Linear Algebra is a notoriously hard class, but he made sure we were prepared for the exams. He is really good at explaining hard concepts and he is also very kind and respectful to students
Dr. Miller is super great, a very clear lecturer and also very fair and skilled at writing quizzes. I loved his 213 class. He is also a very nice guy and approachable during office hours.
I liked Dr. Miller a lot! Funny and a good lecturer and impressively fast writer on the board. We kind of created inside jokes as a class together which was fun

Very kind, thoughtful, fun professor. He makes class fun and you can tell he cares about each student's success. Patient and respectful with questions. 

Only complaint is that he just wrote on the board so dang fast. I had to choose between copying down notes vs. understanding the lecture, cuz there just wasn't time to do both. 

A goat regardless

Dr. Miller is a fantastic professor. He strives to get to know everyone personally and help each student individually. He teaches very clearly and is always willing to answer any sort of questions. His understanding of linear algebra is very deep and it helps his students to get a deep understanding as well. You need to take this class from him.

Kevin is the goat, definitely one of my favorite professors. He taught this class really well and it's easy to see that he's a super smart guy. He's always open to questions and gives great explanations. It helps that he's a younger professor; it felt like we could relate to him much better. Absolutely will take classes from him again.

This was Kevin's first year at BYU and he was amazing. There were definitely times when his inexperience as a professor showed, but he knows linear algebra well. I did this in the EMC2 Cohort and I'm grateful because I learned a lot more than the other 213 classes, but it was really heavy on homework, but if you stay ahead you'll be ok.

Professor John is by far the best professor I have taken at BYU! His lectures are genuinely hilarious but still teach you a lot. He really cares about making every part of the class valuable and most importantly never wastes students' time!!! The assignments are also actually fun and you can get ahead in the class if you want.
Kevin John is great and so passionate about what he is teaching! The tests are open note and are super easy!
Kevin John is the best professor I have ever had. So interesting and fun. He's awesome

DEFINITELY TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! I wish I could give him more stars; I couldn't recommend him more! You won't regret it. He's the best! (I actually took him for Univ, but I couldn't put that... anyways, he is so great and helped me out tons!!)

Phenomenal professor. I took his ind. study course and it was perfect for me. Each lesson was an entertaining + engaging video lecture (that you can watch on 2x speed), a short quiz (with a retake option), and then a reflection (easy). He also lets you use a notecard for the exams, so it's a fun, easy class where you learn a lot.
Professor John is THE MAN in any class that you take.

Dr. Kevin John is the best professor I've had. He's so empathetic and inclusive to different belief systems which is so refreshing. He truly cares about our mental health and made it a positive, meaningful, and relevant class. One time he could tell we were burnt out, so he told us to use the zoom call time to do something nice for someone. So kind

Such an amazing person. If you want a teacher who really loves his job and cares about his students, this is the professor you want. I also took Comms 411 from him, and it was such a good online class. He teaches things you actually want to know and is very understanding about grading. Prioritizes real understanding and real discussions.
Best professor I've had through BYU.

#1 favorite professor at BYU. Kevin is a passionate, personable, enthusiastic friend who breaks the mold with his teaching style. He is the type of professor who prioritizes you having a meaningful learning experience over meaningless busy work. I have taken 3 different courses from him. He is a Comms professor who is actually good at communicating

Media Effects is the best class I've ever taken at BYU. Period. Kevin does a very good job of teaching the concepts in a way that everyone understands them. Word of advice, the final project/paper is a big one so try to start it as soon as possible. Every Comms student should take this course, as it is very helpful and useful for all the tracks!

Somehow Media Effects was the easiest class I've taken at BYU and perhaps the one where I learned the most. I took it online and still loved the lectures and learned so many applicable things. Dr John is so funny, passionate and personable. I think every comms student should take this class!

I wish I could have Dr. John for all of my COMMS classes! His lectures and discussions are about topics that are interesting and he's respectful of every opinion. He is very real and isn't afraid to discuss "touchy" subjects. He's great at making every student feel listened to and is great at explaining hard topics. One of my fav professors at BYU!

Kevin's lectures are engaging and thought provoking. He cares about his students and invites each to share their perspectives. Homework was just as interesting and engaging. I feel this helped the concepts we learned to really become part of our understanding. This class was simply so amazing and mind-expanding. Take this class!

Dr. John is awesome and I highly recommend taking any classes from him! The class was online and you can go at your own pace, although I would do a module a week. The lectures are great and I learned a lot from them. We covered a lot of different topics and also had (an optional) 30 minutes a week to join a Zoom discussion and talk about the class!

Dr. John is the best in every aspect; as a class professor, an advisor, & a person. He cares deeply about his students, and truly wants the best for them. His teaching methods are super engaging and really fun. As an advisor he goes above & beyond-helping you immensely & wanting you to succeed. Truly an amazing person!

Really fun and easy going professor. I thought the content was interesting but, even if you didn't, it was a very easy class and a really good way to get a COMMS elective. Only one midterm and a final. Only one project that is graded very lightly. Highly recommend.

I've taken a few classes from Kevin at BYU and I can honestly say he is the best professor I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and wants to see us succeed. He understands how stressful college can be and focuses on helping us prepare for the future. I would highly recommend taking a class from him!

Kevin is an INCREDIBLE professor. He knows what he's talking about, but he's great at being able to simplify and explain the material. He made the class so accessible, so you never have to worry that you might be sick one day and suddenly be 3 chapters behind. Kevin also made his office into a "safe space" for his students. 10/10!

Dr. John is a lively lecturer that has a genuine interest in his students. His online courses are very well organized, and he provides clear study guides for exams (midterm + final.) Includes a final project, but students are granted a lot of autonomy regarding the execution. Honestly, why would you take this class from anyone else?

Kevin is one of my favorite professors, I've taken several classes from him. His classes aren't hard, he trusts you to put in the effort on your end to learn the material and doesn't plague you with tests and meaningless busy work. Everyone respects him because you can tell he is an expert in his field and he genuinely wants his students to succeed
I've taken Dr. John every possible chance. Best professor ever. His classes are legitimately what a college learning environment should be like.

Kevin Johns is an awesome instructor! I enjoyed his COMMS 411 Media Effects Class. I took it through BYU Independent Study. He is enthusiastic about what he teaches and makes the lectures fun! He makes himself available for questions or concerns. It's an Independent Study course, so that's saying something! Take this course! You will be glad!
Best professor I've had. He knows his stuff, makes it easy to succeed, and has a great sense of humor. Lectures were never boring.

Super funny guy with really interesting lectures. Honestly, just show up and pay attention and you'll get an A, no problem. He genuinely wants his students to have a good time and understand why the class matters.
I am Groot. (Translation- Good guy, good with kids)

I actually took COMMS 417 in the Spring which is Advertising Research Methods, but that wasn't an option listed in the course code thing. Kevin John is seriously such a cool guy. He won't push you if it isn't something you aren't interested in, but is more than happy to elaborate and teach you more in depth if you are interested. Take his class!

Cutting edge and brilliant! One of the best professors I know. Dr. John genuinely cares about every student and has an open door policy. He has an incredible and lovable energy! He gives a lot of autonomy to the students (so the class is really what you make of it), while providing tons of expertise, mentorship, and insight to the topic. Take him!!

Such an easy class. I put off most of it until the final weeks and I passed with an A. His lectures are interesting and relevant. There is a pretty big research paper/project at the end, but he says himself he doesn't want it written academically. Take this class!

Kevin, or Dr. John if you prefer to be super formal, is the best professor I've ever had. I've had a lot of professors in BYU's communications program and all of them are better than any other professor I've ever had. Kevin even tops them. He's the best of the best. I've taken two classes from him and loved both and learned a lot in both.
BEST PROFESSOR AT BYU BY FAR! I wish Kevin John could teach every single class I have at BYU!

He was a fantastic teacher, and I met with him during his office hours multiple times during the semester. As others have said, no midterm or final, but he made the quizzes harder to make up for that, so make sure you study! Other than that, he is the first professor I felt was a kind of mentor for me.

Professor John is hilarious and really relates to students. I wished that his class had been harder and a little more in depth some times. I took a class from him in the evening, so he often skipped over things to move faster. Overall, he was a funny teacher and the class was an easy A.

This class changed my perspective on communications. I didn't know what to expect going in, but Kevin challenged us to figure out what we were passionate about, and to work toward that. The class ended with a final project, which was a chance for me to deeply explore the things in the class that were interesting. I loved this class!

It's pretty much an easy A, but that's because he wants you to learn on your own. He hates busy work or making us do projects that aren't useful, so I really love that. Quizzes are easy and there were no midterms or final-just a final project. If you're just exploring communications without being serious, he's the guy to take it from.

Absolute legend! Includes memes in his powerpoints, pulls up random cat videos if he gets bored, and presents the material in a fun way. Would take every class from him if I could. Show up to class to take the quizzes, no midterm or final, and a final project that is on whatever you want it to be. Literally

Dr. John is awesome! he really cares about whether or not students are learning from his class. No textbook, midterm, or final. You have a quiz every week instead so make sure to show up. Awesome class, awesome professor.

One of my favorite professors at BYU. He's young and knows what it's like to be a student and thus acts accordingly. Class was super easy, but I learned a ton. Lots of power point slides, but he was a great lecturer, so I was fine with it. He even told us not to bother buying the book

He was the best! Literal quiz question: "Draw a picture of a dinosaur." If you skim readings you will do fine on the quizzes. Lots of powerpoints but loaded with pictures of cats. (he loves them) He's a student himself so he's super chill, "Lowest presentation score was 46......out of 50." He's funny, take 411 from him.
He is the MAN. Seriously an awesome class. He makes the theories and effects fun and interesting. Quizzes are fine, just do the reading.

Great guy, makes the material easy to understand. This section is way easier than others, but keep in mind you won't get the same intro to secondary research (Mintel, etc.) that you would get if you were to take it from Callister. He also helps out a TON with the final project, which is great, but also kind of inhibits you learning skills yourself.

I took 317 and 411 from him this semester and he has been the most down to earth professor I've had at BYU. He's always willing to help and makes the class as easy as he can. He is concerned about you learning the material and grades easy. Take him if you can.

Loved Dr. Kevin John, he is a hero, however, not yet a Doctor. But he is close. But you should take his class. Numbers make my head fuzzy like a storm of boredom. But Kevin was an expert at making it interesting.

Professor John made what would have been a boring class into a subject that was genuinely exciting. He was hilarious, and was willing to help us in and outside of class. If you have the chance to take a class with "Dr. John," DO IT!

Professor Augustine Adams is a skilled and gifted legal educator who cares deeply about the legal profession, about her students, and about ethics and morality.

i've been to 5 different colleges and 2 law schools. kif is one of best profs (top 3) i've had in my life. ever. clear concise. good natured. good personality. she IS available outside class, and i dont think the other criticisms are accurate. you can't please everyone, but she comes damn close.
Good rule/Bad rule

Thank god for Kif! She's been my torts professor during a visiting stint at Boston College Law. She brought clarity to my first year of law school - pretty strict use of socratic method (but with humanity and humor) and extremely clear teacher. Challenging class, but my best class first semester.
One of the best professors I had in law school.  She is one of the most engaging and proficient users of the socratic method.  I learn ALOT in this class.

Kif is a fabulous teacher. I think she uses the socratic method better than any other professor in the law school. Her class is fair (I hear race relations and feminism are super hard, though), and she teaches very thoroughly. Unfortunately, she is heartless if you need help out of class.

I enjoyed the class and love the subject (torts). She was very helpful to my study group. Final was issue-spotting and tested your typing skills. I found that discussions got off-topic at some points and a few students usually dominated the discussions.
Probably my best 1L professor.  Class is interesting.  She asks very detailed questions, but is very friendly, good-natured, and doesn't act condescending.

A capable person, but teaching techniques could be improved.  She has her disciples who are enamoured of her because they have never been exposed to a teaching female with brains.  In turn, she "performs" as a curiosity.
likes to perform for the peanut gallery.
I highly recommend this professor (unless you're looking for the easiest path, as thinking in class is required)
Kif is great.  Anyone who rated her poorly is full of crap, or bitter.  She is brilliant, and recently won a fullbright scholarship.  She's the best professor I had my first year.

This class was pretty easy as far as homework. There was about 3 hours of lectures every week which can be annoying if you get behind. Take good notes and use the TA reviews and you will be fine. I didn't ever use the textbook for studying. The lectures are pretty boring but he cracks jokes every now and then. Average class for a general.

Lots of homework and lectures to watch (but can also just read the textbook and watch review to get an A), hard to contact outside of class but had GREAT TAs that helped. Nice that was online and interesting material.

Don't take this class if you value your education. Canvas said we could opt out of buying the expensive textbook, so I did but they got mad at me. The modules were locked but out of order. He went off topic during lectures a lot, and some of the stuff he said was very concerning. This guy should not be teaching. The TA was the only reason I passed.

Im not interested in Micro Bio so I didnt enjoy the class but if you are interested he probably is a good teacher for it. An 85 is an A so if you put in enough effort on the tests you can get an A. Dont use AI on the essays and youll get a high grade.

I'm the type of person that sucks in online classes so the class was probably harder for me than the average person. That being said, I think that this class is totally doable. I'd attend the TA reviews before the test seeing how it was more guided to the test than the study guide. Do both if you can.

Professor O'Neill is a hilarious professor. He applies situations to real life to help you understand and remember better. I  was never worried about my grade in His class. He counts attendance but not everyday, but still you should show up to most lectures. He takes a lot of time answer any/all questions (good or dumb) from students.

One of the topics for a writing assignment was "The problems with the theory of evolution". Whether or not he wants to 'believe' in something that is strongly scientifically grounded is up to him, but students should not be expected to discount or disprove something that the wider scientific community and literature endorse.

This class was basically just AP biology. The threshold for an A was only 85%, so it was super easy to get a good grade in the class. He's a funny guy, but he would constantly have plugs about abortion and evolution that were not always factual or relevant. I'd recommend the class overall just because of how easy it is.

The easiest class I have ever taken, 95% of the class got an A. The papers and tests are super easy and short. Dr. O' Neill is super nice and he gives out candy at the beginning of every lecture. Attendance was for a grade but the lectures were unhelpful and I never opened the textbook. Just learn from the review slides and you will be fine.

I found this class really difficult; although, I'm pretty sure most don't. Dr. O'Neill is funny and makes things pretty easy to understand. You got a lot of TA's in this class, so make sure to find the good one who can teach tailored to you, some are not great. Really gonna wanna be able to explain everything to someone in detail before a test.

You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches, but he often gets sidetracked during lectures that can be a bit hard to follow. The textbook is also difficult to read, but you do not need it to do well. His testimony is incredibly strong though, and I loved hearing it in class. My suggestion is to use his TAs as much as possible if you can.

Professor O'Neil is high energy and clearly cares a lot about the class. It was fun and exciting and there wasn't much homework. The online assignments and in class TA review prepare you perfectly for the tests. In class information can be dense and a bit sporadic on certain slides, but the tests themselves are on the simple ideas. Would recommend.

Take MMBIO 121 from Dr. O'Neill! His lectures were always incredibly interesting, and he makes difficult topics like cellular respiration easy to understand. It's obvious that he is passionate about both the subject matter and teaching and wants students to be able to walk away feeling like they were able to grow by taking the class.

Professor O'Neill is amazing! The workload was pretty reasonable and the lectures were super engaging. Tests can be difficult at times, but not impossible. His love for others makes class an enjoyable experience. I honestly wish Professor O'Neill could teach all my courses.

Dr. O'Neill was a great teacher. His classes are so interactive and he is a genuinely great guy. The tests are hard, so preparation is necessary. But it is very easy to pass, because of his Irish grading scale.

Professor O'Neill is a super sweet, funny guy that cares a lot about his students. He has to be one of my favorite teachers I have had. The work load is pretty reasonable and though the tests can be difficult, they aren't impossible. As long as you pay attention to the lectures and do the readings, you should be fine.

O'Neill is nice and always makes his students laugh. He has an Irish accent and makes lectures entertaining. His class was easy for me (I enjoy bio) but I know many people struggled. You have to write 3 papers. It was a good class but I felt that it could have been structured better. Often the textbook assignments were not aligned with the lecture.

He has really interesting lectures. I am someone who really struggles to understand science and this was a tough class for me. He assumes a lot of times that we should already know this stuff. I didn't have an opportunity to have any interaction with him as he hands all online stuff to his TA's. Nice guy, but not a fan of teaching style.

Dr. O'Neill is a great professor! One of the misconceptions is that he's a creationist but really what he believes is that evolution was a divinely guided process. He loves immunology so he's great if you want to do something immunology related in the future like myself. He does his best to answer any questions people might have too!

Take this class from him! I took it online, but his in-person lectures are much better, I would recommend in person class. He is finny and has great lectures. A lot of material to cover, but you'll do fine if you take notes and attend exam review sessions. Great class overall, not too hard if you put a little work in every day.

Honestly this guy sucked. Constantly telling you that what you read from the book is b.s. and that evolution is a bunch of nonsense. Not sure how BYU allowed someone who doesn't follow the word of wisdom (he is fat) to teach a class.

ONE OF MY ALL TIME FAVS.I really like his lectures. They are all recorded powerpoint lectures, but he presents them from his Ipad and annotates them as he goes. He interjects a good amount of humor and gospel principles into the lessons too. The tests are difficult but there is enough material in the course that the tests wont hurt you too bad.

He's very passionate about his work and is really funny. I took the class online but would recommend taking it in person. His lectures are much more animated and easy to follow in person than online. The test content was difficult but an A is 85% so it's doable.

This class honestly felt like such a waste of my time and tuition money. O'Neill is a super nice guy, but he crams his pro-life, creationism views down your throat in a science class of all places. I learned little to nothing from this class. Never felt prepared for the exams and lectures are just Powerpoint slides. Great TAs, not great professor.
He's an awesome professor! Makes the subject seem super interesting, and it doesn't hurt that an 85 is an A... but I would 100% take another class from him!

I love Dr. O'neill!! He keeps class interesting, and he only really requires us to know the overall concepts. I'm not a bio major so it was pretty tough for me, but he is very understanding and the tests are the only difficult part of this class. Even then, we had a TA review and class was cancelled the whole week of. He's a real gem.

Class for me was 100% distance learning. Good class, like AP BIO just more in-depth. Prof O'Neill is really kind and inspirational and you can tell he loves what he does. Sometimes it was hard to know what we needed to know for the tests though. That being said, tests for me weren't difficult, I ended up with a 95% in the class with an 85% A cutoff

Prof Oneill is a GEM. I loved him. He's Irish so that was a real motivator to attend his lectures. If you just purchase the online textbook thing, you don't need the book. You can even finish all the learning curves in the trial period (completion). He has 3 writing assignments & three tests. An 80 is an A-. Would recommend bc he's precious :)

Dr. ONeill is such a cool guy. I did pretty bad on all the tests and still ending with an A because of weekly quizzes and other assignments that he gives you specifically to help your grade. Take this class if youre a microbiology major, but be prepared to study to do well on tests.

Professor O'Neill is one of the best professors at BYU! He's smart, funny, and passionate about his subject. His class is *super* hard, though. I'm not a Bio major, so maybe I just didn't get it, but you do really have to work in this class. Tests are really hard, but he's always willing to work with you! Take this class for sure!

Dr. O'Neill is awesome!! He cares about his students. He's willing to help people outside of class, and he is very understanding. He is so funny and that makes lectures not boring. 85% is an A because the tests are rough. Read the book and study what he talked about during class on his powerpoints... but focus on the book. Mondays are quiz days.

Prof O'Neill is a GREAT professor. He really cares about the class material, and explains it in a way that's easier to understand. Whether this class is required for your major or you're taking it for a GE, you can't go wrong with O'Neill.

I enjoyed Dr. O'Neill's teaching style. He puts things in layman's terms and makes an effort to help students get a good grade. The tests were much more difficult than I anticipated. If I were to take it again, I would read all the assigned chapters and attend all the test reviews.

Dr. O'Neill is a nice guy, and his class is pretty easy. An 85% is an A, so as long as you do the work it's not bad. He's funny and likable. The down sides to the class are that it's dull if you don't love biology and the tests are pretty difficult. If you don't mind boring lectures and can study a couple of hours for a test, it's a good GE class.
Excellent

Amazing, amazing professor (and class). I literally made an account on here just to review him. 330 is a concept-heavy class, and Professor Germane does an excellent job of explaining them. He is really aware of struggling students, he made several adjustments throughout the course to help us. Hope to take another class from him before graduating.

This class stressed me out more than any class I've ever taken at BYU (including American Heritage). The project specs are vague, but the tests he runs on them include edge cases and trying to guess what he's thinking is impossible. There are no TAs, and he's not super available to answer questions; the documentation on racket is minimal at best.

I took CS224 from Professor Germane, and in that class, I struggled to understand a lot of the content. I said this in the BYU professor evaluation, and I was scared to later see him as my CS330 professor. But from the first class period, he has done a spectacular job of making sure that we understand. Massive improvement, and a great teacher!

Kimball is definitely one of the top contestants for best cs professor at BYU. Clear grading and very lenient. This class has some challenging labs but you don't have to complete them all to get an A. Very interesting topics. Great, easy cs elective.

Probably my favorite Professor I've had at BYU so far. He took a class with a difficult curriculum and concepts and explained it so that students of all different levels could understand. Plenty of opportunities to ask questions and is always willing to help one on one. Will definitely be looking for other classes to take from him.

He's outstanding. My only regret is that he wasn't teaching 224 when I took it. I had 324 with him in the spring and he's one of the best teachers I've had at BYU. He literally stayed up helping kids with their labs at 11 pm the night they were due. Super committed to the success of his students and very fair with what he asks in HW and on tests.

Fantastic professor and explains concepts really really well. I didn't really take notes in this class but still did fine because he taught lectures so well. I would 100% take from him again. He's also a very fair grader and was willing to dive deep into my code with me to help solve a bug.

Great professor. Very willing to help outside of class. Go to his office hours. This class is hard. To succeed: Read the BOOK before lecture and after to consolidate concepts, work with a friend on the labs. Labs are puzzles. Two midterms and one Final. 5 labs.6 Homework. This class is very time consuming. Without a doubt, take this from Kimball.

Kimball is a great! One of the best CS professors I've had at BYU. He really cares about his students. I was really impressed by his awareness of how well the class was understanding things during lectures. He tries really hard to make sure that everyone is understanding, and if what he is doing isn't working, he will adapt. Take a class from him!

CS 224 is a notoriously difficult class. I had a difficult time with it, but with enough work and help from the professor, I was able to do well. In the past year he's worked through the course material with the other professor, and cleaned it up for us so it's better. He does a great job.

If you're looking for stimulating conversations about the human condition and your place in the world, Kim is hands down the best professor at BYU. If you work, she will make you a poet, regardless of your poetic skills entering class. Understanding, personable, and funny. Take Kim if you're looking for a class on poetry

Kimberly is brilliant. I was weary of taking this class as it was three hours long every Tuesday night, but I enjoyed every minute of it. I would say it was my favorite class, and Kimberly is my favorite professor I've ever had. Highly recommend taking this course from Kimberly if you ever get the chance.

So, so mind-expanding. Left every day with my thoughts about poetry turned upside-down. She's funny and approachable, and her standards are really high, but you'll thank her for taking you seriously enough to call you on your BS.

Kim doesn't usually teach 360, so it was a new experience for her. It showed, but I still felt like I learned a lot about the role of literature in early America. Like others have mentioned, Kim gives a speech on the first day of class about how difficult her class will be. Don't let that scare you away—it's not so bad. I say take her classes!

Kim is excellent (I have taken 2 of her classes so far)! On the first day she talks openly about how difficult the course wil be. She isn't lying. Her classes are hard and she is 100% honest about your writing (which means you will improve a lot). If you aren't looking for an intense, stretching learning experience, please don't take the class.

I struggled with this class. The first day she told us how hard everything would be-I should have listened. Lectures were interesting but hard to take notes on.  She really is a hard grader when it comes to essays.

Kim is incredible! She is by far the most intelligent professor I have had at BYU. Her lectures are stimulating, intriguing and interesting. She makes Shakespeare come to life! Her class is difficult- she is a hard grader but actually teaches you how to become a better writer.  She is very helpful and is generous with time spent with students.

Johnson's class was extremely stimulating.  She is brilliant and doesn't stifle her very scholarly vocabulary which made me feel like I didn't speak English sometimes :) But I learned a lot of new words from her.  The work load is manageable.  The way I look at poetry and write poetry has substantially improved as a result of her class.

I loved this creative writing class. She's serious about helping her students improve as writers. But she doesn't micromanage your style as a writer. Tuesday class consisted of discussing assigned reading (usually less than 20 pages.) and Thursdays we turned in a creative writing piece between 4 lines and a page. Then we workshopped.

Definitely the best professor I had the whole time I was at BYU.  She's tough on grading, but you'll never find a person who's better at their job than her.  Very kind and willing to help.  Fascinating discussions too.
Tough grader on papers, but she is such a fascinating teacher. have her tell stories every so often - you will NEVER be bored. one midterm - not hard at all. just be wary of those papers!
AWESOME, totally recommend her to anyone!!!
take her class
Hip. Smart. Kind. Approachable. And you learn a lot of good, good things.

Very nice professor, but she tries to do way too much in a single semester. About seven different papers, group projects, etc., there were multiple occasions where from start to finish we had less than a week to complete a paper. Definitely do not take this class from Prof. May if you already have a big courseload for the semester.

Professor May is awesome and cares about helping her students. There's a strict attendance policy, but class is often fun because she makes it interactive. Obviously a ton of writing and academic research, but she breaks it up into more manageable chunks. She gives detailed feedback on assignments. More than half of our class ended up with an A.
Very tough grading criteria, and the assignments have very specific and nitpicky instructions. She is not a fair grader. Wouldn't recommend. Don't take this class from her.

Professor May was always very respectful and helpful. I didn't always feel the grading criteria was very clear, but she lets you re-do a lot of the assignments based on her feedback (if you want to). It's a lot of writing, but definitely doable, and she does a great job breaking the final paper into manageable chunks.

Best English/writing professor I have ever had.  Very kind hearted teacher that helped me learn how learn how to write much better, and was willing to give whatever grade you worked for.  I spent a lot of time writing, but it reflected in my grade.

Mrs. May taught the material well and gave very clear grading criteria. She was available outside of class to give feedback/help, and she gave second chances on assignments (although with some additional requirements).

Most humble prof I've had (without being overly self-deprecating or insecure). Solid projects. Criteria for her projects were very clear. Criteria for Department-issued final paper was an absolute mess. (Their fault.) But, she did very well in simplifying criteria and guiding our research. Messed up LearningSuite HW due dates & changed deadlines
She's fine but I might recommend taking the crucial editing class from another professor

Prof Hammari is so kind and wants you to do well. She will answer the same questions over and over until you understand, but she doesn't just let you get away with anything. Do the work and you'll get a good grade. She grades fast and fairly.

This class was great! Dr. Hawkins cares about his students and is incredibly knowledgeable in the area of Latin American politics. Don't expect it to be the easiest class in the world, but do expect to learn a lot!

Good guy, but I wasn't a huge fan of the class. Way too much reading for what we got out of it. The class was built mostly around his own research. The final (20% of the grade) had nearly no information on how to study. Everyone went into it pretty confused. This class was the best example of a "high-minded", ivory tower academic course I've taken.

Both my TA and Professor for Poli 150 have made what could have been an engaging and interesting class into a frustrating drag. They have both been very nitpicky, unclear about their expectations, and kind of patronizing in general. I also am frustrated that they seem to be okay arbitrarily changing the weighting of assignments mid-semester.

One of the worst professors I have taken in the Political Science department. His grading standards are extremely unclear, he is very unforgiving with students, and he changes assignment weights randomly through the semester. He will often criticize student's responses in class in front of students which discourages participation.

I loved Professor Hawkins. This class was incredibly straightforward and I felt like I genuinely learned so much. Utilize the TAs for friday labs, they are so helpful and STUDY for the final. Midterm and final are almost entirely free response, know your definitions and key words.

Professor Hawkins is a very nice guy and a great teacher. He goes on tangents a lot, and his lectures do sometimes feel boring, especially since everything we learn is in the reading, but it's nice to get clarification in class. He posts slides online, and attendance is only mandatory for the TA lab once a week.

He's such a sweet guy. He's more of a research-professor but definitely puts in the work in his lectures. His friday labs are amazing, you get to know the TA's more and are more one-on-one with them. Truly wants students to use the resources BYU offers.

He is good but he is not great. Very average. He gives biased definitions that are incorrect and only useful in this class. Lectures are boring and unnecessary at times. The class wasn't difficult though, so if you need Poli150 he's not a bad option, but there's probably better.

Weekly 1 page essays. If you go to the TA's, they can help you meet the criteria for the essay assignments. Make sure to do the quiz before class. 
Great teacher, he's the goat fr. Very good at involving the class. I really enjoyed his class.

Hilarious guy. I don't remember any problems with his teaching. Timed 20 min short little quizzes on readings (usually about 15-20 pages). Paper due every week, seek help from the TAs on those labs. The midterm and final were not easy, especially for a 100 level class, but I did learn a lot.

Cannot recommend Professor Hawkins enough. He is probably the most entertaining professor I've ever had, and made me fall in love with the politics side of the IR major. He cares about his students and explains this clearly, in an engaging way. There are weekly papers and readings twice a week, but honestly I enjoyed those since they're relevant.

First off, Professor Hawkins is an awesome professor. The guy is absolutely hilarious. The class on the other hand was pretty mid. Lowkey made me change my major from International relations to Econ. Not a hard a class, not an easy one either.

Professor Hawkins is amazing! This was the first class I took for my major, and I really enjoyed it. Although this class is relatively difficult for a GE class, I recommend it. You have reading and quizzes before every class, and lab's due on Fridays so it's pretty work heavy. But as long as you follow the rubric and meet with the TAs, you're good.

Professor Kirk Hawkins is one of the funniest, most intelligent professors that I have ever had at BYU. His humor filled lectures are more effective than most at grabbing my attention. Furthermore Professor Hawkins uses labs to ensure that you understand the content that he is teaching and gives lots of resources if you are struggling.

Professor Hawkins was great! He is super respectful and truly cares about the subject and his students. His lectures were mostly good, it just sometimes took a long time for him to get to the point. Overall highly recommend!

The class is a bit more rigorous than a typical 100 class, but still an amazing class. Prof. Hawkins is a really good lecturer, his lectures were very engaging and I learned a ton. If you pay attention during lectures, do the readings, and meet with the TAs, you will do good in this class. Get help from the TAs on labs!

I really enjoyed this class! The subject matter was interesting! Lab essays every week aren't too difficult, as long as you paid attention in class and did the reading. The midterm/final can be difficult, and count for a large chunk of the final grade though Professor Hawkins/TAs are always willing to help and I would recommend talking to them!

The lectures were amazing. You had to go, and often the same material was covered in the readings, but he was so good at speaking and making it understandable and relatable that I didn't care. There were 10 papers we had to write during the semester, but they were only one page and weren't bad at all.

Beware tests, know the vocabulary.

Honestly, he's a nice guy and gives interesting lectures. That's why he doesn't get a 1. However, his grading on tests and quizzes is pretty ridiculous. You have a quiz due before each class and a lot of the answers are short response, and he will dock you on everything and anything. Really has made me pretty pissed the entire semester.

Professor Hawkins is great, which makes up for the really hard tests. If you take this class, you are probably taking it to learn and not just to pass the course. He teaches the content well and sets you up well for taking other classes in comparative politics.

I don't think it was the professor, so much as it was the class. Poli 358 was the worst class I've ever taken. The amount of DENSE reading of this class and the absolute overload of information was just way too much. I've never had to read so many political papers, and then be quizzed and tested on such specific things. It was awful

Prof. Hawkins is a really intelligent person and an excellent professor. When I compare his class to other 100 level classes, his was a bit more rigourous. . However the grading curriculum is very clear, so if you follow the rubric you can get consistent good scores. I learned a ton in his class and liked it a lot

I loved this class - it was the intro to my major and Dr. Hawkins was so helpful! Even when I got Covid and had to go online, or had a concussion, he really made sure I was given the help I needed. 10/10

Professor Hawkins was great. He was pretty funny and the lectures were very interesting: he knows his stuff and teaches it pretty well. There is a lot of homework, daily quizzes (open book) and textbook reading, along with weekly papers. I feel like he and the TAs really wanted us to succeed and cared about us students.

Professor Hawkins is a great teacher. Really funny and very informative lectures. Attendance and textbook reading are graded, but if you do the work, the class isn't that bad. There are weekly essays about the stuff you are learning. Overall, the class is really interesting and Professor Hawkins makes it fun with his deadpan humor.

Disorganized on LearningSuite, missed a quiz that cost me a decent amount of points on a grade. Did this outside of his normal schedule for posting quizzes. On the off chance you saw the email about it pater that day and got it done before midnight it was no problem. Were not all that lucky. Hawkins makes this class unnecessarily more difficult.

Kirk Hawkins is a treasure. I loved taking 250 from him- the content was really interesting, and the class discussions were fantastic. He's very understanding, I learned some great skills. That said, there is a lot of reading and writing that goes along with this class, so if you have trouble with reading especially consider yourself advised.

Prof. Hawkins is a great teacher. He assigns a lot of readings but you can usually skim them and be fine on the quizzes. He's also very fair about grading, and he'll work with you if you need help with homework. His research is also really well known, so if you're looking to be an RA you should try to get in good with him.

Professor Hawkins is very knowledgeable about the subjects but his lectures are very dry. It is hard to pay attention in class because it is so boring and he just repeats what was in the reading, but you have to go because he does in-class quizzes almost every day. No long papers for the class which is great.

Dr. Hawkins' class was a nightmare. A lot of busy work with unclear expectations and insanely harsh grading. The class was taught by both him and his wife, the latter being much more rigid as a person and as a grader. I'm sure without her in the mix the class wouldn't have been as miserable, but still I would avoid if possible. BYU offers better.

He is really smart, and thus is a tough grader.  You can never really know what is going to be in the midterm or final. This class felt like a 400 level class with lots of tough readings and harshly graded summaries of each reading. He sometimes is funny and is willing to help during his hours. Good luck...

I loved the topic we studied. I learned more in this class than in almost any class I've taken. That being said I spent at least 8 hrs a week on homework for this class and barely got by with a B. If you are passionate about comparative politics and international relations take this class otherwise it might be one to skip over. Tests are killer.

Professor Hawkins is a fun guy, but as a professor isn't very good. For this course at least there are little instructions on the big assignments and even less course objectives for the class as a whole. He grades tediously and to sum him up is what he said to a student, he would grade more harshly/lower the grade if they went to his office.

Professor Hawkins is a great guy that is extremely intelligent. He was a valedictorian at Duke University. The negative is that he thinks everyone thinks like a valedictorian. He is a very tedious grader and marks off points for dumb little things. His tests are hard and I had to study a ton just to get a B.

Professor Hawkins is a really nice guy who is very patient and will give lots of slack. He really knows his stuff and does a fairly good job as a poli sci professor engaging the students. The tests are much harder than the daily quizzes, but you can still get an A if you study. There's lots of simple HW, but it helps you understand the material.
If you need to take this class then do it. Otherwise, find another class where you can actually participate. Lectures are super boring and his exams are harder than they should be.

Oh boy... Great teacher, SUPER difficult class. For someone who's never had experience with politics or government (like me), this class is really challenging. Weekly readings with online quizzes, midterm and final, 15 page final paper, multiple class presentations and lots of assignments that require hours of group work. Really demanding class.

Professor Hawkins is a good guy. You don't really appreciate him until you go to one of the review sessions and realize that his TAs know so little that he is a breath of fresh air. If you do all the readings, follow the Blog paper instructions, and study hard for the midterm and final, the class is an doable A.
