Good teacher. Tough class based mostly on theory. Daily quizzes are tough, as are the tests. Wasn't my favorite teacher, but he's a good guy.

Interesting topics, but daily quizzes will kill your grade if you don't stay up on the reading. Hawkins can be funny, but he sort of mumbled a lot and not all class time was productive. I didn't look forward to going to class.

He's a pretty good teacher, especially for the size of the class. In other reviews, they criticize the TAs for strict grading of quizzes, but quizzes are now self-graded, so that's not as much of a problem. They are very strict on grading tests, however. I do feel like I've learned a lot from the class and would recommend it to other people.

Class was a little hard, but Hawkins is a terrific teacher. Stay on top of everything! The quizzes will kill you before you know it if you ignore the readings.Go to his office, he's VERY willing and helpful. And be warned: the TAs, like most people in positions of power, MUST parasitically feed on the blood of lowly mortals.

I thought this was a great class. A good balance of quantitative and qualitative analysis. He is one of my favorite professors at BYU. Not an easy A, but very much attainable if you stay on top of things.

Pro. Hawk (aka The Hawk) is a pretty funny guy, but he doesnt bother much to talk with students. TA's are the ones you talk to and they can be tough graders for an entry level class. Daily quizzes are given. They are annoying and just lower your grade slowly till you cry if you dont do well on most. Daily readings (needed for quizzes) are 15-20pgs.

Dry humor that can be pretty funny once you get used to it. Must attend class since he usually has an in-class quiz at the beginning of each class. There are only 2 tests, the midterm and the final. The hardest part of the class is that the TA's are harsh graders.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class.There are daily quizzes but the secret to doing well is answering the study questions he gives you while you do the readings.There are also current event questions on the quizzes but they deal mainly with elections and democracy worldwide. The midterm and final are mostly written so be prepared to memorize memorize.

Hawkins was one of my favorite professors. His lectures are always clear and to the point and he always offers help with the assignments. For the readings he provides study guides which are super helpful. If you do what he asks you to, you'll be able to get a good grade.

I liked prof., but class was more difficult than it needed to be. The TAs were rough. Prof. Hawkins tried to say funny things, but he has a very dry sense of humor. This was my major, but this class has me rethinking that choice, just because it was tedious and monotonous. I learned useful things, but not enough to keep me interested in politics.
his TAs are awful. This class is much different than all my previous Political Science classes. His lectures are interesting but seriously his TAs kill the class .

I came in declared a poli sci major, this class killed all of my interest. The TAs are merciless when it comes to grading. There are in-class quizzes so attendance is basically mandatory; in my experience teachers who require attendance do so because their lectures are worthless and if they didn't nobody would show up; this class was no different.

I found him fairly entertaining. I enjoyed his class, but I did have a background of interest in the subject. He certainly didn't destroy it.The TA grading can be a little arbitrary at times, but he allows for appeals. In upper-division classes he is a little business-like and punctilious.

I took two classes from Hawkins this year. If you are a decent, good, or excellent writer, his upper level courses aren't terribly difficult as long as you do the readings and your own research. Hawkins is very approachable. He encourages class participation, so make sure you're always prepared.  Hawkins is a fair grader at the end of the semester.

Professor Hawkins is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. Fresh, smart and helpful. The class has a lot of work, but it all really helped for the midterm and final. Try not to miss class because a lot of what he says is on the final but not in the book or powerpoint. Do the reading because you will ace the quizzes. Very good class.

Hawkins is pretty good and not really hard. his lecture can be a little boring at times but you need to go cause half the time he'll trump the n=book with his own defintions. Quiz's are easy if you do the readings and focus on the study questions for each reading. The test was not very hard at all he tells you exactly what will be on it.

Hawkins is not a powerhouse lecturer. His style can put otherwise excited students to sleep. Be prepared for the tyranny of the TAs. In an attempt to legitimize their own intellectual standing, they grade extremely draconian. Be prepared to memorize a bunch of arbitrary titles of concepts that you already intuitively know. Material feels contrived
Although attendance isn't mandatory, there are daily quizzes that have a big effect on your grade.  A lot of studying is required.

The class is very front loaded with readings and pass/fail summaries- 2/day down to 1/day at the end of the semester. Ask questions to clarify expectations for the 3 papers and the group presentation. He pushes back when students ask question to spur conversation and thought, which is helps to internalize the mass info you'll learn. Solid workload.

Hawkings is a great teacher, always willing to meet with his students.  His quizzes are fair and lead well to the test.  Lectures are great, he's a funny guy. The course is the best planned course i've taken, everything leads to the papers.

Professor Hawkins is a great person and he knows his subject well.  The TAs grade everything, so you should really be trying to live up to all of the five TAs' expectations rather than his.  I learned a lot from the text and a moderate amount from the labs. Daily quizzes were usually fair; I enjoyed attending Kennedy Center lectures for class.
No Comments

Hawkins is a good teacher. You have to do lot of reading, and write simple summaries, plus 3 small papers. The final project is the three papers you've already done. He is super helpful. Choose your topic fast or you'll be behind. If you think this class is hard, change your major to HFL or drop out of college. It's the easiest class I had.

Great teacher.  Learned a lot.  Was very willing to work with you and help you on your capstone.  Grading was fair and not too many assignments to bog you down.  Would definitely recommend him for your capstone.
Great teacher.  Challenging, but never throws any curve balls at you, you know exactly what you'll be tested on.  Great teacher.
Incredible teacher. Takes his students' work seriously and gives a lot of useful feedback.  Great sense of humor.
Professor Hawkins is so sweet (and cute).  His stories about Latin American politics are great.

He is a very intelligent teacher. He is fair with grades. If you keep up on your reading, quizes and tests are simple. He does do group projects but we will have to learn how to work with others in the "real world" anyway. He has clear structured lectures and readings. He does has an enjoyable dry sense of hummor.

Excellent course.  Funny teacher who will help you out whenever.  Skim the readings with provided study questions and quizzes/tests are easy.  For final project pick your mission country to study.  One of the best professors I've had here through 2 years.

I tried taking this class from another professor and it made absolutly no sense.  But Hawkins teaches the material very clearly and has will structured lectures.  There is a big group project so get in a smart group that will work hard.  One of my favorite classes at BYU.
Don't ever take a class with this teacher!!!

Hawkins is cool.  He really cares and is always available if you need help or just want to talk.  Loves the students and class is great.  Really interested in the subject matter, and a really brilliant guy.  Learned my name in a class of 300 kids.  Take him--just choose your group well.
nerdy guy, but sometimes funny and quite easy if you do the readings and pay attention half of the time in class

Don't know how much these other people paid attention, but Prof. Hawkins is the best, hands down. Class discuss. are wonderful, sure there're quizzes and reading, but we're in college now. The class works towards prepping for a final paper, so decide your group & country fast & work hard. Loved it!

Pretty dang lame.  He's a jerk about the class rules.  He makes you do group projects which just end up on one person's shoulders.  He isn't funny but thinks he is.  On the other hand, the tests are pretty easy.  Oh, did I mention DAILY QUIZ.  Need I say more.
An excellent teacher, very helpful with international students.  Patient and funny.  A bit serious, but a very good teacher.  A smart one and very considerate to his students.

Makes an already difficult class impossible. Acts like this is your only class and expects way too much of the class in a normal semester. Avoid his theory class if at all possible. You'll thank me later.

There is a fair amount of reading, like most history classes. Professor Larsen clearly cares about the material and his students. In-class TopHat questions are easy if you keep up with reading. Stay consistent with inquisitive assignments, and you'll be fine. Making up absences is easy. Tests are not difficult and are a smaller part of the grade.

The inverted class structure made lectures feel redundant. Attendance was mandatory, you have to pay an extra thirty five dollar fee for an application (TopHat) that has questions you answer in class and tracks your location so it only works if you are there in the lecture hall. Making up for days you miss or are sick are significantly more work.

He tends to be picky when it comes to written answers. For a general class, he expects a lot more than the usual. We had to memorize a lot of countries just because he thought we should know them. There is a lot of dates and random specific things to memorize. Also, a couple video group projects.

The course itself is structured very well on Canvas, there are just so many quizzes and major essays that break your grade. You can tell he knows what he's talking about and that he really has a passion for the subject, but that doesn't translate to assignments. They are very nit-picky and hyper critical. No extra credit, tons of textbook readings

Expects you to know material to the same depth a historian would. A ton of homework and super hard tests with very specific questions about broad topics. Probably the hardest class I've taken for just a GE credit. If you just need a GE, take a different class.
Not worth the GE credit. Just take it from another teacher

I had a good experience with the class. I liked how it was organized. Taking online helped me to learn everything at my pace. I never did the readings and I was fine. The test were kinda hard, but I didn't think it was anything out of the ordinary. Two 5 page papers, two midterms, and one final were the big assignments. Overall I would recommend.

I liked Dr. Larsen, but I don't think I would take his class again. Multiple times throughout the year he would spend the majority of class on topics that had nothing to do with the course material, then we wouldn't get everything done in lecture. He expects very specific answers to very vague questions. Really nice guy, but not a great teacher.

He is cool and knows history but he expects you to answer questions as he would. Very picky about all essays and ID terms which are on his tests. You need to read about 6 pages of the textbook a day which is a lot. If you want to buy into history and learn this is a course for you. If you just need a GE credit look somewhere else!

The course was well organized but lots of work: 2 five-page essays, weekly quizzes & discussions, 2 midterms (with an essay question each) & a final (with two essay questions). Dr. Larsen is knowledgeable and gives phenomenal video lectures. Warning: there's lots of reading the first month of the course. I enjoyed the flexibility of online.

History minor here. Course has weekly quizzes (some with short answer prompts) and discussion boards. Midterms have 50 MC and 1 essay each. Final has 100 MC and 2 essays. I was drained after taking the final. It was way too much for me. Very straightforward course and I felt like I learned a lot. The material was interesting and Dr. L cares a lot.

I appreciate Professor Larsen's concerns in caring about us, but his class is heavy on reading. I only did pretty well in this class because I contacted the TA for help on quizzes, memorized my essay responses and study terms, and memorized maps at least a week before the exams. I would say be organized and review the material often  to succeed.

While the instructor is helpful and responsive to students, our work never seems good enough. This course has too many assignments, many of which are falsely labeled as short. The unrealistic expectations put on students seem to be devoid of any understanding of the student's life outside of this class alone.

I took HIST 202 online and it was set up extremely organized but very unreasonable. You are required to write 6+ page papers and write an essay as a section on every test with NO notes. Studying was brutal and so time consuming and my grade was never great. 3 quizzes (closed note) and a discussion every week

I spent 9-12 hours a week on homework form this class. There was about 3 quizzes a week,2, 5 page essays, 2 midterms, and a final. He requires that we write 6+ paragraph essays for each midterm and 2 for the final with no notes. He gives us 4-9 possible prompts but only 4 show up on the test so you have to study enough for ALL of them.

One of the best human beings at BYU. Genuinely cares about each student and their wellbeing. Very approachable outside of class. He is passionate about his material. If you can get a spot in one of his classes, DO IT!!!!

Very clear and well put together class. This was online and expectations were laid out explicitly so you know exactly what's going on. Weekly quizzes and discussions and 3 essays (one of which is dropped). Not too hard of a class if you pay attention. I'd recommend him for anyone not looking to kill themselves for GE credit.

The course material itself is not too difficult alone, but Professor Larsen makes it very easy to understand if you a) do the reading, and b) listen in class. He is extremely accommodating, and you can really tell he cares about you as a human way more than as his student. Professor Larsen will go out of his way to help you and is great overall.

This was an online course, so the lectures were videos. However, I really enjoyed the course content and the lectures were super interesting. Prof Larsen has a clearly organized course. The homework quizzes and papers are not bad but there is a lot of reading required. Great class!

Professor Larsen is AMAZING. He does everything he can to help his students understand the content and pass. I had many extenuating circumstances and emergencies and he was so willing to work with me. Keep up with the assignments and readings and everything is pretty straightforward. HIGHLY recommend!!

This was hands down my favorite class I have ever taken at BYU. My class was at 9 in the morning, and I was still excited to get up every day and go. The lectures were all so interesting, and Professor Larsen is so knowledgeable. He is also one of those professors that really cares about his students and wants to help them understand and succeed.

Professor Kirk is a miracle worker. I honestly have hated History classes for most of my life. Not because of the material, but because of the assignments. Professor Kirk sets clear expectations, the format was easy to understand and keep on top of assignments. He was a very generous grader on both tests and papers. Wonderful, engaging lectures.

Professor Larsen was great! Although we weren't in class, he still found a way to connect to his students. It was a lot of reading, but he makes sure it is only stuff that is relevant. He gives good feedback and is willing to help students. He assigns readings and provides videos to give extra insight and clear things up which is very helpful.

Professor Larsen is a great professor and really knows his stuff. I would definitely recommend taking his online class. He makes online much more doable with videos of his summarizing and explaining harder concepts. Very intellectually engaging. Would take again.

Kay. Here's the thing. He's a super good prof. Lectures are very fluid, quizzes are simple if you do the online Q's from Traditions & Encounters (basically copied & pasted),funny on occasion, and asks for tons of reading. I winged a lot and did fine. For tests, ALL material for it is in the syllabus. Mult Choice are the quiz Q's. Tough but good.

He gives very interesting lectures and is great at explaining history's events. His quizzes and papers are also good if you put in a normal amount of effort. However, his tests are brutal hard and require LOTS of studying. Make sure to study weeks ahead but other than that you will certainly learn a lot.

Great teacher with very interesting lectures; however, the tests are brutal hard! The quizzes and papers are fine if you're willing to put in a normal amount of effort but make sure to start studying for the mid-term and final weeks ahead of time!

The man gives perfectly-timed, fluid lectures without a single glance at notes or slides. Every time. His tests are brutal (I spent 5 1/2 hours on the midterm) but you know every possible question from the first day of class. Not much reading, but what was assigned was very interesting. Basically, you should take any class Larsen offers.

Dr. Larsen is incredibly knowledgeable and is a great lecturer. Plan on spending obscene amounts of time preparing for the Midterm and Final, but he gives you the questions in advance, it's just up to you to invest the time. Hard, but a doable A. Would highly recommend him. (Also, you can see his previous ratings under "George Mason University")

Korianne is y favorite professor that I have had so far. She KNOWS HER STUFF. She is truly passionate about this industry and she cares for her students. She creates a safe environment for people to learn in and helps you reach your full potential. She is constructive and never makes you feel like you are not good enough.

MDT students only. Super easy A and lots of extra credit just do the work. She can be really unorganized but that usually won't affect your grade but you may be confused on due dates a lot. It was COVID tho. Class was set up workshop style. Some reading assignments, weekly practice records, random quizzes.

Korianne is one the most genuine instructors I've ever taken. She cares about her students like no other. She will push you to be your very best without ever making you feel like you are not good enough. With constructive criticism, there's a fine line to walk to achieve growth without tearing a person down, and Korianne dances on it effortlessly.

Korianne is amazing. She really loves what she does and loves her students. I felt comfortable working with her. She cares about you and your success as a singer. I never felt pressured for anything and always felt welcomed. She always likes to laugh. I would recommend her to anyone and everyone.

Korianne Orton Johnson is the BEST voice instructor I've ever had!  She is encouraging, en lighting, and I found my own voice through her instruction.  She is a very hard-working and giving individual who truly cares!  I cannot say enough how I've grown! SHE ROCKS!:) I want to be her someday!

She is so amazing! I learned so much from Korianne. She is very nice and absolutely hilarious and loves what she does. We became friends through my voice lessons and I'll never forget the great lessons she taught me! I increased my range significantly and learned how to use my voice effectively. She is a great teacher and a great person.

Prof. Carlston was great! She was really engaging, especially because this course was taught once a week in the evening. We were actually learning helpful things to prepare for what law school might look like. She's very available to help and talk things through until you understand.

She is one of the most thoughtless professors and feels competition with her students  You can score a high on the test and she will disparage you, ignore you and try to cut you down.  Her lectures are long on ego--short on substance.  She ignores legal realities because she could not hack it as a real lawyer.  Totally NOT BYU quality! Total EGO
She's the best. Hands down. Take from her.
Professor Carlston is the best! Everything was simply laid out. Just do all the modules on time and you will do well in the class.

She laid the course out so simply online. This class is one credit and the course load reflects that. The most useful part of the course is the weekly interviews with a different lawyer. Dr. Carlston asks good questions that help the interviewer answer questions students may have. 10/10 would recommend this course and professor.

I had to scroll to see why a student wouldn't give her a 5 star and a 1 star in class difficulty because I can't comprehend why you wouldn't. For a student who is looking to go to law school I found it very insightful. But if you are a rando, then it's the easiest A you'll ever get! + Kris Tina is just the sweetest kindest lady you'll ever meet.

A very immersive class that helped settle some concerns about attending law school. Professor Carlston is witty and informative to all of the class and our questions. Not many assignments, but attendance is mandatory since it is a one-day-a-week type of class. I would recommend taking it for anyone who isn't sure if they want to go to law school.
Each week we got to hear about the different things you can do with a law degree. It was very informative and I looked forward to the lectures.

I took the intro to law class fully online and LOVED it! Professor Carlston is amazing. This class was super easy. Just watch the videos, and the 5 question quiz will be a breeze. I 10/10 recommend this class if you're thinking about law, or even just curious about law.

Attendance required, but always worth it. This class gave me the confidence to pursue a law career I'd thought was out of reach. Hardly any work required outside of class time. Great lectures. Really helpful if you're considering the law. Doesn't push you one way or another, just helps you come to your own conclusion. Take this fun class!

This is a Pass/Fail class. Watch a recorded interview with different attorney each week, contribute to the discussion boards, and write a reflection paper. That's it. Easy class, but invaluable if you're considering a law career. She cares 1000% about her students. Take this and STDEV 365 from her. Thanks to her, I'm now planning to pursue the law.

Dr. Carlston is good at soliciting feedback from the class and I enjoyed taking the law lecture class from her. However, the class was in the evening and was two hours at a time, so it felt like it dragged on a little bit too long. It's pass/fail, with 85% or above being a passing. There was very little that needed to be done outside class.
The class is great as long as you treat the lectures like interesting podcasts and not homework with a deadline. The interviews can be very interested if you go into them excited to learn about Law.

This is the second time I have taken this class, and both semesters were great! Just a simple previously-recorded Zoom lecture to watch every week, a small quiz, and your typical online "post and respond to two of your peers" Canvas discussion each week. Kris Tina always does a good job with the interviews and pulls out interesting aspects of law.
Took STDEV 170 online and it was awesome. Great for people who want to go into medicine but don't know exactly what.
I took STDEV 170 online so didn't really talk with the professor too much but the class was awesome. Definitely recommend if you want to go into medicine but don't know exactly what.

A great option for anyone who needs an extra credit to keep their scholarship (which was me lol). Some of the interviews were really interesting! You learn about the different jobs within the legal field and that's about it.

Professor Carlston is amazing! She's super nice, funny, and her lectures are very engaging. The only textbook you need is a book you read at the beginning of the semester. Other than that the rest of the assignments are case briefs and memos. Attendance is worth a big chunk of your grade so make sure not to miss class! Overall, loved her class.

Super easy 1 credit class. I have absolutely no interest in going into law but just needed one more credit this semester. I actually ended up really enjoying the class and I learned a ton about different law professions! Highly recommend whether you are actually interested in going into law or just need one credit.

Perfect amount of work for a one credit class. Also a great class if you're debating pursuing law school or not. Helped me a lot in my decision. Professor Carlston's goal is just to get you to understand what it's like to have a career in law, so the class is just set up to help you succeed, in school and in life. Definitely take this.

The class is bare-bones and effective; Prof. Carlston literally conducts a zoom interview of a different lawyer each week, has you take a brief quiz to make sure you paid attention, and assigns two short subjective papers. She is strict on late assignments so be sure to turn things in well in advance.

KrisTina is literally the best. She is super on top of responding to email questions outside of class and I feel like STDEV 365 was very helpful for getting a better feel for how law school actually operates. The assignments are not diffcult and I still felt like I learned a ton. Really fun and very enlightening, I always recommend her classes.

She spent a solid 10 minutes describing the plot of Toby McGuire's Spiderman. Overall, great class! It's taught by a few other PPA advisors as well, so you get a lot of perspectives that are fully informed and accurate. 100% recommend this class, I feel like I'm gonna get into med school now. :))

She is very nice! Her law class is very helpful in learning about law school and how to prepare and study for law school exams. It's not really in depth but gives a good overall view of the first year of law school. Like a crash course. She is more than willing to talk after class and in her office hours too.

This is the easiest A of my college career. I loved hearing from the different lawyers. KrisTina would frequently ask the questions I was thinking. At times the lawyers would get a little beige. She is SUPER bubbly and very willing to help you. She has experience in the field and knows a thing or two.

This class consists of various lawyers talking about their work experience and how they got there. I found it interesting and enjoyed the various POVs we got. The attendance quiz can stay open during the lectures (if you are taking this online then watch them at 2x speed). The papers are easy and I learned a lot.

This was an awesome class, if I wasn't graduating I would take this class over and over. It was very intellectually stimulating and thought provoking each week to watch the videos and learn from different lawyers. This class helped give me the confidence to make my decision regarding law school. Loved the class and loved KrisTina!

What an amazing class and professor. She is so knowledgable and clearly loves all of her students. This class honestly proved to me that I want to be a lawyer and work in government. Take this class from her if you are wondering what a law career is like!

This class made me want to be a lawyer, before I took it I was on the fence about it. If you are looking for an easy class that will help you decide the question, "Do I want to go into law? Yes or no." then take this class. It's only an hour a week and maybe a paper every other week.
A lecture-based classs. Totally a waste of time if you were not interested in law school.

Super awesome lecture series. I don't know if I want to do law, but I loved hearing from the people who came in every week. This was an on-demand online class, so it was super chill. And the assignments were super easy as long as you watch the lectures. Professor Carlston is really helpful too, and you can call her if you have any questions.

This class was one of the easiest and most interesting ones. Class had very few assignments and if there was they were easyyy. Attendance matters but the class is once a week so it's not hard. I am not interested in law but I like hearing about these topics and I needed a credit so this would be a good choice for anyone looking for an easy class

I would only take her class again cause it was an easy A. Just walk in and play on your phone for an hour. I found a few of the speakers to be lacking in actual knowledge of being a lawyer. One was an apple store employee lol. I learned a thing or two but it was not great. If you want an A or just a breather between classes this is perfect for you.

Kris Tina is a little disorganized. She tries to make sure that everyone is involved and tries to get students to question there own opinions. Because she wants everyone to participate, she moderates the discussions in class and will change the subject if she doesn't like the direction it is going. She tries to be fair in doing so.
Fun class to learn more about law, Super Easy A. Grade is almost entirely based on attendance. Class structure is that every week you get to hear from different people in the Law field.

This class is great if you are interested in the world of law. All you have to do is show up and do iclicker quizzes (you have to be on time to class). She gives a lot of extra credit and the work that is required is fairly easy. Great class for a filler if you need more credits but is only 1 credit.

I love Professor Carlston! I took three of her classes this semester and absolutely loved her. She makes her classes fun and engaging. STDEV261 was a little heavier on the reading, but it was all super interesting if you want to learn more about the law. Her other classes, 168 and 260, are mostly attendance based. My favorite teacher at BYU!

This class is ridiculously easy. Show up and you pass. It's super helpful for students considering a law career. The guest lecturers give you a clear picture of what different law schools and different law careers entail.

Easy A, it's a 1 credit course. A great window into many different types of law; you should take this if law school is on your mind. If you decide on law school, Prof. Carlston is awesome about helping you out. She helped me make a plan, and told me about an internship opportunity that I'll be doing next semester now. Super helpful.

Kris Tina is great. This class is so easy. No joke. Just show up every time and write a paper at the end and you will get an A. Plus she is an awesome teacher. You really learn a lot from her classes. I would want everyone to take this class and professor.

Attendance graded by iClicker. Two click ins, so don't be late/skip. Two papers one for final, just do them and you pass. You have to ask a question in class that you then have to write a paragraph about. Kinda sucks though, because there are always those jerks who ask a million questions every class.

I've taken every available class from Kris Tina, and she is the best. I'm way in to all of the legal stuff, but she teaches everything in a down to earth manner that I think could make the subject interesting to anyone. Super easy to pass as long as you attend.

Lots of extra credit and all you really have to do is attend. There are a couple papers/assignments, but they're short and infrequent.  The lectures are interesting and the speakers she finds do target many areas of the law. She does not make exceptions for any sort of emergency, so do make arrangements and be prepared. It's worth taking.

Doctor Carlston is a nice person but I had a really hard time understanding in her class. There are no prerequisites listed but the terminology and issues were all way over my head. The class is "easy" because she makes it that way. It got me to think, but it was not clearly organized and I didn't learn as much as I hoped to.

Super interesting class that gives you a really wide exposure to attorneys from every field. This is the easiest A you will ever get at BYU. Take this class--really interesting, super easy, and gives you great insight into the life of a lawyer. Don't miss class. If you talk to Kris Tina during her office hours, she can give you great pointers.

If you do not get an A you need to drop out of school. You attend class and turn it assignments periodically and you get an A. Also this might have been one of the coolest classes ever. If you have any interest in the law YOU NEED TO TAKE THIS CLASS!

Professor Carlston is a great teacher. She seems to really care about her students and wants them to succeed. She has a lot of background knowledge on law, and even though I'm not planning on going to law school, I still greatly enjoyed her class.

Kris Tina is a wonderful teacher. I disagree with the student who commented that you needed background knowledge to succeed in this course. I have taken 3 courses from this professor and have enjoyed each one. You simply have to complete assignments and meet the requirements outlined and you will get an A.

I've taken 3 classes from Prof Carlston now (including Legal Lectures and Constitutional Research), and they've had fair grading policies and required no legal background. I guess if you have no background in college-level reading or writing, you could have an issue. Still, I think the previous commenter may have had a singularly bad experience.

Dont take this class if you havent been exposed to the law world before. This class has no requirements stated. Believe me you need requirements to get everything in class. I thought this class was a getting-to-know class and learn the most before going to law school but no! You can expect much confusion if you have no previous knowledge of law

I love Professor Betts! This was a super chill class with lots of fun assignments and lectures! As part of the class you get to volunteer in the elementary schools which is also really fun. If you are considering majoring in Elementary Education, take this class from her!!

Professor Betts is the sweetest. She genuinely knows what she's talking about and ensures there is active engagement during lectures. The fieldwork is perfect for seeing whether you'd like to teach kids, and her advice on good teacher qualities helped even more with that exploration.

Professor Betts is great. This is a great class to take if you're trying to figure out whether or not to do Elementary Education as a major, mostly because part of the class is volunteering in elementary schools once a week! To be honest lectures were pretty boring and weren't very often about what it's like to be a teacher. But overall good class!

The class felt a little disorganized. We did a lot of group projects and  presentations back to back which got really repetitive. It was often a little unclear what she was expecting of us on assignments. Other than that her class was pretty fun!

She is the most caring professor and has genuine love for the students. It was fairly easy and guaranteed A. Loved that classroom experience was required. She has a lot of experience and knowledge and brings in people who also do.

Work load is fairly light, only a couple of major assignments. Professor Betts is very sweet and she is very passionate about what she does! If you go to the classes and do the work it is almost a guaranteed A.

Professor Betts is super nice, but I don't feel as if I learned much from taking this class. It only occurred once a week and she cancelled it several times. I was excited to learn about education, and we really only drilled a few topics over and over. Super easy A, and it was fun to volunteer in classrooms, but I wish we went over more topics.

She deducts points for reasons that don't seem relevant to the story. Complained my teen character didn't sound "adult" (it was a YA piece). She clearly has a bias against fantasy. She also has a weird beef with Grammarly. Even though the class is "Fiction", we just read literary fiction. We're only allowed to write short stories.
not very understanding. shared personal political views in a way that made me feel uncomfortable in class.

I'm glad I took this class from Professor Chandler. She was really helpful and caring, and clearly wanted every student to succeed. There was a lot of reading, but most of the material was fairly short, and there weren't daily reading assignments, which was nice. She did have us handwrite a lot (at least a page, basically every day).

Prof Chandler is kind and caring, which ultimately made her a good professor. When the semester gets tough, she's very understanding and patient. There are tough papers, but this is a writing class so I expected that. I felt that she graded fairly.

I really liked Professor Chandler. For this class, you write a picture book, a MG short story/novel chapter, a YA short story/novel chapter, and a fourth project of your choice from one of the other three categories. She's respectful and helpful, with optional meetings during class time. She cares but also gives real feedback on your writing.

She's very nice and the class isn't difficult, but I often found her feedback vague or confusing. I don't feel like it helped my writing as much as other professors I've had. She seemed tired, so maybe this was just an off semester for her.

Professor chandler was an excellent writing professor. She was always clear what she was grading on, although occasionally I was left wanting a bit more final feedback to explain my grade. All in all a great professor with lots of relevant experience.
Professor Chandler is really friendly and easy to work with. She gives plenty of time and preparation to complete papers, but the papers are still taxing.

This is for 318. Prof Chandler was very particular when grading which made writing frustrating. It got to a point where I didn't trust her with my work because it felt like she didn't care about it and just wanted me to write in her preferred genre. She is a nice lady but not a good teacher. I got an A but wouldn't take another class from her.

Professor Chandler is a very nice person but she grades very toughly. The writing assignment directions are fairly vague but then she is very particular about what is turned in. She definitely prefers contemporary pieces over anything fantasy which was a little annoying. I didn't feel like she care to make me a better writer

Prof Chandler is an inspiring professor who adequately teaches you the fundamentals of creative writing. I learned so much about the creative process with her as my professor. She gives excellent feedback and creates amazing discussions to have in class. I loved her and this course dearly; I highly recommend taking it!

She is the best! The papers can sometimes be confusing and hard to write, but she is always willing to help you. She regularly pushed due dates back when she knew we already had a lot going on. I learned so much from this class!

This is for ENGL 318R! Easy reading quizzes. Nice person but can give harsh feedback. We only wrote 4 short stories the entire semester. Also, she really wanted us to go on a walk with her at Provo River (like, what?). Doesn't value opinions that don't align with hers. At the end of the semester, I feel worse about my writing. Avoid her if you can.

I loved English 218 with Professor Chandler. She gave such good feedback and it was so easy for me to improve my assignments based on her response. I looked forward to this class every day, and was so excited to attend. 10/10 would take again.

I learned a lot in this class. She might be one of the tougher graders but most of the people in my class got an A. She cares a lot about her students and is willing to work with them!! I feel like I improved as a writer.

Professor Chandler is absolutely amazing, but she does not make WRTG150 the cakewalk that it's considered to be. If you're looking for learning and actually improving your writing, take it from her. If you're looking to coast, look elsewhere. She grades papers subjectively.

A very encouraging freshman class. Gives good feedback on papers, but you MUST do well on the 3 papers to get a good grade. discusses with the class a lot which is cool to talk about and hear new ideas. encouraging, pushes your limits of writing, lots of group work, overall a solid choice for a writing class!

Professor Chandler is kind as far as English professors go, and her grading criteria is clear. However, she is one of the toughest graders I've ever had. She grades honestly, so you have to do well on the three papers. Make sure to run your papers by the TA before turning them in.

Chandler is nice but I did not vibe with her or this class. She felt superficial and hard to connect to. Class was so boring and pointless, I felt like banging my head on the wall each class period. I could've put more effort into papers but still I think her grading was subjective. She wasn't a tough grader though. Easy class, didn't do readings.
Sister Chandler is the MOST caring professor I have ever had. She truly wants you to succeed and as a mostly freshman class, it can be very encouraging for your first semester. 10/10 recommend

Prof. Chandler was enjoyable in class - she allowed students to be a part of the discussion and contribute. She is skilled with contemporary YA, but if you are interested in writing other genres (like fantasy), this professor is not for you. Her grading criteria is vague and not up for discussion, and she is more like an editor than a teacher.

Like all writing 150 classes, your grade is really based of three papers. We also had to do some mini essays, but if anything, those essays helped. I absolutely loved coming to this class first thing each morning. She wants you to succeed so participate and MEET WITH HER FOR YOUR PAPERS. Doing so saved my grade and a lot of stress. 10/10 recommend

Prof. Chandler is very sweet and is always willing to meet with students. The class is mainly based on 3 papers and the final. Make sure to brush up on your grammar bc she doesn't really go over it and it can hurt you on the final. Meet with her to go over all your papers before they're due. It's the only way you'll get an A. 93 is an A. No EC.

Please take WRTG150 from Kristen. She is truly amazing. She is so helpful, I emailed her all the time about my thesis/outlines essays and she always answered me and has made me such a better writer. She often brings candy and she is super nice. She pushed back a lot of our due dates; she really genuinely cares for her students.

Kristen is THE BEST!! It's obvious that she really cares about her students. She wants us to succeed in her class and in life. The 3 papers are tough but if you just do the things she suggests during revisions, she gives you a good score. Take it from her!!

Professor Chandler cares so much about her students. Discussions in class are good, and help with your papers. 3 papers are your main grades, and she helps you revise so that you can get a good grade. Up to 3% extra credit, and she lets you rewrite one of the papers at the end of the semester for a better grade! She's awesome, but a tough grader!

Dr. Bromely is super funny and talented! I was hoping for slightly higher level guitar instruction, but the class is basically just jamming for an hour twice a week, which is still fun. She does make you buy her guitar method books which is a little bit annoying because they are kind of pricey and you probably won't use them after the class.
Great class. It was a lot of fun and she makes sure grades aren't stressful.

Easy class, showing up is literally 90% of your grade, she doesn't care about grades but rather making sure you learn. I had absolutley no guitar experience going in and now can play most songs coming out, she is amazing! She also has the coolest testimony ever
Professor Bromley is so much fun! Class time was enjoyable and I learned a ton. Books are somewhat expensive but worth it.
Easy class. I knew a little bit of guitar before the class but I learned a lot! She is so chill and funny.
Incredible teacher. Willing to work with her students. Very engaging and funny. Knows her stuff. She let me make up many classes that I had to miss because of work:)

Prof Bromley is AMAZING! Very accessible and accommodating. Her focus is us learning the guitar and doesn't hold students to any crazy standards. Super easy A if you show up and play. She truly wants us to enjoy the guitar. I loved her stories and the pace of the class was great. I would recommend this class to everyone!

Attendance is most of your grade, but its a fun class to attend. You submit a weekly practice log (2 hours outside class each week) and the midterms/final are small group performances in class. The pacing is perfect and its a great chance to get better at finger picking, bar chords, reading notes, performing, etc. Dr. Bromley is the best!

This is a solid class. You show up and play guitar. Sometimes you do group projects which are in place of class. The teacher is awesome and talented and the homework is just practicing guitar. If you enjoy practicing this guitar or if you need two credits, take this class :)

Professor Bromley is the greatest ever! She is so funny and just wants everyone to learn the guitar! She is incredibly talented as well! I learned so much! On the first day she made it clear that the grade should not get in the way, but that she wanted us to focus on learning the guitar... As a result, she hands out extra credit like water!

Dr. Bromley is such a chill teacher, but actually so good. This class is very easy, if you have even a little bit of guitar knowledge you should take it. It's an easy A, but I learned a lot about guitar and had fun doing it. I also got to jam with other musicians! Great way to fill up your schedule if you need more credits for scholarships

Dr. Cook is really kind and caring for each of her students. Her lectures are often long-winded, but she really knows her stuff and likes to teach further in depth than what is required (but it won't necessarily be tested on). Get to know the TAs, take good notes, do the extra credit, and review the slides before exams, and you'll be just fine!

Dr. Cook's class is not that hard if you study and do the extra credit. She's a great teacher and gives a lot of extra credit assignments, so getting an A is not hard at all. She tells you explicitly what she tests on and even specific things that'll be on the test. The classes and lab are long, so it might be hard to keep it up all year, though.

Amazing professor! She is so caring and just wants you to succeed in her class and life. She makes an effort to know you personally, makes the class fun, and gives massive extra credit. Easy to get an A+ if you put in a little bit of work. Felt like AP Bio. They make sure to have awesome TA's. If you can handle the night class it is so worth it.

she was great but it felt like the coursework was being adjusted frequently. i personally enjoyed listening to her TA more, but maybe its a matter of peference. do all the extra credits (helped with getting an A), study well before exams. TAs r very helpful

Dr. Cook was an amazing professor! She cares so much about students and know how stressed everyone is and is always willing to work with you. She gives out so much extra credit and as long as you stay on top of lab homeworks and do make up work for your lab quizzes, it's not too bad. Would definitely take again.

She was an amazing teacher, fun, and also knew the material really well. She would have some crashouts on some days when she would be in a mood. But a minor inconvenience, a ton of extra credit, and a relatively light workload.

Dr. Cook has lots of knowledge and experience that are perfect for anybody in an entry level biology class. Sometimes grading criteria are unsettling but she gives a lot of grace. Eager to answer questions and interact with students. Very caring and passionate about what she's teaching.

She was never really there and all of the learning I got from the classes was only from the TAs (who constantly had to work overtime). Her teaching style was really scattered and she would put out a bunch of information at once on the whiteboard and then erase it before I could fully absorb it.

Dr. Cook is great! She lectures well but do know her 3hr lecture blocks can be pretty brutal sometimes. Dr. Cook absolutely cares about her students and wants them all to succeed. Lots of extra credit opportunities! TAs were great as well. All round a wonderful professor, long labs & lectures were worth it to take it from her.

The first unit is pretty heavy, and the labs are ridiculous but besides that, this class was such a blast, thanks to Dr. Cook.
 Dr. Cook is the most caring professor I have ever met; she wants nothing more than for her students to succeed, and is so understanding. I adore that woman. All I gotta say is DO THE EXTRA CREDIT.

Professor Cook is intelligent and passionate. EASY A. She is a great lecturer, but her three-hour night lectures are killer. The three-hour lab is the worst part of this class. You could easily get these done in 30 minutes. They feel like preschool classes and are a waste of time. The TAs are amazing, but the curriculum for the lab is ridiculous.

Professor Cook is probably the most understanding professor on campus. She knows that grades matter and gives her students every opportunity to do well in her class. Lectures are interesting and if you go to her test reviews, you'll do well on the tests. Lots of extra credit opportunities! Bio 130 is a tough class, but she makes it easy to succeed!

Dr. Cook is an awesome teacher. She clearly wants her students to understand the material, but she also understands that grades are important to most students. She provides tons of extra credit opportunities.The class is lecture heavy, but the lectures keep you engaged most of the time. I mean, its impossible to be engaged for the entire 3 hours...

Dr. Cook is an outstanding professor who offers many opportunities to strengthen your grade through extra credit. The lab inspires those who want to pursue a path in biology further. TAs are helpful and give the best advice on what slides to look over to be test-ready. Good intro class! The lecture is a great place to multi-task! Great person!

I really enjoyed Dr. Cook's class. I felt that she was very energetic and passionate about the material she was teaching in Bio 130. I felt that the lab portion of the class was the hardest aspect, particularly the quizzes that we had to take on the previous weeks lab material. Dr. Cook is super willing to help you out and tests are easier.

Dr Cook is a great teacher who cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I recommend this class to anyone looking to take biology. The three hour lectures are kinda rough sometimes, but they're worth it in order to take the class from her.

I highly recommend this professor! She goes through lectures fast, but there aren't any surprise questions on the test and she has reviews to prepare you. She is so passionate about the content and makes it far more interesting because she wants to apply it to our everyday lives. There is also TONS of extra credit.

If you need to take biology, definitely take it from her! She cares about all of her students and gives ample opportunities for them to succeed (so much extra credit!). The tests are in the testing center, but the final is just in class. She is super understanding, and you can email her about anything. I have already suggested the class to friends.

Dr. Cook is one of the sweetest and kindest professors I've had. She really cares about her students and their success and will do everything to help you succeed in her class. She is so passionate about Biology that it makes it fun. Her tests are very fair and she doesn't try to trick you. 3 hour lecture can get long but would recommend it from her
She is one of the best professors I have ever had! Get ready to work hard but honestly, she is incredible. ABSOLUTELY take it from her!!!!

One of the best teachers. She gives a lot of extra credit, her tests are extremely fair (if half the class misses something she takes it out), and just overall so kind. I agree with others that the lab didn't really help with learning the material. Lectures did.

Dr Cook is very caring and her class was really good. She offers a TON of extra credit and as long as you go to lecture, reviews, and study you will do fine on the exams. There is some busy work but I thought it was interesting. The one thing I struggled with is the lab portion (3h a week) and it never actually helped me understand the concepts.
She is an incredible professor and person. She really wants to inspire students and help them understand. 100 % would recommend.

This is the hardest first-level biology class but Dr. Cook made it easy. She spends a lot of time in her office hours going over the concepts and simply explaining them. The extra credit opportunities were sooo helpful. It is an interesting class and I learned a lot.

One of the best professors I've had. I had a lot of personal situations during the semester I took her class, but she was always super accommodating and didn't make me feel guilty for needing extra time on assignments or exams. You can tell she loves teaching the class and wants her students to do well.

I had a hard semester. Lots of family emergencies. Dr. Cook was only more than accommodating. I highly recommend her. She's a fair grader. Her tests are fair as well. Labs are mandatory. They can be boring at times (especially if you have already taken BIO100), but just go to them and relax. Study. Do your due diligence. And you will get an A.

I don't care what all the bad reviews say. Professor Cook was one of the BEST teachers I have ever had. Her tests are easy if you actually studied for it, and provides lots of resources to help study. Plus, she has plenty of extra credit opportunities.TA's are great as well. If you are struggling with a topic, she will be more than happy to help.

I liked Prof Cook a lot! She does a lot more than most professors to help you out. Her goal is to eventually rewrite the BIO 130 curriculum, but she needs a few years experience teaching it before she can do that. As a result, the lecture is admittedly a bit of a mess, because she's trying to see what works. I still recommend the class though!

Only good thing is there's extra credit opportunities. This class is awful because of its structure. Lectures are long and overstuffed. Tests are insanely hard. Concepts are only briefly covered in class. Lab book is horribly written; unclear, and clearly has an agenda, especially towards the end of the semester. Cook is nice, but class is awful.

Professor Cook is an angel and will do whatever she can to help a student if she sees they are trying. She does a great job at explaining the material although those 3 hr classes can seem real long. She offers up to 8% extra credit and her tests are pretty straightforward. She is very easy to get in contact with and is a gem.

I took this class my first semester of Freshman year and I was really nervous at first. Doctor Cook made this class a blast. She was caring and her love for biology is so evident. Her tests are straighforward, especially if you go to her reviews! She also gives a lot of extra credit. Take this class from her!

Kristin was amazing. She cares a lot about her students and really gives you every opportunity to succeed. She has several in-person review sessions prior to exams (attend these!) and lots of extra credit is offered. She posts her lecture slides after class (use to study). I bought the textbook but did not use it once. 100% recommend this course!

Ciarah is a sweetheart. She cares about her students, and she understands that not every student is a bio-major. She provides ample extra credit opportunities. The homework load is manageable. The tests are easy IF you attend the test reviews. She explains complicated concepts clearly and is accessible outside of class.
She is more understanding of student problems. Very considerate and always makes time to explain the material for better understanding.

Ciarah seems to really care about teaching the class. There are professors that just go through the motions each semester and only update their slides every 5 years, but she actively engages in teaching Bio and makes sure that everyone gets it. There will be light papers each week, but they're super easy. Show up and pay attention and youll do fine

Ciarah is a really nice person and you can tell she cares a lot about her students, but this class was pretty difficult for a 100 level class. There were writing assignments, quizzes, and other homework due each week. Lectures were interesting but they often felt rushed, leaving me very confused when it was time for a test.

Great Teacher- many assignments and papers due, but they are easy if you come to class or do the readings. You don't need to have a lot of Bio knowledge to pass the class- she explains everything super clearly and holds reviews before exams. She's super liberal with extra credit too!!

This was an INSANELY HARD class for being level 100. In class you briefly discuss things and then the tests are intense and seem impossible. Each week there are essays, quizzes, and homework packets due.

Ciarah is the best science teacher I've ever had. She always makes time for her students and really wants to succeed. We had fun and spiritual assignments in class and easy homework outside of class. Go to all of her reviews!!! She basically gives you all the test questions and answers in the reviews. She is amazing! Take this class!!!

She is always willing to make time for her students, and thoroughly teaches everything on the tests, which were almost all take-home. They are also a combination of short-answer and multiple choice. She really cares about her students walking away having learned a lot and developed their worldview. I really enjoyed her class. Take it if you can!

She's caring and fun, and goes out of her way to get to know students individually. Most tests were take-home and open book. Don't buy the text book. She only assigns one reading the whole semester and I just checked the book out at the library for that. She sometimes goes through her lecture slides kind of fast, but that's my only complaint.

She's amazing, take her WRTG 150 class! Her workload is very manageable and the lectures and in-class discussions are really enlightening. She's very compassionate with student workloads as well. She's great!

Cannot recommend her enough! You can tell she cares about her students and their success. I was worried about writing a ton of essays, but her focus is more on the quality of your writing than the quantity and she walks you through the skills she teaches and helps you apply them! The readings aren't too much and assignments aren't too hard.
Professor Jolley is the best! She always is in an uplifting mood and her positive energy is contagious! She is easy to work, and if your papers meet the grading criteria she is a good grader.

Professor Jolley is amazing! She is so kind, good at what she does, and cares about you and is always willing to help. The best teacher I have had at BYU. Readings due before class which were all online, around 2-3 things you have to read and comment on, pretty easy, just say your opinion and you'll get a good grade. Papers take time but not bad.
Very clear grading criteria, and oftentimes a very merciful grader. Is not the best at writing feedback in LearningSuite, but is happy to provide specific feedback if asked.

Dr. Matthews is awesome! She's really funny and is willing to work with students if you need an extension, extra credit, etc. I took English 203 from her and I would recommend it if you're looking for a very manageable course that will teach you a lot.
Class was pretty chill if you keep up on the readings, and Dr. Matthews is super sweet and really cares about her students and about what she's teaching.

Dr KLM is super awesome! She's a quirky lady who really cares about her students. Most of the class was framed around BIPOC authors which made the class discussions interesting, since the vast majority of the class was white lol The homework was easy. The tests required you to write a lot of essays, so make sure to read.

Dr. Matthews is amazing. Really cares about her students and builds relationships with them. This class (African American Lit) is hard to do online with a mostly white student body, but Dr. Matthews is so good at helping people unlearn harmful systems. She helps students feel heard without allowing harmful or prejudiced comments to go unchecked.

She's nice but she wasn't a good fit for me, and neither was her class. Took African American Contemporary lit. But not one person in that class was Black. The discussions felt fake because no one ever, ever disagreed. It was like a class of the Emperor's new clothes. She might be better in a different class though. Nice person.

This is a class on feminism, just so you know! You read a lot and then class is all discussion on the reading. If you don't like class discussions this might not be the class for you. Dr. Matthews is very nice and funny, yet I don't agree with everything that is taught. Some very opinionated people are always in class so it can get negative.

Professor Matthews makes American Literature fun. Her lectures are more like discussions, and she is engaging, funny, very smart, and a fair grader. Midterms and final consist of multiple short essays on the reading material. You have to read the material to get a good grade, but an A is definitely attainable.

Professor Matthews is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. She is well-aware that this class is taken for GE credit by her students so she tries to make it as interesting as possible. Her lectures are worth coming to class for and the readings she assigns are totally doable and super interesting. Take this class!

I loved taking ENGL235 from Dr. Matthews. She's actually so funny and makes you think about the readings and how the themes relate to today. There were 2 or 3 midterms, 4 response papers, and the final. She takes attendance but I definitely skipped a lot of classes because its really not necessary if you know a lot about the readings.

Kristin is the most genuine, caring, and kind professor I've had at BYU. She assigns interesting, worthwhile reading and leads substantial discussions. Her class isn't just "academic" is has intersections with real life. She's really approachable and accessible in office hours, generous with grading, and wants everyone to succeed. 10/10 recommend

Dr. Matthews is super hilarious and very approachable.  If you enjoy American History, English, and having discussions about them, take this class!  Coursework includes lots of readings (ranging from a few poems to short stories and lengthier pieces), four essays, 2 midterms, notebook checks, and the final.

LOVE Dr. Matthews. She learns everyone's names and I feel like she knows me. Go to her office hours with any questions because she is very approachable. The class is discussion heavy, which I love about it, but if that's not interesting to you, maybe it's not the right fit. Class time is more interesting if you come prepared with the reading done.

Dr. Matthews is the kind of professor that I inspire to be. If you put in real effort to her class - attend all lectures, complete all assignments, really use her suggestions in your papers and try to contribute in a meaningful way - you will leave her class a stronger writer and thinker. This is not an "easy" class, but it is worth it.

Dr. Matthews is incredible. I came out of her woman's lit class with a new perspective and new skills of analysis and discussion on this subject. Discussion-based class sessions on various readings (essays and novels throughout the semester). A midterm, a paper, and a big project as a final. Fabulous class. Dr. Matthews is an incredible person.

Dr. Matthews is incredible! I have never had a professor more engaging intellectually stimulating!  She grades harshly, but don't let that steer you away.  She is always willing to help students and grades harshly as a teaching tool to help us become better writers.  Dr. Matthews is passionate about American Studies.

Dr. Matthews is tough, but it was worth it. There is a LOT of reading, two tests, and and three papers which she grades hard on. Class is mostly discussion, and Dr. Matthews chooses excellent texts, although her outside readings are a little dry and difficult to get through. Take her class, but expect to work very hard for an A.

I've had several classes from her and I have nothing negative to say about her. She is really concerned about her students and wants to get to know us and make sure that we are enjoying the class as much as she does. Her classes are hard, but doable and WORTH IT. You will learn a lot and grow a lot in her class.
Awesome awesome teacher.  Very friendly, relates well with students and creates a great environment for learning.  I will definitely take another class from her.

She is a very capable professor and knows her stuff.  A hard grader, but fair.  She gives great feedback on papers and is definitely invested in her students.  She uses a LOT of outside material which sometimes draws away from studying the actual LITERATURE, but it's interesting nonetheless.

I love Dr. Matthews! Though she can be a somewhat hard grader on your papers, she gives you plenty of suggestions and comments and returns things back quickly. She also is very prepared for class and keeps a discussion going the whole time. There is a lot of material, but the class goes by so quickly!

She is a really a great teacher! She keeps the discussion interesting even when the subject matter isn't. She has a great sense of humour too. I would recommend anyone to take a class from her. She gives a lot of helpful feedback on papers which shows how much she cares about her students. I will definitely take another class from her.

Great class! Professor Matthews is really a great teacher. She cares about her students and that they do well. Grades fairly. She really wants to help out. Sometimes class can get a little monotonous, but overall she keeps it fun and entertaining. She is really great. I reccomend taking a class from her for sure!

Dr. Matthews is awesome! She's fun and makes the discussions interesting. She obviously cares about her students and is always available when you need help. This class was challenging but very worth it. I came away with a greater appreciation of the things we studied, and an ability to research papers effectively.

Dr. Matthews is an amazing teacher. I actually learned how to write much better in this class and she was constantly available for help with writing. It's not that hard to do well in her class as long as you do your part and there are many opportunities to do that. She's very down to earth and a fun teacher overall.

She is a way good professor. She has an awesome way of teaching that keeps things clear and interesting, and she's down to earth so her advice is useful and she's not condescending. I really want to take a class from her again!

Trust me on this one.  You will not regret taking any class from Dr. Matthews.  Possibly the best teacher at BYU...I've had a lot and she is out of this world.  If you don't love literature, sign up for one of her courses and you soon will.
I LOVED her class! She is a crazy genius with amazing clothes! Good shoes too... But mostly she is a wonderful teacher. I am considering failling her class so I can take it again.
Professor Matthew's class was my favorite at BYU this semester.

She is really good at making you think about your topic.  She helps you try to make a good argument and makes you feel good about your essay.  You get plenty of time to do your essay and you get a lot of help to perfect it.  I recommend this class.

She is brilliant.  Without a doubt, one of the best teachers at BYU.  She is honest, real, and intelligent.  It is refreshing to have a teacher who is relatable and realistic.  BYU should invest in more professors like Dr. Matthews.
She gave great feedback on writing samples and worked to keep us interested in the class.
I enjoyed Prof. Matthews class for many reasons, but mostly because she was interesting, brilliant, and chose good literature to study.  The reading load was pretty heavy, but doable.

She is great!  Very approachable and understanding about personal circumstances.  Don't be afraid to talk to her.  The lit she has you read is extremely interesting.  At times class discussion lagged because of unclear prompts from her, but overall a superb class.  I would definitely recommend it!
She has really great discussions and she'll get you thinking. She's also very approachable about papers and theories about the class.
She made American lit not only interesting but fun.  I really enjoyed her and her class--take 293 from her if you get a chance!
Professor Matthews is the best thing that has ever happened to BYU. Not only is she beautiful, but she knows everything there is to know about literature, and explains it in a clear and helpful way.

Honestly the best professor I've ever had in my life. I actually MISSED going to her classes! She's brilliant, funny, and understanding of every situation. I beg of you to take from her if you have the chance!! If you pay attention in class and participate then you are good to go!

One of my favorite professors that I've ever had in the department.  The class consists of a lot of discussion and isn't too hard if you pay attention.  Tests are primarily an essay question and a few short answers.  Not too bad.
excellent

I don't really understand of the negative reviews.  I enjoyed the class, I would actually look forward to the class discussions.  It was the best class I took this semester.  The reading is not hard at all, and she basically gives you an automatic 100% on the papers and assignments just for effort.
It is an amazing class and she does a good job teaching it.  There is a lot required in a short amount of time (as a block class), but she'll give extra credit.  Just stay on top of things.

This class is ridiculous.  I am extremely interested in the subject and she ruined it for me.  She shows no mercy for any extenuating circumstances, makes you write pointless papers, and assigns enough reading for a 4 credit class.  It is not hard, just stupid.  Take it from someone else!!!
This class was life changing for me. Kristy is extremely inspirational, and made me care and love a class I had no interest in at all.  If you need to take this class take it from Kristy!

She was AWFUL!! She never gave direct answers to any conceptual question. She never gave feedback on anything. TONS of reading and a ridiculous reading quiz at the end of the semester to be sure you read. Spent maybe the last two weeks talking about teaching implications. The rest was all talking about racism and how we are all ****.
run away as fast as you can

No Comments
Prof Rimmasch cares about her course content and her students. If you pay attention to her lectures and study the material you are practically guaranteed to enjoy the class and get a good grade.

The class isn't easy but Professor Rimmasch IS easy going and WILL prepare you with all the informtion you'll need, if you put in your part. Is there extra credit? Yes. It's super easy and saved my grade. I don't know of a single person more knowledgeable about the humannites other than Prof. Rimmasch. Makes for super intriguing lectures.

Dr. Rimmasch is super passionate and kind. I took IHUM 201 and 202 from her at the same time. I was a little scared at first because I am an international student, and music and arts were new to me, but she helped me a lot with this. I wish I could take all my classes from her.

Prof. Rimmasch is so kind and caring! The lectures were very interesting and the tests manageable. A short 1 pg paper almost every week and textbook reading heavy but for a 1 class a week it was very manageable. Enjoyed this class sooo much and she takes time to get to know her students! Also so passionate about what she teaches!

Dr. Rimmasch is super passionate and kind. She always lets you know exactly what she is testing on.  Majority of tests are on Art and Music identification, which are easy points. The other test questions are very straightforward and she will never try to trick you on the test. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Short Papers about every week.
Love this professor! Super supportive even if you aren't doing too well in the class! Super kind and invested in your learning and wants you to do well! I'd take classes again just for the professor!

I absolutely love Professor Rimmasch!! Intelligent, understanding, caring, the list could go on. 
Reasonable workload, which was very manageable even over a spring term. There are frequent writing assignments, but in my opinion, they were very easy if you are a practiced writer. Lots of memorization as well, but similarly very doable if you study.

This professor was really good and has tons of extra credit! Her writing assignments were sometimes confusing, but if you go to class you would be fine. There are 3 tests worth a huge chunk of your grade. Study after each class and you should be okay!

Professor Rimmasch was super chill. Honestly, the class wasn't difficult as long as you do the readings. Plus she gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit. 
She's very caring and is always asking how you're doing. I'm not really one for the arts, but I kinda liked it because she was so passionate about what she was teaching.

incredible! She structures the class so the beginning of the semester is more reading heavy/harder content and later it's more chill. She also provides a lot of extra credit at the beginning as well to balance it out. The tests include a lot of content but she gives you all the resources to do well. Makes the content really engaging.

Professor Rimmasch is amazing! Her class is well-structured with weekly papers and tests, but she genuinely cares about her students. Unstuckstudy was super helpful for preparing. Definitely worth taking!

Professor Rimmasch teaches by far the best humanities classes at BYU, ideal for majors or general requirements. The workload is manageable compared to others. If you don't overload your schedule, you'll succeed. Show up, take notes, and do the extra credit—you'll do great! I'm taking her 202 class because she's awesome to work with.

Professor Rimmasch is great! She is a really great professor and knows her stuff. She can answer and question you come to her with and is very easy to contact if you have any questions.

There is a decent amount of homework and the tests are hard, but if you participate and attend the lectures, she covers everything you need in class.

I loved her Western Humanities class. The way she taught made me interested in visiting Greece, Rome, Istanbul to name a few places. There is a manageable amount of work and the extra credit she offers boosts your grade a ton.

Professor Rimmasch is awesome. She really gets everyone involved in the lectures and keeps things interesting. She always prepared us well for the tests and I gained a lot from her class. You will need to come to class prepared to take notes and spend time outside of class writing analyses, but it isn't impossible to get an A.

She is very passionate about the subject she teaches. She is also very personable and I felt like I had a relationship with her just from being in her class. The class was 1/week in the SLC center. There was a small paper due every week before class, which was then talked about in class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would recommend it.

Professor Rimmasch is incredible! I would love to take every class from her if I could. Her syllabus is very clear and grading expectations are very accessible. She genuinely cares about her students. She knew my name within the first class and major things going on in my life throughout the semester. This class is worth the time and money!

Class attendance is necessary to succeed. There are 3 tests total but no comprehensive final. The tests are very hard but study hard and you will do well. There are also weekly readings and papers on the reading but lightly grade. Professor Rimmasch is very kind and cares deeply about each of her students and will help anyone 1on1 when requested.

She's an amazing professor and she cares for her students and how they do in her class! She has a deep passion for the arts and humanities, and she brings that passion to class! Her enthusiasm makes the learning process enjoyable and engaging! She is willing to help you wherever you're at and is very supportive!

She is amazing. Simple studying of terms and a little paper to write each week. She is super understanding as well and sets you up to do well on tests! I love her class and would absolutely retake it!!

She is HER. One easy response paper due each week and then 3 tests in total. Tests are a bit harder but mostly because of the amount of material there is. But for how stupid and difficult GEs are at BYU, this one is extremely reasonable and well structured. Rimmasch is kind, thoughtful, and is a great prof. Would highly recommend.

I would highly recommend taking a class with Professor Rimmasch. Although the tests were pretty difficult, she made her expectations clear and attainable. Her lectures were enjoyable, but be ready to participate in class quite a bit. You can tell that she is really passionate about what she teaches and she's a kind person. Overall great Professor!

Great professor that is passionate about the subject. She took the time to know all of us by name. Her tests are long and very specific, but she provides you with all the resources necessary to know everything. PowerPoint slides on Learning Suite, etc. It was a great GE class to take once a week at the salt lake center!

Sister Rimmasch is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. She is caring and does all that she can so that her students can succeed. She sets very clear expectations for the class on day 1 and provides all the necessary resources to do well in the class. If you come to class, take notes and study, then you will do very well.

Professor Rimmasch is passionate about humanities and really cares for her students. She is the nicest person ever. She offered extra credit for filling out our study guides, which saved my grade! Tests are very detailed on things that we talk about in class. Fill out the study guide while she talks as your notes and memorize ALL the music and art!
