My program isn't at all related to Humanities so I took this class for credit fulfillment at the Salt Lake Center in the Summer. If I knew I would like it so much, I might have taken it anyways. Prof. Rimmasch is really passionate about what she teaches and genuinely cares that you learn the material. Lots of it, but it's interesting and enjoyable.

Professor Rimmasch is the best professor at BYU. She really cares about you as her student and will do anything and everything she can to make sure that you succeed in the class. In order to be successful you need to go to class and soak in all the info that you go over in class and study it. She will also reward effort.

Professor Rimmasch is one of the best, if not the best professor at BYU. She really cares about you as her student and will do anything and everything she can to make sure that you succeed in the class. In order to be successful you need to go to class and soak in all the info that you go over in class and study it. She will also reward effort.

Professor Rimmasch is an excellent teacher. She is very passionate about humanities and draws you into her point of view where history and culture come to life. I honestly was not looking forward to this class but it became one of my favorite classes of the semester. She makes studying for the tests very straightforward. Loved this class!

I didn't even know what humanities was before I took this class, but Professor Rimmasch made it one of my favorite classes that I have taken at BYU. I took this class at the Salt Lake Center so it was only once a week and each lecture was super interesting and went by way fast. The only homework we had was writing a paper and some reading.

Professor Rimmasch who puts a lot of time into each lesson and wants each student to succeed. I took 201 and 202 because of how much I was able to learn. It is one of the tougher classes I've taken at BYU and requires a lot of work outside of class to succeed.

Professor Rimmasch is a WONDERFUL teacher who really cares about her students' success and learning. I took IHUM 201 and IHUM 202 concurrently from her. Here is the bottom line: Professor Rimmasch gives you everything you need to be successful in this course, but whether or not you are successful is based on how much effort you put into studying.
I enjoyed her class more than I thought I would. This course is extremely organized and easy to follow. But be ready to memorize a lot of things like paintings and historical styles.

Professor Rimmasch is amazing, I would 100% take her again! She cares for her students and structures the class so you can succeed. Tests are strictly on lecture + alot of info, make sure you go to class. Papers are easy, 7/10 or more for doing it, make sure you know the material for class discussion bc she will call on you. Read just for papers.

Take this class from Professor Rimmasch! She teaches clearly, her assignments are straight forward, and you learn a lot. She loves what she teaches, which really got me to appreciate art more. Just do the little assignments, participate in class, and take good notes, and you'll do well in the class. (Bonus: IHUM 202 counts for two GenEd credits)

Professor Rimmasch is a great teacher! Her passion for humanities makes the content very interesting. There is a lot of reading, but it's manageable and mostly interesting. Attendance is mandatory, and all the test questions come from class. The assignments/papers are easy and short . Just follow the rubrics. Take Professor Rimmasch for IHUM 202!

This class wasn't hard by any means, just need to grind on exam weeks. Really know the art and music. I got a 95. I never read the textbook really, nor the stories, I would just kind of skim them and write the papers. Just make sure you get 10s on all the papers and you can average like 87s on the exams and get an A. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT PAPER.

I liked Dr. Rimmasch. Her tests were memorization-heavy, but it's not the end of the world if you don't do as well on the test. She gives plenty of opportunities to participate and be engaged in the class. Assignments are regular but mostly graded on completion. I would recommend her for Humanities 201 :)

She was the worst teacher I ever met. I took the first midterm in the Spring and it was the hardest test ever and you were given like an hour to complete a 3 hour test. She was not accommodating or helpful. I failed the first test and was forced to withdrawal b/c there was no time given and she would not let me retake it for any reason. Horrible.

You need to attend lectures and take very good notes to be successful in this class. Tests are quite specific, but not cumulative, so you can really improve each test. Take good notes, study hard, and participate in class and you'll be fine. Class content is somewhat interesting even if you aren't super interested in art. Good class overall.

Professor Rimmasch is an amazing teacher who cares for her students. You still have to show up to class and do some work to get a good grade. There are 3 exams, weekly 1-2 page papers, and ALL of the info on the test comes from class so pay attention! You can get an A if you pay attention, study, and participate in class!

Professor Rimmasch is a gem to have at BYU. I took IHUM 201 and 202 from her, both online. Her classes are very manageable if you do the homework and go to class. She says what's on the test in lectures. Humanities classes can be a hassle, but her passion makes class engaging. Take these GE classes from Prof Rimmasch if you can. You'll love it!

I'm not going to lower my rating because this class was difficult. She is kind, supportive, and passionate about the class. Outside of the tests, everything is an easy completion grade. Tests (3, never comprehensive) are hard, but if you take good notes (!!!) and study hard you can do well. Test material is all from the lectures.

Tests are VERY specific and worth 70% of grade. She is a very nice lady, but the tests are to you to require the most minute of details from class--who said which quote, even when it wasn't in the reading. She tells you in class that the historical background is for understanding , not the test, but then tests on that info. Not an easy gen ed..

I'm still in the class and I just took the first test. It is pretty ridiculous for a general. Way too much information is expected to be memorized. It has been straightforward so far but the amount of reading that you need to do is stupid. The tests cover an insane amount of material, and it is way over the top. Would not recommend it.

I've had Professor Rimmasch for both IHUM 201 and 202, and she was excellent in both! You do have to memorize a lot for her tests, but that's the case w/ all of the IHUM classes. Make sure to take good notes (she lets you take pics of her slides), use Quizlet, and do the response papers. Readings can help, but you are only tested on her lectures.

Professor Rimmasch is incredible! You'll have to memorize A TON to get an A. But getting an A will be in your control. There are 1-page (double spaced) papers due once a week. But you get full credit as long as your papers had 3 quotes and are free from grammatical errors. I'm so happy I took this class from Rimmasch though. 10/10 recommend.

This was one of the hardest classes I've taken so far at BYU. It is difficult to know what will be on the tests because you cover so much material and the questions are very specific. There are also readings each week, and especially toward the beginning of the semester they are very long and very difficult to understand. It's a tough class!

She's the most amazing professor I've had at BYU. She's passionate about the class and makes it interesting (even if you don't like history). She's willing to help and work with students. There are several short papers (1-2 pages double spaced) on the reading. However, they are easy to do if you do the reading.

Holy cow bruh why don't you just call this an art history class. You'll need to memorize a a hundred terms per test, each of which are over 20 percent of your grade. She doesn't give you the presentations and if you miss a slide its over for that. She sounds passionate about the material but doesn't help to remember the facts. Weekly Papers too.

Professor Rimmasch is so passionate about the humanities and makes her classes so enjoyable! The grading criteria for papers is very straightforward and if you listen to the lectures, you'll be prepared for the exams. She is the perfect professor for anyone who doesn't have an appreciation for the humanities--she'll change your mind!

Professor Rimmasch is seriously the best professor I've had. I hated history before I took her class, but she explains things in an interesting way and keeps everyone involved. We had eight short reading response papers to right, but they are super easy to write if you do the reading.
Sister Rimmasch is an amazing teacher. She presents the information you need to know for tests, in class. Didn't think i'd like this class, but i was dead wrong. Really awesome!
great course. makes you really work for your grade! good material

Actual difficulty would be a 4, but she's SO good at teaching that it should be a 2 or 3. I put 4 because you DO need to put in effort to read and write. Everything is so organized and her expectations are clear. Tests are hard, but class average was an A- because, again, she taught everything so well. She loves what she teaches and is just so nice

Professor Rimmasch is amazing. She cares about her students, is clear in what she expects, and tells you exactly what you need to know for the tests. The final is just like the other two midterms (noncumulative). There are 10 one page papers due based on the readings she assigns. There was a 10 point extra credit assignment available. TAKE HER!

Prof Rimmasch made this class really enjoyable. You can tell she is passionate about what she is teaching and it makes the lectures more interesting. Just show up, take good notes, and do the readings and you will succeed. Would definitely take again from her.

I'm not an art/english major (not even close), so this class was perfect for me. She has a well-designed class structure. Go to class, take good notes, and study hard for the exams. Other than that, the class was easy and straightforward. She is definitely one of my favorite professors at BYU.

Lectures are really interesting. You have to take good notes in the class. But if you take good notes and study well for the exams, you should be able to get an A. It feels like it is a lot of information to memorize. During the semester it feels stressful. But by the end of the semester, you'll see that her class wasn't too bad.

Prof. Rimmasch is amazing! She really cares about her students. Her classes are not easy, but if you do the work and pay attention to the lectures, you will do well. She does not take attendance, but the lectures are absolutely essential to doing well in this class. Everything writes on the board is important and will very likely be on the test
This was one of my favorite classes and I decided to take both 201 and 202 classes with her. Better be in class and take notes for her tests. Great lectures that are always interesting.

She really helped me become enganged in the learning. You can tell that she really enjoys what she is teaching you and really cares about your grade. She is a professor who is rare to find when taking general education classes. I would definitely take her again no matter what course.

Mrs. Rimmasch was a very personable teacher! She was very caring and really worked with the students when things came up. The class only met once a week so it was important that you were there each week to learn the material needed for the test. If you showed up and did your readings, the tests weren't too difficult.
Very knowledgable and caring of your success. Bonus: she is a great teacher and explains things well. Lot of reading but it's all fun and worth it because her class discussions are great!

Lots of memorization, but tests aren't hard if you take good notes in class. Many good reading materials and really felt like I learned something rather than just trying to get a good grade. She is very caring and truly loves what she teaches!
Great teacher!  love her!
Excellent professor. Very knowledgeable, wants to see you get an A.
This was a really great class. She is a great professor!
Very knowledgable about the Humanities. Tests are straightforward and simple if you attend class and participate in lectures.

She is an awesome teacher. She makes note taking easy and clear. Tests are exactly as she prepares you for. she knows her content well and makes it interesting I want to go to Europe now to see all of this history!!!

Dr. Rimmasch was AMAZING... as a nursing major, I had little interest in humanities, until I took this class with her. Engaging and taught the info clearly. Class was relatively easy... go to class and you'll do well on tests. Offers extra credit. Definitely in my top 5 of favorite professors at BYU!

I love Professor Rimmasch. I wish I would have taken my other humanities classes from her. She is very kind, very structured and I learned a lot from her. She expects a lot from you but you walk away from the class knowing so much! She is an incredible teacher, seriously.
Good class

Sister Rimmasch helped me love Humanities.  At first I felt soooo out of place...I do nursing, not humanities.  But she helped me see that Humanities has importance in the world, and helped me gain confidence in it.  You definitely need to study for tests and be in class (no powerpoints--just notes).  But if you do, you'll grow like mad! She's grea
Attend the classes then you will do fine. she gives all the info you need to know for the tests.

She is absolutely amazing, everything that we cover in class is on the tests, so just pay attention! It's easy: read, come to class, study, and get an A. She is crystal clear, and always gives extra credit chances for struggling students. Very passionate and WANTS us to pass her class!! The best teacher ever. She really made a difference for me.

Professor Rimmasch is very passionate about her class so learning is interesting. She prepares you for every question on the tests. She encourages participation so that everyone is engaged in the learning. I loved this class and would recommend Professor Rimmasch to anyone and everyone!
She is wonderful! I encourage you to take this class.  She honestly opened my eyes and made my generals fun.

I recommend taking a class from Prof. Rimmasch. She makes you work for your grade, but at the same time she will go to great lengths to get you a good grade. She really wants you to pass, if not get an A.  She is organized; classes have the same format (lecture, discussion, art slides) She knows the subject very well and makes the class run smooth

Kristy Rimmasch was one of my favorite professors of my college career thus far. Her class was really tough and challenged me but I learned a lot and had a great time and I felt like it applied to my ever day life in a way Humanities doesn't always succeed at.
Professor Rimmasch is an excellent teacher. She is fair and fun. She is willing to work with you if you need to make accommodations for life's interruptions.

I learned a lot!  She is always very prepared with first hand knowledge.  She teaches about places she has visited with lots of information which is very interesting.  She is very king and helpful.  I would highly recommend her class.

This was my favorite class at the BYU salt lake center. I initially took it because I knew I would love learning about musics' effect on the arts in this time period, but had no idea I would also love many of the weekly response journals we had. Take this class with a few friends or make a study group. The tests are pretty detailed, read the book.

Rimmasch is a great teacher that doesn't waste time. She tells you exactly what you need to know to pass the class. She explains everything clearly and really wants her students to succeed. She is interested in the subject so it helps long classes be entertaining. She is a fair (and generous) grader and helps students. GO TO CLASS and take notesA.

Professor Rimmasch is a fantastic teacher! She makes Humanities interesting and fun to learn! She likes interactive learning so be sure to do the reading so you can contribute to discussion. She teaches you exactly what her exams contain. Gives out great study guides for each exam. I recommend this class for anyone wanting to be more cultured. :)
Sister Rimmasch is wonderful! She is very knowledgable about the subject she  teaches and makes it very interesting. I would love to take other classes from her!

Sister Rimmasch is a marvelous professor! I took my Humanities 202 class from her and wished I had taken all my humanities classes from her. She is very clear as to what she expects and is very attentive to students. She is passionate and knowledgable and fun! I totally recomend her.

Sis. Rimmasch was so fantastic! She has a very clear way of teaching and makes sure you are prepared for her exams. The class takes some work but it is definitely worth it because it makes class time enjoyable. She has fantastic study guides for each test, so make sure you take great notes in class and you should do fantastic! Good Luck!
This was a great class! Nice variety of art, literature, music, and architecture. She gives you a study guide for exams that really help prepare and is positive and very kind. Take this class!

I loved taking this class in Salt Lake at BYUs Business College. The classes were much smaller than at Provo which made it much easier to learn and get help. I don't normally like generals or the humanities but this was an exception. If you go to class and participate you should be fine. I took this my senior year so it felt easy.

I really enjoyed this professor and this class. You have to do the readings and really focus on notes in class. The professor is great and will keep you interested in the class. Put the effort in and you will love this class.

This was the first 3 hour block class that has kept me engaged from beginning to end. I never felt bored, even though art has never been particularly fascinating to me. Prof. Rimmasch knows everything about the subject, but at the same time meets you on your level so you don't feel dumb. I learned a ton, and would recommend this class to everyone!

I loved Sister Rimmasch!  She was extremely helpful and respectful of others thoughts and ideas.  She does have a 1 page paper due each week, but it's easily manageable.  Going to class really does help with the test.  I would definitely take this class from her!

Her lectures are boring and hard to follow, but she is very nice and helpful if you have any questions. Easy one-page papers due each week. She gives out study guides but it's still pretty hard to know to what to expect on the tests. Tons of art and music memorization. Very time consuming.

Knowledgeable teacher! Cut class short by approximately 10 minutes every week. Good teacher. Make slide shows for visual portion of tests! Written assignments due almost every week. Very respectful of differing view points. Seems to love her job. Take good notes, pound the visual portion and music portion into you head! Stay up to date, study!!!!!

She made Humanities interesting and enjoyable. There is a lot of reading and writing but none of it was busy work.  She was very respectful of student's points of view and grateful that we were prepared so we could have meaningful discussions. Come to class every time, take good notes and do the assignments and you'll do well.

kindest lady ever! If you are good at memorizing then you will do fine and if not you will still do well! she is so helpful and her lectures are really put together. we had to write response papers but they were extremely easy! I am just an average student and i did really well in the class.

Tough class but not really hard.  Lots of reading each week with one page papers due on the reading.  Lots of memorizing, but honestly its very easy to cram for.  Tests are easy if you take good in class notes...and she is a very fair test grader....I bombed the first test and did good on the last two...she boosted my 1st test to match.

Sister Rimmasch is a very nice and helpful teacher.  She doesn't worry about any curves in her classes. Her presentations are excellent, and they are all you need to know for the tests.  I never read the textbook once.  Take great in-class notes because that is where all the questions on the test come from.

She's a smart teacher who knows what she is talking about. She assigns a lot of reading and expects response papers on a lot of them. You have to memorize art and buildings, knowing the title, artist and locations. She's a sweet lady, she's just tough.

This is a hard class, but she made it interesting. She really knows the material. She is excellent with the use of classroom time and her syllabus was very clear about what to expect. If you take good notes, you will know what to expect on the tests.  Written assignments made up about 1/3 of the grade and tests the rest.

She expects people to know as much as she knows. She assigns too much homework for one class. She has a paper due every week- which she grades pretty hard on. Also the tests are hard. It is based on what she has said in class, aka: attendance matters, so if you missed you're screwed.

She really knows her stuff but, expects too much of her students.  There is way too much reading every week and a ton of memorization that is pretty challenging. There are a lot of papers so that helps your grade out but the tests are difficult to predict.
Too much homework. I am a senior and I have never had this much homework. I have more homework in this class than my other 9 credits combined including my 4 credit hour stats class.

Dr. Pierce cares a lot about this class. She had very interesting lectures and I learned a lot. That said quizzes were very difficult and required a lot of studying outside of class- much more than a 2 credit class should require, let alone a religion class. If you're looking for an easy religion class for credit, this is not the one to take.

This class was horrible. So so much necessary busy work each week, expect 4+ hours of straight reading and journaling a week. the final exam was 120 questions. this class was not spiritually edifying at all because of the insane amount of work and prep I needed to do to get an A. horrible....

I remember thinking, "I could easily just memorize her slides and ace the test without going to class," except that she didn't post her slides! Her lectures were so boring! She would ask for discussion on her questions, then only let one person comment, and then move to the next topic. The tests had many arguable answers, but only one was right.

The professor is nice. That is about it. The class is insanely hard and the tests and quizzes are impossible. The questions are extremely specific and it is hard to know exactly what to study for. It felt less like a religion class and more of a rigorous history class. The tests for my 3 credit were easier than these tests.

This is the hardest religion class I've ever taken at BYU. I had high hopes for this class but it's so bad. If you have the option, I would take ANY other religion class, even one in person. It's literally not worth it. The lessons are insanely long and the exams are so difficult. The mean score on the first exam was 69%…for a religion class.

She is a kind person.The lectures were interesting from a historical standpoint - information heavy. The questions she puts on the quizzes are insanely specific. I copied the slides she taught from in class word for word and still did not do well on them. This class didn't further my spiritual growth at all. I would not recommend taking it.

This class was awful, like most online ones. The reading workload was overwhelming with little payoff—I felt no spiritual growth, only dread and anxiety. Test questions were overly specific while material was too broad. She expects you to spend hours on reading. (I've spent more time on this class than on four others combined)

Professor Pierce is very kind and I enjoy having class with her. She does a good job making the lectures informative and engaging.

Class is mostly lecture with frequent writing assignments, but they just require you to share insights and questions from the readings. There are also projects, but they aren't hard and you are given plenty of time.

Felt like a history class instead of a religion class. Was really focused on Christ as a "Warrior King" which I didn't love and felt very subjective to test on. Tests were difficult and unclear to study for. Lectures were long, but interesting from a historical standpoint. If you're into that great if you're not, good luck.

The tests were what broke it for me. The lectures are good, although I'm not sure what I need to know on the slides as there's just a lot of quotes from the scriptures. Then I received a list of topics to study for and when I get to the tests I bomb it, despite taking notes and trying to study. Why are the tests so hard? Did I miss info in class?

Professor Pierce is a kind person and very knowledgeable. However, I really disliked her class structure. Lectures slides were just walls of text, and they weren't posted on Learning Suite. I always felt like I was frantically writing down everything and I rarely felt the spirit. Tests and quizzes were oddly specific and heavily weighted.

She's a wonderful person. Really cares about the students and the spirit is always there! The tests are challenging and weighted heavily. Even if I studied a lot I sometimes wasn't sure how to answer. But she does give great feedback about how to improve and she really wants to help.

She is very kind and sweet, however this class was very difficult for a religion class and I felt that I did not get much out of it. The quizzes and exams are quite hard and require knowledge of small details from lectures; the lecture slides are not posted on Learning Suite. I don't think that students were well prepared for the exams.

Get ready for an archeologist's take on the scriptures! 
Lots of assignments that were pretty easy. She is very kind and spiritual. 
Attendance is mandatory and slides are usually not posted, so don't plan to skip class. (most of the content on tests and quizzes is subjective but comes right from her lectures)

I felt like I spent a lot of time taking notes and didnt get much spiritually out of this class. Wasn't a big fan of the 4 quizzes that were 10 points and worth 24% of the grade. I feel like we didn't learn some of the content on the quizzes or it was mentioned in passing. She does care about her students I just felt like she wasn't the best for me
Pretty mid class all around. Tests are really hard for some reason.

She taught well but take good notes! The quizzes can often cover random pieces of information. Often, I found that I had taken notes on the wrong things in class and my notes were useless during the quizzes. (You're allowed notes on quizzes but not tests)

Prof. Pierce has a background in Archeology and her knowledge with Hebrew and other ancient languages has given me new insight to the scriptures. I think the lectures are interesting, but you need to take really good notes! There are 4 quizzes, 1 midterm and 1 final and they are weighted SO heavily. You have to get an A on both exams to get an A.

Lecture slides are walls of text quoting scripture with little context actually written. Her teaching style did not work well with my learning style. I also feel like there was too much work for a 2 credit class.

Professor Pierce teaches a very interesting class. She is knowledgeable and her lectures are fascinating. I found it difficult to stay awake sometimes because it isn't super interactive, but the class is designed to make it easy to succeed. She wants you to learn something and grow your testimony in whatever way is applicable to you.

Dr. Pierce is really cool, but REL A 250 is hard and confusing. I wasn't sure how any of the lectures fit together and the class was extremely content heavy. There is about 8-10 chapters of reading per week. The tests are pretty difficult and there are 4 quizzes, worth 10 points each, and they are weighted way too heavily.

Lectures are long and bland, with an informational overload. The tests are surprisingly difficult, and it is difficult to know what material from the lectures will be on the test. And there are no textbooks or slides posted so attendance is a must.

Professor Pierce is great! She is very passionate about religion and provides so many unique perspectives using her archaeology background. Insight into ancient times using artifacts and translation made this a enjoyable class! Workload is light, but tests and quizzes can be more difficult than you expect. By far my favorite religion class yet!

Professor Pierce was the best! Probably 1/1.5 hours of reading work a week, with occasional open note quizzes. Service hours required and a final project of your choice. The midterm and final are super approachable, just make sure to attend the TA review. Her lectures are great, and her archeology background gave cool context to the content. 10/10!

Krystal Pierce is an amazing professor! I learned so much and felt the spirit every lecture. Study guides are vague but work with the TA and Professor Pierce to best prepare for those. A light assignment due the day of every class, not bad at all!

Professor Pierce is an amazing teacher for this class! She is so funny and just a great teacher in general. Her background in archeology adds a lot to the class when she adds info about ancient history and how it connects to the scriptures. Tests and assignments are easy, just make sure to take notes and study.

This was an online class composed of lessons from several different BYU Religion professors. Professor Pierce only ran the logistics and webinars of the class. Didn't get to know her too well, but she seems nice. Each lesson took me a while. So much information to memorize/learn. But it's doable. Attend TA reviews.
An amazing professor. Took this class online but it was super easy. Plenty of time to do everything that's required.

Prof. Pierce is fantastic! You have to do some reading assignments outside of class that aren't bad at all, and there's only 2 exams which if you go to the review sessions you will ace. She is an archeologist so she has an awesome perspective and she's very smart. She loves her students and helps them feel the spirit!

I liked Professor Pierce, for a religion class this one was pretty easy, all tests were online which I really appreciated, her lectures move really quickly but she has a lot of knowledge about the scriptures because her background is in archaeology. The final project was super easy, this is a great class.

Professor Pierce was super kind and aware of our individual needs. The tests were straightforward and only tested on things covered in the lectures. The lectures were engaging, but I wish she had more time to discuss the content because she knew so much more information that she didn't have time to share.

I've read the Book of Mormon many times, but this class gave me a greater perspective and I learned a lot! I liked the discussion format of the class. Also, Sister Pierce's archaeological background provided a lot of cool insights. You will read half of the Book of Mormon for this course as homework, but that's the only homework.

Professor Pierce is an incredibly kind and caring person. She helped me to understand the Book of Mormon better than I ever have before- she has lots of cool experiences that go along with the course topic! Though I only talked with her personally once, I always felt loved and like I belonged. I would definitely recommend her and Religion 122.

Great Professor! You really need to attend class otherwise you will miss a lot of information as she does not post her slides. Homework is super light, and we only had two tests which if you studied the review you were fine! She sticks to the Book of Mormon and teaches straight doctrine so be prepared to receive lots of information!

Prof Pierce is great! She's funny, kind, and genuine. She loves the material in a way that makes you have a greater appreciation for it. Quizzes are open note and book so as long as you listen in class you'll do great! The TAs give super detailed reviews for midterms that make it a breeze. Great class

SO GREAT! I want to take all of my religion classes from her! Doesn't give busy work, but the work she does give is super manageable. Really understands the material and gives addition info for understanding and a deeper knowledge. Replies quickly to messages and very caring and flexible when you have things pop up.

Fantastic professor! I enjoyed her class. This will be the easiest religion class you take. No papers, if you go to the TA review you should be able to get 100% on the exams, and the end-of-semester project is super easy. You can find professors that will inspire and connect, but if you want an easy class that doesn't challenge you, this will do!

This is honestly what every religion professor at BYU should try to be like. She cares more about you learning than making you write a bunch of essays where you just drag your testimony out to the point of exhaustion. Amazing teacher who actually cares about her students. Learn from her, BYU professors!

Prof Pierce was great! This class is SUPER easy and you never have to write a paper. Both the midterm and final were really easy and had extra credit questions. The TA's are really helpful and their test reviews basically answer all the test questions.

I loved this class. She brought her own view of the BOM and connected it to her personal studies in different countries. She took attendance a few times but also doesn't make slides available online. If you miss a class you can talk to her TA for the slides. Easy quizzes/tests, and for the final project you can do whatever you want.

yall, i kid you not, THE EASIEST class you will probably ever take at BYU. Even easier than seminary I thought!!!! She is amazing, literally just wants her students to succeed. You can tell she is so passionate about the Book of Mormon and it was so spiritual. TAKE IT FROM HER YOU WONT REGRET IT

Professor Pierce's class was honestly one of my favorites! Her class is really manageable, as long as you show up and take notes. All her quizzes are open not and open book and we only had a midterm and final (with study guides based from the tests). She is very accommodating really cares about her students

Prof. Pierce is super knowledgeable about the BOM while still being spiritual. She encourages questions (no matter how simple)and discussions. I did feel bored at times because the slideshows and class format are the same every day. Super easy class if you take good notes and the reviews given by the TA are a lifesaver!!

BOM reading assignments are due twice a week but you can do them ahead of time and they take 10 ish minutes each. We had one test, project, and final. Expectations are clear and she is willing to work with students. Very educated and entertaining to listen to. Tests are hard but study guides and reviews are offered. Overall easy class. I <3 Pierce!

Prof P is truly a rarity in the religion department. She is unbelievably caring towards her students and welcomes intelligent conversation in class. Her lectures flew by. Her quizzes and tests are a little more difficult, but as long as you take good notes, you'll be just fine.

She was fine. As a person she seems really nice but she had a way of trying to make things deep and academic that really aren't that bothered me a bit. Some test questions are needlessly complicated and tricky; if tests aren't your strong suit it might be a challenge. She does send out a study guide that has everything you need to know which helps.

I loved this class! Probably my favorite this semester. Prof. Pierce is AMAZING. She's so caring and has an incredible testimony. I'm gonna miss her class. When I say you read textbook, I mean Book of Mormon.
Professor Pierce took over my class halfway through the semester, so it was a little disorganized, but she was still an awesome. Her lectures give a lot of new insight into the Book of Mormon.

I would NEVER take from Professor Pierce again! She was so hard! Her quizzes were unrealistic! She would pick random quotes from the Book of Mormon and then ask you to name who said it! Her tests were soooo hard and even though I took good notes and paid attention in class, I felt like I was being tested on things I had never heard of! :( :( :(

Professor Pierce is a super nice and fun teacher, but her class is deceivingly hard! You feel like you do nothing all semester then BAM!! There's the final! She will pull random quotes and you need to know who said it and such! Tests are killer!!! Don't take if looking for an easy A! If you don't work, you won't do well!

Sister Pierce was an averagely inspiring religion professor, although I did zone out a lot (my fault, not hers). The homework she assigned was graded on completion and easy. Her tests were a big surprise. You must memorize quotes and know specifics. However, I ended up doing okay despite less than exemplary performance on the midterm.

Sister Pierce is super nice but her class is ridiculous. She asked us a question about how many moons Coriantumr was with the people of Zarahemla. You have to know random quotes from the BoM for her tests. In addition to that, she has several essay questions on each test. Do not take this from her.
She literally wants you to memorize the whole book of mormon... please don't take her class...

She really places it on the student to succeed. Her papers and quizzes are easy, but be prepared to die on the tests. The only homework she assigns nightly are the basic scripture readings. Week to week, this class is a breeze. When it comes down to it, if you don't study hard and aren't good at tests DO NOT take this class

Sister Pierce is so great and her lectures are interesting. Reading questions and a few essays. Watch out for her tests. They are killer! She asked us to identify who said a certain quote from the BoM, without any references or study guide. Just random quotes. She is nice, but her tests were just overly hard with no useful study guide.

Professor Pierce is great, and such a nice friendly lady.  Quizzes are directly from notes and scriptures, so pour over them (open book but it's VERY specific).  A couple of essays that as long as you do you should get an A on them.  Tests are very difficult, so study hard, and you should do great in this class.  Not much homework, just reading ?s
Professor Pierce is very nice and understanding! The assignments are easy but the tests and quizzes are difficult so take good notes!

Sister Pierce is super nice and genuinely cares about her students! She is more than willing to help you if you ask! She loves class participation, so speak up! She doesn't really give busy work, just a few 1 page essays and reading questions, so it's up to you to study hard for the tests! Overall I definitely recommend prof. Pierce.

Pierce is a super nice lady. The class isn't terribly hard, but you have to take it upon yourself to know your stuff for the exams. Would highly recommend if you're looking for a professor who isn't going to overload you with work.

The trek to SLC is worth it. All his assignments have a purpose; he makes sure you leave the class knowing the Constitution. The class discussions are phenomenal. The tests are not hard. Just do the reading and go to class, and you'll be fine.
Lectures were usually pretty interesting lots of student participation there is textbook readings but its not a ton he surprised me with how much I liked the class

Take American Heritage from Brother Fertig! He is so sweet and his tests are easy and super fair. Going to the Salt Lake Center was worth it. No essays, easy quizzes and a few assignments, 2 midterms and a final.

This class was amazing. Bro Fertig is the absolute best!! So worth going to SLC. I loved that classes weren't just lectures--there were a lot of activities that made the course very engaging. Readings are super doable and the tests are very straightforward. Couldn't recommend this class more!

Kurt is the absolute GOAT. I took this in summer in SLC and it was ABSOLUTELY WORTH IT. He's a retired police officer so he's got tons of super cool stories that illustrated some of the principles he was teaching. Super nice guy, and the class was so straightforward. I studied hard for the tests, but they weren't bad at all. TAKE HIS CLASS!

GO TO SLC, THIS CLASS IS WORTH IT. I don't know how people are still taking American Heritage at BYU. All I did was read the textbook on the train and studied for exams (3) on the weekends. I loved Brother Fertig. Classes were not lectures, just activities and lessons that kept everyone engaged. Tests are SO straightforward too.

Brother Fertig is absolutely the best!!! He is very passionate about history, and his lectures are very engaging and interactive! I highly recommend taking A HTG with him. No essays!! There is a 5-question all MC quiz at the end of each class over the assigned textbook reading, but so easy! Two midterms & final, all MCQ. No trick questions!

TAKE AMERICAN HERITAGE FROM HIM! Seriously he is the absolute best. He connects the class materials to the real world and government and the tests aren't super hard. There is a quiz every class from the $10 textbook for the class, but lowest 3 scores are dropped. He has so much experience and is so passionate about what he teaches.

Brother Fertig is the best!
I am so glad I took American Heritage from him. He makes the AHTG content/load doable and interesting! The way he teaches this course is amazing, and he knows so much. This was my favorite course I have taken from BYU, and I 100% recommend taking AHTG from him if you can!!!

Brother Fertig is the best. I would recommend everyone take AHTG 100 from him because his class is directed more towards learning rather than random, tricky facts. Reading is minimal compared to others professors and what he expects is straightforward. He is also very caring, interactive, and an amazing professor!
Professor Fertig is a great teacher and knows what he is talking about! I learned a lot in this class and I think it's absolutely worth going to Salt Lake for!

Bro. Fertig has an amazing background and truly wants you to learn. He understands that this class is required for all students and takes that consideration to his assignments and exams. He makes class time enjoyable. Take his class (even if you have to take the train up there)! His exams are easy if you study the material for a couple of hours.

I took a leadership course from Professor Sandholtz. I could not be more impressed. I learned so much and was actually excited to come to class each day. There is not an overwhelming workload and everything assigned was actually super cool. He was so engaged and responsive. BYU is super lucky to have him and I would highly recommend.

He walked into class on the first day, and it took me a solid 45 seconds to realize it wasn't Elder Eyring. 
He greeted me by name and I just stood there like... "the Spirit of the Lord has descended for he hath discerned my name.  10/10, spiritually intimidating in the best way.

Would recommend as a future apostle.

Don't bother. The semester long project was "how to get seniors engaged in HR"..?  You have to pay for multiple hwk assignment materials (it's cheap but still?)  Exams are online/proctored, but weirdly difficult.  Attendance mandatory.  Guest speakers that don't have anything to do with HR?  Watched Selma in class uncensored.  Super uncomfortable.

The lectures were super boring, the assignments were inconvenient and also boring. The exams were frustrating and also boring. 
This class is just an expensive checkbox on the way to graduation.

I mean... What can I say. HRM 391 is one of the worst classes that we are forced to take. I'm not sure how much the professor has in deciding that, but wow, terrible. He tried his best, was very kind, etc, but him or the TA's randomly graded things extremely harshly. Like, I was shocked.

He was a nice guy, but he would dock points from assignments without giving reasons. At the end of the semester, he said he was going to dock students who missed classes, but that was never mentioned any other time or on the syllabus. Also, he curved the class down so do with that information what you will

Prof S is a nice guy. I will give him that. He treated this class like everyone wanted to be there and that it was the most life-changing class ever. However, all the assignments and especially the group work were SO tedious and pointless. It was brutally boring at times. He is big on feedback, so I hope he learns from this class.

Kurt looks like Henry B. Erying. Nice guy, caring, but super random grader. I'd lose points for reasons I can't explain. This class was the typical college class that nobody would want to take but the university mandates it. He tries to make it engaging by putting you in a team and that definitely helps. Overall feels like busy work.

fine professor but really picky grader. Said on the first day that he tries to make the average grade in the class a B. This led to many of my assignment getting points take off for really no reason. just to be picky and deduct points. His class seems better than most MCOM classes but grading unclear and unreasonably picky.

I enjoyed taking MCOM from Prof. Sandholtz. I've heard that the class usually has a lot of busy work, but I didn't feel that way with him. Prof. Sandholtz is inspiring and gave great feedback on both oral and written work. If you can nail the grammar test, you won't have to worry about your grade. I highly recommend taking the class from him!

Professor Sandholtz is a tremendous professor. He got rid of assignments we felt were busy work. He was sensitive to everyone in the class. He is an inspirational teacher and made a class I wasn't wanting to take enjoyable!

Wow, professor Sandholtz is one of my all-time favorite professors. I have learned so much in his class. He genuinely cares for his students, and he gives constructive feedback that really helps you improve. He is passionate about what he teaches and is fair to all of his students. I highly recommend him as a professor.

This class is so practical and valuable, and Professor Sandholtz is the one to take it from. I took his class in the spring, and he can make a three hour class feel like there's still not enough time. There is a ton of great discussion, group activities and projects, and he makes it very clear what you need to do to pass. I loved it!

This class was one of my favorites. Kurt Sandholtz, was a perfect mix of fun, engaging, driven, kind, and practical. I learned brilliant communication and presentation skills. We had a lot of practical life assignments that never felt like busy work. The textbook was also easy to digest and I retained a lot of the info (he also brought snacks)

GREAT Professor. HARD class. Grading was ruthless and done with ambiguity. I had to fight to get back points that were unnecessarily marked off. Nevertheless, I would take another class from Prof. Sandholtz again in a heartbeat. He's super qualified to teach the course and I learned a ton from him.

One of my least favorite classes at BYU. Professor Sandholtz is a nice guy but he made the class harder than the material would naturally require by grading ambiguously. I felt that he kind of developed favorites during the semester and I was at disadvantage because of that.

Great background, very qualified to teach course. Lots of work, but super relevant (other classes, career). Class feels like workplace. No late work. Easy to fall behind, DON'T WAIT to start big projects. Tough grader, but better him than your boss. Knows his stuff from grammar to presenting to networking. Soak it all up. Awesome professor!

Take MCOM320 from him! My friend was taking this class from someone else & I was shocked by the amount of assignments & grading system. Sandholtz is such a great teacher. He teaches clearly, gives challenging assignments, & gives helpful feedback. He is also very understanding! He was kind enough to let me turn in a few assignments late.

Professor Sandholtz is great. The lectures are always enjoyable and relevant. This class definitely makes you step outside of your comfort zone, but it is totally worth it. I would definitely recommend taking MCOM 320 from Sandholtz. He is a tough grader, but he is fair and makes his expectations clear.

Don't take anyone else. He is reasonable and very caring. Explains concepts well and always takes complaints/comments into consideration. All writing assignments felt beneficial, no busy work. A very practical class. Highly recommend to any major.

Prof Sandholtz is an amazing teacher!  He is very lenient and often adjusts assignments according to students' needs.  We do a big research paper as well as a team presentation, but he gives you everything you need to succeed. My favorite part of class is his inspiring and thought-provoking lectures.  Everything we learn is applicable and useful.
You can tell that he cares and he's definitely the best person to take MCOM from. Very caring, clear, and nice. A lot of group work but it's not annoying.

Prof Sandholtz is one of the most helpful, caring professors I've had at BYU. He helped me prepare a presentation for an interview and submit an article for a student newspaper. He wants his students to succeed--not just academically, but professionally as well.

GREAT PROFESSOR! His teaching style and his way of explaining were very easy to understand. The curriculum wasn't the easiest, and the grading was a little harsh, but all in all he is an outstanding professor.

I hated grammar. (This was the last class standing between me and graduation.)  Professor Sandholtz is everything you want in a professor.  He made class interesting and applicable, he is incredibly knowledgeable, he is a terrific educator, and he has a very likable personality.  It is not an easy A, but it's doable. Highly recommend him!
I like how he purposefully doesn't call on the students who make lots of comments and welcomes input from the introverts.  He is funny, people-oriented, and has a great teaching style
The ONLY teacher to take this class from.  He is THE BEST.  VERY helpful.  Clear to understand.  Wonderful.  Insightful.  Fun.  Teaches you a lot of valuable things!!!
Very good professor. Easy if you pay attention in class.
EXCELLENT Professor. He makes the topic very interesting. He has a lot of industry experience that he applies to class. One of the best professors in the Marriott School.

GREAT teacher, very interested in your thoughts and provides interactive, enjoyable lectures.  Tests aren't TOO bad and papers are picked apart, but that mostly depends on TA.  I learned a lot, take from him if you want to learn the subject, not if you want an easy A.
A great lecturer but his tests are a little difficult.

There is a lot of homework for this class and be prepared to do a preclass reading before every lecture. The content in this class gets dense pretty fast but Professor Pratt does a good job at helping you navigate through the concepts.

Brother Pratt is amazing! I would take classes from him again and again. He is very willing to help you and very loving. He knew all of our names on the first day because he had studied them with flashcards and he was always very personable. He even drew a little cartoon on one of my tests!

Dr Pratt really helped me to love 290, I was surprised that it became one of my favorite classes. His lectures are gripping and fast paced, you really have to keep up, but he welcomes questions and addresses them patiently. One of his main goals is to help you expand mentally and will help with tough problems. Came to love proofs in his class.

This class is hard but I think Dr. Pratt makes it the easiest it can be! Lots of homework but it was necessary to understand the material. I went to his office hours every week, and he has them everyday at different times so you should hopefully be able to make it if you have questions. He is very kind and funny. 10/10 recommend!

The class was difficult fs, but Dr. Pratt was a lot of help. He's a lot of fun in class and even more personable at his office hours. Homeworks were due at 7 pm, which was difficult since I worked until 8. So it's best to work ahead also because he offers to work through homework problems in class. The final was a lot easier than the midterms :)
Math 290 is a hard class, but Dr. Kyle makes it really digestible and easy. He is also really funny.

Pay attention in lectures and take good notes and you'll do well in the class. Makes the material engaging and understands it deeply, great at answering questions. Several group projects throughout the semester with fun applications of the class topics.

Kylee is by far the sweetest professor I've ever had! There is reading due every class period, but skimming works. Reading reflections also due each class are simple and quick (a few sentences). Discussions are amazing and Kylee is willing to work with you and accommodate for needs. There were several opportunities for extra credit!
Great class. Lots of fun discussions. She is a great teacher. Not graded harshly. Great content.

Kylee is an awesome professor and really cares about her students! The class does have a TON of reading due each day and you have to print off your reflection and bring it to class to turn it in, so you have to go to class. The topics covered are very beneficial and helped me in my learning and going forward in my career!

So frustrating that you have to turn in a daily reading quiz everyday. Also the class was mostly a discussion. Test questions come from reading quizzes that we didn't go over in class. I learned a lot from her because she's a therapist but this class has a lot of busy work.

Kylee is an incredible professor. The only problem is you have to turn in reading quizzes everyday in person, not online. Also she randomly has pop quizzes in person. Other than that if you are ok with going to class everyday you should be good! Class is pretty straightforward. She is a MFT and I learned a lot from her.

I would not recommend Kylee. She puts on the face that she is accommodating, but she isn't genuine. There are TONS of assignments & they aren't productive in your learning. She teaches like a therapist which is frustrating in academic setting. You have to print your reflections everyday. Test is specific and on things we didn't explicitly discuss.

She is a great professor, but the class was very repetitive. I got very bored. It was also hard to have it during the summer term because the classes were way too long. I felt she just stretched the lecture longer than it should. She worked hard and I loved the different presenters that she invited to come.
I loved this class, and although there was a lot of emphasis on the same issues, it is very helpful to learn about other cultures.

This was the most meaningful class I've taken. Professor Marshall taught difficult topics in a validating and accepting way. Readings can definitely be a lot sometimes, and there are a few papers. Overall, this class was extremely applicable and perspective changing. I would definitely recommend Professor Marshall!

I think she did a great job of tackling sensitive issues in an open-minded way, NOT from one political perspective. In fact, politics were never even mentioned. I learned so much in her class and she was just so great to work with. Very kind and accommodating to student needs. All assignments are pretty simple and very meaningful. I love her!

Professor Marshall was a great professor. She was respectful and validating. She is extremely knowledgable in her field and did a great job of explaining touchy subjects. I would recommend her to anyone. All of the assignments are worth while, but pretty easy if you follow the rubric.

Kylee's emphasis on becoming a "healing influence in the world" was a powerful theme throughout all of our hard discussions. The ethnic group and personal cultural presentations were both great learning opportunities. However the class is taught exclusively from one political perspective; certain views are misrepresented and vilified.

Kylee is the best! There isn't a textbook, but there are required readings each day that are posted online on the library reserve. Sometimes the readings were a little long but they were always relevant and inspiring. This class is amazing, and Kylee does a great job of facilitating brave conversations about difficult topics. 10/10 recommend!

Honestly, I can see why Kylee has so many great reviews. She is really nice, and is a young teacher so she is more relatable to college students. I struggled a bit with the organization of this class. Granted, covid made things difficult, but I always found myself a bit confused about what was expected/when things were due, etc.

Kylee is an amazing professor and this class honestly inspired me in so many ways. A few things to know is that there are a lot of readings. I spent more time reading in this class then in any of my others. The readings are pretty interesting though so you will like them. A lot of the class is discussion based so sometimes can get off track.

Kylee is really great. She does a great job of making people feel comfortable voicing their ideas and opinions whatever they may be; as someone who always hated commenting in class, I actually was able to do a lot of that in her class and felt like it was well received. Overall a very good experience and I learned valuable things about myself.

Kylee is the most kind and compassionate individual. The course content covers many "difficult to talk about" issues and Kylee makes the learning environment very comfortable for everybody. There was quite a bit of reading, but the course layout makes homework very doable. Also, there is no course textbook which is a plus!

Kylee was an amazing example of having vulnerable conversations and how to approach understanding individuals who suffer oppression and discrimination. Attendance charted through in-class quizzes. Large amounts of reading done in preparation for each class. 4 main projects/papers. Midterm and final. Really eye-opening class.

I loved taking this class from Kylee! She is very passionate about this subject and she genuinely cares about her students. She respectful of people's individual concerns/opinions and makes people feel comfortable participating & being vulnerable.

Kylee is a phenomenal teacher. Thanks to her, this class has been one of the most impactful classes I have taken at BYU. I know that I will refer back to the concepts and truths that Kylee taught in this course for the rest of my life. It has honestly changed the way I view the world.

I loved Kylee. We talk about a lot of hard issues in this class and she approached every student's perspective with compassion and neutrality, something that is exceptionally difficult to do when it comes to such emotionally charged topics. The grading criteria was very reasonable and if you put in the effort, there is no reason not to get an A.

Kylee is the best! You can tell that she really cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. There are reading reflections due each class and a few short papers, but they aren't hard and are usually pretty interesting and useful. This has been one of my favorite classes I've taken and I would highly recommend to take it if you can!
Kylee is a great teacher. She really knows her stuff and cares about each persons opinion. You will grow in this class if you have an open mind. Life changing class.

I love how respectful she is and how real she is! She understands when there are times in the semester that are hard for students, and she makes changes to fit the class's needs. Her honesty and her ability to be personal with us provided an atmosphere of growth and learning. What a joy her class was!!!

This class was probably one of the most influential classes I have taken at BYU. Kylee was great and presented hard and emotional material in a way that helps you apply it to your life. She cared about student and our experiences. Would recommend to everyone. Life changing!

Kylee was so great! With her experience as a therapist I felt like she was really respectful and non-judgemental to her students. I learned a lot about how to be more understanding and loving towards those with a different background from me. Pretty easy class! Recommend it!

Kylee is probably one of my favorite professors so far. She is so kind fun, and she has an amazing ability to create a good space to talk about some heavy topics. There are quite a few assignments and readings, but as long as you do them and attend class you should get an A with no problem. I recommend Kylee in heartbeat!

Kylee is awesome. I love how relatable she is. She brings the course to life. It's a heavy course emotionally because we talked about difficult subjects, but I loved it. No reason to not get an A if you come to class, do the readings, and participate. I'm not usually a big participator, but she makes me feel comfortable doing so. 10/10 recommend.

This was probably my favorite class from BYU. Kylee is the nicest teacher ever and made the class really enjoyable. There is a little work involved, but as long as you follow the directions she gives you, there is no reason not to get an A. This class was inspirational and Kylee did a fantastic job. 10/10 would recommend.

Kylee is a great professor! She is so caring. Her assignments are very fair. You do have to do a reading reflection every class, but they are only a few sentences long. The tests are fair and the papers are not difficult! I highly recommend taking this class for Kylee!

Kylee is Awesome! She is kind and understanding of students. Her class is based a lot on participation, so you need to be in class! That said, you get points everyday, making tests less heavy. There are a few papers, but they are all basically opinion papers so they are pretty easy. There are readings and a short write up before each class.
She's a great instructor! I did the online version and it went great. You have to record a few videos which feels awkward, but she's just looking for effort.
Highly recommend taking Instructor Pyne! She's awesome, explains things well, and makes you feel filled in body and mind. I really enjoyed this online yoga class.

I LOVE HER!!! She makes the class de-stressful and it always put me in a good mood. She also pays homage to the origins and names of yoga poses which is super cool. It was very much a go-at your own pace and level  class which was very inclusive and nonjudgmental. Also go to her ice cream shop! Thank you Kylie Pyne :)
The only class Ive ever wanted to be early for to just to sit and chill. I even went to 2 of her classes in the same day. She is just amazing. Follow her dog on Insta @heylisten_navi

Homegirl was a fantastic instructor! She helped me move my hips like Shakira from the 1400s. She took great interest in our lives and treated us like we were homies. We stretched like a croissant. Check out her YouTube channel and leave a like and comment. Be sure to share the videos on Facebook like a 50-year-old mom who is trying to be cool.

Kylie is an amazing instructor! I've taken her Yoga class 3 times, and she does a better job than any other yoga instructor I've had at explaining things, giving advice and modifications, and being kind. She gives short power point presentations about different aspects of yoga at the start of some classes, teaching a bit of the religious side too.

Kylie is the best yoga teacher I've ever had. Hands down. She clearly teaches because she enjoys yoga and the students. She is so good-humored! She creates a comfortable environment in the class and instructs to everyone's level, but she will challenge you to try new things! I'm planning to take her class again! Truly a homie.
a precious angel. loved taking yoga from kylie
Great instructor. Very down to earth and just wants to get you doing yoga. Would take again.
Kind, funny and helpful. She asks for requests for what to focus on each day.
She's probably one of the sweetest people ever, loved taking yoga from her

I loved taking yoga from Kylie! She sincerely cares about her students, and she makes yoga fun and doable! She would always take requests from the class before we started, and she always found ways to make class fun, even at 8 in the morning! It was definitely one of my favorite classes!

Definitely take this class with Kylie! She is literally amazing, she knows so much about the industry and you can see how much she cares about public relations. The certifications in this class were cool to have and the presentations are really interesting and easy!

Kylie is such a fun professor. I took her night class, but she never let us out later than 7. Her assignments are easy, but she does take a long time to grade. There are a ton of group projects, so sit by friends! Overall, Kylie is super passionate about what she does and is super engaging.

Kylie is SO FUN. I know evening classes suck usually, but this one is not bad at all, we never got out of class later than 7pm. She does social media for BYU's official account which is so cool, and is always SO willing to do letters of recommendation, help with internships, etc. There are a lot of group projects in her class so pick a good group!

Kylie is hands down the best professor I have had at BYU! She genuinely cares about each of her students and is always willing to help out with future endeavors or assignments. Night classes can be difficult to go to, but Kylie always made it worth it to go! I definitely recommend taking her class to anyone needing to take COMMS 333!!

She honestly had a condescending tone the entire time I took her class. Her emotions felt forced and not genuine. Overall an okish teacher, and just an ok person. It also took her forever to submit grades. She didn't have assignments graded from week 3 until week 10.

Kylie is so sweet! She makes her lectures fun and interactive, loves what she does, and has great resources! She is the social media manager for BYU so she really knows what she's doing. 10/10 would recommend.

Kylie is so fun! She's really passionate about social media and what she does and does a great job helping students be entusiastic about it. She makes class really fun and very interactive. There's just three assignments and they're all pretty straightforward and she doesn't grade too hard. I loved this class and can apply what I learned!

Ok, stats just isn't easy for me, but most people get an A. I would recommend her. Tests are open note and slides, so you might not even need to study. Homework after every class, but it takes like 15 minutes

Retakes for all tests and homework. Open note and open book. As long as you go to class and complete the homework this class should be a breeze. Loved the teacher, would bring us candy on the analysis days and seemed to genuinely care about us. Would definitely recommend!

I did not enjoy her teaching style. Lectures are very boring and she is not good at explaining anything. Basically you have to teach yourself the content-luckily the class is set up so you have multiple attempts on almost every assignment.
I think sometimes she has a hard time conveying stats concepts to students with no stats knowledge. It was pretty confusing sometimes. Overall not too hard of a class though

I love Dr. Gunter! She is so sweet and caring. She teaches things very clearly and offers a lot of resources for her students to suceed The tests are open note and allow retakes, so the class was very low stress.

I don't love her teaching style. Lectures are very boring to listen to, and if you're not already good at math, it feels like you have to meet her at her level. There are lots of opportunities to get a good grade, and tests are open note which is nice, but I feel like I ultimately taught myself the whole course.

Her teaching style is not my favorite but overall she's not a bad professor. Attendance really matters especially for in class analysis days. If you miss one day then you'll be very lost on the homework, but if you show up to class and pay attention the class isn't too hard. Your grades on exams and projects contribute a lot to your final grade.
The class itself shouldn't be hard, but her lectures were not terribly engaging, and she was just reading off the slides. She was fairly helpful during office hours.

The class isn't hard and she gives many opportunities to get a good grade. If you want an A you can get it. The only thing I didn't like was her teaching style. Most of the time I would teach myself the material because listening to her teach made me confused. But it was an easy enough class and an easy A.
Pretty mid at teaching and not rly engaging with the class

This class the same no matter which teacher you take it with. Same tests, homework assignments and slides. Professor Gunter's teaching style was not my favorite. I often got confused when new concepts were introduced in lectures because she explained easy concepts in a way that seemed complicated to me. Overall, it's not bad if you do the homework.

Prof Gunter was super nice and you can tell she cares about her students, however she didn't explain concepts very well. The class itself isn't difficult, there's multiple attempts for homework and 2 attempts for every test.

The class itself is pretty easy. If you just show up to lectures and do the homework you'll be fine, you can use notes on everything including tests. Prof. Gunter herself was not my favorite I didn't love her teaching style. She just read the slides and it was hard to understand concepts. Luckily the class is more monkey see monkey do.

Great class, good professor. Teaches clearly and answers questions. Tries to make sure all the students are set up for success and understand the material. TAs are super helpful as well! Tests are a significant portion of the grade, but if you study and do the homework it's all the same concepts on the tests.

This is one of the easiest classes I have taken at BYU. I don't think it remotely matters what teacher you take they are all set up the same way. If you want to get 100% on every assignment just do any assignment in the TA lab. Teacher is sweet, but I bet there's better ones.

She wasn't good at explaining concepts; she taught the difficult stuff way too fast, and it would take her multiple attempts to get the class to understand what she was teaching. The course itself was easy, with 4 tries on homework and open-note tests. She had lots of practice problems in class, which was helpful.

Very confusing lectures, difficult to understand and follow what is being taught. stats 121 is an easy class. I think the Stats teachers use the same slides for all the sections, it would likely be more beneficial if she would have customized her lectures. At least it may have been more interesting.

Class in itself was easy, I would not take a class from her again. I am an athlete and have University Excused absences for games, and she completely disregarded these and just told me there was nothing she could do and dismissed them. I dropped a full grade from assigments I was unable to do because of missing class, even though I had no choice.

Pro Gunter was great! She was caring and funny and did a great job teaching this class. She always stayed after class to help students. Honestly the easiest class and it probably doesn't matter who you take it from. You have 2 midterms and a final and little homework every week. As long as you go to class and pay attention you'll be fine.

Your whole grade is literally based off three exams, but that's the stats department policy not Prof. Gunter's. She's fine, honestly it doesn't really matter who your professor is. There's a stats lab open from 9-5 Monday through Friday that is super helpful if you get behind. Highly recommend.

Professor Davidson was one of the most incredible professors I've ever had! I loved his lectures and he cares so much about his students. He handles the content really well and, while his tests are pretty hard, I feel like he did a really good job trying to prepare us for them (if you go to class). 10/10 recommend!
I love Professor Davidson! This is a pretty hard course, but he does his best to help and is a very compassionate professor! I learned so much in this course, super interesting.

Class structure: a research article reading before each class, 6 practice quizzes, a semester project/paper, 3 exams (final is not cumulative!). I thought the course content was super interesting and thorough and Dr. Davidson is extremely knowledgeable in the field. He is also very kind, caring, and willing to help students.

Professor Davidson is a great teacher! He is a nice genuine dude and I like how his class is structured. He gives you you opportunities to make points back with teams and honestly that helped me learn a lot by discussing it with my teammates. Just do the readings, go to class, and take good notes and you'll be fine.

Nice guy. The class is just hard. Semester long project. In class quizzes that can be difficult if your group didn't do the reading. Exams are pretty tough and I never seemed to get all the free response points. Idk if he's teaching this class anymore in the future though, I wonder why.

Prof Davidson is a kind guy. He is pretty tough in his exams, the study guides don't match what he looks for on the exams. Study and know the slides like the back of your hand. Your grade will depend on it. There are 3 quizzes weekly which are easy but long reads. He also does not get back to emails easily so be cautioned

this is a pretty sensitive course topic, and I think Lance is the perfect personality to teach it. He handled every lecture with grace. Lots of readings. the semester project isn't difficult but stay on top of it from the beginning.

There are 3 reading quizzes every week before class but they are fairly easy (don't refer to them for tests tho because they're not really applicable). There is a semester long project that I would suggest not waiting until the end to do. He mostly just teaches from the slides so I found it didn't matter too much if I went to class or not.

Dr. Davidson is my favorite professor at BYU. I loved this class so much. It is very test heavy. You also have a reading quiz due before each class, and a semester project. The information you learn is amazing. He also offers test corrections if needed. Seriously an awesome class and professor. I had an amazing experience in this class.

Overall, the class was okay. The homework is heavy reading, so I didn't get a lot out of it. A problem I ran into was that too many times, my contributions to discussions would be ridiculed. I gave an expected answer and it was called "brutal". That made participation uncomfortable. As long as you don't try to contribute, I feel it's an okay class.

When I first started this class I was a little nervous that the topics of obesity and weight management would not be handled with a compassionate and thoughtful hand. However, I was incredibly relieved to see that this was not the case! He is caring, thoughtful, well-rounded, curious, and ready to learn and discuss, while also emphasizing humanity.

I absolutely loved this class. It helped me to apply a lot of what I had previously learned in my major. Dr. Davidson is so kind and attentive! I felt cared for, known, and important in class, Study ALL the slides for the exams and attend class and you will do amazingly well.

He is the kindest most empathetic person you'll ever meet. He genuinely cares about you. That being said, his class is difficult and requires a ton of effort. Make sure you know all his slides like the back of your hand; graphs, stats, and all. But you'll be better off for it, I feel like i really understand physiology now

I have worked with Dr Davidson before, but this was my first time taking his class. He is very organized despite his busy life and cares so much for his students. By far he is the most caring, kind, and passionate professor I have taken a class from at BYU. The class is straightforward and the material isn't too hard if you have taken physiology.

Do not waste your time taking this class from Professor Davidson. All of the answers to his tests are answers that he believes are correct. The class is simple because you already know all the material but your grade will struggle because of the challenging readings and tests. Heavily weighted tests and extremely boring lectures.

Pretty worthless class. Tests are filled with a bunch of nonsense random data points that are all very similar so it's hard to differentiate between all them. Tests averages are low 70s and even high 60s. Wouldn't recommend the class. It was a very annoying class.

I absolutely love Dr. Davidson. Throughout the semester, he showed his students that he cared about them individually and that he truly wanted them to succeed! He is test heavy and has difficult exams, but I think that comes with the subject. Hard exams, but I learned more in this class than any other I've taken at BYU. I recommend!
Good guy. Hard Exams. Daily Homework. Team Quizzes in Class. It's a tough class. Like test averages were low 70s... but it was a fine class. Just freaky hard.

I was impressed on the first day of the semester when he already knew every students name. He really cares about his students and wants to help you succeed. I had a hard time paying attention in class but attendance isn't mandatory, you can learn well enough from the readings and PP slides. I did feel like the tests were a little difficult.

Doesn't make you come to class, I watched the recording on 2x the speed and it was very doable. Never read anything. Just quizzes over research articles that have nothing to do with the tests and review quizzes that are helpful for the tests. Just take good notes and use the study guide as well. Easy.

Dr. Davidson's class was very enlightening. He covered every aspect of obesity in an understandable and interesting way. He is also a really nice guy to talk to. I took his class online at 8 am and was riveted the whole way through.

Dr. Davidson is a great person and professor. This course was doable, relevant, and honestly has some of the only info i'll use as a healthcare provider that I learned in my undergrad. He's also anxious to help students find opportunities like research teams and getting published. He's a gem.
Dr. Davidson was an awesome professor for EXCS 480! He cares about his students' success. He is very accessible outside of class.

Nice guy, but did not get anything out of lectures. Reading quiz before every class on a research article that doesn't have anything to do with the tests. Everything you need to know for the tests are on the slides (so I stopped going to class). Information is straightforward. Easy A but don't expect to get much else out of the class.
