Lance Davidson is so caring. You have pre class reading and quiz, as well as in class group quiz. 480 just pre class quizzes, all super easy. I crammed studied both and pulled a B. I struggled understanding the info, not only did he let me take the exams in his office. He constantly gave the entire class full credit. Whole class is curved a lot!

He boasts about knowing everybody's name. He doesn't prep his lecture slides until the night before lecture. He is as confused as he is confusing at lecture. All tests aren't available until day 2 because they aren't finished. His work ethic is comparable to a 6th grader. He needs to put less time into memorizing names and more into his teaching.

He is one of the nicest professors I've had. I can tell that he personally cares for his students & wants to help them. I took him for 463 & 480! Both require reading & quizzes but not much homework/assignments outside of that. His tests in 480 are easy but in 463 they are hard! He seems confused at times & wish he linked 463 more to exercise.

Yes, Dr. Davidson is a very nice guy, but he is an awful professor. He is constantly confused during his lectures. There's a ton of reading due before each class with a quiz and then team quiz in class. The quizzes aren't too tough but the tests are nothing like the quizzes. The class average on every test was barely a passing grade. Don't take him

this class is SO HARD. probably the hardest class Ive taken at BYU. the professor is kind. he doesnt not curve tests though and pretty much has no mercy. the class average for tests is always incredibly low. the readings are a huge word vomit. this class takes 15-20 hours a week of studying. would not reccomend unless you want to get wrecked
Had him for beginning racquetball. He is a great guy, fun to be around. Great coach!

This class is the epitome of what I believe a 400 level college course should be. The material is challenging, but Dr. Davidson has created a learning environment conducive to lifelong learning. Hands down, fav professor I have EVER had. Pre-class: assigned reading and quiz. In class: Discussion based class with ppt supplementation and team quiz.

This class was my favorite at BYU. Dr. Davidson required a lot of reading and quizzes, but I can honestly say I learned more in this class than most of my other classes combined! He does a semester-long application project that counts as much as a test. You're pretty much guaranteed to get full points if you follow his rubric! Great teacher/class!

He is a fantastic teacher and one of the most caring professors I've ever had. His lectures are fascinating and he does a great job explaining difficult concepts. I loved his class so much that I TA'd for him for two semesters! His class has the same average as the other 463 classes; it's a difficult subject but he makes it interesting and fun!

Dr. Davidson is an excellent professor, the best I had at BYU. He expects a lot of you, but gives you the support needed to do well. His class is well-structured, it's a lot of quizzes but several are dropped, meaning you can bomb/miss a few without worrying about it. He also curves the exams as needed.

One of the best professors ever! Do the reading and go over powerpoints to succeed. He is organized, straightforward about what you need to know, understanding, and not cocky/intimidating. If you have questions, he will always make time for you and discuss until you understand. He places spirituality as a high priority for his class and in general.

course summary: before class- read abt 10 pages, closed book quiz; in class- teacher led discussion 10-15 min (not material related, mostly religious talk), next 10-15 min group quiz on reading (note:still no material covered), last 15-20 min of class powerpoint; tests- puposefully confusing, not straightforward, vague questions. overall: terrible!

This class is a 2 credit class that mostly reviews material that I have learned in other course with some extrapolation. I have spent more time in this class on reading and quizzes than I have doing anything else. His teaching philosophy is that you read, and are quizzed on material before you learn it in class. His pre-class quizzes... SPECIFIC!

Dr Davidson is one of the most engaged teachers I've had at BYU. He wants you to do well but expects you to really learn. The material is difficult, but he really helps you to learn it. Come to class prepared and you'll do well! He expects a discussion in class, so it's on you to learn the basics beforehand and come with questions.

This class was a joke. He admitted in class that he "hadn't looked at the book in a while"... His tests are impossible to pass, poorly worded questions. He expects you to learn everything from the book, take a quiz on it, and then retake the same quiz in class as a group. The bulk of your grade is tests (20% each). He won't take feedback from you.
THIS CLASS WAS SO HARD! He basically makes you learn everything on your own. Everything is about group work. His tests are impossible. TAKE SOMEONE ELSE!!!!

80 quizzes in one semester? He is your guy. One reading quiz and one group quiz every day. He is really helpful though and very friendly. This would be a saving grace if he knew how to write tests. Nearly every question is "which of the following would not..." All things considered, I got an A and he is very nice but his class can be annoying.

This is how all teachers should be! He is one of the most genuine people you'll meet! Sincerely cares about you, will spend time outside class to help you succeed. Generous in giving back points for unclear questions. About an hour+ of reading each class which 2 quizzes depend on. Keeps work spread out if kept up. Worked hard for a B+, but LEARNED

Class setup. Read a chapter before every class take a quiz on LS on that chapter. Take same quiz in class with your group. After quiz there is only about 10 minutes left for Dr D to lecture. He is not the best at explaining concepts and it gets confusing.

Well-structured class, not too hard but not too easy. Learned a lot, enjoyed his lectures and got a generous grade. Super friendly and genuine guy, wants you to succeed, incorporates the Gospel in good amounts and good ways. I wish every BYU professor was like Dr. Davidson! Reading+quizzes 3x a week (takes about an hour each), group quiz each class

Dr Davidson is an amazing person, however he stumbles in his explanations a lot. It becomes very confusing. I usually get an A in my classes but with him I have only been getting less than that. It is not because he doesn't try to help. He is just very confusing on the way he explains things. Because of his participation system, lectures dont help.

One of my favorite classes at BYU yet! It was his first time teaching, so he stumbled a bit here and there. But he is willing to help you in ANY WAY. He cares more about your learning than he does a grade. His tests were doable, but studying is required. he provides a study guide. There are weekly quizzes that are easy. All in all, a great teacher.

Truly cares about student's learning, not so much about the grade. There's hardly any reading in the textbook and he is very interactive in class. He tests on mostly the topics brought up in class, so it's a good idea to go.

He is such a tough grader, takes points off for things the lectures said to do. He talks down to you, he likes to feel smarter and better than his students. He always talks in a condescending tone. Even going to class, doing the readings, taking notes, and working hard isn't enough to do well in this class. You're set up to fail.

I personally didn't learn too much in class, and there was never a clear answer on questions asked from neither the teacher or the TA's. None of them were helpful. I received a few rude emails from the teacher and he seems very condescending and non accommodating. Exams did match the criteria very well from what you learn in lectures.

Holyyyyy he was horrible. I had him last semester and it was my last semester at BYU. NOTHING made me want to leave more than this class. He grades so weirdly- he seems to have OCD or just likes to be mean and condescending to students. He likes to be smarter and I got some of the most rude emails from him. DO NOT TAKE FROM HIM! RUN AWAY. SO BAD.

I was probably a very annoying student for Dr. Erickson, but despite that, he was super respectful to me and genuinely cared about what I thought.  The course design is simple and the exams are very doable.  If you just show up to lectures, do the reading, and go to the TA reviews, you will be just fine in the class.

Does not care about accommodations, won't give straight answers, TA's didn't give any help and always said to ask a peer. You could tell his political stance and it always bled into the lesson. He doesn't care if you lost a loved one (I did), still have to go to class. I really hated this class even though I liked this subject previously.

Dr Erickson knows what he's talking about, but he's not good at teaching it. His lectures were confusing and meandering. His answers to student questions were often unhelpful. And on the labs, expect to get points taken off for stuff you didn't know you had to do. My main tip? Visit the TA, and they'll explain it better.

Love Dr. Erickson! He really cares about his students and genuinely believes in what he teaches. Addresses controversial topics, but respects other viewpoints and encourages people to think for themselves. Relates content to scriptures a lot. Teaches with activities and funny stories. This class has made me a better person. Lots of reading, though.

This class is hard, but Dr. Erickson does a great job of teaching and making sure you actually understand the material. There is a lab due each week that is hard, but the TA's are SO helpful and make it doable. There is a midterm and final, both of which are open book, open note, open everything--still time-consuming though. Highly recommend!
He is very liberal and tests are very foreign. I wouldn't recommend taking the class in general.

There was a written assignment every week and if you follow the instructions you should be fine. Sociology was such a foreign concept to me and it made the class a little bit more difficult but if you go into the class open minded you should be fine.

I really liked how open-minded Professor Erickson is. His lectures are super interesting, and his only assignment is writing a one-page paper each week. My only complaint is that his tests were pretty hard for me but I barely studied and never read the textbook. He also will give you 50 points as long as you don't miss 7+ days. Super nice guy.

The class was not too hard. It has very little homework (1 assignment a week). The tests are not too hard either. Make sure you listen and follow guidelines or else you will receive a lower grade. There aren't many assignments so do them on time because you cannot submit late work. It is a very interesting class and Dr. Erickson is awesome.
Course was pretty clear and straight forward. There are few things that you are graded on.

Not going to lie, Dr. Erickson grew on me. His lectures can get boring sometimes but if you really listen, you can learn some pretty cool stuff. There are 3 exams (2 midterms, 1 non-cumulative final). You have a writing assignment due every week on Friday. Just pay attention in class (I didn't really) and you could get an A.

Dr. Erickson's papers were incredibly difficult and his test questions obscure. In addition, he had trouble getting through lectures despite the class being 75 minutes long. When he asked questions during lecture he seemed to be looking for specific answers, and many of these questions were inappropriate to ask in a classroom setting.
Very interesting class, he cares a lot about his students.
GOAT

During the class, I didn't like it a ton. The lectures were sometimes boring and the weekly write-ups were graded  harshly. The tests were also super specific. But I got into a rhythm and by the end of the class, it was ok. Now, I use my knowledge from this class all the time. It might sound cheesy, but it's changed how I see the world honestly.

Erickson was awesome. Obviously the class is hard and he can be a bit vague at times but he genuinely cares and the class is seriously not as hard as the reputation it has. He really wants to help you so definitely reach out! He's also awesome with extensions if needed. Take a class from him!

Clear requirements and expectations for the assignments and lectures. The tests are straightforward. There are in-class quizzes to help record attendance. He brings up topics tactfully and it was an inspirational course

Hard class, tough grader for sure, but he and the TA were super accessible. Labs took a long time, and I definitely recommend working in groups / learning from each other and helping each other figure things out. Don't skip class! You need the lectures.

Very impactful! You can tell he really cares for all of his students (and loves Stata!). Yes, the class isn't the easiest, but everything hard he has the students do has a reason. There is a textbook but he just had us use an online copy of it that he gave us access to for free. Prof. Erickson is one to take if you want to learn a lot!

I personally didn't love SOC111, but that has noting to do with Professor Erickson. I thought he was funny and a great teacher. He knows a lot about the subject and although we have differing political views, I didn't feel like he taught biases in class. Great class for a GE. TA reviews were super helpful to the tests.

If you did well in 307 you'll do great here. His grading criteria is not always clear, but the TA will help you if you go to her. It's was hard but I really learned something new each week and he pushes you to really understand the material instead of just copying interpretations. That's what I liked about it. Labs take awhile.

Must be a mind reader to pass this class. He has a hard time dumbing down material and wants you to be "intuitive" about the assignments, but doesn't teach you how to do that. He expects you to learn more in the prereqs than you actually do. He wants you to do it his way but won't teach you what that is. He isn't specific in assignment prompts.

The professor Is very layed back. (except about masks) Lectures are really boring. You have 1 assignment every week and then 2 mid terms and a final. Go to the reviews to the tests, because they are basically word for word of the tests. He was a good professor, I just wasn't interested in socially and took it as a GE.

If you are required to take sociology, I would recommend completely switching your major and career choice before I recommended taking this class from Lance Erickson. Class was the biggest joke and the only reason people show up is because there are in class quizzes. If it weren't mandatory, no one would show up. Total shmuck. Peace out Lance.

Lance Erickson is the worst teacher I have ever had. I'm a senior, so I've had my fair share of teachers and no one comes close to this guy. He has NO idea what he is doing. Every time I sat down, I bonded with some random person over the fact that this was our least favorite class, we had no idea what was going on and he just absolutely sucks. Run
he is a really nice guy and i genuinely enjoyed sitting and listening to his lectures in class but the tests are really confusing and hard and the essays each week are graded very hard also.
His lectures were not very well organized and honestly it was really hard to stay awake. every friday there was a writing assignment due and they were really hard and complicated.

Erickson is my favorite professor and this has been one of my fav classes, and I'm not even a Soc major. The class was incredibly easy and he is so chill and funny. Weekly papers are short and get easier throughout the course. You get full attendance if you show up 75% of the time. If you have to take Soc 111, take it from him.

Class wasn't super hard (especially if you skim the reading and go to review sessions) but there are only a handful of things in the gradebook. Weekly essays can be confusing. And it should really not be 1.25 hours long. But Lance is funny and I learned a lot. This class made me think, even though I already had a very liberal-minded education.
A researcher pretending to be a professor. He should be working in a lab or some place that requires minimal human interaction let alone teaching.

Lance is such an interesting dude, like the reviews before me state, the reactions were hard at first but easier as you went along. As you start out in the class a lot of people can agree that it's quite boring. But the further you go into the course, the more interesting it gets.

If I could say one thing about Dr. Erickson it would be that he CARES. He truly wants you to do well in his class and he is very available outside of class. He was willing to bend over backwards for our class and was extremely understanding. I loved taking his class and would recommend him to anyone interested in sociology.

Professor Erickson is a really great guy. The class is hard to get used at first if you've never done sociology but he does a good job making it relevant. There are weekly assignments and quiz questions throughout the class, so you have to stay on top of things and attend class to do well. His tests aren't hard if you study the vocab from the unit.

I really enjoyed this class. Lance was good at listening to opinions and explaining himself. He made me very interested in sociology. The weekly reactions were hard at first, but got easier as we went along.

Lance is a great guy, the kind of guy I'd want to invite over to my house for dinner lol. I really enjoyed his class. He got through all of the course material without ever rushing the class. The weekly reactions are nothing to stress about and the tests aren't long and are reasonable.

Lance is my favorite professor that I have! He's such a kind man and is so willing to explain things in further detail and help you with anything you may need outside of class. He's a great professor - hilarious, personable, engaging, and great at explaining things. Take sociology from Erickson! I'm considering switching my major because of him!

Great professor! Very understanding and willing to help to any need that students may have. His grading criteria is very clear and lectures are very discussion oriented. He expects you to come prepare to talk about what you think on the readings. You get full points for attendance if you go at least to 80% of the lectures. Take SOC111 from Lance!

Lance was a great sociology professor! His tests were derived directly from the book and the lectures so there aren't any surprises. Put some effort into your reactions and you will be fine. Super easy class, never did the reading until a few days right before the test.

Very kind and understanding, super nice guy and a great class, very discussion oriented and he is very patient with questions. Tests are harder than you would anticipate, run through the review sheet with him to make sure you know what you're supposed to, take good notes, slides aren't posted, run through writing assignments with TAs beforehand.

3 Tests all MC, if you come to class & read you'll do fine - they are not tricky and usually bumps the class average up. 12 Short papers due weekly - put some effort into it and you'll get 100%, 2 are dropped. I liked the way he taught. The course opened my mind and gave me new perspective. NOT A HARD CLASS. I spent 2hrs/week on homework &reading

I'm a Junior minoring in Sociology and I completed this intro class last (ironically). I can honestly say this class had the most confusing layout of any of my other sociology classes. Reactions were graded harshly. Tests were completely ambiguous and poorly written. In his defense, he hasn't taught this class in about 6 years so he is learning.

Made an introductory sociology course far too difficult. As a senior studying microbiology, and with many humanities classes under my belt, there is no reason that I should be struggling to keep a B+ in a 100 level class. Tests are ambiguous and poorly written, and with 500 points in the class, every point counts. Take someone else!

Lance is a really good teacher and I loved SOC111 ( I'm a soc major so I am biased) However, a lot of people didn't like him, but that's because they were so one-minded. DO NOT TAKE SOC CLASSES IF YOU ARE NOT OPEN-MINDED. One of my classmates posted a rude comment about Lance, which made me so angry, it was so unfair, because he's an amazing teache
I learned a lot in this class.  There are not a lot of assignments so you need to do well on the few he has.  Tests are completely essay form.  Nice man
He's a terrible teacher. He doesn't teach anything useful in the class and we never know what he wants. Tests are poorly written.
Here is your chance to be bored and get a C.

An A is possible, but be prepared to set aside around 4 hours weekly for   homework. STATA isn't too bad,if you need help with the syntax both Lance and the TA are really helpful. I don't recommend missing class or skipping the mini-assignments(even though they're worth barely anything) they build on eachother and prepare you for the exam.

Take this class from someone else if you can.  The TA did all the work.  He believes in trial and error as the best teaching method, which makes for some really frustrating assignments.  No rubric and hardly any instruction, but will dock points because you didn't guess what he wanted you to do.
Course is well-organized. Complete the mini-assignments on time!  Go to the TA's office hours weekly and you'll do fine.  Pay attention in class and ask questions!

Cool guy, terrible class. Unorganized. Everyone learned everything from the TA. I don't remember anything from the class, I just wrote what the TA told me to write into STATA. Take it from someone else!

This class was really easy. Proffesor Erickson is really nice and doesn't try to overwork you. The class consisted of reading all 10 chapters of the book(super easy read),1 Midterm, 1 essay, 1 final and 5 assignments. Got an A easily definitely a fun class. The tests are way easy if you were paying attention. Go to test reviews overall great class

So long as you show up to class and read the book you will likely get atleast 1n A- in the class. He's hilarious and puts more than enough time to each of his students if you just ask. Great guy, easy class, recommended if you need the credit.
Professor Erickson was such a cool guy. He brings interesting viewpoints to class and makes you think. This class changed the way I look at society, loved it. 2 tests, 1 essay = CAKE.
Interesting class, not very difficult if you show up every day.  Sometimes I didn't agree with his views, but it wasn't hard to understand what he talked about.  Not a bad class.
A very easy and interesting class.  Two exams and one paper.  Both relatively easy.

Professor Erickson is such a nice guy! He's so willing to help you, but only if you ask for it. Sometimes classes get a little hard to pay attention to, but at the same time, some of the topics are very interesting. The TA's are great, just make sure you go to the review sessions and go to class.
Funny guy. Makes it interesting. Really not too difficult of a class if you just do the assignments and take notes.

He is a great teacher. He is pretty funny and teaches the subject well. It will make you think about life from a new perspective. You don't really need to read the book much, but it is fun to read anyways. The first half is better than the second, but it is all better than psychology. It is not very difficult.

I liked Lance a lot. The class is super interesting (and beats the heck out of the beginning Anthropology classes) and I have learned a lot of things that I can apply outside of school. The work is pretty easy, just stay up with the chapter reading and get the few assignments passed in. Take from Lance, he is pretty funny and really down to earth.

Lance was my favorite teacher at BYU so far. His class was amazing, and it helped me realize that I might even want to major in sociology. He is way funny, makes class interesting, and tells good stories. He is really helpful. The textbook is great- you could probably do okay without reading it, but I LOVE it! It's SO interesting. Take this class!!

Professor Erickson is great! His lectures are interesting and very informative. You can get by without the textbook. Tests are easy, assignments are easy, and you get points just for going to class and answering questions with your iclicker. Great class!

Great professor. Can get by without the expensive textbook as long as you always attend class and take freakishly good notes. Lectures were SUPER good and informative. You get that "hey that's actually true isn't it." thing going quite a bit. Enjoyed his lecture on the marriage meat market. So fitting for byu :)

His class is really fun. He is funny and has pretty good jokes. Don`t take offense, he tells embarrasing stories about himself, too. I liked being in class, but sometimes the lecture can get confusing. The test whatsoever is kind of hard, espeically for internationals,based on the grades.
Class was not too hard. Prof.is funny and he made the subject interesting. The book is great as well and I enjoyed reading it.

Really funny, tests were easy, homework a breeze...  No reason to not get an A in this class.  Some students will try to debate terms and their definitions - just ignore them, their logic will only confuse you.  Enjoy his humor, don't take offence.

I really enjoyed this class, it was my favorite of the semester. Erickson was funny and made the material to understand. Easy class if you read the textbook and attend class. 1 midterm, group assignments, short paper and a final. Plus points for inclass questions and attendance (easy points). Highly recommend, So interesting!
Not too hard. The material is pretty interesting. Prof. Erickson can be boring sometimes but he means well and has his students in his best interests

I have a natural interest in people and this class was thus very interesting for me. I like Lance a lot. As written below, his lectures can get boring. Even though reading the book is not required, I'd recommend it because it's way good. If you put a lot into the class, you'll learn a ton about sociology in general. I'd recommend this class.

He's a good teacher and a very nice guy, but his lectures could drag on at times. He likes to include a lot of class discussion. He is very willing to help with application of ideas and the paper, and it is an easy course if you just attend class and understand the basic concepts.

All about managing risk through insurance and tax law. Not at all what I was expecting.  And the class is dull as all get out.  He basically just reiterated the readings.  Made it really hard to want to go. Too bad really.  He's a really nice guy, and super flexible about due dates and such.

He's a funny, nice guy, but the class itself wasn't that great. Seemingly pointless lectures, but the textbook is easy to read and interesting enough. A few of the class readings are actually pretty interesting.

He's an ok professor.  He's really nice but it's hard to pay attention to his lectures.  They can get pretty boring.  His grading scale is quite easy and its not a bad class.  The paper you have to write is a pain but not horrible.  If you just want a good and easy grade, then take it from him.

Really enjoyable class, he really has a desire to help, go to his office and talk to him and you'll feel good about the class. Does a good job of making it interesting. He's younger, though, and so less experienced if thats a problem for you.

Cool class. The readings are very interesting and classroom discussions were entertaining and at times humorously heated. At times the discussions were good examples of what we were learning but very long and drawn out. Entertaining but we got the point 30 minuets before. Fun teaching style.

Erickson is really helpful, he wants you to succeed. He's also pretty entertaining, and I enjoyed class. Tests are pretty easy, if you study you'll do well on the tests. The paper is a beast though, and pretty pointlessly hard.

Very interesting class. Made me think about a lot of different things. Tests are specific but he gives you a study guide. Study lecture notes. He is very smart and nice and will answer all your questions. Get his help on the paper!
Pretty good teacher. He's a nice guy, and it's an interesting course. Quizzes are really easy, especially if you read the chapter first. Lectures necessary for doing well on the test - take notes!

Was quite excited to take this class but very disappointed with teaching. Attending is a complete waste. Often, most of class is taken up by irrelevant discussion. Ties to cram important information in the last 5 minutes since he wastes the rest of class. A supersenior friend who’s a soc major highly recommends taking this class from a better prof.
Really interesting discussions. Basic Sociology but I still learned a lot.

this is a new professor. so.. he doesn't have it all together yet. this past semester was his first time teaching his own way. tests are only on lecture, the book is only used for open note online quizzes. it wasn't hard, but id take soc from a more experienced professor.. he is nice though. good guy.

He is a good teacher, he is new and is still learning how to keep the class under control.  If you do the readings (which are very interesting) the quizes are a piece of cake (open book also) and then the test is easy as long as you review basic terms and slides from class (as long as you attend and understand what the slides mean).  I learned a lo

It is a fairly tough class as far as quizzes and tests.  There is not much negotiating room on answers on tests.  He is a very nice guy, but I just had a couple of bad experiences with negotiating with him.  Don't let that stop you from taking the class.  He is a new teacher--still learning so cut him a bit of slack.  Overall, I would say my experi

I was not overly impressed with him.  I LOVE sociology and was expecting a lot more.  There was a lot of work in the beginning of the semester, but almost none at the end.  Readings were not pertinent to tests, but were quizzed each week (very frustrating).  Student and teacher frustration could be felt during every class period.

He required reading out of the textbook almost weekly but then the tests were taken strictly from lectures.  No one knew what to study for the test, it was poorly written, and then he did was not willing to disregard the poorly written questions.  He is a new teacher and cannot keep the class under control.

I disliked this class with a passion. The tests were written poorly, the teacher is very closed minded and the grading is too hard for a 100 level class. If you ask for help he tells you your problems are in your head. The online quiz and assignments are always failing. Do not take this class.

Young and new to the university. As a professor, I think he needs a little more experience, but he is helpful and available for students. He's even funny from time to time. The readings he requires are really good. I enjoyed the class.

He has a very rigid view of poetic style and heavily edits student work to match his own preferences. The feedback can feel dismissive of original student voices. He has not effectively taught the techniques he claims to cover, and his specific expectations for writing poetry remain unclear.
Lance promotes great discussion. He breaks up the class with fun activities. He did take a while to post the full syllabus. He's a fair grader. He has good people skills.

Took this class a while ago. Dr. Larsen is an amazing guy and poetry genius. He's very willing to meet with you and help you. Some teachers let you slide with vague, mediocre writing, but he won't. As someone said, a negative rating says a lot about the student, not him. No one has helped me improve my writing more than Dr. Larsen. 10/10 recommend.

I hated the subjective grading criteria. Impossible to get more than an 17-18/20 on your poems. Cant use ANY abstractions. He doesnt use Learning Suite, so you have no idea what your actual grade is until it's too late. I've excelled in creative writing throughout all of schooling. But he didn't like my writing style, and thus my grade suffered.

Fun class unless your creative interests don't match up with his. If that's the case, be prepared to be called out/shut down in front of the class. He doesn't correct writing techniques (voice, tense, phrasing, etc) but often tends to attack your topic. He comes across as "my technique is the only right way." Fine, It's his class; just be warned.

Dr. Larsen is a fantastic teacher! He has incredible knowledge and experience, and the lessons I've learned about creative writing in this class are irreplaceable. He is very willing to help students. and encourages your best work.
Poetry is tough but Lance will give you lots of extra help if you need it.

Excellent professor, excellent man. He's the poet laureate of Utah and rightly so. This guy is a poetry grandmaster, vanquishing the uneducated with his mighty trident of metaphor. Life-changing class. If you gave Dr. Larsen a bad rating, it says a lot more about you than him.

Plan to have your writing read and discussed by the whole class in front of you with you not being able to speak. A lot of reading and a lot of writing. Much more than I expected for a 200 level class. Overall, it is very helpful and Larsen practices what he preaches.

He's a very good teacher and very nice person. However, he is a big fan of poetry and it was definitely the main focus of the class. If you aren't a big fan of poetry then look for a different class, because you'll have to read a lot.

Dr. Larsen is great! He's super approachable and is definitely willing to spend time with students to improve their writing. The workshops, writing exercises and class discussions were very helpful for me in figuring out what I needed to improve in my writing. You'll love this class!
I would recommend him for any class.  He's a very successful poet and one heck of a nice guy.  He will really help you become a better creative writer.
Hands down the best writing teacher I've ever had.  Pay attention to what he says and your work will improve.
Outstanding teacher, great person, encourages writing at all levels.  Taking a class from him should be required to graduate.
Great guy, kinda shy, get to know him personally and he will help you alot. Loves his poetry, great writer. I became a better writer after taking his classes. There's alot of reading for 300R.
You will have a hard time finding a better writing teacher anywhere.

His geology class was AMAZING. Highly recommend. He cares about it and makes you care about it too. Walk in labs were cool. Occasional group pop quizzes. Good variety of assignments and small field trips were fun. It's a 101 course so just pay attention and do the assignments for a pretty easy good grade.

The hardest part was the semester-long group project, but it's broken up into weekly segments. Landon was such an amazing professor, he is VERY passionate about what he teaches and he truly wants us to understand what we are learning. He's an all around great guy. Do your assignments and you'll do great.

Prof. Burgener is SUCH a fun guy. I took a geology class from him for GE credit--I'm not very rock savvy--but he made the class massively enjoyable. His passion for this field is infectious. We had weekly group assignments, reading, etc (all manageable), plus fun activities. If you need an interesting, easy physical science GE, this is your class.

Dr. Landon gives great lectures, and you can tell that he is invested in his students' success. He provided useful real world examples for every concept that we discussed. Since he is a newer professor,  he knows how to relate to undergrad students and gives solid advice regarding study strategies, etc. The textbook was not needed/useful.
Tough class, but very doable. Homework load was light, so personal study was required to stay up to speed.

Dr Landon is the best. Lectures are great. He refers the textbooks chapters for every class, but you don't need the book if you go to classes. His grading criteria is clear, participation and attendance is 5%, and tests are 70%. He learns everyone's names and calls people out to participate and makes sure you are comfortable. Take it from him!
Econ 380 is very difficult but Dr. Landon made me exited to come to class. He is soft spoken, smart, and extremely selfless. I would highly recommend taking classes from him.

Great professor. Econ 380 is a beast, but he's a good lecturer and is very willing to work with students one on one to clear up misconceptions. As other people have said (and he himself says), the textbook is dense and completely optional for this course; I did just fine using my in-class notes and the practice tests to prepare for his midterms.

Dr. Landon is awesome. Super smart but also super approachable, and he really cares about his students. He did a good job getting me excited about economics! Econ 380 is tough, but he made it a lot better and was very fair. Definitely take it from him if you can!

He's really solid. The material covered in this class is really tough, but he teaches it really well and makes it managable. The textbook is completely optional, I recommend going to his class a couple of times before buying it. I don't think you need it. Overall, Dr. Landon is super chill and makes a tough class about as enjoyable as possible
Really great class, was definitely a huge jump from 110, but Dr. Landon made the material digestible and was always available.
Easy A & gradings. He provides tons of useful suggestions that could help my future careers & graduate school studies. Take him if you need easy credits!
Easy A & gradings. He provides tons of useful suggestions that could help my future careers & graduate school studies. Take him if you need easy credits!

Homework was often very challenging relative to lecture material, and poorly explained. Memorization expectations for tests seemed over the top. He is good at telling stories, and not teaching content. Dr. Baxter is hard to get ahold of outside of class time. Feedback on homework wasn't given on assignments sometimes until after an exam.

He rushed through lectures and spent lots of time on anecdotes. Really interesting, but not as helpful for exams. He tests on what he knows is important for you to have learned, but doesn't make it clear ahead of time. If you take from him, get very familiar with the textbook!

Dr. Baxter is a very knowledgeable professor and I am grateful to have taken the class. The homework was sometimes more open ended which I appreciate because I think it accurately simulates real world engineering.

Dr. Baxter was nice for this simple class, but he was a bit boring to listen to and he didn't really make the purpose and direction of the class very clear. It was a little difficult to figure out what exactly he wanted from our presentations.
I severely disliked his class. He was disorganized, spent most of his time on tangents, and wrote confusing homework assignments. The TA's got me through the class.
Excellent class and instructor. Made an otherwise onerous experience useful and interesting.
Did a great job but could be more organized.

He is a really sweet guy, but not a very clear teacher. Use the your TA as much as possible, they usually can explain the material more on student's terms. Dr. Baxter is too much of a genius to be understandable.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Dr. Howell is a great teacher. His tests were very fair and homework was managable. He discusses topics that are useful outside of lecture material such as graduate school, the FE and real life engineering problems and ethics. I highly recommend him for this class.

Dr. Howell is the man. He is very clear about what he expects the students to do. You basically know whats on the test before he gives it. He also really cares about the students and he gives lecture on topics like grad school, real engineering problems, engineering ethics, etc.

Lowke loved this prof. quizzes once a week; actually really nice. forces you to study the content in bite sized chunks instead of cramming everything in before the exam. homework once a week; took a while, kinda tricky, but I got 100 on everything. can submit hws in groups of 4. tests pulled Qs from hw and quizzes, which was really nice.

Dr. Lefgren is the GOAT of BYU. His lectures are super organized, and his lecture notes are even better.  tests and quizes are very fair. Goes the extra mile to support for students, and you can tell he's committed to your success. Among all the great profs I've had, Dr. Lefgren stands above the rest. Do everything you can to take a class from him.

Dr. Lefgren is the best Econ professor I've had at BYU! He's hilarious, a great professor, takes his students to lunch, and is very personally involved. The exams contain questions from the homework and quizzes, so if you do your homework and quizzes, you'll do really well on the exams.

Professor Lefgren is undoubtedly the best professor in BYU econ department. His lectures are exceptional, breaking down complex concepts into easily digestible explanations. He also grades fairly, and his TA is very supportive. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, I recommend doing so without any hesitation.

Dr. Lefgren is an awesome professor who communicates difficult material in a clear and understandable way. His lectures are often scattered with solid life advice and dry humor, which makes them extremely engaging and entertaining. Easily my favorite econ class thus far thanks to Dr. Lefgren!

His teaching skills have some merit, but they're not good. For me, his blatantly advertised system of favoritism is very off-putting. He not only admits to it, but he puts time & effort into an actual score just to know if he likes you or not, which doesn't count towards your grade. He also talks about it way, way too much; gives narcissist vibes.

Dr. Lefgren is a great professor, one of my favorites. I found his dry humor absolutely hilarious. If you come to class, take notes (especially when he puts anything on the whiteboard), and give a solid effort to the paper (you write it as a group), you'll be just fine. Do NOT be afraid to take this if you didn't like 388. It's very different.

Great professor. My only complaint is that quizzes and tests were based around trying to read his mind instead of understanding the material, but you get a good sense of what he wants just by going to class. I would recommend Dr. Lefgren and ECON 488 to anyone wanting to learn more about econometrics.

Love this man. The class does teach you how to think about econometrics intuitively. Lars does a brilliant job at this - hes one of the best. Be engaged in class and youll do fine on quizzes and tests. Start paper early for good feedback. Textbook is good too.

Very easy compared to other Econ classes Ive taken. I thought the quizzes were not as hard as people made them seem: most of the answers are right out of the lecture or on the sample quizzes. Gives amazing feedback on the project if you start early. A lot of the difficulty of the class is just changing how you think so it matches Dr. Lefgren

Dr Lefgren is awesome. Econ 488 is pretty abstract, but Dr Lefgren gives lots of examples which helped build my intuition. Everyone hypes up the quizzes, I didn't find them difficult if I listened in class and studied an hour or two for each one. He did take-home open-note exams that took 5-6 hours. I highly recommend Dr Lefgren's class.

Prof. Lefgren is one of my favourite professors in the Econ department. He cares a lot about his students, his lectures are funny and engaging, and he teaches very clearly and succinctly. 300 and 400 level courses are not easy but I'd recommend him for any course he teaches. I'm taking 488 with him now and it's just as good of an experience as 380.

Lefgren gives little to no resources for you to have success in his class. His lectures are off topic and confusing, his notes don't match up with his lectures, there are no set answers for any homeworks which makes studying for tests hard. Thirty percent of the grade is based on weekly quizzes which are hard. Good guy, but honestly, awful teacher.

Dr Lefgren is really a great professor and has enjoyable lectures. Every piece of actual information is surrounded by at least five stories and tangents, so you have to pay attention and attend lectures or else you'll be lost trying to do the homework. His tests and quizzes are not hard as long as you've done the homework and been to class.

Super good class! He sheds so much light on how economic research actually works and does so in an interesting way. Assignments are reasonable and he is willing to meet one-on-one and help with any concerns. This will help you understand other 400-level econ classes better.
Dr Lefgren is an amazing professor. He's kind, funny, and great at explaining difficult concepts in a way that makes them tractable.
I'm really grateful he decided to step in and teach 588 in Dr. Frandsen's absence. He taught us a lot of valuable things this semester.
Dr. Lefgren goes out of his way to help students. Very funny and kind. His tests and assignments really teach you how to think critically.

Econ was just a hard class, and I didn't do great. He was a decent guy, but his voice was really boring. It was hard for me to pay attention (which I obviously didn't do a ton of anyway), and Lefgren was a decent teacher and a good guy, but personally, after this class I am more turned off to economics than I am to him.

Funny guy, but this class is not for everyone. Conceptual, but extremely vague on concepts. I did well in 388, but this class is nothing like 388. The entire class is so subjective, because of that, it was extremely difficult. If you can learn to think the way he thinks, you'd do well, if you can't, you suffer.

I don't think there was a single day when I went to class and didn't laugh at something. He's hilarious! It kept momentum and interest going throughout class. Whatever you do, read the book, especially if you miss class. He focuses heavily on using examples to explain material. He's not the best at teaching, but he always answers your questions.

I really enjoyed Lefgren's class. It might not be for everyone though. His lectures are funny, but can be hard to follow since they don't follow a clear structure. Make sure you read the book. I felt like his lectures help you understand after reading, but his tests can be vague or unclear, although he usually adds points after for those errors.

The worst economics proffesor I have ever had. Has lectures are boring, cover things learned in the book, and are disorganized and slow. Really slow. His grade highly depends on the tests, but the tests are awful. Full of ambiguous questions. This class is dificult, not because the material is hard, but it is hard to know what he wants.

Really hard class, but so inspirational. I felt like I learned a ton during every lecture. I left econ 388 with so many questions, and this class answered a lot of those questions. He's an excellent teacher. There's a group project/paper, he gives pop quizzes sometimes, and the required readings are research articles--pretty cool!

Couldn't imagine going through the Economics major without him. He is incredibly funny. His class is tough, but so are all Econ classes. Know all the homeworks, quizzes and practice tests backwards and forwards and you will do well on the exams. One of the best professors I ever took at BYU.

So Dr. Lefgren himself really isn't a hard professor. I think the actual subject of ECON is what's hardest about this class. Econ was extremely challenging and by far the hardest class I took at BYU. He tries his best to change and improve the class during the course of the semester, but the tests are SUPER difficult and the wording is confusing.

Fun class, interesting material, but during the entire semester, it seemed like he wanted us to read his mind. There was no real method or steps to how we were to answer questions. I do recommend taking the class because of the applications, but I wish the course was better designed.

Dr. Lefgren was a great professor, easily one of the easiest ECON classes available and he makes sure that you can laugh consistently.  As long as you make sure to put in the work throughout, you should be fine. Be aware that most of your grade comes from the three midterms and the final even though they are not that difficult

Lars is the best. He is one of the most genuine professors and his dry sense of humor is absolutely hilarious. His Econ 110 class is way easier than Kearl's or Pope's. Do the homework and keep up on the reading and you will be just fine.

Dr. Lefgren was a great professor, easily one of the easiest ECON classes available and he makes sure that you can laugh consistently.  As long as you make sure to put in the work throughout, you should be fine. Be aware that most of your grade comes from the three midterms and the final

Its ECON 110, so what can you really expect? Professor Lefgren is probably the easier way to go for this class as far as homework. Tests are challenging, lots of assignments, but he is fair about the grading. Professor Lefgren teaches well, but sometimes has a hard time articulating the principles clearly. Has a pretty funny, dry sense of humor.

Easily the best professor in the Economics department . Dr. Lefgren's teaching style is engaging and interesting, not to mention entertaining. He takes the time to learn your name and get to know you. The class is tough, but you can certainly succeed if you put in the time. Dr. Lefgren is one of BYU's best.

He was generally disorganized, thus you can't really see where you are in the class as you go. We always got points back on tests because they have ambiguous questions he made up he felt bad for, mixed with online questions you may or may not have gotten on hw. Nice person, just doesn't seem to prepare much for the course.

Dr. Lars Lefgren's Econ 488 class may be the most valuable you'll every take at BYU. The material is so powerful and well presented. Plus Dr. Lefgren is hilarious. The downside is that the quizzes are pretty tricky, so watch out there.

ECON 488 is Dr. Lefgren's baby.  His conversational teaching style, his irrepressible wit, and very practical finals combine to make a great class taught by an amazing professor. The finals are take-home, open-everything (except other students and teachers). Every ECON major at BYU should take this class.

Easy, easy class. Do the homework (and practice questions), review the slides, and the tests are straight from it. Averages were low, but you literally just draw supply/demand graphs over and over again. Lars is chill, friendly, nice to students, and tells a lot of real-world applications. Great professor.

Professor Lefgren has a good sense of humor. The class is brutal just like the other ECON 110 courses, but it's not Kearl. You will have to work hard to understand concepts. Don't expect to just memorize things.

I was worried about ECON-110 - didn't want Kearl. Lefgren was available, so I took him.  The lectures weren't great (monotone and pretty impromptu), but the textbook was OK, I suppose. Tests were difficult (e.g., MC with choices A-J, with compound choices). HW isn't bad. Short writing assignments. iClicker points.  Not sure how I did yet. Caution?

He's a great guy and is really willing to help. It was always really hard for me to pay attention to lectures though. Maybe it was because it was at 2pm and I was aways falling asleep, but I feel like I got more out of reading and homework than I did from lectures. This class is interesting but is not for the faint of heart.

Dr. Lefgren really cares about his students and wants you to do well. He regraded our third exam to give partial credit  because he felt bad about its ambiguity. However, it is Econ which is a difficult subject so the class requires a substantial amount of work. However the online material is very helpful as are the TA recitations.

Although a great man and hilarious teacher beware. I took an overwhelming work load and wanted an easier Econ professor. Rarely did I leave a lecture understanding more than I did not understand. He even confused himself a handful of times to the point where students had to correct him. And his tests are super subjective to his crazy view points.

I have no idea why his ratings are so high. His monotonous voice lulls everyone to sleep. Lectures are very boring and unprepared. Econ 110 is tough no matter what, I wish I took it from someone more passionate about what they teach, not someone who wishes they were at home.

The homework itself is easy, as it comes from an online, third party system (Aplia). However, the exams are next to impossible. I am not just over exaggerating this. The class average on the 2nd and 3rd exam in this class were both below 50%. Beware of this class from this professor.

Lars is a champ. He is really helpful and is concerned about his students' success in his class and in their future careers. His 382 and 488 courses were both great experiences. Even though the subject material might be a little deep sometimes, he is always willing to help you understand, if you can articulate your confusion.  Also he's hilarious

I have hated most of my experiences in the BYU Economics program, but Dr. Lefgren was a diamond in the rough. He's so witty, and a legitimately superb teacher. This class was daunting at first, but he made it as clear as it could possibly be. I LOVE YOU LARS.

Dr. Lefgren is a funny guy with an interesting dry humor. His tests are predictable because he posts practice exams that follow the same format. My only qualm was that he would spend much of the class talking about irrelevant things and then do one example really fast on the board. Concepts were tricky. I had to spend a lot of time in the ta lab

Entire class is reading & discussing papers. Take right after 388, it helps put that class in perspective. Semi-pop quizzes to ensure reading & attendance. There's a group paper/project. Midterm and final are take-home, open-note & open-paper. Quizzes are a lil tricky, but grading overall is fair. He's all about brevity & honesty. I recommend him.

Professor Lefgren is great! Its rare when you get to laugh in an econ class, but the lectures were really entertaining. I struggled in the class, but he encourages group work, and if you get with some good people you can get through it.

Professor Lefgren is the best ever! I loved coming to class every day and I actually changed my major to Econ after this class. He is so helpful and so funny and really gets to know each student individually. I wouldn't mind if every single one of my econ classes were taught by him.

Professor Lefgren is my all time favorite professor at BYU. He is hilarious, cares about his students and will take time out of his day to explain a concept you are unsure about. The class is a little bit tricky, you just have to learn how to study for it. I wish he taught more econ classes at BYU.

Lefgren was by far one of the best professors i've ever had. He explains difficult concepts really well and makes extra efforts to make sure everyone understands what he is teaching. He makes class fun and even makes dull concepts entertaining. He knows all his students by name. If I would have I would have taken every econ class from him.

Hands down the funniest professor I have ever had.  He explains things well and spends extra time when needed.  I am retaking but I still do not regret taking it form Lars.  The material can be difficult and the tests are hard but he provides past exams quizzes to study.  Be sure to do well on the in class quizzes.

Lars lives up to his reputation. He is a very good teacher and a very nice guy. Try to take both 380 and 382 from him. I took 382, and he already had his favorite students that he knew from 380. He doesn't interact with the ones he doesn't already know. but if you get to know him, you will have a great time in class. He grades very fair.
He made it really fun to come to class, which automatically helps with learning. He's amazing.

He really is the best.  Don't need textbook, Quizzes each week (study 4-5 previous semester ones and you'll ace them), MUST go to TA lab and do homework there. It takes 1/3 of the time and you'll get a 10 on it. He gives all the previous semester quizzes, midterms and finals. Study those and you'll be fine in the class. He's a really good teacher!
my favorite teacher
This was a great class. Lars makes the concepts easy to understand (compared to the book) and the class is actually really, really fun. Overall it is a very good class.

Don't buy the book unless you plan on taking 382 as well.  Lefgren was brutally honest with everyone, and I'm pretty sure one kid dropped the class after Lars made fun of his shoes. He learns everybody's names and backgrounds so he'll have more ammunition.  Provides past exams and solutions which are VERY helpful.  Hopefully you'll win a $3 lunch.
Lars, the others have said is the most entertaining and funny professor I have had at BYU.  He teaches clearly and makes the class time go be fast.
his class was really good. he would teach until everyone was either understanding it or just too stupid to ever get it. funny and provides quite a bit of help for the tests which are quite difficult.

Most likely the most hilarious teacher at BYU.  If you cannot take sarcasm well, don't even think about taking this class.  However, if you take it in the morning, you will get your ab workout in here.  He busts through the calc a little too fast, but he makes the conceptual learning very understandable.  It is an experience to say the least.

Lefgren is a strange professor. He has his favorites in class (on a first-name basis with several female students). Not a poor teacher, but not helpful in office hours and loses patience easily. Can be petty at times, but overall fair.

Lefgren is without a doubt the most interesting, intuitive and humourous teacher I've ever had at BYU.  Class is cool, but the material is hard.  If you go to class, do all the homework and get in a good, hardworking study group, its not difficult to do well.  Also, in my opinion, his grading techniques were more than fair...especially on tests.
The best the fairest and most entertaining teacher you will find that teaches Econ.  Class time goes by so fast with Lefgren.
One of the best instructors I have ever had. He is able to take complex economic principles, and put them into terms that anyone can understand. I really enjoyed his class!
The man is a riot! He's more helpful than any other econs professor i know. Dont expect a good grade though, he's all about challenging you, which i guess depends on each individual.
He's a good lecturer, learns your name, spends extra time if needed on a concept and writes challenging tests.

Great teacher, he has a lot of fun and is entertaining.  He will stay on a subject until everyone gets it, he cares about how you do in the class.  But he teaches difficult material, which isn't his fault.
Lars is, hands down, one of the best teachers I've ever had.  If only every professor knew how to organize a lecture like Lars...

Lars is a good lecturer who has fun with the class.  He teaches the class at one speed - fast.  Some of the concepts are difficult to grasp, and he refers most people to his TA's.  Overall, he's a fun professor, but fairly difficult.

Lars is a very difficult teacher. His grading curve is a little lower for the Econ 380 class than others in the department. He is however very merciful (if he notices that you put A LOT of effort into the class.) He's pretty funny too.

Dr. Smith is an extremely nice woman, she truly cares about her students and the subject she teaches. Unfortunately, I have never seen a more unorganized, mismanaged class. Her deadlines are made off the most inane logic I've ever heard, and most of the assignments are a waste of time. She is constantly late but will dock you 30% if you're late.

She is really, really nice but it seems like she's teaching kindergarten. LOTS of small assignments that aren't worth very much but can be time consuming. I'd be a rich man if I had a dollar for every time she said "this isn't meant to be busy work." The tests were tough but worth very little. Get ready to put lots of time into this class for an A.

This class is a mess. It's just bad. She's all over the place and both the schedule and syllabus change about every week. Just bite the bullet and do all of the busy work with a smile, pretend to be interested in class, and participate. You don't want to risk getting on her bad side. Viel Glück.
Lots of busy work, way more than necessary. And Pro. Smith isn't organized at all. The  class is so confusing because you never know whats going on.
Her exams are hard, but they don't count much towards your grade.
Super helpful, but useless. Her grading is not constant at all, some days she is super nice, other days super tough.

Super nice and funny. Will try to help you and always will make time for you. However she changes the homework assignments a lot and sends out  emails the evening before changing or giving assingments, which leads to half of the class not having it right.

(IMO) She spends too much time discussing personal grievances rather than course material. The course is rather disorganized, as she is not good at keeping the schedule up to date.  Because of this, the students are often left guessing at when assignments are due. The weekly assignments and term projects are mostly busy work.

She is awesome! So friendly, funny, helpful, caring, but fast paced! She gives you a lot of practice though. Classes prepare you very well for the exams! Without asking her, she brought me books to help write my research paper. She responds to e-mails very quickly and is very reliable. If you do the homework and put it some effort, you'll get an A.
Professor Smith is serious about helping each student succeed individually.  She is very caring and energetic.

I love her! She is always in a good mood. She gives you tons of practice to help you understand the concepts. The 3 exams were all take-home exams, there is normally 1 homework due each week, and a 3-page research paper at the end of the semester. I told her what I was writing about and she (without asking her) brought me books about my topic.

Probably the most unprofessional professor I have ever had. She changes the syllabus on a regular basis and adds assignments. She communicates far to often through email after class and is not clear in what you are to be doing in class. She knows her stuff, but doesn't teach it well. She is helpful to students but is still very confusing.

Dr.Smith is a very caring professor and will go out of her way to help her students! Not much emphasis on exams. They're worth little of your final grade! With that in mind, the course is very disorganized, assignments change constantly and things aren't always very clear! But an interesting class!

She is wonderful! She explains everything in detail to make sure you understand it. She makes class fun, assignments aren't too hard and they are always pertaining to class. No busy work. And she really cares about each one of her students!

Dr. Smith loves what she does and her classes are very interesting. That said she's disorganized, comes to class late, and tends to go on  political rants. Other than that, she's incredibly helpful and usually answers my emails in an hour or less and she'll do everything possible to help you out if you need it. Great teacher for German Linguistics!

Dr Smith is an amazing teacher!  I am so glad that I took her class for phonetics.  I understood German pronunciation and spelling by the end of the semester.  She was a delight to have in the classroom and explained the jargon better than any one else I've met.
Very knowledgable, cutting-edge of her field.

Prof. Smith is an awesome teacher! That said, the class is tough. She assigned us two additional papers-not on the syllabus-the last week of class! She is great, so if you can handle how disorganization, take her! No tests, 4 presentations, daily reading and worksheets (she dropped 7 though), one group paper/project and one 10 pg. final paper.
I really enjoyed this class. She is really excited about what she teaches, and really knows what she is talking about.  There is a lot of work, but it really helps one understand the material.

She is an awesome teacher who is always excited about what she teaches--and it's infectious. There was a ton of work that wasn't on the syllabus though. But she listens to her students, so if the homework gets out of control just let her know. Totally worth it, just keep up on the homework. There were no tests in this class--not even a final.

Prof. Smith is by far my favorite teacher at BYU. She really loves what she teaches, makes class interesting, and is willing to help any time. The class required a fair bit of work, but it was worth it.
This is going to be a long semester. Unstructured class and under-qualified as a professor

This was a hard class for me. I also took it during spring term so it moved twice as fast. Professor Cutler helped the 3 hour class block fly by. Even though I wasn't super interested in the course material, it was a fun class. She was really good at connecting Christ to the course material and had relevant stories.

Not sure why I can't create an IS401 option, as that's what this is for. Prof Cutler was great! I came into the class a little worried due to her poor ratings but there were zero issues. Maybe she's different for 201, but for 401 she was really in her wheelhouse and I thought her personality and teaching style were great. Would take again
(for IS 401) She is engaging and unique. The group work was fun and helped me stay engaged.

Kind, passionate, and fun lady who knows her stuff well enough. The class will be tough for Freshman no matter who you take. If you want a good grade, actually read the MyEducator chapters and take special care to watch the videos for SQL, VBA, and web development. AI is allowed in this class and it can really help on tough projects.

She is super supportive of the students. The course itself is rigorous, especially without previous coding experience. The best part is that she gives study guides for every test that allowed me to get near perfect scores on almost all of the exams. Also, no final exam!! Attendance not required.

The beginning of the semester was difficult due to limited resources, challenging exams, and a heavy homework load. After receiving feedback, she improved by providing more exam preparation and slowing down during lectures. She is kind, but I would choose a different professor if given the option.

Professor Cutler is a great professor who teaches the IS 201 material with energy and expertise! Because the course moves at a fast pace, it is important to come to lecture prepared by completing the readings and watching the assigned videos. I would recommend taking IS 201 from her for an engaging classroom environment while learning IS concepts.

Very upbeat professor, they do a lot of in class examples for the content so if you follow along it's really not that hard. They do go kind of fast but anything you miss is online so no reason you shouldn't get a good grade in the class

Prof. Cutler is an incredible professor. She always asked for feedback on how to improve the class and immediately implemented it. She can be fast at times but if you do the readings and are prepared for class she moves at a great pace because there is a lot of content to cover. SOO many resources to help you succeed in the class.

This is for IS 401. Great and understanding professor. Many students didn't do well on the first exam and she adjusted the later exams to be more reasonable. Made boring content fun and enjoyable to learn.

Professor Cutler is very receptive to feedback and is very caring. Each class and assignment is organized and very thought out. Anyone that gave her a bad review is just mad because she actually expects something out of them and they wanted a cake walk. To be fair, the content was relatively dull but she made the most of it.
Middle school teacher that got a college teaching gig. No bueno.
she does a bad job of earning student respect in the IS405 course because the assignments are tedious and often busy work, complemented by her underwhelming and less than helpful lecture style

Our personalities did not jive, and I did not enjoy most of this class. I did however appreciate that she responded to feedback and made the final much easier than the first midterm. Most of the class before Scrum feels like a waste of time.

This was for IS 401. The semester isn't even over yet, but I've had it with this professor! She is a pain in every way possible. Boring lectures and a nit picky grader. She asked for feedback, but it was too late in the semester and didn't even implement it. Great lady with a great heart but just made a super valuable course unattendable.

Prof. Cutler was great. The course was hard but that's because IS is hard to learn and teach. She was kind and had good lectures/practice problems, she went fast but she also had lots to cover. TAs weren't great, ChatGPT helped more. If you miss a few points on tests, it drops you lots (4 pt each, 25 Q). She listened to our feedback though.
Nice enough as a person. Just not great at teaching or managing the course. Truthfully don't think the material helped her, but the grading was just so nit-picky and the learning was frustrating

Prof Cutler wasn't my favorite professor but I think a lot of that had to do with the class. The content was interesting but sometimes it felt like the class was out to get you. The first few tests were hard to study for cause they didn't really make it clear as to what to study. Homeworks and projects are kind of a pain too.

Professor Cutler cares a lot about her students and listens to their concerns. She walks through everything in class and always has a number of TA's up at the front to answer any questions you have mid lecture. The homework and projects are difficult. It is very easy to make a simple mistake that can affect the rest of your assignment. Be vigilant!
Professor Cutler is a good professor. Lectures can be a bit all over the place, but the class is organized enough to where you really can't get lost.
I quite liked prof Cutler, she's younger and invested in helping us understand the content. I appreciated that she took criticism and changed the way we take tests part way through the semester.

I really like Professor Cutler personally; I think she try's really hard to respond to her students and take feedback, but the school has set up this class making it harder than it should be. The tests and projects were very nitpicky about small things. The textbook doesn't explain things very well and Professor Cutler moves very fast in class.

Prof. Cutler is so amazing and kind. She responds to feedback well, about halfway through the semester she had us take a survey about how we were feeling about the class, and there was a notable shift in her teaching style after getting the feedback. The course requires a lot of time/effort, and grading is strict, but Prof. Cutler is great.

Professor Cutler is really nice but this class is not really set up for you to succeed.The tests were unnecessarily difficult and you only get one try on all the homework. The subject is not hard to understand but the class is just set up awfully. The other teacher teaching this class offered 5 points of extra credit while she only offers 1 point.

I do not understand how she is still teaching. Moves so fast thru the coursework and she does NOT teach she just kind of works thru the questions at full speed. One time someone asked her what Dim meant when we do VBA and she just said "I am not sure, I just know that we put it" and then kept working. She does NOT know how to teach. Just work.

Professor Cutler is genuinely so sweet and caring! She always starts her lessons with a brief inspirational and spiritual moment. The readings were straightforward and always encompassed what we needed to know for the homework. She always gave an outline for what to study for each test. She is a hard grader, but the TA lab is awesome!
Professor Cutler is super sweet. Just not a great teacher and the class is very nit-picky. She takes away points for pointless things even if done 100% correctly.

took IS 201 with her spring term. class is hard and lectures were 3 hours long and lectures weren't the best. BUT she was always really nice and brought us treats and things many times. was struggling with things and she was super willing to talk to me and make a plan with me. so i love her, it's just a really hard class.

Instructions for assignments were always confusing. Rough grading and she will be taking points off for the smallest things that sometimes we didn't even know about. The study guides were somewhat helpful.

She has a keen ability to take simple concepts and make them complex. She put a lot of effort into cute in-class activities, but there is not a lot of learning. So out of class she sends links to super long videos and articles where you are expected to take in all the material. (These will be nitpicked on a microscopic level on the exams).

This was her first time teaching this class so there were a few wrinkles but she was very good at asking for feedback and ironing things out. She is always looking for ways to improve and will likely become a great professor. Class was boring and everything was pretty much group work. I could have gotten an A without ever coming to class.

I thought that Professor Cutler's lectures were great. This was her first semester teaching, and she was humble and willing to change the course. She asked for feedback multiple times throughout the semester (and implemented it). A fairly busy class, but the assignments were just time-consuming, not difficult. It wasn't my busiest class.

Class was not difficult in terms of material but the most time consuming class ever taken. For every assignment you have in other classes expect 3-4 for her class. Your grades all come from group projects essentially but you are given very specific roles in those groups and so your grade relies on other people and there is no adjustment for this.
Arguably one of my least favorite professors I have ever taken a class from. Your grade is not based on individual efforts but rather relies on other people to do their role

This was Prof. Cutler's first semester teaching a new class, so of course there were some kinks. Overall, there were a lot of small assignments, but they were never a big deal. Prof. Cutler made learning scrum fun, and I think as the class continues to evolve, it will become more meaningful for students (especially in the core).

She is a very kind person and for her first semester teaching, not too bad! I did feel this class was a little overkill though. There are a LOT of assignments, quizzes, readings, and projects that became very tedious and most students became very apathetic half way through. She also tends to contradict herself between assignments and lecture.

Great person and in class lectures are unique - though a complete waste of time. She created the (poor) course material. Heavily penalized those who are not good test takers. Every single reading quiz is proctored and ridiculously hard. Averages are around 65-75%. Quizzes you on technicalities. Says inaccurate things in class as if its gospel.

Great professor! She gives you lots of opportunities to learn by doing! The content of this class is very practical and will basically prepare you to be a part of any development team once you graduate.
Great person and passionate about what she does but this class was just annoyingly tedious. Better to learn this stuff once you enter the job force than from some pointless busy work class.

One of the most knowledgeable, genuine, and kind professors on campus. She is so understanding of her students' situations and is willing to work with them to get them the credit they need, makes sure office hours are available if you need them, gives good feedback and tries to make the course as accessible as possible.

Professor Hatch is literally one of the sweetest people I've ever met in my life, let alone a professor. You can tell she is really passionate about what she teaches! Very accommodating and often brings candy. DO NOT SKIP LECTURES, though- seriously. There's a ton of reading, but duh, it's a literature class. One of my favorite GEs at BYU

Excellent class lectures, tests were quite hard. Tests give a passage of text and you identify which of many texts it came from. Slides NOT helpful for tests, just used to lead discussions. For a good grade, HAVE to go to class + do readings. She's a v caring person, will work w you. Has a study guide for tests, use it. Too hard for G.E., I think.

Pro. Hatch is amazing! Great teacher, extremely kind. Genuinely cares about you. Success in this class is not too difficult. Read the stories and take notes as you do about the themes and characters. Participate in class, take notes, and you will lock all those things in. I would not say it is easy, but very doable with a bit of time and effort.

Professor Hatch is amazing. There is a ton of work for this class, and the readings were honestly brutal for me sometimes, but they were really interesting. For me, this class was kind of exhausting, but it wouldn't be for everyone, and she really cares about her students.

I loved this class. There were a lot of readings but they were all interesting. If you go to class, do the readings and take notes on the discussion as well as the slides, then you should have no problem doing well on the midterms. I also would encourage meeting with the TA's and Professor to get guidance on the final paper.

THIS IS A VERY HARD CLASS. Most difficult class I have ever taken and had the heaviest homework load out of any of my classes this semester (including ochem). The midterms are crazy difficult there is a lot of reading. But Dr. Hatch is such a good professor! Cares so much for each one of her students! She will do anything to help you!

so easy and you learn so much from the course. assignments may sound intimidating at first but she gives you plenty of time to complete and would give everyone extensions, also she gives out free candy. readings were so fun and had me contemplating about myself, it will stick with you for a long time. such a stress free class

Take this class from Dr. Hatch! She's super nice and cares about her students. Not too hard, 2 in person midterms, a final paper, final project, some assignments, and then 2 journals a week. A good amount of work, but nothing that is overly difficult or stressful!

TAKE THIS CLASS! Laura Hatch is AMAZING. Never had a boring lecture. She really cares about what she teaches, which makes it better, and she really cares about you.
