She knew everyone's name and would bring candy. Her whole focus is helping you relate with and love the material. One semester-long project but it's broken down into easy chunks.

The texts we read and the discussions Dr. Hatch leads on them are incredibly thoughtful and meaningful. I will think about ideas taught in this class for years to come. I took this as a throwaway general while a senior in the business school, and it ended up being one of my favorite classes. Dr. Hatch is the reason why. She is fantastic.

I absolutely adore Professor Hatch! She is passionate about the subject material she teaches and you can tell! This was easily one of my favorite courses that I have taken at BYU. There is a lot of reading, but you can skim the material and be fine. She is also easily accessible outside of class and is always willing to work with you.

Doctor Hatch is one of the kindest, most thought provoking, and by far my favorite Professor I have had at BYU. The literature to which we explored in CMLIT 211 acted as both inspirational and the catalyst for a change in my major. Truly I could not recommend Doctor Hatch more highly.

Her classes are all discussions of the text she assigns and they're interesting, but you really don't need them to pass. Honestly, as long as you actually do the reading and occasionally read through her slides you will be more than fine. She's one of the kindest professors I've had and is very understanding of any extenuating circumstances.

Very unhelpful and is a difficult grader. The lectures were painfully boring. Overall I would recommend people to take a different course, or a different professor at least. Also she's one of those professors who uses her own (AWFUL) grading system. For example, you  must reach a 92% to get an A-. A 91?  That's a B+. Every level is 2% higher.

In order to get the grade you desire you don't just need to learn the material, you need to know how to explain your assignments in ways that she wants to hear it. The class is subjective. A big part of the grade is based on participation. This is also subjective and she gives you a shot in the dark participation grade based on her opinion.

I got really frustrated when I realized she does read through some of your assignments. I would ask questions that would never get answered. Your bigger assignments, some she reads, some she just gives 100%. If she actually reads your work, good luck. She docked me .5 points just because she wished I wrote on a different topic.

Laura Hatch is great, but I hated the material. Lectures were just discussing the reading from the night b4. I stopped going after the first midterm and did fine. Reading checks due b4 each class, 3 tests, and a 10 1-page entry journal due by the end. It's an easy A but I thought it was boring as frick. If u gotta take this class she's a good one.

I was really scared to take any Comparative Literature class because English is not my thing, but Professor Hatch was amazing. It was like going to book club three times a week. She is very understanding and caring towards her students needs. She is also very interested in your opinion and bases assignments on it.

Prof Hatch is so great. She is super understanding and approachable and is very passionate about what she teaches. She assigns lots of reading but emphasizes which parts are most important (and understands that this class is not most people's #1 priority), so the assignments are never as bad as they sound. Easy A. Low stress.

She truly loves what she teaches which is a breath of fresh air, but I personally found the stuff boring. The lectures sometimes droned on but there are sometimes interesting stuff. My biggest complaint is that she requires very specific wording for the free answer on the test so I would recommend taking really good notes on what she says in class

Professor Hatch was lovely. But the workload was RIDICULOUS. This was a GE and was my most time consuming class (context: my other classes were upper 300s). For example, we were assigned the entirety of the Iliad over 9 days, and the reading schedule did not improve. Completely unreasonable for a GE. DON'T take this class if it's not in your major.

I loved taking this class. Professor Hatch is great and I really enjoyed listening to the lectures. I found myself more interested in the texts than I thought I would be. As long as you do the reading and pay attention in class youll do great.

I love Laura Hatch. The first thing that struck me is how passionate about the subject matter she is. The class has a lot of reading in Spring/Summer, but she made me engaged in the material. I did not think I would love this class as much as I did. I will always have fond memories of it. She is a gem.

Professor Hatch is an amazing teacher. She remembers things you told her about yourself from the first day and is always interested in your accomplishments. She is super helpful when you ask questions and makes everyone feel comfortable. As long as you put in a little effort this is an easy and interesting GE.

Professor Hatch is so kind! Her lectures are really easygoing and it's fun analyzing various forms of art. As long as you make an effort, you'll do great. Not too much homework. Overall really fun and easy GE!

This class was not structured well, but if you pay attention you will be fine. She is one of the most understanding and kind people I know, and she does so much to help you succeed in the class. I didn't do great because I didn't lock in, but it is not hard to get an A in this class. Submit reports on time and focus!
Seemed mostly like a lot of busy work, she is forgiving but I would only take this class if school is your passion lol

Dr. Jefferies is the most disorganized professor I've ever met. Every assignment and test will have several things seriously wrong with them. BUT she is very aware of her shortcomings, very open with students, and very forgiving of student errors.We literally asked her not to have a final and she was all for it. Wants students to succeed.

Dr. Jefferies is incredibly scattered and always has an excuse for her lack of preparation. Exams are miskeyed, due dates are changed, class is cancelled, exams are cancelled. Her classes have absolutely no structure. I would rather have a difficult class with clear expectations.

Dr. Jefferies loves her students! She often has to re-explain herself which can be confusing. She lets you do test corrections which lets you really learn. She rewards you greatly for coming to class with treats and answers to questions you wouldn't have known otherwise. Do not rely too heavily on the slides. Lots of busy work.

Fantastic teacher. She cares about what she teaches and makes it seem exciting. She designates a day to go over the drafts a week before the papers due. It helps a ton and then take it to the writing lab. Do this, and you will do great in this class. I learned a lot and I think it is a great class to take your first semester to ease into collage wr

This class by far took the most time this semester, but it was worth it. I wish I was able to take it when I didn't have a full course load. I would love to have spent more time on it. She is a great teacher and has a creative writing background so emphasis was put on creativity. Not as much emphasis on professional research writing.
She is a great teacher. If you show up and do what was assigned you will easily pass
Really enjoyed this class. She was specific about grading requirements and what she expected from the students. Very enthusiastic about writing.

Her style, skill, and passion was contagious and she made it matter. I put in enormous amounts of work, more than Chem105/Chem106. She made me want to write and do everything I did about my audience. Incredible and NOT an easy A. I felt myself improve in her class but it came with sacrifice. She is there to help always. Would recommend with **

Laura is an excellent teacher! One of the nicest people ever. Will always help you out or clarify an assignment. Takes considerable effort to get an A; you really have to work hard but it's definitely do-able. My one complain is that their was quite a bit of busy work but I think this pertains to all WTG 150 classes. Work hard and you'll do great!

Professor Dutson is amazing. You know exactly what she's looking for in a paper, and if you're struggling she will make sure she can meet with you, even if it's by phone or Skype. You can tell she's really passionate, so class is exciting. As long as you show up and do the work, you'll do fine. I would definitely take another class from her.

Professor Dutson will make you a very good writer. However, she is a pretty harsh grader, especially when it comes to stating things concisely. She hates "fluff"(unnecessary filler words) Class is fun and she is very interesting to learn from. However if you want a super easy A, I would not recommend her.
My favorite english teacher at BYU! She is a fantastic teacher. She teaches with great clarity!

I think the biggest thing I took from her was a love for writing. Being taught by a passionate teacher who loved the power writing gave one was very inspiring.  Even better, she didn't teach us about all of the rules of writing, but rather taught us about how there are no rules if you are deliberate.  This class was a challenge, but a good one.

FANTASTIC!  I absolutely dread writing, but her class was definitely one of my favorites that I have taken!  She is so passionate about the subject so class is never boring!  Go to class and do your assignments to help with the essays.  Getting an A is hard work, but totally doable.  Put your best effort and it will show!  Take it from her!!!!!!!

Laura is AWESOME! She puts energy and enthusiasm into writing. She went from being a business major to being an English major, so she just has some neat perspectives on writing, people, and the world. She will always help when asked, and she wants to see her students progress. I would highly recommend her :)

Laura is amazing. She stands on her chair to express her lesson. You learn more than WRTG 150 or whatever she's teaching you, you learn a passion for learning. Best professor hands down at BYU. Harder but worth the work.

One of the best professors I've had.  Always willing to help you with anything.  Not an easy A, but very achievable.  You WILL learn a lot in this class! I would highly recommend her course to anyone that wants to become a successful writer in a college setting.

She's not necessarily the easiest teacher, but she's easily one of the best. She really cares about helping her students succeed and I felt like she was really willing to help me with my writing however she could.

She is the freaking goat. She is super caring and wants everyone to succeed. She doesn't judge you for your spanish level. She stopped teaching us halfway through the semester because of family issues but my time with her was awesome. There is homework but she grades super easily. I would definitely take it from her.
She is so kind and cares for all of her students. She wants them all to understand the content. She's great.

She's a very kind lady and you can do well in her class but you can't make mistakes. It's hard to know what she wants. The class was quite disorganized and her grading was pretty unpredictable. Assignments would appear randomly at the end of one of her many emails and then we couldn't turn in late work or do extra credit. Overall the class was ok

While I hated this class, I didn't hate her. She's a great professor and really cares about her students, but I counldn't stand the class. There is SO MUCH homework as well. Also she uses Canvas and I've never had such a poorly organized class/professor/Canvas page. I was consistently confused about what was due and when.

While I enjoyed the structure of the course and her teaching method was effective, this course felt more like a social justice course disguised as a Spanish course. Every single piece of literature that we read or analyzed was about racism, sexism, or discrimination and social inequality. A more varied reading selection would be better.

Overall great professor! She cares about her students and provides many opportunities to learn. She was really helpful for explaining grammar. The homework didn't feel like busy work, and the readings were interesting and relevant to what we talked about in class. I felt like she prepared us well for the exams.

Dr. Truman truly was an amazing professor. She strived to make sure her students felt comfortable always and always was super reasonable! There are a lot of reading but not super hard to understand. Some of her criteria for writing was unclear to me but if you talk to her she is more than willing to help you out!

Doctora Truman is awesome! She's super kind and funny and makes the lectures engaging. There's a good amount of work, but it's organized well so you always know what to do. She truly cares about her students and how they're doing and always has office hours to offer support. One thing to be aware of is that there's no late work accepted.

Dra. Truman is awesome and does a great job teaching. The work load was consistent but easily manageable. She teaches concepts clearly and is very caring and wants you to be successful. I would definitely recommend her, as she doesn't try to make her class hard or be mean, she just wants her students to learn and put in some effort.

Doctor Truman is focused on the well-being of her students and making her classes as fair as possible. It is clear that what she cares about most is the true education and growth of her students. Her classes do not have a lot of busy work and her lectures and homework are connected well to the exam. Just do the classwork and you will keep an A.
She's super understanding and you can tell she really cares about her students. It's super easy to get an A in this class if you just go to class and do the work.

Professor Truman is really awesome, she wants you to learn and will do everything in her power to help you do so. There are a lot of readings, but they are interesting and not too long for the most part. You only have to write like 3 short essays which is really nice. She is understanding and willing to change due dates as well.
It is a great class and you recieve lots of help and feedback.
Professor Truman is amazing! She cares a lot about her students and see's our perspective. She gives good and helpful feedback and promotes respect in the class. She is a very fair grader too.
It was a great time and she was super understanding.

Dr. Truman was wonderful and I really enjoyed her class. You can tell she cares about her students and is very accessible outside of class. This class is not very difficult, but also a great learning opportunity. It's also a great way to meet peers who appreciate the language like you do! Highly recommend this course and Dr. Truman.

Dr. Truman is incredibly kind and caring and was usually personally accessible outside of class via email. The homework for the class was not too bad when it made sense, but I found myself needing to reach out for clarification regularly. The online textbook we used had activites built-in that did not work half the time so that was frustrating.

Doctora Truman does a good job explaining grammar and getting class participation. I think there is a lot that has to be done online and a large focus on Reading hard articles and understanding them enough to write about them. That and Grammar make up a large portion of class material.

Great teacher, tough class. The semester I took this all of the course material got changed to a new curriculum which was hard on both the students and teachers. However, Dr. Truman was very understanding concerning difficult materials and made an effort to adapt the class to give the best chance for learning.

Dr. Truman is an amazing and caring professor. She's amazing at Spanish and helped all of us in the class learn to appreciate how other people speak. She's very kind and approachable if you have concerns or questions and she's genuinely concerned about your wellbeing outside of class. Would highly recommend taking a class from her!!

I love Dra Truman! She is empathetic and truly cares about her students and their overall well-being. Some criteria/preparations for midterms/finals were not as clear as I would have liked, but she is a fair grader and wants you to succeed.
Dra Truman is a great professor, overall I enjoyed the class, the workload is pretty easy to manage. The only thing is the criteria aren't very clear for the exams or the papers.

She knows her stuff, she's a very good teacher. The course organization is a little rough though, which may have been because she was trying out a new textbook. Several papers to write, not always with clear guidelines on what she wants but not too bad altogether. Tests are pretty easy and open book.

Professora Truman is super awesome! She really cares about her students and is very willing to help. Don't expect this to be an extremely easy A; you need to put in time and effort to get a good grade.
Very open about the changes in curriculum and willing to work with what we wanted

Dra Truman is a great Professor. She cared about us and adjusted to make things fair, the class felt personal. The class I took was a pilot program and was harder than I expected, but totally reasonable. A good class for learning grammar, but don't think you can get an easy A just with mission spanish. You will have to work.

I love Professor Truman. I was so nervous about this class and felt insecure about my Spanish but when I talked to her about it she was kind and worked to help me feel comfortable and improve. You can tell she cares about her students and genuinely wants them to have a good experience in the class. The amount of homework varies by week,

Dra. Truman is very caring and made herself very accessible to her students. Classes are always fun and have lots of participation. Assignments weren't always explained well and homework load varies quite a bit unexpectedly. This made it hard to get into a rhythm with the class. Overall great class, my Spanish improved a lot and she grades fairly.

This class offered countless growth opportunities. The combination of reading, writing, speaking practice, and grammar lessons was incredibly beneficial. Dr. Truman is an outstanding teacher—understanding, fair in her grading, flexible, and always open to new ideas. I would take this class again without hesitation!
She is literally amazing. I was sick a lot and she carried me through this class. I love her.

Dra. Truman is super caring and really wants to help her students learn and do well. The homework load varied a lot from week to week, the due dates weren't very clear, and the assignments weren't always explained very well, but the grading always seemed fair. Overall, I enjoyed the class and found it very helpful in improving my Spanish abilities.

Doctor Truman is a very good person and a great teacher, the class was a bit harder than I originally thought it would be, but definitely nothing beyond reasonable. Lectures are good, some days have very light homework and some have a ton, but overall it is a good class, you just gotta be very organized and on top of things.

She is a knowledgeable and inspiring teacher. This class will push you out of your comfort zone regarding the Spanish language. The class is heavy on reading. The canvas is disorganized which made it hard for me with due dates or knowing which assignments to work on during the week. Overall, I learned a lot and Prof Truman cares about her students!

She is awesome! She listens to the students feedback and provides opportunities to not only get good grades but better your spanish. There are a couple essays throughout the semester, not too bad. And the exams are part written, part grammar, both open note. If you go to class,complete all your assignments on time, no reason you won't get an A.

She was very clear about what she expected of us, and was willing to work with us.  She explains grammatical things well and worked through quizes and tests with us to help us learn from our mistakes.  Lots of good feedback.
She is awesome.

She is a great professor and I had a good experience overall. The class was a little disorganized but it was also a pilot program, and she was understanding and willing to adjust things if needed. There are two big essays and two cultural writing projects, plus readings with quizzes based off that and grammar. Exams were open note. Would recommend!

We focused on a new curriculum this semester so she was very understanding and forgiving. She's super genuine and truly desires for her students to succeed. As long as you do the readings and homework, the class is great!

Dra Truman is pretty awesome. She is genuine and clearly wants her students to succeed. There's quite a bit of reading homework to prepare for classes. Not really an easy A but she has clear expectations and understands that most of us are return missionaries and not Spanish scholars
She was really great but the class I took from her was a pilot program that had a lot of problems with it. As far as her teaching goes that was great.

Dra. Truman is a good professor and really does care about your improvement in Spanish. You are graded on attendance and there are a lot of papers to write in Spanish. Its not bad with grading but I felt it was disorganized at times about what's really due and what's not. The class felt chaotic for me and it was not a great experience overall.

Professor Truman was a great teacher. I'm a return missionary and this class was pretty much what I expected. It was more focused on the cultural aspects in Spanish speaking countries than I initially I thought. It is a good class to see if spanish speakers want to continue studying. Expect 2-4 hours of homework outside of class a week.

Dr. Truman is seriously the best! I was really nervous about taking a Spanish class because everyones abilities are different. She teaches in a way that helps everyone and wants to help you improve. Her expectations from the class were clear and if you worked hard you could meet them. The work load is manageable but you have to stay on top of it.

Dra. Truman connects with her students and genuinely cares about them. I expected the class to focus on grammar but was surprised by its emphasis on culture and writing skills. She sets clear expectations and holds students accountable. While it's not an easy A, paying attention to detail and putting in consistent effort makes success achievable.
Professor Truman is very straightforward and helps prepare you well for the different exams.

Dra Truman is great. Class is always fun. From what I've heard from my other friends in Span 321, she's as good as they come. Pretty steady workload that isn't too much but you need to stay on top of. Only frustrating thing is late work isn't accepted but grading is really slow so you don't know what you've got the whole year. Liked her a lot tho.

You get two free absences in the semester but she's a good teacher fs. The only thing boof was that she took forever to put stuff into the gradebook so didn't really know what I had during the semester.

Dra. Truman facilitates a lot of fun, interesting conversations in class and makes the material (whether it be literature or grammar concepts) more easily understandable. She's very patient as you speak but also corrects your mistakes, which I like. Some days there is a lot to read and expect a few big projects but the workload is doable.

I really liked Dra Truman. She knows her stuff and everything is on canvas in an organized schedule so its pretty chill. I didn't do too much work outside of class and got a 97%. She's clear on what's going to be on the tests and her classes are pretty fun if you have good chemistry with the other students and the teacher. I had a great time.

Professor Truman is really awesome! If you show her you care and want to improve on your spanish she will help you do so and give you the grade you deserve for your work! It's not an EASY spanish class but it is worth it!

She's a very kind lady and you can do well in her class but you can't make mistakes. It's hard to know what she wants. The class was quite disorganized and her grading was pretty unpredictable. Assignments would appear randomly at the end of one of her many emails and then we couldn't turn in late work or do extra credit. Overall the class was ok.

Pros: Class size is small, so it was fun getting to know the class and Professor Truman really cares about what she teaches.

Cons: Deadlines changed and were unclear, everything was straight from the textbook, and you get graded on your professionalism.

Overall Professor Truman was a great, she knows her stuff and cares about her class. However there were not many graded assignments, some of the hardest hitting grades came from pop quizzes and assignments done in class, there wasn't a opportunity to redeem points and fix your grade. Overall the class and grade expectations were very disorganized

I could always expect Profe Truman's class to be engaging and social; this is not a class you can/will want to fall asleep in! While I felt that some aspects of assignments were unclear or slightly disorganized, Profe Truman is incredibly compassionate and willing to make time to help. NOT an easy class, but if you put in the work you will enjoy it

One of the best teachers for this class. I appreciate how she worked things out with me and the class if we messed up on an assignment by accident. She teaches very well and the class is fun! The quizzes, tests, grammar, and homework have to be free of every error and be good quality. I worked hard to get the A in the class!
She's a good professor. She is new but she tries her best and wants to help students. She does have a lot of pop quizzes on readings.
Professor Haddock is well-educated and easy to understand. You will not regret taking a class with her. Just be aware for IHUM 101 we had a midterm every 2-3 weeks. Otherwise, a really chill class.

Ridiculous, to say the least. She does not know how to use Canvas or any of the proctoring technology. She has a no-AI policy. Not even for note-taking or brainstorming... She doesn't teach and lets the TAs handle everything. I highly recommend never taking this class. My other Humanities classes were actually enjoyable, not just busywork.

The class had one purpose: to get the credit. Don't expect anything more from this online class, it's a pointless box to check that stands in the way of graduation. The class expects way too much for a general education class that not many people will ever need again past the final.
Really funny professor with engaging lectures! Expect online readings and quizzes due before each class, but they usually take less than an hour. All exams are multiple choice and are pretty simple.

Difficult content! Use your TA's, they are there to help you! The exams were hard, so go to reviews and study hard. The textbook readings are long. This class was interesting because of Dr. Haddock. She was creative in giving her lectures and the stories she told.
The class was super easy, and you can tell it's something she's passionate about. As long as you pay attention and read the textbook, you should get an A.

Professor Haddock is great! She is an amazing story teller and makes it easy to remember little details during tests. There are only 3 exams and the final isn't comprehensive. Lots of papers but they are all fairly easy with lots of extra credit opportunities. There is a lot of reading that has to be done before each class however.

I loved this class! Humanities isn't really my thing but she made it so engaging. She teaches everything that shows up on the tests, and gives you friday labs with test prep (very helpful)! Very little assignments, easily graded essays, online textbook. Exams are also proctored online. She ends every class with "Bye, Love You!"

The only thing I didn't love about the class was the TA. She did most of the grading and would mark down some silly things. Lauri always did an amazing job in the lectures though, and she gave us alternatives to the exams which were a lot less stressful. I loved Lauri!!
This was awful

Dr. Haddock is great at communicating expectations and reminders for the course. She was super kind and spent time answering my questions and emails. You can tell she cares about what she teaches and about her students. Highly recommend.
Her class single-handedly made me want to drop out of college. condescending, prideful, and just a bad teacher

She teaches like we are learning how to load nukes in a submarine when in reality we were just analyzing a play or something. Get ready to memorize a lot of random stuff that you will have to delete from your memory the millisecond that her class is over
Lauri Haddock is the type of professor who puts nitpicky deceptive questions on her syllabus quiz. This class was a joke

She takes her job teaching waste of time classes more seriously than professors who provide useful education. So many assignments, so many tests, so much reading. I have watched 5 minute youtube videos that had greater impacts on my education than her entire course. Total joke.
The Professor was great, however, I thought her TAs graded harshly.

definitely take this class from her, such an easy A. at the end of the unit, you have the option to make a video on what you learned instead of taking a test which i liked a lot better. she is so kind as well. her ta is a bit of a harsh grader tho

Just busy work. But if you want an easy A, this is the class. You can get away with not doing the reading since its online but there are still a lot of dumb assignments. 2 weekly quizzes, weekly discussion boards, 2 midterms, 4 small papers, 1 final. You can get away with doing the bare minimum and still get an A but it is time consuming.

Impossible. She does not pair down the study guide at all, so you have NO guidance on what will actually by on exams. You can study for 2 weeks and it won't matter. DO NOT take from her. She managed to ruin very interesting material. Spend hours reading textbooks and canvas pages. Basically have to memorize massive passages of literature for tests.

Professor Haddock was passionate about the class. The outside readings were organized; she put direct quotes from the textbook on the test, so I highly recommend reading it. Most of class time was spent looking at examples of art, not the material you need for the tests. Tests weren't difficult but required studying the textbook & study guide.

Professor Haddock was actually super awesome. She is a really good storyteller and makes the lectures pretty interesting. Lectures aren't mandatory, but the TAs take attendance in labs once a week. Lots of exams, but they're not too bad. You do need to go see live BYU performances and write about them, but other than that, the class isn't hard.

Professor Haddock was fun overall, however the class had 6 tests in total (proctorio) and a short essay every week or so, along with 3 long essays. The TA's didn't grade anything until the very end so you never really knew what to work on. Grading criteria not clear.

She is a phenomenal teacher. I had a hard time in the class in the beginning because it was my first semester at college. She was very helpful, and going to her office hours was an extremely good experience. Wonderful person. Make sure you go to all the lectures and do all the homework; there can be a lot to take in, but she makes it interesting.

Dr. Haddock was great. I took her for IHUM 101 which I thought was going to be memorizing needless dates and places of historical arts. I was pleasantly surprised that it was more of an art literacy 101 class. Her lectures are fun and engaging, her attitude makes you want to learn more about art. Make sure to do the readings and you'll be chilling.
I really liked her lectures, she's really passionate about what she is teaching. She is very kind and funny. I totally recommend her! For every test, we could just film a video, super easy!

DO NOT TAKE HER. The tests asked us to finish quotes from the textbook, which wasn't covered in class. The TA said only 5% of the test came from lectures, the rest from random textbook and module content. We also had to attend $40 worth of performances, including an opera, MOA, Men's Choir, and a play. Homework was excessive.

Absolutely horrible class. Lectures are useless. Online textbook and so many readings. Study guides are so long and don't even help much on test. Random questions. Third exam on music is worst test I've taken in my entire life. NOTE: I study a lot and get good grades, I try very hard, and this class SUCKED. Please take it from a different professor

Ok so she is amazing. Her class is not. If you are a freshman dont take it. It can be overwhelming. SO MUCH READING. She doesnt teach you, you have to teach yourself with the book. Put in the work and you will get an A. It is just way harder than a GE class should be. 4 2-page papers. Have to spend your own money to go to BYU performances.

Prof. Haddock's class is tough, but engaging if you put in the work. Lectures are hit-or-miss, but the reading is essential. Tests can be brutal, so use unstuckstudy ai and attend study sessions to stay on top of the material. Overall, a challenging but rewarding course.
She is a great professor and she really cared about the students. I would take her again. I took her for IHUM 201 and IHUM 202 and loved both

I had little-to-no interaction with her during the online course, so a lot of your experience will be dictated by the TA's. Most of the course is pretty fun and easy. The tests are the trickiest part. It can be difficult to predict what will be on the tests, even if you go to the TA review. Overall it's a really interesting subject though!
I had an extremely negative experience with this professor

I took IHUM 201 as an online class. I'm honestly not even sure how to rate the professor since she was completely hands off the entirety of the class. The whole thing was run by the TA's and they seemed semi-clueless and weren't very helpful. The tests focused on memorization that was barely covered in the class. Good luck, you're on your own.

Honestly, the Professor was terrific; however, her TA's really screwed everyone over. Easy class overall. However, tests were unnecessarily hard and allowed for rarely any room to improve. Would take it again, but beware, it's difficult to receive an A in this class. It is harder than my Humanities 201 class.
She was okay. Her class was easy but then the exams were brutal out of nowhere. My TA was horrible and took an average of two months to grade a 1 paragraph mini essay. Friday labs are mandatory.

Professor Haddock is a wonderful person and lecturer. However, her exams are extremely difficult because it covers so much information-you never really know what to study. You do a lot of reading and write tons of papers. Also, you have to attend performances throughout the semester that you pay for.

It sounds like she is a fantastic professor in person, but Professor Haddock really fumbled this online class. She is unreachable by email, assigns readings that are never discussed further, and never provides information beyond the textbook -- no additional lectures or context, just reading from the textbook and taking quizzes on specific details

Professor Haddock is very nice and personable. I learned a lot in her class. The one criticism I have is that often the subject matter of the tests and lectures didn't quite match up, but other than that this is a pretty easy class and professor I would recommend.

I took 201 online and 202 in person and enjoyed being in person with Professor Haddock so much more. She's really funny and knows her stuff. She keeps the lectures entertaining and wants it to be an enjoyable experience for her students. There's a few fun assignments, essays and the exams aren't easy but definitely doable.

I never really interacted with Professor Haddock herself, but the IHUM 202 on-demand class is great! It's nice to take it at your own pace. There are lots of readings, 3 tests, and 3 papers, but the content is engaging and easy to follow. I wouldn't take humanities any other way!

Lots of papers that you have to write and lots of reading are required for the class. Exams consist of essays and multiple choice. You better hope you have a good memory to memorize all of the little things about the humanities.

Great, fun lectures, she's very personable and you can tell she cares. She works with you very well and made a GE class interesting. Tests are fine IF you take good notes & study well for them. She dropped assignments/pushed due dates back a few times which was really nice. Would def take another class form her!

Prof Haddock is really kind and you can tell she cares about her students but her tests are SO HARD! Shes a really anecdotal lecturer which keeps class fun but she never tests on the stories she tells so even after a TA review I felt very lost. Would recommend as a professor but needs to rewrite the tests to cover what you actually learn in class

Tests were very specific and had things like who said a quote or fill in the blank for a quote on it. However, otherwise the class was awesome. Lots of reading homework, lectures were pretty good and my TA was great and would give good feedback on papers/didn't grade too hard. Study guides for tests but basically just study literally everything.

I took this class online, I've heard that it's a lot different in person. I really appreciated how the course was laid out in a very organized way. The tests are difficult, but there are opportunities to get your grade up. There were reading quizzes, tests, 3 short papers, and a few participation assignments that were easy points.

Lauri Haddock made Humanities so cool and interesting. I loved hearing her perspectives, and she even had lots of pictures that she had taken in the Visual Arts unit. Tests are somewhat tricky, but a study guide is provided, and your grade isn't weighted.

Professor is super sweet, class is SUPER hard. I took it as an art GE credit and it was my hardest and most time-consuming class. My TA graded papers hard and the tests covered lots of information. We only had 4 exams meaning everything you learned all semester was compacted into only 4 tests. Lectures were pointless. Readings were necessary.

IF YOU ADD THE CLASS LATE the first paper is due the second week of classes, right after the add/drop deadline. Was able to get it done but took a lot to catch up on two weeks of material and an essay! Prof Haddock is pretty uninvolved and the TA's grade everything. The course had a lot of reading/memorization. Tough second midterm bc of that.

I love humanities, but I was really disappointed by this class. Prof. Haddock's lectures were mostly useless, and her Canvas was a mess which made it really hard to stay on top of things. One of the most disorganized classes I've ever taken. Tests were hard and extremely specific. She seemed like a fun person, but her class was a huge pain.

I absolutely hated this class despite liking the subject of Humanities. Her lectures aren't worth going to because she just talks about the most useless stuff. Her test contains random facts from the textbook that weren't emphasized at all. Her Canvas is also not organized at all and hard to navigate. DON'T TAKE HER CLASSES!
Great professor! I learned so much from the lectures in this class!!! The TA is what makes it difficult because some grade harder than others. I definitely recommend professor haddock!

I loved this professor, but the thing I hated about this class was my TA. There were two lectures every week and one lab with the TA. I happened to get a terrible TA which made this class way worse than it would've been.

I love Professor Haddock! She is a great lady who really does care about her students. If you want to take an interesting class and have it not be that hard, take IHUM 101 from her! She really helps prepare you for the tests and make her lectures interesting!! Great lady!!

I took this as an online class, which I think was a good call because there is SOOOO much information to memorize, and none of the tests or quizzes or assignments are due until Saturday night every week. I think that the class had great structure to it and if you don't mind a lot of reading/if you find the material interesting, it's a great class!

This course was online. You will have assignments due every Saturday. 1-2 Quizzes a week that include 15ish questions with an essay question at the end. You will have 3 papers on readings. You will have 2 midterms and 1 final all online proctored with Examity. Its a good course and a great professor but a little tough.

For a general class, you do an absurd amount of reading and writing in this class. You have to write 3, 3-page papers on very dense and hard-to-understand readings of at least 50 pages. You are also not given any rubric or any real guidance as to what you're graded on. It is classes like this that give general courses a bad reputation.

This class is ridiculously detailed and the tests are incredibly anal and require you to remember tiny details from numerous sources. You will hear from the professor maybe twice in the semester and the rest of it is the TA's or the textbook teaching you the class.

Prof. Haddock was so awesome. She was super nice and reasonable. The final was not comprehensive, which was so great. Her lectures were super interesting. Like all classes at BYU, the class was hard. But no surprise. But if you study you will be fine. I ended with an A. Take the class from her for sure.

I took this class for a GE and it was too much work for my preference. She is a kind teacher but TA's do all the work. The workload mainly consists of reading, and the tests can be really random sometimes. The class gets a lot more fun nearing the end of the semester. Overall, not a terrible class. Look up Quizlets to help prepare for exams! :)

Textbook is your lifeline. Dr. Haddock is SO funny and interesting, and I absolutely fell in love with this class the first month or so, when she would enthrall us with Renaissance artists, etc. But her lectures quickly became useless, and she didn't expound like she had before. Still a good professor, but be ready to do lots on your own.

Professor Haddock is a funny and loving person however the class was rough. tests were hard and so random that it was almost impossible to get an A on them. weighting scale is what saved my grade. if you put in effort for essays they will boost your grade because they are weighted the same as tests. do the extra credit and essays + you'll be fine.

Not a great class. I just needed it for my arts GE and I'm so glad it's over. The tests were tough. Three three page papers on the MOA, a ballet and an opera, weekly short essays, those were a breeze though. Five exams I think. Mandatory Friday labs. I didn't enjoy the class but I got an A without slaving away too much.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Haddock is the worst person ever at BYU she assigns so much reading and never responds to emails she has no compassion and she is super strict about her assignments for a GE class

Genuinely loved Professor Haddock and enjoyed this class. Tests are proctored and pretty difficult, several papers and weekly short essays. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but TA labs on Fridays are. I enjoy learning about the arts, but I can imagine this class being less liked for someone who doesn't.

Prof. Haddock is seriously the best professor ever. Her passion for humanities is palpable and her lectures are fun & engaging. She's hilarious & cares deeply for both the subject matter & her students. Just do the reading (which is very light and highly engaging), go over the provided study guides, keep up on your assignments and you'll be good :)
Do not take the online version of this class. Get ready to do hours upon hours of work if you do.

Alright, so Prof Haddock might not be too bad, but the online on demand remote delivery version of this class is hell. I was doing it during summer term and it was worse than the anatomy that I did in spring. Plan to spend at least 20 hours/week on it if you actually read anything. I've done 3 years at BYU and this is the first class I've dropped.
No structure. No Lectures. read the book and take an asinine test. awful class.

Prof. Haddock is the BEST! Yes this class is hard, but the curriclm is set by the chair depart not her. keep that in mind when you get hit with all the work. This is a GE course. You learn a ton. You read great things learn art history. Her lecture videos are wonderful. Shes accessible caring w/top TAs who really help you. She listens to feedback.

I loved Lauri!! She was a great professor, I loved her lectures and she was super sweet! My only caution would be dont take this class during summer, its a ton of work pretty much all the time, but she does help you out and shes awesome!
I am a STEM major and so humanities was not something I thought I would enjoy, however, Professor Haddock's class was enjoyable and very manageable. I would definitely take another class from her!

I loved her so much! Her lectures are so interesting and I learned so much in this class! Professor Haddock made me want to study and be excited about the material we were learning about. I would definitely take another class from her again! She made sure we understood what we were learning about and had amazing stories to tell, as well.

I took this class having read the other reviews and thought that this would be a decent class- I soon discovered how mistaken I was. She grades your assignments tougher than any English teacher that I've ever taken and the tests include questions that are derived from random facts found in countless assigned readings. The workload is overbearing.

Take this class from her!! There's 5 papers (but not that difficult), about 6 or 7 in-class quizzes, 3 exams (final not comprehensive) on Learning Suite. Her "textbook" is different websites about people/time periods. The tests are multiple choice and very doable. She makes the lectures interesting and has a lot of knowledge on what she teaches!

Professor Haddock is amazing. She's very knowledgable about the material and keeps it interesting. As long as you engage with the lectures and take notes you'll do well on the tests. There are a lot of readings but it's generally a very straightforward class. Prof Haddock is amazing & I'd def take her class again!!

Lauri was amazing and has personal experience and knowledge on each section we covered. Slides are posted, though they just guide her class conversations. Use the "Need to Know" for each section on Learning Suite. This class was enjoyable. You will need to study for the exams, do the readings and actively participate in class and you will be fine.

She was a fine teacher but did not prepare you for the exams. Expected you to remember everything she said and basically memorize the book (there were exam questions about obscure quotes from the text). The homework and essays were fairly easy, but the exams were killer.

Awesome online class. Read, take open quizzes on it, then 50 question test. I read and wrote down questions and then just crammed the questions right before the test. And not cumulative! She really knows how to communicate out to students what she wants and I actually really learned some humanities things.

She doesn't go over nearly everything that appears on the tests. I only got an A because I taught myself everything. The lectures feel very unprepared and she often just goes through the preprepared lessons that are already on canvas. On the last day of class before the final we watched a snowman movie instead of reviewing. Class is a waste of time

It's so damn bland but it's easy. For sure do this online. The first few lessons are interesting, but when it gets into music, dance, and theatre, the class gets super dry and the tests get extremely trivial. I was borderline A / A- with with spending 45 minutes / week (except for the two essay weeks) including reading and quizzes.

Professor Paxman is such a nice person who clearly cares about us. She makes assignments easy and I swear she extended the test deadline on every test we took. Homework was like once a week but it was 2 paragraphs tops and some reading. If you study for the 4 tests throughout the year, you will get an A.

A few papers throughout the semester. TA's are the real teachers in this class. Haddock's tests are too specific and she doesn't give information needed in class or anywhere else to do well on tests. Her lectures are funny and interesting but totally useless. I DO NOT RECOMMEND.
Does not cover test material well. You can attend all the lectures and read the assigned reading and still you get to the test and feel unprepared.

Unsympathetic, expects you to study everything she says even once, study guides don't contain all text info, TAs uninformed on texts and assignments, thus review sessions aren't indicative of exam content. Each class feels like it was put together the day before, feels like an online class, lecture teaches little.

I took IHUM 101 online from Professor Haddock. The class has quizzes due after every lesson, and either a short writing or a discussion board. The tests took forever to study for. A study guide is provided, but aren't super helpful. Overall a great and easy class, though that I would recommend.

GREAT lecturer. Funny and engaging. Take notes (she doesn't post slides). Mostly graded by two 8-page papers and three online (closed book/notes) multiple-choice exams. There are also quizzes (not pop quizzes) on NON-textbook readings. Textbook readings are long and dense; the exams are 75% from lecture and 25% from the textbook reading.

Here's the thing. She's a great lady, but when I took IHUM her class was NOT organized well, assignment due dates and test weights fluctuated immensely, making it very hard to know what was required for an A. Less than 20% of my class ended up with an A. Test are crazy specific, and assignments are graded on TA discretion.

This is my second class with Lauri because I enjoy learning from her! She's a great teacher, understanding, very reasonable, and loves what she does. The class has several quizzes every week, 7 one page papers on literature, lots of discussion boards, and a couple of tests. Great class to fill a couple generals!

professor Haddock is a really nice lady and she really cares about humanities, but her tests are way too specific. She completely changed the grading scale 3 days before the final and if you skip labs your grade goes way down. take an easier class to fulfill this GE

I loved this class; it made me feel like an educated person. Professor Haddock is passionate about the Humanities and her lectures are interesting, if not always important to the material on the tests. If you study throughout the semester, you'll do fine on the tests. The material you will be tested on is clear.

3 days before finals, the gradebook was completely restructured. Assignment groups were no longer weighted, and two assignments that had been dropped all semester were no longer dropped. My grade changed completely. Tests aren't over concepts but very small details from readings. Pro Haddock is incredibly kind, but I would not recommend her class

Professor Haddock is great! I will definitely be taking a class with her again. It seems like the work is relevant to the course (not much busy work) but some of the videos can be long. She cares about her students and loves the topic. You will leave this class with a new perspective on humanities!
I loved her sooo much. The class was interesting and she made her lectures engaging and fun. 10/10 would take again.

Great teacher! Super passionate about what she teaches. Her class isn't hard, easy to get an A. Three four-page essays (based off of live performances, so it isn't hard), but TAs are really easy on the grading for them. Super fun class, easy, and not a lot of homework. Study guides given for tests, so as long as you go over that you'll do fine.

She is awesome but her tests weren't always based entirely off the study guides she gave. You will get an A as long as you actually do the work. She is super nice and you can tell she loves the subject and cares that all students understand it. You have to go to multiple things outside of class but they are pretty cool to attend.

Her quizzes don't test on concepts, just random adjectives out of random sentences from long readings. I read them 3+ times and usually got 7/10 on quizzes. Her lectures are not necessary for the class and usually end up being her talking about her vacations to Europe. I was excited to learn about humanities but am disappointed with the content.

Professor Haddock is a good professor, honestly this class is pretty easy and doesn't require a whole lot of effort. It doesn't really matter who you take this class from, as long as you can memorize things before tests. If you actually really want to learn about art and stuff then her lectures are great. I tend to fall asleep, but I'm a heathen.
She is amazing.. connects everything back to God and tells the stories with passion. Super caring, funny, and engaging. Would take this class again.

Be prepared to memorize a lot but her class is SOO good. You just have 3 tests and two papers. She is clear on what is expected and she lectures clearly. She is very inspirational and I loved her class. Take her classes, she is the best!!

Wonderful teacher! I took two classes from her. If you can memorize, you will do well. She lectures very clearly and the tests are very straightforward but they writing the answers out, not multiple choice. Her papers and tests are not hard and if you talk to her about a bad grade, she is REALLY good to help you to do better. Take her classes!!

Honestly this was my least favorite class I've taken at BYU and I don't think I'm being harsh in that. Her tests test the most obscure things and don't even follow her study guides very well. Her class is okay besides the tests (still WAY too many assignments, quizzes, discussion posts, etc though but not hard) She's a nice person though I guess

I don't like world history, but I loved this class! Prof Haddock does a great job at showing how interesting history is & changed my mindset of it. Her tests are very fair. You need to go to class though because she doesn't post her slides. Class was kind of hard for me, but not most. Definitely take this for your Civ 2 GE, from her if possible!
I loved class with Sister Haddock. She is an amazing teacher, I had her for Book of Mormon part one as well and I just loved it.

She's an ok teacher. Some of her lessons are very boring. She doesn't teach the Book of Mormon in great depth. Basically a Sunday School level education of The Book of Mormon. She is a great grader! She gives people 100% as long as they try. Her study guides make her 2 tests extremely easy.

She is amazing. This class takes a moderate amount of work, 2 5 page papers, 3 exams and a final group project, plus a few quizzes. But she is so amazingly willing to work with you. She even let me retake an exam!!! And, even if she hadn't have, I would still retake her. She makes humanities come alive, even for a Nursing major like me. I loved her

Lauri is AMAZING! She really made the Book of Mormon come to life. The class was very spiritual and didn't focus on factual details! I was worried about taking a religion class at BYU, but her class is EASY and life changing! Her test was difficult compared to the very light workload in the class, but other than that TAKE FROM LAURI!!!
If you ignore the fact that she's a genocide denier, great professor! Good lectures, not much work other than a paragraph on the reading once a week. Easy tests straight off the study guide.
Sister Haddock is such a great professor! She's much easier than most of the religion professors here and makes it easy to get a good grade if you do your work. Her lectures are very inspirational.

Professor Haddock is an awesome teacher! You only have to write a couple simple and very-easily graded papers and read some chapters before class and write what you liked about them. She is understanding, willing to work with you, and really cares about her students. Highly recommend!

Overall a good class, though did tend to get boring at times. She obviously really knows the Book of Mormon and cares deeply for it and she expresses that in her lectures. The midterm and final were both online and were very easy. Other than that you're only graded on daily reading.

She's really funny and makes the subject matter interesting, she's a great lecturer who really cares. But her tests are IMPOSSIBLE. I studied like crazy way in advance for all her test and still didn't do well. The only other assignments are quizzes which are similarly insane. The final is a group project which was just the worst.
I absolutely loved her class! Her lectures were amazing, and she had a very clear grading criteria.
Overall a good class where I learned a lot, but lots of reading. Very straightforward for assignments and tests.

Lauri Haddock is one of the best professors I have ever had. Her lectures are fun and engaging and she knows her stuff! I came to love the course content because of her clear, exciting way of teaching. She is an excellent story teller and makes history interesting.

Professor Haddock is perfect for a Book of Mormon class. You still learn a lot without overwhelming homework. The reading reflections are a 1/2 pg about what you learned, and the 2 tests are definitely manageable.

Dr. Haddock has a way of helping her students see the good in themselves and the world around them. She is an amazing lecturer and is very willing to help and goes the extra mile to help students. She is amazing!!

LOVED this class and loved the professor. I didn't even buy the textbook. If you can memorize, you'll be set. There are two five page papers and a handful of reading quizzes but not to bad. Great TA and the tests are easy if you pay attention, memorize, memorize and go to the reviews. She is INCREDIBLY gifted and helpful. Take her class, I LOVE her
Greatest teacher ever!! I LOVED her class and the work load was very reasonable. If you can memorize well, you will do well in the class. I LOVE Sister Haddock!!
I loved Professor Haddock! Her class was so fun, and her lectures were very interesting. You HAVE to go to class, but it's worth it! Definitely would recommend.

Reading assignments from the Book of Mormon Every Day, and you have to write a 1/2 page report on what was significant to you. It's super easy, and makes up most of your grade. There are 3 tests and 3 papers. Everything is pretty much completion, and the tests are a piece of cake if you pay attention and read. Sister Haddock is amazing!!!

I'm not usually into Humanities, but this class made me love learning about art and cultural history! Sister Haddock is an entertaining and  informative teacher lecturer and is very willing to work with you.

Professor Haddock is a great teacher!  You can tell that she loves teaching and loves humanities because she teaches passionately and is always very excited and energetic. I would definitely take this class again. Professor Haddock was so entertaining. I loved attending class. Lots of memorization, but I just remembered a lot of it from lecture because it was so memorable!

Professor Haddock is awesome! The lectures are super entertaining and as long as you go to class and take notes and go through the terms to know in the text book, it's easy to pass. I loved this class so much that I'm taking another class from Haddock next semester.

Professor Haddock was so amazing at teaching a not so exciting GE course! She brought the gospel into the class that you wouldn't expect for Humanities. Professor Haddock was the best teacher I have ever had at BYU. I am a science major and I normally do not likerelate to artsy subjects like humanities or the people that teach them. Two five-page papers without much background throughout the semester. For a GE, I learned a lot. She keeps things interesting.

Sis Haddock is a phenomenal teacher. She teaches you how to learn and gives you the tools to grow as a student, not just in her class. Proffesor Haddock is one of my all time favorite professors at Brigham Young University. She was fair and was willing to listen to her students. Terrible, Terrible exams. We didn't go over half the content that was tested on. Not worth receiving a poor grade unless you don't care about grades, then it is an interesting class. Interesting class, terrible exams. No multiple choice or true or false questions

Absolutely terrible. her class should be a grammar course because clearly that is more important than the concepts. SUCKS don't take her.

Great Professor and great class. Test are hard, a few quiz's and two papers to write. So over all not bad. She is always willing to help you out with anything and cares about her students.

This is the second class I've taken from Prof. Haddock. It's the class I look forward to the most because she he a unique ability to make learning interesting. She's passionate about the subject. Sister Haddock is the best Humanities teacher out there. I'm not necessarily a fan of artsy stuff (I took this as a GE), but Sister Haddock made me love this class. She makes it really easy to get an A as long as you put in an honest effort. I definitely recommend taking her class!!

AMAZING profesor! I've taken both HUM classes from her and I love it! I am a science major, so I always dreaded the arts requirements, but she made even me love the subject. She is such a great lecturer and so willing to help. I honestly loved going to her class- I looked forward to it!

Sister Haddock is one of my FAVORITE professors!! She worries about your grade and will go out of her way to help you, all u have to do is ask. Tests, are more lecture based than reading. Professor Haddock is the greatest teacher ever! I wish that she could teach all of my classes. She is just absolutely awesome!!!!!! I love going to her class! She is hilarious, and the lectures are always interesting. You can tell that she truly cares about what she is teaching. Sister Haddock is the best! I've taken Ihum 101 and 201 from her, and plan on taking 202 from her. She is  passionate about what she teaches and she really cares about her students.
