I really enjoyed her classes, even though the tests had a lot of trivia questions on them.  She's very personable and tries to develop good relationships with her students.  I always appreciated her insight and enthusiasm.  She'll get you addicted to beauty!

A GREAT teacher. but very difficult. I respect this teacher a lot, and would like to take another class from her. But id rather get a good grade in a mediocre class, then a bad grade in an excellent class. I'd audit, but not enroll.

everyone is downplaying how hard she is.she has the humor of ellen degeneris, witty, but her tests are fill in the blank. she's merciless. take every opportunity for extra credit.she grades reports hard,must know obscure terms, dates, and people. my TA was a brat & didn't know anything at reviews
Test didnt really have anything to do with lectures.  But she is a really cool person...sometimes tends to favor some students, but overall, she knows her stuff

The class itself, as far as the lectures go, it is really entertaining and she kept me entertained daily with her humor.  The exams are insanely difficult, I would not recommend taking this class lightly in terms of academics.

Prof. Haddock has an engaging teaching style and a clear, contagious love for the course material.  You will attend multiple cultural events and write papers detailing your experiences, so be prepared.
This is one of the best ways to get an Arts/Letters GE.  It's pretty hard, but well worth the effort.  She is the coolest teacher- one of my favorites.  Take it from her and you'll love it.
Wonderful professor! was very good at reviewing things in class really wants you to do well.
Her class is amazing.  She brings enthusiasm and excitement to class. I learned a ton of things.
Laurie Haddock is the best teacher on the face of the planet!!  Even if you don't like Humanities, take the class.  She'll make you love it!!

Makes you love the subject material and you really learn. The outside work is all related to what you are learning about. Her tests are somewhat hard but if you study and attend class you are fine.i went to Europe with her I loved it that much!
Great teacher she really enjoys the subject and helps her students enjoy it too. A bit of work but it is worth it
Outstanding.  She made me want to major in Humanities.  She is by far my favorite professor.  Honestly made me love the subject matter.  Outstanding.
Great teacher.  Makes Humanities a fun subject.  She enjoys teaching, and you can tell that she wants you to get a good grade.
Awesome teacher!  Definitely take from her!

Loved this class not just because it was supper easy, but because it was also very enlightening and interesting. I learned a ton and I now appreciate art and the humanities tons more. If you have to take any humanities take whatever you can from Lauri.
Lectures are boring but the class is pretty easy
If you are a guy this class will bore you to death. But it's pretty easy.
Her lectures are very interesting
Class is interesting & easy if take good notes and study them.  Way cool.

I took him during Winter 2025 and see is a nice professor. Every story he shared was an opportunity to learn real life application and I never felt he was showing off his experience or life. He cares about students and would help you. Easy lectures and he curved the quizzes a lot.

Lee gets to know everyone in the class by name and genuinely wants you to succeed. He will call on people randomly, but not in a condescending or intimidating way. You don't get to pick your groups for the 3 group projects, so it's difficult when others procrastinate or are incompetent. The discussions about world news were great.

Professor Daniels is a great person. He is truly there for the students benefit. There is a definite learning curve with the class. It is completely possible to get an A. 
The coursework is difficult, however, he is looking for quality effort. The projects are difficult, so make sure you always start early on them and put a lot of effort in.
He'll talk more about himself than about international marketing.

Prof. Daniels is the real deal, massively successful in business, former stake president/mission pres, so he has a lot of executive experience to draw from, and he shared these nuggets with his students. His "Gospel MBA" devotionals at the beginning of class were so good, & he got to know everyone in class personally. That said, homework was tough!

From what I can tell the class is more organized after Covid. There are 3 major group projects (10+ pages), 2 quizzes a week, and a case study a week. Case study rubric is unclear and the TA started its own rubric and didn't share the rubric with us. Overall the class is not that bad, make sure you put in a lot of effort on the group projects.

Read the other negative reviews and pay attention to them. Daniels gives students a week and a paragraph of instruction to write 8-10 page research papers. W/o a rubric to clarify expectations, we always did poorly. He says all of the information is provided on the class website to prepare for tests. That is not at all true. Requires specificrecall

I had Lee for both the international marketing class and the intro to international business class. The classes are pretty much the same, so there has to be a structure and plan even if it doesn't seem like there is. Whenever he told us about his experiences, it was for our benefit and not just to brag about his accomplishments. Great teacher!

Pretty much all of the reviews have some truth. He does like to flex on us every chance he gets and there is no organization, syllabus or structure to the class. However, this was a great option to get advice and expertise applicable to the real world. Classwork and the homework have no correlation. Class discussions are whatever he feels like.

Do not take as a causal elective. Take Global Negotiations if you want an intl class. Daniels *humble* brags half the class about his wealth, experience, and connections. He wants so many specific things, and doesnt tell you upfront. Get ready for some begging after long hours of ambiguous work. Our class average on project 1 was  66% (44-82).

Dr. Daniels is an amazing professor and his class was probably the most valued class I have taken at BYU. He cares about his students and offers to looks over the resume of each of his students (I did it and it was a big help). The class wasn't too hard although it wasn't super well structured, but the lessons you will learn can make your career.

He isn't as bad as some of the comments are describing him. Honestly, not that hard of a class. Yes you have 3 group projects where you have to write a 8-10 page report. but distributed between 4-5 people it isn't too much work. There was never a syllabus that was given out which was my biggest complaint, but tests were off powerpoints and not hard

This class is hands down one of the best classes I have ever taken. He teaches more real life applications and I feel like I learned so much. I started a business during that semester and he was extremely helpful and available outside of class time. The class is a little more difficult, but trust me, its worth it.

Only one midterm and a Final, both of which are cake because he gives you the notes/powerpoints to study beforehand. Group projects, but not difficult. Grades them tougher than he should. Attendance isn't mandatory as his lectures aren't very useful, but more gospel related. Great guy, easier business class. I'd recommend him for sure. Not too hard

He loves the gospel which is great but he seems to forget that he is supposed to be teaching a business class. We once spent an entire class period talking about the hierarchy of the church. Lots of group work with little explanation. Lectures are basically either him telling stories or talking about current event homework.
best class I've ever taken hands down!

Professor Daniels is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. His lectures are applicable to real life business and he gives very beneficial career guidance. He has accomplished a lot in his life and the stories he shares are to help you understand the content, not to brag. Put in some quality effort on projects and you'll get an A.

Prof. Daniels teaches according to what you need to know in the real world. I loved his class structure. Tells a lot of great stories about his personal experiences working in the US and abroad that you can apply in your future careers. I HIGHLY recommend taking this class from him.

Former stake and mission president. Former CEO of ATT Asia. Participated in various investment capital groups. Great guy. I actually thought he was really humble for what he has accomplished. He's very lenient on classroom content. You don't need the book. All of his tests come from slides and discussion. We did questions from the book maybe twice.

It is the best Business class I had at BYU. I feel that I learned useful things for my future career. However his tests do not reflect what we learn and I couldn't get a better grade then a B. However if I had the choice to take the class again, I would. I gained a ton of his class and the group projects are fun too.

Don't listen to the other comments. Prof Daniels has worked hard to be as successful as he is, and I respect him for that. He gives lots of real world examples and his lectures are very applicable and helpful to our future. For a 400 level class it was cake. Grades hard on the group assignments. He is a great man and knows what leadership is.

STAY AWAY! This guy brags about all the money he has made, the class is disorganized and there is A TON OF WORK! Five 8-10 page papers with presentations. If you want your life to suck, take his international business class.
He is an awesome man. He really cares about his students and is so willing to help you. Tests are open note, so do your work and it is an easy class!

Wonderful man with a load of business knowledge-horrible teacher. Class was disorganized and I learned very little about intl marketing. He told a lot of stories about Japan and his travels to every single country, but it had very little to do with the class. He'd give assignments and then "teach us a lesson" by bashing our work. Take it to network

this class was so much fun! really great teacher, i was reading the reviews and i completely disagree. i learned a lot and learned what it will be like to work in the real world. he tells a lot of stories, and who cares if he is wealthy. i enjoyed learning from the millionare

This class was challenging, but i really liked it. I learned about the real world unlike a lot of classes taught at BYU.  Peers grade your presentations; which i felt was very useful. He does tell a lot of stories but i learned a lot. If you like to learn straight from the text book and just lectures and slides, this may not be the class for you.
I thought he was great. He used a lot of his own experiences to bring reality into the curriculum.

He was awful.  He bragged constantly and thought he was amazing.  I found his wealth (which he mentioned several times) sickening.  I was so distracted by how much I disliked the man I learned nothing.  But if you have a thing for millionaires - go ahead and sign up.
Never sticks to sylabus because he doesnt plan anything.  Just shows up and whatever pops into his head is what we study.  I learned nothing in that class.  STAY AWAY!

Professor is a great professor and has a lot to contribute to the class.  He is funny, easy going, but also not a push-over.  He grades according to real world business styles.  End of the year party at his place in Park City was GREAT!  Highly recommend!

The TA's of CS329 made this class a good experience for me. Many were online to answer questions, even at random hours of the day, and they always provided good feedback. I barely attended lecture and simply worked through the material provided on GitHub. I think Professor Jensen has improved on responding to questions nicely as well.

Professor Jensen is a good person with good intentions, but he moves so fast through the lectures and anything coding related, and wasn't the best at answering questions from students. It was a great class, and I enjoyed it a lot though. I wish he was more respectful when students would ask questions. Hope he reads this and notices.

GOAT about sums it up. He actually knows whats up in the software world and is willing to voice his opinions. Show up to class, don't procrastinate chess, and don't antagonize the TAs and you'll be fine. Tests were a breeze, the project a little harder but not bad if you have ever coded anything by yourself before.

He's a fun and energetic guy with entertaining lectures, but not great at listening to students' questions. His responses were often sarcastic or he would imply that the question was unnecessary. This created an environment where students were afraid to ask questions despite it seeming like at least 50% of the class was confused at any given point.

Want candy for getting the right answer? Jensen's your guy. He has years of work experience that make him a great teacher for QA and DevOps. His github instructions are very clear and easy to follow, most assignments were step-by-step tutorials. Forgiving late policy. He is very friendly and wants to help, just ask your questions.

Jensen is a goofball, fun and engaging. He's not afraid to make mistakes during class and challenge your thinking. Review the github before class and get 2x as much out of the lecture. I got a concussion and fell behind, he helped me catch up 1-on-1 in office hours. He is very caring and just wants students to have a good experience in his class.
Awesome class! If you read the material and put around three hours of work a week. This will be your lightest class. Plus, the lectures are super fun and Professor Jensen is a great professor!

Prof Jensen did a good job handling this class. No final/midterms, just a semester long project of building a website. Class is more an intro to the topic and there is a decent amount you have to learn on your own if you want to do anything off the beaten path of the example project. Lectures were somewhat engaging but don't put off deliverables.

Certain types of students love Prof. Jensen go to class once and see if you're part of that minority. Don't ask questions in Discord, or he'll lambaste you like the class dunce. He falsely accused others of using GenAI. Only saving grace is you don't need to show up to class to get an A. Get used to hearing, "I gave up money to come teach you guys"

I never once asked a question in class or on the class Discord because I saw him respond poorly to several students. If you want an easy class, 329 isn't the worst option, but I wouldn't recommend Jensen for any class. I couldn't make it through more than 5 lectures. You could give one a shot and see if you like his style, but I don't get the hype.

I know that a lot of people loved this professor. I totally get it. We spend the year just working on one project- our website. There also wasn't a final or midterm. HOWEVER, we barely learned anything in class. I feel like I had to do most of my learning with Chat GPT as my guide. Would not recommend.

If you are going to take CS 240, Jensen is a great choice. He helps you really understand the concepts, not just for the big chess program, but how to apply it to beyond that. While lectures aren't required, it was still good to get an introduction to what you'll be working on and how you can expand it to future projects.

Prof Jensen was amazing! I don't normally go to class for cs since most classes have so many online resources but professor jensen explained things so well that it made it worth it. He is always willing to take questions and takes the time to explain until you understand. CS 240 is a lot of project time but is very manageable if you stay up on it.

Very optimistic and caring professor. Sometimes a little overwhelming in character and course material, but if you are actiively engaged you will learn a LOT about really essential CS topics. Would recommend for both 260 and 240 especially if you are looking to do full stack development in the future.

Professor Jensen did a great job. He cares about his students and is very helpful outside of class. It was fast paced initially which was maybe overwhelming at the beginning of the class but it was great to have a slower pace towards the end of the class. I feel like I learned a ton from his style of teaching and his lectures.

If you're going to take CS 260 from anybody, take it from Lee Jensen. It's clear that he has put in a lot of work into course development to make it approachable for students while still learning a lot. This class is what you put into it. You can do the bare minimum and get an A, but there's a lot to learn if you put the time and effort in.

Lee is a great teacher for 260. The class consists of creating a website and adding various technologies to it throughout the semester. There is a website that walks through everything you will need to do, so you don't need to attend class. Lee really enjoys teaching this and loves the course material. If you stay on top of it, it is an easy A.

Professor Jensen is authentic, caring, and energetic in lectures. He manages the class well, is very active on Discord, and wants to help you succeed. Attendance isn't required and you can get an A with the bare minimum, but don't let the website get ahead of you--it can easily become unmanageable. Good class to take concurrently with CS 240.

Very optimistic and encouraging! Teaches his students to be excited about the material. There is a LOT of content in 260 and it gets overwhelming quickly if you are really trying to carefully understand it well. Lectures are sometimes confusing and hard to follow but overall a good professor and the material is doable if you are proactive.

He's an amazing teacher. Helps students out, gives tons of learning opportunities, and makes it fun. This is a challenging class though so make sure you make time for it. You can get by doing the bare minimum but you can really learn a TON if you try.
So fun, he teaches amazingly well. This has gotta be my favorite class I've ever taken. You should take cs260 from professor Jensen!

Dr. Jensen is awesome as a human being and a teacher. He breaks down hard concepts/projects into manageable pieces. It's probably the easiest computer science class out there because he does a good job making it low stress and you still learn a lot! Also if you participate in class sometimes he'll throw chocolate at you:)

Professor Jensen is an awesome guy. Super passionate, always smiling, and always accessible. Would answer Discord messages in any channel on the server within usually the day. If you're looking for info on the class, be careful to not let the assignments creep up on you. It can go from easy to impossible in just a week.

Professor Jensen is a real nice guy and really passionate about his work. This was his first year of teaching and he did well. I did most of my learning through the tutorials that are part of the course work, and I didn't learn that much from class itself. It's also VERY easy to spend TONS of time on the assignments/projects if you're not careful

Dr. Johnson was a great teacher. He states early on that if you miss 3 classes unexcused your grade drops one letter grade per absence past 3, so take that into consideration. but the class he teaches is fascinating. He ties familial relationships and mental health to physical health. great class overall. would definitely take it again.

He pretends to be caring, but then is extremely rude and narcissistic. You can only miss class 3 times or you fail the class. He countered me absent for having my camera off during zoom once, even though I talked to the TA About it. He is honestly ridiculous.

I loved Dr. Johnson's class. It's a hard class but so worth it. He teaches family life differently than most other teachers. He makes you think through things. I appreciated his lectures so much! He has great TA's that grade everything. Very concerned with students getting the most out of class as possible. Lots of reading and a paper every week.

He really knows his stuff and adds professional insight wherever the discussion leads. TAs are extremely tough graders; it takes a long time to figure out what they want. Each exam is a 2-hour timed essay so you have a lot of control in what you choose to write about, which I loved. You learn SO much in this class!

This class is an open discussion, and it's not fun. Lots of reading, he has a thing for the SNS and PNS systems and you talk about those all the time. It gets really frustrating. I don't feel like I learned anything from the class because he never lectures, just presents opinions and people can hold to their own beliefs. Disappointing class.

I got a 0 on an assignment although I turned it in, I just missed part of it because he never answered my questions. I explained the misunderstanding after and he didn't even give me half the points. I personally felt bitter ever since... Otherwise, he is a nice guy, class is kind of boring but the content is very relevant and you learn a LOT.

Professor Johnson is a really interesting teacher. I learned more than I have ever learned in any SFL class in this class and with him as the teacher. There are a lot of papers and the class is not very easy but it is definitely worth it. If you listen closely to feedback and work with him then the class will go smoothly by the end.

Definitely unique. It's all open class discussion. Dr. Johnson has a really refreshing perspective on family life. He's very down to earth, understanding, honest, and has emphasis on physiology and nature in therapy. I loved taking his class. It expanded my thoughts and I  still continually ponder the ideas we discussed in class. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Dr. Johnson's class was my favorite. He requires you to do readings and a paper before class, so you can bring ideas and thoughts for a class discussion. I really liked this set-up, but there were a couple students in my class who complained about it. If you're truly interested in family processes, this class is so awesome.

By far the worst professor I've ever had at BYU. Mostly contradicts himself. Spent class time trying to get ideas for his research.  Miss class more than three times, even if you're sick&don't have a doctor's note, you're grade is reduced a whole letter. TA is terrible and ridiculously hard at grading,&you write papers before discussing.  STAY AWAY

Professor Robinson was an incredible professor. She has so much knowledge and loves what she teaches. She gives great examples in class and love participation. She is caring, humble, forgiving, and compassionate.  You couldn't ask for a better class and professor. I learned so much and really appreciated the TAs as well. You will love this class.

This class was so frustrating! She started doing a flipped classroom format, which was supposed to reduce our workload but actually doubled it. The TAs were great, she was very nice, and the content was interesting, but it was hard to enjoy the class because it felt disorganized. Not super hard, just frustrating.

Nice person, but her class is SO frustrating. Each class felt pointless to attend and like I could learn it better on my own. She rarely answered questions and would instead refer to TA's which left us feeling like she had no idea what was going on w content she was teaching. Not hard to get an A, just go to TA hours and study reviews for exams.

Professor Robinson was nice, but her TAs were really the ones in charge, I felt like she never really knew what was going on. Also, a 95% is an A. Easy grading for assignments, but the test questions were very specific; you either knew it or you didn't.

She's a really nice lady, but I'm not even gonna lie sometimes I'm like are we sure she's a professor? She basically just reads off of her very long and very boring slides and when asked questions often doesn't know the answer or contradicts herself which leaves everyone super confused. The TA's teach better.

The grading was never clearly outlined, even if you go to TA office hours and ask explicitly. The professor grades nothing except for the final paper-- claiming over and over how great it is that she doesn't give us a final-- when she totally did, just in the form of a fat essay. She's a nice person but the class is so frustrating.

She was fine. Never responded to emails, lectures weren't that exciting, not a lot of new material that we didn't already cover in other classes. She does have lots of clinical experience. Just one exam, some quizzes that don't have very clear grading criteria, and some pop reading quizzes. Not a very hard class.

She is amazing! Professor Robinson cares about her students so much, and she could not make it more clear! Her TA's are awesome and they are all so willing to help you where ever they can. I had so much fun in this class and learned so much. All while feeling cared for and supported! 10/10 would recommend

The midterm and final are easy despite how she tries to intimidate you about them. The papers (reports) aren't bad either; they just take quite a bit of time. The quizzes are in class, and you don't know when they will be or what they cover, so you basically need to review everything. Overall, this class is not as scary as she makes it out to be.

I had mixed feelings about this class. There are two big papers that are a lot of work, but if you use the TA, you will do well.  Tests are easy because you get a study guide.  Quizzes are random and could be over just about anything since the last one.  Some of the material was really good, some not.  She likes to read off of slides.
Sister Robinson is cool. I enjoyed the class.

Sister Robinson is very approachable and puts a lot of effort into making her class spiritual.  Wrong class to take if you want to be entertained, but if you enjoy serious class discussion or self-reflection driven by well-thought-out questions, this is the class for you.

I enjoyed this class, Sister Robinson is very nice and flexible. Quizzes and tests are pretty easy if you just do the study guide and we always had interesting discussions during class. I would definitely recommend her!

Professor Robinson is okay, but this class is one of the most boring I have ever taken. It was a struggle to pay attention every class. Luckily, it's a really easy class and the midterm and final has a study guide that pretty much gives you the exact answers for the test.

I didn't like Robinson at first, but she grew on me over the semester. Midterm was written; final was non-comp, mostly T/F, a little matching. Both tests had great study guides. Quizzes were the curve ball: never knew what was going to be on them! Papers seem daunting at first, but once you start them not so bad, & lots of TA help available.

Nice lady. This was her first time teaching Book of Mormon and so she wrote some of the test questions really strangely. However, she was very accommodating to  adjust as necessary. I really felt the spirit a lot in her class, she made them very personal always.
Robinson is a good teacher/nice lady. The big writing project is not hard and you can get a good grade. And her tests are easy if you study the study guide that she gives you!
I'm not sure how Ms. Robinson became a teacher, but she is not interesting or engaging. Wastes time, complains, and has bad grammar in her e-mails. Make no mistake, this is no professional.
No Comments

Ms Robinson is a good teacher, although some of the class topics are kind of boring (medicare? ugh). The writing projects are not bad, and everyone gets a good grade on them. She believes in the "repentance process," so if you don't do well on a test, you can make up some of the grade. I didn't have to though: tests were not that hard. Ms R rocks!

I've taken lessons from her, as well as had her as a chamber group coach. She's often vague in what she expects you to do, and doesn't really push/inspire as much as I'd like. Friendly enough, but unprofessional in many ways (she was late a LOT as my chamber coach - came late more often than on time).

Dr. Morgan is a fantastic teacher. She cares about each of her students and is genuinely interested in their progress. I rated her as a hard because she expects a lot from her students. She wants them to excel and practice well for their grade. She is an amazing violinist, teacher, and friend. Take lessons from her if you get the chance!

This is the second class I've taken with Dr. Johnson and he is the best! This class is hard, but you learn so much and he's always willing to help. Make sure you get a head start on all the projects and go to lecture!! He loves participation and a bit of botany gossip... I'd recommend taking any class with him!

Maybe my favorite professor. Learn the material in lecture well and fill out the study guide after each class to stay on top of things. Go to lab, ask questions, and think through the weekly quiz questions and you'll do great. He is super passionate about botany and is so kind. Genuinely looked forward to this class and love applying what I learned

I don't love plants, and expected this class to be boring, but Dr. Johnson was super passionate and kind and really got me hooked on the subject. Amazing and super helpful lectures, and review sessions, clear and in-depth study guides, and allowed for you to review midterms and get points back. Labs were fun, and exams were reasonably difficult.

Loved Dr. Johnson's class! He cares/knows a lot about the subject. Knew every student by name and sometimes brought little treats, he really wants you to succeed :) Gotta work for the grade tho--A was a 95, but provides partial test makeup points. Attendance wasn't mandatory but major for exams and weekly quizzes (all taken in person in class!)

Professor Johnson was really nice, but for some reason this was one of the hardest classes I have taken in a while for a 200 level course. The material itself was like learning a new language and there was a lot of time spent in class and outside of it. The tests were very specific, and you have to know the specific words and terms.

His lectures aren't available outside of class, don't miss! He makes his expectations clear and instructions obvious. He loves plants and you can tell, so this class is just a fun one to have. Quizzes every Friday were reasonable, and tests were difficult but you knew what to expect. One of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU.

Professor Johnson was great! Attendance and good note-taking are key though. I don't mean like write down everything he says, but he will put stuff on the board and those things should be written down. Very approachable and very real. Is more than willing to talk about gospel-related things but only when relevant. Tests are taken in class.

Dr. Johnson is one of the kindest professors I have ever met. He really cares about his students and is always willing to answer question or give extra help when needed. He remembered the names of every single person in my class. He's a great teacher, explains concepts clearly, & I always felt prepared for tests and quizzes.

Professor Johnson was one of the greatest professors I have ever had. He truly cared about what he was teaching and he also cared a lot for his students. His test can be hard, but if you go to class and take good notes, you will do great! He did test corrections and was always available when we needed help with anything. Take Johnson's class!!

His lectures were inspiring and amazing. He really understands the material. There was a textbook, but I didn't end up needing it for the class. If you need it for additional supplementary guides then it is perfect for you. He is shy, but really loves teaching the class.

Dr. Johnson deserves every good review. Botany is hard, but he is an incredible teacher, funny, and cared deeply for our success. I've never had an interest in plants but his passion for the subject was contagious. The textbook was super helpful as well. Our class loved him. You won't have any regrets taking it from Dr. Johnson!

Professor Johnson is the best! He is extremely personable and is very willing to help you with whatever you need. If you are taking his BIO430 class, you get a lot of hands-on experience with identifying plants. Be aware that his BIO230 class is on the more difficult end and you'll really need to study, but he is such a good teacher!

Knows his stuff and cares about his students. Grading is fair--you have to get a 96 to get an A but grading is very lenient. Takes a good amount of studying but not really any homework outside of class, which is nice.

Tests were difficult, the materiel was disorganized from many different sources: labs, lab guides, lectures, various slide shows, textbook. It made the tests hard to study for as the study guides were long and vague, and it was hard to know what material to prioritize studying. Major time commitment even for a 4 credit class.

Professor Johnson's teaching style made BIO 230 my favorite class I've taken. The content is no walk in the park and you're expected to be familiar with everything but that was no surprise. Johnson teaches with whiteboard and markers so I doubt you can pass the class without regular attendance. He's fair and wants his students to succeed.

I took BIO230 my freshman year at BYU. Really cares about you and your success. Recently reached out to him for a LOR and he still had some assignments to help him out. Was willing to help go over assignments and lab reports any time that worked for both of us. I felt that his tests weren't too difficult if you studied and paid attention in class.

Professor Johnson is a really good guy and is very forgiving but his tests are pretty hard. His study guides are not very good and I was usually confused on what to study. Professor Johnson's BIO 230 class is fine.

Dr Johnson is a super genuine and caring professor. His class covers a lot of material and the tests definitely aren't easy, but he gives extra credit opportunities and curved the class at the end. The labs weren't super useful; most of them were virtual and weren't super informative but that wasn't totally his fault.

Dr. Johnson is super nice and gives really good lectures! He writes out notes as he's lecturing, which helps you know what you need to know for tests. He uses lots of diagrams, pictures, and specimens for visual people. You can tell he really cares about the students.

I've learned more and retained more information in this class than I have in any other class here at BYU. Dr. Johnson is the greatest professor I have ever had and is the most kind, sweet, and amazing person I have ever met. His classes require a lot of work but are extremely interesting and you learn a lot. I highly, highly recommend Dr. Johnson!

He is exceptional. The most caring professor Ive ever had. His class is a little difficult, but it is worth it with lots of interesting facts. He is very humble, which is rare for professors, but he is still brilliant, so dont hesistate to ask questions

Dr. Johnson is the best teacher I have ever had. He cares so much about you and about your success. His classes (both 220 and 430) are challenging and it takes a 96 to get an A, but he is extremely fair in his expectations and grading. You have to put in the time to learn the material, but he doesn't try to trick you on tests. He is amazing.

Dr. Johnson is a hard person to describe. He is quite and doesn't act like a lot of other professors But is genuinely very funny and caring. His class is intense but after tests, it feels reasonable in hindsight. No trick material or mass memorization. The class feels like it is worth the money. He is a stellar guy. Iv got mad respect for this guy.

As a senior, this is the first class I have had that feels like a true college class. It is hard because you learn so much, not because it is made to be challenging or weed people out. Dr. Johnson is a spiritual giant and super humble but dont let it fool you because he is an absolute genius. Most caring professor I have had. I love this man!

Lots of challenging material (for new botanist), but taught well (e.g. notes and drawings on board, pictures, physical plants passed around). Passionate about plants. Funny. Meet with for help. Quiz every Friday, questions provided ahead of time. Great exam study guides--just be sure to look at BEFORE each in-class exam, better yet--each lecture.

Im not gonna lie, its a hard class, plus plants arent too interesting for most. But hes an amazing teacher. I was struggling, so he went out of his way to help me out. If youre worried about how youll do, talk with him and hell help you out.

Dr. Johnson was an amazing professor and I loved every minute I spent in his class. He provides study guides and all the information in lecture you will need on exams. I rarely looked at the textbook and performed well on tests. Study the guides given and you should do well.

Dr. Johnson is a great teacher! His classes are hard, and have a lot of material, but he makes sure it's done in a way that doesn't get overwhelming. He is soft spoken but every once in a while slides in a dead pan joke. Dr. Johnson cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

My favorite professor! So caring, knowledgeable, and humble. His courses made me want to be a botanist. Take him every chance you get! His teaching style is AMAZING. I learned SO MUCH. You need to study, but put in a little time and an A is very achievable. He will work with you and help you if you just reach out. I took him for BIO220B & BIO430
The multiple choice part of his tests is very hard, but the rest of the tests are manageable. He's a really good guy, and does a great job at teaching and answering questions.

I LOVED this class. It is one of the favorites I have taken at BYU, mostly because of Doc Johnson. He is an amazing professor. He makes you work hard, but I have never had a class that was more fair or organized. His study guides are amazing and you learn a lot. I'd take it again. If you're going to take Bio 230, take it from him!!!

Doctor Johnson is an incredible teacher and a great guy to have as an influence in your life. This class has a lot of vocabulary and memorization, so be sure to know your stuff for the tests. But if you put in the time, you will be totally fine. He sincerely cares about his students and if you start to fall behind, he'll help you out. Fantastic man

Dr. Johnson is awesome! Very funny and he makes you love plants with his passion for the material. The class is very well structured, tests and quizzes are clearly outlined and you'll know what to expect. He's a very fair grader and you get what you put into it. The tests require studying, but if you put the time in you can do really well.

Dr. Johnson is one of the best teachers at BYU. He is so kind and is a perfect balance of grading hard but not too hard. His tests are pretty in-depth but if you study and pay attention you can do great. If you study and put in some work you will not only get an A but learn a ton! Plus Johnson is such a nice guy and you will love being around him.

Professor Johnson is a wonderful professor. He is dedicated and passionate about the material. He makes sure that he is available for students and makes a concerted effort to help people. The material is taught well and the grading and tests are fair. Pay attention in class, do the homework and reading, and ask questions and you will be fine.

Doctor Johnson is literally the best professor and most caring man I have ever encountered. He will bend over backwards to help you succeed and is aware of how each individual in the class is doing. He's very approachable and is great for giving advice.
Dr Johnson is an incredibly fair teacher, willing to help you succeed. His class is data intensive, and he understands this so he stresses concepts over rote memorization.

Dr. Johnson is a great professor, probably my favorite at BYU.  Really kind and helpful, willing to work with you.  Really cares about his students.  If you really want to learn take a class from him.  I loved this class!  I feel very confident in my abilities to identify plants because of this class.  You learn so much, take it!

Really sweet guy. Take really good lecture notes and put your time in studying, and you'll do fine. If you have a question to ask, he'll always take the time to answer it and is really helpful.  Take the class!
This won't work.

She is super nice, but not a good teacher. We focused a lot on content that in my opinion doesn't matter. Felt very repetitive of all the other PH courses. Most of the semester is working on your capstone project. Very boring lectures that don't seem applicable. Like I said though, she's super nice.

Very nice, but not great at communicating at all. Super boring classes that felt meaningless. Spent most of the semester learning about how to be a good team player. A mandatory class, but oh my goodness was it boring. Also weirdly kind of rude to students.
Very kind professor. Difficult content load but its all relevant and good stuff.

Not sure why she has many bad reviews. She cares about her students and offers lots of extra credit opportunities; one of them includes consulting with her throughout the semester (very helpful). There is a lot of content, but she can simplify it along with her TAs. She is very understanding and is willing to you if you ask.

This class was such a waste of time and was so time consuming. But if you are reading this, you probably have to take it anyway. Just pray that you get a good group because you will be working with them the whole semester. Pick a community partner that is easy to work with. 1 midterm, a final paper and some other random assignments/quizzes.

If you are reading this before taking this class, I am sorry but you are probably too late to change your emphasis. This "capstone" honestly makes you wonder what the heck is health science in public health, really regret keeping this emphasis and this class is just super sad to have as a final hurrah for public health

Dr. Novilla is a great person; very kind and she has something nice to say about everyone. However, this class is a lot of work and pretty disorganized. There's no other choice for HLTH 495, so just check learning suite often to make sure you're not missing anything.

Dr. Novilla is super nice, however, she often has content on the quizzes and tests that was not in her lecture or in the readings. She is both lecture heavy and project heavy. On the projects and assignments there is very little instruction and no rubric. If you can take the class from someone else I would highly suggest doing so.
This professor is literally the worst professor I have ever had in my life, I can literally not think of a single good thing to say about her. Horrible that I have to take it from her and only her.

She is kind and sweet but the class itself is awful. I have never been in a more unorganized class. Learning suite is never updated and TAs don't really know what is going on. Like other reviews have said, she wants both a project and lecture based course, but it simply doesn't work with the format. Disappointing end to my public health undergrad.

Genuinely, she is the worst professor I have ever had during my time at BYU. Novilla wants to teach about medicine rather than public health and does not focus on the integration of public health within healthcare. If I were BYU, I would have her teach a pre-med class instead of this one. Very disappointed this is the last public health required.

An extremely disappointing end to my undergrad in public health. It's like she expects every health science student to be pre-med, and for someone who isn't, the class just feels completely pointless and frustrating. I have never had a worse experience in my undergrad. Her class is disorganized to the point that it is difficult to succeed. Expect to pick up a lot of the class's mess with your own out-of-class time.

The TA's tried their best, however the tests were so difficult and trying to simple things like environmental factors or social factors felt more subjective than concrete. When she taught it was so confusing and hard to know what was going to be on the test. The homework took so much longer than it should've. Shes nice! Take it from someone else.

Dr. Novilla is so kind and sweet and she is the smartest professor I have ever had, but this class was very difficult. You will easily get a good grade because there's a million extra credit assignments but all of the exams are long and difficult. I don't have enough space to write everything I want to in here. So all I'm going to say is take this class from literally anyone else. Dr. Novilla is a super sweet and caring professor. She is very compassionate to her students, however, the class itself is chaotic. Very disorganized and you frequently do not know what is going on.

Literally the NICEST person ever, get to know her outside of class, DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, exams are hard, but again she is the nicest soul. Powerpoints and readings are excessive and not super nessecary, but the group worksheets have a lot of the test questions.

Dr. Novilla does care about the students but gives lengthy lectures. They give lots of information but she doesn't always answer your questions in a way you'll understand. Dr. Novilla is one of the nicest people I've ever met but I did not enjoy her class. Her lectures were redundant and her tests were brutal. 12 page study guide for each test. Dr. Novilla is an AMAZING professor that really cares about her students. The material can be challenging, you just need to keep on top of everything and you'll be fine.

Dr. Novilla is THE BEST professor at BYU. I was reading the other ratings and I want to debunk the idea that she is unorganized. She is so organized and very knowledgeable. Literally, never take a class from her. Such a waste of time. Dr Novilla has a kind heart and wants every student to succeed! She loves her students and makes every quiz and exam are straight forward. the class has super interesting material and is about the right amount of work for a 3 credit course. I will definitely take more classes from her!

So the class itself is not terribly difficult, but her organization is all over the place and you won't get a clear answer out of her for what to study for. Basically, the TA's will save you, email them ask them to have test reviews and they will go over the actual specifics of what you should be studying for.

Dr. Novilla is an extremely busy woman with a ton of responsibilities both at BYU and outside of BYU. However, she cares about her students and is always accessible. Its just one of those situations where you put put the right answer on the test, but the professor decides that on that data its the wrong answer because the full-half-moon woke up on the wrong side of computer keyboard and the hard-working TAs cant explain why you got it marked wrong. not worth the frustration, stay away

Very nice person, WORST PROF AT BYU. She does not teach what is on the exams. The lectures are a monologue of mostly wasted time. Waste. Of. Time. 75 minute classes, and I couldnt tell you what we were taught. Whether it was a day literally nothing actually was taught, or a day where she just read her 75 slides+ lectures. Least favorite teacher of my life. 75 minutes class includes wasted 30 minutes of spiritual thought and 45 minutes of her talking nonstop. she just reads nonstop, doesnt respond to emails. Wow, this was seriously the worst class I have ever taken at BYU. Dr. Novilla was so unorganized and it was clear that the class was a complete afterthought. The TAs basically do everything. Honestly, will probably end up with100% in this class, mostly from extra credit, but still hate it. Wanted to love it, but feel so much stress & uncertainty. The class feels incredibly disorganized and you will never feel like you know what you are supposed to be learning. LSuite is confusing, hard to find the right readings. Get ready to be constantly reading a book/study for this class. Talks the entire lecture, SOOOOO MUCH BUSY WORK and projects, and it's simple information that I feel like could be taught a lot better in a different way. This is the first rate my professor rating I've ever left. I know she means well, just not my favorite style of teaching at BYU.

Dr. Novilla is one of my favorite professors. She is so knowledgeable and so kind. Her lectures were very informative and indicative of what would be on the test. She offers a lot of extra credit and opportunities to meet with her outside of class. The course content is also very interesting. I definitely recommend this class!!!

She is INCREDIBLE. I've never had a professor make her class so applicable to the real world, and she is so willing to help and meet outside of class. She wants to get to know each student, and is willing to help with networking and other opportunities for resume building! Not an easy class, but 100% worth it!

Dr Novilla is super sweet, but I feel like she rarely remembered what she taught us in class. The TA's did basically everything for her, and I felt I was in better hands with the TA than with her. Her tests were moderately hard and she had a lot of free response questions. The quizzes are extra credit which was a life saver.

Professor Novilla really care about her students! However, her class is hard to follow. You can never be sure what will be on the test or what she actually expects you to learn. I would be cautious taking a class from her again because I was constantly stressed about what I should be learning.

Dr. Novilla is one of my favorite professors. Shes so humble and kind and funny and Ive always enjoyed her lectures. Shes very knowledgeable. Ive taken a few classes from her and each has been phenomenal. My only complaint would be that there is some busy work but overall youll learn so much.

Course involves 3 book reviews, a semester-long research project, quizzes, and 3-4 field trips. She is very caring and truly wants you to become a better PH practitioner. Her personal schedule sometimes gets in the way with assignments, so deadlines get pushed back. Some assignments don't have clear criteria, but she isn't a tough grader at all.

Nice professor. 4 tests and a final in the class. The first test was pretty easy but the rest are really tough. She uses the whiteboard for most of the class and then posts a huge PowerPoint after with a whole bunch of other things on it so it is difficult to really know what you'll need for the test. QUIZZES ARE EXTRA CREDIT! How cool is that!

I took this course the 1st semester it was offered at BYU so it was a bit disorganized/directions were often vague. However, Dr. Novilla was flexible if u got confused/made a mistake. Great course for future health providers interested in public health. 2 book reports, 1 long-term group research paper which u present a poster on, grand rounds-style

Dr. Novilla cares more about her students than any other I have ever met. She offers INSANE amounts of extra credit. As an MD she offers valuable insights into the anatomical and physiological side of chronic disease. There is a lot of homework, but its pretty straightforward. TA reviews and the concept mastery checklist will help for tests.

Dr. Novilla has to be one of the most caring professors at BYU. She always takes care of the students needs and will push back assignments if necessary. The material is needs to be memorized for the exams, which there are a lot of questions that come from lecture and homework, not as much from the textbook

Dr. Novilla is by far my favorite professor. I have never met someone more selfless and caring than her. She meets with each student and talks about the class every quarter. She offers lots of extra credit. She knows SO much about chronic diseases and is an amazing teacher. Study the slides and go to the TA reviews. I absolutely loved this class.

Dr. Novilla's class was amazing! She is genuine and caring, and her lectures are very interesting. She offers lots of extra credit throughout the semester but you have to work for it still. Exams based off the lecture and slides are posted on LearningSuite. Some group projects, so better hope you get paired with good classmates.

Dr. Novilla is one of the best teachers I have had here. She is so caring and she knows all of her students and really wants them to understand chronic disease. This class is really heavy on the pathophysiology, which can be a bit frustrating because this is a requirement for Public Health. She offers A LOT of extra credit, which is very helpful.
Great class by Dr. Novilla. It was VERY challenging, but also very rewarding. Tests are extremely hard but she gives lots of extra credit throughout the semester.

Dr. Novilla is AMAZING.  She is a harder teacher because she wants you to succeed.  If you meet with her outside of class hours she literally gives you the test answers.    Don't need the book unless you want to study in-depth for the quizzes (I didn't and still got an A)  You will love her and the class!!

Dr. Novilla is hands-down one of the kindest profs ever. Meets w/ students individually before every test, cares about your life. Class is physiology-heavy, which I liked but may not be your jam. Dr. Novilla's class had a lot of potential to be a great class but it was so much work and I feel like I didn't really learn anything. Her tests are impossibly hard honestly it's what I imagine medical school exams are like. If you like ridiculously amounts of work without a great grade take her class.

Dr. Novilla cares a ton about students. I love that she cares about humanity in medicine. People say her class is too hard, and it's true that taking physiology would make it much easier. If you read, though, you can figure out. Her tests  aren't super easy but she prepares you for them.

Dr. Novilla has been the most kind & genuine professor I've had at BYU. She works hard to make sure each student has a clear understanding of the material. She teaches in detail the anatomy and physiology of chronic diseases - and this is absolutely necessary to truly understand a chronic disease. Not an easy A, but definitely doable.

BEST Professor ever! Her lectures are fascinating, albeit detailed. If you are pre-med, this class will be your favorite, if not, you might not like the details as much. I thought it was on the medium difficulty side, but she does offer extra credit! You will need to study for 4 tests, and a final, look at slides and study guides! Awesome class!

Mrs. Novilla is a good and caring professor. Studying her slides and making flashcards can get you up to an A- or maybe even an A. In order to ensure an A you will need to take very detailed notes during certain parts of her lecture. Her lectures can seem unorganized but if you read the slides before class you'll be fine. She offers extra credit

If you want to take her class, take physiology first, it will be much easier to understand what she's teaching. She's brilliant and such a wonderful person! But it's a lot of work, and if you're a public health major it is NOT worth it.

I have to defend Dr. Novilla. Her class is tough, but she is an amazing teacher and person. She knows her stuff and teaches you well. I learned more in her class than in all of my other Public Health classes combined. The class isn't easy but she will personally tutor you and help you succeed. She'll even give you extra credit for getting help!

Dr Novilla is a nice woman but regrettably a TERRIBLE TEACHER!!!!! Her class was so difficult and for students who are doing public health (which is what this class is for) just STAY AWAY! her tests are impossible,difficult to understand both because of her accent and because she talks to fast and over your head. Only relevant for MED students.

Dr. Novilla does go into detail of anatomy and physiology but if you're a health major why would that bother you? This is your major! Duh! She is very smart, kind, and helpful. I always look forward to class! She brings treats and plans fun activities. I put easiness as 3 because it's not an "easy A" but it's not that bad at all.

Dr. Novilla is definitely one of my favorite professors, but if your not interested in going into medicine, take it from someone else. As far as difficulty, on a scale from HLTH 100 to CHEM 351, it's about right in the middle.

I have no idea why everyone else is saying Dr. Novilla's class is so hard.. It's really not. If you do the readings from the textbook and pay attention in class, the tests are easy. She is absolutely brilliant but DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER. She talks way above your head, and it doesn't matter how much you study, her tests are impossible. The highest score on the final was C and she didn't curve grades at all. Completely ridiculous and time consuming.
Take this course from somebody else unless you're premed. It's really that simple. If you're not premed, you're wasting time. If you're premed, this is for you.

Great class for premeds. Difficult tests; some questions don't make sense, but others are great--better questions for teaching than most professors use. Dr. Novilla is very smart and highly intelligent than most people I know. Her class is designed for serious and dedicated medical students. Her test are mind boggling.

This class is extremely hard! The amount of work that she requires is ridiculous. The tests are almost impossible to do well on even though you can study for weeks/hours. DO NOT TAKE IT FROM HER! Tests are IMPOSSIBLE (study hundreds of slides and study guides for 15 hours, and still fail test), lectures make NO SENSE. Wow.  If you don't have a life, don't have a wife, don't care about your grades, TAKE HER!  :)  For the rest of us who have a life, stay away.  I regret 100% of the time I spent taking this wasteful class.  I am sad that people sacrifice so much to receive this quality of education.  What a deception.

Such a great class. i think it was a nice balance between anatomy, physiology and life application. there is a lot of memorization but read the book and look at the lecture slides and you are golden. great class. she knows her stuff!

my favorite professor in the health science department! She knows her stuff. It depends on why you are taking this class. This class is a challenge, but Dr. Novilla is an amazing teacher. She is extremely helpful if you ask and she does a good job explaining difficult concepts. Highly Recommend.

Dr. Novilla is a very knowledgeable professor with a lot of experience.  She is excited about the subject she teaches and she is willing to help anyone who needs it.  Her tests are hard and confusing, and lectures are a bit boring, because they are repetative.  Write on the board,repeat.  Despite the difficulty, I have still learned in this class.
RUN, RUN far, a horrible teacher!

An extremely helpful teacher! She is willing to go out of her way to help any student who is willing to put forth effort! Probably my favorite professor here at BYU... don't pass up the opportunity to take a class from her, you won't regret it!

This class was excellent! It really wasn't too difficult. Of course if you have a better health background (Bio, Physiology, Anatomy etc) things are going to be easier. I didn't and I still did well. Study! And you'll do great!
