Super easy class, and Professor Dunn makes it very easy to succeed. He really gives a broad view of what a career in Food Science would look like!

This professor is very kind and caring. Office hours were a must for me. It took me a second to get comfortable with the way he lectures, but I learned to love it. His tests were hard for me, but he wants to help you.

Dr. Bakker is awesome and will do anything to help his students. He even does his office hours in the junior core study lab, so he's frequently available for homework help. He tries to be pretty interactive with his lectures and goes through example problems in class which is awesome.

I hated taking Calc from Bakker. He would always have a mistake in his lectures that he would have to fix during class. He was very unclear about what would be on the tests. He is bad at lecturing. The only thing that got me through this class were the TA's.

He did not know how to teach at all. He added complicated things in his lectures that you didn't need to learn which drew out the lectures and made them more stressful. Terrible at teaching, half my class went to the lectures of other professors.

He knows his stuff but he is unaware what is on the exam. Thus, students are often ill-prepared and perform poorly. Additionally, he mostly teaches using proofs, but his slides contain lots of typos which makes it difficult to understand

This class was weird. Lectures were tough, there was a lot of tough homework. I thought I would fail the exams, but when I sat down to take them, I was more prepared than I thought. Dr. Bakker comes across as a less than effective professor, but he knows what he's doing (and he's really good at refocusing the lesson when people get distracted)

Professor Bakker cares about his students more than any professor I've had in my three years at BYU. His tests are very fair, even though the material of the class is of course difficult. He has forgiving policies about dropping homework assignments, etc. 10/10 recommend Dr. Bakker for ACME!

Lectures tended to introduce a concept with its theory, then an example or two. In my opinion, most of the learning in the course happened in the lab/TA portion, where concepts were explained in greater depth. As such, the TA you get greatly influences your success in the class. Make sure you know your 112 material. The class is curved nicely too.
Great prof! You can tell he puts a lot of work into his lectures and that he cares about his students.

Professor Bakker is kind and caring, but his lectures are generally all over the place. 95% of your understanding of this class needs to come from you studying on your own because lectures are mostly unhelpful. HW assignments due every day Mon-Sat. Heavy workload.
He really wants his students to learn. He likes to do examples in class before I really understood, which made it kind of hard. Tests are by the department so the teachers are similar.

Dr. Bakker is a GREAT professor! He explains concepts clearly and gives both theoretical and simple explanations. He works through examples in class and the homework really prepares you for exams. Its not an easy class no matter which professor you have, so you do have to put effort in. But hes definitely a solid choice for calc 2!

This class was so hard. It's hard to separate the material from the professor, so it's hard to say how much of that was from Dr. Bakker. He has a good attitude and my grade got curved from a 77% to a B-, but that depends on how well your section does. Online hw due the night before every lecture, written hw due in every lecture.

This class was so much harder than it had to be. The material was fine but Bakker's class period and TA time was such a waste of my time. I stopped going to all 5 periods and just learned it from looking up homework questions. Take from someone else but if have to, be ready to get a bad grade unless you dedicate 100% to learning on your own

Great Professor. A lot of your class experience will depend on which TA you have, but he is available multiple times per week to help and does a good job explaining the course material, giving both the simple and complex explanations, but letting you know before he teaches anything you do not need to know.
Get Priddis if you can. Very hard time explaining concepts, skips steps while teaching. Tough time explaining, even in office hours. Nice person though.
It was hilarious how bad he was.

Probably the worst professor here on campus. He doesn't teach useful information in class (he goes on too many tangents about weird stuff and proofs that aren't on the exams) and expects you to completely comprehend the subject by studying a glitchy online textbook. Save yourself the trouble and spend your tuition on a different teacher!

Great professor! This class will be difficult and require a lot of time no matter whom you take it from. I spent about 10 hours a week outside of class doing homework. Dr. Bakker always starts class with a prayer and is always willing to answer questions during lecture in order to help you out. Tests are 75% of your semester grade.

Dr. Bakker is fine for Math341. I doubt I would've preferred a different professor. The material is just hard. Class was useless for me unless I really thoroughly studied the material before class. Then it was like a refresher to help me commit to memory the things I already learned. He goes fast and it's so easy to get lost if you don't read befor

I liked Dr. Bakker's homework--both online and written. It counts for a small portion of the grade. Dr. Bakker is a nice guy, but class was mostly proofs, and I wish he would have done more examples. The grade is heavily based on tests. Dr. Bakker does a good job keeping his voice tone interesting, but I did most of my learning from the book.

Professor Bakker is a really smart guy and it shows when he teaches... but it would often go over my head and I would tune out easily. He shows a lot of proofs in class and I think most people learned how to do the assignment largely from the Webassign and through Slader and Khan Academy. Really interesting and difficult class though.

Dr. Bakker is a great guy, his class was just weirdly difficult.  I got a C+ and so did most of the other people in the class.  His lectures are packed with information, but usually the homework was still over my head.  You could easily skip class and read the book and learn just as much as in lecture.

Dr. Bakker is the most caring and accommodating professor I have ever had. Lectures can be a little dry, but Dr. Bakker really knows the material he is teaching. I am not a big fan of the class in general, so Dr. Bakker definitely helped me stay interested enough to do the work.

Great teacher! The class is hard that's to be expected with any math class at a respectable university. The workload is high, but that's decided by the department; not him. Plus he was very flexible with due dates. Very clear and all ways willing to help. Definitely one of the best math teachers. There is a reason he won a teaching award.

Facts: Expect HW to be due 3-5 times a week (mix of online and written). Expect LOTS of tests--4 midterms and a final.  Opinion: Dr. Bakker is the man! If you can commit to learning the language of mathematics, he explains things crystal clear. ALWAYS willing to help. Holds his office hours in the math lab to maximize availability. Great guy!

Dr Bakker's lectures are basically straight out of the book, so if you learn better from reading-don't worry about going to class, just read the book. If you learn better through listening-go to class. Also, the homework was way harder than the tests. The tests were fair, the HW just stunk. HINT: the solutions manual to the textbook is online.

Dr. Bakker is the best math professor I've had at BYU (I'm a math minor). Everything you need to complete the majority of the homework without help is presented in a clear manner in class. For the one or two problems that are too tough, he is extremely helpful in office hours. Learn to speak the language of linear algebra and you'll be fine.

Dr. Bakker gave interesting lectures, but reading the textbook is essential to truly understanding what is going on. He moves through the subjects really quickly and since he teaches multiple sections in one lecture, you can't really ask questions in class. Recitation sections are incredibly helpful, if you have a good TA.
Bakker is a really great professor. The lectures are informative and engaging (at least as engaging as math can be). The tests are not too difficult if you grasp the homework and concepts.

Dr. Bakker is a really nice guy. He really likes proofs so he would spend a lot of time during lectures writing out the proof for a formula and often times it confused me even more. I would have rather been given example problems. However, he is willing to help if you ask him. Study groups are helpful, and the Math Lab tutors can help as well.
Dr. Bakker and Dr. Jarvis are the best professors in the math department. Dr. Bakker really cares about students and wants them to learn. And this class will be hard no matter who teaches it.

Best 341 professor hands down. Probably one of the best in the Math department. I've talked to many other students and they agree. Solid lecturer, very clear, interested in the subject, and super helpful both in class and in office hours. 341 can be really hard, so you want him since he makes it more than manageable in terms of homework and tests.

Dr. Bakker is the man, he is the guy you want as a teacher. I'll be honest, 341 is a hard class so you will need to work hard. However it will be like that no matter who you take it from. Dr. Bakker is very reasonable with grades. It is hard to like a teacher who teaches a hard class which is why he doesn't have perfect ratings. Choose him.

Dr. Bakker is the man! I wish I had him for all my other math classes. He is always well prepared and SUPER organized in his notes. His reviews are extremely helpful in prepping for the tests. He's fair, nice, always willing to help and THE BEST MATH TEACHER I'VE EVER HAD!!

Dr. Bakker makes it very clear what he wants you to learn in the class. His lectures are organized, and he does a good job at teaching difficult material. All of his lecture notes are available for review. His exams can be tough if you don't study, but they are very fair. I was scared to take this class at first, but Bakker helped me to like it.

Great professor! He was very clear, you knew exactly what to expect to see on the exams, he made his class notes available online, he offered extra credit, was always willing to help. And class at 9:00 AM was somehow very entertaining. Excellent professor!

Hands down the greatest math professor I've had at BYU. Unfortunately he's not teaching Differential Equations next semester. But he's so awesome that he's offered to help me with the subject material anyways. His lecturing style is REALLY good. Lots of proofs but he always does some examples so you can see how everything ties together.
One of the best math professors I've ever had. The material can be hard to grasp sometimes though, no getting around that.

Hands down the best math professor at BYU.  His lectures are interesting and engaging.  He gives great answers to difficult on the spot questions in class.  He is extremely helpful outside of class too.  You can tell he has a passion for teaching math.

Fabulous Professor!Very clear lectures & posts all lecture notes online.The recitation sections were great to better understand the specifically challenging problems.Tests were hard & challenging, but they do give partial credit.Very confusing exactly how the curve works, & to this day I don't understand it.I would take from Dr.Bakker again!
Great teacher. He was always very helpful and more than willing to work with the students. I would definitely recommend him to others. If you can't hack the class, don't blame the teacher.
Excellent math professor.  You have to do the homework to succeed in the class, but his lectures are wonderful. He also comes to the math lab regularly to help with homework questions.

Dr. Bakker is one of the best math professors I have ever had. He taught the material really well and cared a lot about helping students. He was extremely approachable. His class is harder if you do not get proofs; however, he presents the material in a way that the proofs build on what you need to learn.
Great teacher.  Difficult concepts, but he was ALWAYS willing to help you understand.  Gives opportunities for extra credit (pulled my grade up 2 letter grades).

I have never in my life had a more excellent teacher than Dr. Bakker. His lectures made it easy to take relevant notes, he was there in person in the math lab to help out with homework, and when I had a crisis where the grader didn't grade a lot of my homework, he took care of it. If you have the chance, take math from the proud canadian Dr.Bakker.

Teaches by proofs, I love mathematics with all my heart so luckily I was able to learn the concepts all on my own.  If it weren't for that, I would be completely lost.  He rarely does examples or real applications

Dr. Bakker is really a great teacher.  I've had him for 113 and 343 and I would take every class from him I could.  He is extraordinarily good at teaching in a manner that helps you visualize what you're doing.  He holds office hours, where he can help you one-on-one.  It's a tough class, so go to his office hours.
This class was incomprehensible. I later retook it from another teacher and it made complete sense. Bakker is really nice and willing to help outside out class though, so that is good.

This class was pretty much incomprehensible to me. He mostly goes over proofs in class. Probably my worst math class at BYU. Bakker is definitely willing to help outside of class though. He is a really nice guy.

I took this class before and HATED it, then tried a different teacher and HATED it. When I got to Bakker, it was refreshing to see someone animated enough to keep me awake even through a boring subject. His tests were reasonable. I didn't like having to complete computer lab assignments, but that might be required because it was honors.

The class was pretty tough, but Dr. Bakker is a genius.  He goes over problems in class and was always really helpful in the Math lab.  The homework is tough and mandatory, but the tests are easier.  Even so, I still had to go over everything we learned in class by re-reading the chapter in the textbook.
This is an intense class, but Bakker is very clear and complete in his explanations of complex topics. I strongly recomend Bakker for anyone attempting the course.

Takes alot of time to explain difficult concepts and does it well.  I stopped by his office a couple of times and he spent an hour each time explaining concepts to me with no problem.  Very interested in helping students.  Great Professor.
I wouldn't take a math class from anyone else.  He will give you all of this time to explain concepts.
Great teacher for such a tuff class.
he is a really great teacher.  Our class always had the best test score average because he taught so well.
Very good teacher. Enjoyable as a person and a teacher. Takes time to make sure veryone understands. Wants evreyone to do well.
I had him for Math 303, but he also teaches 302. He is the first Math teacher who wrote a proof on the board in lecture and I actually understood better afterwards.
He is freaking awesome!  And his TA is HOT!  He is a great teacher and he really cares about his students.

The class I took was British Lit for a G.E. and I really liked it! Class tends to be just a discussion & lecture, and it's really pretty chill in class. There are mainly bigger papers, but Dr. TM is very happy to help in any way! She wants her students to succeed and is more than willing to meet with you and help you with your assignments!

Dr. Thorne-Murphy is fantastic! I did not know much about Victorian Lit before her class, but now I feel that I have a good understanding of themes and patterns of the era, as well as a wide variety of the major authors. She is soft-spoken and generous with her time, which makes her approachable and a great professor. I recommend her classes!

Prof Thorne-Murphy is a kind person that just loves Victorian lit. She loves comments from the class, and values every contribution. The short fiction editing project is fun, reasonable, and actually gave me something to add to my resume. I learned a lot without doing a ridiculous amount of work. Definitely recommend this professor.

Professor Thorne-Murphy is a joy to learn from! She loves what she teaches and is very knowledgeable. I took a Victorian Christmas literature course (randomly specific) from her on accident but decided to stay simply because she loves it so much and provided an excellent selection of texts! Very kind and always willing to talk outside of class.

Prof. Thorne-Murphy is extremely fair in her grading and helpful in her feedback. She cares about her students and never makes the coursework unnecessarily difficult. Class is a mix between lecture and workshopping the papers. I found the class very easy to keep up with, as she has several "checkpoints" set up throughout the paper writing process.
Such a fun class! The professor is very clear and makes the readings fun including a lot of class opinions and ideas about the readings. Recommend 100%

This class was one of the most valuable experiences I've had in college. I really felt like I understood the Victorian Period by the end, and at the end we all studied little-known works of the period and analyzed them. It felt like we were really treading new ground.
She is so kind and helpful to all students. She takes a personal interest in your learning experience. While she expects a lot out of her students, she doesn't expect you to do it all on your own.

Great teacher. She knows her stuff and makes class a discussion which is really informative. You have to read because tests are short answer and essay - comparing texts. She is very organized and plans her class so you are not overwhelmed. Would definitely recommend her - allows you to revise papers too.

Great teacher. Fun class--I learned a lot. Make sure you pay attention to the lectures (take good notes) and study your BUTT off for the tests--don't put off the reading or it'll catch up to you. Expect to be challenged, and to grow a lot. Great overview of literary analysis. (Take this BEFORE the 290 sequence, if you can--makes life much easier.)

Professor Hadfield is a really nice teacher and wants her students to succeed, but she teaches in a way that is not very engaging. This class has tons of reading. I bought two books for this class and didn't use them at all.

I barely finessed a B- in this class. I'm grateful I got to grow my knowledge about Africa, but I would never take a class from her again! There is so much reading, and if you miss one day, good luck because the next day you walk into class. BOOM a Pop quiz you FAILED!! I would rant more but I have no characters left. Honestly... just run away!

I loved taking Modern Africa from Professor Hadfield! She is really knowledgeable, passionate and kind. I also love to read, and this class is very reading heavy. Be prepared to read a couple full length books with other readings interspersed. She is also a tough grader - you need to be thorough about all the little details in your responses.

Dr. Hadfield is one of the best teachers. She is a passionate advocate for South Africans, having published books about their history and apartheid. She will help you understand their past and current situations through their eyes with great empathy. Dr. Hadfield is not only a history teacher, but she will help you learn to write. Take her class!

Dr. Hadfield is highly knowledgeable; a South African history expert, accomplished speaker, and published author, with a patronizing confidence. Her teaching method requires significant advancements in skilled writing, lacking progressive smaller steps. Though appearing supportive, her grading is harsh, making it hard to feel successful in class.

AWFUL!!! Does not explain concepts or the large paper at all! Does not help students in need of assistance. Completely degraded myself and my learning process. Gave horrible feedback and said I had a learning disability!. BYU needs to look into her! I was so distraught with my grade and she tossed me to the curb, not helpful with future educators.

Good class and good professor. Dr. Hadfield is very accessible and will help you refine your scope and focus for the 12-15 page paper that has been mentioned in these reviews. If you don't participate in class, it will feel boring, so you get as much out of this class as you put in.

I loved Professor Hadfield! You have to write a 12-15 p paper, but she's so accessible and willing to help you with every step of the research process. Her professional focus is on Africa so the class is only focused on learning about that. Participate in class discussions! I learned how to write better college essays because of this class!

The only class at BYU I absolutely hated! You can tell Dr. Hadfield is a very good researcher, but a TERRIBLE professor. She speaks so quietly and slowly that it's hard not to fall asleep and it felt like I learned nothing. I wanted to learn to become a historian, not take a history class about Africa. Take it from anyone else if you can!

Great,kind prof! Africa focused class. Mainly readings and source analyses, in class u discuss them, participation graded, raise ur hand every class. Big 12to15 pg paper and presentation. Loved this class,some excred,lot of reading,interesting, gets u used to hist. reading lvls. Take if ur good writer and willing to work for A,maj classgot Amin orA

Her teaching goes in circles. She knows a lot about her field but is bad at teaching what the class is. She will ramble about Africa but not talk about being a historian. None of your readings really apply to what the class is about.
I had a lot going on outside of class and probably should have failed, but she was very kind and willing to work with me. Very knowledgeable and interesting to listen to.

The lectures are PAINFUL to sit through. I love history, she manages to make world history boring! Her essays are graded on a weird scale, and she expects you to read her mind on the requirements for essays. If you have the misfortune to take this boring class, make sure that your essays are centered on Africa, because she loves Africa.

I loved Professor Hadfield! She's compassionate and is always willing to talk to you outside of class. I didn't feel like I knew exactly what was wanted for the papers most of the time, but she worked with me to understand. You pick one topic to study about for the whole semester. There are only 5 assignments though.

Professor Hadfield is so smart. The whole class is about South Africa because that's her specialty, and most of the class is focused on a 12-15 page research paper. There's some other assignments, and they all take a lot of time. I spent more time doing homework for this class than any of my other classes, but I got a lot better at writing.

I like Prof. Hadfield but be prepared to read 1-4 articles that are on average 10 pages between each class. Had to read 4 articles, listen to 3 interviews and write a complete analysis over the weekend. Does not take into consideration that you have other heavy classes when she loads the homework onto you. Ended up hating the class, just to much.

I enjoyed Dr. Hadfield's class. She knows so much about African history its really impressive. She was very accessible outside of class and wanted to help me with my research paper as much as possible. She was helpful and kind. I didn't really identify with her because of my personality per say, but she was a great teacher.

I really liked Dr. Hadfield's class. Because her focus is on African history, she gives a really cool perspective on world history. But European history is a little harder for her to lecture on. I would definitely suggest taking her class if you've got any kind of  foundation in world history. She appreciates participation and is kind and caring.

Dr. Hadfield is brilliant and has a knack for illistrating history. Her class challenges you but with hard work and interest an A is very possible. Something I enjoyed from her class was the historical comparison between different authors. Dr. Hadfield is one of the most genuine professors and truly wants her students success, ask her for help!

Dr. Hadfield is an amazing professor who makes her HIST 200 class fun and interactive. She is accessible and wants to build good relationships with her students, and the small class size of 15 helped to make this possible. This course is just for History/Social Science Majors. I learned so much about colonial Africa and it has opened my perspective
She is very informed about her subject, but no matter how hard I studied I still received a C. And I have never had a class with SO much reading- multiple LONG books.

Dr. Hadfield is an extremely knowledgeable professor and I really enjoyed her class, I learned more about South African history than I ever expected. She really has the desire to help her students better understand history and will push you. The class is centered around a major research paper, and outside of that the assignments are not very big.

Dr. Hadfield is a really great professor. The class is a lot of work, and you will have a lot of reading, but it is very well structured and she knows so much about the subject. I found her to be very fair, and willing to help students out. You have to put a lot of time and effort into her class, but it is absolutely worth it. I loved having her.

Professor Hadfield does not deserve the harder critiques of her on here. Her speciality is African history, so when she teaches a basic 202 class, it's natural for her to bring in her emphasis. The assignments are fair and she really knows her stuff and really cares about the students. She has been a fantastic teacher.

I've done more pre-class reading for this class than any other at BYU, BUT she is an amazing teacher and she knows SO much about Africa and African history. She is an amazing teacher and class discussions are so fun and eye opening, if you've done the reading. Highly recommend

Prof. Hadfield is a good professor, but I wish I had known how seriously to take the readings. Don't even look at your phone or she will get upset. She was very lenient when I had a mess up on my paper and let me re-do it. She is good at explaining African history. Just remember that this is NOT a class you can skip readings or just skim over!

Pretty good professor. Very African-focused in her approach to history, but I thought it was kind of nice to get World History from a different perspective than we always hear. Lectures can be a bit boring but my class was really quiet so that probably contributed. Readings are long and not super necessary.

Huge focus on South African history but you learn what you need to as a historian-Huge research paper that you work on the whole semester and a document analysis each week-2 journal entries per week and participation in class is noted down by TA.  Lots of reading but the final is a 2 paragraph essay. She is very open and willing to help students.

I learned next to nothing about world history. She often plays "read my mind" on essay assignments. If you DO take this class: 1) Africa is all that matters. Focus all of your essays on examples from Africa. 2) Go to her office early in the semester to figure out EXACTLY what she wants on the essays. But even then, it probably won't be enough.

honestly im not one to get on to Rate my professor and rant about how terrible a teacher/class is, but honestly this calss is rediculous. everything thats graded hsa nothing to do with what goes on in class, and her grading is harsh. the assignments often times dont make sense and the lectures are as dull as they come. look for a different teacher.

This class was absolutely terrible.  I went to class everyday, payed attention, and did what was required. (Although it was almost impossible to get a good grade)  I have always loved history and have always excelled in the subject.  This has been the worst class that I have ever taken in my life.  I will never recommend this class.

This class was co-taught and professor Hadfield was one of the two. She was definitely the weak link of the two. Her lectures were confusing and questions were so poorly worded that no one in class had any idea how to begin to answer them. She is very nice and willing to help.
If you get an A on her essay tests it's ready to be published. Expected to know everything, and more of a African World History class.

This was a great class! Dr. Hadfield really knows her subject (she speaks the clicking language, has met and interviewed famous Africans, etc. She is really helpful and willing to work with students. It was a lot of work (two tests, a research paper, tons of reading) but everything was relevant and interesting. Excellent course and professor.

I liked Dr. Hadfield. I don't think she could possibly be any clearer about what she wants on the tests and papers. Just follow instructions, and you'll do really well. I didn't read the textbook most of the time, but I listened in class, took good notes, and got an A. She also offered opportunities for extra credit. I would take her class again.
So knowledgable and willing to help students one-on-one. A good experience.

Don't be scared to talk to your professors after class. I was never lost, and she was super open if I disagreed about a grade and changed an essay score. Slightly boring lectures, but it's history and there are 200 people. It's just the subject. Smart way of assessing knowledge. Not some BS multiple choice that you forget the next day. Great prof

Sounds like her 200 courses are bad, I wouldn't know. I took her history South Africa class and best decision I made. She was amazing, it is her speciality so things were really interesting. Her topics were great, and best thing of all no tests! There was a term paper, but if u need help she goes above and beyond, and will help u. I loved the class
Worst class ever. Agreed with what everyone else is saying. Grading makes no sense whatsoever, and by far the most boring lectures I have ever attended.

The worst class I have ever taken at BYU! The other ratings are right on when they say you do everything she asks on assignments and tests and still wind up with C's with no explanation. Terrible lectures, terrible structure, and nothing seems to be applicable. Avoid at all costs!

The worst class I have ever taken. She gives you a list of expectations for the tests and assignments, and even though I met them all, I still got C's because I didn't "write enough." Class is honestly painful to sit through and it feels like NOTHING applies to our lives.

This class is awful.  Honestly painful to sit through.  The grading scale is incredibly ambiguous. I always felt like I answered everything that she asked and met all of the expectations, but wound up getting C's.  When I would ask why, the only answers I got were because I didn't "write enough." I just hope to pass so I never have to take it again

By far the worst clas I've taken at BYU. It's clear Prof. Hadfield doesn't know how to teach college students. Be prepared to learn everything on your own. The tests don't gauge what you've learned in the class at all and the lectures WILL put you to sleep. If you have to take this class, take it from someone else!
Extremely difficult to deal with and goes out of her way to make things harder. Seems to target certain students too.

Online class through Canvas. If you stay on top of your assignments and due dates, it's a super easy and informative class. The few times I needed clarification I received an email within the same day. There is a group project at the end of the course, so make sure you communicate with your group in advance!

Professor Miles is so sweet and caring. NURS 180 is an on demand class so you don't get to see her a ton, however, her expectations are clear and grades fairly. Definitely take this class from her! It was an easy A as long as you stay on top of the assignments.
Professor Hooley is amazing! Her lectures are super funny and she always lets the class out early. Even though the class is super easy, you still learn a lot. Take this class from her!
Made the information digestable. Class has an online option and lectures usually didn't take the whole time. She prepares you SO well for the tests.

If you are going to take comms 300 you actually need to take it from Professor Hooley. She makes every single lecture spiritually uplifting and I felt like I was actually learning something new each week and wanted to learn more. There are a few papers, and short essay question midterm and final but lots of extra credit is offered.

She's the absolute best, I can't imagine taking this class from anybody else. Media law can be so boring but she gives tons of extra credit, helps you out a ton on assignments, and she is overall just the most fun and positive person ever.

Super caring teacher. She has a lot of experience in law and she knows what she is talking about. I thought the content was a little boring but she made the class much more interesting. You could tell that she really cared about us and was trying her best. Definitely take the class from Professor Hooley!!

Professor Hooley is so great! Her lectures are so fun and entertaining, but also full of stuff you need to know. She is very understanding and genuinely wants you to do well in the class. The tests are mostly writing, but they are not too bad. She offers her class on Zoom which is also nice if you are unable to attend one day. Highly recommend.

she quite literally is iconic, like she just wants us to succeed and know that what we're learning is important. one of the best professors I've ever had and she made me want to come to class and participate even though it wasn't required. girlboss fr I would do anything for her
Greatest teacher ever, easiest clas. Don't take it from anyone else

Prof Hooley is THE BEST professor I have had at BYU. She is so efficient with time, teaches super clearly, and tells you exactly what you need to know. She tries to ensure everyone is set up for success. Tons of extra credit, super accessible outside of class, beyond willing to work with you. Don't take Comms 300 from anyone else.

Hooley is a Hoot, and definitely one of my favorite comms professors! Media Law is boring but she made it so fun! Homework is also soo easy and you'll get full points on everything just by turning it in. Her TA was awful at grading stuff on time tho, and the textbook is expensive but besides that, it was a great class. Take comms300 from Hooley!

Professor Hooley is caring and keeps lectures fun. The blended option was nice, so I watched some lectures remotely. Exams aren't too difficult if you keep up with what's discussed in class and readings. She brings food sometimes too!

Professor Hooley is awesome! She really wants you to succeed in this class. She allows for anything that allows you to do well in the class. She is very organized with her Canvas content. She gives a good window for due dates. This class was only once a week so we had a good amount of time to complete the readings, quizzes, and discussion boards.

If you don't take her class you're missing out so much. For the subject material would normally be so boring but she brought a lot of life to the class and I actually looked forward every week to going to class. She cares so much about every student and her energy lights up the room. TAKE HER CLASS

This is a blended course and she records her lectures. Professor Hooley is my favorite! She is an easy grader, nice, and willing to help her students. You have 2 short papers and 2 exams. Stay on top of things because it will only make your life easier because the class is already super easy!

If you have to take this class or, TAKE IT FROM PROF HOOLEY. She is the best!! Wasn't too happy about having to take an evening class, but I ended up looking forward to it every week. She prepares you so well for the tests and they are all open note. She is so funny and kind and the lectures were so relevant and engaging.

I LOVED DR HOOLEY! She is sooooo funny and easy to talk to and you can tell she really cares about her students. Midterm and final are really easy especially because you get to use an outline you've worked on all semester!

She is the coolest teacher, she invited us all to her thanksgiving and I considered skipping my family dinner to go to her house instead. She teaches everything in such a simple way and then asks you to explain everything in the same way on the tests which is so convenient. Also any notes you take can be used on both the midterm and final!

Hooley is the best!!! She makes media law enjoyable and easy to understand! She's an easy grader, flexible, understanding, fun, offers extra credit, and lets the class out early. Throughout the semester you make an "outline" which is basically just your notes that you can use on tests! The tests were never stressful or hard if you use your outline!

Prof Hooley is awesome. She always lets you out early and every term we learn about she talks about real-world issues to help you remember. The test is open note and really not bad. I don't really do the reading ever and still understood everything.

Hooley is one of the funniest professors I've had at BYU. She makes sure to get to know her students and encourages less lecturing and more class discussions. She makes the course easy to understand and does all she can to make sure you do well. I would take every class from her if I could. Really knowledgeable but can break it down effortlessly.

Amazing professor! If you have to take this class definitely take it from him! His lectures can feel long at times but he keeps them entertaining and allows for lots of participation to share thoughts. His exams were very straight forward and easy as long as you study the material on the study guide.

Professor King is an incredible professor. I took his class spring term, which was twice a week for three hours each time. The readings were really interesting and were manageable to do each week. He was a very helpful professor and truly wanted his students to succeed. He shared really cool stories that made the class super engaging.

I took this class during the spring term, and I highly recommend taking it. It was a 3 hour evening lecture, but Professor King really brought the energy to the class. His lectures are engaging, funny, and memorable. Weekly journals and tests are easy, and he gives you all the study material you need. He is very considerate and accommodating!

He loved talking about ancient art. He skillfully used stories to help us remember each piece. Three hour art lectures were exciting and he even brought jolly ranchers. Weekly Journals were easy. Would recommend his class to anyone. Study the two study guides for exam one and exam two, and you will get an a.

Professor King was awesome! I took his 3 hour weekly night class. He was very upfront that the night class would be rough, but I thought he did a great job. He was very realisitic (it is art history after all) and  funny during all of his lectures. The weekly assignment was easy and he gave you everything you needed to do really well on tests.

Probably the funniest professor I've ever had. As a senior it was nice to just have a class based on lecture. Weekly assignments were cake and I never studied any dates on both exams and still got B+'s on both. Also a really really good teacher

I took the 5-8 pm lecture and it was ROUGH. Could not stay awake for the life of me. One journal a week with two exams (he gives you the exact things to MEMORIZE). If it's your last option for your GE then take it, but just know that it will be impossible to pay attention in. Easy A in the end though.

Professor King is amazing!! I took the 3 hour night class and while I probably won't take that long of a class at night again, due to my own attention span, professor King kept the class SUPER engaging and is very passionate about it. Tests were part memorization (art ID and vocab) and then an essay, but he gives you everything you need to know!

Took the 3 hour once a week section and I wouldn't recommend it. Lectures were boring and I paid no attention. Attendance was mandatory to pass the class. Although I never paid attention in class I got an A because I studied for the tests (all were relatively easy) on my own. King's lectures were always all over the place, following them is hard.

She is a sleeper. I'm surprised her rating here is low because she was very helpful and understanding when i had trouble with assignments, definitely recommend for this class. Just be on time to class, if you're there and listen and are friendly she will respect you and it can be fun.

Honestly, this course was not very enjoyable. She uses dozens of paper handouts in class instead of online assignments and it's kind of overall messy. She doesn't accept late work and the classes were boring.

I wish I had waited and taken it from someone else. She's a nice person but her office hours were all over email and she made it very difficult to ask questions. Subsequently when I did ask questions I often felt ridiculed. There is no support if you don't understand the material, especially grammar. Wait a semester, take it from someone else.

She can come off as pretty harsh, especially at the beginning of the semester, but she genuinely cares about the class and the students. The course material is set for 321 so she doesn't have much control over it, and sometimes she can explain concepts in a confusing way, but do all the assignments on time and study and you should have an easy A.

I loved taking this class from Profesora Blackwell. I was initially nervous because of the reviews on here but she's honestly such a great teacher and her class was super entertaining. She doesn't have much control over the course since SPAN 321 is the same for everyone but she was always willing to help and answer questions.

One of the worst teachers I've ever had to be honest. Won't let anything be turned in late even if she messed up the assignment. Not enthusiastic at all and can't explain well because she's a native. Sometimes she's kind of mean or cold towards students. Very negative experience

Professor Blackwell is a very nice lady, but her class was neither good nor bad. It was tedious that there were lots of times throughout the semester on which due dates were switched last minute or assignments were added out of nowhere. The exams aren't very hard neither are the assignments, but she can be very picky about certain things.

I LOVE her. She cares, she's brilliant, she's hilarious, she's organized, she's understanding. Only 3/14 of us got A's. TIPS: DO the little assignments 100% along the way, they will pull your grade. EVERYTHING for the tests is straight from the textbook. Tophat took some time getting used to, but I LOVED it by the end. I learned soooo much :)

Neither love nor dislike. She clearly likes her job, but the class isn't super entertaining. You answer questions and work in groups a lot. None of the homework isn't hard, but it often seems pretty tedious. If she's available as a choice just go for it.

She's so cool, I liked her a lot. Really helps with your understanding of Spanish. May not be your style if you want an easy A, but she will help you out for the end test that covers up to 19 credits.

Not the nicest lady. There are so many dumb assignments in this class. All my friends that I talk to have said this was the easiest class for them. Not the case with Blackwell. Very harsh grader on papers and the dumb thing was is that the format she told us to write in was wrong on her syllabus. No rubric, and when I asked she said she forgot it.

Span 330. Worst professor at BYU. Hands down. The lectures were extremely boring. We had to write a page or 2 analysis of a Spanish poem in Spanish before each class twice a week. The average score for the midterm was 52. He gave us a study guide and said "Everything on the test is on this study guide." That was not the case.

He was an absolutely fantastic teacher, and quite possibly my favorite Spanish teacher here. He really worked with his students and made it so entertaining. I was always excited to go to class. I just wish he taught more classes.

Yeah, he's an alright teacher. He knows stuff. However, his grading is questionable especially on the papers. He's not very clear on what he wants and then will give a bad grade if he feels it's not up to his standard. Anyway, this is purely anecdotal, my second class with him. You'll need to really pay attention to patterns in what he's teaching.

Professor Sherman was great at explaining important points and making the class engaging and applicable. I wouldn't take him again though because the grading tended to be arbitrary, inconsistent and unpredictable. He had students grade each other, took points off if we didn't say exactly what was on his slides and graded participation very harshly.

I loved taking this class from Professor Sherman! From the very beginning he lays out his expectations for you, and if you follow them you will do well in class. The tests are not too hard, just make sure that you do the readings and fill out/study his study guides. He is very willing to help, and his lectures are not monotonous and boring.

He brings a different perspective to the New Testament, leveraging his background in Greek and ancient Christianity. Sometimes I feel like I could teach the religion classes but I certainly don't have the knowledge he has. There are very few things your grade hinges on, and he seems allergic to giving full credit to anything, so watch your grade.
Great teacher and very knowledgeable. I always learned a lot from his lectures.

Very knowledgeable in New Testament history and the Greek language. His lectures are very informative and interesting. You learn a lot more than normal religion classes. If you're looking for motivational, I wouldn't recommend him, but if you want to learn more, he's your guy.

Dr. Blumell is VERY intelligent with bible studies so this class felt more like an ancient history class than a religion class. You really have to stay on top of the readings and the review guide is a LIFESAVER. I think I went into it thinking it would be an easy BYU religion credit but I was wrong. But the content is insightful and worth the work!

Dr. Blumell is one of the best professors I have ever had a class with. His lectures are insightful, uplifting, and he has a profound knowledge of Greek. He is also especially caring. During the semester I had a family member who got sick and he was more than happy to work with me on absences. I definitely recommend his classes!

Dr. Blumell's class was more academically rigorous than most other religion classes that I have taken at BYU, but well worth it. I learned much about the New Testament. His tests can be hard, but if you use the provided study materials, you will be fine. Well organized, great professor.

I don't recommend him. Lecture was always kind of boring and dry. Felt more like I was in an ancient Rome history class rather than a religion class. Tests were pretty brutal. I filled out the study guide as he was teaching, studied it, and went to a 2 hour TA review session and didn't do well. Too intense for a 2 credit religion class

Pro Tip: If you're taking the 392R class, get his study guide from the beginning, make a list of everything on it, and then fill it out as the course goes. Will make the tests phenomenally easier. Tests are brutal as far as religion tests go, but I learned a ton in this course, and he is extremely caring and willing to help. Very responsive!

Man, throughout the whole semester I would come back and read professor Blumell's reviews and I just didn't see it!! Yes, he is very smart but BEWARE of the pop quizzes. The lack of posted lecture slides is obnoxious and he expects you to remember random things. Test questions often times vague match up with the study guide so listen intently....

As you've read, there is a lot of super cool history intertwined into his lessons. I personally think that while the lectures don't play out like devotionals, and they aren't the kind of spiritual that will ever make you cry, it definitely helps your personal study become much better as you begin to understand the bible like never before.

GREAT class!!! You have stupid quizzes but less than 5 in the semester. If you take the study guide to him, he pretty much tells you what you need to know. Just memorize, memorize the study guide and you'll ace the tests. Papers are easier topics and it's just one longer one, 5-6 pages I think. Attendance does effect yo grade. Not a stressful class

He's quite intelligent but weak at conveying it in an accessible manner. It's a class all about memorization, if you like that, you'll do great. It's shallow doctrinal analysis but deep contextual analysis. I learned more about the origins of the bible, Jewish culture, and ancient language than I did "Jesus Christ and the Everlasting Gospel"

Do the readings and fill out the study guide, and you'll be fine. We had 3 grades (multiple choice and essay, but he gave the essay question at the beginning of the unit) and we had to read the gospels. No outside essays. If you put in the work, you'll get an A. I learned a lot in the class, but it wasn't always super spiritual.

Dr. Blumell is a leader in his field, and his knowledge exhibited in the lectures reflects that. He talks fast, but is still engaging with the things he shares in lecture. He shares some interesting things that you don't hear in sunday school. Tests are manageable and clearly outlined for you in the study guide for each exam.

I loved this guy.  He teaches just like I like.    He knows Greek and Hebrew, which is amazing for a bible class. He is able to cover a lot of information in a very easy to understand way and I loved going to his lectures. However, I can easily see that many other people won't find him as awesome as I did.

I LOVED this class. He is always excited to share any knowledge he has and he just wants you to learn everything you can. His exams are well-balanced and if you're interested in the material you'll do great on the tests. I got more out of it without putting in as much work as I originally expected. The pop quizzes were the only thing I didn't like.

Professor Blumell really knows about the ancient world and helped me a lot to understand the basic reasons of early Christianity. His class has  a lot to cover in a short period of time which calls for a lot of reading and a lot of material to cover during the tests. He tried to prepare us as best as possible.

Prof Blumell is my favorite religion professor. He clears alot of stuff up, and is not significantly biased like normal byu religion professors. You learn a lot that can clear up once contradictory passages. He is a true scholar.

I really enjoyed this class. Professor Blumell has taught about the New Testament at several different universities, so he has somewhat of a less-biased BYU perspective on a lot of topics. That being said, this class is definitely more of an academic type of religion class. Be prepared to put a lot of effort in, especially in studying for tests.

During the first couple weeks of classes, I did not like Professor Blumell and his class. But he definitely grew on me, and has become one of my favorite teachers.  He is extremely smart and teaches a lot of facts that don't really warrant you to feel the spirit a lot, if that means a lot. His personality is an acquired one, but the class was great

He's seriously a genius. If you're looking for a warm/fuzzy religion class, this isn't the one for you. He is VERY factual, & also fluent in hebrew and greek. He's one of the most knowledgeable professors I've ever had. 3 tests, assigned readings before class, 1 paper, read 2 of the gospels. TAKE GOOD NOTES - slides are NOT posted online.

I can only imagine that somone who didn't like this class had no desire to actually learn. Dr. Blumell is an amazing professor and I have never gotten so much out of a religion class. If you read the assigned chapters, you will find this class very easy.
So the tests are pretty straight forward, but if you have any special circumstances (a death in the family) good luck getting any extra help or adjusted time tables.

Blumell does a very good job of explaining the New Testament using facts and his great language background. He never tests students on his personal beliefs or concepts, the class is largely factual and is basically the perfect balance of facts and inspiration you'd expect from a university level religion class. His lectures can be dry though.

I have REALLY enjoyed Dr. Blumell. He is super knowledgable in the New Testament and sheds light on subjects that you've never thought about before. I loved studying the New Testament... if you make this your "scripture study" for the semester, the class really is a breeze! Tests--got over 90 on all, just study the study guides!!

Dr. Blumell has a great knowledge of the NT.  His knowledge of Greek and Hebrew makes the material interesting.  Study guides are really helpful in preparing for tests.  One response paper & 3 pop quizzes dispersed throughout the course.  Can't miss more than one class wo losing points.  Also, a HW reading of Mark and Luke.  Very good overall.

His lectures are great and it was interesting to know more about the Bible. His tests are not tough, but there's a lot of reading. Only 3 pop quizzes during the semester and 2 take-home quizzes that were really easy. Also demands reading Mark and Luke for a 5%. Great guy, always open to questions and tries to answer them as clearly as possible.
A great Professor and I learned a lot. I enjoyed the class regardless of the fact that it was a lot of work.

Dr. Blumell is a Bible genius and you will learn so much from him. He is one of two faculty at BYU who can read ancient Greek, so he will teach you cool things out of the original Bible transcript that you would never learn anywhere else. However, if you're looking for an easy A, look elsewhere. You will earn your grade in this class.

His class is really interesting, but his tests aren't great. One of the Questions was "Who was the governor of Cyprus during Pauls first mission." He goes really in to detail which is awesome in understanding the background. But his tests require you to know everything. This class is only 2 credits and not worth it if you want a nice easy REL class

If you're looking for a class that combines spiritual learning with background to the NT, this is the professor to learn from. It's not easy if you don't study, but if you do, the scriptures come to life and you learn about jewish history at the same time, which helps you learn the NT.

He's a good teacher, he's generous with his study guides, so if you look through his study suggestions and slides a few times you are golden. He's also fair when it comes to grading the paper, if he sees you read the material and put in the effort, he will give you an A. Class was interesting and I enjoyed it overall. Memorize the dates!!!

Blumell is very knowledgeable & uses his time wisely to get across the material you need to learn. However this class required much more work than a 2 credit class should have! There were 2 very hard papers. Tests had essays & short answer. Only take class if you already know alot about the subject of early Christianity & have tons of time to read.

I don't usually write reviews but I must say that I loved taking this class from Dr. Blumell.  He really knows his stuff and his lectures are always really interesting.  I was very impressed with how well structured his lectures were. If you want a NT class with great historical background mixed nicely with spiritual learning then take his class!

LOVE this class. Dr. Blumell is a fantastic teacher. You will learn a ton of background info about ancient Judaism, which is very helpful for overall understanding of the NT. Tests aren't difficult at all. The paper is scary, but not impossible. This class is more academic than spiritual, which I really appreciated. Great class, great teacher!

Very knowledgeable professor. A useful class. I learned a lot more than in most of my previous religion classes. Some study is required, but very manageable. One six-page paper was required. I complained about that a lot, but in hindsight, it wasn't that bad.

It was nice to take a religion class from a scholar of the Bible. Professor Blumell really knew what he was talking about. It was cool that he could teach us about the ancient languages different manuscripts were written in as well. Although I didn't like writing the long response paper, I did learn a lot from it.

Lots of Background information and knowledge of the time around the NT.  He can speak and read ancient Greek, and does frequently in class, which can sometimes be interesting. Spends a lot of time on technicalities and you are tested on things that he does not emphasis on in class.  Great guy, but there is just a lot of information.

Despite this mostly academic approach, the spirit was still very strongly present, and affirmed that what he was teaching was true.  It allowed me to get closer to my Savior, and better understand him, in a way that would not be possible in a setting such as Sunday School, but that required an academic focus.  I loved this class!
He is super knowledgeable about the new testament and all his insight was great. my least favorite thing about taking the class was the 6-8 page paper.

I felt that Professor Blumell's class was more academically and historically based than spiritual. He is a nice guy but wasn't very friendly and personable. However, he is very informative and knows his stuff. Pop quizzes are not multiple choice but fill in the blank. He gives a lot of announcements at the very beginning of class so don't be late!

Great guy. Easy to talk to. He has pop quizzes but gives you the questions the class before. Highlight the key scriptures he mentions. He uses slides but everything you need to know is in the Book of Mormon. I would recommend bringing a new cheep BoM and underline the scriptures he talks about.

Dr. Blumell is a great professor.  The lectures were very informative and I learned a great deal about the BofM that I hadn't previously known.  He studies ancient Christianity and uses it to help understand the events that are happening as we are reading them.  Very informative!  One of the best religion classes I have taken
Really nice professor and knows the subject matter extremely well.  If you want to know about the history and background of the New Testament his class is the best!!!!

A great professor on BYU campus!  He really knows his stuff and ancient scripture.  Even though he's totally an expert on the subject he's still very humble in that he likes to engage the class in discussion and hear others' viewpoints.

Dr. Blumell is an amazing professor to take for New Testament. Since his areas of expertise lie with the New Testament and Ancient Christianity, the background he provides to understand the New Testament is absolutely Fabulous! I wish I could take him again to learn more about Christianity in the Scriptures. Fantastic Teacher, Highly Recommended!!!

Dr. Blumell is proffessional- but not boring. He likes discussions in class, and fits true to his first day explanation of the class. It's not sunday school or too analytical. I had another Religion class this semester and felt more edified in that one, but this class isn't a bad choice. He is understanding and knowledgeable-- Critics aren't fair.

Really enjoyed Dr. Blumell.  Religion professors can never make everyone happy with their balance between the historical details and spiritual content, but I thought Dr. Blumell did it very well.  One paper, which wasn't tough at all, a couple of quizzes, and 3 exams.  Exams, if you review a bit, aren't bad.  Recommend.

Acts-Revelation is usually a harder course.  He likes to test on obscure things in text like names.  However he has a decent balance of easy vs hard questions.  In class quizzes are hard because at times picking out an obscure reference from Paul in the KJV is hard.  He knows his stuff!  Take this class if you want real history in your rel class.

He says the first day his class will be difficult.  There is only one paper and other than that if you read you will be able to get an A.  Extremely interesting, class is more history based than others, but cool to see a new perspective on the bible.

Oh my word!Dont let other people fool you with how amazing this teacher is.Hes such a joke.He likes to brag about all the ancient scripture texts he can read and just uses the class as an ego boost.His tests are ridiculous and its basically like am.htg for BOM. we even had to know governmental systems...take from somebody else!Not spiritual at all!
Dr. Blumell rocks. He has a great balance between academics and religion, but you still learn the text well. Highly recommended.

Lincoln Blumell is one of those amazing religion professors that has found the right balance between scholarship and spirituality. I loved his insights, the workload was very light--great for a psycho chem major like me--and the spirit is there. If you get the chance to take a class from Professor Blumell, jump on it!

Dr. Blumell is an outstanding teacher and a great person. He put the scriptures in a way that made me want to go home and do the next reading every single night. He's super knowledgeable, brilliant in terms of ancient scripture, but also very humble and likable. He really PROVES the veracity of the text while also encouraging your testimony.

Dr. Blummel is a really nice guy, but he has the perfect voice that lulls you to sleep.  All you basically do in that class is go over what you read the day before in Powerpoint Presentations that take up the whole class time. He has pop quizzes on the readings, but they're really easy. Good person, I just didn't enjoy him as a teacher.

He is the best! Class is always interesting, and he PROVES the truthfulness of the Book of Mormon to you because he's an expert on ancient scriptures. The tests are hard, but if you study the study guide and pay attention in class everyday, you'll do just fine! He's the best!

I really enjoyed going to his class and learning both the historical and spiritual background in the New Testament. He is a genius, but not one to make you feel stupid at all during class. He is a humble, amiable, and approachable professor. I would recommend him.

I thought he was a good teacher, and I learned a lot in the class. We didn't have a book or packet, just the scriptures. It was a lot more history-based than some religion classes, but it did seem to get more spiritual as the semester went on. The class wasn't too hard, but be prepared to attend class every day, and to study for the tests.

Really great professor. He knows a lot about the ancient world and relates historical things to the Book of Mormon to PROVE its truthfulness. He is very interesting and you actually learn things. He really teaches things to you.

Dr. Blumell is a decent Book of Mormon teacher.  You don't dig super deep into the spiritual aspects of the scriptures, but you do learn a lot of the historical backing behind it, seeing he got his Doctorate in something about ancient scriptures (he reads papyrus for fun).
Linda is literally the best. If you get offended by her get tougher skin. She is honest in the best ways and cares about her students a lot. Best teacher
She kind of reminded me of Meryl Streep in Devil wears Prada at first but then you realize wait she's so lovely and kind and genius and pushes you to be so much better. Everyone loves Linda!!!

I LOVE LINDA I WANT TO BE HER WHEN I GROW UP. I have taken a lot of classes from her, 245 was the 1st. She can come across as aloof but is really just a kind, introspective creative genius. Ask her about her hobbies they are so cool. She is so cool. Do everything you can to make Linda your best friend (especially if you are applying to the GD BFA).

I absolutely love Linda and this class! She has weekly 1:1 meetings with each student, giving clear and helpful feedback. She's great at helping you improve your ideas and pushes you to become a better designer. Linda is caring and thoughtful—highly recommend her!

I ADORE LINDA REYNOLDS!!! She is so caring and makes an effort to build relationships with her students. She is honest and gives straightforward feedback, yet does so kindly. She will never critique you without helping you work through problems you are having. Linda is one of the best professors to ever work at BYU. Cherish your time with her!

Linda is amazing! I love her so much! She makes you work for it and will be honest with you about what she thinks (sometimes brutally honest), but she knows what she's talking about and always tries to be kind and respectful about it. She really tries to help prepare her students for the BFA application, and is more than wiling to help with it.
I love her the most in all the world.

Linda is great! She's hard to please, but she's never mean about it. She forces you to push yourself the very most to do well in her class, which allowed me to come out of the class with my very best work that I'm proud to have in my portfolio. She's also very caring and kind, and definitely wants the best for you.

I LOVED Linda! My class was smaller since I took her over the summer, but I received one on one feedback, which is what I needed for sure. She's a very honest and caring professor, also sooo funny. She was vulnerable in showing her work and explaining the meaning. I learned so much able design through her teaching style. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND!!

Linda is first of all, caring. You can tell she loves her students and she's real with us. 115 was great, especially for graphic design pre-majors since she's part of the GD faculty. She has a visual preference for asymmetry and a "graphic" style. I like how we all got to present and talk about each other's projects and get feedback from everyone.

Linda really knows her stuff, and taking this course from a full time faculty member lets you know what to expect in the program. Sometimes the projects are a bit vague, but they let you be creative and think about the project more. She's very honest in her critiques, which can be hard, but so useful long term. I grew a lot in this class bc of her!

While Linda is not easily understood, she is brilliant. She makes you work for it, so she comes of more confusing and hard. But her projects are designed to evoke creativity. I've been able to do my best work in her class because she has so much knowledge and talent that she is willing to share. I would take every class I could from her.

Linda is a wonderful designer, but the projects can be quite difficult to understand at times. Grading is also a little confusing, because there isn't a good system of feedback in the classroom. Overall, if you're in her class, you can definitely do it! But I would recommend another professor.

Linda is very interested in her students and is just there to help! She is very friendly and has such a creative eye. Many of her assignments were confusing at first but as you get to know her and ask for her input, you will really appreciate her thoughtfulness into her rubrics, and appreciate her feedback.

Linda is an amazing person, but to be completely honest, I don't think she is cut out to teach graphic design anymore. The projects are always super confusing and I remember coming home one day thinking I was a terrible graphic designer despite all the feedback I had received from other sources. I recommend taking this course from another professor

This is a good professor if you're looking for an easy A. The class was 3 credits but I did almost no work outside of class besides the big essays and projects. I did the readings for the first few weeks, but stopped when I realized they didn't mean anything for my final grade. She also gave out a lot of extra credit

Professor Tanner is great! She is always willing to work with you and gives helpful suggestions when you have conferences with her. The class is reading-heavy but overall manageable. A lot of the downsides of this class are from writing department requirements and not Professor Tanner herself.

I LOVE Lindsay. I didn't think I would after reading the reviews on her, but she is amazing. She is funny and keeps things interesting. Plus, she shows you how she grades so you know exactly what to expect on the assignments. She gives plenty of time to work on assignments and gives good feedback through meeting with her one on one.

For a grad student, she is really great. She is super funny and relateable. She looks to the students for feedback on what she can do better. There are only four papers due for the class and they're not that bad. She doesn't weigh your grade entirely on the score of your papers, so you can relax and just learn.

I wish I had gotten a different professor for WRTG150, Professor Tanner is so focused on rubrics and grading that she doesn't ever help the students get the actual concept she is supposed to teach down. The second paper into the semester was beyond confusing, and we were pushed to finish it without ever understanding what we were supposed to write.
Super funny and nice. She's willing to work with you and she listens to the class' concerns. There are semi-diffcult papers of course, but also easy homework assignments that help your grade.

I'm not sure how long Lindsay Tanner has been teaching, but, from a student's perspective, it doesn't seem like she's yet found how to teach well. She gives quite a few readings to accomplish, yet only discuses one or two of them; it's a waste of time. She's confident in her teaching style and doesn't always listen when told it's not effective.
Dr. Howard is a great teacher. She is a harsher grader for formatting than any of my 300 or 400 level professors.Every class was basically the same thing. Easy A, not super helpful course

I don't love writing, and this class is a lot of writing. She doesn't permit any use of AI except for a few assignments near the end of the class. I did the textbook readings during the actual quiz and did 90% or better on quizzes. She really cares a lot about her students and you can tell from the way she speaks in emails and messages.

she is kind, fair, and very helpful. the class itself is not too bad, but there certainly is busy work pretty consistently. its impossible to get a bad grade if you actually do the assignments. if you want a writing class to expose you to scientific writing in biology, id say she is a great professor to take it from.

Bio 316 has a giant workload of a class and it was all online. Given this workload she made sure to cater to my needs and was lenient on her grading. She gave clear feedback and was always helpful for students who wanted to learn. If you do the work you'll get a good grade.

It's really a shame that professors like this are allowed to teach at this university. I have never met someone less professional and more egotistical. This is a completely online course, yet she is totally unreachable and unresponsive to any attempted communication. She could not care less about any of her students. Avoid at all costs
