I actually took ELING 273. Professor Johnson is spectacular! She is so caring, so fun, and great at trying to make somewhat boring class material as fun as possible. She's easy to reach outside of class and really does care about the success of her students.

This is for LING 452. SO. MUCH. WORK. At least 2 quizzes a week on readings that take 2+ hours, 1 mini project each week, a midterm, a final, AND a 7-10 page paper. Possible to get an A, but she makes you work HARD for it. Kind professor though, and she's willing to meet with you outside of class.

I learned so much about linguistics from her and learned outside of linguistics too. She is a great lecturer that keeps you entertained and her course is pretty easy if you do all the reading and show up for class. Her assignments are not hard at all and the exams are a breeze if you pay attention 50% of the time.

Pro. Gunther is AMAZING and so nice. Great professor and actually connects humanities to every person pursuing any major to make the class worth your time. Interesting in-class conversations. Spring term had 2 tests, reading assignments, and 3 papers. Don't bother getting the textbook, but get the books somewhere. Easy but really rewarding class.

Take this class from her! I took it in the Spring, so it was very reading heavy, but other than that this class was a breeze and super easy! I always felt the Spirit so strongly in her class, even though it isn't a religion class. The tests were super easy as well!

I have never been a huge fan of the humanities, but after having Professor Gunther, I would have taken a million more of her classes. She tells history like a story, makes everything in the class feel relevant, all while teaching about art, literature, and their relation to us today. She is incredible and cares deeply about her students.

Pro Gunther is passionate and kind! She cares about the students and their success! Lectures can be long, but she tries to break them up with different interactive elements. Homework wasn't super heavy, but be prepared to read. You need quite a few books for the class. Tests are long but super easy as long as you pay attention!

Guys!! Lisa is by far the best IHUM 201 teacher ever!! She really cares about her students and she puts so much effort into her class! The readings arent bad and are super short! She is such a good teacher and makes the class so easy! I dont ever waste my time to write these but if youre going to take IHUM 201 this is the lady to get it done from!

She was amazing! She has been my favorite teacher I have taken from at BYU. She was so amazing and so passionate about the topics she talked about, but made it doable for non humanities majors. TAKE IT FROM HER!!! Easiest general by far all due to her. Don't get behind and do the work but it's so easy because she makes it so doable.

My favorite professor I have had. She was so caring. She invited students to come to dinners at her house, she knew our names, and she was understanding about home work and assignments. The class was interesting and engaging.

I am currently in her class and I usually dont review teachers often, and if I do, it's at the end of the year. But I just love her! I have absolutely no interest in humanities, but she is so passionate and relates it to our lives, and loves what she teaches. She makes it so easy to understand. Pretty easy tests withs barely any essays! Take her!!

Prof. Gunther is super nice and so willing to help. She wants you to succeed in class and makes that possible in every way. idk why some people are saying this class was hard and the tests are long. I finished every test in under 15 min and there isn't a ton of homework. Compared to the other humanities GE classes this one is def the best.

She is such an awesome teacher! I originally took ARTHC 202 and I absolutely hated it but her class completely changed my opinion on arts and literature and it's by far one of the most interesting GE's that I've taken. She has a ton of energy/love for the subject while also having an understanding that none of us are going to major in humanities.
Very kind and helpful. She likes her job and is understanding.

professor Gunther was super nice &  a really caring teacher. i will say her lectures were super boring which made it hard to learn. definitely not an easy class &  lots of memorizing. i took this as a GE &  it was just not interesting to me at all. i would recommend spending 20 minutes a day memorizing the art &  you will be fine in this class.

She does a really good job at teaching this class in a way that is interesting for people that are not interested in humanities. Study guides for exams are on learning suite, just learn what is on there and you can do well on exams.

I loved this class, Prof Gunther is the best! Lectures were entertaining and you can tell she has a passion for the subject. There were 2 online exams, mostly MC but some free response. If you fill out the study guide and take notes in class you will be fine. Highly recommend this course for a general! Workload is reasonable, no excessive busy work

Gunther is an awesome professor. All material is covered in lectures--and covered well. She is engaging and educational. Readings are very beneficial and are discussed in class, but they aren't all required for passing the class. Her exams consist of a lot of memorizing, but it is all learned through repeated exposure and learning in class.

Fun lectures, good interaction and discussions with the rest of the class.  She's great at using history to relate to current life and affairs.  She helps you think about your life experiences, the gospel, and becoming less judgmental of others, or at least seeing things from others' perspectives.  Loved the class!

Fun professor.  I loved the class discussions, it really opened my eyes to a new way of thinking about life and the gospel. Self reflection papers made me really think about my past experiences. Definitely one of my favorite classes at BYU.  If you take the class, make sure you attend the final review!

It was clear she is very passionate about what she teaches and made it enjoyable to learn about these things. Classes are lecture heavy, lots of assigned readings, but most were heavily discussed in class, I didn't do all the readings and still got an A, she is very kind and goes out of her way to help you get a good grade you deserve.

Prof. Gunther is very knowledgeable in her teachings. She explains things well and is very open to questions. Her tests are very long and hard and there is a lot of writing involved. She gives you a study guide with everything you need on it, you just have to study a lot of things.

She was a great professor and help on everything. Sure the lectures were long, but if you actually do your work and have a general idea of what is going on in the readings, you will get an A. I honestly think anyone would really enjoy her class if they put in very little time.
awesome professor. does review sheet before tests. i wish she taught ihum202, would definitely take it.

Loved the lectures and class. Shes passionate about the subject matter which made me much more interested in it than I thought I would be. I took for a GE, but she helped open my mind to thinking about life, history and the humanities in new ways. Fantastic class, highly recommend. Not too hard to get an A.

Dont get me wrong, she is nice out of class; However, taking this class from her is not the move. most people take this course for the GE credit and she makes it unnecessarily difficult for those looking to just simply get the required credit. her lectures are long and boring. midterms are hard. gives pop quizzes. and write papers. not fun or good.

Her class was unnecessarily difficult. Midterms are incredibly long and impossible. 60+ free-response/fill in the blank with no word bank. Most boring lectures ever and I would watch every minute of the class go by. She talks the entire time and has no engagement with students so good luck staying awake. There are easier professors, take from them

Her lectures are just her speaking for 50 minutes and she'll mention something and say "You probably don't need to know this," and then put it on the exam. Her tests are incredibly difficult, always 60+ questions, fill in the blank, with no word bank. Save yourself some trouble, avoid this class from her

I took Comparative Animal Physiology with Dr. Bailey, and I loved my experience! The way her class was formatted is super conducive to learning, and has assignments that help you prepare for the open-response exams. Although they require applying yourself to the material, she took extra care to be super accessible to students. Great class!

Very easy class. Week-to-week assignments are short articles and then answering questions on them. Attendance, 4 quizzes on each unit, and a final project make up the rest of your grade. Take this class from her for an easy bio GE.
Her tests are very difficult but it forces you to learn what is being taught.

I really liked professor Bailey. She really cares for her students and wants everyone to do well. She isn't an amazing lecturer but the class is simple enough that you'll do fine if you pay attention. She records and posts all of her lectures. The lab was a complete waste of time. The tests are 24 mc worth one point and 3-4 frqs worth 4 points each

Bio 130 isn't an easy class. Dr. Bailey understands this and really works to have her students truly understand, rather than memorize, course material. Midterms can be difficult, but Dr. Bailey does care. Lab quizzes and homeworks will determine much of your grade. Challenging beginning bio class, but definitely not boring.

I love Dr. Bailey, You can tell she cares about her students and wants to do what she can to help them succeed. She explains concepts in a detailed way in class. Additionally, you are able to improve your midterm grades through the final. However, the 3 hr lab in class wasn't super helpful, but the lectures made up for it.
The course was honestly more challenging than I expected, and the labs and tests were hard. The grading system was pretty good though.

Dr. Bailey is very kind & a great professor. However, there were some aspects of the class setup that I didn't love--mostly how we went into lab knowing (& learning) basically nothing, only to be taught what we needed to know next lecture. Studying in a group is the key to success in this class. Also, DON'T buy the digital textbook. I used it once.

Dr. Bailey is both very kind and great at teaching. However, there were some aspects of the class setup that I didn't love, like going to lab basically knowing (and learning) nothing, only to be taught in the next lecture what would've been nice to know before. Also, DON'T buy the digital textbook. I used it maybe once.

Dr. Bailey was a great professor for BIO 100, and the way she structured the course made it easy to follow along. During the semester you will be working on a project that culminates with a final poster session. The tests are 3 quizzes based off the standards for each of the units. Take this class if you get the opportunity!

Dr. Bailey's lectures are not my learning style. She often has us reason through concepts before telling us about them, which takes up a majority of class time, that she runs out of time to thoroughly teach the concepts for her class. The 3 hour TA lab was a waste of time and didn't help me learn any content for the class.
Bailey has good lectures and lots of resources. She is also very available to help. Lab is the most pointless 3 hours of my life but that isn't her fault. Just take notes and you'll be fine.

I would not take her class again. I didn't like her teaching style; she often made us reason through topics before actually teaching them. She didn't spend enough time on important material. I studied for hours and still didn't improve. Her tests were short with no room for mistakes, and I really disliked the lab TAs.

I personally would not take this class, we had 4-question quizzes and 3/4 questions are choose all that apply (heavy on GPA). She was very nice, but I feel like I didn't learn much in this class. GO TO LECTURES and take notes! The tests are a heavy application of topics we learned, so you need to really know the information.

I love Dr Bailey so much! Her class was pretty hard and time consuming but she is very clear on helping you succeed and gives tons of practice questions before the exam!  I highly recommend this class! Don't be scared of how hard it is. They have lots of TA hours to get extra help and she really has been my favorite teacher so far!

She is one of the nicest ladies ever, so kind & puts effort into learning our names. The way this class is designed is rough. You're supposed to go to lab before learning about the material in lecture, but the lab is very confusing, and doesn't allot time for explanation, and lecture is a review of topics that were never initially explained.
She did amazing and she really wants to help us improve in our lives!
Dr. Bailey is an amazing teacher. She cares about her students, wants them to succeed. It was a great experience learning from her.
I love Dr.Bailey so much! She loves her students and really wants them to learn.

Professor Bailey is very kind and cares about her students. She is very quick at answering emails and always wants to help you. She grades tough, but is always clear about grading criteria and wants you to do your best.

BIO280: She really wants you to learn and is passionate about the material. You need to thoroughly know and explain the material in order to get full points on her tests. You actually have to learn, not just memorize. She talks fast but is very available for student questions. Very helpful and accommodating if you are sick or have other issues.

Professor Bailey is really nice and I'm impressed with her ability to memorize all of her student's names. I also liked how she had multiple grading scales so more people had the chance to get good grades. Our tests were all open note, but there are tests every 2 weeks. Attendance/Participation is mandetory. We had to write a giant paper.

I don't like biology. Didn't want to take this class. But Professor Bailey made it bearable. She understands that most of her students don't really care about biology and are not going to major in it. So she makes it as personalized as it could be with her fantastic grading scale. Really impressed by her taking the time to memorize everyone's name.

Dr. Bailey was my favorite professor this semester. She is amazing and makes her lectures fun and interesting. She knew everyone's name the first day of class and never failed to show that she truly cared. She always set us up for success. The only warning is that her class is NOT easy and takes hard work to do well. Would absolutely recommend.

Professor Bailey is THE BEST! Biology is not something that I particularly enjoy, but she made class fun and did a good job explaining concepts. There are 7 exams as well as a final, but it's all open-book, open-note. She also uses several grading scales to calculate your final grade (the highest grade across all the scales is the one you get).

Dr. Bailey was very available to help and her lectures were interesting. Biology doesn't come easy to me, so it was a harder class for me. THE TA'S ARE THE BEST. They are super helpful and there is always one available. Her assessments are all open book, but they're application based so they can be tricky. Overall a pretty good class.

A lot of work. Professor Bailey is awesome. However, some of the big assignments (5 in total) makes your life miserable. She required use to do peer review journal that will kill your grade.(Which is graded harshly and not lenient). Secondly, you will have 3-4 modules to finish a week and includes TQ and practice test+Assessments. not recommended

Professor Bailey is awesome. The course content are hard! If you have never taken AP bio I would not recommend this class! 5 big assignments for essays and papers that graded strictly by her TAs .All the assignments makes you semester miserable and having a hard time to study. If you are a hard worker then go for it. But if not, reconsider!!!!!

AMAZING!! I'm not interested in biology but because of Professor Bailey, BIO 100 was my favorite class. Prof. Bailey gives a good amount of homework, her lectures are interesting and engaging, and she prepares her students extremely well for the tests. There is a textbook but it's not required (I never used mine). I 100% recommend her class.

I loved Dr. Bailey! Her "Do Your Homework with Dr. Bailey" sessions were amazing. As long as you paid attention in class and did the practice tests, the formal assessments were very manageable. I didn't love her TQ's because I thought it was kind of dumb to ask myself questions that I had already known the answer to. She made biology interesting!

Pretty solid class, lectures are interesting and participation is encouraged. Her 5 option grading scheme is amazing and fits any learning type. iClicker subscription needed ($16), take notes and stay on top of the written assignments and you'll be fine. Great GE class!

One of the best professors I've had at BYU! She specializes in biology education and you can tell she's done a lot of research in how to teach the class. I wish more professors did that! TQ assignments involve studying with/teaching a classmate, so it's a good class to take with a friend. All tests are open note and open course material.

Probably the easiest way to do the GE credit. No textbook needed. I just did homework the whole class and then would use the PowerPoints to find the answers for the open book mid-terms. Easy A for pretty minimal effort. She is a good lecturer and makes the material pretty intresting. I learned some stuff but will have forgotten 90% in a week.

Liz Bailey was the worst professor I have ever taken a class from. She is unable to teach well, it goes to show that teachers should not be teachers just because they have a PHD. Her class was confusing and her test even more so. She gave us information but never taught us to apply it and all of her tests were applications tests. DONT TAKE FROM HER

Negatives: -WAYYYYYY too hard for a ge -class goes by fast, you fall behind a lot. -TA's weren't the best on getting help -unless you love bio, it sometimes gets super boring and confusing. Positives: -Learn about the covid vaccines and other cool things -Dr. Bailey is super nice -Great grading scale -you learn to work hard

I am a humanities major who usually hates having to take a science course. Enter Liz Bailey. She is one of the kindest, most caring professors I have had! Truly cares for her students and provides 6 different grading schemes to help all learners succeed. I loved the ways she prepared us for tests- having us teach students and take practice tests.

Dr. Bailey is such a great professor, makes the material easy to understand and gives you many opportunities to learn and become pros at the material. And even then, she makes sure you receive the best grade possible, which lessens the stress of the class. Great professor.

Loved Dr. Bailey! Her grading scheme is super fair, gives you plenty of opportunities to show that you understand the material-one bad test will not define your grade. She is helpful and patient and is easily works harder than any other professor I've ever had in helping make sure that students understand. This is the Bio teacher you need

I really enjoyed Dr. Bailey's class! I'd taken AP Biology the year before, so the class wasn't very challenging for me, but I still enjoyed attending lecture and hearing her insights. "Lab" was generally the most pointless 3 hours of my week, but that's mainly the department's fault.

Dr. Bailey is great. She really cares about students succeeding and gives as many opportunities for us to receive help as she can. Required homework through the week is minimal, so taking initiative on doing the optional practice problems is a good idea to do well on exams. There isn't any busywork and you can learn a lot if you want to.

Dr. Bailey is an amazing professor! She makes biology interesting. Her lectures are engaging and she makes sure the class understands before moving on. There are 6 exams and 6 small research assignments, but as long as you put in a bit of effort you'll be fine. She even uses five grading scales to give you the highest grade. Take BIO 100 from her!

She was honestly a good professor and made biology interesting. It's just that I felt like the workload was heavier than it needed to be. Besides SIX midterms, she also makes you do a series of 6 research assignments (and these do not drop the lowest scores or zeroes unlike the midterms can). Come prepared to work hard, and you'll be fine.

It's been a rough experience with Dr. Bailey. Her adaptable grading scale is nice, but her lectures are much more simple than her confusing exam wording. You have to sort through mazes of complicated words to see what she's getting at. Acts sympathetic to students, but shuts them down at times over genuine concerns because she has to be right.

Amazing. This is the least I've hated biology, her lectures are very engaging. She's completely on your side, I've never seen a professor do more than she does to help her students succeed. Gives clear points on exactly what will be on each test, and has multiple grading schemes to help you boost your grade. Still be ready to work and study though!

She is phenomenal. She gives good lectures, is always available or has TAs available, and her tests are fair. The best part about her class is that she has several grading schemes that cater to the different ways people learn (if you do well on the final but not on the tests, if you do a lot of homework but not well on the tests, etc.)

Sister Bailey is an incredible teacher! Her teaching is well set up to enable real learning. Really fun class to be in. Willing to change things to respond to criticism and overall just really cares about the students. Her tests can sometimes feel rigged but they honestly aren't. Once you put decent effort into it you'll get good grades.

She is super sweet and really caring, but this class has been unbearable for me. I feel like it's a huge game of learning how to think like Dr. Bailey instead of really learning Biology. It's nice that the tests are only worth like 6% each, but having a test every 2 weeks (6 midterms and a final) is just too much. Like HER, just not her class.
She tries her best to teach and is usually successful, but getting a good grade is tough if you don't think critically on her tests.

it really depends on if you are actually interested in Biology. She wants you to actually learn the material and teaches accordingly. Very tricky questions. Great if you want to learn biology, but if you don't really care and just want to memorize facts to get a good grade like myself to focus on your major then it's not the best experience.

Dr Bailey was my favorite professor this semester! She is a really great lecturer and makes sure everyone understands the material in class. She also is available outside of class to meet with to answer any questions and go over test questions with you. She legitimately cares about her students!

Liz Bailey is one of my favorite professors at BYU! She really cares about her students -- she quickly memorized everyone's names and she always encourages us to come to her for help. This was definitely a difficult course, even for me as a bio major, but if you study, work hard, and use your resources, it will be a great experience.

Doctor Bailey made Bio100 fun! I was impressed that she took the time to memorize everyones names. Where she has a couple of classes of 120 people, thats pretty impressive! Her tests are tough, but she gives a lot of study material, and if you study you will do well on her tests.

Dr. Bailey was an amazing professor. The class isn't too hard, but I learned and retained so much. She's done a lot of research on education to make it easier to learn everything. It's important to turn in your assignments on time, but there are a few extra credit opportunities.
Dr. Bailey cares a lot about her students, and wants each student to succeed. I thought it was cool that she took the time to memorize all the students names!

Dr. Bailey was probably my favorite professor of the semester. I've never had a professor who cares more about his/her students as she does. Not an easy A, you definitely have to put some effort in, but the way the material is structured really helps you to learn naturally instead of just forcing you to memorize random facts. I 100% recommend her!

BIO 100 was one of the easiest classes I've had because Dr. Bailey teaches it so well.  Her lectures are very easy to understand.  Take good notes and do the work and you will do very well.  I don't know why everyone says she is so hard...  This was one of my favorite classes so far.  If you need help, she will provide it.

Dr. Bailey is a wonderful teacher.    Since this is just a GE class she doesn't worry about going into depth about things that you don't need to know, but she does make sure you understand the material.  She is all about learning by participation.  TQ assignments weren't my favorite but REALLY helped prepare for the formative assessments and final.

Sister Bailey was my favorite professor this semester.  She is great at explaining concepts in lectures, and makes biology interesting.  She assigns a fair amount of work during the week, but it will really help you learn.  She makes sure you are prepared for the final and is willing to help explain anything you don't understand.

I like Dr. Bailey's passion for biology! She knows what she is talking about and she has done a lot with her education and career. She assumes that most students have a basic knowledge of biology --and that stretched me, being newly returned from a mission (last biology class in 9th grade). The beginning was very stressful, but it got better.

I have mixed feelings about her.  She is a super nice lady! She provides you with TONS of resources to be successful.  However, her tests are BRUTAL and even if you feel like you are understanding the material, you will feel like you aren't being successful in the class.  I hate Biology.  But I managed a B+ in this class.

Dr. Bailey expects a lot out of her students. For my BIO 100 class, she expected us to read the material beforehand, and come to class ready to briefly discuss it. For someone not good at science, this was very, very hard. If you don't like biology, don't take it from her.

Dr. Bailey is an outstanding educator.  She expects her students to put time and effort into actually learning the material, and gives plenty of opportunities to get help.  She genuinely wants her students to succeed. Her class was definitely one of the best I've ever taken.

Professor Bailey 's always willing to help and answer questions.  The tests aren't the easiest, but if you study you won't have a problem.  She keeps the class interesting and only gives homework that's actually helpful to the grade.  Her grading system grads on how well the subject is learned, not just on busy work.  Recommended!

Dr. Bailey does all she can to help her students. Awesome TAs willing to help, takes your best grade from five different grading scenarios. Some test questions were a little ambiguous but she was willing to give you the points if you had good reasoning and took the time to talk to her. Lots of work but it prepares you for exams if you stay with it.

Dr. Bailey tries. Her class is pretty tough for a 100 level class. She knows what she's talking about but is unable teach it in a clear, non-confusing way. If you fall behind expect to stay behind unless you put in some extra hours.

I adore Professor Dixon! She is one of my favorite professors I have had at BYU. MCOM 320 can be a tough class, but it teaches you so much, and Professor Dixon does her best to help you succeed. She always gave great feedback on the papers I turned in and was so helpful throughout the semester. Definitely take MCOM 320 from her if you can!

Liz is my favorite human! She incorporates Christ into everything she does and is the embodiment of everything good! She walks you through assignments so you know exactly what you're doing and you do a lot of assignments together in class. Not a lot of lecturing which is nice! She is an incredible woman and you should take M Com from her!!!

Liz is one of my fav professors at BYU! MCOM is hard in general, but she made the class better and I enjoyed going to class each day. She genuinely cares about each student and wants us to do well. The hw still requires time and effort, so don't slack, but she broke up the big assignments into manageable pieces. Take MCOM from her!

Prox Dixon loves each of her students, and clearly wants everybody to succeed. That being said, grading criteria wasn't always completely clear. To understand her expectations, meet with her. She would explain things in meetings that hadn't been fully explained in class or on the rubric. Overall though, she was really sweet, and I learned a lot.

I have a theory that the students that do not like her because don't like to put in the effort. She will motivate you to become a better person. This class is somewhat hard because it prepares you for the real world. It is not a class that can just be walked through. if you put in the effort, Liz and this class will help you grow greatly.

Liz is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. She is incredibly skilled in the material, and if you take the course seriously, she will be very invested in you. She is the director of the MCOM program and really tailors the experience to your needs. I definitely recommend and would encourage everyone to take MCOM320 from her!!

Liz is AWESOME! She cares about each of her students and gives amazing lectures. The people giving her the bad reviews are probably the students who didn't show up to class or ask for help. If you show up to class and ask for feedback before assignment deadlines, Liz will help you, and you will succeed in this class. LOVE. HER.

This class was, by far, the most unorganized I have ever taken. While the professor is very kind, kindness means nothing if efforts are swallowed up in unclear criteria and ridiculously weighted, pointless assignments. Assignment dates moved around constantly. Kindness means nothing if it not backed up. I would rather drop out than take her again.
Liz is awesome!! She is so kind and always willing to help and give feedback. She is an amazing teacher, I want to be in class because I learn so much from her.

Kind and passionate teacher. I recommend her 10/10.

Favorite teacher line: "We're friends you just don't know it yet."

Professor Dixon was not my cup of tea. Her canvas page was difficult to navigate, and her lectures and class were so confusing. She was a super harsh grader even though the instructions for assignments were unclear. Didn't work with me when I asked for partial credit for some late assignments. Take this class from another professor.

Liz is my favorite professor I've had at BYU so far! I took MCOM during Spring term, which was stressful, but Liz really helped me to enjoy the material and appreciate its relevance. She shows she cares about each student. She's an easy grader but gives great feedback, so you can learn by failure without stressing about the end result.

I absolutely loved taking MCOM 320 from Mrs. Liz. MCOM 320 is challenging regardless of who you take it from. Liz made this class bearable. She is literally one of the best professors I've had at BYU and just cares about her students so much. 10/10.

She is a good lady and caring, but she never replied to my emails even though I wanted to ask about gradings. You need to do exactly what she wants us to do if you want to get A in this class. The class wasn't organized well, and it seems like she didn't communicate with the TA enough.

This might be one of the best classes I took at BYU . You learn a lot and you make good friends. Liz is a fantastic teacher. She focuses on principles, she teaches you how to be a better communicator and a better person. Loved it. Lots of work, but worth it.

Liz is a good professor and I learned a lot from her. However, her grading criteria and syllabus are unclear. If you want to get an A in this class, please take another professor because she will curve down the final grade at the end of the semester. Only a few students can get an A with a super high score (They got around 99 out of 100 !)

Liz is a fantastic human being. She really cares about students. I took the class during spring online during COVID. I don't recommend taking the class online if there is an in-person option because getting to know Liz personally is essential! She is your friend. If you take in Spring, don't take anything else with it! It's worth the hard work.

Taking this class from Liz will be THE BEST decision you make during your undergrad, no matter your major, background, or anything else. The class is rigorous, but you will come out a better person. You will have to think; really thinkand CHANGE. Ask for feedback on all your assignments. The TAs and Liz are happy to help. MCOM+LizNew You
I liked her, but the class just felt very subjective. Do exactly what she wants and suck up to her and the TA's and youll get a good grade. She is a wonderful lady though.

Liz is the best prof and this was by far my fav class at BYU, not because I love business communication, but because Liz made me see the value in what she was teaching from day 1. She kept us engaged. The textbook is free. It's not an easy A, but it's valuable & useful work. There was a line out the door to hug her on the last day of class. Do it.

I'm conflicted with this rating. On one hand, I LOVED the class itself and Liz is a great personality. However, everyone was confused about what exactly was expected on assignments, with only a vague rubric to help, which resulted in losing points for things never discussed in class. Also, your grade basically came down to the group project.

Liz is great and I've learned so much from the class. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. With that being said, the organization leaves a lot to be desired. Everyone comes to class confused about what exactly we were supposed to do for assignments; there are no clear instructions for assignments. Just vague rubrics.

Not sure why this class and teacher have such raving reviews. Aside from grammar principles, I feel like everything we learned was common sense. Liz's communication style is boisterous. It was hard for me to pay attention to what she was saying. Learning Suite organization was not good. Full of things from previous semesters. This class felt silly.

Best class I have ever taken at BYU. Liz is literally the best MCOM teacher. I had a lot of friends in different classes and their teachers were psycho. Liz knows everything about grammar, so she will help you A TON for the MCOM standard grammar test. I learned so much from this class. Work hard and you'll do fine. Only one test! So, that's a plus!

Liz is an awesome professor and she knows her stuff. The class is not easy, especially the first part of the class, because of the grammar test. You can't get away from it by taking another professor, but Liz teaches it very clearly.

Liz is so great at what she does. I am in 7 classes this semester and this one by far had the most assignments, but she does a good job of building them all on each other so by the end you feel like you can do anything in business. I am way more confident in all the business skills but I should have taken this with a lighter load!

For the rest of your life you won't be able to send an email without checking your grammar seventeen times. Other than that, I loved this class.  Group projects were fun, and honestly it's not THAT hard, if you actually do rough drafts you'll get an A. I would absolutely take it from Liz as well.  She's a great teacher and she wants you to do well.

MCOM 320 is arguably the most useful class I've ever taken, and I can't imagine anyone teaching it better than Liz.  This is a very hard class.  Lots of work, especially at the end of the semester, but Liz teaches very clearly, and provides lots of help for her students to succeed.  Don't take MCOM from anyone else.

Liz Dixon is my favorite teacher at BYU thus far. Her expectations are very clear and if you stick to them and work well in your group for your project, you will get an A. Very willing to help students. Keeps the students actively engaged and is a great presenter. She has taught me some of the most valuable/applicable skills I've learned at college

This was an EXCELLENT class. Liz really cares about her students. I felt that her expectations were always very clear, and she is ALWAYS willing to meet with you or go over your assignments before they're due to help you get the grade you want. She's a seasoned pro, she knows what she's doing, and this class will help you get-and keep- a job.

I would not recommend you take this class.  Professor Dixon comes across as snooty and brash- not my idea of a good teacher.  The expectations and grading criteria are poorly communicated- important announcements, requirements for assignments, and other information is communicated only in class and not in other ways. Save yourself the trouble.

Liz Dixon is a very good professor.  She wants her students to succeed.  In this respect she is unlike any other professor I've met.  Her class is a lot of work but she still makes it engaging.  If you're not afraid to work hard, then take her class; she is amazing.

Liz is an incredible teacher. She is likely the best teacher I have had at BYU. Here classes are hard but she always lets you know what to expect. She cares a lot more about her students than about the norms of the departments she teaches in. GREAT TEACHER!

Liz is a great teacher. One of my favorites. She is a hard grader, but she always lets you know what she expects. She doesn't let herself get tied down too much with the departmental norm, which is nice. If you want to learn a lot, take Liz for Mcomm 320. She really cares about her students and is always willing to help. Great lecturer.
She is easily one of the best teachers I have had EVER. I learned a lot from her. Great class. Take it from her if you can.

Probably the best professor I've had at BYU. Very professional and very helpful. Everything she teaches is very applicable to real life applications (I use what I've learned every day at work). You have to go to class to do well. She can be a fairly touch grader, but her expertise exceptional teaching are well worth it. Great Class.

Liz is an awesome, inspiring teacher.  But her grading is VERY strict.  If you take this class, you will learn to write like to have never written before, and she will help you as much as you need.  But make sure you have time to dedicate--this is NOT a "bs" class!

Liz is an amazing teacher. She was excited and passionate through every lecture. This was by far my favorite class. You learn information you can really apply to the read world. Take from LIZ! She's the best!

I really enjoyed this class! It was very uplifting. Everything was very clear and the workload wasn't too much. Professor Snow is always willing to answer any questions you have and knows so much about family history work. She gives you so many resources to help you succeed. I highly recommend taking this class from her!

This class was wonderful! Professor Snow knows her information and conveys it in a clear manner. She is also fantastic to work with. If you have questions or concerns she is happy to make herself available to help. She really values learning, so she and her TA's will work with you to help you succeed.

This class was not my favorite. I just don't think im that interested in family history. It was hard to understand instructions for assignments and I often would need to ask her how to do it for everything. But other than that it was really chill.

This class is probably the easiest religion class you could ever take. Professor Snow makes it really easy to pass, she gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. If you miss an assignment or have to miss class. 100% would recommend, she is the sweetest professor you'll ever meet.

love love love her!!! she is so sweet and genuinely wants you to succeed. the nice thing about the big project is that you are constantly working on it throughout the semester, so you don't need to stress about it at the end. it's honestly not a hard class at all, def take it from her!!

She's a very sweet lady and she loves her students. The project was easy and you do a lot of it in class so it's nothing to worry about. I was able to get most of the assignments done fast. The class felt more like Sunday school than an academic class which I didn't like, but some people do. Overall, she's a solid choice for a religion elective.

Professor Snow is amazing! She is so sweet and caring! She has a great testimony of family history and loves to share it. Because of that, I feel like she was very understanding. It's a super easy class and there is a lot of extra credit. Take this class from her!
Can't recommend Professor Snow enough. Super easy class, and especially great if you're looking for a religion class that focuses more on practiced skills.

Prof. Snow is incredible, caring, and so passionate about what she teaches. Taking this class was such a great experience, and I never felt stressed; it's clear she just loves teaching about family history! There's participation and weekly assignments, but they're all super easy to follow, so as long as you show up you're golden. Take this class!

I think so highly of Professor Snow. She occasionally would send me emails with links to sources that related to my family. She was very forgiving of mistakes and was always willing to work with students. I missed a couple of assignments and still got a very high A in this class.

Sister Snow did a great job at teaching family history. I honestly only took this class because I knew it was going to be an easy religion credit, but I genuinely came out of it with a new appreciation for family history! Assignments were all straight forward. No exams. She is awesome!

Snow is the GOAT. She is super sweet, super understanding, and very knowledgeable. I was never stressed in her class! The homework is super light compared to other religion classes, and she really wants you to succeed. Just make sure to choose an easy research family and you will have a blast! Cannot recommend Snow enough, she is awesome!

Awesome! I loved HIST205 so much I TA'd for this class. ProfSnow has both a degree and is an Accredited Genealogist with ICAPGen (International Commission for the Accreditation of Professional Genealogists)- check their website- for Spain, 1 of 2 people in the world currently! Ample opportunity to earn an A: clear guidelines, extra credit!

Professor Snow is super awesome. She cares about her students and always gave inspiring lectures. She said that she had been dealing with some difficult things at home and my heart goes out to her; I admire her for coming to class every week and helping her students feel loved. BYU is lucky to have her. CANNOT RECOMMEND THIS CLASS ENOUGH!!!
Professor Snow is awesome! She really knows her stuff and is dedicated to helping students develop passion for family history. Really straightforward class, expectations super clear.
Best religion class ever!! I never rate professors but professor Snow is so kind and really works to make it a stress free class while still learning so much! 10/10 recommend.

Sister Snow is so sweet! Easily my favorite religion class I've taken at BYU, I definitely gained a desire to learn more about my family history and keep doing the work outside of class. The spirit is definitely in her classroom.
Prof. Snow is a literal sweetheart and her class is super spiritual and easy. Super great option for an easy religion credit when you have a tough course load.

Sister Snow knows so much about family history. She has such a passion for it. She does run through slides super quickly and without much explanation, but the family history project was so cool. This was a good course and a good teacher if you want to get your feet wet in family history.

Best professor ever! Snow is the sweetest, and she really cares about her students. Assignments are way easy (d/n fall behind). If you don't like your grade, she lets you resubmit for a better score. No midterm...the final is a piece of cake. Got me to love family history and develop a new appreciation for it. Take this class...amazing experience!

Professor Snow is amazing! Her class was very simple, yet I learned so much about family history. Her grading is clear and she gives second chances for anyone who is willing to take them. She truly cares about each student and wants everyone to come closer to their ancestors. Would recommend this class to anyone. Easy religion class!

Loved this class! Assignments were easy with clear rubrics. Sister Snow really cares about the subject and helped us to love it as well. She's very easy to reach and ensures that her TAs are as well. Final project was worked on over the whole semester, so just keep up with it, and the final exam was super easy as well.
Really easy assignments if you will just read the instructions. Lectures mostly talk about different types of records. But the semester starts and ends with doctrine

Sister Snow was the best teacher. She cares so much about family history it's inspirational. The material and slides are all posted online to review for the most straightforward test at BYU. She assigns talks and scriptures that she will discuss in the lecture slides. She takes attendance so be on time! It is near impossible to get lower than a B

Professor Snow helped me to get more into family history/Indexing. Some of the projects are unclear or a little confusing. Others are a breeze and are super easy. There was only one test in my class and it was an online mid-term that she went through before we took it. She takes attendance every class so make sure you show up!
Easiest class at BYU, and interesting. Take this class for one of your religion electives.

Professor Snow's family history class is amazing. She does a really good job of starting from the basics and working up to the more involved concepts. You work through a single family doing all of the in depth family history research for them. A majority of the assignments come from doing that. Some of the assignments are even completed in class.
Professor Snow makes family history very clear, easy, and satisfying. She's very willing to work with you. She's also very passionate about family history.

Professor Snow is the most respected professor at BYU so far that I have seen. I love her so so much. Please take her classes, she works with everyone and is so spiritual and loving. Highly recommended!

Best class and professor ever! She is a sweetheart and I learned so much about family history during the course. It's the easiest class I've taken at BYU, great religion credit. Would 100% take it again. Attendance matters.

LOVED this class! Take this class from Professor Snow! Pretty easy and straightforward but you learn a lot about family history! The rubrics are clear and it is not too much work. You do have a big final project that is done throughout the semester so don't procrastinate on that.

I took this course wanting to get a better feel for family history work and I really enjoyed it. If you work on your research logs for your projects a little bit at a time consistently then you will be just fine. We had a lot of freedom to choose what family in our tree we felt inspired to research and it was rewarding to hear what everyone found.

I took this class last semester and the other reviews must be fake because it was a HARD class. The concepts are easy but Pro. Snow and the TA's will dock massive points if even a period is off in a citation. Your entire grade is based on a project, and they will dock you whenever possible. She's very kind and passionate about what she does.

I love Professor Snow and I loved this class! It is so interesting, and she is so nice. This class is so easy and teaches you so much about FamilySearch and how to be better at genealogy work. I really enjoyed it!
I loved taking her class, she knows a lot and she cares about her students a lot.
One of the best classes I had. Super easy and insightful, totally recommend it.

STDEV 120 is necessary for international students, and it gives good information required for living in the States.  Prof. Ogden is very kind and patient, but could use improvement with the electronics. The class is very easy, just a few simple one-page essays and open-book quizes. You have to attend, because 30% of your grade is attendance.
Logan is awesome! He makes class engaging and wants everyone to succeed. Highly recommend this class as an easy elective
Logan is so kind and funny. He helped everyone to feel comfortable - even those who have never danced before. I hope he keeps teaching because he's the best!
Logan is hilarious and makes social dance fun and not awkward, which is impressive.
TAKE THIS CLASS. Packer is so knowledgable and the lectures are super interesting. 10/10!

Take this class if you're trying to fulfill the letters GE. It was super easy and lecture heavy but he was very entertaining. There is a textbook but I never used it and we never needed it for class so save your money and don't buy it. There were 3 papers and 2 assignments but they were all fairly easy especially for a BYU course.
One of the easiest classes I've taken at BYU. I am not a philosophy major, but Professor Packer was an awesome guy and made the class very doable.

Prof. Packer is a really great guy. Only a few papers that were pretty easy, so it was mostly showing up and listening (no need to take notes really, just enjoy his lecture). Very kind and willing to be flexible according to what the students need. Great class to fill your letters GE.

Professor Packer is amazing! His lectures are very interesting and he is funny. He understands that his class is not the only class we take and is flexible with due dates to ensure we can accomplish all the assignments without too much stress. You can tell that he cares a lot about his subject matter and his students.

I think Professor Packer is great! He is super sweet and caring and always checks in on us. He understands that this is a general and doesn't overload you with busy work. There is one midterm, a few papers, and one short presentation. No homework. He prepares you super well for each assignment so the assignments aren't really a big deal.

Professor Packer's lectures were interesting and assignments were straightforward! Something challenging about this course, however, was that students did not have grades for 60% of their coursework well into finals week. This made it difficult to write the final paper!

We students had trouble getting responses from him (though some reasons weren't his fault, due to life's chaos), and my TA never responded to emails, but the class is taught from a shared template, so this wasn't a big problem at all. In the end, our final was accidentally due one day early- but he had an amazing final exam review. Nice guy!

Bro Wells seems like a kind person, but not my favorite professor. I spent hours upon hours upon hours each week for the class. I took the term version and probably spent over 10 hours a week on this class. There is obscene amounts of reading and then there is a big project too. It was more work than calc, calc 2, or any other class I've taken @BYU

Professor Wells is very excited about what he teaches and clearly cares for his students. However, I found him to be mildly disorganized in the way he structured his class, and I felt like the content was easier than it should have been. Overall, he's not too bad! Definitely a very caring person.

He is the BEST!! his lectures were so insightful cause he is such a smart guy. He has an interesting story which makes it easy to respect him and trust him. He was a great mentor to me spiritually. This class is easy just like all the other 250s. the big project can literally be anything. I saw people who clearly didn't spend 10 hrs get full pts.

Univ isn't the most interesting class but it is very good for building a community at BYU, and Dr. Allphin was great at caring about our individual growth and success. She is awesome and made class interesting. She has a strong testimony and was very spiritually strengthening.

The class is hard. She is so passionate which I think can lead to a bit of an information overload, but everything is on her slides. There is a lot of info, you'll want to attend her lectures, but just put in the effort. As tough as it is, she doesn't want you to fail, and she'll support outside of class. She's an amazing professor.

Lecture slides are very word heavy, the TA's are unhelpful and there is so much information that you need to memorize for tests. You may think that the few assignments that she has sounds easy but they are incredibly difficult and take up a lot of time. She is an amazing person but I feel like she isn't really teaching.

This was the worst class I have taken at BYU! She just reads her slides word for word, and you can tell that she struggles answering questions that are "off-script". You pretty much just have to memorize her slides to do well on the tests. She does not promote learning, only memorization. I do not know how she has remained a professor!

The class is just lectures, 5 exams, and a small paper. Would not recommend the class unless it's your major or your passionate about ecology. She's super knowledgeable and always ready to help in office hours. Test's are very lecture dependent and require heavy memorization. She is truly passionate about ecology but it can be an info overload.

Dr. Allphin is an amazing person and so passionate about the subject. But there is way too much information in this course, don't let the 100 level fool you. This class takes a lot of your study time. The content is interesting but this class is memorization-heavy and assignments are graded harshly. Start memorizing from day 1!

I have spent multiple hours on her essays just to receive a 50%- 70% grade. Which is supposed to be two to three paragraphs, which ended up being around two pages. In class, she goes over slides that are FULL of information in a tiny font that you can bearly read. Then she picks small details from each slide to put into the exams. Try to avoid her!

This course is one of the most insane classes I have ever taken. For each exam, expect to have 50-70+ pages of single spaced notes that you have to memorize. Your exam answers are nitpicked to find any excuse to take as many points off as possible. Unless you have a photographic memory, this class will consume your life.

I admire Dr.Allphin as a female professor among a majority male staff, but her teaching style is just not it. Her ways of conducting class/tests are pointless. I have taken 3 classes from her now. Stay at home and just go over the slides yourself its the same as if you'd attend class. Too much emphasis on memorizing and not real understanding

One of the worst professors I've had, lectures are pointless and monotonous since she reads slides verbatim and tests are absurdly difficult for no reason. I stopped going to lectures after a week and was still able to get a B+ in the class by teaching myself which tells you pretty much all you need to know about the effectiveness of her teaching.

This class is way too hard for a general! The amount of content we have to study for tests is insane. I studied for days and felt like I never received a grade that reflected that. I have yet to see her give out full points for anything. Going to class seems pointless, as she just reads straight from the slides. Each slide has paragraphs of info.

She's a good person and you can tell she is super passionate about medicinal plants but I feel like the structure of this course was the downfall of the class. There were just too many cultures and plants to cover to the point where she had to read the slides word for word to get everything in. The lectures weren't necessary, she posted the slides.

As a person she's great. But honest to goodness, I hated this class. She reads off the the slides which makes coming to class worthless. Memorization is extremely heavy and she doesn't have very many grades which makes your grade on each assignment very important. Overall I was very frustrated with the class and felt like I wasted my time.

Over the last two decades I have only come across a couple of teachers who are worse at teaching. Great person, but she is a lecture machine. You have to purposefully stop her lecture if you want to get anything clarified. She doesn't seem to like questions and is not very good at responding to them and she doesn't teach you how to do the homework.

I really liked Dr. Allphin as a person, but it was impossible to get an A on any assignment even after revision and direct feedback. You have to memorize practically everything. There are about 6 assignments the entire semester aside from 2 tests and a massive group project. I've never seen so much expected from a GE class.

An amazing professor who really cares about her students. She teaches extremely well and makes the class possible. True her class is harder than most and she knows that herself. She posts slides but doesn't record lectures, and makes lots of remarks that arent on the slides, so go to class. She was the first professor I ever had that I felt cared.

The class felt very pointless, as she just read off the slides. If you stay home and read the slides you're getting the exact same experience. Also won't answer your questions. When I approached her for help on my group project she told me my questions weren't important and wouldn't help me with them. Very frustrating.

this girl does not know how to teach! just reads off the slides and 9/10 I fall asleep during lectures. I clutched the midterm and studied for like 5 hours the day of the test and got like a 70, just a lot of memorization. she's an amazing scientist and researcher, but not a great teacher

I did not like the way that Dr. Allphin taught her class. She reads directly from the slides and puts like three paragraphs on every slide. The tests are so long and so hard. She is really nice though!

The worst class I took this semester. So hard to get a good grade because there are so few graded assignments (midterm, group paper, final) and if you do poorly on one you're screwed. She reads off of PowerPoints for the whole class, every class, and the tests are complete memorization so beware of that. Not for me, especially not as an elective.

Professor Allpin is a good teacher, but this class is insanely hard for a GE. Tons of memorization. Her tests are really long and very specific. You never need to go to class, she posts all the powerpoints online. The group project is dreadful and graded really hard. I'd skip this class and take her Ecology class, it's much better.

Dr. Allphin is a great lady, but it felt pointless to go to class. She always posted her slides, but you still had to go to class unless she gave a pop quiz for attendance. Very few things she actually graded and lots of memorization. One big group project that was just not fun whatsoever.

A really fascinating class. She is fair and is willing to help if you go to her but she is a pretty picky and tough grader. Fill out her study guide, it's basically the same as the test. The test writing section is grueling though and is A LOT of memorization. It really isn't too bad just don't underestimate it even though its a GE class.

I loved the lectures (for Medicinal Plants) and Prof made it super interesting and definitely knew intimately what she was talking about (wasn't just a prof standing there talking about stuff, she had experience and background in research). Absolutely loved it. Exams were super hard (A LOT, COMPLETE MEMORIZATION) but totally worth it and doable.

She is an amazing person with a great passion for her work. She is very intelligent and helpful outside of class. Her class was difficult and her exams are incredibly intense. You really have to know all the details. I would not recommend if you are looking for an easy A; but if you genuinely want to enhance your knowledge, she is the best

She's a good person with a lot of knowledge, but this class is way too hard for an entry level class. The grade is basically based on one midterm, one final, an one group paper. She doesn't know how to use technology very well, and she takes a LONG time to get your grades back to you. Mostly pointless memorization. Don't take this class.

This class was interesting, but it was way to difficult for a 100 level GE class. I got a better grade in O-chem. She makes you memorize a lot of pointless information about plants and regurgitate it back to her. Learn this stuff is important, but there wasn't a whole lot of teaching or learning going on here.

This class was amazing and I'm so glad I took it! But it is NOT easy!!! There was so much information to retain and papers/projects/exams were graded pretty harshly. You definitely have to work for your grade. Start memorizing plants early on because you need to know them well. Overall a really cool class and a great professor. Would take again!

She's super passionate, but lectures do not prepare you for a very intense and in depth test. Test's in my opinion were too hard for a GE credit. You needed to know pharmacology, different cultures medical systems, and different plants from each culture. Pretty intense class, but I loved how much I learned from it.

This class covers a lot of material, but I've never learned so much from a teacher in my entire BYU career. Yes, the tests are long and hard, but I have walked away with so much applicable knowledge. You have to work to get a good grade in this class, but it is worth it. Plus, if you need help she is ALWAYS available. I loved this class.

It's the same thing in every class: 3 Exams HEAVILY weighted to your grade, class is 3x a week, with long powerpoints that you have to memorize to get a good grade. TOO MUCH info that you have to know EVERYTHING about. Two of her exams took me a whole 3 hours to finish and even after that long I cried. Don't buy the book. And seriously, reconsider.
Ridiculously hard for a GE. Way too much information to retain for the midterm/final. Do not take
This class is interesting and fun but was way too hard to be a GE credit. Tests were very difficult and grading seemed unfair. I would suggest taking a different class to fulfill this GE credit.

DON'T TAKE- there are better options for general credits. taught like a high school class- just reads from slides. Grades solely based on midterm, final, and giant group project. unclear grading criteria

DR. ALLPHIN IS AMAZING! I learned SO MUCH and she's been my favorite professor! She's so passionate about her subject that you can't help but love it too! She ties in the spiritual aspect so well! Also, she brings food samples to class :) Take notes in class and study. She provides a ton of resources and I WOULD RECOMMEND THIS CLASS TO EVERYONE!!!

She always said "I will grade this at a 100 level" but her tests were still challenging. Her passion for what she taught was amazing and she was such a kind and helpful professor (always offered to help outside of class) but you have to put in the work. Group research paper and project worth lots of points, and difficult tests. Fun class though.

Dr. Allphin is so passionate about what she teaches! I learned a lot. She gives A LOT of information each lecture, so take good notes and look at her slides later. Everything she talks about are on the slides. Her study guides are very thorough, so look at those if you want an A. Don't procrastinate studying for her midterms, there's a lot of info.

Professor Allphin is really enthuasiastic and teaches the class well. The grade is based entirely off of two tests, a presentation, and a paper, so its not a lot to work with. She does offer some extra credit. The best way to get a good grade is to pay attention in class.

Dr. Allphin is great!  She cares a lot about her subject and is super willing to help you outside of class if you need it - she wants you to succeed! My favorite part of the class was her last lecture where she connects plants and conservation with the gospel.  So cool.

Dr. Allphin is awesome. She is passionate about plants and wildlife, and loves to teach. The TAs are really helpful too. The hardest thing about the class was the group project. MAKE SURE YOUR GROUP WILL ACTUALLY WORK TOGETHER! If they don't, you will get a bad grade and will hate your group. Otherwise, it's awesome to learn all this stuff!

Unique and interesting class. Tests are tough but she gives you study guides that totally prepare you. If you study them you will do well. The group project paper and presentation are worth  a ton of the grade but she is super helpful and will revise your paper if you ask. Overall an easy class with little homework and a nice professor.

Dr. Allphin is very willing to help her students with their homework. She lets you come into her office to work on the problems and even double check your work before submitting it. She gives lots of extra credit. If few students are present, she sometimes gives everyone bonus points for showing up. The tests are fairly difficult, but I got an A.

I took Cultural History of Medicinal Plants. It was a GE for me and I wasn't too interested in it. She is a nice professor, she knows her stuff and she is very passionate about it. She has pop participation quizzes so go to class! Also 40% of your grade is a group paper and presentation so pick good people to work with and don't procrastinate!

She really makes you know your stuff!  Exams are long and in depth.  She gives you a study guide and if you really know what's on there, you'll be fine.  She likes to talk about herself and her research, and it's usually on the exams.  She's always willing to help with homework, past exams, etc.  She's great to work with

As far as the class goes, it's very clear what you need to know for tests. Her lectures are a little mundane, but you will always be able to tell what will be on the tests because she gets really excited and she emphasizes it. I would totally take it again, she is a great person!

Dr. Allphin is an adorably sweet person, but she's not the best teacher. She flies through slides each lecture and fortunately she posts them online or you wouldn't get down half the information she goes through each class period. I liked her class, but it was a lot harder than I thought it would be. Don't think you can just slide by.

She usually reads directly from her PowerPoint slides. However, sometimes she will expand on subject matter or give personal stories related to the material. If you learn better by listening rather than reading, I recommend attending often. There are occasional field tripscampus walks that I found useful. Tests are all factual memorization.

Honestly, Dr. Allphin is a nice person, but a lot of her slides are taken right off of Wikipedia. She is irritating and reads directly off her slides. I found skipping class and simply reading the slides online to be more helpful than actually going to her lectures. She is a nice person, but a really terrible teacher.

Very nice person but she was not at all clear with any questions asked. If you did not understand her explanation the first time, you were screwed.Interesting class that turned into a lot of rambling. She also had a lot of family problems that crept into scheduling. Her reviews for tests are the worst I've seen but at least she has them.

Dr. A is awesome! If you go to class and review the material you will be fine. She expects you to be a college student, so I can see why people complain. She wants you to succeed and will help you if you are willing. Great class and great teacher!
Love the class and have learned a lot.  Think the lectures are really good.  The paper for the class and presentation are done in groups too, how cool is that!

Class is demanding, but most points are based on class discussion & papers.  Professor is willing to read papers as many times as you want before the due date & help get it perfect, so get it done early and get an easy A.  Midterm and Final are not easy, but as long as you study the slides and go to lecture you should do well. Book supplemental.
Same class as BIO 350.  If you come and listen then do the study guide the tests aren't that bad.  Professor is very willing to help students out.
Her lectures are fun to listen to but very hard to comprehend. I didn't enjoy the class because the tests were very hard and the TA was completely USELESS! The book is only needed for online quizes.

She was preoccupied with other responsibilities so she couldn't focus on the needs of my class. She also completely missed one class without alerting anyone. She doesn't respond to emails and refused to give a decisive response on the date of our final. One term paper and about 4 mindless quizzes. She's really unclear about what to study for tests.

Class isn't too hard, but not easy either. Professor is boring and sometimes clueless. Almost daily online quizzes (easy), 4 short journal reviews, 1 short paper, 2 midterms and a final. Textbook is useless, but required for online quizzes. Attendance not mandatory, but helpful.
Her class was difficult but she was more than willing to help during her office hours. The tests were multiple choice and essay which I appreciated.

This class was hard...there are online quizzes for each chapter, but you can use the book so you basically don't have to prepare at all for them. There are no assignments basically so you have no way of knowing what the tests will be like. They are loooooong and essay and hard. I took ecology and it was tough. Barely pulled off a C.

she said that coming to lecture was helping us; I thought the tests were so hard that maybe I should be skipping class to study for it instead of coming.  This class takes self-discipline because there aren't worksheets or mandatory problems to keep you on track.  I think she's respectable, but the class is time consuming at test time.
Loved this class! She really knows her stuff and challenges students.  I took Ecology with her as well, and it was a bit harder, but I loved her teaching style.

I love biology, and her ecology class pretty much sucked the joy out of learning from my soul. She talked about herself far too often - I think she likes the sound of her own voice a little too much. She tried to get us to do useful things on the test but didn't prepare us in class to be able to be successful. Sorry - didn't like her.

So I generally suck at microbiology, but she's good at explaining things and she and her TA are available 24/7 to answer questions. The tests are 100% from the slides. So go to class. Tests aren't easy, but she gives you a massive study guide and if you do it, you won't have problems. She's also a country singer---which is cool.

Dr. Woolstenhulme made ecology fascinating and easy!  The tests are quite difficult and have essay parts, buy overall you'll do much less work than in other ecology sections.  She's especially good at explaining the mathematical models.  I recommend her 100%!

Probably my favorite class I've taken at BYU. Brother Marks loves the students and wants everyone to succeed. You have to be on time to class every day to be there for the daily quiz (generally easy), and must be prepared with a page of single spaced thoughts about the reading. Be ready to talk EVERY class period about your thoughts and opinions.

I cannot recommend Dr. Marks enough! I've seriously never had a professor that genuinely cares more about his students than he does. All this class requires for homework is a printed out page of comments from the readings assigned for each class and then the final exam (which he gives all the answers to in class)Come on time and you won't regret it

This man genuinely deserves a ticket straight to the Celestial Kingdom. He is kind, passionate about what he teaches, knowledgeable, and really loves his students. There's no electronics in this class but you won't want to use them anyway because it's so engaging. Worth waking up at 8 am to be there.

He's amazing! His goal is for understanding not grades. The only assignments you have are daily "GEMS" (2 paragraphs on your ideas of what you read for each reading), daily quizzes (answers are from previous lectures (don't stress about them), and ONE FINAL TEST (gives you the answers to the test every day of class! He genuinely loves us!

DR. MARKS IS AMAZING!!! BEST CLASS OF ALL TIME!! stress free, gospel focused and uplifting class. Dr. Marks is so so so kind and cares about the success of his students! Go to class and do the papers (always one page only) and you will LOVE it. He GIVES you the exam questions every day so you know exactly what will be on the ONE test in the class.

I have never had a professor who genuinely cared for and believed in his students so much as Dr.Marks. His class is my favorite I have taken at BYU. There is a lot of reading and writing involved and he needs paper copies so have access to a printer. He offers lots of extra credit, so if you miss class, you can get those points back pretty easily.

Super nice professor and a really great guy. Class was very easy, and you get all the answers you need for the final and daily quizzes

The reason I wouldn't take him again is just because I'm not a huge fan of his teaching style. Super "devotional" heavy and it feels more like a religion class rather than actually studying theories.

This class taught me so many valuable things that I think about everyday. Dr. Marks is incredibly caring and has perfected a format that allows you to truly learn and feel the spirit. There are two readings each week that you have to write one page about but they get easier as the semester goes on. Only one test.TAKE THIS CLASS, life changing.

Amazing. Heavier course work load because he asks you to write a page single space of personal applications/thoughts from the reading assignments. We learn in class by listening to his and our classmates' personal experiences. He literally walks you through the final. He loves his students and sincerely cares about LEARNING, not memorization.

The nicest professor you will ever meet. He starts a quiz every day RIGHT on time so don't be even a half minute late. He wants everyone to participate at least once a class. No phones/laptops in class. Super inspiring and caring.

The sweetest man to live! Professor Marks cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He really takes the pressure off the grade and helps you focus on the learning. Most everything is graded on your honor and he gives you answers to the final exam throughout the whole semester.

Dr. Marks was hands down my favorite professor and one of the kindest faculty I knew at BYU! If you have a chance to take his class, sign up! You won't regret it. Class is engaging, readings were interesting, and it was a class that really invited you to think rather than regurgitate memorized facts. 5 stars!
The love and true kindness I felt from Brother Marks was remarkable. He is a true gem and very close to our Savior.

Dr. Marks is one of the most genuine, kind, understanding professors I have ever met. Attendance is really important for the class, but you want to be in class because you learn so many important lessons from him, from the readings, and mostly from the class discussions. This class truly changed my life and I am forever grateful for Dr. Marks!

Dr. Marks creates a spiritual environment where we feel safe to share our story and get to know each other, learn from each other and edify each other. 1-on-1 chats encouraged. Daily reads with 1-page ungraded write-ups take time but keep us on track. Daily quizzes (be prompt) are straightforward and prepare us for exams. Clear grading. THE BEST!!

I had another professor tell me that Brother Marks is the nicest person on the planet, and it's so true! He truly cares about his students and teaches in a manner that shows that. His class does have readings every class period but they are worth the effort put in. It was amazing that I could learn so much from my classmates and from their stories.

This was the keystone experience of my bachelor in Family Life. You must take this class from Marks! Every class I felt so inspired. BEWARE: DO NOT SHOW UP EVEN 10 SECONDS LATE AND DO NOT SKIP WRITE UPS. The quizzes (easy) are worth 28% of grade and the single page reading write ups are 56% of grade. Thats every class. The readings are AWESOME.

I love everything about this class. Brother Marks helps everyone in the class to bring the Spirit. His classes are guided mostly by the students. Its not a hard class and I (as well as my other class members) have gotten so much out of it spiritually. I also know many members of my class which is nice :)

Brother Marks is the best professor I have had at BYU! I took his SFL 336 and SFL 460 classes. The classes change your perspective and outlook on life.  I have become a more loving, understandable disciple of Christ. I am grateful for all of the truths I have learned from his classes.  It has all changed me for the better.  Its worth it!

Brother Marks is literally the best professor at BYU. I've never met anyone more kind, caring, and genuine in my life. His classes completely changed my life. They aren't difficult either. Do the reading and don't miss class and you can easily get an A, but the lessons you'll learn from his class will matter much more than whatever grade you get!

He teaches class a very organized way and helps us apply the class learning to real life. We had a decent amount of reading and reports, but it was totally applicable and fun to do. He is also caring for each of his students' well-being. I wish the class would not end.

Dr. Marks is one of the best professors I've ever had. His class isn't easy, per se -- you are expected to do the work and be there  -- but he is incredibly kind and straightforward. On the first day, you'll know everything you need to do to pass. He is uplifting and edifying. I learned so much from him and all the students in my class.

Dr. Marks is fantastic. I took SFL 460 from him, and that was after dropping it from the other two teachers. Dr. Marks was wonderful, and he cares so sincerely about all of his students. If you go to class (yah, daily journal, but it took me like 30min each night. Not hard at all), and take notes when he says to, it's a breeze. TAKE 460 FROM HIM!

One  of the most caring professors I have ever had. Class structure is a 1pg single space response paper due every class period based on reading, and quizzes the first minute of class. No tests, no makeups. Gives you all the final exam questions. His methods are surprisingly effective; I learned so much in this class. About 2 hrs of reading/class.
