Dr. Marks is one of the best teachers I have had. His grading scale is very high. You have to work really hard to get an A. But he is very kind and helpful, and his grading scale made me invest more in the class and therefore I got more out of his class than others. If you stay on top of the homework and come to class every day, you do just fine.

BEST TEACHER I'VE EVER HAD!!! Brother Marks one of the kindest, humblest, and sweetest men that I know! He represents the Savior. This class was clear and straightforward. It was consistent. You know exactly what to expect. I reccomend this class even if it's not a requirement. Attendance and punctuality are extremely important. TAKE SFL 460!

I loved taking a class with Professor Newbold. She is so kind and caring and her class is low stress. Your grade is almost completely reflection based. It will take some time but you will get out what you put into this class.

She is like a modern Christian church no-label denomination youth pastor who's "cool" and "in with the kids". I'm not sure how to describe it, but if you're the kind of person that thinks its funny to hide silicone Jesus figures everywhere you'll love her class. Sometimes it feels like everything is supposed to be silly until she just starts crying

Too many personal experiences shared to support her lack of content. If you're someone who wants to feel feelings over the spirit, this is a class for you. Her assignments are mostly busy work, and usually were given randomly. End of the semester project was overly complicated and felt mushed together. Do not take....

I honestly have no idea why she is rated so low on here. I had a wonderful experience taking this class in the spring term with her. I really learned a lot about the Savior from the Book of Mormon. Sister Newbold has a wonderful testimony of the Gospel, and loves sharing that with her students. What you put into the class is what you get out of it.

This class was awesome! We learned so much about the Book of Mormon! It is the type of class where there are not many assignments and 0 tests - the main thing you need to do is read the book and be willing to come to class and participate. Focus is to grow spiritually and learn more about the Book of Mormon and our Savior Jesus Christ.

I hesitate to say this, but I feel it's important to share my experience. I found her teaching style difficult to engage with. The lectures often felt unstructured and more like off-the-cuff thoughts rather than well-prepared lessons. At times, the delivery came across as overly authoritative, which made it harder to connect with the material.
Only reason why I got an A- is because I misread the prompt for the final. She is a good lecturer and a fair grader, but the class organization leaves something to be desired.
Unorganized and unprepared. I wonder if there is a refund option at BYU. Sunday school format and a lot of fake tears.

She is incredible!! If you want to strengthen your testimony of Jesus Christ, Sister Newbold is your girl. The class is based on your feelings and you don't have to fake it if you don't feel strongly about something. Just know Sister Newbold is really here to help, listen, and especially teach about Jesus. She loves Jesus!

Her grading system felt inconsistent. I was marked absent by mistake, and the attendance quiz score was never corrected. She could be rude at times, and the lectures didn't feel genuine. She cried almost every class period, which made the environment uncomfortable. Letters of accommodation seemed like an inconvenience rather than a priority.

Honestly, the best part of the semester ending is just being done with this class. It's easily been the most cringey and frustrating class I've taken at BYU. Every day felt awkward. The whole vibe was uncomfortable, and it felt less like an actual college class and more like a forced discussion space. Overall, pretty disappointing experience.

Lots of reading. Homework is reading, projects are reading, final is reading. Lectures are interactive, you will not be sitting and listening. You do not have to memorize names or dates. More opinion based on how you feel about the readings

I really enjoyed this class. The workload was weekly reading and an assignment you fill out to go with it. Each assignment builds toward the final project, making it easier if you stay consistent. The professor is kind, insightful, and energetic. I would recommend this class.

She is a very nice person but not my favorite professor. Lectures felt simplistic and I didn't come away with many new insights. Homework is more than most other religion classes, but there are no tests which is nice. You can tell she cares though

At times, her teaching style made me feel uncomfortable in class. Although she is kind, I found it challenging to form deep connections or gain the insights I had hoped for from this course. This was not the religious learning experience I expected at BYU, and I would consider looking for another teacher.

If you want to pay for a long-winded Fast and Testimony meeting, this is for you. It's amazing one person can cry every single class. Class consists of her telling the class she and Christ loves us. When she's not talking about surface level themes, it's testimony. I'd rather pay for a class and learn rather than sit and watch someone cry

I wouldn't recommend her class unless you're okay with it feeling like a paid Sunday school class. Her instructions and expectations are often unclear and inconsistent. Materials aren't posted when they're needed, and she doesn't take responsibility or acknowledge these organizational issues.
She gave a lot in spirit and hw but none of it was too much

The instructor is approachable and relaxed, but the class itself felt loosely organized. Discussions often stayed on the surface, and I didn't come away with many new insights into the Book of Mormon. Because of that, the mandatory attendance policy felt unnecessary. I was hoping for a more structured and engaging experience.

Prof. Newbold clearly cares a lot about the BoM and connecting to students spiritually, so class time is usually very nice and spiritual. But academically, the class is a mess. Instructions are poorly explained/unclear. She claims not to assign busywork, but you'll find yourself repeating tedious assignments every week. Overall, I don't recommend.

Prof Newbold is very caring and is great at connecting with her students. I loved having her class and looked forward to it. There are no tests but there is a decent amount of hw. I spent about 2.5 hours a week doing it. Would for sure take something from her again.

This teacher knows the Book of Mormon along with other scriptures inside and out. He truly cares about each student and plans many different options for the lecture depending on where the discussion takes us.

The course felt overly basic, and I did not gain much from the class sessions themselves. Discussions lacked depth and relied too much on student comments, which made the course feel opinion-based. The course was disorganized, and the assignments on Learning Suites were frequently missing or posted late. Overall, my experience was below average.

Sister Newbold's testimony and Christ-like example are amazing! Class time was more like a discussion than a lecture, which I enjoyed but it also sometimes felt disorganized. No exams but lots of homework: two weekly journals and an extended final project with weekly time logs. Some unclear expectations but worth it for the phenomenal teacher.

If you are looking for a class that is intended to be uplifting but may also feel confusing due to limited instructions and inconsistent organization, this may be the course for you. The professor is kind but can be confusing when giving instructions and may not be as clear or organized as many other college courses.

The final was worth too much of the overall grade, and the requirements were not clearly explained. The class was not very uplifting and often felt repetitive. The instructor was difficult to work with and did not come across as very compassionate, which made the course harder to engage with.

Lori Newbold is the most Christ-like person I have ever met. Sister Newbold's class was one I looked forward to every week. You can get so much out of this class just by showing up. There were only two weekly assignments, and no tests, and it was seriously my favorite class!

Prof Newbold's lectures were inspiring and spiritual. There's no tests, but you get 2 weekly assignments which can sometimes be a lot but manageable. Plus, they'll help you a ton with the final, where you use all completed work for a bigger project. Overall not too hard, though keep track of the syllabus, sometimes she waits to post assignments.

Great class. Professor Newbold really cares about her students and puts in an effort to know each one individually. Assignments and projects are kind of a lot of work, but not hard. There is definitely a good amount of reading as well. Some people say that her instructions are unclear, but I understood for the most part. And there are no tests!

Final, project was the most long annoying thing. Very unnecessary but at least there won't any tests. She started off by having 2 assignments a week that become very repetitive but by the end we had a lot of randomly added assignments. I love her so much very funny and caring but her class wasn't my favorite.

Two journal assignments a week plus a reflection later on for the final project. If you pay attention to instructions for the final project you'll do fine. I'd much rather have more assignments than an actual midterm and final.

So... the final is pretty much the only thing you have to work on, just do the attendance and everything else will fall into place. Also don't expect any help from the professor, and there is a lot of work but it's just not worth it because they're not that many points.

Final's rubric? Seems like it's messed up since all the options have the exact same requirements.
Homework? Twice a week, until she slapped on a third assignment, also then a fourth sometimes. Also two over break. Also a fifth sometimes. Also they're all copy pasted. Also claims "never gives you work that doesn't have meaning"

Final project was worth 50% of grade. She absolutely refused to work with me in regards to a misunderstanding about unclear assignment requirements. Very tough grader and attendance is mandatory. Three or more assignments a week that were incredibly lengthy and took several hours.

The professor doesn't know how to organize things. She didn't even have the final project on learning suite until the week before we turned it in, which we worked on for the whole year, so I was confused. The assignments are weekly journals, and they get very repetitive. She's very nice and caring, she just doesn't know how to organize the class.

She was great at the beginning, but not organized at all. She does not make clear the instructions on the final project and was all over the place when I tried to email her. I would not recommend her class-- because of her lack of communication about the final project my grade tanked.
She was so chill and works with you. she is very kind as well. definitely recommend

Lori is a great teacher. I had her for REL 121 book of mormon. Each week you have 2 assignments to turn in by the end of the week and are graded on attendance for each class. Homework probably took me an hour or an hour and a half per week. Final project at the end of the semester took a couple hours. She is very kind and loves her students.

Her assignments were so repetitive. The final was time consuming, tedious, and incredibly confusing. I didn't learn much about the book of mormon which was dissapointing. It is somewhat easy but the assignments are painfully boring and time consuming. She is a great person but not a professor I'd recommend.

She is very passionate and truly cares about the Book of Mormon and her students. The assignments can feel repetitive, with weekly journals and similar class discussions throughout the semester. The class is very easy, and it's not hard to keep a 100%. The final project is a bit of work but you're given plenty of time, and there are no exams.
It felt like she was making things up as the semester progressed. Not really well organized, neither really informative. It was repetitive and frankly not engaging. I wouldn't take her classes again.

All Sister Newbold cares about is that through the Book of Mormon you are growing closer to Christ and it's awesome! Only homework is weekly journals and occasionally sharing what you've learned to someone else. My testimony of Jesus Christ and the Book of Mormon grew so much because of this class!

Sister Newbold is so loving and caring about all of her students. Her lessons are the definition of guided by the spirit. She is able to teach difficult topics so well and lovingly and likes to find Christ in everything. My only gripe would be the long and very repetitive assignments but don't let that stop you from her amazing testimony

This is a class structured in the most effective way to grow your testimony and understanding of the Book of Mormon. Sister Newbold is extremely knowledgable and loving. Her assignments are formatted in a way that you get out what you put in. Her class is not difficult, but it certainly gives you the opportunity to grow.

Being a nice person doesn't necessarily make someone a great teacher. Many of her assignments felt like busywork and didn't really relate to the class content. Her lectures seemed somewhat superficial, almost like a seminary class. There was also too much homework for a religion class. So, overall, I'd recommend looking elsewhere.

Professor Newbold is so kind and thoughtful. She has such a way with teaching the Book of Mormon that is downright inspirational. I am extremly greatful I took her class. The weekly assignments may feel like boring or repateive to some but with the right mindset, it can really help you evaluate yourself on your spiritual journey here
She was awesome. She is not a tough grader at all and she cares not only about you but also about the content of the class. I would 100% recommend her.

Copy pasted homework assignments with 7+ steps per assignment twice a week plus up to two more assignments on weekends on holidays with the single most vague final project I've ever done.
Reliably goes over class time which makes it difficult to complete the online participation assignment after class which closes ten minutes after the class ends.

She genuinely loves everyone and wants us all to grow our testimonies. Her lectures are very powerful and she molds her lessons to what she feels prompted to teach. No tests or quizzes. Simple assignments through out that help grow your testimony and understanding of the Book of Mormon.

Sister Newbold is the best! There are no tests whatsoever, the thing that matters most to her in this class is strengthening your relationship with the Savior. Definitely take her class! There are weekly assignments based on readings for the week, but they are beneficial to your testimony and she is such a kind and understanding person.

Sister Newbold is an amazing person and does care about the students and wants us to grow our testimonies and grow as people. However, the class was very unorganized and hard to follow. The weekly study Journals were very repetitive and boring at times and the final project was unclear and hard to understand what exactly she wanted us to do.

She is suchhh a kind teacher and her lectures are just exactly what I needed. I struggle with anxiety and depression and her mental health background really seemed to help her to teach with the kind of love that I need. Good amount of homework, not hard.

I absolutely loved Lori as a teacher! The homework load was super easy and NO TESTS! She cared about every student and made such an effort in class, I loved learning from her and would recommend her to everyone

Sister Newbold is one of the most Christ like people I've ever met and brings the Spirit to class so well. She wants you to learn about the Savior and Book of Mormon instead of just memorizing stuff, so there's no essays, exams, or quizzes. It's just two weekly assignments/journals about what we learned from weekly reading. She makes it fun!

Sister Newbold is an amazing person and teacher. I took her Book of Mormon class, and she had no tests, quizzes, or lectures. Instead, every class she leads a discussion about our reading that week. The assignments are tailored to increase your relationship with Jesus Christ by connecting the Book of Mormon to your life. She is caring and funny.

Sister Newbold is SO refreshing to have as a professor. She takes the Book of Mormon class and gives it a whole new meaning. She redefines the purpose of taking a Book of Mormon class and shifts it away from pure memorization and essay writing, to focusing on your personal relationship with Christ. No tests, no quizzes. 2 weekly assignments.

Loves karaoke, what more can you ask for. She helps with all the reading. A good example of high expectations and high love. It's a lot of reading but she said you're not expected to understand everything the first reading. That's what she's there for. The lectures are life savers when it comes to the readings so be sure to pay attention

Dr. Williams is strict. TA's have too much grading power and too few criteria. You'll read non-stop. The quizzes were unrealistically hard, with all 5 answer options seeming correct. Essays are based on the grader's opinion. Some kids loved the challenge, but I did not. Liberal-leaning course.
The class was extremely difficult, but doable with enough studying.
Great class. You will need to know the material well, but understanding general ideas and forming arguments is more important than memorizing minute details.

Dr. Williams is the best professor BYU has. She cares about students, she genuinely wants them to learn and succeed. She will do whatever she can to help you understand concepts. She gives hope and optimism to the world. You read hard texts in this class, but she encourages you through it. Taken any and every class you can from her.

Now that I've taken POLI 202 from a different professor, I realize how great Dr. Williams is. The material is confusing, and there is a LOT of it. But she breaks it down so that it is easy to understand, and even interesting. The papers are the hardest component of the class, but exams were doable if you know your stuff. Practice questions are key

Dr. Williams is a great teacher, but this is a hard class. Theres lots of readings and every few weeks there will be a random pop quiz that counts for attendance. The lectures are so so, not too boring. The real problem is the TAs, they grade way too harshly. See them each time you write a paper and attend all reviews and youll be fine

I took Poli 201 because it fulfilled both a major requirement and a GE for me. Despite being able to kill two birds with one stone, I really regret taking this class. Professor Williams provides good feedback, but her tests are vague and the TAs are given too much control over grading. The class was a pain to both attend and study for.

This class was taken as a general for me. There is a lot of reading! Her tests are odd. She gives you a quote and you are expected to know where it came from, who said it, and who wrote it. The TAs are primarily responsible for grading your tests and essays. If you are looking for general credit, take a different class IMO.
Save yourself your stress and do not take any class from her unless it is last resort

This class is hard for absolutely no reason. The grading is based on opinion. Your TA has an opinion on the topic, and if you do not write about it, you are screwed. There is no clear correct way that they want you to answer questions. It is opinion based and they grade extremely hard even though they claim they will not.

Dr. Williams is an engaging teacher and the lectures were always interesting. That said there was a ton of reading, and the grading was the harshest I have seen so far. If you feel that everyone should be able to get an A in a class from putting in enough work, probably not the teacher you are looking for. If you want a challenge, she gives it.

Great professor! She doesn't allow laptops or phones in class, which I didn't love, but aside from that, this was one of my favorite classes. She knows her material, involves students in class discussions, and is incredibly helpful in office hours (so are the TAs). Grade consists of two 5-page papers, 10 participation quizzes, midterm, and final.

Dr. Williams had really interesting and dynamic lectures, but if you don't do the assigned readings you will be super bored. Also, though she does not record attendance, she does have random pop quizzes to score your participation. The class had five grades: the quizzes, 2 papers, the midterm, and the final. Was super helpful at her office hours.

I have never been interested in Poli Sci and took 201 for a GE requirement, but it became one of my favorite classes. Prof. Williams requires a lot of reading, but she knows her stuff extremely well, asks good questions, and the lectures are very intriguing if you participate. Only graded assignments are quizzes, 2 papers, and a midterm and final.
I loved this class. It was definitely one of the most challenging classes I've taken but the lectures were great and Professor Drake clearly cares about everyone doing well!

Best professor I have had at BYU. He cares deeply about the topic and about helping you understand it. His class felt very focused on helping you have an academic experience with early Christian literature rather than just assigning busy work. Everything he does as a professor is crafted to help you succeed as a student.

I honestly really enjoyed this class. The reading is heavy and necessary to participate in in-class discussions. Study guides are provided for exams, but you must know the content well to get a good grade. Even with the heavy load, I loved this class and Professor Drake; the lectures were interesting and engaging. Highly recommend
He is very organized, passionate, and helpful. Tests are difficult and there are many short essays to write but it's not to bad.

Professor Drake is so amazing and so fun! The class will be difficult if you don't read or take notes, but if you show up to his lectures (which are amazing) and actually read what is given, you'll have no problem. This was my favorite GE at BYU and I think everybody should take this class from Prof. Drake for their Letters requirement.

Professor Drake was incredible! I loved how enticing his lectures were. There was a lot of reading, but I found it all really interesting. Attendance isn't really necessary, but you are required to answer a question he asks on any given day. If you do the reading and show up, you will be just fine.

Professor Drake is very fast paced which can make it hard to keep up with lectures. I hardly did any of the readings during the semester but read them all and memorized the material the day before the finals. The exams are very memorization based so cram before and you'll do fine. Final was 50% and midterm was 25% of the overall grade.

Professor Drake is AMAZING!! I don't even like reading literature but this class was so interesting and Drake made every lecture fun! He also lets you know exactly what is expected on each exam!! I would definitely take another class from him!!!

Prof Drake is the most accommodating professor I've ever had and very accessible outside of class. He bends over backwards to help his students succeed. That being said, the paper, project, and exams require hard work. The lectures are really interesting because he's very passionate. Overall a great guy who remembers what its like to be a student.

If you love diving into the study of ancient literature, ancient ideas, and fascinating history, this class is going to be a dream come true! Professor Drake is genuinely one of the best professors I had all year and has set the bar way too high! Your worldview is going to be expanded beyond what you ever thought possible.

Dr. Drake is an excellent professor and I'd gladly take another class from him. His lectures are very passionate and he obviously cares about and knows a lot about the subject material. He treats you like an adult, which is great, and is very open to meeting outside of class. Tests are not terribly hard as long as you actually study.

His lectures are pretty fast-paced, and while he doesn't take attendance, you'll want to be there. There is a bit of reading outside of class, and an average of one, two-paged paper a week. He does provide opportunities to extra credit though and accepts late work. He's super engaging and very passionate about what he teaches.

Incredibly kind professor who wants the best for his students. Class is what you make of it. Prof. Howard is very knowledgeable and funny. Grades are almost entirely based on attendance, so if you plan to miss more than 1 class you won't get an A.

Not a particularly interesting class; it's supposed to be analyzing music since 1720, but was actually only about exploring racism, cultural appropriation, and misogyny through a musical lens. It's much more of a sociology class than it is a music class. That being said, it is the easiest class you'll ever take, and he usually ends class early.

Professor Howard is truly the best professor I've had here at BYU. He is so inspirational and so funny! His philosophy of GE's makes his class actually enjoyable and so neat to learn from him! His accent alone also makes the class so much fun. He has such a neat perspective on life and art and music, if you can snag a spot in his class, KEEP IT!
Just take his class, no needs to hesitate.

This was such a great class! I've had Dr. Howard for two different classes now and have LOVED IT! He is so willing to talk to you and help you understand the concepts he is teaching! I actually really appreciate that he requires you to come to class because he teaches about so many interesting concepts! All the assignments were easy! Easy tests!
Most woke teacher I've had but that doesn't super bug me, relaxed enough that its worth it for sure

An easy A class with a passionate professor. While the lectures are engaging, the class lacks depth and rigor. Focus on attendance and assignments rather than actual learning. Unstuckstudy AI can help with efficient prep for the easy quizzes.
W prof wooooooo

Sure, it's a GE. Two in fact. I take classes to learn and I found myself disappointed in this class. I don't feel as if it deeply instructed me in arts or civilization. Dr. Howard's enthusiasm was great, but it was always way over my head and he seemed to suppress it to focus on minority music. It left me empty, wanting more.

I think this class was genuinely one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. All of the assignments were based on completion. If you did it, you got credit. Professor Howard is kind and respectful. The assignments were creative and fun. Attendance was 50% of the grade, but I felt it was extremely reasonable for how easy it was.

TAKE THIS CLASS. I took it for two of GEs and I plan on taking MUS 201 with him. He is such an easy grader and I've never had an easier class before. Not only that, but I really really enjoyed all the hw and assignments and I know nothing about classical music. I'm here to help you out, take this class for your GE.

If you're looking for an easy civ 2 class so you can graduate, take this class! Super easy A, just do the assignments and go to class (attendance 50% of grade). Small assignments, no tests, easy final project. Class content was a bunch of pointless political propaganda, and I didn't learn much, so overall didn't love the class. But hey, easy A.

Solid professor. His lectures cover everything that is on the tests. Homework assignments are really easy. Lectures were very interesting. Only reason I don't give him a 5 is he is adamant on not putting his slides online. You'll need to take pretty detailed notes on all of his lectures to do well on tests

The 202 coursework is completely new and different starting this semester. Still an amazing class with a bit of HW, but with more interesting topics like pop, classical music, and modern music. If you turn in your work and do it it's a very manageable A. He covers a lot of Asian and Hispanic cultures so IDK what the black racism review is about.

Your grade is primarily based on attendance (at least it was for the night section), so make sure you will be able to attend most lectures. Dr. Howard was accommodating when I had a difficult situation and you can tell he's very passionate about the subject material. He's also upfront when he was teaching a subject that's not his area of expertise.

This class was so different than Music 201 (which I also took from Howard). It was more about cultural appropriation. I took the 3 hr night section, and Dr. Howard always let us out early which was amazing. The assignments, midterm, and final were all easy (no tests, just short projects), and I walked away more informed about culture and music.

I loved Pro. Howard. I took this class to cover my civ two credit; it was the easiest class ever. If you participate, you get a good grade. There was a midterm in this class, but it was just a super easy paper. There are long readings, but that's it. No final, it is a good class.

Prof. Howard is a very easy A. My complaint is that four weeks in, 9/10 lecture hours have been ENTIRELY devoted to black-specific racism. No acknowledgments of other races. This has been really frustrating for me and not what I was expecting for a music culture class. If I wanted to learn more about black racism, I would've taken SOC 112.

EASIEST GE CREDIT! To be fair, I took this over spring semester, but Professor Howard wanted everyone to end with an A. We took the tests as a class so the only thing we were really graded on was one essay (which is basically completion). He wants his students to succeed. He's also really funny and makes history really entertaining.

Learned a lot in lectures and the class was very manageable. His in-class ID exam #2 was pretty challenging and could be tricky if you weren't prepared, so make sure you know his expectations for it well in advance. However, they may be changing the organization of the class soon so be sure to double check that before signing up for the class.

While the lectures are super entertaining and his passion for music and the arts is contagious, the class is too easy. He gave us the answers to tests. The seven quizzes weren't due until the end. They were open for infinite submissions and the right answer was highlighted after the first attempt. Little to no required effort = little learning.

Prof Howard is the funniest professor I've had at BYU! Such a kind, caring man and SO knowledgeable about everything art, literature, and music related. He explains things very clearly and welcomes questions. His passion is contagious - he even managed to make opera interesting. If you're taking Music 202, take it from him!!

Prof Howard is awesome. His lectures are fun and engaging and there was rarely a dull moment. His class is very test heavy though. 70% of your grade is all tests but he will prepare you well for them. Also, the final is the same questions from the previous midterms and he opens the midterms so you can study them before the final. Minimal homework.
This class was fantastic. Dr. Howard made it enjoyable and provided everything needed to succeed. I would recommend this class or any of his other classes to anyone.

Fairly easy class. Definitely still have to study and although attendance is not mandatory, I definitely recommend going. For some reason I didn't realize that there was literature and art also in the course, not just music. Anyway, I learned a lot and had fun doing it!

Dr. Howard is amazing! His lectures are so fun and he is really smart. The class isn't too hard, as long as you don't try to cram at the end, because you have to memorize a lot for the ID exams. If you're taking MUSIC 202, definitely take it from Dr. Howard.

Very easy class, yet enjoyable and engaging. Wants students to succeed. Mainly graded by the ID and online exams, but they are straightforward. One of the most popular professors at BYU, so get ready for large lectures and long waitlists for the class.

If you are needing to get your CIV 1 & 2 GE's out of the way take Music 201 and 202 from Prof. Howard! Seriously, his classes are SO straight forward, simple, and easy (IF you study well for the exams). As mentioned in other ratings, this class is test heavy, so expect that but don't sweat it too much. Could not recommend this class more!

Prof Howard was hilarious, his lectures are not necessary but I go because they are hilarious and interesting.  You are given everything you need to get a 100 on all the tests, easily the easiest class I have taken, but also one of the most interesting.  He is also very spiritual and sweet and genuinely one of the nicest people you will meet

This is an interesting class. Attendance isn't mandatory but definitely helpful in preparing for the tests. You have 3 tests throughout the semester (2 midterms and the final) that are open book & open note. The hardest part on the tests is listening to the music and having to identify who wrote it and the name of it.

I've taken MUSIC 201 and MUSIC 202 from Dr. Howard now and let me tell you- MUSIC 202 was WAAYYYY harder. I love Dr. Howard as a person but the tests are very long and difficult (even if they are open note!) and nothing you talk about in class can prepare you for them. The ID exams are very stressful but study and you'll do well.

I LOVED Dr. Howard! This class was so fun and I learned a ton, because the lectures were super interesting. Tests are pretty easy because they are open-book and open-note, so there's not a lot of memorization. Pretty much no homework necessary. Dr. Howard is one of the nicest, kindest professors on campus, so I'd definitely recommend him!

one easy writing assignment. the whole class is based off of the exams. Exams are open book, open note, and open internet. However, they are long and take a long time to find the answers.SUPER easy GE if you are looking for one. totally worth it, just make sure you save time for when the tests roll around to find the answers.

Dr. Howard's an entertaining lecturer and he knows his stuff.  The class is very interesting and informative and he always has a fresh take on old topics.  The tests are long and difficult, but they're open note and book, so it's doable.

Prof. Howard is one of my least favorite professors I've had at BYU because he is conceited and rude. He openly shares controversial opinions and tries so hard to be woke that he's a jerk. Thinks he's funny but he's just weird. The classes were boring and the tests were SO HARD (you DEFINITELY need the textbooks - 7th edition is the best one).

His lectures are amazing. The tests are open book with no time limit, so it takes a while to finish them, but they are pretty straight forward. He is hilarious and makes learning about ancient art and music fun. He is straightforward about what he expects and makes his class really manageable.

As a whole class, there isn't many assignments for Music 201 (or 202 for that matter because it's identical in structure with just different material). Dr. Howard is an amazing professor. There's a reason the waitlist for this course is so high. Come to class, take good notes, all quizzes and tests are open book/note, one real writing assignment.

If you don't enjoy history and need to fulfill your Civ credits, take this class. So much easier than the World Civ classes. Open book and note quizzes and tests (this could change though). Take notes during class to help on tests. One short paper, easy. I have the textbooks, never used them. I didn't give too much effort and I got an A-.

Lectures were great, really entertaining, Dr Howard knows how to read the crowd. My only (and biggest) complaint is the tests. Open note/ book, yes, but some answers come from some obscure line from the textbook that he didn't really touch on in class. Wouldn't be that big of a deal if tests didn't make up 70% of your grade. But as a person, 10/10

Professor Howard is actually the best. This class is E-A-S-Y. Every test is open book, notes, and course materials. Though a 94% is an A it is literally impossible (unless you don't try) to get less than that. His lectures are AMAZING (he has the BEST Australian accent), he's hilarious, and though this was a 3 hour class we always ended WAY early.
Class is easier with prior music knowledge.
Fun lectures. Always ends class early. Not a lot of homework. Review your class notes and the textbook before tests and you'll be fine. Low effort class but you still learn a lot.

You don't need to watch any lecture videos or read anything. All quizzes are online and tests can be done in groups. The easiest A of my life, especially at BYU. He is super funny and chill as well. Best GE ever!

Dr. Howard is a cool guy, and the class was very easy, but I felt like there wasn't a ton of effort put into the class. That is, all the lectures were recorded from a previous semester, and there was very little live interaction.

Seriously this is what all GEs should look like. He made it so interesting and not stressful, I could actually focus on learning instead of getting tons of reading done. It was an easy A since the tests were open book, which was super nice. Don't bother with the textbook though, it's so heavy and you will never use it.

Dr. Howard teaches this class very well. I have difficulty understanding art because of my Asperger's but I was still able to understand what I needed to get an A in the course. I am looking forward to taking Music 202 from him as well.

Highly recommend! The hardest part (pre-Covid) was the listening part of exams where he would play a clip of a song and you had to know composer/song title/genre. But if you attend lecture and TA exam review sessions, you'll be fine. Dr. Howard was pretty funny and very generous (open note, open person exams for the most part).

This was an easy GE. Because I wasn't stressed about the courseload, I could actually enjoy the material, which was a nice break. I took the class on-demand, so Prof. Howard let us work through the content largely at our own pace, going more in depth only if we wanted to. He is super down-to-earth, and he knows the material very well.

Prof. Howard explains materials concisely and is a quite quirky aussie. Most of the difficulty ratings were presumably done pre-online where tests were closed everything. Without notes, it would take some effort for an A, but Prof. Howard's teaching makes up for all of it.

This class was soooo great! Takes the stress away from your GE course load and allows you to actually try to enjoy the material without wanting to die the entire time. Dr. Howard is incredibly knowledgeable on what he teaches and he's pretty funny. Definitely recommend this class! There's a reason the waitlist is always 200 people long.

Everything was done in groups, all the exams, literally everything was open friend/TA/internet/book. The final is made up completely of questions from the midterms, so it was an easy 100%. Coolest teacher in the world, made learning fun, and made the topics extremely interesting. This is how learning should be.

One 500 word essay and open note reading quizzes due at the end of the semester. Open note and open group midterms. I only put in work the week of midterms/final. Easy way to fill the Civ 1 req but also pretty worthless class. Howard seems nice enough and passionate about the class but never interacted w/ him. Textbook can be found online for free

This class is super easy and a good choice for the Civ 1 GE. The only assignments are a few quizzes with unlimited retakes, open-book, open-other-people midterms, a reflection paper, and a final that is copied verbatim from the midterms. Howard is also an interesting and engaging teacher. Definitely take him.

This class is pretty easy. I took it online during COVID and all of his lectures were like 20 minutes, and super straight forward. He knows his stuff, even if it isn't that interesting. He keeps it light and fun and you don't need to kill yourself over this GE.
Loves what he teaches, few but easy assignments, and he's very approachable. I love Dr. Howard!!
I love this class. Super easy if you pay attention and have a brain. It feels more like a 2 credit class. Great lectures, long exams(but open book so...)

This was, quite frankly, one of my favourite classes at BYU. Professor Howard is a phenomenal teacher, and his lectures were some of the highlights of my week. The class isn't especially easy but is in no way inordinately difficult. Very little work outside of class. During my semester he would coach you if you emailed him for help during tests.

I took this class entirely online during COVID-19. It was super easy, and the tests were all open note, internet, friend, TA, etc. The final is literally copy and paste questions from the midterms, and there is only one paper which is pretty much completion credit. Would recommend for a super easy 3 credit class.

This class is really easy. Almost everyone got As. You have to put in work in filling out the open book/internet/ta tests, but its not very hard overall. Dr Howard is very inspiring and he will change your life, even if music history doesnt interest you.

Dr Howard is a genius. For a GE this class is insanely easy. If you dont get an A, you did something really wrong. The tests are open TA, professor, internet, and you can take them in groups. This class will change your life
Prof. Howard is awesome. A super respectable guy who is really easy to understand and get along with. Funny too. The class was pretty easy, but you'll learn if you apply yourself.

I took this class over the online spring semester, and unlike my other classes, it felt as though I was in the real class! Dr. Howard is an amazing teacher and I never felt as though I was missing anything that I would have been experiencing had class been held in person.

Since COVID-19 made this class online, EVERYTHING was open book, open friend, open internet even. I didn't really study and easily got almost 100% on the tests. And there was only one short writing assignment. Best class ever. Dr. Howard's lecture style is really engaging, too. I highly recommend this class (at least online)! Seriously, take it!
Easy GE for something that does not interest me at all. Open everything tests.

Easiest class ever. You don't have to go but should to pass. He lets you take the midterms with other people and you can email him to get the right answer if you can't figure it out. He gives you the in class test to study and then when you take it, the test is open everything. He was hilarious and really cared for the students
Professor Howard is passionate about music, and is overall a quirky, smart professor who cares about music. As long as you buy into the class, you get a lot out of it.

I've never enjoyed attending a lecture as much as I did with professor Howard. He's smart, tells great (and relevant) stories, has the best jokes, and is thought-provoking. Plus, he doesn't expect you to spend all your time on his class if it's a gen ed course. Seriously, take his class. You won't regret it.
I love Dr. Howard! First of all, he's Australian and I love listening to him talk, and he's also such a great person! He is very open, friendly, and caring, and knows his stuff!

This class was amazing! I felt that I was actually able to learn the material without the pressure of having to take the tests by myself. He gives you resources to do well on the exams. The lectures are so interesting and engaging. He is very funny and his accent makes the class even better. I'd highly recommend taking this class for your Civ GE!

Funniest prof I've ever had. Class isn't mandatory, but he's funny. Get the textbook - midterms are open note, book, everything. Throw a quizlet together for yourself of art examples (go beyond his slides!), listen to the music a bunch, and you'll be just fine on the exams. Final was open everything because of corona. Adapted really well for that!

I loved Professor Howard's class! He has a great sense of humor and is a solid storyteller. One written assignment (10% of grade), 9 online quizzes (20%) that can be retaken unlimited times, and 5 exams (3 in class, 2 online, 70%). Final is closed-book, rest are open. Very caring, engaged, and inspiring teacher.

Dr. Howard is great. Quite possibly the the coolest feminist who I have ever met. His lectures are funny, two in-class identification exams, two online multiple choice tests, one final in class, one easy written assignment: all tests are open book, note,.etc.. You need to put work in to get an A, but it's far from impossible.

Dr. Howard is HILARIOUS, and he makes the past come alive. I was surprised at how much he helped me to enjoy the material. His exams are difficult (even for me, who has heard most of the music before) but if you take notes and prepare, you'll do fine (open book/note/website/classmate, except for the final). No HW except one paper. Awesome class!

Loved Prof Howard, he is really funny and makes class really engaging. Hie tests weren't too bad which caused me to really genuinely love the artsy material that we were learning even though I'm studying something completely different. Made strong strides to ensure that I got him for 202 as well

Professor Howard is hilarious and relatable, but beware the tests. I was able to work really hard and do well in the end of the semester, but I don't think anyone was prepared for the first test and very few did well. The tests are identifying mystery and known examples of art and music. The first two are open book, but they are still quite hard.

Dr. Howard is Australian, so it makes class more enjoyable. He has a very firm no late work policy, so beware of taking this class too lightly. His ID and Multiple choice exams are open "anything you can carry into class except for the internet" but the final is closed book and closed note. This class really is exceptional.

I loved 201 from Professor Howard so much that I'm taking 202 from him next semester. He has great lectures. There aren't very many things in the grade book, just a few quizzes, two midterms, a paper, and the final. However, everything except the final is open note/book/partner so it was pretty easy! Go to lecture, take good notes, and you'll pass.

*everything except for the final is open book/note/friend* I took a 2.5 hour long class of his at night so it was a little hard to stay awake sometimes but he does have day classes. He is the funniest professor I've had, and he will listen to each and every comment people have. Use textbook for the midterm, because it's open-book. Favourite class.

I took this class for general credit and it was amazing! I've always loved music, but because of Dr. Howard, art came alive for me too. He tells the best stories about the people that you learn about in class and he helps on the online tests. There was a lot to do in this class, but if you keep up with the reading and go to reviews, you'll be fine.
He is a very enthusiastic professor which makes the class enjoyable, but you definitely need to be willing to put in effort to pass this general.

This is a pretty chill GE, especially since he change it for this semester so the midterms were open note. The first midterm was still pretty hard compared to the second one and the final. Lectures are pretty average, and other than a brief writing assignment and studying for the midterms you don't have to do any other work.

I loved going to lecture every other day. He is a super entertaining lecturer and he is super smart. The class itself however is very very difficult .First of all, the class is barely on music. Its more about art and literature. Also, you have to know all the specifics of the midterm and final. In the end however, he curves it hardcore.

Dr. Howard is my favorite professor Ive had at BYU! His lectures are fascinating and you can tell he is so passionate about what he teaches. Hes super funny and makes the class more focused on learning than on homework, which I loved and appreciated.

This guy is funny, but he is not the greatest teacher. Only take this class if you love learning about really artsy. I really did not like this class, and, considering that most of the students are only taking it as a GE, he makes it way too hard. Also, tests are open book online, so it is super easy for people to cheat.

Loved him and his approach to classical music. The lectures feel kind of useless when the test rolls around. He does a good job of preparing you for the final and was nice enough to drop a midterm but I sure needed those to scrape an A out of it. Don't take if you have a rough schedule because reading is necessary

I'm split on rating Dr. Howard. He's a nice guy, but class structure is bad. Granted I didn't care too much about this class since it's just a GE, I didn't read the textbook, but I took notes during every class and got 50s/60s on all the tests. If you read, you'll probably do better, I just didn't care. Workload is light, but class isn't easy. Meh.

Super funny lectures, but the tests are ridiculously hard, difficult to prepare for them, they basically try to trick you. His lectures don't necessarily apply directly to the tests. You have to study super hard for the tests and you need to read the textbook, but its hard to know what to focus on in the reading for the test.

Kinda wish he was my sunday school teacher instead of my professor. He'll definitely give you the grade you deserve and offers you no mercy, but he knows his stuff and his dry whit is HYSTERICAL. One of the more sleep-inducing classes I've taken at BYU, but a fairly easy GE.

Professor Howard is great. Sassy Australian and very passionate about the subject. The only thing's you're graded on are: Quizzes (which you can retake until you get 100), 1 Written Assignment, and the Tests. The Music ID Tests are easy but the one thing about this class is the Multiple Choice tests are super hard! But, he makes it worth it.
Easy GE. Definitely recommend if you dont want to do too much work. Prof Howard is hilarious so it makes lectures interesting (but you dont have to go). Fairly easy A.

Super easy. Tests are basically vocab, study for an hour and you'll get an A. The final is verbatim questions from the tests, so its the easiest thing ever. Professor Howard is really funny and passionate, and has a great accent. 10/10 would take again

Dr. Howard is probably overqualified for teaching such basic GE courses. That knowledge, combined with his wit, make lectures very entertaining. The material covered on the tests is very ambiguous and seems to be based on random tiny details from the text more than anything else. Still, it was an easy enough class which only required 1-2 hours/week

Hes super funny, has a great Australian accent, makes lectures easier to sit through. Not a lot of homework, but his tests are HEAVILY detail oriented so you need to pay attention in class, take really good notes, and read about what he goes over in class to make sure you can remember everything.

Makes you read the entire textbook. Said the tests we needed to study the terms in the textbook, but were then many questions not about those terms. Isn't very clear on what you need to know for tests. Other than that all you do is write concert reports for 4 concerts, which isn't bad.

MUSIC 202 is the best class on BYU campus! And I wouldn't have wanted to take it from anyone else but Dr. Howard. He is not only hilarious and entertaining; he is so passionate about music and about the arts. You don't want to pass up these two classes during your time at BYU! They're hard work, but well worth the effort!

Pretentious, think he knows everything. His lectures are entertaining and informative, but awful in that you have no idea what he will test you on. His tests are ludicrously difficult. He doesnt care about his students success. If youre not good at writing, you wont do well.

I would 100% both of these classes again just to hear Dr. Howard teach! He's an Aussie and he's absolutely hilarious. I would highly recommend making yourself a detailed study guide throughout the course of the semester. DO THE READINGS. READ READ READ. Can't emphasize that enough. Despite challenging exams, definitely my favorite classes at BYU.

If you take notes in class on everything he says, that'll be enough to get you a high B on the tests. He curves the grade at the end. My friends used the book and did slightly better on the tests than I did. Easy class to cram for. No homework

Your grade is mostly two tests. If you go to class that will help, but you HAVE to study the book to do well. I didn't put in much effort and finished with a B, but it got curved to an A-. I would recommend this class, but only if you're willing to read & study a lot. Great professor (hilarious, sassy Australian).

Dr. Howard will keep you rolling on the floor laughing and lectures were really interesting. However, don't assume that just because you come to class you will do fine on the tests. The tests are extremely difficult and WILL require much time spent studying outside of class. I definitely wouldn't recommend for someone who misses class frequently.

Dr. Howard is by far the best professor I have had. I looked forward to his lectures with great anticipation. They are very interesting, full of humor, and leave you as a better person. The class itself is content heavy and mostly based on the midterm and final. Study groups will help a lot

Professor Howard is one of my favorite professors at BYU. He is SO knowledgeable about the subject that it blows my mind sometimes. His lectures are engaging, interesting, funny, and just overall incredible. His Australian accent is another plus. The ID exams can be a little difficult, but he provides plenty of study helps.

Dr. Howard is a cool guy and he really loves what he teaches about. There are about 7 quizzes and an essay that are easy. His tests are very hard and need lots of preparation and your grade depends a lot on the tests. His tests have lots of random details about composers, artists, and architects that are hard to study for. Hard class great prof.

Dr. Howard is great. Very interesting lectures. Don't procrastinate listening to the playlist for ID exams. Take specific notes on what he says in lecture and study them well. I did mediocre toward the beginning of the class but then I started studying harder and it became a breeze.

I loved Professor Howard. He's Australian so its really fun to listen to him talk regardless, but he always makes lecture interesting. 4 tests, 2 ID (open note) and 2 written exams in the testing center. ID tests are easy, written exams are pretty tough if you don't read the textbook or take good notes. Quizzes can be retaken so very easy. Worth it

This was my favorite class this semester. Dr. Howard is so witty yet eloquent and I truly was inspired by all of his lectures. He helped me develop a true love for learning. Sure, the tests are hard because there is so much to remember, but you will learn so many amazing things in this class.

His lectures are hysterical and enlightening. He truly cares about his subject and helps you care about it too. If you put time into preparing for his ID exams they are very doable and you can get an A without too much stress.

Howard is a good teacher and is passionate about music, but I found the tests extremely difficult and they are worth the great majority of your grade. Don't bother buying the textbook. The content is fairly interesting but again, the written portion of the test is way too hard. Didn't love the class but did like the teacher.

Dr. Howard is funny, and his austrailian accent just doubles the fun. his class is not hard, just show up and write notes. My best strategy was recording the lectures and playing them back at high speeds before tests to cram. It worked really well. It's a history class, so it's memorization, not figuring stuff out; make connections: this is the key

So much memorization. I guess that makes sense for the nature of the class but there was so much reading and homework and the it didn't seem to match the test very well. It was a very difficult class. But Dr. Howard is a lot of fun and very entertaining.

Dr. Howard knows how to keep your attention even if you are not a music major. He does a good job of covering the vast amount of information in art history at a pace that isn't hard to keep up with. The class I am in is test heavy, but he gives you the tools you need to get a good grade. He is also hilarious. Overall a really good professor.

Dr. Howard's lectures are informative and captivating. He definitely knows what he's talking about. The tests are not difficult if you pay attention in class. He will give you all the information you need to succeed during the lectures. It's clear that he wants all of his students to do the best they can in his class, and he is prepared to help.

Amazing lecturer. Austrailian. Writes the "spoken word" for Music and the Spoken Word. Knows his stuff when it comes to music history. It's good to have a foundational knowledge of music. Your grade is dependent on 4 tests (2 identification tests and 2 testing center bubble-in tests).  He usually curves. Study before tests and the class is easy.

Dr. Howard is an extremely knowledgeable and engaging lecturer. I took the evening section and the 2ish hours went by very quickly (and I always looked forward to going to class). Tests are ridiculously detail specific, so make sure you take amazing notes in class and read the textbook closely, but you can get an A if you put in the work.

This is definitely not worth the two GE credits! I'm a music minor and am very interested in music and art history, but this class was not at all interesting. Practically your only grades are the midterm and final, so if you don't do well on one, your GPA is ruined. You can listen to the playlists all you want,  he does not make the ID exams doable

The funniest professor ever. His lectures are very informative, and you must go or the class will be much harder. He tells you the stuff you need to know. STUDY your rear off for the tests. Tests and one paper basically make up your grade. But he really helped me learn a lot and love music and art history. don't procrastinate the music listening!

Dr. Howard is hilarious and I love his accent! He makes lectures interesting even though the information wasn't terribly interesting (at least to me). The tests are extremely difficult even if you study forever beforehand. Study the specifics!

Dr. Howard's lectures are funny and informative. Read the text, take thorough notes, and begin listening to class music at the beginning of the semester and you should do just fine. There are also usually a couple extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Howard's lectures are funny and informative, but he often falls behind schedule so you should make sure to read the text as well. Read the text, take thorough notes, and begin listening to class music at the beginning of the semester and you should do just fine. There are also usually a couple extra credit opportunities.

He is a great teacher. Hysterical and he gives great lectures. The quizzes are online and easy to take. Not much homework, but make sure you do the little homework that is given and you will pass the class with flying colors.
Professor Howard is a very good lecturer. I took a once a week, 2.5 hour lecture class from him, and he managed to keep our attention and make the content interesting.

Professor Howard is great!  His tests are pretty difficult, but he definitely doesn't set you up to fail.  Extra credit was provided and the other assignments were easy to ace.  Howard is a funny, engaging lecturer who expects a lot from his students but also knows their limits.  I'll be taking Music 202 from him next semester!
Awesome Class

Dr. Howard is hilarious, gives great lectures, plus he's Australian! The exams in the Testing Center are indeed tough, but if you study you'll do alright on them. All the other assignments can more than make up for however you do on those exams, plus there's a curve. Very interesting class and a great way to help take care of your Civ requirement.

Dr. Howard is freaking hilarious. His lectures are awesome. You NEED to go to ALL of the classes to get an even remotely good grade. The tests are s combo of memorising famous music pieces and works of art. The written portion of the test is pretty easy if you go to class. Such a good class!!!

This class really required a lot more than I expected from a GE 202 class. It seems as if he is just trying to mess with your GPA at times. If you are looking for an easy civilization credit this is NOT the class you are looking for. Dr. Howard is a good guy, but it seems he expects all his students to have knowledge of a music major. unreal.

Dr. Howard is a fantastic professor. He works to instill a love of the material in his students. The tests are very challenging, but like any other college course, if you apply yourself you can do well. I would definitely take again.

This is a tough class. Dr. Howard is a very captivating professor; however, the lectures still get tedious. Paying attention in lecture and reading are essential for doing well on the tests, which focus on many small details.  There isn't any homework besides reading and some easy quizzes, though, which is nice. There is a short essay.

Dr. Howard is awesome. He's hilarious, and makes coming to class enjoyable. His tests are wicked hard but there is a curve that helps. I would highly recommend Dr. Howard to anyone needing a Civilizations credit.

Professor that loves what he teaches & is excited to share knowledge. Two parts to his midterm & final: in class ID & testing center portion. The ID exam is easy if you pay attention in class and take good notes. The other half is difficult unless you have really studied for it. It is an interesting class if you like art, music, architecture & lit.

Sure, he's funny. If you want to audit the class to get a laugh, I would recommend it. I did better in Econ 110. I'm going to tell everyone to avoid this class if you want to pass the class with a decent grade. His tests are very tricky and their the only thing in the class so your grade is shot if you screw up on one. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

He's Australian so that made the class better lol. BEWARE: this is more of a humanities class than just music, you cover music, art and literature. The tests are WAY hard, you have to read the book if you want to pass them but other than that you don't really have to put much effort into this class.

Dr. Howard definitely makes my top five at BYU that really impacted my life. Very passionate about his subject matter and truly cares about his students doing well. Yes his class requires lots of reading and you actually have to study for his tests, but lets be real, we're in college. He only expects us to act like the adults we are. Great teacher!
Tests are hard, but there's a hefty curve. He loves what he teaches, and that definitely shows. Not a lot of work. Do the reading, go to lecture, pay attention, takes notes. You can get an A.
He's a super funny guy, which is the main reason I took the class, but the tests are still incredibly difficult (even though you don't really have to memorize dates and such)

Dr. Howard is fantastic--definitely one of my favorite professors! He knows what he's talking about, and he does it in a way that keeps you interested. His lectures are always highly amusing. Sure, maybe the tests are hard, but if you take good notes in class and keep up with the reading, you should be fine.

Dr Howard has been the worst professor I have had during these three years at BYU. Dr Howard frequently went on tangents where he spoke only of his personal convictions of feminism and opinions on politics and morality. His use of MicrosoftWord to type out snippets of notes as he went about his two hour monologue was unprofessional and ineffective
I didn't enjoy the class or learn a lot from it.

Don't expect this to be a music history class. It's more like a humanities class. I took it because I thought it would be about music, but so much time is spent on art, poetry and literature. This should not be called a music class. It is a general humanities class. Super dissapointing and I couldn't get out in time before the drop date :(

I've taken 3 classes from Dr. Howard and love him. Yes, his exams are hard, but if you go to the TA's you'll be fine. For the listening exams memorize as much as you can for them about the piece. The scores should be your best friend. Overall though, loved the class!
Life-changing class. I will never listen to classical music the same way again. Professor Howard is an unparalleled lecturer. I signed up because I had to, but I loved every minute of class time.

This was definitely one of my favorite classes at BYU. Dr. Howard's lectures were very good, and I learned SO much! The tests aren't too bad as long as you have attended class, paid attention, and taken good notes. Dr. Howard is really funny and Australian. Overall, I would highly recommend this class and professor!

Dr. Howard's lectures are very entertaining. He doesn't ever help you with test prep but if you take good notes and go to the reviews before the tests you should get an A on the tests. Quizzes are fairly easy and can be taken throughout the whole semester. Listen to the assigned music a lot in order to study for the music ID exams.

I found this class pretty challenging as a science major.  It is easy to prepare for the majority of the written test, but I never discovered how to completely prepare for it.  You will need to shell out the money to buy the cd's for the ID exam because I tried to do it just by listening to the songs on spotify and it didn't work.

Absolutely hilarious and a great teacher! His tests are killer, I'll be honest, but if you go to class and take really detailed notes and read the textbook you'll be fine. One of my favorite classes by far!

Maybe my favorite class at BYU, and my funniest teacher. Passionate but chill, so interesting &made me want to know everything about every topic. I had the class 3X a week at 8 AM and looked forward to going every single day. The tests are accessible if you've done the reading throughout. It's hard to cram because there is a lot of material.So good

Professor Howard is a very entertaining and engaging teacher, and he loves the subject.  He does go off topic sometimes, and I wish the focus of the class were a little different (we covered the 1970s minimalists, but not Chopin or Tchaikovsky), and the midterm and final require studying, but I still recommend him.  Just take the tests seriously!

He is a genius and made this class interesting. I would have found the material boring had he not taught it. Make sure you read and review throughout the semester, and don't try and cram for the midterm and final because there is SO MUCH information to study. The class is more of a humanities class than a music history class but I still enjoyed it.

His lectures are interesting & fun to attend. Always read the reading in the textbook, although the extra reading in the back of the book is pretty useless. His music ID exams are pretty easy, but the actual exam is extremely hard...studying for it is pretty much hopeless.

Dr. Howard was easily the most easy-going and hilarious teacher I had this semester.  Between Monty Python references, random jokes, the whole Australian thing, and even being part of MoTab, I loved coming to this class. There's only a couple of quizzes, a midterm and a final, and one paper as assignments, so be sure to pay good attention in class.

I looked forward to going to Professor Howard's class every day. He is extremely entertaining and makes the information interesting. Absolutely no busy work throughout the semester, but the midterm and final were very painful. Make sure you get lots of help from your TA for the paper; it is worth more than you think.

He is a great teacher. The class is pretty hard because of the massive amount of material covered. There is one writing assignment, and it isn't hard at all. There are online quizzes designed to help with midterms. You have to study a ton for exams, but I would definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Howard is fantastic!  The course is so-so in difficulty, but the material is intriguing and Dr. Howard is engaging and helpful.  Plus, he isn't too bad on the eyes.  And that accent... If you're debating which course to take for Civ2, this is the one.

Took this class in the Evening. This was the most difficult class I've taken. He's an interesting teacher but the midterm and final are killers. My head felt like it was going to explode all the random stuff I was trying to remember to get a good grade. I'd suggest taking something else for Civ1. Mix 33%(music/art/literature) wasn't expecting that.

Dr. Howard is the man! I took Music 201 from him after I loved his Music 202 class so much. This class is so easy, there is one paper, a midterm, and a final. Yeah, the tests are hard, but the class requires so little work besides going to class that it's totally worth it! Also, Dr. Howard is one of the funniest lecturers you'll ever have.

Dr. Howard is a great teacher. His lectures were interesting and entertaining, and he did a good job of communicating the concepts needed for exams. Class is easy, only 2 exams and 2 assignments. Take good notes and you'll be fine on tests. This is not a hard class, and it satisfies that horrendous Civ2 GE requirement.

I really enjoyed Dr. Howard's class. His lectures were always informative and he was just a really funny guy. You learn a lot about culture and cover a lot of interesting material. His tests were pretty killer, but if you did the readings and studied hard you were able to do relatively well.

I regret taking the class, mainly because I am not a music major, if you are, I am sure it would be worth the amount that you have to put into the class. He is a good teacher, but just not worth the work for a civ credit. Tests are unreal, it is true, and the papers are worth more than you think. Hard class. Tough to do well in.

This is a challenging but interesting class. Dr Howard clearly loves what he teaches and is entertaining. The essay assignments are hard but fortunately not worth much. For the ID exams I just listened to songs until I had them memorized and I got As. The testing center exams are hard though. I got a B- but ended up with a B+ because of the curve.

I learned many things that I did not know before about music. however if you want to get an A you have to extremely study a lot before the tests. If you read every thing that asks you to read before each class, you will do fine in the tests. The tests are very hard, and sometimes you have to guess what could be the answer if you did not read.

His lectures were always entertaining and he's a really funny guy. I studied hard failed the midterm and studied hard for the final and got a D because of the awesome curve I managed to get a B in the class. I also learned so much and it got me really interested in art history. Take the class, it's hard work but totally worth it.

Dr. Howard is great.  Read every week and go to every lecture.  The tests are hard, but not impossible.  He also gave the class a 6.5 percentage boost at the end of the semester.  He keeps lecture interesting, and clearly loves what he teaches.  Great way to pass humanities.

everyone is right, tests are hard, impossible to know what is on the test, but most of the facts are in the textbook and what he emphasizes in class.  To do well take notes in lecture and while reading the textbook.  If you don't read the text, or read it casually expect a C (or lower).  It is possible to do well, you just need to study (hard).

The tests used to be online, then he found out that a student was googling the answers, so without changing them at all, he put them in the testing center. The average grade on the test would be a C- and he wouldn't curve the tests because according to him, tests should be like the SATs: impossible to get a 100, and on material you've never seen.

Absolutely the worst class I've ever taken at BYU. If you like bad grades and pointless facts about art, this class is for you. If you want to learn about music, don't take the class. You won't learn much. The tests are ridiculous. The class is pointless. I am very disappointed in BYU. I came here to learn. I didn't in this class.
Very exciting and great teacher.  Clear and understandable and really helps you understand the deeper parts.

He is an amazing teacher! So funny! This is now my favorite class because of his lectures and the things he teaches- its so interesting! The tests are very hard and there is alot of information to take in. But go to lectures and he will make it more clear.

Dr Howard is funny and engaging.  He's a really good teacher, but this class has very little to do with music. We didn't even talk about music until maybe a month into the semester.  Tests are pretty tough, but he's a great teacher. I'd take a class from him again.

HIS TESTS ARE RIDICULOUS!!! seriously they are impossible, he himself said that when he reviews them every year, he doesn't know all of the answers - has to look up the answers.  he is a great lecturer, though.  interesting, funny, accent, everything you could want in a professor.  tests will murder you.

Dr. Howard is the greatest teacher in the world.  This class is much easier than the other ridiculous Humanities classes.  I felt his tests for this class was straightforward and his lectures are so interesting.  As long as you keep up with the readings and listening to the scores, it'll be no problem to do extremely well in this class.

He has a cool accent.  I had to take this class in the evening and it was way too long.  The tests were ridiculously hard.  I wouldn't take this class unless you nuts about art history.  The class has very little to do with music.

Uh... he's cool and all, but the tests are so ridiculous. There are no straightforward questions that have straight forward answers. I felt like I was guessing on every question I answered. I think too much is required of you for a G.E. class.

One of the best professors I have ever had. His lessons are terse and enjoyable, and he's one of the funniest professors on campus. Both Music 201 and 202 are very difficult classes, but well worth the work. Take his class(es)! Seriously!

Dr. Howard is AMAZING! Hysterical, interesting, insightful, and all-around incredible. His classes are some of my most favorite, and memorable in my college experience. You learn SO much, but it's fun with him! Great insights and experience from Dr. Howard! TAKE THIS CLASS!

Great professor who really cares and has a way of getting the material across in a way that you just can't forget or not understand.  I don't think there's anything he ever explained that I didn't understand the first time he said it.

Professor Howard is a great lecturer and entertaining when he teaches. He's very down to earth. The class is interesting too. The only drawback is that the tests used to be open book and online, but now they are in the testing center, but they are the same test. They're a little difficult. Interesting class though.

The class is really tough, but Professor Howard is a great teacher and so much fun. I loved coming to class. There is a multiple-choice midterm and music identification midterm. Same goes for the final.

I loved coming to class.  Professor Howard is very fun.  Very hard tests, but very fun class.  All you need to do is study the book.  It is all in the book.  Sure it takes time and it is hard to memorize stuff, but getting an A in this class is totally doable with some work.

This is an incredible class. Don't think that this is going to be an easy GE credit though. You learn sooooo much, and he is absolutely hysterical! If you go to all the review sessions, read, attend class, ask questions, and study like a maniac, with a curve you'll get a good grade. His accent is incredible too! Ask about his crappy american accent

I am a foreign student and found Mus 201 to be one of the best classes I took at the Y. There are 2 in class ID exams (easy, open notes, attend reviews and listen to the CDs), 2 papers (way easy) and 2 testing center exams (quite difficult), quizzes are open book. Really enjoyed Dr. Howard's SHORT lectures and a good sense of humor!
Fascinating lectures! Amazing teacher! Pretty hard, start studying for the tests early, but definitely worth taking. Willing to work with you if you need something. Cool guy and cool accent!

Dr. Howard is a really great professor. There is one midterm and one final, which is not comprehensive. The tests cover a lot of information so cramming right before the test is not going to help. I really liked lectures whereas others thought he was boring. I really liked the class. Also there are 2 papers, 2 ID exams and online quizzes.

The lectures are great and fun to listen to, especially if you are into music. It is fun to listen to him speak because he has a great Australian accent; also, his sense of humor makes class more interesting. There are four tests; two music id's and two multiple choice.  The multiple choice tests are hard! Even hard study doesn't guarantee a B.

Professor Howard is awesome. Seriously hes such a funny guy his lectures are so entertaining. The title of the class is misleading its not just music but basially humanities with a little more music than a humanitites class would have(if that makes sense)so theres still art literature architecture etc. i'll be honest the tests are really tough

Great guy; really funny. This class doesn't have nearly as much "music" involved as I thought it would.  There are a lot of humanities-type things involved.  Be aware.  I'd take it again though.  Prof. Howard is fantastic.
So far a really awesome teacher; a must take for people who love music.  Also, the class counts toward two general requirements.

I took Dr. Howard for 201 and 202 they were the best classes I've ever taken at BYU.  Yes, he's tough and expects you to be mature and responsible, but it's doable.  He is the most entertaining lecturer I've had.  He's hilarious and has a neat perspective because he's from Australia, complete with the cool accent.  I learned so much and loved it!

He's a fairly entertaing lecturer (and he has a great accent). He's cynical at times, which can be a bit refreshing, but maybe a bit offensive to some, I don't know. The tests are hard, as they say, but are doable if you know the material and can think through multiple choice questions. Better choice than taking Hum 201 and 202, in any case.

Testing center exams are now closed note which sucked.  They are 30% of your grade.  ID exams are another 30%, quizes are 20%, and papers are 20%.  An average class, not super hard, but not really easy either. I just crammed for the tests for like 12 hours reading the chapters. I'll prob get an A.
