In class ID exams are still open book/note, but you really need the notes for the testing center exam which is not.  He won't say what he's going to focus on in the tests.  At times he assumes everyone in the class knows all about music--meters, tonality, moving fifths, triads and other things and doesn't go over what they mean.

Dr. Howard is so much fun and a great teacher.  Attendance isn't mandatory, but you should go or you'll be in trouble for ID exams.. and it's fun.  THE MIDTERM AND FINAL ARE NO LONGER ONLINE and open note.  They're in the testing center with no notes and just as hard.  But graded on a curve now.

Great class! Take this to cover civ. requirement. The tests take 3-5 hours because you have to look almost every answer up in your book and notes.ID tests are easy and papers are a joke. Dr. Howard is soo great, and he loves what he teaches.

Howard is a pretty awesome teacher. You write 2 papers which are a breeze, and there's 2 ID exams, which arent hard, but the online tests are open book start n stop and HARD!!! going to class DID NOT help w/ it. It was all wikipedia for me. Took FOREVER. So as long as ur prepared for that, youll do fine. TAKE THIS INSTEAD OF CIV!

good heavens, I love this man! The class was early... but so good that I actually got up in the morning to go (most the time). The midterm took about 5 or 6 hours to take... and the final longer. But they are both online, and open note! sooooo... it's a very fair chance.         If you do you're reading everyday I bet this class would be a breeze

Dr. Howard is HILARIOUS! The Australian accent is the cherry on top. The class by nature is a challenging one, but he tries to make it as painless as possible. One of my favorite professors and classes. I would highly recommend it! Great way to cover the Civ. requirements!

Really enjoyed this class and the professor.  An easy way to take care of the civ requirements.  Dr. Howard is passionate about his class and is very thorough.  Go to class, take good notes, and keep up and you will do well.  One of my favorite classes that I have taken over the past 15 years!

Dr. Howard is sooo great! So far, he is one of my favorite teachers at BYU, and this has been my favorite classes so far. The class is very interesting, and covers not only music, but also art. It is a fairly easy class, you basically just need to come to class to get an A, and you definitely want to come to class because the lectures are awesome!

Once referred to as the "gospel according to Luke" this has been, by far, my favorite class. Dr. Howard not only covers the material well, but makes every lecture entertaining. He often tries to apply the concepts we are talking about to an LDS standpoint, which is really great, and he never fails to include humor in his discussions.

uh, LOVE dr. howard. his class is great and the tests really are not that hard, they're open note and open book. reading helps so when you take the test it doesn't take you forever to find all of the answers. almost our whole class got A's or B's this semester. it's an easy class.

I loved it! He has an amazing accent, and if you attend the lecture and take notes--promise you'll be fine. The tests were  hard, but there are only 2 and they are open book! You can take all the time you need! Plus, if you go to the TA Review before the test, they'll go over everything you need to know.

Brother Howard's class is very hard. It doesn't seem  hard because he just lectures on material from the book. Wait till you get into it though. For the midterm and the final you have to recognize music, literature, and art and where it came from and who did it. The tests are ridiculously hard.

He as two open book tests online and an in class test where you have to identify certain types of music and paintings.Not terribly difficult,just make sure you go to class,notes are super helpful on the tests.And he is not lenient on late work (so you will have to write 2 short research papers as well)Oh and he has a super cool Australian accent!

Dr. Howard is one of the most entertaining and passionate teachers I have had.  His class is easy, if you stay caught up.  He is laid back mostly, but there are a few things that he makes it clear he will not tolerate, and if you get on his bad side, I can see how you might not enjoy this class.  But, just do what you're asked and you'll love it.

Howard has VERY interesting lectures.  He's full of energy and excitement and loves what he teaches. 2 online tests (open book, open notes) were fairly difficult, even with the book & notes.  2 music/art recognition tests (in class) that were hard but doable.  I would highly recommend this class & this professor for the Civ 2 GE.

I took this class Spring semester and found it pretty challenging. I loved the teacher though, he was hilarious and loves talking about this subject matter. The class is really interesting. The two in class tests are pretty easy if studied for and the online tests i found really challenging, just because we didn't cover half the material in class.

Dr. Howard is hilarious! Attendance isn't mandatory but I went to his class just because he was so entertaining. His in-class tests are a bit hard so you need to study for them. If you take notes in lecture it really helps you do well. Overall I thought it was a very worthwhile class.

Dr. Howard is awesome. Lectures are VERY interesting and relevant to what you're tested on. Be sure to pay attention and take notes and you'll do well. 2 tests in class recognizing music & art pieces. 2 tests online.  All tests open-book, open-note. Also some online quizzes and 2 short papers, but those were really easy and didn't take much time.

This is a great professor! His lectures are incredibly entertaining and there are review sessions before every exam. There's a weekly quiz and two midterms, but they're all open-book, open-note. If you take a lot of notes you will be FINE. Everything on the test was in my notes or in the book. The 2 papers are cake.  Do the work and you'll be fine!

He's a very good teacher with good lectures. The only thing I disliked was that he was very unforgiving for late assignments. I don't blame him,perhaps I would be the same way. But really, stick to the deadlines--don't expect mercy.

I really enjoyed his class, he has a great sense of humor and is willing to go back and explain more about things that people didn't understand.  Tests can be pretty difficult, but if you study hard you will be fine.  He tells you exactly what to study and that really is what is going to be on the exam.  Note-taking is a must.

Very fun Professor.  He's an avid Monty Python fan with this enormous wealth of knowledge of music and art.  It's a fairly easy class so long as you take good notes, and it definitely wouldn't hurt to crack the spine of your book, either.

Dr. Howard requires weekly quizzes based on lectures.  They are open note, but if you don't have notes, you will fail.  I have found this is a class I cannot miss unless I want to fail the weekly quizzes.  You're required to write 2 papers, and parts of the exams are identification.  The class is not solely on music.

I had Dr. Howard for Music 201 and 202.  I actually did better in the class when I stopped going to class.  I didn't like it very much but now I appreciate classical art and music more.  The best part about the class was his cool accent.

He loves to teach and that readiated from him every day. He always kept us entertained. However, those thinking that it's a MUSIC class, it's not! It is art history. I have no problem with art history, except for the fact that I didn't want to take an art history class. There's a little music in it, but it's not worth an entire semester of art.

Dr. Howard is a great professor; I took Music 201 and 202 from him.  The tests are hard, but not impossible.     He makes sure that there are plenty of review materials available.  Don't miss lectures, take good notes, and try to read before class.  Study with friends, and use the learning objectives!  These were my favorite classes. Lots to learn.
Funny teacher with cool Australian accent.  Interesting lectures.  Tests can be tough, but grading is heavily curved.  About 1/3 of the class gets A's and A-'s.  Great way to fulfill GE requirement.
He is a really good teacher and really knows his stuff, but without the help of the textbook and basically any resource you can find, it's really hard to do well.

Fantastic class! A lot more actual music in 202 than in 201. With a couple hours of studying, ID exams are pretty easy. I usually managed about a B+ on Testing Center exams by reviewing my class notes really well. The essay Dr. Howard requires can be fun if you choose a good topic. GENEROUS curve--at end of semester, top 50% of class gets A or A-.

STUPID HARD CLASS!!  Someone told me that it wasn't that bad.  She lied to me!  Awful awful class.  Be prepared to be slammed with a ton of material that is impossible to memorize.  The TAs weren't that great either.

I took this class a few semesters ago and still remember much more information than any other class. I took it when we still had to write a crzy paper, but I heard they did away with that. The ID exams are fun to study for with friends at 3 AM, making weird ways to remember things. HEY WAIN!!

Prof. Howard is a very fun teacher. Although some of the material could be boring he make it fun. The tests can be a little difficult if you don't study (enough), but it is a good class. He is not confusing at all... I enjoyed this class and his method of teaching. I recommend this class if you are looking to fulfill a GE.

He's a great teacher!  I really loved his class.  The ID exams are easy as long as you review the music and art.  The testing center exams however are kind of hard to study for because of the detail in each question but it is possible to get a really good grade on them.  Overall the class is very enjoyable and he has the most awesome accent!

2 Art/Music ID exams, which are easy, and then 2 Testing Center Exams, which are extremely difficult.  No amount of studying will adequately prepare you for those 2 exams.  Luckily, the curve is VERY generous in the end, so you're always doing better than you think you are.  Howard is a decent teacher with a cool accent.  Keep up on the readings!
His tests are hard and detail oriented, but his class is really fun and informative.  A very rewarding class if you are willing to put in the effort for the tests.
pretty sassy but nice in the end

I've taken from this professor three times because he is such a great teacher. His tests are really hard, but once you get the hang of them they aren't. He is detail oriented because that's what music is: detail oriented. I love this professor!
2 hard tests and 2 very easy ones. The paper is not hard, just long. He teaches extremely well and makes it easy to pay attention because he's not boring. Plus, he has a cool Australian accent.

The tests are very detail-intensive; however, the class is very interesting, and his grading is fair.  A word of advise on the paper:  make sure you get a nice TA to grade it.  Specify who you want to grade your paper and talk to them beforehand.

A very difficult class, but very rewarding. Don't take this class if you are worried about getting an "A," (although about a quarter of last semester's students got A- or better). Dr Howard is very well educated and lecture is interesting. This is a great option to fulfill the G.E.

This class is set up to make people fail. the "professor" teaches everyday class with the idea that what he is saying is somehow inportant to you or at least will be on the test.then you come to the test's that are worth 20% of your grade each and they want the small details the stuff that no one would have thought to study.Don't take this class

This class was so hard! I really didn't like it and I love music and art and literature. Dr. Howard is a great teacher but his tests were killers. And there was a 10 page research paper that was so stupid and pointless. Unless this class becomes easier I would not suggest taking it. Audit it if you want to learn more about art and music.

He's entertaining, but he doesn't teach very well.  It was difficult for me to know what he wanted us to learn from the lecture.  He tests on material we're supposed to have read, but he never even mentions some of it in class.
So. Cool.

I loved his classes but they are definitely much easier if you have a background in music, because sometimes he doesn't explain in detail.  Great personality and fun to listen to.  Because of his 201 class, I decided to major is Humanities:Music.  The tests really aren's as big a deal as everyone says.  He lets you drop the lowest test/paper score
The test are hard, you have to memorize a lot of information. However, he is cool, but the TA's i did not like.

He made the lectures pretty enjoyable, but if I had the choice, I would have taken a different class.  The testing center Multiple choice exams were sooo hard.  I learned a lot in the class, but my grade didn't show it at all.

This class wasn't as hard as everyone says it is. All you have to do is memorize titles and artists. The testing center exams are meant to be difficult to prove if you read the chapter or not. He grades on a HUGE curve, too! He is a master musicologist, and I recommend this class to anyone!!

Dr howard was a nice guy but only take his religion class if you want a very objective look at the BoM. It's not bad, but I'd be hard pressed to say I felt the spirit in there more than a few times. He's a really nice guy though, tells funny stories and has an awsome accent!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS unless you are very good at memorizing.  In-class exams are very difficult.  This is definately the hardest civ class.  Go elsewhere.  That said, he is a nice person and an entertaining lecturere (especially in the afternoon).  This class is very time-intensive.

took both civ classes.  Just get help from the TAs.  There are three different tests per section.  Not too hard if you really enjoy visual art and music.  don't get caught up in the specifics.  get the general ideas and apply it to all the tests.  prof. has random ideas...keeps class entertaining

If you think you can find an easier class, take the other class! The testing center tests are sooo hard, I could never know what we were gonna be tested on! The in-class tests are ok if you can memorize more than 30 figures! You can't procrastine, if you do it, you will do really bad in this class!
He made the class much easier than it could have been.  I took 202 from Johnson and it almost killed me.  It was still a lot of work, but Howard was cake compared to how hard it could have been.

Holy crap the worst class I have ever been in in my entire life.  The boredom was my fault, but studying for 10 hours before a test and getting a 56 on it??    (this happened 5 times too)  but it's a great class for procrastinators, you can put stuff off forever.
Great teacher, but not a really easy A.

I've taken 3 classes from Dr. Howard.  Two of them were incredibly easy to get an A in, but taking the civilization course was a killer.Hhe was unclear as to what we should know about.  The only thing in the civ class that kept my partially awake is his wickedly awesome Australian accent.
Dr. Howard is an awesome teacher. He is very hard (at least for me, I can't memorize anything to save my life). But I enjoyed his lectures and interpretive dancing.

Dr. Howard is one of the most interesting teachers I've ever had.  He definitely knows his stuff.  It's fun to go to class, and just listening to his accent makes it worth being there.  The tests are a little difficult, but he has a very lenient grading policy that makes it easy to get an A.
Brother Howard is great (especially his accent!).  The class is very informal and laid back.  It is fairly easy as well.
Hard course...but a great techer to listen to.

Dr. Cox is the nicest guy, and this class is awesome! Easiest A I have ever taken at BYU. If you show up to class, you'll get an A. Everything is basically self-graded. He genuinely cares for every student and gives good advice to live more positively!

I took Professor Cox's online Positive Living course. It was fairly easy and simple to navigate. The one thing was that Professor Cox was completely absent, which is what should be expected from an online course. You often forget you have a teacher.
Classes were super fun to be in and you learn a lot. Basically all of the work is honor code whether you did it or not but even then it was super easy. Would reccomend

Weekly reading quizzes. A fair amount of projects which are easy to bs. A final paper that I spent like 30 mins on and got a 100%. Very easy A, a baby could get an A. Attendance is 20% of your grade. I feel like I did nothing but got over 100%. take this EASY class.

You basically choose your grade in this class, and Professor Cox is quick to explain that a grade is not the point of this class. If you attend and participate you will get so much from this class. I wish I'd done more because he literally sets you up for success. This should be a recommended course for all students because its seriously so helpful

Professor/Dr Cox is amazing!!! Makes the class seem very light, easy to learn, but also very inspiring. He's very passionate. Loves it when people participate and pitch in their thoughts and questions. He makes a lot of jokes too; you can't help but to smile and laugh every class period. If you need to take this class, take it through him!!!

This class was one of the best things I did this semester. He is so fun and engaging in his lectures! I was able to learn a lot without being overly stressed about my grade. He does ask students to work with classmates often, so be ready for that. Overall, great professor and a really great class!

Dr. Cox is awesome! I learned SO much from him in a low pressure environment and I really appreciated that he recognized that student development classes are not students top priority class and therefore dont need to require hours of work. Minimal homework and maximum learning perfectly describes his class.

He's a decent professor! His lectures in the first half of the semester are kinda dry, but the topics covered and the book we read in class are AWESOME. It's an easy A. As long as you do the assignments, you can get a great grade!

Such a great teacher! Everything in the class is taught in promotion of "intrinsic learning" so Prof. Cox encourages you to only do the assignments you want/have time to do. I had to miss 85% of the classes, but still got an easy A and he never judged me at all for it. Textbook is engaging and content is useful. Absolutely love this class and Cox!
Cox is a great teacher. Good personality, happy to help, and very friendly. He's a very easy grader, and attendance is optional.

I enjoyed the class. It's purposely very easy and relaxed. The hardest thing to do was present a couple of times in front of the class. There were readings and worksheets to do, but they weren't too bad. Also, everything is graded on the honor system.

Cox was awesome! This was literally the easiest class that I have had at BYU by far. He basically gives you 100% on everything if you turn it in. There are no due dates for any of the homework assignments until the last day of the semester. If you are taking a lot of hard classes, I recommend taking this one with Cox. It is so easy to get an A in.

Professor Cox's class is outstanding. Such an inspirational teacher! Great man and everything in his class is due the last day! NO TESTS! Everything is self graded expect for a few presentations that are done in class! Amazing teacher that really helped me to explore future opportunities.

This class was the greatest! Mostly self grade assignments. I really enjoyed the course and although going to class was not really mandatory, going was entertaining and fun. He is a great professor and is kind and understanding. Lenient with deadlines. I've recommended this class to so many people.

Stressed out? Need 2 chill easy, A credits? Take this from Dr. Cox. Nothing due until the end of the semester, you learn a lot if you decide to put in the time and get something out of it. And Dr. Cox makes an effort to learn his student's names and make sure we're understanding the material. Gives you some good tools to deal with life.

Jon is the best! He cares and trusts his students. The class is easy and you can learn a lot if you do everything you are supposed to do. Definitely take this class from him. He is soooo chill! Don't take it from anyone else, Jon is the best!

Jon is amazing, this class was awesome. He is a genuinely kind and caring professor- learned everyone's names. Made some cheesy jokes but you learn to love him. Very very intelligent. This class is only helpful if you want it to be- its an easy A either way, but if you dont put in the effort you wont enjoy it. course1 was interesting and relative.

I really enjoyed my time in this class. I learned about time management, happiness, spirituality, life planning, & decision making. We had to read a book and a few other powerpoints but you have the whole semester to read it & it was interesting. Professor Cox is hilarious and attendance isn't mandatory. Would recommend. Easy A and you learn a lot.

Loved this class & this professor! Probably one of my favorite classes that I've taken! I learned a lot about myself, & about useful tips to help make good decisions throughout my life. It was also spiritually uplifting. The class was relaxing & lectures were very interesting. No due dates; just turn in everything by the end of the semester.

This class was literally the easiest. You have to read a book and take quizzes on it, but there are no real due dates, just as long as you do it all before the last day of finals. It is a really easy A. There are hardly any assignments at all. Professor Cox is really chill and just wants to help the students and not stress them out.

Jon Cox is awesome! His class is an easy-A and it helped me understand myself a bit, too. Definitely take either if you want to bump your GPA a little or want to learn about yourself more (or both). One paper, a few open-book tests on a book about Willpower (which was a really interesting book) that take like 5 minutes to take.

This class changed my life! If you go to class prepared, you will learn a lot. Or, you can just show up for the easy A. Lecture was fun, no tests, the book is interesting, and lectures are there is lots of class discussion. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Life planning and decision making is an amazing class. Brother Cox is engaging, funny, clear about what he wants, and really cares about the students. The class is not super demanding, 2hrs. a week tops. Plus, you learn a whole lot about yourself. The textbook is  interesting and an easy read. This is a MUST TAKE for anyone at BYU.

I'm not sure why Dr. Cox has gotten any bad ratings because everyone in my class loved him. He was so nice to students and a really good teacher. He made good use of class time, answered all our questions, and is a super laid back guy. I learned a lot in this class and was surprised to find it more interesting than I expected.
He was funny and helped keep us calm when we were frustrated.  He was willing to work with everybody and wanted everyone to do well.
He did a good job considering the syllabus he had to work with. Tried to help the students as much as he could. He was very approachable.

HORRIBLE TEACHER! His lab was absolutely pointless to go to, a waste of time. Landon Poppleton teaches with him, he is good, but Jon is horrible! I don't know who is going to be teacher b/c Layne is gone, but take it from someone else
He tried his best with Layne's sylabus but the class still sucked. He seemed nice enough, fairly laid back.  Landon Poppleton was better.

Professor clearly cares about what she is teaching. The material can be somewhat difficult at times, and professor Finau does a decent job at teaching it. Professor Finau is a great teacher, but she lectures assuming you've already read the assigned reading. To understand the material and her lectures, you must do the assigned reading every night.

I wish Dr. Finau taught the class more. Her TA's taught well over half of it and it didn't seem that they were in line with grading and exceptions. Obviously she wants to give them teaching experience, but they made the class harder. The final is easy if you have a good group and you put in time, but the class is very demanding about reading.

Dr. Finau herself was a pretty good professor when she was actually teaching. However, she often seemed dismissive of peoples experiences and would fish for answer after asking "open ended" questions. The class is really heavy in reading and writing, though it's not impossible.

The class and its subject material was interesting, but it is mainly busy work, but it easy to get an A. Dr. Finau wasn't there a lot of the time so the TA's would teach a lot. The TA's were by far the worst part about the class and the grading on the daily assignments were harsh. It is very book heavy, but the tests were easy and in class.

Doctor Finau is an incredible instructor and human overall. I loved listening to her talk about her own culture, as well as hear her dissect other cultures we discussed. This class opened my eyes to so many details that go into cultures and ethnography, it's a class I think everyone should take!

I love Dr Finau, but she rarely taught the class. It was usually her TAs and they were some of the worst I've ever had when I was in the class. They took off points on assignments for the most nitpicky things. I think if the TAs were better I would have enjoyed the class more.

One of the best Professors you will ever have at BYU, she is super caring and energetic, really makes you engaged during class, her TA's were great, atleast when I took her class. There is a lot of reading, but no mid terms and finals was pretty easy. Do be prepared to be writing a lot of essays though.
I loved Dr. Finau! Very passionate about the subject and cares about students. Lot's of reading but very doable.

I honestly really enjoyed this class! I will say it is A LOT of papers and assignments for a 101 class, but I love the professor and most of the readings where somewhat interesting. I think this class is easy for some people and harder for others, it seems like it really depends on who you have as a TA. Overall, a good amount of work but enjoyable!

Professor Finau is SUPER nice, but her class has a TON of reading. If you take it 3 times a week you have to read 20-40 pages and write a 400 word homework assignment on the reading before each class. Also these homework assignments are given no credit if you turn them in late, so beware of that. The reading is hard and often boring.

Dr. Finau is so amazing!! She is so funny and caring. I took this course in the summer, and it was a decent amount of work but nothing too crazy. There are 3 required books and essays and quizzes that go along with the reading. There is also a final group ethnographic project which is actually pretty interesting! No midterm and final exam was easy

I loved my Anthropology class with Dr. Finau! She is hilarious and so relatable, and you can easily tell she is passionate about the subject, which makes her thoughts in lectures pretty impactful. The workload is reasonable, and the grading criteria are mostly clear. And the TAs are fabulous! Highly recommend taking a class from her!

Dr. Finau was AMAZING!! She is so easygoing and funny. There is required reading, a couple of papers, and discussion posts, but if you stay on top of everything and pay attention, you'll be fine. She also has great TAs that made the class super awesome!

I took Professor Finau's Anthropology 101 class and we read 3 books and wrote 2 papers. Expect to do discussion posts over the reading, as well as quizzes. The final was over the last book we read (super easy if you study)! There is a group project but her TA's are amazing and will guide you!

Overall, 10/10 would take this class again, I loved it!

The content is simple. Attendance and participation are graded. Main complaint was the quality of the tests and quizzes—frequent typos made questions confusing. When students asked clarifying questions, her answers often made things less clear. The class isn't hard to pass, but with the poor organization, I wouldn't take another class with her

Dr. Eyestone is lecture based but includes regular group discussions and class activities. She cares to make an engaging learning environment. Her tests may seem specific sometimes but if you go to the TA review sessions they are completely doable. She is a very fun and enthusiastic professor.

It was tough to stay awake in her lectures, as most of the lass was either fluff or 'group participation' where it was structured as her asking for people's opinions and writing them on the board. She mainly just taught touchy feely nonsense, but the TA for the class (Heather) is absolutely goated for reviews. Nice person, not academically rigorous

Dr Eyestone is very passionate about positive psych. However, the classes can be a lot. Group work is stressful at times, I know a few students find it hard. It's often rushed. Classes often go over time- those few minutes count. But the material is useful. Lots of reading. I like the wellbeing strategies. TA review sessions are not timed well.
Super fun, easy A. Really inspirational if you buy in, and doesn't feel like lots of busywork

Engaging and insightful teacher, but nearly impossible to get an A. Study for 12 hours straight? You still won't be prepared for the tests. They are 33% of your grade and made to be as difficult, misleading, and random-detail specific as possible. The study guides are too broad and the questions will be over the one tiny detail you didn't study.

Dr. Eyestone is the sweetest teacher! Always came with enthusiasm! Took her in Fall 2023 as a freshman and I loved everything about her class. Attendance is large majority of grade and I got an A- only because I would sleep in and miss class. Few assignments; do a wellness activity for a week and report on it. A final group project. All super easy!

Dr. Eyestone is very old school. No laptops or phones allowed and her lectures are so boring. Lecture slides are outdated and missing material and the book is not the only source for readings and quizzes. Pretty common sense stuff on how to be happy. The TA is not helpful at all and forget about participation points, only attendance counts.

Fantastic class. It's designed to help you learn tools to think in healthier ways. I loved the lectures as they were discussion based, allowing me to apply the concepts. I came away feeling more in control of my thoughts and emotions, and improved my relationships. The homework is useful, tests are easy if you go to the TA review. Changed my life.

Dr. Eyestone was an extremely frustrating teacher. The topics in her class were common sense- stuff like "How to be happy" but the tests were an entirely different story. Tests are purely opinion-based so learn psychology according to Lynn Eyestone if you want to do well. She also doesn't allow laptops and will shut it on your fingers. Goodluck.

I LOVE Prof. Eyestone. Her positive psych class was one of my favorites at BYU ever. She is a fantastic lecturer, and super available outside of class. Her tests were totally manageable as long as you paid attention in class and went to the TA test reviews. Can't say enough about this class and Prof. Eyestone- seriously. LOVE her.

She is very enthusiastic about Pos. Psych! Graded by 3 Well-Being Strategies you want to work on throughout the semester, 3 tests, attendance, reading quizzes, and a group presentation on a chosen pos. psych topic. The class was not hard, I liked the content of what we were learning, sometimes the lectures seemed to go on forever though.

She's an amazing teacher who explains concepts in ways that make sense. The tests are a little difficult bc they pull info from the lecture & textbook & it's just a lot to remember so study hard. Tests are 65% of grade. Other assignments are easy. TAs do most of the grading so she just teaches the class, but her classes were always interesting

Professor Eyestone is awesome, and I wholeheartedly recommend taking this class. It is a pretty easy class, but one of the most influential that I have taken. The TAs grade pretty much everything, but the rubric's are super clear and it is hard to do poorly. I did not LOVE her tests but they were okay.

This class was harder than it needed to be. It is an 8am class and if it wasn't mandatory attendance, her lectures are not relevant for the test. She will assign lots of reading and then go over a few things in class. The test will include things that are not in the Study guide. If you're looking for a less academic class with hand games, take it.

Dr. Eyestone is a very nice person, but I'm not sure she was well-suited for the class. Our class had a lot of concerns about test questions, and she didn't really budge on curving the test or throwing out bad questions. She oversimplifies a lot of the concepts.

Professor Eyestone gave great lectures and was a nice person. However, her 3 tests were the hardest I've ever taken at BYU and 66% of the grade. They required over 30 pages of memorization and had 7 essay questions and 75 multiple choice so they took hours. The TA's weren't allowed to give any help on studying for the test besides the study guide.

This is an easy class and Professor Eyestone is a kind professor. She wants the best for all her students and you can definitely tell. However, this class is more of a self-help class than learning psychology. Class materials sometimes misrepresent scientific literature and cite unacademic sources. It wasn't what I was looking for but that's ok.

This class was MY FAVORITE! You literally learn science-based ways to be happier! Super easy to earn A's on everything for the class! TA reviews really help with the two midterms and final! There is 1 group presentation project, weekly open book quizzes, and 3 well-being strategy projects. 100% recommend taking this class for everyone!!

Dr. Eyestone is the most positive and happy professor I have ever had. It was refreshing to have her class as my 8am class. She has a lot of knowledge about various psych studies and is a really good listener. Her classroom discussions are great. I wouldn't say that the class is difficult at all though.

Definitely take psych or soc 350 from her, she is amazing and she makes even boring content interesting. She made me think I liked sociology/social psychology which I have found out through other classes is definitely not true. However, she is probably one of the best teachers on campus.
I love Prof. Eyestone! She knows her stuff. She is willing to answer any question. She is not the type of teacher who gets defensive. Very refreshing.
Above-average professor. The smaller class size is conducive to a more intimate and engaging learning experience. The final exam is pretty intense. Definitely recommend taking the course.

Dr. Eyestone is a queen!! She creates a really great environment for class discussion but still teaches factual information. There are always funny little demonstrations in class and fun assignments. Not a crazy hard class, just do the weekly papers and you will be fine. Exams are fair.

I love Dr. Eyestone. Her lectures are always very interesting, and she does a good making the concepts stick in real life. The assignments aren't hard (some of them were fun). Don't worry too much about reading the book. She posts the slides from each of her lectures right before the exam, so that helps a lot! Take her class for Psych 350!!!!!

Eyestone is a solid teacher and does a good job of making a very discussion oriented class. Make sure you don't miss an assignment. Since there arent a ton of assignments, each one can hurt your grade if you forget it. The assignments are not hard. Attendance is important for surprise participation grades and to know material. Take this class.

She's the best! Always loved her lectures! She asked good questions that created good discussion, she respected everyone's thoughts, and did many object lessons to help us learn the concepts. There are a few one page papers, including reviewing research articles. If you go to the reviews for the tests and go over the study guide you should be okay!

grade based on 4 exams and 2 assignments based on work during semester. No extra credit is offered and tests have few questions so each point lost affects your grade greatly. He often goes off on tangents which are interesting but make preparing for tests difficult. Study guides aren't enough to be prepared for the tests so listen and take notes.

Professor Williams is super nice, but the final gradebook is 6 things, 4 being exams. The exams are also not long (like 10 questions), so each question is worth a TON - and the examen de repasos don't help much... Pay attention when he goes off tangents in class and WRITE IT DOWN! That is what he is going to test on, and there are no slides.

Professor Williams is such a sweet man, and this class aside, I really really liked him. However, he doesn't use slides and just expects you to remember everything. There are no assignments, just tests. Tests include random stuff we talked about once. If you don't already have a good foundation in linguistics, this will be very hard.

Professor Williams is a good professor, he relies a lot on the textbook which is where all his homeworks come from and the tests. He has examenes de repaso before each test that are pretty much exactly what the tests will be like. He gave us the option if we wanted the final to be comprehensive or not so that was super nice.

Professor Williams is awesome! The class material is challenging and there is quite a bit of reading, but he goes over everything so clearly in class that the test ends up feeling very doable. He is hilarious and makes class enjoyable.

He's a really great guy, but this class wasn't enjoyable. He keeps class entertaining, but also brags about how often students have reported him to the dean's office. He was pretty lenient on grading, but never was clear on what was on tests or how he chose the grading criteria. Honestly I'd take him again, but you gotta know what you're in for.

While I have no care or desire to learn any more about Spanish Linguistics, the professor at least made this class bearable. He is a funny and kind man who ranks among my favorite, if not the favorite, Spanish professor so far. Everyone should take a class with him ESPECIALLY to hear the best non-native Spanish ever recorded since the dawn of time.

Professor Williams is awesome! Really cares about helping students improve Spanish grammar. Tests are very fair and exactly the same format as the practice tests. Sometimes the midterms are open book, take-home as well! Easy A, and great professor. He is from Wales, has an awesome accent, and speaks the best Spanish of any nonnative I've ever met.

Great teacher. He is funny and provides a great class. Homework helps you understand the lecture which is correlated to the tests. Do the homework and listen to his commentary on it in class and you will do well!

Prof Williams actually seems like he knows what he's doing, unlike a lot of other Spanish professors I've had. 326 is a tough class, but Prof Williams really knows his stuff. Four exams that take 20 minutes each, all taken in class. They're heavily based off of the practice exams, so that's nice. But still, it's not an easy A. You gotta work for it

Professor Williams is nice but is an extremely tough grader. His assignments are based out of a textbook that's not very straightforward. Thankfully homework is graded only on completion. Exams are very hard to do well on. There are translation portions where he's looking for one specific answer out of many possible ones. Not a fan of his class.

Ive taken two classes from Professor Williams and have loved both experiences. His grading criteria are very, very clear and Ive never felt blindsided by any assignments. Very predictable workload and its okay to speak English in class. All Spanish students should take at least one class from him!

Wonderful professor to listen to (sweet Welsh accent). His lectures are usually interesting, but sometimes I have been bored by the material. Accessible and understanding. Two of our tests were take home, but he is not an easy grader. The class is predictable, which is nice.
Prof. Williams was very adaptable and cares a lot about his students.

4 total tests, he gave 2 as take home tests. They are pretty tough though. Gotta make sure you know the material front and back. Attendance is not mandatory, although he does take roll and you will be lost if you don't go. Do the homework before and study the study guide. Homework every class (32 assignments) but it's optional to do it. Expect a B.

I respect Prof Williams. He is knows a lot and wants you to understand the material. The problem is that there is SO MUCH material. I felt like I was drowning in all the concepts we covered. If you keep up with your homework and reading you'll be fine, but do it before class or you'll be totally lost. There's several papers, but they aren't hard.

This was a great class. Professor Wise is very knowledgeable in his field and he definitely knows his stuff when it comes to phonetics. Beware that this is one of the tougher Spanish classes. You will not pass by easily if you don't study.
Class was a little confusing, sometimes the way he responds to students  can pass by rude, i don't think he means it that way though.
Prof. Williams is the man!  I am dying to take another class from him.  He teaches VERY well and loves his students.  Take him for sure!

He is super good!!!  He wants everyone to do well, and he ensures that we understand the essentials.  If you want a class that is fun and you learn at the same time, take him.  His Welsh accent is the greatest, and he also speaks perfect Spanish (Castellano de Espana).

He is an amazing professor that really cares that the students learn.  He knows an incredible amount about the Spanish language and is more than willing to share it if he is asked.  The class is easy if you read, do the homework and ask questions when you don't understand.  I want to take another class from him!
Really knows the subject material and is a blast in class.  One of my favorite professors that I've had.

Bro. Williams just wants his students to learn, and you can learn a LOT from him.  He will talk after class and answer any questions you have.  NO BUSY WORK!  Tests are easy, but only if you read the book and come to every class.  Best teacher I have ever had (I have 135 credits at two universities).  He's Welsh, but his spanish is incredible.

He is probably my favorite professor that I have had here.  I loved his class.  He is a very nice guy and more than anything is worried about making sure that everyone learns...and so everyone does.  He doesn't throw in any extra busywork or anything else to try to make the class harder than it should be. If you take the time to learn, you do well
Great teacher.  I enjoyed re-learning Spanish grammar from him.  I was a little hesitant when I found out that he was from Wales, but his accent is amazing.  Highly recommend a class from him.

He rocks, he is from Wales so he has a hilarious British vocab, i laughed so hard that i cried on occasion in his class.  The only things graded are the tests and the essays, everything else is for participation.  Very easy and very fun, it was my favorite class!

It's very important to him that his students understand everything, and will take time to help each of them.  The classes are really fun also, but we still learn a whole lot.  Best Spanish teacher I've ever had!

I loved her. I have never had a better professor at BYU. She truly cares about her students and she is passionate about what she does. She sets up the class in a way that helps you remember what you've learned and pushes you to use what you are learning each day.
She is so great at making the class applicable to real-life. She is well-educated but also a working mom so she has a good balance between academics and understanding that school is not everything.

Dr. Kganetso is the best! There are 4 tests in the class and the lowest score is dropped. All the tests are open note and open book. This class is a lot of group work, but she gives plenty of time in class to complete the group assignments.

The class was great except for a couple of things. She only let you see assignments about a week ahead of time. Also there were group activities/projects during every single class, so if you don't like group work, this class is not for you.

Dr Kganetso is a gem! Great class for learning to apply knowledge to actually teaching. Basically the entire class is group work and discussion which was fantastic. Easy A as long as you put in the slightest effort. She is caring and willing to work with you. If you have to take this class, she is the right choice!

This class was challenging, however, Lawler provides all the materials to succeed. In the online class, the course is outlined very clearly and everything on the test is taught in the lessons. The TAs provide a review before each of the 4 midterms + Final. She allows a full front to back cheat sheet for each midterm and 4 in total for the final.

I loved Professor Lawler! I took Physical Science 100 for my General requirement during summer and she made it extremely possible to get an A even if you aren't 100% a lover of science. I really loved how much help she provided (practice exams, TA videos and hours, etc.) and she helped me when I was needing extra time on things.

Not sure how her ratings are as low as they are. I took her class online and she made it more than possible to get an A. Cheat sheets on tests, plenty of study practice and material, and TA reviews made exams doable. She is also a lovely person! Highly recommend taking this class from her.
This lab is run by the TAs and showing up and doing the work will guarantee you an A.

I'm an economics/business student and had a genuine in this material in the beginning. Then exams started. The workload consists of about 4-5 hours of online videos, and add. materials due each week. There are 4 midterms, one the week of finals, and a massive final. These tests consist of application questions that are incredibly hard and deceiving
Good online class, very straightforward and broad scope. Very well organized and lots of resources. TAs are always available and help prep for exams well.

There wasn't a lot of instruction. You basically just taught yourself everything and it was hard to get in contact with TA's. The exams are hard and half the time I felt like I have never heard of half the things even though I had read all the textbook chapters and stuff. There are 4 exam and a final and the last exam is the same week as finals.

I think online was the way to go for this class. Everything was due on Friday, so be sure to not procrastinate your stuff or you'll be stuck with everything all at once. Take good notes because you get a sheet to use on exams.

This class is well organized! I was not at all interested in STEM, but I found the concepts to be super simple and fascinating. She really knows to break it down and touch on the most important concepts without going too deep. I low key love science now because of her. It's not a hard class at all. You can have a page of notes during your tests.

This class was a mess. She talks a lot and likes to carry on, and that is reflected in her writing too. Every lab had pages and pages of confusing instructions, and the TA's never really knew what to do either.

If you aren't a stem major, online is the way to go. Dr Lawler has the course organized really well and gives plenty of things to help you succeed: extra credit, required TA check ins, multiple attempts on assignments, and note sheets on tests. I'm really glad I took this and recommend it to anyone!

This class might be my least favorite in all of BYU. It is not very clear what is expected of you. It's clear she hasn't given clear instruction to the TAs either and you will all be confused. Her grading scale makes no sense.  She'll make you stay in class even if you've finished your work early.

Prof. Lawler is kind and fun, and the course isn't too bad, though there are some difficult concepts every now and then. As long as you keep up with the readings and lessons, you should do just fine. The exams aren't very hard either, especially since the questions are very similar to the reading quizzes and you get to have a page of notes.

The only reason I did well in this class is because I took it online. There is a lot of material and the exams are extremely hard. There are 4 midterms and 1 final. The online version of PHY S 100 is easier than in person and I feel like the grading system is better. No labs which is nice, but go to the exam reviews.

Lady is very talkative, honestly too much. She keeps you after class sometimes. And just roasts you and your assignments if you do anything wrong… rarely shows up and the TAs really didn't even know what were going on half the time. Overall, bad class structure. But it was fairly easy in the sense that you can get a good grade pretty easily.

There isn't much interaction with Dr. Lawler as the class is run by TAs. Grades are greatly dependent on attendance but if you have a good lab group you should be just fine. Overall a fairly easy class.

If you have chill TAs and a good group you'll get an A. Dr. Lawler came in once every couple weeks and pestered us with questions that were beyond the scope of the class. She's a bit odd & can be condescending, but the class itself is super easy. Just beware, they can be nitpicky on lab reports but if you read instructions closely you'll be fine.

Super rude. I went into the TA lab and wasn't even talking to her and she came up to me and made me feel stupid for asking a question. She is really smart, but she comes off as condescending when you talk to her.

First of all, I'm so sorry if you have to take this lab under Lawler, may you find peace. Secondly, the lab wasn't terrible because I had the coolest TA's ever. If you get bad vibes switch lab sections ASAP because it'll make or break your grade. Lawler always had issues with everyone's experiment even thought she wrote the guide. Just meh yknow.

The class difficulty is a 4, but she is a 5 in difficulty as a professor. didn't interact w/ her all semester & the one time I did, she was extremely rude bc of her miscommunication & she doesn't even follow her own rules. love it when a professor tells a student that they are "annoyed" that a student is holding them accountable

I highly recommend taking the online version of PHY S 100 especially if you are a senior or even junior not majoring in STEM. You don't have labs to attend. All you have to do is read the textbook and do the online lessons and assignments, which are a majority in multiple choice form. Content can still be challenging. Tests allow 1-page cheat sheet
The class is pretty easy if you have good TAs which i did.  It's 2 hours a week and you need to be there.  If you do that you're basically gonna get an A

PS100 is the hardest class I have taken in 5 years at BYU. However, the flexibility of the online format helped, and Dr. Lawler was very kind and accommodating. She even removed late penalties for me a couple times. Tests are key in PS, but we were allowed one sheet of notes on exams which made a HUGE difference for me. Highly recommend Dr. Lawler

Dr. Lawler pretends that she is trying to help you learn to read and perform good experiments, and then does not do it. She does not teach, she criticizes students for not knowing things she didn't teach them, and she presents false data from unreliable sources on topics she has no expertise. She is a horrible professor. Do not take her courses.
I have only interacted 2 times with Dr. Lawler so far and both times she was extremely rude and condescending.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS ALL ONLINE—it was my biggest mistake. There's so much work, and you have to be super diligent to keep up. My TA was a harsh grader, and there were so many tests that were ridiculously hard. The TA reviews were helpful, but it didn't make up for how awful the class was. Worst class I've taken at BYU.

Dr. Lawler is a sweetheart, this is more on the TAs... If you hate your TAs (they are who run your class) or group (I liked my group), then you'll have a ROUGH semester. Our TAs were sooooooooooo lame. I did learn how to write a lab report, but boy did I hate peer reviewing so much. Not very good. No other way to take it, though. DO NOT MISS CLASS.

If you want to learn the "one true science" in a way that will make you feel dumb, this is the place for you. The TA's run the show, and usually do a okay job. Dr. Lawler kinda moseys around asking questions that don't make sense half the time and whipping out mathematical models meant for a 300 or 400 level class. 96% is an A.

Lab is totally run by the TAs which is good, they can be helpful. Lawler comes in every once in awhile to just harass the groups. Tells you that you're wrong, lets you know again that you're wrong, and again one more time, but doesn't care to tell you why. For a one credit class it's not worth to listen it so try to take with someone else.
Is not there for a lot of the times. When she is there, she will fire multiple questions at your experiment.
Take the lab from this professor if you hate yourself

You will rarely interact with Dr. Lawler.  The entire lab is run by TAs.  Look, this class is awful, but it isn't difficult.  An A is a 96 and the class average was a 95.99.  Show up, make a good group, divide tasks evenly, and this will be barely a blip in your semester

I never met Professor Lawler bc the lab is 100% run by the TA's. The class is about 90% group work in the form of essays and writeups. The grading criteria for the lab reports is not clear, so you get docked on tons small things. Become besties with the TAs because they are so helpful when writing the lab reports and getting full points.

Arguably the worst class offered by BYU. The course content was not relevant to my career path whatsoever so it was difficult to stay engaged, but Professor Lawler doesn't really help her case. There's a ridiculous amount of homework each week and there are four midterms with a comprehensive final. Find anyway possible to not have to this class.

Her practice exams are significantly easier than the actual exam.

I thought making the practice harder than the exam was common sense :'(

She's great! You have to work hard but its not too difficult to get an A. She does call people out for mistakes, but its not to embarrass anyone, its just to teach correct grammar. I enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

Hermana Williams is awesome. If you are looking for a fun Spanish class that will actually help you learn and practice then this is it. You have to do homework which is mostly just time consuming but it is necessary if you really want to learn. I studied quite a bit on my mission and I know Spanish well, but this class still teaches me.

I honestly learned a lot in her class. Showing up to class is super important and you do learn a lot. She moves fast has a Spanish accent(Spain) so beware of that. She jokes around quite a bit. If you study well, you will learn a lot and get a good grade. Homework is graded on effort and has an answer key. Her Test reviews are a great help.

The class is easy for those who learned spanish abroad, and with a little personal study you can get As on tests. But honestly Señora Willams doesn't explain the grammar concepts very clearly, so if you don't know those very well take someone else! She is hilarious however and allows the students to joke around and have fun in the class.

I didn't like her, she's very harsh. Only teaches off the powerpoints, coming to class was useless. I didn't feel comfortable going to her with questions because she wasn't very helpful in explaining, I learned more from my other friends in different sections. Def. wouldn't take again, most hated class all semester.

She was AMAZING! I've had very few professors who care as much as she does, and she really bent over backwards to help me with some stuff I missed when I got sick. She's the best professor to take it from. Also, she's really fun. Take it from her!

Hermana Williams is great. She explains concepts very simply and helps you to work out the kinks in your Spanish. The class is a good balance between being easy but also learning some more grammar details that you may not have known before. Highly recommend her for 321, she's super nice and a great teacher.

Professor Williams comes across as "strict" at the beginning, but she is hilarious, makes class interesting, and very fair and understanding. The class is very structured (all 321 classes do pretty much the same thing) so I would definitely recommend taking it from Prof. Williams--you won't be bored and the grading is very fair.

Hermana Williams is spectacular! She's funny, nice, and teaches extremely well. I'm not even an RM and this class was still great. It's super easy as long as you do the homework and study for the tests. Coming straight from High School Spanish can be a bit hard, but Hermana Williams helps you through it all. She's phenomenal!

This is a great class for RM's. I was the only non-RM in my class, so it was a little rough going from AP Spanish to this class, but Hermana Williams makes it clear what she expects and helps you succeed. There is a lot of homework (busy work) every night, and several lecturas to read. Do the work, study, and you'll be fine.

Professor Williams is the best professor I have ever had. She is hilarious and very clear. She tells you exactly what she expects and follows the syllabus perfectly. The class is ridiculously easy. If you don't get an A in this class then you either didn't try or you don't know basic Spanish.

Hermana Williams is awesome. Class was easy and fun sometimes. Helps to fine-tune your Spanish. I took the class having served stateside and the Spanish was no problem. She's a good teacher and good at explaining things.
Great professor. Great class. If you speak fluent Spanish, it's an easy A. Profesora Williams is the best! Super fun and entertaining class.

She is such a likable person, and she is so helpful whenever you need it. This is an easy class if you've mastered Spanish.  It is only about grammar, so you won't learn much about composition or conversation. You will just review (in-depth) the harder grammar concepts.

Professor Williams is incredible. She's strict and no-nonsense, but has a great sense of humor. Classes are engaging and she does require participation. She lives and dies by her syllabus, making this an extremely organized class, which is something I personally loved. Tests are easy as long as you pay attention in class.

This class was my favorite this semester. I love her! Very informative and helpful. She's got a touch of sass and a lot of Spanish pride, which fuel her funny side-commentary and witty personality. It was pretty straightforward and easy too. Overall a total slam-dunk.

GREAT professor. She knows her stuff! Mabel is super helpful, and explains concepts well. The class was professionally kept, but way fun, too. I barely studied and got an A because we discussed concepts in class until they were well understood.
She is great! More than learning lots of grammar, we had lots of fun. It was a very enjoyable experience.

I thought this class was a piece of cake, but I was surprised to find that other RMs struggled. I guess if you did language study and had native comps it'll be easy, otherwise maybe not. She's a native speaker so sometimes it was hard for her to explain concepts in a way that everyone could understand, but she keeps explaining until you get it.
She is an amazing teacher.  She wants each of her students to understand and will take her own time to help explain.  Two thumbs way up for her!
I loved her! partly because i served my mission in Spain, haha, but i found the tests and homework super easy and felt she explained the grammar concepts really well.
She is a great professor. She is really great at making sure you understand the material. She keeps everyone involved and knows how to be professional but fun.
No Comments

Do not take any class from him. His lectures are extremely boring and not helpful for the exams, there is way too much reading to be able to comprehend it all, and he is terrible at keeping up with emails/grades. The class was based more off him just rambling about certain things and his Spanish is very choppy.

This has been my least favorite class at BYU. The readings are not very engaging, and the lectures are worse. It takes forever for him to grade assignments and exams, so you don't really know how you are doing in the class till the very end. There is no way for you to make up points if you do end up doing poorly. Take it from a different professor.

He didn't get the first exam or any written assignments graded until the last week of class, but he offers no extra credit to make up points. Lectures are not super engaging, and the readings are worse. Nice guy, accessible outside of class, but definitely not my favorite. He doesn't offer feedback on anything. Take this class from someone else.

This guy is nice but crazy. You have 3 textbooks for the class and he assigns 10-30 pages of reading per week . Class is just a spoken summary of the readings but with little to no slides. My class started with15 kids and only 9 made it to the end. 4 of us got A's. He gives a final video project, a final news project, and a final exam. Avoid taking

I love Profe Wilson! This is literally my favorite class I have taken at BYU. Do the assignments and the readings, but the content itself isn't too bad. He'll give feedback and help you out with questions. His class isn't the easiest ever so not everyone's favorite, but I felt like all the assignments actually prepared for me the exams well.

Spanish 351. Lectures are unorganized and boring. He asks dense questions expecting a profound conversation from that question. He lacks passion for the content matter making it difficult to want to enjoy the class. Spanish literature from any professor has got to be incredibly boring, but professor Wilson takes boring to the next level.
He's cool, but this class was the worst. Boring as heck, has a bunch of readings, and he is a TOUGH grader.

Professor Wilson is my favorite professor. Some may claim that his lectures are boring. That's only true if you're not outgoing in his class. If you are willing to participate frequently and dive into the subjects addressed in class, you will look forward to going, just as I did. The final project is also extremely fun. I have no real complaints.

I absolutely loved Profe Wilson! He is funny, genuine, a good teacher, and helped me love Spanish culture. Yes, there is a lot of reading for the class, but if you do it and pay attention during the lecture, you can easily get an A. The class is extremely well organized and I learned so much. You will not regret taking from him!

Here's the thing, for this class, attendance is a must. Most of the information on the test will be covered extensively in class, often going over homework assignments. Unlike the others, I only had one end of year project and no papers. This class was on the easier end and one of the more interesting spanish classes I have taken. Would take again.

Dr Wilson is a nice guy, but I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND this class. The lectures were incredibly boring and dragged on forever. He required like 3 or 4 books, which would have cost me over $200 to rent or buy. I didn't buy them and just relied on lectures to learn what I needed to. got a B. So it wasn't too hard to get a good enough grade, just BORING

Span 455 - Dr. Wilson is a nice guy and he means well. He grades for grammar but not content, so I usually got As but no feedback. However, his Spanish isn't very good, his lectures are boring and lack structure. He used visuals twice in the entire semester. He asks you to buy - not rent, or go to the library - six textbooks. You read a ton.

Pretty strict professor but the class is honestly what you make of it. Very accessible outside of class and is a fair grader. Has high standards but I feel like my Spanish improved tremendously after his class. Lectures are important and the information will be on the tests so pay attention. Do your readings then come to class for clarification.

Please avoid this professor. He made me dislike the subject. He assigned a crazy amount of reading that is essential for tests. Strange assignments that don't facilitate learning. I missed many points because of super small grammar mistakes, never because of content. Grades participation in class. If you want to learn or an A take someone else.

I've never rated a professor before but after this terrible semester with this guy I want to warn anybody considering taking a class from him. Electronics Nazi. Too many writing assignments and too much reading. Bad, painfully boring lectures. He doesn't ask good questions in class discussions or on tests. 3 big projects requiring 10+ hours each.

He gives long, boring lectures and seems fairly uninvolved with his students' experience. There is lots to read, way too many assignments and on top of that he's a tough grader. However, he is passionate about what he teaches and speaks Spanish very well. I know I could have worked harder and been more positive but overall I don't recommend him.

His Spanish skills were amazing and I learned lots of meaningful things that I have used in other classes. Loved how he used many resources to teach us about different concepts of Latin-America. Passionate about his work. If you do the homework, and do not procrastinate the final project you'll be fine. Tests are mainly on the lectures.

There is a fine line between what is challenging and that it helps your learning. This professor takes it to a challenging level that doesn't allow learning. You end up being to preoccupied with cramming or pointless assignments that dont have anything to do with what you read in the textbook. He has work for you to do just to have you do work.

Very intelligent person, but not a great teacher. Lectures were very dry and hard to follow along with even when you'd done the reading. I wish he'd taught more in English because his personality actually shows through when he does. Not hard to pass but class is torture. Won't make you want to stand on your desk and say "Oh, captain my captain."

Profe Wilson is a decent teacher. Sometimes the lectures are a little dry because he just talks and doesn't use much of a PowerPoint or anything. He appears serious so it's hard to gauge his humor at times, but he is really nice and helpful. The final paper is graded pretty heavily, but the homework load is manageable and the tests were not bad.

He has great dry humor, exceptional language skills, and is passionate about the subject material especially when it concerns Southern Cone stuff. The final project was a research video documentary and it was FUN. His class is well organized and all the material is really fascinating. Go to his office hours, he's willing to chat and work with you.

I am about 1/3 of the way through the semester. He bothers me so much that I figured I should write a review before I forget to warn students thinking about taking his class. Take it from Prof. Sherman or another professor. Trust me. He makes the class stressful. Unclear about expectations. And you have a 10 page paper along with 3 exams. I'm done.

He loves literature and his Spanish is phenomenal. He is a good writer and teaches his students skills to improve their writing abilities. On the flipside, I feel  he cuts off students before they can properly respond to questions and he wasn't clear/unfair with reading quizzes- Slightly condescending.

The classes are interesting and Prof. Wilson speaks Spanish really well. The most frustrating part of the class was not getting feedback for assignments. He takes a long time to grade anything and it makes it hard to know how you are doing in the class.

Profe Wilson is really cool, smart, stylin'. and super hilarious at times. He speaks really good Spanish and his lectures were enjoyable. However, I was frustrated sometimes with the assignments. The instructions tended to be a little vague but he left feedback like they weren't and graded a little harshly.

Good person but annoying professor.  For example, he assigned two 90 min long documentaries to watch for 1 class period. He assigned over 15 essays, homework like crazy,  a ridiculous 10 min video presentation assignment,  etc, etc. NO ONE HAS TIME FOR ALL THIS!!! picky grader. I would NOT take him again. Treats students like they're dumb.

Prof Wilson is awesome.  Super laid back and just a cool dude.  You have to do a decent amount of reading but this class is not hard at all.  Just participate in class and do the readings and you'll be totally fine.  Lots of little assignments but they're not difficult at all.

Professor Wilson is a really nice guy and he speaks Spanish really well. A lot of times I felt a little bit unsure about what we were supposed to do for a lot of the assignments, and he grades everything really tough. Just get ready to do a lot of busy work for this class.

Prof Wilson is super cool.  Class is pretty laid back.  Just have to print off readings that aren't in the book--coming to class and class participation are everything.  Lots of little assignments but they really aren't difficult.  Great class that I would recommend to anyone.

Really enjoyed his class and his teaching. He gives you a lot of little assignment (at least one every week) and big readings, so he expects you to spend time working on his class. Readings are important for the tests and you cannot pass the class if you skip often. In general the class was not hard, but it was time consuming.

Prof. Wilson is good and bad. His Spanish is okay. As a class we all felt kind of left in the dark on assignments. His tests aren't hard but he is picky on essays. He does love what he teaches so that's good and if you go to his office he is more helpful. Class really wasn't that hard but it wasn't that enjoyable either.

I really liked Professor Wilson. It was sometimes hard to see the big picture, and you do have to keep up in class, but it was good overall. Professor Wilson is smart and funny, and the class is enjoyable. Also, he speaks phenomenal Spanish... I don't know what the person who wrote the review before me is talking about at all.

Can't really speak spanish. He messes up on basic grammatical principles I dont' know how he is a spanish professor. Never really knew what he wanted. Confusing and very dry. He makes poetry and literature even more boring than it already is. Don't take this class!!

Dr. Jacobson has been one of my favorite professors at BYU so far! This was her first semester teaching this course, and she did amazing. She always gave extra credit questions on quizzes and prepared you well for the exams. This course is difficult for sure, but Dr. Jacobson does everything she can to help out.

My favorite class at BYU so far. It involved reading an awesome textbook then attending awesome seminars. Each exam had both review slides and learning objective documents listing every topic that'd be on the exam, so you could always prepare for it well. Also, she's very nice. My advice: make flashcards!

Professor Jacobson was fantastic, especially as this was the first class she taught at BYU! There was a lot of content to go over, but Professor Jacobson wants to help you understand. You can tell she cares about her students and that she wants them to succeed. Tests were challenging, but she gave clear learning objectives to help study.

Fun class, can be rigorous, but if you stick to the recommended schedule she gives you, you should learn the material well. Also, lectures are interesting and she does a good job of explaining content. Tests are very fair and are consistent with the learning objectives she gives.

She is fantastic! She really cares about her students and makes success in this class achievable. She is a hard grader so be sure to not give anything half effort, she'll be able to tell!! She understands that this class isn't the most interesting content at first and does a lot to help us do well with writing the literature review.

Great professor, great course. Very well organized. Clear learning objectives that highlighted key parts of lectures and readings. Exam questions directly related to LOs. Very engaging, well prepared lecturer. Mixed lectures with practice questions and object lessons to help material stick. She was always willing to meet to help clarify content.

Nothing on the test was ever discussed in the lecture or office hours.Tests are badly written. There is no efficient way to study the test. Expect to take the test with knowledge of Biochem, anatomy,cellular biology,molecular biology and a test written by a disorganized new teacher.

Dr. Jacobson was open to both feedback from us and giving feedback to us.  If you stay on schedule, the work for the class is super manageable.  However, if you get behind, it can be really hard to catch back up.  Dr. Jacobson also really respects our time and us as people, so was willing to work with us for whatever we needed help with.

Dr. Jacobson was a great professor! Despite being new her class was very well organized and clear in what what expected of us. She was a tough grader so be sure to pay attention to the rubrics and even ask her for feedback before you submit, especially for the lit review. She's a great person that clearly really cared about students as people!

Dr. Jacobson was awesome! She's a new professor but she did an amazing job this semester and she was super encouraging. You can tell she loves BYU and wants to help all of her students. She was willing to answer questions and was very responsive to emails as well. Take Neuro316 with Dr J!!

She is amazing! So helpful with all of the questions, so relatable and makes the lectures and assignments fun and applicable. She is quick to help whenever needed and you can tell she is passionate about her job and here for student success. I am excited to hopefully take more classes from her in the future

Dr. Jacobson has been one of my favorite professors at BYU so far! This was her first semester teaching this course, and she did amazing. She always gave extra credit questions on quizzes and prepared you well for the exams. This course is difficult for sure, but Dr. Jacobson does everything she can to help out.

My favorite class at BYU so far. It involved reading an awesome textbook then attending awesome seminars. Each exam had both review slides and learning objective documents listing every topic that'd be on the exam, so you could always prepare for it well. Also, she's very nice. My advice: make flashcards!

She understands that this class isn't the most interesting content at first and does a lot to help us do well with writing the literature review.
