She's a great person that clearly really cared about students as people!

Dr. Jacobson was awesome! She's a new professor but she did an amazing job this semester and she was super encouraging. You can tell she loves BYU and wants to help all of her students. She was willing to answer questions and was very responsive to emails as well. Take Neuro316 with Dr J!!

She is amazing! So helpful with all of the questions, so relatable and makes the lectures and assignments fun and applicable. She is quick to help whenever needed and you can tell she is passionate about her job and here for student success. I am excited to hopefully take more classes from her in the future

Prof. Heward is easily one of the best religion professors I have had at BYU and makes class a lot of fun. Not a stressful workload at all; you have one chill assignment each week. This is how religion classes should be: feeling the spirit in class.

Brother Heward was very focused on spiritual development over grades, so the class was pretty easy (mostly completion based work). If you're looking for an easy A and some spiritual enlightenment, he is the professor for you, but if you want to learn the details of the restoration, probably look for a different professor.
Best religion professor ever!! Cares more about your learning and testimony growing than testing you.

I would recommend anyone take foundations of the restoration from him. His discussions of difficult topics regarding church history were respectful, thorough, and informative. He is hilarious while still keeping an overall spiritual tone in class. Although attendance was not required I still wanted to attend every class. Easy tests and assignments.
He is an amazing professor. There's weekly readings that are sometimes a lot to read but he picks out readings that are beneficial. His lectures are great because they are factual and spiritual.

Br. Heward is a really fun guy, and I enjoyed being in his class. I found the work for this class to be very manageable, though there is a lot of reading. This class has a lot of ground to cover, and I did occasionally feel like some questions I was looking forward to being answered were simplified or glazed over, despite his best efforts.

Brother Heward is so kind and knowledgeable! I loved going to class. Learned so much about the D&C this semester. Readings are very manageable and come straight from D&C. There is the same repeating assignment all semester. You just read 10 chapters each week and He shares deeper insights and context on them. Great teacher. Very diligent. No tests.

The professor is a great guy who clearly cares a lot about this stuff but is bad at teaching the class. Lectures would often get lost on some random tangent that had little to do with what we were supposed to be talking about. The assignments varied in terms of application to the class. Plus we had a final despite the class being project based.

The lectures were optional, but man, anyone who didn't go was really missing out. He did a great job of teaching and applying church history while discussing any sensitive subjects directly, but with care and understanding. He was great at answering questions and basing discussions on students' curiosity about the topics.

He's a really great guy and I can tell he worked hard to understand all this material and become a professor. He gives fun lectures and fills up the classtime with information. Something I will mention is that there's quite a bit of reading, but the assignments are easy except for the field trip to salt lake, so watch out for that.
Good guy. Cares about his students.

Bro. Heward is super caring and passionate! He knows every student by name. One assignment per week, 10 sections of D&C reading. Very manageable and a few other assignments to end the semester. Light class load. He does not teach from slides so his lectures were sometimes hard to follow.
Professor Heward really cares about his students! He takes the time to memorize every students naemes which makes you feel really valued. Hes awesome!
Super great professor, it's my second time taking one from him and have loved it. Highly recommend

Only one online test (final) and it's super low stakes. Explains concepts very thoughtfully and honestly, which strengthens testimony and respect for saints of the past. And he makes class a fun and inviting environment, learning everyone's names. Def take!

I liked hearing a lot of his stories, but we did go off topic a lot in the beginning of class. If he does go off topic and misses some topics, he will make up for it by either delaying the assignment he needed to talk about or getting rid of that assignment completely. He is pretty entertaining and engages a lot with the class.

This was the most dysfunctional course I have ever taken. We went weeks without being taught more than his storytelling of BYU football. When he did try to teach, it was only for a few minutes and did not follow the readings or any clear rubric criteria. The last weeks He tried to teach new material to justify giving us a final. Avoid this course.

Piece of cake. Most of your grade is just completion. That said, readings could be a bit lengthy. This class felt like seminary in college. There was just 1 exam— which was the final— worth 6% of your grade. Assignments weren't hard, and were rather enjoyable. He's disorganized and a bit vague with instructions but is fair, caring and Spirit-led.

Brother Heward was an amazing professor. He focused entirely on our testimonies and growing spiritually. He was very entertaining. The assignments didn't feel like busy work at all and I actually enjoyed them. There is a lot of reading but that's to be expected in a religion class. Overall, an easy class and I really enjoyed it.

Bro Heward made it seem like the class would be hard but I thought it was very reasonable. There's a fair amount of reading but not many assignments and they're pretty easy. He is a little disorganized so sometimes due dates got pushed back because he forgot about the assignment but you can really tell he cares and loves his students!

Class is a little harder than other religion classes, but good. Includes multiple papers and quite a bit of reading. A volunteer project too. Really faithful and testimony building discussions of hard topics.

I loved his lectures and the class in general. It wasn't what I initially expected for the class. He's very focused on learning about and approaching the issues from the perspectives of those who lived through the events, and he can tend to jump around a bit. Personally, I found this fun and I feel like I learned quite a bit.

Professor Heward demonstrated Christlike love for each student and even had all of our names memorized on the first day of class. He worked hard to foster a collaborative learning environment within his classroom. His knowledge of Church history is inspiring. I learned details I had never heard before, and everything was presented to build faith.

Was amazed by his passion and knowledge of the subject. He was personally inspirational and the course itself, while reading and lecture-heavy, was relatively simple to move through. Assignments aren't too difficult and are geared more towards personal growth. Could've been more organized, but I was impressed by his ability to help the students.

Don't worry about the comment on class organization—Dr. Heward already keeps things clear, and if he ever missed explaining an assignment, he pushes it to the next week. I really like his teaching style; the readings are engaging, and he explains topics through compelling stories and multiple perspectives.

I feel like I give teachers the benefit of the doubt and aren't hard on them, but he wasn't a great teacher. Not hard, but he didn't teach well. Went over random history details, not main topics, and got off topic so easily and took long pauses it was lowkey hard to listen to. I skipped many days even though I'm not the type because it was boring.

Overall an interesting professor but would not recommend to someone who wants the class to be organized from the beginning. Very clear that he knows a lot but lectures are a but all over the place, as well as due dates. Decent number of small papers/written assignments throughout the semester, 2 exams that only account for about 12% of your grade.
I loved this professor, if he taught other classes I would definitely take him again. He's a perfect mix of being incredibly knowledgable in his field and super chill.

Brother Heward was one of my favorite teachers I have had at BYU! I got a lot out of the class and he always made it engaging. There were assignments every once in a while but Brother Heward was always there to help. He wants you to succeed. 10/10 Would take again!!! If he taught other classes I would 100% take it!!

Great professor cause he dives into topics by looking at things at a personal level (i.e. with polgamy he focused on specific stories and personal problems, making the issues much more humanized). Also unlike most professor he's not a broken record and leads his classes by the spirit rather than just spitting information in your face. Loved it.

Sure he might be a little disorganized but Brother Heward is one of the most caring professors I've had. He cares so much about what he does. He covered sensitive topics very well and I learned a lot from his class. It was not difficult, just do the assignments and you'll be fine. A lot of reading and assignments for 2 credits, but not too hard.

Honestly, the C grade was my fault (I just got lazy at the end). If you want to take Seminary in college, this is your class! All the reviews that say this is a disorganized class are 100% true. Brother Heward cannot get all his ducks in a row to save his life, but other than that, I loved it! Truly a very great guy, and clearly knows his stuff.

Heward was an awful professor for me. He is incredibly disorganized. Most time was spend talking about what we should do for the assignments. I felt like his "lectures" held no real value and it felt more like we were babysitting a kid that wanted to tell random stories.

Would take again. Speaks to you as equal and is very caring. Has a decent amount of assignments, but dropped lots of them when he realized it might be too much. Seems pretty new, but he is totally on your side. Talks about difficult topics in an approachable way. Lectures are more like engaging stories. Will help you with assignments.

Don't get me wrong, Professor Heward is a great guy, but the amount of papers he has us write is insane. I have more work in this 2 credit class than a lot of the 3 credit classes I have taken in the past. He's super funny, inspirational, and engaging. If you want a fun professor at the expense of writing a lot of papers then this class is for you.

He is unorganized and there was not a clear goal of the class. We talked about assignments too much and yet, nobody knew what he required on anything. It seemed like he had never taught this class before. I wish I had dropped the class, but he didn't even publish the course until the add/drop deadline. Do not take if you actually want to learn.

Brother Heward was amazing! He connects so well with the students and is very motivational when he teaches. He also does very well at explaining church history and looking at the context of everything, helping us understand why things happened the way they did to the best of our ability.

I love Brother Heward!! He's such a great person and gives such good lessons. He talks about controversial stuff and he's never biased. He doesn't post a ton of what he teaches online, though, so going to class and taking some notes is really helpful for the tests. He makes study guides, and they're easy to fill out if you take notes.

He was very scatter brained and would forget to tell students about the assignments until the day before they were due. He would randomly delete assignments or change them. The material covered in class didn't relate to the material covered in the test. He was a fun teacher and loved to be connected to students but didn't teach well.

Bro. Heward is awesome, and this is a good class. One complaint: there were 7 assignments due that were associated with the final. A little cumbersome to have so much due on the last day of class. With a little planning you should be fine.
Foundations of the restoration was awful. Don't take this class. Heward is cool but I did not like the class.
Bro. Heward is an amazing teacher but even better person. Such a humble guy that is willing to get down into some aspects of Church History that not many do. Can't recommend him highly enough.

Brother Heward is a wonderful professor. He clearly is very passionate about religious history, and knows a lot. He does a very good job expressing complex or difficult ideas. There are a lot of readings, but they're generally interesting and helpful. Highly recommend his class!

His lectures and the reading were the most beneficial part of this class. I would for sure attend his lectures because he gives great insights and makes you think with a better perspective about people from the past.

Professor Maclane is the best religion teacher I have ever had. He is super funny and loves to use personal stories to emphasize the concepts. I was on the edge of my seat almost every class period because he was THAT engaging. 10/10. I would recommend him to anyone.

Brother Heward is a remarkable man and very fun to work with. Had some very connecting conversations with him and truly wants each student to excel in the classes and to learn fundamental principles. Very fun and entertaining classes. Would take his class any time. He has been my most favorite professor.

Brother Heward is an incredible professor! He teaches with such insight, reverence, and humility; he cares about his students' success. Course Content (Spring/Summer): readings, fact sheets, 1 paper, midterm/final on Learning Suite. I would HIGHLY recommend this professor! If you're looking for a meaningful, humorous religion course, take from him!

Brother Heward is the BEST religion professor at BYU. Although the course covers controversial topics, he thoughtfully prepares lectures and is always open to questions. He is funny, insightful, meaningful, and engaging. I wish I could take every religion class from him! TAKE CLASSES FROM HIM!!! You will LOVE it!

Brother Heward is an absolutely incredible professor. He is such an example to me and invites the spirit into his lectures. He is so good about relating doctrine clearly, and humbly. He has a great sense of humor and I truly looked forward to coming to his class. If you put in the work, you will do just fine in the class. He is great!!

Overall a great professor. Really awesome guy and is really funny. Tests aren't too bad. Is transparent about what will be on them. He is fair and really cares about his students. Sometimes tough to get ahold of outside of class though. Also has a lot of assigned readings for lecture, not quizzed on them but included in test.
Occasionally difficult to work with and get in touch with but overall a good class and teacher. Structures paper to help you do well on each of them.

Bro. Heward is awesome! He is so kind and cares about the success of his students. He is very humble and is open to suggestions about how to improve. There were only 4 papers, which didn't take up too much time, and there is a small pre-class quiz before every class period. Very manageable. One midterm, one final.

He is an amazing teacher and a great man. You will learn so much about church history and he brings a strong spirit. There are two tests given on learning suite, weekly readings, and a short paper due every two weeks. He just wants you to learn and grow and feel the spirit - so there aren't ridiculously tough assignments.

Prof. Heward was a good teacher. His lectures are kind of boring, but he can be weird and entertaining. There are two tests which are on learning suite and then a really easy 3 question quiz before each class period. There are 4 papers due throughout the semester, but they are all pretty easy and graded VERY easily. Take this class from him easy A.

Brother Heward is so passionate about the things he does, the class, his family and everything. He has such a strong testimony and is so inspirational. I loved attending his classes as a break from all my other hard classes.

Dr. Heward is a great guy! He gives you a fair workload, but it seems like busy work to me. He is extremely fair and generous. Go to his test reviews and you'll get an A on the tests. Easy A. Boring lecture. I skipped most classes. Tons of assigned reading!!

Brother Heward is very smart but can sometimes be very boring in lecture. The assignments and readings are easy if stayed on top of. Professor Heward is very understanding and willing to work with you.

Brother Heward is the BEST!! His class is super easy and as long as put in some effort you will easily get an A! Both the midterm and final are on learning suite which is always nice! However, even though the class is easy it isn't boring! Each class period was awesome! I always learned something new and definitely would take this class again!

Easy A. Learningsuite midterm and final. You have to turn in one large paper and several other small ones every other week. Assigns a ton of reading, but it is self reported. Lectures were pretty funny. Young professor still figuring stuff out, nice guy. Gives out extra credit and holds reviews. I hardly showed up the 2nd half, but still got an A.

Aw man, Brother Heward is great! He steers away from blindly accepting gospel teachings and let's his students think, ponder, and learn for themselves! He is very respectful when doubts and concerns are expressed and presents touchy topics methodically and effectively. Take him! You won't regret it.

Brother Heward is such an enlightening professor. His passion is tangible every day. There is a fact sheet every other week that is a summary of one of the two units of those two weeks. Two tests, and he gives reviews for both of them that are super helpful. The tests are on learning suite which is super nice. And then assigned reading before class

I LOVED taking 225 from Bro. Heward. Easy class. There is one assignment due every 2 units so a very fair work load and I actually enjoyed the assignments. Midterm was very easy and he gave a very helpful review beforehand. He is a very good teacher who cares about his students and wants this to be a spiritual experience. Highly recommend!
Professor Heward was awesome! One of the best religion classes I have taken at BYU so far! He is so kind and very willing to help anyone that needs help! The class was very easy and I learned a lot!

Bro. Heward is a fantastic teacher! His lectures are engaging, informative, and spiritual. I would highly recommend him to anyone! The assignment load is reasonable and he prepares you really really well for the tests.

Bro. Heward is a very good man. You can't help but to like him. This was his first semester teaching, so he had to figure things out. The midterm was hard, but the final was easier, I think that he adjusted. I think he will be a great teacher, and he is very willing to work with students, but I did fight hard for my A although little homework.
Brother Heward is amazing. Hes funny and spiritual and I enjoyed his class a ton. He is definitely the best religion teacher Ive had so far. Id totally recommend his class to anyone.

Brother Heward has been my favorite religion professor at BYU. He genuinely cares for all of his students and is very knowledgable about the restoration. He's super funny, but knows how to make class really spiritual. There's a decent amount of reading, but most of the time they're interesting articles. Definitely take his class if you can!!
Tough grader!

She is a great online teacher and very enthusiastic about the material, and as a result, the help she gives is usually very good and helpful. She is very knowledgeable about the course and takes part in chats.
Macy taught me not to be afraid of 51/50s or bugs crawling on the walls.
Professor Halladay definitely provided a good idea to how bangs should look. She's great... I don't remember the class, but it seems like she's good...
Amazing class, and Macy is awesome. Not as easy of a class as i thought, the blog gets annoying but still a worthwhile and pretty easy class.

macy is great. she definitely is helpful and makes me feel comfortable as a girl in the class. i have this strange desire to become the best that i can be around her and constantly have a craving for learning and passion guava smoothies. definitely a class worth taking

I am a little confused about what her actual role is in the class, but when she teaches it is a lot of fun and I learn a lot. The class is easy, the blog sometimes is annoying but over-all for a 2-credit class not bad. Macy is pretty understanding about late assignments and stuff.
Easy class. The songwriter's showcase is a good opportunity to give a performance. If you want to learn songwriting in a systematic and complete way, however, this class is not for you.

Stu is pretty cool. He is very knowledgeable about music and the music industry. The class focuses more on writing and completing songs than music theory or music production. I felt like a lot of people were more experienced than me, but I still enjoyed the class. I write songs as a hobby so it was nice to dedicate time to writing.

This class was great. He doesn't go super deep into music theory or the nitty gritty, rather he goes into the mindset and method of songwriting and what that looks like. If you've written music before, you'll find it easy. If not, it will be challenging, but worth it to learn something new.

Stu is super chill. He focuses more on actually writing songs with lyrics than on music composition or theory. His goal is for us to feel more comfortable writing songs and receiving feedback on how to improve them. We have to write 5 songs throughout the semester, and that's pretty much it. It's a super fun class, and I highly recommend it!

Sadly this class was not what I expected. I wanted to learn a bit of theory and structure for songs and how they're put together, but this class was little more than "you learn songwriting by writing songs, so go write songs" 5 times. It was easy, but I think the class failed to reach its potential for what you actually learn if you're new to this.

Stuart has to be one of my favorite musicians, as the lead singer and songwriter of Fictionist. I can't believe he teaches songwriting at BYU, so this class was a dream come true. He has a very open approach to songwriting ("there are many entry points to a song") and great ways to get ideas, like free writes. And he has a wacky sense of humor.

Stu is the coolest. Hilarious person and super duper easy class. He encourages you to explore what you can do as a songwriter and not be afraid of stepping out of your comfort zone. Awesome teacher, awesome class.

Professor Dresden understands that, for most people, WRTG150 is a GE credit and not the class they are most excited for, so she does a really good job at keeping the class simple yet enriching. She also makes it very easy to get feedback on papers by making a signup sheet for short appointments, which I really appreciated.

Prof. Dresden is by far my most favorite professor I've ever had. Other professors could learn a lot from her. I loved her class so much. She was very open and encouraged good, safe discussion on hard topics. This helped all of us to become better writers. I learned so much in her class and I'm so grateful I had her as a teacher. Take her class.

Professor Dresden changed my life! I took this class over Zoom and the lectures and discussions were always engaging. There were 3 papers and a final exam. If you sign up for a paper conference, you are almost guaranteed a good grade. I hate writing but I absolutely loved this class. Brownie points if you get her Harry Potter references!

Professor Dresden is a solid choice for writing 150. There were only 3 papers and class was mostly just fun little activities. She does conferences before each paper is due and gives you specific suggestions on your paper. If you don't like writing, Prof. Dresden is the way to go for this class.
She is a great professor but can be hard to reach outside of class. If you show up and do the work you will get an A.
Professor Dresden is honestly amazing. She cares about her students, and gives solid feedback! I learned a lot, and it was an easy class! 10/10 recommend

Prof. Dresden is awesome. Her classes are fun but also teach you a lot about writing. She is very caring and every time we had papers she will read the paper and provides feedback. Get advantage of her office hours, participate in class and work serious on you papers and you will get an A. Also make sure you have seen Harry Potters movies haha

Dresden is a wonderful professor! She seems pretty intimidating at first, but she is really easy to work with and super encouraging. She teaches the material really well. She doesn't put the grades in until pretty late, but she grades very fairly and is very clear about what she expects. Fairly easy A if you come to class and do what she asks!
Great teacher. Gets you through WRTG150 just fine.

As long as you can show that you've made improvement over the semester and are able to reflect on that, you'll do well in the course. The class is writing heavy (of course), but she splits up the papers well, making everything very manageable. Often times she even gives you the option for group work, which makes everything WAY easier.

I loved Dr. Dresden. You have three big papers, but she breaks it up and helps you every step of the way. She is funny, relatable, and teaches the content in an engaging way. I left this class feeling very prepared for writing in the rest of college.

She was great. She knows everyone in the class is not an English major. She has is structured so that it is an easy A if you make the changes in your paper she specified. Shes quirky and fun. Don't talk when she is. She was late getting papers back every time, which was frustrating because I couldn't learn from my mistakes. Easy A.

For a writing class it was very enjoyable. It makes it very clear what her expectations are and what she wants. She also goese through the writing process very throrougly, she breaks it down piece by piece so that you KNOW what you are doing. She wants you to you suceed. Just have to do some reading, writing and have a sense of humor.

She was the best writing teacher I have ever had. She was entertaining and funny and connected really well with the students. I used her office hours all the time and she helped me excel in my writing. She gave useful tips and told me directly what I needed to fix.
Dresden was awesome. Her classes were engaging and enlightening. She was very willing to work with students on essays. 10/10 would recommend.

Dr. Dre has become one of my very favorite people as well as professors here at BYU. She cares for her students and is seeking to give full marks on any assignment you do. Basically, just do you best, be good at applying feedback, and you'll do great in the class. Don't take it from anyone else!

She is an absolutely AMAZING professor. She is kind, funny, and a great teacher. This was my favorite class. I loved every single class period that I went to. She is very willing to help you with all of your assignments. I LOVED her as a professor!!!

Dr. Dresden is caring, clear, and very fair. She let us pick our essay topics. She let us do group work for the final essay, which is unheard of for normal WRTG150 professors. She really pushed us to be mindful writers, and she is an amazing professor. Her goal was to help us NOT HATE WRITING so she made class fun and applicable. She's the best!
She's incredible!! She really cares about the individual and wants only the best from each student. Definitely make use of her office hours if you want to do well in her class
A great professor, who has sculpted her own teaching style and it works!

Professor Dresden is awesome and super straightforward. She clearly explains what each paper should be like and when it is due. She grades you based on how you improve from paper to paper rather than your paper vs. a perfect one. Knowing this took a lot of pressure off because I really do not like writing.

Like everyone else, I did not want to take another writing course. But Prof Anderson makes it great. I ended up caring about this class WAY more because she helps you to learn and engage so well. She's a super nice grader, offers lots of extra credit, and is just the greatest ever. Show up and try and you'll get an A and have a great time.

I really enjoyed taking my writing class from Prof Anderson. It's a lot of writing (surprise), but the way she has the class structured makes it easy to not fall behind. She also has interesting prompts and allows a lot of freedom. I couldn't have asked for a better experience in a writing class, and I feel I gained skills I can use in the future.

Best Writing 150 Professor hands down. She cares for students and is very accommodating. The projects are great and not super time consuming. She sets us up for success in every unit. The final isn't super hard. She gives us all a mental health day we can take instead of going to one class during the semester.

Prof. Anderson was so kind and truly cared about her students. She was always willing to help and gives extra credit opportunities as well. She is incredibly understanding and cares more about your health and what you learn than your grade. She is a great teacher. The workload is very reasonable and spaced out.

Professor Anderson is amazing! She lets you rewrite your papers up to 100% if you wish to do better. There are 3 papers and 1 presentation for the course. For this class there is a certain page requirement she has to assign, but she gives you help and only requires you to write the minimum. I love her and she is always willing to help!

Professor Anderson was the sweetest! She always was willing to help and give feedback, and she offered extra credit. Participation is graded, but she does offer mental health extra credit. The assignments were very manageable.

Professor Anderson was great! Every paper/project was very well explained and planned out so that I never felt like I was cramming. Professor Anderson is super kind and caring and wants all students to succeed. She did some fun activities in lecture and made writing 150 a breeze. You will be graded for participation, but she offers mental health EC

Pro. Anderson does a great job presenting the material. She takes attendance and gives participation grades, but there are chances for extra credit. I didn't read the textbook and did just fine. There are 3 main projects/writing assignments, with some other busy work as well. Overall a great professor to get rid of the writing 150 requirement!

This professor was probably the easiest class I have had for a 300 level class. She was super chill and as long as you showed up to class and pretended to participate and pay attention you would get full credit. She really did care about us and wanted to see everyone succeed in her class. You also get extra credit for going to the writing center.

Prof. Anderson was great!  She's very fair and provides plenty of chances for extra credit. An A isn't hard to get IF you try hard on all of the assignments and do as much extra credit as she gives. The textbook is NOT fun to read so I didn't really read it and did fine without it lol. WRTG 150 is just a really hard class in general so be prepared!
She is super caring and down to earth and let us really explore different ways of writing, and gave me super good feedback that helped me to know how to improve and produce quality writing.

Prof Anderson is smart, caring, helpful and inspirational. It is important to show up to class (the class size is pretty small - 20ish students) and there are 3 main projects, including an 8-10 page research paper. If you turn everything in you will do well. LOTS of extra credit opportunities. VERY understanding of mental health, gives extensions!!

Like everyone else, I did not want to take another writing course. But Prof Anderson makes it great. I ended up caring about this class WAY more because she helps you to learn and engage so well. She's a super nice grader, offers lots of extra credit, and is just the greatest ever. Show up and try and you'll get an A and have a great time.

I really enjoyed taking my writing class from Prof Anderson. It's a lot of writing (surprise), but the way she has the class structured makes it easy to not fall behind. She also has interesting prompts and allows a lot of freedom. I couldn't have asked for a better experience in a writing class, and I feel I gained skills I can use in the future.

Best Writing 150 Professor hands down. She cares for students and is very accommodating. The projects are great and not super time consuming. She sets us up for success in every unit. The final isn't super hard. She gives us all a mental health day we can take instead of going to one class during the semester.

Prof. Anderson was so kind and truly cared about her students. She was always willing to help and gives extra credit opportunities as well. She is incredibly understanding and cares more about your health and what you learn than your grade. She is a great teacher. The workload is very reasonable and spaced out.

Professor Anderson is amazing! She lets you rewrite your papers up to 100% if you wish to do better. There are 3 papers and 1 presentation for the course. Super harsh on attendance. Not willing to work with students and lectures are pretty tedious.

Madeline was a very fun person to learn from. She is super funny and uses that to her advantage in lectures and discussions! The class was pretty discussion heavy, but it never felt like too much. The information was super interesting, and the workload was not bad at all. Def recommend learning from her if you can!

She's very understanding and has your best interest at heart. Her class wasn't very difficult, and very insightful. This class is designed for people who don't really know what they want to do in art, or are just interested as a hobby. But attendance is mandatory unless you chat with her first!

would not recommend. I took this class cause I wanted to become a better painter, and we did NOT learn anything about how to paint. we mostly did dumb seminar discussions where we talked about stuff like color (which is great, but doesn't teach us anything about how to paint). also, i spent around $350 on art supplies, as did everyone bc we had to

Dr. Steiner made a subject I didn't want to take 3x a week into a class I was glad I took. We broke down 7 books over the semester with a wide variety of assignments (essays, diagrams, discussion panels). Dr. Steiner's feedback did improve my writing. (I also felt somehow every other student in the class had taken ALL of her other offered classes.)

I had Dr. Steiner for 389. She is one of my favorite professors in the department. She is caring, smart, and genuine. Her classes require you to show up and give it your all, but as long as you communicate with her about expectations and stay on top of reading you won't need to worry about your grade. I learned so much from this class.

I would definitely recommend Professor Steiner for 293. She is very knowledgeable and passionate, and she has very interesting thoughts and questions for discussions. I discovered my love for late American poetry. She is kind of particular in grading written work, but not too badly, and she'll give good feedback that shows what she's looking for.

Such an amazing professor and human being. She is so passionate and knowledgeable about everything she discusses in class, whether it be class content or personal issues. She invites the spirit without being pushy or uncomfortable. Would 100% recommend her for any English class.
She is amazing! Normally not a fan of English classes but I loved her class! 10/10 take again.

I am in love with this woman. She is incredibly compassionate and smart and an AMAZING teacher. She tends to think her class is the most important thing in your world, but to be fair, I did feel changed by it. The amount of writing and reading was tough and it required my whole soul. She gives great, specific feedback and also welcomes feedback.

Dr. Steiner is always willing to discuss the concepts of her classes in depth and really dig into the material. She is an extremely kind and knowledgeable teacher that has a clear organization and goes the extra mile to prepare you for class. If you do the readings and come prepared then you'll enjoy the class. Wants to see you succeed in class.

I really enjoyed taking her class. She is really loose with her class schedule, so if something isn't covered, it will either be pushed back or completely removed. She provides any books in the syllabus that are harder to get ahold of, which was really nice. She said she won't accept late work, but she does if you're reasonable about it.

It's hard to get away with not doing the reading before class because there are a lot of discussions. She chooses course materials and assignments with a lot of thought and care, so though it may be hard, it will be worth it. Read assignment descriptions thoroughly and make sure to hit all the points. Participate and you will have fun.

Dr. Steiner is a fantastic teacher who I had for ENGL 203. She gives a reasonable amount of homework and her tests are easy with the amount of preparation she gives. She is a very personable teacher who really wants her students to succeed. She was accommodating, insightful, and kind. Would definitely take any of her other classes.

Dr. Steiner is a very reasonable, kind and interesting professor. She made the content interesting and personal, and it's clear she is really passionate about what she teaches. There are a lot of assignments in the class, but they are reasonable and help in learning the class material. Would 100% take another class from Dr. Steiner.

Very kind and sweet. She was very accommodating for the situation I was in. There is a lot of reading in the class, but thats to be expected from a English literary history survey course. She provided a study guide with what was going to be on the test. Greg teacher. Would take another class from her.

Professor Steiner is a force to be reckoned with. She has a brilliant mind and a calm demeanor mixed with a good amount of humor that pulls you into her lectures. You'll want to pay attention during class and know that papers are the bulk of your grade so pace yourself and meet with her for feedback throughout the process. Fabulous class.

She's a relatively new professor but has extensive experience and education. You can tell she's still figuring out her teaching style and confidence in the classroom, but she also asks good questions and designs intentional assignments.

Professor Millett is amazing! This is one of my favorite classes I took for my major. She is very respectful and will work with you and be accommodating. I love the way she makes her reading assignments and she gives you study guides for each reading so you know what to pay attention to. Lectures are awesome and I would take from her again.

This is a pretty easy, but interesting class. Lots of good class discussion. Only one big writing assignment. Easy midterms if you study. Dr. Millet is very merciful and accomodating. Class is organized and easy to follow. I'd take again from her.

She's awesome. So kind and willing to help however she can. It was a super engaging class! The majority of assignments involved interviewing an adolescent and volunteering with them. Would highly recommend this course to anyone. Super lax, but you learn a lot!

Dr. Millett is amazing!! She's super professional but humble and willing to work with you if you have things come up. She is a great lecturer and assigns a lot of smaller homework assignments which is super helpful for your grade. Discussions were interesting and she is really knowledgeable. This was my favorite class this semester!

I love her!! She is so clear with what she teaches, easy to understand and remember, and clear with her expectations. She is a newer teacher and is very humble while still being reasonable and holding boundaries. She is so consistent and makes it so easy to succeed. 10 hours of voluteering with adolescence is required a semester.

My favorite quote from professor Hughes is "don't worry, there won't be any programming in this class." The class is easy so take it for a free A, but expect to have your time wasted on low level arts and crafts projects. If you're hoping to get a job after college this class isn't going to help you. A complete waste of everyone's time and money.

The professor can't teach, has no industry experience, and has no concept on what the industry needs you to learn. This won't prepare you for a job and is massive waste of time. Take this class from a different professor.

It's 2 years since I graduated and started working in the industry. To this day this class is my go to example for how school fails to prepare you for industry. Amanda was the worst teacher I ever had. She lacks real world experience. Don't waste your time, take a class that teaches you engineering instead of how to make cardboard prototypes.
Glorified arts and crafts class in a sense. Very easy.
I loved this class from Dr. Hughes! We learned lots of great topics in design and building a user experience. We learned different prototyping methods and the projects were great!

Professor Hughes was a great teacher. It was a fun class with some fun labs. She knows her stuff and has a very good eye for design and will give good feedback for your projects. She's nice and has a sort of mom sense of humor and is always willing to help. The lectures aren't boring and uses a lot of questions/surveys to facilitate discussion.

She means really well, but lectures are sometimes copy/pasted from the readings. Attendance is required for credit, which is a joke because you could sleep through class and get the same amount of information, being nothing. She's very nice and you can tell she likes what she's talking about, but she's not a great teacher.

Kind, funny, and understanding. Three tests, weekly lab, and weekly reading w/ required notes. TA grades everything. Content was new and informative, but much overlapped with prior classes. Not sure how I'd have succeeded without that background—some exam questions covered material I don't recall being taught in this specific class.

Dr. Christensen is nice, funny and knowledgable. She is a great professor. However her TA this semester was terrible. A strict grader with no empathy at all and poor explanations for grades. I've never had to write a negative review but this TA made me furious. Great professor though.

I loved this class with Dr. Christensen. As others have said there are a few quizzes, labs (done during class time), a semester long project (but it is spaced out so it's not bad!), a few readings/discussion boards, and tests. A good grade is very achievable! Plus Dr. Christensen is funny and cares about her students. Would 100% recommend!

I really liked Dr. Christensen! There were a few exams on LS and a semester long project, but nothing too crazy or difficult. Both her and her TA respond to emails quickly, and her lectures are easy to follow (especially with the "exercise snack" breaks in the middle). 100% recommend this class to fill your EXSC elective credit.

Mandy is great, I enjoy the way she teaches this class. Not excessive with the workload, encourages good real-life application, a decent amount of group work - but not the kind where your grade depends on others. no complaints

This is a great class if you are trying to fulfill that requirement for exercise science. Tests were low stress on Learning Suite but they were slightly more challenging than I expected. Definitely take this class you will probably learn something and earn a very doable A.

Dr. Christensen is a good, engaging teacher. I enjoyed her lectures because she is funny, teaches clearly, and interacts with students a lot. Study the slides, quizzes, and in-class worksheets for tests. The final is NOT comprehensive. For all other assignments, she is an easy grader. There is a semester long project that is not too difficult.

She was my internship supervisor, pretty chill. Got 100% on every assignment. You just gotta write a little paper every couple weeks, and literally nothing else. Never talked to the woman, so idk if she's a good teacher but she gave me an A+ so I like her.

Pro. Christensen was my supervisor for an internship I did so there wasn't much class time. Just had to turn in a weekly paper reflecting on my internship each week and the TA would grade it. Never really interacted with Pro. Christensen except for one group zoom call at the beginning of the semester. Internship is pretty independent which is nice.

I really did not enjoy this professor. She basically just teaches off of the ppt slides and doesnt explain further then the info presented. But, in the tests, youre asked way more in-depth questions. Also, theres 3 finals, and a midterm. It was way more stress than I expected for a two credit class.

She is a very nice lady. The class has some really good information that comes from the ACSM Exercise Physiologist Textbook. Lectures are pretty boring, and I was able to study all of the information from the PowerPoint slides for the tests, so I stopped going to class. Good for an easy A, and good info if you're interested in Ex Phys Cert.

Profesor Garcia's class was not at all overwhelming or difficult. There are readings before every class and sometimes the lectures are heavy and boring although it wasn't anything that was too difficult. There are couple larger assignments that take more time so get started on them early. She is a very forgiving and easy grader!

Profe García is sweet & really cares about what she's teaching, but the class is poorly structured. Lectures are incredibly long and dull and don't plan on getting thorough notes from the slides. Occasional pop quizzes on the readings. Midterms are difficult to understand because of poor formatting and are heavy on written responses. Attend class!!

don't listen to the other reviews. she gives you plenty of opportunities to participate and if it seems like she doesn't, it's only because no one is participating. she is so sweet and wants you to succeed. she will always grade on the side of the student. super accessible outside of class. def take this class from her

I would take this class from someone else. She will just put a powerpoint on and read straight from it. There's no discussion or engagement outside of her asking you to read a part. Her exams are poorly formatted and it is never made clear what she wants you to know for them. She expects you to participate but rarely gives opportunities to.

I wouldn't recommend this class. Lectures are hard to sit through and follow—she speeds through text-heavy slides with little explanation or interaction. There's almost no discussion or active learning, just reading slides aloud. Study guides are unclear, and though she grades easily, it doesn't make up for the poor instruction.

I feel that she was just very disorganized. I never truly understood how to prepare for exams except go to class and memorize a bunch of things that ended up being only like 5% of the exam. I feel like if she was more organized and I knew what I was supposed to be getting from lectures I would have enjoyed her class a lot more.

Honestly she is great. She is a very easy grader and very nice. Homework is mostly readings and unless you have a quiz that day, you are fine to not always do them. Tests/instructions are a little questionable but she grades so easy that it doesn't matter. Just go to class and you're totally fine. I honestly really like her and would take her again

This class was the reason I decided to drop my minor in Spanish. Lectures were long and boring, but your grade will take a hit if you don't go. The class was suuuper unorganized and I have never seen a worse layout for exams. Take span 330 from anyone else.

Oh boy, this class was terrible. She was kind and graded relatively easily, but her easy grading hardly made up for her unclear tests and lack of instructions. The tests on learning suite were formatted terribly and make up 60% of your final grade. Attendance was required but almost impossible with how mind numbingly boring the classes were.

The worst class ive ever taken in my life. Her course is unorganized, dry, ineffective, boring, and overall a waste of my time. The only positive is I could finish my other class homework while she droned on for an hour about who knows what. Please save your soul and dont take her.

Dr. Garcia is clearly very knowledgable and passionate about her subject, but her course isn't very well organized. Tests are poorly worded and lectures aren't very engaging. If you participate and go to office hours she's very accommodating. It's definitely an easy A if you show up and comment a few times per class period.

Dr. Garcia is wonderful. Her lectures are extremely dry but very helpful--as long as you jot down what she talks about, you'll do well on exams. She is a /very/ easy grader. She's also quick to reply to emails. Not the most fascinating class I've ever taken but I'd take a class from her again in a heartbeat considering how relatively easy it was

The class structure was not my fave. Very disorganized and at times confusing/unclear grading criteria. She lectures mainly by reading straight from the slides. She is very caring and kind, and the class is fairly easy, but there's a lot of material covered and it can feel overwhelming at times.

Honestly just a super disorganized and confusing class. It was really hard to pay attention in lectures, very boring. Hard to know what to study for tests, but she grades easy. Papers and other projects were very ambiguous and had no rubric or expectations. Prof Garcia is a very kind lady, just find someone else to take 330 from haha

Professor García teaches a great class! If you go to class, read some poems, and turn in assignments you'll be fine. She cares more that you try to complete the work than if your thoughts are ground-breaking and original.

Lecture heavy. The online class was two hours every other day and those two hours were full of powerpoints and lectures. If you don't like to participate, this is your class. You can comment every once in a while and zone out. However, that makes tests difficult. LOTS of reading every night- the material will be on your tests.

I have never been so bored in class. Guys, never. S I even liked the readings, they were interesting, though odd but lectures were tiring. One point in her favor, I had a B in the class but I got a 93 on the final, and she surprised me with that as my final grade. ��

This class obviously requires a lot of reading, but Professora Garcia is a super easy grader. If you do the assignments and try a little, you will get a 100. Lectures can be long and boring but it's a really doable class. Just make sure you go to class (she takes attendance and it ends up being part of your final exam grade) and take notes!

Her lectures were honestly painful to sit through, especially online, but she really does try. The material just isn't interesting. Very few assignments and are almost guaranteed to get a 100% on them if you complete them. Tests were proctored on LS and the worst format I've ever seen, but not too hard I suppose. Pretty easy, sparknotes everything

I had high hopes for this class but was sorely disappointed. Lectures were sleep-inducing yet way too fast, and she would never post slides on Learning Suite afterwards. I never knew what was going on, and there were so many assignments with unclear grading criteria. Very smart lady, but not a great teacher. Take this class from someone else.

She grades really easy and will tell you if there will be a quiz. She gives exam study guides that are basically the exam, study them really well and you'll do great. She goes very fast in lectures, and doesn't post her slides, take notes and compare with classmates before the exam, read the material as much as you can if you miss take good notes.

She can be a bit dry in her lectures but I still learned a lot from her. Her class was very EASY, it gave me a break in the middle of the day. She assigns two papers (she's not a hard grader) for two short books. you will read a couple short stories before class and then analyze them in class. She's a very nice lady, is super chill; an easy A

She is a super sweet lady. The class was pretty boring, but she cares and is literally the easiest grader of all time. For a 400 level class, it's a breeze. Workload and reading was very reasonable. Never anything to cry about. Occasional pop quiz to beware of. We had a fun day to recite poems.
This was the easiest Spanish class that I have taken a BYU, if you go to lecture and pay attention you'll get an A.

Look, she is a great person and loves what she teaches, but class is so boring but it's not bad if you get into it. The one thing that gets me is that no one has any idea what is going on, when things are due, what to study for tests, and it doesn't seem like she does either. I am taking this for my language certificate. It was worth it, barley...

Sitting in class is miserable, and you have to attend to get credit. worse 50 minutes of your day. She is a tough grader when it comes to tests. 3 total tests, one take home, the other two nobody knew what to study because she didn't give a study guide. She is smart, but nobody could care less about what she's teaching. Beware.

Look at the reviews. The tests are not too hard, but class is dreadful. There is a very low level of interest-she is really dry and boring. If you like literature, don't take this class, it will help you to not like reading anymore. We never had fun in lecture-no videos, nothing. I wouldn't recommend her as a professor as there are better options.

If you like literature, don't take this class. She will ruin it for you. If she can turn something I love into something I dread, she will do it. Her lectures are very boring and dry. Don't expect to have fun or enjoy lecture. It is pure lecture. I wouldn't really recommend her as a professor, you can easily do well, but it isn't worth it.

This class is ridiculous. She is passionate about literature, not as much about civ, which was disappointing because it is a civ class.  There is a ton of reading and several assignments. The reading takes time to understand, and you have to be prepared for random reading quizzes.  If you like powerpoints, this class is for you. I found it boring.

There is a lot of reading to do.  I found many of them difficult to understand and/or follow. Be prepared to spend lots of time on the readings, and read them before class. Attendance required with lots of class discussion. I was disappointed in her personableness...sort of non-existent. You've got to love the material almost as much as she does.

Do as she says, follow her instructions as perfect as you can and you will be fine. She is very passionate about her stuff, don't mess with her. She teaches as if she was in South America, so you must behave in class(No eating no talking). She is harsh on papers. I learned a ton, if your Spanish is rusty she helps a lot. You can get an A, I did.

She is a pretty cool teacher, all things considered. She is very dry and doesn't mess around at all. If you love literature and discussing it, she is good to take but if you start contradicting her ideas, watch out. She's good at what she does and makes class relatively challenging.

Killpack is simply fantastic. I would probably take him for every class if I could. As for controls, the class is tough, but worth it because of how cool it is. If you have time in your schedule it is worth it.

Dr. Killpack is absolutely one of the best professors at BYU. He's kind, understanding, and genuinely gets excited about the material. He's also incredibly humble and always invites suggestions on how he can improve.  Don't get me wrong, the class is really hard, but Dr. Killpack makes things as simple and doable for students as possible.

He's the most relatable and caring ME professor I've ever worked with. Wants you to learn something and wants it to be useful to you. Just wants proof that you've learned something. Gives a completely fair chance on tests and hw. Open note mostly no time limit or well over enough time allotted. I was excited to go to class because of his lectures.

Best capstone coach ever. He is one of the best professors you will have at BYU. There aren't many professors that you will consider a friend after taking their class, but he is one of them. He's very intelligent and an easy recommend.

Dr. Killpack is a great, sincere guy. He's very helpful outside of class and treats everyone very respectfully. He understands students. Tests aren't easy, but they are interesting. He gives a few extra credit opportunities and did curve things a little at the end of the semester.

Favorite professor at BYU. Lectures were engaging every time, doesn't teach from a pedestal but as a peer. Very good at explaining in class. Tests were hard but doable. You can really tell he cares about the class and wants us to succeed.

He cares a lot about his students and obviously enjoys engineering a lot. Lectures are engaging and if you see him during office hours he's incredibly helpful (much more so than TA's). Homework is moderate, tests are really hard. Overall a great professor though.

Killpack is a great guy/very reasonable. However, his tests were also very hard and his lectures somewhat dull (it's hard to make engineering measurements interesting). That said, he does his best and really cares about you and you're learning experience. ME362?  Be prepared for long homeworks, group lab projects, and more fun than you can handle.
Best french teacher I've ever had. He is so funny and keeps class super engaging. I learned and laughed a lot.

This class is difficult by nature but Dr. Olivier makes it as engaging and manageable as possible. His expectations are really clear and he allows a lot of help on assignments (using the writing center and allowing retakes). There is a lot of reading because it is a literature class. This was one of my favorite French classes.
Professor Olivier is awesome! He knows a ton about film and the class was a super fun environment. The assignments are super chill and the final project was really easy. I'd highly recommend.

Professor Olivier really made international cinema more accessible for me. I came into the class as a rank novice and left feeling confident about my ability to analyze film. He was extremely flexible on assignment due dates. Very grateful for this man and his unique perspective; definitely take this class from him if you get the chance.
There's a lot to do to keep up in this class, but Prof. Olivier was one the best profs I have had. He was knowledgeable and helpful, and also understanding and flexible with tests and deadlines.

Love him. I really struggled at the beginning because I came from French 4 in high school. But he was understanding and willing to work with me. I progressed more in French in his class than in a couple years in high school. He is very down-to-earth and relatable and taught me so many things in addition to French. I'm so glad I stuck through it.

I loved going to class. Prof Olivier was hilarious and caring. . I would definitely recommend his class. All the other Profs in the French department do grammar tests, but his are just essays. If you talk to him he is super willing to make things work for your grade.

Prof. Olivier is the best. He really cares about his students and is an amazing professor. I wish I could take another class with him. He explains the material very well and his lectures are entertaining.

Professor Olivier is a great teacher. He is passionate about the subject and gives great lectures, but doesn't ask too much participation during them. He was good at giving positive feedback on assignments and presentations. He's very respectful, too. This class requires a lot of reading, but Olivier made it fun and interesting.

This was a fairly easy class. I really like him as a person, and I feel that he's a good teacher. I do feel like he gets off on tangents easily, and I would have preferred if we didn't switch into english as often as we did, but I guess that's just personal preference. A good guy, and a solid teacher. He's a solid choice for a french teacher.

Prof. Olivier is a true gem. He makes class exciting every day, and he helps us understand why French literature should be important. He's super nice! The class isn't too bad, just a lot of reading and reading quizzes. There are four papers, three unit tests, and five grammar tests. I really enjoyed my time in his class and I'm sure you will too.

He's one of my favorite professors. He's a super chill, funny guy, but he's also a really good teacher. He wrote the whole curriculum for French 202, and he put all of it online because he's a true homie and isn't trying to make us broke college kids pay for textbooks. (He also has some cool clothes ask him about it.)
Class was never boring. He has had such an interesting laugh and has a way of keeping everyone engaged. Possibly the most likable guy you'll ever meet.

Professor Olivier was one of my favorite professors I had this semester. I was nervous going into the class; I was a first-semester freshman who had taken AP French, but I wasn't really sure what to expect out of a college course. On the first day I was a little intimidated, but I decided to stick with it and I am so glad I did.

He's awesome! He teaches French literature in ways that make you feel like you're actually going to use the material in real life, rather than just memorizing things for a test. He explains really well and his lectures are hilarious. Absolutely would take from him again.

Marc Olivier is a great teacher. He is a super nice guy, and is really interesting to listen to. He wrote the textbook for French 202 and gives it to his students for free. He is probably my favorite professor at BYU. If you can take a class from him, I would suggest you do it.

I absolutely adore him. I have learned so much in his class. He is so intelligent and funny and presents material in a very interesting way. I have been taking French classes for years, and no teacher I've ever had teaches grammar better than he does. If you leave the BYU French program having not taken his class, you are surely missing out.

Great! French literature is hard but he really focuses on techniques to help you get through the readings wout getting frustrated. He's helpful, good at explaining and analyzing, reasonable, friendly, and laid back. If you're not interested in lit and history I would definitely take it from Olivier. Not to mention he wrote the (free) textbook.

He's a great teacher! Tons of energy and he loves what he teaches. Only thing is…I kind of wish he would take a little more care with his wardrobe. For someone who is in and out of Paris, he wears a lot of jeans. Not that that's relevant to his teaching…but just a thought.

I didn't like 201, but Prof Olivier's 202 class made me interested in French again. He's got a great sense of humor and he really knows how to explain both literature and grammar. All the other teachers use his material, so I'm glad I got to take the class from the guy who wrote the book (which is online and FREE!) Awesome class!

Prof Olivier is the best. The class is very organized and easy for those who are willing to study and do the readings. You have to read a chapter online before each class and then there is a quiz on each chapter online after class. The material is great, the teacher is hilarious!! This class was awesome.
I loved Olivier's class. He expalined concepts that I had before found confusing in a very clear way. I would definitely take  him again.

This was the first time he taught his photography class and it was amazing! I loved the freedom we had to learn when we didn't have to focus on tests, instead we got to show what we learned through photo-essays. it was an excellent class and I really hope he teaches it again because it was awesome!
Easily the best class I've taken at BYU. You learn a lot, but the class is still easy. He's pretty funny too.

I loved this class!  Don't get me wrong, it wasn't terribly easy and I worried about tests and such, but Prof. Olivier was an awesome teacher!   202 was perfect for learning a bit  about classic French literature, and you can tell that Olivier likes the material and wants to see you succeed and love it too!

Ok, I absolutely HATED every semester of French previous to this. I was just plowing through for my English major...have..to get...through...Grrr! [insert tearing out hair here]. But in this class I've felt like knowing French actually has some uses, and I'm not a complete French moron. He's a great teacher and wants you to enjoy French literature.

If you are thinking of taking 202 from anyone else then you are an idiot! He is a wonderful teacher--amazingly good. No textbook (all online and really cool and interactive too boot). He isn't "super easy" but if you try you will do well (drops lowest quiz score). He dresses like a normal professor I don't understand those other comments here.

He is a fantastic teacher; he explains difficult concepts so well and helps the students understand a lot of stuff about French culture. All the 202 reading is online, so the only required text is super cheap! He is amazing!

He is awesome! Thank goodness I took his class. He is so much more fun and clear than any other French professor. He is entertaining but also makes connections in a way that I totally get. Not to mention the entire class is online and therefore free. No Textbook!!! Don't take 202 from anyone else!!

The most amazing teacher I have ever had. He's fun, entertaining, and he teaches well. I would arrange my schedule to take classes from him whenever possible. I've had 4 classes from him, and they were all fantastic. J'heart Paris!

Oh my gosh. He was the greatest teacher ever, not to mention the fact that he dressed well.  His classes allow you to learn a lot about the subject, but in a way that you will remember and possibly even find useful in the future.  Of course, it does help that he's easy on the eyes.  He has some truly awesome shoes.  Gotta love that hair...
He is a really funny teacher, but he also gets to the point. He dresses so awesome dude
This class was freaking awesome.  I learned a ton about the basics of French lit, but we still got out of class way early almost every day.  If you have to take 202, take it from him.

Quite possibly the best professor at BYU. He's helpful, polite, and teaches IN ENGLISH when it's easier (most of the time). On top of that, he's hilarious!  The class is fairly easy, but don't let that fool you - you LEARN more in his class than most others.  I'd take him again if he taught any more classes I need.  Don't hesitate - enroll today!

<<Les belles fringues d'aujourd'hui seront les "sweater-vest" de demain!>> -Hippolito;  Great prof, great style, knows his stuff.  However, if you don't like groupwork or lime green "lava lounge" shirts, alors... fais gaffe!
Great professor, hysterical, good dresser and so much fun.  His tests are fair and is knows what he's talking about.  Great class, great prof.

Olivier is a great guy, fun dresser, but his class wasn't my style. Lots of group-work-ish stuff. It was an easy enough class, though, and I can't say olivier doesn't do what he can to make it fun. Some people might prefer a more conventional class.

This is one of the coolest teachers I have ever had. He is very fair and makes class and learning fun. He's a great dresser, but I think it's unfair to say that he judges his students on thier appearances. I highly recommend him....I would take another class from him any day.

He's a good teacher--funny, smart, organized etc.  But I felt like he judges your appearance.  Most BYU professors dress like its 1987 still.  He is so in style though that you wonder what he thinks of your clothes.  Go to Paris and get a new wardrobe first or you'll be invisible in his eyes.
This class was interesting, easy, fun, infomative, laidback, and engaging. The online lessons are excellent, and Professor Olivier is hilarious. This was my favorite class Ive taken at BYU so far.

The class is a lot of work,  but Dr. Olivier is very approachable and keeps things interesting. Don't expect to learn lots of details about history, this class is made more for you to think and write, not learn what was going on in such and such presidency of the 4th Republic.

I didn't know what to expect at first, but I loved the class. He has a way more interesting approach to history than other classes. He actually makes you think for yourself. But, hey, if you don't like that, take a class from Thompson (she'll tell you exactly what to think).

Prof. Olivier is creative, well-dressed and extremely kind. Explanations are clear & class is a lot of fun, too. I don't know what the loser who criticizes him was smoking. Definitely take any class you can from him.

I have also taken his 202 class. I would, honestly, consider him to be one of the best professors on campus. He loves his topic and it shows, and he is very knowledgable. The work is all fun and intellectually stimulating. He is approachable, friendly, and likeable. TAKE HIS CLASS!

I highly recommend taking this class.  Olivier is fun and laidback.  He makes the subject interesting and has online lessons to supplement and help you understand the reading.  He knows a lot, enjoys teaching, and just makes the class fun.  This is my favorite French class so far.

Dr. Olivier is a good prof.  He doesn't expect unrealistic effort, but he rewards it if given.  He seemed a bit unorganized, and the class really puts the brunt of the load on the last month before finals.  Be ready for it.
He is a great teacher...very smart and has a lot of experience in french culture literature. I really recommend this class.
Rude, unhelpful. He talks about other professors behind their backs! He almost publicly lambasts students' efforts. DO NOT take him!!

He was a great professor. Homework consisted of watching movies or reading stories and writing a one page prompt about it also two bigger projects. The tests were formatted like an AP test a few fill in the blank questions, a bunch or short response, and one longer essay. It was a pretty easy class as long as you take good notes and go to class

Professor Yamada was a really fun and engaging professor. Make sure to participate in his classes and do the prompts and you will get a good grade. The only difficult part of the class in my opinion were the exams, because the study guide was really vague. Overall, a great class and a great professor.

Prof. Yamada teaches through discussion. Participation in class discussions matters! Never skip lectures; take notes on readings, movies, and lectures. Do not take this class if you hate the horror genre - watching one or two movies with horror aspects is mandatory. Tho I did learn a lot about East Asia through this class, and found it enjoyable.

Workload was more than I would like but still manageable, and sometimes you get to watch anime or k-dramas for homework! Marc was hilarious and very engaging in class. Exams were tough and kind of nitpicky and his study guide is really vague. Overall tho I loved coming to class, just the stuff outside of class kind of sucked. Marc is great tho!

Dr. Yamada is cool and class was usually fun. We watched a ton of movies, and a few of them were actually pretty good. My main issue is that EVERYTHING was free response, and it felt like Dr. Yamada and the TAs just took points willy nilly. It seemed like no matter what I wrote, they just made my grade whatever they felt like on that given day.

Dr. Yamada is an engaging professor, and there is a great mix of informational readings and fun movies. I enjoyed the material and discussion-based lectures. There are 2-3 page-length prompts a week and movies we are required to watch outside of class. Tests are also very long and the toughest part of class to me! Overall, a very enjoyable class!

Yamada sensei is pretty good. Overall it is a college-level class, so be ready to read some stuff. During the second half of the semester, we are watching movies, so it's pretty chill. Yamada sensei is chill and he is always prepared for his class. I would recommend him

I loved taking this class from Dr. Yamada! It was such a fun class and Dr. Yamada managed to blend his humor and the content of the class into an extremely enjoyable mix. He places a lot of emphasis on class participation and is heavy on outside work, but it's mostly movies, episodes of TV or anime, or smaller passages from books. Overall super fun

Attendance and engagement are really important in Prof. Yamada's classes but you won't want to miss them anyway. He is quite funny and his lectures are easy to follow. You will spend a lot of time outside of class but it's mostly short readings, videos, or movies. Just make sure you understand the basics of the material and you should be fine.

Prof. Yamada is the best. I have taken multiple classes from him, and his lectures are always engaging and fun. Course is structured really well, and there is a decent amount of homework but it's not difficult to do well on.
good guy, easy class, small class, fun

Prof. Yamada is awesome. He structures his class extremely well and helps you improve as a writer. He gives honest feedback and makes you feel like you learned a ton by the end of the semester. Really funny too, and has cool takes on culture.

Great class and pretty easy overall. You get to watch a lot of movies for homework. He makes it super fun and easy. Also offers extra credit. A couple of group work/projects but not that bad honestly. Homeworking is reading or watching something before class and writing a half-page response to a question.

Professor Yamada was so understanding. I was hospitalized during his class and he was so willing to work with me to reschedule a test and some assignments. A lot of group work, which I didn't love, but his lectures were really great. The testing system he uses is through the humanities center, which was weird and they were long, but doable.
A lot of effort and time to do well in this class but you won't regret it. He's inspirational.

Professor Yamada is awesome! His lectures were clear and entertaining and he made class interesting by incorporating a variety of activities and group work. His exams can be hard, but as long as you study, the class isn't overly difficult. I learned a lot!

What a guy! I didn't want this class to be over. I had so much fun. He is a pretty tough grader, but he will help you. I never disagreed with the feedback he gave, I thought it was fair but I do think he takes off more points than necessary on big assignments for a class graded by so few things. We only used a textbook for the first month at most.

Basically, you show up and watch movies. Do the assignments and you can skip the final and still get an A. Attendance is 20% of your grade, so it's really important that you go. You don't have to talk in class for a grade, so there's no pressure. You're going to find at least one movie that you love here!

Professor Yamada is one of the funniest teachers I have ever had. I thoroughly enjoyed his class and would look forward to what we were going to learn each day. He uses activities such as tea parties, skits, and film evaluations to keep the class engaging. My only warning is that the midterm and the final exams are VERY difficult, but worth it.

Professor Yamada is by far one of the best professors I´ve had at BYU! I took his East- Asian Humanities class and appreciated the diversity and fun of his lectures. Grades included a 1 pg. write up for each to every other class, class participation, and 1 midterm and 1 final. Overall a fun and easy class if you stay up on readings-writing.

Professor Yamada's class was really engaging and interesting. There aren't many assignments, so the midterm and test are huge parts of your grade. However, the tests aren't too bad if you study for them. You watch a lot of films and read pdf's of some textbook that he posts on LS. Really enjoyable class, would recommend!

Professor Yamada is very engaging and a great teacher, even though much of the marterial is boring. You need to participate in class for part of your grade. Tests are fairly difficult but if you put in effort it isn't crazy bad.

Dr. Yamada is both knowledgeable and fun! His lectures are engaging and his presentation slides are clear and well designed. Be prepared to participate in class discussion and write multiple papers. He grades papers strictly, but he's one of the fastest graders I've ever met. I got my scores back within 24 hours every time.

Professor Yamada is THE best! He cares so much about his students and makes a point to get to know you personally. He is also super funny and an excellent teacher. He is a kind of tough grader, but gives really great feedback and is always willing to work with you. Would recommend!
Marc is really chill and makes class fun. He really knows his stuff and if you participate, you will do well and have lots of fun.

Professor Yamada is great! He learns the names of all of his students early on and exhibits a genuine interest in the lives of students. He is also SUPER funny. The class was fun, but grading was tough. Even our TA had only gotten an A- when they took the class. There are multiple group projects and short writing assignments due each week.

Professor Yamada allows his students to learn effectively through fun, engaging lessons. We made videos about Asian pop culture, watched ghost stories, and had a Japanese tea Ceremony but with chocolate. Professor Yamada is intelligent, thorough and loves to help his students. I would take his class again!

I've had Yamada a few times, and each different class has been wonderful! He is great at connecting with his students and is genuinely interested in our thoughts and feelings. He has the unique gift of interacting with students on a friend level while maintaining professionalism.

His junior seminar on Postmodern culture literally changed the way I see the world and construct reality. Funny, accessible, brilliant, organized, etc. You instantly feel comfortable making jokes directed at him or anyone else on day 1 and everyone is chatting and laughing before and after every class. EVERYONE should take a class from him.

Prof Yamada is the best professor at BYU! By far my favorite prof all semester. His class is mostly discussion based and values all comments without judgement. He does have high expectations, especially for essays, but is willing to help at any time. Only a midterm and a final that pull directly from the class. 10/10 recommend taking this class!
