He is so funny and really loose and helps his students open up and make comments. He really just wants you to discuss the ideas learned in class so that you can remember and apply the material. The class itself was not too hard, the material is interesting. The tests were big and harder than I expected though. Worth my time. Had a lot of fun.

Professor Yamada was very funny yet effective about the way he lectures.  He knows what he is talking about and teaches  in a way that makes you think critically.   Want to do well in his class?  Go to class and participate! His tests are difficult if you do not attend class.  Just go to class!

Dr. Yamada is one of the most accessible professors on campus. He's funny, connects well with students, and is incredibly organized. Expectations are clear and he incorporates old material in with the new so you're always reviewing as you go. The tests are extensions of everything we do in class. He prepares you well. Also just a great person.
He worked well with helping students on their papers.  He tended to interrupt people while they gave comments.  The activities in class were very helpful with learning the material.

Grading is very fair. 20 short writing prompts, one midterm, and a group project.  Attendance is Mandatory but the class is never boring and Prof Yamada always makes class interesting. He's an amazing teacher and I really learned things that will stick with me for years because of his teaching style. He doesn't make you buy a textbook.

His relative youth and semi-controversial sense of humor keep the atmosphere light while his hand-picked course material  is deep and accessible enough to students to ensure stimulating classroom discussions and genuine learning. He is level-headed, has integrity as a professor, genuinely cares for students, and will work with those who struggle.

Dr. Yamada is the man. Super funny, great lectures and knows how to keep you involved. He is the perfect mix of loose and strict. I would take this class 20 more times and learn something new each time and still love it.

Japanese Film is a great class. One of my very favorite at BYU. Yamada sensei makes it so fun and easy. Just watch the movies, take good notes, and you can use your notes on the quizzes. 3 easy papers, and an easy final exam. I thought it was an easy A, and I looked forward to classlearned a lot!!

Professor Yamada is the best! He is nice and great to get along with. He genuinely cares about his students and their grade. He is willing to help you out if you come to him. There was a lot of class discussions, an easy weekly quiz ( you can use your notes on most of them), a few papers, a midterm and final. This class was AWESOME!
I loved this class! The material is challenging but not overwhelming, and you will learn a lot.
Great Teacher! Great Class!

Yamada sensei is a stud. He is fresh out of Cal Berkely and is easy to get along with. He wants you to succeed and will help in any way that he can. You can also chill with him after class for a couple minutes and talk about anything. He takes a time-consuming class and makes it fun. I learned alot. If you put in the study time you should get and A

Marci is amazing.  You do have to specifically seek out personal feedback, but she's very clear in what she does and does not like, so if you can adjust your dancing accordingly, you'll be fine.  And she is REALLY patient.  Like, almost too patient sometimes.  Show you're willing to work, and she'll work with you.

I really enjoyed this class.  I'm not terribly good at dancing, but she was really able to help me improve and all of her feedback is constructive and useful.  I would highly recommend Marci to anyone taking 380.

I have taken 380 from everyone you can, and Marci is the best. She improves your technique and teaches well. Her class is faster paced because it has an hour less per week so it is more difficult for 1st time students, but it is possible if you put in the work. 380 is  a step up from 280. Expect to have to practice.

Marci is definitely somewhat intimidating, but she's a nice lady and she knows her stuff. Yeah she's not super bubbly, but I wouldn't back off a class just because she's teaching it. Also, 480 in the Winter is SO fun; you learn west coast, salsa, New York hustle, and two step. I would definitely recommend this class. :)

A+ teacher! This is an advanced class for standard ballroom dancers.  Marcy is amazing at her craft.  She has incredible experience teaching and is gifted in being able to identify ways to improve your dancing.  She can come off as stern or cold at the expense of efficiently communicating feedback.
Learned a lot but was intimidated by her teaching style. She really doesn't work well with people who haven't been dancing for years or don't understand things right away.

Marci is very knowledgeable about dance, and it's obvious in the way she teaches. That is to say, she doesn't teach "beginners" (i.e. people taking 380 for the first time) very well. She focuses a lot on technique, and doesn't go over the actual footwork/movement that goes into a step very much. She'll tell you WHAT to fix, but not HOW to fix it.
Awesome teacher. She's just nice and fun. Except when grading... tough grader.
dedicated teacher

Marci has been my favorite dance teacher because of her knowledge of the material and desire to help the students.  It is refreshing to be in her class because she is so organized and focused.  She really cares about the students.

No idea how her ratings are so low. I basically only did the assignments+homework for this class, copied and pasted every single question and answer into a document and boom theres your test. Every question and answer is the exact same as hw and assignments. Easiest class I have ever taken in my life and Hoskins is a joy. Plays the harp for you.

This was an online class, so I didn't interact with the professor even once, but the class was great. There are usually 3 units per week, each with reading, a lecture, and a quiz. If you do the reading the put in effort it's an easy A, very good for a general!

This was an online physical science course, so there wasn't much direct interaction with the professor. However, the course was well-organized and easy to follow. The material was interesting and the workload was light, which felt appropriate for a general education science credit.

I LOVED Professor Hoskin's class. She understands that most students are taking this class for a GE, so she makes the content applicable to real-world issues. You can tell she is very passionate about what she is teaching; she took us on field trips and played her harp in class. The exams aren't graded heavily and are open everything.

She is awesome! There is a lot of homework, but part of her philosophy of learning is by getting in repetition, and if you understand that, then it can be an enjoyable class. I felt like I learned a lot through it. She's extremely willing to help with anything and is genuinely a great person. Highly recommend for a GE!

I don't know why other people didn't like her. She was nice and did a good job explaining material and was quirky but fun. I took this class as a junior and I figure most people taking this are freshman who don't know how college works. Don't bother buying the textbook I never used it. TA reviews were super helpful and exams weren't too hard.

Lectures were very confusing. I didn't really vibe with her teaching style. I felt like I learned more from the online content and TA reviews than the in person lectures. I would have been cooked if it wasn't for the TA reviews and being able to bring a study sheet into the exams. DON'T buy the textbook. Complete waste of $.

This was a difficult class, but a lot of that was out of Professor Hoskin's control. However, it didn't feel like she always knew the info. Not really a class I looked forward to at all. If you take this class, be prepared to learn most of the content on your own and GO TO TA REVIEWS - those are what got me through!
DO NOT TAKE. DO NOT TAKE. DO NOT TAKE. Trust me when I say you will regret it. Not enough allowed words on this post to explain how much I did not like this class and teacher. Just do not take.

The sweetest girl but didn't learn jack. If you're looking for an easy A, this is it. But if you actually are wanting to understand anything then look elsewhere. The lectures are all over the place & she pretty much just reads off of the slides and laughs the whole time.

Professor Hoskins made this class pretty difficult. Not like she could control a lot of it (PS100 is an unnecessarily difficult class) but she really breezed through lectures very quickly, and oftentimes if we asked a question about the content or the class itself she would consult her TAs like she didn't know, overall couldn't explain very well.

I stopped going to class halfway through the semester and my grade went up. She does not explain anything well, she looks at the TAs in confusion, I do not think she has actually read the book. This class is very time consuming, but not impossible to do, just do not take it with her.

This class was very hard and time consuming when it didn't have to be. She didn't ever complete a thought during lectures, sped through material on the slides so I couldn't take notes, and looked to her TA's when answering questions as if she was not sure herself. I couldn't get anything from the lectures and taught the material to myself entirely.

If you are looking for an easy GE then this class is good since the exams only count for 10-15%. The rest is mainly homework, which is easy but time-consuming. However, the class felt very irrelevant. She reads off of 100's of slides and goes very fast. Confusing explanations on topics. Too much information. I learned more from the textbooks.

please do not take this class from hoskins. this was her first semester teaching this class and it shows. she did not explain concepts well, and it felt like she literally just read the slideshows and then moved on too fast for me to take notes. it took hours of work outside of class to understand the material. would recommend randy skinner tho!!

Professor Hoskins unfortunately does not know what she is talking about most of the time. I never seem to really learn during her lectures, and she never sounds confident in her answers. The TAs are much more helpful than her, and I feel like I learned more myself than I have from her.

I really do not want to give a bad score to a teacher, but this class just feels a lot harder than it was meant to be due to the professor's explanations of the readings. I feel like I am not ever really sure what she is explaining and even when a student asks questions the answers feel kind of all over. TA's are your best shot at understanding.

She's definitely still getting used to teaching, so lectures weren't super organized or helpful and I ended up skipping most of them. The class often felt like a high school substitute teacher was covering material they weren't fully confident in. That said, the course itself was pretty easy and tests were manageable.

Ive never had a worse professor here at BYU. She doesn't know the content, cant explain basic 100 level concepts clearly, and rambles in lectures. The test is the same across sections, and it covers things that were never mentioned in class. The TA's know and explain the material better than the professor and they should just teach the class.

Marianne Baker helps you love to write.  At least that's what it was like for me.  She KNOWS what she is talking about and actually CARES about her students.  She made me really enjoy writing essays and doing research for them, and that's coming from one that thought english classes would just be drudgery and busy work.  Great class. No complaints.
Dr. Forest really cares about you as a student. She has great ideas, and is super easy to talk to. I would take another class from her without hesitation. Strongly recommend!

She only had one extra credit opportunity this semester and it definitely saved my grade. The TAs grade your papers and they grade tough. I emailed Forest and she was willing to take another look at my paper. She helped me reach my goal of passing the class with at least 90%. Dr. Forest really is so sweet and understanding, but beware of the TAs.

Dr. Forest's class is not hard but you definitely have to read and attend lectures or you will miss things. The TAs have stricter standards than she does, but she won't override them, so just make sure you know what your TA wants out of the short writing assignments. Overall a good professor and a good class-- not easy, but very doable.

This class was by far my least favorite class I have ever taken. Lectures are incredibly boring. There are no engaging ideas and no interaction with the class. Tests are unnecessarily hard, and instructions on assignments are very unclear. The grading on assignments is super harsh. There is no feedback on what you did wrong either. Don't take it.

I enjoyed this class, and at times it felt more like a comedy show than a calculus lecture in a good way. He explained the material clearly, though the homework was more challenging than expected. The written assignments were graded strictly, and the three midterms were difficult. Overall, it was a challenging but manageable course.

He's super laid back! Might give you some points back if you make a case. He's funny and relatable. He's more of an explainer rather than a lecturer. He helps understand and tie concepts together before presenting the content which leads to less rigor and less writing on the board. I'm an auditory learner so it works well, but others disagree.

Dr. Allen was excellent! I loved his class. I was concerned that since I wasn't a biology/neuroscience buff I would struggle, but he did an amazing job of making complicated topics clear and easy to comprehend. His method of testing is very fair. Cuts all the busy work. I highly recommend this class. He has lots of experience and knows his stuff!

Dr. Allen is proof that a class doesn't have to be hard to make you learn a lot. I feel like this was one of the most educational classes I took at BYU and it was very enjoyable and relaxed as well. I'd take everything I could from Dr. Allen.

Dr. Allen is great!  I was nervous about taking this class because comments I had read emphasized that a neuroscience background would be helpful.  But Dr. Allen is crystal clear and  makes a potentially difficult subject fun and easy to learn.  His tests allow you to explain your answer for full/partial credit if you mark the wrong answer.  Great!

Love it. Take anything you can from him. kind of odd, but always entertaining, and so funny. If you have to skip class you can always catch up by reviewing the powerpoint slides on blackboard and reading the textbook. pretty unorganized, but definitely one of my favorite professors at BYU.

Professor Allen was amazing! Very helpful, made tests fair, & is very kind. Loved this class and loved this professor. Really great teacher. I did poorly, but honestly, if I'd put more effort in, I'd have done better. He tells you exactly how to get good grades, no surprises or trying to trick you in exams. I very highly recommend this class.
Fantastic Teacher. Helped me decide my major: Psychology all the way. The tests were well written and he allowed for comments on answers. TOTALLY TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

I think Professor Allen was an awesome teacher, the only thing that bugged me about his class is that he wouldn't post grades throughout the semester, although most everyone in the class did fine. I would reccomend taking Psych 111 from him, he's a really funny guy!

Random--Random--Random. The class was great, somewhat unorgaized, and easy. I really like Dr. Allen and would reccomend him for anyone taking 302. He makes it a lot easier than some others. His wife taught one day. . . kind of weird situation, but whatever. Two ACDC quizzes.
Dr. Allen is a great professor. This class consisted of 5 small quizzes, a midterm and final. That's it. No busy work and no papers! He's interesting and clear

Professor Allen is great.  The first day of class he showed up with his entire face black and blue from a rugby game.  He is funny and a great teacher.  He really knows his stuff and only teaches you relevant topics.  His test are multiple choice and easy if you do your reading.  He always has a test where the answers are A.C.D.C It's his fav. band

Prof. Allen taught the PSYCH 111 course for the first time in Summer 07 and as far as I know, will not be teaching the 111 course in the future. Prof. Allen is a funny guy. He makes the material interesting and it is quite clear that he enjoys teaching. His tests are straight forward, multiple choice tests. Even the final.

Prof. Allen is an awesome teacher. He makes class intersting and educational at the same time.  His test are all multiple choice and super direct with the lecture material. If you are looking for a good professor and an easy way to learn, I would definately go with Dr. Allen
Great teacher. Focuses on what you need to know. You still need to study for the tests and I recommend attending for the great stories.
He's a little absent-minded, but very willing to help you and work with you. If you can get past his apparent excess of rugby concussions, he's a great guy.
He told really funny stories and always let our night class out early.  I enjoyed him and learned a lot too.
lots of material covered, only multiple choice tests
Dr. Allen's a nice guy, and in many ways a good teacher, but I actually think, for this class anyway, he was TOO easy and didn't cover nearly enough material. I felt shortchanged.
Good teacher and great guy, very entertaining, very smart.  Class is straight forward with no busy work. If you attend and listen can easily get and "A"
Super easy A that Professor Ammons makes fun and interesting. Very knowledgable about music and has so many interesting facts. Show up and do the projects and you will get an A.

Professor Ammons is AMAZING!!! Take him for this class. He wants everyone to succeed and knows that this is for a GE and its an extremely easy A. I loved his lectures, he gives us so much freedom with our assignments so we can write about whatever we want as long as it is on topic.

Very interesting class. Gave me a new perspective on music. Classes always get out early (a 2 hr 50min class is usually between 1hr-2hr). Grade based on a 5 or so assignments, none of which were overly challenging.

This class is only graded on 3 tests, but the tests are SUPER easy (literally copied from the homework). Dr. Ammons is hilarious, and his lectures are short and concise. Class was scheduled for two hours, but the longest it ever went was 40 minutes. Take this class from Dr. Ammons!

His actual in class teaching is fine. However, the ai grading system they use is broken and makes most assignments impossible to do. They have too much trust in it and will trust the word of the ai over the word of the student. It's also an all or nothing grading system, so you can do 99% of an assignment and get a 0 because you forgot 1 thing.

Professor Clement is a very caring professor who wants every student to succeed. However, get ready for a TON of work involved in CS260. It feels like you're learning a new coding language every week, which was difficult. Professor Clement does a great job of providing extra credit opportunities, and I loved his spiritual moments and field trips

The CS 224 online section lacks clear examples for the homework and slides. My suggestion is sign up for the online section but go in person. Doing so will give you a more lenient homework and project schedule compared to an in-person section. Dr. Clement is always there to help you if you need help.
Not really present, doesnt express ideas thoroughly or easy enough to understand

He is a nice guy, but boring. He talked about what coding you are doing, but hardly about the practicality of actually doing it (how to code), which made it hard for me. You build a website but the class structure is bad. Later checkpoints (JavaScript and React) are harder. Class attendance almost isn't worth it; I learned from google and chatGPT.

The lecture side of class wasn't really necessary at all since the online notes had all the important information. The class also isn't given enough time for your knowledge of these topics to actually stick. My final project ended up using so much copy & paste because of this. Wish it could be extended to a full year instead of one semester.
Most of it was online for me so i hardly ever saw the professor. You just read some github pages and work on your website.

Great class. Some bugs in the material because they just moved from Vue to React but otherwise a great class. Lots of projects but they were pretty easy. Some homeworks and two exams but altogether very doable.

It isn't a hard class, but there isn't a whole lot of help. The TA's honestly can't help you learn, but they aren't harsh graders. You are asked to copy and paste a lot and I didn't feel like I learned a lot from the course. Professor Clement is a nice guy, it isn't necessarily a bad class, but if you are going to take 260, don't take it from him.
Honestly just difficult to work with, doesn't do a great job of structuring lectures or tutorials to cultivate learning, and doesn't do a great job of assisting students that show a need for help.

Dr. Clement is a great professor and a great guy! He really wants you to succeed and gives you the resources to do so. I took his online, on-demand class and would highly recommend this format for any CS student.

This is a remote, on-demand class, so I didn't interact with Dr. Clement much, but when I did, it was only positive interactions. The class is not too difficult (there are a number of large projects), but I learned a ton of very useful skills. I would highly recommend taking this class from Dr. Clement!

Weekly labs (for the most part) aren't easy but professor gives lots of videos that offer lots of help. Also, a good TA queue. Reading quizzes are fine because they have unlimited submissions. Exams aren't too bad.

Complete waste of my time and tuition money. 90% of the class is online tutorials that you can already use for free, and any tutorials made by the professor were awful. After turning in one assignment late I was told I was "in danger of failing" even though there's no penalty for late work. Save your time and take something more useful.

Clement did a bad job explaining how to code anything. He gives huge assignments and no guidance. Most of the projects shouldnt have been hard, but without guidance it would take hours of meeting with tutors to even understand the data structures, let alone code them. I recommend you take classes from a professor who actually teaches you.

Didn't enjoy lectures at all, made most of the labs way beyond our capacity and I think they were an ineffective way of teaching us the concepts that he was trying to teach. That being said he's better than Roper

This was the worst organized class I have ever taken. It was clear they were changing the order of the units, but it felt incomplete. More than once, we were expected to use a concept that we would learn later in the semester. Relied heavily on online resources outside of class to get a good grade.

I liked Dr. Clement. His class was really hard, but I think that is the point. I spent 15+ hours a week on his class, sometimes more. I give him four stars because his rubrics and class material weren't very organized.

He always had very helpful videos to help you get started on the labs if you needed them and knew the common places where students would get stuck. The code is more complicated, so you have to identify most of the bugs yourself. Readings built nicely and made the quizzes easy. Super useful programming skills.

Clement only hindered my learning in this class. His only teaching consisted of occasional videos for the labs wherein he would contradict the written instructions and also the github lab specs. I didn't finished a single lab with a confident feeling about the material--and this is coming from someone who gave the class + TA's wayy too much time.

Dr. Clement really cares about his students. CS 235 is not the easiest class, but he prepares you well for each lab you do over the semester. He was almost always willing to meet with me when I got helplessly stuck. He is super flexible with due dates as he knows students are trying to juggle their lives and his CS projects. I love this dude.

Dr. Clement is not one of those CS teachers that wants to see you suffer. He genuinely tries to help students succeed, understand concepts, and have fun. Even though the class was on demand, I felt that he was really trying to be a part of the students' lives. When I had trouble getting labs done on the assigned date, he was willing to work with me

(Taken OnDemand) Great class for programmers on the data structures that hold memory (vectors, lists, etc). The concepts were taught through reading quizzes, which were sometimes hard to follow. Labs are computer graded so you know your score beforehand. Lots of work outside of class. Maybe 7-8 hours a week on average, depending on your bugs.

I've never felt as overwhelmed as fast as I did at the start of this class semester. He throws you in headfirst, expecting you to figure out the Linux command line, a new (terrible) IDE, and the monstrous weekly labs completely on your own. I think it's largely the class, though, not the professor.

Professor Clement is great. Lets your turn in assignments late. Make's it easy to get good grades. Is super nice and very understanding. The only strange thing about 260 is that for must questions, he just googled the answer. But, I guess thats what most web programmers do these days.

If you thought 142 was a breeze, I'd recommend taking the online section of 235. There really aren't lectures and you can just do homework, labs, etc. on your own, which was really nice for me. Assignments have unlimited retakes and the grading is pretty lenient as long as you follow what's going on in the class.

This was the most difficult class I've ever taken. Prof. Clement does a terrible job explaining concepts and the labs are incredibly difficult. He would create such a needlessly difficult framework you'd have to follow that I would spend 5-6 hours every lab just trying to decipher his code before I would even start my code. Don't take from Clement!

This teacher is the nicest and one of the most understanding people I've ever met. I had a rough semester dealing with personal problems and every time I emailed him he was caring and helped me out. Never had someone as great as this.

One of the friendliest professors you'll ever have. Great guy. Very easy class (like I-didn't-take-the-midterm-and-still-got-an-A easy). The course teaches hirable skills such as Node, (Basic) AWS, MongoDB, and VuejsI just wish we got into more the more robust features of each of them. Really wish it pushed me more than it did.

It is an online class. He really cares about students. Although it is an online class, he always answers student's questions as soon as he can. The e-book is somewhat helpful, but you can find a free version of it on the internet. So, opt it out. If you take an online course, make sure you understand the reading. Some of the Labs are really heavy.

Good, funny, genuine dude. Took him for CS235 and it was great. Took him for CS260 and it seemed like he was just using tutorials made by a different prof, and didn't even look at the tutorials until in class with us. I stopped going to class because it was useless, and the tutorials are easy to just do online, outside of class.
He is a really nice guy, but his lectures really just are not helpful. I took CS 418 and CS 260 from him and rarely attended class because they just weren't helpful.

Dr. Clement is the best professor in the CS department right now (writing this as a senior). His classes focus on writing actual code that help significantly with the labs. I felt that I have learned more in the two classes I have taken from him than anyone else.

Way too confident in the relevance of his class to the industry, but it is just an intro to web programming. Easy class. Doesn't use a book. You'll teach yourself everything online but its a decent start. BYU really should have a second part to this course to cover more depth but they'd rather send you to Dev Mountain for this kind of programming.

Professor Clement is a very caring person. He doesn't quite fit the beastly CS BYU teacher mold because he truly want to help you succeed and will do his best to help you understand. I do think that he is a bit outdated in the technologies that he is accustomed to using. I'm not entirely sure he has a background in profession web development.

418 is great with Dr. Clement. Majority of the work is through Rosalind problems which are like small coding interview questions. Choose your own language (most do Python), group projects are super interesting but slightly more challenging. Really enjoyed this class as a CS elective. Most of the quizzes you can turn in late at no penalty.

CS 260 does NOT teach you how to code. It teaches you how to copy/paste and tries to teach you over 6 programming languages in 4 months (I've learned nothing). Prof' Clement is nice but he doesn't even know what he's doing half the time and will frequently ask students what's wrong with his code during lecture. Don't take CS 260 from Clement.
Great teacher! Fun to listen to, very willing to help you learn, wants you to love coding! Wants all of us to get A's and makes it very possible to do so! By far one of the best CS teachers!!!

Doctor Clement has been my favorite CS professor I've had while at BYU. He cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He helps by giving a good amount of code on each lab and if you know what you're doing, you never need to go to class because he publishes everything online. I could not give him higher praise! Take him if you can!

Dr. Clement is so awesome. He is a perfect example of how every professor should be. He main focus is not to fit students into a bell curve, but really cares about you learning the material and enjoying the class. super caring, and unbelievably understanding. He wants you to succeed, and will do anything to help you get an A.

Professor Clement basically just wants you to get through the material and complete the labs. The class is set up so you will succeed. He gives you a lot of the code, so technically you could just copy/paste some things; however, I felt that I learned a lot in Professor Clement's class. Good professor, good environment.

Prof. Clement's web programming course is very doable. Unlike most 3-credit CS classes, it actually feels like 3 credits instead of 6. You do some very cool projects. There are two midterms and a final, but they're not hard. You could get through the class just through copy-pasting, sure, but all the resources are there for you to master it.

Awesome guy, great class structure. Learned more in this class than any other CS class. At times there was maybe too much copy/paste. There is SO much material taught but it's taught in a simple way and in a way you can succeed. I'm going to finish with 100% in the class. Can use internet on assignments and tests. 10/10 would recommend.

Super great guy, awesome, caring professor, but this class was an absolute mess. The class is very poorly designed to actually help anyone learn anything. Mostly you learn how to copy and paste. Easy A, but I am no more capable of web programming than when I started the class 4 months ago. Very frustrating assignments.

I dreaded CS 235 but he made this class awesome and even changed up the labs to make it easier.  He even threw out an old one and made a new lab to help us learn the uses of maps (associative arrays). Remember this class is based off the text book so all of the lab code is found there.

Good: he's a genuinely great guy. Explains the material well. Easy to get lots of extra credit. Bad: labs are time consuming (not surprising for a CS class).  Sometimes the specs he would tell us in class were different from what the TA's would tell us, causing confusion. And, there were easy but in-class quizzes each day, worth 10% of your grade.

He explains things well, and it's interesting, albeit a bit slow. I preferred to just read the textbook and get it over with. He relies a lot on the textbook, to the point of directing students to just copy the book's code on some labs, which I thought was kind of lame. Also makes us do UMLs for every lab, which are totally the worst.

This class is mostly seniors doing an easy elective. If you are an underclassman, however, expect a challenge, because the prof goes FAST and you WILL get lost.  You frantically try and keep up in class and then learn everything by yourself at home via tutorials. He IS forgiving, which is SO nice.

Dr. Clement is really nice and cares about his students. We often programmed during class together and he taught us whatever we needed and wanted to know. At first I didn't like the freestyle structure of the class but it grew on me. I learned a lot of valuable skills and technologies. Dr. Clement is great!

Far and away my favorite CS Professor at BYU. Clement cares about students, and will do whatever he can to make sure you are successful. Tests are fair, projects are interesting and worthwhile, and anyone can get an A if they try. This is my second class with Clement, and I would honestly take any class that he teaches

This is one of the most hated CS classes at BYU, but Bro Clement made it much more enjoyable than I expected. He expects more out of his students than most of the intro-level CS professors, and I think that's a good thing. Students that don't like Bro Clement as a teacher usually just want an easy A and for everything to be spoonfed to them.

This semester he said he was trying something new and I don't think it quite work out... First half of the class was fairly useless server programming  in C (I have to say I enjoyed it anyways), but the second half of the class there were too many small projects which left me with almost no time for the big final group project - web app.
Dr. Clement was really awesome for 418, definitely would recommend him.  Very willing to work with students one on one.

This class is definitely not a giveaway, but taking the time to come to labs and class will get you a good grade, especially if you do them early for extra credit. He had an "inverted classroom" where we would go through lectures at home, then come to class and work on portions of labs and homework. I never opened the textbook (web was sufficient).

He was super helpful and understanding! The Testing center had a weird schedule one day making me completely miss a part of the midterm and he let me retake it at the end of the semester. He has the lectures online to watch at home and then does help on hw in class. Very funny and entertaining, keeping the class interested.

Dr. Clement structures his lectures around what we think we need help on. This can be good or bad depending on if you have CS nerds in your class who want to talk about unrelated topics all the time. Going to lecture was helpful because Clement would give advice on the labs. Some labs took me a long time. Easy A if you do all the work on time.

Dr. Clement is very helpful. He spends a lot of class time working through examples. This can be boring if you've already done the lab for the section, but he mixes in helpful hints for everyone. The class is time consuming, but it is easy to get a good grade if you actually do the work.

Dr. Clement was very personable, and helpful. Some classes were not really relevant, but he'd usually make it worth your time with invaluable lab help. You MUST read the book, and reference it often. My quickest lab took 4 hours, my longest closer to 15. He tells you that your math ability is a good predictor of your success in the class.VeryTrue.

He's a pretty good professor.  His teaching style was somewhat pedantic, and class was quite boring from time to time, but the information he gave was applicable.  He generally seemed to know what he was talking about.  He called for volunteers a lot. I stopped attending class to dodge that bullet, and I still got an A.

Clement is good. However, I didn't really like his teaching style. It's lectures and examples, and you should read the book before coming. The book's the most important thing for this class. Others seem to like him, so maybe it's just me. But, let's just say this class is why I've decided against a CS major.

Dr Clement is so helpful. He will take up an entire lecture just to clear up one single question that you have. He invents new ways of explaining things all the time. He teaches to the students not just information. He dose not teach out of the book but you are required to read it.I couldn't have asked for a better teacher!

Dr. Clement is super nice and really wants every student to understand. He's willing to answer your questions in class. Class time was sort of hit or miss. The tests are exactly like the quizzes. GO TO THE LAB FOR HELP! Labs took up a lot of time, but an A was very doable.

Professor Clement is very good at programming, but the class I took (Intro to Programming) was a bit hard to keep up with.  He was very helpful when I asked him questions during office hours, though.  He was a good professor who cared about students - go to him with questions, not to the TAs.

Dr. Clement is the man! I would take any class I could from him if I were you. His teaching style is very loose, and he goes off on tangents a lot, but you learn so much during the semester. Midterm and final are easy, as is homework. Projects, however, are tough just like any other CS class. Take 360 from Clement and no one else!

Dr. Clement is so funny!  The class is really easy if you read and attend class.  I had no Programming experience before, and now I feel comfortable doing  lots of programming.  Its a really fun and interesting class.  The TA's are also really helpful,
Dr. Clement is the man! Don't take CS 142 from anyone but him!

Most of the time I spend on this class is in the lab. You work with TA's much more often than with the prof. I went to the class just for participation points. Tests have 2 parts: multiple choice test and program test. The MC test is extremely easy, don't worry. Just focus on the program test. It took me 10 hours on average for each.

Dr. Clement is very helpful and interesting, but more so one-on-one than in lecture.  The textbook is good; read it.  He spent most classes going through slides, but the occasional in-class programs were fun with a good group.  He was at times unexpectedly hilarious, but most of the class had tuned him out and missed those few brilliant moments.

He really cares about students and is a good teacher. My favorite CS class--I learned a ton! 6 projects; generous sample code and tutorials made them pretty easy, but I still felt a big sense of accomplishment. For passoff, TAs just played with our projects a little. A lot of extra credit was available. 2 tests were average; study review examples!

Dr Clement is really nice, and he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. However, if there weren't participation points, I wouldn't have gone to class at all.  Lecture was extremely not helpful, I only passed this class because I read the book on my own, did the quizzes, and got lots of help from the TAs. Good class overall though.

Dr. Clement is very understanding and helpful - when you can find him!  He is rarely in his office and lab and doesn't answer his phone.  E-mails sometimes take a while to get a response.  His teaching ability is pretty good, however, in the classroom - especially when he prepares for lecture before class (which seems to be about 2/3 of the time).
No Comments
Very nice guy
He teaches like his students are in first grade, and doesn't know the material.
Callister is by far my favorite teacher at BYU. 417 is hard where you are learning statistical tests in a program, but he is really patient with you and makes himself available if you are struggling.
Fantastic professor. He really cares about his students and is excited to talk about the material outside of class. Would 10/10 recommend him for any class he offers.

Dr. Callister is a GREAT professor, this class was interesting, although group work online is tough. He has set it up in a learn first half, present second half format which I like. No final for this class and a pretty easy midterm if you do the readings.

It's not that this class was difficult - it was just completely unrealistic. There is absolutely zero flexibility when it comes to late work, or mistakes (including the first days of class).Tough luck for someone working a full-time job. If you're looking for flexibility in your schedule, don't take this. I aced the final and project, still got a B
He struggles with the online format, and is a little disorganized. Seems like a cool guy though.

Late work isn't usually accepted if you miss something. He's a good guy but he's very disorganized with the class schedule and assignments which can be frustrating. You'll work with a real brand on teams like other ad classes.

I took the Persuasion class ON DEMAND and LOVED it. The class is structured simply; every week you have some reading. On TUE you can post to a discussion board or participate in a 30 min discussion, both about the reading. Then you have a quiz each SAT. Every 3 weeks there's an assignment where you apply the material to your life (easy). 2 tests.

Took his COMMS309. He wants you to be a "scholar" but that just means his class isn't busywork. Everything you do helps you internalize what's being taught! His grading was very fair and helpful! He helped our group outside of class with projects for the adlab and gave great feedback. Always answered our texts & was willing to meet with us on zoom

Super engaging class! There were assigned readings before each class which could get long, but were interesting. There was a quiz most classes on the reading which were really specific. But the midterm and exams are oral exams and he sets it up to get a good grade. There are also 2 presentations that help boost your grade. Overall, I loved class!

Pretty light amount of work. First half of the semester we had a couple 15-20 page articles to read and we just discuss in class for full credit if you were there. Then the midterm was a small group discussion with him. Second half was power point presentations of a different world religion and the final is going to be the same thing.

he's a good teacher, but definitely not for everybody. assignments are few. you really have a midterm (oral exam), a semester long class project where you do research for a real client, and the final. he does want you to take lead and not be told everything you have to do. if thats not you and you just want to cruise by, I suggest another teacher.

he wants scholars not students-you wont get a good grade if you just do the work-he expects you to immerse yourself in the material and become 2nd nature to you-the midterm is an hour long oral exam where you're presented with problems and you have to give solutions on the spot based on the material-don't take if you don't plan a career in business

Amazing! I would love to take another class with him. He really emphasizes that you learn & apply material, rather than just memorize for tests. One oral test, one statistics test, and one semester long project with a client (you learn a lot from this). If you attend class, do your reading, & contribute w/ the project you'll enjoy Callister a lot

I loved this class-it was interesting and very applicable to the Comms. dept. Dr Callister wants "scholars" not just students...he is pretty firm about that and you will disappoint him if you turn out to be merely just a student. However, his classes are fantastic and I would recommend this class to anyone who really wants to expand their horizons.

Callister is an awesome teacher that really knows how to be down to earth and reasonable. His class can get tedious by virtue of the subject matter but overall he makes it a great experience. Highly recommended

Great teacher! He taught this class a way he never had before. Each class we'd read an article and discuss it in class. Very simple but very engaging. You need to read the articles or it'll be obvious in the discussion. No tests a few quizzes (basic). Midterm/final you meet with him with your group and discuss what you learned. 1 group presentation
I took 230 from Callister and loved it.  He is a great teacher and will take his courses in the future if i have the chance.

Dr. Callister is very knowledgeable! He is a little soft spoke, but he teaches the material in a relatable way. I didn't realize how important the 101 class would be, if you learn the concepts you will do so much better in the rest of your comms classes! Tests are challenging, but if you put in the time, read the book and study, you'll do great!

Took class 1+ yr ago & now that I'm graduated and working in marketing, I think about this class every week. It turns out to be VERY pertinent, useful info. That mean and mode stuff never made sense to me and I hear it all the time now! Survey techniques are priceless too. So I suggest taking advantage of the class and Dr. C's great teaching.
Callister is a good teacher. He can be a little unclear sometimes, but the stuff that is unclear isn't generally important in real life. Lots of little assignments, but it's easy to do well on them.

I've taken Professor Callister every chance I've had. He really loves his students and is one of the very best teachers at BYU as far as the ability to communicate effective. He learns everybody's name in the first 5 minutes, too :D

A very good professor.  He understands the material well, has a lot of real-life experience.  He turned what I thought would be a really boring class into something I actually enjoyed.  Stay on top of the material because the class starts very easy but gets harder as it goes on.  Lots of little assignments to work on, but they help you learn

Prof. Callister is a good teacher. He keeps the class interesting, even though it was 2 1/2 hours long. The only difficult part was the final ad campaign, but it was fun to work on anyway. The tests are a little too strongly tied to the book, but overall they weren't too hard. Definitely take the class from him.
Callister is a good professor for 317.. he is basically immersed in research so if you're into it (even if you don't know it yet).. take it from him!
Lots of material. make sure you work hard on the project for the client, it was somewhat forgotten because he loves the academic side of the class, the application for the client took the back seat.
Great teacher, passionate about the subject, and very helpful in relating knowledge from class to the real world.

Prof Callister is one of the best teachers I've had so far. He loves advertising and shows that every class. He gives a review for every test, which are very easy if you follow it. Very laid back. Got an A in class.

Br. Callister is a really cool guy.  The class is laid back but you still learn something.  If you don't like group projects, you might want to take the class with some friends or something.  But, yeah, he's a great guy and teaches well.  I can't complain.

I love Brother Callister! He rocks! He makes you think. He knows his stuff and really prepares you for the tests. He has a lot of experience in the field and knows what you are to expect and teaches what you need to know.

Really great guy.  I wouldn't say he was the greatest teacher, or the most interesting, but he wasn't difficult.  Gave us study guides for tests that pretty much guarnateed good results if you studied them..  I recommend him.

Honestly professor Callister might be the best teacher at BYU. His class is so fun and you can tell he loves what he is teaching. He is very personable and explains things very well. Tests are super easy and all the info for them can be found in the book. i had no interest in advertising before this class and now i love it!!!!
He's a great teacher, he understands this is an entry-level class, but treats it like a professional environment.  I learned a lot and really enjoyed myself.

Great professor! Amazingly helpful for EVERYTHING! Great teaching style as well as great interaction and relationship with the students. You can approach him about anything and get great help. He has great respect for his students and motivates them to learn in a fun and clear way.

Callister is a great professor. His class is interesting, interactive and way fun. Tests aren't too bad, and he even invites the class to his house for a Christmas/Study party at the end of the semester. Way cool guy, way good class. If you're interested in Advertising, take it!

HE'S SO AWESOME! SO chill. Gets to know all 100 kids names! He really does care & is flexible & understanding. You watch 4 movies & do worksheets on your own. The first few weeks are reading & discussing, which is actually extremely interesting, but after that it's all presentations (fun debates) & the reading is on your own. SO FUN & INTERESTING!
Get to know someone in the class and make your own team.  Go to reviews and you'll do great on the tests.  Callister is a man without guile!  He's the best!
He had us over to his house for donuts and a review session. Very cool.
This class is mildly interesting and not too difficult.  There is a lot of work, but its not hard.

His actual in class teaching is fine. However, the ai grading system they use is broken and makes most assignments impossible to do. They have too much trust in it and will trust the word of the ai over the word of the student. It's also an all or nothing grading system, so you can do 99% of an assignment and get a 0 because you forgot 1 thing.

Professor Clement is a very caring professor who wants every student to succeed. However, get ready for a TON of work involved in CS260. It feels like you're learning a new coding language every week, which was difficult. Professor Clement does a great job of providing extra credit opportunities, and I loved his spiritual moments and field trips

The CS 224 online section lacks clear examples for the homework and slides. My suggestion is sign up for the online section but go in person. Doing so will give you a more lenient homework and project schedule compared to an in-person section. Dr. Clement is always there to help you if you need help.
Not really present, doesnt express ideas thoroughly or easy enough to understand

He is a nice guy, but boring. He talked about what coding you are doing, but hardly about the practicality of actually doing it (how to code), which made it hard for me. You build a website but the class structure is bad. Later checkpoints (JavaScript and React) are harder. Class attendance almost isn't worth it; I learned from google and chatGPT.

The lecture side of class wasn't really necessary at all since the online notes had all the important information. The class also isn't given enough time for your knowledge of these topics to actually stick. My final project ended up using so much copy & paste because of this. Wish it could be extended to a full year instead of one semester.
Most of it was online for me so i hardly ever saw the professor. You just read some github pages and work on your website.

Great class. Some bugs in the material because they just moved from Vue to React but otherwise a great class. Lots of projects but they were pretty easy. Some homeworks and two exams but altogether very doable.

It isn't a hard class, but there isn't a whole lot of help. The TA's honestly can't help you learn, but they aren't harsh graders. You are asked to copy and paste a lot and I didn't feel like I learned a lot from the course. Professor Clement is a nice guy, it isn't necessarily a bad class, but if you are going to take 260, don't take it from him.
Honestly just difficult to work with, doesn't do a great job of structuring lectures or tutorials to cultivate learning, and doesn't do a great job of assisting students that show a need for help.

Dr. Clement is a great professor and a great guy! He really wants you to succeed and gives you the resources to do so. I took his online, on-demand class and would highly recommend this format for any CS student.

This is a remote, on-demand class, so I didn't interact with Dr. Clement much, but when I did, it was only positive interactions. The class is not too difficult (there are a number of large projects), but I learned a ton of very useful skills. I would highly recommend taking this class from Dr. Clement!

Weekly labs (for the most part) aren't easy but professor gives lots of videos that offer lots of help. Also, a good TA queue. Reading quizzes are fine because they have unlimited submissions. Exams aren't too bad.

Complete waste of my time and tuition money. 90% of the class is online tutorials that you can already use for free, and any tutorials made by the professor were awful. After turning in one assignment late I was told I was "in danger of failing" even though there's no penalty for late work. Save your time and take something more useful.

Clement did a bad job explaining how to code anything. He gives huge assignments and no guidance. Most of the projects shouldnt have been hard, but without guidance it would take hours of meeting with tutors to even understand the data structures, let alone code them. I recommend you take classes from a professor who actually teaches you.

Didn't enjoy lectures at all, made most of the labs way beyond our capacity and I think they were an ineffective way of teaching us the concepts that he was trying to teach. That being said he's better than Roper

This was the worst organized class I have ever taken. It was clear they were changing the order of the units, but it felt incomplete. More than once, we were expected to use a concept that we would learn later in the semester. Relied heavily on online resources outside of class to get a good grade.

I liked Dr. Clement. His class was really hard, but I think that is the point. I spent 15+ hours a week on his class, sometimes more. I give him four stars because his rubrics and class material weren't very organized.

He always had very helpful videos to help you get started on the labs if you needed them and knew the common places where students would get stuck. The code is more complicated, so you have to identify most of the bugs yourself. Readings built nicely and made the quizzes easy. Super useful programming skills.

Clement only hindered my learning in this class. His only teaching consisted of occasional videos for the labs wherein he would contradict the written instructions and also the github lab specs. I didn't finished a single lab with a confident feeling about the material--and this is coming from someone who gave the class + TA's wayy too much time.

Dr. Clement really cares about his students. CS 235 is not the easiest class, but he prepares you well for each lab you do over the semester. He was almost always willing to meet with me when I got helplessly stuck. He is super flexible with due dates as he knows students are trying to juggle their lives and his CS projects. I love this dude.

Dr. Clement is not one of those CS teachers that wants to see you suffer. He genuinely tries to help students succeed, understand concepts, and have fun. Even though the class was on demand, I felt that he was really trying to be a part of the students' lives. When I had trouble getting labs done on the assigned date, he was willing to work with me

(Taken OnDemand) Great class for programmers on the data structures that hold memory (vectors, lists, etc). The concepts were taught through reading quizzes, which were sometimes hard to follow. Labs are computer graded so you know your score beforehand. Lots of work outside of class. Maybe 7-8 hours a week on average, depending on your bugs.

I've never felt as overwhelmed as fast as I did at the start of this class semester. He throws you in headfirst, expecting you to figure out the Linux command line, a new (terrible) IDE, and the monstrous weekly labs completely on your own. I think it's largely the class, though, not the professor.

Professor Clement is great. Lets your turn in assignments late. Make's it easy to get good grades. Is super nice and very understanding. The only strange thing about 260 is that for must questions, he just googled the answer. But, I guess thats what most web programmers do these days.

If you thought 142 was a breeze, I'd recommend taking the online section of 235. There really aren't lectures and you can just do homework, labs, etc. on your own, which was really nice for me. Assignments have unlimited retakes and the grading is pretty lenient as long as you follow what's going on in the class.

This was the most difficult class I've ever taken. Prof. Clement does a terrible job explaining concepts and the labs are incredibly difficult. He would create such a needlessly difficult framework you'd have to follow that I would spend 5-6 hours every lab just trying to decipher his code before I would even start my code. Don't take from Clement!

This teacher is the nicest and one of the most understanding people I've ever met. I had a rough semester dealing with personal problems and every time I emailed him he was caring and helped me out. Never had someone as great as this.

One of the friendliest professors you'll ever have. Great guy. Very easy class (like I-didn't-take-the-midterm-and-still-got-an-A easy). The course teaches hirable skills such as Node, (Basic) AWS, MongoDB, and VuejsI just wish we got into more the more robust features of each of them. Really wish it pushed me more than it did.

It is an online class. He really cares about students. Although it is an online class, he always answers student's questions as soon as he can. The e-book is somewhat helpful, but you can find a free version of it on the internet. So, opt it out. If you take an online course, make sure you understand the reading. Some of the Labs are really heavy.

Good, funny, genuine dude. Took him for CS235 and it was great. Took him for CS260 and it seemed like he was just using tutorials made by a different prof, and didn't even look at the tutorials until in class with us. I stopped going to class because it was useless, and the tutorials are easy to just do online, outside of class.
He is a really nice guy, but his lectures really just are not helpful. I took CS 418 and CS 260 from him and rarely attended class because they just weren't helpful.

Dr. Clement is the best professor in the CS department right now (writing this as a senior). His classes focus on writing actual code that help significantly with the labs. I felt that I have learned more in the two classes I have taken from him than anyone else.

Way too confident in the relevance of his class to the industry, but it is just an intro to web programming. Easy class. Doesn't use a book. You'll teach yourself everything online but its a decent start. BYU really should have a second part to this course to cover more depth but they'd rather send you to Dev Mountain for this kind of programming.

Professor Clement is a very caring person. He doesn't quite fit the beastly CS BYU teacher mold because he truly want to help you succeed and will do his best to help you understand. I do think that he is a bit outdated in the technologies that he is accustomed to using. I'm not entirely sure he has a background in profession web development.

418 is great with Dr. Clement. Majority of the work is through Rosalind problems which are like small coding interview questions. Choose your own language (most do Python), group projects are super interesting but slightly more challenging. Really enjoyed this class as a CS elective. Most of the quizzes you can turn in late at no penalty.

CS 260 does NOT teach you how to code. It teaches you how to copy/paste and tries to teach you over 6 programming languages in 4 months (I've learned nothing). Prof' Clement is nice but he doesn't even know what he's doing half the time and will frequently ask students what's wrong with his code during lecture. Don't take CS 260 from Clement.
Great teacher! Fun to listen to, very willing to help you learn, wants you to love coding! Wants all of us to get A's and makes it very possible to do so! By far one of the best CS teachers!!!

Doctor Clement has been my favorite CS professor I've had while at BYU. He cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He helps by giving a good amount of code on each lab and if you know what you're doing, you never need to go to class because he publishes everything online. I could not give him higher praise! Take him if you can!

Dr. Clement is so awesome. He is a perfect example of how every professor should be. He main focus is not to fit students into a bell curve, but really cares about you learning the material and enjoying the class. super caring, and unbelievably understanding. He wants you to succeed, and will do anything to help you get an A.

Professor Clement basically just wants you to get through the material and complete the labs. The class is set up so you will succeed. He gives you a lot of the code, so technically you could just copy/paste some things; however, I felt that I learned a lot in Professor Clement's class. Good professor, good environment.

Prof. Clement's web programming course is very doable. Unlike most 3-credit CS classes, it actually feels like 3 credits instead of 6. You do some very cool projects. There are two midterms and a final, but they're not hard. You could get through the class just through copy-pasting, sure, but all the resources are there for you to master it.

Awesome guy, great class structure. Learned more in this class than any other CS class. At times there was maybe too much copy/paste. There is SO much material taught but it's taught in a simple way and in a way you can succeed. I'm going to finish with 100% in the class. Can use internet on assignments and tests. 10/10 would recommend.

Super great guy, awesome, caring professor, but this class was an absolute mess. The class is very poorly designed to actually help anyone learn anything. Mostly you learn how to copy and paste. Easy A, but I am no more capable of web programming than when I started the class 4 months ago. Very frustrating assignments.

I dreaded CS 235 but he made this class awesome and even changed up the labs to make it easier.  He even threw out an old one and made a new lab to help us learn the uses of maps (associative arrays). Remember this class is based off the text book so all of the lab code is found there.

Good: he's a genuinely great guy. Explains the material well. Easy to get lots of extra credit. Bad: labs are time consuming (not surprising for a CS class).  Sometimes the specs he would tell us in class were different from what the TA's would tell us, causing confusion. And, there were easy but in-class quizzes each day, worth 10% of your grade.

He explains things well, and it's interesting, albeit a bit slow. I preferred to just read the textbook and get it over with. He relies a lot on the textbook, to the point of directing students to just copy the book's code on some labs, which I thought was kind of lame. Also makes us do UMLs for every lab, which are totally the worst.

This class is mostly seniors doing an easy elective. If you are an underclassman, however, expect a challenge, because the prof goes FAST and you WILL get lost.  You frantically try and keep up in class and then learn everything by yourself at home via tutorials. He IS forgiving, which is SO nice.

Dr. Clement is really nice and cares about his students. We often programmed during class together and he taught us whatever we needed and wanted to know. At first I didn't like the freestyle structure of the class but it grew on me. I learned a lot of valuable skills and technologies. Dr. Clement is great!

Far and away my favorite CS Professor at BYU. Clement cares about students, and will do whatever he can to make sure you are successful. Tests are fair, projects are interesting and worthwhile, and anyone can get an A if they try. This is my second class with Clement, and I would honestly take any class that he teaches

This is one of the most hated CS classes at BYU, but Bro Clement made it much more enjoyable than I expected. He expects more out of his students than most of the intro-level CS professors, and I think that's a good thing. Students that don't like Bro Clement as a teacher usually just want an easy A and for everything to be spoonfed to them.

This semester he said he was trying something new and I don't think it quite work out... First half of the class was fairly useless server programming  in C (I have to say I enjoyed it anyways), but the second half of the class there were too many small projects which left me with almost no time for the big final group project - web app.
Dr. Clement was really awesome for 418, definitely would recommend him.  Very willing to work with students one on one.

This class is definitely not a giveaway, but taking the time to come to labs and class will get you a good grade, especially if you do them early for extra credit. He had an "inverted classroom" where we would go through lectures at home, then come to class and work on portions of labs and homework. I never opened the textbook (web was sufficient).

He was super helpful and understanding! The Testing center had a weird schedule one day making me completely miss a part of the midterm and he let me retake it at the end of the semester. He has the lectures online to watch at home and then does help on hw in class. Very funny and entertaining, keeping the class interested.

Dr. Clement structures his lectures around what we think we need help on. This can be good or bad depending on if you have CS nerds in your class who want to talk about unrelated topics all the time. Going to lecture was helpful because Clement would give advice on the labs. Some labs took me a long time. Easy A if you do all the work on time.

Dr. Clement is very helpful. He spends a lot of class time working through examples. This can be boring if you've already done the lab for the section, but he mixes in helpful hints for everyone. The class is time consuming, but it is easy to get a good grade if you actually do the work.

Dr. Clement was very personable, and helpful. Some classes were not really relevant, but he'd usually make it worth your time with invaluable lab help. You MUST read the book, and reference it often. My quickest lab took 4 hours, my longest closer to 15. He tells you that your math ability is a good predictor of your success in the class.VeryTrue.

He's a pretty good professor.  His teaching style was somewhat pedantic, and class was quite boring from time to time, but the information he gave was applicable.  He generally seemed to know what he was talking about.  He called for volunteers a lot. I stopped attending class to dodge that bullet, and I still got an A.

Clement is good. However, I didn't really like his teaching style. It's lectures and examples, and you should read the book before coming. The book's the most important thing for this class. Others seem to like him, so maybe it's just me. But, let's just say this class is why I've decided against a CS major.

Dr Clement is so helpful. He will take up an entire lecture just to clear up one single question that you have. He invents new ways of explaining things all the time. He teaches to the students not just information. He dose not teach out of the book but you are required to read it.I couldn't have asked for a better teacher!

Dr. Clement is super nice and really wants every student to understand. He's willing to answer your questions in class. Class time was sort of hit or miss. The tests are exactly like the quizzes. GO TO THE LAB FOR HELP! Labs took up a lot of time, but an A was very doable.

Professor Clement is very good at programming, but the class I took (Intro to Programming) was a bit hard to keep up with.  He was very helpful when I asked him questions during office hours, though.  He was a good professor who cared about students - go to him with questions, not to the TAs.

Dr. Clement is the man! I would take any class I could from him if I were you. His teaching style is very loose, and he goes off on tangents a lot, but you learn so much during the semester. Midterm and final are easy, as is homework. Projects, however, are tough just like any other CS class. Take 360 from Clement and no one else!

Dr. Clement is so funny!  The class is really easy if you read and attend class.  I had no Programming experience before, and now I feel comfortable doing  lots of programming.  Its a really fun and interesting class.  The TA's are also really helpful,
Dr. Clement is the man! Don't take CS 142 from anyone but him!

Most of the time I spend on this class is in the lab. You work with TA's much more often than with the prof. I went to the class just for participation points. Tests have 2 parts: multiple choice test and program test. The MC test is extremely easy, don't worry. Just focus on the program test. It took me 10 hours on average for each.

Dr. Clement is very helpful and interesting, but more so one-on-one than in lecture.  The textbook is good; read it.  He spent most classes going through slides, but the occasional in-class programs were fun with a good group.  He was at times unexpectedly hilarious, but most of the class had tuned him out and missed those few brilliant moments.

He really cares about students and is a good teacher. My favorite CS class--I learned a ton! 6 projects; generous sample code and tutorials made them pretty easy, but I still felt a big sense of accomplishment. For passoff, TAs just played with our projects a little. A lot of extra credit was available. 2 tests were average; study review examples!

Dr Clement is really nice, and he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. However, if there weren't participation points, I wouldn't have gone to class at all.  Lecture was extremely not helpful, I only passed this class because I read the book on my own, did the quizzes, and got lots of help from the TAs. Good class overall though.

Dr. Clement is very understanding and helpful - when you can find him!  He is rarely in his office and lab and doesn't answer his phone.  E-mails sometimes take a while to get a response.  His teaching ability is pretty good, however, in the classroom - especially when he prepares for lecture before class (which seems to be about 2/3 of the time).
No Comments
Very nice guy
He teaches like his students are in first grade, and doesn't know the material.

I never do reviews on rate my professor but I felt the need to do so. This professor was not a good teacher. His lectures are so disorganized and confusing and don't even help you on the tests. His tests are extremely hard, long, and excessive. He didn't prepare students for his tests at all, my hours of studying felt pointless. Don't recommend.
lectures were organized and assignments were unclear. overall don't this guy.

Dr Choate brings strong knowledge of European history and does a great job explaining how major events connect to larger ideas. The class is organized and is clear, which makes expectations easy to understand. there is a very clear path to sucess. And his lectures are awesome! From his time in the MIlitary he brings an incredible perspective.

This is one of the best classes I've taken at BYU. Dr. Choate is incredibly qualified to teach a War Strategy class and brings remarkable insight to the subject. His courses are all structured similarly, which is a huge plus as long as you're prepared to work hard, the criteria to succeed and earn a good grade is clear and very achievable

It's true, he can be a little disorganized, but the mans a retired Army Colonel- he knows what he's talking about. His lectures are engaging the readings are interesting and his assignments are very open. There is a lot of wiggle room. If you meet with him outside of class a few times a good grade is almost guaranteed.

Dr. Choate is a super awesome professor, his lectures are always really interesting and he's really good at answering questions in class. He is super helpful if you go to his office hours and will help you with any of the assignments or tests.

This is my second class with Professor Choate and it was really good! I got super sick right over midterm and he was super helpful with extensions! Lectures are super interesting but can be fast paced with lots of info so look at what is required to know and focus in on those notes verse the full lecture. Quick response to emails! Use the resources

This is my second time taking this class. I had a really bad experience with the professor the first time and it left me thinking about dropping out of BYU. I had no confidence in myself, my writing and any value I could add to the field of History. Professor Choate did the exact opposite! He builds up his students and helps a lot! Choose own topic

We got to choose our topics which is nice and isn't always allowed for other capstone classes. He gave amazing feedback and was always willing to talk through ideas. I chose a tough topic that can be sensitive and hard to work with and he encouraged instead of discouraged me but also checked in often! His life is so interesting! Smaller classes!

Professor Choate has become one of my favorite teachers quickly. The first days lecture scared me but it got better quick. It is a 300 class and hard, but he is super willing to help and support his students. He shows genuine care for his students. He is incredibly smart. Go meet with him and you will be fine! He is really interesting and kind.

I learned a lot in this class. Dr. Choate knows a lot about his subject. He gave good writing advice. His lectures are a bit all over the place, but the midterm was not picky on the specifics. For this class, the lectures are just to help you become a better writer. He let us choose any topic for our paper and allotted a lot of revision time.

DONT CHOOSE THIS PROFESSOR!!! Professor Choate is a nice guy and very knowledgeable, but his lectures are incredibly confusing and disorganized. I felt underprepared for every exam and the study guides were useless. TAs were no help either. His class is way too hard, especially for a GE credit class. Save yourself the trouble and pick someone else.

Professor Choate is smart but not a great teacher. He was rude when students didn't understand, lectures were chaotic, and assignments were unclear. The workload was overwhelming—tons of outdated readings and long essays on exams. The course was stressful and made learning almost impossible.

He's a great guy and really cares about the subject. However, he's too smart for his own good and has a difficult time transferring his knowledge over to students. He's a little disorganized, and lectures are extremely yappy. However, the work load is reasonable, and the course is not graded too harshly. Work hard and stay on top of your work.

Prof. Choate is an odd duck. This class was insanely disorganized, and good luck following a lecture. He's nice enough, but I used ChatGPT heavily and worked with the TA for most stuff. I didn't get much value from class, but attendance and participation are mandatory. Lots of reading, so good luck. I'd skip this one.

I've never rated someone on here before but this one is worth it. I normally don't care about how incredible my professor is, but this class was simply awful. All my classmates and I were frustrated that he didn't teach history in a way that was helpful. All of the learning that we did for the tests was outside of anything he taught us. Just don't.

Dr. Choate is a really smart professor and knows a lot about history, but his lectures were disorganized and difficult to follow. His tests seemed to draw on very small details only mentioned in class. Lots of reading and the tests drew on the readings as well. All in all, nice guy and super smart, but there are easier ways to get this credit.
Dr. Choate is an amazing guy! He's super passionate about history and makes the lectures interesting. Go to TA reviews and use the study guides and you will do well.

Dr. Choate is one of the most knowledgable professors at BYU. His life experience is amazing. Pretty run-of-the-mill as far as difficulty goes, but the grading criteria is clear. He is a very easy grader (and most of the stuff is done by the TAs anyway... so go to them for assistance). He changed the way I thought about history. Two thumbs up!

Here's the deal. If you want a pretty easy HIS 202 class, this is your guy. Everything is on Learning Suite day 1. So everything you need to know for the midterm, final, essay, etc. are there. He is a quirky professor, but obviously passionate about his craft. I liked him.
Hands down my favorite professor. The classes are more on the difficult side but he is always available and willing to help. His grading is very reasonable and fair.

This guy is amazing! One of the best professors I've ever had. He is so caring and willing to talk with students. Lots of discussions and group activities. LOTS of reading! Reading reports due every week. Learned so much, it's incredible!

I enjoyed Dr. Choate's class. No one complained how hard it was, but it wasn't an easy A for anyone. Pretty middle of the pack as far as difficulty goes. Staple. I would definitely take him again. Nice guy and really awesome outside of class. I would recommend him to anyone.

I know it may seem as though this guy is worth your time, but be not mistaken. He served in the military so he obviously has great moral character, but he is not a good teacher. I have had better elementary school teachers. Do not take this class from him.

DO NOT take this course from dr. choate. great guy. but TERRIBLE teacher. i probably learned more studying the midterm and final reviews than i did going to his lectures. not good at explaining things. he just throws in random things during his lectures which you haven't discussed before which makes it even harder to follow the lectures.

Dr Choate is awesome and I highly recommend taking a class from him! He's super knowledgeable about what he teaches and is just an all around cool guy- he was the US ambassador to the Sudan! He is really passion able about what he teaches. That being said, for a GE this wasn't a super easy class and required some time but it was totally worth it.

Dr. Choate is really a great guy. He's funny and quirky and has so much life experience. But his classes are confusing. His lectures are difficult to follow. This class should not be listed as a POLI SCI class. It's history. It was a disappointing class. But like I said, Dr. Choate is really great. Class was pretty easy. Just read and study.

If you have the opportunity to take this class from a different teacher, then do so. Dr. Choate is a great guy and I respect him for serving in the military, but he just isn't a good teacher.
