I have talked with other students in my class and they are as confused on the material as I am. He doesn't really explain what he is talking about.

Professor Choate really knows his stuff. It is awesome because he always allows time for questions and discussion so there are many opportunities for further clarification. Even if a question is over an obscure topic, he knows. He really enjoys this subject and his lectures are interesting and thought-provoking. Pay attention and you should be set!

Dr. Choate knows how to be a historian. He focuses a lot on the historicity of a study which provides a new perspective but his actual lectures are VERY hard to follow. Take notes on the study guide on your laptop otherwise when you review for the exam you'll be frustrated. He changes requirements and test setup at the last minute with no warning

Professor Choate is the most caring and helpful professor I have met at BYU. His lectures are very inspirational. Some questions on his tests are not covered in class but can be found online or in the textbook. Very approachable inside and outside class. He really cares about you!

Hardest 200 level class I've taken. Way too much reading assigned and weekly papers. Don't really need to do all the reading. I haven't done hardly any of it, just summarized things, crammed for tests from the review guide (which consist of writing 5-7 short/long essays) and still am going to get in the B+/A- range. Lectures are pretty interesting.

Dr. Choate has not shown me that he cares about his students. I am taking his HIST 202 class and find that it does not feel like a 200 level class. He gives way too much reading, and doesn't explain things very well. I would not recommend taking a class from him.

Choate is one of my favourite professors in the History department. His lectures are brilliant and dense; be prepared to write a LOT of detailed notes.  Tests are hard and long, but if you study, you'll do well. As a person, he's delightful. Very kind, knowledgeable, takes a genuine interest in his students. Can't recommend him highly enough.
Really interesting guy. Class is very dry and kind of unclear on what is expected of you. I did feel like he was better than other history professors I have had

I absolutely loved this class! It's not the easier class ever, but for a civ class it's really not bad. Dr. Choate knows SO much about history, and he cares so much about his students! He's super easy to work with, and he I loved the approach he takes to teaching history - he focuses on themes rather than specific facts. Great class!

Great professor. His lectures are very clear and he's brilliant. His assignments seem a little daunting but in reality he doesn't grade them very hard.  His tests are very hard and very exhausting, give yourself 3-4 hours to take them. He's my favorite professor at BYU.

This class is hard, there's not doubt about that. Dr. Choate expects a lot from his students but you will end up learning a ton if you put in the effort.  He's always willing to help if you have questions and is very approachable.  The reading was interesting which is good because there's a lot of it.  He's probably my favorite professor at BYU.

Dr. Choate is a very good teacher.  I loved his lectures, I thought they were super interesting and the reading wasn't dry. But, he gives a heck of a lot of reading and you're expected to know it for exams.  His tests are long and exhausting. Give yourself 3 hours to do his tests.

Great teacher and great guy. Not necessarily the easiest class ever, but definitely worth it. Lecture was interesting and consisted mostly of class discussion. He is always willing to help you out whenever you need it. I'd recommend him!

If you have to take Historian's Craft TAKE IT FROM HIM.  I have heard horror stories from fellow peers about their professors. Unlike the others, Choate lets you choose your topic for your research paper,& it's the only big paper you have to write, as compared with 2 or 3.  The reading each week isn't too time-consuming, either & it's interesting

Great professor, super informative, easily understood and really addresses students needs. An incredibly nice guy who really enjoys teaching. Class is mainly lectures but does have peer discussions as well. If you pay attention and read the book, the class is very doable.

Very enthusiastic about this topic - I'd recommend the class to anyone interested in WWII. Not super tough class, but sometimes it was hard to make myself go. He was a good lecturer, but sometimes he was a bit scatter-brained.

Dr. Choate is very intelligent. Unfortunately, I did not have a good background in history before taking his class and consequently, I was buried in lecture. The main problem is that there is no textbook. If we had a text to study between class, I think that things would have been clearer.

He is a history buff that loves the subject.  However if you don't share that love, the class is difficult.  He covers a lot of material in a short amount of time.  His emphasis isn't on memorizing dates and times, but connecting ideas throughout time.  A hard teacher, but loves his material and loves the students too.

Tests are unbelievably difficult. He is kind of goofy...meaning he has a lot of strange ideas for helping...which in turn doesn't help. You don't need to read, but you do need to buy the books to reference them. He gives the chance for 5% extra credit, and unless you do it to supplement your grade, you'll die.

He is a nice guy but if you don't like history, this class won't make it any better. Tests are way hard, lectures cover tons of info. He's nice if you have questions, but be prepared to do a lot of test prep on your own. I would say to see if you can find an easier class.

At first struck me as very stringent, but when I talked to him after class--frustrated with a low paper grade--I realized how sincere and kind he is.  Very helpful.  Loves the students.  Grades hard, but will show you how to do well if you are willing to.  If you love the subject, you will love feeling like you took a class which really covered it.

He is a great professor, very knowledgable and helpful. I also took His307 from him and found him to be brilliant. Yes he is hard but you are in college not highschool. Every class should be hard because you are being tested. If your a slacker you shouln't be in college. But if you love European History you should take his classes

What a GREAT teacher! Quiet possible my favorite teacher at BYU (I have had many) He is willing to work with you and understands if personal issues come up, his assignments are fun, and challenging. His lectures are supplemented with pictures, and video clips to bring the material to life. I pulled off an A- , but I earned it

Choate is a good teacher.  His lectures were interesting and useful.  He actually used lecture notes, too,  which is always a plus.  His tests and papers were fair and he gives study guides.  The group projects were cool.  He made the material interesting, and he knows a lot about history.

I thought this was a great class. Professor Choate has a log to knowledge and enthusiasm for history which shows. He is very helpful and knows a lot. He did talk kind of fast in lecture but overall a good professor
Not a good lecturer.  He tries to cover copius amount of information in class.  If you are a slow note taker, do not take him.

Although he is respectful to the students, he is not a good teacher. His lectures are not coherent and he does not emphasize important points. He writes ambiguous terms on the very edge of the overhead. I did not learn from his class. He's a Yale graduate, but he absolutely cannot teach.
HE wasn't that bad!! Come on I actually thought he was funny! Sure it was hardish- but you can still pull a B pretty easially if you really study
Nice guy, bad lectures.  You have to do a lot on your own.

Impossible to get a good grade in his class.  Work load isn't bad at all and papers are easy to get good grades in.  Lectures are impossible to follow and tests are way harder than expected.  The average for the class on the first test was like a 60%.  If you're in his class prepare for death

This guy does not know what he is talking about. He even confuses himself. The class work isn't that hard, but lectures are more boring than watching re-runs of the PGA tour. The plus side is that if you study your brains out for the tests, you will do well. But man, is he bad.

The lecutures were very unorganized.  I hated going to class.  I found the test were more difficult than I was expecting.  I have always been a good student, but I do not think I will do very well in his class.
He has interesting lectures, but his tests will take you by surprise.  Not that much work required for the class, but it is hard to get a good grade.

Professor Christensen is hilarious! Lectures are very entertaining and sprinkles in lots of good life advice. If you want to skate by and do the bare minimum, I suggest a different professor. But if you are honestly trying your best, he is very helpful and will easily be a favorite of yours! I've already taken more classes from him!
Hands down of the best professors I've ever learned from. His quizzes are the only hard parts of his class, but other than that, I really enjoyed his lectures and he strengthened my testimony a ton.

He is a wonderful teacher and I loved being able to learn more about History from him. He emphasized tying out understanding of the Gospel into History, not using the Gospel to direct our understanding of History, instead he uses History to deepen our understanding of the Gospel.

An amazing guy and professsor. His lectures are so good. He does have a weekly quiz that some people find difficult but he offers extra credit on it and as long as you do the reading you'll do fine. His tests are well written and short. Attendance is important. Pretty much though he's just an amazing professor so take his class.

I LOVED THIS CLASS. One of the easiest classes I've ever taken at BYU. Very entertaining lectures and only one chapter of reading per week (super boring textbook, but readable), with one weekly quiz in class. The questions on the quizzes and exams were very straightforward and always what we covered in class. Easy A, but so fun & I learned a lot!

Super engaging! He incorporates gospel principles into every class. There are readings and weekly reading quizzes. These quizzes are not difficult if you've done the assigned readings. People have complained about the amount of readings but they have been cut down immensely over the years. This is nothing compared to American heritage!

Best history prof I've ever taken. However, there is A LOT of reading to do in this class. One chapter each week, with a 5 question quiz each Thursday. The quizzes were tough if you didn't go to TA labs. The 5 questions were usually easy once I got into the swing of things, but #6 was a random detail in the chap. Wouldn't count on 6/5 every week.

His lectures are awesome and most of the assignments were great. The problem was the weekly quizzes. There were 30+ pages of assigned reading for each unit but the weekly quizzes would be just 5 questions about seemingly random details from the reading. I did all the readings but still did poorly on these quizzes. Oddly memorization-based course.

For a 201 class Professor Christensen is a difficult grader. I'm a history major and many of our classes are research based, Professor Christensen loves memorization based quizes and a teaching style that is very different from the rest of the history dept. If you take his class be prepared to throughly study the textbook and lectures to suceed.

This is one of my favorite classes -- he is such a good professor and I loved attending his lectures because he taught modern applications to ancient history and I learned so much! The tests are pretty simple if you attend class and study, and there are 3 short essays. There is a quiz every week but if you do the reading you'll be totally fine.

This class was one of the most difficult generals I've ever taken. Grades are based on very few assignments and it's really hard to recover if you miss something. Essays are graded harshly on things that are never mentioned in class. The lectures were really interesting and engaging but if you need a good GPA, I definitely wouldn't recommend.

I took his class this semester and it has been one of my favorite classes ever! He's funny, well-knowledgeable, and is an engaging teacher you will enjoy listening to. Also, the textbook readings are long, and you have to read them, because you have weekly quizzes that ask about annoyingly specific things in the chapter. Be ready to work hard!

Wouldn't take this class again, quizzes are weekly and you have no idea what the questions could be on the large amounts of reading you had to do in between. You do learn a lot, but way more difficult than it needs to be.

This class was a pretty solid general. Lots of reading, but you can do well on the quizzes by doing the reading and going to TA hours. The professor's lectures are interesting, but he tends to get political and sometimes makes mildly offensive comments. The tests are based on lecture, and the assignments are easy if you follow the rubric.

This is probably the hardest class I've taken at BYU. Lots of reading. Don't believe him if he says a quiz will be easy or obvious. It almost never is. There aren't very many assignments, so recovering from a bad grade is really hard to do. I really hate this class lol. I'm a decent student and have never felt more helpless.

this class is such a joke. Weekly quizes that he claims arent going to be too hard yet they pull from such niche info in the textbook. Like its unreal. Its a class for try hards and this professor seems to not care that everyone here is taking it for a general and not our major. I promise you will regret this class.
I don't think there's a professor with a gamer personality. He's the epitome of those who can't do, teach

The dude knows how to teach. He is a somewhat difficult professor but he truly cares and really taught me how to research and write better. He always incorporated the gospel as well, which was nice! Highly reccomend!!

If you're a history major, take this class from Dr. Christensen! He gears the class towards prepping you for an actual career in history. Everything he teaches, he actually practices and he shows it. He didn't assign any busy work so the class is very self-guided. It was tough, but very rewarding.

If you're like me and skim textbook readings (or skip them completely), you'll struggle in this class. The weekly quizzes pull information directly from the textbook, and you'll fail unless you took meticulous notes on the assigned chapter. The study guides are vague and don't prepare you for the tests. Take HIST201 from someone else.

PROTECT THIS MAN AT ALL COSTS. I WISH TO PERSONALLY THANK HIM. I NOW LOVE HISTORY BECAUSE OF HIM. HIS HUMOR IS PEAK! HE ADDRESSES HOW BYU CULTURE AND MODERN CULTURE CAN BE EXPLAINED BY HISTORY WHICH IS SO COOL AND MUCH NEEDED. ASSIGNMENTS ARENT HARD. I WOULD CREATE FLASHCARDS TO STUDY EACH CHAPTER. VERY GENEROUS GRADER. HONORED TO TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

I have despised history pretty much my whole life and I was not looking forward to this class in the slightest but Prof. Christensen really changed my opinion on history as a whole. His lectures are so interesting and his expectations for you are so clear and easily understood. Easily the best class I've taken at BYU.

An easyish class because the workload isn't that bad, but it's hard to get an A. I would spend a couple hours reading the entire chapter of the textbook, but it's hard know what's important to remember. So, I switched to listening to the podcast his TAs did (Dorm Room History on YouTube). About 45 minutes of listening and I understood more content.

If you love history you'll probably enjoy his lectures. Lots of readings, with in class quizzes once a week. Study guide isn't really helpful for preparing for the tests. A couple papers on additional lengthy readings. Spent lots of time not knowing what I should be looking for.

Loved his lectures, has a dry, kinda sassy humor that makes his classes that much more entertaining. But there IS a ton of readings, with weekly quizzes (so pay attention.) Tests were difficult, but reasonably so. You'll read the Popul Vuh, but it's not bad. Overall, great teacher, I love going to his class

He is one of the best professors I have ever had. I loved him so much. If you can take anything from him then DO! I learned so much and everything he teaches is so helpful and logical. Made me want to switch to history and major in that. He made a class that could have sucked into one of my favorite college classes

Be prepared to do a lot of reading/studying for in-class quizzes, which were difficult (helpful study guides for midterms/final though). Aside from that, this professor is wonderful! I especially appreciated how he tied elements of the gospel to class content. I genuinely looked forward to each lecture! Not an easy class, but definitely worth it!

I loved having Christensen! His lectures were always great and he was very funny. You will have to read pretty much the entire textbook to get an A because he gives a lot of quizzes on it, but his lectures cover all of the material you need for the final.

I loved this class! His lectures were incredibly enjoyable and he only puts what's on the slides on the test. There was an extra book we had to read on our own and had it's own separate test. The exams are super straightforward and more general. Also three short essays that are easy to ace. I did all of mine the night before and got 100%.

I enjoyed this class a lot. Professor Christensen is hilarious which makes his lectures both informative and entertaining. You have to read around 30 pages a week in order to do well on his weekly quizzes, but he offers extra credit and the exams are very easy if you attend all the lectures.

There is tons of content in the book, but he narrows it down to specific things to focus on. He could make this course much harder. Work with your TA and study throughout the semester and you will be fine. Send your writing to the TA for help.
He is hilarious and you can learn so much from his lectures if you choose to. His BoM lecture is insane!

Tests are worth 55% of your grade which is atrocious especially since there is so much content in the class and you have no idea what you will be tested on. He provided study guides but they were actually worthless on the midterm and final. Take this class from someone else who knows how to set up a class for students success.

Dr Christensen was fantastic. His lectures are super interesting, coming from someone who doesn't care for history. A large part of the grade comes from weekly quizzes based on the readings and his lectures. They're pretty simple if you've come to class and do the reading. Only 1-2 hours of HW a week. Despite what some people say, he's awesome.

This class is pretty easy and straightforward, but the professor is a little insufferable. And never ask a question that you could conceivably find out the answer to on your own or he will make fun of you.

The way he structured his class just seemed unorthodox. Weekly quizzes that destroy your grade if you do bad on them, but didn't help your grade if you aced them. He claims his test questions aren't specific, and for the most part they aren't, but he'll often throw in an outofpocket question from some random chapter about something never discussed
Not a great teacher and test content is not covered in the lectures. His TAs are also the worst TAs I've ever worked with, they have no clue what they're doing and their grading is very inconsistent.
Great teacher but does not prepare you for weekly quizzes or tests. Class grading is very test-heavy, and he is very specific about citations.

The lectures were boring and he doesn't let you take pics of the slides or post them. There is a textbook ch for each week and 1 quiz a week which are okay if you read. The tests are challenging and very detail focused so you have to study. The TA's were not helpful when writing the papers and were very particular. not my fav class but not bad.

Easily my favorite class. He's funny and makes good analogies to help the history connect. Felt like I was actually learning, not just getting a grade. Quizzes in class every week, go review with TAs beforehand and they'll be a breeze. Same with tests and papers. Textbook is helpful, read as much as you can, but if you miss a bit it's okay.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class because the lectures were interesting despite the topic being pretty boring. I felt that the tests were harshly graded and because they were a large part of the grade it brought my overall score down a lot. Make sure that if you take this course to do the readings and use Quizlet to study for the in-class quizzes.

Dr. Christensen is hands down the best history teacher I have ever had. You can tell he truly loves his job and history. The tests, weekly quizzes, and four one page essays are easy. He has clear expectations for the class and has amazing lectures. If you pay attention during the lectures, take notes, and read the chapters, you'll get an A.

Prof Christensen is the best professor at BYU. I hated this class at first because I don't love history, but overtime I really enjoyed the lectures. Everyone should have a chance to take from this man. He's too cool and loves his job. King Arthur the TA is graduating but go to the other TAs and they will help you SO MUCH! Lit lit lit class.

I really liked this class! Honestly, it's only hard if you don't read, don't go to TA hours, and don't pay attention in lectures. If you do, those things you'll be fine. He is straightforward and open to meeting with you if you have any questions. TA hours also help a lot to understand important concepts. Overall, great professor!

There are 3 tests that are pretty difficult. There are 4 essays that are not too complicated. Weekly quizzes are pretty challenging. There are some options for extra credit. It is a challenging course but the easiest way to get this credit in my opinion. Christensen clearly loves history and makes the lecture entertaining.

Professor Christensen is an incredible lecturer. He's genuinely really funny and has a ton of passion and knowledge about his course material. Be prepared to read a LOT because a large portion of your grade comes from reading quizzes. I would 110% take another one of his classes because I learned a TON and enjoyed it a lot.

Brother Christensen is such a great lecturer and his love for history is infectious. He always makes sure to interweave life lessons, too. That being said, watch out for the weekly quizzes, they can get brutal. You need to do the readings and show up to class, too. Overall, it wasn't an "easy" GE class but I wouldn't choose any other civ credit.

This class was life-changing & Prof. Christensen was amazing! He taught me how to become a better researcher & got me excited to write about history. Tough grader, but pushed me to new heights & encouraged me to work hard. You gotta be dedicated & stay on top of your work, but you will learn a lot. Permanently changed my perspective of history.
Dr. Christensen made the class super interesting and very achievable for non-history majors. There is much work to do and it's easy to pass.

Professor Christensen was amazing! His lectures always kept us engages despite their length. Weekly readings take about an hour or two out of class and material is quizzed. Take notes of his powerpoint slides, and study those notes, you will do fine. He has one midterm and another test over the book Popol Vuh. Six 1-2 page writing assignments

This is my favorite professor because of how amazing his lectures are. The course isn't easy and I'm not into history but I am so glad I took it with him. In addition, I went to talk to him about two of my short essays that the TAs graded and he gave me a hundred percent on both so make sure you ask him questions. Overall amazing

Least fav professor I've had so far. The course would be great if you could just sit and learn, cuz the lectures are super interesting. However, he does not set you up to succeed. He tests on such obscure things, so you have to study every single bullet point of notes. Take from someone else if you just need it for a general credit. Not worth it.

one of the best lecturers in byu for sure. class is a good mix of history, spirituality, humor, and learning. just watch out for weekly in-class quizzes that can get a little tricky, but if you go to the TA review hours, you'll be okay. best professor for history 201 credit!

Mark knows a lot about history and is a good teacher. I recommend his class. lots of reading and there are quizzes each week based on the reading. They aren't too difficult though if you do the work you can get a good score. There's a lecture everyday so it gets a little repetitive but he's good at keeping you engaged.

Professor Christensen is awesome! His lectures are very interesting and all the test information is right in the slides. There is a weekly chapter and quiz. Before the quizzes go to the TA lectures, they really helped!

He is a great teacher and makes history more entertaining than it should be. Funny jokester. The class consists mostly of textbook reading and a quiz each week. TAs are very helpful! He implemented a study guide for the test and it helped. The tests are not too hard if you study. Overall, I enjoyed my experience. I hate history, but I love Mark!

Professor Christensen is definitely the one to take for History 201. His lectures are great, and it's important you show up for them as the notes you take are directly reflective of the material on the weekly quizzes/midterm/final. Make sure to go to TA office hours for help on the weekly quizzes and reading responses!

Probably my favorite teacher ever here at BYU. Amazing lectures that help you find an interest in any section of history. Fairly light load, wasn't too overbearing with assignments. Fantastic teacher and wish i could take him again.

Professor Christensen made history so interesting. He taught boring parts of history in an entertaining way and always made connections to modern life. Not politically charged at all which was refreshing for the humanities department. Get to class a bit early and ask the TA's your questions. I wouldn't want to take history from anyone else.
That he is amazing
He is the best professor ever.

LOVED his class and lectures! So good. He teaches history in a way that's super entertaining and applicable to everyone, and I felt that the workload wasn't too heavy. It's pretty doable. The ta's can be a bit rude but other than that I loved everything about his class!! don't miss an opportunity to take a class from him

Prof Christensen was an amazing professor and I really learned a lot in his class but it was tough to get a good grade. The readings are boring and long and the quizzes test obscure facts. The TAs will save you in this class. Overall liked the lectures and would take again but be ready to study and be with the TAs for hours to do well on tests.
Prof Christensen is a great lecturer. He is straightforward about what he expects and stays consistent. Highly recommend!

Dr. Christensen's lectures are the best! He is hilarious and makes even the more bland parts of history at least mildly interesting. However his tests and weekly reading quizzes have no study guide or anything which can sometimes make it feel like you're going on a wild goose chase to internalize as much as you can before regurgitating it on a test

Good teacher with enjoyable lectures. Makes history interesting for sure, but his tests/quizzes are pretty specific with no study guide or studying advice other than "read the textbook". Some bigger readings/essays throughout the semester, but they are manageable. Pray you have a good TA and go to their office hours to review before tests.
Professor Christensen was a really good teacher. His course is really strait-forward and if you follow the syllabus you'll be fine. Super awesome experience.
Just kinda an average professor. No real feelings either way. Teaches history well, can be really funny at times, but nothing that will blow you away. Be prepared for weekly quizzes.

He actually seems like a super chill dude but the class is not really set up to help people succeed.
Why?
1. There is nothing posted on LearningSuite so you need to look at the syllabus for everything
2. there are no study guides or things to give you extra help
3. both major midterms were placed only two weeks apart being open on a weekend only

I did enjoy listening to his lectures but he did not set you up to succeed in the class. He gives quizzes once a week about random things from the textbook and gives you no warning on what they will be, so basically; I have read the textbook about three times in preparation for those quizzes. Go to study sessions with the TAs for quizzes and exams!

I got an A in every other class but this one was incredibly difficult. He downplays how hard and specific his tests are. The class is very unorganized on LS. He doesn't inform students of what's ahead. The lectures would be fine except that every Friday he has a 5 questions quiz that is incredibly specific and often haven't even been covered yet.
I loved this class. The content was interesting and Professor Christensen is really funny and really passionate. You have to make sure you read the textbook to do well on the weekly quizzes.

Professor Christensen is a really great teacher. He made class fun and interesting, and he is amazingly sarcastic at times. He clearly loves history and loves teaching, and you can see that in the way he interacts with students. Honestly, the hardest part of this class was the reading and weekly reading quizzes, but that wasn't even that bad.

If I could just go sit and listen to professor Christensen's lectures, then I would love this class! I feel like he didn't realize just how difficult his class is though. You're only graded on a couple things, and the weekly quizzes are very unpredictable which is challenging. He gives great lectures though.

Absolutely loved Professor Christensen's class! He's a super funny and sarcastic guy and his lectures were funny and applicable. He does such a great job teaching usually boring subjects (at least for me). There are weekly quizzes but they aren't hard if you've read the material and studied for them. I will definitely take a class from him again!

Honestly, he is a phenomenal teacher. I loved taking this class from him. He is sarcastic and hilarious, definitely making for good lectures. Weekly reading quizzes, but they are only 5 questions (with a bonus) and not that hard. If you try, you can definitely pull a good grade. HIGHLY recommend!!!

Professor Christensen is super funny, and is super knowledgeable about ancient America. Most of your grade is based on a few essays, and he expects some participation, but for the most part, the class is just discussions based on some fairly entertaining readings.

Christensen is a good person and an ok teacher, but I think his course his set up poorly. Graded on very few things (weekly reading quizzes, 3 exams, 1 paper) so if you don't do great on 1 thing, you're screwed. TA's aren't very helpful, don't provide reviews or study guides for exams-makes it hard to study.

He's absolutely hilarious! I loved him. Weekly (easy) quiz on the reading. He gives exact outlines for the notes and uses those same notes to write his tests. There is one big paper, which had a frustratingly vague rubric, but generous grading. Only downside is he won't post notes, so if you miss class, you have to find a friend.

Very funny and charismatic guy. My favorite class last semester. Showing up to class is crucial, as he doesnt post his slides on learning suite. Some people dont like his 5 question quizzes, but if you come to class and skim over the end of the chapters, you should be set. Plus theres a bonus. The TAs keep the questions fairly straightforward.

The lectures were pretty good for a GE history course, and the workload wasn't so bad either. However there were some administrative issues such as changing test dates without announcing first and not being flexible with in class quizzes. The tests are ABSURDLY specific, even though he claims to test us only on "major patterns" of history.

Professor Christensen is amazing, one of the best professors at BYU. His lectures are engaging and informative. He's a straight up guy and is very clear with his expectations which is so nice. There are weekly quizzes but if you come to class and do some reading, you'll be fine. Tests aren't too hard. And he's funny, so coming to class is worth it.
Interesting class, but what I liked most was Professor Christensens takes on life and spirituality. Do the reading, take notes, and you will be fine.

Prof. Christensen was super funny, but I seriously struggled in this class. Weekly reading quizzes are pretty easy, but the exams were rough. They're made directly from his slides, but there's a lot of broad information that's hard to remember. Super interesting content, hard to remember and hard to come back from a bad grade.

For tests he doesn't give you any ways to focus your studies and says "study your notes" which is literally everything from the whole semester. He is vague for what he expects from us. His slides and lectures don't make sense and his teaching is all over the place, and we bounce from topic to topic and place to place. He is also very condescending

I've really enjoyed this class with Profesor Christensen. I loved his lectures and I feel like I have a greater understanding of the world. The only assignments are reading quizzes every week, a short paper, and a couple of tests. This class requires some work but if you try you'll definitely get a good grade. Overall I loved this class!

Professor Christensen is fricking awesome. I absolutely loved him and he was one of my fav profs. Really funny and engaging. Lots and lots of reading is required for this class. Entire semester revolves around 3 tests (one being about a book), a book report, and a weekly reading quiz. Not a lot of opportunities to save your grade on previous grades

Prof. Christensen is a great dude. Super funny and really cares about his students. Quizzes every week are based off the readings (which aren't super long) so do them! Don't skip class because the exams are based totally off his slides. Overall great class, super eye-opening.
Difficult, but doable

Professor Christensen is in no way a terrible professor, however, his class was very difficult for me. There are about 2-3 hours of reading after each class and all of those hours of reading boil down into 5 questions that will make or break your grade each class period. I did not like the organization of his class, but he is very knowledgeable.

His lectures are entertaining and he recognizes that not everyone is a history major so he tries to make the content applicable to everyone. Makes it very clear how class will go and how to get an A. If you do the reading, the class should be no problem.

If you want to be a high school history teacher, this class is for you. I think that less than 10/160 students answered a question all semester long. He is a super nice guy but the class was way too hard. Tests try to trick you with no review at all. Hours of reading weekly followed by 5 question weekly quizzes that decide your whole grade.

Listen up if you got B's in history in HS. This class will not be easy, or fun for you. And I tried hard to have a good attitude. I'm just giving to you straight. I did none of the readings, and my cousin did all of them, and we both got Bs - the exact same grade. He doesn't do extra credit or zoom chat. He's funny, though.

Nice guy. Makes a lot of jokes in class, and is very open-minded. Tests are directly from the reading and lectures, so they aren't too difficult. The two papers on the books we read were very difficult though, particularly as there wasn't a clear path to get a great grade on the papers. It's an overall easier class. Makes a good Gen-Ed.

Professor Christensen is a nice guy, he is really passionate about his work. He tells some nice stories in class. Study, study, study the notes for the tests!! He was a little unclear on what he wanted in the essays, but go to the TAs and ask them. The weekly quizzes were hard too, but go to the TAs for help. He isnt lenient on rounding points.

Great choice for a Civ 1 credit. To succeed do three things: 1. Read the chapters, especially the broad summary paragraphs 2. Write down the slides and know them well (don't worry about dates, there was never a question about dates) 3. Don't procrastinate the papers and use the TAs to make sure you did them right.

Prof. Christensen is an AMAZING teacher and really chill& understanding. there are 2 papers (which you will get a good grade if u actually read and try), 2 tests (are just on lecture material so write that down!) and chapter quizzes from the textbook. which can be hard but as long as you are decently prepared you should do ok. overall amazing class

How can anyone find his class hard? He never tests you on specifics like dates and names and everyone I knew who skimmed through the textbook and paid attention to his lectures got an A. The weekly quizzes are insanely easy and the tests are not hard. I'm not a great writer and didn't do all the readings but he still gave me A- on the essays.

Prof Christensen is a super great guy. He really cares about his students and is great during his lectures. There are weekly textbook readings, but if you read you will be fine. There are also two major papers, but he grades them super hard. I spent weeks on mine and only got a B. Like I said, he really cares about his subject and loves to teach it

Professor Christensen was a great guy and made this class very doable. There are quizzes every week, and you have to read the textbook if you want to pass them. Only 2 papers, a midterm, and a final, so you aren't graded on much. I would recommend taking this class for an easy history credit.

Prof. Christensen is a hilarious teacher. He tries to make history relatable and understandable. There is a quiz almost every week, 2 essays, 1 midterm and a final (that's it), so if you're not a good test taker, maybe rethink your choice. Besides that, Prof. Christensen is a really great and caring teacher. Totally recommend him.

Professor Christensen is very clear about how you'll be graded. He wants you to take careful notes of every slide in lectures, so if you miss a lecture make sure you get the notes from someone else. He's funny and engaging in his lectures, though not big on class participation. He's responsive to emails, but not very willing to be flexible.

There is one chapter of reading per week which comes to about 10 pages a class max. He then lectures on the third. Quizzes each week require the reading, ask TA's questions from chapter to pass! Also 6/5 possible on each quiz. The test is from lecture notes: GO TO TA HOURS. The first paper wasn't bad, the book was shorter than it looks.

Fairly easy quiz every week to test you on the weekly chapter, lots of extra credit. Midterm and final are entirely based on his slides. One long paper on City of God but as long as you use quotes and justify you will get a good grade. Nice guy and funny lectures.

By far the easiest Civ 1 professor. All you have to do is read a chapter and take a quiz each week. I always went to the TAs right before and they would give all the answers. The tests are so easy (1 midterm and 1 final not cumulative), and only have the most basic concepts from the lectures. The essay is really easy too (just 4 pages). SO FUNNY.

He's chill, and this was an easy class for the Civ 1 GE. It's mostly lecture, but he's engaging and funny. Quizzes every Friday, one midterm, a final, and one paper (although he might be adding another). The TAs are almost always available, and he has office hours as well, but the TAs do the grading. *I finished this class online due to Covid19

Honestly, this class wasn't nearly as hard as some people made it out to be. His lectures are really fun and interesting, and if you pay attention and come to class you'll do well on the midterm and the final. Some of the weekly quizzes are tougher, but not anything crazy if you try on the readings. Overall, a really good professor!

Some people like his style, but not me. Youre graded on very few things: 20% in-class quizzes that are tough, 25% on a paper based on a long book reading, and 55% on two exams (midterm and final). Weekly quizzes were short answers and nit-picky from large readings, essay grading not fair, and tests had some short-essays. Take it from someone else.

Mark is such a great guy! He tries his best to make lectures interesting and fun with cool references and funny jokes. There is a chapter of reading as well as a quiz each week which is doable. You have weekly reading quizzes, a midterm, paper, and final. Not too much work, I just studied my notes and the last pages of the chapter for quizzes.

I have LOVED having Professor Christensen. This class overall was my favorite at BYU. He is very clear in what he expect and to be honest he doesn't expect much. If you read and go to class the class will be a breeze. There is extra credit. He is understanding. I loved his lectures. PLEASE TAKE HIS CLASS- YOU WON'T REGRET IT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This is the hardest class I have ever taken at BYU. It is the only A- I have ever received. There are reading quizzes every week that are ridiculously hard. They are worth a good portion of your grade. I would read the chapter 3 times and take notes and would still only get a 3/5. If you are taking this class, take it from a different person!!!!!!!

This class was my favorite for the semester. Despite what most people may say, the work load is not that hard. You read 20 pages a week split between 3 days (about 6.5). Once a week there is a 5 point quiz on the chapter. Other than that, there is one midterm (based completely on his slides) and one short essay on "The City of God" book. And final.

Life lessons, thats what you'll get out of this course. MLA is not good enough, Chicago style is business. Get ready to read. You have to make it clear you participated each class, that is how the participation grade goes. I would not take it again.
Fantastic Class, great lecturer. Very consistent in the routine, you cover one chapter a week, have a reading quiz each week.
Chill, down to earth guy

Even if you love history like I do this class will still be boring. Every single day he just reads off his slides and expects you to write every little thing down. Not interesting at all. He is an extremely hard grader, especially for a GE class. Even if you talk to him about your grades he is very unforgiving. Doesnt seem to care about students

He's really passionate about history and always accessible. I didn't like the class mostly because I wasn't interested in ancient history at all. There is a lot of textbook reading and in class quizzes every week. The first test was really hard to prepare for because he doesn't hold exam reviews and there is a ton of material.

Worst class I've taken at BYU. If you're not a good test taker, don't take his class because 70% of your final grade is based on the midterms/final. If you don't frequently ask/answer questions, you won't get above a C on your participation grade, which is a significant portion of your final grade. Readings are long and quizzes are very specific.

Professor Christensen is one of my favorite teachers at BYU! His lectures are amazing because he is HILARIOUS! He always gives you enough time to write down everything from his power points, which you should use to study for the weekly quizzes! Reading the textbook helps a lot as well. Definitely take this class from him!!!! :)

Prof Christensen was really easy to listen to in lectures and is obviously very smart and passionate about his field. Lots of reading and weekly quizzes, but if you ask the TA's you can make up any and all quizzes for full points at the end of the semester.

I loved his lectures! He was really interesting and passionate. But there are only 2 exams, and its really hard to prepare for the first one, and it was a difficult test! By the final, you know what to expect, but I might be too late. Also there's a giant novel you have to read and write a report on and its worth a huge part of the grade.

He's a nice guy! I struggled in the beginning of the semester because I wasn't sure of what he wanted. But, I met with him, and after that did great in the class. You have a quiz every week, but at the end of the semester, you can make up any quiz for full points. The readings do take a long time, and the paper wasn't my favorite.

Three papers, a dozen or so quizzes, and participation points. Lectures are fun! He grades papers pretty generously, but the quizzes are hard. You have to really dig into the readings to do well. Our class quiz average was a 72% overall. If you go in and talk to him for advice on the papers, he'll tell you just what he wants and you'll get an A.

For HIST201 he was engaging and an entertaining teacher given the course material. Readings before every class and the essay book did take some time every night, but if you pay attention and do all that is asked, it's not hard to get a B. Doing the necessary hw was often better than all of it. Overall a great guy and a good route to fulfill the GE

Dr. Christensen is awesome. His research focuses on religion in Latin America and is able to answer basically any question you could bring up. His quizzes are pretty easy if you do the readings and come to class. The three papers that he has you write are very straightforward and not too difficult to write. Solid class.

I loved this class! He really cares about what he teaches and relates well to his students. He will take pauses during the lecture to make sure everyone writes down the info on the powerpoints (also serves as the study guide for the test but he won't post them so take notes!). Quizzes are weekly and easy as long as you go to class and do the readin

I don't particularly enjoy history, so the lectures could get boring at times. Professor Christensen does treat his students right! He remembers what its like to be an undergrad and realizes that this isn't our only class. There is a considerable amount of reading, but no real homework. One paper, one midterm, weekly quiz, and the final.

This class was an absolute nightmare! History is not my forte to begin with, and the professor could be pretty boring to listen to. I didn't know what I should focus on to prepare for his exams. He also makes you read a way long book in addition to the normal text just for the purpose of writing a 3-4page paper. I do not recommend this class!

Christensen is very insightful and makes what would normally be a very boring class, be interesting. I normally find World Civ boring but he's funny and makes the class interesting. The textbook isn't too bad, but he also makes you read another book as well (City of God) that is a little over 500 pages.

His actual in class teaching is fine. However, the ai grading system they use is broken and makes most assignments impossible to do. They have too much trust in it and will trust the word of the ai over the word of the student. It's also an all or nothing grading system, so you can do 99% of an assignment and get a 0 because you forgot 1 thing.

Professor Clement is a very caring professor who wants every student to succeed. However, get ready for a TON of work involved in CS260. It feels like you're learning a new coding language every week, which was difficult. Professor Clement does a great job of providing extra credit opportunities, and I loved his spiritual moments and field trips

The CS 224 online section lacks clear examples for the homework and slides. My suggestion is sign up for the online section but go in person. Doing so will give you a more lenient homework and project schedule compared to an in-person section. Dr. Clement is always there to help you if you need help.
Not really present, doesnt express ideas thoroughly or easy enough to understand

He is a nice guy, but boring. He talked about what coding you are doing, but hardly about the practicality of actually doing it (how to code), which made it hard for me. You build a website but the class structure is bad. Later checkpoints (JavaScript and React) are harder. Class attendance almost isn't worth it; I learned from google and chatGPT.

The lecture side of class wasn't really necessary at all since the online notes had all the important information. The class also isn't given enough time for your knowledge of these topics to actually stick. My final project ended up using so much copy & paste because of this. Wish it could be extended to a full year instead of one semester.
Most of it was online for me so i hardly ever saw the professor. You just read some github pages and work on your website.

Great class. Some bugs in the material because they just moved from Vue to React but otherwise a great class. Lots of projects but they were pretty easy. Some homeworks and two exams but altogether very doable.

It isn't a hard class, but there isn't a whole lot of help. The TA's honestly can't help you learn, but they aren't harsh graders. You are asked to copy and paste a lot and I didn't feel like I learned a lot from the course. Professor Clement is a nice guy, it isn't necessarily a bad class, but if you are going to take 260, don't take it from him.
Honestly just difficult to work with, doesn't do a great job of structuring lectures or tutorials to cultivate learning, and doesn't do a great job of assisting students that show a need for help.

Dr. Clement is a great professor and a great guy! He really wants you to succeed and gives you the resources to do so. I took his online, on-demand class and would highly recommend this format for any CS student.

This is a remote, on-demand class, so I didn't interact with Dr. Clement much, but when I did, it was only positive interactions. The class is not too difficult (there are a number of large projects), but I learned a ton of very useful skills. I would highly recommend taking this class from Dr. Clement!

Weekly labs (for the most part) aren't easy but professor gives lots of videos that offer lots of help. Also, a good TA queue. Reading quizzes are fine because they have unlimited submissions. Exams aren't too bad.

Complete waste of my time and tuition money. 90% of the class is online tutorials that you can already use for free, and any tutorials made by the professor were awful. After turning in one assignment late I was told I was "in danger of failing" even though there's no penalty for late work. Save your time and take something more useful.

Clement did a bad job explaining how to code anything. He gives huge assignments and no guidance. Most of the projects shouldnt have been hard, but without guidance it would take hours of meeting with tutors to even understand the data structures, let alone code them. I recommend you take classes from a professor who actually teaches you.

Didn't enjoy lectures at all, made most of the labs way beyond our capacity and I think they were an ineffective way of teaching us the concepts that he was trying to teach. That being said he's better than Roper

This was the worst organized class I have ever taken. It was clear they were changing the order of the units, but it felt incomplete. More than once, we were expected to use a concept that we would learn later in the semester. Relied heavily on online resources outside of class to get a good grade.

I liked Dr. Clement. His class was really hard, but I think that is the point. I spent 15+ hours a week on his class, sometimes more. I give him four stars because his rubrics and class material weren't very organized.

He always had very helpful videos to help you get started on the labs if you needed them and knew the common places where students would get stuck. The code is more complicated, so you have to identify most of the bugs yourself. Readings built nicely and made the quizzes easy. Super useful programming skills.

Clement only hindered my learning in this class. His only teaching consisted of occasional videos for the labs wherein he would contradict the written instructions and also the github lab specs. I didn't finished a single lab with a confident feeling about the material--and this is coming from someone who gave the class + TA's wayy too much time.

Dr. Clement really cares about his students. CS 235 is not the easiest class, but he prepares you well for each lab you do over the semester. He was almost always willing to meet with me when I got helplessly stuck. He is super flexible with due dates as he knows students are trying to juggle their lives and his CS projects. I love this dude.

Dr. Clement is not one of those CS teachers that wants to see you suffer. He genuinely tries to help students succeed, understand concepts, and have fun. Even though the class was on demand, I felt that he was really trying to be a part of the students' lives. When I had trouble getting labs done on the assigned date, he was willing to work with me

(Taken OnDemand) Great class for programmers on the data structures that hold memory (vectors, lists, etc). The concepts were taught through reading quizzes, which were sometimes hard to follow. Labs are computer graded so you know your score beforehand. Lots of work outside of class. Maybe 7-8 hours a week on average, depending on your bugs.

I've never felt as overwhelmed as fast as I did at the start of this class semester. He throws you in headfirst, expecting you to figure out the Linux command line, a new (terrible) IDE, and the monstrous weekly labs completely on your own. I think it's largely the class, though, not the professor.

Professor Clement is great. Lets your turn in assignments late. Make's it easy to get good grades. Is super nice and very understanding. The only strange thing about 260 is that for must questions, he just googled the answer. But, I guess thats what most web programmers do these days.

If you thought 142 was a breeze, I'd recommend taking the online section of 235. There really aren't lectures and you can just do homework, labs, etc. on your own, which was really nice for me. Assignments have unlimited retakes and the grading is pretty lenient as long as you follow what's going on in the class.

This was the most difficult class I've ever taken. Prof. Clement does a terrible job explaining concepts and the labs are incredibly difficult. He would create such a needlessly difficult framework you'd have to follow that I would spend 5-6 hours every lab just trying to decipher his code before I would even start my code. Don't take from Clement!

This teacher is the nicest and one of the most understanding people I've ever met. I had a rough semester dealing with personal problems and every time I emailed him he was caring and helped me out. Never had someone as great as this.

One of the friendliest professors you'll ever have. Great guy. Very easy class (like I-didn't-take-the-midterm-and-still-got-an-A easy). The course teaches hirable skills such as Node, (Basic) AWS, MongoDB, and VuejsI just wish we got into more the more robust features of each of them. Really wish it pushed me more than it did.

It is an online class. He really cares about students. Although it is an online class, he always answers student's questions as soon as he can. The e-book is somewhat helpful, but you can find a free version of it on the internet. So, opt it out. If you take an online course, make sure you understand the reading. Some of the Labs are really heavy.

Good, funny, genuine dude. Took him for CS235 and it was great. Took him for CS260 and it seemed like he was just using tutorials made by a different prof, and didn't even look at the tutorials until in class with us. I stopped going to class because it was useless, and the tutorials are easy to just do online, outside of class.
He is a really nice guy, but his lectures really just are not helpful. I took CS 418 and CS 260 from him and rarely attended class because they just weren't helpful.

Dr. Clement is the best professor in the CS department right now (writing this as a senior). His classes focus on writing actual code that help significantly with the labs. I felt that I have learned more in the two classes I have taken from him than anyone else.

Way too confident in the relevance of his class to the industry, but it is just an intro to web programming. Easy class. Doesn't use a book. You'll teach yourself everything online but its a decent start. BYU really should have a second part to this course to cover more depth but they'd rather send you to Dev Mountain for this kind of programming.

Professor Clement is a very caring person. He doesn't quite fit the beastly CS BYU teacher mold because he truly want to help you succeed and will do his best to help you understand. I do think that he is a bit outdated in the technologies that he is accustomed to using. I'm not entirely sure he has a background in profession web development.

418 is great with Dr. Clement. Majority of the work is through Rosalind problems which are like small coding interview questions. Choose your own language (most do Python), group projects are super interesting but slightly more challenging. Really enjoyed this class as a CS elective. Most of the quizzes you can turn in late at no penalty.

CS 260 does NOT teach you how to code. It teaches you how to copy/paste and tries to teach you over 6 programming languages in 4 months (I've learned nothing). Prof' Clement is nice but he doesn't even know what he's doing half the time and will frequently ask students what's wrong with his code during lecture. Don't take CS 260 from Clement.
Great teacher! Fun to listen to, very willing to help you learn, wants you to love coding! Wants all of us to get A's and makes it very possible to do so! By far one of the best CS teachers!!!

Doctor Clement has been my favorite CS professor I've had while at BYU. He cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He helps by giving a good amount of code on each lab and if you know what you're doing, you never need to go to class because he publishes everything online. I could not give him higher praise! Take him if you can!

Dr. Clement is so awesome. He is a perfect example of how every professor should be. He main focus is not to fit students into a bell curve, but really cares about you learning the material and enjoying the class. super caring, and unbelievably understanding. He wants you to succeed, and will do anything to help you get an A.

Professor Clement basically just wants you to get through the material and complete the labs. The class is set up so you will succeed. He gives you a lot of the code, so technically you could just copy/paste some things; however, I felt that I learned a lot in Professor Clement's class. Good professor, good environment.

Prof. Clement's web programming course is very doable. Unlike most 3-credit CS classes, it actually feels like 3 credits instead of 6. You do some very cool projects. There are two midterms and a final, but they're not hard. You could get through the class just through copy-pasting, sure, but all the resources are there for you to master it.

Awesome guy, great class structure. Learned more in this class than any other CS class. At times there was maybe too much copy/paste. There is SO much material taught but it's taught in a simple way and in a way you can succeed. I'm going to finish with 100% in the class. Can use internet on assignments and tests. 10/10 would recommend.

Super great guy, awesome, caring professor, but this class was an absolute mess. The class is very poorly designed to actually help anyone learn anything. Mostly you learn how to copy and paste. Easy A, but I am no more capable of web programming than when I started the class 4 months ago. Very frustrating assignments.

I dreaded CS 235 but he made this class awesome and even changed up the labs to make it easier.  He even threw out an old one and made a new lab to help us learn the uses of maps (associative arrays). Remember this class is based off the text book so all of the lab code is found there.

Good: he's a genuinely great guy. Explains the material well. Easy to get lots of extra credit. Bad: labs are time consuming (not surprising for a CS class).  Sometimes the specs he would tell us in class were different from what the TA's would tell us, causing confusion. And, there were easy but in-class quizzes each day, worth 10% of your grade.

He explains things well, and it's interesting, albeit a bit slow. I preferred to just read the textbook and get it over with. He relies a lot on the textbook, to the point of directing students to just copy the book's code on some labs, which I thought was kind of lame. Also makes us do UMLs for every lab, which are totally the worst.

This class is mostly seniors doing an easy elective. If you are an underclassman, however, expect a challenge, because the prof goes FAST and you WILL get lost.  You frantically try and keep up in class and then learn everything by yourself at home via tutorials. He IS forgiving, which is SO nice.

Dr. Clement is really nice and cares about his students. We often programmed during class together and he taught us whatever we needed and wanted to know. At first I didn't like the freestyle structure of the class but it grew on me. I learned a lot of valuable skills and technologies. Dr. Clement is great!

Far and away my favorite CS Professor at BYU. Clement cares about students, and will do whatever he can to make sure you are successful. Tests are fair, projects are interesting and worthwhile, and anyone can get an A if they try. This is my second class with Clement, and I would honestly take any class that he teaches

This is one of the most hated CS classes at BYU, but Bro Clement made it much more enjoyable than I expected. He expects more out of his students than most of the intro-level CS professors, and I think that's a good thing. Students that don't like Bro Clement as a teacher usually just want an easy A and for everything to be spoonfed to them.

This semester he said he was trying something new and I don't think it quite work out... First half of the class was fairly useless server programming  in C (I have to say I enjoyed it anyways), but the second half of the class there were too many small projects which left me with almost no time for the big final group project - web app.
Dr. Clement was really awesome for 418, definitely would recommend him.  Very willing to work with students one on one.

This class is definitely not a giveaway, but taking the time to come to labs and class will get you a good grade, especially if you do them early for extra credit. He had an "inverted classroom" where we would go through lectures at home, then come to class and work on portions of labs and homework. I never opened the textbook (web was sufficient).

He was super helpful and understanding! The Testing center had a weird schedule one day making me completely miss a part of the midterm and he let me retake it at the end of the semester. He has the lectures online to watch at home and then does help on hw in class. Very funny and entertaining, keeping the class interested.

Dr. Clement structures his lectures around what we think we need help on. This can be good or bad depending on if you have CS nerds in your class who want to talk about unrelated topics all the time. Going to lecture was helpful because Clement would give advice on the labs. Some labs took me a long time. Easy A if you do all the work on time.

Dr. Clement is very helpful. He spends a lot of class time working through examples. This can be boring if you've already done the lab for the section, but he mixes in helpful hints for everyone. The class is time consuming, but it is easy to get a good grade if you actually do the work.

Dr. Clement was very personable, and helpful. Some classes were not really relevant, but he'd usually make it worth your time with invaluable lab help. You MUST read the book, and reference it often. My quickest lab took 4 hours, my longest closer to 15. He tells you that your math ability is a good predictor of your success in the class.VeryTrue.

He's a pretty good professor.  His teaching style was somewhat pedantic, and class was quite boring from time to time, but the information he gave was applicable.  He generally seemed to know what he was talking about.  He called for volunteers a lot. I stopped attending class to dodge that bullet, and I still got an A.

Clement is good. However, I didn't really like his teaching style. It's lectures and examples, and you should read the book before coming. The book's the most important thing for this class. Others seem to like him, so maybe it's just me. But, let's just say this class is why I've decided against a CS major.

Dr Clement is so helpful. He will take up an entire lecture just to clear up one single question that you have. He invents new ways of explaining things all the time. He teaches to the students not just information. He dose not teach out of the book but you are required to read it.I couldn't have asked for a better teacher!

Dr. Clement is super nice and really wants every student to understand. He's willing to answer your questions in class. Class time was sort of hit or miss. The tests are exactly like the quizzes. GO TO THE LAB FOR HELP! Labs took up a lot of time, but an A was very doable.

Professor Clement is very good at programming, but the class I took (Intro to Programming) was a bit hard to keep up with.  He was very helpful when I asked him questions during office hours, though.  He was a good professor who cared about students - go to him with questions, not to the TAs.

Dr. Clement is the man! I would take any class I could from him if I were you. His teaching style is very loose, and he goes off on tangents a lot, but you learn so much during the semester. Midterm and final are easy, as is homework. Projects, however, are tough just like any other CS class. Take 360 from Clement and no one else!

Dr. Clement is so funny!  The class is really easy if you read and attend class.  I had no Programming experience before, and now I feel comfortable doing  lots of programming.  Its a really fun and interesting class.  The TA's are also really helpful,
Dr. Clement is the man! Don't take CS 142 from anyone but him!

Most of the time I spend on this class is in the lab. You work with TA's much more often than with the prof. I went to the class just for participation points. Tests have 2 parts: multiple choice test and program test. The MC test is extremely easy, don't worry. Just focus on the program test. It took me 10 hours on average for each.

Dr. Clement is very helpful and interesting, but more so one-on-one than in lecture.  The textbook is good; read it.  He spent most classes going through slides, but the occasional in-class programs were fun with a good group.  He was at times unexpectedly hilarious, but most of the class had tuned him out and missed those few brilliant moments.

He really cares about students and is a good teacher. My favorite CS class--I learned a ton! 6 projects; generous sample code and tutorials made them pretty easy, but I still felt a big sense of accomplishment. For passoff, TAs just played with our projects a little. A lot of extra credit was available. 2 tests were average; study review examples!

Dr Clement is really nice, and he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. However, if there weren't participation points, I wouldn't have gone to class at all.  Lecture was extremely not helpful, I only passed this class because I read the book on my own, did the quizzes, and got lots of help from the TAs. Good class overall though.

Dr. Clement is very understanding and helpful - when you can find him!  He is rarely in his office and lab and doesn't answer his phone.  E-mails sometimes take a while to get a response.  His teaching ability is pretty good, however, in the classroom - especially when he prepares for lecture before class (which seems to be about 2/3 of the time).
No Comments
Very nice guy
He teaches like his students are in first grade, and doesn't know the material.
His 204 class is heavy in tests and homework, and no late work is accepted. However, he's better at explaining concepts than almost any professor I've ever taken. Highly recommend for hard classes.
Dynamics is a difficult class, but Dr. Colton makes it enjoyable. He is incredibly kind and you can tell that he cares about the students and the material.
Stay on top of the milestones and do each one well and you should be good.

This is a difficult class but this teacher is amazing. This professor and the other professor (magelby) have the same homework assignments and tests but his lectures were way better. He really understands the information and he is great at answering questions. He's engaging and funny. Our class test average was 15% higher than other class's.

Dr Coltons teaching style is mostly walking you through how to solve problems in class with some theory and conceptual backup, and then he sends you off to do the homework on your own. He answers emails quickly, as do the TAs. I reviewed the book and the homework, and scored above a 95 on all the exams

Dynamics is a difficult topic, but Dr. Colton teaches it very well. 6-15 difficult homework problems a week, 2 midterms, and a final. He cares a lot about the class; after we didn't do great on the second midterm, he cancelled the class project to lighten our load. I enjoyed his lectures because his love for dynamics is contagious.

Professor Colton is a very straight-forward, no funny business kinda professor who wants his students to come prepared and to take advantage of all their resources. Effective in his teaching style and problem-solving methods, but can be a snarky with students if they ask ignorant questions. Very hard tests and homework, but doable if you study.
Tries to be funny, comes off condescending. Tests were confusing, full of trick questions, and much more difficult than the other sections. 100% take a different teacher for dynamics.

This class was very challenging conceptually, but Dr. Colton does a great job of breaking things down, teaching them in a learnable way, and being there to help students. I would highly recommend getting into a study group early on, because some of the homework problems are extremely long and confusing.

To be fair, this class is the introductory seminar for mechanical engineering, so Professor Colton did not lecture all that often (it was usually guest lecturers). That being said, Professor Colton is inspirational, caring, kind, and very passionate about the success of his students. He is so kind and clearly wants the best for his class.

I really enjoy Dr. Colton's teaching style. He does a good job of explaining difficult concepts in simple terms and answering student questions effectively. He is very candid about what he does and doesn't know. I recommend this class to anyone who likes mechanics.
Super chill class
Easy and clear course. The teacher is a super nice guy and most of the lectures are interesting and useful.

Dr. Colton is a good teacher, but this class is hard if you're coming from a background not super familiar with electronic components. Give yourself lots of time to work and troubleshoot on the project. (It was just one semester long project with checkpoints and labs to "help" with the overall project). Quizzes were pretty tough.

This class format is the bomb! Great, informative, and engaging lectures. Weekly quizzes. No tests. No homework. Just labs (sometimes difficult) and a really fun semester long project. (The project can be really tough and frustrating) Lectures are frequently cancelled to provide more time for your project. Dr. Colton is cool and enthusiastic.

Super easy class and easy going guy. It is obvious that he cares about his students and tries his best to pack the lectures with useful things and inspirational people. This class is nothing to stress about and I genuinely looked forward to it. I also don't know if he will in the future, but this semester lectures were recorded to watch later.
ME EN 191 is a seminar class, so if you show up, you will pass. Professor Colton is a super nice guy, and is willing to help you explore the many branches of Mechanical Engineering.
Dr. Colton is a very good professor who is both engaging and knowledgeable. He meets with students and groups individually and offers support and help.
This was the ME seminar class, so it was mostly guest lectures rather than Colton lecturing himself. I think he ran the class really well though. Class is a super easy pass or fail.

Dr. Colton did a great job teaching this seminar class. He didn't personally teach a ton, but when he did it was great. He set the class up in a very logical way, with very clear grading standards. Super nice guy.

Being a seminar class, it was mostly a bunch of guest lectures about mechanical engineering, so most of the time Prof. Colton wasn't actually teaching. But when he did he was pretty good, very clear. This class is so easy, pretty much all you have to do is attend lectures and fill out a report about them.
Loved this class. Tough material, but Dr. Colton is awesome and explains things very clearly. Would definitely recommend. He seems to be the favorite professor in the ME department every year.

Dr. Colton knows his stuff, and can teach effectively.  The grading was exceptionally harsh on homework assignments, as in lots of people got D's and F's.  I'm not sure if he hires the TA's, but they're mostly incompetent, only useful for the answer key.  If you work with Colton personally, he really wants you to learn, and is understanding.
He won't give any feedback on how you did on the milestones or the presentation, so just expect an arbitrary grade assignment.

Dr. Colton is the man! By far one of my favorite teachers so far. He's very good at teaching. Crystal clear. He's entertaining. Very down to earth guy that is easy to talk to. Everything just makes sense when he teaches. Homework is reasonable. But tests can throw curve balls. I had an A in the class until the final.
Very clear teaching style, he is always eager and willing to help in his office. The class takes work and time, but I wouldn't want to take it from anyone else. Excellent professor.
He is very organized and hard working. However, his tests are very tricky, even when you know the material. His grading is merciless on tests, its mostly multiple choice with no partial credit.

He is a nice professor. Always ready to help. Homeworks are hard, exams are hard too. But if you look at the posted solutions of the homeworks, before taking a test, you may be able to do good on the test. However he gives several unexpected questions on exams which may rip you off, if you do not know the material very well.
Excellent teacher!  Very very very useful, although the exams are a bit tough.  But he is very fair, very professional (doesn't get sidetracked in class), and knows how to teach.

I always found him in office hours during office hours.  More than willing to answer any questions you might have or explain a concept over.  He always knows the material very well and is pretty laid back. He knows there are things other than his class, but expects you to learn the concepts. Great Teacher!
Willing to help but examples done in class were not clean, end complete. More importance to modeling systems could have been given in order to help students model system.
No Comments
Excellent teacher - knows the material very well - willing to help individually or the whole class - recognizes that there are other things in life outside of his class

I loved New Testament Gospels with Dr. Ellison! He knew everyone's names from the moment we walked into class & maintained this loving environment the whole semester. He is an amazing teacher. He knows what he is talking about, how to teach it, and how to help you learn it! Exams were a little hard but I learned a lot. Highly reccomend!

His class on parables changed my life. He's the absolute sweetest and kindest professor I've had at BYU. Lectures were amazing and made me see the scriptures in a whole new light. If you can take a class from Dr. Ellison, DO IT! You will not regret it.
absolutely the goat! Loves what he teaches and the students and did so much over the semester to make the class as easy as possible. I would 1000% take a class from him again.

Very caring, made class lectures very interesting. Has a clear passion for what he teaches. Assignments were sometimes docked a couple points without a clear explanation why, but still not a hard class. For spring term, it's a lot of reading, as with any spring term class, but totally manageable.

Take a class with him if you can!!! He was so sweet and funny, I enjoyed every lecture! I always came away inspired. There is a good amount of homework to do. Each page would take me around 2 hours, but he always told you exactly what you're looking for. You just have to go to the verses he says. Absolutely take this class!!

Dr. Ellison is a fantastic professor. I loved his class. Some say that his homework was too much, but I felt like it was very pointed and worthwhile. I gained real insights from every homework assignment and in-class lecture. He also is a genuinely kind person who will work with students who need help.

Dr. Ellison is kind, inclusive, and such a joy to be around. His lectures are academically engaging and spiritually uplifting. He connects with his students and is aware of people's diverse experiences. The workload is manageable and the course is very well-structured so you always know what to expect. You won't regret taking this class!

If you ever get the chance make sure to take a class from Mark Ellison! He is amazing and I think he knows everything that one could possibly learn about The New Testament. And you can tell by his demeanor and how kind he is that he has spent his life studying it.

Though Mark Ellison is a very nice guy and has very interesting lectures, the tests and homework aren't worth it. I did almost double the amount of homework on this class than my other 3 credit classes. The tests are so specific and there is no good study guide to help prep you for them. There's about 2+ hours of homework for every class.

Professor Ellison is just the most wonderful human being. Every day in class lifted my spirits and taught me more than I had ever known before about Christ and His faithful disciples. He has truly opened my eyes to scripture, encouraging the class to be “surprised” even as we re-read the stories we have known since childhood. I loved it all!

Do not take this class from Dr Ellison!!! It was the opposite of a testimony-building class. The amount of homework and reading every week was insane.
