His tests are incredibly hard and require so much memorization of chapters and verses. The amount of work I had to do in this 2 credit class was almost double my 3 credit class. Not worth it.

I love Professor Ellison! His class was super spiritual but also academic and taught me a ton about the Old Testament. There was a ton of reading since it was a term class but he was aware of that and would cut it down as much as he could. His tests had really clear study guides and he had a few short essays that were also easily graded.

I cannot say enough good things about Dr Ellison! He makes sure every student feels so loved and cared for, he is 100% one of the best profs in the BYU religion department. Really impressive historical knowledge and understanding of other faiths. Clearly structured assignments, straight forward tests, and easy semester long project. Take his class!

Best religion professor at BYU as far as I'm concerned. I'm honestly not a big fan of the way religion is taught at BYU but Bro. Ellison makes it good. He has amazing lectures focusing on spiritual things, and he cares about the students. There's a decent amount of work but if you don't get behind this is the best class at BYU.

I loved Dr. Ellison and his New Testament class! He cares about his students and does an awesome job of including everyone. His lectures were great and involved discussions. There are weekly quizzes, reading assignments, and a semester-long project, but taking this class with Dr. Ellison is worth it!

Solid choice for a religion professor, you have reading quizzes (open note and book) and a big project you work on throughout the semester, but they aren't bad. Pretty easy grader and the lectures are pretty interesting. Definitely a testimony building class in such a welcoming environment!

I loved this class. We had one midterm which wasn't bad, one short paper, a creative project, and a final. Don't procrastinate the creative project like I did, but it can be whatever you want so that helps. Dr. Ellison is so nice and really cares about his students. He is super passionate about the new testament and can teach you a lot.

Dr. Ellison is so passionate about the New Testament and the Gospel of Jesus Christ. He genuinely cares about his students spiritual learning and wants to help. There are quite a few readings for the quizzes but they are skimmable. He is an amazing and interesting lecturer.

A very nice person who really cared about his students and the topic. The homework and tests were not that difficult. He made the topic interesting. He was very respectful and included everyone into his lectures.
Never taken harder tests from any of my classes at BYU, especially for a religion. Test heavy. Not worth all the stress.

The lectures were very interesting and helped me to think deeper about the gospel. However the study guides that were due every class period took me a lot of time, around one hour and half to two hours. The creative project and the paper on Jesus in art was what changed my grade the most. These two things were also graded very harshly.

My favorite religion professor ever! He really helped me to think deeply about the material. You have to participate and study for tests but it is still easily possible to get an A and so worth it (sometimes the TAs grade harsh). You have SQs before class that you discuss in class and a Creative Project that is 18% of your grade.

Mark Ellison is one of the best men I've ever met, to say nothing of professors. I learned so, so much and enjoyed every second of his class. The homework assignments and lectures are dripping with care and thoughtfulness.

TAKE A CLASS FROM HIM! You won't regret it, it literally changed my life. I took RELA 250, Christ and the Everlasting Gospel. I honestly couldn't imagine a better professor than Ellison. The lectures are interesting and I found myself sad when I missed class because I missed out on an awesome opportunity to learn from him. You'll learn so much

Super nice guy. Have to go to every class or your grade will plummet. Real testimony builder, but not the easiest A. Lots of reading for homework and then a quiz before each class, open note and pretty easy. Midterm and final are pretty hard bc you have to memorize some scripture passages, but still doable. One paper and a project

Dr. Ellison is such a great teacher that I've taken him twice. His lectures will really help you learn the material better, and all his test questions come from reading quizzes. If you do what he asks, you'll get an A. He also has such a great knowledge of the gospel that anyone would benefit from hearing. Take him if you can.

I am so grateful for Dr. Ellison. He is such a nice person who really helped me love the new testament! I loved his lectures. Don't miss class - it will kill your grade. You will have an online quiz due before every class, but 90% of the test questions are from those quizzes, so work hard on the quizzes and you'll be prepared for the tests.

Dr. Ellison is the best professor BYU has to offer in any field. He cares about students. He knew everyone's name, remembered student's important events( like their performances, papers being published, etc.) and even attended a few events to support his students. Best lectures ever! Be prepared to be enlightened! He is on your side when grading!

Dr. Ellison is BYU's best. He focuses each lesson on Christ and explains doctrine from a historical perspective. He is funny, brilliant, and very sensitive to his students and their circumstances. I am not a fan of any religion courses at BYU except for the two courses I have taken from Dr. Ellison.

Dr. Ellison is amazing! He is so kind and loving and will always do his best to work with you when circumstances arise. His midterms and finals are hard but the rest of the homework is easy and educational.

Christ and the Everlasting Gospel - buy the hard copy of the Wayment New Testament translation (e-book doesn't work). Great professor. Little bit of a harsh grader. Lots of reading before class (1-2 hours). Super nice and willing to help. You get participation/attendance grade, but you just review what you read beforehand.

Dr. Ellison was a great teacher, and I learned so much about the New Testament and Christ's life. If you pay attention and do the homework the tests aren't bad, and honestly even though the homework can be a lot it is really good. Basically you learn from the scriptures directly in the homework and from him in class. 10/10 would recommend.

Has an excessively long assignment due before each class. The class is supposed to be centered around Christ, but Dr. Ellison focuses more on the historical aspect of the New Testament. Lots of before class reading. Very caring teacher, you can tell he loves each of his students. Tested heavily on historical and trivia stuff from the NT. Great guy.

Great professor! Loved the organization of the class. Good balance between historical information and spiritual application. Open-book quizzes between each class, and a weekly portion of a semester-long project, but very manageable. Would definitely take class from him again.
Dr. Ellison is so great! He has a great sense of humor and has an amazing knowledge of the gospel! Even though I feel like there was too much homework for a 2 credit class, I would take him again.

I love brother Ellison so much. I would take his class over and over again. This is still one of the most spiritual religion classes I have ever taken. He turns everything you knew about the New Testament upside down and then shows you how the correct meaning directly applies to your life. Loved this class so much!

Great professor, I learned a lot about the New Testament. Lectures were enjoyable and the readings were applicable. You will have to work a little bit, but an A is definitely achievable if you put in the time. One of the kindest people I have ever interacted with. He will always help you with whatever you need.

This class was fantastic. Dr. Ellison is very knowledgeable, organized and cares about each student. He posts his powerpoints after the class so you can review. He has you complete a pericope project, part of it is due each week so it was easy to stay on top of the project. Review the quizzes and powerpoints often, then the tests are easy.

Dr. Ellison calls himself a historian and a Religion Educator, and he is a historian. You will see how he concentrates his teaching on history facts and the trips he took. I always loved the New Testament, but reading it this semester was not productive at all. Dr. Ellison will give you a ton of homework and expect you to know the historic details

I absolutely loved this class. There is a good amount of reading, but I gained a love for the New Testament. Brother Ellison is very knowledgeable and gave me a new and deeper perspective of the New Testament. Would highly recommend this class!

He cares about individuals a lot. I truly felt he cared. He is willing to help if you ask. He is very knowledgeable. The class is very detail orientated though. He definitely makes you work for it. Clear grading criteria. Not TOO hard to get a good grade if you put in the effort. I'd take another class from him. Beginning of the semester is scary.

Dr. Ellison is a great religion professor. He teaches the doctrine really well, but he also focuses heavily on the emotional side instead of just the academic side of the Gospel. I read the Book of Mormon and BOM study guides several times on my mission, but he still taught new things and things in ways that I had never thought of before.

Dr. Ellison is probably one of the sweetest guys I've ever met. If you skip class, it can really hurt your grade. Finals and Midterms are based on his reading quiz questions, but they can still be tricky, especially on the final. Class is very insightful. No extra credit and a 94 is an A. Takes lots of time and dedication to get an A for 2 credits.

Dr. Ellison knows each of his students' names and makes an effort to get to know them. At the beginning of the semester, the reading before every class period was insane. After the midterm student evaluations, so many people mentioned it so he made some changes and it became a lot more manageable. Looks for very specific things in tests, kinda hard

A refreshing break from the typical "detached robot professor" stereotype. Not only does he know his students individually he genuinely wants to help them pass this class. If you're willing to put forth a bit of effort (not an unreasonable amount) you will come out of his class not only with a solid A but with a love for the New Testament.

Passionate. Care about his students individually. His knowledge of the scriptures and ancient culture is mind-blowing. 10/10 would recommend because Dr. Ellison teaches with the power of the Spirit. Uplifting and enlightening.

Dr. Ellison is a great teacher and his class is decently challenging. The Isaiah paper is kind of rough, but there's a creative project that's pretty fun. There's a lot of readings and quizzes to go along with them, but the quiz questions pretty much give you the test answers word for word. I would definitely recommend him.

Dr. Ellison was amazing. I'd take from him again any time. If you do the reading, use the quizzes he has online as a reading guide, you'll do great, basically everything grade-wise stems from that. You can expect a couple papers and an end of semester project where you have a lot of freedom to do whatever you really want.

Professor Ellison is such a nice guy! He really tries to help his students learn. I would definitely take this class again from him. You have a quiz that has to be completed before every class period, but they are not too hard. I actually enjoyed them.

Really cool class, really enjoyed it. Not very difficult, but did learn a lot. You write a couple papers, but they aren't burden some. The criteria is really clear and the papers were interesting and engaging to write. Tests are not too difficult, although you don't get to use your scriptures.

Dr. Ellison is a super great guy and I felt that the course was laid out pretty well, but the final was significantly harder than anyone expected. His lectures were pretty good, but I found it hard to stay focused sometimes because he just wasn't a particularly captivating speaker. You can't go wrong with taking BoM from Ellison

Each lesson has material well organized. His lectures are amazing and I felt like it was the right balance between spiritual doctrine and contextual information. There are reading assignments before class, but overall very do-able and rewarding. TAKE ELLISON!!!

He really cares about his subject and his students. It was hard for me to stay focused sometimes, found myself checking the time a lot. More of history class, not that spiritual. You can speed through the readings for the quizzes. The midterm is easy if you study, but the final is really hard. Sincere, genuine person, just not my favorite teacher.

He is very well organized and truly knows his stuff. I typically would zone out in this class. He is passionate about what he teaches, but there is a lot of readings that I never fully read but I still did well on assignments. I have a better understanding of the BOM but not my favorite class.

Dr. Ellison is really nice and you can tell he cares about his students. But his lectures are really easy to zone out in if you're not 100% into it. The final was a lot harder than the midterm, so make sure to study the entire semester's power point slides. He lessened the amount of homework after the midterm and the class became bearable.

This class was a great different approach to study the Book of Mormon, and Dr. Ellison taught it beautifully. Each lecture was rewarding to attend, and the readings were not only applicable to the lecture, but also to your own personal scripture study. As long as you show up to class and do the readings, you will be able to pass the class.

I've loved being in Dr Ellison's class. He loves the Book of Mormon and teaches it beautifully. He has found a great balance become academic and spiritual learning. He listens to student feedback, promotes good class conversation, and is always available if you need extra help or just want to talk. None of the work in this class is a waste!

I love this class! It is my first religion class at BYU and Dr. Ellison is so great I'm taking New Testament from him next semester. He works really hard to listen to the concerns of his students, and answers questions. He tries to memorized everyone's name. I love how we get to focus on personal ministry for the final project.
Cares a lot about his students and wants to be the best teacher he can be. Tries to find a balance between too much (work, historical background, spiritual relevance, readings etc) and too little.

I learned so much in Professor Ellison's class. He really cares about the course material and his students. He is very understanding about grades if you talk to him. There is about 1-3 hours of homework per class which can sometimes be a lot but if you do the reading you will ace the midterm. I felt the spirit almost every class!

I loved his class. It definitely requires work, but not more than is expected from a religion course. Despite being a life-long member of the church, I learned a lot from him and would love to take his class again.
Not very clear on instructions. Prefers artistic works on final project to research papers. Make sure you sign the roll!  Only takes that into account for participation over actual participation.

Brother Ellison is a fantastic teacher: I am in his BofM Class - He teaches with the spirit and often references interesting ancient texts, modern stories, and even archaeological info. ( he knows SO much). He cares about what he is teaching, and wants his students to succeed. He gives feedback on all assignments and has communicated well w/ me.

I took this class in his first semester of teaching, and he did pretty well for his first time! The class itself is tricky, but his teaching methods were consistent. The best thing you can do is find a group to do the homework with. He wasn't super available outside of class, and neither were the TAs, but he was a nice guy.

I learned so much from this class. It's really good if you have an interest in philosophy whatsoever. Professor Frame is an amazing teacher and really knows his stuff. There's daily reading and a few quizzes but it's not very difficult. He cares most about you learning rather than grades.

His field of study is philosophy of education, and it shows. He doesn't rush, he teaches things that he cares about, and he cares about you as a student. Wants you to learn but not going to make you miserable. Super intelligent and will help you get where you want to go. Personalized learning. Highly recommend.

Prof Frame is pretty passionate about philosophy, so his class is fun in that sense. I didn't find the course engaging or applicable. I thought I'd learn a lot about philosophy and the meaning of life, but we read more about utilitarianism and whether or not you should lie to Nazi's. It's fun but your not going to learn stoicism.
Professor Frame is awesome. He's super funny and knows what he's talking about. He really wants us to succeed!

Professor Frame is a great guy. His logic course contains a lot of challenging concepts but he does a great job of breaking them down and making them understandable. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but it helps a ton. He is also easy going with grading. At the end of the day, he just wants to help you master logic.

Professor Frame is AWESOME! Super funny and nice guy. I took this class for a GE, and it ended up being super engaging and interesting. Frame wants everyone to do well in the class, and I did not have to stress about finishing with an A. Overall my favourite class from last semester.
Great guy and fun class, he cares more about you learning and understanding topics than grades. Lectures can get erratic but they are always interesting

Professor. Frame is awesome. Super easy but enlightening class. I loved his philosophy on learning and feel like I learned a lot in his class. The essays were actually fun to write and he gives awesome feedback to encourage more learning. Take his class!

Professor Frame is a caring professor with engaging lectures. His main focus is for you to learn through coming to class and participating so attendance is mandatory. But overall the class is very easy with only two papers and two online exams which are all very doable. Awesome for a GE class. I would highly recommend Professor Frame!

His actual in class teaching is fine. However, the ai grading system they use is broken and makes most assignments impossible to do. They have too much trust in it and will trust the word of the ai over the word of the student. It's also an all or nothing grading system, so you can do 99% of an assignment and get a 0 because you forgot 1 thing.

Professor Clement is a very caring professor who wants every student to succeed. However, get ready for a TON of work involved in CS260. It feels like you're learning a new coding language every week, which was difficult. Professor Clement does a great job of providing extra credit opportunities, and I loved his spiritual moments and field trips

The CS 224 online section lacks clear examples for the homework and slides. My suggestion is sign up for the online section but go in person. Doing so will give you a more lenient homework and project schedule compared to an in-person section. Dr. Clement is always there to help you if you need help.
Not really present, doesnt express ideas thoroughly or easy enough to understand

He is a nice guy, but boring. He talked about what coding you are doing, but hardly about the practicality of actually doing it (how to code), which made it hard for me. You build a website but the class structure is bad. Later checkpoints (JavaScript and React) are harder. Class attendance almost isn't worth it; I learned from google and chatGPT.

The lecture side of class wasn't really necessary at all since the online notes had all the important information. The class also isn't given enough time for your knowledge of these topics to actually stick. My final project ended up using so much copy & paste because of this. Wish it could be extended to a full year instead of one semester.
Most of it was online for me so i hardly ever saw the professor. You just read some github pages and work on your website.

Great class. Some bugs in the material because they just moved from Vue to React but otherwise a great class. Lots of projects but they were pretty easy. Some homeworks and two exams but altogether very doable.

It isn't a hard class, but there isn't a whole lot of help. The TA's honestly can't help you learn, but they aren't harsh graders. You are asked to copy and paste a lot and I didn't feel like I learned a lot from the course. Professor Clement is a nice guy, it isn't necessarily a bad class, but if you are going to take 260, don't take it from him.
Honestly just difficult to work with, doesn't do a great job of structuring lectures or tutorials to cultivate learning, and doesn't do a great job of assisting students that show a need for help.

Dr. Clement is a great professor and a great guy! He really wants you to succeed and gives you the resources to do so. I took his online, on-demand class and would highly recommend this format for any CS student.

This is a remote, on-demand class, so I didn't interact with Dr. Clement much, but when I did, it was only positive interactions. The class is not too difficult (there are a number of large projects), but I learned a ton of very useful skills. I would highly recommend taking this class from Dr. Clement!

Weekly labs (for the most part) aren't easy but professor gives lots of videos that offer lots of help. Also, a good TA queue. Reading quizzes are fine because they have unlimited submissions. Exams aren't too bad.

Complete waste of my time and tuition money. 90% of the class is online tutorials that you can already use for free, and any tutorials made by the professor were awful. After turning in one assignment late I was told I was "in danger of failing" even though there's no penalty for late work. Save your time and take something more useful.

Clement did a bad job explaining how to code anything. He gives huge assignments and no guidance. Most of the projects shouldnt have been hard, but without guidance it would take hours of meeting with tutors to even understand the data structures, let alone code them. I recommend you take classes from a professor who actually teaches you.

Didn't enjoy lectures at all, made most of the labs way beyond our capacity and I think they were an ineffective way of teaching us the concepts that he was trying to teach. That being said he's better than Roper

This was the worst organized class I have ever taken. It was clear they were changing the order of the units, but it felt incomplete. More than once, we were expected to use a concept that we would learn later in the semester. Relied heavily on online resources outside of class to get a good grade.

I liked Dr. Clement. His class was really hard, but I think that is the point. I spent 15+ hours a week on his class, sometimes more. I give him four stars because his rubrics and class material weren't very organized.

He always had very helpful videos to help you get started on the labs if you needed them and knew the common places where students would get stuck. The code is more complicated, so you have to identify most of the bugs yourself. Readings built nicely and made the quizzes easy. Super useful programming skills.

Clement only hindered my learning in this class. His only teaching consisted of occasional videos for the labs wherein he would contradict the written instructions and also the github lab specs. I didn't finished a single lab with a confident feeling about the material--and this is coming from someone who gave the class + TA's wayy too much time.

Dr. Clement really cares about his students. CS 235 is not the easiest class, but he prepares you well for each lab you do over the semester. He was almost always willing to meet with me when I got helplessly stuck. He is super flexible with due dates as he knows students are trying to juggle their lives and his CS projects. I love this dude.

Dr. Clement is not one of those CS teachers that wants to see you suffer. He genuinely tries to help students succeed, understand concepts, and have fun. Even though the class was on demand, I felt that he was really trying to be a part of the students' lives. When I had trouble getting labs done on the assigned date, he was willing to work with me

(Taken OnDemand) Great class for programmers on the data structures that hold memory (vectors, lists, etc). The concepts were taught through reading quizzes, which were sometimes hard to follow. Labs are computer graded so you know your score beforehand. Lots of work outside of class. Maybe 7-8 hours a week on average, depending on your bugs.

I've never felt as overwhelmed as fast as I did at the start of this class semester. He throws you in headfirst, expecting you to figure out the Linux command line, a new (terrible) IDE, and the monstrous weekly labs completely on your own. I think it's largely the class, though, not the professor.

Professor Clement is great. Lets your turn in assignments late. Make's it easy to get good grades. Is super nice and very understanding. The only strange thing about 260 is that for must questions, he just googled the answer. But, I guess thats what most web programmers do these days.

If you thought 142 was a breeze, I'd recommend taking the online section of 235. There really aren't lectures and you can just do homework, labs, etc. on your own, which was really nice for me. Assignments have unlimited retakes and the grading is pretty lenient as long as you follow what's going on in the class.

This was the most difficult class I've ever taken. Prof. Clement does a terrible job explaining concepts and the labs are incredibly difficult. He would create such a needlessly difficult framework you'd have to follow that I would spend 5-6 hours every lab just trying to decipher his code before I would even start my code. Don't take from Clement!

This teacher is the nicest and one of the most understanding people I've ever met. I had a rough semester dealing with personal problems and every time I emailed him he was caring and helped me out. Never had someone as great as this.

One of the friendliest professors you'll ever have. Great guy. Very easy class (like I-didn't-take-the-midterm-and-still-got-an-A easy). The course teaches hirable skills such as Node, (Basic) AWS, MongoDB, and VuejsI just wish we got into more the more robust features of each of them. Really wish it pushed me more than it did.

It is an online class. He really cares about students. Although it is an online class, he always answers student's questions as soon as he can. The e-book is somewhat helpful, but you can find a free version of it on the internet. So, opt it out. If you take an online course, make sure you understand the reading. Some of the Labs are really heavy.

Good, funny, genuine dude. Took him for CS235 and it was great. Took him for CS260 and it seemed like he was just using tutorials made by a different prof, and didn't even look at the tutorials until in class with us. I stopped going to class because it was useless, and the tutorials are easy to just do online, outside of class.
He is a really nice guy, but his lectures really just are not helpful. I took CS 418 and CS 260 from him and rarely attended class because they just weren't helpful.

Dr. Clement is the best professor in the CS department right now (writing this as a senior). His classes focus on writing actual code that help significantly with the labs. I felt that I have learned more in the two classes I have taken from him than anyone else.

Way too confident in the relevance of his class to the industry, but it is just an intro to web programming. Easy class. Doesn't use a book. You'll teach yourself everything online but its a decent start. BYU really should have a second part to this course to cover more depth but they'd rather send you to Dev Mountain for this kind of programming.

Professor Clement is a very caring person. He doesn't quite fit the beastly CS BYU teacher mold because he truly want to help you succeed and will do his best to help you understand. I do think that he is a bit outdated in the technologies that he is accustomed to using. I'm not entirely sure he has a background in profession web development.

418 is great with Dr. Clement. Majority of the work is through Rosalind problems which are like small coding interview questions. Choose your own language (most do Python), group projects are super interesting but slightly more challenging. Really enjoyed this class as a CS elective. Most of the quizzes you can turn in late at no penalty.

CS 260 does NOT teach you how to code. It teaches you how to copy/paste and tries to teach you over 6 programming languages in 4 months (I've learned nothing). Prof' Clement is nice but he doesn't even know what he's doing half the time and will frequently ask students what's wrong with his code during lecture. Don't take CS 260 from Clement.
Great teacher! Fun to listen to, very willing to help you learn, wants you to love coding! Wants all of us to get A's and makes it very possible to do so! By far one of the best CS teachers!!!

Doctor Clement has been my favorite CS professor I've had while at BYU. He cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He helps by giving a good amount of code on each lab and if you know what you're doing, you never need to go to class because he publishes everything online. I could not give him higher praise! Take him if you can!

Dr. Clement is so awesome. He is a perfect example of how every professor should be. He main focus is not to fit students into a bell curve, but really cares about you learning the material and enjoying the class. super caring, and unbelievably understanding. He wants you to succeed, and will do anything to help you get an A.

Professor Clement basically just wants you to get through the material and complete the labs. The class is set up so you will succeed. He gives you a lot of the code, so technically you could just copy/paste some things; however, I felt that I learned a lot in Professor Clement's class. Good professor, good environment.

Prof. Clement's web programming course is very doable. Unlike most 3-credit CS classes, it actually feels like 3 credits instead of 6. You do some very cool projects. There are two midterms and a final, but they're not hard. You could get through the class just through copy-pasting, sure, but all the resources are there for you to master it.

Awesome guy, great class structure. Learned more in this class than any other CS class. At times there was maybe too much copy/paste. There is SO much material taught but it's taught in a simple way and in a way you can succeed. I'm going to finish with 100% in the class. Can use internet on assignments and tests. 10/10 would recommend.

Super great guy, awesome, caring professor, but this class was an absolute mess. The class is very poorly designed to actually help anyone learn anything. Mostly you learn how to copy and paste. Easy A, but I am no more capable of web programming than when I started the class 4 months ago. Very frustrating assignments.

I dreaded CS 235 but he made this class awesome and even changed up the labs to make it easier.  He even threw out an old one and made a new lab to help us learn the uses of maps (associative arrays). Remember this class is based off the text book so all of the lab code is found there.

Good: he's a genuinely great guy. Explains the material well. Easy to get lots of extra credit. Bad: labs are time consuming (not surprising for a CS class).  Sometimes the specs he would tell us in class were different from what the TA's would tell us, causing confusion. And, there were easy but in-class quizzes each day, worth 10% of your grade.

He explains things well, and it's interesting, albeit a bit slow. I preferred to just read the textbook and get it over with. He relies a lot on the textbook, to the point of directing students to just copy the book's code on some labs, which I thought was kind of lame. Also makes us do UMLs for every lab, which are totally the worst.

This class is mostly seniors doing an easy elective. If you are an underclassman, however, expect a challenge, because the prof goes FAST and you WILL get lost.  You frantically try and keep up in class and then learn everything by yourself at home via tutorials. He IS forgiving, which is SO nice.

Dr. Clement is really nice and cares about his students. We often programmed during class together and he taught us whatever we needed and wanted to know. At first I didn't like the freestyle structure of the class but it grew on me. I learned a lot of valuable skills and technologies. Dr. Clement is great!

Far and away my favorite CS Professor at BYU. Clement cares about students, and will do whatever he can to make sure you are successful. Tests are fair, projects are interesting and worthwhile, and anyone can get an A if they try. This is my second class with Clement, and I would honestly take any class that he teaches

This is one of the most hated CS classes at BYU, but Bro Clement made it much more enjoyable than I expected. He expects more out of his students than most of the intro-level CS professors, and I think that's a good thing. Students that don't like Bro Clement as a teacher usually just want an easy A and for everything to be spoonfed to them.

This semester he said he was trying something new and I don't think it quite work out... First half of the class was fairly useless server programming  in C (I have to say I enjoyed it anyways), but the second half of the class there were too many small projects which left me with almost no time for the big final group project - web app.
Dr. Clement was really awesome for 418, definitely would recommend him.  Very willing to work with students one on one.

This class is definitely not a giveaway, but taking the time to come to labs and class will get you a good grade, especially if you do them early for extra credit. He had an "inverted classroom" where we would go through lectures at home, then come to class and work on portions of labs and homework. I never opened the textbook (web was sufficient).

He was super helpful and understanding! The Testing center had a weird schedule one day making me completely miss a part of the midterm and he let me retake it at the end of the semester. He has the lectures online to watch at home and then does help on hw in class. Very funny and entertaining, keeping the class interested.

Dr. Clement structures his lectures around what we think we need help on. This can be good or bad depending on if you have CS nerds in your class who want to talk about unrelated topics all the time. Going to lecture was helpful because Clement would give advice on the labs. Some labs took me a long time. Easy A if you do all the work on time.

Dr. Clement is very helpful. He spends a lot of class time working through examples. This can be boring if you've already done the lab for the section, but he mixes in helpful hints for everyone. The class is time consuming, but it is easy to get a good grade if you actually do the work.

Dr. Clement was very personable, and helpful. Some classes were not really relevant, but he'd usually make it worth your time with invaluable lab help. You MUST read the book, and reference it often. My quickest lab took 4 hours, my longest closer to 15. He tells you that your math ability is a good predictor of your success in the class.VeryTrue.

He's a pretty good professor.  His teaching style was somewhat pedantic, and class was quite boring from time to time, but the information he gave was applicable.  He generally seemed to know what he was talking about.  He called for volunteers a lot. I stopped attending class to dodge that bullet, and I still got an A.

Clement is good. However, I didn't really like his teaching style. It's lectures and examples, and you should read the book before coming. The book's the most important thing for this class. Others seem to like him, so maybe it's just me. But, let's just say this class is why I've decided against a CS major.

Dr Clement is so helpful. He will take up an entire lecture just to clear up one single question that you have. He invents new ways of explaining things all the time. He teaches to the students not just information. He dose not teach out of the book but you are required to read it.I couldn't have asked for a better teacher!

Dr. Clement is super nice and really wants every student to understand. He's willing to answer your questions in class. Class time was sort of hit or miss. The tests are exactly like the quizzes. GO TO THE LAB FOR HELP! Labs took up a lot of time, but an A was very doable.

Professor Clement is very good at programming, but the class I took (Intro to Programming) was a bit hard to keep up with.  He was very helpful when I asked him questions during office hours, though.  He was a good professor who cared about students - go to him with questions, not to the TAs.

Dr. Clement is the man! I would take any class I could from him if I were you. His teaching style is very loose, and he goes off on tangents a lot, but you learn so much during the semester. Midterm and final are easy, as is homework. Projects, however, are tough just like any other CS class. Take 360 from Clement and no one else!

Dr. Clement is so funny!  The class is really easy if you read and attend class.  I had no Programming experience before, and now I feel comfortable doing  lots of programming.  Its a really fun and interesting class.  The TA's are also really helpful,
Dr. Clement is the man! Don't take CS 142 from anyone but him!

Most of the time I spend on this class is in the lab. You work with TA's much more often than with the prof. I went to the class just for participation points. Tests have 2 parts: multiple choice test and program test. The MC test is extremely easy, don't worry. Just focus on the program test. It took me 10 hours on average for each.

Dr. Clement is very helpful and interesting, but more so one-on-one than in lecture.  The textbook is good; read it.  He spent most classes going through slides, but the occasional in-class programs were fun with a good group.  He was at times unexpectedly hilarious, but most of the class had tuned him out and missed those few brilliant moments.

He really cares about students and is a good teacher. My favorite CS class--I learned a ton! 6 projects; generous sample code and tutorials made them pretty easy, but I still felt a big sense of accomplishment. For passoff, TAs just played with our projects a little. A lot of extra credit was available. 2 tests were average; study review examples!

Dr Clement is really nice, and he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. However, if there weren't participation points, I wouldn't have gone to class at all.  Lecture was extremely not helpful, I only passed this class because I read the book on my own, did the quizzes, and got lots of help from the TAs. Good class overall though.

Dr. Clement is very understanding and helpful - when you can find him!  He is rarely in his office and lab and doesn't answer his phone.  E-mails sometimes take a while to get a response.  His teaching ability is pretty good, however, in the classroom - especially when he prepares for lecture before class (which seems to be about 2/3 of the time).
No Comments
Very nice guy
He teaches like his students are in first grade, and doesn't know the material.

I love Mark. He's a great person and artist. He's an ok teacher. It's obvious he knows what he's talking about, but he is not good with technology or assignment clarity. I was constantly worried that I was missing an assignment because he didn't have them in the schedule on LearningSuite. Great person. Great Artist. Not great teacher.
He is an amazing person but his class was super unclear and disorganized.

What to even say about Dr. Graham? How do I sum up this eccentric genius in 350 characters? We love him, he has great teaching philosophies (especially about grading and late work), and sometimes we get homemade treats and get to go to the park. I'll miss Dr. Graham's classes when I graduate.

Dr. Graham is highly respected in the program and is honestly really nice and very passionate about art/art education, but I think he's slipping off his rocker a little bit. He often changes assignments/due dates/etc. and there were a few times when he would suddenly decide to hold class off-campus, all without announcing first.

This class is generally interesting, but the Kritik platform is causing me a lot of stress. I get anxious every time I receive an email or text about a deadline I've already met. I also don't find peer grading helpful. It seems like everyone is just taking points off because we're expected to be 'critical.'

Dr. Hansen is a great guy with a lot to give. Much of his experience was in finance at Ford and he leans heavily into that. He's a decent professor, though basically just gives a surface-level overview of econ 110, but then wants you to apply the principles to a real company. It's a cool project, but he doesn't give much direction on how to do it.

Save yourself some money and don't buy textbooks or other materials. Just go to class, look at the homework answer that is associated with the quiz, and make sure to review all the concepts and calculations for the tests. He is a super funny guy but also likes to get political haha. Not sure how much real-world experience the guy actually has.

Professor Hansen is such a wonderful person. He really cares about all his students and did an excellent job facilitating conversation on some thorny discussion topics in our strategic thinking class. I left each class feeling closer to him and my classmates. Definitely take strategic thinking from him if you get the chance!

Strat 392 is an easier version of Econ 110. Dr. Hansen's closed-note tests are straightforward and as long as you study you should ace them. There are a dozen quizzes about the chapters you read (easy points if you pay attention to his HW reviews), a big group project, and several group spreadsheet assignments. Take Strat 392 from Dr. Hansen.

If you're taking STRAT 392, TAKE IT FROM MARK! He is one of my favorite professors I've had at BYU. He basically does the homework for you in class sometimes. He really cared about his students, he learned all of ours names, had good stories, was extremely fair. I greatly respect him as a person and as a professor. Lecture was occasionally dry.
Dr Hansen is a really kind guy. His class is fairly easy. The reading is pretty much unnecessary you just need to review the homework that he posts in order to do the quizzes.

Professor Hansen is a great guy. The course is very lecture heavy, and they can be dry at times. Also, there is a large portion of the semester that we just are shown demos of different products and it is hard to pay attention and/or know how it will affect our grade.

I got so little out of the lectures that I stopped attending class. A lot of the class time was wasted on things that didn't matter and when we were talking about the material, I didn't understand it from professor Hansen. I learned everything in this course either from the TA or on my own. I'd take it from someone else even if its a little harder

Absolutely loved this class, great insight into biotech entrepreneurship. Not particularly difficult, but extremely interesting and you end up learning more than you feel like you learned. He likes to hear himself talk, but he's not obnoxious and has a lot of valuable info so it's all good
Great teacher that is passionate about what he teachers. His lectures get a little long, but not a bad class at all.

Super kind, just a big ol' teddy bear. A few group projects, a good amount of online quizzes, participation in class, and a couple tests are your grade. Didn't open the textbook once. Show up to class and you'll do fine.

Dr. Hansen is a kind man who is accessible and will help you understand the material well. Managerial economics can be a little bit dry sometimes, but it was the first econ course I've taken where I felt like we could actually apply the concepts in real life. Quizzes are tough if econ isn't your strong suit, and the tests can be difficult.

I hated to format of this class- we spent 3/4ths of it reading a case study before each class and discussing it in class with unclear direction. there were 3 quizzes, 1 exam, and 1 giant group project, which I also hated. The packet was required because it has all the case studies. The exam was difficult because there is no textbook and little prep

Had Professor Hansen for Economics of Strategy Fall 2015. He was kind and taught very clearly. Five group spreadsheet exercises and one group consulting project during class. All relatively easy. I'd definitely recommend him!

Professor Hansen was by far the best teacher of the core. His teaching method is so clear and is not condescending when you ask him to explain something again or a different way. Very clear expectations. In class problems are super helpful. He really cares about your success, not just in class, but in life. Wonderful person and great class.

One midterm, one final.  There are about ten quizzes, and five homework assignments. Hansen gives hints to quizzes before, and reviews them after.  TA holds a review for homework and gives answers. Grading scale is very generous, so it's easy to do well. Hansen is amazing- he cares about students, is entertaining, seems so nice. Great teacher.

Mark Hansen is a rockstar. one of my favorite professors for sure because he is so helpful and so nice. he would spend class periods going over quizzes BEFORE we took them. so obviously it was easy. this class was my favorite from the core because of him. cant say enough good things. but yes its boring, all of the core is.

One of the best teachers I've had at BYU.  Cares about students, is clear and concise, and is very nice.  One of those guys that you can talk to about anything.  Easy-going, laid back, but still a very effective teacher.  The class can be difficult (what business classes aren't) but he's fantastic.

Great teacher! He really cares about your experience at school and wants you to succeed. If, you are struggling all you have to do is talk with him and you'll be able to work something out. Overall a great teacher and great guy.
Best teacher I've ever had in my life! SO impressed with him and the class! I will be eternally grateful for him!

Amazing class! He was the best teacher I've ever had! I didn't do that well in the class because I was lazy but he was willing to work with me and help me get a good grade. I'm more than thankful for him and all he did for me and the other students! Like I said, BEST TEACHER EVER!!

It was an interesting class. His lectures are boring, but really helpful if you listen. He tries to make himself available, but he doesn't have a TA, so if you have a question, you are at his mercy as to when you will hear from him. He does his grades by comparing your answers to the entire classes, which usually ends up hurting you.

Professor Hughes is a great teacher and a really nice guy! Math 290 is tough no matter what and there's definitely a lot of homework, but he made lectures easy to understand and was always willing to answer questions or give individual feedback. Instead of three midterms we had six quizzes throughout the semester, which I liked.
Dr. Mark Hughes is hands down the greatest professor I have ever had.
Very good, good at math and such

He is just generally super nice and pleasant to be around, even when math class is the last place I wanna be at 9am on a Monday morning. He gets on the students level and explains things super well. As long as you attend class, you should be fine in this class.

Awesome teacher, he's very helpful if you want to talk anything about his subjects. Attendance is not mandatory, but the slides he uploads sometimes lacks steps that he forgets students might need. Also, you'll need to ask questions to understand. The difficulty level is only because of the class itself, he does his best to make things manageable.

Mark was my favorite professor ever. The practice tests he gave before the midterms were very similar to the actual test so the tests weren't too bad. He's the sweetest funniest guy and you can tell he really cares about everyone in the class. Would recommend 1000%

He is a great guy. He wont remember your name, but he really cares about you. He is funny and has amazing lectures prepared every time. He is one of the best math professors I have had because he teaches super intuitively. BTW, expect a lot of homework.

I really enjoyed his class. My class had Math 213 and Math 215 with him and he was great. I found that he was really fair in the homework and assignments. It was clear that he truly cared about us and wanted all of us to do well. He was also really fun and down-to-earth. He set realistic expectations and showed it is ok to not be perfect.

Professor Hughes is the best! I had him for Math 290 and Math 213 and he was fantastic. Super funny and knowledgeable. He enjoys math and is super helpful. You have lots of homework in Math 290, but it is manageable. Definitely take a math class from Professor Hughes. One of the best at BYU.

MATH 213 is not an easy class by any means. The tests are lengthy/not easy, and you have to work a fair amount. All that being said, Professor Hughes made this class as easy as possible. His class notes were easily accessible, along with ample review material. And I looked forward to going to class because he always made things interesting.
Great professor
Professor Hughes really is there to help you. He is also good at teaching. If you can take a class from him, do it!

I LOVE Professor Hughes! He is super caring about his students and will do anything to help you. He also stops and asks for questions a lot, and goes into depth about concepts and makes sure that you really understand how things work rather than just having you memorize formulas and take his word for it. He's pretty funny too :)

Mark is a phenomenal teacher. He's incredibly laid back and is always cracking jokes and willing to take time to answer any and all questions during lectures. He also structures the course in such a way that really sets you up for success by having pre-class videos that cover the material and making himself available to help anytime. Great guy.

Dr. Hughes is the best. No matter who you take this class from it won't be easy, but he does a great job of explaining concepts making them clear. He really wants his students to succeed and he is very understanding. My only complaint would be that he usually goes 5-10 minutes over every class period. Other than that, he's all you could ask for.

Mark is literally the only reason I have survived the math department. He is an amazing professor. Extremely patient even with the seemingly dumbest questions. Did great in an online setting too. The class is hard. The math department makes the tests (so dumb), so they are super hard sometimes, not quite reflecting what you learn.

Professor Hughes is awesome! He made pre-class videos to introduce us to the material, his lectures were clear and funny, and he took time to answer every question. The pre-class assignments and the homework were very reasonable.

This class had more to learn than all my other math classes put together. The pace was extremely quick and I spent 3 hours a day on homework. Tests were brutal. Professor Hughes is really kind, teaches well, and answers every question patiently. We didn't often finish the lesson material, though. I took this online during COVID.

He's funny, he's engaging, he's readily available to answer questions (in class and out) and makes sure everyone understands before moving on. He also really knows his stuff. All around a great guy and great teacher to work with and be taught by.

He sends out lecture material before class which helps a ton. Hes funny, engaging, makes sure students understand, encourages questions, and is super clear when teaching. He is efficient with time and makes math fun. I wish all math classes were taught by him. Content is tough last half of the class! Theorems are critical to know well.

Dr. Hughes' lectures were so straightforward and clear to understand! He's great about answering questions and making sure you're prepared for the test. Make sure to really go through the current practice exams he sends out because they're an accurate representation of the actual tests.

Dr. Hughes presented the material clearly. His lectures were entertaining because of his random sense of humor. Going to class was completely optional There wasn't a lot of homework. My beef wasn't with him or the class, but with the tests.

Professor Hughes is very intelligent and his love for math just shines through in his lectures. It was like watching a little kid peruse a candy store with each eigenvalue, orthonormal basis, or invertible matrice more savory than the last. He is a great man and I definitely recommend him as a teacher.

My class was the first that 213 was taught at BYU, but Dr. Hughes handled the transition seamlessly. Besides being a great professor, he is a great person and he is invested in not only helping you succeed in the class, but to truly understand the material and appreciate it. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it!

This was the first time 213 was taught, which made it hard since he had to adjust from a 3 credit class to a 2 credit one. It was a little frustrating in the beginning as none of the material had context and we often heard "I can't explain it now, you'll understand later." Tests weren't too hard, but you did have to memorize names of theories.

Dr. Hughes has been the best math teacher I have had at BYU. He puts together very consistent, organized, and helpful power points to guide the class. He has open office hours that you can feel very comfortable going to for any question. He really wants you to understand the material and is great at explaining it.
Dr. Hughes was fantastic. I heartily recommend him to anyone for Linear Algebra. He explains the concepts clearly and is super funny in his lectures.

Mark truly is an amazing professor. I enjoyed learning from him. I will say, however, that although Mark was great, the class was just eh. Obviously there are some professors in the math department that think that confusing and tricky multiple choice exam questions are the way to go but the fair exam questions I'm sure came from Mark.

This is a tough class, but Prof. Hughes explains the content well and is happy to answer questions. He uses powerpoints instead of writing notes on the board (except for example problems), which isn't my style, but you can print out powerpnts ahead of time if you want to. The first month of the class is much easier than the rest of the semester.

Hughes is awesome. Congenial and good with explanations, and very accessible outside of class. That being said, this was a time consuming class. Free textbook with all the material. Tests are doable. Based on what other 290 students said about their profs, and my own experience with him, would mega recommend Hughes for 290.
He is a great guy. Lectures were easy enough to follow. He cares about his students and is also funny and real. He makes a real effort to relate to us and understand us. Highly recommend.

By FAR the best professor I have taken a math class from. I really love math so maybe I'm biased but he is so funny and his lectures were easy to follow and understand. He is just a really cool guy and I would recommend taking any class from him.

Calc 2 is a beast regardless of who you take it from. Hughes is a good guy, he keeps things interesting with his self-deprecating humor. He is a super smart dude so at times he goes a bit fast for the pace of the average student but overall he is pretty clear in his instruction and is patient with students.
He is awesome. I strongly recommend you to take his class. He clearly explains concepts. He is caring, kind, and generous. However, it won't be easy.

Calc 2 is just insanely hard (for me)- that's not his fault. He's a fantastic teacher: he posts lecture notes, posts past tests showing how to do the work, teaches concepts well/clearly, & really cares about his students.

WOW, Professor Hughes was by far my favorite teacher. He's funny and doesn't mind joking around with the students, but he also really cares about teaching you and making  sure you understand concepts. He's always willing to meet with students about homework, questions, test grades, or anything. Linear Algebra was tough but he makes it way better.

Dr. Hughes was a great professor. I really enjoyed his teaching style, and I thought he was funny. Of course, the class was relatively proof-heavy, but you can't avoid that in linear algebra, especially since all the linear algebra classes are standardized at BYU now. He was a really good professor to take it from.

Dr. Hughes was always more than willing to help me whenever I had questions on the material. Linear algebra is, by nature, a tough class. But he made it interesting and understandable. From what I have heard from other students in other classes, he may be your best choice when it comes to professors for Math 313.

Dr. Hughes was a great professor. He is always willing to help during office hours, even those students that come every day. He is decently easy-going and compared to the other professors, he helps a lot more. (Giving a key for the study guide for each test and, although not giving proofs, going over them with you).

Professor Hughes is my absolute favorite professor. He's funny, helpful, and very down-to-earth. He's consistent with office hours and is very good at explaining tough stuff clearly. On pi day, he let us all bring in pies and brought some in himself, too. If you can, take linear algebra (or anything) from Prof. Hughes!

Amazing guy! The way he taught the material made it very clear. Written homework was fair, although it often focused on little random proofs. Online homework definitely helped me understand the material.  He was always willing to answer any questions. Very nice, very funny, very genuine.  I would take all classes from him if I could!

Great professor for the subject. Linear algebra is tough but Professor Hughes wants his students to do well and will help whenever he can. Go to his office hours-THEY HELP A TON!!! If you put in your time you will do well in the class.

Awesome teacher.  Super funny and entertaining.  He makes class very enjoyable.  The class is challenging because of the proofs on test, but very doable.  Dr. Hughes is one of the best teachers I have had.  Explains things simply and clearly.  I would highly recommend him.
Epic.

Brother Hughes is a great teacher.  Personally I hate the subject and material (Linear Algebra kills me), but that is by no mean his fault and he makes it bearable.  He is funny and really cares about his students.  He has office hours and is always willing to meet with students about tests.

Mark is a very cool guy and approachable teacher. You can tell that he is passionate about what he teaches, and is eager to help his students learn. He is good at explaining difficult concepts, and answers complicated questions clearly.

From previous experiences I just thought linear algebra was going to be inexplicably difficult. However, Dr. Hughes  made the material understandable and rewarding. He has spent time outside of class and office hours to personally help guide me in my career and to answer a wide variety of questions. Very approachable, funny, and a natural teacher.

2nd place is not even close. Mark is the best math teacher I have ever had. He made the lectures fun and exciting and sensible. He could easily understand questions from the students and explained hard concepts with great clarity. I rather enjoyed going to his class, and I expect you would too.

Most confusing lecture I've ever attended.  He would mix up variables within a problem (using the same variable for 2 separate quantities).  I'm really not sure how he made math, which by itself makes sense, so dang confusing....I switched out after a week.  Could handle it.  I suggest you do the same.

This class is hard because he says to read different things in class than he said to read on Learning Suite. The textbook is really wordy and hard to follow along with. It is hard to understand what the assignments require and see feedback sometimes. This is an intro to AI class, but it is verry difficult to follow the book if you are new to AI.

This is a rating for his MSB 490-R or AI in business class but it is brand new. The worst class i've ever taken. He made every single student across every class buy his $65 textbook that was made completely by AI and is barely functional.

Easy class if you follow along with the videos and do the work. It is fun, interactive work rather than extensive reading and lectures. This class is set up to help you learn and succeed, and the grading criteria is very fair and transparent. I wish Mark taught all of my classes.
Love this guy fr fr
Great, spiritual, engaging teacher for UNIV 101.

Keith is amazing! He is incredibly smart, and he prepares you well for Intex. The tests are a piece of cake. It's a difficult subject matter but he works with you and makes it worth it. The only downfall is that he isn't great at responding to messages if you need homework help. He is also a spiritual giant and very uplifting.

I am sorry Keith is an amazing person but this class sucks. In class he goes way too fast and while the textbook is good the homework IS THE WORST! The questions are super vague and Keith and the TAs are terrible at responding to students questions in a timely manner. Assignments take HOURS and your sanity. I want my life back.

I had a fantastic learning experience in IS 455, which actually got me interested in data analysis. His textbook has all the information needed for INTEX, and I can tell he really cares about his students and their learnings. Class is hard but definitely doable and you'll learn a lot!

Doctor Keith is amazing! His classes always made me feel good. He is fair when it comes to grading. Your grade isn't defined by the group work you do on INTEX because he curves fairly so your efforts actually reflect your final grade! His assignments and exams can be challenging but his TAs are very helpful!

Keith is a great professor and explained things super well! There were 2 opportunities for extra credit and he gave a 4% curve at the end of the semester. If you just do all the reading and follow along with the videos, you'll be golden. Pretty straightforward class
D.r Keith answers super fast. Be ready to live at the TA lab, it is tough class, take it with easy classes!

Professor Keith made this class quite simple. If you watch all of the videos and follow along, you should really have no problems in this class. Professor Keith's videos were the easiest to follow and he does an amazing job explaining things. I got on a Zoom call with him one day because I was confused and he helped me a ton! 10/10 professor!
it would be nice if he were more exact with his explanations
Super respected, and very kind and approachable. Big recommend.

Outstanding Professor! Dr. Keith is the most genuine and sincere professors I have ever had. Dr. Keith was able to take every experience level and get to a useful end state of understanding. Because of his presence and approach it was easy to stay engaged and really enjoy every minute of class. Loved his calm voice and demeanor.

Dr. Keith is a good guy, but his lectures are often pointless. Overall I had a bad experience in his class. In one instance, I raised my hand to share something in class and he openly mocked me during the lecture. Definitely would choose other instructors before taking another class from Dr. Keith

Dr. Keith is one of the best professors I've ever had. He really knows his stuff and works like a dog to make sure that you have the best opportunity and access to learning the material. No other professor that I've had has made me excited to come to listen to his lectures... Except maybe Kearl...

Prof Keith is very nice but in this class he doesn't exactly teach. He just does the assignments with different data and then you apply it to your data. Attendance in most class periods isn't necessary because he posts videos of what to do on his MyEducator. Overall good teacher.
He really responded well to questions and requests for clarification

Dr. Keith is so awesome! He truly cares about all of his students and does  his best to make class lectures relevant and preparatory for the projects, homework, and exams. This is one of the most difficult classes I've taken at BYU because I'm not super great with computers, but I'm so grateful I took it from Dr. Keith! He had great TA's too!
Dr. Keith's videos are the most useful part of class.   He is hard to reach outside of class and responds late to emails.  Good subject material but would recommend another professor.

The material is tough, but I chose Mark Keith because he is one of the best lecturers at BYU. He teaches best practice methods and is incredibly effective at not only the HOW but the WHY behind his methods. I love this guy and would HIGHLY suggest taking IS classes from him. Truly one of the most Christ like people I know.

This class is challenging but this professor teaches the subject well. You have to work in this class but Prof. Keith makes it clear and easy to follow. He is also an outstanding guy, REALLY nice. I transferred into his class from another professor and was glad I did.

Personally, this was the most challenging class I've taken. There are often two portions of each exam with the first being in class and extremely time-constrained, and the second half being either in the testing center or a take-home portion. Dr. Keith is a fantastic teacher and is always there to help. Work hard and you can learn anything!

I don't know what he's like because he says at the beginning of the semester that you never have to come to class so I never did. The homework is very straightforward and easy to figure out on your own. Tests are a breeze. Easy A.

Super easy class, great professor. Class attendance was not mandatory for my section. Homework was a breeze- maybe 1 hour a week. Tons of extra credit if you attend class. 2 tests, taken at home. Really just extended assignments.

Professor Keith was a good teacher and the class wasn't especially difficult. Attendance isn't required and you can take the tests whenever you want throughout the semester so you can skip ahead. Some of the assignments had difficult content, but I'm not especially computer savvy, most people will be fine.

By far one of the nicest PEOPLE I've met in my entire life. The guy has the soul of an angel. The class is very straightforward. I find excel pretty easy so I skipped ahead and finished the final at least a week early. Go to class and you'll get extra credit. Don't go to class and you'll still get an A.
Show up to class for extra credit. Sometimes he helps you with the homework during class. He is funny and willing to help.

This is a easy A class, but you will have to do your homework assignments. Pay attention to given projects they are worth a decent percentage of your grade. I didn't go very oft to this class, but was able to get an A

The classes are pretty boring, but I think that's because the subject matter is so simple. Most of the learning is done outside of class. There is just one homework assignment a week, usually took me an hour at the most. Only 2 practical tests. Dr. Keith was a good teacher, he explained things well and answered questions that were asked.
He is a good teacher, although he can be a little confusing on more advanced topics. He is definitely willing to help. The assignments are easy, and there is a TA lab if you get tripped up.

Dr. Keith is the Man!! He really knows his stuff and he knows how to teach it. He defiantly is one of the best teachers at BYU. I would defiantly take this class from him. Not to mention, our class had the highest average out of all the IS201 classes. that's how good of a teacher he is.

Professor Keith was super dry and really hard to pay attention to. The class was only once a week for 1 hour but it seemed to stretch on. I wouldn't have gone if not for the in class assignments he does to make people come. You learn everything you need to online. Not hard at all.
The class content is mostly taught on-line. He will go through examples in class, but a lot deals with the content online. So make sure you read!

Lectures are totally pointless, except for the in-class quiz. I remember once, I counted and it took him 12 tries to demonstrate a function we needed to know for the homework that week. But, the class is a breeze. The online text he uses wasn't written by him, so it works.

I enjoyed his class.  I had already taken IS 201 before this class so some of the topics were a refresher.  He introduced many topics and gave us hints on how to get full credit on the assignments.  He is beyond-knowledgeable in the Information Systems department and knows more than any other Excel wizard that you have ever met!  Take it from him!!

I can't say enough good things about Keith. Not only is he one of my favorite human beings ever but one of the very best professors I've ever had. I'm not an IS major so I was worried about this class, but Keith made it well worth it. So understanding and makes sure you really get the material. Takes time to get to know you and truly wants to help.

Keith is an awesome professor. Very fair, and very concerned with the welfare of the student. He made it fun to be in class, and offered a lot of help to students. Highly recommended to take from him.

I came into this class not knowing what HTML was. Know I a want to major in IS! What a sweet class. Dr. Keith is the most sincere teacher I have had and wants his students to succeed. He will help you understand how to solve problems with technology. If you are not interested in technology, then you will still gain valuable problem solving skills.
Loved this class and loved Dr. Keith. He is a great guy and he actually cares about the student. He tries really hard to make sure everything is clear. I enjoyed this class a lot!

He is a great teacher that is always willing to help and work with you!  There were times were my grade didn't seem right or because of a format misunderstanding on the test i went and talked to him and he was very willing to work with me to get a better grade.  He posts helpful videos online also to help you study on topics that you may forget.

Great professor! He is very willing to work with you on your grade discrepancies. He really knows his stuff, but goes a little fast in class at times. BUT gives videos for you to study later. You can tell that he really cares about his students, and logs teaching at BYU.

Not very helpful, he doesn't write the exam and doesn't know anything about it at all.  Coming to the exam review of Gaskin is a little bit helpful, but his exam review is such a waste of time. You have to study by yourself.
He's a good teacher but a new one to BYU. Thus, I think the class will get better. If you work about 5hrs a week, you should get at least an A-.

I took this class in Winter 2013.  Book and packet, totaling around $110 are required. It was Dr. Keith's first semester at BYU and I thought he was a great teacher.  The course is a lot of work, but I think it is that way no matter who teaches it.  He seemed to do his best in helping everyone understand the material.

confusing class.  He spent too much time talking about the basics in class and would never get to the harder concepts, rather would tell you to do that for homework on your own.  the other teacher (gaskin) came and taught multiple times, and he seemed a lot more on the ball.

Dr. Kempton is an amazing professor, and cares a lot about his students. He will go to the devotional every week with you if you take this class. He's not a strict grader on exams, and he's happy to talk you through a problem if you need help.

I loved Dr. Kempton! This was a difficult class, but he was always willing to help. He was understanding about having a hard time on exams, and gave good feedback on how to do better. thought he was a GREAT professor and would not have wanted to taken the class from anyone else. Class is also curved, which was really nice. 10/10 recommend his class

This class will be really hard no matter who you take it from. He explains the concepts well in his lectures, and offers extra credit if you attend all the devotionals with him. He's always happy to help and give extra explanation during office hours. It seems like my exams were graded pretty leniently, which is surprising for a proofs-based class.

Good professor, the amount of homework was a bit overwhelming. There were assignments due 6 days a week, and I often felt that the expectation was that we should sacrifice studying for other classes so that we could get our work done. However, overall it wasn't a terrible experience.
None of the homework was tedious, and he was great at lectures.

Dr. Kempton is great but the class moves so fast that it's hard to have enough time to practice each concept. I found this class pretty difficult because the tests and homework assignments were often different from the things we discussed in class. To be prepared for tests definitely focus on the practice exams—those are what will prepare you most.
BEST. He was a nerd, endearingly. We were easily able to understand difficult material, the way he taught. The lecture before each exam was dedicated to review. *The textbook was online.
Dr. Kempton did a great job at teaching us Calc 2. The work load is not that bad. Take Math 113 from him! Written Homework can be sometimes tricky.

Professor Kempton is amazing! He taught very clearly and had a good mix of teaching concepts and doing practice problems. He loves his subject in a super endearing way! To me, he sets the standard of how a math teacher should teach. Calc 2 is tough material, but Professor Kempton made it as easy as it could be! Take MATH 113 from him!
Professor Kempton is an awesome professor. You can tell that he loves math and teaching. I would recommend taking his class.

He is humble, caring, and can explain concepts clearly. He definitely likes to work with students and makes sure everyone understands. Tons of office hours. The exams is a bit tricky but are very doable. Not a hard class, and I enjoy every lecture he made -- feel like having a wonderful math journey with him each time. Thank you, Dr. Kempton.

He can clearly explain linear algebra in many different ways.  He really cares about making sure the students understand the concepts, and the applications behind them.  The proofs can be tough, but the tests are very reasonable.  If you have to take linear algebra, definitely take it with Kempton
Took it during fall semester 2019. A great professor who really cares his students.

He is pretty funny. I enjoyed his lecture a lot. He taught the materials very well. And this class is an easy math class compared to calculus. Homework is not very heavy. Mid-terms and final are pretty easy as well. I highly recommend taking his classes.
I loved Dr. Kempton! He is so kind and makes linear algebra fun/easy to understand. He is super accommodating and willing to answer any questions you may have.

Dr. Kempton has a contagious love for math. You can't help but feel how much he loves the material, and how he wants to help students succeed. He makes a lot of quick jokes, and he's always willing to help. Definitely go to office hours if you need help with homework! I wish he taught higher level math classes so I could take one from him again.
Dr. Kempton is great! I love that he records all of his lectures. Linear Algebra is so much more doable with him.
The best math professor I have ever had. Take linear algebra from him!

Dr. Kempton is a great teacher. His lectures are clear and straightforward, and he made it a point to stop and answer questions regularly despite it being a 200-person online class (with lots of questions). He's very accommodating and cares about his students.

Dr Kempton was a great professor. The subject of the class (linear algebra) was difficult, but he explained things in lots of different ways to help things make sense. He has a good sense of dry humor, which helped me pay attention. I definitely recommend taking this class from him.

Math 213 (Linear Algebra) was great with Professor Kempton. You can tell that he appreciates the math and wants to pass that on to the students. There is a lot of stuff that you go over, but he makes it easier to review by posting class lectures and slides. The most difficult thing for me were getting used to proofs.

Dr. Kempton is absolutely amazing. He always makes sure that the students understand what he is teaching before moving on. He gives quite a bit of homework though. Make sure you learn the definitions of the different things and the characteristics of theorems, as they show up on tests. He's a great choice!

Professor Kempton is great! He's a such a nerd, but you can't help but love him for it. He explains tough concepts clearly and slowly. But it is a lot, so attend the review sessions. Even as we started doing online classes mid-semester for COVID-19, I still felt like he cared. Make sure to keep up on webassign. It's not a lot, but it's important.
He made a tough class so clear and easy to understand. Also just a super genuine guy and will do a lot to help you succeed in his class. 10/10 would recommend

Dr. Kempton is an amazing guy who make linear algebra intuitive and easy to understand. He was so patient with people's questions and really tried to make sure everyone was good before moving on. The class was pretty easy as long as you stayed on top of homework. 213 is basically 313 without any of the difficult proofs.

Dr. Kempton is one of the best professors I have had at BYU--definitely the best math professor. He explained concepts clearly, answered questions courteously and understandably, and did a lot of small things that helped me learn. He's probably the most enthusiastic professors I've had. I am studying EE and wish he was teaching more math courses .

I love Dr. Kempton! He is always really excited about the material he's teaching and it makes class so enjoyable. He's good at explaining clearly and showing examples. He's also pretty good about letting you ask questions during lectures and answering them.

Dr. Kempton is very much a math nerd. You can tell by how excited he gets about the concepts. That being said, he is a little awkward but he explains the concepts very well. The best part was hearing him trying to apply devotional topics to math. :)
