Professor Showalter is very passionate about what he teaches, and I feel that was the saving grace for my experience in this class. There is lots of reading and homework. This class accounted for 80% of my total effort toward school for the semester. Tests make up the dominant portion of your grade (65%) and the final is cumulative. It's a beast.

This class literally made me change my major to economics. I loved Showalter's lectures and how he applied what we learned in the textbooks before class to real life. Definitely a lot of work, but if you dive into it, it is super interesting and applicable to every aspect of life! Professor Showalter did a great job making assignments meaningful.

This was a tough class, but I was also taking 18 credit hours. Maybe don't take this class with more than 14 in a semester if you are wanting an A. The final is 35% of the grade and it's cumulative which is what killed me. He is great and classes are enjoyable, but if you take the class you really need to have time to dedicate to it. Lots of HW

DON'T TAKE EOCN 110 FROM HIM. There's so much weekly homework that ends up being pointless for your grade because it's all determined by the test scores. The tests are insanely difficult and nothing like what's talked about in class. Attendance is mandatory but pointless. I spent hours studying for tests and still did not do good. WORST CLASS EVER!

Professor Showalter is a nice professor with lots of knowledge and a passion for what he teaches. 
That being said... he missed the mark. His class structure requires a lot of pre-class and post-class work, with the lectures feeling useless. Tests are insanely hard and different from class. The only way I survived was tons of time and the TA lab.

Structured where you teach yourself before class with online textbook--not too hard b/c textbook has lots of practice material online. Lectures aren't meant to teach, but review/apply. Exams worth a lot (35% final, 15% each for 2 midterms). One of if not the only 110 profs to give up to 5% extra credit guaranteed if you attempt practice questions.

Showalter is a cool guy, but his lectures felt useless. Usually, class is him rambling about something. The textbook and class time didn't feel like a helpful use of time. The only way I was able to do decent in this class was relying on the TA's and classmates. Be prepared to read a lot and spend lots of time with challenging material!

This guy talks really fast and goes through material very quickly so be sure to do the pre-class readings so you're not too lost in class. Lectures are mostly skimming over the textbook readings so don't rely on them too much, go really in depth in the textbook readings and do all your assignments and you should be good. This class is hard.

Professor Showalter is great outside class but sometimes struggles to teach tough concepts, making it feel unfair to expect high mastery from students. The class leans more towards math than theory, with tests often math-heavy. The Cengage textbook is poor, with poor explanations. Difficult problem sets but they may help with tests if mastered.

Professor Showalter genuinely cares about every student. The content of his class is complex, but he does everything in his power to help his students get good grades (like tons of extra credit). His tests usually include the extra credit questions and practice exams. If you put in time and effort, you should be able to succeed in his class.

This class was so hard but so good. The TAs were a lifesaver, and it is a must to attend the TA lab. Professor Showalter gave great lectures, but the tests were made up of extra credit problems and practice test questions. reading is crucial, be he sets you up to get an A if you take advantage of all the resources he is providing.

388 is the hardest class in the major and frankly the hardest class I've ever taken. Take directly after 378 if you can. Showalter is the nicest guy and really cares about his students. He is extremely math heavy, and if you don't go to class there a good chance you'll be very lost. TA's office hours are vital for success.

So... 388 is basically just linear algebra proofs with Professor Showalter. The lectures weren't necessarily entertaining, but the class was set up ok. I just memorized the proofs I could and did ok on the tests. I was on the early track though, so 388 has changed since I took it. Cool guy. The textbook is thicker than a milkshake with no milk.

There are a lot of assignments to keep track of, but Professor Showalter is pretty clear about what to do when. The homework questions and in-class questions didn't really reflect the kinds of questions that were on the midterms. Professor Showalter knows his stuff.

Econ 110 is not necessarily a hard subject, it is just a lot of information. Professor Showalter is great though, he is very organized, so understanding and has the fastest response time on a question from a Professor I have ever seen. He sets this class up for you to succeed, but you do have to work for it. I highly recommend Prof Showalter

This was the worst class of my entire life. I have never been more miserable. I spent hours every week in the Econ lab and barely scraped by with a B. Professor Showalter is a nice enough guy but does not provide enough resources for how to succeed on his impossible tests. If you can take any other class besides Econ 110 do it. It sucks.

ECON 110 is a hard class, period. Every teacher is gonna seem difficult because the content is hard and you have to learn a lot. That's just the way the class is. As far as how Showalter does at making the class understandable, not insanely hard, and genuinely interesting, I think he did a really good job. Great guy, just be ready to work hard.

I took econ my first semester and even though I find the material challenging I really like Showalter! He gives us opportunities for extra credit and ways to make up for it if you don't do well on the midterms. No matter who you take it from it is going to hard (for most people) but from talking to others it seems he's the best one.

He is brilliant and he teaches stuff well, the only issue is that the class is very poorly structured. Reading, lectures, homework and tests are all disconnected. You might want to take linear algebra before taking this class.

Take this class! If you have any interests in Health Economics at all you can't go wrong with Dr. Showalter. You won't find a more caring and genuine professor than him. The class is heavily discussion based and there are about 4 groups presentations during the semester. Great class and even better professor.

This is a great class! The class is primarily discussion-based, and I enjoyed going to class and talking about current health economics issues. Professor Showalter is brilliant and a great teacher. You will have 2-4 presentations that you give in class, and there is a TON of reading. So it takes a lot of time but not too difficult.
Best teacher I have had at BYU. I took this class 2 years ago and still remember almost every example he used. I saw that his score is low and have no idea why, great professor.

I wouldn't consider myself an economist by any means; however, I have taken other considerably difficulty classes such as CHEM 105-107 and performed better in those than in economics. Honestly, if you put a ton of time into it, you can do better than I did, it just wasn't at the top of my priority list of classes.

The lectures were good and he tries. You really do need to read to understand what is going on. He offers Extra Credit, which helps prepare for tests but are a lot of work. Exams are very difficult. The TAs help as they can. He tries to make the class interesting and it is worth it to go. A difficult subject.
Prof. Showalter is great at teaching Economics, which in itself is a tough subject. Study a lot and attend every lecture while taking substantial notes.

Great professor and class!! Tons of reading, but no other assignments until the very end of the semester. 70% of the grade comes from the term paper and the final so you really have no idea how you are doing until the end. Final exam is all essay style questions. Interesting class, tough one if you NEED an A ( b/c grading is all subjective).

This class is the hardest class at BYU and Showalter tries his best to make it doable, but falls short. He gives a lot of opportunity for extra credit, but the tests are very difficult. He tries to meet with students to show he is helpful but he will just tell you to go meet with the TA and the other 200 students in the class and to"just do better"

There is a LOT of reading for this class and you have a quiz each lecture so you have to read (he lets you use notes). I really enjoyed the class discussions and learn a ton from other students since you all take turns presenting the academic papers. There is a 10 page paper due at the end and the final is an essay test on 10 of the papers you read

Professor Showalter is a solid choice for Econ 110, but the course itself is pretty difficult. There's a lot to cover, and the tests are harder than the assignments and are a large chunk of the grade. You'll want to go to every class and spend lots of time on the book or you'll get wrecked by the first midterm. It's doable if you work hard, though.

Dr. Showalter did a great job explaining economics. His tests and homework assignments are pretty straightforward, and everything can be found in the textbook. His lectures for 110 are based pretty much completely on the textbook, so if anything is confusing it can be cleared up with a little bit of reading

Economics is difficult and it makes sense that it takes a lot of work to understand it, but wow! I am SO glad this class is done. It was frustrating when not all of the content would be covered in class. Some test questions were written poorly (like incorrectly). Do the EC from the start. Econ lab can be helpful. Be ready to work!

Showalter is a fantastic teacher. He is very good at breaking down complex economic concepts in his lectures. As far as teachers go, he is one of the best teachers I have had so far. If you take this class prepare to work and study hard. There is a lot of homework that is necessary to understanding economics. He cares about his students.

This class isn't as bad as people make it out to be. Professor Showalter is great at helping you understand the material and gives great in class examples. The tests are incredibly challenging--I spent three hours on one once. Do the homework, study, and you should be fine.

Dr. Showalter shows an incredible respect for students. This class is a 400 level Econ course, so like many others, you will read many academic papers. Dr. Showalter outsources most of the lecture time to rotating groups of three students which serves to vary the class lectures. One of the better 400 level courses from what I hear.

This bro does not teach what is on the test. You have to learn all the difficult concepts of econ by yourself which is clutch. I would recommend taking showalter over any other teacher because you can get up to 5 percent extra credit. His tests are manageable but you have to study your life out. If I did not take this class, I would have a life.

He looks like Michael Scott, and teaches like him too. He doesn't teach anything that is on the tests. They are super hard. This is the first B that I have ever gotten in college and probably my last. If you enjoy taking classes that you have to learn everything on your own and work super hard and STILL fail the tests, take MARK SHOWALTER.
HE IS THE WORST

I really struggle with Economics, so maybe I am biased, but this class is hard. He is a nice guy, makes lectures interesting and fun, but he won't take a lot of time answering questions (if you ask he will answer, but he won't fully do it, or he'll do it fast!). I went to the lab once, TAs just talk very loudly and I can't concentrate...

I didn't do the extra credit, super boring lectures they seem rote like he doesn't understand the application, only the theory behind Econ. he doesn't understand technology, I forgot assignments because he uses both LS and a separate website. He doesn't update/post grades until after the final. Face reminds me a little of Michael Scott.

Econometrics is an absurdly difficult subject to study, so it's going to be a challenging class, even if you're an amazing student. Showalter is on every of the best though! He's caring and will always have your back. He'll become your best friend after this class

Most Econ professors either focus on Micro or Macro Economics. Showalter does both. I wish I took from Kearl. All my friends that took from him complained how hard it was, but they got the better test scores. He does not prepare you for his impossible tests and his lectures are the most boring things on this planet and are rarely helpful

Great class. All assignments are online, so you get immediate feedback and the ability to retry problems until you understand. Showalter was good as pulling in real world examples to describe the economic theories. The class is more theory heavy than math heavy, so it isn't hard to do well if you are able to visualize the big picture. Great teacher

I retook Econ 110  and had to work hard for my grade. The great thing about his class is that he offers extra credit and replacement exams (he will explain the process). The only reason I got an A in this class was because i formed a study group at the beginning of class and we helped each other out through the whole semester.  Exams way heavily.

Econ110 is rough, but I think Showalter was a decent professor. I think his lectures should be focused on helping us get through homework and exams. I spent more time on Econ110 homework than all my other homework combined. Text book is huge, tests are huge. Although, if you are bent on taking Econ110, you should probably take it from Showalter.

Prof. Showalter really enjoys his job, and this makes it enjoyable to come to class. He does a great job teaching, and you are guaranteed an A if you do the extra credit. Granted, its hard extra credit, and I didn't do it myself :)  Based on what I have heard of other Econ teachers, make sure to take it from Showalter! He cares and enjoys it.

Hardest class I have every taken. This was my first economics class and it was really frustrating because the teacher just assumed that everyone had taken some sort of economics before so he didn't explain it clearly. There was absolutely no application to our lives and it just looked like graphs on the chalkboard. The TAs helped, but didn't explai

So I just took this class to fulfill my GE credit but I ended up loving it!!!!! And, so I switched my major to Economics. He really seems so passionate when he lectures and that helps the students. His tests are pretty hard but I think he curves them. He really cares for the students so if you have questions, ask! Going to the TA lab helps a ton!

Dr. Showalter tends to say "um" alot when organizing his thoughts, but knows his stuff and is interesting to listen to. Offers some limited extra credit and grading is fair. Read the book and do the review tests multiple times as 2-4 of the problems show up on the real test. Changed my major to Econ.

Dr. Showalter is a great guy who is always willing to help you if you talk to him. The class, though difficult, is doable as long as you are willing to work hard to get a good grade. Tests are pretty tough; you have to really know your stuff to pass those. I would recommend Showalter for Econ 110.

I really enjoyed this class. He's a great teacher though the material can be hard. Do the readings and make sure you understand it because there probably won't be enough time to get everything in class

Professor Showalter was a pretty good. The TAs are what made this class possible, though. I went to 6 review sessions a week but it was still extraordinarily difficult to get an A. This class is hard, simply put, but if you put in tons of time, you can do it. Be friends with the TAs and do the God-sent weekly bonus assignments--they help a ton.

Dr. Showalter is a great professor. He explained concepts clearly in the class, and he helped me to understand the concepts that were most difficult for me in the assignments. I would recommend doing the assigned reading before class, and then doing the assigned homework after the lecture. Also, taking the practice exams several times really helped

Dr. Showalter was a professor that provided entertaining lectures.  You seemed like you were learning a lot in class until you had no idea what to do on homework and basically fail the tests.  Do all the extra credit or else you wont pass the class.

This class is tough. And it sucked. I have friends who take this class with Kearl. At least in that class he is specific to prepare you for the exams. Showalter does his own spiel rarely relating to the hw readings and never relating to the exams. Humorous guy, but that doesn't matter when I need lectures to help me pass exams. TA's are no help.

He is an awesome teacher, but this is a difficult class if you aren't adept at economics before taking the class. His tests are very difficult, and he has homework every night. His lectures are very entertaining. Participation is mandatory because you have in class problems.

Brother Showalter is an incredible professor. By no means do i consider this class easy, but I found it very interesting. I had no interest in economics before this class and now I am an econ major. Bro Showalter knows how to make a difficult subject easy to understand by using videos, stories, and current events to teach the topics themselves.

Dr. Showalter assigned interesting papers that introduced and explained the developments in Health Economics. While it was a lot of reading, the course was well organized and I knew what to expect each day. He was able to present well, discuss a multitude of relevant material, and knowledgeable about the recent events pertaining to the course.

So I gave this guy a tough rating a while back, but now that I am in grad school, I am realizing that what he taught, though difficult, was actually spot on. I am better prepared than my peers when it comes to econ thanks to his class and teaching. Use the TAs, they help a ton, and be ready to spend lots of time on Aplia.

Showalter. Good man. Horrible teacher. I didn't learn ONE THING from his lectures and hardly learned anything from the homework assignments. The assignment are SO TIME CONSUMING yet they do almost nothing to prepare you for the tests. Speaking of which, the tests are almost impossible and he doesn't curve them. Really rough class.

Showalter is a smart and nice professor; however, he doesn't teach well. He tests on in-depth material from the book and crazy algebra problems that are not remotely discussed in class. To do well on tests, go over the practice exams and discuss the crazy problems with TAs.  The extra credit makes success possible. Take the class from someone else.

He's a good guy but the lectures are useless. Seriously, just teach yourself from the book and really, really study the practice tests. They saved me. BUT be prepared, this class is super, super time consuming and the material in general is tough.

Awful. Stay away. He doesn't even teach what is on the test. He gives you software that you use to teach yourself, and even that is terrible. It is extremely difficult to understand and the questions are misleading which leads to lower scores. You will have to spend 4 hours a week reading and then another 4 hours doing homework each week. AVOID!

Showalter is a great guy. Makes a big effort to get to know everyone in his big classes. His lectures don't help you at all on the tests. You will do well in this class if you do the practice tests, extra credit, and work really hard.

I took Econ from Butler and didn't do too well. So I had to take it again, and this time I took it from Showalter. I really believe that I did well in this class for two reasons: 1) I did all of his weekly extra credit work and 2) the online aplia is a much better option than doing homework out of the book. Take 110 from Showalter. Or else.

Honestly, going to class is a joke. He doesn't really apply much outside of what we learn through the online reading. The only reason I went to class was for iClicker points. But even those are worth .1% of your grade. Just a hard class in general and seemed to make no effort to make it easier.

It's a good class but's it is hard material. Showalter understands that it's a bleeder class for many programs so he doesn't make it very easy on you or anyone else. If you do the work and actually pound the concepts into your mind then you will do well. Funny guy, hard class.

This class is VERY time consuming and the material is beastly. It's kind of like drinking from a firehose. Prof. Showalter is funny but his lectures have little to do with the actual tested material. I can't speak for future classes but the practice test SAVED my grade, the TA's are very nice and helpful.

Dr. Showalter is a great guy. Very kind and willing to help you out in any way. The TA's were awesome too. I would highly recommend doing all the bonus assignments and making sure to do well on the homework. Tests are hard, but if you go to the Econ lab and do the practice test you should be fine. Hard, but worth it.
Be prepared for lots of reading, too much to be honest.  He is a good guy though and is willing to work with you.  As far as econ classes go his is not too hard.

The class is a joke. You are required to go so you can get iclicker points, but you learn NOTHING. I wish I could just stay home and read the book since it is 10X more beneficial. Also, there is a heap of busy work, and he makes you spend $150 on Aplia and an online text...money you will never get back. BYU, re-evaluate econ 110 course please!

Take Econ 110 from Showalter. There is online homework that takes up a lot of time, but it is for your benefit. Class was interesting, but not relevant to do well in class. His practice tests are SO helpful! He also offers bonus problems for extra credit. Also, utilize the TAs.... they help so much! Got an A.

Showalter is a great guy. I really enjoyed him as a person, but the class is just difficult. He does a descent job at explaining things, but the material is rocky and sometimes his logic isn't easy to follow. I did take half of the course from Butler, and a few weeks from McDonald, and it seems easiest to get a decent grade in Showalter's class.
My favorite class that I ever took at BYU.  Prof. Showalter makes class fun with all of his stories and examples.  It has been the most influential class that I have ever taken.

I felt Dr. Showalter was a very impersonal teacher.  I went in to his office to talk to him on several occasions and each time he came across distanced, awkward, and overly professional.  Not the best class, wasted a lot of time.  I'd recommend taking it from another teacher.

Dr. Showalter is the worst professor I've had at BYU. I found him arrogant and ineffective.   I can't speak for his 110 classes, but in 465 we read 60+ pgs of homework each day and then in class he would just ask what everyone thought, followed by his insightful 'ok.'  I did fine grade-wise, but he and the class were a waste of time. Bad teacher.

Fun class. You read academic papers for each class. It can be A LOT of reading. However, you're not expected to understand much of what you read, as long as you get the general idea. Big paper due at the end. Final isn't too rough. It's all discussion format. I enjoyed that. Reading the papers can be pretty stretching though.

It's got the reputation for being a tough class. Econ is just hard. I love prof Showalter he is a rock star. A lot of people stopped going to lecture cause of the web homework, but I kept going I thought it was helpful when he would go over it.

Hard class.  Lots of busy work.  Professor Showalter is funny and a good professor, but he doesn't do a good job of telling you what you need to know. TA's are pretty much useless and good luck getting timely email responses from the professor, but overall it was ok.

Prof. Showalter did his best with such a large class and a challenging subject. The class has a lot of busy work that doesn't correlate with the exams. His lectures were interesting, but again didn't really correlate with the exams. You use Aplia for online textbook and homework- if you do well in the class it is bc you teach yourself well.

He looks and acts like Michael Scott from the office. I really liked this class and thought he taught it well. A ton of homework but no thing too hard. Great class, makes you look at life in a different prospective.

I don't think Dr. Showalter's lectures could get any more boring.  There were a lot of homework assignments that had nothing to do with the tests.  Your only chance for the tests is to study the practice tests like crazy.  Although I didn't like this class, I have heard that he's one of the better teachers to take it from.

Hard class, but not that hard if you put in the work. I didn't really like him or the class that much, but it really wasn't that bad. TAs were pretty useless though. The easiest 110 class from what I've heard.

Lectures and homework assignments never correlate to test questions. 3 homework assignments a week plus extra reading out of a separate book and the Wall Street Journal. Tests are killer, TA's don't know anything, teacher talks about application to life, not application to graded problems. Class was a waste of my time and money.
Good class.  He requires a good amount of work mostly to bump your grade up.  If you do the work, and study in groups, you will succeed.  Probably the easiest of the 110 profs.
Gives way too much work, not helpful, incredibly hard tests that are nothing like the homework.  Take someone else if you can

Extremely nice guy! Prof MS does a very good job in keeping in touch with every student in a class of 250 students. His lecture is very interesting but not so helpful. The tests are ok, if u know the stuffs, u will be fine. The textbook is excellent. The works are quite heavy for a 3credit course. But in general, I would pick him if i were u.

Probably the most relaxed Econ professor.  His teaching is laid back, and the tests will hit you if you dont put in the work. Go in to the TA lab and get a 10 on every homework assignment. If you do the Mankiw problems, the tests will be fine.  The curve makes the class just like any other at BYU.  I would recommend him.

This is a really tough class, but I think Showalter is the best teacher to take. He tires to make the class interesting. Most everything correlates directly to the textbook, and he covers the material very clearly. Lots of work. 2-page essay every week. 20-40 online HW questions after every lecture, plus reading. 2 midterms, comprehensive final.

This class is a very difficult one. I feel Pro Showalter did a very good job at explaining the material. He lectures very well, though just paying attention is not enough. You will need to go to labs, do the homework in groups, ask questions, and make sure you understand the principles to be able to get points on the stretch questions on the tests.

Great professor. Atmosphere in the classroom is rigorous yet relaxed. His homework and tests are very difficult. Much of the material on the tests are not covered in class or on hmwks. But this is econ...that's the point. He follows the econ philosophy that the really smart kids can figure the new stuff out. Tries to create a natural bell curve.

I didn't go to lectures, as they were essentially regurgitated directly from the book. Going to the labs help more than lectures. Do the readings and the homework, and with the curve the class isn't that difficult.

Professor Showalter is a great person and knows his stuff well. Classes are intense and he doesnt teach whats on the homeworks, so GO TO LAB and WORK IN GROUPS. His tests are KILLERS but he curves mercifully. On top of it all, hes very relaxed and fun.

Great guy, and really applies economics to real life in his class, but his lectures don't really help out with the homework.  Study the textbook, and prepare for the tests since they are very hard. As a side note, he looks and talks like steve carrell. He is very funny.

He was a great professor. I love his lectures, they are both interesting and applicable. He really helped me understand economics and actually helped me apply the things I was learning in my life. His tests are killer. The class average is usually in the low 70s.  There is also a lot of homework and reading, but you will learn a ton in this class.
Easiest guy to take the class from.

Great teacher.  Does a good job at teaching the material.  His tests are a killer, but the homework load isn't that bad.  If you do the reading and homework and go to the lectures, believe it or not, but you actually understand the material!  The tests are a little hard (average test scores usually in low 70's). But a good choice for ECON 110.
This was the hardest class i have ever taken. I didn't know what to study for the class. The lecture didn't help, the homework didn't help, the book didn't help. And i tried hard.

Don't be fooled - this is the hardest class in the major, but Showalter does a great job. Very down to earth, very good at explaining both the technical stuff and the applications. He worked under Mankiw in the White House, and also helped edit the textbook.

Signed up for it pre-mish, got text, oddly all chapters but those on "leftist" economists eg Keynes were assigned. Ended up not taking then. Signed up for it again post-mish; new reading list politically motivated (eg Skeptical Environmentalist; he belittled the book's critics in the syllabus). Will take from other prof+learn econ not his politics.
Daily homework assignments and class is a waste of time.
He's pretty good. In my class he taught just out of the book -no extra things added.
Dr. Showalter is an extremely good, but also quite difficult professor. He is excited about the subject matter and is adept at getting students excited about it.

Showalter is probably the easiest of the Econ teachers, but the class is still hard.  There is a ton of work to do throughout the week, but the tests are very moderate in hardness.  The assignments are fairly easy and they bring up your grade if you do them.

Lots of busy work with assignments due on days when there is not class. Does he have a clue  people work and have other classes? His busy work takes up too much valuable time, I guess it makes up for his boring lectures or the fact that he cannot teach. Moreover, the costs of books, the APLIA program, and a magazine subscription are ridiculous.

He seems to be boring.  Daily work to stay ahead.  Online quizes as well.  Interesting at first and then appears to be boring. Tests are harder and the key to make it is labs and classes.  He tests on his stuff not necesarily from the text.  still better than kearl.
He was not too tough. Probably easier than any other Econ professor.

Dr. Showalter can be funny in his lectures and often provides a comical "break" from the lecture somewhere in the middle. He provides basic insight into the economic principles as they are presented in the text. Daily coursework is about the amount to be expected; this is not a particularly exciting class. A GREAT alternative to Dr. Kearl.

I really liked Dr. Showalter's class. He's really funny and his lectures stick to the text for the most part. The class moves very fast because there's so much material to cover since BYU combines micro & macro material into one semester. There's quite a bit of work, but it's bearable. A good alternative to taking Kerl.

Brother Showalter can be really funny at times but this is economics so it's not so easy to stay awake in. Lots of work, 2 chapters fromt he text, 2 chapters from a novel, an essay paper every week, 3-5 quizzes per week, 3 midterms and a comprehensive final but overall I liked him.
Prof doesnt test on same material as teaches in class.  Lectures are ok but not the greatest.

I took GWS 390R with Professor Esplin and she was wonderful. This was a research class and she always made sure we had the resources and support we needed to meet deadlines complete our work. She is so caring and it's clear she loves her students so much. I would absolutely take a class from her again!
I love Professor Esplin! She is so intelligent and very kind.

I have taken 3 classes from Professor Esplin and she is one of my favorites at BYU. She creates a great atmosphere for expressing opinions and getting into the material. Conversations are thought provoking and always answer the "why does this matter" question. Be prepared to read, but its worth it. She gives good feedback on your papers.

I really liked Dr. Esplin. She assigns a lot of things to read, but I wasn't particularly bothered by that since I was interested in the material. Lectures were sometimes dry since she was constantly trying to have a group discussion about the texts we had just read, but I would recommend the class if you're interested in it.

Professor Esplin expects you to read a lot. In class, most of what we did was just review what we read, and I felt like there wasn't a whole lot added. She grades fairly, and the first couple of assignments were easy to understand, but after the first term, I felt that the speed of the class greatly accelerated.

Dr. Espline is amazing, I thought that this class, GWS 222 would be super feminist and she would be super liberal (not my cup of tea) but this classed really opened my eyes and made me more aware. There is a lot of reading, but the tests aren't that hard. All of the other assignments were due at the end of the semester so don't fall behind.

Professor Esplin is honestly one of the kindest professors I have ever had. While I don't totally love the class structure (you literally just discuss the readings as a class, which can be frustrating), it is a worthwhile class, and from what I've heard about other professors, she's the best one to take it from. Beware, though, the tests are HARD!

I took this class as a GE and it was my least favorite class. You are expected to read A TON and if you aren't interested in latin culture it's a hard class to enjoy. Not a terrible professor, but not my favorite either. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone.

Professor Esplin made me love reading even more than I already did. There are a ton of readings but I enjoyed almost all of them. Lectures are very participative and she is caring and funny. All comments in the class are welcome. Definitely my favorite class this semester. The tests are not super easy but she gives all the material necessary!

Dr. Esplin is so genuinely caring to her students, she wants to see you succeed. Her lectures are very interesting and she tries hard to immerse you in Latin American culture as much as she can. Not a lot of work but readings are assigned for each class, few essays (2), and two tests (midterm and final). This was definitely one of my top classes.

Professor Esplin knows a lot! There are many readings but nothing exaggerated. Pay attention to the things she comments from the texts you read because that helps you in the test. Attend the lectures and do the readings and you will be fine. Overall, great professor, would like to take more Latin America classes with her.

Friendly demeanor while teaching and just meeting with you in person. Shows movie clips, music clips, art, and literature. Tests are lecture-based and not challenging if you attend class (not lots of memorizing because it's based on what you got out of lecture). I felt much more knowledgable and cultured about Latin America after this course!

Participation is not required in the class, but it's a much better experience to make comments because it's a theory class and you'll understand better. She's friendly, very educated, has a down-to-earth attitude, and has appropriately high expectations for the course but I never felt concerned about my grade. Loved her mixed media approach.

Bumped into Professor Esplin 2 years after taking her class. Still remember my name! She is understanding, easy to talk to, and passionate about her subject. Her class was purely enjoyable for me. I learned A LOT and you will too.

Here's the thing: in Esplin's class you are assigned a ridiculous amount of reading. I skimmed about ten pages total and got an A. She recaps in class everything you should have learned from the reading (and consequently what you'll get tested on). She's very clear about expectations. I'd buy the books but don't stress about reading them. Not hard.

A TON of reading, a ton of attendance points, a ton of pop quizzes on reading, a midterm, and 2 papers. She grades SUPER hard on the essays, and basically your grade on the essays will be the grade you get. NON-negotiable with illness/personal issues.

Professor Esplin is great. I took this class to cover a GE. There is definitely work involved, including a few days with some long readings, but if you have any ties to Latin America at all a lot of the readings will actually be interesting. You HAVE to go to class  - there are no study guides for the test, but they are fair tests.  2 short essays.

Professor Esplin is very reasonable and kind. The class is  100% based on reading; it's what your tests and assignments are based on. I really learned a lot from this class and the reading load wasn't too bad in the end. There are several graded in-class papers. Key to passing the two tests is doing the readings and participating in class.

I took this class for a GE and nothing more, but ended up loving it! Professor is not super personable, but she is a good teacher. The description of the tests were overwhelming, but if you attend class and do all the readings the tests are very straightforward. There are two papers that also seem stressful, but they are not graded harshly.

One of the best humanities classes I have ever taken, not only do you learn a lot and get a wide variety from Latin America, but you will talk about past and current issues surrounding Latin America. I would definitely recommend taking this class, Final exam is not comprehensive, but be sure to study and do the readings.

I think Professor Esplin really knows what she's talking about. Her classes are very organized and they go over your assigned reading. Turned in 2 papers (not too long, about 4 pages), but only had 1 midterm and then the final. Tests are not hard if you go to class and pay attention and do your readings.  She is nice, not boring. Its a good class.
Prof. Esplin is very intelligent, but a tough grader. In my opinion her grading of papers was just all about whether or not she liked it, regardless of obvious quality.  HEAVY workload.

Teacher Esplin is the kind of teacher that loves to read and will make you read a lot of book, but most of them are really interesting. In the class she loves to go over the reading and if you take notes from what she talks innclass you will do great in the exams

Prof Esplin is really great. She really knows and loves the material she teaches, and she's incredibly helpful and flexible with students' needs. If you are interested in the Humanities, you'll love her class! If not, you might get bored.
Very caring and invested in the class, frequently reached out to me to ask what he could do to support me, and gave very entertaining and educational lectures. Learned a lot and loved the class.

Marty is a great professor because he cares so much about his students! He creates a safe environment in class. The most time-consuming part of class is the volunteer hours; the work load wasn't hard. He communicates expectations clearly, and is willing to work with students outside of class. His enthusiasm for social work is contagious!

This class was super easy and everything I learned was valuable. Marty cares so much about his field and it was so fun to learn from him. There were a few easy quizzes, 2 papers, some short writing assignments, and 20 volunteer hours. He gives you many options for the hours, but contacting an agency early is important!

I learned a lot in this class from Marty. It was very valuable information especially if this is a field you are looking into. He told current stories. He loves talking to his students 1x1. Participation was definitely appreciated. I missed a ton of class but watched zoom recordings on 1.5x speed for slightly less credit and still loved it.

I did not have a great experience in this class. He seems to know very much about the topic, which was helpful, but he is very unaccommodating and - to simply put it - seems very full of himself. He was often bragging about his success as a therapist and did not come across as genuine. The class was easy, but it was not an enjoyable class.

This class is super easy and interesting. The only downsides are 1-he tends to drag on and the class sometimes is boring and 2-you have to volunteer for 20 hours but there are cool places to volunteer. The tests are super easy matching questions and it's not a big deal to miss class. Marty really cares about what he does which is cool to see

Marty is one of my favorite professors. If you're interested in social work, I highly recommend taking from him. The reading wasn't bad, and honestly you could get by without it, but the lectures were great. I looked forward to class. There are twenty service hours required, but they're a breeze. Easy A. Take from Marty if you have the chance!

Marty is a really great choice. He is so knowledgable and passionate about social work. The only slightly difficult part of this class was filling required volunteer hours. Marty will give you a list, but many organizations require weeks to certify volunteers. Start volunteering EARLY and with multiple places, so you aren't in a bind at the end.

I LOVED taking this class from professor Matheson! He really cared about his students! Class was super easy - 20 volunteer hours, a presentation, interviewing a social worker, and two papers, which sounds like a lot, but I took it summer term and it was a breeze! Class is mostly discussion based and Marty is super respectful of everyone's opinions.

Marty is such a sweet and caring professor. I loved learning from him. The class involves 20 hours volunteering, a presentation, interviewing a social worker, and 2 papers. Other than that, just read the textbook, complete a couple vocal quizzes, and you're basically done! Very manageable and inspirational class. Great class discussions as well!
I'm half way through the semester and enjoying Marty's class (one of the best classes I've taken at BYU so far). Really nice person as well!

Professor Matheson was great. He is definitely one of the most caring professors I've ever met at BYU. He is kind and understanding to his students. He told many stories giving examples of what Social Work is really like day to day. Easy class, just a couple vocab quizzes and no final. It's an easy A, and he's such a nice guy.

This course was by far my favorite I've taken at BYU so far! Professor McFarland is incredible and really gave me a whole new outlook on life. I looked forward to every class and loved participating in discussions. I think every person should take this class at some point!

Literally amazing. This class alone was truly life changing and opened my eyes to many issues I never knew about. For teaching a class that can sometimes have touchy or difficult subjects, professor McFarland does an amazing job at changing perspective while also leaving you to form your own opinion. Yes, there's a lot of reading, but so worth it!

Seriously one of the coolest women on campus. This class has changed my whole outlook on life, and I wish everyone would take it. Readings to do for every class, but she makes it fun and switches it up with videos and songs sometimes. 3 main projects throughout the semester. Test is essay/short answer but it's open note.

The professor is organized and knowledgeable, but much of the course promotes pro-LGBTQ+ and pro-trans perspectives that conflict with Church teachings. Students at BYU who want their education to align closely with the gospel may find their views challenged or uncomfortable.

There is a lot of reading in this class, but it is so so worth it. Professor McFarland is such a genuine and caring person and you can tell that she loves what she does and is passionate. The class is completely life changing my outlook on life has changed and I would 100% recommend this class with Professor McFarland to EVERYONE.
INCREDIBLE CLASS. Lots of outside reading. Don't procrastinate your final paper. You know your final questions at the beginning of the semester. Be prepared to have your mind blown. So good

This class is one of the few college classes I took that I would say was life changing. There's a lot of reading, but it's always so worth it. The lectures and material change your perspective and you can feel Professor McFarland's passion. I will 100% always recommend this class to anyone! If you have to take it, take it from Professor McFarland.

MaryAnn was incredible! This class honestly changed my life. Lots of assigned readings, with a reading response due before each class, but she tries to pair it down so it's less work for you. One research project (present your findings in a video presentation submitted to Canvas), a 6-8 pg research paper, an open-note final exam. HIGHLY recommend!

This class was taken to fulfill a psych prereq and it was so worth it. Class had great discussions and while there is plenty of reading to do each work the grading isn't tough and as long as you go to class and complete the assignments you'll be fine

Cares so much about the students and the topic. Homework stays consistent so you know what to expect and a lot of the readings are fun. If you're going through something, just make sure to talk to her and you will be taken care of. Really fun class, always looked forward to it.

This was such an inspiring and enlightening class. I took it for a general, but it inspired me to take other global women's studies classes. Professor McFarland is such a wonderful instructor. She is so well informed about what she teaches, and so understanding of everyone's circumstances. The classwork was manageable and pertained to the class.

This was a great class! Very interesting an informative. Assingments are pretty straighforward. Some weeks reading is pretty heavy but not bad if you don't leave it to the last minute. A somewhat politically charged class with some unique opinions mixed in but overall a great class with the opportunity to learn about a lot of important issue.

It's my belief that everyone at BYU should take this class, especially women. Professor McFarland is amazing and GWS 222 is the only college course that I've found myself actually looking forward to. The material assigned is very insightful, I've met many people in the class that share similar beliefs with me, and the discussions are enlightening.

Professor Mary Ann McFarland is my favorite professor ever! Her lectures are interesting and you can tell she genuinely cares about you. You do have a large amount of homework, but it is the most enjoyable homework I have ever done in college. If you are interested in taking this class you should definitely take it from this professor.

I LOVE professor McFarland!!! There is a lot of homework and reading, but it's very interesting. There are a few big grades, but mostly it's just homework, discussions, and attendance. This class makes you think deeply, and the class discussions are amazing! Everyone should take this class!! Also she truly cares about every student.

Professor McFarland was wonderful. All the readings were fascinating and completely changed the way I view the world. She handles sensitive topics really well. My class had awesome discussions. Her grading criteria is really clear, you can't do poorly in this class unless you do don't do the work. Couldn't recommend enough!

Mary Ann is passionate about what she teaches, and very well informed about the issues we discuss and existing research about it. She does a great job of integrating popular culture and media into our discussions and assignments, and puts into practice what she teaches. Great facilitator of class discussions.

The course was disorganized. Assignments would pop up the night before they were due, which made it hard to plan ahead. Discussions had a lot of potential, but the students didn't have a lot of opportunity to share their thoughts and questions.

Dr. Davis is one of the best at BYU! She truly cares about her students and actively uses feedback to improve the class. The course is difficult with lots of tests and memorization, but she makes it worthwhile and supports you with helpful memorization strategies and lab activities that really reinforce the material.

Professor Davis struggles to teach effectively. Lectures lack clarity and structure, and she fails to build constructive relationships with students. Her inexperience is clear, and students may want to look elsewhere.

The beginning and middle of the course were fine. But in 301, towards the end there's a big project that is kind of overwhelming and I wish she would have prepared us better for that. Most of us had to have an extension on it, especially because it was combined with our 10 hour practicum! The only upside was that she was quick to answer emails.
She's awesome! Typically have one reading or video to watch then write 1 page response! Makes the learning fun! Interactive in class! Guides are perfect for tests. I totally would take again!

Come to class and complete the assignments and it is an easy class! She cares about her students and is patient. She has fun activities for the class to do together that we can use in our future classrooms. Side note: she does tend to speak very slowly which made it a little bit difficult to stay completely alert during lectures at times.

Dr. Knell is an amazing teacher! I learned so much about Immersion Education and I felt prepared to tell others about its structure, mission, and results. Highly recommended for anyone who is even considering the Dual Language Immersion minor.
Prof Eyring is quite simply the best professor I have ever had and one of the best people I have ever known. She has changed my life for the better.

Prof. Eyring was incredible and my favorite professor after four years at BYU! She was so engaging and passionate about this subject. She has high expectations for her students that really push us to succeed. Accommodating and engaging and interesting and so intelligent. It was truly a joy to be in her class.

Prof. Eyring is everything I want to be and more! I would take any class from her. She is so genuine and kind. Her lectures are truly fascinating, and I couldn't help but be interested in everything she taught.

If I had to describe what it is like to take a class from Mary, I would say profoundly life-changing. She is one of the greatest people I have ever met and I genuinely looked forward to every class period. I can not say enough good things about her or her teaching style.
Her grading system is unique to her and her alone. No matter how hard I tried she wouldn't give me an A on a paper and followed it up with a better luck next time note to me at the end of the year.

Mary is a tough grader, but she is also an amazing teacher. I learned more about literary criticism and how to write well in this one class than during the rest of my undergrad. Mary was also very compassionate and was willing to work with students like me who were struggling at times to keep up. She is AMAZING!
My first and favorite English professor. She got me a job and encouraged me to continue in the major. Wonderful teacher and person.

Hardest part of this class is that she has really high standards for papers. But, she's very helpful during office hours, making an A on a paper totally do-able. Prof. Eyring is so good at making difficult material accessible and at building a syllabus that is interesting and fun (not just the same early American texts you've read 12 times already)

Eyring was awesome! Difficult class, but if you enjoy intellectual conversation and expanding your world views this class is extremely enjoyable. Lectures feel like a large in depth group discussion where opinions and comments matter more that crossing off the boxes to get through the lecture.

Dr. Eyring is brilliant. While the class is lecture-heavy, if you listen, you will learn a ton. She knows what she is talking about. What's more is she cares for each of her students and gives really helpful feedback. She is willing to work with you. And she is just a gem of a person overall.
Helped me love a class I didn't think I would like

She's a great teacher and very knowledgeable. Her lectures are usually very advanced and confusing. Notes are mandatory if you want to do well on the tests (only one midterm and the final). Helpful feedback on papers. TONS of reading, so be aware of that. She's great though, and very open to all viewpoints and perspectives.

Dr Eyring is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. She prepares for her classes so well and gives really great lectures and facilitates great discussions in her class. The tests were hard but there weren't many of them. We had to turn in reading responses every class but if you do them you get credit. I 100% recommend taking her  class.

Professor Eyring is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students and their academic success. I thoroughly enjoyed her class and actually enrolled for another one of her classes! She is a fair grader, and validates all of her students comments and gracefully incorporates them into the discussion. The exams are difficult, but doable.

Dr. Eyring actually cares about her students and wants them to learn. She asks for feedback from the class and wants to know how she can improve. She is really funny and class goes by quickly. She incorporates a lot of class discussion rather than just lecture. I wish I could take her for every English class at BYU!

I adore this woman; she is such a fantastic teacher. She is incredibly intelligent, kind, funny, and organized. I learned so much in this class. There's a lot of reading (like every English class) and a short paragraph response due every class period, but every assignment was well worth it. She cares about her students and gives excellent feedback.
She is amazing! not only is she gorgeous and nice, but also a great teacher. Lots of student participation. I think I want to be her when I grow up.

I adore her. Her class is challenging, but she does it to make you stretch yourself. She helped me numerous times, and always made herself available, even out of her office hours when I couldn't come. She validates everyone's comments and opinions no matter how dumb you may feel when you contribute.

Her tests are usually extremely hard, and her grading is tough, but you won't learn the basics better from anyone else. She's engaging, well-liked, and knowledgeable about all of the topics. Discussion is everything in this class, and it works well for her. What a fantastic teacher; I would take a class from her again.

Professor Eyring is so knowledgeable in English. She will learn your name and talk to you personally if you need help. You will get a good grade so long as you show up to class, participate, and make an effort on all assignments. Don't fall behind on the readings! If you want to learn English take Eyring!

Besides simply being an extraordinarily nice person, Dr. Eyring is really helpful during class time. Her lessons help you understand everything from the reading and learn how to apply your knowledge to a variety of topics.

She is super awesome and helpful! The projects are difficult, but her grading is really fair. She is super smart and gained a lot from taking this class. If you go into it with the attitude of following all her instructions, you will do great. She is also really understanding of extenuating circumstances.

I cant say enough good things about Mary Jane. I had her for both 276R & 378. Shes been one of the most caring professors I've ever had. Shes so helpful & she really wants us to succeed. Shes clear about what is expected from us & knows more about the FACS Ed program than anyone & shes got so much real life experience with teaching FACS. love her!!
Good experience, however, class feels extremely long due to the many personal stories she shares. Final projects were so fun!
Mary Jane is pretty cool. She'll let you call her M.J. She has decades of experience and it really shows. She's a great resource to have.

The class is fun but felt like it was made to try to trick you into failing. They block the responses of quizzes so you can't study. I got sick, missed one of the quizzes and the response was “the due date has passed”. No flexibility, no understanding. She feels inferior and tries to compensate by being unreasonable.

Super subjective. I keep failing assignments purely because "I didn't read the fine print." Professor has a God complex on making this class harder than it should be. I'm taking way harder classes this semester to worry about this one.

Run! I was expecting this to be a fun online class, but nope. Super subjective grading, little to no instruction. I emailed her weeks ago and never received a response. Was charged 50 dollars for a textbook I wasn't even aware of.
There was no study material for the tests! She made the class way harder than it should have been. Would not recommend!

This professor is so unnecessarily hard. She will dock so many points for the most useless things. She refused to give me a day of extension because I had a fever of 102 and couldn't get out of bed to make a lasagna and she docked a ton of points for it being late. There is no reason in the whole earth that this class should be this hard.

Dr. Allen was incredibly caring and responsive to questions and needs. His lectures were very clear and all concepts were explained well. The homework did a great job of preparing students for the tests and all tests were very fair.

Dr. Allen is an awesome professor! He does tons of examples in class and is super kind and approachable. He's always happy to answer questions and replies to emails really fast. Grading is fair, and he records his lectures, which is a lifesaver if you miss class. The textbook was a free pdf. Definitely would recommend!
Dr. Allen is one of the best professors I have ever had. He genuinely cares for the students and is a great and reasonable teacher. One weekly homework assignment and a page of notes for each test.

One of the worst teachers in the ME dept. Lectures consisted of him working through a 45 minute problem. Often getting the answer wrong and then looking to us to see if we can find his error. We of course have no idea what is going on either. Bad at teaching. Nice otherwise. Do yourself a favor and skip class. I went every day and it was worse.

He prepares you well for tests, which are not bad. The homework is not bad. The group project is easy. He brings in lots of real world examples. This class has lots of real world application. He really cares about his students. He shares life advice which I appreciated. Easy to get his help out of class. Cannot recommend Dr Allen or ME 437 more.

Dr. Allen did a great job of making the material applicable to the world around us. He used lots of examples in class which made lecture a lot more interesting. He also gave us a very open-ended final project, which I really appreciated and was helpful for learning.

Professor Allen was a very reasonable professor, especially in terms of how much woek was required for the class. The homework load was reasonable, we had one group project, tests were about average on difficulty and he taught in class what was needed for the homework. As long as you pay attention, you'll do fine.

Dr. Allen is a very personable guy and spent the time to explain the concepts. There were plenty of opportunities to ask about things that were confusing and he was always happy to go back and explain. The course load was pretty standard for ME classes. Nothing so difficult that it stood out but also challenging enough to force learning.

Dr. Allen is an amazing professor. His lectures were a joy to go to and I especially loved the insights he would share about life. He is very kind, caring, and wants to do all he can to help you learn. Sometimes in his lectures he gets carried away and whips out some professor magic that can be hard to follow but other than that he is awesome

Dr. Allen likes to move quickly through the class slides which come from the standardized Jensen-McLain notes. He prioritizes lecture time working examples on the board which I prefer, even often getting to the HW. We had a lab and project which he has high expectations for, but he is eager to meet with each group to help! One of the dept's best!
He was a great professor, very fair and cared about what the class wanted to know.

Dr. Allen is a good teacher, and he really helps students out. I received help specifically with tests. Unfortunately, that wasn't enough to help in my case. The tests are difficult, and he grades pretty strictly but he's a good teacher and I highly recommend him for Kinematics. Be wary if you have Testing Anxiety though, you may want to study more
Good class.  Dr. Allen teaches the concepts very clearly, and nothing in this class is too difficult to understand but it is very useful stuff.  Would definitely recommend.

Dr. Allen is extremely knowledgable about dynamics, which is good if you can keep up. Sometimes he tends to loose people (myself included). However, if you go talk to him during office hours he can usually help quite a bit and explain concepts well. He also is a great guy, really cares about his students and their progression.

Not a particularly difficult class, and the material was learnable, but the format was frustrating. Dr. Allen is a harsh grader, which is difficult because the two midterms and the final project (all of which he personally grades) make up 82% of the total grade. On projects, he would take off points for things that were not mentioned in the rubric.

Im really disappointed with this class overall. I took this class thinking I might major in Latin American Studies, however, this class completely ruined that. If this class is a reflection of other classes that I would potentially be taking in the LTAM studies program, then I don't want any part of it.

He is a nice, fun guy, but very unorganized. Little mention of a final until the last month of class (20% of grade). Long delays for grades. Intensive workload. Final paper 35% of grade. Lots of confusion and miscommunication with unclear criteria. You pretty much have to teach yourself the subject matter. I don't feel like this class is worth it.
He REFUSES feedback on grades.

I HATED this class. It was like three classes combined in one, with all of their assignments piled on top of you. It was simultaneously a Latin American History class, a Research Skills class, and a Lecture Series. There was a TON of homework and little assignments. That being said, if you talk to the teacher a lot, you would prob be fine.

The worst class I have ever taken- this professor made it so hard. The beginning of the semester was so homework and reading heavy and on top of that we had the most tedious "scavenger hunts." Heavy assignments are worth 1% of your grade as well as simple things. 55% of your grade is the final exam and paper. Only take this class if you have to.

Overall he's a great guy and a solid professor, but there's SO MUCH WORK in this class. The work isn't very hard, except for the final paper, because grading criteria is really clear. But the sheer amount of work is just pretty overwhelming, especially because many of the assignments feel quite pointless.

Matt is new at teaching the intro to LAS class, so I don't want to be too harsh, but his class is very poorly designed and he requires WAY too much work, about double what BYU is allowed to give students based on the school's credit:hours ratio. So far he's been okay about changing unfair deadlines, etc. But he's easily threatened and unhelpful.

His lectures are good, but he always gets very behind in his teaching schedule, sometimes missing entire chapters that are on the exams, so there's a lot you have to review by yourself. But he has youtube lectures and good practice exams

I've taken Dr. P for chem 351 and 352. He is a good teacher but what saved my bacon in this class was his voice overs. His voice overs differ slightly than what he teaches in class, but I would watch his voice overs and condense those notes and cross verifed them with what he taught in class and studied those notes and did very well in the class

I've taken Dr. P for chem 351 and 352. He is a good teacher but what saved my bacon in this class was his voice overs. His voice overs differ slightly than what he teaches in class, but I would watch his voice overs and condense those notes and cross verifed them with what he taught in class and studied those notes and did very well in the class.

Dr. Peterson is a nice guy and his chem 352 class was like 15x easier than the guy I took 351 from (Ess). I think I went to class like 5 times and didn't really even do the homework. Probably not the best for MCAT/DAT prep but it was a nice change of pace.

I don't get why people like this guy. Lectures were incomprehensible and your entire grade was only the tests. The only good thing was tests were similar to practice tests. First time I have ever gotten a B in a class despite working super hard. It's frustrating to know if there was just a 5-10% grade cushion, I would have gotten an A.

I've taken both 351 and 352 from Peterson, not by choice but because the department only offers his section very often. Peterson's grading is entirely based on test scores, don't expect to get more than a few percent from doing the homework "assignments". No online resources and incomprehensible lectures. Try to take from someone else.

Matt Peterson might be the greatest chemistry professor I've ever had. Very funny lectures, makes complicated concepts simple. I would recommend two things:1) Don't miss days. His lectures are great, but if you miss three in a row you WILL fall behind. 2) Really key in on the exams. Do the hw and practice exams. Your grade will thak you.

As a student who cares a lot about grades, this is the ochem class you should be in. All lectures are posted on YouTube, and he gives big hints and extra credit points in class. He is so kind and helpful and a very generous grader. definitely requires you to put in effort, but ending with above 100% is totally within reach. Dr. P is the best!!!!

His class was fine. Don't expect to learn much from his lectures. He goes on long, meaningless tangents. A handful of students just eventually stopped showing up to lectures and watched his YouTube videos that taught the concepts more thoroughly. . If you can get the concepts down in the context of the practice exams, you can do well on his tests.
It's 5 tests, but they're usually the exact same as the practice exams if not very similar. I would take OCHEM from him again, great class.

This was my second attempt at ochem 2 and it went a lot better. Dr Peterson is great! His lectures are clear and very useful and he tries to tailor the class towards pre-health tests (MCAT, DAT, GRE), which is very helpful. He loves to joke around and has lots of creative ways to remember concepts. I took this in the summer term and it was great.

His tests often included 1or 2 extra credit points or were graded about 128 possible/125. They were also very close to practice tests. For the parts that weren't the same as practice tests he heavily emphasized in class. His videos are very helpful as well as the textbook. It is very possible to do well if you put in the time. I highly recommend!

Dr. Peterson was truly my favorite chem professor I've had so far. He is super engaging and funny during lecture, although he does not always cover all the necessary material. As long as you are willing to do all the reading outside of class, you will be set. Offers multiple points of extra credit and gives great practice exams to use to study.

I can't say enough good things about Dr P and my experience taking this class! I was terrified of Ochem coming into the class, but he makes it possible to do well. Exams are very similar to practice exams. His recorded lecture videos are great. Textbook readings really help with understanding. funny guy. Please take this class from him!!

Dr. P was great. There are no surprises on exams and he gives you a practice exam to take before each exam to help prepare. You have to be self-motivated and do a lot of textbook reading and studying on your own, but if you put in the work, you will be successful.

Ochem is hard, and you will struggle. Prof P prepares you well for the exams and gives you lots of hints in lecture. He's not always the best at explaining concepts but he is hilarious. Enjoyed attending class. Read the textbook regularly. Five exams are the only thing graded. The practice tests are pretty much the same as the real exams.
Organic Chem with Dr. P is tough, but he sets you up for success. Focus on the exams, utilize the practice materials, and try unstuckstudy alongside other study tools - it really helps!

Dr Peterson is a great guy, but it was often really hard to follow him during lectures, so most of the time I learned the material from the textbook and my TA. There's some material that he just expects you to learn on your own too. The only grades in the class come from 5 exams, however they are incredibly similar to the available practice exams

He's taught this class for so long, he has it down to a tea. He's a good lecturer, lots of analogies, and teaches clearly so you can understand. Grade is 100% test, which puts responsibility on you, but it's a difficult class, he makes it enjoyable and doable. He preps you very well for each test, and knows the MCAT DAT and GRE well, super helpful.

I loved taking OChem from Dr. P! I was a little nervous that 97% of my grade would be the test, but he's very clear about what will and will not be on the exams and he prepares you well for them. It was nice that he didn't grade the homework, because then I could focus on the gaps in my knowledge. Yeah it's a tough class, but I would recommend him.

Organic Chemistry is a tough course but Dr. Peterson is a good, fair, and entertaining professor. There's a lot to know but he is very clear about what will be on the exams. Your entire grade is based on 4 exams and a final (NOT cumulative) so studying for these exams is crucial. He has practice exams that are almost identical to the real exams.

Like other reviews of the majors section have said, this is graded only by your exams - but I promise that's not a bad thing. He prepares you well for exams. If you use the resources he gives you well, you will do very well in this class. He is reasonable about what we need to memorize. He likes dad jokes :)

He gives us every resource you can imagine, and we know exactly what will be on the tests. You can tell that he really wants you to understand and excel in his class. Because we are not graded on homework, we can worry less about completing assignments about stuff we already know, so we can spend more time where we need it and enjoy the subject.

I took him for the majors section of O-Chem I. His tests are very memorization based, so if that works well with you, like it does with me, take it from him. I really enjoyed his lectures and enjoyed the class overall. It's purely graded by tests, so be wary of that.

Grading comes entirely from midterms and exams, so you need to be willing to devote a ton of time to teaching yourself the material before coming to lecture if you want to succeed. Dr. Peterson is one of the better professors to take the major section from, but you might as well take a non-major section where you get credit for homework.

This class was difficult, each test is 20 percent of your grade. He decided to teach the material in a different and confusing order, so we learned some of the ochem 2 material, and skipped some of the regular stuff. Tests are difficult, it is possible to pass if you use the practice tests and study early, but I would avoid. Lots of memorizing.
This class was an absolute beast. 97% of your grade come from exams and each exam takes a lot of prep. Start studying early enough and you'll be fine but it does take a lot to do well on them.

This class... This class is the hardest class I have ever taken. Yeah, there's office hours, yeah, there's TA hours, but Dr. Peterson focuses so much on teaching you tricks for the MCAT, DAT or GRE, that he neglects to teach you any actual OChem. expect to spend 30+ hrs a week studying to barely pass the tests that are 97% of your overall grade.

Dr. Peterson gives wonderful lectures. Hes funny and kind, and really wants to help students who want to learn. OCHEM is simply a tough class, no matter who you take it from. However, he gives you all the tools you need. Do the reading, do the optional homework, go to office hours, and do the practice exams and you will be sufficiently prepared.

Worst professor I've had at BYU. Very unhelpful and gives very vague answers to questions and emails. He'd change content last minute before exams making the organization of his class very confusing. He decided to not curve the class last second making a 95 an A. Upon reaching out about rounding up my 94.8, he was no help and extremely cold. Avoid.

Dr. P is a great professor! I thought his explanations were very thorough and really helped me to understand the concepts. After his class, I feel very prepared for the MCAT and I felt prepared prior to his tests. Watch out though--your entire grade is exams, and there are no re-dos or make-up points.

He's an ok good teacher, but he focuses on the nuances of the concepts he teaches and so it can be hard to understand exactly what he's trying to teach. The class is dang hard, but he is understanding and gives free extra credit for every test. He's not too personable and would not recommend taking this class if you want a Letter of recommendation.

I am just posting this to say I agree with what some other people on here said. He really cares, gives bonuses and regrades, and is a fun guy. Like another person said, the amount of time studying for this class to get a decent grade is way less than for other classes. A lot of the test questions are trick questions though. 5 to try and bring it up

His lectures take a long time, but I really enjoyed his personality. He is very different when you talk to him individually, and he is honestly not very supportive of students. Almost every question on every test was kind of a trick question, and his "hints" for the test were to study literally every concept.

If you are taking Ochem cause you think it'll be easy you will be blown out of the water. No professor can ever make it an easy subject, but I think he does as good as anybody could. I took 1 from Michaelis and 2 from dr P, and to study the amount I did to get B's on his tests I would've gotten at most D's on Michaelis' tests. This class is easier
Not a very kind or caring teacher. His online lectures too WAY longer than actual lecture classes. Not very approachable. Very much regret taking this class.

I took the 100% online class. I think he is a good teacher. He makes it possible to understand the basic concepts of Organic Chemistry. His tests are crazy hard but he gives us half credit for answers he thought were too hard. With an avg. test score under 60% I got a B- in the class. Go to office hours for hints. Also, tests are 95% of the grade.

This is the hardest class I have EVER taken. Got in late and never caught up, TONS of technical reading, only grades were tests, and tests were impossibly difficult (multiple choice w/ 4-7 answers). Before this I never got below an A-. Peterson does curve+some free points, but class still wrecked my GPA. Take w/ caution. (taken during Fall 2020)

Wow. I dont have much to say about this professor. Pretty awful teaching and does not respect anyone. You would be very unfortunate to have him as a professor. Does not explain anything correctly and then provide tests that are designed for you to get a low grade. Stay away if at all possible.

Taken during covid of Fall 2020. The only thing that goes on your grade are 4 tests. The averages on the tests were usually in the 50-60's but he did curve the class a lot. if you learn better from Pre-recorded lectures/ flexibility you'll like it. Lots of equations to memorize but it didn't seem as hard as everyone made ochem sound!
His tests are so different from any of his practice problems, it makes it very hard to prepare for. And if you fall behind you will not pass this class.

Dr. Peterson teaches a hard subject, but explains it very clearly and simply. Online classes needed a lot of self-motivation to do well, but he was very helpful in the problems he assigned. Grade was based off of just tests, but after each test he would go back and add in points for nearly-correct answers.

I took this class entirely online during COVID-19. Dr. Peterson had everything posted way ahead of time, and he was very specific about what we needed to know for the tests. The only tests I took were multiple choice because the testing center was closed, but they were very fair and based off of lecture material. I would definitely recommend!

Beyond dreadful professor. This is a tough course, you're going to need a mentor who makes it EASIER to learn unlike him. He prerecorded lectures (COVID) which ended up being WAY longer than if we had just had assigned class time. I would suggest using Khan Academy or any other Youtube chem videos if you want to make any progress in your learning

No matter what good things you read about him, he is the worst teacher i have had in all of my college career. He doesn't care about you, he isn't merciful when you are pleading for help, during covid i took him online while i was working and couldnt access TAs or other students for help, and he didn't respond to emails. WORST experience ever.

I enjoyed the ochem series. I personally thought that his free-response tests were not too hard. He gives you hints in class as to what will be on the test. His online tests after Covid-19 were hard, though. I would recommend taking him only in person. The grading is almost 100% tests, so if you get a D on one test, you're done. Solid choice.

Dr. P is a fair tester and generous grader. That being said, your grade is solely determined by your test scores (literally nothing else goes in the gradebook), so if you get A's on 4 of the 5 tests and a D on one like me, you don't have anything to balance the bad test score out. the transition to online was rough but not entirely his fault.

Go to class for the HINTS! OCHEM is a really hard class and Dr. Peterson made it a lot easier. I'm not sure why people are hating on him but I think he is one of the most caring ochem professors I have had. The online exams during COVID were hard tho. I'd suggest taking him in person if you can. I got lost on some of the online lectures.
