Dr. Peterson gets a bad rap because Ochem is difficult and students don't put in the necessary time to do well.  He is great, office hours are helpful for before and after exams.  Find a TA and have them help you through the sample exam. It's a different amount for each person, but if you put in the time you will do well. Straight from the book.

Peterson has been my favorite chemistry teacher. You have no homework but if you do  the problems you will be set for the tests. OChem is a class where the amount of time you put into it determines your grade. If you read the chapters you will be good and if you don't just look at the summaries. You need to go to class to get iclicker points.

Dr. Peterson is easy to approach and helpful during office hours. But plan on teaching yourself most everything from the book. Tests are killer. My TA said that some lectures are word the word the same from the semester he took the class -- right down to the jokes. Hes good though!

Dr. Peterson was an awful professor. Tests are the only grades in the class and he does not care how well you do on them. He is unable to help unless your situation fits on his scale as being "legitimate".  He sees his ego as being more important than your success. DO NOT take this class from him!!!!

This was the worst class I have taken at BYU. There are no other grades in the class besides 5 tests and some iClicker points.  He does not go over in lecture what he tests you on, and will not be there to help you when you are struggling, even when you are trying your best. DO NOT take this class from him, he does not want you to succeed.

Not a very good teacher. Just showed powerpoints I found to be useless and everything I learned was on my own. Almost always something wrong with the tests and he never gave points back. Overall rather confusing, I managed a reasonable grade but did way better in 352 which is much harder. take from someone else.

I never rate professors, but Peterson was bad enough that I need to let it be known. His lectures are rambling and unclear/unplanned, and his tests are insane. He has no compassion for students and only cares about his ego. His class has a 2.7 average GPA (I didn't make that up, I got that stat from the dean). DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM!

Dr. Peterson is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He himself admitted during class that he never really planned his lectures. He kind of just talks about whatever comes to mind. He doesn't prepare you for the tests and is a horrible grader. You have to find at least 2 grading errors on ur test or he won't regrade. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

Dr. P is a good professor. Lectures are less organized than some, but still understandable. Funny guy, which helps. Always available for questions. Grading policy is fair- offers regrades on each exam. Posts practice tests for each exam, sometimes are nearly identical on actual exam.  HW questions often show up verbatim on exams.

The only thing I didn't like about Dr. Peterson is his grading system. He grades in deciles, which means that the top 10% of the class gets an A in the test, the next 10% get an A-, and it goes down like that. So sometimes even if you get over a 93% on a test it won't be an A. But he explains the material well. Focuses on premeds often in lectures.

I don't know why everyone else has a problem with him.  I took organic chemistry from him and from another professor and preferred Peterson.  His tests are very straightforward and you will get a good grade if you study hard.  I also liked how he doesn't collect homework and I felt like I had more control of my learning that way.

Not a very good teacher at all, pretty inconsiderate of students and doesn't really care about helping you learn. Likes to just get through the material and get done with the agenda at the end of the day.

Best Ochem professor at byu! I know because I had all the other Ochem professors as substitutes during the semester. Ochem is hard no matter who you take it from but Peterson makes it interesting and tests fairly.

Dr. Peterson is the best teacher that BYU has to offer in the Ochem department.  I am a premed student who doesn't have a huge background in the subject, but he was able to make it interesting and made the tough work more bearable. Because he taught me in a way that was down to earth, I ACED the ACS exam.  Way better than everyone else!  TAKE HIM!

No matter who you take ochem from at BYU, it'll most likely be one of the hardest classes because of vast amount of material. I liked Peterson, his lectures kept me awake and I sometimes learned to appreciate organic chemistry. Go to class and read the book and you'll survive!
He's good. I liked him for Ochem

Dr. Peterson was the most helpful professor that I had at this University.  He is by far the fairest teacher in grading policy, and he taught in a way that kept me awake.  TAKE HIM.  You will learn OChem as long as you actually study (and yes, you should go to class, you will do better.)
He is a nice teacher, very helpful..

Everybody is hatin on Peterson, but I liked him.  Ochem is going to be hard no matter who you take it from.  Its true, he does waste large chunks of class time on weird tangents or jokes.  But 352 with him was WAY easier than 351 with Savage.

He is a genuinely nice guy, but not a good teacher. Wastes a lot of class time and just teaches from the slides. He makes your last test hard, even though the one before it is the ACS test, which tests all of your knowledge from 351 and 352. If you can take this class from another teacher, do it.

Stay away from Peterson.  It was such a joke of a class.  He doesn't deserve to be called a teacher because he never actually taught - just clicked through slide after slide of someone else's powerpoints.  What a joke.

Dr. Peterson expects his students to study like they actually want to learn about ochem.  A struggle for many, but I thought he was awesome.  There are 5 midterms, which I thought were better than 3, what others do, because of the enormity and detailed nature of the material.  Only 3 would make studying for just 1 near impossible. Pete's the best!!

He's a great guy, and pretty funny, but the subject is super heavy.  I never fully understood a couple concepts, but that's only because I didn't read the assigned reading before coming to class.  He assumes that everyone has read and teaches like that.  If you don't like that, don't take O-chem at BYU, at all.  They all teach that way.

He uses power points that are copied pages from the book. He mumbles at lot and can't explain the concepts very well. I love o-chem but wanted to kill myself in this class. I found it hard to stay awake during the lectures. The only reason why I went was for the extra practice he gave in class. Do the practice exams...it will help a lot.

All of your grade is based on your tests and no he doesn't drop your worst grade, so if you bomb a test (which is easy to do in this class)it's almost impossible to recover in this class. He is a decent teacher and will try his best to help you understand the material, but I personally feel the TA's were better at explaining difficult concepts.

Your grade is based entirely on your exam scores.  Your final grade is dependent on your class ranking (how you compare to other students). Wished we had buffer points with quizzes or hw.  Slides are just photocopies of the book. Take someone else.

Tests are hard and account for your entire grade (i.e. no hw or quizes). Lecture is useless, so I stopped going completely. Normally this is okay because he sticks to the syllabus. On one test, however, he deviated and switched a chapter. This destroyed my grade. So go to class right before the test. One redeeming quality is that he's pretty funny.

I thought Dr. Peterson was hilarious.  His corny jokes keep you paying attention.  He was reasonable and not on any type of power trip.  His tests vary in difficulty, but he changes the grading scale according to class averages. The class is hard, but this is OChem, it's just the nature of the beast, it has nothing to do with Dr. P.

Dr. Peterson makes organic chemistry entertaining. Teaches strictly what you need to know for his tests as well as for the MCAT or DAT. As long as you can learn from the book, attendence isn't mandatory in my opinion.

All tests are free response and the final MC. The grading was not really consistent on free response and the averages were all over the boards. It was very inconsistent in difficulty of questions / concepts tested etc. take it from someone else like Neilson.

He's not super exciting but his class is straightforward. No graded homework which is nice. He follows the book very closely. If you understand the reading there's really no point in going to lecture because he just repeats the book.

Dr. Peterson is very straight forward with his teaching and is not trying to trick you at all.  The tests come almost directly from his packet and the homework from the book. If you can memorize mechanisms this class is very manageable.

Well, I thought it was a decent class. I barely went and still got a good grade. This class was a cake walk compared with Flemming. I really loved Flemming, but it was nice not to have to go to class: Tips: do the homework, study the recitation packet, and read if you don't understand. Class wasn't all that useful or interesting.

I never went to class, just studied the lecture guide and did the homework for as many hours as i could in the two days before each test, bought the acs final review book and studied it for two days straight before the final and got an A. Its all memorization of reactions and mechanisms. He puts questions directly from the homework in the book!!!

This was a very hard class.  I took it summer term, which meant that Dr. P's 5 tests (and a midterm), came out to something like a test every week.  That being said, I enjoyed the class.  I was mostly frustrated because I got 92-94% on all the test except one (and the final), but he still gave me a B+.  95% is an A, which seems a bit extreme to me.

Understand his notes and you'll understand the book. Understand his notes thoroughly and you will get at least an 80 on the test. I found his teaching style rather simple and easy to understand. I gave him a 5 on easiness but I'm not one of those genius kids that gets A's (C in 351 and C- in 106). Great professor!

I got a bad grade. I bombed the first two tests. Got better and then on the final got a 76% on it. The class average was 67%. So in essence I progressively got better in the class, did well on the final and the most I could get was a d+? I went to talk to him about it, he wouldn't, said to e-mail him, I did and said that's what I got, tough. BEWARE
Don't take anyone else, his lecture notes make it so you don't have to take a single note all semester.  Very straight forward tester, and really a nice guy.  Best teacher I've had at BYU.

One of the best chemistry professors out there.  His class was very entertaining, and I learned so much.  His tests are free response and he is extremely friendly and approachable.  Such a great teacher, I would most definitely recommend him.

This is one of the best chemisty teachers that I'd ever had. He is by far the best O-Chem teacher. He knows what he is talking about and explains it in a manner where the studentes can uderstand. His tests are write on and some problems come from the homework. Very approachable, he even wrote me a letter of recommendation for med school. TAKE HIM.

He made a boring class more interesting by making jokes and applying chemistry to everyday life.  Yet, his multiple choice chemistry tests are frustrating and result in a lower grade than a written test.  It is hard to know what will be on his tests, because he sometimes pulls questions out of nowhere.
teaches well, tests hard but not imposible, not aproachable.
One of the better teachers I've had.  Very clear on what will be tested and what won't.  He made the best of a tough class.

He started off as a nice guy then he turned into a jerk the last few weeks of class.  I'll never know where that came from.  Kind of an interesting class.  I agree that he is not very approachable, but then again, what chemistry teacher is?

I liked this class. I thought he was very organized and outlined exactly what we needed to know for the tests. He's a funny guy too. However the course is tough and you'll have to study a lot to do well.
Lectures are supplement to the text. Like any class it is vital to read chapter before lecture. Sort of a nice guy, not your first choice for a professor though, but does a good enough job.

Ehhh... I took this class over again from another professor and I got an A(i loved it from this other prof)... so don't take it from Prof. Peterson. He doesn't explain the material at all and his tests don't coincide to his lectures.  Bad class.

Very good teacher.  If you like organization, he's the professor for you.  He is into detail and he is very clear about what will and will not be on the tests.  Tests are still hard, though.  Lots of studying for this class.  READ THE BOOK!!!  DO THE H/W!

I didn't understand the material at all in this class.  I thought I understood it until I got in to take the test and all of a sudden, everything he said in lecture had nothing to do with what was on the test.lectures are fun,but he's not easy to approach
Very nice guy. His lectures were very clear, but his test are extremely hard.

He is a generally nice guy, his lectures are basically reading through the powerpoint slides he gives you.  His tests are fair and best of all the final isn't comprehensive.  Overall a good teacher, but don't ask for a letter of recomendation-apathetic
Wasn't nice to me, made me cry.
Sometimes can be confusing, but over all pretty good.
No Comments
Good O Chem teacher

He REFUSES feedback on grades.

It was simultaneously a Latin American History class, a Research Skills class, and a Lecture Series. There was a TON of homework and little assignments. The worst class I have ever taken- this professor made it so hard. The beginning of the semester was so homework and reading heavy and on top of that we had the most tedious "scavenger hunts." Matt is great! Very personable and respectful. He goes through things quickly so I recommend learning Excel on your own.
His TA was absolutely awful. The worst. Beware..... They grade you on things that are not on the rubric. And when you ask the TA to explain, they have no real answer for you. Play the mind games and you will be fine.

MBA 555 is a waste of time. We learned virtually nothing throughout the semester then had an incredibly specific final exam that a lot of people did not do well on. I found most of the assignments useless and wish we would have spent more time on actual marketing practices such as segmentation instead of stress management. Project is cool though.

Matt is a great professor and such a chill guy. His class is probably the easiest of the core because it requires a lot less reading and the group project has more spread-out deadlines, which makes it feel more manageable. Be sure to pay attention in class!! The class material is not the most engaging, but Matt really tries to make it interesting.

He is great but I felt that he taught all the concepts very fast. It was hard to follow along with excel and other concepts. I wished he could have spent more time explaining how to analyze concepts as well.
Matt is great. He makes the concepts easy to understand and uses his expertise in market research to give real life examples in class.

Matt is a nice guy for sure! But this class was pretty boring. It felt like most of what you learn in the class could be summed up in about an hour. But the class moves very slowly through research methods that are just pretty intuitive and that we have been using for years through high school.

I had Matt for both Marketing Research and Consulting, and he does an awesome job of taking his career and consulting experiences and making them applicable to you. His powerpoints are super helpful, and all of the work is aimed to give you meaningful experience. Grades are kind of ambiguous, but if you pay attention and do the work you'll be fine.

His lectures are good, but he always gets very behind in his teaching schedule, sometimes missing entire chapters that are on the exams, so there's a lot you have to review by yourself. But he has youtube lectures and good practice exams

I've taken Dr. P for chem 351 and 352. He is a good teacher but what saved my bacon in this class was his voice overs. His voice overs differ slightly than what he teaches in class, but I would watch his voice overs and condense those notes and cross verifed them with what he taught in class and studied those notes and did very well in the class

I've taken Dr. P for chem 351 and 352. He is a good teacher but what saved my bacon in this class was his voice overs. His voice overs differ slightly than what he teaches in class, but I would watch his voice overs and condense those notes and cross verifed them with what he taught in class and studied those notes and did very well in the class.

Dr. Peterson is a nice guy and his chem 352 class was like 15x easier than the guy I took 351 from (Ess). I think I went to class like 5 times and didn't really even do the homework. Probably not the best for MCAT/DAT prep but it was a nice change of pace.

I don't get why people like this guy. Lectures were incomprehensible and your entire grade was only the tests. The only good thing was tests were similar to practice tests. First time I have ever gotten a B in a class despite working super hard. It's frustrating to know if there was just a 5-10% grade cushion, I would have gotten an A.

I've taken both 351 and 352 from Peterson, not by choice but because the department only offers his section very often. Peterson's grading is entirely based on test scores, don't expect to get more than a few percent from doing the homework "assignments". No online resources and incomprehensible lectures. Try to take from someone else.

Matt Peterson might be the greatest chemistry professor I've ever had. Very funny lectures, makes complicated concepts simple. I would recommend two things:1) Don't miss days. His lectures are great, but if you miss three in a row you WILL fall behind. 2) Really key in on the exams. Do the hw and practice exams. Your grade will thak you.

As a student who cares a lot about grades, this is the ochem class you should be in. All lectures are posted on YouTube, and he gives big hints and extra credit points in class. He is so kind and helpful and a very generous grader. definitely requires you to put in effort, but ending with above 100% is totally within reach. Dr. P is the best!!!!

His class was fine. Don't expect to learn much from his lectures. He goes on long, meaningless tangents. A handful of students just eventually stopped showing up to lectures and watched his YouTube videos that taught the concepts more thoroughly. . If you can get the concepts down in the context of the practice exams, you can do well on his tests.
It's 5 tests, but they're usually the exact same as the practice exams if not very similar. I would take OCHEM from him again, great class.

This was my second attempt at ochem 2 and it went a lot better. Dr Peterson is great! His lectures are clear and very useful and he tries to tailor the class towards pre-health tests (MCAT, DAT, GRE), which is very helpful. He loves to joke around and has lots of creative ways to remember concepts. I took this in the summer term and it was great.

His tests often included 1or 2 extra credit points or were graded about 128 possible/125. They were also very close to practice tests. For the parts that weren't the same as practice tests he heavily emphasized in class. His videos are very helpful as well as the textbook. It is very possible to do well if you put in the time. I highly recommend!

Dr. Peterson was truly my favorite chem professor I've had so far. He is super engaging and funny during lecture, although he does not always cover all the necessary material. As long as you are willing to do all the reading outside of class, you will be set. Offers multiple points of extra credit and gives great practice exams to use to study.

I can't say enough good things about Dr P and my experience taking this class! I was terrified of Ochem coming into the class, but he makes it possible to do well. Exams are very similar to practice exams. His recorded lecture videos are great. Textbook readings really help with understanding. funny guy. Please take this class from him!!

Dr. P was great. There are no surprises on exams and he gives you a practice exam to take before each exam to help prepare. You have to be self-motivated and do a lot of textbook reading and studying on your own, but if you put in the work, you will be successful.

Ochem is hard, and you will struggle. Prof P prepares you well for the exams and gives you lots of hints in lecture. He's not always the best at explaining concepts but he is hilarious. Enjoyed attending class. Read the textbook regularly. Five exams are the only thing graded. The practice tests are pretty much the same as the real exams.
Organic Chem with Dr. P is tough, but he sets you up for success. Focus on the exams, utilize the practice materials, and try unstuckstudy alongside other study tools - it really helps!

Dr Peterson is a great guy, but it was often really hard to follow him during lectures, so most of the time I learned the material from the textbook and my TA. There's some material that he just expects you to learn on your own too. The only grades in the class come from 5 exams, however they are incredibly similar to the available practice exams

He's taught this class for so long, he has it down to a tea. He's a good lecturer, lots of analogies, and teaches clearly so you can understand. Grade is 100% test, which puts responsibility on you, but it's a difficult class, he makes it enjoyable and doable. He preps you very well for each test, and knows the MCAT DAT and GRE well, super helpful.

I loved taking OChem from Dr. P! I was a little nervous that 97% of my grade would be the test, but he's very clear about what will and will not be on the exams and he prepares you well for them. It was nice that he didn't grade the homework, because then I could focus on the gaps in my knowledge. Yeah it's a tough class, but I would recommend him.

Organic Chemistry is a tough course but Dr. Peterson is a good, fair, and entertaining professor. There's a lot to know but he is very clear about what will be on the exams. Your entire grade is based on 4 exams and a final (NOT cumulative) so studying for these exams is crucial. He has practice exams that are almost identical to the real exams.

Like other reviews of the majors section have said, this is graded only by your exams - but I promise that's not a bad thing. He prepares you well for exams. If you use the resources he gives you well, you will do very well in this class. He is reasonable about what we need to memorize. He likes dad jokes :)

He gives us every resource you can imagine, and we know exactly what will be on the tests. You can tell that he really wants you to understand and excel in his class. Because we are not graded on homework, we can worry less about completing assignments about stuff we already know, so we can spend more time where we need it and enjoy the subject.

I took him for the majors section of O-Chem I. His tests are very memorization based, so if that works well with you, like it does with me, take it from him. I really enjoyed his lectures and enjoyed the class overall. It's purely graded by tests, so be wary of that.

Grading comes entirely from midterms and exams, so you need to be willing to devote a ton of time to teaching yourself the material before coming to lecture if you want to succeed. Dr. Peterson is one of the better professors to take the major section from, but you might as well take a non-major section where you get credit for homework.

This class was difficult, each test is 20 percent of your grade. He decided to teach the material in a different and confusing order, so we learned some of the ochem 2 material, and skipped some of the regular stuff. Tests are difficult, it is possible to pass if you use the practice tests and study early, but I would avoid. Lots of memorizing.
This class was an absolute beast. 97% of your grade come from exams and each exam takes a lot of prep. Start studying early enough and you'll be fine but it does take a lot to do well on them.

This class... This class is the hardest class I have ever taken. Yeah, there's office hours, yeah, there's TA hours, but Dr. Peterson focuses so much on teaching you tricks for the MCAT, DAT or GRE, that he neglects to teach you any actual OChem. expect to spend 30+ hrs a week studying to barely pass the tests that are 97% of your overall grade.

Dr. Peterson gives wonderful lectures. Hes funny and kind, and really wants to help students who want to learn. OCHEM is simply a tough class, no matter who you take it from. However, he gives you all the tools you need. Do the reading, do the optional homework, go to office hours, and do the practice exams and you will be sufficiently prepared.

Worst professor I've had at BYU. Very unhelpful and gives very vague answers to questions and emails. He'd change content last minute before exams making the organization of his class very confusing. He decided to not curve the class last second making a 95 an A. Upon reaching out about rounding up my 94.8, he was no help and extremely cold. Avoid.

Dr. P is a great professor! I thought his explanations were very thorough and really helped me to understand the concepts. After his class, I feel very prepared for the MCAT and I felt prepared prior to his tests. Watch out though--your entire grade is exams, and there are no re-dos or make-up points.

He's an ok good teacher, but he focuses on the nuances of the concepts he teaches and so it can be hard to understand exactly what he's trying to teach. The class is dang hard, but he is understanding and gives free extra credit for every test. He's not too personable and would not recommend taking this class if you want a Letter of recommendation.

I am just posting this to say I agree with what some other people on here said. He really cares, gives bonuses and regrades, and is a fun guy. Like another person said, the amount of time studying for this class to get a decent grade is way less than for other classes. A lot of the test questions are trick questions though. 5 to try and bring it up

His lectures take a long time, but I really enjoyed his personality. He is very different when you talk to him individually, and he is honestly not very supportive of students. Almost every question on every test was kind of a trick question, and his "hints" for the test were to study literally every concept.

If you are taking Ochem cause you think it'll be easy you will be blown out of the water. No professor can ever make it an easy subject, but I think he does as good as anybody could. I took 1 from Michaelis and 2 from dr P, and to study the amount I did to get B's on his tests I would've gotten at most D's on Michaelis' tests. This class is easier
Not a very kind or caring teacher. His online lectures too WAY longer than actual lecture classes. Not very approachable. Very much regret taking this class.

I took the 100% online class. I think he is a good teacher. He makes it possible to understand the basic concepts of Organic Chemistry. His tests are crazy hard but he gives us half credit for answers he thought were too hard. With an avg. test score under 60% I got a B- in the class. Go to office hours for hints. Also, tests are 95% of the grade.

This is the hardest class I have EVER taken. Got in late and never caught up, TONS of technical reading, only grades were tests, and tests were impossibly difficult (multiple choice w/ 4-7 answers). Before this I never got below an A-. Peterson does curve+some free points, but class still wrecked my GPA. Take w/ caution. (taken during Fall 2020)

Wow. I dont have much to say about this professor. Pretty awful teaching and does not respect anyone. You would be very unfortunate to have him as a professor. Does not explain anything correctly and then provide tests that are designed for you to get a low grade. Stay away if at all possible.

Taken during covid of Fall 2020. The only thing that goes on your grade are 4 tests. The averages on the tests were usually in the 50-60's but he did curve the class a lot. if you learn better from Pre-recorded lectures/ flexibility you'll like it. Lots of equations to memorize but it didn't seem as hard as everyone made ochem sound!
His tests are so different from any of his practice problems, it makes it very hard to prepare for. And if you fall behind you will not pass this class.

Dr. Peterson teaches a hard subject, but explains it very clearly and simply. Online classes needed a lot of self-motivation to do well, but he was very helpful in the problems he assigned. Grade was based off of just tests, but after each test he would go back and add in points for nearly-correct answers.

I took this class entirely online during COVID-19. Dr. Peterson had everything posted way ahead of time, and he was very specific about what we needed to know for the tests. The only tests I took were multiple choice because the testing center was closed, but they were very fair and based off of lecture material. I would definitely recommend!

Beyond dreadful professor. This is a tough course, you're going to need a mentor who makes it EASIER to learn unlike him. He prerecorded lectures (COVID) which ended up being WAY longer than if we had just had assigned class time. I would suggest using Khan Academy or any other Youtube chem videos if you want to make any progress in your learning

No matter what good things you read about him, he is the worst teacher i have had in all of my college career. He doesn't care about you, he isn't merciful when you are pleading for help, during covid i took him online while i was working and couldnt access TAs or other students for help, and he didn't respond to emails. WORST experience ever.

I enjoyed the ochem series. I personally thought that his free-response tests were not too hard. He gives you hints in class as to what will be on the test. His online tests after Covid-19 were hard, though. I would recommend taking him only in person. The grading is almost 100% tests, so if you get a D on one test, you're done. Solid choice.

Dr. P is a fair tester and generous grader. That being said, your grade is solely determined by your test scores (literally nothing else goes in the gradebook), so if you get A's on 4 of the 5 tests and a D on one like me, you don't have anything to balance the bad test score out. the transition to online was rough but not entirely his fault.

Go to class for the HINTS! OCHEM is a really hard class and Dr. Peterson made it a lot easier. I'm not sure why people are hating on him but I think he is one of the most caring ochem professors I have had. The online exams during COVID were hard tho. I'd suggest taking him in person if you can. I got lost on some of the online lectures.

I really love Dr. Peterson, he is a kind, funny, and smart man. His free response exams were very straight forward and he would give you hints on what to study. After corona hit, his MC exams were really hard and only had a 2 hour time limit. Overall I really enjoyed him and he ended up giving us a nice curve at the end of the semester.

Dr. Peterson is a solid professor for 352. He gives lots of hints as to how to prepare for tests. Free response tests were pretty fair, but the online MC tests after the COVID-19 pandemic started were much harder. OChem is a difficult class in general but Dr. Peterson teaches it well, loves the subject, and wants students to succeed.

Dr. Peterson is the worst teacher I could have taken Ochem 2 from. After COVID, he put an extremely short time limit on exams and many I talked to had to guess because they ran out of time. He is very disorganized and tests significantly on random facts rather just focusing on fundamentals. By the end, I was at a loss for how I could have done well

Dr. Peterson is a great professor and a very kind professor which isn't typical of most science professors. He really cares and wants to give as many hints on what is important for you to know as a chemist in the future or for future grad school exams. For us his tests were free response and worth your grade. Homework is not for credit.

I'm not sure how he is as a chemistry professor but his religion class was absolutely awful. He is so slow he didn't cover even a third of the course material but still tested on it. His lectures were awful and super boring and had no useful information. The tests were completely unrelated to anything spiritual and took me over two hours each.

Definitely the easiest choice as far as O chem professors. With Dr. Peterson I got an even better grade than in gen chem. Very straight forward about what is and isn't on the test. The homeword isn't graded but was super helpful.

Dr. P is a great choice for OChem 351. He tries hard to teach in an understandable way instead of textbook language like most professors. He is approachable. Your grade is just iclicker and tests. I've taken ochem before with a different professor and withdrew, and Dr. P made the experience way better. Tests are hard but thats Ochem for you.

I was really nervous going into OCHEM, but I made the correct choice in choosing to take it from Dr. Peterson! He is a good professor, and he really cares about his students and their success. He is constantly giving us hints ( "this'll for sure be on the test"), and really knows his stuff. He has a good sense of humor as well.

Once you accept that OChem is going to take much more effort than your average 3 credit class it's great! Dr. P is hilarious, loves OChem, loves Monopoly references (and many other references), and loves to give Christmas presents to students, i e tells you specific things that will and will not be on tests. Took 351 & 352 from him, dont regret it!

I took both part 1 and 2 from Dr. P. Organic chemistry is tough. You need to put in the time. Read the book and do the assigned problems and you should be fine. COME TO CLASS. He gives so many hints for the test. He's such a nice and funny guy, and I think he teaches really well. He's very accessible outside of class. Loved this class and Dr. P!
OChem is naturally a difficult subject, but I think Dr. Peterson is the best person to take this class from at BYU. His tests are based heavily on what he says and emphasizes during lectures.

Very nice guy, but awful teacher. Hardest class I've taken at BYU by far. Grades are based completely on tests and tests are very hard. I studied 30 hours for a test and got a 62. I ended up withdrawing from the class as to not get a C. I would recommend looking for another professor for Ochem 2!

2 stars because his tests were unnecessarily long and hard. His exams were 50 problems, all multiple-choice. I'm a slow test taker, but his tests took slow to a whole different level. I took 8 hours on one of his midterms. If you study really hard and know your stuff you won't take so long but it's not worth it if you can take from someone else.

Ochem is just a hard class, no getting around it. The tests were really tricky. Dr. P is there to help! The textbook is your best friend. Focus on what he emphasizes in lectures and work hard. His grading system helps you out at the end.

OCHEM is hard but Dr. P doesn't make trick questions or anything on the test. You just have to pay attention in class, study the hw problems like crazy from the book, and you will do okay on the tests. Plus, he does a grade curve at the end of the semester, where top 10% grades get an A, second top 10% gets A-, 3rd top 10% B+, and so forth

Dr. Peterson knows this class is hard and expects you to put in a lot of work, and a lot of time outside of class to succeed. I love that he doesn't get carried away in obscure, difficult material - he makes most content understandable. Study his PowerPoints before class if possible and make flash cards. Generous grading system.

Ochem is tough, however dr P made it enjoyable. He's very helpful during his office hours. Also love how he teaches eternal concepts of why chemistry is important :) His tests were multiple choice-- except for the final. Non- comprehensive final which was nice. Do the practice problems in the book and pay attention to what he emphasizes in class
Great teacher who knows the material and expects you to know the same. His tests are tricky so be careful with them but if you study and prepare for his exams then you should do well in the class!
Dr. Peterson really cares that people do well. The dectile system he uses can only help you. Work hard, do the homework, and you should do OK. The material is tough, but he is a very fair teacher.

His lectures are pretty clear and enjoyable, but he often spends too much time on easy topics and not enough time on tougher ones, but the book covers those areas. The book is your best friend. His tests are reasonable; just put in the time and do the homework problems (even though he doesn't collect the homework), and you should do fine.

I honestly don't understand all the bad ratings for Dr. P. He has by far been one of my favorite professors at BYU. He takes a class that has a rep for being a nightmare and breaks it down into something that seems completely doable - and it was. He is pretty clear-cut on what he will test you on. Put in the time, and you'll do fine! HILARIOUS too!

Dr. Peterson gets a bad rap because Ochem is difficult and students don't put in the necessary time to do well.  He is great, office hours are helpful for before and after exams.  Find a TA and have them help you through the sample exam. It's a different amount for each person, but if you put in the time you will do well. Straight from the book.

Peterson has been my favorite chemistry teacher. You have no homework but if you do  the problems you will be set for the tests. OChem is a class where the amount of time you put into it determines your grade. If you read the chapters you will be good and if you don't just look at the summaries. You need to go to class to get iclicker points.

Dr. Peterson is easy to approach and helpful during office hours. But plan on teaching yourself most everything from the book. Tests are killer. My TA said that some lectures are word the word the same from the semester he took the class -- right down to the jokes. Hes good though!

Dr. Peterson was an awful professor. Tests are the only grades in the class and he does not care how well you do on them. He is unable to help unless your situation fits on his scale as being "legitimate".  He sees his ego as being more important than your success. DO NOT take this class from him!!!!

This was the worst class I have taken at BYU. There are no other grades in the class besides 5 tests and some iClicker points.  He does not go over in lecture what he tests you on, and will not be there to help you when you are struggling, even when you are trying your best. DO NOT take this class from him, he does not want you to succeed.

Not a very good teacher. Just showed powerpoints I found to be useless and everything I learned was on my own. Almost always something wrong with the tests and he never gave points back. Overall rather confusing, I managed a reasonable grade but did way better in 352 which is much harder. take from someone else.

I never rate professors, but Peterson was bad enough that I need to let it be known. His lectures are rambling and unclear/unplanned, and his tests are insane. He has no compassion for students and only cares about his ego. His class has a 2.7 average GPA (I didn't make that up, I got that stat from the dean). DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM!

Dr. Peterson is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He himself admitted during class that he never really planned his lectures. He kind of just talks about whatever comes to mind. He doesn't prepare you for the tests and is a horrible grader. You have to find at least 2 grading errors on ur test or he won't regrade. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

Dr. P is a good professor. Lectures are less organized than some, but still understandable. Funny guy, which helps. Always available for questions. Grading policy is fair- offers regrades on each exam. Posts practice tests for each exam, sometimes are nearly identical on actual exam.  HW questions often show up verbatim on exams.

The only thing I didn't like about Dr. Peterson is his grading system. He grades in deciles, which means that the top 10% of the class gets an A in the test, the next 10% get an A-, and it goes down like that. So sometimes even if you get over a 93% on a test it won't be an A. But he explains the material well. Focuses on premeds often in lectures.

I don't know why everyone else has a problem with him.  I took organic chemistry from him and from another professor and preferred Peterson.  His tests are very straightforward and you will get a good grade if you study hard.  I also liked how he doesn't collect homework and I felt like I had more control of my learning that way.

Not a very good teacher at all, pretty inconsiderate of students and doesn't really care about helping you learn. Likes to just get through the material and get done with the agenda at the end of the day.

Best Ochem professor at byu! I know because I had all the other Ochem professors as substitutes during the semester. Ochem is hard no matter who you take it from but Peterson makes it interesting and tests fairly.

Dr. Peterson is the best teacher that BYU has to offer in the Ochem department.  I am a premed student who doesn't have a huge background in the subject, but he was able to make it interesting and made the tough work more bearable. Because he taught me in a way that was down to earth, I ACED the ACS exam.  Way better than everyone else!  TAKE HIM!

No matter who you take ochem from at BYU, it'll most likely be one of the hardest classes because of vast amount of material. I liked Peterson, his lectures kept me awake and I sometimes learned to appreciate organic chemistry. Go to class and read the book and you'll survive!
He's good. I liked him for Ochem

Dr. Peterson was the most helpful professor that I had at this University.  He is by far the fairest teacher in grading policy, and he taught in a way that kept me awake.  TAKE HIM.  You will learn OChem as long as you actually study (and yes, you should go to class, you will do better.)
He is a nice teacher, very helpful..

Everybody is hatin on Peterson, but I liked him.  Ochem is going to be hard no matter who you take it from.  Its true, he does waste large chunks of class time on weird tangents or jokes.  But 352 with him was WAY easier than 351 with Savage.

He is a genuinely nice guy, but not a good teacher. Wastes a lot of class time and just teaches from the slides. He makes your last test hard, even though the one before it is the ACS test, which tests all of your knowledge from 351 and 352. If you can take this class from another teacher, do it.

Stay away from Peterson.  It was such a joke of a class.  He doesn't deserve to be called a teacher because he never actually taught - just clicked through slide after slide of someone else's powerpoints.  What a joke.

Dr. Peterson expects his students to study like they actually want to learn about ochem.  A struggle for many, but I thought he was awesome.  There are 5 midterms, which I thought were better than 3, what others do, because of the enormity and detailed nature of the material.  Only 3 would make studying for just 1 near impossible. Pete's the best!!

He's a great guy, and pretty funny, but the subject is super heavy.  I never fully understood a couple concepts, but that's only because I didn't read the assigned reading before coming to class.  He assumes that everyone has read and teaches like that.  If you don't like that, don't take O-chem at BYU, at all.  They all teach that way.

He uses power points that are copied pages from the book. He mumbles at lot and can't explain the concepts very well. I love o-chem but wanted to kill myself in this class. I found it hard to stay awake during the lectures. The only reason why I went was for the extra practice he gave in class. Do the practice exams...it will help a lot.

All of your grade is based on your tests and no he doesn't drop your worst grade, so if you bomb a test (which is easy to do in this class)it's almost impossible to recover in this class. He is a decent teacher and will try his best to help you understand the material, but I personally feel the TA's were better at explaining difficult concepts.

Your grade is based entirely on your exam scores.  Your final grade is dependent on your class ranking (how you compare to other students). Wished we had buffer points with quizzes or hw.  Slides are just photocopies of the book. Take someone else.

Tests are hard and account for your entire grade (i.e. no hw or quizes). Lecture is useless, so I stopped going completely. Normally this is okay because he sticks to the syllabus. On one test, however, he deviated and switched a chapter. This destroyed my grade. So go to class right before the test. One redeeming quality is that he's pretty funny.

I thought Dr. Peterson was hilarious.  His corny jokes keep you paying attention.  He was reasonable and not on any type of power trip.  His tests vary in difficulty, but he changes the grading scale according to class averages. The class is hard, but this is OChem, it's just the nature of the beast, it has nothing to do with Dr. P.

Dr. Peterson makes organic chemistry entertaining. Teaches strictly what you need to know for his tests as well as for the MCAT or DAT. As long as you can learn from the book, attendence isn't mandatory in my opinion.

All tests are free response and the final MC. The grading was not really consistent on free response and the averages were all over the boards. It was very inconsistent in difficulty of questions / concepts tested etc. take it from someone else like Neilson.

He's not super exciting but his class is straightforward. No graded homework which is nice. He follows the book very closely. If you understand the reading there's really no point in going to lecture because he just repeats the book.

Dr. Peterson is very straight forward with his teaching and is not trying to trick you at all.  The tests come almost directly from his packet and the homework from the book. If you can memorize mechanisms this class is very manageable.

Well, I thought it was a decent class. I barely went and still got a good grade. This class was a cake walk compared with Flemming. I really loved Flemming, but it was nice not to have to go to class: Tips: do the homework, study the recitation packet, and read if you don't understand. Class wasn't all that useful or interesting.

I never went to class, just studied the lecture guide and did the homework for as many hours as i could in the two days before each test, bought the acs final review book and studied it for two days straight before the final and got an A. Its all memorization of reactions and mechanisms. He puts questions directly from the homework in the book!!!

This was a very hard class.  I took it summer term, which meant that Dr. P's 5 tests (and a midterm), came out to something like a test every week.  That being said, I enjoyed the class.  I was mostly frustrated because I got 92-94% on all the test except one (and the final), but he still gave me a B+.  95% is an A, which seems a bit extreme to me.

Understand his notes and you'll understand the book. Understand his notes thoroughly and you will get at least an 80 on the test. I found his teaching style rather simple and easy to understand. I gave him a 5 on easiness but I'm not one of those genius kids that gets A's (C in 351 and C- in 106). Great professor!

I got a bad grade. I bombed the first two tests. Got better and then on the final got a 76% on it. The class average was 67%. So in essence I progressively got better in the class, did well on the final and the most I could get was a d+? I went to talk to him about it, he wouldn't, said to e-mail him, I did and said that's what I got, tough. BEWARE
Don't take anyone else, his lecture notes make it so you don't have to take a single note all semester.  Very straight forward tester, and really a nice guy.  Best teacher I've had at BYU.

One of the best chemistry professors out there.  His class was very entertaining, and I learned so much.  His tests are free response and he is extremely friendly and approachable.  Such a great teacher, I would most definitely recommend him.

This is one of the best chemisty teachers that I'd ever had. He is by far the best O-Chem teacher. He knows what he is talking about and explains it in a manner where the studentes can uderstand. His tests are write on and some problems come from the homework. Very approachable, he even wrote me a letter of recommendation for med school. TAKE HIM.

He made a boring class more interesting by making jokes and applying chemistry to everyday life.  Yet, his multiple choice chemistry tests are frustrating and result in a lower grade than a written test.  It is hard to know what will be on his tests, because he sometimes pulls questions out of nowhere.
teaches well, tests hard but not imposible, not aproachable.
One of the better teachers I've had.  Very clear on what will be tested and what won't.  He made the best of a tough class.

He started off as a nice guy then he turned into a jerk the last few weeks of class.  I'll never know where that came from.  Kind of an interesting class.  I agree that he is not very approachable, but then again, what chemistry teacher is?

I liked this class. I thought he was very organized and outlined exactly what we needed to know for the tests. He's a funny guy too. However the course is tough and you'll have to study a lot to do well.
Lectures are supplement to the text. Like any class it is vital to read chapter before lecture. Sort of a nice guy, not your first choice for a professor though, but does a good enough job.

Ehhh... I took this class over again from another professor and I got an A(i loved it from this other prof)... so don't take it from Prof. Peterson. He doesn't explain the material at all and his tests don't coincide to his lectures.  Bad class.

Very good teacher.  If you like organization, he's the professor for you.  He is into detail and he is very clear about what will and will not be on the tests.  Tests are still hard, though.  Lots of studying for this class.  READ THE BOOK!!!  DO THE H/W!

I didn't understand the material at all in this class.  I thought I understood it until I got in to take the test and all of a sudden, everything he said in lecture had nothing to do with what was on the test.lectures are fun,but he's not easy to approach
Very nice guy. His lectures were very clear, but his test are extremely hard.

He is a generally nice guy, his lectures are basically reading through the powerpoint slides he gives you.  His tests are fair and best of all the final isn't comprehensive.  Overall a good teacher, but don't ask for a letter of recomendation-apathetic
Wasn't nice to me, made me cry.
Sometimes can be confusing, but over all pretty good.
No Comments
Good O Chem teacher

He would assign assignments based on how many kids were in class, so if you weren't there, you would miss out. Even if you complete assignments according to the instructions, he doesn't give full credit.

Brother Wheelwright is my favorite teacher at BYU. He is always looking for ways to revolutionize his teaching and grading methods. Although his class is slightly more challenging, it is manageable because of his exceptional organization and you wont learn more from any other teacher. No bias, you can trust this review.
Great professor who cares about his students! Has a big group project in place of a final exam. Highly recommend!

Wheelwright is awesome. He cares a LOT and I appreciated that he talked about spiritual aspects as well as scheduling. I learned SO much. I recommend taking this class at the same time or after 311 (estimating) bc you will cover similar content. The semester-long portfolio project is easy to accomplish with milestones and lots of feedback.

You can tell that Bro Wheelwright really cares about you and is passionate about teaching & construction. He's very good at directing discussions. He's very helpful when you talk with him one-on-one to answer your questions and give you guidance (in class and life). He clears up confusion very well. No late work but he'll work with you to help you.
Bird course, you only need a 70 overall for credit.

Chem 201 is literally just a 7-week program on Lab Safety. You do lectures once a week, complete an open-resource assignment, and then take a final that is also open-note. But the lectures are chill and you get to practice using a fire extinguisher, which is awesome!

Only 7 weeks and you only have to go 7 times. Class was very straightforward. Was lecture heavy but had some fun demos. If you pay attention and go to class it's an easy pass. Tests / HW is open lecture notes so there's no pressure.

Great guy! He understands that it's just a lab safety course for majors/minors so it's very low key. Everything is open note. You get to use a fire extinguisher at the end of the term so you can always look forward to that!

Professor Allen is very kind and clearly cares for his students. He makes lectures fun with his personality and makes you want to learn. There is one assignment for each lecture (one every week) and one midterm and one final. They're all open-note and you can retake all of the weekly assignments. Overall just really great and easy.

He's super understanding and willing to work with you if you need to miss a lecture, there's only like 6 classes though so try to go every time (part of your grade is attendance). Tells lots of good stories, super chill class. Also, it's only a term, so if you take it during fall or winter it'll only be half of the semester.
It's a pass/fail class and fairly easy. Grading is based on quizzes and attendance. We were allowed to use the lecture slides while taking the tests, so it was very stress-free.

Matt is a humorous guy and you'll enjoy 201. It's a pass/fail class-- like driver's ed for chem. Showing up for lecture is part of your grade, so be sure to go. All of your quizzes and tests are online, and you can use the PowerPoints and google to complete them all. It's not too hard to pass unless you literally do nothing.
Professor Allen does his best to make the class an easy pass. If you show up for lectures, and do your online quizzes (which are open-book open-note open-internet), then you're bound to pass.
He's Awesome

This is a tough class, don't get me wrong. But Dr. Asplund is great at teaching the tough material in a way that is manageable. I would recommend him over pretty much any other chem professor I've taken classes from.

This class kind of depends on your TA. You don't ever see the professor. The tests are most of your grade and they don't prepare you super well for them. However, do your best to study and watch the TA reviews because those are helpful. It's also a lot of work for a one credit class. It's mainly a class to just get through, but also do-able.
Loved my TAs. Who is Asplund? Couldn't tell ya.

I took Chem 107 and honestly didn't know he was the professor over the class, it's mostly TA led. Chem 107 is very outdated, I don't think the class has been reorganized for years. We mostly have to teach ourselves things outside of class since we don't really have a lecture, and the tests are pretty difficult.

CHEM 105 is not an easy class, and he definitely taught me well enough, but I learned more from my TA than from Aslpund. Lectures were easy enough to follow, and he always blew something up on Fridays. Talking with students in other classes, their classes had higher grade averages than ours, but oh well. Stay on top of your work, and youll be fine.

I never saw this professor. The class is all based on material he did not write. TA's run your class & the bar to be a TA seems quite low. The pre labs and lab reports are super confusing. The disorganization, lack of explanation and guidance make this a rough one. Watch Raymond's reviews for exams and review your lab manual and you'll do good.

I could not dislike a class more, extremely test heavy, average test scores were in mid 70's. Depends on your TA but they don't help you when your confused and they are the most nit-picky graders. Class makes you feel like you can't do anything right, kills the joy in participating in a lab. Chem 106 was easier. Skip if possible. 3 credit class min

New concepts but if you start the homework early in the week and read the textbook before class you'll be fine. Similar to an extremely advanced chem 111 (broad spectrum of concepts). Dr Asplund is super technology savvy and has extremely organized slide lectures that go along exactly with the book. I put in about 2 hours a week and ended up fine.

Dr. Asplund is very knowledgeable about Physical Chemistry. His lectures are sometimes difficult to follow but if you come to class having done the reading they are not too bad. The textbook is very helpful. Tests are very reasonable.
Hated this class. So poorly structured. Tests are so hard and they don't give you the necessary resources to do the assignments or take the test.

Just awful experience with this class, tests were always much more difficult in lab than in lecture and they don't give you clear study materials, the practice tests aren't super indicative of what you see on the exams

Chem 107 is annoying. TAs try their best but they are required to essentially nitpick all of your work looking for ways to take off points. You never actually see a real professor. Lab manual is poorly made. Way too much work for a 1 credit course. Exams are hard, rely on TA reviews and you'll make it.

Well I never actually met or saw Dr.Asplund so I can't say much about him. In 107, a TA runs the whole class & all the course content was created years ago by someone named Rebecca Sansom. Lowkey the class was confusing and required so much of your time for only 1 credit hour. There's really no easy way out of this class but the TA's got your back!

Professor Asplund's class was challenging, but engaging. He covers a lot of material, so staying on top of the homework is key. I found unstuck AI and the TAs really helpful for studying and staying afloat. Overall, a solid course if you're willing to put in the work.

Dr. Asplund is a very nice guy, he really cares about the students and wants them to succeed. His lectures were not the most helpful, I often had to relearn things from the book which explained way better. You will read a lot. Beware that tests are not very similar to HW. HW is more math based and tests conceptual based. He did curve the class.

Hardest class I've had. His lectures weren't my favorite and I didn't think they helped me much. Homework is math based, but exams were conceptual based which was challenging for me. He is very forgiving on exams which was lifesaving. He is a very nice guy and is helpful in office hours so go to those. If you put in the effort, it's a doable class.

Very challenging class. Lectures are hard to get into, but once you understand his style, it's easier to follow. He is very helpful during office hours, often breaking down concepts to more manageable pieces if you ask questions. Often was helpful to students who needed accommodations.
Horrible professor. Would never consider taking a class from him ever again.

This is a one-credit lab; however, the amount of work outside and inside of class is more like three credits, forewarning. As well as being test-heavy, little to no study materials were given for the exams, and the professor is often unresponsive to emails. TAs grade assignments and grade very shallowly, and it is very hard to work with them.

I changed my personal scripture study habits based on how he taught us to study for chemistry. Strong gospel emphasis!

Lots of homework, but prepares you for exactly what will be on the tests. He repeatedly tells you that the practice problems will teach you better than he can.

Exploratory lab assignment once a week, takes about an hour.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. At one point 25 of his student were failing the class, the average for all the midterms was about a 68%. There were only two students that had an A throughout the semester. Midterms are not curved and are designed to trick you. I had to use YouTube to teach me how to do everything.

Chem 105 is a hard class, but I think other professors make it easier. Professor Asplund would get behind in lectures and never really cover the stuff we actually had to know for homework and tests. Luckily I had a good TA, but I had to figure out a lot of things on my own.

I really enjoyed this class in the end. Professor Asplund can be a really interesting lecturer, but he sometimes gets behind what he wants to get through in a lecture and will speed through some material to catch up. The homework (especially problem sets) was really important for studying for exams, but I barely used the textbook.

Dr. Asplund is great: he was so available and welcoming in and out of office hours, making this class a lot more manageable. His lectures are good and you can tell he knows a lot and cares about his students. Lots of homework, but if you use it to study for the tests, you will be fine. I had bad TAs, so while it wasn't easy, Asplund made it doable.

Very heavy into lectures, I'm not sure I ever used the textbook, maybe once or twice. Three non-final tests make up 30 or 45% of your grade, plus the final, but if you do better on the final, he'll replace your lowest midterm with that grade 

Hard course, but I would take it from him again!

Very mid. The course was challenging, and He would speed through all of his material to make sure we were caught up. Wouldn't give very detailed explanations on how to use the equations and other tools that he gave us. Focused heavily on the conceptual side of chemistry, but wouldn't answer a lot of questions during class. TAs make it or break it.

I worked as a TA for this professor and two others (Hansen and Woodfield). Asplund is the middle ground. His lectures follow the topics but frequently get off topic. Cares about the students, but doesn't take the time to teach the concepts in a helpful way. If you take from him, find a good TA, they're your best resource.

He is the best lecturer on earth. People like to critique his lectures because he doesn't spent 50 minutes explaining how to solve problems, but that's not what he is there for. He explains concepts in a straightforward and intriguing way. He managed to make one of the most painful classes at BYU enjoyable. P.S. every single concept is important!!!

Dr. Asplund was nice enough, and the class is hard no matter who you take it from. The course load is intense. He has so much homework assigned and they don't really line up with the tests. The final is easier than the midterms.

Incredibly homework heavy, especially since he does not really teach anything. Tests were created to fool students, including unknown concepts, and multiple reminders that "I'm going to try to trick you on this". Zero concern for students. Lectures were useless, and he would rather play the cello than spend time explaining things in a rational way.

This class was difficult, but the big thing here is you need to study the concepts he puts on the study guide rather than just doing the practice exam or looking through the homework.  If I had done this on the first few exams I would've gotten an A. Study hard for the tests and use all the resources he gives you and you'll do great.

Chem 105 is work heavy no matter who you take it from. Asplund is one of the best choices. I learned in lecture just fine. You don't need to do readings, but you have 2 homework assignments per lecture. They took me probably 45 min- 1 hr each. Tests follow these problems really closely though. Practice problems and use the TAs and you'll do fine.

If you can find a better professor to take CHEM105 from do it. Professor Asplund makes his exams so much harder than any of the homework or practice worksheets that are given. I'd avoid taking CHEM105 with him.

This is a 1 credit class that he doesn't seem too invested in. It's disorganized and learning suite deadlines often aren't correct. He's pretty lenient about stuff like that though, so the class wasn't too hard. He was really nice and wanted to help if anyone expressed confusion.

Professor Asplund seemed to want to be helpful, but the tests were often different from what he taught in class. His lectures were hard and confusing to follow, he would frequently go off on tangents that didn't matter. The class average on his tests were frequently below passing and he wouldn't curve tests. Definitely take chem from somebody else.

If you can find a better chem professor at byu, take them instead of Asplund. He is very test heavy and the tests are so much harder than the homework and problem sets he gives out. He actively tries to trick you in the exams. Attendance isn't mandatory but he has quiz questions every class that is worth points so if you miss it does add up.

Chemistry should be difficult, but not THIS difficult. He speeds through content and makes the exams 10x harder than anything you learned in class. TA's are amazing, but there's only so much they can teach you in recitations. I ended up withdrawing from his class and will be taking it with another professor.

Without a doubt the worst professor I've ever had. He tests way above what is taught in class and through the homework. When his TA's wouldn't show up for their labs and I emailed him about it, (he's the head of the chem 105 course) he jumped to their defense rather than holding them accountable. Absolutely pathetic professor.
Amazing professor! Gave us so many oppurtunities to get extra credit or curve the class

Dr. Asplund is incredibly nice and very helpful outside of class. His lectures get a little too deep sometimes, mainly because he is very passionate about what he teaches. He also takes a long time to grade things so be aware of that. One of the most friendly professors here.

Dr. Asplund did not care if anybody learned. The average on all the tests was 60%. He showed up, presented his lecture, and left. No questions asked, no participation occurred. He would just stand there and derive endless equations without giving the big picture, and without doing any examples. In addition, the class was extremely disorganized.

For higher level chem classes it seems he is a good choice. For chem 105, I would go a different route. Dr. Asplund is a genuinely good guy, but he has been in the field of chemistry so long that he forgot what it is like to struggle over new concepts or even sig figs. He's too smart and fast for the average joe taking beginner chemistry

Dr. Asplund is an understanding teacher and is very kind. Chem 105 is a hard class. If you don't get a good TA, you won't get much help because the class is large. If you're going to take this class, make your schedule so you have no other hard classes because this will take up all of your time.

The lectures move too quickly to learn anything in the classroom so you have to read the whole textbook to understand the course content. Dr. Asplund makes his tests extremely difficult and emphasizes conceptual questions. A challenging class but actually my favorite.

Dr. Asplund has the hard job of smashing all of PChem into 1 semester. It's a very fast paced class with a lot to learn and a lot to do. Because of the sheer quantity of material he has to teach, he does seem to rush through a lot of things during class so DO THE READING. However, he's very approachable and willing to help you in his office hour

He has no mercy for his students. The week before finals included a homework assignment (8-12 hours), midterm (4 hours) and group project (easily 8 hours/problem). His lectures are focused on deriving the math of Pchem, but he never shows you how to use the equations. DO NOT GET THE EBOOK! The equations are unreadable and he did nothing to fix it.

He's a pretty nice guy, but that doesn't really translate to his ability to teach. His lectures are often tangential and lack purpose and direction. Although his tests were ridiculously difficult the grading was to the student's advantage. Ultimately I learned next to nothing from him, I made it through with a decent grade because of the TA's.

Dr. Asplund spends most of the class period going through what was in the reading and adding his two cents. Homework easily takes up 10 hours each week. Don't expect this to be an easy class. There are weekly Moodle assignments that are very easy to forget about. Overall, he's a sweet cinnamon roll of a professor who's teaching difficult stuff.

Dr. Asplund mainly focused on regurgitating whatever was in the book. There existed a huge disconnect between what was taught in class/book and what was expected of us to complete in the homework/exams. He failed to present the BIG PICTURE of P-Chem. He always focused on mathematical derivations that didn't help students learn the material.

Dr. Asplund is my favorite Chemistry professor at BYU. He's quirky, fun, and a great lecturer. He does a good job of making things understandable and not being too long winded. The homework assignments take 6-8 hours, and are near-impossible without working with a group/getting TA help, but they help you prepare for the tests that are just as hard.

I took his class Spring Term and it was probably the hardest class I've ever taken (also worst grade I've ever got). Asplund is cool and super smart but the nature of this class is hard. Huge amounts of homework, 3+hour tests, quizzes, and you are given a ton of information. This class is doable but don't take it in the spring or summer like I did!

The concept of this class is actually really fun, and the labs really help you learn the concepts. However, this class requires WAY too much for a 2 credit lab class, with the papers being due every week or having to do a presentation. Dr. Asplund was relatively helpful, better than he was in CHEM462.

Professor Asplund is a caring teacher, even if it's hard to keep up with him sometimes. He can move pretty quickly, but is always willing to slow down and go over tough concepts if you're brave enough to ask. When you ask him questions after class is over, he'll drop what he's doing just to draw on the chalkboard and answer your questions.
This is not an easy class, but Professor Asplund is definitely willing to help you out. You have to study hard for this class, like super hard.

Dr. Asplund is an awesome teacher! He's so much fun and explains stuff really well. He was always happy to answer any of my questions during class or in his office. I was usually able to go get help from him in the office. Chem 105 is a hard class with a lot of busy work, but Dr. Asplund makes it a little more bearable.

P Chem is a very difficult class, but Dr. Asplund does a good job making it understandable. He's great to work with, and is definitely willing to help you outside of class. He cares more about understanding concepts than the nitty gritty.

Best professor i have had yet. He is smart, blows things up a lot, engaging, and really WANTS to help you. Biggest pointer is to meet with him whenever you're stuck and spend time in the Chem lab. I saw his rating was low and was sincerely offended because he really helped me grow drastically! He also allows you to get back many points on exams too

He is so smart and really knows chemistry but his lectures can be confusing and he doesn't really teach to the tests. I relied heavily on the TAs and they taught me more than Asplund. Be ready to work hard.

Dr. Asplund is very knowledgable and has interesting lectures. The only problem I had is that he likes to go in-depth into material that is not essential. Made it very confusing. Other than that he is a good professor for a hard class

Dr. Asplund is a genius and he really cares about his students.  His lectures are funny and entertaining at times, but also contain huge amounts of information, so take good notes!  PLEASE be sure to do all of the online homework.  It has a real impact on your test grade.  Do the class like he says to, and you will be amazed at how well you can do.

No matter who teaches it, Chem 111 is a hard class. It's a weeder course, a rude awakening to remind you that you're not in high school anymore. He tries to make the class entertaining, but it's easy to get lost in how quickly he moves through material.

Not going to lie: this class was really hard. I had to work hard to make a B in the class. Hes good professor. He really knows his stuff and you can tell he is passionate about it. He is encouraging and he wants his students to learn! He really cares for his students and his office is open when you need to talk. I learned so much in that class!
One minute he would be talking about an atom, and the next how space is created. Don't get me wrong, he really tries, but it just didn't work.

Hard class, but if you go to his office hours HE WILL HELP YOU.  I went nearly every week and also GO TO THE TA LAB.  I went to the lab 3 hours per week and that's what saved me. He loves chem & does awesome demos basically every week, so that's fun. Tests are EVIL but Asplund is a good teacher. He curves grades at the end, I had a B- but got a B+.
I was not impressed.

Dr. Asplund was definitely the worst teacher to take Chemistry from. The tests are standardized across the department. His class averaged a 65% on all the tests. He told us he would curve them at the end, but he didn't. Just don't take it from him. His lectures and homework were not representative of the tests at all.

Really not very helpful. What was learned in class was not nearly enough to pass the class and it's difficult even with help from the TA. Expect a lot of time and work outside of class reading, doing homework, studying, and trying not to go insane. GOOD LUCK!

If you are looking for an easy class that you don't really deeply learn anything but regurgitate information then Dr. Asplund isn't for you. BUT if you are looking to really understand chemistry and truly learn then definitely take his class. It's hard but he does everything he can to help. Very good one on one.

He knows so much he can't dumb it down for people taking chemistry for the first time. I would do well on test reviews, but the actual test would kill me. IClicker quizzes to make the professor feel good about his teaching and not your learning. Confusing- I learned more from the textbook and had to hire a tutor to pass.
Professor Asplund is not very clear in his lectures and he is not very likely to help you if you go to him during office hours. Tests were a lot more difficult than the review.

Dr. Asplund gives interesting lectures, but his tests are pretty brutal to the point of being unfair. He demands 100% concept mastery, so be prepared to spend a lot of time in the TA lab. Still hard to get a good grade even if you're trying your hardest.  Makes a lot of mistakes during lecture, which I find pretty annoying.

Dr. Asplund really helped me LEARN the subject. He teaches what you need to know, plus a little more background so it's clear. He gives you all the tools you need to do well, and he is more than willing to help you.  I  I wish he taught the later chemistry classes. It IS a hard class, but he makes it a lot easier. Good luck!

This class is demanding.  It was really interesting but there is just SO much thrown at the students that is was easy to fall behind.  He was a good lecturer and the demos were fun.  If you have to take the class, he is a good choice.

Chemistry is hard regardless, so please don’t shoot the messenger. Plus,the dude can rock a bow tie. I took it during summer, which was killer, and a tip:do practice problems! Put pencil to paper and figure. Truthfully that’s all chemistry is: problem solving with matter in reactions and its relationships with natural phenomena on a molecular scale

Chem 105 is a hard class no matter what professor you take it from, but Prof. Asplund seems to be a little harder than most. He does have fairly low cutoffs for grades, and lots of homework and extra credit to boost your grade. If you fall behind, you're doomed. I put my heart and soul into this class and got a B. Plan on living in the help lab.

Of course chem 105 is hard with any teacher, but it was fun to have it with Asplund. It does come at you thick and heavy but it is completely doable. Go to the TA lab for help. And dont stress so much. You will get a better grade than you think

Dr Asplund is one of the most knowledgable and enthusiastic teachers in the department. I couldn't imagine taking this class from anyone else. Chem 105 is hard, and there's not much you can do to change that, but Dr Asplund does a great job of making the material relatable and interesting. One of my all time favorite teachers. Brilliant, approachable, and has a great bow tie.

Dr. Asplund loves chemistry. He's a nice guy that wants to help and blows stuff up regularly. He rambles about things most students don't understand a lot and it can be confusing. THIS CLASS IS HARD. I got my first B ever. READ THE TEXTBOOK and form a study group. It's the only way you'll survive.
By far my least favorite teacher.  So unhelpful and unclear.  Doesn't teach at all, I had to teach everything to myself.

Personally, I really like Dr. Asplund. He tries to show you applications of the principles you're learning and blows stuff up regularly. The material comes fast and thick and the tests are beastly, but it's doable. IF YOU GET BEHIND YOU WILL DIE. Keep up, put in the time, take good notes, use a lot of grey matter and you'll be okay.

I know my rating seems harsh, and Professor Asplund is a great guy outside of the class, but too much happened to ignore.  He would put stuff on tests that homework never covered, almost no teaching came during class itself, that was up to the TA's, and he made it a 5 day class.  Nice guy, wouldn't take a class from him again though :/

Tips to getting through: All the chem 111 tests are standardized, so it doesn't really matter the teacher. Make sure you get the homework done. The earlier you do it in the week the better. I had never taken AP chem or bio, but I did well in the class and it was really interesting. Though it seems impossible it isn't. You have to put in 5-20 hours

This is a tough class, but Asplund teaches well. He likes to goes off subject but it works, you have to read before class to answer the iclicker questions. He blows things up every week and he really tries to be fair. This class requires a lot of dedication. With hw, assessments and labs but they all help for when the exam comes around.
