Terrible Teacher. Makes everything confusing. I used to enjoy Chemistry until I took it from him. He is awful at teaching. His tests are ridiculously hard. He puts things that don't even make sense on them. I really hated this class. Take this class from someone else if you can. NEVER take it from him. He wants to see you fail.

This class is tough with any professor, but Dr. Asplund turned out better than I had first thought.  Interesting lectures although he sometimes went on a few tangents. He did explain some of the concepts well though and is a funny/smart guy. I liked how after an exam, he would go over each question later.  He also added a few points on exam grades!

Asplund is my favorite professor so far! If you get the chance,take this class from either him or Dr. Lamb (I've attended lectures by both; Lamb is a little more helpful, but Asplund is way more fun). Chem105, although difficult, with Asplund was my favorite class this semester and I learned A LOT. Great professor!!
He's super confusing and used other teacher's powerpoints. Also, the tests DO NOT follow what he said in class or what the book says. The tests are WAY hard.

DO EVERYTHING IN YOUR POWER TO GET THIS PROFESSOR. I took Chem 111 as my elective--I'm a Physics/Astronomy major--and I stayed in the class because of Professor Asplund. He's brilliant, kind, dedicated, and obviously loves both his subject and his students. If you're not afraid of work and actually want to learn, this is the PERFECT professor!!! :)
Very difficult class but he really is helpful and cares about the students.

Professor Asplund is a very enthusiastic teacher, he clearly has a love for chemistry. However it seemed like he didnt explain things to thoroughly, and made mistakes in work that students had to correct him on. Unless you really enjoy chem, dont take this class. Its a lot of work, and lots of stress.

Honestly, this was one of the hardest classes i've ever taken. Most people did extremely poorly but Dr Asplund is probably the best  option for this class. He explains the concepts really clearly, though you have to be paying attention in class. I got an A in the class only because i would actually listen and read the book. Me and 2 others.

Prof Asplund is great!  He is so enthusiastic about the subject, and he is always doing experiments and demonstrations that keep class interesting and relevant.  Lots of material is covered, so it's tough, but you can still come out with an A if you work hard.

super excited about teaching! the tests didn't seem to always go right along with what we learned in class. The tests often had many correct answers and you had to pick the BEST. Best advice is to get a good TA mine graded hard and would mark off if the answer wasn't EXACTLY right. try getting CHAD as your TA, he is a million times better then mine
Great professor- really excited and energetic about science. take notes, read the textbook, and go to Chad's reviews.

This is a very tough course no matter who the professor is. I would honestly recommend Sevy over him. The main thing with Aslpund was how often he would boast about how much experience he had, yet he was hard to work with if you had a problem. The TAs are the people who save you.

He's fun in class and he is knowledgeable,but he doesn't teach much.  He expects his students to be future revolutionary scientists and figure everything out but themselves.  He'd rather have the appearance and prestige of being a hard professor than teaching.  Which is good because that's exactly what he does.  Doesn't care about helping students

I loved professor Asplund. Lectures were fantastic, maybe I am a bit of a nerd but I found them fascinating. It was not a science class I was used to it was far more entertaining. PHYS100 Is a freshman class and it was easy and stress free! I say if you have any interest at all take the class, it was worth every minute I spent in it!
In short, professor good, course sucks. Nice guy and blows stuff up on Fridays. Didn't learn much, just took it for the GE credit.

The only reason I passed this class was by going to Chad's review sessions. I learned nothing in class and only went to get points for the daily iclicker quizzes. I really dislike physical science and hate that it's a GE, but at least Prof. Asplund blew stuff up on Fridays.
physical science wasn't the best class, but this guy is my new favorite teacher, absolutely hilarious, he doesn't try to make (Fake) things funny, he justs presents it that way,
Great teacher. I thought I would hate the class before the semester really started--Professor Asplund proved me wrong.

Dr. Asplund is an incredibly approachable professor. He is funny, and tries very hard to make a very difficult subject (Quantum Mechanics) comprehensible. We frequently had a study group outside his office at the table in the hallway, and he was very friendly and willing to offer help.

This is a really hard class.  I basically took notes to keep myself awake and paying attention--they didn't really help when studying.  Working in study groups is the best way to understand material and get homework done.  Asplund is really flexible with grades and a good lecturer.

You HAVE to keep up on the reading to do well in this class--had daily quizzes.  Tests could be tougher than they looked.  Some pretty tough concepts; don't miss class. Pretty entertaining, though--he blew something up for us every week.

Hard class overall but Dr. Asplund is a good teacher.  The tests were definitely difficult but the department makes them, not Dr. Asplund himself.  Be sure to attend class so you can take the in-class i-clickers; you'll need all of the extra points you can rack up!  Also go to the labs every week and do the reading!

I suggest taking Physical Science from Asplund. He's a good teacher, and blows stuff up most days (very fun). I hated the tests (getting between 60-80%), but he's not the one who makes them (it's some other professor), so you might as well take those stupid tests and have a GOOD teacher, rather than having to take them anyway and having a bad one.

Professor Asplund is so intelligent. He really knows what he is talking about. I really enjoyed his class. His tests are hard, but it felt good that he expected you to know a lot. He is flexible with grades at the end of the semester depending on how everyone does. Take this class from Asplund--He rocks!
He doesn't explain things well at all. Class is pretty much worthless, except for the mandatory quizzes. The only way to pass the class is with the help of the TAs. Tons of homework.

Haha.  I have no interest whatsoever in this subject but asplund is a hoot.  Read the chapter go to the lab and this class turns into a very A-able class.  Dont do the reading and you wont get an A.  The guy blows something up every friday...good times.
He makes a very unapproachable subject very approachable.  I can't think of a better professor in the department to teach this class.

He really cares about whether or not his students understand what is being taught.  He takes the time to help his students and will explain things as often as needed.  More teachers should be like him.

Asplund's cool. He's funny and blows things up every Friday, candidly admitting it has no connection to the material. He's more of a chemistry expert, so he can't explain all areas of science with equal clarity, but if you do the readings and ask questions of TAs, you'll be okay. Not a hard class if you do the work.
No Comments

I was not looking forward to this class at all, but Asplund made it interesting and even fun. He isnt very good at explaining material for tests (he included lots of unnecessary info), but thats what TA sessions are for. I would highly recommend him to non-science major students.

Poor guy - I'm sure he is a nice guy, but just has a horrible time actually explaining concepts for PS100 students to understand.  Make sure you understand it well from the book or tests will get you.

I took 101 from Debra Wells and that class was tough; if you have the option I would definitely take it from Professor Christensen. The tests/overall pace of the class is challenging, but he grades really leniently. If you put in the work you can get an A.

Great professor, Dr. Christensen is down to earth and very knowledgeable - You interact with the TA's far more often than the actual professor so its kind of dice roll if your TA is good (for the most part, they are all decent though). Chinese is not to be taken lightly. I wouldn't say the content is really difficult, its just a TON of studying.

Great professor! Only thing was the workload doubled at the start of the middle of the semester. It was very time-consuming, so def worth 4 credits (it should be more imo.) Also two dialogues a week to memorize. 12 characters to memorize per week (until he started making it 24 so that's how my grade dropped lol.) Super fun class tho! Loved my TA!

Dr. Christensen is a good teacher and builds lots of learning opportunities into his lectures. That said, there is a TON of work outside of class with memorizing characters, narratives, and audio practice. He is a generally lenient grader, but the sheer volume of studying necessary to succeed makes this class exhausting at times.

I took CHIN 345R. It was a great class and I learned a lot. There was a ton of textbooks and a ton of reading but overall it was so interesting. We also had to read a few novels and write book reports on them but they were super good reads. There was no big tests, just a few papers. Loved this class and would totally take from him again.

Dr. Christensen is really great. Lectures largely consist of him reflecting on his time in China and Taiwan (but still very educational). He has really interesting perspectives. Class has a consistent amount of reading and writing books and small papers, but he doesn't give any tests, so overall very doable. Would take from him again.

Super easy A class! Even though the class is super easy, you can learn a lot about Chinese and teach Chinese from him. The whole class is very discussion style so you definitely won't fall asleep. Most homework is less than one-page reading reflection, and his grading is not harsh at all. Very fun and easy class.

Great professor. He is fun and organizes the class effectively. Most of your grade is daily dialogue performances and quizzes. There is a lot of work outside class, but if you do it you will be fine and he is an easy grader. Definitely recommend.

Dr Christensen is caring, and great at answering questions. This class isn't easy but he will answer your questions, and the workload is heavy, but all useful. At first he seems a little cold and hard to read, but in the end he's just the caring but stoic dad who expects a lot out of us, but always loves us and wants to help us and see us succeed.

Though a lot of the class is taught by the TA's, Dr. Christensen helped me to thoroughly enjoy Chinese. This became one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. Chinese is hard, yes, but if you study consistently this class (and 101) are certainly manageable. Ask him about his visits to China, and he has some good stories.

Okay, here's the deal: it's Chinese. Get ready. It's really hard, and, unfortunately, there's really no way getting around that. Dr. Christensen is good because he motivates you to prepare for class--because you have to read Chinese characters in front of the class once a week. And you have to memorize two dialogues a week.

Prof. Christiensen was great.  The class was easier than I expected. i took chinese teaching from him.  It was really just reading the textbook and writing small papers the entire time.  Just make sure that you develop an opinion on the topics you discuss.
He comes off as an emotionless, almost mean guy sometimes, but he's ok if you get to know him. His Chinese is poor, like most BYU Chinese professors.
Dr. Christensen is great! He is very patient and his teaching methods are extremely effective and helpful. I LOVED THIS CLASS!!!

Loved Christensen- He is very insightful and gives lots of valuable information. If you have the time to put in to this class, you will do fine. If you don't have time, good luck. Overall I loved this class and really learned quite a bit.
Christiansen is a good teacher yet his tests and quizes can be difficult if you do not know the characters. TA's are easy graders just as long as you get a good one.  Good class all in all.

you are required to take this class if you want to be a TA, however, he will consider his students who major on languages.  you won't have an opportunity to  get paid by teaching Chinese. yet, you will get "a grading paper." nasty work !!! save you money do not take his class!!!
Good teacher. Solid on doctrine. Makes the material accessible. Only uses the scriptures.

Chinese is difficult and time consuming, but Dr. Christensen is an excellent teacher, and he makes the material more interesting with culture insights. He is there to help you learn and will help in any way he can. Attendance is absolutely necessary if you want a decent grade.
Great teacher. Fair grading and if you do participate in class and do your homework then he makes it easy to get an A. Great insights to chinese teaching, really earned my respect.
Dr. Christensen is an outstanding teacher. He is very demanding, and studying for the weekly character quizzes are usually huge time investments, but if you're dedicated you can get an A.

Language classes are difficult depending on your aptitude for learning languages. I think this class moves at a very fair rate, with plenty of time for review. He focuses on performance (memorizing dialogues) which is actually very effective. Quizzes are fair. I think Chinese is like learning 2 languages, because the Characters are not phonetic.

A very fun and interesting class.  Very difficult but that is to be expected with learning a language, especially one like Chinese.  Make sure to get a good TA if you can and study and keep up with the class.

amazing, AMAZING, AMAZING teacher! If he was teaching all the classes at BYU I would be extremely happy.  Straight teaching, he is your friend.  Go to him and talk to him, he will even remember your chinese name.  He makes funny classes and they are easy to learn. HE IS AMAZINGLY HOT!

This class was not the easiest class that I have ever taken but I went every day and took notes. You can use your Book of Mormon on the exams, and you can write notes in your Book of Mormon. I didn't to great on all the tests but there is a Plan B option that helped me out a ton. I got an A in the class.

Good class, he is a great teacher--but the class seemed to lack worthwhile material... things that were really applicable in life. Funny guy, usually entertains you throughout the class, but not particularly a great "learning" class.

Brother Christensen is a lovable person. He teaches with the spirit and comes well prepared to class. If you do what is outlinedin the syllabus, this course is not only an easy A, but you will learn to love the D&C. I would take a class from this professor again.

He is hilarious! Also, he's very knowledgeable.  I look forward to his class everday. He gives obvious hints as to what to look for one the tests.  The only downside is he does go a hair too far with his sarcasism, Occasionally a little light-minded.  This is the exception rather than the norm.

Amazing teacher!  I feel spiritually uplifted after every class.  His tests are fairly easy.  Any notes you make in you scriptures you can use on the test.  He is funny and keeps things interesting.  He is more about the doctrine than about the history in the book of Mormon.  If you want the history/wars/cities, he is not the teacher for you.
AMAZING TEACHER! THE BEST YET

Bro. Christensen was a great teacher.  I loved a lot of the things he had to say, always bringing a bit of his own ideas of the gospel in, but always letting us know it was personal opinion.  His tests can be tricky, but he throws questions out if a majority have issues with them.  Completely fair in his grading.

I liked Bro Christiansen. I think alot of religion teachers get cought up in testing and looking smart but he is just fun, and he loves the gospel. He knows how to transition really well from laughter to teaching and he's not afraid to tell you what he thinks about gospel topics. I thought that he had some really cool insites into the scriptures

This class was a joke. We never touched the book of mormon... ever. All he did was lecture on all the weird aspects of mormonism. It gets very irritating, and you find yourself uncomfortable with what he is saying most of the time. He has his own personal agenda's. but the number one most horrible thing is: his tests. They don't even come close to
Good teacher.  Fun class.  Not an easy class but well worth it!
Dr. Christensen has done a good job laying out this class; the sections he teaches are entertaining and productive.  The TAs teach two-thirds of the class so make sure you get a good one.
Hard class, teacher is fair though and makes it doable. I'd recommend him, but make sure you get a good TA because they can make or break your grade.
Make sure to cry every night because it's so much fun.

He also teaches Chinese 102. He's strict, but one of the funniest and best teachers I've ever had. It's far from a blow-off class, but sets you up well for the future. He's flexible and an easy person to respect. If you ever can, take a class from him.

He is probably my favorite teacher I've had here at BYU! He's so funny - I can't think of a time I went to that class and haven't laughed at something he said. He moves a little fast, which might make it difficult for some people, but as long as you're paying attention, it's not that bad. Totally would take one of his classes again!

I liked this class because I did learn way more about programming than I ever had before. I will say he goes over concepts fast, so I needed to get help outside of class. He is super willing to help though and is flexible with deadlines. I described this class as the most complicated yet relaxed one I've ever taken, but overall it was pretty good!

Professor Gibbons is a really helpful and knowledgeable, but class was pretty hard to follow. His slides are just text, so if you're a visual learner it's hard to get anything out of them. Plan to spend a lot of time googling and teaching yourself. It's doable, but difficult, so be prepared.

He is wonderful at explaining things. If you are attentive, you will catch many hilarious comments that make class really enjoyable. He is quite kind and very approachable. He will not make you feel like you are an idiot if you don't understand.

I like Professor Gibbons a lot--he made coding super clear and his grading was beyond reasonable. I think because the class was online, though, I'm not sure I learned enough to be valuable to anyone, and the program doesn't really have an advanced version of this class.
He is one of the only professors that teaches programming in a way that inexperienced programmers can keep up with.

Professor Gibbons classes were probably the most valuable classes I have ever taken at BYU. He has a way of maximizing the time to benefit ratio. You definitely do have to put in time, but everything we do in the class accelerates our ability to learn and apply different aspects of code. The best coding courses on campus are taught by Prof Gibbons.
Funniest professor I've ever had. I love his sense of humor! His classes are project-based, so you really apply the things you learn.

This guy knows his stuff. He is an industry professional who teaches part-time. He explains programming concepts so well even a child can understand! I would recommend this class for any major who is even slightly interested in learning web development. Rock solid class.

Professor Gibbons is different from any other teacher I have had. We were learning PHP and he really focuses on real-life examples. However his projects do take a lot of time but he is super flexible when it comes to working with you.  The only reason someone would get anything less than "A" is if you stop trying, he is really willing to help you!

Dr. Grey gives amazing lectures. I learned so much about ancient temples and it has helped me to have a more meaningful and worthwhile temple experience today. TAKE THIS CLASS!! It is so worth it! Lots of reading, but it is interesting content.

This class was an HONRS class, but Dr. Grey's lectures were interesting. He was enthusiastic as he taught. There were a lot of readings, but they were fast reads, and he connected the readings with his lecture nicely. I did feel like sometimes he was "performing" rather than teaching, but I would take another class from him. I learned a lot too!

Professor Grey's class is a deep dive into biblical temples and history. Prepare to put in the work, but you'll gain invaluable insights. Unstuckstudy was a game-changer for studying the dense material. Attend every lecture - he knows exactly what will be on the exams.

Dr. Grey is one of those professors at BYU who focuses heavily a context-based reading of scriptures. Through this class I learned so much about ancient Judaism, Christianity that enhanced my biblical literacy and inspired me to learn more.
Tries to fit waaay too much in his lectures, but don't miss any of them! Amazing class and great professor.

Some ratings complain that his class isn't spiritual enough but I think it depends on your application of the material. He is passionate about helping students develop biblical literacy to strengthen personal faith and to better equip us to build bridges w/ other faiths. It helped me connect to Christ, His word, and other Christians more deeply!

This was a new class talking about ancient/biblical temples. Dr. Grey knew the topic very well and the lectures were amazing! The reading assignments were easy to follow and directly correlated to class discussion. Tests were a little difficult but as long as you attend class, Dr. Grey was very explicit about what would be included on the test.

This class greatly improved my Biblical literacy and my understanding of temples both ancient and modern. Dr Grey cares greatly about the student experience and is willing to adjust the course schedule or pacing to help facilitate understanding. This was probably the best religion class I've ever taken. 10/10 for both class and professor.

Professor Grey is one of the most stellar teachers at BYU. I recently took his Temples of the Biblical World class (392R) and loved it so much. The lectures were stellar, I actually found that the workload was really quite easy, and I'm not even an ANES student. If you are willing to put a bit of effort in, you will learn SO MUCH. 10/10 recommend.

This class was slightly more intensive than most religion classes. You must be willing to put in a bit of work, but if you are, the return is amazing! I learned so much about biblical temples and it gave much-needed context to modern temples. Prof pointed out exactly what would be on the exam. It is clear he cares about the topic. Highly recommend!

This class is very insightful and I learned a ton. I came out with a much deeper understanding temple ritual and symbolism. It was a little bit more difficult than the average religion class but completely worth it. His exams are a lot of memorization, but he points out in class almost exactly what will be on the test so there were no surprises.

Grey is super knowledgeable and passionate. The class was more difficult than other religion classes I've taken. Lots of memorization was required and I had to do more than usual preparation for tests. If you don't have time to spare for a hard rel. class, don't take this one. Also, expect to only email TA, because prof doesn't reply...

You could tell that Prof Grey really cared about the topic, but the expectations for this class felt pretty absurd. The tests are closed notes and consist of extremely difficult, detailed questions. I spent more time test-prepping for this class than I did for any of my upper-level major classes. DO NOT take this class if you are not an ANES major.

Class is more historical than spiritual. Tests are 75% of your grade, Hw assignments are 25%, and attendance is mandatory! If you miss more than 1 day, you get -2% of your grade. His tests are difficult. He helps you in his lectures by saying what might be on it, but most of his questions are select all that apply so its confusing. Beware beware!

This class is brand new, but I can tell that Dr. Grey is an amazing professor. I enjoyed my time in this class. If you want to learn more about temples, I would recommend this class if it's offered in the future. Dr. Grey talks fast and is a cheerful man. If English is your second language, it might be difficult to follow his speech.

I took the biblical temples test run class. Learned so much! He is super great and knows his stuff. His lectures are engaging! There is a lot of reading during the week, but the tests were super easy. I don't know how his other classes are but he is a great professor! Definitely recommend!

Class was a new perspective on the NT with background. Professor Grey was knowledgable and taught clearly. The class organization was structured well. You can't submit any of the smaller assignments late, and they are worth 1% of your grade so beware of that. You're prepared for tests very well and the questions are typically very straightforward.

Fantastic lectures. Changed my perspective on the new testament completely. Knows his stuff. Willing to answer difficult questions. Speaks a million miles per hour, because he wants to tell you everything about the topic at hand. You can tell he loves what he does. Class is pretty easy.

Professor Grey is fantastic. He comes into class every day with a skip in his step and you can tell he loves this material so much and he can't wait to share the goodness with everyone. My whole perspective on Jesus Christ and the gospel was enriched. His grading is clear and the class is straightforward and easy if you are basically invested.

Professor Grey approaches the New Testament from a very academic perspective which I appreciated. It helped me feel the spirit and gain a deeper testimony when I actually knew the context of the scriptures. Tests are 100% multiple choice and there are no papers. Overall a pretty good class.

I very much enjoyed professor grey this semester. He truly made me excited to go to class and learn more about Christ. Throughout the whole class you really can see that this man has a strong testimony of Christ and has learned so much about Him and wants us to learn about Him as well. He cares about our opinions. Really amazing teacher!!!!

This class was my favorite religion class at BYU! Very informative and structured simply. You are graded on reading assignments/notes (due before class, took about an hour for each one), attendance, and five non-comprehensive exams (to which he gives you the answers in class ahead of time so you definitely want to attend lectures). Very fair class!

Dr. Grey was easily one of the best professors I've had here. He is unique in that his lectures are very engaging and have the central purpose in helping people better understand Jesus Christ. The curriculum was very clear, and if you put in some effort, you gain a lot of new insight and appreciation for the course material. Highly recommend!

Dr. Grey takes the New Testament and teaches about the historical context as well as the contents of the New Testament.  He is quite passionate about what he teaches and his lectures are really fascinating.  He asks for our thoughts frequently, which sometimes makes us go overtime.  Overall, he's a great teacher.

Cannot explain the love I have for this man. Has an unbelievable understanding of the New Testament, and the outside context of what is not easily found in the Bible. He has great insights and makes things very easy to understand. Homework due every class, not too difficult. Exams that he prepares you very well to succeed on!

Dr. Grey is an awesome teacher. He gives you a super good understanding of the New Testament, but his tests aren't hard at all; he literally gives you the test questions beforehand. This is the perfect class to take.

You guys HAVE to take a class from Dr. Grey, he's amazing. His class was by far my favorite, and I left class every day feeling like I knew Jesus so much better. Dr. Grey has a super fun, happy energy and you can tell he really knows what he's talking about and he loves it. None of the work is super hard and it's all really interesting.

He has truly been my favorite religion professor at BYU. I'm continuing to study at BYU after I lost my faith in the church and this class was very friendly to that situation. We are heavily focused on the New Testament and it is very much a scholarly look at the gospels. This class made me want to study Jesus so much more.

Dr. Grey is awesome! I loved this class. He wants you to succeed and provides everything you need. Very spiritual class and informative about Jesus Christ. Very clear reading assignments and if you go to class you will know everything you need to. Workload was not heavy.

This was the last religion class I needed and I am so glad I got to take it from Dr. Grey! He is so enthusiastic and knowledgeable about not only the Old and New Testament, but he also taught us about the history of Jesus and the world around him while he was alive. I thought it was so cool! The homework doubled as a study guide, too!

Dr Grey is PHENOMENAL. You can tell that he is truly passionate and excited about his work and area of study. His lectures are very engaging, but he does talk fast (he has recorded versions of lectures on LS which are useful). The readings are reasonable and he clearly lays out what is will be on the exams. You won't regret taking his class!

I feel like this is a bit more work than a 2 credit religion class should be BUT i think its worth it because hes awesome. He does the more history side of religion which i personally appreciated and enjoyed. Super interesting. You can tell he cares about your opinion and your grade.

Dr. Grey has probably been my favorite religion professor out of any I've had at BYU (he was my 6th). This is not glorified Sunday School, this class felt like an actual college level course. He leans heavily on teaching the history and context of the material, and his tests mostly focus on those kinds of facts, not his own interpretation.

Dr. Grey restored my faith in BYU Religion Classes! He focuses on the historical side of the New Testament, but it's so you can better spiritually understand the scriptures in context. Just graded on reading questions and 4 exams. The reading questions actually feel worth doing, and the lectures tell you everything on the exam. Take his class!

Dr. Grey is a very enthusiastic teacher. His class is really historically based which puts the content into a fascinating perspective. It was really cool learning what he taught. He always says he's outlined what will be on the test, but it was still sometimes unclear. Also, the homework assignments are long and have some confusing questions.

INCREDIBLE professor! You will NOT regret taking a class by him! He is so knowledgeable about the context of the scriptures, he is guaranteed to blow your mind! Because classes are so good, they go by way fast and it leaves you wanting more! TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!

I loved this class. He focused on a lot of the history of the New Testament which was SO cool. I learned something new each week. Some of the homework takes a long time but they were mostly pretty quick to fill out. He is so smart and you could tell he had a plan for each lesson. Fill out the homework, take notes in class to study, and you'll pass.

Dr. Grey taught me so much about the nature of Jesus this semester. We studied the context behind the bible stories in great depth with a heavy emphasis on history. We had to memorize specific dates and events, but the learning payoff was worth it. He literally told us what was on the exams. Don't let this fool you, the exams are not a breeze.

Very incredible professor. Loved his historical approach. The memorization of maps seems hard at the beginning but is way worth it. Would recommend for anyone that wants a good university class on religion and not another seminary class.

I loved learning about the history of the New Testament and now I feel like I really understand Revelations (a massive accomplishment). Dr. Grey is very clear on his study guides and about what will be on the test. That being said, it felt more like a history class than a religion class. If you like that, then take this class.

All tests and quizzes were online and he gives you a very detailed study guide and tells you what material will be on the test in every class. Attendance is mandatory and you have to pay attention during class or else you won't pass. He gives super intense homework assignments. You won't feel uplifted though - it's essentially just a history class.

Pray for first for Charity, then Hope, then Faith, read everything, attend, and pay close attention to his PowerPoint Presentations. You will pass with an A. The reading is a bit more extensive, but if you do it with real intent you will feel and end inspired. Awesome teacher.

Dr. Grey is great! Lectures are based on hw guides you fill out before class. He says the exact information needed for the test, directly from hw. He teaches the historical background and builds from that to ensure greater understanding for the spiritual aspect. If you study the material from class you'll do well on tests. Cares about his students.

If you want to become a serious student of the scriptures, take a class from Dr. Grey. He teaches fascinating lectures about what is really in the scriptures and what the books and letters really meant to the original audiences. It will enrich your scripture study and your knowledge of the gospel and of Christianity as a whole.

Dr. Grey is passionate about 1st century Jerusalem and the Jesus that ancient Palestine would have produced according to our understanding of the culture, politics and Judaism of the time. He wants students to comprehend Jesus and the New Testament in context. Some of the tests are harder than most religion tests. Lots of weekly reading.

This class is not spiritual. It is a good class if you want to learn history, but not what most people look for. Also, he didn't handle online lectures very well. He cancelled the last day of class to add some extra time on his lectures, but ended up giving us almost two class periods extra of lectures to review right before exam week, not cool.

Professor Grey does a great job lecturing and really knows the material inside and out. The first unit had a ton of Dates and Locations that you had to memorize but after that, it wasn't too much work. He tells you exactly what will be on the test and gives a compressive study guide before each test so you always know what you'll be tested on.

Grading is simple: hw completion, exams, & don't miss class. Exams are multiple choice & very short. The hw is one set of reading questions before each class. There is a lot of reading, but the hw is very specific about where to find each answer, & the material is so cool! No papers, low-stress, amazing lectures, & so many scriptural insights!

Grey was an awesome teacher. There are reading assignments due before every class but they don't take too long. The study guides are pretty specific and he helps you know exactly what you need to know for the test during his lectures.

This class is a LOT of work. Dr. Grey's up front about it, and you learn a lot because of the work you do, but nonetheless this is not a class to take for an easy A. I spent 3-4 hours a week doing the reading assignments and corresponding questions. Dr. Grey was also consistently behind, but he gave us study guides to compensate.

Easily the worst class I have ever taken. It feels like the tests were designed to trick you. Tons of reading with very long and annoying short answer homework. Each one was roughly 3 pages. Boring lectures. His class feels like it was designed to pinpoint unnecessary parts about Christ. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Dr. Grey is my favorite religion professor at BYU. His lectures are FASCINATING as are all the readings. You will learn a lot about the context and history of New Testament as well as more about who Christ is. The readings are all relevant and he prepares you very well for the tests. I absolutely recommend you take this class from Dr. Grey.

Grey is VERY boring. Yes I learned about the New Testament and Paul, but He would reteach the same things multiple times WORD FOR WORD. He gave us a review for every test because he was BEHIND on teaching. I had emergency surgery and he refused to give me his slides because I was "Absent." I got an A but would NEVER take from him again!!

I loved Dr. Grey. It's a good class. He tells you what will be on the test, so if you come to class and review what he said, you will be fine. No essays, just tests and a couple of easy assignments a week.

Dr. Grey was by far my favorite professor that I had for religion. He was very kind and cared deeply about his students and the material. He gives you everything to succeed in his class. Be ready to read a little bit as every assignment he gives you is about 30 minutes of work but the tests are straight forward and he gives you a study guide.

Dr. Grey offers a new way to look at the scriptures and the gospel of Jesus Christ that have changed my life. His lectures are inspiring and he is so approachable! The student comes first in his classroom and he keep things light with his humor. Lectures and reading assignments are more than enough to excel in exams and the class. Amazing teacher!
He was a very understanding professor and gave great review sessions before each test. Would highly recommend.

Professor Grey has been one of my absolute favorite religion professors. I feel like a lot of religion classes feel like glorified Sunday School, but I really felt like I was getting a University level education in this class. He is very knowledgable about what he lectures, his lectures are entertaining, and he's very accessible outside class.

Professor Grey is amazing! He really shows that he cares about each student, and you can tell that he is truly passionate about what he teaches. The units are broken up into 5 smaller tests throughout the semester, and he is really good about telling you when something will be on the test during his lectures. The homework is graded on completion.

He is an absolutely phenomenal teacher. He was super approachable, very concerned with how his students were doing, and very fair in all of his grading and tests. His class was incredibly spiritually uplifting. My favorite religion class by far. I would often talk to him after class about deeper topics, and he was always super respectful.

Doc Grey was amazing! I learned so much about Christ and feel a lot more knowledgeable. This class will help my scripture reading for my whole life. Doc Grey is hilarious and the class is a super easy A if you go to class.

I loved Professor Grey and he has been my favorite professor at BYU thus far. If you take this class just don't miss class! After the first absence any unexcused absence is 2% off your final grade. Still worth it though!

Dr. Grey has been one of the best professors I have taken at BYU. While his class was rigorous for a religion class, the material he covered and the depth and context he provided in each lecture has impacted my outlook on the New Testament dramatically. He shows very genuine love and concern for all students and I highly recommend taking from him.

Dr. Grey is so passionate about his subject and it is infectious. The homework is graded on completion and the test questions are formed from what is discussed in both homework AND lecture, not just one or the other, so you know exactly what to study. He can get on (related) tangents and get behind in class sometimes.

nice guy but class felt kinda dry to me... for some reason I kept getting B's on every test even tho I always went to class and studied everything he told us would be on it.. maybe I just wasn't willing to put enough work in because I was prioritizing my more difficult classes that matter for my major... harder to get an A than I usually like haha
TAKE HIM FOR CHRIST AND THE EVERLASTING GOSPEL! Favorite religion professor I've had at BYU and I've taken all my religion credits.

Dr. Grey's class was great for a religion course. Downsides: REQUIRED attendance or grade will be docked beyond like 2 absences. Reading questions before class worth 25% of grade and can be very time consuming. Upsides: great lectures. Easy tests if you do the reading question assignments. Overall Easy A and fulfills a general.

Prof Grey is THE BEST religion professor I've had. The lectures aren't generic Sunday school lessons. He connects the OT, NT, BOM and historical writings together to help you truly understand and love Jesus . I will always remember this class. He challenges you to see the bigger picture and consider ideas that you haven't before. I learned so much!

What an amazing professor! He really knows his stuff and really wants his students to succeed. Five tests- Very clear and he allows partial credit for the multiple answer questions. The final is not comprehensive! Reading assignments- Full credit for completion, used as study guides for tests GREAT professor! Would take again!
He teaches your, and inspires you in your mind and in your heart! Do class work, and you will do well! Listen, learn, open your heart.

I love taking this class! Dr. Grey is simply amazing, and the Spirit that comes when I come to his class makes me so eager to learn more from him. He knows his stuff and does a great job of answering questions even outside of the curriculum.

I was very disappointed by this class. While Dr. Grey's lectures were informative, I didn't feel that he respected his students, I felt that he expected too much for a religion class and I felt the class focused more on the secular, less on the spiritual. Exams are heavily weighted which puts unnecessary pressure on a religion class. Take elsewhere
Dr. Grey teaches the new testament from a more historical perspective. I absolutely loved every minute (even though I am not a very religious person). Fairly LGBTQ+ friendly.

Dr. Grey is an incredible teacher that knows SO much. I learned more than expected from his class and loved going to lectures. There were 2 reading assignments due before each class that were sometimes lengthy and you are only graded on those and four tests. If you study the tests aren't hard, but there are 4 Qs that are hard & risk a low grade

I merely quote: Dr. Grey is great. Now, we could take the maximalist ground and say that his class will be the best you'll take at BYU, or we could take the minimalist ground and say that you'll hate it, but I think the best thing to do is take the moderate middle ground and say you'll really enjoy his class and learn a lot. This is so cool, guys!

No complaints. He's the best lecturer and he's so excited about what he teaches. The info just sticks in your brain because he's so happy about it all. But sometimes the assignments aren't clear and if you ask, he'll just say "well it says it in the rubric" but it really doesn't. That's my only compliant. Other than that, he was fantastic!

I love Dr. Grey! I had him at the Jerusalem center and it was awesome!! He is so passionate about what he teaches that it rubs off on you. You do have to pay attention and work hard in class but it is so worth it! Ask Dr. Grey about latrines

Ah Dr. Grey. My favorite class. I really learned so much and enjoyed the class even with its rigor. The context it provides to the Bible was so essential to my understanding of scripture. Dr. Grey's enthusiasm is infectious and he is so personable and connects well with his students. We were all obsessed with him. I'm a disciple of Grey.
Dr. Grey has been a terrific professor at the Jerusalem Center. He is very knowledgeable about the material he is teaching. His lectures and entertaining and you learn so much from them.

I changed my major because of Dr. Grey and it was the best decision I've ever made. I've always loved the scriptures, but he brought a depth and understanding that I had never experienced before, and I learned more than I had thought possible. I didn't even need to take this class, but did because I found out he was teaching it.  Highly recommended

Emphasis on historical context of NT. Easy A. No papers, just 4 multiple choice tests. I did the homework in my free hour before class. Grey seems uninterested in addressing the implications that the content brings up for common LDS understandings. He has a lot of content to get through, but sometimes can seem slightly disrespectful to questions.

Minimal work for a guaranteed A and a guaranteed testimony builder, exactly how a religion class should be. He really likes to go into the academic, unbiased side of the life of Jesus, which I found interesting. Tests come straight from the reading assignments and lectures. Lectures are usually very interesting, but sometimes kind of sleep inducing

Professor Grey has great insights and really helps you understand the scriptures from an intellectual stand point and not just the spiritual stuff, but he does both so it's a great mix :) Just go to class and take good notes and you'll do well if you study.

Dr. Grey is a great guy and he is very passionate about what he teaches. My testimony grew so much from being in his class. There is a homework assignment due before every lecture. The only thing on your grade other than these homework assignments are the tests which are really easy if you do the assignments. Take this class from him!

Looking for an easy-A religion class? Don't take this class from Dr Grey. Looking to learn a TON about Christ and the historical context that he lived in? Take this class from Dr Grey! It's SUPER lecture heavy and pretty boring in class sometimes but he gets really in-depth and teaches a ton about Jesus' life and the time that he lived in.

Dr. Grey is fantastic! He's very up front at the beginning of the semester about the kind of class he teaches so you know exactly what you're getting. There aren't any papers or projects that try to force spiritual experiences. He focuses on the history of the text so that his students can better understand/teach from the scriptures. He's the best!

Dr. Grey is the BOMB DOT COM! I wish he taught every religion subject, because if he did, I would be there. There is a person down below who says his lectures aren't spiritual and questions  whether he believes in the divinity of Christ. Uh... this person was having a bad day because his classes are extremely spiritual he DEFINITELY loves Christ.

Professor Grey is the best teacher I have had here at BYU! I specifically waited to take Rel 212 until he was teaching it again and am so glad that I did. His lectures are so interesting and educational. He teaches not just the scriptures but the actual history behind them which makes them so much more meaningful. I highly recommend him!
Not poor. Grey believes in Jesus. Swell guy.

Passionate about the subject. Current scholastic knowledge about scriptures. Communicates in fun, happy, clear way. Very friendly to approach and encourages students to think deeply. He is great at not superimposing our culture onto the authors of the bible. The hw improves learning from the reading, not detracting. Strong testimony of Christ.

Really good at  applying context and making you think about Christ as a human being rather than a God.  If you want everything taught in an LDS framework, this isn't the class for you.  I wish he would testify at some point; I question sometimes whether he believes in Christ's divinity. If you are looking for a spiritual experience, look elsewhere.

I've taken multiple classes from him and I would take more if I could. He is easily my favorite professor on campus and I appreciate his focus on historical context within the scriptures rather than being really Sunday school-esque.

Professor Grey is the best religion professor at BYU. His lectures were incredible, and nobody knows more about the time of Christ than him. I would easily be doing him a disservice if I did not rate him a 5. This class changed my life and views of the New Testament.  In simpler terms, Grey is amazing. Youre crazy if you DONT take his class

Everyone seems to like him on here, but I wish I would've taken this class from someone else. He's somewhat arrogant & talks too fast. He's always rushed in class. The homework takes forever & there are 5 tests. 94% is the cut off for an A.

Dr. Grey is an amazing professor. I left class feeling like my mind had been blown every single time. He is extremely passionate about the life of Jesus Christ and the New Testament, thus it shows in the way he expresses things, which is then contagious and makes learning easy. His tests are not difficult, and homework is somewhat minimal.

Easy religion class. I still learned and thought his lectures were interesting as well. There was a pretty easy reading assignment due every class (twice a week) and those were the study guides for the tests. There were a few more tests than normal but they were pretty easy and only 25 multiple choice questions. You are graded on attendance.

This was honestly the best religion class I've ever taken. Dr Grey is one of a kind! His lectures and even his homework blew my mind every time. I learned so much from him and looked forward to his classes. His tests are extremely manageable if you do the homework and study guides. They outline EXACTLY what will be on the test! TAKE FROM HIM.
He's an expert on the history of the Bible, the most insightful religion class I've ever taken.  Two thumbs up

Professor Grey is great. This is the 3rd class I have taken from him. He gives great historical background, cultural context, and multiple perspectives to the scriptures. He doesn't spoon feed you anything, but won't overload you with homework. Tests are very straight forward. His classes have really expanded my knowledge of the scriptures.

Dr. Grey is fantastic. He really knows his stuff and completely made me see and understand the world of Christ in a new way. His class is spiritual but also very educational. He makes it very easy to get an A. If you do the assignments and attend class, you will no doubt do well. He also loves class discussion and encourages students to participate

Dr. Grey knows his material really well, and is passionate about what he teaches. He really wants students to genuinely learn, and not worry about grades, so he structures his class accordingly. If you just do your homework and go to class, the tests are more than fair. Really energetic, so class is not boring at all. GREAT learning experience.

If you want a religion teacher that teaches the history of the text, this is your guy. I learned a lot about the history of the New Testament with Dr. Grey. You MUST do EVERY assignment and study for the tests - I got straight 92s on all 4 tests but got a B+ because I missed 4 assignments. Put in the time and you'll get the grade you want.
If you're looking for an easy Religion class, this is not the class. But you will learn a lot with Dr. Grey

This is a great class. Dr. Grey looks at the second half of the New Testament from a very academic setting. I learned a lot from this class. It has increased my knowledge of the scriptures and doctrine. He does require more work than most than most other religion professors but it is well worth it. Don't take the class from anyone else!

The religion class that will bring your GPA down and requires too much work for religion credit. Lectures were the same every class with different content and skipped back from Old Testament to New Testament plus some. Sure he's nice, but his teaching was either rushed, crammed, and or confusing. Tests mix ups answers and blends questions together.

Dr. Grey is awesome! He is an archaeology nut which he uses as a foundation in his approach to the course material. On many homework assignments he gave us outside sources that provided historical context for the chapter(s) we were covering and it made the New Testament really come to life. Not to mention I really enjoyed his lectures. Recommended!

He was a great teacher and he is very knowledgeable about the subject matter. He uses interesting viewpoints and looks at the NT with a historical context. His tests were much harder than I expected though! You will have to study hard in this class!

This man is amazing! He is the kindest, most interesting BoM professor. He's one of those Mesoamerican archeologist professors, which helps him to give the coolest insights. And he explains Isiah in the most chrystal clear way in the Isiah chapters. Just fill out the homework and study it for tests and you'll be golden! Tests aren't too hard.

Matthew Grey is the bet professor Ive had at BYU. He definitely gives a different view point than I think many of the other religion professors teach. It is so refreshing and I stay interested in every lecture. He is very animated and. I think he does a good job at distinguishing opinion from doctrine. Tests are based off homework, so do it right.

Dr. Grey is AMAZING! This class was definitely my favorite this semester. Before this class, I had not been really interested in the New Testament, and now I love it. He makes the gospel of Jesus Christ truly applicable. His tests are kind of difficult.. they are completely based off of the notes/homework, so you have to get it right. Easy class!

Amazing professor. I changed my major because of this class. Teaches from a historical perspective and is so insightful. Tests are super straightforward and if you know the material you'll do really well on them. Would recommend Grey to absolutely anyone.

Dr. Grey teaches the Book of Mormon from an interesting perspective because he's an archeologist and deals with facts and history.  He brought to light new details I'd never heard of or considered, which enhanced my testimony because the things he said were logical and made sense.  I particularly liked his Isaiah approach.  Tests are piece of cake.

Fantastic class and fantastic teacher! Brother Grey's lectures are always thought provoking and engaging! He presented the information in ways I had never previously considered! Greatly enriched my understanding of the Book of Mormon!

This is a good class. The professor doesn't study it as a "devotional" perspective. This class is a study of the history of the New Testament. While it is spiritually uplifting, it is more like intellectually enlightening. 2 questionnaires weekly, which also act as the study guide for the tests as well. Final is not comprehensive. Good class!

This is the first religion class I've taken that is not all touchy-feely. He is an archaeologist and teaches mostly the history. I have always hated history, but MAN, he teaches so well and is so energetic and insightful. GREAT PROFESSOR

Grey was a good teacher for Book of Mormon. Each Class you are assigned 10-15 questions due the next class. Your test is the same questions as the homework just in multiple choice form. As long as you keep on top of the homework, you'll be good.

This class changed by life- Dr. Grey is seriously amazing and I learned more than I could have imagined. A whole new perspective- he really knows his stuff. Do the homework- super helpful for tests and for class. He is ALWAYS willing to answer questions and help.

Definitely one of my favorite BYU professors! He really cares about students and helping them be successful and learn things that are useful for their entire lives! The assignments are not especially difficult BUT extremely effective in helping you learn! I wish I could take all my religion classes with Grey!

Dr. Grey approaches the Gospels in a way that varies from the regular methods and is more effective. He is passionate about the subject which makes the class enjoyable. The workload is not very challenging (like the other comments say) but if done correctly, you will learn so much more than you'd think. Dr. Grey is by far my favorite BYU professor.

Unfortunately, you can get by with doing absolutely minimal and mindless worksheets. Study them and you'll do well on the exams, but you can easily get an A without really knowing the material. Too easy.

Very high quality. The combination of a scholarly perspective with spiritual insights made the class more rigorous, but more interesting and enjoyable, than most other religion classes. Homework and tests were generally easy, but were good gauges of learning.

Brother Grey is the best and most amazing religion teacher I have ever had. My understanding of the scriptures and my testimony of Jesus Christ increased. He is a well educated professor, and that makes his teaching unique. I highly recommend him!

Great professor! Willing to meet with you outside of Office Hours to help you understand the material (highly beneficial). Reading questions every week always match the lectures he gives. If you do the work, you should have no problem getting an A! Wonderful professor- would take again!

Great teacher! Background in archeology allows for a very interesting historical perspective on the Book of Mormon. Assignments guided your reading and the tests were straight from homework and lecture. I gained a stronger understanding of the BoM.

Bro. Grey was fantastic. I felt like the final had some questions that weren't on the reading questions (test q's come directly from hw), so I got an A-. good class. only graded from HW and tests though, some people might not like that. No extra credit. Lectures were amazing.

u answer some reading questions before each class (get 100% if you attempt each question, and he goes over the questions in lecture), and 3 exams and a final all very reasonable.The most efficient work load ive had in a religion class. Highly recommend Bro Grey, hes always happy and I learned SO much about Jesus Christ. Don't take from anyone else.

By far the best religion class I have taken at BYU.  I had heard great things about his class and was not disappointed.  His lectures are awesome and time seemed to fly.  His background and education added so much to his lectures and was very enriching.  I highly recommend this class.  If you pay attention and do the homework you will do great.

Dr. Grey is one of the best teachers I have had. I would highly recommend him. I plan to take another class from him. He is so knowledgeably, and he is also a very interesting lecturer. If you  go to class and do the homework, you will get a good grade. Great teacher.

His class is decently easy if you take the time to do the homework thoughtfully. The tests are completely based off the homework, so if you do it wrong, you're doomed. He has very opinions and teaches them as though they are doctrine. I fell asleep in his class almost every time.

Professor Grey is great. He shows you all about the actual places and geography in history, and you understand it completely. I now know why Nephi wrote in Egyptian, but with the "learning of the Jews." I understand Isaiah now. That alone should be worth a lot. I don't usually feel like I learn much from classes. This one, I did. A lot

Dr. Grey is awesome! I love his historical perspective. And I feel like I have come to know and understand the scriptures more than I have in any other religion class. He isn't afraid to challenge traditional ideas and really makes you think. Tests are super easy if you do the reading questions everyday.

I love this class, he has his own to teach, but gives really helpful material. Exam questions are based out of your homework, which I think is so clever and fair. Interesting insights of the New Testament

Pro. Grey is a good teacher. Requires a lot for a religion class, but he loves the material and loves teaching it. The tests were straight forward and easy if you did the assignments. Takes a very historical approach to the NT, but it was definitely interesting.

This was one of the best teachers ever! I highly recommend him. I've never learned so much about the Book of Mormon before. He is extremely helpful. Assignment due each class that is actually helpful, enjoyable, and not hard. The questions from these assignments are the exact ones on your test. No writing assignments. Seriously, take from him!!
He has a really interesting perspective, from his really archaeological background. He gets you really excited about things you've never thought of before.

I learned a ton in this class! I didn't think I would like approach with his emphasis towards the historical stuff but I loved it! Tests were a bit difficult for me but other than that I loved the class

Take this class! Dr. Grey was the most informative ancient scripture teacher I've ever had, and I left that class realizing that I had never really understood the New Testament. Easy tests that take all of the questions from the homework assignments. Cinch of a class and learned a ton

Course homework/content described in comment below. With that covered, this was the best class I have ever had at BYU, hands down. I have never learned so much new stuff about the gospel that really helped me grow. He is chock full of information and he is so reasonable with homework and tests. He is so passionate. I LOVED New Testament.

No writing assignments and multiple choice tests. Need I say more? There is a reading assignment due almost every class, but he tells you exactly which verse to find the answer in, and all the test questions come from those assignments. If you just read through them before the tests you should get above a 90% on the test. So easy. Learned a lot.

professor grey was an incredible teacher. I had him at 8 am and had no problem staying awake in class. I learned so much in his class, and your really get into the history of the BoM, not just the same things you've been learning since primary. He's basically the Indiana Jones of Religion Classes. If you want to learn and have fun, take his class.
Professor Grey was a GREAT professor! I loved his historical/academic focus on the Book of Mormon. You learn so much but you do not feel stressed by the coursework. Definitely take from him!

I really like Professor Grey. He gets so much out of scriptures, he is very intelligent. Such an easy class. There is a reading assignment every day (easy) and then if you study those you will be prepared for the tests. Overall great guy, class wasn't always very spiritual but I still learned a lot.

Dr. Grey is a great professor.  He is really concerned about the class and if they understand what he is teaching.  However, I felt like I didn't learn very much; he is not a very engaging teacher.  If you're looking for an easy A, this is the one to take, but if you want to learn a lot, take it from someone else.

Great class. Awesome teacher that really loves material. Very kind. He has great assignments that count for 40% of your mark (do them and you'll get a hundred percent on that part). The tests are slightly challenging. But pay attention in class and study. He is an ancient near eastern archeologist so he is brilliant with this stuff.

Brother Grey is a great guy, but definitely not my favorite professor. If you're looking for a super easy A, this is the class to take because there are no papers and all the homework is completion, but I didn't feel like the content was challenging enough for me to get much out of it.

Brother Grey is so great! He is sincerely concerned with whether or not his class is being understood. No papers to write, just study guides. And all the test questions come straight from the study guides. Perfect.

Professor grey is great! loved his class I learned a ton from new testament. Very passionate about his subjects, does make you read a lot though. Some of the reading doesn't seem important, but some is really cool. Kinda favors suck ups, but thats all teachers.

I love Brother Matt Grey. I met him in Jerusalem (long story) and he was very kind. He is an archeologist and knows all the facts about Jesus' time. His supplementary readings were very interesting original sources: did you know Josephus wrote about John the Baptist? He knows everyone's name, cares about you, and is super excited to teach religion.

Grey is a complete stud. He hooked up an end of the semester pizza party combing his RM class (all dudes) with his freshman class (mostly girls). His kids are adorable and his wife is a fox. Class really isn't hard - just interesting. We had like one test, and the questions were STRAIGHT from the Study Guide. He is a genious. I learned a TON!

Brother Grey is awesome! It was by far the hardest Book of Mormon class that I have taken, but so worth it! He required a lot of reading form the book and also a packet, which included things that not very many people know or think about regarding the Book of Mormon. If you have the chance to take a class from him do it!

Brother Grey is AMAZING! He requires a lot of reading (especially packets), but it really does help. There is only one test (the final) which is really easy if you did the reading. As long as you read everythin and go to class, you will get an A!
Bro Grey is a GREAT teacher!  He is very helpful and truly cares about his students.  He will be your friend!  TAke his class and you'll do well and learn a lot.

Bro Grey is amazing.  Although he isn't a full-timer but a grad student of Middle Eastern Archeology at andrews univ. he is great and - call me Isaiah - will soon rank with the likes of Susan Black, Randy Bott, etc.  He enables you to get the big picture and dig way deep at the same time.  Very clear, precise, energetic, friendly teacher.
A smart guy but cannot teach to save his life.

I was excited about the subject, but how he treated me was demotivating and alienated me from it. He seemed intent on bullying me regularly in front of the class. It did make me grateful for the fact that no other professors at BYU have ever treated me this way. If Matt Jones is what college is like at other places, I'm so glad I chose BYU!

Do not take this class from Dr Jones. He wastes most of the time in class on irrelevant topics. You will not learn anything from him and will most likely spend a significant amount of time on the mountain of assignments given each week. The class is disorganized and he rarely prepares you for the topics covered.

Others summed it up pretty well but AVOID AT ALL COSTS! I had no idea what was going on the entire semester. Had a D- going into the final and failed the final. Then he gave me an A-. It was nice to see that but IT WAS NOT WORTH IT. I didn't learn ANYTHING!

At the beginning of the semester I was under the imppression the professor Jones just wasn't a very good professor. He struggled to get his point across and the average grade on his exam was about a 50%. However as the semester went on he frankly got ruder and ruder to students.

I have had bad teachers before, but none of them were nearly as bad as Dr. Jones. It is one thing to not be good at teaching; it is another thing to actively make the learning process more difficult. In general, having no teacher would be better than having Dr. Jones as the teacher--you'd learn more in less time and with much less frustration.

Dr. Jones is the sweetest guy, but a very difficult teacher. Lectures contain little to no relevant content, yet attendance is mandatory. Exam averages were 30-40%, homework is super hard group projects, and no points are given for correct answers. AVOID THIS CLASS! DO NOT TAKE IT AT ALL COSTS!

I'm going to be as fair as possible about Dr. Jones:

The good: He is willing to help you outside of class, he's very accessible, more than most professors I've had.

The bad: Absolutely everything else about his class. He's horrible at teaching, wastes time in class, disorganized, and unfair with grading. He's by far the worst I've had at BYU.

He will either be your favorite or least favorite professor. He isn't great at teaching... like at all, but he clearly cares deeply for the students and wants you to succeed and will do anything for his students. He would even come to your group study if you ask, but really you will be doing all of the learning by yourself unless you understand him

The amount of group work in this class is terrible. It makes it much harder to learn. Dr. Jones is nice, but very bad at running a class. Very disorganized on Learning Suite. He is very unclear about expectations, and his grading feels random. I hated every day of this class.

Hero. Dr. Jones is hands-down the most accessible and helpful professor I've had. He holds 2 weekly "problem solving workshops" where he will do your homework on the board while explaining it. His class is set up differently than most, and is extremely effective if you read and put in the work. Everything he does is to help you succeed.

Dr. Jones is amazing. I recommend that everybody take a course from him. If you are interested in just getting by with minimal effort this is probably not the class for you. He holds his own recitation sections twice a week in addition to class in order to help students out. He really cares about students and focuses on mastery of course outcomes.

Dr. Jones is an amazing professor. I have had him for both thermodynamics and heat transfer and currently conduct research with him. He is incredibly bright and helps you learn so much about effective uses of time. He has high expectations for mastery of course outcomes. Anybody who genuinely wants to learn should get to know Dr. Jones.

I have had many horrible professors but Jones is the absolute worst. His classes are a waste of time. He talks about being an influential engineer and what that means more than the actual material. Then when he talks about material, he goes over very trivial details and expects you to learn everything in the book by yourself.

This class is seriously hard. The tests are times, four questions, impossibly difficult. Up until the final, however, everyone has a shot at an A! He really just cares about learning and being able to see that you've learned throughout the course. I've never had an ME professor who cared so much about students and made himself so available to help.

I absolutely loved Dr. Jones class. It was difficult no doubt, but I came away feeling that I had really learned the principles of Thermodynamics, not just that I had done a bunch of book problems all semester with all the knowledge to be forgotten after the final. This class will teach you, and if you like learning you will love Doctor Jones.

Dr. Jones is probably in the top 5 best teachers I've ever had. He really helped me learn the material by teaching me how to approach a problem. He really changed the way I thought about school. He has tough tests, and you need to do all the reading, but all of the work pays off - if you do it.

Dr. Jones cares more about his students learning and becoming influential engineering more that any other professor I've had. His class can be some work, but if you actually want to learn the material then he is your man.

One of my best classes at BYU. Dr. Jones expects a lot in reading and hw (he takes a philosophy of helping you teach yourself - great for visual learners), but if you do the work you can have a very deep understanding of heat transfer. Much of class is just answering questions. Tests are cool - interesting, practical, challenging, fair problems.

Heat Transfer is a beast, but Dr. Jones was a champ. He puts forth a lot of effort to teach it well and he expects you to put forth effort in learning it. He really cares about his students having a solid understanding. Tests were brutal, but they weren't cheap shots. If you want to master heat transfer, Dr. Jones is definitely your guy.

Dr. Jones knows Heat Transfer. It is a difficult subject and a difficult class. The homework is very time consuming. The TA's were very helpful in doing the homework. The exams were hard but were open book and were very fair. Getting a good grade is possible but it is a lot of hard work and time.

I liked the professor and class a lot.  Heat transfer was a difficult subject, but Dr. Jones made himself available to help.  To do well in the class you had to do the reading everyday.  The tests were challenging, but they were also open book.  I feel like I very clearly understand Heat transfer now
Really good at teaching heat transfer, but the work load for the class was well beyond the 3 credit hour status the class has.

Dr. Jones is a terrible teacher.  He doesn't lecture at all.  Classes are a waste of time.  He feels insecure about the material and it is manefist by useless attacks on students.  You would be better off taking heat transfer from a vegetable.  I was interested in heat transfer coming into the class, but Dr. Jones has ruined any interested I had.

I really learned a lot from Dr. Jones.  He expects you to read and try the homework before class and then he just does examples and answers questions all class period.  He is super helpful - he even would come down to where our group was studying and sit with us and help.  Pretty tough class, but excellent teacher.
So smart, to the point where he couldn't fathom not understanding some concepts.

I really tried to go into summer semester with an open mind and positive attitude. Profesor Linford was a good guy but makes his tests harder than they need to be and it felt like he was trying to trick us on them. I didn't feel like they tried to cut back on any of the material so I do not recommend taking it in the summer.

This class is hard and extremely content-dense so it will be difficult no matter who you take it from. Doctor Linford did a good job simplifying concepts in lectures, and was very willing to talk about how exactly to prepare for tests and exactly what content would be tested. However, most of your learning will probably have to happen on your own.
Great class! Teaches hard concepts clearly. Make sure to do your homework. Test prep is extremely helpful, be there for review days.

Professor Linford is a really good guy and a great teacher. While the class is just a hard class, he makes his expectations very clear. He is very knowledgable on the material and I thought taught what is very difficult material for some people in as clear of a way as he could. I learned a lot in this class!

This is Chem 105, so it's gonna be hard either way, but Doctor Linford is very good at preparing you for the exams. Before each exam, he goes through every question and tells you what you need to know to solve each question. The exams are very difficult, and the class is very heavy, but if you put in the work and the hours, you can do great.

He was not willing to help, makes the class much harder than it needed to be. I am retaking the class at SLC, and it showed me how much harder he made the class. There is so much homework, and not helpful on tests. He also writes the tests to confuse you. It is a hard class but he made it harder than needed to be.

Pretty decent job at explaining things, but the lectures were super boring. He did no demonstrations or experiments in front of the class all semester, just powerpoint lectures. The quantity of material is vast, you have to be consistently studying if you want to succeed. Totally possible to do well in the course, but it is a big time commitment.

I recommend him for Chem 105! He would review concepts in the lectures multiple times to make sure we understood it well. He tells you the concepts of each question on exams, so you know what to study. Prepare for lecture by doing the readings and smartworks before, and you will be able to understand the lecture very well, and do good in the class.

Dr. Linford is very likeable and just a kind, fun person. Definitely a hard class, but study consistently and take your time on tests! Test questions can have really tricky wording but it's all stuff he went over in lecture. Study really well exactly what he says will be on the test. Homework can be annoying but it is mostly helpful.

Professor Linford is a funny guy and often talks about God in his lectures, which is great. He lets you know what each question is on for the exam but in order to do well you need to study hard. He has tricky wording and loves to throw in surprises for his exams. His final exam is straight forward and because of it I went from a B to an A-

He tells you what's on the exam, but you won't get a good grade unless you study for a week straight before. Tons of trick questions on the exam, and the wording is not what he prepares you for. The homework load is unimaginable, with each assignment taking hours to complete. Unfortunately, the best professor for this class.

Chemistry is going to be a hard class no matter what. His lectures are pretty good. The tests are hard. He tells us what each question is going to be on on the test so it is pretty easy to study for. You have to study a ton if you want to do well though. There's quite a lot of hw but it helps prepare you for the test.

Exam 1 class average was 81. Exam 2 class average was 71. Exam 3 class average was 68.8. It isn't that hard to see that this isn't just a "hard class", but fundamentally doesn't prepare you for exams. He may tell you the topics covered on the exam, but the questions on them are not like the ones we practice during the units at all. Tanked my GPA.

Loves chemistry, and will give you all the info you need to pass. Two homeworks due every other day, on average. They weren't too bad. Tough exams that require understanding and critical thinking (but all multiple choice)! Take lots of notes and try to tune in. A sweet guy who seems nervous, but really cares. Good teacher for a hard prereq class.

This was actually my second time taking CHEM 105 due to a poor grade last semester. Dr. Linford was a great teacher for me! He broke down the concepts in a way that was understandable. This class has a ton of homework, but if you stay on top of it, it can be doable. He goes through every single question before the midterms, which really helps.

Fun guy! Exams are 70% of the total grade which I appreciate as a good test-taker, but be aware of that if you aren't like me. I loved that he would go over every question on the test beforehand and explain what you need to know. Stay on top of homework, it can pile up. Make sure you can take good notes, he goes through material quick.

The problem with Dr. Linford is that he seems very condescending when he teaches these concepts because they are so "basic" to him. He gives a lot of homework that is unrelated to what is on the exams. His exams are impossible to study for, even though he will tell you what will be on the exam. I have A's in all my classes, not this one. Stay away.

I was a TA for this class. He is smart, but was very scatterbrained. I often had to completely reteach concepts in recitation. CHEM 105 is hard, but his tests are the most straightforward (he will give you all the concepts you need to know), but you still have to know it. If you have a good TA, you will be fine because they will carry.
