We used no textbook, just interesting primary source readings that really threw you into the material. Much preparation is needed for the tests - mostly essays; gives helpful comments on the test to prepare you for the next.

Mason was the worst teacher ever!  I would rather suffer a horrible and painful death than sit through his class.  Avoid at all costs!  I agree with the other guy's comment...postpone graduation if needed!!

Tests were horrible - not his fault, though. I think the test are written by a panel of professors and TA's. You are tested on you ability to decipher the question, not on what you learned. As far as Dr. Mason was concerned, he seems nice. Who your TA is will affect your grade; they do not grade uniformly.  Pray for a good TA!

I thought the topic made for a great class but was very dissappointed.  He had us read a couple of interesting books but several bad ones.  A lot of the time I felt like he wasn't  teaching correct information.  There was a history teacher taking the class and almost every time he came there would be a difference of opinion on something.

Wasn't a bad class. Can get an A if you study well. My problem was that some of his information in lecture was completely opposite of what I learned in American government. Just little things, mostly, but they really bugged me, because I knew some of his information wasn't really correct. Kind of disappointed, because I love American history.

dont let the comments here daunt you.  paying attention to his example stories will get you through a lot, and anyway, there is a MASSIVE curve on this class.  instead of a high fail(high 50s), i got a C.  as for Mason, i reccomend him.  he keeps class interesting.  the only class this semester i couldnt sleep through :).

its not as hard as everyone makes it out to be. Other than the obvious stuff(paying attention, going to lecture blah blah) Make sure you know every historical figure talked about (not hard, like 20-30 per midterm) and also know the video clips that he uses for examples

Take this class from another professor. Postpone graduation if necessary! While the class is suppose to be on the principals of the American founding(which he'll to you to study), the exams test you on your ability to absorb random useless names and dates. The professor is misleading, and it seems he'll do anything to flunk you. Avoid at all costs!

Professor Mason is amazing.  I'm not a big fan of history classes, but he helped to make this class very bearable.  The tests are hard and sometimes seem to require obscure knowledge, but he's a very good teacher. Remember to take good notes, attend labs, do the reading, and know your notes for the test.  He's really funny, I would recommend him.

Oh, my Gosh! I am really getting crazy, just because I took his class. It looks easy and enjoying in the beginning, but after taking the 1st exam, you'll understand that you were complitely wrong. Prof. Mason tries to be funny, but actually he isn't at all. He really is prepared, but not enough to make us understand and love our American Heritage.

Professor Mason is very funny. His lectures are effective, though his Powerpoints seem a little unorganized at times. His tests aren't exactly accurate representations of how well you know the info. The class is a challenge, but definitely do-able.

Great class! Don't take it as a Freshman, if you take it Jr. or Sr. year you'll do a lot better, and its a lot easier! You have to do all the reading, come to all the lectures, and Labs and you will do fine! You just need to stay above the average grade and you'll get an A. The Lectures were fantastic, take notes on everything!

This guy's great! He knows the stuff and if you don't get he'll explain it...and you'll actually understand his explaination! His tests are hard, but the lectures are interesting and you can learn real easily from them, especially his from his clips. Take him!
I loved this class. Mason gives very interesting lessons and it gets you into the class. Tests are really hard, but do-able.

He is one of the best teachers I have ever had.I take his classes even if I am not interested in the topic because I know if he is teaching it the class will be awesome. He is the kind of teacher that knows your name and shows you he cares about you. TAKE HIS CLASSES THEY ARE GREAT!
He is the best history teacher that I have had at BYU. He explains US history in a way that you have never thought about before. This was a great class.

His lectures put me to sleep and his tests were very hard, but not an impossible class if you are willing to put the time into it. Get lots of help from your TA and you'll be fine. My worst grade at BYU, but I wasn't interested in the subject.

Always available during non-class hours and very attentive to your questions and concerns. VERY DIFFICULT GRADER!!! He expects more than perfect writting, but he helps you reach that level, too. He will help you uncover writting skills you never knew you had. Very personable.

I was thrilled to take this class, but it was insane how hard it was. You are expected to read 6 200-300 pg books and another on your own. He said he would grade the tests easy b/c he didn't give out a review, but that was far-fetched. He's a little unclear with his materials too.

Personally i found mason a bore! I colored probably 7/10 days in this class. Tests are just impossible-focus mostly on lecture when you study, he likes economics and the contagion of liberty.Take  notes on the movie clips, they are on tests and it is hard to remember by then what they were about aga

Dr. Mason is a good teacher, I learned alot from his class. Make sure you study for his hard tests. Go into the lab and make use of your TA's in lab. I really enjoyed his class, he is quite quirky and if you notice he squats throughout the whole class. We counted once- 81 times in 45 minutes!!!!

His class is my worst grade so far in college.  His tests are ridiculously impossible.  He will always have 2 answers that are pretty much correct so you will find your self guessing on the majority of the test.  Would not recommend at all.
The tests were just insane!  They were so hard!

This class was the hardest class I've taken, but Prof Mason is a pretty cool teacher.  You can tell that he loves the subject he teaches, and it makes the lectures more interesting.  The TAs are helpful if you go to their office hours.
Very excited about what he teaches.  Makes classes interesting.
He's definitely got a lot of self confidence-he can be pretty crazy at times.  He's not a bad teacher, but the tests are hard. Can't get out of it though, it is AHtg :(

His class was kinda crazy.  He really helped the class remember the random information that we needed to know for tests by showing video clips and crazy little dances.  It was a fun class that i will remember the information longer than a week after the semester ends!
i think that this is a really interesting class. before taking this class i dreaded learning about history but he makes class worthwhile. the tests are pretty hard and there's tons of reading though.

He is very willing to answer your questions, and he makes his lectures fun and interesting.  A few suggestions: sit in the front row so you can ask questions during class and he'll even talk to you before class starts.  Also, do ALL the reading.  He's very nice and helpful.  I highly recommend him!
He is a great proffesor!The only thing that is hard is that there is a lot of reading and the tests can be difficult.The class is really cool though.
He is my favorite teacher this semester.  he makes the class very interesting and understandable.  I highly recommend him.
Awesome, this guys lectures are allot of fun.  He takes you on a wild ride into the past.  Very motivational
best history class I have ever taken. I learned and retained so much of the information. I highly reccomend him. His stories are so interesting and it was a three hour class and went by really fast
had him at a school before BYU.  good lecturer even better when asked questions.  grading is sometimes vauge but not trifle.  good person who will eagerly help if asked.
He was a good teacher, but he is very vague on grading assignments and your grade is very subjective to how he feels about it. Doesnt have class very often and doesn't require much.
Great teacher.  He is a good lecturer. Made class interesting. Likes opinions and comments. He is a great guy and a great teacher.  I learned a lot and not too much homework either.
I loved this class! Dr. Memmott is the best professor I have ever had and is definitely the most inspiring! I absolutely recommend taking his classes.

Dr. Memmott really cares about his students. I learned a lot in this class because he's very good at explaining difficult concepts. His lectures were engaging and his tests were fair. A lot of the learning is done through homework and there's not much guidance for it, but TA's and his office hours are a must when you can't figure out a problem.

This is my favorite Chem Eng class I've taken so far. Dr. Memmott is an amazing teacher and always strived to make sure we understood the lecture content before we left class. Tests are challenging but you get a page of notes. Homework can be somewhat difficult, but he makes himself available to help if you're confused on anything. Great professor!

Loved this class and Dr. Memmott! He allows a page of notes for each exam, so they aren't bad at all. There's a decent amount of homework each week but they are manageable. Dr. Memmott is really caring and tries to facilitate your learning the best he can. He really cares about his students.

Dr. Memmott is a very good instructor but sometimes he is a bit unclear on what he wants to see in a problem, especially in one of his Open Ended Problems on a test. Aside from that, he makes one of the hardest classes very manageable and a little funny with his attire.

Dr. Memmott is a great guy who cares a lot about his students. He is always willing to help outside of class and is very understanding of students' needs. He goes out of his way to provide interesting and challenging problems for tests and weekly Open Ended Problems. However, it is often difficult to understand what he's going for. Very confusing.

Dr. Memmot is an excellent professor (and one of the best in the department). Fluids is required and it's inherently difficult, but he works hard to make sure you are prepared for the difficult material. His weekly OPS are great learning opportunities if you put effort into them. Also, make sure to erupt into applause for him over small things.
Dr. Memmott was a really good teacher. He was tough, but you could tell the class enjoyed him. He was very helpful, both inside and outside of class, and was always fair.
Dr. Memmott proves that you don't need a belt to be a good professor. Lectures can be nebulous, but his door is always open to guide you. Textbook was needed, but many online PDFs available.

Nuclear engineering is a tough class, but he makes it so interesting that you want to put in the extra effort to really learn the material. He adapted to the needs of the students after the first exam and was always willing to help. You can walk in his office whenever he is there and he is friendly and helpful.

Hey, it's Fluids, it's not going to be easy. This class gives a lot of homework. Dr. Memmott is a pretty good teacher, but his absolutely best quality is how much he cares about his students and what he's willing to do to help you. You can walk into his office at any time and he'll be happy to help. I was amazed.  Very good guy. I respect him.
His class is WAYYY too confusing. be sure to put every due date on a separate calendar at the beginning because he does not mention anything in class.

Good professor, if you like someone more focused on learning and application than memorization and grades. He moves at a quick pace and is very intentional with his lectures. I didn't agree with everything he said but he was a super nice guy.

I have concerns that his REL 200 class is so elementary. It is honestly just repeating what we learned through LDS culture while promoting his own family. I felt like best question he ever answered was only answered 50%, most were poorly answered. He teaches like an auctioneer. If you weren't one of his missionaries, then he is kinda distant.
There's not a ton of work for this class but you need to be there. Professor Richardson is awesome and cares about his students.

Participation is required; he makes you sign every day. 2 assignments every week, and all you have to do is press I did it. Two midterms, and both are very simple and easy. Very funny and has a deep love for missionaries and the gospel.

Mission Prep with Brother Richardson was engaging and well organized. Class discussions were interesting, and the homework was manageable and relevant. The course helped me feel more prepared and confident moving forward.
Prof. Richardson makes this class highly engaging. This brough the apostles to life for me. This course was super interesting. Go to every class.

Fairly easy grade-wise, but I wanted this class to make me feel more prepared and excited to go on a mission, and it really didn't accomplish either. Lots of busywork, and the content felt superflous and unecessary to becoming a good missionary. I appreciate his testimony as a person, but as a professor his teaching tactics didn't make sense to me.
Very silly and story focused guy. however he took the class very seriously compared to others i have heard of. Felt like seminary.

This was a very easy and enjoyable Rel class! Lectures were from the heart and truly prepared me spiritually and mentally for my mission. Exams could be practiced until memorized, and no real final. Go to class for credit and Blue Book assignments. Readings are minimal and can be done ahead. Richardson cares deeply about his students and teachings.

I can honestly say that my testimony of missionary work & the gospel has been multiplied. I don't know if I will serve a mission, but this will forever be one of the most valuable classes I'll take. Brother Richardson has so much experience with missionary work: his mission, mission pres, MTC branch pres, and general Sunday School Board presidency

I LOVED taking mission prep from Brother Richardson! He is so enthusiastic to teach, and his lectures are very engaging. I learned a lot in his class, and the homework was very easy. I would recommend him to anyone!

FOR SURE, TAKE HIM! He is genuinely the most caring professor ever. The midterm was super easy since he provided the answers. The lectures were engaging, and while attendance was mandatory, it wasn't hard to show up. Homework only took about 15 minutes and involved reading his assigned scripture verses after class. Best class ever!

Professor Richardson is AMAZING! He definitely knows his stuff, but makes the learning process so fun as a student. There's some readings, papers, and tests, but if you put in effort you will do great! It's honestly an easy class, but I loved going to his lectures because I always left feeling uplifted. 100% recommend him!

This class is really fun because Brother Richardson has a lot of hilarious experiences with many of the apostles, making their biographies feel very personal. He is incredibly knowledgeable and loves teaching. Great professor!

the class is easy peasy. really easy to stay on top of every thing. but i felt like sometimes his lectures were too comedic and not serious enough. I did love when he would get spiritual. I feel like we would have made it farther through the material if he would stop cracking jokes.

Awesome lectures by someone that really knows what he's talking about. However, the class organization is very messy and can get chaotic very quickly. You may turn assignments in the day it says, you may not, and you may be asked to turn in things that aren't due yet. If you can figure it out, you'll have a good grade, but that can be tricky.

Lectures are long, he talks SO fast, and he doesn't really interact with the class during class. It felt very impersonal and discouraged me from going on a mission. There wasn't a lot of homework and the tests are okay enough, but personally I didn't feel like it was worth my time. Nice enough guy but not the best teacher.

Loves to lecture about basic topics for mission prep. If you have no idea what to expect from a mission, he's great. He spent multiple lectures talking about how if a missionary looks, smells, acts, dresses, and speaks like a missionary, then they must be a missionary. Would recommend a different teacher for mission prep

For "Living Prophets," he was so great, and the 2nd half of the semester had really interesting lectures. He tells personal encounters he has had wither general authorities, and you can tell his testimony is strong. You will have to do mini-assignments before each class period, but they're pretty easy to do (usually just a reading or a lil paper).
Absolutely NO assignments in this class. All you have to do is show up to class and mark off your readings. And don't worry, the readings are really short. 100% would take this class again.

Took mission prep with Brother Richardson and loved it! Met some amazing people and he really helped us learn and prepare for missions. He's insipring and knows the Gospel. He's testimony is great and learned a lot. You have to attend class for credit.

Brother Richardson is the sweetest professor! I took Living Prophets from him and absolutely LOVED it! It was such an uplifting class and felt the spirit so many times. Weekly readings are just the biography of the apostle you're on and their most recent talk from general conference. Exams were so easy. Take it from him!!

Professor Richardson is an outstanding individual as well as teacher. I left every lecture feeling intellectually enlarged, inspired, and more prepared than I previously had been. His lectures are never boring! His grading scale and criteria are clear and there is not too much work required outside of class. I recommend taking any of his classes.

Super easy religion class that didn't feel like seminary so I think it's the perfect class. He knows all the living prophets personally so he adds in fun stories to the material. Very little reading in the class, no essays, and the test questions are given beforehand so you can easily get 100% on the tests. (There were only 2 tests.) Spiritual too!

Professor Richardson is one of the BEST professors! He is very good at being engaging and making class fun. He also has a lot of personal connections to the apostles and tells great stories because of it. The workload is like any other class. Readings, tests, and a few quizzes. Super easy and straightforward. He's not trying to trick you.
He is so fun and makes you love the gospel.

Quirky, but nice. Attendance is part of your grade. Study his notes and the tests are easy, other than the final. The final had some obscure questions on it. Richardson was 2nd counselor on the General Sunday School Board so he knows the Apostles and Prophet very well. Had lots of fun stories. Put in the time and you will do well. Great teacher!
The BEST religion class I have ever taken!  He is so charismatic and has the best stories!  I would take any other class from him in a heartbeat.

Brother Richardson is the best TEACHER on campus. No one else is even close. I say teacher, because he teaches. If you come ready to learn, you will learn more than you could have imagined. He meets with the Apostles on a weekly basis. Trustworthy and very very very doctrinaly accurate and sound.

Professor Richardson is in a class of his own. First religion class I have taken on campus where he was able to balance achieving a fair grade but also inspiring and enlightening us spiritually. Easy class. But very inspiring class at the same time.

Excellent professor! The way in which he constructed his course encouraged me to learn for myself. Assignments consist of readings (for which you only report if you did it or not) and short, copy-and-paste papers. Tests are reasonable and predictable, no trickery. Take the course, come to class, do the assignments according to rubrics and get an A.
Prof. Richardson knows D&C better than any professor I know. His tests are incredibly easy (class average was 95%). You will learn A LOT from him. I strongly recommend his class.
Living Prophets from Brother Richardson has been my favorite religion class at BYU....by far! TAKE THE CLASS - it will change you and your appreciation for modern day prophets.

Best religion class I have taken at BYU.  Brother Richardson is super passionate about what he teachers and you learn a ton of useful information that really enriches your general conference experience.  This class taught me more than any of my other religion classes.  A must take class
All religion classes should be this way! If you do the reading and come to class, you get a good grade. Brother Richardson talks a mile a minute, so you will want to print out his powerpoints.

I took his marriage and family class and felt like I learned a lot. You should attend class, as a lot of what is in the lectures is in the tests. You have readings each class period and just have to mark if you read them. There is an assignment where you have to grow a plant, which just keep trying or talk to him if you are having a hard time.

Brother Richardson is so entertaining. I always look forward to his class. He is so funny yet he can easily be very spiritual. He works with the First Presidency and the 12 Apostles so he ca give great insight about what these men truly are like. I am going to miss this class and I am so glad I have been able to take it!!!

Brother Richardson is the best teacher I have had at BYU. He answers all questions, and makes class fun and interesting. He knows all of the apostles too, so there is no one better to take living prophets from! Do whatever you can to get into his class

Take any religion class from Richardson because he is an absolute hoot! Only problem is you have to attend almost all lectures or he lowers your grade significantly. Besides that, he's enjoyable and hilarious and knows his material. Go to class and you'll get an A easily; all his assignments, notes, and tests are on Blackboard. Great guy.

Brother Richardson is one of my favorite professors I've had at BYU. If you are going to take Living Prophets, take it from someone who sees them on a weekly basis! He has so many personal stories with the Apostles, it's awesome! He's also super entertaining and his tests are exactly the same as the pre-test. Take Living Prophets with him!

I took this class just for the extra credits and an easy A, and it turned out to be my favorite class of the semester. He is an incredible teacher and I learned so much about the gospel from him. Also, he is in the general sunday school presidency for the church so he has a ton of personal experience and he knows his stuff.

The Living Prophets with Brother Richardson was OUTSTANDING! Honestly, it was one of the best classes I have ever had. Brother Richardson is funny and very sincere about what he teaches. It's just a good time. Also, he is in the General Sunday School Presidency, so he has personal stories and experiences with all of the apostles. Life changing!

This marriage prep class was amazing. He is very friendly, very funny, very upbeat, and always does his best to make sure students' concerns are answered. You get out what you put in (law of the harvest), and he makes it very easy to learn a ton of great things. Take a class from him!

Outstanding teaching and insights. Requires reading checked with online quizzes (based on completion only) and growing a plant. Clear and precise teaching makes getting the A very doable. Tests are online and open book. Best religion class I have taken thus far (even better than Bott).

Amazing, AMAZING professor. I have such an amazing insight to how marriage and family is supposed to function. If you take Rel C 234, take it from him. He is funny and really cares about his students and wants the best for all of us. Listen to what he says and you will really be blessed. Best professor yet.

Great teacher.  He talks really fast, but he's compensated for this perfectly with power points and fill-in-the-blank notes packets, so you can catch everything he says instead of freaking out about notes.  Tests are easy, but I learned a lot fro studying and taking them.  I'd love to take him again.
He is really concerned with each student. I felt very welcome and that he cared about each student. I didn't like growing the plant or the tests, but he gives good study guides.

MOST VALUABLE CLASS I'VE EVER TAKEN.  Matt welcomes questions and is very respectful of questions.  It sounds cliche, but I really think this class changed my life.  I'm keeping my notes.  He combines good relationship methods with sound gospel principles.  His understanding is unbelievable and ... deep.  I will take any class I can from him.
busy work... he makes u grow a plant... that plant project is kind of out there...

Dr. Richardson is by far one of my favorite religion professors on campus.  I took Living Prophets from his last year and therefore decided to take Marriage and Family from him.  He's passionate, knowledgeable, hilarious, and runs his class smoothly.  Easy to get an A.

Great teacher, speaks extremely fast. The class was super easy as long as you didn't miss points on the busy work. You have to read things before class, grow a plant and write a paper on it, and take one test in the testing center, one on blackboard and one is a presentation to a roomate or friend on the things you learned in class. Fairly easy.
Amazing teacher. I wanted to go to every class. I learned a ton, and he helped me grow spiritually. I would take this class again. The tests are a little tricky.
He's cool and he's pretty funny. It's an easy class... he gives you everything you need to study for beforehand. The class had cool information, too. I'd take him again, for sure.
Fun teacher but tricky to study for.  Most of what is on the test he will barely mention in class.  Take good notes or you might miss it!

I was really disappointed with this class. He tries to cover every little detail without focusing on really important topics. He also doesn't remind you when things are due and refuses to ever make exceptions if something goes wrong in your life and you forget to turn something in. Tests aren't too difficult but they are tricky
He is an amazing teacher! He makes class so fun. Get the notebook of notes, it makes studying for tests much easier. As long as you go to class and study a bit, you will get an A. Amazing teacher

He is the best teacher!!  The class was amazing and so interesting.  He is totally fair and tells you exactly what will be on the tests, and if the scores are low he will drop questions.  The textbook is actually online on the institute website if you don't want to buy the book.  Takes attendance everyday, reading log is on blackboard.  Loved class

First half of D&C, super enthusiastic, incredibly knowledgeable, really cares about the students, reasonable tests, homework is just to read, and one doctrinal paper which isn't even in essay format. I love this guy! Lecture slides are available but not everything he says in class are on them so there's still a reason to go. I recommend this guy!
Very enthusiastic about the subject.  Interesting material, easy class as long as you read and study.

Professor Richardson was a great professor.  I really appreciated the time spent in this class. He gives great study guides for the tests.  I wish I could take the second half of the Doctrine and Covenants with Brother Richardson, but he is only teaching one (full) section.

I added the class like a day before the deadline, so I missed a couple of journal entry things; I also didn't know we were supposed to go online everyday and confirm that we had read, so I almost failed this way easy class.  He worked with me to work it up to a B, but I wish someone would have mentioned the daily assignment.

Professor Richardson is a great teacher! He was really fun which made the class a lot more fun 9am in the morning. His lectures are based on PowerPt Presentations, gives a review sheet before exams. His test pretty much follow the review sheet. You will be fine in this class! I would recommend it again!
He was OK, not great. His humor gets annoying with all the stupid Robin Williams-type voices he does  but overall not too bad. It is easy.
Awesome teacher, awesome class. Easy to get an A as long as you go to class.  Bro. Richardson is hilarious so I actually wanted to go class.

I loved this class!!!  He is such a great professor-- my only critique is that he lets students comment too much...  that gets old really fast when the same married know-it-all students keep offering their experiences... gag me... but Richardson is GREAT!  Tests are easy-- straight from class lecture.

He is the best professor I've ever had. Class is awesome, you learn a lot and feel the spirit all the time. Easiest A ever but you still learn tons and helps you prepare! Barely any outside work and you get tons of free points. Take this class!!!

An easy fun teacher.  He taught the Doctrine and Covenants just the way it should be.  We were required to read and but no busy work was involved.  We learned what was necessary.  GREAT!  Our only text book was D&C itself.

Only worth your time to audit this one.  Interesting lectures, but the tests are over useless lists.  I couldn't believe what the final was over.  Had nothing to do with what the whole semester had been about.  I'd say don't take it unless you've got nothing better to do.
I really enjoyed this class.  Each class was fun to be at and I learned a lot from Bro. Richardson

Wonderful teacher. Lots of fun stories to teach principles, lots of insight. I honestly looked forward to every class. Tests are not hard. I learned a lot... I would definitely recommend this class with Bro. Richardson!

Wonderful teacher. Lots of fun stories to teach principles, lots of insight. I honestly looked forward to every class. Tests are not hard. I learned a lot... I would definitely recommend this class with Bro. Richardson!

Brother Richardson is one of the best teachers I've every had. His class was honestly not that hard if you put some effort into it...and with the subject matter being taught it will benefit you in to the long run to do well. He wrote me an amazing recommendation too! Take this class!
Great guy. Fun class to listen to. Not much work, and tests are simple. The best scenario would be to bring your fiance with you, then it would be more effective for you.

He is really easy to pay attention to because he is so fun and energetic. I took his D&C class and learned a whole lot, but I only did OK on his tests. There is no way to see the answers unless you go talk to the secretary, which is kind of annoying. It was a good class.

He is very energetic and has a sincere love for the material and students. He does talk fast though and goes fast through his powerpoint. I recommend him and would personally love to take another class from him.
I was not a huge fan of this class.  I don't thing that principles were taught well and we were tested on memorized lists rather than on anything important.  I do not recommend this professor.

He is the king of powerpoint. Interesting class, but seemed repetitive. Tests were vague and not fairly graded. He is a good teacher though and made class fun. Other than the tests easy class. Little outside class work

Know the material, and you'll do fine. He's fun and intergetic. He makes class so interesting. I was scared to take a class on marriage, but it's been one of the best classes I've ever taken. It makes you look at life differently.
EXCELLENT teacher - my favorite religion professor ever. Take Teachings of the Living Prophets and LDS Marriage and Family Preparation. He shares great stories.
No Comments

Bro. Richardson rocks!  He has a vast knowledge of the living prophets and shares it through his testimony.  Best religion class I've taken.  As long as you read/memorize the material tests are pretty easy.
A smart guy but cannot teach to save his life.

I was excited about the subject, but how he treated me was demotivating and alienated me from it. He seemed intent on bullying me regularly in front of the class. It did make me grateful for the fact that no other professors at BYU have ever treated me this way. If Matt Jones is what college is like at other places, I'm so glad I chose BYU!

Do not take this class from Dr Jones. He wastes most of the time in class on irrelevant topics. You will not learn anything from him and will most likely spend a significant amount of time on the mountain of assignments given each week. The class is disorganized and he rarely prepares you for the topics covered.

Others summed it up pretty well but AVOID AT ALL COSTS! I had no idea what was going on the entire semester. Had a D- going into the final and failed the final. Then he gave me an A-. It was nice to see that but IT WAS NOT WORTH IT. I didn't learn ANYTHING!

At the beginning of the semester I was under the imppression the professor Jones just wasn't a very good professor. He struggled to get his point across and the average grade on his exam was about a 50%. However as the semester went on he frankly got ruder and ruder to students.

I have had bad teachers before, but none of them were nearly as bad as Dr. Jones. It is one thing to not be good at teaching; it is another thing to actively make the learning process more difficult. In general, having no teacher would be better than having Dr. Jones as the teacher--you'd learn more in less time and with much less frustration.

Dr. Jones is the sweetest guy, but a very difficult teacher. Lectures contain little to no relevant content, yet attendance is mandatory. Exam averages were 30-40%, homework is super hard group projects, and no points are given for correct answers. AVOID THIS CLASS! DO NOT TAKE IT AT ALL COSTS!

I'm going to be as fair as possible about Dr. Jones:

The good: He is willing to help you outside of class, he's very accessible, more than most professors I've had.

The bad: Absolutely everything else about his class. He's horrible at teaching, wastes time in class, disorganized, and unfair with grading. He's by far the worst I've had at BYU.

He will either be your favorite or least favorite professor. He isn't great at teaching... like at all, but he clearly cares deeply for the students and wants you to succeed and will do anything for his students. He would even come to your group study if you ask, but really you will be doing all of the learning by yourself unless you understand him

The amount of group work in this class is terrible. It makes it much harder to learn. Dr. Jones is nice, but very bad at running a class. Very disorganized on Learning Suite. He is very unclear about expectations, and his grading feels random. I hated every day of this class.

Hero. Dr. Jones is hands-down the most accessible and helpful professor I've had. He holds 2 weekly "problem solving workshops" where he will do your homework on the board while explaining it. His class is set up differently than most, and is extremely effective if you read and put in the work. Everything he does is to help you succeed.

Dr. Jones is amazing. I recommend that everybody take a course from him. If you are interested in just getting by with minimal effort this is probably not the class for you. He holds his own recitation sections twice a week in addition to class in order to help students out. He really cares about students and focuses on mastery of course outcomes.

Dr. Jones is an amazing professor. I have had him for both thermodynamics and heat transfer and currently conduct research with him. He is incredibly bright and helps you learn so much about effective uses of time. He has high expectations for mastery of course outcomes. Anybody who genuinely wants to learn should get to know Dr. Jones.

I have had many horrible professors but Jones is the absolute worst. His classes are a waste of time. He talks about being an influential engineer and what that means more than the actual material. Then when he talks about material, he goes over very trivial details and expects you to learn everything in the book by yourself.

This class is seriously hard. The tests are times, four questions, impossibly difficult. Up until the final, however, everyone has a shot at an A! He really just cares about learning and being able to see that you've learned throughout the course. I've never had an ME professor who cared so much about students and made himself so available to help.

I absolutely loved Dr. Jones class. It was difficult no doubt, but I came away feeling that I had really learned the principles of Thermodynamics, not just that I had done a bunch of book problems all semester with all the knowledge to be forgotten after the final. This class will teach you, and if you like learning you will love Doctor Jones.

Dr. Jones is probably in the top 5 best teachers I've ever had. He really helped me learn the material by teaching me how to approach a problem. He really changed the way I thought about school. He has tough tests, and you need to do all the reading, but all of the work pays off - if you do it.

Dr. Jones cares more about his students learning and becoming influential engineering more that any other professor I've had. His class can be some work, but if you actually want to learn the material then he is your man.

One of my best classes at BYU. Dr. Jones expects a lot in reading and hw (he takes a philosophy of helping you teach yourself - great for visual learners), but if you do the work you can have a very deep understanding of heat transfer. Much of class is just answering questions. Tests are cool - interesting, practical, challenging, fair problems.

Heat Transfer is a beast, but Dr. Jones was a champ. He puts forth a lot of effort to teach it well and he expects you to put forth effort in learning it. He really cares about his students having a solid understanding. Tests were brutal, but they weren't cheap shots. If you want to master heat transfer, Dr. Jones is definitely your guy.

Dr. Jones knows Heat Transfer. It is a difficult subject and a difficult class. The homework is very time consuming. The TA's were very helpful in doing the homework. The exams were hard but were open book and were very fair. Getting a good grade is possible but it is a lot of hard work and time.

I liked the professor and class a lot.  Heat transfer was a difficult subject, but Dr. Jones made himself available to help.  To do well in the class you had to do the reading everyday.  The tests were challenging, but they were also open book.  I feel like I very clearly understand Heat transfer now
Really good at teaching heat transfer, but the work load for the class was well beyond the 3 credit hour status the class has.

Dr. Jones is a terrible teacher.  He doesn't lecture at all.  Classes are a waste of time.  He feels insecure about the material and it is manefist by useless attacks on students.  You would be better off taking heat transfer from a vegetable.  I was interested in heat transfer coming into the class, but Dr. Jones has ruined any interested I had.

I really learned a lot from Dr. Jones.  He expects you to read and try the homework before class and then he just does examples and answers questions all class period.  He is super helpful - he even would come down to where our group was studying and sit with us and help.  Pretty tough class, but excellent teacher.

I took this class back in the winter, and it was hands down my favorite class I have ever taken at BYU. Dr. Seeley cares so much about his students and their learning. He also cares a lot about their spiritual growth as well. Put in the work, and this class will help you grow so much. Overall, such a wholesome class.

I've never disliked any of my professors in my four years of college until now. I felt like I was constantly trying to read his mind, and his tests, which are all free response, make you lose points for the most ridiculous reasons, things that weren't even asked for in the question. I could've done better with a different professor and so can you

Dr. Seeley was great! He really knows his stuff and makes you think. Tests are fully free response which is tough, but if you understand his grading criteria and expectations you should do great. The content was super interesting and relevant in everyday life. The final is worth 35% of your grade so get ready for that.

I love Dr. Seeley. If you have a solid background of anatomy and basic physics, you'll do just fine. He really cares about each of his students and you take so much more out of the class than biomechanics. I'd take another class from him in a heartbeat.

He has probably been my favorite Professor to this point.  Most of the exams questions are pretty similar to the problems we did in class, so if you pay attention in class you should do well, but they are free response questions. He cares about the students more almost any other professor, and is more concerned with our success instead of grades.

You need to go to lecture if you want to do well in this class. That's where he gives all his info, learning suite doesn't have all of it. He REALLY cares about his students. Best teacher I've ever had at BYU! There's a group project and lots of scientific articles you're assigned to read as well

Might be my favorite professor I've ever had. He realizes there are things more important than grades, and just likes to talk to us. Intentionally assigns things he thinks are beneficial, in and of class. He gets to know everyone by name, and is very friendly and fun. Sometimes class isn't structured super well, and maybe not the best at test prep.

Prof Seeley was a great guy, and super interesting. He was easy to get in contact with, and eager to help. The grade was just weekly readings, a few group projects, and tests, the latter affected your grade heavily. Although he says not to worry about grading, he is a tough grader, and wants specific answers. The tests were all free response.

Dr. Seeley is a wonderful man and will help you connect the dots between what is taught and how to apply it. This class is hard because the tests are all free response and challenging. What you take away from the class is very useful, but if you need to pad your GPA, then dont risk it. Regardless, youll make a good friend with him!

The class was okay but I wouldn't recommend. Know physics 105 well. He also talks about his research and makes you read his publications which I found annoying. Didn't learn as much as I would have liked and you don't have much control of your grade to due the free response tests.

Best Professor at BYU in my opinion, his class is interesting and engaging, and his test are actually very representative of what you learn in class. Not just multiple choice, but short answer. Willing to work with you, wants everyone to succeed.
Take this class from a different teacher. He doesn't teach you and the class is not set up to succeed.

Absolutely amazing professor! His tests are all short answer but really easy if you generally understand the concepts with a few physics problems. Reviewing his posted slides made the tests simple. He really wants to help anyone that asks. He offers occasional extra credit that's enough to make a difference. Having taken physics is also a big help.

If you have not taken physics do not attempt this class. Professor Seeley does not explain anything and his TA might as well taught the class. Blake is a way better teacher and should probably be teaching the class. There are no practice questions and have fun with all fill in the blank tests. Take it from another teacher trust me.

Prof. Seeley is by far one of the best professors I've had at this school. He cares for his students a lot and is a great resource to talk to about anything. His lectures are great and the content isn't too hard if you've taken Phscs 105. The tests are fair and straightforward and often gives you free test questions in class. Overall a great guy!

His class is probably my favorite at the moment. The lectures are interesting, and you can tell he actually cares about what he talks about. The grading on quizzes can be kind of tough at first, but once you figure out what it is he wants you to write, it gets way easier. He is really nice and helpful!

Dr. Seeley is one of my favorite professors at BYU.  He is clear and fair with what he tests you on, and frankly if you have taken physics his class is really easy.  He cares a lot about his students.  Take from him!

Dr. Seeley is a great professor. Class discussions helped me better understand the concepts of the course. Out of class reading assignments are not long, but are important for class discussions and tests. Tests are much more conceptual than mathematical, and all free response, which I found refreshing. I would take another class from Dr. Seeley!

Dr Seeley is by far the most personable and willing-to-help professors that I have had an interaction with at BYU.  He understands that his class shouldn't take up the majority of your life.  He is very clear about expectations, he is funny, and his tests are easy if you come to class and work through the practice problems that he does with you.

Awesome professor! He won't test you on anything that he doesn't talk about in class so take good notes and do practice problems to get a good grade. He is very personal and strives to get to know each student individually. Take the time to get to know him and utilize his office hours... He's great!

Dr. Seeley is my favorite instructor I have had at BYU.  His class made me want to get a graduate degree in biomechanics.  His class is extremely fair and the test are super representative of what you have actually learned.  Watch out, because there is no regular required homework, but if you don't do practice problems on your own you may struggle.

Great professor. He is very willing to help. There isn't a lot of homework. The first test was rough because I didn't know what to expect. Go back and see tests, use office hours, he is great at helping where needed.   For sure recommend him!

Dr. Seeley is great! Utilize his office hours- he is very willing to help.  Your class notes/online chapter outlines are your best resource for the tests. Class was very discussion oriented, and interesting. Take your drafts to him for the group project before its due and he'll give you some good pointers.

Doesn't care all that much about his students success. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HUNTER! If you have to take it from Seeley, don't listen to what he says about whats on the test. If he says not to worry about something, worry about it. Unless you get like an 88% or higher on his first test your chances of an A are shot.

One of my favorite teachers at BYU! More interested in helping students than anything else. Gives plenty of opportunities to go see him, and his classes are really good! Learn a lot and have a good time, makes the material more interesting! A physics background would make the material easier
Great teacher.

Seeley is very responsive to students. His grade breakdown is 20% midterm 1, 20% midterm 2, 20%  final, 20% "assignments" and 20% group project which he will proofread for you. The tests can be difficult especially without PHYS 105. However, the assigments are easy, and everyone can get 100% on them which really boost your grade.

Great guy! Physics 105 will make this class much easier! He is very nice, learns your name, always looking for ways to improve his teaching. He really cares about his students! Everyone else pretty much covered it.

Good professor and helpful.  The tests are not a good measure of your learning.  They are usually just 30 MC questions, and if you don't do well there is no way to salvage your grade with any other assignments.  Take PHSCS first and you should be alright.  He's a very nice, good professor otherwise.

I think Dr. Seeley was a great professor, no real assignments so if you don't do well of the tests, you pretty messed up. He was sometimes pretty confusing, but as long as you have guts enough to point it out to him, he'll clarify. Should take Physics 105/107 first. Not a really easy class, but an A is really achievable
GREAT teacher!  He really wants you to learn and is always willing to help you outside of class.  He's funny too.
Dr. Seeley is AWESOME!  He actually cares about his students and wants you to succeed.  He is humble guy and still loves to learn.  Great class!  Great guy!  You will love Dr. Seeley!
No Comments

SINGLE GREATEST CLASS + PROFESSOR EVER. 
He explores spirituality deeply in class. Love poetry, writing literary analysis, and want to develop your capacity to understand the spirit? Class is for you. Prepare to receive real feedback on essays. He's incredibly loving and meets with students individually during the class when class size is small.

This class is very light on assignments, though the ones he does give you are very dense. There is a lot of arbitrariness to his grading style, as what you wrote about from the reading isn't what he sees in the poem. The lectures are very engaging, and his insights will blow your mind, though they often feel more suited to a Sunday School lesson.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had (Senior), he definitely pushed me to be better, but was fair and very responsive with feedback. He tailored his class to his students and seemed invested in each of our success. Actively hunting to take another class from him!

By far my favorite BYU professor. Absolutely brilliant. Definitely requires investment in the class though. I didn't mind because the class is just so interesting and he's a very engaging speaker. Take Wickman if you want to think a lot.

Only take Doctor Wickman if you want to learn how to both read and write art, with countless revelations. Classmates have complained about Wickman's tough grading; but paired with his detailed and passionate feedback on each assignment, I believe my peers are only complaining about their inability to write well and the effort they have to put in.

once I found my groove in this class I was very grateful for the simple setup. Because there were so many readings, we very rarely had other assignments besides just doing the readings. His perspective is great for any struggling with the gospel. Also lets you redo any big assignment and will pretty much give you an A just for reattempting.

Professor Wickman is a really tough grader. When grading your essays, you might get docked points if your opinions are different from his. His corrections are not always of your writing or analytical skills and according to feedback from the writing center, many of his corrections are actually just wrong. He is nice but is unfairly strict.

I was a student of Professor Wickman when he first came to BYU. I was stumbled on this and thought I'd throw in my two cents. He's brilliant and will stretch your intellect. I went to law school and credit the rigor of his courses with my performance on the LSAT and my success in law school. He's not easy, but neither is anything post-grad!

I have to say I'm very surprised with all the other ratings I've seen so far. Yes, Professor Wickman is intelligent, but not in a  way that necessarily helped me learn.  He's the type of professor for those quirkyethereal types (you know who I'm talking about). Listening to his lecture is kind of like reading an esoteric critical theory paper.

Dr. Wickman is brilliant. He opened my mind and made me stretch my thinking. I quickly learned that a good paper gets a B and a great paper merits an A. However, rather than being a frustration, this quality made me push myself and I got SO much out of the class. If you work hard, you can get an A and you will be glad you put so much in!!!

Hardest professor I have ever had, but also the most thought-provoking. Brilliant man. Had my mind blown every single class period. The only thing I can complain about is that the readings were very long and often above our reading level. Assigned reading was a chore, but lecture brought the ideas to life in a fantastic way.

Brilliant. Most likely, you will feel extremely intimidated throughout much of the course, and worried that you will not likewise be brilliant enough in your work. But, after it all, he is very helpful, and I learned so much. You will come out a better writer, and have better critical thinking skills. I hope to take another class from him.

One of the most dynamic and engaging professors I've ever had. His philosophical insights and level of analysis blew my mind daily, and changed forever the level of critical thinking I aspire to in writing and engaging with texts. Difficult but fair grader. Take a class from him!

INTENSE. He is brilliant&moves at a rapid-fire pace. Starting out, I struggled bc I thought he was pretty elitist&he's a tough grader. But I came to really like him&learned a ton. Don't turn in anything less than brilliant originality on your papers or he will destroy you. Not for the faint of heart or those with only a cursory interest in lit.

Like others have said: he is an absolutely brilliant professor. The way he analyzes the literature... would take me years to come up with such analysis. While I know that many of my classmates felt daunted by his obviously surpassing knowledge, I really did not find the class unreasonable or too difficult. I, without a doubt, recommend him.

Prof. Wickman is the most dynamic lecturer I've ever had a class from.  He challenges you to not just read literary theory, but to engage with it.  He is also very helpful with your research and writing, and provides lots of chances for feedback and revisions.  Because he's active in research, the class deals with current and not outdated questions

Lectures are very information-dense; I'm a fast typer who takes notes on a computer and had trouble getting everything.  Pretty interesting.  He was team-teaching the course with two other professors, and I don't think I enjoyed his unit quite as much as I enjoyed the other two.

My favorite professor so far, and my favorite class this semester.  The class is demanding but not overwhelming.  Grade based on three essays, one beastly research paper, and reading quizzes.  Do the reading, pay attention, work hard and you can do well.  Lectures super interesting and Wickman is hilarious.  Take him!

Just as everyone has already said, Prof Wickman is brilliant and creates a dynamic environment in the classroom; however, it's a hard class. We had three short essays, one research paper, and daily quizzes. The text book was difficult to read. Also, the class is sort of a combination of hard-core literary theory and Scot lit.

Dr. Wickma is VERY hard, brilliant, and amazing if you're looking for a class where you'll learn more in a semester than other professors might teach in two years.  No surprises from him; lots of changes to keep improving.  Everyone should take at least one class from Professor Wickman.

Very dynamic, interesting lectures make all of Professor Wickman's classes entertaining--however, make sure you're taking notes, not just laughing!  Make sure you actually know the material--the tests will be difficult.

One of the best classes I've ever taken.  Professor Wickman is brilliant.  He helps the class make connections we'd never make on our own.  Absolutely student friendly.  Fair grader.  I learned more in this class than probably any other, not just about literature, but about how to think.

One of the best classes I have ever taken.  Lectures (discussions) are really intense--make sure you're good at taking notes!  Fair grader, very liberal revision policy.  Not a class for the faint of heart, though: our grade was based solely on essays, and there's no way possible to BS your way through them.  Pay attention, work hard, learn a ton.

Incredibly well-formatted class. I loved Dr. Properzi and learned so much from him, but it's true that his tests are tough and his attendance policy is very strict. He is a little eccentric in his preferences (eg: no taking notes on a laptop) and not as warm as some religion professors are, but incredibly educated and experienced.

You can really tell that Prof Properzi is really passionate about this class. That being said, I think the only way I got an A in this class was through divine intervention. Tests are purely memorization of random facts and the amount of work he assigns is kinda wild for a 2 credit class. I loved this class but I also love that it's over now.

Brother Properzi is a great professor. He definitely knows what he is talking about. There's a lot of information, but if you listen and try to understand, you'll be fine. You can tell he is passionate about what he is teaching, and he wants you to succeed! He sometimes goes on long tangents, and it's easy to get lost in the sauce, but that's all.

Choose another professor. I think I'm a good student (dean's list, etc.), and I thought I would be fine when he said his class is hard. I was wrong. Anticipate 30 pages of reading and two hard quizzes a week (which others cheated on). Attendance strict, lectures boring. Average midterm/final was 80%. I've heard other professors are better/easier.

Tests are way too intense for a 2 credit religion. He's a smart guy, but he needs to realize his class is unforgiving. It kinda seems like he wants students to not do well. His attendance policy is super strict. He's a nice guy and has some cool assignments but the tests and attendance policy is cause enough to try for any other professor first.

If you're not gonna make this 2 credit class your top priority, it's gonna suck. The reading is redundant, the tests are overly difficult (80% avg), the attendance policy is strict for you to watch him read slides. Nothing about this class was fun/enlightening. Tests were just memorizing foreign words for specific religions, not worth it!

Lowest grade ever. He's a nice enough guy but your GPA will tank if you don't treat this as your most important class. Hardest attendance policy (can only miss 2 classes) and you need to memorize the slides if you want to do well on the tests. His favorite type of question is "which of the following statements is false" You've been warned lol.

Little allowance of online notetaking. Long textbook readings with potentially easy to miss answers. Quizes on readings timed 5 mins, only 4 questions. Lectures were well formatted but were the only place for necessary info. Limited options for extra credit. Great teacher, but could get boring sometimes imo. Should have a decent time.
Tests aren't easy and lectures are a bit bland, but he gives you everything you need in the slides. He really knows his stuff. Take good notes and study them before the tests and you'll be fine.
Great teacher, hard class, you'll be fine.

Brother Properzi is very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter. He likes to keep to a schedule, but he's also very open to questions and class discussion, as long as it doesn't derail the lesson topic. I appreciated his lectures and course content, as it helped me understand many trends in greater Christianity.

If you want a class that gives you an easy A, don't take this class, but if you want to be spiritually and intellectually challenged this is the class for you. Brother Properzi is very passionate about teaching his students the world's different cultures and religions, which is reflected in his lectures, I would definitely take the class again.

I got 90% on both of the exams and still somehow ended up with only a B+. That just tells you how unfair his grading is. He has the strictest attendance policy I have ever experienced at BYU. You can only miss TWICE, which is ridiculous. The reading is pointless and has absolutely nothing to do with the lectures or exams. Crazy 2 credit course.

Properzi wasn't a terrible teacher but his lectures can be quite dull. He also has the worlds strictest attendance policy (only allowing two absences for the whole semester). He also take pride in making tests very hard. There is a quiz on each reading we do.

Dr. Properzi is so kind and has a super strong testimony that is inspiring! His knowledge of world religions offers such a great perspective that you don't often get at BYU. His tests can be a bit tricky but won't tank your grade. The religion department has certain requirements for all classes so you won't find an easy class, but his is great!
Great Professor, one of my favorites.

Dr. Properzi is a very interesting teacher, but he is very strict about attendance, only allowing 2 absences for the whole semester. His tests are confusing and often phrased in a way that is unnecessarily tricky. He is very knowledgeable and I enjoyed learning about Christian history from him.

Punishing attendance policy (5 absences and you automatically fail the class). Test questions are specifically designed to trip you up. I attended every class, took notes, & studied for 5 hours and barely got a B- on the midterm. For a 2 credit class, absolutely punishing. Lecture quite boring. Could be taught in a more interesting way.

Professor Properzi is a really great person. What I loved the most was his ability to relate the things we learned in the Old Testament to our own lives. He just makes you want to be a better person and makes you feel like you can. Take a class from him.

Dr. Properzi is a great person, but his lectures got kind of boring sometimes, which made it hard to take notes in class and do well on tests. Attendance is required and you can only miss class twice before it starts really hurting your grade, so that's tough. The material of this class is interesting, I just wish the lectures were more engaging.

Attendance is MANDATORY, and he doesn't put it in until the end of the semester. Lectures are lengthy and dry. I'm sure he's a nice guy but I definitely didn't enjoy the class and wouldn't take it again, PLEASE find a different class for your religion credit.

The most self-centered teacher I've ever had at BYU. Day 1 he says that he predicts 25-30% of the class would drop because he makes it seem hard. And it is. 12+ pages of reading 2x per week for a quiz that's 3 MINUTES LONG. And it's actually closed note. THE TESTS ARE SUPER CONFUSING AND SPECIFIC. I studied for 8 hrs for the midterm and got a C.

Reading quizzes are open note, but 3 minutes. THAT'S NOTHING. I honestly don't know how people do okay on them cause I can't even pay attention to the book it is so boring. The class has interesting content but can also be so boring. A lot of work surprisingly for a 3 credit class.

I loved this class. I learned so many things about a topic that I didn't know well. Professor Properzi teaches very well and obviously loves the subjects he teaches. Don't get me wrong, it is a difficult class and you need to do the readings and pay attention, but that makes sense due to the high demand and unique subject matter of the class.

Professor Properzi isn't very entertaining--however, I can tell he cares about the subject and genuinely wants his students to succeed. I enjoyed the class itself but that might just be because the subject interests me rather than the way it was taught. My advice is to do all the extra credit and make sure to study the powerpoints.

The class itself was fine, just be warned that reading quizzes are timed (3-5 minutes) and there's no study guide for the exams, so take really good notes and pay attention in lectures (even though they're a bit dull)

This was by far one of the hardest classes I've taken at BYU which is really sad considering it is a 2 credit religion class. The TA's and Professor are not understanding and could care less about your grade even when you reach out ahead of time for help. There is a lot of reading that you have to know top to bottom for difficult 3-5 min quizzes

This class was way too difficult for a 2 credit class. Quizzes are timed 3-5 minutes which is absolutely ridiculous and he gave no help for tests and was completely complacent about having a high C average on the midterms. Would not recommend this class at all. Not worth it
Dr. Properzi is a good person. Even though his lectures can be a bit dull at times, he truly cares about his students and is passionate about what he is teaching.

Quizzes are timed, 3-5 minutes for each quiz. He expects you to take notes on everything in class even the stuff on the slides. As far as tests go, the average is about a 78-82 which is just wrong for a religion class at BYU. I would recommend any other religion class over this one.

The subject matter is interesting but lectures can often be dull. The reading quizzes give you either a 3 minute of 5 minute time limit, which is a ridiculously short amount of time and is very frustrating. There are a lot of assignments, tests, and quizzes for a 2 credit religion class and the Professor and TA's aren't very understanding.

Professor Properzi is a great person. However, his class was the really lecture heavy and he doesn't help you prepare for the exams. The quizzes are timed, between 3-5 min, and it kills your grade if you aren't fast on your feet. I would not take his class again.

Brother Properzi is absolutely amazing. He has such a soft and tender spirit about him. He loves his students and knows a good balance of making the students work for the grade, but being understanding as well. Don't underestimate his abilities, he's incredible.

I freaking love Dr. Properzi! He is super down to earth and I appreciated his willingness to listen to students. He really cares about what students are getting out of his class and it shows. The workload was light especially for this class being 3 credit hours. I have no complaints with this class!

This was my favorite class this semester and Prof. Properzi was a big part of that! The class was engaging, interactive, and incredibly insightful. You can tell he is passionate about the subject and that makes you love it even more. There is a lot of reading, but it's definitely manageable. I highly recommend this class!

I absolutely loved this class. It is very eye opening about many parts of the world. He makes it so members of the church can see truth in every religion. It can be challenging because most of the information will be new. Missed points on daily quizzes will add up quickly, but if you study the chapter well before (about 10 pages) you'll be fine!

I loved this class and think everyone should take it. Properzi cares about his students and is available outside of class. You have to put in the work for a good grade but it is worth it. Quizzes and reading every day and papers due periodically. Properzi helps his students have an appreciation for all religions. Very interesting. I learned tons!

This is an interesting class and it fulfills a global awareness and religion credit, so it's worth it! It's hard because it's a lot of information you're not naturally familiar with, and there are quite a few papers and projects. Properzi is super cool and he relies a lot on student participation, which is part of the grade. An awesome class!

The course material was fascinating, and felt like a unique combination of philosophy, history and religion. He is super organized. The tests were difficult, but his extra credit opportunities made up for it. Difficult for a religion class, but worth it if it's interesting to you. Do the readings, and show up to class every day to get an A.

He is so intelligent! I could feel that he respected the other religions. You have to read the textbook because there is a daily quiz in class on the readings. There was an overwhelming amount of info in the readings. If you do the assignments, go to class, complete the assignments (really easy BTW), and study for the exams, you will get an A.

The readings really aren't bad (max 10ish short pages per class period) and if you do the readings, go to class and actually study for exams, then you'll easily do well. His class is very structured, reasonable and predictable, which I appreciated. He is very sympathetic/respectful towards and knowledgeable of all of the religions he teaches about.

Professor Properzi really helped me to appreciate other religions. He also cares about you as a student and knows you by name. Do all the readings, follow his study guides, and review for the quiz given every class. I didn't think I would end up with a good grade but the extra credit helped a lot.

This class takes hard work. The tests are explicitly over the powerpoints, but you have to do reading out of the textbook for quizzes that are during the first five minutes of class, so don't be late! It's very interesting and he explained things pretty well.

all the reading is for quizes, which make or break the grade, his lectures are completely different which makes up the tests... Lots of study, reading, and writing, with big assignments mixed in. Take it if you want the dual credit for global awareness, but it will be tough. I didn't feel very connected to the religions we studied

Relatively easy for a 300 level class. Loved the subject matter, but didn't love the teacher. Seemed impersonal and at times quite boring. There is a lot of reading required, but if religion interests you, I recommend taking this class. Tests and papers are fairly easy.

Bro Properzi was a fine teacher. The course material is really what kept me going in this class. If World Religions wasn't so interesting then I probably would have hated the class. There is TONS of reading. And the quizzes are hard and the exams are extremely hard. Would probably had a better time with a different teacher.

Bro. Properzi is awesome, he keeps it interesting and really wants to get to know each student. As long as you go to class and do the readings it's not too difficult. He really cares about creating real experiences outside the textbook, so we were required to attend a worship service which was awesome. I'd recommend this class to anyone.

Mauro is an awesome professor. He is very knowledgeable and gives great lectures. Be aware however that he intends for you to earn your A. If you take this class do the reading and know what you have read. That being said he has a great class.

This class was absolutely amazing in terms of content learned, and Bro. Properzi is an excellent professor and has it organized in an excellent fashion. Beware, though: this class is not easy. There are multiple short papers and the reading is intense. But, if you're genuinely interested in the content, the course is an absolute joy!

He makes you read the textbook before class. Reading quizzes are a large portion of the grade. There are a few, kinda large assignments, but they're not too hard, mostly reflection. Lectures are always engaging and insightful. He opened my eyes to the world.

Most work I've ever had for a 2 credit religion course, it was a little ridiculous. I found lectures pretty dry and boring, but he is very knowledgable if this stuff interests you. If you are looking for an easy religion class steer clear. If you do take it, you will learn a lot.

Professor Properzi is incredibly inspiring. I took this class because I needed a unique spin on religion classes, and this one was great. The subject material was fascinating, but Professor Properzi always added an extra level of insight and really helped me think deeply about my beliefs. Tests are fair and homework is one reading a day with a quiz

Brother Properzi is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. World Religions as a class covers a lot of material which makes it difficult on its own, however, Properzi is clear with what he expects, insightful with the material and incredible helpful as a professor.

Reading the assignments is incredibly important. Everyday in class he starts with a 5 question quiz based of random facts in the reading. Skipping class will kill your grade, but the lectures are interesting so its worth going. Tests are a little hard.

Great, great teacher. Openminded on a variety of religions and shows you how to find beauty in religions that you might not believe in your self. Not gonna lie: this is a hard class (as all good college courses are). But if you actually want to learn and feel spiritual in a religions class at the same time, this is it.

He is quite objective in his lectures. He is really knowledgable about the subject and very willing to answer all questions and help prepare for tests. Quizes can be tough - impossible to pass if you don't read all of the readings before class.

This class, while interesting enough, is a ton of work. Between 20-40 pages of textbook reading for every class, with minutiae quizzes so that you really need to read all of it. You'd better be well prepared for the final. Also he's pretty strict on policy and doesn't give a lot of leeway if you miss a deadline, even if it is for a good reason.

This was by far THE best religion credit I have taken at BYU. He's a very organized professor and tells you exactly what will be on the test. There is a lot of readings and outside work, but it's usually interesting on a level beyond just getting the grade. The text book is extremely important as his quizzes are based upon it. Take world religions!
Professor Properzi is strict but organized. His lectures are engaging and the reading is interesting. The quizzes every class and the number of assignments for a 2 credit class did get old though.

Really enjoyed his class.  Tests are straight forward and is always willing to answer questions. Reading quiz for every class, it can be tough but if you complete all of the other assignments it is really not a big deal.  He offers 20 points of extra credit. Would definitely take another class form him.
Great guy. Takes an active interest in students and their learning. Expansive knowledge of his subject matter.

What a great guy. Bro. Properzi is very knowledgeable and I learned so much from him. Attendance is mandatory and there is quite a bit of reading and other assignments to do. A lot of work for a  2 credit class, but definitely worth it. My favorite class so far at BYU!

The class was actually my favorite of this semester. Readings are mandatory if you want to do well but if you do them, you will pass the weekly quizzes. And the test, he takes straight from class power points that he gives you access to for studying.

Professor Properzi really knows his stuff.  He has tons of awesome experience and that really shows.  He makes it seem like the class is going to be super hard, but as long as you do the reading and go to class it's pretty easy.  The tests and quizzes are super simple.  If you want an easy A, this is not for you, but if you want to learn, take it!

I almost didn't take this class. SO GLAD I DID! It's fascinating, useful information. I understand myself & those of other faiths better. Highly recommend to all. Prof Properzi is upfront about what you have to do to succeed in class. Do what he says and you'll be fine. He's a fun guy, knows his stuff, & asks great questions for class discussion.

Brother Properzi is my absolute favorite religion professor at BYU. I've taken both 351 and 352 from him, and I've learned more in these classes than I have in any other religion course. I would highly recommend both of his classes. The classes require a little more work, but the reward is well worth it.
He is just quite dull. He is not an entertaining lecturer. I just wasnt captured by what he was teaching and it made it really painful to study and learn.

Brother Properzi is an excellent professor.  I loved his lectures!  As long as you do the reading, you will ace the Quizzes - which are a significant portion of your grade.  He is hard, but fair.  Lots of opportunities to earn extra points which is helpful since tests are difficult.  Awesome class!

Brother Properzi is my favorite professor thus far!  He is hard but fair. I loved his lectures!   This is a very interesting class.  You will learn to appreciate other religions. I would love to take more classes from him.  Very, very good!

Prof. Properzi knows his stuff and he asks very interesting questions that make you think.  The class is challenging but very fair.  If you do the reading quizzes are easy and when I went to his office with questions he was very helpful and kind.  You will learn to appreciate other religions
This class was difficult to understand and the professor wasn't very helpful when I had questions. There was a quiz every day and no matter how hard I studied for it, I always got a low score.

Brother Properzi knows his material and you can tell he is passionate about his topic. However, too much talking from his part takes place. Not too much correlation with the reading you do on the book, besides the daily quizzes. If you are not too interested in WOrld Religions I would suggest other classes.
Professor Properzi is the best professor at byu. This was the best class I've ever taken from the religion department. The test are not hard at all if you use the study guide

If you follow the syllabus and do all of the assignments, an A in this class is not out of reach.  Properzi's lectures are nothing out of the ordinary, but they aren't horrible either.  He is a kind and caring professor who is willing to give you the help you need.  For the tests, follow the study guide exactly and you should be fine.

I learned so much from this class. I suggest that you do the readings before class because then, you will be able to get good grades on the quiz and the tests. The study guide helps you a lot on the tests tho.
Great class! Quite a lot of work for one credit, but I learned a lot.

He was a great professor and the class was fascinating, but Islam and the Gospel was a lot more work than any other 2 credit religion course I've ever taken. It wasn't like he made it ridiculously hard, there's just a lot of material to cover. THis should definitely be a 2-3 credit class. But like I said, it was worth it because he was awesome.

Professor Properzi is an excellent professor who REALLY knows his stuff. Considering the fact that our class only met once a week, he was able to very clearly and effectively teach us a lot in a very short amount of time. Very kind and helpful professor, and I really hope to get another one of his classes again.

Dr. Properzi was very organized.  Everything that happened in the class was indicated in the syllabus.  He is not out to trick the students.  Read the syllabus, do the readings before class for the quiz, and take advantage of the extra credit opportunities and you will be fine.

Brother Properzi is a really good teacher.  The class was very interesting and he taught it well.  As long as you keep up with the reading you will do well on the quizzes, and the study guide prepares you for exactly what's on the test.  The class was easy as long as you do the reading.

Best class ever. It completely changed my perspective and feelings about the religion of Islam. There's an easy 4 question quiz for each class that covers the assigned readings and four additional assignments through the block that are simple. The only test is the final and it's a piece of cake. I got 356/360 points in the class and I  hardly tried
