Dr. Properzi is a great professor. His assignments and tests were not difficult if you put in some effort. He went into depth and taught with clarity.
The class is straightforward, the study guide is the key to succeeding on the tests, and going to class is absolutely essential.

His lectures are super interesting and he starts really good class discussions. He takes himself pretty seriously though and his tests are kind of hard. Attendance is mandatory and he doesn't like it when people talk in class.

Great class.  You actually learn things about church history instead of the watered down Sunday School version (and this is the perfect environment to do such things).  Not only is he clear, honest and thoughtful about Church history, he makes it something that you can learn from.
Awesome class and competent, though-provoking professor. Really useful background knowledge to better relate with people of other faiths.

Dr. Properzi is a very nice professor.  His class felt a lot like Sunday school-he encourages discussion within his class.  Daily work is simple--either a scripture journal or reading a book.  He gives you a study guide for tests.  However, you have to attend class to do well b/c his powerpoints aren't super useful!

The professor's class was interesting and informative. While the class was not an easy A, a good grade is easily possible with the proper effort. I learned a lot from this class and would take this class from him in a heart beart.

Great class! Very interesting and well-taught. A lot of info and a # of assignments, so it will keep you busy, but worth it. Great lectures; good powerpoints; you'll learn a lot and keep interested. An "A" is very doable if you put in the work; short papers and quizzes help spread the grade from just tests only. Awesome study guides for tests!

You should take a class from this guy if you have the chance, he's a great professor.  Class was truly  interesting and left me with a better understanding and appreciation of Islam.  Workload: read ch b4 class + take quiz (not too bad, drops some too), some 500word papers and a final.  If you go to class and do the assignments an A isn't hard
Great teacher! If you want a teacher that will really teach you, he's your man.

Very interesting class. At first I was very excited to study the material but as time passed and as my attention decreased, I started to get somewhat frustrated with the daily reading quizzes. The class takes time. But if you enjoy it, you will be fine. Don't take if you want an easy A.  Properzi is awesome! You will enjoy him.

Go to class. Do the reading before class for the quizzes that are every class. Very detailed study guides can help you get an A if you work for it. Not easy, but an A is entirely possible if you give the effort.
Very interesting and fairly challenging (you have to memorize what each section is about), but not particularly spiritual.

Dr. Properzi was a blast to learn with. He provides a great insight into the D&C but I felt that almost everything we learned was relevant to me and my study of the scriptures. A great pick for a D&C class!

Very organized and detailed in his explanations. Quizzes are easy and come straight from the readings. Readings are generally short (3-5 pages) but he's hoping to switch to a new textbook in Fall 2012 so that may change. There are 2 tests, which are difficult but not brutal by any means. Fill out the study guide, study, and it'll be an easy class.

Great teacher. He really makes you think about the scriptures and takes things deeper than expected. He is really knowledgeable and does not shy away from the tough questions that relate to our religion.

He opens up your mind to the truth you find in all religions.  Hard work but all worth it...he gives you a detailed study guide for the exams and curves them.  Expects college level writing but willing to help and answer all your questions.  Very knowledgeable and approachable.  It's a 3 credit class in every way but will never regret taking it.

Professor doesn't teach.  You have reading assignments and videos. After you are quizzed on the reading/videos he pontificates about the subjects.  He grades more like a English professor.  Grammar is too important to him. Very knowledgeable. His tests are HORRID.  His questions use uncommon language.  The questions ask about useless details.

Enjoyed this class.  Only 1 credit hour, so I think that's a challenge to the prof, but I feel Dr. Properzi did great with this.  I thought everything we did with the class, readings and assignments, were worthwhile, interesting, and did not count as busy work.  Book isn't boring.  I think I really learned a lot.  Definitely recommend.

His powerpoints are mundane. You must attend class to get points for the quizzes! He has no idea what are on his tests and is no help if you ask for clarification from the study guide or help on the daily quizzes. Information was very interesting, but the way he presented it made it very boring.

This Professor's a good one to go with this class. Powerpoint lectures each class that are clear and easy to understand. Reading assignment between each class (not too long, 10-20 pages, small book) for a quiz given each class. Test was straight forward, study guide to help. He teaches the class really clearly and really well. I'd suggest him.
Greatttt class. Greattt professorr!!

Great class! Not that hard contrary to what the previous person said.  He gives a very detailed study-guide for the exam and curves the grade.  He said on the first day that being a 3 credit class it is the hardest religion class but he still manages to make it enjoyable.  He always answered my emails within an hour, never had that from any prof
You think the class is easy, but then the you take the test.. They are very detail-oriented and quote "tests from Hell."
Excellent course.  gives a good overview of Islam.  Professor knows a lot, and has some really interesting experiences, ask about the Vatican.  Italian Professor, speaks perfect English.
He was a great professor, and he was very knowledgeable about the material. His passion for the material made class always very interesting.

Overall, I really enjoyed this class. Dr. Properzi is a great teacher who really loves Islam.  I learned a lot.  If you just do the assigned reading (which isn't too much) the class isn't too difficult.

This was a great class!  It was really interesting, I learned a ton, and Professor Properzi was always very prepared for class.  I really appreciated how well-organized the class was because it was always very clear what was expected of us and it was a very even work-load throughout the block.  There are also no exams except for the final.

This was a really informative class - walking in knowing almost nothing about the Islamic faith, I feel like I have a good understanding of the basics now.  Dr. Properzi did a masterful job showing what the real belief system is behind Islam and the Qur'an.

I think this was a really interesting class, more of a focus on, Islam rather than Islam and the gospel, though some out of class papers focused more on that. He did a good job of teaching in different ways. He uses power points, but there were also some good class discussions and interesting videos. Do the reading, go to class, and you'll be fine.

I took Brother Properzi's World Religions class. I LOVED IT SO MUCH! I learned a lot. All of the assignments we had were valuable to learning. He is willing to answer any question you have, and he is knowledgeable. You need to do your readings to do good on the quizzes. Tests are easy if you follow the study guide. I loved Brother Properzi's class!

I really loved this class and I learned a lot. Brother Properzi is an excellent teacher and isn't afraid to tackle the hard questions.  He knows how to lead a good class discussion. His tests are not difficult if you do your reading and follow his study guide. I would highly recommend D&C with Brother Properzi.

Great class! You have 2 midterms and a final, and the study guides for them are directly related to the questions he is going to ask. He has an extensive religious studies background so he teaches not just the doctrine but also the reasons behind things. Definitely recommend taking the class from him. I got an A, and didn't have to do a lot.

Professor Properzi was a lot of fun.  He doesn't shy away from difficult questions that he is asked, and he will bring up topics that many other people refuse to touch.  I really enjoyed our discussions in class and everything that I learned--some from new insights and viewpoints he brought in and others that I just hadn't known before.

Good lectures, good information. I think everyone should have one of his classes at least once. Talks about as many controversial subjects as he can. Tests are hard though, really need to study very well. Assignments aren't too bad though.

I gained a much greater awareness of admirable and diverse religions in this class. Moreover, I was able to use the knowledge that I gained in this class to ace a lot of my exams in other classes, and now whenever I come across someone of another religion, I can discuss their religion with them without feeling ignorant or uneducated.

Great class and if you want an A it is clearly within your control to get it.  He has passion for what he teaches and is respectful and welcoming of all your comments.  He tries to make you think, is honest about his own perspective as LDS, and overall seeks for the good in all religions.  I would highly recommend this class

Mauro Properzi is one of the best professors I've had through my 4 years of school.  He is so enthusiastic about the course and the material! He teaches it very well, with an excellent balance between the text, experience, class participation, personal projects, and well-written exams.  Phenomenal professor; not afraid to tackle tough questions.

I loved how he taught this class. Very professional, very informative. The class is hard-don't be deceived. If you read, pay attention in class, and try to take an interest in the material, you shouldn't have a problem getting an A. I felt that he was very concerned with my learning the material and even took time outside of class to discuss more
Dr. Properzi is a great professor and definitely wants to help his students understand the material.

I loved this class. Dr. Properzi is very knowledgeable and gave a great perspective on the religions of the world. I would recommend this class to everyone and Dr. Properzi is one of the best professors you can take it from. The test were tough but he gives a great study guide, and curves to the highest grade. Loved that class and the teacher.

Bro. Properzi is a really great teacher. I took his world religions class and it was a really fun class, plus he is so knowledgeable and tries to find the answers to questions he doesn't know. His class wasn't that hard, the homework was only like 4 pages of reading a night, and you don't have to take very many notes; everything is on blackboard.

I have no idea what all these people are saying about this guy. Dr. Propertzi was amazing. His class was not very difficult which was nice because it gave me a chance to freely enjoy the subject material w/o the stress of things. Yeah his tests are hard but there is a huge curve. To those who whine about his tests, try studying.

I took World Religions from Professor Properzi, and it was the best religion class I have taken so far. He covers a lot of detailed material and his tests are not easy, but the study guide for both tests tells you exactly what to study for each question, in order. Don't take his class if you don't want to learn and don't care about world religions.

Professor Properzi is a professional in his own right. He effectively assits students with their concerns and questions with respect and consideration. Dr. Hansen provides many opportunities to succeed. There are plenty of assignments, quizzes, & reflections that can help your grade. The material is a little tricky, but the practice questions after each lecture and study guides are helpful. Her lectures are also fun and interesting to listen to.
Her lectures were good. I did well in the class by watching the lectures, answering the practice questions, and doing the closed and open quizzes.

She has a very clear and effective teaching style. I especially appreciated how organized the class was each week, with lecture material presented in a way that was easy to follow. She also provides practice questions that help students prepare for the quizzes and exams.

I don't usually give professors ratings, but Dr. Hansen deserved it. I took the online version and this is truly the best online class I've ever taken, especially for a course like physiology. Her grading is very straightforward and her lecture aren't full of fluff. She teaches you what you need to know, and her tests are based on exactly that.

Dr. Hansen is a precise, clear teacher. She teaches you what you need to know and expects you to know it come test time. I appreciated her streamlined organization of the online physiology class. Despite the rigor, it was easy to keep track of things and know what was due and when.

Dr. Hansen is really engaging. I appreciated no textbook readings in her online CELL 305 class. Its a 4 credit class so material is heavy but she teaches it very well. The exams aren't as heavy or memorization based. Theres a lot of applying concepts which helped me understood concepts way better. She is a great teacher!

Dr. Hansen creates good, quality videos that are well-organized. With this class, there is a lot of homework and things to do throughout the week, so try to stay on top of everything. The tests are usually pretty fair, but some have questions about things that weren't covered in great detail in the lectures

Dr. Hansen is amazing! She is so funny, caring, knowledgable, and really cares about her students success. Her class is difficult but physiology is just a difficult subject in general because there is so much information to learn. She makes it fun, engaging, and really helps you through the learning process. Great class. Would take again.

Dr. Hansen's passion for the subject is infectious, which makes it quite an interesting class. The class is difficult particularly due to the numerous tests. The variety in assignment types assists in gaining a complex understanding of materials and challenge students to understand how each physiological process impacts each other.

Hard class, mostly due to the tests that were hard to prepare for. Other assignments and essays were straightforward. Lecture videos were interesting but got longer and longer as the semester went on. Dr. Hansen is awesome though, I really enjoyed her perspective on current issues from a scientific perspective.

Beware of how many exams you will take. We took one every 3 weeks, and it was a lot. Sometimes the pacing just felt really rushed, some weeks, and there was barely anything else. Breaks and other things were not accounted for in the online section. Overall, it was a great class and a great professor, but the pacing was just horrendous.

This was my second time taking physiology at BYU, and Dr Hansen taught it in a way that made it both applicable and understandable. You can tell that she is very passionate about the subject, and there are so many opportunities to practice the material. I would recommend this class to anyone who needs/wants to take physiology.

Dr. Hansen was a phenomenal professor! She explained difficult concepts clearly and with a sense of humor, which I really appreciated. The course was very well organized. This class is a lot of work, and I think the only reason I made it through was because of Dr. Hansen.
She was a great lecturer and tries to get us interested about the class. She does quizzes and things to help you prepare for the class. A hard class but she is a good teacher.

Get ready to take good notes. This might be the most well organized online course I've taken so far. Dr. Hansen is passionate about physiology and is invested in your learning. Sometimes it's hard to get a hold of her, but when you do she's extremely responsive. The exams are challenging but doable.

Professor Hansen is very helpful and had very good lectures! All the information was very interesting and the TAs are very helpful. I feel like some of the exam questions were really random and hard to know what exactly to study for without just memorizing the whole lectures. But overall good class!

This class was just ok. There is just a lot of fluff that you have to get through in order to get what really matters. I wish there were more practice problems to know what things the teacher was looking for.

She does an awesome job explaining all of the concepts in her lectures. She makes sure you can understand apply what you learn. She cares a lot about you gaining the most that you can out of this class.

This professor is very knowledgable in this field and conveyed the course material clearly. She is approachable and friendly, and genuinely interested in the success of her students. The material was difficult to learn and memorize, however the instructor provided opportunities for us to review and apply what we learned.

I was a little worried about taking this class online, but I ended up really loving it. Dr. Hansen is a great professor and her passion for physiology makes the lectures interesting and easier to understand. The content itself is really interesting and applicable. The course is test heavy but if you put in consistent time it's really manageable.

Fascinating general physiology class! Heavy at times, but manageable. Lecture videos are usually helpful, and quizzes are fair. Using AI to make practice problems will help you do really well. Four midterms and a final that felt no more difficult than the weekly quizzes. Prepare to put in a lot of time, but expect a good grade for your effort.

If you're taking the online course, there's 2-3 hours of lecture per week prerecorded with subtitles. The exams aren't too bad, but make sure to keep up with videos or you will be swamped. The exams are definitely in detail, way more detail than any of the practice problems, but it's more about remembering all the information than trick questions.
Lectures were helpful and good. Exams were hard.

Dr. Hansen seems like a good person who is passionate about physiology. The class was definitely difficult, and you should expect lots of homework and hours studying if you want to do well. It's a good option if you need to take Physiology online, but the lecture videos were long and content-heavy.

Taking Cell 305 online is a solid option if you need to. Everything you need to know is in the lectures, and while the tests are tough, if you focus on mastering the study objectives, you will do just fine.
No complaints! I would take Dr. Hansen again any day!

Honestly such a fun and interesting course. Professor made the class super interesting and did a good job being clear on expectations. Content is difficult but it is a 4 credit class so it makes sense. I really enjoyed this course.

The content was pretty straight forward. Exams were pretty fair. The lectures were long and Dr Hansen would go off on long tangents that were not useful at all. Some of her personal views were clearly expressed, and she sounded annoyed a lot of the time. She also made some scientifically false claims. Other than that, super easy class

This is a class that you can definitely get a good grade in. The learning objectives are key to knowing what will be on the test and how to score the best grade you can. There is 4 midterms but it didn't seem too overbearing.
Dr. Hansen does a great job and this online class is informative and convenient.

It is a difficult class, made more difficult by the amount of information required for the tests. This class requires a lot more information than your average physiology class. Professor Hansen made the lectures enjoyable.

My biggest gripe with her is that her lectures could be so much more shorter if didn't go off on long tangents in every video. She also made it hard to study for the exams because she does not provide any extra info or reviews. But she does a good job at teaching difficult concepts and the course is decently organized. It's also not super hard.

Dr. Hansen is funny but her anecdotes and tangents made lectures feel unorganized and long. She interrupted herself often which confused me & I didn't love the lectures. There is no textbook, no posted slides, and hardly any reading material, so you better be a good lecture listener... and be okay re listening to her tangents for test prep.
Great Professor!

There is lots of content in the lesson videos but she makes it very intriguing and well worth. Use the study guide questions before each weeks lesson and re-watch the videos throughout the semester to keep the info fresh for the final comprehensive exam.
Dr. Hansen's class is very organized and set up for you to succeed. Loved this class and learned so much!

Professor Hansen made me love biology again. This class gave me the freedom to be able to take it during a difficult semester. The exams are hard but fair and preparation matters a lot. Would totally recommend.

Honestly loved all of the material in the class I just wished that it didn't feel so rushed during the whole semester. I loved her lectures and she was honestly pretty funny. The exams were not bad at all. It is a lot of memorizing concepts/processes but the material is interesting. Not much interaction with her but you can tell she is passionate.

I took Physiology online. It was difficult, but not more than you'd expect it to be. The tests were fair, and the lectures were useful. Prof. Larson goes off on tangents in lectures, but they helped me remember the concepts better. The homework was all useful, and the final project didn't take too much time. There weren't any exam reviews.

A lot of content and this professor doesn't do a great job of explaining concepts. Her lectures are outdated so half the time she was talking about things that were due that weren't even part of the curriculum anymore so I got confused. Tests are hard and she didn't help prepare you for them. Extra credit was provided in 2020 if you got a vaccine…

Took CELL 305 fully online and loved it. No textbook needed—the lectures give everything for tests. Rewatching lectures was super helpful. I just wish there were ways to interact or study with classmates. Overall, flexible, clear, and a great class.

The professor ignored two of my emails and took a week to respond to a third. Videos are outdated and she often gives her opinion which adds nothing intellectually and simply makes the video longer. She may have some passion for teaching but has no passion for helping her students.

This class lacks support. Professor Hansen and TAs never replied to my emails for help. Quizzes and tests don't match the material, and there are no reviews or guidance. Content is outdated from 2020, and the professor communicated only once. I wouldn't recommend this course to anyone hoping to learn or earn a fair grade.

She was good, sometimes got a little lost in lectures. The material seems easy til you get to the tests where it gets much more involved. She focusses on processes and more molecular than systematic. Good professor, though the material could be more test specific

Pros: Hansen's teaching abilities are good. Class content is easily accessible for review, and test questions on exams are usually fair.
-

Cons: Her videos are outdated. You can hear her children screaming in the background in most of the videos. She often shares her hot-take opinions which may not be enjoyable for everyone.

Take this from Dr. Hansen! She is AWESOME! My new fav professor! I was very nervous for this course, especially at the beginning because she seemed a bit intense in the first couple lectures. However, don't let that scare you away! She teaches in such a clear and concise way. Online is nice because you can pause and rewatch difficult concepts.

Dr Hansen is fine, nothing special, just fine. Her recorded lectures need updating and they're really long and cover a lot. This was said previously, but she doesn't write letters of rec, which is annoying since she teaches an upper-level 4-credit science class. There are no test reviews and her tests cover a lot. She had to really curve the final.

Prof. Hansen is alright as a teacher, but a few times during the semester she would say something in a lecture and then test you on it BUT the correct answer on the test is the opposite of what she said. So take what she says in lecture with a grain of salt. Also, she won't write any recommendation letters, even though that's part of her job.

She has a clear criteria of what you need to know for tests (as long as you understand everything in the learning targets you'll do well). She also offters quite a bit of extra credit, though some of it you have to go looking for. The TAs are wonderful, reach out to them to help you and you'll do just fine.

I loved taking this class from Dr. Hansen. The online format makes the workload very reasonable and flexible to your schedule. There are weekly lectures with simple homework assignments and quizzes. Things to look out for are the writing assignments and the exams. They are proctored and closed notes. The textbook isn't needed, just take good notes

Lectures can be material heavy but she makes it interesting and everything is online so it's not too bad. Exams are all open notes. Found textbook online. Labs are a bit hard so definitely don't miss lab days! Overall she's laid back, conversational, and offers a lot of extra credit. Totally recommend, easy class if you put at least some effort.

If you need to take this class, take it from Dr. Hansen. She is incredible at teaching! Her class is set up in a way to allow you to succeed, if you put in the work. Would not recommend taking it during the spring/summer term. Tons of extra credit but some of it is hidden so always read the fine print on everything. Absolutely LOVED this class.

I took this as an online class and it was unreasonably difficult.She goes on random tangents and she gives no clue to what is material and what is just her talking. The lectures are overly complicated and long, and the organization of her lessons are simply confusing. I feel like I learned more in my high school biology class about the same topic.

11/10 professor. Weekly quiz + HW, test Q3 weeks. There were a few departmental questions on the final and they seemed easier than her tests; nevertheless, I would recommend this class again and again. Excellent lecturer, great course organization (promotes retention!), plenty of EC. Learned a ton and feel better prepared for the MCAT!

Dr. Hansen is incredible. Her lectures can be long sometimes but are always so interesting. She is so real, and makes an effort to make her lectures funny and engaging. There are tests every 2 weeks, but if you study as you go, it's not a problem. She loves physiology and you can tell! CELL-305 online from her is AMAZING. Highly recommend!

Dr. Hansen is legit. Practically done with undergrad, but this was of my best decisions. If you're taking physiology you'll want to know it well, and this is the place to do it. Lol @ the freshmen saying "worst prof i ever had" haha; PDBIO 120 is like the first class you take at BYU and there's a lot worse to come. Godpseed.

Professor Hansen is the worst professor I have ever taken a class from. The tangents in her lectures are confusing and have nothing to do with the lesson. She does not explain things clearly and tries to make it as hard as possible. I am a straight A science student and absolutely hated this class. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS FROM PROFESSOR HANSEN!
Was a mom with two kids while she was teaching class, still did a killer job. Best part is here tests are straight forward and not trying to trick you! Great professor.

Dr. Hansen is great at teaching concepts and using real-world examples. Her humor is awesome- it makes the class more enjoyable to watch! Each lecture has a hw assignment and a quiz. You can go over the hw with a TA before submission. STUDY HAARRDD. FOR. QUIZZES. Though time-consuming, you're left prepared for the test. Hard yet rewarding class!!

I loved Professor Hansen! She has an interesting sense of humor that I really enjoyed. Her lectures are interesting and she does a good job of explaining tough subjects--she does talk really fast though, so be prepared for that. The TAs are gold! Go to their reviews! A good class, but be prepared to work hard!

Dr. Hansen is great! This was her first time teaching PDBIO120 and the fact that it was covid made it a little harder, but I really enjoyed her class! There's a quiz and a homework every week. Use the TAs!! You can seriously get 100% on every homework because they will meet with you and make sure you understand everything. Overall, great professor!

In her recorded lectures she mumbles at amazing speeds random facts about biology, all while getting distracted and going on tangents. Her lectures are challenging to learn from and her quizzes and midterms are impossible. I do understand that online class is hard, but still this was a terrible experience, nothing to learn from Melissa.

Dr. Hansen was an ok teacher. Bio is hard no matter who you take it from. However, I felt like her exams were impossible. During her lectures she goes off on these tangents and you have to try and figure out what will be on the test and what is just random fact. She has one lecture that is slightly inappropriate and just seems very unnecessary.

This is a difficult class but she is a great teacher and explains concepts well. Everything on the test is from her powerpoint (which you have access too) and lectures. You have one homework assignment every week and a quiz every Tuesday. She has a few group projects that I enjoyed because its an easy 50 points and you'll take an exam every 2 weeks

Great teacher, quite funny. Seems fair, occasionally curved a test for us, reviews the homework and answers with you during office hours, don't bother with a textbook, and just review the slides frequently and have them down for tests. A lot of material, and if possible, don't take it in the two-hour blocks, it was a little much sometimes.

Professor Hansen is amazing! She knows her stuff and is willing to help you if you actually go in and want to try. Granted, most of my studying every week was for this class--lots of outside studying. Professor Hansen is a great teacher but she does speak extremely fast. Use the learning objectives because that's in the test.

Dr. Hansen is the best professor I've ever had!!!! She is so hilarious and makes even the smallest parts of physiology extremely amusing and interesting. She gives weekly quizzes and homework, and she gives a test every two weeks or so. The tests are tough but doable if you understand herPowerpoint slides. You don't need the textbook!

Dr. Hansen is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. She is so passionate and excited about physiology but ALSO is a fantastic teacher, willing to re-explain in different ways. Extra credit given throughout the semester. DO NOT GET THE BOOK. Everything you need to know is on her slides. She is HILARIOUS and had the entire class laughing often

Dr Hansen is the kindest funniest professor and gives great DAT/MCAT prep. The class is insanely easy as long as you attend, no reading required. Coolest, most interesting course on campus, inspired me to change career plans (in a good way). Super approachable in office hours.

Dr. Hansen is super funny and relatable on a personal level, however, she is very unwilling to work with students when it comes to grades. She won't give credit if every person gets a question wrong on a test. There is a test every 2.5-3 weeks which take days to prepare for. I went to her office hours and reviews and still struggled to keep up.

Professor Hansen is one of my favorite professors at BYU. Her class was amazing! She made learning about physiology so interesting and she's really funny. You have to stay up on the material to do well on the quizzes every Monday, but it's very doable. The tests are fair as well and she usually offers a little extra credit on them.

Dr. Hansen is easily one of my favorite teachers at BYU and Physiology my favorite class. She teaches difficult concepts clearly. She teaches from power points, which she gives you access to. They are essential to studying. She's very kind and willing to work with students. She answers the tough questions and doesn't make you feel bad for asking.

What a legend. She's funny, smart, and caring; three dynamite teacher qualities. In all seriousness though, this lady is the type of professor that other professors should strive to be like. Put forth the necessary time to do ALL of her assignments and you will appreciate the intricate nature of our bodies. Take her, you won't regret it.

Dr. Hansen has to be one of my favorite Professors as byu. Physiology is tough and there is tons of memorization but she really helps you out. There are weekly quizzes that I hated at first but then when it was test time I only had to study a few hours because I had studied so hard for the quizzes. STUDY THE SLIDES and you will get and A.

Awesome teacher. Super down to earth and really gets what it is like to be a college student. Her lectures are great and clearly outline what you need to know for tests. I wish she taught more classes than PDBIO 305 cause I would take all of them. Quizzes require studying but if you pay attention, take good notes, and do the homework, you're gold.

Dr. Hansen is probably my favorite professor at BYU. It's a difficult class with a lot of tests, but she lets know exactly what you'll be tested on. She makes an effort to know everybody's name, even if it's a class of 100+ people. Her office hours are super helpful. Basically, she's the best and if you have to take PDBIO 305, take it from her!

Professor Hansen is a fantastic teacher, she has worked hard to make lectures interesting and clear cut. The tests reflect tit for tat her powerpoint slides. Study hard. She is helpful, caring and funny.

This class is no joke! Especially if you haven't taken chem and physics (like me) there was a learning curve. That being said, it's extremely possible to succeed if you put in the time. She doesn't want to fail you and balances tests/quizzes with easy hw assignments and lots of hidden extra credit. Find a TA you understand and go to reviews!
This class is difficult, but Dr. Hansen is a great teacher. You definitely have to work for it, but a good grade is achievable. She is totally willing to help you and answers any and all questions.

Dr. Hansen is one of my favorite professors! She does talk really fast, but is very willing to answer any questions. She posts her slides, so I would recommend recording her lectures & then going back & looking at the slides for studying. Her tests are difficult, but if you study for them, you can do well on them. She is hilarious!

By far one of the best professors, if not the best, I've had at BYU (and that says a lot after all my years here). There's a lot of material in this class, but she does an amazing job explaining it while still leaving time for any questions you have about the body. Best hour of my day. Would definitely recommend taking this class from her.

Dr. Hansen is one of the worst professors I have had at BYU. She is a really nice and funny lady but I highly recommend finding a different teacher for this class. I felt like she was trying to show off to her students by stating facts and processes as fast as she could with no explanation. I had to relearn everything after class with the TA's.

She talks really fast but posts her slides online so I would go back and use those to study. I would also recommend recording the lectures and going back to take notes so you can really grasp everything she is saying. Really awesome professor all together

Don't buy the textbook! Everything you need to know is on her slides. Dr. Hansen is really funny and candid. I thoroughly enjoyed the class. If you took anatomy it should be a pretty easy to do well. The TAs held a weekly review session and Dr. Hansen had office hours where you could ask anything and review your past exams.

Look out for her extra credit gems. She hides them throughout the tests and assignments. Gives a good boost. Tests are really hard and will sometimes test on stuff outside of learning outcomes but overall is pretty consistent. Recommend going to her office to study.

She completely knows her stuff &is an excellent teacher; she doesn't hesitate to answer questions &is very professional, but funny. She offers tons of extra credit and, although her tests are difficult, they are fair. She has extremely clear grading criteria and no book/class attendance is required, though it helps tons. She even learned our names.

Really cool professor and way down to earth! You can ask her any question about the human body and she'll mostly likely know it. Lots of info, so I recommend looking over the slides again right before/after her lectures. Make sure you read instructions because she'll throw in some hidden extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Hansen was a fantastic professor.  Physiology is a tough subject and there is so much material, but she does a really good job of laying it all out for you.  She is extremely willing to work with you and answer any questions you have.  The class is hard and takes a lot of work, especially when studying for tests, but it's worth it! Take her!
Prof. Hansen in AWESOME! She is very relatable, understanding, and easy to work with. Her lectures are engaging, and funny. She makes physiology fun!

Hansen is amazing. Lectures are slide based but that makes studying for tests really easy- study objectives correspond to slides. She's hilarious, and really helpful. She learned my name & most everyone elses also. I love this lady, class was interesting and inspring. Take from her! Dr Dave's class had to learn concepts outsie of class-not Hansen.

Professor Hansen's class was one of the most boring I've taken at BYU. Literally everything you need to know for the tests is on her slides (her slides are great!) and lecture feels pointless, but you still have to go to class at least on Wednesday or Thursday to take the pop quiz. She drops 3 quizzes.

Best class I've ever taken, and my absolute favorite professor. She's a real classy lady and she really understands her students. They need to name the life science building after her. I'm getting emotional just talking about it. Be prepared for quizzes, but she'll help you in any way you need. I only used the book every once in a while.
Awesome professor, really cares about students. Dry sense of humor, still able to relate with students. 5/7, would take again.

Melissa Hansen is one of the best teachers i've ever had!! Definitely pay attention in class, study every day because she does pop quizzes. Seriously though, she's the best. #MelissaHansenForPresident

Alright, listen up. 100% take from her. I asked past students and TAs in both classes, they were right. pdbio305 is a beast but Hansen is the best professor for it. expectations are CLEAR, organized. her classinteresting, engaging, inspiring, enjoyable. a ton of material but all powerpoint/objectives basedan A is possible. she's very reasonable.
She's just a straight up good professor.

I really enjoyed Dr. Hansen's class. She teaches you a ton of info but it's extremely organized and her tests are on exactly what she teaches in class. If you go to class, study for weekly quizzes, and study all the learning objectives before each test you can definitely get an A. She also gives extra credit and is fair in grading.

Dr. Hansen is really funny and seems like a nice person. I had a really hard time in her class though because she moves VERY quickly and doesn't use the book. She wants you to understand her slides but a lot of them have very little explanation. Likes smart students, but makes you feel silly for asking questions that she might not want to answer.

Very straight-forward personality & it shows in how she writes tests. We had 4 midterms of varying difficulty with no curve. Pop quizzes in-class hurt my grade but if you review you'll be fine. I only used the textbook to review.  I don't think she prepared us for the final though, usually people get a perfect score, but it was curved 5%.
I had to use the textbook to understand the learning objectives. The book was much easier for me to understand than the lectures. Take from someone else.

Hands down the best class I've taken at BYU. Dr. Hansen is the most helpful professor and the class is very straightforward . Don't buy the book, you'll never use it. Study the learning objectives and you'll do great. Quizzes every week that can be hard if you're not reviewing the lectures. Take it from her!

Dr Hansen is hilarious. Her lectures are always exciting, but she rushes through them very fast. She is very smart and consequently has a sort of condescending attitude towards those who struggle in the class. She is willing to answer questions but I didn't feel like she cared too much. There is a pop quiz every week.

Dr. Hansen is amazing! I have loved taking physiology from her. She is so passionate about physiology and that enthusiasm really shows in her teaching. Lecture is never boring, and she is always willing to help students. She gives learning objectives with each lecture, which helps a ton with studying for tests. Take this class from her!

Dr. Hansen teaches a really tough class and she somehow makes it very clear. I like that she's funny and tells stories to make the class seem a little less intense. She still expects you to work hard and know the material, but if you're doing well in her class then you'll be just fine.

Dr. Hansen is obviously very bright and well versed in physiology, but I really struggled with her teaching style. A lot of reading straight off slides, or worse, she'll show you a diagram and lack any sort of explanation on it other than what she says in class, so when you go back to study you find yourself in a puddle of confusion.

Professor Hansen is young, relatable, and fun to listen to. She's so bright and you can tell she's really passionate about physiology! Lectures were entertaining and her tests were straight-forward (she makes it very clear that she'll test you on the learning objectives from the slides. You don't have to guess what to focus on.) Loved the class!

She's awesome. I learned SO much from this class and Dr. Hansen made it easy to understand. Don't get me wrong, the material and amount of studying wasn't easy but the way she taught made complex concepts easier. I didn't use the textbook once so don't buy it. Her teaching ability is sufficient to understand all the material.

Dr Hansen was one of the best professors I have had here at BYU. She is so willing to help you understand the material. She is very approachable in office hours and is willing to help you. The learning objectives at the start of each lecture are essential. Know those and you will do great. Lectures are entertaining. Take it from her!

Dr. Hansen is a wonderful teacher. Her lectures are interesting and funny even if the subject matter seems like it would be boring. She really made me love learning Physiology which is awesome, because that's not always how teachers are. She is always available and willing to help, take this class from her! I wish I could have her again!
She is super funny, She knows her stuff, and she understands the students because she is young too. She is a great teacher! I would take it again from her in a heart beat.

Good class,  know the study objectives and you will do fine. Dr. Hansen is way nice and a pretty lady, and it is very clear what you need to know for the tests. I found it wasn't really necessary to go to class or have the textbook, just read her powerpoints and know the objectives to a t like i said and you will get a good grade no problem.
Melissa makes the lectures funny and does a good job teaching!

Dr. Jones is so great! She cares so much about her students, but it is a pretty hard class. Lots of readings and the tests go over things we barely covered a lot of the time, and even stuff that isn't in the study guide, so review your notes very carefully! But the content is so interesting, and she makes it super engaging.

This was her first time teaching this class, and it was a breeze. She gave incredible life advice. You can tell she's kind, and she is very open about her tattoos and life. The kind of teacher you would want to seek for internship help.

Dr. J is really great and knows her stuff. Be ready for lecture to not cover any of the readings, but you will still be tested on the reading material. You'll get to know her personal life and trauma because she uses herself as an example a lot. She really cares about her students and is super funny! NO LATE WORK is accepted

She is an amazing professor, a lil tough grader but not too bad. You HAVE to volunteer 20 hrs throughout the semester so make sure you have time for it. She really explains everything and it makes it so easy to understand.

Professor Jones is a great professor and always makes herself available for her students. I have taken 2 classes from her and every time I am grateful for it. She is incredibly open which makes her classroom feel safe and welcoming. I would highly recommend taking a class from her!

I found Dr. Jones' incredibly narcissistic and prides herself on the fact that she is an anomaly, has an ACES score of 6, and uses class time to trauma dump on her students instead of go to therapy. She is not a good teacher provides inaccurate study guides and includes things on the exam that we have never discussed before.

I loved Dr. Jones! I took 383 from her and absolutely loved the course material and the way she taught it. Her exams are tough and are a big part of your grade, but pay attention in class and make flashcards to study ahead of the exams and you'll be fine. She truly cares about the material and about her students, highly recommend!!

Dr. Jones is fantastic! I took 383 from her and she made the material so engaging and I looked forward to going to class every week. Her class is graded heavily on exams, and she grades them pretty harshly, but if you pay attention in class and make flashcards you'll be fine. I highly recommend taking any class from her!
Dr. Jones is such a good professor!!! She made this class very doable and allowed for a lot of in class work and collaboration to make sure everyone understood the material. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

This is just a hard class no matter who you take it from. Lots of new material and terms, but Prof Larson was a great professor. She cares about each of her students and she knows what she is talking about. The TA lab was not helpful, my roommate was more helpful than them. Just be aware that this class requires a lot of studying and effort.

She can be confusing at times but it's very clear she knows her stuff and she's willing to help you. The majority of the learning is done online so it doesn't matter all that much who you take it from
All I can legally say is Professor Drake's class is every Thursday from 3:30-4:45. If you want straight, clear, and not monotonous lectures- go to that instead.

The class is super organized no matter which professor you take it from. Tests are weighted the most but are only like 20-30 questions so that's hard. Because it is a mixed class you pretty much have to do accounting homework everyday to stay on top of it but it isn't overwhelming. A very doable class if you put in the work! Larson is great!
404 is a tough class but Professor Larson teaches everything so clearly and I felt prepared to succeed in the class.
Most of class is spent doing problems but I feel like Professor Larson explains things so clearly and makes it so easy to understand.

Her and Prof. Drake co-teach this class. Personally, I learned way more when Professor Drake was teaching. Larson is still a great person and teacher. But if you have the option I'd go with Drake over Larson, you'll learn the material way quicker. That would mean you learn online from him and he does lecture. Lectures weren't as helpful with Larson

The class is hybrid - online and in-person. Because Professor Drake does most of the videos, I felt like He was my teacher to be honest. Both Larsen and Drake are great. They teach accounting via real-world scenarios, and they are both so funny. I loved this class. The exams aren't too bad as long as you study for them.

Accounting 200 is a well-organized class, and Larson did a great job leading class activities that give you practice with what you learned online over the week. She helped me understand the material. With work, this class is doable.

Super easy class, just watch the video's and understand everything on the quizzes and you'll be fine. Professor Larson's lectures were kinda boring but she taught everything needed fine. Barley did any studying and only ever missed one question max on the midterms.

This was an amazing teacher. The class is hybrid and has online main lecture work you do every week and an in class portion that goes more in depth. The online section is split between her and another professor who is very funny. If you take time to learn the material, it's easy to comprehend. I got a 100 on everything without a lot of study time.

Professor Larson was by far my favorite professor this semester. Although she was teaching a class of around 800 students, I was never bored in her lectures. The class itself is considered a difficult one by most students, but Professor Larson managed to explain things very clearly. 100% would recommend.

Professor Larson was great! This was a blended course; lectures were posted on Canvas, and in-class time was spent working through study guides with peers. 

The midterms were fair and reasonable overall, though a few questions felt a bit ambiguous. No extra credit offered.

Overall, would recommend.
Amazing professor! Engaging lectures and lesson videos. Plenty of resources to succeed. If you study and keep up with the homework, you will be fine.

Nice professor who provides a lot of resources. She often had us try to solve problems with a partner, but this usually resulted in them teaching me something wrong lol. Test questions seemed to differ a bit from practice problems which threw me off. Overall, though she's great.
Prof. Larson is the GOAT! Tons of resources to succeed, makes accounting applicable and interesting.

She is really great at explaining things clearly. She also somehow answers questions and encourages participation in a giant auditorium. The Canvas course is the most well-structured and organized one I have ever used. You can really tell she does everything she can to help her students succeed in the class.

Professor Larson taught clearly, course was well organized. Initial learning came from recorded lectures  and was then reviewed with practice problems in-person. The tests are weighed very very heavily. 
Many recorded lectures by professor Drake were super funny/entertaining so he is a great option too that I would recommend.

This class is partially asynchronous, you meet once a week for an in-person lec, the rest is thru lec vids and slides. It's structured well, with mini quizzes after each lec vid that help your understanding of the concepts. There are a lot of quizzes, for each module, there's a graded review quiz and a module quiz taken after the lec vids.

The Accounting 200 material is standardized so the difficulty of the course isn't up to her. She teaches well and explains the content in a way that's easy to understand. Honestly is a very good professor!
TAKE THIS CLASS FROM DRAKE!!!!! She talks so fast and moves on from slides while you are still trying to write things down. Drake is way more entertaining and actually makes you enjoy accounting.

She's super kind and engaging despite the class being so large. She explains the concepts well and the TAs are very beneficial as well. There are many resources available to get an A and do well on the midterms and tests.

Amazing professor and person. I didn't do well in the class, but one day I cried to her after lecture because I missed the 3rd exam attempt and she was so understanding and gave me an extension no problem. It is very possible to do well in this class especially with the extra attempts and TA's, but it DEFINITELY would take time and effort.

I really enjoyed this class. It is outlined in a very straightforward manner. You do the online work throughout the week, and then meet once a week to review the material and apply it to practice problems. There are a bunch of TAs to help if you ever need it!

The content itself can be hard to grasp. Prof Larson sets it up to help you succeed between the helpful lectures and the and tests you can review and take up to 3 times. Most of the learning is done in the recorded lectures and your own time and class is more of a review. Definitely a challenging class but Prof Larson made it the best it could be.

Prof. Larsen was nice and had good lectures. The online and in-person lectures were super informative and I learned lots this semester; however, the final exam was crazy hard. I'm a good student but the final had tons of questions on things we barely discussed and the questions were tricky with a ton of answers that are so close to the real answer.

This course proved to be the most difficult and time-consuming part of my schedule, but I attribute that to the class itself and not the professor. Professor Larson is a very kind and very clear teacher and mentor, but the course expectation is simply difficult as you are asked to memorize and retain loads of information for closed-note exams.

The whole structure for ACC200 at BYU is set up for students to succeed. I honestly don't have a negative thing to say about the class. I actually quite enjoyed accounting once I figured out how the 3 Financial Statements interacted. I would advise getting familiar with the TA lab and attending all the lectures.
Really great teacher!!! Not her fault the class is difficult and time consuming (thats the curriculum), but explains the subjects very well and does her best to help us succeed

it is a good class but a lot of people find it hard. I think the system is a lit bit mediocre because they allow 2nd and 3rd chances on the tests to allow mediocre people earn an 80 in the test. Other than that class is good and but self learned.

Tough class, great professor. She is very honest with us throughout class, telling us exactly what kind of class day it is and what we need to know for exams. The only problem with her courses is that it is hybrid online-offiline, so sometimes you'll have up to 6 hours worth of videos you need to watch before class. That's not on her though.

Professor Larson is so dope. Super nice and clearly cares about her students. The class is tough, you really gotta apply yourself, but if you take the practice quizzes over and over you'll get the hang of it. Good luck yo

Dr. Larson is great. She designed the ACC 200 course, so she can answer any question you throw at her. The class is standardized, so each professor has the same materials, but Dr. Larson is great at explaining the more difficult concepts. Class is less math-based and more concept-based, so don't be intimidated by it.

I love Professor Larson! She teaches challenging concepts well. I was worried going into this class but honestly if you stay on top of the modules each week, and don't do them all in one day, you'll be fine. TA reviews were really helpful for the exams.
Great teacher!

I took 200 from Professor Larson as a blended course, and I loved her. I really don't like accounting, but she made the material engaging and truly wanted every one of her students to understand and succeed in the course. It's a pretty heavy workload, but start the weekly modules ahead of time and you'll be fine.
Prof. Larson is an amazing teacher and provides so many resources to help you in and outside of class!
Awesome teacher! Loved the structure of her class and her dedication to her students learning. Definitely take notes even though they aren't required and you will do great! Loved this class!!

If I could take every class from Dr. Larson I would. She made accounting so interesting, and easy to understand! She explains things very clearly in her lectures and I appreciated the clear layout of the class as well. She cares about her students and wants them to succeed as well which is great for such a large lecture hall! 10/10 recommend!
Hard context but she does a good job of explaining.

Professor Larson is great. She is very passionate about what she teaches and truly wants her students to succeed. The videos are very well done and I like the set up of the class. Lectures are good but not mandatory if you really don't want to go, but I enjoyed the review of the weekly content. She is always willing to help and the TA's are great.

She responds fast to emails. The class size is huge, so you are in a lecture hall with a few TAs walking around to answer questions while she teaches. She is very enthusiastic about what she does and really wants her students to succeed. Accounting 200 content is not very hard.

The class is heavily focused on online lectures and assignments, but if you stay engaged and use tools like unstuckstudy ai for study prep, you can succeed. The professor is helpful, but attention to detail is key for the tests.

I'm taking this class during spring term. Classes are 1 hour and 15 minutes long, and there are 2 classes a week. You have to complete 2 modules a week, and each module contains a pre-quiz, about 1 hour, 45 min of vids u have to watch, and then another quiz. Multiply that by two, and you're spending about 6 hr of lecture-watching and classes a week

Professor Larson is an absolute superhero of a professor. I felt like I had an unfair advantage in the Junior Core having her. She explains things so simply and is so receptive and willing to help with all questions asked during class. Her ACC 200 class is the reason I found my passion for accounting and her ACC 404 class just deepened that passion

Professor Larson does a fantastic job of explaining difficult concepts. She anticipates what will confuse students and makes challenging topics much more simple. She definitely knows her stuff and will help students who ask for it. I would definitely not recommend skipping class.

The class is primarily online driven. If you do not learn well in this manner then you will struggle in ACC 200. The lectures are all videos, and she holds class once a week to go over a couple practice problems. Overall, she seems to make accounting more difficult than it should be. At least the homework is light?

Prof. Larson is incredible and cares for her students. This course was well-organized, so I knew exactly what I needed to do to succeed. Before class, students watched instruction videos before engaging in lectures to practice content. Prof. Larson knows and loves what she is teaching. Every resource is available to students who want to do well.

Class was great, I bombed the first test just because I didn't know how much attention to detail mattered--it's everything in this class. I got A's on the next 2. The content is very clear though there is a lot, half of the lectures were online, which were very good. I loved how straight forward everything was... jut pay attention to the details!

If you struggle with online courses, DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE! Find an in person. I got by because I hauled the last two units. That aside, Professor Larson is great and cares for her students. She will make an effort to help you. GO TO THE TA LABS!
Class only once a week, not much work throughout the semester, but you are required to memorize lots of specific terms and situations and different things for the cumulative final and midterms.

The videos explain things well, however, the practice problems are nothing like the tests at all. Definitely need to study a lot for this class and isn't too hard if you study. She can explain things well, but its hard to do well on the tests if you are given the ample practice problems to be able to study.

This is a very difficult class. I spent hours studying for exams and doing the online coursework. She was very nice and respectful, the lectures were pretty engaging. Most of what you learn for the class is online and most of my videos weren't even her, they were other professors in the program. Prepare to spend lots of time studying and learning

You go through one module per week on canvas that take about 3-4 hours overall to complete. I went to this class in person twice this whole semester and did alright because its basically an online course. The tests are difficult and contain some content not included in the module. Study hard and watch the TA reviews online.

You have to teach yourself everything through these online videos and in class you just go over what you watched. The tests feel unfair (I studied hours for each test and got B's just because the material was just not the same). there are few graded points outside of the tests to make up for it. Its easy material set up in an unfair way.

Set up with pre-recorded videos on canvas. Throughout the course, 3 different professors explain the concepts in videos, so if one teaching style doesn't match your learning style, you usually get at least one other perspective from a different professor on the same concept. Study for exams and come to class, but the class itself wasn't that hard.

Rest heavy and are different then what you practice. The final is even different from the midterms. There is a generous test curve (retakes with an 80 cap) however it really only benifits the lower half if the class. With this I tend to get an average 80% on tests (the first time) and this tended to get extremely frustrating for me

Blended course so the weekly workload consisted of about an hour and half of videos and then a 10 question quiz. You get 3 attempts on exams but after the first one they are capped at 80%. Definitely go to lectures, we go over a packet in class.
She is amazing! I loved the class. I saw that my friends that didn't watch the videos really struggled in the class. The people that did watch the videos did much better on the tests and quizzes.

If you want to do well in this class, she makes the expectation clear and understandable. Her lectures are very helpful if you come to class prepared. Other than watching the online lectures I did not need to dedicate much time to this class. All of the assignments help prepare you for the exams which are not too hard. Highly recommend this class.

Professor Larson is a phenomenal teacher. She radiates professionalism and expertise in all of her lectures, but this doesn't prevent her from explaining concepts clearly. I enjoyed attending her classes and loved this course. I'd recommend it to all majors.

This was a really good class! Whatever teacher you have won't really impact the class since most of it is online videos and assignments apart from lecture once a week. Professor Larson was super kind and friendly though, would 100% recommend taking this class from her!

This blended class is very well organized and easy to keep up with. The TA lab and office hours make it very easy to get help when needed. You are not graded on lecture attendance, but should go as often as possible because some of the material is only covered in face-to-face class, and you have 3 attempts on the midterms and the final!

Loved everything about this course but the only thing I didn't like was I felt like a lot of the exam review was content not even on the test. Everything else isn't bad but I know the tests were hard for almost all students however you can retake all exams and have the next one cap at 80% which is nice.

Because this is an online course, there is pretty limited contact with the professor apart from the lecture once a week. Most of the learning and work is on an individual basis but there are TA hours every day and so many resources available for students- this is a course designed for as many people to succeed as possible!

This class is required for most business majors, so you kind of just have to suck it up and take it. The online modules are pretty long, but you only have one day of in-person lecture which is nice. There is a lot of detailed accounting information on the exams, so make sure to study.

I took this class a couple years back and it was so easy. But I stopped going to class a couple of weeks in since she just confused me with super complex problems that the videos and exams never had us do. Still got a super easy A while barely doing any work. Currently in the Accounting Jr Core

I'm an accounting major, so this class was quite easy for me. It was a lot of work, but the concepts made perfect sense. As for the professor, she just confused me in class so I quit going to class a few weeks in and still got super easy A's on every quiz and exam.
Prof Larson is wonderful! Most of ACC 200 is online through canvas, so she just reviews topics we learn ourselves in class. She cares about her students and is always willing to help.

Professor Larson is a great teacher. She teaches topics very well. I would spend the week doing my homework and be confused by some things on the video lectures, but when I got to class she always cleared up any questions I had. Just be ready for lots of work outside of class. Studying for tests is crucial. She gives you three attempts on all tests

Accounting is hard and there are only 3 exams the whole semester, but there are lots of resources to practice . TAs are available basically 24/7 which is super helpful. Attendance is not mandatory but for sure go. Study super hard for the exams as they are not long so only a few wrong and your grade will be low.

TAKE ACC 200 FROM HER!!! Most of the class is on Canvas, (online, open book quizzes and videos) but in class she is a very good lecturer. Not sure if she teaches every semester, but if she is available take it from her!!!

Honestly, I was worried this class was going to be really horrible but I actually liked it. I'm not an Accounting major either. They redesigned the course to simply the amount of content they teach. It's impressive. The teach the MOST important things and kicked out everything else. I learn more because they make the lectures very engaging.

Honestly this class is just a series of videos that you are gonna use to teach yourself. Professor Larsen seems great and puts effort into her teaching, but her involvement is pretty minimal and her lectures are not near as applicable as the videos you'll be watching (side note, her voice is pretty annoying). Great skills learned, mid delivery.

The course is just videos that are pre-recorded so it doesn't reflect on the professor very much. That being said, when we did go to class once a week, she was awesome. Very easy class if you stay on top of the weekly work. I think the reason some people think this class is hard is because they procrastinate and have no work ethic.

This was honestly the hardest class I have ever taken, but it has also been one of my favorites. I learned so much. The tests are extremely hard, but if you pay attention to the lecture videos and practice a ton. You will be fine. I love Prof. Larson so much! She is amazing and truly wants her students to succeed.

I had very little interaction with Professor Larson. Classes were interesting but felt pretty redundant after the online videos. I'd recommend going if you are having trouble and to get a few points on tests but I mostly worked on other things during the class. She's a wonderful person though and does care about her students.

Professor Larson is wonderful, I was a little worried about this course but ended up enjoying it way more than I ever thought possible. She makes it about so much more than accounting, but really helps you to remember what matters most in life and education. She designed the course so you have plenty of resources to succeed as long as you use them!
Dr. Larson is great but the class itself is just a lot of lectures and learning math at home. Some people like it, some hate it.

I enjoyed the way Professor Larson taught the weekly lectures, but having completed the online modules prior to meeting in person, I didn't find them particularly productive for me. Thus, I would recommend going to class only for extra help, or the budgeting lecture was really cool. Otherwise, a very well structured class with clear expectations.

Professor Larson is great! She cares for her students and is good at helping them understand difficult accounting concepts. The class is set up in a very organized way. Be ready to put a lot of time each week into this class. Exams are challenging, but if you are willing to do lots of practice problems you will be fine. Also Norm is the goat

Fantastic teacher. I really enjoyed the lectures and she is extremely understanding yet firm in her expectations. I enjoyed the second half of the class more than the first because after you learn the basics she then can start explaining concepts using personal life stories which I loved. Dr. Larson cares about BYU, the students and her role in it.

Took ACC200 freshman year. It's basically an online class taught through recorded lectures with weekly meetings where Larson goes over important topics and problems. As long as you stay on top of your modules, the class shouldn't be too difficult. Make sure to do the modules before you meet for class that week.

Prof. Larson is WAY good! Many say that she doesn't do the teaching herself, which is somewhat true. One lecture a week isn't enough to teach us everything, but I liked it more this way because it gave us more time to do practice problems outside of class instead of falling asleep in a lecture. Advice: do ALL practice problems  and you'll be okay.

RIP to anyone who takes this class after 2022 because you won't have the GOAT Norm Nemrow giving the recorded lectures. Besides that this class is incredibly straightforward. She basically gives you the content of the final exam, but you will have to study. Pay attention to the videos and in class lectures and you should do well (or at least pass).

Professor Larson is so caring! She's really straightforward with what you need to do to succeed in class, don't be a weekend warrior! Watch the videos and make sure you understand the homework and the tests aren't terrible. She also moves the grading scale at the end by a percent or two which was awesome!

Melissa larson is amazing! the class is super organized and structured. she truly gives you the resources you need in order to succeed. You have test retakes which helped me the most in my learning. It is a difficult class but the TAs are great

ACC200 is doable. Professor Larson is spiritual but she tests students hard on details and a lot of tricky questions on the exams. Accounting is very detail oriented, if you finish review quizzes and module quizzes then you will be fine.  Go to the TA Lab, some of the TAs may not be acquainted with 200, pick the one who knows the content.

The class is completely doable if you do the homework on time and spread it throughout the week. Professor Larson was easy to contact, and the TAs are always happy to help. She is inspiring and wants the best for her students in and out of the classroom. Homework is mainly video lectures because it is a hybrid class. Review for exams ahead of time.

This is the class to take if you want to teach yourself accounting.  Melissa Larson doesn't know how to teach so instead of doing her job she assigns 4 hours of videos to watch per week.  Also, professor Larson will not help you at all, doesn't matter your circumstance because she doesn't care about you at all.

This class is a lot of work, which mostly consists of watching video lectures and quizzes. If you study, pay attention in class & while doing the hw, & make sure you set time aside to understand the material, you'll be fine. It's a lot of work but it will make sense if you try and go to the TA lab! She's a good professor & is great during lectures.

I loved the lectures with Prof. Larson because she is very fun to listen to and has really good stories. She makes things very clear when she explains them. Accounting will take a lot of your time, space it out and don't be a weekend warrior. You will have to work but it is not too challenging if you put in the effort and time.

You basically just have to teach yourself. You're given about 4 hours worth of videos to watch every week, and then a zoom class once a week... Not a great way to set up students for success. I studied probably 6+ hours for each test and never got above a 75. Tough class, if you don't like sitting down and watching videos for hours, beware.

Acknowledge the stats on this class! really good course, both Professor Larson and Norm were great at teaching complicated material. I really enjoyed a blended class, don't let that push you from taking Accounting, try it. Homework was given consistently, nor did I think that those assignments were very hard. I really really loved this class.

This is a tough class. Attendance isn't required, so I rarely went. The 3 tests are a worth 60% of your total grade, but they can be taken 3 times (Attempts 2&3 capped at 80%). Do all the practice problems and practice exams, and then go over stuff that's challenging with TA's and you'll be okay. Expect 6ish hours a week on homework.

I went to class three times and never showed up again. In class, she'd present crazy difficult problems that would literally never show up on the test. In order to do well, I'm not kidding, just do the practice problems over and over again until you know how to do each one perfectly and you'll be fine. I did that and got like a 96 overall.
This class is a part time job. A class of 1400 is a joke. Prepare to live in the TA lab and be lost. Tests are overly tricky and can absolutely tank your grade. Proceed with caution

Prof Larson is one of the best professors I've had. I had a difficult start (mental & physical health things:) & she was so understanding and accommodating. Can retake any exam up to three times. NOT an easy class; I spent like 4 hours/day outside of class working. Be prepared to work like crazy. TAs helpful. If you take ACC 200, take from Larson.
This was the most organized class I have ever taken. If every class was run the way that Professor Larson and Norm ran things, there would be peace in Zion.

Professor Larson is great! Her material is very organized and you know what to expect up front! She also gives great study resources to prepare for the test so use them! As long as you put in the work to learn the material you should do well in her class! 

(Tip: I recommend taking the review quiz for each module before you take THE module quiz)

Be prepared for the tests! The first two I didn't study that much and did okay. When I actually studied, everything actually made sense and I did great on the final. You just have to put in the work and you will succeed. It really isn't that bad of a class, you just need to, spread the work out through the week. Don't do it all Saturday night.

Professor Larson gave some of the best lectures this semester. She's incredible. Her class is structured so that students can learn LOTS. Her TAs are incredible as well and teach more simply than any TAs I've ever worked with. This is a hybrid class, so the class meets once a week and the rest of the week is independent studying.

The class has provided every was possible for students to succeed. Dropping lowest scores, a TA lab open every day in person and on zoom, retakes on test if you get below 80%, class in person or over zoom, review sessions going over the questions you get wrong, and a supportive teacher that wants you to do well. It is easy if you put the effort in.

Professor Larson has been my favorite Professor! Accounting 200 covers a lot of materials and the way she uses videos and canvas developed with Norm (a former professor) helped me learn it all! Truly she strives to and succeeds at teaching with the Holy Ghost in a way I've seen no other professor teach. She genuinely cares about her students.

Loved this class! Acc can be boring but she made it fun. You learn mostly from video modules (loved the vids! Clear, easy, fun). Can take exams up to 3 times (2 & 3 capped at 80%), 10q quiz each week (not too difficult & open note), 5q recap quiz every week unlimited attempts. If you can do the practice exams without help you will do great on exams

This course was super well organized and designed in a way that emphasized learning. Professor Larson is an amazing person who truly cares for her students and wants them to do well. The class is pretty hard but Professor Larson did everything she could to make it more enjoyable.

Professor Larson actually cares about students and didn't just spend class going over stuff on the final but stuff that we could actually use and that will make us financially successful later on. I went to class not because I wanted to get a good grade but because I actually LEARNED something. That is how education is supposed to be. Props 2 her.

I loved this course! I was so scared to take Accounting in my first semester of college, but it was one of my favorite classes. It was super hard, don't get me wrong, but I loved the video format. I took hand-written notes of everything on the slides in the videos. Got a 95% on the final. Prof was great and I might major in Accounting now!

Prof. Larson is such a sweet lady who genuinly loves her job and cares about her students. She allows 3 attempts on all exams (2 and 3 attempt are capped at a B), but the amount of time this class takes shouldn't be under stressed. One other note of advice- if you don't like video lectures, that's all the teaching you get.

Professor Larson is easily the best professor I have ever had at BYU. She cares so much about all her students and genuinely wants you to succeed. The class is very well organized and easy to follow. If you put in the work you can do very well! The lessons take a long time to complete but they are super interesting and easy to understand.

Don't get me wrong she is a great professor and you can tell she is caring. The only thing is the workload in this accounting class, if you want a good grade expect to put in maybe 6ish hours of work per week for this class and if you want a great grade for you to be going into the TA lab
Professor Larson is one of the most caring professors out there. She takes the time to make sure students understand, which is crucial in a class with 1,000 students.

I did the hybrid class, it was about 3-4 hours outside of class and a 75 minute class once a week. The way the course material is set up is so clear and well put-together. The practice problems and slides are so helpful for studying for the exams. Put in the time and you will do well.

Professor Larsen was so amazing. She was very inspirational and I could tell she cared about us. Dont get me wrong, the class was hard. But so are most classes at BYU.
