If you work hard and study you will do great. We only met one day a week and mostly learned from videos made by a retired BYU professor, Norm. His videos were great.

ACC 200 was a completely online class, yet somehow Prof. Larsen made me feel like she cared. It was very clear what was going to be on the test and the homework and lectures prepared you for it. Almost all of the lectures were recorded by a guy named Norm. If you put in the work, this class is very passable.

Professor Larson is such an amazing professor!! I'm not passionate about accounting, but she made it really interesting! I'm glad I took her class. There is a lot of homework every week - 2-4 hours of videos a week plus other assignments, but if you don't procrastinate you'll be fine. Tests can be hard though and they will hurt your grade.

I took ACC200 after fin201 so it felt pretty easy and lots of chapters were a review. Honestly, some of the easiest material Ive had and it just clicked. Good class set up and well organized! I thought it was a very good class for people of all disciplines and there were lots of resources to help learn and study. Straightforward tests as well

Professor Larson is amazing! She made class interesting, always seemed relatable, and outlined a clear plan for the class so if you had any questions, you knew to look at canvas because she set everything out before the semester started. She was honestly one of my favorite professors! Also, thankful for the 2nd and 3rd chances she gives for exams
This class has semi hard content, but if you watch the lectures and do the practice problems, it isn't too bad. It is the most organized class I've ever taken.

Professor Larson was amazing. Accounting 200 wasn't the easiest class but she structures it in a way that helps you be successful in it. Even though the class size was 800+, she still made it seem like she cared about the success of every student which was impressive. Highly recommend taking this class from her. Also shoutout Norm, love that guy.

This was a great class! The content was very well organized and accounting is a pretty easy subject. I put about 3 hours/week into this class and I feel like it was not too hard to get a good grade. Just do all the practice problems and study well for the tests and you'll be fine!

This is a very tough class, but if you put in the time and effort you can pass. If you pay attention to Professor Larson's and Norm's lectures you can learn everything you need to know. There is about 3-4 hours of videos to watch every week, so it is time consuming. Professor Larson tries to make it as simple and easy as possible though.

This is hands down the most well-organized course I have ever taken, online or in person. Most work is done online. I loved having videos instead of a textbook. Prof Larson's lectures are helpful (and spiritual!). The TAs are fantastic - use them! I didn't find the course too difficult, just stay on top of it. I'd HIGHLY recommend Prof Larson!

Professor Larson is super awesome! She definitely knows the material well and wants you to succeed. She's very helpful and willing to explain things if you don't understand. She's great at giving explanations and told stories as she taught. She was especially inspirational about things that matter most and helping you see the value of accounting.

Although Professor Larson was nice, she did not do a lot of teaching. If anything, Norm (the guy who taught the prerecorded lectures) was the one doing all the work. The class itself was very difficult, although doable. The quizzes were a very useful study tool, so be sure to look them over before every test.

Larson is great for ACC 200. Not too much HW and I found the classwork very interesting. I set aside 1 hour every day for this class and it got me an A. Professor Larson is super approachable and very easy to talk to. If you have any questions, you can ask her after class or join the TA Zoom session and ask them. Very fun introductory ACC class.

She's such a sweet, caring woman. It's a hard class, but she does her best to help students succeed. The TAs are basically always available, and you have three tries on the exam (although the 2 & 3 attempts cap at 80). There is so much work outside of class though, and it was definitely stressful. I had to work very hard in this class for my grade.

I think my rating is influenced in at least some small part by my hatred of accounting in general (really, is there a less intuitive subject? or a more artificial one?), but I just need to say it: SHE DOESN'T ACTUALLY TEACH ANYTHING. She gives you materials and says "go." I didn't attend a single lecture, 93% on the final. No teaching value at all.

Prof. Larson was a GEM. The accounting class she has put together is incredible. The best class I have taken at BYU, even though the material was hard. TA's are so willing to help, and you feel like you are needed in the class. Just incredible resources. Larson was always so helpful and shared inspiring stories in class!

Professor Larson isn't a great teacher, at least in online format. I think the main problem is people who shouldn't be in college asking questions that waste everybody's time, but she always seemed stressed and rushed and didn't add to what the pre-class videos taught. She spends too much time teaching college students how to take a test

The class takes work, but I wouldn't say it's super hard. It's a lot of memorization and remembering where things go, and if you stay on top of it from the beginning it'll make it sooo much easier. Professor Larson is a great teacher. She explains things well, the class is forgiving, and you can tell she cares.

Professor Larson really wants to give students every opportunity to succeed. She provides a lot of review material and practice problems. You watch lectures from Norm throughout the week and then attend one lecture with her. She gives second and third chance exams to raise exam scores, and overall is a great and understanding professor.

Prof. Larson and Norm are a power duo! Norms videos are entertaining and do a good job of explaining concepts for you, and Larson cares about her students. With videos and quizzes every week, as well as two midterms and one final, you definitely have to work for it, but its doable and rewarding. Best option for ACC 200!

The class is structured phenomenally. Online video lectures with Norm and one lecture with Prof Larsen. Norm's lectures are fantastic! He makes learning accounting engaging and easy to understand. Prof Larsen's lectures were generally unnecessary if you paid attention to Norm. You can tell she really cares and wants to help though.

There is no reason a hard-working student should not perform well in this class, Prof Larson makes it impossible to fail with her amazing structure. You can get away with not attending weekly Zooms, but she goes over things that aren't in the class videos that do get put on the test. Each test has 2nd and 3rd chances for up to 80%.
Best professor EVER! I definitely worked to get the grade I got, but prof Larson gives you all of the tools to be successful. She made ACCOUNTING enjoyable.

I LOVED this class! You have to work hard to do well, but it's not that bad. Watch all of Norm's videos (he is a legend, great professor and funny videos), do the practice problems, and go to the weekly lecture by Professor Larson. TA reviews are also very helpful. This is the most well-organized class I have ever taken with plenty of resources!

Though it was online, this class was not difficult at all. You watch some fantastic lectures of Norm and inspirational ones of Prof. Larson once a week. This was rather an enjoyable time and such a great blessing to know these people. For exams, make sure you go over the practice tests at least 5 times then you will be fine.

Not gonna lie, it was a tough class that wasn't super forgiving. However, the teacher was great and Norm was amazing. If you work hard then you should pass easy. She gives second try exams and did curve a little at the end. Not saying it will be an A, but you won't fail.

Professor Larson's packet had lots of flaws that were irritating. But whenever I emailed her she responded within an hour with a clear explanation about something I didn't understand. Not a difficult class if you do the work. I only attended our weekly class twice

Tough class but very clear. very organized. Online lectures every week with a short open book quiz at the end. Tests were harder than quizzes because they are closed book and note and the questions are one step higher. to pass them, you need to do ALL the homework and understand the questions, not just memorize them. she also gives practice tests!

Prof Larson is awesome, even though ACC 200 is primarily taught through module videos by an older professor. Incredibly organized and cares about her students. The tests are always harder than you'd expect, but if you overprepare you'll do fine. Requires self-discipline to stay on top of things as it is essentially a on-demand remote course.
Tests can be super hard, but her and Norm's lectures are great. SUPER easy to get ahold of when there is a problem.

Professor Larson is the most organized professor I have ever had. The way she has set up her canvas is very simple and makes staying organized in the class very easy. This class takes up about 6-8 hours a week just watching Norm videos and taking quizzes. If you put in the time and stay somewhat on top of things this class is easy. Study for tests!
At BYU it doesn't really matter who your acc 200 professor is because most of the class is taught by the Norm videos anyway.

The format of the online class is really challenging, even with the live lecture once a week. Utilize and magnify all the resources they give you. I can tell that they want you to succeed, but the test grades don't lie (and they won't round your grade up at the end of the semester).

This class is a lot of work, but if you put in the effort, it's not too difficult. Professor Larson is so kind and caring, and she truly inspired me in every lecture. Most of the class is taught through videos made by Norm Nemrow, who is the bomb, just beware that they can get a bit boring. Pay attention and study hard and you'll be fine

Best online class to take during covid. It's clear what you need to do and when and how much weight everything has. Prof Larsen really wants you to do well. Literally made to be an online class way before covid happened and it's format works really really nice. Have to try really hard and remember that every single point counts. Lots of homework.

Yo, this class can be HARD. However, it's not impossible. I got a C because I kinda gave up towards the end of the semester (My fault not the professor's) I will say that you have all the resources you need to succeed and get an A if you want it. Proff Larson is great and I would definitely recommend her for whoever has an interest in accounting.

Professor Larson doesn't do much of the teaching in ACC 200, you learn nearly all of the material from Norm in pre-recorded modules. ACC 200 is not bad if you don't mind tedious, yet basic math (addition, multiplication, etc). Her online course is set up better than any professor I've ever had; the structure makes it easy to prepare for exams.

Accounting in general can be a difficult course. While there may be something to say about the difficulty of teaching online, Professor Larson's class is structured well. Tests can be brutal, but the reviews leading up to taking the test are key!

Prof. Larson made ACC200 a highlight of my week. I reluctantly signed up for this class based on my disgust for accounting based on my high school experiences. If you are on the fence about taking the class, take the class. Just be ready to commit a lot of time to get a good grade. It sure isn't easy, but it is worth the hassle. Plus Norm...

ACC 200 is a very challenging class. Professor Larson also doesn't really teach you anything, that's Norm's job. It has interesting material but just got dry after a while. But ya very challenging class and having assignments due Saturday at midnight make Saturday nights stressful.

A very very difficult class. The videos that are supposed to teach you are very hard to follow and understand. The class lectures do nothing. I spent HOURS studying and doing homework EVERY week (over 10) and never got higher than a 75% on a test. The worst part is that I honestly don't even know what I missed. Just don't take this class.

Great class, pretty easy to get most of the topics, but the other 10% of information you will need to study hard to commit to memory, which is what hurts you most on tests. While the in-class (or live remote delivery) lectures aren't mandatory, there is some information that appears there that you won't find anywhere else. Not a bad class.

Professor Larson was a great professor and she really did want us to pass, however there were hours of videos to watch and take notes on. The shortest amount of time I spent watching the videos for homework was about an hour. The longest time was over 4 hours. She herself is very willing to help you outside of class which I very much appreciated.

Professor Larson is incredible. Expect to do your homework and study hard, and the lectures will be amazing. She does an awesome job of teaching both course material and how the gospel ties into everything you learn about. I honestly think everyone should take this course, if only to learn about life, and how to be a good person and student.

Professor Larson is an amazing professor. If you're into accounting and think you can keep up with it, take it from her! She really cares about her students. However, the class itself was difficult and a LOT of work. The exams were probably the worst part.

The class itself was difficult at first. The tests are worth a lot, and the material isn't very intuitive. But the course is very well-organized, and there are tons of TAs to help with any questions. There is a review quiz every chapter that has 5 random questions from any of the previous chapters, which is super helpful later in the class.

Tests are about 60% of your grade. I enjoyed this class and Prof Larson was very concise and straightforward. It's a lot of work, but TAs are accessible all normal business hours. It takes a lot of work, but it is so worth it. This is the most organized class I have ever been in. You will know when assignments are due, and the resources available.

I am in awe of anyone that gets an A in this class. This is such a hard class. You don't think it will be bad until you start taking exams. Then you quickly realized how screwed you are. I spent at least 15 hours every week and I did horrible on every test. AVOID THIS CLASS.

Though this class is quite a bit of work outside of class do to it being a hybrid it is great. She teaches the material in a very simple way and gives you every resource necessary to make sure you do well in the class. If you are willing to put in the work you need to do well you can ace this class.

She is a great teacher. Accounting was pretty straightforward. Go to lecture, pay attention, keep up with all the online homework and you are golden. Class isn't super difficult if you stay up on the Norm videos. Also, tests have fewer questions which makes every multiple choice answer count.

Prof Larson is my HERO! I love her. The class takes effort, but the expectations for the class are very clear and all the resources you need to succeed are handed to you. The exam study guides and review quizzes are so helpful! Larson makes the topic interesting and she tells great stories from her career and motherhood.

Fantastic. She has high love and high expectations. Her class shreds high school study habits, forcing you to become better. She does everything in her power to empower her students and help them grow. Such a high-caliber professor. I learned almost as much about life as I did Accounting. She's honestly incredible. Highly Recommend.

Professor Larson's class takes work but it is definitely well worth it. She focuses on helping you to succeed. This class takes a lot of time outside of class because so much of the instruction is video based. Take the practice test and keep you quiz grades high!

In the beginning this class was tough, but in the end I loved it! Professor Larson does a good job of explaining things but it's still important that you do your part outside of class. It's easy to get behind so just stay on top of what's being taught. If you need help don't hesitate to reach out to the Professor Larson or the TAs!

Solid professor that teaches the material well and has reasonable expectations for students. The online material does a great job at teaching accounting, but sometimes there wasn't much connection between the online material and the lectures. There are four very easy papers throughout the semester and about an hour of work a day. Don't get behind!

Professor Larson is very smart and LOVES accounting! She shares her passion for it in class and really works to help you understand the material. You'll need to dedicate several hours a week to homework, review videos, and quizzes, but if you stay on top of things, this class is totally do-able!

Professor Larson has been my absolute favorite professor at BYU so far. Her class is the most organized and her expectations for you are so clear that if you just do what she advises you to, you will succeed. Accounting comes naturally to some more than others, but she sets you up for success as long as you put in the time necessary for this class.

I took her Accounting 200 class, and she was an amazing professor. SHe is so nice and she gives amazingly lectures. You have to watch a lot of videos in preparation for class (yes, you HAVE to - or you will not pass), but the videos are pretty engaging and explain the material very well. Not much homework other than that.

Professor Larson's class is a great intro to accounting. Professor Larson does a great job at explaining the hardest concepts like bad debt expense. However, know that she teaches once a week and every other chapter has to be done out of class. The class is curved and some assignments are dropped, so the class grading is forgiving.
Best Professor ever. Learning contents are extremely useful and she explains really good. Take it from her you will not regret it.

I absolutely loved her class. It took effort, but the grading material and content was very straight forward and clear. She also provides ample material to you in order for you to master the material. You get the grade that you study for.

Prof Larson is amazing! Yes, the class requires a lot of time, but the work itself isn't too hard. She is great at explaining things and I've learned more practical things for life in this class than I have in any other! Highly recommend.

I honestly wish I could have gone to class more, you learn moslty from online matterial which is a great help, but she could explain it more in detail sometimes and was very inspirational. I loved her lectures. Do all the online help and practices and you should easily get a B. I had an A until I messed up on the final and it brought my grade down.

Sister Larson is an amazing professor! She is so kind and is a great accounting teacher. She explains everything really well and sets up the class with a structure designed to help you succeed! 10/10 recommend!
I think her class was useful, but it was very difficult. If I had known anything about accounting before taking her class, her class would've have been easier.

This class was not my cup of tea. I didn't like the math involved and she wasn't great at explaining it. We had to watch SO many videos at home and it was frustrating to have all the extra work. She was so kind though.

I'm not majoring in accounting, but Prof. Larson made me want to take more accounting classes. She was easily one of my favorite professors. You have to work hard, study, and stay on top of your homework, but she's really clear in how she grades from the beginning. I would recommend this class (and any class by Prof. Larson) to anyone.

Hope you like staring at a screen for hours and hours every week, you're expected to learn everything on your own before coming to class for "review." The dude in the videos hasn't worked at BYU for atleast a decade. I'm not sure is Prof. Larson is just being lazy or doesn't want to teach us herself. Wait until winter semester and take Stice!!!

Professor Larson is amazing. She makes a class of 800 seem smaller by working with the students one on one and walking around. She is such an admirable teacher. The worst part of this class was watching all the videos. It took at least 3 hours every week. The final is a beast. Good luck.

She is passionate about accounting and is easily accessible outside of class. However the videos and homework killed it for me. There are hours of videos every other day and you really have to know the material inside and out to even get above a B. Take this only if you have a light schedule since you have to invest a LOT of time to do well.

Professor Larson is a great professor, one of the best I have had. Her enthusiasm for ACC is obvious, and her lectures are great. Do not fall behind. Do some ACC every day and you will do great. Really enjoyed Prof. Larson's teaching style, and how she incorporated spirituality and real-world applications into the course. Excellent professor.

She was a fantastic teacher and had such an organized courseI loved it! Shes very passionate about it and I feel like I actually walked away from the class having learned something, which I cant say about all classes.

Professor Larson is a great teacher, and she is very kind and does well at teaching. But this class was the hardest class I've ever taken. It kind of sucked having it half online as well, soo many hours of watching videos to understand how to do things. There was so much work but mainly the tests were so hard. Most people don't pass the first exam

Professor Larsen does a great job at explaining the material and her lectures are usually insightful but unless acc comes easy to you, be prepared to study hard for the tests. Her tests are manageable but you need to do pretty good on them to get an A. The worst part of this class is the hours and hours of stupid videos you have to watch!

Acc 200 is half online and half in class, so you only attend one 75 min class a week. The online material is mostly videos that I personally liked. The average on tests are usually Cs, but if you really take all the practice quizzes and watch all the videos it is possible to get an A.

The whole entire class is based on a quiz on Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday. Don't take this with other hard classes. I love accounting but she made it with so much extra homework and assignments. It's easy to get an A on tests though because you can go back and take all those quizzes again and again to study (tests are legit the same questions)

Hard class because.. accounting. But Larson does a fantastic job explaining things and making more practice and help available if needed. Expect a grade that reflects your effort. The material is spread across the semester in a way that promotes learning in the best order possible WITH real world applications (my favorite part!)

Prof Larson is amazing. She's my favorite professor I've had at BYU. She cares for her students and explains things very clearly. There is a lot of work, but she clearly explains what is required and provides all of the resources necessary. Be ready to work hard. As long as you put in all of the work and use the resources, you'll do great!

Professor Larson is an outstanding teacher, and although the class can be very rigorous and challenging at times, if you keep at it eventually it all comes together as the course is set up very well. The grading is organized and she is clear about what is expected.

Wonderful woman and professor. She makes it very clear what you need to do week by week. To do well on tests, I'd recommend watching all of the recorded online TA reviews! This class is very doable, you've just gotta do all the work expected of you (which is way bearable!) . She cares a lot about you, and this class is very fair and straightforward

This is a great class. Professor Larson is helpful, clear, and positive. Assignments are not very difficult but they can take a few hours. Most of your learning will be watching the accounting videos made by the previous professors. Class is mainly a way to get more credit and get clarification on the more difficult concepts. Can't wait last minute

Melissas super cool and just a nice person in general. This class can be kind of hard for some people but I found it to be really simple as long as you just do all the assignments and take the practice tests. THE VIDEOS CAN BE SO LONG. If suggest buying the packet with all the slides and then u can kind of skip around in the videos

Great professor. No real text book since you mainly watch videos. Like most of the other posts, if you spend the time to watch the videos and work the problems, you will do well in the class (but, I guess that's the same for every class). She is a great person.

Prof Larson is easily the best professor I've had! She is so clear about what needs to be done and when. She knows her stuff and she does a good job of connecting the content to the real world. The lab was helpful. Steady stream of content that needs to be done so don't get behind. She's so good she almost makes me want to be an accountant!

Prof Larson is a great teacher! The class moves fast and you have to keep up. There's only 1 in class lecture per week but 2 online lectures you have to watch each week. If you make time for the class and the online quizzes, you'll do great! I never found this class overwhelming. This has been my favorite class so far at BYU!

Professor Larson has Accounting 200 set up as one of the best run classes at BYU and my personal favorite. The homework is important to complete, but not excessive or very hard. Going to lecture was always a blast, sit next to people that understand the material well. The tests weren't bad if you did the practice exams and review quizzes.

Professor Larson has hit the amazing balance of creating a structure that if followed- makes it almost impossible not to get a good grade in this class. I think on average I spent 7 hours a week on this class (outside of the class hours)- but in doing so, I really began to understand accounting. She is also incredibly caring!

Prof. Larson doesn't usually teach Accounting 310, which is unfortunate because she did such an amazing job at it! 310 is the hardest class I have taken at BYU. It is a weed-out class. Even though it was super tough, Larson was very supportive and caring and I felt the spirit more in her class than any of my others. Take her if you can!!!

The class is incredibly easy if you are logic oriented and have a rudimentary understanding of how a balance sheet works. That said, you have to truly understand what equity is, how assets and firm interests are financed, etc. If you are able to grasp the basics well, the class is great. Test 1-95, 2-100, 3-100, Melissa is a phenomenal teacher.

The class is hybrid so you watch vids & only meet once a week. Pretty difficult material but if you have self discipline and actually put in time studying you'll know exactly whats on the test. The class is curved so the average score is a B. Shes willing to work with you and wants you to succeed. No textbook. Loved this class, just work for it!

Melissa Larson is a gem. Learning accounting is like learning a new language and it is not easy nor does it just come naturally, but Prof Larson does a really good job of giving you lots of resources to succeed. She genuinely wants all of her students to perform well, and you can tell. Take her class seriously, and you can get the grade you want.

She was a very nice teacher who clearly cared for her students. Some of the concepts in that class were very challenging. The tests were pretty difficult, but were not that bad if you worked through the study guide.

Accounting is a very difficult class and is very time consuming. With that being said, skills taught in both 200 and 310 can help you in your personal life no matter your career. Her class is very clear, well structured, and pushes you to grow. She wants you to get into your respective programs, and will do all she can to help you make that happen!

Professor Larson has literally changed my life! She is the only reason I have ever even thought about being an accountant. She is a great professor and really cares for the individual. She does her best to prepare you for exams. Accounting isn't for everyone and I think that is what could make this class difficult for some.

Although this class is difficult, she does a fantastic job of teaching it. She's very clear at explaining the structure of the class and what you need to do to succeed. If you spend enough time going through the practice exams and review quizzes, then you'll do great. If you're struggling in the class, she is happy to give you individual advice

This class was incredibly deceptive. The work load drastically increased after the add drop date, and the final is much harder than she leads you to believe. Before student ratings, instead of using the class to prepare for the final she gives a feel good speech to get higher ratings then made the final much harder than it should have been

I took her class last semester. I just missed the next grade up. I tried to talk to her and all I got was a mass email. Out of respect I did not try again. I just found out that she moved at least one students grade up. Melissa Larson fair I think not. I have never been so disappointed in a professor.

Professor Larson obviously cares about her students as much as she can in a 500 student lecture class. The online course was extremely user friendly and was the best way for me to learn. She does a lot of practice problems in class that you walk through with her. It's a very doable course, but make sure it's your focus that semester.

I went into this class expecting the worst but it was actually quite easy. Just pay attention in class. The online videos you have to watch really aren't that helpful as she goes over all the material in class anyways, just use the online slides to do the reading quizzes. Make sure to do the practice exams and you'll do fine.

I really liked Professor Larson. She is a great teacher and made sure to point out ways the material can be applied in the real world (even if you aren't an accounting major). Her tests aren't easy, but if you put in the effort to study you shouldn't have problems.
I regret taking ACC 200 from professor Larson. I would recommend taking it from someone else. I wish she was more helpful and understanding. The average on her tests were not very high.

She is one of the best! She is super nice and always willing to help. She knows Accounting like the back of her hand. She is amazing because even with over 500 students she can still make the class interesting enough to capture everyone's attention. I thought this class would be boring, but I changed my major to it! LOVE HER

Professor Larson gave us huge practice tests. The tests are required to cover absolutely everything that could be on each midterm and on the final, so if you completely understand the practice tests, you'll do great on the tests. There's tons of resources and practice problems that take time to completely understand, but getting an A is clear cut.

Professor Larson was an incredible teacher. The class is structured in a way that makes it possible for anyone that's willing to put in effort to succeed. There are a lot of out of class quizzes, and you will need to devote a good chunk of your week studying for this class but that is the nature of accounting.

Don't listen to bad reviews. Prof Larson is VERY caring and helpful, but your success doesn't depend on her. Class only meets once/week to review online lectures by Prof Nemrow (retired BYU Accounting legend). Commit to watch them closely and PRACTICE! Put in the time. Class is less content/more application. Tests are fair. USE THE ONLINE TA LAB!

Melissa Larson was an OK teacher. Her teaching doesn't match up the tests and quizzes. The class curve was like the person said before. It was 4 question out of all the tests taken. There are question on the test that she does even not cover. I would not recommend her
FYI for anyone taking this class in the future. In fall 2017 this class curved a little more than 1.5% in favor of the students.

I really enjoyed this class. You definitely have to try to succeed but an A is totally achievable. Professor Larsen is a very kind and caring teacher who responds really well to questions despite the large class size. If you watch all the Norm videos and do the assigned practice problems then do the review quizzes before tests, you will do fine.
Professor Larson is amazing! Accounting is a hard class, but she approaches it very well and lets you know what is expected. Do not get behind on the homework, study for tests, and you will do fine!

This is kind of a hard class... if you rush through the hw and don't do all the practice problems and set yourself up to have tough tests. Just watch all the online lectures and do all the practice problems and take it seriously and you'll be fine. Also, she throws in random questions from the yellow in class sheets so STUDY THOSE YELLOW SHEETS!!

Professor Larson was an amazing teacher who truly cared about us students. She was fair and taught interesting lectures. I had class once a week but the rest of the week, I spend on average 6-9 hours watching accounting videos online - the main learning experience. The class solidified concepts. The videos were WAY too long, but were informative.

She's a great professor who is very good at teaching difficult concepts simply. ACC 200 is a hybrid class (both online and 1 class lecture/week), and she has it very well organized. She gives you plenty of resources to succeed, even though it's a tough class. Watch the material, do the homework, come to class and you will do great and learn a lot.

Class is tough but do-able. I never studied other than the homework and maybe two hours before each midterm/final. Lots to know and things get confusing after a month or so. Prof Larson knows the material really well but doesn't answer many questions in class. Go to TAs for help.

She is so amazing and now I am majoring in accounting! You definitely have to put in the work though. Kind of a lot of hours per week watching videos and doing practice problems but thats normal. The practice tests prepare you for exactly what is on the test so do them and you'll be fine

Prof. Larson is super energetic and works hard to get the class involved (hard considering there are 500+ students) She provides tons of materials to help you prepare for the tests and leaves review quizes open so you can improve your grade. The course itself is hard, but she, as a teacher, does an amazing job!

Professor Larson is prepared, organized, energetic, and enthusiastic. I appreciated the careful preparation that went into structuring this course. Unlike so many classes, I was able to find a step-by-step guide of what I needed to complete each class period. I would recommend Professor Larson to anybody.

Melissa Larson is really likable and a great teacher, but the problem is that her teaching doesn't match up the tests and quizzes. This class just became a hybrid class, and the system does not work well. There are hours of video each week. Test questions often have more than one plausible answer and aren't covered directly by material.

Professor Larson is one of the most effective teachers I've ever had. She understands what is going to trip people up and focuses class time on practicing those concepts. If you follow her recommendations accounting comes much easier.

Professor Larson is always available outside of class to offer help if you seek it out. The lectures were really long and the homework took well over 8 hours to complete every week. I basically lived at the Accounting lab my first semester and it still didn't get me a good grade. Larson is a great teacher though.

I really loved Professor Larson! This was my first business class and I really enjoyed it because her lectures were interesting, she talked about real life stuff and brought her own personal life into it so the class wasn't so boring. There is no textbook but there is software that you definitely want to watch to understand the material better.

This class requires a lot of work but Mrs. Larson is the best teacher I have ever had at BYU. She knows the material extremely well and is really really good at explaining it. I hated all the reading and videos outside of class but she was really good at explaining it in her lectures.

This was one of the first classes I took getting home from a mission and after making a career change from medicine to pre-business. The class was very straight forward. It was very clear what I needed to do to be successful. Larson is very organized and very good at explaining and teaching. This was not an easy A, but a VERY possible A.

There's a lot of software to watch outside of class, so be prepared for that, but if you can understand Norm then the lecture part should be more examples of using it. Which shouldn't be too hard. Prof. Larson is nice and easy to talk to outside of class, and the TA lab is really helpful

AMazing teacher! Very organized. She teaches clearly and the information is relevant. The homework is watching videos that go over test material. There are practice exams to help prepare you. I would easily take a class from this professor again.

Dr. Larsen is great, she makes the expectations very straight forward (she will email you before every class period). Accounting can be pretty straight-forward or confusing, depending on the student and how much time you commit to it. Stay up-to-date with the online lectures and study the practice exams and it's not that bad.

Professor Larson is amazing. Seriously my favorite prerequisite for the business school. This class requires you to study, but the expectations are clear and if you put the work in an A is extremely possible. The class is very well organized and its is obvious that Professor Larson cares about her students.

This is a very well structured class. Professor Larson is passionate and manages the class well for there being 500 plus students in there. Follow along in class (don't feel overwhelmed if you feel lost, you get fed more info than you need), and then tackle the practice tests literally 3 times before the test. If you can can do that, you'll be ok

Professor Larson is incredible. The subject of accounting can be an acquired taste, making it hard to get sometimes. But, Prof. Larson is very effective. She supplies resources given to succeed and achieve the grade you want, and it is specific on how you can. It just depends on you to do it all consistently throughout the semester.

I do not think the class is hard if you prepare well before lectures and make sure you understand each lesson by doing the practice problems by yourself. This is one of the best classes ever, so applicable!
Professor Larson is incredible! She teaches very well and is a fantastic professor. I would recommend taking this class from her if possible.

I LOVED this class! If you keep on top of the work and watch the software, you'll be fine. Study for the midterms and finals and do the practice tests... they help a ton! Sister Larson is the nicest person and really cares about her students. You're in a class with like 600 people but you can still tell she really cares about her students!

GREAT professor. Very organized, clear expectations, and sets you up for success should you choose to do the work (Which is definitely required). It's a hard class, but if you know the material well enough to do well on the practice tests, you will do well on the tests themselves.

She was a great teacher, effective, commanding, knowledgeable, relatively interesting for the course material. If you want to understand the material and do well on tests you must sit through a couple of hours of online accounting video materials per week, which I had a hard time doing. Liked the prof, disliked the subject matter. You can do it!

She is the best! She made a difficult class so much easier. She knows how to explain things in an easy way and she is always willing to help. She is always walking around looking for students with questions or problems. She is an excellent teacher. The class is very organized and if you put in the effort you can get an A. Definitely recommend her.

Professor Larson is good at making the lectures interesting, and overall it was a good class. Just be aware that it will take a lot of work time outside of the classroom. You do a lot of independent learning through software video lessons, and you have two quizzes a week. If you keep up, you will be fine. Just don't get behind.

Professor Larson is a great person, and does well at explaining the content in class. Although if you really want to do well in this class, you will have to be your own teacher. You have to really study and do the work she assigns or you will not do well on tests. There are only three tests that make up 60 percent of your grade so don't slack!

Prof. Larson herself is very engaging and very good in teaching the content. But I cannot stress this enough: THIS CLASS IS HARD!!! It is a weed-out class (and she admits it) for the Accounting program, and if you aren't fully invested in the lectures and outside of class readings, you are going to have a really hard time. Tests are very hard, too.

Prof. Larson is an amazing teacher with a very organized class. She makes accounting applicable to everyone. That said, it is a HARD class. The tests are what will make or break your grade. Though she says otherwise, the class is meant to weed out those not qualified for the accounting program. Great teacher, but not easy.
Lectures are clear and as long as you did the homework you will understand what is going on. She explains well and fast so be alert.

I would take this class over again if I could. Professor Larson is one of the nicest people and she really wants to help. Also she is super good about responding to any questions you have. Loved this class even though it was kind of difficult,  as long as you use all your resources and put in the effort you will do great!

Professor Larson is FANTASTIC. Her lectures are great, she gets to the point and explains the material well. You will spend plenty of time outside of class with the software but if you put in the time you will do well. Larson clearly outlines what you need to do, and doesn't make you do unnecessary busy work. GREAT CLASS.

She made Acc 200 enjoyable and the lectures were never boring. The information learned will be helpful in and outside of college. Make sure to spend plenty of time studying for the tests. If you go over the practice exam multiple times you will do well!

Professor Larson is one of my favorite teachers at BYU! Accounting is hard, but she makes it fun and she totally changed my entire view of accounting and now its my major. If you take three seconds to go up and introduce yourself it makes a world of difference. The practice tests REALLY help!

Professor Larson is the BEST.  She is so amazing in the way she teaches. I don't necessarily call myself good accounting but it was a doable class and subject because of her. She loves what she teaches but doesn't expect all of us to love it as much as she does. She is approachable and easy to understand. One of the best professors on campus!

I loved Professor Larson! She is AMAZING! Great lectures, always gave clear and specific instructions, and you could tell she cared about you even in a lecture full of 800 students. She inspired me to do accounting! Definitely hope I have her for another accounting class!

Prof. Larson is an inspiring person to learn from! She took time to answer all my questions and personally meet with me. She is very understanding and a great mentor. What you put in to this class is what you will get out. I worked hard and I loved the material. Apply yourself.

I felt babied in this class. It wasn't very clear or as rigorous as Fin 201. I was bored in class. It's norm or bust. The online textbook is very lengthy and unclear. I got an A- with very little effort. You either get this stuff or you don't. Some definitions are very subjective. Need to really pay attention to handouts and quizzes. Don't slack.

I loved Accounting 200. It isn't for everyone, but Melissa Larson made it a great class. The software (Norm Nemroe) is really dry, but teaches a lot. Be prepared to work, but this is a class everyone should take. Great class!

Good -Extraordinarily clear grading policy -Everything is very well-planned out -Provides a LOT of resources to help you succeed -Accounting lab is awesome -Tests weren't terrible  Bad -Video watching assignments were as much as 4 hours/class -Graded on attendance -Tests were pretty tough, but at least straightforward -No extra credit

I loved Professor Larson! She really understands accounting and is willing to help you out when you need it. She explains concepts clearly in class. We usually only have class once a week because the other days we are watching videos on the online software. The tests are tough but learn the concepts in the practice tests and you will do well.

I loved this class because it was fair. Professor Larson had very clear expectations for us. It's very possible to get an A, but you have to watch the software as scheduled, attend class, and study until you know the material backwards and forwards for the tests. Professor Larson is entertaining and helpful.

Professor Larson really changed my perspective of accounting and business. Expect to spend long hours on software, and don't get behind! Don't rely on your notes on quizzes or practice problems to study for tests (everyone fails the first one, but still study). Super helpful class for anyone. Changed my major to accounting because of this class.

I loved my Accounting class, despite the horror stories I found everything in the class to be very fair and doable. The software is long but it really does help. I loved how she tied in gospel principles in class and shared her real life stories with us. She made me love Accounting and I am considering to major in it.

Prof Larson is an amazing teacher! She really cares about helping her students succeed and provides them with all the help and reminders you need to stay on top of things. Acc 200 is not an easy class but doable!!! Just get ready to watch a lot of lecture videos and take lots of notes!

Professor Larson was an AMAZING teacher. By far the most clear teacher I've had at BYU. Though there is a lot of homework involved, you know exactly what to do, how to do it, and when it was due. I liked this class a lot.

Professor Larson changed my perspective on school work and study.  She has the most organized class I've ever seen and that helped a ton.  It's a hard class and it's meant to be.  It will take up time, but it's worth it.  There is a small curve, but just don't get behind and it'll work out.

She is an excellent teacher and provided many resources to help us learn. I enjoyed lectures because she explained concepts well and didn't bore me. There was a lot of work outside of class. It was a hard class. There are lots of opportunities to learn. I had no problem with the professor. It was just a hard class.

Prof. Larson is the best acc teacher out there! She seriously gives you every single tool to succeed. This class is so organized and she tells you exactly what to study. Youre going to have to work for it, i studied like crazy for the tests but if you dont get behind and go to the TA lab you have no reason not to do well.

I love Professor Larson. She is awesome. Really good teacher and makes it really interesting. Downsides: in-class  lectures sometimes moves really fast,  there are a lot of test questions that are logic not problem based that are hard to prepare for.  TA lab is really helpful. She is a really good teacher. Put in hard work and you'll do fine.
She's amazing. That's all.

Prof. Larson is fantastic! She details everything you need to do from the very beginning. All you have to do is do the work. It's a lot of HW, but it's manageable if you pace yourself with some HW each day. Prof. Larson is extremely helpful and clear, and really wants her students to learn and understand accounting. Could not recommend higher.

You have to do A LOT of work outside of class but that being said, Professor Larson is a great teacher and helps you to understand the concepts taught in the accounting videos you are supposed to watch. Tests are pretty tough but she gives practice quizzes that are similar to what will be on the midterm and final so you just have to study those

Great Professor! Clear teaching style, she teaches complex topics to the understanding of an entry level accounting class. Lots of group work. To get an A get ready to dedicate 3 or 4 hours of homework per class period. Tests were tough but manageable if you study.

LOVED Professor Larson! She is an accounting machine. iClicker quizzes were used to record lecture attendance, but lecture was only held about every other class period. The rest of class consists of software days using Norm's lessons. Professor Larson is super sweet and ready to answer any of your questions. Tests are tough but doable if you study.

My favorite thing about Prof Larson was all of the materials she had available to help you succeed. She had practice quizzes, online software with more practice questions, recordings of her going through problems, handouts in class, powerpoints of all her lecture material, office hours, TA labs. It was a lot of work, but I learned SO much.

Professor Larson is amazing. She is charismatic and really cares. She wants students to understand. The class is super well organized. That being said, the class is TOUGH. 2 hours+ of videos to watch per class and quizzes every period. Nice thing is you only have to go to class once a week usually. It feels great once it's over and conquered!

Professor Larson is the bomb. One of the best and brightest they have in the accounting program and they chose her to teach the entry level accounting class. The class is large, so spend lots of time in the TA lab to understand things. You watch lots of software and take online quizzes for every class period. She is super sharp, always on the ball.

She loves her students and really wants you to succeed. You will need to work for it though! This class is hard because you cover so much material, the class size is about 700 students, and it is a really competitive pre req. Despite all that I can say she may be one of the best professors at BYU.
Gives clear and concise explanations.

Wow! Professor Larson is the best. Work hard and keep up with the work load and you can easily get an A. Spend time learning the material, not memorizing it, and you will do excellent on the exams and quizzes. Also, the software is bomb!! This class will make you want to be an accountant.

You can get a good grade in this class as long as you do the work. Be sure you set aside enough time to do the software. It is so important to this class. Tests are just like the practice exams--do them and make sure you understand it all and you'll do well. Prof Larson is great. She makes it interesting and understandable and wants you to do well.

Professor Larson is awesome. She is super helpful and a great teacher. Also makes the class somewhat interesting. She is super on top of things and is also reminding you about upcoming assignments and she really wants you to do well int he class and really wants you to do well in accounting. Take this class from her.

Professor Larson is THE MOST organized professor I've ever had. She is so on top of it, and somehow is so there for you and loving to her students even in a lecture hall. Accounting is very hard for me but she made it fun! (textbook noted is online software)

Professor Larson is great. The accounting program just tries to weed out people in ACC200 so it is a rather difficult course. The tests are hard and there is a ton of material to cover. I learned a lot but there was a lot of unnecessary busy work involved as well.

She's a good teacher with a difficult class.  Higher work load than other classes.  Only has class about 50% of the time, if you don't have class you watch 2-3 hours of accounting video.  She explains difficult topics well.
This class is basically learn on your own. The class is just going over what you learn and make sure you understand the topics.

Prof. Larson is an amazing person and professor. Go to her office hours! She is always willing to explain hard concepts. It is evident in the way that she teaches that she loves what she does. I put a lot of time into this class and I loved it! If you are dedicated and use the TA's and Prof Larson you will get an A. 100% recommend her.

Professor Larson is a very kind, helpful, smart, courteous teacher that teaches with clarity and focus. Class attendance is a must, but you wouldn't want to miss it anyway. The workload is exaggerated slightly, but you CANNOT afford to get behind. If you pay attention to the software and in class, budgeting time, you'll succeed.

Professor Larson is an awesome teacher! You will learn so much new information in this class. You learn most of the material through a software system where Norm will teach you all that you need to know. Class was mainly a review of the software, but she also talked about some topics that Norm doesn't discuss in his online lectures. Great class!!!

Professor Larson is a wonderful teacher. She provides many different ways to learn the material via class, reading, video, etc. You only go to class half of the time, and the other half you do a software. I enjoyed this class a lot.
This class was very challenging, but that is simply because there is a lot of material. Professor Larson is a very good teacher and impressed me on day 1. Tough, but worth it without a doubt.

She is the BEST teacher. She teaches everything we need to know. She stays focused and on track. She explained everything. The class is difficult, but doable. Do the work and you will get the grade you deserve. BEST TEACHER

Prof. Larson only teaches half of this class. She leaves the other half to be taught by a software program that cannot answer questions. The study guides give no clear indication of how you will do on the tests.

There was a comment below about the practice tests not being similar to the real test. That is a lie. They are almost identical, only the numbers and answers change. Study hard and care about the material and if you put in the necessary time you will do great. Larson is super organized and helps you never miss assignments with weekly emails.

Professor Larson is an amazing teacher! She teaches clearly and provides lots of resources to help you practice the concepts. She was really helpful when I had questions. If you do everything she provides for practice and do all of the software, you can ace the exams. She's also good at applying accounting principles to daily life.

Melissa Larson is the most organized professor I have ever had. The class is tough but there are no excuses because you are told exactly what you need to do to be successful. This is my favorite class I have ever taken. Great material, great teacher, great software. The tests are comparable to the practice tests just a little more tricky.

Prof Larson is probably as good as it gets when it comes to ACC 200. The class is definitely tough and demanding but she does a really good job keeping things interesting. You basically go to class once a week and her lectures are very good. She explains things well and offers great practice exams in order to get you ready for the midtermsfinal

It's broken down into software days and in-class days but really it's software days and software + in class days. Get ready to watch hours and hours of Norm's software every single week. Tests are the majority of your grade and they are extremely hard. Study all day and you'll still get a 70. Teachers nice but won't help with your grade at all.

You need to know everything that she tells you and that you watch in the software to do good in this class. This class should be your priority. I do not recommend Professor Larson if you are not a good test taker.

Everything is taught by the software and Prof. Larson just reviews it. This class is graded on testing ability. Tests are worth 60% of your grade. Tests are tough, different from practice exams, and have surprise questions. Quizzes are taken every single class period. No extra credit allowed. Softwares are 2-4.5 hours in average.

Professor Larson is a good person.  If it was not for  Norm's Software I would not have done as good in this class. She goes through everything too fast and expects you to know what she is talking about. Tests are tough and different from the practice exams. Tests have tricky questions. Make sure you remember EVERY word taught to get an A.

Professor Larson is fantastic and VERY organized. The tests are difficult but if you work hard on the practice tests and in-class worksheets you will do well. She sends out weekly emails with reminders and tips that will help you a bunch. Do not get behind on the software. Take this from her! (I think she is the only one who teaches it anyway)

Wow. Professor Larson is one of my all time favorite professors. She made me fall in love with Accounting. Classes are super interesting. Tests are exactly like practice tests. She is always there if you need help. The accounting lab is THE BEST- it is practically always open and the TAs are extremely helpful. I would love to take this class again!

She's a great teacher, and the material is really clear. The practice tests are very helpful. There are a lot of assignments (post class quizzes and software work), but she gives a lot of leniency. Great professor, Highly recommended. Actually made accounting interesting.
Really helpful. Professor Larson has been by far my favorite teacher this semester. Tests are tough but that's a basic expectation for an accounting class.

This class uses software so you go to class half the time and watch online videos for the other half. The first test is the worst so don't freak out  but the class really wasn't that hard as long as you work for it. DONT GET BEHIND

Larson is by far the most organized professor i have had at byu. and that organization translated to me being more organized and scoring high on tests. accounting is hard, but if you put in the time you're golden. she teaches very clear. love accounting because of her!
Hard class, but if you watch Norm, do the quizzes, and go to class you should be in good shape. TAs can be helpful for trickier parts

She is a good teacher but the software program is actually the one that helps you the most. She is there in the class to help but sometimes is hard to understand. You need to keep up with the software schedule. If you don't follow what you are suppose to do before class, you will not understand anything she says.

Professor Larson is hands down one of my favorite GE teachers here at BYU. All my other GE Professors are terribly boring and there is so much busy work. Her class is awesome because everything she gives you helps you learn the material and prepare for the tests. She is super helpful and teaches very well. I would recommend her class to anyone!

Prof. Larson is great. She is very helpful and whenever you are struggling with a concept you can always go to her office during her office hours and she will explain you. (Make sure you have meaningful questions). Exams are tough because they can be tricky. If you like Acc you will like prof. Larson.

Professor Larson is a great professor. She knows what she's talking about and has a great affinity for explaining it to students and somehow make accounting sound interesting. The class is a little boring and you have to watch a lot of "software" but Professor Larson is great and should come highly recommended.

In terms of the actual accounting process (journal entries and such), she won't teach you much herself. The online videos will be where most of the information is taught. Class time, is spent on applying what's in the videos (sometimes). Prior to the first test, she spent a lot time trying to convince us to become CPAs.

Professor Larson was a fantastic teacher! It is very clear what needs to be done in the class and outside of class. She was a very good teacher making the topics covered clear for students to understand. She was always willing to help each person individually even though I was in a class of 500. I would highly recommend this class!
I would take her again.
Great class and teacher. Half the class is online so that's nice that you don't have to go into class half the time, but it does take a bit of time. Be ready to work hard, but great class.
Really interesting class but tough tests and an incredibly time consuming class

This is definitely a tough course anyway, but if I were to recommend a professor to take it from is would be Professor Larson. Her lectures are very clear. If you do the reading assignments, it's super easy to follow along with her in lecture. She's happy and excited and helps you learn. I'd recommend her for Accounting 200.
Professor Larson is an awesome teacher. I think she explains things really well. Make sure you do your practice exams and pay very good attention in class!

Professor Larson is a good teacher.  The class itself is relatively difficult, and it requires a lot of time outside of class. The videos for the class are essential as they teach you most of it, and then in class she expounds upon it, really helping it to make sense. If you put in the time and effort an A is definitely attainable.

I took Accounting 200 because I had to take it to get into the business school.  I went in thinking that it would be boring and just number-crunching, but Professor Larson really made accounting come to life and applicable.  She was really clear in her lectures, sent out helpful reminder e-mails, and you can tell she truly cares about her students!

Professor Larson is great! She really knows her stuff. She keeps you interested in class. You have to go to class to take the iclicker quizzes that is only graded on participation. But class is fun (most of the time) so you might as well go. I highly recommend her. I think she is the only Acc200 teacher anyways!
She really seems to know what she's talking about and gives great lectures.

I ABSOLUTELY LOVED HER CLASS!!! She really made the material easy to understand and gave us every opportunity to do well! There are in-class and software days. The software days are when you learn most of the material through an interactive textbook but you need to go to class to solidify the information!

Great class. Professor Larson does everything she can to help her students succeed. It is clearly defined and understood from the beginning what is needed to get an A. If you put in the time, you will get an A. If not, you will fail horribly.

Dr. Norm Nemrow is pretty much the real teacher of the class because everything is taught on the software that students have to watch. She is good at helping to fill the gaps and does her best to make concepts clearer.

Easy class if you watch the software videos. TAKE THE PRACTICE TESTS. Almost everything on the tests comes from the practice tests. If you do well on the practice tests you will do well on the actual tests

Professor Larson is amazing! She is willing to stop and explain a question even though the class is huge. The harder topics are covered in class while the easier topics you cover yourself. Send out weekly personalized email with all the class information. Take accounting 200 from her!

Sister Larson is great! The class is kinda really boring, but you know that if you're getting into Accounting. She makes it as good as it can be. As far as professors go, you're not gonna find a better one.

Sis. Larson was AMAZING!  Her lectures were great and she would always explain the most difficult topics in class and then require you do the easier topics on your own as homework (she somehow always knew which concepts were the most difficult).  She brings professional expertise to the classroom and that cannot compare with many other professors.

Best ACC Professor!!! Prof. Larson cares so much about her students. The time and effort she outs into helping you stay on track is astounding. ACC 200 is a little tricky as a subject, but I highly highly recommend taking it from Larson. She is personable, very responsive to emails, etc., and a pretty good lecturer

Professor Larson is by far my favorite professor at this school. The way she teaches is so clear and easy to understand. She really sets things up for you to get an A, the rest is just whether or not you want to work for it. She teachers to huge classes, but makes you feel like it is a 20 person size class. LOVE HER!

I LOVE Prof. Larson! She is funny and really cares about each of her students.  She is responsive, and puts a lot of time inside and outside of each class. She also sends out weekly emails reminding you of class info. HARD class but very valuable. Do ALL the work and this will be a great class! I highly suggest finding study groups. Choose Larson!
Great class and great professor. Her content and grading scale are clear. Reviews are very similar to tests. Just do your work and you will do fine.

Awesome teacher. Engages the class and makes the topic interesting for everyone. Most of the work is done with the software but she explains the most difficult topics in the most clear way possible. I would recommend her to anyone taking accounting.
All you have to do is pay attention hard core during the software, and use the practice exams they are a life saver.

She's got my vote, hands down the BEST professor that I have had at BYU. Follow her schedule and do  everything that she says. This class has to be your priority if you are going to succeed. I wish I could take all my accounting classes from her.
Excellent teacher! She understands the difference between engaging the class and doing pointless class activities. If only more teachers could figure that out!

I liked professor Larson a lot and from what it seems, her tests are a lot easier than Stice's. 28 online quizzes after every class, along with software. She did well at explaining concepts. Any accounting class at BYU is going to be a beast, so expect to work.  I would take her again for sure!
Great Professor. Plus her voice sounds exactly like Ellen DeGeneress's so that makes things even better

Prof. Larson was awesome. I had her for both financial accounting classes in the Junior Core and was so happy because of it. Taught with clarity, helped students whenever we needed help. One of the best professors at BYU.
Great professor, I can't recommend her highly enough! One of the best that I have had at BYU, it is a shame that she can't teach every section of the Jr Core
Fantastic teacher!  Always took the time to help and explain.

She is an amazing professor. Accounting is difficult, but she has a way of explaining things very clearly.  She is always willing to help in any way that she can.  She is one of my favorites I have ever had.  Take her if you can!
Awesome class and teacher. Very helpful and always looking to make our experience better.

Prof. Larson has a way of making the concepts sound simple until you actually try to do the problems!  Hard, Hard, Hard.  But she is compassionate and helpful.  She makes herself available and cheers for you.  Amazing professor.
Cares about students, and strives to make even the most difficult subjects understandable to every single student.

Extremely helpful professor. She will explain things in many different ways if people are having a hard time understanding, so everyone can get it. She is willing to really help you get the material and succeed. Very kind to students in general. I haven't met anyone who didn't like her in our classes.
I had a really great time learning from Professor Newberry! She was understanding and kind. She had really well thought out and fun activities and she made the best of our class time!

Dr. Newberry was great! Don't let the bad reviews scare you. She is so kind and class was fun. She has a couple extra credit assignments which helped cushion my grade, allows for a revision on the midterm, and all book quizzes and the final were open book. Sometimes the class felt a little time-consuming and like busywork, but it wasn't difficult.

This class was fantastic and I really enjoyed it. There is a required book you will need for weekly readings. Each day in class has an associated assignment that is completed in class. Attendance is not graded but is important so you can get those assignment grades. She is very helpful and accommodating.

I loved this class and it was a great experience. I was afraid of it because of the negative reviews but they are wrong. Dr. Newberry is amazing and I got so much out of this class. She allows for revisions. For example I got like a 70 on the midterm and resubmitted and got a 90. Take this class from her.

I don't know why Dr. Newberry has so many bad reviews because she is a great professor! Some of the assignments are time-consuming (like reading the chapters), but if you put in the work, then you get a LOT out of the class. She does a great job adding variety to the class and making it engaging. I highly recommend it; you will learn a lot.

BEST CLASS EVER
SO APPLICABLE TO TEACHERS
INSPIRED
Not that hard, just budget time well. You DO need the text book
She has a bad RBF, but she is not mean, just communicate with her
lots of fun activities. I wish I has taken this class closer to graduation so that it will be fresher for student teaching
This class reminded me why I want to teach

Dr. Newberry actually was great. I was expecting her to be worse based on all these reviews, but I really enjoyed her class. She knows her stuff, she's just strict on attendance policy.  Most of your points come from in class activities so do NOT miss the class. It was a fair amount of work and very enlightening.
Easily the worst educational experience I have ever had with a professor.

She is really bad at communicating how she feels with her students. I think every student had an issue with trying to get on the same page with her, you have to really dig deep with even simple things like basic assignment expectations, due dates, ect. If you are on the same page, it is likely not a similar page as much as it is her page.

I was nervous to take the class from her because of the reviews I read. None of them were true. She is a nice and caring professor. She grades harder, but allows for revision. Her lectures are fun with interesting activities. She genuinely cares about her students. Please take from her. The final was stressing me out, but I just did it not that bad

Dr. Newberry really knows what she's teaching, isn't a super hard grader, and her assignments take a lot of time but are pretty doable. There's a lot of reading and you lose points if you miss class, but it felt like a pretty standard 300 level college course. I was scared by the old reviews, but it wasn't bad--I learned a lot, and she was cool.

RUN AWAY! She knows her stuff but over the top with assignments. So much unnecessary busy work and a bad grader. Most entertaining thing is we listened to Weird Al and she was getting into it. Bad tests, bad assignments and TERRIBLE with teaching classroom management. Good theories but activities not helpful at all in the real classroom. STAY AWAY.

Dr. Newberry is definitely proud of being a Ph.D. However, she is not a good teacher. She doesn't explain the assignments thoroughly and her rubrics are useless since she doesn't follow them and they are not clear. She is very arbitrary in her grading taking points from students for literally nothing (at least not that she explains). WOULD GRADE 0

She did not make it clear what she wanted, we had a lot of busy work and pointless assignments. She let us redo certain assignments for a better grade, but she and her TA were very arbitrary in grading our essays and we are expected to provide tons of details. If you go over the limit, they will take an inordinate amount of points! RUN AWAY!

She contradicts her lectures with her style of teaching. She called me out in front of the entire class more than one time and was unapologetic when the reason I was on my phone was that I received news that my dad had cancer, also she can't really handle confrontation with her students. The class was interesting, she made me not want to go though

Good: Every assignment has a rubric. She lets you redo certain assignments for a better grade. She uses lots of participation activities. Bad: She is super inflexible. Because there are so many in-class assignments that you can't make up, missing even one day can lose you 30-40 points. It felt like we were teens who needed managing, not adults.

I really enjoyed Dr. Newberry. The ratings are correct that she is a tough grader but some of the assignments she lets you redo for full credit. You must come to class! In class, she gives assignments that are graded but they are graded for effort. Class was fun and engaging. Also, no final exam, or midterm exam that is based on memorization!
Good teacher, but tough grader. Assignments are relevant and don't feel like busy work. Group midterm, no final. Class is long and you will feel it at almost 3 hours once a week.

Dr Newberry is SO knowledgeable & I learned SO much from her class. Yes there's work but you can redo assignments to earn a better grade. She's organized & clear about everything. As long as you do the work you'll do fine! I really enjoyed class with her. She reminded me why I want to be a teacher & to not let anyone make me feel less because of it

Pretty good at teaching, and the assignments helped in learning and were changed with each new section, helping group similar material in your memory and preventing endless repetition. That said, there was a LOT of work, and she starts off running. Took in spring, felt close to expected. Might be worse in Fall/Winter. A bit tough grader, fun class.

I really enjoyed this class. Yes there is work, but for the big assignments lets you turn them in twice to get a better score. She is very clear with her instructions and its all pretty easy if you just put effort in. The class was interesting and interactive. Probably my favorite teaching class I have taken. I felt like I learned a lot .
Hardest teacher I've ever had at BYU. Take this class from anyone else.

TERRIBLE, TERRIBLE class. We had so many things to do which is expected but her grading and the grading of the TA was absolutely ridiculous. Thankfully there were things that could be redone for more points, but even then the class drove me crazy. Do yourself a BIG favor and do not take from Dr. Newberry.

Ridiculously hard grader. Very critical, and takes an inordinate amount of points off assignments for minor discrepancies.  This is a class about teaching, and yet she's never taught anything BESIDES this class. Take from one of the other professors in the department.

Dr Newberry is passionate about her subject matter, which is clear, but she makes this class a ridiculous amount of work to get a good grade. You can redo most assignments for points back, but she grades so specifically on general things, you waste time.  Her TA does most of the grading, and she's just as difficult. Take this from someone else.

I thought Dr. Newberry was a good teacher who made it clear what she wanted, but the class felt a lot more like high school than college. Tons of busy work and somewhat boring/pointless assignments. I don't know why she had such a high difficulty rating though. Honestly if you do the work you'll be totally fine.

The class was not easy to just "coast through." You definitely need to go to each class, even though attendance isn't taken, because you do so much in class for credit. Just go and take advantage of the opportunities to correct and re-turn in work, and you'll get an A (I did!). Just follow the rubric and ask questions! She's INCREDIBLY nice!

She structured the class to be nothing but busy work. Every assignment is "read this chapter/video and then write a 4 page paper on it". There are many of these. She is extremely nit picky about the grading on these. You end up doing every assignment by just going down the list on the rubric rather than trying to actually get anything out of it.

I expected this class to be pretty easy but interesting, and it was very interesting but surprisingly time-consuming. I learned A TON, though. It'll definitely help my teaching, but you've got to commit yourself to this class to do well. I felt like I was constantly summarizing chapters from the book. Dr. Newberry is a great teacher, though.

Dr. Jones is so great! She cares so much about her students, but it is a pretty hard class. Lots of readings and the tests go over things we barely covered a lot of the time, and even stuff that isn't in the study guide, so review your notes very carefully! But the content is so interesting, and she makes it super engaging.

This was her first time teaching this class, and it was a breeze. She gave incredible life advice. You can tell she's kind, and she is very open about her tattoos and life. The kind of teacher you would want to seek for internship help.

Dr. J is really great and knows her stuff. Be ready for lecture to not cover any of the readings, but you will still be tested on the reading material. You'll get to know her personal life and trauma because she uses herself as an example a lot. She really cares about her students and is super funny! NO LATE WORK is accepted

She is an amazing professor, a lil tough grader but not too bad. You HAVE to volunteer 20 hrs throughout the semester so make sure you have time for it. She really explains everything and it makes it so easy to understand.

Professor Jones is a great professor and always makes herself available for her students. I have taken 2 classes from her and every time I am grateful for it. She is incredibly open which makes her classroom feel safe and welcoming. I would highly recommend taking a class from her!

I found Dr. Jones' incredibly narcissistic and prides herself on the fact that she is an anomaly, has an ACES score of 6, and uses class time to trauma dump on her students instead of go to therapy. She is not a good teacher provides inaccurate study guides and includes things on the exam that we have never discussed before.

I loved Dr. Jones! I took 383 from her and absolutely loved the course material and the way she taught it. Her exams are tough and are a big part of your grade, but pay attention in class and make flashcards to study ahead of the exams and you'll be fine. She truly cares about the material and about her students, highly recommend!!
