Dr. Jones is fantastic! I took 383 from her and she made the material so engaging and I looked forward to going to class every week. Her class is graded heavily on exams, and she grades them pretty harshly, but if you pay attention in class and make flashcards you'll be fine. I highly recommend taking any class from her!
Dr. Jones is such a good professor!!! She made this class very doable and allowed for a lot of in class work and collaboration to make sure everyone understood the material. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

I loved talking Ways of Reading from Professor Reed! She is an amazing teacher and person. It is easy to see how much she truly cares about both her students and readings. Prof Reed always made sure to give good feedback and listened to our feedback about the class.

Great professor! I hate english and writing and I actually enjoyed Writing 150 from Dr. Reed! Interesting and informative lectures, and instead of endless essays there were only a handful of manageable, and actually enjoyable projects!

No tech policy in class. The section professors are the ones actually grading your work, so get to know them. I wish they graded stuff within a month, but that might just have been mine. The content of the course is pretty simple, but I would recommend going to the RWC for each big paper for a last check, because grading can be a little harsh

Good professor. Clear rubrics. Reading assignments before every class. After 3 absence, each absence docks your grade. Grad students over groups of 20ish students; they are the one grading your writing, so they matter a LOT. Get to know the section professor! I never needed to go to Dr. Reed's office hours. One group project worth about 10%.

Professor Reed's class isn't super hard, and I feel like overall it was a good class. Attendance is mandatory and graded. There are about four major assignments, and textbook readings that aren't difficult. Pretty standard class!
Prof. Reed is the best! She understands pedagogy so well, and everything she requires us to do is something we will need in the future. It is all immediately applicable, and she is a joy to know!

Dr. Reed is the best! She is so kind, so genuine, and so knowledgeable. I learned so much from her. She gave us a diverse set of readings that were so useful and applicable. I highly recommend her classes.

Even though I don't enjoy writing very much, I felt that professor Reed's class was very practical and not at all filled with busy work. There is a good amount of extra credit to pad your grade, the rubrics are super clear on what is being graded, and she is not a stickler for things like using MLA format or perfect grammar.

Professor Reed requires atttendance!!! You can only miss at most 3 days. I feel like every time I went it was pretty useless. she can be pretty boring and half the time i dont know why we're learning the things were learning. You will get an A in the class if you do all the assignments and show up.

Professor Reed is by all means a wonderful human being. I'm taking the time to write this review is simply because I have roommates that are taking the same course from different professors. Their professors are much more relaxed about deadlines and rewrites, hence why I would suggest taking the course from Professor Philips or someone else.
She is great. The class is very easy, as long as you do your work you will get an A.

This class was pretty easy, just a bit time consuming. I felt like the lectures didn't teach me that much but attendance is mandatory so you have to go anyways. Papers were graded pretty easily, not hard to get an A or even 100% if you read the rubric.

Honestly, don't take Writing 150 from any other professor. Professor Reed is super understanding and so chill. The class is as difficult as most 100 level required courses. But Professor Reed is an interesting lecturerer and she genuinely cares about the students. Teaches the information so well and super clearly.  Clear rubic and a fair grader.

Writing 312 is hard because it's an advanced writing class, but Dr Reed's criteria is good and she gives great feedback on how you can improve your writing. Make sure to take the time to meet with her after you write your drafts so she can help you. I took this class during Spring Term so it was very, very fast. Work diligently and you'll do great!
She is a fair grader and cares a lot about her students. She will always make time outside of class to discuss current projects or give feedback. I would highly suggest taking her classes!

Dr. Reed is wonderful. She clearly cares about the students learning and the assignments are structured so that you apply what you learn. She is so understanding about due dates and life. There is a fair amount of reading due for each class, and consistent assignments, but if you stay on top of things it never feels like too much.

I LOVED Dr. Reed. We read a lot of really diverse pieces and she was super open to all perspectives.  She was a fair grader and engaging lecturer. As a queer student, I am very appreciative that she made it clear 100% from the very beginning that she and her classroom were safe spaces. I always felt spiritually safe and enhanced in her class.  5+

Prof. Reed is a Gem! Get ready to learn some amazing things-how to write better, develop your style-she gives good feedback, creates a caring class, w/smll class size, she takes time to explain things. She changes course from student feedback/needs. My writing improved & so did everyones. 2 midterms-No final exam! WooHoo! + her TAs help a ton.

TAKE ANY CLASS YOU CAN FROM PROF REED! There is a lot of reading and it can feel heavy, but I really recommend working through it because you'll learn a ton--I skipped some and my grade was fine, but I regret missing the info honestly. She's kind and respectful and really wants you to succeed. Class assgts are very clear--and FUN! V helpful class!

Nothing too crazy in this class. I'd say the papers were graded pretty fairly, I never felt like I got grade lower than I deserved, but it is not easy to get as, on the papers. There are some other small assignments that can help your grade but definitely not an easy a.

Dr Reed was so great! Her course was so organized and well thought-out. About 3 big papers with smaller assignments throughout. The readings were really interesting and relevant. She is a great professor and great lecturer!

Dr. Reed is hands down the best professor I've ever had. She has mandatory meetings one-on-one with you to discuss your papers and how you can improve. She genuinely cares about all of her students. You will be a better writer, reader, and researcher after taking this class.

Fantastic professor. Very self-aware that this is a GE for most people, so doesn't make it too difficult. A decent amount of writing, but it builds on itself, so it's a very doable workload. If you need a GE advanced writing credit, this is a great professor and class to take.

This class was hard but definitely taught me how to write. Dr. Reed is also the most caring professor I've ever had. She makes herself available outside of class and has 2 mandatory one-on-one meetings with you. She provides valuable feedback on each of the 3 papers you write. Attendance is a must for good peer feedback. Take from Dr. Reed!

Meredith is the best! The class has a lot of meaningful assignments and I rarely felt like I was doing busy work. Even though it is a writing class, there were only a few major papers. For each one she gives you plenty of time and has a lot of workshops. I would definitely try to take a class from her if you can.

I loved Dr. Reed because every single assignment had a very clear purpose to help us improve our writing. She was totally open and willing to help us outside of class. She really cares about her students and their progress. I loved Dr. Reed and this class! If you have to take 251, take it from her!

Dr. Reed was a really great professor. Her grading wasn't too hard and she was interesting and really knows her stuff. I appreciated having her because I feel like she listened really well to the students and took their needs into consideration as well. She genuinely wants to help her students become better writers. I would 100% suggest her!

She seems like a helpful teacher until it comes to grading. It's very difficult to determine what she's looking for because there are so many criteria. I spent well over 6 hours working on a paper and still got an unsatisfactory grade. She places less value on the overall paper and gets very nit picky.
She was a cool teacher
I really liked Meridith. She was a cool teacher. She was helpful, too, and hands on. She's pretty fair--if you think otherwise, just go have a word with her one on one! It might make a difference!

Definitely take this class from Meridith! She is more interested in helping you actually become a better writer than giving you meaningless assignments. She loves class discussion. She lets you vote on an attendance policy. This is a good class if you are just looking for an easy A, but it also can challenge you and help you become a better writer.

Honestly, the best professor I've had at school. She cares about her subject, she cares about her students, and she makes the subject matter so, so interesting. The work isn't hard, and class goes by quickly. Take this class from her. NOW.

Professor Reed is a very kind, caring person, and she is probably my favorite teacher at BYU. She is clearly very intelligent, and I really respected the things she said in class. I learned a lot of interesting things in the class, and I overall enjoyed my experience.
FANTASTIC professor. Take it from her!! Meredith is so understanding and truly wants her students to excel. You must take her class. Most beneficially GE--solely because of the professor.

Meridith is really great, she makes the class fun to go to. She's really cool, interesting, and fair. I've actually learned a lot, and I originally thought the class was going to be boring and difficult, but it was a lot easier than expected and I've elarned a ton. Meridith is smart, helpful, and great at teaching!
Meredith was a great teacher. Great style. Very clear. Very good at explaining.Very engaging. Made a hard class into a very interesting and fun class.

This subject isn't my favorite part of English,  but Meridith made it as interesting as it could possibly be. She made sure we knew what was going on and made us all feel like our comments were heard and insightful. It was hard to participate every day but she graded very fairly and everyone did well and loved the class.

INCREDIBLE professor. She's young, has a great sense of humor and is very relate-able. She knows how to teach and allow the class to have fun at the same time; I had an absolute blast in this class and learned a lot, too (and all if not most of my classmates felt the same). Take a class from her if you get the chance!!

Great class and professor. I love Meridith's style of teaching - the discussion boards and class discussion works really well. The readings are hard at times (dense, technical), but I found it really engaging. Assignments make sense, and grading is very fair. I'm not in the major - I just took it for fun, and I loved it. I'd recommend it to anyone.

I heard that this class was pretty hard but Meridith made it really interesting and insightful. She is really good at explaining the topics and especially at provoking good discussions in class. I loved Meridith's teaching style and wish I could take more classes from her. Great teacher and great class!

Super great professor. Assigned lots of readings, but was very patient in explaining the difficult ones. Some weekly assignments that were very easy. The tests were written and they graded with a lot of allowance for mistakes.

Dr Kay was a delight, despite a three hour lecture I enjoyed it because he is engaging and interactive. The class was a requirement but I genuinely found it interesting. The assignments aren't very hard and help you learn the content very well. The two tests are rough though it's a lot of writing at once.

Dr. Kay is a good professor, but his lectures are a bit boring and can be difficult to sit through. This class was tough, but if you use the TA, and study the exam guide you will be more than fine. His exams are handwritten essay questions that he creates. Overall, not as bad as I thought it was going to be, I reccomend taking it from Dr. Kay.

Dr. Kay is a good professor. The exams are essay questions, and he gives you a study guide of 8 questions from which he selects 4. START THE STUDY GUIDE immediately and you will be fine. He also has historical readings and textbook readings, you have to write about the historical and report on class discussions. Good class, very much enjoyed it.

This class with Dr. Kay could be difficult at times, but overall pretty interesting and not too hard. We did weekly discussion and reading reflections which weren't too bad or difficult. The topics could be confusing but Dr Kay helps a lot. The tests seem hard but as long as you study all the potential prompts well and use the TA it'll be fine.

I can't comment on workload, because his PSYCH classes are very different from UNIV 101, but I love Dr. Kay. You can tell he cares about his students. He's super nice and a psychologist, I would feel safe going to him with any concern. The UNIV class was kinda boring, but that was because of what BYU forces, not because of Dr. Kay.

I took this class in the Summer semester and was disappointed. I read the reviews and thought it would be a great class. He seemed unprepared the entire semester and lectured and many things that we never used in class. I think this would be a great class to take in the Fall or Winter. DO NOT TAKE DURING SUMMER. But trust the reviews for Fall.

Professor Kay is knowledgeable and passionate. As he teaches it is exciting to analyse and understand further. He is very open to questions and regularly encourages deeper thought. The exams are not very hard and the TA was very helpful. We would basically get lots of the answers from the TA so we could enjoy learning. Assignments are we aligned.

Professor Kay knows his stuff well, but he makes you feel like you are all learning together. His lectures are very engaging if you ask questions and apply yourself. As long as you take good notes and study well, the tests are straightforward as well. He was an amazing professor for an introductory psychology class. I would highly recommend him.

Dr. Kay is pretty chill, and his course isn't that bad. Lots of reading and a decent number of easy assignments. His lectures were long, and a lot of the material didn't seem to be important to what we were tested on. He did prepare us for the tests, and he curves them to 86% average. Overall a pretty easy A if you read, study, & take good notes.

Dr. Kay was a great professor. He made his lectures interesting and interactive. The material is difficult but do the reading and the assignments and you'll be fine. He gives you the slide notes and study guides before the test to take notes with which makes the material easier to learn. Overall a great experience, definitely recommend this class!
Best psychology professor I had at BYU. Cares about his students, and knows his stuff. Thanks for being a great teacher!!

Dr. Kay is such a caring man who always incorporates videos and other examples into his lectures. I would not recommend PSYCH 210 at 8 am because it isn't the most interesting class. Most of the grade is participation, and the exams are open note and online, but they are graded pretty harshly.

I had Dr. Kay for PSYCH 111 and LOVED him, so I took 310 from him, and figured out ir was very different. . Most of it is based around a knit picky database that he or the TA's didn't really know their way around. He was willing to work with us and meet with us, but it'll be harder than other 310 classes because research is his niche.

Dr. Kay is an awesome guy. Super nice and cares a lot about his students. He teaches well and you think that you are prepared for tests, but he really does not teach what is covered on the tests, making this class fairly difficult. The class is focused lots on group work so you aren't prepared for the tests when they come.

Professor Kay is a great teacher! He really respects everyone and makes you think. Sometimes, it's not very clear what we were supposed to be studying for exams, but if you go to his office hours and speak to him, he does a great job of working with you.
He is an incredible teacher, and you can tell he really cares about his students. There is nothing negative to say about him. If you can take a class from him, do it!

He's such a kind teacher! This class is basically one big project, but he and the teaching assistant were more than willing to help every step. I was a bit stressed with creating my own experiment, but Dr. Kay was super understanding and very patient when I needed extra assistance. He's definitely the professor to take this class from!

Dr. Kay is awesome. I had this class when BYU switched from in-class to online. He was SO patient with me and helped me EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. I asked for help. And he gave me full points for the assignments. You can tell that Dr. Kay knows a lot about what he teaches, and truly cares about his students.

Dr. Kay's Psych 210 course is what you make of it - you can easily slop through the work, reading and quizzes, and honestly, you'll get a good grade (if you're good at faking it) OR (and recommended) you can become the best student/ learner you'll ever be. He promotes critical thinking and the development of YOUR opinion. Be ready to work - or not.

"Do all the problems in the back of the textbook! I promise if you can complete the chapter problems without the answer key, you'll do amazing on the tests. His practice exams are very similar to the actual tests. He is super caring and wants you to succeed. He knows the class is hard and is incredibly helpful with any questions you have.

Teaching style is very problem oriented. He mentions doing an extra credit assignment of practice problems from the book, if you do that (like actually do it, not just look at the answers and think you understand it), chances are you'll be chilling and not stressed about cramming for this class come finals time. Best of luck!

Andrus' class can be a challenge, but with the right preparation it's manageable. Definitely use the textbook and take advantage of study aids like unstuck AI to supplement the lectures. Attend class and stay engaged - it pays off on the exams.

Chances are, if you are one of the students who left an awful review of this man, you didn't spend enough time studying on your own. If you prepare for lecture, his lectures make sense, clarify what you need to know for the exams, and are entertaining. Exams are by far the easiest in the department. IF YOU PUT IN THE TIME, best option for ochem 2.

Ochem is hard, but don't make it harder by taking it from him. His lectures are basically practice the whole time, he ignored questions in class, and I felt like it was expected to teach myself everything. The average grade on our final was AWFUL and no one felt ready for it. When I asked him for help he lied to my face about one of the tests. BAD.

Prof. Andrus is probably one of the worst professors I've had. His lectures are hard to follow & he only writes on the chalkboard. There are very few assignments in the class, so beware if you aren't a good tester. His exams aren't incredibly difficult but they dont prepare you for the ACS final. OChem is hard enough & this guy only makes it worse

Andrus does not prepare you well for the tests he gives. It's clear what you need to know but expect to learn it on your own. Class is a demonstration of his ability to do chemistry, not his ability to teach it to anyone else. Take it from someone else if you can because you might actually learn something.

this guy is the worst chemistry teacher at the school. when you go into ask for help he seems very annoyed. his lectures do not prepare you for the test. but I will say if he's the only option it is possible to sneak by with a B. if you want an A wait for another teacher.

Your best chance in this class is to study the text book. His lectures do not reflect the tests. I had an A the whole semester and then his final dropped me down to a B, be prepared to take the ACS final. His writing is kind of hard to follow and goes really fast, watch out for that.

I would say doing the HW book challenge is worth it if you know you are going to end up in the high C or low B area. Otherwise don't bother because I spent probably an extra 15 hours a week working on it for it not even to count. It's a heartbreaking thing TRULY devastating. I'd wait a semester if he's your only option

Andrus is the worst lecturer at BYU. He comes to class and is unorganized and proceeds to do practice problems on the board, rarely taking time for questions and if he does, he sucks at answering them. If you read the book, you should do fine but beware random things he talks about in lecture will likely make it on the tests. ACS standardized final

Only took it from him because he was the only one teaching it this semester. My main beef with the class was that we finished all the Ochem 2 material by the end of October. Everything from November 1st through the last day of class was spent on biochemistry material, including 2/4 exams. ACS final was our final.

If you have a problem with Andrus, it's likely you don't read the book. If you read what you're supposed to before class, his lectures are 90% practicing the reading and can be very helpful. If you approach him with questions he's very kind and helpful. We only had one pop quiz all semester and his midterms are easy if you know what he says to know

I despise how Andrus's lectures flow. After having Dr. Nielson for Ochem 1 this has been a HUGE disappointment. However, his tests are so much easier than Nielson's! If you are good at self-teaching yourself (aka reading the textbook very thoroughly) I would recommend Andrus simply because his tests are much easier than Nielsons. Extra credit!!

He is a good lecturer, but does a poor job of clarifying all content needed to be successful on the tests. I completed his hw book challenge but was not awarded any points for it (or at least it did not change my grade at all) I was very disappointed by this after putting in all that work. He also was not consistent with what is in the syllabus.

Took Andrus for both OChems. OChem 1 was much easier than 2 with him. The textbook he uses is superb, so I really relied on that and felt like it taught me the material and then I could review it in class during lectures. His tests are okay, but the free response questions are really difficult. Pray you get a good TA cuz there are some lame ones.

Dr. Andrus is probably the most disorganized professor I've had at BYU. Lectures were chaotic and did not flow, which was disappointing after having an incredible experience with Dr. Nielsen in O Chem 1. He was pretty aversive to questions; he usually ignored raised hands or gave roundabout answers. Tests were doable but the final was impossible.

What you should know:
- Pre-class readings aren't required but are crucial to saving time and being successful
-  Andrus uses class to practice not to teach much
- Tests are reasonable
- Be prepared for an occasional pop quiz
- Pace yourself and space your studies/hw so the material sticks
- Give yourself some grace--OChem is TOUGH

He's a nice guy, but his class is just alright. You have to read the textbook before coming to class or the lectures aren't helpful. His tests and teaching style are good for learning mechanisms, but not for preparing you for the ACS final. A lot of the class was doing really well until that final. I'd recommend taking the class from someone else.

This man is the worst professor I've had. The material from ochem 1 to ochem 2 isn't harder, but working with him and understanding his lectures was a chore to say the least. He is very socially and mentally absent when it comes to his students and their needs. Even if you can't get into another professor, I would wait a semester than take from him
Lectures are hard to understand unless you read the entire chapter in the textbook carefully. Sometimes beneficial. Study groups and TAs will be your saving grace

The worst professor at BYU. He does not care about his students and his lectures are confusing and sometimes not related to what we need to know. I never review on here, but please do not take this class from him Ochem is already hard enough.

Do not take this class from this professor, its hard enough and he made it 10x worse. Multiple times I reached out to him in need of help and he did not  care to  help, his tests  are very difficult, and his lectures are horrible and very confusing to follow or see the point. The only way to pass is to memorize the textbook.

I'm usually an A+ student. Worst professor I've had. Don't expect to learn anything in his lectures; you have teach yourself from the book.  "I'm great at chemistry myself but hate teaching and the students." sums up his attitude. STAY AWAY! You will be grateful you took it from someone else. Never felt like he cared or wanted the best for students

Dr. Andrus was a decent o-chem professor. His lectures were semi-helpful. His grading criteria are very clear. His tests were fair albeit difficult. This class is not assignment heavy and you really have to study on your own. Read the textbook, it is very helpful.

I've had Andrus twice and it's been miserable both times. In lectures, he's facing away from the students and drawing mechanisms. Explanations are lacking and he is a jerk when you ask him questions. A student in my class asked a good question, the 2nd day, and he said "just stop." Then ignored them. Go to TAs and do the homework to do well.

His tests aren't as bad or as long. Read the book before going to class, then for lecture u already have an idea of what's going on, and then he would explain and expound.
 
Lectures r VERY organized. He laid out all the concepts one by one with practice problems in class. We only had like 3 "pop" quizzes. 91% was an A, and there was a curve.

Worst professor I have ever had. All I'm going to say is class average on the ACS final was a 66%. The ACS is a standardized Ochem final given in the US.  Based on the outcome, it is clear Andrus does not know how to teach, doesn't care for students' success, and does not prepare you to do well. Class average was below 80% and he didn't curve.

Ocher is hard, but Dr. Andrus makes the class very doable. The work load was not too much, there were a couple pop quizzes but if you paid attention in class they aren't too bad. The exams are also very very fair and reasonable, nothing you haven't seen from him before. He is not the best lecturer sometimes but his exams makes up for it!

Andrus is the worst teacher I've ever had. Hes a big jerk. Never would allow questions in class, made my friend cry in his office hours, lectures were useless, no organization, had an exam 3 days before the ACS final, and treated you like an idiot if you asked him anything. He publicly humiliated a student in front of the class. Rely on TAs/ book.

Lectures were useless unless you already read the book and understood the material beforehand. The TAs and book will be your saving grace.  Andrus is an intelligent guy but has no idea how to explain difficult concepts in a clear way and tests often included material we hadnt even covered yet. Dont take from him unless you like teaching yourself.

Definitely the worst professor I've ever had at BYU. Extremely rude to students, doesn't answer questions in class, and made the comment 'I see you all look discouraged' and laughed out loud. The 4th "midterm" was two days before the scheduled ACS final, giving us no time to prepare. Tanked my grade. Lectures useless. Beware at all costs.

Worst teacher I've ever had.  Bad teaching style, and lectures are a huge waste of time, but you still have to go to class for random pop quizzes.  I had a near 4.0 GPA until this class and  I work hard, but his style of teaching sucks. O-chem is hard, so find a teacher that makes the class easier.  Andrus takes a hard subject and makes it harder.

OChem is hard, no going around it. His lectures aren't terribly clear, the textbook and the TA's are what end up teaching you. Practice problems are what saves you and take really detailed notes. "Curve" can really help too! Buy the ACS Prep Book for the final!!!!! Prepare to spend at least 2-3 hours a day on this class.

I felt like I had to teach myself the entire time through the textbook and TA lab. If you aren't extremely well prepared before coming to class, you won't learn a thing. He's a nice person, but probably not my first choice as an instructor for this class.
Dr. Andrus is a good lecturer though he is terrible at answering questions. do the reading before class and it will all be clear, don't do the reading and the lecture will be meaningless.

This is a very difficult class. You will only do well in the class if you teach yourself from the textbook and go to the TA's all the time! He does not prepare you well for exams at all, and there are a lot of them. If you have another option for ochem, take the other option.
Isn't very understanding of his students

Dr Andrus is the best bet for a good grade. Very nice guy, makes you take the ACS exam which is difficult but I recommend buying the ACS practice book and you will ace it. Also he will curve the class average if it is below 80%. Do the practice problems lecture! Test 1 and 2 are easy but 3 hits you hard so work hard and do the HW/quiz problems.

I really enjoyed Dr. Andrus' class. It was very well organized and I was always aware of what was going on and what I had to do in order to do well. I appreciated that he was very efficient in going over the material. However, I would say that reading the textbook was more helpful than the actual lectures.
Dr. Andrus is a very sweet man who is a very boring professor. I stopped watching the lectures because they didn't help me at all on his tests. Go to the recitations!!

Prof Andrus make you work for your grade. He doesn't do much teaching, just a high-level overview so rely on your book. His tests aren't too bad but be prepared to study and prep for everything as he provides no study guides. Beware of the ACS final! It Wrecked my grade and being with the abnormal students that understand this does not help.

I took Andrus for both ochems, but I got an A in 351 and a B in 352. His tests are not super difficult if you do a ton of practice problems, but the 352 final was ACS and cumulative for both semesters and it tanked my grade. He posted his lectures on Youtube so I watched them all after class and that was a lifesaver. BEWARE THE ACS FINAL IN 352

His lectures were understandable, but reading the textbook is a MUST. His testing schedule is brutal. Any emails you send him will receive a not-very-personable 3 to 5 word response that will most likely be a hard no if you're asking for any kind of favor. Good at teaching concepts, but doesn't seem to care about individual students very much.

You have to use the textbook along with lectures. He spends most lectures doing mechanisms, which are not heavy on tests. Most test content is from the book. His tests aren't the kind you can just ace without studying. 4 midterms and final, the last midterm was 3 days before the final. No TA reviews before tests. 1 HW and 1 Quiz each week usually.

Dr. Andrus is super intelligent but that can't go without saying how mediocre he is at teaching. 5 tests with the 5th testing being the ACS final. Prep yourself via the book because his lectures are more of a TA session. Don't expect much in terms of a study guide or test prep. One of the hardest classes I have taken and taught myself.

In terms of grades the average in our class is much higher than any other class. But his teaching style is okay nothing great. He lectures a ton and doesn't slow down for students to write things down. Also my biggest annoyance with this class is that we have a "midterm" 2 DAYS BEFORE OUR SCHEDULED FINAL that covers all of 351 AND 352.

This is a difficult class. Dr. Andrus does not do the greatest job of prepping you for his 5 tests throughout the semester. If you are really wanting to succeed, pay attention to the book and constantly review the material. It is not an easy class and Dr. Andrus fails to truly you prep you for the exams.

Going into this class, I knew that it was going to be pretty hard. I think that his teaching style didn't really click with me right away and I didn't clue in until too late that you really have to rely on your textbook to teach you the coursework. Someone told me that you should use the textbook to teach you then use Andrus as a TA during lectures

Professor Andrus does a great job in lectures, but you will only be able to follow along if you read the textbook! Definitely read read read the textbook. The lectures and quizzes and homeworks felt supplemental to the book. Very clear grading, and you can tell he wants students to do well in his class. Hardest class I've taken at BYU so far.

I think Dr Andrus is great. Class is very straight forward and I always knew what he expected of us. I wish lectures were a little more engaging. But then again, most of it was pre-recorded because of COVID so with that in mind I think he did great.

Dr. Andrus is a legit good guy, just not so great a professor. He's really intelligent and I think he sometimes struggles to "dumb-it-down" for his students. He is usually quite vague in lecture, and make a LOT of assumptions of his students' comprehension, usually to their detriment. If chemistry comes easy to you, you'll probably be okay.

His lectures are mediocre at best, and while he likes to stress that he wants to help students, he is the least available and least helpful professor I have ever had the displeasure of taking a class from. I almost always get an A in my classes at BYU, and this was only the second class I did not, largely due to how unavailable he and my TA were.

Dr. Andrus is interesting. His lectures aren't amazing, but they aren't bad either. The TA recitations were really what helped me understand. The best part is the practice tests; they are very very similar to the actual tests, so make sure you do them! I skipped chem 105, 6, and 7 and went straight to this and it was manageable (but challenging).

A lot of reading is required, but honestly it was the easiest chemistry class that I have ever taken. His tests were super straight forward, and he was always willing to sit down and answer questions. I would 10/10 take a class from him.
He was a great professor. He understands us when it comes to grades, and tries his best to give as many A's as he can.

I loved taking ochem from Dr. Andrus. Its a really tough class but its worth it! Its been my favorite class Ive taken at BYU! I started off really poorly in the class and almost withdrew but Dr. Andrus told me to stay strong and keep going! I did and it was totally worth it! Hes clear and upfront about the material but tries to make it fun!

Ochem is hard but Dr. Andrus was significantly easier than the other professor I had. Tests were very similar to practice tests in questions and difficulty. Never felt like he was trying to trick me on questions. Quizzes and homework combine for about 30% of the grade and are very doable. An A ended up being an 88 after a hefty curve. Best option.

I've had three different O. Chem. professors at BYU and Dr. Andrus was by far the easiest. Even the TA's say he is the easiest professor to take O. Chem. with at BYU. His tests are extremely fair. He doesn't try to trick you, but tests you on what you know. I would highly recommend taking O. Chem. from him.

He's a difficult professor, but he outlines what students should expect for passing the class. He explains everything clearly, and often goes over test problems in class, verbatim. Great professor, would take again.

He was very inconsistent with the other professors who taught this class. He taught on many subjects not found in the textbook and which are very difficult to study. I felt he wasn't actually teaching to the university standards but to his own and it shows when he asks questions in class and nobody can answer them. Memorize everything or fail.

Dr. Andrus is the best professor for your grade (more quizzes/graded homework, and easier tests), but doesn't teach super clearly. You'll have to work really hard before class to learn the material as his teaching style is kinda random and not as much teaching as it is just talking about Chemistry. Reading before class is a MUST.

He gives random pop quizzes to make sure you come to class and stay on top of the readings. Cramming is bad in his class because of this. He doesnt assign to much HW; he only gives you what you need to master concepts. His tests are fairer than all the other professors. Id recommend taking his class

Professor Andrus KNOWS his stuff. That's what I enjoyed about him. You can ask him any question, and he'll have the answer. Read chapters and do practice problems before lecture because there are in class quizzes that are worth a fairly good portion of your grade. I would take him as a teacher any day.

The course material comes hard and fast. He is a genius! Went to an ivy league school on scholarship! The first half of the semester, it seemed like he was teaching over our heads. I did a lot better by reading the book before class - even if I didn't understand it then. He is also easily accessible. Also, use the TA labs - it saved my life.

I learned SO much in this class, including how to sift through material; Dr. Andrus offers a lot of fun facts that aren't always relevant to the test or curriculum, which can make it challenging, considering the latter half of the semester is very memorization-heavy.  However, he is extremely kind and willing to help.  Don't miss class!!

Lets's be honest, Dr. Andrus isn't the best at understanding and answering student questions. He loves chemistry and often took up the entire class talking about something irrelevant. I often left the class wondering why I came. Bottom line is, know what is on the test then memorize the heck out of it and you will do fine

He's a solid teacher, but seems to forget that students are taking more than just his class. Expects you to work alot. The hardest thing in this class was keeping up with readings and memorising literally everything. His tests are hard, but it's good preparation and makes the final seem easier. Overall a good teacher and willing to answer questions

He really is a nice guy who genuinely loves chemistry. With that being said, however, I would never take a class from him again. His lectures go all over the place, and he expects you to remember kind of obscure things. Its a gamble, depending on the day, if he will be nice to people who have questions, or treat them like they're stupid.

He is very hard to follow sometimes during lectures. He puts some random things from lectures in his tests sometimes that you would never expect to be on a test (like a specific molecule's effect in a certain drug). But, he has a big heart and loves his job! And is always smiling!

He can be confusing and hard to follow when teaching. If you'r really struggling to understand a concept, ask the TAs instead. However he is kind, caring, and interested in your success. Tests are very hard but he wants you to succeed and he is always willing to help students.

Dr. Andrus loves what he teaches but it is often hard to follow him and his lectures.  I took his class Spring Semester with no other classes.  I got an A because I formed a study group, became good friends with the TA, and basically lived in the TA lab all semester.  Get ready for a lot of reading, memorization, and application.

I TA'd for Doctor Andrus after taking this class and thoroughly enjoyed sitting through it, again. Dr. Andrus is extremely knowledgeable about his field and is probably the happiest lecturer I've ever taken. Be careful to note any interesting facts that he repeats, as they will probably be on tests. Study the book and dedicate lots of time to class

Tough class but I really enjoyed it. Professor Andrus made it interesting and applicable. Tests were hard but the review material was very helpful. Definitely worth turning in a regrade- the TAs will give you points most likely. Extra credit at the end of the semester bumped my grade up two letter grades.

Nicest guy in the world but lectures were so confusing and tests were pretty tough. However he is very encouraging and gives students lots of hope. Study the textbook 100% to do well on tests and form a study group.

He is a genius and wants to share as much as he can with us but most of us are a little lost. Very nice man and gives you hope until the last day of class and the TAs were lifesavers. Dont fall behind! Go to OChem lab and talk to the TAs.

His lectures seemed a bit scattered at times, but it's just because he's genuinely interested in the topics that he wants to tell us all of the interesting things he knows about them. His tests are very reasonable and don't blindside you. He has consistent office hours and plenty of them. If you go to him he will tell you what is most important.

He was so fair and consistent. I loved this class - not because the material was super interesting to me, but I knew that my grade would reflect the effort and preparation that I put into it. There are no surprises. Its hard because of the amount of material - that's just the nature of the beast. I loved this class.

Be prepared to spend a LOT of time for this class. Material is fascinating and Dr. Andrus did a great job teaching it. Make sure to read the sections before coming to class, or you won't understand as much during lecture. I wouldn't say this a difficult class as far as material, you just really have to put your hours in if you want to do well.

Let's face it, chemistry is not easy, so don't expect the class to be a breeze.  With that said, Andrus is a fair grader and willing to help.  This was my second time in chem 285 and after comparing tests, his were MUCH easier (no tricks!)  He keeps things simple and if you keep up on the hw, a good grade is possible.  Would take from him again.

Andrus is a really good, fun guy, but didn't work well as a teacher for me. I usually ended up confused at the end of class. Things seemed jumbled sometimes and I didn't feel prepared for the final! Even though Andrus is a great guy, I would try taking this from someone else.

A nice guy but not a very good chem 101 teacher. Lectures were pointless and I was always more confused than before class. Got frustrated when asked questions. Tests were way harder than expected because we hadn't been prepared for them in class.

Andrus is a great guy. He does lots of demos in class and has a bunch of really bad chem jokes. He's pretty available for office hours, and is willing to help. Overall, he's a pretty great professor, and I'd take a class from him again.

He's a great guy but not the best teacher. I found lectures pointless because he left me more confused after class than before. The book is very helpful. I used this as my teacher. He stands at the front of the room and talks to himself basically. He gets frustrated when people ask questions. He loves chemistry but isn't good at teaching it.

A fairly straightforward class.  Sometimes in class he goes off on problems that are much more difficult that you will need to know.  The tests are easier than the book problems and the problems done in class.  Do the sample test.

It's sad when you feel Chem 105 was easier than 101. I now have taken both. Andrus just writes on the chalk board how to do the problems and half the time you can't hear him or read his handwriting. He contradicts himself when it comes to due dates. He seems to get annoyed if you ask him more than one question. Chem 101 shouldnt be worse than 105.

Dr. Andrus cares a lot about his students. It's very possible to get an A in his class. You're going to have to rely on the chemistry lab along with Dr. Andrus, the TA and the book because these three are incomple resources by themselves.

He was always saying if you need help come to me. so my friend and i went to get help and he gave us the cold shoulder and told us to go look at the cabinet. His tests are not too hard and overall pretty easy class but can be rude when going in to get help.

Fantastic teacher.  He lectures straight from the book, and bases the exam questions on the text as well.  He clarifies his expectations well and also gives many examples of problems in class.  Definitely need to study, but getting an A shouldn't be a problem.  I never enjoyed science until taking this class from Professor Andrus.

He is friendly but don't mistake that for helpful, clear, and easy. Rewriting already previously written problems does not help a class learn. When asking him questions he is too technical in his explanations. He may be great for upperlevel classes but too technical for chem 101

Chem was just a general requirment i had to get out of the way and in high scholl personally i hated the subject. Yet, Prof Andrus made it fun and inersesting. He was by far my favorite teacher of the semester. I would strongly recommend him to anyone!
nice teacher and very helpful.. i really appreciate him...

Dr. Andrus does a good job of explaining the underlying concepts behind the reactivity you need to learn in Ochem.  I enjoyed his class.  He has a smile on his face most of the time he lectures, I don't understand how you could like Chemistry that much.  Anyway, he is a good teacher.

Great teacher, really cares about his students. A very fun and entertaining lecturer. Random take home and in class quizzes. His tests are very straight forward, and only tests you on material you have studied, he isn't trying to trick you like other OChem prof's.
nice teacher, willing to meet with you anytime and help you out with your quizzes, etc. you will be prepared for any national test (DAT, etc)

Really caring guy; always willing to help.  Random in-class and take-home quizzes, but he drops hints about them so you usually have some warning.  Fair expectations.  Nice sense of humor.  Take O.Chem from him!

though his teaching was very weak atimes,i liked him.60% of tests is multiple choice,and 40%-free response.His tests are not insane at all!He is funny, he is encouraging.He has random in-class quizzes.The secret to passing his class is this: Make sure you do the reading and understand the material before class! Take notes in class! Get to know him.

All these other comments are from people who must've aced his class.  For the average student, he doesn't explain anything well.  70% of the class doesn't know what he's doing.  He only uses chalk board, never powerpoint.  Don't believe the previous comments.
Great Teacher

Very good Professor. Knows his stuff and wants you to know it too. Very comprehensive of students and their lives. You can tell he loves what he does because he is well prepared to teach only what's important, and organizes everything in a way to allow students to learn it as well if they try. I was very impressed. Good job.
He is one of the greatest professors I have had. He was very flexible with the students and was very capable of explaining everything well.  If your going to take o-chem take it from him.
Had to learn ochem from the text book/kaplan book, learned more in one month of kaplan review than 8 months in his classes. awful teacher
Professor Andrus rocks!
No Comments
Great teacher that knows his stuff and how to explain it clearly.  If you work hard in this class, a good grade is possible because you'll actually learn the material.
Good teacher. Fun to listen to.  He knows his stuff and does a good job.  Class isn't super easy, but he's a good teacher

Dr. Shepherd is super nice, and it's clear that he knows a lot about acoustics. However, his lectures are so boring. This class made me glad that I don't have to take any more physics classes for my major.
Textbook is not required, but offered. Must attend lab but class is not necessary. He makes the lectures fun and enjoyable.
He made the lectures fun when they could have been very boring. Before every test he goes over how to do each question. I don't like physics, but I would take this class again in a heartbeat.

Pro Shepherd is a nice guy, but I would not recommend taking phys 167 from him. His lectures consist of him reading off slides verbatim, and he has a hard time explaining concepts. I will say he clearly cares about the students!

Class was a little boring, but he made it pretty easy to get a good grade. Literally goes over what every single test question is on before exams, which made it easy to know what to study. He is very passionate about physics and he clearly wanted us to succeed and do well, but I found his lecture style a little monotonous.

Great professor; teaching style is unique but works. The content is difficult, but the tests aren't too bad with basic understanding. He is very open to discussing the tests before test day, so take good notes in his review lectures, as he covers the test problem by problem.

This class is the only physics class that I disliked and it absolutely sucked.

His round 1, round 2 teaching style was awful and meant the first half of our homework assignments were meaningless and took 5 minutes. While the second half took up to 2 hours.
It made for a very inconsistent semester where neither round really cemented the concepts.

Out of all the teacher, in all the grades, in all the schools I've ever attended, one stands alone and his name is Micah Shepard. It amazes me how someone so boring and bad is allowed to teach at an accredited university. I found the material to be somewhat interesting, but his terrible teaching made it so boring. Do not take a class from this man.

Labs are graded by participation. This class is EASY as long as you study for the exams (there is a unit review which details every question topic). Concepts are confusing but are easy to memorize. Shepherd is enjoyable to listen to. You can not show up to lectures and still do well. As long as you apply yourself to the unit reviews = easy A

Dr. Shepherd is a good teacher. He teaches engaging lectures, and breaks down potentially confusing subjects. However, know if you miss a class, you will NOT understand that topic any time soon. Do your best to not miss class, otherwise you have no hope of understanding that topic.

Dr. Shepherd has lots of fun demonstrations. His teaching method is focused on concepts, then computations. Tests were very clear and he spelled out what we would actually be tested on. He's genuinely kind of funny, in a physicist way. Textbook reading was graded on the honor system by time spent (up to 45 min). Homework isn't too bad.

The class was set up very simply. He is very geared towards physics, like it made sense to him so sometimes he would skip steps. He has a passion for physics though and had cool in class demonstrations. The tests weren't too bad, but there were not a lot of resources for studying.

Being that this was his first semester teaching this course, it was a little difficult for him to explain the concepts clearly during lecture. However, the homework, reading, and conceptual questions were enough to learn the material well. Tests are not a large portion of the grade. He is a nice professor, and he is trying hard to improve.

Tests were not a huge part of the grade.12.5% for each of the 2 midterms and 20 for the final is pretty gracious. Homework is interesting since the grading for conceptual things is never understood by the merciless graders. This was his first time teaching the class so I feel he will get better. He gives great lectures that prepare for exams

I don't think he taught the lectures very well but he is such a caring person and will do his best to help you understand the material. He is very accessible and responds very quickly to questions. His tests are also very easy.

He's a newer professor and this is his first time teaching the class so his teaching style could use some improvements, but I assume he will polish his delivery over time. He is accessible and prepares you well for the tests.
I never felt engaged in his class and they were mostly useless for the homework and tests. You'll do fine if you read the textbook and get work done ahead of time.

During the conceptual portions of the class, it was really interesting and he was good at conveying the concepts. During the computational portions this class was confusing, lectures were unclear and unhelpful. I spent more time on this class than my 4 credit math class. Lots of HW, 2 exams and a final, out of class labs, graded 45 min readings.

I loved this Professor and this class. I'm not much of a physics person but this class was manageable. There are a lot of hands on opportunities during the lecture periods as well as the labs. Take advantage of TA/office hours, study for the exams, etc. The only critique I have is I feel like the professor wasn't the best at clarifying questions.

I loved Dr. Shepherd! His lectures are very organized and prepare you well for the exams (4 exams total). He's passionate about what he teaches and engages the whole class. Labs are mandatory for your grade but you can get full credit by just going! Great class and you learn a lot of really cool things!

Grades weren't only determined by exams. Labs are participation only and worth a good portion of your grade. Did test reviews in class and gave the topic of each question for most exams which was awesome. I was terrified for this class because I'm not a science person but I actually learned the concepts from him and got an A, he's amazing

This class was awesome! Prof Shepherd is very knowledgeable and he prepares you well for the tests. The class topics are often very interesting and have practical usage, even if you aren't taking this because of your major. The textbook was way more in depth than it needed to be, so focus more on the lectures than the reading.

I took the class just to fulfill a GE credit but I ended up learning a lot of fascinating things! The lectures are entertaining and engaging and he prepares you well for the tests which are all pretty straight forward. You also get some neat experiences like touring the anechoic and reverberation chambers in the ESC.

I had Prof. Shepherd last semester and he is amazing! He teaches concepts very clearly and the class was very organized. I had never taken a physics class before, so I was really nervous about this class, but it ended up being easier than I expected. There is a lab, but you're only graded on attendance for those, and they are pretty interesting.

I loved this class! Dr. Shepherd made the concepts very clear. The textbook went into more depth than you needed to know, but he always told you what you actually needed to know. Labs were fun and only graded on attendance. Daily quizzes aren't too bad. Enjoyable class!

Prof Shepherd is by far one of my favorite profs I've had at BYU. He doesn't just assume the class knows what he's talking about, and he explains the basics very plainly and simple for everyone to understand. Labs were super fun, I've never had a class I was genuinely excited to go to before. If you have a chance to take from Shepherd, do!

Very disorganized. First of all, the syllabus was never published, the resources on learning suite are scarce and unhelpful, and the professor is unresponsive. I never received a single response to any email I sent. Important details were constantly missed causing often affecting students ability to complete coursework.
Dr. Arts is very interesting and knowledgable professor. His grading is a bit unclear sometimes but due to the in-frequentness of them it makes it really easy, final was easy but make sure you study

This class is fairly easy to do well in if you attend class. You get two chances for every quiz and the final is literally just a repeat of all of the quiz questions throughout the year (which you have access to). He can be a little hard to follow at times, but does a pretty good job of explaining difficult concepts.

Professor Arts is very intelligent and insightful during his lectures, they made me think but were hard to follow and got boring. He doesn't really use a lot of slides and the quizzes he gave were really difficult. Lots of essays but they were not super difficult as long as you went to class. Easy class to pass but difficult to get an A in.

Lots of lecturing, and lots of bizarre pieces of information. It was incredibly difficult to know where to focus my learning. He did try to be personable at times, but he mostly just lectured, often with a PowerPoint, and used a lot of vocab I wasn't familiar with.

Arts is not going to make you like Logic if it isn't something you're already interested in. If you do like it however, he does a superb job at explaining logical concepts. If you consistently attend lectures and do the readings then you should get an A in his class. He usually provides multiple examples, so you get many opportunities to understand

One thing to note from all these reviews: If you don't like philosophy you probably won't like professor Arts. Not because he is the problem, but because you just don't like the subject he teaches. If you do like philosophy then professor Arts is awesome and I would highly recommend him! Prof. Arts has been my favorite professor so far in college.

Very lecture-heavy, then a quiz about every other week about what we learned. The papers had no rubric so it was hard to know what to do because there were very few descriptions. There are 100 points in the class so one point is 1% of your grade. The test was extra credit, and the professor did open a quiz for me after it closed, he was very kind.

Dr Arts is a sweet guy, he was always willing to extend deadlines for me. Most of lecture goes right over my head, but if you do the assignments (like one a week, super light) and go to lecture you'll be okay. he ended up giving me 10% extra credit, tho idk if that was because I told him I was trying really hard and still doing bad or just cuz.
Y'all are gonna laugh - I literally took 2 voice recordings to show my friends how boring this class and professor were. (if you've taken this class, you get it) SO awful.

Professor Arts was nice and I enjoyed his lecturing...but the course itself is awful. No information, no syllabus, no grading rubric, and in order to get an A you had to write far more than the requirements for the papers. The class quizzes were composed of confusing questions and the overall quality was extremely poor.
I love professor Arts teaching style. His lectures are so interesting and clear. Homework is straightforward. Great GE class. Never thought I would like a philosophy class.
Professor Arts is hilarious and is very passionate about what he's teaching. There was some ambiguity as to what was expected of the students on a week-to-week basis, but overall, a good professor.

Professor Arts made philosophy fun and interesting. He knew his stuff, yet welcomed discussion and never made me feel dumb for not understanding concepts. He's kind and made an effort to get to know the students. I wish I had more opportunities to take his classes. I looked forward to coming to class!

Prof Arts is passionate about philosophy & very educated. Took this class just for a GE credit but it wasn't bad. Kinda paper heavy but I never read the textbook and only skimmed the readings needed to write papers. Final is 10% EC and just repeated quiz questions, which is why I got an A. Boring class but easy to be successful!! Take it from him!

I love Professor Art's class so much. His lectures are extremely insightful and the way he discusses philosophy makes it easy to look back on and analyze on your own. He is super understanding about late work and offers the final as extra credit. I found the homework load completely reasonable and came to look forward to his lectures.

Professor Arts is a really nice guy, but this class was ridiculous. There were five homework assignments and four tests and they made up your entire grade. I didn't find the lectures hopeful and relied on the textbook, mostly. It's a great book, but I spent most of my time stressing about my grade. Not recommended if you're a lecture-learner.

The best thing going for Brother Arts is that he is very kind and genuine. He gets to know his students and wants you to succeed. The course itself is tough, though. Each assignment is worth 5-10% of your grade, and so there's only about 10 assignments for the semester and the questions are tricky. Final is extra credit. Nice guy, tough class.

Logic is already a hard course, Professor Arts makes it a little harder. If you are comfortable teaching yourself from the textbook, you will be fine. If you need homework help or get easily confused- DO NOT take from him. Great guy, but his teaching methods were unhelpful and circuitous at best.

There are not many assignments in class. He is very wordy and hard to understand, but pay attention because the answers he is looking for are often not in the reading. He grades hard on the papers, and the instructions are not clear. ASK HIM QUESTIONS-It will help! He expects a lot, but put in the work and reach out with concerns, you will be fine.

There are not many assignments in class. Quizzes, papers, (8 pg paper) midterm, and extra credit final. He is very wordy in class and hard to understand, but you need to pay attention because the answers he is looking for are often not in the reading. He grades hard on the papers, and the instructions are not clear. ASK HIM QUESTIONS-It will help!

This class was ridiculous. He has very specific and strangely worded quizzes that are worth most of your grade and does not cover the material on them fully in class! He is also very vague about other places to find the information. You will not do well even if you feel you have learned the material well.

The top score in my class is a 92%, and only one student got above 90%. He only has a few papers and quizzes, so the class isn't too work heavy, but it is very difficult to understand. He is vague and does not always cover what is on the tests. The class is a pretty easy C but nearly impossible A. Do NOT take this is you want a high college GPA.

Professor Arts is a great professor. He has a slight accent since English is his second language but he's understandable. Best compliment(s): easy grader . He also cares about students. Totally willing to work with you if you're late for an assignment. Best criticism(s): he's REALLY lecture heavy and can be boring if that's not your learning style.

YOU GUYS! I got all As and high Bs through the semester and got a hard earned C- in this class. Professor Arts is hard to contact and his quizzes do not reflect anything learned from in class. Everyone I spoke with from my class had low grades! Save your gpa, take it from another professor. I promise youll thank me later!

Really hard grading, oddly specific quizzes. Although I got full marks or A+'s on every essay, despite how hard the midterm essays were graded (19/20 for me), I got 2/5 for most of the quizzes because they're written to confuse you. I would have an A in the class if not for these quizzes; instead, I have a C. He doesn't respect your time in class.

I personally loved Arts. We had a great class and we all participated regularly. He's honestly a goofball so don't be surprised when he messes up. His classes aren't structured so just watch him do the proofs. He eventually was teaching slower than what our homework covered so thats annoying but its a very interesting topic.

Even the other professors in the department will tell you not to take this or any other class from him. Often made mistakes in correcting homework that took the entire class to resolve. Forgot to teach an entire half-unit before a test. Not sure why he still works at BYU, avoid Prof. Arts at all costs. The only way to get an A is the textbook.

Very dry lectures. Overall grade is based on a few papers (no grading criteria is given so you just have to wing it), a midterm essay, and a multiple choice final. He doesnt grade too hard on the papers, but it is difficult to know what he is looking for. Only take this class if you are interested in REALLY understanding the views of philosophers.

Worst class structure I have ever seen. The textbook was never mentioned and the paper grading criteria was non-existent. The worst thing was the comprehensive final, (We had no idea on what though) and worth 25% of the grade. No real study help and despite the average grade being an F he didn't curve the test. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Philosophy is interesting stuff, but his lectures are extremely dry with little to no class involvement. The criteria by which he grades papers is very unclear, so if you don't write what he's looking for you will get a low score, and since there are so few assignments this can really mess up your grade. I would recommend taking from someone else.

The book was way more helpful than the professor. He even told us the day the test opened that there would be a whole extra unit and a half we hadn't even covered in class that we would be tested on that. Completely unclear expectations and difficult to get any help from him. He wouldn't even tell us where the logic lab was. DO NOT TAKE FROM HIM!

He is a great person but some great people should not be professors. He requires you to know things that he has not gone over in class for the tests. There is a TA lab for this class which all other 205 classes had access to which we did not because he never told us about it. I'm not sure he understands how to help his students learn effectively.

PHIL202 was one of my less stressful classes. It still required some effort for papers and studying, but was very do-able. There were about 6 papers (variable length) but no tests (besides the final). Arts is a bit dry, but he is a fair grader and knowledgeable in many subjects.  Go to class, take notes, ask questions, and enjoy the class.

each week you will have either a quiz, short paper, or 4-5 page paper due. I took his class once a week on Tuesdays so every Tuesday something was due. He lectures the entire class period and tries to get you to think really deep. You will read at least 10 pages of a story or book each week.
Professor Arts explains philosophical concepts in a way that helps you understand and makes you think. Although the grading criteria could be more specific, his class is fairy easy.

I love Dr. Arts as a person, but I would never recommend this class to anyone! He doesn't really teach you anything, you must teach yourself all of the material. His grading criteria is incredibly confusing. He tests you on material that hasn't been covered yet. His lectures are really dry and full of tangents. Easy enough class but you won't learn

Michael Arts is quiet and subdued but super chill and very reasonable. The class is entirely lecture-based, but with an involved group it can be an interactive discussion at times. Your only grades are the occasional critical papers or summaries of historical texts-- no homework. The material is interesting and Arts is just a really great guy!
Michael Arts class on Wittgenstein changed my life.  Literally the most important class I took as an undergrad.

I took his class at UVU (he teaches here in the evenings). Yes he doesn't involve the class in his lectures, but if you actually listen to what he's saying, it's brilliant. Most people just don't have the attention spans requisite. The guy is a great teacher, but you have to be willing to actually pay attention to what he's saying and not zone off.

I got a 100 on the final and only briefly looked at the study guide. He grades easy on the papers. The lectures can be dull because he doesn't involve the class, but he is EXTREMELY good at explaining difficult philosophical concepts in an understandable way. Take his 202 if you're a phil major that needs a good basis for future classes

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!! Worst class I have taken at BYU. Lectures are boring, course is very disorganized, the final was ridiculous. I got an A on all the papers but an F in the final. The study guide for the final was a joke. It helped out with 3/40 questions. Class average for the final was a 56. He doesn't grade on a curve either

The grade is based on 4 papers, the midterm, and the final. Its an easy class to pass, but with a few catches. The four papers are never explained and the topic is generally given in one sentence. You should not hope to understand what you need to write for them. Further, lectures are dry beyond belief. Take literally any other class over this.

He doesn't care about you or your education. He is simply there to get paid and he doesn't "give A's because not everyone can get A's or there would be no point in grades." So instead he gave half the class C's. I will NEVER recommend this professor for any course. Extremely disappointed in BYU for hiring him since he doesn't promote BYU's aim.

I don't think he ever gives full points on papers. And he said he isn't "paid" to give feedback on what you did wrong on papers. On 20 point assignments he gives you 15-16 if he doesn't think you did the assignment right. 17-18 if you did what you were told. 19-20 if you went above and beyond what you are told. Wouldn't suggest this class.

Hate this class because he is completely unclear on the writing assignments. He never updates canvas to show what he expects on the writing assignments, and if he does it isn't until hours before the assignment is due. What good does that do? To know what is due you have to go to class. Would not suggest this class!

Arts is one of the best teachers I have ever had.  He is more of a philosopher than a professor.  Lectures are kind of dull towards the middle and end of the semester, but are not necessary since the class has only six take-home assignments.  Highly recommend.

He's got a great sense of humor and he's a fantastically clear, logical lecturer. I find myself enjoying his lectures even though I hate the topic. He's got a cool accent, too. He's not too hard of a grader. Class attendance not mandatory for success.

Lectures are not necessary for completion of assignments. Did not provide feedback on papers for which he docked points, making it impossible to write to his liking on subsequent assignments. Dull and arduous class.

Professor Arts is extremely intelligent and knowledgeable. Genuinely cares about his students, and is very friendly. The entire grade for the class is based off of papers summarizing philosophical texts, these papers have nothing to do with what is lectured in class. I didn't attend class for the last 2 months and walked out with an A.

This professor is genuinely smart, and if you try to take advantage of that fact you can learn a lot from him.  The hardest part is that you feel challenged in your thinking in this class, but listen to him, trust him and he won't lead you somewhere you shouldn't be.  Overall one of the best classes I have ever taken.

Great professor! He focused on a few key ideas and explained them in depth until anybody could understand. Interesting lectures. All the assignments (including midterm and final) are papers. You're in luck if you're a good writer. Not my strength, but I did well anyway because he was happy to give me specific feedback on the papers when I asked.
Arts is brilliant! Anyone will learn a great deal from taking a class from him!
Brilliant guy but not a good class. Your final grade is a paper. Class is worthless and he is unclear on what he wants. Great if you want to learn how to write a good philosophical paper.

Brilliant guy but a stupid course. Class is pointless and he is very unclear about what he wants. Your grade is a paper. If you want to learn to write a good philosophical paper though he is perfect for the job.

This is honestly the easiest civ general. All you have to do is write short summaries, critical analysis, and your written midterm and final. I'm not much of a writter and I will either be getting a A or A- in this class. You do have to read A LOT but you are going to have to for any civ class you take. Seriously, take this class!

I know students are signing up for classes now, so I wanted them to know that he is great! He knows philosophy inside and out, he has a testimony (which can be hard within philosophy), is a fair grader on papers. The class is nice because it is only papers, lecture is normally funny, but can be long. I tell everyone to take his course!
I absolutely loved him! He knows everything about everything! The class was interesting, but really I could have not even gone and still gotten an A.

If you're familiar with basic phil history and can write well, you'll be fine in the class. I was going through some issues and went to class left than half the time, but still managed to get an A because I scored well on the test papers. Don't take any of the writing assignments for granted though; you have to have to say something worth reading.

I got a 4.6 GPA in high school & I consider myself one of the best writers on campus but this guy is so tough on his grading standards. the textbook (Great Conversation)wasnt very clear or useful. the important stuff comes off blackboard. start the assignments early for a better chance. six writing assignments. good luck! will have as teacher again

Experienced and intelligent. Not an easy A, but knows what he's talking about. You have to pay attention in class, and when you do, you will be amazed how much you can take in. Keep up with the textbook reading, it will help clarify dense material. One of the best and smartest professors I've ever had.

I don't know why people complain so much about Arts. If you know how to logically organize your ideas on paper and be somewhat creative, you should be able to get an A without too much sweat.  Just 6 assignments in the semester.It also can go a long way in giving you some perspective in life.Arts does a great job of applying philosphy to the gospel

Classtime is spent on philosophy topics on not on how to better the paper, which is the majority of the grade.  He is hard to understand and always gives negative feedback. He also posts grades publicly for all to see.

The final paper is all that the grade is. He will tell you what he wants your arguments to be, and if that's not what he thinks than your job is a lot harder. The smaller papers before the final are to help you with the final, but receive no score. Class Lectures are confusing, so dont worry about taking notes, no test. Just final paper!

I have never felt more frustrated with a class at BYU.  The lectures were fun but completely irrelevant to the class.  His was never clear about his expectations for assignments, and the syllabus might as well have been tissue paper.

I loved Dr. Arts. I reccommend taking him later on in your college career, when you're confident in your writing and discussion skills. He is very interesting and encourages the students to really think, rather than just parroting information. He usually grades only on a few essays, so you should be comfortable with writing.

Heck of a philosopher. Not so good at teaching. His syllabus had nothing to do with the class. Class attendance was nearly pointless but his lectures were somewhat interesting. Only and final grade was an eight page paper. Didn't learn much about writing though. Take him if you want an easy semester and interesting conversation.

I hated professor Arts. This was a freshman English course which you wouldn't have been able to tell if it weren't the title of the class. Professor Arts lectured everyday about reading that maybe 20 percent of the class actually read. Our entire grade was based on the final paper. I felt that going into the class I could expect a professor that wo

Arts teaching style is random and has no meaning. he never lectures on the same thing in two lectures and never repeats himself. if you missed the info, then too bad, you're in trouble. He doesn't explain his grading methods. i would not recommend taking this teacher unless you are looking for someone to kill all interest in philosophy.

I'm suprised to see that Dr. Arts doesn't have better ratings.  You only have about four or five assignments for the class and they are all take home.  Dr. Arts explains everything really well and clearly.  I recommend taking careful notes and then preparing for assignments by going over questions with a group.  Great class, not too difficult A

Dr. Arts' greatest strength is his ability to give extremely precise and clear explanations of difficult philosophical concepts.  Some have complained that he doesn't give feedback, and I thought so too when I got a B on my first essay. However, during class he explained the errors that lost points and sure enough I had them. Great teacher.

I loved this class!   Really, Arts is one of the most intelligent people I've ever met.  He does a great job explaining abstract principles.  He expects A LOT from students!  Expect to work HARD for your not-quite-an-A.  Arts' lectures aren't the most engaging unless you put effort into learning.  The class content is facinating! I recommend it!

Prof Arts is an excellent teacher. His teaching style is not flashy, but it's very logical & clear. He is the best-read Philosophy professor I've had and understands what he is talking about. He says some pretty funny things, but most of the class will not get his jokes. People that don't like him don't have a logical mind for philosophy. Take home tests.

Very measured in his words. His lectures are almost always engaging which reflects his familiarity with a broad range of subjects within philosophy and without.  Not the easiest class, he demands a lot from his students but you gain confidence and learn a whole lot.

Our class only had 12 students in it.  Arts drilled us with Phil. and made us write and re-write until we knew what we were doing at the end of the semester.  He made us think HARD.  He is really smart and always has an answer (or question) for every philosophy.  An AWESOME teacher that requires students to be somewhat dedicated.
Professor Arts is passionate about the subject matter ... my class with him had only six students, and I really looked forward to our class discussions. His accent can be a bit of a challenge.

He gives no clear explanation of his expectations for various assignments. Students are then shocked to get their papers back (which they thought they did  correctly) with a C or D on it, but no other teacher-made markings to explain  what they did wrong. Arts is very well-read and knows his stuff. lectures are informative if u can stay awake.
The course material was pretty difficult, but then this was a 400 level class.  Professor Arts definitely knew what he was talking about, though he does go off on tangents occasionally.
