The biggest key to success in his class was in working through, learning from, and practicing the homework problems. They were time consuming but very effective at facilitating learning. Use the TA lab. There are actual labs too.

Dr. Ware is actually the best. He's hilarious, and he does a really good job of teaching and structuring class well. The way homework done seems like a lot of work (and it does take a while), but it works to make sure you understand the material. At least 100x better than my high school physics prof.

I personally didn't like Dr. Ware as a professor. He is a pretty good guy, but really hard to learn from. Almost everything I learned from this class I taught my self using outside resources. He was hard to contact and didn't work well with students who had accomadations. I also felt the homework and in class work did not prepare me for the tests.

I spent about 11 hours a week on this class. The homework is long, and there are tests every other week. That being said, the TA lab is a blessing, and it's easy to find people to help you understand the material. At least one grade out of every category is dropped-I ended up just skipping one of the labs. Lots of work, but you do learn a lot.

Physics 121 is not as bad as people hype it up to be. There will be a point where you don't understand something on the homework because there wasn't enough class time to go over it, and that's where you go to the TA lab. Dr. Ware was a pretty good teacher, some of the content can get kind of dry, which is why he tells a joke every class.

Physics 121 is completely doable. Just make good use of the TA lab. 6 midterms are a lot but one of them will get dropped and if you understand the homework, then the tests shouldnt surprise you. Lectures can be really dry but Dr. Ware is a nice guy and he always posts his slides which is super helpful.

What I have to say: 6 midterms, 15 hours a week dedicated to this class, and a Venn diagram where the circles don't overlap. (To explain the last one, lectures have nothing to do with what's on the homework and tests.) Dr. Ware is nice enough but a little boring and hard to follow. This class isn't structured very well.

Dr. Ware does his best to cover the information required by the various departments who influence this course. That being said, this course is unnecessarily difficult for a 100 series, and requires you to spend exuberant hours outside of the class room studying the material. On top of all that, this course has six midterms and one final.

Dr. Ware really cares about all of his students. The class is really hard, with 6 midterms and a final. Be ready to learn fast, a lot of material is covered quickly and not really reviewed. Dr. Ware is a great guy, he did a wonderful job teaching the class. I wouldn't take the class again, but I would take a class from Dr. Ware again in the future.

This class took so much time away from my other classes. There are 6 midterms and 1 final. He drops one midterm which is nice and will sometimes curve it but that means there were only 4 classes between each test. Be prepared to spend 20 hours a week on this class.

Dr. Ware is one of the least "help the students" oriented teachers I have had in my 3-year career at BYU. His test questions were unclear, and he refuses to give students points back even when their work is right, just not done "his way." I would never take a class from him ever again.

A lot of work for the class, which is typical. Make use of the tutorial lab and study groups! Dr. Ware cares about his students and will provide you with the information and resources for you to pass! Attendance quizzes in class, one test dropped, and 2 homework assignments a week with a slight curve. Very straightforward!

By now you've read that he's a hard teacher and there's a lot of homework. True, but you NEED to take Dr. Ware. Here's why: you're probably an engineering or CS major, and he will prepare you for your major. If you plan on taking ME101 later, Dr. Ware will have you totally ready after taking 121 from him. Also, he curved our tests and final grade.
Interesting and funny lectures. We had tests like every other week. Even though lectures were long for TTh, they were made enjoyable. Beware of the final, you should really know your stuff.

There's lots of homework in this class, but none of it was busywork and was all necessary in order to cover the concepts. Dr Ware is a clear and concise professor who gives you exactly what you need in order to do well in the class. His lectures were very useful to me and I felt like I learned every class. He also tells daily jokes which is fun.

Dr. Ware is a fantastic professor! The homework is a lot harder than lecture practice problems so you have to really work to understand it. The tests are a bit easier though, the TA lab is a big help for the homework. Lectures are entertaining and really helpful. Spent about 12-15 hours a week outside of class. Exams basically every other week.

So this class was by far the hardest class I have ever taken. Dr. Ware is fine, but he sometimes doesn't cover everything in lectures because "you will learn when you do the homework." (Or in my case struggle through the homework for three hours at least each assignment.) If you need to take the class, just live in the TA lab and you should be ok.

Easily harder than any other class I've taken. I have a (somewhat diminished) level of confidence that I'm not an idiot, but this class killed me. I spent at least 15 hours a week on homework, not counting the SIX EXAMS we had to take over the semester. If you have no previous physics experience like me, get ready for your worst semester.

A LOT of work for a 3 credit class. Homework assignments would take up to a couple of hours, which in addition to the walk-in labs and SIX midterms was a big workload. However, all of this work will teach you the physics concepts well (better than lectures will). Lectures are pretty solid, the highlight being he tells a quality joke every lecture.

Lectures sometimes felt pretty confusing and pointless. You'll really need the internet to learn a lot of the concepts. His lectures were alright because he always stopped halfway through for a break to tell lame jokes that were so bad they were funny.

Schedule of work is very specific and repetitive, easy to schedule but there is a LOT. 6 exams during semester make 40% of grade, and the final is another 30%. Enough EC to boost your grade by 1-2% but not much more. Not available much. Not great at explaining concepts if you don't get them right away. Online textbook used but it is free. Funny.

Worst class at BYU. There was so much work including a ton of homework that is graded in the most ridiculous way. 6 midterms and a final worth a combined 70% of your grade. Lectures were mediocre and a waste of time because the tests and homework were way harder than anything in class. Textbook was free but confusing. Most stressful class I've had.

Good guy, tells jokes every lecture, is clear & organized with the semester's assignments, good at drilling concepts into your head in a simple manner. Like with any weed out STEM class, if you put in the work, you can do very well in his class. I took 4 years of physics in High School but now I feel like I've understood physics for the first time.

The way he explained things did not make sense a lot of the time. A lot of work for a 3 credit class (2 homeworks, 2 quizzes, 1 lab every week, midterm every other week) Subsequently, the tests did not affect grade as much since there were so many. Overall good.

Great teacher! Teaching style made me actually love physics. Tells jokes in class to help keep you awake and he does plenty of example problems. Homework is hard and long but really helps with all the tests.

His teaching style isn't my favorite, but I suggest finding a group at the beginning of the semester so you can study and do homework together. There is tons of homework. If you haven't taken a physics class before , like I hadn't, the class is going to be pretty difficult. The tests were challenging for me at the beginning, but you get used to it.

I stopped doing the readings because professor Ware explains concepts better. He tells jokes halfway through class which helped me stay awake. His tests were very predictable based on homework and problems done in class.

Dr. Ware is a really nice guy. He really does care about us, but he doesn't have the best teaching style. It is pretty much spend a lot of time outside of class reading a textbook that might as well be written in a different language, then coming to class and going over very simple problems and concepts, then having ridiculously hard homework.
He is a really good teacher. He is really nice and does jokes everyday to keep you engaged since it is a long lecture. You do have to spend a lot of time in the physics lab doing homework.

I love Dr. Ware. He really cares about his students. If you don't like to work hard then chances are you will not like this class. Many of the reviews on here are because people don't appreciate the workload and the class is hard. However, he makes the material interesting and tells hilarious jokes

Two reading quizzes, two homework assignments, and a lab due every week. Also 6 exams, which is kind of nice because they take less than an hour and there isnt much material covered. Class itself gets pretty old after a while, its structured exactly the same every time, and its mostly practice problems. He doesnt do too much of explaining.

He's a good teacher and knows what he's talking about. He's very entertaining in class and is a friendly guy. He has us use on free online textbook because he didn't want his 500+ students each semester to be spending hundreds each, which is great. He does have us take exams twice a month, as he says it has helped raise his student's grades.

Dr. Ware assigns labs on your own time, reading assignments, and time-intensive homework. On average, I spent 10-12 hours per week outside of class. Lectures are mediocre at best. Sometimes his examples are helpful, but I found a lot more luck with the textbook and the TA lab (the TA lab is the best!). Tests and grading are very fair.

This class was hard for freshmen and people who hadn't had much math. I wasn't in that boat, but it was still too much busy work. I was somewhat interested in the subject material, but Dr. Ware had a patronizing teaching style that rubbed me the wrong way. Lecture attendance was required, for the grade, at least. He had some good jokes and demos.

I took this class my first semester, and I had no idea what I was getting myself into. I managed to scrape a B, but that was after tons of studying and outside work. The homework was difficult and time consuming, almost never took me less than an hour per assignment. A really cool guy, but his lectures are confusing at best. Wouldn't take again.

Dr. Ware is a great teacher, but the homework and tests are tough. You have to be able to combine the concepts he teaches in class in order to do the problems correctly. Hes extremely helpful though, and is willing to meet after class to help.
This class takes a lot of work but he does a good job of explaining things and making class interesting.
He's good. Fair tests. Just make sure you take your time to think them through.  Competent guy, his jokes were fun. The class is easy enough to get an A.
Dr. Ware teaches physics in an intuitive way. He would prepare a set of jokes for every class to keep us awake halfway through class.
Great teacher and had his curriculum well organized. In the middle of class he takes a break and tells a joke every class which is great. He knows what he is doing.

Ware is really a great professor! He wants you to succeed and structures the class in a way that you really learn the material. It was definitely not an easy class, there is a lot of homework and it takes a lot of time, but he is really a great professor. I highly recommend him!

So, the homework for this class is unnecessarily long.  It took me 3 hours for each assignment (two a week) because of the weird grading rubric when it would have taken me 1-1.5 hours otherwise.  Both the homework and tests are very difficult, but luckily there's a heavy curve so my 85.6% in the class turned into an A-, so I can't complain much .

This is the step by step guide to how to get an A in Dr. Ware's class:  Step 1. Learn to teach yourself physics, because only about 20% of what is covered in lecture ends up on the test. Be prepared to see a whole bunch of stuff you never learned in lecture on the tests, and to spend hours on homework that is often not related to the tests either

Don't buy the book. They have them in the physics tutorial lab (where you should always do your homework). The labs are dumb just find a group (on learning suite messages) to do them with and they will be easy. The lectures were interesting (live demonstrations). Overall, the class was tough but I learned a LOT.
Great teacher, but one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. I loved learned about the concepts but struggled a bit with all the equations and formulas.

Dr. Ware cares about students understanding the concepts.  He doesn't have any office hours but he stays after class to answer questions.  He tells jokes halfway through lecture because he realizes that people are falling asleep.  The class is a typical Physics class so don't expect it to be easy but it is definitely possible to get a good grade.

Dr. Ware is a great professor and guy. The class is really difficult, in my opinion too difficult. I had taken AP physics in high school and knew a lot of the stuff, but the homework would still take hours and the tests can be really tricky.  Great guy, I like his jokes, but the class is very difficult.

He is an okay teacher. His class requires much more than BYU's standard 2 hours work outside of class for every 1 in class. Students have to do most of the learning on their own. If you are good at math/science, especially if you took an AP physics class, the work isn't too hard, it just takes an excessive and unnecessary amount of time and energy.
Great professor, he knows his stuff. The homework is very challenging, and the exams are weighted quite heavily.

Dr. Ware is very funny and entertaining! However, his classes are very lecture based, and since I wasn't a science person, I found his PS100 class difficult. Most people did not, but I'd recommend him still; great professor and always willing to help. I used the TA lab more though!
great guy. Really funny and entertaining.

Professor Ware was great! Although his jokes were very cheesy (and he knew it too), he was always lively and easy to understand. Class was basically just the textbook chapters regurgitated onto  powerpoint slides, which he posted online. He was able to explain some hard concepts clearly. Pretty easy stuff if you study, just lots of tests.

Come to class to participate in the iclicker quizzes, go to the TA reviews they really help, and a ton of the lowest scores are dropped overall. 4 tests + final. TAs give all the answers in labs for homework. Dr. Ware shares a goofy joke halfway through every class (:

The description for this class makes it sound like it's an overview of tons of different kinds of sciences, but really it's pretty much only physics and chem. Dr. Ware is funny and does his best to make the topic interesting. Tests are tricky because the lectures are basic info but the tests expect you to know the topic deeper. iClicker attendance.
Usually, we have a few worksheets and an essay but nothing that can't be completed in the lab sessions. Make sure you read the chapters and take the quizzes. Also, expect cool demonstrations.

Ware lectures and goes over the reading the night before. If you read the textbook and attend class, you'll pass. The TA's are the one who grades and can really save your grade before a test with their reviews. He drops like 5 quiz grades which is very nice

Dr. Ware is such a nice guy, and although he isn't the most interesting lecturer in the world, if you pay attention you will learn a lot. 90% is an A, they drop like 8 in class quizzes, 4 homework assignments, and as long as you read you should be fine. Homework assignments every week that TAs help with.

Pro Ware was great! He always started class with a prayer and tried to relate to spiritual topics. GO TO THE TA TEST REVIEWS! They are essential! Go to class! There are iClicker quizzes everyday but he gives you the answer if you just attend. His lectures were long, but he tried to make them as interesting as possible. His slides are posted online.
He's good at explaining concepts. Not a very hard class, I wouldn't mind taking other classes from him if I was into science. He's interesting and nice.
Class isn't too bad if you do the readings and take the daily quizzes. T.A.'s seem to be super helpful too.
Classes are super boring and hard to stay awake. Posts slides online so just study them before the test. The test are easy but have a few tricky questions. Pretty easy A

Dr. Ware is a pretty good guy, jokes at halftime, but made mistakes with math and even variables mixed up in lectures, which is not good when you're trying to follow along. More or less clear, most of your time best spent in TA lab 2x a week doing the HW, which takes some time but is pretty easy. Straightforward, especially with TA help. Overall OK

Great professor! I didn't go to him for help with material bc my TA was amazing, so the TA lab is helpful. Easy quizzes, fair tests, no projects of any kind. Don't skip lab, you get to finish all of your homework in there and go over the topics that are tricky. Take this over chemistry if you have the choice. Take notes and you are golden.

He is amazing. Lectures are clear and interesting. Go to your labs, his TAs are super helpful and you will learn a lot from them. They are always available to help and are well trained in explaining difficult concepts.

I had a physics class before taking this one. This class is very difficult and hard to understand if you don't have a good background in physics. The professor is funny and tries to explain everything fairly well but the majority of your learning will come from the homework due twice a week. Get to know the TA Help lab.

Dr. Ware is fantastic.  This is a difficult class.  Not impossible by any means, but it requires work.  Dr. Ware does an excellent job of helping otherwise hard-to-understand concepts stick.  And he's hilarious.  Love this man!
I'm glad I took 2 years of physics before this, because he was useless in explaining concepts. Half the stuff he says, he contradicts later. The textbook and TA's in the ESC are better teachers
Professor Ware was helpful at describing the material and he actually cared about his students. Some of the concepts get pretty confusing, but TAs and Professor Ware can help with this.

Every day he asks if we've read the textbook before class and if we have we get points. The in-class quizes were super easy because he would help the entire class get the right answers. Halfway through lecture he stops to tell a joke. Your TA grades all HW and your essay questions on tests so it depends on how hard the TA grades.

Let's be honest... who takes Physical Science and really wants to? Overall, it's just a G.E. you have to get over with. Dr. Ware makes it a little more bearable but I just don't like the things we learned. He tells a joke in the middle of every class and gives you answers to all the quizzes... Just get a good T.A. who can help with explaining!

Ok this guy is a piece of work, seems very friendly and everything. The tests are off the wall hard, I got 100% on all of the homeworks but could only score close or below the class average on the tests. Really unfair, unclear questions (even to native speakers, how does he expect international student to understand?).

Enjoyable lecturer. I'd never taken physics before, and it's been two years since I did any math, but I still thought most of the material was well explained. The homework was time consuming, but that's 121, not Ware. It frustrated me that we didn't do a lot of practice. He'd work one problem on a topic and go on->no good way of studying for tests.

The material really isn't very difficult. The textbook isn't too helpful, but reading it is required. For more intuitive topics, he explains them very well. But for stranger topics, his explanations seem to confuse people.

Lectures are mostly practicing problems and kinda hard to follow.  Homework is time consuming.   Textbook is difficult to learn from since it goes way in depth and is generally unclear. TAs: pretty helpful.  I found searching internet/youtube for tutorials helpful.  Berguson subbed on a review day and I thought he explained concepts more clearly.

He did a good job making the class pretty entertaining with jokes and such. He made concepts I had previously struggled with more bearable. For the most part his descriptions were pretty clear. The tests weren't too hard. They were a lot like the homework, only slightly harder. Not a bad class.
Not the most fun or easy class, but that is the department, not him. He is a funny nerdy guy and made a boring class more enjoyable.

This was a great class! Dr. Ware tells jokes in the middle of class, sometimes shows youtube videos, and has interesting experiments and toys that relate to the topics that help bring interest to the class.  The TAs are really helpful in understand the homework.  Their is a lot of work, and you spend a lot of time.  So be prepared to work.
I really enjoyed this class.  Professor Ware is very good at explaining concepts.  It is a hard class, but he makes it fun and is always willing to help his students. I definitely recommend him!

He is a really fun teacher and I overall really enjoyed the class.  He is good about showing real life application in class.  The Tests are not too hard but not too easy.  I would highly recommend going to class as well.  Also the TA's are super helpful!
The class was quite difficult. On the tests, you had to apply things you learned in class, so they were pretty hard. You learn a lot, though. His jokes were entertaining :)

Class was extremely dry. At times I noticed that a huge chunk of the 200 person class would be sleeping. The tests were tough because it was hard to know what we needed to study specifically. Avoid taking this class with Prof. Ware

Boring teacher. Speaks in monotone. Doesnt prepare before class and you can clearly tell. Just reads from the slides. Homework easy because you do it in lab. Tests are hard. I would take it from someone else.

Speaks in a monotone (often sans microphone), appears to just read from the text, and responds to questions incomprehensibly. He tries to keep the class roused with an occasional joke, but couldn't maintain most of the hall's attention. The tests were difficult, but the TAs and reviews were good. Still, I wouldn't recommend him.

The professor is nice. He tries to keep everyone awake with his joke. But when it comes to the real stuff that you need to learn for exam. He speaks so soft. So weird!!! Besides, I have worst nightmare with my TA. He spends 15' of beginning class for:.....teaching Yoga post and talk about his study in Dinosaur. A good TA is essential to survive
Overall, I thought this class was pretty difficult, but Professor Ware was one of the better teachers.  He's organized and clear with lectures.

Professor Ware is an excellent professor.  Although I found physical science to be quite challenging, his lectures really helped with understanding difficult subjects.  You can go to any TA's lecture.  If possible, I recommend going to Chads.  He is your key to the exams... (he sometimes gives you answers)

I really was not interested in the subject material but Professor Ware understands that it is general class you have to go through and tries to make the best of it for you. Homework is easy if you go to labs, test are difficult but doable if you study and prepare for them. He is very friendly and helpful and tries to alleviate boredom through jokes
I am not a big science person but I enjoyed this class for the most part, the joke half way through class was really nice : )

Prof. Ware explains everything absolutely crystal clear. He tells jokes in class, and makes the demonstrations a lot of fun. He explains the concepts perfectly and once you know them, the tests are a cinch.

Make sure you buy your clicker before the first day of class or else the bookstore will run out and Ware will dock you for it! This course is one where it's easy to get a B+ or A- but hard to get an A. You have to get 100% on everything but the exams if you want an A, which actually isn't too hard to do, but then you've got to get B's on the exams.

physical is not the most fun class in the world but Prof. Ware did a great job of making it entertaining. He always told jokes, tried to make it interesting and such. He is very helpful and nice and explains things well. You should definitely take this class from him.

Professor Ware is an excellent teacher. I have absolutley no interest in physical science but he does very well with making the class as fun as possible and makes himself available to the students. Homework is easy if you go to the TA Labs.

Nice and funny guy, but if you don't like science there's no way you can get around a dull class. He was one of the best I attended, but requires you to read each chapter before you quiz every day. Where you really learn everything is in the lab, get a good T.A. and go to the lab!

Ware is an excellent teacher! Lectures can seem boring at times, but he always has a joke ready to keep us awake.  There is some reading, but the homework assignments are easy, especially if you go to lab.  Take the exam at the beginning of the semester - it's exactly like the final, and it won't count against you!

Professor Ware makes a huge effort to make Physical Science interesting and fun even though the actual material is not.  He tells jokes every day in class and does fun experiments.  Once he came wearing a superman shirt and let a student shoot him in the chest with a ball launcher.  I would recommend his class!

I absolutely loved going to the lectures. Ware was fun and the demos were helpful. The best demo was when he popped the balloons near the end of the semester, you'll understand when you see/hear it. I didn't do very well on the exams and I hated the textbook but I learned alot from the lectures and would definately recommend this professor.

Ware was a great teacher. He was funny and interesting to listen to. He always told jokes and had cool demos. The lab section was pointless, but you can't really get out of that. I also thought the texbook was really confusing. Pretty typical of a GE class, but Ware made it interesting, and even fun. I'd definately recommend him.

Great Professor! He knows his stuff, and tries to make things fun for everyone. He's very clear and will help you if needed. I totally don't like the subject, but he made the class fun.  The jokes wake you up if you're having trouble staying awake (during the  more boring lectures especially).

He's awesome! He uses good power point presentations, always tells a joke, and tries his best to make class interesting. I really enjoyed him as a teacher. He's funny, he's admittedly a science geek but very endearing and a great teacher. Makes this class memorable, even though it's a yucky general ed class!
I hate this class, but Professor Ware is a really good teacher. He tells a joke everyday in the middle of class, probably the worst jokes ever but he tries to make class fun. Very helpful and clear.

I love how Dr. Call structures his classes on Learning Suite. The assignments are informative but largely self graded, which allows students to learn in a low risk high reward way. He also offers retakes and rewrites.

I love Professor Call! His lectures were very entertaining and fun to listen to, which makes the content stick. He also tried to know everyone's name, which I deeply respect. It made the class feel seen and connected, which was another great thing to put together study groups. The tests are pretty doable if you study. He's seriously the best

I loved Professor Call. He's kind, and funny, and I would definitely recommend taking IHUM 201 from him. There is a lot of reading and some of the literature could be difficult at times, and you have to write a paragraph for each reading assignment. He does cover it all in class, which helped catch me up on what I did not pick up on.
Amazing class, not to hard and you learn a lot.

Prof. Call is a stud. Loves the subject matter and is passionate about it. The course is manageable, with small readings from a textbook and open-ended questions relating it to the course. Occasionally long readings like whole plays or books, (if you understand the concepts you'll get by). He's friendly, funny, kind and looks like Ferris Bueller.

Loved this class!!! He gives you 10 attempts on all tests, so if you don't get an A, it's your fault. You have three papers to write, buts it clear what is expected. The lectures are interesting and you learn a lot. He is the best teacher to take it from!

Professor Call is passionate about what he teaches and his students. He interviews each student twice and knows their names! There is a lot of work in his class: 3 papers, 3 culture activities, 3 tests, 2 interviews, and daily reading w/ writing assignments. You can retake the tests and one paper! Not hard just super time consuming and tedious.

Professor Call really wants you to succeed. If you are willing to put in some time and effort you can walk away with an A in his class. He is super passionate about what he teaches. Some of the readings are pretty heavy and hard to get through and the papers can take a good amount of time, but the tests for us could be retaken, which was huge.
Absolutely degrading professor.
Professor Call teaches IHUM 201 with passion. The class has a heavy workload, but his engaging lectures and willingness to help make it worthwhile. Unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for study prep.

Professor Call is such a great guy! He did his best to learn everyone's name in a class of 150+ students. His lectures were super fun and he makes everything in this class seem so interesting! The reading was difficult at times, but compared to the other classes you can take for Civ 1, this is by far the easiest option. Would definitely recommend!

Professor Call really is passionate about the humanities. I learned a lot. There are a lot of assignments and lots of readings that need to be done on time. This class, however, will culture you in a good way. Call is a good choice for IHUM 201. The tests are retakeable, but the study guides are really broad. The final is a test and an interview.

Very kind and caring. Final was an interview- a little intimidating but I feel like he graded very easily. Midterms were difficult for me but had unlimited retakes so no problem. I spent about 1 hour after each class doing homework/readings- sparknotes works well :)

I liked Professor Call but I had a really hard time with this class. There was SO MUCH READING and hardly any of it made sense. We had three essays and two midterms, and the midterms were nice because we had unlimited retakes. But we never got to see what we got wrong. The essays and tests and content were all difficult to understand.

Professor Call is a decent professor, but the class itself is pretty hard. The tests are split into 3 sections, literature identification, art identification, and then just random multiple choice about what you learned that unit. He gives study guides that help with the art identification but other than that they aren't great

Lectures were awesome; he is passionate about the subject. The content is interesting, but be ready to memorize some art pieces, and spend 1-2 hours reading the lit before each class. We did 3 papers and 3 tests, but he let us take the tests multiple times with no penalty. The final is an interview with him where we demonstrate content knowledge.

Professor Call made class really fun and engaging. My only complaint is how much work there is outside of class. Between spending multiple hours each week playing video games, doing homework assignments, writing papers, watching films, reading an entire novel, and studying for his exams, it was way too much work. Felt like way more than 3 credits.
Super fun professor. He is a great teacher and is very entertaining.

This class missed the mark. Don't be fooled by the course description. Several assignments were either extremely over our heads (for most of the class, they required prerequisites we had not taken and that were not listed anywhwere) or indecent. Lectures were good, but the work outside of class was insane.

There were two BIG problems with this class: 1) It was like two classes in one, each with a significant amount of work required (math and humanities); and 2) The humanities content, especially for the last third of the course, including movies, movie clips, and literature, was inappropriate, in my opinion, with profanity and obscene content.

Professor Call is definitely heavy on reading and he makes you earn your grade. However, I honestly really enjoyed his lectures and he got me excited about learning things I never thought I'd be interested in! I loved the papers we wrote and honestly found the class really fulfilling. However, if you want an easy general, look elsewhere.

Professor Call is an engaging and passionate lecturer -- he gets and keeps you excited about literature! Speaking of lit -- there is a lot of it. Be prepared to schedule reading into your weekly schedule. The subject matter in this class is intensely interesting -- I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to learn for the sake of interest.

Professor Call is so passionate about history. His class is pretty much all lecture, but I really enjoyed his lectures and he did a great job of keeping students engaged. There are a lot of readings in this class, but you can get by without doing them once in awhile. There are 3 papers and 3 tests which make up the majority of the assignments.

I hated this class so much. Do not take it from him. I worked the hardest I have ever worked for this class and it wrecked me. When grading, he ripped into me every time. He was so harsh. He expects you to read like 6 full length medieval novels for this class. It's unreal how much he wants you to read. I truly cried over this class lol.

This class was way too much work for a general. The exams are intense because there's so much he expects us to remember but then the test questions are short. Example: final exam we must know 50 pieces of art but there are only 15 art questions on the exam. I did not enjoy this class
Professor Call is the best! His class was honestly just so much fun, and his lectures were always engaging. There's a lot of reading for the class, but if you put in the work you'll do fine.

I struggled with this class at the beginning. There is a ton of reading and the papers were a little difficult. However professor call is super nice and willing to help. He really loves what he teaches and  you dont always have to compete all the reading because he goes over most of it in class. His lectures are super energetic.

Dr. Call is such a sweet guy and very enthusiastic about what he teaches (which actually helps), but insane amount of work for a GE. The final is cumulative, the midterms are really detailed, and there's essays and quite a few other assignments throughout the semester. Overall good class, but so much unnecessary work and memorizing

Professor Call is a great teacher! There is quite a bit of reading, but it never took TOO long. The grades are heavily impacted on tests, but his study guides and reviews are big helps. If you understand those well, you'll do OK. I took his 201 and then his 202 class just because I didn't want 201 to end!
Great professor! He does a great job teaching and an amazing job explaining. He's not a hard grader and makes the class really fun. I would take more classes from him again.

He is a great professor! His classes and homework really make you think about the world we live in. I would take all of my classes from him again. There is quite a bit of homework but is doable and you learn a lot.

Prof. knows what he's talking about. There's a lot of reading, 3 papers, 30 short answer paragraph essays, and 3 exams. He's not an essay grader but also not a harsh one. Attendance for my class was mandatory because of it being online due to covid. Overall, Call is a good professor and I would take from him again.

The essays were painful for me, but you get to choose your own topic. The readings are heavy (I usually didn't do all of them). Prof is pretty funny, but I found myself zoning out in lectures. If you want an A in this class, you basically have to get a 93+ on all 3 of the tests.
Professor Call is a good guy and makes class interesting. Tests are extremely heavy and even if you study it is impossible to take a good grade.

Prof. Call is a kind person and smart, but this class was not well structured for an intro course. The readings were massive and took up a lot of time. Most of your grade is based on tests, so if you don't do well, your grade suffers. The tests have very specific questions from the readings that were ridiculous. Take it from someone else,

Professor Call is an epic professor, really knowledgeable about humanities and pretty chill guy too. This course has a ton of reading as homework, and you need to do it or at least know what happens in the reading to pass. It has 3 papers too, but these aren't so bad if you have good TA's that can help you out in writing them. Overall a good class.

Professor Call was a great teacher who was clearly passionate and very knowledgeable on the subject. There was way too many readings, but if you skim the book and watch videos on youtube about each class period you will be fine. There are 3 papers and 2 midterms that were not too bad. Not bad for a general class!

Took his class a year ago and he deserves better than a 3.9. It is true that there's A LOT of readings to do but his lectures amazing. I learned so much from him and he's one of the most thoughtful and caring professor I ever met at BYU. If you pay attention and take notes, you'll be fine. Seriously, his lectures are SO GOOD. Take it from him!

He is super smart and cracks some actually funny jokes but there is a ton of reading, especially compared to other humanities professors here. I struggled to understand the lengthy texts which is what a majority of the class and test is centered around so I felt lost almost the entire time because of the limited discussion on some of them

I could not tell you how many times I have cried because of his class, nice guy, hate the outline of the course. The tests are all based heavily on the readings that he hardly goes over. Save yourself and do not take this class. There's less heartache that way.

Prof. Call does really well with making the lectures engaging and the material enjoyable to learn about! It's a class with lots of reading (he can't really help that), and the tests are based heavily off the readings.
He is very passionate about what he is teaching which is nice, but it is a general ed class and he gives a lot of reading. The tests are heavily based on the readings.

Professor Call is a really good professor. He is very clear during lectures about what is important. The class was not hard, but the TAs that I had were absolutely awful, which made it quite unenjoyable. If he picked better TAs, the class would be a solid 10/10.

Dr. Call is amazing! I never write one of these, but I felt that he deserved a review to say how great he is. His lectures were so interesting. I have take many history classes before and really love studying it on my own, but he made connections and taught me things I hadn't known before. He is also super genuine and remembers everyone's names.

I loved Prof Call!! I actually looked forward to his lectures every other day. He is super funny and energetic. The class is a good amount of work but very doable. He prepares you for tests so well. I don't test well and I got a 93 and 94 on our first two exams. He is awesome and makes sure to have great TA's too. Papers are hard but doable.

One of the most down to earth, relatable, and open-minded professors I've had to date. Very approachable and incredibly accessible. Has significant insights, and will make this material relatable and useful for you.

Why does he only have a 3.9? I know. So yea, you read a lot in his class. But his lectures are SO GOOD. I was fascinated from start to finish. I almost got an A while skipping a lot of the reading. And the reading I did do was really eye opening. This was surprisingly interesting, funny, and even spiritually uplifting for a humanities class.

I took this class online. There is SO much reading, so prepare for that. It wasn't the worst, but it was a LOT of work. You really had to work a lot to get a good grade. Each chapter had a short answer which was self-graded. Then 3 essays and 3 closed-book tests (with 3 more essays). Not sure if it's different in a lecture setting, but lots of work

Professor Call was extremely helpful to me with each assignment. He truly cares about his students and wants us to succeed in his class. His lectures on Hamlet were absolutely fascinating. I've had him for 350 and have been his TA. My favorite thing is that he is extremely clear about grade expectations. Very knowledgeable about the Humanities

Take humanities 201 from this guy! Professor Call is a wonderful teacher who really cares for his students and knows what he is talking about. You can tell he loves what he teaches and, as a student, it is easy to love it too! Get the online textbook, it's cheaper and you don't use it enough to pay for the physical copy. You'll learn a lot!

This teacher was the best teacher. I liked him so much that I am taking another class from him next semester. His class is a bit difficult with a lot of reading and homework assignments. His TA's this semester weren't the best as they were never accessible and took forever to put grades in. However, he is an amazing teacher.

This is my second class I've taken from Professor Call because he made Ihum 201 so enjoyable. I don't LOVE the humanities, but he made every lecture entertaining and funny and he is super helpful and relatable. One of my favorite professors.

This class needs to be a priority when you are taking it, or you need to like the material. I love Humanities and am a Humanities minor, but even I found myself studying a lot for the midterm and final. Professor Call makes classes engaging, and I loved attending our lectures. There is a ton of reading, but if you like the material, it flies by.

I took this class online while being out of state and it was a very good class. There was an insane amount of reading but to be honest, I rarely read the whole assignments. I read summaries and watched YouTube videos to help understand the basics of the story. There are 3 papers (3 Pages each), 2 midterms, and 30 short responses(easy & self graded)

This was a difficult class, but if you do the reading and attend the lecture, you'll be fine. Professor Call makes the content really interesting and you can tell he genuinely cares about his students. His class was one of my favorites!
He is a great lecturer, and made class enjoyable to participate in, but there was WAY too much reading to do.
Excellent professor, very smart and professional but also very fun.  Made us laugh a lot.

Professor Call creates a great environment, which is really important, especially in a tough class like this one. There are four papers all on literary criticism with Molière's plays, but I was surprised that I got really good grades on them. Call is happy to meet with you to discuss paper ideas. I highly suggest it; it helped me a lot.

If you read at least some of the material and sparknote the rest, read the textbook reading, and attend class, you should be fine! It's not an easy A, but I've learned so much and he is the best professor I've had, just about. There are a couple of papers, but he helped me come up with a thesis for both papers. So wonderful.

Prof Call is super entertaining and always has the class laughing. He definitely knows his stuff.  BUT be ready to read so so so much. I spend ridiculous amounts of time reading for this class. You have to write a response before each class about the reading so you can't skip out. Plus, the tests are hard b/c theres many questions about the reading

DUDE you will read more for this class then you'll read for all of your classes combined.... he's a good lecturer bc he knows his stuff, but literally you have to read so much and then do a response about the reading before each class. His tests are hard because they're all about the readings. I don't recommend, especially if you hate humanities

I love Professor Call! He is a great teacher and it is obvious that he loves the humanities. He is also an effective mentor and always looking to help his students succeed. Super fun guy, super fun class. He grades on a higher plane than other BYU professors I have had-- which I appreciate. He asks for excellence and gives great feedback.

This is the first, and probably only, time I'll rate a professor just because I liked him so much.  Crystal clear, kind, great feedback, super intelligent, humble.  This professor is the best I've ever had.  He had a small assignment due every class period and for that there's reading to do, but he makes me like like the material.  Take this class!

Okay....he is a hard teacher. There is a lot you have to read and know for the class. It's pretty much mandatory you go to the class to do well on the tests. That being said, he is very nice and you can tell he loves what he does. Also--all of the tests and grading is fair. It's just ALOT to study.
I love Professor Call! He is so knowledgable and every lecture is fascinating. He's fast-paced, clear, and reasonable. Very willing to help you if you are organized. Great teacher!

Prof Call is the best. He's super helpful and always willing to help you with the material or even internships. He gives reviews sheets and in class reviews before tests. The class requires quite a bit of reading, but what Humanities class doesn't? He's super funny and creates a great class environment, seldom gets off topic, and is a fair grader.

I loved this class! Prof Call was able to lead engaging discussion in his class. The reading was enjoyable and the assignments relevant. He gives a lot of helpful feedback on all the papers and grades easy enough. I also loved our final project. Definitely my favorite class and favorite professor so far.

Dont take this class if you can help it. Professor Call is nice but the course is a "jack of all trades, master of none" deal. The papers are hard and he and his TA are not on the same page when it comes to grading. I am a theater major and only got an 80 on the Theater paper. You dont learn much that counts as "humanities"

Prof. Call is a really nice guy and loves his subject. However, his quizzes and tests were beyond ridiculous. Most of the class agreed that there wasn't enough time during the tests, and the grading is pretty subjective. It ended up being my hardest class so far.

Dr. Call loves his subject. I would really have a hard time seeing why a student wouldn't like him, and I think our entire class loved him. He knows his material, such a kind and quirky guy. Good sense of humor, which comes out as the semester progresses. Take his class!

Super nice guy.  Not too much outside work required.  Tests are mostly essays which are annoying but you have topic options to choose from.  3 fairly easy essays (3-4 pgs) during the semester.  Quizzes on selected readings but you can just spark note them and you'll ace them all.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! I hated it. The class was interesting but he is ridiculous. His tests are hard and so are his quizzes. Even if you do the reading, its hard- if not impossible to get a 100 on the quizzes. The papers you have to write...good luck. Unless you write the way he wants you to. A complete waste of time. I am not impressed!

I LOVED Dr. Call and this class. It is obvious that he really loves what he teaches. A lot depends who your TA was and mine was great! Each test has a very long study guide, but if you study all of it you will do well on the tests.
I would recommend taking HUM 201 from Professor Call- he gives out a study guide for each test and you ONLY need to worry about what's on that study guide- NOTHING ELSE. This makes for easy studying.

Even though I was deeply interested in the subject material, I had a hard time keeping myself awake, perhaps due to the early hour (for me.) I would recommend taking the class with a friend and sitting in the front. Good class, easy to know what to expect.

Dr. Call is amazing and very amicable.  He knows his stuff and can make it really interesting.  Tests aren't on bubble sheets, which was intimidating at first, but turned out not to be too bad.  Three essays, nothing too difficult.  Definitely take this class from Dr. Call!
Great guy, not mean or intimidating at all.  Fun lectures, he ties in media to make it more enjoyable.  Helps you know exactly what to expect on the exams.   heart of gold.

Professor Call is a great guy, who really tries to make class both productive and enjoyable. He has reading quizzes often, so you really have to make sure to attend class every day, and do all of the reading (which is sometimes a lot, and other times, almost nothing). The tests aren't too hard if you take good notes.   He also grades very fairly.

Dr. Call is very knowledgeable. It's obvious that he loves what he teaches. If you go to class and study the study guide, you should have no problem on tests. The reading is vital, but not hard. Not only is it a doable A, this class teaches you so much. And it's useful!

Prof. Call is great at teaching and explaining things.  He is great with the tests, they are just right with how hard they are.  I was in the honors sections and so he required us to read a lot, and you do have to study for the tests, but they are doable and fair.

He can be interesting to listen to, but he often makes contradictions. Most of the class was really easy, but 50% of our grade was given in the last two weeks of class- a 10-pg paper and a final, but were graded by the professor instead of the TA- like all the other assignments were- which killed my grade, not being used to his style of grading.

O.K. To clear up the confusion. There are 2 Prof. Michael Call (Sr and Jr).  Both are amazing teachers.  This will explain the different ratings.  Sr has a master study list for his classes and so testing is easier.  Jr was still working out some of those handout kinks. But both are amazing.  They both are passionate and will take the time to help.

In my opinion, a great teacher.  You will be required to read a lot, but it is from a variety of texts and subjects so it stays interesting enough.  He definitely knows the subject and has a passion for teaching, and really cares about his students succeeding.  He will definitely be flexible, without being a pushover.  A is definitely possible.

I am a business major, but really enjoyed Professor Call's class.  He prepares well and engages in interesting discussion during every class.  Don't get me wrong--this class is not easy.  Reading assignments between every class, frequent quizzes, discussion board before every class, essays, and intense tests.  Extra credit offered. A is possible.

I am currently enrolled in the class and I like it a lot.  Professor Call is a very nice man and I think quite funny (in a quirky way).  You have to be willing to work in this class.  If you are a lazy you will not do well.I think he definitely knows what he's talking about and he does genuinely care about his students which is very refreshing.

If you like reading for hours, writing about something you donʻt care about, and like someone talking you to sleep take it from Call. I am very surprised that BYU is hiring such poor quality teachers.

Had him for independent study class. Prepare to do more work than ever before. In a single lesson he had ten pages of notes, 5 readings from C& V and 3 (50) page plays. Then you have to take a quiz and write an essay. Take it somewhere else if you can. Horrible experience.

I took an independent study class from him. This guy is a joke. His syllabus is very vague, but he will dock you heavily if you donʻt include everything he wants. The guy is a clown. Totally unwilling to admit that he is wrong. I am graduating BYU with a 3.8 and this is the worst class I have ever taken. Take it at BYU if you can from someone

What a great teacher. Possibly the best at BYU. I learned so much. Tried to keep it interesting. Made sure we understood each section. He spent extra time on a subject id the class was not understanding. Plan on lots of writing.

Wonderful class and wonderful professor!  He really knows what he's talking about and he's really good at breaking it down for people who don't.  He's very open to questions and encourages discussion.  I learned so much and really enjoyed it!

I actually really enjoyed this class!  He gave you the information that you would need to study and the exams were exactly from the lectures, not just totally random.  I learned a lot and did pretty well.  Just pay attention and you'll learn and do well!

AMAZING professor! Very interested in making sure everyone understands and follows the material. He's understanding of different situations and does absolutely anything he can to help you succeed. Offers a lot of extra credit opportunities and each test comes with a study guide. One of my favorites.
I was completely frustrated by this class and this teacher. Grading was ridiculous. I highly discourage taking this class or take another section if you can.
No Comments

He is an amazing teacher, incredibly knowledgable and very nice. I am a senior and this senior seminar on Impressionism has been the best class in my major--very interesting topic. I would highly recommend him and the class. The key to doing well is to go to class and do the work--you will get what you put into it!
Really nice. Class is interesting. He cares a lot about the class and puts forth a  lot of effort.  Some of the readings are long and boring.  His tests are pretty hard.

He's kinda goofy but he does know his stuff. Definitely do the reading, quizzes kill ya if you don't. Go to study sessions with TA, go into his office or send in journal entries early, and do all the extra credit. He's super nice and was so helpful when I went into his office to see how I could improve my grade. Not the most scintillating, though.

Call is a fun guy, and he makes class interesting. He’s really into his subject and is excited about teaching his students. Incredibly nice man and fun class. However there are way too many quizzes, and papers. It’s possible to get an A but you have to keep at it and work really hard.

My idea of the perfect Hum teacher. Clear expectatiions. A lot of matierial is covered so don't get behind. Memorize the art work he gives you in the outline early on and the tests are fine.  I loved his knowlegde and humility. He was willing to help as much as needed. There is no reason not to get an A if you are willing to read.
Great Professor. Honest interest in student's learning, and very skilled at applying and demonstrating concepts. Assessment was fair. Class was captivating and upbeat.

I was completely frustrated by this class and this teacher. After taking this class, i have no interest in humanities. Grading was ridiculous. Criteria was given AFTER the assingments were turned in and graded. The class average for the class overall was 65%. I highly discourage taking this class if you have any interest in enjoying humanities.

His tests are hard.  The study guide it around 5 pages and out of the 30 multiple choice it seemed that maybe half were actually on the study guide.  The average on the final was a 67%.  I didn't find him all that helpful when confronting him with questions.  He definately was not one of my favorite professors.

Dr. Call was one of my favorite teachers this semester. There was a lot of reading, but most of it was enjoyable. He's great about asking for feedback to make the class better. He really wants everyone to do well and wants to help students be successful. He has a great sense of humor and could make me laugh. He gets to know everyone by name too.

I thought that some of the subject matter was interesting but he was not.  I feel he knew what he was talking about but his passion is not very contagious.  Tests were rediculous and the reading was outrageous. His papers were fine and if you write them well you will get A's on them.  Good luck on the tests!
Lots of reading, but you will know a lot of new information about the ancients when you are finished. I had to study a lot, but it was a great class.

Dr. Call is an excellent professor, very helpful and willing to help students. He loves teaching and the subject matter and is effective at helping you understand. His class was NOT an easy class but rewarding. LOTS of reading, difficult but well written tests. He also did a good job at bringing spiritual insights into the lessons when appropriate.

I graduated early from high school and took this class with independent study this past spring.  You write one-paged papers for every lesson.  Make sure you include everything that is on the speedback assignments in the essays.  Assignments are open-book.  Tests are difficult, but I got an A- overall.  Lots of reading! Final not comprehensive.
He's very clear and concise.  He is very supportive of his students.
This was a really good class.  It wasn't really easy, but I learned a ton.  I'll definitely take another class from him next semester.

I hated this class and I thought that Dr. Call was kind of boring and a hard grader (then again, I was engaged that semester), but still, didn't like the experience at all.  Would not take him again, ever.

I didn't expect to enjoy myself in this class, but I actually had quite a bit of fun. You don't have to really go to the lectures to get a good grade, but I did study quite a bit out of class. The two things that helped me survive were his helpfulness outside of class and his funniness in class. I'd take another class from him.
He is great.  Interested in the students, clear, and fun. Has all the notes on ppt in blackboard, that's a plus.

He is not knowledgeable on the subject and does a very poor job on such to say subjects. He grades papers very harshly and has no desire to help you. I got an A in the class but trust me Dr. Call is a waste of time. Dont take him. If i was BYU I would fire him immediately. I have no beaf with him it's just that he is average and mediocre.

You have to keep up with the reading because there are quizzes in the discussion groups. I slept through much of the lectures and still did fine because he puts the lectures online and has good study guides. I enjoyed the material, but not Prof. Call

WOW--go to your TA section and you should be fine. lectures are entirely pointless. he'll ramble on about pointless art junk and you'll just sit there wondering WHY you are even there. Knows what he's talking about but the class is lame. Papers were graded hard, but tests were fair

Prof. Call is entertaining and really gets excited about the class. A good TA is nice, but you have to keep up in the reading if you expect a good grade. Prof. Call makes it easy top do well. The tests are very straight forward and right off the study guides.

I love the subject, and the homework taught me a lot, but his lectures were dull and confusing.  Call will often ramble for about 30 min, and once the class is asleep, he'll subtely throw in the need to know for the tests, which often is missed by most.  Pick a better professor.
he is very nice. his study guides are very helpful and his tests arene't too bad if you know what's on the study guides. getting a good ta really helps you stay interested.
I hated this class.  I think he is not very knowledgeable, extremely unclear, and boring.  Don't take him.
A real jerk!!

Dr. Call seems to know about art himself but can'tt teach it to save his life.  He is horrible at giving students time to take notes, and he grades essays much too harsh.  If you have  a choice between choosing Dr. Call or a swarm of killer bees, take the bees.    SERIOUSLY
Dr. Call was a fairly interesting techer but he was really condescending -- he asked a lot of stupid questions and expected us to answer. His tests were pretty hard but fair. Lots of reading.

Can't help but admit this class is boring and probably would be with any professor.  Dr. Call is nice professor, he really does know your name, but his lecture aren't the kind that get me interested in Humanities.  His course work is fair, his test review sheets help. Good teacher. Boring class.

I took this class for a GE, but I loved it! Dr. Call really knows what he's talking about, he's been to the places and seen the art live. He also makes a point to know his students. I never talked in class and he knew my name! Go to class and do the study guides and you'll be fine!
he is very nice and helpful. he gives really good long study guides.. but his test are fairly difficult. class is interesting... lots of reading for the class.. but here's a hint (sprak notes)
No Comments

Very interesting teacher - enjoyed the lectures very much.  Tests are semi-hard but you get a very specific review sheet with all you need on it and you get all the powerpoints online.  Homework is mostly reading and a few short essays.
I loved Professor Child is Portuguese is amazing and a really enjoyed his class! I was rarely bored in class despite the content being somewhat dry (grammar rules). Would highly recommend.
Highly recommend! Professor Child is a genius in linguistics, Portuguese, and language learning. The class is mostly made up of lots of small assignments, so the load is manageable.

Dr. Child is great and his accent is perfect! He definitely knows his stuff and he is always willing to help you but 326 is a beast! By far the hardest Port. class. All his tests except the final are take home and your grade depends on the tests. His questions tend to be very vague so the more you write the higher you will score! Hard to get an A.

The class is test heavy, but if you take the time to study the material, you will succeed. The class is designed to use relevant, real-world examples, so there really is no dull moments or busy work without meaning. Assignments and exams are graded quickly, which means he cares about giving useful feedback. His pronunciation is on point!

I've loved all my Portuguese classes at BYU, but Mike's phonetics class was my worst one yet. Mike is a good teacher, really cares about his students, but the class itself was set up only through PowerPoints and going over a huge quantity of material. I felt swamped keeping up with it all since he had to move on so quickly.

Prof. Child was by far my favorite teacher this semester! He is super caring for everyone and really wants to help us learn good Portuguese. He is totally willing to give help outside of class. He is very reasonable on his grading, not to easy but not to hard. He knows both Brazilian and Portugal Portuguese and can do both accents perfectly!

Dr. Child is one of the best professors at BYU. He is great at explaining difficult material, makes the lectures fun, and is very caring and helpful towards his students. I definitely recommend taking a class from him.
Mike is awesome!! He is a great teacher- doesn't go too fast or too slow, is genuinely interested in you as a person not just you as a student, funny, and you can tell he really loves portuguese.
Professor Child is a dedicated teacher who cares about his students.  His classes are interesting and fun, while at the same time challenging.  Definitely worth taking.  I recommend Professor Child!

Professor Child is an awesome teacher! He teaches from a Portugal perspective, even though most students prefer the Brazilian perspective, but he will do anything to help out those who want to learn from a Brazilian perspective. Very easy to understand, very concerned about his students. I HIGHLY recommend him!

Professor Child is extremely helpful and very understanding. He expects an honest effort in the classwork, but he does not expect perfection. Very easy to understand and makes learning a foreign language a good experience.
He's an amazing teacher and an awesome person. I learned a ton! Also, he's really hot.

Michael is an awesome professor and a delight to be around altogether. The final project for SOC 300 is tough and pretty time-consuming and I wish I would've worked on it throughout the semester instead of all at once - don't be like me. Other than that the class is pretty straightforward.

Michael is hilarious and witty, and very knowledgeable and qualified. Tells great stories, has fun lectures. Attendance is not required and the class content is really not too challenging, but if you like it then you can go as deep as you want. Michael also gives great book recommendations. He did pick his nose once during class though.

DR. COPE IS AMAZING! He is by far my favorite professor in the soc department! All of his classes are so well organized, and he is so personable and cares so much about all of his students. The content was also super interesting! There are 4 exams, weekly assignments, and a huge research proposal that you can ask for help/feedback on!

Bless his heart, you can tell he is an absolute n to the arc to the ssist. Sound it out. He gave the most incredible lectures, and as long as you're willing to memorize HIS definitions, you got that down. See him in office hours. Very smart and interesting, but completely full of himself, despite insisting he is not. Take his class.
Quiz every week about reading. He gives SO many extra creidt assignments. His lectures are the best. Chose this professor he's the best!
Michael is great! He tries hard to make his discussions engaging and keeps his homework assignments on a super manageable level. I would definitely recommend this class.

I absolutely loved Michael and I loved this course. Everyone should take it. I appreciated how he looked at the content through a sociological lense. I think this perspective really drew me in (as a sociology minor lol) instead of the other two professors I went to one class period of then dropped. Glad I got into Michael's section in the end!

Dr. Cope is seriously my favorite professor at BYU!!!! He does such a great job explaining concepts and class expectations, and he is awesome at creating a safe space for students to share their thoughts on the topics we are discussing. This was also such an awesome course, so so cool for a sociology elective.

Michael Cope's classes are some of the most engaging and enjoyable classes on campus! He is so fun and knows how to interact with students in productive and entertaining ways. He is incredibly insightful and pushes you as a learner in the best ways!! Take classes from him!

He's amazing. So kind and funny. I learned so much and was super engaged every single time. You're not gonna like him if you have fragile masculinity and a close-minded perspective, but I don't think that'll be an issue if you're signing up for Michael's classes. He's super awesome and I highly recommend him.

Absolutely hilarious and incredibly unique. I found him slightly impersonable 1-on-1, but he was overall engaging and made learning actively fun. The test weren't too hard but you did have to read several full books. It is very easy to enjoy his lectures.

Michael Cope is one of the best professors I've ever had at BYU! He is absolutely hilarious and this course is designed for your success. Seriously, I went to class just for some amazing entertainment and a great feel-good study environment which I really appreciated.

Michael is amazing and goes above and beyond in every way to make sure his students succeed! I found the class content to be hard and the tests (all done in class) were stressful for me, but if you reach out to him he will work with you until you get it. I recommend him as a teacher if you are interested in sociology and willing to work hard.

Dr. Cope is a great lecturer and I really enjoyed this class.  The content we covered in class is probably not the most important for students just starting to learn about sociology, but I took the class to help prepare for the MCAT and it was all pretty relevant to MCAT sociology.  Overall, it was a pretty interesting and remarkably easy class.

Michael is awesome! He genuinely cares about his students - offers tons of extra credit, and even offered to copy and paste our midterm grades as our final exam grade so we could have less to stress about. Honestly you can just sparknote the books he assigns, but they are super interesting and worth reading. Highly recommend as a GE!!

Michael is the best professor I've ever had at BYU! He is so funny, and makes his lectures fun and interesting. He assignments are not hard, and he offers a TON of extra credit. He also just cares about his students so much, especially about their stress levels and well being. Take this class from him, it's an easy general credit and so much fun!!!

Exceptional teacher. My favorite class I've taken at BYU thus far. The class is very easy but the content can be a little harder to understand. He only gave us 8 assignments that were all really easy, only we had to read 3 books as a class. The tests were easy, especially the final lol. Gives easy extra credit but rarely does except late work.

Take the time to get to know Dr. Cope. Excellent person who can really open your eyes and change your perspective on a lot of life. Because I made the effort to read a book of my choosing for extra credit he showed me a book that truly changed me for the better. Very intelligent and kind and reasonable. Yes it was an easy enough A.

Michael is easily one of my favorite professors so far. He cares about his students and has worked into the schedule off days so that we could focus on other classes. There were 8 online video assignments that were super easy and two exams on learning suite. There were no study guides for the exams but they were not too hard.

I really appreciated how he prioritized the students over himself and his bell curves. He cared about our mental health and would often express concern. There is a bit of reading, but most of the books are short. The assignments are not hard, but the tests can be a little tricky. Tests come from application of lectures, so I recommend attending.

He doesn't grade on attendance, but I recommend showing up. Michael is super funny - even though the subject matter could get heavy, he kept the mood fairly comfortable. You read a few books, but they're interesting and the assignments are straightforward. He is very fair and you can tell he cares about the students and our learning.

My favorite professor at BYU by far. He is so caring, very funny, and super fair. He loves his job and is their for you to learn, not for you to memorize stuff. Everyone should take a class from him and more professors should follow his example.

Michael is a great professor and it is obvious that he cares about his students. He gives great lectures and a lot of redemption and mercy points for the exams. You are required to be there in person and skipping class makes your grade drop. I would take anything by him again. One of the best classes.

His syllabus is a little scary but this is genuinely the best class I've ever taken. He says there won't be extra credit opportunities but nearly every exam has some sort of "redemption points" opportunity and he is so kind as a person and such an incredible and entertaining lecturer. Would 100% take this class (or any other class) with him again.

This class was not my favorite, I feel like he tried too hard to "fit in" with the students and it just made it kind of awkward... We only had four books to read for the semester and then our book review videos, so it was really easy, but pretty boring. Overall, I don't feel like he was very accessible and I wasn't very satisfied with the class.

MICHAEL IS AMAZING!!! I'd definitely take another class from Michael. You leave class wanting to help the world and people around you. Learn a lot of hard things but very enlightening and important to be aware of. I loved the books he assigns very fair tests and easy book assignments. If you have the opportunity definitely take his class!

Michael is hilarious and manages to make an inherently boring class pretty interesting. You have to memorize a lot for the tests, but he is a very fair grader. I definitely recommend taking classes from Prof. Cope.

You cannot go wrong taking Michael's class. He might try to scare you the first week, but hold on and just take the class. He is incredibly clear on his expectations for every assignment and test. He never wanted to trick you and truly has your best interest at heart. I felt like there was a very appropriate work load for a 3 credit class. DO IT!!

This class was easily one of my favorites! I came in prepared to be bored and to struggle but the lectures were very interesting, informative, and funny! He is fair, principled, helpful, and very understanding. Be aware of deadlines and homework because the class for us was not on learning suite and was all on paper instead.

Professor Cope is a good professor, his lectures are engaging and he seems to care about his students. However, the exams were very difficult and specific! You will never receive a study guide for an exam, and anything he has said in class could be on exams. Write down everything he says and go to class and you'll be ok.
Have to be there to turn in assignments

Michael makes the content extremely engaging! Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you go you will learn the content. The class is organized so that it is assignment/ reading heavy at the beginning of the semester and tapers off, so start strong and ask for help with the initial assignments because the TAs and Michael are knowledgeable and helpful.

Michael is honestly a great professor. His class is really well organized and he actually cares for his students. It is lecture heavy but he is engaging and makes the subject matter less brutal. The homework is pretty minimal, but his expectations are high with what you do turn in. Follow his directions exactly and you'll do fine. Highly recommend

I really enjoy Michael's classes and look forward to an opportunity to take more. He is pedantic in his grading. The final paper/project at the end of the semester is a research proposal which is great experience. However, in his grading there is much for to do with little, fixable issues than grading on the quality or validity of research design.

Michael cares about the well-being of his students a lot. Michael once reached out to me personally after seeing my unsatisfactory grade on an assignment to help me understand it better. He made the workload the easiest and was most accommodative of all my professors when the pandemic hit, though the class subject itself is pretty difficult.

His tests are all written answer (meaning, no multiple choice or T/F) which is hard so you really have to study. Thankfully he helps his students when they need it. He is really kind in answering questions, but sometimes his explanation of things is a little overly academic (like he could explain things simpler I think.) He is funny and caring.

Michael (he goes by his first name to everyone) is quite a character! He's a nice guy and I liked him, but he's very quirky and jokes around a lot in class. He's surprisingly strict in his grading, but is totally cool about changing your grade if you can make a case for yourself. He did a good job with a class that is inherently boring and hard

I know, a women's studies class from a man, but Michael presented the information in this course amazingly! He suited the assignments to our specific class and how we decided we wanted to learn. Weekly write-ups on assigned readings and a couple of self-directed projects. This has been my favorite class at BYU!

This class is hands down the best class I have taken at BYU. Michael is incredible and really wants his students to succeed and will help you any way that he can so that you do succeed. For the first time at BYU, I feel that I can succeed as a college student, thanks to Michael.

I loved Michaels class. It was hard and you have to work for your grade, but he is available to make appointments to help with grades whenever you need. He also is funny which I appreciate because it makes lectures more interesting!

Michael is an incredible professor. He frontloads the course, which is scary in the beginning but the homework is always manageable and it makes the end of the semester less stressful. I was never afraid about what was going to be on the tests. The content on the tests was very fair. As long as you study his in-class reviews you'll be golden.

Michael is an amazing professor, and I wish I could take all my sociology classes from him. He is a super fair grader, and the class is very front-loaded, which is intimidating at the beginning of the semester but is really nice at the end of the semester. He is always willing to help students if you reach out and come to him. He's hilarious too!

Michael is an amazing professor. Honestly, if I could take all of my classes from him...I would. He is very straightforward about what is expected and he doesn't waste your time with anything that isn't important. We talk about real world ideologies that will change the way you view the world. He is a great professor. Highly recommend.

Michael is one of the best professors I have had at BYU. Typically I do not do well on tests and have to rely on all of the assignments to get good grades, but I always felt prepared for his exams and felt that they were very doable! If you go to class and pay attention, Michael will make sure you get a good grade! Made boring material enjoyable.

HATED this class! 10/10 do not recommend! The tests and quiz questions for this class were super wordy and next to impossible to answer whether you'd done the reading or not. I also felt that Michael was unprofessional in his jokes and the way that he controlled classroom participation. I always left this class frustrated and unresolved.

Michael was a great teacher! I took this class for a GE requirement and I HIGHLY recommend it. He's very funny and sarcastic, but also very aware of sensitive subjects in his class. He will NOT post any slides or lecture materials online, or study guides of any sort, so you really need to go to class. I personally loved going to class though!

Michael is definitely different from your typical BYU professor - but that's what makes him awesome! He's very real, which is an important thing in a course about multiculturalism. One of my favorite classes though - I know my attitudes changed! Go to class and go to see the TAs for help with the papers.
