Michael is awesome! He's unlike any other professor at BYU. He's funny but sensitive to the concerns of the class. This was one of the most fun classes I've taken, and he actually cares about his students and loves to help u out if u need it. I love his class. Truly the easiest GE I have taken at BYU. I am sure that I will get an A. Easterling was really caring to me in my situation. I really liked how it was not just lectures everyday and activities instead.

I cannot explain this class to someone who's never taken it. Professor Easterling is well meaning, but dreaded waking up every day because of this class. Pay attention in class and review before exams and you'll be fine!

I thought that Professor Easterling was very funny in the classroom, but I also loved how he was always teaching us life lessons trying to help us be our best. Professor Easterling is AMAZING! He truly cares about his students and wants them to do well academically, spiritually, and professionally. Professor Easterling is extremely inspirational and always relates humanities back to the Gospel and the 4 aims of a BYU education!

I enjoyed professor Easterlings class and the way he taught. He always reminded us what was coming up and what was expected. Lots of group work, but it turned out to be fun. I have never had a class were we designed and made a sticker. A couple of the people from my group have become close friends of mine. I will take another class from Easterling.

Lots of assignments that have don't necessarily have to do with the subject of the class. A lot of it feels like busy work. Mandatory group assignments that have to be done outside of class create logistical problems as students have different schedules.

Professor Easterling was amazing. I hope I can take another class from him in the future. He makes the topics in class fun. But most important he really cared about us. If you get to take a class with him you are lucky.

LEGIT: BEST TEACHER EVER. I've never heard anything but kind words about Professor Easterling (and that says a lot). His classes are fun to go to because he makes each lecture fun and engaging. He cares very much for students' understanding. One of the nicest professors I have ever had. 

For sure - EASIEST CLASS i have ever had.
Loved Professor Easterling. Loved his class. Will take again.
Claims to be accommodating, and is completely unreasonable with his class format. I reached out on multiple occasions and all i get are long emails which are completely useless. dont take.

Loved Professor Easterling. best class I took last semester. The layout was easy to follow and the reviews helped me remember stuff for the tests. Good class, and really interesting stuff we learn about. Watched a couple movies, have a research project, and each class we  do some group work. Easterling is very cool. He is always willing to help, I have met with him a couple times in his office. Good class, good teacher.

I definitely recommend. I think he does a good job of providing easily digestible information and resources about each topic. Our group meetings have good structure and collaborative documents. Not mindless reading, tests aren't stressful, the "gospel insights" are always super cool. Raises awareness of respecting other religions and culture.

Way too much work for this class. Professor Easterling is a really nice guy, but I feel like he expects too much. He assigns way too much busy work. I am a senior who just took the MCAT. Felt like I was taking OCHEM again. Class wasn't insanely hard, just took way too much time. Really good professor. Class was average difficulty level for college. But he made it fun. I thought he was pretty straight forward with how he grades and what he expects. This was my 2nd class from him. If you need a humanities class Easterling is your guy.

This class was ridiculous. It wasn't too hard, but it took so much effort to get an A. You will have a million assignments in this class, and it is like all busy work. lots of writing, and he's kinda picky about it (never gives full credit), but overall the class is the easiest you're gonna find for this GE credit. Easterling is such a GOOD person and he cares about his students. Not like your traditional lecture class at all. Lots of in class discussions and different activities and presentations. I like that we were not just sitting around everyday looking at slides listening to the teacher.

Easterling is great. Go to class, participate, work with your group. Pretty straight forward. Also when you need him to help you, he is there to help. Great teacher.

Professor Easterling makes this class super engaging. He genuinely cares about students and sends helpful reminders. With the free textbook and resources like ChatGPT and unstuck ai, acing the exams is a breeze. A great class - would highly recommend!

He cares about his work but he needs to chill with emails. He sends several per week. Most info could be said in class but he lectures the whole time. He never ends on time. I have never left a review for a teacher whose class I am currently in. Professor Easterling just went above and beyond for me as a student. I have never had a teacher that really showed that they genuinely cared about my success as a student until now. Thank you! I will never forget this.

Professor Easterling is the right right choice.
I love Mr. Easterling. One of the very best teachers I have had at BYU. He is very focused on us as students. It's not false either, he really cares. Like I said one of the best!

I loved how he organized this class. I loved how caring he was towards each of us. I loved that he would send our reminder emails about assignments and the like. Professor Easterling is a great professor, and i loved how he brought the spirit with him into our class.

I'm in my last week in his humanities 202 class. It has been very fun. Not just fun amd game. I have been learning a lot about the humanities and life. Easterling really wants us as students to focus on becoming the best we can become. And I have learned things that will definitely help me for the next three years. Really good teacher.

I really enjoyed professor Easterling and his class on India. Reall y cool stuff that we covered in the class. Not hard at all as long as you are following along with the online work. Mr. Easterling was an amazing professor, funs class periods, make sure that you attend class to get all the information for the exams. Attendance is not really mandatory, but if you attend you will be able to pass the exams with ease. Very relaxed and relatable professor.

I believe that in person discussions significantly enhance the strengths of this class. Great chance to meet people around you. Truly I enjoyed this class.

This blended class is structured very well. I appreciated how it was organized with readings, self checks and quizzes, and group discussions. I don't think I have ever had a professor that cared more about me - as an actual person - than professor Easterling.

BEWARE! Many student athletes take his class and sway his RMP scores. He is extremely disorganized, shuts down students rudely if their answer isn't what he wanted, and his tone of speaking is dramatic (might sound petty, but it gets old FAST). Strongly advise picking a different professor.

Super lit! Loved the reminders he'd drop on Learning Suite about our assignments, readings, and all that research stuff. I'm not really an "A" type of student. But he gave us this semester long Deep Work extra credit assignment which has honestly changed how I approach my classes and assignments. Really clear layout and system for Sharing and talking to other students and receiving feedback from the TA and the professor! Lots of opprutunies to recieve extra credit. I enjoyed the class discussions, unit collaborations and the quizzes after every section. Professor Easterling is great and really cares about his students and their performance.

This was the best humanities class I have ever taken (small sample size as I am an engineering student). I recommend. Good content, teacher made it fun, and the classes were often group discussion vs straight lecture. I prefer more interactive classes.

I have never felt more catfished by rate my professor in my life. I took him solely because he had a lot of reviews and had a 5 rating. He was unpredictable with assignments sending out emails the day before class that we needed to do some sort of readings

Professor Easterling really cares about his students. I graduate in a few days and I wish I had taken this class earlier as a student. PS - He Loves the AIMS of BYU

Terrible. Don't take IHUM 243 from this guy (for some reason it wasn't in the list of options to choose from but this is the class I took). Absolutely go for his class. It's a humanities thing, but he turns it into a vibe. Legit, I've discovered tons about myself in this class, and it's been a whole journey. Professor Easterling. He is the review. 5 Stars for the Man!

He is the best! His class is the best! I am planning on taking his IHUM 243 class in the future.
Great guy. Great class. I am a STEM student, but professor Easterling made the humanities accessible and understandable. I recommend.

Easterling is definitely the professor to take a humanities class from. If you are new at BYU take his class. He is great and he cares.

I loved professor Easterling's class. Really inspired me to be a better student. I didn't expect to learn everything I learned from a Humanities class. I would love to take another class from him.

Loved his class. Great lectures. I didn't want to take any Humanities classes but he really made it worth while.

Great guy. I'm glad I was able to take his class. He loves the material, the subject, and his students. He gets an A from me.

I loved professor Easterling's class. Clearly he loves what he teaches and to shows in how he teaches and interacted with my class. Great teacher and I loved his class. Really opened my eyes to the human existence. Fun group project and some basic research assignments. His lectures were very interesting and covered stuff that was fun to learn about.

I took his Spring class. Straightforward class and what I expected from a general education class here at BYU. I thought Professor Easterling was great. Very kind, very understanding, respectful and understands what it is like to be a college student. I would definitely take a class from him again.
Yes, yes, yes. 100%. Professor Easterling is a great teacher. Loved his class. If I can take another class from him I will. Bet.

Michael Easterling is a good professor and loves what he teaches about. It is a really good GE class that helped me understand why the humanities are important. He introduced me to a lot of things I've never seen or heard before. He is also very nice and very considerate of everything that we as students have going on.

I like professor Easterling. I enjoyed his Spring term class. He helped me with my writing. He helped me with my thesis statement and really explained how important it is. Never had anyone do that before. He would help me with a lot of feedback and so great instructional questions. I felt like he really cared about me as a student and person.
I can't speak for anyone else but this class was awesome!!!!!!!!!!!!! I heart emoji Professor Easterling!!!!!! Yeah, for real.

Let me say that without Professor Easterling I would have probably failed this class. I had a lot going on personally during the Spring Term and he was understanding, easy to contact, and willing to work with me. He talks about empathy a lot in class, but it's not just talk, he believes it and practices what he teachers. I am super grateful.

Awesome class. Only book I had to get was a graphic novel, which that is cool. Seriously really enjoyed everything Professor Easterling shared. He is a good guy and was easy to work with when I had to make up a couple assignments.

Really enjoyed the class. Professor really made the tests straight forward. Quizzes are straight forward as well as long as you actually do the reading. Good class. We talked about a lot of important issues and I saw how the Humanities relates to and interprets our world. Also I was 5 points away from an A and he helped me out. Thank you!

Loved this class. Awesome lectures. 3 hour class is tough but that is Spring and Summer at BYU. Seriously loved the class and Professor Easterling. Everytime I reached out to him he helped me, if I had questions he gave me great feedback. Great experience for me.

These lectures were really boring with a high expectation of participation. This professor makes you feel belittled and expects you to have lots of knowledge on the subject. Exams are hard and based off the lectures so takes lots of notes and do not space out in class!
I really like Professor Easterling. Good class, good material. Yeah, that is his review. -The End

Just finished his Humanities 202 class, for my GE credit. Very worthwhile class. Good teacher, teaches some pretty interesting stuff. Spring Term class are 3 hours which can be tough but that is the University not professor E. Yeah I'd take a class from him again.

LOVE Professor Easterling. He's respectful, reasonable, and truly cares about students. If you go to class, participate (you can just volunteer to read a slide if you're shy), and take notes, you'll get a good grade. Easy, fun class.
I love this guy! What a class. Just finished today. Best gen ed class I have taken at BYU. Cool professor. Nice. Caring. Seriously go to class and get an A and learn some cool stuff.

Professor Easterling passes my review (unlike some other professors). Guy is a stand up guy. Actually cares about the students as much if not more than he cares about the material he teaches. Real solid people person. He was understanding of everything going on in my life and did all he could to help me navigate the semester. Thx chief!

Good teacher. His class is great. I selected "Skip Class? You Won't pass." because almost everything on the tests come from his lectures, which are actually very enjoyable. He has a great sense of humor, although I think it might be lost on some students over Zoom. He let me make up a couple quizzes I missed for personal reasons. Nice, very nice!

This professor really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. There is almost no homework. With the 2 papers that are due, hes willing to help you make sure they are on the right track before you turn them in for a grade. Really reasonable if you have questions or concerns, just email him. The lectures were really interesting too!

Real straight up class. Lectures have all the info that's on the test, so take diligent notes. Most readings are short. The two longer ones are enjoyable, you fly through them. Professor Easterling is clear in what he requires for the larger assignments. He wants you to ask questions/for clarification, so don't be afraid to reach out!

This class is the best humanities class you can take at BYU. Michael Easterling gives great lectures, and demands just the right amount of work. The 3 test you take aren't bad, there's two big essays that you have to turn in on the class day of class, but otherwise the reading is light and there's virtually no homework. You won't regret this class.

Brother Easterling is a good guy. Has a good class. Genuine with students and super relatable. The only reason I select test heavy is because a large percentage (40-50%) of your grade comes from the 3 tests. However, they're very doable if you attend class. He also let me do a couple make up assignments.
Loved the class. I graduate next year and this was my last GE course. Professor Easterling was really nice and had nice lectures. I just went to class and the test were easy for me.

Professor Easterling gave great lectures, and i learned alot of stuff i really had no idea about before. Fun class. He truly cares about his students and helped me alot. If you need the GE course i advise that you take his class.

10 star review!!! I loved the class. Seriously Professor Easterling is a lot of fun. I definitely could have gotten a better grade but as I am graduating this month I admit to slacking off more than usual - sorry Professor E. But for real people you have to take GE classes, so take one that in entertaining & educational. I learned & had fun.

Loved Professor Easterling. Class was awesome. I learned a ton of awesome stuff about the Humanities and really about society in general. Sorry he class was very straight forward, he is funny, likes to play around, provides plenty of chances for extra credit, and I really enjoyed his lectures. He asks questions and will push back to make us think.

I have honestly never had a professor that cared about his students so much. He is easy to get a hold of and he wants to help his students. I got a B+ but honestly without his help and mercy I'd have gotten maybe a C- if I'm lucky. I had serious personal issues and he went out of his way to help me. Also the classes I was at were awesome. Thank you

Awesome professor. He loved making us think about things. I love how he realted so much of this to us as students. I'm not a humanities guy, but Ioved him and would definitely take his class again. I learned a lot.

just another humanities professor at BYU that thinks they are the first person to play Devil's advocate to BYU students. He doesn't write his own tests, all copied from other professors, and gets lots of information incorrect. When students would point out his mistakes, he'd make up some excuse. He says he's not a hard grader, but don't believe him

Extremely rude to students. Grades very subjectively. Absolutely no guidance on deadlines or guidelines for assignments. There were two really awesome classes during the semester, but mostly class was hard to get through.

Loved Professor Easterling's class. He engages with all of us students. Asks for our input all the time, and I really liked how he would push each of us to think more about our answers by pushing back and not just allowing "primary answers". I am grateful for teachers that make me really think.
I loved his class, his grading is very merciful, and his teaching is quite engaging. If his class has a seat, sign up ASAP!

Professor Easterling was awesome! His lectures were very interesting and I learned so much. He doesnt have us buy the textbook which is so nice and the readings he assigns are short but really cool historical documents that were very interesting. His tests were very fair and come straight from his lectures. He has extra credit opportunities!
Awesome professor, very caring, fun and interesting lectures. Super grateful I took his course!

Prof Easterling really cares and is willing to work with you when you need extra help. He can have a condescending tone when responding to comments but you gotta realize that he doesnt mean it. He is a good guy and wants his student to succeed. If you attend class and take good notes youll get an A. I enjoyed the class. Very reasonable grading.

Found the difficulty level for professor Easterling's class to be right on par with 200 level classes at BYU. Very enjoyable lectures, he doesn't just show us art & to memorize, he dives into the history of the painting, the artist & asks us to share our observations. He is always saying that everyone's point of view matters. Cool guy that cares.

The class was hard but only because I dont really understand art and the humanities and that stuff. As a math major I dreaded taking this class but Easterling was great and made the class fun. Very understanding and will work with you. I missed a couple quizzes and he let me make em up. Lectures are fun, he love to having fun with us.
Easily the best and most interesting GE class I took at BYU. I'd take him again, but I've graduated and am off to work in the real world. Seriously this guy cares and is super nice.

Easterling tests based on what is interesting to him, not what matters, so we memorized his favorite art pieces and other comments he made. His manner is condescending and rude towards any commenters he doesn't agree with. Tests and quizzes are full of trick questions. Easterling promotes communism, which does not align with the values of BYU.

So i didn't get the best grade in the class but probably had something to do with me taking this as my last class to graduate. What I will say is I never liked the Humanities until I took Professor Easterling's class. He showed us some many incredible things! I would recommend!

Professor Easterling is super cool. Very accessible. He cares about his students and was willing to work with me when I needed him. If you can you should definitely take his class. Went over fun stuff in his lectures.

I am a humanities major, so maybe it came easier to me than some others, but the class was great. Simple and easy to follow, we studied a lot of very interesting things. I really enjoyed learning about graphic novels & feminism in his class. Also really enjoyed the group project at the end of their term.

I loved taking Professor Easterling's class. I got an A and he did make me work for it, but he is a real gem. He is more than willing to go above and beyond to help any student get an A in his class as I can attest. Very nice guy. One of the best things he told me is "this is college, what you did in HS was nice but now you have to raise your bar."

So...I have no idea what these people are talking about. Professor Easterling is the bomb. Super cool, good lectures, loves what he teaches & honestly cares about his students. He worked with me so that I wouldn't fall behind when I had to leave town and couldn't be in class. I think so of these sour grapes maybe from dumb students. Take the class!

Honestly I'm baffled his ratings are decent. He is by far the worst professor I've had. He refused to update the grades, tests on material he doesn't cover, requires participation but belittles each student that asks what he considers a 'dumb' question. Terrible with communication and not willing to work with you. Do NOT take this class from him.

I recommend Easterling to everyone. It was an enjoyable class because he only teaches about things he likes. If you go to class and take notes, you'll get an A. Homework is very minimal in this class as well.

I loved this class! I learned so much about the artwork and cultures post-Renaissance and people in general. He is a great guy who is really passionate about the subject matter. NO heavy reading or homework! Just 2 papers and a group project due at the end of the semester. I had so much fun this semester, I'll really miss his class. 11/10 DO IT!!

Prof Easterling is an amazing professor. He is insightful and passionate and keeps it real. The subject is extremely interesting and you will become a more well-rounded individual if you take this class. He doesn't post slides, so the only way to get the notes is by going to class. If you participate and put in the effort, you'll get a good grade.
His lectures are amazing and he makes you want to come to class. There are two essays and little homework, but amazing class! Would take again.

Professor Easterling is one of the best teachers I have had. He is very cultured and has interesting insights on the world. Lectures are compelling and he adds depth to the content. You do get graded on participation and he doesn't post any slides so the only way to get the notes is by coming to class. Tests are not the easiest, but manageable

Easterling is a great lecturer & I learned a ton from his class. Upsides, you don't have to buy the textbook and the material is interesting. Downsides, there were always things on the test that were never covered in class so you had to go to the TA review if you wanted a good grade. Overall, good class to take if you need to get GE credit.

Great professor, great class, would take again. Go to class and its really easy. Nice to have a professor that treats you like adults rather than kids. Seriously awesome lectures. I would absolutely retake a class from him. One of the assigned reasons was Maus (a graphic novel) and that was fun.

He is a very interesting man, but really likes to rant. The tests are extremely difficult if you skip classes and you should probably write down everything he says, even if it seems obscure. If the TA has reviews, GO, that is the only reason I passed the class. He's terrible about grading in a timely manner and a significant score is participation.

Michael is a great professor! The first like three months we had almost no homework! Once the quizzes started you do have to do some readings, but it's not difficult. His lectures are hilarious and I have a great time in his class. Just make sure you go to class, a lot of test questions are based on what he says in class.

Horrible test writer (tests aren't very fair). Goes on rants and tests you on material he didn't cover because of rants. The class is very test and quiz heavy, and he will brag about how consecutive classes have all failed certain quizzes. Currently, only one person is scraping by with an A in my spring class. I'm 6% above the average with a B+.

Professor Easterling is a wonderful teacher! His class can be tough, but the more you do the readings, attend class, and participate the easier it becomes! He give amazing lectures that provides today's real world context to several topics from hundred of years ago, why art matters, and the exploration of the human existence. He is a must take!
Professor Easterling is a good professor. He makes you work for the grade you get. But his classes are fun and students are encouraged to share their thoughts and opinions on the subject at hand.

Tough teacher, but you really do learn a lot. Lots of great class discussions. Don't skip class, the tests are mainly from the lecture. I really enjoyed the material covered and would definitely take a class from Brother Easterling again. He is funny and will crack himself up which is funnier. But most of all he relates with his students.

At first I sold him short, perhaps because this is an intro class. Come to find out, the man was a pro break dancer, owns a big business, and has extensive knowledge about his subject matter. Lot of respect. Class itself was pretty easy. And Easterling, if you're reading this, I did the music prep the night before everytime, and got 100% on each HA
Good teacher. Not the best, but I've had far worse. I would for sure take a class from him again if needed.

Honestly one of my favorite professors so far in my college experience. He understands how it feels to be a student & relates with us empathetically. He enjoys the material and makes it enjoyable and relatable for his students. Not super difficult, do the work, go to class & you will be ready for the tests. Definitely take his class if you can!

Prof Easterling is a very caring guy! His class is a lot of fun. He cares about this topic. I really didn't want to take a Humanities class but needed the GE credit to graduate, but his class was super fun, informative, and would definitely take again!

So here is the thing with Professor Easterling. First off he is awesome and cares about his students. He is kind enough to grant assignment extensions to studemts that ask amd explain why they need it. Also his class is not hard. Want to get an A? Go to class, take notes & participate. He tests off of his lectures for about 90-95% of the test.

Prof Easterling is fun, tough, interactive, enjoyable, caring, and pushes you to be a better student. The class was fun. We covered everything from art to Graffiti, from classical music to rap, ballet to break dancing, philosophy and social issues. We even read part of a graphic novel. I would definitely take anither class from him.

Professor Easterling is a really nice guy. He wants his students to have a good experience in his class. He wants us to have fun but we are also challenged to learn. He helps push his students to excel and will be seen by some as a hard grader because of that. You will cover a lot of interesting things in his class.

Professor Easterling is a good guy, and he really cares about what he teaches. But he is not very organized. His writing assignments were unclear, and he didn't update the syllabus when he updated the assignments- so if you miss the one class where he explains the assignment, you won't be able to do the work.

Prof Easterling is an amazing guy and a great teacher, but he expects way too much out of a 2 credit class. Tests are insanely hard and there's lots of written homework. I learned a lot but I almost drowned in the workload.

Boring lectures--he mostly shows videos and reads off Wikipedia. In addition, his grading criteria is unclear on written assignments, and the syllabus and schedule on Learning Suite don't match each other or what he actually does in class. Take this class if you want a pretty easy but boring class; if you're interested at all in learning, don't.

Teaching in class is quite good, he's good at explaining things. However, the homework and class structure is incredibly vague and makes no sense, and you're going to lose a lot of points because you didn't do things that the assignment didn't tell you to do. Getting a B in this class is not too hard, but getting an A is extremely difficult.

Dr. Goodrich is literally such a dawg, he taught so clearly and was great at ensuring that the students had a decent understanding before moving on. He would dedicate time in class specifically to answer questions and had a very understanding late work policy. He'd also relate stuff to gospel topics in really insightful ways, which was cool.
Professor Goodrich was amazing! Kind, fair, and explained things well. You can tell he puts a lot of effort into making sure his teaching is the best it can be. For sure would take again!
Dr. Goodrich is so awesome. Has the biggest heart and knows what he is talking about too.

One of the best CS professors I have had. Explains concepts very well and allows time in class for students to sit with the material and generate questions. He is also very understanding of the fact that we are students with other classes and things going on, and he works to help us succeed in ways that are still fair to everyone else.

Amazing professor with a huge heart! I love his teaching style, as he truly teaches for understanding rather than to check boxes. He's also very accommodating of student's needs and willing to work with you to help you succeed. Only complaint would be that grading assignments can take a long time, but that's not his fault.

Dr. Goodrich is a good person and a good professor. He does all the possible help to let the students understand the topic. You can access Zoom recordings and many accommodations from him. Also, if you are experiencing something hard, he is the person to talk with. He will listen and think about the solutions with you together.

The class consists of 2 online tests, one Midterm, one Final. (50% of your grade)
The class also has 26 total homework assignments which are alright to complete. (10% of your grade)
The main task is the projects (40% of your grade); there are a total of 5 of them, and each of them are straight monsters. they each take a ton of time as well.

Dr. Goodrich is the most student-centric professor I have ever had. During his lectures, he explains concepts excellently, pausing at times to gauge the understanding of his students and allow for questions. He makes homework and projects exactly as challenging as they need to be for students to learn concepts from them, and not a bit more.

The numbers here don't lie. Don't overthink it- if you have the chance, take from Dr. Goodrich. He is dedicated to his student's success and makes an otherwise difficult course manageable. This is a low risk, high reward professor. Lectures are well worth it.

Super cool professor. Definitely cares about how you do in the class. Did it in python for the fall semester, which was super nice. Worth going to class. He explains the concepts are a lot more clearly than the book does. Would recommend and wish that he taught more of the CS core classes. Terrific professor and terrific person.

Amazing person and professor! However, this class is NOT a walk in the park. The homework and tests are pretty easy, but the 5 big projects are really difficult. As long as you stay on top of those and go to the (super helpful) TAs often, you'll do great.

Dr. Goodrich is incredible, he is a rare type of professor who really helps you learn and develop a passion for the material he is teaching. His assignments are not necessarily easy, but every single one will help you learn the content better, and he is very accommodating and willing to work with you. I really can't recommend him enough

Dr. Goodrich is possibly the best professor I've ever had. He pauses in lecture for us to synthesize questions, and his explanations are easy to comprehend. He is very understanding and reasonable with late points when life gets complicated -- sickness, breakups, mental health. He really wants us to succeed -- I would recommend him to anyone.

If you have to take CS236, take it from Professor Goodrich. He's a very caring professor who does an excellent job at breaking complex concepts down into understandable material. His late policy for projects is also pretty laid back so there's no need to stress big time about missing deadlines. Overall a great professor
Such a good professor. Cares about students a lot, and willing to give help. Very willing to give extra time for homework if you have a valid reason.

Goodrich is deeply concerned about his students, their well-being, and their education. While his classes might not be the easiest, you can rely on him to present the content well and give useful and relevant assignments. Overall one of my favorite professors at BYU so far.

His top priority is that you learn the material, and it's obvious in the way that he conducts his class. It's structured so if you go to most of the classes and do all the homework/projects, there's no way that you won't learn and get a good grade. The projects aren't light, but they are definitely doable. Probably the best teacher I've had at BYU.

If you need to take 236, take it from Dr. Goodrich! He is such an amazing professor and an amazing person in general. He really cares for you and wants to see you succeed, and he works hard to make sure you understand the material taught in the class. Goodrich seriously rocks!

The projects SUCKED but that wasn't his fault, more-so the 236 class as a whole (as those were universal across professors). He was super caring, funny, and explained everything so well. He went so out of his way to adapt for students' needs and I loved his class with all my heart. He's probably my favorite professor so far at BYU too :)))
cares about his students. take his class!!!!!

Professor Goodrich is an amazing teacher. He puts his heart and soul into his lectures and wants you to learn a lot from each class. He will go at the pace of his section and facilitates questions extremeley well. Projects are indeed beefy, so if you procrastinante you will drown and get behind. I love this man.

Goodrich is the most understanding professor I've ever had. He is very cognisant of how the class is catching his teaching and will adapt his lesson plan on the spot to cover difficult concepts. He'll explain things one or two different ways to ensure everyone understands. This class can be a burden, so take it from Goodrich for the extra support.

Professor Goodrich is one of the best teachers I have had at BYU. He genuinely cares and puts in a lot of effort towards class. The TA's are helpful and the subject material is difficult, but Professor Goodrich is a good teacher and a good person.
Fantastic Professor.

Dr. Goodrich is an absolute saint. I took this class in Winter 2021 and it was online, but he was by far the best Zoom lecturer that I have ever had. He always made sure to leave space for people to ask questions. He explains things well. He is also willing to help students who are struggling. The class was pretty hard, but he was great.

Dr. Goodrich is very concerned with his students' success and structures the class in such a way that students can learn the material well and do well in the class. He canceled class a lot, some of that was planned and some of that was due to his circumstances this semester. He always made up for it tho, and we were able to learn all the material.

Best prof I'd had in the CS dept! Cares a ton, wants you to succeed and is willing to work with you. He is super versed in the material so the readings and lectures are often 200% than what you actually need to know for the tests and projects, but that means he's also great at answering questions. Good class

Professor Goodrich is amazing!! It doesn't matter what the class is, if Goodrich is teaching it'll end up your favorite! The class itself began by throwing you into the deep end, but after a while it becomes easy to follow along. Goodrich is funny, understanding, kind, and knows what he's talking about!

Pretty brutal class but I don't think I could've handled it without Goodrich. He was a fantastic lecturer, did a great job of answering questions and anticipating and caring for students during difficult times.

Dr. Goodrich is the most sincere, caring, understanding professor I have ever had at BYU. Its professors like him that make me proud to be here. He is an extremely clear teacher, and is constantly working to ensure that he is providing maximum value. He is incredibly understanding with outside circumstances effecting homework, labs, and test.
Best teacher for the semester. Second time taking this class and by far he made all of the concepts sooo much easier to understand.

Goodrich & Decker are a great duo! I wish this dept had professors like this in every core class for the first half of the CS program. A lot of students fall out of the program b/c they feel like they don't belong. These profs are very conscientious of that and constantly trying to innovate how to make tough material accessible to more students
Such a sweet, caring man. Not too hard of material and a fantastic teacher.

Tests are a cakewalk worth 50% of the final grade. Labs can be difficult, but there's nothing new on the coding side that you haven't seen in 235. The theory is a bit abstract at times, but Dr. Goodrich is good at explaining new concepts in depth (almost to the point of boredom). Great professor, definitely take a class from him if you can.
CS236 wasn't my favorite course but Dr. Goodrich is such a kind man. I wouldn't take the class again, but I would take him again.
He does an incredible job teaching a very complicated topic. He is very meticulous and ensures that every student understands to topic. Overall GREAT professor and class!
He is super nice and its not a hard class. Do the hw, do the projects, the tests are way easy and boom youve got an A

Best online course I've taken! He clearly explains concepts without dragging too much. He's also great at showing how the concepts apply to real life. The projects are difficult, but fascinating! He and the TAs are always available to help out (over Slack and Gather). Difficult yet fascinating class. Goodrich is a solid choice for this course.

This class is SO MUCH WORK. It was one of the hardest CS classes for me. So I didn't get the grade I wanted, but Dr. Goodrich was one of the best professors ever. Always willing to help outside of class, and gave me extra points on multiple labs because my IDE had crazy problems that semester. He really slows down during lectures which was helpful.

Really liked Goodrich, not sure why I struggled with the class so much. I retook it from another professor later on, and the labs were just crazy difficult both times around. He's a professor who does well with a large class, but also cares about the individual, which is great for getting feedback.

Took fall 2019. Great guy. Super funny, makes a hard subject enjoyable. He is significantly easier than the others who teach 236, so definitely shoot for him. He wants to make it doable, and he does. The readings were really hard to understand, but in class he always explained exactly what you need. You could get by without a ton of reading.

I only used the textbook for homework. The only reason I got a C is because I didn't do the last lab. His late policy is super lenient and his lectures are clear and easy to understand. Goodrich is hilarious on accident. It doesn't feel forced. 10/10 would choose him again

Best all around professor I have had at BYU. I had heard nightmares about CS 236 but he made it very easy to do well. Tests were incredibly reasonable, and homework was very minimal. I would recommend that everybody take a class from Dr. Goodrich.
He's awesome! Really likes teaching, and has a great sense of humor. Merciful with late deadlines too.

Amazing lecturer. Very kind. Explains concepts well. Minimal paper homework (just a couple problems to practice the concept, 30 min max). The 5 lab projects obviously take more time, but Goodrich works with the TAs to make the help sessions useful. Lets you take in 8.5 by 11 sheet of paper to tests. DO THE UNIT TESTING FOR THE LABS. Great person!

He is so good at explaining difficult concepts. He uses the whiteboard very well and teaches towards different personality types. For example, he will occasionally pause class to let introverts generate questions and process concepts being taught. I really appreciated this as an introvert.

Prof. Goodrich is like the Bob Ross of the CS program at BYU. His teaching is always fun and enjoyable. The class itself covers some difficult material and programming labs, but he really tries to make the process of designing the labs intuitive and straightforward.

Dr. Goodrich hasn't taught in a while and is a little disorganized right now, but he's getting better at it. He really wants the students to succeed and is willing to change deadlines if it's reasonable to. The class itself is rather straighforward IF you already know discrete math. Coding projects are not bad either.

5 labs that build on top of one another and weekly written HW assignments. Dr. Goodrich is a nice guy, but I felt like his lectures were all over the place. He would talk about his own research and other stuff that didn't relate to the HW. I ended up going to Dr. Barkers section instead and loved it. Wanna pass? Start labs early. Work with TAs.

Prof Goodrich is awesome. CS 236 is less awesome. This class is going to be pretty tough no matter what but Goodrich is the one to take it from. He's clear and works hard to make sure his students understand what he's teaching.
Dr. Goodrich is always prepared for class with lots of examples. Extremely good at explaining hard concepts.

One of the best teachers I have ever had.  He's just a really cool guy.  He cares about people learning and is fair with grades.  He is perceptive to needs of the class and will adjust the class according to those needs.  No complaints, CS 236 is a tough class but I highly recommend Goodrich.

Goodrich really cares about the learning process and will frequently change the schedule to adapt homework/projects.He is great at explaining difficult concepts. If you've got the option between him and another professor, I highly recommend Goodrich.
Great teacher. Great class. Mostly I wanted to give him the chili pepper.
Phenomenal teacher. This is a tough class, but he genuinely cares about our learning. It's a bit theory-heavy, but he really tries to provide reality-grounded examples.

Dr. Goodrich takes special care to ensure that each student understands the material, which is admittedly quite dense. Very difficult class, but you can't go wrong if you do the readings and seek frequent help from Dr. Goodrich. He provides lots of solid examples with each lecture that drastically helped my understanding.

Great teacher, very fair tests, ta's were super helpful, but like any cs class the workload is super heavy. two homeworks a week along with 5 projects. The tests were on the basic concepts and not on defintions and the nitty gritty details, which was super nice. The projects are far more time consuming than 235. Overall the class was amazing.

It's a tough class, don't underestimate the workload... but Dr. Goodrich honestly cares about our learning. He's flexible in the schedule to make sure we learn, rather than simply get all the assignments done.

Very difficult class, but Dr. Goodrich is the best professor I've had in CS. The material is very tough to understand, and it dives a great deal more into notation than we had in 252. Dr. Goodrich is exceptional at explaining hard concepts with great examples.

Hard class overall, if it wasn't for Dr. Goodrich it would be hard to see where you going with all the stuff the whole time. TA's are complete idiots, grade down without even looking at your solution. Wouldn't pass the class if Dr. Goodrich didn't look over my tests to confirm that my solutions were right. Got 20-30% of the whole grade back.

Dr. Goodrich is the best teacher I have ever had. He cares so much about his students. Not just that they do well in the class, but that they do well in life as well. The class was difficult, but he did a wonderful job of explaining hard concepts. The tests were an accurate representation of what we talked about in class.

He is a good guy, but not a good teacher. He encouraged students to learn from the textbook and other students, and gives a little bit help. I think his way of teaching is totally different than other teachers. For me, I don't like the way he teach.
Really cares about you as a student. Does a lot of group work, but it ends up being extremely helpful. He's very good at explaining things clearly.

Best CS teacher I've had at BYU.  Take cs 252 from him -- just make sure you read the book and ask questions in class about what you didn't understand from the reading, and you'll do great.  If you can understand and complete all the homework you'll do great on the tests.

I love, Dr. Goodrich.  He is my favorite CS teacher at BYU.  No joke.  The only students who complain are the ones who don't read the book, or if they do, they don't understand it, and then fail to ask questions in class.  I asked tons of questions and he answered them all.
Covers difficult topics, but teaches them clearly.  Attendance, while not mandatory, is expected, and you will miss out on valuable info if you skip.
The class is a little tough, but you feel like you learned a lot.  He chooses relevant topics to teach and can very effectively explain complex ideas.

Best CS professor I ever had.  The class he taught was quite awhile ago, but I still remember it.  Sure, he makes you turn stuff in at the beginning of class, but he is always prepared for class, is engaging and is fair.

I don't know who is more of a "dong"--someone who demands that homework be turned in at the beginning of class, or someone who disrespects the professor by spending class time doing homework. Dr. Goodrich is the best CS teacher I have had so far. I have never had a professor who cared so much that we understood the material.

Don't rate the teacher bad just because you sucked it up in the class Mr. "Dong". Just change your major. Goodrich is the best CS teacher I've had so far. He is extremely intelligent and adds a lot of vitality to the learning experience. The subject material isn't easy, but he prepares you well and grades fairly. He's a very likable guy.

This is a ridiculously hard class, but Dr. Goodrich teaches it as best as anyone else. He's a great professor who cares about learning and that the students understand the concepts. He grades hard on HW and tests, but fairly. Very willing to answer any questions during and after class/office hours. Take this class from him.

Great teacher. The material was hard but he was able to teach it effectively. Willing to spend more time on difficult parts. Very demanding and a hard grader. You must do perfect to get an A. He really cares about his students and will go the extra mile to help them succeed.

Great professor, he's excellent at teaching concepts in class.  Some people said it was hard to know what would be on his tests, I don't agree though.  Pretty demanding and he expects a lot, but he's entertaining and will teach you the topic.  I'd take him again.

Difficult concepts, but Mike makes it as fun as possible in class with the way he teaches. He is very clear and as the semester ended, he dropped a few classes because the students needed more time on concepts than what was previously allotted.
Tough class but great teacher.  Explains things very well and he is very personable.

Dr. Larson crushed sport psych! It is offered on-line and has a lot of writing assignments, but they are pretty easy and applied, so you feel like you are getting a lot out of them. Two big projects. One where you create a deliberate practice project and one theory of change about things that help athletes change. Would totally take again!

I took Sport Psychology online from Dr. Larson. There are several instructors that provide the videos, so they are interesting and there is good variety. Weekly assignments or quizzes, but they are easy. I learned a lot that I have applied to my own sports and think the mindset shifts and deliberate practice are great. Would totally take again!

I actually took Psych 338 from Dr. Larson (sport psych). I LOVED the course. Lots of cool athlete stories and applications. There are assignments every week, but they are more reflection or application and aren't hard at all. There are a couple of bigger projects, but I thought they were fun and useful. Great and relatively easy class!

Dr. Larson was excellent. I learned a ton in his course and received good feedback throughout. He really cares about the students and has a lot of personal and clinical experiences he shares. Would highly recommend!

I took Psychopathology online from him. It was very smooth. Clear expectations: Read (or listen to) chapters every week, take a reading quiz, watch his video lectures, and participate in discussions. There's one big paper that was quite a challenge &, I felt, graded harshly considering they only gave you 6 pages for a lot of content. Good teacher!

Dr. Larson was one of those teachers that thinks his class is the only class his students take. He easily gave more homework than my other 5 classes combined. He's a nice guy, but he teaches his class at a graduate level. I lost my scholarship because of how tough his class was. His test questions are incredibly ambiguous and difficult to do well.

Professor Larson is a great professor. He knows his stuff and teaches very clearly. His tests are another story though. He will take random sentences in the textbook and then test you on that information. His review guide is useless and so are the TA's because they don't get to see the test. If you need 342 take someone else.

Too much reading and memorizing for this online class. Instead of learning content related to psychology, it was more about knowing the names of 101 things (parrot style). I should have chosen Psyche 343 instead of this one.
This was my favorite class, even though it was online. Good mix of learning types. Lectures were super engaging. Dr. Larson makes it easy to suceed if you try.

I love Dr. Larson!! This was an online class but I still felt so included. He met with me via zoom every time I had a question. He used careful terminology when discussing heavy material. Mental health is a hard topic to cover, but Dr. Larson did it with such professionalism. He has so many interesting stories; I just LOVED this class.

This was one of my favorite classes at BYU. It you are looking for an easy A, this isn't it. But it was the most rewarding class I've taken. The TA's give really helpful feedback and were always available for help. There's also extra credit which is awesome! Great course, highly recommend!

I had a bad experience with my TA, so it is basically under the teachers jurisdiction. Too much reading, and the online class is run at a cut-throat pace, with no room to make-up work. Not a great experience

Idk who is complaining about this class. True, the TAs take themselves way too seriously and knock off a few points during power trips, but the tests are straightforward if you do the SG and watch the videos. Quizzes- just watch the lecture vids and go to end of each chpt. for the answers, thats all the reading I ever did. Seriously, not bad.

This teacher knows his stuff, but he was a chip on his shoulder. I found the class to be structured well, but it has too much content for a 3 credit class. The grading for my paper was not partial, and the load is more suited to a masters level rather than a bachelor's. Avoid this class if possible, no easy rides here for sure.

The class in itself is quite interesting, but the professor rubs me off the wrong way. The paper grading criteria is scrutinized to the max, and the answers to those weekly quiz questions are tricky as heck; meaning that you gotta study your backside off.

This class was hard and it is a lot of memorization. Dr. Larson was super helpful with my accommodations. I also had a wifi glitch during the final and he reopened it so I could take it and pass the class. The class is a lot of work, but it is really interesting. I would take it in person instead of online if you could.

I took this online so I only got to know him through the lecture videos. This class is pretty straightforward. I learned a lot and appreciate the expectations set forth so that I was confident in the grades I would get. You pretty much get out what you put in. Super glad I took this class from this professor and in this format.

In my opinion, a terrible class, and poorly taught. Each week you get a 40-page reading assignment and then a 5-question quiz which can be on any single sentence from the reading. Not only that, but he tests on things that are in the textbook but he doesn't go over in lecture. Also, even though it was on-demand, didn't have until end of finals.
The class was pretty straightforward, so you know what you will get. It is a little tough though, and I found this teacher to be a little arrogant at times. No slacking off here, get ready to read!

I LOVED this class and LOVED Dr. Larson. It was a difficult class--you definitely have to work to get a good grade. However, I probably learned more from this class than any other class. It is structured in a way that is conducive to true learning, not just regurgitating information. He is a psychologist so he gets students and is understanding.

You'll have to put your time into studying for this class, but it's very doable and Dr. Larson is PHENOMENAL. He teaches everything so well, and really cares about his students. 2 tests, 1 paper, and a final. Reading quizzes every week that are 100% doable if you just read the chapter. Amazing class that really teaches everything about the DSM-V.

This class was AMAZING, I loved the content and the professor. Dr. Larson is so kind and willing to work with you. He is very good at responding very quickly and is very happy to work and help you. The class is hard though, study and truly participate to not just know but understand the content and you will do just fine.

I loved Dr. Larson but this class was pretty rough. There is a lot of textbook reading and the quizzes & tests can ask pretty hard questions. Also the TA's are very tough graders and it seemed like they looked for reasons to mark off points. Dr. Larson gives amazing lectures, but this class definitely requires a lot of work.

I took this class online so it may be different for students who take the in-person class, but the structure of the class was reading the textbook with a supplemental video from the professor. Dr. Larson would share real-life examples of what we were learning to help us understand the material and make the class more engaging.

I really enjoyed taking psych 342 from Dr. Larson. He really cares about the subject, and about helping students to learn. His explanations are very clear. His TAs can be annoying graders. They are just really nit picky. They definitely look for reasons to dock you points. They took off 1/4 of a point from a case study I wrote.

This class was challenging, but not impossible. Attendance was mandatory with a reading quiz due at the beginning of each lecture. There wasn't any busy work in the class, as the only grades were quizzes, exams, and the semester paper, though he did offer a little extra credit. It's important to do all the readings and study on your own to do well

Dr. Larson is awesome! He knows his stuff, he's a very dynamic and engaging teacher, he gives fair exams that aren't too difficult, and he is always so positive and kind to everyone! I really enjoyed going to class every day and I learned a lot from taking this course. I would recommend Dr. Larson to anyone!

I put off this class until my last semester because I was worried about it, but Professor Larson was so great! He has set up the class to help students learn the material, even though it is difficult stuff. I ended up loving the material a lot more than I thought I would because of how clear he made it. Definitely would recommend him!

Favorite class at BYU! Dr. Larson is an amazing lecturer, he simplifies difficult concepts and has lots of cool personal stories from his experience as a psychologist. He's engaging and fun to listen to, and he makes sure you really understand the material. One paper that wasn't graded too hard. Two tests that were pretty easy if you paid attention

Dr. Larson is amazing at explaining neurological processes that affect psychological disorders. He has lots of experience that he shares in class. The class itself has lots of material, but I would recommend him for the clear class setup and his great teaching ability. He also welcomes any and all questions.

Love Dr. Larson!! This class was my favorite of the whole semester, and I am not even a psychology major. The extra projects he has you do are super cool, and the lectures are really interesting. Tests are difficult, but totally doable if you put in the time. Dr. Larson is really helpful with any questions.

Larson is entertaining and straightforward. For the chapter on sexual disorders, the class had an open discussion about sex--no awkward metaphors! He gives points back for bad test questions. Work-load is manageable, in-class quizzes, 1 paper, 2 exams, 1 final. You must study hard, but the class is more about learning than memorizing. Loved it!!

Really great to ask very difficult and specific questions to. Clear, fair, and a great lecturer. Out of class experiential learning (about 2 hours per week at mental hospital) required, one 6 page apa paper, 3 tests with class average around 85%.

Larson is a very good teacher, that is, he explains things crystal clear and you learn a ton in this class. Personally, he kind of rubbed me the wrong way and seemed arrogant and disrespectful to students. Expect a lot of work and it's not an easy road if you're looking for an A. Super interesting material though

Abnormal Psych was amazing and Dr. Larson made it interesting --and it was a 3 hour night class. He's kind of a tough cookie but really willing to help you if you need it. Tests were medium-hard but I think they were fair. Lectures were so good. And he's funny, so it lightens the mood. Overall, my favorite class at BYU and a great professor!
He takes difficult subject material and explains it in a way that even a child could understand.  Best teacher I've had at BYU, no question about it.  Take whatever class you can from him!!!

Best professor on campus hands down. He makes the class so fun and so enjoyable (even though it was a 3 hour night class). The tests are so straightforward and not tricky whatsoever. Even more, every test question comes straight from the study guide. TA's are very helpful too. Very fair class.

Great class, great teacher. Quizzes are at the beginning of class and you need to do the reading because some of the questions are pretty detailed. A few papers, it is a little more work than I'd like from a one  credit class but Larson makes lecture so so fun!

I felt like I had more work for this class than some of my 3 credit classes. You have mandatory quizzes at the start of each class from readings, and make sure you read the little specifics cause that is what you're quizzed on. My TA was an APA format king, so he liked to be brutal with that. But, Dr. Larson is a great man.

I wasn't too thrilled to take this class since I'm already farther in the major but this teacher made it interesting. He is funny and engaging. His class isn't too difficult. There are quizzes for each class period based on the readings. There is only the final which he gives a study guide for, 2-3 papers and an assignment. Easy class with him.
Dr. Larson is so so chill.  I had a lot of fun in his class and learned a lot.  He is a great teacher and very passionate about what he does.

Dr. Larson is a great teacher. He has a way of getting you involved in the material you are learning and getting you interested in it. Make sure to get input from TA's on the papers before tunring them in!

Dr. Larson is a fantastic teacher! There is no other professor like him at BYU. He is so spirited and it's obvious he loves his career. He lays out the honest truth about the Psychology field, but shows how great it can be as well. EVERYONE LOVES HIM.

Do not take Psych 304 from any other professor.  The lectures are engaging and not superfluous, his study guides are crystal clear and the tests are extremely fair.  He made me think psychological testing is a really interesting subject.  The TA's were nuts but he changed the grading system to iron out their nuttiness, he is that fair.

Extremely engaging class and professor. I took this class only because I knew the teacher was great, having no prior interest in the subject, but this became my favorite class and motivated me to change my emphasis to Cognitive. He makes the material fun and interesting, and "fact finding" is one of the coolest things I've ever done! Worth the work

Very fun, entertaining professor. Tests were very fair--bad questions are thrown out. His TAs were good, and gave good feedback. You're definitely held to a high standard, but if you go to class and pay attention, you should be fine.

Best professor at BYU. I had no interest in this class prior to taking it. Really understands how students learn best. The tests are the BEST tests you will take at BYU. They are crystal clear and you always know what he's asking, and he shows you the stats after the test. Take your paper to the TAs. Especially the introduction!!
He is a great teacher...one of the best that i have ever seen at BYU

Dr. Larson is easily the best lecturer in the department. His teaching style is very engaging because he is energetic and you can tell he is obviously fascinated by the material. That said, there were three very hard papers and three moderately hard tests. You can't just get by without studying in this class; you really have to know your stuff.
Loved Dr. Larson. He really cares about the students and the learning. He learns everyone's name. I learned a lot from him in this class.

Amazing professor! His teaching skills are incredible. He is very personable. He makes sure students understand the material and used practical examples. I learned a ton in this class and I attribute most of it to Dr. Larson's quality teaching skills.

Teacher is enthusiastic about very boring material.  This makes the class doable.  He is entertaining and uses a lot of neuropsych examples when he teaches. He is a young professor who is trying to get good ratings from students.  He definately earns them.  His is a fabulous teacher and I HIGHLY recommend him.  Very, very energentic.
He's one of the best professors in the department. Definitely take 304 from him. He makes all the material make sense, and his classes are WAY fun.

AmAZING!!  Love this class and the teacher.  He is really fun and can make the most boring material interesting.  He understands how people learn so he applies many different methods to the class so that everyone can learn.  BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE HAD IN A LONG TIME.  TAKE ANY CLASS FROM HIM.  This class would be alot harder with any other professor

I loved this class. He is really easy to listen to the lectures are fun. He really wants you to learn and does everything to make sure you do. The homework is a good amount, not too much, not too little. Plus he's easy to look at.
He's an AWESOME teacher!  He makes lectures really fun and interesting and it's an easy class.  Take 304 from him if you can!

Professor Lavers's class is really good content wise— good tips on writing as well as incredible readings. 

Professor Lavers is really good at helping students with disabilities. If you have a disability or feel like you will otherwise need accommodations, Professor Lavers will be more than willing to help you. Please come to him if you need help.

Prof Lavers is amazing, he does everything he can to help his students succeed. Definitely the easiest univ class from what I've heard. Next to no assignments. Very calm and non-stressful environment. He gives great life advice, loves to talk with students about their goals, and reads super cool stuff in class. Def taking a class from him again!

MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR. Very kind and cares a lot about his students. He gives thorough & helpful feedback. He cares most about his student's education, not grades etc. He is also hilarious and has a contagious passion for literature. I came out of this class in love with Shakespeare. Changed my writing forever. Take a class from him!!!!!

Easiest class I've ever taken in my entire life. All you have to do is go to class. You just email him the grade you think you deserve at the end of the class. Nothing is graded. The final is written on a 3x5 notecard and you just have to write about what you learned in the class.

Michael is amazing! This class changed how I think about writing and makes it much more purposeful. All reading is in class, assignments are well-explained and super manageable. I learned so much and didn't ever feel stressed about the course. Take this class from Michael!

Easiest class I've ever taken! Michael is awesome, we just read the book (mostly in class) and talked about it. There were no assignments the whole semester, our final was writing what we learned in class on an index card. It counted for two of my GEs, take this class!

MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR @ BYU AHHHHH. He gives feedback on your work like none other, makes the mundane fascinating, is brilliant but never @ the expense of you feeling dumb. his teaching environment is very calm & open, and if you listen he makes the most hilarious comments lol. he makes learning about learning not grades :,)


plus brings treats >>

SHUT UP I LOVE THIS GUY. He is the best professor in the world. Class is EASY. I didn't do any of the reading and it didn't really matter. He wants everyone to get a A, he's hilarious, and I teared up a couple times just hearing him talk about how much he loves poetry and literature. He is a precious soul.

Super easy general, but the way Professor Lavers designs it allows you to learn so much! I found that I enjoyed the books we read and learned way more than I thought I would. He wants you to learn about the pieces rather than always be stressed about the grades you get. I recommend this class to anyone. Homework is reading a little every day.

Professor Lavers is such a kind, caring professor. This class has a lot of reading, but almost all grades are completion based so if you do the work its really easy to get an A. His class is very positive and uplifting and a great way to fulfill a GE. I would definitely recommend taking it again.

Seriously the BEST class I have ever taken. Counts for Civ 2 and Letters. Lecture once per week and then a podcast to listen to in replacement of the second lecture. Each lecture begins with an easy reading quiz, no tests. I got a 100 in the class with little effort but Michael made me love books I didn't think I'd love. Favorite professor EVER!!

TAKE THIS CLASS. Covers letters and Civ 2 credits. SO EASY. Michael is so kind and sets up his class so you actually can enjoy reading. Just three projects throughout the semester that are super easy and you do weekly writings about what you read that literally just require any type of response. He's a very lenient grader. He's the best.

Michael is honestly my favorite professor. He cares about each of the students deeply and wants your thoughts. There is a ton of reading, but it is all so worth it. He also had a podcast and that was super fun to participate in. He's profound, deep, kind, and Canadian. Get ready for this class to change your life.

Michael is one of my favorite professors so far! He was super kind and accommodating to me when classes went online/I had a family emergency. He is so passionate about poetry and listening to him gush about it really inspired the class and made us love poetry, too! Gives great feedback and creates a safe environment for open discussion and growth!

I enjoyed Professor Laver's creative writing class. He gave good feedback on all the major writing assignments we did and genuinely seems to care about his students. There was a quiz given at the start of every class, so attendance was basically mandatory. The lectures were sometimes boring even for an english class.
Your grade is literally only the quizzes we take every week and they don't get graded until the very end of the semester so it's hard to know what they expect. Overall the class is easy.

Professor Lavers was my favorite professor at BYU by far. He really wants to help and gives wonderful feedback on writing. There is much to read, but it is definitely manageable and all very important to the class and very entertaining. A seriously life changing class and a passionate professor to match.

Prof. Lavers is one the best, most thoughtful, most inspirational, and most life-changing professors I've ever had. I recommend all my friends, even non-English majors, to take his course. He's very thoughtful and cares about individual students very much. His lectures are always interesting and the workload is more than reasonable!

The professor does a good job at teaching the material. The only problem is the amount of work in this class, which is something I don't know if he controls. If you are an experienced coder, it will be easy. As for me I am not and did not take CS 110 before so I spent hours every week on the homework. One week I spent 17 hours on one project.

He teaches with live coding demos on most assignments and is very flexible/attentive to what the class wants to learn. He teaches different database types and applications with a heavy focus on SQL at the start similar to CS393. Final project is a good resume builder.
You can definitely tell how much he cares about his students. He typically arranges class in a "choose what you want to learn today" format, which sometimes is very helpful, but other times it isn't.
Love his spiritual messages that he includes in class.

This class is helpful in preparing for technical interviews for full-time/internships. You work on LeetCode problems while also making you talk more to your classmates, which is also super valuable and helpful. Reynolds is extremely knowledgeable, experienced, and kind. Would recommend for an easier and valuable cs class, especially to get hired.

Professor Reynolds is alright. I had him for CS452 and while I found his stories from Microsoft interesting, I don't think he's my favorite professor. His class isn't very structured and often times we voted on which material we wanted to cover and which assignments we did or didn't do. He does have a lax late policy though

Amazing professor! You will get what you want out of this class. If you're struggling with coding interviews or leetcode problems, I'd highly recommend. 

He goes out of his way to help his students prepare for the job market. I've never had a professor who helps in this way so well before. 

He's also super smart and teaches very well.

One of the best teachers I had at BYU. Really cares about his students and listens to what they need. Very smart, good at breaking down complicated problems and helping students have their own "Ah Ha!" moments. Approachable, reasonable, I wish I took more classes from him!

Does a great job of explaining tips and tricks for programming interviews, both coding and otherwise. Helpful during class, which usually focuses on student questions about a programming topic. Expect practice problems in class. Attendance isn't necessary if you're comfortable with LeetCode, but still helpful for non-coding feedback.
I enjoyed his effort to make each class fun and engaging. Would take again!

He is so kind and helpful. He does everything in his power to help his students understand coding and is always reminding us to come to office hours. If you're familiar with coding, you don't need to go to lectures, but he always goes over questions people have with the hw and such during class. Also entertaining.

I actually took 452 but it wasn't an option for the listed courses. Is super laid back with the schedule, willing to work with a student who needs extra help (or to be challenged).  Can make for confusion or disorganization but if you communicate with him on any of it he is good about clearing things up or correcting anything that seems unfair
Not too hard for a CS class. Dr. Reynolds did a good job helping us understand difficult concepts and knows that we are all just trying to get a job/internship.

Professor Reynolds really cared about his students. Lectures were very helpful for difficult concepts, but course was structured in such a way that most of the learning was done by programming practice than spoken word.
Brother Reynolds was awesome. Really liked the structure of the course, it was super helpful for technical interview prep. Largely participation based, I would recommend it to everyone

Unless you reach out to him, you don't interact with Professor Stark that much, but he had accessible office hours which was nice. The TA's were extremely helpful and knowledgable, definitely recommend attending their exam reviews they are sooo helpful! Overall it's a lot of memorization but not too hard of a class!

Honestly the worst class i have ever taken. I would never in a million years take from him again. This class made me want to change my major. If this is your only class you're taking, and you have 7 hours per day and are dating a TA, then maybe. Maybe in person would be better?? There is no lecture, just slides and lab terms. It is so messy.

I took anatomy online, and it was so hard. Prof. Stark didn't post any lectures, just some often confusing slides. I mostly learned from the textbook and google. Also exams are in person, unless you get express permission from him to take them online. Tests are SO hard, but a good chunk of your grade is open note quizzes.

This course is very difficult and the only reason you'll survive is by being consistent. Each lesson takes 3-6 hours and there are 2 per week. This class is SO much work. The exams are not too detailed, just attend TA review sessions and review the lab terms. Its a cool class, but everything is taught by the TA videos. Don't ever read the txtbook.

Save yourself the trouble. He never engages with his students, he's so difficult to work with when you have a problem or question. You will be tested on material not in the posted content, if you take this class get really comfortable with using the internet and looking it up.

I was so stressed about this class. The guidelines for the class were very clear. He was awesome! It is a very hard class, but he is willing to schedule meetings to help you understand better. I have taken anatomy at two different colleges with different professors. He was by far the best!

I took this class after failing CELL 220 and I found this to be so much easier! So many study materials are provided to you and the layout was clear and manageable. I recommend learning the material a little each day instead of cramming it all and definitely reserving time to study, but overall I think this is the best you can get for anatomy!
Dr Stark was a great Univ professor! He cared about our success as we began our journey at BYU! Highly recommend!

He does not teach this class. One time we saw him, he said he didn't know all the material but we needed to. Never interacted with students. This is a hard class, but you can do it. Be prepared to study every day for at least an hour. Start the lab terms as soon as the class starts, DO NOT wait until Lesson 5 to start, you will be behind.

I do not know who the professor or the TAs are. I was left completely in the dark for this class and I had no idea how to study, the TAs only reached out to specific students and my assigned TA did nothing to help me. If you can take it online from someone else, I would do that.

I wish I took the in person rather than online anatomy but everything was through the TAs so I don't feel comfortable giving him a higher rating since everything good came from the TAs. I'd recommend taking an in person anatomy compared to online because it is NOT easier

Did not interact with Dr. Stark at all, but the TAs are amazing! Always so helpful, understanding, and hold reviews that help so much for exams. The organization is easy to follow but very time consuming. Learning the material and lab as you go makes exams so much easier. I would recommend this course over in person anatomy to anyone!

Not much interaction with Professor Stark himself, but he and TAs are always willing to help you. If you study both the lecture content and the lab material thoroughly, exams aren't too bad. TA reviews are your best friend. Overall I loved this class, highly recommend.

Online anatomy worked out pretty well for me! As others mentioned, you don't interact with Dr. Stark, it's all the TA's. Canvas was well organized and easy to follow. The TA's this semester were nice though pretty hard to get ahold of and regularly canceled meetings and reviews on Zoom or never started them. But study a lot and you will do fine!

I took this as the online and I HIGHLY RECCOMEND. I normally don't do the best with online classes but this one is a must. They have TA videos for each section which are a big help, and access to the online McGraw Hill textbook is amazing. DO THE APR, it's an online program where you can quiz yourself on all the body parts, I memorized everything!

Most of the interaction in this class comes from the TAs, but they are awesome!! Anatomy is hard and has a ton of material, but if you go into class knowing that and with a mindset to study a TON, you will have plenty of resources to help you get the grade you want. I was so scared to take anatomy, but I ended up loving it!! Such a great class!

As others have said, the TAs run this class. However, it's a good online class with many study resources. Anatomy is a tough class, but the TAs and material make it easy to have all the information you need for the test. One downside to the class is that the only grades are the quizzes and tests, so much sure you study hard.
