Every lesson was just fascinating. MacKay is great. 10/10 recommend.

I had to turn in 16 assignments in the first week of the class. I have never had such a heavy workload here at BYU. I found myself doing more than 8 hours of homework for literally 16 assignments that are worth 4 points each. Each assignment has its own reading on top of plenty of pages each week in the textbook. This class was a joke.

Take this class! I wish every college student had access to this course, it was very eye opening, made me think a lot, but not difficult at all. I wish I hadn't taken it in a Spring term, I'd have loved to have more time to consider the things we discussed in class. 
Only complaints: Doesn't grade till the end, hard to reach outside of class.

This is the first religion class that I have genuinely enjoyed and felt the spirit. He is all about experience-based learning and there weren't any exams. I was able to grow as a person and learn how to be more appreciative and loving toward other religions. I think that it was cool how he would challenge my way of thinking about certain things.

MacKay knows his stuff. It is clear that he is passionate about what he teaches and clearly wants to help others learn as well. The class was not difficult, but I did genuinely learn about other religions. The tests were clear and open notes, as well. He makes expectations obvious and wants students to succeed.

If you wanted to take a World Religions class to distance yourself from the Mormon perspective, don't take this class from him. If you want an easy A and easy homework and no final exam , then take this class from him. Nothing was graded until the very end, but nothing was difficult. Quizlet is your friend.

He talked about other religions in a positive light and taught how all the major religions can be beautiful beliefs with good intent. The homework was always helpful and interesting and was not hard. My only complaint is that he did not grade anything until the last couple weeks of class.

This was the most incredible class I've ever taken, and Prof Mackay is a big part of that in the way he presents super fascinating concepts and leads discussion on them. This class literally changed my outlook on life... participate! Not hard, although some modules took me hours. Incredible teacher, albeit not the easiest to reach outside of class.

Super easy class. Modules to watch before class (can take some time), in class assignments that are easy. Final test questions come from quiz questions. Again, super easy. Additional assignments are also very easy. Overall, I didn't enjoy the structure of the class. Information overload. However, it was easy...I just didn't learn all that much.

Prof MacKay is a good guy and teacher. Occasionally his homework and lectures can bounce around a bit and be a little unorganized. However, all of the content is there and he does a good, fun job teaching it. I think his perspective of other religions is amazing and he is very respectful. A decent amount of time in homework but it isn't hard.

Dr. MacKay does a good job dealing with World Religions. I'm sure that it is hard because sometimes students would say things that were not correct and he would still find a way to be respectful. His class helped me respect other religions. He lets you disagree with him as long as you back up your arguments.

I had some serious setback with health. Dr. MacKay was so helpful. I learned so much in this class. There was a lot of work, but he is so transparent about what he wants from you that you can get an A without jumping through hoops and worrying about deceptive questions.

- If you're looking for an A this is your class, but I can't talk for an in-person experience. We had assignments that were graded on completion and we had a database of questions that he took questions from and that was our final. He does a good job of organizing the class. Only complain is that he is not very accessible.

He kind of disregards doctrine when talking about some principles, and really isn't my favorite person. The same students tend to dominate the online lectures, and they were all very strange. I learned absolutely nothing, but apparently you don't need to learn to get an A. Hated the teacher & Class, but loved how easy it was (maybe 20 min/week)

One of my favorite religion classes. There were interactive lectures do every week that were just completion grades, one assignment about class discussion, and sometimes another assignment during the week. Not much work. There was also just a final, which was super low stress. Definitely recommend taking 351 from him.

My response is for a COVID semester, so it may not be relevant otherwise. Mckay used tech in good ways. His discussions were interesting and spiritual. Test was not too bad, but I worked more than I wanted to in this class. McKay is helpful and flexible.
Robust, but not overly difficult. Very cool class. Don't take if your looking to do any work.

NOT EASY. I learned a lot about other religions in a very positive way. He pushed me to understand them while encouraging me to respect them. It took a lot of time. The assignments were cool. the Emodules were way better than a textbook, but had occasional glitches.
So interesting. Hes thought and kind. Careful about load. Way more than just a world religions class.

Every other class period instead of going to class he posts a video of himself giving the lecture and you watch it and fill out the study guide. It is to your own benefit to fill it out well because he bases test questions off that. There are 5 unit tests that make up 80% of your grade and they ask lots of specific questions which can be tough.

He is very broad and easy when it comes to the lectures and quizzes but on the test he is very specific and asks questions not mentioned in the lectures, the 5 tests of the class are almost 80% of your grade so he does not teach whats on the test. he says he takes the questions from these notes you fill out but that isn't true

he is absolutely amazing ! super respectful, we have amazing discussions in class and he's very flexible when it comes to assignments (which are very little to start with ). I admire his determination to make sure that everything he knows and tells about a religion is correct. i would a hundred percent recommend ( plus you can get a good grade )

Sometime I hated him, and sometimes I loved him. He opened up my eyes to themes and knowledge within the Book of Mormon that changed how I few sacred text. If you are interested in the nitty gritty of the restoration of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, he has the doctrine. He just struggles sharing it in a way that is appealing. Easy A if you care.

To be honest, I am not quite sure what this class was. I read through these reviews before taking his class and was confused and it all made sense when I actually experienced a lecture. He has an interesting way of lecturing in that material does not really make sense. He is super fair, kind and makes it possible for anyone to get an A though.

This class was LITERALLY an answer to prayer. Brother MacKay is so passionate about what he teaches, and I learned SO MUCH about Joseph Smith, the Priesthood and temple covenants. I had a great experience in this class. I took it to learn more about Joseph Smith and it strengthened my testimony in SO MANY WAYS. Completely inspired. 100% recommend.

Easy A, not an overwhelming class. You learn a lot about the early church and Joseph Smith which is both really fascinating and important! Super solid class, I would recommend it to anyone because you learn a lot and its not unnecessarily hard and is low pressure

I honestly feel like this class was not taken seriously by professor Mackay or any of the students in the class. I only took this class to get a religion credit. The class didn't go that much in-depth into the world's religions and I didn't really take much away from the class. However, if you want an easy A this is for you.

Great! He challenges your way to see things and pushes you to analyze principles with critical thinking. If you are used to the "baby boomer" way to learn religion, don't take his class. If you are open to new ideas and really want to learn, go ahead and take it.

I absolutely loved Professor Mackay. This was my first semester at BYU (transfer from UVU) and my testimony has grown significantly. I loved the readings he gave us, right amount of workload for 2 credit class and really enjoyed his lectures. I always looked forward to class. My understanding of Joseph Smith and the temple grew significantly.

Class emphasis is great but inefficient, boring, out of topic, and full of attempts to be funny. Grading starts after the finals follow by hiding the grades tab, final grade is viewed only on transcript. Yeah no tests but no feedback. Great at ignoring/useless replies e-mails. He should be a Sunday teacher, reading is great but class is not.

Dr MacKay provided the most inspirational and spiritual learning atmosphere I've ever experienced in a religion class. You could skip the readings or lectures, as he didn't give any tests. But I found myself doing both the whole semester because HE'S THAT GOOD. He pushes you to be open-minded and is blunt about church history. Just inspirational.
He is awesome. The people who wrote negative reviews took his summer class and didn't do there work. He knows his stuff and honestly is a friend I run into on campus

Whoever doesn't like MacKay is just pissy because he tells doesn't hide church history and says truths about LDS culture that people don't want to hear. Take this class. Easiest A of your life, and his testimony is amazing. He will make you love the prophet Joseph Smith for who he is, because after working on the JS Papers, he is an expert.
Great teacher, I love his lectures. Got on here just because of how good he was.
very inspirational and knows how to teach and have a good time..

By far the best religion professor i have had. Sure he can be very disorganized with the grading, but it was so easy that i never really had to worry about it. There are a few assignments that take 5 min max to complete, and a midterm and final. For the exams, he literally will give the answers in class for his review. Easy A

He is a great guy with a lot of great ideas. If you want an A I would recommend taking good notes. His tests are online but surprisingly hard. They cover content from lecture that you cannot find elsewhere. He does post his slides but they look like a 5 year old made them and don't help much.
Good guy. Not a huge fan of some of his ideas, but he is passionate about the topic

EASIEST 2 credits of my life! We had a reading assignment (which was sometimes long but usually not horrible) for about 70% of the class periods, and each required a VERY short writeup about the reading. Attendance graded. Midterm was all essay but all open book online. This guy is way chill and the lectures and readings were quite fascinating.

Extremely disorganized class. The semester is already over and finals are finished and only 33% of the points are entered into the grade book. Brother MacKay's lectures are disorganized and his tests even more so. Take this class from someone else. Class isn't hard but his lack of direction makes it confusing. It feels like a graded Sunday school.

I believe that Brother MacKay thinks that he has a spot in the Bible because this class is nothing but "the gospel according to MacKay." His lectures are disorganized and his tests are unclear. I personally think that he should have his job taken away because he does not fulfill the objectives and purpose of BYU.
Show up, learn. he will get side tracked with tangent questions, so speak up if you want the answer to the assignment of the day if he doesnt get around to it

Professor MacKay's class was the easiest religion class I've taken so far. Having little to no stress about the assignments or tests made it easier to listen to all the crazy stories he talked about in class. Assignments were short and we took an open book essay test for the midterm, then no final.

Favorite professor in the religion department. His grading is disorganized but if you do the readings and the "essays" (typically a pgh or two) you'll get an A. I could tell Dr. Mackay knows what he's talking about (he worked on the Joseph Smith papers) and he doesn't water things down and approaches difficult topics with nuance and expertise.

He is a nice guy, I didn't like that he said he was open to hearing other opinions even if they contradicted his but then during the term i shared my thoughts openly some which were different than his and he gave me a lower participation grade. He also graded my papers harder and skipped over my hand often in class.
don't do it. trust me.

Personally, I disliked this class. I felt like he used too many words and confusing diagrams to make a simple point which ended up being really confusing and many times I left not knowing what I was supposed to get out of the lectures. It felt disorganized. I don't feel like he answers questions clearly; instead, he goes in circles.

10/10 would recommended. Great class and lecture. All tests are open book/open note/ take at home. Which is great. Missing lecture affects your grade however you dont want to miss a lecture because the class is intriguing.

Please take from Brother MacKay! He is hilarious and such a progressive guy (something I really appreciate in a religious professor). His lectures were so spiritual and truly intellectually enriching, it's not just like Sunday school. Literally, all you have to do to pass is go to class. I cannot recommend him highly enough.

Brother Mackay is a way awesome professor for a religion class. I've taken him for D and C and for church history and he's the man. His midterms are easy, finals sometimes even easier. He gives great lectures and is willing to discuss the hard questions.

Take 225 from Dr. Mackay if at all possible!!! He is super funny but also knows what he's talking about and doesn't shy away from difficult topics. I learned something new and felt the spirit every time that I went to class. This was my favorite class that I have taken at BYU, if you show up and do the group projects then you will get an A.

I have never left a review, but he was the worst religion teacher I've had. He was very disorganized. He won't upload grades until right before the grades are due. When I asked for an explanation of my final grade, he responded with erroneous claims. I questioned his claims but he never responded. I couldn't do anything because grades were final.

Charismatic professor, and even better lecturer. People complain about not posting grades, but if you do the weekly assignments he will more than likely give you a 100% on all of them-- not a big deal. Big midterm, but there's no final. Take the class for interest in the subject b/c the readings are long, but worth the time. I loved the class!

22 reading assignments. One LS midterm. No final. Attendance worth 15%. Grades?? Don't worry, you'll never see them! He could be the most lit lecturer, but he can't carry out the responsibilities of being a professor and seems all around apathetic about teaching, even if he does love the subject matter.

The class was no very well structured, and Dr. Mackay never posted grades. It was impossible to see how we were doing throughout the semester. He says the first class that this will be the easiest class ever taken, but the class is actually demanding for a class. The readings are interesting, but class does not necessarily go with the readings.

If you want an easy class, THIS IS IT. He literally dropped the final... you just gotta go, do the group projects and he will never grade you hard if you're engaging with the material. The class is not really spiritually edifying, mostly comes at it from an academic perspective but super interesting.

Bro. MacKay is funny, and that's about it. He is very knowledgeable and takes an academic approach to the class, but he so heavily emphasizes theory and opinion over doctrine that nothing about this class was spiritually enlightening. Furthermore, he is so terrible at supporting his opinion that there is little intellectually stimulating, either.

Amazing professor! I loved having him teach my Joseph Smith history class. He is so knowledgeable about church history, as he was on the Joseph Smith papers committee. Plus, REL C 341 has been so enjoyable, spiritually enlightening, and EASY with him. We have 1 reading and short paper per class, and an open book midterm and final. Amazing class!

Dr. MacKay is a straight fire ball savage. His unlimited knowledge of teenage mutant turtles is unbelievable. If you attend his class you will surely be shell shocked (no pun intended ;) by his intelligence. I would highly recommend you take this unbelievable course. Go Utes

Lecture based and manageable. I learned more in Dr. MacKay's class than any other class I've taken at BYU. He addressed things I cared about and introduced me to new ideas that I was unaware of before. I have been thinking about his lectures ever since the class.

Dr. MacKay is funny, down-to-Earth, and knowledgeable. Going to class is enjoyable and I learned a lot about church history that I hadn't known before. The tests were slightly difficult because the questions were specific and it took considerable time to prepare and you weren't guaranteed a wonderful grade. He doesn't always cover planned material.
This class wasn't difficult at all, but it taught me a lot!

The people below me must be stupid or something - this guy is perhaps the best religion professor at BYU. There's no reading, no homework (except for 5 "assignments" due at the end of the semester), and the midterm/final are online (he gives you the answers beforehand, plus it's open note). Missed 3 weeks of class and didn't impact my grade at all.
Pay attention in lectures and you'll pass.  He makes it easy but the class is still interesting.

Honestly a gem of a professor, because he doesn't make religion class ridiculously difficult like some professors do. If you do the 5 assignments (deadline date of end of semester), go to class & answer the daily topic's question, you shouldn't have a problem at all getting an A. Can be frustrating to get in contact with, but the TA's are helpful.
Brother MacKay is a really great person, but he should not teach a class at BYU. He is so unorganized and impossible to contact. Seriously take this course from another teacher and save your grade!

Prof. Mackay is a great man and very knowledgeable, but as a teacher I would never recommend. He postponed putting any grades in until after the semester was over and then had lost or messed up some. His grading criteria is unclear and even absent. You may think you understand an assignment and then still not get a good grade. Take at risk of GPA

Dr. Mackay is so amazing! If there was anybody to take a class about Joseph or D&C, he's your man. He is very straightforward about what is expected. He reminded us of the final project several times several weeks before it was due, which shows that he wants everybody to pass. The worst grade he assigns for the final project is a B+.

Brother Mackay was a great teacher. He works with you and if you are willing to try to get a better grade he will let you take stuff over. He always emailed me back immediately. His lectures are boring and really not beneficial. The material is easy to comprehend and you can do it on your own. I highly recommend him if you would like a good grade!

He is extremely knowledgeable about church history and doctrine, but he doesn't expect his students to be. The class is an easy A with just an hour or two of out-of-class work each week. Open book tests were easy. Don't expect to learn much about the D&C. He teaches church history and tells us when the D&C sections fit in. We didn't even read them.

He is very knowledgeable and full of historical information, so if that's your thing then you'll like it. But if you want to actually learn about the D&C, this class isn't for you. He just talks about general Church topics rather than actual D&C material. Felt more like a Sunday School class than a BYU course.

Prof MacKay was amazing! He is the best religion teacher I've ever had. He worked on the Joseph Smith Papers and so he is an expert on early church history. He's passionate about the subject and wants every student to get an A. His lectures were fun and I learned things I never would have anywhere else. This is a must take class for any BYU student

He is by far the greatest professor I've ever had. He has all of the quizzes and tests are online and open book/powerpoint/etc. so you can focus on learning what will help you spiritually instead of every detail of church history. He is incredibly knowledgeable (it will blow your mind) and I PROMISE this class will change your life if you let it.

Dr. MacKay is a religion professor that isn't shy about the "edgy" topics of church doctrine. He isn't going to sugar coat anything. I wouldn't recommend this class for someone whose testimony is easily shaken though. His class is great for people who are not afraid to ask the controversial questions. Dr. MacKay usually has some excellent answers.
If you want an easy seminary like class take someone else. Reasonable workload. Never shy about interesting or hard topics.

Great class from a great professor - a spiritual history course analyzing  the early days of the church, and respectfully addresses many of the crazy stuff of the church from that era (from money-digging to polygamy to temple). Timed open-note tests through Learning Suite and the final project aren't hard either.

He is very passionate, a great guy who loves church history. However, his grading isn't exactly clear. His midterms take too long and they are all essay questions. Yes they are open note take home but the essay questions are vague and include too much information for 300- 500 word essays. I liked him but I would recommend someone else.

Requires several hours of video watching, along with reading, outside of class before lecture, and then expects class time to be a "discussion". This was rarely the case and largely he spent time discussing things that the church had no official stance on. WAY TOO MUCH WORK FOR A RELIGION CLASS.  Recommend taking this class from anyone else.

Don't get me wrong, this class is easy as pie--just a ton of busy work. He seems to have done away with the pop quizzes-just 'assessments' that are really for taking roll. Tests (2) were laughable. Don't take unless you love sensationalistic Mormonism--he loves to spend years on the 'edgy' topics. Also super prideful. Avoid if you value sanity.

Best religion professor at BYU. Doctrinally sound, intellectually engaging, and materially I had never heard before all semester long. I would sit in his lectures every week without the class. I hated the quizzes and tests.

Such a great professor! He's super passionate about the subject and has amazing insights. Probably the best religion teacher I've had. He really wants you to understand the material so all quizzes have been open note and powerpoint, this includes the final and midterm! Seriously take D&C from him.

MacKay was awesome! He knows so much about the Doctrine and Covenants and can explain it in a way that is logical and not an approach known by many. He finds information outside of the book just as important as informantion inside the book. So it makes for a dynamic class. His quizzes and tests are online and not very difficult. I recommend him!

Bro Mackay is super chill. Here's the low down. Class lectures are alright. Small open note/unlimited time quizzes each week, very easy. have to find 3 doctrines in the reading each week. super easy. Midterm is 1 hour timed, open note/open class slides.  Final is unlimited time, open note, open class slides. An alright class overall. VERY EASY A!!!

He knows his stuff and he is incredibly passionate about it. You can use notes and powerpoints on all quizzes and tests and there are no papers for this class. If you take the time to go through slides while taking your tests and quizzes, this class should be real easy. Dr. MacKay is very chill and funny.

Solid course. Dr. Mckay lit up the class every week, tests were all open book, and I felt like I was constantly learning something I hadn't known about. I had already taken the second half of D&C; I now wish I had taken it from Mckay.
Religion professors are generally EFY like, but not Dr. MacKay. I actually felt that my religion course was part of my education.

Brilliant and passionate! His lectures evoked great discussions. However his exams are unorganized and unforgiving since they rely on knowing the most minor of details about church history. (Location of Martin Harris farm ) Find another professor In time he should know how to present the facts he wants his students to know for exams.

Take D&C with this professor ONLY if you really love memorizing tiny, useless details about names and dates. I took D&C with this professor and quickly became unhappy. He largely ignored the actual content of the book, preferring to focus our grades on whether Joseph Smith got to Missouri on April 6 or on April 7. He is very passionate, though.

Awesome professor! His class was not that difficult. He had weekly quizzes and a midterm and final. Everything was open notes. They're timed, but I wouldn't worry about that. I finished the quizzes and tests in about 10 and 30 minutes, respectively. It's more than enough time. The negative comments about him are from lazy students. Take his class!

Dr. MacKay knows everything there is to know about church history and wants you to know it too. Great lectures. He is very helpful and goes out of his way to help his students. One of the best religion teachers I've taken from.

He knows everything about Church history.  His goal is to make sure that you learn.  You have weekly quizzes that are open note and the test questions are taken from the quizzes and are also open note.  If you want to learn more about the Church, take this class.
Dr. MacKay knows more about Church History than anyone I have ever met! His lectures drew me in and he was always willing to help students in the class do better.

He is very knowledgable and the lectures are interesting however, power points are unorganized, quizzes have trick and loaded questions,  we never knew what we got wrong on quizzes, the midterm is extremely hard and is an 80 question test that is timed for only an hour. Only way to do well in class is to visit his office once a week

Great teacher, If he taught other classes I would sign up for every one. Extremely knowledgeable. Keeps the lectures fun and to the point. The tests are out of this world hard. you basically cannot have a life if you want to pass them, but he makes up for it by his style and attitude. great teacher.

This is the first class I have loved at BYU. MacKay kept me wanting more. His test are hard, but he gives you options and gives you the opportunity to learn in the best way possible for you. His TAs give away all the answers, so go to their office hours.

I really didn't think he was as great as alot of other people do. You'll spend 99% of time in class taking notes instead of listening to him lecture because he doesn't post his slides. Additionally, his exams are difficult to study for, even if you have his notes from class you have to know them in such exact detail that its difficult to do well.

I took a research class with Dr. MacKay and it was fantastic! Although this course was demanding he gave me all the tools I needed to do well.  I have taken other classes from him as well and he is a fair grader and always willing to help. Great teacher

An amazing teacher!  He brings up historical topics that makes students think about new ideas. Organized, interesting lectures, tests were fair and he cared about the students.  Overall great teacher.

Dr. MacKay's World Civ class is great! Some of my classmates have been mad, but that is only because BYU students are book burners. If your afraid of open discussions and new ideas you don't belong in college. But if you are ready to learn this is the professor for you!

Very good teacher.  The tests were reasonable, and the writing assignments were actually sort of fun!  The text book was very interesting, but almost totally useless at the end of the day.  The tests were all based 100% on his lectures.  Take notes.  Don't miss class, you lose lots of points if you are not in attendance on certain days.

This class was hard work, but by far the best class I have had a BYU! I have never received such detailed feedback. I have taken 6-7 other history courses and did not learn as much in them as I learned in one class of Dr. MacKay's. Highly recommended
Take this class, he is the best teacher I have ever had. His class was challenging, but awesome.

This class made me think, Dr. MacKay has a way of engaging history in a scholarly and often provocative way without driving you crazy with, for example, the details of obscure towns in China. I was undeclared, but I have now become a history major--after being pushed over the edge because of this class. Take it, work hard and become a change major.

Dr. MacKay shines in small seminar type classes.  Hist 390 (Hist. of Science) was one of the defining experience of my education, and this was largely due to Dr. MacKay's dynamic engagement with the students and with the material.  He does expect you to work hard, but never will you feel that your time is being wasted. Highly recommended.

I took this class during spring term, so it was a bit rushed. Prof McKay is a bit boring most of the time. He tries to be "provocative" and get students to argue with him. He gave us a project where we had to make a podcast, which was a pain! Other than that, easy papers and tests. I got a good grade with little effort, maybe thats just spring term

I found him to be obnoxious and a bit of a narcissist. Also he has a ridiculous grading scale (96 is the cutoff for an A?). If you miss one paper, you're automatically down to a C in the class, but those are pass or fail. To get an A you just need to memorize the answer to 40-80 essay questions.

Interesting lectures, Thinks he is funny (only sometimes), encourage him to tell stories about his time fighting terrorism or his bike. He give you tons to study for the test, but the tests aren't that bad. I am going to take another one of his classes, so I will tell you later if he is good in an upper division.

Most people in the class absolutely loved him. It was clear what you needed to know without going to lectures, but the lectures are the best thing about the course. Eventhough study guides tell you exactly what to study it was very challenging. great class, great teacher.

Whole grade rides on the midterm and test, but it isn't hard because he gives you the answers to all the possible essays. Lectures are interesting but pointless, so don't worry if you miss a lot. People complain about the response papers but if you turn them in on time they're way easy. Just study the possible essays he gives you and you'll do fine

your entire grade comes from the midterm and the final.  for the midterm we had 83 possible essays to prepare for, and you don't know which ones he'll give you.  I filled a blue book.  if you're just looking for a C you'll be ok, but if you're the type that wants all A's find someone else.  also, in order to get an A you need a 96% or higher.

Good teacher. Going to class isn't necessary because he gives you all of the answers to the final and midterm, but his lectures are interesting. Everyone complained about his grading system because response papers hurt you if you don't turn them in but they're easy. Just do them. Take HIST 202 from him for sure.
He was my favorite prof. in the history department. He is fun to listen to and fair in his testing.

TAKE THIS CLASS! Prof MacKay is da bomb. If you don't mind reading and you love exciting lectures and engaging teaching styles, plus someone who interested in your learning, take this class! Remember to talk to him not his TAs, he offers tons of help for struggling students.

I hate history, I hate that I had to take this class, I told Prof MacKay this! He seemed OK with this and helped me get a B+. He was always willing to help, but refused to make it an easy class. Though many students thought his class was to hard for a GE, most felt they got a ton out of the class in the end.

He made me think in ways I have never thought before...very interesting...but very time consuming class...plan on reading everything...and reading crazy hard books (Imagined Communities)...overall though I would recommend this class!
One of the best professors I have had a BYU. He was fun and interesting, but the work in the class was challenging. He was a little disorganized and it was hard to get an A.

After reading the comments my fellow students wrote about Prof. MacKay below I am wondering if we had the same professor! His class wasn't perfect, partly because it was tough, but I enjoyed it-especially his lectures. I got a B- and I am usually a B to B+ student, so I suppose if you want an easy A don't take this course.
Dr. MacKay is really passionate about what he teaches and his class is really easy. Just read the chapters and ask for your quizzes back... the secret to an A.
Passionate about the subject although the lectures seemed almost useless for getting a good grade.  Most of the grade comes from quizzes based on reading the chapters.

Dr. Jones is great. 356 is a fun class that allows you directly to apply what you learn to a project of your choosing. The grading is a little whack, and sometimes a bit ambiguous, but overall it makes sense, and as long as you stay on top of your work, you will be just fine. Great class, great instruction, lots of fun!

Professor Jones was seldom prepared for class and was the worst at explaining anything. He'll never give you 100% on an assignment because his philosophy is "you can always do better." Plan on getting a B if you try your absolute best in his class because you're not perfect and Professor Jones only gives As to perfect people.

356 is a fantastic class. While once a weird unstructured elective, it now assumes you can program and allows you to see the UX process through two projects (mobile & desktop). Dr. Jones is hilarious and has a lot of solid opinions about user experience design. I absolutely loved this class and would definitely take from Jones again.

CS256 is a different kind of CS course. I found the material interesting but the class layout was frustrating. The grading often felt subjective. He's a nice guy and knowledgeable but the class wasn't very well organized. I think he wants to improve it though.

Let's cut to the chase, CS 252 is just a horrible class that all CS majors are forced to take due to the traditions of our fathers. Dr. Jones actually made it bearable. He has a good sense of humor, explains things fairly well, and the exams aren't too hard (the homework is insanely difficult however). Take it from Jones, avoid Ng at all costs!

Honestly, class is fairly uninteresting and Prof. Jones admits it. But he does a great job cutting the busy work and getting to what matters. He'll make it entertaining too. But for the harder concepts the TA's will be your best friends. I highly recommend him for making this dull class managable

Dr. Jones rocks. He takes complicated subjects and makes them very understandable and approachable. He's really funny and chill and an all around great teacher. Class time is well spent, and the projects reinforce the topics you're covering, without making you spend too much time/effort on pointless details. Highly recommended!

I've never had a better teacher in any subject than Dr. Jones. He has the rare gift to treat students like equals and friends, while still maintaining an atmosphere of learning. He will do anything to help his class understand, and is very entertaining during lectures. I will take every class I possibly can from him.
This class is fairly pointless - but Dr. Jones is great! Take 252 from him if you can.

Dr. Jones is one of the best professors I have ever had. What a cool guy. He is very helpful, and very smart. Very willing to meet with you anytime regarding the class material and labs. Take 312 with him, and you will absolutely LOVE IT. Projects weren't hard at all. He pretty much goes through the algorithms in pseudo code in class.

Dr. Jones is the kind of prof you wish taught all your classes. He makes the toughest concepts seem easy without dumbing them down, and has extremely forgiving grading policies. If you don't take his class, you're missing out!

Best professor I have ever had.  The concepts are difficult, yet he presented them in a way that was easy to understand.  Lots of hw and the projects are tough, but once you 'get' the algorithm, it really isn't that hard and not that many lines of code.  He's extremely willing to meet to help out.  Now my fav. class, and I thought I would hate it.
Not only is he easily the best teacher in the CS department, he may be the best teacher I've had at BYU. I'd take a class I'm thoroughly disinterested in just to have him again.

Amen to the previous poster, Dr. Jones IS the best lecturer in the CS department. Very clear, very helpful, very fun to listen to, I haven't had better.  The assignments and homework in this class do take a lot of time (probably too much homework for how many projects there are) but you will learn a lot.  Yes, Dr. Jones for President!

Best teacher in the whole CS dept. 312 is not an easy class, but he teaches it well and, get this, actually assigns a fair amount of homework and projects that correlates with a 3.0 credit hour class!  Vote Mike Jones for dean.

This class was honestly so easy that it felt like a waste of time; attendance was mandatory, but we almost never did anything productive in class. The homework was easy, but you have to buy the expensive textbook to complete it. Overall, not a hard class, but very difficult to want to attend class or do well because there is not much instruction.

Super nice guy!  We talked more about adolescent development than classroom management.  I learned a lot about adolescents but I don't know if I really left the class feeling ready to manage a classroom.  Very homework-light.  Super nice guy, very easy going.

Very easy class, minimal effort to get a good grade. But if you want to learn how to manage a classroom, this isn't the class I would take. Instead, if you want to learn all about the philosophy of adolescence, this is the one. We just listen to his stories as a therapist, and try to make connections to teaching. Not very instructional or useful.

I learned zero helpful info from Dr. Richardson. His stories were long and off topic. Assignments/readings were easy, but did not help me learn actual skills for my future classroom. The only good thing was he brought some students in one day for a panel. Otherwise, it was irrelevant stories from his private therapy practice or from 20+ years ago.
Mike was a great professor! Light workload and good stories! You are expected to grade your participation at the end of the semester. Very accommodating and understanding.
I liked him. He has expertise and I think it will be helpful. I didn't enjoy how much he had us learn from our peers about classroom management, but besides that I liked him and this class.

Professor Richardson was fantastic! His assignments are clear and easy to get all the points for--this really allows you to take your time and learn the information. His focus on adolescent development was enlightening, and he has lots of great experiences that he shares. At times I felt like he rambled but he has lots of good information!

Prof Richardson is amazing. He focuses primarily on adolsencet development, which seems like it wouldn't help classroom management, but it does. His class is very easy, and he is very knowledgeable, kind, and loves his students. He has so much experience in schools and shares many fun stories. He's a wonderful ally to marginalized students.

He makes it so you don't really have to stress about grades and can focus on trying to actually learn. Lectures are really inspiring. He does like to get distracted telling stories, but I felt like the stories helped to illustrate the principles so they made more sense to me and were more memorable. Go to class and participate, and you'll do fine.

One of a kind professor. Reminded me of what it really means to get an education. Learned things from him that are hard to learn in a classroom. Went into the class expecting very little, came out with a whole new perspective on things that will be carried with me as I go onto teach. Definitely a teacher I will always remember.
This class is SO easy, but you learn SO much! Amazing, real life, practical learning. Would highly recommend to anyone wanting to keep a good GPA, and learn a lot.

One of the best professors I have ever had. He is extremely kind, knowledgeable, and interesting. He has an endless supply of life stories that he shares during the lectures to keep students engaged and interested. As a professor of student development, he definitely practices what he preaches. If I could give more than 5 stars, I would.

Nicest guy in the world. Uses amazing stories from his life to illustrate complex theories. Believes in student autonomy. Lectures got a little long at times and he can talk a lot, but you can't help but love him. You'll get out of this class what you put into it.

Dr. Richardson is an awesome guy. I learned a lot about empathy and caring for the students I teach. He had some very insightful stories, but sometimes he talked a lot when I wish we could have participated more

Dr. Richardson believes in having you grade yourself, and whatever grade you think you deserve on an assignment, that's what he gives you. He tends to ramble on in class and goes off on tangents, but he values student input and feels that learning is a shared experience. Very nice professor who definitely brings a unique perspective.

Mike is more interested in what you become as a teacher and person than he is in your scores and homework. He encourages engagement in the class process as well as the content; he let students make choices about how they would fulfill the midterm and final assignments and altered requirements accordingly. He wants students to own their education.

Best class taught by the best professor I've had at BYU. There's simply no way to describe how much of an impact he and his course have had on my life. He teaches through many stories and real-life examples, so it may not be your way of learning. I certainly wouldn't have expected it to work for me, but come with an open mind and it will be filled.

Brother R is the MAN!! He teaches his class with great knowledge. If you have the chance to take him TAKE HIM! Have to write small 1-2 page papers on the reading and how it would affect your teaching style or experience of your life. It was way easy to do. 1 group project and final is NOT in the testing center.

Best class I took this block. I can't explain how much Mike taught me about LIFE. He made what could have been an incredibly boring class OUTSTANDING.  I normally hate listening to professors tell random stories, but Mike's stories aren't random at all. They always have a point, they teach you SO much, and help you remember what you learn.
His class was great! I LEARNED a lot! its not about grades as much as it is about learning and he is a great teacher so everyone learns! i highly recommend this professor.

I wouldn't take professor Shamos class again. It was a very homework heavy class with lots of pointless readings that you will be tested on. I felt like at time some of his questions were a bit condescending and made you feel dumb. Just overall would not take this class again.

This class exceeded my expectations. I really enjoyed the layout- he gave us a broad time frame to complete a few lessons. It was very doable during the summer term and it helped granted me a flexible schedule. He is very understanding and is willing to work with you. I have *actually learned* so much about church history from this class.

There was a LOT to read, and often it felt like busy work. The lectures were a little dry. However, the tests were fair if you did the work and studied a lot. While this may not have been my favorite religion class, I learned a lot and thought the grading and expectations were clear.

Really good guy and leads on some great lectures. He runs a poll at the beginning of class to which topic we would like to hear. The coursework is a lot, but I usually could get through one weeks worth of work in 1.5 hours. Straight forward. Study for exams, but know he is not trying to trick you. It is all in the learning outcomes!!
A ridiculous amount of reading and homework. He'll say an assignment will take an hour but it will take 2.

I am at UVU and took HIST1700 with Shamo. It's my last prereq, and he was my last option for credit because I registered late. Shamo teaches with intent to inform, and wants his students to succeed. I value the class, but it does cause me some stress. Glad I took this specific class for my last prereq.

Bro Shamo is a great teacher and has a very good understanding of the subject. There is a decent amount of reading for this class to get an understanding of the history of the church with reading checks that are not too difficult. Put some effort into the assignments and you are guaranteed an A. Make sure you study for the midterm and final.

A 2 credit religion class at BYU shouldnt be the hardest class you take at BYU. I took it blended during Spring, it was half online and half over Zoom. Tests(2) are just random facts about the apostles and are really hard. Each unit(2perweek) has two long lessons and 3-4 assignments. 2 big projects. Study guides are lists of readings, vague at best

Bro. Shamo was great! You learn a ton about the Living Prophets. His dad worked really closely with Pres. Hinckley and others for a long time, and he sometimes came to class (Zoom) to share fun stories. The readings are top-notch and help you learn a ton. He asks a lot of leading questions, so if that grates on you you'll have to get over it.

Brother Shamo is a spiritual giant. His lectures were very interesting and you can tell that he knows what he is talking about. I took this class during corona and it consisted of weekly homework assignments that didn't take long. We had one test and one final which means you have to study hard for those but I would recommend taking him!!
He is very nice and passionate about the topic. The project at the end of the semester sucks it is so much work but that is in every Foundation of the Restoration class

Bro. Shamo was so cool. Lectures really well. Course was very clear and well laid-out. You felt the Spirit and learned a lot every lecture. The reading assignments were especially enlightening, though I believe they are standardized across the department. Took this class during corona and he adapted well to the online setting.

He is an amazing professor and an amazing guy, but his online class seemed like a lot more work than it needed to be. It was lots and lots of reading, and after you've read your fourth conference talk of the day it starts to all blend together. Regardless, I learned a lot about each of the individual apostles and I enjoyed studying them all.
Gave me help even though I didn't deserve it. Take him if you can!

I loved my class with Brother Shamo! He is very knowledgable, genuine, caring, and helpful. There was a good amount of reading but if you stay on top of it you'll do just fine. There were three exams, five reading quizzes, five homework assignments, and one research paper. Definitely get Brother Shamo if you can!

Asks for a lot of participation, but when you give a comment or ask a question he just says "mmhmm" and moves on with the lecture. Lots of assigned reading not related to the lectures or exams, but you have to read for the pop quizzes. Basically review the power point slides before the exam and you'll pass. Easy class, just not my favorite prof.

Brother Shamo is a fantastic professor. He offered me help outside of class on my final paper, and lent me some really excellent other sources which he owned for my paper. He's very knowledgeable. There were pop-quizzes from time to time, but it wasn't really anything to worry about if you had done your reading.

If you're looking to learn, I would recommend Bro. Shamo! But if you want an easy A, this ain't your class. He'll definitely make you work for it. You have long, intense reading assignments every week and the possibility of being quizzed on them every week. Tests aren't super difficult, but not easy: Anticipate studying 2-4 hours/test for an A

Bro. Shamo is the man. Seriously, best religion class I have taken at BYU. Amazing, well structured and well-researched lectures. LOVES the material. He's hilarious, fair, and really cares about his students. Exams are fair and the assignments aren't unreasonable. Might be too much for some, but I really enjoyed it.

This class was the worst religion class I have ever taken. He doesn't follow the syllabus, he expects you to study material a few days in advance because he might randomly decide to squeeze two days of syllabus material into one class and give you a quiz on it without any warning. He kept us an hour late after class so he could cover random stuff.
Great teacher!  Learned a ton!

I loved taking this class. I took it at the Salt Lake Center and was impressed with his knowledge of the history. He has a history background and wove it in perfectly. I enjoyed every class and felt inspired to be better multiple times. The tests are not "easy" but if you study well you will pass them well. Grading for tests and papers was clear.

A very caring professor. One of the few in the department that made an effort to learn my name even in the big classes. The labs in this class require a significant time commitment, but Dr. Wirthlin does provide good resources to be successful on them. He's a busy research professor managing lots of different things, but fixes errors quickly.

Dr. Wirthlin is a great professor. He teaches very clearly and all of the content is useful. He makes an effort to learn your name and get to know you. He tries to make the tests fair and threw out a bad question once. The labs are time-consuming, but a ton of fun and very practical. I really appreciate how he talked about church things as well.

Professor WIrthlin is a SWEETHEART. He made us bagels on the last days of class, his labs were usually very clear and the TA's were helpful. The HW's were doable and the tests weren't too bad (if a question was dubious he would take it out). He's just genuinely a really nice person. Take his class, you won't regret it!!

Loved Dr. Wirthlin. He spends a lot of time making this class better for students. Tests are difficult, but not impossible. You'll need to show up to class for easy in-class quizzes, though. Very willing to work with students t make sure they succeed in the class. Easily would take classes from him again.

So far, every lab has had typos and mistakes in it. Also, half of his pass off scripts for the labs don't work correctly. Lectures go by so fast that the in-class quizzes make no sense. He's a super nice guy, but he leaves mistakes on homework, labs, and even exams. That speaks volumes about how much preparation he puts into the class.

It seems he isn't able to spend any time on the class and everything is unprepared and filled with errors. He can't get lab grades back to us on time so we're getting docked for the same mistakes several labs in a row, not to mention his grading criteria is incredibly specific and changes lab to lab. Interacting with him was a waste of time

Dr. Wirthlin is a great lecturer and is very passionate about FPGA and digital system design. The homework and lab instructions are super clear, and if you pay the efforts, you will gain a lot out of this class in the end.

Overall a very well designed course. Lab instructions were clear, midterms could be tricky sometimes. Lectures were good except when he had his grad students teach. Homework due at the end of every week, don't wait until the last day to start it or you lose your Friday evenings.

Dr. Wirthlin is a fantastic 320 professor. Why? This is his personal bread and butter work. He knows this stuff well enough that he will not only be able to help answer any class questions, he can also teach you much more if you're interested. Homework, Labs, Tests were all tough, but manageable. There is no reason you couldn't get an A.

Wirthlin does a good job at teaching the material. The class can be hard to stay awake in but that is because of the material and not so much the teacher. He knows his stuff and wants to help you. This is evident by him showing up to the lab every week and checking with every student personally to see if there are any problems.

He is not a very good teacher.  He knows this.  He tries really hard to improve.  I wrote a scathing email once and he asked me to come to his office so he could take notes on each of my complaints and he applied it to lectures that week.  Talk to him about any concerns.  He will listen and help.  Great guy.  He really cares about students.

The class was recently restructured so there is some confusion.  He is also still learning to balance homework and lab load, so you can easily be assigned a load of work all requiring access to the DigiLab

I just LOVED Dr. Weeks! I had her for a hands on research class and loved the experience so much. She was so genuine, it was clear she loved what she did, and she was really good at helping her students not only love the material but understand it. I would recommend taking any class from her! :)

I love Trisha Weeks!! She is so awesome! Take her class! She is so chill but you are expected to work. You can get away with reading the reviews and not the textbook but if you do read, lectures are a lot more engaging. She is a brilliant professor! She's almost like friend, she understands how college life is. Take her! She is leaving BYU soon.

Trisha Weeks is by far one of the best professors at BYU. Her lectures are uplifting and insightful. You can tell she has a strong testimony of the gospel, but also a keen understanding of the scientific findings. You will not regret taking one of her classes!
I enjoyed Cognitive Development with this professor. Trisha is a dedicated teacher and answers students' questions every class period. (The tests are not difficult.) I would take this class again.

Great professor. You have to read every time before class out of a hard textbook, but it's fascinating. She knows her stuff! She is also very spiritual. Love her as a professor, friend, etc. Tests aren't too bad if you study.

One of the best professors I've ever had! Was very respectful and easy to get along with. Read the book, follow the reading guides and show up to class and you should do well.  She knows her stuff and if you put forth at least a little effort,  you'll learn a lot of information about the subject.  Highly recommend taking a class from her.

She really knows her material and wants you to understand concepts more than memorize facts so you can apply them to life. Class discussions were really interesting. She reviews for tests with the class and goes over the exams to give time for questions. Quite a few assignments, but they are pretty easy and helpful to apply concepts.

Trisha is a great teacher! She leads class discussions more than lectures, so that keeps class interesting. There are assignments once every couple of weeks, but you get full credit if you follow the rubric. The tests are based exactly off of the study guides. I never did the reading and just studied a lot for the tests and got an A in the class.

Class lectures are based of the textbook reading guides and are full of really great discussions. The study guides are based of the reading guides and the tests are very straight forward and right of the study guide. 14 assingments, but really easy to do. She drops your lowest test score.  One 5 page research paper with annotated bib.
She is really laid back. good class. She uses a lot of youtube clips and movies to demonstrate her point.

Topic is very interesting. During lecture she asked us first what we liked about the reading and what we wanted to talk about. Only after this would she turn to PPs. In class assignments make class mandatory. She enjoys teaching and helping her students learn. Tests were not bad at all. For the end group project she lets you choose your group.

Her class was highly disorganized, and she seemed unable to fix it. Her TA was overworked because of the lack of her investment in the class. I was really disappointed in this class. I don't write reviews often, but this was so disorganized and the teacher didn't seem super knowledgeable if you asked an expanding question on the material.

She means well; however, she is not a good teacher (she struggles teaching material). Everyone in our class has been confused the whole semester. She struggles giving clear direction and is very disorganized. I would recommend taking this class from someone else if you want to actually want to learn and understand what's going on.

Mindy was super nice and caring. Even though the class was a little disorganized, I still learned a lot and enjoyed the different projects. You have a weekly quiz, but they aren't too bad. There are no midterms or exams, which makes learning less stressful and more meaningful. Classes lived off of participation, but I never said anything and did ok
If you want a pretty easy A then take this class. It is pretty boring and most people did other homework during the class, but you do learn a little bit.

This class wasn't difficult because of the material but because of the lectures/grading criteria. Dr. Brown rambles and is really difficult to follow. There are daily in class activities that feel pointless. Every project felt like she had certain timelines or expectations in her mind that weren't clear to students. Also takes forever to grade.

Wasn't super engaged in class at times, but she is nice and wants class participation. Got a decent grade even though I used the textbook for every quiz with a 10% point docking. Do well on quizzes, take notes for reflections, look ahead at things that are due, set aside time for some volunteer hours...and there are no exams! Just papers

I would not recommend taking 315 from Dr. Brown. Many people described the class as discussion based but in reality it was here talking for an hour. Expectations for where we should be on papers was never clear and she explained in class assignments/ papers poorly. When asked to clarify nothing improves. Nice person but so confusing.

Dr. Brown is kind and cares so much. Easy A: no tests, only 1 project, 1 paper, and weekly (open-book optional) quizzes. Personally, lectures lacked depth, were disorganized, and not engaging. It's clear that she wants meaningful student participation, but most students don't bother taking notes (because no tests) and work on other classes.

Dr. Brown's adolescent development class was awesome! I learned so many great things and lots of great discussions daily which is where most of your learning happens. No tests which is awesome. She is so fun, funny, and truly cares about everyone. The work load is not bad and very doable. Great class and would definitely recommend taking it!

Dr. Brown's infant development class was so great! She is an awesome professor, very knowledgeable, and has lots of research experience. If she doesn't know an answer she will research it and find an answer for you. She is fun and funny and makes class enjoyable. She truly cares about everyone. It is a pretty chill class and you still learn a lot!

I love Dr. Brown! We had one group project and one final paper, but both were very doable! No tests in this class! Class is discussion based - I was engaged in class bc I didn't have to cram study for tests. She is the most caring professor I've ever had. She wants students to succeed and has taught me information I will use for the rest of my life

This class was clear and easy to follow. Dr. Brown is the most caring professor I've ever had and truly wants her student to succeed. NO TESTS in this class!! We had readings to complete before class, a project in the middle of the semester, and a final project. You work on chunks of the final project throughout the semester so it is very doable!

One group presentation, and final paper, no exams. She really cares about her students, I don't know why her ratings are so low on here. She has really good answers to any questions asked, backed by gospel principles, research and lots of personal experience. Take this class from Dr. Brown she is a great professor, knowledgeable and passionate!

I loved this class! There are weekly quizzes that are open book, a couple of projects but no exams. She really adjusts her lectures to follow the way that class is going that day, and allows for lots of interesting discussions. She has really good answers to any questions asked, backed by gospel principles, research and personal experience.

Mindy is so nice and caring, and you can tell she really cares about her students. However, this is one of the most pointless classes I've taken at BYU. She has no lesson plan, her thoughts are so scattered and all over the place. It felt very unorganized every class period, but you have to go in order to get an attendance question for points.

She was very easy in class. Things are graded easily. She gets flustered sometimes but that is it. I don't know why she is rated so low here. She loves her students and wants them to succeed. She does everything she can to help you succeed and learn.

Dr. Brown is caring and did a great job of creating a safe place for her students. She cares. But class was all over the place, and the students taught 70% of it. It felt like a waste of time and that she couldn't answer tough questions nor did she really teach us. Basic recap of freshman human dev. Bummer, because I was so excited for the course.

Mindy is caring and kind! If you have trouble following someone who doesn't have a super clear lesson outline, I'd probably suggest another teacher. However, I loved Mindy's discussion-based teaching style! I was always intrigued. We did quizzes and chapter readings on our own, and Mindy taught other stuff that wasn't in the textbook. No midterms!

She is SO chaotic and hard to follow. She relies completely on class participation to "teach" the class, but she really just wanted to hear our weird life stories. She gave quizzes on material that she had never even mentioned once, and I had to teach myself all about adolescent development on my own. Super frustrating and not worth my time.

Mindy is very excitable, caring and likes her job. I had trouble feeling like she was teaching a preschool class with how energetic she is. What concerned me most was how much of the lecture she prepared (not much) and then how heavily she relied on student presentations to teach the material. I had to learn about Infant Development by myself.

If you have the chance to take a class form Dr. Brown, DO IT! Her lectures are very discussion based and assignments consist of participation points, a couple small assignments, a group presentation, sex ed debate, and one paper. I loved her style of teaching and she used awesome personal examples in her lectures. TAKE HER CLASS!

Professor Brown makes her class extremely hard and it is so difficult to do well on assignments. The rubrics aren't available for most assignments, but then she'll give you a bad grade because you did not follow the rubric. She also failed almost everyone on a ROUGH DRAFT of a huge paper. I have never been graded so harshly on the smallest things.

I love Dr. Brown! She is a new teacher and is super willing to be flexible to meet students' needs. She is so caring and wants us all to succeed. The class itself is fine. One midterm and final (aren't too bad), a couple article reviews, a project (easy), a paper, & a sex education debate. Very doable class. Dr. Brown is a great choice!
I think she might be retireing which is so sad, she is great if you do not care about having to write
it was just kind of boring. she is super sweet but i fell asleep a few times in class. super sweet, but she is into the medieval niche and that is just SO hard to get into. easy grader though

I really like Professor Wilcox, she is cares a lot about her students. She makes you write essays instead of exams which is amazing! She is my go-to English history professor. I definitely recommend her class!

She was wonderful! So knowledgeable on the subject she is teaching. She is so caring and kind and ready to help you in anyway necessary. EXTREMELY fair on grading, I never questioned the grades I received and her policies are so wonderful and fit to students needs.

Professor Wilcox was so sweet & a great teacher! Most of the quiz material is dependent on class discussions about the reading so attending is important, but she is helpful and understanding in the circumstances where you have to miss. The material isn't always the easiest but she is great at making sure everyone gets the help that they need!

Professor Wilcox really cares about her students. She is constantly asking how she can improve as a professor and answers emails pretty quickly. Her lectures are a bit boring but you get used to them and can understand what's going on. She is great and I would definitely recommend taking this class from her.

This is the second class I've taking from Prof. Wilcox. I highly recommend her for ENGL303. She will hold your hand and walk you through the whole process of writing a piece of literary criticism. Attendance is mandatory and, the majority of her lectures are pointless. Class time would be better spent working on papers.

Prof Wilcox is the SWEETEST human ever. I absolutely adored her, even though I absolutely loathe lit classes & had zero interest in the subject matter. She incorporated female writers & authors of color into the curriculum, & was so kind with extensions/help. Even though some classes were boring, she loved us (esp when we laughed at her jokes!)

Wilcox is a great professor. Shes soft spoken and the class seems boring at first, but if you pay attention youll hear how funny she is and how interesting the stories actually are. She is very educated and cares SO MUCH about her students.

Prof Wilcox is a wonderful person; she is caring, accessible, easy to work with, and, most importantly, she is passionate about British Literature! Though I was not super interested in the subject matter, class was always enjoyable and though the material can be a bit dry, the class often flew by. I would highly recommend this class for 291!

Miranda is one of, if not my favorite professor at BYU. She not only is passionate about what she teaches, she genuinely is a kind person who is trying to help students succeed. I have taken 3 of her classes and she has worked with me in and out of class on career planning and writing letters of recommendation. She is AMAZING. Such a good person.

Professor Wilcox was so wonderful! She is actively engaged in helping with the writing process which made this class so much better for me. It was a literary criticism course and I struggled with my thesis at first, but through one on one feedback from her I was able to finish with some really great work. She is very kind and genuinely cares.

The most caring professor that I have ever encountered in my entire college career. If you're looking for a class that will genuinely teach you a lot about Brit Lit in a non-overwhelming way with a teacher who really cares about you, then definitely take this class from Dr. Wilcox. Homework was great and really interesting, and she cares.

I absolutely adored Professor Wilcox! She is so loving and caring. I also loved how much she made class a discussion. I learned a lot in this class, though at times the reading was hefty, I felt that her assignments, papers, and tests were very straightforward.

Loved this class so much! Professor Wilcox's lectures were super interesting and made the reading a lot more accessible. She cares a lot about her students and is there if you need help. Highly recommended if you want to learn a lot about early English literature.

I've taken two classes from Professor Wilcox. She's great! She's soft-spoken so sometimes class isn't the most exciting, but she's a good teacher. She cares about her students and wants to help them succeed. She's very accessible, and gives good feedback on assignments.

This class was great! I learned a lot, and was able to get a lot of help with my writing. Some say her lectures were boring, but that is only the case if you are not engaged in the conversation. She's the best and will help you develop better critical thinking skills.

This is the 2nd time I've had her (I took 291). The survey class had a lot of work, but that's typical . I 1st thought she was a boring, but then I realized she makes jokes all the time if you listen. Taking her for Medieval Lit is the best. You have digital dialog posts for all readings, but they're only graded in your self-participation things.

I absolutely love Professor Wilcox.  She was very accommodating and kind, while still holding a rigorous course.  I felt that her grading was fair and that she always gave us all the information needed in order to do well in the class.

Dr. Wilcox is a very cute and sweet lady, but not the most interesting teacher. The class is manageable as long as you keep up with the readings and study before the two tests. She gives you a week to revise papers after the due date, and is VERY helpful in paper conferences. Not the easiest course, but I enjoyed it.

This class was okay.  I had a hard time learning from Dr. Wilcox because she isn't very assertive or engaging.  I had to engage myself every day, and (as an average college student), sometimes that was difficult.  It's a lot of work, but no more than any of the other survey classes.  She wasn't bad, just a little dry.

I felt like this class was somewhat helpful, but it was extremely boring. We studied the Canterbury Tales, but we only focused on four tales the whole semester. It just got old really quickly. Dr. Wilcox is always ready to give help and is a decent teacher, but it was boring.

Dr. Wilcox is a sweet lady, and her class isn't bad. However, sometimes her classes aren't the most interesting to attend. She knows her stuff, but can be a little boring. She is a stickler for MLA format.

The best English professor that I have had. She is very clear in her expectations and grades fairly. There is a lot of reading but that is to be expected. Her specialty is Old English so that part of the class is especially good. Dr. Wilcox is fantastic!

Mrs Wilcox is very approachable and would love to help you with your paper. She does conferences to with your paper and grades on improvement. Very sweet but she'll rip your papers apart. Welcome to English! Tests are difficult but not impossible. Keep up with your reading (passage recognitions).

I really enjoyed this class! She asks for lots of feedback on what works for students and what doesn't and then she changes the class up a bit every semester to try to fit the students needs better. There were lots of cool activities for class, and the classes are very much class discussion - not lecture. It's not an easy A, but I loved it! :)

Dr. Wilcox is a nice lady, but not a good teacher. She is very passionate about what she does, but that's not always a good thing. She is soft-spoken and it's difficult to take accurate notes. Readings are ok, you have to do a Blackboard assignment for every class. They're not bad, you just have to remember. Tests and papers are pretty ridiculous.

The class is very difficult for no reason at all. Lectures are extremely boring, you have to respond to a prompt for the reading every. Single. Class. Period. The test was very difficult, and her papers are ridiculous prompts and ridiculously graded. She's a sweet little lady, but the class was horrible.

The class is way too hard.  It is also very boring.  She is a kind person, but grades so harshly that you really struggle to get into the class.  There is a ton of reading and 4 papers with responses due on the readings every class.  The mid-term and final take about 2-3 hours and require a lot of study.  Too much work and no reward.

Stay away!  She is a very nice lady, but this is the hardest class I have taken at BYU.  She grades so difficultly that it takes any passion or ambition you might have for writing away.  Plus, the class is very boring.

Dr. Wilcox knows quite a bit about the subject material, and she is willing to help you try to succeed. This class requires a lot of reading, and-I won't lie-she is a tough grader on papers (only 4 at 3-4 pages each, though). Her tests are difficult but definitely not impossible. I'm not sorry I took this class, but it was pretty hard.

I really don't like this class.  It's not very interesting, and she's a very unfair grader.  I would strongly advise against taking it.  A paper written supposedly at the appropriate skill level for a sophomore (of which there are many in the class) receives a C or D.
No Comments

She is amazing. Class always has A LOT of discussion and debate. Mandatory attendance and reading responses. She grades those easy either check or check plus. Her test was exactly what I expected--long, but she all from the reading and class. She has two papers (only 5 pages) which she grades hard. Wonderful! Helpful, funny, wants you to succeed.

Dr. Whiting is THE best, hands down. I would take every class from her if I could. Her lectures are always so engaging, and I always felt excited to participate because what we were learning was very applicable. Lots of reading, but I learned a ton!

The nicest professor at BYU without a doubt. She wants you to succeed, and she'll do whatever she can to help you out. The class is organized well and has really interesting concepts. Pretty simple homework, but you have to stay on top of it. I'd 100% take another class from her or would recommend her to anyone!

Professor Whiting is an incredible and kind professor. I took Ling 110 & Ling 201. She explains concepts clearly, makes plenty of time for in class discussion, and is passionate about continued learning. If you have a question she can't immediately answer in class, she'll come to the next class with a researched answer and gathered thoughts.

Dr. Whiting is easily one of my top favorite professors at BYU. She genuinely cares about her students and wants to help them learn/develop a passion for learning. Her assignments are very practical and well-explained. Since there aren't many assignments in the class, each is worth a lot of points and participation (based on the reading) matters.

Grades super easy. Lots of reading (and the textbook choices weren't my favorite), but very easy to skim. Regular digital dialogues, but easy and short ones. Classes were fun topics and presentation style was very good, but not really new information. Attendance for credit.

Loved this class! This class is very easy to get an A and interesting. All of the assignments are super manageable and actually help you apply what you learn. The grading criteria is very clear and simple. She welcomes and encourages questions and the discussions were interesting. Overall a great class, and I would 1000% recommend her.

I've taken two classes from Professor Whiting, LING 201 and ELANG 522. She has extensive notes and information and is always prompt to research more if she can't answer a question. She outwardly cares more about the students than I've ever experienced. She's a sweet woman with a lion's heart. Take her if you get the chance.

Dr. Whiting is an absolute gem and I loved her discourse analysis class. I'm not usually the kind of student to raise my hand to respond to a question or to give a comment, but the way she runs the class is super open and a safe space of sorts where everyone is sharing excellent answers or ideas.
ELANG 362 - Dr. Whiting is the kindest, most caring professor I've had at BYU. The class was interesting, yet the coursework was very bearable. Highly recommend taking a class from her!

Super interesting! Professor Whiting did a great job soliciting class participation and teaching to a wide variety of linguistics backgrounds. There was one group project (to construct our own conlang), but she was very conscientious and assigned groups by when people were available to meet. Tests were open book, open note, nice and simple.

She's super nice and the assignments are so easy. You have to make a post and comment for each day's reading and then there were two really easy projects and they're easy to get an A on. The midterm and final are also open note and open internet, at least this term. She's really nice and actually a great teacher take her!

If you're debating taking a class from Professor Whiting, DO IT. She has a very interesting style in that she doesn't have any quizzes or exams, but she assigns small papers to engage critical thinking and simple application. I loved this class because she allowed me to write freely about what I had learned instead of assigning pointless tests.

Super easy class for a GE. The assignments are very clear and very easy. I didnt learn anything because I always slept through the zoom classes, but I still ended up with a 99% in the class. Sister Whiting is always available and replies quickly to emails. TAKE THIS CLASS!
I enjoyed this class and what I learned.

This class is one of the best classes I've ever taken. You have to complete 10 smallish papers by the end of the semester and read the textbook. The textbook and homework itself are very fascinating and you will spend 20 minutes or less each week on it. Professor Whiting has a background in Russian and each class is always a good discussion.

Prof. Whiting is fantastic!! Clearly explains each concept and makes class and homework enjoyable. Helpful and accommodating to the individual. Minimal homework, mostly lecture, practically no tests of any kind. Classes are a time for discussion. Expect to write several responses over the course of the semester. Highly Recommend!

She doesn't do any teaching herself and outsources to youtube videos, classmates, and ai. She likes tricky word problems that trip you up and relies on gotchas that have nothing to do with chemistry. The exams are horrendously ambiguous and she seems to confuse even herself when writing them. Her style makes me feel like I'm in middle school again.

This was the worst class I've ever taken. She takes a long time to respond to emails which is frustrating for an online course. The study guides are either missing information or have extra information because the class was designed for a term, not a semester. Don't take this class.

Great class and professor, but it's kind of hard to follow.
