It covers a lot of material with not a lot of time to master it, but Dr. Hopoate-Sitake did the exam reviews herself and they were very helpful! Most of your grade comes from the tests - 4 midterms and a final. She is very kind, as are the TAs. She answers emails and is happy to help.

Nice professor, rough course. Reviews may or may not be posted on Canvas, and there's no real final review just a written study guide that doesn't match the exams. Expect to teach yourself and spend far more time than expected. Very hard for a 101, with lots of busywork. Consider Chem 105 or in person instead.

This class was extremely difficult for an introductory course. She is not a part of any of the content, and every week you have 10+ assignments, and are also supposed to grade other people's work. The exams are very difficult with low averages. If you are looking to take chemistry, do not take it from this professor. Please save yourself.

This class was very heavy for a 100 level class. The homework every week takes a long time and the written assignments were the bane of my existence. The average grade on the first test was like a 50%, perhaps something about the class isn't going well when scores are that low for an introductory course. I would try and take this from someone else.
Super hard to get ahold of and when scheduling meetings with her she never shows. TAs run the whole class. Exam heavy.

Lots of stuff to buy outside of what BYU says before class and it's a lot to do for an online course with written homework and online homework. Tests are either easy or hard in my experience but the TAs are really friendly. Never met or talked with the teacher so no opinion on her. If you want to take chemistry only take this teacher.
She is a great teacher and always willing to work with you. She teaches well and really wants you to learn.
She is super nice and cares about her students but it is definitely a work heavy class.
Great teacher. Lots of work but none of it is super hard so just stay on top of it and you will be fine. She is super helpful and willing to work with you for your grade!

Had for Chem 101. Most of the class wasn't even her own material. The pre-recorded lectures were not her own, and the lectures themselves seemed to be from the late 80s. The subject was hard, and the lack of support throughout the course made it harder. The TAs were the saving grace for the course.

The class is just hard in-general, but online was super tough for me. This professor was not accessible on the canvas course or through email, I had to go through the TA's to get anything resolved with her. The layout of the course is pre-recorded videos (not of Dr. Sitake) and they're okay, TA reviews will save you!

This class was very disorganized. The teacher did not have more than two weeks in advance showing and she would move due dates within a week of things being due. We also had to pay $70+ for a discussion board that was pointless and another online homework format. She also made a discussion due during finals week which I did not think was allowed.

I took just this class during a summer semester. To succeed reach out to the TAs and understand and do the homework. Tests sometimes through out random questions that weren't taught especially the final but show a ton of work and you can get points for it. Overall the class was good because I read these ratings but put in the effort.

The professor is well intentioned but this class is extremely disorganized. None of the lectures were by her and it did not appear that she had gone through the content of the lectures. She also promised to do things but never did. She does give EC, but its random and happens more by accident than purpose. Overall I dont advise taking this class.

This class was so unorganized. Professor Hopoate-Sitake was helpful and accessible outside of class, but I was constantly catching mistakes in the study guides & homeworks when they were posted incorrectly. Confusing layout, not a great online class. So frustrating, especially for a difficult subject. The TA's saved my life and my grade!

I took this class over the summer as an on-demand class and it was all over the place. None of the lectures or videos were from Dr. Sitake herself, and it felt like I was completely learning on my own. The few times I did email her the responses came late and I heard from my friends that they had similar experiences with late or no responses.

I loved Professor Sitake. She was incredibly spiritual and always ended class with a story about herself. I took her night class that ended at 9 PM and you could tell that she was really tired and had trouble teaching sometimes. However, her tests were manageable, and her TAs were AWESOME. She's also very approachable and wants you to succeed!

Dr. Sitake is apparently easier than the other BYU CHEM 285 professor, however, the class is still extremely difficult. The only way I understood what was going on was reading the textbook and attending every TA review session I could. To the future pre-nursing majors taking this class- DO NOT let yourself fall behind in this class. Good luck!

This class was so disorganized and confusing. Professor Sitake would get upset at students for asking questions, and students often corrected her work in class because it was incorrect. The multiple choice tests were difficult. If it were not for the TA's, I would have been completely lost.

I thought Professor Sitake really wanted all her students to succeed. There were times that it was hard to follow her when she was teaching, but honestly you do well in the class and you learn the material you need to.

I would only take her class again because I heard she's easier than the other teacher, but that doesn't mean she's a good teacher. She didn't even understand what she was teaching most of the time and was corrected by students who had read the book or by her TAs. Go to TA reviews. Weekly homework that takes hours and 1/2 of the test is open book.

Professor Sitake means well, but I never understood what was going on in class and I don't think she did either. She did not teach material effectively (or correctly, even), then got frustrated when we asked clarifying questions. I learned everything from the TA's and the textbook, but that often wasn't even good enough. Tests are unpredictable.

Worst professor and class i have ever taken. one time, we hadnt gone over the material for a certain homework assingment and when asked to push the due date back, she got angry and frustrated and just said we were going to have to take the late grade or get more questions wrong.

She has a long way to go. She doesn't understand the material, contradicts herself, super unorganized, will change due dates and how long the exam is open for, and her lectures are not helpful at all but she takes attendance. Maybe it was because I was in her night class, but she was always exhausted and it seemed like she didn't want to be there.

She will not tell you when homework due dates change, and will teach material in class for a solid 20 minutes before realizing she was wrong and has to re do the entire thing. The textbook and the TAs will be your best friend. If you do the work, you'll probably end with a good grade, but you'll hate every minute of it. At least she drops one test.

V disorganized, audio quality on zoom was often terrible making it hard to learn, expect to teach yourself most of what you learn, tests werent too bad. She is sweet but struggles to teach effectively. Rely on TAs. Grading criteria actually makes for a pretty easy A or A- but at the expense of the stress you will have to deal with. Good luck :)

SO UNORGANIZED! Everything about this course and professor is confusing. No one had any idea what was going on and never felt prepared for exams. Taught myself everything, the average in the class was somehow an A-, but you are often left wondering what the crap is going on!?

Professor Sitake is the worst professor I have ever had. She seems like a nice lady but she doesn't understand the curriculum and would have to ask the TA's or us for help, or she would just randomly skip to another subject to cover up her mistake. Don't take a class from her unless you absolutely have to.

Professor Sitake was an extremely confusing Professor. She was constantly contradicting her own words and teaching opposite of what the textbook said, she would teach something wrong and never correct it, ask the TA's or the class if they knew how to do stuff because "she forgot." Her MC tests were so hard & unfair. Overall the class was a disaster

Sitake comes to class and it is just a mess, her TA's have to correct her constantly. She gets frustrated when people ask clarifying questions. You think you have studied by reading the textbook and such but that doesn't help much for the tests. She just is all over the place and confused when teaching. She's nice but her teaching is unprofessional

Dr. Hope was awesome! I had to miss a week of classes and she could not have been more accommodating. She made me want to learn about bio-chem! Tests aren't too hard if you know what you're doing. Highly recommend!!!

Professor Belknap is the best teacher I've ever had. He pushes you to do your best, challenges your abilities, and inspires you to excel. Work hard, ask questions, and apply what he teaches and you will succeed.

Monte is an amazing teacher! He really pushes his students to be the best they can be and helps them in any way he can. I rated him as a hard teacher because he wants his students to work, but he makes music fun and worthwhile.
Excellent performer, great teacher.  Teaches well how to be organized.  I would prefer more "playing" instead of "talking", though.
Prof. Belknap is a great teacher with a funny sense of humor (once you get to know him)

She is wonderful. I took the class Fall 25 and I'm surprised at the negative ratings. She has clear rubrics and gave examples in class of what we were supposed to turn in, unlike other jr. core professors. Pay attention in class and actually learn the material yourself instead of using AI, you'll be just fine. TAs and seniors can also help so much!

Although nice, Bale made it very hard to succeed in the course. Giving little to no instruction's for major projects and deadlines, which made it hard to receive a decent grade. Even when following the rubric and going above and beyond, a mediocre grade was received. Her rubrics are no help.

Bale is a super nice person. However, her class is hard to navigate due to the lack of in depth teaching and vague rubrics, making grading harsh. The material is hard as to be expected in the Jr. Core. However, hard material in combination with little to no course structure, makes this class very hard to navigate even for students who perform well

Very kind and knowledgeable, but struggled to teach advanced material. Instructions and grading criteria were unclear, and the class felt underprepared for major projects. Not what I would expect from a 400-level course.

In my opinion, this class has the hardest material in all of the Marketing Junior core, but man, Bale is a rockstar at teaching it! She cares so deeply about the class, and you can tell she loves what she does! She takes time to consider how every class is feeling about concepts and adjusts her schedule accordingly. She's great, I loved it!!

I love her! The course material is hard, but it's a jr core so it's to be expected. She handles tough material so well and is always willing to help. She doesn't give an easy A, but if you do your homework, pay attention in class, and don't use AI on every assignment, you'll be totally fine. She's such an awesome individual!

Professor Bale is an amazing teacher of content that cares so much about her students. I was a student from her first year, and I had teammates that better understood the content, but I loved how spiritual she was. I could always go to her for anything, and she was so approachable. She knew we struggled with the content and tried to help us always.

I can confidently say that the skills I learned in Bale's class were the reason I secured a full time offer from my internship. Bale's class material is really not that hard, if you put in the time and effort to prepare and pay attention to the lectures in class. You work a lot in groups which can be tough if everyone does not pull their weight.

I love Dr.Bale! I now work for her and her husband as a research assitant. This woman really cares for her students and is so willing to work with you on anything you need help with! Also the ratings that are negative are wrong! She really cares and she actually helped me get my fulltime postion at NielsenIQ. Loved the class and loved her.

Dr. Bale was so incredibly sweet and caring. The class material is tough, there is no debating that, but she does an amazing job trying to meet students where they are at so they understand it. She gets a bad rap due to the rough stat content she has to deal with, but she is a great professor and a better person. Just have to put in effort.
Was an amazing professor. He taught me everything I need to know and would definitely recommend

Not the most memorable class, but it wasn't bad. Professor Cummings is funny and direct. He provides plenty of opportunity to succeed in the class. The material is difficult, so studying is critical, but the majority of the class ends with an A.

Class was relatively easy, the assignments weren't too difficult. Class was mandatory once a week, but very fair grading and drops a good amount of assignments. Show up to the midterm and final review in class - he goes over most of the questions and all the topics you need to study. Easiest 3.0 credit class I have taken.
Bad test questions.

Professor Cummings is great, like he is actually the GOAT, super funny and kind. The class is very straightforward, if you attend class, especially on exam review days, and pay attention, you should do well. If you study your notes on exam review days well, and listen to his suggestions for the participation questions, you will do SUPER WELL.

This is the first rate my professor review i've given been professor Cummings is such a goat i had to leave a review. He is smart, kind, and just overall a great guy. The class is easy, if you go to class you will get an A. Honestly couldn't recommend this enough.

Morgan is a great teacher and a good guy. I read reviews from ratemyprof before taking his class and everyone said it was easy. Thinking this i didnt study very hard for the tests and I bombed 2 tests. This left me with a B+. He "tells" you what is going to be on the test. I would recommend writing every single word down he says and studying hard

For Buisness law: Cummings is my favorite teacher at Byu, his lectures where useful and straight quality. He had very interesting stories, and great readings that where useful. Cummings is very respectful of student time and very efficient in teaching well without lots of time wastful busy work. I would highly recommend this teacher.

HOLY boring! But I was required to take this class, and I recommend him for the professor. He pretty much tells you on the days of the test reviews what will be on the test exactly. I didn't really do the readings and I got by just fine. Honestly, class isn't necessary besides the day of the test review.
He's great

Very manageable workload. Difficult exams, but he conducts very extensive reviews so if you pay attention it's easy to get an 80. Lots of videos and readings to do, but it took me probably a few hours a week. You do need to go to lecture once a week for part of your assignments.

I don't know why so many students are ripping on him when he's been AMAZING! He literally tells us 80% of what's going to be on the test WITH the answers + there is a curve so you're guaranteed an A- or above. People who got less either didn't do the HW or really didn't try. It's honestly an interesting but crazy low effort class.

He's a chill guy but the TA's are HORRIBLE!! You don't get partial credit for "A&Rs." Sometimes the lessons are really long. He does have good review sessions before tests but he talks fast and tests are difficult. If it wasn't for the TA's, this class would be enjoyable.

Do not take this class in person. He curves the online class 15% more than the in person class. The tests are law trivia and somehow it is a difficult class but you learn nothing at the same time. No idea why it is a required class. Made me want to rip my hair out because it is so annoying

Low level judge with literally no knowledge of how law actually works. Memorize his wrong answers and don't ask questions. If you like professors who mumble and write poorly worded exam questions, you'll love this guy

Prof Cummings is SO GOOD!!! His review sessions are a MUST and a LIFESAVER. He makes it super clear what is tested and what is not. He is a practicing judge in Utah and offers such cool real-life insight into so many cases!! Such a blessing to have the opportunity to be taught by him. The class is easy, and he is super cool. Take it with him!!!

This class was super easy! A couple of online videos and minimal homework each week. Before each test, he has a exam review where he straight up gives you the exam questions and tells you exactly what to study. Classes were fun and he gave you hypothetical court cases. Each week he gives you a question to answer, so make sure to attend class.

It is an easy 3 credits. Professor Cummings is awesome and straight up goes over the exam questions and tells you what you need to know for the exam. If he doesn't mention it in the exam review it wont be on the exam. That being said I still scored between 82-88% but ended with an A-. Go to classes for the A/R questions and they're easy. Good Luck!

Cummings is a good guy and his class highlight is doing a great job at preparing his students for exams. Nevertheless, beware of "A&R" assignments. These assignments are critical thinking questions given at the end of each class period disguised as an attendance grade but he (and his TA's) grade them quite harshly. Dropped me from an A to a B.

Cummings is a funny guy. Class was mostly online learning with some kinda boring videos, but I think Cummings makes law as fun as it can be. He is very helpful with providing an outline for what we need to know and study for tests, which I appreciated the most. If you need or want to take this class, Cummings is the guy.

Great Professor would highly recommend! Morgan answered questions and clearly outlined the course, you learn a ton and everything is set up to make the most of your time. Morgan also uses public articles and podcasts instead of an expensive textbooks

I wasn't sure if this class was going to be hard or not and it turned out to be so easy! Weekly workload isn't a lot and you just hop on zoom once a week. He is a super cool and kind person who you can tell really cares about the class. No textbook required. Definitely take it from him!
Professor Cummings was great. Took this class online this summer. It moved quickly but was doable. Gives study guides for the exams and tells you exactly what's on every exam. Would highly recommend.

Professor Cummings was absolutely amazing. He's a super nice person, and the class sets you up for success. There are a lot of assignments that you can use to buffer your grade, and then Prof Cummings does midterm/final reviews before every exam that tells you what you need to study. He also clearly knows his stuff and explains it well.

Awesome Professor! It was a great online course that only met once a week and didn't require a ton of homework. There was some reading but the most important material is from his lectures and weekly videos. Also, for his test reviews, he literally goes over half the test questions. He wants everyone to succeed. Great online, chill course!

Professor Cummings is an awesome professor that cares about his students. His lectures emphasize real life scenarios which makes it easier to understand the concepts. He explains things clearly and inspires students to be the best version of themselves. Take this class with him!

Phenomenal professor! I cannot say enough good things about Morgan. The class was not difficult but you still learned a ton! He has assignments that can only be completed if you come to class, so make sure to be there every class.

Prof Cummings is great. He formerly worked as a lawyer and is now a judge, so he knows his stuff and is constantly giving examples that are based on real life situations. The class itself isn't too hard if you do the readings and show up, but it's a blended class so sometimes it's hard to stay motivated on keeping up to date.

Super easy class. The lectures were interesting, but you honestly don't need to pay attention. He does a study review where he tells you exactly what to study for each test, which made it a lot easier to study.

Professor Cummings made his course enjoyable through his dry humor and interesting examples. I felt that the material was a great overview of business law concepts. Although the course material is subjective in the real world, he made it very clear to the class what we needed to know to succeed in his class. Also doesn't require a textbook.
I wouldn't take this class from anybody else if you have the ability to do that! I wish he taught more classes honestly

Professor Cummings is awesome. He explains the topics really well and cares about students. He does a thorough study review before every exam and it is very helpful. Do the homework and pay attention in class and you'll get an A or A-. Highly recommended!
If you have the option to take this class for your major, do it. He makes it a piece of cake and you still learn a lot.

Nice guy. Would always make self-effacing jokes at the beginning of class. Cared about us doing well. Fairly easy class. He basically gives all the answers to the test in the lecture before. The rest is just light reading and a few quizzes. I enjoyed the class and would recommend taking it. Solid teacher for ACC 241.

Solid professor. The best part\ of the class is when he offered real or fake court cases and then asked you to talk with a partner to determine what you think would have been ruled. I liked the layout of the class. Great guy. Would take from again.

I absolutely loved Professor Cummings and learned so much in his class. This class is doable, just DO NOT get behind. The assignments and quizzes take lots of time. Loved the on-demand setting though and working through canvas. My only negative feedback is the TA's grade everything and it's SUPER annoying. And they were tough graders.

Professor Cummings is great. Definitely take ACC 241 from him. As long as you watch the videos from each section and take super good notes during his review lectures before tests you will get an A. He teaches things very simply and gives good examples of each topic so that they are easy to understand. This was one of my favorite classes.
Great professor and a great class. I learned a lot without ever being stressed by this class. Prof. Cummings is a very experienced lawyer and does a great job teaching an intro to business law.

I am taking this class on zoom during the spring semester. I enjoy our lectures and the homework and exams are not bad at all. This is probably one of my favorite accounting classes. The semester isn't even over yet and I know that I am going to get an A. Take this class with Professor Cummings!!

Professor Cummings is super clear and his reviews were very similar to the tests. Attend the reviews. The readings weren't always super helpful but the videos he posted were great. Class is more of an application of what you learned. Great class and a great professor.

Prof. Cummings does an amazing job with this course. Historically, I had heard that bus. law was one of the harder, more dry reqs in the business school. But not with Prof. Cummings. Everything is so straightforward. Grading criteria is clear, he preps you extremely well for tests, and you're not given assignments that take up unreasonable time.

It was a really straightforward class, and the exam reviews were super helpful. The homework was always a little different (discussion board, quiz, research a current event, etc.). The exams weren't terrible, and his study guides are incredible. Use them during the exam review to take notes because he goes through every bullet point. Great class!

The assignments and exams are fair. The study guides are accurate, and his exam reviews are incredibly helpful. The videos are really informational and clear, and I like how he makes the material relatable. He is really responsive to the chat in Zoom and just a good guy. I really enjoyed the class and never felt like the grading was unfair.

Professor Cummings is great! The class is straightforward and he does exam reviews that practically tell you everything you need to know for the test. He drops quite a few assignments, so I never felt stressed. Easy A! He has awesome videos that explain the material in a simple way. Study for the exams and you'll get an A.

This guy is a chill professor who truly wants you to succeed. He's open to suggestion on what topics you actually want to learn. I didn't mind his voice I thought that was a weird way to judge him in the previous ratings. Experienced professor that will give you a good experience.

He admits that he is monotone, but is actually pretty funny. There is a lot of unnecessary information that is presented in the lectures. During the review classes he does a great job of narrowing down the content to only the essential things.

The course was entirely based on quizzes and tests which often didn't match the in-class material. The class was okay for checking off a box but I wouldn't recommend it for someone who actually wants to learn more about law.

Yes, his voice is monotone. Law is dry at times, but class was all right.  10+ online quizzes, 3 midterms (drops one of them), and 1 final. Textbook reading is essential.  Test questions were often based on application of law, which class, unfortunately, often was not. I would've changed that. Class average curved to B+, though.
Get's a bad rap for his slightly monotone voice but the lectures are very interesting and concise.

Professor Cummings is not a great professor.  Take this class from someone else if at all possible.  He is not a good teacher, and his tests are super hard. The class average on the first test was 71%.  The highest score was 91%. Test questions are confusing and not clear.  He is super boring too.

She is wonderful. I took the class Fall 25 and I'm surprised at the negative ratings. She has clear rubrics and gave examples in class of what we were supposed to turn in, unlike other jr. core professors. Pay attention in class and actually learn the material yourself instead of using AI, you'll be just fine. TAs and seniors can also help so much!

Although nice, Bale made it very hard to succeed in the course. Giving little to no instruction's for major projects and deadlines, which made it hard to receive a decent grade. Even when following the rubric and going above and beyond, a mediocre grade was received. Her rubrics are no help.

Bale is a super nice person. However, her class is hard to navigate due to the lack of in depth teaching and vague rubrics, making grading harsh. The material is hard as to be expected in the Jr. Core. However, hard material in combination with little to no course structure, makes this class very hard to navigate even for students who perform well

Very kind and knowledgeable, but struggled to teach advanced material. Instructions and grading criteria were unclear, and the class felt underprepared for major projects. Not what I would expect from a 400-level course.

In my opinion, this class has the hardest material in all of the Marketing Junior core, but man, Bale is a rockstar at teaching it! She cares so deeply about the class, and you can tell she loves what she does! She takes time to consider how every class is feeling about concepts and adjusts her schedule accordingly. She's great, I loved it!!

I love her! The course material is hard, but it's a jr core so it's to be expected. She handles tough material so well and is always willing to help. She doesn't give an easy A, but if you do your homework, pay attention in class, and don't use AI on every assignment, you'll be totally fine. She's such an awesome individual!

Professor Bale is an amazing teacher of content that cares so much about her students. I was a student from her first year, and I had teammates that better understood the content, but I loved how spiritual she was. I could always go to her for anything, and she was so approachable. She knew we struggled with the content and tried to help us always.

I can confidently say that the skills I learned in Bale's class were the reason I secured a full time offer from my internship. Bale's class material is really not that hard, if you put in the time and effort to prepare and pay attention to the lectures in class. You work a lot in groups which can be tough if everyone does not pull their weight.

I love Dr.Bale! I now work for her and her husband as a research assitant. This woman really cares for her students and is so willing to work with you on anything you need help with! Also the ratings that are negative are wrong! She really cares and she actually helped me get my fulltime postion at NielsenIQ. Loved the class and loved her.

Dr. Bale was so incredibly sweet and caring. The class material is tough, there is no debating that, but she does an amazing job trying to meet students where they are at so they understand it. She gets a bad rap due to the rough stat content she has to deal with, but she is a great professor and a better person. Just have to put in effort.

Dr. Argyle is nice, caring and decent at explaining things. If you struggle with 8am classes, this will be a hard semester for you. The final was unexpectedly hard, but everything else was pretty easy. He doesn't love hearing that this class has a lot of busy work, but that's kind of what it is.

Dr. Argyle is a great teacher, and for 311 it's clear his focus is on understanding and life application rather than creating a rigorous course. He hands out a ridiculous amount of printed material, so this can be hard to organize. Homework is fairly easy and usually only 3-4 hours a week; almost never on weekends.

Dr Argyle is very passionate about receiving a real education. He wants you to really learn stuff from his class, not just go through for the grade. However, a lot of the stuff we did really felt like busy work. Toward the end of the semester the workload got a little excessive. But throughout the rest is was very easy, so I guess it balances out

Dr. Argyle is a great professor to take a class from. He's always willing to help you if you're struggling. There are quizzes at the beginning of every class period that test you on the reading, so make sure to be on time. If you're allowed a notes sheet for exams, put unit conversions on there. They're needed for the problems and he forgets them.

Dr. Argyle is a great professor. He explains challenging subjects well, and cares about the success of his students. He is very fair and is pretty accepting of late assignments, etc. Tests are straightforward. He has daily quizzes, so being to class on time is a must, but he gives out lots of extra credit on the quizzes in case you miss some.

Really listens to and cares about his students. Tests were not too hard, he lets you use cheat sheets. Homeworks feel a lot like busy work, but at least they usually didn't take too long. He is a funny guy and the class is actually fairly interesting and really important for the Chem E field. Quizzes at the beginning of every class for credit.

What a guy. Morris Argyle is the actual bomb dot com. If you can get him, TAKE HIM. This man knows how to teach. Learned a ton without the stress of a normal class. Easy A, very fun, laid back class. Cool guy, respects his students, and loves what he does.
Dr. Argyle's class is extremely easy yet very helpful for Chemical Engineers in the industry. He is very enthusiastic about BYU sports and really funny.

Super easy teacher. Tests were all open notes, and he gives you the notes. You are set up in teams and do projects together. You need to show up, especially for the team projects, but honestly it was the EASIEST CLASS I HAVE TAKEN AT BYU. Super nice guy too. He wants you to learn, and he wants it to be fun. You get candy and prizes.

Brother Argyle is a great professor. He is funny, spiritual, and he cares about his students. He really does his best to teach leadership attributes. Tests are open notes. There are several group assignments throughout the semester for students to have a chance to practice being a leader. He does not make the class harder than necessary.

Argyle is a great professor! He teaches based on the students' learning styles, he is very kind and patient with his students, and he has a lot of knowledge! Loved his class and learned so much about leadership.
Very reasonable about grading. Class time was relevant. I would take another class from him.

Dr. Christensen is friendly and has great lectures. I would definitely take it from him, however that won't change the fact that the hw is VERY time-intensive, and back-heavy. The last 8 weeks we had one 10-15hr project due every other week ON TOP of the already long hw. I get that it's to build up skills, but it was a lot and TA grading was picky.

I love Professor Christensen! More work than I was expecting it to be, but overall the homeworks and projects were pretty fun especially once you get used to solidworks. The one challenge I had was that the TAs are pretty picky in grading and often dock you for minor things and arbitrary "cool points." It also seemed inconsistent from TA to TA.

He was experience in the industry and provides a unique perspective on the topic. Good teacher, lectures were enjoyable. That most problematic part of this class is the grading system. Large staff of TAs who grade homework and projects and often contradict each other. Lack of consistency in the grading process was very frustrating.

Dr. Christensen teaches the material well. The homework projects are straightforward but they have a tendency to take WAY longer than expected. I imagine that is just the nature of a CAD class though. The expectations are clear and if you are thorough, you'll get the grade you want.

Great, very applicable material taught in an understandable way. Personable and approachable, you will spend lots of time on group projects, and the homework isn't difficult, just pretty time intensive.

Professor Christensen was great. I took this during a COVID-19 year, so it was like a hybrid course. The lectures have little to do with the homework; they are general principles that can be applied to design but not focused on the homework. The TA's are super harsh graders and at times not very helpful. Working in teams helped me a lot.

Dr. Christensen is great! The class is structured in a way that feels like it applies to the real world. The projects and homework assignments are very applicable to the real world. I felt like I really understood how to use CAD at the end of the class. The one problem I have was with the grading of the TA's. It was inconsistent and harsh.

He's a good guy. Makes lectures interesting with lots of real-world experience. The TAs are important in this class -- Prof. Christensen doesn't teach the lab, a TA does. He's a fair guy and cares about students. Projects can be time consuming.

So much homework in this class. You will spend a lot of time doing frustrating things. The skills you learn are great, and you learn a lot. Christensen usually didnt know how to use SolidWorks, and spent the first few minutes of class trying to figure out which buttons to click. Besides that he was very easy to work with and very personable.

Professor Christensen is great! The only problems I ever had were with the TA's. If you ever have problems in the class just talk to Professor Christensen and he will do his best to figure it out. This is the second class I have taken from him and I can tell he genuinely cares about his students.

Prof. Christensen is the only guy that teaches the CAD class at BYU, so it's not like you can avoid him.  His class is just okay, in the beginning, the class time was helpful.  After 6 weeks, I felt like I could have learned from looking at some power point slides.  The class does require a lot of time, but that's not his fault.
He was a great professor, and really related to the students. It was his first (and maybe last) time teaching Statics, but he really worked to understand it to help us as well. Super great guy!

Professor Christensen is super funny and engaging, but his class is very difficult.  Expect tons of work.  Sometimes I had nearly 20 hours of work in one week just for this class.  The TA's do the grading so your grade kind of depends on who sees your homework and projects.  If you are having grade issues, talk to the professor.  He's reasonable.

Made us use Inventor instead of one of the other well known and more commonly used CAD programs, and then didnt know how to use the program. We would spend the entire lab trying to teach him how to use inventor. To be avoided.

This class takes lots of time for modeling stuff but it's not hard just long. Professor Christensen is expertly clear, concise, and keeps things simple and straightforward. Grading is done fairly. Don't procrastinate at any time and you'll get an A. Sad part is after you take this class you may never get another byu ME prof. As good as Christensen
I learned a lot in this class. Brother Christensen is the nicest teacher I have ever had and he puts a lot up on the board so its easy to take notes. 100% I would take it from him again.

The class is just one of those classes where you have to spend a ton of time on it, but its not  hard to get a decent grade with him. He's reasonable and will give you points back if you go to his office hours and explain problems to him. Overall it was a time-consuming class, but it wasn't all that horrible.

This rating is for 281. I'm a big Dr blades fan. Some tableau stuff is super tedious and way harder than it should be but you learn a lot of good stuff in the class and it's a worthwhile stat elective imo. I think she customizes the class really well to make things more manageable. The project is interesting too.

She is an awesome person and teaches very well. Sometimes it can be hard to figure out exactly what we're learning how to apply it to problems, especially as you go on in the class. That being said she's really funny and makes class enjoyable.

Lectures are great and very useful. Half of the class is doing a practice worksheet in partnerships. The hw is harder than the exams, also the floor for an A is a 95 but it is doable if you prep for the exams well. Overall she taught the material well but the class is just hard in general.

(this review is for stat 281, data viz) This class was interesting. I liked the assignments okay, but unless all you care about is Tableau, do not take this class. Literally all we did was follow along with her as she made graphs on Tableau. I would have hoped to use other software as well, but I understand that not everyone in the class codes.

Ngl at the start of the semester I wasn't the biggest fan but prof blades is honestly the best. I really like her teaching style and how much she cares about the students. Go to TA lab for homeworks. She is super smart and an awesome teacher.

STAT340 is notoriously challenging, but if you are going to take this class - take it from Blades! I can't speak highly enough about her. She cares about her students and their success so much and it is apparent through the way she teaches. She has daily class activities/worksheets which were extremely helpful, so I would suggest going to class.

Dr. Blades is the best professor I've ever had. She is motivational, funny, teaches clearly, and gets to know all her students. She reached out to me personally a couple times in the semester and helped me feel supported. Start homework early and it won't feel too overwhelming. All the homework actually was useful and she was very transparent.

Dr. Blades is awesome. She gives personalized feedback on every test. She is a little intimidating in office hours, but it's because she has high expectations for her students and expects you to put in work and do well. The class is hard by nature, and she's very well organized. She wants the class to bond and got us all tater tots. A+ professor.

This is my 2nd class w/Dr. Blades. SHE IS THE BEST IN THE DEPARTMENT! Her class is well organized and she teaches everything you need to know for homework and tests during lectures. Exams were difficult but doable. Her tests are difficult but they are a lot like the homework. I can't say enough good things about this class.

Dr. Blades is by far my favorite stats professor at BYU. Her lectures are interesting, informative, and well-paced (even for me, who hated 240). She made 340 accessible and meaningful. She gave hard/long hw/tests, but gave personalized, encouraging feedback on the first midterm and was always responsive and respectful when students asked questions.

This class is one of the hardest in the major, so I think most of the difficulty comes from the course material. Dr. Blades is really caring. She has high expectations but is willing to work with you and help you if you meet with her outside of class.

She is so knowledgeable that it hurts a little. She expects us to know a lot more than we actually do. She is a very tough grader with the homework, which you have once a week (and are very difficult).

Some things about her management of the class is a bit odd and different, but her teaching is very well organized. ORGANIZED is the key word in her teaching, and it helps us remember and understand what we're doing. Lots of homework and grades hard, but you will know the material very well by the organized manner that she teaches. Also very caring!

Dr. Blades cares really deeply. She goes over the code in class and gives you real-life data sets to work with. She also helps you get to know your classmates really well. Her office hours really helped, too. Beware, she does grade the hw assignments harshly--go into the TAs before turning in. And the format of her tests are tricky. Still, 5/5!

Dr. Blades really cares about her students. Her class is pretty easyjust check your hw with the TAs and you will be golden. She definitely teaches for understanding and is great at helping us use code. I loved working in small groups in class and the experiments she chose to do. Oreos first real class day too!! She is great!

Blades was the best, she's one of my favorite stats professors. She is a genius, yet is able to explain things simply/clearly to her students. She goes fast and what she says in class is important so don't miss. She also is very willing to help if you go into her office.

Blades is the most difficult stat professor I've had during my time at BYU. Homework was graded with the most scrutiny I've ever experienced, and that scrutiny was inconsistent depending on which TA graded your work. She obsessed over being addressed as Dr. or Prof., the final project was graded much harder than the first steps were. Avoid her!

She's usually great at explaining things, but occasionally moves too fast (probably because shes a genius.) Dont miss class. Homework's only due about once a week, but its time consuming and graded with scrutiny. The tests are pretty hard and very different from the homework. But she lets you use a free online textbook and is helpful and kind.

Dr. Blades is a fantastic professor. She is incredibly smart, and by the end of the course I was amazed at how much I had learned. She is very willing to offer help and individual assistance if you ask for it. Her rubrics and grading are clear and fair. I'd definitely take more classes from her.

Dr. Blades was extremely good at explaining the things we did in class, and I felt like she was very clear on instructions for things involving code. However, I would say that everything except for the tests were graded with unreasonable standards. Be ready for intense scrutiny on all HW assignments and the final project, which take loads of time.

Blades is fun and easy to understand, but no one ever got 100s on anything. Doesn't give clear expectations and counts off a lot for little things (nitpicky). 2 midterms, final and a group project. My group lost points because she expected us to know exactly how to write a professional report, but overall easy. Go to class if you don't know R/SAS.

Dr. Blades is so funny! I was worried about taking this class during summer but it wasn't bad. The lectures were long and sometimes really boring (2 hours/day for summer) but helpful. I used the online book. There are nightly quizzes and twoish written HWs but not hard. Use the TA labs, they're super helpful for tests.
Very entertaining. Some material on homework not taught in class.

I took this class during the summer so it was fasted paced but Dr. Blades was able to convey all the material without rushing over anything. I got the CMU textbook just so I could stay ahead of the class but it's fine if you don't. If you look at the exam review and the notes the quizzes,tests,and finals will be easy after a while!

Easy class. I didn't even buy the text book she posted her lecture slides online and the homework is all through learning suite (I wouldnt but the book). 2% extra credit for participation with i-clickers in class . Lots of  tests but they are easy (85-90% class avg) . I thought the material was boring but she made it bearable.

Dr. Blades is a great professor; I'm glad I took 121 from her! Because so many students take this class as a GE, she just teaches what you need to know for the test, and doesn't branch out unnecessarily. It's a delight to be in her class; she is just so funny! She explains the material very well, and is always open to questions during lecture.

Dr. Blades' class is relatively difficult, but she is a fantastic professor that makes the class enjoyable. The content is very applicable and interesting, and Dr. Blades makes it fun and is very entertaining.

I love Sister Blades.  She is such a sweet woman.  I actually took Stats in High School and failed, but I got an A in her class!  For me, she was a great teacher and really helped me to understand.  She cares about you and wants you to succeed.  I would DEFINITELY take it from her again.

Take from Prof Heaton or Prof Reese. They are more straightforward and have shorter lectures. Prof Blades drags on the same topics the entire time, so if you're a slow learner, Prof Blades is a good choice! Keep up on the credit quizzes and the CMU Checkpoints, study for the tests, and you'll do fine.
The class is really hard and there are lots of tests.

I loved Professor Blades. She is very kind and caring. The course is somewhat easy for a math class, but it does take work. As long as you come to class and study it's not too bad. She is very good at explaining the material and on top of that she's really funny.

Admittedly, I am terrible at statistics. That being said, Dr. Blades was always there to help me. She specifically remembered my name and would ask me after lectures if I understood the concepts, which is something you don't typically get in a 300-person class.

Professor Blades was a great teacher. The material isn't very interesting, but she's funny so lectures weren't bad. She is incredibly clear and is willing to answer any questions you have. This class is so easy: three credit quizzes a week that don't take long at all. Definitely take stats from her if you can!

I was in Professor Blade's flipped lab, which I LOVED! We had 1 lecture, 2 lab a week vs. the usual 2 lecture, 1 lab a week. Blades only taught in the lecture and they always seemed long. The TAs taught lab :) She is a nice professor and will help you if needed. There are many opportunities for extra credit as long as you attend lecturelab.
Professor Blades is really clear and doesn't mind explaining it multiple times. She is very interesting and there are lots of opportunities for review.

Super good teacher. If you struggle in math, take the class from her because she is way clearer and just a better teacher than other stats professors.  She is always willing to help, there are so many lab opportunities and reviews if you do not understand. Attendance is optional but you get extra credit if you go. Great teacher.

Really great teacher and good at explaining concepts and keeping students engaged. The hardest part about her class are the tests. but those are department-wide so it doesn't matter what professor you take for STAT 121- you have to take the same final.   Highly recommend her. She really cares about her students.
I enjoyed being in her class.  She's a smart lady and definitely knows what she is doing. It's not easy, but if you put in time and effort you will succeed!

The Final is a killer (and it will kill your grade). She does not prepare you for it at all. The rest of the class is doable. Extra credit (bringing breakfast, being on time) is available. But don't waste your time and money. It's not even worth 1 out of 1000 points. She will never tell you how much it is worth... That's because it's worth nothing.

Very nice professor. You will feel great about her class and think that you understand everything until you take the Final. I had an A throughout the entire semester (and on both midterms). But the Final was unimaginably difficult (I studied 3 times more than for either midterm). I received a D on it and ended up with a B+ in the class...

This class was very easy. I took it spring term which likely helped, but it is likely easy any semester. I did not buy any of the textbooks or notes and was just fine. Prof. Blades is great. Really clear and helpful. I definitely recommend her. But it doesn't matter much who you take it with because the material is standardized for all instructors.

Good professor with a boring/hard class.  She explains everything very well.  The tests are departmental and hard-so go to her reviews.  They are the best I went to.  The TAs are not super helpful in open lab.

Pro. Blades is a pretty good teacher. Lectures are long and fairly boring, but you'll get a better grade if you stick it out. I never used the textbook (waste of money). Two homework assignments a week (can get most of it done in TA lab). Some extra credit available.
She's way cool and easy to follow.  I wouldn't take Stats 121 from anyone else.

Prof Blades is a very efficient teacher.  She goes quickly but not too quickly...most of the time.  She does big class group activities sometimes to keep us awake and entertained, even in the huge lecture sections. Wasn't very difficult, just study the excellent review materials she provides and you'll do great on tests. :)

She cares a lot about her students!  I failed one test and went to see her for help and she spent an hour with me going over the material and reteaching it to me. I then got a 95 on the final!  I think she is a better teacher one on one - but she is still amazing!  She really wants her students to succeed!  Go to her office hours if you need help!
She did a good job trying to make the material sound interesting to those of us who were not so excited about it.
Very Well Taught considering the large amount of material that needed to be covered.

I took STATS 221 from Dr. Blades.  I thought that the class itself was boring, but Dr. Blades tried to make it as interesting as possible.  She's young and pretty chill when it comes to HW, quizzes, etc.
No Comments

Top Tier teacher at BYU. doesn't take things to seriously and makes going to class not a drag. makes the class fun and not just about doing the work. Homework isn't very hard , and she is very willing to work with you. One of the Best Teachers at BYU for sure

Excellent professor, easily one of my favorites here at BYU. She cares about the students, is funny and entertaining, and the course is overall very light. Easy class to get an A if you do the homework (there isn't very much)

Sister Baxter is a top 3 professor. I had no expectations coming into this class and she hit all of them out of the park. This class easily became one of my favorites this semester. I feel like I developed well as a writer and she is very supportive of her students. She is also HILARIOUS. I have never laughed more in a college class in my life. .

Writing 150 is kinda an obnoxious class but Professor Baxter made it really fun. She does well to connect with her students and make everybody comfortable in class. Obviously there are a lot of papers but she gives clear criteria and is a kind grader while also giving lots of extra credit opportunity.

Professor Baxter was an excellent instructor. She graded assignments honestly and fairly, and the papers were manageable. Attending and paying attention in class was sufficient, as the textbook was not a difficult read. Assignment rubrics and instructions were consistently clear and easy to follow.
She was an amazing teacher and she made every class very enjoyable.

Professor Baxter was a good professor. Honest and fair grading with assignments. Papers were reasonable. Pretty openly political at the beginning which was not necessary for a writing course but was a good teacher. Textbook was used but listening in class will be enough. Rubrics were clear and so were any directions for assignments.

Professor Baxter is a very good teacher who takes the time to make sure we understood the principles taught. She always reads everything we write and gives us the best feedback on how to improve our writing. I highly recommend her as a professor and if I come across any more classes of hers, I'll be the first to sign up! She genuinely cares for you

She is really energetic and funny. She cares about your writing and attempts to help you improve. She lets you choose your own topics and is lenient with some grading if she knows you did your best and exhausted the issue.
Great teacher really cares!

Really nice and helpful, she cares about her students and wants you to learn. Take Writing from her if you actually want to improve your writing. Grading is easy to an extent - you can get an A- fairly easily, but it takes some serious effort to get an A.
She is a great professor with a sense of humor.  She also can be flexible about deadlines if you really need it.  I enjoyed the topics we wrote about and ended up getting very good grades.
No Comments
I love Natalie!  She is so much fun and very helpful.  She wants you to do well.

WARNING: there is a ton of reading and small reading responses. It is not that bad though. I never read any of the books and still got an A. Learn his system, play his game, and you should be fine.
WORST CLASS EVER. Kramer and his TA's are terrible. DO not take this class from him.

Kramer is a great guy and honestly has interesting lectures which I enjoyed, although I wish they pertained more to what was on the test. I spent so much stinking time reading. The tests aren't too bad if you get the big picture. 1 reading and a 1 page response due each week. 2 4pg. papers. And 2 2pg cultural event reports. It's just a lot of work.

Professor Kramer was just not very organized and unapproachable.  There are hours upon hours of assigned reading every week, and usually two chapters with four chapter quizzes each per week, in addition to an essay or book, and a paper.  Every week.  Unnecessarily difficult for a GE, like for real.  Steer clear.

This is a GE, but I spent more time writing for this class than all the others combined. At some point, I quit going to lectures because he spent the majority of the lecture talking about the homework rather than the material. Also, be prepared to use three website (Not Learning Suite) for this class. Some of which, you have to pay quite a bit for.

He treated his classes like a glorified TED talk. All about him and what he wanted to say, little actual intellectual content provided. He offered no test review other than vague study guides, no specificity whatsoever. No feedback was offered on any work, papers or otherwise. Attendance was claimed to be mandatory, but lectures were irrelevant.

Professor Kramer's a-spiritual, rambling lectures made me wonder if I'm qualified to teach at the University level, because all he does is talk in circles.  His lectures were about as useful as your appendix.  His test reviews were so ambiguous and the material is so vast, that it makes you pull your hair out trying to figure out what to study.

This class was mandatory for me to take. I attended class every day because sometimes we would have quizzes that were used for attendance points. Although these quizzes were not worth a lot of  points I sill came. There are also TA reviews every Friday so if extra help is needed in the class one can attend. Professor Kramer cares about his students

The structure of the class was lacking. After a couple months of the class, the class was still vague, and our objectives were still uncertain. I did not enjoy this class, and it was very poorly taught.

Worst class I have ever taken. Class started on January 8th, and on February 1st, he was still spending 10 minutes a class talking about the syllabus. He grades extremely hard on the weekly papers that we have to write. And to make that even better, the TA's give absolutely NO feedback. Worst class I have ever taken.

I really like Professor Kramer. He is a tough grader, but gives good feedback that helps you improve. He is really knowledgable about the topics he teaches. Discussion in class is always interesting thanks to Prof. Kramer. I would definitely take a class from him again. I enjoyed his teaching style.

I agree with everything said about Kramer's lectures.  Fascinating, engaging, and thoroughly applicable.  You will definitely read in this class (I read most of three books in Norwegian), but by the time I took it, the syllabus didn't change a bit.  I knew exactly what I was getting into, and I loved the small class size and the seminar feel.

Dr. Kramer is by far my favorite professor at BYU. I have taken multiple classes with him and would take more if I could. He is not always easy, but he is reasonable. He gives helpful feedback on papers and teaches with enthusiasm and clarity. There was not one class session where my mind did not feel expanded tenfold. Take ANY class from him.

Dr. Kramer is tough but he's such an engaging lecturer and everything he teaches is so current. He's great at explaining tough topics, both in class and in individual meetings. You'll work for a good grade, but you will never want class to end because discussions are so good.

The class was super hard, but he is really good at explaining the material. I loved the material more because of how he explained and always knew I could as questions. He knows what he is talking about. Just listen and don't be afraid to ask questions.

Kramer was an awesome lecturer. He makes you feel comfortable enough in his class to ask questions/discuss. The grade is based almost entirely on writing... the papers are hard to get an A on. Use his office hours. He really changed my opinion on humanities. Tons of reading and buy the textbooks. Not a super easy class, but I still recommend it!

This is required to take the Norwegian Danish credit exam.  The syllabus was constantly changing and readings were in both languages, sometimes hundreds of pages long.  Plus a lot of projects were held until the end of the semester.  Difficult class.

I don't like humanities at ALL. Kramer helped change that, a little... Best teacher for the subject. 6 1-page papers. 2 3-pagers, and 1 5-page final paper. He does not care about length and format as much as content. Very relaxed on when assignments are due. I turned all but 2 assignments in late (some very late) & got almost full credit. Good pick

I did not feel that his class was very fair.  I understand this is just my personal opinion, but I was often confused because the dates of assignments were constantly changed and unclear. Tests were picky; you had to memorize lots.  He even lost one of my exams, luckily found it later.  I really didn't enjoy this class at all.

Made me appreciate art.  Very interesting class discussions.  5 short papers, 2 longer papers. Semi-easy to do. 2 Tests, 1 Final. Tests are harder, but I got A's on all of them by outlining all the chapters & memorizing the paintings in class & the text.  Sounds hard, but it's really not if you do it as you go. If you do that, you'll ace the tests.

Like all of his classes, this one is very thought-provoking.  Be prepared to think.  In a class this small, you should be prepared to participate regularly, because those who do seem to grasp the concepts better.  Grading is mainly based on two midterms, journal entries on the readings, and the final paper.

Such a difficult topic, but he made it almost comprehensible. You have to think very deeply. I thought I would get a bad grade, but I didn't, so he must be generous. He wants original thinking on the paper and final. I've taken him before and will take him again because he is a very good Humanities professor.

I learned a lot about theory in this class, but it's really hard . Grades are based on basically 3 randomly chosen assignments (which are graded impossibly), a 12-pg research paper, and a final. Dr. Kramer is a great guy but I wish I had more assignments to help my grade.

I've never really been interested in Humanities. But after having Kramer as my teacher I look at art in a whole new way! I loved this class and highly recommend him as a teacher. There is alot of reading and the tests are kinda picky but the class is very reasonable if you put the effort into it.

Nate is such a great teacher!! This class was good because you really learn a lot, but the tests, readings, and papers (only 3 short ones) are all very reasonable, and even a little easy to do. I still remember the stuff I learned from his class, and it made me want to be a Humanities major!! :)

He's a way nice guy, and really stimulates meaningful discussions well, and is open to any view points.  Sometimes plays devils advocate to get people thinking more.  I really enjoyed the class and thought He was a great guy.  The papers are critical essays, rather than the long boring research papers required in other HUM classes.
Brother Kramer is great. I learned a ton and really developed critical thinking skills. Tests are easy if you study for them and utilize the TA. Great class for discussion.
This was my first Hum class so I was a bit nervous, but I really liked him.  His classroom management was OK, and we had great discussions. He helped me look more deeply into books and pictures.

Dr. Kramer is a nice guy.  He remembers your name and comments.  He makes you feel comfortable enough to make comments.  The class has 2 midterms and a final.  You also have to write 4 papers (3 pgs) and go to 2 culture events.  The class is very fair.

This class was awesome! I did not look forward to this class at all but Nate was incredibly engaging and taught with real world application. He boosted my confidence in writing and helped me through personal consultation and helpful exercises (there was NO busy work). Seriously, take him.
THis is the man. The most down to earth teacher you're gonna find. He make class interesting and uses current events to teach his lessons. he's easy but you still learn a lot
Great teacher. He's a fun guy who makes the class entertaining and interesting. Loved his class
Caplin is a teacher who is passionate about making learning practical. He has a sincere desire to help empower his students.

Dr. Caplin is hilarious, extremely intelligent, extremely knowledgeable, approachable, friendly, everything you'd look for in a professor. Very laid back in a good way. 10/10, would pay to take class again!

This was one of my favorite courses.  Even taking this course in the last year of my Master's course, I learned a lot about how to improve my writing.  Class was so entertaining!  The teacher made the material fun and interesting.  I learned about current events, improving myself, and writing all in one course.  I highly recommend this course.

Dr Caplin is one of the best writing teachers at BYU. He is funny, and always keeps the class entertained, while still managing to teach the material. He's a very smart guy and is extremely helpful. He tries to build a friendship with everyone in the class. Everyone who takes his class loves him. :) So take his class! You wont regret it!

The class wasn't hard overall because it was university band, but you definitely need to practice, as with any other band class. Prof Seamons was great at teaching the music, but when it came to concert logistics I was left very confused and didn't really know how the concert was supposed to work until we were doing it.
A great band director. Approachable, caring, and insightful.
Dr. Seamons is amazing and one of the best band directors I've ever had! Take symphonic band you won't regret it. The people in the band are also so amazing.

I highly recommend taking Symphonic Band! Dr. Seamons cares a lot about the band, including how we perform and who we are as individuals. He even cares about the people in the back of the band haha. Definitely the best band director I've ever had!

Best band director I have ever had. Related things to the gospel and really pushed us to be the best band we could be without losing our respect. Knew everyone's name and really sought to have a person connection with you.
Dr. Anderson provides a very streamlined course and keeps lectures and exams simple.

One of the best professors I've had. Professor Anderson gives super clear and engaging lectures, and he loves answering questions in class. You can really tell how much he cares about the subject material and his students, and he'll even go and do research for you if you ask a question that he doesn't know the answer to.

Professor Anderson is great! He is very passionate about his field, and he takes time to explain difficult concepts. He takes time to answer other questions, and he is very engaging. The main assignments are a quiz after each lecture, which were very helpful for understanding the material and the exams. Everything is based of the slides. 10/10
He a great teacher and is great a answerign questions
Amazing professor. Said It was his first semester and the whole class was blown away because we all thought he had been doing it for years!

Professor Anderson was one of the most talented lectures I have had the pleasure of taking a course from. Lecture slides were entirely exam relevant and drove the course of the class, but he always took the time to answer any questions students had while still finishing on time every class.

I absolutely love Professor Anderson. He's probably my favorite Professor I've had here. I took Psych 111, and his lectures are super straightforward and his class is really interesting. He loves answering questions, and his course and expectations are clear. 100% recommend.

He is an amazing teacher, clear expectations and cares about students. Test material only came from material he lectured on, mostly multiple choice. He cares a lot about students. Super engaging lectures. He doesn't input assignments ahead of time into Canvas, but goes over upcoming assignments in class. Everything is listed on his syllabus.

He's very kind, approachable, relatable (young millennial), and willing to help - especially with the paper, which is a big chunk of your grade. I got a B+ on the midterm, but the easy pre class quizzes put me at an A. Final grade probs A- or A

GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS! 

Light homework, solid learning, just make sure you study well for the exams

Dr. Anderson is an incredibly kind man who always makes himself available to his students and their questions. This class was difficult for me, as someone who studies with STEM, but he did a good job of taking time to explain concepts fully. The exams are more difficult and there aren't a lot of assignments in this class to help fluff your grade.

Good professor
Take good notes on lecture- everything is on the exam, and there is no study guide.
Accessible outside of class, values your time.
Nathan is a great teacher and you will have fun learning the concepts of contemporary. But also he never answers his emails and is randomly tough on grading.

Nathan is really awesome. I'm surprised he didn't already have an RMP profile. He started dancing in college which was great for a newbie dancer like me. Really helped me grow as an artist but still lots of great technique.

This was a hard class but Professor Crane was kind and caring and taught me so much. He really knows his stuff. It was difficult subject matter but i was challenged and i really learned. I love Dr. Crane! Highly recommend.

Sometimes lectures were disorganized, and the flow of the class was confusing. He has lecture videos that are extremely helpful to review before you take the exam. He would get feedback often and would change the way he taught, which improved the class as time passed. Overall, a hard but semi-interesting topic; be prepared for a ton of work.

No student in the class had an A until the curve is applied at the end. This reflects a failure of the instructor. Students should be able to succeed in a class before a curve is applied. Most students did well on tests, but did poorly on the group projects because they were graded harshly to widen the distribution or lower the class average.

ME 472 is an awesome class. I think it is the best class I took at BYU. It really got me ready for real world applications. The class was a little disorganized but Dr Crane was shaking things up. It think it will get better and better. He is very understanding and reasonable.

Dr Crane is a great guy. He really knows his stuff and he provides lecture slides with all the needed information (and worked-out examples). The homework problems are challenging, but come in pretty manageable volumes. The tests are challenging as well - they are timed, in the testing center, and on LS (on a chromebook) with an equations sheet.

The hmwk is very, very hard. His lectures and lecture slides are very disorganized. He is very unclear about expectations for projects, which happen to be  worth a large portion of your grade. He's just not a great teacher.

The problem for those taking 372 is that Professor Blotter is also a horrible teacher, from what I hear.

Dr. Crane is really fun and has done a lot of amazing things with his career. The course information is crucial to ones ability as an engineer, so take it seriously, but the structure of the class wasn't very helpful. I found reviewing notes quite difficult as ideas did not connect and lectures weren't structured to connect concepts.
Dr. Crane is very knowledgeable, but it doesn't mean he knows how to teach any of that knowledge. He is difficult to follow during lectures and often seems disorganized and scattered.

Dr. Crane is decent at teaching, I will give him that. His grading is absolutely awful, and it is VERY UNCLEAR what he expects with reports and assignments. This is the second class I have had with him and I hope it is my last.
I enjoyed Dr. Crane as a professor, but I think he's a bit tough on grading. I did learn a lot in the class.

I took this over Spring Term during COVID so despite the typical difficulties that come from making a class online in such a hurry it was a great class. Machine Design is a hard class no matter how you teach it but I believe this is one of the less stressful options for that class offered at BYU. Great professor, glad I took it from him.

Dr. Crane is great. I took this class from him before it updated to the new class standard (which is much much better now) but despite the poor formatting of the old class (not his choice) I felt he did a great job. He takes real interest in his students, he knew a lot about the material and was happy to help.

Much of the material was not organized well, so the lectures were confusing. It was like the homework was not related to the quizes, which were not related to the tests, which were not related to the projects, and everything was a lot of work.

Lectures are very dry. He occasionally asks for our opinion on how to improve the class, but he never changes those things. If you ask a question, be prepared for an answer to a different question or a reason he doesn't know the answer. Notes are disorganized, lectures are confusing, and homework is unnecessarily long.

I genuinely loved this professor and the content he taught. He was passionate about the subject and taught it well and with some humor. He did introduce a group project however, and that detracted heavily from the content of the class. Overall I enjoyed my experience.

While I want to give him the benefit of the doubt because he seems like a good person, I'm not a huge fan. Pretty poor at giving feedback. Felt more rude than helpful.

Also, not a fan of one tardy and one day absent being the same penalty to your grade. It's incentive for students to not go to class if they're already late.

Twyman is a good guy but the class is super disorganized. The lectures don't make a ton of sense together and the projects and assignments are super disconnected and you're graded super harshly on quizzes for things that don't matter.
The most disorgnized professor ever

Professor Twyman was one of my favorite professors. He gives plenty of warning ahead of assignment deadlines and let us know if we should budget more time for an assignment. He is excellent at giving feedback and really appreciates your interaction in the class. Underrated.

Professor Twyman is a good professor who knows a lot about UX design and gives good feedback. DO NOT think you can get away with not doing well on a single assignment. There are no tests or heavily weighted assignments so even just getting a single high point question on a seemingly innocuous quiz or other assignment will drop your grade by like 5%

Not sure why people don't like him so much. His class isn't amazing, but it's easy and he's a genuinely good person. Willing to help when asked and teaches the class well enough for me to get something out of it. We just had a few assignments that were easy and he was good at preparing us for our capstone proposal.

Hes a descent guy but not a good professor. He requires students to do assignments without teaching them what to do before, then tells them they did it wrong. Students need to redo them afterwards if they want to do well on their final pres or capstone. MISM students should have access to a better more effective professor for their capstone courses

He's extremely knowledge of UX Design. When you needs help on an assignment, he gives super good feedback. Some students don't like him, but he's genuinely a nice guy. His courses seem to get better year after year when he incorporates feedback from students.
Class organization was confusing and hard to figure out. Probably the worst organized and taught class of my entire 4 years at BYU

This is the most arrogant professor I have had at BYU in the 4 years I have been here. The class materials were disorganized and the professor seemed to have a chip on his shoulder. I would avoid. Try Mark Keith.

I have fewer grievances with the professor himself and more with his organization of the course. It was confusing and it felt like no one knew what was supposed to be happening most of the time. It was very easy, but that may have been because I didn't even know about the readings. He's a nice guy and is willing to help when asked.

Dr. Haines treats us like members of any major professional orchestra. He demands excellence. Every performance with the philharmonic has been electrifying. I'm not sure how he does it, but he delivers, and the audience loves it. I feel like he should be much more opinionated about his music making, and demand more of us more often. Amazing person.

Dr. Haines was great! There is a rating on here that says they got a bad grade from missing the REQUIRED dress rehearsal, but Dr. Haines made it clear from day 1 that there were 2 extremely important dates we could not miss, the dress rehearsal, and the concert. BYU will excuse it if you are prepared. It's only one rehearsal a week, and it was fun!

Letter of the law person. Not willing to work w/ you. It is a 1 credit non-audition orchestra but I missed the 1 hour middle of the day dress rehearsal due to a scheduled exam that went over. He told me there was nothing I could do & gave me a C as my absence "affected the rest of the ensemble." Save yourself the stress & join a community orchestra
