He is so kind and navigates difficult topics well, sharing personal experiences and creating a safe environment for students to do the same. Really wants you to succeed and willing to help outside of class. There are only a few assignments and they are somewhat different from what is talked about in class, so start early and study hard!
Very nice. The exams do focus a lot on the readings, so don't skip them! There is also important content covered in the lecture so it is important to attend.

Was so excited about this topic but this professors lectures are not intellectually enlarging, regurgitated materials from other family study courses already taken, makes generalized comments on statistics, attendance is not mandatory yet the exams are based on a HEAVY amount of material from lectures and textbook. easy grades are sometimes a waste
He was amazing! He used his personal experiences to help explain hard concepts. He is so willing to help students struggling! His Exams were hard, but if you study and go to class, you will be fine.

Prof Leonhardt cares a lot about his students but doesn't have a ton of experience with what he teaches, which makes it hard to take him seriously. Honeslty, I felt like this class was just a bunch of information you already knew being spit back at you.

Professor Leonhardt is great and I really enjoyed his class! However, you do have a 10 page paper that is worth like 40% of your grade and his tests are pretty hard. His tests are based off the lectures and reading (so attendance isn't mandatory but it is hard to pass without it). Overall, great class but he is a tough grader.

Professor Leonhardt is one of the best professors at BYU. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to see each of them succeed. His lectures are very engaging and even powerful. He approaches extremely painful and sensitive topics with empathy and compassion. He's very kind and accessible outside of class. 10/10 recommend this course!

Dr. Leonhardt is so kind, clearly cares about students, and is very accessible. His lectures are well formulated, include student discussion, and are very applicable. I will say there are very few assignments in the class and thirty percent of your grade is a final essay. The essay feels  intimidating but if you start early and get help its doable.
This class was great. Attendance isn't mandatory but lectures were always good so you wanted to be there. He's very accessible outside of class. I would recommend!

I got an A and hardly attended class. If that's your thing, this is a great class for you. It's a bit of a shame because he's an awesome person and a great lecturer, but when you're a busy student it's hard to go to class when you know you don't "have to".

Nathan is amazing. In the first weeks of class he asked to meet with all of us so that we could get to know him, and so that we could feel like we could turn to him whenever we need. The class isn't "easy" but you will genuinely learn so much. I couldn't recommend him enough.

I can't say enough good about Dr. Leonhardt. It is so clear that his goal is student success. That doesn't mean this class is "easy"... but it's 100% doable. He offers help on every assignment, he's accessible, and prepares you extremely well for every test. His lectures are extremely interesting, discussion based, and uplifting.TAKE THIS CLASS!!

This was a great class. I felt I learned a lot to help me in my future career and just overall in my future family. Dr. Leonhardt cares so much for his students and is passionate and grateful for his job as a professor. Highly recommend!

I LOVE Nathan, his classes are some of my favorite. He's always has a funny story to tell and makes classes and lectures SUPER enjoyable. I always love going to his classes. He is always willing to help you improve and gives detailed feedback so you know exactly what you need to do to get better.

He is an amazing professor! All his advice and critique is very helpful and comes from a place of good experience. He is always willing to help you one on one and answer your questions if there are any concepts you're struggling with. Highly recommend.

I'm always amazed at how Nathan knows exactly what I need to do to improve an assignment. He's crazy smart and incredibly talented, and I genuinely look forward to his classes. You'd be lucky to have a professor that wants you to succeed as much as Nathan does.

Nathan cares a lot about his students, and really wants them to succeed. He can give laser precision feedback, this might sting to some people, but realize its in the best interest of your abilities. He also will not hold your hand through the class, but he will give instruction and feedback that matches your personal drive.

He's a fabulous professor. He's more fun if you're more fun, so relax and enjoy his class. You'll do really well if you listen to his advice. He wants you to succeed! He's also one of the better professors to get feedback from, because he'll tell you honestly what's wrong with your art, and then he'll make you laugh so you don't feel like dying.

He's one of my favorite professors here! His lectures are amazing, although sometimes he goes off on tangents. To quote his catch phrase, "oh wait! That reminds me of a story!" But all his tangents always seem to come together in the end and relate to the lesson plan. Truly amazing, would defiantly take a class from him again!

He definitely knows what he is talking about which makes classes more enjoyable. He clearly outlines everything as well as grading; he doesn't try to hide anything or doesn't try to undermine you. He truly wants the best for his students but if you don't put the work in don't expect him to bend over backwards to help you at the very end of the term

He was a nice guy. Basically was not present the whole semester, we saw him once. That is fine, I understand that is how lab classes are. Wish the TAs would be more prepared to explain the content. But, this new system they made is much easier than the older system. Just not a very fun class but easy. Also just hope you dont hate your group (I did)

This lab is better than physics 107 but still not great. There is not much direction and you basically just mess around with equipment for most of the time. You have to create all of your experiments yourself and there are some lab reports and oral presentations which aren't too bad. No exams which is a plus.

I don't know if this is more of a reflection on Dr. Powers or the physics department but the lab classes are a total joke. Only saw Dr. Powers on the first day, and spent most of the class messing around with equipment that we weren't taught how to use to design our own experiment. Didn't learn anything and felt it added nothing to my knowledge

The physics labs have not taught me anything & are seriously the worst. 108 with Powers was better than 107 with Lawler at least. If you have a bad group, it will be so much harder. You basically play around with random stuff on the table and have to understand what it means without getting clear direction. TAs are stingy graders and a 96% is an A

Despite not having any E&M experience prior to taking this course, the projects and activities were very doable. There are only two exams, both on circuit analysis. Dr. Powers is a fantastic professor, he cares so much about his students and is very helpful when preparing for exams. Group projects and group work are the majority of your grade.

Labs at BYU are generally pretty bad because you never interact with the professor and are just kinda left to your own devices to create experiments. There are no tests but there are a lot of reports that you have to do in groups.

Hardest class I've taken at BYU. Given I'm not a natural physicist but man did this class kill me. Large homework assignments due THREE times a week, with absolutely brutal late credit policies. He had entertaining demos that were fun (didn't teach me anything tho) I feel like I was teaching myself literally everything (with the help of chegg)

As a professor he is not bad, but the problem is the tests. Two of the midterms are online at home, but I would much rather have them on paper. They are mostly free response, but because the tests are computer-graded you will miss questions just for rounding differently. If they had been in the testing center I would have had no problem.

Professor powers was a new professor when I took his class, and that was obvious. His class scores were about 5-10% lower than the other physics 105 professor. However, he is a fantastic guy and does his absolute best to make sure you understand the material. I only wouldn't take this class again because physics sucks. Homework heavy, hard tests.

Dr. Powers is a fantastic professor. Well organized class that gives students a lot of freedom to design experiments to learn more about physics and the scientific method. Class isn't too hard as long as you participate in class and go to the TAs for quiz corrections.

Dr. Powers really cares about the students and is very approachable.  He wants you to succeed and understand the physics.  The one thing to be careful about is that most things are groupwork in this lab, so really choose your lab group well the first couple weeks.

He was never really there and grading was left completely up to TA's, which could be frustrating at times since different TA's graded on different standards. Sometimes it felt like a waste of two hours since we didn't learn anything, but it was easy and not extremely hard to get a decent grade. Make sure to actually comment on your peer reviews!

Class was stupid easy. Powers didn't teach us anything; he was only in class on the first day for about five minutes. Many reading quizzes were ambiguous and ask about things that aren't "taught" (ie. read from a page on Max that often has many typos). If you follow the lab report instructions exactly, you'll get an A (which a 96 or higher).

Extremely passionate about physics and a nice guy, but the teaching slacked big time. Concepts were not well explained. Powers never explained the foundation or the difficult concepts, but rather random concepts that didn't help me learn what we actually needed to. I recommend getting close with a TA in this class and they will teach it better.

I think Dr. Powers is a great guy, but I never learned a single thing in lecture. We would take a ton of time to go over one problem, and hardly go over any of the concepts that were in the homework and in the quizzes. It felt like the dude from catch me if you can became my teacher.
Dr. Powers is one of the kindest people I've ever met. He really cares about our progression as students and teaches us to be true leaders. I wish I could take another class from him.

The class content is pretty difficult and unique but he does a good job of presenting it. It's a lab class so the model is just a bit different. He was always very inspirational and spiritual. The quizzes and assignments can be difficult, but you can typically get points back by working with the TAs.

Easiest class at BYU but if you want to use your time effectively it's not here. Two hours of in-lab participation is required for a project that could be easily done in 20 min. No teaching or lectures of any kind and experiments are self-designed. A TA is present for labs, you will likely never see or interact with a professor.

I like Powers as a person but this class isn't very well organized. The lectures and homework are pretty disconnected. It takes half the lecture to explain a simple concept, and then the homework and quizzes will have problems we've never learned how to do. TA's are EVERYTHING. It's his first year teaching this course though so I'd give it time.

physics 107 is a standardized class kinda like chem 106. However, you are free to do whatever you want during the labs (design your own experiment) Pre-lecture quizzes are tough, and grading scale is tougher (96% is an A) but it is doable. just make sure you hit all the points in your lab report.

Pass this class by being shameless and going to TA hours. Seriously I cannot stress this enough. You HAVE to go to the TA's. They will teach you what you didn't learn in lecture. Textbook isn't really needed. I stopped reading it halfway through the course. Powers is better than cheryl davis because I think he is clearer in his teaching methods.

This was the biggest waste of a class. Every week, I sat with my group and we made up these useless experiments that taught me nothing, and then we all sat and made up two pages to fill up our lab notebook. If your TA was a hard grader you were screwed for the lab reports. Pray you get a good TA

This class was a mess. I always left lectures confused. We were never specifically told what was going to be on the tests so you just had to guess. If you didn't have a good TA, you were basically screwed for the whole semester. Save yourself the stress and take physics from anyone else.

This was Dr Powers' first semester teaching lecture, so most of the bad came from his teaching coach, who was in charge of the course setup. Lectures were mostly conceptual and dont relate a ton to the other work. He's so passionate about physics and he really loves his students. I think in a few years, he'll be the best physics professor on campus

I actually had him for physics 105 this semester but it wasn't an option for the class name so whatever. Anyways, he is so confusing during lecture. He is all over the place and you will not even know what's going on. All we do is draw free body diagrams. There is no explanation of concepts or the math behind them.
All the grading depends on your TA. I do not think it increased or deepened my physics knowledge at all.

The class was a mess. Everything is left for the TA's to teach and grade. There was no structure and everybody was consistently confused. Your grade was completely dependent on how hard of a grader your TA was. Mine was terrible, therefore our class average was significantly lower than other sections. Pray you get a good TA.

Honestly, this is the easiest class and Dr. Powers is super nice. This has nothing to do with Dr. Powers, but what a WASTE of a class and time. This is 2 hours a week I can't have back that I mindlessly sat there and BSed a stupid lab report. Let's get real and drop the requirement for this class? Total waste of time and nothing learnt.
This class was very easy. You had to show up and do work in class, but outside of class there was no work. It had a very clear grading criteria, and I feel like everyone can get an A in this class.

Literally useless. The class says no prerequisites but he expects calculus based error statistics on your lab reports. He also doesn't tell you what to experiment on and then marks you down when your experiment doesn't add to the scientific community. He's the epitome of a PhD professor with no idea how to work with undergrads. Waste of a semester.

This class is different from phscs107. Theres very little use of formulas and plug and chug. The focus is on conceptual understanding it seemed like. There are also two exams, or group projects really. They are the same as normal labs except you write a lab report. You need to turn in near perfect work to get an A.

108 is the lab and it should be a pass/fail class, but to get an A you need a 97%. All grading and instruction is by the TAs, who grade minutia pretty harshly. Dr Powers, when he's there, is willing to explain concepts and meet with students to help with the exam and final, but your grade is still up to the TAs.

I like this class because you aren't required to rush through the lab, you can go slow and talk out concepts with your lab partners. The downsides are most TAs grade harshly and assignments require odd things to earn full points. Wish they would combine the three little weekly assignments into one so I didn't keep forgetting to do them.
Dumb class, he knows that labs don't teach us much; so he tried to make the class more difficult with weird wording and asking us to go about it in a ridiculous manner.

This lab is fantastic, but you will have to rely heavily on the TAs and keep track of all of the homework well. Your never gonna get out of lab early, so pace yourself and you will do well. Dr. Powers would come in to talk to us and answer questions we had during the labs, and he is a super cool dude.

Dr. Powers is good at teaching (helps you to figure things out for yourself/explains well), but he could improve as an administrator (a lot of assignments, some were due at weird times and I forgot them). As of winter 2017, you'll learn really learn the material, but it's the work of a 2-3 credit class. Give yourself enough time and it'll be great.

(FYI THE CLASS I TOOK WAS THE LAB SECTION) Labs were long - finishing was rare for anyone in the class. Some were quite tedious, became repetitive and eventually a chore. I learned just fine, but the class would have been boring without my lab group and the TAs, who were quite amusing.

If you're a MathEd major, you should take a class from Bro. Priddis just to see the way he teaches. Possibly the best teacher I've ever had. The way he encourages the class culture, responds to students' questions with respect, manipulates the class to best fit students needs, connects with students individually, makes it extra fun... incredible.

MATH 290 at BYU is a difficult class but having Dr. Priddis helped me make it through the class. He was very kind and willing ti help students in any way possible. He was happy to answer questions, meet with students in office hours, and was accommodating to students busy lifestyles. If you are taking 290, take it from Dr. Priddis!

Doc Priddy is epic. I loved going to all of the lectures and he made learning Calc very fun. He always made sure that students had access to outside of class resources and whenever I needed help with assignments I could get it from either the TAs or him. Super energetic professor, only fell asleep a couple of times (thats on me). Labs are mandatory
Definitely has a passion for his class and cares about his students. A bit loud but in a fun way.

Would be higher but his lectures were such a mess. He would waste lots of time reviewing old material and answering questions. Besides this he's a great and caring guy and his office hours are very helpful. He's great at hyping you up for exams as well.

Calc 2 is hard. Prof is very knowledgeable and can answer questions. Often run out of time for most content in class. He has notes online to review what was in class. Not many study guides were given. Tests are hard and detailed. On average 2 homework per day. lots of content but this is probably the best professor for the course.

This course isn't suitable for those without a solid math background. The practice tests are lacking, simply urging you to self-practice during class. What I've gathered from this class is that textbooks and homework don't really prep you for the exams. If you're aiming for an A, steer clear of Cal 113 with this professor.

Funny guy. However, is not good at teaching what matters. Tends to ramble about misc. topics and never gets around to teaching material that is on the test. 100% dependent on Khan Ac. to teach me. Recitation attendance is 4% of your grade, also NOT helpful for learning the basics. Homework is doable, but if you aren't a math major I would avoid him

I can't imagine a better professor for 290. He's super organized and I felt like I knew exactly what I needed to do to do well in the class. The book is awesome. Short readings, all 5-10 pages, but super helpful. Definitely read it. Some of the homeworks are tricky(not super long but tricky) but the tests aren't as bad. Take him! He's incredible!

Dr Priddis is a fantastic teacher who makes math very understandable and is great at answering questions. I felt very comfortable not understanding material and felt I was able to ask questions. He is also extremely compassionate.

Dr. Priddis is an incredibly caring professor. He wants each individual in his class to learn and grow intellectually. I loved his lectures because he gave us the opportunity to think during class with example problems, and he made us laugh.

Dr. Priddis is a great teacher. His lectures include a lot of class participation, and he will work with any student on any problem until they understand what's going on. He's approachable and friendly, in addition to obviously being very smart. I would highly recommend any class from him.

Algebraic geometry is an awesome subject, but requires a lot of machinery to set up. Professor Priddis is the perfect person to take this class from as he teaches the core of the subject while also explaining the commutative algebraic prerequisites as well. He is very accommodating, nice and an excellent lecturer.

I liked Dr. Priddis overall. He's really big into group projects and homework assignments (up to and including a giant group project replacing the final), so if you're into that, go for him. Class is just a review of the reading, so I usually just half-listened on Zoom or dipped. So big on having good office hours and really wants your success.

Seriously a great professor and a great person. Take smaller classes from him-I had him for calculus and it was just not the same. He is super funny and remembers everyone's names. Pretty much all assignments are group work but the way he sets it up you never get stuck with a dysfunctional group and he holds everyone accountable for their own work.

This professor makes abstract algebra fairly easy to understand. That's saying a lot. It's a tough subject but when I took it from priddis he organized it such that I could understand almost everything. The homework was done in groups which was tough at first but I grew to like it. His midterms aren't too hard if you study for em. Great professor!!

Dr. Priddis helps the whole class to understand, and will keep re-explaining something until everyone understands. He is genuinely interested in your success, but expects your participation (in the best way). TAKE HIS CLASS!

Dr. Priddis really cares about his students doing well in his class. If you struggle with anything he will do whatever it takes to help you get there. His lectures were focused and clear and tests were hard, but he always tells you exactly what will be on them so you know how to study. No surprises or trick questions, just math.

Dr. Priddis is an amazing professor who really cares about his students. He encourages participation and questions. He is extremely accessible before, after, and outside of class. I really think he's one of the best math professors at BYU.

Okay, I love this man. He is mega friendly, has great stories, took feedback from students, and even invited us all to lunch. That said, this man could not keep the class on track. He would take so many questions that he would never finish a lecture, which was bad cause the department tests are hard. I gave him 4 stars because I hope he's changed.

He was a great teacher but was a little slow and boring for me. He also spent to much time answering questions that we wouldn't get to the new material until the last 10 minutes. Then the next class he had to answer questions and got behind even more but never pushed the homework back. Then the homework was 3 days ahead of what we learned in class

This is a very difficult class but dr. Priddis was very helpful and competent. Sometimes the way he explained things made it harder to grasp the bigger picture. Discussing it with him individually and asking your specific questions helps a lot and is almost a requirement in order to do well.

Dr. Priddis was a good choice. He tended to get sidetracked during his lectures, but he really cared about his students. He would have his office hours right after class in the math lab, so it was very easy to get help from him. Even if you were in the math lab not asking for help, if he saw you he would swing buy to see how you were doing.

Dr. Priddis is the absolute best! He will work you no matter what. He is always so kind and will go over test questions as many times as you need to understand. He will assign you practice problems so that you feel comfortable. I wouldn't take this class with any other professor!
Cares a lot, explains the concepts amazing, listens to student feedback. I understand everything he teaches. Work load is reasonable, and he was a good perpective on what is considered too much work.

Math 113 was a really difficult class, but Dr. Priddis definitely helped me succeed. There's a lot of Homework, but it helps you learn the material so you feel more confident with it. Dr. Priddis is also very available and strives to help everyone pass. Would definitely take a class with him again.

Dr. Priddis one one of my better professors this semester. He usually didn't get through all the slides every class but he made sure to cover all material. He is very patient and answers all questions. His grading is more than fair.

Professor Priddis is an excellent professor who passionately and elegantly explains mathematical concepts in a universally comprehensible fashion. However, be warned that the course is very test heavy, with the final and midterms comprising of 25% and 50% of your grade, respectively. Plan on spending >5 hours outside of class reviewing material.

Dr. Priddis is incredibly caring of his students but you have to put in the work. Find a good study group, actually do homework to learn, and study well for the tests. If you are learning as you go (not just absently solving), the tests really aren't too difficult! Dr. Priddis is super nice, so sit in the front. Lectures are mostly examples.

Dr. Priddis is awesome! He explains calc in a way where you understand the concepts and can come up with the formula for the integral yourself, rather than memorizing a bunch of equations. He also cares about his students a lot, and made an effort to get to know his students despite it being a large lecture class.

Dr. Priddis is a caring person and wants all to succeed in class. It was very helpful to go to his office hours and have him explain the material one on one because it tends to get very jumbled together in the lecture. Difficult class, lots of homework, and hard tests. I'm glad I got it over with and dr. Priddis was very helpful

Dr. Priddis is one of my favorite professors ever! The thing that stuck out the most to me was how willing he was to help students outside of class. He came to the math lab and remembered people's names. He sent helpful emails with homework tips and provided lots of study material for tests. Great professor!

Prof Priddis is a capable professor who loves math and his job. He is always willing to help students and does his best to learn peoples' names. Over all, I enjoyed this course and would take it again.

Dr. Priddis is the best math teacher I've ever had. The textbook is hard to understand, but Priddis makes everything clear in his lectures. There's lots of homework, but it just improves your abilities. He clearly cares about his students and wants to help them succeed- I would recommend taking MATH 113 from Priddis above any other professor

Dr. Priddis did a very good job at teaching a very difficult class. You could probably survive on just the textbook, but having him work through proofs in class always helped me understand better what was going on. The homework is difficult, as it pushes the topics beyond the text, but Dr. Priddis was always willing to help in and out of class.

Great person but plan to spend your whole life relearning the material in the math lab. His class often feels scattered. Gives plenty of extra credit opportunities so it is not too hard to keep a good grade. Plan to spend at least two to three hours on homework prior to each class.

Dr. Priddis is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He really cares about your success. He invited our class to eat lunch with him every other Thursday. Even though the material is difficult, he makes it fun to learn. TAKE 290 FROM PRIDDIS. Just do it.

Dr. Priddis is literally the best!This class is really hard, but with his help, it becomes easier and enjoyable. He really cares for his students. He has very flexible office hours and it always willing to help. He also communicate effectively with all the class through dailyemails. Many extra credit opportunities. Without a doubt take it from him.

Calc 2 was extremely difficult, but he was very understanding and was always waiting in the math lab to help. He is passionate about math and understands that not everyone is a math major. He has in-class quizzes as well as Reading quizzes, but they are really easy and is there to help you. Test are a majority of the grade & HW is mostly to help

Dr. Priddis is an awesome guy! He does a pretty good job teaching calculus. He has office hours for students to come in to get help, and he is very easy to contact. Math 113 is an extremely hard class! I would usually spend 4-6 hours doing homework for every class period we met. The tests were extremely difficult and very long.

Dr. Priddis was an awesome calculus professor! He was pretty funny and often told us math jokes. Lectures were useful for learning the information. There is quite a bit of homework, but it is not worth very much of your grade, so it's nothing to worry about. The tests were not too difficult if you put in the effort.
He's a great guy, the class is just hard. He genuinely wants you to succeed and makes time to meet with you. Just put it the time and you'll do okay.
Dr. Priddis was awesome! The way he explains things in class, especially with the form to solve problems. I would definitely take from him again!

Dr. Priddis cares a lot about everyone in his classes. He tries to get to know each person. His method of teaching surpasses any previous professor I have ever had. You have to actually care about the material though. Don't take this class if you can't handle committing lots of time to understand the topics. That being said, Doc makes it worth it.
Dr. Priddis is extremely intelligent and unravels calculus in a simply way. Take Math 113 from him.

He is super smart and makes awkward math jokes. I enjoy this class, a lot of the class is spent answering questions so not a ton on the material. I would suggest working outside the class to create a strong foundation, and then come to the lectures with questions.
Great professor, likes to have fun and explains stuff well. Overall a very kind man who cares about his students. He will help you get the grade you want in the class.
He is a great teacher and a great guy. We all love him.

I love Priddis! In addition to regular dept homework, which has a very low grade weight, he has you write a short summary of the reading before class and also has application projects from time to time. He has great math jokes and is so kind to his students, he really cares about the kids and math!! Take Calculus 2 from him, you won't regret it!

He has a great sense of humor, which helps a lot. He has you read the textbook chapter to be discussed in class and then write a short summary of it, due before class starts. Written hw due by end of class, online hw due at midnight. Lots of work, so plan on spending lots of time doing it. The class is difficult, but that's just part of calc 2.

Priddis is the man. He prepares you so well for all of the tests. Sure, there's a lot of homework, but still our class did much better than any other calc class, and much of that is due to him. I just wish he taught more math classes so I could take another one from him.
He is the most most helpful calculus teacher at BYU.Tests are easy,graded easy and willing to regrades if students want to-Very friendly and party teacher during final test
Great teacher. It's hard because the math department dumps all the homework on you. it's not his choice, but he'll make the load as easy as possible. very fair. loves to teach and is good at it.
He knows math very well
Nate was an awesome teacher-probably the best math teacher that i've had ever.

Calc 112 is not an easy class, but Nathan was a GREAT teacher! He explained things methodically and was always willing answer questions. Fair, friendly, and responsive. I would highly recommend Nathan to anyone wanting to take 112.

Grad student, tries hard, will probably get better, terrible explanations. Online homework didn't really match the style of the tests. Gives past years tests as study material, but the four teachers each take a turn writing an exam. Test 3 is ridiculous, lots of F's. The class sucks and the dept doesn't really care. I'd try for a different teacher.
Grad Student.  He tries hard to be a good teacher.  He knows his math, just learning how to teach it.  Tests are from the Department (test #3 is hard, everyone fails it.)
I loved Dr. Rockwood's class! He is extremely knowledgeable and caring! Tests are a huge part of your grade, but he does allow for test corrections! I have learnt a lot from him.

He is the most disorganized professor I have ever had. He had needless pop quizzes that were two weeks behind the content. He never posted a syllabus, so we had to guess what our grade was based on. The TAs contradicted each other and did not understand his grading, so it was impossible to figure out how to be better. Many did not like his class.

He made the content very interesting and sometimes hilarious. This class always gave me stuff to think about in my other classes when I was bored. Maybe not life changing but a great way to knock out a GE and learn some cool things about history and philosophy.

I would recommend this course to fulfill your civ credit. The course was very average. There was nothing glaringly good or bad about it. There were weekly reading quizzes, two essays, and two tests that included multiple choice and short essays.  The lectures were informative if not exciting.  Dr. Rockwood memorized everyone's names.

Each class was an open discussion where any answer was the right answer if you could defend it, but the tests were obviously not that way. It left me super confused and I never knew what any of the right answers were, getting some of my lowest test scores yet. That being said, Dr Rockwood is a great person and an engaging teacher

Good options for the GEs (Civ 1,2 and Letters). Makes you take notes by hand, have to attend lectures, buy an iClicker for attendance, exam heavy (does allow test corrections though), weeky readings with a quiz (two attempts on quiz and the only homework), TA wasn't the most helpful but if you study his slides/pay attention can get an A.

I wouldn't recommend this class. Exams are extremely difficult and most of your grade is made up of the exam scores. There's no real study guide either, he advises you to write your own practice exam based off of what you think he will test you on. I'm a straight A student, studied for hours, attended every lecture and never knew enough to do well.

This was the best class I took my entire time at BYU. The readings were short and interesting, the workload was very small, the lectures were amazing, and Rockwood is just a great guy. There is a ton of extra credit as well, I didn't do well on the paper but still got an A. Take this class at all costs!

Dr. Rockwood probably is the best lecturer I've had at BYU. He is incredible at facilitating discussion and breaking down complex topics. Taking PHIL 201 and 202 from him was an awesome way to knock out my civ requirements. Tests are hard, but if you study you'll be alright. The class is more about doing philosophy than memorizing stuff.

Professor Rockwood was a fantastic professor. His lectures were engaging and interesting. I went into the class only planning to take it for the GE credit, but I ended up caring about the philosophy too. Professor Rockwood allows test corrections and makes it possible to do well in his class. Not too much homework either
Dr. Rockwood does a good job of making complex concepts accessible. He is a fair grader and is very clear about expectations for the course. I would recommend him for upper-level classes.

Dr. Rockwood is an excellent professor I took several classes from him and I learned a lot from him in each class. His lectures are perfectly pitched, there are lots of opportunities to discuss concepts and participate. He is very good at validating comments and teaching for understanding. He is also very accessible outside of class.
Professor Rockwood is a great professor. Class discussion is interesting, and the homework is NOT excessive at all. It is a different way of thinking but it is a great class to take.

Professor Rockwood is awesome. His pre-class readings are super helpful, lectures are concise and interesting, and he facilitates fantastic class discussion that helps prepare for the test. He gives a simple study guide as well, take notes in class for sure. Great professor.

The readings are almost always extremely entertaining and thought-provoking, although there is a good amount of assigned reading per week. The lectures are always very involved and he gets you to work toward understanding philosophy yourself.

The material covered in this class is very interesting and I loved it. Prof. Rockwood was great in guiding lectures. The grading and reading assignments were a bit weird, though. The entire week's worth of reading was expected to be done the weekend before and there were online quizzes and review quizzes on it. Tests were not easy, GO TO CLASS

Professor Rockwood is a really solid professor. I found there to be a weirdly high emphasis on religion in this class but that's not unexpected for a BYU class I suppose. Other than that it was fascinating subject matter and professor Rockwood is clearly knowledgeable about it. I learned a lot in this class and it wasn't too difficult either.

prof rockwood is so hype! i was really worried to take this class before it began, but it wasn't nearly as bad as i was expecting. things on the lectures correlate to the exams, one assignment and a few readings are due over the weekend. just show up to lectures and you'll be chilling. it's not a super hard class--he doesn't like technology btw

This guy is absolutely terrified of technology. To the point where using any kind of electronics in class takes off about 20 percent of your grade. Dropped the course within the first 15 minutes of lecture 1. Strange that a philosophy professor is so closed to other methods of learning than pencil and paper. Major red flag.

Dr. Rockwood is great! If you attend class, do the readings, and have good arguments in your papers then you should be fine. All the test questions come from the lecture slides. He is a very kind and generous professor.

I really enjoyed philosophy prior to taking this class, but this class was somewhat a bust. Extremely vague on grading criteria, the TA's seem to grade based on their opinion even if you fully answer the prompt correctly they will mark you down. THE TESTS AND QUIZZES ARE HARD! I got an A in the class so it is doable, but not the best experience.

Personally, I felt that this class was great for me---along with History of Philosophy 2. Not only did I learn the content but also felt I grew as a thinker. It is a lot of reading that tends to be hard to understand, but as long as you come to lectures it isn't hard to understand.

Prof Rockwood is a good professor. He makes the material approachable and relevant. His papers are graded fairly and the assigned reading is a very reasonable. 
Downside: We couldn't take notes on laptops and that some times it felt like we spent more time talking about students' opinions than we did discussing the actual opinions of Philosophers.

Dr. Rockwood is the best professor in the philosophy department! A lot of writing is involved, and it can feel like a bit much; however, the frequent amount of writing and feedback from all the papers ultimately helps you become a better writer. If you want to be a great writer, take this class! The class is doable and suited for a 3rd-year student

Great. Two exams, not the easiest to study for but he sounds like he is going to prepare you for lectures a lot better now in the future which is good. There were two papers but I was able to write each just in a single day, not too difficult. You can rewrite the papers if you do poorly on them and get points back. Weekly required readings.

This was my least favorite class this semester. The formatting is awful and the assigned readings made no sense. If you unfortunately find yourself in this class, make sure you come to the lectures because it is the only way you will understand anything. I definitely recommend coming to office hours too before the tests.

Loved this class! Engaging lectures that made me think. Tests in testing center, but he is clear on what you need to know. Quizzes and readings each week, but he shortens them so they're easily doable in time. Graded on participation, but his lectures are interesting and easy to listen to. Two papers but they're interesting and chance to revise.

Professor Rockwood is a really good teacher! The weekly quizzes are tough, but once you get the hang of them its better. You won't do good withouth the TA's helping you with essays. But the class is super interesting.

Class was very interesting, but it is very hard to study for exams and know what he puts on them. Finishes writing them about a week before you take them. Lots of reading, quizzes can be confusing but they are doable. 2 big papers, TA grades. We would cover something for a while in class but it wouldn't be on exam so make sure you know everything.

Not much homework other than the quizzes once a week. Class is carried by interesting material, not prof. Rockwood. Decent at lectures but unclear on what he wants you to get out of the class. I studied for hours to get a good score on the tests, and it worked but it took more of my own prep than his teaching. TA's are hit and miss.

He was honestly pretty terrible. Would put the scores in wrong so it dropped your grade and then not reply to your emails. Pretty inflexible to student feedback and was kind of rude. Reading quizzes were pretty difficult and were for upcoming material he hadn't said yet so you never knew what to expect. Put scores in wrong and then wouldnt respond

Professor Rockwood is a great teacher! Going in to this class I didn't like philosophy at all, but by the end I really appreciated it. He is good at respecting everyone and giving everyone an opportunity to participate. Extra participation also gives extra credit. A lot of reading, however, and two big papers.
Quizes are uninformative and hard, and the tests are the worst. The lectures dont prepare you for it and you can use tech in the classes. Highly recommend skipping this class.

Those who say his quizzes are hard might be those who are not used to reading philosophy. I've taken a couple of philosophy classes before this and I thought the quizzes were not that hard. You just have to go slowly at first and utilize searching the text for keywords. His lectures are captivating and he is passionate about what he teaches.

The lectures are decent. I feel like I learned a lot but my grade didn't necessarily reflect what I learned, more like I just played the game to get a good grade. His quizzes are hit or miss, though he switched them up this semester so they seem a bit easier now. As for prof. Rockwood, he clearly loves philosophy but idk how he feels about students
Nice lectures Hard exam Tricky questions Poor guidance Harsh TAs Would not recommend if it's your first Philosophy class.

The quizzes aren't that bad they just require you to read a lot. We could revise our papers, but your grade will depend on your TA. The exams are though, he curves them depending on how the class as a whole performs. If you're only taking this class for a GE, and philosophy is not your thing, you'll be very bored, but it's a doable class.

This class was HARD. Weekly quizzes are terrible even though you have two attempts. Students complained about this and he seemed not to care, even though almost everyone was doing bad on them. Tests are extremely difficult and it is worth more than 40% of the grade. Slides are informative and TAs are helpful, but I still felt like he did not care.

There are weekly reading quizzes that are HARD. There is a Short paper and Term paper worth a combined 35% of your grade. These are graded harshly. Your 2 tests are combined worth 40%. These are no joke either. This is a difficult class. You need to be willing to work hard. He has good informative lectures that he works hard on.

Great professor. He knows his stuff. The readings and quizzes are short. There are two short papers. He let us revise papers which was great. Just do the readings and assignment and come to class and you'll be fine. It's the usual difficulty

Weekly readings on direct philosopher writings. Vague quizzes on the readings (you have 2 attempts but there is no specific grading after the first attempt, so you end up guessing on the 2nd attempt and everything becomes confusing). Gets in-class opinions through surveys, but there's so many opinions that it's confusing what's the right answer.

Worst philosophy professor I have ever had. The class expectations are fairly loose, so don't be surprised when you lose points for something that you didn't know you were supposed to do. Quizzes consist of vague wording and trick questions. Really doesn't seem to care about student learning/success. Take from literally anyone else.

It is clear Dr. Rockwood doesn't care much for the success and growth of his students. You read the material and have to take quizzes before he lectures on it leaving you to guess his interpretations of philosophy. He also makes claims about thinkers that are legitimately under researched. One of the worst BYU classes I've ever taken.

Honestly, one of the worst professors I've ever had. The questions in the tests and quizzes are incredibly vague. Feedback I was given for essay questions on an exam was that I should have included details for a concept that was not mentioned in the essay prompt. I received a 0 for that essay question. Take this class from any other person.

Rockwood gives weekly quizzes every week that are so difficult, usually not more than 1 or 2 students (out of more than 100) can get a perfect score on them. Tests are also extremely difficult and make up most your grade, along with 2 papers. I studied hours on hours for exam and only got an 85. The class is too much work for what it should be.

If you like philosophy classes where you are able to develop your own ideas this is not the class for you. His teaching style is that he is telling you what the theories are and what they mean and that is fact (Especially when talking about Locke). He also insists on having tricky multiple choice questions that confuse you more than anything.

DO WELL ON THE MIDTERM AND FINAL! His classwork is chill and his lectures are decently interesting and engaging. Overall, the class isn't hard and he's a good teacher. Tests are a big part of your grade so you have to budget your time and study a lot to get an A.
HARDEST TESTS. you will have to pay 110% attention during every second of class to do well on any test

Professor Rockwood is super nice and very relatable, and I liked how his online class included LOTS of opportunities for participation and debate :) However, I thought that the weekly reading quizzes were pretty difficult. There is little homework, though which is nice. You only have one reading quiz a week and two papers for the entire semester.

Prof Rockwood is very knowledgeable about philosophy, and he wants his students to have a good understanding of the subject matter. His lectures were good, and he provided a lot of opportunities for student involvement. The only frustrating part about the class was that I had no idea what my grade was until it was finalized, so I was very stressed.

By far my favorite class that I took this last semester. Lectures are super interesting and engaging. He offers extra credit and if you just apply yourself on the papers and quizzes, you'll be fine. I looked forward to going to this class. I only spent about 40 minutes on homework each week, and a couple hours writing each of the two papers.

You better get a good TA. Tests/papers are all written responses and subject to interpretation by the TA's. Quizzes require your own interpretation of the text and if your thoughts dont match Prof. Rockwood, you get it wrong. Class content is interesting but not worth stress about your grade. No one got a 100 on either papers nor tests. no curve

Awesome professor with great patience and understanding. I took his Phil 202 and 205 this semester, and got A- and A respectively. His lectures are interesting and inspiring, and he likes group discussions. Quizzes are once a week. Midterms and exams are not hard. Participation matters.

The homework was the hardest part of the class. It was only once a week, but it took a while because the readings were hard. Class discussions can be dry and he spends a lot of time on the same topic until everyone gets a chance to share their opinions. Tests seem to be graded on weird criteria that I don't understand, but they aren't too bad.

Prof. Rockwood was a great choice for Phil 202- he really spends a lot of time engaging the class in discussion. He was super accessible after class and always loved a good question. The class will be tough if you don't like philosophy

Just to give you an idea--he always wears converse with his suits! He is younger and easy to work with. However, he does not allow any technology in the class. That bugged me at first but it actually made class better. The tests seem hard but he grades them very generously. He also admits if he made a mistake and will give back points.

He is an awful professor. Nate deserves a post because this class is very subjective. His quizzes are impossible, even with the reading, and his paper is graded subjectively as well. Take any other GE. I regret my choice to take this class.

Class is very straight forward and easy to get into the swing of. Lectures are interesting (maybe not if you don't care about philosophy at all) and participation is encouraged. Some people may struggle with the fact that this is a philosophy class, not a science class and therefore you have to think about things differently, but Nate is great.

Are you a Philosophy major? No? Then don't take this class. It was definitely interesting but I wouldn't recommend taking it. The readings are kinda difficult and there's just too many concepts and philosophers to remember. Definitely not one of my favorite classes. If you're a broad thinker, would recommend. Math or science brain, no.

Ethics from Professor Rockwood was one of the few classes I took at BYU that I would consistently go home and discuss with my roommates. Each class various moral problems were proposed, and then we would discuss what we thought was right and compare that with what philosophers said. Extremely fascinating. I thoroughly enjoyed this class.

This class was so strait forward. If you showing up to class and having half a brain, you will past the class. The tests are solely about the material covered in class. Brief review of his slide before a test is sufficient. He likes asking philosophical questions to engage the class. Attendance is required. Light homework. 1 quiz a week.

Good easy class of you just want a quick A for a GE. Very lecture heavy, the slides are a repeat so honestly, just take the test, answer a claas question or two while getting other homework done in the class itself. You can definitely feel his biases in the class, it's best not to show opposing research, he gets a bit flustered with that.

Nate is a great professor. This is honestly a pretty easy GE for BYU. Lectures are long since most of the lecture is just conversation, arguing for or against a certain topic. I got really confused in class, but after going through his slides on my own, I understood the concepts. This is a good GE if you are looking for something chill/interesting.

Dr. Speirs does research in experimental fluids, which really shows in this class. Since the course is Experimental Fluid Mechanics, he clearly knows the material and brings real expertise to the lectures. The class was very helpful overall, and Dr. Speirs was a good lecturer who explained concepts clearly.

He graded homework with leniency. The lecture slides are surprisingly comprehensive with all the information you need to study. We have midterms like every 2 weeks which was overwhelming at times. TAs are helpful with homework issues. I dont know why he is graded so low, he did a good job. He researches fluids and shares it in class which is cool.

He was alright. Grading was entirely subjective and he would often take off points because the "grade distribution was way too high" (he literally told me this). TAs aren't very useful. Tests aren't too bad, but lab reports and the project make up most of your grade. If another professor is offered, I would avoid Speirs.

I can not recommend this guy less. He is completely unhelpful and is possibly the worst subjective grader I have ever seen. Good luck getting any sort of good score on a paper/lab report. He doesn't tell you what he wants to see. And when you don't put exactly what he wants, he'll take off an absurd amount of points.

Dr Speirs turned what is supposed to be the one of easier classes in the major into the hardest one. The grading is completely subjective and he will take off nitpicky points in order to lower the average grade in the course. He is completely unapproachable and unwilling to help students outside of class. Easily the worst professor in the program.

He is really open for you to come by for help during office hours. The tests were really fair and didn't have a time limit. The class is naturally hard, but Dr. Speirs made it much more manageable. He is a really nice guy. 10/10 would recommend taking the class from him. 
(textbook was optional)

Professor Speirs is incredibly knowledgable in fluids, which is his area of research. Concepts are taught clearly and the class is well organized. Lectures are tied into interesting real word phenomena. He also does examples in class, which are similar to what is found on tests & homework. I would definitely recommend Professor Speirs for fluids!

This class and teacher were a joke. It should be the easiest class of the major, but the worthless grading rubric and grader who gave everyone an 82 on any and all lab reports made it the hardest. The feedback on these reports, which are 55% of your grade, was TERRIBLE. Machine design was easier. Dr. Speirs just shrugged and did nothing to fix it.

I genuinely loved this professor and the content he taught. He was passionate about the subject and taught it well and with some humor. He did introduce a group project however, and that detracted heavily from the content of the class. Overall I enjoyed my experience.

While I want to give him the benefit of the doubt because he seems like a good person, I'm not a huge fan. Pretty poor at giving feedback. Felt more rude than helpful.

Also, not a fan of one tardy and one day absent being the same penalty to your grade. It's incentive for students to not go to class if they're already late.

Twyman is a good guy but the class is super disorganized. The lectures don't make a ton of sense together and the projects and assignments are super disconnected and you're graded super harshly on quizzes for things that don't matter.
The most disorgnized professor ever

Professor Twyman was one of my favorite professors. He gives plenty of warning ahead of assignment deadlines and let us know if we should budget more time for an assignment. He is excellent at giving feedback and really appreciates your interaction in the class. Underrated.

Professor Twyman is a good professor who knows a lot about UX design and gives good feedback. DO NOT think you can get away with not doing well on a single assignment. There are no tests or heavily weighted assignments so even just getting a single high point question on a seemingly innocuous quiz or other assignment will drop your grade by like 5%

Not sure why people don't like him so much. His class isn't amazing, but it's easy and he's a genuinely good person. Willing to help when asked and teaches the class well enough for me to get something out of it. We just had a few assignments that were easy and he was good at preparing us for our capstone proposal.

Hes a descent guy but not a good professor. He requires students to do assignments without teaching them what to do before, then tells them they did it wrong. Students need to redo them afterwards if they want to do well on their final pres or capstone. MISM students should have access to a better more effective professor for their capstone courses

He's extremely knowledge of UX Design. When you needs help on an assignment, he gives super good feedback. Some students don't like him, but he's genuinely a nice guy. His courses seem to get better year after year when he incorporates feedback from students.
Class organization was confusing and hard to figure out. Probably the worst organized and taught class of my entire 4 years at BYU

This is the most arrogant professor I have had at BYU in the 4 years I have been here. The class materials were disorganized and the professor seemed to have a chip on his shoulder. I would avoid. Try Mark Keith.

I have fewer grievances with the professor himself and more with his organization of the course. It was confusing and it felt like no one knew what was supposed to be happening most of the time. It was very easy, but that may have been because I didn't even know about the readings. He's a nice guy and is willing to help when asked.

I genuinely loved this professor and the content he taught. He was passionate about the subject and taught it well and with some humor. He did introduce a group project however, and that detracted heavily from the content of the class. Overall I enjoyed my experience.

Also, not a fan of one tardy and one day absent being the same penalty to your grade. It's incentive for students to not go to class if they're already late.

Professor Kramer is a fantastic teacher. He keeps classes very engaging and makes every reading worthwhile. He is very passionate in what he teaches and cares for his students

Professor Kramer is amazing!! There is a ton of reading and subject material for his class, but he makes a tough subject fun. He's really funny and is very fair with grading and deadlines. If you go to his office hours he'll go through an entire paper with you if that's what you need.

Taking another class from Dr. Hansen was an absolute blast, this class was so fun with the field trips and people within it. Though since this was his first time teaching the class things were a little tough, a bit unorganized. Homework was fully effort based but some weeks it was really difficult, do the homework before you learn kind of thing.

Dr. Hansen was a great professor! The class very fun, and I learned a lot! I took the online class, and lectures are divided up into sections, quizzes can be taken twice, and exams were sufficiently challenging. There are a lot of discussion assignments, but they weren't boring like other online classes, and were easy to get full points for.

Professor Hansen was awesome. I wasn't sure about soil science at first but it was fairly interesting and you will definitely learn some new things. Class has a decent amount of homework but nothing crazy maybe like 2-3 hours a week. Great teacher and the lab was very easy as well.

I honestly don't understand how anyone has given this professor anything but a 5 star rating. Hands down one of the most caring and genuine professors I have ever met. He's so understanding as long as you're trying your best and he can tell you're trying your best. He has such a sweet soul and just wants his students to succeed and be happy.

I know Professor Hansen primarily teaches as a life science professor so this review might not count in that regard, but I had him for University 101 and I have to say he is one of the greatest people I've ever met. He cares about the well being of his students and is passionate about his work. Couldn't have asked for a better professor and class.

I took this class and the lab, and Professor Hansen is a great professor. While I didn't enjoy the class being online and had difficulty understanding the material, he was always willing to help answer any questions. He genuinely cares about connecting with his students. The labs were fun as he truly wants us to share his enthusiasm for soil.

I had Dr. Hansen for three classes this semester and he is genuinely one of the best professors I've had. He cares about the subject and the students and does what he can to make the class more manageable. The online format wasn't my favorite, but Dr. Hansen really does give you all the resources you need to succeed.

Dr. Hansen is one of my most favorite professors I have had at BYU so far. You can tell he is very passionate about what he does and cares so much about the students! PWS 282 as an online course was tough for me but if you email him or any of the TA's questions they are happy to help and answer really quickly. Take a class from Dr. Hansen!!
Great professor!! He really cares and is super awesome. Definitely take classes from him
He is my favorite professor at BYU. He is very accommodating and wants the best for his students. His lectures were interesting and he explains everything well.

Dr. Hansen is amazing and he cares a lot about your success. The class is online and the workload is probably an average of 2 hours per week not including study. Definitely go to office hours for the math parts, he will help you never forget it. He holds exam reviews that are CRUCIAL to go to. You also get a math equation sheet to use during exams.

This class is online! This made it harder for me to learn!
Neil, was great though and had test reviews in person. That, paired with my personal cramming, was the most successful thing for me.
Dude this class was my favorite class of the semester. Prof Hansen really is an expert in his field and I felt like he cared about me personally. Take this class if you are considering it!!

Great teaching. You can not go wrong with Professor Hansen. He is very involved with his students and wants each of them to succeed career-wise. He is very lenient and understanding and cares more for your learning than needless busywork. I would highly recommend any of his classes!

Dr. Hansen cares so much about soil but even more about his students. I wasn't sure how I felt at first about taking a soil science class but after this semester I have learned to really appreciate the intricacies of the soil all around us. Even though it was online the lectures were informative and the material was well paced.

I did not enjoy this class as much as I thought I would because it was an on demand class. He was spotty with when and how often he posted lectures and assignments. He kinda waited until the end of the semester to post a lot of the lectures. The quizzes are tough in my opinion but the exams are made from the quizzes.

Great professor, very understanding and will work with you! I went in to this class expecting to hate it but I ended up with a much deeper appreciation for soils and their importance. Has reading but doesn't expect you to do all of it. Says "I hope there are more important things in your life than soil science." :)

This is the second class I've taken from Dr. Hansen. I really enjoy his classes and teaching philosophy. Attendance isn't mandatory and he doesn't ask any trick questions. He covers what you need to know and nothing excessive. A very balanced class that didn't stress me out.

Dr. Hansen is a great teacher. I have taken two of his classes and he made both of them very enjoyable. He is passionate about what he teaches which helps make the material more interesting. He is a very reasonable grader and it is not hard to succeed in his class. He is a very friendly person as well and willing to help students outside of class.

This was a really easy class. Maybe an hour a week of work. The textbook was actually pretty good. Lectures moved pretty slow so it was really hard to stay focused, and I didnt feel like I would be missing much if I didnt go. But no complaints really.

Dr. Hansen is a great teacher and is very passionate about soils; however, his class doesn't always effectively invite others to feel the same way. If you aren't naturally interested in soils, this class will be tough. The textbook is a very dull read, which doesn't help.

The class has a few quizzes, a large project, two midterms and two long in class quizzes. The material is actually a lot more interesting that you would imagine. If you ever get confused, Dr. Hansen is always available to help. I learned a lot in this class and it was very manageable. He also might be the nicest man in the world.

Dr. Hansen is a great teacher! He understands that a lot of different kinds of people may be taking an intro-level PWS class, so he tries to make it applicable and interesting to everyone. He has a passion for soil and helps students get excited about it. A very reasonable teacher, and it's not hard to do well in his class.

Dr. Hansen is great guy and this was a very interesting class. Attendance is non mandatory but you should go. There are reading quizzes but they are easy. Also has a couple projects but they are easy to get full credit on. The material was more difficult for me to learn but Hansen and the TA's are great.

This is a one credit class on careers in environmental biology. It is really easy and you get to learn a lot about resumes and cover letters. Professor Hansen is a great teacher and helped me a lot with networking to find jobs. Overall, its an easy class with a lot of benefits.

Dr. Hansen is a wonderful professor who cares about his subject and teaches it in a clear, fun way. He gets to know each student. He gives his students lots of opportunities to get involved in hands-on learning, through field trips and soil labs and other ways. He is so, so kind. He is a very fair grader and very understanding.

Dr. Hansen is such an effective teacher. He requires you to read the textbook outside of class. But his lectures makes everything you read about come together and make sense. He's very caring, and you can tell he's passionate. He made soils, a class that probably would have otherwise bored me, interesting. By the end of the semester I actually care

Prof Hansen really cares about his students. He is funny and acknowledges the lectures can be dull at times, so he doesn't expect too much. The work load is pretty light, especially for a 3 credit course, and it counts for 2 GE's. I've really enjoyed being in his class and would recommend him to anyone.

Dr. Hansen does an assignment called "Brown Bag" where he meets up and has lunch with a group of students from his classes. This is so he can get to know each of his students. He really cares about his student's individual situations. If you need more time on an assignment or test and have a valid reason he will work with you. He is very kind.

Dr. Hansen is one of the best professors I've ever had. He does all of his exams in class because he is anti-testing center. His tests are straightforward as long as you do the study guide. You can tell he LOVES the environment and he makes boring things seem so interesting. His assignments are made to specifically get to know his students!

Dr. Hansen is the best- he tries to get to know the students which is great for networking. I took his soil science class and I loved how much passion he has for soil! Definitely do the reading and pay attention during lecture for your own benefit, but he doesn't mind if you fall asleep during lecture lol. Class takes effort, but not impossible.

Great professor. Very helpful when you don't understand something. Made class interesting with activities and hands on assignments. We did lots outside of the classroom which was helpful for learning about the environment.

His assignments & lectures (monologues) provided little groundwork for success in the class & his teaching (telling) was far from thorough. Pretty much nobody had a clear idea of what aspects of his teaching to digest & remained hopeful that a miracle would occur on an exam. It was hard to prepare for class/exams... I would consider other options.

Dr. Hansen is probably the most down to earth professor that I have had. He understands that your a busy college student and will work with you when something gets in the way of your work or a field trip. He's really passionate about what he teaches that help out with some of the boring lectures. But Dr. Hansen is by far one of my favorite profesor

Dr. Hansen is a great guy, but the lectures are on the boring side. For someone not very interested in environmental science, I had a hard time paying attention during lectures. However, I know that he is great for people that have lots of questions about the topics of discussion.

He is kind and truly strives to get to know each of his students. His lectures can be a bit dry--you can get pretty much the same information from the textbook--but if you get involved in discussions is can be more worthwhile. This is a good class to fill a GE, especially if you're like me and have some health problems. Do the reading.
Speak up and get involved in the class discussion. Ask questions. Enjoy the topics along with your classmates. Do these, and he'll be worth it.

Great experience with Hansen. He took the time to get to know each and every student in his class, and it makes a huge difference compared to other classrooms. He was very honest about what would be on tests, and tried to prepare us. You'll need to study hard to understand the concepts, but overall, I'd definitely take another class from Hansen.

Dr. Hansen is, aside from being a good professor, also a spectacular person. His natural kindness and care for the students really helps students enjoy the class and do well in it. If you ask for help, he'll help, and he'll see it through to the end. Awesome guy, awesome class.

Dr. Hansen is adorable. He is so kind and loves the environment so much. He really focused on giving us knowledge on real-world information. The tests were some-what challenging, but doable. He posts all the lectures online which is really helpful and nice. He was a little disorganized at times, but his love for his students outweigh the negatives.
Dr Harmon is the kindest! I learned so much in class from him. He will always help you out and cares about his students.

I love Dr Harmon, he's very kind. This class was super fun and I really enjoyed learning the organ from him. There were 2 midterms and then a final all open note and open organ. They are in class and timed. You take notes in your organ book and there is a bit of reading. there are hymn projects and other exercises to pass off but they are easy.

Neil is AMAZING. He brings a high level of expertise to the organ department. He puts in long hours for his students and caters each lesson to the needs of the student. I loved taking organ from him because of his passion and drive to help students become successful. If you've ever though about taking from him, DO IT.
Dr. Harmon is one of the sweetest professors in the School of Music. You have to practice around 3 hours a week on the organ, but class time counts towards practice.

Nurs 320 is not a very exciting class, but Neil is aware of that which is kind of funny actually. He is a tough grader on papers, but if you ask him for additional feedback he is very willing to help you. Not my favorite class, but doable if you put in the effort
Not a huge fan. Extremely boring class, it seems to drag on forever. Boring lectures, boring readings, annoying voice, and you write alot. follow the rubric, it will save you. Avoid if possible.

He was willing to work with me to help me succeed when I communicated my needs. That being said, if you have any problems with your group you can expect little to no help from him. All of this class involves group work, so if you have issues it will be a rough road. Your classmates can rate you and determine your grade in the end, so good luck.
Professor Lundberg is a great person, however, his class was difficult to sit through. Long lectures- most of the stuff he talked about could have been said in 15 minutes or less. TAs were HARSH!

Neil is a very enjoyable person. He lectures for too long and he knows it and jokes about it, but he is a really kind professor. We cover about 15 min worth of material over the 75 min class period, but this allows you to work on assignments in class. The semester-long group project is where all the learning happens, so choose your group wisely.

He was okay. He restructured a lot of the class, which is why it all seemed so disorganized and thrown together last minute. He lectured for too long on things we already knew, yet we were somehow thrown into the deep end with the projects. The whole cohort was in the class, which was fun. So much work on projects.

Lundy is awesome. I took his RECM 470 class as well, and I think 472 is wayy better. 470 lectures were dry and hard to sit through, but 472 is one of my favourite classes I've taken at BYU. I learned SO MUCH in this class. I was never freaked out about my grade ('cause I don't super care), but also quizzes and assignments weren't crazy scary.

Sadly most TR students are forced to take Dr. Lundberg's class, but I wish we didn't. He is a nice individual who is extremely competent in his field. His classes, however, are excruciating. His lectures are unnecessarily drawn out and it is difficult to pick any info out from them. He asks for feedback, but then doesn't change anything. Not a fan.

Dr. Lundberg structures the class well, outside of lectures. Quizzes, homework, papers, projects, presentations, and tests are fairly balanced. He is a really nice person and is flexible. However, his teaching style is difficult to endure; long lectures yield 10 minutes of real info., which must be sifted out of many repetitive, unclear statements.
Amazing guy easy class good time
Amazing guy easy class good time

Caring, funny professor, but a very tough grader. Classes were more of a ramble, only used a power point a few times. Large novels are assigned and read in the same week-very hard to get the reading done. Reading 4 novels with 5-6 other classes gets very difficult easily. Tests are very niche, memorized information from the guide and 2-3 essays.

Dr. Mason is the funniest. This is my second class from him. Lots of reading, but lectures are engaging & fun. Tough grader, but very willing to help if you're struggling. Very accessible. Exams are no harder than the exams in other colleges like life science (yesthere are exams, and yes you have to study--deal with it). Love him, loved this class.

Work intensive but rewarding teachings of life, literature, & language. Fosters critical thinking & curates brilliant though lofty reading selections. Handles short sighted closed minded students with grace. Pushes students to expand thinking beyond sheltered belief systems. His Infectious enthusiasm inspires us all to make "A Room of One's Own".

Was obsessed with criticizing MAGA. Claimed that "most writers are queer." Talked about almost every mainstream political issue in a way that it was obvious what his views were. He took a poll asking what political party we belong to, and equated people who attended conservative schools with being brainwashed. Made snide comments about the church.

Dr. Mason is a nice guy with a great personality and I found his lectures to be entertaining and definitely kept me engaged because of his humor. However, as other commenters said he is an insanely tough and picky grader on essays. His tests are hard with lots of memorization. Overall his class was entertaining but way harder than it needed to be.

Do NOT take ENGL292 from Prof Mason. Lectures are hard to follow, he is not very willing to work w you, and tests were harder than necessary. He gives a study guide, but there are often terms on exams that weren't discussed in class or readings. He requires poetry memorization, some of which are quite long. 3 papers, 3 exams, 3 poetry recitations

Dr. Mason is a really good lecturer. He's very funny, very engaging, and he really knows his stuff. He doesn't normally use slides, so there's not much visual aid. His tests are extremely hard. TONS of memorization of terms, dates, and people, plus three essay questions and his grading criteria is not always clear. Harsh grader overall. Great guy.

Dr. Mason is by far my favorite professor I've ever had. I took several courses with him and always learned so much. He very much focuses on lectures and discussion, but it's so rewarding and I always felt excited for class. He is also incredibly kind and understanding. Could not recommend him enough.

Prof. Mason is an amazing teacher. I have never learned or retained so much information before. He was knowledgeable and enthusiastic about what he taught. He is a tough grader, but fair. He gives a study guide for each exam, so make sure to really know the terms/people/quotes listed. If you study hard and ask for help you will succeed.

Memorization heavy; 130+ terms per midterm, three poetry recitations, eight papers ranging from 1 to 6 pages-double and single spaced, three midterms all recall/essay questions, re-writes tests every timeno student feedback on questions, no curve, little mercy on late assignments, extra credit often in the morningunavailable, hated the class.

If Professor Mason doesn't like your writing style you won't get an A no matter how hard you try. He expects a lot and is rarely available outside of office hours. His tangents do end up on the tests though, so take extensive notes. I've had him twice and I will do anything not to take him again.

Professor Mason is honestly the best. Hilarious, well-educated, respected, fun to listen to. You will never fall asleep in his lectures. He works hard, grades fairly quickly, gives extra credit and makeup opportunities, and learns everyone's names. I have had him twice now and I love him. He is everything good about the English department.
LOVED Nick and the team-teaching style of this class. SO much reading and lots of difficult concepts, but I wanted to go to class and listen to lectures.

Professor Mason was an incredibly difficult professor, and he was totally worth it. He is hilarious, offers great lectures, and teaches to the individual. He's accessible outside of class and extremely helpful to students who seek him out.

Prof Mason met with us individually at the beginning of the semester and really took the time to get to know us and where everyone served their mission and stuff. Topics of the class were really varied between culture and politics. The textbook is really boring and so are some of the readings but the class is interesting and really easy/engaging

It's an interesting intro course if you're exploring European Studies. A variety of professors come in and lecture from various fields. A lot of reading, and most of it is pretty boring.
