Some of the topics are pretty cool, but some are boring. He's pretty sarcastic and likes to show that he's right about everything, which gets annoying. It's aight.
Greatest  Professor at any University.  Take any of his classes and you will be greatly helped throughout your life.
Best professor at the University without a doubt. Funny and smart, this professor will help you through almost anything. Would take again, saved my semester.

An amazing professor, best I've ever had at BYU. He brings in real world and current events to class, and almost all of class is just discussion, not lecturing (which I always found interesting). The class manages to be funny, inspirational and interesting. You have to attend class, but it's enjoyable so you'll want to. Tough but fair grading.

Dr. Mason was really focused on making sure I understood the material. He is a very hard grader and his tests are hard, but he does it to make you learn, and I learned a lot. He is willing to visit with you as often as you need. Just make sure you do the reading.

I wasn't sure how I felt about his class at first, but Prof. Mason might be the professor who has taught me most in any of the classes I have taken at BYU.  He's hilarious and his lectures are engaging (if you have done the reading). He has daily reading points (which you can make up), and  gives a study guide for his exams, which are reasonable.
Great class with huge reading load. Mason is a great professor- very knowledgeable and made lectures enjoyable. The tests were difficult.

Prof. Mason is a fairly good teacher. Sometimes his lectures are a little dull, and his tests were a pain. My interest in this class (it was Jane Austen) was really high, but the class overall was a little of a disappointment. Lots of reading, but an okay class overall.
He was really funny and made class very interesting.

Awesome, awesome, awesome!!!! One of the BEST professors in the English department.  I learned more from his class than pretty much any class at BYU.  Excellent lecturer, funny, actually cares about students and their lives and is always willing to help.  I absolutely recommend Mason to anyone!
blast, the last post was ENGL 292, not 293. He does British, not American Lit.

Worked hard in this class but learned a lot. The material was covered really well and I appreciated that he gave study guides for the tests. Knows the subject well and delivers it in an interesting manner.
I absolutely love Professor Mason. His knowledge of British Literature is incredible and he teaches it in a way that is interesting and retainable. He's funny, witty, and will help you learn!

This class was a survey of British lit.  Dr. Mason did a fantastic job of providing both breadth and depth in the material.  He also did a great job contextualizing the literature so that we understood its importance in the historical time period.  DO NOT MISS THIS PROF!
Professor Mason is one of my favorites.  His workload is adequate, he is very clear and always willing to help.

All of his classes are excellent.  I have had him more than once, and he is my favorite professor in the department.  He is very well-informed on all discussion topics, provides interesting choices for reading.  Tests are no-brainers (as long as you attend class), and there are only a couple mid-length papers. Highly recommend any of his classes.

Very intelligent teacher and stimulating class.  Grading system and tests are very fair.  Hard grader on papers, but gives good feedback and helps you become a better writer. I definitely reccommend him for this class.

Exceptional professor.  Excellent lecturer and discussion facilitator.  Knows the material like the back of his hand.  Excellent at putting literature in historical context. Stiff grader on writing assignments, but his tests are equitable. The challenge is worth every second!
Pay attention in class and you'll do well on the tests.  Interesting prof, knows his stuff and can relate it to almost any other subject to make it more understandable.
Amazing guy easy class good time

By far the best religion professor at BYU that I have ever had. Nicks lessons are epic and super deep, if your a member of the church that feels like you know most things about the scriptures then Nick will teach you so much more you didn't know. If your not a member don't worry, light homework load and premium lectures definitely take his class.

Professor Fredericks teaches clearly and passionately and is always open to any questions students have. All the exams are open book of mormon and are basically the study guide in test format. He also has extra credit opportunities. If you want an easy religion class that will change your life take this one!!!

Professor Frederick clearly knew his stuff and taught me so much I didn't know about the New Testament. His lectures were always fun and engaging and he was always willing to work with you if you were struggling.

Professor Frederick knows his stuff. It's clear during his lectures but even more so when he just answers questions off the cuff. You will absolutely learn from the New Testament and be uplifted while taking his class. The readings are never hard and 6 of them are dropped. The test is based on the study guide that you fill out in class.

Excellent class and professor! He really understands that some people are there just because it's required and he makes it easy to get an A if you try at all, but also very interesting and informative if you want to learn. Very interesting lectures and perspectives, too!
This is a great class! I learned so much.

Bro. Frederick was great. No attendence quizzes/grade, but you do need to attend to get the answers for the study guide handouts. Lets you see 1 or 2 test questions before. Either a mcq or written test is avalible. I learned a lot without having to stress about this class, def take from him.

super easy class. legit gave you a study guide with questions that would be on the exam beforehand. So your notes for class was filling our the study guide. He'd always ask to make sure he covered everything from the study guide too. Gave two options for exams, written or multiple choice. Great guy and made the lectures pretty interesting!

First of all, I took his grad BoM Seminar, so I'm not sure what his undergrad classes are like. That being said, what an exceptional professor! He knows his stuff, he knows how to teach and run a classroom effectively, and he has a fantastic way of listening to students while simultaneously presenting new ideas and perceptions in a compelling way.

He didn't grade off of attendance, but it was helpful to fill out the study guide for the tests. He provided two options for tests that were multiple choice or a written exam. I took the multiple choice and found that they followed the study guide closely. His lectures were engaging and I learned a lot about the New Testament from him.

He has a great study guide that we filled out during class that covers everything that will be on the test. He has a multiple choice and written exam options based on what you prefer. He is very willing to help people succeed in the class and learn the material. Attendance isn't mandatory for a grade, but it is very important to do well.
A classic, excellent religion class at byu. Good discussions. Just fill out the study guide in class as your notes and get it down before the test and youll get an A easy.

If you enjoy lectures more than participation/group discussions, you'll probably really enjoy this class. He gives a study guide to fill out in class that goes along with the test questions, but they don't always give you the exact info you'll need for that test question. He's really passionate about what he teaches & it isn't too much work.

Please please please take Christ and the Everlasting Gospel from Dr. Frederick!! I learned SO much about the Savior, but the class was never a burden! There's readings assigned for each class that are super short, with a really easy assignment to go with them. He makes it very clear what will be on the test and doesn't try and trick you. The best!!

There are only 14 reading assignments and he drops the rest. Exams are straight forward, he gives a study guide and you can bring scriptures into the testing center. Lectures are a little hard to follow but he provides a lot of insight into difficult topics. Definitely recommend Frederick, it was a wonderful class and wonderful professor.

Class formatting is perfect. Read a few chapters before class and write a *very* brief response. Study guide is very straightforward, he explains the complex parts of the epistles and revelation SUPER clearly and concisely. Focuses on historical/cultural context most (my favorite way to approach the bible)

This class is what you make of it, if you want an easy A it's totally attainable. If you want to dive deep you will find the class super interesting. You can write any notes in your scriptures to use while taking the exams (3 total). 14 reading assignments (2 sentence responses) and a semster long project. WORTH TAKING IT FROM NICK!

Provides a very helpful study guide with the important questions to fill. Essential info only available in lectures. Sometimes blink and you miss key info during lectures. Slideshows are posted online without speaker notes. Outside work is reading a few scripture passages and giving a 2-3 sentence response. 'Religion professor' vibes, but fine.

I loved his class!! It was very simple. He told us that we would get whatever we wanted out of his class. He teaches from power points and tells you exactly what will be on the test. He is very kind and I learned a lot from him!
He's great! He lets you decide how much work you want to put into things and what your grade will be. His study guides are very clear, and his lectures are great!

His study guides make this class a breeze. But even if there's something you feel like you didn't do as well on, he's willing to talk to you about it and bump your grade up a bit if he feels that you have an understanding of the concepts and you just weren't able to demonstrate it as well in the assignment/test.

I loved my class with Bro, Frederick. He teaches about the history behind what we read along with spirituality very well. There's a study guide for each midterm that if you fill out throughout the semester, you will be well prepared for the tests. He's always willing to go over questions you missed and give points back. Homework is mostly reading.

Brother Frederick is a fantastic New Testament teacher. If you do the study guides each class, you'll be well prepared for the tests which determine a lot of your grade. He offers exam reviews before each test, and is happy to go over questions. I wish I had found him earlier to take more from him. He had grades entered quickly and fairly.

Nicely balances cultural background with spirituality and research. Does not have annoying reading assignments like some profs, mostly just go to class, with typical multiple choice exams that have very clear study guides, and aren't trying to trick you. Has a semester-end project and reading reflection, both easy. Big recommend!!

Professor Frederick is the best religion professor I have had at BYU, and I have had just about every great religion professor. It's informative, interesting, and uplifting. This is the best religion class at BYU that nobody ever talks about.

Professor Frederick is knowledgeable and willing to work with students. The class is history-focused, but with manageable tests if you stay on top of the readings and notes. Unstuck ai was a great study tool alongside the course materials.

Professor Frederick is a great religion teacher! I took him my first semester, and it was a great way to ease into college. He has pop quizzes, usually once a week, but they are super easy if you do the reading. Speaking of the reading, there's not a lot of it! It is not an insane amount to overwhelm you.

Dude professor Frederick has been the dopest and best and GOATEST religion professor I've had. He made the new testament so awesome and blew my mind every lecture. I took it in the spring and it was awesome very light homework and cool final project and pretty easy exams.
Great teacher! Would take again
seriously one of the most accessible teachers. I have ADHD and the format  of the class really helps, the study guide forces me to  follow along  its so  nice! I never rate teachers but I love him

SO knowledgeable about the gospel. 3 tests (including final), a few surprise attendance quizzes, daily pre-readings (you can easily pass without doing), and an easy semester-long project to "bring you closer to Christ" - you decide for yourself what your project will be. Test could be a bit tricky, but not awful. Overall, a good class.

He is one of the kindest professors I have met. The course is heavily history based, having to memorize a lot. Hardest religion class I have taken, however, he cares so much about your grade that he'll give you points back if you go to his OH. He genuinely just wants you to learn.

I LOVE this man. I don't even have any more required religions but I took it because I like him so much. He is so reasonable and really wants everyone to succeed. He does not give unnecessary busy work, has incredible lectures, and gives an essay or MC option for the test. I learned so much about the NT and he approached touchy subjects so well.
Professor Frederick was very knowledgeable and was willing to work with students. If you go to class you'll get an A. I missed a lot of class but still passed so it was okay!
Super interesting and knowledgeable guy. Tests were good. There was also a project.

2nd half of the New Testament w/Bro. Frederick has been awesome. Lectures are super interesting, and learning about the context of everything has been super insightful. I think he tackles tough topics quite well.

Most of your grade will come from the exams which are very doable if you just study the study guide. I highly recommend this class.

Brother Frederick is amazing! He takes a very academic approach to teaching the New Testament but I learned so much! Other than reading you don't have to much outside of class, but you are tested on what is discussed in class and the info most likely is not on his slides. He is gives points back on exams if you go over the questions with him.
Only religion professor worth his salt at BYU. Focuses a lot on the historical context which was really interesting. The only religion class I have ever actually enjoyed.

Professor Frederick has a lot of fascinating insights, is great at applying the context of the New Testament to the world/church we live in today, and he is easy going. All of the work is very straight forward, even the exams that have very direct study guides.

Professor Frederick is an awesome religion professor! His tests were easy as long as you followed the study guide and did the readings. Just stay on top of everything in his class and you'll be golden

Dr. Frederick was a great professor. He really knows his stuff. A lot of the grade is based on the tests, but if you show up to class and take notes on the insights he shares then you should be okay. One project. The only required book we had was the New Testament, and we were able to use different versions. Would take again in a heartbeat.

This class was sooo easy which is nice. Very little reading and the tests are pretty easy if you fill out the study guide. Brother Frederick is super nice. The class was definitely more focused on historical context than doctrine/feeling the Spirit. Lectures were informative but not exceptionally interesting.

You need to be in class to know what you need for the tests.
Take thorough good notes and you'll do great. Each test is your choice essay or multiple choice(I did multiple choice).

My 1 criticism: there were surprise reading quizzes he said there would be a lot so if you did poorly on one it wasn't a big deal--but there weren't that many quizzes.
Tests were ok, but you did have to devote a good amount of time to them. Otherwise very easy. He was a very good teacher. He was pretty engaging and kind.

He is the most chill dude ever and I learned something valuable every class period. He is great at giving historical context so you can better understand stories in the scriptures. There are frequent quizzes from the assigned readings bu they arent hard at all. He also provides a study guide to fill out while you listen to the lectures.

Tests seemed a little harder than they should be but if you knew the study guide super duper well you'd be fine. Lectures are interesting and inspiring. I learned a lot. Professor is very knowledgable and willing to help us understand. Random quizzes on the weekly scripture reading. Projects are easy- you'll get a good grade if u do the assignment.

BEST RELIGION PROFESSOR EVER. I learned so much about the Book of Mormon and I appreciated his unique perspectives on the doctrine. No homework except some easy readings before class. Tests are easy and you can choose the format you want to test in (MC or essay exam). He's super flexible and chill while still being spiritual and awesome!

I really liked this class and bro Frederick. He really focused more on the teaches rather than personal beliefs. He offers both a essay exam and multiple choice based on what you think you'll do better on. It's clear that his focus is on allowing his students to learn rather than making the class hard.

By far my favorite religion professor that I've had so far. Amazing lectures, and teaches great, inspirational things about the church. Has you think about and learn things you've never really stopped and considered before. You have both a multiple choice and essay option for the exams. I definitely recommend taking a class from him.

AMAZING PROFESSOR. By FAR my fave professor at BYU. Will take many more classes from him if I can. Class super easy but lectures are AMAZING, made me rly want to come to class. I learned so much + look at the BOM in a whole different way now. Super SUPER grateful I took this class. Exams all MC, no FR, and you can use scriptures. 1000/10 recommend

This has been without a doubt my favorite course I've taken at BYU. Brother Frederick captures the spirit of what BYU is about. He opened my mind to so many different ideas and his class was very provoking. He was very fair about grading and trust his students. I loved this class.

I personally did not like the way this professor taught. I was often confused and I feel he complicated the Book of Mormon to a point where I wasn't interested in learning about what he was saying because it was too complex.

Love Professor Frederick! Have taken 2 classes from him and both had very good lectures and easy reading quizzes. You can choose between a mult. choice midterm or essay. He respects everyone's thoughts and genuinely sees his class as something that shouldn't affect our GPA  but something that helps us spiritually.

I learned a lot in this class! His expectations were clear from the beginning and it is easy to succeed in his class. We read a new translation of the bible which was something I had never done in a religion class before

I loved this class! He did a great job at inviting the spirit into his lectures and I learned so much from him. Class time went by super fast every time. His tests can be a little confusing but if you fill out the study guides you should be fine

Second class from him because I love his lectures so much! Opened my eyes to the Mormon church and Mormon cultures, makes me rethink my religion, in a good way. prof strips the Mormon religion to the bare essentials, which allows students to regrow testimonies on their own. Lots of reading, but if you keep up then it's not that bad

Great class! He lets you know at the beginning of the semester that you can pick between writing essays or doing multiple choice for the exams, and he gives you the essay questions and a study guide to prepare. I did the essays, and they're open scripture and notes and I've gotten A's on both so far (there are three exams). he posts slides online!
Brother Fredrick is a solid teacher. I enjoyed the lectures and its a nice low stress class. Theres not an overwhelming amount of reading. Good guy, good teacher.

Awesome and easy class! He gives you the option of doing multiple choice or essay exams PLEASE trust me and take the essay exam, it's a LOT of writing but if you attend class, take notes, write down scriptures that back up the principles GUARANTEE 95-100% on exams! Only hw is reading in the BOM which can just be your personal study! Attend class!

He's a good guy, but his lectures weren't very interesting and I had a hard time paying attention. He posts a study guide at the beginning of each unit, so it's best to just fill the study guide out during the lectures. Tests are either essay or multiple choice (your choice) and they are open scripture.

I can confidently say Professor Fredrick has been my favorite religion teacher. His lectures always included historical and cultural background (which I feel is important to understand when delving into ancient scripture.) One thing to note however is that very few things go on your grade. Only 3 or 4 pop quizzes your exams and a final project.

Professor Frederick is one of my favorite religion teachers. He goes out of his way to make sure you aren't over-burdened by homework. Very open-minded and sensitive. If you absolutely the love the Church, are having questions about your faith, or are not a member at all -- doesn't matter. He's great. Light readings, final project (easy), 3 tests.
My personal favorite professor at BYU, I cannot wait to take another class from him in the future.

Dr. Frederick is a great professor! He teaches clearly, has simple and straightforward reading assignments, and his essay tests are easy A's. The only thing is that he doesn't really look at his students while he teaches, which can be a little weird, but overall, he teaches with love and respect, and I learned a lot from his class!
Amazing professor and best religion teacher I have had! His lectures are very insightful and I enjoyed going to class. Definitely plan on taking more classes from him.

Brother Frederick is incredible. Do yourself a favor and take his class. Reading assignments were never horribly long. Expect one pop quiz a week, which you'll want to do the reading for (but a deep read is not necessary). He offers a choice between multiple choice or essay for exams, and there's an easy semester project. Very spiritual lectures!

teaches to open your eyes to see the scriptures in a whole different way, not only teaching us about our religion, but WHY and HOW we believe these things. reading a lot on your own time, but reading is the only hw other than a end of semester project
Book of Mormon class is only okay. But taking New Testament the second half from him is amazing. That's his area of expertise and it's fabulous. Very academic class.

Professor Frederick is one of the best religion professors I've had. He offers two kinds of test, multiple choice (which is very focused on testing what details you remember from the lectures) or an essay question test (where the questions are based on general lecture concepts and your response is expected to be supported with lecture details).

I was super lucky to be in a small class of only about 15 students taught by Bro Frederick over Spring Term. I absolutely loved it! I took Teachings and Doctrines. He took the time to get to know each of us, provided multiple ideas and interpretations of each topic, and was super respectful our individuality. The essay exams are not very tricky!

I love this professor. His class is exactly what you want a religion credit to be. There are a couple major grades, a few more minor grades, and you learn so much. He is very inspirational, thought out, teaches things that you have never heard before, but doesn't overload you. Very managable work load. 10/10.

I'm not sure why a lot of the other ratings are so good. His tests are way too difficult for a religion class. Maybe these were put on before his class was on zoom, but lectures are not engaging and reviews sheets for the test are way to vague. Do the written tests!
His tests are way too hard. Makes you memorize scriptures but doesn't tell you which to memorize for the test. Good guy, but I wouldn't take his class.
Lectures are not very engaging and his tests are way too difficult for a religion class.

2nd time taking a class from him because it's what a religion should be. He is so knowledgeable about the material and so if you actually pay attention you will learn a lot. Tests are 70% of your grade but if you take the essay one it's way easy.
The final is 20% of your grade. If you do all the HW youll be fine. As far as a religion course, its still full of boring stuff but its not as hard as other courses.

Prof. Frederick is the best religion prof I'd had at BYU. Really cares about the subject and his students and does his best to help everyone succeed. Gives the option to take a multiple choice or essay version for every exam, so you can play to your strengths. Really helps you to understand the New Testament

He's a very good teacher and I learned a lot, the lectures are deep and informative. You are basically graded on the 3 exams, 3 essays (1 is dropped), and quizzes in class. Take the essay exams for sure, you will get a significantly higher grade on them and you will not have to study as much (but you will take 1.5+ hours on it) but it is worth it.

You are basically only graded by a quiz once a week, a final project, and the tests. The tests are 70% of your grade, so basically whatever you get on the test- you get in the class. He gives you the option of a multiple choice or an essay exam. He prepares you well with the study guide, but I still would spend around 2 hours on his written exams.

Not the most popular or exciting professor, but he is very knowledgeable, and he provides the resources to pass tests and the class. I enjoyed and looked forward to his class, and he is a solid backup if all your favorites get snagged. Easy project at the end to be done.

I find that BYU students are after three things when it comes to choosing the best religion professor: easy class, spiritual, and interesting lectures. Well this guy has all three! Do yourself a favor, and take this class. You won't stress, and you'll walk out of class feeling lifted.

Daily "yes/no" quiz about reading. Choice of MC or Essay exam (essays get better grades). Discussion based, but still clearly tests from PowerPoint concepts. Humble, genuine, super manageable homework: 2/3 completion type essays graded, reading quizzes, BoM project. This guy is a real gem. Totally recommend.

Brother Frederick is a really good teacher with a subtle sense of humor. Sometimes I got bored during lectures but overall it was a good class. Tests weren't too bad and the reading isn't too heavy. Just make sure to pay attention, keep up with the assigned readings, and you'll enjoy the class.

Participation: There are discussion boards in this online class which have to be revisited twice each week (your original post and responses to others have to be posted different days). Amazing lectures: the webinars are the only times we got to hear them, but Bro. Frederick's insights were really cool. LOTS of reading, but great topics!

I really enjoyed Bro Frederick's class. It's how I think Rel classes at BYU should be. Not too hard but makes you think about the gospel in a new way that strengthens your testimony. Weekly easy reading quizzes just to make sure you read, exams aren't bad at all if you take notes in class, and there are a couple of short papers that are not hard

He is a great teacher. He really helps you understand interesting things. I would take from him again. He allows access to all his slides to prepare for the test and you choose if you want to take multiple choice or essay. He prepares you and is good. There are a couple small quizzes on reading but they are not bad at all. Not hard but learn lots

Great professor. Pay good attention in class and you won't have any problem doing well. I did feel like he labelled a bit too much of his opinion as "truth," but that's really the only negative thing I can say about him.

Dr. Frederick is a great professor. He uses some non-LDS resources and references which shows the New Testament in action. It is nice to hear other gospel scholars interpretations. Exams had a MC or essay option. Essay questions you get in advance and can prepare responses. Some work required for the class, but easy A. Highly recommend.

Bro Frederick is a great prof! He knows so much about the Book of Mormon and is a very reasonable grader. His assignments are clear and he gives his students enough opportunities to receive an A. Tests aren't too bad and he gives you the slides from lectures to review along with a study guide.

Bro Fredericks has been my favorite religion professor. He is upfront about expectations and really reasonable about grading. There are no surprises with his assignments, and he's a respectful, fair guy who treats you like an adult and puts the responsibility for success in his class back in your hands. Just do the work and TAKE THE WRITTEN TESTS.

(Took during Summer). Bro Frederick organized his class super well. Everything was clearly laid out on LS & the syllabus. Now, I wouldn't say it's an "easy A" class - at least for me, but the workload is what makes it worth taking. Very reasonable and more Rel profs follow suit. It's the tests that basically determine your grade.

Really great professor. You're tested on his interpretation of the scriptures (as presented in the lectures), which could annoy you if you interpret the passages differently, but this isn't a problem if you approach class open-mindedly; don't abandon your own opinions, but respect, learn from, and study his. You'll learn SO much.

Best religion professor. His class is real, reasonable, and not too difficult. I notice other religion classes have a lot of useless busy work and readings, but his expectations are perfect in my opinion. He formats his class very fair, so you can take either essay exams or MC exams.

Prof. Frederick was awesome! He was so willing to work with me on my grade, even after the semester was over. He seemed to genuinely enjoy teaching and gives two different test formats (essay or multiple choice), which can be super helpful for students who learn/test differently. Do your reading and assignments and pay attention to study guides!

This guy is a winner. He makes getting an A really attainable, not with an easy class, but with options for students (extra credit, various exam formats, papers, etc.). He is a great guy. He would be great teacher especially for students who may be are more liberal, not that he is super political.

This is my favorite religion class I've ever taken. Frederick focused a lot on the historical background of the New Testament, which really helped me have a better picture for what is going on. I also felt like I got to know Paul as a person. He offers the tests in 2 formats, and if you do the essay exam, you get a better grade. 10/10

Frederick is an amazing teacher. He is super knowledgeable about the scriptures and is really passionate about what he is teaching. His tests are hard, but he gives the option of taking either essay or multiple choice tests so that you can do your best based on how you test best. He also gives extra credit opportunities. Would definitely recommend.
this guy is a genius. he know his stuff and gives super cool facts and the work load is very light. i enjoyed this class a lot

Listen up! He's great! He's willing to meet with you before and after a test to talk about it. Take advantage of that! It saved my grade! There are 2 forms of every test you can take. Take the essay. He gives you the essay questions before hand, so you know what to expect. Be specific, meet with him so you know what he wants. You can get an A!
Deep lectures, very spiritual and respected professor. Prepare to be enlightened and leave class feeling good.

Brother Frederick was an amazing teacher! He taught me doctrines that I thought I already knew, but taught them differently to help improve my learning. Very inspirational! He prepares you so well for the tests, and allows you to choose between an essay exam or multiple choice exam. I would definitely take his class again!
I've really enjoyed his class. You will learn MANY new things EVERY single class!
Posts all the slides online with stars next to the important stuff, but pretty tough tests

I loved his New Testament part 2 class! He is amazing at lecturing and I felt that the workload was light. You basically have to come to class and take great notes. His lecutures are very interesting and he has much more of an academic approach. I felt I really learned about the context of the New Testament. My favorite religion professor!

Frederick is by far the best religion professor that I have had at BYU. I've taken from all of the supposedly "best", but I was unimpressed. He's just a real guy that cares about his students and pays attention to students' questions. Most of your grade comes from the tests, but he offers a variety of extra credit opportunities and grading options.

This class just was not my favorite. It wasn't that it was too hard, because it wasn't, and he offers so many extra credit opportunities-if you put in the time you will definitely do well in this class. That being said, I did not learn anything about the Book of Mormon, or really even feel the Spirit in this class-it was rather disappointing!

Awesome teacher. Learned so much from him. I took a New Testament class from him previously and loved him so much I decided to take this one too. Teaches with the spirit and also teaches so you learn new things. Very straightforward from the beginning. Impossible not to get the grade you want becuase he gives you every opportunity to get it.

Frederick was a solid professor. He gives a lot of opportunities for you to have control over your grade, like extra projects and stuff you can do for extra credit. He's not looking to make you do busy work. He hand selects the assigned chapters because they're important, not because he wants you to suffer. He doesn't present his opinions as fact!
Would Recommend to anyone. Won't regret taking any religion classes from him. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. If you try you will get an A.

Prof. Frederick's teaching style is a little different from most, but I really liked it. This class gives new perspectives on the Book of Mormon you won't get in REL121-122. The lectures could be a little longwinded at times, but I was never particularly bored in class. The way your final grade is calculated is catered to you, which is really nice.

Definitely my favorite religion teacher at BYU. He explains very clearly what is expected and how you can get an A. If you are good at taking tests this is the professor for you. I did no busy work just took two midterms and a final. Tests are passable if you study and attend his class lectures, which are actually interesting and worth going to.

Super easy, as should be a religion class. You choose which assignments to do (if any). You could just take the tests and have that be your grade. Lots of extra credit opportunities. You choose your grade. Teaches in a very academic analysis of the scriptures.

Prof. Frederick is great! His religion class is a perfect mix of academic and spiritual. You basically earn the grade you are willing to put the work in for because of the way he has class set up! Lectures are amazing, organized, and well-though out! I learned so much about the Book of Mormon

Great class. Great spiritual humble guy. He always accepts comments and questions and knows how to make you feel like your comments are right. I would definitely recommend this class. Just do the reading

Not only was the class spiritually uplifting, but he makes sure you are getting what you really need . He provides a few different ways for him to weigh your grade, you can add unlimited extra credit on exams, and he pays attention to the important things in the class. He doesn't make you focus on minute things and really cares about the students.

I can't speak highly enough of him. Incredible professor. Not because he is nice or easy or spiritual, but because of how much he taught me about the doctrine of the BOM. I've read 2 ne 31 40 times (at least), but he BLEW my mind away on the day we discussed it. EVERY DAY is like that. And honestly if you know the main chapters of BOM it is easy.
SUPER easy grader. Honestly one of the easiest classes to pass as long as you go to class and do the reading that's assigned.

Frederick is great! I learned so much more from him than any other religion class.  If multiple choice tests arent your thing, he gives an essay option. I would suggest keeping up with the reading even if you think you know the Book of Mormon really well. Quizzes are on the reading and i never got less than 100 even when i just skimmed the reading.
Brother Frederick is great! He offers so many different options to help you in this class. Tests are tough but he offers an essay option. He is a great guy.

Best professor ever. Seriously someone needs to give this man a raise. I'll never see the new testament the same again. Professor Frederick made every lecture interesting and it was crazy how easy it was to stay engaged during class. He teaches perfectly. PERFECTLY! I will take every religion class he teaches if my schedule permits. A++++++++++

I loved this class. Bro. Frederick knows his stuff and will try to answer any question that comes up in class. This is a very intellectual class where I felt like you weren't getting the run around or going back to seminary where its was all about feeling good. Keep up on readings and take notes and it's not bad at all.

Brother Frederick is amazing!!! Such a great class. He is a very good lecturer, making it fun to listen. He leans more towards an academic approach to the New Testament but also incorporates applications for today in a very interesting way. He sees things a little differently, expanding my own perspective of the scriptures, the church, and life.

I actually really liked Brother Frederick's class. Lectures were long, but i took it spring 2015. The curriculum isn't all that interesting, but it was an easy A. He offers different grading options and you pick what you want. I wrote a paper for 9% back on my final exam. He's way chill, and gives good study guides.  I would do it again!

I have never once in my entire life wanted to skip one of Brother Frederick's classes. I learn so much in every single class. He always addresses questions in class (this can be annoying when there's the one girl who has a 15 minute comment every week) and really wants students to learn. I would take every single religion class from him if I could.

Dr. Frederick is a good guy and really knows his stuff, but his grading is rather harsh. If your not a good test taker, your going to struggle.  I studied a lot for the tests but still got Low B's, high C's. He weighs his test to 85% of your grade. He does however give an alternative to lower that to 40% if you complete journals(kinda of lengthy).
awesome teacher. he teaches really well.

-Great teacher, I would definitely recommend him! -Essays (Optional) 1pt. extra credit per page. -Journals (Optional) If done they lower the weight of your tests scores. --Gives a fantastic study guide. -Respects students and their ideas. -Quizzes are given in class so its important to go.  -Reading is optional (Recommended!).
Not my favorite teacher, easy though. Lectured are boring, very analytic. Least favorite class due to the lack of energy in his lectures.

Every religion professor at BYU should learn from this man.  Brother Frederick is clearly very interested in the material that he teaches.  He makes it interesting to his students.  His reading assignments are not mandatory and overly stressful.  He lays out on the first day of class the way to be successful.  Daily quizzes aren't hard.

You will not be sorry for taking Prof. Frederick. If you pay attention in class and read (reading the NT was my only homework), you will get an A. He gives you everything you need to know for the tests. I loved his teaching style. I recommend him without reservation!

The class was great, with a greater emphasis on historical and doctrinal aspects of the New Testament. Dr. Frederick is very intelligent and one of the most down-to-Earth professors I have seen. If you have a problem with something, come talk to him and he will find a way to make it work. His tests can be moderately challenging.
My favorite religion teacher at BYU. He understands the subject well and takes time to answer questions. Doesn't make religion class stressful. Highly recommend taking class from him.

Favorite teacher thus far. Understood what a religion class should be. No homework. Offers extra credit. Surprisingly funny. On the test the class average was lower than what he wanted so he just raised everyone's scores. Best teacher for religion!

Amazing professor! His class is that impossible combo: an easy A that you learn a ton in. It makes you sad passing the class is easy because you actually *want* to study for it. Engaging lecturer, makes the New Testament accessible and fascinating.

Easy exams! I have a greater appreciation for the New Testament taking from him. His approach to the subject was way I preferred to learn in. Has extra credit opportunities all throughout the semester in case you fall behind. I enjoyed his class.

At first I was intimidated and didn't know what to expect on tests, but they weren't too bad if you looked over the study guide. Super likable guy. His class focuses a lot more on the scholarly side of the NT and not as much as the "spiritual side" of things, but it was fun and not too hard. Leaves you in control of your grade with extra credit.
Awesome guy. Piece of cake class. Take him for whatever you can. He's wonderful. He sees religion courses as they should be- uplifting to attend but not a heavy work load since we have other courses.

This guy rocks! He seems formal on the exterior, but is witty and laid back. You can get whatever grade you want with extra credit opportunities. I learned a lot and enjoyed it. Plus, he looks like Dwight Schrute! I ask you, can you beat that combo?

This is how every religion course should be! Absolutely awesome teacher with a focus on learning the scriptures. Tests are easy. Class is fascinating and focused. He knows his stuff and is the best religion teacher. I wish I'd found him earlier to take more classes from him. You'll learn a lot and still not have to worry about your grades or GPA.

Bro. Frederick is an intelligent man. Your grade can either be solely exams (mc w/ sg) or half exams, half journal entries. Extra Credit: write an essay before the exam. Number of pages of the essay is how many percentage points extra you get on your exam grade. He is a 'names' guy, but not difficult. Class is always interesting and exams not bad.
He is a really cool guy. You know he is super intelligent. Really relaxed. He leaves your grade up to you. Explains concepts using modern examples. Nice guy, interesting class, easy grade. Just read.

This guy is unbelievably smart & so humble about it. His lectures were always enlightening and worthwhile. Tests are mc, but he lets you write an essay for each test if you want for xc. I never needed to write an essay & got an A in the class bc tests were always very fair. Go to class, take notes, do his study guide, and you'll get an A
great teacher, makes the grading quite easy and allows you to get the grade you want.  He knows a lot of good information and makes the class interesting, would recommend him

Great teacher! Easy class! The entire course consists of 3 tests no essays, no projects and the final wasn't comprehensive. Just look over the review before the test. He even reads the questions and answers to the test during class the day before the test. Really great class to take if you want to learn a lot and not have to worry about your grade!

Bro Frederick is a FANTASTIC teacher. his tests are ridiculously easy. if you pay attention and attend class it's hard to fail. his study guides cover exactly whats on the test. he answers any questions you have in depth and on top of that he looks like dwight shrute! you just can't get any better. TAKE ANY CLASS YOU CAN FROM BROTHER FREDERICK
Bro. Frederick did a great job teaching, I was in an RM book of mormon class even though i'm a freshman, it was a great experience though. He is a great teacher.

Hands down the best professor I have had in any subject at BYU. I would sign up for ANY class that he teaches. He is Clear, interesting, funny, straight forward and has great reviews. TAKE ANY CLASS YOU CAN FROM Bro. Frederick!

Hands down, the BEST religion teacher I've had at BYU. The tests are exactly what we've covered in class, so if you come to class they're easy. The essays are not mandatory, but they will help your grade if you write them. Every lecture is interesting and thought provoking and available as a powerpoint online.  I highly recommend taking his class.
Awesome professor. Extremely good at communicating ideas, and gives fair exams. You know what you need to study, and what the themes are. No tricks.

This class was intense! It covered a full year of introductory Latin in 7 weeks. I entered the class worried that it would kill me--especially since I've never studied a language before!--but Nick is an AMAZING teacher and he made everything really easy to understand. If he can make me understand a full year of Latin in 7 weeks, he can do anything.

I am quite impressed! He is so comical, but to the point where you can learn very well! Puts things in simple terms so you can understand them. Tests were worded a bit funny sometimes, but other than that, they were relatively easy. You can tell he really cares about the welfare of the students in his class.
Awesome teacher, he was very funny, but spiritual at the same time, and really helped me understand the book of mormon. He even looks like Dwight Schrute, which is a plus.
Bro. Frederick is a very pleasant, likable person.  He's knowledgeable and has a good sense of humor.  His tests are easy and fair, and he doesn't require too much work for the 2 credit hours.

AWESOME!Great teacher!Easy class its a good way to get your GE class done.Lots of reading but spark notes comes in handy.There is a quiz the beg of every class but they are easy and just test to see if you read.He also tells you what he is testing you on so tests are easy.He really loves teaching this subject and it shows.He doesnt try to trick you

Good teacher. There is a lot of reading for this class. The reading and attendance aren't required, but the class is hard if you don't. Only 3 take home quizes and 3 tests, all essay. Grades fairly easy and lectures won't put you to sleep.

The BEST religion teacher I have had at BYU so far.  He cares about the students and makes sure that a religion class is actually do-able, especially if you're not an RM or a member! He is hilarious and made every class enjoyable. He is also very intelligent and offers great insight on the New Testament. He looks like Dwight from "The Office"
i wasn't necessarily interested in the class. but he's a good teacher and way layed back, so that made the class much better

AWESOME! Take any class you can from him. He is such a good teacher. I never did any of the reading until about the day before the test. I skimmed the reading and went over his study guide & powerpoints. Not that hard to do well. Tests are completely essay, and I did really well on them. 3 papers, 3 quizzes, 3 tests. He is also way down to earth!

This class was very informative and interesting without pointless memorization.  Going to class is important.  Sometimes questions on tests were confusing because one or more of the multiple choice answers were said in class.  He wants everyone in the class to get an A.

He is a great teacher! He knows a lot about the subjects discussed and is very responsive to student input and questions. The tests are easy, but time-consuming b/c they are all written/essays. EVERYTHING on the tests is discussed in class, no tricky stuff - so make sure you go! PS - LOTS of reading.

He is SUPER smart. I learned SO much. His class was easy. If you go to lecture, take notes, read, and pay attention you can get A's on all the tests without any further studying. He was very lenient with dude dates. Great teacher!

Professor Clawson's class was amazing! She definitely knows her stuff and organizes her classes really effectively. The discussions in her class are super insightful and she is generally so smart, so caring, and so supportive. Yes, there are high expectations but she really walks you through each step and is willing to help when you need it.
VERY harsh grader. So many detailed assignments are added in her section that other sections don't have to worry about. Deducts great amount of points over journals for example. Workload is too much.
This is a review for ENGL 325 (Visual Comms). Deceivingly rigorous but grading is generous. Many unit assignments ended up being over 10 pages long.
Really nice, helpful, and a great class.

I didn't see a review for WRTG 316 from Dr. C so I'll post one. I loved WRTG 316 from Dr. C and if you need to take technical writing, you should try to take it from her. She's great at helping you get through the writing process or if you have questions. Assignments are clear and your given time to work on them. The class was also a lot of fun

Dr. C is amazing, by far the best writing professor I've had. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The assignments are challenging but really practical, and she structures the class to be useful for your future. She is also hilarious! If you put in the effort, you'll do well, and have a great time doing it!
Prof. Clawson is one of the best teachers I have ever had in my life.
She is such an amazing professor!! She was so understanding with all of her students. Her class genuinely made me a much better writer. Take this class from her!!

Amazing teacher. She will push you to grow and really learn the concepts you learn but she gives you so much time to work on them in class and always makes sure her class is a place of comfort. Love her. She changed the game for me. i would recommend her to anyone wanting to learn but also wanting an easy writing class.
Mrs. C is amazing. She is a great teacher and mother. She works so hard for us.

Take this class if you really want to understand technical writing. Though she says that she has removed a lot of the "fluff," don't let that deceive you. This class is tough and you will have a lot of work, but you will leave knowing everything you need to about technical writing. I would highly recommend Professor Clawson.

Everyone thinks prof C is a tough grader. She talks tough but if you just get the page count right and pretty much follow the directions you can write a bunch of crap and still get at least a high B if not an A on the assignment. Also I took this during Coronavirus so I stopped this class once I hit a C grade for a pass. She's also pretty funny

This class sucked. I officially found the worst class at BYU. So much busywork, she assumes we have nothing else going on in our lives and we have to give priority to her class because writing is SO important. So disorganized, most of the time I had no Idea what was going on. No clear grading criteria work your butt off and you still won't get an A

A literature review, a couple easy group assignments, and a presentation. Nothing bad or hard at all. NO TESTS. Only downside is that she is completely disorganized and you hardly ever have a clue about when to turn things in or how to, which could hurt you a ton.

Mrs. C has been one of my favorite professors at BYU. She really formulates the class around her students and what will benefit them most. The Lit Review is hard and time consuming, but she gives you plenty of help and is clear and fair with her grading. As long as you put in the work, you can definitely get an A. Take ENG316 from her!

Nicole Clawson is not your pioneer Utah Mormon. Yes, probably descended from pioneers. Yes, from Utah. Yes, Mormon. However, she has a refreshing perspective that makes class unique and enjoyable. Lectures are fun. They are more fun if she drinks Mountain Dew prior to/during class. She is really nice and getting an A should be expected.
She's a great teacher but does grade harsh. The class high is an A-. I would expect to not get higher if you take her class.

She is a great Professor. All through the semester she kept making the assignments applicable to our individual fields. She allowed us to choose the topics for our projects to keep us interested. She grades well, keeps class interesting with anecdotes, and teaches the material really well.

Really awesome. Despite being a Gen. Ed. she really expected us to learn things. She applied everything to the workplace, so you're actually learning writing skills that you will use, which is cool. She will grade you for real, but it isn't too bad if you do the work. If I had any other writing classes I'd take them from her.

I really enjoyed her class. I took it over the summer, so assignments were constantly due. Class periods, however, were catered to explaining and helping us with the homework assignments, and we had an occasional "work day" when we didn't have class. After the huge literature review was done, the rest of the class was a breeze. Just do the work.
Good teacher

Nicole was so incredible! She has been the only English professor I've had who gave me individual feedback and helped make difficult assignment seem achievable. I actually grew as a writer because of her class and my confidence in my writing sky rocketed because of her honest critique and personal assistance. She also has a great mob boss accent.

She's a great young teacher. I did enjoy her class. But she is a hard grader when it comes to the writing assignments. If you follow her criteria she will give you a good grade. The attendance policy in Writing 150 is bogus, if you miss more that 2 classes it will affect your grade.
Mrs. Clawson is an awesome teacher. She gives great feedback and will make you a better writer. She never spends the entire class lecturing and keeps students involved. My favorite teacher by far.

Nicole is awesome! She took a potentially very dry subject and class and jazzed it up so that I enjoyed being there every time. She cares about her students and is very accessible after class to meet with. I strongly recommend having her as a professor.

I would highly recommend taking from Mrs. C! She has a fun and young personality that makes her class an enjoyable place to be. She also organized the class well and everything that you are required to do is truly for your benefit, there's no busy work. That being said... THERE'S LOTS OF HOMEWORK. But you will become a confident writer because it!

If you don't enjoy writing, this is a great professor to take from. Class lectures are fun and engaging, feedback for writing is constructive and helpful, final is a presentation and short essay. Heavily graded on writing (rhetorical analysis, opinion editorial, Issues/Research Paper and multimodal project). Mrs. C is a great professor.

Mrs. Clawson is a very personable, brilliant and helpful professor. Her lectures are crystal clear, her grading criteria is clear, and unless you're a typical procrastinator you should get an A. The only reason I got a B is because I dropped the ball with some pretty crucial assignments and turned them in late.
She's a great professor who cares about her students. It is a ton of work but she makes it easy for you to do it.
Mrs. Clawson is amazing. Writing 150 sucks but she makes the class great. It's not the easiest class and does take some effort, but it is fun and I learned a lot.

Dr. Clawson is a really good teacher. Just make sure you thoroughly read the grading rubrics she gives you for the assignments as her in-class descriptions of what is expected are pretty vague.  Pretty easy class, just lots of busy work.

Writing is a subjective subject. Clawson likes gory metaphors and colorful similes. If you have a metaphor for murder in your piece, keep it. The book is available in the library. Don't get the book of essays. Google the one you need. Don't get the blue book either. Use owl Purdue. Not everything is on the syllabus.

Mrs. Clawson is great! If you're just trying to get through writing 150 then she is a great way to go.  She is always very helpful and open during her office hours so you can just bring your papers to her during those and she will offer great suggestions on how to improve them.  You don't have to take a whole lot of notes but should still attend.

Professor Lauper is amazing! She truly cares about her students and wants us to succeed. This course also is set up really well to introduce students to FCS. Don't worry about transportation to observations, she makes sure it works out.

Professor Lauper needs to be flooded with reviews only 5 star level. This woman is incredible and by far my favorite professor I have had at BYU. She knows her stuff, is organized and is an amazing teacher and professional. This class was so valuable in my trajectory in becoming a teacher as Nicole cuts out all the fluff and is so inspiring!!

Prof. Lauper is probably a nice person, but this was the worst class I have EVER taken at BYU. Love to sew, but *hated* this class. Spent 12-15hrs/week over the semester on homework. It was a nightmare & she was not flexible or helpful at all. I'm normally a very good student & felt like I tried my honest best, but was set up to fail. Do not take.

I love Professor Donahoo. You can tell she really cares about her students, and she is so helpful when it comes to not understanding a difficult subject. Easily one of the best professors I have ever had.

Professor Donahoo might be my favorite professor I've ever had! She was great at explaining concepts and answering questions. She also shared amazing spiritual thoughts and I could tell she cared about her students. The accounting jr core is hard, but I don't think there could be a better professor to teach auditing!

Professor Donahoo is amazing! I knew nothing about audit going into the semester, but the course was very well designed and even without taking notes and just skimming the textbook, I learned everything I needed to know in class. I found the test very easy as well if you just study the slides.

Audit is a tough class but Prof. Donahoo has the class organized in such a way that it makes it much simpler. Everything you need to know is in the lectures, and she makes sure to put any important information in the slides so students can access them for study outside of class. 

Great professor that made a tough class not so bad.
Phenomenal. Fantastic. Superb.

This was professor Donahoo's first semester teaching and she slayed. She loves Taylor Swift and Audit is hard ! It is not easy class and a lot of concepts you have to work on . A ton of quizzes . She was a great teacher and very inspiring spiritually. She is not teaching next semester ... Sad

This was professor Donahoo's first semester teaching and she did a fantastic job. Audit isn't the most exciting topic but she kept it interesting and engaging. She was a great teacher and explained difficult concepts very well. 10/10, would recommend.

Professor Lauper is amazing! She truly cares about her students and wants us to succeed. This course also is set up really well to introduce students to FCS. Don't worry about transportation to observations, she makes sure it works out.

It was a nightmare & she was not flexible or helpful at all. I'm normally a very good student & felt like I tried my honest best, but was set up to fail. Do not take.

For an online science class, it was very easy to do. However, it is a lot of work, so the workload is expected since we don't meet in person to do things like rock identifications, etc. Everything is open note, but don't just rely on the internet. Studying is super important in this class since some of the assignments are really hard.

I like Professor Ortiz and I can tell she cares about geology however I didn't find her teaching style to be helpful. Her assignments felt overcomplicated for no reason and there was a TON of busy work. Exams are open book but are still really, really complicated again, for no reason.

Almost all generals at BYU seem to try to prove a point by being harder then they really need to be, this class is no exception. There is a ton of seemingly busy work that is very tidous after. The tests are hard and take a chunk out of your day, even if they are open note. I would reccomend taking anything else really if you value your time.

For online, frankly there is a lot to do every week. It's not hard work but it's annoying after a while. The tests are actually a bit difficult and proctored, however, you have the book and basic google searches available. The final is just a paper so that was helpful. I think taking this was better than physical science but im not sure.

I really liked this professor. She was very caring and made accommodations when needed. She cared a lot about helping us learn the content. Homework was very manageable, I would finish the week's work on Wednesday or Thursday. Two tests and a short final paper. Highly recommend taking this course from her.

If you hate yourself take this class. The assignments are so monotonous and all you do is read pages and pages in the online textbook about rocks. The exams are open note but still pretty tough. Do yourself a favor and take anything but this class unless you want to learn useless information for hours on end.... :(

A pretty chill online class. You'll have a lot of readings, the majority of instruction is done through them, but you'll also have reading quizzes, weekly discussions, and activities. A reasonable workload. Prof. Ortiz is nice and always willing to help students that reach out, but there's not a lot of interaction with her otherwise.

This was my best experience with an online class. I think the bad reviews here are from students who were lazy and were looking for an easy A from an online class. Easy assignments, easy readings, it's all open book, note, and google. I would be done with the assignments by Wednesday. I didn't feel it was busy work, it was short/sweet/effective.

Sadly, this was one of the more unfulfilling classes I have taken at BYU, and I often take online classes. The workload seemed pretty heavy, and even on the last week of classes there were still quite a few assignments. Nicole seems nice but some things could be adjusted to give each assignment more purpose. As is, it felt like a lot of busy work.

While there is a lot to do, she makes the class structure very clear and organized. I enjoyed how she taught her class and found it very easy if you just put in 2-4 hours of work a week. There are also really fun Google Earth activities. I also liked the occasional spiritual overlap. Overall I enjoyed the course and I am a finance major.

I thought this course was challenging but very educational. There is a lot of work and sometimes it feels like busy work. The teacher didn't seem super knowledgeable about the subject. Her test reviews were scattered and she didn't seem like she knows what she is doing.

If you are going to take this class to fulfill a GE like I did - don't do it. I don't think her class is good for students who aren't geology majors. There are 2-3 quizzes, 1-2 homework assignments, discussion posts, and a reflection due each week. Her tests are open note but they are super hard. I would not recommend this class.

Prof. Ortiz is really kind. You could tell she really cares about the students well-being, and she wants them to succeed in the class. Classwork is pretty average, however, I had the hardest time with the tests! They are open book and open internet, but they were so hard for me. I did everything she suggested and still didn't get the best score.

This class was harder than it needed to be. There were lots of technical difficulties my semester that made it confusing. There's a lot to do each week, including busy work. The midterms are open book and open note but they are kind of massive and overwhelming. The professor was fine, she didn't make or break the class.

This was a really chill class. Weekly quizzes and geotours (with accompanying help videos) and Dr. Ortiz was available to meet via zoom. Not an easy A, but an achievable A. I was really nervous coming in that I would not do well because I am not a STEM major, but I did great. I am glad that I took this class for part of my Physical Science GE.

Easiest classes I have taken. Prof is always there to help and will hold review sessions that go through every GeoTour assignment and Rock Lab and sometimes she gives the answer to questions. I have to look at YouTube videos to help explain hard concepts sometimes, but it is a great course. If online classes aren't for you, probably don't take it.

Professor Knapp is super kind and knows her subject really well. She teaches things very clearly and is really understanding. The homework was very light and the tests were pretty easy, but I still felt I was actually learning. AMAZING professor, I highly, highly recommend taking any class you can from her. I loved her classes!

Prof. Knapp has been my favorite professor at BYU so far. She is really caring and makes you aware of exactly what you need to know for all of the tests and other assignments. She is also very compassionate and will be a lot easier on you at the beginning of the semester. If you review and understand the study guide then the tests will be a breeze
I love Profesora Knapp!  Seriously would take all my Spanish classes from her if I could.  Very helpful feedback, very understanding.  Span 322 with her has been great!
Dr. Y is seriously amazing. She offers test review every single class period, so don't miss it! Her tests are MC/3-4 essay questions, but she lays out the essay questions in class and during reviews.

Dr. Yamawaki is amazing! She's so kind and caring and her class was incredible. She taught so well, everything was thought-provoking. The tests really weren't that hard and I'm not a good test taker. She's absolutely worth it. I enjoyed every class we had.

Dr. Y was my absolute favorite professor at BYU. Her class changed the way I think about a lot of things. I have never been so excited about reading a textbook to attending class. My fiancee and I would literally read the textbook out loud together. She is a genius and knows what she's talking about when it comes to research. Go to test reviews!

Professor Yamawaki is very intelligent but has a hard time getting across what she means sometimes. You need to read the assigned chapters (there's quite a bit of reading) and go to the reviews, but overall the material isn't too hard. Dr. Yamawaki gives 4 tests and 1 group project, so you better do well on those big assignments.

So I couldn't understand her sometimes. Her English was fine but you really have to pay attention because the essay questions are from the lecture and they are very subtle sometimes. I found the class to be hard just because of that. Other than that it wasn't bad.

One of the worst teachers I've ever had. Her TA was also no help. I did end up with an A- in the class but that was after putting in a TON of work. Pay attention in class a lot because the TA is no help when it comes to in class material. She is only good at helping with the book and half the tests are over lecture material

Dr. Y is THE BEST! I loved her so much! She is super funny and willing to work with you and she just the sweetest person ever. I am so sad this is the only class I get to take from her. Best class I have ever taken at BYU.

Yamawaki is passionate and interesting. She cares about students and wants to make you look at the world in a different way. Go to class and do the readings and you'll do fine. She is fair and wants to help students that she can tell are trying. Yamawaki is hilarious too.

This was my favorite class this semester. Yamawaki is an entertaining and caring teacher. Her tests are difficult and require actually reading the textbook and taking notes in class. Gives study guides and emphasizes when something is important. 3 tests and a final, group project, extra credit. I looked forward to going to class.
Terrible class. Would never recommend the class to anyone. The exams are ridiculously hard. If you don't have to take the class, or if you can take it from someone else, avoid her at all costs!

This class requires that you actually do the reading from the textbook and attend class.  The MC part of the test is based on the reading and the essay is based on lecture, so both are necessary.  If you do both, you will do fine in the class.  Yamawaki is an entertaining teacher and her lectures are fun.  Occasionally she is hard to understand.

If you don't really have to take this class, then don't. It is the hardest class I have taken in my college career. The grading system is ridiculous, only 4 tests,a project,and extra credit. The textbook is disorganized and confusing, which makes the test even worse. The review sessions don't help because they aren't specific.DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!

Yamawaki's personality is funny and you will often enjoy her lectures. :) But, your grade is mostly base on exams (no quiz) and her exams are HARD. The avg is 80-84. The way she tests you requires you to take notes every waking minute during class. Take this class only if you don't mind getting a B.

This course is mainly based on your exams, but you have a project and extra credit to boost your grade. Dr. Yamawaki is a sweet, caring and understand professor. If she sees us struggling, she will help the class do better on the next exams. Make sure you go to the lecture, take good notes, and listen to her when she says something is important. :)

Her tests were ridiculous! She never said what we were supposed to know for the test in her lectures and then ended up asking obscure things that she maybe mentioned briefly in class. There is a huge language barrier and has a hard time explaining anything outside the 'official definition' DON'T TAKE HER AT ALL!!!

Very entertaining and interesting lectures but test items didn't make sense and test was hard. Essay is graded by TA so it depends on their knowledge. The thing I struggled with the most are the tests. Items are poorly written and doesn't cover knowledge you attain in class. She also LOVES stats so a lot of stats were incorporated which I hated!

She is a really nice and entertaining professor, but her lectures are unorganized and hard to follow. The tests contain multiple choice (questions come from textbook) and essay (questions come from random things she tells you in class and they are graded tough). I wasn't a big fan of the class and I wouldn't take it again or suggest it.
Fun class!!
I loved her! She is one of the best teachers!
Very helpful and fun. Has strict rules for grading, but not really difficult. Sometimes hard to understand what she is trying to get at (due to language barriers), but a great teacher. Take her!

I loved, loved, LOVED this class! But here's the thing: it's hard. You have to read the book, show up to class, and attend reviews. People don't do this and then complain, but if you do, it's a very manageable class, and very interesting and fun. Dr. Yamawaki is hilarious, and always willing to help students. Take this class!
She is so fun. As long as you go to class, read the chapter, and study for the tests you'll do great.
The tests are awful, not based on fact but the professors opinion.  Class is fun, but you don't learn much. She often rushes through lectures skipping valuable information.

I love Dr. Yamawaki, I have taken her classes and have been on her research team. She really cares about the material she is teaching. Her interest in students  and their well-being surpassed my expectation. I loved the class!
She is wonderful. Test is very hard, but if you study hard, you can get A. She is funny. The lecture makes me think.
Test was hard, but great class!
Dr. Yamawaki is fun and extremely helpful. LOVE LOVE LOVE her!

tests are challenging. She made class interesting and she got me excited to do research. She has a tough subject when teaching the gender class but she really makes you think. I enjoyed her very much. She has a heart of gold.
She tests nonsense just so she doesn't look bad.

The textbook was very interesting. I felt she was determined to be vague to the point of being ridiculous about what to expect for the tests. She's a very nice lady, but due to her language skills  it was difficult to understand what she wanted us to focus on and her lecture style is halting and disjointed. I wouldn't take the class from her.
She is funny.

Yamawaki is the best! She's so open to everyone's opinions. The tests do require you to read the chapters carefully, but it's not that bad. Her class is totally worth taking despite the ambigious multiple choice tests.

The class was fun, but not very good if you're interested in anything other than stereotypes you already know.  I found the tests tricky and not very representative of what had been learned.  What makes that frustrating is that your grade is almost entirely dependent upon these standardized tests.

She is fun, keeps your interest, makes you laugh each class and is very frank.  I loved every lecture, and the reading is interesting.  The only bad thing is that I feel the tests are very poor demonstrations of what you've learned.  But she's very helpful.  The group projects are fun.  There are 4 tests & 1 group project, that's your entire grade.

Fun lectures and nice lady, but tests are really really hard.  Its like she picked the most random questions from the book so its almost impossible to study for them.  Also, the questions are ambiguous so its even harder.  Be very very careful taking her because grades are based on the tests.
Horrible class! Ya she's kinda funny but that doesn't help you on the tests!

She makes the class fun, and she is a very cute lady. She is very helpful and approachable and willing to help in any way. The class itself was not terribly enlightening. I didn't really learn much new, but it was a good experience overall.

She is so funny! I had a hard time understanding her half of the time, but it didn't matter anyway because she doesn't test from her lecture. The tests were pretty tough, but I heard it all depends on the TA (they provide a study guide). Mine sucked and it wasn't worth my while to even look at the study guide because it only helped out with 2 quest

I thought this class was so fun.  The book is pretty feminist but it made class discussions pretty entertaining.  The test comes from the book's questions bank.  I've heard she's terrified of tadpoles.

Dr. Yamawaki is a wonderful teacher. Anyone who doesn't like her probably never comes to class! She will answer any questions you have and she always gets back to you very quickly.  I learned so much in her class! I wish she thought more classes!
great teacher!
Dr. Yamawaki is a great teacher.  Tests are difficult, but I have learned so much from her.

Terrible teacher.  Does not know the subject herself - why does she think she can teach someone else?  Avoid at all costs.  There are a number of other more qualified and intelligent professors to take 220, 306, and 320 from.  FYI pish-et = Piaget.  "Any questions? no? grreaaaat."
The class is very fun and interesting.  She is the best teacher!!

Very easy, uninteresting class, but she made it as interesting as she could. She's such a sweet and strong woman- I really liked her.  It's true though, the accent gets in the way just a bit. FYI, "correration"= correlation.

If you can tolerate the word "genitaria" (genitalia), then you'll do just fine.  Go to class if only for the massive debates that are pretty funny.  Oh, she doesn't like it when you're neutral, so be loud and proud about everything.

I've had her for three psychology classes.  Tests are from the book mostly, the essay questions are from the class. She gives you the answers to the essay questions and they aren't in the book. Make sure you go to class to get the answers to the essay questions!!!!
Dr. Yamawaki is a great teacher!! I just love her.
Dr. Yamawaki is extremely helpful and funny teacher.  Focus on reading the text, power point and study guide.  Extra credit saved me. Group presentation was an easy assignment, but it was fun.
really funny and entertaining! Read the book, view the powerpoints, do well on the presentation.

She is so funny to watch! She really gets into her lectures. Her tests aren't so bad either, if you do the work and the reading then you will do fine in this class. I love her personality. Extra credit is very helpful.
She is very helpful.  Interesting lecture.
read the book, use the CD that comes with it, the tests are all multiple choice with very specific answers.  The class is kind of boring cand dry but hey, you win some you lose some.
Great lady, very nice. Test were ambiguious but OK.

Prof Gardner made this a very straightforward religion class. There were short readings before class with easy in-class reading quizzes, and the slides and lecture were easy to follow. I appreciated that he did not make arbitrary or unnecessarily difficult tests and projects just to fill time. Quick, easy, & uplifting religion credit

Respectfully, not the teacher for me. He claimed that this was the easiest religion class- and he was right. However, I am not a fan of religion teachers being closedminded about other perspectives or questions. Some students had questions and they were brushed off. Also I never thought I'd hear the term "anti-mormon" so many times in a class.

Brother Gardner is the most kind loving guy! He really cares about his students and wants to see everyone learn and succeed. As long as you did the readings, went to class, and the few assignments the class is very doable to get an A in which I loved because I was able to actually focus and prioritize learning and strengthening my testimony. 10/10.

This class was difficult for me to stay engaged in, and I felt I didn't learn as much as I have in other religion courses at BYU. Much of the class time seemed centered on reading directly from slides, which made it harder to stay involved. Incorporating more discussion could make the class more engaging and impactful. AVOID HIM!

Bro Gardner is the best religion professor. I've taken multiple of his classes and he provides a good ballance of learning without it being hard to get an A in his class. He genuinly loves all of his students and does a great job.
Such a nice guy! Easy A and I feel like I got something out of it! Take it from him!

He takes pride in making his class easy, but it ended up feeling pretty boring for a college-level course.
