It's one thing for a religion class not to be super hard, but it's another to take a class and feel like you aren't gaining any new perspectives on the gospel. His humor also felt dry and didn't add to the class experience.
Open note exams online. Very chill lectures. Attendance is mandatory but you can miss 2-3 times without much effect on your grade. Highly recommend if you have other tough classes in your semester.

Bottom line is: If you want almost a guaranteed good grade in a religious course this is the professor for you. The assignments, projects, and midterm exams are incredibly easy. However, the professor is dull, unengaging, and dry. Attendance is required, so it's hard to take the class seriously when your grade is being held hostage.

This class is extremely basic, and I wish I had never added it to my schedule. It's boring, lacks depth, and often feels awkward. The professor's sense of humor is odd and doesn't really work. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone. Look for a different professor who will actually make your time and money worth it.

Super easy class. Lectures were actually interesting. Exams are open note and the study guide basically gives you the answers. In class quizzes every lecture to make sure you did the readings but they are short and easy. If you need an easy religion class, this is the one.

Very easy religion course. All you have to do is show up to class and take the quiz, there are a few readings outside of class but super short. Almost no homework, all exams are open note. There is one essay but it's graded easy and very short. Bro Gardner teaches well and knows his stuff! His classes are interesting and it is so easy to get an A.

Professor Gardner is super awesome! He shares lots of cool experiences, and you can tell that he loves what he teaches. This class has basically no homework outside of class and two total projects that take barely any time. The exams are all open-note and lectures, so it's hard not to do well.

I felt uncomfortable with his jokes throughout the class. I expected an uplifting experience, but the course was mostly centered on him and his humor. It relied heavily on PowerPoint with very little discussion, making it feel like a one-sided lecture focused on his voice rather than student engagement.

This class felt like a poorly run Sunday school experience. The course was superficial, offering very little depth, and the environment made it difficult to take the class seriously. I would strongly recommend avoiding this class.
Professor Gardner was an amazing religion teacher. I would highly recommend. I looked forward to showing up to class each day. He made lecture fun and entertaining. Tests were very easy.
Super chill guy. Very light religion class - no paper, just a little group presentation and a “project.” Open note tests. You have to go to class cause there are attendance quizzes.
Not uplifting, boring and very uncomfortable.

The easiest religion class I've ever taken, and I still felt the Spirit and learned a ton! There's two open-slide midterms, and all the answers are in the slides. Two projects, but the group one is easy and you can work on the other one in class. Attendance quizzes are easy, but necessary. He's also so kind and knowledgeable. I'd highly recommend!
The class was not engaging, and I didn't learn as much as I have in other religion courses. I don't plan to take another class from him.

Professor Gardner is my favorite religion professor (so far) at BYU! Every single lecture feels like a devotional. He is so honest and faithful about hard topics in church history. I was surprised by how much I learned! There's a short quiz each class about the assigned readings, one 6-page paper, and 2 exams. I highly recommend him!

This is probably my favorite religion class I've taken at BYU! You could tell how much Brother Gardner cares about his students. I thought the lectures were fascinating and inspirational. I've never said this about a religion project before, but I really loved the gospel topics project, and thought it was really helpful and insightful for our life.

GET NORM! He loves what he teaches and you can feel is love for the restoration in his lectures. There is barely any homework and the midterm was the easiest thing ive ever done. He just wanted to create a space where we could ask the hard questions about church history and he was so good at answering the questions everyone had. He was incredible.

Brother Gardner is a quieter lecturer, but the experience and viewpoints he brings to the table are diverse and interesting. His focus is on your spiritual growth, not a grade. This is not a class you'll stress about.
"I don't like to call it a final exam, because that makes everyone have an empty feeling. In their soul." 
-Bro. Gardner

This is by far the worst religion class I've taken. Avoid this professor. The material wasn't inspiring or engaging, and he isn't funny. He comes across as awkward, and the lectures are dull. Too many readings!

I've been in this class over the summer, and honestly, I've hated every minute of it. The professor isn't approachable and keeps trying to be funny, but it just comes off as forced and awkward. Not my favorite professor at BYU by far. The whole vibe is uncomfortable, and his assignments are honestly just lame.
Not the best class. He was nice but not great. I had a hard time feeling the spirit and didn't get much out of the course. Lots of readings and too many slides for a religion class.

Not a fun class. He was not the best religion professor, nor my favorite religion class. In fact, it was the worst. I would not recommend it. If you like a professor who is on a high pedestal, then go for it; otherwise, find a teacher who is reachable and personable. I was not uplifted in this class. It was superficial and boring.

Such a good teacher that made it clear he cared more about us actually learning than just giving us a grade. It was the easiest class I have ever taken, you just had to show up to take reading quizzes every class and do three projects across the semester.

I really loved this class! Super easy to get a good grade because he cares more about your testimony than the grade itself. Was very open about what was on the exams and makes meaningful projects that I  will apply throughout my life. I would definitely take this class if you are looking to learn and make a good grade.
Don't take this class! Look for someone who is better prepared and not just trying to be funny.

I have no idea why people are rating Dr. Gardner poorly, he was awesome! His classes were spiritual, and most importantly, his class was REALLY manageable. It would be almost impossible to fail his class. Attendance is required, but there were quite a few days when I wasn't able to make it and I still easily got an A. Best religion class ever!
I did not like this class. It was confusing and his teaching style was not my favorite. Find a more engaging professor. He loves talking in his lectures and you will have to fight to stay awake.

He is super nice and caring! I loved how the class is focused on spiritual growth rather than deep doctrine. I learned a lot about the prophet and apostles. There are attendance quizzes that require reading but they're easy. A midterm and a final, and the final is open note. Both are easy. Three easy projects. Lots of discussion during class.
I was really bored in this class. He seems like a nice guy, but it wasn't like most of my other religion classes. SO MANY slides!!! Not enough discussions. Get ready to listen to him talk.
This was not my favorite class. I don't recommend him. He often gets off topic, and I did not feel like I was learning new things. Find a different class.
Spiritually uplifting, just like a religion class should be. Unless you go out of your way to try not to, you will get an A in this class.
I was bored out of my mind. Not my humor and felt basic.
Professor Gardner is the best! Such a great class that facilitated the spirit in way that was beneficial for me. The assignments were very manageable and tests weren't bad at all.

Professor Gardner is great for an easy credit for foundations. I love that he gave us the questions and answers for the exams + open note! No stress test taking was great for me. I learned a lot but he is hard to pay attention to. Sometimes you tune out because he can be kinda boring. Low stress but also not my favorite faith professor.

Really chill and easy class - not much homework at all just an attendance quiz each day but he drops four. Can come off as condescending at times and not the most engaging lectures but overall worth it for how low stress the class is

Really knows his stuff and is not afraid to dig into the hard things. Gives as few assignments as possible. He's not the most engaging lecturer, but it's easy to follow and the presentation is well made.

This class felt more like a seminary class than a college-level course, which didn't meet my expectations for a BYU religion class. I didn't feel a strong connection with the professor, and at times it seemed like he looked down on students. I wouldn't recommend it to others looking for a more academically engaging environment.

Homework was 30-60 minutes of reading before class, and 2 short papers throughout the semester. Only 2 tests that are super simple and open-note. He has attendance quizzes, but a few of them are dropped. He really tries to make life easier for his students. Brother Gardner prioritizes inviting the Holy Ghost more than busywork or tough grading.

Literally take it from him. Super chill guy and genuinely cares about you. Homework was non existent other than 2 easy papers throughout the semester. In person quizzes each class but as long as you have common sense and read the readings before class you are set.

Genuinely the best. He understands that, as students, we do not learn through homework assignments. Exams are open notes; we can refer to all class slides. He learned all the students' names before the first day of class! Just the sweetest guy, and he knows what he's talking about. Takes all questions and answers them sensitively yet profoundly.

Brother Gardner has a wonderful background in uncovering and answering hard questions in church history. He dissected issues in a way that was never stressful. All tests were online and straightforward; he took care to make sure that this wasn't a hard class, but that you came away with increased confidence in your understanding of the restoration.

Professor Gardner was AWESOME. He's an expert in his field and is very enthusiastic about sharing his expertise and knowledge. The lectures were interesting, and it was not difficult to get a good grade as long as you showed up to class.

Brother Gardner is absolutely amazing! The lectures were always so full of the Spirit, curriculum is well constructed, and he has a lot of insider knowledge to share because he helped write the institute manuals! There are two tests, super easy open note. He cares so much, is so kind & accommodating! Would definitely recommend, I loved his class!
Brother Gardner is amazing! He cares so much about what he is teaching and about his students. I would definitely recommend his classes!

I loved him! Very engaging content, he's very knowledgeable. He makes the class focused on learning about the gospel, not on doing homework or getting a good grade. I would definitely recommend it for anyone.
He's chill
One of the best religion professors at BYU.

I loved Bro. Gardner's class! He has awesome spirit filled lectures and is super knowledgeable and friendly. The actual class is very easy. You just do the readings and then there are in class reading/attendance quizzes which are really straight forward. There are two short, simple essays. Easy, fun class that will help you grow spiritually!

Brother Gardner is so caring and makes each lecture enjoyable. He understands as students that we have other classes and makes sure not to overload us with homework. I took him during the winter semester and in the class we had two papers to write, attendance quizzes in the beginning of each class, and the exams are pretty simple. Amazing teacher!

He is the best religion professor you could have at byu. He knows how busy students are and so his classes are to be enjoyed without extra stress. There's no busy work but the assignments you have are interesting and simple. 10/10

This class was amazing. Even though the content was based on the history of the church Brother Gardner was really good at being guided by the spirit to make all of his lectures applicable to his students today. he is super caring. The few assignments and tests were REALLY easy:)  attendance required but he drops 4.

Professor Gardner is literally the greatest Religion professor I have had at BYU. His class is focused on learning the gospel and feeling the spirit. There is pretty much no homework, and all the exams are super easy. If you want to learn church history without the stress of mid-terms and busy work, then take this class.
He grades really easy.

This class was probably the easiest religion class I have taken at BYU. The only things that took some time were the projects, but they are very straight forward and simple. The exams were open note and his slides had all of the answers. This class was spiritually uplifting and easy - the way it should be. Take this class from him!

Brother Gardner is a phenomenal professor. He cares deeply about his students and does a lot to make class an enjoyable experience. He is kind, considerate, and sincere. Taking his class added value to my life.

Professor Gardner is awesome! In the Living Prophets he makes things super low stress and is really understanding of what its like to be a stressed out student, so would often make accommodations to help us out. He does do reading and a few big projects but they're way easy. He really wants us to not be stressed out.

Brother Gardner is AMAZING! I wish all religion courses were like this! He is wonderful at creating a spirit filled experience, shows genuine concern and love for his students, and helps you learn. There is a password based quiz for attendance, but you have basically 4 allowed absences. There were a few projects, but they genuinely add value.
Homework and exams are super easy, he's super understanding and really funny. I would take him again any day.

Dr. Gardner is amazing and his class is very attainable to get an A in. He makes living prophets so interesting and is so passionate. His projects are very practical, which makes the class enjoyable. The projects are always designed to help you strengthen your testimony. You won't regret taking his class.

Highly recommend taking Living Prophets from Norm. Super easy to get an A, and you will learn a lot from him. He has a lot of cool stories from working at church HQ that he shares throughout the semester.
The best, most understanding professor! The course was fairly easy, but attendance is mandatory.
Great guy. Take his class

Bro Gardner is the Goat. Awesome class. We only had one exam (a midterm) and two projects to which he was super lenient. He was kind and I turned my midterm and both projects in late and got full credit. Good person and interesting lectures.

Brother Gardner is awesome. He is focused more on his students feeling the spirit and being uplifted than making it an unnecessarily rigorous course. There were a few assingments but none were too difficult. Attendance is required, but he is also very willing to work with you. All around just a great stress free, uplifting, and enjoyable class.

Brother Gardner is awesome! His lectures are always so spiritual and he really shows that he cares about his class. There is reading and in-class quizzes each class period, but they're super easy. There were a few projects but they were very simple and doable. His exams are pretty easy and straightforward. I highly recommend taking this class!
He is an awesome professor and really helped me want to go to class. Take him if you want an easy but inspiring religion class.
Brother Gardner is an extremely dedicated and kind instructor. The homework isn't work heavy and he is considerate of your time and late work.

Brother Gardner is a phenomenal professor and truly cares about his students. Not a difficult class, by design. The assignments he gave us were very clear, reasonable, generous in grading, and actually effective.
I've never written a review but he is awesome. Genuinely just cares about the students.

Amazing religion class. He sticks to the doctrine and has a lot to offer as a professor. Only 3 big projects/ assignments and they were very reasonable and actually informative. Midterm and final were both very straightforward and manageable. Highly highly recommend Bro Gardner for this course!
Amazing professor! Funny, great lectures, and willing to work with his students.

Norm is the best. Attendance is mandatory but you get 4 free misses throughout the semester. 1 Midterm, 3 easy projects, that's basically the whole class. Exams are open note. Chances for extra credit too. if you need another religion class TAKE IT FROM NORM!

Super great professor!! Absolutely recommend taking any class you can from him! He doesn't believe in busy-work that doesn't actually help, so his course is set up for the most learning but isn't hard at all.
Super easy take it from this guy lots of spiritual experience in this class
I loved this class! Brother Gardner was so kind and the class was very easy!
Brother Gardner is the best! Loved this class
TRUST ME, take this class from Prof. Gardner! He's very kind and understanding and it's not hard at all to get an A. There's one group project but it's easy.

Gardner is the best! He clearly knows his stuff and gets excited talking about church history and the restoration. I didn't know someone could talk about that stuff and make it not boring. A couple chapters for reading before class, reading quiz each class, and like 2 other assignments during the semester make it a very chill class.
Bro Gardner is awesome, knowledgeable, and very spiritual. It would genuinely be difficult to do poorly in this class.

I love Professor Gardner! He was very lenient in class and would practically give you the answer. He is also lenient on the midterm and final. He is such an awesome guy and you could tell that he cares about his students. Make sure you do the extra credit! It is super easy and boosts your grade a ton.
Professor Gardner really cares for his students! His lectures were inspiring and he really knows his stuff about church history! Coursework was easy!

This man is amazing!! Definitely take this course. He explains things very very well and gives his students so many resources for answers to their questions. He's always offering extra credit and he is very kind. He has helped with the Gospel Library app and helped write the Institute Manuals. Also taught at U of A Institute.

I loved Brother Gardner! He loves what he teaches which makes the class interesting. All of the assignments were pretty simple and graded very lightly. He truly cares about his students and their success.
He's a great professor! I would highly recommend him. As long as you do the readings, the quizzes are easy and the essays were graded very easily.

This class was most definitely my favorite this semester! Brother Gardner knows so much about the topic he is teaching which allows him to be more adaptable within lectures and make class so fun/entertaining! There are quizzes at the beginning of each class, but if you do the reading you are all good. I highly recommend taking this class from him!

This was one of the best religion classes I have taken. Brother Gardner did a wonderful job teaching the class. It was his first semester teaching at BYU but has more than 2 decades of experience teaching institute. I can't recommend him enough. I hope to take another one of his classes in the future.

Professor Gardner was an amazing teacher and I absolutely loved coming to his class every week. The classwork was very little, only some pre-readings every class and a couple short papers. He did everything he could to make sure we had a spiritual growth and understood what we discussed in class. I would love to take another class with him.

Professor Garner is so awesome. He loves what he teaches and is always open to questions and helping you to find answers the correct way. He provides extra credit opportunities and the exams are open note!
So easy and nice! Informative at the same time too :)

This class was great. My testimony grew so much, if you are planning on going aim a mission and want to develop your testimony of Joseph Smith take this class! Brother Gardener really cares and puts effort into the lesson. He answers questions and wants to help you. He is so understanding.

He was a great teacher! He's passionate and caring and wants us to do good and learn about Jesus Christ. He wouldn't put a final in unless BYU forced him to put one in. He just wants us to know that we are loved and he wants us to use the class to strengthen our testimonies and learn how to find answers for questions. :)

Brother Gardner is an amazing professor. His class is the best class I've ever taken at BYU. He only had a few assignments and the 1 midterm and the final were open note. He cares more about helping your testimony grow instead of testing your ability to memorize information.

He is a knowledgeable and passionate teacher! I learned some great things about the restauration and gained perspective on answering gospel questions. The quizzes every class weren't too bad, especially if you did the reading. He told us the questions that would be on the tests beforehand, so it was easy to be prepared for tests.

I absolutely love Professor Gardner for his love of the subject matter and the sheer depth of his knowledge. He would cover very difficult church history topics in a thoughtful way and was very good at responding to any questions students might have. Class was super easy, yet interesting.

Brother Gardner is the best ever! He is soooo nice and super knowledgable. I felt the spirit every class and my testimony in the Restoration has definitely grown. the work load is super easy which is amazing because you can actually focus on the most important stuff. He always linked things back to Jesus Christ. Please take this class from him!

10/10 would take this class again. He lectures every class, but he is funny, caring, and knows how to teach with power. He handled controversial church topics very well. Both midterm and final were open note and online. Only 2 easy papers. 3 question reading quizzes at the start of every class. TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM

He is an excellent teacher. He is so willing to help all of his students, and he makes it very easy to get an A in his class. 
All tests and exams have been open note. Each lecture would have maybe 30 minutes of reading to complete in advance. There was a easy 3 question quiz at the beginning of each class. 
Definitely take his class.
Professor Gardener is an amazing professor who is here to increase his students' testimony and confidence in the restored gospel. He does as much as he can to get every student a good grade.

Incredible professor. Class has a few assignments that are not graded harshly, the main focus is learning truth and doctrine. The readings are much lighter than other religion classes yet still have all the content you need. My favorite religion class at BYU, 10/10 take this class from him and no one else.

Class is well organized and super easy. Great class to take for a religion credit during a hard semester because this class offers almost zero additional work. Fun and caring teacher who understands the content he is teaching.

Brother Gardner is awesome! He is very inspiring, and you always leave his class wanting to know more. He gives readings for every class but can easily be read or listened to in a few minutes. I learned a ton in this class, and my testimony grew even more!

I created this account just to review Professor Gardner. He creates a stress-free, supportive environment with engaging lectures on church history. The assignments are meaningful, not busy work, and the final is open note/slides. He's very accommodating and helped me when I traveled this semester. Highly recommend!

If you're looking for a meaningful but easy religion class take this one. There is only one test that's open note and on learning suite and only two big projects that take time but aren't hard. Gardner's lectures were always super meaningful and you can tell he cares and prays for the students in his class.

His class is super easy and it's hard to fail his class. He has an attendance quiz with a password before class and are allowed to miss 2 classes. Overall all the projects, assignments, and homework are not hard at all.
such an easy class, meaningful projects yet easy grader. Final exam was open note and open slide

Norm is a great guy and a great teacher! He loves the things he teaches about and is very knowledgeable. If you stay on top of it and are aware of whats going on in class, you will get an A. Fun class!

Super nice professor, cares for the students a lot. Has a lot of passion for the topics he teaches, which is interesting and engaging. Not a hard course as long as you stay on top of the homework and start early on the projects he gives you.

I LOVED this course and the way professor Gardner approached teaching. He is very knowledgeable and kind towards all students. Has a strong testimony and doesn't want anyone to go unnoticed. Quizzes for attendance are easy if you do the readings. Not a hard course and very spiritually/intellectually enlarging. Take religion from him!!
Professor Gardner was kind, caring, and a great teacher! His lectures were entertaining and he did not force participation. I enjoyed his lectures and I loved his slideshows.

Brother Gardner is super awesome and caring! Living Prophets is super well taught and he does a great job with his lectures. There is attendance quizzes for each period, but they are easy. Extra credit is available.
Great professor! Loved his lectures and the way the class is open to discussion and solving problems.

Seems like he thinks everything he says is the most profound thing ever, and will often disregard students' contributions to discussions after asking for the class's thoughts. Readings and corresponding quizzes are pointless, test is easy if you do the study guide. I can't stand his lecture style, and it feels like I have not learned anything
He says some questionable things. There is a lot of reading and it's pretty fast paced, but the tests are easy if you use the study guide. I'm glad I got to take a class from him before he retired.

I would not suggest taking a class from Professor Parry. Going into office hours he was very kind, but in lectures he says at least one wildly innapropriate thing a week. He also is very political and insists his side is correct and if your beliefs contradict to his, your thoughts are incorrect and bad. So much reading as well and he goes off topic

Homework load varied, sometimes only looking at a painting before class, sometimes reading half a book. The reading would cover several hundred pages, then he would assign a response question in class about an incredibly small detail within the reading. Gave us only a few minutes and wanted a deep, in depth response. Would go on political rants.

I know recent ratings are based on an incident from class, but to speak more generally this class had attendance questions every class that were graded pretty harshly & graded on a software that costs $30. Long readings before class but its Humanities so I expected that. Easy tests but they don't count for much of your grade and a big final paper.

Dr Parry was a fun professor to take a class from. He brought a different perspective to the way I saw the Humanities and I loved every lecture I was able to attend. He has his flaws, we all do and I am sad that people come here under the cover of anonymity to defame and complain about him because his opinions differ from yours. Please Do Better.

Dr. P is genuine & funny. His whole mission is to develop wisdom, compassion, & understanding. I learned a lot & as long as you listen to the lectures & do a little prep work outside class, you'll be good. Everyone has their own opinion, so don't get offended cause we're adults in college now. Let's just be kind. He's a great guy

People be crying too much, he is not a bad professor. There was one specific incident he apologized for and it was sincere. People get offended when you disagree with them. Ignore some of the latest ratings.

As mentioned in other reviews, Dr. Parry cancelled class 3 weeks before the end of the year, due to a huge negative response to his lectures. He is very tangential, and often talks about things that don't have to do with the class. There is a LOT of reading, 3 exams, and a paper. He also requires a $30 software to answer participation questions...

Class was cancelled 4 weeks before the end of the semester due to complaints from students. Professor went on long religious and political tangents and was disrespectful to those who believed differently. Besides that, you'll answer an attendance question every class that is graded harshly, have 2 fairly easy exams, 4 textbooks, and a final paper.

Coursework is fair, but lectures are often derailed by personal commentary. Parry makes concerning remarks about women, minorities, and Christians that many students find inappropriate, creating an uncomfortable environment and distracting from learning. If you dislike left-wing politics in a non-political setting, look for a different professor!

Dr. Parry is incredibly kind and loves to have discussions in class. He can get a little lecture heavy, but he is one of the most caring profs I've had. He will always make time to meet with you and answer your questions and loves tying in current events or pop culture into the humanities. Really recommend.

He sounds like Thomas S. Monson and so when he says words like "sexy" it's hilarious
LOTS of reading, lots of memorization, doesn't give out study guide very far in advance. 
Start the final assignment early, its 3 papers. Class is always available on zoom so that was awesome. 
He was very accommodating and kind!

I was worried about the workload because of all the reading. However, Dr. Parry's lectures give you all the info you need, despite the hard texts. You are basically graded by exams that he gives you questions to in advance, three papers due at the end of the semester, and attendance points. Would take again for sure. He's a homie fr.

I did not feel like these ratings adequately prepared me for what to expect from Dr. Parry. I kept a running list of the wild, inappropriate, and disrespectful things he said in class. The class was an easy A and Dr. Parry is a nice guy, but I think many students left the class totally disinterested in taking a class in the humanities again.

Dr. Parry is a very nice man who clearly wants his students to succeed. His class has a ton of readings. Attendance at lectures is mandatory. His lectures can be boring, and he tends to ramble a lot, but he also practically gives you the test beforehand so it is worth it.

ok I saw these ratings and was scared to take this class. This is the BEST ihum 202 class I have seen and taken. I have heard of these classes being super hard, and time consuming as it covers 2 generals. It can be boring, but there is a zoom for class and he prepares you well for the tests...you just fill in the study guide. BEST CHOICE

Professor Parry is by far one of the best humanities professors I have had at BYU. If you are looking for a class that will be an easy A, this class would not guarantee that, however Doctor Parry will give you every resource to help you succeed in his class. He is extremely easy to reach out to and meet with and is extremely helpful in office hours

Professor Parry is the most helpful person ever. He cares about your success and will do anything to help you pass the class. I had certain circumstances that made the class difficult but we met several times and he made accommodations better than the accessibility center could ever.

Prof. Parry is great, but his teaching style was not very structured. He likes to take tangents often. There's a Zoom class option. Don't do it. You will not pay attention. Tests are matching questions, free-response artwork ID, and multiple mini-essays (you can write beforehand). Most of the grade is your final 3 essays, so get ready to write.
So much reading. His lectures are a little boring but he is a really nice guy and he is a reasonable grader.
Dr. Parry is a homie fr

Dr. Parry is hands down the best professor I've ever had at BYU. His perspective is so powerful, and his love for his students is palpable. He gives his students a lot of freedom when it comes to his assignments and his lectures are always enjoyable.
Dr. Parry is a great guy, his social commentary in class is 10/10. Just show up, read the directions on assignments, and do the study guide - you'll get an A

Gives you NO feedback on critical assignments that are worth a significant portion of your grade (like 60% kind of big for one assignment). Grades you on your own insights that you gained from the class, again with no feedback on why you get the grade you got. Really unfair. Provides no direction on how to improve. TAs were also not helpful at all!

Professor Parry is very respectful of other peoples opinions but I will say if you dont want to know his opinion, dont take this class. He is very outspoken about his political views and randomly trying to relate them to the 1700s. The class is really easy though and as long as you participate you get credit. & The insight journals are easy.

Dr. Parry is AMAZING--I've taken multiple of his classes simply because he makes a point to help you out if you have any accessibility issues, and he'll tell you on the first day that he knows what it's like. He cares about you so, so much and loves to hear what you have to say. If you work hard he'll love you for it. I love his notes on my papers!

Overall, Dr. Parry is a good choice for a humanities class taken as a general. Hes very passionate about what he teaches, the TAs are very helpful, and the exams are very doable with the thorough study guide he gives. Personally, I felt he went on a lot of tangents that distracted from class and expected this class to be a top priority of of ours.

I LOVED this class with Dr. Parry. There's quite a bit of reading, but it's very manageable even with little effort. Exams have a clear study guide & journal entries aren't bad either. I'd recommend studying for exams with a friend or two, it really helps. I felt like lectures were always interesting and I had a lot of fun going to class.
Dr. Parry is so kind and incredible! He knows so much about the humanities and obviously loves it and his students! I love his classes.

JOEEEEE!! Theres just something about Dr. Parry that I absolutely love. He expects A LOT of reading but if were being honest you can get by with minimal effort. I happen to think his lectures are awesome and you get a lot of cool life lessons out of them. Hes not for everyone but I loved his class. Exams arent too hard either.

Dr. Parry is so kind! His lectures tended to be boring for me but I still enjoyed class due to his obvious care for his students and the subject. I would recommend him as a professor but be prepared for heavy reading from 3 different textbooks. The class is graded on only a few assignments but the written aspects are not graded too difficultly.

Parry is a good professor who knows what he is talking about (even if his lectures can get a bit boring). He tries to encourage discussions in class and is respectful of everyone's opinion. There is a lot of reading for the class and only a few assignments-- 8 journals and 2 tests. He's a pretty easy grader and is very accessible outside class.

Your grade is just weekly papers and a final essay and test. You really don't have to do the readings and you should still be able to participate in the class discussions. He encourages a lot of discussion - even on uncomfortable subjects - but that's philosophy. He also gives great feedback on the papers and it's not hard to do well

This is just a lecture class, so all you need to do is show up and write a response paper about the guest lecturers. Expectations are super clear and full points awarded for completion. Good opportunity to explore philosophy in a low-stakes way. It's a pass/fail class and only one credit, so pretty straightforward. Parry is great!

I can see why some people might not like Dr. Parry. He can talk a lot, but I have him in a smaller class, and He takes quite a bit of feedback from class members. You may also dislike his propensity to talk about controversial and uncomfortable subjects, but that's one of the reasons I like him. I love the way he challenges my worldview every day.

Professor is great and teaches well. But he has a low voice and late in the afternoon in a dark classroom... It was often hard to pay attention. There is a ton of reading but it isn't really necessary, just recommend. All old philosophy so its hard to understand. If you like philosophy, go for it. If you want and easy general, look elsewhere.

He gets up and talks for two hours. Usually never about what you want to learn. The most useful part was the final review with the TA. However, that being said, his class is really easy. Essays periodically than a simple final. Easy grade, not much learning done. And if you want to keep up with reading, it's insane, and not worth it.

You've got to have an open mind, especially when what is discussed in class goes against the beliefs you were raised with. If you participate and voice your thoughts, be ready to be instantly shut down and told you're wrong.  He tells you that there isn't a "should" or "should not" in the class, but he still tells you that you're still wrong.

This class should only be taken if you want to double count Bio and Letters. Otherwise its completely pointless. I did appreciate the different view of global warming GMO and evolution. I also did enjoy the books we had to read, but the teachers(Yes there are two teachers) have long boring lectures about the books.

Such a hard class, especially after my expectations from 201. If you don't have background in the subject, he isn't going to help you, which is dumb since it's a general. It seems impossible to get in his good graces, since he might not have any. Very difficult course, not sure if it's worth the double-dip Civ/Letters credit.

Honors 120 was an interesting class to say the least. Dr. Parry is very entertaining when he goes on long rants. Just know that the TA's grade pretty much all your work, so that can be discouraging sometimes.

Dr. Parry was a pretty good professor. You really need to show up for lectures. The majority of your grades are based off of your almost weekly one page papers (you need to submit a rough draft and a final page) and the passport assignments. The problem I have with Parry is that he is concerned mostly with philosophy which can be less clear-cut.

Dr. Parry is nice, but lectures were mostly tangential. I got the impression that even he wasn't sure what he was talking about. We were ill-equipped to handle the topics "explored" in class, so papers and discussions were highly superficial. I love the idea of the honors program, but this class was so disappointing I'm not continuing in it.
Interesting class, confusing lectures. Gets you to be more open-minded, though!
I did not like this class at all. Though, I'm not sure if it was the class itself or Dr. Perry's approach on it that made it so unappealing. Definitely wants you to put a LOT of work in

Dr. Parry tends to ramble a lot.  Sometimes it's hard for me to follow his lectures.  Most of the time I feel like my time is wasted in his class.  I've talked to a lot of students who feel the same way.  It's an easy class - you only write one page papers every other week - I just find the class extremely boring.

He is a funny, entertaining speaker. He's really interesting in teaching critical thinking (I'm preparing for the MCAT, and this class is good training for VR). I didn't find the quizzes and final as easy as others did- I really had to study hard. Even so an A was definitely possible and he'll bend over backwards to help students.

Main portion of grade comes from a "Great Question" journal. Absolutely DO NOT leave the journal to the last minute. I really enjoyed his class though, he is a good speaker and has interesting lectures. Sometimes an assignment would be confusing but he was happy to help whenever there was a question. Exams and final require substantial studying.
Excellent. Parry is flexible and picks great profs to present. Embraces different viewpoints and keeps discussion lively. Sensitive to issues facing the church today. Very helpful too.

The lectures were sometimes dull but other times interesting. You take a 5 question quiz every friday with TAs. (easy!) A LOT OF READING! textbook is slow! Test are EASY. BUT you also have to write 10 half page papers and the TAs are mean hard graders! I liked this class and got an A by studying so its not impossible.

60+ pages of reading per week and  weekly quizzes (non-multiple choice) with just 5 questions. You have to read and go to boring lectures where he just rambles to do well on the quizzes. The 3 tests are easy and everyone gets similar grades. It's the insight journal (10 entries) that determines7 your grade. The TA's are ruthless graders, so beware.

For this class: Go to lecture!!! and pay attention. He often gives out ideas of what will be on the Friday quiz in class. Assignments: 10 quiz scores (2 will be dropped out of twelve). 10 one page (single spaced) papers- pretty easy and the TA's will give you feedback. 2 exams and a final. Final is not comprehensive. Perry is great. Do the reading!

Dr. Parry is a wonderful teacher. He knows his stuff and is passionate about it. The class has a lot of reading, but be sure to do it for the weekly quizzes. Tests are way easy if you just read and pay attention in lecture.

I really enjoyed this class. I know a lot of people who didn't, but I personally thought it was very interesting. Professor Parry is extremely insightful. Just read the textbook/stories (use sparknotes) and write down everything he says in class and you'll get all A's on the tests. Don't procrastinate journals! Do them as you go!

Great class, highly recommended to fulfill a general credit!  Quizzes are once a week in lab, so be sure to do the readings for the week (or at least read the spark notes!).  Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you aren't going to do the reading then I would definitely go to lecture and take good notes!

Attendance is mandatory because there are pop quizzes once a week. He loves the subject but he goes off on tangents... A LOT. Luckily he really cares about his students and doesn't make his tests too hard. The papers were stressful and the pop quizzes were difficult at times, so it's important to pay attention. Okay professor.

My favorite professor at BYU! Dr. Parry is approachable, insightful, and knows something about everything. Tests are 50pts multiple choice and easy, mainly memorization. 3 essays, 1-2 page single spaced, half of your grade. He grades fairly. Wrote my 3 essays a couple days before the end of the semester, got an A.

Dr. Parry knows everything about anything. He offers great insights and shocks you with how much he knows. He also has a witty sense of humor. It's really great. He likes to get to know his students and really cares about their learning. 3 papers, he grades tough. Tests and quizzes are easy though, so long as you do the readings and can memorize.

Professor Parry really helped me get into the subject. There are quizzes once a week, so make sure to do the readings. The tests aren't that hard, but make sure you know about all the things on the study guide. He is willing to help you out on the three papers that you have to do, so take advantage of that.

Dr. Parry is an intelligent, compassionate, knowledgeable and sincere professor. He is heavily invested in the material itself but just as interested in inspiring love for the subject matter in his students. He is thoughtful and open-minded. Definitely my favorite professor at BYU.

Dr. Parry is a cool guy; he's not afraid to say things that are usually taboo at BYU (in a good way). But DO NOT take this class if you don't enjoy writing papers. 3 of them are half your grade. I skipped class 2/3 of the semester and got A's on the tests though. You NEED to do the reading; those failed quizzes'll haunt you. HATE PAPERS=HATE CLASS.

Lectures were unorganized but were very interesting to listen to. The exams throughout the semester were really easy but 30 plus percent is based on the 3 essays due at the end, so its difficult to say how I will do... Overall an enjoyable class.

Haaaated this class, probably because I'm not a humanities nerd. I felt most of the literary "masterpieces" that we read were filled with smut. Condescending, he accused me of plagiarizing my ideas in the portfolio. Said my papers were "too scholarly" for the scope of the class. Sorry I'm not as dumb as you want me to be. Elitist expectations.
The class requires heavy reading. Dr. Parry is interesting and very respectful of different cultures and ideas. He really knows what he is talking about.

I really enjoyed this class. His teaching style may not be for everyone, but I found him very easy to listen to. He really wants the students to enjoy the subject actively. Not too much work, just stay on top of reading - don't get behind at all. There is a lot of reading. I'd suggest this prof, I'll be taking 201 from him.

He really wants you to learn how to think in the field of humanities but his teaching style really doesn't accomplish this. and he grades the portfolio really harshly because he wants you to think up something he has never heard (btw he has doctorate, masters, and bachelor degrees, nbd). also some of his TAs are AWFUL

Dr. Parry is a really wonderful teacher. He is very eloquent and knowledgeable. He assigned us to read a lot of wonderful books, we had weekly reading quizzes on what we had read, two easy midterms, and three one-page papers.  Easy A if you take the time to read the books and pay attention in class.

His teaching style didn't work for me. I found myself falling asleep almost every class period (which I never do). I was unsure all semester what to write the final papers about, and it was never really made clear. Overall, not the best class.

Dr Parry's class is alright.  If you read cliffnotes or do the reading you will get an A without going to class, except for the lectures on art, you need the notes for those for the tests.  The tests are easy, the weekly quizes too if you read.  The papers are kinda tricky, you have to write what he wants.

Would have said this was easy a week ago, but he just graded our final papers. Graded them way too hard! Dropped my grade 8 points and will now most likely keep me from a scholarship. Needs to realize that not all of us are humanities or english majors! Tests are easy, but the final paper is more important. If you want an A, be a great writer!
Easy tests. Boring lectures. Required attendance on Friday Labs to take the quizzes. Grades the final portfolio of 3 1 page papers way too hard! Overall not my favorite teacher ever.
Awesome professor, easy class. TAKE IT.

Dr. Parry is the best. His tests are really straightforward and fairly easy if you go to class and take notes. Doing the reading is important though because the weekly quizzes are harder than his tests. The biggest part of your grade though is three papers. Dr. Parry is really funny, very knowledgeable, and absolutely insightful.

Must attend Discussion Grp on Friday's for quizzes. The readings he assigns are wonderful, however if you do not have enough time. Go over spark notes. Easy paper assignments. Exams aren't too difficult but do require to read text selections and memorize art. Impossible to know what he will quiz you on. Fairly easy class but time consuming.

Dr. Parry was great.  Lots of in-class discussions, only papers were short paragraphs, on which prompt and helpful feedback was given.  The tests were easy-he's not crazy about tests-so if you did the reading (or even did Spark Notes and attended class during discussions) you'd be fine.  Same with quizzes- attend class so you don't miss them.

Dr. Parry is awesome!  First couple of classes seem a bit boring, but once you get into it you'll see that he has some great insight not only about the text/art, but about life.  Looked forward to this class more than any other. If you go to class and do the reading you'll be in great shape.

This man is amazing!! He knows and loves the material and really wants to get his students to feel the same way. He is super smart and you can tell he is a very knowledgeable man. Also, he is really helpful and kind and easy!!! He makes his tests really easy as long as you go to class and pay attention; he's not out to get you.

Favorite class so far at BYU!!! The guy is soo smart and there's no doubt that he loves what he does. This subject could be really boring with the wrong professor, but he makes it SOO interesting... TAKE THIS CLASS FROM DR. PARRY... his tests are fair and the papers are very forgiving in the way he allows you to fix them. not much busy work. A+!!

Favorite class so far at BYU!!! The guy is soo smart and there's no doubt that he loves what he does. This subject could be really boring with the wrong professor, but he makes it SOO interesting... TAKE THIS CLASS FROM DR. PARRY... his tests are fair and the papers are very forgiving in the way he allows you to fix them. not much busy work. A+!!!

One thing I really liked about Dr. Parry was that he read the mid-semester reviews by students and actually DID something about it.  This class is very interesting & I liked his lectures but there is quite a bit of reading + papers so it requires a time commitment.  He's very friendly & approachable and (especially for a GE ) I really enjoyed it.

I could tell he loved the subject however I found his "today" examples out of place and immature. I was looking forward to studying the classics but I felt that I didn't learn anything insightful and deep. maybe it was just my misperception of humanities.

He is an awesome professure!  His lectures are intresting and help you to understand what the humanities is all about.  He is really nice and easy to talk to.  He will also work with you if anything comes up in your life. I highly recommend him!

Dr. Parry is incredible. He has so many interesting insights into our course material. He is incredibly fair. He is easy to talk to espcially if you do not understand something. He is so willing to help. He is very personable but demanding. I have learned so much in his class. I would recommend him to anyone.

Dr. Parry is such a kind man and easily one of the smartest men in the dept. He's also SO REFRESHING! The first day of class one kid asked if he could move onto a different slide faster because of the nude sculptures in it. Parry told him he better think of dropping the class if the images bothered him because it was the first of many. I loved it!
Great Teacher! Loved the class and I felt everything was fair. Test to Papers are all graded fairly. I recommend him...take him!

I could feel Parry's love for this subject. Interesting class. Just do the reading and pay attention in class. No format to his lectures, he just talks and you take notes. Fair tests, fair teacher. I recommend him.
I loved this class and Dr Parry. He is interested in what he does and presents the material in a way that is easy to understand. Go to the discussion sections and you will be fine.
Good Teacher, good lectures.  His test are a bit scattered in content, but if you're willing to put in a lot of reading time you'll enjoy his class.

I loved this class.  I'm not a fan of the grading system, but if you're willing to do all the assignments and spend a lot of time reading, you learn tons.  I walked away from the final with a great feeling.  I love Humanities even more now.

I love Dr. Parry! His assignments and tests are reasonable, but they still challenge you to learn and think. Sometimes his lectures are hard to follow because he jumps around a lot, but if you've read the text beforehand, it is much easier to know what is going on.
since taking the second half of this class with another teacher and hating my life... i've realized how truly awesome doctor parry really was
I loved his class. He isn't afraid to discuss things or to dive into interesting subject material. I would recommend his civilzation class to anyone.
Dr. Parry is a great orator and discussion leader.  He's also just a great guy with interesting things to say about course material.  He makes things applicable to life, too.
ditto
I loved Professor Perry's class. It pushed me intellectually and I loved every moment of it! He is an incredible teacher whom I highly recommend.

Dr. Ofa taught me so much about body stigma and intuitive eating. She obviously knows what she's talking about. She encourages class participation and loves to hear all perspectives. One of the easiest classes I have ever taken taught by literal sunshine in a bottle. The big assignments are an easy paper and a presentation.

I took Professor Hafoka for performance psychology and absolutely loved it. She is so sweet and works hard to give personalized lectures. Participation on discussion days is important but the course is completed based on your own effort. She's super understanding so don't hesitate to ask her for help/accommodations.

Econ 110 is one of the "hardest" courses at BYU. I'm a senior and went into it terrified but it's not bad AT ALL! There is some math and the concepts can get confusing but professor Stoddard does an amazing job. The quizzes are unlimited attempts, she drops your worst midterm, the TAs are so helpful. Textbook not required. Use the note packet!

I cannot recommend Dr. Stoddard enough. She is brilliant, radiant, and articulate in expression. I was in awe each class lecture. I am a psych major, and she made the class relevant, accessible, and digestible. If you want to not just survive but learn to enjoy and thrive in Econ 110, take her class! Also, the practice quizzes are your best friend.

It was professor Stoddard's first semester teaching 110, and her strong advanced knowledge made her a great teacher. She is the cutest, kindest professor ever and is so on top of responding to emails. Tests are very fair and she doesn't trick students with trick questions on exams. Same slides & class setup as Price, but different exams

If you can take ECON 110 from Dr. Stoddard, DO IT!! Econ is hard, but the concepts are totally learnable if you do the practice quizzes. Dr. Stoddard is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. She is a phenomenal professor and is one of the few who is aware what concepts she needs to review. I can't recommend her enough.

Econ 110 can be a challenging course, I actually took it twice, but Professor Stoddard made the lectures interesting and enjoyable. She is genuinely one of the BEST professors I've had in my three years at BYU.

Professor Stoddard is amazing! She is very knowledgeable and genuinely cares about students. Lectures and homework are manageable, but you do need to put in work, it's still a challenging class. She offers helpful grade drops (including a midterm). Her exams felt fair, and the textbook was useful for understanding the material.
This was the first semester she taught ECON 110 and by far the best professor I have ever had. She took a hard subject and made me understand fully. Really really suggest taking it from her.

Professor Stoddard was really great. You can tell she really cares about her students and lectures were pretty good. She has you do a lot of practice questions and is always willing to answer questions. She is really nice and is very fair. She's good at giving reminders too.

Easily one of the best professors in the department. She is organized and fair, and so kind to her students. The course material was fascinating - it made me change my career path. Tests were long but not bad, and I learned so much applicable information about the world. This is a must-take class for your electives.

If you're an econ major/ IR with the econ route, carry on your way. If you took poli 300 as your coding language for stats, I do not recommend this class. You are expected to walk in fully knowing stata and the problem sets are similar to 300, but with a econ subject topic and absolutely no mercy in the grading. Interesting lectures though.

This class was not very engaging for me, but I just needed to take it for credit. She looks for very specific answers on tests, which can be slightly frustrating, but she's a really nice professor. Genuinely so passionate about economic development and just wants other people to feel the same way. Not a bad class to take.

I can't imagine a better professor! Dr. Stoddard is so caring and committed to her students having a good experience. I thought the lectures were great (maybe slow at times, maybe?), the workload wasn't overwhelming, and the tests were straightforward. 
Definitely different than other Econ classes, at times it felt more like a sociology class.

Dr. Stoddard is an amazing professor. She cares a lot for her students and provides very interesting lectures. The content of the course felt a little dry at times, but overall I had a really good experience in this class. Make sure to study hard for tests since they make up a large part of your grade.

Prof. Stoddard is so caring and understanding, especially during COVID. The content of this class is so well set up--it was my favorite class of all of college. She brings up such important questions about development that changed my entire perspective. Be sure to read the research papers she assigns and go to class! Only way to pass the tests.

Dr Stoddard has cut back on the reading from past semesters--still lots, but less. Tests are easy (there's more math on the first test than the rest of the course combined). Highly recommend this class for its content and relative ease.

She's great and really kind, but her lectures are really dry. Excluding the math equations, everything is really intuitive. Theres a giant research paper to read before every class. It's a great topic, but I feel like more expertise would be helpful.
This was the best class I've taken at BYU. Dr. Stoddard is inspiring and I learned a lot from her lectures.

This class is OK if you like reading academic papers. You have to read at least one before every class. She puts multiple article questions on all of the tests. There were 10 in class quizzes based on the articles. Her lectures are extremely boring. She fell behind on the material a lot and forgot to post study guides and homework multiple times.

The reading in this class is way too extensive. In a typical week you have a problem set (that often includes watching a long documentary, a stata assignment, and a few regular math questions), anywhere from 2-4 long econometric heavy articles to read (they are dense), and a textbook chapter for every class. Also a semester-long book report.

The content of this class is interesting, but the lectures are dull. This class has more reading than any class I have ever taken. Not only is there a lot of reading, but professor Stoddard asks questions about minute details from the readings. Honestly, the overbearing workload of this class ruined the content for me. I would not take it again.

She's a great teacher and person. Very passionate about what she teaches. Makes you want to change the world too. Grading is bad and strict though. Reading is overbearing as well. From first-hand experience, I think she gets offended when students say that something was confusing because English is her second language. Not an easy A. Great content.

Great teacher and a really interesting and enlightening subject. Makes you think about poverty alleviation and the practicality of solving world problems a lot. Not a difficult class, but you have to attend because of pop quizzes. She's fantastic too.
One of the best professors I've had. She is truly inspirational and helped me fall in love with Economics. She is very helpful and understanding.
I thought the material was dull and simple. It doesn't seem like you have a higher chance of getting the pop quiz question right if you do the reading or not, so be prepared for frustration there.

Expect a lot of pop quizzes, you have one about every other class period so you have to do the reading and come to class prepared. The test are written and multiple choice, the final wasn't comprehensive. There is one book report, but if you choose a good book it's not bad, only about 5 pages long.

Olga is friendly and knowledgeable, and she brings an personal perspective to the issue of development. The class is one of the easier 400-level courses. Lectures follow the slides provided by the textbook publisher, so not really essential to show up. The midterm/final reviews were enough.

She's a super sweet lady and wants you to do well in the class. The tests are pretty difficult but as long as you pay attention, come to class (she gives a pop quiz about once a wk), and do the homework you will pass.
Super caring and very knowledgeable. Pretty too!
AWESOME class
She is great!

Dr. Johnson is clearly a gifted teacher, one of the finest at BYU. He loves material science and it's infectious. That being said, this is a difficult class for sure. Tons of projects, labs, and hard topics.

He is a nice professor, explains most topics clearly, and is accessible outside of class. He is pretty organized and wants you to succeed! The class, by its nature, is very challenging and it requires a lot of self discipline to stay on top of it all. Beware of the iClicker reading quizzes, they are unpredictable & count for more than you think:')

This class was fun and Prof. Johnson is very knowledgeable but the grading criteria was always iffy, even when talking/checking hw with the TAs. Exams can also be nit-picky, but if you take notes on the slides you should do well. You don't need the textbook. Be detail oriented.

Professor Johnson is very good at explaining concepts in a simple way that is easy to understand. He also organizes the course content very well and is focused on student hands-on learning over simply "covering material".

Dr. Johnson is a solid teacher. Very knowledgeable and genuinely cares about his students. The material is difficult, be ready to work. Some homework can be a real pain. One big group project at the end of the semester. Overall, about what you'd expect from a ME class.
Not always clear as to what he was testing. Good professor that is probably still learning how to teach. He is very smart. 382 is not a terrible class, but the grading criteria was never that clear.

Dr. Johnson is a newer professor so he is still getting established. He basically lectures from slides which have some material not from the book. He is really nice and willing to help if you ask. Lots of reports, homework, labs, and quizzes. If you study his slides, took good notes, and do the reading you'll do well on exams.

Dr. Johnson is awesome! The class isn't easy, but I really enjoyed taking it from him. He cares about your learning and is always willing and ready to meet with you if you need help. He's very passionate about the material, which rubs off a bit, so that was nice. Lots of reading and material to cover, but I'm really grateful for what I've learned.

This online class is rather intense in the summer. However, Sis. Tuttle was approachable and I appreciated her insights in class. She is super easy to contact and is happy to answer questions. Very caring and considerate. I really appreciated taking this class from her!

Rigorous exam proctoring (needed a 2nd external webcam) and poor execution of canvas. Homework keys given frequently did not match homework. Exam study guides were not comprehensive and failed to mention things that would be tested. Suprised and disappointed with the quality of this class from an otherwise knowledgable and kind BYU professor.

Wouldn't recommend. You need a 94.5 to get an A. 87% of your grade is exams. On top of that, the professor isn't the one who made the videos with the material so there is a disconnect between the lectures and tests. No slides, only some diagrams. Tests are only available online on Friday and Saturday. Online seems appealing, but stay clear.

All of the videos were made by another professor (which makes the exams interesting because she includes things in the exams not covered by the videos). She was gracious when students pointed this out though. The content in this class is challenging, but it is only a time consuming class during the weeks with exams.

Maybe its just the online version, but the tests had content that wasn't given as much attention as it should've in the videos. I think there was a disconnect between the tests and the video content taught because it was some other dude that was giving the videos. The content wasn't anything crazy, just a bad format imo.

In my four years at BYU, I've never had a female science professor so I looked forward to this class. But I took this class online and learned that the lectures and assignments were made by Dr. Wood, not Dr. Van Ry. I liked the class though, since it was the least demoralizing chemistry class I've taken at BYU, even though it's a bit disorganized.

Dr Van Ry is very clear about what she wants you to know on her exams.  Do the study guides and go to her office hours and work hard.  If you can do that you'll get a good grade.  She definitely cares about you and wants you to succeed so definitely talk to her as much as you're able.

Her teaching and exam style take some getting used to, but her expectations very clear and her lectures are very engaging. She wants you to LEARN biochem, not just memorize stuff to pass a class. Go to office hours as often as you can, take good notes, and this class is totally doable. Biochem is just a grind no matter who you take it from.

Do not take this class from Dr. Van Ry!! She was terrible at lecturing and was a really tough grader. Had to drop this class because of how difficult it was and how unhelpful she was. I went to her with mental health struggles and she was not very supportive or nice about it. Please take this class by anyone else but her.

Dr. Van Ry cares a lot about her students but is not that great at actually teaching. Her lectures are disorganized and are hard to follow. The handouts she made were also messy and hard to follow. If you want to do well in her class form a study group fast and go to her office hours and the TA office hours.

Dr. Van Ry cares a lot, and is a practicing scientist, but from my perspective she is not a great teacher. Her lectures are rambling & disorganized. She provided handouts to help prepare for tests, but even these were handwritten & hard to follow. I also had trouble accessing her annotated slides, so test prep was a nightmare. Avoid if possible.
Absolute disaster.

She is very smart and did a good job of teaching her smartness to her class. She offered sooooo many chances for extra credit and her exam reviews were spot on. She always asks if people understand and ways for her to improve. She is also a great and funny. She is very approachable.

This was definitely one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. But honestly, Professor Van Ry really does want to give you as good of a grade as possible. Her tests aren't multiple choice, so she has more leeway with grading and can give you partial points for problems. Having study groups and going to TA office hours and reviews is crucial!
This class is hard but doable. Make sure you go to lecture, form a study group and ask ta's for help. She has super helpful reviews before exams which help you know what to focus on.

Dr. Van Ry is brilliant, although at times she appeared disorganized, and often students in the class helped her correct little things during lecture like an out of place OH group. However, she shared with the class how she is dyslexic and has worked hard to overcome it. free response Tests were graded on very specific criteria. Still recommend tho

Unless you are already prime at Chemistry, you are going to have to sit in the front 3 rows and attend every review and watch lots of youtube. Honestly she seemed confused herself about the material and uses her own terms. I took this class from Sitake the semester before and everything I learned was SO DIFFERENT. Guess I'm taking it a 3rd time.

I have mixed feelings about Prof. Van Ry. As an individual, I respect her and admire how smart she is. However, being intelligent does not always extend to the teaching side of things. Chem 285 was a hard class simply because it is hard material to learn. Van Ry tried to teach, but I honestly ended up teaching myself the entire semester.

Professor Van Ry is an amazing human being. I remember coming into her office hours once and expressing how overwhelmed I was. She encouraged me to keep trying and to not give up. This has been the hardest class I have ever taken, but if you work hard you will make it! OH MY, THE TA'S ARE THE BEST. They saved me and will prob also save you.

Professor Van Ry is so all over the place in lecture that I decided to stop wasting my time going. Go to every weekly and test review held by the Ta's! They teach more in an hour than Professor taught in a week. It's frustrating paying thousands of dollars to have someone who does not know what they're doing trying to teach you chem. Worst teacher!

Rate my professor isn't at all accurate for Dr. Van Ry. She honestly is a real gem of a chem professor because she genuinely cares about the success of each of her students. CHEM 285 really is a hard class, but her encouragement, superb TAs, and availability outside of class really gave us all the tools we needed to succeed. Give her a chance :)

VERY hard class, but not impossible. I do have to say that it is not so much the teacher, but the course itself. Professor Van Ry cares about her students and wants to help them as much as possible, but this class is just plain difficult. Go to every class, attend every TA review, get a tutor, make a study group and you will be set!

Pam is such a nice professor! She really cares about her students. The class is super hard though. I've never gotten such a bad grade on an exam until this class. You have to do lots and lots of studying and memorization! She does offer a little bit of extra credit which is nice.

This class was one of the hardest things I have ever done. I loved Professor Van Ry as a person, but I wish I never had taken this class from her. Class was all over the place, very disorganized. I could never really tell what was important for me to know, or just a side topic. The TAs were life savers! Without them this class would be impossible!

Professor Van Ry is a nice person and truly cares about her students, but she is the worst professor I've ever had. Her lectures were all over the place and rarely ever made sense. The only reason I passed is because I went to every TA review and they basically taught us all of the material that Professor Van Ry was supposed to teach us in class.

I enjoyed taking this class from Dr. Van Ry. It was her first semester teaching it and I think she was very fair in how she taught and graded. She really cares for her students and wants everyone to do well. Reading the textbook is probably one of the most important things to help on the tests.

Dr. Van Ry had a bit of a rough go this first semester of Biochem, but it ended up well. She is very approachable, hates it when you beg for points, but very willing to help even though she is really busy. Don't be fooled by the beginning of the semester, the hardest part is the end. DO THE READINGS! That and TA reviews are a must. Very little HW.

Dr. Van Ry cares about your learning and is very approachable in my opinion. She was often forgetful and struggled to teach clearly, especially with it being her first time teaching the course. She wasn't my 1st choice. If you find yourself in the same situation though, I wouldn't worry too much. Especially as she gains experience.

Very kind. near impossible to access outside of class. Claims she is too busy to respond to student emails, but isn't that part of the job? Takes forever to get back with grades, so not sure how she prioritizes her time if not around students/teaching. Anyone who is taking her for biochem & trying to get into med school needs to reevaluate.

I took this class from her the first semester she taught it and that definitely showed. Her test questions weren't always clear on what she was looking for (b/c she uses her own terminology wrong on the daily), but when I went to talk to her she just told me I should've known what she was asking. If you can take this class from anyone else, do.

Professor Van Ry is extremely educated on the subject of biochemistry, and she often assumed the rest of the class was also on her level. The tests were difficult but fair. TA review sessions were extremely beneficial.

Chem 285 is a hard class (especially for a freshman) but that is not Dr. Van Ry's fault I have been at BYU for 3 years and I have NEVER had a teacher care as much as she did. Totally accessible outside of class and will help you out (individually if needed). She has her slip-ups but tries her best and gives you everything you need to succeed

Van Ry is very kind & truly cares about your grade and is very spiritual. CHM 285 is already a very difficult, random class with a lot of material packed into 1 semester. I had to do all of my learning outside of class. The book and TA lab saved me. There are a lot of assignments, weekly quizzes, MC and FR tests, attendance, and a 1% EC chance.
Chem 285 is a tough course and definitely takes a lot of work but Professor Van Ry really cares about her students and does everything she can to help them succeed.

This was Dr. Van Ry's second time teaching CHEM 285 and it shows. She came from teaching high school chemistry to a near 300-level bio-organic chemistry class in college. I felt she wasn't qualified to effectively teach this class. I struggled big time. Be prepared to teach yourself the content...

She is very sweet and a nice lady, but she cannot teach. She justs rushes through her slides and reads them word for word and doesn't explain them. I had no idea what was going on most of the time. The tests are insanely hard and are nothing like the homework or practice problems. Most difficult class I have ever had. Attendance is taken every day

Tests are unpredictable. Lots and lots of memorizing. Very smart but not very good at breaking down things if you dont understand a concept. Doesnt answer questions effectively. Tests are weighted heavily, worrys about the average a lot wont curve tests. She does care about her students. Rushes through lectures tests arent similar to class HW

Professor Van Ry was a sweetheart. It was her first semester at BYU and unfortunately, it shows in her teaching. She is very knowledgeable, but she had a hard time dumbing things down for us. Her lectures were hard to follow and reading the book before coming to class was a must to understand. This class was a beast even without Professor Van Ry.

Dr. Van Ry is the SWEETEST lady, and brilliant, but BRAND NEW and struggles actually teaching. So, I had to teach myself most of the material in this class, and the TAs taught the rest. This class is already INSANE without having to try and teach yourself everything. Would recommend taking from someone who is EXPERIENCED in teaching this class.
Super easy. Chillest teacher i've had
I love him so much! I actually took for SWELL 191

Super nice guy. Doesn't know a whole lot about bowling but I preferred it that way because I just wanted to bowl more. He taught us some techniques the first few weeks but after that we just got started right away, so I basically taught myself but I liked it that way.

There was a little teaching on bowling technique near the beginning, but mostly class was "Lanes are open, break some records!" If you wanted his help you could find him and ask for feedback. Once I saw him playing clash royale while bowling with students.

I took beginning volleyball for kicks and giggles, and it was exactly what I wanted! We did basic practice drills 2/3rd of the semester, and then just did scrimmages the rest of the time. He let us play music and often joined our teams to fill in! So much fun. Just make sure you actually go to class!!!
HES THE BEST! Take his classes he is so much fun!!!

Awesome class!

You can only miss five class days, so beware that, but super chill and it's just a fun environment. Coach loves the sport and is funny too.
Par is so caring and funny. He makes class so fun. Attendance is your source of grading in pickleball so you can't miss any days. but other than that, really fun class recommend!

I took the beginner soccer class, it was basically just scrimmaging every day. It was pretty easy, although I wouldn't recommend it for true beginners since the rules of the game weren't really explained and most of the people there were already good at soccer.

I took all-girls basketball from him (SWELL111). The class was so fun! He teaches a little at the beginning and then you just play pick-up. As the semester goes on, you just play more games. You can miss like 5 classes. He's a chill guy and will find ways for you to make up stuff if you miss more.

BYU gym is gross. My acne got bad during this semester and my doctor said that it is probably because of an unclean gym environment. He doesn't really do anything other than supervise. Except he starts everyday by talking about something somewhat related to the class so I felt bored or like i was wasting time, you can miss five classes.
super fun guy! I took beginning volleyball with him and he made it awesome! great environment

Par Kalberg is literally the BEST guy ever!!!! He made volleyball so much fun. He is actually hilarious and makes everybody smile. I don't think he's a volleyball player but he taught us well. Take volleyball from him; you definitely won't regret it! My favorite class this semester by far!!!
Super boring. Talks too much instead of just letting us workout. Good if you've never worked out before in your entire life.

I took his soccer class and it was great! It was the 2 hour term class and we did like 30 minutes of drills and then the rest of the time was spent scrimmaging. He was fun and offered some extra credit if you missed too many classes. Beware: the intermediate class is a lot of pretty experienced players so make sure you have experience playing.
