Left us in the dark to build a game on our own. Only one exam if you mess up it is over (and you will mess up bc his exams focus on topics that we barely cover in class or he said it won't be on the exam). I never understand anything in the lectures bc he usually just reads the slides.

His exams are really hard and a lot of times he brings up content he said he won't on the exam, or we have never covered before. Does not offer any time of extra credit assignments even most of the class didn't do well. All midterms and final were scheduled at 7am which was the worst thing ever.
I really like Paris, it's a hard class, but if you're an animation major it's really importatnt. Graphics is cool!
Tough class, but really enjoyed it. I have no interest in animation, but was still my favorite class at BYU. The labs are super cool! Prof. Egbert is a really good professor

Don't take this class if you're not an animation major! There are 2 midterms and 1 final, all timed but doesn't give you nearly enough time. No extra credit, no curve. Little guidance on projects. Got 100s on all projects and homework but averaged an 81 on exams (50% of your grade) so I got an A- in the class and lost my scholarship. Not worth it.

Dr. Egbert is a wonderful person, however, his class was very difficult. I felt underprepared for exams since they relied on linear algebra knowledge, but the labs were super cool and provided applications for the concepts in class.

Great teacher and a fun class. You don't need to be artistic- the class is focused on algorithms/math. You learn OpenGL, write a ray-tracer, and final project is to build a 3d video game.
Tests were kinda hard though, and I didn't feel well prepared for them. There is no homework, just projects and tests. I spent about 7 hrs/week outside class.
An amazing professor, really cares about his students and what he is teaching.

You could tell Dr. Egbert was phoning this class in.  He would review his notes right before, and just read off old powerpoints. We were told that a particular homework would be on the test, even though it wasn't due for another two weeks. Class was pointless, and I'd estimate that 50% of students didn't attend. Workload was light and easy though.

The graphics class was time-consuming but a lot of fun, and Dr. Egbert is an enthusiastic professor. His tests can be somewhat hard because the tests have little to do with the programming assignments. I'm very thankful I took this class from him.
The Best Computers Teacher I have ever had
Dr. E. is an excellent professor.  The class is hard but he makes it fun.
He's a really fun teacher and does a good job of keeping the material interesting.

Dr. Egbert is a great and fun teacher and knows his stuff very well. He teaches classes that are fairly demanding (they're supposed to be that way) and his tests aren't too easy, but he's willing to work with you IF you stay on the ball (if you're a   procrastinator you'll just get a shrug). If you don't slack off, you'll do well (I got As and A-s)
Dr Egbert doesn't seem like he enjoys teaching.  He is often confused at students questions and answers them awkwardly.  The course isn't that bad as long as you devote all your social time to it.
No Comments
No Comments

The structure of this class isn't my favorite. You just read the textbook (which is concise and well-written), and then watch lectures where he regurgitates exactly what you read. A lot of his exam questions are trick questions. Good luck if you take this class.

I feel like Professor Vehrs is caring and helpful, but 95% of this class is learning by yourself. There are only 4 practicals, including the final. I feel we really didn't have the time to go over the concepts adequately in class and there weren't a lot of assignments that applied what we were learning. Overall, it could have been better.

I liked the textbook for this course. It builds upon past knowledge and uses pretty simple terms. I don't like that the online class expectations are different than the in person class, but the lectures he recorded are good and clear. A lot of extra credit is available! Hard but interesting class

I went into this class trying my hardest and just felt beat by the end. The quiz and exam are super specific (and he makes the online class do way more calculations than the in person). It just felt harder than it needs to me. I still ended up with a good grade, but I think I would have enjoyed the class more if I took it from someone else.

If you need slides, choose someone else, but if you're engaged in the class, you'll do just fine. He's slightly monotone but smart and good at teaching! Read the book and be ready to answer questions during class. Fill out all the study guide questions and you'll be fine! This class is super applicable for life so get the most out of it!

Doesn't use powerpoints of any kind. Bases lecture on his own textbook, which he wrote (and which is decent). Was a very boring lecturer, although he tried hard to mention things he would test on. Difficult to pay attention to. Offers a ridiculous amount of extra credit (my grade got bumped by like 6%). Graded by weekly quizzes and exams.

He seems to take relatively simple topics and explain them in the most complicated way possible, all without any visual cues or power-points, just a man speaking in a monotone in front of a class for an hour.

His textbook (which he wrote) is just as dry and complicated, just hundreds of pages of the most bland reading you've ever seen.

Take this class in person!Dr. Vehrs is so smart, and he emphasizes what you need to know for the tests. Tons of extra credit opportunities and tests were very fair. He wrote his own textbook to lower costs for students, and it is such a help for the class. Go to lecture, attend the TA reviews, read the book and you will be golden.

DO NOT TAKE ONLINE. confirmed to me by multiple TA's and Dr Vehrs himself that online is more difficult and rigorous than in person. No late work accepted, quizzes are extremely specific and he loves trick questions. So many "select all that apply".  Dr Vehrs is a dry lecturer, but is otherwise a very nice person and willing to help you out.

I took this class online and it was the HARDEST class I've ever taken at BYU. He takes simple concepts and makes them way more challenging and confusing than they need to be. His quizzes and tests are insanely challenging and his lectures are up to 3 hours long. It's hard to retain everything when there's so much to memorize. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

This guy sucks. Take this class in person. He makes the online class harder for no reason. The TAs told us in an in-person review that the online class is a lot harder. Trash class and professor. Dr. Vehrs your online class was the worst experience I had at BYU.

Dr. Vehrs was a nice guy and wanted you to do well. Was always willing to answer any questions. Expected you to read from textbook that he wrote but I never did, and I did fine. His quizzes are difficult, and tests can be tough. Study quizzes and go to reviews! Beware of "pop quizzes" in class. 25 points possible of Extra Credit awarded.

Awesome professor, he writes his own book and its the best book I've ever had in college. Tons of extra credit, well laid out class, go to class, read the chapters, put in the work, and you'll get an A. I think there is up to 5% extra credit as well.
Kindest, best teacher there is. Take his class

Physiology isn't my favorite but Prof Vehrs made it engaging and interesting to learn about. I had him in person but his teaching style wasn't my favorite so I switched to his online section and it was way better! Lectures were straightforward and I understood what I needed to know in the class. He offers extra credit which is nice.

He is really boring to listen to. I recommend watching the recordings on 2x the speed b/c he talks slowly. Take great notes in class and get TA help and you will do well on the tests. I like how they are smaller and spread out, makes it easier to remember difficult info. He gives extra credit that saves your grade as well.

I took both Ex Phys and ECG from Dr Vehrs, and they were both great classes. He is a little dry when it comes to lecturing, but goes above and beyond to help students. These classes were both really easy, which is nice for 400 level classes. Read his textbook, as the chapters are usually short and have good info. Take these classes from VEHRS!

Dr. Vehrs is very organized in his approach to teaching exercise physiology. He has videos that are straight and to the point that you can watch. He wrote his textbook and it is very clear and simple. Also: YOU DO NOT NEED TO KNOW THE KREBS CYCLE!! He curves tests and gives extra credit. He responds promptly to emails. He is a man of the students.

Dr. Vehrs is probably the best professor I have ever had! He is so organized, and it's evident that he really knows what he is teaching. He has great videos online and his textbook is super easy to read and so well-written. Quizzes and tests are the only assignments and are very doable (extra credit offered too). I would take every class from him!

He teaches very clearly, but very monotone. He was also pretty condescending and would guilt the class when we didn't know the answer to one of his questions rather than just explaining. He does get a lot of extra credit that helped my grade a lot though! He does teach difficult concepts well. Always goes over the time limit so beware of that!

Dr. Vehrs is amazing. He teaches so simply and uses repetition so that everything is clear and sticks with you. The material is difficult, but Dr. Vehrs taught it in a way that was so understandable. He knows his stuff inside and out. He gives tons of extra credit and makes sure help is always available. Would definitely take from him again.

There are two midterm exams before the final and a quiz every week. If you want a good grade you will need to stay awake in class, take notes in class, go to the TA's reviews every week, and read the textbook. Any less than this will most likely result in a less than desirable grade. Dr. Vehrs is a smart instructor you just need to pay attention.

This is a hard class, but if you put in the work by reading the book and studying you'll get an A. You can earn 6% extra credit and let's us retake one of the two midterms. I was intimidated by the textbook at first, but it's clear to read. DO THE STUDY GUIDES AND BACK OF THE BOOK QUESTIONS. They helped A LOT (some were used in the weekly quizzes).

Vehrs is the best option for this course. It's a hard class but with how he lectures the class is doable. If you read the textbook and take notes in lecture you will pass with flying colors. Especially since he provides extra credit that boosts your grade by 6%. Take vehrs!
Doesnt teach much at all during class & is super unorganized but if you read the textbook a lot & spend a lot of time studying it, you can still do okay

Vehrs is a pretty dry guy, but very smart and clear nonetheless. He wrote the textbook and it correlates well with what he says in class, making the material he wants you to know very clear. Quizzes every Monday and 3 tests make up your grade, but he offers a substantial amount of extra credit. Highly recommend!!

Tough class, but doable with Vehrs. Weekly quizzes and tests make up your grade. He seems to fish for certain answers on quizzes, but if you pay attention in class and read the textbook you can do fine. He wrote the textbook and it's awesome. Make sure you do the extra credit, it lifted my grade up about 6%. Quiet and monotone, but knows his stuff.

Dr. Vehrs is an awesome teacher and I loved his class. He cares about his students and is great at explaining hard concepts. Would highly recommend taking his class. Also, he offers lots of extra credit!

I'm usually pretty good at school, but this class is kicking my behind. Don't take it unless you love reading 20 hours a week for one class and learning about things that aren't on the test. It's not a good class.

I loved Dr. Vehrs' class. He wrote the textbook that he uses (which is exceptionally well-written, in my opinion) and all of the answers to the quizzes and tests come from the book. That being said, it's still difficult because there's so much information. Sometimes his lectures are pretty dry, but the course material is fascinating.

People are dumb. Best teacher I've had at BYU. I even switched from Davidson to Vehrs. He offers 25 points of extra credit, so I ended up with over 100% in the class. He wrote his own book, which has summary points and questions at the end of each chapter which he uses for quizzes and tests. His tests are completely multiple choice now!!! Take him.
Horrible teacher!! He gives horrible feedback in the form of questions... This class is so hard, and he is no help.

This course was the most difficult class I ever took at BYU. I have taken Anatomy, Stats, accounting... nothing was more difficult. The reason? Dr. Vehrs teaches some good material, and the course book teaches a lot, but the exam material is more in depth than what is taught, and requires the student to expound on what is taught in order to pass.

I really liked this class from Dr. Vehrs. He knows his stuff and he really wants his students to understand it too. You can tell that he enjoys what he teaches. It was a pretty tough class, but I really enjoyed it. You will learn a lot in his class.

Be forewarned. This class, as mentioned, is extremely difficult. I would tell anyone to take from another professor. He expects you to memorize his wording exactly for quizzes and tests.He is very smart, but very condescending to students. He is not helpful at all.The TAs are who saved me in this class.He lectures out of his own book, line by line.

A very nice, very smart guy, but I found the class extremely difficult with an obscene amount of specific memorization to his liking. The concepts are fascinating, but beware, your responses to each quiz and test must be perfectly exact to get them correct. The TA's are very helpful. I found his quizzing/teaching style often condescending.

Highly recommend taking this class from him. Not a hard class at all to get an A if you go to class and take notes. I barely read the textbook and ended the class with a 99%. Super smart and knows physiology well! He is particular in free response answers but they are the answers he gives in class lectures. Go to TA reviews!!

Dr Vehrs is an awesome teacher. If you want to learn exercise physiology, this is the teacher to take it from. It is by  no means an easy class, but he helps make tough concepts easier to understand. He is very clear about what he wants you to know & wrote the book himself which is an awesome book & very helpful. I would highly recommend him!!

I agree with the people right below me. This is an extremely difficult class. If you don't memorize exactly what he says you will have a real hard time. In-class quizzes are free response and if you do not answer exactly as he says in class it will be counted wrong. NOT an easy class to slack off in your senior year

This class is way harder than it should be.  Vehrs is extremely boring to listen to, it is actually more exciting to read the text book.  He is very anal about answering questions exactly the way he wants it worded.  I would definitely take this class from another teacher.

Don't be misled by the 3.5 easiness people have given prof. vehrs.  This is a great class but very difficult. Lots to memorize and he demands you to memorize an answer in the way he thinks in his head.  If you put it in another way that's not in his wording, he will mark it wrong. He is ridiculous. Ta's saved me but still not worth it
the exams are difficult. make sure you memorize what he says in class.

Online quizzes are open book and relatively easy. In class quizzes are a lot harder. He will go over a lot of what will be on the in class quiz during class if you listen carefully. Tests get more and more difficult. His wording can be very tricky and he expects very specific answers on the free response. Reading is essential.A lot of work required

Dr. Vehrs is a great teacher, He make difficult concepts very easy to comprehend. His study guides for his tests are great, go to the TA reviews for them and you will do well on the tests. He has in class and online quizzes from the textbook. The textbook is way cheap and really helpful, he wrote it himself. Go to class, you should do well.

Fantastic material! Knows his stuff for sure! HOWEVER, unhelpful at office hours,annoyed when you ask ?s, secretly shreds exams before comprehensive final (he really does!), no TA, he wrote the book, very tricky, unforgiving exams with little clarification afterwards. He is a good guy but is more interested in his research than teaching students.

I loved this class! His online quizzes are open-book and open-note. Tests weren't hard if you listened in class and took notes. He simplifies the harder material very well. He encourages a lot of class discussion - he doesn't just lecture the whole time. He asks questions to make you think about real-world applications.

Glad I wasn't the only one that thought quizzes were hard. He had several online quizzes that seemed harder than the in class ones. Tests were a bit tough. I thought the final was the easiest of the 4 you'll take in class. 3 tests, a comp final, about 10 in class quizzes and 7 online quizzes. Not a cake walk here folks. Don't expect it to be.

Quizzes are very difficult. Be prepared to devote a lot of time to this class. Reading is essential. Check your Mastery and memorizing is key to doing well on Exams. Overviews are essential to quizzes. Great professor but very technical. Great class overall but difficult.
If you study in this class you will do well. Quizzes are easy at first but then get harder. Great Overall teacher!

Easy class, he explains everything very well. Definately read and underline everything he talks about in the text book- his quizzes kept getting harder as the semester went on, but he gives out 20 points of extra credit.  Great class.

This class was pretty good. I wasn't too fond of the quizzes- I never knew what to study. They are short answer/multiple choice/true false. There are 5 tests with number four being on the last day of class (it stinks). The final is comprehensive. He's very monotonous, but at least the subject material is interesting. I recommend him.

His class seems really boring at first because it's all easy review but as you get into the semester you see that he is a great teacher and you learn a lot of cool new stuff! DEFINATELY TAKE IT FROM VEHRS. very informative and easy!
Most painfully boring teacher I have ever taken a class from.  Relatively easy class, but ridiculously boring.

Dr. Vehrs is a great teacher; best science teacher I have ever had. He knows how to explain concepts, and he won't move on until he knows everyone understands. The test are clear and he doesn't try to trick you. I would take him for all my science classes.

Dr. Vehrs is one of the best teachers that i have had at BYU. He tells you everything you need to know and goes straight from the text book. And the book is pretty cheap! definitely take this class and anything else from him!!! so easy to know what to study!! Pretty easy to get an A
Pat's pretty friendly, and I learned a new, enjoyable activity in this class.  The only downside is with so many students, it's a bit hard to get personal instruction.

Dr. Vehrs was an awesome teacher.  There is no book to buy, you just need to go to class to get the notes.  I did very well on most of the tests and he tells you about every quiz you have, which are very easy.  All in all, a great professor that I would definitely take again.

he is an amazing teacher.  he knows how to explain even the most difficult of concepts.  he makes class enjoyable and you really look forward to each class period.  i would defintely take another class from him!!
No Comments

Don't buy the book, just print his notes off of blackboard. Pretty clear, and tells you literally everything that you will need for tests and quizzes, and he tells you every day that you will have a quiz. The tests are in class, and literally took me about 17-19 minutes each. I think everyone got an A or B.
Good Teacher, it was only weightlifting but I felt that I what I wanted out of the class, and even learned a few things.

I absolutely LOVE Professor Andrade. She is one of the best professors I've had. She is dedicated, prepares her lectures, is a flexible grader, and loves to have the class engaged. She cares about her students and responds to emails quickly. There are some reading assignments, but not impossible. Definitely a 10/10!

She's a really nice professor and I enjoyed her class. Always answers emails promptly and is understanding and respectful. Class is very lecture heavy which I found interesting, but the final was a lot harder than I anticipated based on the lectures and few homework assignments throughout the semester. I wish I would've known to take better notes.

She's a very caring professor and is quite lenient with her grading. We spend most classes just discussing poems or stories, which can sometimes be very interesting and sometimes quite boring. The only thing that made me nervous was that I had no idea what the final would be like.

Love Dr. Madden. This is a workshop class, so it's mainly discussion and no lecture. Dr. Madden is very helpful, gives good feedback, and an overall great prof. He doesn't believe in traditional grading, so if you show up and do the assignments, you're guaranteed an A. 3 personal essays that are workshopped in class, discussion posts, and ERS.

This class was so much fun! We had to write 3 long-ish personal essays during the semester and class time was used to workshop these pieces. Everyone was so kind and helpful and I just loved the way the class was organized. There was quite a bit of reading, but it was doable. This class made me love writing more!

I enjoyed this class, there was a lot of writing opportunities and most of class time is spent giving feedback with other students. Prof. Madden talks about publication, which is helpful. The assignments aren't hard and I feel like I learned a lot. I would say that class dynamic is not really what I'm used to so that was hard for me personally

Professor Madden is a great Professor! He carries himself in a calm and collected way that really invites the Spirit into each class. He treats each student as an individual, and is sure to memorize your name soon after meeting you. He teaches really well, and makes class fun. He is a really talented writer and an exceptional teacher!!

Pat is a cool guy and gives great feedback. I've taken his class multiple times and always love the books we read (inspire me to write in new ways). Downsides are that his syllabus/grading criteria are confusing/inaccessible. In general, he is not quick to respond to emails and is unavailable after 3pm on Friday through Sunday (for family time).

This class is fun for those who have an actual passion for writing. My only critique is that the workshops seem to be a bit redundant. Everybody always wants more details. It's hard taking critiques from peers who aren't experts or professionals with writing. Pat gives good books and sources to open your mind and allows creativity in writing.
Pat's class changed my life for ever. Seriously, it did. This class is the bomb.
His hotness is a little distracting. But the class is AWEsome.

This was one of my favorite classes I taken at BYU.  It converted into a lover of the subject matter (creative nonfiction).  Professor Madden is very good.  However, I let myself get behind on assignments since he didn't say we were going to be accountable for them.  Make sure to keep up on your quote journal and readings.

Great class to take if you want to improve your writing skills. The class is laid-back but still professional. Dr. Madden is very insightful and more than willing to help you any way he can. His feedback is always helpful and constructive.
Pat provided superb feedback on my writing and really desired for the whole class to succeed. I hope to take the course again.

his class was lots of fun. He tries hard to help all students feel comfortable and help them succeed. He is interested in teaching not just having students memorize and regurgitate. Well worth the time!
This is one of the classes where you will get an A if you work hard. Don't expect the teacher to spoon-feed you.

Prof. Madden gives you a lot of useful feedback on your writing to help you improve. The class was structured well so that you had the opportunity to read a lot of poetry/short stories/personal essays before you had to start writing your own stuff for that section. I sometimes felt that ordinary class time was wasted, but workshops were awesome.
Great if you are serious about writing.
he doesn't teach, it is a waste,
His teaching style only works for people who are serious about learning, not those who want to sit around and be lectured. He's a great teacher, very different.

I was all excited to take this class, but the Professor Madden doesn't teach.  He finds ways to use up the class time, like movies, discussions, quizes, and student reports. The papers don't deal with analyzing literature. My high school AP class was better.
He is a great teacher! I'm not done with his class yet so I don't know how hard his grading to be, but it will be worth it because I learned so much. And there's no tests! Only papers and quizzes. :)

Patrick Steffan is awesome. He is so funny, and the lectures and assignments are all super chill. You have a semester long project, but the TAs are amazing and literally walk you through every step. It's a great class! (this class used to be psych 309 but they changed it to 313. It's the same class though)

Loved it! You could never show up to class and still get a good grade, but I liked coming because he had fun videos! Takes a long time to respond to emails, but he is very kind and a great professor. Take this class if you love psychology and if you are ready to learn a lot!! You must read the textbook!!

This was such a chill class, and I really enjoyed the content. There's a lot of work to do, but it's not overwhelming. The project is broken down really well and you get really good feedback from TAs. One of my favorite classes I've taken as a psych major yet.

This class was pretty easy. I didn't pay much attention to lectures or keep up with the reading and still got an A. Just watch the review sessions and study the guide—that's all you really need. You get points for attending lab, which helps a lot with the big group project. You can pick any topic, so it can be fun!

Very well-qualified to teach this course. Caring and attentive to questions or concerns. Professor Steffen provided several extra credit opportunities, and had very clear and straightforward expectations for assignments. He made long lectures fun with engaging videos and you could tell he knew the material very well. Highly recommend Prof. Steffen.

Dr. Steffen's lectures are somewhat boring but attendance is graded daily. There are three 4-6 page papers, three exams (in testing center), weekly timed textbook quizzes, and a final class presentation. I recommend reading the chapters of the textbook because this will be the best preparation for exams. Overall, lighter class work than most.
Very unclear, you have to figure things out on your own .
Requires a few out of class sessions for biofeedback (take ~1hr each). His lectures are good and he's a super nice guy. He keeps things interesting by sharing personal stories or fun videos.

His class is well organized and his TAs are a great support to the class. I enjoyed the concepts and found the videos he shared in classes very entertaining. He asked many questions to keep lectures engaging. Overall, one of the bestdesigned psych classes at BYU with some of the easiest tests. I would take any class Dr Steffen teaches.

I really wanted to enjoy this class, so I tried to stick out the class periods a few times, but they were pretty meaningless. He just reads off the slides and it's clear that he can't fully answer student's questions. The exams aren't horrible, but poorly written.

I took this class because I thought it would be interesting, and it was a total waste of my time. I pretty quickly stopped going to class because he just reads off the slides and doesn't really discuss the nuance behind concepts. Doesn't feel intellectual at all. But if you want an easy A, this is the class.

Pretty boring class honestly but wasn't too hard. Most people skipped class most of the time. 3 total exams, 3 easy papers, weekly reading quizzes, and taking a few personality tests make up your grade

He was a super nice guy, but I stopped going to classes mid-semester because he just reads off his slides so I did just fine doing the readings on my own. The TA in our lab was crucial and carried a ton of the course and teaching weight. Disappointed by the lack of knowledge I got from lectures.

This class ended up being my favorite psych class and I'm planning to TA for Dr. Steffen next semester. A bit more difficult than your average psych class but I loved the material and it really shaped my career goals and view of my life. I wished we had exam reviews and sometimes felt like I had to teach myself but it was doable and the TA helped.
Very fair teacher. He is a good teacher, who is approachable and just good overall. One of the better teachers that I have had at BYU.

He's a great professor who knows how to explain concepts really well w/ good examples. I loved the class discussions & thought his lectures were really interesting. They were pretty much just repeating what was said in the textbook though. The three papers were super easy and the quizzes were open book. The tests werent too difficult if you studied

He is a good person don't get me wrong, I just felt like his class was just reading off the slides. It was super hard to pay attention. Be aware of his demotivators. (I'm dead serious). I was struggling and he was willing to meet with me which was appreciated, but I felt like I learned more from the book than class.

Dr. Steffen is a knowledgeable and well-organized professor. My only complaint would be that he has a tendency to interrupt students who are asking questions and answer them before he knows the full question, so questions don't really get answered that well. Homework load is very manageable. TAs are Essential to your success in this course.

Professor Steffen is AWESOME! His lectures are less about recounting everything from the textbook but more on making the content applicable to your life. He's also really funny and his lectures and assignments are very chill. I felt 0 stress taking this class and learned a lot!

Dr. Steffens class was one I always looked forward to. A lot of psych classes can be a bore but he keeps you involved and entertained. You can tell he really cares about his students. I wish more teachers were like him.

Honestly by far one of my favorite professors I've ever had. Not only is he super caring, but he's absolutely hilarious too. I recommend him to anyone! If I could I'd retake his class. Word of advice, put in the time and if you have concerns about the class just talk to him!
Hes such a nice guy and his slides always make me laugh which is cool

Lectures were great, but the essays are really, really demanding. Get started on them early! Nit picky grading and point deductions, so follow the rubric carefully. Hes nice, the class is nice, it wont change your life but youll have a good time.

On the first day of class, Dr. Steffen said that if you hadn't taken 381 you wouldn't do well. It really was no problem for me though! Simply go to lectures, review the slides, and you'll do well on the tests. The papers are easy and are helpful for understanding concepts for future tests. Loved how interesting the material and glad I took the clas

As a psych major, the name of this class may worry you, but this has been my favorite class at BYU so far. Dr. Steffen makes this subject fun and easy to understand. There are 3 papers, but they are super easy and help you apply what is taught into your own life. They are good test preps too. If you go to class, do the reading, you can get A.

Dr. Steffen is great and his class is really easy to do well in if you actually try to pay attention in class and do the readings. The papers are super easy, you just have to follow the rubrics he gives you exactly, and then you can get 100%. He is very fair.
Easy, but the papers are a pain and are very subjectively graded. His midterms are pretty easy and if you know the video clips and slides  you'll do well on the papers and midterms.
Super easy. Really interesting. Take it.

This is the easiest class I've taken at BYU by a long shot. There's a lot of useful information in this class, and even though it was easy, I still feel it was worthwhile. It's the only class I've taken where you could just pay attention in lecture and do the reading and be prepared for the tests. Would recommend to anyone.

Tied for my favorite course at BYU. Dr. Steffen keeps his material clear and more concise than other professors. Interesting lectures. He is very helpful both inside and outside of lectures. He takes the time to explain difficult concepts and makes sure everyone understands before moving on. His tests are not bad if you study the lecture slides.
Great class and great Professor. Make sure to study vocabulary words from the textbook and you'll do great on the tests. I highly recommend Dr. Steffen

Dr. Steffen is fabulous. He is a great teacher. The class is pretty easy too! His current TA is also amazing. If you go and talk to him, or email him, then he is super helpful and will aid immensely. His name is Dominic. So if he is still the TA, then there is no reason not to take Dr. Steffen's 382 class!

Dr. Steffen is awesome! Psych 302 has the potential to be insanely boring and tedious but he makes it manageable and fairly interesting. He is very organized, and if you read the chapters you will do well on tests. Only one group paper(spread over semester). Daily quizzes. 3 Tests. Definitely recommend taking it with him.

302 is supposed to be a hard and time consuming class but Dr. Steffen made it fun and manageable. For the research project he kind of leaves you on your own but he is willing to answer questions and help you in anyway. You just have to approach him and take time to ask. As for the lecture slides they are no longer black and white!

This teacher is really good. 302 is naturally a difficult and TIME CONSUMING class but he makes it bearable. My class period was 2 1/2 hours long but it wasn't bad with him as the teacher. If you need any help, GO TALK TO HIM. He is really open and willing to help any student that just asks. His tests aren't bad either but do require some studying.

Dr. Steffen is fantastic. His powerpoint slides are in black and white, so if that offends you, stay away. However, his slides (and lectures) are simple and interesting. Textbook for the class is easily best I've had in college. His tests are extremely fair and the material is fun to learn. Take this class if you want to like school.

Weekly quizzes which were just the vocab from the chapter - super easy if you have just looked over everything.  Great professor!!  Makes Psych 302 quite manageable.  If you can take it from him, make sure you do.  You will either end up with an A or A-.  Shows lots of funny video clips.

Professor Steffen is a cool teacher and always plays funny applicable video clips. He does kinda leave you to fend for yourself when it comes to the research project. Especially using qualtrics and sona was very detailed and hard to figure out. Overall a relatively easy and useful class.
Great professor. 302 is a hard class no matter what, but he was always willing to help and give you extra time if needed. You have to take 302 for the psych major, so take it from him!

He gave very vague instructions on papers, homework assignments, group work! He was disorganized. His tests are okay, a little difficult just do the reading. My TA was useless. Don't expect to know exactly what you are doing in this class.

Class is boring. Monotone voice for 2 hours...I fell asleep almost every time. Tests are easy, and you get a lot of chances to edit the paper. VERY disorganized and unclear about expectations, which makes it difficult when he grades so harshly on papers. Class is a ton of work, so his lack of organization made it tough. Our TA didnt help us at all

Steffen is super helpful and understanding.  He provides extra credit and makes the two hours in class bearable.  He lets you have several rewrites on the paper.  The class seems overwhelming at the beginning, but he makes it manageable.

Dr. Steffen was an awesome teacher...really chill and really helpful.  He lets you do multiple rewrites on your research paper so there's no reason why you can't get an A on it.  He is very clear about what he expects from you and your research project.  It's a time-consuming class but he paces it well and makes it very doable.

I really didn't like this professor. He's pretty arrogant and his class is way unorganized and he changes dates all the time on the syllabus.  There is simply not enough time to do everything he wants. I loved my group, so that helped. Your study, two tests, and quizzes are your grade. Class time was usually useless. My advice, get a good group.

I actually really like Dr. Steffen.  He's a really nice guy and the class is fairly simple and easy.  One problem is that he changes dates, for example, he told the class that we would have three weeks from the next class to complete an experiment and then the next class period announced that it was due the next class period.

Dr. Steffen is the man! He is SUCH a chill teacher. He's so helpful and laidback! If you're going to take 302--which is a hard class and requires a lot of work--definately take it from Steffen. His teaching style and grading makes it really hard NOT to do well! He's so chill!
Better than the other sections.  He is easier, but not as good a teacher.  This is still the hardest classi have ever taken.  Don't get a crapy group.  That is everything.

This class is time consuming because you actually conduct a research experiment, but that's the situation with all 302 classes.  Steffen's class was easy to succeed in and helped me learn a lot. I would definitely take this class from him.

Steffan is straight forward, and open minded and guileless individual.  Kind and generous, could have been an awesome resource in understanding spss if we had walked through it with him, just watching was confusing.  fairly easy class if you put in the licks, he's just a solid dude.

This class was SO easy, you have a lot of work with the research project and all, but the tests you take individually and with your group, and your individual grade only counts for 30% of that tests grade, definetely an easy A!

VERY easy class. You have to attend though, cause that's pretty much all that counts on your grade.  No tests, very little assignments (which are a piece of cake). I have heard other 101 classes are hard, so if you can take from Steffen.

This class is really easy, it's required for all Psych majors.  You will have an assignment due every week, you need to make sure that you do them, because there aren't any tests or that many points, so every point counts!

Dr. Frandsen deserves all the love he gets. Very engaging lecturer, very caring professor. However he wasn't the best teacher. Lectures are hard to follow because content will be mixed in with unrelated tangents. For someone who has trouble concentrating, it was often difficult to extract what I needed to know from his lectures. Otherwise 10/10!

Professor Frandsen was super caring; class always felt very comfortable and informal, and I never felt like there was a bad time to ask a question. Material moves pretty fast for a science for non-majors class---but I attended every time and I was able to stay afloat. Frandsen advertises his office hours every class, so he's super easy to access.

Loved this class but really only because of Prof Frandsen. He made it entertaining and helped everyone feel seen. He gets to know you by name. Stay up to date on reading. Go to class. Study for exams and you will be fine.
Dr. Frandsen is awesome. Teaches a lot of material in a way that makes it manageable and accessible for everyone! Also he is hilarious and keeps you entertained in class. 10/10 reccomend.

Textbooks are free online. This was a great GE class. Prof. Frandsen makes sure we understand how the material is applicable to our lives and focuses on lifelong learning and application. He's funny and creates a good environment for learning. I never felt dumb asking questions.

Professor Frandsen is a really nice guy, and really cares about his subject. He is really funny, and makes each lecture fun and entertaining even if you don't like the subject much. If you do the reading, you should be okay!

I loved Professor Frandsen and he is so funny! I liked his stories and was always engaged in class. The content of this class is hard! But if you expect that and expect to study for the tests, then you will do okay. Go to TA's and get to know them. They are very helpful and good to work with. This class is difficult but doable.

Frandsen is a super nice guy and he is super funny! But this class is a bit difficult if science isn't your thing and I think sometimes he forgets it's just a general. You do read a lot and the exams were a bit different then the study guides and so I felt confused at times. This is a good class if you have an interest in science.

Professor Frandsens a very nice guy, but I did not enjoy his class. Students would ask random questions that had nothing to do with the material being tested on and he would go on tangents about them daily. I had to teach myself through YouTube because we wouldnt make it to the material in class. He wants his students to do well, but I struggled.

I took this class instead of Biology because I am not a science person. It was super interesting! At times, I was scared for my grade and stressed about all of the projects and stuff, but it all wasn't bad in the end. The tests were easier than I expected, and he gives bonus points and curves them. GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS FOR HOMEWORK ASSIGNMENTS!!!

Conservation Genomics Prof. Frandsen is young and energetic. He work has worked and studied conservation topics his whole career so he was very knowledgeable. He often had to go out of town this semester, but when he was here for his office hour he was very helpful. He sets clear rubrics for his assignments. I rarely did the pre-class text readings
Professor Frandsen really cares about the success of his students.

Professor Frandsen was super helpful, especially with covid restrictions. Course was fun and interesting. Attendance helps a lot, but if you have to miss a class, its not the end of the world. He's really personable and just a good guy all around. Just stay on top of things and take decent notes and you'll do fine.

Very understanding and wanted students to succeed! He offered mid-course evals to help improve the class & even some extra credit opportunities(which changed his initial syllabus standing on EC). Lectures were super interesting and the TAs were helpful. Homework and quizzes were consistent and given ahead of time with at least 1 week+ to complete.

Paul Frandsen. What a guy. Super funny. VERY passionate about what he teaches, and really willing to help students out. There's a lot of reading from the book The Gene, with a short quiz every week. My class was partially online, and he did a really good job at organizing everything and was a great online teacher. Take him!
Dr. Frandsen is an awesome professor. He cares about his students and made me want to study Genomics.

I loved Dr. Frandsen and this class! Once we got past all the more technical, biological concepts and started talking more about the application of genetics, it was a lot more interesting and fun. I tell everyone to take this for their biology credit because it's a fun way to get the credit that also changes your point of view on the world.

Dr. Frandsen is a wonderful professor. You can tell that he loves his students. He was incredibly easy to work with and was very open to feedback. He also offered help to students outside of class. His lectures were great, but be aware that there is a lot of content that you need to understand for tests. He also does daily quizzed in class.

Pretty easy class. I didn't do the reading and did not feel hindered by it. Tests were reasonable. Dr Frandsen is friendly and willing to answer questions. He is intelligent. He sometimes under-explains complicated concepts, but always provides more thorough explanations when asked. In class writing prompts and quizzes, graded on participation.

This is the best professor I've had at BYU. He listens to his students and is very considerate and reasonable in his assignments and grading. His tests aren't designed to trick you but to truly test your knowledge and the review sessions really help. He's willing to work with you if you need extra help and is very understanding.

For a student with mental health problems I would recommend do not take this class. His class can be very triggering if you don't like to be put on the spot weekly. He is not available outside of class, and he struggles with social skills. If his lectures were recorded, he would be a great professor.

This was the worst class of my entire undergraduate and graduate experience. If you were good at reading Godfreys mind, you did well; if you werent, you did poorly. Oh, and dont even think about trying to get help from Godfrey because hes too busy. His instructions are not clear, he values brevity over thoughtfulness, conciseness over learning.

This ethics class was the biggest disappointment of my MBA experience at BYU. To me, it was a totally wasted opportunity to have meaningful conversations about understanding your own ethical framework and then applying that to real world situations. We just spent time on his pet project - personal finance classes for elementary students.

Didn't come as arrogant as other said. Alsi, it was his first time to teach strategy - he didn't have a clue what he was teaching. I like professors who blends real world experience and theories. Godfrey was not, so the class was boring; overall, comments from class is that they didn't learn as much.

EXCELLENT TEACHER.  He teaches to benefit your life, not to simply cover the material.  No tests.  No real textbook.  You read a bunch of business cases and articles, but that is it.  No busy work at all.  I strongly recommend you take a class from him if you can.

Professor Godfrey is one of the best teacher's I've ever had. He GENUINELY cares/loves his subject and the students.  He is willing to help out with other things outside of class.  There is no text book and readings are not graded, but you must participate in class because it's 30% of your grade.  Easy class if you participate and get to know him.

Seems a little arrogant at first, but as the semester went on I really came to like him. He turned out to be really laid back and genuinely interested in helping the students.  The grades are pretty subjective, so make sure you participate and get on his good side, which isn't that hard because he's a really nice guy.
He is one of the few teachers where I really felt like I learned something valuable throughout college.

Avoid this chump. Arrogant, smug, holier-than thou attitude. Told us on first day of class that he had fasted on how to help us, and his answer was "don't accept crap from them."  Beware of his arbitrary grading--35% of the grade is class participation, so he basically gives you whatever grade he wants based on how much he likes you.  Very annoying
Jenkins is a solid Math teacher, proofs are hard and he grades hard so go to class and learn from him to get the best grade you can.

I had a tough time with the pace of the class, but Dr. Jenkins was always willing to meet to explain. While it was tough, I would not have taken the class from any other professor. It was clear he wanted his students to succeed, and never made us feel bad about asking questions. If you take this class, take it from Dr. Jenkins! 10/10 recommend

This class will be hard no matter who you take it from, but Dr. Jenkins is a good option. He has a discussion question at the beginning of every class about applications of what we are learning, and he's always happy to help in his office hours, or throw out homework questions that don't make sense.

Man, this guy is the best math professor I've ever had! Go to class -- you'll have amazing lectures and know what proofs you have to know (there are a lot in the textbook that you don't have to know). The homework is not very heavy (although the TA grades them pretty strictly), and the exams are pretty fair. Not an easy class, but worth taking it.

I was terrified for Abstract Algebra but Professor Jenkins made it great! Homework wasn't very long and after lecture was very manageable. Reading required before class, but it was very helpful. He and his TA also have lots of office hours to help out. And his tests were very fair! Take this class from him!

Professor Jenkins was great for Abstract Algebra I. The class was very well-organized, and we didn't have a ridiculous amount of homework each day, but we still learned a lot. Jenkins is super cool and really funny, and his lectures were always great.

Dr. Jenkins is a great professor. He's very clear. His tests are fair. 371 doesn't seem like a tough class until you get to the test and lose a ton of points on definitions. Math is nitpicky though, so I guess it's what we sign up for. Overall, Dr. Jenkins was an awesome math professor.
A lot depends more on your TA than your teacher, but he was pretty good at explaining the concepts most of the time.

Dr. Jenkins is a jolly guy; he jokes about the marker fumes messing with his head every time he makes a mistake. He teaches in a clear way that I could grasp. He gives a math fun fact halfway through every lecture, so that's cute. Calc is a 4 credit class, so there's lots of homework, but it's a good thing because you need practice to learn.

Dr Jenkins cares about his students and wants to help them succeed. The lectures were helpful and the reasonable amount homework was designed to help students learn. He is always open to questions. I felt that I understood the material well, but my test grades did not reflect that. It is difficult to get As on tests. Otherwise very reasonable.
It's really hard to get 100% on the homework assignments, but it is possible. He's very helpful outside of class and will always answer questions in class.

Dr. Jenkins's lectures were engaging. He did a good job at keeping the class's attention while explaining difficult material. His tests weren't easy, but weren't impossible, either. He's a great math professor.

Professor Jenkins is a favorite.  His lectures are clear and explain complicated subjects from the book.  He is clear with his expectations and is extremely helpful during office hours.  Tests are very reasonable in time and content, they were only based on what was covered in class.   Gave good feedback on tests and homework.  I would recommend.
Dr. Jenkins is a great lecturer.  You have to read the book before class, which helps a lot. He answers your questions and gives you clear study guides for the tests, so you know how to study.

I was apprehensive at the beginning of this class, I didn't know what I had gotten myself into. Dr Jenkins explains difficult concepts VERY well. His test are fair, homework is extremely helpful, no busy work, and he's just a great lecturer. Highly recommend.

Dr. Jenkins is a good guy. Very approachable and considerate. A lot of times it seemed like his lectures didn't really prepare you well for the homework. The math lab will be your friend. Not the worst option out there though.
Professor Jenkins is an excellent professor. He speaks very clearly and helps answer any questions you may have. Very well structured class. Great guy, makes class worthwhile and enjoyable!

Dr. Jenkins is honestly the best professor I've had since being at BYU. The readings prepared us for lectures, lectures prepared us for homework, and homework prepared us for the test. Everything was fair. It was difficult at times, but he was always available and willing to help. Take this class from him!

Dr. Jenkins is probably one of my favorite math professors so far.  He cared about the students' success.  I had no idea what Abstract Algebra was going into the class and was a bit nervous, but now I really miss this class!

Readings before each class and lecture follows the reading. I went to class because it helped me understand the principles and concepts better. The test were good Multiple choice were difficult but short answer consisted of problems like our hmw and what we covered in class. He is a good teacher and is willing to help. He is funny. good class.
His lectures are clear and he's pretty funny. Very reliant on textbook use -- required readings before every class. Smart guy.

This class is not for the faint of heart. It is a TON of work,the exams are over the concepts but over questions 3x harder. Professor Jenkins is awesome during lecture but my TA , Mason Victors, was rude and unwilling to help with homework questions/exam questions. My advice is to take this class seriously. Study hard & become bff with the Math lab

This class is just outright hard, for me atleast.  Professor Jenkins does a good job teaching it and the TAs are alot of help.  I have never been good at calculus but I atleast am able to understand most of it from this class, so it must be good.  Theres quite a bit of homework, but if you do it when its givin, its not overwhelming.
Extremely funny... And a great teacher!

I wouldn't ignore the student who said Jenkins was hard, as another reviewer suggested. This is a difficult course if you aren't a math genius. Jenkins is willing to help, but I put in hours of study time and went to his office hours frequently without satisfactory results. It all depends on what your strengths are. But he will try to help you.

Prof. Jenkins is great! I was in an honors section, so we had a smaller class size, and he was always willing to stop to answer our questions and explain problems.  His explanations are clear. Office hours are helpful. I had never taken calculus before this class, and yeah calculus is hard, but I highly recommend Jenkins, he's the man!

Great teacher. Really patient, even when someone asks him a question in class that has been asked a billion times and we are all grumbling. He is happy and enthusiastic about his work. The tests are easy and definitely doable (not like he makes them anyway) and the homework doesn't take too much effort.
I tend to fall asleep... But that's only because it's Calculus at 8AM...
The class is difficult, and his tests are harder than the assignments. He's very willing to help you but he's one of those brilliant people that has a hard time explaining things.

Dr. Mangelson is really good at explaining the concepts at the start of each class. He spends about 20-30 minutes lecturing each class.  Even though the class is 3 hours, he is only there for about the first hour; after that, it's just the TAs. Most of the class is just work time, but you have to do it on the engineering building's computers.

To be honest, the labs are difficult starting out, but Dr. Mangleson and his TAs were a huge help to me and by the end, I had a good handle on the material. They are willing to break things down into their most basic steps to help us gain understanding. The TAs are also available outside class, which is good for more difficult labs.

This is one of the easiest and most interesting tech electives, in my opinion. The labs are really time-consuming, but pretty rewarding when the robots actually work. Dr. Mangelson is reasonable and he does a good job at conveying the material. His exams are some of the easier ones I've had in the ECEN department

Dr Kerry is super knowledgeable and cares for his students at their success! I loved how he taught. The lectures had nothing to do with his tests which was frustrating and he gives lots of readings! I did enjoy him and his class but it was definitely very difficult! I have lots of respect for him!

Royale carried this class.If you are looking to be a bookworm the next semester you are in for a real nice treat.He graded everything so so late,instructions were overkill.None of the lectures even relates closely to what his tests were.Stay clear away from this class at all costs.I took Chem this semester and I had more homework here than in Chem

You know that scene from Interstellar where he says, "MAKE HIM STAY!"? Well that was me. Wish I got out of that class when I got the chance. He gives an insane amount of homework and his lectures have nothing to do with what we're tested on. Really knowledgeable but he flaunts it - his class is more about philosophy than actual history.

A monument to disorganization and intellectual vanity.Assignments lack clarity, standards shift weekly, and lectures drift into boredom and self indulgence.The professor values flexing knowledge over understanding. Handwritten essays feel punitive.Time consuming and useless. The professor is rarely present yet demands attendance to usless lectures.

This class is an absolute ego trip for Dr. Kerry. Readings, assignments, lectures, and tests are all completely unrelated from one another. If you have any vague knowledge of history, the lectures will be pretty boring, but he will teach it like he is the first person who's ever talked about this. Read the prompts and rubrics closely on essays.

Professor Kerry cares, but his class is a disaster. The course is disorganized, assignments are confusing, and rubrics don't match prompts. A crazy amount of work, take useless quizzes, and memorize useless facts with almost no actual teaching. The workload is overwhelming, lectures are off-topic. This is the worst history class I've ever taken.

Do not take this as a GE unless you want to dedicate your entire life to reading books and writing essays. I had to take this as a senior and I've never experienced a class with such a ridiculous workload. Steer clear if you want an easy general.

Professor Kerry was an interesting Professor. There were tons of readings and papers due every week. His lectures were very interesting but didn't have anything to do with the readings. He is super caring and understanding though and wants you to succeed in his class.
Dr. Kerry is the best professor at BYU. full stop. Each lecture is exciting and informative. He engages with everyone in the class and the back-and-forth banter is fun

Dr.Kerry is the bestest professor ever. He cares about his students and their success very much! Only criticism was that a lot of us were confused about expectations for assignments. But Dr.Kerry is extremely understanding and wants everyone to succeed. He's also the smartest person I think I've ever met. I would take his class over and over again.

This class was one of the most transformative I have taken at BYU, largely thanks to Dr. Kerry! I have never felt a professor care for my learning experience so personally. He even showed genuine concern for me outside of class too. I never truly worried about my grade because I knew Dr. Kerry would reward thoughtfulness and hard work. 1000/10.

Dr Kerry is the best! He is so knowledgeable and has so much to teach about world events. He respects student opinions and loves to hear our thoughts and ideas. Make sure you look at the syllabus!!! It will tell you pretty much everything you need to know. Would love to take more courses from Dr Kerry!

Dr Kerry is deeply thoughtful & clearly cares about his students. However, I'd strongly advise any LGBTQ students to steer clear. Dr. Kerry is a phenomenal professor who truly cares for his students and wants everyone to grow intellectually. His class gave me amazing opportunities to learn, but it was also really difficult. I love Dr. Kerry, super inspirational and his lectures were super informative without being overwhelming, he's really good at explaining difficult concepts! Class wasn't bad either, just a few projects and papers. Worst thing about the class was the final, which was all on the textbook we barely touched and was super long.

He was very interesting and inspirational in his lectures, but it is too much work for a history I just need to check off. the midterm and final are long, the TA told me the midterm takes 5 hours. if the midterm is 28% of your grade and the final is 35%. So if you're not good at history or a bad test taker like me don't take it!
Best Professor at BYU! Highly, highly recommend taking if you really do want to learn and grow as a student and a person.

This class wasnt terrible but was not what I was expecting. Im not very interested in history & world civilization, if you are then this is the class for you. Throughout the course there is lots of readings a short papers & it made it seem like the lectures were irrelevant to the homework. You can tell he has taught at Princeton & Oxford

He's my favorite professor I've ever had. Extremely inspiring. I left every class feeling like a better person, as he extended the study of history far beyond the text book and applying it into our lives. Lost of reading, he assigned multiple full novels for us to read, but that was honestly one of my favorite parts. Life changing class.

Dr. Kerry gives a huge workload, but if you're willing to put in the effort you'll be fine. It's a really rewarding class and Dr. Kerry is a fantastic person, always willing to serve as a mentor and friend to his students.

Dr. Kerry is a wonderful man, however his lectures are hard to follow. They are also more like something you'd find at Harvard. I enjoyed the writing assignments, but the reading was quite heavy. The final was based on things you were expected to research outside of regular class material, which made it hard with my tight schedule.

Dr. Kerry's education was at Berkely, Chicago, Harvard, Oxford (2 phds), and Cambridge. He subscribes to the European pedagogy - no busywork - but BIG weights on 3 papers and 1 final. Look him up - served in House of Lords, renowned lecturer on the history of ideas - BYU is lucky to have him. More of a Harvard Lecture than "GE" class. Incredible.

This class is just writing. Dr. Kerry has 5-6 essays for the semester and nothing else. I didnt know that I was signing up for a writing class. It was difficult to follow what he was talking about and I didnt get much from his lectures. It was unclear what I needed to take notes on. Dr. Kerry is a good man but I wont be taking his classes again.
Incredibly helpful. I should have failed because I turned in everything late but he was willin to work with my schedule. The class isn't an "easy" A but you learn a ton and he wants to help you.

This was more like a philosophy class than a history class.  I didn't like it at all.  The whole class is about writing essays on many books you read, and you have to respond to a philosophical prompt question.  I don't recommend this class for anyone looking to just fulfill a general and get a decent grade.
This is the greatest professor! He is so knowledgable and makes learning interesting. Take this class or any class from Dr. Kerry!

Modern Germany: Look, I agree that Kerry is an intelligent, great guy, but this was the most difficult class I have ever taken, and was a big thorn in my side. His big "microfilm" project took me almost 20 hours to complete, 4 book reviews for a total of 12 pages, along with the research paper at the end. Be ready to put alot of time into class!!

I absolutely loved this class.  Professor Kerry is amazing.  I learned so much not just about the subject we were studying, but also about life in general.  He is hard and expects a lot, but he also loves to help you and work with you.

The most amazing professor I've ever had. No matter how cliche this sounds, he changed my entire perspective on life. He is absolutely brilliant, so humble, and he will do ANYTHING to help you succeed, no matter what your major. Supplies extra books to read, very cool. NOT an easy class, but you learn more than you can imagine. Best teacher ever.

The IDEAL professor. Wise, humble, and endearing, he helps you learn and takes a genuine care in your individual scholarship and goals. Every class was worth attending as he keeps it interesting and constantly challenges you. For those who just want to get a good grade and get out, Dr. Kerry isn't for you. Those that actually want to learn...

Absolutely brilliant!  He's a tough grader but don't let that scare you; just rise to the excellence he expects by working hard, and you'll be SO happy you took the class.  I learned an incredible amount from every class and every assignment.  He changed my life!  He transformed the way I look at learning.

The best professor I've ever met at BYU, hands down.  Best class I've ever taken; the 2 1/2 hours zoomed by every week.  I've become pretty disillusioned with GE's at BYU, but Dr. Kerry's classes are amazing and honestly life-changing.  He takes time for individual students like no other professor I've worked with, and he's been immensely helpful.

Kerry is a wonderful professor. If your interested in History or majoring in it, than it is the place for you. If not..beware. His lectures are meant to be intriguing and mind opening...not to prepare you for exams. If you have a passion for learning he is your man. I got a C in the class after all my reading but I still thik it was 100% worth it!

Prof. Kerry is the most brilliant professor I've had. The class is hard but you learn SO much. The lectures are amazing. He combines history with ethics and philosophy and even with a 2.5 hr class I never got bored. Don't take this class if you are not willing to do work. There is lots of reading but you can skim it.

to be fair he is a really great guy and cares a lot about his student's. on the downside he is very preachy and attendance is mandatory. he gives a lot of work but it's mostly just busy work (journaling, memorizing terms) but sometimes class was good. it's just too much work for what you get out of it and he is VERY flowery.

I've never met a professor that cares more about his individual students than he does. I forgot to take a test and he emailed me and offered me a chance to take it again. I wouldn't say the work he assigns is difficult but he grades very hard, he expects a lot for what he assigns, and he assigns relatively little. He's absolutely brilliant!

Hands down the hardest class I EVER took at BYU, but by far the most rewarding. Even though he was always behind on his office hours he was more than willing to sit down and talk. You get the grade that you put the effort in for. I recommend him to everyone!

This would be a good class to take if you are majoring in History, or if you like history. For a general it was pretty hard. I did all the reading, spent a lot of time on the two papers, and studied a lot for the final and ended up with an A-.  Lectures were really interesting (I thought), and thought provoking. Dr. Kerry is a pretty cool guy.

Dr. Kerry-nice guy but class was awful.dont go to class,he even tells you that you're never tested on lecture material.only one exam,the final,an essay test.often late for class,came30 min late for final!he only came after someone emailed him!lots of books,papers graded pretty hard.grade is mostly 2 papers and final.i would not recommend this class

Supposedly great, but only so so! HE WINS THE OVERRATED CONTEST. Though I was told he cared for is students more than any professor, I found this was not true. Dr Kerry is hands down the best professor at BYU.  Taking classes from him has made me a much better student.  You will have to work very hard, but it is totally worth it.

I took the class because I was told he was awesome, but I didn't like the class at all.  He's very nice and smart, and when he lectures it's pretty good.  But he's always late to class, he's a bit patronizing at times, and treats the class like it's a 490 class (all about writing a research paper).  I guess it just wasn't what I was hoping.

Amazing teacher, good man. Very smart and thought provoking. His class isn't a boring lecture its engaging and requires you to think and formulate opinions, so be prepared to work but also to learn about the subject and yourself

Scholarly, respectful, unbiased. The most scholarly teacher at BYU. He is interesting and makes you think. His class requires you to think, but all the work is interesting and never dull. My favorite teacher at BYU.

Dr. Kerry is one of the most brilliant professors I have ever had the privlledge of taking a course from. While his course is demanding it is definitely worth it. I never had a hard time paying attention in class even though it was two and a half hours long. He really cares about his students and their learning. Best professor I have had at BYU.

Professor Kerry is amazing. I like, want to be him. He really cares about students. He wants  them to actually learn and think for themselves. He genuinely wants everyone to succeed but he will not call poor work good just because he cares about you. He is a pusher. But awesome. Best teacher I've ever had. Brilliant.
Great teacher, hard work but you know he cares.  You earn the grade you get.  I'd take a class from him again in a heart beat.
Fascinating class!!  I highly recommend taking a class from Dr. Kerry.  This was one of the hardest classes I've had at BYU, but it was worth it.

Dr. Kerry is incredible. I have yet to have a teacher so dedicated and so qualified. The man is brilliant and confident but quite the opposite of pompous. He will never be unkind but he also doesn't let unintelligent comments go without being corrected. This was the best class I have had at BYU.

Kerry actually cares. so intense, but so worth it.  i went in to talk to him about an assignment i was stressed about, he bent over backwards to help.  Still remembers my name and talks to me every time he sees me, and i was the quite kid in the corner that never spoke.  Best teacher i've ever had.  best class ever.

Wow, this is the most intense human being I have ever met. He probably never sleeps. He analyzes everything (even the words of your prayers) down to the most minute detail.  Very intellectual, very intense. Be on your guard when you open your mouth around him, because he'll make you realize that you've said something stupid.

Omigosh! I can't say enough good about this man! So smart, so compassionate and dedication like you rarely see at the collegiate level. I loved this class. Yes, he is demanding and you really have to pay attention to the lectures, but because he's so wonderful you want to do well for him. He's SO COOL & an extrememly interesting man. Lucky wife. :)

Class is crazy hard.  It is interesting subject material, but way too much reading.  Tests are extrememly hard, and you have to memorize what exact people and what they thought about everything even when they were only mentioned in passing.  He is a very smart man, but this class is HARD!
Dr. Kerry is amazing. Although his class is difficult, Dr. Kerry loves interacting with students and wants to see students succeed. Large amounts of reading and writing are required.

Dr. Kerry was passionate about teaching history, relating the human experience, and passionate about helping his students both academically and personally.  He taught me some great lessons.  I was lucky to have him.

amazing- this is the best class i've ever had. dr. kerry is the most intelligent man i've ever met and will literally stay until one a.m. in his office just discussing ideas with you. very difficult classes, lots of reading- but the material is phenomenal

Dr Larsen is an awesome teacher! this class taught me so much. He has lectures on one day and case studies on the same topic the next day, which is super helpful to prepare well for quizzes and tests. He knows so much about medicin, but doesn't judge students for gaps in knowlage. He tested on important key topics and not random facts.

He worked as a pediatric neurologist for his career and now teaches neuroanatomy and neuropathology. It's a crime not to take a class from him. Neuroanatomy is hard regardless of who you take it from, but Dr. Larsen is so encouraging and has incredible lectures and videos of his own patients with conditions you learn about in class! He's amazing!

By far one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. That being said it is also by far the hardest class I have ever taken. The class moves fast and you have to get your stuff down. there is a 10 question quiz every week and it does actually affect your grade. He is concerned, and he loves his subject.

Dr. Larsen was a great professor and always willing to share his knowledge with those who are willing to learn. The class material was not difficult but requires studying (like any good class). There were weekly reviews that are KEY to doing well on quizzes and exams.

This was a very well organized class. I knew exactly what I needed to study because he gave us a list of learning objectives. Also incredibly knowledgeable! Feel free to pick his brain about anything!

Dr. Larsen is an extremely knowledgeable neurologist who is very passionate about neuroscience and medicine. Neuroanatomy is basically the neuro unit of medical school, and Dr. Larsen taught at medical schools for many years. He is a wonderfully kind man, extremely helpful and clear, and always ready to help out the students. Take 360 from him.

Dr. Larsen used to be a practicing Doctor, so he has an awesome perspective that other professors don't have! His lectures were very engaging, and he often showed videos of his patients that he diagnosed. This class truly increased my love of the brain and the human body. Class isn't too hard if you just do weekly readings.

Dr. Larsen is the best. He is a retired pediatric neurologist and shows examples of his own patients in class! Dr. Larsen's learning objectives are very clear and he offers several extra credit opportunities. If you study, you can succeed. You'll have chances to take Brown or Matheson for other classes, take Larsen!

I loved taking neuroanatomy from Dr. Larsen and recommend it to everyone. Generally, this class is hard but he does a great job at teaching the material. I thought his quizzes and tests were fair. I think he offers his students a ton of benefits because he is a trained pediatric neurologist which really shows when you get to case studies.

I loved Dr. Larsen's Neuroanatomy class and would recommend it to all neuroscience majors. He teaches in a very creative and charismatic way. He cares so much for each of his students and genuinely wants each one to succeed. Neuroanatomy is a tough class, but taking it from Dr. Larsen makes sure it is a fun and interesting class.
blamed the class when the average score on the exam was lower than every other neuroanatomy class. Nice guy but didn't really teach to the quizes.
I would recommend going through Brown or Matheson instead. Both are much better options that teach more closely to the quiz/exam material and don't blame the students when exam score averages drop.

Dr. Larsen is great. He knows what he is talking about, loves it, loves students, and is really sincere and honest about his expectations. Highly recommend this great man as a teacher. Hes kind of old school, which is the best part.

Dr. Larsen is an amazing professor. He's kind, humble, and upfront about his expectations. Grades are based off of about 10 weekly in-class quizzes, the midterms, and final. Dr. Larsen is an awesome professor and is very enthusiastic about teaching. He is a retired pediatric neurologist and taught at medical schools for many years, so he really knows his stuff! Dr. Larsen knows his stuff. It's clear that he knows the brain inside and out, and all of that knowledge comes from practical field experience! It's clear he's no stranger to teaching either. I loved this class! I would take all of my neuroscience classes from Dr. Larsen if I could. Really nice, very knowledgable and teaches simply. Study tip: Make flashcards! This is one of my favorite classes I have taken at BYU and I love professor Larsen. He cares that his students do well and takes the time to help each student. He clearly is passionate about the subject matter and Ian very knowledgeable. He was a doctor before and worked at UNMC too so he has lots of firsthand experience and knowledge.

Amazing professor! He is so passionate about the subject matter and makes a challenging subject enjoyable and understandable. Clear class structure, well organized. Study well for the tests and quizzes and you'll do fine.

There's a lot of bad reviews here, and though the course was hard and information-dense, I thought he did a good job highlighting the important things and explaining concepts. All of his lectures have detailed illustrations, too.

This is the worst class you could ever take. I took it online to have more flexibility, WRONG! Assignments are due in the middle of the day and he is the pickiest grader. Too bad there isn't a rating lower than 1...
Rude in his grading and unnecessarily hard, doesn't help but his responses are condescending. Tests are also very difficult, the test averages were below 50%
I didn't listen to the bad reviews, but please listen to this one and don't take from him. You will regret it.

Avoid taking MMBIO241 with Prof. Evans if possible. He sets an unreasonably high bar and seems to delight in making the class overly difficult. However, using Unstuck ai and other study tools can help mitigate the challenge.

Ya it's all true, I did well in this class but it felt like the class was designed to work against you. Dr. Evans assumed the worst of people and graded very harshly.
