Dr. Savage is an amazing lecturer! We had a sub for a week and we were dying to have him back when he got back! I really struggle with chemistry, but he teaches very well and is so enjoyable. Tips: Don't sit too far back (he only uses blackboard and chalk) Organize/categorize and leave spaces in your PAPER notes (he goes back and adds things a lot)

This class is hard but Savage is easily my favorite professor. He's super funny, he made organic chemistry interesting and difficult concepts understandable. If you put in the time you can be successful. TAs were a life saver and Savage loves to have students come to him with questions. He'll make you love ochem. Don't take ochem from anyone else!

I love Dr. Savage! He's so smart, but not condescending and helps you elevate your understanding. You definitely want to be prepared to study/work EVERY DAY or you WILL fall behind. He's very clear about expectations and will go over tests with you and try to give you point back. Everything is free response, go to TA reviews and you'll be great.

Dr. Savage is an amazing professor. He is so smart (had a phone meeting with the FDA during class one time about something he helped develop), but he still explains things in a way that anyone can understand. He made learning ochem fun. The tests are difficult, but they are completely fair. His lectures are amazing, but he doesn't use powerpoints.
Fantastic lectures, willing to help in any way he can, do your part and he will help with the rest. Dont. Miss. Class.

Professor Savage is a really wonderful teacher! It was a hard class, but he did a wonderful job of explaining and applying the material to the students. He doesn't use a textbook, so you can't be tested on anything that he doesn't teach in lecture. To do well, you really do need to review the material often and probably go to some TA reviews.

Challenging course, but put in work everyday and go to TA labs and you'll be set. Everything you learn is so relevant to life, so it's super enjoyable. Material from lectures isn't posted anywhere, so make sure you go and take good notes. Everything on tests is from lectures, weekly quizzes & problem sets. This was my favorite class and professor!

I loved the way professor savage taught! The material is difficult and be prepared to study everyday. There are no powepoints and it is very lecture heavy. Take crazy good notes and try to attend all the lectures. The TAs are lifesavers! Loved this class

Professor Savage is a good professor and he is very good at explaining concepts, he just moves very fast. CHEM285 is a hard subject, and he expects that you continuously study everyday. There is a weekly quiz given every Friday, and his tests are free response, so you better know your stuff. The TA's do an amazing job trying to help so go to them!

Dr. Savage is by far the best professor I have had so far. He is so smart and knows how to teach students. Go to lectures and write down everything! There are ta review sections every week, and I recommend going to at least 1 or 2 every week. They will help you ace the weekly quizzes. This class is hard, but study your notes and you will succeed!

Dr. Savage is literally a genius and the best professor I ever had. He made tough material like organic chemistry seem fun and understandable. However, it is a 4 credit class, and as such, if you want a good grade you HAVE to go to every lecture (even though attendance isn't graded). Make sure you go to at least one TA review a week.

He clearly loves the material. He takes the class in super depth and his tests are HARD. He went past what any other teacher went over. I recommend taking it from a different teacher. I got an A-, but I went to 7am reviews, skipped classes to go to his office hours and spent all of my time for this class. He loves his students but makes you suffer.

Honestly, Dr. Savage is the best professor I have had at BYU. The class is hard, but not ridiculously so. I have never looked forward more to a class in my life. I hate studying, yet I actually liked studying for this class. I wish he taught all of my classes at BYU.

Good choice. Great at explaining things and if you study for the tests you will get an A. There are always a couple questions on the tests that are tricky but for the most part it fair. He is pretty entertaining but sometimes goes on tangents. It is less work than normal chemistry classes but is still a chemistry class so you have to study.

TAKE 285 FROM DR. SAVAGE!! I had heard about how hard this class was before I took it and it ended up being one of my favorite classes that I have taken at BYU. Dr. Savage is so good at explaining hard concepts and he is really fair in his grading. He really loves what he is teaching and genuinely wants to help you understand the class content.
This class is the easiest class I have taken so far. It is about 1/4 the difficulty compared to Chem 105. I studied about half hour a day and I still get 97 on the first exam.

Dr. Savage is a genius so sometimes gets ahead of himself but asking him to explain again always helped me and he was always willing. He told us to read the book but it is at such a lower level than he teaches at that it isn't worth it. This class was DIFFICULT but I genuinely enjoyed working my tail off for the grade I got. He made me love ochem!

Very knowledgable about chemistry, but is not good at teaching it. He is a higher level chemistry teacher, so he taught way above the level we needed to know. His tests are extremely difficult and only based on lectures that are not posted, so do not ever miss class. If you are not passionate about chem, do not take this class from him.

I'm sure Dr. Savage is a great person outside of the classroom, but this class was unnecessarily difficult. There is no actual way to study for his tests, and his tests are based solely off his lectures which do not include slides or information from the book. Good luck.

Every good thing the previous comments have said about him are true. I'm only taking a point of because he could learn how to use technology and post our grades online. And missing a day of class is hectic as there is very little online material to help and the textbook is pretty much useless. But be prepared to fall in love with chemistry.

Honestly, this became one of my favorite classes of the semester. I feel like I come out of class learning something valuable every day. However, the class can get very overwhelming if you don't stay on top of it. Study every day. Tests are pretty difficult, but going to the TA reviews every week helps. Go to class. It's very possible to do well.

Dr. Savage told my class that he decided we were "too good" for the Chem285 curriculum, so he decided to teach us a higher level of chemistry. The problem is that none of the concepts were in our textbook and he doesn't do powerpoints- so good luck reviewing after class. Also, missing one day can easily make you fail a test. Don't. Miss. Class.

The best professor I have had at BYU. Lectures are insightful and engaging and you learn everything there that you need to know. There is no homework or textbook, which I LOVED. This is the type of class we hope for as undergraduates - hard but well worth your time. With that said, if you are a textbook learner, this class might not be for you.

You must go to class. Again, you MUST go to class. None of the lecture material is on learning suite. He does not do powerpoints and a majority of the material you cannot find through google. You need 2 to 3 hours a night to study if you want a decent grade. However, I will say Professor Savage cares a lot and his office is always open to you.

Dr. Savage is a brilliant man. He is so passionate about chemistry, and he has ignited a flame within me for it! He explains difficult concepts very well. Class graded by 4 tests (200 points each) and HW/quizzes combined (200 points). Use the TAs, get a good study group, and USE HIS OFFICE HOURS! Your life will be changed if you take his class!

Dr. Savage was an amazing lecturer! He gave applications for the material so that it was actually interesting, which can be hard for an organic chemistry class. His quizzes were pretty simple, and his exams were tough, but the class was definitely doable. Take advantage of the weekly TA reviews and attend his test reviews so you can get some points

THE MAN. I've had to work harder than I ever have in my life for this class, but he has really instilled an appreciation for chemistry in me. He usually teaches higher level classes, but he's good at making sure everyone understands the new material. Tests are free response which was great because he'll give points back. Go to TAs and office hours!

Dr. Savage is an amazing professor and he really knows his stuff! This class is not as scary as some people make it seem. You have a problem set each week, which is your homework. Quiz every Friday. His exams are all worth 200 points and are free response, but his TA's have them all graded by the next week. He says to read the textbook, but its NA

His lectures were not good. He doesn't answer question well in person or during class. He doesn't use the textbook so it's hard to teach yourself the material. The tests are entirely free response and are difficult. I'd definitely recommend taking the class from someone else. I preferred taking it from Dr. Castle.

Dr. Savage's lectures are great (and absolutely necessary to attend if you want a good grade). He explains confusing topics as clearly as possible and asks for questions when students aren't understanding. His office hours are also helpful. And it can be difficult to have him for 352 if you didn't take 351 from him, but it is definitely doable.

Proffessor Savage takes a lot of time to prepare awesome lectures and you can tell he loves teaching. It's rare to see someone as successful at research to give as much time as he does to teaching well. You have to attend class and it takes more studying than your normal class but don't take it from anyone else.

Dr. Savage has a great lecture style, but since he doesn't use a textbook and doesn't assign homework, attending lecture is CRITICAL. It's a hard class, but if you make an effort to do well and are responsible enough to prepare for and review his lectures, it's possible to succeed in his class.

For those who were born after the Sermon on the Mount, fear not. You will feel as they of old after every Dr. Savage lecture: impressed, illuminated, and inspired. His very presence oozes supernal wisdom, yea, every uttered word commands the unabridged reverence oft reserved for men who have slain dragons with their bare hands.   Good professor.

I enjoyed taking Professor Savage's class. Sure it was a challenge and lots of time, but he is the best to do it. He doesn't require a textbook or any homework. The grade comes from a dozen quizzes and a few tests. You have to spend time out of class to seriously study to get a decent grade.

If you like learning how and why things work, he's the O Chem teacher for you. His lectures are fascinating and he teaches slowly and clearly so you can write everything down (no laptops allowed). Very tough grader on tests but the grading scale puts a nice curve in.

Arrogant guy, but good at teaching. Weekly quizzes were stressful, but they forced you to be on top of things.  Some of the things on the tests came out of nowhere, but if you have a knack for O Chem (I didnt) you could figure it out. All of the TAs were A+, use them! Youll learn a lot of cool stuff, but definitely not an easy A
Dr. Savage is great. He really helps you out if you need it. The tests are very tough. Go in for help and try to go to as many recitation sections as possible.

Dr. Savage is the best professor I have ever had at BYU.  He is a very good lecturer.  He doesn't use a book, which I loved because I do not learn well by reading things out of a text book.  His lectures are jam packed full of important information so you can't miss class, but he makes the class time so interesting that you really learn a lot!

He is pretty darn good at lectures. The only problem I had with him was that he expects you to read his mind. If you don't use the exact wording he wants then you won't get the points even when your explanation is SPOT ON. On my 1st exam the TA put "too long" on my explanation, then I got docked for being too concise on the 2nd. Truly savage!

He is so good at teaching! I hated Chem 105/106, but Dr Savage has helped me to love chemistry because he teaches the WHY behind everything. He won't expecting you to know something that has no evidence to support it. He is very reasonable and does not add tricky questions to his test. Take it from him!

Dr. Savage focuses on the "why" aspect of organic chemistry, makes you understand the real driving forces and background behind reactions and data you would straight up have to memorize with other ochem professors. He hates memorization. After both classes I see the world differently and developed a passion to understanding the "why" of stuff.

Dr. Savage is an awesome lecturer and freaking intelligent, but with that comes his arrogance... He can be pretty condescending at times. If you can stand that I would definitely recommend him. Best professor I have ever had and you will definitely leave the class viewing the world differently.

Dr. Savage is without doubt the toughest professor I've had at BYU.  That being said he gives incredible lectures and I learned a ton from him.  I'd recommend taking O chem from him, but this class will make you work are the tests are very difficult.  Don't buy the textbook.

Dr. Savage was a wonderful teacher. He was very respectful. His lectures were clear and he was more than happy to help during office hours. That said, this is a very difficult class. There is no required homework, but in order to do well you should plan on studying 1-2 hours a day, at least. Don't bother buying the book. I didn't

His style of teaching is crystal clear and he gives relevant quizzes.  There is no actual homework, because he lets you choose how much to study.  Sure, he tests hard, but that shouldn't deter you.  He focuses mostly on the why of chemistry and not memorization, which will prepare you best for the MCAT.  Attendance isn't taken but don't skip!

Savage's tests are very difficult. He is a great lecturer. I never thought I would enjoy learning about OChem, but here I am, signed up for the second half with him. Go to the TA reviews and review class notes carefully. And don't be surprised if the last test question is something you've never encountered.

Won't be an easy A, but Savage is by far the best teacher for it and will teach you to ask the kinds of questions necessary to understand the world. This level of critical thinking is invaluable (I'm talking to you, premeds), but also makes for some tough exams. Treats you like the adult you are. Useless out of lecture--use TAs!

His tests..................... Make sure you buy a gallon of ice cream before each one. Besides his tests though his class was awesome. He's great about giving points back if he thinks his TA's were sticklers in grading the tests, and he's very into his students' learning. Favorite chem class so far. Hard but rewarding class

This is an extremely hard class. Dr Savage is the best though. He teaches the material so clearly that you will learn just by going to class. His test are very hard but don't get discouraged. Put in the work and you will succeed. Go to multiple TA lectures they teach differently and tell you what to study for the test.
Awesome professor, and excellent lecturer and text-maker.

If you are not a chem major do NOT take Ochem from Savage.  I am a bio major and it was just too much for me. I loved how he focuses on the "why?" of chem, though. But he isn't very kind when you go ask him for help and makes you feel quite stupid. USE THE TAS! Other Ochem tests barely scratched the surface of what I needed to know for his class.

Dr. Savage, didn't prepare our class for the ACS, had ridiculously difficult exams, is kind of egocentric, didn't explain tricky concepts very well, loves to play "guess what's in my head", mocked students when they didn't know an answer or answered a question incorrectly, and was unpersonable during office hours.  To succeed, learn legilimency.

I left a review for Dr. Savage in 0415 and it was removed. I don't know if people are allowed to filter out bad reviews to make them appear better than they are but mine is no longer here. Dr. Savage wasn't willing to offer genuine help to me when I was struggling in the class. I tried to see him outside of class 2 times. A- is NOT the ave. grade.

Honestly, Dr. Savage is a great lecture teacher, but a very tricky tester.  I like chemistry but it is not my life and not something I love.  I am taking it because I need to.  I enjoy chemistry but Dr. Savage made it really hard.  Compared to other teachers, there is less structure, and in my opinion, he doesn't prep you well for tests or the ACS.

If you can, take Ochem from him!  He is clear in his explanations and entertaining in class.  Grading is 20% weekly quizzes, 80% exams.  He gives useful handouts throughout the class and posts a previous exam before each test so you know what to expect.  Homework is optional, but I recommend still doing it.

Doctor Savage is the man. He focuses on the "why" of chemistry opposed to memorizing the infinite amount of "what" there is. This gives his students a clear advantage but having said that it's a tough class. If you don't understand chemistry up to now, you'll have to make up for it. I wouldn't take it from anyone else if I did it again. Study hard.

Dr. Savage's tests feel impossible and the grading is kind of ridiculous. It's all or nothing on each of the questions and since there is no homework, it is kind of hard to practice for what is going to be on the test. The fact that there is no graded homework is nice but handouts with lots of practice problems would've helped in this class.

Dr. Savage is one of the best professors I've had at BYU of any subject. Organic Chemistry is tough, but he is able to break it down and teach it simply enough to understand on a deep, fundamental level, instead of just memorizing things. If you have to take OChem, take it from Savage.

Dr. Savage was one of my favorite professors! His class is not easy, but the material is very well presented and I learned more in this class than possibly any other class I have taken. Advice: always attend lecture, take good notes, study for the weekly quizzes from your notes, and don't read the book. You will love him!

Dr. Savage is amazing.  He really helps you understand how and why ochem works.  He is genuinely interested in his students and happy to get to know you and help you understand things.  I looked forward to this class every day.  I wouldn't take O-chem from anyone else and can only hope that my future chem teachers are like Dr. Savage.

Dr. Savage is easily the best teacher I've ever had. He makes o chem completely understandable. The TA recitations and weekly quizzes help a lot with preparing for the tests. His tests are difficult, but if you understand everything in lecture, you can figure all of the questions out. Don't buy the book, I never read it once.

He is the best professor I've ever had in my educational history. I'm not very smart, but if you go to all the TA review sessions, You'll get at least an A-. Grading is very fair. 90% is an A and/or top 10 is an A and so forth. Don't bother buying textbook. I never needed it. Highly recommended. You'll see the world differently after his classes.

Fantastic teacher.  If you're looking to take the MCAT I would take his class even if you're not a chem major.  His class is tough but by the end of both sections, the MCAT orgo is a freakin breeze in comparison.
He is the best in the chemistry department.  I wouldn't want any other teacher to explain this difficult material.

Very, very good professor. Really cares about the students. He wants to help you understand everything. Pretty difficult class but gives you lots of help and explains everything SUPER well! Highly recommended.

Best professor I have ever had! I absolutely loved his class but it was hard! He will push you above and beyond but he will do everything he can to help you understand the material.  Go to all the recitations possible.  He is the bomb!
Dr Savage is an amazing teacher.  The class is really hard, but it is super interesting and he really makes the class interesting.  Super funny, super approachable, and super awesome!

Hard...overloads with information on every class period. Expects you to know things that he tells you but that you cannot check in the book or anywhere. No homework, but that is what makes it so hard. It is hard to tell if you are keeping up or not.

Best. Professor. Ever. Dr. Savage is what a teacher is supposed to be. He teaches deep understanding instead of memorization so you can generate the reactions on your own. He cares deeply about his students and offers many opportunities to discuss tests and receive help. Your mind will double in size.

This class is hard, but it is so worth it. Make sure you go to TA reviews and study well for quizzes and tests. Dr. Savage is amazing at teaching as well as making it applicable to everyday life. I would definitely recommend taking this class from savage. Just put in the work, and you can get an A.
Professor Savage was great! I would definitely recommend you take it from him.

His lectures were alright, his tests were extremely hard if you didn't study a ton. He didn't use the book at all. He says at the beginning of class that he's going to go "above and beyond" the book. Which he does.
very professional and helpful...
Great professor. I had to work hard in the class, but he explained concepts well and showed interest in the students. I would recommend him to anyone taking organic chemistry.

By far my favorite chemistry class at BYU. Super applicable and interesting. Get a good study group and meet consistently, that is the best way to do well. Focus on the challenge problems from the back of the chapters as well, other than that I never read the book (I just focused on lecture notes) and I got an A in the class. Have fun!

Dr. Savage is one of the best teachers I have ever had! He makes sure that you actually learn why things happen and do not just memorize. His wants you to succeed, and gives you all the tools necessary. If you study getting an A is not too difficult.

Awesome. I was terrified of taking Ochem, but I really loved going to lecture. He does an amazing job of explaining difficult concepts in an understandable way. It is most important to him that we learn and understand what he teaches. He is very accessible and approachable. There are tricky questions on exams, but he is generous with points.

I agree whole heartedly with all the previous statements! Awesome teacher! Make sure you take it from him! I have a roommate who took it the same semester as me from a different teacher and doesn't understand the half of what I've learned in Savage's class

Dr. Savage is one of my favorite professors of all time!  He completely changes how you approach classes for the rest of your college career.  Ochem is hell if taken from other professors but enjoyable if you take it from Savage.  TAKE IT FROM SAVAGE!!

From what I heard, I never though I could enjoy Organic Chemistry but he does an excellent job of making the material and the class in general interesting and entertaining. It certainly was one of the harder classes I've ever taken, but it was certainly one of my favorite. His tests are tough, but if you understand the material you can get an A.
Best prof. I ever had. His class taught me how to study for the rest of my schooling. Best O Chem professor by far.
Great teacher, keeps things interesting and you actually understand. Not an easy class, but will prepare you well for 352.

Guy Dorius & Dr. Savage are my absolute favorite professors at BYU. I LEARNED & UNDERSTOOD Chemistry thanks to Savage. Study lecture notes & make up your own practice problems. Get help from him or the TAs. Study well & take time to think on exams. It's crazy to say it, but I enjoyed Organic Chemistry. I almost changed my major.

His lectures actually clarify instead of confusing you even more. tests are a beast, but they aren't unreasonable. The key is to NOT GET BEHIND and DO PRACTICE PROBLEMS! You will learn faster and more efficiently by working out problems then you ever will by reading the book for hours. it goes so fast if you get behind you will never catch up.

Great teacher.  Does everything he can to make OChem interesting.  He is a born teacher.  If you study, you will understand.  I attribute my great score in the O Chem section of the OAT (Optometry Admissions Test) to Dr. Savage.  Take this class!
Most skilled teacher.  You will receive best understanding of chem.

Dr. Savage is probably the best professor I've had at BYU. I absolutely hated chemistry before his class, now I love it. His lectures are very organized, and you don't really use the text at all, which is good because it is confusing. His tests are really hard but doable. They stretch your understanding and make you think. Awesome teacher!

Dr. Savage is a great teacher. He knows exactly what he's talking about and explains things very well. His tests stretch your understanding and are difficult, but the class is graded on a curve. I learned a lot from him, and I'd highly recommend him.

Prof. Savage was awesome! He interacts with his students really well and makes O. Chem easy to understand (as easy as it can be anyways). He doesn't just teach what happens, he teaches "why" things happen. His tests are somewhat hard though, but I think that makes his class better because I feel it helped me learn more.

Dr. Savage is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. He shows respect to all of his students and was always willing to help during his office hours. His class is not difficult if you pay attention during lectures and learn the reaction patterns he teaches. And take notes on the random facts (like paint drying etc) because he always tests on it

Savage really is a good teacher, he knows a lot about chemistry and he loves it.  But he is not easily available and seems to make things harder than he needs to. He plays favorites a bit with students, and he tests on material from future sections way too much.  Nice guy but I would recommend another proffesor.

Savage is an amazing lecturer!!  I started out reading the text, but eventually stopped because it wasn't doing me any extra good.  His tests are beasts, and you have to study like mad for them, but given that you don't have to do much else, the class is very little work and a lot of good information.

Dr. Savage makes this about as easy as it's going to get.  He was helpfull, but I rated him a 3 on helpfulness based on availability.  I had trouble finding him or a TA with enough time to help me with all my questions.

Dr. Savage is the best teacher I have had at BYU.  Everyone says that it is really hard, but I am not sure why.  Dr. Savage is such a good teacher that if you listen very closely during class, that is enough.  I didn't ever read the book the whole semester and I got an easy A.  That's how good he is.
Is class is way too hard and for no reason. Everyone I talk to in other OChem classes have it much easier. In addition, he is a complete jerk outside the classroom.

Professor Savage enjoys what he does, that is why he still teaches even though he's tenure. He is brilliant and explains things in class so they're easy to understand...That's where the warm and fuzzies end. He's tough to talk to. He won't set up appointments outside of office hours, so if you have class during his hours...tough.

Savage is a Savage!  He writes test that are 4 pages long and makes questions on the fourth page that he expects few students to be able to answer.  He is a great teacher  but I think the test are way to complex.  He also claims that you can stop by his office for help but then when you are there you feel like you are a burden to him.
His teaching style will shock you and make you mad at first. Once I figured it out, I only apent about 3 hours studying outside of class. He is a great teacher...and very helpful.

I took Nielson and bombed. I retook it with savage and I think he made all the difference.  Sure it was my second time around, but he was much more interesting to listen to and he explained things much better.  He does grade tougher but what he doesn't tell you is that he'll curve it all at the end of the semester to make up the difference.

I was dissapointed with this class.  One of Dr. Savage's favorite teaching methods was saying, "If you don't know this, you should be worried," while it was apparent that all of the people around me were lost.  I suppose this class will be a lot better, though, when there is a recitation section attached.

This was, as you would expect, a very difficult class, but Dr. Savage really boiled things down to the basics and made what you need to know feel very reasonable and managable.  Still a lot of work but not impossible.  I definately recommend him.

He cares a lot about the students learning the material... not just to do well on the test, but really understanding the concepts.  If you take good notes, and study hard, you will have the fundamentals down.  His tests are challenging but reasonable.
Very well spoken and he knows his crap.  He can explain like no other professor I have ever had...and this is my 5th year at BYU!
Best science professor I've had!  Very passionate about Ochem and lectures are usually entertaining.  Tests are very hard; he makes you work for a good grade.
awesome teacher, very helpful and funny. his class is hard but if you study the notes you'll be fine.

Very hard class--but worth it.  He was an effective teacher and new all of us (hundreds) by name.  Tests are very difficult--especially the 4th page.  O-chem is not memory, though, you understand it--for real.
Dr. Savage may know his stuff, but his only goal is to make the class hard.  If you want a chemistry class without the incredibily hard stuff on test..do not take from Savage.

He is the best professor I have ever had.  He teaches really difficult material really well.  But you have to study hard!  I mean really hard, and that doesn't guarantee you a good grade.  His tests are impossible.

He clearly loves his job and is very humble. Because it's a blended class, most of the learning is done on your own by reading the textbook and watching the lecture videos. However, you do have to go to class to complete the case study analysis. While he did help a little on the case studies, it largely felt like we didn't do much in class.

Ok. Not amazing, not bad. Boring lectures and graded attendance like we're 4th graders. He does trust us to not cheat on exams so they aren't proctored, that helped testing anxiety SO much so I felt much more calm and confident going in.

It's a lot of content over the summer so be prepared to have a heavy workload. Bro. Conrad is very lecture-heavy and doesn't go over the math very much.Prepare to sit in the class and hear him ramble for a long time.  If you do the math problems and READ then you'll be fine. He does let you use notes and your textbook for your tests which is nice.

Brother Conrad is a fantastic teacher, and really knows what he's talking about. The class has a pretty heavy workload for just a term, but in a semester I'm sure it's much more manageable. Despite the work, the lectures are super helpful and the TA's are always ready to help. He offers tons of extra credit, and gives you tons of resources.

If you do the assigned homework and understand it you should be alright. He requires students to attend his lectures for participation credit. Be prepared to spend thirty minutes talking about some spiritual implication that doesn't matter. He doesn't spend enough time reviewing for the tests. So just study on your own during class.

Brother Conrad is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. Our class was small, but he would offer to meet with students who had to miss class or did not full understand the material. The homework is easy if you go to class or do your reading. I would definitely recommend taking this class from him!
good

She was honestly great. The people are hating on her cause they didn't do the bear minimum. She knows what's on the test and gives you everything you need in class if you pay attention. In the blended class if you understand the read and learns you'll be fine. The tests can be specific but it's really about knowing how to apply what you learned.

If you are thinking of taking this class for a GE, don't do it. Interesting information, but there was a ton of content. Dr. Williams is really nice, but stuck very strictly to the curriculum, and was not open to discussing newer health studies that are now embraced in the new 2025 food guide.

Professor William's class was difficult but I learned a lot. She gives you all the resources (practices homework, practice activities, comprehensive quizzes, carefully picked TA's, etc.) to prepare you for each test and the final. Her class is set us very well. If you have to take this test I would definitely  recommend this teacher.

Dr. Williams is great! She gives just the things that you will need to know for the test and helps you practice. A few assignments here and there, but make sure you do the read and learns before class, those will help you remember the content. Tests are very application based so make sure you know the material.

To do well study in groups!!! All of the info comes from the lectures and the slides aren't really set up in a way where you can get much information from them. Type as fast as you can in class, and then go over the study guides with your classmates to fill in any gaps! This class was hard, but honestly so much fun! You'll learn a lot.

Her reviews are extremely vague. This class, especially the final, all felt like I was being set up for failure. The tests usually go over the most obscure things. Her final is AWFUL. I put in 5+ hours studying each day, feeling confident in my application of knowledge skills, only for it to be insanely difficult for no reason.

Professor Williams was great! Overall, this class was really interesting. The material is super applicable to your life and she did a good job teaching it. The classes were pretty lecture heavy and it was pretty important to do the reading to make sure you learned everything but it was a fun class.

I really liked Dr. Williams. She's super nice, understanding, and knowledgeable about nutrition. However, taking notes during lecture is tough because her slides don't have much info on them and you kind of just have to write down everything she says. Overall good class, but it isn't organized in a super intuitive way

Get assignments in on time over anything else!! It's not too hard if you like nutrition and can read a long boring textbook. She does this thing where everything is due at 5pm thinking we'll go to bed early but I just stay up until 2 am the night before because I know I can't get it in by 5 the next day if my classes end at 2pm.

I absolutely loved this class! I would say there is a bit of reading so read the textbook if you want to succeed because the tests have a lot to do with reading. her lectures were super helpful to understand the textbook more! Make sure to read before class and you will be set.

The lectures were not helpful. The tests were beyond difficult, and I had to study for an insane amount of time to get the grades I wanted. The study guides were also not helpful whatsoever. A nice lady, but I would not recommend her as a professor.

We stayed on schedule and learned all of the material on time for the exams. The exams were relatively easy but the reading felt disheartening at times. I often skipped the readings and studied based solely on my class notes and that worked out well enough for me.

Took online-FRUSTRATING.  Page numbers assigned in modules don't align with book pages. Lectures don't match the same terminology as the readings or tests. Beware the mineral/vitamin/water chapters. I studied for over 8 hours and only made minimal progress. When I pointed out these mistakes, was ignored by TAs. Learned a lot, though.

This class had a lot of real world applications, and I loved that she connected it to the gospel. Homework assignments and discussion posts were easy. The test were not easy. There was lots of information to memorize, and I often felt like what was on the study guide didn't match what was on the test. I studied for so long just to get okay grades.

I recommend taking the online version if this professor is your only option. Her lectures weren't helpful, and you'll need to rely on self-study to do well. If possible, choose a different class for your GE requirement. I got an A in Chem 105 and Math 113, but this class required much more time and effort to achieve the same grade.

She does not know how to teach in class, and the material covered does not align with the questions in the testing center. Attending her classes is not helpful; I learned the most from the textbook. Do not take a class from her.

There is a lot of reading before class, and it usually takes me about 4-5 hours to finish the connect homework and the readings. Some topics she said are online reading and self-studying, and she will not cover them in the lecture.

From what I've heard Prof Williams is the best to take for NDFS 100. She was great and made lectures engaging and provided real world application that helped terms stick in your head. Lectures are super important for tests. Tests can be challenging so definitely study hard and do the text book readings to get all of the content

I really enjoyed learning the material, and I feel like the lectures well-reflected what was on the exams (though the exams often seemed more confusing). Dr. Williams was also more than willing to answer questions during or after class, and she did whatever she could to make sure we learned the material.

Such a great teacher! Made nutrition interesting and gospel-focused! The lecture slides had little information on them so it was important to go to class. The tests were hard because they used application questions instead of just asking you to memorize facts. That being said, it really helped you learn the material.

I felt that what was talked about in class was not reflected on the tests. It felt as though the homework and the lectures were very basic and the tests were not. Other than that, I felt that Dr. Williams was passionate about the class and her strength was in making the lectures interesting.

I took her hybrid class so it was a lot of online work but you can find everything for NSDF 100 on Quizlet so if you use that and the provided study materials you'll do great on the tests and quizzes. I recommend showing up to class or you'll get lost and behind fast.

I honestly liked Williams. tests are \difficult but if you work all the way along, you're fine. There is a lot to memorize but thats how nutrition is regardless of the teacher. Test questions can be specific, so know your stuff. I spend like an hour/week on non-test weeks and usually study about 4-6 hours for each test and have done really well.

I usually consider myself good at getting along with professors, but Dr. Williams does not play nice. The lecture and slides are unclear and the review worksheets are garbage. The learning objectives dont reflect what's on the test. The slides dont even match the information in the textbook. LET THIS BE YOUR WARNING. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Don't take this class unless you have to!! Dr. Williams' lectures were hard to follow and there wasn't the same information on the slides posted as the ones she went over in class. Her tests are unnecessarily hard as they test on things that weren't taught in class or in the book. I also felt the information presented was outdated. Good luck

The slides were not very detailed so you did not have everything you discussed in class to study unless you took really explicit notes in class. You have three test and final and if you fail one it is hard to make an A in the class. You also have about 1-2 homework assignments and 1 quiz a week. Interesting content but YOU HAVE TO STUDY A LOT!

Did not enjoy this class. Professor's slides were not very informational, so it made it difficult to review for tests. The tests were also super specific. Seemed to be unnecessarily difficult for a 100 level class. I did learn a lot, but I'd only recommend taking this class if you have to.

Honestly, I loved this professor, but I wish her tests weren't super specific. You are expected to memorize a ton of material and then apply it to different situations. She threw things in we did not cover in class or we just briefly covered, so make sure to do the reading as well. This was a great class, just more difficult than I expected

Taken as a blended class which was not the most fun. Pay attention in lectures and do not skip class unless you want to be confused. She specifically goes through in class what she wants you to know for the exams. Take good notes! You cover lots of material so start studying early. Read the textbook for help and do the practice exercises online.

The tests included really randomly specific questions. If you don't study everything completely you will not do well on tests and quizzes. This class was interesting but more difficult than I expected. Dr. Williams is very sweet and gave interesting lectures.

The main problem here is the hybrid curriculum. Having 1/3 of the class online is an absolute nightmare (particularly when the online resources are horrendous). Very test heavy, but if you do the reading and adequately prepare for the midterms and final you can pass . Bad lecturer but if you miss class you will do significantly worse on the tests.

Class was tough. Exams were especially difficult and so many quizzes that are worth so little points. Don't go in expecting this class to be easy, you really have to do your part by memorizing a lot, reading, and take good notes. She cares but she also goes by the rules, a lot. don't expect her to go easy on you. good luck

One quiz per unit, three exams, and a couple (not hard) projects are what go on your grade. You'll do great as long as you show up and take notes. Don't rely on the lecture slides, and I would highly recommend doing the learning activities.

Dr. Williams is a very intelligent woman and knows her stuff. If you are planning to major in NDFS/Food Science/ Dietetics, I recommend you take this class from her to actually prepare you for future classes. If you're taking this class for a GE, maybe it's not for you.

Dr. Williams is not bad, she taught everything that was tested. Know that you shouldn't even THINK about skipping class, take VERY good notes, and study everything she said in lecture especially (book is helpful, but lecture is more important). Conceptually it's straightforward, but the subject requires memorizing. I did not think tests were hard.

You can tell she really cares for the students and believes in every one of us that we can handle difficult things. If she didn't care she wouldn't push us as hard to think critically for the exams. She really allows us to strive for the grade we want. All we need to do is do our part by attending lectures, reaching out to the resources she provide

I loved Dr. Williams. You could tell she was very passionate about her lectures and made them interactive, constantly taking comments and questions in the middle of her lectures and always had a review day the class before a test where she and TA's walked around answering questions. This is a class everyone should take just for life to be healthy.

Prof. Williams is the best choice for this class. Even though she doesn't take attendance, you will want to go to class because she says things in class that you need to know that aren't on her slides. She makes the class interesting and fun and has a real passion for it. She is pretty accessible outside of class and will help you out if she can.

I had to withdraw from this class because it was so test heavy and I felt like the tests were super hard and not based on the reading at all. You defenitly have to study and not take this class with any other classes. She is super knowledgable but her tests are so hard and not based on class material.

genuinely was the only class I hated. Content was interesting, just a bad professor. quizzes are worth such little points but there were so many questions and exams are worth so much. She gives no extra credit and the quizzes are your assignments. If you do bad on her exams there's probably no way to make up for it.

There are people who just shouldn't be professors, she is one of them. She treated me unkindly when I didn't understand something and was very passive aggressive about it. Don't take her class, if you need to take one and she's the only option, just wait till next semester.

If you would like a condescending professor who makes fun of students during class, has no rubric for grading but grades harshly and very subjectively, has 2 other instructors teach the course during the semester, and takes points back on assignments even though the TA originally gave you 20/20? Then, Dr. Williams is for you! I hope she sees this.

She teaches you in a way where she assumes you understand everything she's teaching. The exams were very difficult, no matter how hard you study for it you're not going to receive the grade you want because the questions are so specific and things she never spoke of during the lecture. Wouln't take her class if I knew it was going to be like this.

Williams' teaching was vague and she didn't go in depth at all with the concepts. Terrible teaching. TA's weren't useful at all either. Exams are heavy and most of the questions are application based but because of her teaching you don't understand the concepts as well as you should. Don't take her class unless you want to fail.

This was a somewhat difficult course but Dr. Williams was really involved and available to all her students. It's a class where it's definitely not weird to ask questions during lecture if you don't understand something. The tests were the hardest part for me.

Professor Williams herself is a really nice person and is very passionate about nutrition. However, this class was way too hard for a 100 general class. It was very fast-paced and you had to memorize so many specific facts, numbers, and definitions. I could barely keep up. Would recommend finding an easier professor for this class.

This is definitely the hardest class I've taken. It seemed like the test asked things we didn't really learn from the reading. It was a lot of homework. I've heard mixed opinions; some people said it was super easy or super hard. You won't pass if you don't show up to class. The professor was nice though and willing to help when needed.

Professor Williams talks VERY FAST during lectures, so get ready to write quickly. Her tests were pretty hard, she seemed to test on knowledge of little facts said during the lecture rather than knowledge of a concept. She was did a good job of engaging students during the lectures, which is hard to do for a zoom class.

I took this class instead of Bio as I am not a science person. Class was all on zoom due to COVID, and she rushed through most classes, with little in depth prep for tests. No option to see the slides after class, and the amount of tests were nuts for a GE class (We had like 5 total). I would rather take bio a hundred times than take this class.

She was a fine professor, but nothing amazing. Some of her lecture power points were not super well organized and jumped all over the place. Slides were available to review after class so that was nice. Tests require a good amount of studying. No opportunities for extra credit.

P. Williams treats you like your a pro so become one or you'll fall behind. Do the reading before the lecture, try your best to follow along, and memorize early for the tests. She goes fast in class, and the online quizzes are not too bad if you read. Do well on the little things! I'm not a bio person and this was a great substitute!

This was probably my favorite class thais semester. Dr. Williams is the nicest person ever. You can tell that she cares about all of her students. The slides from her lectures are always available and her lectures were super clear and easy to understand. Definitely recommend taking this class.

Highly recommend this online course for an easy GE credit. I mostly used her video lectures rather than the textbook. Lots of short/easy activities to practice. A few easy discussion posts. A few bigger assignments where you just need to follow the rubric. Easy to do from home and at your pace. Just do the work for an easy A. Organized really well.

I felt that this class should be informative and basically common sense to a lot of us. However, I felt that it was basically a memorization course. Yeah sure there were easy common sense things but the tests were tricky and there are so many tedious details that had to be memorized. It was harder than what an entry level nutrition class should be.

Professor Williams is great. Lectures are clear, concise, and easy to follow. I found the textbook almost unnecessary since almost all of the material is covered in class. Not the most "fun" class, but I found the information I learned interesting and useful. Great class.

Honestly, every NDFS100 class has the exact same material. That being said--I did visit another professor one day because I was sick. It made me appreciate Dr. Williams's ways of teaching. She's clear, concise, and I don't think she is boring at all.

The class is the same material no matter who your professor is, so all the tests and assignments are generally the same for each NDFS 100 class. Professor Williams was a good lecturer and kept us involved in the class with discussions.

Professor Williams was a bit boring and dry, that being said, I also don't really care about the class she taught. If you need this class and want an A, take from her. But it's not the most interesting, in my opinion.
Good lectures, very clear on what we need to know about the tests.  Good assignments for making the information applicable to yourself.  Goes out of her way to help students who need help.
Attendance isn't strictly mandatory, but Dr. Williams is a great instructor. She makes class interesting and productive, and you'll do much better on the tests if you attend.
I really enjoyed this class

Dr. Williams is the best!! I would take her class over and over again. Super insightful and incorporates the gospel when appropriate, also. The assignments are given with a step-by-step instructions guide, so if you follow the instructions you basically get full credit. Her tests aren't too tough. LOVED this class!

Go to TA Reviews and the tests are a breeze!  This class is so relatable to real life, and I would take it again for sure.  The assignments are not difficult.  The lectures are interesting.  Don't ask stupid questions, or Dr. Williams will give you a "duh" response.
She is great teacher and the class is relatively easy if you attend and pay attention. The TA's hold reviews and tell you everything you need to know of the test. Definitely recommend the class!

Best teacher I have EVER had. She's upbeat but not in an annoying way. Really knows her stuff. Normally I don't like female teachers but she was awesome and I would totally make her my BFF. Also you'll learn a ton of useful things you can use your whole life. Half-listen to lecture and memorize the lists of vitamin functions(etc) and its an easy A.

This class is the bomb diggity! Dr. Williams does a great job teaching. the class is always interesting, and you'll never fall asleep haha. One thing though that kind of ruined my grade is I misread instructions for an assignment, and because I forgot to add something to the assignment I lost soooo many points. So be sure to read the instructions.

Dr. Williams is awesome! I love going to her classes every week and really learn something new each time. She follows the book really well, and the TA review sessions are just like the tests. There are group problems before every test, but they do help. There are weekly open-book quizzes online and 3-4 tests. I'd take the class again!

If you need to take intro to Nutrition, take it from Dr. Williams! The tests are so easy if you go to class and read the material. Literally, I almost got 100s on all of them. There's a lot of group work in class, which can be tedious, but overall an easy class that you actually learn a lot from.

Interesting class. Dr. Williams's lectures are easy to follow and are fairly interesting. There are a lot of tedious work to do though so just be prepared for that. Tests are fairly easy because a lot of the questions are common sense based.

She is very nice, upbeat, cheerful and always willing to help if you need to meet with her. Lots of quizzes but they're open book. Tests a little hard so do your reading, go to lecture and attend reviews by TAs. Study groups help a LOT for test prep. Lots of memorizing. Interesting course overall and if you do your part, you'll get a good grade.
She knows her course material well! Although it is definitely  a class you need to attend! Her quizzes are fine but her tests are rather difficult. Not my favorite course.

Take her! She's wonderful to listen to. I enjoyed every minute. The guide tells you exactly what to study. Don't expect to slide through without doing your part. Excellent teacher, excellent class. Worth the time and effort.

Dr Williams is absolutely fantastic! Print off the slides as she goes fast during lectures. She knows her stuff and is great to work with pleasant to listen to. This does not mean that the class does not require work, study, and reading, but it is laid out nicely and you will be glad you took the class. Study what's on the guide and go to reviews.

MUST go to class; she posts half blank slides online so you can't skip. She doesn't write the test; expect to NOT know about 20% of the information on every test. FRUSTRATING. Assignments/quizzes (open book) are easy, but the tests are over stuff you didn't cover. If you ask her a questions, she will give you a vague answer to what you DIDN'T ask.
He is a great guy, as long as you ask questions you will do good.

BIO165 is difficult without programming experience, but he does a great job walking you through concepts and building fundamentals in computational biology, especially compared to other intro CS courses. 165 has many assignments, but most of them do aid in better understanding of concepts and offer practice in problem solving and critical thinking.

Worst professor I've ever had. Extremely disorganized, disrespectful, and a harsh grader. Exam-heavy, but the exams are ambiguous, and he wants you to read his mind. I had to take this class as no other professor was teaching it, but if you can avoid him, please do. He clearly doesn't care about student success, even though he says he does.

I took his class online from a teacher under him but had a confrontation with him where he made me feel like a child that didn't know a thing. Didn't have a good experience in this class and after thinking I might want to do bioinformatics I don't want to touch it with a 10 ft pole.

This class is a lot of work. So many multiple-hour assignments and frequent written tests in the testing center. Aside from these issues with the workload, Dr. Ridge's lecture videos are actually quite good. He explains hard algorithms clearly. He's also very nice in person and is fair when you talk to him.

Dr. Ridge is here for research not for teaching so good luck meeting with him outside of class. His class is disorganized and you have to go to the TAs for everything. You have to live in the TA lab to pass this class. They explain concepts better than he does. Grades are also pass fail so your grade is not a good reflection of concepts you know.

Dr. Ridge is here for research, he's not here to be an educator. All or nothing points are very common, so if you miss one small detail and your code fails, you fail. Exam questions are written quite cryptically, so you spend half of the time trying to figure out what is being asked. BYU's bioinformatics department continues to disappoint.

While multiple-choice questions were sometimes frustrating, the main part of the grade is programming, so it wasn't a big deal to get a bit turned around. The concepts were well explained and easy to follow. Labs were pass/fail but you know the criteria and you get unlimited attempts so it's not as bad as people are saying.
All of the grades are pass/fail so if you miss a small detail in a large assignment you get a zero. You practically have to live with the TAs to pass this class.

This was hands down the worst class I have ever taken. It is unbearably disorganized and full of errors. The Prof. is a terrible question writer, his questions are extremely general and always looking for specific answers. If you haven't programmed before you'll spend your entire life in the TA lab. A lot of the points are all or nothing. Awful.

I really enjoyed Bio165 with Dr. Ridge. I had never coded before, but this class gave me a very good introduction to python. I went in to work with the TAs a couple of times, and they were very helpful and patient. Dr. Ridge is very passionate about bioinformatics, and his lectures are engaging. This was one of my favorite classes at BYU.

I really enjoyed this class. He provides all the resources necessary to get an A, and it's a reasonable workload. I use the programming we learned in this course all the time in my current biology research. Take this course! (Also, I would give him the hot chili pepper if that was still an option.)

Dr. Ridge is one of my favorite professors at BYU. His lectures are simple and well-explained and he has a good sense of humor as well. I decided to major in bioinformatics after this class, but I would HIGHLY recommend this course for any biologist. The concepts we learned are essential for any modern-day scientist!

I started with no python experience, worked really hard, got 100% on almost every HW, LAB, and test. Still didn't get an A because he made the Final timed and gave it a weird different pass-off driver. Pop-quizzes affected my grade, which he told us they wouldn't. He took over a month to grade some of our assignments. 95% for A. Good luck

This class forces you to work hard. But it's great! It's definitely not the kind of class that you can procrastinate until the day before the exam to study. Regular homework assignments and quizzes keep you studying daily throughout the study. As long as you can put in maybe 30 minutes a day to review and practice, it's for sure manageable.

This class takes a lot of your time and by the end of the semester you still haven't learned anything. Huge waste of time. Dr. Ridge focuses on the bioinformatics majors or those that have previous knowledge of programming. If you have no background of programming be prepared for a long, tedious and worthless class. TA hours are basically mandatory

Dr. Ridge is a nice guy but bad teacher. He looks for very specific answers on his homework, labs and tests without giving specific questions. So either you need to be a mind reader or spend hours with the TA's. You will see the rest of your class with the TA's and learn to love to wait to have your questions answered. lectures  worthless.

I wish there were tags for: expects us to read his mind can't do anything without the TA's makes it harder than it needs to be Dr. Ridge needlessly complicates a very easy class, and students are able to get 100's on his exams yet don't do well on the homework, quizzes, or labs. Please avoid this class at all cost, or expect to be frustrated.

I am without words. This class feels like a waste of time to students who aren't BI majors. Lectures are unbearable irrelevant, and it was so frustrating to have things explained by the TA's that could have been talked about in class. Also, the homework system only allows two attempts/hour and does not make it very streamlined to study anything.

So this class has to be one of the biggest jokes of my college career. Dr. Ridge's lectures are terrible. He does not explain the principles well, and there is a clear lack of variation in his examples. In order to finish homework assignments you have to go to the TA's who are much better at teaching than he is. The entire semester was a nightmare.

I loved intro to bioinformatics because of Dr. Ridge. He convinced me to major in it. You'll need to study well for the tests. This class is probably the best way to get exposed to programming for the first time. It's much better to take this class before C S 142. Dr Ridge is also very inspirational! I highly recommend taking his class.

Dr. Ridge was a good professor for BIO365/CS418. I liked how he didn't seek to fill class time with empty lecturing; he told us things we needed to know, then gave us time to work. A lot of us procrastinated the semester project (worth almost half the final grade) in spite of his warnings. I felt like I learned a lot & it was good grad school prep.

The class wasn't organized perfectly, which is understandable since it just got restructured. The programming labs and group projects were fun and meaningful; if you put in the work you'll learn a lot from this class. Lectures mainly focused on helping us with tougher algorithms, which went a little bit slow for me, but they were helpful.

Echoing what others have said, his intro to bioinformatics class is really easy for those with programming experience. But I still learned useful things. He seems a bit distant toward students, but he's definitely willing to help when you talk to him.

Dr. Ridge is a clear lecturer who is very helpful to beginning programming students. As an experienced programmer taking the class for my major I was pretty bored, but I still learned new skills. If you have programming experience this class will be a breeze.
Dr. Ridge is a very helpful, very involved teacher. He teaches very well, and with the class prep guides, you need to attend anyway. Overall a great teacher, would take again.
This was an easy class for someone with programming experience.  Otherwise, it is a great introductory course.  Dr. Ridge is very helpful in and out of class.

Pretty easy if you've taken CS 142 or higher.  If you've never done programming at all, it would've been more challenging but not at all impossible.  The TA's and the professor were very helpful.  Go to class.  Ask for help if you need it.

He's a really great guy. He will push you past your limits and help you improve and expand out of your own style some too. The work is a lot, so be prepared to have some nights with little to no sleep. Overall he's a good professor and is a great option for this painting class. You will learn a lot.
arguably one of the best art professors. he will push you to your potential and never sugarcoats.

I had Peter for two classes and LOVED him. It feels like he truly takes time to understand your work and wants to figure it out. I think he changed the way I create as an artist and made my artwork feel important and valued. Hes great take any chance you can and hes a well respected artist in Utah!

Peter is a very nice person and is always willing to talk to you about your work! Just because this is an art class it is not an easy A. Be ready to put in at least 5 hours a week outside of class on projects!

He does not just give A's for pity, you work and earn it. He has a very refreshing way of letting you find your voice, and accepting it even if its not his style of artwork, while still showing you how you can improve. Be ready to work hard in his class, but if you are in it to become a better artist, he will 1000% help you get there.

I absolutely LOVED Peter! He challenged me in so many ways and I became a better artist by the end of it. He cares deeply for his students and is always willing to give you feedback or brainstorm ideas. He is a tough grader, but it pushes you to do better. You put in what you want out of this class for sure. 10/10, take a class from Peter!
Peter is a great professor, but he LOVES to talk. Like he would talk the whole 3 hours sometimes. He never gives out 100's so be ready for that. Otherwise, take a class from him, you'll learn lots.

He individually helped the students with their paintings but still allowed us to have or own voice and style.  He is very down to earth and very approachable.  My confidence with oil paints has increased a ton.  Before I had no idea how to handle the paint, but now I feel like I can make a good painting! mostly in class, 1 out of class per week.
Peter Everett is AMAZING. He is incredibly helpful, insightful, and sincere. Take a class from him if you can!

Freshman seminar = AWESOME. You'll have lectures from artists from all over the country, even some from Europe, etc. It's definitely a lecture hall, but a great one at that; I loved every minute of it. We just had class once a week with a summary of the lecture; piece easy. It's a pass/fail deal, so actually go to the lectures. GREAT class.
No Comments

I took a pass or fail class from Peter.  All we had to do was show up to 12 lectures out of 15. I loved going to them because there were many interesting visiting artists from around the world.  It is a one credit class and all you have to do is show up! i loved it

This is not an infant development class; this is a researching/writing class. It was purely reading/writing assignments based on complex articles. The work took forever and is the most I've ever had to do, even more than higher classes. I was disappointed that the class was not as advertised and that the difficulty took away from learning.

Lots of research reading.This class is time consuming but not necessarily difficult. Assignments are not graded harshly if you meet the criteria. This class truly made me feel like I was learning, becoming a more articulate writer, and a better critical thinker. Dr. Reschke asked deep questions and created engaging discussions.

If you want to learn how to read research then take this class. I can't say I didn't learn about infants because I did, and it was interesting, but if I had the chance again I would not pick this professor. Dr. Reschke expects a lot. It was very hard and time consuming!

Honestly I learned so much. His class was time consuming, but he is good with preparing you for test questions and how to format things. Lots of group discussion, pick a smart group! Lots of assignments , but you get in a routine. The assignments are helpful for the tests. Use the TA slides!! Also the tests are hours long so set that time aside.
I learned a lot in this class. Although I don't love research or reading articles, I thought it was really informative.

If you are hoping to actually learn about infant development, do not take this class. If you are hoping to learn how to read research papers and spend a million hours doing so, then definitely take this class. Each assignment is based off of reading and dissecting research papers that barely cover topics related to infants. It's unnessarily hard

like the other reviews said he teaches through research articles. i wasnt always sure what to take from lectures or readings but the quizzes are open note and open readings. he definitely cares a lot about the topic which is why he would go over class time regularly. there's three midterms, a final paper, AND a final exam.

This class is not about infant development, it is an understanding research articles class in disguise-- don't be fooled. Structure is very haphazard but not necessarily "the worst." You will probably not learn anything about infants, but I suppose you may get exposed to what working with researchers is like. It's online, that's all I cared about.

Honestly I was super excited to learn about infants and how they develop, however this class was a really big disappointment. All you do is read research articles and the class is literally revolved around them. I felt like Professor R didn't teach anything and I was really bummed because I didn't learn much. Sadly, I don't recommend this class

Peter is really accommodating. I had an emergency and missed an exam. He helped me get it done and allowed me the full points I deserved. My only beef is that I lost so many points over specifics. I.e. I would get 75% on an assignment bc I forgot to capitalize a letter in the references or didn't double space. Not cool to get a C bc of one mistake.

If you're sick of the information regurgitation format of most classes, then this class is for you. You will actually learn and will become equipped with raw information. As an introvert, I normally hate group work, but discussing our thoughts in groups became my favorite part and I will truly miss my group. Im already taking another class from him

You absolutely need to be ready to read, but it is so worth it. Dr. Reschke is my favorite professor at BYU, and this class taught me so much. His class is a combination of reading scholarly articles, small group discussions, and lectures. There are a lot of quizzes and assignments, but he makes it clear how to earn the most amount of points.

Dr. Reschke is an amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and is flexible. His class seems overwhelming at the beginning of the semester, but there is a huge learning curve. It gets easier and he is willingly to work with you. He adjusted things throughout the semester and asked our opinion on due dates, test lengths, etc.

I absolutely loved this class! Going into it, I heard a lot of negative comments about the workload and structure of the class, but I think that Dr. Reschke's class structure is one of the best there is. I have never learned more from a class at BYU and I would recommend anyone to take this class! He also shows a genuine interest and care for us!

this class is boring. He is a really nice guy. But the amount of work you need to do every week is crazy! Reading 3 or 4 scientific articles that are so hard to understand. And assignments that take forever to do are only worth like .4% of your grade. That is the most annoying part. All of the reading assignments and writing are worth so little.

this class is boring. I appreciate that Dr. Reschke allows us to skim read or focus our reading on the important parts of the articles. That being said the material is incessantly dry and is incredibly hard to understand. He is a nice guy though. But the class is just reading off of slides. No textbook- you read articles. ALOT of them.

Dr. Reschke is great. I postponed this class until my last semester because all the reviews about "so much reading" scared me off. The reading is literally not bad at all & his entire class is very straightforward. He does not try to trick you. If you just do the reading, you will be set for class, quizzes, and exams. He's a very kind professor.

This was definitely one of the hardest classes I've taken at BYU, but was also one of my favorites. Dr. Reschke requires a lot of reading, specifically research articles, and all the tests and quizzes are short essay, but it really is such an amazing class! You do group discussions every week that are honestly so great. 10/10 would recommend.

This class was by far the hardest class I have ever taken @ BYU. Should have been 5 credit hrs. He is super kind & flexible & will work with you & gave us a week off once! I learned a ton, but I would NOT take it again. If I failed, I'd probably pick a new major. LOTS of research articles & APA is super crucial & I lost a lot of points bc of it.

Super difficult but I 10/10 recommend it. At the beginning I was extremely bitter/stressed about the reading/ assignments, but through the semester I realized my article analyzing and writing skills had improved a ton! I worked my butt off, but I learned so much and feel so much more capable. Prof R is kind, and responds to emails quickly.

If you don't have to take this class, don't. This was honestly one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. And the worst part is it is unnecessarily hard. The amount of reading and assignments every week is ridiculous. This class has potential but is ruined by the difficulty.

Professor Reschke is an incredible person who you can tell really cares about his students, but the amount of work he assigned for an undergraduate class was insane. Must read multiple scientific articles every week and heavily annotate them, hard tests, pop quizzes. Class was good but if you're looking for an easier class take from someone else.

This was the hardest class I have ever taken. He set it up like a graduate-level course and there were over 40 academic articles that we had to read, and fully annotate before class periods. I spent so much time outside of class just reading and the required research paper was very difficult to write. Take this class from someone else if you can!!!

Dr Reschke is very nice. He loves this subject, and tries to make it interesting. Just make sure to take a lighter load of credits when you take this class-- it'll take a HUGE chunk of time out of your week. LOTS of readings, lots of notes, big research paper, exams, etc.

I loved this course! It is definitely heavier on the homework load- but if you take good notes on the reading (which is all articles/free chapters- no paying for an expensive textbook!) you will be prepared for the test. He really cares that you actually learn applicable material and connects everything very well at the end. Worth the effort!

His class seems overwhelming at first, but is set up to really learn the material. The tests are fair and exactly what you would expect. If you take good notes on the readings, then it is hard to do poorly. He really cares about his students and wants to see everyone succeed. It's quite a bit of work, but very doable.

I worked with Dr Reschke in the Center for Emotion and Cognition for SFL 403R and I loved it! It was engagibg and thought provoking. Because it is a capstone class it is a bit different than other classes he may teach but he really cares about his students and wants them to succeed

Dr. Ruda is amazing. He is hilarious and truly cares about what he is teaching and the students in his class. He is always willing to meet with students to help them understand the content better. He wants to help us become better nurses and I loved his class. Probably the only 8am I never felt sleepy in because he is so engaging.

I absolutely loved this class with Ruda! He is so personable and funny. I will say that make sure you are very aware of when things are due because he doesn't accept late work, no exceptions. His lectures are so fantastic and he has such a passion, he really wants you to succeed and gives so many opportunties to ask him questions! 10/10

I absolutely have LOVED Dr. Ruda! If you are lucky enough to be in his class, you will have an amazing time. He is super caring and funny. He understands circumstances in life that are unavoidable and difficult and is willing to help you through it. He is rooting for you and truly wants you to thrive!

Dr. Ruda is an amazing professor, all of his lectures were so interesting and entertaining! exams were fair and straightforward. all of the contents of the exams were either covered in lecture or through the TA's review slides. The quality of his teaching is impeccable, you can tell how much he cares about nursing and the students!

Dr. Ruda is an incredible professor!! His lectures were amazing. He is very passionate about what he does, and it shows in the way he lectures. He truly cares about each of his students. He is very open to feedback and accessible outside of class. The class is a lot of work, but it is manageable. I would highly recommend Dr. Ruda.

Petr is HILARIOUS and really cares about his students. If you are lucky enough to take a class from him you will be laughing. He gives great insight to clinical practice and thinks outside of the box for interactive learning experiences.

Business Systems is a lot of work, but if you put the time in, writing a paper about a business that you are passionate about comes easy. Phil is SUCH an advocate for us, and it really shows. He will do all he can to set you up for success. I've had multiple classes from Phil and I wish I could have taken more. He's a great professor and friend.

Phil cares about his students and really gets to know them personally. However he is the worst professor I've had in this department. His lectures are disjointed and confusing. The final for the class consisted of questions asking for his opinion. The tree journal is purely busy work. Overall, it's a terrible class with a kind professor.
Phil Allen really knows what he teaches and has a lot of experience he can draw from and use to teach. He is a very good resource to have, and is flexible in his teaching approach.
Phil is the best professor I had in college. I feel like I succeeded in his class because he became my friend as well.

Phil is soo amazing! He cares so much about his students and the program. I have had him for many classes and always enjoy learning from him. He is very energetic and enthusiastic about the classes that he teaches. This class has been the best class I have taken at BYU and I have loved it because it has taught me so much!

Professor Allen is an awesome teacher. He loves his students and really desires to create a personal relationship with them. He desires their success and is always there to help. His classes may require hard work but Professor Allen is there to help and support you all along the way and understands the importance of having fun along the way.

Dr. Phil team teaches this class with Dr. Stewart. Dr. Phil really cares about the students in the class. He tries to answer questions to the best of his ability. He is very knowledgeable and helpful. This class wasn't as helpful as I thought it would be, but not a waste of my time.

He team teaches this class with Greg, but Greg is the one who grades the project and seems to be the lead professor.  Dr. Allen though is super nice and gives great feedback and actually seems to care some about his students.  Definitely go to him for help on the project not Greg or TAs.  Do not take this class if you do not have to!!

Phil was a great teacher and really personable. If you're not a project person, don't take the once a week class (esp. the evening class), it's way too stressful. My only regret is not taking a class from Prof. Abbott SOONER! I'm a senior and his class was my last religion class and it was truly the best REL I've ever taken. Go to class and he will literally tell you word for word what is on the exam, but also his lectures are so fun! Made my 8am class WORTH IT! TAKE! THIS! CLASS!
Awesome! He brought the New Testament to life in a way I didn't know was possible.

Mr. Abbott did a great job of focusing on the social and political context surrounding the New Testament. He takes students seriously.
