There are always more details he'll excitedly share if anybody asks questions. For my other exmos, this one is good. He spends more time on Judaism than modern Christianity. A nice break from seminary-style classes.

Doctor Abbott is great! He understands that religion classes shouldn't be hard, so it's very manageable. He tells you exactly what's on the exams. His lectures are engaging and very historically and factually based, which I really liked, but might not be for everyone if you're looking for the most spiritual class.
I took this my senior year and was honestly my favorite religion class.

Dr Abbott is knowledgeable on the New Testament and encourages questions. His lectures are very straightforward and his teaching style is engaging and at times humorous.  He explains his expectations for the class well at the start of the semester, and gives you the resources you need to do well in the class. He's very caring and a great teacher.

Professor Abbott studied ancient languages and scripture so in this class you're not getting a seminary lesson but I love the depth and the really useful things that I learned in his class. You do not have to write any papers! I think that that is more than fair for a religion class
Wonderful teacher, you can tell he enjoys what he is teaching and that he knows what he is talking about. Favorite class so far :)
Amazing professor, prepares you well for the exams

Somewhat overrated. While the class was well organized, the material felt repetitive and lacked new or meaningful insights. I didn't feel a personal connection with the teacher, and he came across as less approachable and engaging compared to other religion professors I've had. It wasn't my favorite class.
Actually learned new things

The lectures were absolutely amazing! He gave a study guide for everything that might appear in the test. (AKA nothing not on the study guide would be on the tests) All the tests and quizzes were on learning suite. Overall, I definitely recommend taking REL A 211 from him!

I loved this class! I felt that this professor's teaching was both academic and spiritual. I saw scriptures in new ways and learned new things every class. There were reading quizzes due before every class, but I didn't think they were very hard. His tests were also not too difficult. I think about the things I learned in this class all the time!

Dr. Abbott ROCKS. This guy knows his stuff and his classes are engaging and interesting. I learned something new each time which is not usually my experience in religion classes. His NT class is non-harmonized which is so much better, I actually understood the differences between the synoptics. SO COOL. He tells you exactly what will be in midterms

Professor Abbott is an amazing professor. His New Testament class was my favorite class this semester by far. He is extremely knowledgeable on the subject. I looked forward to his class every day. You know exactly what will be on the test. Also, there are no papers. PLEASE take his class.

I came for a more academic approach and that's what I got. The exams are far easier than much of the content discussed in class and he's super transparent about what you need to know. Got better at lecturing as the semester went on. Did a great job illuminating scripture, very passionate about the material. Less devotional, more historical.

He's amazing! I'm taking the 2nd half of the new testament from him next semester. Lectures are really engaging and insightful. Tests are super straightforward, everything is on the study guide/from quizzes. He focused a lot on cultural significance for ancient people, and often translates into Hebrew and Greek.

I loved Professor Abbott! I've actually taken two of his classes now, and both were awesome. He is crazy amazing. He is very clear about what is on all of the exams, homework is consistent and easy (reading with a little quiz two times a week), and he really has helped the scriptures come alive for me. Would highly recommend him to everyone!
He was an awesome lecturer.  Super entertaining.  Tests are worth 70% of your grade, but he marks everything that will be on the test on the lecture slides so they are super easy.  Take from him!

Great class. Not seminary! No personal essays! Learned a lot. Would recommend to anyone wanting to understand how to interpret (and how not to interpret) the New Testament. Only weird thing is the way he basically gives you the answers to the tests, but I don't think most students would consider that a negative.

Professor Abbot is absolutely phenomenal. His knowledge of the New Testament surpasses any text or lecture that I've read or listened to. He's extremely entertaining and keeps the class engaged throughout the entire semester.

Love this professor! I rated him as easy not because his content was easy, but because he is very clear about what is on his tests. He gives a study guide that you fill out as he lectures. He's a newer professor but don't let that scare you off. I've taken 2 classes from him now, a New Testament and Book of Mormon, loved them both. Take his class!

This is the second class I've taken from Dr. Abbott because I love how he marks what you need to know on the slides for the tests. He's also an interesting lecturer and helped me actually learn new things about the Book of Mormon this year. New Testament is definitely his specialty but he's still both a good and easy choice for 122.

SUCH a good teacher! Each slide labels exactly what you need to know for the test! It makes it so much easier to learn and pay attention when you aren't worried about writing every little detail down!

Abbott was such a good professor for New Testament. His lectures and knowledge about the New Testament were awesome, and he was such an interesting professor to listen to. Short open-note quizzes in between each class. Exams are really easy and straightforward if you know the study guide.

Dr. Abbott helped me learn things about the scriptures that I never knew. Rather than regurgitating popular insights into the scriptures that everyone's already heard in Sunday School, Dr. Abbott provides actually new knowledge about the scriptures and introduces new ways to look at the scriptures. Quizzes and tests are pretty easy.
Dr. Abbott is amazing. He is one of my favorite teachers I've had at BYU. He gives real, quality, insights and helped me learn applicable knowledge of the Book of Mormon.

Professor Abbott is my favorite ever! He teaches in such a good way I recommend him 10000% to anybody who wants to learn and doesn't want to do much work. Quizzes and exams were relatively easy and about the book of mormon. take his class!!!
Lectures are fun. He gives us study guides of everything that's on the test and tells us during class what exactly in his presentation will be on the test. Attendance is mandatory

LOVED this professor. the lectures were amazing and with his many degrees and expertise in ancient society, you gain amazing new insight into the scriptures by putting them in context. Highly recommend. There is a quiz for each class, but they are easy and open note. the exams are very easy, he tells you exactly what will be on them. no papers

Lectures are phenomenal and reading quizzes are straightforward. He highlights on his slides the things that you need to know for the midterms and gives students many opportunities to participate. He includes quite a bit of historical context along with modern context to help explain the Gospels. Great choice for any religion class.

He is such an amazing professor! His lectures are super engaging and he gives out super helpful study guides for his midterms. There's a 10 question quiz after each class and he's an easy grader. Super nice guy 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Abbott is a very engaging speaker and a funny guy! There are two reading quizzes each week and three midterms. He tells you exactly what will be on them and provides study guides. Fill out the study guides during the lectures - it will save you a lot of time. The reading quizzes affect your grade more than you think they will, so be careful.

Dr. Abbott is a phenomenal teacher. I walked away from each lecture having learned something new and insightful. He has great energy and is very passionate about what he teaches. No papers, just reading quizzes twice a week on your own time and one exam after each gospel learned. Exams 2-4 are comprehensive, but very manageable. Take his class!

Dr. Abbott is awesome. I enjoyed his classes. He makes sure that you know. exactly what is going to be on the tests and has awesome insights. He also doesn't give out writing assignments which is awesome.

Professor Abbott is an expert on the material taught. He literally says what will be on the test in the slides and during lecture. His tests are short and they reflect what was taught in class. 10/10 I would absolutely take his class again.

I loved this class because it was very intellectually engaging and full of good information. He made it very clear what would be on the test by literally saying it and giving really good study guides. I aced all the exams because of that. 2 weekly quizzes based on NT readings, not too hard. 100% would take him again. He's a very engaging speaker.
He provides great insights into the New Testament and teaches in a way that is engaging and really dives deep into the hidden facets of the gospels.
He's super nice. There are no tests. The homework is pretty brutal. There is a bunch of reading and you have to make 5 annotations. It is an easy class though, just a lot of busy work.

This class is definitely work heavy, but if you do it on time it's manageable. The lectures are very interesting and have definitely helped me understand the difference between world and religious views of the family. Brother Allred is really kind and personable, and I enjoyed the emphasis on class dialogue and discussion.

Good class, not too hard. Unfortunately he added a final project during the semester, so beware of that. Before each class there are between 10-20 pages of reading (conference talks etc) and you need to make 5 annotations/comments to get credit. These assignments drained the life out of me, but you can skim pretty easily and make some comments

I loved this class so much. He did a really good job explaining concepts, and understanding the concerns of the students. He also has a few class periods where he scheduled interviews with students to get to know them and answer questions. Bro. Allred really cares about the students and wants us to find answers to our questions.

I LOVED this class. The lectures were very spiritual and interesting. He welcomed lots of participation and it was cool to hear from different students. No exams but you do have reflections every few weeks as review of what you learned. Also have to submit lecture notes and have two readings a week that around 10 pages that you are graded on.
Yeah, there are a few readings per class, but they aren't too bad. Class was always very interesting, and the guidelines were very clear. Do the stuff and show up and you'll get an A.

I took Eternal Families and it was awesome. Prof. Allred is super approachable and genuine. He leads very insightful discussions and welcomes participation. Homework is manageable and the AI-auto grader for reading participation is pretty easy to get 10/10 points (just make a few comments ever other page). Probably my favorite religion course!

Although Professor Allred doesn't give tests, he does give case studies and deep dives about every other week that take several hours to complete. Also, every class you are required to turn in detailed notes on the lecture that day. They are not hard, but I would have preferred to be able to listen to the lecture without as much note taking.

Good professor, I learned a lot in the class. Assignments are chill, easy A. For Perusall readings just make sure to have it open for a while and have 5 long comments spread evenly. Homework doesn't take  too much time.

Amazing professor. Loved the in-class discussions and conversations.
But the readings are so long and AI shouldn't be grading spiritual readings. Twice a week we were expected to read almost a dozen talks with AI graded annotations. Too much for a 2-credit class
One of the greatest professors for religion I really loved the lectures, they were just mandatory and I had to miss a few times for work so my grade was docked

Amazing Professor! The class itself can it a little boring only focusing on one paragraph of the Proclamation each week, but his slides and stories are super engaging. No tests or quizzes, a super easy religion class I would recommend.

There were some weird lecture topics, and the lectures never seemed all that productive. We discussed prophets very little and the lectures seemed to be focused more on his theories and interpretation of doctrine instead of prophets. Some class discussions got SUPER off topic and verging a little too much on sacred topics. Easy A, but didn't learn.

Firstly, he's a nice guy. I didn't find the class very spiritual. Tons of reading with annotations graded by AI. spiritual comprehension shouldn't be graded by AI. Also, I always so busy checking the boxes to do complete the overly structured notes that I never had time to learn. Extra assignments biweekly made a lot of work for a 2 credit class.

Really easy class. Professor Allred was really good at keeping the class engaged and was able to address difficult topics with lots of professionalism. Readings during the week take some time, but it is easy to get an A on them. No midterm.

Br. Allred is super inspiring and kind. Absolutely loved his class and lectures. I learned so much and felt the Spirit every class while learning so much. There are a few assignments every week but definitely manageable. No midterm and easy final. Just set some time aside for it and you'll get an A.

Brother Allred is a super nice and engaging professor. His lectures were very enjoyable, my only complaint was that there was so much homework. We'd read 3-5 talks in preparation for each class which we needed to annotate. And there was a paper due every week. They weren't incredibly difficult assignments it's was just very time consuming.
Graded by AI that only gives 8/10 for following class directions perfectly.
Great!! He really strives to understand the students.

Such a great professor! He did a great job explaining doctrine, was very respectful of students' opinions, and I felt like he genuinely cared about all of us. Reading assignments are AI graded, which is a bit annoying, but you can bump your grade up with the other assignments, which were very straightforward. No midterms, and a super easy final.

Br. Allred is a great lecturer and I always felt engaged in the lesson even though I had the class at 8am. There aren't any exams, but there are weekly essays and the homework is busy work. It's graded by AI which doesn't work great. Overall I think it was a great religion credit.

I really liked Brother Allred and felt the lectures were the highlight of the class. The assignments did get a bit repetitive but if you actually try, you'll be fine. There are no exams which is a bonus but you do have to submit lecture notes after each class which helped me pay attention. Before each class you have to make 5 comments on the readin

Busy work is just busy work. 5 writing assignments a week is too much for a religion class. He had an AI grade the assignments which I find appalling. The AI would say things like "not enough time spent" or even "didn't close and reopen the assignment enough times." Just because you take out midterms and tests doesn't make you a good professor.

Brother Allred is amazing, and I always looked forward to this class! He cares a ton about his students and does a good job facilitating some sometimes difficult discussions. The grading for the comments on reading assignments is done by AI and it can be pretty stupid sometimes, but you just have to keep adding stuff until it says they're good.

No exams which is super nice. However this teacher uses AI to grade his assignments. For example, he said we needed a minimum of five posts on the discussion boards (which were AI graded). When I approached him about the grades I felt were unjust, he wasn't willing to negotiate or change the grades even though I fulfilled his requirements.

Dr White is really relatable and makes a point to give assignments that feel application heavy. You analyze real data sets and complete regressions for them. The tests weren't too bad, but the test reviews are not helpful. He is very funny, but class was really just him lecturing for 1.25 hours which got boring and hard to follow the theory.

Dr. White is fantastic one on one and the best professor during his office hours. TAs are also way helpful. However, I felt the lecture was very far from helpful. I learned more just pulling up his slides on my own and going through the material that way. The homework takes FOREVER. It's like a final project due every week. Exams are not great.
Solid choice for stat 330. Great dude and reasonable grader. The class was super interesting and applicable.

I loved him! The class isn't very difficult if you go to class and pay attention, and he and the TAs were very helpful. I enjoyed his lectures, and the material was interesting. He posts the slides from class, has attendance quizzes, and allows a note card for tests. I 100% recommend him for any class!
Very nice guy. Always willing to help and holds office hours often. Very generous with grading and isnt too harsh. Really interesting class too
Han är så jätte bra! Den bästa svenska läraren vi har haft!
He's a fun professor and lectures very clearly. The content for this class isn't inherently complicated, so studying the homeworks and quizzes will prepare you well for his exams.

Dr. Manwaring is a good teacher. He just came from industry and has a lot of good insights. You will have online reading and work in zybooks before each class and weekly in-class quizzes. His tests are pretty tough, and have much more to do with the C coding language than embedded programing. Most of the class grade is the labs.
Assignment instructions and feedback were vague and unhelpful. Liked to argue with students.

Dr. Monson is a good guy who loves his field of work. However, his class was difficult to navigate -- assignment instructions were often unclear, and his lectures were tough to follow at times. With one week to go in the class, we had TWO things entered into Learning Suite. Study hard for the tests and form a good group for your group project.

Nice enough guy but a pretty below-average professor. His teaching style is characterized by going off on frequent tangents and being very lecture heavy. Often talks over students when they try to ask questions. As of now it's the end of the semester and he's only graded one assignment: the midterm. Take a poli sci class from another BYU professor.

I would never take this class again, even if I had to. His lectures are pretty boring, homework is a lot of work but doesn't really help grade and tests are annoyingly long. If you are not a strong test taker, this class is not for you. I wish I had taken another class instead of this

I like Professor Monson as a person, but as a teacher I would say he's just okay. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches which is great, but his lectures can seem a bit pointless and at times tangential to the course material. The class itself is not very difficult though, so it's a great alternative to American Heritage.

If you like political science, you will probably like POLI 110. I don't like this subject so I had a hard time. Going to each class & doing the readings are important. He encourages use of office hours. The final for my class is cumulative. If you're looking for an easy class, don't take it. If you work really hard, you'll do fine.
Is reasonable and easy to work with, exams are on the longer side.

Professor Monson is clearly an expert in his field and highly passionate about political science and civic engagement. His teaching is laid-back and though this was a 1-credit survey course, at times I wished he packed more content into his lectures and organized them more clearly. Overall a great guy.

Professor Monson's lectures made me want to learn more about the governmental system in America and encouraged me to learn more about the topic. He's very willing to meet with students and work with the class on deadlines and workload. This class was very interesting for me and I hope to take another class from Professor Monson in the future!

Lectures were boring but he's a fun guy. Tests aren't too hard and you have two papers but he's nice and works with the class to make sure people get acceptable grades (he will curve at the end of the class or drop lower assignments). Homework can be annoying but use the book and it's easy and goes faster.
Definitely one-sided professor. Both his lectures and the textbook are very one sided on the political spectrum. He pretty much just lectures his opinion the whole time. Would not take again.
So unclear and makes you feel inadequate
Easy class if you do the readings and go to class.
Although I didn't have the same views on Politics as Professor Monson, I was able to really enjoy his class and learn a lot. He was an incredible teacher.
If you are a political science major than you will like this class, but other than that it is kinda boring but worth it if trying to swerve American Heritage

Honestly, I had an amazing experience in this class. He is so FAIR. If the students aren't successful he is willing to curve and make things fair. I went to him with help on an essay I was struggling with and he was so kind and helpful. His lectures are pretty entertaining even if you aren't interested in the material.

Professor Monson is a great guy. Very respectful to students. Poli Sci is really boring to me but he teaches it in an engaging way. DO NOT take this class if you struggle taking tests. There are 2 midterms and a final that count for basically your entire grade. Also his learning suite was never updated and hard to navigate. Not super clear.

Professor Monson is one of the most caring professors I know, in spite of the large class size. I met him after bombing my first midterm, and he gave me specific advice and even a conditional offer of revising that test's grade if I showed marked improvement. However, the class's content was dry and lectures felt like recitations of the textbook.

Professor Monson is truly an amazing professor! Though he has a large class, he cares for each of his students and encourages them to come and see him during office hours. Being a Poli Sci Major, I found this class very interesting but Professor Monson does a great job at engaging those not in Poli Sci. Relates Gospel topics to politics.

Professor Monson is a really nice guy. You can tell that he is very genuine and caring, but this class is seriously ridiculous. He just thinks out loud for his lectures and there is no real structure. The TAs wrote the test about a week before we took it, so it was poorly written. Some of the TAs have even said that they are lost in the class.

You are probably better off taking POLI 110 from a different professor. Monson told us before class that he doesn't teach 110 often, so it might be a "a bit of a bumpy ride." He doesn't provide any study guides nor does he emphasize in his lectures what is on the exams. On the upside he is an interesting guy to talk to.

This class is a joke. It uses a software called "Inquisitive" that isn't fair. One question will ask you to sort 6 statements into true or false categories; get 1/6 wrong and lose all the points. Lectures teach 2% of the material on quizzes, but you still better show up in case there is a random participation quiz right at the beginning of class!

This career lecture class was really helpful! You'll get an A if you attend and do the writeups. But you cannot miss more than one class! Make sure that before you take this class that you don't have too many trips planned that semester.

Prof. Monson was great. A little disorganized sometimes, but you knew that he always had the student's best interest at heart. Very approachable. Tests were typed, and not that bad if you paid attention in lectures. Lots of discussion in class, lots of real-world application with a semester-length group project. My favorite class of the semester!

I took 318 from Dr. Monson his first time teaching it. I think he was more interested in his 305, which is fine. BUT I still learned a lot. Tests are typed, vocab and application heavy. We had to design a campaign strategy for a real world candidate. Good class. He is blunt, so know that (he is SO funny). Interested in students' success.

210 with Dr. Monson is a great choice. He wants to engage you in actual political science literature, not just a intro textbook. I'm grateful for this foundation as I move into upper level American classes!

Very textbook heavy, lectures are dull and pointless, but it is political science so that's expected. tests were based on how well you know very specific information in the text book so make sure to read before your test!

I am a political science major so this class was naturally interesting for me. Prof. Monson is very informative and knows a lot about the topic. I respect him and his expertise. Lots of reading in textbook and he does require you to read a book on the 2012 Election and write a paper. Take it if you are semi interested in politics.

Gah. There is no way to make Pl Sc 110 interesting, but Prof Monson tried. The class is borin g as anything, but he'll try to make it bearable. This class is passable, so might as well take it from him.

Monson will go on long tangents that are irrelevant to the test. You have to go to class because there are some days you'll get vital info, but other days class will be a waste of time. He's not very clear and he uses the TAs WAY too much for grading. He's not bad, but he's certainly not the best.

Terrible professor. Not devoted to class at all because he's always out doing some kind of campaign work. That's why he leaves everything grading-wise up to the TAs. Alan is cool but Kyrene is a snob. Poly Sci is pretty useless no matter who you have. Not recommended

This class was rubbish. He teaches like a pompous professor who does not care about the students' learning. Also, the way the TAs work made it impossible to get a good grade without seeing them constantly. Overall,an extremely boring, unhelpful, and useless class.

I thought class time was useless because he would get off on weird tangents or teach on things that weren't even important. I got a good TA so I didn't suffer much from that, and I am not bothered by the TAs because that is how college classes work when there are 300+ students. Overall he is an okay teacher
Really great class!
Grade is dependent on TAs who are college students themselves and their grading on papers is very subjective. Study guides are vague and Professor goes too fast in lecture.

Dr. Monson is amazing.  I had a hard semester with all my classes (i.e. I was in the ER) so I got a D in this class.  Let's put that aside.  I loved this class.  We both would talk about everything related to politics and the science of it at his office.  He became a really good friend.  He teaches well and I'm just not good at PLSC.

I knew that Professor Monson was an engaging lecturer when I found no trouble staying awake in my 8:00 class.  Tests are vocab heavy, so be sure to focus on that while studying.  TAs can be inconsistent when grading blog posts, so be sure to go and talk to your TA about your post before you submit it.  Overall, time consuming but not too difficult.
Although Monson is funny, I thought class time was useless. The TA's were awful and they're the ones who determine everything! Learned more in my high school government class. Disappointed!
Interesting class, however, your TA basically decides your grade. Each TA has to stay on the same curve AKA they give everyone B's on the writing assignments.

Monson is sickkk! He wants you to learn, but still have a social life. Only had 6 quizzes in class, and he lets you drop 3 of them. Best PLSCI 110 teacher there is. (trust me, this is my 2nd time taking the class)

I had this professor at 8am but had no trouble staying awake during class. He is engaging and entertaining, likes to show lots of video clips. There is quite a bit of writing but it isn't too bad. The tests can be pretty difficult. Go to the TAs for writing and test reviews. Dr. Monson is awesome. I definitely recommend taking government from him!

I LOVE Monson. On a small group level he is very engaging. he cracks jokes in class and is very good at answering questions. He will take the time to help you during his office hours or if you schedule a meeting with him. The textbook isn't used in class until test time. But, go in to see him before the test and he'll give a good idea of content.

Your grade is basically decided by the TA's. Everything is graded by them, so get to know them and their political persuasions early. If your TA is conservative you better not disagree and vice-versa.  Very little structure to the course; no rubric to the writing assignments and 20 page "study guides" to help prepare you for the tests.

Overall, interesting enough to get me out of bed in the morning.  While TAs do the grading Professor is willing to talk to any student and very considerate of students lives and issues.  Very chill, almost to the point he may appear apathetic, but if you go to him he will make it a priority to help you. DO NOT play games in class.  He hates it.

Garbage. The lectures were cool at first, but you learn nothing from them and they get old. 75% of the class will be surfing the web at any given time -- the only reason you go is for the quizzes that he throws out to punish those that skip class or bail on class.  Grades all depend on TAs
Professor is horrible! Incredibly arrogant and unwilling to help students. Avoid his classes at all costs!
At first he was as dull as can be! But sit in the front, don't fall asleep take notes- got really into it. Read book. Final was easy and tests pretty simple.

I like Prof. Monson! For a class that could be boring he made it entertaining. The tests can be hard cause you have no idea what's going to be on it. It's everything from lecture and reading. He posts a study guide that isn't real direct, but if you learn everything on it, read the book, go to lecture and don't be lazy you'll have no problem.
Has TAs grade blog posts. Professor tests on his tangents, so pay attention. SO unhelpful. Withdrew and feel awesome about it.

Lectures drag on, but overall they are not to necessary. I read all the chapters the day before each test and did well. Be sure to read, the tests are heavily taken from the book. TA reviews helped a lot. Paper grading was a bit unfair, because it was graded against the other papers in the class, not just on quality. Made me mad. Overall ok class.
Very condescending and not willing to listen to students.  Didn't see any of our grades until final grades were posted!

Lectures were simple and well delivered. Each test was difficult multiple choice, but the short answer and essay saved me. Lectures weren't required, but textbook reading is. Tests were straight from textbook material, lectures provided extra insight and some good laughs. Go to TA's for help with papers, they will (and want to) save you!
Not helpful at all when meeting with him. Condescending and made me feel like an idiot. Didn't enjoy his teaching style and graded way too strict on papers.

Professor Monson is great!  I don't enjoy studying government, but he made it interesting enough to engage me during the 3.5 hour class periods of spring semester.  He is more than willing to go through your essays with you one and one.  The tests are straight forward. No reason to not do well in this class if you put in the work.

Professor Monson is a great guy.  The lectures are quite boring and it's tough to stay awake.  MC questions on tests are on minutia from the book.  Essays aren't that hard--make sure to see YOUR grading TA multiple times before turning in assignments.  Overall -- not too hard of a class.

If you any type of background in Amer Govt you will be bored out of your mind in lectures. I didn't think coming to class was worth it, but he gives in-class quizzes every 2-3 weeks so you kind of have to. Tests are pretty easy as long as you read the book thoroughly. The essays make this class difficult. TA's are picky and grade  pretty hard.

I had a background in American Government before taking this course so the material was mostly review. This made lectures particularly boring. It was not uncommon to look around the room and see half the class asleep during Professor Monson's lectures. I don't have anything against Professor Monson personally, I just thought his lectures were rathe

Anyone with even a basic knowledge of  American government will find lectures boring,but Prof. Monson is a pretty cool guy. The TA's are a completely different story. I could never get any useful help from them  and got low scores on my papers simply because they didn't like what I was writing about. It was a joke!
One of my favorite classes.  It made me want to minor in PoliSci Teaching.  He really wants you to succeed in his class.

The class sucked really bad, but Monson was great. Whenever I needed help, he met with me one on one and did everything possible to help. On the other hand, the class was horrible. Interesting stuff, but there was  an incredible amount of reading, my TA was not helpful at all and grading was extremely hard. I felt like there was too much expected..
Execellent lecturer.  Made a topic I wasn't really interested in kinda interesting. Hard writing assignments and increasingly hard tests.

Professor Monson is a really nice guy, his tests were just average and my TA treated me very fairly. I didn't get an A cause I am government retarded but it would be quite simple if you have an sort of background in this area. Monson is a nice guy and recommend him

This was the worst Political Science class I have ever taken. If you want to know about exit polling, take this class--cuz that's all you'll talk about. Lectures were irrelevant to the tests, the TAs were worthless, review sessions sucked, grading was impossible to please... The best part of the class is when we had a subsitute.

Ok class. Lectures can be pretty boring but overall not too bad. He can be funny sometimes. The TAs grade extremely hard on the papers and on the essay portion of the exams. Write to what they are looking for; they want a typical essay from high school and grade the format more than content. I lost points for an intro paragraph that was too long.

I'll admit I occasionally drifted off to sleep during the tangents he was especially animated about, but I overall enjoyed this class. He is extremely helpful and forms study groups with the TA's for the students. Reading so many books is a little tedious but he lectures over them in class so it's not...entirely mandatory that you read them.
This class was awesome!  The tests were kind of hard, but not unreasonable.  Monson is great!  He was my favorite professor this year.

This class was a lot of fun.  If you are taking the Exit Poll class, be sure to add this class, too.  It was fun to be on television, and the professors were very helpful in preparing for the TV appearance.  I had a lot of fun, and would highly reccommend the class.

I enjoyed the class.  It was interesting because he discussed relevant topics. I enjoyed him using video clips during the lectures. Over all he was good. You have to study hard and keep on top of things if you want a good grade.

This guy is boring and unreasonable. I went to resolve some concerns with him. Not only would he not hear my concerns, he got emotional with me (upset, rude, etc.) As a senior, I've seen lots and I've never been dealt so rudely by a prof. before.
If you want to have good grade....Don't take it. TA is really tough. His lecture doesn't help the test

Not a bad class; did get boring sometimes. Lectures cover most of the book material, so I only read it as a good review for the test. I had no serious TA issues. Take your paper into your TA a couple of times before turing it in. Since he/she will be grading it, they'll tell you what you should fix before it's due = better grade.

Monson and his T.A.s are two different deals. He's a little rough around the edges, but all in all a good teacher. He knows the stuff and is very clear. His T.A.'s don't know their butts from a hole in the ground. They'll make unfounded claims against your papers. Read the book and know the terms for the test. Know them with depth.

This class sucks. The professor is good, but the TA's are crack heads. They grade super hard, and never tell you what you are doing wrong. Tests are easy if you know the vocab, and the quizzes are even easier. The papers are terrible, especially the first one. Again the TA's are terrible.

His lectures get monotonous. It is an interesting class though. I learned a ton about American Politics. Lots of reading though. LOTS. His TAs grade hard and are not always helpful at the review sessions. If you read the newspaper everyday and keep up on the long long book chapters, and stay awake during class, you might do well. It takes work.

Good Class, he is a fun and interesting teacher most of the times. The quizes were really easy if you just kept up with current events. The tests were a little difficult, but the TA's all had HUGE ego's and graded the papers super hard! Watch out for that.
the weekly quizzes sucked, but it's really easy to guess on them. the tests are really easy if you just know the vocabulary from the chapter. papers are tough though because the TAs grade super hard.

The best part of class was looking around and seeing 50%+ asleep.  Interesting class, but kind of tough.  The TAs grade pretty tough.  The tests are designed so that nobody will get an A, but nobody will fail.
This class was very boring and involved a ton of reading.  If you are going to take this class do not take it in the mornings because lectures will lull you to sleep.
really knows his stuff, and wants you to understand.  can be a little monotonous so taking the class early in the morning might be tuff.  take it from me.

He is a great guy and great professor and will always help you. His lectures can be kind of boring and this is not an easy class, but it's definitely doable. The only really bad thing about it is the TA grading system, which can make it impossible to get an A.
Gets off subject, but knows his stuff.  He's a current events and polling junkie, and I like that kind of stuff.

I liked this course, but I enjoy teachers who get off subject, talk about current events, and allow for class discussion. If you prefer a more structured course with study guides for tests, this is not your guy.

I absolutely adore Quinn! He's very knowledgeable about European history and I learned a lot from his class. He is a tough grader, which is sometimes frustrating, but I would take his class again just because of how much he cares for his students. He is always checking up on them and seeing what he can do to minister to them. Love Quinn!

Professor Mecham is a tough grader and has a lot of experience teaching, but man this dude is one of the most caring people I've met. He loves his students, what he teaches, and I would take his classes over and over again regardless of the grading just to learn more from who he is as a person. Great guy and prepares you for real life experiences.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

If you're used to your one credit lecture taking up one credit of your time, then you're in for a treat. Get ready for unbelievably harsh grading on weekly responses (almost impossible to receive full points), three essays including one on a book read entirely outside of class, and extra mandatory lectures. Save yourself!

Knows his stuff, but his lectures are hard to follow---despite attendance being required by in-class quizzes. They're trying out a new homework system this semester (W26), and it's been polarizing. Some love, others don't. (I'm in the latter.) Haven't taken the midterm yet, but he says he's aiming for a mean of 77%.

Super interesting class. I enjoyed learning about all of the different AI/ML methods/models. Snell clearly likes the material and is passionate about it. Unfortunately, he is not the most responsive and the tests don't perfectly reflect what we learned in class. However, if you attend classes and do the homework, an A is definitely attainable.

Tests were vague and had a low average. Planned the midterm the day before, said the canvas portion was multiple choice, it was 20% free response. Lectures were not helpful or a good use of time. TAs were inacessible and more than half of my coursework was ungraded when I took the final

Smart guy, knows the material and explains it super well, very good at helping students learn. He is not a good administrator though, and doesn't know learning suite well. What's more is he didn't design this course and so what he teaches and what's tested/on homework is sometimes different.

Professor Snell is a good teacher, but it seemed he didn't have enough time to adequately plan out the course. The first half was mostly online which was helpful, but the second half felt all over the place at times. The assignments and tests are not hard, I stopped going to class and doing the readings halfway through and still got a B.

I loved almost everything about this class. The projects were fun, the lectures informative, and it's clear that Dr. Snell cares a lot about the students. He gives you the autograder ahead of time for most of the projects, so you really know beforehand what your grade will be. One thing to note is his tests are really hard.

The second to last day of finals, every student in our class had 100%. On the last day of finals my grade unexpectedly fell to 88% after several assignments were added to the grade book. I felt the last few assignments were graded unexpectedly strict to get a distribution of grades BYU would like. I wish grading was more timely and consistent.

Dr. Snell is a great CS teacher. I've taken him for another class as well. That's why I want to be clear that this only has to do with this class. The pre-requisite is CS240, but that didn't do me any good. I would recommend taking machine learning first (it's big data) since this class is a mess otherwise. I didn't understand anything.
Tough class but professor snell is awesome. He really does care and will work with you. Farily entertaining as well. I would definitely recommend him!

Great guy - put forth an honest effort to make the course useful and interesting and overall succeeded. The class was a little scatter brained at times... but I think this is more of an indication of the course's structure/content than Dr. Snell's teaching. Tests were interesting... do the labs early and any bonus you can and you'll be ok.
Awesome class, awesome teacher. Get started on the labs early, and you shouldn't have any trouble.  I highly recommend Dr. Snell.

Dr. Snell is quite willing to help with projects and assignments - but you have to be self-motivated to get done on time. Fun projects. Tests were somewhat confusing - study more than just what the study guide says.

Great teacher. Very clear and interesting. Very understanding of students' needs. Willing to adjust deadlines if necessary. Offers meaningful help on projects. I'm probably gonna take another class from him next semester, I guess that speaks for itself.
Great professor. Genuinly interested in students and the class and makes the material easy to understand. Get a head start on the labs though, they can take some time!

Great teacher, knows a ton and is actually very good at sharing that knowledge.  Labs require 8-10 hours per week of work but you learn a ton and it is very applicable.  The class and teacher were better than expected!
I'd take a class with this professor any semester.  He teaches very well and focuses on material that's important.  This professor is HIGHLY recommended.

This is the worst class I have ever taken. I wouldn't recommend it to my worst enemy. Professor Evans grades incredibly harsh and forces you to meet with him if he feels there is any remote indication of AI use, even going through questions too quickly will get you a 0. Which is insane considering it is multiple choice. I hate science now.

Do not take this professor unless you have to. Worst class I've had. He treats everyone like they're cheating and nothing is ever good enough. Grades are insanely picky, docking points for tiny things like wording or spelling. Zero empathy, zero flexibility, just a constant power trip.

DO NOT take this professor. He would comment on everything you do at the most random times and take away points unless you meet with him. He was really rude to me the one time I did meet with him and did not give me points back.
I wouldn't recommend it. I had to drop "it" before it got worse. I would rather wait another semester than try this class, it's not worth it.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! I REPEAT DO NOT!! He is a picky grader and comments on literally every you write. He literally gave me a zero on my quiz. I took this class thinking that it would be little flexible for my schedule but I hate to say it was the most demanding class ever. I would rather take it with a professor on CAMPUS!!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Genuinely have never been so frustrated at a class, let alone an online class before. Dr. Evans will comment on literally everything you do. You think he won't have time? "Oh there are too many students he won't go through EVERYTHING I do and critique it...." WRONG. He will. Please, please, please don't take this class.

There's a lot of bad reviews here, and though the course was hard and information-dense, I thought he did a good job highlighting the important things and explaining concepts. All of his lectures have detailed illustrations, too.

This is the worst class you could ever take. I took it online to have more flexibility, WRONG! Assignments are due in the middle of the day and he is the pickiest grader. You spend most of your time learning to meet his unrealistic expectations and you don't learn. Jusst take it from an on campus professor!

He literally states in his syllabus that he will not teach you everything you need to know for the homework and quizzes. He expects you to take principles from lectures and research to answer the questions. Each lecture (3/week) comes with 40-70 homework questions that you have to do this for. This class in insanely hard and makes me hate science.

Too bad there isn't a rating lower than 1...
Rude in his grading and unnecessarily hard, doesn't help but his responses are condescending. Tests are also very difficult, the test averages were below 50%
I didn't listen to the bad reviews, but please listen to this one and don't take from him. You will regret it.

Avoid taking MMBIO241 with Prof. Evans if possible. He sets an unreasonably high bar and seems to delight in making the class overly difficult. However, using Unstuck ai and other study tools can help mitigate the challenge.
He doesn't really teach and gives you way too much homework to be able to actually learn the material yourself. He's also not very nice.

Many of the things we were tested on were not mentioned in his lecture videos. He expects his students to look up the information if it is not included in the lecture. There are no exam reviews for any of the tests and the way questions are asked are intended to trip you up.

Ya it's all true, I did well in this class but it felt like the class was designed to work against you. Dr. Evans assumed the worst of people and graded very harshly. The final was keyed wrong by 20% (I suspect he did it on purpose) so everyone thought they failed, then he changed it last minute. That's just an example, it's bad

Dr. Evans has truly mastered not the field of teaching biology, but rather making you believe you're in a nightmare from which you will never wake.

Okay, but really. He recommends you to google instead of following a textbook, removes points for the most unnecessary things, teaches immaturely, and is a condescending communicator. Save yourself.

I had the unique displeasure of taking 240 AND 241 from Dr. Evans. Huge mistake. His tests are far beyond the scope of the class, and often feel like a reading comprehension test rather than an exam testing my understanding of the content. His objective seems to be to make students hate molecular biology. Don't understand why he still teaches.

Dr. Evans is a very intelligent and well-published scientist. However, he lacks empathy, respect for students, and trust in students. Every time I spoke with him I felt belittled and intimidated. His tests are unreasonably difficult. He made an active effort to remove helpful ressources and restrict the way that TAs could interact with students.

BIGGEST regret of BYU was taking MMBIO 241 from Evans. 241 could be a really cool class but he goes out of his way to make things impossibly hard and has no care for helping you succeed. He's rude, condescending and grades unfairly. THIS IS YOUR WARNING. DON'T take a class from this professor.

So so so bad. Do not take a class from him whatever you do. I have never dealt with with someone so rude and bad at teaching. Horrible professor who does not care about his students or helping them succeed. No extra credit, no retakes, no second chances. He always assumes the worst and that students are cheating.

Dr. Evans was the rudest, most inconsiderate professor I have taken a class from. His quizzes were unclear and almost everyone got below 75% on all of them. Dr. Evans was never willing to help students who had to miss class. He caused a lot of unnecessary stress and anxiety. Dr. Evans is condescending and makes students feel like they're not smart.

Dr. Evans is the most inconsistent professor I have ever had. He is currently using all of the teaching materials that were previously used by another professor, and then he changes all the quizzed/tested material so that it is beyond the scope of the course. DO NOT EVEN CONSIDER this professor, not worth losing your 4.0 GPA on a 1 credit class.

TAKE FROM ANOTHER PROFESSOR. I don't know how he can make this 1-credit class as a 3-credit one, but I feel that the only thing he wants is to fail students. He even told the TAs not to help students too much. It's not worth it to take a 1-credit class with such a bad setting from him.

His ego gets in the way, making a 1-credit class a 3-credit class. He tests us on concepts that he has not explained and makes seemingly simple topics very complex in order for his students to lose points.

This platform doesn't allow me to accurately rate just how appalling this professor is. I wouldn't even call him a professor. You will not be quizzed on what you have been taught, and to your surprise, you will find you will also not be taught. Grades in a fascinating way, his favorite number is zero.

This professor is pretentious, rude, and unhelpful. The material he uses (all of his lectures + the lab notebook) are several years old, created by another (much better) professor, and his tests are both deceptive and contain new information not included in or unrelated to the course material. Avoid taking a class from this professor.

Most likely the worst professor I've ever had the pleasure of taking at BYU. Quiz grades are ridiculously hard and half the material is never taught/covered. If you like guessing on every other question, Evans is the man for you. Hardest class I'm taking this semester and I'm generally a straight-A student. TA schedule is wack, seems unprofessional

Dr. Evans has turned this 1 credit course into a living nightmare for all of his students. He teaches approximately 5% of the material covered on his assessments, and is the worst professor at Brigham Young University. My 4th grade science teacher could do a better job. If there are any other 241 options at the time you're reading this, run.

His quizes are open internet but his questions are impossible to find anywhere. Hope you like reading journal article after journal article just to inevitably guess and then have to write about why your answer is or isn't correct. Tests are impossible to study for because he has about 10,000 quiz questions that could possible be on each exam.

This professor made learning impossible. If you didn't achieve an A+ in Honors Chem you'll be lost. Paul doesn't give explanations on subjects, nor is emphatic to confusion, and he doesn't want you to succeed. If you like guessing 90% of the time, he's the right teacher. Don't think about getting help anywhere else, he will fail you for doing so.

Dr. Evans' conduct at the University and in the community is abominable. He is frankly unkind, condescending, and derogatory toward students. Please take this class from anyone else. Dr. Evans will likely attribute his poor rating to the difficulty of the class, but he is just a tremendously difficult person. I don't know how he still has his job.

Wow. I have never had such a bad experience with a faculty member. His class made me reconsider my major and even my life plans. He is constantly correcting students' syntax and punctuation while the majority of the course contains glaring errors even I wouldn't make. This man made me cry on several occasions. He is condescending and unkind.

The worst professor I've had at BYU. He is very strict and merciless which I'm fine with as long as the professor can but he couldn't do even do that. I avoided his office hours because he would assume I hadn't watched the recorded lectures if I didn't understand some concept and just made me feel dumb. I never left his office hours feeling good.

Very disorganized. He said we could use any textbook online for the class. His lectures were prerecorded, out of order, a complete mess. I did not like the fact that the course was online and the lectures had almost no content in them. Each class lecture was about 15 minutes, his class was a disaster. For those taking MMBIO240 choose someone else.

The curve at the end of the class will save your grade, but getting there is torturous.  The test averages are always ridiculously low because the information included in the lectures is only a fraction of what you're tested on.  That's not a secret - he's proud of his philosophy.
Really hard class. Definitely use the TAs or Dr. Evans to succeed in this class. There is a massive curve at the end of the course.

This professor should be fired. Absolutely worst class I have ever taken. Not only does he make it extremely difficult with his lack of teaching skills, but he goes out of his way to make his students feel inferior and stupid. He will track how long things take on canvas and question everything you do. He will accuse you of cheating every chance.

This class is the worst class I've taken in two years. Skip this on-demand class, I promise its not easy. The class avg on tests was 50% but there is a massive curve at the end. DONT TAKE IT... STOP SCROLLING, trust me.

Worst professor I've had. I went in to ask him questions sometimes outside of class, and he acted very condescending. The material he taught honestly was not that hard, but I would spend HOURS studying for the tests (doing practice questions he provided) and some of the questions would be about things we had never talked about. Don't do it
R Paul Evans arrogant and rude. He really doesn't care about his students. Do not have him as a professor. You will regret it. Honestly he is just a terrible human.

Absolutely horrible. "lectures" were short videos with questions not related to the vid. He does not know how to make a class work at all. I dropped after two lectures but my friend taking the class now is in literal he11. I'd give it 0 or negative if I could. can't learn ANYTHING
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Wait until next semester if needed.

I think Dr Evans would like to believe that he has negative reviews because his class is difficult. Or maybe because students can't comprehend his intelligence. But, he really has negative feedback because he acts arrogant and is certainly condescending (a common word you see in these reviews). His class is also a mess. Very disorganized.

The hardest part about it is the tests, but Dr. Evans gives you what you need to succeed. We were encouraged to form study groups. Mine had three people including me. It was my lifeline in this class. Don't skip this part! Going over quizzes together, which are open-neighbor, saved me. Evans teaches you to think like a scientist; good MCAT prep!
Please do not take this class from him. It is not worth the sacrifice and time you'll be spending.
No mercy. Incredibly difficult tests. Condescending. Please do not take this course from him if you value having any free time. Worst professor of my college career.

This is the worst class I've ever taken. The lectures and quizzes/tests have almost nothing in common. He expects you to know things before the start of the semester that I haven't even had to learn for classes that have MMBIO240 as a requirement. I can't run out of awful things to say about this class. Take it from another professor, seriously.

Please do not take this class. There is no assigned material, only a couple videos that he makes. The average test grades were mid 50's. If you find a mistake in his grading you have less than two days to tell him to get points back. If not, even if you are right, you will not get points back. Find another professor.

He is always available for "help", but he will never answer any question. He always responds with a question. There were times when I just stopped asking because it was so unhelpful. Half the questions on the test are from things he did not teach in the lectures, but expects you to know as if you were a molecular biologist.

Evans is very accessible to help students, yet just as condescending (even to his TAs). Average test scores in the class are in the mid/low 60s. His tests are long and hard. He doesn't provide any text to study from either. Be prepared to study lots on Google and then be blindsided on tests. The saving grace for me was his massive curve.

Took this class fully online (remote delivery). Video lectures don't cover everything so be ready to Google a lot and ask the TAs for help (you can ask Dr Evans but it might turn into a verbal microbio quiz you aren't ready for). Do the practice problems online over and over. He says buying the book is optional but it helps a TON. Hard class.

I have never had a professor be so condescending and unsympathetic towards me even in hard circumstances. He doesn't teach anything but expects you to understand molecular biology on a Ph.D. level by finding things on your own. His tests could belong to a different class. Seems like a good guy, but I have never hated or struggled in a class so much

The worst professor I've ever had. Extremely strict on grading and unclear about the parameters of assignments- as in, said I could use the internet on an assignment then accused me of cheating at the end of the semester and docked my grade a ridiculous amount. He's very intrusive, unwilling to listen, unhelpful with ?'s, doesn't care abt students.

No assigned textbook because "life doesn't have a textbook". Short lecture videos that don't answer many of the questions he asks. I've never felt so belittled when asking a professor for help understanding a topic than I have talking to Dr. Evans. The only helpful thing about this class were the TA hours nearly 8AM to 8PM. Worst class I ever had.

Lecture videos are useless. Exams and Quizzes are on things that have never been discussed in lecture videos. He seems nice but is really a very creepy, condescending and nosey person. Do not take his class. Worse class I have taken by far.

Pros: Teaches the most basic parts of Molecular Biology Cons: The class is supposed to be about the deeper subjects of Molecular Biology, which he tests and quizzes on without teaching. He is disrespectful and berates students for asking for help avoid like the plague. Heck you'd learn more from getting the plague and asking your doctor questions

SKIP THIS PROFESSOR. I cant say enough bad things!! His lecture videos are beyond pointless. The quiz questions have absolutely nothing to do with his lecture videos. He tells you to get answers from google. His test questions are insane. If you try to get help from him he's very condescending. This class is a waste of money. Take anyone else.

So first things first he teaches you maybe 1/3 to 1/4 of what you need to know for his class. His lectures cover a couple topics that you then understand but he expects you to learn almost everything on your own. He gives "learning objectives" that are profoundly unhelpful and you have no set book to read so you don't really know where to find help

He provides all the resources you need to succeed and is very willing to help outside of class, but is very condescending towards students. The class is great if you don't minds dealing with being treated that way. One really good thing about him is that he encourages students to seek out the truth and be proactive about their learning!

Dr. Evans taught a "flipped classroom" which only works if you ask follow up questions and look up things you don't understand. The class can be frustrating at times because you lose points at every part of the class but overall it was a class that teaches you how to analyze lots of complicated data and make sense of it.

The class structure is absolutely appalling for this class. It consists of us being tested heavily on information that he has legitimately not taught us about and expects us to research completely on our own. The only thing you will learn in this class is to memorize 500+ answers form his study guides to even survive the tests.

Took MMBIO 240 online & he's awful! 2-3 weekly lessons you complete by watching videos he recorded before each question, except half the videos don't answer the question & require you to search the web or other sources. He says "Hwhich," "hwhat," or "hwhen" in every video. Weekly quizzes, multiple tests, and final. Recommend to someone you hate.

Professor Evans is a terrible professor. He is a wonderful person, but he does not answer questions well. The questions he asks are confusing and misleading. He doesn't teach the material on the tests that he creates. This is by far the hardest class that I have ever taken. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!! I learned absolutely nothing from him.

His class is an absolute joke. Need I say more? He gives you study guides that have nothing to do with the material you are studying, and then tests you on that material. He's definitely not a good professor to take any subject from.

Biggest mistake of my life taking this class. Dr. Evans is a nice guy but don't think I learned a thing and it was more about being able to memorization beyond what is humanly possible. I took this class online and would never wish it upon anyone.

Dont take this as an online class. Take it in person. Please. This class requires clarifying questions that just cant happen online. Dr. Evans was awful in responses to messages and usually just referenced his syllabus rather than helping me through a problem. If it doesnt fit in your schedule, take it another semester.

Honestly Dr. Evans is one of the best at BYU. Study the study guides and you're guaranteed a good grade. Take detailed notes on lectures and talk to him or his TA's, they are all awesome! Also one of the funniest professors I've ever had. Work hard, the subject is difficult regardless who you take it from, but Dr. E is by far the best choice!

Professor Evans was super funny but I strongly disliked this class. I studied the study guides religiously because that is what his tests were primarily based on but because of that I feel like I truly learned nothing. There was so much material and I took this class in spring which made the work load almost unmanageable.

Evans is by far the worst professor I've ever had. Class is worthless, but you have to go for the iClicker quizzes. What he "teaches" barely coincides with what is on the study guides/tests. Be prepared to teach yourself everything from the 500+ page study guide. I studied over 20 hours a week and barely scraped a B. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!

Good guy but I really would recommend another teacher. The only reason to go to class is to try and get points on iclicker questions. Didn't learn a thing from lectures and just memorized study guides to do good on tests. Doing that only get you so far, final is pretty hard.

Worst person to take this class from. Does not teach you one thing. Relies on study guides that are 20-30 pages long. These study guides will save your life but they take forever to go through. Tests are hard and have nothing to do with the lectures. I'd consider taking it from someone else!
Didn't learn anything. Probably because he didn't teach anything.

Dr. Poole is a good teacher if you are ready to hit the ground running to learn mmbio. There is no required textbook for the class so it's hard to learn and you are expected to know a lot before class. If you are willing to put in the work to learn, he's great, otherwise, if you don't know anything like me, you will struggle.

Best class to take if you're planning on med school. He's way harder than the other MMBIO professors but it is well worth it if you're willing to put in the work. The amount you learn in his class is incredible, perfect prep for the MCAT and his tests really push you on critical reasoning and concept application. You become an independent learner.

I loved this class with Dr. Evans!  He is always super willing to help outside of class.  His teaching method is perhaps a bit sporadic, yes, but it's really interesting if you try to listen and follow.  The great thing about his teaching style though is that he teaches you to think effectively, not just memorize.  Do the study guides though!

Dr. Evan's lectures are rather pointless but he has graded iclicker questions (as in you have to get the right answer for points) every single class. Class really is rather pointless. He gives out study guides and previous tests so study those for the test.

Dr. Evans expects you to become an independent learner. He tells you what you need to know on the study guides, and expects you to learn the concepts via Wikipedia, Youtube, and other resources. That skill was more valuable to me than the details of the class. He also does webinars to let you watch from home which was nice.

STUDY GUIDES ARE THE KEY. The test comes mostly from those EXACT questions. Even if you just remember the right answers, the tests will be a breeze. If you don't study though, you will get HAMMERED on the final. He front-loads/scares you the first week. Textbook isn't necessary, but occasionally helpful. Rent it, or use the ones in the TA lab.

Dr. Evans loves to ramble on about pointless things. He rarely explains challenging concepts, and expects you to understand what he is speaking about. Every other student I questioned about his class either said "I have no clue what is going on," or "I hate this class."  Would recommend NEVER taking MMBIO 240 from him. EVER.
Going to his lectures was pointless, he rarely taught things we actually needed to know for the test.

Dr. Evans is a 10 on the scale of entertainment value, but his lectures certainly feel disconnected from the coursework organization. He has an obviously brilliant mind, and often seems to overcomplicate the material in-lecture. Keys to the game: strong understanding of the central dogma and a lot of reviewing the test study guides. A LOT.

I took this last Fall & still have nightmares about it. Science classes are hard simply because the material is hard. But I still, to this day, don't know how Dr. Evans hoped to help us learn with his teaching style. His class is completely based on memorizing all semester and then throws a comprehensive final at you. I learned absolutely nothing.
I had a horrible experience.  Worst teacher I had at BYU and worst class I ever took.  He is confusing and has weird humor.  Hard class.

I like Dr. Evans, I thought he was funny, but he frankly has an abysmal teaching style.  Lectures do not make any sense unless you read the textbook beforehand.  You will do well in this class if you are good at learning the material yourself, lectures aren't that useful but he gives Iclicker quizzes in class so you will want to be there each day.
Tests are brutal, and he does not guide you very much in telling you what you need to know. He just expects you to know everything.

This was a tough class but Dr. Evans gives students every opportunity to earn points and do well in the class. He is a bit unorganized at times and his tests are difficult so go to class! If you want to succeed in his class make sure you study all the past tests that he makes available for the students to review.
He was unclear and unhelpful. You had to learn everything at home and on your own and then class was no help at all. Very much disliked this class.

Never disliked a class more. The lectures suck as in you study at home and then get to lecture and feel like you're in the wrong class because you have no idea what he's talking about. I felt like nothing prepared me for the final. The TA's took the class from another professor and even said Evans was way harder. AVOID!!
Good

If you understand/memorize the study guides you can get an A. Has "Take Home Quizes" which get tough towards the end of semester. Is a little difficult to understand what he teaches in lecture. I used the textbook a fair deal.  Naturally an MMBIO class at BYU is going to be difficult--class average was a little high at 78%.

Dr. Evans is the absolute worst professor at BYU. He does not care for his students, nor for their education. On each take home quiz he asks us to check our own grades, and report to him if there are any mistakes. I did so, but he laughed and said that he drops some anyways so it didn't matter. I got a 0 instead of the 9 I had earned. WORST TEACHER

Professor Evans is a great guy and has a lot of humor in his lessons. However, he does not necessarily teach exactly what he tests on. He has a study guide for 10+ chapters with up to 100 questions on each study guide. His tests are pretty much memorizing these 1000+ questions. If you like to memorize and not learn anything, this class is for you.

This class is a joke. The only way to do well on the tests is to straight up memorize the study guide practice problems. That means memorizing 2000+ complex problems. He is a funny guy, but his lectures have no correlation with performance on the tests.

All I have to say is amen to everyone's comments. Great guy with a good outlook on life and science. He really wants to help you and will if you go to him, which is very difficult because then it causes even more work for you. I would absolutely NOT take this class again from him. It was the worst class I've ever taken and I suffered for it.

The class was really hard, and you need to work for your grade. He's a really funny guy, and can make some edgy, racy jokes at times.  This guy is really smart, and can lose you easily. Just study the study guides, and you'll be fine. No text book required.

Dr. Evans has a funny sense of humor, as in he's mostly crude and very egocentric. He's very smart and I'm sure is a spectacular scientist, but his lectures prepare you minimally for the exam. Expect to spend an excessive amount of time outside of class learning the material and reviewing the study guides.  I would recommend a different professor.

Horribly disorganized class. The only reason I went to lecture was because of the in class iClicker quizzes given nearly every class. He is always trying to make jokes, many of which can come off as offensive. Does not respect students very much. I would advise to take this class from anyone else but Evans.

He obviously knows the material he's teaching... But doesn't convey it very well to the students. It's hard to tell what you should write down and the homework is never directly related. The tests are basically copy and pasted study guides - and because of this I don't think many of us got much out of this course, no real learning. Don't take it.

Since the first day, I wanted to be this guy's TA. He leaks intelligence into anyone with a basic background in biology and a desire to learn. Hammers good habits for critical thinking into you. Has good, original ideas for effective teaching. Not everyone agrees with that. Prepares for MCAT. Offers online option for lectures. No textbook needed.

Dr. Evans is an interesting professor. He has plenty of good stories and is always in a good mood. BUT his class is very confusing. He is a bit scatterbrained and doesn't really teach lectures in a logical way. I don't feel like I learned very much cell biology.  PS He deserves all those chili peppers and the #1 ranking. He's a smokin hot dude.

By far the worst teacher I have had at BYU. Never take molecular biology from him. His lectures are all over the place and very disorganized. It was hard to even understand what subject we were talking about. He was no help at all and I didn't learn a thing.
Amazing professor. Lectures to prepare MCAT or DAT testing.

It may seem like the class is hard, but honestly just study the study guides and you will get an A. He pulls almost all of his test questions from the study guides, which you have access to all semester.

Dr. Evans is very confusing and the material is very disorganized. I was very dissatisfied with the course overall. I went to every class and tried hard to understand the material. Evans, however, expects most students to already have an above average knowledge of everything we haven't learned yet. I would for sure avoid taking this class from him.

Great, funny guy, not a great teacher. Doesn't convey material in an understandable way. No textbook required, but should be. Lectures are unorganizedrandom. Tests:70% of questions come from study guides, be prepared to study 70+ pgs of pure questions per test. Must study 10-20 hours a week in order for an A or B, unless you know material already.

Dr. Evans was an amazing teacher.  People either loved him or hated him.  He is very funny and keeps you entertained.  His class lectures were recorded and you could remotely view the lectures and participate online, for example if you were out of town.  Requires you to think critically!! This class seriously helped prepare me for the MCAT.

Hardest class ever, not because of the material, but because he is so disorganized and hard to understand. He is smart, but a HORRIBLE teacher as far as helping students Learn. His grading policy is pretty nice, but what he tests you on are a complicated mess of things you have never seen before. I studied 9+ hours for tests and failed all of them.

Dr Evans is smart and knows his stuff but it is way too hard to follow. There is so much information and the class was not organized. Don't have to buy a book and he has study guides. The first test is almost identical to his others but after that the questions on the test are really wordy and hard to understand
Haters are going to hate, but he knows his stuff.
Dr. Evans makes this class unnecessarily hard. His lecture prepare you minimally for the upcoming tests and his study guides have way to much extraneous information.
WORST. TEACHER. EVER! so confusing in lectures and wasn't very clear when you came to him for help. He often made you feel dumb for asking questions. I do not recommend him, EVER!

Awesome teacher very fair, you can attend class online, he allows for regrades. Although I didn't do super well in this class, I must admit that it was fair. For the final we got to take in a 8 by 11 piece of paper. This class overs a ton of material. LOOK AT PREVIOUS EXAMS, STUDY GUIDE QUESTIONS, AND TAKE HOME QUIZZES contain >70% of the answers.

One of the worst teachers at BYU. If not for in class quizzes I would have never attended lecture. He doesn't teach towards his tests ever. The only way to get a decent grade is to MEMORIZE THE STUDY GUIDE QUESTIONS he posts online. He pretty much uses those questions to make up his tests. Really useless class though.
Lectures are scattered and hard to follow. Evans is a really funny professor though.

AMAZING Professor. I saved this class until the last possible semester because I had heard such awful horror stories. Not the case. If you want an A you can easily have it. He gave us an exam to study off of and then repeated the questions on the actual exam. Boosted my MCAT Bio score 4 points! I learned so much and it was easy! TAKE THIS COURSE!

He is a nice guy. He has a Q & A review session every Monday night online, which was very helpful at times. He was very willing to help. His classes do seem a little disorganized. His tests aren't bad if you read through the objectives and do ALL of the practice problems. In-class iClicker questions are worth part of your grade. Good professor.

Really personable guy, and while I didn't take mmbio 240 from him, my experience says he can't be as hard as some of these people make him out to be. His tests correlate so well to his study guides it is crazy. I do agree that his lectures are scattered without an overall picture, class is kind of useless at points. Not terrible, but not great.

I was very excited to learn the material for this class and came out very disappointed due to the unorganized nature of this class: the lectures aren't clear, the materials provided aren't helpful and I don't feel like I actually learned anything even though I got an A-. For the final he let us make a full page of notes, yet the average was a 68%

My hardest class this semester. One of those classes that you feel you can do nothing for to raise your grade. In class quizzes are difficult and so stressful. Take home quizzes each week, that you hope you will do okay on, but end up being pretty hard.

Professor Evans is a poor teacher. Don't take it from him! His lectures are confusing and have nothing to do with the tests. The worst teacher I have had at BYU. Most frustrating class I have taken. I didn't learn anything.

This is the most frustrating class I have taken during my time here at BYU. While he is down-to-earth he makes no sense, is not helpful, expects way too much from students and is strict. If you want to memorize over 100 pages of information for each test then his is your class.

By far the most frustrating class I've taken at BYU. An extremely personable man, but his class lacks any sort of organization. He does not frame his lectures, so you have all of the specifics without having any sort of overall picture. Science is what I do, and I love it, and this has been the first class that I have hated going to every lecture.

The class overall was pretty good. I've seen teachers use the learning objectives and study guides with more success--he wants you to learn so much that I already don't remember much of what I had to learn.
