Honest review of this professor would fall outside the guidelines for RMP. Do not listen to other bot reviews here. She does an extraordinary poor job and supports blatantly opposition views of the church.

I loved loved loved taking this class!There is a fair amount of reading, but it's honestly not too bad. There is a lot of out of class workshops required, but if you get them done it's not too bad, and they are useful! I now have the tools required to do family history, and I got to learn a lot about my family on the way!
She has been the most kind and compassionate professor I ever had, and she taught some really interesting and eye-opening things. She is fair, not too tough, highly recommend.

Honestly, a really good teacher. Class was super easy if you do the work. Readings and attendance help your participation grade. Weekly digital dialogue posts. 1 page essays for the two midterms. 10-14 page final exam essay. Play the game and you can get an A no doubt. She is super nice.

Dr. DeSchweinitz is one of my favorite professors at BYU. I've taken several classes from her and she has been my mentor on a lot of research. I've loved each of her classes. I highly recommend taking a class from her. I'm planning on taking more from her.

The worst professor I have ever had. Honestly, if you have the chance, run away! She is super sweet, but as an instructor, she terribly falls short. She does not help you in your papers throughout the whole semester, not even if you consult with her every week during office hours!

Her class required a lot of reading and it took a big chunk of my time outside of class to complete all the required reading. It was an interesting class and she is very passionate about what she teaches. It was a discussion based class, so you have to come prepared with thoughts on the reading in order to get the participation points.

She is tough. I am not going to beat around the bush on that one. She expects a lot from her students but is also willing to help them out if they need it and ask for it. I took her for my capstone because I knew she would require the best of me, and push me to excellence. Hardest professor I have had, but also the best!

Dr. de Schweinitz's class is fairly easy. If I would have actually read all of the reading, the online quizzes (which are open book) would have been a cinch. Also, There are only three papers and a mid-term. Occasionally there are fast-writes, which are easy. The final is two take-home essays. Take this class.

Absolutely loved de Schweinitz's class and learned so much. She challenged us to go behind the texts to find the root of the author's biases and perspectives. The workload is appropriate for an upper level History course--you'll read at least a book a week + paper. I found her personable and helpful, I just had to ask! Highly recommend.

If you have another choice for The Historian's Craft, take it. de Schweinitz is very smart and interesting, but there's not a more arrogant or demeaning professor in the department. If you do take this class, don't make the mistake of asking questions or challenging her perspective.  She will vaporize you and your grade.

One of the best classes I have had at BYU.  Most of the lectures are based around discussing our readings.  She is more interested in ideas than names, dates, and places.  It wasn't that hard to get an A if you did the work.  I would recommend this class to anyone that wants a different perspective on American history.
Probably the worst teacher i have had my entire collegiate career. She truly makes no sense when communicating with the students. Someone needs to clue this woman in.

This class helped me to think deeply and differently about african-american history.  This class is worth taking.  Was not that hard.  No textbooks but lots of reading although the books we read were all very interesting.  It is not that hard to get an A

Dr. DeSchweinitz is awesome! I am so glad I took Historian's Craft from her because she is one of the few teachers who truly teaches you how to write a paper. She's also really helpful when coming up with thesis ideas and sources. There's a lot of work involved but you'll find that with all Historian's Craft classes.
Meh. Attend class, take notes and do the readings and you'll be fine. Sometimes she'll talk about white men with a smirk on her face but she's not always uber-opinionated. The class was meh.
The class was alright. Just read and take notes in class and you'll be fine. I've fallen asleep several times in class and am still doing well. Do the quizzes too.

An excellent class.  Prof De Schweinitz presents detailed information, and then encourages students to explore their personal takes on the issues through class and group discussions, and writing assignments.  The self-directed and exploratory expectation for writing assignments is a reasonable and useful expectation in an upper-level class.

I learned more about US histroy from my high school teacher. Tries to give different perspective of history focusing on monority groups. Class was never very interesting. Class is not difficult and you can get a good grade with minimal effort.

Its obvious that others have had the same experience I have with this person.  Not only is she difficult to deal with, but her expression is completely indifrerent when you need her help.  Beyond all of her personal misgivings I truly sensed that she herself couldn't understand what she wanted outed of her students. The whole class was perplexed.

I really liked this professor - the class was interesting, and the assignments were really enjoyable. There is a variety in her syllabus that makes it easy for all kinds of students to find their niche. Definitely take this class if you're interested in Women's history.

I could not stand her personality.  It seemed really artificial with the typical liberal professor slant.  Ivory tower compassionate.  Kind of a bleeding heart.  Has two hobby horses.  Blacks and women and how they've been wronged.  All of us white middle class males are the greatest threat to society.  Got really sick of it.

She is very vague, whether it is on assignments or on the actual subject matter.  If you want to learn about blacks and women, take this class, but she won't teach you things you couldn't deduce yourself.  She never corrects people when they say something untrue in class.

She's not my favorite history professor but she tries really hard. Plus her final is a take home so that's a bonus! Be warned that there is a lot of writing, but those writing assignments will pull up your grade. She lectures a lot so make sure you take good notes.

I actually really enjoyed this class.  Prof. de Schweinitz is new, and it is obvious, but she has really good intentions.  I feel like her classes will improve as she goes along.  The course load was light, it's possible to get by without doing the readings, and as long as you come to class, take notes, put forth a little effort, you'll be fine.

I found this class very frustrating. There was a lot of reading and a lot of papers. She is unclear about what she wants and deviates from her syllabus. She kind of adds whatever she wants. I would not take another class from her.

She is a little unclear on what she wants on her papers, but grading is fair and not harsh at all.  I would take this class again.  One page paper due each friday, but again grading is not bad.  Work load is not too difficult.

Yes, not the greatest class, but not the worst. She is new and has some kinks to work out. For a 300 level class I found the workload to be actually very doable. I got a high A on the test without doing all of the readings and without too much effort. In my opinion, a good deal of professors in the history department are much much worse.

This is the worst class I have had here at BYU. She never explains anything. She never tells you how she wants papers done or what is on the test. Very unhelpful. There is a lot of reading. She has a paper due every other week. I did not learn anything in this class that I had not already learned from worthwhile classes

She is an amazing and really caring teacher. I actually took her for Psych 341, but it wasn't an option to choose from on here. She really wants each student to succeed and will do anything she can to help you. It is a little reading heavy, but all of the assignments are actually applicable and fun. My favorite class I've taken in college.

You know exactly what to expect from her! Everything is very clear and grading is fair. Class discussions are super engaging if you let them be and you learn a ton. From this class I learned how to better read research. I cannot hype up Dr. Weidmann enough! There is no better professor at BYU!

I took Psych 341 (Personality) with Professor Weidmann and LOVED it! She is my favorite professor ever and this was definitely the best class I've taken at BYU. She cares so much about her students and is passionate about what she teaches. There are no exams, just quizzes every class. I loved our discussions and learned so much. She's the best!
She is a great professor! She helps her students individually if they need it and she teaches difficult concepts in a way that is helpful. I would recommend taking classes from her!

This class was not about world music, it was a library research class. I wanted to learn about music but instead we had class prep assignments that would be 30 pages and big project was reading an ethnography and finding other sources with citations. No exams which was great, I don't feel like I've learned much of anything. Take another general!!

This class was not what I was expecting. We didn't learn about world music cultures as much as we discussed the philosophy of music and its connection to our identity. Mildly interesting, but expect that. Stopped going halfway through. Lots of really busy work that takes up time; we read about 20 pages almost every week for Class Prep Assignments.

This class was a slog. Super easy, just loads of easy busy work. I tried to be engaged and found a few things interesting but overall it felt like the class shoved other cultures down my throat. I love other cultures and they have amazing attributes but this was just overstretching it. She is great as a person but I did not enjoy the class.

Unbelievably boring. Class felt like going to nursery. Easy GE, but never felt engaged or learned anything. Honestly just felt like a big waste of time. She's very nice and cares about her students, but not the best teacher. Constantly going on about DEI - class felt like it was only about why we need to be nice to people who are different from us.

Easiest class at BYU. I took it for the Arts GE and didn't feel like a GE. I probably spent 2 hours every week outside of class working on assignments and this was in the Spring. No Tests or Quizzes, instead lots of easy assignments, in which you can easily get 100 percent. Also lots of extra credit. I ended up having a 107%.

Dr. Reed is awesome. She is passionate about music and has great insights to offer on the different topics covered in class. She is very kind and respectful. The topics covered are interesting and helped me view music and culture in a new way. I would highly recommend taking this class!

Professor Reed was amazing. She doesn't overstep bounds with this GE. She knows that most of us were there to fulfill the credit. The class has no due dates and no exams. There are around 30 assignments that can be completed at any point. Highly recommend taking this class!

Music 203 was so fun with her! I took it over the summer, so the material was spaced out differently, but I genuinely enjoyed the large project we did. It was basically an annotated bib, and she is very sweet and just wants to help. She is very passionate about world music, and knows how to handle tough questions and scenarios. Very respectful

Dr. Reed was an amazing professor! I took this class summer semester, and she was very understanding of each student's needs. We were allowed to turn in all assignments late with no penalty. There are no exams, just a research project that you work on throughout the semester which is very easy. I highly recommend!!!

Dr. Reid is so nice! She made this GE easy but interesting, and I gained more awareness of music. Lectures aren't worth a ton of points, but I liked her comments and stories. We would often discuss a musical example and the reading assignment. Sometimes I missed the reading assignment beforehand, and I was still fine participating in class.

If you're looking for an easy--but still fun and engaging--class for the arts GE, this is a great option. Lecture attendance was definitely not necessary, and there were no tests, but I went to the lectures because they were interesting. She did "show and tell" at the start of class and we watched musical artists and discussed them, which was fun.

Dr. Reed is delightful, and this class was so easy, but also very interesting. Most of the assignments are pretty easy, and the only bigger assignment is a research project, which is very personalized, and is split up into sections, so it's pretty easy. Definitely would recommend this class with Dr. Reed!

Dr. Reed is great and is really understanding of the different circumstances of students. She cares about the students and understands that her class isn't the only class her students are taking. Every assignment is pretty much completion. Easy A, but also a high-quality professor. Would recommend taking this class.
This class was so so easy. I didn't show up for half the semester and I still got a 107% in the class.

The kindest professor ever. She will work with you on anything you need, and her class is very easy. There's a bit of work, but it teaches you a lot, and you're able to explore things on your own. Go to her class! You'll learn something, and she's super funny and just wonderful to be around. I loved going even when only 3 people were there.

I absolutely love her. She cares a ton about students and was great about working with people if you needed help with something. The project for the class was easy and let me explore what I wanted to. It does a really good job of showing you more perspectives and just bringing a nice view of worldwide music and cultures.

Dr. Reed was a great professor! I learned a lot about ethnomusicology in her class, and doing a project based on what I was interested in allowed me to apply what we were learning to something that I wanted to learn more about. We listened to a lot of music from a lot of different cultures, and it really felt like it broadened my perspective.

Professor Nielson is so kind and cares so much about his students and their success. The only reason I didn't love this class is because it was very unorganized. There weren't any clear expectations set from the beginning and a very large portion of our grade ended up being determined by the final.
I hated the actual content of this class, but Professor Rex is really nice and will remember your name and ask you how you're doing. Nice guy, just a bad class.

Very nice and genuinely cares. Tries to cover up when he doesn't know something. He's American, I wouldn't expect him to have all the answers. It is his second language and a culture he had to learn like most of us. I respect professors who admit they don't know something and get back on it. Very "woke" and it shows. So be careful.

Professor Rex did a great job. I had him as a handball instructor, and he was very passionate and ready to help anyone. He wasn't afraid to give good tips so students could get better and was also available outside of class. Everyone in the class seems like they were included well.

His lectures are interesting because you just learn about culture, music, and history. There are 3 homework assignments a week (sometimes), he cancels class a lot, gives you lots of extra credit too. The big project is really fun and he gives you plenty of time to prepare. Exams are open book, open internet, etc. He is super nice and helpful

Rex is a really cool professor. He is very knowledgeable and passionate about Brazilian culture. I learned a lot in this class! The readings are very difficult, and they're done before almost every class. Once you fall behind, it's hard to catch back up.

Professor Nielson is a great professor who really cares about what he is teaching and his students. He is always available to help students out, and he is fair in his workload and grading. Be prepared for lots of reading, but that's to be expected with a literature class.

Professor Nielson has studied and understands Brazilian culture well. His passion for Brazil can be seen in his teaching. He listens to his students and makes adjustments to the class based on feedback. He cares for his students and enjoys knowing them personally. Above average for a non-native professor and communicates the material well.

Rex is a great professor, and you can tell that he really cares about what he teaches! You have to do the readings and make sure you stay on top of things, but overall the class was a great experience. Make sure to study hard and be prepared for the test and you'll be fine.

Terrible professor and class. He doesn't seem to know a lot about what he's teaching but he pretends really well. His language is confusing and he makes up words that don't exist in Portuguese - I checked them. As long as you pretend you like him, you get a good grad.
This class is awesome and I learned a ton about Brazil. Prof. Nielson is fair and kind and was always available. I loved it.

Prof Nielson is a very caring towards his students. I really liked that he was determined to give feedback from tests so everyone can go over what they missed for the final. His tests aren't bad if you study. Only complain is his lectures are sometimes hard to follow because Portuguese isn't my native language. Overall great guy, pretty good class!

Rex is the kind of professor who lets you understand the material until whatever threshold you want. He won't force you to dig deeper into the material, and only students that put in zero effort to 339 think it's a waste of time. But, if you want to actually learn something and leave the class a more learned student, take his class.

Great Professor who really cares about his students. You will enjoy the class as it is a bit of a break from the usual stress of BYU. The only reason why anyone rates him as lower is because he doesn't have the best accent and sometimes swaps Portuguese words for Spanish. These flaws are extremely minor/rare and he's still a wonderful professor.

I do not know how he is a professor in Portuguese with that Portuguese! He needs the students participation at all times in his class,  to balance his lack of knowledge. He is a very social person and likes to talk to everybody, but I was expecting to learn and have classes in Portuguese, not in English. Very disappointed with his class :(
Wow really disappointing class. His portuguese is really bad which might explain why he doesn't talk much and just lets the discussion wander aimlessly. Two thumbs down.

We sit around in a circle and discuss the readings. The discussions have no real direction and are very superficial. It was frustrating because I felt like it was all subjective to students opinions and we didn't really learn anything. Rex is nice but he's more concerned about being liked than teaching anything useful.

Rex is genuine and caring. He is interested in his students-- their personal interests, successes, and happiness. His classes and assigned readings are demanding. However, his classes are engaging and enjoyable. He encourages participation and is always respectful. He is incredibly smart and passionate about the subject matter. Phenomenal teacher

He is a FANTASTIC teacher! He is one of very few teachers that really cares about his students - not just an A in his class, but to be successful in life. He was always willing to help with whatever, is funny and made class enjoyable, and genuinely interested and involved in the course and students. I totally recommend any class from this teacher!!
Rex is nice but his portuguese sucks. Total gringo. The class is easy enough you can get away with just reading the summaries online

Rex is a great teacher, he is a stickler with the papers that you have to do. By the end of the semester I really enjoyed Portuguese literature. This class is very doable, but you need to put in the time, do the readings, go to class, there are a lot of ideas that get thrown around in discussion try to think of how you can use the info.

Rex was a very fair teacher. I did not particularly enjoy the class, at no fault to him, I am just not a fan of poetry or the humanities. He found ways to make it more interesting than the average person. He is a very "cool" teacher. very hip and concerned about his students. We rearranged our desks into a circle every class period. How cool is tha

Dr Brunson's Biological Anthropology class was delightful! She did a great job of breaking it down into sections that all made sense. I also really appreciated her use of science to dismantle racist views in the world. I highly recommend taking it from her!

Dr. Patterson is clearly in love with his subject and his enthusiasm is contagious. Be sure to read for the daily quizzes, but know that he is generous in grading those. Class felt like hanging out and talking about interesting models of behavior. Homework was typical of an econ class. Meet with him, he's amazing!

Great lectures, everyone should take a class from Dr. Patterson in the economics major. He makes it very interesting and knows how to help very well. A great teacher and someone who really wants you to do well. It does not take an incredible amount of work to understand the course and get a good grade.

Dr. Patterson is great, I have recommended everyone in the major to take classes from him. He really cares and is a very easy person to connect with. Every teacher should be more like Dr. Patterson. The class is very easy to get a good grade as long as you do a realistic amount of work.

There's a lot I could say about this class, but Dr. P does a great job making tough concepts easier to understand. He explains things really well and always had good answers to my questions. The projects and assignments weren't too bad, and overall the class was actually pretty fun and interesting. Just a heads-up: don't bring root beer to class;)
This class is eye opening and Dr Patterson is amazing.

His class is incredibly engaging, and I look forward to attending every session. He genuinely cares about each student's success, consistently offers thoughtful feedback, and is always responsive and helpful over email. If you have the opportunity to take his class, don't miss it, it's a truly rewarding experience.

Great option if you need one more class to graduate. Readings are a bit heavy, but you can skim most and get the main idea for quizzes. What I like the most is the demarcation between neo-classical and behavioral economics -- it really altered my viewpoint toward economics. Dr. Patterson and the TA were very helpful, humorous, and salubrious.

Rich is a really nice guy, but this class was so unorganized. The syllabus was wrong, learning suite was a mess, and due dates were all over the place. He tries his hardest to be a good teacher, but some concepts were confusing and not taught well. He cares about the students and there were some good spiritual lessons learned.

Patterson is like your nerdy older brother helping you with your homework. Super good guy, tries really hard to be a good teacher. Sometimes his explanations were confusing, but the material is pretty straight forward. I got away with doing maybe 50% of the required readings and did just fine. Good class if you're just okay at math.
This class is set up well. Homework is beneficial and tests are fair. The professor will help you if you get stuck or lost. Put in the work and you can get a good grade.

I wish I could say that I learned a lot in his class, but honestly, the lectures were super boring and unnecessary.  I could have gotten an A without ever going to class and just watching the videos.  He seems like a decent guy, but I feel like I mostly taught myself and didn't learn a lot from this class.
He is a nice guy but I hated the content of this class. Lots of work for a one credit. The TAs were the most unhelpful.

This class was mostly taught by Seth, with Peter jumping in every few classes. This class was fine. Honestly, I feel like this class had a ton of work for a 1 credit class. There was a new project pretty much every week. You got good feedback on the projects. But I feel like I spent more time doing homework for this class than my 3 credit classes.

Professor Rich is a nice guy and passionate about teaching. The coding projects do take a long time but they are straight forward, just tedious. If you stick to the rubric you can get all of the points you need and if you miss something you can resubmit it for more points at any time.

Prof. Rich is great! He is super funny and he really cares about all of the students in his class. The work is never too difficult in this class, but some projects take a really long time and are a very time consuming. I enjoyed taking this class a lot more than IP&T 371.

Professor Rich was really nice, and super easy to contact out of class. His assignments were sorta unclear when he explained them, but there is a rubric on each assignment so if you read that it will be fine. The TAs were super helpful, and I was in the lab three times this semester. This class is a lot of work, but fun when you figure it out!

When I took the class it was lead by one of his TA's so I'm not sure how much is his protocol and what is her's but the class was pretty strict with grading. They have a rule that is you receive less than 75% on an assignment you get a 0. You can make it up later but it's pretty stressful watching you grade go from 99% to 69% from one assignment

This feels like a 2 or 3 credit class based on the workload each week, but I understand the importance of coding in elementary schools now, and a basic understanding of block code. Although it was a lot of work, almost everything we did could be used in your future classroom. And Peter was a great teacher and was super willing to help.

Professor Rich is great and very helpful! The class isn't the easiest because you're learning how to code, but he does all that he can to help and everything is straightforward. His lectures are very helpful. Definitely seek help outside of class if you need, the TAs and Professor Rich are great resources.

This was an incredibly challenging course for a one credit class. The grading is harsh and you have to redo each assignment if you don't do well enough on it. Each project took me around 15+ hours. And there are 7 total along with other homework. I was able to get a decent grade, but I feel that I taught myself and class time wasn't very helpful.
The IP&T classes in general are way more work than a one credit class, so be prepared. But Professor Rich knows his stuff and is willing to work with students.

This class is not my favorite. It was a ton of work for a 1 credit class. There are a handful of big projects that take a lot of time and I did not really enjoy coding. The rubrics are pretty specific, but you can resubmit assignments. Dr. Rich was very helpful in troubleshooting my coding, but I am glad this class is over!
This was a really fun class! Professor Rich does a great job introducing concepts and helping with troubleshooting with projects. He is very understanding and gives great feedback on homework.

Love Dr. Rich but struggled with the class! There's just so much work involved and I was clocking over 10 hours a week sometimes on a ONE CREDIT class. I felt like I learned a ton but I would have loved more in class time to complete assignments

This class was way too much work for a 1 credit class. Some projects would take hours to complete. But Prof Rich was great. He explained things in a concise way but we never had enough time to finish in class. Coding is not easy to learn and 1 hour classes a week is not enough. Learning to code was fun but we just didn't have enough time.
The class is fine, but it is a TON of work for a 1 credit class. Some assignments took 30 minutes, some took 5-6 hours and there is one due every week.

This is a great class. It's difficult because I hadn't coded before but this is a class meant for teaching elementary coding so that means its actually doable. Coding takes more time than you think, but the TAs have lots of lab hours to help and everything is graded on clear rubrics. You can always resubmit assignments too for full credit. 10/10 :D

You definitely have to work in this class - there are coding assignments due every week. That being said, Prof Rich walks you through the assignments during class so if you go to class and follow along you can pretty much knock out the work. He is great about answering questions and you can redo any assignments for a higher grade.

I have tried so hard to like this guy. But if you are an elementary education major, be wary in taking this class. It is a one-credit course, but you will be working 5-10 hours per week on each assignment. The grading is unclear and you will likely be docked points for unknown reasons. This is my least favorite class at BYU so far.
For a professor that teaches social problems in the US, he certainly does not help social problems in the US. Extremely rude and inconsiderate.

When I took HONRS120, it was Dr. Gill's first time teaching the course, so he was a lot more enthusiastic about the program. I really liked how he talked about disciple-scholarship and tying the gospel into education. He didn't interact much with the students and definitely relied heavily on the TAs, but his lectures were entertaining.

I did some research credits with Dr. Gill and I finished feeling forgotten and unimportant. Our interactions were very surface-level and I felt unprioritized and like it didn't matter if I was in his research lab or not. I've had way more professors who have made it clear that they wanted to mentor me and invest in me, but Dr. Gill was not that.

Dr. Gill was pretty strict and seemed aloof, like he didn't care about the Honors 120 students very much. He left most of the discussion and constructive feedback to the TAs. He was way more interested in his biology work than teaching a class based on interdisciplinary thinking.

The class was interesting but expectations for assignments were difficult to understand and even the TA's didn't know what was happening. Also, 50% of the grade happened in the last couple of weeks of the semester, which made things stressful. Dr. Gill cares about learning, which was inspiring, he just needed better planning and organization!

The class was pretty much all essays based on lectures. Because of the class size, you almost never talked to him and only met with your TA. Towards the end of the semester, it felt like the quizzes were meant to be hard rather than see if we knew the info. It felt unnecessarily difficult for a prerequisite class.

Professor Gill is fantastic. Super great orator, really cares about students and is so passionate about his work. The class itself was tough, lots of essays, some readings that got posted the day before they were due, but Dr. Gill himself is amazing.

This class was not even really taught by Professor Gill, it was usually guest speakers and the TAs. This was his first semester teaching honors 120 but it was a little disorganized and harder than I expected. There were essays every other week and long readings with reading quizzes before every class. But he is super friendly and nice!

By far the most disorganized class I have ever taken, and I am a senior. Long readings and very little direction on how to carry out certain tasks for projects. Most of the class was always confused, which at least made grading more lenient. Not hard to get a good grade, but very frustrating trying to figure out how everything works. Good luck

Class is SO disorganized. All the due dates are based on 2020, the TA's don't know what exactly the teacher wants. I find myself stuck because I don't know that the teacher expects. No tests. Weekly quizzes are tough and pointless. 3 projects that you work on, but he doesn't teach you how to do any of it. Overall frustrated with structure of class.

He puts a lot of effort into the videos which was refreshing, but the class was super heavy, tons of reading, lots of very long papers with super vague instructions and expectations that took the place of midterms. Weekly quizzes were also very difficult. The final project is a beast, and nobody, including the TAs seems to know whats going on.

He seemed like a nice guy, but thats about the only good thing I have to say. So much of the class was busywork and I felt like I didnt learn a single thing. The lectures and quizzes didnt really like up, and the quizzes are a big part of your grade. Not the hardest class in the world, but definitely the biggest waste of time.

Get ready to grind on the weekly (open note) quizzes. He didn't give any tests this semester. The final project was a group project, which I didn't like, but it wasn't graded very harshly. Getting an A in this class isn't hard but will take some work.

Great guy and his honors class was fairly easy. The class has a big group project for the last half of the semester which became a little laborious. Many of his assignments are pretty ambiguous, but if you are good at reading between the lines and inferring things, then you'll do fine. He doesn't love taking questions or comments during lectures.

I took BIO 350 online from Dr. Gill during the pandemic. This class is a lot of work, but it is possible to get ahead if you stay on top of things (lectures, quizzes, readings). For us, the final was a group project that was 30 percent of our final grade. Be sure to find a good group so that the final project isn't stressful, and you will be fine.

Worst class I have ever taken, definitely do not recommend this course. There was so much homework, so many papers, and the instructions were not clear at all. Furthermore, there was little to none human interaction. All the work was done by the TAs. Simply awful.

I did not learn a single thing from this class. Definitely do not recommend. Lectures, textbook, and quizzes do not line up information-wise. Unnecessarily difficult class, took way too much time to complete assignments. Tons of readings. Several large assignments.

AVOID BIO 100 AT ALL COSTS. I'm sure Prof. Gill is great in normal settings, but the online format is terrible. I'm an engineering major with 17.0 credit hours, and I HAVE MORE HW IN THIS CLASS THAN ALL OTHERS COMBINED. It's not hard, but it's so repetitive. He never lectures but occasionally sends a "you can do it" video. You've been warned.

Absolutely worst class I have ever taken. This is a basic generals class and has 10x more homework than any of my other advanced classes. It is poorly formatted and I have't heard a word from the professor on any topic. He does not teach or lecture whatsoever, he just finds random assignments online and has you do them. about 15 hours a week worth.

I don't think I've ever hated a class as much as I've hated ecology from Dr. Gill. It sucks because I was excited for this class. He teaches you how to be an ecologist rather than about ecology in general. His lectures are all over the place and his quizzes are hard. There are no tests but the projects are not well explained. Do not take!!!

Some people when they heard that I was taking a class from my dad, thought it was going to easy for me, I had to put in a lot of work though. It's a long class, because first we have the lecture and then we have lab right afterwards . Honestly I didn't study for the tests as well as I should have, but he does have review sessions, so you'll be fine

I was honestly not the biggest fan of Dr. Gill. He was an amazing person and you could tell he cared a lot about Biology, but he was not very clear about what was expected for tests or assignments. It also didn't help he left for 3 weeks in the middle of the semester to do research and we took a test while he was gone

I loved his bio letters class! Really made such a great effort to keep the units interesting and understandable. The first half of the class was very hard but then it got loads easier. Super funny and caring guy. Very passionate I highly recommend taking a class from him.

The readings are long and the homework is very time consuming. Tests are highly based on understanding content inside and out. Anything taught in class or in the readings will be used on the tests. He does give extra credit that should be taken advantage of! Its a difficult class but it eases up towards the end of the semester.

Dr. Gill was the probably the best professor I've had so far. He really cares about his students. He wants you to understand the material but realizes not everyone is a biologist.. He has a good balance between science and religion and was very reasonable. Only complaint, there weren't clear criteria for grading but if you put work you'll do fine.
He's a good guy and a good teacher. It's nice because you can totally tell he is in love with Biology. I would take from him again!

I learned a lot from Prof Gill. He is a great guy who genuinely cares about his students and their understanding of Biology. There was quite a bit of reading, but as long as you do the reading you should get an A.

The worst and hardest class I've taken at BYU. There is no textbook so the curriculum is entirely up to Dr. Gill. The problem is he only glosses over important information in lectures but expects you to know specifics. Assignments are much more complicated than they need to be. You can literally study for days for a test and still not do well.

I really enjoyed the Biology-Letters class that Dr. Gill co-taught with Dr. Call through the Honors Program. Dr. Gill managed to make biology accessible and interesting, even to student who weren't particular interested in it. He made himself available after class and gave me great feedback when I asked for it. Really stellar guy and fun teacher.

I took the Biol-letters class from Dr. Gill. Probably a different experience than taking a straight biology class from him. But I really respect him as a professor and as a person. From my experience, if you take good notes during lecture, you'll be just fine. He really cares about the students and seriously loves biology.

Professor Gill is awesome, he understands that most of his students aren't interested in studying Biology. So he structures the class to give education that would be useful to non Biologists. He is always willing to talk to students and even encourages visits to his office with extra credit. Not textbook, but assigned readings are long, but cool.

Professor Gill is the best! He makes biology exciting and applicable to his students' lives! Do the homework and go to the reviews before the tests and it is easy to get an A. Overall, I would highly recommend this class, unless you are really into biology and you prefer to be taught with a textbook...

Professor Gill was one of my favorite teachers. I am not into science but he really helped me understand Biology and he made the classes very  interesting. We did many hands-on activities in class and the homework/tests weren't extremely hard. If you pay attention and understand what he is teaching, the homework and tests are fairly easy.

Professor Gill is a really great teacher. The class is fairly easy if you take notes and pay attention in class, which isn't hard cause his lectures are fun. The homework takes time, but is also fairly interesting. Loved the class!

He's a good person, but he wasn't really focused on the class. It seemed as though something was always on his mind. The lectures were confusing and very long. However, he did have some fun object lessons. I would recommend finding someone else.

UNIV 291 was one of my favorite classes last semester. Despite stringent exam and essay grading, I loved the lectures and class material. Dr. Gill was great at involving the class in what was being taught. When teaching about DNA, we extracted DNA from strawberries; when we learned about genetics, we did a simple experiment with m&m's. Loved it!

Professor Gill is a really fair and nice teacher.  His lectures are interesting, and if you pay attention, take good notes, and use the study guides, you'll be fine.  Homework aren't hard but can take a while, so don't put them off.  Also laptops and phones aren't allowed out in class, in case that's a deal breaker. Overall a great class.

The tests and homework were difficult, but he has review sessions weekly that are a TON of help. Go to those and you'll have no problem. Very nice guy, he rounded up my grade at the end of the semester because I'd put effort in and asked him for lots of help.

Prof. Gill is really a great teacher. This class was team taught with a history professor, and Dr. Gill made some great connections between the two disciplines. He definitely is not an easy teacher, but I liked the challenge. His lectures were peculiar and refreshing.

He team taught this class and honestly the other professor never really gave him the opportunity to teach. However, when he did teach, it was amazing. He was able to make great connections between topics and I learned a lot from him. He likes to sing hymns at the beginning of class which is fun. He's entertaining so his lectures go by quickly.

The class honestly isn't as hard as everyone is making it out to seem. If you pay attention in class and look at the study guide before the test, you'll do fine. His class is extremely organized and he lets you know exactly what you'll be learning and what you'll be tested on every lecture. He sparked my interest in biology and loved the class.

Professor was an amazing professor and sparked my interest in Biology. He expects very little, and if you go in to see him, even if it's just once right before a test, you're almost guaranteed a grade boost. He's very helpful and his lectures are great. There's only 6 homework assignments the whole year, so it's not a lot of time outside of class.

Definitely not your average biology class. The material covered is not what I expected. There isn't a book, so you just scribble down as much as you can in class. His lectures move fast and topics aren't thoroughly explained. Integrates religion into class. Review sessions are helpful for tests. Oh, and he hates phones.

Really funny guy, the homework projects are a little intense but lecture is usually very interesting. He takes a very good approach towards biology for those who aren't majoring in it. I'd love to take another class from him.

DON"T TAKE THIS CLASS! He doesn't teach biology! I have taken a real biology class at my last school and it was a 100,000,000x better then this. He doesn't have a book or anything to study so you better take good notes in class or else. I just hate that this is supposed to be a biology class and we don't learn any of the traditional biology..

The good thing is that he is super willing to help and is a very nice and funny guy.Professor Gill's classes don't have much structure. Moves at an extremely fast pace and makes it hard to follow along. Not great at explaining things.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. This class was interesting however, Professor Gill's lectures have absolutely no structure. There is no textbook and the tests are HARD- all written. He also gives ridiculous, long assignments that really didn't help me learn the concepts at all. There are much better bio teachers out there so keep looking.
Prof. Gill is a great math instructor. This was an online course but Gill made it painless. He is very understanding and helpful and there if you need him. I do recommend his class.

Professor Gill's classes were awesome and I looked forward to going to them every day! Every day we would learn a new concept and then move on to the next one. That was my only problem with this class. I felt like we had so many concepts to learn and so I wasn't really able to completely learn any of them. Plus the tests were SUPER hard!!

Professor Gill has good intentions but his class doesn't have any structure. He doesn't use a textbook so basically he can put whatever he wants on the tests. Don't expect the tests to be like the study guides either. He loves using ridiculous words that are synonyms for easy words like parsimonious. Probably the hardest Bio 100 teacher out there.

Professor Gill is funny and engaging, so going to class is very entertaining. A lot of the course is big-picture based, so there isn't a lot of specific biology you need to learn. The material is presented in an interesting way. He tells you what you ought to learn at the beginning of every class, so you know in advance what the test will contain.

If you have any interest in Biology, take this class! Dr. Gill is hilarious and teaches in a really engaging and interesting way. That being said, if you're just taking BIO 100 to check off a GE, there are easier teachers. Go to review sessions for the tests and you'll be fine. I have done really well in the class, and have loved it.

There was not any Biology used in his class. All we talk about is ethics and conceptualizing things. The tests are all written and opinionated. We have to write an 8 page research paper on the concepts of Biology. He has made me dislike Biology altogether. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Dr. Gill is incredible. I thought I hated science, but he made biology so interesting and accessible. He teaches with a great "big-picture" perspective. Don't worry about your grade--tests can be tough, but he offers plenty of help and some extra credit. His test reviews (the ones he personally conducts, not the TAs) are so helpful!

Great teacher! I would take him again if I could (and have it count for something). He makes lectures & class time meaningful and concise. He may share stories, but all are relevant to the lesson. I learned concepts that extend far beyond the classroom - if you're interested in that kind of thing. He is super helpful & always willing to help!

Gill is such a nice guy! His tests are extremely hard, but the curve that he gives is really good. Paying attention to EVERYTHING in lecture will be really important because he will test on these things.

Gill is AWESOME. I HIGHLY recommend him! I'm not a science person either...and his class was very thought provoking and relative. GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS. You will be well prepared if you do the study guides and go to the review sessions. You will have fun and learn interesting things about life. This guy is just great. DO IT.

I am not a science person, but Dr. Gill was one of my favorite professors at BYU! He uses lots of videos, hands-on experiments, and guest speakers in his lectures.  Dr. Gill loves biology and incorporates the spiritual aspect into almost every lesson.  He even personally teaches study sessions before exams.

It was enjoyable coming to class and I felt like I learned a lot, but I was frustrated with the course during it because of the research papers which were super time-consuming, the tests which were pretty hard, and the readings. I felt like I did not know what was to be expected. I ended up with an A- though so I was pleased with that.
Awesome teacher, he really made biology interesting.  You have to actually do the readings to do well, but they were all actually fun and applicable instead of just memorizing a bunch of junk.

This is the worst class. I found the class enjoyable, and actually like the topics we discussed. I actually talked about topics outside of class. Grading was awful spent 15+ ours on a paper and got a poor score and felt like it was one of the more well written papers at BYU. You must be a chosen one to do well. (get to know the teacher)

Gill was a good teacher but his tests were hard. Almost all the questions were short-answer. There is no textbook so everything on the tests is based on lectures and external readings. Ended up with a good grade in the class, but was frustrated with the class the whole way through.

He really helps you apply biology to life.  He cares a ton about your ability to use science.  The tests are hard, but manageable.  Spend a lot of time with his great T.A.'s.  This is a hard GE, but worth your time.

Dr. Gill is a great professor. He is funny and interesting to listen to. The homeworks and the research paper are not hard at all. Just make sure you go to the TAs or Dr. Gill for help. He has lots of office hours and is always willing to help. The tests are hard though. But as long as you go to the review sessions (all of them) you will do fine.

Dr. Gill is a great guy and is really willing to help. That being said, because there was no textbook it was really hard to follow his thought process sometimes. Way too much work for a 100 level class. I took this as a GE and to fill up space but ended up spending WAY too much time on all the busy work and the big research paper.

Class was very interesting - he uses videos, stories, real-life examples instead of a textbook lecture. Heavy use of I-Clicker for attendance. Gill and his TA's want to help whenever possible and hold infinite review sessions for everything. Great guy, really loved the class.

So I actually am not at BYU right now, but at SUU. I know Bro. Gill because he is in my home family ward. Over my spring break I had a bio assignment I was struggling with & he let me come to his home & he helped explain it better. It really helped & he did a good job of it! He's a very nice man & you can tell he loves what he teaches.

Don't take Bio 100 from Prof Gill, especially at 8 am. It's extremely hard to stay awake. He is very nice and enthusiastic about the subject, but he is not a very good teacher. The test questions don't really relate to what you learned about in lectures. Take Bio 100 from someone else unless you want to do a 30 hour, 5-6 page BIO project.

I had taken biology twice before this class and  could never get more than a B- needless to say I was frustrated that I had to take it again. This class was still hard, but Professor Gill is always so willing to help if you go into office hours! I ended up with an A- in the class and I LOVED the class! Take BIO 100 from Gill!

Prof. Gill is great!  He explains concepts well and really wants you to understand.  Not a really easy class, but if you do your work and study you can do pretty well.  His test curves are awesome and really help.  Would recommend!

So many emotions for this professor..I loved his lectures, he does hands on activities and ties things to the gospel. There is no textbook and his tests cover lots of random things. This makes studying hard and overwhelming. Go to the TAs for help before tests! I feel like I learned a lot and appreciate bio way more now. Overall a good experience.

I love Prof Gill!  Not an easy teacher by any means, but he has left an impact on my life that will not be forgotten.  His lectures are a blast while also being very interesting.  He cares about his students and has a passion for what he teaches.  His tests are hard and in his own words, "I love making hard tests!"  This is not an easy A class.

I wouldn't recommend him for Biology...his lectures are all over the place, and you don't have a textbook to study from. He's not ALL that bad, but I would definitely say to find a different professor.

This guy is hilarious!! He is always smiling whenever he lectures and is really into his subject and wants his students to feel the same way. It was a pretty fun class, they dont have a traditional textbook but just lecture about things they feel are interesting or are important to us today. Tests are a lot of writing but i did fine. Lots of fun!

Dr. Gill and Dr. Johnson are great teachers. I enjoyed the lectures; however, I left not fully understanding what was taught. They presume you have a pretty good knowledge of Biology beforehand. There tests aren't multiple choice and except to spend hour and a half to two on their tests. Definitely not the teachers for those who don't like BIO.

One of my favorite classes, but not the easy A if that's what you're lookin for. Dr. Gill and Dr. Johnson both give really hilariously informative lectures and it keeps the class engaged and wanting to learn. You will need to take good notes and show up to class to do well on tests, but the teacher reviews help a LOT. Take from Johnson & Gill!

Gill is AMAZING!!!!! He's so passionate and dorky that it keeps me interested. He is very helpful and so are the TA's. It is not a fact-regurgitating MC class. He helps you synthesize information and think more like a scientist. Take HIM! You have to study but its worth it. Doable A!!!

One of my favorite classes however if you are looking for an easy A this isn't the class to take. Dr. Gill delivers entertaining and interesting lectures and I felt he took a more general approach to biology. You will need to take good notes and show up to class if you want to do well on the exams.

He was the most inspiring teacher I ever had!!! He is very fair! It was abit challenging but I learned SOOO much ~ isn't that why we are in college? I am still talking about things I learned in the readings and lectures~! May not be for some ppl but if you apply yourself you will be glad you took this class! He will go out his way to help you!

Dr Gill's Class is a lot of fun, and a nice change from the other teachers at BYU. You have a Nature project experience that, according to him, should take you 40 hours. His tests were impossible, he prided himself on his open answer tests. Not one test has any multiple choice questions!! I recommend taking it from someone else.

I thought he was great, but he has a very different style. He has no text book, which means attendance is a must! His tests are also all free response questions, which are graded subjectively. However, you can make as many office appointments as you want. He will help you with anything. He made science very applicable and he was funny. I loved it.

Professor Gill is educated in his field however his class is awful. It is very unstructured and unpredictable.He doesn't care that most of his students do horribly on his exams--which are impossible by the way. There is no text book and the short stories we read instead are pointless. I do not recommend this class to anyone.
Great teacher and really interesting lectures but the free response tests and the TA grading are terrible. Overall great class and he gives opportunities to bump up your grade

He is a great teacher! He loves his subject and shows interest in his students. He makes everything so interesting! I don't usually enjoy science but I found myself not wanting to miss his classes. What he teaches is very applicable to us today. He doesn't have a textbook but he uses essay books that are so funny. I would recommend him to anyone!

Professor Gill is very animated and tells great stories about biology. However, he expects you to know a lot about biology already. The homework assignments are easy but the tests are terrible. They are all free response. I learned nothing about biology in this class, this class should be an optional biology class. There is no textbook

Take Richard Kimball if you don't care for American Heritage. HUGE curve. I think I ended the class with a 45% or something and I just assumed I failed.. I checked my map middle of spring semester, i got the credit and I actually ended with a D+. hallelujah amirite. I got like 35% on every test. Like take him if you truly don't want to take AHTG.
Professor Kimball was really entertaining and taught the course clearly. He was very merciful and gave a big curve on all the exams and final grade.

Kimball was a good lecturer and teacher overall. However, this class in general just sucks. It really all depends on your TA. Don't take other hard classes with this class, and if you can don't work too much if you want to get an A. If you turn in everything, regardless of grade you will pass the class. Also there is a huge curve at the end

Professor Kimball was a little vague & hard to understand in lecture but he knew what he was talking about. I liked the textbook and weekly TA lab. Tests were strange, I wish they would just set up the class curved. American Heritage is great!! I now understand America a lot better & I like how the history is set up to teach the concepts.

Everyone hates on American Heritage, but I actually thought it was a pretty easy and enjoyable class! I never did a single one of the readings, I either went to the review room or had AI summarize them. Kimball's lectures were generally pretty engaging.

NO MORE AHTG SLANDER. This class is SO GOOD. Dr. Kimball is fantastic in every way. Dry humor makes his lectures really super awesome. You interact with your TA way more than the professor. Grade is primarily exam based (but there are a few essays). Lots of readings but they aren't too bad (& they're super interesting). BIIIIIGGG fan of this class!

He explained things very well (and is engaging) and had lots of resources to help condense and cement the concepts into your brain. Going to the review room as often as you possibly can saves your grade! (15 minutes daily) You have to read between every class (sometimes 40 pages). If you work, you can do well!

The content of this class is FASCINATING. I learned so much & loved going to lectures! It was not an easy class though. Attendance isn't taken in class, but if you miss one lecture, it's really hard to catch back up. Spent a TON of time reading, going to TA reviews, and studying for exams. Passable, but NOT easy. (should be a 4 credit class imo)

This class isn't hard, a bit time consuming and the test questions are unreasonable. To second what another student said, it really feels like you are being tested on random facts rather than broad concepts. Like one question was literally identifying who said a specific, unimportant quote in one of the required movies. Essays are harshly graded.
Take American Heritage from Professor Kimball if you have the chance!! I had heard a lot of scary things about the course but Kimball makes it engaging and really manageable.

Kimball made the class entertaining. American Heritage is a hard class but if you go to the review room daily, you will be fine. All the homework is reading, and to do well in the class you have to understand all of it. Kimball gives the least about of reading to do though, so I highly suggest taking him as your professor.

Dr. Kimball has been a great professor. That being said, it I disliked that many test questions felt like I was being tested on fun facts rather than important material. Regardless, there are reasonable curves and this class isn't hard to pass, but it is harder to get an A.
Few better than Dr. Kimble. Thoughtful discussions in class and he is endlessly generous with his time and insights. A true mentor.

If you are taking the history capstone and are interested in sports, Professor Kimball is the guy to take it from. There is always a lot of participation in class and time to listen to not only each other, but advice other students have for you. He loves what he does and makes sure to always leave good feedback to help your success!

Dr Kimball is a nice guy. He's always willing to take questions on lecture and discuss test questions on his office hours. If you're an international student, register for the International only session. TA lab attendance is a must, the quizzes aren't enough to prepare you test. Ask ChatGPT to make practice tests with the content, trust me.

I was scared for this class but it was actually great. Loved what I learned. It requires a lot of work, but it never felt too overwhelming. Pay attention to lectures, both what he says and the slides. Pay attention to the readings. Take good notes. Go to review room!! I did all that and studied and ended with an A. Dr. Kimball is great and fun.

Explains concepts in a way that really makes sense. There's a LOT of reading, three papers (including a semester-long service project), two midterms, and a final. He wants you to succeed. My TA at least was great, and so were the TA labs, so I think he teaches them well. Study early and with a group. Participate in lectures - it makes his day.

Get prepared for lots of reading and taking dense notes during lectures. The TAs and review rooms are the saving grace of this class, if you want a good grade you HAVE to attend those to really understand the material. The exams are test heavy but with lots of studying and understanding what he's looking for they are doable. Def recommend Kimball!!

Professor Kimball was amazing! His lectures were engaging, and he obviously loves American History. I absolutely loved taking this class from him and felt so engaged and connected to the past. The essays were tough, but if you do the readings for them, you will be okay. Focus on understanding major concepts, and you'll be alright!

As a junior, I found Kimball's class to be manageable. If you want to do well in this class though, you really need to do the readings, go to lecture, and take good notes. (Expect about 2-3 hours of reading per week.) We had weekly quizzes on the readings in lab, two required films, and three papers. We also had to do 10 hours of community service.

Listen up everyone! If you're going to take A HTG, take it with this man! I'm an international student and had to learn 90% of this stuff for the first time, but Dr. Kimball made the lectures entertaining and fun and I enjoyed learning because of him. Sure, the readings are alot, but that's why you have review rooms to help you understand them

Professor Kimball made American Heritage bearable. He's super funny and I found it easy to pay attention to him. There is a lot of reading though… like a lot. But as long as you don't procrastinate you should do fine

I think anyone that has anything bad to say about Professor Kimball probably just has an animosity against American Heritage. Professor Kimball was super funny and made lectures super interesting and engaging. This class isn't super demanding assignment-wise, do the readings and go to lecture. The exams are the hard part, get ready to study hard.

A HTG gets a bad rap, but honestly it's overstated. It's not that bad with Dr. Kimball, you can definitely get by only by going to lecture and doing zero readings, it's just that the tests are a little hard and heavily weighted. Anyone claiming this class is right wing propaganda is just plain wrong, quite the opposite. A few essays, weekly quizzes

Dr. Kimball was hilarious and entertaining in a really dry way. There is a mountain of reading, which is really good to do but just attending lecture he basically tells you everything he wants you to know. Doing really well with taking notes in lecture will get you a decent enough grade. Really not too bad of a class.
Insanely test-heavy!!!!!
Exams worth more than 65% of your grade is diabolical. Been here five years, this is easily one of the worst three classes I've ever taken
Loved this class! He is extremely funny and really loves sport history. 10/10 would recommend. You read three books and the tests are reasonable.

I thought this class was super fun and that Prof Kimball was great. He's a pretty nice guy and once you understand his style of humor, you realize he is hilarious. As long as you do the readings and come to class, it isn't that difficult. He isn't a tough grader but there are multiple long readings in this class.

Professor Kimball's AHTG100 is challenging but rewarding. His engaging lectures, TA support, and unstuckstudy AI made the workload manageable. While the grading is strict, staying on top of readings and study sessions can lead to a great grade.

The class is too hard for a GE. While people have complained that AHTG is conservative propaganda, I felt like he was a fair professor who didn't attempt to make excuses for slavery like some might. But, the class is horrible. Hours of reading. The amount of times in test review when they said "this answer is correct but not what he's looking for"

ATHG is a lot of memorization and not necessarily in a fun way. I didn't do a single reading but attended every lecture and took good notes. Go to the TA reviews for the tests and do not procrastinate on studying or the essays and you will be fine. Would definitely take from Kimball though (but maybe not freshman year like I did)!

I absolutely LOVED this course with Professor Kimball! He is ridiculously entertaining but clearly knows his stuff. While there were a ton of readings, they are totally doable if you don't push them off. Go to the TA for extra review and you will be good. Take from Kimball!!

Dr. Kimball is one of my favorite professors overall and really makes the class worth taking. My roommates had Pope, and while they had only complaints for AHTG, I found myself sad when the class was ending. Just stay on top of the readings and go to a TA lab when you don't understand something, and enjoy the lectures, cause Kimball's hilarious.

Professor Kimball is the best. I've never liked history, but I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures. That being said, the class is hard! I went to every TA review, throughly did the readings, studied for hours, and was still not able to get an A. I wouldn't recommend taking this as a freshman, but when you do take it, take it from Kimball and work hard!

The class was not hard--the grading was hard. AH was one of my favorite classes I've taken, and Kimball was an entertaining and phenomenal teacher. Most people's grievances come with how hard things are graded, which is true. But if you really try on your essays and ask for feedback before turning in, go to test reviews, you can get an A.

I took American Heritage my freshman year (unfortunately), But I am so glad I took it from Kimball! All essays only need to be 500 words and his lectures were surprisingly entertaining. TA's can be really hit or miss so taking really good notes is very beneficial in the long run. Overall great class.

Professor Kimball is the one you want to take American Heritage from. I dreaded taking this class and took it my senior year and it wasn't bad at all. Kimball is engaging in his lectures and is a really kind guy. The only thing to note is that TAs make a big difference so hopefully you get a great one!

Kimball is the professor you want for American Heritage. Yes, American Heritage is hard, but only because of the tests. The curve will help. I got 78, 72, and 79 on the exams, and I ended with a B+. There are a lot of readings that are important for tests. Kimball is hilarious. Study groups will save you. Only 3 papers: less than 600 words.

If you take this class from Kimball, it will be one of the best classes you take at BYU. I never understood why AHTG gets such a bad wrap; his lectures were really entertaining and well explained, and I was always aware of the expectations. Sure, it's a lot of work and study, but I honestly enjoyed most of it.

Kimball was funny and lectures were entertaining. If you have to suffer through american heritage, definitely take it from Kimball. Overall the class was interesting and just lots of reading, but the tests were crazy hard. In labs TA's tend to say "this answer is right but there is a better one" so tests were hard to get good at.

Dr. Kimball's lectures are awesome. He's hilarious while also getting the concepts across. The class is curved between all the students in your TA's labs. There is a lot of reading in this class, but actually doing the readings and going to the TA reviews as much as possible will help so much.
Great lectures, always had a good time. Reading is so important and the tests are wordy and hard to understand. But, overall it was a good class.

Our TA told us in the first lab we would be "competing against each other." Took this class as a junior and it made me lose my 4.0 (I'm a pre-med/STEM major). Kimball was nice and his lectures were interesting but there were no study helps for exams and the amount of irrelevant readings was ridiculous. BYU needs to figure this whole AHTG thing out.

Kimball was fine, lectures were ok but the tests were ridiculous. I did really well on all of my quizzes and assignments... they were actually pretty easy but the grade is so heavily based on the impossible exams that it is hard to actually succeed.

best american herritage teacher. the readings are brutal and weekly quiz was impossible. tests werent too bad as long as you pay attention in class. be ready to take good notes in lecture and come every time. only two big papers that were short. he was so funny, lectures were almost always engaging even though its a boring subject.

This is probably one of the best professors I have ever had. Dr. Kimball manages to make his classes intriguing, informative, and make you want to learn more. Whether you're fond of history or not, you will find his lectures interesting. The class is difficult, yes, but the curve is super helpful. He's a great guy and I'm sad to leave his class.

Dr Kimball was a good professor for this subject, but American Heritage is notoriously hard and his tests and assignments are harder than they needed to be. He grades on a curve so there are only so many good grades he'll give out. If you want to do well with him, stay up on the reading and go to the Review Room as often as possible.

Such a good professor! Lectures are interesting, engaging, and fun. The midterms/final are hard, and even harder to prepare for, but take good notes and do the reading and you'll leave the class feeling fulfilled!

Dr. Kimball is awesome. His lectures are very engaging and really focus on valuable content, despite this class material being very broad. The TA reviews are VERY helpful, and studying lots for the test is necessary to succeed, but this class is certainly doable. It is graded on a curve, so only the top 10% or so in your lab get an A.

Professor Kimball is AMAZING! His lectures were entertaining and you can tell he is passionate about what he is teaching. The tests were really hard, but there are TA review rooms that can help. I didn't do a lot of the readings, but if you do the assigned readings you should be fine on the quizzes and tests. I loved this class!

Dr. Kimball made me look forward to every lecture. He made the material entertaining and engaging. American Heritage is not as hard as people say if you attend the T.A. reviews two or three times a week. When combined with a strong understanding of the reading, these can almost guarantee your success in the class.

American Heritage is a very difficult class, but compared to the other professors, you want Kimball! He was very entertaining and you can tell he is passionate about what he does. Missing lectures is hard but they aren't boring. The papers are graded by your TA and none of them were long. If you go to the review room you will do well on the tests.

Phenomenal professor and amazing course! American Heritage is rumored to be difficult, but I promise it is worth the time. I didn't find the content itself particularly difficult, just the work load for those who are unmotivated. Professor Kimball was hilarious in lecture while making sure we get down all of the most important concepts.

Take this class from Dr. Kimball!! I absolutely loved this class and Dr. Kimball's lectures are really good. Prepping for midterms and finals was a little hard but as long as you take advantage of the TA lab you'll do fine! Make sure you do the readings since there are weekly quizzes in lab and you are curved against those with the same TA as you.

I love Kimball with my whole heart!!! Nicest and funniest professor I've ever had, he is so sweet but this class is HARD. Lots of reading and very vague tests and little resources. Pope's class is 100% more difficult, without a doubt take it from Kimball!!!

As an international student, American Heritage is way too hard for a GE. And if I am being honest, neither of the lectures or the TAs were helpful at all. Also, the readings are SO long it usually takes me hours and hours trying to get through & understand it. There are two midterm exams and a final exam, and they are all too hard and unnecessary.

Kimball was pretty interesting but the class itself isn't too bad...every lab you take a 5 point quiz and there are 3 short papers. The tests are definitely difficult and there aren't a lot of resources- no study guides and TA's are usually unavailable or just don't explain concepts well. Overall participate and read the textbook and you'll pass
Run.

Honestly, I have been very afraid of this class and have put it off to my Junior year. It was not as bad as I expected it to be, however, if you do not have a significant amount of time allotted for studying, I would advise taking it a different semester. Tests are tricky and so are the quizzes taken in lab each week.
I mean... it's American Heritage. Terrible class. But Professor Kimball was funny and the lectures weren't complete torture. He was respectful and overall a good guy.

% of grade: Exams-65%, Essays-22%, Weekly Quizzes-13%. Requirements of the 3 essays, 500 words: 10hrs of service, read 12 different articles, read Frederick Douglass. 2 required Textbooks, lots of reading. No study guides for exams, basically expected to know everything. There are TAs & a Review Room to help, but I prefer not to be there 24/7

Love the lectures for this class. They are pretty entertaining and he's a funny guy. The readings can be a bit strenuous with two different textbooks but if you get behind on them it doesn't really matter as long as you do them before quizzes and tests. The tests are pretty difficult but the going to the TA lab definitely helps.

Professor Kimball does an excellent job of making class engaging and funny, especially knowing that no one really wants to take American Heritage.  There is a lot of reading - that won't change based on the professor, and he does put a lot of questions on the tests from the videos he shows.  If you go to TA Review room then you'll be set.

I had a great experience with AHTG, Professor Kimball was great! Hilarious lectures, 5-point quizzes every week in lab. The three essays and the tests comprised most of the grade. Study hard and set aside time for the readings, but if you take advantage of the TA lab throughout the semester as well as before the tests, you should be set.

Obviously AHTG is a hard course at BYU, but he assures you that you will leave with at least a C. The TA access is amazing and helped so much. I think he is the easiest AHTG professor you can get, basically memorize the lectures and go to the TA reviews and you are set. 11/10 would suggest.

Terrible class. Good Person. He is a nice funny guy but this class made me hate learning about American history. I love history and passed the AP US history test but couldn't figure out this class. I never missed a lecture did every bit of reading and studied alone and in study groups, but I never was able to get a test score over 70%.

I LOVED PROFESSOR KIMBALL. I always heard that American Heritage was a BEAST, but I loved it, and I think it was all thanks to Kimball. He was kind, funny, and always had captivating lectures. He is incredibly smart and is able to explain complicated concepts in an understandable way - and he's hilarious. I would take American Heritage again.

I really liked Kimball, his lectures were engaging and organized. He's kind of funny too. But, his tests were unreasonably hard. I thought I did great on everyone but failed everyone. The curve saved my grade. 
Tips: Go to review rooms, study A LOT, do the readings(and understand them) and pray for a good TA. AHTG is hard though so Good Luck!

Professor Kimball was amazing! This was my favorite lecture to attend. The weekly reading quizzes were the class's most difficult part, at least for me. A few of your quiz scores get dropped though. The papers are short but require reading. If you work hard, study, take notes, and use the TAs you'll be just fine! TAKE KIMBALL!

I went in expecting the class to be super hard, but it wasn't too bad. Make sure to keep up with assigned readings and pay attention to lectures. The only homework we had was the readings and a few papers that weren't super long. Only negative was that he would ask some questions on the test about specific details from videos we watched in class.

Dr. Kimball is a great teacher and good at explaining the concepts, although it is a tough class. Weekly quizzes on the readings (LOTS of readings), 3 short essays, and exams are very difficult. The material is interesting but I had to study a lot! TA's are very helpful, and I was grateful for the curve at the end of class.

Professor Kimball gave engaging lectures and I feel like the essays and readings were a reasonable amount of out-of-class work. If you're taking this class, definitely make time to go to the TA reviews, they hold multiple every day in the library.

Kimball was fun, but I felt that his exams were very subjective and unfair. Go to the review room to understand how they want you to think about the concepts. It isn't a very straightforward class. There were random grades assigned to the essays with little to no feedback.

Kimball had good lectures and was hilarious but this class is ridiculous for it to be a GE. The TAs even told us that only 20% of students end up with an A in the class. No matter how hard you study, you never know if you're prepared for the tests. TAs also make or break the class/review rooms, so if you get a bad one, good luck.

Great Professor!
Loved the class

Kimball was a great professor. His lectures were interesting and easy to follow. American Heritage has a bad reputation but with Kimball it was a lot better than I was expecting. He made a difficult class more enjoyable.

I really liked Professor Kimball. He was a great teacher and had very engaging lectures. I know a lot of people hated American Heritage but he made the class enjoyable. I would definitely recommend taking it from him. I also would recommend going to the American Heritage Review Room. It is super beneficial and helps to solidify your understanding.
I personally hated this class but Professor Kimball was very nice. He gave interesting lectures and was easy to follow. American Heritage is annoying no matter what, but that's not his fault.

All AHTG classes are structured similarly, but I don't think you'll find a better professor to take it from than Kimball. He's super funny, has engaging lectures, and has content that feels really important outside of the class.
I only bought the CH textbook and was able to find most of the other readings on course reserve/online for free.

Professor Kimball is the best lecture professor for american heritage. The class wasn't as much of a bear that I thought it would be. Just go to the review room everyday, rewrite your notes, read the articles and just be a good student that wants to learn. Your Ta will make or break the class if you don't go to the review room. It is so helpful!

Would highly recommend this class. AH isn't as hard as people work it up to be, Professor Kimball didn't have me stressing about too much.
