The class itself is pretty easy, you can get 100% on all lessons and class work, and you even get a full page of handwritten notes on all the tests. I would highly recommend taking this class from him!

This class is so entertaining, and Professor Sandberg is such a caring guy. He genuinely wants you to succeed, and is so willing to help you out in any way you may need. Overall, the course is tough when it comes to exams, but the class work and labs are an easy A. I highly recommend Professor Sandberg for your Physical Science credit.

I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! Honestly my favorite professor so far. The class is challenging but I feel like he is a good teacher. There is a decent amount of homework but go to class and pay attention and you can get a good grade. GO to the lab!!!

Very friendly, good at remembering names.  Classes were kind of repetitive or boring in terms of information learned, but he is also sometimes fun, hit or miss. Good at focusing on spiritual things too.

Brother Sandberg is a cool guy, but his class was unorganized and rushed. We always ran out of time so lectures often weren't completed. The TAs weren't a lot of help- my section TA had no idea what she was doing and the exam reviews were surface level. The exams didn't line up with what was emphasized in class. Weekly essays were easy enough.

Professor Sandberg was awesome! He doesn't get to control everything since most of the class is run by the PS department(not my fav) but he did the best he could to make our classes enjoyable and prepare us for the department wide tests. An A is 90% and a large portion of the class got an A for final grades. Super funny guy & internet famous haha!

I LOVE SANDBERG! If you have to take it from him. It seemed like those who didn't take him low key struggled and were bored. Sandberg goes over the material well and is funny. There is reading between most classes and there are class questions used for attendance. There are a decent amount of assignments and labs help. The grade scale is lowered

Brother Sandberg is amazing! He brings the gospel into every lecture, encourages participation in class, and has been super understanding with the switch to online classes. He drops your lowest hw and quiz grades and you can email him questions about the take-home tests. FYI the hw is annoying, so get a study group so you don't get bored with it!

He is one of the most genuine, caring, best guys I've ever met. There were around 200 people in our class, and I'm pretty sure he knew most of our names. Phy S 100 is pretty much standard across all the profs/sections, but Prof Sandberg made it better. There are iclicker quizzes every class that are participation. Tests are hard-ish, so study.

Physical Science has a department head and all the classes are the same. Bro. Sandberg throws candy, has jeopardy, and connects PS100 to the gospel. I had really fun in that class and hate science. The most important thing is getting a good TA. There are test review sessions and a lab where you can get help! Bro. Sandberg is a great choice.

His class was awesome. He's a lot of fun and makes class very lively. The only problem was that he didn't seem to know the concepts of everything he covered. Somethings he is an expert in, but other subjects it kind of felt like he was still learning too. He didn't explain things super well which made the class a little harder, but I liked it.

Dr. Sandberg was a nice guy but not the best professor. This was his first semester teaching, and it was somewhat apparent at times. It didn't help that all tests were department exams, meaning they were written independent of what he taught. His demos were sometimes cool, but he didn't manage time between them and slides very well. An A is doable.

Professor Sandberg was a great professor who really cared about his students. He was always willing to hold extra test reviews if he felt his students needed extra help. Also made sure to connect what we were learning in class to the real world which was really cool.

Really lecture and reading heavy. Lots of lenience with reading quizzes and attendance quizzes (10-13 of each are dropped) but not so much on HW. Do all the HW as its 35% of the grade and only 3 are dropped. your score on final replaces your score in class, but study for the midterm and read the articles (there is a essay about them on the test).

If you get the chance, take PS 100 from Dr Sandberg. He cares about his students and makes the subject fun. I was worried this class was going to be boring and irrelevant, but his 'Reasons You Should Care' slides at the beginning of each class were amazing. Dr Sandberg was by far the best PS100 teacher this semester.
Sandberg is the man.

I would not take PS100 from any other teacher! He is funny, caring, and very clear on what is expected in class. He goes the extra mile to be funny, relatable, and do visual demonstrations to help understanding. He helps you understand why it is important to know science in your every day life. He also brings candy for some of the demonstrations.

If you're taking Physical Sciences 100, take it from Sandberg! He is hilarious, cares for his students, and really brings life to the subject. I didn't care too much for science before this class, but Sandberg really helped me to love it! He does great demos and examples to help you understand the concepts. He knows his stuff!

Brother Sandberg does a great job of incorporating the gospel into class. He is very funny and generous (candy after tests). He doesn't write any of the tests, but the lectures plus the TA's and walk-in labs will save your grade, which you will have to work for!

Prof Sandberg is the best. All the physical science classes are the same in regards to tests (4 + final) , quizzes & homework. Sandberg does tons of demos that help you understand the material better. SO funny and keeps the class entertaining. We've had other professors step in and sub for him before when he's gone, and without fail I fall asleep
Just the worst class. Unclear project direction, everything is disorganized, and if you miss one small detail, you are severely punished.

This class was much better than 225, and I feel that Dr Vanfleet was very supportive and helpful, but it wasn't always clear what was going on and what we had to solve. There wasn't much structure to the class and I still don't know what my final grade is since there was not posted scale. Dr Vanfleet was helpful, but a bit more context would help.

This class was unnecessarily difficult. Even if you finish the labs early, they make you stay and do busy work until class time is over. Lab reports and tests were graded strictly. Grading was very behind, and very few people ended the class with an A. If you need to take this class, Dr. Vanfleet would be great, it's just the class is not good.
Great teacher. Really cares about teaching the material more than making life hard for the students. If you try to learn, you will do great.

Dr. Vanfleet was a great guy and was very helpful but I think physics is a difficult class to teach in general. Every problem is a different type of story problem so you may understand the concept but have a hard time applying it to different situations. Overall the class wasn't nearly as time consuming as they claim. 4-5 hrs a week max, not 20.

You're going to get a TA for this class. You'll never even see Dr. V once. So it's up to the TA on how well the class goes. It's a hard class no matter who you have as a TA though. Concepts and equations are difficult. They often expect alot from students in the given time frame. Fun, but I dreaded it every single week. 12 labs, 2 papers, 0 tests!

Engaging lecturer.  PS100 is a standardized course so the teacher you have doesn't matter all that much but I'm glad I had him because class was always interesting.  He's a good teacher and did remarkably well considering it was his first time teaching the course - he has a very good general science knowledge.  Recommended.

This was a really fun class for me and it was the first physics class that I had at BYU where I learned something new from high school.  Dr. Vanfleet was a very good teacher and having the homework due only once a week really helped me want to do it, compared to other physics classes.

Electromagnetism is probably the most difficult subject to teach,  so I don't think the difficulty of the class is a reflection of Vanfleet's teaching skills.  You just have to actually take the pre-class reading assignments seriously, because he can't possibly go over everything in class.  Be prepared to devote a lot of time to this class!
The concepts and math of this class are very difficult, as far as physics teachers go though, he is the best I have had.

Very time consuming class, but not as difficult as people say it is.  Don't get behind or you'll get trashed.  Dr. Vanfleet does a good job teaching a difficult subject, but the class progresses too quickly.

Dr. Vanfleet was a great teacher. He explained the material well and answered questions. The class is essentially a review of basic physics, so if you're like me and want to review basic math & calculus, it's not going to be a great help. However it does get you thinking and brings back a lot of stuff you learned before. Not a lot of work.

I would say that Dr. Vanfleet honestly does try to do a very good job.  Unfortunately, electromagnetism is a difficult subject to teach.  I don't think that this class would be easy with any teacher... but I do think that Dr. Vanfleet will help you with anything you need.  Lectures are pretty worthless though.

The amount of work required for this class exceeds the reasonable amount for 3 credits. Dr. Vanfleet's lectures are of very little help. I got an extremely good grade, but with absolutely no help from Dr. Vanfleet. 6 tests, 3 homeworks/week, 10+ quizzes, 3 reading quizzes/week. Dr. Vanfleet doesn't care that you have other classes.
Dr. Vanfleet isn't a bad teacher at all. But the Physics department really needs to drop its ego and make this class more doable. I only got a decent grade because Dr. Vanfleet has a generous curve.

Dr. Vanfleet is an exceptional teacher.  He is very friendly, and teaches physics very well.  I like the way his homework, tests, and quizzes are organized.  I've been here for three semesters, and he's the best teacher I've had.

Dr. Vanfleet spends a lot of time answering student's questions in class, which results in a somewhat scrambled lecture style, but he is on the ball and fair.  You can tell he is concerned about being a good teacher.  Tests are mostly multiple-choice, meaning no partial credit.  The overall grading curve is generous (90% A, 85%A-).
Really hard . . . Shis lectures seem not to apply to the Homework,and the book to neither. As a warning to all - DONT TAKE THE ONLINE SECTION!!!!

Really expects you to already know the stuff. Rough going for those who don't already know lots about electronics and magnetism. Lectures are worthless but you need the points for in-class quizzes and the clicker quizzes.

I found this class quite a bit harder than 121 or 123.  There is a lot to do, but that's nothing new in physics classes.  The tests are mostly multiple-choice and particularly difficult.  He has test reviews and post-test summaries.  I'd recommend him over anyone else who teaches 220.
Gives good examples and explanations of concepts.  Covers material at average rate.
was very difficult to understand....just like the book.
I've had better classes. Tons of work is expected and lectures arent terrific at clearing up confusion. He doesnt really clear things up, but rather speaks the exact same language as the book.

Dr. Vanfleet is a great teacher. He always explains himself sufficiently, and gives us real life applications for the concepts he teaches. Very friendly and sociable. Loves helping you to understand material if you ask him.
A good guy. I recommend him.
Class was challenging and very informative.  I really enjoyed his lectures and they really help you understand the material.  Homework takes a lot of time.

I like his way of bringing up examples of everyday things that relate to physics.  I've had physics before, so this course is to try to help me make sure I learn the stuff.  However, I tried to give an easiness rating that reflects other students.
Took him for univ and he was chill. Cares about the students a lot and is very nice. Classes got a little boring sometimes though.

This teacher is amazing, definitely in my top 5. He's hilarious and really cares about his students. He spent a lot of time to learn all of our names and a little about us, and talks to us before class. There is some hard stuff that's taught and it will take some extra work. Make sure to go to office hours or ta hours for help and you will be set.

Dr Warr is the most caring professor I have had. He challenged me in a way I have never been challenged at university. His humility and humanity is apparent in the way he teaches, and I respect him deeply. His class is not for the faint of heart. It is not an easy A, but you will learn more from the effort you put in than any other stat class.

This professor is incredibly patient and kind. However, the class average on exams is 70-76 percent for all exams. He curved the midterms but did not curve the final even though the average was a 76%. The TAs don't get to see the exam, so the reviews don't prep you. Extra credit is intricate and usually doesn't help. Lots of hw.

Great guy. Truly cares about his students. His teaching can be sometimes difficult to follow. The TA's are not allowed to know what is on the tests so they are little help in that direction.... Tests can be extremely difficult. Once again, great guy, extremely hard class (even for someone that is naturally good at math).

Dr Warr is one of the nicest people you can take a class from. However, the problem I saw was that He writes his own exams, putting the most obscure and difficult cases of content, even multiple times putting content that was never discussed in class. He purposely steers exam review away from those questions. He will not hand out any free A's.

Warr is an amazing professor. He is very caring and personable. He learns everyone's names by the first week of class. I thought his lectures were very helpful and related to the homework and tests well.

Professor Warr is very kind and accommodating, however I felt his class was particularly hard. I struggled with the concepts, but maybe this wouldn't be the case if stats/probability is intuitive to you. His homeworks and exams were long and rather difficult, and there were 3 hw's a week which was kind of a lot. I've heard Grimshaw is easier.

The lectures could be a bit confusing, but I really think it is just because of the course matter rather than him specifically. He took the time to learn every student's name and would ask a couple at the beginning of each class how they were doing which I really appreciated. The tests were extremely difficult.

Dr. Warr is good at explaining concepts. He or any of the TA's are a great resource! The tests are the hardest part because the study guides aren't one-to-one, there can be mistakes on the key, and the multiple choice questions are all or nothing. The format gets easier throughout the semester. Make sure to spread out homework over the week!
Great teacher with real world experience that helps you understand what the pros are going to want

Dr. Warr is a surprisingly personal professor. And by that I mean he takes it on himself to learn every students names outside of class and before class he tries to personally speak to a few students everyday. Insanely nice guy. Lectures can be a bit boring (he's sort of a plain, quiet type) but he will bend over backwards for you if you reach out

Professor Warr is happy and caring though hes timid and I wished he would have broken out of his shell to teach more energetically. His lectures relied heavily on PPT slides. I felt some classes I could have done the reading and skipped class. The material itself was fairly straightforward with a few challenging concepts. Not hard if you study!

Professor Warr is a great guy. Lectures can be slow at times, but doing the readings and coming to class will answer all questions that you have. He is always available to talk to you via email or in his office. I recommend taking any stats classes from Prof. Warr!

I really respect Dr. Warr. He's one of the most humble, caring professors I've had. His lectures may focus a bit too much on proofs, but then again, it's a stats theory class, so that's kinda what you signed up for. I felt the homework assignments were usually reasonably long and quite helpful.

Tough class, he expects a lot. Very difficult weekly homework assignments at inconvenient times relative to the lecture schedule. Doable class for sure, but very old fashioned lecture style that doesn't make a lot of sense usually. Focuses on proofs way more than he should and kinda ignores the purpose / meaning / use of concepts
One of my favorite professors in the stats program. The class is not easy. But he is great at explaining clearly and answering questions

Dr Warr is very kind, but do NOT take STAT 240 from him. Idk if it's cause it was online through zoom, but the way he taught that class was absolutely horrible. I was talking with a TA after, and they agreed that it was terrible. You won't follow half the things he's doing or talking about during class

I thought Dr. Warr was a very real person with weaknesses (sometimes has trouble solving problems on a whim). From my point of view, his weaknesses made him accessible and respected. Very kind. Will make sure everyone understands (sometimes to a fault). Curves all the tests. Easy A if you study a little bit.

Dr. Warr is a real professional. He always takes time to answer questions, lectures slowly enough that you can take notes and ask for help, and only has one homework assignment due per week (it's long but doable in a night if you have to). Straightforward teacher--no games, just great teaching. Best prof to take during COVID-19 for sure!

Dr. Warr is so kind and caring to all of his students!! He really wants to make sure everyone understands the concepts. The class isn't too hard and the tests are definitely representative of the homework/lectures. Not very much homework, but there are quizzes every day so attendance matters!

Dr. Warr is a one-of-a-kind teacher. He truly is the teacher of this generation. His understanding of the statistical realm is unparalled by anyone I have met. The way he explained ANOVA to the students in lectures is awe inspiring. He is quite honestly a statistical genius and the care he has for his students to succeed is genuine. I felt loved <3

So I love Dr. Warr. He is like a father to us. You need to show up to class in order to take the quizes that he has almost every class. No matter how many stupid questions you ask Dr. Warr will still answer them with patience and love.

Professor Warr did a great job of making sure questions were answered before moving forward in the lectures. I felt like I had all the resources to finish homework on time and the homework was representative of the tests.

For better or worse, Dr. Warr made sure everyone understood concepts before moving on in class. With practice, the tests were not too difficult, and they included open-book take-home portions. Dr. Warr is very good at explaining difficult concepts.

This class was pretty math heavy for a statistics class (integration by parts, proofs were detailed) but I learned a ton. You could tell the prof put a lot of work into the class and was very eager to help us learn. We had take home tests that accounted for 40% of the midterm/final and were open book/TA/internet. Would take again.
Great professor, very understanding and kind.

This class was chill. Attendance is not mandatory because he has recordings of all the lectures, which were lowkey better than being in class. Exams are all multiple choice and hard, but make sure to memorize the calculations and key points from the TA reviews, and you will do fine. Heads up, there is a LOT of homework due each week online.

Chemistry is not my thing, but Dr. Watt made the class enjoyable. He really cares about students and has a lot of extra credit opportunities available. There is a lot of homework, but it does a great job of preparing you for exams. His demonstrations are the best!

Professor Watt was a great fit for me. He is a nice guy, and cares about his students and what he teaches. Lectures were good, and the TA labs were good too. There is a ton of homework in this class, but for good reason... If you can do well on the homework, you will usually do well on the tests. He also gives a lot of extra credit to help you out.

Professor Watt is seriously the best option for taking chemistry! His teaching style is very user friendly. If the reading didn't make sense, his lectures always cleared up any confusion. He really wants you to succeed and gives so much extra credit. I learned a lot in his class, but I definitely had to put a lot of work in
Dr Watt gives lots of extra credit!

I love Dr. Watt. However, I strongly dislike chemistry. That being said, he is a great teacher, and if you set aside a lot of time, you will do well. He gives a lot of extra credit and is always willing to help you. I found the tests to be slightly difficult, but if you are going to take chemistry take it from him! He is funny, truly loves students

professor watt is an amazing professor. However some lectures were rather confusing for me. It is a harder concept so having difficult lectures comes with the process. Go to his office hours! he will 100% help you. He also gives an amazing amount of extra credit. Only thing I would say it some of the TAs were quite unhelpful and confusing.

Professor Watt is amazing! He loves chemistry and loves teaching it. He really cares for students and addressing questions and concerns. He understands that life happens so he gives a TON of extra credit! He gives practice problems in class and he also has all of his lectures PRERECORDED for students to access and review.

Dr. Watt is exceptional in his teaching. He has a deep understanding of the material and does a good job sharing it with the class. I honeslty hate chemistry, but I enjoyed his class. The material is comprehensive and the exams are demanding; however, there are many extra credit opportunities available to help compensate for any lower grades.

i LOVED Brother West as my teacher for Psychology of Design! He is very caring & makes a point to get to know you His lectures are interesting & he likes to have fun in class, but you need to do the readings before class if you want to understand everything. Group projects are actually good, & his testing is fair. No cumulative! Easy A if you try

I took this class through BYU online. Professor Richards is wonderful. Very clear, good feedback, available during office hours, and made the course interesting. It wasn't all just reading, but engaging videos for hard to understand concepts, interactive assignments, and short (non-graded) quizzes.

I had a great time in public. Dr. Wilson explains the concepts well and his tests are lengthly, but you'll be well prepared for them if you understand the homework and the practice tests. I took this class with a lot of friends which made it engaging and had a really good time with the policy project because we chose a policy that was interesting!

Dr Wilson is an amazing professor and this class provided me with a more well developed perspective on how economics can impact policy. The lectures are very laid back, but he always help to apply the principles into real world scenarios with lots of opportunities to participate in class.

Dr. Wilson's 398 course was put together well, and flowed very sequentially. He's an amazing teacher, and prepares you to do very well on his exams. Dedicate more time to your final project than you'd think, but he genuinely cares about what you care about and your success in this class and beyond. 10/10 amazing professor.

Really eye opening lectures but the second half loses momentum. The homework takes a lot of time, each assignment is like two in one. There is a textbook part and a STATA part. Be sure to make friends fast because the group project is a significant part of your grade and there are senior students who are only interested in the minimum effort.

Really great professor. Class is hard but if you put in the same effort for this class as you do for your other Econ classes, chances are you'll see it pay off more here. Lectures are straightforward and simple. Great at explaining things

Best Econ class I've taken at BYU - hands down. Econ 475 was the best class with the best Econ professor at BYU. Lectures are great, very engaging. The material is not too difficult. 6 problem sets and 1 midterm. Tests can be a little challenging, but not terrible. Group research project. 100% recommend taking this class. Very interesting material!

One of the most unstructured classes offered in the Econ program. We didn't have a TA, the actual person who was supposed to be our TA was a student that was also taking the class. The first test was not even close to homework problems. I would recommend visiting Dr. Wilson's office hours at least 5hrs per week just to get a sense of what he wants

Professor Wilson is amazing, he takes a tricky subject and really makes it doable. I don't know if I have met a professor that cares more about their students than him, he really wants this class to be the best experience for you and responds really well to feedback. Take 381 from Wilson!

Dr. Wilson was a great teacher and macro was one of my favorite classes I took at BYU. The material is really helpful for life skills. The most helpful thing for me was taking the practice tests - they are a very good example of what the tests will look like.

Professor Wilson is the best professor in the Econ department, hands down. He is great at explaining difficult concepts, really cares about the students, and his class was fun. The homework isn't too bad. The tests are pretty lengthy but Wilson prepares you well for them. One of the nicest men alive. Take this class from him.

Professor Wilson is awesome, I took 381 and 475 from him. He is a great lecturer, classes are always very interesting and knowledge is applicable to the real world. Typical amount of homework for a 300 level econ class, tests were hard, but you should expect that in this major. Favorite professor at BYU by far. Also, take 475 if you get the chance.

Riley's dope, he cares about your success and cares about you learning the material. His lectures were good, hw's were fair and the TA's were always there to help. Lots of test prep material, tests were fair. It wasn't a cake walk but if you show up and do the work you'll be fine! I'll take him again for econ 475.
Dr. Wilson's great, but this class is a bear. Hardest final I've ever taken in my life. If you take this, GO TO CLASS it makes it so much better and his lectures are great.

Dr. Wilson is great at teaching macro. Really cares about expanding your perspective on the economy, and understanding Econ basics. Most of your homework are group problem sets. Theyre a little tricky sometimes, but you can compare with other people in the class and usually get full points when you turn it in. Lots of questions are from textbooks.

Wilson is great. He really tries to make his classes manageable for his students and you can tell he wants us to succeed. During his classes he is always paying attention to the students to try and figure out if they are understanding what he is explaining-- and if we aren't, he will explain it again in a different or more simple way :)

I loved this class! Wilson does a great job of applying this to the real world, so everything you learn is put within a real-world context. Maybe it was because lots of stuff was going down Macroeconomics-wise Winter 2021, but this class was so interesting. Wilson is a great teacher, and the workload was not bad at all.

Great professor. Very willing to provide assistance to students who need it. The class is definitely hard. Reading helps a lot, and it will take effort to understand concepts. Tests were challenging. The applications were very relevant, and I felt it helped me understand and know where to go to educate myself. Would recommend.

Prof Wilson is a really refreshing professor. He's super organized and on top of the material--and there's a ton. The homework and papers were not too extensive as far as a typical econ class goes but the exams were pretty killer. They really test your fundamental understanding of the concepts. But he ends up curving the class pretty generously!

Professor Wilson is awesome. One of my favorite professors I've had. Genuinely cares about his students' progress, and tries to better his teaching to help people learn. Provides you with lots of material to do well on the test, and is a genuinely good person. Loved taking this class from him.

Good professor, he was engaging, even in an online class. There's not too much homework, but the tests were pretty difficult. The class was on a curve though so it was more about just doing well relative to the average. Overall it was one of the more interesting econ classes I've taken and I would recommend it.

Dr. Wilson is a young professor that tries really hard to improve, so he asks for lots of feedback and applies it in his teaching. You're graded on easy tests (2 midterms and 1 final (not cumulative)), 12 problem sets, participation, and reading House of Debt and writing about it. All of it is easy, its just about 1-2 hours a week outside of class.

This class was awesome, and Brother Eaton does an incredible job on his lectures. Unfortunately many students were completely tuned out on their phones/laptops :( He has no tests, just required reading assignments and essays, but they were very fair.

I have absolutely loved Brother Eaton's classes. This is the second class I've taken from him and he does an amazing job of making everyone feel cared for and bringing the Spirit. The first day of class he already had names memorized. He does a great job of clearly explaining his expectations. If he's teaching, take the class. You wont regret it!
A very easy and well organized class! Just do the readings before class, show up, and that's about it.

Eaton was by far the best religion Professor I've ever had. Lectures were engaging and I understood every single concept. Do yourself a favor, though. Show up to class. It will be very hard to pass his class if you don't.
It will seem like a lot at the start, but it really isn't. Take it from Brother Eaton. Trust me. Also great insights!
Class was really easy and he is super chill. Each week there are several very simple things to submit, so just don't forget to get the easy points. Attendance is essential to pass.

I liked Professor Eaton. He was a good professor for mission prep and did a lot to try and help us to become better missionaries. We did have prep assignments before each lecture. The final was also kind of annoying. However, altogether he's a good teacher and a good guy.

Brother Eaton is an excellent disciple of Jesus Christ! I loved the structure of the class and lectures! Essentially, the work is two 40-minute readings a week and a two-paragraph write-up every two weeks, so your learning is your responsibility, and I learned a boatload.

The class is self-guided, you get what you put in. 40 minute topic studies between classes, no tests, a moderate amount of essays. Attendance is a huge part of the grade as the class is discussion based. Even though sometimes I had trouble focusing during lecture, I would take his class again!

LOVED this class, he is such an awesome guy. There is lots of reading in the Gospel Library notebooks, but they can be used your whole life. I felt the spirit so strongly. There are essays every other week, but they aren't too hard. Take this class its so fun!! Also, he makes you make a group chat with everyone around you, so you aren't alone.

Professor Eaton's class is simple. You are assigned 40 minutes of reading before class but you self-grade every reading. There are no tests and homework is light (a few essays). I did feel like he was trying too hard to make us feel the Spirit instead of just letting us recieve personal revelation. Also great at answering questions.

This was one of my favorite religion classes. We had to sit by the same group of people all year and participate with them, but it was fun to get to know people. However, there is a policy if you miss over five classes you automatically fail.

If you like skipping class this is not the class for you. Attendance matters, if you skip more than 5 classes, you fail. Honestly the workload was pretty light, no tests, and 5 essays things and a final project. Glad that this class is wasn't as hard like other religion credits at BYU, but it was a times a bit boring.

Brother Eaton is great, he learns everyone's name before the first class and makes connection with everyone in the class. This class helped me feel prepared for my mission and strengthened my testimony.

I recommend Bro Eaton's Foundations class for your religion credit SO LONG as you take it with friends. That way, you can all share the attendance code with each other! And it's more fun with friends. But there's pre-class reading (40min), a few short reflections/essays, and weekly goals. If you burn out, this class is easy to "keep working" in...
He explains material clearly and gives organized lectures. He is good at answering questions and making sure students understand. The class is frontloaded with most of the work early in the semester.
I've taken Brother Eaton's classes twice and loved them. He's funny, good at teaching, and passionate in his subject.

He's awesome! Super kind and caring. Amazing insight and I loved the ideas talked about in class, that he had us study, how he had us read and journal, and the assignments were very good to grow your testimony and learn how to help others.

Brother Eaton knows what BYU students need out of a religion course. The course isn't very hard but with the type of person he is, you're motivated and actually want to do class preparation and learn. He also has a huge emphasis on addressing hard questions which is super pertinent to today.
Great class. Take from him.

Professor Eaton is a really good person. He cares a lot about his students and even memorized our names. He is a little traditional and strict when it comes to some of his opinions on what missionary service should be, but I think it's important to be exposed to different perspectives. He is pretty funny too. I'm glad I took his class.

Quite possibly the easiest class I have ever taken. VERY hands on class, which was good considering it was a mission prep class. One of those classes where you get out of it what you put into it. He does a good job answering the hard questions and not glazing over the hard parts of a mission.

He thinks he is in a movie. Puts on background music when he bears his testimony. If you want a no test project based class, then this is the one for you. Just get ready for the lawyers version of the gospel.
Brother Eaton has great stories and experiences with the brethren. His class was more of a Sunday School vibe. Take the class if you want the easy A religion, not if you want to dive deep into D&C

Brother Eaton was really good at teaching study skills, but his lectures could be a bit long and boring. Also, the TAs were strict on grading, where they would mark students down for small errors or leave vague feedback.

I took REL 250 with Brother Eaton and loved it. He teaches amazing study skills and I feel like I learned a ton. He has essays every other week, but they aren't that bad, and I learned a ton by doing them. He also encourages people to ask questions. Overall, he's an amazing teacher and I highly recommend any class he teaches.

Professor Eaton is kind, and if you are prepared to come to class and do the short written assignment weekly, you will get an A.I didn't love the lack of historical focus. He is not a historian. Not my style of religion class and I was bored the whole semester. Nothing against him, just make sure you pick what you want out of this type of class.

He is the best. No midterm or final. The class ends in a capstone paper that is 4 pages long. The spiritual content of the class is also great, very uplifting. Would 100% taking this class from Brother Eaton. He was a Mission President in the Federal Way, Washington mission.

You do have to attend lectures for attendance. He will fail you if you skip. There are papers due every other week that you have to submit a draft for. There is no final, it's only a four page paper. Brother Eaton is respectful and is always willing to answer questions, especially if they are tough ones.

One of the best teachers I have ever had. I felt the Spirit often and took many good notes. No exams, only biweekly essays that are simple and teach you a lot as you write them. Engaging lectures and I have found myself using the skills he provided us for the Gospels in day-to-day scripture studies. Can't wait to see him in the Celestial kingdom.

Very easy class. Wasnt the most engaging lecturer, he focused a lot on discussion and didnt go crazy with like actually teaching his own insights or his own stories, but when he did they were good. No test, only essays that are pretty easy and straight forward

Im writing this as I am taking the time to prepare for finals and also write a stupid five page essay for this class. Super frustrating. The class homework itself isn't hard it's just busy work. You have something to do literally every single day of the week. It's mad annoying. having to be forced to use study skills that you don't like is crazy.

Brother Eaton was great! I learned a new fantastic way of studying and am able to retain all of those insights and learnings through the use of notebooks in gospel library. There was a short essay every other week which wasn't bad at all as well as about 40 minutes of guided study per class. I was hesitant at first, but it turned out for the best!

Brother Eaton was a good teacher, and classes were insightful. Attendance is mandatory, but no exams; just several letters to a friend discussing tough points of doctrine. Before each class, you have to study for 40 minutes, but he tells you what to read and gives you options. Good class!

This was a good easy religion class! Class time is mostly comments from other students which was good at times but I found it hard to pay attention most class periods. I wanted more from Brother Eaton and to learn more about the restoration itself. But overall it is a great class!
If you want an easy Foundations of the Restoration this is the class to take! There are no tests and hardly any homework

For reasons unknown to me, I don't really like Prof Eaton. He's a nice guy and has some great stuff to say. What you get out of this class is ultimately up to you. You can do the bare minimum and sleep in class, or listen and dig deep. Pre-reading every class. Weekly quiz. 1-2 page essay every other week. No exams, just a longer final essay.

Classes are mandatory (with an attendance code provided... so unless you have a friend in the class it would suck to miss any lectures) and they honestly aren't very engaging. I usually just did homework during the class. There are no exams which is super nice and a lot of the quizzes are auto-graded on completion. The papers aren't difficult.

I love Professor Eaton! He has such a strong testimony and so much knowledge about church doctrine and history! SUPER easy class, no tests at all. There's a considerable amount of homework, but it's really easy. Most of his lectures were really interesting, but every once in a while they would drag on. Awesome class, I would take it again!

All three of the stars I'm giving Eaton come because his class contains zero stress. However, his lectures felt three times longer than they actually were because he bounces around topics like an energetic frog jumping from lily pad to lily pad. Also, 75% of the lecture is him letting the same 4 students raise their hand and make a comment.

This class is quite easy. You read scripture before class and work on a goal each week. You have am paper every other week, always the same prompt. No tests. Attendance is mandatory for your grade. Hes a great guy says some really inspirational stuff. He teaches doctrine so well and in an interesting and funny way.

I would highly recommend Brother Eaton! There is a lot of work for the class, but it is all meaningful. He had so many interesting insights and utilized class participation and groups in a way that was not painful by any means. Brother Eaton really cares about getting to know his students and is very approachable. Great professor!
Rob Eaton was one of the best religion teachers I have ever had. He is a stud and will 100% be exalted.

Overall, it was a pretty good class, and Brother Eaton is very knowledgeable. I appreciated hearing his insights, but it wasn't necessarily my favorite religion class. As far as assignments go, there are pre-readings before every class and short essays every other week. It's almost impossible to get 100% on the essays, but I always got good grades.

I am a big fan of Brother Eaton!! He really helped students grow and his emphasis was on helping students utilize all resources possible in their lifelong discipleship. Funny and engaging, will take from him again.

Brother Eaton uses Canvas and has literally 0 tests in his class. The only big projects are the small essays every couple weeks and the 5-page essay at the very end. So basically you just chill during the lectures and you learn from other people's insights from the readings. I love how Brother Eaton gives us so many ways to study the scriptures!

Idk. The readings don't feel like they pertain to the class sometimes and you don't really go over them. He is obsessed with ChatGPT for some reason haha. But he's so caring and found time to have 1 on 1 convos with students. I just didn't love his course layout. No tests, but that meant attending class felt pointless at times. Not my fav REL class

This class is titled "Christ and His Everlasting Gospel", but this was definitely more about how to study the scriptures, we did not study the Savior as much as I wanted to. Super easy, just not the class I was expecting.
Great teacher!
He was one of the best religion professors Ive ever had. The way he answered questions and encourages us to look for ourselves was inspiring. He is a Legend of a man

This is the best class I've taken at BYU. Bro Eaton is amazing. All of his lectures begin with answering questions. None of the assignments are busy work and all of them help you grow a stronger testimony of Jesus Christ and his restored church. Bro Eaton's lectures are always engaging. He goes from talking in a funny accent to powerful testimony.

This class substitutes tests for essays and busywork. Be warned however that the essays are due biweekly and during the height of midterms, it feels like you have one every week. He was also incredibly unclear about the conventions of these essays and wanted them in a particular format. The TA are known to be harsh graders and unhelpful.

One of the greatest religion professors here at BYU! I will be walking away from this class with a stronger testimony, not just with facts memorized for a test. No tests in this class, just papers, but the papers are easy and worth your time. I wish more religion professors thought like Brother Eaton!

This class was really hard for me to focus in. Lectures were often scattered with Professor Eaton fiddling with ChatGPT, pulling up random YouTube videos and sharing irrelevant stories. Lectures always went over time, and he said some questionable things regarding people who had left the church. You also have to do so many useless essays.

Very caring and truly wants to help you strengthen your testimony of the Gospel and of Jesus Christ! Spiritual class and a great way to better understand the "gospels" in the Bible! Teaches you lots of study skills that make scripture study more meaningful! Work: 40 minutes of class prep per day, 1 pg paper every 2 weeks, weekly spiritual goals :)

He was an amazing teacher! You just have to prepare for 40 min before class starts and the whole class is just him trying to answer and discuss our questions! If you prepare beforehand it is a breeze! No tests but a final paper at the end.

The value you get from this class completely depends on how much effort you put in. You grade yourself on most of the assignments, and the essays were pretty easy. Attendance was mandatory until the last week of the semester when he removed attendance from the final grade. So don't bank on that carrying your grade.

Excellent professor. Really helped make it a class focused on spiritual experiences. Class was used for discussion and answering questions. Great gospel discussions. One essay every two weeks and a final paper, but no tests the whole semester. He was clear about the grading policy and wants his students to succeed and grow their testimony.

Super easy class, just make sure to do the readings. Prof. Eaton is very kind and knowledgeable, and he encourages questions about difficult gospel topics and does his best to answer them while making it clear what is doctrine vs his opinions/thoughts. I didn't expect to appreciate this class as much as I did!

Brother Eaton is an awesome teacher. I took him for the Restoration class. He doesn't have huge tests, but most of your grade will come from studying in-between classes, coming to class, and writing (easy) papers about different gospel topics. Most of the class was him answering people's gospel and church history questions.

Bro. Eaton really cares about his students and what he's teaching. He focuses on helping students develop skills in his class that they can use in the future. He didn't make the class too hard and there are no tests, just short papers were you explain our beliefs and why they matter in letter format. Solid choice for 225, I enjoyed his class.

Brother Eaton rocks! He is so kind and has a real passion for what he is teaching! There's a paper & goal setting activity every other week, reading for class prep, and the final was a 4-page paper. Attendance matters, but class is nice so that's no worries. You totally feel the spirit in his class, and there are no exams, highly recommend!
I loved Dr. Eaton. He is very caring and truly wants his students to succeed. The class is super easy, but you also learn a lot. Light grader too.

Foundations of the Restoration was good with him. Pretty simple, honor code based assignments. I low-key felt like he was constantly trying to prepare me for a bash, but other than that the class was good. No tests just a simple 4 page paper at the end of the semester.

This was foundations of the restoration. Super easy. No midterm or final. 2 weekly assignments to read for 40 minutes. Gives you great resources! 1 weekly assignment that takes 10 minutes. Really helps you learn and grow. You can only miss his class twice so plan on attending. If you have a good excuse i hear its easy to make up.

For foundations of the restoration it's a lot of gospel discussion. You need to attend lecture but homework outside of class is not super hard or tedious. I absolutely loved having him and would gladly take him again.

If you're looking for a seminary class, this is it. But if you're interested in rigorous historical inquiry, look elsewhere. Brother Eaton stated explicitly that he doesn't follow the BYU learning objectives, he has his own idea for what the class should be. Namely, practicing developing shallow arguments based on cursory examination of the issues.

Professor Eaton is an incredible person and professor. He always made sure we felt engaged in his stories and his thoughts, and he was very intelligent. He had a lot of interesting things to say. In seminary, it was hard to learn things I didn't already know about religion, but not in Eaton's class. He taught me so much!

This is the best religion class I have ever taken! His classes are so engaging and he is a really good guy. The classes don't feel like lectures but discussions, and he is willing to answer all of your questions. No tests either, so I feel like I can just go learn and feel the spirit.
Such a good guy. You can really tell he practices what he preaches. Make sure to show up as attendance is graded. No tests, just studying assignments. The epidemy of what a religion class should be.

I was scared to take this class because of the heavy topics addressed, but brother Eaton is the absolute best. He genuinely cares about our relationship with Jesus Christ and our testimonies. He gives you truthful and straight-forward answers but that are also faith-promoting. He really is a great teacher in the savior's way and discussion leader.

He was the best professor I could've asked for when it came to taking a mission prep class. He takes the time to get to know his students. Bro. Eaton is a very spiritual person and does a wonderful job preparing young students for their missions.

Rob Eaton has been influential in my personal preparation for my mission. He very clearly cares about his students and wants to help us reach our potential. He has so much kindness and respect for his students and is amazing at answering difficult questions. The overall class is very easy, but you get out of it what you put into it. 100% recommend!

Professor Eaton was a very knowledgeable and great teacher! I would take his class again for sure; the workload is light with no tests and it is a stress-free discussion-based class. Could you try to come to class with a question for him to answer? He was very nice and I was glad I found his class. Testimony grew so much!

Such a great professor. His classes and lectures are inspiring, and focus on learning about Jesus Christ, rather than classwork. Super kind and caring, and will help you in anything you need help with. No tests, just one page essays, and prep work. Take Foundations of the Restoration from Brother Eaton!

Brother Eaton is wonderful. His Mission Prep class helped me decide to serve a mission, and he celebrated when I got my call. He takes the time to truly get to know each of his students and makes sure you know you are important. His testimony is tangible and inspirational and I would LOVE to take another class from him in the future.

I would 100% recommend Professor Eaton to everyone. He is such an awesome guy who genuinely cares for his students. He even knows all of his students by name. His objective is for his students to learn and spiritually grow. This way of teaching creates a relatively low-stressed class.

He is a quality religion professor. I took him for Rel C 225. He teaches the doctrine really clear and straightforward. You make a study journal/study for 40 minutes twice a week from a list of scriptures. There's 1 four-page paper at the end and 2 paragraph assignments every week. No final. He covers hot topics throughout the restoration very well
One of the easiest classes that I have taken. Everything is very straight forward and not very hard. He makes class super fun and makes you want to come each time.

He is very passionate about any topic. He has obviously done his research and knows what he is talking about. He isn't demeaning though, actually quite the opposite. His desire is really for his students to learn and to grow. The love he shows in every class is quite impressive and is evident in his teaching style. You'll love to participate.

Professor Eaton's class will help you strengthen your testimony. He is very cautious of teaching the doctrine and principles taught from the prophets. His classes are faith promoting and focused on us an young adults. He relates what we are learning in class to our lives. Seriously one of my favorite professors! You won't regret taking his class.

Having served two missions and been a mission president, Brother Eaton certainly knows what he's talking about. His lectures are engaging and he incorporates some role-plays into class time; however, this is definitely one of the classes that you will get more out of if you put more in.

Professor Eaton's Missionary Preparation class was truly exceptional. His genuine concern for his students' success was evident in every lecture. The course provided invaluable insights and skills, creating a supportive environment for personal growth. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a meaningful and well-guided preparation for their mission.
This class is very focused on self-driven study and increasing discipleship. You will get out what you put in. That being said, the bare minimum is not difficult.

Rob is a great professor. I had zero experience coding or anything programming-related, so the class was really difficult for me, but I always felt like I could ask Rob for help. Ask for help from Rob and classmates, and you'll me okay.

Rob Reynolds is probably the best professor I've ever had. He cares so much about his students and is willing to spend time really answering questions and focusing on what the students are interested in. He's not going to just hand you all the answers, but I think that's a good thing. His classes are really the whole group learning together.

Professor Reynolds is a nice dude, and a solid teacher, but wasn't super approachable as an online teacher which made it hard to get help on assignments. If you're already familiar with programming you'll do fine, but for a class meant for beginners, there was a lot of basic information he never covered.

The other ratings are true! In the last 3 weeks of class, he introduced a new coding system that none of us (TA's included) have ever used that was extremely complicated + finicky. Acted annoyed when anyone needed help. Then he up and left us during the last 2 weeks of class + finals week to go to Japan on sabbatical. TA's were clueless, good luck

Professor Chaney is a very nice guy but this class is a waste of time. Unfortunately it's needed for PH major. There is no organization in the lessons and he just teaches whatever he feels like at the time. The class is all group projects and tests. The coding you have to do also makes no sense because neither the TA's or Chaney know how to do it.

I have a hard time knowing how to write this review, but overall I struggled with this class. Dr. Chaney is such a kind guy and I don't have problems with him as a person at all. I just was constantly confused in his class and always felt unsure. It's all group work except a couple assignments and the tests. Also, TAs never responded to my emails.

Within the first week of class I was already so confused. He skipped over topics he said he would cover, didn't address assignments found online, and didn't give any information about the textbook. He was never clear on whether or not to take notes, and just overall so confusing. He was never clear about anything.

Robbie is such a caring professor! I would recommend meeting with him one-on-one to prepare for the exams, and go over the study guide. The group projects can be annoying depending on the group you're assigned. You do have the option to switch groups after the first project, and you do leave a peer review which he takes into account when grading.

I went into this class really nervous because of some of these reviews! Turns out, Dr. Chaney is a great teacher who really cares about his students. I had a totally fine experience with the group project, and he was great about responding to our emails. He also goes around the class multiple times and provides direct feedback on your project.
Amazing professor. Super kind and willing to support students. Encourages students to learn on their own through group research project.

Dr. Chaney isn't your classic professor. He doesn't have PowerPoint lectures and he doesn't have any lecture content posted on LS. However, I enjoyed his style because it taught me to think outside of the box and to actually listen to what he is saying instead of scribbling down a bunch of notes from Powerpoint. He cares a lot about his students!

Work in groups (not chosen), so good luck if you get a group who doesn't put in effort. We wrote an entire research paper on data we collected ourselves with few and very vague instructions - almost as if he wanted us to figure it out ourselves. TAs even didn't know what was going on sometimes. Nice guy but poorly structured class.

His lectures are so vague!!! You better have enough drive to teach yourself cuz he does nothing. Frustrating really. He expects everyone to be on the same page as him without teaching anything. Required public health class and he's the only teacher so good luck

Robbie is a super nice guy! His class can be a bit confusing at times as there is no traditional lecturing or stuff like that. Most of class was spent working with our groups on a 7-week project. Overall, a great teacher and class.
Group projects are big for this class! But Professor Chaney is more than willing to help out. Super helpful professor!

You definitely need to take a class with him or you're missing out. He's super chill and loves what he's teaching. This course is public health, so naturally it has group work, but it's manageable. This class is spiritually uplifting and helps build good skills.

Dr. Chaney is an amazing teacher. His class was all group projects, no tests, and class discussion based. I've learned more in his class than all my other major classes, because he helps us learn through hands on experience instead of making you memorize stuff to just regurgitate on a test. Take any class from him you can.

Kanye West could have taught more intellectual lectures. Do not try emailing him because you will never hear back from him. Also, trying to ask him questions was painful. You will most likely not get a direct answer. Makes you hate group work more than anyone thought possible. The spiritual 5 minutes at the beginning of each class was good though.

Biggest waste of time of any class I've taken at BYU. He teaches you nothing and just reads from his slides (which are posted online). At the end of the semester I had a question about grading and he ignored my email. You read a talk everyday and try to relate it to public health. One of the group projects is to write an essay together (dumb)

I loved Robbie, but didn't love the class. He doesn't teach much and anything scholarly you learn will be done on your own. That being said, I liked all the projects. The individuals are much more valuable to me than the group projects but really, if You don't work well in groups, maybe this isn't the profession for you. Easy class. Just prepare!

Robbie is one of my least favorite professors at BYU. You might think you know what is going on with the class, but he is a hard grader. He will give you all positive feedback on an assignment, and then you will still get a B. I wish he would explain what he is taking points off for. The semester-long group project is busy work and a pain.

Robbie is my favorite professor here at BYU. He really cares about public health and wants to make a difference in the world. He is motivating in helping you find out what changes you want to make  and how to make them happen. I took Health 330 and Health 432 from him. Highly recommend him! Also, he is willing to help with anything outside of class

Robbie is the man. His class is awesome. The worst thing is that he is really confusing on what he wants you to do but is super helpful when you ask him and will email you back within 24hrs. Also, your group evaluates you and it affects your grade so hopefully you make friends because if not your grade will reflect it.

Class is based on group collaboration- you'll work with an assigned group the entire semester.   If groups aren't your jam, take it from somebody else.  NO EXAMS. No textbook.  Five individual and group quizzes (not hard), five individual projects, and five group projects.  GPs are "real life" type projects, IPs are written assignments.

He tries too hard to seem cool, and it comes across as fake. I would have preferred a class that spent more time studying the scriptures and less time on articles or readings that seemed intended to show how smart the professor is. Overall, this was not one of my favorite religion classes at BYU.

Amazing professor, very knowledgable about the academic material surrouding his class subject. I disliked professors in the past because it seemed like they taught from their opinions. Professor Taggart was the opposite he shared personal insights mixed with selections from "the best books." Also his slides are just amazing, absolutely beautiful.

Professor Taggart was the best introduction to BYU I could have had. Through his amazing lectures, he is able to invite the Spirit and help students learn so much more about Christ and the scriptures. I highly recommend!

He is a spiritual person for sure which shines in the online classes he had to do in the semester. In class lectures I had a hard time because he felt like he was trying pretty hard to be “cool.” He talks about being in a punk rock band as to why he acts how he acts. It just felt performative and took away from the spirit for me. Avoid his class.

AMAZING TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!! Super funny guy! He made every class exciting and treated all his students with so much love. If you have questions, GREAT, he will help you with them. Also he used to be in a punk rock band so that's pretty cool! All the assignments were pretty easy and fun. TONS of extra credit opportunities too!!!

Lectures were AMAZING! If you are looking for answers and to strengthen your testimony, take this class! There are 2 tests (so easy) and a creative project that you work on the whole semester, which can literally be whatever you want. Brother Taggart is so spiritual, funny, will sing out of nowhere, and has the best lore. SUCH A COOL GUY!

I seriously loved this class. I felt the spirit so strongly in every lecture! Brother Taggart is so in touch with his students and talks about the realities of life, which I loved. He helped me to understand scripture better and connect it to myself. If you can, take this class from him!

There could've not been a more spunky individual I have ever met. Yes, a TON of reading and yes- BIG projects throughout the semester (There's 2). But man is he silly and makes classes engaging. Super fun teacher and will make even the most boring of topics interesting to listen too. Loved the amount of insights I gained and felt it was worth.

Brother Taggart is amazing! He's hilarious and so passionate about the gospel. He gets so excited which is funny but also inspiring. I didn't get a great grade because I skipped a few too many classes and procrastinated assignments but if you just stay on top of things it's probably not that hard.

HE LOVES HIS STUDENTS.  He is a professor who cares about what he teaches. The class if you don't understand the book of mormon really helps you get a better grasp on the importance of it on us. Many times throughout the semester he would make us all laugh as he jumps on the table and at the end of class cries over God and His love for us.

Professor Taggart is amazing! The lectures are spirit-filled and so good and tests just take from the lecture questions that he has us fill in during lecture. Only one essay that is graded easily and a semester-long project that is fun to do. There is a bit of reading but not too bad and helps you grasp the content. Overall, perfect religion class
This class was an absolute 10/10. Would definetly reccomend!
Can we clone him please? He's so amazing and LOVES his students. He also loves the Gospel of Jesus Christ.

TAKE PROFESSOR TAGGART! His lectures are incredible, and he cares so much about his students. His projects and essays (very few, dw) are genuinely helpful and interesting. He radiates the love of Christ. He provides so many extra credit opportunities that even if you missed a test it would be difficult to do poorly in this class.

It felt like Professor Taggart had a checklist of 50 things to talk about each lecture and he would talk at 1000 mph until he checked them all of the list. I wished many times he would just slow down.

Super easy class though. If you want an easy A just go to lecture and fill out lecture guides. Lecture guides themselves are essentially the final

This was my 2nd class with Bro. Taggart and it was super good! I got a lot out of his class despite it not being super time consuming. Take him if you want an easy but super uplifting and spiritual religion class!
Professor Taggart is a great professor and is extremely enthusiastic. His tests are easy, and he grades lightly on everything.

Such an amazing professor! There are many aspects of the church that are challenging for me, and he does a great job acknowledging the nuance in the church. I felt the spirit super strong in class. The class itself really isn't too challenging. There are two tests but he has lecture guides that corollate pretty closely.

Love this class! 3rd class taken from him! Easy and most inspirational religion classes! His classes are what every religion class should look like. There are lecture guides (similar to questions on the exams) that you fill out each class.

Take Bro. Taggarts class! He invited the spirit so much, I have never learned so much in a religion class. I looooved his class-however, there was a lot of reading, every class had a preparation report assignment, and there was a semester long project as well. So it is a lot of work, but definitely worth it and not very hard at all!!

I loved Brother Taggart's class. He's just an awesome human being who loves all of his students. He's super funny and the class was always laughing at his jokes. Seriously take any class from him, you won't regret it. Super funny and spiritual lectures!

Professor Taggart was easily my favorite instructor this semester! His lectures are always inspirational and will have you leaving his classroom feeling inspired. I wish he could teach every single one of my classes. He is so funny. engaging, and cares so much about what he teaches. He is the man.

TAKE RELIGION FROM HIM! He is an awesome teacher, and for someone who struggles with some things in the church, I have never felt the spirit more strongly than in his class. I learned so much and was inspired every day we had class.

Bro. Taggart is a great professor! His course was super easy, and he gives lots of extra credit opportunities. As a calm person, sometimes his larger-than-life personality was a little too much for me, but I know that other people enjoy that, and it did make the class more interesting. Overall, great professor and class! I recommend!

Brother Taggart is absolutely amazing and one of the greatest lecturers I have seen, I cannot recommend him enough. His testimony and stories are incredible and inspiring. I didn't know I would be able to feel the spirit in a class literally every time but he was able to make it happen. The most caring, loving, and hilarious guy you'll meet.

Brother Taggart is AMAZING!!! I had him for Christ and His Everlasting Gospel, and it is the most beautiful class I have ever taken. You can get so much out of this class if you put in the effort. Not too difficult, and every single lecture was absolutely phenomenal. You will grow your testimony so much and feel inspired literally every day!

Brother Taggart was probably my favorite religion professor I've ever had at BYU. He is so loving and knowledgeable. Going to his class every day was such a privilege as he helped me make new connections to the scripture. He was very clear on his grading which I appreciated, he had over 700 students so sometimes waiting for grades is slow.

Brother Taggart has a heart of gold and explains the gospel absolutely beautifully. Not many assignments at all, just one project and one paper that you have all semester to work on. He is willing to meet outside class and talk you through anything you need, and in many of his lectures he followed the spirit and answered a prayer of mine.
He is amazing. He helps you understand the scriptures like no one else can. As long as you show up you can get a good grade in his class.

Professor Taggart is incredible!!! His lectures are SO entertaining, so heartfelt, and so inspirational. Take his BOM class. There is lots of reading (so worth it) but tests are easy if you follow lecture guides. He is so much fun and will help you find Jesus, truth, and love. My mind was blown everyday too, he is so knowledgeable of literature.

Brother Taggart is absolutely amazing. Not only is he a great religion professor, but he is also extremely caring, compassionate, and forgiving. When I admitted to dishonesty, he was willing to work with me to help me move on in peace and spiritual growth. I was really struggling in that time of my life and his support is what got me through it.

Like most religion professors, he's out of touch. It's an easy A, but the tests are annoying. He'd mention one thing on a random Tuesday morning one time, then test you on it. He also tests you on stories about his personal life, which I always thought was strange. There are lots of extra credit opportunities, so nobody should get below an A.

Absolutely incredible. Exactly what a religion class should be like, except maybe even a little too many extra credit opportunities. There were readings for each class and a short weekly assignment, one short, easy paper, and then the term project you are supposed to spend an hour on each week. He is super powerful, knowledgeable, and loving.

Bro. Taggart is the best! His lectures always flew by and made the Book of Mormon interesting! Although this class doesn't require much work outside of class (1 hr for a project a week and reading before class), I got a lot out of it This class was exactly what a religion class should be: no stress and uplifting.

Such a passionate teacher. Knows his stuff. Outside reading. Easy midterm and final. He provides lecture guides to help you study. Final project you work on throughout the semester, don't procrastinate on it. Go to the lectures they're awesome.

His lectures were always spiritual while also fun and engaging! The lecture guides outlined the key takeaways from every class and they were all you needed to study for the tests. Organized class with lots of busy work, but it's easy to do well and have a great experience. You do have an end-of-class project and a mid-semester essay.

Brother Taggart is amazing! His lectures are simultaneously hilarious, engaging, interesting, and so so spiritual. His class felt like it took 20 minutes. I never got bored, and I always had great takeaways. You need to understand the scriptures for the tests, but if you study for a little while, you'll get an A no problem.

Bro Taggart is so amazing and I 100% recommend taking the teachings and doctrines of the BOM from him! I learned so much about the BOM from this class. Attendance and readings are required to get a good grade but it's easy. There are also a lot of extra credit opp that can boost your grade a ton! This guy is genuine, humble, and a spiritual giant!

Brother Taggart is amazing.  He has a great understanding of the scriptures which leads to amazing lectures.  He deeply cares about all his students and is there for you for any problem.  His papers are very easy to as well as the tests.  This class really helped me better understand the Book of Mormon and prepare for my mission.  he is amazing

He is one of the most caring professors I have ever met; he truly loves all his students, and his lectures are life-changing and spiritually uplifting. He makes class something you look forward to every week.

One of the main reasons I attend Institute is to feel spiritually strengthened and to deepen my testimony. However, with Brother Taggart's teaching style or approach, I did not feel spiritually nourished or edified. The environment didn't foster meaningful gospel learning or spiritual growth for me.

If you want to genuinely grow closer to Christ through some fun and engaging assignments, Bro Taggart is your guy!
He has some of the best lectures I have ever been part of, and he always teaches you something new about the scriptures, be it big or small.
Brother Taggart cares!!! And he is so interesting to listen to so I never even think about falling asleep during class.

I didn't love Taggart as a teacher. His tests were difficult, and really the only thing that affected my grade. In my opinion, religion classes should be a place where you can truly feel the sprit, instead of being overly stressed about tests, and sadly that was not the case for this class. I felt more stressed with this class than my O-Chem class.

Brother Taggart was an absolutely amazing teacher. Every time I went to class, it felt like a fire hose of information. I loved learning so many things and thinking through concepts I had never really examined before. He is absolutely hilarious, but he is completely serious about how much he cares about you and the gospel. Ask the hard questions!

I loved having this BOM class from Brother Taggart! He makes the lectures so much fun and I can tell that he pours his whole soul out to his students. He wants us to learn so much from the scriptures and he creates a lot of opportunities to do so. Attendance is important and you have to write notes in BOM. Tests are open BOM!
Brother Taggart is a really great religion professor. He cares about his students, the course is a pretty standard BYU religion course.

Brother Taggart was so fun! He is a very high-energy & fun prof, & while that might not be for you, the lectures were always super insightful! I felt like there were times where we were rushed for time, cramming lectures into the last few minutes, but I still learned a lot! Weekly readings & assignments, 1 paper, 1 midterm, 1 project, and 1 final!

This is for REL A 121. Bro Taggart is fantastic! His lectures are insightful, well-planned, and very interactive, with beautiful visuals, and an emphasis on people who aren't featured as much in the scriptures. We had 1 paper and a final project, both of which were easily manageable. Hands-down the best religion class I have ever taken.

If you're reading this and considering which professor you might take REL 275 from, you will not regret having Brother Taggart as your professor! He is amazingly energetic, full of life, and a very kind and compassionate soul! 11/10 recommendation!

Brother Taggart is a great teacher. Each lecture was inspiring, and I always left with new insights. The workload is super light; the main priority is weekly assignments based on scripture reading. I would totally recommend taking any class from Brother Taggart.
The most chill religion professor ever. He is awesome, super funny, and would totally recommend him to anyone.

Professor Taggart is by far my favorite professor EVER! You can really feel how much he cares for each and every one of us, and he is so passionate about the scriptures! He jumps up on tables and yells and its so entertaining hahah. Could not recommend this class more!

This is my favorite professor I've had EVER! He would jump on tables, chairs, and shout throughout his lectures in funny, captivating, and entertaining ways. He is also a really great test writer, he is willing to adapt some difficult questions, and gives good study materials.

I took Brother Taggart's 121 and 122 classes, and he is the best. His assignments are focused on spiritual development and not just on learning obscure Book of Mormon facts. The paper and project you do during the semester are also focused on personal development and being creative. His lectures are fun and anything but boring.

Bro. Taggart is AMAZING! As someone that struggles with a lot of metal health, he has always been extremely understanding of my late work. There are 2 essays you have to write, but they aren't hard at all. He's a hilarious story teller with an insane amount of passion for what he does, and his mind dives deep into the meaning behind the BoM. 10/10!

I LOVE BRO TAGGART!! He is so awesome and gives the best lessons. Every time I go to his class, I leave feeling empowered and loved! He loves when you ask hard questions and will help you through anything! 100% recommend taking a class from him!

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! His class was nothing short of life-changing for me. His main focus is for you to have a greater understanding of the nature of God. He isn't afraid to dive into controversial/scary questions and encourages us to do the same. I always left his lectures feeling the spirit and feeling an increased sense of God's love for me.

An exuberant, passionate, kind, and thoughtful teacher and an incredible lecturer. I would sit and listen to him expound theology for fun. He brings a level of love and zeal to every class period, while also making the course work relatable, grounded, and useful.

If you get the chance, take his class. You will not regret it.

LOVED this guy. He is the reason I am serving a mission. I never really got into the Book of Mormon before coming to college, so the midterm and final were a tad difficult for me. But I still got an A. Easy class and great guy, he is passionate, and he truly cares about his students.

Prof Taggart makes this class understandable and easy to follow. If you want to do well in this class, he makes it clear what you need to do. If you show up and complete the assignments you will be just fine. He provides a lot of insight into the BOM and really cares about his students. If you need another religion class, this is the one to take!

While I didn't particularly enjoy Brother Taggart's lecture style, I still learned a lot from him. He cares a lot about his students and is a really easy grader on the few assignments we had. Tests were online and pretty easy too. If you want an easy religion class, Taggart is a great bet!

Professor Taggart is the best! He is hilarious. His lectures are always filled with spirit. I am always learning something new from the scriptures when I go to class. Professor Taggart makes sure the class is focused on the scriptures and not the grad. Homework is super easy and test are open scripture. Take religion from him!!

Professor Taggart is amazing! His lectures are engaging and inspiring. He has taught me a lot I didn't know before. Assignments are very easy, just readings and sending out a weekly spiritual thought. Tests are more difficult, but they're open scripture and all the answers are in the scriptures/in your notes so if you pay attention they're fine.

I am not a member and took his BoM class and had a blast! Just a testament to how awesome he is. No mandatory attendance, with grades relying heavily upon a self report/reflection made every week. If you have the opportunity to take his class, DO IT!!!

I LOVE Prof Taggart! He was so funny and had so many life stories that tied back into the lesson. They truly showed his process in the Gospel and how passionate he is about the scriptures.
