Just have to read the scripture chapters before class and find something you loved about them and write in a discussion board. Love his class!

THIS MAN IS AMAZING! I genuinely think he takes top spot at BYU for THE greatest professor! He just radiates light and love for His students! His teaching style is phenomenal,he is interactive with the class, and teaches hard Book of Mormon concepts and principles exceptionally! I have never been so excited and inspired to read the Book of Mormon!

Robbie Taggart is the greatest teacher I've ever had.  I've been the kind of person who in their religion classes has just done homework for other classes but the first day in professor taggart's class I put away my homework and never touched it again.  He is so engaging and funny in his lectures and knows the Book of Mormon like no other.

Guys, if you're reading this then take a class with Robbie Taggart! like I literally left class every day ready for the rest of my life. He's inspiring and full of life, he makes you laugh every day but brings the spirit so much. I think I wrote one actual paper and just read the book of mormon every day to be ready like truly I love this professor

Brother Taggart was a phenomenal teacher. I don't think that there are many people out there more caring and understanding as he is. Our lectures were always filled with awesome discussions and questions. I would take this class over and over again if I could! I hope he teaches other religion classes in the future.
He facilitate great discussions.

One of the best classes I've ever had at BYU. He focused on the U.S. Constitution and balancing managerial, legal, & political values. Class discussions were awesome & assignments were relevant. Wish I could take another class from him!

Nahh y'all are just soft. Take the class seriously and if you have questions or an issue, talk to him. He doesn't baby the general credits which is why I think he gets heat but he's hilarious and wicked smart.

He's a pretty tough grader, but he'll tell you why and how to improve. Great at scheduling office hours. He knows his stuff like nothing else and can be sarcastic. Listens to criticism and is great about answering questions. He does expect you to do work (you're at uni, what did you expect) and he will reciprocate the work that you put in.
Colson is awesome. He teaches theory super clearly and gives everyone a chance to share their thoughts. 10/10 guy.

I don't think that he deserves all of the bad comments. The class is a lot of work, but he's not. There's a lot of reading which is the hardest part. Very discussion heavy. 3 papers and 2 tests, so not too hard. It's not a fun subject, but he tries to make it interesting. Accessible to students and understanding when you ask for an extension.
Hilarious and very passionate about what he teaches. Reading assignments are big.
Tough graders who expect more than is listed on rubrics and assignments. Very time consuming class. Expect to teach yourself mostly everything using the textbook and videos they have you watch.

Professor Colson's class was awesome. The discussions were engaging and fun. There was a lot of reading, but I was rarely bored by anything we had to read. The readings and lectures provided beneficial insight into African culture that I would not have otherwise been exposed to. Overall, the class and Professor Colson were great.

90% of your grade is papers. He does not grade the papers until the very end of the semester. He does not include feedback on most papers, and the ones that he does, are not enough to give you ideas for improvement. He is nice but an extremely hard grader. I worked really hard for an okay grade.

I see a lot of bad ratings, and maybe his other classes are set up differently, but Prof. Colson was super nice and understanding. The source material/reading was relevant and interesting. There aren't a ton of assignments, but he was a fair grader so it wasn't a problem. This is a discussion heavy class. Take him for IHUM 311.

I took IHUM311 from Dr. Colson (btw, I'm a math major so I had no idea what I was doing) and he was AWESOME! He structured the whole class to the students and he encouraged interesting discussions in class. He also chose very relevant and interesting texts for us to read. Fair grader, and not a ton of writing or reading. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

I wouldn't recommend this class. The amount of reading that he expects is way unreasonable. I didn't enjoy the lectures and in my opinion, he couldn't care less about his students. Definitely more work than it is worth.

I absolutely loved having Dr. Colson for Humanities of Africa. It was a really small class and I was able to participate a lot. The lectures were a little dry, but that was mostly because of the other students rather than Dr. Colson. I now consider him a good friend and am incredibly greatful for what I've learned.

Although Professor Colson is a nice person, I would not recommend this class. I finished my final a week ago, and 50% of the assignments for the semester have not been graded yet. He rarely gives an A on an assignment (most assignments are papers). He also assigns 80-100 pages of reading/week and his class lectures are identical to the reading.

Prof. Colson is an OK choice for 350. You can tell he's SUPER smart, but sometimes his explanations of theory aren't very clear. I was sometimes left MORE confused after his class. He's a bit curt and sarcastic, but he's open to questions and does a pretty good job of valuing in-class comments. Lots of reading. 3 short papers, 1 long. Fair grader.

I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Colson's class. He was respectful of each student's opinion. He asked thought provoking questions, sometimes with no answer, and he treated us with respect as we had class discussions and tried to wrap our minds around the subject material. He was intelligent, and I found him to be very approachable about grades.

Overall, I enjoyed Dr. Colson's class. I thought his lectures were interesting and that he has a good sense of humor. However, there is an overwhelmingly amount of reading for this class. I had no clue on how to effectively study for his tests. It was stressful. Luckily, the TAs were nice when grading the short and long answers.

Dr. Colson is unbelievably knowledgeable about these topics and brings his knowledge to class in a very entertaining and interesting way. I came into the class with very little art analysis experience and left feeling very confident in my ability to write about the humanities. I took this as a general and would highly recommend it.
The material in the class was fine and fun, but Dr. Colson is just kind of rude.
Loved his class. He made every lecture and reading interesting. The class required lots of reading and writing but every assignment was interesting and insightful.

If you love humanities, he's a good professor. If you're taking this class for a GE, don't, you will forever regret it. An hour or more of reading per class, heavy on papers and other writing assignments, and difficult tests. He also struggles with accepting opinions and ideas of students, making class discussions somewhat difficult.

The homework in this class is not difficult, but it can be time consuming. There is a big difference. The readings were not valuable to my education and made me feel as if he was using them to compensate for his lack of knowledge about the material. He is very condescending. Those who love his classes are not serious students but mindless lemmings.

I get the impression he gives random grades. He isn't clear. Worst is his attitude. He treats students poorly. He doesn't seem very bright and tries to cover it up with hostility, passive or direct. Take a different class. I don't think he was ever good at anything so he just ended up here.

First of all Dr. Colson is incredibly rude and condescending. Second of all, the problem is not that his class is difficult because it is not. The problem is that he is incredibly vague about the grading criteria and offers no explanation as to what separates good work from bad. Classes from him are insulting and a waste of time.

Prof Colson knows his stuff. You can tell that he truly enjoys and is knowledgeable about his field.  This was the most demanding class of my semester. Lots of reading and overall comprehension. Two papers on two literary works, two art analyses, three tests, two cultural events, etc. He does a great job considering how much material there is.

I found the course load to not be overbearing: 8 reading responses, 2 Cultural Events, 3 Exams, 2 Papers & chapter quizzes. Professor Colson on the other hand is awful. When asking for help, he directs you elsewhere. Assignment descriptions are scarce and vague. He interacts with students disrespectfully. He and his TA are rarely on the same page.
Seems to lack focus and not put much genuine thought into the subject when teaching. Maybe he wasn't meant to teach or has personal issues affecting him.

Colson is one of my favorite professors at BYU. As a Humanities major, I LOVED taking 202 from Colson. He teaches the material with enthusiasm, and is easy to get along with. If you are not a Humanities major, I can see this class being a bit excessive for just GE credit, because of the readings, but I loved this class.

Professor Colson definitely knows his stuff but he puts way too much information for a GE in this class. He's terrible...plain and simple. We talked about a urinal for 20 minutes one time in class.....that's just sad. Save yourself from tests where you are memorizing 50+ paintings, authors, and time frame....Beware of Colson....Beware!

There is so much work for a GE! Don't take it from Colson! SAVE YOURSELF unless you like reading 30-40 pgs of textbook a night and 2 full length novels with 3-4 pg. papers for each. He likes the material but doesn't do much to make it interesting. He likes to hear himself talk. Grading is harsh and not on a curve...you've been warned.

There was a lot of busy work for this class.  several papers, which where graded like it was an upper level english course.  Dr. Colson knows his stuff, but this is a tough class with way too much work.

Save yourself from this class. The guy is nice and helpful, but the amount of work for a GE is insane. Take the 202 class from Perry, or anyone really, and you will be pleased. I took the gamble in taking it from him without a rating on this site, and it was a huge mistake. Three 4 pg papers, 2 cultural event reports, 3 long mid-terms, 3 hr. final.

It often felt like I was not being taught what I needed to know. I basically taught myself everything. The tests were difficult (not impossible), but I would have gotten a 0% if I had not studied on my own. There is reading that never really gets explained. I often felt like Dr Davis did not really feel for the students. Not impossible. Doable.

I really dislike the class itself, because literally all learning happens outside of class. The things you learn from the readings are completely unrelated to what you do in class. The instructions for the in-class labs are often vague and unhelpful, and to his credit Dr. Davis did try to help everyone.

My second class from this professor and I only came back because I had to. I do not feel like he does an adequate job of explaining the what he expects from you when taking 225 or explaining concepts. The worst part of this class was when a question he explicitly told us would not appear on the test, appeared on the test.

Brother and Sister Davis have a very weird style of teaching. It was really frustrating at first to understand the class structure, but after a week or two the class was pretty easy. The lectures don't prepare you super well for tests.

The only reason why I am taking Physics 220 from Robert Davis and his wife is because they are the only people teaching it. I only ever write poor reviews if I personally believe a professor is a poor teacher as well as a difficult person to get along with. Unfortunately Mr. Davis and his wife exemplify both of these attributes.

I hated 121 with him. Barely got an A. But for some reason 220 wasn't so bad. The class structure was almost completely different. It was still hard, and I still feel like he didn't really prepare us for the tests. Maybe it just took a while to get used to his style. I'd avoid him but the class is doable. A good attitude makes all the difference!

Br. Davis cares. A problem with this class is it seems that he expects you to be able to derive equations from concepts, which is hard. Lectures covered elementary problems, and the gap between them and the homeworks was a joke. It did get better by the end, but honestly you need to go to lectures comfortable with the textbook material. to succeed.

Physics is hard, flat out. But I feel like lectures never helped me on the homework. Most learning was through figuring it out on my own with other's help, which is what they want, but it took so much time that it never felt worth it to me sadly. Tests are exhausting, and be ready to figure out how to study for them. Not the worst, but not the best

Pros: always starts class with a prayer. Tries to help you understand in office hours. Cons: teaches vague principles but rarely anything specific to help with homework/tests. Lots of poorly-worded questions. Makes you teach yourself the homework but doesn't give you the answer key so you have no way to check your work and verify correct learning.

One of the worst organized and structured classes I have ever taken at any institution. Terrible lecture structure and even worse TA section structure. Made it very difficult to understand the material.

It was fine. I felt like lecture sometimes wasn't super helpful because it was general or not with the homework. There is homework every day but it is never excessive. I probably should have done the readings and that would have helped... Group work heavy but in a good way, I promise. If you're good at physics this class will be a breeze. Not bad.

Was scared to take this class because of reviews & had never taken physics before, but I really enjoyed it. Class set up really helps you learn thoroughly. Tests are hard so give yourself plenty of time to prepare. Lectures aren't very helpful, but buy into their teaching style 100% and spend time on the homework and you'll do well. LOVED lab.

This was a fairly difficult class, with a lot of homework, but I didn't really feel that there was more than was necessary. Brother Davis was always willing to meet with students in office hours to help you understand the material better.

Came into Physics 225 expecting to hate it. Throughout the semester, however, with the long hours spent on discovery/learning projects and in-class activities, I came to love it. He gives you many extra credit options and emphasizes your own discovery and learning. Hardest class ive ever taken, but I learned so much. Amazing class and professor!

PHSCS225 is an experimental class and does a lot of projects in which you start with reading materials. Some of the reading materials are not directly physics-related such as a book with the title 'lift'. Lift, in short, is about a book about how to make your working space more others-focused. Dr. Davis does not live up to that and is a hypocrite.
Awesome professor. You learn so many applicable things in this class and it's super interesting! He cares a lot about his students and wants you to learn and succeed.

Rob is so smart and so chill. He's able to explain complex concepts simply, making it easy to understand. There are reading assignments posted for every class but they are usually case studies related to what we're learning about which makes it super interesting. He's a great teacher!

Rob is a great guy! Not a fan of how he structured the class. He is very unclear about what his expectations are. Grade is mostly dependent on a couple of tests. He also has you write a paper for which there is no rubric. Doesn't respond to emails, but does get back to texts.

I took 501 with Rob and he is the best. His tests are based on understanding core concepts, not memorizing stupid facts. He is clear what will be tested, and if you ask what the free response questions will be based on, he will tell you what exactly you need to know. Class was awesome if you prepared for it, and he is up to date on research.

Dr. Hyldahls class is enjoyable and was one of the most interesting classes ive taken at BYU, but he lacks clear grading criteria. sometimes, what he expects is not clear so it was always hard to anticipate whether assignments were done correctly or not.  If you miss a lecture, you may miss very important info, so going to class is crucial.

Dr. Hyldahl is quite literally the best professor I have ever had. I have attended three universities and he is the best! He cares more that you understand the concepts than your ability to regurgitate answers on to a test. If you don't take EXSC 320 from Hyldahl you are making a mistake.

This was an overall fantastic class. If you go to Dr. Hyldahl's office hours he is very helpful. He did well at making this class applicable to not just athletic training majors but everybody. Awesome teacher, awesome class

I tried hard in his class but didn't do well. His class is extremely boring too. You show up, maybe do an i-clicker quiz (not too difficult), then he just reads his powerpoint slides that you can access online, EVERY SINGLE DAY. The tests are alright but you don't know what will be on them, and there's a paper you have to do, which sucks.

Dr. Hyldahl is an amazing teacher. Instead of speaking at us, he teaches us. You can tell he is passionate about the subject and knows his stuff. You'll have around 8 quizzes but he usually warns you before. Study for hard for them. Go to the test reviews and memorize the review slides for tests. I wish he taught more classes!!
Highly recommended as a cycling instructor. Ride the bike, listen to Red Hot Chili Peppers,  pass the class.
I loved this class! I highly recommend it!

Fantastic teacher. He is easy to talk to and very clear on his expectations for the class. Textbook reading was required but you don't use most of the book. Tests were challenging but the study guides were extremely helpful. You get out of the class what you put into it. I would love to take another class from him in the future. Great professor!

Professor Hyldahl is a really friendly teacher and very approachable. He is pretty clear about the expectations for the class and has study guides that tell what you need to know for the tests. The only complaint I have is that he often posted readings the night before they were due, but the reading load was relatively light.

Dr. Hyldahl is fantastic!  I loved his class.  It was his first semester teaching at BYU when I took it, but he is so dedicated to helping students.  He creates study guides that are extremely helpful for the test.  If you don't know or understand something, don't hesitate to meet with him!

Science isn't my best subject, & it's difficult to like it when the course is structured to be hard, but Prof Kowallis is a great guy. Cheerful, loves to answer questions. LOTS of tests. Reading test due before every class and attendance test in class. I didn't like the Physics unit, but everything else was like an AP class in high school.

I really appreciated Prof. Kowallis. He is kind and it is clear that he wants his students to succeed. This course was one of the more difficult, or maybe time-consuming courses though. There were quizzes for each chapter and lots of tests. I had to spend considerable time in the TA lab, which was helpful. Granted, science isn't my #1 subject.
It's been years but I really enjoyed Dr Kowallis!

I'm not a fan of science, so that may be part of the problem, but I felt like I didn't know what Kowallis was talking about most of the time. He wasn't necessarily boring, but he wasn't super entertaining either. He was mediocre. The class itself isn't hard, it's test heavy. I felt like he got distracted during lectures and often went off topic.

The fact that I hate PS100 has less to do with Dr. Kowallis and more to do with the structure of the class, but he really did not do anything to make it better. Lectures were boring and all a restatement of what the chapter for the day said. You can tell that he's been teaching this class for a decade or two

Brother Kowallis is amazing! He brings the Spirit into class every day! He was very understanding when I had health problems halfway through the semester. We didn't have a final, only a final project, which was great! The material is interesting and he really knows his stuff. He helped me solve a block in my family tree in about 2 hours!
Dr. Kowallis gives really good lectures! He knows all of his students and makes sure everyone is involved and understands. The demonstrations were really cool to watch as well!
I love him! He has been teaching for a long time now and he still has it! He really cares about you and makes the class feel like a family instead of students.

Dr. Kowallis is wonderful. He wants each of his students to succeed. The nature of PHYS100 meant a lot of work, a lot of content, and a lot of tests. But, as far as Dr. Kowallis goes, he was very willing to help us as best he could. For the class, I would suggest going to the TA lab.

I adore this professor. This was by far my favorite class...I made lifelong friends and a lot of that is because the teacher made the class friendly and let us get to know eachother. The professor learns all our names and cares about each of us. He wants us to succeed.

Professor Kowallis is a great teacher and a great man but many of the aspects of the class are dictated by the nature of the course as opposed to his teaching style. As a non-science major this class was difficult for me but I learned a ton. The textbook is your bible for this class. Utilize the help offered by TAs. Attend class and lab.

The best religion class. He shares interesting information and I learned so much that I can apply to my own life. I learned a lot about my family history and he is such a caring professor. He goes out of his way to help you  with anything. No tests, only quizzes and assignments which are actually fun. Highly recommend!

Brother Kowallis was a great teacher for Family History. He really knows what he is talking about and is always willing to help any student with any problem they have. He gives assignments every week or so but they aren't hard. There are no tests, just a project due at the end that you are supposed to spend about 15 hours on throughout the semester

Once I realized that the lectures were basically covered in the posted powerpoints and quizzes, I lost all desire to keep going. I already lack much desire to work on the frustrating world of family history. Did teach me a lot though.
He explains things clearly and takes every question seriously. A genuinely good man who really knows his stuff. He's funny too and keeps lectures interesting. I would recommend him to anybody.

Dr. Kowallis is a WONDERFUL teacher.  He cares so much about his students, takes the time to remember names, and asks you how you're doing.  He's fun, engaging, very humble, and honest.  He's usually clear, but if you don't understand at first, ask questions until you do.  It's worth it!  Very small class & you can get to know other classmates too.

Dr. Kowallis is a good teacher-- He cares about his students and their success in the class. I would recommend him. The key to doing well in PHY S is getting a GOOD TA. So make sure you find a  TA that explains the concepts well, and makes it semi-interesting.  The TA's are the ones you will interact with the most.

Really good teacher for this required class.  Bart uses a lot of interesting demonstrations to explain difficult concepts.  Plus, the workload is very light unless you're one of those lazy sacks stuck in high-school mode where you expect to get a good grade by simply showing up.
Good at explaining. He does not make the class out of reach for good grades. Good activities used for learning.
Prof. Kowallis is awesome! He's very good at explaining concepts, and making class fun.  I thoroughly enjoyed his class.

Grades can be overall lab, attendance and tests, or just final.  Tests easy if attend class and labs, but difficult when don't.  All PhySci teachers give same test,so if concerned about grade,doesn't matter which teacher you have.  Kowalis is approachable& somewhat entertaining, but doesn't  grade anything, that is all up to the TA's.

Very nice, and interesting man. Large class but the Labs are very helpful. Go to the reviews and make sure you know the concepts. The tests are all conceptual and the same for any ps 100 class at BYU. The book was easy to read and chapters were short and sweet. Buy the lecture packet! Very easy to take notes on. Exciting experiments in class.

okay,I took this class based on theses ratings.....I'm not sure if I am unintelligent or something but I did not do so well in this class.Dr Kowallis is a good professor,but the tests were just weird for me.When I was learning I thought I got everything ,but when I took the tests it was just bad...( you really really really have to know how to appl
Kowallis is a great teacher. I hated physical science but he made it kind of interesting. He practically gives you the answers to all the clicker quizzes. Also very good at explaining the concepts.
He is a really good teacher.  Only problem is he is a bit of a monotone, so you might fall asleep in class.  If you read the chapters and go to class you will get an A for sure.

He is a great teacher.  I wish I could have him for every science class.  He is informative and answers everyone's questions.  The TAs aren't really that useful, and lab is not neccesary, but I didn't open the book at all and got an A.

I LOVE kowallis. he is really funny, and he explains everything really well. he takes the time to answer questions even though we had a huge class, and he explains it in a way that you understand. i never touched the book, i skipped some labs and some classes, and i still got an awesome grade. take this class from kowallis!!

He knows his stuff and is a great guy, but since the class is so big, you dont interact with him much.  It really comes down to whether or not you have a good T.A. who is available to help you.  Tests were hard because you had to understand the concepts fully in order to apply them.

Good teacher, his lectures are fairly interesting, but the TA's are not helpful at all! At least mine wasnt. Tests are fairly easy, but i found it kind of hard to study for them. Sometimes the material on the test is not in the book, which is not very clear. Grading is very easy though. Overall a B class.

He was nice, however he also talked to us as if we were children and he started answering your questions before you even got finished asking them. Which sometimes meant he went WAY off base. Quizes were easy but tests were more focused on the small details. Good but not Great teacher

My favorite teacher at BYU! He explains things very clearly and is a great guy! I think he is so great because he genuinly loves teaching. Go to class each day to complete the clicker quizes (which are easy) and labs. I found it very helpfull to read the chapter each day before class. Go to 2 review sessions and you'll be prepared for the exams

I loved Kowallis! He is this kind of eccentric old dude who turned out to be a really good teacher, good at answering questions and explaining concepts. It is important to keep up with the reading in this class because the tests cover a LOT of material. Going to class is also important, but everyone ends up with a good grade!

I love Dr. Kowallis!  He explains it so clear and well that I noticed physical science elements in my life.  He is so well organized and so caring about his students.  If I were a geology major I would take every class he teaches.  There is only good to say about him.
Very great

Professor Kowallis is a very clear teacher. He really wants to make sure that the students understand the material. He is very good about answering questions and preparing students for the test. I highly recommend him for Physical Science.
Awesome guy, knowledgeable and helpful too. A fair person, a true teacher, not one of those arrogant know it alls that makes cryptic blithering while in front of the class.

Professor Kowallis is one of those teachers who genuinely cares about his students doing well.  He is willing to go over concepts as many times as necessary if it will help the class.  The TA review sessions can be helpful but arn't that important or necessary.  Just go to the end of semester reviews and the final will be a breeze
Professor Kowallis was very dynamic and did his best to be as clear as possible. He truly wanted all of the students to understand. He made science come to life.
this class was very boring and i have a very hard time staying awake!
Great teacher. He is the best for p-sci 100. Tries his very best to help you get an A. All you need to do is show up every day.
very nice and sweet. i hated geology 111 before i took his class, but i absolutely love it now.
Just go to the review sessions before each test :)
From what I have heard, he is the best teacher for the 100 Physical Science. His lectures are great and very clear. Tests pretty easy. I don't like science but I don't mind his class at all.

Everything is in the book, though he does make some concepts clear through experiements. Tests are a lot easier than I thought they would be. Not detailed, just basic concepts. Memorization not that necessary.

Oh man, what an easy class.  If you attend lecture and read the book, an A is in the bag if you don't slack off.  Much better than other 100 teachers, with a nice strong voice.  Overall, one of the better GE's.
Excellent teacher, makes concepts very clear.  Very helpful (espicially if you actually attend class).
Great guy.  Very willing to help you if you don't understand.  I never really liked science but he applied the subject matter to the gospel and made it as interesting as possible.

Well, it is nice that he gives you the notes as you walk into class but they have nothing to do with the tests.  His lectures are pretty boaring and he doesn't teach well.  If you want to teach yourself you can take it from him.
His lectures are way helpful and the experiments are totally awesome, but everything is in the book. He's a great professor!
All taught in class available in book.  How about something more in class?  Enjoyable field trip!  Enjoy some of the fun discussions.
If I am going to wake up at 8am, the teacher should at least have the common courtesy to wear clothes and shower. Being intelligent doesn't excuse a lack of personal hygiene.
you don't need to go to class at ALL if you read the book.  But, if you have time, his lectures are seriously very fun and interesting.
I couldn't convince myself that listening to him was worth waking up at 9 on Friday mornings.
No Comments
He's a great professor; he hands you the notes as you walk in and posts the powerpoints online.  p.s. He has cool eyes, check 'em out!
Rummaged thru students clothes at fieldcamp looking for fossil student had found
He's the easiest teacher for this class, and he hands out notes for you!

He is a good teacher and understands when it comes to problems that come up for turning in your homework. It is a credentialed SOA class, so it is, by nature, difficult, but if you make it your main priority as far as classes go, you can succeed. He also had 3 percent extra credit, which helps because exams are 80% of the grade.

He is definitely in my top five favorite professors. The content is hard and takes a lot of work outside of class to get it down but the way he teaches it just clicks. I felt super prepared for the tests and the homeworks really helped. He is more than happy to help and answer the any question we might have.

Professor does a good job explaining things, was a bit unorganized at times. Attendance isn't mandatory and most people didn't show up but seemed to do fine in the class. There are group projects throughout and a couple HW assignments due a week. The tests are half in person (in class) and half take home which is nice. The material isn't difficult.

Dr. Richardson is a great guy who cares about his students. He clearly knows what he's talking about and will go around answering any questions you might have. I enjoyed learning statistical programming in R from him and I learned a lot. He wants to help you succeed.
Best movie star and producer. Really wants students to succeed and takes the time to make sure it happens. Lectures are engaging and fun. Would 100% take from him again.

Very, very kind man. Excellent course to take before moving on to Machine Learning or other advanced regression courses. Had a great sense on what was functionally useful for us in python without overcomplicating concepts. For Stat 220, gave tons of leniency on grading. Occasionally hard to contact and follow in lecture, but he is very considerate.

This class certainly wasn't easy but Prof. Richardson made it enjoyable. He is approachable and friendly when it comes to his teaching style. This was his first year back teaching this course so he acknowledged he didn't have an established mojo but he still taught exceptionally well and helped his students succeed. He's the best out there!

Dr. Richardson was incredible, albeit a little disorganized. He very clearly cares about the success of his students and makes a point to be accessible outside of class. The material was very very difficult but Dr. Richardson taught clearly and organized the class to enhance understanding. I loved taking his class!!!

Outside of class he's a bit more awkward but in class he's a goofball. Most homework and tests are easy and straight from lectures. And I think pretty much all hw/tests were open book. I put the least amount of effort into this class and ended with a B- or C+ still. Don't think you could go wrong with this guy.

There was never a dull day in Dr. Richardson's class! He's great at engaging his students and keeping them entertained through his lectures. This was his first time teaching the class, but he did very well! He started to restructure the class so by the end it felt very comfortable. Not difficult at all. Great teacher to take from for any class.

Dr. Richardson is a fantastic professor! This was his first time teaching this class and he did quite well for it being his first time! Probably was my favorite programming classes I've taken at BYU. He clearly knows his stuff and is excited about helping students learn the material. He is truly interested in everyone and helping them succeed!

Dr. Richardson knows his stuff, but he isn't the best at communicating that knowledge clearly. He is however good at re-explaining concepts if you let him know you are confused, so speak up! His slides are the most useful study tool, some students never came to class and learned the material from the slides and hw just fine.

He started the first lecture by telling us he hadn't updated his slides from last semester, and that the major feedback he received was that his slides were full of mathematical errors. He doesn't prepare for class, and I wouldn't have passed without The Infinite Actuary or a similar resource, which I'd definitely recommend for IFM and his class.

Covering material for SOA Exam C: somewhere around 80% of the SOA syllabus.  He makes it much easier to understand than the book does.  Great at answering questions and helping students who need it.  Homework load isn't bad - I almost wish there were more for more practice.  Tests are straightforward but be careful not to make stupid mistakes.

Took his class on "Inference." Average grade in the class was a 91.39%. Dr Richardson is absurdly smart. Great lectures, but he goes fast sometimes (there's so much material). Class is easier if you understand calculus, read the book (book is not necessary, but it can help), go to class, do ALL homework and study with other people. He's fantastic!

Great class. He's always approachable to students and his lectures are super fun. He's pretty good at walking you through difficult concepts in class. Attendance is not necessary and he gives extra credits.

Professor Parrish is a very kind guy. However, I  found his teaching style very difficult to work with. Class and lectures consisted of him reading off the slides without much extra insight or teaching techniques. If you want to succeed it seemed to require learning the material completely on your own and then using class as a review. Test heavy!

Mostly memorization of his lecture slides, don't bother buying the textbook; it rotted under my desk. Content is hard, but doable with personal study and attending weekly reviews. Each exam had a group retake, and at the end of the semester you could average one of the scores. Parrish is so funny; I loved his lectures. He motivated me to learn.

I think Dr. Parrish was a solid professor. I really enjoyed his lectures and every bit of content on the tests came straight from his slides. He loves what he does and is really good at explaining hard concepts. It's a hard class, just be ready for it.

I really feel that Dr. Parrish only teaches because he has to (research is his passion). He was not very accessible for help, reviews weren't helpful, tests were really hard. I would study excessively and still would perform poorly on tests. He is a really nice and a great guy, good lecturer. But never felt like I could succeed.

Dr. Parrish is a new professor at BYU who really cares about helping students to understand these concepts. NEURO 205 is a hard course, and Dr. Parrish has high expectations for us to think critically on exams. Just review his PowerPoint slides, go to the TA reviews, and you'll do fine on exams & in the class (I generally didn't read the textbook).

Main difficulty is knowing what info to prioritize and how to prepare – study guides are pretty general while questions are very specific, often testing parenthetical distinctions. However, one exam can be averaged with a group retake, there were two extra credit opportunities (+.5%), and the final was curved. One the whole I felt it balanced out.

Dr. Parrish is amazing. Getting an A in the class is absolutely doable, but will require effort. Being a neuro major is just hard. Parrish gave all the information you needed for exams and shared his passion for the material. He cares so much for his students, and he provided extra credit when it seemed like the students struggled with something.

The content is so cool but he ruins it. He is constantly correcting his exams and quizzes because the students find questions that were written poorly. We got some points back which is nice. But he DOES NOT teach us what is on the exam. DONT EVER take from him.

Other reviewers nailed it. On tests, a few options will be true and you have to pick the one that's MOST true; very hard, even if you know the material. Quizzes are the only other points and don't match the exams. My advice: make a flashcard for almost every slide to memorize and then have an AI bot feed you practice tests once it's time to cram.
His tests questions are horrible and the TA reviews do not help at all. You can tell he is not super invested in the class because he is terrible at teaching the course. Take from Matheson instead.

Super nice but he does not teach the class well. Your grade is solely based on the exams and newly implemented quizzes. He asks some fair questions on the tests but others are very convoluted. Lectures are very dry and long. The content is interesting but take it from a different professor.

Nice guy, but terrible at teaching this class. 70% exams and 30% proctored online quizzes. No study guides, homework or practice tests to show you what you'll be tested on. Doesn't let you see what you got wrong on quizzes. Lectures are dense and confusing, and tests are mostly based on memorizing minute details. I felt like I was set up to fail.

Dr. Parrish had high expectations for the class, pushing us to learn the material well. This class prepared me well for future neuroscience classes, helping me learn what study techniques work for me.

I feel that my classmates described very well what Dr. Parrish was like as a professor. Great guy, but the class set up was horrible. Gave unfair advantage to some students compared to others and his tests were very hard with little knowledge on what to focus on when studying. I wouldn't recommend his class.

I'm a 4.0 student and got a B+ in this class.  The tests are wicked hard, testing on very small details brushed over during the class presentations, requiring students to essentially memorize every slide he ever presented in class.  There are no study guides.  He grades harshly on group presentations.  His lectures are too fast and unclear. Booooo.

Great guy, really like him as a person. As a professor however, not so much. I took his class for neurobiology and many times had to do my own learning because topics weren't explained well. Tests were more difficult than they needed to be, lectures covered too much information without a good explanation. Does offer test retakes that are averaged

Please do not take a class from Professor Parrish! He does not give a clear study guide, and he doesn't explain things clearly. I always came out of class confused. This class is full of material, and he tests on things that are briefly mentioned. He uses trick questions too. He's a nice guy, but not a good teacher.

Dr. Parrish is a super nice guy. He is super patient and eager to explain a concept when you don't get it. You can really tell that he means it when he says that he wants to make sure everyone is on the same page. Definitely recommend him!
Great professor!  Cares about the students and he knows his students names.  Show up and do the work, and you'll be fine!
Dr. Parrish is awesome. Super nice, fun, knowledgeable, and ready and more than willing to help. He wants you to succeed! I would recommend.

such a kind, sweet professor. he really really pushes for us to expand our testimonies and go on missions, and is so nice to talk to. it makes me sad how many people rated professor smith badly! i would recommend his class if you want to go on a mission.
great teacher, great guy, professor smith's class is great for mission prep. if you dont like to get called on to answer questions all the time then i probably wouldnt take him

Brother Smith is so sweet and incredibly kind, but the organization of this class made it difficult to learn. There are multi-select PMG quizzes due each week that are tedious and difficult. The final was also horrendous. That being said, I did feel the spirit in this class! Brother Smith cares, he just doesn't always execute it gracefully.
Bad protect yourself now

There is a lot of work for this class, but if you stay on top of it it's very easy to get an A. I enjoyed the lectures and we got to practice teaching lessons in class. I often felt the spirit and feel better prepared for my mission after this class.

I wanted to like this class, but I didn't. Every class was the same. Class dragged on and was very boring. Brother Smith called on the same people pretty much every day yet still didn't know a single persons name. The class set up was also very unorganized. He is passionate about teaching the content, he just doesn't do it in an efficient way.

Great and caring guy. Class is wicked easy. Little amount of assignments but you have to come to class and participate. Tests are ok, long and specific tedious questions. They all come from Preach My Gospel. Its open note so its easy to get 100%, tests just take forever. Wouldn't take again because it is boring and not useful information.

Our class had 15 people, last day of class he still asked me my name. 1-2 quizzes due every week. Ten questions each but they are all "multi-select" and he is  against opening the quiz and letting you review them. Final is 16 short response questions(5 sentences minimum) along with 30 "multi-select" MCQ. I wanna go on a mission less now

I did not feel the spirit at all in this class. Lectures felt like he was reciting PMG and not actually teaching by the spirit. Assignments were due on Saturday nights, and you were not allowed to turn them in early. He made me want to serve a mission even less than before. I don't recommend this guy if you are on the fence about serving a mission.

It makes me sad that Brother Smith got so many bad ratings. Even though his lectures could be a little repetitive, he is such a kind person and is always smiling. The class was super easy, you just had to keep up with some readings and then take really easy quizzes at the end of most weeks.
He is passionate about the gospel and is very helpful if you talk to him. He is always smiling to. He expects normal effort but is a great professor
I took his religious freedom course and he had very inspiring lectures. The homework was straightforward and he is easy to talk to for help.

This class was very straight forward. We would come to class and practice preparing  and teaching lessons together. Brother Smith is a super nice guy and is willing to work with you. Overall I really liked this class and it definitely helped me prepare for my mission.

I'm glad I took this class because it made me read Preach My Gospel (and boy do you read PMG). BUT I would recommend taking Mission Prep from a different teacher. I still can't tell you what was taught--it was kind of disorganized and there never seemed to be enough time for us to participate. Good class--recommend another teacher.
Don't recommend.

Professor Smith is awesome and respectful and kind. He is knowledgeable about missionary work and the gospel. He can teach you a lot about the doctrine if you are open to it. He is good at facilitating discussions and getting participation.

There is little outside work. I spent maybe 30 minutes to an hour a week on homework for Mission Prep.

I liked this class and learned a few things about teaching the gospel. Unfortunately, lectures were often boring and do not teach you too much. Tests taught me nothing because you have to read through the entire preach my gospel to find the answers. This class isn't hard to pass but could be taught much better and the tests should be changed.

He's a nice guy but the class is just dull. You're better off just reading Preach My Gospel because the quizzes and tests are all copied from it. He occasionally has some good insight but not enough to make the class worth it. There is way too much work for a 2 credit class. The tests are also really long for no reason.

It's funny how I feel like I am no more prepared for my mission than when I started this class. Don't get me wrong the class was cake. But honestly, it would do you better to take any of the other religion classes.

I honestly regret taking this class so much. He made sexist comments in class on a regular basis. He encouraged sexual assault victims to go help their attacker repent (so dangerous). Midterm was 3 hours of just quoting Preach My Gospel with a promise that the final will be exactly the same. The only saving grace is that its open note. Do not do it

I took his course on Mission Prep. Honestly, I found that my Book of Mormon class prepared me much better for  a mission than this. The lectures aren't particularly engaging, and you basically have to do the same assignment five times. However, I felt the spirit a few times and enjoyed some of the life experiences he shared.

I don't know why Professor Smith has so many bad ratings. He is an extremely good professor, cares about his students, and is super engaging with good stories. There is some homework you have to do outside of the class but not an insane amount. If you put even a little bit of effort in, you'll get an A.

Lots of busy work, lectures were kind of boring. Too much work for a religion class. Tests were crazy long, weird and hard. Midterms and final are online, 2-3 hours long, open note. The quizzes and tests were based on word for word preach my gospel.

it is sad that prof. Smith has alot of bad reviews, he is a very caring professor. He did have alot of work but its university so it makes sense.I think professor smith really explained how to be a good missionary. It was sad my class was on their phones half of the time. If you really pay attention and put effort you will get alot out of it.

Elder Smith is kind and has a wealth of experience to share in the class. Discussions are engaging because everyone who takes the class wants to be there. There is a final essay and op-ed for potential publication to practice persuasion. You read prophetic teachings and the most important court cases/opinions. This should be a core religion class!
I loved this class so much! Brother Smith really knew how to explain Preach My Gospel! The class is an easy A as long as you show up. The final is pretty long, but it is open note.

Brother Smith is a great guy, just not a great teacher. Honestly, this class made going on a mission seem like the most boring thing ever which sucks since I already have my call and am excited to go. He focuses too much on Preach My Gospel and not enough on spiritual matters. Midterm and final are ridiculously tedious and take so long to complete

Prof. Smith is a great guy with a lot of interesting things to say. He has great insights and I always felt the spirit in this mission prep class. I felt like I left the class having a better understanding of preach my gospel. The only thing I didn't appreciate was that he often called on people randomly and rarely remembered our names.

This review is for the "Latter-day Saints and Religious Liberty" class. Dr. Smith is a very nice guy. He is fun and extremely well-respected in his field. The class is an easy A if you show up to class and do the assignments. His lectures kind tend to be super dry if there isn't a lot of class participation. He isn't very tech-savvy.
He is my uncle and I love him he is very cool and nice.

Overall, I liked the class and professor. He is caring and loves teaching his students. The worst part about the course was the 3.5 hour midterm and 3 hour final. Both were open book, but extremely tedious... The homework assignments aren't too hard. Attendance is graded.

Prof. Smith is super nice and he cares about the students, but he was not my favorite teacher. The lectures were boring and the tests were ridiculously long. Weekly assignments have to be submitted on Saturday, not sooner, which isn't my favorite. You can get a good grade in the class, but I didn't learn much or enjoy going to class.
Extremely Tedious Exams, Lots of busy work

his exams were tested on the most minuscule and redundant details in preach my gospel and extra reading assignments he gives out. We absolutely had to memorize the words found in the hands out and books or else we would fail the exams. This class took up a lot of my time and does not encapsulate what a true missionary should be.

He's a really great person and cares deeply about his students and the class. That being said, he is not a good teacher. Calls on students randomly who usually have no idea whats going on, tests and assignments were pretty easy but super super long. (Midterm took 2-3 hours). Lectures not very engaging but felt the spirit a few times.

2 exams: open book and 3 hour timer. 7 quizzes: 10 questions, 30 minute timer, open book. Exams were redundant and questions were not as clear and were very broad. Easy A class but I did not learn as much as I thought I would on how to be a missionary. His style of teaching wasn't very effective and found a lot of what he assigned to be redundant.

I am surprised Prof Smith has so many bad reviews. I took REL130C during spring term, and it wasn't too heavy. Participation matters, but homework assignments are easy, most of them I did during class. The TAs are tough graders, but Prof Smith cares about his students and is willing to work with them. The two exams are open book.

Lectures aren't engaging. Exams/assignments are easy but time-consuming. The questions are worded weirdly, making you second-guess everything, and he gives no feedback. Everything comes word-for-word from PMG, but then it feels like you learn nothing. Don't take from him if you have a busy schedule or want to grow spiritually.

Easy A but the professor was not my favorite. He would unnecessarily pick on students and I was constantly worried about being called out. Did not feel like a safe learning environment. All assignments were easy and tests were open book but the teacher made the class awful.

This class was absolutely horrendous. The teacher rambled on, never gave us time to teach our lessons, and unnecessarily put students on the spot. I feel absolutely unprepared for my mission. DO NOT TAKE FROM THIS TEACHER.

I like the guy, he seems like a genuine dude and is really passionate about the gospel. But his teaching style is absolutely unbearable. He would ramble on for the whole class and use up the time meant for teaching the mock lessons we prepared. The work for the class was poorly planned and the TAs were an absolute wreck, only 1 of the 4 responded

Mission prep with Prof. Smith was an easy A. He has lots of assignments but the content is all straight out of preach my gospel and they are easy. Participation is important. Lots of readings sometimes but I just skimmed them. Tests are open note and open book. Great teacher and I truly grew and learned lots from Prof. Smith.
Do not take any of his classes... TAs aren't good. He cant even remember our names. He calls on you whenever. Asked me if I had a learning accommodation? he aint it. warning you now.

Prof smith is decent. His lectures can be spiritual but thats if you can stay awake for his whole lectures. He takes 4ever to grade. His assignments are easy but take time. His midterm took me 3 hours! He will make you feel dumb if you don't answer his question the way he wanted it answered. over all pretty easy if you do your work and go to class.

Do not take this professor! I took Mission Prep from him and did not learn a thing. His classes were basically BoM Come Follow Me but were boring and not very spiritual. We rarely had the opportunity to teach (only 5 times all semester) and each time we only got 5 minutes. He also calls on people to answer randomly and is overall a bad teacher.

He was  interesting. I quite liked his spiritual insights but how he handled the logistics of said class was a pain. He didn't answer my emails, he required a physical textbook despite one being free online, and almost didn't grade some assignments by the end of the semester. He felt like a substitute teacher rather than a college professor.

Prof. Smith is a good guy but his teaching style of HORRIBLE! I dreaded coming to class and hated being in class. If you make any comment during the first 5 minutes of class, you are screwed. He WILL call on you and only you for the rest of class RELENTLESSLY. I learned to not participate or make comments. Get ready to write a LOT of papers.

I love the BOM, but I dreaded coming to this class every week. Prof Smith makes one student stand the entire time and answer questions. It's super awkward and uncomfortable. He's also very subjective so if your answer isn't spot on, you're wrong. He made multiple comments that were pretty offensive too. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM!

I really loved this class and enjoyed the insights that Brother Smith had on the Book of Mormon. It was my favorite religion class at BYU. I appreciated that he let us take our education into our own hands. You were not required to attend or do the readings, but both of those things helped with the test. There were no dumb "daily" quizzes.

Brother Smith was great, he had the spirit and used his experience as a mission president to teach you a lot about being a missionary. The organization of the class was kind of confusing though, assignments weren't put on learning suite in advance which was annoying. But, the requirements were very simple and it was easy to get an A!

DO NOT I REPEAT DO NOT take ANY class with him!!!!!! He is a really nice guy but his class is the dumbest thing ever. I learned absolutely nothing and I dreaded attending his class. The tests and quizzes took so long and were subjective. He never answered questions and I don't think any student wanted to be in his class. seriously awful experience

I did not find the lectures to be very spiritual. We had several essays that were graded on unknown criteria, and the majority of the test was also graded subjectively. He also picked a student question-answerer of the day. This would test if the student had read, but it would humiliate them publicly if they hadnt.

Awful. Nice guy, but his papers were insane and graded on an arbitrary scale, the tests took between two and three hours, and he occasionally taught straight-up false doctrine. Readings weren't uploaded until the morning of, and he'd call on a student to be the "question-answerer" for the class.. even though he'd upload the homework an hour before.

Prof Smith seems like a quality guy, but I would avoid taking his Book of Mormon class. He is really slow to grade assignments. He doesn't respond to emails. All of the assignments are essays with no clear criteria for grading, it is very subjective. Class is spiritual and not academic which I was ok with, but imagine how a nonmember would feel.

Prof Smith is a great professor. His lectures can be really spiritual and give insight on more than just the scriptures. He does have a lot of readings, from scriptures and conference talks. Attendance isn't mandatory but going to class helps with understanding the essay and exam prompts. He gives extra credit for class participation.

He is a great guy but harder than it needs to be. Expect to write several essays for the class, they are graded fairly hard without a clear criteria as to what constitutes an A. The tests are NOT multiple choice and are not just on BOM but also a bunch of conference talks. They are however open scripture and can print talks, test is timed though.
Great professor and make the difficult concepts easier

Robbie shares a lot of great stories, at the expense of focused teaching. I personally struggled with this teaching style. Content wise, his lectures are great and very effective, but with lots of tangents. Some comments and stories also felt condescending, like he thinks he is the wisest person and he has personal duty to share his life wisdom.

Will do anything for just about anyone. Always willing to put in extra hours to help you succeed. Lectures are well put together and abundantly clear. It's hard to imagine someone teaching the course better than Robbie. If you're into actually learning calculus, do whatever you have to to take this class from him.

Robbie explained things in a way that a child could understand while still treating us with respect as adults. I think that a lot of this class depends on how good your TA is too, and mine was great. Attendance is not mandatory but it definitely helps you succeed. Use the Organic Chemistry teacher on youtube to study.
He was the first person who truly made math make sense to me. He is incredibly charismatic and kind, and you can tell he genuinely loves teaching because he cares so much about his students.
Genuinely the Goat. He is a great teacher that really understands the material and can explain how the mathematics actually work, and not just saying things to memorize.
Genuinely the Goat.

I definitely recommend taking Calculus from Robbie! He was an amazing professor who deeply cared about his students. He is funny and really knows the content well. He is also accessible out of class. It was my favorite class last semester!

This professor is literally the best. If you can get into his class, DO IT. His tests in this class were nice because he gave very very good test prep. He also sometimes works with you on homework problems during class to explain things and get you ready for the homework. Love this guy.

This class is super hard but he tries to make it easier; he cuts homework problems he doesn't like (for good reason) and he will prepare you well for the exams. Honestly best professor you could take from for any ACME class. However, he does get sidetracked easily and will often talk about irrelevant things during class and office hours.

Math 112 at BYU is just a hard class in general. Professor Snellman (everyone calls him robbie) is by far the best professor I have ever had. He's engaging and he teaches calculus in a way that makes it seem simple. I took calc in high school and thought this was going to be a disaster. He helped me gain my confidence.

I wrote a review before the end of the semester I didn't realize the atrocious grade change to account for the weight of the final. I haven't even taken the final yet and my grade DROPPED from a 96.5 to an 89. I messaged Robbie, he said "The grades change weight because the final is now in place". Absolute joke, favorite teacher in college though.

Robbie is a real one! He is a super genuine and thoughtful guy, and his lectures are entertaining because of the personal experiences and stories he shares. Be aware that his calc 1 class was not nearly as hard nor as in-depth as the AP Calc AB class that I took back in high school. 

Overall, great guy, and great at explaining things simply!
THIS IS THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER TAKEN FROM. Such a man of the earth. Take any class from him and he will give you his 120% every class period. He is always there for you.
Robbie is one of my favorite people I've met here at BYU. His lessons are nothing short of understandable, entertaining, and insightful. There is no other professor I would take for 112 than him.

Without a doubt one of the best teachers I have EVER had. You GOTTA take Snellman. He shows such genuine care for each of his students and explains concepts like no other. He's hilarious and will also motivate and inspire you. You'll learn life lessons from his crazy interesting life story and you'll love it. Learning is a guarentee I promise you.

Hands down best teacher I've ever had. Super fun and explains concepts very well. Homework 6 days a week but shouldn't take you more than 45 minutes each. He'll answer any questions and genuinely cares.

You gotta take Snellman. Not only does he make sure everybody understands concepts, but he also goes out of his way to make sure our classes are inspiration and motivation-driven. Funnily enough, he doesn't require attendance, but in a good way, that made me discipline myself to go as I know that this class is hard but rewarding.
OMG!!! Best teacher EVER! I took Calc in high school, but I didn't understand it until I took it
Explains topics extremely well and is great at keeping you engaged

Robbie was an awesome professor who genuinely cares about you as a student. He has really cool stories and is very straightforward with his teaching style. And take advantage of his resources outside of class! (reviews and office hours). TA recitation for 112 was just doing HW problems too, so it was optional just like lecture attendance.

Calc 1 is not an easy class, but Robbie makes it super enjoyable. He is by far the best math professor I've ever had. MAKE SURE TO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF HIS REVIEW SESSIONS. He is fantastic. Highly suggest.

The best math teacher I have ever had. He helped me discover the joy of math again. It was some hard content sometimes but it felt manageable because he taught it so well. Super down to earth guy, great stories and will do a HW problem in class, has a real desire to help the students
Take classes from Dr. Snellman!!! He is truly one of the best teachers I've had in my entire life. He is encouraging, GREAT at teaching, and funny. Can't recommend him enough.

Calculus is difficult no matter what. But! Robbie made this class actually enjoyable. His lectures were really beneficial and helped me understand the content. I recommend going to his office hours anytime! He is always willing to go over homework and questions, especially in his office hours. 10/10 recommend math 112 with Robbie!

Robbie deserves every single great review that's been written about him. He does a fantastic job of teaching calculus in a way that allows you to learn while having fun. His lectures are super interesting and he goes to great lengths to ensure that we as students have access to resources and enjoy learning.
Robbie makes calculus engaging and accessible, even for math-phobic students. Attendance is a must, and the TA recitations are super helpful. unstuck ai and the free textbook make studying a breeze.
super awesome teacher, very real and very funny, it was super engaging and really very manageable class. there was graded daily homework but it was very manageable, and tests never had surprises

I think he did a great job at teaching calculus and it was clear he cared a lot about his students and didn't want them to fail. He tried his hardest to be down-to-earth and relatable in order to teach us math effectively. I can't recommend him enough, he's FANTASTIC!

I never took calc but was always good at math and I could not handle this class. I actually paid a ton of attention in lectures but I had to self teach everything I actually wanted to know. it felt like a review for people who already learned calc in highschool. Robbie rambles and wastes lecture time acting like a "cool teacher"

Robbie was the best professor to take calc 1 from. He was able to describe the material in a way that helped everyone understand whatever topic was covered. He tended to rush through the end of the lecture but he would stay after for any questions anyone had. Make sure to do the homework as it is a major part of your grade.

Robbie is the best teacher you could take Calculus from. He is very considerate of his students and very good at answering questions. He has respect for his students that no other professor has. He is very accessible and approachable and does a good job helping struggling students. He is the closest thing to a perfect math professor.

Robbie is awesome! Please take classes from him. He is so funny and engaging in class and you can tell he knows his stuff extremely well! In Math 112 just come to class and do the homework and you'll do well on the exams.

Robbie is by far the best math teacher I have ever had. He gives amazing lectures and you can tell that he really cares about the students. The class difficulty rating is entirely based on how well you are prepared, I was already exposed to calc in an AP calc class last year, but Robbie set us up for success with loads of practices and extra help.

Robbie is really outgoing but tends to tangent in class, so he doesn't cover all the material. This makes homework and tests a lot harder. He also will tell you what to expect on tests, but then put material on tests that he never mentioned. Tests also have very few questions but weigh a lot.

Robbie is the best professor I've had at BYU. He genuinely cares for his students and is super knowledgeable. I dislike math in general, but yet at the end of the semester, I found myself sad that I wouldn't have calculus anymore, because I liked Robbie so much. Can't recommend more.
Robbie is the GOAAATTTTT. My favourite ever. He is super motivating and explains everything in such clear terms. Such a solid guy.

Robbie is IMPECCABLE- best professor I've ever had. His lectures were so clear and concise, and he explained everything so well. He's also SUPER motivating, and he inspired me to WANT to learn calculus. Absolutely incredible.
Robbie is hilarious and gets off on tangents during class, but overall he is incredible at explaining concepts in class.

"Robbie," as he asks to be called, is an absolutely amazing teacher. Calculus is tough, but I'm convinced he makes it easier to understand than any other professor out there. He points out the common mistakes students make very clearly and warns students about them, cracking jokes and telling anecdotes all along the way.

Robbie is the best teacher I've had, hands down. I'd taken calculus previously, but I needed a refresher after two years so I decided to take his course. All of the details of his teaching--even down to his handwriting, demonstrate the great effort he's put in over the years to make complicated subjects like these understandable to us. 10/10

Absolutely fantastic. Absolutely spoiled because he's such a great teacher. He actively tries to help each student succeed and explains everything so simply. He makes everyone genuinely feel like they can excel in math. Absolutely phenomenal. The only down side is he doesn't teach Calc 2 (math 113) which depresses me.

This was sort of my third time taking calculus. Robbie taught in a way that I actually understood it for the first time. His great personality even made me look forward to it, which is beyond crazy. I have never liked math, but I would be willing to take this class again as long as Robbie was the one teaching.
He is an amazing professor.

Robbie (as he goes by) is a great professor- he's a guy of strong character, has great penmanship (hallelujah) and gives engaging lectures. When you keep up on homework and go to recitation (lab), you'll be prepared for tests.

Robbie is the best!! He's one of my favorite math teachers that I've had. Calc 3 isn't always super intuitive, but he did a great job explaining all the concepts and why they work. The homework isn't too bad, although it often looks decievingly short (4 homework problems can end up taking 2 hours). Take this class from Robbie if you can!

Robbie is the kind of professor who makes you like going to school. His lectures are fantastic, he cares about his students, and he is the most reasonable person when it comes to exams and grading. He won't trick you, the expectations are always crystal clear. He's easily the best professor I've ever had.

Robbie is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He explains the material so well and answers every question thrown at him without ever making someone feel dumb. The course was a little tough, but with his help, it was doable. Please take him for any course you need to, you will not regret it.

I've never been good at math, and I didn't ever take calculus in high school, so this class was difficult but Robbie made it all worth it. He is so kind, such a great person, explained everything so well, and really prepared us for the exams. I felt like I could actually do math for the first time in my life.

ROBBIE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD!! Calculus sucks and it was not an easy class, but I'd take all my classes from Robbie if I could. He isn't always on time for office hours, but he is willing to stay late to make up for it. He knows what he's doing and is great at answering questions. It's easy to see him as a person, not just a prof.

Super engaging lecturer and you could tell that he really cared about the class. Attendance is not mandatory, but GO TO THE TA RECITATION. The recitation groups are small and the time with the TA is very helpful in getting the homework done.

lectures were good, never understood content very quickly but others seemed to. Got our first test grade back a week before the final so not ideal. Had him for 112 and he was much better. Still would take again and would recommend taking him over other teachers.

By far one of the best professors I've ever had. If I could take every math class from Robbie I would. Tests are completely fair and not tricky. As long as you study you will do well! He knows every concept super thoroughly and answers any questions until you understand. Also cares enormously about his students and the world around him. 12/10!

Robbie was an amazing professor, super awesome guy. Super good at teaching, but sometimes glances over some things if he thinks you already know about it, so make sure to ask questions! Super funny, and was able to keep the class entertained and engaged the entire class. Loved him!
I love Robbie's teaching style. He is super fair and only tests on things he covered. He has very clean boardwork and explains concepts clearly.

Robbie always taught in a super clear way. He let you know what would be on the exams, and since the homework could be rather challenging the tests were easy. He would never put annoying trick questions on exams that would maybe be mentioned once in class. Don't take DiffEq from anyone else if you can! He is by far the best of the professors.

INCREDIBLE. Very fair, inspirational, real and genuine, I truly have come to love math because of Robbie. This class is tricky but he teaches it in a way that is easier to understand. Homework was harder than the tests so I always felt prepared. Tests were very fair and he prepares you well. I would recommend Robbie to anyone!!

Robbie was a joy to learn calculus from. I'm someone who usually struggles with math and he made the content digestible and made the lectures the highlights of my week. You can tell he cares about his students and creates an environment of mutual respect and honesty.

I took AP Calculus in high school but didn't pass the test. This class was perfect for giving me that credit I needed. I showed up probably 2 times and got a B. Everything is pretty much online. I missed some tests but Robbie was super chill and let me take them later. He's amazing.
Robbie gives amazing lectures and teaches very clearly. He's always ready to explain different ideas in multiple ways so that it gets to every student.

In the grand scheme of things, Robbie is a great teacher. I REALLY didn't care for his soap-box moments but if you came to learn math you will learn math. Excellent at making sure you can understand complex topics.

Dr. Snellman is a compassionate and straight-forward teacher. He teaches exactly what you need to know and is always looking to improve as a teacher. He is humble and down-to-earth. I totally recommend taking calc from him. He breaks things down to steps everyone can follow.

Calc is hard no matter what, but Robbie was my favorite professor I have ever had! He was so accessible to the students, would try to make lectures as interesting as possible and always tried to show us the real world application. If you're going to take calc, take it from Robbie!!

great teacher who clearly puts himself in the shoes of his students in preparation for classes, when giving homework, and creating tests. I thought the class was as easy as a calculus class could be. He gives around 6 assignments a week with opportunities to go over these problems in twice a week recitations. Great class and again, great teacher.

Robbie Snellman is nothing short of amazing! He's interesting, funny, and engaging - everything you can ask for in a professor. He explains complicated calculus in a simple understandable way. Robbie is also open with the class about his mental health struggles, and has shared his strong testimony with us. Easily one of the best professors at BYU!

Robbie is the best! I took 352 during the Summer Term and he did a great job of explaining the material. He didn't assign tons of homework, but just enough so you could understand and do well on the exams. Robbie is super caring! I wish he taught all the math classes!

If you have to take calc take from Professor Snellman. Attendance was not mandatory but lectures were engaging and super helpful so I tried to never miss. Homework due six days a week but the assignments weren't too long. He seems to really care about his students and is super nice and willing to answer questions.

Robbie is an amazing professor. He genuinely cares about the success and learning of his students. He is incredibly knowledgeable and his lectures are organized and easy to follow. He provides a huge array of tools to help you succeed, including TA recitations. I recommend going to those even if you think you know the material for the practice.

Robbie obviously cares about his students and what he does, and he is completely willing to answer questions. I really liked Robbie. His lectures were very amazing and engaging and always took time to answer questions. I would definitely take any class I could from Robbie!

I had never taken Calculus before and Robbie did a great job teaching the material. There is homework due everyday except for Sunday. Even though that is annoying it made me really learn the materials. Recitation was also really useful to figuring everything out.

This guy is super caring and taught well! Calculus 2 is a beast no matter who you take it with, but with Robbie, it was fine. Watch his reviews for the test, and go to TA recitations.
