Robbie is an amazing professor. He really cares about what he teaches, and he cares about the students. This class is intense and hard, but Robbie helps a lot. It's important to do all the readings and homework. If you put in the effort, it's not too bad.

Fantastic prof. He's an awesome guy in addition to being a great teacher. He's really good at explaining difficult concepts simply. Very understanding and straightforward. I'll take all of my math classes from him if I can. Assignments are written and online, and tests are simple and go over what you learned in class.
Amazing professor. He is personable and can explain concepts in many different ways. He gives good motivating examples. He also hosted reviews and wanted you to succeed.

Robbie is Awesome! His class was the first math class I've ever taken, and I spend all day wishing I was back in Calc 2. He knows so much, and gives TONS of outside material. The man cares, and knows how to rein the class back in whenever we lose focus. There were times I was going on 2 hours of sleep and the man helped to focus. A real one fo sho.
You can tell Robbie cares about his students. He will respond to emails and answer any questions you have.

Best math professor I've ever had. Robbie really cares about his students and goes above and beyond with accessible notes as well as pre-class lecture videos with examples that tie in perfectly with the class. I'm now in my 4th math class at byu (math 334) and I wish that I could have taken every math class with him.
Robbie is the best math teacher Ive had. He made Calc 2 very easy despite a lot of people saying its hard. He is very fair and understanding. Really good guy.

Robbie is by far the best professor I've ever had. If you have the chance to take a class from him and you don't, you've sold yourself short. He's honest, caring, and will answer your questions to the best of his ability. Don't get me wrong, the material is tough, but he'll do his best to help you understand the concepts and succeed in his class.

The nature of what Robbie teaches is hard but he makes a consistent effort to help his students. The class is quick paced but if you keep up you will be just fine. He is well respected by students and for good reason. He provides useful material for tests! His class is straight forward and he doesn't try to fail you if you put in the work to learn.

Lowkey Robbie is one of the best teachers I've ever had. You can tell he is very passionate about what he does, and he is very very good at it. He knows the material inside and out and he is ready for any question. He explains things so clearly, and is just a chill guy that cares a lot about his students. Take any class you can from Robbie.

Robbie really cares about each and every one of his students. Its really amazing to see a professor desire to connect with his students the way Robbie did. He also helped to explain the class topics really well. The homework load is a lot but its manageable and Robbie helps to explain hard concepts too. Overall, his class was one of my favorites.

For the first time in my life I was excited to show up to a math class. Robbie challenges the norms and shows that math can be done differently. He is very concise, actually cares, and teaches with astounding clarity. Provides a plethora of exam review material and hosts review sessions. Calc is a beast, Robbie will help you tame it.

Robbie is not here to play games but he really does have students' wellbeing at heart. A wonderful guy, but if you do the bare minimum assignments you are going to have a rough time. Like C+ rough time lol.

I learned a lot from Dr. Snellman. He's very kind, explains the material clearly, and is easy to follow. One of the tests we took had an erroneous question and Dr. Snellman assured us that he would make sure we got all the points on that question since it was a mistake. He cares about his students and is passionate about math.

Robbie is a great teacher. He ALWAYS answers questions and you can tell he really cares. He explains things well. That being said, this class is HARD. Especially if you havent taken a math class in a while. This class is a lot of work and is fast paced. My GPA took a hit from this class, but Id totally recommend taking it from Robbie! He's great!

Best math professor I've ever had. Hard class, my GPA suffered, but he is so caring towards students. Takes time before class to focus on the positive. Hated the class and work, LOVED the professor. The class tanked my GPA but he is a great professor the class work is just overwhelming at times

I loved having Robbie as a teacher. He explains things clearer and differently than has other teachers. Favorite teacher so far. Even in a huge 400+ online class, he ALWAYS clarified and helped when somebody asked a question. He's also a very nice person. Robbie is the best math teacher I've ever had. While it is a tough class, Robbie clearly explains the material and if you have a question he takes time to answer it. I chose Professor Snellman because of all of these glowing reviews, but I did not have this experience with him. His class felt really hard to follow, he acted really cocky, and I barely got a C-... I didn't miss a single lecture, did all homework, and this class tanked my GPA. He might be better in-person instead of online.

Robbie is amazing, incredibly caring for all of his students. Even in a class with 400+ students, he gives caring time to each person who asks a question. He designs his courses VERY well, he has really put in a lot of work so that his students have all the resources they need, including lecture videos, notes, etc.

Best professor I have ever had. Cares about his students and takes time to answer questions, even in a large class. I didn't use the textbook, relying on lectures and videos he provides, though you will need to buy it to access the grading program. Tests were moderately difficult, but fair. Lectures were engaging and taught material well

Took Math 112 with Robbie. I did not have a professor that understood his students so well. Very respectable teacher always giving support and help in areas that I (and other students needed). Robbie is without a doubt the best the BYU Math Department has to offer! Grades are extremely homework dependant and if you skip them you won't pass. If you want to learn to love math, this is it!

You sign up for 5 days of class. 3 is lecture with Robbie and 2 is TA recitation. On the days of lecture, there is an in-class quiz that you need to complete. Robbie a well-respected professor and is optimistic and tries to encourage us to be too. He explains where certain equations come from and it's really helpful to understand the math concepts.
Professor Snellman is simply the best at BYU. If you don't take calc from him you done messed up.

I took AP calc in high school and it would have been way more work without that background. But Robbie explains things in a really clear way and really wants his students to understand the material. in a remote class, I felt like lecture was interrupted frequently by questions that could be answered in recitation. But I fully recommend Robbie!!

I mean.. it's calculus, so it definitely wasn't my favorite class, but Robbie is probably one of my favorite professors of all time. Even with 400 other students, he makes people feel like they are capable and can conquer the beast that is calculus. If you have to take this class TAKE IT FROM HIM!! You won't regret it!!

Robbie is an extreme kind professor who explains Calculus well. If you don't understand, he will gladly reexplain the concept or problem respectfully and in a new way which will help you understand. He is the best math teacher I have ever had and would recommend him to anyone and everyone.

This man has a difficult class to teach. Math 112 is not the easiest, but Robbie teaches this class and makes it 10 times easier. Yes there is a decent amount of homework, but this man really cares about you. He does not squander the time in class, and he prepares you for the tests. You still have to earn your grade, but Robbie makes it manageable.

Robbie has very engaging lectures, he's is accommodating and accessible outside of class. The only complaint I have is a few times he didn't know how to do some of the homework problems. Incredible material, has already had carry over to my software engineering job.

Best professor I have ever had. He cares so much about his students. He makes videos and does practice problems for every concept throughout the class. He makes the most difficult topics understandable. He wants his students to succeed and does everything he can to help them. His tests clearly reflect material from class. He's the best!

Robbie is literally the greatest professor I have ever had. He is so knowledgeable and takes time to answer each students questions. He provides multiple real-world examples for each concept we learn. I can't recommend him enough!
cool beans.

Robbie is 10/10. Calculus is hard and you will put in effort, but he makes class worth it. With online classes he really tries to make sure we can get the help we need. He always records lectures and other videos to help with the homework. It is obvious he cares about his students and how they are doing. Definitely take a class from him if you can!

Robbie was amazing! Stellar growth mindset, gave outstanding lectures, is very, very concerned about student learning. Is super relatable and loves math and teaching. Only beef was a bit of a mixup b/t LearningSuite and his syllabus that caused confusion about which assignments were to be dropped, but it felt like a one-timer. Love him, 10/10.

Robbie is the best thing to have happened to BYU math. He seriously cares and doesn't suffer from 'The Curse of the Expert.' His knowledge of math is vast, but his pedagogical skill surpasses it. He is very clear in explaining difficult concepts. Best professor I've had at BYU.

Robbie is the best math teacher I've ever had, and on top of that he is an amazing person. He wears his heart on a sleeve and tells you straight how things are working, but he cares deeply about you. He also is a big cyclist which is awesome. His lectures are super helpful in understanding calc and the tests are tough but fair. Definitely take him!

Great person & teacher. Yes, there were moments in the semester where the material was confusing, but Robbie wants you to do well. This was his 2nd time teaching Num Theory, so I'm sure the next time he'll be even better. Take him!

Robbie cares more about his students than any professor I've had. He added extra office hours midway through the semester and was always willing to help out. He is always well prepared for class and went out of his way to find examples of the concepts we were learning. I would highly recommend taking any class Robbie teaches.

He is the best math professors I have ever had. He can explain difficult concepts in a way that you are able to understand it almost intuitively. If you go to his office hours, he is always willing to help with homework or talk about pretty much anything. If you have the option to take a class from him, do so. You will not regret it.

Robbie is just a wonderful professor. Number Theory can be a technical subject but his (very neat and organized) lecture style made it easy to follow. He's also one of the most caring people you'll meet--he makes a special effort to lighten up homework around midterms so that you're not super overwhelmed. Overall one of the best teachers I've had!

Robbie is by far the best math professor I have ever had! He is kind, helpful, and explains things in easy to understand ways. The class I took was linear algebra, and he was super helpful with the concepts. He's also rather funny, and has great stories that don't get in the way of his teaching. I definitely would want him to be my teacher again.

Robbie is one of the most amazing math professors at BYU. He is clear and he teaches at a good pace. He always makes sure our questions are answered and is super down to earth. I was terrified of linear algebra but he made it so easy to understand! He is also always willing to meet with you if you need extra help understanding the material

Dr. Snellman has been the most effective math teacher I've ever had. He creates a safe class environment, encourages questions, and has a gift for explaining difficult concepts in easily-understandable terms. He also really knew the "so what" behind the material. He has a gift for connecting with students and gave us confidence to succeed in math.

Robbie is the man! He loves and cares so much for his students. He is really inspiring. Im pretty sure hes willing to do anything in his power to make sure you succeed. The labs arent required, but I found them very helpful. Take any and all classes that you can from Robbie. Hes the best math teacher Ive ever had.

Robbie is one of the best math teachers I've ever had. He cares about every student in his class and gives them every chance to get help. His lectures were always interesting and clear. I never left class confused. If he is teaching a class you need to take, take it from him.

One of, if not the, best math teachers I've ever had. Truly cares so much about his students and it shows in his lectures. He's not scared to be real with life discussions. He understands how difficult college is and he's willing to work with you. Fast response via email. He understands that math isn't most people's favorite, but he loves it.

Great guy. He really cares about the students and their learning. I ended with a grade higher than I expected because of him. He is also very clear in teaching concepts. His office hours are also very helpful. Highly recommend

Robbie is the best! He broke his jaw at the beginning of the class, but came in a few days after surgery because he felt that somebody needed him to be there! I absolutely loved his class. He is the best professor ever! He will also help outside of class. He is the most down to earth person I have met. He really wants us to be successful!

Robbie is amazing! He broke his jaw a few days before classes started and he wasn't supposed to come in for a few weeks but he came in to teach after 2 days because he cares about his students so much. He prioritizes students and fights for us when it comes to midterms and the final. The homework is helpful and reasonable, and lectures are great!

One of the best professors out there! Robbie cares so much about his students and I am not just saying that. He gives you ample opportunities to succeed in the class and is very flexible with his office ours. He puts the students needs above his own.

Best professor I have ever had. He understood that beginning calculus can be difficult at first so he really worked with us to make sure we understood. Most caring person I know. If you put your time and effort into this class, and with the help of the professor, this class should be one that you can succeed in.

Robbie was my absolute favorite teacher at BYU. I took Math 112 as well as Math 313 from him, which was so lucky. He cares so much about his students, takes every question seriously, answers emails quickly, is so willing to help in his office hours, and never misses an opportunity to inspire his student. Recommend 100%. It is hard, but worth it.

I bit off more than I could chew last semester and fell very behind in Robbie's class. He was very understanding and gave me many opportunities to make up my grades. I never left his class confused, and I wish I had utilized his office hours more, because he was always helpful and available. Fantastic professor.

Robbie is an amazing math professor. He is so organized and no question is a dumb question. You always feel comfortable in his class asking questions if you don't understand something, even when you feel like everyone else gets it. If he doesn't have time to help you out in class, he's got great office hours and will work with you 'til you get it.

The Math Professors at BYU are all pretty great in my opinion, but Robbie is probably the best. He's very good at relating with students and makes math fun, interesting, and silly at the same time. How many people can say Linear Algebra was their favorite class so far? I'm one of them.

Robbie is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. His teaching style is clear and coherent. He is an amazing teacher if you want to master the topic, or if you just want enough understanding to pass. He cares a lot about his students (and people in general) and will do a lot to help them succeed. I highly recommend him to everybody!

Robbie is definitely the most FANTASTIC professor I've ever had. His lectures are clear, easy to follow, and entertaining. He's inspirational and approachable and you can tell he cares about his students and wants us to do well in the class. He even held an extra final review session just for his class. I wish all my teachers were more like Robbie!

If the other reviews haven't convinced you yet, know that you are getting the cream of the crop with Robbie as your professor. I haven't met a professor who genuinely cares about his students like him.

Robbie (you can just call him Robbie), is literally the best teacher I've eve had. He teaches the concepts in such a simple way. Calculus has never been so easy. He encourages students and is extremely approachable. I would give him 10 out of 5 if I could. I want him to teach all my courses, math or not math.

I understood Professor Snellman and what he lectured on almost always which is a big deal when it comes to math. He is clear, precise, and doesn't waste time. He also doesn't rush through if someone has a question. He is very honest and open, and I admire him a lot.

Robbie is an incredible professor, one of the best math professors I have ever had. He cares about the students and wants them all to succeed. He is understanding and relates well to all the students. He explains topics clearly and makes them easy to understand. He is an incredible person and professor. Highly recommend, you will not regret it.
Great professor! Genuinely cares about his students and if they are learning.

Robbie is really a one of a kinda type of guy. He cares more about his students than almost any professor I have ever seen. His lectures are entertaining and will keep you awake. He is able to evaluate your question, see where you're coming from, and answer it extremely quickly. HE WRITES SO QUICKLY, just be warned. He'll fight for his students.

Robbie is the coolest Math Teacher out there. Hes young so he connects well with the students and reads his class so well that he can see when a new topic is hard to understand. Genuine and down to earth he even offers extra credit. If you take ANY type of math class, see if he teaches it

Robbie genuinely cares about his students and their success. He explains concepts in such a way that makes you feel like you could teach them yourself! Rather than just giving steps to memorize, Robbie really helps his students understand the why behind the steps they are taking. If you can take from Robbie, do it!! You will not regret it.

MY ABSOLUTE FAVORITE PROF!!! Robbie is incredible. He is always willing to help, makes tough concepts seem simple and he really wants everyone to be successful. He is so much more than just a teacher. TAKE THIS CLASS YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT!!!!

I never do this, but Robbie literally is the BEST in every way possible. Couldn't have asked for a more stellar guy. He teaches clearly and inspires everyone to do hard things. I honestly don't have enough good things to say about Robbie. He is an inspiration and made hard material understandable. Don't think twice, take Calc from Robbie!

Robbie really cares for his students. He really wants you to succeed not only in his class, but also in life. He wants students to talk to him not only for math but also personal help. The first midterm Robbie was really mad with the graders so he gave us extra credit to make up for it. He knows the struggle of a student and really wants to help.

Tied with the best math teacher I've ever had. Great at explaining difficult concepts in simple ways and very inspirational as well. Not only did he make me want to be a better student but a better person. You don't find teachers like him often, I give him my highest recommendation hands down!

Robbie is hands down the best math teacher I have ever had . He explains concepts clearly and questions are always welcomed. He also has a great relationship with his students and you can definitely tell that he cares for each of them and wants them to succeed. I would 100% take another class taught by him again.

You can tell that Robbie really cares for his students and wants them to succeed, not just in math but in life in gernal. He explains things very clearly and is always more than willing to help you out outside of class. He's also pretty funny, has interesting lectures, and is pretty relatable.

This guy. Just the best. He is a super humble guy and is not obsessed with himself. He wont assume that you understand math like he does, but will explain every concept simply and clearly. He makes efforts to know his students by name and he LOVES questions in class. His main goal is always to make sure students feel confident in the material.

Robbie is amazing. He does an incredible job of explaining math in laymans terms. Hes driven to help every one of his students succeed, and it shows every time he teaches. He really inspires his students to succeed not only in math, but in life.

Robbie is the best math teacher I have ever had. He took a challenging subject and taught it to my understanding. He makes sure to teach about applications of linear algebra and makes it relative to the real world.

He does a really good job teaching linguistics. He makes the topic fun and applicable to learning how to better communicate. He cares about the course and wants to help us better understand the language. Tests could be challenging, but I don't think they were unfair. The topics came together in some cool ways by the end.

He understands the assignment of teaching returned missionaries.  We talked about culture, grammar, tidied up some skills we learned on the mission, and mostly just talked and joked around every class about the homework material.  Interesting readings, they require some translating for weird words, but three credits? It felt more like 2 credits.

Profe Strong is cool, but at times it was difficult to get an answer about the grammar from him. Granted they are difficult concepts but sometimes the answer would just be "yeah I don't know either that's just the grammar". Besides that good professor and it wasn't a hard class. Tests are really hard to go over though, they're under lock and key.

SPAN321 is the go-to post mission class so you're gonna ace it anyway, but Profe Strong always makes things super fun and interesting. I always enjoyed going to class. Tests are big but nothing you can't handle. There's a good amount of homework, make sure to stay on top of it. It is really easy to get an A in this class, he wants you to enjoy it.

In this class, Professor Strong goes over the basics of Spanish linguistics. You'll need to be in class and copy down all the notes in order to do well on tests. He's a very nice teacher and tries to make the subject as fun as it can be.

Great guy, but WORST teacher I've had. He's very disorganized, does nothing to help prepare you for exams, and is super picky with grading free response tests. Lectures and notes are a must, but they are SUPER BORING and it's just him talking for 2 hrs. There are few graded items, and an A is luck more than effort. DO NOT TAKE! You are warned.

Overall, a really great guy, but this class is not like other spanish classes. You'll have to study hard. If you know his notes really well, the exams are doable, but they are mostly open response and you really have to know your stuff. His teaching style is hard for some people to follow, but just know the notes. Tests are weighted heavily!!
Take notes!! Hardly any homework in this class, but the tests can be hard, so study those notes regularly. He is a very caring and kind man. He will treat you fairly and wants the best for you.

Prof Strong is incredibly likable. He gives no homework (seriously, zero) all semester, but 5 quizzes, 3 fairly easy assignments, and 1 final exam form your entire grade. If you take notes in class and test well, this will be an easy A. If not, buena suerte.

Professor Strong was one of my favorite Spanish professors I've had at BYU. I found his Spanish 326 class to be very helpful in improving my pronunciation and accent. Quizzes and final are easy if you study based on his study guides. Attend lecture, pay attention, and you will be just fine. Loved this class!

Profe Strong has great lectures and is funny! He does write what he is saying. Maybe it takes more time, but it makes it easier to understand. The textbook is helpful, but he goes over everything in class, so it is more like an extra resource. He did not give midterms - more like quizzes that were pretty simple. Also gives lots of helpful examples.

It would save Prof. and the students a lot of time if he had slides made in advance instead of writing notes on the whiteboard every time. Attendance matters, but you can technically ace the test w/o going to class & by filling out the study guide from reading the textbook. I feel that he didn't adapt well into online-instruction. But he is caring.

An awesome, funny, and sincere guy who loves Spanish. It's just that the class itself is a beast and he doesn't do a great job of organizing Learning Suite to make the class easier to follow. MUST study well for the tests or you will fail them (just ask me about my 2nd midterm. I did ace the final though). Pay attention and you shall be fine.

Love Prof Strong! He's hilarious, ALWAYS available to help. Meet with him if you don't understand. Grades on exams and a final project, no assignments. Go to lecture to learn all material, if you stay for reviews and complete the study guide (and study normal amount) tests aren't bad at all. Textbook helps a LOT! Reasonable class, no extra homework

(I took him for COMMS 304 which wasn't listed). Robert Walz has experience in journalism and teaches media law. The course includes weekly case studies, reading quizzes, a required textbook, and a group project. There is no attendance requirement except for the final. Lectures cover the material and follow the assigned readings.

This was a weird class. You'll get an A but you won't learn a thing. He wants you to use AI instead of learning skills and he doesn't actually have the skills that he's teaching. He wanted to do our group project (filming and editing a video) himself instead of letting us do it. He is a nice guy but take the class from someone else if you can.

This class is taught online and Professor Walz has some videos. The concepts he teaches are great and you learn about some of the major world religions and how they are connected with media. The content itself is interesting and not too hard, and make sure to keep up on the readings.

Loved this class and love Bro. Walz! I'm a comms minor and was nervous to take a 400-level class but it was super doable! Lots of reading but you can kinda skim. Weekly optional webinar that I loved. Same general format each week. One midterm and final. Bro. Walz is super passionate about this topic and made it so interesting! Highly recommend!

My favorite professor at BYU. So helpful, funny, and easy to get along with. I was excited to go to his classes, which is rare for me. The material was fascinating, he makes it super fun, and everyone loved him. I would take every class from him if I could. Do yourself a favor and take his class if you're in the comms major!

Prof. Walz was good. The class itself isn't too hard to pass--show up to class, take notes, and do your readings. Quizzes were hard-ish, make sure you pay attention while you read. Main issue with the Professor is he has a right-wing bias that is VERY evident in his teaching. Misinformation often spread in class. Still, not too hard.

Brother Walz is the best! He's one of those professors you're happy to see on campus. He wants his students to succeed inside & out of his classroom. He keeps things chill & is very understanding & accommodating to his students based on their needs. He strives to make the material applicable to students of varying interests & majors.

Borther Walz is probably my favorite comms professor at BYU. He makes you work for your grade--take assignments back to him to fix and get full credit if you need!! Be persistent haha. He knows what he is teaching and does so in a dynamic way. This class will definitely prepare you to work in the real world. Also, he is hilarious.

Super easy class overall. DO NOT PROCRASTINATE THE PROJECT. If you do, it's still possible to pass with a good grade, but you may die from the stress. He is SUPER funny. Lectures are all hilarious. Go to them if only to listen to a million excellent jokes.

Walz is the man. He gives INCREDIBLY helpful feedback on every assignment. He has you work on every assignment in class and no homework at all (and when you're done you can leave). There are quizzes you have to take online every single class but you can get them all done in advance. Seriously a great class for a great grade. Offers extra credit

He is a great professor. I only have one complaint and that is I'm an athlete and missing class nearly kills you! We have daily quizzes in class and missing them hurts your grade pretty bad. Attendance is crucial. I really enjoy going to class though because I think the content is easy to understand and interesting. And the tests are easy as cake.

I love professor Waltz, I was per-advertising but he made it all so interesting that I started thinking seriously about Journalism as well. I loved all parts of it! He was super helpful in Labs as well :)

Brother Walz is entertaining, funny, and a pretty easy professor. It's refreshing to have a class where I can relax and still learn valuable information. There are only two tests throughout the semester, and the lab assignments are fun and easy and you get lots of TA help! Definitely take!

Professor Walz is hands down my favorite teacher so far at BYU. He really does care about your grade, and wants you to get an A. The tests are a breeze as long as you know the study guide. Coming to class is mandatory because of daily quizzes, but it is a great class, and duh, if you're enrolled in school, you should expect to have to go to class.
Fantastic Class and Professor. Really knows how to get the most out of you. Really cares that you learn what will be most helpful to you as you try to get a job. Pretty easy as well

LOVED Professor Walz. If you want to be any kind of journalist (or even if you don't), take this class. Super interesting. He was a reporter for KSL so he has all kinds of experience. I want to take as many classes as I can from him!

Bro. Walz is a BOSS! Take his class. Attendance is mandatory w/ daily quizzes, but he makes it fun. Former Reporter, so he has fun stories/experiences. Labs can be tough, but plenty of help available. I didn't read one chapter in the book & got an A-. So much extra credit stuff you can ace this class easy.
Professor Walz cares about his students!! He would set up a private appointment with you if you need help. He wants and helps everyone to pass and get A.

Brother Walz is the best! He has experience as a TV News reporter, so he really knows what the business is like and what they're looking for. As a person, he is awesome. He is funny and carefree. He gave us all of the answers to the final! He wants everyone to get an A and cares about his students. Take it from him!

Bro Walz is so chill. There is no busy work and he's really helpful. But he MEANS it when he says start the final project at the beginning of the semester. If you wait to the last minute, you won't make it.

Professor Walz cares more about his students and their desires than any other professor. Extremely passionate about reporting, motivates you to work harder. Class important to attend you'll learn a ton and want to be there anyways.

I really enjoyed Brother Walz. He has interesting stories and is a very personable, funny guy. There are a handful of essays, which are pretty easy and graded easily too. He gives you the material that will be on the tests so those aren't too hard either. There are quizzes every day which are hard (class average usually 6/10) but he curves them

BEST professor for Comms. Seriously, take his class. You won't have the full BYU Communications experience unless you take from Prof. Walz! He knows what he's talking about, and he loves what he does, so you really can learn a lot. He's a die-hard reporter and that's what you want in a professor. TAKE IT!

He was a great teacher with a lot of experience and gave lots of real life examples. He got people from the major to talk in class. Class isn't mandatory and the final is a PIECE OF CAKE, but go to all the labs because that is where you make/edit projects.

He has been my favorite Professor so far. Although the class is easy I actually learned a ton and wanted to be in the Broadcast Program even more. Its a great environment. He also gives opportunities to Job Shadow him when he is Reporting for ABC 4 news.  And he looks like David Bowie.

this was the easiest class ever. we just watched movies. Walz cares about Communications and Communications students, which is a refreshing change from other teachers. However, you don't learn a whole lot from the class. grading system was unclear, but I got an A anyways. Definitely recommend

I was not looking forward to this class but it ended up being awesome! Walz is the best! You watch a lot of movies and write basic papers. You do research that takes time but Walz makes it soooo much more enjoyable than other professors. Walz actually cares about comms students, unlike some department chairs! If you can, take this class from Walz!

I don't know who said he's hot, but thats weird. Anyways, the class is ridiculously easy. It's EXTREMELY basic, which I guess I understand, but it was really redundant for me. He gives a review before the final going over EVERYTHING on the test and it's open notes, so there is really no need to read the book or even go to class besides your lab.

He was the greatest teacher ever! And his assignments were fun and his lectures were interesting.  Basically all you have to do is go to class and take notes.  He uses the book for online quizzes but I never read the book and did just fine.  He also gives you all the questions and answers to the final if you just go to the class where he reviews al

LOVE HIM!!!  Prof. Walz is the greatest instructor for broadcasting!  So easy and a fun class.  Love going to his class and participating in his lectures.  What you do in class is very useful. Highly recommend him.

Prof Walz is a freelance broadcast reporter who loves what he does and knows how to teach it, along with other Communications fields. He is a bit unorganized sometimes and runs through slides fast, but he explains concepts with good examples and the 2 hour class is entertaining enough that it doesn't drag on forever.

Take this class from Walz! Easiest class ever and super enjoyable. Quizzes, midterm and final are all on Blackboard and open note. Group project was easy and fun. My only complaint is that sometimes the quizzes wouldn't be posted on time and sometimes he went through the slides super quick. No big deal, though, you'll still get an A.

Professor Walz was awesome!! Not only was his class like super easy, but he was also very insightful and I learned a ton! All his quizzes and tests are open book and online, so nice! The group project is also so much fun (making your own website). Take a class from him! Easy A
great teacher. he teaches very well and easy to understand
ammazing teacher and funny you have to take him.

He refuses to grade my videos. I spent literaly hours on each one, turned them in, he took the CD, & lost it. Instead of telling me he can't find it, he gives me a B in th class, & I figure it out myself. So I call him, email him links to my vids online, he tells me he'll take care of it, but now, 4 months later, he still refuses to even look them!

This class can be a little hectic, but anyone in a comms major needs to be able to deal w/chaos. Br. Walz is great about working with circumstances. I learned a lot in this class ... it inspired me to aim for reporting. Br. Walz really encompasses every part of comms and is not overly demanding.

Br Walz is one of my favorite professors at BYU! Some may complain about the class being "disorganized", but it's actually taught in the organized chaos typical of a news station, so you see what lies ahead. Very helpful and so nice! He's clever and really cares about his students! He was great during his office hours, really willing to work w/you.

Bro. Walz's class was awesome!  One of the most enjoyable classes to be in. He teaches you but he is very entertaining. The class is really easy if you just go and try.  Quizzes and tests (we only had a final and 3 quizzes) are all open book/note.  I never used the books except for on the final which you take online. Great guy, kinda unorganized.

He really didnt seem like he knew what was going on. The quizzes and tests are all on black board and are super easy, you can use you notes. He seems very unorganized, and it almost seems like he just gives out grades at the end of the year depending your test scores.

If you do what you're suppose to you will get an A in this class, its as simple as that.  If you go to class you will know about all the assignments he cancels, all the due dates he postpones, and exactly what you need to know on the final. He's cool. The labs are frustrating but everyone goes through it, its not his fault. I would take him again.

I liked this class but it wasn't very structured as far as grades were concerned - nothing was posted to blackboard. He's really good about answering questions and making students feel at ease. He dropped one of our packages when all of the comps. in the Avid lab got infected with a virus, so that was nice :] I liked him as a prof.

Time consuming class!! Plan on about ten hours a week honestly in doing your stories for the Daily News...but other than that Walz is the man. Super cool and knowledgeable. Teaches you from experience on how to successfully be a reporter vs just reading what others said. Good professor.

Although mass communication is easy to understand, Prof. Walz conducted his class in a disorganized manner. Each week students are required to complete a quiz on assigned chapters.Prof. Walz failed numerous times to post this quiz on time. Overall, nice guy, easy class, but the inconsistency can make all the difference between an A and an A-.

Walz made the 2.5 hours go by so quickly! (plus a lot of times he let us out early) He was interesting and you can tell he loves what he does.  I found him to be a little unclear about some things but I loved how all our tests and quizzes were online.  That includes the final! I would recommend him any day!

This class was an easy A.  The professor, however, was not that great of a help. His sarcasm and attitude made him come across as self-centered.  He is also sloppy with grading- he doesn't update Blackboard and he even messed up a few of the students final grades.

Does a very good job showing me what a Television News reporter's job is like.  Very practical advice, good examples, and no useless material, or wasting time.  Lecture is easy, lab is very time consuming (10 hrs per week), but worthwhile.  If you hate 325, you'll probably hate being a TV news reporter.
All over the "entertainment" news, completely gimmicky, but doesn't really show you how news SHOULD be done. Broadcast went downhill when Paynter left...

Prof. Walz is a great teacher and he wants students to like him so the class is easy but you still learn a lot.  He is funny and class is entertaining.  He knows his stuff because he has been in the business for a long time.  Great class and easy A.

Prof. Walz is awesome. He's very nice, very fair, and very understanding. Also, he knows a lot about Broadcast Journalism. I loved going to his class. Just make sure you watch his news reports and you'll likely get a good grade on the current events tests.

I thought he was a great teacher. Took his once a week, two and a half hour night class...only went an hour and a half every time. Would cancel quizzes if students complained enough. Reading assignments every week that if you do you'll ace the quizzes. Tests are just repeated quiz questions. Easy, easy but still interesting and fun.
Brother Walz is AMAZING! His class was easy but the T.A was terrible.  Very bad at getting back with emial.  However, take it from Brother Walz. He is the BEST.
Best professor out there.
Really unhelpful.

Not helpful whatsoever, I don't exactly know how this guy even gets a paycheck for what little he does. He can't even send a Zoom link correctly. A rock could run this class with more efficiency. Don't take this class until they revise it unless you want to waste your time.

Nice guy, but take this class from someone else. He doesn't teach, has us debate in class. LOTS of busywork, lacks instructions. The semester ends in less than 2 weeks and he hasn't graded a single assignment (how do I know what my final grade will be?). Gives no feedback, hard to know how you do on assignments. Class runs long every time.

Easy class, just a lot of busywork. Amazing funny teacher. He is willing to help the engaged, genuine student. Sometimes he takes a sec to grade things so that stressed me out a little but overall it was easy.

He is fantastic. I absolutely love the guy! He is so funny, and by the end of the semester our class felt like a mini family! He even invited the whole class to his house for dinner one night and then go to the temple after and it counted for a main project! He is so fantastic and fr, take his class trust me on this one.

The class was mainly readings and then discussions during class. You can't miss the readings cause he'll ask what you thought of them. Don't be late to class either or he might mark you tardy depending on the day. But he made the class fun and spiritual too, if you're going to take SPAN 321 take it from this guy.

This class was very decent. I thought the lectures were ok, but he barely taught grammar and almost no vocabulary. If there was a new grammar principle we went over it for one class period then never again. When asking questions he wouldn't really give any context to what he's asking about and just say your name. Decent guy but class was uncomfy

I LOVE LOVE LOVE PROFESSOR MORALES!! I recommend him to EVERYONE. He is by far my favorite teacher that I have ever had. I was extremely nervous for this class, but he made it so fun. By the end of the semester, your class is like family. Spanish gave me so much anxiety before; now I feel confident. He is a genuinely great person. TAKE IT FROM HIM.

Profe Morales is GREAT! He's so funny and his class is so much fun to go to. All of the classwork is really lowkey, a couple small writing assignments and tests that are pretty straightforward. He brought us donuts on halloween. He cares about us and made a point to get to know us. The class was never stressful. Take Morales!!

I felt pretty unprepared for the tests, I was also told that he wasn't going to take attendance, but then my grade dropped for missing a few classes. The course material wasn't very hard, just make sure you read all the poems/stories, because that is what you'll be tested on.

Ok this class is the easiest thing ever but Prof Morales was not helpful. He does not communicate with students very well and he made life much harder than it shouldve been. The online course had issues every week which is frustrating. If you want 3 easy A credits, take it but he might never respond if you ask him for help

Guys this class is not what you expect. There are no real lectures. Each week there was something wrong with Canva and whatever system they use to administer assignments so I would miss points here and there for no fault of my own. Professor tries but its just an overall worthless class. A waste of 3 credits.

Roberto Morales is really caring. This class (for the medical professions) was really easy. You do assignments that are super easy. This is an online class, so Professor Morales did not physically teach us, but he did weekly zooms. He is very understanding and works with you if you have questions or issues. Overall, this class was great!

Honestly was pretty excited for this class, Spanish for Medical Professions, but I've never been more let down in my life. Nothing against the professor since this class has no lectures. You read the textbook and take a quiz. Every week. That's it. There's an occasional presentation or paper but no learning whatsoever. WORST CLASS EVER. DO NOT TAKE

Someone who took this class told me material's easy & professor's a nice guy, but VERY disorganized. We're a month in & this last point's so true I'm already rating him. Syllabus & LearningSuite contradict each other, students ask him about assignments after almost every class (b/c unclear). Gives avg of rough & final drafts as final score- weird.
Top hat is the worst. Wouldnt recommend taking Spanish from him as the new Spanish textbook is horrible and I felt I didnt really learn a lot. Very nice guy though

Mr. "El guapisimo" Morales seems strict and military cut throat at first but he's really a chill professor. Don't be afraid to mess around a little and have little fun in the class. Funny dry humour type of guy. Take advantage of asking him questions since he is very knowledgable as well

Profesor Morales seems like a stickler the first few days of class but he really is super fun! Just do your work on time and check both the syllabus and learning suite because sometimes stuff just pops up. We had a class activity where we went to a Spanish endowment session and then had Ecuadorian food and honestly that made the class worth it

Profesor Morales is great! I was intimidated by him at the beginning but he was actually very caring and was just looking out for all of us ;) the class is mostly grammar, and there are two presentations. He isnt super organized with how he runs things, but he kind of lets you take the reins and if you use your common sense, you will do well.

Prof. Morales's class was so fun. He is really friendly and by the end of the semester the class was almost like a family. He invited us to his house to eat Ecuadorian food for extra credit! Like?????? If you do your homework and turn in the assignments, you'll do great in the class. He is not forgiving about late work, however, so don't get lazy.

Senor Morales is the most caring professor I have ever had- he invited us to a barbecue at his house! However, be prepared for him to ask you about your dating life in the middle of class. Class homework load was super light- about 20-30 minutes, 3 times per week.
He wants to see you succeed and offers a lot of extra credit. There is a lot of participation.
Professor morales means business. He is a nice guy but can seem pretty strict sometimes. He was willing to work with you if you need help, and he does really care about his students.

Profesor Morales is a great teacher. He has a great sense of humor and really cares about students, and wants them to do well. He likes do things his way at all possible--the Spanish Department kind of annoys him--and I really liked that. Some Spanish teachers just want to prove their students they don't know Spanish, but he's not like that at all.

Dr. Hancock is a great teacher! He moves quickly but cares deeply about the success of his students. He will always take time to answer questions and help the concepts make sense. Dr. Hancock prioritizes the actual learning over the assignments. This means that you have to take a more active role in learning. Ask questions. Dr. Hancock is amazing!

Dr. Hancock is so talented and is great for piano lessons. He is very knowledgeable about music, so pick his brain. If there are three things he particularly loves, they're Rachmaninov, Broadway and Film Scores, and duets.

If you're taking a different class than theory, go right ahead. He's very nice and wants you to get 100%, but I have not learned ANYTHING in class. He talks about related things, but doesn't actually employ a single understandable "teaching" skills. I'm leaching off of the schedule and reading from my friends in the other sections. We're way behind

You would literally have to be trying to get anything less than an A, he gives out 100%'s like candy. That being said, I felt like I learned more from doing the homework than from going to class. To be fair it was at 9am and I did skip class a lot, but the fact that that didn't even nick my grade tells you something

I LOVE DR HANOCK! TAKE HIM!!!!!! I probably would have dropped out if I had had anyone else. He is crucial to being able to live through all the required courses. He is the best human being ever. Take him now.
Professor Hancock is a phenomenal teacher and so talented!! His goal is to help us be our best!

He is very kind and cares about his students and it's an easy A. But I'm a visual learner and he expects you to just follow him has he plays on the piano and just talks about whatever he is doing. There is no organization to his teaching. You can pass his class but not learn anything.

Dr. Hancock was absolutely fantastic. Very kind and considerate. He gave great feedback and advice, and was concerned about helping his students progress as individuals. He spent time getting to know me so that he could help me achieve MY goals. He's an amazing man, and he definitely earned my respect, both as a musician and a professor.

Dr. Hancock is an amazing person! I looked forward to my music theory class every day. If you are someone who really struggles with music theory, you might want to take from someone else. In this class we do a lot of fun things, but we don't go over the theory in depth as much unless someone asks a question.
He really knows his stuff. If you have a question during class he will take as much time as you need to help you understand.

I have really enjoyed taking piano lessons from Dr. H.  He is very interesting to talk to about music and the like.  He can really help you take your piano skills from great to excellent.  If you are willing to learn and be teachable you can learn a lot from him.

Professor Mortensen is one of the funniest professors I've ever met. She is very knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches and is strict about using correct grammar. She has a strong personality and is a phenomenal public speaker. You'll never have a dull moment in her class, highly recommend.

Bro. Cook is amazing. He loves philosophy, loves teaching and loves his students. He also doesn't treat the class like the center of attention. He lectures well, leads good discussions and has very clear grading criteria. If you try, not hard at all to get an A. Never even touched the textbook.
Class was just lectures, and I never did the readings. Overall a pretty easy class, but your grade is based mostly on just a few quizzes.
Brother Cook is seriously the best! Cannot recommend him more, very understanding and willing to work with his students.

This class was pretty easy. He will tell you, you need a textbook but he never references it in class so I wouldn't recommend getting it. You only have one assignment and its to write an essay that he makes you turn in a couple if drafts throughout the semester and gives feedback so they're super easy and a couple of midterms that are also easy.
The course is well organized .He is very passionate about the subject, encourages thoughtful discussion, and brings humor to class. He does a good job making philosophy engaging and approachable.

Prof. Cook taught such an enlightening class and was open minded and thoughtful. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches. The class was graded solely by tests and one large paper. The tests are easy and open note, and he gives extremely thorough feedback and lots of help throughout the process that makes the final paper very easy to write.

This class was amazing. I really liked the topic of the class. Unfortunately, the professor made it hard to want to come. Lectures were boring, paper was graded very harshly. There was no rubic for the paper and he would count off points for not saying it exactly as he would. I would take this class but with a different teacher

Roger is the GOAT. Pretty funny dude, love how he lectures by staring at the floor and pacing back and forth in front of the classroom, his philosophical musings flowing from his lips like honey. The class is pretty easy. The tests were open book & note. Lacks tedious assignments and quizzes and whatnot. Honestly a great guy and I learned a lot.
Amazing teacher, it is lecture-heavy but engaging. The grading criteria is extremely clear. All tests are open note. Don't buy the textbook, I never read it once.

If you're interested in a philosophy of religion course that also does apologetics then this is a good fit for you, but if you're just interested in the academic study of philosophy of religion, I would take it from someone else. This is probably the only course where I felt the quality of instruction and material was hurt by being at BYU

Most boring class & professor ever. I did no work, still got an A, IDK how. Learned no new skills or knowledge. Went in excited to learn philosophy, then stopped coming to class halfway through. If you actually want to learn, take Ryan Davis. Bro Cook just bashes on the trinity and traditional Christian thought, without even going in depth.

His exams including the final are open note and the TA posts a PowerPoint with all the answers. There is an 8-page paper due at the end of the semester but it is pretty easy and he helps you with by grading outlines. I also went in a couple of times to office hours and he proofread my entire paper and told me what to fix and I got a high A on it.

Easy GE class! DO NOT GET THE TEXTBOOK! He only gives tests based on the powerpoints, which are open note. I returned my rental without opening it once. He does a great job of making the class interesting while not putting too much pressure on memorizing everything about the ancient philosophers. If you are looking for an easy GE, this is it.

The classes are pretty lecture-heavy and can seem kinda boring but if you pay attention in class then they can be really interesting! There is a big research paper but he is so willing to give feedback and work on it with you throughout the semester. The exams are all open note and book! If you pace yourself then you can easily get an A.

Professor Cook is a great guy and teacher. The class has 5 tests, a research paper, two outlines for that research paper, and attendance. The research paper is half your grade, but he literally prepares you for it all semester and isn't a super harsh grader. If you go to class and do your work, you should definitely get an A.

Don't judge Brother Cook too quickly. At first, he seems like an old boring philosophy professor. But he is funny and cares so much. The tests are open notes, so they're super easy. Put effort into your research paper. Go to his office and he'll help you find sources and streamline your arguments. Overall, super interesting class. Would take again

Brother Cook is extremely helpful. The large majority of homework for the class was one 8-10 page research paper. This was a lot of work, but taken over the whole semester, it was not that bad, and Brother Cook will help you get everything you need for it really easily. The lectures could be better organized, but it was generally very engaging.

Also, for the journals, you don't have to be in class. I missed almost every day except the journal turn in and got a grade I am satisfied with. Just look over the PowerPoints that he will go over in that week and journal about them, and the TAs will never know that you weren't there.

The midterms you will no doubt get an 100% if you go to the TA reviews and take pictures of the slides. All the answer will be on those. You have 4 midterms and a final. The research paper is worth 50% of your grade so good luck. The one bad thing is if you are not on the professor's level of understanding you won't understand.

Super sweet guy. Class is easy if you know this one thing: TAKE NOTES BY PHILOSOPHER (keep all things about plato together, all things about stoics together etc.), his tests mainly ask things about specific philosophers so that is important. Tests are open slide too which is nice. Try to take notes in class.

Super easy. Show up to lecture, copy his slides. Tests are open note and entirely based off of powerpoints. You need to write 2 papers, one short and one a 10 page research paper, but you have all semester to work on it and he grades papers nicely. Super easy class. Awesome GE!
This is a very discussion based class and at times it was a little dry, but if you can push through that, this is a great class and made me fall in love with philosophy.

4 midterms, all open book/note/internet, just uses the time limit to help encourage you to study (it doesn't hurt, go to TA review sessions). Lectures were not great, the material just isn't entertaining. 50% of our grade is the paper which means tests aren't the biggest deal. Very nice and helpful but the class structure was confusing

Professor Cook is amazing. He really cares about his field and his students, and really does everything he can to help you succeed. Exams are pretty easy, they are short and open book. There are 3 short papers that are pretty easy too, and one 8 page research page that makes up a majority of your grade. Really awesome guy, would 100% reccomend him

Professor Cook is a great professor, and VERY knowledgeable about philosophy. His level of commitment to students is pretty rare! He really cares about his students and is super willing to chat or help with paper outlines during his office hours.

To be warned, most of your grade rides on very few assignments, but it isn't too bad.

I took this class in the summer, so the lectures were twice the normal length, which often made it difficult to stay engaged. Professor Cook explained things well and in an interesting way, and I learned a lot from this class. The quizzes were hard for me, and I highly recommend getting started early on the research paper. He isalways there to help

Roger Cook is super nice and his class is pretty easy. His lectures were super boring and he mainly talked about philosophy of religion. He has some weird ideas and always feels the need to take down other religions. I found it hard to do the class work because of the content despite it all being pretty easy.

Bro Cook was a super awesome professor. If you are stuck with anything in his class, he will help you! He is very willing to help his students succeed, and I definitely would recommend taking his class.

Always accessible outside of class, and encourages visits to his office. Class is mostly graded on a 8pg essay, and weekly quizzes (open note, but timed) given in class. Overall a great guy that cares for his students and is more than willing to work with you to boost your grade at the end of the semester as long as you have worked hard throughout.

If you don't do well on timed tests this class is NOT for you. Cook was very accessible throughout the year, and was always willing to help. The issue that I ran into was that his weekly quizzes were pretty difficult, due to time limit, and are worth 36%. Essay and test heavy, with a10pg essay, worth 40%, but that and the final are pretty easy.

TAKE THIS CLASS. The quizzes are open-note. The final exam was open-note. Prof Cook is super, super kind. If you need a grade changed or some help he is very open to meet with you. The class lectures are boring, but you can do hw for other classes and he doesn't care. Compared to your other options for GE professors, Prof Cook is extremely easy.
Honestly, super boring. I have a 3.99 GPA and was struggling in this class cuz the quizzes were so particular. Don't recommend at all.

I loved Roger Cook! There is a major research paper but it was fun to write especially because he sat down and made the outline with you and followed up. I would 100% take from him again, I wish he taught more than 201 and 215 as he is awesome!

Brother Cook was one of my favorite professors this semester and I was able to bond with him! He definitely cares for all his students and gives everyone a fair chance to earn the grade they deserve. The research paper heaviest graded assignment but the quizzes still matter since they were only 4 questions. Great class!!
He's a great teacher, difficult course material. I would recommend this class for the CIV GE. He's a really likable guy that really just wants to help you understand basic philosophy.

Brother Cook is amazing! We had a research paper that we worked on during the semester and he was always willing to help out. I personally struggled with the material, but lectures are very interesting and you can learn a lot by taking good notes. Overall he loves what he does and I recommend taking his class.

Brother Cook's class turned out to be my favorite class of the semester. In lecture, he does a great job helping students respect a wide variety of viewpoints and seek truth among them. He cares about students and often encourages them to see him in his office for feedback on their papers. As the cherry on top, he's a very entertaining storyteller!

Awesome class. Do everything during the semester that you need to and the class is fairly simple. I had such a high grade going into the final that I only needed a 26% to keep an A. There is a good amount of reading, but they are just to learn. 2 one-page papers, one big research paper on your own topic, attendance/participation, and the final.

What Bro. Cook did great was that he made you never worried about grades but motivated you learn and think deeply, especially the digital dialogue assignment. Compared to other GE classes, the contents in this class are super easy and interesting. He is also very smart, kind, and understanding! 120% recommended!

This is a Mormon apologetics class, not a philosophy of religion class. Cook has good intentions, and works hard to help his students succeed, but his definition of success is justifying your/his testimony of the gospel. If you want a professor that actually pushes on your assumptions and wants you to grow as a philosopher, look elsewhere.

Professor Cook is amazing! He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He's easy to contact, always willing to help, and so understanding. Not to mention he is a genius! This class had me thinking about the world in a completely different light. Wonderful professor and class!

Excellent lectures, evocative philosophical problems, AND AN A+ MUST. He is always enthusiastic about philosophy and likes to help his students. Just take his class for GE, get ready to enjoy wonderful ideas from classmates, and meet with the professor no matter when you have trouble with the outline, the 8-page paper, or the final. Harrison

I am really glad I took this class from Brother Cook. I am not usually the type of student to interact with a professor but he was so accessible and I got a ton of help from him. There is an 8 page paper but he helps you prepare so it is not hard. He will make a lot of comments on papers but does not doc too many points. Great class!

Professor Cook is very well intended but this class is super dry. His grading seems to have no rhyme or reason attached to it. Based on the reviews, I was really excited for this class but I dreaded going to this class because it felt like a complete waste of time.

Amazing lectures. Loves to interact with students. If you are taking it for a GE, it is worth taking; he might even just make you fall in love with philosophy. 8 page paper is a little intimidating but not awful; I did it over summer term and I was fine. This man is the best!

This class was easy and engaging. Cook really cares about his students. The only difficult part was an 8 page paper. He encouraged office hour visits, so I came once a week for help on my paper. He helped me find great sources, put together an outline, and make sure my paper was well written. He's a great source for any with religious questions.

I took this class for GE credit and it was probably my least favorite class I have ever taken. Dr. Cook is incredibly intelligent and is very passionate about the subject, but philosophy is just not my thing. Lectures tend to drag and blend together and the research paper (the majority of your grade) is killer.

He really cares about his students & wants you to do learn a lot & do well in the class. There isn't a lot of work, just one big research paper that you work on the whole semester but he helps you a ton with it and so it really was not bad at all. His tests are straight forward & multiple choice. This class was a solid choice to knock out a GE.

Pros: he LOVES his students. He encourages discussion but also points out the main points we need to know for the tests. Basically tells you what to write in your research paper to do well on it. Cons: 100 points total, so every point counts. He will take off points for tiny things on your papers (I got a 4.98/5 on my research outline).

I really enjoyed this class. Interesting way to talk about religion. He took attendance but all material is posted on the slides online. Tests were pretty easy, all multiple choice. The only hard part of this class was the 8 page research paper,  but he is willing to help you a ton if you meet with him.

Freshman year: Cared about students, but class was boring and papers were a matter of figuring out what he wanted. Senior year: Polar opposite. New teacher and a new man. Still cares about his students and class was engaging. He has developed so much as a teacher. I can't say it enough: Phil215 from Cook is A MUST.
Lectures are long but he tries to make it as fun as possible. He is very loving and understanding, so don't hesitate to ask for help. Papers are rough but he helps you every step of the way.

Amazing man, great teacher, very helpful.  Willing to help students with papers and assignments, in fact encouraged us to come by his office. This class was fascinating and inspirational. Take Philosophy of Religion from Brother Cook!

Awesome teacher! He's extremely passionate about the philosophy of religion.  He gives great lectures and was a huge help with the final paper. I learned a ton in this class and I think it's a perspective on religion every student at BYU you should get. If you like to think deeply about faith please take this coarse!

Brother Cook is well-intentioned, but sometimes his teaching style is difficult to follow. For me it has been quite a challenge, but I know other students in the class understand him fine. I go through the power points that he uses after every class to make sure I am familiar with the material.

Brother Cook is amazing. So willing to help. Taught extremely subjective material in an objective way. Got us thinking. If you're afraid of challenging your faith with the views of people of different beliefs, don't take the class. But I loved it because it strengthened my faith  has helped me to relate to people of different beliefs.

Professor Cook is one of the best at BYU. Take this class from him. You won't regret it. His tests are very straight forward and he will really help you out in any way you need. Tons of office hours and he will help you with anything you need. Didn't  buy textbook, missed 30% of classes, still got an A-. More importantly though you'll learn lots!

Professor Cook is the best instructor I've had at BYU, and I graduate next semester. I wish I could take every class I have remaining from him. He literally does all he can to help you succeed in his classes short of just making the course uselessly easy. He is so good at answering questions. I learned so much in his classes.
easy teacher, took this class to fulfill a GE. Just write what he wants (he'll tell you) and you'll get a good grade. Put forth a little effort and you'll be sweet.

Bro Cook is a nice guy. He'll do his best to help you out. His lectures are not always riveting but all his notes are online, so you can easily go back over them. Reading isn't necessary. The tests are sometimes obscure. His cat jokes and personal examples are weird. Average teacher.

I have attended BYU for many years. Roger Cook is by far the worst professor that I have ever had. His lectures are disorganized. He is a nice guy, but if you are not a philosophy student he will ignore your comments or openly demean you. Tests are not comparable to what is taught. Tests are obscure. TAKE THIS FROM A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR IF POSSIBLE

After years of being in school, I have never had such a bad professor. Yes he is easy to talk to, but he doesn't care what you have to say. It is his way or no way. He doesn't stay on topic, and his lectures are so boring. This class was a joke and the worst class i've ever taken. I highly recommend not taking any course from this professor.

Very unorganized. Had to get textbook off amazon because he forgot to tell the bookstore we need a text for the course.  Had to take tests in class because he forgot to submit the tests to the testing center.  Monotone voice, mostly reads off powerpoints during lecture.  10 page research paper is 35% of your grade.

Brother Cook has to be one of the best professors on campus. He gave specific examples of what would be on tests, and the tests were always based on lectures, no surprise questions. He is not only approachable but LOVES when students talk to him. He took time to go over our research papers with all of us before they were due. Funny cat jokes too.

I absolutely love Brother Cook! It is a very in depth class where you have to think about things deeply. It is a discussion based class. I love Cook because he is so respectful and wants to help you the best he can. I was able to do well in this class for my first semester at college. It is very interesting and he cracks the class up all the time.

I love professor Cook. I recommend him to everyone interested in taking either writing 150 or philosophy 150. the class is very small and personal and he is willing to help you with anything you need. honestly, you'd be foolish to not take this class from him. he's the best teacher i've had at BYU thus far and I am so thankful I had him.

Extremely easy class. I studied way to hard for his tests. They're super easy. Great guy. Explains philosophy pretty well. Makes a lot of awkward cat jokes. A lot of class discussion, which can be annoying in philosophy if you have the wrong classmates. Bottom line easy A, and kind of interesting class.

I took this class to fill the WRT 150 credit, but it was amazing. Prof. Cook was EXTREMELY helpful and caring. Be willing to do the work-which can be difficult-and you will see your efforts pay off. He gives a lot of feedback on papers which helped My writing improve. The class focuses more on ideas than mechanics. I definitely recommend it!
He is extremely helpful, and a great teacher. He asks a lot but is understanding. I would take any class from him.

I loved this class. I was worried at first about how well I would do/how much we would have to read. This class is extremely doable.  Bro. Cook knows his stuff and makes the class really interesting by relating the topics to us.  This is lecture based, so lots of ppl found it boring, but he is invested in helping you get an A.

I wouldn't say that this is an easy class; Bro. Cook definitely makes you put forth a significant amount of effort to get an A.  However, he is extremely helpful and really wants his students to succeed and become better writers. Get to know him and you'll be able to tell that he cares.

Pretty simple class. Do the work and you will get the appropriate grade. Your grade really represents how much time you put into the class. I think anyone who put an hour into studying got 100% or higher on the exams. He will edit and comment on your papers for as many drafts as you are wiling to write. I put in 3hrs/week and got a 99% as my total.

Brother Cook is amazing! He is so nice and actually cares about taking the time to help out his students. He is also hilarious. The tests are super short and really easy.He likes to give bonus points too on tests and quizzes, so it's possible to get over 100% by the end of the semester.Just come to class and pay attention and you'll do fine.

He was such a bad professor it was incredible. I feel like I am an intelligent person, but that is not what gets you a good grade. Brown nosing gets you a good grade. He is scattered and biased. Do not take a class from him

Easy A; it's probably true that he has favorites. I know, because I think I was one of them. He has a mormon bias; to a non-believer it makes the class frustrating. Though I give him credit - He knew I disagreed yet still liked me. He can definitely grow on you.

Brother cook is a good professor. He wants you to do well. If you want to do well read the essays and ask for his help he is alway willing to help you and makes time for you. Its a philosophy class its different then the norm. He could improve on following the syllabus more. I put my dues in and got an A.

Not worth it at all-the guy teaches whatever he decides is the truth-which is often wrong, even according to the book (which he worships). He obviously plays favorites, and grades on a double standard according to who he likes. If you take him, brown-nose like crazy and you'll do ok. You will HATE the word 'Remarkable' by the end of the semester.

I felt he did nothing but talk about how much he hated cats...every example he gave had to do with how much he hated cats and definitely has favorites. We didn't follow the syllabus at all and the tests took forever to get back.

Professor Cook is a really easy going guy, really easy to work with. Always willing to help. I dont like Philosophy at all so this class was way boring. Cook just lectures everyday. Each week there is a reading assignment, maybe a quiz.There are 3-4 page written midterms that are easy just time consuming. Also a 10 page research paper.

I really liked his class. If you have a smaller class then you get a lot more out of it. I took this during summer, and it was nice to get the credit out of the way while actually learning some philosophy.

Cook is a weirdo!  He constantly makes awkward comments. I swear he makes up "facts". We didn't follow the syllabus timetable at all. His comments on papers often don't make sense, and he favors girls over guys--especially if the girls are cute. No privacy on papers because everything is posted and responded to on Blackboard threads. Easy A though.

Cook has no idea what he is talking about. He grades his papers on an absolutely arbitrary system. Extremely unorganized. Most of class we just talked about how to use Microsoft Word and how to correct punctuation. Take his class and you'll see, and regret it.

Dr. Cook is a little unorganized and takes a while to get your papers back to you. Then when you finally do get your papers back you can't understand his comments. Midterms are take home which is nice, but he takes so long to get them back to you that I didn't even understand why I missed anything. You also have to write a 10 page research paper th

Professor Cook is extremely nice. He is willing to help if you ask. HIs lectures are boring; they consist of powerpoint presentations and can be hard to follow. The class was graded on in-class quizzes (difficult to prepare for), a midterm and final (purely essays), and a big research paper. It was more work and I learned less than I expected.

Good Class, the tests were fair, but his grading was difficult to decipher. He does a good job of presenting the law and managing discussion in the class. It was nice to have a 400 lvl class with any major papers.

I am not a philosophy-minded person at all, but I liked his class. Midterm is take home. He gives you the essays for the final ahead of time. In class quizzes are easy if you do the reading, because he tries hard to grant you points. A 10-12 pg paper if 30% of your grade, but you can choice an topic you want. Take him if you share his hate for cats
one of the most helpful teacher's i've ever had, he eas always willing to come before class of stay after to help and insisted that we call him at any hour of the night for help, he dosent sleep

I found the class pretty interesting and there were no tests so that was excellent.  It was a writing class, so obviously we had a few papers but he lets you turn in as many drafts as you want and gives specific comments on your writing.  As long as you try in this class you will probably get an A.

Loved his class, it was pretty easy.  I only used the textbook once for an essay, but outside of that his lectures are so good you don't need to read.  Or, you could read and not go to class if you'd like.  All tests are take-home except for the final.

Anyone can get an A in the class. You can turn in most papers as many times as you want to get a better grade. To those that think it is not philosophical, guess what? Its 150! Take higher level courses if you want to do high philosophy.

Bro. Cook is a really nice guy, and really flexible with grades, however, I did not learn a darn thing about philosophy or writing!  I felt like I took a huge step backward, and I am a freshman in college.  If you want an easy A, you've found it.  If you care about writing, class organization, or learning philosophy, find a different class.

Roger is a great guy.  Get to know him.  If you are in his office and in constant contact with him your writing will improve.  My writing has improved so much.  Class is pretty random and the papers are sometimes tough, but he will help you a ton.

If you are willing to work, he will help you improve your writing.  Papers are turned into drafts.  If you are looking to learn about philosophy and philosophers, take an intro to Philosophy class.  If you want to improve your philosophical style writing, take Phil201!

Great class that helped my writing a lot.  It was a lot of work and a challenge.  He is a very helpful teaching and interested in helping the students.  He is particular about the content, but if he sees that you're putting in the effort, you'll get a good grade.

He is a really nice guy, but not a very good teacher.  We didn't really talk much philosophy... besides his own bizarre philosophies.  My writing didn't improve even though I got good grades on my papers, and whenever I'd go in for help, which he was always willing to give, I came out more perplexed

Roger is unlike any other teacher. He is so willing to help you get a good grade in the class. he will let you turn in 4 or 5 drafts per paper, and he'll assist you will all of them. He is particular about the content of the paper, but that's how good ideas are learned, by imitation.
