He's such a good man, but he is an AWFUL teacher. He wont' give full grade unless u write what he wants. He would never make grammar or style corrections, just content. His theories are a pain in the neck. and gives then as if it was doctrine...Hated the class and the teacherm though he's a nice guy

Way cool, lots of class discussion. He explains everything really well and gives lots of attention to each individual student. Not super easy though, you've got to write good papers and know the material fairly well. Makes class fun and is genuinely nice.
Cares about his students deeply. Is willing to give you an A as long as you ask for one basically. Recommend to anyone.

It was a very boring class, but very helpful. fulfills a general education requirement, and teaches very efficient argumentative skills for writing future papers. He's willing to take time to help anyone, thoroughly, and is a generally very nice guy.
very kind, but disorganization can be a headache.

Dr. Harrison is awkward in the best way. His lectures are conceptually helpful, but don't prepare you for the homework. Go to the TA lab and his office hours for that. He is very reasonable about giving points back on exams and offered 1/4 test corrections. Also, bug him about replacing the lowest midterm with the final because he did for our year!

Tests were 60% of our grade despite having at least 10 hours of weekly homework, and I felt there were a few surprises on each test. Its an absolutely brutal class but Dr. Harrison is really nice and puts all his materials online. Learn the content yourself before you come to class and you'll be able to ask good questions, it helps a lot.

Dr. Harrison is an excellent professor. He is calm and humorous, making lectures enjoyable and easy to understand. Excellent at answering questions, very accessible to get help. Exams were long (10-11 free response questions) but very fair and graded on the nice side. Would 10/10 recommend.

Lectures are very dense with information and he knows a lot about the class. It's a very difficult class and the tests are tough but it's easier than CHEM111. Tests are difficult and require you to really understand the material but very doable.

Doctor Harrison is so kind!  I found a lot of success in his class by reading the chapters from the textbook that would be covered before each lecture.  The written homework each week was pretty tough, but we were always welcome to come in to his office hours and he would help us work through the problems.

I took 518 from Dr. Harrison. It was a very fun and low-key class. His tests are open book, open note, and open published scholarly article. He was very accommodating in many ways and is overall super nice.

Dr. Harrison is a really good professor and lecturer.  I would recommend his class to anyone.  It's very difficult and the tests can be brutal, but there isn't any getting around that in a chem class.  Go to his office hours after exams!  He's usually willing to negotiate pointage.

I love Dr. Harrison. He is one of the sweetest genuine teachers I've ever had. I will say, his tests are super hard, it was obvious he is used to teaching higher level. Go to class, but especially go to office hours. He would hold outside reviews for those who would come ask for help. Very understanding on giving points back on tests. Wants success

Nice but BAD prof, cried sm over 106. Take Sansom, she has 7 mini exams but curves +drops 2. Lectures confusing/useless +ppts have some wrong answers. For (4) exams do practice tests/review ppts, go to office hours, and do hwk in the TA lab w Addy. Hwk 3x a week. Use txtbook to self teach. Hard final, 3.5 hrs, 20 mc 71% avg, 8 SA 63% but lil curve

Professor Harrison is a great guy, and genuinely wants to help his students. Attending office hours was super helpful, and he was often willing to give a couple points back on exams if you felt your work deserved more credit. great class except his tests were super difficult and problems were often worded differently than what we did in class.

Professor Harrison was super nice, caring, and helpful outside of lecture. Definitely go to his office hours to get clarification and before exams. His exams were really fair and if you study they arent too bad.
This class was definitely difficult. Dr. Harrison is a caring, respectful professor, but he can be boring in his lectures. He goes over a lot of practice problems in class, which is really helpful.

I had to teach myself a lot of the material, especially with the textbook. Professor Harrison is very intelligent, but I was often very confused in class. We did experiments a lot instead of clarifying confusing details.

Professor Harrison is a genuine and intelligent instructor. That being said, his lectures can get boring at times as he isn't always enthusiastic about what he teaches. Also, it's not too difficult as he teaches the concepts well enough and there aren't ever any curveballs on the tests.

Professor Harrison is an awesome professor. I was hesitant based on these reviews, but was surprised on how great the class is run. He is very passionate, teaches clearly as he builds upon the subjects, not too much homework, and tests are very similar to homework problems, not trying to trick you. He loves to answer questions and teaching!

Professor Harrison and his class are fantastic! I was a bit scared to take from Professor Harrison based on Rate My Professor Reviews, but I definitely recommend taking from him. He is very accessible by e-mail, after class, and in office hours. He is good at explaining Chemistry, and gets the class going right with a prayer and spiritual thought.

Dr Harrison is a great professor, and is very passionate about chemistry so you'll vibe well if you are too! He is very kind and more than fair with grading, and he really wants to make sure the students understand the material very well. Only a few tests and not too many assignments throughout the week, and he prepares students very well for them.

Professor Harrison is a great professor! The homework and tests were manageable and there was plenty of help if needed. He made the effort to get to know his students and made it a very fair and good chemistry class.

Professor Harrison is a super sweet guy but he is not a good teacher, he struggles to explain things and all the tests are written. I really only got actual help when I went to his office during hours, other than that this class was really hard and I felt like my grade didn't reflect my work.

If you have the option to take a different professor... do it. Dr. Harrison is a smart guy but does not for the life of him know how to actually teach the concepts. My friends who took this class with a different teacher had a way easier time, while everyone with Harrison struggled. His tests are harder and had more HW. Would NOT recommend at all.
He was a great professor.

Overall professor Harrison is a pretty good teacher. Sometimes he doesn't teach very clearly during the lecture, but he was very helpful outside of class. Going to his office hours before every exam and asking questions cleared a lot up. Going to the TA lab with questions also helped a ton. You will have to work hard. Do the reading beforehand.

He's a nice guy he really is, but his lectures are so confusing that I'm often left more confused then if I had just stayed home. He'll take an already complicated subject and convolute it to the point that it's impossible to learn. If you're a really really good self-learner you'll be fine, otherwise you should probably look elsewhere.

If you don't like chemistry you won't like this teacher. You can't expect to just go to class and get the information clearly from the lecture if it doesn't come ready to you. He does do many more in class problems than other professors and you usually have a chance to change your answer and work with others on them. I found that helpful.
Lectures can be pretty boring. The tests are hard. I'm sorry if you have to take this class, but you'll make it through, I promise.

Dr. Harrison is really nice and willing to go over concepts with you outside of class. However, the lectures are not clear. The iclicker questions required for attendance often require knowledge of a concept that hasn't been taught yet. Read the book on your own to get clarification and go to TA reviews. You can get an A but it requires work.

I don't know why the ratings are so terrible for Dr. Harrison here. He is a fair professor and he was accessible during his office hours and was willing to help. The tests are difficult and so is the course. You will need to put time into this class.

Dr Harrison is always willing to help you understand anything if you go visit his office hours. That being said, he doesn't really teach you concepts while in class but instead only lightly reviews material.  If you want to do well you'll need to teach yourself everything that will be covered in that days lecture before class.  Tests are difficult.

"Those who can't do, can't teach."  This class was awful. Lectures were super disorganized and rarely pertinent to the homework. Frequently the professor would miss his own in-class practice problems and each exam had multiple items keyed incorrectly. I honestly think it's a disgrace that I had to pay to teach myself all semester. Nice guy though.

Terrible teacher. He would mess up on his own problems and confuse everyone in the class and then test on things that we had never gone over. Worst professor I've ever had. Prepare to learn everything by yourself and even if you do that you won't do too well on the tests.
I met with him several times throughout the semester,  and he really cares about all his students! He is really good at explaining things. Tough tests though, although it is chemistry...

He sometimes went too fast through the lecture material, but he was willing to stop and clarify when we needed it. He is super helpful one-on-one though, so I would recommend going to his office hours if you take him.  And the quizzes are very difficult, but you are allowed to get help from others/ the TAs on them.  The exams are reasonable.

Dr. Harrison is a super nice guy, and I was a little wary of this class from all the horror stories that people say about how hard it is, but I think he was very fair in his tests and grading.  The online homework is super annoying sometimes, but that's not really his fault.  For sure Dr. Harrison is a safe bet if you have to take this class.

This was a difficult course, but I would recommend taking it from Dr. Harrison. He is willing to adjust the pace of the lecture based on students question. He tries to learn names, is approachable and friendly. Form a study group and do the homework together! The weekly quizzes are challenging, but prepare you for the tests.

I've never taken a more boring class and students of other professors talk about how their professors allow study aids and helps on exam and he won't consider such when brought up in class that other professors are more helpful.

Dr. Harrison is SO nice and laid back. Nevertheless, it's a tough class. For someone who took chemistry for the first time ever in life, I quickly realized that his teaching style is more directed to those who already have a notion of the material. I had to rely on the book to learn how to solve problems. Tests are hard so get help from TAs.

Bro. Harrison= great guy, super nice but then the class... Rough, there are I clickers everyday in class to get some easy points that you will need. 3 short answer exams, super hard and confusing. Nothing like the book problems. Then you have a final, multiple choice and short answer. Good luck when you take this class!

He is difficult to understand and the tests are really hard short answer, and they don't really reflect what is covered in class.  He is a nice guy and he will help you if you ask for it, but he explains it as if you know more than you actually do... which is no help.

He is very hard to understand. He explains problems very poorly in lecture and you have to basically teach yourself everything from the textbook. If you like hard, 20 short answer tests with NO curve and a confusing teacher... this is your class.

PROF. HARRISON IS THE MOST ADORABLE HUMAN BEING. Seriously. That said the class was pretty tough. He doesn't know how to teach well, but the homework is really helpful. He does fun experiments in class almost every day that make things exciting. Go to class because there are always iClicker questions. Tests were pretty tough. They are graded hard.

Brother Harrison is a good teacher who wants salvation and happiness for every student. His class isn't hard, but you need to go to class and keep up with the readings. Start your papers as soon as you know you need to, and stay aware of deadlines and testing dates. You will do great if you do! :D

I had him for Book of Mormon part 1, and it was awesome.  He has a lot of good input.  He grades his tests fairly easily, just put some effort in and show you have some knowledge and you should get some points.  Read your scriptures daily, do the 3 (easy) papers, study for an hour or two for each exam, and you should be fine.

Easily the worst CLASS I have ever taken. Harrison is a great guy, but I couldn't have learned any less. I had to teach myself from the book and that did not work-out too well. He relies heavily on the Iclicker way too much so sit next to smart people.

His teaching style was no good.  He's nice, but seriously, I came away from every class wondering what the lecture was about.  I definitley used the book to try and teach myself.  His tests are very hard and I felt a few of the questions were unfair to include.  Make sure you spend lots of hours with the T.A.s or someone who can tutor you!

Dr. Harrison is a very kind person but is sometimes not very good at explaining things.  However, if you use the textbook and listen to lecture you will know what to study for the test.  Gives practice exams before each midterm which really helped me.  It is very helpful to know a little chemistry before taking his class.

Professor Harrison's class was okay.  I don't really have a great interest in the subject, but he tried to explain things thoroughly and gave interesting facts.  He did some cool demonstrations too.  Reading the book is VITAL, or understanding the lectures is difficult.

Prof. Harrison is very unclear in his lectures and very scatterbrained.Doesn't connect the dots very well.You definitely have to teach yourself the material and the book is mandatory! Iclicker quizzes every class period and was the only reason i went. Other than that i taught myself everything but he does some cool experiments in class.

He's a nice guy, and he'll help you out if you ask, but the book is easier to understand than his lectures. His lectures are somewhat disorganized, and it seemed like the class was always confused. There's no curve, so be careful. Easy quizzes, but really hard tests. Tip: Read BEFORE lectures, and don't forget to do homework/labs (easier points).

You basically have to teach yourself everything...so GET THE BOOK!! You have quizzes in the testing center for every chapter and tests after every 3 chapters. Everyone does pretty average on the tests...so study hard. He doesn't curve anything...and has unorganized lectures. Not impossible though...

I didn't like the way Prof. Harrison taught. He wasn't very organized in lectures and he also wasn't very clear in explaining concepts. I got confused a lot of the time when he tried explaining something. The textbook was actually a lot more helpful than he was. I also didn't think some questions on his tests were fair either.

An interesting class, not an interesting professor.  His lectures were unorganized, it seemed and never very clear.  The text, however was VERY well written and very clear.  The beginning of the class was easy, but most of the class failed the last test and he didn't curve because the class average ended up being a "B".

Dr. Harrison's grading system is really hard.  He is happy to have an average of 75% and he doesn't curve grades at the end of the semester, however, there are many opportunities for a few free points here and there.
Soft spoken guy with a knowledge of many specialties in the field.
Great guy helped me out with tons of stuff. Helped me to achieve the grade I needed.

Freakin hard! Class from hell. Unless your a Chem god prepare to fail every test and be fustrated the whole semester.GO in for help, he's helpful.Evyery teacher is hard though so I guess I would recommend him...hes better than cannon!
Great professor, his teaching methods are helpful if you pay attention in lecuture.  If you stay up on assignments and put forth reasonable effort the class isn't too bad.

Great teacher. As long as you pay attention in class, do the homework, and don't get behind you will be fine. The TA's are great and I highly recommend the Chem lab. Dr. Harrison cares about his students and if you visit him with a question he makes sure you leave understanding the concept.
The nicest guy you will ever meet. He really likes chemistry. My favorite comment of his was that "Chemistry is God's work, it should turn us on!" Great class.

Final was killer. Dr. Harrison is funny in a quiet way- lecture was mostly just working out problems. Use TA's. Go to Dr. Harrison after each test and argue your answer- you'll always get points back! Not a bad teacher at all.
His final is a beast.  If you take hime, make sure to go to him after ever test to try to get more points.

He may seem a little nerdy, but he's young+pretty cool in that he relates well to students.  He's usually soft-spoken and dry, but if you're listening he throws in things that are hilarious.  The class is easy if you have a good 105 experience.  Nice guy.

213 is a tough course, but I really enjoyed Dr. Harrison. He was very easy-going, which eased the stress load. He was always respectful in answering my questions, and I really appreciated that. He's a good man.
He is about as nerdy as they come.  He's hard to understand, and he doesn't understand why you don't understand him.

Professor MacFarlane is an incredibly kind individual. You can tell he cares a lot about his students and the subject he teaches. He has a great sense of humor. His lectures are a bit dense and can be boring at times. There are very few assignments, so the exams matter A LOT. Definitely study more than you think you need to.

Super nice guy that really knows a ton. SO receptive to feedback. If you don't like how an assignment is set up propose a different way to him and he will totally change it. Very clear expectations. Do the work in the textbook and memorize the vocab he tells you to and you'll 100% get an A.

His class only has like 10 assignments(weekly quizs) and two tests(midterm and final) that it is graded on so it is important to do good on them. His lectures are a bit disorganized but he really wants you to suceed and is willing to help you.

I legit joined the class the week of the midterm and was able to get an A on the test. If you do the work in the textbook and study you don't really need to go to class. He is a nice guy and helps when you ask for it. Easy A, just put in the work to memorize the terms

I love Prof. Macfarlane! He's very passionate about his class, but get ready for everything to be published the day of or 1-2 days prior to deadline. His class is a little disorganized but he was very accessible. His weekly quizzes are heavily graded, but besides the midterm and the final that was all we ever had to do. Would take again!

Professor MacFarlane is really nice, but this class was really unorganized. The syllabus and assignments were never published, and we had no idea when tests were. Sometimes, I was not even sure what we were supposed to read for class that day. There are a lot of lectures, and I was not always sure what I was supposed to remember.

Super passionate. Other than that the class was poorly organized. No TA and never answered emails (We are going on 5 with no answer). His homeworks are worth a lot of the grade and the questions are very subjective, no real definitive answer on some. After 2+ years of byu finally made a rate my professor account because of him.

TAKE MACFARLANE! He is one of the funniest most enjoyable professors I've had. He'll love you if you just engage in his class and speak up. Some lectures are pretty long but he's so passionate about his work that I didn't mind. He's all around just awesome to get to know and really makes his class worth coming to.

Basically anything that came out of his mouth was fair game on any test. If that's not your style, don't take from him. Class discussions were interesting at times. I really only took it because I enjoy mythology. The papers were to be kept very short but with that came very tough grading.

An absolute king. He has such an impressive knowledge of classics and the Latin language, and my appreciation for Latin poetry really grew from this class. Hes really funny and super caring, and I thought he graded very fairly. Like any higher level Latin class, it takes a good amount of prep before class each day to succeed, but its so worth it!

Dr. Macfarlane is one of the most impressive professors I've taken from at BYU. Contrary to popular opinion of him going on tangents, I found his lectures to be so interesting and thought-provoking. I definitely had to put in a good amount of work to get an A. But, I loved his class so much I considered switching to classics for my major! TAKE HIM!

Very tough grader. I took this class as a GE thinking it would be fun, but this class was made more difficult than it should have been. He definitely had his favorites in class and if youre not one of them, good luck. He would often go on long tangents that were not relatable to the class. Grading was unfair and hard to receive help on assignments

LOVED HIM! He is such a nice, sweet person and his class is so enjoyable! You do have to do quite a bit of reading, but for me it was "fun" homework because the myths were so interesting! You have to write around 8 short papers, which are graded super easily and are not difficult to do at all. The tests are pretty easy, just pay attention in class!

Every week we had a film to watch (Vertigo, Moulin Rouge!, Elektra my Love, Slumdog Millionaire, etc), then we'd discuss it for two classes. Easy homework, usually just a worksheet or a digital dialog. He knows his Greek & Roman myth and his enthusiasm really rubs off on you. This class isn't offered a lot, but take it from him if you can!

Dr. Macfarlane goes off on whims a lot in class, but it is almost always related to the topic of the text you read before class. His exams are fairly easy, especially if you have a good knowledge of Greek literature (Odyssey, Metamorphoses, etc.). You can get away with a decent grade as long as you cliffnote the reading before class. uses TopHat

The papers are simple enough but incredibly difficult to get a 10. Went and asked why I lost points after 1st paper, had a very clear view of how to achieve full points for 2nd paper. Achieved a 10 (very rare, only given to 3) on the 2nd. Use office hours! Graded only on two research papers, two reaction papers, attendance, and three exams.

Prof Macfarlane was incredibly knowledgable about his subject and smart, but he rambles. A lot. Basically, read the chapters and you'll have a complete understanding of what to know without the lectures, because his lectures are just random tangents that don't help. You should attend class for the mastery images, but his lectures are just random.

The organization of the class does not make sense. He spends most of class talking about the mastery images which hardly ever line up with the reading you've done. His class notes online make absolutely no sense. In his class lectures he quickly refers myths expecting you to know what he's talking about. I was disappointed in this class. Don't take

LOTS of reading. Professor is fantastic, though. Very passionate about his subject. I'll take that over light reading any day. Tests are moderately hard. Do the work and you'll be fine. It's hard to get 10/10 on his reception papers, but not too hard to get an 8 or 9. I don't think he went on inapplicable tangents at all, contrary to other reviews.

Dr. Macfarlane's mythology class is awesome. His lectures are interesting and he teaches to the class's understanding. He & the TAs grade very fairly and openly on papers and tests. He's the kind of testing professor you love--he'll throw out a question if most got it wrong/it was badly worded. Lectures essential for the tests.

I really enjoyed Dr. Macfarlane's class more than I anticipated. He sometimes rambles, but I felt he was always fair on tests and on papers. He is very kind and knowledgeable. The papers are rarely given 10s, but they are not very difficult. Pick a topic you're interested in and its not hard to do well. Pay attention to lecture details for tests.

Dr. Macfarlane is a super nice guy, very helpful. His lectures tend toward rambling sometimes, but the tangents are interesting. You have to do the reading and come to class, but if you do, it's easy to do well. He and the TA will review your papers if you ask them to.

Lectures are horribly organized and impossible to follow. The tests are hard, you have to try and guess what random things the professor thinks are interesting.  He is a very tough grader. I worked hard on all of them and could never get a 10 for very absurd reasons. Some of it is interesting but the frustration is not worth it. Don't take it.

This teacher was terrible. impossible to follow, constantly went on tangents, wouldn't give 10/10 on the papers and on the last day of class he came in and said he took the final as a test run and got a 75 and then said "so you guys should do good" worst teacher ever and obviously did not want class to do well.

Macfarlane is a nice guy but he is too smart for his own good and it affects his teaching. If you dont have mythology knowledge dont take this because he refers to a bunch of info that he assumes you already know. His TAs grade everything and they "never give 10/10." The tests are hard and everyone in class couldnt believe it. The avg was 70%

Dr. Macfarlane is a very good professor.  He doesn't have a big ego and it is very easy to work with him.  He clearly lays out his expectations and expects his students to study and work hard. One of my most worthwhile college classes.

You must have a good background knowledge in some areas however, he does go over the basics in other areas. His class was very dry and half of it was spent with him fighting technology. His only real interest is in the papers, which he grades extremely hard. I was excited going into this class, but this was easily the worst class I have taken.

Macfarlane loves his subject, & conveys that in his lectures to the point where he does go on a lot of tangents. However, he is clear about what will be on the test! He will also give very helpful feedback if you turn in the papers a week early as a rough draft. Just put in some effort! He's always good for laugh. 3 short (2 page) papers, 3 tests.

Though I loved Dr. Macfarlane in smaller classes, he is very difficult to follow in a larger lecture class like this one. He goes on tangents and his tests don't seem relevant to anything he talked about in class. Plus the Tophat and test questions are very poorly worded. Only take this class if you have a great attention span and love myth.

He's helpful when approached one-on-one. He goes on tangents A LOT!!! Attending class: participation is 7.5% of your grade. The papers were a pain. Don't expect to get more than a 9/10 on them. Tests are fairly ridiculous--testing on stuff that we never covered in class; he would get some of his own questions wrong sometimes.

Professor McFarlane made his classes interesting and fun.  He does go on tangents on occasion, but his tangents are interesting and useful. The papers required aren't bad at all, and his tests are fair if somewhat difficult.  I really recommend him!
Professor Macfarlane did not provide a syllabus, he did not return papers and he spoke disrespectfully to his students. Horrible class environment.

I never sleep through this class. Prof. Macfarlane is funny and intelligent. Other "raters" have said that he goes on tangents (and he does) but they are really *interesting* tangents. He is one of my favorite professors.

Prof. MacFarlane is really great! I loved his class, and it isn't as hard as everyone says. Just keep up on the reading and memorize what he tells you to and you'll be fine. I would recommend going to class. He is really nice and sometimes funny too!

Prof McFarlane is a really interesting guy.  The class was not super difficult, however, he did spend a lot of time on tangents, and the the tests were on the material we were supposed to have covered in the lecture.  Fun class to attend, and I learned a ton about how classical myth can be used in the modern day.

This class is  time consuming.  There is a lot of day-to-day reading. Don't get behind!  Attendance is beneficial...I had to miss a lot and suffered for it.  Bro. MacFarlane is a REALLY nice guy.  He's happy to see you succeed and will give you as much help as he can.  The TAs are useless.

He is so quirky! His lectures are hilarious and interesting but he does go on tangents. The tests are not as bad as everyone says. Just do the reading. Most of the material is covered at the beginning of the semester after that it is just interpreting plays. sparknotes is sufficient for the plays. easy points by memorizing paintings

Absolutely awful. Terrible class and the teaching was worse. Class often had nothing to do with anything.  Some of the tests didn't come from class or textbook so some questions were a wild guess.  If you have to take this class (and I'm sorry if you do) find a different teacher.

MacFarlane is a good guy, but I thought this class was horrible.  Especially for it being offered at a GE it was really hard.  The tests were really hard, and I felt that no matter how much I studied, it wasn't enough.  He wouldn't give any assistance or guidelines on what to study.  It was a really frustrating and dry class.

I took a myth class once, loved it and went into this class thinking I'd learn more. Wrong. It's everything I already learned but incredibly boring. Dr. MacFarlane is pretty random. He puts his slides online and the TAs are in charge of grading. Don't take this class thinking it'll be fun. Essays on tests and you're required to memorize paintings.

Extremely interesting class but I recommend knowing the Orestes myth beforehand- It's his favorite and the object of many tangents. Haven't taken a test yet, but the papers are very engaging. Not a lot of work outside readings, but you DO need to do them to understand discussions. Most myths covered in class. Good background in art history a bonus.

I am extremely disappointed with this professor. He doesn't write the tests - the mythology geek TA's do. He doesn't grade the assignments, the TA's do. He straight out told us in class that a 100% A is not possible for any assignment, no matter how hard you try. This isn't one of those "you do the work, you'll be fine" classes. Deeply disappointed
Truly one of my favorite teachers ever. If you need help-- ask. He will help. Entertaining and extremely smart. You will have earned a good grade, but he is a great professor.

This was unfortunately probably my least favorite class... Prof MacFarlane rambles on about nonsense half the time and the class is EXTREMELY boring. I always dreaded going to class and you are expected to know more than you are taught. Class is just a reiteration of the reading and is pointless. Don't take it from him.

Everything is based on tangents. You spend like 2 days talking about when Penelope "knew it was Odysseus" and how the "Orestia theme relates to EVERYTHING" Take it from another teacher or another letters course.
Excellent course if you're interested in academia.  Professor MacFarlane definitely knows his stuff, but often goes on tangents.  There is also a lot of reading, so beware!

This class is not for the weak at heart, and I would only suggest taking it if you already have a love for mythology. If you take it just wanting to explore, you won't like it. Class is based on the themes of The Oresteia. You read the entire Odyssey, Metamorphoses, Apollodorus, Mourning Becomes Electra and another random play.
He's a man who's so humble he can speak straight into your brain...  A great example of the phrase "lion of the lord."

This was by far my favorite class at BYU, though I will admit probably my hardest class as well. Dr. Macfarlane definitely knows what he is teaching. I came into his class with an interest in Greek Mythology and came out with a love for it. This class is difficult--not for the weak--but the skills learned will help you in every class afterwards!

I liked Greek Myth going in, came out disgusted with the subject- stories & characters are totally screwed up. MacFarlane is smart (has bowties & weird hair), but so random. His tests are all on his tangents- go to class. Lots of reading (from dry texts or Greek tragedies). Tests are hard-no mult choice, papers arduous. Take another Letters course.

Great professor! Probably some of the most important and relevant things to your life, you will learn in this class. He had a great approach to wellness. Its super easy too and great to take online during school or summer, especially if you want a chill class while you're vacationing or working. You do have to buy a textbook, but its needed.

I would not recommend this professor, you are heavily graded on the 2 exams and a final. There is not a lot of preparation for the exams, just a TA going over the slides for 10 min. for the final the TA's gave us an hour recorded review which was much more helpful.

If feels like he organized this class when he first started teaching in 1999, his TAs run the class. I soon discovered that some things that are quizzed in the class are not found in the readings. If you decide to take the class there is a Quizlet that some saint made a few years ago, it got me through this class. May the odds be ever in your favor

Exams are 80% of the class and it seemed like it was set up to fail every time. Doesn't make sense because I'm in another one of his classes and that one is significantly easier. Have to retake it and insanely frustrated, wish I could take it in person but for some reason it's only offered online with this professor.

Theres a lot of work in this class, you have to do an assignment and discussion every week but there is only one midterm and a final that are straight from the study guide and reading quizzes. Benefitted my personal life as well
Overall, he is a solid professor. You have to work to get a good grade but he is understanding and a pretty chill guy.

I took EXSC 387 online as an elective. The course hasn't been updated since 2001. The data is all from 1990. He taught me nothing useful - I learned more from reading 3 books just for fun. Tests are full of random facts, but the TA review made them easy.
Super easy and the course work is very light. Make sure to focus on the quiz questions because they make up half of the finals. Also don't turn in anything late!
This class had awesome Ta's, and it was clear what was due each week. If you keep up with the readings and weekly assignments it is very doable!

I took this as a general ed for Social science, and not only was it super easy and chill, but I found the course to be very informative and we had clear objectives for each chapter we read.  Would definitely recommend him for this class, only downside is the textbook had to be purchased through him, but otherwise, can‘t recommend him enough!

My absolute favorite professor at BYU! He not only cares about the body, but treats it like the gift it is. He knows so much about wellness. I love learning about what he has to say on the Compression of Morbidity. Every module made me think really hard about how im living my life. I have changed a lot of my habits because of this course.

This class was honestly so great! There isn't too much to do and no busy work which I like. The quizzes are open note and so you can always do well on those if you look at the material. The exams are based on random statistics/small details that just had to be memorized, which is what caused me to get an A- but other than that, the class was great.

This was one of my favorite classes I have taken at BYU. Pro. Hager was very accessible out of class and always willing to help if there was a concern or question. The class material itself was easy to learn, and there was an easy one page writing assignment and discussion due each week.

This is the second class I've taken from Ron Hager and it's easy. Weekly assignments are a discussion post a quiz and sometimes a 1 page paper; rarely took more than 30 minutes. Exams are straight forward and the TAs tell you what you need to know. I never had to read the textbook since the information is on canvas.

Dr Hager created a very comprehensible and cleanly organized course that was easy to follow and fun to learn about. Overall, he is a remarkable teacher who is willing to work with students, be forgiving, help with grades, and listen to concerns. Would highly HIGHLY recommend.

I took this class online and it wasn't too much work, just a lot of textbook reading. For tests, review the study guide, slides provided by the TA, and, most importantly, the reading quizzes. Overall, the class wasn't too hard, but I wasn't super engaged with the subject matter. Also, found it odd that the textbook was written by the professor.

I learned a lot of valuable material through this course but you have to read and memorize a lot. Lots of the studies are outdated but they do help you understand the material. The assignments are fun and i enjoyed them but the examinations are extremely long and specific. The TA is amazing. Overall, I enjoyed the class but get ready to read.
Easiest online class I've taken at BYU
Such a chill class, literally spent like an hour a week on it and got an A

He is really nice and definitely passionate about his subject! I took this class in person, and I have heard it is better than taking it online since we get extra credit. I studied a bit before every class for the quizzes and got a lot of extra credit and that also made studying for the midterm easy! If you're good at memorizing, this is an easy A
Do like rinse and repeat nonsense? Do you like reading out dated studies? Do you enjoy doing discussion boards??? Then this class is a perfect fit for you.

Took this as an online class and it was actually super easy but meaningful. I learned a lot and it helped me improve my health and wellness. Easy A but not a useless class. Just textbook readings every week that aren't very long and you write a reflection. 2 hours tops of homework a week

Easiest class ever. I spent 1 hour a week on this class. You have to buy the $100+ online textbook written by Profesor Hager and the extent of your learning is just reading the textbook. Each week there is an online discussion board and a 1 page reflection assignment which gets pretty repetitive.

The textbook for this class is the only textbook that I have actively enjoyed reading. There is 1 midterm and 1 final. Each week there is a chapter of the textbook to read, an ungraded quiz, a discussion post, and a 1 page summary of what you learned. That's it. The TA reviews are super helpful for the exams.

This class was super simple. It took me like 60-90 minutes a week. He is very monotone, but you learn very cool stuff, and the quizzes are open book, which helps you know what he wants you to know, but get a good grade. TAs were all super helpful too.

This online class with Prof. Hager is a breeze. The workload is manageable, and the tests are easy if you prepare properly. Definitely check out Unstuck study for helpful study tools alongside the course materials.

Exsc 221 was exactly what I wanted out of a GE. It was full of real-life applications that changed my thinking about how I ate and exercised for the better. I was able to get all of the work done for the week in 2-3 hours, and I appreciated the flexibility since it was all online. Exams were worded weirdly but material reused from ungraded quizzes.
Great TAs saved me! such a cool class too
So much extra credit that an A is super possible!
not sure why this appears twice but this class was awesome and so easy!!
Very open schedule especially with tests, you can get ahead and basically take them when you want. super easy class

I asked ronald to re take a test after an emergency happened during that testing week and he was very unsympathetic to my cause. Tests also count for about 80% of your grade. 

Additionally, he makes you spend $80 on a useless textbook you'll never end up using. (yes he wrote it)

If any other students are considering taking this class- DONT!

I actually loved this course so much!!! The textbook was expensive but I really enjoyed reading it every week. This class has a consistent work load and is quite stress free considering its a 3 credit class. I very much recomend.
Very clear expectations! Very helpful as well.
SO EASY. learn a lot too. chill online class
not sure why there's two of these but he's for real amazing! Easy class I'd for sure take.
Textbook was included, cool class, I'd take it over the summer or spring as it's offered year round and not that much work at all. Super easy
In person was awesome. SO MUCH extra credit that it's impossible not to do well. I'm sure the online course isn't bad too
Awesome class! Great one to take in the spring or summer as it still isn't a ton of work even with everything being double speed
Not sure why there's two of these but seriously he's awesome! One of the nicest guys on campus
Awesome professor. Has the opportunity for lots of bonus points in the in-person version of the class so I'd do that one but online is probably great too!

I highly recommend this class! Not only is it really applicable and useful information, the class is so easy and enjoyable. The assignments actually help you learn and aren't just busy work. You read a chapter of the textbook, do a couple activities that take like 10 minutes and write a reflection with super clear prompts. Super easy.
Funny and great guy, lots of extra credit is possible. Would 10/10 recommend taking the class, pretty easy stuff

Took this class in person and it was awesome. Extra credit on almost every quiz makes a huge difference and a booster to your grade. Not sure why he has anything but 5s on here, easy class and a great guy
Absolutely awesome professor to take any class from. Not sure why he has any negative reviews. Most chill guy ever and the class was cake. Also took 387 from him and it was very similar

Overall solid course. However, a lot of the textbook doesn't track with current science and good recommendations for health and wellness. An example is recommending 50g of protein per day, which everyone knows is way too low for optimal health and fitness.
Dr. Hager was so great. He cares for his students and the subject. Tests are easy if you prepare appropriately. Highly recommend this class!

There is a quiz and discussion every week which were manageable and not difficult to get 100%s on. There are 3 exams total and they are pretty hard. They weigh a lot grade-wise so unless you do super well, they tank your grade. The questions have tricky wordings and they test you on obscure things talked about once. Content was good and applicable.

The class itself is pretty interesting. However, almost every study is super outdated and you have to read a lot of them. Work isn't bad and it's organized, but the exams were not very fun. It's a lot of memorizing old statistics and random facts. Learned a lot of important things though.

An awesome professor. Pop quizzes were bad at first but literally all the answers are from the notes, just got to look at everything. His humor is pretty interesting but I found him funny. Also, super caring and a great guy.

Professor Hager did so good with this online class. It's set up so it is super easy to learn and understand what's going on. A manageable workload as well. It is 100% possible to get an A in this class, I just didn't apply myself very much lol. It was my first semester, and I was taking 13 in-person credits and kept forgetting about this one.

This class was super easy. One page assignment per week and 2 discussion posts. There was one midterm and one non-cumulative "final" exam. My advice is to obviously do the assignments and then just memorize the TA reviews/study guide. I never read, only skimmed so I could complete assignments.

This is the second class I have taken from Hager and both classes I have enjoyed! It helps that I find exercise science interesting but I have enjoyed learning from him and his assignments feel intentional. I never felt like I was doing busy work. I didn't interact with Hager much as this was an online class but when I did he was great.

I think a lot of people rated this class poorly because they were expecting an easy A and didn't do the work. Exams are not bad if you just do the assignments throughout the week. Just actually study... *eye roll*. I also really enjoyed the material! I felt like I could start applying what I was learning in the class right away.

Save yourself and don't. Ridiculous tests. A required reading segment suggested keeping clothes that were too small too encourage weight loss. The research we read was outdated. I overheard him hating on queer individuals and "woke" ideologies with other exercise science professors in the hallway... unprofessional.

Tests are hard and ask for a lot of random facts over concepts so study hard for those. Information in the course also seemed a little outdated. Took it as a gpa booster and that was a mistake. Even if you score perfectly on all of the assignments you still have to pull an A on every test to get an A in the course.

Professor Hager is not super fun to listen to, and sometimes explains things like there's only one right way to be healthy, but the class was easy. Assignments are pretty much the same every week which is nice because you know what to expect. Review the quizzes and go to the TA reviews and you'll be fine for the exams.

My class was online so I didn't meet the professor. The tests were almost insultingly easy. Just be aware of the required textbook. felt like the entire point of this class was to get me to spend almost 100 dollars on a textbook that the professor himself wrote and can't be bought anywhere else, and now can't really be resold. I felt scammed.

the professor is not involved, all communication go through his TA's, which has been unreliable. It has been hard to figure out what is expected of us, and how he wants us to do the assignments. Not a clear course

All I have to say is that the tests are really unfair and heavily weighted into your grade. The quizzes and assignments are barely worth anything so don't spend a lot of time on them-- they won't really matter in the end grade-wise anyways. Terrible pedagogy.

The only complaint I have is the lack of variety in this class. We pretty much only did the same 2 assignments for each unit and sometimes there was something else as well. It was a good class and I learned a lot but I started getting tired of the same thing haha

This class was very informative and basically just encourages you to live a healthy lifestyle. Tests are not too difficult so do the practice questions! You will see them on the test again. Fill out the study guide that is sent out and you will be fine. Only took me about 2 hours a week to do the weekly reflection and discussion board.

Hager is a very nice guy and really cares about you. Lectures were super boring though, and his tests were way harder than what you would expect in this class. Pop quizzes happen very often to BEWARE and they're not that easy.

Super easy class, probably spent an hour-ish every week. Exams weren't too bad, but sometimes the grading on the reflection assignments every week was a bit nit-picky (but that's also my own spaciness). Interesting class tho whether you're an exercise science major or not. Recommend for everyone!

The class is pretty easy for the homework and quizzes. The tests are pretty unfair though, you have to memorize basically every part of every study he gives you (which is 3-5 per week) in order to do good on the tests. Professor Hagar doesn't really interact with the class at all. I would recommend taking a different class.

Awesome online course. Info is presented simply. You have to read a lot, but you can skim the studies if you make sure to read the material provided by Hager. Tests are very similar to the weekly quizzes. If you have good background in anatomy, physiology, and nutrition this will be an easy course.

This class is really easy and interesting. It is pretty much reading the textbook and completing a few assignments including a weekly one-page paper. The only downside is the expensive online textbook.

EASY online class, spent maybe an hour a week on the work. You gotta buy the expensive, professor written online textbook which sucks, but use control F and you can find all the answers for the weekly homework. Tests are easy, look up a Quizlet and that's basically all the answers. Professor seems like a nice guy, never really interacted with him.

Thought this class would be interesting but, NO. If you take it, do not purchase the 2000+ page text book. waste of money. Tons of busy work! The tests were the most frustrating part for me. All our reviews did was tell us to re read the text book smh. Many test questions were unheard of and opinionated. If you take this class, you're on your own.

This was a great class for social science credit. Spent 1-2 hours a week. Material was interesting and helpful! An online textbook that cost $80 is required though. For the test he gives you possible test questions in "self checks" and there are helpful quizlets. Exams proctored but you can take them anywhere it is quiet and you are alone!

this professor was absolutely awful. Had no interaction with his students at all and the online course was outdated and extremely boring. Many of the test questions were not even discussed in the textbook and the answers to them were opinion based which doesn't work if we never get to see or meet with our professor.

Super great class. Everything was simple and very clear each week. You don't have to spend much time per week on the work. I usually just do it in an hour or so on one day. Interesting content too! Super fun and easy but useful class! No matter your major, this class would be amazing for you. Ron is awesome!

Overall a good and average class, I will say I felt the textbook is super repetitive. Also, the e-textbook was like $80 (which is a lot for an e-book) and I felt like the quality was terrible, and it was written by the professor, just a waste of money for a GE class. The Canvas course was convenient though.

This was seriously one of the best classes I've taken at BYU. I took this online during summer term so it was fast paced, but everything was due on fridays so it was easy to keep up in the class. The TA's were helpful as well and I learned a lot

Easy class honestly and a great one to take during spring term. It is mostly busy work, each week you will have a group discussion and a one page, single-spaced, paper to turn in. It is kind of a lot if you take it during spring but it is very easy. The content is interesting as well. Tests are literally so easy, just review study guide!

Professor Hager is passionate and enjoys the lecture material. He sometimes gets off track during lecture but it is mostly cool stuff he is talking about. There are only 3 big grades for the exams and then a small percentage of your grade is a project and quizzes. Overall, Professor Hager is kind, understanding, and just an outstanding guy.

Every week you have a discussion response, a one-page response based on questions from the chapter of the textbook, and one quiz that can be taken as many times as you want. There is one midterm and a final. It was a pretty easy class! I had very little interaction with the teacher and TAs, so you're basically on your own.
Doctor Hager is a a wonderful professor. He has a great sense of humor and always has a good story to share. He makes the material entertaining. Definitely worth taking this class from him.

This class was pretty easy considering it was online. You have to read the textbook, do a discussion, and write a one page paper single-spaced every week. If no other Social Science classes interest you, take this one, you can pass it easily!

I recommend this class for your social sciences credit! The class was easy and applicable. My TA was great! Very responsive and helpful. If you read and do the assignments, it's an easy A. Don't do what I did and forget a week though, because that will bring your grade down a bit. It's hard to forget about the assignments though

A relatively easy class as long as you read the book/do work. Ended up being my favorite class this semester. The material is pretty engaging and you can tell that Prof Hager is really passionate ab what he teaches. There are only two tests (midterm and noncumulative final) and the reviews prepare you perfectly. Def recommend for an online course!!

This class was both hard and easy. It was easy in they were really loose on grading and got 100% on most of my work, but it was a ton. I had to write a short paper (among some other things) every week so if you're okay writing that much every week, be my guest. Tests weren't too bad though, just fill out the study guide and review the self checks.

I've taken a few other classes from Hager and have had great experiences in all of them. This class was full of great info, but the information that was tested on the exams was really random and pointless in my opinion. He didn't test on concepts, but rather specific statistics from each of the lessons. I wouldn't recommend taking the class.

I took an online version of this class and never actually interacted with Prof Hager a single time. The class is an easy A, I spent maybe 2 hours max a week doing the total homework and readings. Some of the homework is pure busy work, but it still isn't hard. This is a great class to take if you need the general or credit.

Really nice class, with honestly life changing material. Not too much homework to be done either. Tests were definitely harder than they were in 221, so make sure you actually study kinda hard for them. Great to take if you have other heavy classes this semester.

Took EXSC387 (BYU online) and EXSC 221 (Ind. Study) from Hager. Great professor who is passionate about what he's teaching. Content is interesting and applicable to every day life. Would absolutely take another class from him.

So insanely easy. If youre looking for 3 credits that require no effort, science of wellness is it. I honestly didnt read the textbook, most of it is common knowledge. You do discussion posts and a reflection paper on each chapter and thats it. Theres a paper but it took me less than an hour to write. The tests took me about 30 min. Sooo easy!

Professor Hager's science of wellness class is one of the easiest classes I have taken. It's very clear and structured and you know exactly what you need to get done. It's easy to get into a routine and complete assignments quickly. You learn a lot about how to better your health. The TA's also create great study guides for the tests.
This class is super easy. If you do the assignments on time and read the textbook, you will get an A

I preferred other classes Professor Hager has taught. This one was fine. It was fairly easy, but the tests are a bit random and obscure. Normally that's not a problem, but tests make up like 80% of your grade.

If you take this class don't expect to be taught anything. All he does is make you read a bunch of articles that say the same facts over and over again. then, he will ask obscure test and quiz questions that force you to read all of the stupid readings. Honestly, he is not a teacher. All he does is give you stuff to read. I could've googled it all.

I took this class online, and it was super easy. The class is super structured, so you always know what to expect. Because it is so structured, there is no variety in assignments or activities, so it can get a bit boring and tedious. Also, I don't think the professor communicated with the students once, so it felt like the TAs did most of the work.

Super easy class. It seems like a lot of work, but the assignments are the same every week. There's a midterm and a final that make up 50% of your grade. They're both really easy, and the TA's make a really great review for it.

I could not stand this class. So much outdated information about health and no room to explore other ideas and opinions. Sure, it was easy and I spent about an hour on it every week, but I would not take this class if you are wanting to really learn about health and preventing disease.

This is a very easy A if you do the work (and the work is the same every week so once you get into a routine it feels like nothing). It was a nice way to reflect on your health. I will admit I feel like I didn't learn a ton of new concepts, but I definitely learned how to improve my health.
Ron Hager's EXSC 221 Intro class is a breeze. But it is some of the most useful information I have learned my whole time at college. I highly recommend this class.

I didn't expect to like this class but it ended up being one of my favorites! It's online so there's not lots of communication with the professor but when I did talk to him he was so nice and helpful! He's really smart, and I learned a TON! There's not really a lot of homework. This was a perfect class to take for this GE and I really loved it.
The tests are very specific, but the in person TA reviews really helped!! If you have taken microbiology, physiology, or organic chemistry, then you should be fine!

Pros: This is probably the easiest class ever. Cons: Class material is superficial. Don't expect an in-depth study of important topics; it's mostly brief, general definitions or pure opinions. The E-textbook: costs over $80 and is SUPER outdated. No, you can't borrow someone else's textbook, no you can't take the class without it. Pay to win

TAKE THIS CLASS! Not as rigorous as other exercise science classes, but still really interesting stuff! Not a ton of personal interaction but the class is very user friendly. Study guides were great representative of the classes and the weekly self checks often were helpful for studying! I would take this class again!

I truly truly loved this class. I would 100% take it again and I loved the pace of it as well. It kept me busy each week but the "busy" was stuff I was really interested in so I enjoyed it and actually looked forward to reading a chapter and doing an assignment each week. He is very passionate about wellness. He's a little monotone sometimes.

Easiest class ever. Took me a 1-2 hrs to finish whole week of class. I enjoyed the discussions with other students. Just do the textbook reading and skip the podcast videos. Easy class if you're looking for one

Not only is this a great class where you learn a lot of applicable info, its a pretty easy class. Because I took the online class, I mainly interacted with the TAs but if you email them a question, they will respond. If you memorize the study guides, you will do well on the test. Go to TA test reviews!!!!! (they sometimes tell you answers)

Prof Hagers course is one of my favorite that I have taken thus far. The information is so applicable to our daily lives and although theres a bit of textbook reading, it really doesnt take too long. The quizzes are basically half of the questions on the midterm and final. Definitely would take another class from him.

I liked this class and definitely learned a ton. There was a decent amount of busy work and I didn't always like reading the outdated health studies. But overall I liked the class. It's not hard, just go to review sessions for tests and you'll do great.

If you want to get an easy A, take this class.  If you want to do a bunch of B.S. assignments on a weekly basis, this is the class for you.  Heres how the class works:  Each week you have to complete one reflection assignment (one page single spaced essay) and make three comments on the discussion board.  Lots of busy work. I wouldnt take it.
I enjoyed this class. I'm hoping to go d1 in collage and study sports science and this was my first collage online course. He was pretty good

This is a class that you can definitely take online. Not much to do each week, it probably took me 2 hours at the most to get stuff done. The only reason I didn't like Hager was because he teaches according to his own opinion. It's difficult to do well on tests unless you know exactly what he believes about the topic.

Great man, awful class. I took it through independent study so that might be a huge reason why, but it was literally just reading the textbook he wrote (that was very redundant) and writing essays at the end of the chapters. It wouldn't be as bad if it didn't take like a week to read each chapter. They were ridiculously long and painful to read.

He's a great guy with a soft heart, but we were many days behind schedule because he likes to tell stories....a lot of stories. You do have an almost daily quiz at the beginning of class on the previous lecture, but other than that there's not a ton of outside work. It's a fairly easy A if you show up consistently.

Ron Hager designed the class, doesn't actually grade. He does upload lectures though... I don't even watch them because he talks so slow. Every week you upload a 1 page single spaced paper answering six questions or so. They're not difficult, but kind of long. The tests are decent and there is a final paper as well. Good class to improve wellness!

I loved this class! Although he doesn't give clear study guides you can get an A by studying PowerPoints and knowing basics about the material. Little interaction between student and professor, but he is extremely smart and hilarious which makes for a great professor during lecture!

Dr. Hager is the bomb! He is hilarious. He was SO HAPPY to have me come in and chat during his office hour. His lectures were fascinating and even spiritually uplifting. All you had to do to get an A is study the powerpoints for an hour or two before the test. Whether you already eat healthy or not, you will enjoy his lectures if you listen.

Professor Hager does not give feedback on assignments and he does not interact with students at all. Assignments are repetitious, which makes them simple, however, little is actually learned. The exams are given without preparing you and study guides are vague at best.

Most of the class was interacting with the TA's because of the volume of the class, and I only interacted with the professor when I emailed him a question. This class is wonderful! It taught me so many positive and healthy mindsets to have towards life, and has given me so much perspective. Even if you don't need the credit, take this class!

I took this course online, which I usually do not like online courses but I liked this one a lot! There is quite a bit of work involved but it is easy and interesting! The tests were easy if you just studied the study guide and the self check quizzes.

Daily quizzes of previous class's material but around 9 are dropped from final grade. I didn't buy the book for it, slides about the relevant chapters are posted and discussed. Almost no discussion, all lecture, somewhat opinionated, seemingly repetitive info. Tests were alright but had some confusing questions, class reviews weren't very helpful.

I really enjoyed this class. The workload wasn't too much, and with it being an online class I was able to work on it whenever I wanted to. The weekly assignments were easy, and study guides for the two tests were given. Everything I learned in class I can use beyond the course.

Dr. Hager is a funny guy and passionate about his material. Leads to extremely long lectures (big room  zero engagement) Readings and quizzes were easy. There are three non comprehensive exams for the whole course, each worth 27% of the grade. Classic crunch of a bunch of powerpoint's and article abstracts to prepare for tests. Fun diet assignment

This is a fairly easy and pretty interesting class! You take tons of quizzes but he only graded the top 16 so in the end I would say most if not all have over 100% on the quiz section. I didn't do much work out of class and it was a lot of life-applicable information. The TAs will save your grade if you listen.

I have really enjoyed this class. There are a lot of in class quizzes at the beginning of class, but just review the slides from the time before and you'll be good. So, it is important to go to class because of those quizzes. One project which is easy, a decent amount of reading, but not hard. TA reviews for the tests are great and are in class.

If you are looking for an easy A and also the biggest waste of time, Hager is your guy. He cancelled class more often than not and when we did have it we would watch Ted talks. I was disappointed because I was excited to learn about the content, but felt I did not get my college tuition's worth out of the class.

Hager is easily the best teacher I've had at BYU. Super passionate about health. I have learned so much from him and his tests are very fair. If you go to class and study, even just a little, you'll do great.
Take Hager. Nothing else needs to be said. Such and easy and chill class. Easy A.

Professor Hager is a great guy and really loves teaching this class, which makes it enjoyable. He had a quiz almost every class on material from the previous lecture, but they weren't difficult and often is very forgiving with bonus questions and drops 4-5 of them. Good class, good teacher, not very difficult if you pay attention.

Pro. Hager's a nice guy and all, but his lectures were incredibly boring.  I tried to take notes in class, but he goes off topic forever and then we're quizzed on the previous class material everyday that we weren't able to go over.  Just read the class slides before class for those quizzes.

Dr. Hager himself will tell you that this class teaches you basically two things you already know: eat right and exercise. The rest of it is basically knowing the relevant stats from the slides. Dr. Hager hits you over the head with those two principles so much that it is a class that can actually sink in and inspire you to change the way you live.

Dr. Hager is a nice guy and very passionate about this subject, but I didn't like his class. You have to be present in every class to take quiz based on extremely obscure details and figures from studies you're supposed to have read. His tests are easy, but an A is a 95, so if you mess up at all, you're toast. Lecture is very dry.

Go to every class early and memorize details from the previous class like percentages and numbers and you will be fine on his quizzes. He gives lots of extra credit to buffer your grade. TA reviews will save your bacon. DO NOT take this class lightly, he will teach you SOOO much about life and perspective. Dr. Hager is an amazing professor.
I did not like the class. You have to prepare for a quiz every time and they are not easy. The lectures are boring and the slides don't make much sense.

Honestly love this guy. He's so cool, he's real, he wants you to do well. Quizzes frequently in class, if you want an easier way to get an A make sure you pay attention in class to do well on quizzes because they're worth 15% of your grade. If you study for exams you should do well. He gives great extra credit opportunities.

TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HAGER. He is such a great guy and is really funny too. He only gives a couple assignments for the whole semester that aren't too hard. I would love to take another class from him. He understands students and makes things fun and interesting. I also want to be a healthier person.

Good professor. Class isn't very tough at all, you just need to show up since there are quizzes at least 2 times a week at the beginning of class. Always goes over the time limit on lectures. Nice guy and cares about what he is teaching.

Dr. Hager is very simple. It is an easy A. He gives quizzes every class at the beginning but you can leave after and he doesn't care. Beware, he makes you do a near-vegetarian diet for 4 weeks. Don't bother buying the textbook. I never touched it.
Easiest class ever!   only reason you need to show up to class is for the quizzes and he knows it and is ok with that.
I took this at the same time a friend took another teacher's 387 course. We both slacked, I got an A- and my friend got a B-. This is the easiest 387 class available.

Professor Hager is passionate about this topic and an interesting teacher. Class had attendance quizzes (but only the top 12 were kept), a project, and 3 tests. The class was a little disorganized at times, and tests were guaranteed to have a couple questions that were never covered. Do the readings and pay attention in class and you will do great.

20 attendance quizzes (only 12 count towards grade). Two midterms, 90 questions each, all multiple choice and T/F. This class is pretty easy. Hager's lectures can kinda be all over the place and without focus, but he puts the slides online. His lectures can be fun, though. Funny guy. He gets pretty excited about health.

18 attendance quizzes (only 10 count toward your grade). 3 tests are doable: incomprehensible in some sections, absurdly easy in others. Only one project besides that. Sometimes Hager puts color charts on the test in black and white, making them impossible to read. You will see material he didn't cover on almost every test. Read the articles!
Awesome, super laidback professor. Very interesting material. Didnt have to study too much for tests. I really enjoyed my time in this class and learned a lot. Easy A.

LOVED Dr. Hager! This class is life-changing and he is so enthusiastic about exercise and wellness. He is funny, helpful, straightforward, has had lots of experience in what he is teaching and he is so positive. He even brought in the author of the book, "The Culprit and the Cure", we used. Take this class! You will become more healthy for sure.

I really like Dr. Hager. This class was really easy, but also really informative. The tests were a tiny bit harder than I thought they would be, but I got b's on all of them. I learned a ton and didn't hardly have to do any work! What more could you ask for? Hager is a really cool guy and the class is really low stress.

This class is the bomb! Coach Hager actually knows what he's talking about. I learned more in the two months in class than the 6 years i played tennis in middle and high school. Plus, the exam is really easy and he'll tell you the answers word for word. Highly recommend to anyone needed an easy GE credit!

Ron Hager is the freaking man. The guy loves tennis and knows what he's talking about. One of the most interesting guys I ever talked to. Seriously Ron is tight. He loves his students and really just wants to chill with them. Keep representing Ron!

In all fairness, it was this class I hated, not him per say. It is taught by a different professor each week and frankly, it sucks. It's too hard to get help, you never know how to prepare for tests, assignments are fruitless and I totally hated it. If you have another way to fulfill the University CORE requirement, please do it.

Intro to Allied Health Professions was an easy class. A new speaker/profession would show up and you had to write down notes. Bam....Once a week. Easy. The Final is a self-evaluation, no biggie. Cool to learn about other professions but honestly it was too boring for me. I should have brought a pillow to class.

Motor learning: Great, easy class. We took a quiz every day, but once you took 1 or 2 you knew what to expect and it was pretty easy to get 100% (the 2 lowest quiz grades were dropped). Tests were straight off the study guide. There was no textbook. It's kind of boring sometimes, but he's really interested in the subject and we do cool labs.

I LOVE Dr. Hager!  He is a wondeful man and a good teacher.  He has helpped and inspired me in my accademic and career choices.  He is funny too!  This class and the labs are fun.  I reccomend any class from Dr. Hager, especially this one.

He is seriously the coolest professor, way funny! The best tennis instructor out there. His more serious classes are a little too easy and I'm not sure I learned all that much, but he's a great guy, i will definately take future classes from him.
best way to get an a is to do this class online.  you can get most of the class done in roughly 2 hours.  keep up with the log writing and you'll be in great shape(all kinds).

Two comments: First, take the online section!  It's super easy and you can do tests and quizzes whenever you want.  Second, the tests are harder than you might think, so make sure you review well for them.
easy on line. you can finish early in the year so that you arent stressed to finish the quizes during finals week
Extremely easy class, if you take it online (which is the best option).  It doesn't take long to complete either.
Easy easy easy class! Take it online! I hardly had to do anything and got an A.
best teacher around. will do anything to help. funny as all get out too

I struggled to feel like Ron was teaching us anything that I couldn't learn on my own from YouTube. Class felt useless because he spent most of the time yapping. We didn't even touch Pro Tools until midterms. This class is not suited for anyone outside of the commercial music major. We never used the textbook. He's pretty checked out of school.

When I took the class (Fall 2021), half of the semester was just student presentations. When HE's teaching, it's incredibly engaging and fun, if a little dry. But the student presentations were just people awkwardly reading Wikipedia copy & pasted onto a PowerPoint. Really disappointing class and I hope he's removed the student presentations.

I LOVE this guy. He is a gifted AMAZING musician with a neat perspective on things. I genuinely gained a huge love for jazz and Black history. Easiest class I've ever taken. No need to buy textbook just attend class consistently the first half and then occasionally (once every 2 weeks or so) after group presentations begin. You won't regret taking.

Super easy class, a few memorization based tests, one presentation and then going to three concerts is pretty much the whole grade. Prof Saltmarsh is a great guy, clearly passionate about the subject, but the class was overall pretty boring & super easy to skip. Good general class though, I'd recommend it. Don't buy the $120 textbook-no need at all

Intro to Jazz w/ Saltmarsh was by far the easiest class I've taken at BYU. I spent abt 10hrs total on homework outside of class throughout the semester. Went to class once a week & didn't buy the textbook (I knew nothing about jazz), but still got an A.  Be there for your presentation, review midterm slides, & go once a week and you'll get an A.

I only give him a 5/5 for being so easy. He's not a particularly gifted teacher, and the lectures were pretty boring so I spent most of my time doing other homework. The only classes you really need to go to are when you're presenting or for the test reviews. If you memorize the study guide (quizlet) you'll ace the tests.

Not an easy A class because you need a 95 to get an A. Rent the textbook from chegg (not BYU bookstore). Most of the class is just students giving presentations so attendance is only mandatory on the days you are presenting. Tests are online but video proctored. There is listening, multiple choice, and a written question on the exams.

This is a great GE class! There are 3 midterms and a final each with a listening section for certain songs and a multiple choice portion but they are not too hard. PLUS there are study guides with everything you need to know. Prof Saltmarsh is also just a super cool guy and you should go to the concerts he performs in throughout the semester!

Take this class!!! Super easy GE. Professor Saltmarsh is super knowledgeable and passionate about jazz and his lectures were always so fun. Study guides covered everything that would be on the exams. Kind of a hard grader on the concert reports. Other than that, easy A!

He knows his stuff about jazz and it's a pretty easy GE. Unfortunately I took it in the first semester he taught it and the way the class was structured left a lot to be desired. Overall though, it's an easy class and the content is enjoyable if you're interested in jazz. Lots of extra credit at the end of the semester.

Professor saltmarsh is a very sweet and cool guy but he only taught for half of the semester, the other half was the students teaching giving presentations. The lectures could sometimes be a little boring. The tests are very doable and easy. There were a couple of opportunities for extra credit which were great. Overall the class was pretty good

He is a very talented musician- but not so much a teacher. Everything in the lecture was in the textbook so going to class was not very beneficial. Interesting topics but I felt like there could have been a lot more depth. Half the semester was student group presentations about musicians so not really worth the tuition money unfortunately.
An easy A class

Ron knows his stuff.  He grades by potential - so it may seem a bit subjective, but put do your best and put the work in, and it's both worth it and a lot of fun.  It was his first semester teaching, so he still needs to develop a "repertoire" of things to teach.  But he has a very fun and very musical personality.  You'll love him and the class!

Considering the fact that this was Ron's first semester at the University, he did a fantastic job making the subjects come alive and giving us interesting and challenging projects to complete.  He's not a super easy grader, so don't expect him to hand you points if you haven't earned them.  This class will take up some of your time.
Easy class, pretty much gave us the test, homework, and quiz answers every class. If you miss a few assignments its hard to catch up, but other than that great class

Professor Harris is a really funny guy and his class is super easy. More than half of the time he went over the homework in class so you didn't have to do any at home. He even gave the whole class 100% on a test because we got behind. If you show up to class and pay attention then this class is really easy.

I took Intro to Geology. He's hilarious and passionate about Geology. He cares about his students and is really friendly and caring. He's super helpful and makes sure we understand concepts. For almost all assignments he goes over the answers and gives us chances to change our answers. He uses the platform tophat instead of learning suite.

I absolutely loved Spanish 321 with him. I could really tell that he cared about the success of his students and did everything he could to help us.
