There are a lot of reading assignments that take a good amount of time that are important for the discussions in class but most of them were enjoyable. Overall the class was fairly easy and enjoyable.
Gives homework and then reviews it in class which was very helpful. Reviews with students for tests. Explains grammer concepts in and out of class in both languages.

His spanish is pretty good and he's good at explaining things. Most homework is done on canvas, and it's pretty straightforward! Maybe 2 hours of homework a week. If you go to class and follow the instructions you'll get an A.

He's great if this is your first Spanish class. A lot of fun and gets everyone involved. There's tons of small assignments that aren't too hard so the test/projects don't hit your grade too hard. Exams aren't bad if you study for a couple hours. Class introduces you to Spanish literature which is tricky, but he makes it easy to ease into. So solid

Outstanding teacher who really wants you to succeed. Focuses a lot on the gospel and love participation when talking about the readings (poems and short stories). He cares for his students and is willing to help a lot! For the tests, make sure to go over the study guide well and personally study the grammar and you'll do fine!

Guys you have to take a religion class from prof Barron.  He is super funny and fosters amazing discussion.  If you want a fun religion class that's not stressful, take this one.  I've taken lots of other religion professors and they make everything super difficult, but I really loved Ross Baron's class.  Also there's not exams which is awesome.
Best religion professor at BYU. No exams, focused more on just being inspiring and teaching the doctrine and feeling the spirit. These bad reviews are just to make less people take the classes.

Ross Baron is one of the most unaccomplished professors at BYU. There is nothing you will gain from any of his classes that you wouldn't already have from just reading the course materials. I cannot emphasize enough how pointless taking a course from Ross Baron is, as it ranks among the worst experiences I've had at BYU.

Brother Baron is very passionate about what he teaches. His lectures are very engaging and the work for the class is very light and easy to navigate. There are no tests but attendance is mandatory. There is a pre class reading every class and 2 longer writing assignments. The class is very fun and engaging.

This was my first experience with a religion class at BYU. Brother Baron knew everyone's names by the third day of class. The class is super discussion based, so come to class. No tests, only a reading and associated writing assignment before each class, plus one or two larger assignments throughout the year. Brother Baron is super knowledgeable.

He has such unique insight and does a good job of leading class discussions. It's a discussion heavy class which is nice because it opens up a space for all kinds of questions. Brother Baron also cares about you a lot. He knew the whole classes names by day 3!

Narcissist know it all. If you have a different opinion or conclusion then him he will try and embarrass you by telling you how smart he is. His view of religion is one sided and bias. Does not allow students to have a dissenting opinion. Outside of church correlated material he has done little to no research to the wider scholarly evidence.

Brother Baron is awesome! I had him for REL A 211. In my opinion, this class was exactly what a religion class should be. It was mostly open discussions, and I always felt comfortable participating. Brother Baron is VERY knowledgeable about the scriptures and teaches in an accessible way! He even learned everyone's names by the 2nd day.

His teaching style didn't connect well with our age group. He often let the class talk about topics that felt surface-level or off-track. I was really looking forward to this course after transferring from BYU–I, but it didn't feel like a typical BYU Provo religion class—more like a seminary setting. I wouldn't take him again.

I dislike the instructor's teaching style. He relies too much on students during class. I don't pay tuition to learn from peers' comments. If you like being put on the spot or constantly contributing, this might be your class, but I wouldn't recommend it. He tries too hard to sound smart and too little to connect with students. Big disappointment.

Brother Baron is honestly the best religion professor I have had at BYU. He does not do exams, rather short easy reflection papers that are super easy and honestly inspiring to do. Grade is based upon doing the reading and attendance. TAKE THIS COURSE W BROTHER BARON

Class is laid out so you can learn by the spirit. Participating in class will help you get the most out of it. Attendance is mandatory, but the class is awesome and it't fun to be there are participate. He really makes you think about gospel concepts, but it isn't stressful if you don't know everything.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. The lectures often feel disorganized, and he frequently relies on students to fill class time instead of delivering structured and uplifting content. As a senior, I can confidently say that this class was one of my least enjoyable experiences at BYU. The readings and assignments felt like busy work, and the teacher was boring
My favorite religion professor. He is so engaging in class and has super interesting insights.
Incredible classes! He is full of faith and knows so much which amazes everyone every single lecture. The class is not hard, it's easy to get a good grade.

Probably the best professor I've had yet. He cares so much for his students. Natural scriptorian. Charismatic lecturer. Listens carefully and responds thoughtfully to questions. It's very clear to me that he has incredible knowledge, faith, and love. Excellent guy and excellent professor.

Brother Baron is so awesome! His class is really interesting I had AH HAH moments nearly every class cause he knows so much. Attendance is SUPER important in this class, but there are no tests only two 1000 essays. Each day before class you do the reading and a 200 word assignment. This was one of my fav classes of my college career.

AMAZING CLASS! It changed me... I thought we'd be graded on the readings but we were not. The class is demanding, just like any other SFL class. The tests are long essay questions on which I spent hours but loved! I always got A's on those. Show up, do the readings, and follow his instructions for papers and tests and you'll get an A!

Roy is one of my favorite professors at BYU! His coding class had a lot of work, but Roy is very understanding and really cares about making sure his students succeed. He takes class time to give everyone personal advice about applying to graduate school which I really appreciated. Hard work, but he cares a lot about the students!

Class involved coding a large number of articles for Dr. Bean's research. Not the most interesting capstone class, but it was alright if you aren't planning on going to grad school. Would not recommend for someone who needs research experience. The coding is tedious, but you can do it from home, which was very convenient.

Honestly one of the best classes taken at BYU. Dr. Bean is an amazing professor that really makes you think. The information in this class is life changing. It should be required for all students. A few papers but they are pretty easy. You have to come to class to do well but it is so interesting that you don't want to miss.

Research class. It's only like 2-3 hours of work every week depending on the journals you are assigned to code. Easy A! This is an easy capstone and he gives invaluable advice about grad school. Hopefully you get a good partner to code with. Attendance is big and helps you. No-capstone students don't have to write a paper for the class.

LOVED this professor He''s super personable and relateable and you can tell he really knows his stuff He''s tough when it comes to tests and he definitely expects you do do the readings and participate in class but he loves hearing students opinions on the topics discussed SUPER GREAT PROFESSOR

Nice guy that keeps lectures funny and light, but is use to teaching graduate level classes. Reads from Powerpoints, few assignments, random pop quizzes, and no study guides. Tests are unclear and difficult.

Class discussions were interesting but not related to the tests. He reads from the powerpoints... and that's about all you get from him. There are hardly any assignments so your grade is based on tests. Tests are hard, even if you study. He does not give a study guide. He is not very open to feedback.

Incredible professor. His teaching was fantastic. The perspective that I received in his class changed my outlook on life and on members of other races and cultures. I highly recommend Dr. Bean's class

It was his first time teaching the course so things were a bit unorganized at times but he made class very enjoyable. Very interesting subject matter; he really challenges your ideas about race and culture that you didn't even know you had. Not too bad if you can tolerate the language of the devil.
He is a nice guy but he went off on very random tangents, a lot of very boring literature. He doesn't accept any late work, none at all which can be a pain. Nice guy tho

He really, really cares about you learning spanish. He loves you and you can tell. The coursework isn't too bad, either. The assignments are simple and straightforward, and honestly interesting if you apply yourself. A lot of what you do is application, such as the two major assignments being a short 5 minute podcast you make with a classmate.
Class is not the most organized.

Honestly he is like the cutest human ever. Did I understand at any point what was going on in this class or when things were due? no not at all, but he's really sweet and super chill about everything. As long as you do the homework you'll get a good grade. He's also super passionate and wants you to succeed

Prof Veragray is super awesome and caring! Canvas was a pain with due dates and stuff but he always worked to try and get things set up, just pay attention to the pre-work in canvas and go off those due dates, not necessarily the ones actually posted. He is super funny and wants students to succeed.

Profesor Vergaray was amazing. He is hilarious and so much fun. The only downside of this class was that the canvas system was often confusing and unorganized. However Profesor Vergaray was very helpful when the system had problems.

Hilarious and very enjoyable Professor! Makes learning very enjoyable and interactive. Tests are a very important part of the grade. Getting good grades on the test is very doable and he is very mericiful.

Professor Vergary prepares excellent and interesting lectures. He utilizes a variety of learning strategies. He makes reading and pre-class homework a priority. Doing these homeworks is crucial for success in class. He is very understanding of students needs. He loves teaching. He makes the students laugh every class.
Professor Vergaray cares about his students and wants you to really learn Spanish. He wants you to learn and use what you learn.
Light hearted and understanding. Good at teaching as well

He is very kind and always very understanding if you have any problems. He is a pretty generous grader and the assignments are pretty self-explanatory. There are a few days when the pre-class reading takes a while, but other than that you just have a few articles to read before each class. He cares deeply for the students and their success.

Recommend this class to all SPAN returned missionaries. Prof Vergaray is a riot, incredibly witty and just whimsical. Very loving man and helps you grow your love for latino culture. The course includes a lot of group discussions and projects but is doable and rewarding.
Profe Vergaray is among the best professors I've ever had at BYU. He understands how to explain the Spanish Language and is an engaging lecturer. Cannot recommend him enough!

Prof. Vergaray is THE best teacher to take 321 from. He cares so much, and really tries to make sure things are understood and that they happen. Was easy to work with when I had to miss class, and gave me a couple extensions when needed!

He is awesome, cares so much about his students and makes his lectures geared towards the tests. Excuses late work a lot too. I'm pretty sure Spanish 321 is the same Canvas course (same homework and tests) no matter who you take it from, and none of the material is difficult and there's short homework assignments that don't take very long.
Ruben Vergaray is amazing! He really cares about his student and his course is very flexible.
Professor Vergaray is probably the nicest professor I have ever had. He always puts a lot of effort into his lectures and teaches in a fun way. I would definitely recommend his class.
This is a great professor to take SPAN 321 from. Super fun class, super easy and chill.

Not hard at all, he's super entertaining as a professor and it's clear he cares about his students. He really wants you to succeed. It's not a hard work load but you just gotta do it. Some of the stuff is kind of boring but it's good review. Attendance is necessary but he doesn't really mark tardys.

I loved Professor Vergaray! He is funny and entertaining to listen to even when the lecture subjects are not very interesting. He teaches clearly and tells you what is going to be on the tests. Homework is not to bad. Expect to spend 30 - 45 minutes on homework around 3 times a week. Sometimes it's less. If you are taking span 321 take it from him!

Professor Vergaray is an amazing professor! I really enjoyed coming to his classes, he made learning spanish enjoyable and he truly just wanted us to succeed and learn. There is a fair amount of reading for the class, but I felt like it was all helpful. I highly recommend Prof. Vergaray.
I really enjoyed this class! The professor is great and you can tell that he is very caring and wants to help you succeed! I would definitely take his class again!
He was awesome; I never had a more accessible class. It takes time, and there are lots for readings but if you just take time to do the work you'll get an A no problem

Professor Vergaray truly cares about his students and is eager to help. He sets you up for success in everything you do and prepares you well for the exams. The class is pretty easy if you stay on top of assignments.

Professor Vergaray is one of the best professors I have had here at BYU. He cares so much about his students and really wants you to not only get a good grade, but actually learn Spanish. I would HIGHLY recommend that you take a class from him!
Prof. Vergaray is the best! 10/10 recommend taking it from him. He's super understanding and the assignments aren't difficult. You can also tell that he cares and wants his students to succeed.
Awesome Professor! Very good at connecting with students and having fun lectures. His reviews are very helpful for the tests and he is a very easy grader. Would definitely take him again!

I loved this class! Profe Vergaray really cares about his students and gives plenty of opportunities for them to succeed. It was a pretty easy class, we mostly read short stories and poems and discussed them in class as well as reviewed various grammatical concepts. I highly recommend Profe Vergaray for anyone looking to take SPAN 321.
He is easily one of my favorite professors. He is such a funny guy, and you can just tell he cares a lot. I felt like I learned a lot, but it was a pretty easy class. 10/10 would recommend.

Very inspirational. He always kept his classes very interesting and made us laugh even at 8:00 AM. He was very reasonable with grading, and really just wanted to help us learn. One of my favorite professors.

This professor does an awesome job of helping students succeed! It was an easier class than I expected, the assignments were very straight forward and the class is organized well! I wish I got more feedback on my writing, although I got an "A" in his course I am not sure how much I improved because of it

The class content is pretty simple, as long as you show up to class and turn in the short assignments before lecture you will pass with an A. Homework typically does not take very long and Profe Vergaray is really good at answering questions about the readings and teaching grammar principles. He cares a lot about his students and  makes class fun!

Literally the best. Genuinely cares about his students and understands that college is stressful, so he makes sure his class isn't. Teaches you exactly what you need to know to do well on the exam. Super easy grader on essays as well, but gives great feedback when you ask. SUPER smart, super spiritual, I would take every class from him if I could!

I 100% recommend taking a class from him. He is hilarious and awesome and he really wants everybody to get a good grade. He understands that you are taking lots of other classes and tries his best not to overwhelm you. He's willing to work with you on grades and he is just an awesome teacher that explains things clearly.

Professor Vergaray es lo mejor! Seriously, this guy is so caring and loves his job. He comes from a humble background and just wants you to succeed and do your best. This class is super easy, but he teaches you a lot. Do the work you're given and you'll get 100%. Best Professor for Spanish at BYU you'll find.

Professor Vergaray is one of my favorite people on Earth. His class was probably my favorite college class so far. He is wonderful at interpreting the different materials you go over: literature and art. He is very much on the students' side, is an easy grader, and prepares you well for the test. He would even tell us what to watch out for.

If you're taking SPAN 321, take it from him. He knows Spanish so well (he is a native speaker) and he really cares about YOU! If you've been wishing for a professor who truly cares and shows it, he's the one. I can't say enough good about him. Plus the class really isn't hard, you learn as much as you want to, and getting an A isn't bad at all.

Professor Vergaray is amazing. He cares about students a lot and is very willing to work with you when stuff comes up. He has beautiful spanish and is an engaging teacher 100% of the time. He's hilarious but never gets in the way of material. 5/5 would take again.

literally the best professor ever. soooo much extra credit it's impossible to fail unless you do absolutely nothing. i've never left a rating for any professor but I had to for him because I seriously lucked out getting the chillest and kindest professor. definitely want to take from him.

Profe Vergaray is honestly the best professor I've had. Is so kind, caring, spiritual, and fun. Lets you turn in homework late, which was a lifesaver with my other classes. Tons of extra credit. Tests were not super hard either. Love this man. He's an inspiration. Truly.

Probably the best teacher i've ever had. Please do not take this from anyone else!! He really wants you to succeed in the class. His lectures are very interesting and interactive. Attendance isn't mandatory but come to class with the readings done because they are discussed in class! Honestly he made me feel more confident in myself. BLESS HIS SOUL

One of my favorite professors I've ever had. DON'T TAKE 321 FROM ANYONE ELSE. Gives tons of extra credit and deadlines are very loose. Willing to work with you and wants you to be successful. Lectures are entertaining and he is hilarious.

SPAN321 from Professor V was one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. He teaches the material well, but the workload and expectations of students are fairly low. He really is hilarious and caring. Overall, super easy but still high quality!

This guy is THE BEST!! Probably my favorite teacher so far at BYU. He is really funny and really relaxed. If you are going to take SPAN 321 I wouldn't take it from anyone else. He is seriously awesome!!!

I'm currently in his class, and I have to say, he's really funny. Like his lectures are always great and he is really easy with grading. You really dont't have any hard deadlines, he's willing to work with you. Classes are good to attend but you can miss some without falling behind. 10/10 recommend SPA321 with Prof Vergaray!

For RMs, it should be an easy class if you can easily converse in Spanish. online textbook contains all the assignments for class, the tests are over grammar and the stories you read in the textbook. This class was not hard it just took some time to do the work. make sure to read the stories multiple times before taking the tests.

This class was way too easy. I didn't learn a single new thing about speaking or writing Spanish (since I already studied it for two years as a missionary!), just about miscellaneous elements of Hispanic culture.

Everything that everyone has written is true. He is easy-going, makes class fun with jokes and media, and truly cares about students and what we're learning. He is a bit confusing sometimes when teaching grammatical principles or answering specific questions, but the class is easy enough that it's not an issue. Great choice for a 321 professor.

Professor Vergaray was by far my favorite professor this semester. He is extremely helpful and is always willing to help out when needed. He makes class fun and is good at getting everyone to participate. I would definitely recommend him to anyone planning on taking Spanish at BYU.
I really enjoyed this class ! Profe Vergarays style of teaching is very inclusive and he makes it fun !!

Class was awesome. Loved Prof. Vergaray and his style of teaching. Very caring and easy going guy, who is always willing to help those who are struggling to understand. Class load is rather light, and I didn't find anything too difficult. Wish he was teaching more Spanish classes. I'd take them from him in a heartbeat.

Great professor and I look forward in having him again. So far the semester isnt over but I feel inclined to rate him. He has a profound and diverse knowledge in Spanish literature/culture which makes understanding the language even easier. You will have hard moments but its all apart of learning a language. He really cares for you to learn :)

I took GEOL 101. There was a lot of vocab, but the tests were reasonable. Dr. Kerry does a great job of teaching the content in an understandable way and offers lots of extra credit opportunities. We also got to do some hands on work through field trips which I enjoyed.

RUN-take from ANY other professor. Friendly but poor teacher. Brilliant TAs didn't understand her disorganized typo filled assignments. Some lectures should be combined and some spread out. She asks "yeah" and most sit confused. If 1 student knows the answer, she moves on. Boring slides-nowhere near BYU level. Brutal final-70 question in 1 hour.

I took GEOG 101 from her and honestly don't reccommend to anyone. The class was doable, but unless you love geography, it's super boring and she just reads the slides the whole time. It's also heavily graded on Kahoot quizzes, so if you do poorly it will affect your grade. I'd say stay away.

Dr. Kerry is really knowledgable about statistics.  If you attend class, you'll learn everything; we only used the textbook for analysis tables. When she goes through example problems pay attention because she goes through pretty fast. If you're still confused after class, just ask for help and she's happy to give it.

Dr. Kerry is very friendly, and though she uses slide shows pretty heavily (which are interesting but can feel repetitive), she does her best to make the class enjoyable. The assignments are easy, though the data response ones can feel like busy work. She also does Kahoots throughout the semester :). Make sure to study hard for the two tests.

Dr. Kerry makes this class boring. She just reads from the slides the whole time which have paragraphs worths of info on them. No idea what to take notes on. She also doesn't know how to turn the volume down when she plays super loud music in the class. Attendance is mandatory but you could just read the slides at home and get the same out of it.

Biogeography is a fascinating subject, but Dr Kerry is NOT the teacher to take it from. She basically read from her powerpoints (which were taken from the textbook, which made the readings irrelevant) and the lectures were incredibly dull. I felt like I knew a lot more (and cared more) about biogeography than she did.

While I was an undergrad student at BYU, I took her class. Her reading material is very heavy and yet very interesting. The professor, is a very tough cookie. You have to actually learn and do the work which I really appreciate in a professor. I highly recommend her class but dont expect to get an easy A.

Dr. Kerry is a pretty good instructor. She successfully takes statistics and applies them so that they can be used geographically. She and her TA were very helpful and willing to work with students. There was a good amount of guidance for difficult projects but watch out for the final. It is a doozy.

Dr. Kerry does a great job explaining the concepts, but lecture can be extremely boring sometimes.  I feel like we didn't spend enough time on the basics and jumped into the deep end of the pool before we knew how to dog paddle.  Should be easy if you have a statistics background.  If not, good luck.

Dr. Kerry is great. She is British with a unique teaching style, but i liked it. This subject was intimidating, as I wasn't crazy about the subject, but she was fantastic. Her grading is really quite fair and consistent. I would recommend taking a class from her.

I loved Dr. Kerry!! She is british so her style of teaching was very different but it was refreshing. Her whole class is based off essay writing and evaluation. The class took work but it was well worth it. One of my favorit geography classes yet.

The assignments are easy, though the data response ones can feel like busy work. She also does Kahoots throughout the semester :). Make sure to study hard for the two tests.

Dr. Kerry makes this class boring. She just reads from the slides the whole time which have paragraphs worths of info on them. No idea what to take notes on. She also doesn't know how to turn the volume down when she plays super loud music in the class. Attendance is mandatory but you could just read the slides at home and get the same out of it.

Biogeography is a fascinating subject, but Dr Kerry is NOT the teacher to take it from. She basically read from her powerpoints (which were taken from the textbook, which made the readings irrelevant) and the lectures were incredibly dull. I felt like I knew a lot more (and cared more) about biogeography than she did.

While I was an undergrad student at BYU, I took her class. Her reading material is very heavy and yet very interesting. The professor, is a very tough cookie. You have to actually learn and do the work which I really appreciate in a professor. I highly recommend her class but dont expect to get an easy A.

Dr. Kerry is a pretty good instructor. She successfully takes statistics and applies them so that they can be used geographically. She and her TA were very helpful and willing to work with students. There was a good amount of guidance for difficult projects but watch out for the final. It is a doozy.

Dr. Kerry does a great job explaining the concepts, but lecture can be extremely boring sometimes.  I feel like we didn't spend enough time on the basics and jumped into the deep end of the pool before we knew how to dog paddle.  Should be easy if you have a statistics background.  If not, good luck.

Dr. Kerry is great. She is British with a unique teaching style, but i liked it. This subject was intimidating, as I wasn't crazy about the subject, but she was fantastic. Her grading is really quite fair and consistent. I would recommend taking a class from her.

I loved Dr. Kerry!! She is british so her style of teaching was very different but it was refreshing. Her whole class is based off essay writing and evaluation. The class took work but it was well worth it. One of my favorit geography classes yet.
L professor

Great professor! Very little HW, with optional extra practice. HW took me 1-2 hours max per week. Lecture did a great job preparing for it. Exams are all MC, though they have A-H options usually. Hardest part was the lab, especially since I had no C coding experience. Very inspirational too, and had a lot of days set aside to review. Take from him!

Hard class, but Dr. Camacho is a good lecturer and the class is overall well organized. He respects students and is willing to admit when he's made a mistake and make up for it. He seems to understand what being a student is like. He is a tough grader and there's a midterm 1 week before the final, but there are plenty of resources available.

He's not a professor that lacks knowledge in the area that he's teaching, but he does struggle to convey that info to his students. He also tends to assume that he knows what you need and goes off on a tangent that doesn't really help you and he often came off as rude to me during class and outside class.

Dr. Camacho is a great lecturer. He really knows how to teach a large class and fills the shoes of great university professor. The class content is difficult towards the beginning of the semester but slows down later. He frequently gave life advice at the beginning of each week that helped pick up your spirits and motivated you to keep trying.

Dr. Camacho gives very good lectures and listens very well to feedback from the class. He does reviews for every quiz and exam. The content is difficult, but that's the nature of the class. The labs are quite difficult if you don't stay on top of them. Usually 1 homework per lecture and 1 lab per week. Answers questions asked during lecture well.
He knows his stuff. Wasn't always able to teach the most difficult concepts, but he made class enjoyable
Dr. Camacho's silicon photonics design class was great. He was very flexible with grading and with the project details. Very interesting lectures too.

I did not like this class at all. Camacho is obsessed with proofs, and theoretical math, which isn't very helpful in teaching engineering. He would spend all of lecture doing proofs using 300 level math concepts, and spent no time teaching us what was on the homework, and what was on the tests. You have to teach yourself everything.

Dr. Christensen is a good person, but he struggles teaching to students' levels. The material is difficult and his teaching was hard to follow. At least once a class even he would confuse himself or not know the answer to one of his questions. The course is also low resource and you can't teach yourself the content without a TA. Overall, not good.

Dr. Christensen is a professional and experienced professor. However, he is not a gifted nor accessible teacher. His class is lecture heavy with no resources beyond readings and on the spot lectures. His lectures are scattered-brained and he tends to be overly repetitive and redundant in what he talks about. Well meaning, but not a good teacher.

Class structure just felt confusing, and I didn't feel like I learned much in class, besides the things I learned on my own. We had pretty good discussions in class, but the class wasn't really my favorite.

DO NOT take aristotle from him. The lectures are dry, the readings are horrible, and the tests are extremely difficult. He focuses a lot on the worst parts of aristotle (logic and metaphysics) and skips some very important things (politics).

The course idea was interesting, but the execution was terrible. It was impossible to know what to take notes on, or what mattered for the exams (which were most of the grade). Taught logic very poorly (I learned most of it on my own). No extra credit, even though students were begging for it. Posted homework 2 days before the due date.

Professor Christensen loves having intellectually stimulating discussions. However, he is incapable of writing a coherent exam. He is disorganized and utterly inaccessible outside of class. He never responded to emails, and his TAs were no help. He would forget to post homework or reading assignments. Exams are worth 80% of the grade and are hard!!

The book for this class was descent and the videos helped as well. Class attendance is important since that is when HW is randomly collected. I received a lot of help from the TAs. I would go to Will if he is still the TA since he was the one that graded everything.
He was a super nice guy and really wants the students to succeed

I didn't love this team-taught honors class, but I did like Dr. Christensen. As others have said, he's really disorganized, sometimes changing assignments two days before they're due & neglecting to put together useful study materials for the more complicated parts of logic/philosophy. But his lectures were fun & he encouraged fruitful discussion.

Dr. Christensen is literally the worst professor I have ever had. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS. His lectures are confusing, his tests have questions that are designed to trip you up, he is extremely inaccessible outside of class, not even his TAs know how to do his assignments.

Professor Christensen is a great logic teacher. He wrote his own textbook for the class. It is a descent book. Just follow along with the readings and do the assigned problems before coming to class and it should be an easy A.

Professor Christensen is a bit disorganized with his 305 course. He was very unclear and non transparent about tests / grades. He is not very good at teaching the material simply and he seems unaware of the concerns / questions that most students have. He is overall a respectful and kind person and he will listen to your concerns.

This class is a breeze: interesting, easy, and time-flexible. Metalogic requires more comprehension than practice, so the textbook is a great resource. Although closed book and notes (flashcards are not allowed), exams are still doable if you watch the recordings, read the textbook, and fully understand the contents. Great class and professor!
305 is a brutal course but Dr. Christensen is great. The material is tough but his lectures are so clear.

This class is an esay A for math majors. Dr. Christensen is intellegent, patient, and respectedly. The only challenging chapter is the Godel's Incompleteness, which is comprehensible if you read the textbook. Hoping PHIL 405 to be more challenging. H. L.

I had Dr Christensen for both 205 and 305. Both were very easy for me. I never needed the TAs. The textbook is worth a read, especially for certain problems, but I didn't have to use it all the time. Dr Christensen is always very kind and willing to listen to student concerns. He even pushes assignments back if students aren't getting it.

I took this class hoping for more of a Philosophy class, but even though it wasn't, I do feel like I saw things from a different perspective because of the class. The class is graded basically based on a handful of random graded homework assignments and 3 exams. Not an easy A, but still pretty easy if you ask me.

This class was not really a philosophy class; It was a class on how to diagram and prove first order and truth functional logic. With that in mind, this class was a lot more difficult than I was expecting, but I really liked the flipped model that Christensen used. Go to the TA lab for help frequently to make sure you understand the homework.

I've had multiple classes from Christensen, and found him to be a great teacher. Find out if your class is traditional or flipped: when I took 205 from him, he taught the lectures via 10 minute YouTube he recorded, and it meant that I spent less than 30min/week on the class.  305 was traditional, and while the grades were easy, it was more work.

Class is just review of hw, lectures are on LS/youtube usually about 10 mins, never more than 20. HW collected randomly at beginning of class 8x/semester. Prepare to spend a ton of time in the TA lab. Great TAs, walk you thru hw and test review. 3 tests, take-home, test review exactly same format as test.

Dr. Christensen was fantastic. A good amount of reading but nothing too burdensome. Weekly quizzes were super easy and only 4 questions. 5 papers the whole semester which were also easy. Midterm a little bit more tough but manageable. I highly recommend recording lectures and listening to again. It makes the class remarkably easy.

He is a very smart man but comes off as arrogant. Lectures last about half the class period. He believes that all of his students grasp difficult concepts and breezes through them. I found the class and tests extremely difficult

Dr. Christensen is wonderful teacher. His classes are interesting and I've learned a lot. He doesn't require a textbook, but links you to all the readings online. Weekly 1 page papers, a midterm paper, a final paper, oral midterm, and 2 question final. Sounds like a lot, but is a pretty light load.
Christensen is Great. :)
Such an easy class. Requires a lot of reading but I hardly read and still got an A-. He is a really nice guy who cares about his students opinions and doesn't give any busy work.
he is AWESOME!  he's interesting and entertaining. class isnt too hard, just lots and lots of reading
He is an awesome teacher. It was such a good class. I want to minor in philosophy now!

LOVED him! I couldn't wait for class. He is so cute and so smart and interesting. And the class was fascinating. If you DO your reading and actually think for yourself you'll be fine. PS Our TA was great (Fall 09)

Well, in theory the class is easy. But I was so uninterested and found the classes so boring I never did the work. I would not recommend him, but if you have no choice, well, you'll survive. Nice man, just boring and pointless class.

I loved his class. He's a great teacher and with the upper level class he really tries to have lots of discussion. His grading was straightforward and gave students opportunities to revise their paper if desired. I learned alot, and was always excited to attend class.

I really enjoyed his class. You read parts of five books and a packet. The reading is mostly really good. He answers questions and is willing to talk after class. There daily quizzes, and six one-page papers throughout the semester.  I really learned a lot about logic and found a huge interest in philosophy as a result of this class.

Professor Christensen is an incredible teacher! You need to make sure that you keep up with the reading (there is a lot). Quizzes online every day, but as long as you actually read you will do just fine. Take home tests and a couple papers.  More or less an easy A if you like to read.

Love this class--make sure you keep up with the reading and go to class, otherwise tests and papers will be impossible.  Sometimes he's a little unclear about things, and his TA doesn't know how to grade, but if you go to his office and talk to him, he's more than willing to help you out.  Great professor.

I like Christensen; I thought he gave a little too cursory of a glance over topics, but then again, this is an introduction course. He'll speak with you afterwards and not brush over topics too quickly.  I really like that he opens up the philosophical arguments for our rebuttal.  Good guy.

Ryan is an awesome guy.  He's a little quirky and the discussions frequently got side tracked, but he is very helpful and an easy grader.  He really wants his students to do well.  I highly recommend him as a teacher

I really got nothing out of the this class. He assigns reading for every class period and then discusses it in depth through lecture.. very boring class, very difficult to sit through. I got a B and I listened to hardly any of his lectures but the class work was fairly demanding. Take this class from a different professor.

I found it more useful to read the sparknotes than go to class.  Quiz every class period online.  4 papers, although grading does not make any sense.  He doesn't know how to use blackboard, so communication with students was a problem.

Prof Davis is nice and knows his stuff, but he focuses a lot on the Old Testament & class is lecture heavy. Get ready to spend lots of time on the daily homework & the quizzes every other week. Exams were kinda hard since some questions are free response and the multiple choice ones can be specific. This was one of my hardest classes this semester.

This class was my hardest class during the semester. Tests were very difficult and the questions try to trick you. I spent hours studying for his tests. The exams also take up most of your grade. He has really good insights about the bible and he's a caring teacher, but the tests are unbearably difficult.
Professor Davis is very nice and kind. However, his tests are insanely difficult, and there is a lot of written homework. I would recommend being ready to take tricky tests.

He a good guy and is very insightful and knowledgable, but the homework is unnecessarily long and frustrating. The reading questions are redundant and pointless. It takes forever to do, and left me wondering why I'm spending hours doing religion homework that just makes me frustrated and annoyed. I feel like we could be learning more in this class.

This proffesor has really good lectures, that taught me a ton, but he requires strict attendance, and is very homework heavy for a 2 credit class. His tests also didn't have clear study criteria. It was just study my massive slides. The tests are 6 or so random essay response questions making grading slightly subjective. This class is very mid.

Honestly his Religion 121 is SO EASY! Of course you have to study for the three exams he has, but if you go over the slides he had posted, you'll be fine. He doesn't allow you to use the Book of Mormon on the exams or outside material, and he gives you online quizzes every other week.

Lectures are straightforward and easy to understand. I like how you are graded, There were homework assignments, quizzes, and tests, just like any other class. No projects or other fluff. No scriptures allowed on tests, which was difficult at first. Sometimes the questions on the tests and quizzes were out of the blue. Remember details and study.

If you are looking for an easy chill religion class. This is not it. He is great guy but focuses on the old testament. The test answers are the learning objectives but he does not give you the answers. A lot of answers were what he said in class and if you missed it then good luck. Take from anyone else because it is not worth your grade.

If you are looking for an easy religion class DO NOT TAKE FROM RYAN DAVIS! He has a phd in Old Testament so this is pretty much an old testament class rather than Book of Mormon. A 3-6 page assignment is due before every class, attendance is graded. Tests are HEAVILY weighted. Better for an RM or someone who is VERY familiar with books of scripture

Professor Davis is a kind, caring, and accessible professor but his tests are VERY different from his learning outcomes. As someone who has read the Book of Mormon multiple times, knows the stories, and studied all of the learning outcomes I still could not manage to get A's on his tests. His religion class was MUCH harder than it needed to be.

Dr. Davis is AWESOME! Literally one of my favorite professors so far. The class is lecture but lots of discussion so I had no problem staying awake for this 8am class. If you study his slides, any bolded homework (which isn't much), and anything he clearly emphasized in class, you'll do well. He's very clear and I always knew exactly what to study.

So the tests were pretty specific but he is open to constructive criticism and will do what he can. He's a good teacher and shows that he cares about what he is teaching. Esp New Testament, he really showed another side to it and I loved what I learned. I recommend.

Very Nice and Smart guy. He gives inspiring lectures and he expects YOU to learn. I always discuss with him about the scripture after class. If you are hard-working and love the scripture, you are going to learn a lot from him.

Super nice guy and very approachable. His lectures are just very lecture heavy. He might ask a couple questions but it is mostly just him talking. When it comes to his test, the study guides he gives you are very vague and broad and then he looks for specific answers on the test. Would not recommend.

I have no doubt Ryan Davis is a nice guy. But he doesn't understand the point of an on-demand remote delivery class. You have to turn in assignments during the specific week they are due NO WORKING AHEAD. I emailed him and he wouldn't budge. I took online because I wanted to work at my own pace, not move with the herd.

The online Christ and the Everlasting Gospel was a good course; we learn a lot and Prof Davis is inspiring. However, the amount of work required in this 2 credit class is just unnecessarily high. Each wk: 2 60-90 minute modules/week, with 5-10 paragraph-journal responses for each, plus a discussion and responses, another project 1hr/wk and quizzes.

Not a hard class but also not a blow-off class. Reading questions are due before every class along with a biweekly quiz. If you know the learning objectives and watch the test reviews you'll be ok.
Really nice guy! LOVES the Old testament. The entire first unit is on the the Old Testament and heavily referenced throughout.

Bro Davis is awesome, the Spirit is always present in class, I was always able to take something meaningful away from the classes, and the grading is very clear and the test questions are exactly from the study guides. The pre-class readings weren't always my favorite but they normally aren't too long and they are relevant.

I took his Rel A 275 class. His lectures and power points were informative but his tests were harder than necessary for a religion class. They were also in the testing center. Learning about Jesus Christ in the Book of Mormon was important but his grading was a little unforgiving.

Good teacher, light work, takes feedback seriously, and uses relatable scenarios to explain ancient scripture culture. Reading questions due before each class that take about 15 mins, reading quizzes every couple weeks that are a breeze if you payed attention in class, 2 midterms and a final that are a little tricky, but very doable.

Davis is passionate about religion and Old Testament and cares about what he teaches. He wants us to be passionate as well. He was very quick to learn everyones names.
Homework is very doable and not hard. Classes are lectures, you will learn the most in class. No part of the class is secret, ALL answers to the test are said in class. Great teacher

I took REL A 275 with Dr. Davis, and it was life-changing. I learned so much about the gospel. He's a super nice guy, and lectures are good. All the tests were multiple choice, but there was a lot of homework - reading questions for every class that each took me over an hour. Worth it though.

Loved the lectures. He kept it to the basics. Never tried to trick us. Test questions came word for word on the slides which were made available to us. I never felt overwhelmed and I felt like I spent a very appropriate amount of time completing work for this class with everything else going on in my life. He is very inclusive and caring.

Very boring lectures. Test questions are often poorly written and I felt like they were unnecessarily tricky. One of my hardest classes that semester and really shouldn't have been. I usually love my religion classes so it was very disappointing. Please take my advice and find a different prof, one of the worst classes I've taken at BYU
Dr. Davis is an incredible professor and I learned so much in his class! As long as you do the reading assignments and study for the quizzes and tests a bit, you will do just fine in the class!

Brother Davis is a great professor. I did not have too many problems with him other than the fact that it is sort of difficult to study for his tests. We were told to "make our own study guide" for the test which he could have been more specific on. I loved him as a person but I work and test better when I have something to refer to.

This is the best religion class that I have EVER taken. Dr. Davis knows exactly what he is talking about and he knows how to make the class both intellectual and spiritual. His tests are easy if you pay attention in class and study the power points (which are always posted online). The reading assignments are easy, but you HAVE TO DO THEM to pass.

Professor Davis is an amazing Professor! His lectures uplifted and taught me so much. He's very clear about what's on the tests and what to study. Attendance is mandatory and there's hw every class that takes like 20 min to do. This is how religion classes should be. I was able to learn so much, but wasn't stressed about my grade.

I love Professor Davis. I think he's so good that I decided to write a review. He focuses a lot on context and understanding what the writers meant to say rather than how we interpret it with our modern, western lenses.

The lectures were boring. The class was challenging as I never payed attention. it's not an easy A even if you pay attention. Dr Davis became frustrated a couple times with the class for our lack of interest and participation.
Loved Brother Davis! He was so funny and made the Book of Mormon applicable, which can be hard to do sometimes. He is very accommodating and approachable.

My experience in this class was great! I enjoyed my professor and felt that they helped me push myself academically. School is school so I couldn't get past that but I really enjoyed my time this semester with this teacher and class.

Brother Davis is overall a good professor.  It was his first time teaching Book of Mormon at BYU, so that might have been a reason for some of the downsides of this class.  I felt that there wasn't a lot of creativity put into the lessons and they could be dry at times.  He is very clear about what he expects from you, tests and quizzes are fair.

Bro. Davis really cares about his students. There's lots of discussion in class, and he does a really good job of directing the discussion instead of taking it over. You do have to study to do well on the quizzes and tests, but everything is straight from the reading or from his lectures.

He has a degree in Old Testament studies and his insights can be pretty interesting. There is a nice balance to class discussion and lecturing and he is extremely nice. I don't know why everyone else is complaining, its still a college class. Don't expect that just because you have read the BoM you will pass. You still have to study to get an A.

Brother Davis is great, he is a really nice guy, and is super helpful if you ask. He does like focusing on Biblical history and other ancient stuff, because that's his thing. He does have super random things on his tests and quizzes that aren't in the power points and are just things he mentions once in class. There is also quite a bit of homework.
He's a really nice guy and really funny, but he tends to drift more towards the Bible in our lectures, rather than focus on the subject of the Book of Mormon.

He tries his best but isn't very helpful in lab. Because he's a professional, I think he leaves out helpful tips that may seem obvious to him but isn't to students new to the lab setting. Lecture weren't too helpful for lab but at least told you what the name of what you'd be doing was... to then learn on your own outside of class.

I've had Dr. Cordner for many classes, and he is the best! He cares about his students, and he is insanely smart. He always included spiritual messages and random stories that went along with his lectures. It was very entertaining. His exams are hard. You basically have to memorize everything on every slide. But, they are not impossible.

Dr. Cordner is an amazing professor. He truly cares for his students and is passionate about microbiology. He has a strong testimony of the gospel and shares it often with the class. I enjoyed the labs and look forward to taking classes from him again. Make sure to read the slides for the quizzes and you will do great! No final exam.

Dr. Cordner is super passionate about what he teaches and really fun to learn from! He's very understanding and patient with his students and has a super strong testimony. This class is just an intro to general lab techniques (a prerequisite for the MLS major) and there isn't any outside of class work, but do review slides for the quizzes!

There is a ton of material to know from this class. Dr. Cordner is one of the nicest professors on campus, and is the best at weaving spiritual insights into lectures in a meaningful way. At times, I felt he could have streamlined our learning a little bit, but the tests are fairly straightforward. Just tons of material.

WARNING:MMBIO majors do not take this class! It's part of the MLS major, so it's very different compared to other MMBIO courses. Dr. C is my favorite professor though. He is incredibly kind and holds great office hours. You just have to go to him prepared with all the questions you have. Great mix of learning and the spirit. Gives extra credit!
He is a decent professor, really young. He  comes off as really nice and timid, but could be a lot more helpful than he is.
Dr. Cordner really cares for his students. He LOVES hematology. Go to the Reviews, they will save you. There's a quiz every other week or so. His tests are fair and straight forward.

Dr. Cordner is the best professor! There is a lot to know for his classes (just the nature of the MLS beast), but he is super clear on what he needs you to know, which makes the program much more bearable. He truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed!
Sadly, this was the worst classroom experience I've had at BYU. I often felt that students were not treated with much respect. The class material is interesting, but I'd take it with anyone else.

Professor Pratt is very intelligent and has a very clear class structure. He is very fair and thoughtful about the assignments he gives you. Exams are all on Excel which I liked. You do have to do a lot of studying in 410 to get the material down but it is still a great class, I really enjoyed learning the material.

He can be intimidating, but he really cares about students, always open to give advice on how to improve in the class. This class requires a lot of time to work but is very interesting material, and Pratt does a good job a teaching hard concepts

Professor Pratt can be a little dry, it's true, but if you actually engage and participate in class you will really enjoy his lectures. The HW assignments are easy, so people walk in over confident for the tests. If you want to get good scores, pay Close Attention in Class, then go home and Review all your notes 1-2x and you'll do well.

Least favorite professor I have ever had. Makes you feel dumb when you ask questions even though he doesn't explain things clearly. Super full of himself and the tests are super hard. Be ready to spend lots of time on cases. And don't ask pratt for help on anything because he doesn't care.  Do yourself a favor and take it from Iverson.

Honestly, thought this class was pretty good. HW has answers in the back so youdon't have to worry about your grade - however I noticed most kids wouldn't even do the hw because they just wanted to finish ASAP. I took the tests pretty prepared and others thought it was tough but IMO, they had been cutting corners the whole semester... overall 9/10

Professor Pratt is unwilling or unable to help you if you're falling behind in class and don't understand the material immediately. Textbook and slides aren't much help either. Exams are worth 75% of your grade.

Makes you feel like an dumb if you ask a question in class. He is trying to rush through so much material that he won't slow down or go back when you don't understand something. Textbook is not much help, his powerpoints only make sense if you understood the lecture, so basically all you have is your notes to help with assignments and cases.

Imagine a parent explains to a 6 year old how to ride a bike. The child has never seen a bike before in person, not even a picture. The parent draws a stick-figure-like picture of a bike and explains in words how to ride the bike. Then the parent gives the child the bike, without training wheels, and expects the child to be able to ride.

Great guy that teaches a dry, tough class. Tests are harder than you think. Group case study projects take a lot of time/work, start early. He's not afraid to tell you that you're wrong but he does it in a totally respectful way. I have no complaints about him, he is just strict. Hard grading and zero late work policy. Don't take 401/410 together

Professor Pratt is an amazing FIN 401 teacher. He is honestly my favorite teacher I have had at BYU. The workload for this class is very big, but manageable as long as you don't get behind or procrastinate. Professor Pratt is an excellent teacher and offers lots of help with office and TA hours. I would definitely recommend taking from him!!

I enjoyed all my finance professors, but I think Prof Pratt refined the way I approached finance the most. His class had 3 test, 5 cases, and problem sets. There was no great way to prepare for the tests or cases or to control your grade. I loved him as a professor and enjoyed going to his class and hearing his lectures.

Dr. Pratt is one of the smartest and best professors in the Marriott School. If you like professors who always tell you good job, and don't correct you when you're wrong then you probably won't like Dr. Pratt. He doesn't hesitate to tell you if you are wrong about something, which for me was nice, since I like to know when I'm doing something wrong

Professor Pratt is a solid professor. The class material wasn't particularly fascinating to me, but he did a good job explaining it and keeping my attention. Our tests got progressively a lot harder, which was frustrating because you never knew what difficulty level to expect. His homework is reasonable and prepares you pretty well for the tests.

Professor Pratt is a great teacher, probably my favorite last semester. He teaches in a way that is easy to understand and doesn't use monotonous power points slides.  He is very careful when answering students questions, and doesnt hesitate to tell you when you are wrong. ( He isn't mean about it, and it is hilarious at times).

It's up to you to keep up & write notes; no slides. The tests are 70% of the grade w/ virtually no study guide & little guidance as to what to study. He basically says, "Just know it all" which is crazy, since you had to take your own notes & it's impossible to listen & take notes on every single thing. He's not too helpful if you don't understand.

Hill is a great guy. I took 330 and 355 from him. He takes forever to grade things. He cares about what he teaches and class is fairly enjoyable. He knows a lot and is willing to share it with you. Lots of quizzes but if you do the reading and take notes they're easy. 330 had daily quizzes, 355 had pop quizzes but we were warned that we'd have 12

Its a really easy class but man these lectures are so boring. He talks the entire time and I wish he would switch it up and do something different. Everyone is checked out. He is really nice and understanding so I respect him but its really boring to go to class

Professor Hill clearly has a passion for the topic, and the works we read were really interesting. He gives good insight, which makes class interesting. He cares about grading, and it was nice to receive detailed feedback on how we could improve. As long as you do the readings (which aren't a lot) and attend class, you will do well in the class.

Dr Jensen is the best professor I have ever had. I have taken GEOG 212, GEOG 285, GEOG 313, and GEOG 349 with him. He genuinely cares way more about your 1st wellbeing 2 you learning, and probably 10th on his list is your grade. Classes are easy, but you learn a lot if you pay attention. He may go on tangents ab stuff he's passionate about tho haha
I only had him for Univ101 but he was super awesome. Very inspiring and fun! I would take a class from him again! He's a real friend and a great person to talk to about anything.

This was Africa: South of the Sahara. It was easy, Dr. Jensen is very knowledgable about Africa and we had some pretty awesome discussions. The class was easy, 4-5 small papers and take-home finals. He cares more that you're there, learning, participate, and have an opinion more than anything else.

This wasn't a very hands on class. We did a couple things in ArcGIS but not very much. I feel like it was more centered on things covered in lectures and the textbook readings. Professor Jensen is honestly a super nice professor and he is very passionate about what we are learning.

Nice guy but focus is heavily on the theory of GIS (long/tedious textbook reading responses) and not the technological skills. Other than a few tutorials and working on the final project step by step in the GIS lab I didn't actually touch ARCGIS. The plus is that he genuinely cares about his students - just wasn't the best class structure for me.

He is so sweet, genuinely cares, and is super enthusiastic about what he teaches. He explains things well, but everything is lecture heavy. He's def a morning person- tbh the only way I got through those early mornings. Not a lot of direction on the assignments themselves, so you've gotta go to class to know how, but super easy! Exams are open note

Dr. Jensen's class was lecture heavy. We did have weekly lab assignments where we went through ENVI and Earth engine tutorials. Midterm and final were take-home, open book. One 5-7 page double spaced paper. Overall, not a difficult class and includes interesting content.

Such a kind professor, very funny. 2 exams, he made them open book so you get 100%. A couple of small assignments but you can get help and get 100. TA is GREAT. Weekly chapter questions. Lots of extra credit. Group project where everyone gets the same grade. He is so kind, he lets people who are struggling get in a group and get that same score.

He's a really sweet guy, and cares about his students. His lectures are good, although sometimes a bit dry, but that's not really his fault, it's because of the subject. HW questions each week, and a couple labs. One midterm, one final, and a final project. The TA is really helpful! Go to seem them for help with questions/labs.

Awesome class. Lots of lectures but he usually kept them interesting (also often got sidetracked). Weekly reading assignments with questions and some assignments from ArcGIS Pro throughout the semester. One large group project at the end. One midterm and a final. Very understanding and helpful.
He's a good guy! He gets distracted very easily but overall good class. Make sure you ask the TA for help!

At the beginning,I was so worried about this class because his lectures are so boring and complicated. I usually couldn't follow what he was talking about and would end up zoning out. The homework is confusing and kinda hard, but the tests were surprisingly simple. They are all open answer, but as long as you go the test reviews, you'll get an A.

Great professor. He makes a difficult concept easier to understand and appreciate. GIS is hard, but he is willing to help. TA was helpful in class, slow to respond to emails, and graded hard. Buy the online textbook, because there are weekly chapter review questions. Enjoyable class for such a difficult subject. Final was hard. Use the GIS lab.

Jensen was always in a positive mood and happy to interact with students. He encouraged students to talk to their professors and create good relationships with them. He's clearly passionate about his work. About the class- it's wonderful! Not every professor is interesting, but still good to hear about different aspects to geography

GEOG 100 is a lecture based class where different professors from the geography department come and talk about themselves and their work in the field. Interesting sometimes. You also have to read a chapter from a book a every week and do a little write up on it. Not too bad, you can skim the chapter if you need to to do the write up. Very easy.

I really enjoyed his Geog100 class! I took it simply to better understand geography and the career opportunities that the major offered. I wanted to get a better idea of whether I would be interested in majoring in Geography. I found the class interesting, educational, and very helpful for exploring the major. I highly recommend it.

Dr. Jensen is awesome! One of my favorite professors. GEOG 100 is a class that everyone has to take but with an interesting book and guest speakers every week, Dr. Jensen makes it interesting. Be sure to come every week, read the assigned chapter and do the summary. Instead of having us buy the book, Dr. Jensen had us find it online for free.

Dr. Jensen is great. I was really worried about the class in the beginning of the semester but after getting an A on the midterm I felt good. The lectures do not really help you on your homework but are critical for the tests. Especially ppt slides. Thing that frustrated me is that Learningsuite does not truly reflect your grade.

Super easy! Have to read a chapter from the textbook each week and do a single-spaced write-up about it. As long as you do it your golden. Class time is just presentations from professors in the department.

Prof Jensen is fantastic.  His lectures are fun and he knows the material super well.  Attendance isn't mandatory but he'll occasionally do attendance quizzes.  I'm planning on taking as many classes from him as possible.

Prof. Jensen is AWESOME!  My favorite professor at BYU.  He also knows the material inside and out.  He's always smiling and in a good mood.  He gets to know every student individually, and is ALWAYS willing to help.  His assignments can take awhile though.  I would take it again just to have him again as a professor.

Only really need book for weekly homework.  Gets sidetracked but lecture still rarely lasted whole 75 min.  Puts effort into knowing everyone's name and something about you, tries to get everyone to participate in lecture.  Very encouraging.  Tests are about 30 q's nearly all short answer because he wants to know that you know the material.

Dr. Jensen is one of my favorite professors. He makes lectures interesting (as far as the subject matter permits) and the assignments in the class are somewhat fun to complete. I never felt like my time was being wasted which can be a problem with other professors.
Don't worry to take his class. There is no problem with him. If you don't like him, it's your problem.
Good teacher, real nice and helpful.  Cool topic.  A bit goofy, but in a good way.  Always happy and joking around.

Great Teacher! Only down part is a lot of assignments....I forgot one lab and almost got a B because they are weighted so heavy! But a great teacher! He gets side tracked but usually on good things like football! Had a take home final! Seriously great teacher you will love him. He will help you with ANYTHING!!!!!!!!!!
Dr.Jensen is the best member of the Geography faculty, hands down. He's great. I'd take a bullet for him.

I think Dr. Jensen is great! I wasn't looking forward to this class at all, but it's my favorite class this semester. I feel like I'm actually learning something useful and that not many people know :) Each Friday is a lab day where we work on homework, and if we need more time to work and understand it he's not afraid to take more time
I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Jensen makes the class fun and interesting. I would definetly take a class from him again.

Professor Kellems is one of my favorite professors. He is super easy to work with and has great lectures. I feel like I learn a lot in his class, and I want to learn a lot in his class. I would recommend taking his class!

CPSE 402 - for 2 credit class, I think it took itself too seriously. We had to do group assignments and meetings despite being on demand. Some of the quizzes had random and specific questions that were unnecessary. He uses canvas instead of Learning suite.

I had a super good experience with Dr. Kellems as my teacher. He truly is an expert in his field, and could answer almost any question you had on the topic. He is not a hard grader, and as long as you turn in your stuff on time you will get an A.
such an amazing teacher. he clearly cares about every individual student. not test heavy and is so willing to work with you to figure things out.

Dr. Kellems is a really nice professor. His lectures can be kinda boring and they move really fast. But he is super helpful if you ask for help and he wants you to succeed. There are quizzes for every chapter and 2 exams, the questions on the tests are pretty specific which is hard but he helps you prepare and review. Overall I enjoyed his class!
Ryan is a fantastic professor and changed the way I think about digital marketing. Definitely take his class if you can!
No tests. Very application-based. Super easy A if you participate in class and do your assignments. Best class for learning digital marketing!

Just graduated from BYU in Business and Ryan's digital marketing class was BY FAR my favorite. There was not even a second of busy work in the class, most of the assignments are you taking what you learn to work on your own business. The experience in this class got me my first job out of graduating. Take it!

He is one of the only professors that actually is good connecting spiritual with secular. He is the most genuine guy ever. He is young & connects easy to his students and honestly is just a good friend to have. He prepares amazing lectures and is very well read in Digital Marketing!! I loved being in his class and learning all his tips and tricks!

He is a very nice guy. He knows so much about SEO. I came to his class knowing nothing about SEO, and walked out with so much knowlege about SEO and about life in general. I would 100% recommend this class to anybody who is interested in learning about SEO, Google Ads, Facebook Ads, and so much good stuff!

Ok this guy is so epic, he can reach you so much about digital marketing. He teaches great about Facebook ads, Google ads, growing on social media, improving SEO. My only complaint is that hes so dope and holy that he was translated already so idk if he will be coming back to teach
Sadly, this was the worst classroom experience I've had at BYU. I often felt that students were not treated with much respect. The class material is interesting, but I'd take it with anyone else.

Professor Pratt is very intelligent and has a very clear class structure. He is very fair and thoughtful about the assignments he gives you. Exams are all on Excel which I liked. You do have to do a lot of studying in 410 to get the material down but it is still a great class, I really enjoyed learning the material.

He can be intimidating, but he really cares about students, always open to give advice on how to improve in the class. This class requires a lot of time to work but is very interesting material, and Pratt does a good job a teaching hard concepts

Professor Pratt can be a little dry, it's true, but if you actually engage and participate in class you will really enjoy his lectures. The HW assignments are easy, so people walk in over confident for the tests. If you want to get good scores, pay Close Attention in Class, then go home and Review all your notes 1-2x and you'll do well.

Least favorite professor I have ever had. Makes you feel dumb when you ask questions even though he doesn't explain things clearly. Super full of himself and the tests are super hard. Be ready to spend lots of time on cases. And don't ask pratt for help on anything because he doesn't care.  Do yourself a favor and take it from Iverson.

Honestly, thought this class was pretty good. HW has answers in the back so youdon't have to worry about your grade - however I noticed most kids wouldn't even do the hw because they just wanted to finish ASAP. I took the tests pretty prepared and others thought it was tough but IMO, they had been cutting corners the whole semester... overall 9/10

Professor Pratt is unwilling or unable to help you if you're falling behind in class and don't understand the material immediately. Textbook and slides aren't much help either. Exams are worth 75% of your grade.

Makes you feel like an dumb if you ask a question in class. He is trying to rush through so much material that he won't slow down or go back when you don't understand something. Textbook is not much help, his powerpoints only make sense if you understood the lecture, so basically all you have is your notes to help with assignments and cases.

Imagine a parent explains to a 6 year old how to ride a bike. The child has never seen a bike before in person, not even a picture. The parent draws a stick-figure-like picture of a bike and explains in words how to ride the bike. Then the parent gives the child the bike, without training wheels, and expects the child to be able to ride.

Great guy that teaches a dry, tough class. Tests are harder than you think. Group case study projects take a lot of time/work, start early. He's not afraid to tell you that you're wrong but he does it in a totally respectful way. I have no complaints about him, he is just strict. Hard grading and zero late work policy. Don't take 401/410 together

Professor Pratt is an amazing FIN 401 teacher. He is honestly my favorite teacher I have had at BYU. The workload for this class is very big, but manageable as long as you don't get behind or procrastinate. Professor Pratt is an excellent teacher and offers lots of help with office and TA hours. I would definitely recommend taking from him!!

I enjoyed all my finance professors, but I think Prof Pratt refined the way I approached finance the most. His class had 3 test, 5 cases, and problem sets. There was no great way to prepare for the tests or cases or to control your grade. I loved him as a professor and enjoyed going to his class and hearing his lectures.

Dr. Pratt is one of the smartest and best professors in the Marriott School. If you like professors who always tell you good job, and don't correct you when you're wrong then you probably won't like Dr. Pratt. He doesn't hesitate to tell you if you are wrong about something, which for me was nice, since I like to know when I'm doing something wrong

Professor Pratt is a solid professor. The class material wasn't particularly fascinating to me, but he did a good job explaining it and keeping my attention. Our tests got progressively a lot harder, which was frustrating because you never knew what difficulty level to expect. His homework is reasonable and prepares you pretty well for the tests.

Professor Pratt is a great teacher, probably my favorite last semester. He teaches in a way that is easy to understand and doesn't use monotonous power points slides.  He is very careful when answering students questions, and doesnt hesitate to tell you when you are wrong. ( He isn't mean about it, and it is hilarious at times).

It's up to you to keep up & write notes; no slides. The tests are 70% of the grade w/ virtually no study guide & little guidance as to what to study. He basically says, "Just know it all" which is crazy, since you had to take your own notes & it's impossible to listen & take notes on every single thing. He's not too helpful if you don't understand.
