I absolutely loved Brother Sharps class!! His teaching style was just what I needed. There is an urgency and excitement with every lecture. He helps you know what is on the exams ahead of time so I only missed one question on the final. If you are taking a Book of Mormon class you HAVE to take it from Brother Sharp!

Bro. Sharp's class is great for returned missionaries that already know the Book of Mormon like the back of their hand. If that does not apply to you, DO NOT take from him. The midterm and final cover information he doesn't cover in class, and his lectures are a lot of him spewing information and reading long quotes off his slides.

Brother Sharp's class is insanely good!! The way he goes through the scriptures is eye opening. With that being said, this class wasn't super easy. Don't let the open scripture tests fool you... they are super tricky. I never missed class and took very detailed notes in my Scriptures and still didn't do super well on the tests.

Brother Sharp taught in a way that made the lessons engaging and applicable. Also, after taking the final he met with me and showed me on the slides and in the scriptures where we had talked about the ones I missed. He also curves the final to raise the class average as high as he is able to. If you want a professor who is on your side take him!

Sharp knocks it out of the park teaching and takes his job seriously, but with the right amount of humor. Will totally change your perspective on the BoM--Makes you work for your grade though. Has an open ended project you're supposed to spend more than 10 hours on, two papers, and two tests. The final was WAY harder than I thought so beware.

Dr. Sharp is an amazing teacher! I am studying to be a teacher and have written down so many ideas that I want to use when I do my student teaching soon. There was a great blend of humor, inspiration, and what he referred to as brain sweat. Definitely a boost to my testimony but also my other studies. I highly recommend you take this class!

Professor Sharp teaches exactly how religion classes should be taught. His focus is clearly on the Savior and on helping students improve in their own relationship with Him. I left class inspired and grateful for my Savior.

Brother Sharp has paid a price in the scriptures and his lectures are so powerful! I was nervous about taking the final and he took the time to meet with me and answer some of my questions from the review slides. It is so nice having a professor who cares and who wants you to succeed.
BEST PROFESSOR AT BYU! I have loved Brother Sharp's lectures and his stories are the best. The grading was very fair and was just the right balance for a 2 credit class. LOVE this class!

Super nice guy, but that's where the good news ends. His lectures are ridiculously unorganized and impossible to follow. Between the readings, semester long project, and papers, the workload is higher than a lot of my more serious 3 credit classes. Good chunk of exam questions are on stuff that hasn't even been covered-Please do not take this class

This class was really good in terms of getting us to read the Book of Mormon differently. Brother Sharp helped me get motivated to study the scriptures on my own. I had to study a ton for the final but the study slides helped me do well. All in all I learned a lot from this class and it really helped me feel closer to Christ.

Hes really a great guy. His lectures are really interesting. However in terms of BYU cores he focuses more on intellectual enlargement than any of the others (definitions, things in the language/ writing). If thats the way your testimony grows youll love it! Even if its not hes super nice and interesting to listen to. Hard tests though.

Some professors like to follow the mantra, "less is more". Bro Sharp likes to follow the mantra, "more is more." This class had more work than I had in any other religion class. It got kind of ridiculous. He is a very kind professor and means well, but if you don't keep up with the assignments, you will struggle.

This class was very straightforward and I liked that, for the most part, I was in control of my grade throughout the semester. You do have to stay on top of things but as long as you do you will be fine. Brother sharp really is an awesome teacher!

I am a non-traditional student and so coming back to a university has been challenging in many ways. This class has shown me why I love BYU and why I am so grateful for the opportunity to take religion courses with my other studies.

100 percent spiritual uplifting, hands-down inspiring, and zero percent stressful. Everything you need for tests is in the "know for test" slides in each powerpoint. Be consistent with the weekly assignments and occasional papers and your grade'll be great. Takes time, yes, but not stress. Sharp is a powerful teacher. Great boost to any semester!

Brother sharps enthusiasm and passion for the gospel definitely made a big difference for me this semester. The assignments were pretty straightforward and outlined on learning suite. The exams stretched me but also forced me to take a lot of notes in my scriptures (which I am actually grateful for). He met with me individually to answer questions
I absolutely love how focused Brother Sharp was on the Savior as we studied the Book of Mormon. This class has been a spiritual journey for me and I have come so much closer to Christ because of it.

Brother Sharp gets what teaching is all about. You know from day one that your learning and spiritual growth are his number one priority. As a religion professor he does a great job of balancing spiritual motivation and interesting doctrinal study. He definitely makes you work for a good grade, but it's totally worth it. Don't miss this class.

This class has been the highlight of my semester! The lectures moved fast but always seemed to bring the Spirit. I have always loved the Book of Mormon but Brother Sharp helped me appreciate its depth in a new way

Brother Sharp cares more about your spiritual growth and personal development than an arbitrary grading system. This class was so refreshing! My testimony is stronger and I feel more committed to the church because of this class.

I don't usually get on here but I felt like I needed to put a plug in for this class. Brother Sharp is hilarious and helps the scriptures come alive! This was my last religion class and definitely my favorite.

I really enjoyed my experience in this class. Appropriate work load for a two hour religion class. You DO need to study well for the tests but you can use your scriptures in the testing center which was very helpful (I got an A on both tests:). i guess the thing I liked most is that we always talked about being better lifelong readers of the BOM

Brother Sharp's passion for the gospel is contagious! In a typical class he will walk us through a couple of chapters in the Book of Mormon, share wonderful insights from those chapters and then help everybody relate to what we were learning by sharing a powerful story. This is what a religion class at BYU should be like! 10/10
Brother Sharp teaches the scriptures in a very personal way. The class was very interesting and also strengthened my testimony. As long as you stay on top of the weekly assignments you will be fine

Great Professor. His tests are not subjective, which is extraordinary for a religion class. He is very caring, and wants each of his students to do their best. As long as you keep up with the readings and report your progress you should do very well in his class.

Solid choice for Book of Mormon. Even though the class I was in was very large I felt like Brother Sharp really tried to connect with us. There were weekly assignments, a semester long project, and a midterm and final. While we learned a lot of historical details about the Book of Mormon it was done in a way that was inspiring and exciting!

I learned and felt so much in this class and my testimony of the Book of Mormon is so much deeper because of it. I have come to appreciate that the The Book of Mormon is way more complex than I initially realized. I recommend this class to anyone wanting more from their personal study of the Book of Mormon.

Brother Sharp is great! Homework doesn't take much time but is inspiring! There's a 10 hour project that you get to work on the whole semester, which I loved. You get to pick everything about the project and it's really fun. He cares a lot for the class and has great experiences to share. My testimony grew and I have a new perspective on the BOM.

This class showed me a new way to read scriptures. I have learned how important it is to pay attention to every little detail. What I appreciate the most is that I feel like I now have the tools to study this way all the time. If you want to get more out of your scriptures study then take this class!

Such a great class! Take Stats from Professor Hardy. He is very fun and keeps class interesting. The tests are exactly what you learn in class and the homework that you do.

Dr. Hardy's lectures drag on and most of his jokes aren't funny. The homework is pretty easy if you take the time to do it though. The lectures are necessary for some days, but I felt like a lot of the class time was a waste of time. I would not take this class again from Hardy.

Dr. Hardy was an awesome teacher.  Let's be real here folks. Statistics. Not a class to cheer for, but Sam made it bearable.  If you are going to take Psych 301 definitely  take it from him!  He is funny, helpful, and all around nice guy.  Huzzah for Dr. Hardy.

Sam was very helpful. Sometimes he did make things seem a little more complicated than they really were. I thought the first test would be hard but it wasn't. If you go to him with questions he will help you very well
Sam is a great guy, and is so good at helping you understand the writing process and how to write a really good paper. I learned so much in his class!

Dr. Hardy is a great guy. You can tell he has a really good heart and he really just wants everyone to do well in his class. Unfortunately, when I took Personality from him it was his first time teaching the class and it was really unstructured. It was still a pretty easy class, though, and I actually did learn a lot.

Had Hardy last semester.  Extremely helpful and nice professor.  It pains me to say that his tests and assignments are difficult in that you never quite know what it is he wants from you.  You can know the material thoroughly and still do poorly on his tests.  A good person, but he takes relatively easy topics and makes them overly complicated.

The TA's grade EVERYTHING (not good) and people were barley passing the written parts of tests. Anything that was subjective hurt your grade.  Tests were split into multiple choice and essay. I got a 98 on the multiple choice, but 74 on the essay. Yet, I have gotten A's in every writing class. Also, very heavy on reading and busy work.  Avoid him.

Dr. Hardy is very helpful and will go out of his way to make sure you understand the material. His tests aren't hard, and he's pretty flexible about the homework. Come to class and it should be a fairly easy A.

I liked this class and thought it was useful. His tests are pretty easy. He mixes religion in when it's appropriate. He also brought his mom in, which was fun. This class also helps if you're interested in working with high schoolers, or even as a parent the information would be useful in understanding what adolescents are going through.

Sam is a great professor. He is very nice and does all he can to help students understand. The homework is very easy. The tests are kind of long, but very simple.  The people complaining about terminology just didn't care enough to learn the material well, otherwise they would have understood it crystal clearly.  Take this class!  He is awesome!

Sam is an amazing teacher, as for those complaining about terminology on the tests it is harder but that is college.  His class is by far the best stats class I have taken.  He makes the subject matter clear and easy to understand.  If you read and do the homework this class is an easy A.  I reccomend this teacher.

Sam is so nice and helpful.  He is just starting out, but he learned a lot from last semester.  His tests are really simple and he does everything possible to help you.  I would definitely suggest taking this class from him!

This was Sam's second semester, so he's learning...but slowly. His TA's were more knowledgeable than he seemed to be, his HW was nice (once a week) but very redundant. Tests used tougher terminology than lectures. Lectures were unclear many times. He's willing to help and a super nice guy, but wouldn't recommend him for a few more years...

This is Sam's 2nd semester teaching so he's learning. But man he's a slow learner! His TAs knew more about stats than he did! He doesn't explain things in a way that is immediately clear. Uses a lot of terminology but doesn't explain. Tests use more complex wording than lectures. Homework is redundant. Nice guy though! Not my favorite professor...

Very fun lectures, but hard to follow. Tests weren't too hard, but there were some things on the tests that weren't discussed on class or in the lecture slides. Assignments weren't too hard, tended to be one a week. Would just spring things on you at times, but they weren't too hard. I don't like science, but I had a good time in this class.

He cares a lot about the material, and this comes through in his lectures. His class is designed not to be easy or to take tests, but to educate you in the material in the most effective way possible. There are many opportunities for different learning styles, and online accomodations for students with difficult schedules.

Should've been a comedian instead of a professor! He's entertaining but teaches the class like everyone's a geology major and knows the lingo. Lectures are wild and hard to follow, learned more from when his ta taught the class. Tests are insanely hard

Please, please do yourself a favor and take Professor Hudson's class. His lectures are incredible and you'll learn a lot whether you are planning on a geology major or not. He is super funny and respects all of his students. He doesn't mind explaining concepts over again. I loved his class SO much.

Professor Hudson understands that most students are taking this class for a GE, so he makes it VERY doable and fun. Not a hard GE at all! Don't take geology from any other professor! My husband and I took the class together & both really enjoyed it even though we don't like geology. The study guides are very clear, and the tests aren't very hard.

I wouldn't say this class is just an easy A, you do have to put effort into it & if you don't study for the tests you won't do well on them, but there are study guides & if you understand everything on those you'll do great! Yeah you can miss class and be fine but why would you event want to miss when your professor is as good looking as Hudson?!

I haven't been to this class in weeks and just use the textbook and get A's on the exams. Lot's of extra credit opportunities. Only 4 short, easy labs. Assignments are graded easily and only 1 a week if that. Lectures were boring so that's why I never went. One group project but it was making a poster and didn't have to present it. Easy GE class.

I don't know why this class has such an easy rating. It is not tough to get a good grade, but it does require a significant amount of work. The grading was pretty arbitrary on all extra assignments. You definitely need to read the book at least to some extent to do well in this class. There is a lot of reading.

Prof. Hudson is an amazing professor who really cares about the students.  Easy class for those with no passion for science.  There are a few field trips, but not difficult.  Quizzes for every lecture, but they're not too bad and not weighted heavily.  Easy tests and easy A.

Prof. Husdon is a good lecturer. He knows his stuff and clearly explains it. He offers some extra credit and is super willing to help. Pretty easy class, I would suggest taking it. Also the experiments are interesting.

Good professor. Understands that most students are not Geology majors. Tests are pretty average for a GE, just pay attention in class, review the quizzes and go to the review session and you should get a good grade. Prof. Hudson cares about students and wants you to do good in his class.

Dr. Hudson is a great geology teacher. His lectures aren't the most interesting, but he teaches the subject well and will help you out if you need it. I highly recommend doing the reading in the book and studying hard for the tests. If you do that, you'll do fine.

Super easy A as long as you read the chapter before class and at least pay attention to the lecture. Hudson makes a bomb study guide to use for the tests, which are fairly easy as far as science classes go. Funny professor who genuinely cares that you get a good grade.
Easy A and Professor Hudson is a good guy and a good teacher. He made the geology more interesting than I thought it would be.

Hudson's class is easy and fun- even if you don't like the subject. Minimal homework, a few assignments require a trip to the Dinosaur museum and there is a field trip, just take a buddy and it's fine. He clearly outlines what is expected for tests and assignments. He is fair and will make the subject more entertaining.

Great teacher! He understands that the students taking this class only need it for GE credit so he makes the material easy to understand but still very interesting. He is super willing to help if you don't get something or have questions, and very forgiving if circumstances arrive/accepting late work. Open book quizzes for every class.

I didn't even care about geology until this class. Hudson is very personable and I found him hilarious. He is dedicated to helping the students. He made learning hands on and fun for me. I actually enjoyed doing assignments. Go to class, pay attention and study a few hours a week and you will be golden. TAKE THIS CLASS. Best GE I've ever taken.
He has high love + high expectations for students. If you don't understand something, just ask him.

Best Spanish class I have ever taken. Profe Lopez perfectly balances giving applicable assignments with flexibility. He's funny and understanding of life situations. There is 1 midterm and 1 final and both are reasonably easy. You will likely spend ~2 hours/week.

Fascinating class, the professor is amazing and can be quite humorous. Content is very dense, as this is essentially an introduction to both translation and translation theory. Uses English more and is more difficult than other Spanish classes at BYU, but worth it if you're interested in translation. Workload isn't that bad, and he grades nicely.

Professor Lopez has found a wonderful balance of engaging lectures in class while still being funny and personable. There is lots of "busy work" in this class (3 or 4 assignments per week), but it is very manageable. Exams are extremely easy. Overall, would highly recommend this class from him.

This class was challenging and I learned a lot, but it is set up for you to succeed! Professor does a great job of giving feedback and making sure assignment deadlines (and exams) are fair! Overall, loved this class and I feel like I learned a lot :)

Lots of little assignments that are somewhat easy to complete. Focusing in class and his exam review sessions (during class periods) and completing homework assignments (2-3/week) will lead you to success. Great class and would have loved to take more from him. All 323R/323B classes are the same by the way.

Everything is essentially a completion grade. Super chill 3 credit class. Sometimes the assignments are annoying but just do them and you get 100%. Class sometimes isn't the most engaging but you get attendance points for going. Super chill dude too. If you need extensions on assignments just email him.

Professor Lopez is amazing! You can tell he really cares about his students and wants us all to succeed. He is going to do everything in his power to allow you to do well in his class. His expectations are clear and it is obvious what is being asked in each assignment. Would definitely recommend taking his class.

I really enjoyed his class! At first, it can seem overwhelming, all that you have to do each week, but as you get into your routine, it becomes a lot easier (and means there's less pressure for the final exam!) Pay attention in class- he throws in some of the funniest jokes in lectures, and if you don't pay attention, you'll miss it. Highly rated.

Professor Lopez is so caring. He answers emails so quickly, gave me excused absences on every day when I was sick for 2 weeks, and is so helpful and awesome. The class was a bit boring sometimes with lots of reading. He calls on people randomly in class so pay attention. I actually improved my overall Spanish by a lot because of his help.

Professor Lopez was one of the best professors I've had at BYU. The course was interesting (he's developed it himself) and everything felt like it had a purpose in being taught.

He gave me extensions on assignments when I was super sick, and responds nearly immediately to every email.

Take this class and professor if you can!

Profesor Lopez's class was super easy and the easiest tests I've ever taken at BYU. He has so much helpful information online for each assignment and knows his stuff about the spanish business world. Great guy and even greater professor. I would reccomend his class, even if it's at an inopportune time, to anyone!

Professor is super funny, nice, and the class is set up well. Everything that will be on the test is covered clearly. And if you ask him for additional help he will go over everything. The final is 25 questions picked from a bank of 50 questions that has been available all semester. Participate= easy, easy A. 
Professor is an amazing man!

Maybe it is different during covid times but I decided to drop his class because he elected not to teach and to just have the students complete busy work out of a textbook. I thought high school was over but I guess not for everybody.
So, yeah. Pretty average; don't expect greatness.
He is a really good guy. I liked the class and it wasn't extremely hard, he didn't give out a ton of busy work. Also a great sense of humor.

I've taken several Spanish classes from Lopez and would recommend him for any class. He is passionate and knowledgeable about his subject and cares about his students. Things to know: lots of reading, schedule can be a bit confusing, check your email right before class, he sends emails with important info.

The first day of class, his Spanish accent brought tears to my eyes and the eyes of my neighbor. I cried because it reminded me of my mission in Spain. My neighbor cried because he couldn't believe the Spanish accent was so ridiculous. Awesome class.

Dr. Lopez is a great professor, I really enjoy taking the translation courses from him. He cares a lot about his students' success and is always available through email or outside of class to answer questions. I learn a lot in his class and he gives great feedback on translations. He sometimes cancels class so check your email before you go.

He had some interesting things to say in lectures, but regarding the course content itself, it was more helpful to read the book. He tended to talk a lot, doing little more than repeating what's in the book. By talking so much, he didn't allow much time even for his own plans. I wish we had done more actual practice and application.

Professor Lopez Alcalá is a great teacher! He makes sure that we understand the material being presented, takes the time to answer questions and explain in detail, is willing to help outside of class if needed, and genuinely cares about us as students. I learned a ton in his class and loved how he connects it to current global and national events.

Profe is one of my favorite professors of all time, and definitely one of the most caring. Class is all grammar so it isn't super exciting, but he's funny so it is somewhat enjoyable. Very helpful teacher, 4 250 word essays, 4 tests and an article reading log to be filled out 3 times a week. Take 321 from him, he's fantastic

Great teacher! He is very knowledgeable of the language. If he doesn't know how to answer your question then he will research it and come back with a solid answer. The class was straight forward work wise. Easy if you served a spanish speaking mission, I didn't serve a spanish speaking mission and Dr. Lopez was very helpful. Take Dr. Lopez!

This was a great class and Dr. Lopez is a great teacher.  He really tries hard to help his students understand the concepts, which for me are quite difficult.  All of the homework together was pass/fail and there are lots of tests and thus many opportunities to do well.  Be diligent in studying and you should do fine.

Professor Lopez is a very professional guy who presents himself well. He is super nice. But, I felt that attending class was a waste of my time. 3 translation texts, 1 final in testing center, weekly reading quizzes out of the book. Good guy, boring class. Take it for an A to B grade depending on how hard he grades you.

Easiest class I've taken at BYU. Also arguably the most boring. If you're trying to get the 16 credits and an easy A enroll. If you want to be enthralled by lectures and enjoy going to class, don't take Spanish.

This was his first semester teaching this course, but I thought he did a fantastic job. He works really hard to help each student learn the material, and he is incredibly knowledgable on the subject matter. Not too much homework, and all of it is very beneficial. Only 2 tests! Definitely recommend him for any Spanish Class!!
He speaks really fast in class, but as long as you keep up with the daily assignments, it is an easy class and he is always willing to help.

I loved Professor López. He genuinely cares about each student and does everything possible to help us understand each concept. He is hilarious but also very inspirational, and has an incredible knowledge of the spanish language. The tests can be difficult but he will help you prepare well in advance in class. Best professor I've had at BYU!

Profesor Lopez is an incredible professor that really cares about each student and is more than willing to work with you to help you understand the material and succeed in his class. So sad he won't be my teacher next semester!!!
Great teacher. He knows the answers to your questions and if he doesn't, he won't fake it, he'll find the answer and tell you the next day.
Professor Lopez rocks. He's one of the best professors I've ever encountered in my life.
Best professor I've had at BYU. He tries to meet your goals with the class but makes you work for it too.
I wish I could take all of my Spanish classes with Profesor Lopez! He truly is great!

Professor Lopez is the person that has helped me learn, and apply what I have learned, better than any other professor I have had at BYU thus far. He takes time to answer any question you may have through email, or meet with you personally, and cares more about the student's growth and ability achieve their goals than merely giving out a grade.

Profesor Lopez is seriously the BEST. I am super sad that I will not longer be in his class! He is from Spain and speaks English with a British accent. His knowledge of the two languages is phenomenal! He is hilarious, super nice, and wants his students to succeed! If you do all the assignments in the class, you will do well in the class!

Professor Lopez is my favorite professor I've ever had at BYU.  He treats us like adults, he teaches incredibly well, he genuinely cares about each student. The preparation he puts into his classes is amazing, and it definitely has an effect on how much we learn in class. Charismatic, funny, interesting, effective. Gotta take his classes.

Professor Lopez is bar none my favorite professor at BYU. Apart from being a native Spanish speaker, he has thoroughly studied the language as well as English and as a result knows just as much about grammar as he does about translation. He is always willing to meet with students to help or discuss anything and does all he can to help them.
Great teacher! Cares more about you understanding the material than any other professor I've had. He is always willing to work with you and help out.
Best teacher for 321, no debate. Hilarious. Sometimes class was a little boring, but it was a great course overall.

I took Spanish 321 with Professor Lopez and loved it. He's a great professor; he very clearly tells us everything we need to know before tests; his class might get a little boring at times, but I think that's just the subject material. I recommend him to anyone taking Spanish. I learned a lot, too.

Very knowledgeable, easy to understand, gives a lot of examples to clarify his teachings. His materials are really helpful and he has a passion for the field he is teaching. He is also an excellent person, very respectful of his students, always ready to listen and to share ideas.

Excellent teacher. His teaching methods are a bit different than what Americans are accustomed to, but that's because he's from Europe. Very kind, and very easy to approach with questions and insights. Many people say his grading is a bit nit-picky, but that's because he's been in the industry and knows what we need to do to actually make it.
Very great professor. If you ask him for help or clarification, you'll get it. the tests are fair and the work is not busywork nor overwhelming.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! I took him for ASL 201, and I learned SO MUCH from him - I see improvement in my skills from every class. He is absolutely HILARIOUS! You can tell he has a passion for ASL and it is apparent when he teaches. He cares about all of his students and is such an amazing person. Will be taking his class again in the near future!

Sam Farley is hilarious and I absolutely loved his classes. He taught my ASL101 class, and jumped at the chance to take 201 from him. He's really nice, flexible, and hilarious. He'll work with you, just make sure to communicate. He's kinda a goof too. I loved going to class every time. You'll never leave class and not have laughed in class.

I have taken several classes from Sam and he's the bomb. It's definitely worth the evening classes. He has a full-time job outside of teaching so he doesn't give you extra stuff he doesn't want to grade. And will probably let you out early if there's a 49ers game happening. He has kids in college and just gets it. Love this guy!

Sam is the best! His class is a lot of fun - a nice break during the week. My class had a lot of laughs and inside jokes by the end. You will have homework, but it only takes about 1-2 hours a week. You'll have opportunities to attend Deaf events (2). My signing improved a lot!

Sam may be the best professor you will ever have at BYU! He is highly qualified for his job and goes above and beyond to make sure you have a great experience. You see his students come first for him, and he wants to make sure they're okay. I always left his class feeling better than I did going in. Definitely recommend!

AMAZING PROFESSOR! I took him for ASL 201, and I learned SO MUCH from him - I see improvement in my skills from every class. He is absolutely HILARIOUS! You can tell he has a passion for ASL and it is apparent when he teaches. He cares about all of his students and is such an amazing person. Will be taking his class again in the near future!

He'll work with you, just make sure to communicate. He's kinda a goof too. I loved going to class every time. You'll never leave class and not have laughed in class.

He has a full-time job outside of teaching so he doesn't give you extra stuff he doesn't want to grade. And will probably let you out early if there's a 49ers game happening. He has kids in college and just gets it. Love this guy!

Sam may be the best professor you will ever have at BYU! He is highly qualified for his job and goes above and beyond to make sure you have a great experience. You see his students come first for him, and he wants to make sure they're okay. I always left his class feeling better than I did going in. Definitely recommend!

She's a great professor. Cares about her students grades and good at communicating. She can even change the deadline for you if you communicate to her. There are a lot reading and writing, but it's a writing class, so it's reasonable.

Great overview of creative writing, though Prof. Sorenson primarily writes essay form and thus has somewhat of an expectation that students already know how to use this form. She's very helpful and accessible outside of class, but doesn't believe in giving 100% grades. Class is based on participation and improvement, which is nice.
Love her! She's great and really cares about her students. Isn't terribly difficult. Plus she gives lots of opportunities for extra credit. Totally reccommend her.

I loved this class! I really don't even like writing very much, but this class is straightforward and fun. She is so nice, and takes time to help you individually. It is pretty easy, but you learn a lot too!

She is a great teacher and is really great in giving you back useful feedback to improve your papers! She really care about her students. She may grade papers a bit harder than an average WRTG150 teacher but if you do your best on your papers and go to writing center and make sure you follow due dates for every assignment, an A is very doable.
I don't like writing, but this class wasn't horrible. I feel like grades are very subjective on the papers though. I really learned a lot in this class.
Wonderful teacher, really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Will offer help and some extra credit. Do the work on time to a good standard and you will do well!

She cares about her students very much and is a very open-minded individual. She is very clear and professional when it comes to deadlines and grades. Keep the deadlines! Don't be late! And do all you can for the extra credit. You will get an A.

This class is easy to get an A in AS LONG AS YOU do the work and do it to the best of your ability. Also take advantage of the extra credit she offers on your essay's by going to the writing center! It helps your grade a lot.

Dr. Hope is the sweetest person! Her lectures are entertaining, and she makes hard concepts easy to understand. I highly recommend her! The TAs make a study guide for each lecture, and if you understand the study guide, you will do so well in the class. Such a chill and fun class. A 95% is an A, and its only that high because its so doable.

The class is structured almost entirely around exams, with an in class quiz every other week. Lectures dive into very specific examples of biological concepts without clearly explaining the underlying ideas, leaving students expected to already understand the material. Unfortunately, the readings don't align well with what's covered in class.

I LOVEEEE Dr. Hope. She is so funny and amazing. The only reason why her class is hard is that is 95% is needed for an A. If you just memorize the study guide they post on learning suite the exams are almost the same, and super easy.

I loved having Dr. Hope. She actually made my day in class. The class is a lot of memorization, so pay attention in class and study group. Her tests are multiple choice which is also nice. Overall, Dr. Hope is just awesome.

She's an awesome MMBIO 240 teacher. Her live-drawn in-class slides are better than usual PowerPoints (in my opinion), they have lots of good visuals, and she knows INCREDIBLY well about the topics she's teaching. Weekly reviews also helped a lot. Overall, she really helped us remember all the different molecules and what they do

Hope is so loving and funny. If you like the high pace, ADHD, teaching then she's for you. Her slides often look weird because they are always hand drawn, but her structure of teaching is great. prepare for the learning activities!

Dr Hope is the best! What she teaches in class is exactly what's on the exams. If you show up to class and take notes, you'll get an A. No homework assignments. She is super funny and really cares about students as well.

Dr. Hope is amazing! She really loves all of her students. Attendance isn't mandatory, but its pretty vital for success, she uses a lot of visuals and drawings for her lectures. There are quizzes every other week that really help you to learn throughout the semester and prepare for tests. I would definitely take her again and for other classes too.

Pay attention in lecture and do the study guide and youll do well. She changed the grade scale so a 95% is an A. This kind of kills considering you only have 5% wiggle room to get an A. But its doable just work hard. This class is heavy on the memorization.

Dr. Hope is the kindest and most caring professor I have ever had. She truly loves her students and makes that very clear. Her lectures are always fun and entertaining. She has a five-minute break in the middle of each one. In addition, she is just a super funny, happy person whose good mood is infectious.

If you have an iPad. Take Professor Hope. If you don't. Don't take her. It is very hard to take notes in her class unless you have an iPad. She writes things down on pre-made slides so you will need an iPad. 95% is an A which is tough and the tests are weighted very heavily.

Dr. Hope is the funniest person you will ever meet. The class material is the most boring class ever but she makes it fun. She annotates screenshots on the projector. She posts slides after. 95% is an A which is why the class is "hard" but it's achievable. 5 in class quizzes, lets you correct with groups for half credit, TA's were hard on grading.
Dr. Hope is very passionate and makes her class very interesting! It's possible to get a good grade in this class!
Great funny professor

I can't speak on her biology but she is truly such a caring and sweet professor! She was always smiling and made UNIV so easy! If you need a good UNIV professor TAKE HER! She literally brought treats every day and as long as you went you go credit for the class (super easy especially compared to some of my friends' UNIV classes).

I had Dr. Hope for UNIV 101, so I can't speak to her biology, but she is a very sweet and caring individual! She brought snacks to every lecture and was very accomodating with deadlines. Also, her UNIV is much more interesting than any of my friend's classes. If you need a good UNIV professor, I would very highly recommend!!

I only had Dr. Hope for Univ but she really is a kind and caring person. She made sure that everyone was able to get credit for the class and did not put any pressure on the grading of it, very flexible. I can't really comment on her ability to teach Biology courses, but if I was to take one, just based on her character, I would.

Dr. Hope is a great professor. If you need to take a mmbio class, take it from her. She really takes her time to explain things, and she is very reasonable. One of my favorite classes ever! She is so nice and is really easy to talk to. The study guide is so helpful, and it really helped me to learn! Overall, great class.

10/10 recommend Dr. Hope. Her tests are easy, especially if you do well on the learning activities (in class quizzes) which prepare you really well. Dr. Hope's lectures are a little dry, but the outside of class study groups with the TA's are amazing (ask them lots of questions). I'm not great at bio, but I put in the work and easily got an A

Be warned getting a A in this class is pretty hard but not impossible. She bumped a A to a 96 if I remember right. The class is SUPER test heavy, the TA's take notes in class of everything that could be included on a test which is so nice if you just study those notes that they gave through and through you will do well. Tuff but doable class.

Dr Hope was amazing! I took MMBIO 240 with her and it was great! I think some of the low ratings are due to the MMBIO 240 class itself. It is a difficult class no matter who you take it from, but Dr. Hope was an amazing teacher! I highly recommend her for this class, and any MMBIO class honestly.

Dr. Hope was my best professor I have ever had. I have taken her for both MMBIO 121 and MMBIO 261 and she was amazing in both. She is incredibly thoughtful and teaches super clearly. She makes her expectations really clear, and provides a study guide for each exam. She even taught one of my exam reviews once! An A is 95%, but it is super attainable

So kind and fun! She cares a lot about her students and creates breaks and community in the middle of each lecture. Especially after MMBIO121, this class just takes the general biology you should already know from other classes and goes more in depth on DNA and protein synthesis. Not that difficult, and she makes it really interesting!

Dr. Hope is top tier. She clearly cares about her students, and pushes them to succeed. As for any class like this, effort is required to do well. Dr. Hope designed the class to elicit student success, and I appreciate that. Lectures can be hard to follow, but easier if you go to them and pay attention. She made a hard class fun.

Dr. Hope is caring, but her class is tough—95% is an A, and exams are 70% of your grade. A strong start is crucial. Lectures and TA reviews are essential, as her iPad notes aren't clear without context. Got As on every exam and still finished with a 94%, missing the A mark by 1%. Take this class if you're okay with an A- or really love bio.

Professor Hope genuinely cares about all of her students and is super sweet! For this class at least she took a bunch of diagrams from the textbook and would draw on them with her iPad. It worked for the class but you have to make sure to follow along. TA's have study sessions daily (you go for class credit) good class overall!

Dr. Hope is one of my favorite professors at BYU. Her class was very organized. She had learning activities, study groups, and TA reviews before exams so it was always clear what would be tested on. It is a 95% to get an A but it is very achievable. This is a great class!

This is an easy enough class and she is a great person. However, her lectures are very boring and hard to pay attention during. All she does is scribble on her iPad and it's hard to tell what we are even looking at.

Dr. Hope is awesome. However, the lectures tend to feel pretty unorganized and its hard to grasp what you are meant to extract from it. It is a HUGE info dump. An A in the class is a 95% which is lowkey kinda hard to achieve. Also, the mandatory study groups are just... ok. Often the TAs kinda just sit there and chime in sometimes.

This class was the best course I have taken at BYU. You get to go on three field trips, and you get to know your peers so well. I made friends and laughed with these people, and I wish I could take this course every year! Dr. Hope is so sweet and hilarious. I would recommend this class to every student attending BYU, interested in MMBIO or not.

I took extremophiles with Dr. Hope and it was such a great experience! The class itself is pretty easy with it only being a term class and most of the grade weight coming from the field trips and participation. I loved Dr. Hope, she is very caring and hilarious, I also learned about some potential career choices in MMBIO.

I did all Gen Bio classes and learned the most from Dr. Hope. Her lectures consist of drawing and going over concepts which for a visual learner like me was a game changer. She walks through the processes and dissects them. Her TAs were great and I always felt prepared for tests. She does require a textbook, but it was good supplemental material.

Don't get the textbook. She only tests based on material that she covers in class. The exam review questions are a perfect way to study. Tests are extremely fair and easy. The 95% A cut-off shouldn't scare you at all. Dr. Hope is also super funny and very helpful in her office hours.

Use her study guides to prep for tests, and you will do great!

Group homework weekly (1-2 dropped), coordinate with other students.

Quiz every Wednesday (2 dropped), harder than the tests.

Tests are all multiple-choices, questions are from her posted study guides and past quizzes. Review her lecture notes to study.

Not the clearest lectures.

Is caring, but very disorganized. She jumps around a lot and doesn't explain things clearly. A lot of unfinished sentences. Lectures feel like completely different and unrelated concepts. Just don't take MMBIO 240 from her. Most of my learning was outside of class. Doesn't teach, you will have to teach yourself.

Dr. Hope really cares about her students and tries to make it a good experience. She is new to teaching this course and the textbook sucked, so this semester was tough, but I think it will be a lot better in the future. We went over some basic things too much and then glossed over really complicated things sometimes.

Professor Hope has such as kind heart! However, this class was a dumpster fire! Lectures were jumbled, chaotic, and disorganized. It was impossible to follow what was being taught. I left every class feeling confused and defeated! The weekly quizzes were BRUTAL! This being said it was her first semester teaching this class so it might get better.

DO NOT TAKE MMBIO 240 FROM DR. HOPE! She is very carring and you can feel the love that she has for her students but the course was very unorganized and the lectures were hard to follow. The cap for an A was a 95% and there is not extra credit opportunities. You also only get 2 lectures a week due to weekly quizzes.

Professor Hope is an amazing caring person but MMBIO 240 was all over the place. It was her first semester teaching the course so she was still figuring everything out but most of my learning was outside of class. Most of the time it was very unclear what I needed to know. The textbook was little help.

Dr. Hope is an amazing person; however, she was not the best professor for mmbio 240. Her lectures were all over place and many incomplete thoughts. The TAs carried this class because they were the ones teaching us outside of class! Also, the textbook was very hard to understand, so it didn't help much.

Dr. Hope is funny and kind, but her class is hard core. To take notes, make sure you can draw along with her either on a tablet or on paper, and DO THE READING before Wednesday quizzes. She's a wonderful teacher, but it can be easy to get lost in the lectures. Go to TA hours! They know what you will need to know and will prune down info for you.

She is an amazing woman, however, lectures were very difficult to follow, containing a ton of incomplete sentences and unfinished ideas. TAs and professor would teach different things. There are weekly quizzes that have no clear explanation on what the quizzes will be about. 95% is an A. Tests are easier though.

Dr. Hope is very sweet and cares about her students, but her lectures are so hard to follow. She jumps around a lot and doesn't explain things clearly. A lot of unfinished sentences... She is accessible outside of class and willing to help. If you take this class make sure to go see TAs often and study with other people in the class.

Dr. Hope's lectures are indiscernable. Her "slides" are just a PDF of random pictures which makes notes difficult. She's tends to jump around a lot. Lectures feel like completely different and unrelated concepts. Just don't take MMBIO 240 from her. She's nice, but I would prefer if her slides were compiled by another professor.

She is literally so nice!! You will feel very loved being in her classroom. That being said, the class is very difficult. The study guide has everything on the test but the tests ask for very specific pieces of information. The weekly study groups are super helpful. If you're not good with test taking or you're bad at memorizing...good luck :)
Fair grader. Need to go to class because everything taught is tested. She comes in with energy and fun!

Dr. Hope is a super nice professor and she really cares about her students. That being said, this is a tough class and the tests look for very minute details so make sure to study hard and don't pass up a detail that you think is too insignificant to be tested. I'd recommend her as a professor regardless though.

Dr. Hope is an amazing professor. She really cares about her students and is super approachable. She really wants everyone, including those who are taking the class as a general like me, to have a passion for microbiology. Go to TA reviews weekly. I made the mistake of not going and suffered a bit for it. Dr. Hope is awesome!
A literal saint. Explains things super well, super fair grader, very kind. You know she loves you from day 1.

Prof. Hope is a really fun teacher! She has a goofy personality that made MMBIO 121 really entertaining. She can be a little scatterbrained but she is good at tying things back to her lectures. Attendance was mandatory once a week out of 3 lectures. Material can be difficult at times but she is good at repeating and repassing over material.

Dr. Hope has been one of my FAVORITE professors! She is honestly the most caring professor I've ever had! She cares about her students and wants them to succeed! She is very accessible outside of class and is willing to help in any way she can. The weekly 'outside learning' meetings were only useful if you asked questions to the TAs.

Dr. Hope is literally the kindest proffessor I have ever had at BYU. She lectures clearly and makes all of her class notes available outside of class. She is so willing to help students and you can tell she cares about you and wants you to succeed. Theres not much homework, a couple papers and some online reading quizzes. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Dr. Hope is really nice and genuinely cares about her students. She's got a sense of humor, but sometimes it just gets old. (Easy) weekly reading quizzes, three writing assignments (also easy). It's the tests that are hard. And worth a lot of your grade. The study guides are tedious, but they're thorough. 95% is the cut off for an A.

This class was DIFFICULT and is probably my least favorite MMBIO class I've taken at BYU. LOTS OF DETAILS you have to know for the tests, which were really hard. The A cut off is a 95%, with no curves or extra credit. Dr. Hope is helpful (go to office hours), but I don't recommend this class. It reminded me of Organic Chemistry. Study hard or die.

A very practical class to take with Dr. Hope. Teaches some super valuable lab skills, is very helpful whenever something isn't making very much sense, and as long as you show up and participate the material isn't very difficult and there isn't a ton of homework.

Dr. Hope is super nice. The class was really hard (95% for an A), but she definitely does her best to ensure that the students learn the material and the class average was high (89.99%). Accessible out of class and really friendly. Take pictures of the board to make sure you don't miss anything and tests are worth 70% of final grade so don't slack!

You have to get a 95 or better to get an A, so this is a hard class. But Dr. Hope is clear in what she teaches and in what she expects you to know for tests. I think this class was one of the most fun and interesting I've had at BYU. It helps that Dr. Hope is hilarious! Work hard and follow the study guides and you'll do just fine!

First off this is not an easy class and an A is 95%. That being said Dr. Hope is an awesome professor. Her test are hard but that is only because there is a lot of material. She gives a really good study guide and her tests are not tricky at all. If you know the material you will do good. She is a great instructor that explains things well.

By far my favorite professor so far. She is so smart but makes sure every student in the class understands the material. She is so funny and makes the whole class laugh. Her tests are based directly off the study guides so if you take the time to fill those out you are set to get good scores. Go to study groups, and do the extra credit.

I loved Dr. Hope. I hate science, but I loved this class. She posts study guides to fill out before each exam. Memorize them, and you'll get an A. She offers extra credit, too. Show up, take notes, and you'll do great.

I thoroughly enjoyed every class with Dr. Hope and felt like she cared about her students. I would suggest you do the readings ahead of time and attend lecture. She lectures off of her iPad with drawings and such and posts the slides after. These really only make sense if you put in the time beforehand. If you dont like her, its probably on you.

Best class I have taken at BYU, hands down. She was so engaging and loves immunology. Weekly reading quizzes, most everyone got 100% on them. Her study guides were clear cut, and she didn't have anything on the test she didn't tell you about. Lectures are definitely mandatory (no powerpoints), but I never wanted to miss her class.

She's a good lady, but I didn't really learn anything from her. She just draws on her ipad and lectures so it's hard to learn anything and retain information. There are study groups each week you attend but it's not very helpful. She does have test study guides on LS so it's best to find the answers from the textbook and study those.

Dr. Hope is an amazing teacher! Ive taken two classes from her now, and both times its been great! Shes super fun and quirky, her lectures are great, and her tests are easy if you pay attention in class. Lectures arent posted, so its important you go to class. Homework every week with textbook readings, and study groups every week as well.

Super great class. You learn a ton but Dr. Hope makes it really doable. Her lectures are very interactive. If you ask a question she always knows the answers and takes the time to explain difficult concepts.

Dr. hope is awesome! Class is not very hard tests are very clear; lots of extra credit. Not that hard to get an A if you pay attention during class. She also brings much more of health and disease topics that make this class much more interesting than PDBIO 120 for an entry level coarse. Day to day work is quite light; tests require some studying

Good teacher. My only problem was this was her first time teaching a entry level class so she was use to upper level things and she made the class similar to what a upper level class would be material wise. Its all doable but I found questions on testes to be worded in ways where I had no idea what the answer was but knew details of the answer.

I love Dr. Hope! Her class is pretty tough, but you will learn SO many cool things, and overall its worth it! She is super nice, hilarious, passionate about teaching and her subject matter. You need to pay attention, take good notes, and study hard; but its not impossible to get a good grade if you put in the work. She is a dynamic and fun lecturer

This was a very deep and detailed course for being an entry level course, but I still enjoyed it. Dr Hope really knows so much, and has a good sense of humor. There wasn't a lot of homework, but I had to study a lot because of how much depth there was in the material she taught. She is a great teacher.

She's a fantastic lecturer and a clear grader. There are no surprises in the course; stay on top of the syllabus and you'll be fine. She come across as very competent and well-prepared in her lectures, and finds a way to make even pedantic biology seem accessible and sometimes even interesting.

Coach Marks is awesome! She really helped me improve in volleyball this semester. I was worried that taking intermediate instead of beginner wouldn't be a good fit for me, but I improved so much, so I'm glad I picked this class. I had a ton of fun!

Coach Marks taught the course like we were high schoolers. We had our midterm in class and spent the last 15 minutes chatting. She relied on slides and internet content, even making us listen to a podcast with her husband. It felt like she didn't grasp the material, and attendance was the biggest part of our grade.

The class felt like so much busywork There was way too much reading and most of the assignments felt pointless The reading checks have questions with the most random little pieces of information within the 30 pages of reading that we were supposed to know. I feel like she didn't know that much about the topics because she couldn't answer questions
Will help you improve, great and fun class!

Coach Marks is one of the best professors at BYU. She cares about her students. She did 2 min. conversations with each of her students in the class. She really cared about what was going on outside of their academics. You read the assigned textbook chapter and write a one page reflection and take a 5 question quiz for each class. Highly Recommend!

Professor Marks is nice, but the class felt disorganized. There was constant busywork—daily reading quizzes and papers due every other day. Lectures were mostly personal stories instead of useful, evidence-based material. She also didn't seem very enthusiastic about her job.
Taken volleyball twice now with Coach Marks and she is the best. Really good at helping you improve your form and she cares about seeing her students improve!

She is really nice, but I felt like most of the class was her telling stories about her life. Class did not seem backed by much evidence and I felt like she was often teaching her opinions. The content is extremely easy and likely stuff that you already have heard of before. She was very accommodating, however, which I appreciated.
It's volleyball. She's aight I guess
This was my third semester taking a volleyball class from Sandra, and I'm going to try and take another! SO so fun, minimal work required, AND you can miss up to 5 days
She definitely deserves the title of coach. Allows you to miss five classes (and some make up work if you do more). Final is open notes. Take it from her.

Coach Marks is a caring and kind teacher. She made class work despite my class section being a quite boring bunch. Class is easy, make sure you do the reading to be ready for the quiz every other class or so. There are bigger tests which are easy as long as you do the study guide. Shes great!

I took Marks for EXSC221 (not an option to rate) and she was amazing. There were textbook readings before class which were expanded on in class. Attendance was mandatory and there were weekly 1 page reports, but the class was not too difficult. I learned about general human health while feeling cared for as an individual. She's great.
You're allowed to miss 5 days and the final exam is super easy. Take it from her! She's also super sweet.

Coach Marks is awesome! Best professor I've heard from talking to friends about other vball professors. She doesn't lump you with the same people every single class, so you get to meet and play with everyone. Awesome class! Final is super easy, just need to attend class to pass. She actually played with us and can tell she cares about everyone
easy pass obviously. She is a great coach and we had a fun time playing. If you enjoy vball and want to get better take it !
Coach Marks was super understanding. The class is a P or F and you likely won't fail anyway. The final test is super easy, straight out of the slides. Super informative class.
Best volleyball instructor I've found at BYU. 10/10 would recommend, especially for the intermediate class!
This a good class to help you work on goals in life. She cares a lot and gives good advice.

Coach Marks was an amazing teacher because she really cares about her students. She wants us to improve in all parts of our lives. She really wants to help students, especially if they are struggling. The class was pretty easy and has a light homework load. Have to attend class or you have to make it up.
Super easy, low stress, tests. Great teacher

I LOVE Professor Sephton.  She cares about the students, is gracious, understands the concepts inside and out and creates an enjoyable and interactive course.  I was not expecting to enjoy this class as much as I did.  If you are on the fence, take her class!  For me, the quizzes were hard, but they were not weighted very heavy.

Dr. Sephton is AWESOME! I took her Spring term class and, for a 3-hour class, she made it very fun and interactive. We had one group project, but lots of group discussions. There were lots of readings and quizzes on the readings (allowed one page of notes), but the tests are on a few chapters at a time and open book/notes. She is so caring too!

Dr. Sephton is amazing! She cares about her students and is always willing to help answer questions. She gives students a chance to learn through application and share what they've learned in meaningful ways (poster competition, teach others,lead a lab meeting). She has a passion and deep knowledge of her field which is reflected in her instruction

Dr. Sephton is a super nice professor and really cares about all of the students. A about 30 minutes of each lecture is devoted to discussing the topics in a group setting. It isn't hard to get an A as long as you are actively participating in the class and engaged in what is happening.

I am a TA for Dr.Sephton's psych 111 course, this is my second semester being a TA for her (fall 25-Win 26). Dr.Sephton is organized, supportive, and communicative. She fosters a collaborative and respectful environment. Expectations are clear and she is always open to questions and feedback, she creates an inclusive and engaging classroom.

Sandie was wonderful to work with and very supportive! She offered many opportunities to learn more in our lab, and helped me receive training to be a meditation teacher. She was very organized in getting us into lab roles that we were interested in and cared about what we wanted to learn. Her lab managers were also amazing!

Dr. Sephton is an amazing professor who is incredibly kind and understanding. Her class is structured in a way that truly minimizes stress, which I really appreciated. There is a fair amount of reading and weekly quizzes, but it's very manageable if you stay on top of the work. I would definitely recommend taking her class!

She is such a kind and compassionate person which makes her wonderful to be around. She truly cares about what is being taught in the class and that passion is displayed during her lectures. The class is not difficult in the work provided but it can be difficult in how it challenges our worldview.

Dr. Sephton was great. I could see how this class could be very difficult without the right teacher, but with Dr. Sephton it's hard not to get an A in her class. Only 3 exams (open book, online, no final), and you can retake each one with your TA group if you want. She makes class and projects fun and productive, and also offers extra credit.

She was very nice and cared. Quizzes were hard and not based on lectures. You meet with your group every class which breaks up lectures, test were awesome because they were open note and book and an opportunity to group test. I would recommend over all other psych 111 classes.

I highly recommend taking psych from a different professor. Her lectures don't help with any of the quizzes, only the textbook readings determine your grade for quizzes( it's a LOT of reading). She also takes attendance for a grade when the lectures are lowkey pointless. I will say her exams are open note and open book so an A is very achievable.
You will spend a good amount of time on reading, notes, and quiz/test each week but you will get an A. As long as you read the textbook and do the assignments you will get an A.

Most of the content is learned by reading the textbook. By the end of the semester I had pretty much read the whole book because that is what all the quizzes were based on and the lectures didn't cover everything. This class also had group discussions at the end of every class period which were super fun!

Most of what you need to know for the exams, you get from the readings (although you don't have to read every word, just glean the concepts). The lectures go over some of the readings, some other content you'll need, and some cool stuff for fun or for examples. It's lecture heavy, but you do spend part of class in a discussion group, which was fun

I had Dr. Sephton for PSYCH 111, and she is amazing! She's the kindest and most caring college professor ever. This semester, tests were open-note and open-textbook, and were taken first individually and then with your 10-person discussion group. This really helped me learn the material but also not stress too much about memorization! AMAZING!

Dr Sephton is amazing. I took her PSYCH 111 class and it was honestly not bad at all. There is a bit of reading and quizzes due every week but if you stay on top of your work you will be fine. She's so sweet. Would take again!

Dr. Sephton is super great and has such a passion for this topic. I think this class is one of the most eye-opening and important ones in the psychology program. The work is not hard at all, but it's all very insightful and rewarding. I feel like this class, unlike most, teaches things that I feel actually apply to my life.

I can't emphasize enough how amazing of an experience it has been to have taken Psych 305 with Prof Sephton. I've been able to watch as myself and my classmates work through our own biases that we didn't even realize we had. We've all become more caring and aware people. She encourages ALL viewpoints, and only asks that empathy drive what we say.

Her lectures are super informational and she does a great job of relating these lectures to the real world, and helping us know why what we are learning matters. She wants to help each student succeed and is willing to help accommodate you. Her lectures are full of a lot of information but she provides helpful lecture outlines with important info

I actually am taking her Psych 111 class, but there was no code option. Dr. Sephton is seriously one of the kindest professors. She is so patient with her students and truly tries to help them succeed. Her TA's are so good and they reach out when you struggle, she does an excellent job with training them. The tests are open book!

Sandie has been such an amazing mentor for me these past 2 years. I first took a class from her my sophmore year and have since been her TA. It is amazing to see how much she cares about her students and how much she trusts me as a TA. She always is looking at how to better her teaching and making the experience meaningful for the students.

Dr. Sephton was my professor and later my mentor as a TA, and I cannot recommend her enough. She was highly influential. I learned to study effectively, research, write reports, take ownership of my learning, and immerse myself in programs and events. Her class sharpens critical thinking- professors like her are rare. I'm thankful for her example

Dr. Sephton is amazing! She's kind, supportive, and truly cares about her students. She's super engaging and makes learning meaningful and fun, while also offering great research opportunities and mentorship. One of the best professors at BYU, take her class if you can!

Dr. Sephton is the most caring and influential professor at BYU. When working in her research lab, she expressed deep concern for my individual career and interests and is a mentor who changed my life. She is brilliant, with wide interests from biology to psychology, which means she can address questions about the biological basis of psychology.

I was Dr. Sephton's mentee in the Psychology Mentored Research Program in Fall 2024 and Winter 2025 and it was a great experience. Through weekly meetings I was able to learn from her and how she operates in the research setting. She is huge on hearing and listening to students as well as incorperating their thoughts and ideas into her research.

Dr Sephton is an amazing person and great teacher. She draws from a wealth of experience in research from her career and life experience and enriches each lecture with powerful and real examples of subject matter. I enjoyed getting to take two classes from her and get to know her as a professor. I wish I could take classes from her in grad school!

Dr. Sephton is unique in that she really makes you think about the world in a different way. She supplements textbook content with literature so you really learn the science, but also what's changing in the scientific landscape and who the major researchers are in health psychology. She cares about the success and well-being of her students.

I've worked a lot with Dr S as a research mentee of hers. That has been a phenomenal experience resulting in several posters and papers, and ultimately my admission into a PhD program. I would not be becoming a scientist, or certainly not at my current pace, if it weren't for Dr S's dedication, mentorship style, and capacity to build up mentees.

Dr. Sephton is one of the most generous, empowering mentors I've had. I've worked with her as a lab assistant, her TA and taken PSYCH 381/305 from her. She helped me secure a grant for mindfulness training at UConn so I could teach mindfulness classes for her lab! The doors she's opened for me have been life-changing and she is the best professor!

Holy moly.... if you want a professor that challenges you, inspires you, and makes you think about the world in a different way... Dr. Sephton is the way to go! Not only is she beautiful and wise, but she really makes me think about the course material.
She was okay. She taught maybe 3 lectures for the entire semester and the rest was group presentations. Overall, the class is easy to follow along and easy to get a good grade.

This class honestly didnt even need a professor. I learned hardly anything. Dr. Sephton was extremely difficult to communicate with and get ahold of, and she gave so many excuses. Her grading policies were very unclear. Definitely would not recommend her as a professor.

She was almost completely inaccessible by email. She put assignments into canvas after they were due and input quizzes with no questions, so when you took the quiz you would get a zero. She taught two lectures on psychobiology the entire semester and expected students to teach the rest. She wasted a ton of time on mindfulness assignments every day.

I really regret taking her class. Recycles the course from previous semesters. Not good at answering emails. Too much busy work and she doesn't teach. She led 2 classes and the rest have been student led presentations. 40 min presentation so if you don't have a good group, good luck. Lazy teaching style. So disappointing, take from someone else.

This class was disappointing. Labelled neuroscience elective, Learned meditation skills. She gave 3 lectures total, then had the students prepare assignments, test questions, rubrics, and lectures for the last 10 weeks of class. I learned nothing about psychobiology. Her canvas was bad, and we had to retake assignments she formatted wrong. Easy A

I took Prof. Pendleton's Comms 300 class online. Weekly discussion posts, weekly reading quizzes that you can redo, and 2 papers. There's also a course outline assignment. 1 midterm and a final. The course outline assignment is ambiguous and it seems like Pendleton wants it that way. She can be tough to reach, but really nice and knowledgeable.

I took this class online so obviously there was a lot more homework and reading than a normal class. Professor Pendleton is super nice and really fun. I don't like learning about laws (but had to for my major) so I wish I would've taken this class in person. Lots of quizzes but if you study for them you'll be fine. A good starting online class.

Professor Pendleton is a lawyer still trying to figure out how to be a teacher. She has interesting and entertaining experience, but she fluctuates her grading style, sometimes being incredibly difficult and sometimes being the easiest thing ever which can be frustrated. No one knew what their grade would be until the last day.

Professor Pendleton lectures for the entirety of the class. Her assignments are extremely broad and difficult to interpret. The exams are long and difficult and you really have to fight for your grade in the class. She defers a lot to her TA, who is a harsh grader. Lastly, she is unapproachable and difficult to reach outside of class.

My favorite class this semester. It's so easy, the tests are concept based mainly, so know the stuff, but if you go to class and listen and you'll pass. She's a lawyer so she knows her field, and it's very useful stuff to know so you don't get in trouble in the future. She's respectful to everyone's politics, which I respect. Just a little reading.

All of the French professors at BYU are great, but Dr. Phenix is maybe the best of all of them when it comes to caring about students. She learned all of our names in the first class and working on making class fun, relatable, and inspiring. Would highly recommend taking 321 or one of her other classes from her if you're up for the challenge.

I took this class while not being an RM so that explains the grade, class was awesome, she's a great professor. Make sure to get your speaking/writing/grammar lab appts set up ASAP or it's super hard to get in.

One of the greatest professors I have ever had. She cares about students and wants us to learn life lessons. She tied French history to our lives today, the gospel, and future society. Truly so smart and very kind, willing to take questions and feedback. Dr. Phenix is the epitome of high love, high expectations, everyone should take her class.

Dr Phenix is THE BEST! she is sooo inspirational and such a boss woman. There is a big paper at the end of class that was actually such a beast but she is so helpful and encouraging. Take this class from her!

Honestly I loved Professor Phenix' class. She really makes an effort to turn a class that could be so boring, into something fun and interactive. She has a positive outlook and is an optimist grader. She really knows her french too! When you take her class, be ready for fun and to take lots of grammar quizzes (you get infinite attempts) Formidable!

Dr. Phenix truly cares about her students. She loves to laugh and knows how to help you become competent in the french language. She believes in her students and encourages participation. Some of the organization of the class is unclear, so be sure to ask questions. Use your resources like the French Writing and Grammar Lab!

She is a fun professor. I'm not sure if the class was tremendously hard because that's how the class is or because of how she organized it, but this is the hardest class I have ever taken. About 8-12 quizzes due before each class and many readings. However, she is willing to help you outside class and also explain things in class. Very fast paced.

Dr. Phenix is the best. She makes it clear that she cares about you as both a person and a student. Class was always entertaining, since she always incorporates fun jokes (and various jabs at Provo culture) there's never a dull moment. I saw legitimate progress with my French too, especially in my writing. Would highly recommend her class!

Pros: fun and chill. Easy grader. Readings aren't necessary to do well. Accepting of all dialects of French. Cons: For a paper, the syllabus said to do 450-500 words but elsewhere it said 550-600 words. I wrote 497 words and didn't realize til after. I emailed her and explained what happened but she docked me anyways like what the heck.

Dr. Phenix is a great french professor for returning missionaries. She is extremely knowledgeable and gives great feedback on the writing assignments. Don't buy the readings or the textbook, huge waste of money. She is also a really great person so that makes the class easier feeling like you are learning from a friend.

This class was so chill. If you take FREN 321 from anyone else, it'll actually be hard. I honestly stopped reading the book because she was way better at explaining grammar rules than it was. I put minimal effort into this class and got an A really easily. Just pay attention in class and do the hw and you'll be fine. Your french will improve a lot.
Dr. Phenix is AMAZING. One of my favorite professors ever. I highly recommend taking her class, she cares so much about her students and is SO fun.

It was a Good class but might have been different because of COVID but lectures we kind of pointless. Lots of writing in the class which is challenging but Madame Phenix is always willing to help and gives good feedback.

I adore Dr. Phenix. She cares greatly for her students and is always willing to help during the writing process. There was a lot of reading, but honestly some of it could be skimmed. The reading quizzes weren't worth much anyways. I highly recommend her and this class.

Dr Phenix is incredible. I hate history classes usually, but she made French history soo interesting. She is hilarious as well. A TON of reading for the class with reading quizzes in class most days, but she does it so that the discussions can be amazing. The test is a lot of writing and there is a 10 page paper at the end, but she helps so much :)

There's a lot I admire about Dr. Phenix. Her compassion for her students and her passion for her subject are at the top of the list. While the concept of studying largely from primary sources is great for authenticity, it's less great for college students doing a number of other demanding classes. FYI, she will catch your every grammatical mistake.

If you plan on taking French 321, take it from Dr. Phenix. She is amazing, and although French 321 is a hard class, she makes it very doable. She constantly offers to meet with students outside of class and is willing to help out in any way she can. Take it from her! You won't regret it!

SO. MUCH. READING. She uses primary sources, which is really cool, but also takes so long, and she quizzes you on it. She is so flexible and will help you if you have concerns. She def cares about her students but, if you like structure, this isn't the class for you.

I loved sister Myers! She was just a genuinely sweet human and cared about every student. She showed up every class with a smile and was always willing to meet outside of class for extra help. There were only 3 big papers which I didn't think was too much and she is a very nice grader! I would totally recommend this class-great option for a GE.

Prof Myers is the sweetest but pretty disorganized, class was cancelled more than it was held. The class discussions and weekly homework are not relevant to the big assignments done throughout the semester and you don't get much feedback on our papers. That was fine for me, but if you need more guidance with writing this is not the class for you.

I love her! She is very understanding if you need an extension and is totally willing to give you feedback on your writing. We didn't have class on Fridays. It was a personal writing day. There are a lot of little reflection assignments where you just say how your writing went that day, so it's easy to keep your grade up.

Sarah is a great teacher. She cares most that you learn and provides leeway for each of her students to do the most they can. We had a textbook but we really only used it once. She is truly one of the sweetest people you will ever meet.
