I hate science but he made me laugh every lecture. I wish I didn't have to earn a grade in that class because I didn't do so well because it's a hard class. But I do recommend this teacher
Bruce is the coolest guy ever. hilarious, amazing, probably the best science teacher i have ever had. i hate science (even after taking his class) but he makes it funny and worthwhile.

Class set up well. Ta's are cool and helpfull. assignments are easy and done in lab. EZ points. Daily quizzes are easy too. FUN. Prof is funny and cool. tests are short. Book practice quizzes have lots of errors, but they have it online to practice which is helpful at times. To get an A thru B- take this class from him.

bergeson is great but the class sucks. what he goes over in class has nothing to do with the tests. the tests are tricky and require to be able to apply information to weird questions. go to the ta test reviews and they help with the tests a lot. bergeson makes the class as interesting as it can be.

He is such a funny man and really knows the subject well. He has lots of really fun experiments and is always cracking jokes. He makes the subject seem less dull and really follows closely with the textbook. The tests are from the textbook and take good notes on his slideshows and go to the TA review sessions for the tests they are really helpful
Very engaging and light-hearted discussions. Tries to keep the heavy material light. Hilarious! Lot's of cool in-class experiments.

Hilarious teacher! He entertains you, but also explains the concepts very clearly. I loved him. Also, he is very helpful if you go to him about valid concerns with the test. You have to take Physical Science from Bro. Bergeson!

This guy is the only reason I made it through PS100.  Seriously, I looked forward to going to lecture every day - attendance wasn't required but I wouldn't miss it for the world.  He made potentially monotonous subjects riveting.  Simply hilarious too - absolutely love him.
Good class. Nice ratio of serious and fun stuff. Tests make sense. And the atmosphere in class and labs does not make you stressed out.

He is awesome!  I always thought it would be hard to stay awake during science lectures, but he is hilarious so it was easy!  I loved how he explained everything and tried to bring experiments in whenever he could.
I hate science and was dreading this class, but I love going to it now! He loves the subject and gets totally excited about it, it's awesome! Also very entertaining!

Great teacher!  Science can be boring if you don't have someone make it fun.  Prof. Bergeson did just that: his lectures, the demonstrations, and the jokes make class truly enjoyable.  He takes hard material and does his best to help you understand. Don't rely on TAs: they are inadequately prepared.

He's a great teacher--very entertaining! His lectures are fun and helpful. Make sure you keep up on the reading to get the most out of class. The class isn't too bad if you have taken physics and chemistry in highschool. He does a ok job of explaining, but TA's are a big help if you are confused.
His lectures are quite animated so he is easy to listen to.  His sarcasm bothers some, but I was fine with it.  He is average at explaining concepts.
this guy is great!  for one thing, he looks like freaking steve kerr...but honestly, he knows his stuff and i've never seen anyone have so much fun teaching a class.  what a hoot!

Bruce is the best!  I guess if you're not scientifically minded, he might not be the best, but he makes class way fun!  He's very passionate about his objects lessons and blows stuff up.  Come on, that's cool.  I looked forward to lectures every day.

A nice guy with a lot of sarcasm.  Don't ask a question in class because he'll make you look dumb.  Very helpful and friendly if you call him at home, almost like he's a different person.  The tests were dumb.  Only a nerd could get an A.
Only answers to the name Bruce and calls everyone in the class Bruce.  Always starts class with a joke.  Funniest teacher I've had.  OK teacher.

Bergeson is clearly doing time in this class.  Humorous and good with object lessons, but can't seem to answer a lecture question with anything other than sarcasm.  Expect to rely heavily on lab T.A.s to clarify concepts.

If he could clearly explain concepts to the non-scientifically minded (everyone who takes Phy S 100) as well as he could tell jokes, then he'd be much better. First I was confused, then disinterested, then asleep, then absent. He tries his best though.
He's hilariously enlightening
No Comments
Obnoxious!

I think Professor Bradford is a really good option for American Heritage. Just study the write up's he gives you really hard and you'll be fine on the exams and essays. The write up's have all of the information that will be tested on so the textbook and lectures don't really matter. Lecture's are boring but he did the napoleon dynamite dance once.

It's test heavy and there are mini essays every week but the criteria is very clear so if you follow it you'll be fine. He tends to ramble or spend more time on a subject before moving on. Because of that we were behind schedule since the beginning of the semester. He provides writeups you can study before class so you know what he'll talk about.

His organizational skills are bad. He has quizzes due at really weird times of the morning, doesn't go over assignments before they are due, and his writing assignments ask for the impossible as far as being able to answer all his questions in the limited amount of word space he gives you. He is not aware at all of the needs of students.

He's one of the best professors at BYU. His lectures were very clear. Final can be pretty tough, but as long as you study your notes, handouts, and homework problemsets, you will be totally fine. I also loved speaking to him in Japanese!

Dr. Braithwaite's lectures were really interesting. This was for HONRS, but I felt like he really cared about students. However, I felt like his grading was a bit unfair as he had really high expectations on more creative assignments, such as the final project. Overall, I really enjoyed him as a professor and would even take another class from him.

Dr. Braithwaite is awesome! He is incredibly engaging and you can tell he cares deeply about the subject matter and his students. The course seems intimidating at first but it is definitely manageable. Tests count for a lot of your grade and the rest is group project grades and weekly quizzes. Not an easy A, but definitely worth the work.

The class was organized very well. We had lab on Tuesdays to work on the group research study and lecture on Thursdays. He talks pretty fast and covers a lot of content in the lecture so don't worry about writing everything down. Professor Braithwaite has high love and high expectations and he wants to help his students prepare for grad school.

We met once a week for lecture and lab to work on the group project, which is what you'll be doing the whole semester. He would always go over time during lecture, but for lab, my group would usually be able to leave early because we would split up tasks to get things done quickly. Tests are worth a lot and hard, so definitely use the study guides.

Scott's great, I'd love to be his friend but his class was not my style. Way too heavy of a workload, and I get he wants to "prepare us for grad school" but that's not everyone's path. I get the idea of wanting to challenge us but at the same time, we have 5 other classes. Most likely a department issue, but hopefully they can make adjustments.

One of my favorite professors. He is committed to making sure you learn, and also preparing you for the future. He is very open-minded and conscientious. The TAs were pretty on top of it too. I took this in the evening, but he worked hard to make lecture engaging and get us out a little early. Lab was short too so it was almost never 3 hours.

Professor Braithwaite is nice but his class is unnecessarily hard. For someone who teaches how to make tests, he had plenty of ambiguous questions littered throughout his tests and quizzes. One of the toughest classes I've taken at BYU but it shouldn't be. Most of us aren't planning on writing tests our entire career. Made me lose my scholarship...
This was the best class I took at BYU so far. It's what I was hoping for when I declared the major. I don't even like the topic, but his teaching made it good.

This guy is the definition of sarcasm. He can be funny at times, but quite honestly his sense of humor was a bit obnoxious. I don't think he's a bad teacher or anything, just not my cup of tea. This class was hard, but welcome to BYU I guess... (I should've gone to UVU)

Prof Braithwaite is a good professor. For a relatively uninteresting class he made lectures enjoyable. His tests are really hard, which makes sense because its literally a class about writing good tests. Unfortunately there's no way around this class because its required, but I'm confident Braithwaite is the best one to take it from.

I took this class on Thursdays from 4-7 pm--this made for long classes but Dr. Braithwaite did such a good job at keeping us entertained. The exams were hard but manageable. TAs were amazing and super helpful throughout the semester. There is a group project that you work on throughout the semester and weekly reading quizzes.
He's hilarious and smart. The class is super organized and stretches you. Best class I took in the major!

I took this class on thursdays from 4-7pm which was nice, but also sucked because lectures were very long and full of important material, but because we had to cover so much, we went through everything really quickly and then had to go to lab for an hour (6-7pm) which allowed us to get help. Tests are hard. Semester long group project

He is kind of a punky guy, but he genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to be happy, successful, and understand the content. It isn't a difficult class if you show up, pay attention, and do the work. It could be a terrifyingly difficult class but he does a great job of giving everyone the chance to do well.

Professor Braithwaite is a great teacher, but Psychometrics is somewhat difficult. The tests are tricky, but he gives good study guides. If you put in the time (several hours) and effort to prepare for tests, you can succeed.
I loved this class. It's one of the few I will remember from my time at BYU.
What a boss. I want to be like him.

there are 2 midterms and you 'design' a test in this class. The write up is simple, but make sure to show each section to the TA's before you turn it in. If you have a good group, this class will be a breeze.
Such a good teacher, I wish he taught more classes. I never thought I would be inspired by a class about testing, but this class changed me for the better.

I took this in the spring and it was great. He comes off as kind of conceited at first, but he knows his stuff, he's funny, and his lectures are interesting. There is a semester-long group project, but it's possible to get most of it done during lab. He makes it sound like his exams are way hard but they really aren't that bad.
I loved this class, and I definitely didn't think I would.
Best professor at BYU. Take this class from him!

His lectures are incredible and he motivates you to learn. That said, this class is REALLY hard--he believes that most BYU classes are too easy. The tests are definitely the hardest I've ever taken. The weekly quizzes are closed book and demand a lot of careful reading of pretty boring material.

Put this class off for as long as I could, to be honest, would have rather stapled my right ear to the wall than take a "testing" class, but I sure lucked out. Braithwaite is not only a fantastic teacher, but he made this class enjoyable. I am actually going to legitimately miss coming to lectures. Makes things easily understandable. Tests are fair
Don't let the haters scare you off, this is one of the best classes is the department if you take it from him. Changed my whole opinion of the major.
Best class in all four years at BYU.

I felt like he was trying to do more than so many of my professors. He taught about testing but actually tried to connect with us and give real advice about how to succeed in the field. Most important class I took.

Funny and charismatic, but SO conceited! The whole first class we just had to ask questions about his life. I spent hours reading and studying for the 7 min. quizzes only to find that some of the questions aren't even in the textbook! Group project is led by a TA not well explained. Tests are made to trick you, and are only based on lectures.
One of the most important classes in shaping my thinking about Psychology and pretty much everything.

Great professor who makes a really boring subject somewhat interesting. You can tell he knows his stuff, and I looked forward to his lectures. The group project is the easiest I've ever done, and you get almost all of your homework done in lab. The tests are lecture-heavy, so go to class and take notes. Average class, but great professor.

I was not looking forward to this class, but it was so good. I actually kind of care about science and how it informs psychology. I hadn't thought about that at all before. He oversells how hard the class will be, but makes all your effort worth it. He puts a ton of time into making his lectures good. I loved this class!
Best class I took at BYU

He is pretty arrogant, honestly. He thinks that his class will be this life-changing class that you have to work incredibly hard for, but it's pretty standard. He's not a bad professor, and the class itself wasn't too hard. The expectations are straight forward and if you follow guidelines, you'll do fine!

I feel like this is one of the few classes in the major that really stretched me, in a good way. He's trying to do more than just get a bunch of people through the material. One of the best teachers I've ever had.
Braithwaite is a great man and a scholar to boot. Awesome and helpful TAs also! Made this class actually enjoyable.

Well structured class. Picked good TAs. Very clear on what he wants from you. Very easy paper that you do all semester in groups. Tests are very doable if you follow his slides. Tries to be funny too hard tho.

This class is relatively easy. Have the study guides open during lecture and fill it as he goes through his Prezi. He is super funny which makes this dull topic entertaining. I wouldnt have wanted to take 309 from anyone else.

Although this is one of those "core classes" that you dread in psychology, this easily ended up being one of my favorites of the year. Dr. Braithwaite is the BEST. His lectures are engaging and he really knows how to help you learn. The homework load is really manageable, because you can do most of it in lab.

Easily the best professor on campus. Every class should be taught by him and every test should be written by him. Always always always take a class from Scott Braithwaite if you have the option. If you study, you can do well. He writes the most fair tests I've ever taken and his lectures are hilarious. This was my favorite class at BYU.
I have no idea how he made us laugh so much when hes talking about psychological testing. This was probably the best class I took at BYU.
I wish he taught every class in the major!

Dr. Braithwaite is hilarious and so smart. I thought I was going to hate a class just on testing, but it ended up being one of my favorite classes in my whole college experience. The class involved a long group project that we had to pick the first day, so be careful about who you choose to be in your group.
Best experience I had during my time at BYU.
I was not looking forward to taking this class.  He not only made it tolerable, but actually made it really fun and interesting.  I miss not being in school because of classes like this.
Such an unexpectedly good class.  He is what makes the difference. One of the highlights of my time at BYU.

Wow. He is amazing. He tries to scare away students on the first day who don't want to work hard. Stay in the class. It is manageable and his style of teaching is some of the best I have ever seen. Study well for his tests. Go the reviews! AMAZING. Made a potentially boring class really really worthwhile.
This was kind of experience I hoped to have in college classes.  Interesting, challenging, and helped me get better insight about what I want to do in Psychology.

He's a fantastic, knows what he'steaching,cares about the students. Lectures are funny and teaches the material really well. Tests are very challenging BUT Everything you need to know on the test is on the study guide - use it and you'll ace the tests. Take Psych 309 from Scott Braithwaite!!

Braithwaite knows what he is doing. He is a great test maker and so the tests are a good measure of your knowledge. However, this usually means either you know it or you don't. Study guides are given. Majority of the class is a semester long group paper- unavoidable for the class. I would take it from him. Decompression videos are hilarious.
One of the best experiences I've had at BYU even though the material is dry. He more than makes up for it with his teaching skills.

Dr. Braithwaite is my all-time favorite prof. He makes me miss not being in school. Hilarious guy, super interesting lectures, and killer (& realistic) lifecareer advice. There are quizzes on the reading, not too bad though. The group project is time consuming but almost all of it is in-class, which was so nice. Loved him, the class, and the TA's!
Definitely one of my favorite professors!
Material is dry but he somehow makes it funny and interesting. He's the best professor to take this class from.  I wish he taught more classes so I could take those from him too.
I was so surprised how good this class was.  Not an easy class, but so worth it! He cares about students and wants them to do well.

Who knew that I could be so inspired by a class about Testing and Measurement.  I learned so much about how to be good at my profession and how to develop my abilities in life in general.  Life changing class.

Im a psych major and Scott is definitely the most capable and competent professor I have had. Not the easiest, and he can sometimes be full of himself, but for good reason. Work hard and you will get an A. Study guides are almost word-for-word like the test so KNOW THEM and go to reviews. I learned so much about psychology, take it from him!
I'd take it from him
I took this graduate class as an undergrad, and yes, it was hard.  That said, I learned A TON, and love stats now because of him.  He goes out of his way to help students succeed.

Braithewait is hard, and he tells you that he is. Lectures for the most part are fun and easy to listen to, he has a great sense of humor. He warns you and says that Quizzes will be on whatever day he wants, but they will be on the scheduled day. Read the book, go to class and you will be fine.

Dr Braithwaite will tell you, he's not the easiest one to take this from (he doesn't want to be, he wants you to actually learn stuff), but he's SO great. He makes pretty boring material way more interesting, and tests are straightforward. Read the book to do well on quizzes
Best professor at BYU, hands down.

This is such a difficult and potentially boring subject, and Brother Braithwaite is the only person I know that made it actually fun to learn. His class lectures were funny and easy to follow. He really has  a passion for his subject and is absolutely hilarious to listen to. He is the hardest 301 teacher, but definitely take the class from him.
Great teacher. Makes an intense subject interesting and fun. Reading is a bore and labs really make you stretch. Prob the best teacher to take if you really want to learn the material.

I thought this class would be super boring, but he actually makes it really interesting.  He's tough and expects you to know what you are talking about but the tests are super straight forward and easy if you use the study guide.  The lab assignments are hard, but it is that way with any 304 class.  I'd definitely recommend him for this class.

SUCH a great class. Not only is he super brilliant and helpful, he's SO entertaining and goes over things like 50 times with you. Extremely personable; tries hard to make it a positive experience for everyone. It's hard, but that's because it's statistics, duh.

Dr. Braithwaite is a fantastic teacher! This is not an easy class--he tells his students on the first day that he is the hardest 301 teacher, and it's true. But you learn so much from him and he really wants his students to succeed, so he's willing to give you a lot of extra help. He'll give you great grad school advice, too!

Take the time to really go through Dr. Burt's exam review videos. Some of the content is directly from them and not in the mastering chemistry homework. Also take advantage of the TA reviews or any practice questions they offer (often very similar to exam questions). This class really isn't bad at all and Dr. Burt is really nice.

I was very nervous about taking this course but I am so grateful for Professor Burt. He truly cares about the students and wants everyone to succeed. If you actually put in effort and study for the exams, you will do well.

He's passionate about chem and goes beyond the facts by explaining the why. Your TA heavily influences how prepared you are for exams. Grading is test-heavy with fill-in-the-blank, so you must know your stuff. Read before class, know unit conversions and algebra. No prior chem experience—challenging but I loved this class.

I did great on the homework, I read and reread the textbook, but when it came to anything Professor Burt made (the exams and quizzes) I always did poorly. It was frustrating to work hard and never feel like it was up to par with what was on the exams. You really have to have a helpful TA or I don't know how you'd get through this class!

Professor Burt is a knowledgeable and accommodating professor. However, his lectures are extremely confusing and go way too far in depth for an intro chem class. Also, the homework is super easy and then the exams are really difficult, so it honestly feels like you're getting tricked. I would recommend taking this class from a different professor
So many tests. He tends to ramble during lectures and not get through all the material. Homework is weighted a lot. His lectures weren't easy for me to follow. You NEED a good TA to get a good grade.

This class was way harder than it need to be. I still don't understand why we had to take so many exams... 5 for the entire term! 

Class structure aside, there were a lot of technical issues. We had multiple instances where the study guide and practice exam covered the wrong topics. Even the Exams covered questions from the wrong unit!

This class is tough! But it's a college chem class so what do you expect. But Prof Burt is awesome! His lectures were always engaging and enjoyable. I enjoyed attending class. Lots of HW and lots of study but you'll be fine if you put in the effort.

Dr. Burt is a great professor. Records all lectures so you do not need to attend in-person. Dr. Burt will grant extensions on homework and excuse absences, very flexible and understanding! He does cool demos in class to keep the class engaged. Attend intersessions held by TAs, they will help you on exams. Shoutout to TA Shelby, he's the best!

Professor Burt was actually my favorite! He is very accommodating. The tests were not difficult if you went to the TA lab and did the homework. They were also online instead of the testing center which was super nice. He always had a different bow tie on and there were always such cool demos in class. Highly recommend taking this class from him!

I really liked Dr. Burt's lectures! He had lots of demos that were super fun to watch! There was a lot of homework and the program was hard to work sometimes. Test's were so hard and I didn't use the TA's enough so that didn't help me. So I would take this class again but I would change my own study habits. Good class and professor!

Dr. Burt is one of the most flexible professors I've had. You can watch the lectures online from home or in person and get full attendance points. There is a lot of homework, much of which is tedious. Ultimately, the class is set up for you to succeed.
I really liked him his lectures are fun. Lots of homework but it is really helpful and prepares you for the test. GO to your recitation it will be helpful.

On the first day of class, Prof Burt walked in with a bowtie. Really great and funny, and gives lots of demos. The tests were a bit difficult and there was a lot of homework, but I ended up really enjoying the class. TA's were great and accessible outside of class. A lot of scores are also dropped, and you can miss a few lectures. Highly recommend.

This man is my favorite science professor that I have had at BYU. Gen Chem is obviously hard but his learning suite is extremely organized, his tests are based off of exactly what the TA review goes over, and he makes the class fun (lots of demos). Definitely would recommend doing the textbook reading before class, I think thats where I went wrong.

Dr. Burt explained difficult concepts well, but this is chemistry! He recorded lectures, posted slides, and included many demonstrations. I don't know if he'll change his tests, but study groups outside recitation would've helped me so much! I hated the smartworks and getting penalized for each attempt.

Dr. Burt is the best science professor I've had at BYU. If you are a visual learner, take it from him. He uses slides and is very fair. Using Chegg will help you in this class lol, bc the class hw is on Smartworks. All of his tests this semester were online which was very convenient

Dr. Burt is an NMR wizard, and he organizes the lecture portion of 455 in an incredibly effective way. He gives you the tools you need for homework, which prepares you well for exams. Collaboration with other students is encouraged. His lectures feel a bit rushed at times, but he's eager to chat about NMR outside of class you ever have questions.

Dr. Burt is awesome. The class was hard, but it was also taken during the spring semester so everything was condensed. His lectures are engaging and he is fun! His interest and engagement during the lecture make it exciting. Tests are hard but if you do the practice tests and review with TAs you will be ok! Good luck!!

Dr. Burt is a great guy and obviously wants the best for his students. His lectures seemed a little rushed though and I ended up having to teach myself most of the content. He is very educated and knows his stuff but teaching it is a little bit harder to follow. Great guy though!

Dr. Burt has been by far one of my favorite professors at BYU. He truly want his students to succeed and if you reach out to him he is more than willing to find ways to help you do well in the class. There is a lot of homework but it helps you know the concepts better for tests. I have learned a lot and definitely recommend taking his class!!

Professor Burt is an amazing professor. The class was tough with lots of homework but that is any Chem 105 class. Professor Burt was passionate about chem but he always stayed on topic during class and only talked about relevant information. He also has a good moral compass and he respects his students. I recommend Burt if you have to take Chem 105

Tests are 70% of the grade and they are super hard. I took this during spring and some days i spent 12 hours straight on this class. The homework felt tedious as most of the concepts were pretty straight forward but it's a lot of work.

Dr. Burt is an excellent professor. He clearly knows his stuff, but more importantly, he can explain it in an easy to understand way. He also makes it clear what will be on the test and what you will not need to know (until higher level classes). His lectures are amazing. 10/10 would recommend.

Dr. Burt is one of my favorite chem professors. If you are deciding between him and Macedonia, take him! He is very clear on what concepts will be on the test, takes the time in class to explain concepts, gives extra credit opportunities as well. Chem 106 is like any other chemistry class you have to work for you grade but he is a great teacher!

Dr. Burt is super smart, and you can tell he wishes he could go more in depth in this class. He's really good at answering questions and preparing you for the weekly homework. He is also accessible outside of class and helpful with lab reports or assignments. Would take again.

Hes more worried about getting through lecture than to explain things clearly/answer questions. Ask for help and hell basically tell you to do mastering chemistry, as if we arent already. Concepts arent crazy difficult but you pretty much have to teach yourself. Lectures mandatory but a waste of time. He does drop 1 of your 2 first midterms

I found Dr. Burt's class to be extremely difficult for a basic level chemistry course. Dr. Burt's lectures were rushed and confusing and his explanations weren't much help. The tests are really hard and sometimes there are questions on them that we barely covered in class.

Dr Burt is really good at teaching basic chemistry to all levels and making sure everyone is on the same page and understanding the material. The online homework is sometimes tedious, but it's manageable. I highly recommend this class for the general chem credit, especially if you took high school chemistry.

Great teacher. We had 6 midterms and 1 final , but they were all pretty fair. Personally, I really liked having an exam every other week or so. It kept me on top of the material and each test covered less material than your typical 3 /4 midterm and 1 final chem class which helped me have more time to understand each concept a little more in depth.

Don't take Burts class. Very bad idea. Take it from Macedone. When I talked to students in Macedone they seemed to hate life a lot less than I did. Burt doesn't explain things well and thinks we know a lot more than we do. I did okay in Chem 105 and thought it would be about the same... wrong. I did significantly worse in this class. 0/10

If you can, take 106 from someone else. For some reason, the homework for Burt seemed longer and harder than the homework from other professors. 6 midterms and a final. My one issue with his tests is that on the midterms there is a 2 hour time limit and the final there is a 3 (its 3x longer than the midterms). Its ridiculous.

Professor Burt is a genius. Sometimes a little too smart for this class but he tries his best to dumb it down so we can understand. He is fast paced and expects you to stay up to date so don't get behind. Overall, he is a solid teacher but with some quirks. Put in the effort and you will do fine.

Dr. Burt is a great teacher. Not only is he good at what he does, he makes it fun to learn. He's super passionate about chemistry. The class is a little harder if you don't understand the math, but if you work hard and do the homework, you should do fine.

The guy is a genius. I took it during the summer so it was a little faster than usual, but definitely doable. You definitely work for your grade but Dr. Burt is very fair and has even offered plenty of extra credit. He is really good at explaining hard concepts, but you do have to study to really understand the concept on your own. I give him an A.

Dr. Burt is great. He loves chemistry, and makes sure that you understand the WHY behind all the equations and concepts. I took the class during summer term so things moved laser-fast. The class is definitely hard, ESPECIALLY if you struggle with math. However it is very doable if you work hard; he's been my favorite chemistry teacher so far.

Professor Burt does a great job of preparing you for his tests, his in class reviews are very helpful. The online homework was extremely long and heavy at the beginning of the semester, but towards the end the number of problems got shorter. If you put the work in you will do well in this class.

This class was really hard for me, but chemistry isn't my thing. Professor Burt is a nice guy, and his lectures clear, but he moves really fast and doesn't always go in-depth enough for me, I had to do a lot of catching up outside of class. You'll work your butt off for this class, and I wouldn't recommend skipping. Be prepared.

Knows his stuff, not always super clear when he teaches tho. Often he would run out of class time and not get through all the material and expected you to learn it on your own or go to his office. There is always homework after each class period. Doable class if you study and keep up on the Homework

Dr. Burt is almost too smart to teach 106. He has a really hard time explaining things on a basic level so that everyone understands. A lot of time the examples he did in class were completely different that what we saw on the homework. 3 exams are only 20 MC and 7 FR questions so you have to be basically perfect. Nice guy, but very tough class.

Dr. Burt was a great teacher. I did okay in Chem 105 but I felt that Dr. Burt taught 106 really well and I was able to pull off an A. Attend lecture, do all the smartworks (I did them all in a study group), and go to the tutorial lab for questions. Chemistry is generally tough, but I think Dr. Burt made it as easy as it can be. I recommend him!

I love Dr Burt! Slight curve to tests. Participation IClicker quizzes in class. He drops your lowest test score and replaces it with the average of your two higher scores. I bombed the first test and did well on the other two and still got an A. He gives a review before each test and the review slides are EXACTLY the test. Best 106 teacher for sure

Chem 106 is a difficult class if you don't try and put in the effort. If you do the reading, really understand the smart work homework, and study really well for his exams you will do well. If you don't have a good understanding of chem 105, this class will be difficult. The notecard he lets you take into exams is a life saver!!
Terrible teacher, take from someone else. If you ask a question in class expect to hear, "come talk to me in office hours, we need to get through these concepts."

This was a really tough class, but I think it would've been that way no matter what professor I had. Reading assignments and homework for each class, with 4 tests and a final (lowest score is dropped), and you can use a 3x5 card. This class involves lots of math; I needed extra help to pass. Having a good understanding of 105 is critical as well.

Dr. Burt is a good teacher. Chem 106 will be hard no matter who you take it from. I found his lectures to be extremely boring, but with that said I find chemistry to be extremely boring. I thought he was very fair and went out of his way to help students. Good choice for any chemistry.

Professor Burt was great. It is a chemistry class. It is going to be a lot of work. But his lectures and personality made the time go by fast. He made sure that we understood concepts before moving on, and I felt completely prepared for his tests and final. It's a lot of work, as all chemistry classes are, but I would definitely take him again.

I took him during summer term, which means covering a lot more material than normal. I had to spend quite a bit of time a week doing homework, reading and prepping for tests for his class, but his lectures and humor were fantastic. I always loved going to class. Apart from the tests, everything was practically participation. Would take him again.

Burt is a likeable guy, but be warned: Chemistry is not for the faint of heart.  You have to put in effort.. A lot of effort.  The 3 tests (drops one and averages the other two) and final were out of this world.  He did give a nice curve at the end.  Homework due every Wednesday.  iClicker quizzes everyday in class.

Dr. Burt is probably the most merciful chemistry teacher at BYU. He dropped the lowest test score, let us use a 3 x 5 note card on all of our tests and he curved the tests and even the final. His lectures were not necessarily amazing but they were good. He gave us many opportunities to succeed. HOWEVER, Chem 105 is not easy from any teacher.

Alright is essential vocabulary in his class. If you've already graduated from college chemistry or are Einstein then you might as well start praying now, because this class is for people who are that smart and have no social life. passing with an a, pfffffff, you have a better chance of finding gold.

For Chem105, he drops your lowest midterm and averages the other two, so that was very nice. The tests are RIDICULOUSLY hard, but all of the Chem teachers have similar tests, so you can't avoid it. He is a great person who loves what he teaches! Take from him (if you HAVE to take chem)!

Okay, so the class sucked. BUT, Scott Burt is the most wonderful teacher I've ever had. He has this little chuckle he does that just makes my day every time I hear it. He is a really nice guy, and you can tell he genuinely has a passion for what he is teaching which really affects this course. TAKE FROM HIM. HE IS GLORIOUS.

Professor Burt is a great guy and a good professor, the only down side is the class he teaches. I enjoyed going to class to see him blow stuff up, but if you are going to take this class, get ready because it is going to be one of the hardest things you have ever done in your life.

Prof.  Burt is one of the quirkier professors at BYU. He's very excited about chemistry and he loves the material he teaches. He's pretty flexible with grading. However, this class lives up to its reputation, it's not for the faint of heart and if you're not motivated you will struggle, no matter the professor you take it from.

Dr. Burt is one of the quirky professors here, so that makes the class fun.  Stay on your toes though, as he is also one of the tricky ones as well.  Be sure to read the exams Q's very carefully, and get a good mental concept for a principle, rather than working out specific problems when studying.  Talk things out with people, that helped me a ton
Took this class my first semester at BYU and it was horrible. His tests are ridiculously hard, I mean seriously, this is Chem 101! Don't take from his if at all possible.

Professor Burt is an awesome teacher. His lectures are very clear and he clearing explains problems as he goes through them step by step. Tests aren't too bad and he is fair and will drop questions that everyone misses. Tests follow the homework so as long as you stay up to date on the homework you will be fine.

Unless you are a chemistry genius or you have 20 hours a week to study for this class, this class is extremely difficult. He writes the tests expecting the average to be around 70%. The tests are impossible. The average on the second test was 50%! I know that chemistry classes are hard, but I guarantee you can find an easier one than Dr. Burt.

Nice guy, very clear and easy to listen to. This was his very first time teaching 106, so he did pretty well if you take that fact into account. Exams are super easy, homework is long. Make sure you go to class and ask a lot of questions. Get a good TA!

Dr. Burt is awesome and totally helpful. He is passionate about what he does, fun to impersonate and funny (intentionally and unintentionally). His lectures can be a little confusing at times but he is more than willing to help you. If you read the book and do the homework you will get an A. I would take this class again

I highly recommend studying the material before class and getting a head start on mastering chemistry homework. He is very approachable and wants to help people succeed. His free response questions were pretty hard overall his tests were easy. I would take from him again

one of the worst professors i've had in my whole life. the average on his second test was 32% for the free response, and he laughed about it during class. He curves his grades but it doesn't quite help, you have to depend on yourself and understand everything by your own.

Dr. Burt is as good as you're gonna get for Chem 105. I took the class during summer term and didn't fell like it was too overwhelming. However, if your not willing to hunker down with the text book and work extra practice problems don't expect to do well.

Nice guy, no doubt. A little quirky and likes to blow up balloons. His tests are hard, tells you that you need to know everything we've covered. Not clear explanations. If it wasn't for his TA, I would have had no hope. Try to find someone else, but if you can't, be prepared to work hard. Then again, maybe it's because I took it over the summer.
I took the class during summer and managed to do well. Nonetheless, It is all up to you to get the grade. He provides opportunities to learn and improve the grade. Don't rely on his teaching though.

This class was ridiculously hard for a 101 class. I took 2 years of chem in high school but wanted a refresher in college before 105. Even with my previous knowledge and continuing to study, the tests were over the top hard. The rest of the class is fairly easy, but the tests make up such a large percent that it is extremely difficult to suceed.

He is a very funny, and nice, but his lectures are pointless. I had to teach my self out of the book. The labs are very easy, and the homework is not that difficult, but his exams are HORRIBLE!!!! Hard class!

Professor Burt is great. Chemistry is a tough subject, but he's always willing to help you out. TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OFFICE HOURS! He's way helpful and friendly if you go to him for help. Tests are difficult but doable and it's possible to score well if you're willing to study. If you take the homework and labs seriously they'll boost your grade.

Chemistry is difficult. He writes the tests to be much harder than the standardized chemistry final. Weekly labs, but they are easy and you can drop two. His lectures can be confusing, but he has office hours. He is so helpful during office hours. If you take advantage of that time, I encourage taking from him. Class average is around a 75%

He's a nice, nerdy guy who really does care about teaching--he always says he loves to have people ask him questions in office hours. However, his expectation is that most people will get C's, and he curves things that way. The tests are a lot harder than the homework. If you want to do well, be a chem genius or put in a LOT of time.
Worst teacher I have ever had. Class is useless and tests do not represent what is In the book. Choose a different teacher!

I took this class my first semester in college and it stinks. Try to not take this class at all, and if you must take this class avoid taking this teacher. He expects you to put 15+ HOURS for his class alone in order to get an A -_- and he also  makes his test so that the avg grade is a 70-75. AVOID IT! worst class of my semester.

Brother Scott is a good guy and teaches well. He loves to make things explode and i love listening to him say "mass". hilarious. BUT BE CAREFUL. you may think you know chemistry but the tests are killer for some reason. especially the final. other than that the class is cake.

Class was ridiculous. He was all over the place and made tons of errors while teaching and on exams. However, I took the class during spring term so it was super fast paced and this was his first time teaching the class. I would take someone else if possible.

I regret taking this class. Professor Burt expected us to come to class with the concepts already mastered. He was unclear about his expectations on quizzes and skimmed over the material. He clearly enjoys chemistry but does not lecture effectively. The TA was not helpful either.

This was a good class but it did require lots of work.  As long as you stay on top of each section you will do fine.  Professor Burt is very nice and tries really hard to cover all the material.  The class consists of exams, a final, iclicker quizes, and labs.  If you just do your work you will do fine!  And Prof. Burt is a great teacher.

Easy - as an introductory class should be. Dr. Burt is a friendly guy who wants to get to know you and makes himself readily available to answer any questions or concerns you might have. I highly recommend this professor.

This class was extremely boring but not all that hard. There was a ton of busy work and you have to attend the lectures, but the tests were similar to the homework. The final is given by the American Chemical Society and isn't like anything we'd ever done before. Plus you have only 55 minutes to do 60 questions. It stinks.

He's really one-track minded.  If you don't understand what he's talking about, stop him and ask questions.  He's very helpful, but his TA's are sometimes hard to understand.  He offers tons of help, but it's not always the easiest way to understand.  I learned best by reading the book.

Such a nice and funny guy, but he has no idea how to teach chem. He got most of the inclass questions wrong-and has iClicker quizzes everyday that you have to attend class for. I had to teach myself the material because he doesn't explain it well and mastering chemistry is a joke. Hard tests/hard labs-especially for those who have never taken chem.

Dr. Burt is a wonderful chemistry teacher. 101 is essentially high school chemistry. I think people who say he's bad just have a tough time learning chemistry b/c their strengths are elsewhere.  He'll help you on any occasion, I emailed him all the time. Stay on top of your work, go to class for i-clicker points, do the labs. It's totally doable

He is a great person and seemed to genuinely care about the students. His lectures were dumb, I didn't learn a thing. I taught myself the course. You have to go to class only for the i-clickers which are dumb. The exams are impossible and are not close to what you do on the homework. He expects way too much on the exams. Skip chem 101 if possible!!

Took him Fall 2008. Nice, but only taught the basics in class, and expected you to know much more advanced material for the exams. Labs were too difficult-- basically had the TA tell you what to write-- and not helpful. I would not recommend him!
His tests were IMPOSSIBLE! He was a great guy and was very likeable but he gave homework on the weekends and had very difficult and timewasting labs every week. His final was ridiculously hard.

He is a nice guy, and really smart, but the class was really pathetic. I pretty much taught myself the material, but still had to go to class for the iclicker quizzes. I kept getting marked off on stupid things that shouldn't matter. The tests seemed easy but then everyone does terrible and he doesn't curve it well. This class was a bad experience

Such a nice guy. VERY willing to help and wants you to learn. But he is a RESEARCHER, not a PROFESSOR. His tests at first were easy. But  mid semester, things got so so hard. I spent hours studying, going to all the reviews,go talk to him, and still get a D on the tests. THey were impossible-I did everything I could. TONS of homework all year.

He is very good at explaining things, but his tests got ridiculously hard as the semester went on. The work load was horrible and even though I did okay on the tests I got marked down random points from labs, iclicker quizzes, and online assignments.  The assignments took about an hour and there were 4 due each week, even over thanksgiving break!

Professor Burt is the best! He is so enthusiastic and just an overall great guy. He loves what he teaches and he brings that message across to his students. If you want a professor who is into demo labs and awesome ties, then he is the man for you!

Prof. Burt is an amazing professor!  He really knows his stuff and loves his job.  He is alays willing to help if you need it.  He does give points for days you are their but his class is enjoyable so it is easy to go.
He is a total chemistry nerd but expains it in simple terms. I enjoyed his class and found him very eager to help students. I would recommend this professor.
best teacher ever!  make sure you get him!  he is hilarious, LOVES his job, does a fabulous job teaching and is just an all around great person to learn from!

He is like an amazing professor! We always do crazy demos involving him catching stuff on fire or blowing stuff up! He really enjoys his job and you can tell. Plus he has a very good sense of humor. He is very easy to approach and truly cares that you learn in his class. I really did enjoy his class.
Professor Church is awesome! Each class started out with talking about current pop culture moments in the media. Tests are not hard if you study. He is super caring and his lectures aren't boring.

Dr. Church is a great guy but I would never recommend COMMS302 as an elective. This class was way more academic than it needed to be and the whole course is structured around a semester long group project. He sometimes taught like we were as knowledgeable on the topic as he was. Not terribly hard, just poorly structured in my opinion.

Prof. Church is a stud. The course itself can be a bit dull, but he livens it up. Readings are primarily from a textbook and most homework is doing a reading quiz at home. 2 Group projects. Prof. Church cares about his students, doesn't get nit-picky in the grading system, and usually got us out of class early. Teaches well, discussion based.
He's great.

Honestly, the syllabus terrified me, but Dr. Church is so much nicer in person and in class! He is a strict grader but, in my experience, a kind one! He lays out all the criteria plainly in the rubrics, so if you follow them step by step, you'll do well on all the assignments. The course is changing for the upcoming semesters, but he is awesome!

I honestly did not like Professor Church's class at first because the readings were long and the quizzes were hard for me. But as I figured out the material and listened to his lectures, I grew to love this class! Only write notes on what the agenda asks for, do super well on your writings, use quizlet to study for the tests.

Professor Church is great, but his grading is so tough. That screwed me over a few times. The class is interesting, but there are a few times you'll wonder to yourself, "Is this really an academic discipline?" For example, you'll do readings about laugh tracks. Other than that though, the class got me excited to apply for the program.

The class is based on a final project where you decide what you want to do in the first few weeks and I feel the class "discussions" are ultimately pointless and KILL the momentum you have on the final project. These discussions consist of analyzing methods that most of the time have no bearing on the final project

Make sure that you actually do the reading because he doesn't always go over it in class and you'll need to know some of it. Dr. Church is a funny guy and actually cares about his students. The coursework isn't awful and the assignment criteria are very straightforward. If you're a decent student then you'll do well.

He's awesome. This class was pretty demanding, but I enjoyed it because the things we were talking about in class were so interesting! Do your readings for quizzes (I found it useful to make a quizlet for each one--makes the quizzes a piece of cake). Dr. Church is super supportive and easily accessible outside of class. Take this class from him!

He had really engaging/interesting lectures and cared about the students but the homework he required outside of class was way too hefty. The class only had a few really big assignments that were a lot of work and graded really harshly by the TAs, so you had to do perfectly if you wanted a good grade. His class was way too hard for an intro class.

Make sure you're comfortable with a group final project before signing up. Church gave good lectures. Take notes+ follow his agendas for the readings and you're set for the test/quizzes. Other people said his grading was picky, but I didn't have trouble with that. If you follow the rubric you should be fine. Frequent visits to comms labs on campus.

Dr Church is such a great professor. He teaches Comms 101 really well but also gives insights to all the branches under the school of communications and teaches beyond the classroom. He loves this subject and you can tell. He has great TA's and is always available for questions. He's a fair grader and as long as you try you'll get a good grade.
Dr. Church is hilarious. He is a fun, genuine guy and so understanding and caring. Comms101 was a fun class with easy assignments and a great atmosphere. If you take this class take it from him

Dr. Church is phenomenal. Very passionate about the class material and teaches it in an accessible way. You need to show up to class and do the work, but as long as you're honestly putting in effort it's not a difficult class. You need to have been reading the textbook in order to do well on the test. Definitely take this class from him!

I think Dr. Church is a great professor. The structure of his pop culture class is focused around creating an analysis on a text in the media. It felt more academic then it needed to be. I personally don't like pop culture and this class reinforced that opinion. I would suggest taking a different elective, but Dr. Church is great.

- I loved Dr. Church's class. He is funny and keeps the class engaged throughout lecture. The quizzes can be kind of tricky, make sure to read his agendas before you take them. For the rest of the assignments, go to the TAs, they are the graders and know what you need to turn in. If you need to take this class, definitely take it from Dr. Church!!

Dr. Church is the best! The pop culture class was so interesting and so relevant. Even though the class was entirely on zoom, it never felt stuffy or boring. He utilized zoom really well and managed to still make the class fun. He also gives great feedback for the term paper and the class was overall very well organized!

Dr. Church was pretty funny; I actually enjoyed this class but there are a LOT of readings (and quizzes on the readings). The reading quizzes are closed notes and closed book, so make sure you actually comprehend what you're reading. The quizzes are short, so one question wrong means you don't get an A, and you don't get to know what you got wrong.

Dr. Church is honestly amazing. At the beginning, the quizzes were a little difficult even having done the reading but in the end, the class was meaningful, engaging, and interesting. I highly suggest taking COMMS 101 from Dr. Church

Dr. Church is hands down the best professor I have had at BYU. I wish I could take all my classes from him. He managed to make the whole 2.5 hours hilarious and the class was so involved. I feel like I got to meet everyone in the class and we just had a blast! Follow his agendas before class to ace the quizzes. This class is relevant, a must-take!

Great professor with great lectures. There are (almost) daily quizzes (he doesn't tell you what days you will have them) that come from the reading so you HAVE to do it. If you do the reading they aren't hard though. Super fun class with interesting assignments. I did not think he was tough grader as long as you did the assignments.

Absolutely loved this class and Dr Church! You have 1 or 2 pop quizzes every class over the readings so you actually have to read them. But the text is so interesting that you wont mind it! Lectures are long but so interesting they feel short. Dr church really values input and brings a lot of insight to the world of communication.

the class meets once a week, so you have to read a lot before class. He has one (or two) in class quizzes per class to check understanding of your readings. Church's lectures are the most entertaining and fun out of any class I've ever taken! LOVED this class, and LOVE dr. Church!

Dr. Church is amazing! I've taken two of his classes and I loved them both. He is so incredibly helpful and truly cares that you succeed. He responds to emails quickly and is always trying to make himself available for assistance. His class is interesting and engaging and the assignments aren't too hard or too tedious. Definitely recommend him!

This class was seriously amazing. I went into it planning on dropping it but after the first day I was hooked. He made evening class so enjoyable. His lectures are great, the readings are interesting, and the projects aren't too bad. We had two big group projects a midterm and a final with a few other minor assignments. Seriously take this class!!

Professor Church is great. His lectures can be a little dull at times, but for the most part they are engaging and interesting. He doesn't believe in busy work, which is great. The readings aren't overwhelming and are usually not too bad.

He incorporated real world issues, his research, and spirituality into his lectures. Sometimes dry lectures, but spring classes are long. He's up to times with pop culture through his research which adds some fun! He's a super tough grader, but I appreciated it because it was out of a genuine desire to push students to their best.

I really liked Mass Media. Not only is the class really informative but Dr. Church is a pretty cool guy. His knowledge of media is vast and his testimony is genuine. If you do the readings and pay attention in class, you'll do well. Assignments are fun and discussions are interesting. Highly recommended.

I really respect Dr. Church and his teaching styles. All his assignments had purpose, weren't busy work. He leads great discussions and gives everyone a chance to speak. Does a great job keeping the lectures on task while also hearing students out when they have an insight. Encourages learning by the Spirit even though it's not a religion class

I LOVE Dr. Church. He's funny, passionate, intelligent, and so kind. By far my favorite class of the semester. It's not hard, you learn a lot in class and the textbook, 2 tests, 1 paper, a fun video project. There are quizzes in class so don't miss. The class is discussion-based and spiritual and would benefit anyone. I highly recommend Dr. Church.

Dr. Church is a fantastic teacher. He has organized his classes wonderfully. You aren't asked to do more work than is necessary, you are always reminded about important assignments (and well-prepared for them), there are great discussions in class, and Dr. Church genuinely cares about you as his student.

Dr. Church is a stud. I love the way he runs his class and how he treats his students. He memorizes everyone's name and has a special way of making the class feel comfortable sharing our opinions and comments. He respects the views of the students and is super good at applying everything we learn to the gospel, and to our lives. Good class!

I loved this class! Church has very clear expectations, and if you do the readings and come to class, you'll do well. The study guides show exactly what are on the tests so if you put in effort, they aren't too difficult. There's a video group project that's actually super fun, and he really helps you see real-world application of the concepts.

Dr. Church is an awesome guy. He is passionate about his job and respects the students' ideas and opinions. Although the class had over one hundred students, he made an effort to learn every single student's name. The readings for the class were intriguing and his tests are easy because he provides a study guide with everything you need to know.

Dr. Church IS THE BOMB. He is  the best! He really is inspirational and caring, and as a younger professor, he is more sympathetic & understanding of the rigors of student life. There are not enough good things I could say about him & this class. If you're thinking about taking from him, go sign up right now! Do the hw, go to class & you're golden.

Dr. Church is awesome. His lectures are always focused on the bigger picture and how the concept applies to today's issues. Would recommend to any major. Don't bother with the reading, just go over the agenda and you'll do fine on the reading quizzes. Super fun and interactive discussion!

Dr. Church seems like a serious guy, but he really knows his stuff, which is awesome. This class is all about media and I've never met a smarter guy on the subject. From the Walking Dead to political debates to drones, to Pokemon Go, this class is very current, and Dr. Church makes it awesome.  Random reading quizzes throughout, tests aren't hard.

Super passionate teacher but if you want an easy A, I would suggest taking this class from another teacher. This COMMS101 class is way harder than the other ones. The pop quizzes for the readings are kind of dumb. Don't read. Study the agenda on LS instead. Once I stopped doing the readings and memorizing the agendas I got 5/5 on the quizzes.

I really enjoyed this class. It wasn't too hard, to be honest. If you just apply yourself a little you will get a good grade. Random quizzes, but look at the Agenda posted and you will get 5/5.  Talk with the TA if your super concerned about a project, but its pretty easy to get a good grade if you just follow the rubric.

I'm not even a Communications major and I loved his class. He was always interested in looking at the bigger picture and looked at how this applied to today, which I personally loved. To pass you do have to actually pay attention in class and do the readings. I'd highly recommend this class to anyone!

I loved this class. It involved a lot of reading and thinking but not very much "busy work" which  I really appreciated. In class participation is a must, but the content is interesting and professor Church is excellent at leading discussions so it is very fun. There is a term paper that is difficult, but Professor Church is incredibly helpful!

Dr. Church is fan-flipping-tastic!! If you are truly taking this class for credit in Communications, you will not regret taking it from him (I don't understand why anyone wouldn't like him...??) You just have to expect lots of work and great rewards for working hard. He doesn't give assignments without a good reason! Also gives extra credit :)

Honestly I have NO clue why people have said that his lectures are good... His lectures are INCREDIBLY BORING. They exactly mirror the readings that he forces you to be very particular about due to his obnoxious pop quizzes.  There are other teachers for Comms 101 and I would recommend ANY one of them because they actually want you to do well.

I really loved this class and Prof. Church! He makes the lectures interesting and always is trying to facilitate class discussion. He does give pop quizzes, but they are really easy if you do the reading. He doesn't post his lecture slides online, so going to class is a must. Other than that, he is very clear and helpful!

Dr. Church is awesome. He is really smart and knows a lot about what he is teaching. He teaches in a way that everyone understands and he is very helpful. We also watch funny videos and he always cracks jokes. He is a stand-up guy and I would definitely recommend him.
Scott Church while interesting to listen to was often vague in his testing questions and sometimes even posed trick questions which were misleading and unnecessary in terms of learning.

This class wasn't nearly as exciting/interesting as I thought it would be. Often times I thought we over-analyzed things a little. That being said, it's everything an elective course should be. Church is a fair grader and you should be able to get an A with a decent effort. Take the course or any class from him.

Dr. Church genuinely cares about the subject and his students.  Unfortunately, I found the class rather dull and quite a pain.  He has pop quizzes that are based on the textbook and outside readings, a few projects, a midterm and a final.  Not a lot of points available, so when you miss a point here or there, it really adds up to hurt your grade.

Prof. Church is a caring and effective teacher.  I didn't think I would learn much in the course because I have been speaking all through my education but I learned important new things. It was fun delivering speeches with other students and it is a stress-free atmosphere. It is a fairly easy course with great instruction and feedback.

Best class of the semester! I genuinely enjoyed going to Prof. Church's class. The discussions are interesting, and he makes it fun for everyone. He incorporates funny YouTube videos into the lessons. Make sure to do your reading for the class quizzes and do the assignments (easy!) and you'll be fine. I learned SO much in this class!

Great professor! Even in my class of 100, he memorized most student's names, and the class discussions were very interesting. He loves student interaction. The workload is pretty light and he's willing to explain assignments in more detail to you if you need it. He gives great study guides for all tests. Fun class!

Dr. Church is awesome!! Even if you aren't majoring in communications, this is a great class. His tests are very straight forward so you know exactly what to study! We had reading quizzes quite frequently but as long as you do the reading for class each day you'll be fine! We had great discussions during class and he is extremely helpful!

Take this class from him! I really enjoyed going to this class and listening to class discussions.  He makes lectures interesting and entertaining.  A short paper, a final video and two test, so the workload is light.  Textbook reading is enjoyable and light and he is very helpful for any questions!

He does a very good job with spiritual thoughts but other than that, he seems very lost in the material- we go on lots of side quests and he often comes off as patronizing when students ask questions. His tests do not really cover the material in class & the asymmetry in lecture vs tests is very stark and made it difficult to prepare for class.
Unclear expectations & very disorganized. Takes a long time to explain concepts. Has poor communication skills which confound the difficulty of understanding how to succeed in the class

I was disappointed to find out how little original content this class would go over. If you are expecting a class filled new content, you will be disappointed. Dr Condie is very nice, but it seems like he does not prioritize this class. There is poor communication and expectations that are not obvious.

If you're new to finance, take FIN 201 instead—Econ 450 doesn't build on the BYU Econ core. The course is better suited for students with a finance background. Early lectures were engaging and left us wanting more, but later in the semester, structure declined and several class periods were spent on current events rather than core material.

Pros: Good lectures. Great spiritual thoughts. Interesting to talk to.

Cons: Poor class organization. Tests were difficult to prepare for, not because the material was difficult, but because the disconnect between lectures and homework and lack of study guide.

Final grade distribution (num students in parentheses): B- (3), B (4), B+ (1), A (6)
dr. Condie has bomb spiritual thoughts and is a great guy. His lectures are good and he uses a good textbook that is actually interesting. He's a very open and caring guy!

Solid professor. Seems like he really cares about his students. The class material is pretty challenging, but he does a good job of explaining it in lecture. The homework are tough, but they are graded on completion, so you don't really need to do well on the homework to succeed in the class.

I love Dr. Condie, and I felt much more prepared for grad school after taking this class. That was partially because of how insanely difficult this class was, but I do feel like I am capable of handling grad school after managing this course. The 4 PSs each take an insanely long time, so be prepared.
Love Dr. Condie

Dr. Condie consistently demonstrates that he really cares for his students. He not only cares that we succeed in this class, but that we leave this class well prepared to succeed in graduate school. The material in this class is very difficult for everyone, but Dr. Condie understands that and spends lots of time on the most difficult concepts.
Dr. Condie was great and cared a lot. Tests were difficult, but you'll be fine if you read the textbook.
Be prepared for a project that will take at least half a semester to complete. Also be prepared for tests as it is a huge part of the grade.

Condie doesn't require attendance but he does random pop quizzes for your "attendance grade". His exams are hard but so are all other exams in the economics department. I got a C in the class but I also was bad at reading the textbooks. We did not have a lot of homework which I loved. I also thought he was pretty funny in his lectures.

I loved Professor Condie, thought he showed a lot of care for the class, and made clear what the expectations were. If you did the readings, paid attention in the lectures, and focused on the practice tests while studying, it was a pretty easy A.

Professor Condie's lectures have little to do with the tests. I probably could have gotten a higher grade by reading the textbook all the way through. He has a personality that rubs me the wrong way, so take this with a grain of salt. My biggest complaint was the draconian grading scale: "Miss one problem get 66%..." My TA was cool. Hope yours is.

I really like Dr. Condie, but 580 wasn't my favorite. Don't take it unless you're planning on a PhD, and this class might just change your mind. 3 tests each worth 30%. Tons of partial credit. HW is 10% and takes 15+ hours. 5 A's, 1 A-, 3 B+'s, 1 C-. The cutoff for an A changed from a 60% to a 68%, so don't count on the cutoffs he gives you.

Dr. Condie simply did not teach the class. He replaced lectures with recorded lectures of the previous semester. The majority of the grade was based around tests and essays. Tests were ripped from the textbook and unrelated to lectures. Essays were not graded for up to 6 weeks, and feedback was vague. Dr. Condie clearly looked down upon students.

His lectures were super interesting. However, it was really hard to know what to expect for the tests. There was a big disconnect between the textbook, lectures, and tests. It was hard to know how to get an A. Students emailed him several times, but he never responded. Interesting lectures, poor organization.

This is an easy A class, and Dr. Condie is a great lecturer. Read the textbook (a big part of understanding the contents.) His lectures provide many novel and thoughtful ideas in economics. DEFINITELY RECOMMENDED. Expecting his ECON 450 & 580. I see negative comments: these guys lack self-discipline and want clowns as their professor. H. L.
Terrible. His lectures were nothing to do with the exams. He posts in-class quizzes, or nobody would listen to his nonsense. READ THE TEXTBOOK.

I have never seen a more unorganized professor. The dude rants about nonsense in class that doesnt help you on the test. His TAs have no idea whats going on. There is no consistency on learning suite and he is always changing everything so you never know what the latest info is. Not a hard class, very interesting, but not because of him.

Extremely test heavy (87% of grade). Lectures usually just confused me--reading the textbook was by far the best way to prep for exams. I never felt like what he talked about in class was useful for tests, but if you like random tangents about econ, you'll love him. Big disconnect between lectures, hw, and test. Make sure to read the textbook!
I liked Dr. Condie a lot. Very caring and does a good job teaching. If you're interested in taking 580 I think you'll enjoy learning from him

If you have the chance, take 381 from Condie. He's one of the only professors that will give you some easy python experience which is super helpful. As for doing well on tests, if you read the textbook and take notes, you'll be totally fine. He's there to give extra help/feedback if you need him. Great professor.

One of my favorite classes at BYU. Condie did an excellent job making the material interesting and engaging. Super easy to get him to go off on tangents though. Homework isn't too hard and I especially liked this class because you will learn a little Python programming. Tests are hard, but everything you need is in the textbook.

580 was a grad-level course. We never knew what section to read in the book to prepare for lecture. My favorite classes were when he got off topic. He talked about interesting ideas and told us more about grad school. The class material is wicked hard, but that's to be expected. The grading scale is extremely generous.

He teaches interesting lectures that have nothing to do with the exams.  The book for the class, however, is excellent and you should do well as long as you read it regularly.  Condie is apathetic towards his students and uses a decent amount of class time to talk about himself or how "being a democrat in Utah makes you king".

No TA. Evident that he doesn't want to be teaching his class. Random tangents and long boring lectures. HUGE disconnect between lecture, HW, and exams. Extremely arbitrary grader. Office Hours are little to no help. HW based on completion with no feedback. Responds to questions in a very condescending manner. Just all around frustrating.

I had a tough time with Dr. Condie. The course was poorly organized. We spend weeks doing derivations on the board and the midterm only tested intuition. Huge disconnect between lecture material, homework problems , reading content, and test material. Unfortunately, I would not recommend taking this course from Dr. Condie.

Taught the course different from other professors in the department, which gets a little confusing, especially wth the TAs. Tests on things not on lecture, but yes in the textbook. Homework assignments were too easily graded, while the tests were far harder. Read the textbook. If econ doesn't come naturally to you, pick another professor.

Funny teacher, engaging, given the subject matter.  His biggest problem is in test preparation.  He leaves you high and dry trying to prep for his tests.  The practice tests given are nothing even remotely like his real tests, and he doesn't do much to help you before midterms or finals.
Really clear teaching.  Funny Guy.  Good dresser.  Great Class.

Condie is a really just average. He shows up to class, gives a long lecture with a lot of opinion and irrelevant remarks in there, puts a third of the class to sleep, and does helpful problems on the board occasionally. He's sarcastic, kind of impersonal, and doesn't seem to care much about the students. Mediocre experience--would NOT take again.
He's great. Take him. Class was pretty easy.

Really funny guy although his lectures were dry at times (sorry if thats confusing but its true). His tests are challenging but its graded on a curve and he provides reviews which are great. should be noted that the reviews dont include everything for the tests.

I've never written a bad review here, but Dr. Condie really is sub-par.  I've never gotten below an A in an economics class but this one.  It's not the material, because I helped friends with other professors and got the right answers.  Grading was totally arbitrary and there was little correlation with tests, homework, and class material.

Very frustrating course. The first few lectures were well done and clearly organized, but as the semester continued it seemed that there was very little thought put into the discussions. The TA was also very unhelpful and provided memorized answers to questions about subjects. The final was very vague and Condie's questions were hard to understand.
Mediocre. Also, side note, you must be an attentive, effective listener and textbook reader to do well in this class. Walks back and forth and talks all class.
Funny professor. You do not need to read the book to do well, but the book coincides well with the lectures. Exams had several new questions that extended beyond what we did in class.

Condie is an absolutely amazing teacher; he is incredibly funny and intelligent.  Despite the fact that it's hard to present macro without letting your own political biases show through, Condie does a good job of presenting both camps of macroeconomic thought without unduly disparaging or embracing either side; he's one of my favorite professors.

Terribly convoluted style of teaching. Easy homework and moderate exams don't prepare for an incomprehensible final. Difficult not in material covered, but in understanding him. Grading is strictly by standard deviation from the class mean. Take a finance class from the business school instead. My only B in the entire program (I took 388 & 488).

Fortunately the material is terribly easy, but Prof Condie artificially inflates the difficulty by the grading as arbitrarily as he can.  His lectures are fairly boring and not terribly useful. He's not half as intelligent as he thinks he is, which is maddening when he treats you like you're some kind of moron when you talk to him outside of class.

Great teacher. One of the best that I have had. Has a real interest in students and in teaching well. Tests were hard, but not ridiculous and they're curved... so that doesn't really matter. He does random quizzes that are basically attendance and there is homework due every Fri. Especially good class is Aaron is the TA. Dangerously good combo.

He is an Econ professor, and they usually have a hard time communicating ideas so others will understand. Nice, tries really hard to be concise, but not always there. His class isn't that hard, I studied a lot without his notes and did fairly well. Lots of help though online/with study groups with this topic. Would take again.

He has a really funny sense of dry humor, you'll be entertained in class, then you'll go home and realize you really didn't learn anything coherent, just a bunch of jumbled concepts.  The homework does nothing to prepare you for tests, and he seems to ENJOY being ambiguous while he teaches, in order to be funny, instead of concise and informative.

Great professor. I appreciated his correct usage of mathematical language. You shouldn't be in the econ program if you can't figure out math on your own or if you expect the professor to teach it to you. That's why all those math classes are prerequisites. It is assumed you know how to READ math. I found his teaching style easy to understand.

I really didn't enjoy condie... he's just another elitist that passes up opportunities to apply the material to real life so that he can say something is "cosmically cool" without explaining it clearly at all. I would not recommend taking him

Professor Condie was a fantastic teacher. Honestly, his class was a breath of fresh air from all the dense calculus in the other upper level econ classes. He taught economics in a very clear and concise manner. I feel that my understanding of macroeconomics obtained from this class was fantastic. Best teacher in the econ department if you ask me.

Incompetent, I don't know why he went into teaching. His explanations are ambiguous relative to how specifically you are tested on material. Nothing about his lectures prepares you for his poorly prepared exams.
Easy class, he avoided the math in lectures and there was very little math on the tests. If you skim the chapters and learn the basic intuitive principles you'll get an A.
