Get accustomed to hearing... "It's not completely obvious..." as this is an intro to something quite vague. The lectures lack math, concern for student comprehension, and overall clarity. Humorous until you're trying to deciphering the test questions. Fortunately the text by Mankiw is excellent.

He tries to teach economics without really getting into the math very much, and this makes explaining difficult topics very difficult for him. His exam questions are very ambiguous are grading is not that standard.

Professor Condie was fantastic. He was organized, helpful, and reliable as well as funny and humane. He has a great sense of dry humor and is fairly young and connects well with the students. He explains clearly, is fair, and teaches effectively. I very much enjoyed this class!

I have to say that when it comes to explaining difficult concepts he just doesn’t seem to be up to par. Furthermore, he doesn’t seem to take much interest to students and whether they are grasping the concepts or not.
Visiting Cornell student, but he'll probably be here for good soon.  Very nice, but doesn't know how to explain things very clearly, and grading is arbitrary.  An unavoidable B.

My sister got home from her mission so I had to fly home I gave him notice but he had no mercy. Took percentage off of my grade. We go to byu yet he acted like I had control over this. DONT take his class. He does not care about you. He wants you to feel less than. One of those impossible situations where you're never right.

Incredibly rigorous class, especially for a 2nd sem college student not used to the writing-intensive style of exam which he conducts. That being said, easily my favorite class that semester. NEED to show up to lecture. NEED to go in during lab/office hours. Learned a ton. Great guy. Will keep in touch with him for future semesters.

Dr. Cooper is an amazing pedagogue. If you want to learn lots, this is a great class to take. There are mini essays, but you can get 100% on all of them if you just do them. Lots of readings, but not necessary to do them all. I took this as a junior and it wasn't bad, but for first-semester freshmen it could be tricky. An A is totally doable.

I genuinely don't know if he could be more unorganized. Showed up to class and he just said "memorize the map of Asia by Friday" which isn't bad but still. He also refuses to use powerpoints and has pretty bad handwriting so notes are difficult. Don't take poli170 if you don't have to.

Prof Cooper is very good at teaching the material and making it digestible for everyone. There are many essays and four tests. The exams are challenging so be sure to study. Luckily the study guides provide all the information that will be on the test. Very interesting material but a rigid class structure.

Do not take Professor Cooper for an intro level class, he will tank your GPA. Poli 170 was graded so test heavy that it was difficult to do well, when we weren't prepared very well for his super difficult tests that were graded very harshly. This professor seems to take pride in the fact that students have difficulty with his class.

Best lecturer I've ever had. Toughest grader I've ever had as well. Doesn't prepare you for the level of difficulty of his tests. His classes are fascinating but the tests are outrageously difficult, particularly for an intro-level GE poli sci class. Take POLI170 from someone else, it well benefit your GPA. Consider him for more advanced courses.

Hardest class I have ever taken. Took this INTRO class my junior year and barely walked away with a C+ after being a 4.0 college student before this. Assigns excessive reading which you are required to know for the exams which are the hardest graded exams I've ever taken. Seems like he prides himself on students failing, never take this professor.

Professor Cooper is obviously super knowledgable about all of his class lectures. He is compassionate and engaging. in his lectures, and is able to handle questions very well. Heavy reading class, and tests are graded pretty harshly, but he gives clear guidelines after the first test. Would recommend!! He's awesome

He is super fun and his lecture's are easy to understand and engaging. You will have a lot of reading but make sure you keep up. The test are difficult but he is willing to help and offer review sessions. Attendance is mandatory but you only takes it on random days but if you miss class there is no way to get the lecture notes.
He is super fun and his lecture's are easy to understand and engaging. You will have a lot of reading but make sur
Incredible professor, probably the best I've ever had. Knows his stuff. Easily accessible. Do the readings, take good notes, and you'll be fine. Not as difficult as people say he is.

INCREDIBLE CLASS. Take Soviet Politics! Dr. Cooper is everything I feel a BYU professor should be. He was funny, engaging, and brilliant and lectures flew by. He's a tough grader, but he cares about his students so much that I found that to be even more motivating. I feel like a better citizen and scholar because of this class.

Professor Cooper's PLSC170 is a challenging but rewarding course. The lectures are engaging, and the readings are relevant. Though exams are tough, using resources like Unstuck AI and attending office hours can help you succeed. If you're willing to put in the work, it's an excellent class.

Prof. Cooper's POLI 376 class is very difficult (at least 50 pages of reading a night and hard tests), but I learned so much. Prof. Cooper is genuine in his concern for his students, and you can tell he really wants to meet with you and hear what is going on in your life. I would totally take the class again!

DO NOT TAKE. His rating is extremely misleading, and I wish someone would have told me the truth. He is extremely cold and takes pride in grading harshly and students doing poorly. He acts as if this is the only class you are taking and that you should know everything he knows and more. He will not work with you and lectures will have you snoozing.

Tough but very fair grader with good feedback. Interesting class & really challenges you, I'd recommend it! Willing to work with you & invested in your success. A few options for extra credit on tests & when you go above & beyond with assignments. DO THE READINGS

Don't take for a GE and consider another teacher even if its for major. 0 mercy regarding missing class even for circumstances you have no control over and gave him notice for. He grades extremely harshly and expects you to know material as if you have been studying it as long as he has. Nothing you do will be satisfactory for him or TAs.

Professor Cooper was the best teacher I have had so far at BYU. He was very clear in terms of expectations and the readings (which you should always do) though numerous were all directly related to lectures and the course curriculum. Despite the class being mostly lecture-based he did an excellent job of encouraging class participation and debate.

Professor Cooper is knowledgeable and gives fascinating lectures. His class is very reading heavy and there is a lot of material to get through, but he gives you plenty of resources (TAs, review sessions, study guide, time to ask questions in class, office hours, etc.) to succeed. He cares about his students and expects you to put in the work.

Dr. Cooper is the most supportive professor you'll meet. He is not only brilliant, but he is also super prepared for every lecture and gives amazing feedback to those who seek it. I learned so much from his class and became a much stronger and confident writer. Highly recommend!

Dr. Cooper is an amazing professor. He taught very clearly and created a good environment for learning. He did not force his political views on us and taught about all schools of thought equally. There is a lot of reading to do and tests are difficult, but if you study hard and dedicate yourself to learning it is an awesome class and passable.

He is a great professor who cares a lot about your success. If you make an effort to improve your grade and talk to him, it will be a helpful experience. He offers great advice on papers. The content is just hard to absorb because there is so much! So come in with some experience in the topics already.

Very interesting class but Professor Cooper was not there for the students. He is cold and unreasonable. Tests were graded very hard with little feedback. He prides himself in having a "hard" class. Expect to do a ton of reading. Do not take this class as an elective you will regret it.

Professor Cooper is a really informative teacher and teaches his content well. However, his tests are extremely difficult and he has very specific expectations for content on papers and reading questions. As someone with anxiety, he does not provide online options and if you miss class you will not pass.

"it would be a miracle if you even got a B in this class"
this was his response when I asked him how I could succeed and get an A in his class. I loved the material, and I love US foreign policy but he was so nit-picky with me the entire semester--I decided to withdraw from the class after the midterm. Not worth it.

Dr. Cooper is incredibly well-read and intelligent, but his kindness is most impressive trait. I've never had a professor go more out of his way to help his students. Kind, helpful, and sympathetic to student life. Exceptional lecturer. High expectations, but bends over backwards to prepare you for tests and give feedback on papers. 10/10.

I took International Political Econ from him and it was maybe the hardest class I have ever had. Mind you, I am not an IR, Polisci, or Econ major. Excellent lecturer. He really knows his stuff and teaches it well. The readings and lectures are SUPER important if you want to pass. Take very detailed notes because this class is content heavy.

One of the most engaging professors I've had. His tests are difficult, but the material is very worthwhile. You're graded on few things, the class is exam-heavy. Lots of reading. He's always available for students. Straight-A students will be upset they don't get an A in his class, but POLI 376 is absolutely worth your time. Class is heavily curved

"My assumption is that every paper is average, a C grade, until you prove otherwise...". How on earth does this inspire students to work hard to receive a good grade if they are already expecting to get a C on one of the 3 assignments given in the class... Tests are nearly impossible if you don't memorize every single thing he said in person.
This was one of my favorite classes I have ever taken. Dr. Cooper is super intelligent and just a good guy. He is easy to talk to and always makes time for students. Highly recommend Soviet Politics.
One of my favorite professors, truly. He knows and loves the material, gives really good lectures, and is the sweetest man on earth. He's like a religion professor but in the Poli Sci department.

Challenging class, absolutely worth it. Some of the most interesting lectures I've had in college. The paper is difficult and the tests are quite specific, so make sure you take great notes in class. Lots of reading, but most of it is quite interesting. I would 100% recommend Professor Cooper over and over again.

One of my favorite professors. Dr. Cooper is super clear on his expectations. Good amount of readings required, but definitely not anything crazy. Grade is based off four quizzes, two exams, a paper, participation, and 12 reading responses. Lectures are great, super informative. If you're interested in intl politics, take classes from Cooper!

This class is AMAZING! I learned so much about Russia and the Soviet Union. He is very knowledgeable, and if I could I would take the class again, just without the tests and papers lol! The papers are easy and straightforward, but take notes on everything during the lectures. He is one of the most caring professors, and wants everyone to succeed!

Professor Cooper was one of the most caring professors I have had. He genuinely cares for every student. I had COVID really bad in the middle of the semester, and when I reached out, he let me turn my assignments in when I felt better, and opened the test back up for me when I was feeling better. There is a lot of writing and reading! Amazing class

He's an awesome professor and this class was super interesting, but the reading load was like 120 pages a week of dense material. And if you don't read it, you won't do well on the exams. Love professor cooper though !

Great Lectures. Do the readings, they help. Caring and understanding. You have to do 12 small essays on the readings, and the the early ones. Take good notes and study well for the exams. Its a decent amount of work, but an intriguing class nonetheless. You can get by alright without the textbook.

This was honestly a fairly easy class if you just read the assigned articles and understand what they're saying. Great lectures and a fun topic to discuss. The tests are all writing based and in the reviews he gives you hints as to what you'll need to write about.

Prof. Cooper is a great lecturer and very accessible if you ever have questions that you want to take to him directly. With that being said, there is a ridiculous amount of readings that he expects you to do for each class. His tests are difficult and he tests you on some of the most obscure details that he may have only glanced over in class.
Tests are really straught forward. Pay attention to lectures and you have everything you need. Tough grader on papers and pretty strict about late policies etc.

Professor Cooper was great. He assigned a lot of reading but he expects you to skim not read the whole passage. He was very clear what you needed to know for the test and would answer any question you have about things on the study guide. I want to go into IR, but if you're just taking this to fulfill a requirement there is probably easier classes.

I love Professor Cooper! He assigns a lot of reading, but nothing crazy. His lectures are engaging and everyone has a chance to participate and voice opinions. He cares a lot about his students and is passionate about the subject. Amazing professor, always willing to help, meet with you, answer questions, etc.

Dr. Cooper is by far the best International Relations Poli Sci professor at BYU. He provides very clear guidelines for every assignment, gives great feedback on papers and tests, and even though there is a lot of reading, he provides reading questions to guide you through the texts. His lectures are very engaging and he uses the readings often.

He is a great teacher and super interesting but EXTREMELY DIFFICULT. There is a lot of reading and the 4 tests you take in the class are near impossible. I usually do pretty well on in class exams but I failed every single one of them. Plan on taking tons of time to study. Luckily he is great with making time to meet with you if you are struggling

Dr. Cooper is extremely smart, but the world's hardest grader. His tests are very difficult, and I go to class every day, do the readings, and visit his office hours. I'm no slacker! I will probably lose my full-ride because of this class. I've learned a lot, but for me it's just not worth so much work for so little reward. Save your scholarship!

Cooper was my favorite professor in my entire BYU career, especially in the Political Science department. You will learn a ton that will stick with you. Go to his reviews and study the review sheet and you will pass the tests with flying colors. I felt unprepared before reviews and got 80+ on each test before the very generous curve. TAKE HIM!

Absolutely brilliant!! Dont expect this to be an easy class at all, but if you put the work in, Dr Cooper will make what would otherwise be boring, a fascinating subject! I highly recommend him for those willing to learn

I actually really enjoyed this class and the subject material. He is a great teacher and knows what he is talking about. That being said, he expects you to really know what you are talking about and his tests are REALLY hard. There is also a ton of reading. He doesn't use powerpoint so you have to be at pretty much every lecture to do well.

The tests were really hard. I was on the fence of going into political science or not, and this class really helped me decide that I didn't want to. He was a really tough teacher and the tests were really hard on purpose. Buckle up if you're going to take a class from him.

Kind of a dull lecturer (and I didn't love the course material), but he is a solid guy. Fair grader, the tests were exactly as we explained them. Come prepared to class and do all the readings. Follow his advice to be successful in the class.
Dr. Cooper does a great job answering questions, keeps his test purely fact based (his opinion doesn't shape grading). Explains concepts well. Highly recommend this class from him!

Prof. Cooper makes you work for your grade, but the class is worth taking. He is very knowledgeable in his field but still gives students the chance to form their own opinions. Tests are graded a but strictly, but the class is worth taking. Lots of reading.

Professor Cooper's lectures and discussions make the class interesting and understandable. He is a very fair grader and everything in the tests was either clearly mentioned in lectures or made obvious in the reading. Tip: take good lecture notes. I plan on taking more courses from Professor Cooper.

Awesome class! Lots of reading but it usually provides multiple viewpoints so it's perfect for getting a more nuanced approached to issues. Excellent lectures, accessible to students, great study guides, clear about test criteria so you can study effectively, clear about class priorities so you know what to focus on most.

Best professor I have EVER had. If you are on the fence about taking a class from him, DO IT. I would take every class from him if I could. He made me an EXPERT on soviet politics and made me think differently about the world. this class is life changing.

I had a really difficult time mostly due to Pro. Cooper's personality. His lectures are extremely informative and he is well versed in Soviet Politics; unfortunately, he expects you to know as much as he does. He grades very harshly and finds ridiculous terms to quiz you on. It's not about the effort you invest but about pleasing his ego.

Prof. Cooper is awesome! His teaching is on point. He loves teaching and teaches in a way that you can understand. You do need to read a lot though. The assignments are reading responses which are easy. He doesn't grade hard on those. The map quizzes are also easy. I would love to take his other classes!

Dr. Cooper is a fantastic instructor. He has an ability to convey the material in a way that makes sense and matters. His knowledge will intimidate you, though and he expects you to be able to glean the material from his lectures and reading. US Foreign Policy is extensive and broad, but Dr. C makes it accessible and unbiased. Do the readings!!!

Cooper is INCREDIBLE; lectures are engaging/funny/interesting (DO NOT MISS CLASS.) But I studied harder for this final than I ever have for a test in college, and still didn't do well on it. The tests (there's 4) are just so specific and so challenging. Assignments are straightforward and posted from day 1, and beneficial to course. Tough & great!

I've taken this class and his intro class and they've been two of my favorites. Professor Cooper is my favorite professor in the political science department, and maybe at BYU. He's incredibly knowledgeable and makes information easy to understand. He sees grading as a necessary evil and is really fair about it. Take good notes and you'll do well.

Awesome professor! Lectures are very interesting and even though its such a huge class (150 in mine) he always gives people the chance to participate/have class discussion. A ton of reading. Keep up with it and take good notes in class.

Professor Cooper is a great, interesting professor. The class is based on a lot of article readings. Attendance is mandatory because most of what he says in lectures is on the tests. Make sure to take good notes. The lectures, to me, are really interesting and the time goes by quicker.

Lectures are solid and and you learn a lot. Problem is the guy grades tests way too harsh for a 100 level class. To get an A you have to know all the nuances of the material as well as he does. Legit more reading required in this class than all my other classes combined. Get ready to read for hours every night (thought that was only for law school)

There's a lot of reading in this class. Expect 70-80 pages per week. Very solid lecturer and clear grading criteria. His lectures are very participatory--he takes a lot of questions and comments which makes it more engaging.

Professor Cooper is definitely one of the best professors at BYU. He knows his stuff through and through, is a good teacher, has well prepared lectures, and genuinely cares about his students. He's the reason I stuck with the major. The class is hard but worth it. Do the readings (which I often didn't) and you'll love the class more.

Dr. Cooper is a great professor and very, very helpful outside of the classroom. It is VERY easy to get behind because there is little to no accountability aside from 4 or so assessments.  This is no fault of his- he is clear from the beginning. But be prepared to demand rigor from yourself or you will find yourself in a sorry place.

I took 4 classes from Dr. Cooper at BYU, and they were probably 4 of the classes that taught me the most. He is an excellent teacher. He makes you work hard, but his expectations are always crystal clear, so if you do the work you'll get the grade you deserve. You owe it to yourself to take some classes from him!
Professor Cooper has it going on! The class was funny, pushed me to work hard, and enlightened my understanding of international theory and has been a great basis to the rest of the major for me.

Get ready for a rip-roaring good time in this class.  The reading is heavy, but if you think the subject matter is as much fun as I do (and Professor Cooper makes it very fun and interesting), it'll be easy enough.  Just make sure to do all the reading very closely.

Prof Cooper is one of my favorites! His lectures are really interesting and he uses great examples for students to understand the subject matter. LOTS of mandatory reading: Sometimes 75 pages a night! If you do not read or skip on readings, you will not pass since he ties it all together. Tests are hard if you don't read or do the assignments.

I looked forward to the lectures every day. Though there was lots of readings and tests were tough, the expectations were clear.  Dr. Cooper is an amazing teacher, and I would definitely recommend this class or any other class he teaches, especially if you're interested in international politics. You will learn so much in this class!

Poli 170 with Dr. Cooper was amazing. His expectations are clear and fair, and if you attend the lectures and study for the exams, you'll be fine. I would definitely take another class taught by Dr. Cooper.
Amazing at teaching and really knows what he is talking about. There is a ridiculous amount of reading and the tests are incredibly hard, but he uses a grading curve that makes it manageable.

I loved taking this class from Prof. Cooper. He's a very intelligent man and knows a great deal about International Politics. His lectures are very organized and easy to take notes along with. If you go exactly with the study guide for exams and do the readings, class won't be a challenge, Cooper is a very fair grader.

May be a great prof for some, but was literally the worst prof I have had to date (37 credit hours under my belt). He is very unprofessional (rude with a god complex) over email. Exams given include material not spoken of in class, nor on the syllabus.  My grade literally went up after I stopped attending the class halfway through the semester.

Professor Cooper is passionate and gives very interesting examples. I learned a lot about international relations and definitely am interested in learning more after taking this class. Not an easy class though. It's graded based on 12 reading essays (1.5 pages), 2 current events essays (3 pages), and 4 difficult timed essay exams. Take good notes!
Really interesting lectures. No surprises. Homework is very doable. Not graded harshly. Study guides are great help for the exams.

Professor Cooper is without doubt the best professor I have ever had. He is engaging, knowledgable and has a sense of humour, something I think is necessary for the topic. However he has a reputation as an incredibly tough grader and I would have to agree. You have to work very hard. I would take him for everything if my GPA could handle it.

Dr. Cooper has to be the best professor I have had at BYU. His expectations are always very clear. If you do what he asks then his classes are not difficult. They do require a lot of work, but he tells you exactly what you need to do to get an A. He made International Political Economy as interesting as possible considering the subject matter!

Prof. Cooper is an amazing professor and incredibly intelligent. He knows the answers to every question posed in class and is always willing to spend more time explaining to ensure you understand. He is a tough grader but if you do the readings and participate in class you will do well and learn a lot. He keeps you interested and makes you smarter.

Prof. Cooper is an awesome teacher, but incredibly tough. He is very willing to help students, but you will get your butt kicked in the class if you don't study hard. His tests are really subjective and it's easy to get docked on little things. But if you spend a few days studying, you'll do ok.

I liked the lectures and the subject is great. He explains the subject very well and I am engaged through the whole class. My big beef with this professor is his grading system, especially on tests. He gives a lot of essay questions on the test which require a lot of detail and will dock a lot points if one of those details is missing. uncool man.
The professor is one of the best I have had. His lectures constantly fascinated me.  He does give about seventy pages of reading a week so beware.

Be prepared to read and participate in the lectures. The readings can be quite long and dry, but the topicsthemes are super important and interesting. Bro. Cooper has great lectures, with the expectation that his students take an active role in discussions based on the lectures and readings. His tests aren't that bad if you study the study guides.

Cooper is my fav professor. I have taken 2 classes from him, and he is very good about setting clear expectations. I always knew how to prepare for his exams. His lectures are incredible and engaging. The class is a lot of work, and there are lots of readings, but I think he makes sure that anyone can succeed. Take this class if you can!!
Cooper is easily the best professor in the department. He explains very complex concepts in ways that people unfamiliar with the subject matter can understand.

Professor Cooper's class isn't the easiest, since the tests are killer and he has very high reading expectations, but his lectures are the best I've seen. He's happy to help anybody, and knows a ton about what he teaches. If you study for hours to prepare for each of his tests, you'll probably do pretty well in the class.

Professor Cooper is awesome. I took this class for GE credit and had little interest in Poli Sci but he made me love the subject. A lot of ready, but it is pretty interesting if you try to understand it. Tests are semi difficult but the study guide tells you everything that will be on the test. No surprises

Be ready to read.  A lot.  Dr. Cooper's a great teacher, though.  The class isn't easy, but you know exactly what you need to study to get a good grade.  Lectures are engaging and interesting.  Dr. Cooper goes out of his way to make sure his students succeed in the class.

I got an A in this class. It was actually my favorite class that I took at BYU. Dr. Cooper makes everything very clear, and you always know exactly what is expected of you. If you buy the previous editions of the text books he will give you the parts that you need to read from them to get the equivalent education, which means that it is cheap!

One of my favorite professors! totally easy to understand and always willing to help! Work load could pile up a bit sometimes, but he always provided excellent teaching and study guides to help on the tests

Prof Cooper is awesome. His class was extremely well organized and his notes were very easy to learn from. The tests were difficult and graded intensely, but the study guides were very helpful. The only bad part of the class is the massive reading load, but the reading is entirely necessary.

I loved this class with Dr. Cooper! He knows so much and makes class very interesting. While you do need study hard for the test, I don't find it overly difficult and he is definitely willing to help anyone. I would recommend this class to anyone as he is a really great professor who is makes class fun (he's pretty funny) and interesting!

This class wasn't nearly as difficult as I thought it would be. Cooper made it really interesting and applicable, and doing well isn't hard. Tests are based off of the study guides and readings, so keep up with them. You'll regret it if you don't. Besides the reading, which was a little heavy at times, the work load was completely manageable.

Excellent professor who not only knows the material but knows how to teach it. Go to class, takes good notes, and cram before each test. Follow the study guide and be very clear on the essay questions. The rest of your points are participation -- easy A. Textbook reading is not required. People who say this class is difficult are lazy/unintelligent

Extremely organized and extremely fair. This class is tough for an intro-level course, and there's lots of reading, but it's very interesting and it's possible to do well. You will know what to expect on exams because they are exactly what he says they will be: taken from the study guide and reading questions. Highly recommend.

Professor Cooper is one of the best professors there is. He comes off really hard the first week of class, and you will work a ton in his, but you will also learn a ton and if you do what he tells you you will do well. He is very clear on what he wants and that is so helpful. 200 is super hard, but you will use it the rest of your life.

Good class. I love history and politics so it was pretty sweet. Some of the readings are pretty dry but he explains the concepts well enough for you to do well on the test. He can get annoyed when people don't show up, nobody does the readings, or students turn in essays without being in class.
Excellent professor. He was very organized and helpful. His class required a lot of work but grading was fair and I learned a lot.
Hard class, lots of reading, lots of things to know, and lots of time.  A "2" page paper, which was an 11 font, single space paper (so it really turned out to be around 8 pages double spaced)

Prof. Cooper is probably the most fair teacher you will ever have. You have to put in the effort, he expects a lot, but he will tell you exactly what to expect for readings, assignments, and tests. Also, he knows a ton and, unlike some teachers, really knows how to communicate it clearly to his students.

Prof Cooper is truly a wonderful teacher and person.  I had him during a study abroad he did in London, and as an econ major, I was honestly not used to someone teaching in such a clear and concise manner.  He is genuinely interested in the success of each of his students.  I highly recommend taking a course from him, even if PlSc200 is nasty

Prof. Cooper is a good lecturer who cares about his students. He has a few flaws though. First, count on buying at least one textbook that will be very needed for the first two months then never using it again. Second, his grading on essays and papers can be a bit subjective. Lastly, he's scatterbrained and might take a long time to grade tests.
Great class, well taught
This class is extremely difficult, but Cooper made it bearable. He is a great teacher, very helpful and accommodating in a very tricky class. That said, it's 200 and it sucks.

This is a typical PoliSci elective class (i.e. good teacher, boring subject, irrelevant to your education, arbitrary grading, etc.) If you're interested in Russia then you'll love this class. It was just okay for me. Prof. Cooper is a very good teacher though his grading on the tests is very subjective.

I really hated the class, especially the math parts, but Cooper always had such a lively and kind attitude. He provided everything students needed to have success in his class. Just do all the assignments, go to all of the labs, attend all classes, and you're guaranteed to get a B!
He is awesome professor! He is very kind and care about students!  I really love how he teaches his classes!  His class is not easy, but it worths!  Don't worry!  He can take care of you!

Prof. Cooper is a great guy and a nice teacher, but this class is very difficult. Tons of reading, tons of work. Long, detailed projects,and weekly quizzes and practice assignments. He was very helpful and his lectures are clear and help a lot. This class is do-able but its a huge workload. If you have to take it I recommend Cooper strongly.

Professor Cooper is great!  He gives you a study guide telling you exactly what to study before each test and not one question will stray from that study guide.  Get together a good study group and just go through the study guide and you will have no problem.  No outside assignments, just reading and the material is fascinating!

I personally did not like this class. I found Prof. Cooper's lectures to be boring and felt like there was too much reading. He seems nice enough, but I just couldn't get interested in what he was saying.  I am in the class again right now with a different teacher and I like it much better.

I have taken 170, 372, 376 from Cooper.  My favorite teacher so far at BYU.  I have also TA'd for him twice.  LOTS of reading, but it is never just busy work.  Great clarity and his passion for teaching is very clear.  A++++
Awesome professor.  A lot of reading for 100 level class but tests are straight-forward.  An A is easily attainable with study.  Take him!

Cooper's awesome.  I would highly recommend taking this class.  Just a word of warning to those who try to be first to finish tests: you won't do well in this class.  You MUST be as detailed as possible in your responses.  With that said, if you study hard an "A" is definitely possible in this class.
A very interesting class.  Lots of readings, but they are interesting although some are a bit tedious.  Very good lectures.

Cooper is a pretty good teacher, his class is well organized and is assignments are clear and consistent as are his grading procedures, he is not easy and is somewhat demanding.  He is also fairly serious with the exception of a few inside joke asides, probably not the funniest or most entertaining teacher but not the most boring either.

Great Intstructor.  Has a good sense of humor and keeps the class fun.  There are a lot of readings but you don't really have to do most of them if you go to class everyday and take good notes, highlighting important concepts from authors.  Be very specific on tests.  Not too hard to get a B.  An A would be tough.
It was a good class, you really learn a lot and Prof. Cooper is helpful and an interesting lecturer.  You HAVE to do the readings!  It was challenging but worth it.

Do not take this class if you don't plan on doing all the reading!  That said, Professor Cooper is an excellent lecturer and gives students all the help they need to do well.  BE SPECIFIC WHEN ANSWERING TEST QUESTIONS!
Great professor.  Very interesting lectures.  Just keep up on the assignments, that is what killed my grade a bit.  I always enjoyed coming to class.

This class definently is not a slacker class, but if you put forth the effort you will learn a ton and an A is very possible.  There is a lot of reading, but usually he will go over what he wants you to get out of it the next day in class.  Tests are essay and short answer.  Great lectures! very helpful and nice professor.

Dr. Cooper is a good guy, and keeps good discussion in the class, but I found it hard to pay attention to the discussion or find relevance in it.  This class requires a ton of reading, and quite a bit of writing.  There's no multiple choice on the test, but if you pay attention in class you'll be alright.

Not gonna lie, this class is a lot of work. Lots of reading, lots of assignments, but it's do-able. Lectures are really interesting; don't miss class. Tests are hard and you're rushed, but he gives you detailed study guide and if you study it's not too bad. I recommend this class.

Best Political Science teacher I've ever had.  He's so cute when he talks and you can pay attention during lectures.  Readings are long and hard and tests can be rough (you rush through them in class), but overall, it was a beautiful class.
I loved his class.  I hope to get him again for another class.  He is a good lecturer and as long as you go to class and study your notes you will do fine on the essays.

Prof. Cooper is an AMAZING teacher. His class was thoroughly enjoyable and interesting. He is hoilarious and cares persoanlly about the students. He prepares his students well for exams and tell you what will be on them. However, the exams are somewhat difficult, but duable. He was by fare the best teacher I have had in a long time.

I thought his 170 class was farely easy. He does asign alot of reading but almost always tells you what he wants you to get out of it, so you don't really have to do it but it helps. I liked his tests becuase if you took good notes and reviewed them well they weren't too hard. Although Dr. Cooper is a bigged boned hes a pretty good lookin chap.

Prof. Cooper was awesome!  His lectures were interesting, his tests were straightforward, and the readings were all classic Poli Sci essays...a bit long, but worth it.  I'd highly recommend this class to anyone!  Sit in the front.  Sometimes it's hard to read his writing from the back.

I thought lecture was great, but the readings were long and kind of hard sometimes. He grades tests hard, but also adds a curve which helps. I learned a lot about the subject matter, though. A class worth taking, just be ready for the readings.

I don't know what that first reviewer was thinking!  Professor Cooper is an awesome discussion monitor.  He can parse the value from ANY comment (like a seminary teacher, only in a genuine, good way).  He has a hilarious sense of understated humor.

This guy is kind of crazy.  He gives you way too much reading for an intro level class.  He is very self important, and thinks whatever he says is always right, and he is not even open minded about varying opinions.
He assigns a HUGE ammount of reading, although it all is pertinent to the subject.  He expects a lot, so don't take unless you really want to learn and are interested in the class.

He was a great lab professor. Depending on whether coding is your strong suit or not determines how easy this class is for you, takes time. Probably the least difficult of all junior core classes. Lloyd is amazing though, explains things well and willing to take the time to sit with you and debug and understand code.

Dr. Lloyd is a very caring professor. He is endlessly patient with his students, many times sat with me in lab longer than anyone should have to to help me debug code. Cares a lot and very willing to work with you if you have issues.

Took it Spring; he taught both the lectures and the labs. His exam review sections are very helpful, covering all the most likely missed concepts and details in the exams. He is also super accessible outside of class; you can knock on his office door anytime before 6 pm, and he'll help. 20 people in total; 11 got A, 2 got A-; class avg is 92.75.

He taught the lab portion, and the class is organized very well. The labs can be difficult, but we are told what to do in such a clear manner that they don't feel unmanageable. I already had some C programming experience, so these labs did feel fairly simple for me which may not be everybody's experience. That said, most students got an A in lab.

Scott Lloyd is the ideal engineering professor: highly experienced in the field, and deeply concerned about student progress. Very approachable both in and out of class. The projects can be difficult, but he'll stick around for hours and hours helping students through their issues.

The structure of this class is difficult, so the professor can be the difference between passing and failing. The class starts out as difficult. It is essential to do the readings, these are a huge help in understanding the material. By the time I got to the tests, I was able to perform well on them. This is a passable class, just takes effort.

Had him for ECEN330 as well: very kind and willing to help. He knows a lot, but I feel like it is hard to follow how he solves ECEN problems when he teaches and offers help: also, lectures are a little boring. The classes weren't hard though, and the labs were very interesting. He is a sweet person, and always offers to help (And he knows names :)

In both 390 and 323, Dr. Lloyd is both caring and sympathetic to students. He often stays well into the evening to help students struggling to finish labs. Goes above and beyond to make sure we can make the progress we need to. A genuinely kind individual, and has some good industry experience to back up his teaching too. He's here for the students

The class itself is pretty much just self-guided. His weekly lectures were not super helpful in terms of the class, but good to get some weekly inspiration. Not super helpful in lab sessions, though. Willing to accommodate and work with you, though. I think he would be better with other classes, but struggled with this one due to its unique nature.

This class is hard for the wrong reasons. The questions on homework and the tests are confusing (and sometimes the "correct answers" and just wrong), you only get one chance on the homework so there aren't any second chances, and there's no late policy so if you miss something you just get a 0. This class needs some major restructuring.

I'm not sure why there aren't more reviews here, because the general consensus among ECEn 330 students was largely negative. The lectures felt wholly unnecessary, and the labs were graded based on a coding standard that was ridiculously harsh. There were questions on the exams that not a single student answered correctly, and yet they never curved.

He would spend an hour talking about personal achievements and stories, and then the last 30 minutes would be a quick skim of the homework. His lectures were incredibly boring and most of the students would be on other websites. His tests were ridiculous and, when combined with other Junior Core classes, added way more stress than necessary.

Dr. Lloyd is super great + caring. Spends a bunch of time popping into the lab just to see how we're doing and help us with our code, which you don't get from every professor. His lectures aren't always exciting, but he always starts out with an experience from industry or a cool example of embedded tech, etc. Will def take from him again if I can.

I took ECEN 220 twice from him, (had to drop it the first time cause of life stuff), but both times he was just as consistent and incredible. It was during Covid and he was determined to help us learn despite the grim state of the world. Go to him for help, pay attention, and do the HW. He will help you grasp the EE/CE fundamentals!!

Professor Lloyd is a great guy, teaching a hard class. I took it during COVID, so it was all online, and it was his first time teaching it. It felt like he was still getting the hang of things with the lectures. But, he often stayed after to chat, and was always available for help. Very nice to talk to. He has lots of knowledge and experience.

Lloyd is the nicest professor. His lectures get a little boring at times, but he is always available and excited to help you, even outside of class times. I had trouble with certain concepts and he met with me over zoom for about an hour to help me understand. The class itself is tough, but Lloyd is a good choice because he wants you to succeed.

On the Light and Truth study abroad program, Brother Esplin did an amazing job of hands-on informing and inspiring all of the students. I feel like my testimony grew, and felt that Brother Esplin loved and cared for all of his students.

I took RELC320. Professor Esplin is a very caring person, and he is very passionate about what he teaches. The assignments each week are very simple, and there aren't a lot of them. I would recommend as an easier religion class. Tests were also open book.
Great teacher, good lectures. His only flaw is way too much homework for a 2 credit class. The homework is definitely equal to a 3 credit class, maybe even a little more.

I took the independent study version of this course. While the layout and assignments are fairly easy to follow, the tests are super specific and hard. I would recommend searching up quizlets to help study for the quizzes and exams. Pay attention to every little detail in the readings because it will be on the test.

Note: Grades don't really matter for UNIV as it is a pass/fail class. Professor Esplin is an amazing professor! He structured the class so that we would learn a new resource on campus each day and then have a spiritual lesson. He generally cares for every student and is willing to work through issues of academic or personal matters.

All this professor wants you to do is succeed. He is the sweetest Professor I've had at BYU so far. The class has 4 short reflection papers, 4 elective activities(picked from a list, he also allows you to choose your own if you ask him), a discussion post each time you have class, a final project, and other little assignments sprinkled in. Best one

Loved this professor! My testimony grew when learning about the more difficult topics of Church History because he did such a great job answering our questions and guiding us to sources. I took the blended class so I did a lot of reading but you can for sure succeed and I learned a lot doing my Restoration Project!
Great teacher for religion he really cared about the subject and made it possible for every student to get an A if they worked for it

Loved Esplin. Awesome teacher, take from him if you have the chance. I looked forward to his lecture every week. But the blended class is not the way to go though, 4 hours of homework a week... If you just make sure to follow the learning outcomes you'll be fine for the tests though.

The midterms are insanely difficult, with the given study guides and quizzes only covering about half if less of the content of the questions. Some quiz questions become modified from their original dialogue and require multiple choices to be selected when the original question only asked for one answer, making it impossible to properly prepare.

I took the blended restoration class, thinking that it would be less time-consuming because class is only once/wk and inspirational because it's taught by the dean. PSYCH! He expects you to spend 4+ hrs/wk on hw for a 2 credit class. The readings are useless rehashes of themselves. Class was super dry and he gave few participation opportunities.

Taken as a blended course. Lots to read, but it was all interesting. He does a great job at diving into the "difficult" topics of church history. Very factual, unbiased, and faith promoting lectures. Willing to answer any questions. Pay attention to the learning objectives, the tests are straight from them! Great professor.

Wasn't a fan of the blended course setup. Lectures felt like a speed through as fast as possible of what you read online the week before. The online assignments and readings are long, involving lots of D&C sections and conference talks. By only skimming the readings, I still got an A though. Hope to take an entirely in-person class with Esplin.

Prof. Esplin is genuinely a caring person and wants to help his students. However, the blended nature of this course made it difficult. We met once a week, and there he would reiterate a lot of what we learned in the online modules so it wasn't the most helpful. He really does know his stuff though! He can answer any question you throw his way.

I took the canvas/in person combo and it wasn't my cup of tea. There is a ton of canvas reading, but the quality of lectures and the kindness of Bro Esplin made up for it. The lectures were very informative, but he didn't expect you to remember every date. He just wants you to learn more about the church's history and apply it to your life.

Professor Esplin is so awesome. He talks insanely fast, but he stops often during lectures to make sure everyone's on the same page. His lectures are very faith-promoting and informative, and he never avoided the uncomfortable parts of church history. Really solid and honest professor. Course work isn't bad at all, very fair for a religion class.

Very sweet guy, always willing to answer questions. My class was blended, so we met once a week, but as a result there was a lot of hw for a religion class. A little time consuming, but as long as you follow instructions, you'll be fine.

Followed the basic online restoration course pretty closely but with his own insights in lectures. Had some nice lectures and a great testimony. Some of the weekly work seemed a bit much to me for a 2 credit class but you are going to have the same assignments no matter who you take this class from

I learned so much in this class! This was my first religion class and I really enjoyed it. The homework can be a lot so make sure you don't fall behind! I missed an A- by one question on the final and he didn't give it to me :/
Kind man. Little bit of work when you take the course that is half online.

Absolutely loved this class! I learned so much from Professor Esplin. We talked about difficult topics that are often overlooked in the Church which I really appreciated. Definitely would love to take another class from him in the future.

Professor Esplin is amazing!! He is great at explaining the concepts of the class in a clear and entertaining way (often with examples and stories from his own life). Even though the math part of the class could be challenging (the actual math wasn't hard, there are just a lot of formulas to learn), the class was extremely helpful and fair.

Prof. Esplin was my favorite religion professor. Dude is like a textbook. Ask him anything about that restoration that you're curios about. I went to his office once to ask a doctrinal/historical question and he was so nice. He supplied me with tons of academic resources that I had never read before. Average difficulty for a religion class.

The only issue with his class was the quizzes that you didn't know when they were going to happen. Had ten of them and at least one question always seemed pretty obscure. But, if you do the reading each time before class you'll be good. Tests are easy and straightforward. He trusts his students. He also talks really fast.

A great professor. Very thoughtful and respectful lessons, he was always well prepared and open to any questions anyone asked. He spent a lot of time listening to questions and trying to make sure that they had their questions answered. Loved his class!!

I absolutely loved this class. Brother Esplin is so passionate about church history and can answer any questions you might have. He doesn't shy away from the difficult topics (polygamy, violence in early church history, etc.). He also was super understanding and helpful with accommodations and went out of his way to help me do well in his class.

He is my favorite religion professor. His tests are straight forward, so you just have to know the material and you will do great. He doesn't try to make the class difficult at all but you learn a lot. He stays focused on what matters the most and only tests on what you learned in class. He also doesn't shy away from difficult topics.

Brother Esplin is a wonderful human being. His class changed my life and strengthened my testimony a lot. His in-class quizzes were not difficult if you did the assigned reading (normally 12 D&C sections per class). His exams were also very straightforward and came straight from the reading and class discussion. He is amazing!!!

You can tell he is really passionate about the history of the Church. Very focused lectures and always knows how to crack a few jokes in the middle. He even helped me answer some other deep doctrine questions that weren't even related to the class. Keep up with the reading assignments and take notes and you'll do just fine.

He is a caring man and knows a lot about religion. However, he talks really quickly and tends to skim over material. It was difficult for me to feel the spirit in his class because of the fast pace. The class includes a lot of reading, but it is all interesting material. The tests were difficult because there were SO MANY history questions.

Brother Esplin is a sweet professor and lectures were interesting. That being said I would NOT recommend this class. Tests are HARD and he looks for excruciating details. No personal application or spiritual uplift, just facts and history. Felt like I had to memorize historical background of all 76 sections for the final. NOT AN EASY A!!!!!
He's a great professor, his lectures are amazing and I learned a lot! He's very understanding when you need extra help and is accommodating, and theres lots of reading but not much work.

Quizzes are easy and he prepares you well for tests. His class is pretty much how religion classes should be -- you need to read and be present, but it isn't difficult. Tests were worth 68% of the grade -- 20%/midterm*2 and 28% for the final -- but again, they were very reasonable.
Really good class. He's also extremely clear about what you need to do to get a good grade in the class.

Easiest religion class I have ever taken, but Esplin knows the material very well. I loved his lectures and learning about church history. He explains grading and assignments very well. Very lenient on grading and accommodating to student needs. Complete tests less than 30 mins; class average on tests low 90s.

I felt like he made this class way harder and more boring than it should have been. He's a super sweet dude who loves the subject, but literally nobody cares and I fell asleep in the class more times than I want to admit. Very understanding tho, don't be afraid to ask for extensions or anything like that

Bro. Esplin is such a nice man. The class isn't the most interesting, but it's about as easy as they come. There are reading quizzes once a week, two easy papers, and tests that aren't too difficult. Bro. Esplin really wants students to get the most out of the class, and is accommodating if you have any issues.

Lots of reading quizzes, but if you just do the reading you'll get 100s on all of them. 2 essays, graded fairly. He'll give you study guides for the tests (if you ask), and those are SUPER helpful. Test are very much lecture based, so go! Lectures are amazingly spiritual, while still teaching so much about church history. Take this class!

Quizzes and tests made up most of the grade. However, I really enjoyed taking from him! He was personable, kind, and cared a lot about the students! His lessons were focused more on the doctrine out of the scriptures and I feel like I learned a lot!

Brother Esplin is an amazing professor! Get ready for some in depth assignments but if you study and work hard, you'll pass with a great grade! He truly knows his stuff, ask anything and he knows the answer with a bunch of references to back his answers,
I loved this class. Prof. Esplin is one of my favorite Religion professors. If you show up and pay attention you should be fine. Great class

Dr. Esplin is the real deal. He is one of the cutest professors on campus, hands down. Never even had to read the scriptures in his class and i squeaked by with a 72%. Totally recommend the class to all RMs who don't want to study the gospel.... if you know what I mean. ;)
Very dedicated and willing to work with his struggling students. Approachable and inspirational.
Brother Esplin changed the Doctrine & Covenants for me. This is one of my favorite religion classes I've ever taken.

I've completed the required religion credits and looking back over all the religion professors I had, Brother Esplin was honestly one of the best. He teaches out of sincerity and you definitely walk out of class feeling uplifted. He told awesome stories and applied the scriptures to each of us personally.

Honestly this class was not my favorite,  Professor esplin is a nice guy, just he does not teach that good.  He was all over the place, and ask questions in class and no one would know what he was talking about.  His tests are absolutely dumb. He tests you on worthless facts and on the correct wording of verses. I learned nothing from him.

Brother Esplin is by far my favorite religion professor at BYU.  He is down to earth and definitely relatable.  You do have to work for your grade.  There is a quiz every class and some of the test questions can be challenging.  The work is well worth it.  If you are looking to really gain something from your religion class then Esplin is the guy.

Esplin understand what a religion class should look like at BYU. I learned so much but this class didn't take too much effort outside of class besides reading the D&C. He is funny, kind and insightful. I would definitely recommend Esplin!

I guess this class has changed. 1/3 of the class failed his midterm, and his study guides are vague/useless. He's a wonderful person, very understanding if you need to miss class, but tests are ridiculous. His midterm was the lowest grade I've ever received on a test in 4 years of college. Pick his brain, talk to him, but don't take his class.

He's the best! I learned so much in this class. I felt like I learned new things about the history that really helped, but more importantly I learned more about the doctrine in D&C, it was so great. He really cares about his students, and wants everyone to have their questions answered, and to do well. BEST.

Take Brother Esplin's class! I loved him. He has a love for the Doctrine & Covenants and is an excellent teacher. He is funny, and his lectures are always interesting. He grades easily and there is enough easy homework to boost your grade. If you attend class and listen, he will tell you lots of test answers. Study for the tests, though!!

Brother Esplin is seriously THE BEST religion teacher I have ever encountered. He truly knows the material and loves what he does. He helps you succeed, understands that we are busy college students, and really brings the spirit to take. TAKE FROM ESPLIN!!!

Stellar! Knows what he is talking about. He is a motor mouth but has funny stories and insights to share. Tests are not bad at all, just really go through the study guide and listen to his obvious clues in class. Pop quizzes every week and only three tests. Weekly journal entries and some readings that aren't that helpful. TAKE FROM ESPLIN!

Esplin is such a great professor! He knows the D&C like the back of his hand and really wants his students to do well. No useless memorization or busy work, just learning the history and stories in the book. He truly wants you to do well and is very understanding of student's crazy lives. Go to class, read and take notes, and you're good to go!!

My favorite religion professor at BYU. No busy work, but tests do test your knowledge (got around 90% on all three with about 2.5 hours studying for each). Fun, intelligent, helpful, caring, positive, spiritual.
Im a Junior @ BYU and he hands down has been my favorite professor in every aspect. Loved the class. Wish he taught more classes. I recommend him to everyone!

Brother Esplin is a nice guy, but I wasn't in love with his class. Even though there isn't a ton of homework, the tests are pretty hard and I spent tons of time studying for them, but got the worst grade of my semester in his class.

My problem with this class is that instead of testing on doctrine he tested on facts ONLY (names, dates, etc.). It made reading the scriptures feel like homework. Although he's a very nice person and had some good lecture material, I got very little out of his class spiritually.

Brother Esplin is great! The class isn't too hard at all, the tests are really straight-forward (as long as you went to class and know the study guides). He is really helpful and very personable and real. He really implemented the suggestions students had from the mid-course evaluation. Great combination of spiritual and academic knowledge of D&C.

I loved Brother Esplin! He has a clear passion for the D&C and was able to share it very effectively. Class isn't too hard, just stay caught up on readings, study the study guide that he gives you, pay attention to when he says "If I asked you this on a test..." because those questions are always on the exam! Very good teacher.

I love Brother Esplin! I was unsure about taking the second half of the old testament but he made it come alive for me. I was excited to go to every class. All you have to do to get an A is attend every class, work through each study guide he gives you for exams and final (very easy), read before class and write two short essays. I learned a ton!
Bro. Esplin is an excellent teacher, answers questions respectfully and brings the Spirit into every lesson. Is a very captivating teacher. Highly recommended!
Excellent class.  Brother Esplin really cares about his students.  Tests are somewhat challenging, but I'd definitely recommend Bro Esplin.
Take D&C from him if you can! I loved coming to class and I learned so much about the D&C. He's very kind and willing to work with you on anything. It wasn't a hard class, but I still learned tons!

Highly recommended!  Not a difficult class but I still felt like I learned a lot.  Very much enjoyed class periods. Course entails weekly readings/journal entries, 1 short paper (analyze one section), 2 tests and the final, all multiple choice. Excellent at leading and encouraging discussions.  Full of interesting stories, relates doctrine to us.

Brother Esplin genuinely cares about his students. He will make himself available to you. He actually understands that this class won't be your top priority in life, and he knows how to teach the subject to college students. He tells you a lot of the exam questions in class if you just go. The class quizzes are once a week and are pretty easy.

Great teacher. I really learned a lot in this class.  Discussions were well organized but he wasn't afraid to stray from them to answer questions or go into more detail.  Tests weren't too difficult-though there were some questions about specific details-all multiple choice.

he's a good professor. Tests had mostly easy questions but some q's felt like random details. I was surprised by how high test avg's were. This class didn't exactly rock my world but it was still good.

Brother Esplin is the best religion professor I have had thus far in my BYU experience. Attendance is mandatory (but it should be, shouldn't it?). You'll learn the history behind D&C, giving context to the revelations. Your testimony will be strengthened. You'll feel the Spirit without having it spoon-fed like in Seminary or EFY. Highly recommended

Old Testament.  Easiest religion course I've ever taken.  Attendance is mandatory and easy quizzes are given in class. No homework aside from reading and a journal entry once a week.  2 tests and a final with a very high class average (90ish).  Nice guy and respectful of opinions different from his own, which is unique in the religion department.

I learned a lot in Esplin's class. He is way fun, engaging, and knows a lot. However, I struggled on his tests. I did the work I was supposed to and studied, but it felt like there was a lot of material not covered in class.

Brother Esplin is an excellent teacher. He really cares about the students and will take time to help you understand whatever is unclear to you. He tells you ahead of time what will be on the tests and really helps prepare you for them. He teaches both the history and doctrine, as both are important. I would recommend him to anyone.

He might think he know a lot about the D&C but in reality his main focus for the class is on the dates and time. His test are a lot harder than they need to be. To one class he said, "I hope some student fail so that I can give more A's." Obviously cares more about his teacher tenure than his students.

He's the best! Teaches interesting doctrine, not the kind of teacher who makes you memorize useless dates and facts about church history. It sounds cheesy - but I loved the spirit he brought to class. Awesome quotes and stories. Take him if you can for D&C

Brother Esplin Rocks!!  He's such an awesome, nice guy who truly cares that all of his students should understand the material.  If you're taking a religion, and you can get him, do it!  He's pretty easy with the quizzes as long as you've done the reading, but study hard for the tests with the review he gives you!

first time teaching NT in a long time. still quite knowledgeable. I feel like I learned a lot and I enjoyed going to class. 4 papers and 3 tests (summer term), very fair. stays after to answer questions. I liked him. didn't love him for a few reasons (repeats himself a ton, a little hyperactive, sometimes a pushover) but I don't regret taking class

I loved brother esplin class.  His lectures were very engaging, does not he uses a powerpoint, but mostly for quotes and does not rush through the class period to get through every single powerpoint, test easy if go to class, one 5 page paper, but he is a fair grader and it is very eas, take him, he is the best!!!

Super Easy! I love this guy! You have a five page paper (but it's really easy). You also have about 10 quizzes over the course of the semester... so do the reading. Tests are easy if you just go to class (but if you study in the least bit you're guaranteeing yourself an A or A-).

Brother Esplin is amazing. The end. Hands down my favorite class all semester. Very straightforward, very well-read, and a very fair grader, I always feel good after his class. He has a story for everything and knows how to blend humor and spirituality. Take this class!

He is one of my favorate religion teachers. His lectures and very interesting, and his tests are very straightforward,If you go to class, and study your notes you will do fine, loved his class, he is the best

He's a GREAT teacher. Loves what he's teaching and class is always a pleasure. I love that he doesn't teach from his slide show at all. Most interesting and engaging lectures I've ever had.  Also, his tests are very straightforward. He tells you what will be on them and what to study. Only one essay.  GET HIM if you can.
his class is amazing.  if you go to class and take good notes and study them you will do fine.  he is one of my favorate religion teachers at byu so far. take his class you won't regret it.

I enjoyed the lectures, and brother esplin is a good guy, but the tests were harder than they needed to be.  he asks about a lot of specifics that you will never need or want to know unless you plan on teaching religion.  the easiness rating for this professor is deceptively high.

Amazing teacher and amazing man. Awesome guy with high character and very humble. You can tell he truly loves what he teaches. I wouldn't call this class easy, you should study relatively hard, but every lecture he gave was very uplifting and enlightening.

Brother Esplin was one of the most amazing teachers I have had at BYU. I looked forward to going to his class every day.  He knows so much about D&C and he makes everything interesting and clear.  His tests are not hard at all if you go to class and use the study guide he gives.  Take D&C from him if you can-he is incredible and I'll miss his class

Took him Spring 2009. This guy has nailed how a religion class should be-- no giant packet, just interesting, applicable talks.  Easy, intriguing, spiritual assignments.  Understands what it's like to be a college student!  Only some of his tests had questions that were out of the blue, but I always got A's anyways.
Best religion professor I have ever had. Amazing teacher- spirit filled classes without any fake crying! He really is the sincerest and best professor I have ever had.

Easy class. Takes no critical thought, as the assignments are very simple and the exams just test on how well you payed attention and took notes in class. I feel like I learned some interesting random factoids about church history but that's about it. Class would probably be better if the professor required some actual writing/thinking on exams.

He is a GREAT teacher and the biggest sweetheart. if you come up to ask him for almost anything he will help you out. it is an easy A and there is one presentation but it is no big deal at all. one thought paper where everyone gets a 100% if you follow the guide lines. I learned so much and he makes the class very interesting. TAKE HIM!

I ABSOLUTELY LOVED this class and Brother Esplin.  Every class period is so interesting and although class is mandatory I always found myself wanting to go.  The tests are simple and fair and as long as you pay attention in class you will do great.  I would take any class from Esplin...he is FANTASTIC :-)
The best teacher and class, period!!!

Brother Esplin was a very fair teacher. His class was designed for everyone to get at least a B, without taking up a ton of time. His lectures were fascinating and he was always willing to take extra time to help his students.

great guy and all that jazz (he really is awesome) Issues: no possibility for EC.  94% A. So basically don't mess up on anything.  It's really not that hard though.  My only complaints is that he talks super fast.  i can't blame him though, he knows everything EVER about the D and C.

Incredible, incredible man!  I loved this class, and Brother Esplin's style.  He taught with the spirit, had minimal homework and never gave us busy work.  His exams, and the class overall, was very easy if you actually went to class and paid attention--which wasn't hard to do because his lectures were always great!

Brother Esplin is an amazing teacher.  Being in his class is uplifting, I feel so enriched after every lesson.  I learned more in his brief summary of the 1st half of the D&C then I did in my whole class devoted to that subject.  He's great, you should take his class.
Best religion teacher on campus! I loved the class and learned a ton. I would recommend Prof. Esplin for anyone to take. But sign up quick because his classes are always the first to fill up.
Brother Esplin is such a good teacher! I learned so much and it wasn't even hard. I had never really appreciated the Doctrine and Covenants before, but I do now! I strongly recommend Brother Esplin.

I don't want to say anything negative about other teachers, but brother Esplin is definetely the best religion professor at BYU. He is very knowlegable, he has the spirit in his class, and what's the most important thing - he truly cares of students.  I enjoyed the class very much and highly recommend it to everyone.

Great religion teacher. Does not teach his own opinions (or makes it very clear when he presents his own ideas, and does not hold you to them). Tests are multiple choice, based on objective historical background and what is actually in the text (again, not his opinion). Before each test, he gives out a study guide and goes over the material.

Brother Esplin knows the D&C SO well!  He knows the doctrine so well and answers all of the random questions that people throw at him and has quotes and scriptures off the wazoo to back him up!  He's also a very straight forward teacher and will tell you exactly what's on the tests- word for word sometimes.  You get graded on doing the daily readin

Professor Esplin is a great man who dilligently prepares and teaches to the best of his ability.  He truly cares about the needs of the students; sometimes he gets off on random stories, but they make the class interesting and lets just say that nothing can be predictable. I enjoy the spirit felt also.
Amazing teacher!  He's a great guy and really cares about the students and wants them to succeed outside of class as well.

One thing that I have to mention in giving a review of Bro. Esplin, is that he is the most concerned and helpful teacher that I've ever had at BYU.  He goes over the test as a whole class after and any questions that you have, he will answer them. He is concerned about individuals and tries to provide a spiritual environment. GREAT GUY AND TEACHER!

Great Doctrine and Covenants teacher. Have 3 exams throughout the semester and one small project where you basically gather information on 1 section and tell the class about it on the day you cover that section. He really knows what he's talking about and is a great teacher covering both history and doctrine. Love the class would take again.

Bro. Esplin is the man! He is a genius when it comes to church history and the Doctrine and Covenants. He brings amazing insights into every class and applies them to us. He is the best religion professor I've had at BYU! Take him!

Absolutely amazing teacher.  He really tries to demonstrate the applicability D&C has to us right now.  Very friendly and helpful.  Study guides are perfect outlines for the test.  Take this teacher you will learn so much!
Scott Esplin is awesome and he loves what he is teaching which makes it so enjoyable.  He is funny and gets really excited while teaching.  You should definately enroll in his class.
Brother Esplin is such an amazing professor! I learned a lot from his class, but his tests are semi-hard. Otherwise it is a really enjoyable class that I loved a lot!

Easy class as long as you went, did the readings and took the quizzes. Requires a weekly journal that is EASY points.  Tests were semi hard and he doesn't make them easy. When 1/2 of our class had A's on the first test, he purposely made the next two harder. Good teacher, easy assignments, don't worry.

Bro Esplin is great. He class is really easy. The quizes basically just see if you did the reading, no tough details. Very few assignments, two midterms and a final. He gives study guides that are pretty good for the tests. His class is pretty good, He gives a lot of history but keeps it spiritual as well.

I learned a lot from Brother Esplin and plan on taking the 2nd half of D&C from him as well.  It was an easy class overall, but I really liked his style of teaching.  Short quiz every class (I had him once a week), just do the reading.  Also a one page essay, two midterms, and a final.
The class is really easy.  Quizzes are based on if you read or not.  His lectures are a little boring and he talks really fast and rambles on.  A lot more history than doctrine.

I love this man!  He is incredibly knowledgable but is still so humble.  He's downright hilarious, but doesn't let that detract from the Spirit.  He focuses on how the doctrine of the D&C can help us, which is nice.  He really wants to help his students, too, so if you're having any trouble (in or out of class) just go talk to him!  He's fantastic!

He's is a good teacher. I had the night class and he made the quizzes really easy because he was worried that we weren't doing well. He was also really good about giving a study guide that acutally was helpful for the test. He was respectful when people in class asked dumb questions or made useless comments. If you can get in his class, do it.
Show up to class, it's worth your time. Bro Esplin is really in tune with the spirit and has a genuine interest in making sure his students are succeeding in his class.
Easiest class ever.  This is a religion class that won't hurt your GPA. Take him if his section is open.

Brother Esplin is a fabulous professor!  He is great at applying principles from the scriptures to our lives, and teaching us to do the same.  The tests and pop quizzes are pretty easy if you do the reading.

Excellent individual and excellent teacher. An A is possible, but you'll have to work for it unless you're already very familiar with D&C. Don't expect to walk through the class easily, you can't. I do highly recommend him and his class.

Bro. Esplin is great! He is like a great fountain of knowledge, and even humble about it! Very respectful and if you ask a question (even if you think it might be a dumb one) he will always make it seem valid and answer as best as he can. I really look up to him as a person and teacher.

This professor is more than great, he is wonderful!  He goes out of the way to make sure that you understand. He also knows his scriptures, plus he can randomly recite church stories that relate to what he is teaching or whatever you ask of him.  Great teacher I highly recommend him! Tests are pretty easy and quizes are nothing to worry about.
AMAZING!! loved the class! esplin is very interested in his students and helps them any way he can. quizzes was a piece of cake.  doctrine and application was very insightful! take from him for sure!
Wonderful teacher! Really helps you apply the scriptures to your life. If you do the reading at all you'll be fine on all of the in class quizzes. Not a tough class, definitely worth taking!

Fantastic teacher.  He makes it very clear what is on his tests, and the only other thing you need to do is an in-class presentation which really isn't much of a presentation at all.  This is an easy course.  Not hard to get an A

I really enjoyed this class! Esplin is a good lecturer and I learned a lot. The random quizzes were easy, but the tests were sometimes difficult. You know how vague the wording of questions from D&C tests can get!
Just remember to do your reading for the random quizzes. If you take notes  on each section, person, and place at the exam review session and study the section names then you will ace the exam.

Very good teacher.  Balances the church history with the teachings of the Doctrine and Covenants.  Is very knowledgable and willing to help.  Has a great sense of humor.  The only downside is many times we skim through sections and don't really hit on doctrines.  More information than spirituality.  I would take any class from him.
Excellent teacher...very exciting

Class is all history, no doctrine.  Tests are a cinch, quizzes are simple.  Wouldn't reccomend Esplin if you prefer getting new or more info in class, if you prefer a spiritual class, or if you get bored by countless historical facts. You can definitely tell he just came from being a seminary teacher.

Best religion professor that I have ever had. He cares about his students, and has a great balance of history and doctrine. Grading is very fair. He tries to apply the D&C to college life and does a great job at it. If you're looking for a great D&C professor, Brother Esplin is the man.
