Professor Rackham is a great guy. He really wants people to succeed but he also holds each student responsible. You are required to know the material and do the readings on your own. I liked lectures cause he shared personal examples that applied well to the material and helped to solidify concepts. The test were ok but get ready to memorize.
Honestly, a Great professor. He was fair in his grading, and his lectures were very interesting.

Prof Rackham is a great guy, he ties in a lot of cool stories from his business that make the concepts you are learning in class real. I took the online blended version where we met once a week. Honestly not very hard and very chill. Never really stressed about this class and enjoyed learning what was taught.

Rackham is awesome. He knows what he's doing and makes arguably the most boring textbook interesting. Concepts are taught really well and if you pay attention you'll be good. The class workload was manageable and consistent. You'll be just fine if you put in the work. Tests aren't too difficult either. Take from Rackham!

His lecture style is opening the online textbook and reading through it while telling unrelated personal stories. It felt pointless to read outside of class only to have him read it again anyway in class. He wants and makes sure to keep class test scores low. I learned his life story and how rich he is, and I'm not interested in marketing anymore.

I enjoyed Professor Rakham in his marketing 201 class. This class is inherently difficult in that it takes a lot of memorizing. That said, Rakham and the TA's are abundantly clear on what to learn. Being an adjunct professor, I love the real-world examples he brings into everything. I also love the way he sets up the homework in Canvas. Very clear.

Professor Rackham was a fantastic lecturer. I found his class very engaging and entertaining. I heard some rough things about Marketing, but I quite liked his class. Tests were memorization heavy. TAs were phenomenal. There were some funny things the exams, but he ended up working out the kinks.

Professor Rackham is the best!! He is super understanding and helpful. Has a ton of experience not only in Marketing but also in Advertising, so you get a lot of perspective. A lot of assignments but none that are impossible to complete. 10/10
Loved this class and professor so much I applied to be a TA for him!

I really struggled with this class. He included concepts on the test that were never covered in class or in TA reviews. I studied super hard for his tests and luckily knew the material from the readings. This is the first time at BYU where I felt like I had a professor who wanted me to do bad in his class. You have to memorize a lot and study hard.

Truly, don't take this class if you're not passionate about or serious about marketing. So much reading and so many random, meaningless assignments. Trust me. If you don't care about marketing, like I don't, literally take any other class. This one is NOT worth your time. It's not a hard class, just extremely boring if you're not interested.

Professor Rackham was a great professor. Hilarious. Not a hard class, I enjoyed the content we learned. I took the blended/half online class. So there was an online textbook and online modules. Lectures were available in person, on zoom, or recorded to watch later. Very flexible!!! Exams weren't too hard; study with flashcards and you'll do fine.

Bro is like if Hank Schrader became a marketing professor instead of a DEA agent. He made boring marketing material bearable. He's got this sales bro ta named kj that holds exam reviews and those things lowkey saved me.

Professor Rackham was awesome! One of my favorite classes. He's funny & makes the class applicable to real life. Classwork is very straightforward. Tests require reading through the textbook, but the concepts are emphasized in the assignments and TA reviews. Attendance not mandatory but you had to watch the recording of the class if you didn't go.

I don't know why he's rated so low on here. Looking at he reviews, the majority of the 1 stars are a bit bitter that they got a low grade. He's a pretty good teacher and his lectures are what really makes the class so interesting. The exams are a bit tough though. You really do have to study like crazy to get a good grade

I had him for MKTG 403; he is awesome! Sometimes I felt like the Junior Core was too hard for me, but his teaching style is easy to understand and meaningful. His class always made me feel confident again. I am so grateful that he was our teacher. For the person who rated him because of the "hard quiz", all marketing 201 have hard quizzes bro.

I had him for MKTG 403 not 201, but that wasn't an option. Bro. Rackham is a great guy. He was engaging and really caring. I appreciated his light-hearted personality and that he really wanted to see each of us succeed. He brought us the tastiest energy drink I've ever had from his company. He and the TA were awesome and class was super enjoyable.

Look it isn't a walk in the park, but if you're wanting one don't go into business school because it's tough. Rackham's class prepared me well for the junior core. Be familiar with all the information, be intentional with your reading and you'll be prepared for the exams. Rackham's lectures are great and his experience adds a lot to the material

Rackham is great and he has a passion for what he teaches. It's a lot of homework but interesting. The online structure was great and organized. The tests were a bit unfair because we were tested on small, unnecessary details from one line in the textbook. It was frustrating because, of course, no one can remember minute, one-word details.

The professor and his TAs I found to be easy to get ahold of, that wasn't an issue. Overall the online portion is pretty well organized as well. 

The biggest issues are the tests. I've never had a test be so specific to an entire textbook and if you don't have everything from the lessons memorized--LITERALLY--then you are in for it.

The class only meets once a week, but I liked it even though I don't like blended courses. Lots of busy-work assignments that he encourages you to use ChatGPT on. He claims only the top ones get full points, but they're pretty much participation. He doesn't write the tests, so sometimes there will be information he didn't cover. But he's fun.

TERRIBLE! TAs and professor are completely non-responsive. Absolutely no late-work. Extremely disorganized and due dates are always wrong. The slides he uses for reviews are from 4 years ago and completely irrelevant to exams. He tests you on material he has never talked about. Also he doesn't plan lectures, he just skims through the textbook.

Great class. I took it online. Weekly assignments are pretty easy and he tells you to use Chat GPT. Pretty awesome. I loved the content, the professor, the assignments, honestly they were fun and I learned a lot. The part that is hard and sucks - are the 2 midterms and final. I got all B's on the exams but did the assignments with all A's. 94+ is A

The expectations in Professor Rackham's class are clear and the workload is not heavy. The tests really aren't that hard, if you know all the vocabulary from the textbook they're a breeze. I don't know why so many people complain about this class.

This class was extremely exam heavy in terms of weight. A 94 is the threshold needed for an A and there was no final curve at the end of the term so you basically needed to average close to that on the exams (which were vague and often unrelated to course content). To top it all off, the professor never answered any emails. Take from someone else.

I was a straight-A student till this class, and I am already a senior. This class requires a 94 for A, and the exam is tough because it comes from very detailed things in the textbook. I have every single assignment as full points, and I still didn't get A even with more than 30 hours of studying. This is ridiculous.

Professor Rackham's class isn't terrible hard. The biggest downfall is that you have so much busy work and are required to write multiple papers every week. The test is pretty vague for how many points it's worth as well. Not too difficult of a class, just learn very little and have lots of homework.
Literally worst class ever, TAs are mean, never replied to the messages and graded AI essays very harshly even though chatgpt did a great job

Professor Rackham never replies to any message and email. The lecture is heavy and pointless which makes people hate their lives. Projects and Homework are graded harshly, TA are very arbitrary ,give you a 60 even though you put 100% of efforts. The assignment is redundant and not elucidating. If you want a nice drop on your GPA, take it from him

Hybrid class so lectures were only once a week, with the online portion being structured so you knew exactly what you would need to do each week. Prof. Rackham is an actual marketer so it was very insightful to get his perspective, and lectures were more focused on real world application. Only complaint is the TA exam reviews were not very helpful.

He was cool until the last second. Calculators weren't allowed in our exam in the testing center even though they were supposed to be to calculate certain equations... I emailed him after the test about it. No response. Emailed him again. No response. Cool guy, knows a lot about marketing, but I don't think he knows how to be a teacher.

Professor Rackham is a great technical marketer; however, his class is very test heavy and the exam material never seemed straightforward to class/textbook material. He's extremely hard to get in contact with unless you catch him after class. The TA's and himself were never on the same page, and important class info wasn't communicated properly.

Fairly straightforward class. You meet once a week in person but with an online option. You know exactly what you're going to have to do each week. Not overwhelming if you stay on top of assignments. Tests are in testing center but if you study you should do alright on them. TAs do test reviews but are pretty unresponsive if you reach out to them.

The class is fairly interesting, but as a hybrid course, the main source of content that students are expected to learn is the textbook. The textbook, "Marketing Fundamentals" by Swenson, Whitlark, and Rhoads, is absolutely awful. It's an online textbook written by BYU professors that is very unprofessional and imprecise.

All of the materials are horribly outdated. Many of the materials are from the early 2000's(I was born around this time). Considering that this is a MARKETING class, even though he'd say the principle doesn't change, I can say the course owner has been quite lazy. It's just so discouraging to learn things from decades old, often insensitive videos.

Rackham is the absolute best! I'm not a fan of the business school in general, so I was glad to have a caring and fun professor like him. He does well to prepare you for tests, and he's very reasonable as long as you communicate well and in advance. If you get the chance, take from him

SOO glad I took marketing from him. Super easy, took it online in spring. Informative, clear expectations, study guides for exams that made them easy. Really intuitive material. Only thing is you have to memorize a bunch of random stuff for tests, but it's all on the study guides if you fill them out as you go, you're golden.

SO MUCH BUSY WORK. TA's were unhelpful. The tests were impossible no matter how hard I studied. I got better grades in Accounting, physical science, stats, biology, etc. This class should have been easier but there was no structure or help.
Professor Rackham is great! Youll have to rely on the textbook but if you do youll do fine in the class.

So much busy work. I hated this class. Unorganized, TA's will dock you points just because they can, BUSY WORK BUSY WORK BUSY WORK BUSY WORK BUSY WORK BUSY WORK BUSY WORK BUSY WORK BUSY WORK. The teacher is pretty cool though. Don't get me started on the busy work though. Get ready for a week full of meaningless busy work assignments.

Prof. Rackham loves to talk about how he isn't a teacher... Which is obvious in his lack of organization, horrible communication skills, and disregard for his students. He talks about himself (a lot) so his experience seems relevant, but is not aligned with the exam content. TA's did nothing and Canvas was a mess. Expect busy work assignments.

makes his tests way too hard. most of the class is just busy work and does not prepare you for his tests. there are easier teachers for this class. The Ta's were also a joke and it was very disorganized. weekly work was not too hard but it really just didn't have much of a point. no extra credit.

Although the canvas set up was all over the place, I really enjoyed Prof Rackham's class. His stories and lectures are awesome and help you understand the concepts in a real sense. There are 2 midterms and 1 final, all MC, and weekly assignments that are all due on Sat. Definitely enjoyed this class more than I thought I would.
The class is fine, the professor it fine. Nothing negative to say. The professor has good real world experience and decent lectures, but it pretty disorganized in the course.

The course online was pretty messy and a lot was unorganized. TA's might grade your assignments hard. The class was pretty easy though. The class is mostly based on your test grade, and the tests are confusing and in the testing center. I didn't really like the class and was planning to major in marketing but it changed my mind. Lots of memorizing.

Scott gives valuable real world advice, but his teaching is very limited. The course is set up to be very dependent on 3 exams, the questions of which are not written by him, making it difficult to study from lecture notes. The class consistently scored about a 10% lower average than the rest of the department.

Scott is a very experienced professional in the marketing field. As an adjunct professor he has lots of real world experience. You will learn a lot of very applicable lessons in his lectures and the textbook is pretty easy to follow. Highly recommend even if you're not planning on majoring in marketing.

All the reading and videos were done outside of class. Class time was mostly Q&A and discussion. Scott used a lot of real-world examples and was very good at explaining the concepts. Not super hard, just stay on top of things.

Scott is super funny and very relatable. He loves to connect with his students and makes you feel valuable. The class isn't too hard and very doable; just do the homework and you'll be fine! Make sure you understand the concepts and you'll have a great time and learn a lot.

Took MKGT 201 with Professor Rackham in his new class design through Canvas. A lot of homework every week but those are easy and TAs are not tough graders if you follow the prompt. Tests are the usual difficult and if you study for it you can do well. Weekly webinars over zoom were great.

Professor Rackham clearly has a great resume and real world experience. However, he uses material from another professor that he doesn't always seem to know. At times you will feel disadvantaged in his class. To be fair, this was his first time teaching the class.

Hands down the best professor I've ever had. He's an amazing speaker and has a natural talent in connecting with people and explaining topics. Unlike some other professors, actually does marketing for several companies outside of BYU. The man really knows his stuff.
He's a good guy. Classic marketer
Professor Rackham has a lot of insights to offer about marketing and he made the class really interesting! I feel like he applied it to a lot of real world situations and it was great!

Professor Rackham's class was one of my favorites. He didn't make the class unnecessarily difficult, and he taught the material in a way that made it interesting. He is a funny guy who used lots of real-world examples.

The dude is amazing. Took his poverty class and it made me want to minor in sociology. Truly cares about his students and really puts in the work. Lowkey he felt like a dad who stepped up when the other dad couldn't.

Wish he was my neighbor or something. Scott is awesome, the class covers really interesting topics, and it's easy to get an A. Really makes you care about poverty, and he tries his best to be funny. Literally the best.

One of the best professors I've had. He loves to engage with his students and is very caring. He is the reason why I'm pursuing a sociology minor! Definitely take him for your class if you want to increase your understandings about the world.

Scott is the best. I even considered switching to being a sociology major just so I could take more classes from him. He's caring, understanding, and is very student-oriented. I could tell that he cares a ton about his students' success in all aspects of their lives.
the best dude
Scott is literally so amazing! He is so funny and is an awesome teacher. If you are taking univ take it from Scott you won't regret it!!
I love Professor Sanders. Probably my favorite that I have ever had. He cares a lot and I can tell he loves what he does. If you ever have the opportunity to take a class from him, do it!

Genuinely one of the nicest guys you will ever meet. He is so ready to help you with whatever you need in any capacity and is so understanding. He is a professor I hope to stay connected to for life. Definitely take a class from him if you can!

Scott is a stud! I took UNIV101: BYU Foundations from him summer semester. Scott loves his job and wants to see you succeed. He has a strong testimony and loves to connect things to the gospel. He is super easy to talk to and makes you feel like the most important person in the room. When you take UNIV101 take it from Scott!

The best, most chill, kindest, most focused on genuine change and inspiring you to be better professor ever. I would honestly take a bullet for this guy. Also one of the easiest classes I have ever taken (IAS 220), but I still learned a lot.

Super awesome guy! Really engaging lectures that are always interesting! Midterm and final are pretty easy/straightforward and he isn't a tough grader. 2-page report due every week but it is just your thoughts on the topic and is basically graded on completion. You won't regret this class!

One of the best professors ever! Sweet, respectful, great at addressing some of the delicate topics we covered. Graded mostly on 2 page reports done after some of the readings, one midterm/one final, and a final paper (12 pages). Not a ridiculous amount of work, and I feel like I was able to get more out of it because of that.
BEST CLASS EVER! literally one of my favorite professors by far. zero complaints. so doable and just a person you want to know.  Met with him outside of class too to plan career goals!

Sign up for the class. Scott is a really cool guy who has a very unique perspective on development. He has good experience and knows what he's talking about and is super willing to help students if they ask. Sometimes he comes off a little cold, but he really is a great professor. I wish the class was a little more rigorous, but he does a good job.

Scott is so inspirational and I loved the content of the class. It wasnt organized very well though and it often made it hard to know when things were do and what to do on assignments. He cares a lot about his students but also expects a lot from them. Pay very close attention in class or you wont know whats going on

Favorite professor of all time. Never met someone so caring and respectful of their students. Lectures are totally eye-opening. I think everyone should take this class regardless of their major! Tests are essay questions which I struggled with a bit, but he's super accommodating and grades fairly. Wish he taught more classes, I would take them all!
Learned so much! He is the best! TAKE THIS CLASS!

One of the best. He articulates the course material very well. Knows his stuff but does not come off as imposing or intimidating; a very down to earth person! He provides various resources (readings, videos, etc) to understand the material. / EC given, VERY willing to help, 12 pg final paper, no exams only written assessments. Very insightful class

Scott is hilarious and I learned so much from every class period. He is very passionate about int. development. There is one midterm and a final. The term paper is probably the hardest part of the class - it's a minimum of 12 pages but you choose the topic. I would say it's easy to get a good grade if you put in the work.

Scott is a great teacher and knows the subject matter very well. He is great at opening the class up into discussions on salient topics and inviting everyone to participate. I learned a lot about development and social problems and the information is still really applicable to my other courses. This was a great class and I really enjoyed it!

Scott is a great professor. He is a bit intimidating but is actually very open with his students. His lectures were very informative and interesting. I learned so much about international development and the problems in the world. He encourages discussion and you will get more out of the class if you make comments. He really knows his stuff!

Great class, and professor. Starts class with a joke, then gets right into the material. Engaging, encourages participation, wants students to learn and apply. Willing to help or just talk about anything. Knows his stuff and passionate about sharing it. I learned so much and would take another class from him. Fair grader, appropriate work load.
Love him. He knows his stuff and really wants you to succeed
I loved how much he cared about me. The course was good and he was awesome.

Professor Summers is caring and wants the best for his students! Some aspects of Data Analytics are a little unfamiliar and wasn't maybe taught in the best way possible, but I still enjoyed the analytics softwares we learned and the skills that this class taught me!

407 was new this year and should just be combined with 401. Some of the hw prep took 30mins, other days it took like 4hrs. There was no class, we'd meet on zoom for 20 min where he shared something irrelevant to the class, then we work on the assignment due by 8pm that day. Learned some cool stuff, but also was annoyed at the structure of the class

I have a feeling he's a lot better AIS professor than Data Analytics. He didn't know what was going on in this class and was not helpful, but that's also kind of the design of the class - you teach yourself. The group projects are brutal and the classwork takes a lot longer than it should. The tests are the easiest of all the junior core classes.

Always available outside of class. Lectures are great--real world and applicable! Exams are hardest I've ever had--all about rote memorization. Make sure you memorize every line in the textbook or you will not do well. Seriously--every. tiny. line. Note: practice exams are nothing like the real exams.

Dr. Summers is wild. He loves to make jokes and have fun, and he definitely makes class exciting. AIS can get complicated, but Summers is always able to make it understandable and doable. If you need to meet him outside of class to talk about a project or anything he is always available as well. Absolutely loved taking this class from him.
This class is just an intro to nursing, but I liked the way Scott outlined the class. It was super informative and he was eager to answer any questions we had about the BYU nursing program.
Material can be very dull, but he is hilarious to the point where his jokes help you remember things easier.

Summers is an all-around awesome teacher. He speaks slowly and clearly. Class is so enlightening because he spends time working through scenarios and situations that come back for exams. Coursework is tough, especially if you aren't IS savvy. That being said, his amiable personality and clarity made this class enjoyable.
Great teacher! Speaks to you like you're a little kid, but makes everything easy to understand.

great teacher! systems is the most boring thing on earth, but Prof. Summers will make it fun and his real life examples help you understand all the complexities. Read the chapter carefully! Exams are very especific, quizzes not that hard.

He was given the unfortunate break of teaching a crappy subject. Nice guy, pretty funny, enjoyable lectures, if you like the subject matter. He tends to go through explanations way too fast for everyone, but he really knows a ton about information systems and has experience in the field. Not bad overall.
Good teacher--he comes up with interesting ways to teach rather than just lecturing
He is very kind. He offers opportunities to catch up and was approachable and thoughtful.

This is a flipped class style where you listen to the lecture before and then in class you do an assignment with your group. The assignments don't help you learn at all. The exams are half multiple choice and half essay questions. He expects you to know every little detail even if he didn't explain it well.

Unlike other science classes, Dr. Weber's class requires you to do oral and poster presentations that may put you out of your comfort zone. Tests still make up the majority of your grade though. I had to study a ton for each tests to do well, but I never felt like his questions were made to trick me. Good option for MMBio major classes.

This was a good class (Flow Cytometry). Class size was small and the lectures and quizzes were straight-forward. I really enjoyed it. Be sure to go to class; by missing more than one quiz it is hard to get an A. But if you pay attention and do the readings, the class is a breeze.

Readings of about thirty pages before every M/W class. Heavy material, but he provides reading guides so you don't get too bogged down. Science paper presentation each Friday(you'll present in a group once). Tests are 1/3 MC 1/3 Short Answer 1/3 Long Answer. 4 midterms+cumulative final. You'll learn a ton, but also have a ton to know for exams.

Sean Bair really means it when he says he cares. I took his class last year and this year am building a tech startup, so I reached out to him and he spent a full hour with me giving me some of the best advice I've ever gotten! He instantly remembered very specific things about me even though we only spoke like once. He super knows his stuff!

One of the most valuable professors I've had hands down. Because he has owned and sold multiple businesses, his insights are practical and grounded in experience. He is incredibly generous with his time and is happy to meet outside of class to give advice on business or life in general. Highly recommend if you want a mentor, not just an instructor.

Professor Bair cares deeply for his students, both in the classroom and in the real world. He's so cool, in fact, that he took me to breakfast and let me ask him a ton of industry questions. He has vast industry experience, which makes his lectures interesting and boosts his credibility above that of a typical professor. HIGHLY recommend!!
Great class! Sometimes lectures felt like a waste, but Prof Bair knows what he is doing and is very engaging. Good class overall.

Professor Bair is such a baddie and knows his stuff. His class is doable, however, my advice is don't check out because of how doable it is and try to do homework for other classes during his class. Soak in his humor, knowledge, and tips. You will get a lot out if his class if you do that. He's so caring and approachable. Take Professor Bair :)

Basically, I want to be Professor Bair when I am older. He doesn't only walk the walk but talks the talk which is rare with business professors. 

He is super cool with very sound advice for people looking to go all in on business.

Amazing professor! His grading criteria is clear. He is so real and lives what he is teaching! He's funny and cares a lot about his students! I learned a lot in this class and didn't feel like the homework was too bad! There are attendance quizzes but class is very valuable to go to! He does great reviews for tests that make them easier to take!

Professor Bair is incredible! He is so real and relatable and literally lives what he is teaching. He really cares about his students and wants to be resource. He doesn't just show up for the job and clock out when his class is over. He constantly emphasizes his availability and willingness to connect you to anyone in his network! Highly recommend!

Prof Bair is an exceptional human being. While I found the content of the class boring, he luckily made it easy to get an A. He wants you to utilize Chat GPT for absolutely everything, and he would go through the correct answers for exams before we took them. He bought everyone pizza on the last day of class and is just the kindest person ever.

I'm not in this class but I'm rating him because he so so amazing. He's super accessible outside of class and will hook you up if you ask. He's straightforward and will tell you the truth. I highly recommend him as a person and teacher.

Professor Bair is great! He cares about his students like none other! Take the time to meet with him 1on1 if you can. The class is mostly just busy work. But if you intentionally do the homework during the semester, the final project is easy. Idk if it was the TA or him but they were nitpicky on pointless stuff for homework. Pretty ez class though.

Sean is an awesome guy and a great lecturer. He has valuable, current real-world experience in business. 

Attendance is graded. The TA from this semester was awfully harsh and very critical of extremely minute details, so take that with a grain of salt. It's the only thing that ruined my experience cause I would recommend everyone take Prof Bair.

Really loved Sean. Didn't love his TA, I felt like he was an unrealistic grader and had a bit of a superiority complex. Sean does do attendance quizzes each week, and is maybe more work than other strategy professors from what I've heard, but I feel like I really learned a lot which made it worth it for me.

Sean Bair was such a great professor! 100% recommend him for STRAT392. He is funny and really wants to help his students succeed not just in the class but really in their careers. He was always kind, entertaining, and had a good sense of humor. He's great!
Professor Bair was amazing. He had great lectures, good content, and an impactful final project. His TA was a tough grader, but it was a great class.

One of the easiest classes I've ever taken at BYU. He changed a bunch of grades at the end, which bumped my grade up a ton. Sean has said he doesn't care about grades so he wants everyone to get the grade they want. The one downside was that the class was unorganized at times and communication between him and his TA lacked.

He is such an awesome professor. He teaches the content in such a way that sets you up for success. It is one of the only classes at the Marriott School that gives you hands-on experience. Professor Bair is really smart and will make you leave out of every class uplifted. He is well-connected and will always show you how it's done.

GREATEST PROFESSOR AT BYU HANDS DOWN! He does everything in his power to help you succeed in the classroom, and he is happy to help you with anything outside the classroom when it comes to landing jobs or internships. Incredible dude.

Sean was an awesome professor. His lectures were always interesting, well thought out, and applicable. I also appreciated how he was a professional resource to us students (he helped us prepare for interviews, find us jobs, network, etc.) Sean is just a genuinely kind person who you could tell wanted to help us succeed. I loved his class!

Excellent class. Really cares about what the students learn and get out of it. Most of the learning is in the first half of the semester, then the back half is relaxed as you prep for your final project. Absolutely take advantage of this class and take him over any other professor. One of the most enjoyable classes I have taken.

I would retake so many classes if Professor Bair was the instructor! He has a genuine mission to be a resource for each student (he was the reason I got a job post-graduation!) and to use his extensive background of relevant professional experiences to support them. Assignments are all intentional. Easily the best professor in the Marriott School.
Loved Sean, if he could give everybody an A he would!

I loved learning from Sean Bair. While he's not like a traditional professor many including myself found that to be extremely refreshing and exciting to learn from someone who has spent his career in the field and now shares his experience freely.

Professor Bair is a great teacher and human!
He truly cares about his students, and instead of just reciting everything that's on the textbook he would explain concepts in class in a clear way and would give real life examples of them. I also value the time he took throughout the semester to teach us skills beyond the classroom! Would take again.

I learned more applicable, real-world skills in this class than in any class I've taken before--college or otherwise. Professor Bair obviously wants all of his students to do well in his class, but he also genuinely cares about what they go on to do after school and is willing to do anything within his power to help them succeed.

I'm shocked at people saying this class was confusing and that instructions were contradictory/vague. Brother Bair always knew what was going on, he answered all questions and NEVER belittled questions either. He always tried to make life easier for students. If a quiz question was weird, he threw it out and same with dropping assignments. Not hard
Awesome leader, professor, and example. I would take him for every class if I could. He is the best strat392 professor.

I'm shocked at how high this rating is. Sean *is* a great human, but this class is a mess. The instructions are contradictory and/or vague. And when you ask in class, even he doesn't seem to know what's going on. 

It's not that I wouldn't take him again. It was fine. But this will go down as one of the most confusing classes I've ever taken.

Prof. Bair is an amazing professor. He makes the material make sense, everything is set up in a logical way, and he is INCREDIBLY understanding. While the TA made life hard occasionally due to a lack of communication, Prof. Bair himself made sure that everyone could succeed in AND OUT of his class. If you have to take this class, take it form him.

Brother Bair was always willing to meet with individuals and groups. I respect that a ton. The class is tough but very doable and your learn a ton of applicable things. If you are willing to meet with him and discuss things, you will do well. Definitely take STRAT 392 from Brother Bair!

I think I would take a different course from Sean in a perfect world. But, he changed several things for this semester (due to his own whims or to the department's for being too easy, idk), and it went poorly. Completely unexpected grading policies, unknown expectations, assignments that were too hard or too easy, and annoying group projects.

Professor Bair cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He also listens and provides feedback on all assignments personally. I'm shocked people did not just talk to him about their grades and then left bad reviews because they could speak up. He's very approachable and kind. Since those reviews, he has reevaluated and helped all of us.

Brother Bair's AWESOME! I have really enjoyed his class. He's very successful with his own companies so learning from his experience and many current businesses is so beneficial. He cares about the students. He helps to get in contact with people in his network (which is such an impressive network) to introduce students and get a foot in the door.

The quizzes and assignments in the class are ridiculous. Proctored weekly quizzes paired with a difficult assignment or two a week. The TA will dock you points for just about any error your make on any assignment. Getting 100% on anything is almost impossible. Bair is awesome but this class needs to change. WE ARE NOT TAKING THIS CLASS BY CHOICE.

Hardest assignments ever. Basically we get assigned something that is ridiculously hard, if youre dumb like me you do hours and hours of work to complete said assignment and then just end up with a terrible grade anyways because of how hard they are graded. Tough class.

PSA: This class has changed drastically since most of these reviews. Professor Bair told us that he decided to make the class more difficult this year. He still gives simple busywork assignments, but now he nitpicks them and docks points for things not in the instructions. All quizzes are now through Proctorio. One of the worst classes I've taken.

prof bear is the best option for strat, but you really take his class because of the ways it helps you in real life. He'll help any student with anything career related and is the best resource to have. The class is meaningful and the work all feels relevant. wish i could take more classes from him

Sean is the coolest professor at BYU. He brings in so much real-world knowledge which is way more valuable than any textbook. inspires students and connects with us on a personal level. You have to go with Sean

Professor Bair is awesome. He uses class time to tell stories about how certain frameworks and strategic principles were useful for him. He does not assign any busy work. Everything he assigns is to build a skill that he thinks will make you successful in the REAL WORLD. Participation is a big part of your grade. This is the strat class you want.

Professor Bair is the type of Professor that makes the business school great: an industry professional who has been very successful on a number of metrics (an in multiple ventures) that teaches because he loves it and not because he needs to. He regularly shares insights from his experience and he is willing to invest students long term success.

Professor Bair is awesome! He has a lot of real world experience and is genuinely invested in helping his students succeed. He puts a lot of emphasis on networking and makes you practice in class, which I thought was really helpful because otherwise people don't really talk to each other. The class was honestly pretty easy, which was nice.

Sean does a great job teaching the class using his own experiences building and selling companies and is just the type of person you would want to learn about business strategy from. He loses a point because the forced in-class network exercises felt forced and annoying, but ultimately is a very solid choice!!

Great class. Attendance was required. Closed book weekly quizzes and midterm (both very easy). One group project (graded very leniently). And a final (open book).  He's got a lot of real world experience which makes the lectures entertaining. This is by far the most manageable of the core business classes that are required my the Marriott School.
Super great guy. Amazing real world experience. Group project is fun and applicable. MANAGEABLE class which is rare in the MAcc.

Bro Bair is awesome. His class is straightforward and very useful if you put in time. You can get an A without much effort, but you'll miss out on actual learning. I enjoyed hearing about his personal experiences, but I think he sometimes focused too much on them. I gave him a 4, but I think he can improve to a 5 with more experience. Solid choice!

I cannot say more positive things about Sean. He was one of my favorite professors I have taken a class from at BYU. Sean genuinely cares about his students and takes time to get to know them and help them network. I ended up being hired to one of my jobs through a referral from Sean, which meant a lot. Pretty easy class with a stellar teacher.

I had a great time in Sean's class! He really cares about his students, and he wants to help students make valuable networking connections. He'll totally put you in contact with his own network to help you. There's one big group project, but it's broken up nicely so you're not scrambling at the end of the semester. Highly recommend this class!

Professor Bair is a great professor! He is so friendly and easy to talk to - he wants to help you both inside and outside class, and is looking for opportunities to build your network! The midterm and final are super easy, biggish group project at the end of the semester that is not to bad if you do the assignments as you cover them in class.

Great professor! The class was pretty easy, which I personally found desirable since it's part of the business core. The class is extremely useful. Sean explains topics clearly, but more importantly, he helped us build real skills. The class had a focus on networking with professionals along with doing relevant research. Sean has an A+ in my book

Class was easy, but that's not criteria for a 5 star teacher. Sean knows his stuff, but lacks teaching skills. He definitely cares about students, but falls victim to students feeling like class isn't a good use of time. A lot of his material is common sense/basic business knowledge. Good guy, but class was meh and we didn't learn very much.

Professor Bair is a great choice for strategy. He's fairly new to being a professor so I'm excited to see the growth that he makes over the years. He really cares about his students and tries everything he can to make you successful after graduation. There's a group project in the class. This project can be fun if you put in honest effort.

Sean was an incredible professor. His class was a good blend of individual work and group work. His networking activities are awesome if taken seriously and his personal business insights are awesome. If you want an A and a learning experience I'd highly recommend Sean's class.

The most disorganized course I've had in the Marriott School: -Unclear instructions for assignments. -All assignments turned in by email. -Anecdotal stories about the company Prof. Bair sold. I was hoping for a more analytical approach to a course called "Economics & Strategy" - mostly just long lectures and busy work. Would not recommend.
Heavily based on group project and networking activities

He is a great guy. The class itself is kind of boring if you ask me, but he is cool and the class is so easy. Open note midterm and final, easy reading quizzes, and a pretty simple group project are basically the only assignments. Think intro to marketing but like 5 notches easier, that's pretty much the class.

Bets Professor at BYU. He has a lot of real-life experience that makes everything he teaches have validity and very insightful. His only goal is to help his students and share all the knowledge he has. He goes above and beyond to serve. He wants you to reach out even after the class to help you with anything you need. Great connection.
Hes an amazing professor, never participated in a class as much as I did in this one! Would take the class again in a heartbeat.

Prof Bair is very knowledgeable in the business field with some really cool job experience. I loved when he would bring guest speakers in. His quizzes and exams were open book (really straight forward) . The main assignment is a group project kind of like a case competition. I'm so glad I took Bair instead of the other professors. Highly recommend.

Professor Bair is awesome! I had him during his first semester teaching and he is the coolest. He understands how business actually runs so he has applicable assignments, lectures, and guest speakers. He doesn't want to kill you and he will do anything to help you be successful! He is responsive all the time and a good friend too!

Professor Bair is an amazing person, professional, and professor. On the first day of class he told us it wasnt our job to impress him, but his job to teach us and do a good job. Nothing in the class is busywork, he gives awesome lectures, and he brought in amazing guest speakers. One of my absolute favorite classes in the business school.

Not only a great class, but probably one of the most inspirational classes I've taken at BYU. Instead of learning out of date information and spending half of your class doing a simulation game (that the other strategy professors perform) you'll be learning from industry experts on what strategy actually means.
Professor Bair is one of the most genuine professors I've had. He gets it: school is for learning and connecting, not busywork. And he is fantastic at connecting and helping other people connect!
The easiest class you'll find in the business school. Great lectures and has a lot of examples from his own experiences. Genuinely cares about his students.

Sean is a stud. Great teacher that cares about developing your business acumen, learning, and network. Brought in many guest speakers that were very helpful. Learned a ton from the class. The group project is 50% of your grade, so be sure to get that right! Very manageable workload that really allows you to grow in the areas you want to grow in.

Sean's class was very entertaining because of his business experience. The class wasn't too hard with open book and open note quizzes and midterm. A lot of your grade is based on a group project but it isn't graded harshly. He could work on course organization for turning in assignments but overall it was a great class and I would take it again.

Sean didn't have rate my professor rating when I signed up, so I didn't know what to expect. Sean exceeded every expectation. He is good, he is great, he is the GOAT. He brings a lot of real experience to the classroom.
Great professor, good insights both in the textbook and the case studies, and a slightly difficult group project, but overall I would recommend Professor Bair to anyone!

Sean is an amazing professor. He is hilarious and understands what students are going through. His class is pretty easy, but you learn so much. He dives deep into the sections with his own stories and other stories. He also will mentor you if you have any business ideas! Great guy.

One of the best professors I've had and he doesn't even like to call himself a professor! Sean is real with his students and wants everyone in his class to learn, not kill themselves with excessive readings, homework, or projects. Other professors should take notes from him! His real world experience and guest lecturers really helped me learn.

Sean is a total stud. This is how every business class should be. He put a lot of effort into having great guest speakers and making class enjoyable. He even got the founder of Ancestry to speak to us! He genuinely cares for his students and made it a point to learn things about every student even though weere online. Take this class from him!

I loved this class. Sean Bair brought so much more to class than the typical professor. Sean shares tons of real world experience, brought in great guest speakers, and taught only the relevant stuff we needed for our future careers. Homework load was reasonable, some reading and quizzes based on the homework. Group project was not overwhelming.

Professor Bair is amazing! I would highly recommend taking any class he teaches. He is very aware of his students and their needs, and works to tailor class content and guest lecturers to them. Very responsive to students and their questions, and he grades easily and doesn't assign busy work. 10/10 would recommend!

Interesting lectures and workload is extremely reasonable. Assignments consist of weekly quizzes on textbook chapters (open book), a few assignments, a midterm (open book), and a semester group project. We also had guest lectures that were great. Definitely would recommend.

Professor Warnick is insanely smart and cares about you understanding the material. The only issue is that with as large of a class that he teaches is that you don't have much one on one time but instead if you have issues, you have to go to the TA's or go through previous lessons, all of which allow you to do what he expects from you at that time.
Wonderful professor! Genuinely cares about his students and gives them all the resources they can to succeed. Super passionate and gets students excited.

Dr. Warnick is definitely one of my favorite CS professors (tie with Dr. Ventura). I've had him for 1 undergrad class and 2 grad classes. He is very passionate about the subjects and the history behind them. Most of the courses he teaches are not easy and require a good amount of effort, but he tries to meet what the students want and need.

Honestly, nothing that is worth it is easy and this class is a prime example of that. Coding is HARD, and EXTREMELY time consuming, but if you dedicate the time, visit the TA's, and engage in the course and you will come out on top. This is not one of those classes that you can expect to slide by and pass no matter who your professor is.

Absolutely the worst class I have attended at BYU. The grading is completely unfair. You can get the program right, but if you don't have the right "comments" you won't get ANY credit. Not to mention the comments aren't really explained that well in class, so you start with no idea how to do them the way he wants them done.

Although the 142 class says there is no need for prior computer knowledge, Sean definitely expects students to know a great deal about programming - he teaches his lessons in a very unusual (but interesting) way but glosses over things that many people may not know.  Assignments take a LOT of time - his grading is really strict/hard to get points

Prof. Warnick teaches this class in a different way from the other instructors in a good way. He cares about the class and the students. His assignments take time, but are not impossible and the TA's are extremely helpful. I would recommend this professor.
He is a really good teacher. He is super smart and knows a lot about computer science.  He is good at explaining difficult concepts.

Prof. Warnick definitely expects students to have a grasp of some basic mathematics before taking this class. He presents interesting applications and takes time to put the class in the big picture of Computer Science. A good introductory class, he offers every class period for students to come to his office for help with confusing topics.
Dr. Warnick is challenging, but in the end it's worth it and you really understand the material. If you want to be anything more than a code monkey then he's the professor you want.

Dr Warnick is an amazing teacher.  He really cares about the students.  He makes time to help you understand the material if you need it.  The material is hard.  The math is advanced but extremely interesting.

Did not understand a single concept Dr. Warnick covered.  Retook CS312 from a different Professor and had absolutely no trouble understanding the same material and getting an A.  He expects that everyone in his class is attending MIT like he did.  I learned more after I stopped attending lectures and studied on my own.

Homework was assigned and due before the material was covered in class. Dr. Warnick is more of a mathematician than an engineer, so if you're into the more practical applications of CS you might click better with a different professor. The class is hard anyway--I just have a nagging feeling it would have been easier with a different professor.

He has a lot of enthusiasm and passion for teaching his subject, but he goes too fast and was never able to help me understand the concepts. I was able to do extremely well on the assignments and the midterm, but no thanks to Dr. Warnick. I have to give him a thumbs down overall.
I agree with the 9/29/05 post. He's very smart and can explain thing well. BUT, tests are tough+tricky. He also tends to talk too much about things off the topic... instead of lesson stuff.
No Comments
Very enthusiastic about what he's doing, really cares about his students.  He is very smart and his expectation may be a bit too high sometimes.

Professor Bybee was a good teacher and explains concepts well. He has adjustable grading schemes so the chance of getting a good grade is more likely. To do well on the exams I would recommend going to TA reviews which are very helpful. Overall, not a bad class it's just biology so it felt like a review of things I have learned before in the past.

Dr. Bybee is a great teacher. He knows his subject matter and is very passionate about evolutionary biology. There aren't a lot of assignments, so your grade is based on the tests, the lab, and the work for the research paper. The tests are tricky but doable when you study. Dr. Bybee give interesting lectures and requires a lot of participation.

Dr. Bybee was a pretty good lecturer. He often had us work things out with a partner and would reinforce learning with activities. The tests were somewhat difficult, but they weren't too bad after doing a lot of studying. He also has a very flexible grading scheme that makes it a lot easier to get a A in the class.

This teacher is excellent. He is fairly adept at being apolitical. He prepares you okay for the exams, but they are somewhat difficult. Make sure to pay attention to the format, the tests are similar. He gives great instruction, and his TA's are good. The grading is difficult, I don't know how I got an A-. Pay attention, do the assignments.

Bybee is a good professor and made biology interesting for me! There's a decent bit of reading for weekly quizzes and questions do show up on exams that are only mentioned in the textbook. Wasn't sure how to feel about the lecture on global warming because I felt it was a little biased, however that opinion is likely influenced by my own views.

I would say that Dr. Bybee has a great intent to bring others closer to God through his class. I admire that very much about his attitude toward reconciling evolution and religion and other matters. At times he got too political and said he wasn't. The way he administers grades and makes the tests too hard is not something I appreciated.

Bybee is a good man, but a bad lecturer. His signature move is to have you figure out his slides for him with your neighbor. He does not reinforce important concepts; we often wasted time on unimportant things while hurriedly covering main concepts. There are no study guides for tests. I did enjoy his lectures on LDS and evolution.

Professor Bybee was one of my favorite professors during my first semester at BYU. He gives great lectures and explains complex concepts in a very comprehensible way. He's also so funny and makes very class enjoyable.

I believe Seth Bybee to be a good man. He cares for students and likes to lecture. It is evident he loves what he does and tries to elevate student's faith. I disagree with the way he administers the class- I think the grading schemes etc. are a waste of his time and it is irritating to try and know exactly what my grade actually is in the class.

Dr Bybee addresses tough subjects like evolution v. religion incredibly. He's very accepting of every question and people are comfortable asking them. I had a 3:30 - 4:45pm class period that I was not excited for, but this has become my favorite class. Most grades are from just attendance and reading quizzes and completion homework.

I was not excited at all about taking biology but Professor Bybee made it so accessible and interesting. He is a very engaging and respectful teacher and I learned so much and actually really enjoyed this class. Weekly assignments are easy enough if you go to class and do the reading and he has extra credit. Loved it so much very accessible.

Professor Bybee will stress to you to read but the exams did not pull from the readings at all. I suggest attending class to help the most. Lots of busy work with this class but the TA graded fairly. I thought this class could have been more interesting if the professor wasn't bad with explanations and wording on test questions.

He was really nice and spiritual. However the lectures did not help with the tests very much in my opinion. The textbook reading did really help alot. You still have to listen in class though because theres always a few random questions on the test that he only barely mentions once in class. Still a really nice and thoughtful guy though.

Bybee is a real stand-up guy. He wants you to succeed and offers the highest grade of 5 grading schemes.  Recommended for the confident risk-taker who skips class, studies the online lecture slides, and gambles their entire grade on the exams as well as the punctual, studious type. Just check over your exams with the TAs. They misgrade sometimes.

BIO 100 was not my favorite, but I had to take it sometime, and Dr. Bybee was a good professor. He's very passionate about biology, and he loves engaging with the class. Expect to go to lectures and have discussions and debates a little beyond what is strictly necessary for the content.

I loved Prof. Bybee, he was very down to earth and cared a lot about his students, he told inspirational personal stories. I truly felt he loved his job and wanted us to succeed.  He doesn't do study guides, and the review rooms are based on the TA's knowledge. But if you put in the effort, read the book(look on kindle), and study you'll do well!

His lectures were pretty interesting, but his tests were extremely hard. He doesn't believe in study guides, and every time I took a test, I felt like I had studied the wrong things. There was really no good way to prepare for his tests.

Dr. Bybee is such a wonderful professor! He cares very much about his students, engages well with them, and holds meaningful discussions. The workload and tests (of which there are four) are reasonable. He doesn't give study guides for the tests, so if you make sure to do the readings and participate in class then you'll have a great experience.

I loved Prof. Bybee he provides a powerful learning environment that combines the world of science and religion. He has a powerful testimony of the gospel and of biology and it's very inspiring to see that. His class was tough but I learned a lot. Prof. Bybee has different grading schemes, your amount of effort in his class will equal your grade.

Prof. Bybee is such a genuine and caring person. He feels like your dad. His lectures are concise and he will answer any and all questions, no matter what. The TAs can be hard graders sometimes but they are more than willing to help you during office hours. Use their review sessions and COME with questions because it is purely student-driven.
pretty cool class but hard to get a great grade

There are many different grading schemes, so some require attendance and some don't. At the end of the semester he'll go through all of them and give you the highest grade he can. The lecture slides were available online, and studying them and redoing the activities will help you for the tests. The extra credit is longer, so start early.

Loved Bybee! Great lecturer and all around great guy.
However, he had zero idea what was going on outside of lecture (lab, assignments, projects, exams, etc.)
This would have been okay if the TAs weren't quite literally the worst I've ever had here at BYU (4 years).
They graded incredibly subjectively & would send rubrics the day things were due.

I love Dr. Bybee. He makes it clear by his grading system that he really wants students to learn the material and care less about the grade. His lectures are often super entertaining and make going to class worth it. I will say that his tests were kinda challenging, even though they were all about the lectures. I wish there were study guides.

When people say that the professors at BYU are amazing, they're talking about professors like Dr. Bybee. His class environment was absolutely incredible. He is passionate about his lessons, and taught me how to think about life in a new way. Today was our last lecture, and I teared up knowing I wouldn't be coming back after this semester. 10/10!

Professor Bybee is AMAZING and I never thought a biology class could be so uplifting, inspiring, and testimony building! I 10/10 would take this class again. However, exams are tricky, especially the short answer sections so be aware of those and go to the review sessions. Pay attention, work hard, do the homework, and you'll be good to go :)

Professor Bybee is amazing! I really looked forward to attending his class each day, as he made each lecture fun and engaging. You can really tell that he loves his job, and that he has a real passion for the things he teaches. Definitely would 10/10 recommend Professor Bybee.

Dr Bybee is a funny and charismatic professor. He cares about his students and you can tell he loves what he is teaching. He does however travel a lot so pray there are good Tas. The tests are hard so make sure you study the slides which he puts on learning suite. The lectures are super interesting and fun and he offers extra credit.

Read a chapter of the textbook every week and write a paper on it. Then he goes over those concepts the next week to clarify and teach better than the textbook. Pretty funny. Strong testimony. Tests are hard, but you learn through the semester what they're like so you can study better. If you go to the exam reviews the tests are way easier.

The class started out really unorganized and we ended up taking all the wrong reading quizzes which made it difficult. He did make it right when he realized it halfway through. The tests were easy as long as you go to class and study the lecture slides. I thought he was a nice guy. The class had a good mix of learning, spiritual moments, and humor.

Such a cool guy!! I found his class pretty easy and he has a ton of different ways to succeed in the class - and you get to choose your grading method.  His lectures are entertaining and informative. He does do a ton of partner work but its a great way really understand concepts and get to know new people :)

I honestly enjoyed taking this class from Professor Bybee so much!!! If you go to class and participate in the group discussions, you will be well prepared for the tests. Bybee also made the class a spiritual experience and showed how science and religion can strengthen your testimony and that it's ok to have questions. Would definitely recommend!

The semester paper was a pretty big deal, but the criteria were clear and it wasn't too bad as long as you keep up on the work. Things were a little weird because of covid, but he kept the workload reasonable.

Brother Bybee's Bio 100 class is all about application, so for some it may seem a little more work than necessary, but the class helps you understand biology so much better. He is a Evolutionary Biologist and helps those who may struggle with the relationship of religion and science. He has lots of grading options to fit different learning styles.

Very smart and good researcher. Often times his research gets in the way of him teaching, long absences for research trips. Great professor. Great guy. One downside of the class is he picks people to be best friends with and then is a bully to everyone else. He talms a lot behind people's backs making fun of them. Rough price to pay for class.

I loved Dr. Bybees class! He presented several grading schemes and totally made it possible for us to succeed. He was honestly the funniest professor Ive ever had, but at the same time he was passionate about what he taught. Id definitely recommend him to anyone.

Dr. Bybee is very spiritual; his lectures were good and always involved a religious aspect. He's hilarious, but his tests are pretty tough (short answer and multiple choice) and they weigh heavily on your grade. His lectures don't have anything to do with the tests and most of what I learned, I learned from the internet. Tough for a 100 level class

Seriously one of the best classes I've taken. Dr. Bybee is a great teacher and focuses on LEARNING, not just memorizing. If you pay attention in class and study for tests, you should do fine. He does expect you to talk to the people around you a lot, but I thought it was helpful. Heard some great stories too. :)

GREAT lectures, brings science and religion to a place where they can meet and allows students to see how they can coexist! Tests are a little tough due to the written response portion, but pay attention to activities and you will do well!

Dr. Bybee is funny, but his humor is often at the expense of students who participate (he sarcastically roast you in class when you answer). He also does make u talk to ur partner A TON. I felt like I knew the material well, but the tests were CRAZY hard. A GE class shouldn't be this hard. I did enjoy his lectures tho, super inspiring testimony.
He's good

He gives homework and reading every week. Tests are really difficult, but he offers extra credit to help you make up for it. He can be really hard on people and pokes fun at students to make the class laugh. He's funny but it's at the expense of other people. A difficult class and not worth taking for me, especially if you don't like biology.

Tests were very hard. Lots of homework, quizzes, and reading due every week. He teaches as if you are already a biologist and understand all of the material. Made and explained everything harder than it needed to be. I ended up reteaching myself all of the material. This class would only be beneficial if you were a biology major.

Seth Bybee is the BEST teacher for Bio 100. He is hilarious and teaches well, so everyone understands the material. He leaves often to go conduct research and the TAs arent phenomenal at teaching. He is an evolution biologist, which can bother some people in the class. Overall, he is the best teacher for bio 100 and I enjoy his class a lot.

Some people didn't like Prof. Bybee's class; I did. He can be tough at first, but you can see he cares about his students. Bio 100 has a lot to cover, and he does a great job at teaching it. He can also help you get research opportunities! He's an evolutionary biologist- if that bothers you, don't take the class, or take it to expand your mind!

Spent almost two months catching bugs with him in the South Pacific. We are now publishing an unholy amount of research. if you want research, hes a great professor for it. Maybe you dont get along on a personel level with him. thats ok. he will do everything in his power to make sure you get the best experience possible. And he is a great guy!

If you are a pre med student that doesnt want to actually learn biology but just want an easy A to apply for further programs, he is not your guy. Lots of people in class had a vendetta against him because of that and complained 24-7 ALL semester. He teaches bio and holy cow- you will learn how to do serious Research wth him. He is the best!

I never ever write reviews but I had to because Dr. Bybee is that good!! His class requires you to be engaged, but trust me it is worth it. Bybee is funny, super passionate about biology, and brings a spiritual perspective that relates biology and the gospel beautifully!! Go to the TAs and reviews and you will get an A!

The key to success in his class is attending lecture and doing the work. TA reviews are also super helpful. The tests are the majority of the grade, and be warned they are not completely multiple choice. However, Dr. Bybee and his TAs are great at preparing you for the tests. Stay diligent during the semester and you'll do great. It was a fun class

Loved him. His grading system is great. I'm not a big biology fan but I genuinely enjoyed this class. It was easy to understand and he was really inspiring. I literally almost started crying in class once because I was feeling the spirit.

Evolutionary biology isn't my passion, but it sure is Dr. Bybee's. This class is difficult and sometimes kinda boring, but if you've gotta take it, Dr. Bybee is the man. His nerdy humor and enthusiasm will help you get through the class. Dr. Bybee loves nerding out with students, so if evolutionary bio is your thing, you'll love this class.

Bybee is one of the greatest professors at BYU. I took this for a general and actually considered changing my major to biology (like only for a second, but still). Lectures were super interesting and he is so passionate about what he teaches. The homework was simple and helped with tests. TA reviews are a must. Overall awesome class. Take him.

His lectures are fun, he explains the notes and lets you work things out with your neighbor. He is super nice and caring and will answer any questions you have. He also keeps the Spirit in the discussions. He pretty much will do anything to make you pass. One of the best professors I've had. Highly recommend taking BIO 100 from him!

He knows his stuff and wants you to know it inside and out as well. He can laugh at himself and isnt afraid to acknowledge frustrating situations and will help you work through them. doing research? - HE IS THE PROFESSO FOR RESEARCH! He does not mess around with frivolous work. If you are in his lab, you will publish papers.

He focuses on the subject and tells you what you need to know. He is nice and helpful but holds a high standard. No busy work. His grad students are given a LOT of freedom in how they teach. One of his grad students is my all time favorite person. The other.. not so much... the question isnt what is bybee like, its what grad student will u get

What I didn't like about this class was how difficult it was to know what to study. Also, it doesn't help that the cut off for an A is a 95! Overall, there is just a lot of busy work and it is very hard to get a good grade.
Don't take this class if your grade is important to you! The cut off for an A is a 95%! This is the only class that I have taken where I professor has done that to me. Would not recommend this class!

He has many grading curves and he individually applies the curve to each student. The one he picks is the one that will give you the best grade. TAs would hand out answers while looking at the real tests at their reviews. Super easy weekly homeworks. He knows that most people in the class don't like science so he caters well to those needs.

For someone who isn't that great at the sciences, Dr. Bybee sure made learning Biology fun! He is so funny, learned, and spiritual- all at the same time. He breaks down the content very well and doesn't go over-the-top with his expectations of Bio100 students. Ample opportunity for extra credit to pull your grade up. Also, USE THE TAs!!!

Dr Bybee is on your side 100%! He wants everyone to succeed and gives opportunities for extra credit and grades everyone based on their own individual style of learning. I always felt the spirit and had a lot of fun in his class at the same time. It sounds weird but who he is as a professor and what he taught changed my life for the better.

Dr. Bybee is a very cool guy and relates really well to students. He understands that the majority of his students are not strong in the sciences and shapes the class to fit his students. Lectures can get kind of long but he really does his best to keep things interesting. Homework is optional but I would definitely recommend it for test prep.

Dr. Bybee is a great teacher. His class and lectures were always very interesting and engaging, and his love of biology was kind of infectious. He's a funny guy and he cares about his students and their success. BIO100 was probably my favorite GE.
Interesting lectures, very funny.  However, the tests were very difficult. If Bio is not your thing, expect to study ALOT. Keep up with homework and quizzes.

Bio 100 was worth taking with Professor Bybee. It's hard but he was engaging so it's still manageable. His lectures are funny, try not to skip them.  GO TO THE TAs FOR HELP, it works! Go to reviews before exams then look over them w/ the TAs after they're graded. Weekly hw due Friday and quizzes due Monday. Easy GE to knock out (biological science)

I didn't like him at first but his lecture style grew on me. Gives lots of opportunity for participation. Lots of short easy papers and then one longer one but they were graded really easily. Tests weren't bad at all, got As on all of them by going to reviews and briefly looking over the slides.

Bybee is a great guy. He really is such a  nerd about  Biology and clearly passionate. I was really able to feel the spirit in this class more than any other secular class you will ever take. Highly recommend this professor

Absolutely loved Professor Bybee!  He is accommodating, understanding, and really cares.   Also his lectures are hilarious, had us all rolling in our seats. He made me want to take all the classes he offers, and I'm not interested in Science.  His class isn't necessarily an easy A, you still have to work,  but it's an incredibly enjoyable class!

Really enjoyed this GE. He did a great job instilling the passion he has for Biology into his lectures and made it fun. Attendance is not mandatory but I never missed a lecture. He has multiple grading schemes, super awesome. Definitely would recommend, he made bio100 a fun GE.

Dr. Bybee is a great guy.  He does make Biology interesting but is off and on about teaching simply.  I feel his lectures somewhat prepare you for the test, but if you want to do well, you pretty much have to memorize his powerpoint slides. I respect him a lot and is passionate about what he does.
Bybee is a fantastic teacher. I usually don't enjoy biology, but I really liked this class. Go to the TA reviews and you'll do fine.

Bybee is quite possibly the best professor I've ever had at BYU. Don't get me wrong I HATE biology, but his class was the highlight of my semester. No one wants to be in that class (GE class for Non bio majors) and he knows it, so he makes it as enjoyable as possible. His grading is extremely generous. You truly get the grade you deserve. take him

Professor Bybee somehow manages to make general ed biology class an entertaining and interesting course. He is funny, engaging, and very clear in his teaching style. His quizzes are designed to trick you, but there is an alternate assignment for each quiz that is way better. Tests are hard.

Took his biology class out of necessity because it is a required general. I like his like 5 different grading scales. He assigns a weekly homework and then a reading assignment from the text book.  Definitely no surprises. Honestly, quite a boring class but about as good as your are gonna get for a general biology class.
I LOVE THIS GUY. He made class so interesting and fun- It ended up being my favorite class this semester. Dr. Bybee is funny, cares about his students, and he knows his stuff. TAKE BIO 100 FROM HIM.
Bybee is a great teacher.  A quiz and easy quick homework weekly. A very easy class if you just show up to class and pay attention.
Dr. Bybee is a fantastic teacher, he understands that learning is more important than just passing a test! I love his teaching style and he loves involving the students in the lecture!

He's very sincere and understanding. The only problem I had was the way he words things--it's often unclear and difficult to decipher. Other than that, he's passionate and cares deeply about his students. Really stresses the fact that your grade isn't as important as your learning. I don't like biology but I didn't mind this class. Use the TA's!

Dr. Bybee's class was my favorite GE that I've taken, I highly doubt something else will surpass it. He focuses on teaching you the science and then discussing the implications, and is very open and willing to let discussions continue after class has ended. He is excellent at playing devil's advocate, so be ready for great discussion. Good times!
Really easy and interesting. You can essentially skip the classes and just skim the textbook and go to the reviews and you will get As on the tests.
Absolutely loved Dr. Bybee's class. He focused on what was most important, and grades were based on learning not meticulous facts. Would take this class from him again!

Dr. Bybee is awesome. He really knows his stuff and knows how to teach it well. He's understanding and gives you plenty of opportunity to succeed in his class, and his tests are on what he teaches in class so no surprises in the testing center. Great teacher.

This man is bae! He truly cares about teaching and you! He has quizzes and homework but they are so easy and act as a buffer. He offers extra credit and drops your lowest test score. He also brings everything he is teaching to the gospel in the greatest way possible! Take from him!

Bybee is the best science teacher I've ever had. He has multiple grading options that he applies, and whatever one gives you the best score is the one he'll use on you. Drops lowest test, and lets you replace one. Weekly quizes and assignments, but really easy. Tests aren't too bad. Really nice guy, super funny. I loved this class, so easy.

Really fun guy. I didn't care much for sciences before taking this class, but he made it interesting because he's so passionate about it. I learned a lot. Homeworks and quizzes are easy, tests are just fine if you study. He gives you the highest grade possible and wants to help his students. Would always chat after class.

He's a nice guy. The class is incredibly interesting at times, but also kind of weirdly put together and often unclear as to what to study for the exams. He's not very helpful if you come with questions. And you have to go to class everyday to take little 3 question quizzes on the reading. The TA's review sessions are helpful with exams.

Assignments given in class so you have to go. Homework is easy points. Quizzes were online and open book. Again, more easy points. But, the tests were killers. For an intro class, the information he expects you to "synthesize" is ghastly. I got an A but I didn't learn much overall. He likes what he does but expects too much out of his non-bio pupil
I enjoyed his class quite a bit. it was on the 100 level and so it wasn't too intense, yet he had a passion for what he taught

Okay, I ended up with an A in the class, but I hardly learned a thing. Attendance is mandatory, hated going to class. His lectures are boring; he rambles. The homework is easy, but the tests are harder. However, he does curve.

Dr. Taylor is the best professor at explaining difficult concepts that I know of. He cares about your learning, and is willing to give you a good grade. No textbook, so all of the course material is contained in the lecture/slides. The class started out difficult, but once I started going into office hours it became much easier. 10/10!
Do not recommend, 0/10 don't take, course navigation is confusing, she is not a good teacher.
I've heard of the class structure changing, but when I took it, it was a breeze. Assignments and tests were exactly what was taught and practiced in class, and grading was never harsh.

This was a phenomenal online class. It's structured so well and is SO easy. most things are pass/fail. The lectures are very clear with examples. She does not try to shove too much unnecessary info into the class. There are no tests which make the class a breeze. Dr Wilcox is always willing to lend a hand. Take this class!

I really enjoyed Professor Wilcox. The course material was presented clearly, and expectations were easy to understand. She was very accessible and helpful when I had questions.
