The online textbook and concept checks were sometimes frustrating to use, as they felt slow and not very effective for learning. Overall, a positive experience.

The redesign was pretty good and makes the class a lot more doable. Some say this takes up a lot of time, but it takes as much as a 3-credit class normally would take. Prof. Wilcox and the TAs care a ton about the students and are always implementing the feedback from the students. I would recommend this class if you're taking this for a general.

CELL 120's redesign was rough. The “textbook scavenger hunts” were pointless and took 2+ hours despite a 45-minute estimate. Lectures were clear, but online labs felt graduate-level with zero prep and no overlap with notes. The workload was overwhelming — I even quit my job. Worst class I've had at BYU.

If you need to take Cell 120 take it from her! Clear lectures, honestly never read from the textbook and did good. Her and her TA's are always there to help understand concepts, and go through the things you missed. Good reviews, and clear modules with what is due each week. You can easily get ahead if you wanted to!

The work doesn't stop for Holidays, but you can get ahead! In the course she provided many helpful  extra tools: Weekly TA + Professor reviews (live if you can attend), practice problem sheets, readings+videos, lectures, and multiple-chance quizzes. I felt like there was a lot of tests but it was honestly helpful. A ton of material covered!

This class was really challenging for me never have taken an in depth biology class before this, but as the semester went on I felt like I was understanding things a lot better. Wonderful professor and very knowledgable. Was hard but very rewarding.

Homework does NOT prep you for exams (nor do the study guides). Not respectful of students at all. Both a full exam and a final project were due the day after Thanksgiving, with no accommodations (even though there was literally nothing due the following week). She asked for feedback on the course, but deflected any kind of constructive criticism.

I really enjoyed this class. There is clear communication from TAs and professor at all times so you know what is going on. Extra credit is available which is super helpful if you struggle on tests or other assignments. The tests are slowly building off of each other so you are prepared for the final. Opt out of the textbook and just watch videos.

class wasn't too hard, just study and set aside time to complete the modules. SO much extra credit it is insane (retake all 3 midterms for 30 points) also quizzes have unlimited attempts so thats nice. TAs were helpful but the lecture videos included way too much extra content. amoeba sisters on youtube taught me all i needed to know for the tests

She is super great! I loved her class and thought everything was very clear to follow. All of her units are also gospel related in some way. She is easily reachable and gives many chances for improvement. Such a great class!

The tests were very difficult but there are opportunities to make up points. The homework and lectures didn't prepare you well for the tests. There is so much information being covered that it was hard to know what to study for. I studied for hours but didn't do good on the exams. Luckily the extra credit and homework made up for my bad test scores

Not a favorite. Homework did not prepare you for the test well at all. I would study for a few hours before the test and get a pretty rough grade. She once asked for feedback for the class, but then left salty replies to any student who had anything negative to say. boring lectures, but easily accessible. Doable, but I wouldn't do it again

I took cell 120 online last during Fall and I was a bit worried about taking it online but it actually wasn't too bad I could have gotten an A if I had been more organized about deadlines but its pretty easy to get an A in the class. The proctored exams aren't too complicated I studied for a couple of hours before taking them and did pretty well.
Fantastic class! You learn a lot, and all at your own pace. Also, there is SO MUCH extra credit, you would have to try very hard to not get an A.
Very organized class and clear expectations. You are prepared to succeed. Dr. Wilcox explains things very clearly and gives every opportunity possible in an online course to help. Take it from her!

Dr. Wilcox is nice, but the workload was a bit much for a GE class or entry level pre req. BIO class. The late work policy was also too strict. No exceptions to turn work in late for any reason. The recorded lectures were good. So were the unlimited attempts at the weekly quizzes and each midterm could be retaken once for a max of 10 points.

This class was incredibly easy. There are three midterms (50 points each), and if you just retake them after, you can earn 10 points back (30 extra credit points total). Plus you can use your notes and other resources when you retake. This makes it super easy to get a high grade! She explains things so well I think the textbook is a waste of money!

LOVED the class and the professor! Dr. Wilcox is amazing at explaining hard concepts in a clear way. I could never attend her reviews due to my schedule but always watched them afterwards. I'm a science person so the class was easy for me but might be harder for others (the meiosis and mitosis sections for example).

Great class. Took AP bio in HS so it was a breeze, but definitely a great professor. She explained everything very clearly, gave you every opportunity to make up for a poor test grade, if needed. Would highly recommend her for anyone taking this course. I didn't use the textbook, you don't need it.
This professor has so many great resources to help you succeed. I would definitely recommend this professor if you are going to take this class

I took this class online and her lectures were amazing. Very clear format to her class and opportunities for extra credit. Not too labor intensive. Really focuses on students learning and applying the concepts rather than memorizing procedures and random facts. Super willing to answer questions in office hours. If you can, take this class from her!

Dr. Wilcox did a great job. Her recorded lectures were awesome while I took this class online over the summer. I got back surgery during the class and she worked with me awesomely. Would take it again.

I love Professor Wilcox. I took her for PDBio 120 and now CELL 305. I loved her both times. She's super caring, and the class is fairly easy. My one gripe about this class was there were group assignments about once a month, and my group was a nightmare. Everything else was simple and straightforward.

I took Cell 120 online over the summer and let me say that this was a difficult class to take over the summer. Dr. Wilcox was an amazing professor, and I'm grateful for how she set her online class up. Her online class included online lectures, group projects, and weekly quizzes. Her focus is on the application of the materials so know your stuff!

She is amazing at explaining things well. I am a science beginner. I met with her over zoom and she walked me through some of the exam questions I missed. She is very willing to help, she really wants her students to succeed. She gives the option to re-do exams with notes to get a few extra credit points. Great communication.(Summer Term)

She has been one of the best professors I've had at BYU. Her online class was super easy but was very informative. I have never seen a professor teach so simply yet effectively. She offers extra credit on every test and there were at least 4 reviews before each of them. Please take Cell 120 from her.

Dr. Wilcox was one of the most caring professors I've had. The class itself was super well organized and allowed for flexibility without falling behind. I took this class for the biology general and it was the best decision. Lots of extra credit opportunities too if you're not a great test taker like me. Great class.

Taking Phys online was the best decision. There is SO MUCH Extra credit- about 10-12% on every test. Online homework gives you 3 chances. Lectures are clear and the reviews match what is on the test. I love being able to do it at my own pace, this class is not demanding at all for 4 credits.

Probably the single most caring professor I've seen at BYU. She puts jokes into tests to help you relax which are also free points. LOTS of extra credit. I had a 110% for the majority of the semester. Super easy course especially if you took bio in high school. Prof. Wilcox is the BEST!

Put in the work & the class won't be difficult. This was the first semester the class was online.. took a while for the prof + students to gain momentum. Watch profs lectures first! This is how you will learn the content, then do hw. Wouldn't take again bc I prefer in person. TAs are incredible, they pull all the weight. Class is a solid foundation

This is a great class was great. If you've never taken a bio class before, this will be difficult, but if you put in the work you'll be fine. Tests are pretty difficult, so make sure you study hard! The TAs for this class are very helpful, so advantage of them. Also Dr. Wilcox is very caring and intelligent which makes the class easier. 10/10

I really only found two tags that could be applied for this professor or lack of... She really was not present in the online class and the TA's took the class over. The homework did not match the tests and this was the most frustrating. Dr. Wilcox seems nice and everything but at the end of the day her 30 min lectures once a week were not worth it.

Dr. Wilcox is completely on-demand, so you won't attend lectures live. She is really caring and sends out lots of emails letting students know when her office hours are. Her and the TA's have lots of live reviews each week, and even though they aren't mandatory, you should definitely go. Lowest test score is dropped, which is a huge plus.

Dr. Wilcox was great. The only thing that had to stay on your grade was the final. You could drop anything else that you wanted. She didn't make us buy the textbook, but instead gave us links to youtube videos. Her lectures were clear and easy to understand

Dr. Wilcox is THE BEST. Teaches material clearly and presents it in many different ways so its easy to understand for everyone. Provides YouTube video links so you can complete reading summaries without buying the textbook. Really wants her students to understand and be able to apply the material. Lectures aren't mandatory but so worth your time.

Dr. Wilcox was a great professor. She provided videos for us to watch so you do not need to purchase the textbook. The final exam is worth a ton, so studying for the final was quite stressful but for the rest of the semester it was quite manageable.

Chillest grader at BYU. you can drop literally everything except the final. makes it easy to succeed. She teaches to the test, so its good for grades, but tests are difficult, they require a lot of critical thinking. Lectures are simple. DON'T BUY THE BOOK, She has reading assignments for each unit, but has YouTube videos to replace the book.

Dr. Wilcox is by far my favorite professor. She really cares about how her students are doing. She is a great teacher and offers many helpful tricks to understand the material. Her grading is the best because the way it is set up, you aren't screwed if you're a bad test taker. She gives you the chance to get 5% back on exams, and textbook isn't req
Dr. Wilcox is awesome, she really understands college students and she offers the opportunity to watch YouTube videos instead of read from the textbook. Her grading scheme is bizarre but fair.

The class is very well organized. There are 5 homework assignments, 10 reading quizzes, and four midterms. And you can drop any bad scores! Be warned, you can't drop the final and it is 33% of your grade. Luckily, if you have a basic biology background, this class will be a breeze.

Dr. Wilcox is awesome! Her class is not one you can just show up and pass, but you have the option to drop most any score besides the final exam. This is because she wants you to practice and actually learn so you take something away from the class, so it's awesome. She's engaging and caring and gives lots of extra credit opportunities in class.

Dr. Wilcox is so far my overall favorite professor at BYU. Her teaching style is basic but works well, her class is structured very reasonably. The tests are not easy but she gives all the tools necessary to be completely prepared. She's an amazing person to say the least. She's young, and relates well with her students. Must-take if you're pre-med

Not a lot of homework and what she gives is super easy! She's super sweet and puts in a lot of effort to make sure you understand the material. Super easy course, but you actually do learn things, so the best of both worlds! Highly recommend her for PDBIO 120. Also, she gives you a free alternative to the textbook so that saves you tons of money

Minimal, easy homework. Lectures are not fast-paced at all. Lets you drop any exam or the homeworks if you want. Easy A. The average is a 92% right now... All the notes are online so you dont even really need to come to class. She seems to be the much better choice for PDBIO 120.

Solid choice for PDBIO120. She cares about her students (learned ALL 200+ names by the third week). Want's her students to succeed. Tests are hard but if you study you will be fine. Study with a group. No textbook needed. Great general for first year, first semester. Take if you don't like normal Bio

She is the most helpful teacher I have ever had. You may drop all tests(except for final), all homework/quizzes, and literally lets you review old tests and possible test questions. Yes her tests are hard, but then again they are straight forward if you actually listen to her lectures and read/watch the hw. Take her class!! She's way funny, too.

Dr. Wilcox is such a wonderful teacher. She truly cares about each of her students and wants us all to do well in her class. The grading of her class is slightly strange but is very helpful because she lets you drop whatever you'd like! Her tests are hard and confusing but if you study, and with her helpful preparation you'll do great!

Dr. Wilcox was a great professor! Super sweet and allows you to drop all of your midterms if you choose to. The only thing you have to keep in your grade is the final which is hard but if you study enough, you'll do great. She also is very caring and understands that life happens outside of the classroom.

Professor Wilcox is awesome! She's a great teacher. She explains things well and prepares you for the tests. Her tests aren't terrible but you do have to really study for them. Don't expect this to be an easy A class. You have to work for it, but it's very doable. The final can be your grade, but I recommend doing everything because it's not easy.

Loved the class! Record the lectures, she has a lot of info packed into them, It helped to listen to them twice. She really really cares about students and wants everyone to learn the material. Study in advance for the tests and you'll be fine.

Overall a very nice professor but just does not know how to teach well. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well but just is not a good teacher. First day of class she says her tests aren't confusing but her tests are the definition of confusing.

Dr. Wilcox creates a comfortable, clear classroom and course.   Questions are welcomed in the class group setting and personally with her. She teaches well, helps students well, and motivates well.   Extra credit acts as another great recovery net for any difficult topics/tests.

This class is very easy. Dr. Wilcox does a good job of explaining things and the way that she grades is very forgiving. You do the work and you will get a good grade in this class. The homework was very easy.

Strange class.  Most of the material is super easy and class felt like it was a joke.  Dr. Wilcox treated us like little kids and I didn't appreciate that.  Homework was a breeze.  The tests were absolutely ridiculous.  Besides being full of errors, they are designed to trick and do not reflect in any way what we learn in class.

Dr. wilcox is a great professor and is super helpful.  Her grading style is super forgiving and she offers a ton of chances to succeed.  You will learn a lot from her classes!  Little homework.  The only down fall of her class was that you get to the tests and feel like the questions are way harder than any you have done before.

Dr. Wilcox is a great teacher but her tests are hard! You can't just show up to class and think you're good. Make sure and go over the extra packets and outside of class work she offers. It helps a lot with the test.

The class is really easy, and Dr. Wilcox is really sweet, but sometimes she can mess up and get confusing. However the material is super easy and extra credit is offered. She also lets you drop a bunch of assignments, including all of your midterms if you want, which can either help or hurt you.

Dr. Wilcox is great! Lectures are clear and powerpoints are online, tests are straight-forward, and homework prepares you well for the tests. She lets you drop any test but the final, so if you do poorly, just drop the test and learn the information better for the final. Super easy class if you study, and it doesn't take a lot of time.
Dr. Wilcox was a great professor and her class was super easy. Show up to class and work a little in the class and you'll get an a

Professor Wilcox is a great lady that truly cares about her students. I feel like she worked really hard to help us understand the material. The one thing I didn't like about her was that she would teach us the very basics in class and give us easy practice problems to do, and then the tests were about ten times harder than anything we had seen.

Dr. Wilcox is awesome! I think this was her first semester teaching at BYU but she has done an awesome job! As long as you went to class and studied a bit for the tests, you are pretty much golden. Also, the TA's are a great help for the homework and stuff, so that helps out a ton too! Definitely recommend!

Our whole class became best friends, Shamae is so fun and kind. She's knowledgeable, honest, and pushes you to do your best. I learned so many things I didn't know. My only struggle was feeling like I didn't get enough feedback on my drafts to improve them as much as she wanted, but to be fair I did take this class on accident.

This is my most favorite class I have ever taken. Shamae Budd is a truly spectacular individual and she knows what she is talking about when it comes to writing. She will make you work to really find your writing voice and it is so worth it. She genuinely cares about people and wants them to succeed with their goals. I would 100% take this again.

I loved taking this class from Shamae! I will say that this class is not hard, but it's time-consuming with reading, discussions, papers due every two weeks, workshop feedback, final portfolio, etc. I did enjoy it however Shamae will be honest with you about your writing so be prepared to be humbled into a better writer. It was a fun class though!

I had Shamae for my ENGL 218 class, Creative Writing. Shamae is a fantastic professor. She is kind, accommodating, and she gives great feedback. My writing has improved exponentially in her class. There is a lot of reading poetry, essays, and short stories and discussing them as assignments. But these readings are fascinating and really help!!

Dr. McQ put a lot of effort into his teaching! He clearly prepared thought out lectures and helped us understand everything necessary. This made the hardest class I've ever taken manageable. He struggled a little in office hours with less preparation, though.

Dr McQ is actually the best!! 341 is such a hard class but he made it fun! He goes into great depth on his proofs which helps you understand it better and gives a great resource to go back on. His lecture notes and office hours are amazing! I'm praying I can take another class from him.

Incredible professor. I would change my whole major, just to take every one of his classes. He's very new, so it was a gamble to take him, but it paid off big time. His teaching helped me to see the beauty and excellence of mathematics for the first time in my life. He is young, funny, and spiritual. He leads students to discover, not memorize.

Hardest class I've ever taken but I love Dr. McQ! He's hilarious and so good at putting himself in his students' shoes. He put in the effort to reach out and help me when I was having a hard time and didn't want to ask for help myself. Also he posts his lecture notes which are so helpful! One of my favorite professors so far!

Dr. McQ is the BEST! His goofy sense of humor always makes class fun. 341 is a difficult class, but during lectures and office hours, he goes through each proof thoroughly in a way that's (usually) very clear and easy to understand. He genuinely loves and cares about his students, and I love the connections he makes between math and the gospel.

Dr. McQ is the GOAT!!! Hands down one of the funniest people I've ever met (my friends and I quote him on the daily) and lectures are so entertaining. Linear algebra is known for being difficult but he's great at explaining stuff and his homework is super manageable. Also gives lots of cool spiritual insights between math and the gospel.

Dr McQ is the best!! 341 is a beast, but he made it very approachable and took time to make sure that we had all of the resources we needed. He was funny, entertaining, and highly intelligent. I also appreciated his insights on how the math connected to real life and moral principles.

Normally 215 is an online class, but Dr. McQuarrie taught an in-person section of it. He basically helped us through the coding labs. To anyone with any prior programming experience, the course is a breeze. To anyone without, Dr. McQuarrie is there to help you. He is very helpful and explains the parts that might get tricky.

Dr. McQuarrie is awesome! This was his first year teaching here but I could not tell. His explanations of the math were clear. He knew all our names by the first week. He was better at connecting his subject to the gospel than any of my other non-religion teachers here so far.

I LOVE Dr.McQuarrie. He is so funny and makes the math make sense. I kind of thought this class was difficult just because it is hard to conceptually understand what is going on but Dr.McQuarrie will make it make sense. He is also so funny. This man needs a raise!

Shane is the bomb. Despite the labs sometimes being confusing, he is always there to help us understand the content. He's really chill with helping you out and very understanding about problems that arise.
Yo shane is the dopest!!!!!! We love him.
He is a spectacular teacher
Shane is awesome, sometimes it takes a long time to get his help and attention if you need it, but when he gives it it is super helpful. He's a genius
I love Professor McQuarrie! He is truly a professor that goes above and beyond for his students.
Professor McQuarrie or Shai Shai as he prefers to be called is the most intense and enlightening professor ever.  If you can get used to his soul piercing stares you'll learn deep and hidden things.
You have to earn it, but Shane gives fair grades. He's very helpful, but expects you to do a lot on your own. Would take again.

This class was fun,  I felt like I grew as a person. She addresses issues in a way that doesn't seem like a repeat of what I learned in other classes. My favorite thing about her is that she's more concerned about helping students learn than making her class hard. She also offers up to 8% extra credit so it you want an A you can get one.

She's a little too PC for me. I felt like I was getting a lecture from a CNN reporter some days. Shares good thoughts most of the time, but she doesn't know how to express them clearly in a way that doesn't feel like a moral reprimand on American majority groups. I'm all for equality in family life but as a white male, I felt misunderstood.

Shannon is AMAZING. She is so caring, kind, and wants you to succeed. She is very passionate about what she teaches. The concepts I learned in this class completely and positively helped to change my perspective of life, culture, and people. SO GOOD.

She is absolutely one of my favorite professors! She taught us so many incredible things that I have implemented. She's a really great person, but this was the most unorganized class I've ever taken. Great teacher! Shares many useful resources and changes how you view teaching!
She is a paradigm shifter, and totally transformed the way I saw teaching Spanish. Seriously, excellent. It's worth your time.

Hands down the best teacher I have had in my four years of BYU. She is one of the sharpest, most professional, most grounded teachers in the country. Amazing teacher. she's changed my life!
She's super nice and helpful. has a huge passion for teaching

Prof Chrsitensen is the sweetest and genuinely cares about students' lives. Course content isnt the best and the tests are difficult if you dont do the homework! She is always willing to help and takes the time to explain things many times. Would take again!

This class was pretty okay! I took it at 8 am, but she was always excited for us to be there. We worked with table groups a lot, so it was nice when she let us sit where we wanted after a few weeks. She is super sweet and a good professor, even though the class was pretty repetitive. There is a take home and testing portion of the exams.

The professor is nice, but I felt like I wasted time going to class because she was all over the place, and I learned more from YouTube. I wouldn't take this class again. She's not tech-savvy and loses in-class assignments regularly. Not many assignments to help even out your overall grade with homework vs exams.

I adore Sister Christensen! She is so kind and willing to help. Hands down my fav professor! The content is hard and confusing and I don't think its very applicable but if you have to take it, take it from her! There is a take home portion of the exam which is open note and then a testing center portion. You can earn back credit too for half points

I love Sister Christensen! Anyone who watches her teach would know that she loves her students! I felt like this class was the right about of easy/difficult. There are assignments every class day, but most of the time they aren't too bad. And when they are a little confusing, she is more than willing to work with you and help you figure it out!

Sharon Christensen was one of the nicest professors I have had at byu. She was really understanding, and made learning about math fun. She has a grader that does all of the grading, and she was harsher than expected. Professor Christensen fixed any mistakes if you talk to her about it. Pay attention and you will learn a lot.

Sister Christensen is the best! She was so caring and wanted to make sure we all had a good understanding of the content. She was willing to work with students who are struggling, and always wanted to make sure we were okay. She's a great teacher. Homework was never very difficult, and if you pay attention to lectures, you'll do great.

Homework assignment every class, not too hard, tedious. Test corrections are available after every test. A lot of work for 2-credit class. Teacher was SO nice but interesting format. I don't know how well I feel about actually teaching, I just knew what to do to get 100% on assignments and tests. Textbook ($20) that you never use (max 2x for hw).

I actually really enjoyed this class and Professor Christensen. She is very kind and really cares about your success. She is willing to explain/clarify concepts, you just have to ask :) The class format is pretty much the same as 305 and everything is straightforward. Workload is very manageable. Would definitely recommend Sister Christensen!

I learned a lot about math in this class although not much about teaching math. Her teaching style is just giving us work and having us figure it out, she almost never models math problems or gives feedback so it can be hard to know if you are right or not unless you directly ask. There is math homework every day but I didn't find it too hard.
I truly felt like she cared about me as an individual and wanted the best for me. She picked out activities that has helped me to gain a better perspective of the math world.

Professor Christensen's lectures were not very helpful. She starts doing a math problem, and asks the class what the next steps are. She continues the problem with the response that the student gave, and she would get through almost the whole problem before telling us it was wrong. This made taking notes hard. I learned everything from the TA.

Your success in this class depends on your TA for lab, since they are the ones mainly answering your questions. LOT's of hw, but they help your grade. The lectures are very dry, but straight forward and she takes time to explain. Tests have a multiple choice portion (so you get the 4 points or 0). Tests are hard, but fair.

I liked Sister Christensen. She is very caring and you can always go to her if you have any questions or concerns. This class is very similar to MTHED 305 - group work, 2-3 pages of homework, etc. The tests were really long which kinda bothered me, but she is a solid choice. I just didn't like how it was a replica of MTHED 305 - boring!

The lectures were completely useless. I couldn't understand anything she taught until I took the time to read 500 pages of a calculus textbook and teach myself all the material 2 days before the final. She gives only one example per concept and moves on before everyone is able to understand. Not worth taking unless you already know Calculus well.

Self-graded homework twice a week, all of the tests are take-home (including the final). Easy to get an A as long as you somewhat pay attention in class. Textbook is not necessary!!! Only if you want to use it to learn concepts deeper or use it in a future classroom.

Sister Christensen is wonderful! She cares about each student individually, and she allows for test corrections. She was very willing to answer questions and make sure that everyone understands the material. I never felt nervous to bring up questions I had about the material. I recommend her class!

No Extra Credit available. The grading is hard, they almost ask you to have 100% on written homework, or you will lose point the grading system of math dept is harsh during the exam. her lecture is not bad, however, her lecture doesn't cooperate with TA lab very well. it often confuse students and not efficient at all.

This is my least favorite class of all time. Math at this level exists purely to spite you. If Im not going to use the math I learned as a junior in high school, when in my life will I ever need to find the antideritive of a trig function? Aside from all that, Professor Christiansen is wonderful and does her best to help her students succeed.

She's a solid fine as far as professors go, conveys the material clearly and is good about answering questions but isn't particularly entertaining or inspiring. Stay on top of the homework and you should be fine

Sister Christensen has been the most caring teacher I have ever encountered at my 3 years at BYU. She is aways so willing to help if you fall behind or don't understand the content. There is a lot of homework but the answer keys are always posted online and they are graded on completion. She allows test corrections. Great at explaining new concepts

I personally did not like her teaching style at all. She was very vague and it made learning calculus for the first time near impossible. Labs were useless but attendance was graded. If you can avoid her at all, do it.

I took her for MTHED 305 and 306. She is amazing. So organized and always ready to answer questions. Cares about individual students. Teaches with clarity and sets clear expectations. Allows test corrections. She just wants to make sure you understand everything. Would take again for sure.

Sister Christensen is awesome! She did a very good job of explaining everything clearly. She would answer any questions you had and would answer them thoroughly. She made herself accessible outside of class and was willing to work with you as a student. Only thing was class was a little dry, but you're there to learn Calculus not be entertained.
The lectures are somewhat useful, the TA labs are more useful, it was still a pretty easy A since the cutoff for an A was a 89.6 ish and like a 86 for an A-.

She's a nice person but a terrible teacher, really you'd be better off just straight reading the textbook. The homework doesn't line up with the lectures always so I spent a lot of time on khan academy looking up homework problems that we hadn't gone over in class.
Not a bad choice for a teacher. There's kinda a lot of work outside of class, but nothing you can't handle. Tests are fine as long as you study the tests used for past semesters.

Sister Christensen is very nice... but she taught straight from the book, yet made attendance mandatory, even for TA labs. Her office hours were at times that did not work with anyone's schedule. Make sure you have a great TA.

Great professor! Lectures are very interactive,  full of group discussion, and hands on activities. If you don't understand anything she takes the time to help. She gives  homework after every class. You can ask questions about the homework  during class and she is more than happy to explain it.
She is a SOLID choice for a math professor. She is kind, and respectful, AND for sure knows her math. She gives good lectures and the TAs are very good (shout out to Goodson). 11/10 would take again

Sister Christensen is so Christlike, and because of this she does all she can to help you succeed. If you don't understand anything at all, she will definitely take the time to help you. You participate in class in groups, and you always get to ask questions about the homework. I would definitely take from her again.

Sis. Christensen is so willing to help you figure things out and makes things easy to understand. Classes are hands on and enjoyable, and homework helps you learn the concepts. I constantly was having "lightbulb moments" and finally understanding things I never did about math. She is a fantastic example of how to teach kids math. Loved this class!!

She is the most patient person I know. Honestly she resembles Christ in so many ways- her teaching and her patience. Also a great math teacher- but the most important thing you'll learn from her is how to be a saint.

Passionate about topics, sees the humor in history, wont baby you but is fair. You wont like his classes if you want something easy, don't like when someone challenges your opinion, or struggle paying attention in lectures. For history lovers he's pretty perfect. Take notes, review before tests. His classes are designed to challenge you to learn

As others have said, his opinions are 'facts' and he will ignore students who disagree. Loves to bring politics up and insists that he is correct and everyone who disagrees hates truth. Miller is nice, but not my fav professor. Every class was a lengthy, confusing lectures. He taught his opinions as fact. Papers were not graded consistently by the TAs. Exams were INCREDIBLY hard (probably due to the lack of structure and review materials) He curved the tests substantially, but that was only because of the dismal class averages.

I have always hated history classes but Professor Miller's was better than normal. He was the first history teacher who helped me understand why history matters. His class is basically all lectures which are not recorded so you have to come to class. There are a lot of readings but I didn't really do them and I was fine.

Nice guy, and I found his lectures interesting. There are only three book reviews and five article responses, which don't prepare you well for the tests. Yes, he curves the tests, but one outlier destroys it. The tests are specific and hard to study for because there are no study guides or review sessions; the midterm and final are weighted 55%.

The class is interesting but the tests are pretty stout. Not my favorite GE I've taken at BYU, I'd probably take something else if I had to do it over. You definitely should be in class as much as you possibly can.

His lectures are interesting and engaging. He is knowledgeable and offers good insight. There is a textbook but I didnt even rent it and did fine His tests are super hard but he gives a large curve to make up for it. Other assignments aren't bad. You definitely have to attend the lectures and take good notes to do well.

Professor Miller was a great history 202 professor. He took the material and made it incredibly interesting. He has few homework assignments that are easy 1 page essays. He requires a lot of reading but they are manageable and interesting. He helps you see the importance of history and gives you a new perspective on history through his lectures.

His classes were so boring. They were an hour and 15 minutes long and we just sat there the whole time listening to him. It was really hard to focus. The tests were so hard and stressful. He curved them up, but it was still stressful to take them. Lots of reading every class. The lectures focused a lot on his personal opinions of the topic.

Tests are so random and mostly from lectures. SOOOO much reading. Two books and a whole textbook cover to cover. He gives no rubrics or grading criteria for his papers and gives absolutely no feedback, just a number grade. He seemingly grades them based on his opinions. Don't even get me started on his horrible lecture 
(soap box) on feminism.

This class is very heavily weighted by tests, and the tests are really hard. There is a ton of information thrown at you and there isn't really a study guide or TA reviews to help, so you are kinda on your own. Interesting class though!

I was actually really nervous for this class but it was not hard! Miller has so much knowledge and his lectures were so awesome!! There were a couple book responses and the test were difficult but he usually curves all the test by 20 points so as long as you show up to class youll be fine!
Understood his topic well.

I.S. class. Most disengaged class I have ever taken. Received zero feedback. Unsure how someone was able to redo the exam and portfolio. 2 pages to read per (15) lesson(s) from Prof. Miller, an extra book, and straight reading through the textbook cover to cover. Learned a lot but dry & difficult to stay focused. 7 quizzes, 2 tests, 9 papers-Prtfl.

Man I am so torn about professor Miller. On one hand, his lectures are great and the papers arent so bad... but on the other, his tests are nightmares..... You have no idea what to expect on his tests and they cover a lot of material. It is a miracle I passed his class considering the difficulty of the tests given. Pop quizzes are rare.

(I took his indep. study college class in high school so this may not apply to you) This is a reasoning-based class, and as a science nerd I worked super hard for an A+. He let me resubmit the exams and portfolio (hardest part of course). Loved the historical perspectives the course gave me, e.g. global culture & economic and demographic history.

Dr. Miller is a great lecturer and very engaging. The class is graded on a curve so that everyone gets 20 or more points added to their midterm and final exam. The readings are usually a page and you dont really need the text book. Super great class, easy to pass, definitely take him for 202

Professor Miller is one of those gem professors who just blow you away with their knowledge but is also really humble. His lectures taught me a lot about life and how to think outside the box. This was one of my FAVORITE classes. Seriously. It was phenomenal. He is a wonderful teacher!!! I loved each lecture. He grades fair. The tests are hard, but if you attend class then you should do fine, however no attendance is taken.

Miller is great. He teaches history by topic instead of chronology. I left class feeling like I really understood the principles discussed. From the first day, I knew I had to keep this class. His lectures perfectly integrate history and the gospel in an interesting way. There is also test curves!

This class was amazing. It's structured differently than any other history class I have taken.  Teaches history by topic. He's one of those that teaches you more than just subject matter.

Great teacher.  I have had him for 200 and 202.  Very interesting lectures - sometimes boring of course, but useful.  Take good notes and study for the test and you will do well in the class!
Dr. Miller is really nice and helpful, but he doesn't make sense all of the time. He wants you to write like, "See spot run, spot ran fast" No wordiness at all! But graded pretty nicely. Good man.
He is a very intellingent, but humble teacher.  Helps you understand the world better.  Classes were always intellectually engaging.  Loved his style, would go to his class just for fun!
Very personable, very smart and very kind. Tests hard but has a good curve.

Professor Miller is professional yet personable, tough yet fair, and helped me learn for myself how to improve my writing instead of how to "just do enough".  I enjoyed the essays I wrote in his class and the amazing basis of knowledge and training he readily provided in his lectures.

I really enjoyed Miller.  He is challenging and his class isn't for the weak.  But it's perfectly do-able.  I got an A without too much effort.  Miller knows a lot and challenges the ignorance of students.

Doesnt allow his pp slides available for students. He is a know it all and lets you know that you know nothing. Extremely tough on grading. Crazy tests. Not consistent or clear on what he expects from you. The worst teacher I've ever had.
gives great leactures, funny, very helpful and fair

Passionate about topics, sees the humor in history, wont baby you but is fair. You wont like his classes if you want something easy, don't like when someone challenges your opinion, or struggle paying attention in lectures. For history lovers he's pretty perfect. Take notes, review before tests. His classes are designed to challenge you to learn

As others have said, his opinions are 'facts' and he will ignore students who disagree. Loves to bring politics up and insists that he is correct and everyone who disagrees hates truth. Its remarkable to watch. In one class, he was preaching a Marxist view of a coming class-based war, ignoring sincere comments by students who disagreed. Steer clear

Miller is nice, but not my fav professor. Every class was a lengthy, confusing lectures. He taught his opinions as fact. Papers were not graded consistently by the TAs. Exams were INCREDIBLY hard (probably due to the lack of structure and review materials) He curved the tests substantially, but that was only because of the dismal class averages.

I have always hated history classes but Professor Miller's was better than normal. He was the first history teacher who helped me understand why history matters. His class is basically all lectures which are not recorded so you have to come to class. There are a lot of readings but I didn't really do them and I was fine.

Nice guy, and I found his lectures interesting. There are only three book reviews and five article responses, which don't prepare you well for the tests. Yes, he curves the tests, but one outlier destroys it. The tests are specific and hard to study for because there are no study guides or review sessions; the midterm and final are weighted 55%.

The class is interesting but the tests are pretty stout. Not my favorite GE I've taken at BYU, I'd probably take something else if I had to do it over. You definitely should be in class as much as you possibly can.

His lectures are interesting and engaging. He is knowledgeable and offers good insight. There is a textbook but I didnt even rent it and did fine His tests are super hard but he gives a large curve to make up for it. Other assignments aren't bad. You definitely have to attend the lectures and take good notes to do well.

Professor Miller was a great history 202 professor. He took the material and made it incredibly interesting. He has few homework assignments that are easy 1 page essays. He requires a lot of reading but they are manageable and interesting. He helps you see the importance of history and gives you a new perspective on history through his lectures.

His classes were so boring. They were an hour and 15 minutes long and we just sat there the whole time listening to him. It was really hard to focus. The tests were so hard and stressful. He curved them up, but it was still stressful to take them. Lots of reading every class. The lectures focused a lot on his personal opinions of the topic.

Tests are so random and mostly from lectures. SOOOO much reading. Two books and a whole textbook cover to cover. He gives no rubrics or grading criteria for his papers and gives absolutely no feedback, just a number grade. He seemingly grades them based on his opinions. Don't even get me started on his horrible lecture 
(soap box) on feminism.

This class is very heavily weighted by tests, and the tests are really hard. There is a ton of information thrown at you and there isn't really a study guide or TA reviews to help, so you are kinda on your own. Interesting class though!

I was actually really nervous for this class but it was not hard! Miller has so much knowledge and his lectures were so awesome!! There were a couple book responses and the test were difficult but he usually curves all the test by 20 points so as long as you show up to class youll be fine!
Understood his topic well.

I.S. class. Most disengaged class I have ever taken. Received zero feedback. Unsure how someone was able to redo the exam and portfolio. 2 pages to read per (15) lesson(s) from Prof. Miller, an extra book, and straight reading through the textbook cover to cover. Learned a lot but dry & difficult to stay focused. 7 quizzes, 2 tests, 9 papers-Prtfl.

Man I am so torn about professor Miller. On one hand, his lectures are great and the papers arent so bad... but on the other, his tests are nightmares..... You have no idea what to expect on his tests and they cover a lot of material. It is a miracle I passed his class considering the difficulty of the tests given. Pop quizzes are rare.

(I took his indep. study college class in high school so this may not apply to you) This is a reasoning-based class, and as a science nerd I worked super hard for an A+. He let me resubmit the exams and portfolio (hardest part of course). Loved the historical perspectives the course gave me, e.g. global culture & economic and demographic history.

Dr. Miller is a great lecturer and very engaging. The class is graded on a curve so that everyone gets 20 or more points added to their midterm and final exam. The readings are usually a page and you dont really need the text book. Super great class, easy to pass, definitely take him for 202

Professor Miller is one of those gem professors who just blow you away with their knowledge but is also really humble. His lectures taught me a lot about life and how to think outside the box. In other words, he made did an amazing job making such a long history class interesting. Take his class! If you really want to learn you won't regret it!

This was one of my FAVORITE classes. Seriously. It was phenomenal. He is a wonderful teacher!!! I loved each lecture. He grades fair. The tests are hard, but if you attend class then you should do fine, however no attendance is taken.

Terrible class. Lectures were unbearably boring. Tests were based on random facts he puts in the lectures. He doesn't post slides, doesn't do a study guide. Class average is around 65 which he curves to an 85. Expect not to learn anything about history. Most of the class is pass/fail essays. Not worth your time to read books or text book.

Miller is great. He teaches history by topic instead of chronology. I left class feeling like I really understood the principles discussed. He is straightforward and provides lots of interesting information. Tests are heavily based on lecture, but the textbook is good to have. Assignments are spread out and easy: 5 one page papers, 2 book reports.

From the first day, I knew I had to keep this class. His lectures perfectly integrate history and the gospel in an interesting way. He does things thematically instead of chronologically, and the most important thing to note is that it is NOT hard to get a good grade if you attend the lectures and do decent on tests. There is also test curves!

Professor Miller was a great instructor and you could tell he enjoyed what he was teaching. There are a few papers but some of them are pass/fail, and all of them are graded easily. His tests are difficult, but he adds a large curve to each one. He also teaches by topics instead of by a timeline, and I enjoyed learning that way

This class was amazing. It's structured differently than any other history class I have taken.  Teaches history by topic.  For example, we had lectures on the history of the family, of agriculture, of warfare, etc. Probably my favorite GE so far.  Homework load isn't too much. Test are a bit difficult, but he curves it so the class average is a B.

Not an easy A for your GE credit, but Professor Miller is one of the top 3 best professors I have had at BYU. He is passionate, knows his stuff, and somehow makes you interested in things you never cared about before. I studied hard for his tests because of how much I respected him. He's one of those that teaches you more than just subject matter.

I thought this class was great! I loved the way the class was structured and I learned quite a bit. I would often leave class still thinking about what we were learning. Miller did a great job of making the subject matter interesting.

I took the class just for a general credit so I already didn't care for it. Going to class was so boring. I tried so hard to pay attention but I couldn't. Sadly his tests are mostly based on lectures, and the tests were so hard. The writing assignments were a piece of cake. I didn't even read the books for the essays and still got great scores.
Professor Miller somehow managed to make history that I have heard a thousand times interesting again.  His tests are hard, but he curves them, and all the questions are  from readings or lectures.

This was an awesome class! Pro. Miller knows what he is talking about and is interesting to listen to. The class is pretty straightforward if you take good notes and do the assignments. The tests are hard but there is always a pretty big curve, so it evens out in the end. I felt like this class opened my eyes to looking at the world differently.

I LOVED THIS CLASS!! This is one of those rare classes where you learn a ton, but it isn't very difficult.  You have to write 7 short essays.  Five of them are only one page, pass-fail & you can make them up if you fail.  The other two are 3 pages each.  The two tests are hard, but he adds a 22 point curve so the class average is still like 88.

Professor Miller is extremely knowledgeable, however sometimes his lectures seem to go off topic and it's difficult to decipher what is relevant information and what is just him chit chatting. Tests are near impossible, got a 58% on Exam 1, but the curve brought it to an 80%. Overall, too tough for a GE. Only other points are writing assignments.

Professor Miller is really Helpful in class. The writing assignments were huge parts of the grade. He wants you to be concise and straightforward with your writing in order to not take up more space than necessary. After writing, BE SURE to have someone read through your paper and edit it.

This guy knows what he is talking about. The class is very interesting if you want to learn. The tests and assignments can be difficult, but not impossible. I loved the class, but you need to take it seriously if you want to get a good grade.

Looks like Bill Nye the science guy. Very nice, very respectful. Read the primary sources at least- I didn't read the textbook at all the second half of the semester and still did ok. Take good notes and study em! 2 book responses (750 words) and 5 primary source responses, (1 page, SS 11pt font)

Great Professor, Really interesting, he does require alot of reading most of which isnt on the tests, go to class, take good notes and study them and you will get a good grade.  Has an awesome curve, he makes the class average an 85%, really tries to help us do well, great professor, i really enjoyed this class
Teaches things that aren't on the test.  Grades on a curve and isn't that fair.

Very interesting teacher, uses overhead with notes and pictures. Fair, very willing to help students.  Very likeable. Really knows his topic. Even though you have to work, learn alot don't feel like he's too over the top on his expectations.

This was colonial latin america. Professor Miller is one of the best teachers i've ahd in my opnion. Really easy lectures to understand, and his tests come straight from lecture so you can't miss them. Tests a little difficult but just study your notes a ton and you should be good. Really nice guy.
Great teacher.  I have had him for 200 and 202.  Very interesting lectures - sometimes boring of course, but useful.  Take good notes and study for the test and you will do well in the class!
Dr. Miller is really nice and helpful, but he doesn't make sense all of the time. He wants you to write like, "See spot run, spot ran fast" No wordiness at all! But graded pretty nicely. Good man.
He is a very intellingent, but humble teacher.  Helps you understand the world better.  Classes were always intellectually engaging.  Loved his style, would go to his class just for fun!
Very personable, very smart and very kind. Tests hard but has a good curve.

Professor Miller is professional yet personable, tough yet fair, and helped me learn for myself how to improve my writing instead of how to "just do enough".  I enjoyed the essays I wrote in his class and the amazing basis of knowledge and training he readily provided in his lectures.

I really enjoyed Miller.  He is challenging and his class isn't for the weak.  But it's perfectly do-able.  I got an A without too much effort.  Miller knows a lot and challenges the ignorance of students.

Doesnt allow his pp slides available for students. He is a know it all and lets you know that you know nothing. Extremely tough on grading. Crazy tests. Not consistent or clear on what he expects from you. The worst teacher I've ever had.
gives great leactures, funny, very helpful and fair
Astonishing professor. He is very talented and 100% possesses the teaching ability and desire to help you succeed if you will put in the effort. Attendance is mandatory.

Shayne is a fun guy who is very personable. His cross-cultural class was interesting because he has a lot of interesting perspectives. However, the content on the tests was not communicated clearly and I didn't ever know what to expect in terms of grading. I felt completely blindsided and lost which really affected my grade. Very disorganized too.
Dr. Anderson is an amazing, kind, understanding professor who wants his students to succeed. He does a great job creating a wholesome and safe learning environment for all.

I was in SFL 354 and it was AMAZING. I would recommend this class to be required as a GenEd because it was so enlightening. This was not a polarizing class, no views were pushed by the teacher. He encouraged hard discussion and really valued anything everyone said. GREAT teacher! The class was doable. Not hard, but not a "giveaway" A either.

Shayne is one of my favorite professors ever. He really cares about his students. This class is very interesting and beneficial for MFT and social work. He teaches you how to think like a social scientist. The material can be triggering, so class isn't mandatory. One 10 page literature review due at the end but he spaces it out. Tests aren't bad.

Shane was one of the best professors I have ever had at BYU. I would say SFL 335 is a must take if you are in the school of family life,  and interested in therapy. Lectures touch on sensitive topics, but are enlightening and worth it. There is a big paper due at the end of the semester, but you work on it all semester long. TAKE FROM SHANE!
Not the most helpful class, but Professor Owens teaches it well! Not overly difficult. Very fair.

Dr. Owens may be my favorite professor at BYU. He is funny, a great teacher, and is super down to earth. The class requires a below average amount of work to get an A or A-. I would recommend him and the course to anyone.

Professor Owens truly cares about his students. There is quite a bit of reading, but I found a lot of it to be very interesting. He also allows midterm appeals which is really nice. I loved his lectures and he is just such a sweet guy!

Nicest professor I have ever had at BYU. He helps students to truly think about ethics, no matter what their opinion is. He hosts comprehensive reviews before the midterm and final. His class is so light with work outside of the tests and a couple of papers. I would easily recommend Dr. Owens to anyone when they have to take Business Ethics!

Prof Owens cares about his students, but doesn't seem to care about the amount of work required for this class imposed on his students. Compared to other ethics professors, Professor Owens has a mountain of assignments. The TAs also grade harshly despite giving vague or short instructions. Save yourself the pain and take a different professor.
This guy is awesome! He is super caring and it shows. Great guy and the tests are really fair. The only thing was that sometimes the TAs where really tough on grading random projects.

I thought the reviews on here were misleading. He's a super nice guy who actually learns everybody's name in the class....impressive. However, I thought some classes were super boring, the reading quizzes are not worded well. He does let you submit claims on the midterm for the questions you got wrong which I really admired

Professor Owens is amazing! I look forward to his class periods and genuinely hate missing them, they are inspirational and give you a chance to rethink situations - very thought-provoking. The tests are a bit stressful, but I would recommend this class to anyone!

Professor Owens is a gem for BYU! He is super humble and is approachable and kind to all. He goes the extra mile in teaching and preparing test reviews. The class content is interesting and inspirational. He is a top professor for the Marriott School of Business.

Professor Owens is one of the best professors in the business school! He is so knowledgeable but so humble and caring at the same time. His class is full of hands-on learning opportunities that are engaging and intellectually enlarging. He gets to know his students and is such a great example of Christlike leadership. Take his MSB 390 class!!!
This is the BEST professor!! Take this class and any class you can from him. The information is so interesting and he is one of the kindest people you will ever meet! 10/10 recommend!!

THE BEST PROFESSOR! So kind and so good at teaching. All the concepts he brings to life and demonstrates them well to understand fully. Assignments aren't overbearing and are honestly interesting. He prepares you for tests very well.

I took MSB 390 from Professor Owens (Ethics for management) and it was my favorite class I have taken at BYU hands down! He is a fantastic professor, he cares about his students and wants them all to succeed. His lectures are engaging and extremely interesting. He gives a great study guide and review ses. to make sure you are ready for the test.

One the best classes I've taken. This professor was fantastic. There were a lot of assignments, but if you came to class and participated, the assignments were mostly easy and quick (and sometimes done before you left class). Learned a lot of valuable lessons to apply both now and after graduation and this professor's research work is AMAZING.

I believe everyone should have the chance to take a class from Professor Owens. Every lecture was entertaining, funny, informative. He would show us a real life examples, as well as common movie and TV examples that we are familiar with. I look forward to this class every day.

Prof. Owens' class was awesome. He would greet each student at the beginning of class, make a lot of fun lectures, and was genuinely interested in every student he teaches. His quizzes were a little irritating, but his exams were open-book and open-note, and he always accepted appeals for wrong answers. Take this class from Prof. Owens!!

Professor Owens is a wonderful teacher and a great guy. He's really nice and respectful. He and his TA memorized all our names before the semester started. Lectures are genuinely enjoyable. He really likes to keep his class average at like a B+ which is normal but come on it's an ethics class. He doesn't really give helpful feedback on assignments.

Professor Owens practices what he preaches. He is a good man who cares about students. He gave extra credit. He extended deadlines. Tests are open notes. But that is not what makes him a good professor. What makes him so good is how he is a living example of ethics. This class was so fun! I wish I could take it every semester. You need this class!

Dr. Owens is perhaps the best professor I've ever had. I always looked forward to his class. His lectures are dope, the discussion is dope, he's hilarious, and I genuinely learned a lot about how to apply ethics to my personal and business life.

In my 5 years at BYU, this is the best class I have ever taken. And Professor Owens was the best professor I have ever had the privilege to take a class from. I expected this class to be only about religion, but he did an amazing job at teaching all facets of ethics and teaching how to use all points of view to make better ethical decisions.
Sweetest man in the world. 100% recommend

This was probably my favorite class at BYU so far. I love philosophy and business, so it kind of brought the topics together, but I think Prof. Owens took it over the edge for me. He makes a point to be engaging and not waste time. He is thoughtful in his activities and really tries to make the experience educational.

Great discussions in class and the homework load isn't too heavy. Make sure to communicate with Prof. Owens and/or the TA's about the larger papers/assignments so you don't get blindsided by how they choose to grade it. Overall a great class and subject.

Professor Owens is awesome! His classes are extremely interactive but low pressure. He brings the subject to life with games, clips, discussions, and other meaningful activities. His class was super fun, and he is fair and reasonable with grading. Great professor, great class.

Professor Owens' class was a unique experience. I liked that his midterm exam was relatively easy - it involved concepts discussed in class, and he even threw in movie clips to test us on ethical rationalizations. He's a very kind professor and seems very interested in his students' success. He also brought in some fascinating guest speakers.

Business Ethics makes for interesting discussions, but boring readings and assignments.  He doesn't use learningsuite other than for a schedule, which can be a pain and assignments are mostly useless.  Reading isn't necessary for understanding, but required for grade, same with attendance.  Nice guy though.  Tries hard, cares, and listens.

Come to class! The class is so easy and nice, but there were days where she only gave points to those who came to class. Loved the content we covered and how I improved! I cannot recommend her class enough, especially if you want to learn and are passionate about writing!
Coming from a non-writer— Shelli makes writing fun. She cares deeply for her students and inspires through her teaching. I loved this class!

Shelli is the person to take 150 from! She gets through everything you have to do for the semester in a way that allows you to find what you like about writing. She's all about expression, and pretty much anything goes. Super easy class with her, 10/10

Prof. Spotts was amazing! I loved her class! I dreaded taking an advanced writing class at BYU but she made writing enjoyable, easy, and creative. I am not an Elementary Ed major but this class was so worth taking! Her assignments are fun, easy, and simple. I would absolutely recommend taking WRTG 313 from Shelli!
If you take writing 150 you NEED to take it from her, she is amazing.
This class was honestly a breathe of fresh air for me during a busy semester. She is super nice and super forgiving. Definitely my easiest class. There is not very much work at all.

Prof Spotts is incredible. Usually, I hate writing for school, but this class was honestly really enjoyable. Prof Spotts teaches communication rather than academic writing. She sticks to the projects that are required by the department for EVERY Wrtg 150 class, but she alters them to be way more applicable and useful to real life.

Absolutely recommend. Her class is easy, but useful (perfect mix!). She has unorthodox ways... but trust the process! She has really cool tips and tricks (ex: your best ideas come after you hit the snooze button, so take a nap!). You might be making a mistake if you don't take her class. Lax on due dates + lets you be creative and break the rules.

I loved Professor Spotts! She is a super great professor and genuinely cares about all of her students. She understands the heavy load that college is and gives a lot of grace to her students. All of her assignments are actually given with a meaningful purpose and there is no busy work.
This class was so chill and a super easy general credit! Take WRTG 150 from Professor Sports!

Best WRTG150 professor ever! She's super fun to be around and it's more of a discussion based class with a digital dialogue once a week. You have a few projects that you work on throughout the semester. I absolutely hate English and I enjoyed this class! 10/10

Best Professor for Writing 150. Super easy going and gives great feedback. Sometimes I wish should teach more specifics on writing but does give a lot of good tools. She encourages using ChatGPT as a tool to write.

If you like to write, you'll LOVE this class! This is seriously one of the best and most fun classes I've ever taken at BYU and Pro. Spotts is just a joy to be around. Even if you think you're a bad writer but want to improve, this class is for you. She even met with us one-on-one to give us feedback. I LOVED THIS CLASS!!!

Dr. Spotts is amazing and I 10/10 recommend taking her class. She is super kind and accessible, and I always felt happy after her class. She has reasonable workload expectations and is willing to work with you if you need help. Creativity is encouraged.

TAKE WRTG150 FROM HER. So easy and she actually really cares about making you a better writer. Class was fun and she is extremely flexible on due dates. There's a textbook but I never did the reading and it didn't matter much so I wouldn't bother buying it. Shelli rocks

Classes are fun, professor Spotts really cares about you and helping you feel confident as a writer. Plenty of time is given to develop papers and she is flexible with deadlines. Not a class that will overwhelm or stress you. She's the best!

Mrs. Spotts is an amazing teacher. If you have to take Wrtg150 take it from her. The only complaint I can think is that she is a little slow on grading, but this doesn't even bother me because she is such a generous grader.

If you have to take WRTG150, PLEASE take it with Professor Spotts! This is a very "outside of the box" writing class, which I LOVED. You use your own unique style for writing the papers (which there were only 3 of), which sometimes included no official or formal writing at all. I learned a lot about myself and I recommend this class, 11/10!

Shelli is the absolute best!! I heard WRTG 150 was a class that would take up all my time and was jam packed with tons of essays. But this class only consisted of 3 fairly easy essays and a group project at the end. She focuses more on creativity, process, and growth with your writing. Take her for this class!

Best WRTG150 professor. She is a super caring teacher. You need to go to class for attendance points and to understand assignments. She is super willing to work with you and gives great feedback. All the essays are reasonable. Not a heavy workload class. I started to appreciate writing while taking this class.

SHELLI IS THE ABSOLUTE BEST!! My favorite professor I've ever had. She is so caring about her students and is not there to give you busy work. She understands college is a lot of work and we barely have homework in that class. Every other Writing 150 teacher gives so much work and she actually made me enjoy writing.

Super easy class. Very liberal and out of the ordinary. Definitely appreciated her desire for us to enjoy and improve our writing, however, I feel like I didn't learn a lot of the stuff I'm gonna need to know in the future. It was fun to have real-life Ms. Jenn as a teacher though.

Shellie is awesome. She doesn't care about assignments as much as she cares about helping her students become better writers. Super flexible on due dates and willing to help you if you have questions. Do the work and you will get an A, she wants you to succeed.

Shelli is a hilarious, caring, wonderful woman and a great teacher. I always love being in her classroom. Her homework is easy and fun, and she is very understanding if you ever need any accommodations. She cares more about your effort and growth than about grammar or specifics in your writing.

Really amazing professor who cares more about creativity/ideas than punctuation/works cited stuff. She is very caring and her due dates are super relaxed. She is super great and I suggest everyone take this class from her!

Professor Spotts makes it clear from the beginning that you will get an A if you put in the effort. She is willing to go over papers with you and is always clear with instructions. She wants you to improve and I definitely saw that in my writing this semester. Take this class from Spotts. SHE IS THE BEST!!!

Shelli Spotts is the best professor at BYU!! She genuinely cares about her students and their interests, and the assignments are not very difficult at all. I feel like I took more out of this class than any other, and I was able to develop valuable writing skills. If you have to have writing 150, take Shelli!!

Amazing professor who genuinely cares for her students. She's very reasonable and open about whatever a student has to say and is well-versed in her writing. Overall one of the best professors I've had.

Shelli was a wonderful professor. She legitimately cares about each student's growth in the class, and is more than willing to take extra time to help you. Class work was always fun and well thought out. There's are a LOT of writing assignments, but as long as you do all of them with decent effort, you'll get an A, guaranteed.

Professor Spotts is great. She cares about helping you to be a good writer in the real world rather than just know how to write a 5 paragraph essay. She really cares about the students. She took a long time to grade papers, but she was also really lenient about late work so that's fair. Most of the class got As since she was nice with COVID.

The most incredible professor, if you have a chance to take her class do it. I actually wanted to do my assignments and write my papers because she wants us to write them for ourselves no just so she can grade them. She is very creative and personal development oriented and she helps you to feel capable to write just about anything! 10/10

I LOVE SHELLI! She includes a variety of media in her lectures, which keeps it interesting and fun. Her grading is gracious. She genuinely cares about her students, and wants you to do well. Felt like an AP english class w/o the heavy workload. Shelli is sweet and funny and wants her class to be enjoyable for everyone. Also v forgiving of absences!
She helps you like writing and is super chill!

Sister Spotts is hands down the best English teacher I've ever had. She allowed us lots of time and gave us lots of tools for writing our research papers. She also really cares that we enjoy what we are writing and are passionate about it. I learned more in this writing class than any other I've ever had. She is also understanding and lenient.

Shelli is literally the best! Im not a big fan of writing, but her class was absolutely do-able and left me feeling more empowered and inspired to write. She is flexible with due dates and really did all she could to help us feel calm and excited about english and writing. 10/10 would recommend.

Shelli is awesome!! This is a writing class so obviously there are writing assignments. She is very flexible with due dates but expects you to be working on things throughout the semester. She is very understanding to students. You will learn a lot of cool things about becoming a writer! Be creative and do your work and you should be fine!

Shelli is an angel sent from above. She gives you ample time to work in class on the few assignments that are graded. She is more than happy to work with anyone on due-dates, or to meet to go over assignments. This class was not hard at all, but I learned some really cool things on how to be a better writer. 10/10 would recommend.

I loved this class!! Shelli is so good at teaching her students that creative writing has rules, but once you learn the rules, you can break them. There's a lot of reading and writing assignments, but I mean, it's a writing class, so obviously. She's very flexible and really cares that you succeed, so don't be afraid to ask for help.

I took the class (WRTNG150) during summer term and I really enjoyed it. It was my first class my freshman year and it gave me lots of hope for my life at BYU. Shelli was always kind, fun, and not a horribly mean grader. Easy A for me. She basically gave us everything we needed in order to succeed in the class.
She was AMAZING. This is the professor you want for wrt150. A couple of papers through the semester because writing class. The final is a group video.

Decent professor. She graded papers a little harder than I thought she would, but I got an A . She offers up to 20 points extra credit if students go to the writing lab. Sometimes she could be a little picky about random things in papers and assignments. Instructions weren't always clear. Make sure to know what she's looking for in the essays.

Shelli is truly amazing! I tried out other high rated WRTG professors and she was the best. The atmosphere is sooo relaxed. She loves to interact with the students and help them personally in any way she can! She understands us very well. All papers able to do easily with lots of time. Made me want to excel! Definitely take it from her!!

Sheilli is great! She is fair grader, doesn't give a lot of work, and makes writing seem fun. She is a creative writing teacher as well so she really lets you play around with your writing. I learned a lot without having to stress out about my grade.

I loved Sister Spott's class, I would highly recommend you take writing from her. She makes writing enjoyable and is super helpful if you have questions. This is definitely a nice class to take as a freshmen to get you into the swing of college life and will set you up for the rest of you college career because the inspiration she gives the class

Professor Spotts was boss! She is so willing to work with students and is very lenient about late work. Class is fun, but important to go to mainly to just know what's going on. You can probably get by without the text book. Easy A for a GE you don't want to take. She grades essays firmly, but very fair. Very fun class.

Take writing from HER!  Honestly, she's the best!  The classes are fun, engaging, and helpful!  She cares about you!  She wants you to love writing!   Her paper prompts are about things you care about!  She is willing to compromise, allows you to resubmit, and understands that her class is not the only class you have homework for!  She is the best!

You guys, Shelli ROCKS. She is the writing teacher I have waited my entire life to have. She GETS YOU, you learn via Harry Potter and slam poems, tweeting is an assignment, and you will seriously have so much fun and learn SO MUCH. This woman is just filled with brilliant ideas and great teaching techniques. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Shelli focuses on the learning rather than the grades, which is awesome. However, sometimes that can go a little too far. If you're looking for an easy A this is your class but if you love writing and want to be challenged maybe you should look elsewhere.

I really enjoyed taking Shelli's class. Class was always very fun and I legitimately enjoyed going. She gives you a lot of time to work on your papers and often will extend deadlines. We watch a lot of videos, especially slam poetry videos. She is a pretty fair grader and is very helpful if you ask her for feedback on your papers.

I love Shelli! She is an awesome teacher and really gives you great feedback on your papers. She is very lenient on when your paper is due and will give you many chances to work with others to get the best grade on your paper. She also cancels class to go to Sodalicious.

Her class is a lot of fun, she is very realistic and uses practical application to what she teaches. We watch Youtube a lot. Honestly, one of my favorite classes to go to. Time always passes fast, she is super understanding and usually extends paper deadlines. Sometimes we get out of class early or don't have class.
She is never boring. She, for the most part, lets you choose what you write about. She didn't give us tests and reading assignments were given, but we didn't really do anything with that.

Professor Spotts is a wonderful writing teacher because she truly cares for each student. Class is fun and you have the opportunity to write on what interests you. She encourages creativity in writing and teaches more than the basics, she teaches style in writing. By far my favorite writing class!

I loved the teacher. Writing classes in general tend to be boring, but Sister Spotts did her best to make this one interesting. She is understanding, innovative, and multi-dimensional. She's very real, and she treats her students like people, not machines. She's reasonable on deadlines and she spaces out the workload. Definitely take her class!

Shelli was a great teacher- she didn't lecture too long, and when she did it was entertaining and informative. We always knew what we were supposed to be doing, and how assignments would be graded.  She was super helpful and flexible. You can rewrite the papers, which was great if you didn't score as high as you wanted. I loved the class.

Shelli was easily my favorite teacher this semester. She had clear expectations and she made writing fun and exciting. DEFINITELY worth getting up for at 8am.
