Not hard at all as long as you're willing to make the effort. She's very laid back, but also extremely effective, and cares about you doing well. I'd recommend her to anyone!!!
Shelli is so helpful! She really helped me improve my writing and I really liked all of the youtube videos we watched. I would recommend her for anyone!

i highly recommend this class! you have to show up to class to get a good grade so an 8 am is rough, but it is so beneficial for your health and even for your other classes. it's a super fun way to exercise and shelly cares so much about all her students
If I could tell you to take only one swell class at BYU, it would be Zumba with Shelly!! She is such a light, so kind to students and very inspiring. Please take from her and you won't regret it!
She is so awesome and has a calming presence. She really makes you think critically about real-world issues which is cool. Easy grader as well.

I think everyone should take this class just to be more aware of what half of the global population experiences day to day. I thought I was pretty informed, but I learned so much, and the guys in my class agreed that it was a class everyone should take. Sheree is super caring but professional, easy to reach out to, and collaborative with the class

Professor Bench is great!! I also just loved this course, highly recommend. I'm not big on participation so that's where most of my points got docked off, but even then its not a huge chunk of your grade. Lots of readings but the content is great and the assignments are low stress. Professor Bench is very flexible based on class needs.

Sheree is amazing! She's so kind and is very passionate about what she teaches. We talk about some difficult topics, but she handles them so well. There can sometimes be a lot of reading but you don't have to take notes in class so I didn't mind. Very discussion based which I enjoyed as well.

This is definitely a more woke class but opens your perspective. She did a great job with culture versus doctrine and relating hard topics and views to the gospel. Overall I wasn't super interested in the class but would recommend for a ge.

Discussion based class, amazing reading choices. A 1-page reading journal of notes on the readings before each class, and minimal other projects. She is very flexible and cares a lot about her students. She cares about what she teaches, and does very well to help her students understand. I would 1000% take this class again!

Professor Bench really cares about the topics, and the class discussions were facilitated well. You cover some touchy topics sometimes, and depending on students comments things can get dicey. But she handled things well. Attendance is graded but as long as you're there and do the simple readings, you'll get a good grade

Professor Bench is a great professor! I loved this class and I learned soo much. There was quite a bit of readings and notes before every class but they are helpful for understanding the content. I'm so glad I took this class and loved her desire to teach it as well.

Professor Bench cares deeply about women's rights and the class. You read outside of class and discuss basically the whole class on what you read. It's a super easy A and you learn some pretty interesting material.

I absolutely loved this class with Professor Bench! She makes all of the topics so interesting and makes sure to tie the things we learn about in with what is happening in the current world. The readings are long, but they are interesting so it doesn't feel as difficult. She is kind and caring and willing to work with students. Love her!

I absolutely loved this class and Professor Bench. Her lectures are amazing and the material is so important and inspirational. I really think everyone should take this class. There are biweekly readings, but they are never too long and are always interesting. You keep a journal on readings which is graded, but it never felt like too much work!

She's great! Textbook readings are long but pretty interesting. Class is mainly discussion-based, but not everyone has to talk. My workload this semester was heavy but she was great about working with me on assignments. She does a great job will balancing different viewpoints and takes a medium approach to difficult issues. Definitely recommend!

Professor Peterson was helpful and caring. The class is mostly self taught through the textbook, and you complete most assignments in class. She was willing to help/provide clarity when needed and was an understanding grader.

Sheri is great. She makes the class doable. They break things down like in 115 into sections that you pass off assignments on certain weeks/dates during the Semester. This class does require 4 hours of practice time outside of class. This class has made me such a better organist!

Professor Peterson is a sweetheart, but leaves a lot to be desired. The exams are on things we haven't been taught in class. At the end of the year, I had to do a bunch of tests that I had no idea about. This was the class that stressed me out the most! Beware of this class if you're looking for an easy 2 credits.

I took this class to learn to play the organ better in a church congregation setting, not learn how to be a world-class organist, and with the amount of material, that is how it comes across. I would not recommend this class unless you love love love the organ, it is WAY too heavy for a 2 credit class.

Sheri was kind and willing to work with students based on circumstances. However, her Learning Suite isn't organized well, making it extremely hard to stay organized and on top of what is due each week. The TAs I worked with in the open organ lab were terrible. Rude and SO picky about technique.

Sherri is an amazing and caring teacher and she is so patient and willing to work with you and is not strict on deadlines. The class itself though is hard! There are a lot of assignments to keep up with and requires a lot of practice. I'm an average piano player and so a lot of the assignments took extra work and time for me to keep up.

Sheri Peterson is AWESOME! She really cares about her students and wants all of them to pass. This class is a little bit heavy, but I learned a lot and really enjoyed it. My sister took the same class from a different professor and didn't have as good an experience as I did. Definitely take it from Sheri! She's super sweet and literally the best.

Sister Peterson is one of the most caring professors at BYU. I missed a lot of assignments because of COVID, but I put in a TON of work, and she made it work out for me in the end. Tests are rough & mostly short-answer (study the composers!), but doable. It's a hard 2-credit class, but I learned a TON. Highly recommend taking this class with Sheri.

Only take this class if you take it from Sheri. It requires a lot of work and practice, and the tests are ridiculous (though not too much of your grade), but Sheri makes it okay. She is so sweet and kind, and she even takes her students to play the organ in the Salt Lake Tabernacle (only prof who does as far as I know).

Farnes suits those who like a loose, unstructured style. Expect ~3 hours of reading per class with effort-based self-grading, and no compromise from Farnes if you're busy. Class felt unproductive, like a glorified Sunday School lesson focused on dates over real-world gospel application. If you value structure and new insight, look elsewhere.
She's super nice, and definitely knows her stuff. You have a lot of readings, but it's not hard. The midterm and final you actually need to study for though.

Sister Farnes is genuinely one of the sweetest people I've met! She is also extremely knowledgeable in church history, I learned so much in her class! The workload was pretty average and tests weren't too difficult. Overall, I loved this class!

Sister Farnes is a very good teacher and very kind. Her lectures are very good, and I felt the spirit. That being said, there is a lot of reading. A lot of chapters of D&C and dates to memorize. The class felt similar to a history class. Great professor just know there is a lot of reading and work to be done :)

I loved this class much more than I'd expected. Professor Farnes is SUPER knowledgeable, and really wants you to learn. I felt the spirit every time she bore her testimony. Tests were fine with the study guide, and the readings were long but good. A few assignments, but all very reasonable. No busy work, which was a really nice change.

Sister Farnes is so kind and you know she really cares about her students and what she's teaching. This class can be difficult with a lot of reading and retaining it, but you learn a lot and really feel the spirit.  Great class.
She's fantastic. Each lecture was great, and her love for the students was more than evident.

Professor Farnes is kind, and is always so excited to teach about church history! You can just feel the light of Christ radiating from her! She really knows her stuff and approaches any questions with knowledge and respect. As long as you do the readings before class, attend the lectures, and study the study guide then you'll get a good grade!

Sis. Farnes is absolutely amazing. Honestly, I never expected the life changing outcome I received from her and this class. Her class is clear and simple, make sure to come prepared before class and try your best to really comprehend the material. If you do, you'll do great throughout the semester. She's my favorite religion teacher I've ever had.
A great professor who loves the subject matter. Attendance is required, and there is work involved, but worth it.

I want to take this class from Sister Farnes over and over again! I absolutely love her, and she teaches just how religion classes should be taught. I learned SO MUCH about church history, and was never too worried about my grade. She is so caring, and I want to adopt her as my aunt or grandma. PLEASE take this class!

I think that this class was great! Super interesting, and she did a good job of making it pretty intellectual as well as spiritually uplifting. She knows her stuff and is very smart! Cares about students. There are exams, but she prepares you well for them with the study guides and reviews.

She is the sweetest teacher ever and genuinely cares about the material! I took this class over summer and she paced everything out really well. You have to read A LOT, but it's not any busy work. The midterm and final weren't too hard if you studied. I loved her lectures and she is so full of passion and the spirit. Highly recommended!

TAKE THIS CLASS! Show up, do the readings and you will do well. Readings could be long and tedious sometimes but for no other assignments the whole semester it is worth it. Class is heavily discussion based with a couple short/easy pop quizzes thrown in throughout the semester. Midterm and final were easy as long as you go over study guide.

She teaches religion classes how they should be taught. She leads a discussion. The class is structured around us sharing our thoughts and testimonies in class. There are no tests, just a few projects/papers. You read the entire D&C and learn from one another. She is extremely knowledgeable and you can tell she cares. Awesome class! (RELC 320)

This is my second class from Sis. Farnes and I loved her just as much as the first class. She is very passionate about the gospel and I've learned so much about the scriptures and my own testimony. We always had great personal projects and class discussions. If you want to learn to love church history/the scriptures, TAKE IT FROM HER

I love Sister Farnes. Her class was very personable and she showed her love for her students throughout the entire semester. She asks for class participation a lot which leads to beautiful lectures. I took REL 320 from her but the website won't let me add that class code but for REL 320 I had no exams and only 4 pop quizzes that were easy.

I took this class in fall of 2023 but a profile wasn't available. She is absolutely the best religion professor to teach REL C 225! She cares about her students and is passionate about the church and it's history. I learned so much and I fell in love with the saints volumes and D&C. I will for sure be taking a class from her again. An easy class!

I LOVED SISTER FARNES. She was one of my favorite teachers this semester. She does give pop quizzes however they are really easy and self graded. She leads a great discussion and I didn't think it was ever boring. She cares a lot about her students and her students grades. The mid term and test were pretty easy as long as you knew the study guide.

Shes great! You can tell  that she sincerely feels and believes what she teaches. I would of gotten a better grade if I listened more, and asked more questions. What you put into it is what you get out of it. I would take her again
4 hours a day of reading and her tests are in the testing center. Weighted too heavy.

I enjoyed taking Foundations of the Restoration with Professor Farnes. She is kind, caring, and is clear about her expectations for the class. Phones/laptops aren't allowed to be out unless you are working on something in groups. The midterm and final make up a significant chunk of the grade, but the study guides covered everything on both exams.

Dr. Saasa is awesome. Teaches common sense, applicable material. Tons of real-world applications (facility tours, interviews, guest lectures) and it was also very inspiring and uplifting. 20 hours of volunteer work is required, but if you start at the beginning of the semester it's fine. I ended up loving volunteering. Great experience!
Everyone should take this class. A great experience for those interested in social work or wanting to understand how to better serve those around you.

The class was ok, but it wasn't super interesting. She was very nice about grading and the tests. The only thing she was harsh on was attendance. If you're taking this class, just know that you are going to have to do 20 hours of volunteer work with social workers.

Good class, great discussions. Assignments, papers, etc. are easy and not graded harshly at all. Gives clear study guides for exams. The textbook readings are SO LONG, but imma tell you right now, you don't really need to do them. Once the exam rolls around, the study guide will tell you what from the readings will be on the test.

Dr. Saasa is an incredible professor. I learned a lot in her class; she made sure that we learned what we wanted to, always willing to put her lecture on hold to answer our questions. It was a really easy class, but more importantly, a very mind opening class. I 100% recommend her class to everyone.

Very easy class but incredibly boring. Don't get the textbook. Prof. will never give an A on assignments/quizzes and will dock random points with no explanation. Attending lectures is important but there is not homework that can't be done during class. Really nice prof. you can tell she cares but she is a little out of touch with her students.

She is a very caring Professor who gives little homework, just readings before and recaps in class. I would definitely take her again! Her class is in SLC(worth it!) She only grades a handful of assignments the entire semester, so if you overachieve each assignment, you're golden. She is older, but has wise words to say and tells funny stories.

One of my least favorite classes I have ever taken, from a clearly bias teacher. She does not clarify grading rubric, nor does she provide explanations for why points are missed, how to get a better grade, nor can she back up any of the points missed by showing you exactly where her thoughts come from. Worth it to take from another teacher.

Professor Guyon is so nice and she has a passion for what she teaches which I appreciate. Lectures can get VERY long and boring but I always just worked on hw for other classes. The only downside to her is once you get a grade for the first assignment, that's pretty much your grade for the course. Very easy course with a kind professor!

Professor Guyon is the sweetest lady! the classes are definitely brutally long, but 1000% worth it for general credit. It is not a lot of work, and she is very caring and understanding. Definitely take these classes from her!

She is a very sweet prof who is passionate about what she teaches. She'll give you one grade at the beginning of the semester and that'll stay your grade for every assignment. Nobody get's below an A-. She goes over everything you need to know for quizzes/exams in class so just spark notes the readings and you'll do great!

Definitely the best way to get you Civ and Letters credits at BYU. I took 201 and 202 concurently, and they are very easy. All the work that does need to be done can easily be finished on the train ride to/from SLC. Lectures are long, but you can do other classwork during them. She says you need the textbook, but you can get along without it

Definitely the best way to get you Civ and Letters credits at BYU. I took 201 and 202 from her at the same time, and they are very easy. All the work that does need to be done can easily be finished on the train ride to/from the Salt Lake Center. Lectures are long, but you can do other classwork during them.

Professor Guyon is a very kind person. Only complaint is that when we asked why we didn't get full points on the quizzes we were told we didn't necessarily get anything wrong, but we could just do better. No one ever got 100% on any quiz. Lectures are pretty long (especially for spring/summer) but the work is easy enough. Easy A.

She is amazing and loves what she teaches. The textbook says required but I didn't get it and did just fine! You don't even have to read before class, just read Sparknotes or Litcharts during class when she puts us in groups to do the discussions. There is no HW, just quizzes and journals you can complete in class with information she gives.

Loved Prof Guyon, but her feedback/grading was super unclear. If you aren't getting the grade you want, talk to her early in the semester to get feedback (even then it may not be super helpful). She is the sweetest lady, and the class is totally worth travelling to Salt Lake for. Loved the smaller class dynamic as well.

Prof Guyon's class was sooo easy. I didn't show up all the days and still got an A in the class. Her lectures were super boring and long. There is one midterm, a final, 2 journals, 2 essays, and a few easy quizzes. She's an incredibly easy grader (and fast)!

BEST CLASS! Although Professor Guyon's lectures are a bit long, she does a super good job of explaining the material (I didn't even buy the text book and pretty sure most of my class didn't). Spark Notes will be your saving grace for learning material. There aren't very many assignments and she's a pretty easy grader. Definitely take this class!
I LOVED PROFESSOR GUYON. DEFINITELY TAKE HER FOR ENGL 201 and ENGL 202. EASIEST A YOU'LL GET.

This was probably the most boring class I've ever taken. She is a super nice lady but has a hard time explaining assignments, there are also no rubrics for assignments. You have to guess what she wants. They aren't hard but just felt like I could've spent my time doing something more productive than this class. Easy A though.

The assignments she gives are confusing because she doesn't explain them well, and when people ask questions, she doesn't understand what we're asking so she doesn't answer. Also there isn't a TA so you're pretty much on your own. It's an easy class, but it's frustrating to not know what to expect. There are quite a few papers, but they're easy.

So easy. She tells good stories and is really nice. Grading: 6 quizzes at start of class (not bad), 2 essays, midterm and final. If you're considering taking the class, "do it." -Shia LaBeouf, Dwight, Darth Sideous. Anyway, you get the idea
Great class, really nice. Too bad there isn't a 1/2 level of difficulty rating. 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Guyon is such a sweetheart. Very easy course, you don't need the textbook (Sparknotes my friends) and honestly you can show up to class with very little preparation. Only downside is she doesn't answer emails. She is very accommodating to special circumstances. Couple tests, papers, journals, and oral reports. Easy but interesting.

This is my 2nd class I've taken from Sherri and she is the best. It's the easiest class but we did learn a lot about different books from history. Don't buy the book -- I didn't even buy it this semester and I was fine.
Professor Guyon is very passionate about literature. She is kind and flexible. I highly recommend this class, it was a fun one.

Professor Guyon is the kindest little old lady. Its difficult to pay attention in class sometimes because its such a long class, but she makes jokes and gets the class to do group work and discussions. She grades fairly and the assignments are not difficult. Take this class if youd like an easy A for a general credit!

Easiest class ever. Ms. Guyon is so sweet, she is also accidentally hilarious. She says/does the funniest stuff... I was cracking up all semester. I honestly just did my homework for other classes while we sat there and she talked about books. Definitely take a class from her, you wont regret it.
I LOVED Sister Guyon. She is honestly the sweetest. She is so passionate about what she teaches. Hands down the most straight-forward class I've ever taken. She's darling.

So I rented the textbook for 20$ which really helped me with the material, but most students don't get it. I can honestly say her course was easier than any high school English class I had. So sweet, simple assignments, and an easy grader! The lowest grade I got on anything was a 95%

I love Sister Guyon. She loves literature. Her love of the material makes the long class worth it. She can be really passionate and hilarious while still being consistent with the timing of things. You can get so much stuff done during the class. Don't get the textbook. You don't need it unless you want the actual text.

Sister Guyon is very sweet and passionate about the literature. The class can be dry but it's really easy to finish your assignments for her class while you're in class, I did a lot of outside homework too. I didn't purchase the textbook, I'm sure it's handy but I got by without it. The assignments are simple, it's an easy A.

I beg all of you future students: do NOT get the textbook! Save your souls and save your money. I promise you: you WILL be sparknoting everything, and that's OK! That's the only way you'll understand it, and she's painfully easy. Sometime's she'd try & make us read to participate, so everyone would just hide their textbooks under the desk.

REALLY old lady.. she talks a lot but you cant understand her. It is a good class if you don't want to learn anything at all, you just want to hear blathering and get a good grade at the end. Btw, I LOVE ENGLISH!!! And this was by far my least favorite class.

Sister Guyon is without a doubt the sweetest lady. She is very enlightening and knowledgable about the texts that she assigns us to read. Quizzes every other week and mid-terms consist of a 5-6 page paper along with a short test.  You could get all your assignments done in class (I even got other class homework done as well). SUCH AN EASY A!

Sherri Guyon is a sweet old lady who really loves literature. We have to be real here, this class is extraordinarily easy, here to kill those GE's, and really quite a waste of time. You will cover a couple interesting works, but you'll probably read sparknotes more than anything else. Very easy course, worth the trip to SLC for it. Bored to tears!

Sister Guyon is such a sweet lady.  Her class was not the most exciting class to go to unless you are into literature and English.  She is very enlightening and knowledgable about the texts that she assigns us to read.  Quizzes every other week and mid-terms consist of a 5-6 page paper along with a short test.  I would recommend her.

Sweetest old lady ever. So cute. However, driving up to SLC for this class was rough because this was the most boring class I've ever taken, including high school classes. That being said it was also the easiest class I've ever taken, also including high school classes. If you want an A at the expense of your mental activity go for it.

I found her class very informative. She expects a lot when it come to reading and writting, but she is a very understanding teacher and is willing to help and answer questions whenever needed. Overall I enjoyed her class very much, and woldn't mind taking a class from her again.

Professor Guyon is very passionate about what she teaches.  There isn't too much work load as far as a 3 credit class goes, but class attendance is mandatory which was hard because her classes are long and boring for the most part.  She is an easy A, just make sure you do the homework assignments and you're set.  There were also quizzes in class.

Get ready to read a lot of books, you have to read on every week. Besides doing a lot of work, Prof Guyon will basically help you out with anything you need, including extensions on assignments. Barely did work for this class and might end up with an A.
She is so easy. Two, 6 page papers. Come to class, sit back, and relax and you'll get an A. Easiest class I have ever taken. If you need an A, take it here!

I liked Guyon and how easy and relaxed the class was. Two 6pg essays, 3 in class quizzes, and a journal due with an easy midterm and final. If you need to get an easy A for a civ credit, take this. Wort going to Salt Lake for the Easy A.

Professor Guyon is a terrific teacher. Maybe the strongest focus of her class is to make your writing as focused and clear as possible. Her grading system is easy and fair, and the work load is light to medium. She's willing to help with your work if you ask. Overall, professor Guyon's class is great.

She is a sweet lady who wants to help you be a good writer and is willing to help answer any questions you have. She does make the class last longer than it needs to, but her generous grades and clarity make it worth it.

She is very scatterbrained and could probably end an hour early every class, but talks about silly things very slowly so you end at last minute most classes. She is the kindest lady though and will change your grade if you're willing to ask. Easy A or A-. Writing assignments are fair and easy grades. DON'T BUY THE BOOK.You won't need it.
Take English 315 from her!  She is an easy grader and has a very reasonable work load for her students.  It's worth the drive to SLC.
Super easy class. I just read wikipedia versions of the assigned readings and did completely fine. She is very lax on her grading. Easy A.
Wonderful teacher took both sections loved it

She is a super easy grader and an easy A if you go to class and do the work.  Assignments are mild, and there is next to no reading.  She takes up every minute of class even though she could be done an hour early every time...but other than that its an easy class.  You hardly use the textbook at all so I would recommend not buying one.
SUPER EASY. she's a little kooky, actually a lot, but such an easy teacher. if you don't love English more than life itself, take her, get an easy A, and move on.
I enjoyed this class even though it was a lot of reading and writing.  She is a good teacher and will help out her students when confused.  She really helps you with the midterm and final.
No Comments
No Comments

Dr. Pang is one of my favorite professors oat. He knew everyone's names on the first day of class. He is very accessible and helpful outside of class, easy to talk to, and gives great advice. Not only is he a genius and very accomplished in his career, but he is an incredible human, humble, and still thinks the world of his students.

Professor Pang is SO kind. I missed a bunch of classes at the begining of semester and he met with me many times to patiently reteach me all the content. He also invited the whole class to Thanksgiving at his house if that shows you what hes like!
 So caring, never had a professor like him.

I love taking food science from him! There is a lot of content but he is always available to ask questions. This class is smaller so it has an amazing community feel as we all participate! He is a great professor and you can tell he truly cares

Professor Pang is an amazing professor. The course itself is hard, but this is Food Science. Food science involves a significant amount of chemistry and encompasses numerous new topics that many people aren't initially prepared for. However, Professor Pang truly cares about you and wants you to succeed. I wish he were always my Professor.

250 is a content heavy class, but Dr. Pang did a great job at explaining difficult concepts and making the class engaging. He is still new to teaching, but he is very open to feedback and genuinely cares about the success of his students. The tests are difficult and very specific, but you can definitely get an A if you study

Dr. Pang was incredible. It was his first semester teaching at BYU, but he knew every single student by name on the first day of class. I also had Dr. Pang for my lab section, and he did a great job trying to help us really understand the concept. Use the learning outcomes and you'll be great. He's an awesome professor!

Analog Design is not for everyone. You either love it or you hate it and fear it. Dr Chiang has a great understanding of analog design and has been taught by some of the brightest analog designers. If your goal is to become an analog designer Dr Chaing is the person to go to.

I'd say the difficulty lies in the material. Huge amounts of new information dumped on you from the get-go. I think Chiang did a great job in getting the point across. Most of the people that complained didn't read the text. Yeah it's tough to get through, but that's just part of the class. It's engineering. It's hard. Get over it or change majors.

This course is inherently hard, but Chiang just makes it painstaking. His explanations during his office hours are him rattling off information rather than going one step at a time. Often, he will say "It's just fill in the blank" and insert op-amps, small circuit and so on. Sadly, the best approach to passing is self-study and avoiding him.

What can I say, this is an EE class.  Anyone hoping for an easy time is self-delusional.  Book material is rough - par for the major.  Prof. Chiang was willing to adjust his curricula or teaching to help us get through.  Do your research and don't presume anything when you go to see him.  He's very helpful if you've done your due diligence.

There is no doubt that this class is probably one of the hardest in the major, and its pretty obvious that these reviewers are blaming their own failure to understand the material on the professor.  Dr Chiang is a good instructor, and he is one of the few who does and did make changes according to constructive feedback.

Dr. Chiang is not a good teaching professor. He is brilliant and unless you are as smart as he is you will have trouble with this class. I went to see him in his office hours and left feeling degraded and hopeless. His tests are very hard and the preparation material was poor. This class was very heavily weighted on tests.

Very unclear and inspecific in what concepts and formulas to focus on. Spends far too much time on theory and does not know how to simplify and intensify the key concepts. Good at writing down notes on a whiteboard but fails to connect with students and verify understanding throughout lecture. Very smart but should just do research, not teaching.

Great class and great professor. His happiness is contagious. You will get an A on the midterm and final if you study deeply the review material they provide before the tests. Just make sure you are very diligent on the quizzes because each one is a good chunk of your grade. Class is once a week, one week is lecture other week is a group activity.

Professor Greathead is cheerful (which I appreciate so much) and seems to care about students behaving ethically in the future as global supply chain managers and does a really good job as an adjunct professor actually teaching the course material.
Your grade is almost all based on a few quizzes which makes things difficult. He is a great professor and I always loved in-person classes!
This class is pretty easy, I always put the videos on 1.5-2x speed and breezed through the quizzes. I always looked forward to in-person class!

Professor Greathead is excellent. This is one of the most important courses at BYU and there is no one better suited for the role. Getting an 'A' is hard. To earn one, you need to recognize that his rubrics are bare minimums and you need to go above and beyond. The final simulation is challenging and requires prep. It's challenging, but rewarding.
he cared, gave work, but always had an answer for the problem at hand, if you gave some you got some.

(For 211 as well) Class is VERY mandatory and super fun, just games, but have nothing to do with test/assignments. Class every other week. You NEED to memorize all terms and know it all well from the textbook to get an A. If you just miss a few assignment questions and test questions you lose a lot of points. I didn't study much but got lucky.

Super good professor. Homework was light and easy. People who say his mid term was tough are crazy because it's the easiest test ever if you study. Final was pretty easy as well. Attendance is mandatory half of the time, as some weeks its an optional TA lab, and some weeks it's mandatory attendance. Didn't stress at all taking his class.

He is a great professor! He always seems to be in a great mood and all of the classes are very hands on, making them engaging and fun to attend. Only every other week is mandatory class and there are only two exams during the term. All quizzes are easy. The TA was super nice when I met with him for my slide presentation at the end of the term!

Professor Greathead is awesome! Overall the material isn't difficult there's just not much margin for error because the class is only half a semester (and only 3 in-person attendances). I assume this is just how the class is designed regardless of professor though so if you're going to take it then definitely take it from professor Greathead!
Absolutely awesome. :)

Lots of simulations to help your practice. Super engaging. Easy simulation write ups, 2 journal entries, occasional book quiz, book report, difficult midterm, final simulation. Learned a lot, super entertaining, passionate professor who cares.

Prof Greathead is awesome. Super interesting class and you learn a lot of skills you can use in your everyday life. You get to do a lot of simulations throughout the semester that help you apply what you learned. He is a tough grader though. But overall, really enjoyable class and he is super funny as well. Learned a lot

Prof Greathead is SO FUNNY. I would take a class on dirt if he taught it. He is super compassionate about negotiation and wants students to succeed- if you need accomodations, reach out to him. He is so caring. Midterm is TOUGH so study hard but rest of the class is pretty easy if you do your reading.
Funny professor, kind of a lighter course load. One exam and it is pretty tricky. A little overhyped but I enjoyed his class.

Overall, Greathead is awesome and makes class very engaging. I feel like him and the TA's are just nitpicky about assignments and like to find random ways to dock you points when that criteria was not listed on the rubrics.
Professor Greathead makes the material engaging. The class is a breeze if you attend lectures and use resources like Unstuck ai to prep for tests. Hands-on projects are a great learning opportunity.

Even though it was a hybrid class, I only saw him twice the entire semester, and the rest was delegated to TA's, which makes it feel like he is uninvolved.

95% for an A means you need to be near perfect. Attend every in-class session and it is doable, though.
British legend. His classes are very fun and engaging. The material isn't hard but an A is 95% so missing just a few questions will put you at an A-, unfortunately. The class itself is great, though.
Great professor and he has a great accent too!

Honestly wouldn't take GSCM 201 or 211 from any other professor. Greathead was hilarious, personable, and knows what he's talking about. The in-class activities were awesome and quizzes are open note. An A is a 95% though so don't slack off in the beginning cause it can be hard to pull the grade back up.

He's an amazing professor who's super nice. You MUST attend class only every other Friday for in class activities because each one is worth a lot of points. Homework load is very light every week and ANYONE should get an A in this class. Tests aren't difficult with the reviews they give.
Absolutely amazing professor. He made the class so engaging and he is the most hilarious lecturer. I hope I can have him for more classes in the future. Loved the class.

A 95% being an A is just a dumb way of the program trying to make an otherwise ridiculously easy class into somewhat of a challenge. Easy class, but tests are overweighted and EXTREMELY poorly worded, to the point where all answers are subjective and could easily be debated. One of those classes where everything is designed to trip you up

He's an amazing professor who is super nice. You MUST attend class only every other week for in class activities because each one is worth a lot of points. Homework load is very light every week and anyone can get an A in this class. Tests aren't that difficult with the reviews they give.

Greathead is a dawg. Tough to get an A because the midterm and final simulation are pretty tough, but the learning in this class is invaluable. All students should take this class. ESPECIALLY BUSINESS STUDENTS. Should be business core honestly.

Class was overall interesting until the final. Participation is a major part of your grade, and the only way to earn full points is daily comments. I'd also make a note of every time you participate just in case the ta misses so you don't lose points. There is no way to know what an A looks like in the final negotiation, and I'm not a mind reader.

Professor Greathead did a fantastic job teaching the material. He cares about his students and his profession, and that shows. The class itself is quite easy, mostly based on attendance and a couple tests and quizzes which are simple. Take this class from him if you can!
Light but engaging coursework
Prof Greathead is the best! Take from him if you can. Lectures are fun and engaging, and he gives you more than enough resources to succeed in the class.

Great professor, I learned so much about negotiating. The class was very easy, but an A in this class is a 95, which can be difficult to obtain. To get an A: attend all classes, take good notes, turn ALL assignments in, use a variety of negotiating experiences for the negotiation journal, do the book report early if possible, and PARTICIPATE.

One of the best professors at BYU. He is an incredible individual. His lectures are engaging and the material that he teaches is GOLD. He is committed to helping you master the material in his class. He grades in a timely manner and provides fantastic feedback. His simulations are excellent. HE ACTUALLY TEACHES compared to other MSB professors.

Greathead is great. So funny and cool, and truly a teacher who understands that this isn't our only class. Unlike other professors he isn't on a high horse about an entry level class. He teaches the subject with a smile and without ego. So helpful and kind. Take all your classes from him if you can. Seriously.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Great class, full of practicing and real-life simulations. The final is just one big simulation. I learned so much more than I ever hoped or expected to (and I had high hopes and expectations). I STRONGLY RECOMMEND THIS CLASS AND PROFESSOR.
Awesome class and very well organized (part 2). I felt like I was set up for success every step of the way.
Awesome class and very well organized. I felt like I was set up for success every step of the way.

I really enjoyed GSCM 201 with Prof Greathead. If you attend the three required lectures and don't have too hard of a time teaching yourself, this class is a breeze. His lectures are entertaining and insightful. The project he assigns is really feasible, and if taken seriously a great opportunity to learn. Work load is light (max 1.5 hrs a week)

Not my favorite professor. He was not accommodating and wasn't kind. His class was the easiest one I've ever taken. The material wasn't hard and none of the assignments were of any rigor. I wouldn't take this class again or anything form him again, unless I wanted the easiest possible 'A'.

Class grade depends almost entirely on the midterm and final. There is no textbook and the professor does no direct teaching. Entirely self taught class through low quality youtube videos and articles that are linked in lessons. Worst class I have taken yet at BYU.
The Best
Great class, super easy, and great hands on learning opportunities. Professor Greathead was a super positive and welcoming character. Really enjoyed taking this class from him

Crazy easy class. I honestly am not sure what we learned in it. But, Greathead is sweet. You'll love him. Just a happy, nice guy. Attendance is 100% mandatory though. Make sure you can make the classes before signing up, otherwise you'll get wrecked.
He was a super fun professor. Lots of opportunities to apply what you learn in the reading. He has a real passion for supply chain, and it really shows in the activities.
Memorize the study guides given and you should be good on all the tests. Lectures are very engaging and you can care he cares about his students.
Memorize the study guides given and you should be good on all the tests. Lectures are very engaging.

Professor Greathead is so amazing and such a great guy. He knows so much about supply chain and really tries to get students excited about it. His accent is amazing and it makes me want to listen to him constantly. He changed the class to online but it did make it more flexible. TAKE SUPPLY CHAIN CLASSES FROM HIM

Dude is a gem. Class is super easy and you really just need to go to all 3 classes during the semester and do the HW to do well. Tests are not bad if you just study a little bit. He gives clear study guides with what you need to know.
Great class, professor is funny. Well-organized and easy to follow.

Professor Greathead is an interesting teacher when we do have lectures, but most of the class is online. Over the term, there are only 3 classes and 2 exams, and they are worth a ton of your grade. That being said, he is pretty lenient in helping you make those up. I would absolutely recommend this class, and GSCM310, which is the same format.

Professor Greathead is amazing!!! He is so caring and loving to his students. Always wants to know what is going on in your life. I wish I could take a million of his classes. He is always making jokes and had great activities prepared where I could connect with other students even though it was on zoom. Cannot say enough good things about him.

Super nice guy, and the class is pretty easy. It's a 95% for an A, but the work isn't impossible and the exams are very doable. Just be sure to do the study guide and the hw and you'll be fine. He only required attendance for 3 classes, and each class was super interesting and helpful for understanding the material. I highly recommend him.

Professor Greathead, is very understanding, and only has a weekly module, a midterm and final, and a project at the end of the term. The three classes are absolutely mandatory for an A, but he is good at letting you make it up. Overall, not difficult, but be sure to take good notes on the weekly modules, because that is what the study guide is.

I learned so much about supply chain and I loved this class. Greathead is a very nice professor who is very passionate about business and cares about his students. His tests and quizzes are straightforward. I always ask the TA's for help understanding topics and they were fantastic at responding quickly!

took him for 305 and he was super funny and made lectures entertaining. the TA's were quick to respond. easy A if you do the bare minimum. just cram for the tests and go to the TA review sessions, quizzes were all open book. if you need GSCM as a requirement take from Greathead! super easy and relaxed.

305 was a great class, i found the readings interesting and not too bad of a work load (maybe 2 or 3 hours outside of class a week) and the quizzes and tests were straightforward. An A is a 95% so you cant do the bare minimum but if you study and participate an A is possible. Nice teacher and really likable. I did in the summer and would recommend

I've had Professor Greathead for other supply chain courses. This class, global negotiations has probably been one of my favorite classes at BYU. He is an excellent teacher, lecturer, and truly cares about the students. He is inspiring and respectful to others. While also being hilarious. Would take this class ang any other class from him. 10/10.

I had Professor Greathead for GSCM 305 and 310 and I liked him enough to take another class from him. This class (411) is probably one of the most valuable classes I have taken at BYU. The class was great, but honestly the reason it was so good was Prof Greathead. Best teaching method, very caring, very skilled. HIGHLY recommend.

Pro. Greathead is awesome and his class is extremely laid back - especially for a business class. Only had to zoom in to one group lecture the whole semester, with the rest of the semester content clearly listed on Canvas. Cram for 30 min before the tests and you'll be fine. Easy A. Definitely recommend if your looking for an easy term class.
I wish I could take more classes from him

The ENERGY this man gives off is astounding. I would easily take him for every class; he is entertaining, relays information easily, and engages everyone. The in-class activities were amazing! We met 4 times (Hybrid class) and the only other work was readings+quiz each week, coupled with 2 exams. The "textbook" is innovative, but stressful to study

This is a term class and you only meet in person 3 times, but that means that each class is 5% of your grade. His lectures are really funny and engaging with activities. There are weekly readings and quizzes that are open book so it's super easy. The midterm is very straightforward and if you look at the review/study guide you will do well.

Dr. Greathead is a very engaging professor. His in-class lectures are exciting and fun; however, his class has a very high cutoff for A's (95%). There isn't much room for error on the midterm and final, which can be really annoying. If you study you should be get an A, but I still think the grading is dumb for this class.

Great professor, focused on improving our negotiating skills on all fronts. However, there is a lot of weight on the final negotiation, which can be daunting for most. Pay attention and you'll do great.

Ugh. I really wanted to like him. He's interesting and makes class fun. However, he could care less if you fail his class. His class should've been easy but they made the tests worth SOO much of your grade and super ambiguous. And when I asked what to do about a class I couldn't attend he said: "I have 800 students, sorry."

Not the most involved or accessible teacher as he is busy with his own research. The TAs do most of the work and he teaches 3 total classes. New course this semester so it was disorganized. No communication. The tests test you on arbitrary bits of the random readings and YouTube videos. Honestly one of the lowest quality teachers I have had at BYU.

Its hard to rate Prof. Greathead because of how little you see him or even are taught by him. The course is primarily online watching too many hours of videos and taking a quiz on them. If you are in to easy tests, take this course. Be prepared to have to buy case studies a few times in the semester that Prof. Greathead wrote.
greathead is so awesome, with great examples and compelling lectures. you only go to class three times and it is a pretty easy course, just cram for your tests. def recommend for 305

DON'T TAKE IT ONLINE! You have to read the entire text book(20 chapters) to prepare for quizzes and the final. Also, 5 portfolio assignments(includes a research paper) which are even more time consuming. He doesn't give feedback for your papers so you don't know why you get the grade. Basically, you fend for yourself through the whole course.

The lectures are amazing and the course is great. I really enjoyed taking this class and I think it will influence me for years to come. It is always hilarious and engaging. The grading and exams can be a bit arbitrary though.
His class was a fun. However, I think the grading criteria is too tough. Missing a quiz harm you a lot:/
You only have to show up once every like two weeks. It's freakin' awesome. Super easy. Beware of 300.

Show up 3 times to class, and each class is an interactive activity (no lectures). Greathead is cool and funny, I wish he taught the GSCM 300 portion! I went to the reviews and studied for 1 hr before each midterm and final. Easiest Marriott school class yet.
Final is hard but idk how I did well enough on it to get an A. The midterm was super easy though and hw is easy too. Show up three times for half of the semester and you should get an A

Professor Greathead is from England and has a killer accent. He gives great lectures and has great insight. I would recommend him. This class was pretty easy. Mandatory classes are group activities. TA's teach all the classes except for the 3 mandatory classes. The TA's that I had spoke really fast and sometimes it was too fast to understand.

The class is participation based, lots of group projects and in-class roleplay. Prof. Greathead is authentic and cares about his students. Most of your grade is from the Final , an observed negotiation, and a semester-long journal.

As a senior in the Marriott School, this class felt like a waste of time. EXTREMELY EASY, but you won't learn much. Quizzes/modules are open book, so get ready to implement your control-find skills. Required attendance to three classes where you play games together, otherwise don't go. BYU Online feels like Pathway. This class is 95% run by TAs.
Super easy. Great guy, fun lectures, reasonable readings and assignments. His energy and happiness are contagious.

Prof. Greathead is amazing! He's very patient and explains the topics very well. All non-required days were TA reviews, but DEFINITELY GO TO THOSE, they help a lot with the exams! Easy assignments and quizzes. DON'T take this class with BUSM241! The content is similar but taught at different times. A lot of reading, but do it, and you'll be fine!

Most useful course I have taken at BYU, bar none. The course work is light, most days there is a negotiation that you will role play and there will be a right up due the next period. Pay attention and participate in class, most of your grade is based on the final negotiation at the end of the semester (which takes the place of a final).

Fun guy to be lectured by. The material is not hard to learn nor complicated. If you stay ahead on the readings you will come away with a lot of valuable skills up your sleeve. However that won't contribute to your grade. Final presentation/project arbitrarily graded, and very ambiguous minutia test questions.

Prof. Greathead is by far the best teacher I have ever had. His lectures are very beneficial because they are not just lectures, but activities. He is hilarious and good about talking about the gospel as much as he can. Class was a breeze except the last 2 weeks of class make up around 60% of your grade with the final, project and a presentation.
Prof Greathead is amazing! He is hilarious and his accent makes it even better! You should take at least 1 class from him while at BYU, you won't regret it!
Prof Greathead is amazing! He is hilarious and his accent makes it even better! You should take at least 1 class from him while at BYU

Brother Greathead is one of my favorite professors I have ever had! His negotiations class is a class that is relevant and valuable in both the professional world and your personal life. He is a great professor that is sincere and genuinely cares about his students. I would highly recommend his class.

Professor Greathead truly cares for his students. As a MAcc student, it sometimes felt our class was a little unforgiving at small things (such as somewhat ambiguous quiz questions), but really, none of that mattered all that much. His course was clear and straightforward, and you could really tell he loves teaching at BYU.

Greathead is man among boys. His euphonious English accent makes lecture time not only intellectually stimulating but aurally exhilarating. He is the embodiment of sophistication and class. If you are considering a career in Global Supply Chain/Operations, I highly recommend this class for a spanking good time!

Simon is world class. His work experience allows you to really determine if Global Supply Chain should be your major. Lectures are interactive and the textbook reads fairly well. Pre-class quizzes, midterm, final and group project make up the grade for this class.

Professor Greathead is very genuine in how he treats his students.  He wants them to not only succeed in his class but to be successful in their careers and lives as well.  He focuses on teaching applicable material. in I still recall many of the principles that he taught in his classes.  I highly recommend taking his classes! Great personality.

Professor Greathead is a tremendous teacher and his busm 450 class was the most real world applicable class I have taken at BYU.  I feel like I learned more skills to help me in my life and career from his class than in any other. He has a tremendous amount of experience in negotiations and translates that experience to in class teaching.

Truly devoted to developing his students and how he treats people, in and outside the classroom. BM450 will teach you the soft skills that will differentiate you in the real world. Be ready to be challenged on the last project. TBS, if you prepare well, make a real effort and seek guidance before presenting, you will walk out a better negotiator!

One of my favorite teachers I've had here at BYU. Took his negotiations class winter semester and everything he taught could be applied. Seriously, great class and even better teacher. Dr. Greathead will do anything to help his students.

Phenomenal! Directly after the semester I took his negotiations class, I worked in India negotiating with suppliers around the world for the building of our product mix. I attribute a large portion of my success to his lectures in creating value through negotiating. I saved my company a nice chunk of change that summer.  Very applicable class.
One of the nicest people you will ever meet.  He is passionate about what he does and he really cares about the students.  He is willing to build your network and help you outside of the classroom.
Great teacher! Energetic. Passionate about the topic. Great opportunities to learn.  Participation in class is important, but it creates a good learning environment.

One of the best professors I had in 5 years at BYU, and Negotiations was incredibly useful. Last week I negotiated my first job offer, and increased my salary by 12%. This class will earn me THOUSANDS of dollars over my lifetime. Dr. Greathead is warm, kind, professional, fair, and excellent at teaching this class.

Greathead is super funny. I was always cracking up at everything he said during class. On a more serious note, he is really willing to help and make sure you succeed. There is a group project/paper/presentation but its not bad. You will need to buy the textbook. There is one midterm and a final.

Class was great, first test easy, great study guide.  Then the end came.  Study guide for the final test was a joke, and he didn't enter a few grades until after finals (and after teacher reviews).  Then his whole grading history changes and he plunges everyone down the toilet.  Seems to care more about Tenure than teaching.

He added 100 points to the final group presentation and said he would grade them easier, well that was a lie! We went to him for help multiple times; I've never had a teacher be so disinterested in helping. The group project was a rough experience. Other than this, he has a great accent.

Greathead is an awesome guy who really does a great job at making his classes engaging. You can tell that he wants his students to learn and to be successful in life. There is 1 group project though that is worth a TON of points and there isn't much guidance on the project. I had an A- and then got massacred on the project and final.

The material wasn't the most interesting to me, but I loved the lectures because Professor Greathead is passionate about what he teaches. He really cares about his students and is willing to help out where he can. The exams are not overly difficult as long as you have been keeping up with the  reading and paying attention in class.

Class had a light homework load and all went well til right at the end. I had a great grade until after finals a couple assignments' scores were put it. I felt blindsided as the grading was extremely harsh on those last couple assignments where the rest of the semester it was essentially if you turn it in you get full credit. No A for me ): no 4.0.

Professor Greathead was fantastic!  Almost  everyday in class we were negotiating, practicing the  principles we were studying, which wasn't graded.  Usually a quick, one-page paper after a negotiation talking about what you learned.  He is there for the students.  He helped me get my internship!  Genuinely listens to his students.  Fun class!

Dr. Greathead is a dynamic and engaging instructor that can turn even the most boring material into something interesting. He scheduled guest speakers and field trips so that we could see the concepts we were learning in a real-world application.  He is a fair grader and is be available for his students. I would definitely take his class again.

I took this class as a freshmen so the course was rigorous for me. But I don't regret taking the class from him because he is very fun, and makes the class interesting. Although the class was about 3 hours long, the time seemed to fly by and I loved his humor. You do need to read the book and know the vocabs really well. Final project in the end.

Dr. Greathead is the BEST professor I had at BYU. He is so dynamic and loves teaching. I would recommend taking any class from him. My one regret is that I could only take one of his classes. He is extremely helpful and would do anything for his students. Amazing professor!

Brother Greathead's Global Negotiations class was my favorite class I took at BYU. The content was so useful and he did a great job at engaging the class.  Outside of class Bro Greathead was more than willing to help students out with finding jobs or personal negotiations. TAKE THIS CLASS! You won't regret it!

EXCEPTIONAL Professor!Prof. Greathead is really passionate about the subject. He's so energetic in the class, which makes you active. Time flies in his class. He's also really helpful outside class's stuff
AMAZING Teacher!! Best I have ever had. I know people say that a lot but its true. He really cares about making you better. Awesome Class!
Professor Greathead is fantastic.  He really cares about his students and wants you to succeed.  He is passionate about what he teaches and has fun stories.  Full of energy and very likable.

Incredible professor! One, you will NOT fall asleep in his class. He keeps the class interesting even if it isn't your major. Two, incredibly helpful outside of class. He wants you to succeed and will do just about anything to help you do so. I need help finding a job and he jumped on board and helped. Recommend him, hands down!

By far the best professor I have ever had here at BYU. Professor Greathead is fun, genuine, and truly wants you to succeed. BEST PROFESSOR EVER. If you get a chance to take a class from him you will LOVE him.

Super awesome professor who will end up being your friend.  He cares that you succeed in both his class and whatever else that you are involved in.  I was struggling in this class but he took the time to sit me down and get me back on track. Just be willing to work hard and you'll love any class that he teaches!!

Professor Greathead is one of the BEST! if not The BEST at BYU. His ability to communicate knowledge, eagerness to help, and his wealth of knowledge and experience made me even consider Supply Chain as a major. You won't be bored in any of his classes. He has an outstanding ability to engage you in every lesson. I'd pay to be in his class again.

Dr. Greathead has been one of the most inspirational and forthcoming professors I have ever had.  Every class was intellectually stimulating, and every assignment was tailored fit to help us apply the knowledge of the curriculum.

Brother Greathead has been by far the best teacher I have had at BYU. His class puts life into perspective and makes you interested in all kinds of business. He cares about every student and wants them to succeed. After the semester was over he helped me decide which emphasis to choose and was very helpful. I definitely recommend taking his class!

It is refreshing to be taught by professors like Bro. Greathead. He is passionate about the subject matter and you can tell by the way he teaches. He engages his students masterfully. Never a dull moment!  He loves and cares for his students. He is always willing to meet with students individually. His course is challenging but very worthwhile.

Prof. Greathead is an exceptional teacher. He did a great job tailoring the class to students not majoring in supply chain/operations. He is particular and precise in his grading procedures, but as long as you understand his expectations and try to meet them, you should be fine. His tests require attention to detail, but he gives a study guide.

Amazing professor. Has genuine love for supply chain. Great professional experiences in Europe and US. ALways excited about the class. I NEVER got bored. And who wouldn't want to listen to his British accent? It's so cool! Definitely take the class from him if you can.

I have been in college since 2005. Prof. Greathead is the first professor that i have ever felt was interested in me and my well being. He is an amazing teacher. He is so excited to teach the material. HE IS GREAT. I had a family emergency during the semester and he took the time to come visit me and my family and bring us dinner. Very Amazing Man

Professor Greathead is one of the most personable professors I have had.  He is always in a good mood and is the type of professor who will bend over backwards to help a student out.  He also has a lot of business experience and was a great instructor because of all that experience he had to draw from.

Mr. Greathead is one of the best professors in BYU. He is extremely helpful. He will go out of his way to help his students. The best thing about him is his personality. He is always happy and cheerful. It's so easy to talk to him. If you are looking for a great class in BYU with a great professor, this is the one. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED
Very fun class. Tons of professional experience which is great. His tests don't relate to classwork very much but the class was great.
He was a great teacher. Excited at every class meeting and eager to see how his students are doing with extracurricular activities.
The BEST professor I ever had in BYU. I come from an engineering background and this was my first business class ever and he made it my best experience ever. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

When Brother Greathead enters the room, he brings light and joy with him that is extremely difficult to find in a person. Always smiling and positive. Really cares about your learning experience and promotes introspection. Questions are so wonderful because not only are the questions great, but he gives students time to think before answering. Best

Awesome teacher! His teachings are inspiring and he really cares about his students. He does his best to make himself available for help anytime. I strongly recommend taking a class from Professor Greathead!

Prof. Greathead is one of the best teachers I've had.  He is so great at explaining the material and has a lot of real world experience to help illustrate the concepts.  He is so understanding of the different situations that come up in a student's life and is always willing and available to help with anything.  I loved this class!

Dr. Poulter was an amazing teacher. She taught with grace, inspiration, and kindness, but she is also stern in a good way. (Think Mary Poppins) She reminded us daily about the things that are most important in life (think the things that BYU believes in... I can't write them here) and felt like a mentor to me throughout my time in Women's Chorus.

Love Dr. Poulter! She is hilarious, kind, efficient with time, and a great director. Attendance is mandatory with 4 excused absences. She fosters a family environment while also making amazing, high-quality music! Also held optional out-of-class activities (singing in devotional, music videos) that made my BYU experience so fun!

I love Dr. Poulter! She is the perfect director for Women's Chorus. Attendance is required, but you can miss up to 4 days without it affecting your grade. Poulter is the kindest and knows what she's doing! I honestly wouldn't take the class if someone else was over it. You won't regret singing with her.

Dr. Poulter is the best director I've ever had. She is talented, kind, and teaches efficiently. She makes women's chorus a happy place and is always looking out for her students. Attendance is mandatory and graded in all classes, rehearsals, and concerts. This class is a commitment, so look at the calendar before you audition and be ready to sing!
I love Dr. Poulter! She is the best music teacher I have ever had. She clearly loves her students and her work. I can't recommend Women's Chorus enough

Dr. Poulter is simply the best teacher you will ever have. She is astounding in every way and cares so much about you individually. She strives for perfection in a healthy manner (never uses shame as a tactic) and you can tell music and singing is her passion. Rehearsal is sometimes rigorous and a lot of hours and well worth every second of it.

I took women's chorus from her in 2019 and then again in 2024, and she actually remembered who I was (or at least said she did). She's a great person and picks some great music. I'm not sure that anyone really reads these for the choir classes, but she's great. However, Women's Chorus does feel like a waste of time if you have a hard major.

Such a good class! I feel so spiritually strengthened because of this class, and it's so fulfilling being a part of such an amazing program. She's hilarious, relatable, and tries to make everything she teaches relatable and understandable. It's a little easy to feel lost in the crowd, but that's just a consequence of such a large class size.

Dr Poulter is incredible; she is so passionate and caring of all of us in her choir. If you ever have a chance to work with her, do not turn it down. She is very kind, passionate, and talented. 10/10!

Dr. Poulter is such an amazing person, and has a great sense of humor! I love singing in Women's Chorus. This class was always uplifting, spiritually strengthening, and one of the highlights of my day! It's a time commitment to always go to class, but it's worth it. I improved as a singer, and I highly recommend taking from her if you can. :)

I loved Women's Chorus with Dr. Poulter! She always made class fun and engaging, and I always looked forward to going to class. I always felt prepared for our concerts and she has helped me grow as a singer and performer. Many times I would leave her class smiling from ear to ear, and I would definitely recommend taking a class with Dr. Poulter!

Professor Poulter is amazing. She runs Women's Chorus smoothly and efficiently. She is always kind but expects you to put in the work to be excellent. She is not very accessible to individual students (prefers you talk to the Women's Chorus leadership or the assistant conductor).

I absolutely adore Dr. Poulter! She can be a little strict sometimes, but that attitude is what brings out the best in Women's Chorus. She's hilarious  and you can also feel the love she has for music and for her students. Just be aware that choir is a huge time commitment for only 1 credit hour, but to me it is so worth it!
10/10 no complaints. Leads with respect and kindness. Love her more and more each day

I love Dr. Poulter! She is an experienced and impactful conductor who is very respected and loved by her students. She runs Women's Chorus beautifully with high levels of professionalism and care. I love coming to class and I have learned so much under her direction.

Dr. Poulter is the best professor at BYU. She is so inspirational and makes the choir a safe space. She expects a lot from you, it is a big time commitment, but in my opinion, it is absolutely worth it. It should be worth more credits, but what can you do?

Dr. Poulter sets the example and tone for a great Women's Chorus environment and culture. I like that she has clear expectations and plans for each rehearsal (she plans for more than we can do in a day, but we always manage to finish everything we need to). Choir is a big time and effort investment, but the experiences gained from it are worth it!

Dr. Poulter is amazing! While she's strict about phones and attention to detail, it really isn't unreasonable. Asking for 1 hour of time and attention during rehearsal is what allows women's chorus to sound so good! It is a TON of commitment for any BYU choir, but so worth it! Dr. Poulter cares so much about her students and it's a great class!

I love Women's Chorus. I did not join until Winter semester, so I do not know many of the girls in the class. However, it was still a great experience. We made amazing music and I love the high expectations Dr. Poulter has for us. She's strict about phones and talking during class, but I don't mind that. Highly recommend!

Dr. Poulter is a great director and very knowledgeable. My one complaint is that she was a little "all-work, no play" so it feels very easy to be lost in the crowd. Attendance is mandatory as it is the only grade in the class. Also four-and-a-half hours of rehearsal a week plus performance felt like a little much for a one credit class.

Dr. Poulter is one of the best choir directors I've ever had. She is so kind and loving, and still is tough and gets stuff done in class. I have never been in a choir that sounded as good as women's chorus does with Dr. Poulter leading us.

Dr. Poulter is amazing! She cares about every one of her singers and makes and effort to help you feel loved. This class should not be taken lightly: it's a 1 credit class that meets for 4 rehearsals a week, has concerts, and requires outside memorization. BUT it's so worth it! Being in Women's Chorus was one of the best decisions I made at BYU.

I LOVE Dr. Poulter. If you get a chance to take a class from her, do it and consider yourself blessed. She made singing in a pandemic not only doable, but still enjoyable! Every class I came away feeling loved and needed. And she is so good at making spiritual connections! Probably my favorite professor thus far. Please don't miss this opportunity.

Loveliest woman I have ever met. You can tell right away how much love she has for God, the music, and especially her students. I worked with her one-on-one a few times after rehearsal and she was the best voice teacher ever. Even if you are not a music major, take the class just for her. 12/10 I love her

Dr. Poulter is the best director I have ever had! She sincerely cares about her students and believes in their ability to perform, and knows what to do to enhance it and how show that ability to the audience. She has a vision and has a lot of artistic and personal integrity. It's an honor to sing under her.
She is the bomb yoga teacher, loved taking the class from her!
She is at the top of the hotness scale.  Hot pepper x2.  I'd marry her if she weren't married to that other guy....
She is awesome! Loved taking her class and would take it again in a heart beat

I took LING 210 (not an option here) and loved it! Pro. Stanley is very passionate, and he makes difficult concepts incredibly interesting and fun to learn. I loved his class, however there is a TON of material to cover, and while the tests are open note, you will use every minute given for them. Homework can be difficult, but it is necessary.
Seriously awesome!

Dr. Stanley is AMAZING. If I could take every class from him, I would. I took his Applied Phonetics class and the homework was application-based which helped me understand things a lot better. The final was a 10-page paper and presentation, but totally manageable if you start thinking about it early.

Four synthesis papers where we applied what we learned. Short, applicable weekly homeworks (look at them early in the week). The final project was so much fun, but definitely should have started sooner to have more time to write 10 pages. Lectures were engaging, and I never opened the textbook. I'm a repeat student, highly recommend Dr. Stanley!

Cares about his students! Respectful and approachable! No busy-work! All assignments are practical applications of course content. Textbook readings are helpful... but not required. Although attendance is not required, you don't want to miss a single lecture. They are incredible!!
I have taken multiple classes with Professor Stanely and he is fantastic. He genuinely tries to make class interesting and accessible. Thank you, Professor Stanely.

I have taken 2 classes from Professor Stanley and he is incredible. He's a new teacher (I was in his class his first 2 semesters teaching!) but he is so passionate about linguistics that it's contagious. He's respectful and flexible with his students and really did make things I didn't really care too much about way more interesting and fun.

I wasn't excited to take this class at all, but Dr. Stanley made it amazing. He is so passionate about what he teaches, and it shows in the quality of his lectures. He is extremely accommodating and organized the class really efficiently.

Professor Stanley is a great professor, and you should take 240 from him. He knows what he's talking about because he's had first-hand experience with the tools we discussed. The only thing I didn't like was that he posted most assignments on LS right before they were due which made it hard to plan out my homework for the week ahead of time.

I love Professor Stanley! He is so chill - he's totally fine with late work, and he's always willing to help with assignments. He made it easy to do well and learn a lot about various Linguistic programs/tools. There are no exams, although there are a few open book reading quizzes and some homework assignments. There is a semester-long project.

Professor Fluhman is one of my favorite professors ever! If I could take every history class from him, I would. He is super flexible and willing to work with students. We had input in nearly every major paper or discussion. It was a lot of reading, but you could skim it and be fine; daily attendance quizzes on general things from the reading.

Prof Fluhman has the most interesting and engaging lectures but the test are SO hard! So be ready! There are weekly assignments, 2 big tests, 4 books to read, and one 10 page paper. He is hilarious and so caring, but sometimes the class felt too difficult. Overall, it is an interesting class that will challenge you.

Dr. Fluhman is AMAZING! He is caring, funny, witty, and makes class so much fun. He clearly knows his stuff and is passionate about history. His tests are insanely hard and the study guides aren't helpful, but he takes out questions that most people miss. Definitely a hard class, but if you put in the work, you can do well. Take a class from him!

TAKE FROM PROF FLUHMAN!!!!! Every lecture was engaging, funny, and educational. Also very caring- often asked our class for feedback, and gave us lots of extra credit. Weekly essay and lots of reading. Not an easy A. Time consuming, requires high-level analysis skills, and challenging tests. But it was super rewarding- HIGHLY recommend!!

Prof. Fluhman is a wonderful professor. He is very caring to all of his students and gave rebate on exam questions that majority got wrong. The multiple choice section of his exams require a lot of studying and even then were rough. BUT he is very VERY generous on his writing sections. He is understanding and easy to contact for meetings/ questions

Prof. Fluhman is one of the best teachers I have ever had-he loves his students. However, this class was very difficult. You have to pay attention to details DURING his lectures to know material for the tests that are really hard. There was also a 500 word essay every friday based on reading. Textbook helps but you need to know lecture details!!

I was in his first class after he hadn't taught for a decade, so hopefully he learned more from our class. He enforced heavy readings, a reading quiz at the beginning of each class, and the tests were worded wildly and asked random questions. I'd rate him 5/5, because he cares for everyone and loves what he does, but it was hard to do well in class

Love this guy! Tests - multiple choice rough, but he's lenient on the writing part and offers rebates for ?s most the class got wrong. He gets sidetracked, but his rants are hilarious and he hits on all the main points you will need for the exam. Be sure to read as there are (super easy) quizzes on the textbook and it sets the stage for lectures

Love him! amazing teacher with a passion for teaching. Readings are not hard with a one-question EASY quiz at the beginning of class for attendance. He made me laugh every single class, so genuine, cares so much. HIGHLY recommend. He struggles to write test questions sometimes but is great at taking feedback and gives back points for his mistakes.

I laughed and I was inspired pretty much every single day in this class. Fluhman was never afraid to "wrestle" with the tough subjects and the guy is just hilarious.  Also, I learned a lot. #dancegang
You are making the biggest mistake of your life if you don't take a class from Prof. Fluhman. He will change your life.
Great class. Very tough grader. He doesn't know how to write tests.

Funny. However, his tests are 50% essay and 50% multiple choice. The multiple choice is not easy. He expects you to use all your notes to study for it and does not give you a helpful study guide. The essay is even worse. You have to be prepared with an outline of 25 possible subjects if you hope to stand a chance.

Prof. Fluhman is the best D&C teacher by far!  He is incredibly enthusiastic and knowledgeable. I always felt the spirit in his class and the assignments were all easy and helped students grow spiritually. Written assignments due each week along with one midterm and the final.
