Tests are simple but confusing at times, making them a little difficult.
This class was tough but Fluhman is my favorite professor I've ever had. If you have an interest in religious history, do it!

Fluhman is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He is absolutely hilarious, and might be the most historically and religiouslly knowledgable man I have ever met. It is a hard class, but it was a great class.

Professor Fluhman is the best. I loved this class so much. There was an essay midterm and a final that is half essay and half multiple choice. There were two other essays on books that you read and a writing assignment each week (they are pass fail though). Make sure to include as much detail in the essays as you can because that is what he likes.

Professor Fluhman is a very entertaining teacher. He makes lectures interesting with his extremely high energy,thorough knowledge and side facts. His class is easy, if you do everything. There is quite a bit of reading and writing. An essay was due over the reading every class, but getting an A is quite manageable if you keep up. He's pretty great!

Great history class. Professor Fluhman really helped me love history. Very great in office hours to help students. TAKE YOUR ESSAY IDEAS TO HIM to review before writing midterm/final. Two easy essays per week. 2 essay midterm and 1 essay/multiple choice final. Hopefully he changes the multiple choice because they were diabolical.

Dr. Fluhman is AMAZING!!  Very animated, enthusiastic and passionate about both the subject matter and teaching, which is a great combination.  Work load is a little high for a 200 level class, but all the assignments are worthwhile and help you learn a lot.  Definitely take this class from Dr. Fluhman!  He is interesting and funny!!!

you have reading and a responce due before every class with a larger essay on a book due at midterm and finals. The Midterm was just two essays and everyone did very well the final was harder with multiple choice and an essay. Lectures are very engageing and he is quite funny. He is open to suggestions on changing course load such as essay length.

Professor Fluhman is the man. A professor doesn't get better than him. Hilarious, insanely intelligent, very open-minded, and all around a good man. Totally reasonable as far as grades and tests go. I've taken two classes from him and hope I can take more.

Loved loved loved Prof. Fluhman!  He is a master storyteller!  He tells the history in such a way that leaves in an imprint in your mind so you remember it for the tests!  Lots of reading, but he doesn't check it.  He made UT history interesting

Take American Christianity from Professor Fluhman!He is hilarious and energetic yet I always walk away inspired. Tests can be a tad tricky but other than that, reasonable work for a two credit class. And he adjusts bad questions! One of the best professors I've ever had

Brother Fluhman is an amazing teacher! Yes his tests are hard but he will help you if you have questions.  Class is never boring and he always comes to class with a smile.  He will help you with anything.  I would recommend any class from him!

Dr. Fluhman reminds me of Brian Regan a bit, he is hilarious! He is one tough teacher though. Work hard and you'll do fine. He is flexible to consensus and will grade on a curve if the test proves too hard. We were his first UT HIST class he taught yet, but I say he did very well.

Honestly, Professor Fluhman has been the best professor I've had here at BYU. His tests are hard, but I've never felt the spirit so frequently in his class. He knows the doctrine incredibly well, and knows how to tie in the context of revelations with the text itself. I plan on doing whatever it takes to take the second of D&C from him.

Great professor. Brings a lot of energy to class and is passionate about the material. His lectures were very thought-provoking and I found myself thinking about the ideas outside class. Grading is fair (one midterm for which he gives a good study guide) and assignments are useful (10 short essays during the semester).
By far most entertaining professor I've had. Prof. Fluhman knows and loves what he's talking about, which makes lectures even more fun. Tests are hard, but the he makes class is worth it.
Hilarious Teacher but the tests are impossible to know what will be on them. He gives you a review sheet but the way he asks questions makes the tests pretty hard.
Best lectures you'll ever attend.  All tests are class notes, with light supplement from the textbook. If you read "American Jesus" along with the class it adds to the clarity.

Second half of D&C: Fluhman was entertaining and I learned a lot. He is very passionate about Church History and makes you want to learn more. Class isn't that difficult if you don't miss any days and take diligent notes.
Awesome teacher. Lectures are so engaging. Not afraid of exploring doctrines that other teachers get squirmy about. Doesn't make Doc & Cov a church history class which I liked a lot.

LOVE LOVE LOVE this class and Professor Fluhman! If you want entertainment and to be taught this is the class for you! Tests are easy and lectures are incredible. Take any class from him that you can!

Tends to ramble and trail off the subject then expects you to know what to study for the tests. This makes the class a bit hard but lectures are very enjoyable and you get to learn lots of random facts.

Professor Fluhman jokes around and wastes time in his class as if it would end up being an easy A class but I felt lucky to pull a B-. He expects way too much for a 2 credit religion class. I felt that his tests were graded very harshly. Don't bother reading the book, you'd be better off with wikipedia and flashcards. Funny, but not a good teacher.

Dr. Fluhman is a great teacher. The only text we used was the D&C, and I learned how to get more from my scripture study from this class. Dr. Fluhman is an entertaining teacher. His lectures can be scattered, but the study guides help you catch anything he forgets to teach. I highly recommend this class!

Brother Fluhman is an amazing teacher. Assignments and tests are not bad at all as long as you go to class, which, believe me, you will enjoy doing. He is hilarious and inspiring. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND him as a professor.

Very ecletic teaching style.  I did very poorly on the tests despite studying.  I had a hard time following him (he doesn't really use the text).  He is absolutely hysterical though.  If you can follow lots of tangents and disorganized teaching, he is the teacher for you.  I personally did not like this class and would not recommend it to anyone.

He is very passionate about the D&C and knows his church history. Pay close attention in class because his midterms and finals are directly from topics he discusses in class. The lectures are fascinating and he always tries to get feedback and keep people engaged. Great sense of humor and a great class to take.

American Christianity was by far one of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU. Brother Fluhman is HILARIOUS but absolutely brilliant and I learned SO MUCH from him. He makes class interesting with his humor and I was always excited for class. You had to write a few 2-page papers, a midterm and final, both of which I got a 100% on.  Easy but great!

Oh man this class rocks. Br. Fluhman is incredibly entertaining and beyond knowledgeable about the topic. Every class, I laughed my butt off and learned a lot of awesome American Christianity. Book is optional. Tests are fine, just review. LOVED HIM!

He is my favorite teacher ever. I took a second class from him because I loved his class so much. His tests are hard enough that you have to study, but not too bad. His lectures are very entertaining, he makes everything interesting. He really cares about students and getting to know them. Take his class if you can!

Great professor! Teaches doctrine, not his opinion. He's hilarious, engaging, encourages discussion but keeps it on track. Excellent lectures, spirit-filled, and filled with historical context - he loves the stuff and makes it come alive for you. Tests can be hard if you don't take notes.

Great Professor who loves what he does!  This class really taught me a lot and the class is really interesting.  (There is so much thrown at you though).  This class really teaches you about other religions and how to get to know them.  Fascinating!!  Wished the class was more often.  I didn't do any reading and I got an A-.  Tests are not bad.

Brother Fluhman is amazing!  He is energetic, knowledgable, and just so full of spirit and the Spirit.  The study guides are very helpful for the tests.  Do your reading, and you will definitely get more out of class discussions.  My testimony grew from this class.

I must have no sense of humor, he tried way too hard to make fun of "Utah Culture" which might be funny once in a while but it got old really quick.  You never knew what he was talking about because he rambled and told stupid stories and laughed at himself. Attendance was mandatory for your grade and although it was an easy A it wasn't worth it.
My favorite teacher at the Y, as this was my fourth class from him. He's funny and entertaining, but also serious and interesting--the perfect combination, imo. Best teacher around!
Favorite teacher at BYU. Period.

Fantasic professor with the gift of gab. Understands the subjects thoroughly and keeps the atmosphere lively and enjoyable. Very highly recommended. Tests require you to study, but the questions are clear, plus he will review your test after the TA grades it if you disagree with anything. No attendance policy. No textbook used except D&C.

Bro. Fluhman is it. This guy is tons of laughs and really is passionate about the doctrine. He knows his stuff and teaches well. IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR A MANAGABLE RELIGION COURSE, THIS IS IT. This is how religion courses should be. and apparently according to the tomale by his name, he his hot.

hilarious teacher and wonderful class. if you go to class and take ample notes, you will get your A.  he keeps you entertained while learning about the doctrine in the scriptures, which is a hard thing to do in my opinion.  take this class from him.  he's a good man.

Bro Fluhman is an incredible lecturer. This was the first class in which I could easily pay attention the entire time each lecture period. He is lively, articulate, and quite humorous at times. It was also nice to have a religion class with unfamiliar subject matter (Rel 353). I recommend this course to anyone who asks me about religion classes.

He's a fun, insightful teacher. Very open to student feedback especially since this is a new course.Kind of heavy on the reading but at least he doesn't quiz or test you on it.Brings up interesting issues.The tests are easy--based all on lectures, so take very good notes.His exams are very straightforward and he gives you a review sheet.
No Comments

I loved this class.  It brought a whole new look the D&C.  It really came to life with the history, indepth look at the revelations and church history pluggs.  I love the D&C now and I will take any class by Brother Fluhman that is offered.  He is quite possibly the best teacher I have had so far at BYU.
Great teacher. Hilarious and has lots of energy, but brings the spirit into class. He was a little picky on the tests, which were mostly short answer. Great class.

I loved the class. The amount of information he gives you is INSANE, but one of the first religion classes I've taken where it didnt feel like sunday school or seminary. Class was not mandatory, but if you didnt go you are screwed for the tests. Lots of notes, but overall great class.

Lectures are very detailed.  He just rattles off notes, details and facts.  He is a great teacher and is funny but this is a new class and so he's figuring it out.  There are like 5, 2 pg papers and not much reading.  99% of the exam is from class notes.  HE also lets you have a sheet of notes for the test!  Easy but TONS of details

American Christianity: brand new course & Fluhman is perfect for the job.  Interesting lectures and class. Basically just write a few papers, ace a take home exam, and this class is a breeze.  However, there is a lot of notes/material for a 2 credit class. He's the man and this is a great class.

he is the funniest guy around!  he makes learning the material (which is already very interesting) fun.  i learned so much about American Christianity.  he is funny and professional at the same time.  take this class!

awesome, awesome teacher!  Only uses the scriptures, so no other texts necessary.  I looked forward to class everyday and felt the spirit each lecture.  Bro. Fluhman has amazing insight on the D&C and brings an appropriate amount of humor into every class.  Exams are based largely on lectures. Definitely take from him! Funny guy!

The first day in class Bro. Fluhman had me crying, he was so funny.  I loved his class because he kept it applicable to life.  There were times he said things I know I needed to hear, and the Lord was inspiring him.  It was an awesome class.  He really cares about the students and has a huuuuge passion for the scriptures and the church.

If I were you, I'd reconsider taking American Christianity. Honestly, I am super confused in the class because I don't know what is important to know.  I don't really enjoy it. I feel bad because I know he is trying really hard to make this enjoyable, but it just isn't. He is an awesome teacher for any other religion class but this one.
Best teacher at BYU, amazing lectures, you look forward to class everyday
Brother Fluhman is a spiritual giant and inspiring teacher! I loved his class because he always brought the Spirit and he was so down to earth. Don't leave BYU without taking a class from him!

This was an awesome class. He gives very interesting lectures. The tests are kind of difficult, but he tells you what you need to know. Very funny teacher with great stories. I learned a great deal about Church History in his class.
One of the best religion teachers you will have. Take his class or forever hold your peace.

He is, hands down, the best teacher I've ever had. Not concerned with tedious busy work, but wants you to understand concepts and see things differently. I'd feel invigorated after the classes. He's very knowledgeable and respectful of questions and comments; I can't imagine a better teacher. He's awesome! My 2nd class from him, not the last. Great

All these people who have given Fluhman such great rating must have had him after I did.Maybe he is a much better professor now.I didn't not enjoy his class or exams.The exams required information never lectured on in class and not in the book or handouts.When I had him he was on a power trip from just earning his PHD.Arrogant and rude to students.

If you are wanting the highest quality lecture BYU offers, this class is for you. The exams are fair, for once. It will require study and articulation, but your grade will be fair and not inflated or deflated. By far the most moving class I've had as a university student. It's inspired me like nothing else. Best rating I can give.

Easily my best Church history professor (I took all three semesters).  He was the only I teacher I had who willingly tackled controversial questions.  Ironically, however, once we faced them we found there was never any reason to worry.  His class is one of the few the directly fueled my testimony.

BEST RELIGIONS CLASS YOU'LL EVER TAKE AT BYU, I PROMISE. HE'S AWESOME. HIS CLASSES ARE HILARIOUS AND HE REALLY HELPS YOU UNDERSTAND. AND IT'S EASY. HE'S NOT INTERESTED IN BUSY WORK AT ALL, HE JUST REALLY WANTS YOU TO LEARN SOMETHING.
THE BEST teacher I have ever had for a religion course.  Period.  Three cheers for spencer fluhman!

One of the best teachers I've had at BYU. I usually space out in one-sided lectures, but he opens class up to discussion and is a lively orator, very energetic and sharp. Workload is light. His class changed my life in a small way.
Great teacher. Class not jumbled up with busy work. Assignments are good and you will learn a lot but tests are a little harder than most religion teachers. He is worth taking

Great lessons.  INVOLVES STUDENTS.  Treats students as his OWN PEERS!  Study Guides very helpful.  Know those and your bound to score in the nineties.  THOUGHT PROVOKING.  Very honest and humble in presentation of doctrine and theory.

He is my favorite teacher religion or otherwise.  He is charismatic and eloquent and has passion for what he teaches.  He has great insights and loves what he does.  He treats the students as his equals.

He's a real genuine guy.  He wants you to do well.  He has great orator/teaching skills.  He does a great job of feeding off of your comments in class. He's pretty young, but has much to teach.  It's pretty amazing seeing him on fire when he speaks.

Best religion instructor I've ever had. Teaches with the Spirit and dynamic. You have to do several little 2 page "what have I learned" papers and you do have to study for the exams but I thought it was an easy and inspirational class.

I LOVED his class. He is by far the best religion teacher I've had. He's very passionate about the Gospel, and he's incredibly articulate and eloquent. I think he's also very clear; I didn't think his tests were too difficult at all, like others mentioned

Oh I did not enjoy Fluhman's class at all simply because of his ridiculous exams. A lot of the material found on the study guide was not on the test. He was a nice guy, of course. Unless relgion is a strong point for you don't take it from him.
Very good and fair.  Actually gives a fair work load for a two credit class.  If you go to class, tests are easy, very good lecturer.

Did not really like this guy.  Spent the whole class spewing little anti-mormon antidotes (he's doing his doctoral thesis on the stuff) and gave these tests which were impossible to study for.  Easy on papers and you get extra credit for reading.
Bro Fluhman is the best religion teacher i have had at byu.  i liked him so much i also took his 330 class.  his lectures are really good!  definatly take his class if you can.
No Comments
No Comments
Best religion teacher I've had. Very fun and involved class discussions. You have to pay attention and take notes, but there are only two tests and two 2 page pass/fail papers.

Probably the best religion teacher I've had while at BYU. He makes class exciting and engaging, as well as fun and laid back. Focuses on doctrine and discussion. If you have the chance to take a class from Bro. Fluhman, DO IT!

Easily one of the best teachers at Brigham Young University.  Extremely fair and academically minded.  Funny, explains things well, and always willing to work with students.  Unless you try not to, you can get an A in this class.

Great guy. However, the exams really weren't done well. On the plus side, he realized that and fixed them every time! Our first exam was only 50 minutes and in class. It was not nearly enough time, and it was VERY difficult. But, he re-made it better and gave a re-do. The second exam was 3.5 hours, and so long that I STILL didn't finish in time.

Definitely at the top of my list in terms of professors at BYU. He teaches in a way that really teaches you how to solve difficult problems. We always stayed focused and tackled problems head on. He's got great self awareness, can read the room well and knows how the students are doing. 402 is very useful and challenging.

He teaches both 402 and 413 in the junior core. He expects you to study outside of class, but his classes are not terrible. For 402 make sure you do extra practices from the textbook and reachout when you are having trouble. For 413 you just have to watch the videos; I left class after attendence was taken every period and did fine.
He is great, I learned a lot and even got a job thanks to skills I learned in this class. Gives a lot of practice and help.
Love this man! He is one of the best professors. He really cares about students, has clear grading criteria, great class structure. Explains everything so easy that even child can understand.

I really enjoyed Professor Hilton's class for 402. He was a great teacher and constantly reminded us of hard concepts coming up. He was very responsive to questions that came up and was very willing to help students succeed along with most of his TAs.

This has been one of my favorite classes at BYU. Everything was crystal clear and it just made sense. Every concept built on the previous one in a way that made sense. He does a really good job of explaining difficult concepts, especially in office hours. I had questions that were easily resolved once I went and saw him.
Great professor and great person. Does a wonderful job at teaching the concepts.

Prof Hilton is great! I thought he was a good professor with a pretty well organized class and clear expectations. Always willing to trouble shoot coding issues, answer questions, and provide feedback. We mostly learned through videos, which was pretty nice because you can pause and rewind as needed.

I love Professor Hilton and really enjoyed the Junior Core with him, but I never felt that I learned much from IS413. He showed us exactly how to do things out of necessity of the difficultly of the content, but I don't think we were ever able to learn the material deeply. He puts in a LOT of work to help us in the course.

took all 3 classes from Hilton- he is so kind and really wants to help his students. He was a new professor when we started, but you can really see the growth in him as a professor. Truly a great professor who is getting better each time.

This was basically an online class. He told us the first day that class was optional and would just be a time for us to do our homework and ask questions but that he wouldn't really be teaching us anything because all the lectures were online. Online lectures were full of content unrelated to class which was frustrating at times.

The class frankly felt pretty pointless, but Hilton is a homie. If you have a job or internship where you use agile project management, you'll learn probably everything you need to to do well in your job. The class did not feel very effective in expanding a skill set. Hilton is of course awesome though.

Bad course, textbook is 0/10 and most of it you'll be better off if you just watch a bunch of sql on youtube. lectures are just repeat of the textbook, reading quizzes are VERY LOOSELY based on the reading, i.e. you'll have at least 1 question on each quiz that makes no sense and wasn't in the reading. unfortunately is a mandatory course

Great teacher who prioritizes students understanding of the material. Students were expected to watch videos and code along with practice programs before class, and he spent class answering individual questions.
Class was just him helping us with assignments, which could be helpful as long as you don’t stay behind. Great teacher, and very kind and caring.

Professor Hilton is awesome! One of the nicest people I've met. Really funny. Very accessible. He does a lot of examples in the class and that are very useful. The material in 402 wasn't difficult, just the grading structure of his class made it hard to get an A. Just make sure you try on every assignment.

Hilton is a homie. Very caring, gives great spiritual thoughts, taught well, and was very humble and thorough. Also very willing to help. Just practice SQL a lot, and you'll be good. Great sense of humor also.

I had him for both 402 and 413, I enjoyed both courses! It was his first semester teaching the material at BYU, therefore he was developing the course as he went and constantly was seeking feedback. After 402, he had a write feedback and personally responded which was appreciated! I am sure future courses from him will only get better, Great guy!

Prof Hilton was awesome. I had him both semesters of the Junior Core (402 & 413) and really liked both of his classes. Considering he was brand new this year, I think he did an exceptional job. I would take a class again from him in a heart beat! Make sure to follow the rubric for assignments and projects.

This is the second time I have had Professor Hilton as a teacher. Claimed to want feedback from first class w/ him. I gave him feedback about timed tests, and this semester he laughed in our faces about how "dumb" the feedback was. He does not truly respect students. Massive, timed tests, w/ barely enough time to finish. Teaches straight from book
justt the bestest. i know kow hoew too spll correckley now. tanks Spenper!

Spencer was great, the only hw the entire semester is weekly readings, 3 books you have to read, and group presentations on the books, and then a final portfolio consisting of a poem, and essay, and a short story. I do wish there was more structure but besides that, I loved this class and learned so much because of spencer! his feedback is great!

Professor Hyde is one of my favorite writing professors I've had. He's kind and funny, and all of his lectures impact my writing in a positive way. Rather than just simply writing, Hyde gives us plenty of tools and ideas to improve any writing piece. This class and professor is perfect for anyone wanting to improve their writing!

Super great writing teacher! Be prepared to write by the seat of your pants, but also to learn a lot. Class is mostly workshopping with short lectures on craft, but the workshop feedback is quality and the format (writers posing questions to readers) is very helpful! Prof. Hyde is encouraging and gives great feedback.

I LOVED Professor Hyde. He was so funny and he has made writing fun and exciting. The only reason I got a low grade was because I missed some of the essential homework. He is one of the reasons I'm majoring in english. Recommend him 10/10

I loved how Dr. Hyde's classes focused on discussion that helped us engage with the material and think for ourselves in ways that would help us gain inspiration as writers ourselves!  He is super funny and is extremely approachable despite being a very talented and accomplished professor.  I took the class as a STEM major and loved it!

Spencer was amazing! Learned so much from him & how he structured his class. He was genuine about feedback, very kind, and kept a respectful learning environment. I got points back on an assignment because I always participated in class. He's also the fastest grader I've ever met. Expects a lot, but is chill about it. Highly recommend if you write!

I took writing 150 from him, which is not the usual class that he teaches. I usually hate writing classes, but I loved this class. He seemed to care about all of his students, and I was never too stressed. He also gave so many opportunities for extra credit and a chance to rewrite your papers for a new grade. Also, you get your grades back fast.

Spencer is the nicest guy you will ever meet! We wrote 3-4 papers throughout the year, but had no tests. He is not a tough grader whatsoever, and will let you rewrite your paper for a better grade. He really just seems like another one of the college kids. At no point was I stressed in this class. Easy A for sure

This is for 318R as well, since the courses were almost exactly the same. He covers the basic formula of a story and discusses what makes great Literature. The grading rubric is unknown and so his grades are completely arbitrary and theres no way to tell what makes a good story. You read a lot, but dont write a lot, surprisingly. Hes fine.

E321R (the English Department Reading Series) is a hidden gem of BYU. 1 credit class where once a week, you listen to an author/poet/novelist/etc read some of their work and then you write a 250 word response. Fairly easy A and really enjoyable.

Absolutely incredible professor. Spencer is the nicest, most approachable guy and he really cares about your success. He reads and grades all papers and offers wonderful feedback. As long as you do your best and revise according to workshop suggestions, you will do just fine. I would take him for every English course if I could!

Spencer doesn't have a lot of assignments and zero tests. My only complaint other than the fact this class is a repeat of AP Lit & Lang is that when I went to conferences on a paper, he'd tell me things, which I would then work on, and then he would dock me for things he didn't even mention in conferences that I specifically asked about.

Excellent teacher. He is very helpful, cool, down to earth and connects well with the students. Any english class will require a lot of writing but he prepares you well and knows his stuff. All around great guy!
This class helped me a lot in my writing skills and Spencer made something that I was never interested in more enjoyable.
Spencer is a great teacher. He is really easy going but he knows his stuff and is really passionate about writing. He makes the class fun and pretty easy, but you still learn a fair amount.

Spencer was a great professor, the class was pretty laid-back and informal. A very entertaining class. Difficulty depends on your writing ability. He grades you honestly. And he gives you extra credit for using Rate My Professor. I would definitely recommend this class.
Great teacher. Very helpful. Makes class fun and enjoyable.
I really liked him. He was nice,  relaxed and helped the students when they needed help.
Very good teacher, one of my favorites actually.  Grades reasonably and makes class very fun.
He made class really entertaining! He was always willing to help you with your papers. Sometimes class was disorganized, but overall it was a fun class!

Spencer is pretty cool! He's really chill and fairly easy going. You do have to go to each class, but he's really willing to work with you if you have questions or need help with an assignment. We watched a ton of YouTube clips, and class is pretty entertaining! Totally recommend taking this class with Spencer!
We watched a lot of you tube videos which was fun.

Awesome teacher, lots of fun and really knows his stuff. Very compassionate and shows genuine interest in each student. My previous professor disappeared halfway through the semester and Spencer (He prefers you to call him Spencer) volunteered to step in and finish teaching our class. Extremely talented writer in and of himself

Spencer is hilarious and the class is pretty fun (especially if you like YouTube). He's very approachable and easy to get a hold of, but it is kind of up to you to ask questions and learn how to write. Overall, this is an easy class (as long as you know how to write...).
I enjoyed this class. He really helped me understand how to write a good paper. And was always willing to help me.
Enjoyed class.

Fun class, I like how he uses a lot of media tools (videos). It's a pretty easy class. Just make sure you have him tear your essays apart and tell you everything that's wrong with them. And you'll get good grades on the papers. He's really funny, too.

Spencer is really helpful and approachable. When I came to him with a concern he usually was always willing to make an exception. He helps make this class fairly easy, which is a relief to have in a class your freshman year when everything can be way overwhelming.

Spencers class is easy, however its kind of up to you to learn how/what to write about. He is hilarious, and really easy to get along with... But the papers are crap. The grades are ehh. Overall, passible and fun.
Spencer is a cool fun guy, but if you are looking for a class that actually teaches you something, I wouldn't take this one from him.
This class really helped me learn how to construct well written papers. Spencer was very helpful with this.
I didn't learn a lot from his class although he was a fairly easy teacher. He is really funny, too.
Spencer made things easy to understand and his class focuses on the assignments instead of distracting you from them with busy work.
Great professor.

Spencer was really helpful when I asked questions or talked to him outside of class. He was an effective instructor for the most part, but some of the time spent in class was irrelevant. Also, sometimes the assignments were unclear. But overall I would recommend him.

I took his online class. This isn't my favorite subject, but his lectures were interesting and helped me learn the material. For an online course, this was organized well and the assignments were relevant and helpful. If you're not a good online learner, I would recommend the in person class, but for an online class this was pretty great.

So many readings for each day it was ridiculous (2-6 full articles/chapters a day). I don't know how he expects anyone to keep up on top of their other classes and activities. 10/10 don't recommend. I wish I looked at his reviews before signing up for his class. I understand that it is a 3 credit class, but I've never taken a harder class before.

I took this class online and it was ok. There was an exam the first 3 weeks of class and two others throughout the semester and several writing assignments. Not much involvement from Spencer and his lectures are super outdated. Wish this class could have been better!

Super important class to take, Spencer is well informed about so many topics and is great at mediating these difficult topics. It is definitely an upper-level undergraduate class so the work load is a bit heavier but he is super accessible.

Spencer makes his lectures interesting, and he addresses hard topics well. He wants to help you- go to office hours and do the extra credit. However, his grading was very unclear (no rubrics), and there are a lot of writing assignments. Class is heavily based on participation- raise your hand every class or you won't get full participation points.

Spencer is a very interactive and friendly person, and it definitely translated into his lectures. He offers a lot of extra credit opportunities, which is awesome, and he is very passionate about the subject he teaches. Participation is pretty important in the class and there are quite a few writing assignments, but he drops a few for grace.

Spencer is a nice guy, and his lectures were sometimes funny. However, he preaches that everyone's opinions should matter and that we should be open to changing our mind, but the midterm and final exam test essay questions were about proving why HIS opinion was right. No grading rubric, its the wild west. Final exam is a 10 page essay. Thumbs down.

This class is entirely opinion based. Spencer thinks he knows everything and he will let you know. Doesn't give clear rubrics because the "point" of the assignments and papers is to see if you understand what he wants. Grading takes forever, everything is essay and short answer so its hard to understand exactly what grading expectations are.

I would NOT recommend taking his courses.  His TA's are too involved and grade sooooo rough for no reason. I had a B+ the entire semester until the final because the TA gave me a terrible grade with no explanation as to why. I reached out asking why I got docked so many points when I followed the rubric exactly and got ghosted.

Spencer's online recorded lectures were actually great! His tests are so hard though- the final had 60 questions, and 50 of them were true and false. Tests seem more like they are to trick you than test you. You could do corrections for the 2 midterms, but not final. All tests were online proctored. There is a research paper that's 14 pages.

The professor is great but the TA's are so so tough. They grade papers like sharks and I really struggled to do well in the writing portion even after working with the TA who graded mine and met with her almost once a week. Online lectures were insightful and entertaining. Overall not bad but be really careful about your papers.

He had very limited involvement. His TA's did all the grading, and they graded harshly. They would often dock you simply because they didn't like your answer (learned this after meeting with them on Zoom multiple times). Tests are difficult- the questions feel like they're meant to trick you instead of actually testing your knowledge on concepts.

Spencer cares and wants you to succeed, but he makes his class difficult. Go to the TA reviews! These saved my grade and I still studied hard for the tests! The final research paper takes up time, but it's broken up throughout the semester. Revise your paper as you go otherwise you'll be left to revise all of it at the end. I never read textbook.

Can't imagine taking SFL354 from anyone else. Spencer is funny, informative, & truly cared and facilitated genuine conversations about difficult topics. He valued every student's opinion even when students disagreed. Expect to write a LOT for the exams and essay projects. Essay rubric could have been more detailed & explanatory, so ask questions.

This class structure was very nice and easy. 2 midterms and a final but they were pretty easy, just watch the TA review videos and study a few terms and examples of them. The final project was worked on throughout the semester in chunks which made it very manageable. I never once looked at the textbook. Very easy class to do online.

Spencer is very very good in-person teaching. I took online 290 and hated it but 354 and loved it. He is funny, passionate about social sciences and does a lot of humanitarian work. We differed in our opinions, politics, and perspectives but he is always more than respecting and even opened my mind to some ideas I never thought of. Great professor.

This class was alright, but not my favorite. I didn't watch the lectures or read the textbook and did just fine! The TA reviews are what I used to help me for the test because they go over everything you need to know in 30 min. Don't worry about buying the textbook, you don't need it. The TAs graded word for word by the rubric, so 100% use those.

Extremely intelligent guy and has a lot of interesting things to say! However, he says these things with a PowerPoint lecture every single day and it was honestly hard to stay awake. There are also a lot of readings that you have to report on each class. While it was a lot of work it was educational. Just be prepared to read and put in time.

This class is very hard. The TAs also didn't help at all. I met with them at least 5 times and I walked away feeling worse about the class. Your final grade is basically your midterm, final, and final project grade. He required the txtbk and we never even opened it. Honestly, do yourself a favor and do not take this class online.

This class was tough. The video lectures were super saturated with niche information, and that's what you were tested on. Spencer  explains that this course is meant to be tough to make sure you understand the information. There's so much to learn and the course isn't built in a way that helps you retain the information well.

This class really isn't that bad. Wasn't a huge fan of his lecture/teaching style, but I got along okay. Textbook is "required" but it's the same stuff in the lecture, so don't bother buying it. Grading criteria is very clear which I really appreciated. Final paper is easy, it's an accumulation of what you have worked on all semester. (copy/paste).

Terrible class! Everything is opinion based. There is also a paper due before every class. It took about 1hr. There is also a research paper and 3 "lecture papers." Participation and attendance is mandatory. The midterm is in class and was graded harshly.The final is a take home test but 10 pages long. I have never been more frustrated with a class

Your grade in this class is 60% exams and there are only three of them. They're rather difficult, so you really have to study for them. The assignments feel a lot like busy work and don't really prep you well for the exams. Meet with the TAs, though, and you should get what you need.

I did not like research at all before this class but Professor James presented all the information clearly and simply in interactive ways. TA Reviews are SO helpful. There is a research paper due at the end of the semester but it is broken up into manageable chunks. I recommend doing Stats 121 at the same time because the overlap makes both easier.

Spencer was my first SFL professor and I loved him so much I stuck with him and he mentored me basically until I graduated. Hes overly caring and compassionate so get into his office hours and get to know him. He def teaches one of the most difficult classes in the major, but he teaches it well.
Great professor!

I think he genuinely cares about our success if we show that we have been trying our best. There is a 10+ personal research essay that you work on throughout the semester. The grading criteria is clear, but it would be best to have it overlooked by your TA. If you work on it following the schedule the tests and assignments are doable.

I learned a lot in his class but I didn't enjoy the process. I took his online class so it was hard to really get to know him. I will say that the only time that I tried to reach out to him, he didn't even respond. He did give me the arrogant vibe, but I need to know him more to judge.

I really enjoyed this class. Honestly, it felt like a pretty easy A. A lot of people complain, but it was very straight forward. The class is primarily made up of a weekly lecture and discussion and one large research paper that is split up over the course of the semester. Spencer was very straight forward and was willing to work with us!

Honestly, Spencer James is the worst professor I have ever had at BYU. The class really wasn't that bad, but he made it terrible. The assignments were extremely vague. Important details were either left out or he would just assume we knew things that were never told to us. He was arrogant, annoying, and pompous in lectures. Do not take this class.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class, which is surprising considering it's all about research! Every assignment had a specific grading rubric, so it was super easy to understand what they were looking for, which made it fairly easy! TA review before exams were so helpful. He is super funny in person, so take it on campus if you can! Textbook NOT needed.

Spencer is an incredible teacher. He taught us about life and how to use our education to do things that matter. He's a really humble guy and is very real with his students. He's also funny and teaches really well; its an early morning class but it was a good way to start the day. Not too much work either. Great person. Great teacher.

I took SFL 290 online which was a great option. The online system is super easy to use. I've never met Spencer but he seems rad. Tests can be taken in the testing center or online and the entire semester you're working on an experiment/paper. Work load is kinda heavy. My only issue was with my TA and the strange grading system she used.

Spencer is probably my favorite professor I have ever had at BYU. He is the first professor I have had who I felt like cared about my personal success. Seriously, such a good human. Also, he lets you do test corrections to earn back credit and offers lots of extra credit. He made a very boring subject something that was actually interesting.

This Professor got on my nerves so much that I found myself trying to get an A in his class just to prove that I could beat his ridiculous assignments and impossible grading  Also, this guy is super arrogant and rude.  In my opinion his class was way harder than it needed to be especially as a prerequisite. The ta's are your only hope at surviving

The class just fine. I learned a lot about research. Just be prepared to work hard an visit TAs. Spencer is pretty ridiculous in some of his comments. He likes to make students feel stupid and insignificant. He spends lots of time talking about how hard the class will be rather than actually teaching the material. iClicker attendance every day.

I think Spencer is one of the best. I honestly wasn't looking forward at all to take this class, but he truly means it when he says that he wants you to succeed. His tests are a little more challenging than usual, but he is helpful when you seek for it, and gives you opportunities to get back points. I highly recommend the man.

TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HIM! I loved this class and found it super intriguing! It's definitely a class you have to study for and put effort into, but it wasn't hard to understand at all. I changed my work schedule to get into his 8am class and it was TOTALLY WORTH IT. He is very caring and willing to help you out with anything.
He really helps you understand the material in a simple way. Understand the powerpoint slides and you're good. Hard concepts, but he and the TAs are always helpful and willing.

I don't feel like I learned very much in his class.  The assignments were not well organized, the grading criteria was unclear, yet were pretty difficult and graded tough.   He is a super nice person and is very accessible and caring.

Spencer James is one of my absolute favorite professors! He cares so much about the students and really helps them understand the material. Research Methods is not a simple class, but his teaching is clear and engaging. I am so glad that I took this class from Professor James and no one else! He was exactly who I needed. I highly recommend him!

Spencer was actually a good teacher. The class was reasonable, and we had every opportunity to do well; the final paper was split up over the semester and very doable. That being said, I was appalled by his personality. He is quite self-righteous, and abrasive when it comes to sensitive topics. Just be prepared for that and you should be fine!

I LOVE SPENCER! He is the best professor. This class is hard because there is a lot of material, but Spencer makes this class fun and understandable and is SO willing to work with students. Your final paper is written in portions over the semester, and you correct it as you go, which is so nice!! Loved this class!

Spencer is a fantastic professor. Lots of whiny students complain about the workload, but honestly if you just meet with him or the TA's, you'll get an A. You basically write one big paper but it's split up into sections, so by the end it's all done. It's a lot of new information but he is really helpful if you need it.  Lots of extra credit!!! :)

Spencer James is amazing!!! He does make you work, but what is expected from the students is extremely clear.  He is hilarious and teaches 290 so well.  If you are struggling in class, he will listen to what you have to say and help in any way that he can.  Spencer is awesome and I would take this class again! Nicest professor I've had.

if you don't need this class, don't take it. But because most of us HAVE to, take it from Spencer! He is a great teacher and genuinely cares about his students. Throughout the course you will write an big research paper but he makes it manageable by breaking it up into parts along the way. The TA's are tough but its manageable. Not an easy A.

Spencer was without a doubt the worst professor I've ever had. He spends so much time during class talking about random tangents that are often offensive and degrading to those who don't share his opinions. He tells you upfront that his tests are hard, and thinks that a 69% average is good. Just some things to consider-take this from ANYONE else.

Spencer was fine in teaching the material, but I had a hard time with him because he goes on rants during lecture that aren't related to the material. He made many degrading comments about people with depression (which I and many people have). I never felt like I could go to him for help because I would be judged as lazy. Horrible experience.

This class was a pre-req for other classes. But Spencer made it enjoyable! He cares about the students and really wants to make sure we understand the material. If you do the work, and show you understand, you can get a good grade. Study hard for the midterm and final. We got him to change the final so it was not just T/F questions!

Spencer is an amazing person. One of the kindest individuals I have met. He is a wonderful professor and loves to be your friend. The course is not difficult if you put in the work. My absolute favorite professor!

He makes a research methods class as enjoyable as it possibly can be - and I did like it! Go to class, you will never know when he's going to take attendance or give extra points for just being there. I barely ever read the textbook. Take notes on things he says that are not on the slides, as they will benefit you in the class. He's amazing.

Spencer is WONDERFUL. I have never had a teacher so genuinely concerned about his students' success--He's so willing to help you! He is so straightforward and relateable, and he's someone you can trust. I am not interested in research, but Spencer made me actually care about it! He's really funny, and it's worth going to lecture.

Prof. James was the most disappointing teacher I have ever had at BYU. He was completely unwilling to accept responsibility for his class. In addition, the test was a horrible representation of what we were learning in the class-- which wasn't much. The tests are the majority of your grade and he doesn't do anything to prepare you. He's the worst.

Spencer is a great person and a great professor. The class is pretty tough, and you need a 95% to get an A. He breaks down the large research paper into smaller parts, so it is a little more doable. Overall, I think he is the best professor to take the course from, but just remember that it'll be a lot of work! Good luck. :)

I felt that the professor did not explain concepts and terminology very clearly. Directions for papers and terminology was not explained very well for exams and papers.  I would not recommend taking this class from him. Poorly taught in my opinion. That being said, he seemed like a nice guy. Just not the best teacher. At all.

The midterm and final don't really measure what you learn in class. They are worth a ton of your grade and you don't really know what he is expecting from you. Don't take this class if you have ANY other choice...

Obviously research methods isn't going to be a huge party, but Dr. James kept the class fairly interesting. He's fairly new and is a super nice guy who likes working with students. I never used the book - just go to class and take notes on explanations of the stuff on his slides and you'll do fine!

Dr. James is great! He always says you can come to him with any question or concern- he means it. The material itself isn't always that interesting, but he tries to make it fun. He has a fun sense of humor and likes people to have fun and comment in his class! He is very personable too, and tries to learn peoples names. Great professor!!

super chill dude. he even asks you to call him by his first name!I def. got a better grade than i deserved. he's very helpful, he wants you to go talk to him if you have questions. i had to miss class a few times due to illness, but i never fell behind.

I think he is a newer professor, I had never heard of him before. He is a very nice and caring guy! I really hate the topic,it's of no interest to me but he is so nice and the class isn't too demanding. I switched out of Dr Draper for 290 because it was too much,but Prof. J is awesome. We had take home tests, and assignments due once in a while.

Class was one three hour lecture a week, but it never felt boring. Professor McBride is genuinely great and keeps you entertained while giving you a lot of information. You can tell he really cares about what he does and is great at it.

Prof. McBride has been one of the best professors I've had at BYU. His lectures are highly engaging, even for a 2.5-hour class. Homework is limited, so exams are weighted heavily, but his study guides are straightforward, and he reviews test questions in class. If you're willing to make the commute to SLC, this class is 100% worth it.

Prof. McBride is THE BEST professor I've ever had. His lectures are so engaging and you can tell he's interested in the topics he teaches. I'm not a history person but he made me love history. His class is so entertaining and I've learned so much in the class. He teaches in Salt Lake but it is SO worth it. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

This class is 1000% worth the commute up to Salt Lake. Professor McBride is passionate about history and he passes it on to the class. His lectures are amazing and I learned so much. The tests are a little difficult...the midterm took quite a few hours to study for. He does provide a study guide though. The reading assignments are super easy.

This man is the GOAT!!!! If you are having a tough time deciding what general to take make sure and take this one! He is the best! He is actually a professor who cares what he teaches. He actually admits when he does not know the answer to a question. Best teacher ever! I hope God protects him wherever he goes!

Professor McBride is an actual legend. I enjoyed the structure of his class and yes, it is a very mellow class with assignments, lectures, and exams. But he really exudes his own personality and passion into some of the lectures and presentations he gives. I originally taking a class for HIST 202 on BYU's campus but switched to the SLC and WORTH.

If I could glaze this man I would. He is the best! I wish more professors were like him. 2 exams and 4 short essay responses. Grades them super fair. His class isn't easy but is not hard either. This class is the definition of in between. He gives the right amount of work for a 3 credit class. Don't skip out on this class! TAKE THIS ONE!! :)

One of my favorite history classes at BYU—even worth the drive to Salt Lake. It is very lecture heavy but super engaging, so paying attention and taking notes is easy. There are 2 BIG tests but the study guides are clear. 4 papers, graded fairly. Highly recommend—just show up, stay focused, and you'll do great. Prof Mcbride is the BEST!!

Professor McBride is amazing! There are 4 assignments in the class and 2 tests, which are easy if you study. He is very kind and a great lecturer, he made the almost 3-hour class a breeze. It is worth the drive or train ride. Easy general, interesting class, and an amazing professor. Take this class!!

This guy is a legend. Love his classes. One note: his tests are kinda tough! Lots of response/short answers/essay q's, so know your stuff. If you actually study you'll be okay, but it'd be wise to invest some time into preparing for the midterms/final. Hardly any assignments, pretty light courseload. Great dude. Worth the drive/train ride.

Bro Mcbride is the GOAT!! He is one of the best professors I've ever had. It was definitely worth the commute up to Salt Lake once a week. His lectures were actually pretty entertaining and I feel like I learned a lot. There are 4 short essays throughout the year and 2 tests which he gets you more than prepared for. Take HIST 202 from this man!

This class was probably the easiest general I've taken at BYU. The professor was passionate about what he taught and made lessons interesting. Almost no homework all semester. He gave 4 short essays, a midterm and a final and pretty much told you exactly what would be on the tests. Highly recommended.

One of the best people at BYU. Passionate about the material and genuinely cares about his students. I am SO glad I took the class from him, even having to commute to SLC. Worth it, no doubt. He loves discussions and learning things so you feel totally safe in contributing. 4 short essays, a midterm, and a final. He gives you everything you need!

I want to take every history class from Professor McBride! I loved every single one of his lectures and you can tell he cares about his students. There isn't hardly any homework and the tests are very doable. If you go to class and listen you will definitely get a good grade.

Professor McBride is one of my favorite teachers I have ever had at BYU. There were only six assignments the entire semester, four short papers, a midterm, and a final. Make sure you do them well because everything is worth a large % of your grade. I was excited for class every week. He is relatable, engaging, and incredible at teaching material.

Best GE class I have taken at BYU yet. His lectures are great and engaging. Usually lets you out early too. The class before the test he reviews with you the info that'll be tested. Although attendance isn't required, going is import. Overall, amazing class and relatively easy.

By far the best class I took from BYU. He is one of those people that makes you excited for class + makes you want to put your phone away. He understands college and how heavy assigments are, so we are graded on 4 short papers, participation, a midterm + final. If you pay attention in class and take notes, there is no reason you won't succeed.

Professor McBride is such an amazing teacher! His course consists of 4 papers and 2 tests, but the papers are so easy and are based on a short supplemental reading. This was the easiest history class I've ever taken, but I still learned a lot from it.

I thoroughly enjoyed taking professor McBride's history class. You can tell that he is passionate about what he does and he makes the information interesting to learn. He wants his students to be successful and is very clear about assignments and grading right from the start. One of my favorite professors I've ever had.

This guy is the freakin best!! Take Civ 2 from him! He makes sure you are super prepared for the tests and teaches you all you need to know to succeed. Just make sure to do the readings that he assigns and you'll do great. He's way nice and is really helpful. His lectures are interesting and full of lots of info so you won't wanna miss class.

This class is mostly discussion based. You'll get a good grade if you show up and do the assignments. I took it when it was co-taught with Erin Whiting and they taught every other class. They are both passionate about what they teach.

This was a super easy class with very limited assignments. Spence was super caring and accessible outside of class. He also left helpful feedback on each assignment, which you can turn in more than once if you are on time. Attendance is super important, but each lesson is interesting for future teachers.

A great class! He's a very caring professor and the assignments are easy and the lectures feel useful! Take from him!
Spence is seriously the nicest guy and this class was a breezes! I enjoyed learning from him and enjoyed this class. He is very respectful of all opinions and kind to all.

Professor Christensen knows what she's doin'. She is very helpful and wants you to succeed. Her lectures are always very informative and interesting. Overall, she's a great professor!

Professor Christensen is a great professor. She cares about her students and is willing to adjust the class to their need. The organization of the class can be a little bit confusing and there are lots of papers and quizzes, but they all help you learn.

Demanding Korean class. Put the time in daily to review and study. The quizzes were particularly difficult, but Professor Christensen helps you and wants you to succeed. She does a midterm course evaluation that readjusts the course based on the class' ability. The final was a group project. I learned so much from this class and recommend it.
Shes nice, I don't feel like she really taught us. It was all online and then labs in person. Such a fun class though!!

Stacey is the best!! I actually took SFL-110 from her instead of the sewing class. It was a blended course, which I highly recommend. All the book stuff is online, and you get to go to the lab to make the food. TAs/ your lab group can make or break it, so hopefully you get good ones. I actually feel confident in the kitchen now.

Stacey is one of my favorite professors. She is super sweet, and very genuine. She is good at being your friend, while keep a level of respect. The sewing class itself was easier for me, as I have sewn a bit before. Make sure to take advantage of lab hours, or you will fall behind. This was an online canvas class, with labs in person. Plz take it!!

I took SFL 110 w/ Mrs. Stacey. 
This was such an awesome class although there is A LOT of textbook readings to complete each week. Labs were super engaging and I was able to meet so many awesome people through them! I highly recommend taking this class from Mrs. Stacey! She is super caring and really easy to reach.

Overall, Stacey was super nice. However, this class is almost entirely graded and run by the TAs, which is a different story. For an introductory class, it's bad. The projects you make aren't super hard, but the TAs are nitpicky and grade each portion of the projects as if they are grading open heart surgery. Don't take this for fun!

I loved taking this class! The projects are super fun/cute, but there's a few quizzes. There are always videos and helpful TA's to help you if you have questions on the projects, and you can go at your own pace as long as the project is done before the due date. A lot of time spent working outside of class will be required, but this class was fun!

Stacey is so nice! This class is really easy and fun. I have sewn before so I knew a lot of the basics. There are a few unit quizzes and a midterm (which is just the previous answers from the quizzes) the final was to sew something and was really simple. This class does require a lot of time in lab to finish projects, but I would just stay longer.
She's smart and excited about chem. But there's not enough time for her to say all that she wants to say. So identify what's important and what's not. Exams had partial credit.

Chem 105 is by far the hardest class I've taken and I had a hard time doing well even with prioritizing the class but Dr. Smith is an awesome professor and provides lots of resources to succeed. Make sure to study far in advance for the exams. Use practice problems!

If you have to take Chem 105 take it from Dr. Smith! It's a really hard class but doable if you stay on top of the work. I got really sick at one point of the semester and she was very accommodating and helped me get back on my feet. I left her office hours once feeling so hopeful because you can tell she really wants you to succeed.

Explained the content quite well and honestly the best of all the chem professors as far as I can tell. Only thing: beware of the little things. I would have gotten an A if there weren't smaller things not discussed as much in class that appeared on the test. This class is mega-hard, so those few points really matter. Stay focused and consistent!

I LOVED this class. She assigns a lot of homework, but I didn't mind because if you put your all into the homework, you shouldn't need to study much. She does experiments very regularly, usually blowing things up, so don't sit in the front row if you're sensitive to heat :) tests straight-forward, and resources there if you need them.

I LOVE Professor Smith!!  Dr. Smith's lectures are so engaging that it made me actually interested in chemistry!! She obviously cares about all of her students. She made an effort to learn everyone's name in our 200 person class. She is also very good at explaining difficult concepts (her lectures make so much more sense than the textbook!)

Ok first thing first. Chem 105 is just the worst, extremely difficult. That is not Professor Smith's fault though, that is BYU's fault for making this a tough weeder class. Professor Smith herself is extremely kind and knowledgeable. She absolutely deserves the good reviews.

Dr. Smith deserves every good review about her here. Probably the best teacher I've ever had. She has built CHEM 105 in the best way in my opinion. Don't be worried about all the reviews saying CHEM 105 is super hard, if you go to class and do the work you'll have zero issues, especially from Dr. Smith.

This class was crazy difficult and I definitely struggled a lot but aside from grades Professor Smith helped me gain an actual appreciation for chemistry and what I was learning. She is also incredibly helpful and a great teacher. You can tell she truly cares about us. Take chem 105 from her!

Her lectures struggled with poor time management- precious minutes got eaten up with inspirational quotes and lengthy explanations, which made her rush through harder material near the end. Teaches well, just needs to manage time better. The practice problems and practice tests had frequent errors or discrepancies which made things more confusing.

I highly recommend taking this class from Dr. Smith. Chem 105 is a tough class with lots of homework. However, I felt like Dr. Smith was really good at explaining all the concepts and she prepares you well. If you put the work into the class you will be okay.

Lectures are super engaging and there are lots of TA's accessible outside of class. She's great at answering questions in lecture. She will replace all your lowest midterm scores with your final test grade if you score higher on it! This class is online homework heavy so you should plan to spend about 6 hours a week on homework.

Dr. Smith is a truely amazing lecturer! Chem 105 is a VERY hard class but she helps us through it as much as possible. The tools to success are present in this class. Follow her schedule! tests are 15% each (3 midterms) and 1 final (25%). All other assignments are worth about .2 %. Lots of homework and you NEED to stay on top of it!

Dr. Smith is the best professor to take Chem 105 from. Be forewarned that there are pre-semester (extra credit) assignments. However, the built-in labs are super easy. The rest of the class...is hard. I ended up withdrawing end of semester, but I am grateful I initially learned the content from Dr. Smith---who teaches it very well.

Dang, this is a hard class. I'm astounded at the amount of freshmen that take this class. Probably around 5-6 hours of homework a week. The tests are hard, but professor Smith is the best one. She is really kind and is great at explaining things. The TAs are also pretty good. I feel like the textbook isn't very helpful though, I would opt out.

Professor Smith is the best teacher to take CHEM 105. Beware, this class will be hard no matter what, but she makes the tests, so take it from her. She is a great lecturer and is willing to help. Follow her plan on doing the homework, or else you will get overwhelmed. Be prepared for the tests to be hard. Trust, just take it from her.

Course designed to fail you. Lectures are like being in kindergarten then the homeworks are like solving the Rieman Hypothesis with an abacus. Attending was complete time waste, but attendance is mandatory so I went anyways. That said, Dr. Smith is the most manageable 105 professor. Anything subjective or inconclusive can be expected on the exam.

Dr. Smith is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about chemistry. She always strives to make sure really abstract chem concepts are explained clearly and often accompanies lessons with an object lesson. Dr. Smith is extremely organized and always makes it clear what she expects from the students and outlines the course to help people excel.

Really good teacher, jokes, teaches, and has spiritual connections. Class is tough, but if you stay up on homeworks (you have an assignment a day pretty much) and do textbook readings you can pass this class. Exams are fair but subjective and harder than previous mat. Need to be in class for Iclicker questions. Some opportunity to fix past grades.

Chem 105 is a very difficult class, it's a weed out class and that's that. Dr. Smith is the best and only professor that you should take it from. Her students generally are scoring 5% higher per test, and the fact that she cares so much about her students, combined with her genius, really make a difficult experience manageable.

Get ready to lock in! CHEM 105 is a run for your money. Take it from Dr. Smith!!! Her classes always get the highest scores on the exams. Those exams are brutal, make sure you do the practice exams. Homework is never-ending, even on Saturdays. I will not miss this class, but I will miss Dr. Smith and the balloons she likes to explode every week lol

Best professor I have ever taken a class from. Lots of material, but if you put in the small amount of effort required to keep up with it, exams will be easy. Dr. Smith writes all chem 105 exams, and her class average on each exam is typically higher than the other professors'. STUDY HER SLIDES and you will be fine

If you have to take Chem 105, Prof. Smith is the way to go. This class is going to be hard, theres no way out of that, but with Smith you get the best shot at success. She redid the entire course to better prepare you for test and you can tell she really cares about students. There's a lot of homework, but if you stay with it the class is doable.

She introduces a schedule for studying that will benefit you in all of your future classes. Her expectations are very clear. The TA lab is very helpful. She teaches these hard concepts the best of all 105 professors. She wrote the exams used by the whole department. Her average class score is generally 5-10% above the other Chem 105 classes.

Dr. Smith is the best professor I have ever had. The class is still difficult but she brings so much to the table in terms of her ability to explain advanced concepts simply. If you can take her class I would.

She is a great professor. The class is fast-paced and it is necessary to put in the work - the heavy amount of homework is a huge blessing to be able to master the content to keep up with the pace she has to go. Go to her office hours and she will help you with anything. Great professor.

CHEM 105 is a tough class, but take it from Doctor Smith. She's the one who writes the tests and will better prepare you for them. Three midterms, a final, pre-class reading, and two assignments for every class period. If you're willing to work hard, an A is achievable. Make sure you show up to class.

Not nice at all for people that like to take their time and get a good understanding at least for those that are beginners in chemistry like me. More difficult than differential equations which I got a B in. Not any less difficult than all the other science/math classes I've taken. Lectures gave me headaches and I never get headaches.

Dr. Smith is so smart and helps everyone succeed. Obviously Chem 105 is difficult, but she made it 100% manageable. Her lectures corresponded with homework that was actually helpful and not busy work, and the homework corresponded with tests. All expectations were clear. Go to class, do your homework, and you'll pass.

I definitely recommend Dr. Smith. She writes the tests that all of the classes use so she is very knowledgable on what you need to know. She was always enthusiastic during lectures and really loves chemistry. This class is not easy, but if you do all the problem sets and Smartworks, you will know exactly what to expect on the tests.

I see why some like her, but she came across as condescending and rude to me. When I asked questions during office hours, she acted like I should already know the answers. While I liked the class concept, she wasted time reading inspirational quotes at the start and then rushed through lectures, which was frustrating as a student.

Dr. Smith was an amazing teacher. The class was hard but if you read, attend the lectures, do the problem sets and smart works, you can get an A in the class. You can tell that Dr. Smith really cares about her students. She loves chemistry and tries her best to make the lectures fun and engaging.

The coursework will live up to your expectations: 3 problem sets, 3 online Smartwork problem sets, 1 exploratory lab weekly. Mandatory lecture & recitation attendance—but just by doing the homework, you WILL be prepared for your exams if you take the time to understand it!

Would recommend using YouTube videos rather than textbook in most cases.

I think Dr. Smith is the best professor to take chem 105 from. She was really good at explaining difficult concepts in a way I could understand, and as long as you do the homework it's not too difficult to pass the tests. Don't bother buying the textbook, I only used it like 3 times the entire semester.

105 is a hard class with a lot of content. Dr. Smith's lectures are always beneficial and even though there is a lot of homework, it is often graded based on completion and really helps you apply the material and prep for tests. Tests are the majority of your grade, but review her slides, understand homework problems and you will be good.

This was a hard and time-consuming class. However, the format is setup that if followed sets you up for success. Do all the work and spend time in the TA lab and this is the best teacher for Chem 105.

Chem 105 is terrible, but if you have to take it take it from Prof Smith. She is super sharp and a great lecturer. Do all the HWs, they're actually quite helpful. Study HARD for tests. She drops one of your midterms if you do better on the final, but don't count on it to save your grade. To this day that final is the hardest test I've EVER taken.
3 midterms and a final exam, lectures are graded based on iclicker quizes, lecture slides are posted after class so it's fine if you miss a lecture.

I ended up not reading the textbook as much since Dr. Smith taught so well! She is kind in the way she talks to the students and really cares about helping them in class as well as in office hours. It's an incredibly difficult class, but if you truly take advantage of all the resources and take the time to study, you'll have all you need to succeed

It was clear Dr. Smith cared about her students and loves chemistry, but this was a very hard class. Be prepared for lots of homework and studying. Weekly labs were easy and usually only took half an hour to complete. Reading the textbook helped prepare you for lectures but I don't think it's a necessity.

Dr. Smith was the best Chem 105 teacher by far. When other students weren't doing well in their classes, they'd sit in on her lectures and start doing much better on their exams. The class is hard but she handles it well, and if you do the assignments and go to the TA reviews you can get a good grade. Her powerpoints are killer, too.

Chem 105 sucks but Dr Smith is the absolute best! She is super fair and genuinely cares about her students. Do all the extra credit! It seems small but helps a lot. Pay attention in class. Get help early on. Most of all, if you want to have any chance getting an A, take this class from Dr Smith! Be prepared for hours of homework every day.

Don't get me wrong, chem 105 is a hard class. However, Dr. Smith is amazing. Go to the TA lab, stay on top of readings and hw assignments. The tests are pretty hard, you got this! Smith had the highest exam averages of the chem teachers. Her specific lectures had an 88 average the year I took it!! Could not recommend Smith enough!

Chem 105 is going to be insane regardless of who you have, but if you have to take it, take it from Dr. Smith. She is incredible and makes the concepts easier to understand and fun. She is one of the most respectful professors I have ever met and really wants all of her students to learn. Her tests are tough but multiple choice which is nice.

If you take other STEM classes, Chem105 isn't nearly as hard as people say. I could tell that Dr. Smtih cares about her students because of how many names she could remember. IMO recitations were a waste of my time and it was frustrating that attendance was required. She shares a bunch of inspirations quotes that frankly I thought were super tacky.

Professor Smith is the way to go for Chem 105! She genuinely cares about her students and is super accessible outside of class. This class can be tough, but as long as you're doing all of the assignments and staying on top of things, its super doable!

No matter who you take it from, CHEM 105 is a beast, but Dr. Smith does a great job teaching it considering how material-heavy the class is. She does a great job of breaking down complicated ideas, but she would have to speed through the end of a lot of lectures because of how much we had to cover.
Such an amazing professor. One of the best for this super hard class. Doesn't matter how much you study, the tests are still a beast, but overall a good class

Dr. Smith is a great professor, and for such a hard class like CHEM 105, she really is the best option. She is very kind and wants us to succeed, but her tests are hard. Make sure you do the readings and you constantly review past material. She also goes fast in lecture too so make sure you're a fast note taker.

This class is a beast. Doesn't matter who you take it from. Dr. Smith is the best option. Very organized, but there is so much material to cover and she'd take too long at the beginning of class then blow through the last third of the material, which usually included the harder concepts. Tests were super hard, study the slides and the problem sets

She's a great teacher. I feel like she really wants us to understand what she is teaching. It's a tough class with lots of information to get down but she is always open to answering questions and getting to know her students. There's problems assigned after each class to help you understand the content which you will get full points if you do it.

Professor Smith was kindhearted but I felt she did not help me prepare for tests. She made tests unnecessarily hard and I felt like she didn't want everyone to succeed. I have never gotten below an A until I took this class and I felt I didn't have resources to help and her lectures were very hurried and rushed. Kind person though. Get a tutor.

This class was really tough. Professor Smith is great but her tests were super hard and worth 70% of your grade. We also never had enough time during lecture to finish learning the material and it felt super rushed. Be prepared for a lot of homework and studying.

The most organized professor I have had so far. Outlined everything in the syllabus in a very clear way. The assignments were used to help learn concepts better. Lectures were jammed packed with information and usually we didn't have enough time for all of the information which was pretty annoying. Very hard class but work hard and it's doable.
Professor Smith was a great professor but the class is very homework heavy. There are a lot of tests throughout the semester but you are very prepared for them if you attend lectures and talk to TAs.

I recommend taking this class with a religion class and two easy going generals (12 credits total) because this class is hard by nature. Don't take it from Dr. Smith if you aren't willing to put in work. Her tests are incredibly difficult so you have to invest tons of time to adequately understand the concepts. I did enjoy Chem 105 a lot, though.

Honestly, Professor Smith was a good professor and I felt like I learned a lot, but her tests were awful. I mean, none of the lectures, problem sets, review sessions, or textbook readings ever prepared me enough for an exam. If you're looking for a fun chem 105 class with a smart professor this is the one, but don't take this if you want a good GPA

Smith is the way to go for CHEM 105. I took the class from a different professor and had to WD, then took Smith and I ended up with an A! Her tests are incredibly difficult but she explains the concepts very well during lecture. I recommend her if you have to take this terrible class.
