Professor Parker is the best option for NDFS 100, hands down.

Professor Parker is one of the nicest people! She cares about her students, and she is passionate about what she teaches. This class is hard for a lot of people; it requires much memorization. She's super nice, but be prepared to utilize the TA's and take lots of good notes!

She is a really great person. And it's probably not her fault but the schools. The class was way harder than it had to be, hard tests and lots of memorization. I did like the projects we were able to do because they were more hands on based. Make sure to take advantage of the TA lab.

Stephanie Parker is so so kind!! She has a strong passion for what she does. She made lectures engaging and interesting!! I learned so much. The tests are hard and are very memorization based, but she prepares you. Get ready to prep for exams a few days before and to memorize a lot of terms. She is the best nutrition professor here!!

She was an amazing teacher who tried SO hard to make the class super fun and interesting. She brought in food for us a few times. I changed my major to nutrition because of this class. Some of the big assignments took a little bit more thought and time but they were still good. Very good and straight forward tests.

She was super duper kind and really cares about all of her students. She knows her stuff and is super humble too. Probably one of the most christlike people I have ever met. Professor Parker is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. She teaches nutrition in a fun and creative way. I looked forward to her class. The tests aren't too hard; as long as you study you'll do fine.

I loved Professor Parker! I took this class online, and she was constantly emailing the students about the plan for the week and reminding us to reach out to her if we had any questions. I loved Professor Parker! She is very sweet and helpful. The tests feel like they are trying to trick you, but its a department wide thing, so study well. Dr. Parker is the most caring teacher I have ever had. Even though there were more than 300 students in my section, we all could feel her love for us individually. Prof Parker is one of the most caring professors I have had. Her lectures are uplifting and she really tries to help you grow as a person. Professor Parker is great, she loves teaching students about nutrition and you can tell she really cares. I would highly recommend taking NDSF 100 from her, if you get the change. I loved how she tied the gospel and nutrition together in a uplifting and educational why.

If you do the textbook reading and canvas activities you are good to go. All you need are the powerpoints from class which you will have available to download. Lots of memorizing so quizlet is your friend but it isn't hard. I would take her again she was super nice and genuinely loves the material.
Amazing Professor that offers great opportunities to learn! The tests were exactly what she taught so no guess work. Do the study guides and its an easy A.

This class is easy to study for because the study guides are clear and if you know the study guide you will do well on the test. Her lectures are great and she had a few inspirational ones where she connects the gospel to nutrition.

Prof. Parker was so great! Once I got the hang of the class I ditched the textbook and got what I needed to know from the lectures and various quizlets when studying for tests. I really enjoyed learning about human nutrition, but this class was so much memorization of things I don't really care to know. It was a general and I felt it was difficult. Prof Parker is so caring and she knows her stuff and cares a lot about it, but her lectures went overtime, there was a lot of unnecessary info in class, and wasn't on the test.

Professor Parker is amazing and really cares about what she is teaching and talking. This was a very difficult class for me and I had to study a lot more and really pay attention in lectures. Dr. Parker is a wonderful professor. I enjoyed her amiable lectures which contains all the information needed for exams. I took this course to fulfill a GE credit ended up loving the course. Learning about nutrition has helped me to make better choices and eat healthier.

She cares a lot about her students. Nutrition can be hard for some, but if you study you will get an A. The only reason I got an A- is because I slacked off on one assignment and didn't study too hard for the second test. Great class.

Professor Parker is the best! She cares about nutrition and helped inspire the students to love nutrition too! Prof. Parker does so much with this online class to help you succeed! Her videos show she cares, and I love how she incorporates gospel topics into nutrition. She's a great teacher; her personality is lively and you can tell she cares about students. One of her best strengths is incorporating the gospel into her lectures, and I felt inspired on multiple occasions. The exams are usually covered pretty well by the study guides.

I love Professor Parker! She is so kind and goes out of her way to answer your questions. You need to be in class to get the notes because her powerpoints are incomplete. If you study the study guide and pay attention you will do great on her tests!!
She loves her job and really goes out of her way to help her students. The tests are not tricky, everything is straight from the study guides.

Prof. Parker is one of the most caring people I have ever met. She didn't just care whether we learned the material; she also cared about whether we became better people from knowing it. I love professor Parker!! You can tell that she's super passionate about nutrition and has a lot of good insights. Professor Parker is great and she definitely has passion for her subject. Her lectures were pretty long but if you go and take good notes the tests aren't bad at all. She is such a caring and she has a powerful testimony.

Professor Reynolds is a bit goofy and likes to talk. Following her lectures was a bit tough, but the class was simple enough review of high school AP bio. The tests were easy. I didn't really read the textbook.

She always brought in the Spirit during class time and helped us understand which concepts were important to know for the midterms, which were not difficult. We had to write a two papers but they weren't difficult. I would take a class from her again.

Sister Sorensen is amazing! The class is extremely easy which is a breath of fresh air for a religion class. Stephanie cares about each of her students and will call you by name and leave comments on each of your tests and assignments. Tests are open book and open note and can be taken on learning suite which is so nice! 100/10 would recommend!

Your grade is mostly based upon doing the readings (which aren't long) and coming to class. She knows a LOT about the apostles and has some great stories to tell. Tests are open-note, but you would be wise to read through the study guide and prepare your essay questions beforehand. Very inspirational and testimony-building experience!

Ok, Sister Sorensen is the greatest. She is real and funny and understands that students have 8 million other things to do. Show up and sit back and relax and talk about the apostles and prophets. It's great! The papers are easy and insightful and the tests are all open note. I would definitely take her class again!

I loved Sister Sorensen! Her lectures were great! Tests are open notes. You are graded on attendance. Each class you have to listen to two talks or read a chapter and a talk and participate in digital dialogue. There are two papers that are fairly simple. If you do the readings, go to class, and participate you will do well in the class.

Sister Sorenson is so passionate. She loves the things she teaches and it is obvious. She works hard to make the class interesting and help us strengthen our testimony. Take home open note open book midterm and final. Two papers in the semester that take a bit of time, but not bad.
She is a really good teacher. There is one take home test in the middle of the semester; that's the only one all semester and its not super hard. She is really great.

She's a great teacher, totally loves what she teaches and helps you love it too, but her test after general conference was crazy. You were expected to remember a bunch of details from extensive readings as well as a bunch of details from general conference just the week before, and once you bomb a test, there isn't much you can do to fix it.

Sister Sorensen is seriously the most amazing teacher. She cares about what she is teaching which makes the class even better. She tells awesome stories that have to do with the Apostles and is hilarious. 10/10 would take this class again.

Sister Sorensen was a great professor. Very organized and on the ball with just about everything. Her class is arranged where performing well is relatively easy but supportive of offering a good spiritual experience as well.  Take her class, best choice for a religion class.

Sister Sorensen is the BEST religion professor I've had! She is SO sweet and cares about her students! Her class is awesome and you get-to-know the apostles on a more personal level! She is VERY passionate about the subject and you can tell she really loves and lives what she teaches! Take this class!! You won't regret it!! Only 2 easy papers!

Alright, most professors are very unorganized.  Sister Sorensen is THE MOST ORGANIZED PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD.  Seriously, she is incredible.  I always understood what was expected of me.  She is an incredible teacher and very passionate about what she does.  I absolutely LOVED this class.  Everyone should take it!

By far my favorite religion professor yet! She made the class SO easy to get an A if you put forth that effort. I gained SUCH an appreciation for the living prophets and their lives and teachings. The class changed my life. Don't take this class from anyone else because you can't get better than Sister Sorensen!

Well, that was a great class! The Living Prophets is great material in general, but Professor Sorensen definitely tries to mix it up a bit. We have a lot more discussions than lectures, and she tries to mix things up every class so we actually spend more time engaging with the other students than falling asleep.

Sister Sorensen is very passionate about the teachings of our living prophets.  I gained a great appreciate for our apostles and prophets! There is about 15 minutes of reading for each class with a simple digital dialog response. There are 2 major essays, also a midterm and a final. Participation is 30% of the overall grade.

Loved this class! Her lectures are to the point and full of a lot of interesting stuff. I found it easy to understand; I aced almost every exam. You get multiple tries for every homework assignment, and she drops a midterm, so it's really easy to get credit. I highly recommend her if you're looking for a low-stress yet informative class!

Sister Reynolds is great, her lectures were very applicable to the quizzes and the exams. She drops your worst exam in the class (out of the 3, not including the final) which really helped me get a good grade. The online quizzes and homework had 3 tries per question and two or three tries if you miss a question, so it's easy to get full credit.

Professor Reynolds is very knowledgeable in biology and she cares for her students. She keeps lectures interesting. However, attendance is required. The tests are brutal. DON'T take if you're not a Stem major. Definitely go to TA sessions for extra help.

Great Professor, I loved her class. You can tell she loves what she teaches and cares a lot about students. Has clear expectations to help you learn the material but is also flexible and works with students to meet them at their level.

TA's are the goat, literally so helpful. Attend the TA reviews! Very lecture heavy, don't take in the evening if you're trying to stay awake. Sister Reynolds is great but could get distracted easily or ramble. The class was fascinating, just make sure you're prepared for the exams. All mc which was nice.

Dr. Reynolds is a fantastic professor and is always willing to go over material if you don't understand. There are lots of opportunities to boost your grade, and extra credit is offered. Do the readings, and the Exam reviews, and you will most likely do very well. TA reviews are VERY useful with some hints on what will be on exams.

Professor Reynolds is a bit goofy and likes to talk. Following her lectures was a bit tough, but the class was simple enough review of high school AP bio. The tests were easy. I didn't really read the textbook.

Great class, great professor! She's easily distracted, but so caring. The TA's are nice and provide more than enough help for any exams. The tests are tough but she drops your lowest score. I would recommend this class to both Bio majors and nonmajors.

I took this class as a non-science major just for a GE and it was so worth it. The class itself was super easy. The TAs were really helpful and outlined everything we needed to know for the tests. Professor Reynolds can get a little off topic in class, but she is super nice and takes time to answer all questions.

Her lectures are pretty all over the place but she sets up the class for you to succeed. She drops the lowest score from you three midterms and lets you know exactly what to study to prepare for them. If you just study for a little bit before tests and go to the TA review then its a pretty easy class.

She was good and a nice person, however, given her rather scatterbrained way of conducting lectures, I learned more from reading the textbook provided than the lectures, or going to class. The tests are challenging but fair, and if you study well you should have no issue. However, the tests are weighted to about 70 percent in this class, so beware.

Sister Reynolds is SO nice and caring, but I would highly recommend not taking this class from her. She is very scattered, and I ended up learning more by teaching myself than being in lecture. She is also impossible to reach by email which was tricky. Two assignments every week & 4 (fairly simple) tests total. Do the reading & go to TA reviews!!

I was orginally going to take this class in person, but the professor was actually terrible. Glad I took it online, there are tons of TA's and easy help. There is 4 midterms and they are hard. If you study hard they are doable, but hard. Overall a pretty good class!

AP bio but easier. She is funny and laidback, but obviously not as professional/knowledgable as most BYU professors. Take this class from her if you want an easy A while taking Chem 105. Take it from Professor Jenkins if you actually wanna learn. TA's tell you what's on the tests. There are two assignments due a week and readings. Tests are fair.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Not enough words to describe how difficult it was. She talks faster than you can take notes and rambles a lot. TA review material is completely irrelevant to the actual exams. You'd be better off just filling out C for every problem than trying to study, because none of it will be on the test. Nice lady, terrible professor.

Professor Reynolds is one of the most caring professors I've had during my time at BYU. She's so enthusiastic about what she teaches.

There is some homework, but it is very manageable. The tests are tough, but if you study it is a pretty easy class to ace.

For both STEM and Non-STEM majors, I would highly recommend this class for a BIO GE over BIO100. I took it my senior year and felt that the class was very straightforward. Tests were fair and hw was not too hard but still great practice. She is nice, posts slides, and focuses on the most important info, although she is a little scatterbrained.

Such a kind and caring professor who genuinely cares about her students. She answered all questions and explained all topics even if we were off schedule. Takes time outside of class to help cover difficult topics

This is a relatively easy class. Reynolds is a good professor and cares about her students. She is knowledgeable about what she's teaching. However, she is scatterbrained sometimes. There were times where we wouldn't get to the actual lecture until halfway through our 50-minute lecture. Study your notes and go to TA reviews and you'll do well.
Reynolds can be a bit scatterbrained sometimes, but she's always so fun and clearly cares about her students. She makes it really easy to do well, as long as you go to class and do your homework.
Super nice lady who cares about her students. Lectures are boring tho. I just watched amoeba sisters and I was fine. Easy A

Professor Reynolds was an amazing teacher for this class! She really cares about the topic, and she always makes sure you are prepared for the test. Sometimes she does go off on rants about other biology topics, but she does get back on track. If you do the homework and understand them, you'll do just fine.

Professor Reynolds really does care about her students and wants to help them receive the grade they deserve. She's willing to go over the test with you and offers extra credit. I took this class Spring 2023.

Lectures were very basic, but the tests asked more complex questions. She was largely going off of another professor's material and tests, but not explaining concepts to the depth we would be expected to know them. She's super nice and wants to help, but tests were brutal if I hadn't done the reading and extra practice assignments and homework.

Professor Reynolds really cares about her students. She is really understanding with grades and does a good job at preparing you for tests. The TA was also a huge help and did great at explaining. Lectures aren't the most interesting but they are easy to understand and she puts only the info you need to know for the test on the powerpoint.

Do the readings before the class!! I've noticed that those who have a general knowledge of the material before coming to lecture do way better on the tests. Professor Reynolds was a very kind and compassionate professor. You can tell that she really enjoys her job as a teacher! Remember to just do the readings, I would have done way better lol.

She was so awesome!! She cares so much about the students and really wants them to succeed! She made the workload very manageable and really tries her best to prepare the class for the exams. I would love to take her class again!

This was her first semester at BYU and honestly I loved coming to her class. Material can be difficult but her awesome TA helped me a ton. Professor Reynolds cares about her students and wants whats best for them. She doesnt curve any tests because her tests dont need to be curved to get a good grade. 10/10 would recommend!

Dr. Beus's lectures were never engaging and I feel like I know little more about piano literature by the end of this semester. He never once called me by name (I don't even think that he knew it) and he was never clear on due dates or assignment expectations. Unfortunately, he is the only professor for this class so you will have to take it.

I adore Stephen! He's got a great fashion sense, comes to work ready to care about students, and he's definitely nice to look at. He's super awkward, but it's kinda cute. He's also really funny and smart, and I've learned a lot from our lessons.
He is my mentor at piano. He gives great feedback and he is amazing tat the piano. Would highly recommend if you are a piano performance major.
Dr. Beus is a wonderful professor! He's really intelligent and has a lot of insights, and he's really attractive as well. His personality and adorable face make me want to go to class every day.

Class wasn't very helpful. He just proved theorem after theorem, despite the tests being very computationally focused. I did lots of practice problems to prepare myself for the test, which were way more helpful than sitting through class.

His teaching style worked very well for me as a math major, though I could tell that sometimes his explanations didn't click so well for engineering students. He is very focused on making sure that students understand definitions and relationships between concepts. The organization of the online assignments and due dates could use some cleaning up.

I enjoyed this class. Professor Humphries teaches well and provides examples. He is quick to respond to emails and helped me get a few grades fixed. His british accent is also entertaining and he's honestly a chill guy.

This class is fairly easy, so I do not know if the professor matters too much. The practice exams given were really helpful for the midterms, but the homework can be a lot especially with all of the proofs. I do not know if I can confidently say what linear algebra is, but I still got an A in the class.

Difficult material to understand. Lectures are not too difficult to understand. Test review is very lacking and did not cover multiple things on each test, hung me out to dry. Online homework turn in does not work sometimes, hard to properly input answers. Tests are most of your grade. Two bouts of homework per lecture. Not super long, but frequent

This is the worst class I have ever taken at BYU, and not because it's difficult; the computations are quite easy. The issue is, I had no idea what the computations were for, nor could I tell you what linear algebra even is. Prof. Humphries likes to read textbook info off of slides, and everyone was pretty confused every lecture.

So what Dr. Humphries likes to do is sort of tee-ball stuff he's teaching in class, so if your class doesn't have someone who fills in the ends of the sentences (it was me in mine) it could be a bit rough? but he's british and funny and it's a good time of a class! you can pretty much teach it to yourself by reading the book, but go anyways!

The pace was way too fast considering how difficult of a course it is. That said, he does his best to answer questions and be fair on the homework. He lets you know what proofs are going to be on the test beforehand which is nice but if you don't have a whole lot of time to memorize them it's a real struggle.

It's a very difficult class. With that in mind, I still had a really tough time learning from him. He gives plenty of examples, but goes way too fast. If you have the time to do the homework and memorize the proofs on the exams you'll do fine but otherwise I would take from someone else.

Before I talk about this class, I should point out that I did not like proofs at all when I did them back in Geometry. However, I loved professor Humphries class. He is an amazing teacher, the book he uses is very good, he assigns reasonable amounts of homework, and he makes sure students understand the material. Highly recommend.

I loved Professor Humphries, and math 372 is my new favorite class. He was funny, gave lucid explanations, and clearly cared about making the class accessible to the students. The tests were mostly memorizing proofs, which was easy if you studied. He was very accommodating when we went online, giving a generous curve and allowing extra credit, too.

The class consisted of "Here's the theorem, here's the proof, and here's an example". He's absolutely brilliant. He will challenge student who ask questions, and that's when class is effective. His best teaching I saw was when he did small test reviews, but in class lecture was less impactful.

I can see why people may have a hard time learning from Dr. Humphries but he is really smart and knows his stuff. He personally held reviews for the midterms which was really nice. If math is a little bit more intuitive for you, he is a good professor. Compared to other linear algebra professors, he usually had better averages. No grade curve.

Math313 is a difficult course unless you're into pure math . Humphries is definitely into pure math. He's kind of a shy guy but throughout the semester he warmed up and was very passionate. The course is standard department-wide. Daily HW (online then written), 3 midterms and a final. Friendly advice: don't relax after you ace the first exam.

Let's admit it, most BYU math profs aren't the best. This class was really hard for me and I did well in all the calc series but the proofs were difficult. Lectures were straight out of the book - didn't learn much. However, he was very reasonable and would gladly help if you approached him outside of class. Advice: go to the math reviews!

Took Cal 2 from him and I felt I didn't get anything from him. I was able to go to the math lab and learn all these concepts from Kahn Academy instead of going to class. I highly recommend not to take cal 2 from him.

In class he basically just writes the practice problems from the textbook up on the board, so I often found myself asking why I was there. He didn't really answer questions in class, so if you think you need help with calculus, I would take a different professor. But, my TA was awesome, and there are 2 classes a week taught by a TA, so it works out

Professor Humphries is, in my opinion, not able to teach clearly nor concisely. We spent every class lecture going through examples. There was no period where he explained what he was doing. He copies the examples out of the textbook and is not good at answering questions. 3 extremely hard exams and a crazy final. Go to the math lab for help.

This class is definitely difficult, but it's doable. Humphries is an interesting guy. He plays math videos before class starts and sometimes a hint of humor will show through during lecture. I think the hardest thing is that he's really smart, so he sometimes had trouble dumbing it down a bit.

There are better professors out there, look around. Doesn't post content on learning suite, very hard to follow the schedule. Isn't aware of what is due when or what he needs to teach in order for you to finish the homework assignments.

For a math teacher he does an alright job. Lectures consist of the examples that are already in the textbook, in other words class attendance isn't necessary, yet helpful.  No pop quizzes. 3 VERY hard tests once a month and then the final. He will answer your questions in class, but a lot of times the TA's will just teach us the material. Daily HW.

Dr. Humphries is clearly very intelligent and knows a lot about what he is teaching, but I found following him in class to be very difficult. He tends to skim over explanations of concepts and instead does examples on the board all lecture. This was confusing even for me, and I've technically already taken Calculus 2 in high school!

He  tries to connect to the students, but he is kind of a oddball. He gives you midterm reviews which have VERY high fidelity on the actual exams. Study and memorize them and you'll do fine on the tests. Sometimes he is a bit fuzzy on explanations. Also class is important bc he gives you the HW assignment and all the notes on the proofs.

Dr Humphries is a very patient, serious professor.  He goes very fast in lecture but is also willing to help those who aren't math geniuses.  His exams are VERY similar to the reviews he gives with a few minor changes.  The tips to passing the class that were given on the syllabus were really much more useful than I thought.  DO THEM!

Professor Humphries is the best! The homework isn't too bad, and the class actually gets easier as the semester goes on. Lectures are fine, and the accent helps to keep attention. He makes the lectures fun. Sometimes he doesn't explain super well, but he is happy to re-explain more clearly. Memorize the practice tests and passing should be easy.

This class is much more challenging than 112. It's doable, but be prepared to go to the math lab. He's not a bad teacher, but he's a little scatterbrained and will often make little mistakes on the board, like dropping a negative, which can be confusing. A lot of the time, our homework is more proof-based than stuff we'll actually be tested on.

I liked math before I took this class. Dr. Humphries was hard to understand and didn't know some of the material and was constantly making mistakes. He rudely told people to work out the problem in their own time when students asked questions. His test were extremely hard, and I felt like sometimes he didn't teach what was needed for the homework.

His tests are in my opinion very difficult. For his proofs on the test he basically expects you to memorize them verbatim from the book, but he is very nice and willing to explain things over again. Also, he is fun to listen to because he has an awesome English accent.

Very smart, very willing to help. Lots of material that seems hard at first, but gets a lot easier. Just make sure to memorize proofs. Tests are very similar to practice tests, so make sure you know the proofs.

Humphries is great, he takes concepts you can understand to show new concepts that are more difficult. Very witty and approachable. Just ask alot of questions in class and you'll be fine. Definitely recommend him!

Professor Humpheries is amazing! He teaches very clearly and concisely. He is very funny and very witty. His lectures and his textbook are incredibly easy to follow. He is very approachable and will answer questions in class. Just do the hw, memorize the important proofs and do the practice exam for each test, and passing this class should be easy.

Humphries is Amazing! Not only does he follow the textbook and cover everything you need for the exams but he is always willing to clarify or answer questions in class as well as office hours. Get involved in class; he makes it fun and is extremely witty. Super smart teacher, just hard material. Do the practice exams and MEMORIZE the proofs!
Lots of fun, always tells jokes, but teaches clearly at the same time

He's so funny. He goes very fast but is more than willing to help, especially during office hours. It takes a while to get used to his humor and speed, but he is VERY intelligent. Sometimes we don't get it, but be very specific with your questions and you'll probably be fine

Great Instructor. Despite teaching some of the more complex math courses at BYU, he covers all the material. This makes his classes hard, but prepare students for all the other math classes. Very available for help. If you find his classes to hard, read the material, do the work, and let him know about the problems you are struggling with.

I was very dissappointed with Stephen Humphries.He goes very very fast in class and makes it very difficult for students to ask questions in class.At times he would get annoyed with students asking questions.I went in for help several times and he became very irritated with me that I didn't understand his explanation.Not recommended for Math 190.

Once you get used to his lecturing style, the class is fairly straighforward.  He tells you exactly what you need to know and will go over homework problems we didn't get and he finishes every proof that he puts on the board.  You can do well if you just study what he tells you to.  Also has a great sense of humor if you listen carefully.
One of my favorite professors ever!

I really enjoyed this class. It is hard, but he writes out all the proofs he expects you to know  (sometimes several times), and he will actually explain any homework problem that you ask about thoroughly, and he'll give you a list of proofs and things you should know before every test, so if you study you can do well.

After you get accustomed to his style of teaching his class becomes a lot easier.  He is very willing to help students.  We were able to pull him out of his office and had him teach us for two hours right before the final which was very helpful.  He writes out every proof he expects you to know.  Take good notes in class and you do just fine.
He teaches at a supersonic speed, and it is obvious that few can follow what he says.  His responses to questions are useless.
He taught us a lot, but his class is extremely hard. I think there was only one class we did not get homework. His tests are even worse.

Dr. Jones's lectures are fantastic. He teaches so well. It's a God-given gift and he really knows how to break down complex concepts into easy-to-learn steps. The homework isn't too bad, and his tests are honestly a collection of the easiest problems from the homework - no surprises or guess-what-I'm-thinking tests. 100% would recommend to a friend

Dr. Jones is a great calculus professor. He can explain the topic clearly while making sure to answer students questions. Attending lectures is a must, as there are quizzes at the start of every class about the contents of the last lecture, but they aren't difficult or meant to trip you up. The homework from the textbook can be very tricky.

If you are taking math 113, take it from Dr. Jones at all costs! He has a gift for explaining calculus. Because of lectures, I never had any subject that was difficult to understand. He is super nice and has great reviews. His TAs run the lab days, and they generally did a great job as well.

Dr. Jones is by far the best math teacher I have ever had. His class is very organized and his lectures are clear and concise. He genuinely cares for the success of each student in understanding the material covered in class. He makes all his students feel important.

My favorite Math teacher of all time!  He was very clear, gave tons of examples in class and helped me feel prepared for every homework assignment and test.  There were clicker quizzes at the beginning of every class, but they're not hard.  If I found out he was teaching another class I needed, I WOULD DEFINITELY PICK HIM AGAIN!
Very nice guy, but kind of boring.  He likes to laugh at himself.  Take this class at a time of day that you'll be awake.  Do good on the tests and you'll do good in the class.
Brother Jones is very helpful and he's a very creative teacher.  I would highly recommand anyone to take his class.

I love Dr. Jones because he doesn't just teach you the physics.  He always has interesting tangents (eg. into quantum physics, relativity, and religion) and I find myself with a much greater love for physics.  He's one of my most influential teachers.  Highly recomended.

I thought he was pretty funny. His classes were fun to go to, and there were a lot of opportunities to learn things. I thought the tests were hard, and the homework took a lot of time. If you haven't taken physics in high school, be sure to read all the assigned chapters. The book helped a lot.

He's the nicest guy around, though true to Physics Department guidelines, he spends much of classtime going through derivations, which I find to be mostly unhelpful for lower level physics students.  He's exceptionally lenient about assignments and grades, and is willing to help struggling students.  I recommend him.

Refreshingly frank and open, his straightforward intellectual honesty and rigorous methodological attitude and enthusiasm for the material combine to raise even lowly introductory material to the highest levels of interest.  His approachability and calm energy makes him a superlative instructor.
This guy is da bomb

Prof. Jones is a really awesome teacher, he really cares for the students, and asks for feedback at times to see what he can do better.  He is also very helpful, and is there to help his students, and not try to trick them.  The semester I took the class though he did not write the tests, Prof. Clark did, and they were pretty hard.  Take this class
His classes are entertaining and interesting.  I enjoyed the lectures- they also help a lot during test time.  Pay attention in class and you'll do fine.
I thought Prof. Jones did a great job with the lectures and the organization of the class.  He was very helpful for those who needed a little extra help.
He is a really, really nice guy. I just didn't find him to be a good teacher at all.
The model of what a BYU professor should be. Combines Academic learning with insightful spiritual learning. Be prepared for a hard class but a truly unique and good professor.

pro: VERY lenient with assignments, usually willing to change your grades on tests or labs if you come to him after class...nice, amiable guy. con: he isnt the one who writes the tests, so they're usually tough for you, his class is kinda boring, VERY eccentric and giggles to himself a lot.

Prof. Jones is an interesting teacher to say the least.  His class was fun, but not the best.  I'm biased when it comes to ease, because I took AP Physics C in HS, and it was ten times harder than Bro. Jones' class.  He gets off on the most random tangents ever, so class wasn't always helpful.

Class was entertaining. The first test gives the class a false sense of ease, since the other two exams are much harder. The curve is generous and it is very difficult to fail the course if you do the work.  On most levels it is as difficult as a high school senior physics class, especially at first

He is a really nice guy but he is not a great teacher. He tells really stupid jokes which get the nerds rolling but I just slept through the class. I didn't learn very much and didn't work very hard but got an A anyway. High School Physics was more difficult.

Very nice guy doesn't equal very great teacher.  The homework and lectures did very little to prepare for the tests.  He offers lots of oppurtunties to raise your grade. The curve is very helpful.  I think I left the class knowing less then when I started.
I liked his class. Homework is great for understanding, but tests are usually much harder. Paying attention in class helps a ton. Fun class and enthusiastic teaching.

Really good teacher.  A little excentric at times, but it keeps you awake and paying attention.  Really enjoys his job and is leanient with students (turning in things late) to help them get things done.  Do the work and ask questions and you'll be fine.

hw is a big deal, takes forever, just get it done and get it all right.  huge curve a is 80 -100.  labs can be any day of week.  not good prep for tests.  unless you totally understand all the hw and can do it yourself, you'll probably get a b, not bad
This guy is a really good guy, but he is not a very good teacher. Every test I found myself saying, "what is going on!?"  His ability to teach clearly is non-existent.
I really enjoyed his class.  Homework counts a lot, and if you make sure it's right, then you'll be fine.  Gives you homework helps and daily notes.  Good class.  I liked it.
Is extreamly flexible with students when it comes to turning in assignments.  He gives you his lecture notes at the start of class so you don't have to write anything down.

Great guy, but I fell asleep often in the early lectures. Unlike other professors, allows labs to be completed any day of the week. Make sure you have had calculus before. Cool demonstrations. When I took the class, grading scale was: 80%+ = A, 60%+ = B..
worse than Allred!

Professor Moody is a fantastic professor. So approachable, helpful, and inspirational. This class has work to do, but he has it all scheduled out so well that I never felt like the workload was ridiculous. I felt like I grew in love with Japan and gained a much deeper understanding of Japan after this class.

This class had a better structure than 301 with meeting in person only 3 times a week rather than every day, but the FACT class didn't feel as meaningful because grammar was pushed aside to focus on talking about cultural, so new grammar didn't stick for me. He is incredibly passionate while talking about the culture though, so it was cool.

Econ is a difficult class, but he tries his hardest to ensure each student succeeds. It is worth driving up to Salt Lake for. He is very fair and great at explaining hard concepts. The class I took was once a week for two and a half hours, but it didn't feel too long because of the fun videos and the way he teaches.

I'd heard all the horror stories of Econ 110 and was prepped to have my butt kicked, but Prof Moody made econ fairly easy to understand. Make time to thoroughly read the chapter prior to coming to class, but if you can stay on top of the reading, he'll do a lot to make it make sense for you. Exams are also pretty similar to practice tests! 10/10

Taking Econ with Professor Moody in Salt Lake was amazing. He's a phenomenal teacher and explains things very clearly. Econ can be very difficult to understand, and hard to pick up the concepts, but he helps you every step of the way. The class was difficult, but extremely manageable due to his clear teaching style

Steve Moody is the most wholesome guy. 100% worth going to SLC to take Econ with him. Class requirements are clear, and he doesn't make you do busy work. Lectures are SO helpful, so don't miss class. Econ 110 is difficult and requires a lot of work but he made it manageable and even enjoyable. I would major in Econ if he could teach all my classes!

Steve Moody deserves the entire world. I drove to SLC once a week and sat in his class for 2.5 hours without complaint. He is funny, really genuinely cares about his students, and understands the course material really well. He responds well to questions even if they're dumb and explains difficult concepts beautifully. Very responsive thru email

Most of this class is online/TA work, so you hardly work with Moody Sensei but he's kind and willing to help if you ask. The class is a lot of work though and you have various assignments everyday that need to be completed so it was hard to get into that routine at first, but once you get the hang of things, you'll do well.

Moody is super organized with the least amount of busy work possible (minus what the department demands). He organizes his content, gives you lots to practice with and answers your questions in class as they come up so you dont feel too far behind. The class is still really hard and it definitely requires work but its better than the other options.

Japan 302 is the hardest class I have ever taken, but it wasn't Moody-sensei's fault. He was always accessible and cared about the success of each of the students. You have to take the class for the major/minor, so there is no way around it. However, Moody-sensei makes the experience good, despite the difficulty of the course. Great guy! Good luck!

Moody sensei is great! He's super nice and super willing to work with his students' needs. The set up for the course is pretty homework heavy, but none of it is too difficult. Overall great class and if you have the option take it from Moody sensei for sure!

Professor Moody is a great teacher. He relates concepts to real life in interesting ways. Exams are hard but fair. He cares about his students and will always answer questions. Since we only met once a week, there was a lot to cover, so make sure to also read the textbook (30-50 pages per week). No TAs, so homework and quizzes are a must to succeed

Overall the class was fine. Professor Moody was extremely good at answering questions and responding to emails quickly. I felt at times like the in class lectures were pointless and that the book teaches the material a little better. Though it requires tons of reading. The grade scale shift at the end if the semester was extremely minimal as well.

I have taken multiple classes from Professor Moody and he has been a very wonderful teacher. He is very concerned about his students and wants them to succeed. He tries to accommodates all students and their needs. He never makes you feel dumb or inadequate as a person no matter what your grade is. I would highly recommend him.

Professor Moody is an incredible teacher. This doesn't mean his class is easy, it's actually the hardest class I've ever taken, but Professor Moody does everything in his power to make it possible. His lectures are helpful and direct, he responds to emails in a very timely manner, and he is always open to questions. If you have to take ECON, Moody.

If professor Moody wasn't a part of the course the course outcomes would not change. You could literally never interact with him and still get 100%. If you love Japanese and want to study it further, find another way, because this class and teacher crushes your soul. This is the class that convinced me not to minor in Japanese.

ECON is a tough Class and Prof Moody makes it doable. The tests are hard, but he doesn't steal your social life like the other teachers. You work for your grade, but it is also fun to learn how the market works. MOODY is the GOAT.

Professor Moody is awesome. Econ 110 is a tough class but, Prof. Moody a great teacher. He has stayed after class with me a few times to help with concepts and answer questions from previous tests. I highly recommend taking the trip up to salt lake.

The class is taught almost entirely by the TA's, but you get one lecture a unit from Prof. Moody. He's really chill and easy to contact, and tried to adjust the class based on what we thought of the homework. Great class, if you show up and do the readings, you'll do fine.

Professor Moody is a very laid back teacher. He'responds to emails quickly and is always willing to go at students' pace during lectures if needed. He's skilled in explaining Japanese grammar as well as Japanese cultural elements

There is a lot of homework, both reading and memorization of kanji and vocabulary. But he and the TAs are very willing to work with you! He really cares about his students and wants to help you succeed. There are 4 midterms and a final, but he thoroughly reviews the material in the class periods leading up to the midterms.

Although a big portion of your grade comes from your performance in class with the TA's, Prof. Moody does a great job preparing you for the written tests by helping you understand the culture and background of the readings. He also narrows down the 200+ kanji covered each section to lists less than half that amount to study for the midterms.

Professor Moody is very versed in what he is teaching, and because of this, he makes it interesting and fun. You will learn a lot from his lectures if you take him. He also understands that what he is teaching is hard, so he is a lenient grader. Just try your best, he understands and is willing to help.

Prof. Moody is a GREAT choice for 110. He cares about his students and you will want to go to his lectures because he is very good at explaining tricky concepts. This is not an easy substitute for 110 at Provo, but it is a very fair and challenging class. His class made me love economics though, so if you have to take 110 take it from him!

Keeps it real with economy. He makes it interesting and is a great lecturer. I would recommend him because he genuinely cares about his students. Econ will be difficult no matter what but I feel like he does his best to help us within the restrictions set by the department
His Japanese 201 really helped me learn Japanese without being overwhelmed. He makes a good job explaining really hard Japanese grammar!

Econ is hard no matter the professor, but Moody does his best to make the class bearable. The tests are really hard, and there is a lot of reading, but the class itself is interesting and Moody really cares about his students. It was nice to be in a smaller econ class where you could have your questions answered in class.

I have heard horror stories about other ECON110 teachers at BYU, & I'm so glad I went to the SLC center to take it from Moody. Although there is a ton of reading every week, Moody does an incredible job at explaining concepts so they're easy to understand. The class is still very hard, but you'll actually do well if you take it from Moody!
I was really impressed by how genuine this professor is; he really seemed to be rooting for all of the class to be successful.

Professor Moody is a nice guy, but this class is full of tangents and not very useful. He is not the most organized, and not particularly helpful when students have questions. He really is willing to try to help though! But, doesn't always seem to know how. He isn't a tough grader, but his tests are hard. (And hard to prepare for - no study guides)

Awesome Teacher! Taking Econ 110 from him in SLC and it was the best decision I made this semester. I actually liked learning economics from him. Competent, unbiased, and even entertaining. The class was academically and intellectually challenging, but not so hard that it kills you. Very fair grader as far as tests and assignments go.

Professor Moody is a fantastic professor. So approachable, helpful, and inspirational. This class has work to do, but he has it all scheduled out so well that I never felt like the workload was ridiculous. I felt like I grew in love with Japan and gained a much deeper understanding of Japan after this class.

This class had a better structure than 301 with meeting in person only 3 times a week rather than every day, but the FACT class didn't feel as meaningful because grammar was pushed aside to focus on talking about cultural, so new grammar didn't stick for me. He is incredibly passionate while talking about the culture though, so it was cool.

Econ is a difficult class, but he tries his hardest to ensure each student succeeds. It is worth driving up to Salt Lake for. He is very fair and great at explaining hard concepts. The class I took was once a week for two and a half hours, but it didn't feel too long because of the fun videos and the way he teaches.

I'd heard all the horror stories of Econ 110 and was prepped to have my butt kicked, but Prof Moody made econ fairly easy to understand. Make time to thoroughly read the chapter prior to coming to class, but if you can stay on top of the reading, he'll do a lot to make it make sense for you. Exams are also pretty similar to practice tests! 10/10

Taking Econ with Professor Moody in Salt Lake was amazing. He's a phenomenal teacher and explains things very clearly. Econ can be very difficult to understand, and hard to pick up the concepts, but he helps you every step of the way. The class was difficult, but extremely manageable due to his clear teaching style

Steve Moody is the most wholesome guy. 100% worth going to SLC to take Econ with him. Class requirements are clear, and he doesn't make you do busy work. Lectures are SO helpful, so don't miss class. Econ 110 is difficult and requires a lot of work but he made it manageable and even enjoyable. I would major in Econ if he could teach all my classes!
