Dr. Piccolo is amazing! I took bio 165, and the class was a bit difficult for me because I have had no experience with code. But it was clear that Dr. Piccolo understood that this was a new skill for a lot of the students, and he did everything he could to help students succeed. He also taught the material in a way that was not overwhelming.

Not a stats class, this is a coding class! Never coded in my life and I fought tooth and nail to do well, so if I can do it anyone can! TAs are CRUCIAL! Literally so helpful, go to office hours and reviews! Makeup exams for full points was incredible. Piccolo is a great guy--wants you to succeed, just didn't love his "point" based grading system.
BIO 264 is a tough class, but him and the TAs help out a lot.

Professor Piccolo  was great. I've never coded  before, but I was able to do well on all the exams thanks to Professor Piccolo, the TAs, and the study guides. And if you don't want to buy  the textbook, it's  at the library.

This is the 2nd class I've taken from Dr. Piccolo. His class had a unique structure; lectures were completed before class, and most of the class was spent actually coding. I found this very helpful and an engaging way to hold class. He knows his subject well and makes it clear what you need to know. I would highly recommend taking 165 before 264.
I LOVE STEVEN PICCOLO! Very understanding. I only got an A- due to personal inabilities to code. If you know your way around the computer you will be fine

I love Dr. Piccolo! He really cares about his students and he does a great job with this course. I did CS 110 before and took CS 111 at the same time as this, and it was pretty easy, but it could be difficult if you don't have any programming experience. He is super good at answering questions and helping students understand difficult concepts.

Great class, I had never coded before but now I feel like a whizz at R. Enjoyed working with partners on problems in class to get some experience. Exams are well structured and fair with a makeup offered if you fail at first. The TAs were wonderful! Plenty of office hours are set up so it'll definitely work with your schedule.

Dr. Piccolo is one of the nicest professors I've had at BYU. The lectures are all prerecorded and class time was all for working on assignments. He and the TA's were great about walking around and helping with any issues anyone had. Class is well paced and plenty of chances to earn back points if you don't do great on the exams.

Dr. Piccolo was a great professor. His lectures made sense and you can tell he knows the information well. He is available to help outside class, as well as his TAs. His tests are code-based and very doable, and you're allowed to bring notes in. Even if you don't do well, he provides several opportunities to earn point back. Great professor

Great teacher, his readings are clear and his lectures are well paced and easily understandable if you are paying attention and willing to do the readings beforehand. He does do quizzes before every class on the readings but they're open note and not too hard. Also he doesn't have hard due dates for homework assignments which is great!!

The professor was good and I enjoyed his class but the grade scale he used was super weird. For quizzes, assignments, and some other coursework you have to get an average of 90% on all of them to get points for any of them. If it weren't for this grading scale he would get a MUCH higher rating.

Class is structured well; emphasis is on learning skills, not memorization. I hadn't programmed before at all, but things were explained clearly enough most (though not all) of the time. Fair grading; not hard to get an A (especially since you can bring a page of notes to the tests). Piccolo cares about his students and about what he teaches. 5/5

Grading was 90% tests, 10% in class quizzes (3 dropped). I got an A through about 6 hours of weekly work, plus 15 hours of study/test with a total of 5 tests. Getting half credit on missed questions on test for completing an essay help. This professor is amazing and caring. He quickly responded to emails and made me feel seen.

Good professor with a great TA while I was in the class. I had prior programming experience, and the class was mostly a breeze for me because of it. His lectures are decent and explain the concepts pretty well. He and the TA are always willing to help out if you don't understand. Weekly programming assignments and 15-30 min readings before class.

Biostats was blended so lectures were online but necessary. They were lengthy but Professor Piccolo is awesome and super helpful. He made many makeup assignments and opportunities for second chances which showed how much he cared. The class is hard though because it's programming and stats which I had no previous experience in.

This class is tough, especially if you don't have any previous coding experience like me. Overall, the practice problems are very similar to test problems. Attend TA office hours if you have questions and you'll do just fine.

Dr. Piccolo is a great choice! He is caring and he knows python inside and out! I had some coding experience , so this class wasn't too bad. But I have heard it is more challenging for those who've never coded before. There is a lot of homework, but it will give you lots of experience and practice for the test (which is most of your grade).

So much homework! So many quizzes, assignments, readings, labs, lectures... I drowned in this class. However, his lectures are clear, as are the exams. The reviews are very helpful, and he really does his best to make biology fun. I'm not the most interested in science, but I definitely have some fun memories from the labs in his class.

He makes you work for your grade, which means tons of homework and quizzes during the semester. 4 midterms in total, and as a final just a book report. He cares about the students by adjusting the course. His lectures are engaging. I would recommend taking this class from him but it's not all easy!
Overall a pretty easy class, he's very understanding of the work load and overall a good teacher.
Really well-structured class. It is easy to understand and Dr. Piccolo is a great teacher and very understanding and helpful.

The man, the myth, the legend. Such a great professor! Funny and approachable. Practice problems were generally reflective of test content. Final was timed and harder than the midterms. Average grade was an A-. SUCH a valuable course if you have no previous coding experience!

This was the first semester the new BIO365 has been taught. Dr. Piccolo did a good job adjusting the course to be most beneficial to us. You learn R and statistical techniques that are beneficial to bioinformatics. I feel much more prepared to take a bioinformatics position. Reading quizzes every day and homework every night were helpful to learn
I took BIO 465 when it was still half lectures/homework, half group project. It was good. It really did take some work--Dr. Piccolo structured things well to make us stretch and learn.

Prof. Piccolo is awesome he is super humble and will let you know if he is not sure about something. If you ask something and he doesn't have the answer he will send out the answer quickly. He really cares about his students.
Good class but he did not teach very well for what you needed to know. A lot of the things on the test were not discussed in class. Probably take from another teacher.

Dr. Piccolo is one of my favorite professors I've ever taken from. He really takes the time to get to know his students and their individual interests. He knows this (BIO 165) is an introductory course into the field, and he is willing to listen to the class (ex. he got rid of one of the tests because we had too many). I'd definitely consider him.

Dr. Piccolo is one of my favorite professors I've had at BYU. He is smart, has well-organized lectures, and cares about student understanding. He provides ample opportunity for hands-on learning and has a well-balanced curriculum that promotes learning without overwhelming students with work. He will respond to emails immediately. Take from him!

Professor Piccolo literally will stop everything he is doing to make sure you understand and get the help you need. As long as you communicate with him, he is so more than willing to help you out. Obviously you need to do the reading and study a bit, but overall, this is a really good class.

Professor Piccolo was great. He really cares about his students, despite his clearly busy schedule (he specializes in Bioinformatics). I missed class a few times and had a few assignments turned in late (due to sickness), and he still gave me full-credit. Read the textbook, do the online hw, and you'll ace every test
He is a really nice person but lectures were often not helpful to the test and there was a lot of busy work.

Dr. Piccolo is one heck of a guy. I'd say from talking to students taking Bio 100 from other professors, he is probably the best professor for that class. He is open to feedback and loves hearing from students. Class is straightforward, but requires effort. Don't miss more than 3 or 4 lectures.

Really cares about what he teaches and helping students learn. He finds videos that are both applicable and interesting for almost every class. He teaches the class knowing that students aren't Bio majors and makes the material fit the audience. The HW assignments to watch videos and answer a few questions were very interesting. Highly recommend!

Dr Piccolo is a fantastic Professor. It is obvious that his first priority is filling the needs of students. He hasn't been teaching Bio for that long so his class still does have a few kinks, but he is unbelievable flexible and willing to make adjustments based on student feedback. The homework and tests are totally manageable.

Dr. Piccolo is a great guy and really cares about his students, but I wasn't a huge fan of this class. He assigns a ridiculous amount of homework and I found myself spending 6-9 hours a week on homework, studying, or reading for this class. The lectures and homework assignments also don't have anything to do with the test. Wouldn't recommend.

This was his first semester teaching BIO100, so there were several kinks, but midway through the semester he asked for our feedback and completely revamped the class. He's open for improvement. Study guides are nonhelpful (he basically provided us with the chapter headings). Review slides and homework for exams. Exams are 85% easy, 15% guesswork.

Good professor. You can tell that he really cares about his students. This was his first time teaching a Bio100 class so there were a few things he didn't remember all that well, but if he didn't know the answer he would go way out of his way to find it for you. I've never passed a bio class before, but I got an A.

Dr. Piccolo basically goes through the book for his lectures, and has the same structure for homework every week. There isn't a ton of variety in his lectures, but he really wants to have his students be successful, and is very responsive to feedback. I would strongly recommend him if you want to do well in this class.

We had no tests in the class. Most of the grade came from a a project you work on over the course of the semester. If you put in the work, you shouldn't have a problem getting an A. Dr. Piccolo cares a lot about his students and will take the time to help you if needed. He is a new professor and listens to student feedback.

He taught the lab portion for 340, and it was so unpleasant. He is a kind guy and clearly very smart, but he does not prepare us well for the labs. The labs don't end up being very complicated, but he doesn't explain what we need to do, and the provided resources are equally confusing. Some organizational overhaul would go a long way.

340 from Dr. Schultz is the most interesting class I've taken at BYU. Tests are actually not weighted that heavily. He uses a very novel teaching approach that is very frustrating at first, because you are expected to figure things out that were never taught in lecture (lot's of wikipedia and stack exchange). But you learn a lot.

I really wanted to like this class. And the professor was funny.

Okay, we're done with the pros. 

Holy cow, the class is a disorganized mess. Very few resources given. His test questions are entirely different than anything you've seen in class assignments or homework. Prepare to lose your 4.0. Labs are decent, thankfully. Projects are... eh.

Pros: focuses on real-life career application. I really appreciated that.
Cons: SUPER disorganized. He once changed requirements for an assignment the day before it was due, and then again 7 hours before it was due. His disorganization means double work for you. Also, he dressed up as Snape for Halloween, which frightened me immensely.

If you liked ECEN 340, you'll probably like 446. It's a hard class and it wasn't my thing, but it was interesting and useful. Dr. Schultz's tests are very difficult, but they account for a relatively small part of your grade which is nice. Most of the grade is in the projects so make sure to work with others to get good grades on those.

The way the class is organized (as a whole) is very merciful, with many chances to correct mistakes and grow. The class organization when it comes to labs and assignments is incredibly frustrating. Many projects and exams had errors, and the labs had to be broken down after the lectures to understand. Not many TAs for lab periods, too.

The class was challenging and sometimes a bit disorganized. The lectures were great and engaging as his humor and comments are hilarious, and uses a lot of in-class activities that are extremely helpful. Learned a lot from him, one of my favorite classes in the major!

Schultz is the most unprofessional and disorganized professor at BYU. He changes assignment instructions *while* we are doing them. Rarely responds to emails. LS is left blank for half the semester. Everything has typos. The amount of time his class has wasted as a result of these things is astronomical. Not to mention he is incapable of teaching

240 lab. My first day, he was standing right by me doing nothing while I soldered and I asked him a question. He told me to go ask the TA so I didn't get in the habit of going to him to ask questions. Nice. The lab slides were super disorganized and hard to follow. The labs took much longer than necessary because they were so disorganized.

Must take Prof. For how much I didn't enjoy the material he taught, he made the class very enjoyable to attend. He'd make mistakes working on the class activities in front of the class. This also meant you had lots of examples of how to do the homework. I basically lived in his office hours and he was very helpful to all of the students there.

He was the lab professor for spring semester, Mazzeo was lecture. He's a bit disorganized and lab requirements would change during the week. However he communicated effectively and the labs were not overwhelming. He is a great professor. Trust me this dude is great.

Dr. Schultz's teaching style is kind of haphazard and unclear at first - the textbook exists but is pretty irrelevant. Pay really good attention to the class activities because they show you how to do almost everything you need to know. Overall though, I love the guy because he cares about his students and is real with you.

Nice guy. Cares about pedagogy. Design Exams are timed and they are hard. Class usually consists of working through design problems on the board, but Dr. Schultz often explain it in a haphazard fashion unless you ask clear specific questions, which he does respect and tries to answer well. Very difficult class. Try to break up the Jr. Core!

Dr. Schultz was awesome. Finally an engineering class feels like an engineering class! He makes the design approach very doable, and you leave the class feeling empowered and more prepared to enter the engineering field. Spend the time to learn the material fully, and the class will be very manageable.

Dr. Schultz has been one of my favorite professors at BYU!! His lectures are very useful and prepare you for the homework and the exams. He is a very fair grader--if there is a question that is the majority of the class missed he will throw it out. I will definitely take more classes from Dr. Schultz!!

Dr. Schultz took the notoriously difficult 340 and turned it into a very manageable and interesting class. He is a fantastic teacher and focused 100% on making this the best experience for the students. His lectures were incredibly helpful and there was no fluff. Everything covered in lecture was guaranteed to be on the test. Fantastic professor.

Dr. Schultz is easily one of the best professors I've ever had at BYU. He's a great lecturer (probably because he's done lots of personal study on how students learn best) and he always takes time to explain questions and common pitfalls. He is very committed to each student's success. Do your best in his class and you'll love it.

Very easy class, probably because it's only half a credit, but all the same, Dr. Schultz is a good professor. He teaches clearly and it's just a Pass-Fail class so just do the homework and you'll pass.

This is a very fun class. Prof Schultz has a very comical personality. He answers questions and makes remarks that seem to grab your attention. This course only requires attendance to pass as it is a 0.5 credit class, some small projects too but they are flat out easy

he is a great teacher, explain really well. he is one of my best professor in BYU. test are mediocre. He really likes to help student. if anything is not clear in his class, then go to his office, he will make it crystal clear.

This was the intro to electric and comp engineering freshman seminar class. It was very boring and kept switching between topics it would take days to cover and so I didn't understand it at all to things that everyone knows. Group labs were a hassle to get together.
Great lecturer, did a good job keeping my attention. Very helpful during his office hours.

Dr Schultz is funny and does a good job lecturing.  Sometimes he has a hard time explaining difficult concepts.  He's very helpful in his office.  The class was well organized and the tests were fair.  A lot of homework.

This is a challenging course, but Dr. Schultz has shown a great willingness to do whatever he can in order help the student.  He isn't always able to present the material in the most clear fashion, but is still good.
I took EDLF 411 from him, and he team-taught with Spence Weiler. They were a great duo and kept the class super engaging. Attendance is about 50% of your grade, so just dont miss.
Professor Hilton is very kind and I loved his class. I took him for Law and Ethics EDLF411 and he was so easy going and caring. Attendance is about 50% of your grade so make sure you don't miss.

I did not feel that Sterling was super respectful of his students. I got called out over zoom class a few times for dumb things and it made me not want to participate as much. I think he had good intentions, just an interesting guy.

Dr. Hilton's class was not well organized, and very little in the way of clear expectations. There was no syllabus ready day one, and our grading expectations were completely up to him. I did not learn stats well from him. Highly recommend you take online stats instead. Good person, and kind, just not what I aim for in a professor.
CELL 363 Lab. Easiest 2 credits I've ever taken. 5-min hw outside class & always ended at last an hour early. Never saw professor, TA lead's everything.

Funny guy, he would put funny elements into his powerpoints and how he taught. Besides that tho his lectures could get pretty boring. But, he posts them online and the slides are all you need, no textbook. So honestly very straightforward and chill class as long as you study.
Dr. Sudweeks is awesome. He also has great TAs who prepare you for exams (go to exam reviews). Exams are worth most of your grade so you have to do well on them, but they are very fair.

The class is 80% exams. He teaches the material well but I felt behind the entire semester. Most of the time, the lectures cover material for the next exam before the current exam has even started. The lectures are recorded and do prepare you well for the exam. There are a lot of resources to do well but I just didn't like the class structure
This is the easiest lab of all time. Just show up and you'll do great

Material was very interesting, presented in a straightforward manner (slides). Only graded on exams and some iClicker participation points. I enjoyed the class, a lot of students get A's. Textbook isn't mandatory but it is helpful to solidify some of the more complicated topics.

INCREDIBLE! My experience was interesting lectures about how the body works. He knows so much! The class is 90% exam but that shouldn't scare you. The TAs and his lecture slides prepare you adequately for every exam. No homework or readings. The other 10% is Iclicker. Just overall great!

Professor Sudweeks is SOO smart and knowledgeable. If you want to learn, you will. If you want to just memorize stuff for tests, you will too. No homework, only tests. He records all of his lectures, so I'd definitely utilize those! Watch TA reviews!! (They see the test beforehand and can give specific info). Good class for physiology

Dr. Sudweeks is AWESOME. He's great at teaching the content and making it super interesting. This is a pretty memorization-heavy course with a TON of different drugs, but the tests are very doable if you put in the time. There's lots of resources to help you study for tests and no unrelevant work in the course. Iclickers for attendance.

Amazing professor, just a really great teacher and you can tell he loves it. He simplifies very complicated topics and processes to help everyone understand. I took it spring semester and it was FAST. But he did such a good job i recommend him to everyone. Prioritize the class though, there is a LOT of info and the tests are pretty in depth.

Dr Sudweeks is AWESOME. He records all of his lectures so you can use them to study (DO THAT). The class is very test heavy (like 91% of your grade) but there is no homework. The tests are really fair and based on lectures so rewatch them before each exam. He is funny! He is so smart! He wants you to learn.

I loved taking from Dr. Sudweeks!  He focuses on our learning and the lectures are memorable and instructive.  The grade is just your tests and class iclicker participation.  He also prepares you well for a lot of MCAT topics if you're premed.  He is very approachable and you can tell he cares about his students.

Favorite class/teacher I've had at BYU so far, as a senior. Great guy, his classes are super fun and interesting. Don't underestimate the first test though, because the tests do make up a huge chunk of the overall grade. I didn't take the first test seriously and had to work hard to make up for it with the others. Take Phys from Sudweeks!!

I love Sterling more than anything. He made class so interesting and easy to understand, and he's the cutest human being ever. You only have to worry about the midterms but spend time studying and you should do great! Also, don't buy the book, he gives you all the resources you'll need. Take this class! Don't be intimidated by the spring schedule.

Dr. Sudweeks was a really great advanced phys professor. The class went really into detail about a lot of things. The TA reviews were really helpful for studying for the tests. There was a lot of study materials available which made studying much better. The class was really interesting and would definitely recommend taking it with him.

Tests are 93% of your grade, so if you tank one it tanks your grade. Iclicker questions are other 7%. Some extra credit available. Don't underestimate tests esp the final: there is a LOT of info covered that you have to memorize. Great class, but past ratings made me underestimate difficulty of tests. Sudweeks is very knowledgeable and caring.

Advanced Physiology is probably my favorite class so far at BYU. Dr. Sudweeks made the subject clear, interesting, and easy to understand. The class is pretty easy but you will learn SO MUCH. He designs in class questions to help you learn and they work! His attendance policy is very fair, you won't be trashed for missing a few iClicker questions.

while this class was easy A to get as long as you are diligent (50% got A's and the other half seems to not care as much) i would say that its not the physiology class your going to learn the most from, especially if the MCAT is in your future. the test questions are straight off of the slides and someone with no bio background could do well

Dr Sudweeks is a great guy.  He is very congenial and easy to get along with.  I would recommend his course for anyone interested in learning physiology, but without the ridiculous questions and tests that some professors give.  His course was also very helpful for the MCAT.

Super nice guy. Lectures are a bit dry, but solid--which also means you can learn everything from the powerpoints in half the time, if you are so inclined (that said, there are participation points which count for a not-insignificant part of your grade). No homework, just exams (straightforward, memorization-heavy) and a 5 page paper on policy.
Not a bad lecturer, but class can get a little dry. He teaches directly from powerpoints.

Dr. Sudweeks is awesome!  Best professor I've had at BYU so far.  His tests are not easy, but he prepares you for it and the questions are not confusing or ambiguous.  I would recommend him for any class.
Dr. Sudweeks is the man. Best professor I've ever had. Take any class you can from him.

Dr. Sudweeks is my best professor yet at BYU.  He makes physiology a great class and explains the concepts well.  His notes are very straight forward.  Almost impossible to not get a good grade.  I highly recommend him.

Great Professor.  There are participation points and easy take home open-everything quizes to buffer your grade. He tells you exactly what will be on the test.  The material is hard but I think he's the best person to take it from.  I got a B but I didn't study very much.

Sudweeks is the most chill professor you'll ever have.  I had him for 362 as well.  He teaches well, he helps you learn and retain information, he doesn't waste your time.  Tests are fair and predictable.  He's very much on your side and very approachable.  I just graduated and he is one of my favorite profs.

I thoroughly enjoyed the course.  He not only presents the material but also helps you get a grasp on it in class with active participation.  He teaches and tests straight from his outlines.  Highly recommended.
He is a good teacher and his class is well outlined. He also doesn't put any tricky questions. Just study what he puts on his outlines and your done fine.
Dr. Sudweeks follows and tests from an outline that is over the internet. Very nice teacher and fun laid back class.

I had him for ME 426 and ME 510. I like that he teaches from the textbook for each class very closely. My biggest complaint is that he asks very vague questions on quizzes and conceptual parts of exams and expects specific answers. It is hard to know what kind of answer he wants. You'll get penalized if you don't get it right.

I thoroughly enjoyed the class and learned a lot. You definitely need to put in the work to get a good grade, but if you enjoy aeronautics you'll probably like both the class and Dr. Gorrell, he absolutely knows what he's talking about.

Dr. Gorrell is a great professor. I found him to be very understanding and willing to help students. The course material follows the textbook closely. He is old school in the sense that tests are in the testing center and HW is turned into boxes. Lectures follow HW. The class is easier than core ME classes but hw can be tedious. Tests match hw

He holds himself above the students and has little to no respect for their efforts. He teaches like he is just going through the motions and then tests like you have the textbook memorized. Avoid this man at all costs, he actively tries to trick students and will ask a true or false question where the answer is maybe.

In class quiz every week that are conceptual or memorization based. He knows his stuff, but
is old school ie turn in hw to a box, no code on hw, and no ebooks or pdfs of the book. He seems to have a set way of doing things and is not very open to change. The book is heavily relied on to do well. Overall, a good, fair class and I learned a lot.

Dr. Gorrell is an amazing person, and some parts of his class match. He can get a little focused on the formulas and derivations though. But half of the issue is the class. He teaches us how we as to learn, so if you dot as you get standard teachings. When you ask you get phenomenal teaching.

I think he is a great professor. His classes are definitely challenging, but they are manageable if you are willing to put in the work. I took 3 courses from him and enjoyed them all. If you review the material every week in preparation for the weekly quiz, you should do well in the class.

Had a hard time explaining concepts.  His tests were hard and expected students to pull answers out of mid air.  I liked him at first, then found he was a lot less helpful than he made himself out to be.

Nice guy, hard tests. He had a hard time explaining some of the more difficult concepts, and then expected that we knew it for exams.  He was honest, and tried to make up for bad explanations, but if you want to do well, you'll end up having to teach yourself some of the concepts.

At first, class was great. He's from the industry & more down to earth. But he does NOT prepare you for tests. He has this stash of tests he uses - esp. for final that are in that category like I've seen this before, but somehow I have no clue how to do it - good at throwing WICKED curve balls that he has not shown you how to do. It's pretty lame.

As a person, I enjoyed his passion for music. As a teacher, I wouldn't take this class again because the way knowledge is tested is outdated and ineffective, which makes it difficult to actually do well. He expects his class to be the main focus of your semester, even though it's a GE.

He is a nice guy, but his tests are SO hard. You have to know everything to do well on tests. You learn about architecture, art, music, literature, etc. The TA's do test reviews which are lifesaving. You'll do fine if you go to class and take notes on almost everything and also read the textbook and study the material in there.

8 testing center exams in one semester. All "Not" questions, and some had essays. The only reason I did well was due to the amazing TAs! Attend every test review. You have to learn literature, art, music and more for this class. Pretty difficult for a general, but if you're a good test-taker, it's not the worst. I got 64% on the first and 90+ after

8 midterms and over 30 quizzes are the only grades in the grade book. I completed every reading and attended class, but am not a good test taker, and this class broke my 4.0. Very time consuming for a general. It is a constant stressor because there is always a test to study for, and the test format is hard. Get on Dr. Howard's waitlist instead.

I took this class to fulfill a GE. I found it really intersting a wish I had time in my schedule to take the part two course. The professor is really passionate a knowledgeable of everything he talks about. I was amazed at the facts he knew. If you love learning about music and history then take this class. I really enjoyed it!

He is such a great professor! I am so glad I decided to take his class last minute! He really cares about what he teaches! There are a lot of tests but he prepares you for them. If you attend the lectures and read, you will be totally fine:)

Professor Johnson is very knowledgable and passionate about music history and I came away learning a lot. You are only graded on 4 exams. I personally did not find them to be as challenging as they were made out to be. As long as you do the readings, are attentive in the lectures, and listen to/study the music, it is possible to succeed.

8 exams! They are difficult and if you don't do the readings you won't do well on the quizzes or the exams. I put in a lot of time with a study group and each of us felt that the exam scores we got didn't reflect what we were learning. He was a great lecturer and he is really passionate about the material but I'd take this class from another prof.

The Professor is very engaged, loves what he teaches, and helps students a lot whenever possible! However- there are so many tests and quizzes. So many. 3 quizzes a week (open note but still), lots of readings for each quiz, and 8 exams! The exams even overlap a little bit in content but aren't super cumulative. The workload is pretty insane.

There are a lot of tests for the class, but they are not bad. As long as you read and attend the lectures, the tests are fairly attainable. Professor Johnson is very nice and quite funny, you can tell he loves what he teaches.

Professor Johnson is seriously the nicest guy! I definitely recommend this class. Professor Johnson is very passionate about the subject and wants you to love it too. The tests are very similar to the lectures/textbook readings and he wants you to succeed. The TA's offer great review sessions as well.

Quite a bit of reading, but the class is pretty easy. Professor Johnson is a great teacher, and his lectures are very accurate to the test. If you come to class and read, you will do great! I would definitely recommend and take it again!

I LOVE professor Johnson! I don't know why he's rated so low--maybe because of online classes? but I had him this fall semester and he was fantastic! Very caring and passionate about what he teaches. The course material is clear and if you do the readings and pay attention in class you're sure to pass with a good grade!

Don't do it. Literally just don't. He seems to think that 8 midterms and 3 weekly quizzes and tons of pages of reading is an appropriate amount of work for a general Ed course. The amount of reading and exams made me hate this class. His lectures are also incredibly boring. Definitely worst class/professor I've ever had. I still got an A though.

Pretentious! He has a lot of opinions on art, and those are all you are required to know for the class. The format was ridiculous (powerpoints with audio - so you have to download huge files), and it takes a really long time for things to be graded. Not an awful class, but I definitely did not enjoy it.

Had him for Music 201 and 202. He's not that bad, but there isn't much to write home about. 3 days a week you read about 10 pages of the textbook, then watch a 1 hour lecture of him talking and you can't speed it up bc it's on powerpoint. Exam reviews don't help bc it doesn't cover what will actually be on the exam. Loved the content though

If you like excessive workloads for a general credit class, take Professor Johnson, you won't be disappointed. His tests are incredibly specific to the point where if you forget a minuscule detail of a work, you will probably miss a question on the test. Couple that with long readings and you have an enormous amount of random fact memorizing. Yep.

I took this class through BYU Independent Study. You just read the textbook and take notes from that and the supplemental material. The quizzes on each lesson can be tough. The papers weren't horrible but I felt I didn't understand enough to write about the subjects. Study for the midterm and final and study hard for the listening portion.

He knows the material well, and has a passion for it. The grading/scheduling can be confusing, so make sure you get the syllabus and know when the quizzes are due. There's a lot of reading, but it goes right along with the test because he wrote the textbook used. There's also an extra credit EXAM and it saved my life. Go to the essay exam reviews.

Looking for a fun music class? Music 201 may not be what you had in mind. Steven Johnson is a good instructor, but this class covers all of the arts. There are large tests every other week and they are difficult. It's doable, but not easy A material.

I have really enjoyed this independent study class. There are a lot of papers and quizzes to go along with the reading, but I'm grateful for the frequency. As someone said on another review - it's nice to be tested on smaller amounts of information. I have already signed up for his other online class. The learning is great!

Dr. Johnson is extremely knowledgable in his field and had personal experience with most material. He is an older professor so he's more old school. The TA's are extremely useful and are willing to help. Extra credit helps boost your grade. If you do the readings and take good notes you'll do great. Out of class he's really nice and personable.

Although his lectures sometimes dragged on, they did have to do with what the subject of the class was. Its not hard, you just gotta take notes and study the book before the tests. he has more tests, yes, but that means that they cover less info. other teachers give you fewer tests but with loads more info to study for. He does answer q's.

Dr. Johnson can come across as a little gruff at times, but he's actually a nice guy. He is very enthusiastic about the material, but there is a lot, so he tends to move quickly. If you do the reading and and the quizzes before class and take notes you'll be fine.

Great extra credit opportunity which is good because the tests are impossibly hard. Online quiz before each class which a TA who doesn't attend the lectures makes so sometimes they don't line up. Really passionate about what he talks about but sometimes when students ask questions he curtly says "we don't have time for that." That happens often.

Yes, he is difficult, however, I came away learning more about music and history than any other music faculty member. If you do the reading and meet with the TA you will be fine. He's tough but you come away from his class knowing your stuff. If you are interested in learning material he is the way to go.

Johnson makes this class passable. Open book outside of class reading quizzes and 10 midterms are the only assignments in the grade book. There are 6 extra credit 600 word responses that boost your grade if you bomb a midterm. That being said, the class is unorganized and Johnson is a very hands off prof, only lecturing and gives NO info on exams.
You are only graded on quizzes and test. Lectures everyday, but the lectures are really good. He teaches exactly what is on the test. There is a quiz before every class.

I had Dr. Johnson for Music 302 and 303. He can be incredibly gruff, rude, brash, and it often seems that he hates his students. He has made me cry before and is just generally insensitive and rude. However, he does know the subject material. Grades come from tests only, so take them seriously. He gives you the essays beforehand, so plan them well!

I really liked Johnson as a teacher. The class could be pretty boring if you're not interested and engaged in art or history. You definitely need to take notes. When I had him, there were four tough, long exams (with essays), and that's it. No other homework except reading, which you better do. There are extra credit essays that are helpful.

If you feel comfortable writing essays though, he's the easiest music history professor at BYU (but he's still tough).  He is gruff in class, but is among the most personable professors when you meet with him out of class.  Phenomenal lectures.  Only read the scores and essays - NOT the other textbook. It won't help.

Do WHATEVER you have to to avoid taking a class from Dr. Johnson.  The tests are 100x harder than they need to be and you're so worried about passing the test that you don't learn anything. He doesn't give you any info about the tests, he contradicts himself regularly, and it is clear that he doesn't actually care about his students doing well.

So I had a lot of people in my class that really didn't like this teacher. For me, he wasn't really a problem--I figured out how to do well on his tests, did some of the extra credit, did alright. I did best and ended up studying the least at the end when I read the material, and then went to class for his lectures (which are OK). That's key.

Dr. Johnson's class was incredibly hard, and though the TAs were helpful, he definitely was not. His lectures are useless for the test, 100% of the test questions come from his textbook that he wrote himself. The tests have several essays, and you have to just regurgitate exactly what he said about the subject in the textbook or you lose points.

This class was challenging, yes, but if you study and do the reading, then it pays off. Professor Johnson is really passionate about what he teaches, and his lectures are really insightful and interesting. The grading is based on test scores and optional homework essays that count for additional points.

Lectures are informative but overloaded with facts and details of around 1500 years of art, literature, architecture, and music. There are a ton of facts you're expected to memorize and regurgitate in the tests. By the way, there are 6 tests that are one after the other, so there's no stopping.

So everything everyone has said is true. He is difficult to work with and his tests are difficult. He covers too much material too fast. I had a conflict on the final exam which was scheduled and he would not work with me to resolve it. He told me that I had to come no matter what. Not a fun class and not important to my major.

Don't take Music 201 with Johnson. Every test has at least 6 essay questions about works of artarchitecturemusic, and the textbook is like three inches thick, and you're gonna read it all. Not to mention he seems to like making his students feel stupid, asking for their opinion and then callously shooting them down or bluntly contradicting them.

This is already a hard class, and Prof Johnson makes it harder. He is very knowledgeable and knows what he's talking about, but the tests are HARD, LONG, and frequent (I think 10?). His lectures are jam-packed and useful, but textbook material is on the tests too. Overall, heard better things about other Music Civ professor.

Professor Johnson is very knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches. I really liked the material, and the tests were not that hard. However, he's not the nicest professor. I was afraid to ask him questions because he could be demeaning and cold. But overall, I enjoyed his lectures and I value the knowledge I gained from his class.

LOVED the class. One of the most interesting classes I've ever taken. Johnson is very passionate about the subject he teaches and makes the class very interesting, however he is not very personable. Go to the TA reviews, they'll save you.

The lectures are stellar, but the tests are a kick in the face. He doesn't have a final, however he has 10 midterms. Personally, I had to study for each as if it were a final. I spent over 16 hours in the testing center total. You can decide if it is worth it to you.

Graduate school is bound to be a cinch after these classes. It is possible to pass and to get good grades, but the study required to get a good grade is exorbitant. He is a great guy and a great teacher, but arguably the worst test writer ever.

Johnson's class is overload of information that could be helpful, but tries to get through too much material and ultimately you are left just trying to memorizing pointless facts about each piece and not enjoying the material.  This has been easily the most time consuming class I have ever taken at BYU and I graduate this this semester.

Dr. Johnson is very knowledgeable about his field, but often makes demeaning comments to students who do not see things as he does. Tests are given 3 at a time, are laboriously long and cover material not taught in class.  He does not tolerate talking in class, even relevant conversations. Recognize the music and memorize the scores to do well.

Dr. Johnson, on a good day, seems to want to help you, but his course is structured very poorly. Your grade is based on 7 tests, which can be studied for independent of class, so it feels like coming to class is a waste of time. He can get very angry, and lost his temper more than a few times. Tests are time consuming and practically irrelevant.

Dr. Johnson is a good man, but he can be difficult to get along with.  He makes no effort to conceal his occasional anger with the class.  His 7 tests are long, time-consuming,  tedious, and rarely about music.  The extra credit assignments help.  This class is doable, I promise, but make sure you know what you're getting into before you sign up.

His honors Music 201 class is extremely time consuming and very difficult. Your grade is based only on 7 tests. He is disconnected from his students, so you have to go to the TAs if you want to knkow what's going on. He definitely knows a lot and is funny sometimes, but I would advise only taking his class if you love ancient art and music.

Very knowledgeable in his field and passionate about musicology, but he is not tolerant of other opinions. He requires a great deal of focus/preparation for his lectures. The tests were challenging but manageable if you prepared well. He was not professional in giving criticism, singling students out in front of the class. Go to class prepared!

Time consuming class.  I learned  a lot, but it was stressful and had copious amounts of art to memorize.  The TAs grade the essays/tests, so go to the reviews.  He can be extremely unfriendly if you ask a question he doesn't want to answer, or if you have a different opinion from him... speak out at your own risk.  Do the extra credit assignments!

Extremely experienced in his field. Plans lessons meticulously. It's a hard class because there's a lot to learn in a short amount of time, but it's doable if you keep up with it (actually do the reading and listening). If you come to office hours he's really helpful.

Prof. Johnson seemed to be getting by with the minimum effort possible which resulted in the class being more of a "memorize and regurgitate" class instead of understanding or learning to appreciate music. When I asked him for clarification on something he said, he responded in a demeaning manner.

His class, though hard, really opened my eyes and piqued my interest in modern music. The best way that I have heard his class described was "I wish I could take all of the [music history] classes from him without his tests." GO TO OFFICE HOURS WITH QUESTIONS. Come prepared with intelligent questions and he will help you(not during class).

Dr. Johnson's class was one of my hardest, but also most interesting.  Tests are intense, but the multiple choice is straight from the lectures and book, and the TA's grade the essays, so just go to review sessions. Dr. Johnson is extremely knowledgeable and I learned so much from him.  If you really want to learn, take from him.

Johnson is the best music history professor I've had so far.  I really looked forward to his lectures.  He always comes to class very prepared (his power points are extremely helpful) and he is very sincere about his love of music.  The tests weren't hard, but the essays were difficult.  I actually felt like I learned something.
This class made me lose interest in music. I took evening time and it is hard to focus on. Exams are hard.

Subject was interesting, tests okay if you study, but him being "unapproachable" is a euphemism. Seems to think that students are not worth his time, and won't take five seconds to answer your question (but he can tell you in those five seconds how little you are worth his time). Absolutely the rudest and most insensitive teacher I have ever had.

ok, so first off this is an honors class, all grades are in the tests, he does not spoon feed things, but he does make his tests straight from the textbook and his lectures, take good notes, get in with the TA's honestly not that bad of a class, and he is NOT nicer to music majors, just to ppl who participate if he knows your name, its a good thing

His class is not easy, but I loved it! I learned so much! He is slightly biased towards music majors though. 201 has a lot less music than 202, but both also focus on music and literature. I took both halves and even though studying for the tests was a lot of work, I'm so glad I took the classes.

It's a tough class. You will learn a lot. This is college. He doesn't hold your hand, and he's not teaching so that you memorize; those trying to learn so that they can regurgitate memorized facts will have difficulty. Those that are independent enough to keep up with the work and are capable of reading the syllabus will be fine.

Hard class, but I learned a ton. I took Music 201 from someone else before I had Johnson--Johnson takes a lot more work, but I learned so much more. Definitely worth it. I'm neither a music major or an honors student and I got an A in this class.

For someone who's expecting basic introduction to music, this really is little more than that. Worked like a horse for the course. I don't know what is an A but whoever got it must have worked extremely extremely hard. You really learn a lot from the course. The teacher is good but the tests way too hard.

Hands down the worst teacher I've ever had.  I thought the 101 class would broaden and expand my views about music.  instead Johnson's class left me wishing i'd never heard of music in the first place. His lectures are boring and his tests are ridiculous. Only take this class if you are a die hard music student, or you like to be miserable.

This class was not taught on  a 101 level.  I will probably never use most of the material covered.  Boring!  I remember most classes, I could look around and at least half the class was asleep.  The test are a pain in the rear.  He doesn't give any preperation to what is going to be on them.  You must memorize everything.

I took this class thinking that it was 101...o wait, it was! He made it way too hard for a class of students who don't actually study music. The tests were brutal and he offers extra credit but can't be bothered to tell you what you should do. If you are only taking it for your arts credit, find someone else!

I thought he was a really good teacher.  He knows what the subject very well and tries to teach us what he knows. If you do you homework and attend lecture, it's not too bad.  It is an honors class, so it's supposed to be hard.

I thought Professor Johnson was a great teacher.  I was  nervous after the comments I found here but I enjoyed his sense of humor and the information.  His tests were very hard but he gave a generous curve.  He was also very approachable-one of my tests got lost and he was very accommadating.  Know the actual music and genres for the tests.
He lacks the ability to understand that the course is only intro.  He attempts to make students learn things well beyond the acceptable range for introduction to the topic

Dr. Johnson is brillant when it comes to music and art, but what he lacks is people skills.  I found that if you can read his mind you do well, but if you can't, you're screwed.  What he had to say about the subject matter was very interesting and I learned alot from him, but I had a very difficult time dealing with him being rude and insensitive

Horrible teacher.  He's so rude to students and makes the class miserable. He once told us to have a discussion, then when we all didn't stop talking in like two seconds he yelled at us. class is extremely hard. If you have to take this class, know the art. Oh, and dont' ever let him know you forgot to bring your book to class, he makes you leave.

My grandma passed away early in the semester and I emailed Dr. Johnson asking if I could take the first exam early. His response was: the syllabus outlines your options. Those options were, take the test at the appointed time, or drop the class. He was extremely insensitive, and reduced me to tears in class. I dropped the class.

Very demanding and unapproachable in class. Nice guy out of class. VERY passionate about 20th century music: his redeeming quality. If you aren't sure you have the right answer, keep your hand down.  If you're wrong, he'll make you feel like an idiot before you can say "Who really cares about Minimalism anyway?" Remember, bring your scores or die!

Contrary to many of the posted comments, I found Dr. Johnson to be a fascinating teacher.  Also, the class isn't incredibly hard if you attend the lectures and do your homework.  If you want to learn, take this class.

Run sceaming for the hills.  Class is intense and difficult and unnecessarily so. He doesn't bother with silly details such as speaking audibly or listening to students - get friendly with the TAs and go to review sessions - they're your only hope of surviving this academic apocalypse.

The tests are difficult, his lectures consist of powerpoint slides, he favors those students that are music majors, he's abrasive, and I felt like he thought we were a waste of his time.  Take this class from a different teacher.

This class is one of the hardest I have taken at BYU but it just requires a lot of studying. More than you would think. Going to the class helps out a ton too! He explains things in more detail and we usually have discussions in class(which I love) Tough but very interesting class.
No Comments

Dr. Johnson is an awesome teacher. He is very passionate about visual arts, literature, and music.  Definitely my favorite teacher of last year.  Class is only hard is you make it that way.  Read and study and it's impossible to not get an A.

He was quite rude to the students and wasn't at all approachable.  The class was abnormally hard and we had something like major ten tests in all.  If he's the only professor left, take your civ credit next semester!

He's a grouch who will not answer questions or help you at all!  He tests are rediculously hard for a 100 level class.  I have over 10 years of music background, attended every class, took meticulous notes, did the reading and averaged 60-70% on tests. :P

Great teacher because he likes students who want to LEARN.  If you want an easy class, look somewhere else, because the class is ALL about business.  I learned more in this class than almost any other class at BYU.
Don't take this class from him if you can avoid it.

I have now taken 3 classes by this professor and this is by far the best one. He is a very smart man and sometimes has difficulty understandning that not everyone enjoys learning code like he does, but he has organized the class content well to enhance learning for this course specifically.

No one got an A on his midterm. He is very knowledgable on the subject but does not do a good job at relaying that information. The lectures are hard to follow because he assumes that everyone reads through textbooks in their free time like he does.

It should be telling how difficult your class is when every student has a B+ or lower after your midterm. His lectures were extremely boring, I attended only because it was mandatory. Weekly HW assignment. Written midterm that tests you on knowledge of Swift and Swift UI. 2 Projects in the semester. He helps you with videos for the projects. Final is 3 hours in class, but is open internet and past code, just not open person. Can feel overwhelming at times, but class is doable. Definitely don't take with a heavy course load.

Professor Liddle was fine, but it seemed like he didn't really want to be a part of the class. It was a lecture series, so he didn't teach much, and he had his TA do all the grading and set up the lectures. It was the easiest A ever though.
Professor Liddle is a great professor and a very nice person. He knows what he is talking about. Very organized, nice, and overall just a solid professor. I would recommend his classes.

It felt like the class was a review of IS402. I was there for every lecture he gave but I have no idea what we talked about half the time. He loved to wander and he almost never gave a straight answer. I am sure he is willing to help but I was always deterred by the answers he would give in class. He seemed to love to speak in riddles.

I thought Dr. Liddle was a good professor. I think his best trait is his willingness to help students with their projects. That said, at times his lectures would wander into areas we didn't need to actually know about to do well in the class. Dr. Liddle is an excellent professor. If you didn't quite get the lecture, he was always available during office hours, where he would bend over backwards to help. I found the class to be very tedious, but also valuable. Dr. Liddle is great. Very knowledgeable and willing to help. I personally loved reading Zen. It's very philosophical, which is why it has some haters, but it shows a very interesting way of viewing the world and solving problems.
Had us read Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance, why? This class is full of busy work, and boring lectures. If you want to take one of the most unclear classes ever, then this is it!

Steve is FANTASTIC. He is beyond passionate about the topic but also about the students. The way he lectures makes it entertaining and engaging. I listed that attendance is mandatory mostly because you are going to want to engage with his class, but he doesn't take attendance. Study and memorize the slides for the tests.

Peterson was hilarious and definitely passionate. If you were struggling with your grade he would definitely help you to get it up. Not a hard class at all, the only thing was the study guides never really met what was on the exams, so it was sometimes challenging to know what to study for. But if you need a GE take it from him, trust.

Professor Petersen is so amazing. He is so caring and kind. He is passionate about his work! This class is on the easier side but is definitely more test-heavy. There are three midterms, one final, three papers, and a quiz taken in class at the end of every lecture, each worth 5 points.

Great guy and is hilarious! Don't think I've heard someone say “Freakin awesome” so much in my life! Tests can be hard, but as long as you make sure to study the trees each week before lab you're good. That's pretty much the only HW. He is great at explaining concepts and helping us understand. He really cares about his students. Amazing teacher!

BEST TEACHER EVER. I'm not kidding this class changed my life he's so inspirational and a very easy grader. All his assignments are very clear and he tells you exactly what you need to know for the test. He's super engaging and always wants to be helpful. There's hardly any homework just a couple assignments throughout the semester. Take his class!

This class was interesting and Dr. Petersen is such a nice guy. There are weekly labs which you go through during lab periods and also weekly assignments in the ESRI training portal. 2 tests and a final presentation along with a short write-up. Not a difficult class and very helpful if you are headed towards landscape ecology/GIS/remote sensing.

I. LOVE. STEVE. Coolest professor I have ever had. Super down to earth and just plain funny (never heard a professor use "dude" and "freaking awesome" so much). He loves his subject so much, and makes it fun to learn. Tests are a little tough, make sure you study and then you'll be fine. They make up most your grade. Steve is why I'm in the major.

This was a great class with interesting activities during lab and good lectures. Steve is very animated and likes to get everyone involved. One paper, two midterms, one final, 12 or so tree quizzes. The memorization and identification aspect is difficult and can be time consuming but he doesn't make it overly difficult.

Steve is awesome! He truly loves trees. The class is laid out simply: 1 research paper, tree ID quizzes every two weeks, 3 tree mounts, a homework assignment, and exams on lecture material. Show up to class, take notes, and study your trees well, and you will be just fine!

I love Steve. He loves trees so much it's tangible, and he's just such a fun guy. Loved this class, field trips were SO fun! Tree ID tests were tough but he was generous with E.C. Just do study for those. Only downside is his tests are vague and it's not super clear what you need to know or study. But I LOVED the class itself.

Such a great professor! He's always happy to meet outside of class to help and is super approachable. Tests are easy enough if you go to TA reviews and fill out the study guide. Don't need the textbook, all the info is in the Powerpoints which he posts. One 4-5 page paper that you have all semester to work on. Easy, enjoyable class!

Steve is super great and very passionate about what he teaches. He really cares about it and helps the students to care about the course. Sometimes a bit scattered in lectures and gets sidetracked but always makes sure you know everything and are ready for tests. He is willing to work with students to make sure you understand and get a good grade.

Professor Peterson is more of a researcher, but isn't able to teach very well. His lectures are all over the place and often it's just him reading from the slides with some commentary. His tests are really tough as it will include a good amount of statistics and direct recall. But great guy! Learned all of our names on day 1!

Steve is awesome! He made it so interesting to learn about our planet and the biology behind it. The guy was absolutely hilarious about everything too. He would often go on these tangents about what we were learning about and somehow always related them back to the class. Overall, the class wasn't too hard.

Steve is awesome! He made it so interesting to learn about our planet and the biology behind it. The guy was absolutely hilarious about everything too. He would often go on these tangents about what we were learning about and somehow always related them back to the class. Overall, the class wasn't too hard. If you pay attention you're good.

Steve is a great guy, on a personal level. His lectures are always interesting and funny! But his tests were hard. The TA reviews helped but he gave long study guides and half wasn't on the test. He expected us to remember specific details from the lectures. The final wasn't too bad though. And Steve is willing to help students succeed.

If you have no background is GIS, this class is going to wreck your world. Each lab takes at least 4 hours. The assignments are difficult and hard to follow. The inclasificable material in pretty easy and if you can do well on the exams you'll get a good grade. Really difficult class with a great teacher.

Best professor I have ever had. The class is harder then you would expect from a GE science class, but he is very reasonable and fair. He works with students, gives great lectures, and his powerpoints are very helpful.

Professor Petersen is really good at lecturing and attending to his students needs. The class teaches a lot of really cool concepts related to forestry management and how to identify tree species. It is extremely difficult and time consuming. The tests and quizzes require a lot of work. Amazing professor.

If this website was rating how nice of a person he was, then he is the best. Nice and caring, totally genuine. However, this course was ridiculous scrambled. Never knew what to expect on the exam, and his lectures always seemed incomplete. A little disorganized which was very stressful. I learned how to ID trees but nothing in managing them

This guy is awesome. Engaging lectures and literally the only homework was one term paper. You don't need the textbook. I agree though the tests are trickier than expected but the TA reviews definitely help a lot.

Dr Peterson is funny & makes bio interesting. 70% of grade is 4 tests. Despite intense study of guides, slides, reviews & reading I only got Bs on tests. Wouldn't care if they weren't so heavily weighted. Still the BEST option for your bio requirement. Light work (outside of heavy test prep) & great lectures & class. Best BIO option.
Would definitely recommend taking PWS 150 from him. He's the funniest professor I have ever had for sure. Make sure to study hard for the tests and go to the reviews, they can be pretty tricky.

LOVED this class. Take it from Dr. Petersen. Such a fun energetic guy who is immensely passionate about his course. 4 tests that are easy if you just pay attention and go to reviews. There are like 4 assignments, and then a midterm paper, and that's it. He's honestly so pure and I LIVE for it. He also gives out chocolate milk if it's your b-day.
Steve is a great guy, really makes class enjoyable. Pace yourself and really take time to study the trees instead of cramming for the quizzes, seriously. Tests are a bit tricky, but not impossible.

Awesome professor who cares about his students. His lectures can turn into story time but they are enjoyable to be in. The tests are surprisingly tricky, the study guides don't help too much, I usually refer to the book. Essays & small in class assignments make up the rest of the grade. He is a great guy who is very approachable and easy to talk to

A definite (A-plus) if taken by this man. the best and easiest professor in environmental biology. So enthusiastic and funny and energetic. 8 am class and yet he still keeps his class awake and ready to learn. Study power points and tests will be fine. one term paper. Literally have to be the laziest person on earth to fail his course

Dr. Peterson is one of the best professors I've had. The curriculum can be a bit challenging because trees aren't really my favorite thing to learn about, but Steve's enthusiasm is infectious. He is also basically your best friend; always willing to talk and really does genuinely care about you as a person, not just a pupil or a grade. He's AMAZING

I've taken every course Steve offers for good reason. Apart from being a strapping young lad, this man has instilled a strange and bizarre love for the forest and all of its trees. I didn't even like trees until he infected me with this disease. Take it from him. Take all his classes.
Best mentored research there is
This man is so hawt. so is this class if you have any inclination to pursue GIS as a profession.

I don't like science and had to take this to fill a general, but Dr. Petersen was an AWESOME teacher. He actually made this class enjoyable and I learned a lot. Really great teacher and funny guy. Definitely recommend him.
As long as you went to the TA reviews, you were good on the tests. Easy as that. Don't have to go to class at all basically. The reviews and you're good.

I loved Dr. Petersen. I thought Bio 100 would be a killer but he is the nicest guy and his class is pretty easy. However, the TA's are what really save you come test time. Petersen is a great teacher. Only complaints are that he takes a little time to get into the lecture... sometimes 15 minutes. but that is because he is sharing some cool spiritual thought. Steven Petersen is really the best. I'm not usually into science courses, but he made me looking forward to coming to Biology every day. Take Bio from him!!

This has got to be the easiest Bio 100 class you can take.  I had hardly any homework at all for this class, only a couple of reading assignments and a paper.  But that's it.  And the tests are super easy too.  Just go to the TA reviews, and you will get an A no problem.  Dr. Peterson is great: he's super funny and really cares about his students.

DR. PETERSEN IS A GREAT GUY. He makes his lectures interesting, and while he may not stay on topic in class all the time you can still get a good grade in the class if you go to the reviews before the tests. You'll love him as a professor. If you want a teacher who stays on topic, don't take a class from him. But i promise you'll LOVE his lectures.
He was a fantastic professor! He made the class engaging and fun. He was very clear about the content and made a class I wasn't excited about even better!

Good class overall. Tests are killer though. They are around 50 multiple choice, 10 short answer, and then an essay. Make sure to go to review sessions with the TA's because they basically tell you what's on the test.

Bro Petersen is the best! I've always heard Bio 100 is rough but taking it from Petersen made it by far my favorite class. He had all our names memorized on day one. I always left class with a smile. He's hilarious, you will love going to class

Dr. Petersen is the most passionate teacher ever. He is in love with what he teaches and it makes a boring class somewhat entertaining. he is very fun and will try to keep things interesting. offers a lot of extra credit and gives study guides for the tests

Really fun. I don't like biology but I did learn things here. Tons of opportunity for easy extra credit, I got an A- and otherwise would have gotten a B+, maybe a B. Dr. Petersen is the best professor I have had at BYU. He makes things easy to understand and I can actually stay awake in his class...not an easy feat for BIO 100

Peterson was good, just his class was hard to follow.  It seems too much for a BIO 100 class...I stink at BIO and went to class and tried to listen, but each lecture was like..."what???" Dr. Petersen is seriously the funniest, most caring guy in the world. You have to go to class for iClicker points, but the lectures are seriously so interesting--and I hate biology. I am not a fan of biology, but this class was actually pretty good.  Petersen is funny, approachable, and passionate.  iclicker was for points and attendance each class. I loved Brother Petersen. I've never done well in any kind of science, but he made the class understandable and I managed to do just as well in this class as any other. I LOVED this teacher! Was NOT looking forward to taking Bio, but Petersen made it a wonderful experience! Knows your name first day, & is very passionate about Bio! Great class! Great teacher. Knew my name on the first day and did not forget it. Is very approachable and I learned a lot... Lots of opportunities for extra credit. Learned a lot too!

I loved Dr. Petersen. Biology has always been one of my worst subjects but I found this class interesting and completely fair, if not even a bit easy. He's a funny guy and I've never had a boring day in his class.
Interesting class and nice professor.  Tries to call students by name and wants to help them succeed.  Offers lots of extra credit.  Tests are very straight-forward if you attend your lab section.

Oh Petersen is the best! I came into the class hating biology but he made it so interesting and fun with his awesome attitude and personality. You know he cares about you when he calls you by name without ever talking to you before. He is really great at including the gospel into his lectures. He is an awesome teacher and an awesome person.

Dr.Peterson is an amazing professor! He is the most passionate professor I have ever had.  He knew everyone's name the first day of class.  He is always more than willing to help you with anything.  I would definitely take his class!
He was a very helpful teacher. I enjoyed his cheerful attitude and fun personality.
I loved this class! He was so helpful and really fun to have. He had my name memorized the first week without having ever talked to me! His class is fair and I would recommend him to anyone.

Professor Peterson was always well prepared, knows his subject matter, encourages and welcomes student questions, and had most all 0f the 200+ student names memorized on the first day of class. Awesome professor!

I'm not a Biology fan, but Dr. Petersen made it interesting and  got me to class every day. Not really any homework (1 final paper) and tests aren't too hard if you actually study. Petersen is very up front/easy going and I enjoyed his class. Petersen is awesome!  I hate Bio but I actually enjoy his class.  Gives study guides for the midterms that are basically all you need.

Dr. Petersen is a great professor.  He has an amazing sense of humor.  We have a scriptural thought every morning before lecture.  He is fair in all of his grading. Petey rules!

Stephen Richardson is probably one of the better cs department teachers, but the departments grading was extremely tough one slip up on any homework quiz or test and your either stuck with a c or an f good luck there's way more than 3 credit hours worth of work in this class. Expected to sell your soul to get a good grade if your new to python.

He's a great professor. He includes online lectures, so you really don't need to go to class, as they cover more than the lectures. He is very spiritual, encourages participation, and is very kind and understanding. He encourages experimentation and being hands on in your learning. Dr. Richardson is a very good professor for CS111. It's a pretty big jump, and you cover some difficult topics, but he is caring and goes above and beyond to help students. Dr. Richardson was a great professor who was very effective at teaching and applying concepts. His class was pretty good. Lectures are pretty useless, you can skip most of them or just use it as study hall. Good class. The lectures were super boring and were hard to follow sometimes. The labs were very helpful and there is where i learned most of my stuff. I would recommend getting far ahead as soon as possible. The class is easy, but gets harder the longer you wait to do your assignments.

In this class Professor Richardson gave interesting lectures but most of them were theoretical and were there to teach you the basic principles. For most people just attending the labs was good enough because that is where you learn and apply all of the concepts you need for the homework.

This class was pretty easy. Dr. Richardson was really nice, and he always started class with a spiritual thought and prayer (normally done by a student). The lectures weren't super interesting, but I definitely felt like I learned throughout this class.
He's a wonderful person and professor. The class isn't super organized but it is a lot of fun.

He's great!! He had a lot of focus on environmental and occupational health since that's his career field but it was interesting to learn about. He is very fun, engaging, and caring. I enjoyed his lectures and his class! You have a good amount of assignments but they aren't hard or overwhelming. I would definitely take from him again!

This was Steve's first semester teaching 315 and I hope he gets to teach it again! He is super kind, funny, and knowledgeable. Assignments aren't hard and neither are tests. His passion for PH is contagious. I wish I had him for more classes! I would def take it from him if you can. There are attendance quizzes but classes are engaging/interesting

He is an amazing professor. It's not a hard class, and there are plenty of extra credit opportunities and chances to make up work. He is very flexible, and I have nothing bad to say. He's a great person to get to know.

Genuinely the best class I took all semester! Only a handful of assignments, all super easy. Class is super interesting and engaging, tests were take-home style and a breeze. Steve is probably the nicest, most down-to-earth prof I've ever had. There were only 7 people in our class, so lectures felt very personalized and casual. Definitely recommend

Dr. Thygerson is an absolutely amazing professor. I would 100% recommend him and any of the courses he teaches. He is fun, caring, and very knowledgeable in the health and safety field. Definitely can't go wrong with Dr. T!

Such an easy class, but I learned so much!! There are a couple of open notes quizzes, in class group quizzes, and homework assignments that are not hard at all. Dr. Thygerson is the best. He cares about his students and makes class fun. If you attend class and pay attention you will do fine.

This class is very easy if you want an A- or a B+.  you can just attend class and do alright on the tests.  there is not too much work required.  My main issue is that in every test and quiz there are always questions that have not been covered in class and are not on the power point.  I felt like it required a bit of luck to get an A.
A pretty chill class. I was able to just chill on my laptop and still get the information I needed to pass the tests.

It depends what class you take from him. Injury prevention is not a bad class. Occupational health it is. The tests are very hard and the class is not fun. It might not be his fault, he is actually a nice person.

Great Professor! He has an engaging and discussion style approach to teaching. The best part is, is that he shares his work experience with education.

Super funny dude. His grading is very fair. Mid-terms are harder than you would expect but he gives out a ton of assignments that makes up for it. If you keep up with his assignment, it should be an easy A. One of the best teachers.

Great teacher! really fun to listen to and will do anything to help you in his class and in your other classes as well. He helped me with my technical communications class, really helpful. Very easy to talk to and answers your questions well.

Dr. Williams is a silly guy who likes to teach math. His lectures weren't conceptually in-depth, but clearly taught the "procedure" to work through problems, effectively preparing us for the exams. There is a lot of homework, but Prof. Williams' fun demeanor makes it very manageable. He focuses a lot on practice problems rather than junk that makes students fall asleep.
