Super nice guy and awesome professor. Office hours were helpful. This class is just straight up hard. 70% average on the final and some midterm questions were just impossible. But if you have to take calc 2, I suggest taking it from Dr Williams.

Prof Williams is hilarious, and really cares about his students and their success.  Calc 2 (Math 113) is a huge pain, and there is a ton of work (homework is due 4 days a week), but it is clear that Prof Williams cares and wants to help you. Office hours before tests are super useful. Lectures are funny, but move quickly and a bit boring.

Calc 2 is a notoriously difficult class, but Prof. Williams was hilarious throughout the whole semester. He tries hard to engage during lecture (even when there's 200 students in there), but Calc is still Calc. If you want to do well, you have to put that effort in. I would recommend looking over the lesson before lecture to get familiar.

I was scared to take Calc 2, but Williams was the right choice. Practice tests are very similar to the real tests, and if we are starting a unit near the midterm he will push it which other teachers did not do. Lots of homework but it is helpful for the test, lots of help available, and I scored high 90s on the tests.

It's a challenging class, but Dr. Williams makes it manageable. He doesn't bore you with excessive theory and focuses on practice problems, which help you understand the concepts. Go to his office hours, he will work with you to help you succeed.

Professor Williams is a funny guy and his lectures are usually pretty easy to follow. It is a tough class though, and even with the help of the TAs and attending the labs I was not able to get the grade I wanted. Professor Williams is very approachable and keeps office hours. Highly recommend going talking to him if there are issues or struggles.
He is great. Very flexible, assignments are clear and lab hours are plentiful.

Dr. Williams is a great professor and you can tell he loves what he does. That being said, he skips over the types of problems on the exams and only does the easier ones. Very approachable and Labs were helpful for more in-depth questions. There is a lot of homework, but in the end, it is a 4 Credit Hour Course, so you should expect it in a way.

I loved taking class from Dr. Williams. He has a great sense of humor and really cares about you. Though he breezed through slides way too fast to even take notes, about every other day was spent doing examples and working on homework with his help (no TAs) which was amazing. There were never any surprises on exams. 10000% recommend.

HIGHLY recommend! I was initially hesitant about taking this class in the spring, but he's one of the BEST math professors I've had at BYU. He was a great professor that truly cared more about you learning than anything. He makes time for you during office hours and helps you through the problems.

Professor Williams is a great professor that provides all of his students to receive a good grade in his class. It does require a good amount of homework and study but he makes the lectures entertaining!

Brother Williams is a very reasonable teacher. When the test averages are particularly low, he curves and will even drop them. He is very good at giving people intuition for calculus but often does not go into things in depth. Tests are by far the biggest factor for your grade, but he prepares you very well.

Love this man! Super caring and patient. He will literally answer any question and he is really funny! MATH 113 is a hard class and he teaches the tougher concepts well. He teaches the background and then goes into examples, if that's how you like your math classes I highly recommend. Work is manageable and there are 5 midterms + a final.

Pros: really sweet/funny teacher, very forgiving on extending deadlines, does everything he can to help you pass, tests are not hard if you study well. cons: lots of homework (which does help to learn the material), can go pretty fast so you have to be able to stop and ask him questions, and sometimes he doesn't go over enough practice problems.

This class was done through zoom and it was hard to focus with all of the comments . He also isn't very good at teaching concepts if you need him to explain in depth with all of the details that you need to know to understand the concept. I would not recommend this professor.

Dr. Williams is a teddy bear! He went the extra mile to make this online class interesting and doable. Between the thorough lectures, relevant homework, TAs, textbook, reference documents, lecture recordings, and Dr. Williams himself, ANY question you ask will be answered. Class is M-F with homework due every other day, but he grades charitably.

Dr. Williams is my hero. Calculus is inherently a very hard class but he makes it as painless as he can. He does everything possible to give you the best grade. For class he spends the first 20-30 min teaching the topic and for the rest of the time he just goes over examples that you can find in the homework.

Prof. Williams is a great person and definitely cares about his students, however he is not a good teacher. I have resorted to youtube for my lectures because in class he speeds over topics like we have heard them before. He also makes many mistakes when doing problems. Again, great person and lenient with homework and tests but not a good teacher.

Prof. Williams really cares about his students. Because of COVID, our class was held over zoom, and tests were online. It was difficult, but prof. Williams made himself available for help, and also was very helpful during the lectures. He does a lot of examples and explains topics well. He is also just a very kind person in general!
Professor Williams is very good at thinking of what his students are dealing with, and what they need in order to balance justice and mercy. I took him during COVID-19.

Brother Williams is a nice man, but his lectures were dull. They were hard to sit through and I felt like I didn't learn much through his powerpoints. The class was a lot of work that didn't seem worth it.

No math class is easy. He is great at teaching, and explaining the intuition behind the processes. I'd really recommend him. He encourages questions in class, and is willing to change the current day lecture based upon questions. He also answers questions from homework when asked. He'll help you succeed if you try also!

So awesome. I've taken two classes from him. He is lenient, understanding, patient, and explains things well. He is very interested in having the students determine the load of coursework and have a say in how many midterms we take. He's funny and good natured. Just a good guy and a good teacher. He's the most dad-like professor I've ever had.

Great teacher. I took his smaller size class and it was amazing. Homework online and written both due once a week. Makes lots of jokes to keep you engaged. Very willing to stop lecture and review material in order to help all students understand. Very helpful and understanding. 10/10 would recommend for anyone. Final is difficult however

He's great. The only bad thing about his class is that his lectures are boring and hard to sit through. That said, he cares more about students learning than penalizing them for missing assignments. He structures the class by class vote. Super nice and helpful during office hours and class.

Dr Williams was great! He explained everything very clearly and made the most challenging concepts seem simple. Grading was generous, he had 3 midterms and dropped your lowest score, and always had practice tests. Extra credit if you did the online homework a few days early. Always willing to go over any questions someone had on a homework in class

Dr. Williams is a great professor! His lectures can be quick sometimes, but he makes it fun and is understanding. He writes his own tests, so you can learn the concepts well without having really difficult tests that can hurt your GPA. He provided opportunities for extra-credit as well. You will need to work to do well, but it's very doable.

This was one of the easiest classes I've taken at BYU. He wasn't incredibly organized, but I didn't mind that. He did not have a clear grading scale, and only graded a few of our assignments. Very open to talk to about your grades though. Only beef I had was that his T/F practice tests didn't really prepare you for the actual test.

Dr. Williams is really great at clearly explaining concepts. He's also very fair. The math department comes up with the hw but when he saw that students were spending 2+ hours doing the online homework he modified it for his class. He prepares you well for the tests and makes himself available  for students. Highly recommend

He is a really good professor! He helps you a lot with your homework! I never rate professors but Bro. Williams deserves it!  He is hilarious and he prepares you for his tests and the homework are really helpful! I would totally take it from him!

Dr. Williams is the best professor I have had at BYU. He is so helpful. In class, he was willing to work out any problem we were stuck on. He also had great office hours and would respond quickly to emails about problems. He made class enjoyable and worthwhile. Also, he'd give us old midterms to study which were almost identical to the real one.
This class is super hard but he does everything he can to help you out. he gives you practice tests and reviews. its just a really hard class with a heavy workload
Really great teacher! He is very understanding with the class and we could usually talk him into things. He was very kind, but a little difficult at the same time.

Very good professor. Calc is very difficult but Professor Williams gave us practice tests and reviews so we weren't surprised. Lots of homework but doable if you get help from the TA's. I would definitely recommend him.

VERY HARD CLASS. Calc isn't easy, but this class was ridiculous.  The department tests are tough.  This class requires a ton of homework, but the TAs and Prof Williams are very helpful if you go to them.  Don't wait until after the second test to get help with limits. Lots of emphasis on things NOT covered in AP Caluculus AB.
Amazing professor. Dr. Williams is great for one-on-one help. When he says that he will help you if you come to him, he really means it.

Professor Williams teaches the subject material really well and covers everything that appears on the tests. He has some corny math humor too, which makes the class a little more interesting. Calculus is still a challenging subject, even with a good professor. So be willing to study!

This class is hard and a lot of work. Just know that from the beginning. You'll spend a lot of time in the math lab if you want to do well. Dr. Williams is great and really helpful. Interacts well and is very willing to help. Uses humor to keep you awake. The class is hard but Dr. Williams is by far the best professor to take it from.

He incorporates humor into his calculus lectures, is not offended when students find his mistakes, and is willing to help students one on one in his office. He offers old tests as study guides. Although I had taken calculus before, the class covered more material and I understood the concepts much better than my first experience with calculus.

I took Ochem from Dr. Castle and had a good experience, but I enjoyed taking 455 from him even more!  He is an excellent lab professor and really knows his stuff.  He is also super patient with everyone asking him the same question 10 times and cares about his students. The content with Chem is always hard, but it's very doable.
Worse professor ever. Tests were impossible and class average never got above a 70%, he had no sympathy and claimed it would be okay because he curves the class. Even with the curve less t

Definitely don't take this class from Castle, I got in the 60's for each exam, before dropping, then I took O Chem 2 the next semester from Price and got 95-100 on each exam. Take from any other professor, Castle will ruin your chances of getting into medical school.

CHEM352 with Professor Castle is challenging, but rewarding if you put in the work. Attend lectures, use the textbook, and try unstuck AI for efficient study prep. The class is tough, but the learning is worth it.

Super helpful, very knowledgeable in organic synthesis. Went out of his way to help us during lab. He is pretty strict on grading the lab reports, but as long as you have all of the necessary requirements, and are organized in your reports, NMRs, characterization sheets, etc (use the examples on LS) you should get close to full credit. Fun class.

He does a good job lecturing and presents material well. I had no trouble understanding the content thanks to him, but his tests are abominable. Most of your grade is based on pop quizzes on material we haven't entirely covered yet, or in tests that don't even remotely resemble the content we learn in class. Test averages never got over 65%.

Coming into this class I thought I liked Ochem. I quickly found out this class was going to be more of a grind than a joy. He expects a lot out of his students. If you're pre-dental or pre-med I would take it from him. I had to study just 3 days of Ochem after to prepare for the DAT. I ended up getting a 27 on Ochem. I credit that all to Castle.

Dr. Castle is one of the toughest professors out there, that being said, because of his class and the work I was forced to do in it, I aced the Ochem section on the DAT. So the class will make you pull your hair out and probably change you a little bit, but his ability to teach organic chemistry is out of this world. I also took his 352 course btw

Dr. Castle is a good lecturer, but going to class is like drinking from a fire hose.  He also doesn't have patience for questions he thinks are too obvious.  That being said, I did learn a lot and I think he's overall a good teacher, the class is just inherently really difficult.  The final grade is pretty significantly curved.

Exams 84% of grade, 20 MC with FRQ. ACS Final scored raw out of 70 questions. 7~ pop quizzes but 5 graded and 1 replaced from online HW. He is a GREAT lecturer. Do practice questions, flash cards, etc. I feel like I know organic chemistry on a deeper level because of this class. It's not the easy way out, but you will be thankful in the long run.

OChem 2 is just straight-up tough no matter who you take it from, Dr Castle doesn't make it easier. Don't get behind, do the hw problems integrated in the reading sections after each lecture and you'll be prepared for every pop quiz. Exams, do all the after chapter book problems and practice each mechanism he does in class. great and fair teacher

Ochem is hard no matter who you take it from, but he makes it extra difficult. He has a passion for it, but do not be fooled by the good reviews. HIS CLASS IS WAY HARDER THAN ANY OTHER OCHEM TEACHER. DO NOT TAKE IT. I LOVED Ochem 1 from another professor, but HATED this clas.  Average on exams was 60s to 70s (though he curves the final grade).

Make of flashcard of everything he says in his lectures, read the chapters before the lectures, and do all of the homework. Class is very fast paced and you'll need to put in the work. His class prepares you for the ACS final. ACS was much easier than the prep book questions. Go to every lecture, he does go by the book but teaches new things too.

This class is hard but fair. He is really good at following the textbook (which is also really good), and although his lectures are really fast paced he explains things well. His tests are hard, but if you take detailed notes and go to his reviews (which are really good), you can do well. If you stay on top of reading and practicing you'll enjoy it

Castle is very straightforward in what you need to know. His lectures exactly follow the chronology of the textbook so it is very easy to prepare for the lectures. Pop quizzes aren't bad, he drops at least 1 and they are only a couple questions, just don't fall behind. Tests are hard, but no trick questions, just know your stuff. I learned a lot.

This is the worst professor at BYU. I have gotten all A's in my chemistry classes and I couldn't get a B in the class. He makes the tests impossible and his lectures are not that good. He will speed through his teaching, making you always feel behind. Even if you put in the work, it will tank your GPA.

This is the worst class I have ever taken. ABSOLUTELY DO NOT TAKE FROM CASTLE. The average on the exams were in the low 60's. He gives pop quizzes that the entire class does terribly on. I studied for over 40 hours for the first exam and got a 66. He is a smart guy but has no empathy for students and doesn't care about their grades.

He is by far one, if not the most difficult ochem professors at BYU. His tests are very difficult and test on small details-- the class average was usually around the 60% range. He seems to justify this by saying that he'll curve, but you end up going most of the semester without knowing what your grade will be. Wouldn't recommend.

Dr. Castle is really smart and his lectures are amazing. However, the averages on the tests are typically in the low 60s. He curves at the end of the semester but not enough to help the people that actually do well. It ends up helping people that don't. Their grade goes from a C- to a B+ from the curve. If you get an A-, you're stuck with that.

Ochem is really hard and Dr. Castle made it even harder. Dr. Castle is a very good lecturer but his tests are very hard and misleading. He is happy when the average is low. If you do take from him, do the reading, plan 4 hours a day for the class and study like there is no tomorrow. That is the only way I did well. 4 exams and a final. Good luck!

Dr. Castle is hands down the best professor I've had at BYU. Ochem is naturally hard, but his expectations for students are very clear, and his class is very well organized which makes it easy to succeed if you're willing to put the time in. Tests really aren't that bad if you're willing to put the time in to learn the material.

The overall rating for Dr. Castle is misleading. His lectures are actually pretty good, but his exams are brutal and unforgiving. They're not only difficult, but difficult to prepare for, as TA's don't know what will be on the exam, making their exam reviews unhelpful. Pray you don't get sick, as pop quizzes cannot be retaken or excused.

His teaching is superior! Yet he goes above what is required to know as a premed/dent. Thus, I would have preferred taking it from a different professor who might not teach ochem as well (you can always read the stellar textbook on your own) but that grades less harshly so that I could have succeeded (GPA wise) and still felt ready for the MCAT/DAT

Dr. Castle is brilliant and has very organized lectures but Ochem is just a really hard class. It's a good idea to take a lighter semester when you take this class because it will take a lot of your time. Most of your grade comes from your exams. Make sure to spend some time every day studying.

Dr. Castle knows his Ochem and is a great lecturer!  Ochem is super tough, but he explains it clearly.  Tests are all the same format except for the final which is the ACS exam.  He has a lot of extra credit and drops low quiz scores to help your grade (it does mostly come from the exams).

Insanely good professor for ochem. Loved how organized and available he was. Super knowledgeable and just a good guy. Obviously, the class is tough and requires steady effort, but tests were pretty chill as long as you know everything he teaches. Most people that don't like castle is more that they don't like the high expectations he holds.

Dr. Castle is smart and knows his stuff. If all of his students failed he would be happy. His tests are extremely hard and if you want to do well, I would suggest studying at least a week before. This class is basically a full time job if you want to do well. There are pop quizzes almost once a week so attendance is basically mandatory. Good luck.

4 exams + final (ACS worth 2x exams), pop quizzes total to 1/2 exam, extra credit available ~2% of final grade. Can only miss a few lectures if you don't want to fall behind. Tests are difficult, ~60% multiple choice ~40% short answer. Good lectures, do the homework it's "mandatory" for a good grade. A not guaranteed even if you work very hard.

Dr. Castle is the most organized professor I've ever had. He truly cared about his students and wants them to succeed. That being said, I have not had a class that has pushed me more than Ochem. To do well in this class you have to work your butt off and do every assignment that is given out. The HW is extra credit but it's the best way to practice

Get a study group, keep up with the textbook reading, write out all the things you need to memorize from memory. Dr. Castle teaches from the textbook; great lectures, but just going to class isn't going to give you the comprehension needed to do well on tests. Tests are everything.

ORGO is hard no matter who you take it from, but Dr. castle made it palatable. THERE is SO MUCH material to learn in organic chem 1 so you need to get ready to read ahead of class and start preparing for exams EARLY. Dr. castle is one of the better choices but his exams are difficult and I often felt like he made tricky questions that very few knew

Dr. Castle was amazing and very clear in his expectations of the class. He also laid out what our expectations should be. It was a hard class because there was so much reading and homework, but ultimately I feel like I learned so much from this class. It was worth it to take it from Castle.

Dr. Castle is the best OCHEM professor ever. He explains things so clearly and is a very fair professor. He is clear about what is expected in the class. It's a HARD class, but it is doable if you read the textbook and do ALL the homework. Tests are rough, but the final is easier. I loved this class, honestly.

While o-chem is all the difficulty it's cracked up to be, Dr Castle is a legendary and makes it totally possible to get an A (with about 2 hours of studying a day). My advice: take detailed class notes, do the homework problems over and over, and go to all the reviews. The tests aren't hard if you understand principles WELL.

Is this class incredibly difficult? Yes. Is it because of Dr. Castle? No. His class is very well organized, and sets you up for success. Dr. Castle may be a bit more unpopular because he is not a super outgoing guy, but as far as Ochem goes, he's a great professor. Do the reading, and have hope for a grade curve at the end (cutoff for A- about 88%)

Dr. Castle is a great professor. I sold my soul to this class and barely scraped by with an A-. He's really good about explaining difficult concepts but I still had to put in about 3 hours a day to understand what was going on. The tests are tricky but the final is pretty easy if you read the review book. Do the reading and hw or you're screwed.

Dr. Castle is the best professor I've had!! He gives you a syllabus that makes his expectations really clear. Homework is turned in at the end of the semester and its extra credit. Your grade is basically 4 tests and a final. Do the homework/reading and you'll do fine. BEST OCHEM PROFESSOR!! HE LOVES HIS STUDENTS. ALWAYS WILLING TO HELP.

Dr. Castle is great. I loved his lectures. He goes fast but that just how it is in ochem. His tests are hard so study but he sets you up very well. Live in the TA lab and get to know them and you will get good help. Castle is very understanding and reasonable. Also a surprisingly funny guy. Ochem was rough but it wasn't too miserable.

Professor Castle is a great professor. I have dropped OCHEM three times, and he was the professor that actually helped me finally figure it out. He is great at teaching difficult concepts, and overall he is a fair grader. He knows his stuff, and he seems to genuinely care for his students. I would recommend him for OCHEM over any other professor.
Best Organic Chemistry professor at BYU. If you don't take his class you are making a huge mistake.

OCHem is very hard! Dr. Castle is a walking text book. His lectures are very clear, lots of info but very clear what he is teaching. His class is very fair. Tests are hard but if you can find previous test that will help a lot, he tells you to do this.

Cannot respect this man enough, he tries to be really fair. He tells you what he expects on day one and it is up to you to do well and succeed. Lots of homework problems make good practice problems. Tests on material gone over in class and in the textbook. Learned a lot from his class, it is a hard class but worth it if you put time into it.

I love Dr Castle for how he taught OChem. This class could have been much more painful but he does a great job of making it clear and straightforward. If you study the book and do the homework you'll do great. He teaches almost exactly the textbook and it's refreshing. I hated his pop quizzes but they aren't a huge part of your grade.

This is a very tough class and you should plan on dedicating 30+ hours to it per week to get an A. The key to doing well on the tests is to find past years exams and take them as practice tests. My only complaint with the class is that Dr. Castle and some TA's can be condescending when they see that students struggle to conceptualize everything.

I did not have a good experience with this class. I had a small circumstance that the university asked him to work with me on and he wouldn't budge. The TA's mocked students as they graded exams and quizzes in the TA lab, and mine was consistently 20 min late to recitation disrespectful. No professionalism and Dr. Castle couldn't have cared less.

Dr. Castle is a very clear teacher. He has pop quizzes which are a pain to study for. He can have some pretty tricky questions on his tests. If you read everything in the book and do the extra credit homework, and sell your soul to the chemistry gods, then you should get an A.

This class is not for the faint of heart. Expect to study 15-20 hours for each test if you want to get an A or B. There are hardly any points that pad your grade; almost all points come from tests and pop quizzes. However, Dr. Castle is a great teacher, very approachable, and with very hard work an A is achievable.
One of the hardest classes at BYU. Expect it to be a full-time job just to study for it.

Castle is a walking talking textbook. That being said, expect to read through the entire textbook if you want to do well in the class. The textbook will cover things more thoroughly than Dr. Castle will during lecture. He teaches the material in the order they appear in the textbook. This class is very test heavy so expect to study hard for exams

If you take CHEM 351 from anyone but Dr. Castle at BYU, you're making a mistake. As a lector he meticulously covers the material in the manner he expects you to know it. He is also an editor of the textbook, so it 99% matches his lectures. The homework for the semester is optional, but the assigned problems cover every aspect of the exam material.

Castle is a really solid choice for 351. He is a human textbook, so all you have to do is understand what is going on in the text. Really good at answering questions, this guys is really smart. You will have to be fluent with OChem terminology to understand what is going on.

Dr. Castle is the BEST! OChem is hard no matter who you take it from, but Dr. Castle follows the book SO closely that he makes it very straight forward. He works hard to know student's names and is very fair. 7 pop quizzes (but only grades 5), homework is extra credit (but DO it), 4 tests + final, he curves the grades at the end of the semester.

Dr. Castle is amazing!! He gives you about 7 pop quizzes but only keeps 5 on your grade. He's by far the best Chemistry Professor that I've had at BYU. O chem is hard but Dr. Castle sets you up for a success. I feel like I learned more in this class in this semester than I have in any of my other classes combined.

He has been my favorite chemistry professor at BYU - no doubt! He is very well organized, he knows the material like the back of his hand. Students know exactly what he will be teaching the next day because he goes right through the book. His tests are not unreasonably long like my other chemistry classes. Homework is optional but really helps!

Great teacher, second semester ochem doesn't follow the book as closely though, he added several things the book oversimplified, but it is still your best friend for the class. Teaches very clearly, but a huge amount of material to cover.

Absolutely amazing professor, but the class is immensely difficult. I would say O-Chem 2 is more difficult than O-Chem 1, but they both are intense and severely time-drains. I really appreciate the devotion this guy has to be a great professor and care for his students. Eight months of Castle's O-Chem, and then the immense relief of being done.
Tough class. Tests are a little ambiguous and are usually pretty hard. Dr. Castle is a nice guy, willing to help, and very approachable, but the class is a beast.

Organic chemistry is super hard and not my strength at all. That said, if you have to take it, take it from Dr. Castle. He follows the book very well so the class is very structured and it's clear what you may be tested on. Both o-chem classes will eat your time like crazy, so plan on taking a lighter credit load if an A is really important to you.

He is a good professor. His lectures followed the book almost section for section. His tests were a little more difficult, but they were still easier than some other Chemistry classes. He has kind of a quirky sense of humor, but he is a cool guy.

Very nice and very reasonable professor. The class is difficult but he follow the book very closely to it brings structure. You really need to read and do some problems BEFORE the material he will teach that day. If you consistently do this and know the WHY behind the reactions you will be fine. He is very helpful if you don't understand.

The homework is optional extra credit, but do ALL of it. Dr. Castle is a great man, and I thoroughly enjoyed organic chemistry from him. Tests are intense, so prepare well. Take notes on what he is talking about before lecture starts you go over the material and you will remember the material better. Keep up with HW and notes and you'll do well

Lets be honest: o chem is the hardest class Ive ever taken. But I loved having Castle as my professor! He offers extra credit, has a few pop quizzes, and the rest of the grade comes from tests. The tests are hard, but I never felt like he was trying to be tricky. He was very fair! Lectures are good, he teaches up until the bell. Great teacher!

This class was hard, but if you read the book before lecture, do the homework, make flash cards, and practice, you should do fine. About 80% of your grade is tests/the final, so study well for those. There's a multiple choice and short answer section on all but the final, which is the ACS final anyway.

O chem 2 is a hard class. I've heard that Castle's tests are easier than the others but it's still pretty dang hard. His tests do have multiple choice and free response which is nice. Read the Textbook and do the homework problems to study. Also, go to his reviews, they help a ton.

This class in inherently difficult, but Dr. Castle explains things really well. He follows the book EXACTLY, so definitely use that as a resource. Homework isn't required, but you should really do it for the practice. Tests and quizzes are straight forward.

This class was incredibly difficult. If you fall behind on the reading, you can expect to do poorly. The homework is time consuming and sometimes it feels impossible to stay on top of. However, Castle is SUCH a sweet professor. It never feels like he is trying to make you fail like some of BYU's chem department.

Dr. Castle was a great teacher. He respects his students and his subject. He teaches clearly but sometimes flies through things super fast. He does offer some extra credit, but it isn't really worth a lot. Doing the homework isn't required but sure helps!

Dr. Castle was an amazing teacher, probably because he taught in line with my learning style. He writes everything on the board so you can't get behind, the whole class is very structured and laid out at the beginning of the semester, and he is very passionate about the subject. DO THE HOMEWORK, even though it is not required. It helps immensely.

Prof Castle is a jerk who doesn't treat his students with respect. He just likes to hear himself talk in front of the class and won't help students to actually learn. Even if you go in during his office hours and ask for help.

Awesome teacher. Clear, effective, and not trying to trick or demean you in any way. But Ochem is hard, my class averaged around a 64% on the midterms. But he is very willing to help you out during his office hours and all of his tests/quizzes follow the exact same dynamic so they are very predictable and easy to study for.

CASTLE IS SO BORING. You could not pay me to take this class again. I have gotten A's in all my science classes and I got a B- in this class. Unless you have a ton of time on your hands, there's no way you could remember all the material. After taking this class if anyone says the word "ochem" within 3 months I think I will punch them in the face.

Dr. Castle is extremely fair when it comes to tests. He is passionate about the subject, and he truly cares about his students. Super nice guy, super humble, very willing to help outside of class. Best class I've taken at BYU, hands down. If you read before class, do the homework before exams, and go to his reviews, you will get an excellent grade.

The other reviews are right--you really can't get an A without doing the optional homework. I hardly did any and wound up with a B. He uses every second of class to teach. If you don't do the homework everything he says will go right over your head after a couple of weeks. He is the best professor for this class, but o-chem is extremely difficult.

Organic chemistry is hard despite your teacher. Castle was great b/c his grading scheme is very organized and laid out from day one.  Im very thankful for his humor and respect for students even when we probably sounded real dumb. easy? no. The best help you have in a super hard class? YES! read before lectures, he follows the book to a tee!

Dr. Castle is awesome.  Very clear and systematic lectures, easy to understand.  Grading policies are fair, and offers extra credit for doing the homework.  DO ALL OF THE ASSIGNED HOMEWORK!  Test questions are often based off homework questions.  Exams are challenging, yet manageable.  Expect to put in several hours of study daily.

Great Professor.  The class is structured very well and he follows the book closely.  The key to getting an A is keeping up with the work and dong all your homework.  I thought his tests where challenging but fair.  This was honestly one of the best college classes I have ever taken. He also give extra credit which is a nice bonus!

Doctor Castle is literally the BEST professor that has ever lived. He is SO clear on what he asks you to do. If you want an A, then do the homework. DEAD SERIOUS, The homework prepares you so well for the tests that can expect an A if you do it. This class is a lot of work, I put in 3-4 hours a day and ended up with an A in both halves. Take Him!

Dr. Castle is awesome, the best you're gonna get for Chem 351. He is very clear in his lectures, and talks about everything that will be on the test. There are surprise quizzes throughout the semester to make sure you're caught up, but besides that it's zero homework!

He goes over the simplest reactions in class, tests you on the hardest ones, adds MORE to your material to study from than the textbook, and doesn't leave time for questions in class. Class always felt very rushed, but understandable when he did the simplest examples. I never felt class and homework were enough. Make sure you understand EVERYTHING.

Professor Castle may not be the most interesting in class to listen to, but he definitely provides opportunities to listen to you outside of class. He is a pretty shy guy, but is more than willing to help you if you proactively approach him. When he is in a one on one environment he is much better at explaining concepts.

Was not clear on many topics. The quizzes and tests you take have somewhat vague questions making it difficult to understand and answer. The examples that we do in class are very rudimentary and do not help with the homework whatsoever. Not a great experience.

Very good teacher. I loved doing the exploratory labs, they were fun and educational. He gives exam reviews, and so does the TA. The tests can be tough, but I suggest reading the chapter BEFORE class, taking good notes in class, reviewing the notes and book, then doing the hw and quizzes. Time consuming, but effective. Daily iClicker quizzes
Really wants to see students succeed.  Clear on his expectations for the class and does all can to help students do well on his tests.  Going to his review are very helpful before the tests.

Castle is a really great professor, and I recommend him.  He follows right along with the textbook so there are no surprises.  His tests are multiple choice and free response and are much fairer than Petersen's who I had for 351.

I had him for both ochem classes and I would highly recommend him. His teaching correlates highly with the textbook, so if something is unclear, the textbook can fill you in. (And you will be best friends with the textbook for these classes)

Dr. Castle is an awesome professor. He is always willing to explain things to you after class or during office hours. He moves pretty quickly, but the class is very well organized. Tests are challenging, but very do-able if you do all the homework. Wouldn't take that class from anyone else!

This guy is amazing. I can't imagine taking OChem from anyone else. I thought his lectures were great (others think he's dry). A few pop quizzes given throughout the semester at beginning of class, so make sure you attend AND stay on top of the material. Tests fairly, although you'll only do well if you do the homework. Take this class from Castle!

I've never had a professor I like better than Dr. Castle. Very approachable, very helpful to students, very down-to-earth. (We had a review during BYU's NCAA tournament game...right after the review he wanted to know the score and how much time was left haha). Best professor to take O-Chem from if you'll put in the work to learn.

If you have to take O-Chem at BYU, I highly recommend Castle.  HIs lectures are clear and comprehensible.  The homework may not be worth much, but it does prepare you for the tests - so do it!  His tests are part multiple choice, part free response.  The final was standardized.  Attending recitation for this class is a very good idea!

Overall decent, as good as the other professors. Very kind, good guy. Wasn't engaged by his lecture style- tends to have his face in the notes or toward the board and recites longs lists of principles. Test 1 is WAY easier than the others- beware.O Chem is the weeder class for all of BYU's MANY med/dent, so competition is rough, don't screw it up.

Be prepared to work. Homework is a tiny part of your grade, but do it if you want to do well on tests. Book is great. Tests are very fair. In class quizzes (7 given randomly during the semester at the beginning of class) can be difficult if you don't keep up on the material. OChem is hard, but Castle is awesome at teaching it. Totally recommended
Dr. Castle is the bomb! Extremely clear, fair, and though I don't like O chem, he made it a good experience. Take it from him.

Dr. Castle does a great job!  You understand exactly what he expects and he teaches with a lot of clarity.  He also doesn't try to trick you on tests (not to say that they are easy).  He has my recommendation any day!

Dr. Castle is the man to take O-Chem from. He learns students' names, has a nerdy sense of humor that keeps things fun, and really tries to help individually. Tests are  challenging but not tricky. If you do HW (there's a lot...be warned) you'll be in really good shape.

he is a great teacher. he is very helpful during his TA hours and is very interested in his students. during class he fuequently answers question by name showing he knows his students. he gives random quizes to make sure you go to class so be sure to do so. his class is difficult but organic chemistry is difficult in general, so hes worth it.
Dr. Castle is a great professor. Doesn't waste any time and tells you exactly what you need to know. Teaches very clearly. Tests are extremely fair and manageable--just do the homework.
Ochem is a hard class. Castle is good at explaining things, and if you do the homework you should be fine on the tests. If I didn't do the homework, I probably would have failed.
awesome teacher... like this guy

I thought Dr. Castle did a great job teaching the class in a way that students didn't get confused. I went on to TA for a different teacher, who made it way harder by skipping around. If you read the book and do the problems he assigns then you will do great on the tests.

I wish someone else taught 351M and 352M. Dr Castle is awful. Don't expect to get any help from him during office hours. He's very cold. Going to class is very important if you want to pass and the only way to get by is to go to all the recitations given by the TA. I liked OChem before and after I took this class with Dr. Campbell;he makes it awful

Dr. Castle is a great teacher.  Chemistry is the toughest subject in the school and yes this class is hard.  But he loves the subject, explains it well, is always willing to give his time and his tests actually demonstrate understanding, though really dumb kids will say otherwise.  Overall, I learned a lot and would recommend him for this class

Dr. Castle made the class harder than necessary.  He taught solely out of the textbook, which made the class more difficult.  Going to class was not mandatory, but you should plan on attending if you want to pass.  Dr. Castle is one of those people who is very comfortable in the lab, however, he's not a very good teacher.

I really enjoyed this class and thought that Dr. Castle did a great job at teaching the subject and making it easy to understand.  Tests are challenging, but if you review all of the homework problems you will be fine.  I definitely recommend him.  He is very approachable.
Excellent, and wonderful hair
Dr. Castle is awesome.
Very nice, very fair, grades tests fairly easy

Dr. Castle was very nice and he is easy to approach. His class however was very tough I mean O-chem is tough as it is but he uses an open format test that was much tougher for me than Dr. Petersons multiple guess.some how the class average on the tests stayed at mid 60's while mine dropped to the mid forties.

I hate O-Chem!!!!!!!!!!!  It is the worst ever!  I'm so glad it's over.  Dr. Castle was alright, it was just the drab, dull subject manner.  I hated this class.  I also thought that Dr. Robinson was a better teacher.

Great professor. You need to keep up on the reading, because you can do well on the tests and still do poor in the class because of the quizes. The subject was difficult but Dr Castle made it a little more palpable.
Great teacher!  He explains the concepts very well, the tests are hard but well reflective of the material taught in class, and he's pretty reasonable. I would definitely recommend Castle for O-chem

One of the top 2 prof. I've ever had. He cares so much for each one of his students and is such a Christlike man. He is always looking for ways he can improve his teaching - even lecture to lecture. He shares really cool applications of the material. It's helpful if you've taken Diff Eq already. Don't hesitate to go to his office hours for anything
honestly just a really good guy

Dr Charles is very kind, and knows a lot about numerical methods and statistics. The homework load during spring term felt fine, though the labs can take a long time. The reading quizzes are closed book and pretty specific, but my grade ended up fine. Dr Charles shares lots of applications, so you feel like it is useful and it makes it fun.

Dr. Charles is excellent at explaining things so they intuitively make sense. He is very aware of his students and is willing to change HW and due dates based on feedback to make sure that the class is tailored to the needs of the students. I cannot recommend him enough. Even though attendance wasn't mandatory, there are a few in-class quizzes.

His teaching style is very helpful for students. He doesn't often assume that the class has a mastery over a subject even after explaining so he is very flexible with students. His tests blind sided me with the difficulty. Additionally he has a tendency to have a conference before every exam except the final and would be absent from office hours.

I wish Dr Charles would teach all the ME classes! Very kind and caring, excited about the topics, gives great hands-on examples/demos every lecture. Very MATLAB heavy class, but he is fair in grading and workload. Tests are tough but fair. Very willing to help outside class. Open-ended project that we presented at the end of the semester was fun!

Professor Charles truly cares about his students. I loved the layout of the class and he did a great job explaining the material in a clear way. One of my favorite classes I've taken at BYU so far. The tests were quite tough, but he was a fair grader and graded the tests on a curve.

I took ME 273 From Prof. Charles. He is an amazing professor and does a great job explaining the material. He is super understanding and will help you himself if something is not making sense. Definitely take him if you can

Dr. Charles is super kind and caring. He is a smart guy, which sometimes makes it a bit confusing to learn from him in an entry level class like this. He is a good teacher though. Tests and homework are hard. it was a little frustrating when he specifically made tests more challenging so that his class average would meet university specifications.
Best professor in the program. One of the hardest classes in the program content wise - the class itself is not a ton of work, but is conceptually super difficult. Great professor though.
Dr. Charles is an outstanding teacher! He is good at explaining things in ways that make sense.
All tests were open note and book in order to simulate real work environment. I liked the organization of the class and it was well organized.

Great teacher, very clear, kind, and respectful. You read from the textbook, do homework from the textbook, and he helps explains concepts found in it, so you need it. The tests are hard, so study previous homeworks and the textbook to prepare you well.

Possibly the most clear teacher I've had in an engineering class. Everything that I struggled with in prereqs that I should've understood before this class made sense in the single day of lecture when he would review the old stuff. And obviously the clarity continued with the new material too
Loved learning from Dr. Charles! He really cares about his students and does everything he can to help them succeed. I'd take every class from him if I could!

Dr. Charles is one of the best teachers at BYU. He doesn't just read his lecture slides but works to help students understand material. He adapts the class regularly to the needs of the students. Reading is essential because lectures supplement the readings, not review. Homework is doable. 4 hours a week. Tests are challenging but not outrageous.

Dr. Charles is such a kind and caring man. Of course the course was hard because it is a graduate level course, but Dr. Charles does everything possible to make the class doable and even enjoyable. He is constantly bringing demonstrations and models to help explain difficult concepts. The homework was mostly MATLAB but he gave lots of help with it.

Best professor I have had at BYU. He genuinely cares about all his students, and is super humble. Grades fairly. He is super smart, funny, and his enthusiasm and curiosity is contagious- he makes cool little machines to demonstrate principles. Classes are way fun. Ive taken three classes him, and hope to take more if I can.

Professor Charles is very caring and good at explaining concepts in a clear and concise way. The class is structured very clearly and fairly. He has required readings, but honestly this is both helpful for learning and an easy grade boost.

A champ. Mechatronics can be very time-consuming, but is one of the coolest classes out there. Dr. Charles is very helpful, kind, and explains things well. He's brilliant, but humble. He also talked about similarities between neuromechanics and mechatronic systems, which was very interesting.

Is always willing to hear what you have to say and will give you back points is you were able to prove that you really knew the material. His tests are open note and open book but are tricky and make you build off of what you know. His stutter is small and not a problem and is, in fact, one of the clearest teachers I've ever taken. Really good

Dr. Charles is a great teacher. He tends to write on the board and lays out the concepts in tables and examples. He is soft-spoken but confident, respectful of students questions/comments. He has you read 30 min in the text book for each class period. He does pop quizzes which he may or may not tell you about ahead of time. I would take him again.

If you don't know much about social impact, then this is a worthwhile class. If you've already taken classes in departments like International Development, you'll probably be bored. Very soft-spoken and thoughtful guy. Assignments took time but were reasonable

This class is just straight lectures from the coolest people you will ever meet. If you want to learn from social impact leaders including nonprofits, for-profits, government entities and more this is the place. Best 1 credit I have taken at BYU for my future career and self development.
Professor Fox is awesome! He is very passionate about the Global and Community Impact. And he really wants to hear from his students and stands up for them to be heard.

This was the pt class to finish up my business minor. It met only on Wednesdays, and all outside of class work could be done on Wednesday. Lecture each week consists of guest speakers who all work in a social impact field. Very inspiring stuff. Low effort, high reward. Online and open note exams but attendance and pre-class assignments affect grade

Loved this class! I learned so much about what I can do in social impact without working at a non-profit. Even if you don't want to work in social impact, these are inspring lectures. There is a midterm and final but they are open notes so just take good notes on everything that the person says and you'll do fine.

This is an awesome lecture series. I came away from each lecture feeling so inspired and grateful. Attendance is obviously mandatory, but there is plenty of extra credit assignments if you miss a lecture

This lecture series is extremely well-run. Steven is so kind and caring and really connects with the lecturers and makes the class so engaging and fun to be in. You won't regret taking this, or any other class for that matter, from him!

This was a 1-credit lecture series in which social impact pros from all sectors were invited to speak on their experiences. Prof. Fox facilitated these speeches with Q&A and pre-class prep assignments. Prof. Fox is congenial, professional, and caring. It's a big class but he'll get to know you if you introduce yourself. Def a class worth taking.
Great Professor. He helps students a lot if you care about Marketing, and he'll help you understand it really well. His lectures and assignments are great.

Many group presentations throughout the semester, but its not graded. It is hard to sit through, but worth it in the end. If you don't mind the commute to salt lake, I would 1000% recommend. Attendance is required, but homework is super easy. 3 projects instead of midterm and final. He tells you to use AI to make them.

Professor Wiest's Marketing 201 class was one of the best courses I've ever taken. The projects and real-world applications made the material engaging, practical, and incredibly valuable. He was also an outstanding mentor who genuinely supported students and pushed us to grow. I learned an immense amount from this class.

Cannot stress enough how worth it it is to go to SLC to take marketing 201! Prof Wiest and Prof Christensen are some of the funniest guys ever. They don't really believe in the traditional school system, so their tests are just projects and they have barely any graded work. Despite that, they are SO knowledgeable and you learn a ton every time.

Took in SLC. You can miss 2 classes before grade dropped half a letter grade. There are a ton of students take the Front Runner up so it's a party. There is a online textbook that you read for the weekly quizzes (about 5-10 questions) but I didn't buy it and got 100% on most of them. There are no test, just projects for a completion grade.
He teaches very clearly and direct and prepares one for real world situations.

If you're needing to take MKTG 201, it is so worth it to take it in Salt Lake. Steve Wiest and Jerry Christensen co-teach this class and it is the best class ever. The work load is super light, they are hilarious teaching together, and compared to the course in BYU, it is 10x easier. You won't regret taking it with them.

I actually took UNIV101 with Dr. Hoffman. Dr. Hoffman is a super nice guy and genuinely wants his students to succeed in this class. However, he is definitely still getting used to the class and is pretty disorganized at the moment. He tends to grade in a weird way, usually grading everything right before the end of the semester. Be friends with PM

You have to do 20 hours of service for your final and a group project. Brother Hoffman didn't allow in-class time to work on your group project so good luck coordinating with your group on time. Grading was lax and so were the lectures. He said attendance was mandatory but forgot to take it more than half the time. Great guy though!

Easy A, be prepared to read so many confrence talks it almost felt like a relgion class. Had a mid semester eval and many students said they would like readings more aligned with social work (this is a social work class) but he said he would not change because confrence has the best lessons for social workers. TA was also very hard to work with.

SUPER EASY CLASS. You only have 1 class period a week, not 2. 2-3 short assignments every week. Lectures are relatively engaging, but pretty basic (hardcore INTRO class). Brother Hoffman himself is super funny, sincere, and caring. Only had positive experiences with him.

Professor Hoffman is super chill. It almost got to the point where it was a bit TOO chill in class, and there was a lot of busy work. I don't know how much I learned about the field of social work, but we did learn a lot about being a good person I guess you could say. Also, you have to be in class. And the final is a group project. EASY class.

Professor Hoffman is a great person, not the greatest teacher, but you do learn a lot. The start of the semester, you do a bit of homework, but it gets less and easier. He does not always have a set plan of what to teach, so he asks us what we want to learn about, and we have a discussion about that. Oh and btw, no tests! Take this class.

No tests. Attendance is mandatory, so don't think about getting sick. Professor Hoffman is nice, but I didn't learn anything because he doesn't teach. It's a waste of your tuition, and I do not recommend learning about social work from him. If you need an easy A, take it, but you'll have to go to class and read a lot of conference talks every week.

This class didn't teach us about social work. He assigns GC talks each week and asks you to write papers on them. When people ask him questions in class, he literally says, "I don't know. That's for you to figure out." His lectures are also boring since he doesn't know his material well. If I could go back in time, I wouldn't take this class.

I am in the class rn & I was so excited to LEARN about SW but this is a waste of time. Attendance is mandatory but lectures are awful. He jokes for 40 mins & then gives a lot of busy work "to teach yourself." If you want an easy class to sit through and do blind assignments (that take 3 hours a week) take it, but if you want to learn about SW don't
Prof Hoffman was nice I just don't think he knew his material.

I took intro into social works with him and so the material was not suppose to be challenging but simply educational, which it was. This class was also a hybrid class so half online and half in person. Overall, Brother Hoffman was great! He is an amazing teacher to work with and to learn from. I highly recommend taking a class from him!

Super easy class. He literally said on the first day that everyone can have an A if they want. Weekly readings with a writeup (half the time I didn't even read the chapter), 2 short papers, one group project. I spent maybe 1.5 hours a week on this class. Lectures were sometimes boring but overall I got the feel for the profession.

Literally so easy. You had to show up, but you definitely didnt have to pay attention. There were a few papers, some group presentations, some individual (two minute max) presentations, 20 hours of volunteer work, and the best part? No tests. He wants you to get what you want out of the course as you explore social work. I loved this class so much.
Class discussions were a delight. Brother hoffman is new to BYU but he is definitely a positive addition to the faculty. I learned tons and the workload was managable

Best math teacher I've ever had. He explains everything intuitively so you never have to memorize anything. He makes his midterms very managable, not nearly as hard as homeworks. Class average on the department final was 10% higher than the other clases. Take 113 from him!

Awesome professor! This class specifically has a really small class size, so a lot of full class participation and talking with classmates. There is a NCTM book required, but it's not expensive. Attendance is required, and you really do need to go to learn what he's teaching, but I understand stats so much better after this class!

Dr. Jones is amazing! I wish I could follow him around and take every class from him. He understands how students think and what they need, so all of his lectures always revolve around some intellectual need or question that he proposes to the class, and then helps students learn to reason through the answers themselves.  Makeseasy to understand

Dr Jones is frankly one of the best professors I have had the chance to rub shoulders with! He teaches very effectively, very concisely, and always takes care to answers questions in full, or come back to them another day if there isn't time. Very kind guy, and spiritual too! Please choose him if you are worried about math 113!

Failed the first time I took it (from a different prof), but Dr. Jones is amazing! In lectures, he prioritizes nailing the conceptual fundamentals of the topics you discuss, setting you up to tackle the hw probs even though they're more complex than the ones he walks thru in class. He wrote his own (easier) tests instead of using the department's.

Look, it's calc, it's hard. This guy is VERY good at his job and is light years better than other calc professors. My class tested over 10% higher in the final because of his expertise. Take it from him, even if you have to do the M-F schedule. He is easily your best bet.

I always felt he taught in a way that added very seamlessly to things he'd previously taught. His area of research is literally how to teach calculus so he knows how to teach and does it extremely well. I felt that he prepared us well for the tests and I was never blindsided. If you only miss three or less weekdays and one Friday you can get 2 EC.

Incredibly easy intro course to let students know what the Math Education major is all about. It was very interesting and they brought in a different faculty member from the Math Ed department each week. Dr. Jones is very nice.

This is an introduction class, so it is not difficult at all. It was really helpful though to be able to get a taste of what a major in mathematics would look like. There's just a reflection after each class and it's only a term long. Highly recommend if you're thinking about this major!

Look its calculus, its going to be hard. I failed the AP Calc AB test but Dr. Jones really understands how to teach this course. He prefaces units with real world scenarios that are easy to grasp. I had him every day of the week for 50 min and it was good to keep concepts fresh. 3 midterms and a final with online/written hw. Take it with him.

Dr. Jones is the best! I've never been great at math and had a hard time understanding Calc 1, but Dr. Jones explains everything so nicely that it all makes sense! Do not take this class from anyone but Dr. Jones.

This class is hard. You are probably here because you ~need~ to take calc 2 for your major. DO NOT make it harder than it needs to be. Pick Dr. Jones. He will actually prepare you for the tests. He does not make you memorize stuff (there is too much to memorize) but instead teaches you how to THINK in order to work things out on the test. Very fair

Dr. Jones is a phenomenal teacher!  He isn't in a rush to shove info down your throat, but rather he is interested in seeing his students learn and absorb the content. It's not memorizing the hundreds of formulas but understanding them. Make sure to go to the TA's office hours and get help, its a game changer! Dr. Jones will help you love Calculus!

Dr. Jones is an amazing professor. He has a clear teaching style, and the TAs are going to be the best resource for help. MATH 113 is a dense class, fast paced, and challenging. My advice to anyone looking at this class is: only take this class if you absolutely have to. If you have to, take it from Dr. Jones. You will have to work very hard.

Dr Jones was awesome. Calc 2 has the reputation of being one of the hardest classes that you can take, but Dr. Jones explained things in such a way that the material didn't even seem that hard. He also explained the why of things, so you understood the formulas and knew when to use them instead of just memorizing them all.

Dr. Jones was awesome. His speciality is explaining things beyond just like this is what you have to do for the "test". So if you want someone to "put the fries in the bag" I would recommend someone else. But overall, if you work hard and attend lecture you can succeed. I highly recommend going to office hours with him and the TAs (they carried).
Dr Jones is great, I love how ever day he has a new button up shirt!

Dr. Jones' MATH113 class is challenging but manageable. Homework and exams require a good grasp of concepts, but his lectures and available TAs make it doable. Unstuckstudy was a huge help for prepping. Attendance is a must - just stay engaged and you'll do well.

Dr. Jones was the best! He was incredible at explaining concepts and taught incredibly well. Calc II is a tough class, but he made it enjoyable and I looked forward to his lectures. Take Math 113 from Jones if you can!

Dr. Jones did a great job focusing on learning over grades and memorization. I understood what we covered in this class much better than other math classes. I didn't love the smaller sections, but attendance is graded. Only two homework assignments a week, so not too bad. The tests were hard, but each one had multiple review sessions that helped.

Dr. Jones really cared that we knew why we were learning the material. He would often explain using real world examples and had such a clear way of teaching. I almost never got confused when he explained things and he would not move on until everyone understood the topic. He also is pretty funny.
He comes from the MathEd department and it showed. He was an awesome teacher and really focused on us learning the content to remember it and not just to memorize things. He was on our team.

Professor Jones teaches through concepts and intuition rather than memorizing formulas. I struggled with most prior math classes, but he explains where things come from and why it works. Best math teacher I've ever had. Content is difficult, and there's a lot of homework problems. Still, would 10/10 recommend. He is very caring and willing to help.

This is the best professor I have EVER had. The class was so fun and I never wanted the semester to end because of him. He has the classes set up really nicely. The TA's are really helpful and friendly. Please take any class he has to offer because he will help you succeed.

Professor Jones himself is an amazing professor and a great lecturer. My least favorite thing is that TAs teach the small group recitations twice a week, and they not only have to review and do examples, but they introduce new subjects, and they aren't always the best at it. Roughly 6 hours a week in homework, no late work, 3 exams and a final.

The class was not hard, but the grades were so depended on the exams that even if you do well on the homework, the exams will kick you hard. He did not explain things super well and often left the TAs to do most of the explaining.

Steve does his own thing, which works for some, but if it doesn't suit you, good luck. The homework assignments were on a different level from what was taught. I would go to the Math Lab for help, and the very smart students who work there and have taken 314 before would get confused by his homework questions and agree that they are ridiculous.

I can see why many students enjoy Dr. Jones.  However, just be aware that he teaches calculus VERY differently from anyone else, to the point that Math Lab reviews aren't very coherent with what we were taught.  It is also difficult to talk with him outside of class.  It just feels very isolated from everyone else and wasn't enjoyable for me.

You won't find a better instructor at BYU.  He has homework due every day before lecture, 3 midterms, and the grades are weighted heavily on the midterms and final exam.  Sacrifices traditional teaching material in order to take more time demonstrating how to recognize problems in the real world and understand the concepts on a deeper level.
Fantastic. Previously failed calculus, but Dr Jones made calc so much easier. He is the best, only take calculus from him!!!!

Professor Jones is a really smart guy who also knows how to teach. Calc 2 is a difficult class but he makes it much easier. I took this class fall 2023 and did well. Homework was about 4 hours a week plus studying for tests. Attendance was mandatory for both the class and the lab. Great math professor though. Would highly recommend!
Homework and tests are way harder than anything taught in class. Lectures are not clear, he is not that good at teaching.

Many people loved Dr. Jones but I was not a fan. His lectures were not clear and covered very little. The homework was way harder than anything we learned in class. Pray that you have a good TA because mine was the reason I passed. Dr. Jones would constantly brag about making his own tests that were hard and didn't prepare you for the final.

Jones teaches by building on past concepts and always answers questions. You get graded on attendance-- it won't destroy your grade if you don't show up, but it can lower your grade by 3ish points. Beware, new material is taught in the small groups by TAs, not Jones. Use the math lab/TA hours. Tests are hard but no surprise material. HW heavy!

Dr. Jones has an incredible talent for teaching. His MATH 113 class is absolutely the best way to learn Calculus 2. There was a significant amount of hw as expected from a four-credit class, but his lectures made everything clear and his T.A.s were accessible and kind.

Dr. Jones was very clear in his lectures and he made the content easy to understand. Homework was helpful for tests, rely on reasoning rather than memorizing. Tests weren't to challenging but weren't easy either. Attendance is required for recitations and big lecture. Overall, 10/10 would recommend.

Dr. Jones is an incredible teacher. He lets us derive the formulas by ourselves so that we conceptually understand them. One of my favorite parts of every class is when he tells us, take a few seconds with the person next to you and think about what this would be. He gives us so many opportunities to engage with the material, even in his lectures.

Probably the best math teacher I've had. The HWs are very representative of the class. 4 credit class so you'll have it every day and have HWs due 2x a week generally. Don't start them the night before and you'll be fine. The talmage math lab was super helpful. You get points for attendance in lecture and lab.
It is an easy class and its great for figuring out if you want to do Math Education. It also helps you understand the process for the MATHED major.

Lots of professors know a lot of math, but Dr Jones can actually teach math. He explains abstract ideas so they are easy to understand. He teaches a lecture hall, but interacts with students in a personal way, and he engages the whole class. Starts every lecture with a prayer. If you're afraid of calculus, take Dr Jones -- he will make it easy!
Great professor. Difficult subject matter but he taught well so you could learn it. Hard class but enjoyable.
Great professor! Helped me understand Calc 2 thoroughly.

Dr. Jones is awesome! Calc 2 isn't necessarily easy, but he is great at explaining the intuition behind the math which is so much more helpful than memorizing a formula just to "plug and chug." I'd switch to a Math major if Dr. Jones taught every one of my classes!!

I learned to love math through Professor Jones. Calculus is hard, but his lectures made it easy to understand. I really felt like I understood the concepts he taught. Amazing professor and best math teacher I have ever had.
Literally the best professor ever. Super good at explaining how to work through problems, etc. Also pretty fun and engaging. If you have the chance, take your class from Dr. Jones.

Professor Jones is incredible! His was the first math class I had taken in three and a half years and yet thanks to his teaching I understood everything very well. He teaches in such a way that the students really comprehend the concepts of the class, instead of just "learning math." He is caring and extremely respectful. Take his class if you can!

You must take classes from Dr. Jones. I guarantee that there is no other professor at BYU that teaches math more methodically and clearly. I wish he could teach every single one of my classes because he doesn't just write things on the board and expect you to understand, he explains things in a way that anyone can understand and apply.

MATH 113 is not an easy class, but Dr. Jones is an amazing professor and definitely made the class enjoyable! He really wants you to succeed and understand the material. People say that the class is too hard, but I got an A relatively easy. Just study, do the assigned work, ask questions, and you'll do great!

Dr. Jones is probably one of THE best math professors I have ever had the pleasure of taking a class from. He made sure we understood the material, unlike other teachers I have had that simply regurgitated formulas and such. There is some busywork, but it never takes too long. Highly recommend for amazing lectures and caring personality.
I wouldn't say I like Math. Dr. Jones made it bearable.

Limited attempts on WebAssign. Writes his own steeply graded tests (17% each!). Doesn't give you practice problems outside of homework questions on his useless study guides. Spends way too long in class cyclically rambling with filler and over-explaining stupid low-level ideas, so he runs out of time to cover material that he just hands off to TAs.

Decent amount of work, but tests and homework are fair, and he tells you what to study. He's very adamant about understanding the concept rather than just trying to memorize (which is honestly way better). There are daily attendance quizzes so you do have to show up, but they count towards extra credit so it's worth it. The textbook is online.

The class is hard, but Dr. Jones makes everything easy to remember with his philosophy of teaching how everything works rather than just memorizing it. It was definitely harder with how he taught, but in the long run it is so much more worth it to have taken MATH113 from him.

Dr. Jones definitely emphasizes understanding over memorization. He does go rather fast in the class. The tests are hard, but fair. You can use a testing center calculator on all but the final, and there's no time limit. The homework is a mix of online, written, and small projects.

Best option for calc 2. Explained things well, everything was relatively easy. You'll do well if you do the HW (about 4-8 hours a week not including lectures or tests) direct points curve makes a A pretty easy (I got an 102 in the class lol) He teaches really well and he ignores stupid stuff other math professors might take off for

Dr. Jones does a really good job at explaining concepts instead of memorization. He builds his lectures around anticipated questions and really encourages student discussion. I understood this class better than past math classes and got a better grade. My only complaint is he doesn't post any past tests, but they are fair tests, not tricky.

DR JONES IS THE BEST MATH PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD AT BYU. I want him to teach all the other math professors how to teach! The course is well organized, deliberately planned, and each lecture is like going on a flipping journey to understand math more deeply and intuitively. Don't take 314 if you can't take it from Dr Jones!

Dr. Jones is an incredible professor. Calc 2 is very hard but he does a great job of teaching for understanding. If you have to take Calc 2 I would highly recommend him. You have to study hard and do well on the Homework. There is no grade except for homework and tests, so the homework actually matters. Do all the homework and study hard.

Dr. Jones was so amazing to take Calc 2 from. He explains things so clearly and doesn't encourage just memorizing formulas. Homework was due most Tuesdays and Thursdays. Tests weren't too bad. He lets you use a scientific calculator on unit tests.

Dr. Jones is probably the best math teacher I've ever had. He is good at teaching his students to use reason to solve problems instead of just telling you to memorize something. The tests and homework can be tricky, but they reflect the material taught in class and are graded fairly. He's also a really nice guybut don't skip class or lab, ever!

Dr. Jones is a great calculus professor. He can explain the topic clearly while making sure to answer students questions. Attending lectures is a must, as there are quizzes at the start of every class about the contents of the last lecture, but they aren't difficult or meant to trip you up. The homework from the textbook can be very tricky.

Dr. Jones is the best calc professor out there (I had him for 113 as well). He's in the math ed department, and he literally studies what it means for students to understand derivatives and stuff. He teaches conceptually, and tests and homework reflect that and are absolutely fair. Focus on being able to recreate formulas rather than memorize
Best professor I've had at BYU. This guy teaches so well. His tests are super fair.

Of all my calculus classes, I definitely feel like I have learned the most from Professor Jones. He explains the concepts conceptually and then his homework and exams reflect that. Redo the homework to prepare for exams and follow his study guides. A great teacher who cares about his students! And the homework was very manageable.

I liked Dr. Jones a lot, but I didnt feel that the rest of the reviews on here adequately outlined his weaknesses. He is mysterious about what is on the tests (no practice exams), but if you re-work the homework its an easy A. I also didnt like how he tried to explain things that left many more confused, rather than just telling us how to do it.

Best math professor ever. Such a kind, caring man, and has a true gift for teaching math. Anyone could understand his lectures. He teaches so that you never forget it. The homework he assigns is really helpful and interesting too. Don't plan on relying on the textbook much in this class. His lectures are all you need to understand the material.

Dr Jones is seriously such a great guy through and through. Considering how many students are in the lecture, it's amazing how he really does care about each student. He explains conceptually insane concepts in a way that is as understandable as possible, and is always encouraging and uplifting. I highly recommend taking his class.

If you need to take calculus, take it from this guy. He literally studies how to teach calculus for a living, so he is AMAZING! His tests are difficult, but fair and really does want to help you succeed. The TA's are amazing as well.

Dr. Jones is a really great guy. You can tell he really cares about his students. I really enjoyed how he explains everything using reasoning, and he asks his students not to memorize anything. He has a great way of teaching. His tests aren't extremely difficult, as long as you do the homework you should be prepared.

Dr. Jones is one of the best teachers I have had. He does a fantastic job of explaining things and making the concepts easy to understand. He strongly discourages memorization, which is totally not necessary in his class because he teaches for understanding, not for regurgitation on a test. If you can take a math class from him, do it!

Dr. Jones is one of the best math professors for sure. He takes complex ideas and makes them simple. He helps you think through the problems rather than memorize. I highly recommend that you take Math 113 with Dr. Jones.

Not much effort was put into helping students prepare for tests. He didn't hold review sessions or post past tests online (he writes his own tests) but just says to reviews class notes and hw. He also rambles in class about things that do not relate to the tests a lot. If you are someone who enjoys math he might be good for you otherwise don't.

Dr. Jones is one of the best professors I've had at BYU. Seriously if you have the chance take whatever class from him. He's a math education professor and the difference really shows. He made a tough class do-able and I hadn't taken math for three years. He's SO GOOD! I didn't even read the book because lectures were all I needed to understand

Dr. Jones does a really good job teaching this class. Some of the concepts are pretty confusing, but he really knows how to teach it well. Everyone I've ever talked to has said he's the best math 113 professor, and I can't disagree with them.

Steven Jones is among the best professors at BYU. His degree in Math Education set him apart from the others. He KNOWS how to teach math.
