I took multivariable calculus from him and eventually stopped reading the book because he give a better explanation. Do not miss class or you will miss the opportunity to truly understand.

Dr. Jones is by far the best professor at BYU. His ability to make complicated concepts so simple and easy to understand is amazing. No wonder he is a Math EDUCATION professor. So his career is TEACHING math not DOING math. And his TAs? Grad students studying Math EDUCATION. You will not be disappointed taking Calculus from Dr. Jones.

WAY solid professor! He answers everyone's questions in class very clearly. The TA's do recitation and they are all grad students. His class did so well on the department final that everyone's overall grades in the class got boosted 5%. His class also did 15% better on the final than average. Very clear and simple teaching. I learned so much!!!

I would highly recommend taking this class from Professor Jones! His lectures were amazing and you can really tell that he cares that his students actually learn and don't stress themselves out too much. He and his great TA's helped us all learn so well that his sections averaged almost 10% higher on the final exam than the overall BYU average!

Dr. Jones is an excellent professor, and he really knows what he's doing. That alone doesn't make him a good professor, but luckily that's not everything he brings to class. He teaches well and clearly, and makes certain to not place too much of an emphasis on grades (despite this being a very important class, if you're taking it). Best I've had!

Dr. Jones is hands down the best professor I have had at BYU. Math 113 is a rigorous class, but Dr. Jones taught it so well that it was one of my lower-stress classes this semester. He's even better at teaching physics stuff than the physics professors. Really cares about students and about learning more than tests and grades. Take from Dr. Jones!

Hands-down, Dr. Jones is the best math professor at BYU. His PhD in Math Education (instead of Math) REALLY shines through, as does his own ongoing research on how students best learn higher math (esp calculus). His teaching is refreshingly accessible and personable. There's no required reading, and he's very willing to help students outside class

Such. A. Gem. Seriously, I can't understate how glad I am to have had Dr. Jones for MATH113. You can get up to 2% EC if you correctly answer all the pre-class quizzes. Take good notes in lecture as many test questions are based off of in-class examples. His TAs all rock, too! I truly fell in love with calculus this semester!

Dr. Jones is hands down the best math professor I've ever had. There is a HUGE difference between a regular Math professor and a Math Ed professor. He was able to take challenging concepts and use examples and emphasis on understanding to help us grasp them. He cared about our understanding more than our test scores. 10/10 would recommend!

It is hard to imagine a better math teacher than Dr Jones. He is very concerned with learning while keeping an eternal perspective on school (e.g. "You won't remember what grade you got in 5 years, just work hard for the sake of working hard". He teaches well and gives very fair tests.

Wow, what a great man. He made me feel so good about myself listening to him talk about multivariable calculus. Seriously explains things so well, I'm sure a 4th grader could understand calculus after an hour with him. He is truly so kind and such an amazing teacher. I would highly recommend taking any class with him, he's incredible.

Definitely a gem in the math department. He's a math ed instructor, so you know he's a quality teacher. Very good at explaining difficult concepts. Calc III is a difficult class several homework assignments and concepts to know, but he definitely makes it manageable.

Had him for 113 also. Great teacher and person. Register ASAP! Knows what he's doing, has taught this class before. Setup is similar to 112 & 113 - written & online hw (not overwhelming), 3 tests & final. He writes his own tests. Picks great TA's. Go to lecture, since not all written hw is from the book, sometimes he makes up his own problems.

Dr. Jones was amazing! He structured the class very well and I think he taught very well. He focused on helping the students understand not only how to use formulas, but where they come from and how and why they work. He teaches very well and the TAs are great, so you only need the book for the homework problems. Best math teacher I've ever had!

Math 314 sure isn't an easy class, but Dr. Jones is a really nice guy and wants you to enjoy it. His lectures are really straightforward and he wants you to be able to understand things visually and conceptually. If he feels that a question on the test was too hard or confusing he'll curve it. Great class, would take with him again.
Dr. Jones took a fairly hard subject, Calculus II, and turned it into a simple and easy to understand concept. I loved his class. He is such a clear teacher. Definitely take it from him!

Dr. Jones is a fantastic professor. I was a bit skeptical of the value of his phD in math education (why not just study math?), but it really shows. His lectures are extremely clear and enable you to understand the material very well. He's also willing to answer clarifying questions during lecture.

Dr. Jones is amazing, by far the best professor I've had. He does an incredible job of teaching the material, but he also cares more about his students than any professor I've seen. He made the class so much easier and managed to transform math 113 (typically a very difficult class) into one of my easier courses this past semester.

Dr. Jones is easily the best professor I have had at BYU. He is the best TEACHER. He teaches so effectively and helps the class through tough concepts. Love how he teaches to help the students understand rather than memorize. 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Jones cared so much about his students. He understands what it's like to be in our shoes and he connects with the class naturally. He does two to three examples step by step in class and he uses similar problems as test problems. He also added a big curve our final overall grades.

Amazing teacher. Really good at explaining concepts. Goes pretty slow, does lots of examples. HW is harder than the tests, which is nice. The test averages were typically high 80's (!!). You'll be fine as long as you do the HW. Lots of extra credit, picks good TAs. As a senior, ive taken lots of classes @BYU, and he is one of the best forreal

Professor Jones is amazing! I can't remember a single day where I left class without having a good understanding of the material we had just learned and I was always able to do my homework with little help from others

There is homework due every Tuesday and Thursday for lab. His lectures are super helpful. He teaches the material in a way that can easily be understood. There are a lot of TAs that can help with homework (use the TAs).

Dr. Jones is a cool dude. He really dislikes memorization, so he is different in his style than others. He doesn't write which chapter he is covering, and taking notes can be difficult since he derives formulas sometimes and doesn't have memorized steps to solving a problem. You will notice this after a few classes. But take him if he is an option.

Hands down- a true talent for teaching difficult concepts. Very clear, and concerned for his students. Thank you Dr. Jones!! He's given me confidence to learn, and apply mathematics. Take a class from him! He's one I will personally never forget from my college education, and you will probably say the same!

This man is by far, the best teacher I've ever had. He teaches like he came out of the womb doing it! Fantastic at explaining concepts, and is so organized so you get the most out of your hour with him. Honestly the class could've been much harder, but thanks to him, it wasn't. Take from him if you ever have the chance!

Really good lecturer. He definitely prepares well for his lectures and answers questions really well.  I found the class to be simple with his lectures and his TA's were very helpful and approachable too.

One of the best professors I've had at BYU and I'm pushing 80 credits. He is extremely talented in explaining things. His math education background really shows. Take math 113 from him, and you won't regret it.

This class is pretty notorious for being difficult. You have to work for it, but if you put in the time you will definitely learn the material and should be able to do well in the class. The TAs and TA labs for this class are really necessary and very helpful.

Dr. Jones is one of the best professors I've had. I came in the class not having taken math for a long time and was really intimidated, but he taught so well that it wasn't a problem getting it all back. On the final every one of his students got 4% added at the end because his classes did so well compared to others. Study hard and you'll do well.

Dr. Jones was by far the best teacher/professor I've ever had.  The expectations and grading criteria were very clear.  He really cares about everyone in his class and always respectfully answers questions.  There's even an opportunity for extra credit just by attending lectures.  I wish I could take from him for every math class.
This class was pretty hard, but his lectures are really clear. You have to go to the TA class because you learn more material. It was hard, but not too difficult if you do the homework.

This class was so great! I would take Dr. Jones for every math class at BYU if I could. He does his own tests, which means he does one more than the normal Math 113 teacher, but they are written for you to succeed. He puts forth the utmost effort in preparing for each lecture, and wants to help all students improve. There's a curve for the final!

Dr Jones was an amazing professor. He really cares about his students, he explains difficult concepts very very well. He breaks difficult concepts into small, easy to understand ways that you can approach a problem. He doesn't give any extra credit, but if you score well on the daily quizzes, he'll give you up to 2% raise on your final grade.

Dr. Jones does a great job of making complex problems simple and easy to understand.  Great lectures.  He's committed to helping you learn concepts, rather than just memorizing formulas.  He also has a homework schedule that is doable, with assignments due twice a week.

Dr. Jones is a great professor who really cares about his students. He doesn't hesitate to take time out of lectures to answer questions. The class is difficult, but he makes it possible to get a good grade. At the beginning of every lecture there's a quiz and if you do well on them you can get up to 2% EC. I would definitely recommend his class!

I wish it were possible to take this course from another professor. Dr Jones is a very nice man and he cares about his student but tests and participation points are ridiculous. On the tests expect to need to know all the nitpicky details and basically repeat verbatim certain items. Participation points in this class are ridiculous to get

Professor Jones is the best teacher I've had. He is incredibly prepared and organized. He addresses almost every question before you have it. He can relate math to real life and explains why you are learning concepts when you learn them. He's friendly, and respectful. I wish he taught all of my classes!

Best math teacher I've ever had. I struggled in 112 but he made 113 easy. I put forth minimal effort and got a solid B. A is definitely possible if you work for it. Not an easy class due to the material but it's the best way to do math 113. Take it from Dr. Jones!!!
He focuses on what matters most and really cares about having his students succeed. He's a great teacher.

Math has never been something that's come easily to me, but Dr. Jones has made this 4 credit calc class totally manageable! His lectures are clear, and he answers any questions that students have.  He also provides lots of resources to help with HW and test review. Take Math 113 from him, you won't regret it!!
Awesome.

You can NOT go wrong with him. He is amazing. There are daily i clicker quiz questions that you can discuss with your peers (this is a good grade bump). He doesn't want you to memorize any formulas; therefore, his tests are personally written. Take this class if you want to learn how to compute, rather than how to regurgitate formulas. Take him.
I wish I could take all my math classes from Dr Jones! He teaches so much more clearly than any of my other math professors.

Best math teacher I have ever had! His lectures were very engaging and taught in a very clear way. I love his pedagogical model and helps us to understand more than memorize. There were times in class we were all at the edge of our seats because it was so fun. Funny. Super nice. We all felt his number one priority was us.
Better than any Math 113 teacher in all ways
great professor, knows how to teach very well (given his whole calculus teaching research)

If I could, I would have taken him for all my classes in Math! He is by far the most clear teacher I have had. He is very patient as well. His curves are great. Also, his classes almost ALWAYS rate above average in tests, which means the MATH dept. gives you an overall grade boost. His class is great cause you can ride the bus with him to victory!!

Dr. Jones is the director of the Math Ed Dept., so he knows how to teach! He is very clear from the beginning in his syllabus what is expected, and the lectures always went by so quickly! The material is difficult, but he makes it doable. There is usually an upward curve (typically by a letter grade) at the very end of the semester, which is nice.

He's a great guy. He's probably the most clear calc teacher you will ever have. He teaches you difficult concepts by breaking then down into simple ways to understand. And he kinda looks like kip from Napoleon dynamite.

I love the guy. He does give a lot of homework due to the nature of the material, but he stated all the requirements up front and didn't changing anything half way through the semester. He helped make math fun, and he has good TAs.
Awesome. What more can I say. Best math teacher I've ever had. He shows how the problems apply to life, which is good since 80% of the class are engineers.

Great professor, very good at what he does.  A little dry, doesn't come off as easy to approach, but very willing to help if you ask.  He does a great job of handling freshmen. There is a lot of work to do, but he really makes you learn the material and understand it so that you can do more than just pass a test.  Would take a class from him again.

He was the 4th Calculus teacher I've ever had and by far the best.  I would take his class again any day.  He is amazing at explaining the math concepts and really helps you understand the theories behind the problems.  If you actually want to understand the how and why of math, take his class.

He.  Is.  AMAZING.  Amazing teacher.  Explains things using clear diagrams and following along is SUPER easy.  I absolutely loved taking his class (yeah, I enjoyed a math class, that's how good he is!) and I would love to have him as a teacher again.  Overall 2005.
Dr. Jones is amazing at what he teaches and is excellent at explaining it.  His assignments are super long, but the tests aren't too difficult.
Amazing at explaining concepts. Really understands the subject.

Dr. Jones really works hard to show how calculus is actually used in real life, which makes for a much more interesting math class. He makes sure his students understand what he's teaching, clearly explaining any confusing topics and giving great, clear answers to any questions. His tests aren't too bad if you actively pay attention during class.

Take this from another teacher. Leavitt is a great person, but a pretty bad teacher. His lectures are very sporadic, and he doesn't teach what is on the exam. However, it was a pretty easy class, and the TA's are super helpful, so you can get through it easily enough, as long as you teach yourself the material.

Lectures usually got pretty off-topic, honestly not very necessary some days. Tells us to study the review sheets to learn the material ourselves. He's funny and very passionate about biology, but I wasn't a big fan of his teaching style. Lab homework and quizzes are where most of the learning happens. Labs were fun, even at 8am Monday morning!
First of all, I had him for Univ 101. Bro is so chill and funny.

I wanted to leave a good review so bad. He had given the class remediation opportunities on the exams, and I took full advantage of all of these opportunities. I was suffering through multiple losses at the time and was unable to give 100% at 9:00 AM. Come the end of the year, he rounded my grade down because my grade was not fair. Disappointing.

Steve Leavitt is a great guy but he avoids questions during class. His class material also is not organized at all. If you want to teach yourself biology then I would choose him. If you want a teacher who wants you to learn and will go over the course that you're paying for, I would suggest finding a different teacher.

Steve is a great professor for those desiring to have a deeper knowledge and understanding of the basics of biology. The coursework was clear and fairly graded, with the majority of the grade going toward the three exams. Comprehensive reviews are provided by the TAs, and the study guides provide all the information needed to receive full marks.

Dr. Leavitt is very passionate about botany. His class is set up for memorization, rather than actual learning. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and is willing to work with students. Quizzes in recitation and lecture every week. Lectures didn't match the textbook, but you need to read it to understand lectures, which was frustrating.

Dr. Leavitt has instilled in me a deeper love for biology! His lectures are long and often difficult to understand, but he helps you put the concepts you're learning into context. The labs are where the substantial learning happens. The tests are tough! Study the study guides and go to the TA reviews, and you'll do fine.

He's a very passionate teacher and always willing to work with you. A good strategy for studying is a must in this class! I focused on the study guides he gave out for each section (different from the reading guide!), used the book as a reference, studied the phylogenetic tree, and made my own life cycle diagrams and things went pretty well for me.

The lectures were always very interesting! Everything that was included on the test was not always covered in lecture so make sure you read the text book. The tests are quite long but if you attend lectures and reviews you will know everything for the test.

I really enjoyed having him as a professor. The lectures were sometimes confusing and very dense, but he makes material exciting. The exams were fairly difficult, and I had a 89.5 at the end of the semester that was not rounded, so that was a bit of a bummer. He loves using outside books as references, and he loves lichens! Overall a great class.

Super understanding professor. The lectures are thorough and can always review them. He allows you to see possible questions for the quizzes to help you prepare. HE WANTS YOU TO SUCCEED! His labs are wonderfully planned and the TAs are great for preparation of exams. Everything on his exams was fair game whether it was lectures or from the readings

Dr. Leavitt is caring but his lectures are honestly so unorganized. They never made any sense and made me more confused about the class. He gave us a study guide though that was helpful. I would just work on that during class but he also likes to call on people randomly so I had to try to follow along somewhat. Lectures don't help with exams.

He is such a cool guy and it wasn't a crazy difficult class. I think he has a great grading system that allows us to make up some quiz grades in order to learn and improve. Unfortunately, his lectures were not even focused on what we had to learn for tests. Most of us relied on youtube videos to learn on our own time.

Honestly Dr. Leavitt really cares for his students. Unfortunately the class is so disorganized, especially the lectures, they really doesn't cover important information. My lab partners and I had to do almost all the learning ourselves. I feel like the labs prepared us better for the tests than the actual lectures. Hit the WSIK sheets hard! "AHHHH"

He is without a doubt the worst professor I've ever had. His lectures are unorganized and they go off on random stuff that does nothing to actually help you understand the material. I don't care how nice he is, being nice doesn't help me get my degree. His lectures never line up with the labs and the entire semester felt like a guessing game.
So so many long boring lectures. Cool guy individually, very nice, and the class is mostly run by TAs.

If you watch the lectures and take notes, you'll do well on the tests. The labs are a lot of fun and while the lab quizzes are a little scary at first, they're not a big deal as long as you come prepared.

Dr. Leavitt is an awesome person. You can tell he really cares about his students' well-being and success in his class. He was super willing to coordinate extra credit and was very accommodating during a non-traditional semester. I would've liked the curriculum to be a bit more organized, but he is a great choice to knock out an easy general.

Dr. Leavitt is a nice guy and also spiritual, he cares about biology and your success. Downside is the class is kind of disorganized. The labs dont always line up with the lectures dont always line up with the homework doesnt always line up with the test. Key to an A: do the homework and study with the What Should I Know test study guide.

Good professor, bad curriculum. I took this class on-demand during a COVID semester so it may have effected a lot of the curriculum. Professor Leavitt is on your side and cares about this subject. There's a disconnect between the book, the study guides, and the tests. The difficult varies drastically between each assignments and each test question.

Talks more about pedagogy than actual biology. Sad that nearly the entire class is trying to convince conservative students that evolution is real. Makes you do a group project at end instead of final, would've preferred a final to be honest.

Pro Leavitt is a nice guy and he truly does care about his students, but he tries to teach in an abstract way during lectures that just isn't effective. The textbook chapters are super long and he doesn't make it clear what you need to know from it. There are only 2 tests. I took this class live remote because of COVID.

Leavitt rocks. He really embodies what the education system SHOULD be. Minimal tests, reasonable homework/ assignments, and he really emphasizes learning the material being way more important than your grade. He even lets you meet with a TA to get points back on missed questions from the homework and exams. Leavitt is a great choice for this class.

Dr. Leavitt is super passionate about biology, and his enthusiasm is contagious. He's really humble and open to changing whatever he needs to to make the class better for the students. He is a really good teacher and explains concepts very thoroughly. The labs are long and tedious, but it's not difficult

A wonderful man, but not my favorite professor... There's no textbook, so you're expected to use Google as a main tool for filling out the study guide. You're expected to read a book called "I Contain Multitudes" and write a book report on it. It's a fascinating book, but it's not directly discussed in class. The pre-class readings aren't necessary

Steven Leavitt is a super cool dude, but not a great professor, at least when it comes to Intro to Biology. He wasn't very focused during lectures and there was no way of knowing what would show up on the exams. There wasn't a final exam, however, which was nice. And as long as you show up to the labs once a week you should get a fine grade.

Dr. Leavitt has a very different and deliberate approach to teaching. In his class he isn't so concerned about making sure you learn loads about biology as he is preparing you to think intellectually and scientifically about difficult issues in society. His class has impacted me in a way no other science class has before, and I love it.

This class with Professor Leavitt was super fun and interesting. You'll have to do a lot of personal learning but that is just the nature of the class. Prof. Leavitt makes study sheets and reminds you to use them. Lectures are super interesting. At first the class seems hard but we talk about a lot more things than are on the tests. Use the TAs!!

Two lectures a week that were not super necessary to attend. One lab class a week that was mandatory to attend and also where we learned most/all the material. Labs taught by TA so it really depends on your TA.

Doctor Leavitt is awesome. His lectures are kind of boring/not super useful, but he'll often go exact test questions during them so they're worth going to. If you study the heck out of the WSIK sheets you'll crush the class pretty easily. The only annoying thing is the 3 hour lab, but some TAs will review the quizzes beforehand.
Honestly just 10/10 great guy. Really knows his stuff and he makes it so accessible in the course material. He's honestly such a gem.

Prof Leavitt is a solid choice for BIO130, very clear lectures and wants students to love biology. Lecture didn't always pertain to the lab, but it was always worth going to. The class overall is a pretty easy A as long as you do the assignments and study for the tests. TA reviews help alot.

Dr. Leavitt is phenomenal!! He spent so much time letting the class lead the discussion. His only goal was for us to learn. He did not want us to stress over grades. He would pose an idea and have us debate what we think is best! We took the most amazing fieldtrips, spent time outside, and had so much fun! This has been my favorite class at BYU.

If you're okay with being subjectively graded without clear criteria this is the place to be. The assignments are doable and if you have a good group for the midterm and final you will be great and they are not overly difficult for a GE, however if you're someone who wants to know why you missed x points on things not on the rubric go elsewhere

He is a great professor! Really enthusiastic about science and teaching. Always willing to meet with students and help them out. He's clear on his marking and as long as you actually tired you'll get a good mark.
He is super passionate about science (especially lichens). Class is almost always interesting. We didnt have any exams, only group projects. He gets that most of us were there only for the GE.

If you want a BIO100 class that isn't about memorization, but actually learning scientific skills you can apply in everyday life then take this class! There are not any tests but rather little assignments throughout the semester and a midterm web-page and final video with a group. If you're willing to do the work outside of class it's great.

Worst class that I've taken so far. The final project for this class was ridiculous. The final project is comprised of about 6 submissions and all of them are graded subjectively by the TAs. You won't learn anything in this class.

Great professor and passionate about science and education reform. The class is group-work focused and there aren't any tests. There is a midterm and a final, both of which are group projects. He is more focused on you being responsible for what you learn than requiring you to memorize facts. Take BIO 100 from Dr. Leavitt.

Great, passionate teachers. He values class participation a lot. His only issue is that there are 25 assignments for the whole semester, and two huge projects in place of a midterm and final. The projects aren't difficult, but are subjectively graded, so your whole grade depends on those.

Different take on a intro to biology class. There are NO tests and two group projects. There is a lot of reading material, most of it is really interesting and traditional concepts aren't really covered in class. Lectures are interesting. This is a good option for someone who doesn't really care about learning much about biology.

Leavitt talks A LOT about his research--way more than any biology curriculum. There are no tests to analyze what we learned, but I also don't feel like I learned much biology. I showed up at class and I know I learned, but I don't know what. There was no mitosis or mitosis or other bio 100 stuff in this bio 100 class. And group projects-enough said
Really good guy. Didn't have any tests so taking notes was pointless. Interesting midterm and final though, they are fun.
He's a really amazing guy and cares a lot about students. Great professor!
Doctor Leavitt is a great guy and great professor! Go to class and you'll be fine!
I don't know why Professor Leavitt has bad ratings. His class was seriously the best class. All you have to do to get an A is show up to class.

I enjoyed having Prof. Leavitt. He really cares about you and deeply about the subject. His class is easy and he really cares about your grades. The only thing which I found to be tough in the class was that the test was very specific for a 100 Class but again, Dr. Leavitt is a gem of a person and I highly recommend taking his class.

As a person, Dr. Leavitt is great.  He is kind and has a great personality.  However, I didn't enjoy this class from him; there was a lot of busywork and a ton of reading that didn't really seem to matter.  He was very vague with the material to be on the tests, but the TA helped clear things up quite a bit.

This Professor is pretty good. He care about the subject, and teaches it alright. Some homework gets confusing, and you don't know wheat to study for tests, but He responds fast to email questions. no textbook is odd, but workable with the main objective of this class.
Don't take Professor Leavitt. He is very confusing and his tests are incredibly detailed. He has lots of busy work and readings that have nothing to do with the Biology 100 material.
I really did not like Dr. Leavitt's style of teaching. He explains things in the most difficult way possible. Tests are incredibly difficult. Don't take Bio 100 with him.

Take this class! You learn so much and he will walk you through all of it! So funny and kind! Clear grading criteria and you can resubmit for more points. Don't be afraid, take this class from Dr Luke!!!

He is super helpful! This class was tricky but there is no homework if you can get your stuff done during class. No tests, just assignments. You basically just learn how to use R Studio on your own with online class materials and Dr. Luke goes around all class helping students individually. He is super funny and understands how overwhelming R is.

I took this course online, and was very underwhelmed by how little Professor Luke was "present". I understand online courses allow for flexibility, but whenever an email was sent to Professor Luke he would either not respond, or do so a week or two later. The TAs were very unhelpful and disorganized, and would not grade in a timely manner.

I took this course online and it was like Professor Luke wasn't even aware he was a part of this class. He didn't respond to any emails, things weren't graded for months. Feedback was needed since a major assignment is submitted in multiple drafts, but there was no feedback given on any assignments and tons of technical issues.

This class helped me overcome my fear of coding! He is very straightforward and he and his TAs offer help as we work during class. Did not spend much time working outside of class and you get points if you code correctly. So fun and worth it!!

I didn't love this class. It was all online, and not organized well. There is a ton of work you have to do. A semester long group project and presentation, an individual 8-page paper and presentation, 3 3-6 page papers throughout the semester in lieu of midterms, a huge final test, and weekly quizzes and writing prompts.

This is one of the most disorganized classes I have taken at BYU. We rarely heard from the professor and often the TA's did not know the answers to our questions. Help for assignments was always given at the last minute. You're put in groups to help with weekly papers, but my group members were just as confused as I was with our assignments.

Honestly this class was way harder than it should have been. His grading was so picky and didn't match the effort given into each assignment and he was not very flexible with the change in going online. This was the worst most ridiculous class I've ever taken at BYU and I would never take it ever again.

Dr. Luke gives engaging lectures I loved them. The reading is very helpful, but not necessary to succeed. He does a great job presenting concepts clearly and answering questions well. Study for the tests. The project was easy; however, grading felt arbitrary which was frustrating, but that was the TA, not Dr. Luke.

Dr. Luke seems like a good dude. He is a funny, happy, and cheerful man. However, I felt his grading criteria was a bit ridiculous at times (though maybe that was just his TA). I also thought his tests were really poorly written, plenty of questions were very interpretive and required you to make assumptions about what the question was asking.
He is a good professor. Tests are very difficult but the lectures are good

Dr. Luke teaches this class in a way that isnt stressful, and he teaches you everything you need to know and gives you ample time to complete your assignments. Loved going to class everyday because hes so funny too.

Loved his lectures. Tests are centered around knowing concepts rather than just memorizing definitions. That's probably the hardest part of the class is adjusting to that style of test. Great professor, really cares about his students. Wants us to succeed.
Tests are soooo hard but Professor Luke is an amazing lecturer, he goes over all material in his lectures, no need to read the book. LOTS of interesting stuff and he is SOOOO funny.
He is so funny and GREAT lecturer. Pr. Luke goes over all material in his lectures, no need to real the book. Save yourself some money.

This guy is hands down the most engaging professor I have had.  I learned.  I laughed.  He was accessible and interesting.  I wish I could say the same for the rest of my semester.  Take him!  You won't regret it.

The 310 group project is pretty standard, but, Professor Luke made it really enjoyable. His class was entertaining and I learned a ton! (Which, also helped me in 309). Professor Luke is willing to work with students. His tests aren't bad as long as you use the study guide. I'd recommend hand writing the answers, and avoid the group google docs.

Professor Luke is one of my favorite professors I have ever taken! He has taken a class that I otherwise would have hated and made it really enjoyable. He is hilarious, and the class is generally easy. It is helpful to go to class, and he does iClicker points but he provides a lot of ways to make these up if you need to miss class.

Dr. Luke is awesome. He is hilarious, yet doesn't get off topic trying to be funny. His tests can be pretty difficult but I would go to his office hours where he was extremely helpful. Great teacher, one of my favorite at BYU.

Luke is a great teacher. He is funny, respectful, and understanding. The majority of the class is a semester long group research paper- unavoidable for this class so take it from him.  His tests are of average difficulty. He provides study guides. Provides plenty of visuals and laughs if you are someone who needs those. Extremely understanding.
I loved this class from him.  He is my favorite teacher here at BYU and I'm going to take sensation and perception from him next semester.  Awesome teacher and awesome guy.

Dr. Luke made this class amazing- every lecture I attended was worth listening to, and I would find myself distracted from texting to listen to what he was saying. He's that good. Covered a lot of material in class, but if you do the study guides you can't get lower than a B. I will remember a lot of things I learned in this class after I graduate.
Dr. Luke was funny, clear and specific, laid everything out nicely for you. Great guy, great class. Take it!
Was able to hold my interest in a morning class.  Not an easy task.  Entertaining and informative lecturesassignments.  Excellent prof.

Dr. Luke is a really nice guy. He really seems to care about his students and the lectures seem pretty clear. However the text book was a little hard to understand. Also, his tests have a lot of very specific questions that I didn't even remember seeing in the book or the lectures. I studied really hard for the tests and still didn't do very well.
Great class, great professor!!!
One of the best professors I have ever had!  Loved going to his class!!

I withdrew from this class because I couldn't understand his teaching style at all. Retaking the class with Obata, and I just got 100 on the first midterm. He's a nice guy with super dry humor, but genuinely one of poorer teachers I have had here at BYU

It's definitely a hard class, we met every day of the week and the material can be difficult. Dr. McKay is good though at explaining challenging concepts and making them easier to understand. Most Fridays he canceled class and made it office hours, it was easy to go to him and get help. Sometimes the homework didn't reflect the readings/lectures.

Decent at explaining problems. Did lots of examples in lecture, which was nice. Wrote kind of small and messy, so it was hard to follow his work sometimes. Most of your grade is the tests (3 midterms worth 15% and 1 final worth 25%) Overall he's a decent choice for diffeq and I enjoyed his class, but there is probably better.

Professor McKay is hilarious. Sometimes he's not the best at explaining but it's because you don't need that information to do well. His lectures and homework are very good predictors of the test, and he's also really reasonable when grading tests.

Hey, so there is a lot to think about here. He is a tough grader and his handwriting is illegible in so many ways. That all being said, he does try to provide resources and make sure that you know what you are doing. He has practice tests and office hours everyday where you can reach him. If you truly want to do well, you can. He won't make it easy

Ya this guy was not my favorite. No slides, just lectured and wrote illegibly on the board, made you feel like a dingus when you asked a question. 90% of what I learned in this class was done outside of class. At times it felt Nearly impossible for me to get an A even when I put in the work.

One time he assigned 2 problems on the homework then changed the google sheets to 4 problems, so if you already did it (which half the class did) you got a 50% on it, with a follow up email about how he is not changing the scores and we need to pull it up on our computers? (not the problem...) Highly encourage taking this from someone else

I agree with everyone else on here about him being snarky. Beware-- never ask a question. Proofs and no slides, just rambling on the whiteboard for an hour, with no examples. The tests are mostly on the theorems, I spent most the time outside of class teaching myself and trying to learn them. Still did poorly on the tests. Take from someone else.

Linear Algebra is a beautiful subject but take it from someone else! You'll end up teaching yourself the entire curriculum. He is very rude and snarky when you ask questions. He only focuses on theory and writes proofs on the board, without helping students develop a conceptual understanding.

I recommend taking this course from a different professor if you have to take MATH 213. I didn't enjoy lectures and honestly didn't get much out of them. He rudely responds to students if they asked a question that he believes we should fully understand or if they asked him to repeat anything. I got through it but wished I had a different professor

Worst "professors" I've had. He has hardly answered a single question all semester, he just says "oh we'll get to that in 2 weeks" and just acts like its unbelievable that we don't already know the content that he is "teaching". He just sits at the board and writes theorems for an hour. You have to teach yourself through homeworks due every day.

Class is tough but he's very accessible and always helped me with any questions I had. This lectures are also fairly entertaining including his odd sense of humor.
Overall great class
Professor is fine, he's nice and pretty funny, but this class is crazy difficult, would recommend the 3 course route instead.

I liked Professor McKay much more for 314 than 213. He's got a dry sense of humor that you'll either love or hate. He taught most things well, I only had to teach myself a few things online. The homeworks are super short, but sometimes are hard. If you're comfortable in calculus, it won't be super hard.

Professor McKay has the best dad humor out there, but that takes away from some of his teaching abilities. He loves to write a ton of theorems on the board and not really explain them or their relevance. I could probably skip a class per week and learn the lesson in a solid 10 minutes, so that was lowkey nice. Grading is also a little leisurely.

Professor McKay was alright, Linear Algebra is a topic that can get a little difficult, but he did well teaching it. However, the major problem in this class was the slow grading process. The homework was not graded until the end of the semester, which rendered the homework far less useful. The feedback would have been helped prior to the test.

Disorganized, tons and tons of homework. Most other professors required way fewer homework questions than he did. He had no idea what was on the homework or even on the test almost all of the time. He never understood student's questions and seemed to get angry when asked them. His grading system was unclear and disorganized

Funny and nice guy, but man this class frustrated me. He had no idea what was on our midterms or even the final so we basically went in blind (tests are written by other Math 290 professors). There were a few midterms where averages were pretty low and he said he'd curve them later and he never did.  Super hard to get in contact with too.

Professor McKay is an old guy with a dry/sarcastic sense of humor. You know the type, and you know if you can handle it. He will make fun of you, but never means it in a bad way. His class is super definition/proof heavy, and he doesn't teach in an intuitive way. I learned more from 3Blue1Brown videos than from him.

Dr. Mckay is funny and his lectures are unique. I think he's a nice and reasonable guy, but this class just sucks and is hard. It is not his fault. It is very test heavy. Tests are hard, but once again, not his fault because they are written by the department. If you HAVE to take this class, I thought he was a good guy to take it from.

I rarely, if ever, leave reviews about professors. It is November and I would guess that about only 5 assignments out of the 46 given, not including tests, have been graded. Good luck actually getting feedback on your assignments because that will never happen! He also half teaches everything so you teach yourself.

Professor McKay has a unique teaching style - he's funny but can be confusing at times. The homework is tough but doable if you stay on top of it. Using resources like unstuck ai and 3Blue1Brown helped me a lot.

Super awesome professor- tough(ish) class. I didn't read the textbook until partway through... READ THE TEXTBOOK. His lectures were OK- he mostly just read from the book and went through the proofs that you already read. I had a lot of friends that simply didn't show up for the lectures and still passed the class. Funny guy though.

Really nice guy, really hard to read his handwriting on the board. Sit close to the board. Pay attention in class and do the practice tests before class. This class is not easy, especially during the spring, but you can still do well. Tons of homework

This is not an easy class. His teaching can be pretty confusing but Prof. McKay is happy to answer questions and to let you know if your question is beyond the scope of the class. There are 4 homework assignments a week. The exams aren't too bad if you work through all the homework and practice exams.

MATH290 was simultaneously my most challenging and enjoyable class this semester. I learned far more through doing the homework and prepping for quizzes than I did in lecture. Professor McKay has 6 quizzes and a final on top of homework. Professor McKay is very caring and famous for his dry sense of humor.

Prof. McKay is very dry and I find him to be really funny. This class is very hard no matter what. There's so much  homework and there's 6 quizzes and a cumulative final. Prof. McKay is probably not the best teacher, but he's not a bad option. He's more than willing to help you out. Ask questions in class and do the HW in the math lab!!

Hey is super kind! He is good at introducing topics, and also good at staying on topic. If someone asks a question out of scope of class, he tends to just say that. If that matters to you maybe find another teacher, but he teaches this content really well. It's the first time I understand the material, because he's not going in every direction.
Dr. McKay gives good lectures and cracks a lot of jokes if you're a fan of dry humor. Willing to help if you don't understand a concept

I took professor Mckay for Math 213 after seeing all the other reviews on here. He was a nice person, but a living textbook. Mocked students for asking questions, used a 3rd party to grade, and didn't cover everything that was on the exams. This is my first time reviewing a professor because of how terrible my experience was. Homework everyday.

I had Dr. McKay for 290 (A-) and then later on for 314 (A-). I took 314 from him online. He's a very good teacher and instructor and explains things very clearly. He has an incredibly dry sense of humor that I really enjoyed. Don't be thrown off if he seems gruff because he's really quite understanding and will work to help you succeed.

Because the exams for all the Math 213 sections are the same, sometimes there is material that we didn't cover in class on the exams. Relying on class and homework is not enough to do well on exams - practice exams and extra studying. I felt like sometimes he skimmed over really important points in a lecture. He works examples. It was alright.

Dr. McKay taught multivariable calculus in a way that made it approachable. The examples we did in class were usually helpful for homework and my own understanding. He explained ideological connections between concepts and formulas.
Highly suggest studying on your own with the book, the "learning outcomes" sheets for tests, and reviewing notes.

Honestly toughest class I've ever taken. Unclear grading so one has any idea how you are doing in the class. The tests were hard as we never practiced questions like those asked on the exams. I felt that questions on exams were inaccurate reflections of learned concepts. One was expected to master every concept ever taught and be tested on them.

I got by without going to a single lecture, cram studying for tests, and clutching it on the final. With that being said, his lectures were practically useless. He would go on so many tangents, and would constantly get distracted by student questions. Never knew what to expect, and he was never clear on grading criteria and curves.

Really tough class that I think Professor McKay does an alright job teaching. Sometimes he gets disorganized and on some of the tougher questions he got pretty lost which can be really frustrating as a student, but I'm not sure any of the other 341 professors are any better. Fast turnaround on grading. Great guy, really difficult class.

Dr McKay is a good professor.  The class itself I took was hard, but I felt he never went over applications to concepts which made it hard to understand why they matter.  The homework was also harder than what we practiced in class.  However, he is funny, so lectures were at least entertaining.  I struggled, but he's not a terrible professor.
Horrible teacher with high expectations

Dr. McKay is really nice and very funny. It's obvious that he wants the whole class to succeed. He will not explain things in a geometric sense (which is how I learn best). Your best bet is 3Blue1Brown on Youtube if you take this class. I would take him as a professor again though because he's the best the math department has

I'm a mathed major; I've taken a LOT of math classes.  I've taken grad level courses that were easier than 314.  Tests were 70% of our grade.  Grader took forever to get back to us, Prof. didn't curve the grade until the end so you didn't know if you had to withdraw.  His "review" was straight concepts, practice exams were nothing like tests.

I took it during the Summer, it was an awful experience, we didn't have a TA, so we didn't receive any feedback from the daily paper HW. Classes were just a pain because it was a lot of content in two hours. It is NOT worth it during the Spring/Summer, especially with this professor.

He is honestly really nice and very reasonable. Most of the course his lectures were interesting and made sense. Towards the end, it became mostly proofs that were hard to follow and I was lost doing the homework. I expected the class to be hard, so having lots of homework is a given, but overall, I enjoyed how McKay was willing to work with me.

I took for 213 and 334. I hated 213 (A-) with him because he never showed us any application for lin alg so it was very difficult for me to visualize the concepts. I liked him a lot for 334 (A) because he did go over some applications and for some reason he was more personable in 334. He is also really good at responding quickly to emails!

I've taken three classes from him (two As and one -A) so I would say I'm pretty familiar with his teaching style. A few things I really liked but that you may not: his lectures are very similar to the books, he has a very dry sense of humor, he is very organized but a bit inflexible with his class setup. Average difficulty.

Professor McKay was pretty decent in my opinion. He went through examples during class and took the time to answer questions. However, he did sometimes answer questions in a confusing way because we haven't learned the concept yet or because it was something he was going to cover later. Overall, his teaching style worked for me.

Dr. McKay knows his material well. If you go to his office hours, he will *always* be able to help you. DiffEq is a hard subject, and his focus is on teaching you the methods of tackling it. If you ask questions, you'll get answers. The grader I had sometimes missed things, but always gave points back if you made your case. All in all a good class.
Claims to give feedback but just doesn't. Easy grader but does not prepare you AT ALL for the tests. Very narrow knowledge base and can't at all assist students showing a need for help.

He definitely made this class harder than it needed to be. I imagine linear algebra could be taught in a much less complicated way but it seems like he just didn't care at all about his students. I learned everything from reading the textbooks and doing the practice tests before midterms. Wouldn't recommend him to anyone.

I love Prof. McKay, but I maybe don't love his teaching style for Diffeq. I really wish he utilized WebAssign HW to go along with paper HW so we could get more practice and immediate feedback. His sense of humor isn't for everyone. Tests and HW are very hard, HW doesn't always translate well from lectures. Going to retake from a different prof.

I think he's fine as a professor, just not quite to my learning style. I understood most of what he taught in lecture, but it wasn't always reflective of the homework and tests. I enjoyed his dry sense of humor. He picks on students, but not maliciously. He could recognize if he stepped over a line.

His humor is a bit dry and sarcastic, which can sometimes come off as a little rude but he means well! He is always willing to meet and go over any questions you have. His lectures are sometimes a but proof heavy, but there aren't really any proofs on the exams. Overall one of my fav professors and am taking another class from him!

I was afraid to ask questions the whole class. Anyone who asked questions would usually get shut down. He is incredibly smart, but I think he has difficulty explaining things to someone who is seeing it for the first time. Watch out for his cranky days.

He is not very good at explaining difficult topics. Attending lecture is essentially pointless. He makes weird jokes and his class is just a drag. But if you're an independent learner then you can do well as long as you do the homework. I stopped attending class after the first month and passed...

Linear Algebra is a really hard class to start and Dr. McKay just didn't teach in the style that I needed. Nothing made sense and he didn't seem to explain any difficult concepts like at all. Good luck to anyone who has to take this class.

I had him first for 314 Multivariable Calc, then for 213 Linear Algebra. The first was online, second in person. Online wasn't as great because of the format and material, but he was very reasonable and even helped me when I had a problem with the online final since it was harder to get a time. In person his humor landed more and he was even better

I rarely rate anyone lower than a 5, but I just didnt find Dr. McKay to be a good teacher. His lectures were just copying things down from the book, and he wasnt good at helping students understand concepts that seemed intuitive to him. I rarely went to class and just learned everything from the book, which was a way better use of time.

McKay is the first math professor I've had where I actually looked forward to attending class. He's funny and super prompt to respond to messages outside of class (will often give answers too). That said, his handwriting is no good and his teaching is super proof-heavy. sit in the front and be ready to be confused a little. Overall super great

McKay knows what he's doing and does it well. His jokes sometimes don't quite make it, but its nice to have jokes at all. Pros: Good teacher Normal Homework load (8 problems per topic) Easy to talk to Cons: Big class, so not much personal connection

I felt like Dr. McKay was a solid professor. He was good at explaining the concepts in 314 (I wasn't always to good at visualizing it tho, hence my grade.) He only ever communicated through piazza though, which was kinda annoying to me bc I don't like it, but he's definitely a good professor.

He's a good, funny guy, so I feel bad giving him a bad rating, but I don't think he was very good at all at explaining math. All my conceptual, visual understanding of the theories and equations we learned came from outside studying, and I rarely left class feeling equipped to do the homework.

One of my favorite math professors at BYU. He's super good at explaining new concepts in a way that makes sense and ties into math from other classes. The class won't be too difficult as long as you can stay ahead of the homework. The tests do represent a significant portion of the grade so you'll want to study. He's also a good choice for 290.

McKay is a good teacher and the lectures help, but he's very strict with the homework. There are no extensions on the homework and no exceptions, as if you turn an assignment in late you get a zero. Even when I got COVID and was sick and still figuring everything out, there was no extension. Good teacher otherwise, just his HW policy sucks

Math 290 in general is a very well-structured class, and Dr. McKay did a good job of utilizing that. Lecture attendance isn't very necessary if you have a solid grasp of mathematical and logical thinking (and read the textbook!), but I still attended most and got something out of it. His dry humor was definitely the highlight of lectures.

I took DiffEQ from Dr. Mckay online over the summer. He did a pretty good job explaining things. I went through the book after each lecture, and I understood everything that was going on well. He is very willing to answer questions mid lecture if you are willing to speak up. I do like him as an in person teacher better than online.

Professor McKay was a phenomenal teacher. His classes went over the reading and problems like most math teachers, but he was always very accessible for reviews and help with homework. Super funny guy, and will really work with you if you need it!

Professor Mckay is great!! Hard class, but he teaches really clearly and takes time to explain it a different way if he needs to. The grading criteria is super clear and straightforward. Exams are difficult, but he is always willing to help during his office hours. Homework load is not bad.

Math 290 is hard, but if you take it, take it from Professor McKay! It is clear from the beginning how to succeed. He teaches everything in lecture and then you have ample time for homework. He has office hours where he can go over the homework with you and other questions. He prepares you well for the tests and overall makes this class manageable.

Dr. McKay is an excellent teacher, he makes lectures enjoyable with his jokes, and is able to explain difficult concepts clearly. The material is fairly straightforward up until the last 3 weeks when you get into vector calculus. Dr. McKay did an fantastic job of explaining everything clearly. I would recommend reading the textbook (not required).
Dr. McKay explains concepts clearly and is very good at helping us when we don't understand. He is also so funny, his dry sense of humor cracks me up. 12/10 would recommend.

He's a decent teacher. May seem intimidating and like a bit of a curmudgeon at first, but he's not. He likes to keep lectures light with his dry sense of humor. I might give the "most sarcastic person" award.

He's a good professor! He's also a pretty funny one  he's got a one of a kind personality and is constantly making jokes. He doesn't mind if you come to class or not, nor what you do during it, but also doesn't allow for many excuses as to why homework was late. To make up for that, he drops a good number of assignments at the end. Really nice!

Professor Mckay is my favorite math teacher to date. It's a hard class but he's a clear teacher and gets you ready for the midterm. He has a very dry sense of humor which is probably the biggest reason I love him. He's totally willing to be personal with the students. Several other students and I are taking 334 from him next semester.

He's super funny in class and makes you laugh. He is also pretty good at explaining hard concepts and makes it clear what's to be done and how to do it. Definitely top half of math professors I've had.

Steven is one of my favorite professors. He makes a boring subject interesting by his charismatic attitude. He spends the first 10 minutes of most classes by answering the hardest homework problems, as decided by the students. Solid choice for 313

My word, this professor and I clicked. Fantastic "dad jokes" and humor. He was super appreciative of those who would make him laugh in class. The subject is hard. Doing your homework by yourself was necessary to do well in this class. He was very available to help though, moreso than the TAs in my opinion.

I really liked Dr. McKay. He's funny, genuine, and willing to consider your argument if you feel a test question wasn't written correctly. He added an extra page to the free response questions just for me when he saw my large handwriting.

Not a hard class. Homework load is relatively light for a math class. Lectures were a little boring and not super necessary if you read the book. Dr. McKay is funny, friendly, and willing to answer questions about the homework. Tests weren't too bad, and there was usually a curve. Beware of the final though, there's a lot of material to remember.

Professor McKay is a solid Professor. He is pretty sassy and funny which I liked, but I know some people don't appreciate his humor. He isn't the best at explaining concepts, but does a decent job and answers questions well.

Dr. McKay is a good teacher. He's funny and he is good at explaining things. He did teach a lot from the textbook, so if you like studying from textbooks then going to class might be somewhat redundant for you.

Dr. McKay is sassy without apology. I loved it. He is an entertaining and clear teacher. He is always willing to help you during his office hours with hw or concepts. 313 isn't super easy, but Dr. McKay at least kept it light in the classroom! He is a fair grader and is excellent at explaining things most of the time.  Thanks, Dr. McKay!
He is a terrible teacher with random grading. He is so busy that he doesn't even read the questions fully.

Nice guy. Terrible teacher. He mixes up numbers all the time, so for those who are having a hard time following up end up being mislead. I asked him for help one time on a problem, then he just said, eh i don't really want to do all that work. You could honestly miss all classes, and just do the my educator and do good. Bad teacher

Linear Algebra is tough. Mckay is very clear and concise in teaching. He has a dry sense of humor. Occasionally we didn't finish the whole lecture. Tests are department-wide and tricky. Homework is standard. Do the online first. Works through HW problems the first 15 min of class. I respect him. Solid guy.

Professor McKay teaches Calculus 2.  Yes, there is a lot of work, and yes you need to buy the "book." Although there is plenty of work and homework, professor McKay is very understanding and will extend deadlines. He will work with his students one on one and he answers homework questions before turning it in all while he makes Calculus hilarious!
Taught concepts very clearly, although a little dry. Has a good sense of humor and will work homework problems in class that students found difficult.

Not an excellent teacher at BYU. Hard to ask questions in class. He get defensive or belittles students. Most questions we try to ask to each other so we don't get singled out. He misses a lot of material so you have to teach it to yourself through the homework. Tests are department wide and he doesn't help you much to prepare.

Sadly, Dr Mckay has been my least favorite math professor at BYU. He seems like one of those guys who may like math, but he didn't become a professor to teach. He doesn't teach to the test and when he taught us material wrong, we get it wrong on the test, he won't own up to his mistakes. He isn't on the students side.

I also took calculus online through BYU, so I knew that there was going to be difficult. But at the same time, when you pay for the course, you would expect to get a little more out of it than "Read the Textbook," which is basically all his notes consisted of. His syllabus directly says, "do not contact the instructor," which is also off-putting.

I dont go to BYU, took this as a distance learning class. Its a Calculus course so it is going to be a little difficult regardless. You will not be allowed to contact the instructor. Always go through each of the test reviews question by question. The final was olny slightly harder than the three midterms. Be sure to take advantage of the retakes

Dr. Mckay was very clear with explaining the concepts of the class. He moves VERY slowly, and will often get sidetracked. He managed to somehow get through the material, and he was always willing to answer questions. He has a very dry sense of humor; it's great! Overall, a very kind and clear math professor, but he moved a little too slowly for me.

303 is a hard class no matter who you take it from. I liked it more than 302 though. I felt that Dr. McKay understood how hard it was for us and did his best to explain everything clearly. He's very helpful, and his cheesy jokes are a nice respite for your math-jumbled brain. Expect about 2 hours of homework everyday, use his office hours!

Professor McKay knows the material well, but he doesn't make it exciting. You'll have to motivate yourself. When you pay attention he teaches it very clearly, and grading was always pretty clear with limited extra credit also available.
This class is hard. Dr. Mckay does a great job of explaining the material and makes the lectures fun and helpful. Hard, time consuming homeworks are due 4-5 days a week.

Dr. McKay is an awesome professor. I was a little worried at first because I had a friend who took his 113 class a few semesters back and he didn't do so well. I'm really glad I decided to take the class anyway. Calculus is hard, so don't expect to just come to class and pass. The assignments and tests are department specific. Fun!

This was the worst class that I took in my time at BYU. Dr. McKay and his class documents were not (in any way) helpful for learning calculus. He refuses to respond to student emails, and his TAs are less than helpful. He essentially sets you up for failure. The final exam was FAR more difficult than the other 3. Expectations were very unclear.

The class was very difficult but McKay made it manageable. His tests can be pretty tough but he makes it very clear what material is being covered. While his teaching style isn't the clearest, he's a great guy. He was very willing to accommodate students and was always willing to help students.
I''m taking his online calc two and the outline he gives combined with the textbook he recommends are the least helpful documents I have ever used. Horrible class wish I didn''t need it

Great professor! He's really funny, good at explaining, helpful to his students, and a nice guy. The class starts out easy, and then gets progressively harder. Don't let that throw you off. Keep at it and don't give up! His class may be hard, but calculus 2 is probably hard regardless of which professor you have.

Dr. McKay is not only a good professor, he cares deeply about his students. He has incredible patience when teaching, and will always take time to answer even the most basic questions. He is refreshingly grounded and non-pretentious in his approach and his humor makes class enjoyable. Tests were tough, but the curve is generous. Take 113 from him.
He's not intimidating and makes class enjoyable and teaches very clearly.

He's a good teacher but doesn't seem to care in class. He's simply hilarious in lecture and, partly because I took Calc in high school, I understood each concept. I had a great TA, though, who put on phenomenal reviews. The TA saved me and helped me do well. You'll be fine if you know how to do the reviews.

I don't think the concepts were too hard, and he explains very slowly and clearly in class, but his tests are ROUGH. He is a very hard grader. He does curve, but it's still really hard. He doesn't seem to like answering questions much. He is super sarcastic, so if you're sensitive you'll probably be offended, lol.

Dr. McKay takes time to explain every question asked in class, even the simplest algebra. He is selfless with his office hours and loves helping students. He explains things in a way that is very clear and makes calculus bearable with his humor and excellent teaching style.

I really didn't like him. He's incredibly dull. The class is very proof heavy. He's a really harsh grader. He is really picky and he docks you a lot of points for making small mistakes even if you understood the concept. The one good thing I can say is this class had a pretty decent curve which helped out a lot.
Spent too much time proving theorems and equations rather than doing example problems. Funny guy, but lectures weren't very helpful.

This guy was hilarious. If I had to critique something I would say he uses too many proofs. Really funny professor and has a  positive attitude toward the class and also picks great TA's they were especially helpful.
Great professor. Great sense of humor.  He does a good job of explaining the material.

You can tell he's been teaching for a long time because his examples are polished, he can explain things perfectly, and he is a softy when it comes to grades. He was always helping kids one-on-one before and after class. Approachable, he really wants you to come in at his office hours. Dry humor. Dumb jokes, but that's every professor ever.
Loved the class. Just like Calculus BC in High school. Hard assignments online takes about an hour a problem. Exams fair and not too hard. Get a good TA:) He curves grades at the end.
If you want a professor who just reads out of the book for an hour then he will be perfect for you.  Exams weren't too bad though.

This class is hard, but it is a 300 level math class so that is expected. Professor Mckay did ok at teaching, but he grades on a curve which is helpful in the end. He is always willing to help you one on one during office hours and I would take advantage of that.

Dr. Mckay has an extremely dry sense of humor. I think that this came across as rude to some students. He is a quality teacher though. He expects you to understand 300 level math, but that comes with the course. His tests were beasty, but I think that is because Dr. Chow wrote his tests. Dr. Mckay was good about adjusting the grades fairly though.

It may be just a hard subject, but I felt like he made it harder. He would prove an equation the first 40 minutes and quickly shove in the application in the last 10. Class was boring, even though he is pretty funny. Try someone else if you can find someone better.

Dr McKay was constantly making rude, derogatory remarks and comments to students. When a question came up that he did not deem worthy of his time, he would brush it off in a way that undermined the intelligence of whoever asked. He was not open to student's opinions and would dismiss legitimate questions because he was teaching other things.

The material is very hard, and prof. mckay does an ok job of explaining it. he is a really good teacher, but sometimes i think he's been teaching for too long just b/c he spends a lot of class joking with students. but when he's not doing that he's teaching very well and clearlly. i would recomend him.

I'd definitely look for a different professor. He teaches fine, but he literally asked the class each time "What's the matter with this problem?" before he would do a problem on the board. He is completely unapproachable and will NOT work with you on fixing your test. Lectures weren't enjoyable either.

I did learn a ton in the class, but 1. Almost no thanks at all to Prof. Mckay and 2. It didn't reflect on my grade as I'd liked. He just doesn't seem to care about your success... at all. He just proves everything exactly as it's written in the book. Can be funny and friendly, had some great laughs in class. Overall, not recommended.
I found his voice monotone. It was hard to stay awake and he was intimidating, so i found it hard to ask questions

Dr. McKay is a nice guy and he sometimes has a fairly dry sense of humor.  But I don't think he's as great of a teacher.  He doesn't explain things well.  It's hard to read his handwriting.  When virtually the entire class has a question on one problem, he won't usually help us.  He just lectures.  He's a nice guy, but he's not incredible.
Wow this material was hard! But Dr. McKay did a great job teaching it. He's got a subtle and dry sense of humor that relieves that anxiety of tough curriculum. I highly recommend him.

I loved Professor Mckay's class! He explains math very well, for those who already have a good grip on Calc 1. His humor is very very dry and situational, but it usually provides for a few minutes of distraction. Now that the class is over, I'd recommend taking honors, though it is more work. The class size is smaller and you can meet with him.
Steven McKay is a champion. The driest humor you will every find - many days i had to bring extra water bottles. He explains the material well, and made the class, believe it or not, enjoyable.

McKay is awesome. Funniest math teacher I've ever had, and explains the concepts well. Homework is very tough and time-consuming, but he usually does a couple of problems at the beginning of class, and the exams are easy by comparison, which is nice. The whiny reviewers just want high school again with a teacher that holds their hand.

Professor McKay is awesome! He teaches calculus really well, and his corny math jokes are hilarious. Two things to watch out for: on occasion he might not really understand what you're asking him, and his online homeworks can be demonic. Still, I really enjoyed his class.

Dr. McKay is definitely one of the funniest, most entertaining professors I have ever had.  However, his explanations of difficult concepts are often vague.  He takes time at the beginning of class to answer homework questions, which is very helpful.  He is very fair when grading, and curves the tests.  Be sure to do the homework and go to class.
He is a fun professor and is fair.  He will explain things to you when you have a question.
Good teacher.  Likes to make the class fun.  Willing to stop if you have questions.  The material is hard to understand, but his light-hearted attitude makes it easier.

He didn't seem to like his job much. When I would ask for further clarification in class it seemed he wanted me to feel stupid for asking the question. Take Math 113/H from Cardon, he was much much better.

Dr. McKay is an awesome guy.  This class did have a lot of proofs, but it wasn't too bad.  The tests were hard and long and often didn't reflect homework problems.  He answers questions the first 10 minutes of every class.  He gets distracted very easily.  TAs in the mathlab were helpful.  Lots of useless information though.

The worst professor I have ever had! He was very unwilling to actually help me understand the material. He was indifferent towards students who needed clarification for difficult concepts. It was obvious that he did not enjoy his job.

Don't take this class unless you have to.  The tests are ridiculously hard, and he seemed to take pride in the fact that his tests take an average of about 4 hours to complete.  He also isn't helpful in answering questions.  He'll either flat out refuse to answer them or only partially answer them.

Easily one of my favorite professors.  He is more than happy to help students, and he answers homework questions at the beginning of class.  His lectures are thorough and he keeps a light atmostphere in the class.  I'd definitely reccomend taking his class.

The Problem with Professor McKay is that he doesn't teach for understanding.  He assumes you already know everything he is doing and when you ask a question he becomes very impatient and unwilling to really help you understand.  I'm sure he's a great guy, but not an effective math instructor at all, at least in my opinion.

He takes his lectures almost directly from the book and has a hard time clarifying Leon's confusing notation.  I got more out of the review sessions with the math lab TA than the lectures.  The class could have been a lot easier with a better overview of the "whys" & the "how's this related."  Not recommended.

While I enjoyed Dr. McKay's sense of humor, I struggled with the concepts because he tends to write proofs on the board that are straight from the book.  GO TO CLASS!  DO THE HOMEWORK!  If you don't you will struggle when it comes to tests.  Otherwise, homework is 25% of the grade, and that is helpful.  I liked the class.

I had Dr. Mckay for 343 and 113.  He's a good guy and not a bad teacher, but he assigns a lot of homework and his tests are intense.  I spent an average of 3.5-4 hrs on each one.  I sometimes feel like he made the course harder than it needed to be.

He was very intrested in our actually education.  He wants to help you, so don't be afraid to go in during his office hours.  My class was actually a lot of fun and I looked forward to going because of the entertainment value.  Homework is important to understanding to subject material, and he is good about reviewing difficult problems. Recommended

I enjoyed his lectures well enough, and usually was pretty thorough (with all the proofs, etc.) He taught a few concepts completely differently than the book did, so be sure to take GOOD notes. If you study the recommended amount (and have a desire to understand linear algebra), you should do fine.

This was a difficult class, and he didn't really explain homework problems people asked about--he'd "get us started" and it generally didn't help me at all, but he explained things during lectures pretty well, and he's funny. Kind of in a dorky way, but I like dorks. :)

I loved this class.  He was very helpful, and explained everything to you if you went to his office to talk to him.  I recommend Dr. McKay to anyone who is going to take calculus.  The book totally suck, but he is a great professor.  If you need help in the class, go into his office and he can clear all of it up.  Great professor!

This was the hardest class I've taken at BYU, something I blame directly on the professor.  Dr McKay talks to you like you're a math professor.  He will not try to "dumb-down" or simplify the material under any circumstances.  Test questions were in many cases inapplicable to the homework which took incredible amounts of time to do regardless.Avoid

Mckay's teaching style combined with Gardners book makes understanding very difficult for visual learners. I don't think he spends enough time explaining things in class, homework is tedious, and tests are difficult. Alternate teacher strongly recomened

I hated this class.  Lecture was completely pointless to go to and Dr. McKay's humor made class even more pointless.  I know it's a hard class to begin with, but if you can, take it from another professor.  I was not impressed by him.

I am sure good ol' Steven means well, but I consider him one of my most useless teachers.  I learn more from reading Garner's book by myself than I do from listening to his lectures.  He always seems like a grump and didn't seem to care too much about the students. And ps... his humor is lame.

I absolutely hated this class.  He tries to be funny and is genuinely a nice guy, but as a teacher he is not very helpful.  The information he gives in class is practically none.  You could probably do okay, if you have a good TA for lab and never miss anything.
Pretty Funny Guy, whenever he asks a question the answer is probably, partitions!  Tests were very hard and the homework very time consuming, but overall not too bad of a class.
This class is terrible and the professor is pretty funny but doesn't really do much to help learn the hard material.

Dr. McKay is a very good teacher.  Class is pretty fun, and he's flexible with due dates (we had a project postponed a month for various reasons).  Make sure you go to lecture, and possibly the Math Lab, and you should do fine on the homework.  For tests, just go back and reinforce the concepts you didn't feel confident in.
Good guy, likes to have fun in class.  Just has a little problem explaining things on a lower level sometimes.
