The homework for this class is pretty time consuming for the first chapter or so, but gradually becomes less so.  I think the department requires professors to go over proofs of theorems in class, so it's no fault of Dr Mckay's that classtime is sometimes not very helpful.  I think he explains things pretty well. Be ready for incredibly dry humor.

He was the worst professor of my college career! He asked people with a low score on the last test to come talk to him. I redid the test and asked if I could raise my grade.  His reply was,'no, I said that to get the people that weren't trying in the class to come in.' So because I try I don't get points? Not normal. Poor teaching skills, poor prof

Worst teacher of my freshman year, he made the class way harder than it had to be.  I don't know why everyone else liked him so much, because I did not.  The tests have nothing to do with the homework, but according to him, he doesn't make the homework schedule, the calculus committee does.

Dr McKay is a great guy. I really enjoyed going to class, and this was two hours at a time in the summer!  I had to work really hard, but I felt like I was really accomplishing something.  By the end of the class I was worried about my grade, but he must have curved the final.  I highly recommend this professor.
A good-natured guy.  His tests were rather difficult, and the projects were miserable, but the class was enjoyable enough.

Great teacher.  He always treats us as equals and laughs at our jokes and sometimes quotes movies or starts singing...our class is very laid-back and entertaining.  we had a lot to learn in a short time and the tests are hard, but they prepare you for the department final.

Good teacher; makes math interesting and fun, even if his jokes are a bit dry. Is able to teach at your level and willing to answer questions. However, his 2 projects are annoying. Teaches very well, though I wish he were more approachable.
Grueling class.  Good teacher.  proof heavy.
Good Teacher. Answers questions and makes sure you understand stuff. Often very proof-heavy. Worst jokes I've ever heard.

Dr. McKay is a very lively person, actually teaches the material on the board (rather than just lecturing), and goes over homework and questions during class.  The material isn't bad in general, but proofs tend to pop up alot (1-2 on each test).

His lectures were helpful and he did a special review for the final when we asked him to.  He seemed very busy when I went to his office hours, so I was inclined to ask fewer questions.  Despite this he is the best Math 112 teacher I saw (I've visited man
Great guy, but he seems to think everything is a review.  Gets frustrated with people who don't understand the first time.

Dr. Peck is a little spacey, but he always told great stories. You could feel his desire to teach and connect with students. This HONRS class was more creative, so it was a great fit. I learned a ton about birds and biology with limited science knowledge. I highly recommend Dr. Peck and, if you can, ask about his research. It's fascinating!

taking bioethics from Dr. Peck was an amazing experience. He is super understanding, respectful and engaging. He took a little while to grade everything, but he gives great lectures, and the class was fascinating. Only one midterm and a project for the final.

Lots of reading, but if you've at least skimmed it you should be alright on the quizzes. He asks you to examine a lot of controversial topics using different ethical theories, and he makes an effort to find the most accurate data available to fuel those discussions. Thought-provoking and funny (and very queer-friendly, if that's a worry for you!)

Though this class doesn't go into depth on ethics, it covers difficult and important topics that need to be discussed more at BYU. The TA's are easy graders, as long as you put in a good effort you'll do fine in the class. Group project and paper were the final, with small quizzes and reading reflections due each week.

This class is not difficult, it is just A TON of reading. You have to be prepared to present the readings at the start of every class because he rolls a die and selects someone to present for 15-20 minutes. Professor Peck is a good guy however and if you participate, the class will be more fun. 2 exams are not difficult or stressful. Easy-ish A

Dr. Peck's bioethics class is instead a class on political activism. Spent maybe the first 2 lectures actually discussing ethical theory then the rest of the semester was about his personal opinion on political topics and you are tested on this. I should have listened to the reviews instead of wasting my time on him.

Interesting class which is much different than any other science course at BYU. I can see why some students dislike Dr. Peck's style of instruction, but I thought his class was enjoyable, intriguing, and relatively stress-free. Easy A if you put in the work.

I cannot believe I paid money for this. After the two lectures, we never again discussed ethical theories, rather his opinions on topics (which you get tested on btw). I took the class to learn philosophy, not the "thoughts of Dr. Peck." It isn't that hard to pass, but it is an absolute pain. He was so disorganized and the class is busywork.

I wanted to take ethics because it is something I am genuinely interested in; Dr. Peck's class was instead a course on his opinions. He rarely mentioned ethical theories and almost never discussed ethics with any rigor. Lectures were just a time for him to tout his political opinions. It was a dumb class full of busywork--a class I regret taking.

Super easy class. Only work I spent outside of class was studying the 30 mins before for the quizzes. The final is weighted the same as an iClicker quiz , about 7% of your grade. The lectures were pretty interesting too, we spent a lot of time talking about aliens, evolution, and global warming, which beats learning about the structure of cells.

Good man and a really easy class compared to others. When things went online he loaded the homework but from the initial class, it was a super easy class and I literally didn't do any work outside of class except read two small books.

A good BIO 100 professor. There are pop quizzes every class period, and two book reports. The topics revolved mostly around evolution which he puts an interesting gospel spin on. Instead of going to lectures on Friday, we did nature journals, which required observing a plant/animal anywhere on campus for an hour, honestly it was pretty chill

Dr. Peck is a great guy. It's pretty easy to get a good grade in this class as long as you do the weekly quizzes. They are each worth 5% of your grade, but they really aren't hard. He doesn't have any midterms and the final is also only worth 5%. He can be disorganized, but his lectures are pretty good and he's really interesting. Would recommend!

Really enjoyable. Do not buy the textbook, but do study the slides before each class because he has a pop quiz on what you learned last time. He also doesn't have many assingments so they kind of count. Really fascinating guy and class is very enjoyable even if he is technologically impaired...

Professor Peck is pretty hilarious. He's so full or random facts and information and it's incredibly easy to get him to go off on a tangent about who knows what. It's easy to get an A in his class as long as you show up and pay attention. His presentations are a bit wordy, but if you ask him to clarify something he's more than willing to help!

He never gave us any tests, all we had to do was an in class quiz once a week as well as an in class hypothesis once a week. We had only two papers throughout the entire semester. The quizzes could get hard which was sometimes frustrating because that is where the majority of points are but generally pretty easy. He is very passionate. fun and easy

Awesome class, awesome teacher. At first, the class was mostly based off of Professor Koide's class, but towards the end, he started making his own material, so be aware of that. Professor Peck was clearly very interested in the material, which was contagious.

Dr. Peck was a great teacher, but it was his first time teaching Bio 100 so there was NO structure to the class. We basically just learned whatever he wanted to teach us. There's not a ton of work outside of class, but it's helpful to pay attention to his lectures.

Dr. Peck's ethics class seemed easy and great through the first month, but as the semester went on his lectures turned into less of a "what is ethical" to a "what does Dr. Peck think about the subject" class. It is not a very difficult course, but he is a real pain to deal with. Most useless class I have taken, and he is a very strange fellow.

Dr. Peck is a brilliant individual, but his passion for ethics didn't result in a fascinating course. Many of our lectures were boring and dry, with occasional bouts of touching on interesting topics. The weekly writing assignment is a breeze, and the TAs help you prepare well for the final and research paper. Easy class? Yes. Interesting? Depends.

Peck is so funny and genuine. He's been through a lot&has great stories&solid perspectives. There's readings with a page paper&a quiz due every week. The readings can get long but they're still interesting. The TAs are great! Getting an A is totally doable- what is expected is very clear. I LOVED this class, you'll be a better person for taking it!

He's a nice guy, and has some interesting perspectives.  However, he has a tendency to forget to talk about the main part of his lecture and goes off on a random tangent.  That being said, he was funny and his class was actually very easy.  I got an 80 on one of the big papers and still easily pulled an A in the class.

The class was interesting and had some fun topics. But his instructions on the papers you have to write are really vague. And working things out with Dr. Peck is a pain. PS chose a easy topic for the research paper

Dr. Peck is by far the best professor at BYU.  He brings stories to life and is fascinating to listen to.  His stories are as good as the incredibly brilliant books that we writes.  If you haven't read his books, you are missing out on an adventure in your mind like no other.  "A Short Stay in Hell" is an all time favorite.  You won't put it down!
Class was pretty much useless. He's an interesting guy, but it was pointless to go to class, even though it was mandatory because all he did was talk about his opinions, which he tested us on later.

This class is great! Much more eye-opening than I thought it would be. Dr. Peck led great discussions and got us thinking. The TA sections and discussions were great too; I really liked figuring out my thought processes and talking over relevant issues with other students. There's some pretty dull reading and some test questions are kind of vague.

I can honestly say he's been my favorite professor here at BYU because I'm a graduating senior and have had a lot of them. Cares deeply about the subject matter taught and about his students and will go out of his way to meet with you and help you with anything. He's respectful towards everyones comments -- even ones that are truly absurd :)

Long class with even longer readings.  Even though it is suppose to be an exploration into religion and the environment it often seemed like it was heavily focused on making the religions look environmental.
Dr Peck has the most awesome stories in the world. He also has a way of helping you to understand the complexities that exist in different issues. It was an enjoyable, informative class.

Dr. Peck is a GREAT teacher.  The lecture part is very interesting-due to class participation and thought experiments.  The lab portion(run by TA's) is really awesome.  You spend the whole time discussing the issues you studied that week.  A TON, I repeat, a TON of reading.  You'll be easily reading 20-50 pages (if not more) a week.
Not that hard a class, but the professor can be a little confusing. Two tests, two larger papers, and then a one page paper every other week as well as weekly readings.
Best professor at BYU.  You will love his classes and his teaching style.  I wish all professors were more like Dr. Peck.

Good teacher, class not what you might expect though.  Its more about learning critical thinking than about the actual issues, though you learn that too.  You'll have to do a bit of reading for the class, too.
Really interesting lectures, understanding person

I loved Professor Waters, seriously the best 8am I have ever had. He is so funny, I was never bored in class. This is as hard class, and the textbook language was pretty difficult and took quite a bit to understand. I would take this class right after econ 110, having that information fresh made this class much easier.
One of my favorite professors. You will kick yourself if you take 380 from anyone else, even if his classes are at the crack of dawn. Genuinely so kind and cares about his students SO MUCH.

Take 380 from Waters. This is the only 8am I have never regretted taking. He teaches 380 in a way that is very understandable. You will not regret taking this class from him (unless you hate economics). I love this man so much I even follow him on instagram, and he posts pictures of birds and haikus. Very precious, very intelligent.
Hard course but Dr. Waters is awesome. I would definitely take this again from him

Definitely a hard class, but he's the best professor to teach the class. That being said, if you struggle with economics/calculus, this class will be hard for you. He is always willing to answer questions and does a good job lecturing (although it can be confusing, hence the need for questions). If you have to take this class, take it from him.

Waters is great! Super funny and gets to know everyone in the class. He teaches econ concepts very clearly (coming from an IR major). Attend and pay attention to lectures. Review the lecture notes regularly in addition to your notes. Lots of great resources to help you succeed. I just wish he did more practice problems in class.  Loved this class.

If you don't like Dr. Waters, that's on you. His lectures are engaging and make sense, and he makes coming to class a valuable resource. I wish he would do practice problems to connect principle with application, but he has good TAs that help with homework. Take 380 from him, he'll make it easiest to learn as long as you pay attention.

Great personality. Likes to jokingly pick on students. Huge Taylor swift fan so that's fun. Does 2 minute meditations before class that I liked. Homework not super similar to tests so be sure to go to TA reviews. Essays are super easy because we are literally supposed to use ChatGPT for them. Uses a lot of notation that can be confusing.
He is a great teacher. The TA is super helpful. The class is pretty easy if you spend enough time in his office hours. I probably did 1-2 hours of homework a week.

I took this course during a 21-credit load. That being said, this professor was one of the only professors that made me feel like I wasn't wasting my time during class. I felt motivated to pay attention during class because every minute was valuable. His TA is helpful too. The exams are exactly like the problem sets that are due every week.
Great at explaining concepts with real-world examples. Assignments are limited to a Problem Set due about every week and three easy essays.

Professor Waters is a great professor. His humor is sarcastic and slightly demeaning at times but all in good fun. I really struggled with his tests--and I studied HARD. The lectures and homework don't connect extremely well with the test material but he's still definitely worth taking.

Professor Waters is the common cool guy and crappy professor. Nice, open, and has work experience but refuses to give real world examples and vaguely understands the Macro Economy. Lots and lots of math questions and memorizing. Examples in class are a lot different than Homework and tests.
He's great

Dr. Waters is great! Econ 380 is just a tough class, but Dr. Waters does a great job teaching. No more than one homework assignment due every week or two, definitely go the TA lab for help with those are you'll be solid. Tests are very manageable. His lectures are great, he really wants you to succeed and teaches that way.

Great professor with real world experience. His lectures are entertaining and interesting. He knows the material and is great at explaining difficult concepts. He has lecture notes that he provides online. USE THEM. Also, find a group to study with, do the practice exams, and get help from the TA and you will be able to do well in this class.

Dr. Waters has been one of my favorite professors at BYU. I really enjoyed his class! The material is difficult, but he explains things in a way that make sense. I would recommend finding a group to study with otherwise the homework will be very difficult. Also, he was always available outside of class. I went to his office hours at least 10 times!

My favorite professor at BYU yet. Super funny guy, but very knowledgeable and helpful. Accessible outside of class. Cares about the students. The class itself is good toomoderate workload (1 assignment per week that can practically be checked against TA before turning in) and coursework not too challenging. LOVED both the class and Dr. Waters.

Dr. Waters has taught Econ 380 for 16 years as adjunct faculty while working at a consulting firm full-time, and it is very clear that he only teaches this class because he enjoys it and desires the best for students. Economics is not easy, but Dr. Waters explains things so well you will grasp the material. Office hours with him are way helpful!

Prof. Waters is great. He is ad junct and works at a firm in SLC, so he has real-world experience he brings to class which is cool. The workload is moderate, but you have to study a lot if you want to wrap your head around it. Super math-heavy, so get ready to buckle-up if that's not your strong suit. Hilarious and awesome professor though.

Dr. Waters is a great professor who is able to take the very difficult material taught in Price Theory and make it more accessible and interesting to anyone. Waters is a great choice for this class and I strongly recommend him. The class is hard but Waters does his best to help out anyone who needs it.
Really a truly great and funny professor. You will learn so much, it was really a great experience with very doable tests
By far the best professor I have seen at BYU. I strongly recommend his class.
Amazing professor! Easy too (well, as easy as advanced econ goes). Took me out to lunch a couple times, and knows a lot about life. I'd take him again in a heartbeat!
Great guy! This class is a must take from Dr. Waters! Don't make fun of his Dr. Pepper.

380 is a walk in the park if you're pro at calculus. If you're like me, and math isn't your strong point, then you're going to need some help. And having taken six different classes now in Econ, I can say unreservedly that Professor Waters is the most helpful professor I've had in BYU's Econ department. Would have failed the class without his help.
Best teacher I have had at BYU. The material can be tough but he is willing to work with you. Must take it from Dr. Waters.

Dr. Waters' explanations were very helpful and relatable. He demonstrated concern for us in and out of class, and helped to explain econ from an ethical perspective as well as an academic perspective. It was great to have access to all of the lecture notes. Very helpful to students who would like networking or career advice.
Hands down the best professor that I have every had and an incredible human being as well. If he is still there when my kids are old enough, his class will be a mandatory option.

Dr. Waters teaches not-economists economics for his job (he's adjunct faculty) and he is good at it. 380 is  a must take from Waters. Don't worry about buying the textbook. I didn't crack it open more than once.
Great teacher, no way I would take the class from anyone else.

Waters teaches this remarkably well. He's funny, keeps it light, and challenges you to learn the material. It was both rigorous and fair, and if you do your homework, study reasonably well and attend the TA reviews, you can definitely get an A. Take 380 from Waters

Dr Waters was excellent. Subject matter gets dry (duh, it's economics) but he was able to make class enjoyable. Definitely recommend going to class since he explains things better, but most of what he says is in his notes he makes available.

I really liked Prof. Waters. It was an 8 o'clock class, but he was still able to keep me awake. Really kind, fun, relaxed and helpful. Going in to speak with him in his office was the most helpful. Of course, don't be shy to take him up on his lunch offers! Great person!
Waters is legit
Dr. Waters is an awesome professor. His grading is fair and you will do well if you pay attention and work all of the problem sets with the TA's.
One of the greatest professors that I have had at BYU! Pick him up on the offer to go out to lunch with him. He is definitely worth getting to know.
Awesome professor...Clear, funny, straightforward...I don't know why would anyone take someone else for 380..!!

Fantastic professor. His greatest concern is that his students understand. Waters works as a litigation consultant/expert witness, so his main experience with economics comes from outside the classroom, so he has a great perspective. He grades by improvement, so if you fail a midterm but ace the final, you can get an A.

Very smart professor, knows how to present material at an appropriate level for this class. He makes his lecture notes available online making it so the textbook isn't used as much. His notes are much more clear anyway. Goes at an appropriate pace for the class and tries to make sure everyone understands.  Highly recommended

Excellent, excellent professor. Only concerned with helping students learn and prepare for the future. Keeps dry material interesting. Very good at explaining difficult concepts so that anyone can understand. Always willing to help and answer questions. Does anything he can to help prepare for a career. One of the absolute best teachers at BYU.

Great professor, clear notes, and well planned lectures.  The hardest part of this class is making the connection between what he teaches you, and the problems that he gives you.  He teaches you how to think and reason, not how to solve the problems.  The tests were fair, but difficult.  A good TA can make a world of difference.  Great professor.

Great teacher, he has a full time job but teaches part time because he like the students and he is good at teaching.  His lectures notes are very neat and  clear, you will not use the book.  He is a great teacher, and it is a fair class overall, although somewhat difficult.

Easily my favorite econ professor, possibly my favorite professor at byu. very organized and clear in his teaching. the material is challenging, but Waters makes it very doable. He truly cares about his students.

One of the best teachers i have ever had.  380 can be confusing but Dr. Waters is so organized and clear that he makes understanding the material as easy as possible.  It is one of the most important classes offered by the department and it is important to have a good teacher (like Dr. Waters) lay this microeconomic foundation.  I

You can't say enough about Dr. Waters.  He is an excellent teacher, great lecturer, and an even better person.  He genuinely cares about his students, and is willing to help them in any way possible. He is extremely organized and teaches a potentially confusing subject with precision and clarity. If at all possible take his class. Waters is the man
Prof. Waters is awesome. He really cares about his students, and explains difficult material very well. One of the best professors I've had at BYU.
Dr. waters is the best.. He cares about each student, and will help on a very personal level. By far the best proffesor for 380

Wonderful class - I am so glad that I took Econ 380 from Dr. Waters.  The subject matter can be challenging, but Dr. Waters' great organization and clarity seem to minimize that difficulty.  The class notes that he posts for the students are fantastic.  He takes an active interest in the lives/futures of his students (he knew my name right away)

Waters is probably the best 380 prof at BYU. He's a great lecturer and he really pushes the students to know the material. He also makes a sincere effort to help students see some of the career paths for economists. I wouldn't take anyone else for a class as important as 380.

pdf lecture notes make class very organized and test prep easy.  Difficult subject matter, but he explains it well.  Book almost unnecessary, but used also for Econ 381.  Lots of derivative calculus - make sure you know your Math 112!

Awesome teacher! Take him if you can. Great lecturer. He tries to bring in real life examples, either from current research or work he has done as a consultant. Very willing to help students. Funny guy that loves his students. The class is quite hard though, so form study groups and study hard.

The class is very hard, but Waters makes sure you understand what you are learning. His tests are made to make you think without any hints. He cares about his students future and will help if you go talk to him.

Very interesting class but very difficult for the first part of the semester.  Gets easier as things go along and he's a great teacher.  Doesn't curve much since some grades are high.  Good teacher for Price Theory.

This class is very interesting, your homework is watching shows and an occasional assignment to go along with it. Prof Anderson provides the slides from each class and is happy to accommodate students' needs. Only one final exam and a couple essays. Sometimes the lectures can drag on, but overall great class! Be aware assignments are graded late.

Only a couple of homework assignments, which are easy, but papers are graded relatively harshly. He grades things months late, and the final is very intense and with a large portion of the grade. This class was all over the place and lectures get confusing, as he explains film as if you are already a film historian. I wouldn't recommend.

Homework is easy, papers are tough. Beware: some assignments are scheduled last minute (don't expect to know the due dates) he grades things weeks later, feedback on papers isn't that helpful, and the research paper & final are together worth 55% of your grade. Dr. Anderson is a nice guy, but, unless film is your passion, take a different class.

Prof Anderson certainly knows the field he teaches. But this class whooped me. Its long lectures and he goes through TONS of content at a time. They are interesting but Take good notes. Grad was just based on the four exams in the class and a paper you turn in at the end. But the exams are tough and have around 30-50 terms you must know in depth.

Professor Anderson is probably my favorite professor I've had at BYU. He's a quirky guy but he cares so much about history and he can tell when the lectures get boring and tries to make them more interesting! He also is looking to help you, and tried to help our whole class out when he could! Absolutely would take him again if I got a chance!

I found Professor Anderson to be incredibly helpful. I learned a lot. He helps us learn how to effectively write, and is also very kind. He spends hours carefully reading all the work we turn in and gives good feedback. I would highly recommend taking Historian's Craft from him.

This was a pretty good professor, and flexible at times with grading when he feels he's fallen short. When I needed to miss class, the TA's were super helpful. Barely did any of the readings and skimmed when needed and got an A-. Still I got that grade by studying hard, and fill out the study guide during class!! Only one paper, but 4 exams.

I found Anderson's grading difficult to understand, but he was always accessible out of class, so meeting with him about questions helped a ton. you should do fine so long as you take his feedback to heart, and put effort into your assignments (he can tell if you wrote it the night before!)

Really nice guy! Lectures were a little boring and slides weren't super helpful to look back on, so paying attention in class is VERY important. This class had a lot of readings, but you can skimp on a some and still do well. SUPER nitpicky when grading writing assignments, but he was willing to meet with me and improve my essay draft one on one

I enjoyed his lectures but tests were BRUTAL. Didn't feel like test were about lecture material at all. Do not recommend if you're looking for a simple GE, I studied like none other for this class and still got eaten alive on exams. He was interesting, just wish his tests were structured differently.
Dr. Anderson is really funny and very aware of his audience! I will say although no attendance is mandatory, still go. Tests are kinda hard. ALSO DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK, it's a waste of money
Professor Anderson really cares about his students! Super chill and would make real effort to make lectures more interesting. Exams are pretty tough.
Great guy. Loved him as a professor. He's a pretty tough grader. Theres not much assignments but their all written and require lots of effort.

I really like Prof. Anderson. He truly cares about you as a student and tries to make lectures interesting. He always posts the slides, so if you ever miss a day it's not the end of the world. He is funny and engaging and I would recommend him to anybody. Tests aren't too hard either, but require effort and understanding.

tests are all handwritten. if you prepare for tests, you can probably do pretty good. he's super nice and willing to work with you. he won't grade you on the readings or attendance, but it's not a bad idea to show up. you might not fail if you never go though.

Professor Anderson is a nice guy who loves history. The workload is pretty reasonable, and tests are straightforward (class average typically around a high B). He is very understanding and down to earth. I would totally recommend him for anyone looking for an easy GE.

Prof Anderson is a super nice guy. Tests aren't really that difficult, they're just graded harshly. I can't believe I got an A in this class. I do not like history so this class was very difficult for me and required MANY hours of studying. Unless you have a love of history I do not recommend. The comment below about critical thinking is so true!!!

Prof Anderson made what could have been a boring class both interesting and personal. He was reasonable, too--when the university-assigned readings felt repetitive, he dropped a few. He recognized that UNIV 101 shouldn't be our top priority and didn't treat it like that, but made it meaningful at the same time. He clearly cares about his students.
Be prepared for him to say "indicative" a lot. In all seriousness he was a G. Whole class was dying of laughter at all his jokes. Just a chill guy.

You dont need the textbook. Probably spent 30 mins on homework a week and his lectures cover everything you need to know for the test. He understands that your most likely taking the class for GE credit and makes the course pretty easy

Lots of reading but you don't need any of it. He gives you all test terms at the start of each unit. All are covered in lecture, but tests are more than memorization and require critical thinking & connection beyond his lecture points. All free response, no multiple choice.

Graded by 3 midterms, the final, a research paper, and weekly dialogue.

One of the kindest and most accommodating profs I have had. His class is doable if you put in some work. Exams are open ended but you know all the terms during the whole unit. Only other assignments are weekly discussion prompts and an essay. He wants you to succeed but also understands this is a required GE, would recommend!

Professor Anderson is truly a great man and a great historian. He clearly cares about teaching and is completely willing to meet with students and help in whatever what he can. I met with him several times and he was always helpful and understanding about whatever issue. Truly one of the best professors I've had.

Professor Anderson is a great professor, you can really see the care that he puts into the material he covers. He is very enthusiastic and energetic when he teaches. He has an amazing teaching style and the material covered isn't too difficult. However there is not a clear outline for what he expects on the tests, which can be graded harshly.

This might be one of my favorite classes at BYU! There were a lot of movies/TV shows to watch for homework, but they were pretty fun and watching them all was not critical to getting a good grade. Reading was not really required. The class interesting as we went over the history of the 20th century through the lens of screen and radio media.

You can tell that Prof. Anderson really loves what he teaches. That being said, don't bother buying the textbook, just go to lectures, take good notes and you'll be fine. DO NOT procrastinate studying. Tests are based solely on memorization of material so work hard and you can get an A. Really engaging class though so I would recommend!

Like others have said, he's one of BYU's best. Expects participation in discussions, so do the readings. Enthusiastic, knowledgeable, big vocab.

I kept a running list of words he used, here are a few personal favorites: anathema, duplicitously, succinctly enumerated, fomented. He just whips these words out of his pocket, it's pretty impressive.

One of my favorite professors of all time. Class is organized well, with not too many assignments but enough you weren't stressing. One "big" research paper, but he's very accessible if you need help. Very understanding guy who gives great lectures and posts everything online. His tests are all in-class instead of in the testing center, love.

The lectures are kind of boring, but it is a relatively easy class to take. You can download the slides from lecture if you miss class and should still be fine. The test layout is the same for each test, so you know what to expect. For the final, there is an essay, but he shows you the list of prompts and you get to choose which one you write on.

Dr. Anderson is amazing. He cares so much about History and his students. As someone with a love for history, I really enjoyed his lectures. He doesn't assign a bunch of useless assignments and has very clear grading requirements for his assignments and tests.

I have never had a professor who was so disrespectful. His tests are graded so hard. No matter how much I studied or what class notes I took he still managed to find reasons to take off points on my exams. He is a very harsh grader and very condescending. After one of my midterms he wrote on the bottom of my exam "did you even study".

Professor Anderson is great. His TA's are not. Tests are hard but not impossible. Professor Anderson cares and structures the lectures well. I really appreciated having him as a professor. Great guy and a great lecturer.
He has a lot of slides for this class, but he keeps his lectures entertaining and informational. I learned a ton from this class, and he is one of my favorite professor that I have taken.

Professor Anderson is my favorite professor I have ever had! He is kind of a tough grader, but also very fair. He is always willing to help you get the grade you want. His lectures are always super interesting, and everyone in the class has come to love and respect him. He requieres a lot, but it comes from wanting you to succeed.

I can tell Professor Anderson cares about what he's teaching. A Packback assignment due every week, 3 midterms, and 1 final (half of the final was basically midterm 4, and the other half was a cumulative essay). Flashcards worked well for me for the midterms. I got the grade I did because I did not put in the work I should have. Professor is great.

He designed the course so that we learned so much. The packback assignments were kind of annoying at first but I realized later that it helped me learn about whatever I wanted to in the context of the course. Professor Anderson really loves history and what he was teaching about! He knows a lot and is just a good guy.

I loved taking from Professor Anderson and went to class looking forward to his lectures. This course is graded by a weekly online discussion, three tests, one research paper, and a final exam. His tests take a bit of prep, but honestly, just fill out the study guide and make flashcards as you learn the material and you'll be fine!

Such a good professor. Very clear criteria and tests are pretty easy if you know the terms on the study guide he gives you. He's super helpful if you have questions. 4 tests that aren't that bad and one, 3 page research paper that's easy if you ask the TAs for help. Highly recommend.

Professor Anderson is great. He's a really nice guy and cares about all his students. He liked to say a prayer for us before each test. Attendance isn't required but I would really suggest it. Pay attention to his slides/presentation but really focus on what he says; that is where I got the majority of my notes from. Super funny guy, great teacher.

Professor Anderson is very passionate about history and he is good at getting the class involved in lectures. He initially explained the tests to be pretty straightforward but then ended up grading extremely hard and was super picky with our free response answers so unless we were super detailed with every question, we'd get docked many points.

Professor Anderson is a great professor! He takes the time to make sure we feel prepared on our assignments and gives useful feedback. Class discussions are always interesting and a pleasure to attend.

Dr Anderson is a very caring Prof, so he will work with you when needed. His class is very interesting, and he is very entertaining. There are not a lot of grades (a few assignments, a paper, and final), but almost all the "readings" were movies. Overall, great class.

Professor Anderson is a wonderful person and honestly super understanding and helpful. If you love history- this will be a great class for you! However, he often assumes that you know all about terms/events that your 7th grade history teacher maybe mentioned once... Also, the tests are really hard. Like really hard. Take hours and hours of prep!!:(

Dr. Anderson is a really good professor he is interested in lectures and tries to keep everything entertaining. But make sure you study for exams and understand all of the terms or they will be very difficult. Don't worry yourself too much about the readings, as long as you attend the lectures and take notes you'll do fine.

This class didn't have many assignments, but most of them were really hard. Professor Anderson is a really picky grader. He's willing, however, to go over work before you submit it, which I would recommend doing. Nice guy but a stressful class. P.S. I wouldn't take this class as a freshman.

This class is all about writing a big research paper. Class periods are usually short with little need to prepare. Anderson is awesome and super willing to help you outside of class. The TA was great too. Anderson wants you to succeed and is super kind yet honest. He gives good feedback and criticism. Please participate in class, he deserves it lol

Disclaimer: I'm a history major. I loved this class. The lectures were good and the readings helped but weren't necessary. Anderson is nice, patient, and reasonable. Tests required lots of studying but expectations were clear. (I don't think they were too hard.) Very little hw. Take what TAs say w/ grain of salt. Go to class and you'll be fine.
Dr Anderson is super chill and gives good lectures. Tests are pretty hard- you have to memorize a lot. Pay attention, take notes, and ask questions and you'll do fine.

We only had 1 paper the entire semester and he gave us lots of time to work on it as well. The TA's are super helpful if you have questions or get stuck during the essay. If you go to class, or even just look over the slides and understand the concepts then you will be good for the tests, make sure you know the "significances" of the Key IDs

Professor Anderson obviously cares for his students and is very accommodating, especially with deadlines. He is easy to talk to outside of class if you need help and he wants to be involved with his students. He infuses his lectures with some humor which makes class time enjoyable.

He's easy to understand, smart, and compassionate. This class takes effort, but that makes sense for a course that teaches us how to become historians. My advice: try to review every assignment with him before turning it in. If you do it ahead of the deadline and give him time to read it, his feedback gives you a second chance at the assignment.

He's very humble and really respects his students' thoughts. His lectures are really dry, but he does have a little bit of a sense of humor that helps. He's super chill and lets move your test if you're out of town (like for a wedding, etc.) as long as you plan ahead. Tests are all short answer, and there is a paper but it's not too bad.

I learned a lot from this class, and I liked Professor Anderson. I did pretty bad on the first midterm but wayy better the next two, so just make sure to fully understand what the tests entail and study for them. If you have the dates and significance down, you'll be good. A bit of reading, and tests are super important to grade, but a good class!

Professor Anderson does his best at making this GE class engaging and explaining why history is important and applicable in all fields of study. He gives you a study guide at the beginning of each unit so you know exactly what will be on the test. Only one paper and you get to decide if you do it the first or second half of the semester.

There aren't that many things that show up on your grade, which makes for an easy semester, but a tough A at times. If you put a lot of effort into the few tests, and assignments you should be good. He is very flexible and helpful if you ask for help.

Prof. Anderson makes this GE good & bearable. He makes it known exactly what you need to know/understand for his tests & he is very open with your responses. Also, don't buy the textbook. He wants you to read, but his lectures are better for info. I haven't used my book more than twice. He's a great professor for this class & I would recommend him.

As a professor? Very likeable & engaging. As a class? Can get pretty stressful preparing for the short answer tests - having good general knowledge of over 35+ terms. Get started on those ASAP. Only 1 essay. He lets you decide writing it either the 1st or 2nd half of the semester. Workload is basically reading. Just worry about the tests

Dr. Anderson was by far the best History teacher I've had. His lectures were fascinating, and he always paid attention to the needs of the classes, stopping and telling stories when we got bored. This was also the hardest I've ever had to work for my grade. His tests are not memorization tests: he expects you to understand the *why* of history.

His style is adaptable and enthusiastic. He teaches in a very clear manner and implements hands-on learning. There were only half a dozen assignments focusing on the 10-12 page research paper which didn't turn out to be as hard as I had thought. I learned more about how to write research papers than I feel like I would have with with anyone else!

I love Dr. Anderson. He's super relaxed and funny. I'm taking a second class from him now and he remembered my name after two and a half years, from a lecture of 200. Really good guy, very accessible and willing to help. Tests are done in class, which is awesome. Just make sure you stay on top of things, and you'll be fine.

I loved Dr. Anderson's Holocaust class!  Definitely my favorite history class I've taken so far. You do read a lot, but they are interesting and help you learn.  He is so passionate about the topic and knows his stuff.  There's a pretty equal balance between lecture and discussion. He grades papers pretty tough, but the tests are open ended & good.

I took 309 and 498 from Dr Anderson. He was definitely my favorite professor at BYU (no question). He is brilliant yet very down to earth and approachable. His lectures are so well structured and engaging. The homework wasn't too heavy but he is a tougher grader when it comes to papers. Tests were essay format. I learned so much from his classes.
One of my favorite professors at BYU. The class is pretty easy and I've taken more classes from him. Definitely take this class.

Dr. Anderson is very concerned for his students and tries to keep us interested and involved throughout each lecture. You can tell he really loves the material. The exams are difficult, but you will do fine if you understand his expectations, study early, and meet with him after each exam to discuss how you could improve your ID answers.

This man tries his absolute hardest to make the class enjoyable for everyone, it's just unfortunate that it's a history class and boring by nature. He makes some hilarious comments which make it better. Very few grades (4 short essay/answer tests, 1 research paper) which makes it challenging to get a good grade, but he's clear about what he wants.

He is very endearing and it is obvious he wants his students to participate in his class. That being said, his tests are over the top when it comes to a GE course. a LOT of memorization and all the tests are short answer and short essay. If you don't word things the way he wants you to, you will be docked. Wouldn't recommend for a GE class.

Amazing professor if you like history. He is very passionate about the subject. He loves to liven the class up by watching youtube and videos throughout his lectures. He's laid back and willing to work with students. I was sick during a test. I contact him an hour before and he was very accommodating.  Really awesome teacher. Highly recommend
The class was difficult mostly because it required a lot of reading and memorizing. I studied hard, but it still wasn't enough for the tests  that were a huge chunk of our grade.

Overall, Dr. Anderson is just a really nice guy. Although the topics in his lectures were a little boring, he does his best to change them up and get the students involved. Very knowledgable, patient, and willing to help. I would take a class from him again.

This class covers a lot of material but Pr Anderson does a good job at giving us even the basis on each topic. He was willing to work with the students, made the tests easier, and only assigns one paper in the entire semester. If you put some effort in it, it will be an easy class.
He is hilarious and brilliant.

I loved Dr. Anderson. He's very kind and funny. He is also very knowledgeable! He gives really great lectures, even on topics that I had absolutely zero interest in I still felt engaged in his class. Reading can be done without. Tests are a lot of memorization and application, but nothing too bad. One really short research paper that's easy.
Once you take the first test, it's really easy to ace the following ones. All of his tests are the same and he tells you exactly what to study. Super nice.

The class was really interesting, but the lectures could get pretty long sometimes.  He tries to involve students though, which is hard in a big class.  Tests were very straight-forward, and if you can memorize well, very doable.  Very approachable.  Readings were pointless, cus it was all covered in lecture.  If  you take Hist 202, take from him

Prof. Anderson told us exactly what he expected. He gave us a list of terms and the  essay questions well before the tests. One essay, but it wasn't bad at all. He doesn't believe in multiple choice which made tests a bit challenging for me, but they were very fair. He told us that he wants to start doing reading quizzes.

Best professor I've had at BYU. Tests are based mostly on the lecture. No reading quizzes in this class, but does have several class periods dedicated to discussing the readings. Assignments were interesting & largely self-directed. He teaches by theme, which is very clear. I highly recommend taking a class from him.

He is a great teacher and very clear about what he is expecting for tests. I liked the class because there wasn't very much busy work. He just had 4 tests and a written paper. The tests are all written which can be difficult for some people.

He cares about getting to know you- he memorizes all his students names and faces. I think that's really cool. Lectures are interesting- he tries to get the students involved. Course is comprised of 3 written exams (short answerparagaph length) and an essay assignment. Find buddies to study with- and you'll do just fine!

Favorite teacher ever. Lectures are fantastic, highlight of my week. Excellent awareness of the students. Is SUPER passionate about history and is honestly hilarious. Grade is made up of 4 tests and a paper, thats it. Seems tough, but he gives EXCELLENT study guides, it's just up to you to study. Honestly cannot say enough about this teacher.

Fun class.  Though it is a history class, he still allows you to take the subject material and see how it has effected the now.  Fun lecturer who keeps you interested.  Do the reading, he does not require it, but class discussion is so much more enjoyable if you do, and you will do better in the class.

He is a very nice guy. Class is pretty boring. The only thing that he cares about is your test grades and 1 essay. He doesn't care about homework, attendance, or participation. Tests are difficult. This class is basically 100 percent memorization. Would not recommend taking it but it is a GE.

I really liked the class but I dont feel he is a very fair grader. Not only was my midterm grade LOST, but was also docked points on essays for following TA's instructions. There is a HUGE lack of communication between the professor and TAs. The TAs were no help on reviewing my essay and gave me NO feedback on what the prof actually looks for. Poor

Decided to minor in history because of this class.  He actually talks about other parts of the world besides Europe/America, which is AWESOME.  Organize the ID terms by theme and you'll have an easier time studying.  Go to his office hours for help on your paper.  He is very kind and I LOVED THIS CLASS!

I hate essays. Our grade was made up of a 5 paragraph essay for the midterm (w/ a few short-essay Q's as well), two 5 paragraph essays for the final, and a 'research' essay project during the semester. Dr. Anderson is great though, you can tell he gets stoked on history which I like. Not a bad GE.

My first history class was terrible and I was expecting more of the same, but I was surprised by the quality of this class. Professor Anderson has interesting lectures and gets the class involved. I did not like his tests, but I got a B+ in the class anyways.

I absolutely hated my first history class and was not looking forward to this class.  Prof. Anderson made his classes really interesting, and since he is a little younger, tries to put himself in our shoes, so I ended up enjoying it.  For a GE class I really enjoyed him as a teacher

Professor Anderson makes history enjoyable. I did not read the textbook, and I still managed to do well in the class. You will do a large research project, but it's nothing terrible. Highly recommend Professor Anderson, especially if you hate history but need to "get it out of the way."
1 paper all semester.  Quizzes on the reading very infrequently.  Knows his stuff and does his best to make it interesting (to be fair, I'm not a history fan).

Fantastic teacher, very rough grader. There is no homework besides reading before each class, for the pop quizzes, so the work load is really light. He gives you all of the terms you need to know and the topics you need to know for the essays on the tests, but he grades super super hard on the tests to "make up" for it.Take only if good at writing

Great teacher! loved what he taught and how he taught! He really made History entertaining and loved attending his class. His calss is graded simply on essays, if you are not a good writer or do not like writing DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He is a ver rough grader. And it is a history class so very subjective on what you write about.

This semester I got 6 A's and one B-. Anderson was my B-. It's an OK class, he just expects you to know WAY too much for the tests. It doesn't help that he's really picky grader either. What I thought were good essays he marked down quite a bit. Bottom line - if you like written tests then this is the class for you. If not find another prof.

Oh my goodness. take this class! I loved this class. Not only was Professor Anderson a really fun and helpful teacher, but the way he taught and organized his class made it super easy to get an A. The tests were fair. If you take this class, do the readings and study for the tests and you'll do just fine.

Prof. Anderson is great! I would absolutely recommend him to anyone taking this class.He really gets into the lectures and makes it interesting.  The tests are written and not too bad if you study- he gives you a study guide with a list of possible terms and essay questions. He is great. TAKE HIM

I took Hist 202 and it was by far the most interesting GE I've taken at BYU. He is passionate about teaching, he truly cares about you. He's pretty young in the dept, his research area is German Media. Prof. Anderson makes you think about the importance of what is studied in class. His exams are written, if you study you'll do great.TAKE HIS CLASS!

I took it during SPRING. You have to read ca 20 pages for the next lecture (not bad!). Exams are written and you have 1 hr. If you are better at writing and memorizing than at multiple choice, you should take this class. There is also a 5-page paper. Anderson is a great professor- young and very understanding of what work is really important.

I only took this class for a GE but it turned out alright. His lectures are good and he tries really hard to make sure everyone understands the material. The two tests (midterm and final) are written and timed but if you study for them you should be fine. He gives a study guide for them. There is also one paper for the class, which isn't bad.

Professor Stuart is very caring and attentive. The topic of the class is a little hard to wrap your head around at first, but the class is made to accommodate for that; if you ask for help, Professor Stuart makes sure you understand each step so you don't get behind. Workload wasn't too exhaustive, but there are a couple of books to read.

Dr. Stuart understands so much about US History and is very relatable in lectures. Sometimes he tries to be too indifferent to things; it can become confusing, but overall, his class was great. He has a range of assignments for the class, so the exams won't kill your grade if you don't do the best on them. There is a lot of in-class handwriting.

Lectures are the best! He's so smart but VERY understanding. You will learn so much about history and humanity. Book quizzes are no joke! I read every word, studied, and wrote great notes but I was SO disappointed in my scores. Don't procrastinate project. 2 exams=tons of material to study at one time. Do not leave it until a few days before.

This is your classic professor that takes his general class way to seriously4 books worth of stuff during the semester, write a 15 page essay, go to 4 speeches on campus, write 5 essays on news articles, and be ready for a quiz each and every class period on about 50 pages of reading (3 classes and quizzes/ week). Nice guy, unrealistic expectations

I really enjoyed this class! It is not too hard, but there is a semester long project. The tests are relatively easy and there are only two of them. It is very interesting and Professor Stuart is a great lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory, but it will help with the tests if you go to class. I'd highly recommend this class! Take it!

Fantastic professor! He cares about his students & makes the funniest comments during lectures. Assignments are fairly easy & he is not a harsh grader. The Midterm/final are low stress too. Some instructions on his assignments/projects were confusing, but just talk to him & he will help you. Very friendly teacher who wants you to succeed.

Dr. Stuart is a nice person but it seemed like he didn't know what he was doing. Most of the lecture time was spent talking about things that weren't applicable and he was so vague about assignments, most students forgot about them because he just wouldn't talk about them. The class was frustrating at times because he didn't give clear instructions

Dr. Stuart is one of my favorite professors at BYU. He was a mentor and gave great feedback in regards to the projects assigned. He has an amazing way of making you feel inspired about history! Definitely take this class from Dr. Stuart.
One of my favorite professors! Very kind and very open-minded.

Prof Stuart is an amazing professor. He is so caring and will help you with anything you need. You just need to ask him. His lectures were long cause the class was long but I kept super engaged. Also, if you have questions, he is happy to stop the lecture and go off topic to answer questions. Definitely recommend. Not an easy A but worth it .

I am not a history major so yes I did struggle, but Professor Stuart was extremely helpful. He cares and wants you to do well. There was a lot of reading, but I would expect that from any history class. Questions on tests and Q's were fair. Pay attention to lectures and slides! There is extra credit. With some work, you can get the grade you want.

Professor Stuart is a great professor. He is a very humble genuine person who teaches complex topics completely and well. There is a lot of reading, but the readings and class are set up for you to learn. If you show up and care about the class you will do great. I never thought any of his test or quiz questions were unfair.

Lots of reading! You'll be reading literally hundreds of pages of academic articles throughout the semester, in addition to two books. As you complete this reading, you'll be quizzed on very specific details that are buried in the text and that are tangentially related to the main topic; take note of (seemingly) insignificant information.

Easier than you thinkThere are reading quizzes at least once a week, but you'll be fine as long as you ID the important themes/objects in the reading. You're required to read 3 books, but the quizzes are easy. (he gives you the questions ahead of time and picks from those). Grading is very lax and "if you give a crap, you'll get an A"

this is my last religion class for credit at BYU. professor stuart is the best religion teacher at BYU (he knows his material and is humble about it) Just keep up with readings and go to class. only con is his tests are REALLY specific. just regurgitate. NO BUSY WORK IN CLASS. you learn lots in lecture. well balanced between spiritual/intellectual.

Professor Stuart is one of the best professors I have ever had - and not just in the Religion Department. His lectures are full of information and he really encourages discussions in class. Class is always inspirational and is set up in such a way that any question you have is answered in a way that helps build you up.

Very smart and works hard at crafting good lessons. She is incredibly friendly, positive, and flexible! She gives us extensions on assignments, and asks us how we want to use class time. Cares about improving our writing, and gives us amazing, constructive feedback to help us. Genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had. 11/10!!!

Professor Simmons is AWESOME!! You can tell she cares a lot about her students and the quality of her class. She's always willing to meet with you outside of class to discuss your papers and give you feedback. If you have to take WRTG 150, take it from her!!

Professor Sunshine Simmons consistently demonstrated her dedication to helping students succeed every day. She gave great feedback and clear guidelines on what was expected for each project. Another thing that I loved was that she gave us plenty of time to work on papers. If you plan your time out, you won't have to cram-write essays.

Professor Simmons was an exceptional instructor! She was so helpful in providing quality feedback that helped to improve both my understanding of rhetoric and how I could improve each of my papers. She is a very easy grader, just make sure to put in effort on each assignment. She genuinely cares about each of her students too!

This is by far the best writing class I have ever taken. You can tell that Professor Simmons wants nothing more than for her students to succeed. She makes sure that if you need help, the resources are there. She is also very understanding and willing to fit your needs.
Great professor would 100% recommend! Many extra credit options and corrections. Attendance matters, so you do have to show up.

Professor Simmons obviously cares about her students. She also understands the purpose behind what she teaches, meaning she makes the curriculum very relevant to real life and really avoids busy work, which I appreciated. There's a good amount of work in her classes but if you stay on top of it its very manageable. Professor Simmons is the coolest!
Professor Simmons is such an amazing professor who really cares for her students and is more than willing to meet with you and help you out.
Goated professor is literally so caring and friendly. This was the only writing or English class I have ever taken that I enjoyed the content and learned something, the best teacher ever.
Professor Simmons is the best professor I have ever had. Her Writing 150 class is great, she listens to student feedback and is very willing to work with students outside of class.

I LOVED Professor Simmons. The work load for her class was so manageable. All the assignments except for the four big papers are graded by completion. She makes sure to walk you through the four big papers and gives you plenty of time to work on them. She also meets with each student one on one before a big paper and gives you feedback.
Professor Simmons is so kind and caring and work so well with her students! She really wants you to succeed. I would highly recommend taking her class.

I had Professor Simmons for the summer term, and she was amazing! There is a lot of writing and reading, but if you stay on top of it, you will be good. She is also very nice and understanding. If you have any questions or concerns, you can reach out, and she will help you

I had Professor Simmons for summer semester and shes was THE BEST! She is very aware of the workload of students and is always willing to help. She is really clear on the expectations of assignments and is an easy grader. She grades off of effort for the most part so its and easy class if you put in a little effort.
Professor Simmons is really awesome. Her class is not easy, but she is always so ready to help with whatever you need.
Very good professor! Lot's of far left news material but besides that the class was a blast.

Professor Simmons is the Nicest professor you will have. She was my first professor of my college carrer and she was so amazing. She is very understanding and willing to help out, if you go to her office hours she will love you. You need to be sure to turn in your assignments on time but twice I needed an extension and she gave it to me easily.

I loved Professor Simmons. She is caring and willing to work with you if you're having trouble with content or projects. She's also a great writer and gives specific, helpful feedback at project check-ins, then helps you get started on your editing or outline right there. She is also super accessible outside of class and wants you to succeed.

Sister Morris is amazing! She is a fair grader and will genuinely help you improve your writing. She lets you write about topics you choose, which makes writing way more enjoyable. Take this class from her!

Not my favorite class. It definitely felt like I was doing busy work several times. Professor Morris is very nice, but there were several times where I asked her a question related to the course material, and she would just Google the answer in front of the class.
Professor Morris is so kind and considerate! She really cares about students. If you show up to class and turn in your assignments you will get an A in this class.
Professor Morris was super nice! I am a math major and therefore do not have much confidence in writing, but she made this class feel very manageable and easy!

Sister Morris is an amazing teacher. She is super chill and cancels a class a lot in order for you to have extra time to write your essays. ( I didn't need the extra time but it was nice to have class canceled) I never read the textbook and got an A in the class. Sister Morris is a charismatic teacher. I really liked haveing her

Professor Morris is so kind! You can tell that she truly cares about her students. Her lectures are informative and focus on what we feel unsure about. She has papers due every week, but they are short and she gives excellent feedback on them. Although we had many assignments, I never felt overwhelmed.

For 90% of this semester, I had an A. As long as I showed effort I got a good grade, and her class was probably my favorite. Two weeks before the semester ends, on the biggest assignment of the course, I got a 68. My grade dropped 14 points. I was baffled and honestly still am. She grades inconsistently so beware of that if you take her courses

Prof. Morris is a great professor! She gives great feedback on every essay & makes sure she talks with you at least one point during the writing process for most of the papers. She uses classes wisely - for some papers we were put into groups & wouldn't need to go to class the days our group wasn't scheduled for. She knows what she's talking about.

Professor Morris was fantastic! I felt like she genuinely wanted to help me succeed. She was kind and clear when giving feedback on papers and she was fair when grading assignments. I would definitely take a class from her again.

Sister Morris was one of the best professors I've had a BYU. She gave really good writing feedback and I loved her focus on grammar in the class. She is a very kind lady and genuinely cares about the wellbeing of her students. You won't regret taking her class.

Don't get me wrong, she's great. Awesome personality with a passion for writing. Only downside is it was more about what she wanted and less about what you wanted to write about. She had rubrics laid out for each paper, but they were pretty vague; I regularly missed points for things not listed in the rubric.

Honestly felt confused in her class the whole semester on what we needed to do for every class. The class felt a little disorganized and chaotic. Nice lady, but seemed like she didn't have time to focus on the students a whole lot. I appreciate the feedback she gave on papers, you could tell she knows what she is doing!
One of the kindest and most flexible professors I've had. Very reasonable about my accommodations.

Professor Morris is an incredible professor. If you want to learn how to be a better writer, take her class. She is very passionate about her work and her students. She cares about making your experience the best possible. I learned so much in this class and felt that the work had meaning and purpose. She's seriously one of the nicest people I know

I loved Professor Morris. She structures the class very nicely. As someone who doesn't like to write, she is the kind of professor you are willing to write for. She always gives great feedback and as long as you fix the things she says, you'll get an A. She was easy to reach outside of class. Lots of papers but she spreads them out so you have time

Sister Morris was a solid choice for Persuasive Writing. She is very meek and kind! 3 Major papers throughout the semester with a few side projects, no tests! Only thing that make this class hard was the amount of writing, but that's expected. She does a good job helping you along the writing process and is a fair grader. Engages the class as well.

BEST PROFESSOR AT BYU!!!! I am a senior this was my last semester and Mrs. Morris was the first professor in my 5 years here that I felt actually cared that I LEARNED something. She is an EXCELLENT teacher and all of the homework is actually important and worth doing (not much though)

If you don't like writing and dreaded doing the advanced writing GE, this class is for you. Susan allows you to write on things that actually interest you and she cares about you (I missed class cause I needed a mental health day and she brought me candy the next class). Papers build on each other so the daunting 10 page paper is not bad.

Simply the best professor I've ever had!! Doesn't matter if you're an English major or someone who is terrible at writing, Professor Morris will help you improve your writing skills. Class is an easy A if you meet with her outside of class to get feedback on essays--she will tell you exactly what you need to do to succeed.

AMAZING PROFESSOR. If you need a writing credit, take this class. Her class is structured very clearly, follow instructions and you will get an A. Participation points come from participating in class discussions, but you get to know everyone very well. She also brings treats occasionally! Prof. Morris will help you succeed in this class!

If you get Susan Morris for Writing 150 you should thank your lucky stars. Her class is fun, and she's grades fairly. She is always available for feedback on essay's and prepares you for writing in college. I would highly recommend her class to anyone looking to expand their rhetorical capabilities without an overbearing amount of busywork.

Prof Morris cares about each students success and improvement. She offers great critique on papers, grades fairly, and all of the assignments helped me to become a better writer. Sometimes the work outside of class seemed excessive, but nothing was without purpose. Of all the writing 150 teacher, choose Sister Morris! You won't regret it.

Sister Morris is, by far, my favorite college professor ever. She makes a difficult subject like writing easy and approachable. She is always helping you with the essays you have to write, and she makes both the papers and the class enjoyable. She brings food occasionally. I wouldn't take writing with any other professor.

Susan is the bomb! This woman is so kind and somehow makes 2 hour lectures fun. She even occasionally brings snacks for the class! Susan is a fair grader and explains each paper in detail. She is required to give you 12 essays but she's constantly helping along the way! I wouldn't take the class from anyone else!
She is one of my favorite teachers ever. I love her class. I would strongly suggest her for anyone searching for a great writing 150 class.

Coming from the Mechanical Engineering major, I was deathly afraid of taking a Writing 150 Class. To be frank, I think that writing sucks. But Sister Morris made it great! She is a very likable teacher who cares very deeply about her students. The textbook she put together is a collection of Gen Conf talks, famous stories, etc. and is my fav ever!

Holy cow, Sister Morris is seriously the best. I hate reading and writing, but this class was fun and inspiring. The work load is not excessive, and the readings are really interesting and really enhance the class experience. Three main papers that are totally doable. She is so helpful and approachable. I would totally take another class from her.

Sister Morris is a great professor and she is very willing to meet with you and help you with your writing. She genuinely cares about her students and has a strong desire to help all build writing skills. She expects a lot out of her students (not an easy grader and is a stickler for due dates) but she is understanding and focuses on improvement.

I was not looking forward to a writing class but Sister Morris was amazing. There were three main papers, two of them were 6-8 pages, then the last one was a 8-10 page research paper. It really was not hard at all as long as you stay on schedule, she gives you more than enough time for assignments. Nothing was busy work and it was well manageable.

Sister Morris is amazing. I wasn't super excited to take this class from the start, but Sister Morris made it awesome. She helps her students gain a love for the topics she teaches and is super helpful when questions arise. Take this class, put in the work, and it you will get a lot out of it.

Professor Adams was great! The class was very informative and pleasant. Professor Adams has over a decade of field experience so she knows what she's about and shared stories that were relevant to the class. There are some book reviews and I didn't stay quite on top of my project, so I had to catch up at the end. Don't do that and you'll be fine!

Professor Adams classes are very difficult, she expects a very professional quality in your assignments. All that being said, you'll learn a lot from her experience in the genealogy industry, and she provides many opportunities for extra credit. As long as you are willing to work hard and take her feedback seriously, you'll succeed in her classes.

Professor Adams is amazing! She is very knowledgeable in Family History and provides great feedback that helps in professional settings. She knows what she's doing and her classes are always fun. Definitely take a class with her!

Suzy is a very kind person and knowledgeable about editing. However, she grades in a very harsh and completely arbitrary way that seems to expect students to read her mind and copy her editing style exactly. Despite being a very experienced editor, I left this class feeling worse about my editing skills and very discouraged as an editor.

Suzy is a wonderful teacher. She picks assignments and projects that will give you real experience with what you are learning. She is always available to give you feedback or check something before you submit it. There is a lot of reading and assignments, but it's all worth it. She's super accommodating if you have a need, and she's so sweet!
Suzy is awesome 10/10

Suzy is one of my absolute favorite professors. I have taken two classes from her, and am taking two more next semester. She is kind, caring, and so smart. She is so willing to help, and she truly wants her students to succeed. There is quite a bit of homework, but the majority of it was very helpful and educational. 10/10 would recommend.

430 is a really cool class with Suzy. You work with the same group all semester so she has you come up with a team charter and it makes group work so much better. She's a really fair grader with this class and there's no busy work, because you're putting all your effort into your book. She's really helpful when you're not sure how to edit something
Her class wasn't difficult but there was a lot of busy work and some of her lectures weren't very helpful.

I think Suzy is an excellent professor. She's so clear, organized, and intelligent. She's good at explaining difficult concepts, and is always prepared to spend as long as you need to help you understand. Not a super hard class, but you'll learn so much. There are a lot of assignments, but they're all fairly easy and are essential to your learning.

Professor Wilson is great. He makes a tremendous effort to make things relevant to current events. Engaging readings and interesting guest speakers. Very open minded about AI, which created a very helpful and unique learning environment. Intense tests, but there are resources to help. I am very glad I took this course.

Took AHTG in 2022 and he broadcast political views instead of just teaching history. Called everyone who didn't receive the vaccine a m*rderer... &sinner cus even pres. nelson got it so some people didn't follow the prophet. I hope prof. Wilson heals from whatever loss happened! I definitely recommend taking this class, but from a different prof!
He is a super nice professor but he didn't really make UNIV fun, it just felt like the biggest waste of time.

I took UNIV 101 from Professor Wilson, and it was a blast! I lot of people felt like their univ classes were full of busy work, but to me this class was something I looked forward to, and was the best way to start my Monday and Wednesdays. We played volleyball once as a class. I feel like I've made a ton of really good friends through this class!

I took UNIV 101 from Prof. Wilson. He's a smart guy and cares about what he does. He can be a little boring and get off on topics that don't really matter. He tries to have a lot of fun and do what is best for you/the class, so it can change a bit. He's a good guy but I don't know if I would repeat taking one of his classes.

His lectures turned into soap box lectures about the evils of the GOP and how awful trump is without any actual discourse. It got old fast, that being said I got an A but spent a lot of time studying and reading would recommend looking at taking AHTG from someone else.

One of my favorite professors. I loved his lectures. You can tell he really loves America but also isn't blind to the challenges, and he looks at multiple issues from multiple perspectives. 
There was a good amount of reading, but nothing unmanageable. His tests aren't easy, but not bad. when I took it they were far easier than the other AH classes

Professor Wilson's lectures were really boring, and it was a struggle to stay awake each time. The exams are unnecessarily difficult. The amount of reading and homework and labs and such should make this a 6 credit class at least! I spent over 50 hours a week outside of class working for this class.

Week one he told us that in the past students have called his class disorganized and that this wasn't true. I can fully attest that those students were correct. His ignoring this kind of feedback speaks to the nature of what kind of person he is. He grades tough, he NEVER gives clear expectations for assignments, and his lectures are SO boring.

Oh, the dreaded AHT. This class was super hard, especially for a first-semester student. I recommend waiting if you are in high school reading this and deciding whether to take it or not. The only reason I gave him 3 stars was because his structure was very organized and the TAs were incredible. Never interacted with him. Lectures are pointless.
I liked Professor Wilson, but the class was a lot of work. My roommate took the class from Professor Kimball and loved it.

The lectures are pretty interesting, I'll give him that. But this class has no need to be so difficult for a gen ed class. Hours of reading before every class, the tests are super hard, you need to remember even the smallest things that are mentioned, most of the test question come from the multitude of reading assignments. Good guy, bad class

Wilson is pretty alright. Sometimes his lectures are good, he has a good sense of humor so sometimes they're pretty funny. Other times, he's just reading straight from his laptop and it's boring.
